REVIEW_TEXT: Great.....

My family and I had Bubby's brunch on a Saturday morning. Â We got there at 10am and there wasn't much of a wait. Â Tribeca must be a family friendly neighborhood since everyone parked their strollers outside without worry. Â For those with itty bitty ones they do have high-chairs and the changing table is located downstairs. Â  As for the food, I had the Bubby's Breakfast with homefries and ham. Â The ham was a bit dry but everything else on the plate was good. Â I had a taste of my sister's blueberry pancakes and it was delicious. Â The only negative was what looked like a chunk of cheese on the lip of my coffee cup. Â I don't think they make French Onion coffee. Â Our waitress apologized and replaced the cup. Â At $30 per person it's expensive for breakfast + coffee + tax but this isn't your neighborhood IHOP.

I really like this place, but they need to get their menu sorted out. I finally went for brunch, which I'd been eager to try based on reviews and the mouth-watering online menu (sugarfreak.com/fooddrinkâ€¦), but was disheartened when the baked apple with moonshine double cream wasn't available. That's just cruel!

This is one of my favorite places in the US. Awesome! No reservations and the place was packed but the maÃ®tre d' squeezed us in when someone didn't arrive on time. Carol was our server and she was really helpful and made some great recommendations. Simply the best steak tartare!

Make sure you go with a small group of friends that ALL like to share food so you can try 1 of everything that everyone on here is talking about. Â I loved it ALL except I won't know about the breakfast sandwich until the next time I go since this one girl at our table wouldn't give me a bite. Â C'mon! Â I'm always a Savory over Sweet breakfast lover BUT I had a foodgasm for the (you guessed it) blueberry pancakes. Â I'm thinking about the blueberry pancakes right now......

Have been coming here since they opened. The quality has always been great and the selection of bahn mi sandwiches has expanded significantly. I love the bulgogi bomb me and the bahn mi fries. They also have delicious bubble teas and jelly drinks.

It is a quaint little cafÃ© and a great spot for brunch. I ate everything less the plate itself which says quite a bit all its own. An omelet for myself with the perfectly seasoned hashbrowns and salad, my friend scrambled eggs and crispy bacon. We took our time catching up from the little things to big and were never rushed even though it felt as though we were there long enough to have understood if they'd shoved the check at us. Definitely a solid brunch place on a nice relaxing Sunday.

Station House is a Beer Hall, Whiskey Den, and Gastropub located in Forest Hills. Â I was invited here by another Yelp Elite - Will C - for a football game, and I loved it! Â The atmosphere was modern and clean. My faves? - Beer Menu - OH THE VARIETY! Â All of the beers being served on draft are up on a TV screen with a monitor of how much beer is left in the keg. Â Pretty awesome. - Smoked Ribs - Steak Sandwich - Roasted Brussel Sprouts - Truffle Pecorino Fries ENJOY!!

Most Amazing Brunch in the City. Â Everything on the brunch menu is a hit - especially the pan dolce and tres arepas. Â 1 hour all you can drink for $12 with a wide variety of brunch drinks - including mimosas, bloody marys, a few different kinds of margaritas, etc. Service is absolutely impeccable. Â William, The Maitre d', and the rest of the staff are all super nice and attentive. Â Making sure that you are having a great time throughout your entire stay. Â If you are doing the drink special - you will not have an empty glass ever. I haven't been in for dinner yet, but plan on it very soon.
A lot of pony tailed tattooed hunks tending bar. Excellent Aperol spritzs. I would recommend

Nothing not to like here. Was especially good for brunch, and especially if you need kid friendly. They have a whole section for stroller parking. Eggs were fluffy and were amazing with pastrami hash. The grapefruit juice was not so great and tasted like it was out of a bottle, which was the only flaw. Kale omelet was also memorable. Service and hostess were also warm and friendly, and was easy to get a table.
Great place with great food and service. Only here for brunch but will return for dinner.

Over the past couple of weeks I've been to this great new Hell's Kitchen venue twice-great bar (and even better Bartender!), comfortable tables inside and out! As a group we tried the salads, burgers, omelettes and pancakes, each better than the next! A real find!

Heidi's House was by far the best place we ate during our entire trip to NY. My husband ordered the paella and I the mac and cheese with the intention of splitting. Â Although I would have loved to keep them both for myself. Â  The location is mingled with brownstones in the upper east side and is of course small but quaint. Â Doors open at 5:00 and seating was full shortly thereafter with a waiting list already started. Â  I almost wish we'd found this place sooner so we could go more than once.

I almost never write reviews on Yelp, but I really want to make sure this place makes it and continues to put out such great, modern Mexican food! Â My wife and I just got back from a long weekend in Mexico City, and this place brings us right back to the "haute mexican" food we had there. We were there today for brunch and had the scallop ceviche (fantastic - nice sea scallops, as opposed to the bay scallops you often see in scallop ceviches), the torta, which they make in a kind of "French Dip" style and which was FANTASTIC. Â The broth it was soaked in was reallllly good. Â And finally one of those handmade tortillas, fried, with slow roasted pork shoulder, a bit of guacamole, onion relish, cilantro, cabbage and radish. Â It was tied together with a tomato-habanero broth which was just spicy enough. We just had coffee today, but they apparently got their liquor license recently so in addition to the fresh juices they now apparently have margaritas. Â Oh and flambee mango with mezcal soaked cranberries and some sort of ice cream I believe was the dessert special - I wish we had room and that it wasn't 1pm. The few times we've been for dinner Chef Hugo hasn't disappointed either, but I'll leave that for a follow up review.

Rule of thumb: Hole-in-a-wall = awesome food. This theory holds true over 90% of the time...unless you get food poisoning...then that's a different story. (Don't worry, that's not the case here.) My first time here was a year ago with some coworkers that wanted to try the place. My most recent visit was just a couple of days ago on a Scoutmob deal for free regular order of fries (free!). The place is a bit small, so you'll most likely have to take your order to go, but both times the fries came out fresh and delicious, with the right combination of oily goodness on the outside and potato-y softness on the inside. The price for a regular sized order is $4.50, but believe me, it's a heap of fries. Any bigger and you'll have to split it with someone. Your biggest dilemma in coming to this place is choosing the right sauce to go with your fries. There's always ketchup and mayo (which is free), but why get that when there are also 30 other choices written on their chalkboard by the register/frying/packing/saucing station? Each "special" sauce is $1 (if you get three, it's $2.50), but they give you enough to finish off your regular order of fries. After staring befuddled at the choices for a minute, I chose the curry ketchup and Vietnamese pineapple mayo. Both were delicious. I may not be back soon (gotta lose some weight), but one day I shall visit again!

Only Australian food I've ever had prior to coming here was trying out the meat pies at the Tuck Shop on E. Houston and steak at Outback, which I know doesn't count. Wasn't too impressed with either. My friend suggested we try The Thirsty Koala in the ethnic food Mecca of Queens: Astoria. Looking at menu, I noticed they didn't serve koala. Good, leave the cute critters alone. Nothing really stood out as something exclusive to Australia, actually. We started off with the lamb lollies (best part of meal). Savory, juicy, and just the right amount of fat left on to optimize the flavor. The lollies came with caramelized pumpkin, leafy greens (can't recall what kind) and pomegranate seeds which all complimented each other quite nicely. This app could actually be enough for an entree order. For the main dish, I decided upon the steak tacos. You get 2. I could only finish 1. Tortilla stuffed with steak, caramelized onion, pico de gallo, shredded cabbage, cilantro, and chipotle sauce. Very Australian right? Half of the fillings will definitely fall off the taco before you take your first bite. It was ok, nothing special. Looking back, friendly service and our meal in addition to most items on the menu were more American than anything, but it didn't matter as long as the food didn't suck and no koalas were harmed.

I order the $28 beef BBQ during the lunch. The portion was extreme small. The tofu with beef stew, i only found a little bit of one piece of Â beef ,but they made their own tofu and can serve u big portion of the tofu. I won't go back

Great atmosphere, great service by a staff who KNOWS their food and drink and very, very yummy food! Â Went there on a date night. Â My husband had read something about it on "Edible Brooklyn" and was really excited about giving absinthe a go (we had never had the absinth experience). Â We arrived early in the evening - very lovely space with a warm old worldy sort of ambiance. Â We asked the bartender/mixologist what he would recommend as it was our first time. Â He was really helpful and knew his stuff. Â We had the Duplais Blanche and Veiux Pontarlier. Â So very tasty, but we couldn't resist the cocktails off of the menu. Â I ventured on to the Stormy Weather (can't say no to anything with jalapeno) and he had the Whisky Smash. Â As we were drinking we thought...this would be great with cheese! Â So we ordered a cheese plate and went with some suggestions from our very knowledgeable bartender (it is FANTASTIC when the folks at the restaurant know and love food and drink as much as you do). Â Cocktails and cheese! Â It was so good that I went there for brunch with some friends and once again the service was excellent, the cocktails were amazing and as a bonus, the brunch menu was damn tasty! Â Between the 4 of us there were a lot of ooo's, ahhs and oh my gods so yes, we did enjoy our Grilled Burger, Croque Madame and Spinach and Goat Cheese Croissant. Â What more do you need?

I walked back into the apartment Saturday afternoon a bit vexed after watching my team draw a game it should have won. The love of my life said to me, "I haven't left the house yet, we should go out." As we hit the bricks, she continued, "I'd like some good food made from fresh, local vegetables." Now by this she could have meant "let's go to the greenmarket and buy stuff for you to cook" but I was still feeling a bit under the weather from the night before, so I thought frantically and recalled hearing about Rucola because of their proposed a la carte CSA thingy. I had signed up for the email list but only received 3 emails from then indicating that they had items (but they all sounded good: garlic scapes, heirloom beets, and baby lettuces. If only either of us liked beets). Anyway, we walked in to Rucola at 3:45 on a Saturday afternoon. The block was pristine, and the same atmosphere carried over into the restaurant. The place felt both sleek and comfy, attributes that don't often coexist. There was only one other occupied table inside, though four other parties arrived over the course of the meal and the tiny outdoor tables (which were taken when we arrived) turned over as well. But what I really wanted to relate to you was the smell. When we walked in, it smelled so intoxicatingly good that I knew right away we'd hit paydirt. We had eggplant caponata escarole salad a slice of the pizza of the day (capers, mozz, sauce, hot peppers) a slice of the seasonal frittata (cippolini, piave, zucchini) mimosa glass of rose espresso drip coffee The eggplant was great. If I'm not mistaken it had capers, pine nuts, mint, and a little sundried tomato. When my mom makes it she puts in celery and I don't think she uses mint. Usually my mom's methods form my preference, but I think Rucola's version was better. The foccacia that came with it was solid but not spectacular (could have been better if it was warm and a little crispy on the edges). The pizza was also great. The sauce was from cherry tomatoes I believe they said, and it was intensely sweet and flavorful. The cheese was applied sparingly but tasted excellent, and the peppers were even more sparing, which was good because a little went a long way. The escarole was extra fresh and the crutons it came with were nice. The rose, recommended by the server (a friendly blonde lady named Jess [ica?] I belive) was more than sufficient. I thought the frittata was slightly bland, but my wife loved it. The espresso was great, though tiny. This gets five stars because of (1) the high quality of the food and ingredients, (2) the extremely reasonable prices, (3) the seeming intent behind it (emblematized by the CSA idea and the local ingredients, and (4) the virally charming overall atmosphere, including the service and decor.

I admit that i was very drunk by the time we got to this bar, but i remember most of it. Â The place is huge as is the beer list. Â Theres a ton of seating around the bar and a lot of tables. Â Service at the bar was great. Â Theres a big projection screen although it's kinda in a weird spot where you can't see it from the bar and have to turn around and look in the corner. Â I'm pretty sure there was birthday party there for a kid that couldn't have been older than 4, which i found to be a little weird. Â My girlfriend ended up leaving my credit card there and the bartender was really nice when we called to ask if they had it. Â The next day they remembered us and had the card waiting. Â i had a great time there and hope to check it out when it's a little more crowded at night.

Such a cute place, it's a shame that they don't care about the quality of their food. The shrimp dish that I had was floating in a pan of olive oil so thick that it made me a little sick to have mistaken it for sauce. I used a nice piece of bread to soak it up so I would have something in my stomach since the shrimp itself was of the frozen bag variety: tiny, farm raised and LAME. The stars are merely for the coffee and the bread, but frankly I was glad someone else was paying for this meal, because I just don't see why I would bother coming back for either.
I didn't know that it's food stand before I went there. Around 7 dollars for a delicious take-away meal. I see it as a deal.

The name is kind of hard to say, but all you need to know is that it's delicious! Came here upon a recommendation of a friend who LOVES their Hainanese chicken. Since my experience with that dish and Malaysian food in general was pretty limited, I wanted to try it! I read on Yelp how everyone loved their Roti Canai so I had to order that too. Two of those dishes just for me was a bit too much, but I did the best I could. First of all the roti--yum! Loved the curry dipping sauce and the puffy tortilla-like bread. Nice bit of heat in that curry. The Hainanese chicken was very flavorful and tender, and I opted to have the default dark meat version--not only was it a little cheaper, I think it's more flavorful than just the breast-meat version. All in all, very satisfying! The service was good, if not overly friendly, and I'm glad I missed the dinner rush; there was quite a sizable crowd by the time I left. STEPH JUDGEMENT: Great Chinese/Malaysian food in a pleasant atmosphere.

Best pizza I've had in NYC. Â I haven't been to that many, but still one of the best pizzas I've had here. Â There is a trick to ordering pizzas here - don't go overboard with the toppings. Â NYC pizzas are thin crust and are known for that crispy crust - if you get too many toppings - the crust won't be crispy anymore. Â Limit the toppings to 2 or 3 and you'll be good. Â We got pepperoni and mushrooms and the last slice was still crispy 30 minutes after the pizza came to our table. Â  1. Â The sauce - excellent! Â It doesn't taste like tomato paste. Â It doesn't taste overly sweet. Â You can taste the herbs in the sauce. Â You can taste the garlic that went into the sauce. Â The sauce has a good amount of kick too. Â Great sauce! 2. Â The cheese - go and get extra cheese. Â Otherwise you won't get enough. 3. Â The toppings - pepperoni was great, mushrooms were awesome. Â You can tell the quality of a pizza place if they use canned mushrooms or fresh ones. Â They use fresh mushrooms here. Â Also, go get some extra garlic - adds so much flavor!

The food in this place is amazing. Came here for brunch and it was oh so yummy. The yuca benedicto was do die for. So I sacrificed myself. I got it with a sangria which was part of the Â brunch deal. The only thug stopping this from being 5 stars (because the food is great and so is the music and atmosphere) is the wait time. Our waitress was...MIA most of the time. We waited maybe 20 minutes for the check. Bleh, I would definitely come back though. (This was my review for Summer 2012) (Now Winter 2013) I can't tell you how many times I've come here for happy hour. If you're wise, you'll do what I do. I bolt out of the office at 5, hail a cab, then head straight there because this place gets annoyingly packed. The have possibly the best coconut mojitos at the best mojito price you will EVER find in the city unless you make it yourself. $6 for ANYTHING in NYC, are you freakin kidding me?!? I wouldn't believe it if I didn't experience it so many times, so go experience it damnit! You won't be upset.

My boyfriend and I stumbled upon this gem by accident. I was parked right outside and my boyfriend randomly noticed it. Came here after dinner to satisfy my sweet tooth and boy did it deliver. I had a caramel latter with macaroons and it was tasty and appetizing. We didn't have any of the actual food items, but I could see from the dishes around me they looked very good! We will be returning for lunch!

Came here for brunch - The brunch menu is regular american fare with a smattering of mediterranean dishes. I think the prices are ok and the service is good but all in all the food was just a-ok. Nothing to write back home to mommy about. While I liked the ambience of the place, I dont think I will be coming back anytime soon.

GOOD food, semi-FAST service, FREE tea FOOD - I came here for a quick lunch during a break. The Katsu is really really good, very crispy yet warm and light! I got a chicken katsu which came above a bowl of rice with some eggs. My friend got the curry katsu, which was pretty good too. Honestly, this is the best katsu i've had in the city (but i've only ever been to 1-2 other katsu joints). I highly highly recommend it! The prices are also not exorbitant for the location; however, $12 for a bowl / dish that I could only finish half of is all right ATMOSPHERE - The place was definitely filled up but not overcrowded. We were seated within like 5 min during a busy lunch hour. Â  SERVICE - the food was delivered pretty quickly. Free tea was distributed initially and then appetizers / miso soup / sides came within seconds of placing our order. I was pleasantly surprised with the speediness of the service. They were a bit slow with the check process though, but besides that everything was fine. I recommend coming to katsu-hama!
Went past 9pm and it was really busy! Simple menus and the drinks were ok. Atmosphere was a bit rowdy.. fried avacados were on point.

When I walked into B&B a few days ago, the SO and I wanted a simple, hearty burger-based meal, and that's what we got. I confess that when I saw the name of the joint in my Yelp app, I pictured something between Five Guys and Bareburger: the equidistant options abutting my abode. In fact, it was that handsome place I'd passed a few times strolling down Houston, wondering what the heck it was. The elegant "New American" dining room is definitely classy enough for a date or a SoHo starter meal for your visiting parents. It looks brand-spanking new and is very clean and well-kept, and there are enough staff members on hand to make sure it stays that way. At 6 pm on Saturday, there was a 30-45 minute wait, but we were offered bar seats right away--and took them. Tucked into a far (but not gloomy or removed) corner, it was the perfect perch from which to observe the comings and goings. The most memorable sight was a young mom dining with her toddler, whom she sat across from her rather than putting the kid in a baby seat. It was begging to be a video meme. The busy bartender was friendly enough. She served us some tasty Brooklyn Blast double IPAs. There are a few other beers on tap, all food friendly, though the prices are shamelessly inflated ($9 for the BB, and others $8 and up). You WILL be paying for rent here, so don't come to save a buck. Our burgers were very, very good: SO had the classic, cooked to medium rare perfection. As was my "Bash Style" burger, topped with onion and bacon jam, pickles, american cheese, and special sauce. It was definitely an Ivy League burger, both in cost and quality, though a little on the small side. The fries were decent, too, though not memorable. The whipped potatoes, swapped for fries by my dining partner, were delicious. B&B is, as I discovered, a "wine pub" (a budding trend in NY). I would return to try some of their pours and pair them with more ambitious dishes (which they have).

Absolutely the best. I was fortunate enough to come here once before, so on a recent trip, my husband, the pizza lover, wanted to go as well. We swung by for a pie during lunch and since it was his first time there, we went with the large 18 inch standard margherita pizza. Thanks to the fast cooking coal oven, the pizza arrived just a few minutes later, just as I remembered it, with the individual slices of mozzarella splashed haphazardly in the sauce and with just the right amount of basil sprinkled across the top. Upon removing a slice, there was no slippage of toppings and upon examining the pizza's beautiful crust's underside, you could both see and smell the markings from the coal oven. When you visit, don't forget that Lombardi's doesn't accept credit cards, so make sure you have cash. I'm absolutely convinced that pizza doesn't get any better than Lombardi's and my husband is now a converted fan as well!

The food is outstanding, but you certainly will pay for it. All the ingredients are super fresh and incredible quality -- some are even local also. It's a great special occasion kind of place ...the brunch is amazing.

I stumbled upon this place after a show in January '13, and fell in love with their empanadas. Â Recently, I found myself in the same neighborhood after another show and actively sought out this narrow little hole in the wall. Â Now, when my boyfriend and I arrived, the line to get in was out the door - it should be noted that tables are lined up against one side of the restaurant and people have to walk single file up and down the length on the other side of the restaurant....I wasn't exaggerating when I said it was a narrow hole in the wall. Â That being said, once we were seated, we ordered a frenzy of delicious food. Â Everything we ate was outstanding, but if I could only recommend one thing, it would be the fried yucca with guacamole.

Case Enrique is a nice little spot in LIC. Staff: very attentive and polite. Great service. They served this complimentary Cheetos like thing. Very oily for some reason. Guac - wasn't the best I had but it was decent. Lacked flavor like salt, tomato, and onions and not as chunky as the other guacs I'm accustomed to but definitely edible. Beef meatballs - had an egg inside which caught me by surprise. Sauce was a tad spicy but good. Lengua (beef tongue) tacos - I love beef tongue so we had to try it. Beef tongue usually has the chewy consistency I love but this was cooked tender. Chicken something something verde - chicken stuffed enchilada with queso fresco and avocado. At this point I was too stuffed but still good and tasty. Mexican chocolate was very good. Basically a chocolate mousse with biscuits. And.... Mexican coke to drink.
Great halal food!

One of the better ramen shop but very limited seating and not great for large groups. We had to sit with random people during our meal but the ramen was very tasteful and I would definitely recommend checking this place out if you're in town.

Although our food was tasty, I had the seasonal sides-sesame kale, mashed potatoes, I was overcharged from what the menu said, despite having asked two different waitresses! The atmosphere was fun, the music was atrocious.

For my only venture into Queens, I went to Sweet Afton. Â And if offered an invitation to return, I would definitely take up that offer. Â  The vibe of this place is West Village bohemian chic with a preppy twist. Â I like very much! The food here, though limited, is tasty enough to bring one back. Â That burger is oh-so-good. Â Thick, juicy meat on a toasty, warm bun. Â Whew! Â I never thought of myself as pickle person, but I guess frying one made me a believer! Â  Definitely try the fried pickles... As for the drinks, I always veer towards margaritas. Â Sweet Afton's did not disappoint. Â Spicy, sour, and sweet flavors are all in that drink. Â The beers available are also well-chosen. Â Dark and heavy to light and refreshing. One will never leave this place either thirsty or hungry.

I am never disappointed when I come to Applewood. Not once have I thought I really paid too much for something I could have easily made at home. I have been here several times and whenever I can convince my friends from the other boroughs to join me for dinner in Park Slope I often take them here I recently dined there for Eat in Brooklyn with the $25 dollar prix fix menu. I am often displeased with the menu options at many other places and find that they skimp on the good expensive ingredients. This was not the case at Applewood. I had a delicious red leaf salad with preserved meyer lemons and cheddar cheese from upstate NY. I have no idea where they procured this out of season lettuce because it was very tender for this time of the year. It tasted like the lettuce my mom grew in our garden. Â For my main course I had one of the best preparations of sea bass which was served on delicate celery root puree, topped with a aioli and Â pea shoots. For dessert I had a tart rhubarb crisp with amazing homemade cream cheese ice cream. This was all for $25. There mixed drinks and wine list is also wonderful and well chosen to pair with the food. I love this place because they take wonderful familiar comfort foods and bring them to a higher level of enjoyment with fine ingredients and a bit of imagination. The food is beautifully prepared, the waiters are very nice and knowledgeable. Â I can not wait for my next visit.

I went here with my girlfriends for brunch. The food was pretty good but my stomach did not handle the Mexican-as-first-meal-of-the-day very well and I actually felt slightly sick afterwards. My friend and I shared chiquelta (sp?) huevos which were sunny side up eggs on top of a cheese, salsa nacho and meat covered concoction that was delicious as well as a pretty satisfying hamburger. We also got drinks which were pretty good as well. The staff was very friendly as well. Not sure if I would go back, or maybe not for brunch as I'm scared of feeling sickly again.

I waited (at the cafe across the street after putting my name down) for 1 hour and 40 minutes to eat here and I can say that it's not worth the hype. Really, it's not. You have to trust me on this! This place has too much hype that I think a lot of people are brainwashed into thinking it's phenomenal--especially if you're starving after a 2 hour wait (and really, who wouldn't be starving at that point!) My friend and I ordered the Blueberry Pancakes and French Toast. These two items were big on portion. The dressings (syrup, toppings, etc.) are their saving grace, but the actual dishes themselves weren't spectacular at all. The food wasn't bad, but it just wasn't great or memorable. I know I could find equally good/much better pancakes and french toast at various diners around the city. Next time I'll have to get a savory brunch item--ie: The Southern Breakfast, and reassess. But for now, this place is really no where near 5 stars! But I can understand the curiosity--still think everyone should experience "it"--just don't be surprised when the food is mediocre. Their grapefruit juice is great however. It's fresh and very pulpy!

I've been here quite a bit so of course my experience changes but not at all drastic. The service is good during brunch and dinner. It's always too busy for me to have dinner at the table section (without reservation) so I go to the bar section which I enjoy. It's more relaxing and less formal. Their Kafta is to die for- can't help getting it all the time. And the halumi - it used to come with more rice (which I thoroughly enjoyed) and now it's mostly veggies/squash covered in cheese. But it is good! Their brunch menu is quite delicious. Their regular coffee I could do without and the Lima bean plate too. But all in all, it's worth going over and over again. Our bill is never less than 90.00 for two people but you will leave satisfied. Oh and their dessert- the candy bar especially is really delicious. I'm sure you'll like it. Why not give a 5? I am only a fan.

They make a mean cocktail at North End Grill where both your head and wallet will be feeling a bit lighter after only one. North end does offer some great 50% off happy hour specials to local employees, so be sure to ask. As for my favorite, I'd have to go with the Blueberry Mojito. It could stand to be sweetened down a bit, but otherwise it was delicious.

if it is only for their steak & eggs, they would get 5 stars. It is $12, and very tasty. The pumpkin pancake with yogurt sauce is OK too. This is the place the gives most value and taste for the money, I consider 'service to the community'.
This place is awesome.

I was here on Tuesday night celebrating an anniversary. I had been trying to book a restaurant one week before the day and was put on waiting lists. On Monday night I told my wife I give up. She searched and came up with this place and I said sure since it is just down the street. An unassuming building and if you didn't know where you were going, you would miss it. The interior was very nice. For some reason it reminded me of Vitae and a 70's vibe with a modern twist. Lucky for us that we were able to book a table because it filled up fast. Many different areas to eat - high counter communal table, big tables, small tables, and at least one private room at the entrance. The menu and wine list was great. So many good looking dishes that we could have ordered almost anything and I am sure we would be happy. The purple sweet potato break was a nice recommendation to start the experience. We ordered the kale salad and red snapper cheviche. Fantastic! Both were so nice. Savory and full of flavor. We then ordered the pistachio halibut and pumpkin ravioli. Two more wonderful dishes. I wanted something seasonal and it was not filling or too light. The halibut was nicely done and most certainly a winner. We finished the meal with Market Crisp with buttermilk ice cream and one other dessert, pudding or custard with salted whipped cream. That was rich and filling. I like that the menu changes and that it is farm to table. On top of all the great dishes, the ambiance was nice (with the exception of the drunk, cackling girl table behind us that had everyone turning their head to see where the noise was coming from), the lighting, the bathroom was nice, but most of all the great service and the manager. He was at every table checking on everyone's meal. He came to out table twice, and that is customer service at it's best. A wonderful experience overall. {With two more exceptions and that is the couple next to us and T-shirt guy in cougar print slip-ons stretching himself along the sofa and the late couple taking flash photos with their phone several times. Grow up.}

My wife, daughter and I just had the pleasure of eating here during our visit to NYC. It was a great experience. My wife has celiac's and was excited to have some good Italian food and this place was excellent for her needs. My daughter and I ate "normal" food and loved it as well. The owner is there to personnallyake sure you have a nice dining experience and what a nice guy he is. I only wish this restaurant was in boston. The service was excellent as well. I apologize for forgetting his name but he is a nice gentleman from Mexico.
WOW!!!! What a GREAT spot for Greek food!
I'm a fan. I've visited several times and have never been disappointed. Brunch and dinner both, equally delicious. I'll be back soon! PW

I usually come here for dinner and some drinks but today I came for breakfast/brunch and I was pleasantly surprised. I had their eggs benedict and a bloody mary. My friends had their croissant french toast and it was quite tasty. Generally I think that this place is a bit over-rated and over-priced. But I guess you pay for the ambiance and just the fact that you went to a popular restaurant in the city. I still come here since its open 24 hours, and its very convenient. The food is usually good so you can't really go wrong at 4 in the morning.

I'm a little embarrassed to say that I have an obsession with fried foods and it can't get any more embarrassing than when I'm at Pommes Frites. Â I see the fries and I can't help but smile on the inside just a little. Â I love their mango chutney dipping sauce although most have told me their cheese is better. Â Eh. Â Whatever floats your boat.

Came here for a happy hour and was pleasantly surprised. Please note we did not eat here, as that seems to be the source for the crappy reviews. I came for the $5 Sangria and drink specials. We went to the upstairs bar and stood most of the time overlooking from the balcony and watching their GIANT projection TV. I do have to say some things were poorly placed like the HUGE list of beers can't be seen from the upstairs bar at all, nor do they have any signs upstairs listing any specials or beers. But for a cheap drink and a cool ambiance, I will be going back.
Mango Chutney sauce

I love this place. When you're in Manhattan and you're maybe feeling a little overwhelmed by the dodgy pubs and garish pizza parlors, catch a cab to the West Village, walk around, and have brunch at Tartine. It'll recharge your batteries and ground your senses. The food is nothing fancy, really. The atmosphere is what makes Tartine special. Â I started eating there when I lived in NY years ago, and it will remain a staple destination on my NY itinerary.

After being drenched from the rain on the way over to Chinatown we finally made it here and had to wait in line for about 20 minutes to get seated.. darn me for walking next door because if they call your number and you're not there.. you'll have to wait all over again. Immediately after we sat down the server came over and asked us if we wanted the dumplings and since we were starving I guess we got a little too order-happy and had 4 orders of the crab dumplings and 2 orders of the pork dumplings (each order has 8 pieces) and even ordered some shanghai noodles and black bean clams as well. Â  Everything was deeeeeeelicious and had met our expectations nonetheless... Probably one of the cheaper meals we had during our whole trip..
great backyard patio. Â not huge but tables are spaced out well enough. delish burger, juicy & not too bulbous. Â also had a grilled cheese w/ tomato with choice of cheese. Â had the cheddar, yum!
tea is good. cash only.

I have been to Palo Santo for dinner on a few occasions. The atmosphere is cozy, the food is amazing and the wine is wonderful. On my last visit, my party of eight had a reservation for 8 PM. We were seated late due to the party before us taking longer than expected to finish up. While we are all easy going and hadn't said a word, the staff took it upon themselves to bring us a round of champagne to enjoy while we waited and they apologized. This type of service is hard to come by these days but reflects the excellence at this establishment. Of course, the staff is attentive during the entire meal as well. The sangria is notable and the wines from Uruguay are unique and tasty. All around, wonderful.

Great place to grab some good 'ol Chinese comfort food. Forget decor, this is a typical Chinese restaurant that knows how to cook good food. I had their roast pork, chicken and fried egg dish which was tasty. The chicken reminded me of Chinese duck in the way that it was prepared and how it tasted. The garlic sauce that came with the dish was so flavorful. This dish reminded me of the local food in Taiwan-simple, yet tasty.

Oh my lordy lord. All my life I was living in the dark...until I had a chicken and rice platter. I've lived in Los Angeles all my life and not once heard of "chicken and rice". On my last trip to New York, my friends were raving about it and I was so curious, I took the subway to 53rd and 3rd at 11pm to grab myself one of these infamous dishes. Although it was fuh-reeeezing cold, waiting outside and eating my chicken and rice plate with super hot sauce and a runny nose was absolutley worth it! Make sure you bring some napkins. Things can get a little messy with the white sauce... (insert sexual innuendo) Make sure you go to the right one! Don't be fooled by the phonies across the street. The men at the OG cart wear yellow jackets. Puhhhh-lease come to Los Angeles!

I had the spicy tuna don and the spicy totto ramen - both really good. Spicy tuna don was rich and flavorful. Had sesame oil and cucumbers. Very good. Spicy ramen was great. The spicy sauce they used was some chili sesame oil with xo sauce ?? - whatever it was, it was tasty. Noodles and soup were very good. Soup is better than Ippudo just because it wasn't as salty as theirs. Char siu is also better than ippudo but still 2nd fiddle to Minca. I went around 1pm on a Wednesday so 10 minute wait maybe.

Visiting Google one day for work, I planned my day specifically so I could visit Los Tacos No.1. Â I mean, you know, priorities. Â The main thing I miss about working in the Bronx is the great, cheap Mexican food. Â No chance I was going to pass up the chance to get my fix while I could given that Midtown lunch options are generally horrible. Â I got here right when they were opening so there was no line. Â Los Tacos is kind of in an odd pot crammed with 2 other vendors but it's actually the size of a typical taqueria. Â I got my food quickly and made my way to a table outside to feast. I got a pollo asada taco as well as the much raved about adobada taco (roast pork). Â First off, as others have noted the corn tortilla is the way to go here. Â It's the best tortilla I've had on the East Coast. Â The adobada was a bit overhyped but was still great. Â Still if you like rich, caramelized pork, this bud's for you. Â I actually enjoyed the pollo asada a bit more. Â Probably one of the best tacos I've ever had. Â The given toppings were sufficient if a bit heavy handed but complemented the tacos well (my apologies for not remembering the list), and there's always more stuff on the side (radish, hot sauce, etc.) if you need it. If you're in or around the Chelsea market and you love Mexican food, this is a must visit. Â Outside of the Bronx and parts of Brooklyn and Queens I'm not sure if there are any serious competitors. Â I have to assume there usually is a line--others on here certainly say that--and I'd say that it's probably worth it as long as it doesn't go over half an hour. Â Great Mexican food is hard to come by in Manhattan, especially for a reasonable price. Â I'd kill a man to have this as a lunch option by me (maybe not but it is really good).

This is one of my favorite restaurants in New York, and I go there all the time. I love the atmosphere, and I always make sure I get a seat in front of the nice fireplace. The food is wonderful, though I've never tried the desserts, perhaps because I'm scared of loosing my love for the place. The desserts displayed at the bar look a bit gross.. Despite the potential dessert issue, the place is still so great I'll give it 5 stars!

I sometimes see one star reviews and read that the reviewer would like to give zero stars. Well this is the place that I wish I could give zero stars. We had one of the worst restaurant experiences I've ever had in NYC here. They were busy and clearly couldn't handle it. A waiter with a nasty attitude took our order. They were out of a number of things even though it was only 7pm. We adjusted our plan. After waiting over 40 minutes, one of the dishes we ordered came out (we were a four top). Then the waiter comes over to tell us that they were now also out of one of the other dishes that 2 of us had ordered and we should select something else. Â That kind of timing fumble is just absurd. But trying to make the best of the situation we chose other options. After another 25 minutes with half of our party sitting there with no food, the replacement dishes arrived. Then we find that one of the replacement dishes has a hair in it and the other is a shrimp dish and none of the shrimp was deveined. Totally disgusting. We asked for the check and headed to Cafe Cluny. The manager came over with free drink tickets as an apology, but I told him to keep them. We'll never be back. I hope this place goes out of business soon so that a good, well run restaurant can move into what is a super convenient location for me.

The food and ambiance here are top notch. I come here almost once a week since I live down the block. I go back and forth between being obsessed with their udon to being obsessed with their sushi tacos. Their pork betty melts in your mouth, the broth in the udon is rich and has a deep flavor and the sushi is fresh and fatty. Â It's really hard to go wrong here with anything. People are usually turned off by the big communal table but it totally works. I sit there about 90% of the time and I've never felt crowded or uncomfortable. The only reason I'm giving four stars instead of five is because at times the service can be a bit slow and snarky. Also, I find it really annoying that they only take cash.

Let's be honest. Junior's is all about its Cheesecake. Â  If you are true to yourself and go directly to the dessert menu, rather than attempt to make a balanced meal out of the other offerings, you will be much happier at the end of the day. Â Sure, you should have a balanced diet from all the food groups. Â But, those rules go out the window here. Â They don't apply. Â There is no point filling up on what are essentially wasted empty calories in this alternate sweet tooth universe. Â  Just go directly to the multitude of cheesecake flavors and pick one or two. Â If you need something to wash it down, that is permissible. Â  Anything worth indulging is worth overindulging when you know this is a one of a kind iconic moment. Â Go for broke. Â Admit what you really want, and don't feel the need to legitimize. Â  The only rationalization you need is that you dreamed about it, waited so long for this opportunity, and now that it is right in front of you it is time to fulfill yourself with one of the greatest foodie pleasures imaginable. Â  Go ahead. Cream in your mouth. You know you want it.
Excellent coffee, rapid service, minimal time between ordering, paying, and sipping your well-made Intelligentsia espresso/cortado/cappuccino. I'm definitely a fan of this place!

What a cute little place. Came here for brunch for my friends surprise birthday. Staff was super nice and friendly. Expect to wait alittle bit, it is small and very popular. I have never had a fresher tasting mimosa in my life. The french toast was delicious!!! I have a new spot to visit when I'm working in my LIC branch!
Every Monday they have $5 mojitos and some free apps. Can't get better than that.

My wife and I were originally going to visit a neighboring restaurant, but a local friend of mine strongly suggested against it. Â So walking around a bit and we came to Khao Kang. Â A relatively small restaurant with what appeared to be "no menu". Â We saw the chalk board and it said "2 entrees and steamed rice for 7 bucks or 3 entrees and steamed rice for 7.50"... whoa. Â  All the food is precooked and is set up buffet style. Â You point at what you want and they'll pile it on your plate. Â Most of the food was delicious for the price. Â I didn't expect extremely high quality, but it was pretty solid. Â Between my wife and I, we had 5 entrees, steamed rice, soup, thai iced tea and a soda for less than 20 dollars. Â The food has a nice amount of kick to it. Â If you enjoy spicy food and don't want to spend a fortune, please pay these guys a visit.

Had a good time here with a party of 5, we were sat downstairs, reservations were honored, a definite recommend. Good: -$5 happy hour mojito 4pm-7pm -Ropa Vielja is a solid pick -Paella Valenciana is a solid seafood pick -Nice vibe and good food all around -eating downstairs was quieter -good customer service -Short walk from several train lines Bad: -Upstairs seating is a little tight -Upstairs seating is a bit loud

Stop the reviews people! This place is as good as it gets. Small and intimate yes, as Mehta's food provides some of the most eclectic flavor profile combinations you will run across in the city! This place provides a terrific ambiance for romance or friends. One absolutely cannot dine here without trying the "Zucchini Hummus Pizza" or the "Braised Pork Buns w/Apple Chutney"! OMG....if one could make love to food this would be it! Me being an uptown guy have to go on to say it's well worth the ride downtown! What's even greater is that he also offers a great burger as well for those easy going diners. Looking forward myself at returning to rent out their new private dining space they just acquired next door! AMAZING! LOVE THIS PLACE!!! While it could stand to be bigger, there is definitely something to be said about the simplicity of this space. It's all about the food people!

I had the big filet sandwich. It was tasty but fell apart pretty easily. And it came in a basket with fries. For the price and feel of the place I was expecting a little more sophistication from the food. Cash only, and they had to send someone to go get change. at 7:30 on a friday night. surprising.
The Spicy Pork Sausage & Rice Cakes was one of the best things I've ever tasted. Absolutely order it. Wait, no. Actually, you know what? Don't. More for me.

Yakitori is freaking awesome. Â Yakitori Totto is definitely a good place to go. Â It gets busy during dinner time and seating is very limited. Â  The skewers are much tastier than the ones at St. Marks. Â However, the price is much higher and the portions are tiny. Â So, your bill can sky rocket pretty fast. Â Their salmon roe bowl is a must to try for salmon lovers. Â So delicious. Â  Service is ehh... Â Each time I go, I feel hurried by the waitress. Â Understandable since it's a small restaurant and the rent is high but let me eat in peace!

Ahhhhhhhhhhhh (that's the sound of angels singing when you walk in) My other favorite go to restaurant in NYC. I recently went there twice in the span of 5 days on my first visit back to NYC since I moved away. I was so happy I was delirious (and probably obnoxious). So my must haves are.... Sangria - Nobody makes it as good. Period. Roasted Piquillo Peppers - Sea salt and some olive oil. That's it. Simple. Patatas Bravas - Perfectly crispy potatoes with an amazing aioli. I would eat the aioli with a spoon if I could. Fried Chickpeas - Dusted with paprika. Just lovely. Croquetas (ham) - I grew up with a grandmother that made croquetas from scratch. These are better (shame on me) Leche Frita - Recent discovery, shared with a random Italian man at the bar. Light, fluffy, creamy deliciousness, served with drunken cherries (by this point I'm pretty tipsy as well after all the sangria). I'm a chocolate girl but this rates in my top 5 desserts ever. If you live in NYC go here often. Do it for those of us who can't. Please.

Hours after eating the lasagna pizza here we were still saying "wow that was really good pizza" It's a small hole in the wall, grab and go place. Â 3-4 barstools along the wall to sit if you have to. Â Not a dollar slice place, but still very reasonable for a good quality slice with lots of toppings. Â Excellent crust, excellent size of pizza slice. Try the lasagna pizza. Â Will upload photo. Thinking about it makes me want to go back and get another. . . .

I recently discovered this place, it's a quaint little spot hidden on a side street. It was recommended to me by a friend and I decided to stop by on my way to work. The place is small with a table towards the back and a little bar with 4 stools, but the decor and music were lovely. My only complaint is that the service is slow due to the fact that the owner runs the place by herself (which I give her props for). The wait was totally worth it though.. They have a pretty extensive crepe menu, but I decided to play it safe and order something simple, so I ordered the strawberry and nutella crepe and it was the best crepe I've had in my life. And it wasn't expensive at all. Amazing little place, and congrats to the owner, she's doing great!

I've only had the drinks here, but they are fantastic. Both the iced tea and iced coffee are my favorite in the neighborhood. The atmosphere and decor are very nice as well. And I do appreciate when a coffee shop puts your iced coffee in an actual glass and not a plastic cup.

Came here on a weeknight with a good friend. We had no expectations as we were getting our ABC Kitchen cherry popped simultaneously. The decor was very simple, yet modern. My friend and I had seen a number of establishments attempt to present themselves as eco-friendly by using old Ragu bottles as cups and paper towels made with recycled material, so we weren't so impressed...until we read their mission statement, of sorts, on the back of the menu. Everything, from the napkins and silverware to the tables and candles were handmade, recycled and/or refurbished. We were impressed with not only the conscious effort to be eco-friendly with the decor but the food being grown locally, them patronizing small farms, in addition to using non-GMO and cruelty-free animals for their meat. All the aforementioned made this San Francisco native VERY happy! We began with the housemade ricotta and grilled bread. I'm a vegan-tarian, (only eat cheese and some foods that contain dairy) and the ricotta tasted like pure milk, butter and egg whites. My friend enjoyed it a lot and practically ate it all himself lol For my meal, I had roasted brussel sprouts and the mashed potatoes. The sprouts were delish but the mashed potatoes were too creamy. My friend had the char grilled chicken and he absolutely loved it. For dessert, I had the doughnuts and my friend had the salted caramel ice cream. Both were very good and not too sweet, however the doughnut was less flavorful. I'll probably try something else the next time I go. A fantastic establishment to dine with good food, great service and great ambiance. I definitely plan to go again and try new items. Â  4 stars for the noise level and for the horrid pop music blasting on the speakers. Is this a damn club or restaurant? Overall, highly recommended!

Another visit to Crescent Grill and again - so wonderful. We started with the Yellow Fin Tuna Tartare which was delicately Â seasoned with a hint of lemon, surrounded by a delicate filo dough. Under the tuna were pieces of avocado which added a lovely smoothness. The Thai chili sauce had the perfect amount of bite and depth. My husband ordered the Alaskan King Salmon with Black Beluga lentils and smoked tomatoes. The smoky touch was such a great surprise and blended perfectly with the lentils. He said there were some wonderful clear notes to the palate and the salmon was tender and perfectly cooked. I had the lamb shank with hominy and root vegetables. Oh Wow! Lamb fell off the bone, the root vegetables had that touch of sweetness and flavor which comes from fresh vegetables. The hominy grits were creamy and so well seasoned. And atop the lamb was just the right amount of horseradish sauce as a counterpoint the deep flavor of the lamb. Side of charred brussel sprouts with roasted pecans and cranberries: A touch of brightness was added by the cranberries and also in a what I think was a splash of citrus on the brussels themselves. Â  One of the great things about Crescent Grill's chefs, Sean and Milton, is that they know exactly how to get the high and deep notes in a dish just right - the brightness and richness, all without muddying any of the flavors We always begin and end our night with the best bartender of all times; Ryan Chin. What a great person and bartender. He is welcoming and makes great cocktails and he knows his scotches. AND TO ADD TO THE GREATNESS OF CRESCENT GRILL: They now provide free SHUTTLE SERVICE, ferrying local guests to the grill and back home again. I could not believe that we got a free ride home. A FREE RIDE HOME?? Who offers that? On a cold night such as last night, it was a divine end to the evening. We are about 7 long blocks and in the cold that is a long way Â to walk. I am so glad to have this wonderful restaurant in my neighborhood.

I've had some legendary pizza in my day, but Grimaldi's is the measuring stick. It is without a doubt the best I've ever had, hands down. When I daydream about New York pizza, I usually gravitate towards those little hole-in-the-wall joints where fat greasy dudes in stained white tees throw a slice on a paper plate & slide it over a smeared countertop to you. Yeah, that's the authentic NY pizza experience right there. The good thing about these daydreams is that I can be in almost any major metropolitan area & find a joint or two that can pull this off fairly well. Maybe it won't be quite as good, but it's close enough, & close enough is good enough for me. This is why I need to push Grimaldi's out of my heart & throw away the key. Grimaldi's is the one that got away. It's the best there is. There aren't a whole lot of places out there remotely capable of doing it like Grimaldi's (though I've found Gialina in San Francisco to be a pretty nice consolation prize). That's why I cut Grimaldi's out of all our pictures together, & buried all the things it gave me. I'm just trying to save myself the heartache. You understand.
Good Guinness pour - friendly service. Fries were plentiful and slider was average. Good lunch before heading to work... Oh and they have great music - not the typical top 40 crap.

We ate one thing here and one thing only...the Porchetta sandwich ..which was roast pork, a poached egg (though normally not a big fan of poached eggs was amazing), on a sandwiched of amazing bread...portion of each of these is what made it so amazing. The bread baskets are also very good here. The coffee is french pressed and while they offer reg coffee they put the more expensive french pressed coffee on the menu. I don't think I could go back and eat anything else besides this porchetta sandwich...it was just that good.

Verlaine is a great spot to grab a few drinks. Â They have $5 Lychee Martinis which are not only cheap but DELICIOUS. Only qualm is that its TINY and gets filled up pretty fast so be prepared to be secluded to one area.

Been here a few times now for dinner, but this time I tried their brunch. Â My table ordered the huevos rancheros, breakfast sandwich, BLT and chopped salad. Â The plates were well thought out and cohesive, tasted excellent, and generally satisfying. Â  Excellent BMs. Â Sweet, spicy and strong flavor. Â Homemade. One comment is that this place looks great in daylight, and I can't stand how dark it's in there at night. Â Turn the lights up!

came recently, and ate in. i love hole in walls like this place. business is booming at /around lunch time. they have their lunch specials posted behind the counter but seems like most people have been here before. their customers are widely diverse and are not solely hispanic which i like. on average the lunch dish will cost you $10 ish. i tried the chicken with yellow rice and plantains. the chicken was a bit on the dry/tough side but the rice was super tasty - note to self to ask for extra sauce on the rice. cant wait to be back! its one of those places where if you sit by the tables near the entrance, you are going to get knocked just about two dozen times. luckily we sat by the back. find a seat then order!
Loved the Akamaru Modern. Â It had a great silky flavor and satisfied my ramen craving.

Rule: When a new barbeque joint opens a block from your apartment, you go on opening night. Â I follow the rules. Â Except the one to order only as much as you can eat. Â In the case of Might Quinn's, I suggest you break that rule too. This is a simple restaurant for meat munching acolytes Ron Swanson would be proud to call his own. Â Order the brisket, the ribs, the pulled pork and the smoked sausage. Â Now prepare to feast. But you're not done yet. Â Oh no, young padawan. Â There are sides. Â And when I say sides, I point directly to the baked beans. Â What your bemused face tells me is that you think I'm crazy. Â Be that as it may, the baked beans are the stand out of the meal, because they are cooked with all the best bits of the meat. Â The barbeque meal is fully realized as you bite into beans and bits of pulled pork. Â This is not just a side; this is a requirement. For me, I thought a few spicier items needed to be on the menu. Â They gave us a side of hot peppers to appease our neverending spicy thirst, but something tells me that a second barbeque sauce container with an extra kick just might push this place up to 5 stars. All in all, this place will get more and more crowded once it realizes its potential. Â And I will be in line.

I had hope this place was going to live up to its four stars rating by two thousand reviewers... and thank goodness it did =) We walked in at the prime time of dinner with a lobby full of people and we had a feeling it was going to be a long wait...so when the hostess said "It'll be 10 minutes," I had to repeat what she said because I was sure I must have heard her wrong. Sure enough, it wasn't even 10 minutes, we were being led through a dimly lit, modern decor dinning area, with an open kitchen on one side of the wall. We were seated at a long length table, shared with other guests. Even though the restaurant was busy, our waitress promptly presented herself and we were given menus. I ordered the Hirata Buns (as suggested by our waitress for first time guest) and Akamaru Modern. The Hirata Buns tasted like a Chinese Gua Bao, with a bit of kick. It was pretty good. The Akamaru Modern was served with a medium firm ramen, in a flavorful broth. Was it the best ramen I ever had? No. But it wasn't bad either. THREE STARS for the food. What I really like about this place is their excellent service. Our waitress was very attentive. During our meal, she came by multiple times to make sure everything was good. At one point, she came by suggesting that it was best to eat the buns while it was hot (when it gets cold, the bun becomes hard). FOUR STARS for service. Ps. For quicker seating, come either by yourself or in a party of two.

My boyfriend and I came here for our year anniversary. Â The restaurant is elegant yet warm and cozy at the same time. Â For our dinners, we decided to get the 4 course tasting menus. Â For this menu you can order an appetizer, a pasta, a protein and a dessert. Â  I can't remember everything we got because it was about a month ago, but the lobster bisque was delicious and the best I've ever had. Â Both pastas we had were excellent as well. Â For my protein, I got the cod I believe, or some other white fish, and it was very good, but I wasn't as amazed as I was with my earlier courses. The wait staff was really friendly and knowledgeable, and for our dessert course they brought chocolate on our dessert plates that said happy anniversary. Â We had a great experience and a delicious meal, and I would definitely recommend it for a celebration or nicer date.

my roommate and i went here for a post-sandy lunch. we got there shortly after noon and there were a handful of tables seated, but the place was packed with a line out the door about a half hour later. the crab cake appetizer comes with five bite-sized crab cakes which were delicious with the dipping sauce. my roommate liked her meatball kabob order, but i wasn't crazy about my grilled chicken platter. it came with three good sized pieces of chicken breast, but it was a bit overcooked and dry. i'll stick with the dips next time and just carb load on the delicious turkish bread

Restaurant Week Review RW can be so fatal and they did it so well! The space is divided into the bar, large circular tables for groups downstairs, and smaller, more romantic tables in the balcony. I was happy to be sat in the slightly quieter upstairs with my friend B (as far from the freezing outdoors as possible) but would love to go back and hang out at the bar. For RW, we each got two appetizers, an entree, and a dessert. Additionally, their current Lebanon Wine Country special means we were greeted at our table with a tasting of Ixsir wine. The wine was OK (fruity to the nose, but much less flavorful in the mouth) but the gesture was lovely. Our server seemed just as friendly regardless of our RW menu choice and lack of alcoholic beverages. B and I split everything: Mouhamara: a delicious walnut spread Kibbe Naye Beirutieh: beef tartar Moussaka: eggplant deliciousness Chicken Livers: with pomegranate glaze Bass: with peppers & a delicious sauce Lamb Makloubeh: & crispy, yum eggplant ilili Candy Bar (x2): chocolate pudding in bar form with hints of fig & pistachio. The mouhamara and chicken livers really blew my mind. Served with light, poofy bread, everything seemed to get better and better as we ate! I honestly think the main courses were slightly underwhelming compared to how yum the appetizers were, but I'd bet it was the four options to which we were limited. The fish was well cooked, the lamb was good, but it seemed more standard fare. I plan on getting an appetizer (or two) and a drink at the bar sometime in the near future. Our neighboring tables were raving about the cocktails...

Brioche Carameletto: Toffee Glazed perfectly soft brioche dripping with a thick caramel glaze. Sugar overload but that tiny bite was just scrumptious Bomboloni con Crema: Tiny donut holes...airy and smooth with a small filling of light cream. Mouth watering and incredibly light Cacio e Pepe: When someone says "soft scrambled eggs" I never know what they mean. Maialino clearly does. The eggs resemble a cream and are cooked so perfectly. Doused with pecorino and black pepper, a simple breakfast of eggs can give you so much pleasure Frittata Bianca del Giorno: Egg white Frittata. Cooked well and with a heaping mix of mushrooms in it as well as a topping of arugula. Healthy, wholesome and a tasty brunch option Bombolotti all'Amatriciana I ordered the pasta without the bacon. An excellent sauce. The reason they get 4 and not 5 stars is due to the fact that the pasta was quite undercooked. Nevertheless with an true al dente pasta this would have really been excellent. The waitstaff is ridiculously good looking and were actually capable. The restaurant itself has an extremely whimsical and comforting dark wood decor. The sunlight coming through the large windows made it a perfectly cheery brunch spot and the Gramercy Park surroundings makes this an oh-so-chic place. At brunch entrees averaging less than $15, this is also a very very reasonable option. Maialino...I think I may be back soon!

since i've written my first review on difara's, i've had the opportunity to sample some of the other "best pizza in nyc" places. NO ONE comes even close to dom. way to go, buddy xx i've just been reading all these reviews - for all of you complaining about the decor / cleanliness - get over it! Â i've gotten food poisoning from places that LOOKED pristine from the outside. Â but as we difara fans know, the overt can be deceiving. Â and yes, the guy charges a lot for the pizza - but IT'S WORTH IT!!! Â it's not some OUTRAGEOUS price, if you think about it, order a pie and it's very reasonable for what you get. Â and it's still cheap (under $10 per person, especially if you order a pie) - and you get leftovers!!! Â it's still AMAZING the next day - i like to eat it cold, room temp, or reheat it in the oven - the crust stays nice and crunchy! yes, you wait a long time sometimes, but it's a small place, that's your choice, and it goes by very quickly. Â  where else can you just order a regular pie (no toppings!!!) and be in utter bliss??? The cheesemonger plate was okay. They only provided six small pieces of bread for two decently sized spreadable cheeses, and then charged for extra bread (without mentioning it would cost more). Â The meatballs were very good. Unfortunately, the service was slow and it was so loud inside that my friend and I could barely hear each other. I'm not in a rush to go back and wouldn't recommend this place to my friends.

There is no question that the food here is spectacular. The ingredients are quality, the chef showmanship impeccable, and their wine list is just right. But really Lupa? I arrived with 4 friends at 10:30 at night for a party of 5. We were made to wait for 20 minutes standing next to the table where we subsequently sat once our final guest arrived. Clearly 4 of us were there - we were going to eat there. All you had to do was pull up a 5th chair to the end of an already set 4 top. Come on guys - be as awesome with client-service as your food is. So silly. It takes away from an otherwise perfect experience.

Great neighborhood brunch spot away from the crowds on St. Marks. It's a large place so don't worry if you have to wait - the line moves quickly. The only thing I get here is the steak and eggs because it's perfect. The meat is always cooked exactly the way I request it (medium rare) and the sauce is divine. I can't bring myself to deviate from this lovely staple dish but I'm sure there are plenty of other delicious things on the menu. Outdoor seating available in the warmer months and it's cozy in the winter season.

This place is like food heaven! Everywhere you turn it's more and more goodies. Everything is fresh and made in house. They have multiple restaurants within the supermarket. You have to try the pizza and pasta one. The deserts are to die for.... Seeing Dr.Drew there was funny as well. I thought he was going to have an intervention with the mozzarella sandwich.

Spectacular food, great service, and an amazing open service area. I like the prix fixe menu. The food was just amazing, spiced perfectly and presented beautifully. While the main courses are small, I certainly did not leave hungry. The wine was excellent and I am pining to go back already!
I went last night with a friend who has sadly never had plantains! She loved them. I love it Â here every time more and more!

Best. Coffee. Ever. I don't know why everyone is commenting on the food in this place (which I haven't had) and not the amazingly delicious and hearty lattes they serve in the morning. When I was filming a movie over there I would go and get a latte before shooting. Great way to start the day! The service could be better, though. But that's what you get with Brooklyn Hipsters. I can't wait to try the food some day!

We went for happy hour and shared the swordfish ceviche on plantain crackers and 1/2 chicken. Â Both dishes were delicious and almost too much for two. The service was so friendly and attentive, the bar tender answering our many questions cheerfully. Â We're going to go back for a late night band session and cocktails now!

I honestly think this is one of the better brunch places the west village has to offer. Â A great menu, solid drinks and great waitstaff. Â This place can get pretty noisy when it is packed but they do a great job with service and the food is great. Â A great stop for a morning walk from Washington Square down to SoHo.

The food is good for the price. However, the servers are terrible and rude. Their expressions are always frowns and no smiles the whole time I was there as if they don't want to work there or they just see customers as another $8 / per head revenue count.
