Great take-out spot! Â The falafel is really good and I love all the vegetarian sides. Â  They only have a few stools in there so it's more of a take out place. Â They are also on seamless now and stay open later. Â  The food really is fantastic. Â  My only complaint is the way you order. Â  I feel like this could be streamlined instead of only allowing for 2 sides and then charging for another side. Â  I wish they had a salad option where you could add several toppings instead of just getting 1 or 2 vegetable sides. Â  I think i'd probably order from here more if I could order additional sides with smaller portions that weren't as pricey. Â  The lentil soup is also very good.

Totally dive and we loved it. Â  When at a new restaurant we always ask "what are you known for?" Â we order the 3 items the waitress suggested -- fish taco, cuban sandwich and the corn. Â My husband and I split everything. Â More than enough food. Â Best sandwich we have ever had. Â  Downside -- small and cramped. Â we ended up with a seat near the bathroom and my husband had to move his chair ever time someone needed to use the restroom. Â  Other than that --- fantastic NYC spot.

I'd give it 3 1/2 stars if i could. Being from Texas, I would not call their food tex-mex. While they do have quesadillas and a few types of tacos,most of the menu is fried/breaded/bbq so it airs more on the side of southern comfort food. My friends and i dined here last friday. We arrived at 7:30 and place was packed Â (probably due to earlier happy hour) so we did not get seated until almost 8pm. note: it would be worth calling ahead to see if they do reservations. this place is super casual- carnival stuff on the walls, cheesy photo booth so i'm not sure if they actually take reservations. When we stepped in, noise level, way loud. Â The restaurant/bar is not huge, but there were 2-3 happy hour groups that shall remain nameless, that were practically screaming and yelling to each other (blame the alcohol) so that was a little annoying. We figured since happy hour was over, they would leave soon, but they ended up hanging out there for awhile....it was friday so i'll give them a break, Maybe it's calmer on a tuesday night? Waiter: not exactly Mr. friendly. Â He was very straight and to the point when he asked for drink orders. then he ran off and it took about 10 mins to find him again when we wanted to order food. I was almost tempted to grab some other waiter and have them take our order. Then he appeared ( i think he had to go to the kitchen/bar to make a dessert item for somebody) They seemed a bit short staffed. We ordered 1 appetizer(chips and queso) and our entrees. Â Usually in most places, the appetizer comes out 15-20 mins before the entrees, but not in this case. We had our app, and then low and behold, 2 minutes later our meals came out, needless to say, the queso was barely touched. My friends ordered pulled pork sandwich and the fish reuben (which they both loved) One of my friends is also a former Texan...so he is very picky with his BBQ. The sandwich must have been good. I ordered the creole spiced crabcake sandwich. Flavor was good ( a little kick) but crabcake was too wet, soggy. my bun came apart. Â the onion rings i ordered with it were awesome. hot and crispy! Maybe it was the hot weather or the soggy crab cake, but i only ate about 1/2 my sandwich. So when Mr. waiter came around later to gather our dishes, he asked how everything was that evening? Â My friends in unison said they loved their food. I was like meh, mine was ok. He asked why and I told him it was a bit soggy. He told us he'd remedy that. Â He's like, how about a comp dessert? Â Usually I'd jump at free dessert, but then again with the heat...not feeling hungry, So I politely said no. He also asked us about the queso, saying," Why didn't you guys eat that?" Now, one of my friends spoke up saying it was brought out just before the food. Â I think he got that hint. He played it off saying, "the guys in the kitchen are pretty fast." He comes by later with the bill and announces that he comped my dinner off-a nice gesture indeed. Later he then brings out a surprise slice of key lime pie with homemade whipped cream (Also on the house. ) Yum! Â Once again, I totally didn't demand the free dessert but I got it anyways. Â I shared with one of my friends and it was terrific. We left him a good tip :) Pros: -decent service (nice that they tried to keep us happy) -most of Â the food is very fresh/good ingredients (i'd say we were happy with about 3/4 of our stuff) -drinks were good, but a little pricey during non happy hour times -crazy decor Cons: -loud drunk people -long wait to get in -funky location, there is not much around front street, just lots of construction...
Hard to say how long its been since we had been back.. Â Salad was great pizza was very nice. Â As good as I remember..

The home-made noodles are amazing! Â I've been several times and taken out-of-towners and have had great food every time. Â My favorite is the udon, and there are plenty of vegetarian options as well. The atmosphere is modern and neat, yet cozy. Â The staff is nice and the service was good as well. Â I'd definitely recommend!

Came here for my birthday with the bf. Â He picked it. Â Venue was really nice. Â I walked in and was greeted by a friendly entourage of people. Â Bf was already seated and waiting for me. Â We perused the menu. Â I was thinking about the tasting menu but we went with the prix fixe. Â The meal, the service and the whole dining experience started out fantastic but then, as the night went on, everything just went on a steady decline. Â Food, service, everything. Our waiter pretty much disappeared right before the main course. Â Entrees were ok, but nothing special. Â They forgot to put a candle on the cake (though bf had requested it). Â Dessert wasn't anything special. Â  And as we walked out, all the people who had enthusiastically greeted us in just ignored us. Â Weird. Too bad. Â It could have been a really great dining experience I think. Â Not sure what happened...?

Amazingly unique place, drinks and staff. It's a small, intimate cafe. They have a creative variety of health drinks, teas, smoothies, baked goods and healthy food. Cozy neighborhood cafe. A few feet south is the Prohibition Bakery with creative mini cupcakes. Must visit again and again.

Seriously? I don't know what they put in their white sauce, but it's gotta be some combination of magical wonders and creamy white goodness. I get cravings for these insane platters. My standard chicken-lamb-yellow basmati rice-lettuce-flatbread topped with multiple containers of white sauce and verrrrrrryyyyyy few drops of the hot sauce. DONE. It does the job, even if you feel disgustingly full afterwards. Each platter is typically enough for 2 people, but the scent of this cart's food from a few streets away will get you ravenous for the whole thing. Forget about just ending the night here... My friend and I drive from Jersey to eat this. And no it's not hype. I told a friend here from Europe that he had to try it. "It's from a street cart??! You're really recommending a street cart?" Yes. Yes I am.

Let me tell you why this place get's five stars. They see an issue, and work quickly to address it. I listed a couple of major issues I had with this establishment in my previous comment. 1.) Issue with my reservation not being handled correctly; 2.) Â waitress squabble at our table in front of my important out-of-town guests; 3.) music is too loud and rancorous. Â I decided to give this establishment another try with an important guest ( a picky food critic-of-sorts). My prior experience must've been a one-off, because there seemed to be something new in the air at this restaurant today. Here's how Hillstone redeemed itself, and now surpasses most of these other haughty overpriced NYC establishments: 1.) I made my reservation over the phone, and also received a confirmation call 24 hours before the scheduled date from a courteous, and professional staff member who assured me that even if we were early and if there was a table available they would seat me and my guest right away (which is indeed what happened). 2.) Once in the restaurant, we got something of a red-carpet-VIP treatment from everyone including the bar tender and the front-of-store staff. All smiles and professional treatment and my guest (and I of course) was very impressed. We were indeed seated 15 minutes sooner than our scheduled time, and had our coats checked and were attended by two very attentive, helpful, and friendly wait staff. All the wait staff worked in harmony to assist dinner guests, and my guest was impressed with the professionalism in how the wait staff communicated with each other. We took the dinner and dessert recommendations from the waiter, and were very glad we did. (I had the fish special, which was the Sole. My guest had the Pork Ribs). The price is commensurate with the volume and quality of food served, so come hungry! 3.) The music and noise level was just right so that I was not yelling across the table at my dinner guest or the waiters. Â  All in all, our dining experience at Hillstone on E53rd St exceeded our expectation, and we left, full, happy, and with plans to come back on a regular basis. Towards the end of our meal, our dessert was delivered to us by the store's General Manager, Joel Halperin, who was very warm and thanked us for our visit and made sure that we were happy and well taken care of. It is not every day that you receive such professional and warm reception from the Manager at such a busy, popular restaurant. But, this is the place to expect a higher standard of service, professionalism (can I say that word enough times?), and memorable (and addicting) dining experience. Bring your important guests to this establishment, and you will not be disappointed. Recommendations: Try the Grilled Artichokes as an Appetizer. Pork Ribs, Hawaiian Rib Eye, or the Thai Steak Salad as Entree options. Apple Cobbler or the Brownie is a must for Dessert.

Conveniently located a block away from many of the broadway shows, it's the perfect place to stop by for a snack. I got a slice of the strawberry cheesecake which was excellent. The strawberries were flavorful without being too sweet and the cheesecake was velvety and delicious. Definitely worth a stop if you're in the area and craving some dessert.

I'd like to dedicate the following review to my 5 FANS!! I love you all!! Have you ever watched a cartoon and thought to yourself "Why does cartoon food look so much better than real food?"? Â Well, this is something I think about daily. Â I have been on a quest to find that perfect cartoon piece of pizza; you know the one. Â Smoke radiating from the top in swirling clouds, thick yellow cheese dripping over the edge...the kind that makes your eyes jump off your face! Â The closest I have ever come to tasting such perfection is Di Fara's Pizza. Dom, the Pizza Artist only uses the best, freshest ingredients; word on the street is that they are flown in from Italy. Â He treats each pie like a piece of fine art, taking his time to perfect every minute detail. Â It really is quite a show. Â This pizza would make any Ninja Turtle salivate.

Not that this place needs another positive review...but I had such a great time I just had to share!! I knew there would be a little bit of Â a wait so I made sure to arrive before my scheduled meeting time with my friend. Â To my surprise the wait time was only 15 minutes!! Not bad at all! Â We were seated as soon as my friend arrived. I enjoyed a delicious bloody mary which I was surprised I ordered. Â They are not usually my favorite drink as I think I have been scarred for life with an exceptionally foul example only a year ago. Â Cafe Orlin's BM was amaaaazing. Â They are back on my list! My friend enjoyed a HUGE plate of pumpkin pancakes with cinnamon yogurt. Â If it weren't for my Wheat Allergy I would have reached across the table and taken one off her plate!! Â The side salad and potatoes were also a nice touch to the meal. Everything tasted incredibly fresh, and was a nice inexpensive non greasy breakfast. Â Neither one of us could finish our meals and we left stuffed! Â Highly enjoyable...will most certainly be back for more!

I went here today for the first time prior to a tattoo consultation. Â I got a seating super quick, waitress was quick to take my order and food came quick. Â Decor is awesome as hell too. Food was great for the price. Â Taste was great and it was a decent portion. Â I walked out full and happy. Â I would definitely go back again.

I LOVE Penelope, I just wish the line wasn't so long all of the time. Â The staff is nice, the atmosphere is cute Â and the prices are extremely reasonable ($15 prix-fixe brunch and it includes a very yummy Apple Cider Mimosa). My favorite has to be Salmon Wrapped Poached Eggs. Â The whole combination is absolutely delicious. Â I also like the Nutella French Toast. Â For dinner, I love the Spinach and Beets salad. Â I would go a little lighter on the croutons... but other than that - it's really good. As I said, the line can be pretty crazy, usually about 45 minutes to an hour. Â But, if people are willing to wait the long, there must be a reason, right?

The food is absolutely fantastic and they have a good variety of brunch menu drinks. Â  The portions were decent sized and the food was not overpriced as is common with French restaurants. Yum! I recommend getting any of the eggs Benedict for brunch. Perfect flavors. I will definitely go back to try the brunch menu.

I get it. The meat in these burritos are fantastic, but what about everything else? The rice is usually undercooked, the (black) beans seem to be decorative, and other essential burrito elements are overlooked. Do you need chili in your burrito? No. Do you need roasted squash in your burrito? No. These additional "different" fillings over-power what in my mind an amazing burrito should be - simple with every element equally as important. The only importance is placed on the flavors of the meat, and the sides (but seriously why chili? that just makes a soggy burrito to-go!). The service? Eh, the workers are nice yet not that great at listening (probably because they're too busy singing along to the songs on the radio). It's interesting to note that these burrito makers are "young" "fun" and "unique" that I almost forget how bland the Flatiron district is. Don't get me wrong, the place is pretty okay and way better than Chipotle, but if you want an amazing burrito that thinks about all elements of a burrito then go to Great Burrito or Dos Toros. (Sorry FiveThirtyEight/Nate Silver...you got this wrong).

This place has won me over. Another newly opened Indian restaurant in Curry Hill. Yet instead of being another nondescript place where all of the menu lumps together, Pippali really stands out. Starting with the atmosphere...the restaurant is cozy and well decorated, there was a birthday party in the center and many people on dates in the small tables on the sides...4.5/5 Service: awful, the only reason I didn't give it 5 stars. They took forever with our food granted it was 8pm on a weekday and the place was at 80%. We had ordered some Roti and Dal as appetizers and they literally spent that out along with the rest of our entree. The tables become really cluttered with all these bowls of food. And we had to ask twice for the check at the end of the meal...2/5 Food: AMAZE-BALLS. I had the Lagan de Murgh, I was literally scraping the sauce off the plate because it was so good. The boy had the Chicken Murgh that was pretty solid as well. The Bihari dal was probably the best dal I have had in my life, so creamy and delicious. 5/5 Hopefully they work out their service issues because I will definitely be coming back. Note, the food is slightly on the pricier side but I rather pay a few dollars more where I will actually remember what kind of curry and meat combination I actually ate.

I was led here by friend to try their NYC style pizza. Apparently it is an NYC institution that heavily relies on tourists more so than the local clientele. It was a enjoyable experience, but I didn't feel this was the best NYC pizza I've ever had. It was decent, but not the best. What is nice about the pizza is the size of the pies. They're definitely not small! If you get their meatball appetizer, that is enough for a meal in itself. You wouldn't want that for a meal though.... Buyer beware -- this place only takes CASH! There is an ATM onsite if you forget beside the bathrooms.

Gastropub with excellent food and libations! We had the following: Side of Kale - #1 dish I think Duck Confit Pasta #2 dish I love the pork grinds so good! Quinoa Salad Short Rib and Bone Marrow Toast on Country Bread with Bordelaise Sauce. Cast-Iron Chocolate Chip Cookie w/a Growler of Milk - #3 must order item! We also had two bottles of wine that were great! All the wine bottle is $35 so great prices on the wines.

Disappointing. Â Started out well, good cocktail and chicken liver moose to start. Â Went done hill when they came out with our mains when we were still eating out starters! Â Whipped my plate away and I still was eating!! Â My cod on a bed of lentils and greens ( about a teaspoon of lentils). Was very very bland. Â Felt very rushed, sat down at 8.30 and was out of there before 9.30, not what I consider to be a good Saturday night out :-/

My last visit here reinforced Lombardi's place as my favorite pizza spot. Â Topping off the experience is that I took my kids here too and they were blown away. Â Now, alas, they are spoiled. Got two large pizzas, a Citterio Pancetta and Coal oven roasted red peppers and a Sweet Italian sausage and Red Onions. At first, I thought there may be leftovers, but we ended up splitting the last slice. Â I also had a Six Point Sweet Action cream ale, which was OK, but I wasn't there for the beer. Go!!!!

Why do I adore Vesta? For all the right reasons: the warm & friendly service; spectacular food; creative and eclectic menu options; wine list; charming and comfortable interior; and, finally, the ever-changing art on the walls (I especially enjoyed the homage to The Golden Girls a couple of months back); but the real reason I can no longer even think about going to another Italian restaurant is the food! My most recent meal there began with the citrus salad, shaved fennel & toasted pistachios, which I loved so much I've been recreating it at home (to the best of my ability) almost daily ever since. It was an inspiration. The slow braised meatballs in parmigiana cheese & tomato is heaven and everything you would want from such a dish but better. My main course was the braised free bird chicken leg, Russian kale & smashed cannellini beans and it was scrumptious. Â  Mmmm, I can't wait until I go back.
Pizza was pretty good. Â Expected more. Â Overrated.

buttermilk channel I cannot express how deeply felt my love is for you and your beautiful Fried Chicken and Waffles. I want to eat them all day everyday for the rest of my life. Â Thank you, thank you.

Found this little spot right near the Barclays Center for a dinner before attending boxing. Â The service and food were excellent! Â The rose wine on tap was outstanding, and prefect for a warm summer evening. Â The burrata appetizer was so good, my husband and I fought for the last bite. Â My husband had the orecchiette entree and I had the lasagna. Â Perfectly sized potions, and the lasagna was not overly heavy like many places make it. Â The tiramisu was fabulous - light and flavorful, and perfct with the espresso. Â Our server even brought us lemonciello with our check. Â And the best part that with multiple courses and win it was extremely reasonably priced. We live in DC, but next time we come back for an event at the Barclays Center we will plan to eat here again.

This was the place where I tried Chicken and Waffles for the very first time, and what do i think? Really good, like no joke. The waffles were like ACTUAL waffles, not like the ones you get from the frozen food section at some store, and the chicken haha omg, white and juicy, not bad at all...of course this did not kill my hunger, but still, it got some of the job done! :D Next time I head to NYC, im deffinitely coming here again :D
Great place for a dinner, especially if you need a pre or post Webster hall/movie dinner...

I read Anella tried to have someone's review taken down? Â We came here as a party of 8 one night and the hostess told us we'd have to pay a flat fee per person to eat. Â  Huh? Â The place was empty, so we just broke up into two tables and had a kind of miserable dinner experience to avoid being gouged.

what do you do after imbibing a few cocktails at east village?! you head to Mark for their delicious sliders and french fries! oh and possibily milk shakes depening on how hungry you are. Â And let me tell you, I don't feel the slightest guilt Â putting those sliders and french fries (of cos w/o cheese on both) in my belly, blame it on alcohol, but also cos they're so delicious, the sliders are juicy and flavorful! Â I love sitting by the bar and watch how it's being prepared. it's a small place, service and staffs are friendly and attentive.

I had high expectations with all these great yelp reviews but honestly I thought this place was just average. Sure the quality of the fish seemed fresh but the place is bland and the service was pretty bad. Our waitress forget to give us our salads and when we asked about them she claimed she already brought it. I think I would remember if I already ate a salad and I certainty did not. Then she seemed annoyed at us for asking her to please bring them because we certainty did not get them. I got a selection of 12 sushi pieces and a few of them were pretty good but the rest were just ok. And my dining companion got the salmon and mackerel entree but they only had the salmon left and it was very unimpressive. With so many great sushi restaurants in NYC I will probably try one of the other ones next time.

Not going to lie - this is pretty much as expensive as it gets BUT IT'S TOTALLY WORTH IT. Went with the prix fixe menu and every dish was ridiculously good. Â I kept thinking, "this is amazing! this is amazing! this is amazing!" Â (think aziz ansari) sea urchin, scallops and langoustine, porcini flan, farm egg with serrano ham - these were all so good, I could have eaten entire meals with just each of these dishes. Â  don't forget the bread car that roams around, but do remember that there are six courses - I got full pretty fast.

Best.. Damn. Brunch. In. The. City. Â Period. Â  And I'm not just saying that because I live around the corner. Â I would come here for brunch if I lived in Philly, it's that good. My 2 faves: Sam I Am and the Veggie Burger. Â Those fries are to die for. Mmmm Penelope makes me wish every day was Sunday.

yes, the pancakes were worth the hype. Â the syrup could be a taaad less sweet, but i guess that's what makes the pancakes what they are. probably common sense, but if you go during off hours/days, like during the weekdays, it's not as crowded as the weekends.

My favorite soondubu jip! This was my first time at the new location and it's a lot bigger than the old space (two stories, for one thing). I usually get the assorted soondubu (beef, shrimp, clam) and it's SO freakin' good. Their service is really efficient as well.
MoMo - My initials x2, best Sushi I've had in BK, in my hood, right in the wheelhouse. Great place.

This Place Is AMAZING ! Live band , Great food and even better drinks !! Came here on a Wednesday .. The wait was only 10 mins but they welcomed myself and my guy to the bar & Â then we were seated by the best waitress ever (KAYLA) she was super bubbly.. Energetic and very attentive Â  I Totally Recommend this place !!!

When should you avoid coming to brunch here? When there is a huge parade in tow. We made the mistake of booking brunch during a major celebratory event and many streets were shut down. When we finally stumbled in, soaked in sweat and hair matted from the humidity, we were starving and thirst. We looked like hikers lost in the desert. That being said, our friends were forgiving and the french toast is delicious! Three pieces of crispy toast, each piece larger than the size of my hand. And the crispiness lasted through our hour long brunch! The shrimp cobb salad was satiating and I wanted more! (But they say hunger is the best spice). The bacon was perfectly fried, asparagus was fresh and avocado was plentiful. The large salad was filling, even for this bottomless pit of a eater. I might be back but definitely not on a parade day.

Maybe my expectations were too high when I first went to this restaurant, but I was a bit disappointed with the service. The food is very good, but a bit pricey for the amount. The place is soooooooo small (you feel that you are cramped in a small elevator, but not a room) and the decor is too cheap for the prices they charge and the level of service they provide. The wine list is not adequate too. Besides, we ordered a wine form the list and they didn't want to open the bottle just for 2 glasses, though it was priced as per glass. Maybe I will come back once more just for the food experience.
if every restaurant can learn from this restaurant, dining out would be pure heaven.

Fast, no-nonsense flavorful pizza. Maximum capacity of this place is around 8 people, and is run by a Spanish-speaking staff with novellas playing on the TV. Veggie slice had a lot going on, although $5 for one slice is pretty crazy IMHO. A little hesitant about the big green B inspection rating, but it could be something minor I guess.

I went ruby for Friday lunch. I was very happy with food and service. I had pumpkin salad with goat cheese and a panini. My friends had spicy pasta, stake sandwich. All of them are good. We also shared chocolate bread pudding. Two thumbs up! It is a small place with 4-5 tables. not for big group, but good for smaller than 4 people. Lovely service. I don't hesitate to give big 4 stars - but they take ONLY CASH!! If they take cash, i will give 5. =)

You either love this place or you're wrong. Yeah everyone says the sandys are small but come on people! You're willing to wait on line @ Smorgasberg for mini mini sliders made of puffin meat that was massaged by a blind monk or sum dumb thing!! What I do Is usually get 2 or 3 sandwiches to make a super sandwich and wash it all down with some of their corn which is mondo dope.

Excuse the bullet points. - Came here on two separate occasions: graduation celebration lunch with my sister and a random dinner. Seated in the bar/dining area the first time, and seated in the back dining room the second. I actually prefer the first one, especially if you're just coming over after a day in the city and are dressed casually. - The food is very well portioned and the sauce to pasta ratio has been consistently good in my opinion. The portions are right, which I think is essential with pasta. It is so easy to have too much pasta. - I've had the house spaghetti on both occasions and while it's heavy with the basil, I think it is worth the attention. The sauce really is what makes it special. I wish the noodles themselves were closer to al dente, but they've been close to what I would consider 'bloated' on both occasions. Perhaps they don't take in the sauce as well if they're al dente? - The bread basket. I've only had one bread basket that trumped Scarpetta's and that restaurant is closed (Upstairs at Bouley). They give you three different dips/toppings, including the essential olive oil. It's tempting to just gorge on the bread basket, but please don't.. - Scarpetta offers half bottles of wine, served in small glass decanters, which was a nice aesthetic addition to the table. I appreciated having the half-bottle option, for when one glass doesn't feel like enough but you're purposefully out to get tipsy/drunk. - The service was great both times. Patient, easy-going, and very helpful if we had questions. Not pushy, which is a huge plus in my book.

I think it has been a while since I've been able to give a 5-star rating so willingly and happily. Sushi Yasuda takes the cake for the best, simple, pure sushi experience in New York City. It gets compared to Sushi of Gari often, though I'm not sure why, because the two have taken completely different approaches to this delicate cuisine. Sushi Yasuda's Omakase will knock your pants off with each bite. The freshness of the ingredients comes from the highest grade by the suppliers, and the chefs are very knowledgeable about what will taste good to you once you describe to them your preferences. I've never been a fan of uni, but damn the uni here is something I'll never forget. Every bite the chef puts in front of you is an adventure, not because they play with different flavors but because they have mastered how to accentuate the natural flavors of the ingredients. It comes across beautifully, and whether it's for a date or with family and friends, you'll have a fine time tasting good food and having good conversation. It's a must-try place in New York, and by far my favorite Japanese joint.

I loved my experience at the Burrito Box! Funny enough, I had been craving some good greasy Mexican food for a bit and this place certainly satisfied it! While I did order a Quesadia (not a burriito) I loved every bite. Â The steak was a bit gamey, but for $9 I wasn't too upset. Â I was super cheesey too and I liked the salsa and quac that came on the side for dipping. The guac here is REALLY good. Â Usually I find quac to be too salty and over processed. Â This stuff was super fresh and restored my faith in that guac really does exist without buckets of salt. Also, the seating here is super limited. Â When my friends and I walked in, the tables were all full. Â Thankfully some people finished up and we were able to sit down.

The food is still 5 stars, but I have knock them down a star because the wait is becoming absurd. The Â Top Tomato next door is OOB, so I strongly urge Taverna to rent out at least part of that space.

This place is a hidden gem!! I was visiting family in New York and my cousin and I were eager to take part in their boozy brunch. Bottomless Mimosas? Yes, Please! The decor and ambiance was wonderful. We sat at the bar and were served by Jonathan. HE WAS FANTASTIC!! The drinks were amazing and he recommended "the forager" - absolutely divine! My cousin isn't too fond of mushrooms and even she was raving about it!! Â We also ordered the french toast, the scotch egg, and rosemary potatoes. Dishes are tapas style, which is a fantastic way to try a variety of delicious menu items. Â  I do have to say that the hostess, Raquel, was very unpleasant (thus, 4 out of 5 stars). For her to be the first impression of the restaurant is horrible. We almost left. Maybe it's the Souther Hospitality in me that has the expectation of a hostess is supposed to be courteous and inviting, because Raquel was not! We were already in the area but decided to call ahead, she stated there was not a need to reserve a table and to come on in. Once we got there, she stated the next available reservation would be at 3pm. I am just glad we didn't allow her to ruin our experience because the rest of our brunch was extremely enjoyable. All in all, I loved our brunch thanks to Jonathan the amazing bartender and I highly recommend this restaurant to New Yorkers and tourists alike. Just don't pay Raquel any mind. :)
Kids liked the pancakes i had egg whites....dont come for breakfast...2 orders pancakes eggwhites and a pc.of cheese cake....61 bucks? Â No thanks...

NUTELLA PANCAKES OR WAFFLES. AMAZEBALLS. Sorry for capslock but it was earned. It doesn't really matter how early you come on the weekend, there will be a wait. They initially told me 30 minute wait for 2 when I arrived but I was seated within 5 minutes, so don't sweat it. For those looking to do boozy brunch, alcohol isn't served until 12 on Sunday but they let you order it for the $16 prix fix and bring it over promptly at noon. I had the bistro burger along with the nutella waffles and it was the perfect combination. Did I say amazeballs yet? Highly recommend this spot for brunch or even a regular meal.

Love this place. Cute dining restaurant with asian looking seatings. Crowded on Friday nights and probably weekends so I'd say it's better to get here a little earlier. Also, if you come with a group of 4+, the wait is probably going to take you longer. Their crabmeat xiao long bao was DELICIOUSSSS. Huge, JUICY, totally yummalicious and i would prefer it over Joe's (long lines there and so touristy anyway, so why bother?) Good Shang Hai crusine with both cold and hot dishes! My friends and I ordered xiao long bao (so good!), vegetarian duck (nothing special, not recommended, the outter layer aka tofu skin? was a little too dry and hard), drunken chicken (hmmm!), si chuan spicy dumplings (they were tiny compared to the picture they showed on the menu, it was alright...) and dou miao vegetables (yummy!) The total came out to be around $30 for three people, good deal for good quality Shang hai-nese food! Service was good, the place is a little small but cozy and tend to be less touristy (a plus!) Will come again (not bothered with Joe's), good food, everything on the menu looks authentic, great prices. yummy xiao long bao = Winning!

I have given it several tries. I am not going back. Average wait for food from seating until arrival is 2 hours. (I'm not even talking about the wait for a table here.) One time my food never arrived. It is a pity that such a good idea, in such a gorgeous location, is so poorly executed.

I ordered the chicken kebab plate with salad and whole wheat pita. First, the food was delivered over an hour later. When trying to call the restaurant, noone answered. Second, the delivery man didn't follow the explicit directions I gave online -- to not ring the doorbell but to call my cell. Third, the salad was super soggy and they gave me plain white pita instead of the whole wheat I ordered. The food wasn't bad, but it wasn't great. Just not sure if I'll be ordering from here in the near future.

If you're ever in East Village, this is an awesome place to swing by. I'm a big potato nut, so if you're the same as me, try out the generously-portioned fries at Pommes Frites with a friend. The highlight of this place is the plethora of sauces that you can pick from the menu. You're welcome to try out a flavor since they have so many to choose from. My favorite is the sweet mango chutney, but my friend and I also had the honey mustard and the pomegranate teriyaki. Honey mustard tastes like what it sounds like. The pomegranate teriyaki was interesting, as you can definitely taste the teriyaki part. Not sure if I would choose it a second time, however. I wish they had something like this in the bay area, but I suppose it's good for my gut that they don't. :P

If you don't like cheese or bread or beer, don't eat here. Otherwise, it'd kinda heavenly. Ask for the spicy ketchup-y sauce for dipping your grilled cheese. You'll thank me. Great date or group hang out place, it can accommodate everyone's needs. Cash for now. There's an eggy grilled cheese so give it a try for brunch.
Loved their brunch! I recommend going with a group of friends and sharing your dishes to make your way through more of the menu or you will be sure to have food envy of the surrounding tables.

It seems like the general consensus is to get a front row seat at the counter, which is true if you're primarily interested in the "experience" of loud shouting and food getting handed to you on paddles. BUT. If you're even remotely interested in the food, avoid Robataya altogether. I went in with the intention of tasting a variety of dishes. A run down of each dish: 1. Okra - I was expecting to get more than five okra for $5. But never mind the price, the dish came out room temperature. I thought this was coming off the grill?! 2. Shishitou peppers - I suppose compared to the okra, seven shishito peppers for $6 is more bang for your buck. Now if only they could bring this out hot, too. You'd think it's easier since peppers retain heat pretty well. That, unfortunately, is not the case. Secondly, there was nowhere near enough soy sauce. I couldn't even distribute the soy sauce evenly because there was not enough to touch every pepper. 3. Uni Konbu Yaki - Possibly the worst dish we ordered. Grilled sea urchin with salted konbu seaweed. Holy moly...the sea urchin was NOT fresh and overcooked! Dry, pasty, clumpy, and the aftertaste was similar to what I'd imagine a dirty aquarium filter to taste like. The good news? This dish came out piping hot. Bad news? Prying overcooked, dry, clumpy uni out a shell was akin to sticking my hand into a bucket of hot coals and licking it afterward - not enjoyable and not tasty. 4. Tsukune with salt - Came out hot and slightly over salted, but compared to the previous dishes, this was delicious. It was also cooked perfectly. 5. Shrimp (Special of the day) - If the uni was the worst dish, then the shrimp was the biggest disappointment. I was excited to see that the shrimp was a decent size but was sorely disappointed when I bit in to find grossly over cooked shrimp. Rubbery and stuck to the shell. WHY WHY WHY? 6. Yakionigiri with soy sauce - Nicely grilled. Rice was probably cooked with too much water though; it was a mushy mess inside. Evenly flavored. 7. Kamameshi (Salmon and salmon roe recommendation by waiter) - Wow. I think there was a reader who suggested ordering kamameshi to fill yourself up on rice. That makes me feel like I have a black hole for a stomach. This did NOT fill me up. But at this point, I wasn't expecting to leave Robataya with a full stomach. Not unless I intended on spending $200. Back to the kamameshi. The rice here was NOT overcooked. It was cooked very nicely actually, which came at the expense of the salmon, which turned out overcooked, dry, and tasteless. If the salmon were properly cooked, this dish would have been umami heaven. 8. Zouni - Forgettable. A small bowl, but I didn't even bother to finish. The dashi broth was bland, but the chicken was not dry. The mochi was standard. Wasn't scalding hot because then I would have remembered it. 9. Miso soup with nagaimo and eggplant - Slightly disappointed that the nagaimo and eggplant did not add anything to the soup. Not expecting much at this point. Also, this came at the end of our meal. Huh? To be honest, I had already started looking forward to dessert, which was a big mistake because.... 10. Houjicha pudding - Is this a knock off of Kyoya's houjicha ice cream? Um, it tasted like a big ball of "sweet" and "milky." If you're looking for a strong houjicha flavor, do not bother with this dish. Knowing it was a newly opened restaurant, I wasn't expecting experienced waitstaff, so I don't feel that it's fair to comment on their service. It's unfortunate that the food was also a big let down. It was "pretty good" at best and "I wish I could turn off my taste buds" at worst. Also, robatayaki can be a fun and lively experience, but recommending Robataya for that sole reason would be like recommending Benihana for teppanyaki.

I thought I had it good living less than a block away from Blue Smoke, but forget about it - the meat they do at Might Quinn's is mighty indeed. The menu here is much smaller, and you go about ordering food in a similar fashion as you would at a Chipotle - grab your main course, any sides, and maybe a glass of beer to top it off. There's not a huge selection, but they don't need it...at least judging from the taste of what we had. It's a strong statement when the pulled pork is the weakest dish that's served up (I found mine to be tasty, but not as succulent or flavored as others I've had at the annual BBQ cookout in Madison Square Park, or, being local, Dinosaur BBQ). That said, the brisket and the ribs are phenomenally off-the-charts delicious. I don't think I've had brisket that is better-done than it is here - the slices of brisket just fall apart as soon as you slice into them, and there's the right mix of smoky goodness and fatty succulence that is a pure bite of heaven when you start digging in. The ribs might be even better, though - mainly because of that crispy, charred, spicy and smoky rub that's on top of each rib. I don't think I've ever had such a fierce seasoning on top of any ribs I've sampled. Paired with very light sides (you can choose from an assortment of picked vegetables, as well as regular mayo-based slaw or a lighter vinegar-based version), it makes for a very sumptuous meal that will undoubtedly leave you feeling fat and happy. The beer selection is also really reasonable here - lots of good crafts on tap and in bottles, all for a pretty reasonable price of $6-7. It's a pretty bare-bones joint - no fancy seating, mostly a bunch of tables that seat 2-4, as well as a windowside ledge where you can park yourself on a stool - but the casual setting fits perfectly with the casual yet fantastically delicious nature of the food. It's probably a good thing I don't live within short walking distance of Mighty Quinn's, because I would be coming back here all the freakin' time. While it doesn't have the breadth of menu that the main prominent BBQ joints in NYC have, they make up in incredibly top-notch food. A must-visit if you're a carnivore or BBQ lover.

Rushed to Totto Ramen with a friend at 5pm on a Saturday and still had to wait 30 minutes. Once we were inside, I ordered the Mega Ramen and waited for hopefully the meal of my life. I've had better ramen before, but Totto Ramen was the definition of 3 stars: A-OK. Maybe 3.5 stars, but I don't feel comfortable giving it 4 stars. The pork buns were acceptable and definitely superior to Momofuku. Regarding the ramen, the broth was rather one-note (Ippudo's is better), but the noodles were excellent. I have other favorite ramen places in NYC that I will likely never be coming back to Totto Ramen, but I would recommend it to other ramen lovers. Maybe it will suit them better. The place was burning hot, and service was hurried. No worries, I understand. Sitting and feeding so many people in such a small space must be a lot of work.
First time trying these bad babies. Yummy fresh kati rolls. Whats' not to like? Must have if you are not too hungry :)
If you don't pick up the phone, you can't take an order for delivery. Called three times in a half hour and they never picked up.

Like many have mentioned before me Patsy, the original owner of Grimaldi's who got muscled out, is the owner of Juliana's and he came out and greeted us after we had our pizza. Such a nice guy and a really great staff. However, what really matters is the pizza and it was amazing! Best pizza we had while in NY. Skip the line at Grimaldi's and get the original at Juliana's.
Great gourmet food, fast service and affordable prices. Can't really beat that for lunch in New York when you want a quick bite.

You just have to give Bohemian five stars; secret location tucked behind a deli and superb food at reasonable prices! Â The zen rock gardens add to the feel and the staff is a delight. Â Only catch... Â You need someone to gift you the phone number and it won't be me ;)

YUMS! Excellent food and super polite service. I can still hear my server's drawn out "thank youuuuu" and his calm, zen presence. My party of three had to wait more than an hour to get seated for dinner, but the time passed quickly as we shopped in the nearby TIme Warner Center. All of the dishes we ordered were top notch, particularly the meat skewers with scallions mmmm. Please leave room for dessert since their desserts are surprisingly amazing as well! FIVE+++ STARS!

Instructions for eating at Joe's Shanghai: Enter with friends. Sit down. Order the Xiao Long Bao. Maybe two, or three. Each. You know how much soup was in it? I put the whole thing in my mouth and so much liquid erupted out I thought I was gonna freagin' DROWN. Yeah, something like that.

I really really really wanted to give this place at LEAST 4 stars. Honestly, I would have loved to give it 5! Why didn't I, you ask? Read on. My experience started out well enough. I didn't have a menu and wasn't familiar with their dishes, so the girl on the phone was willing to help me chose what to order. Earned one star just for that. Delivery was quick enough, especially considering that it's been snowing all day. No stars lost. Bill was $26.00 (before tip) for 2 paninis and a salad. Eh, a tad steep for sandwiches...but from the reviews I've read I knew it would be worth it. Halfway through my salad though, I realized that I had received something, which I had not ordered: a LONG, thick, black hair....entangled within my tomatoes and chickpeas, as if I had won the grand prize! But really....I had not ordered this. I checked my bill again frantically, though there was no line item for it; I hadn't been charged. Totally free! That was a relief. After I gained my composure and set my salad aside, I went back to the panini, which WAS very good, and hair-free. I will give this place another try because shit happens, everyone else loves it, and it adds variety to our delivery menu drawer....but seriously? ew.

I've been to plenty of diners in NYC, and this one is a bit over rated. The mac and cheese was awesome, but everything else WACK! Nothing is like what they portrayed in the diner drives show. Â I would not recommend going here. please save your money !

We had our 2012 office Christmas party at this Chelsea location. Â We were a party of 18, not a big party, but certainly not insignificant. Â Beyond that, the boss is friends with the owners of Luzzo's for years, so the incident should never have happened. Â Let me correct that, it should not have happened to anyone, especially with a guest who knows the owners, with a party of 18, visiting for a holiday celebration. Â UNFORGIVABLE!!! We had 5:30pm reservations and seated in a timely manner. Â By the time we settled in and were prepared to order appetizers, it was probably around 6:00pm. Â It was close to 6:15 to 6:30 when we started getting food on the table. Â We had a round of pizzas and various appetizers. Â Ovest is renowned for the pizza, and they were good as expected. Â But I was very disappointed by the meatballs. Â They were nothing in particular in flavor and texture. Â I suspect they were sitting in the kitchen for a while because they arrived at room temperature. Â The artichoke hearts were again, nothing in particular. Â I can't even remember the rest because they were all who-cares. We finished appetizers and they took our entree orders around 7:00 and were served by 7:30. Â My entree was ravioli with mushrooms. Â Again, arrived lukewarm and was nothing in particular. Â Fine, we had our entrees and had pleasant conversation. Â At around 8:00pm, a waiter just brings over a tiny metal bucket with a piece of paper in it. Â We were distracted by conversation and didn't pay attention to it. Â A few minutes later, someone noticed the bucket and was curious to see what it was. Â It was the bill for the dinner - totally unexpected given they just cleared the entree dishes. Â Take note, we just finished our entrees. Â We were not offered dessert or coffee. Â They wanted us out for the next party that booked the entire restaurant for the rest of the night. Rightfully so, the boss gets pissed and talks to the manager. Â Come to find out, they booked the next party for 9:00pm and needed to clear the entire dining floor. Â We confirmed the reservations twice with the expected count. Â It is absolutely unforgivable that a restaurant would rush out a party of 18 without offering dessert or coffee. Â If the schedule is tight, then do not take our reservations. Â They knew it was an office holiday party. Â And what office party is done within 3 hours between seating to paying the bill? Â While all this chaos is going on, it was revealed they refused to serve someone in our party another glass of wine earlier in the evening (that would mean we would stick around for longer). Â The boss demands either comp the entire dinner and we will leave immediately, or serve us dessert and coffee, and give the person her wine that she asked for. Â They countered saying they don't have any desserts to offer us. Â They would discount the dinner 30% and comp the gratuities. Â My boss says the waitstaff was fine so we will not screw them on the tips - they worked for it. Â He will take the 30% discount. Â But they must serve us dessert and coffee. 15 minutes later, they served us these sorry pieces of cheesecake that were all oddly shaped - some were large pieces and others small, some were wedges and some squares. Â WTF!!! Â After another 15 minutes and everyone getting increasingly angry, and with mounting tension because the dining room is now cleared and guests from the other party are walking in, we just said let's get the fuck out of here. Never again. Â It is truly sad they were so unprofessional. Â Their pizza is good, but not good enough to be so utterly insulted and mistreated.

Great food, especially good appetizers and specials. We took some of our client friends to Basso56 and everyone really seemed to enjoy their meal. The service was a little slow at times, which was why I went with 4 stars, but we were not in a rush and everything was perfect. A great surprise for the Times Square / Theater District.

Bayou is such a great restaurant, I've been here countless times I'm surprised I haven't written a review yet. Everything on their menu is amazing.. my favorite is the tuna, and the muscles. Seriously can't get enough. The space is small but very cozy and big enough that it's not uncomfortable. Decor is great.. Drinks are amazing! Strong but so so good.. Desserts are great as well. I really don't have anything bad to say about this restaurant except make sure you make reservations because it gets packed!! love this restaurant and will be going back soon for sure!
Everything was delicious! Fast service, cheap prices and tons of food.

This is one of my favorite K-town eateries! The food has a very fresh feeling to it and it's all very tasting. I especially love their homemade tofu - any of their dishes with tofu are great. I had the Kimchi Jigae the other day and it was awesome! They specialize in Korean stews which are the perfect comfort food. The banchan here is fresh and delicious. The scallion pancake banchan is particularly good and not overly oily. They will gladly refill your banchan's upon request, so don't be afraid to ask if you run out. Along with the banchan they also give you a small sample of their homemade tofu. This is one of the best things - it's sweet, soft and tasty. All in all Cho Dang Gol is worth the extra three blocks walk from K-town. The food is seemingly fresher here and everything just seems slightly cleaner. I'm a fan.

I am a huge oyster junkie and when I checked out the website and other Yelp reviews for this place, I was super excited to visit Upstate, especially because I have been looking for a go-to affordable oyster and raw bar joint in NYC for a while. Upstate is absolutely adorable, from the chalkboard menus of the day's specials to the cozy dining area and intimate bar space. Â The service was better than any other place I've been to in New York. Our server greeted us like an old friend and immediately told us about a $12 special that included a beer of our choice and a half-dozen mermaid selects, exclusive to Upstate via a connection of the owner to a person who farms them. Â Although I wasn't that impressed with the oysters themselves - they were pretty flat in taste and were inconsistently shucked (about half of them unfortunately had grit in them and didn't seem properly shucked - 2 of them were mangled and the shells were broken). However, I was soon won back over when another server offered me a taste of a delicious German pilsner they had just tapped. It was light, cold and nutty - a perfect pairing for my remaining oysters. Â  We also ordered the bouillabaisse, which came as one big heaping bowl of seafood swimming in a delightful broth that can only be sopped up by crispy toast. Â I have to say my shrimp, although massive, arrived overcooked and I was a little disappointed by the tiny size of the mussels in the bowl. But the broth was absolutely scrumptious and I soaked up every last bit of it with the bread. Â My dining partner ordered the scallop of the day, which was seared in brown butter and came on top of risotto. Â Although the scallops were perfectly cooked, I was sorely disappointed in the risotto. It was not the creamy, slightly al dente risotto you'd expect. Instead it more closely resembled brown rice, as it was loosely scattered on the plate, lacked the tender bite of a good risotto, and didn't have the consistency of a good risotto that can stand on its own two feet. It was a let-down, to say the least. But yes. Two words. Whiskey cake - the perfect end to a really great meal. I just hope Upstate can sort out some of the hiccups so I have a reason to keep going back!

Working in Chelsea, I've passed by this place numerous times without stopping in. Finally the other day when I was starving and low on cash I ducked in here to grab lunch. It was a bit confusing as there's no menu or board posted listing what they have, but I was basically able to just point at numbers of what I wanted--#1 Basmati rice with #3, a potato/califlower platter for $4.50. Delicious, spicy and filling.

Prolly my number 1 go-to for drinks when I'm in the city with out of towners. Â There are a ton of positives at Rattle N Hum: First: Â The beer menu is just ridiculous! Â Looking for chocolate beer from Siberia that's 8.2% ABV? They probably don't have it, but they most likely have something close. Secondly: The staff is generally friendly. Â I've never been there and gotten more than 7/8s through a beer without being able to place another order, which translates to little or no time without having beer in front of me. Third: Â The crowds are aplenty, but not a bad crowd. I'm timid, and I never feel out of place, which means that the crowd here is much more interested in their friends and their beers than they are in looking cool. Fourth: Â The beer menu is just ridiculous. The only thing keeping this place from a solid 5 in my opinion is the food. Â The food isn't good. Â Like...one time I got a sandwhich here, and I just plain didn't like it. Â However, don't let the lack of delicious food be a deterrent, just don't go there for dinner. Â Go there for pre and post dinner drinks though.

I have been to La Sirene many times and tried most of their dishes and the quality of food and service was above par every time. The duck entree is generous in portion and is very sweet, filet mignon with foie gras is very tender, the goat cheese tart is just heavenly, mussels are always delicious, and they're BYOB! Don't worry if you forget to bring a bottle because a nearby liquor store delivers right to your table. And one time chef himself came to the table and asked how the food was which was very sweet of him. Now, with a bigger dining area, I highly recommend this place.
Best Shawarma I've ever had. Hands down. The meat was so juicy and just a little chewy, UMF so good!

I suppose it's rare to get this many sakes in a western restaurant and if that's you're reason for going (and you have money) this is a good place to sample some very good bottles. However if you're looking for a more rounded evening involving food, service and decor I would avoid. In that order, the good was mediocre at best. Any of the many Japanese/Korean restaurants around town will equal this at half the price. The ingredients weren't fresh and taste overall was of "frozen" and mushy. The service at the bar was very slow and innattentive despite us both asking in English and Japanese. The decor of the basement location still showed the concrete block walls and the accoutrements were just plastered on top. Considering the price I felt it was pretty low rent result. Changes in layout and menu could easily be made to bring this place in line with a true Japanese experience. I hope they will visit some top Tokyo places and emulate a little closer.

I ordered take out from them - curry puffs and bangkok noodles with tofu. Being a fan of Thai cuisine, I have tried many a Thai restaurants, and I would say they were very middle of the road. The curry puffs were a little sweet. The bangkok noodles were ordered spicy, which they were. The tofu was not fried, but sauted, and could have used some more veggies. There was nothing wrong with the food, but it was not great. Cannot comment on the decor or service. Being in NYC, I'll try a different Thai place next time I want Thai food.

I consider myself to be a bit of a pizzaholic so Di Fara's has been on my ToDo list for years! Â We got in line fifteen minutes before opening, a handful of pizza afficionados in front and back of us. Â As the door opened, we shuffled inside, got our order in for a meatball pie and waited patiently on a shared table. Â There was a bit of reverence in the air as Dominic worked his magic! Â Moving in a measured, efficient fashion, he knocks out pies with the ease of a seasoned pizzaiolo. Â A few lucky people got their slices early but we needed to wait for our custom order pizza. Â  In about 30 minutes, our name was called and my cousin trotted triumphantly back with our beautiful pie! Â A bit burnt on one side, swimming with cheese and a bit of olive oil, the pie had a smattering of hand-cut basil and was baked to perfection. Â I waited a bit for it to cool down which was pure torture! Â The first bite was magical, you can taste the three cheeses that are used and the fresh basil on top. Â The crust cracks a bit but holds its own with some chewiness, light and delicious. Â The sauce pops out with bright, tomato flavor and the meatball was perfectly spiced. Â Definitely some first-class, fresh ingredients here, you have to appreciate the details of a master at work. Â  Â  Take em all together and you know you're eating a pie that is uniquely special and made with love. Â  What can I say, it was great pizza but hard to compare it to anything else since I haven't had anything else like it. Â Better than Pepe's? Â Hmmm. Â Better than Totonnos and Lombardi's? Â Probably. Â Best pizza ever?! Â Wow, that's a tough one but just maybe... Â The only way I can find out is by sampling all the other great pies out there, in the US and Italy. Â And that's a goal that I'll happily take on. Â But for now, DiFara's is certainly at the top of the pizza pantheon for me! Update 12/19/09: Just went to Pepe's in New Haven last week and what can I say but Di Fara is still the pie to beat...

this place is a no frills but unique burger joint. Â The burgers and wings are great and they have a good selection of beer. the burgers are big and can't compare to corner bistro, shake shack style, but they are definitely satisfying. Â I usually eat here once a week and have never been disappointed (save for an undercooked burger once). Good build your own salads too. Â can get cramped on the weekends and space is tight so not great for large groups. Â highly recommend for a casual dinner out.

There are few things more New York City than Junior's and its cheesecakes. They have great cheesecake. My personal favorite cheesecake at Junior's is the Chocolate Mousse Cheesecake. It has chocolate mousse, chocolate cheesecake, and a chocolate chip outside layer. Martha's Oreo Cheesecake is my favorite cheesecake but this Chocolate Mousse Cheesecake is a close second. They have locations in Manhattan in Times Square and Grand Central. The original one is in Brooklyn. While their cheesecakes are phenomenal, I have never tried their other food because I heard average reviews about it. For more great dessert spots in New York, please see my personal list at rookerville.com/2014/01/â€¦

This is one of those places I'd like to call butta food - Everything here is good but the food. If I ever come back, I'll be sure to order only the buccatini with a side of moscato d'asti. Lingua (tongue) - slightly sour/pickled with onions - bleh Sardines with honey - kind of fishy Buccatini - best dish of the night Ricotta gnocchi - too rich and lacked the right proportion of pasta to sauce (needed more sauce). I think gnocchetti would be better Striped bass - decent but kind of plain Spicy chicken with a slice of toast and pate - the plain chicken wasn't as spicy as the waiter seemed to indicate and the pate hidden underneath the two thighs was the best part so we just ate the pate Â  Olive oil torta with rhubarb and some creme fraiche - good Blended lemon sorbet with champagne drink - I could really taste the bitter aftertaste from the alcohol so I had the waiter take it away. Mixing a sweet dessert wine with the lemon sorbet would have been ideal. Moscato d'asti - best part of the night

Ate there Friday nite had a reservation and still had to wait 20 minutes for our table.four doors down at their sister restaurant .once seated our server Allison was amazing and made up for the previous inconvenience. Food is excellent. We ordered the sliders, kale,skate and clam chowder topped off with bacon doughnuts. Culinary treat

went back for brunch. even better. boozy and then a nap! oh i love it. if you dont like locanda verde there is something wrong with you. the stomboli was outrageous and we indulged in the ricotta again. i would go just to eat that at the bar.

Been here for lunch (lunch special) and for dinner. Pad See ew with beef - one of the better pad see ew I've had Pad thai with shrimp - could be more flavorful Ratchaburi Crab and Pork Dry Noodles - this is one of my favorite dishes here Roasted Baby Back Ribs - meaty but spicy, pretty alright but I wouldn't order this again
Four stars if you're drunk, two if you're sober.

How can anyone dislike BCD tofu house? Service? Check Food? Check Healthy Appetizers? Check I love dining at korean restaurants. I feel like everything I eat is relatively healthy there, or at least I hope so. For my visit, i ordered the beef tofu stew. They will ask you how spicy you want the stew and will tailor it according to your needs. I got the stew in mild, but really should have gotten regular because my stew came out a little bland, blah my fault. We also ordered steamed dumplings but got order envy when we watched the table next to us gobble down the fried ones. The fried ones looked so much better and yummier and more artery clogging, but whatevers. The stew came out with the appetizer which I really didn't understand...They serve the stew with rice and a slew of appetizers in the beginning. The little plates held broccoli, macaroni and egg and ham salad, squid, radish, kimchi, and even a fried croaker [fish]. They will keep brining you new plates if you manage to finish the ones on your table. BL: I would come back to this place for some soondubu especially with the cold weather approaching.

Stopped by yesterday for lunch Â and happy I did. Walked in and everyone was all smiles and sat us right away. Â Started off with Â Mothers Milk Stout (which is an amazing dark beer if you never tried one). Â Ordered a cuban sandwich with fires. Â Both were excellent, the other choices on the menu all looked great and will be back to try some more.

I've been coming here for almost 3years now & this use to be my all time favorite Â brunch place but won't be coming again after today. They are under new management & a new cook. They have changed EVERYTHING on their menu including their once amazing huge fluffy blueberry pancakes. I came on a Sunday & the place was almost empty when usually on a Sunday their wait use to be any where from 30-45min. I'm super sad & disappointed in what they've done with the place.

I love this place. Â I go here a couple times a week. Â It is a little hole in the wall place that is clean, serves good Mexican food, with a large menu and fast service. Â They do not mess around, the serve a very consistent product and you will be in and out in 5 minutes. I am a big fan of the quesadillas. Â They serve them with fresh salsa, pico de gallo, guacamole and sour cream - all on the side so your food isn't a soggy mess when you get it home.

I've tried to get a slice at several times but I was never able to get a slice because either they ran out of dough and were closed for several hours or they were closed until 3PM. Â I happened to be in the area Sat night around 7:30 so I figured I'd stop by. The line was out the door (but that's not really saying much since the interior of the store is basically the pizza ovens and counter. Â I waited for about half an hour but by the time I got to the counter the line was much longer. Â I don't know how long they probably waited. So I got a slice of spinach and artichoke and a slice of sicilian. Â The spinach and artichoke pizza was thick. Â I mean the dough was thick like a sicilian slice. Â The pizza is rich and definitely good. Â I wouldn't say it's too rich but it's good. Â I also had a slice of sicilian. Â It was crisp, a bit crunchy and thinner than spinach and artichoke pizza. Â I liked it but it was greasy as hell. Â It was on my plate for less than a minute and it was soaked through with the pizza grease. Â No one ever said pizza is health food I guess. Good stuff, but since the hours they are opened are a bit unpredictable, I suggest calling ahead if you are making a special trip to try it.

Loved this hip Italian spot right in the heart of things near the theatre district. Â Such great food here and you certainly won't leave hungry since there is an all you can eat pasta special for only $22.95. Â You get caesar salad and then 3 different types of pasta- served until your heart is content or until you have no more room in your waste band! Â Worth every penny spent- with fast service and friendly waiters. Â  I would certainly recommend this place to anyone who likes authentic Italian food. Â We will take friends here when they come to town. Â It's also very highly reviewed by Zagat.

I've been going to Sripraphai since 2002 and the food is consistently excellent and prices are extremely reasonable. One piece of advice: when you ask for medium spicy, expect to get sweaty and hot! Â The spicy-ness continuum definitelyt matches authentic Thai standards. Other restaurants just don't compare. I recommend this place to everyone.
The eggs Benedict are perfect. The best I have ever had. Â I will always remember this gem and i am envious of residents of lic that have easy access to this wonderful cafe.

I tried the brunch over there. Wouldn't call this restaurant American New. More American Traditional. There is nothing inventive about the dishes. But I didn't have any problem with that. Good comfort food. Don't go there if you are on a diet though. Great service.

You've got friends visiting from out of town? Are they the type of grown men who walk around the streets of NYC drinking beer 30, rattling off slurs in their southern drawl? The beauty of Barbacon is that it's not just for those friends, it's for everyone. Who doesn't love bacon? You love bacon. Your mom loves bacon. Your kids love bacon. You'll all love BarBacon. Be mindful of your veggie friends, they can probably ask for the salad minus the bacon-but they'll be jealous that they care about animals and salivating at your plate. If you're debating going for the chocolate covered bacon, you can skip it. But you'll be remiss if you don't try the sample platter-the jalapeÃ±o will have you changing your order and subbing in jalapeÃ±o bacon rather than the cheap stuff.
Homemade pasta dishes that surely don't disappoint. Â Very affordable as well especially for great tasting Italian food.

It was around 3 am and me, one of my girlfriends and some guy in his early 20s Â that she had just pick up at bar were wandering the streets of the WV. Â We were looking for a cool bar to go to after being at the Brass Monkey's rooftop for much of the night. We stumbled for a couple blocks and walked into this bar. Â I was confused b/c it seemed like everyone was sitting around eating. Â We asked for a table to have some beers. Â Some waiter brings a menu and it dawns on me that we're at THE "Corner Bistro." Â The very same Corner Bistro that I've had bookmarked for months and have desperately been trying to come to. Â So, despite my lack of hunger, I ordered a cheeseburger medium-rare. Â  I don't remember much about it except that it was delicious, absolutely juicy and perfect. Â  However, Â I do remember giving the dude in his early 20s a hard time b/c he didn't order a burger. Â  I would really like to come back when I haven't been drinking for 6hrs straight.

Decent at best. The thai ribs were dry and flavorless. The fried calamari was mostly tough and as my wife said " an epic fail". The shrimp rolls are decent at best but would not order again. My spicey shrimp noodles were the only thing i would go back for. The service was pretty bad as well. No refill of water and no extra napkins kind of service. I dont remember the service at joya being as bad. The food is the same. Nothing special. At least its not expensive.

2.5 stars but rounded up. It's very cheap. And if your priority is saving money then I'd come here and feel good about it. It's a notch above a bad diner but a notch below a good one. The butter, the syrup, the fruit, none of it is high quality. It's all off the sisco truck. The eggs are fine. The fries are delicious. The waffles, the pancakes all of it are fine. Not worth any kind of wait. The decor is fun, but only out of context. This diner is the restaurant version of a hipster. Turning a lack of funds into a really cool thing and making people think its all a choice. I think this was at one time genuine, but now is played up for the hispterati that come here instead of a fancier brunch option, because you know, it's by choice. But really, the quality is not there. I would return, on a weekday, if I was in the mood for a greasy spoon and was in the area. Waiting hours is just nuts. I'm sorry Tom's. I think you mean well.

I update my review to 5 stars. The mix grill was very good. I had the shalafef and it is amazing! The merguez sandwich is great too! And the sauce they use in sandwich is very good. For sure I become one of my favorite spot for Mediterranean food!

This place is right down the street from me. I've been here a few times with my boyfriend and it's always great. We go on weekdays when it's not very crowded and take advantage of their happy hour. Their waffle fries and cider on tap are both awesome!

Nothing here (aside from the cafe con leche and rice/beans) is extraordinary, but I still like coming here. Walking in to this place is like going back in time. First, the prices are straight-up cheap. Second, it has an authentic vibe that's a welcome retreat from some of the other places in the area. Lastly, it's old. How long has that menu been up there on the wall? I love it. They have a decent selection of meats and the menu is different for each day of the week (closed Sunday).

Around 50 bucks a person with dessert, assuming you order no alcohol. Served all tapas style, my table ordered an array of foods including duck egg with truffle, oxtail, and spicy rabbit. The food was amazing.
I had higher expectations because of the ratings. Nothing impressive, pastas were fairly good. Panna cotta was worth a try!

I love going out in the east village and places like this are the reason why. Â  It's small, it's cozy, it's casual, and the food is terrific. Â It has the feel of authenticity and there were several people speaking Slavic languages all around me. My friends and I shared the several appetizers and the mixed-grill for two, which was as it sounds, a giant plate of delicious grilled meat. Try thePita Sa Visnjama (sour cherry pie); it was recommended to us by the incredibly helpful and nice wait-staff and it didn't disappoint.

I ate at Gyu-Kaku on one of its special days - July 4, Jan 1 etc. - when they do an all-you-can-eat deal. Â The selection for the AYCE was good and the service was even better. Â Our server was polite and kept the plates coming at a good pace. Â The price of the AYCE deal is amazing, but the prices of the a la carte menu, considering the quality of the meat, is not as attractive. Â The meat is good, but it's nowhere near top quality. Â So I will come back to Gyu-Kaku for the next holiday deal.

Yeah yeah, they're french fries. Why would I want to wait on this long line to get them here? Â Then I waited on line and now I understand. Â I tried the Peanut Satay & it was amazing. Â I'm definitely going back to try other flavors.

You will have to fold their pizza slice as it will not fit on a standard paper plate. A slice or two will definitely fill you up so be cautious if it's not the 4th meal. But, it's a good way to sober up after a night out, and it will minimize any hangover. This is another centrally located spot after any night time outing. It is also a good meeting point since easy to find and easy to get to. We picked this spot to meet NY friends here on each trip.

Jane's restaurant was a place that I've been dying to go to. Therefore I made a reservation for Jane's for my boyfriends birthday! I was impressed that we walked in and was sat down immediately. Despite many people were waiting outside. We were very hungry, so we got two entrees and biscuits for appetizers. But what upset me was the waiter didn't give us any BREAD! Every other table had bread served but us. Pretty upsetting. -1star. Was it because we ordered biscuits with our meals you just didn't give us any bread? How Rude! I ordered the Benedict Jane and my boyfriend ordered the Lobster Benedict. The potato hash that came with it was good for the first few bites, but then it got very salty. The biscuit that was under the crab cake for the Benedict Jane's got hard. The lobster Benedict was okay as well. I thought it would be an amazing brunch, but my expectations of the entire brunch was disappointing and jane's just didn't quite cut it.

Dropped in for lunch and sat at the bar in The Tap Room. Â Bennett, the bartender, was delightful - warm, efficient and adorable - even when extremely busy. Â The food was great and a good value. All of the staff was incredibly welcoming and seemed genuinely happy to have us there. Â This is wonderful spot and we will definitely return!

We celebrated my daughter's birthday at L'Artusi last night. Â The food was quite spectacular, particularly the pasta. The reason it gets but 4 stars, really should be 3 1/2, is because one of the main dishes, the pork chop, came out 10 minutes after everyone else was served and then was so tough that it couldn't cut. Â We sent it back. Â Wisely, they didn't charge us for the either the offending (offensive) chop or the replacement dish. Â Our appetizers, Dayboat Scallops and Roasted Mushrooms were perfectly prepared and tasted great. Â The aforementioned pasta dishes, Cappellacci and Tagliatelle, just knocked us out. Â We found the Hangar Steak, Branzino and Halibut very tasty too.
Very cheap and delicious dumplings with that Soup Nazi kind of vibe (the cashier's eyes will cut through you). Â $10-12 will feed two hungry people. Â Try the pork and chive fried dumplings

Decided to try this place for dinner. Luckily, it was open late and I was starving. Ordered the pork buns and the Akamaru Modern ramen...both were so good. Maybe my hungry stomach made my opinion biased, but the food was definitely enjoyable. I liked looking over to my neighbors to see what they were eating too. The ambiance is pretty nice and mix of modern and asian decor. I would go again if in NY again.

Best waffles ever!!!!!!! Me and the bf always get the chicken and waffles here. Have tried some sort of egg dish, too, and it was pretty good, but the chicken and waffles are so amazing that we have to order them every time we come. Great Stumptown coffee and friendly service. I've only been on Sundays for brunch and there is always a long wait unless you get here right when they open (desperate, I know) so it's good to get there early.

Really nice place! I had the Kermes Enchiladas...Pulled Chicken Rolled in Corn Tortillas/ Queso Fresco Mole Poblano (Chocolate!!) and tomatillo sauces! Wasn't spicy which was great. Best part of all was they didn't pile on the cheese and they focused more on flavor. Local and newly run mom and pop shop...I hope this place goes far. Affordable! By the way nice backyard too! Going there in the summer.

Yeah, yeah...I know date night is supposed to be about your date...but I couldn't stop talking about the food!! I barely said a word to him. Everything about Buttermilk Channel is excellent. The hostess was as polite as they come, the bartender was helpful in making special cocktail recommendations and our server was knowledgable and attentive. But the food was on a whole different level!! I am from the South and I have to say that they do it just right! I had the fried chicken over a cheddar waffle and my date had the trout over grits. SIDE NOTE: Since we started dating, he's refused to eat grits - a staple of my childhood. I'm proud to say that these were the first grits he actually said he enjoyed! And believe me, that's a small miracle in itself! This is a must-try restaurant ... even if you have to travel from another 'burb. It will be worth the commute.
Fantastic. Do not let occasional lines dissuade you. The food was well worth the wait. I'm still savoring the miso ramen days later.

I wish Yelp let you give half-stars. Because I would probably give this place a 2.5 if I could. TL;DR VERSION: Dark, loud, full of tourists, the menu is terribly confused, they don't use any fresh ingredients in the *actual french* dishes, and the service was a bit scatter-brained. Still, I wouldn't say this place was *horrible* or that the food was inedibly foul. It was just ... meh. Also the price was slightly higher than I'd expect for the market this place is targeting (middle-class tourists). FOR THE BORED: My wife and I just moved to Chelsea, and are looking for a decent local "regular" to stop in when we just don't feel like cooking. It doesn't have to be especially posh, or especially cheap. It just has to be clean, comfortable, fairly quiet, and offer QUALITY food. Le Grainne (the one in Chelsea) is just a few blocks down 9th Ave for us, and the outside of the restaurant is very attractive. So, it seemed a good bet, since its mostly off the beaten path for tourist traffic. The first thing we encountered after stepping through the front door: every face in the restaurant was cast in the cold blue glow of IOS and Android. Not a good sign. On top of that, cliche' 1950's malt-shop diner music was blasting loudly throughout, making it necessary for us to yell at each other, just to have a little conversation. Hardly what you'd expect for a cozy french bistro. For dinner hour on a Sunday, the place was fairly empty, so we were seated right away. The waiter brought water immediately, and left us with our menus. Fifteen minutes later, he came back to offer us a bread basket. We refused it. We were all ready to order by then, but he walked away, and didn't come back for another 10 minutes. at which point we finally ordered.
