Â  I got the merguez sandwich, and my wife got the chicken braillard. It should be noted that aside from the hors d'oeuvres, sandwiches, some of the salads, and some of the Â deserts, the remainder of the menu is basic american, and italian-american "family restaurant" food. At french restaurant prices. The first 5 entrees in the entree list are stock standard italian-american food, and the chicken braillard my wife ordered doesn't even show up on the internet menu. One thing I would absolutely expected on the menu of a FRENCH BISTRO, is steak frites. Nowhere. Sad. I was really looking forward to one. We didn't order any drinks. We just stuck with the water bottle. Aside from the roasted red peppers, my sandwich didn't really taste like anything. I was expecting a little bit of spice from the merguez sausage, but it was just bland and gritty. Also, the roll seemed more like a stock grocery store hoagie bun, than a french brioche. The side salad that came with it had no taste either. It wasn't limp or soggy, but it wasn't really crisp either. It was like eating scraps of paper. My wife reports that the brilliard didn't really taste like anything either. She says the meat and veg didn't seem to be old or spoiled, but just that everything was sort of plain-tasting. Shes' a better judge than I at these things than I, and says its most likely because they don't use fresh ingredients at this place (i.e., grocery store bought, or shipped in frozen). Perhaps they did at one time, but no longer. When we were finished eating it took my wife and I 6 or 7 minutes of staring down the waiter, to get him to realize we wanted the check, and to go, even with our forks overturned, and the napkins on the table. That's just silly. Periodically throughout our meal, my wife's face would light up with the flash of another noisy patron's iPhone camera. I couldn't help but wonder how naive you'd have to be to want your picture taken in this place, and how annoying it was to have to tolerate that when you're trying to have a quiet evening out with your wife. Overall, I'd say the experience was underwhelming and decidedly not french. However, if I had to choose between this, and say, Denny's or Chili's, I'd take this. Still, this place is clearly off the "regular" list for us.

A lovely little nook! The wine selection is fairly diverse, a good selection of European and Domestic vintners. Â The food menu is quite nice, with a pleasing selection of cheeses, cured/dried meats, small plates and other comestibles. The main bar area is rather run of the mill, but inviting. Â There is a second room off the left and up a few stairs which offers bank seating and small tables and chairs. Â There is enough separation that the buzz of the bar can not readily be heard. Â This room is quite comfortable, and offers a relaxed, quiet experience. The staff are very pleasant, eager, and quite knowledgeable. Â  All in all, a great place for an intimate evening or as a prelude to a night out.

Love this place. Everyone who I have ever came here with enjoyed themselves and the experience. Even came across some ball players at times. We usually go to the downtown location but heard good things about this one as well. Their menu is amazing and different which is something hard to get on the money. When going with a group of 4 or more I suggest to get their combo packages they end up being super worth it. If going just as a couple go for the meats that you prefer. The shrimp are amazing and the skirts steak are on the money as well. Also their spicy rice is amazing! only thing is it is pricey and the portion is fairly small. but its worth it. Do not leave this place without having the smores for dessert! brings back childhood memories and tastes great after a great meal. Also can go with one of my favorites lady m cake! (yes they have it! sometimes more than one flavor) Love everything about this place other than the fact that it can get pricey. Have pics but will add from the app. Thanks for reading.

With such a multitude of Italian restaurants in the neighborhood, Da Marcella definitely reigns supreme. I am a devoted patron, and the staff here are pretty much like family. The food here is 100% authentic, awesome, and reasonably priced. The space has a quaint, neighborhood feel, sort of like dining in a small cafe in Italy. The owner, Alessandro, is extremely hands-on, and it shows in the food, service, and overall presentation. Please, I beg you, try the Burrata. It's served over prosciutto, topped with truffle sauce (yes...believe it), atop a crostone...absolutely divine! I have at least 3 of these a week. The tagliatelle bolognese is also a favorite of mine - extremely flavorful and satisfying.

We visit Black Tree at least once a week to try out the week's featured dishes- the "animal" on the menu changes weekly but always, always excellent. Food is locally sourced, fresh, and tasty. And my personal favorite- sparkling wine on tap.

My family and I swear by this place! Â The food is awesome and so is the service, but you better make a reservation or else. Â Always ask for the specials, and don't forget to order the family size dessert.

I have come to conclude..."TITBDSP" (This is the best damn soup period). I ate hear yesterday, I may actually eat here again today. If you want to go to the same restaurant and order the same dish the next day, how can you give it anything less then 5 stars?

Absolutely LOVE this new spot that's just off the beaten path in this up-and-coming neighborhood. Â Great vibe, friendly staff, and some of the best oysters I've had in Brooklyn. Â The veggie-friendly options and excellent beer selection are a major plus. Â Removing one star just because it's a little hard on the wallet. Â I would go a little more often if there were some price-conscious options on the menu for those leaner weeks.

I am giving Casa Enrique 4 stars but my wife would be at 5 so consider this 4.5 stars. Â BYOB is done here, they have a full bar and a selection of about 5 Mexican beers. Venue: In my opinion it's a little too white and the lay-out is a bit strange since the front room seems designed for parties and very large groups with only a big, family-style table and the bar while the back-room feels a bit squeezed. Â However, this could be an advantage if you wanted to plan a birthday there. Â Aside from the whiteness, the floral arrangements were tasteful and attractive and the candles were nice. Â Overall a slightly cramped, but pleasant aesthetic. Food: We ordered guacamole, the crab meat tostadas, fish tacos and chorizo tacos. Â I've seen some mixed reviews here Â about the guacamole and probably because this is a bit of a different take on something a bit tired. Â The color is a deeper green because it appears they really grind the cilantro into almost a paste before adding the avocado which is then just a bit Â more chunky than normal. Â We liked it. Â The crab tostadas were delicious, sort of like crab ceviche on a corn cracker with generous chunks of crab meat, we'll order those again. Â The fish tacos were for me the only disappointment of the meal as they seemed to be just chunks of fried fish mean on a tortilla to which I was supposed to add sauce. Â It was a bit boring but my wife really liked it. Â The chorizo tacos were delicious, with the chorizo served in a ground form with a nice flavorful spiciness and consistency. Â Overall the food was excellent. Service: I've seen some mixed reviews on service as well. Â Our experience was pleasant considering it was a busy Friday night. Â We never had to wait very long to get our waitress's attention and while it took a little bit of time for the guac to come, everything else arrived at just the right time. Â No complaints. Bill: Our bill came out to $65 including tip and tax with two beers not previously mentioned. Â The only thing I found overpriced was the fish tacos at $12 for 2 compared to the chorizo tacos at $8 for 2. Everything else was within reason. Â I think complaints of cost on Yelp are exaggerated... If you want crappy, cheap Mexican then go to Taco Bell or the local dumpy taco place, Casa Enrique is clearly not going for that approach with much more sophisticated food and atmosphere. You certainly are treated to a nicer experience for the money, just see the high reviews on Yelp! Overall, we were definitely pleased with our experience and will be going back soon, I'm sure.

It was a delightful time! The food was great, the service was charming and pleasant, while anticipating our needs and always available to discuss the menu. Just love the BYOB concept. Always have! The chef always made a point to see if everyone was happy. A great experience!

New York Pizza is definitely a sensitive subject to the locals. Everyone has their preferences. Everyone has their opinion on the subject. I'm a tourist. I don't claim to know anything about NY pizza, but I can tell you what I thought of Lombardi's. And I... LOVED it. Seriously this is a great little pizza spot in Little Italy, one of the most famous locations in Manhattan. The pizza is just unbelievable. The cheese, sauce and crust are all spectacular. It's just the perfect combination of crunchy, sweet, salty, meaty, cheesy, and warmth. Â Be ready to spend about 45 minutes to over an hour waiting for a table. It's cash only so make sure you carry at least $60 for a dinner for two w/ drinks. The setting is historical and perfect for a simple, NY pizza dinner, even romantic in a way. I have nothing but great memories going here, and I guarantee you'll have a similar experience. It's cheap, quick, quality, and the service is fantastic. Organized chaos, but it works. Lombardi's is my favorite pizza spot hands down.

Just became one of my favorite places in Manhattan to grab a drink. This place is awesome, they have a great liquor selection and their drink menu is if the better ones I've ever seen. There's two parts to this place...A downstairs section consisting of a bar with some tables on the side. The upstairs portion is set up with tables and a laid back/speakeasy vibe. The drinks are out of his world and very strong. I ordered one of their drink specials which came with rum and it was pretty amazing. Strong as hell but amazing. The vibe is mature and crowd is mainly after work folks from the area. This is by far the best bar in Fidi. Even if speakeasy isn't your thing, if you like a quality drink, this is the place you bed to come to. Hands down one of the best in NYC!

Wow! Â This place is great! Â It's in a small location on Mott street, around the corner from the famous Mulberry Street. Â While Mulberry Street has much history, it doesn't have this level of authenticity. Â  I came with my friend who is visiting from Italy. Â I didn't know what to expect..walking in we were greeted by a man behind the bar in italian! Â I quickly learned that nearly all the staff is Italian and being able to listen to them talk with each other in italian while waiting for the food made even my italian friend say "wow I feel like I'm in Italy." Â  I ordered the Penne Vodka, which i can say honestly may have been the best I ever had. Â It was perfect, al dente, and the sauce was great. Â I ate every last piece of pasta! Â  I hope this place makes a good go because I would love to come again!

Bf and I came on a Sunday evening around 6pm. Â There were no tables available because there was a large party coming in later, but luckily, we were able to sit at the bar. Â The bartender was very nice and friendly. Â He was helpful in explaining certain dishes, and which ones to try. Â  We ordered the chicken wings (medium spicy) as an appetizer, which was very good. Â I loved the sauce on the wings. Â I would definitely recommend pork shoulder dish! Â We ordered the half size dish, and it came out bigger than we expected. Â It was very delicious! Â The meat was very tender and fell off the bone. Â The accompanying bok choy was a very nice balance. Â Also recommend the bone marrow dish. Â It was huge, and very tasty, and also came with one bowl of garlic rice. Â  I wasn't a big fan of their squid ink seafood noodles. Â Seafood didn't taste very fresh to me, and there was also something else about that dish that threw me off, that I can't put my finger on. Â My bf liked the dish though. Â  We ordered the halo halo to finish off the night. Â While we were waiting for the halo halo, the bartender gave us complimentary avocado shakes, which were leftovers from the shakes he was making for another customer. Â He could have tossed it away, but gave it to us on the house! Â Thought that was pretty cool of him. Â  Reservations are definitely needed for this place. Â I think we lucked out seating at the bar, because the next 2 times we've tried coming here, there was nothing available after until after 9pm (including bar seating). I will definitely will be back here, and maybe I'll be brave enough to try the balut!

This place is mostly for women and dates. Everything is dainty and Japanese. The black sesame creme brulee was really good. I'm a big fan of black sesame anything, really. These desserts tend to be less sweet with a subtle nutty flavor. Their selection of tea is also very good and you can get free refills on the hot water. Good place for talking as it is relatively quiet.

Do you like good, cheap beer and pub food? How about a laid back vibe, comfy booths, mellow regulars and a playlist that's full of interesting music? Brooklyn Ice House is the place for you. Found myself here during a tour of Red Hook this weekend. Settled into the corner table by the front door, where we played some Connect Four and Jenga, enjoyed the eclectic yet always quality playlist, and sampled the perfect sweet potato fries (the ideal blend of crispness and chewiness). And they were $3, as was my oatmeal stout. And the barkeep seamlessly took care of us, refiling water glasses without asking (this is a bar, mind you). The pulled pork sandwiches and corn dogs also looked quite tasty, with a number of folks tucking into them. Loses one star for being so far out of the way, but a great spot I would gladly revisit soon. If you're in Red Hook, go to the Ice House.

Well that was definitely a nice dinner for a special occasion. Distinctive food with good selections of beer, cocktails and Scotch (apparently; I can only speak to the first of those). A happening place, but service wasn't rushed or anything. You won't find dishes like this on just any menu. Â The appetizers were delicious. Â We tried the highly-recommended duck meatballs, which were great meatballs, but still just meatballs... Â Calamari fans will not be disappointed here. Â I wouldn't say the entrees were my all-time favorites, but they were creative and even fun. Like I said, not the best soft-shell crab I've had or the tastiest duck I've tried, but a worthwhile meal, no question. A word on cost... Â With a couple rounds of drinks and multiple appetizers for the table, it came out to over $60 a person. Â I'm sure one could get a nice enough dinner for less though.

After hearing so many great thing about this place and how great their soba is so after waiting in line across the street for octopus balls which they ran out and would take 45min just to get them. We decided to go eat here. I been here before but couldn't get in because the wait was forever. We sat down and order ourself a regular hot sake and started to look over the menu, I wanted something with soba and I order myself the special of the night(littleneck with hot soba for $18) and my friend order the fried fish soba. Somehow I was picturing my soba on their own dish and a small soup w.littleneck inside. When it actually came out, it was just a bowl of soba noodle w.clam inside. Dang it cost freaky $18 for that and I keep thinking, for half of that money I could have eaten udon west down the street. My friend bowl came out and somehow it was udon instead, anyway it taste alot better then mine but it still doesn;t beat Udon West. I check in this place and found out that I get a free beer or a small sake and of course I got the sake. It was a nice bonus. Overall this meal felt more FORCE and nothing was really that good,. There tons of reviews on this place but personally i don't see why. The food isn't that good. The soba was ok ish the most. When I was walking out of here, i felt like being rip off and unplease about this whole experience. It cost me $45 buck but the only good thing about this is part of the money goes to helping Japan back on it feet so I was happy about that part but next time i rather donate the money for Japan then trying to eat here again.

I'm currently digesting a very satisfying "basic burrito" from this establishment, and pretty happy about it. Service was friendly and pretty fast, the ingredients were fresh, the portion size was generous (but not Chipotle-overwhelming), and I liked the mix of music playing in the background. Â And I'm glad the prices rounded off so that after tax I wasn't fishing around for pennies. Â (My burrito with guac clocked in at $7.50--no bargain, but on par for lunch spots around here.) I'm a sucker for any establishment that uses biodegradable cutlery and cups, plus the interior is built with reclaimed wood from a farm upstate (and the ceiling is from re-purposed materials too). Â  There's a picture of a bull on the wall, but only one, so perhaps it should be Uno Toro. Â (But uno buen toro.) Next time, I'll try it on a wholewheat tortilla.
Oh my god the wait is so f-ing long every time, both in the restaurant and with delivery. But it is totally worth it, the pizza is so good.

I took my mom here one Saturday afternoon. Reservations are definitely needed for brunch. The menu is eclectic enough for everyone to find something they like. I got the pear, walnut, arugula salad it was light and very good. My mom ordered the BLT&E (egg) and it was amazing - I definitely recommend it - she still can't stop talking about it. My only complaint is that the mojitos were HORRIBLE. It literally was a shot of rum, club soda, rose's lime juice and 1 mint leave. No muddling took place behind that bar - probably because the waif of a bartender's arm would have broken in the process. Stick with mimosas, no one can screw that up, hopefully.

This place serves up authentic Italian sandwiches, and they are absolutely delicious. I get the very popular VIP with the fig sauce. All of the ingredients were super fresh and the fig sauce added something special to the traditional prosciutto and mozzarella sandwich. My boyfriend has tried pretty much every sandwich on the menu and is never disappointed. The wait is extremely long, even when they don't seem to be all that busy. I ordered over the phone, waited a half hour, and walked over to pick them up and they still weren't quite ready. We did have 1 hot sandwich in our order so that could have been the hold up. Prices are also a bit high but that's typical of a place serving authentic and fresh Italian ingredients. They are worth it!

The best option in Chinatown! Â The roasted pig, salt-baked combo (shrimp, scallops, squid), pan-fried noodles, and watercress dumplings in soup are all excellent choices. Â Although the atmosphere is pretty basic, it is more than made up for by the delicious food.

I've been to most of the noodle shops in Manhattan Chinatown and Flushing. Unlike Super Taste, this place has real hand-pulled noodles (you can tell by the consistency) even though the broth can be a bit bland sometimes (remedy this with mustard greens and cilantro). My favorite, though, is the beef knife-peeled noodles. Try it with a plate of the cold cucumbers and the pan-fried (not boiled!) chicken dumplings with their hot sauce. Tasty and cheap.

I've been to Jane several times for brunch and the food is consistently delicious. Today was no exception. I ordered the Benedict Jane - poached eggs with hollandaise sauce over spinach and crab cakes with a side of potatoes - as did my friends and we loved it! The crab cakes were soft and melted in my mouth, and the amount of hollandaise sauce used was just right, not too little and not too much. It's popular and the wait can be long even with a reservation which is annoying. We went early at around 10:45am and were seated immediately which was a nice surprise!

I'm not a big Pizza fanatic or anything but the Pizza from this store is even better than Gramaldi's (One under Brooklyn Bridge). I went on a day where it suddenly started raining. I think the rain might've added to how good it was considering it was cold outside and a Pizza pie was the perfect solution. I ordered a Pizza with Peppers, Italian Sausages, and mushroom. It was fantastic and the drinks to go along with it was not too shabby as well. I ordered a Apple Cider type of drink and some soda float. The service is top notch as well. I haven't been back since I went the first time but I definitely want to go back again.

Delicious udon with flavorful broth! The portions were great based on price, but what matters most for me at a udon joint is how "chewy" their udon noodles are. I enjoyed my bowl, so big ups for that. I went for lunch, but seems like they have great Happy Hour specials, so definitely worth checking out.

GREAT neighborhood restaurant. Â Nestled nicely on the outskirts of Curry Hill, Penelope's warm and cozy ambiance along with its tasty country breakfast dishes has helped create outrageously long lines to get a table. Â Highly recommend coming before 11AM to avoid the rush and definitely try the nutella french toast or pumpkin waffles. Â The pre-fix breakfast is reasonably priced and the service is friendly. Dinner menu is decent, but the brunch is primarily the cause for commotion.
Meh. I've had waaaay better eggs Benedict and cheesecake is good (not best).

It took awhile to find parking, but I guess that's New York in general I guess. The wait was about 10 or so minutes. The place is small and cramped but it's still a fine place to dine with a couple of friends, not so cramped to where you can hear others conversations although you're kind of close to them but it's more of you mind your own party, I mind my own party, we'll converse if we want to. Generally speaking since the place is small you're not allowed to wait inside. Conveniently, they take down your name and number and then they text you when your table is ready, which is pretty cool instead of running around with a buzzer if you randomly decide to change your mind to not eat there (but you should eat there). So we get seated. I ordered a salmon dish that's layered on top of this hashbrown patty with some kind of sour cream and caviar. My friend Celine got the blueberry pancakes and my boyfriend Jaime got chicken and waffles. Â To be honest and not entirely exaggerating, my dish was the best thing that I've ever had in my life. I don't recall the kind of name they had for that sour cream with caviar on top, but it was well complimented for the salmon and hashbrowns. You can taste the freshness of the fish along with the perfect smoked salmon taste. And usually I have salmon with a bagel and sour cream, but whoever thought of matching it with hashbrowns is by far a genius! I mean I did just land from a 7 hr flight and was madly starving, but it wasn't satisfying because I was starving, it was exquisite because of the quality. Christ it was so good and I will not stress enough that that was the best meal I've ever tasted. Celine said she enjoyed her pancakes, but the continuation of sweets was too much but she wouldn't dock it points. She ate what was left of my plate as I had become full, she enjoyed it as much as I did. Jaime does this kind of thing where he moans over food if he really likes it, and he was pretty much doing that the whole time (how embarrassing). Â All in all, he was satisfied as well except for the seasonal beer he got. I took a few sips and we both agreed that there was an odd after taste. I will definitely always come back to this place when I'm in New York, my new favorite spot. P.S. We were in a 5 or 7 hr food coma after this, food game too bombbb
consistently delicious

Visited NYC recently and read a great deal about this place. It lived up to my expectations! I got a solid burger and my fiancÃ© ordered the most ridiculous grilled cheese ever!! It is a typical trendy NY restaurant, where the food is outstanding you have to sit on top of one another and it's pricey. If it wasn't $100 for 2 bloody mary's a burger and grilled cheese this place is 5 star. I would absolutely recommend eating here if you in the west side of Manhattan and you can grab a seat, (it gets packed quick!)

When a place is always packed, it's a good sign. Great food and great wine. They offer a wine flight of 3 glasses and you can try anything from the wine menu, awesome. The food is very high quality. Try the mussels , truffle salad and the pork medallions. This place needs visiting when in West Village.

DINE AT YOUR OWN RISK!!!! Â Be advised if you leave something behind, it probably won't be there when you try to retrieve it. Â  I absolutely have always loved this restaurant, so much so that I took two girlfriends there recently to enjoy a Friday night. Â The food, as usual was really delicious. Â I enjoyed every bit of the experience spent a lot of money and tipped very generously. Â I mistakenly left my phone under my napkin on the table and left the restaurant, when I realized my mistake I was already home. Â I called the restaurant. Â No one took my name or the incident seriously, Â I called again on Saturday and was told it basically wasn't their problem. Â All three of my phone calls made to management were treated dismissively and I was told there had been incidents of this nature there before. Â  After they "questioned" their staff, I called again this morning to inquire as to wether anyone admitted to pocketing the phone. Â I was met with a brusque brush off. Â Each time I called, the staff was extremely rude and unhelpful. Â I was never asked for my name, and each time I asked the name of the person I was speaking with the staff member became very evasive and stated he wouldn't say his name because I might get him in trouble. Â  I understand leaving a phone somewhere is very irresponsible, however when you are dining in a restaurant that you feel comfortable in and spend time and money in... you imagine the wait staff and other members of the restaurant team will be honest and any lost items will be set aside to be returned. Â When I turned on the find my iphone app at home it pinged at the restaurant and then was turned off as soon as I called. Â It has been turned off ever since. Â And yes, it was charged. The owner has refused to take my call. Â And when I asked the manager to rally his staff to return the phone, he told me "we have had incidents like this before and unfortunately these days people are not so honest." Â I refuse to dine in a restaurant with this level of disintegrated disinterest in the well being of a regular patron and their perceived integrity. The phone is an old 4s with all sorts of cosmetic damage. Â As a resell it is only worth about 180 dollars. Â It is priceless to me, with videos of my children. Â I told the manager I was willing to put up a reward and he never took it seriously. Â I am now phoneless and f*cked. Â I hope people in Carroll Gardens are careful and help bring back other French restaurants not run by evasive thieves. Â BAD CUSTOMER SERVICE!!!!!! Â THE CUSTOMER IS WRONG.

Very accommodating, well run, great tasting restaurant. I made reservations for a party of about 8 for a friend's birthday on a Saturday night and there were various people shufflings and the number jumped to ten and they worked with me to get everyone seated (so long as we came in 20 minutes earlier than we'd planned) and even when not everyone showed up they sat us and served with without a single dirty look despite all the people shuffling and calling. Maybe I don't expect much, but they handled it very pleasantly. We were seated quickly and, considering that there wasn't an empty table in the entire place, served very quickly, too. The food was amazing. I think I had the Vaca Frita Al Caballo, which was very good and I enjoyed bites of other people's dishes and enjoyed them all. Seating was a little tight (probably due to the people shuffling) but this made conversation easier and the food took a little longer than we would have liked but everyone had a great time.

So good! I took my boyfriend here for his birthday last night and it did not disappoint. Since my BF is a home brewer, my goal was to find a place with both a great food menu and a stellar beer selection. Imagine my surprise when I found that Applewood has a tasting menu with an optional beer pairing! When we got there they seated us right away, in front of the fire. This was great because it was FREEZING outside and I had just walked there from 4th Ave & 9th St, because the G train was all kinds of messed up. We both got the tasting menu, he with beer pairing, and myself with wine. BF is allergic to shellfish, and the chef was super cool with subbing the 1st course, clam chowder, for the pork belly app. Both were delish! 2nd, 3rd, and dessert course were all amazing. I loved all the wines, and he loved all the beers. They didn't have a beer for the desert pairing, but the moscato they brought us was fruity but not cloyingly sweet like some moscatos can be. There was a little birthday candle stuck to BF's dessert plate, which was super cute. We were both glad no one sang. Haha. We finished off the meal with a coffee, his regular, mine decaf with a splash of milk ( I CANNOT have caffeine in the evening, but I loooove coffee after a big awesome meal). PS, the milk came in the cutest miniature clear glass milk jug. We were a little bummed they didn't do espresso or cappuccino, but the coffee was great so who cares. So all in all the meal was amazing. Tasty food, great wine & beer; a beautiful little resto tucked away in Park Slope, my former hood.

Went to the Frick and needed a pick me up after. Â Sat down at a Â table and had a pot of coffee. Â Coffee was delicious. Â The cookies looked amazing but didn't have room. Â But the decor. Â Ahh. Â Old feel to it. Â Sort felt like Alice in Wonderland sitting at a tiny table. Â Gives it the cool factor. Â Later that night I was talking to my aunt and she stated she has seen a lot of celebs in there. Â Another reason to go back.

Shared dinner with a friend and found two amazing dishes and two good dishes. The best figs I've ever eaten were found here on the tapas menu - they are paired with a basalmic vinaigrette and serrano ham - divine! The grilled salmon was flavorful and nicely paired with a risotto style rice and julianed vegetables. A good blend and well seasoned without being over-powering. The food spoke for itself, which is the mark of a chef who knows what they are doing. The artichoke appetizer was a miss - it seemed like it was trying to be a 'bloomin' onion from Outback with a plate of fried petals. I would pass on this. The chicken kebab small plate was good with a nice tzatziki sauce. Â  Atmosphere is cozy and nice. I would definitely come back here.

I have been dining at La Sirene for the past two years and have no plans of quitting anytime soon! Â It is hands down my most favorite restaurant in the city. I've eaten here on many different occasions- for an anniversary celebration, a family outing, Valentine's Day, a surprise birthday dinner for 8, gossip night with the girls- and they have always been so accommodating. Â I have contacted Chef Didier a few times about wine recommendations and he's so kind to entertain my questions. He's even offered wine that he happened to have at the restaurant when I didn't bring any with me, just so my dining experience could be complete! Â  The atmosphere is relaxed, welcoming, albeit cramped. Â It's part of the charm. Â You won't find any of the pretense here that you normally do at the typical mega restaurants of NYC. Â The service is wonderful and provided by two charming waitresses. Â Sometimes Chef Didier himself will take your orders which is a treat. Â He can be quite bombastic and brash but he'll admit to this himself, saying he is French after all. Â  Now if that alone doesn't want to make you eat here, I can tell you the food is fantastic. Â My order always consists of Â curry mussels and hanger steak. Â I always gravitate to these two because they are so delicious and savory, not to mention comforting. Â The bread basket runs low real quick once the curry mussels come out because I'll sop up every last bit of the broth with bread. Â All the good things to say about the food has pretty much been said in previous reviews. Â I've tried almost everything else on the menu though through my friends' orders and I haven't found one dish I don't like. Â  Â  To sum it up, La Sirene is a lovely experience all around. Â I didn't even get to say half the things I wanted to rave about the restaurant because then my review would never end. Â Honestly I don't have a single complaint and I've eaten at many different restaurants in the city. Â I always come back to La Sirene though! Â The restaurant has not lost any of the charm and deliciousness it's had since it opened. Â Make your reservations ASAP as it is kind of a hole-in-the-wall and don't forget it's BYOB! Â No corkage fee!

I came here with a few friends to enjoy a Saturday afternoon in LIC. It drew us in with its brunch specials ($6 for a mimosa or bloody mary and $3 for refills) and cozy atmosphere. The space itself was decorated subtly for Halloween. There were a few spider webs on the ceiling that were not overpowering and didn't take away from the charm of the space. The dining area is not very big, but comfortable for a small group (I was with 3 other people). The waitress seated us quickly with a friendly attitude. We had a few questions about the menu. She had good knowledge of the items and Â offered her own suggestions. Our food came out rather quickly. I had the veggie burger with truffle fries. The veggie burger came with avocado and a curry sauce on the side. The curry sauce was good but the burger itself could have used a bit more seasoning. Overall, not bad, but I will probably try a different item next time. The truffle fries were very tasty. I could have eaten those all day and been perfectly content with life. The prices are very reasonable. The veggie burger with fries was only $12 and with the brunch special for mimosas, my meal was just about $20. A good place to have a lazy brunch.

hold on to your receipt cause if you don't have it, they will hold your food hostage. mediocre dumplings and noodle soup, but cheap. you get what you pay for. the redeeming thing is that the sesame pancake is AMAZING. otherwise don't waste your time on this place.

I love the vibe of this place. The food is on point. The service is friendly. They have really good margaritas. And their brunch deal is pretty amazing too. It's only con is that it's allllllwwwaaaayyys super busy. But.... $3 delicious tacos?! Enough said.
the best pizza

This is definitely a worth going restaurant. You might want to go there earlier as it's always packed. It opens at 5pm for dinner, we reached the restaurant at 5:30pm and it was packed with patrons already. We waited 45minutes in line and finally able to get seated. Personally I don't mind waited for 45minutes because this restaurant is offering good food and good services. We ordered two appetizers (steamed pork bun and rice burger) and two bowl of ramen. Not only that their broth is good, I think the texture of noodles is good too. Their rice burger tasted better than the rice burger from MOS (a chain fast food restaurant from Japan). Their pork is very juicy, and the taste blended in well with the bun. Everything we ordered was so tasty that I kept telling myself that I need to come back next time! If you are looking for good ramen, don't hesitate to give this a try!

I was so looking forward to dining here after reading so many great reviews. Service was good, $25 wine selections were also good. That's where the positive review ends. Despite making reservations 3 weeks in advance, we were seated at a small two top against the wall, crammed behind Â a 4 top and 6 top. Â The four top was so lcose to our table there was no room for the waiter to stand in front of our table to serve us. Â I could see if we walked in without reservations and were offered that table as the only option. However, the fact that they actually have a table crammed in a corner tells me these owners are pretty greedy to cram diners in every inch of the place. Â  Â Now to the food.. We ordered the beef meatballs as an appetizer, the plate arrived with three almost baseball size meatballs in marinara. They were ok, but I think a mix of veal and/or pork makes a much tastier meatball. My husband had the veal Parm. Nice tender veal, on the bone pounded nice and thin. However the sauce although fresh tomato, was just blah with no flavor.I ordered the three pastas of the day Â Tortellini in brodo, rigatoni with pesto and spaghetti with basil & tomato sauce. I can't say any of the three were worthy of any positive feedback. Â Pasta was overcooked and just all around mediocre. I cannot understand why this place gets rave reviews. We were so very disappointed and although I believe in giving a restaurant a second chance .. We will not be returning to Becco's. Thumbs down !

My only criticism of the pizza I had at Wheated was that it wasn't crispy enough, otherwise I though it was pretty great. It would also be nice if they had a couple starters, on the night I went they only had a single salad. The waitress was super nice and attentive, she gave great recommendations and we felt taken care of the whole night. The owner stopped by to ask us how everything was halfway through the night. Â  I initially ordered the Sunset Park but they were out of sopressata. I ended up with the Clinton Hill which I really enjoyed. The pizza was a good size and if you added a starter would be enough for 2. I also had a cocktail which I really enjoyed thought he name escapes me. The prices are pretty reasonable and I'll definitely be back.

I've been to Caracas Arepas Bar down in East Village and was totally hooked with these tasty Venezuelan arepas. However, I wanted to venture out to Queens to try the Arepas since Queens usually has better Ethnic foods at lower prices than in the city. After reading positive reviews about this place, I decided to come here for lunch today. I walked in, was immediately seated by the energetic and happy Latin (I'm assuming she's Venezuelan) waitress. There are two seating areas here: One is the main dining room and the other a smaller room with about 3-4 tables with a TV. If you're eating alone or want a quieter atmosphere, do go with the latter. I ordered the Sample Platter, La Mami, and the Guayanes Tropical Arepa. I know I know I was hungry and I have a BIG ASS appetite. I also ordered the Venezuelan Soft drink Frescolita which is like the Kolita drinks I've had back in Costa Rica and Nicaragua, sort of like Bubble-gum flavored Soda if you ask me. About 10 minutes later, my Platter came out and it was nicely presented and every item was just so tasty and brought me back memories of my childhood spent eating Latin American food. The platter consists of 3 Tequenos, 3 Mini Cachapas, 3 Mini Empanadas, and 4 Fried Yuca. The Yuca was so crispy and good and I really loved the mini Cachapas (Plantain with White Cheese). Three different sauces come with it and I LOVED the white-green sauce!! After I finished my platter and about 5 minutes later, my Arepas arrive on my table. Man, these were HUGE!!! They were larger than the ones I've had at Caracas Arepas Bar and these things were FILLED!! Guayanes Tropical Arepa consisted of Guayanes Cheese, Fried Sweet Plantains and Avocados and surprisingly the taste was so well balanced of Sweet, Savory, and Soft!! YUM!! La Mami Arepa contained Venezuelan Roast Pork, Avocado and Shredded White Cheese. The Pork was a bit bland but the cheese was good. A little bland for my taste though so I had to add the extremely good hot (Warning: IT IS HOT!!!) sauce that they provide to give it a boost of flavor. But all in all, it was definitely money well spent on good food. Will return in the future if I'm in the area to try other flavors!!!

My latest obsession. No more variable falafel rice from street carts... HP&co. has big portions and multiple options/sides. It's affordable healthy food that actually tastes good. I walk out full for under $8. I want to take away one star for their location not being a block from me, but that's more my fault than theirs. I'll be back.

I hate to say, the food here is just really not that great - bordering on awful. I had the fried chicken, my friend the brisket sandwich. Neither has much flavor, and at $10+ each, with a 20+ minute wait each... Let's just say I won't be back. The chicken has no flavor. It didn't come out hot, the fry was not crispy at all, and the meat, even the dark meat, was more dry than overdone breast meat, so much so that my jaw started to hurt. It had no flavor. Truly an accomplishment if I think about it. The slaw needed salt and had over powering dill. And pickles? I was expecting your standard crisp pickle. It was okra. Gross. Not a fan of the slimy texture. The brisket, also tasteless. I imagine the positive reviewers are just taken by the decor, but really don't know good food.

So I am a regular at their Brooklyn location. For a whole year I been saying there isn't a place as good as this place and finally they open a branch in Manhattan. This place is great all you can eat hot pot esp at this weather. I am not a fan of the Korean bbq. But ayce Korean bbq I'd hard to find unless you go to flushing. The other good thing is that it's same price for lunch and dinner. Â Plus the service is great consider its Chinatown. They have room for big groups too... great location, right by the b and d train.

Two words: Absolutely fantastic. I've been on a slow and steady search for amazing (yet somewhat reasonably priced) yakitori in the city and I think I finally found it. Came with my usual food adventuring friend an hour and a half before closing. Must gets: - chicken skin - chicken gizzard - chicken liver - chicken heart I've never had chicken skin before but my friend insisted me to try at least one skewer. After my first bite, I was sold. Chicken skin is amazing. For dessert, I picked the ice banana which blow my mind. You know it's good when I scarfed it down too fast and heralded a brain freeze of epic proportions.

I've had breakfast here many times and haven't been disappointed. The place is tiny, but if you get in then you feel comfortable. The coffee is wonderful, I could sit and drink cup after cup. In fact, we did, much to our waitresses dismay. Make sure you tip well since you're occupying a fifth of her tables.

This place was phenomenal. Every single thing we ordered was delicious and not too expensive. The service was excellent. Their wine list was huge and had a nice mix of both affordable and crazy expensive bottles. The relatively inexpensive wine we ordered was also fantastic. Highly recommend this place for both dates or group dinners. Well done.

Food is "okay". I would've preferred to stay home and cook myself. The service here is terrible. It took about 15min just to get a soda. The waiter could not get the order right and seemed disinterested. Even the tap water was terrible and we were served with dirty glasses. I will not return.

On day we spontaneously got inside this place and had the Italian meat & cheese. it was so fresh and Â authentic, and the Italian meat was the best that i've ever had in new york city so far. Â  I don't mind tiny table and standing for eating as long as food is that delicious.

I had the green falafel with hummus here. Probably one of the best falafels and hummus I've had in NYC. The place is super small with barely enough room to sit. I give it a 4 since the staff wasn't very helpful or friendly. Maybe it was bc they were closing up but still...

Post Smush ice cream sandwiches down the block, my fiancÃ© and I really wanted something small and salty to snack on. I remembered reading dos toros review in the past and recalling always a line on my way to NYU, we decided to stop in for some munchies to go. There was a line to the door when we arrived but it moved rather quickly. Their menu is simple- burrito, bowl, taco and quesadilla - pretty much chipotle style. There were only 3 tables enough to perhaps seat about 10 ppl as a whole. I ordered the pollo asado taco with black bean, salsa, all the sauces ( I wanted to try every flavor they had to offer) and guac and my fiancÃ© asked for the carne asada taco with guac and salsa. I loved the fact that we can order individual taco since we both weren't particularly hungry. They wrapped each in aluminum foil for us to take. Then we found a nearby bench at union square park to nomnomnom away! The carne asada was a bit overlooked but my pollo asado was juicy and well seasoned. The sauces, guac, salsa and beans were full of flavor. I found it interesting that they put a slice of cheese on top of my taco tortilla. I saw them doing that to all the burritos too. For about 4 dollars per taco, the amount of filling given was pretty reasonable. I don't see it being any better than chipotle however. I actually prefer chipotle since they are options such as whole wheat, brown rice, white corn and extra servings of toppings. Nevertheless a solid 3.5 stars.

Amazing experience at Xixa- from the atmosphere to the wait staff to the food- just amazing. As this was our first time, the waitress (I think her name was Jenna), gave great suggestions on the food. She was informative and attentive to us without being too intrusive on our romantic evening. The duck lettuce wraps, the grilled carrots elote, and the tuna ceviche were some of our favorites. The churros were a perfect end to our meal- crispy on the outside and light on the inside- not chewy at all. All the food was served at the ideal temperature, texture, and with amazing flavor combinations- overall a perfect meal. We'll definitely be returning for another on point meal!

Excellent shabu-shabu place in East Village. Great beef rib-eye and the veggies were good as well. Â We had delicious sake (though I don't think you need to splurge for the expensive sake, which we had done to some degree -- I would get a more moderate one next time). Â  The duck appetizer and the pork gyoza dumplings were outstanding. I love that they finish your meal with ice cream and then tea. Â  Solid place all around I enjoyed the meal very much. Â Would definitely go back.

A solid four-star excellent place, not just cause it's local :) Sadly almost didn't even go in, because our stroller wouldn't fit through the door, but luckily the maitre'd/host/waiter/manager managed to open both doors to let us in. Surprisingly packed for a Monday (granted it was Memorial Day). Kitschy Austrian signs all over the joint give it a very East Village feel. Good German beer list, I ordered a pint of Gaffel (which went surprisingly well with my eggs). I did the sausage brunch combo and opted for the Sauerkraut, and was damn glad I did. Deliciously grilled and nice side of roasted potatoes (same roasted potatoes also accompanied the wife's Wiener Schnitzel). The Wiener Schnitzel is their house specialty, and I could see why. Perfectly done, thinly pounded, lightly breaded Veal... delicious. My eggs did come with a side salad which was edible but nothing to write home about. I wondered if it wouldn't be improved by the use of a better leaf other than iceberg. All-in a very good place that I will surely visit again, not just for my Schnitzel fix, but good Wursts as well.

To the owners: 1. Your waitstaff sucks. I'm sure you're getting into the groove, but no one seems to have a clue what's going on. After arguing over whose section was whose, my waiter basically ignored me. There were 5 staff members hanging out and joking while I waited to order. Â Professional staff and a friendly atmosphere will make people want to come back. 2. Â Your food is overpriced. Nine bones for a biscuit and ham and jam? And an extra FIVE for taters? This ain't soho. Stumptown coffees supreme, but $3 for a large and no refills? Recession specials lure in customers instead of alienating them. Granted Blue had its grime, but the people were nice, professional and the food was cheap. While I love to indulge ocassionally in the gourmet fare, the thought of over priced yuppie gringo comfort food in my neighborhood makes me want to throw up. Lower your prices and train your staff and have a brunch that's actually brunch and you'll not only get my business, but you'll get the after church crowd that lines outside Ministar across the street.
Love this place. Got take out for the first time tonight (lamb taco, pork sandwich, enchiladas). Food was wolfed down in no time. Would gladly go back.
Always order lunch at this great place. If you walk by its clean inside as well. Fast delivery and always fresh. Good burger too

C-H-I-C-K-E-N AND R-I-C-E-! Although I hate waiting in the ungodly long line, it is worth it... I don't know what they are putting in the white sauce but it's obviously working... a Halla Stand has over 1,200 reviews!

I'd like to give it 4.4 stars, maybe even 4.5, but since that's not an option, I'll reserve my 5 stars for the real 5 star gems. FiancÃ© and I took a long lunch break for RW. Despite the good reviews, I didn't expect greatness, especially for $24. To our surprise, the food was actually quite good. Everything was done just right, nice flavors, with good presentation. Both the chicken and skate wings were nice and minestrone was delicious. Â And the best part was the dessert. The waitstaff was actually a bit "too" friendly. Is that considered bad? I don't know. But I don't care too much for 3-4 people coming around every 2 minutes asking if everything's ok, want more bread, water, etc. I'd like to come back and try this squid ink pasta one of these days and see if it's really as good as people say it is.

I love pommes frittes. There's only one thing on the menu: fries. Just pick your sauce. I have to say the sauce I chose the first time completely blew me away. I HAVE to come back and try the rest. I mean, what are they putting in these sauces? My problem is there's always a huuuge line out the door. I never want to go in when I pass by, even though I want to. So I honestly have't been much. Frankly it's a turn off for me. Too bad because the fries are nice.

Great Brunch spot. We had omelette and toast, truffle scrambled egg on country bread, avocado on toast (very delicious) and buttermilk pancakes which are very very good. The pancakes were the highlight for me- melt in your mouth and very tasty. All washed down with an English cup of tea! I will definitely be brunching here again!

Yelp to the rescue again...... though NYC is the city that never sleeps, it seems it gets tougher to find a good local restaurant open late in midtown/theater dist. during late summer. Definitely more a 'dive' spot - but what lacks in tidiness is made up for in great food. We had everything on the specials board (oysters, cod collar, squid, sardines), and everything was delicious. The other yakitori items off the menu were equally great... I'd suggest sticking to the extensive sake selections as the drinks did not seem particularly enticing. the dining room is rather brightly lit for a basement spot, and seating was tight - so be prepared for anything goes depending on who you are seated beside. Thought we were going to have to resort to a chain restaurant in Times Sq, so this definitely saved the night and was a great unexpected surprise.

Who would think that the absolute mecca for pizza lovers just happens to be in Midwood? Â Di Fara's is not just a meal so much as it is an experience, order your pizza, hang out for an hour with friends, and then bask in the warm chessy ecstasy that is Dom's creation. Â Every pie is masterfully prepared by Dom (the owner and pizza god) himself, the best part is watching him take them out the oven with his bare hands. Â Every time I see him cut fresh basil onto my pie I can't help but get child like joy out of it. Â  It is by far the best pizza I've ever had, anywhere. I have ruined pizza forever for my out of town friends by taking them there and setting an unbeatable standard for them. Tehehe Â My favorite toppings are garlic, pepperoni, sausage, but a plain pie is still amazing on it's own. Â Pretty pricey but very much worth it.
Food is good, staff is fine, and the location is well situated. But, I will I come again? Not if I remember I have been there already. Happened! :)

I'm a regular at Mama Pho on Grand, and this place is just as good or better. Great price, more carrots, juicy meat, and a perfectly toasted bun turn this Vietnamese Sandwich shop into a Banh-must. 5/5 Sriracha bottles for this hidden gem.

Again, I am uplifted by my experience at B4!.. Each dish an exquisite delicious delight. The best ingredients used in an expression of high culinary art. Shawn Jones &staff (Helene and Raphael are angels) offer a unique balance of warmth, welcome, professionalism and particular service. It is a privilege to have B4 in our community. Bravo!

the sake selection is pretty daunting and the waitress offered a description of each that was still confusing. Â  its located in the basement of an office building so you feel like youve discovered something special even though the whole world probably knows about this place. Â the food is pretty good and creative. Â i remember cooking wagyu beef on a sizzling stone with butter, and some deliciopus morsels of chicken and root vegetables. Â delicious. Â  would definitely come back!

Our son recommended this restaurant and it is simply great. Â The grilled cheese and tomatoes was delish and my husband had an omelette which he said was equally delish. Â The restaurant had a nice European feel. Â Coffee was good, and the service very pleasant. Â It's a nice local place.

Uruguayan food! That's pretty exotic sounding, isn't it. This restaurant has a filet mignon sandwich served with a fried egg and french fries. The sandwich was quite good; it was very hearty and the meat was quite tender and juicy. They also used what appeared to be some kind of flatbread. They served a garlic-infused mayo with the fries; it was sort of bland but I appreciate the effort. Cozy ambience, friendly and attentive service, good prices.

Went in Yesterday sunday 9/22 for brunch. Â Well to start with they were 10-15 mins late on their reservations. Â This turned out to be more like 45 minutes late. Â We weren't seated until we asked what was going on. Â Turns out they forgot about us! Â to their credit they did give some free doughnut appetizer which was cold but they did try to make up for it. Â  The Server who worked our table Nathan( i think) was great. Â He personally gets 5 stars. Â Very attentive. Â  I ordered the Benedict Jane... Â the crab cake was yummy but then there was the poached egg. Â Someone needs to learn how to poach an egg Â my yolk was cooked throughout. Â  Bad experience over all but the service from our waiter was great which is why they are still get two stars.

I simply love this place. I come here very often and never disappointed. It's not a generic cafÃ© and the food is given a lot of thought. Guiseppe( sp!) owned a restaurant in Sicily for 14 years and is clearly very enthusiastic to introduce the lovely food of Italy to the customers. He uses fresh ingredients and carefully chooses his meat and cheeses. You can taste the subtle flavors in the dishes he prepares. Of course this is a business for them but one both Ellen and G clearly love. Ellen and G are also very friendly people and always greet us Â warmly. I feel like I am entering into a chef friend's dining room and kitchen. Yes it is super cozy. My daughter too loves the grilled cheese sandwich here and rubs her belly in great satisfaction! I highly recommend this place and encourage folks to try.

I don't know how many of you are lovers of the Food Network but this season on Next Food Network Star I became completely obsessed with Justin, the young chef from Brooklyn. Â Such a bad ass. Â And then low and behold he wins! Â This prompted me to visit his restaurant as soon as possible before all of America decided to book a reservation (which is funny because they don't take them). The restaurant is a little bit of a trek from the city to the Bedford/Stuyvesant area but TOTALLY worth it. Â The restaurant itself is a little small (bring more than four people and it might be a bit tricky to fit all of you at a table comfortably) but totally cool. Â It's hipster in the real way not the annoying "hipster" way. Â The tile floor features a skull and cross bones, the table tops are glass with flowers and other scenery underneath and if you are headed to the bathroom make sure to ask the bartender for a marker so that you can graffiti the wall (yup it's encouraged). And when you are done loving the look of the restaurant you can begin focusing on the food which is probably the most random menu I've ever seen. Â My friend and I shared... the foie gras doughnut (famous), the fried chicken, the frog legs, the nachos, and the shishito peppers. The doughnut - I'm glad I tried it but it wasn't my favorite. Â The doughnut was warm which was obviously a plus but I think foie gras and doughnut together is just a little too rich for me. The fried chicken - Other people have given this bad reviews but I thought it was really tasty. Â It was fried the "good" way where there isn't too much breading and the ratio was a lot of chicken to two small waffles which I actually prefer. Â A lot of the places in LA overkill on the waffles. Â Lastly it had like a mango honey glaze which topped it off! The frog legs - It was my first time having them so I can't really make comparisons but for my first foray into frog body parts I thought they were really good. Â Also they were cooked in a Dr. Pepper sauce which I thought was inventive and fun and still tasted great. Â They were also huge which I wasn't expecting and realistically tasted like chicken haha. The nachos - The nachos were suggested by Justin himself who even after winning Star is still waiting the tables at his own restaurant which I thought was really cool. Â The "nachos" that came out were the strangest nachos I'd ever seen! Â They were really more like fried dumplings with gouda cheese inside and then covered in "nacho"-esk toppings. Â Regardless they were delicious! The shishito peppers - I'm still having day dreams about the peppers I had at Blue Ribbon in Vegas so I felt bad for this dish. Â I thought it was an interesting idea to serve the peppers plain and then provide different powders to dip them in but at the end of the day the sea salt grilled peppers at Blue Ribbon just blew these away. My final comment about the restaurant is that when it came to dessert, Justin very nonchalantly told us "We don't really do dessert. Â It's not our thing. Â We have assorted ice creams and serve a ice cream Snickers bar from the bodega down the street." Â My friend and I thought this was hilarious and ordered the Snickers. Â We started cracking up when it came cut in four pieces, still in the wrapper, topped with powdered sugar and a sliced strawberry. Â So hipster ironic haha. Â And it was delicious. Overall loved this place and would totally come back. Â After reading some other reviews I also learned that they have an outdoor area too so I may have to try that next time. Â I highly recommend you try it!
Fun place! Â Long wait, but there's a bar out front with good sapporo. When you're finally seated, the whole restaurant staff cheers! Â Get the pork dumplings and a noodle bowl, can't go wrong.

I really like Buttermilk Channel. Â The staff is very friendly, the food is good, the vibe is fun, and the place is lovely. I wasn't a big fan of their fried chicken. Â For me, it was just too dry and the skin was too crispy (and I love crispy skin). Â Actually, as pointed out by Dan T., the skin was "crunchy" rather than "crispy." Â The burger, on the other hand, is awesome. Â  It's a strait forward burger done perfectly - juicy, flavorful, and satisfying. Â One of my favorite burgers around. Â I really liked the oysters as well; they were super fresh and came with a grapefruit mignonette that provided the perfect amount of acidity to balance the brininess of the oysters. Brunch is also solid here. Â The pancakes and fried porkchop are delicious!

I declare Casa Mono my favorite restaurant in the whole world. No, I have not been to all countries and tasted all delicious morsels under the sun, but I will still make that declaration with full confidence. I have been going to Casa Mono for 2.5 years now, and each time has been more than satisfactory. We always start with the jamon iberico and pan con tomate, it's amazing how such simple dishes can burst with such full flavor. Another great simple dish they used to have was fried pimentos, crunchy with just the right amount of spiciness and greeness. Out of the 50 some odd dishes they have, I cannot possibly review every one. But I can say each was created with great care, from ingredient selection to balance of flavor, from razor clams to sweet bread, from array of colors to the aroma of each individual plate.., they all bring tears to my eyes with the perfection that's rare to find. I'd like to credit Batali but I secretly suspect it's Andy Nusser who's responsible for Casa Mono's greatness...

So nice to have a place like this at Queensboro Plaza! Â Queens and Paupers is definitely cozy. Â It's small, but feels warm and inviting and the staff is friendly. Â The food is solid and beats most of the other options in the area. Â It might not be worth a separate trip, but if you're in the neighborhood looking for a bite, Queens and Paupers will not disappoint.

The setup is really like a cafe/diner feel. Very compact and intimate. There are actually two rooms, one to eat and one to go. It probably can fit Â 20-30 people. With the decorations, music, and smell of the food you'll immediately feel like you're away from the concrete jungle but in some diner in Cuba. Anyone that has been here knows the atmosphere can't be beat! Beautiful & bubbly staff that are always a pleasure I recommend the cuban sandwich, a popular choice, as well as the molletes, which is bread topped with refried beans, melted cheese, and bits of chorizo. The food here can be very heavy, so don't try to eat the whole dish if you can't, and walk it off by walking around Soho. In short: Small place, big portions, nice service. Even better if you can avoid tables next to the bathroom. You will leave satisfied!

Absolutely superb! Â Never disappointed by the staff or the food. Â This is a crown jewel in Astoria's crown. Â Go see for yourself. Â Nothing overcooked, fresh veggies from Brooklyn Grange, wonderful wines in a quiet setting.
Huuuuge servings! I was stuffed AND brought home leftovers for lunch the next day. Friendly staff and delicious food. FREE DESSERT

Oh my - let me set the stage here - random Saturday afternoon and we opted to go wherever YELP led us. My husband insisted on Mexican, but we were wide open as to the actual location... SO - we mapped it out - and found Barrio Chino. Let's just say we're happy we did. I agree with most of the reviews here - TINY place and super-tiny tacos, so don't think you're going to leave here FULL without ordering some extra guac or boatloads of tasty margaritas. (That's what we did). I got the chicken tacos and YUM. Downright delicious... he ordered the fish tacos and we both indulged in Strawberry/Vanilla Margaritas and a Grapefruit Margarita. Not too shabby if I do say so. The seating arrangements can suck if you're not tucked in the back or sitting at the bar - but you've been warned!! If you don't mind - definitely indulge - this place is tasty and the service was perfect.

The wife and I live very close so we come here often when we're feeling too lazy to go elsewhere. Â I'm usually underwhelmed by the food but like the chill atmosphere and sparkling Wycliffe wine a lot. I've had the eggs bene which were decent and the roasted chicken and polenta which is just OK. Â The kale salad is actually very good and one of my main go-tos. Â The wife and I also enjoy the cheesecake which has a great flavor and a different, less-refined texture from other cheesecakes I've had and/or made. All in all, if you're looking for simple fare that's not mindblowing but solid, this is the spot.
The meal quality is so nice and the staff service also so quick with neat uniform and nice attitude so i am very glad and fully enjoying the meal and this environment.

Stop #3 on the NY Pizza taste test. They definitely don't lie that the line for this pizzeria gets loooong. Â We waited at least 35 minutes (which apparently is on the short end esp on a weekend). Â Too much cheese, not enough sauce and not enough crust (not to mention that it was burnt) isn't my kind of pizza.

Fatal mistake: going to a steak house not too hungry and having a friend who just joined me to keep me company. I couldn't order 7 course tasting, so instead, I ordered the lesso misto, which included Beef Short Rib, House-Made Cotechino, Chicken Thigh, and Veal Tongue in a stew. The portion was big and the flavor was nice, but it was not very memorable. However, I did enjoy the very attentive services here.

The entrance is deceiving. Â Inside was fabulous, trendy, modern. Â Food was delightful, drinks excellent. Â Crispy pork was great. Â Service excellent. Â Liked the vintage tableware. Â Great crowd. Â Fresh vegetables are a plus.

Great spot that I would no doubt go back too. I came for the burger and was left most impressed with the chicken lolipops. The meat came right off the bone and was perfectly cooked. The classic B&B Burger was truly classic.
Small shop that was sparsely populated when I visited at 12 on a Saturday. The tacos I ordered were decent. Next time I'll seek out a new place to try, as I feel I got a decent taste of this place.

Great catering & take out! I used Lincoln Station to cater a party this past weekend and everything turned out really well. Â We had awesome salads that would be great at any BBQ, the farro, kale and fennel salads were all big hits (for vegetarians and meat eaters alike!) Â The focaccia bread/pizzas were delicious (easy to share) and the roasted and fried chicken were all spot on. Â They even sent us a small bottle of house hot sauce to go! Â Very thoughtful. Â I would absolutely recommend this place to anyone looking to cater food for a BBQ - much easier than standing over the grill. Â (Side note: we also got some food catered from Dinosaur BBQ, which was good, but didn't compare to the food from Lincoln Station - much better attention to detail with the food!) I wish they offered delivery, but aside from that everything was great. Thanks so much for a great meal!

We went for an early dinner on a Friday night and while the service was spectacular I felt there was something lacking in the dishes we ordered. Â None of them wow-ed us. Â  We ordered the oysters and deviled eggs for starters. Â They oysters were good (baked with a spinach cheese topping?) but the deviled eggs were covered in what resembled the mayonnaise spicy sauce similar to what they put over sushi at low end sushi places. I thought the eggs would have been better without it. For mains we we had the chicken and waffles, the fried chicken plate, fried shrimp po'boy and red beans & rice with sausage. Â They used breaded chicken breast with the chicken and waffles dish (I was expecting proper fried chicken) and the waffles themselves were squishy and were even before they absorbed all the banana fosters syrup it was covered in. Â The other dishes lacked taste. Â My thought maybe they didn't put enough salt in the food, which might be why it was a bland for our palette. The sweet iced tea was actually the best part of the meal. The rave reviews I got from this place prior to our visit were from folks that came here for brunch, so maybe their brunch fare is better? Â For a great dinner though, I'd probably try somewhere else next time.

I was here a week ago. I'm Italian, born and raised, so my review might be a a little harsh. However, I know what outstanding Italian food is supposed to taste, and Bianca doesn't quite pull it off. Cash only, no reservations. Only wine by the bottle. Gnocchi fritti w stracchino: good, but really nothing special. Very ordinary. Fegatini (chicken liver): OUTSTANDING, so soft they melt in your mouth, especially the balsamic vinegar reduction. I'm not even a liver lover. Tagliolini frutti di mare: the pasta was fresh and perfectly cooked, but the sauce was bland and the seafood not fresh... quite rubbery. After what yelpers wrote about this dish, it was quite a disappointment. Lasagne: not the best I've ever had. Despite having a delicate texture, the sauce was pasty and not the freshest. Ricotta cheesecake: tasty but not delicious. Bottom line: definitely authentic cuisine, but just ok.

I wouldn't even bother writing a rave review because of the millions before me who have, but everyone always talks about the brunch, but i went for dinner and was equally pleased! the wait isn't as long at dinner so you still get the experience without the annoyance. 5 of us were seated in about 25 minutes. we ordered the hummus to start which was delicious (and i'm from the middle east so I would know..) and every one of us loved our entrees. Â I got the arugula salad with chicken meatballs and i will just say that we went to dinner about two weeks ago and i am still dreaming of this salad. it. was. perfect. beer was fantastic, too! overall, great place, cute decor, nice waitstaff. only deducted a star because i've always wanted to go for brunch but will refuse point-blank to wait for a table longer than i will be at the table

I don't really have a lot to add to the three hundred some-odd reviews that've already been posted. Lombardi's has a century of pizza-making expertise under their belt and the allegiance of countless devotees to vouch for their must-try delicacies! Any of their pizzas are good as-is. This is coming from someone who typically won't eat pizza unless it's missing the cheese, because I don't really like cheese. Not because of lactose-intolerance issues, but because I find it unappetizing. But the mozzarella has just the right amount of resistance to it, a simple, fresh milk taste that's out-of-this world. I can even stand the touch of sharp Pecorino Romano they add, well, because it gives a nice, salty kick to everything. Their perfectly thin crust is crisp on the outside, tender on the inside, yet still pliable and chewy. The sauce is robust and hearty while maintaining a light, herbal character. All in all, a well-rounded pizza, in form and in principle! The only thing I regret is that, since I was with a group each time I went, I could never order my beloved anchovies because of community objection. Such is life.

Once you enter this quaint little cafÃ©, you feel like you could easily be in Rome. Delicious coffee/espresso drinks pair nicely with an array of tasty paninis. If you're in the mood for something heavier, try the carbonara--one of the best I've tasted.
Not bad. Spicy Noodles are good, but I've had better. Good portions. Thai Ribs aren't bad, but not what you expect. Comes with lemon oil sauce thing. Good value here. Overall I'd say good.

I really want to give it a 4.5, but it won't let me. Anyways I went here for my birthday with my sister. We started out at the bar (of course) and one drink turned to two...which turned to three...which was a problem when we were finally seated and I couldn't read anymore. I tried foie gras for the first time here and it was amazing paired with the strawberry chutney on toast. It's probably the most rich, delicious thing I've ever eaten. For the entree I had a pulled pork sandwich. Usually I'd go with a heavier meat dish but It was an odd hour, like 4 pm or something, so I didn't want to be weighed down for the rest of the day. It was good, but not the best I've ever eaten. While the meat was cooked perfectly, it was lacking a little something. Maybe I'm just used to it with sauce in it? I could only eat half of it (because I was really full by then). One thing I really liked was that the decor was traditional and simple, and it didn't feel pretentious at all. I will definitely be back!

Arepas Cafe is a little hidden gem in Astoria, close enough to all the popular spots yet away from the foot traffic of some of the more crowded restaurants. You'll always be able to walk in and sit anywhere you'd like without waiting, especially now that they've extended the dining area. My ideal meal here is: - A pitcher of passion fruit sangria (yummy and potent) - An order of assorted mini empanadas - An arepa (either the Mami or Pabellon, the latter being really popular because it seems to have the most stuff in it, but you can always add more fillings to an arepa too) - And finishing it off with tres leche and cafe con leche (they claim to have the best - I would agree! In Queens, at least) for dessert And don't forget to throw their green sauce on everything! (except the dessert) I would avoid getting the chicha drink (their version of horchata) with your meal - it's like drinking a full glass of rice pudding and you won't have any room in your belly left for dessert. The sangria is the most expensive item of the meal, but if you skip it, you can easily find yourself with a $25 or less bill for two. Arepas Cafe is a lot cheaper than similar arepas places in the city, with quicker service too.

The first time I went with my girlfriend the place was super packed and had a 1.5 hour wait (Friday; 10PM). Saturday at around 11:30AM though, the wait was nice and short and the food lived up to the hype! Definitely try this place out.

Definitely enjoyed my buttermilk chicken sammich - chicken was delicious and hefty portions - could have stopped at half a sandwich, but come one - who does that... must try if you're in the area - will definitely be going back to try out the other sandwiches.

Took family members here who were visiting from out of town. Wanted badly for the food to be great, that's why i chose it. I had heard good things. The chicken and waffles, the waffles were burnt black. The burger's bun was so stale that we hit it with a fork and it was hard as a rock. This would be no big deal if it was a diner, but the burger is 16 bucks. On Â the plus side, the wine was good. But I wouldn't recommend this place. Prime Meats is up the street and very good. And there are tons of other great places to eat within blocks. Dissapointment.

Had an extremely pleasant experience at the Market Table for a private work event. The Pan Roasted Chicken with sweet potato salad, bok choy, and hazelnut brown butter is to DIE FOR!!! All my clients are still talking about it. Service is superb along with romantic ambience.

Ordered a sammie to work today, having never heard of this place before. Delivery was pretty fast, thank goodness, because I was shaking due to hunger. I got the veal meatball sammie and was surprised to see it fit in a small 6" box. For $10 (+tip)?! Boo, I should've gotten a Viet sammie and gotten more bang for my buck... However, it was a pretty good sammie. The sauce was tangy and the bread was still soft, which I like. I'm usually used to the hard baguettes Viet sammies come in that tend to make me believe that the roof of my mouth is bleeding with each bite. The meatballs were so-so, nothing really special, but the sauce and the cilantro really made it taste fresh. Just wish they were bigger!

Being partially vietnamese and from LA where there are tons of different banh mi stores, I was kind of skeptical at first about how great this place could be. Â I'm glad to say I was presently surprised! Â This is the most legit banh mi place I've found in NYC. Â I love the crispy baguettes & spicy jalapenos. Â  Only downside is that they close so early...6 PM doesn't give me enough time to get down to chinatown for my sandwich fix!

I took a few clients here for an early dinner on a Monday. Â We arrived around 5:45PM and had no trouble finding a table; however when we left at 7:15PM and it was packed along with a crowd waiting outside. The food and service were excellent. Â We had the New York strip and the lamb shank, which my taste-buds are still thanking me for. Great place for a first date ... I'll definitely come back here.

This place is so amazing that I have come here with three different people since moving to Sunset Park a few months ago, (twice in the last week!). I had never tried hot pot before, so it was a fun experience the first time I tried it. It gets packed on weekend nights, so I definitely recommend making a reservation. Â When you sit down, Â you first pick two broths. I have selected the pork marrow and the seafood tom yum each time and have yet to stray because they are both so incredibly delicious. My favorite things to cook are the homemade wontons (they come with a fresh noodle that is equally amazing), the live shrimp, beef brisket, fried tofu, and asparagus. The live shrimp is sort of a crazy dish because they come to you alive, in a closed jar, and you hear them jumping around. You take little tongs to put them in the broth to cook, and they jump around! The waiter can do it for you if you are squeamish, or you can get them 'drunken,' where they dump a ton of sake into the bowl before served so that they basically drown before getting to you. A little sad, if you think too much about it, but the dish is sort of an experience, it tastes great, and the flavor is enhances by the sake if you choose to go that route. I have not had hot pot from any other place, but I get the impression that this is the one that I will forever compare all others to. It is all so fresh, the selection is great, and the staff is very friendly. If you have any questions about how long to cook anything, they will happily take the time to explain everything. I highly recommend this place! Come with at least three people so that you can try a ton of different dishes.

Best corn ever !!!!!! You have been missing out if you've never tried the corn here. Every time I come here, I get the corn and cuban sandwich. Can't go wrong with it. I would give this place 5 stars just for their corn but I can't due to the size of the restaurant and service. It is so crowded in here. They will squeeze 4 people in a table thats meant to seat 2. It's so uncomfortable. You're literally eating on top of one another. Their service isn't the best either!!! My girls and I were waiting for a table of 4 and the lady said it will be about a half hour wait. We were outside waiting and all of a sudden another group of 4 people comes in and she seats them first. We looked at her and she had a guilty look on her face but didn't even bother to explain to us. We ended up leaving. They do have a take out store next door. Order the corn and sandwich there !
