The best chickens wings that I 've ever try.... out of this world.The Chef is amazing and very polite and I had a wonderful time.I will definitely recommend the place,food and good dj Happy New 2015!!!!!
this place is phenomenal spot for brunch !! the duck hash is the best, tastes like thanksgiving!!!
ITALIANO!! If you have a group of people, go to Carmines & you'll know what it means to be Italian!

I've been to Cafe Katja twice now. I love the ambiance and the service has always been great. Had the same server each time (reckon she's an owner). I look forward to Â trying the schnitzel next time and washing it down with an always refreshing Stiegl Bier. Last but definitely not least, they have the best selection of "real" schnapps I've come across in NYC. After my next visit I may have to bump them to 5 stars.

I've been here 10 years ago, and it is still maintained its excellence after all these years. The duck soba is always the one to try. Soba is made in house. Everything every is made the old school way, which is getting hard to find these days. Best part is there is no ridiculous wait here and the price is moderate.
Delicious!
Delicious food! Cannot wait to come back with my friends and family. It is a bit pricey, but it is worth coming! Great for brunches and dinners.

A total cool place with great atmosphere. I got to the restaurant a bit before 6pm and within a half hour the place was totally happening. Rock star chef Jonathan Waxman and famous for the fire roasted chicken. Everything on the menu seemed to hit the just right food note. Quality, portion and presentation. the desserts were delicious, too. Super cool garage like industrial loft setting with outdoor eating in Meatpacking packing full of locals with a young sexy vibe. 10 for food and vibe!

Thankfully we had reservations - we showed up early and could not be seated until our time as the restaurant was packed. Chicken Parmesan was the largest serving I have ever seen and it was excellent. Pizza was terrific. Service was great and the price was right. A very small tightly packed restaurant with lots of conversation so do not expect an intinate evening but the food was fantastic.

stopped by here for lunch - what a gem hole-in-the-wall! delicious food, simple menu, no frills good grub! I had the peril pork over yellow rice. the small plate was more than enough to fill me up and then some! my BF had the chicken. the meat was very tender and flavorful and very reminiscent of my childhood mom-and-pop local food stalls where you run in to grab your lunch or after work meal and rush off back to work or to home. my only criticism is that the meat might have slightly been on the dry side, but the flavor certainly makes up for it!
ramen is always so good. But desert is nothing special. Generally I think ippudo is one of the best ramen places in NYC, except the long line all the time.

Went solo for lunch, so sat at the bar. Their lunch special is fantastic value so gave that a whirl. Started with their famous pork buns. Three months later, I still think about those amazing pillow like buns surrounding the sweet, rich salty pork belly that gave me a heart attack just looking at it. So good. Main was a very passable lamb dish. The details escape me, but it looked good enough for the celeb sitting next to me (you know, the brother from My Name Is Earl) to look over and ask what it was. He was living vicariously though my meal as he just had a plate of pickles for lunch ("I can't eat meat - what would you recommend?"). I mean, seriously, pickles!!? Dessert actually blew me away. The apricot sorbet and thyme mousse was a total surprise. The presentation reminded me of wd-50, but the flavour was truly unique. Bravo.

i ate here last night after figuring out im in the mood for a japanese ramen. came in a narrow entrance filled with kitchen and the girl sat us in the corner. the place was very small and decent.. I ordered some of their home made gyoza which are of an average taste and gave ourselves more time to think which broth to get (pork, pork&chicken or miso) under each broth you get to choose two flavors (soy sauce or salt & garlic.) the ramen was hard but edible and was topped with scallions, seaweed, egg & salty pork. to end it short... the girl suggested i get the minca salt & garlic ramen which pretty much sum up everything... it is really salty and too much garlic.. never even finished it hafway. my bf ordered spicy miso ramen which did not taste miso at all. i would not come back, so much better ramen houses out there.

My friend declared that we HAD to go to Grimaldi's before I left New York, so we cabbed it on down to Brooklyn to get our pizza on. Â It was the end of a long day, I was exhausted, sweaty (it had been like, 85 degrees all weekend), and not even feeling particularly hungry. Â Standing in a long line outside the restaurant definitely did not appeal to me. Â But once we made it inside, the aroma of freshly-baked pizza hit my nostrils and I instantly perked up! Â The crust was thin and crispy and the toppings were of excellent quality. Was it worth waiting in line for half an hour? Â Er...that all depends on how hungry you are.

Haven't been here for the sandwiches yet. They do look mighty tasty though. Â Might have to give in eventually and split one with somebody. Â So I've only been here for the happy hour. Â The happy hour was surprisingly good. Â They have very good drink specials and the waitresses were very nice and attentive. Â I did go on an off night though. Â I imagine it gets a little more crowded and crazy during a busier night. Â Still I had a good time and it was very pleasant so I will be back.
truly the best katsu curry in new york city. and with the baseball themed menu? perfection. can't get better katsu cutlets and savory addicting curry anywhere else in nyc.

Found this place on yelp. Food was fantastic! We had spinach & ricotta ravioli, and the gnocchi (both handmade pastas in house). Â It was top 3 ravioli experience for me based on freshness of spinach flavor and richness of the cheese. The red sauce was perfect! My husband raved about the gnocchi. Service and atmosphere were great. Â PT will definitely become a regular spot for us!

I've been here for brunch and lunch. The food is decent. For me, the best part was the bread - the biscuits that came with brunch and the bread with olive oil. Got the kale omelette which could use more goat cheese. The turkey burger I had gotten for lunch was not good. Service at brunch was slow. Couldn't find our waitress anywhere.

Ate here for a birthday with my boyfriend and family. We tried quite a few things. Everything was extremely fresh and it all tasted delicious. The fish taco is to die for. Comes with a beautiful blue tortilla. Even the quesadilla tortilla is homemade. I recommend the garlic shrimp as well. Nothing like homemade food that actually tastes good. Also, the decor is very clean and simple. I will certainly be back!

Bubby's is delicious! I've had their fried chicken, eggs benedict, blueberry pancakes and huevos rancheros (on separate occasions, people!) and loved them all. As far as prices go, I guess it's a bit on the expensive side for brunch... but isn't this Manhattan? You're getting great food, a fun atmosphere and friendly people... I think it's reasonable. The only downside is the wait time... if you go during normal brunch hours on a weekend, expect an hour or more. My suggestion is to go late-night after some quality partying, since they're open all night long. Nothing better than blueberry pancakes at 4 am!

Fantastic ambiance, amazingly cute staff, literally transports you back to Paris. Croque Monsieur - this is a complete yes. As someone who doesn't even like ham, this one works. It's very unoffensive, thinly shaved, good quality. The bread is super crusty on the outside, soft on the inside. Cheese is melted on top in a non-oily soppy greasy way. Bechamel sauce keeps it moist. It's expensive, but you actually get a really good portion (2 sandwiches) and it's a pretty substantial sandwich, so you don't need more. Servers are attentive and refill waters all the time.

At long last an Italian restaurant in Sunset Park. Food is tasty and freshly made and they obviously care about quality. Prices are reasonable and it's BYOB if you want wine with dinner. Brian and Randy are friendly and accomodating. We've eaten there several times and never been disappointed.

In this area it's hard to find a good restaurant! Â Came here for a client lunch...we loved it. Â Quinoa salad to start, followed by the salmon. Â Delicious. Â Simple, cozy spot. Great service, excellent food. Â Next time I'll be returning for dinner, steak and some Malbac!

This place is amazing! Came here with friend that lives in Astoria. The place was packed!!! We waited 30 min to be seated. Food is soooooo good. So fresh and delicious! Prices are very reasonable. Recommend this place to anyone who loves Greek food!

I was so mad that a curry joint opened up after I moved away from the area. I thought it would be something like Curry House in Hawaii. The rice and curry tasted like it had been sitting around too long, but it was almost closing time. The katsu was perfectly crisp, though. Yum! You have to order the pickles that normally come included with this type of dish. I wish I read the reviews before coming here so I would've known this place is cash only. We had to walk to a little corner store to use the ATM where an old Korean man and some drunk Latin guys were getting in an argument and on the verge of physically fighting. :( I prefer Curry House, but Go Go Curry is definitely more accessible! I can see myself coming back here for guilty fast food fix.

Risotteria is probably my favorite restaurant in New York, not because it's the best one out there, but because they do what I feel is the best job of catering to those of us who can't eat wheat, without isolating all of those people who like to tell me that they'd "die if they couldn't eat bread." The restaurant itself is fairly small, and if you're going in a group of more than two, I'd be prepared for a wait unless you're there at an off hour. They'll sometimes give you free breadsticks while you wait, which is nice, mostly because the breadsticks are one of my favorite parts of the meal. The pizzas and risottos are my favorites. I've tried the paninis, but they seem to be the one thing that might be better on regular (non-GF bread). Desserts are great, and all are gluten free. The chocolate chip and black and white cookies are my personal favorites, and when the restaurant was on my walk home, it used to take quite a bit of self-control not to go in for a cookie every single day. (Especially because they'd occasionally give them to me for free.) I've never been here with someone else on a gluten-free diet, and everyone always wants to go back. I wind up here a lot, not only because I happen to like it, but I have friends who like it so much they've taken to suggesting it on their own. Side note: it's an off-menu item most of the time, but if you ask nicely they'll make you meatball pizza, which is one of my favorite things to get there.

Such an awesome place in NYC - the New Yorkers are spoiled to have this gem in their midst! We got in and the place was mobbed - people everywhere - shopping, scouting for a seat at one of the mini restaurants or bars, drinking...just people everywhere. The market areas - they have a large cheese and charcuterie section, produce, fresh pasta, bread, dessert...everything and it is just like Mario Batali - legit! We managed to get a seat at one of the bars and ordered the cheese and charcuterie plate (and wine if course) and it was amazing. The fresh made ricotta was outstanding - so outstanding that I looked up the recipe and plan to make it and pair it with honey and almonds - just how it was there. Stop in and check this place out - it makes you want to move to Italy...or Eataly. :-)

4.5 stars. Food was delicious. Shared about or 8 dishes with the guys. Drank a lot too. Highlight for me was getting the whole fried pig's head. The Filipino heritage in me kicks in and I went to town on it so that there was nothing left but a skeletal head. Hahahaha. Met the head chef Ilan at the end of the meal. Really cool guy. Love the concept of the food here and the space is really cool.

I've been going to Cafeteria for brunch since 2003 so I have lots of good memories of the place. Â Service is consistently bad and the bevy of hostesses consistently have attitude, but I still go there! Â It's conveniently located and I like their brunch menu. Â I think that I first fell in love with florentine eggs benedict because I ate it first at Cafeteria. Â Sadly, they don't offer this item anymore, but Cafeteria's was my first love. Their famous mac & cheese has expanded beyond the basic to include 2 other versions - and you can get all 3 in a mac sampler. Â They're all good, but the original is still the best unless you really like truffle oil. Beyond brunch and mac, they also have a really greasy yet amazingly tasty Cafeteria burger. Â It's seasoned well, super juicy, and served on a chewy bun that doesn't fall apart when you eat it. Â The fries that come with it are also seasoned very well.

Came here last week with Ben T. and Jaime C. Â They've both summed up our experience perfectly. Â So, I will use (a part of) this review to express my ANGER towards that table of girls (YOU KNOW WHO YOU ARE) who were like.. oh yeah, i see you standing there waiting with your coats on, drooling at the sight and smell of delicious carnitas plates everywhere. Â Yeah, I see you, I'm making eye contact with you, but I'm just going to just sit here and text everybody I know for the next 55 minutes after I've gotten and paid my check... HELLO?? SOMEONE AT LEAST GIVE THESE GIRLS A HINT!! Â Yeah, no help in that area from the host or waiteress... That said, the host and waitress were super extra nice once we got seated. Â They comped us with a free appetizer and two free desserts because we stood waiting for almost two hours, and missed the 8pm 1/2 off tapas deal. They also moved us to a bigger table, once it started to clear up a bit. Â AND they split our bill onto three separate credit cards, without any fuss Also, it would be a disgrace to meat platters everywhere if I didn't describe the carnitas plate. Â So here goes... three tender fatty juicy ribs, three slices of steak, three slices of juicy sausage, one long link of lamb sausage, one pile of perfectly seasoned chicken, a plate of rice and beans, a plate piled high with some of the BEST yuca fries ever, one over filled cup of pickled veggies. Â Total price: $39. Â No, you didn't read that incorrectly. Â Yes, I typed thirty nine dollars. Â Now the question becomes: What are you waiting for??? Oh and yes, we all applauded and cheered when that group of girls finally decided to get up and leave. Â haha, sassy for life.

the best , im a regular at bayou , i love how they carry microbrews like abita , the food is good , i love creole susi , and the pumpkin soup! te decor is silly and inviting its an overall great place to go , they ahve pyscic nights and blues and jazz bands that play weekly .
The lobster feast is very good, whole lobster plus steamed clams, corn on the cob, and fries for $23

if you're reading this and not sure about going to palo santo: just go. it's amazing. the tortilla/avocado appetizer (which is part of the surprising affordable $27 three-course pre-fixe dinner available 7 nights a week) is ridiculous. you'll be wondering for weeks how they gussied up that simple avocado to such crazy deliciousness. and the tortillas. words cannot do it justice. the vibe is just right- intimate, cozy and totally laid-back.

Good food, poor service. I went in with my friend tonight and got seated by the door. Since it's a bit chilly, I asked the waitress if we can switch table. I got "no" even though there was one other empty table. They told me that they have to make a larger table for 11 later. However, as time passed, they just gave tables to whoever came in of that that larger seating without moving us to one of them. Sorry, I can't accept this kind of service.

I constantly feel judged here. When I come with my family, who all speak French fluently (yes, I'm the black sheep) we are part of the gang, and receive wonderful, friendly service. When I've come with other friends, I feel half ignored. The food is pretty good, but not mindblowing. Being that the owner is from Paris (or nearby) you can definitely get the French vibe. If you like the slightly arrogant demeanor and small portions of a true French restaurant, then you'll love this place. I also wanted to comment that I was a bit disappointed that they did not allow me to make any substitutions on the vegetables I wanted in my crepe, which I found strange. For my future crepe fix, I'm heading to Shade in the Village.

first, why does YELP classify this as an italian restaurant? confused. just had a late lunch there today, i do love this place for its energy and look and feel and food and wine selection. not the fastest service but i am ok with that as long as the bread basket is full. i have had nothing but great times here at this place but something keeps me from giving it a flat out five stars. not sure what, will have to noodle on it and maybe revisit later.

Grimaldi's is well served by their PR person - while the pizza is good, the wait isn't. Â This is Brooklyn, and it's hard to throw a rock in any direction without hitting a pizzeria that serves pizza (and more) that is not less than equal to Grimaldi's but without the wait...Come to Bensonhurst or Gravesend...
Have the BLT. You know you want to, and you are thinking 'boring... I should order something Exciting'. Stop. Order the BLT. Best meal I've had in the village.
we ordered this in at my old office, it was really delish. Â fresh everything! Â unique. Â if you love pizza, it is worth going out of your way for.

As most people have said here, it's grilled cheese. Â It shouldn't be $8. Â  BUT, it is VERY good grilled cheese. Â  Tater tots were not that great....sauce was actually pretty bland as well (ketchup and mayo?). Â  I go here for lunch every now and then.....I try to switch up what I get. Â I haven't had anything bad here at all, but the prices are pretty high for what it is. Â  PS- Tomato soup was actually pretty watery and not that great when I had it. Â Haven't had it since that first time. Â  Want a good grilled cheese? Go here. Â Don't have 8 bucks for it? Â Go inside to the food court next door and get something cheaper.

Came here on a super rainy night after a long day of work at a forum in Manhattan. My friend and I drove over for dinner after finding this place on the Y. My friend was hell-bent on Brooklyn, Brooklyn, Brooklyn! It was shortly before Halloween, so even though it was dumping rain, we enjoyed checking out the hood's decorations as we walked from our parking spot on the street to the resto. Quiet night -we had a reservation but it was late and there were only 2 other parties there, but there was a festive air in the joint. We started with Prosecco and bruschetta -oh MY, that bruscetta was delicious. The bread crunchy toastiness coupled with some meaty prociutto and fig jam was amazing. We also shared a Brussels sprouts salad and then... then, came the amazing, incredible bolognese della nonna. We had it with fettucine, which we ordered upon the recommendation of the lovely server, as the fettucine is made in house. Oh, so delicious. The sauce, the gentle firmness of the pasta. I would absolutely, totally go back here again. A delight!

Great food on a rainy cold day! I had the sweet and sour calamari and duck ramen. Both were really good, but I'd have to say the calamari is better. The duck ramen only had three pieces of duck, which was a little disappointing, but the flavour made up for it! The service was really good as well. Overall I'd say this place is a very good value !

Great little Mexican brunch place in the West Village. The fish tacos were outstanding! You get 3 tacos and I ordered 2 with fried fish and 1 grilled. Obviously, the fried was better but the grilled was also yummy. Also had a Michelada....so good!! Note: My friend had the Mexican Eggs Benedict and while it sounded delish conceptually, it was just ok (but not bad); the sauce was thick/heavy and slightly sweet so not what you expect when you think of Eggs Benedict.
We ate some fantastic soul food here. The fried chicken with mashed potatoes were well worth the adventure to get there. Here is our video review of the restaurant. youtu.be/DVFryb8mL04?t=2â€¦

Didn't like it. IT'S NOT AUTHENTIC, IF YOU THINK IT'S AUTHENTIC, YOU'VE NOT TASTED REAL SPANISH CUISINE, PROMISE. And it's such a tease being named for the famous Boqueria market in Barcelona, which is something truly amazing. It's hard to give this place a bad review, but I honestly wasn't impressed. If I didn't know authentic Spanish food, I might give it a 5, but I just can't. Enjoying this place depends on what you're looking for. If you're looking for Authentic Spanish tapas go to the eponymous, Spain on 13th and 6th. That's real Spanish cuisine. If you're looking for a trendy, chic NY/euro vibe in a hip neighborhood with a an 'ethnic' vibe (aka a flamenco playlist) go to Boqueria. Pros: Ambience, location, good prices for Soho, friendly staff, "cool" menu, I guess. Cons (to me): didn't taste authentic, didn't seem authentic, generic NY restaurant group chic, you can get that all over Manhattan. I don't want to throw this place under the bus, because it's a NICE restaurant, I just won't go back because I LOVE Spanish food. (And the tapa didn't even come with the drink, at Spain on 13th, it does, because that's traditional). The 'salsa brava' was tasteless (all I tasted was tomatoes and not the 'brava'). Idk, I just didn't like it. Soho might not be friendly to old world Euro charm, so maybe it's just a more 'new' Catalan that doesn't fit my taste buds.

The storefront is pretty small, so it's super easy to miss when you're walking by. In fact, I had no idea this place existed for the longest time even though I walked by it literally everyday. One day, I happened to glance inside and noticed the adorable, very hip vibe and immediately made Sunday brunch reservations that same weekend with my roommate. Brunch certainly did not disappoint. I absolutely adore the atmosphere of Feast, it reminds you a hipster, countryside-style kitchen with mason jars for water glasses and all wood everything. Loved that they have a set platter of breakfast appetizers with small samples of yogurt, pastries, and more. For my plate, I got a Lemon Souffle Pancake that was actually ginormous and I couldn't finish. The texture was on point -- very fluffy and light, and also not too sweet. The only complaint I could possibly have about this place is the service, which was kinda slow. Also, we were only 5 minutes late for our reservation, but the hostess at the front was not pleased and told us that we had to get out of there in time for the next table at 1 pm...um okay? Whatever, the food was worth it. So basically, in conclusion: Ambience = absolutely 5 stars Food = 4.5 stars Service = 3 stars

I love this place. In fact I cant stop thinking about it. The only thing I would change is that they don't have a cocktail menu, but the wines we chose were wonderful. Â My husband and I got the sardines ( amazing) side of bacon and cauliflower the haloumi salad and we split a steak. Next time I am getting my own steak! I could have eaten 2 and there was a lot of food. I wanted to order more. It was an incredible incredible experience. The only thing that was EGH was the pot de creme for dessert and it was still delicious. I am trying to get myself back there asap!!!!!!

went again, and everything was just like i remembered it. good food. my favorite are those shrimp in butter sauce/white wine. empanadas were great too. tried the calamari and it was a fail. it was really greasy and the oil was literally visible on the batter that didn't seem to stick to the rings. felt like you were just eating grease. they took them off my bill for me without any issues. great custoemr service. the sangria was good. can't say it was really strong but the pitcher they had was worth the deal. a glass was $7 i think and the pitcher was $15 so made more since to get the pitcher, but i did not feel wasted at all. the place is really really small so not sure how people actually get to come here during busy times. maybe you have to make a reservation. not sure. however, when i have been here it has not been very busy. the people that work there aren't necessarily the friendliest people in the world. basically they are short on smiles and just serve you your food and take your orders. so if you are expecting a friendly staff environment, this is not the place. they are not rude at all, but they are just working there. so if you want a place where you can just hang with friends or a date or whatever and not be bothered by some waiter or waitress that used to work at TGIF Fridays with the "fake" happy happy joy joy persona, then, this is the place. If you like the happy happy joy joy service, ummmmm, it aint happening here. good food. cool drinks and great as a pre-game place before going to the Village Underground.

Highly recommend this restaurant. Hanger steak, Filet Mignon, Escargot, Mussels... SOOOO GOOD It's a bit small and the waitress aren't as friendly, also cash only, but the quality is definitely well worth it They could use a lil brighter lighting in the restaurant as well

- service was adorable and so friendly - the blue cheese/bacon salad was yummy and big - shrimp crepe was also delicious - banana nutella dessert crepe was very good as it usually is but my favorite of all was the appetizer sampler... the olive spread was to DIE FOR and the fried chick pea (???) was delicious as well. can't wait to go back!

Amazing dinner and so glad we were able to get a reservation. Sure our reservation was at 5pm on a Saturday but it actually worked to our advantage and all the early reservations got the nice comfy corner seats. The restaurant has a nice vibe and service was attentive but not overpowering. To start I had the chicken liver mousse and my husband had the creamy tomato soup and grilled cheese. Â My mousse was a pretty large portion for just one person and was meant to be shared, but I had to try it and I ate it all up. It was perfectly creamy and smooth and seasoned so perfectly. I was practically licking the jar at the end. For our entrees, I got the burger and the hubby had he skirt steak. The burger was amazing and though I have heard about people complaining of the size, I had no issue with it. I loved the sweet maple bacon and the cheese and egg just completed the burger perfectly. The fries were tasty as well and seasoned just right. I took my husbands bone marrow bearnaise and it was great with the fries. His steak looked good and I was way too stuffed to try it but I do think it came a bit too rare considering he ordered it medium. For dessert we had the cinnamon sugar donuts and they were served warm and with a few sauces. I am a fan of all things dipping but I really didn't enjoy any of the offerings. Good thing was that the donut was perfect without it. A bit crispy on the outside and chewy and doughy on the inside. Oh how I would love to have those in the morning with a nice cup of coffee! Overall it was a wonderful dinner all around and I would definitely recommend it for a nice date night or for a small group of friends!

Came here for dinner last night for the first time and absolutely loved it. Â The space and food reminded me a lot of one of my other favorite restaurants, David Burke Kitchen. the basil focaccia was veey fresh. Â I tried the fried oysters, pork and rabbit terrine, anchovies with quinoa, and burrata as apps. For my main I had the pork loin with pork belly. Â Everything was fantastic, with the oysters being my favorite, followed by the terrine. Â I could've done without the burrata. Â I've had better elsewhere and didn't think it was that great.. Â Overall, we had a fantastic meal here and will definitely come back.
So much hype for pizza that is just, okay.

SO GOOD. A bit out of the way, and perhaps a little pricey for the atmosphere, but totally delicious. Brisket/ribs/other goodness by the lb, awesome sides. At the time it was still BYOB so we got a six of SBock on the way in to make the whole thing legit. I think that was on the outs though. Brisket was just perfect. Perfect. Will totally be back.
Perfection! All of the food is divine. I love the tie die pizza and the ravioli! I have had a few different salads, all of which were wonderful. Probably my favorite restaurant in NYC.

Two Words: onion gratinee (also known as french onion soup in amer-i-cuh) This soup was AMAZING! I passed it around the table at our friends birthday dinner and I thought that someone may cast a furtive glance and dash off with the bowl. It was adored by all. I also had the coq au vin. Spectacular as well. The meat fell right off the bone and the mashed potatoes were a fluffy, buttery little piece of heaven. I don't even have words for the bread pudding. I'm sure all of you have been to dinner and shared desserts and no one wants to be the person to eat the last few bites. Not this time my friends. Every crumb, morsel, and mushy goodness was gone. And then we all cried. The ambiance is spectacular. It feels like a little slice of paris (except a zillion times larger than any restaurant I've ever been in and smoking isn't allowed). Jacques Brel, dim lighting, and charm everywhere. Everyone thoroughly enjoyed their dinner. While I am not sure if I would make a trip out from Manhattan solely for the purpose of trying this restaurant, if you live or happen to be in Williamsburg you should definitely stop in when you are feeling francophile-ish.

Their tacos are amazing -- best fish taco I've ever had. Great atmosphere, great service -- the fact that they're a little off the beaten path is a plus, because if they weren't they'd be insanely crowded.

Does brunch really taste better after a ridiculously long wait time? Not to me! Good thing the wait here isn't bad, unlike some other brunch joints. On a saturday at 1pm, expect a 20 minute wait. Brunch is always leaves me feeling helpless when I have to decide between a savory or sweet entree. Which ever one I pick, my wandering eyes will make me regret my decision. A true first world problem. But this time I let myself have both - the soup of the day (potato leek) and a mango & melon waffle. Gosh that was a good waffle. I was satifisied and my eyes faithfully stayed on my own plate the whole meal.
go early and get the corn and the frozen mojitos.

Reliable, trendy, romantic, casual, formal... good for business, a date, or friends... The Smith is everything you want it to be and then some. Anything you order off the menu is guaranteed to be great. It's always packed, lively. Good scene for people watching, a lot of attractive people hang out in here. Favorite drinks: Sauvignon Blanc by the liter, East Village Passion cocktail, Moscow Mule Favorite apps: Burratta, Mussels, Calamari
we love empanadas from here we have tried all the flavors

Don't let the line deter you from Tom's. Â It's well worth the wait, especially since it moves pretty quickly. Â For two people, we only waited about 10 minutes. Â  Tom's was exactly what I was hoping for- just a simple diner with good breakfast and lunch options. Â Their breakfast items sounded good, and they have a ton of omlettes, but I was looking for a sandwich. Â Tried the brisket with gravy on the side. Â My friend had the turkey club with french fries and we got a side of cole slaw. Â The cole slaw was refreshing and really good- not too mayo-ey. Â The brisket is lean so a bit on the dry side. Â Spooning some gravy on it moistened it up nicely. Â The turkey club was your average good turkey club. Â Their fries are good, especially when you dip them in their special chipotle tasting like spicy mayo sauce! Â  If I could give an extra half star for service, I would. Â They are SO sweet there. Â Fast, efficient, but NICE. Â I asked the waiter what this Cherry Lime Ricky was that everyone raves about, and he described it as Sprite with Shirley Temple syrup, which did not sound appetizing to me, so I declined. Â But he was nice enough to bring both of us a glass of it to try on the house, and it tasted much better than I thought it would! Â  Overall, solid place to go for a cheap, filling, friendly diner.

This is our favorite spot in Park Slope. Â A real neighborhood gem with a constantly changing menu that's always interesting. Â  The service is great. Â Very warm and professional. Â And they clearly put a ton of thought and time into the decor. Â It's funky and interesting, without being distracting. Sit in the back room if there's space, and if they have the coffee creme brulee, definitely get it.

This place is kinda touristy, we realized when we got there. The prices are fairly high (ex..$16 for a small pizza?) and ONE bathroom.... lol. Pizza's good though, not disappointing at least. We ordered a Thin Crust with extra cheese, pepperoni, onions & pancetta... yummm! Not a must, but not bad either. I'm sure we could've found pizza in NY equally tasty for less $$.

Absolutely the best under $10 meal with meat you can get anywhere in NYC, hands down!!! Make sure you go to the one on West corner of 53rd & 6th Ave. For $6 (plus $1 if you want a water/soda) you can get a full meal, actually enough for 2 people. I have yet to down the Rice and Lamb/Chicken platter in one sitting (... though I'm sure it can be done). Yes there is a line (20-40 min pretty much all of the time from Noon to 5am), but it'stotally worth the wait...If you're new to the street vendors in NYC or you just want a filling super-late nite food treat This is THE Place to go! Plus it's Halal (similar concept as Kosher). I recommend the 1/2 Lamb & 1/2 chicken platter over rice with some pieces of pita bread & lettuce salad! Load-up on the white sauce, be very careful with the volcanic red hot sauce though, especially if spicy is not your thing. Grab & go for a picnic to go in Central Park!!! WARNING: Can be addictive & habit forming...Used to going here weekly in the summers, after a late nite out, turned into a lunch fix too.

One of these little piece of heaven that I'm glad I was introduced to! One of my friends brought me there saying it was the best falafel sandwich he ever had. Well ... I would say that was the best ever, but regarding the quality to price ratio that place is definitely unbeatable! A very tasty falalel sandwich for only $2.50 served prepared in a minute and served with a smile: What more can we ask? I have yet to try the other items on the menu, but I would definitely recommend it!
Best eggs i EVER had!!! YUMMM

Have been back many, many times, with groups and dates and just for a drink at the bar. Service is universally pleasant, food well prepared, hot, and flavorful, drinks generous, late night happy hour appreciated. Only thought is price point on food is high for portion size, but quality is correspondingly high, and the value conscious can restrict themselves to small plates and gorge on hamburgers somewhere else. My guess is that you will feel welcome here and enjoy yourself.

A lovely new restaurant in the east village with a warm staff, fresh food, and casual ambience. The prices are reasonable and the beer and wine are local. Found this place by accident, but we will certainly be back!

I shouldn't have gone with my underage god-sister because the point of this cute LES place was to enjoy wine and nibble on the food but I didn't get to do much of the first part. The second part, however, I fulfilled. Our wonderful waitress, who kept an eye on us the entire time, recommended the Popeye quiche. In addition, we tried the Anna salad (beets! walnuts! blue cheese!) and my favorite, the Escargot (mmmmm...I can't get enough of these buttery snails). Dipping the bread into the Escargot juices was so sinfully delicious. Will definitely be back with the boy for a rustically romantic but casual date.

Don't let the B rating and the hole in the wall type place this is discourage you from coming in. The boiled dumplings are some of the best I have had. Nicely thin wrapper and juicy flavorful filling, everything you would want in a dumpling. I had the dry noodles with minced pork sauce and it almost reminded me of a chinese version of spaghetti with meat sauce. They were generous with the pork and the flavors were quite nice. I only wish that the noodles were a bit firmer. Overall it is a good place for lunch and you even get to see them make the noodles and dumplings while you sit and eat. I like the knife cut noodles at Tasty Hand Pulled Noodles more because of their texture, but this is definitely a solid option as well!

I came here two years ago, and I'm still thinking about those ricotta pancakes I had. Â We came here for brunch on a Sunday and it was jampacked, but we still managed to get seating outside in about 30 minutes. Â Only thing I didn't like about the outdoor seating is that it's a small area, and we were seated by the takeout window where a lot of people were standing by and we were located by the trash can.

Went here on an early Sunday evening. We were promptly seated. Â Service was slow, it took them about 15 mins to take our order. Â We ordered 2 apps and 2 entrees which the entrees came out almost immediately after the entrees. Â No time to breathe at all. We ordered the Spinach dumplings and Golden Triangle?(Ground shrimp and chicken inside a fried wonton). Â Both were decent and i've had better. Â Note, there were 2 of us and ONE appetizer is more than enough. For entrees, we ordered the basic. Â Myself, the Shrimp Pad Thai, and my wife ordered the Pad See Ew. Â The Pad Thai was OK, I was excited about what Yelpers said but I found it slightly disappointing. Â It was too tangy, too acidic and not sweet enough. Â The noodles were cooked well though. My wife thought that the Pad See Ew was good, very light sauce and tasty. Â I also ordered the Thai Iced Tea which was delicious and refreshing. We liked the atmosphere and will return for a pre-going out meal. Â It seems more like a trendy lounge with Thai food than a Thai restaurant.

My work colleagues and I went here for lunch. We were sat right away which was nice because we showed up at 12:30 in the middle of the lunch rush. The pasta was very good and reasonably priced. The pizza looked really good and will be on the list for next time we go.

First of all, it took over half an hour for our first course to come out, and when we got it, we were underwhelmed to say the least. Â The half avocado was good (as good as any fresh, ripe avocado is) and so were the 5 3" tortillas (homemade corn), but really didn't think it was worth $7 for the portion. Â The duck soup had a layer of grease on top and was really unappetizing. Â After another half an hour wait for the main course, (at this point we were all starving) my ribeye was so chewy and tough, it was completely inedible (literally had to spit it back out onto the plate)... the yuca was the only good thing on the plate. Â The rack of boar was decent, but unmemorable. Â Overall, this place was a complete letdown.

OMG. This place is basically serving crack. The honey chicken biscuit is worth giving up your first born for. (I added extra honey - DO IT). The brisket is kick-ass as well. So tender and tasty. Don't even think about skipping dessert either. I would love it if someone threw one of these pies in my face. The cinnamon ice-cream is surprisingly delicious. The staff is a bit jaded - but I don't blame them. They're constantly slammed and serving a bunch of hipsters in Williamsburg.

Strolled by this place on a Sunday night and walked in because we saw that the restau was nearly full with people, and that the Yelp reviews were good. We were seated immediately, but I suspect that Meme has a wait on typically busier nights like Friday and Saturday. Loved that the food was relatively healthy yet delicious. I especially liked the octopus and fennel salad! The bite-sized bits of octopus were tender and tasty - a pleasure to eat. We also got the combo platter, which was a generous selection of green falafel, babaganoush, hummus, tabouli, beets, spiced carrots, and soft pita triangles. Everything was fresh, healthy, and delicious. Last of all, we got the merguez sausage that came with salad and hummus. The merguez is a spiced lamb sausage, and had a slight liver-y taste to it that we did not love, but that is subject to personal taste. Meme's a great option for a trendy, relaxed Mediterranean meal.

Had a great brunch here during the holidays. I sat at the bar, ate and drank until I was full. Service and staff were very nice; the food was very good. Average price for this part of town, diners should expect a better than average experience.

there is SO MUCH HYPE about this place, it's kinda crazy. i've had it a few times over the last few years and although its good - don't get me wrong - its certainly not my favorite place in the city. anyway, now that thats aside, lets get to the food - ive had the chicken & rice as well as the chicken/lamb & rice - both are great, don't think you can go wrong with either. they essentially mince up the meat so it all kinda ends up tasting similar anyway. comes with sauces - ones like a ranch and the other is SUPER SPICY! this is really what i love about the dish! i def ask for extra, because you get a LOT of food and one packet of each wont suffice. its also REALLY cheap - $6 and it lasted me 2 meals, though doesnt taste as great the next day when its cold.

Expensive and crowded but always reliably tasty. Love the bone marrow and smoked ribs. Brussels sprouts are good too. Pretty much everything is good-to-great. The only reason I only gave it 3 stars instead of 4 is because I think it's kind of overpriced. Always a good time, tho. Thumbs up.
I love this place! Great service, super friendly staff, awesome vegetarian options and really delicious food. Have been back several times and it's always consistent. Highly recommend.

Was here for my first time yesterday and absolutely loved everything that I ate! Had just gone on a looonng run and had no problem eating the guaco taco, veggie mole (this one's in its experimental phase), and potato kale tacos. Â Each one was awesome! Â Even the veggie mole, which they said still needs tweaking, was so hearty and full of flavor. Â All I think it needs is a bit more heat and then it's good to go. Â I definitely need to go back on a Monday to indulge in more veggie-based taco creations. What's even more amazing about Brooklyn Taco is that the staff truly cares about the food they serve. Â They were so nice and chatty and genuinely wanted to know how much I liked the food. Â They need to open up a bigger shop with a longer counter ASAP! Â Love you guys!

The spicy meatballs were awesome! Â The manager even came up to us at the end of our meal to ask us how everything was. Â He then recommended this yummy dessert with almond blackberry ice cream. Â Great service and food!

Sooo good!!! I came here with my parents for my dad's birthday dinner. We decided to sit upstairs. It has a very nice view of the area and surrounding restaurants (haha). Waiter was very nice (: For appetizers we ordered: 1. Octopus: Now this is the first time I ever had octopus. The visible tentacles always disturbed me. However after reading on Yelp that this appetizer was so delicious, I had to try some. And it was delicious! Not that I have anything to compare it to, really, but both my parents said it was the best octopus they ever had and they regularly eat it, so that must be saying something. It was really tender and in this good sauce. 2. Cod: Also very good! My favorite part was not the cod, actually, but the bread and sauce it came with. Delicious. 3. Crab Croquettes: Probably my least favorite out of the three, but good, and also had a yummy sauce. Main courses we ordered: 1. Lamb shank: my mom said it was delicious. 2. Red rubbed salmon: my dad and I ordered this. It was very good. A spicy piece of salmon with crispy skin over some greens with a delicious sauce - I really liked it, even if it was a little too spicy for my taste. Desserts: 1. Pine nut cake - really good and had delicious ice cream with it! a big portion! 2. Brownie: Good and had sesame ice cream, yum 3. Creme Brulee - sooo delicious with fresh fruits and a big portion! Also the mango tea was so delicious and comes in a little teapot! So cute!!! They have a HUUUUUUUUUGE wine/beer selection.
Was alone. Had curry Ho Fun with dumplings and fishballs. Curry was fantastic! Â  Dumplings not so much. Place is a sanitary B...well it's Chinatown.

Okay where do I begin....... 1 - Meg Ryan sat next us sooooo I guess you could say that's pretty cool and explains a little something about the spot 2 - Very Crowded and there was an hour wait, but very well worth it. Â It is good. Therefore, there will most likely always be a wait. It is that good. 3 - The most important...the Food. When my boyfriend and I go on vacation we make it a point to make the food and restaurant selection the focal point of the trip. Balthazar exceeded our expectations especially when we have such high expections for the few restaurants we select out of a plethora of decisions that New York has to offer. We don't like to be disappointed when it comes to food. Let's just say it was hovering perfection. I had the goat cheese tart and the eggs with the red wine deduction. It kills me that I can't remember the name, but it was very delicious as I am sure everything on the menu is.

Went for lunch. We came exactly at 12:00 and sat in the Tavern section. The table we were sitting at in this section was a bit on the uncomfortable side - to eat at; but it was all secondary when the food arrived. The desert was amazing too. The service was very good as well. Good place to take your parents when they come into town...
Awesome place. Â Johnny is THE man. Â Great food at reasonable prices. My son ordered the Lumberjack and I ordered the Jersey Shore. They serve breakfast all day. We will come back again soon.

3.5 Stars-4... eh 3.75. I'm in the middle! Ah, Tina's Cuban Cuisine. Â Well, I'd been to the sister Sophie's once long ago, which is just around the corner from me in Murray Hill, but since I just ate here for lunch I figured this would be the most appropriate location to review. Â  This location seemed more spacious and cleaner then the one near me (not that I would say this has ambiance so nix the dining in option). Â  My boyfriend goes gaga for Tina's... he says it's all about the beans (which I'd heard has serious garlic + spice) and the infamous green sauce. Â I concur that it's a solid lunch, take-out spot. Â This location happens to be really close to where I work; so when Menkui Tei barked they weren't open (at 11am?! Come on now), I went to Tina's. I looked outside at the lunch special and my eyes clicked with the spicy grilled chicken; standard lunch special with two sides. I was disappointed to find that it was boneless breast cutlet....I was expecting rotisserie chicken like how most Latin places do it. Â Bagh. My fault really. Â The grilled chicken wasn't bad at all and its spice level was perfect for a heat freak like me. Â It wasn't dry, and cooked really well... nice and juicy, and didn't even NEED the green sauce (not that it didn't benefit from it!). Â They dumped in Â a LOT of rice.. too much. Â It was nice and flavorful, if not a bit hard and slightly oily (but I didn't mind this too much). Â Then, some grilled veggies. Â These were good but really more for flavor (lots of chunky onions, tomatoes, and peppers), not really for eating. I mostly left this for the trash. Â  The other let-down was that the 2nd side I'd asked for (aside from rice), was the maduros. Â I actually wanted tostones but they told me it would take a few and I didn't want to wait, so maduros it was. Â They put in like....3. Wah wahhhh. Â They were really delicious, but just few in numbers. Â They were perfectly soft where they should be, and perfectly crisp where they should be, and not greasy at all. Â Ah, sweet oh sweet plantains! Anyway. The whole lunch cost me $10, so I can't complain. Â I'd much rather spend my money on the authentic Mom and Pop places vs some corporate joint with cold sandwiches. Â  Anecdote; the green sauce is good, and they gave me 2 at the register! :) (not even at my request, just cause!). I've always wondered what was in this famous Peruvian sauce, universally known as just "green sauce" , but I tasted at Tina's, lots of zesty garlic, and cream. Â Definitely one of the better green sauces I had (not salsa-esque at all), but I still think the green sauce at Pio Pio tops all else.
The highlight of my dinner was the green tea tofu!

Came on a busy Saturday night with no reservations.. I wanted to come here based solely on the yelp reviews... Thanks, review writers! You did me a solid. Make a reservation! When we got there, we were told there was a 2 hour wait. However, on our way out the door, I noticed a shiny table at the bar area. We squeezed in, and we were able to be served the full menu from there. The area was a bit of a squeeze, but the sweet gentlemen next to us didn't mind at all. Food was BEYOND! OMG, I want to eat there again and again and again. We shared: Garbanzos Fritos - So interesting! They were perfectly seasoned, crispy and fun to eat. Pa Am Oli - Cause I love bread... A good appetizer for anyone who's not afraid of carbs. Langostinos Ajo Pescador - Holy flavorful! Wow.. Cooked perfectly and had such an amazing flavor, I wanted to drink the sauce. Rossejat Rapido - HANDS DOWN FAVORITE DISH! Wow! We requested this dish to be made without chicken, and it was so - so - so - amazing! It reminded me of a dish my Grandmother makes, only better (sorry Gma)! The flavor of the chorizo was perfect, the noodles were perfect... UGH, everything. I want more. Now. Our drinks were also good, but the food was definitely the shining star. If I lived in NYC, I would definitely be a regular here. YUM!

I've only been once, but if I can make it back and have the same experience, I'll update to 5 stars. The gf and I tried getting into Clinton St. Baking Company, but the line was way too long, and mostly tourists, so we decided against it. We found this place and shared an egg sandwich and the avocado toast. They get their bread from Balthazar bakery and it's amazing, and the eggs were cooked very well. The avocado toast was also great, it's basically just avocado smushed onto toast with some spiciness - simple and tasty. This cafe reminds me of Cafe La Maude, which is my favorite place in Philadelphia, and so I can't wait til I'm back in NY to go back to Cafe Gitane.

What's NOT to like? Tiny, intimate tapas spot with friendly service. Squid ink with rice: phenomenal. Patatas bravas, shrimp, fried fish, and lamb skewers were absolutely delicious. The only thing I didn't LOVE was the chorizo... it was good, but not my favorite. I would recommend coming with 2-3 people... 4 max. It'd probably be impossible to get a seat if your party's any bigger.

Gramercy Tavern, thank you for reminding me how rich, buttery, and delicious pork belly is supposed to be (Yeah, I'm looking at you, Chung Sol!). Â Your rack of lamb is perfection on a plate. Â  This is one of the few places that I think should be elevated from 1 michelin star to 2. Â If you're still hungry at dessert time, just get the Peanut Butter Semifreddo. Â You'll go home happy.

This stretch of 9th Ave is full of surprises. Â When I walk down it (usually on my way to Parke & Ronen and/or Billy's) I pass by the restaurants and think, these all look so charming but so similar! Â Le Grainne definitely fits the bill. Â Undoubtedly charming, it fills the French slot in the slew of little restaurants with exposed brick walls, not too many but just enough tables, and a foreign staff to match the cuisine. Â The food is good, and definitely authentically French and delicious. Â The cheese plate appetizer is quite a lot of bang for your buck. Â Mostly everything is, actually - the prices are reasonable bordering on cheap! Â I was craving pasta so I ordered a seafood linguine which was good but not great enough to earn this place that last star. Â One of my companion's Nicoise salad looked much more appetizing. As for the service, it was typically French, but was redeemed in the end when my two friends (both fluent French speakers) struck up quite a conversation with our adorable, if somewhat aloof, waitress. Â I hear the brunch is great, so I'll probably be back. Â A five star experience in what's basically a four star restaurant. Â Mostly this was due to my Franco-phonic (and Francophillic) company, but we had a quite a lovely time here.

The food at this joint is superb, and let it be known that I am only giving them four stars because anytime I ask for water it tastes kind of like watered down tea. Â I usually bring my own bottled or otherwise, and beyond that I have always enjoyed eating here. I usually stick with the classic pho, but companions of mine have enjoyed the sandwiches and pho sate. Â Unfortunately the sandwiches are on my to-do list: one bowl of pho is enough for me and the temptation is too great.

Decent if you're starving, but a tad overrated otherwise. Came here for brunch in a group of 4 + a 4 year old. The wait was about 1 hour and 15 minutes from the time I called and put my name down, though they originally quoted 45 minutes. We were starving by the time we were sat and wanted a taste of everything so we ordered the following and cut everything into quarters to share: Disco Tots: The gravy isn't anything special and takes away from the crunch. 3.5/5 Atomic Fire Balls: Mac n cheese rolled into a ball, deep fried, drizzled with sriracha served with ranch sauce...good on paper but a major fail in execution. Sriracha, one of my favorite condiments, seemed out of place and confusing atop the balls as did the side of ranch. The mac n cheese filling was extremely dry & bland and lacked any sort of cheesy goodness. 1/5 Croque Madame Bread Pudding: This was good although the hollandaise sauce was too thick and heavy for my taste. 3.5/5 Breakfast Burrito: Impressive in size but not so impressive in flavor. If you've never tasted bland sausage, order this. 2.5/5 Heuvos Divorce: Two fried eggs on two crispy tortillas. One with salsa verde and the other with salsa rojo. The salsas had zero kick but were still tasty. 3/5 The Perfect Storm: Â The smoked salmon was the saltiest I've ever tasted. It was almost inedible if not for their heavy hollandaise which in this dish helped to mask the saltiness a bit. Â 2/5 Lunch Burger: Ordered by the 4 yr old, this was actually inedible. Because they were serving to a toddler I assume they were aiming for well done but the patty was severely overcooked and as dry as the Sahara. Even the toddler who loves burgers decided not to eat it after taking just 1 bite. We returned it to the kitchen and credit to them, they didn't charge us for it. But I have to wonder what they were thinking when they put this dish out thinking it was ok to serve to customers. 1/5 Red Velvet Bread Pudding: Moist and unique, this was a pleasant ending to the meal. 4/5 Service was excellent and friendly. The place definitely has a family feel to it Â and maybe we just caught them on a bad day, but IMHO it's not worth the wait or the trip to the ATM.

Long wait outside and another long wait for service of a mediocre meal. The chicken was too salty, the Catfish was lost somewhere inside of the overbearing breading, with a dollop of Tartar sauce on top. Seriously? Mac and cheese was served with a dash of hot sauce on top. Who does that? One of our party ordered Chicken biscuits and deserts to go, only to find that the deserts were not included in the take out order. They don't remember if they were charged for them or not. As far as I'm concerned, the entire meal should have been comped.

I've been living in Bushwick since graduating from college 4 years ago and cannot stress enough how excited I am for this place! I went yesterday for breakfast with friends from out of town and not a single complaint. The staff was amazing as were the owners/managers. They took the time to come to our table to ensure everything was as we wished. I definitely recommend the benedict which can be ordered three different ways for those who eat meat or not. The design is fresh and new and feels very clean. The prices are very affordable. For the three of us to eat breakfast including alcoholic beverages and iced coffee it cost us $43 including tip!! GO now before this place gets discovered and the line is out the door. There were already people waiting when we went for breakfast at 10:30am!

Hello Perilla ..Just a little "Thanks" note for my sons birthday party for four ... ...You welcomed us in with smiles in spite of showing up @ 10 for a 945PM ... ....You had a good selection of Vodka (Grey Goose is fake vodka) and cool cocktails.. ......Pre-Fixe,A-LaCarte,Small Plates plus mix and match...perfect for us greedy gluts.. .......Un boring Â food selection of sweet-spice-savoury..not quite gourmet...but Good .. .........candlelit etc. could be romantic, casual, business ...Versatile Ambiance.. .......... Lil' fancy schmancy touches...amuse-bouche, petit fours.. Nice !! ............We'll be seeing you soon ..:):) Luv SKG and Family

Got there at 10.30 sat, table within 10min. I rocked the eggs florentine w/salmon. Had a lovely sweet note that added a dimension to this dish not tasted before. Place was tight quick and had an intimate touch - the way we all like it.

99 Favor Taste came to Chinatown. Hot Pot lovers' heaven! I was already exposed to the original 99 Favor Taste in Brooklyn. I was not happy 2/3 times I was there. However, I have to compliment on how much better this location is. I did not have high expectations for this place but the dinner service I had the other day really blew my mind! I came here with my boyfriend on a late-afternoon on Thursday for dinner. We were seated and we ordered our AYCE hot pot. We ordered the split pot which comes with 2 soups - we chose the Herbal soup and Spicy Mala soup. We order our usual hot pot ingredients - seaweed, beef slices, lamb, watercress, fish fillet (my favorite!), spam, tripe, tofu skin, and etc. Our Herbal soup was a bit weak that day but the Spicy mala really hit the spot! I notice that this location (although, smaller than Brooklyn), it is a lot cleaner and a lot more organized. The sauce is located in the back, feel free to mix - everything from soy sauce, sa-cha sauce, cilantro, sesame oil, scallions, vinegar, garlic, etc. Mix it up to your liking! What makes this location so different is that the server we had was so attentive - not to mention, he knew Cantonese, Mandarin, and English! My boyfriend and I were speaking to him in 3 languages (because we knew how to say some things better in that particular language!). I really loved how he was so friendly and very eager to start a conversation with us. In addition, he came to us right when we need a refill of our herbal tea or the soups in the pot. My boyfriend even complimented on his professionalism and he's a very hard to please kind of guy. Excellent customer service! Our waiter also used an iPad to take our order - quite unique & trendy experience! The restaurant gets super crowded and loud during dinner service. Make sure you come early to skip the crowd! Be patient and be understanding that your server have more tables to serve so be sure to order just before you are about to finish. Don't forget to also check in on Yelp! for a free scoop of ice-cream!

I have to say I've always been a fan of David Changs and whenever there's not a line at momofuku, I go. So it's been awhile since I've been to saÃ¤m and I've been wanting try their new menu. (I haven't been since they opened because the wait is usually around the block-so new to me). And when the hubby and I were walking by and saw no wait and two stools at the bar I forced him inside before he knew what was happening. We both had the barbq pork sandwich so I can't attest the the rest of the food, but I loved my sandwich. Especially topped with hot sauce. I don't even like coleslaw but I like this one. I don't think i would wait for a table here, but definitely go if there's no wait.

Amidst a bustling street of Korean restaurants, BCD Tofu House offers decent ambience, but fails to impress with its food. Came here with a group of friends over the weekend for lunch and had about a 30 minute wait (they kept saying it would be 10 minutes, but it was much longer). I shared the Seafood Soon Tofu and Bibimbap. The tofu stew wasn't as spicy as we had hoped, but was still flavorful and enjoyable. The Bibimbap, on the other hand, was mediocre. You can get much better in the area. It was kind of cool that everyone got their own fish, but the rest of the sides were relatively scarce in supply. The pros of BCD are that there is ample amounts of seating for large groups, decent service, and good decor. Since this is hard to come by in Ktown, I'm bumping them up to 3 stars, but if you want tasty, flavorful food, check out a different spot.
Very good food and great service. Recommend the orchiette with vegetable ragu!

I brunch alone. Â I'm not ashamed -- I bring a little reading, take my time arriving, don't feel pressured to make stupid small talk. Â I kind of adore it. Brunch places, however, tend to enjoy a) rushing me, b) treating me like a second-class diner, c) staring at me from the hostess area judgmentally. Â  BUT NOT PAPRIKA. Â Not only did I pay a mere $12 for coffee + eggs benedict + mimosa (all of which, by the way, were delicious), but I took my sweet time and actually got to ASK for the check! Â  Also, the gal pouring drinks complimented my turban-wrap, which was the proverbial cherry on top of my Sunday brunch. (see what I did there, with the pun? Â That's the kind of tipsy-delightful mood Paprika puts me in!)
Had the Thyme Sage Roasted Chicken Breast w/ beets -- supa good.

Accidentally stopped at this place for brunch after the crazy new years eve. Excellent food ! Â Value for money. I mean I created my yelp A/C for this. Â Yeah its not he typical chicken tikka masala place or the typical buffet food you get. Its home cooked indian food. It for people like me who savor the Â simple taste of home cooked indian food without the frills. Â  Like they say in punjab ! Chak de fatte.

relatively small space- though i hear they have a private dining space downstairs?- with eggscellent service. they were kind enough to help us stow away our bags while we ate. now say it with me: avocado toast. do it. WITH egg. their shrooms benedict was also really nice, and the coffee/water refills were smooth and quick. overall great neighborhood spot.

I've been eating at/ordering from Ruby's since moving to Soho in April. Over the the past 6 months I've noticed a serious decline in the quality of the food. The roast pumpkin salad - which was my favorite item - should now be called a pumpkin salad since there is no roasting ever. Cold, hard pumpkin really isn't appetizing. Their pastas also have become more gummy, the texture of the Alfredo sauce reminds me of paste. Ruby's used to be my go to for a quick, easy, tasty meal, but I won't go back anytime soon.

Paneer veggie starter delicately spiced and OK. Â  The "speciality" Mutsh (Kashmiri lamb kofta) a disappointment though - a layer of heavy lamb like a burger (and not light kofte at all) with rich but clumsily spiced sauce on top. Â  Had a lot of Indian food but this dish really didn't work. Â Happy to have tasted a Sri Lankan beer for the first time, but unlikely to go back.

For starters, we had no wait to our total surprise. We walked in to a loud, hustling restaurant expecting to have to turn around and go elsewhere and instead we got seated at the counter right away. We ordered the fried chicken buns and a ramen to split. The buns were soft with spicy, crunchy chicken. Loved those and wished there were more of them in a $9 order. We chose the spicy ramen, added soft boiled egg. Broth was good, noodles were soft but less chewy than I thought they'd be. Overall, a belly filling, warming meal in the middle of our trip through the city. I would return if I didn't have to wait. The atmosphere is hectic, the employees yell things to each other and greetings (I'm guessing since it's foreign) at diners as they enter the dining room. Price for what we ate was decent. $32 with tip.
Tasty sausages and pretzels, great beer, a friendly bartender, and outdoor seating. This place is a great find.

Went there on their opening night. Super impressed. The staff was organized. Food came out on time. Everything we ordered was great. We had some type of vegetable dumpling which was unreal, mushroom appetizer, carrot salad (very good,) the skirt steak and chicken entree. No complaints. I will be back.

Extremely unhappy with service! Â  I made a reservation a week in advance and received a confirmation number. Â When I called back to reconfirm my reservation, the manager said their system already delete my reservation without notifying me and I no longer had a reservation. Â The manager did not apologize and offer any alternative. Â Do not go here....

top 5 meal of all time for me. escargot - one of the better things i have eaten. not like classic french style of garlic and butter. very different. bone marrow and oxtail marmalade - another awesome dish. sweetbreads - great fried chicken - surprisingly dry. was thinking this was going to be the best thing we were going to eat. paella - exceeded expectations. i'd want this again. fondue - eh just an all around awesome meal with a ton of wine.

yes, definitely make reservations! Saturday 10:45am, small groups are starting to form... then a couple more comes from the right, the left, and then we all look like a giant bundle as we try to enter the restaurant when the clock strikes 11am and the door is open! the server was very courteous, checking once in a while but not to the state of annoyance. she kindly explained to us the daily special, but my friend and i were there to taste their famous original brunch menu! so we decided to get the classic eggs benedict (poached eggs, canadian bacon, english muffin, hollandaise) and benedict johnny ($15) (chicken sausage, cornbread, roasted tomato hollandaise) bread baskets are serves with either bottled or tap water to your choosing. (their coffee was $6 and orange juice was $3) it didn't take too long before the dishes came out. both came with the side of potatoes (which were fried?- different from the roasted potatoes on other yelper's pictures) the potatoes were nicely cooked but heavily seasoned. the cornbread of benedict was bit too sweet-not too bad, but strange. other than that, the poached eggs were perfectly cooked and the hollandaise sauce glistened as it mixed with the yolk and flowed down to the bottom of the plate.

I came back with the Boyfriend recently and picked up some macarons. On our way to the register, the Boyfriend noticed that they also sell ice cream. I read about it once on Serious Eats but I've never tried it since I'm usually here only for the macarons. He insisted that we try one since I had just recovered from my cold. I opted for the Rose flavor, since their Rose Petal macarons are my absolute favorite. It was delicious! I really didn't taste like any kind of ice cream that I have ever had. It was less creamy and hardly melted at all as we ate it. There was also so much rose flavor in the ice cream that I had to check the ingredients to see what it was made of - rose, rose and more rose!
nice and decent size burger, def recommend to everyone!

All varieties of sandwich are excellent (pork buns, fish sandwiches, etc). Â The rest is tiny portions at big prices. Â Though I must admit, I have been frequenting this spot since it opened and used to be a huge fan, so it's possible I say this because the novelty has warn off. Â  In brief: if you haven't been here, it's a must; if you have, stick with the sandwiches because they're the highlight.

This review is for the burger. Everything I have eaten here has been good but the burger cooked medium rare is my good friend. It is always amazing! The meat is fresh and tasty (I have bought the ground beef they use from marlow and daughters with great results too). I have eaten at Lugers and Dumont plenty of times and this is best burger in Williamsburg.

Awesome place! Once you walk in, you notice all the seafood they have. Smells good too. Fresh and clean. Kinda small place. When it gets packed, it gets really tight. There was only 1 waiter there and every time someone came in, he had to pull the table out so they can sit on the inside. Food was really, really good. I got the lobster roll with old bay fries and gf got linguini with clams and cockles. Lobster roll was excellent, reminded me of Red's Eats in Maine. Not exactly like it, but very close. Better than Luke's Lobster that's for sure. We also had the calamari and NE clam chowder. Both were really good, but the calamari was one of the best calamari I've ever had. It was just so fresh and crispy. Overall, this place is excellent. Oh, and service was also good.

I love this place! Â  It has a Mediterranean menu - plus traditional Eastern European offerings -- cous-cous and kugel are on the menu. Â  I really like that they have a Jewish New Year menu. Â  It's rare to find an original restaurant :)
Just plain awesome. Great meat, great atmosphere and (when I went anyhow) great service. A bit pricey, but well worth it if you're going with friends.

As other reviewed mention, this place is always busy. Get there early. For appetizer you must have the pork buns. Very light and full of flavor. The one appetizer to avoid is the Philly cheesteak egg roll. Not sure why we ordered this. It tasted like hamburger helper in a pizza roll. The ramen was superb! Perfect amount of ramen. This ranks as high as the ramen I had in Harajuku Japan. The price is about $14 for the ramen which might be a skosh high but well worth it.
Went last night for the first time and it was outstanding. I only wish we had ordered the Fried Chicken which smelled and looked fantastic. Definitely next time.

I really got lucky when trying this place. When we first walked in, it was so warm and the smell of zaatar was really strong- in a good way. The seating space is a little small, but luckily they had room for us. We ordered the zaatar pita, which was WAY too strong with the zaatar. The reason why I got it was because my dad used to make his own olive oil/zaatar mix as I was growing up, but this stuff was way too intense. We also had the chicken kebab, which was slammin. It was so good, the chicken was spiced well and moist and the techina was really fresh and tasty. We also had the lambajin, or lamb pizza, which was also really delicious. The entire meal was really good, and I remember it being somewhat cheap, but they lose a star for service - it was really, really hard to get our servers attention. Other than that, I'm totally going back.
This is gooood fooood! you're gonna love it the first time you try it. i prefer it over other halal since it isnt as wet or greasy. the white sause is amazing but watch out for the hot sause.

I just love Ippudo. Here's the trick, put your name on the list, and then go to the Irish bar around the corner for a couple Guinesses (or is that Guini?). Â Come back happy and ready for some noodles. you have to have the pork bun (or try the bun of the day). My wife and I have to go at least once a month.

TIP: Today at 12:15PM, the line for the cart at 53rd and 6th was as long as is always is that time of weekday, 20+ minutes. The line for the exact same food at the Halal Guys cart one block over at 53rd and 7th? Five people long.
Family style with the Fam Bam
Modern, Thai restaurant/Bar. Beautiful deco and exciting menu. Would love to dine there again. A gem in the neighborhood. Friendly staff, but small space though.

I had dinner here with friends. Â The food was excellent and since there were five of us, I got to try a lot of different dishes. Â Most of the menu is small plates, so you can order 2 or 3 for your meal, but there's also a main plates section of the menu too. Â We split a cold mezza to start - hummus, baba, fattoush, labne, and moujadara served with warm pita. Â Excellent. Â Since it was a big night out, we all ordered another a main plate and two small plates each, so we had a ton of food. Â The biggest standouts for me were the Semolina Gnocchi (I've never had yogurt like that), the califlower, and the Warm Eggplant. Â In fact, I'm still thinking about that eggplant. Â The risotto was good, so was the falafel, the cheese rolls, and the phoenician fries. Â My least favorite part was probably the atmosphere - huge, trendy, and loud, but the food made up for it.

Great place. Â Good niche concept run by Â nice group of guys. Â We went for late breakfast / early lunch. Â I wanted breakfast and got a 'Big Tex' Â which had freshly scrambled egg, jack cheese, bacon, and jalapenos on a big dense biscuit (see posted pic) Â It tasted great, was large and filling - and all for a mere $4.25. Â Wife wanted lunch and, after weighing practically every option on the menu, eventually opted for the 3 cheese melt, substituting smoked gouda for goat cheese, along with gruyere havarti and tomato. Â  She went through it pretty quick and was happy. Â I took a bite and then had thoughts of coming back for a late lunch. Â  We shared a fresh squeezed OJ. Â To sum it up, this place really hit the spot.

I am sorry but this place is so bland I think they have really stopped making good food due to their popularity. Â I am 100% Polish and know good Polish food. Â There used to be a nice spot right here in Greenpoint on Humbold St (nothing fancy, typical cafeteria) but they closed shop. Â So I come here several times since. Â I like their pierogi just fine but their soups and their cutlets (kotlety, mielone i schabowe) are not very good at all. Â  While going next door to but some Polish groceries I saw the cook buying soup bases there, the ones that come in powder!!!!! Â Seriously? So you buy a 99cents soup packet and serve that up? Granted the food is not expensive but if I wanted instant soup I would buy it and make it at home. Â When you come to a restaurant you want the broth to be made there. Anywho, the food to me is simply sub par now. Â So I am in search of a new good, casual spot. Â This place may be ok for someone who does not know authentic Polish food. Â But its not that hard to cook it here (its not like Chinese or Indian authentic where you may not have all the proper ingredients around). If you want just ok or mediocre food, come here, otherwise keep looking. Sorry I really wanted to like this place as it is cute and cozy, but I come for the food and its just not good.
Had a celebratory work lunch here and it was the perfect place. Â The sangria was strong and good, the tapas were excellent.
Have been here a few times with friends and every time the sushi is just amazing. Expect good service, fresh fish, and super yummy. Â This is totally worth the 5 stars and more.

good chinese food. dan dan noodles, wontons in hot oil (i was literally eating the oil like the soup when the noodles were gone) and good basics. the spicy fish was too spicy though, and i like spicy, but it left my entire mouth numb.
The food is phenomenal. Â The chefs are right behind the bar. Â It is amazing to watch them cook. Â The flavor combinations are innovative and sublime.

best bbq!!!!!! arrived around lunch time on Saturday - waited in line for 45mins (par for the course apparently) Brisket Pork Spare Ribs Boneless Beef Ribs Pickles Saurkraut everything was amazing and worth the wait. Â washed down with an Allagash White Ale while standing in line! ;)

so incredibly delicious - rustic, upscale comforting american food. great meat and seafood. wonderful service. casual and farmhouse atmosphere that still feels incredibly special. i love that it's not as formal as the dining room. eating in the tavern for lunch is one of the best summer weekend experiences. i loved the meatball and pork shoulder and peach pie. mmmmmm.
Back in the clubbing days, this was one of the hot spots at 4am. Â The food is pretty good. Â But for the price you pay, this place deserves 5 stars.

Jadis is a great place to relax and enjoy affordable wine with 1 friend or 15. Bottles of wine start in the $20 range. The food is pretty good, though the selection small. Highly recommend for a chill night or as a place to meet up with friends before going out out.

Delicious food. Extensive menu. Tons of options for those of you that are Â vegetarians. Reasonably priced. Beautiful outside seating area. Trust me here, get a side of the coconut rice. You won't be sorry.
Really great pizza with a unique, chewy dough. I suggest going later in the evening to avoid the lines.

A five star rating should be rare, but looking back on the dinner and brunch at Rye, there's little that missed. Â Everything we ordered was perfect pitch. The cocktails are splendid. Â I'm a huge Southside aficionado, and make them all summer long at home. Â The Rye Southside beats mine. Delicious--must be the hipster gin. The small bites before the meal are good. The crab croquette rocked, and I savored each bite. Â The parsley dressing on top brought out the freshness. The endive and pear salad with bleu cheese is remarkable. Â I usually treat frisse like parsley and ignore it. But the endive, pecans, cheese and frisse work so well together. I was sorry at the last bite. My beef short rib sandwich with onion spread was quite tasty. Mi Â Vida's bacon (actually grilled pork belly) with brussel sprouts was hearty and good, but too fatty for my taste, though it has to be expected from pork belly. The chocolate cake is really more like a budino, and was the perfect end to a wonderful meal. Great coffee as well. Brunch was fabulous. The BLT had the best bacon of my life. Â No kidding. Â The meatloaf sandwich lives up to the hype. Professional, attentive and pleasant service (though quite hipster with the beards, flannel shirts and unkempt chic). The space is speakeasy classic, with leather banquettes and good lighting. Â  Frankly, this is a 4.5 star rating, but I can't figure out why not five. Â I'll be back often. Â Brooklyn has some of the best restaurants in the country.
I love this place the best Thai food I have had!! I just wish I lived closer ...

Came here for the gluten free pasta and stayed because of the sassy but cute bartender... definitely worth it... ask for Meghan, she's a great bartender and I think she said she even waitresses also, Â she's awesome

This place is great. Â It's very busy, so have an idea of what you want, otherwise the crowd will gobble you up. Â The rooftop bar is good too, but equally busy when weather permits. Â Get there early.
