i have been following chef Edwin since he was at Morrell's creating some tasty signature dishes that really hit the spot. So when he left to open up his own restaurant, I was extremely excited to know that I would still be able to satisfy some of my cravings (i.e his delicious pulled pork tacos are bite size yet mouth watering. The pork is flavorful and tender and the corn taco shell compliments the taste brilliantly). First off, I'm all about ambiance and decor and when you walk into his restaurant, it feels like you are walking into a restaurant in the hip meatpacking district and not necessarily those cookie cutter theater district venues. This place is actually cool and inviting with it's sleek and warm color tone interior. Secondly, the wait staff, from the hostess to the head waiter, are beyond attentive. They are also extremely knowledgeable on all the items on the menu are very happy to give you suggestions and feedback on each of the dishes. We had family from out of town and they were blown away by the food. We started with a shrimp risotto that was absolutely delicious. I had the pulled pork tacos (die!) and the fluke ceviche, which was so fresh and perfectly garnished. My husband had the lamb loin and was practically licking the plate and my aunt had the branzino and was floored on how nicely seasoned it was. The wine list has some excellent selections for all different palettes. The Shapes and shadows pinot noir was one of the tastiest medium bodied, cherry flavored pinots I've ever had. In short, i cannot wait to dine at this restaurant again. I feel like I owe it to the overall amazingness of this restaurant (and its talented chef, of course) to spread the word and get foodies of all ages to dine at this fine establishment!

This place is such a gem! My favorite italian eatery in all of NY. Food is delicious and is served fresh from the oven. Service is great...although it can take a bit at busiest hours. Prices are very reasonable and the ambiance is absolutely a joy. Feels like home! A great place for a date or family dinner!!

how the heck are you supposed to talk s#!+ on the place that started it all?! lombardi's has the true new york pizza! it has that crisp thing crust- where you pinch the center of the crust to fold in half and slice sticks straight up! theres a lot of toppings to choose from but i'd suggest going as simple as possible! (i had mine with sausage, spinach, and ricotta and it was amazeballs!). heck, its lombardi's! you just have to try it!

Excellent service, never disappointed with the food . Vaca frita is on point, as is the ropa vieja. Place is small so expect to wait on a weekend night. Being Cuban I def know cuban food and this place doesn't disappoint.

I am a big fan of any type of noodle/tofu type of soup, so it's no surprise I really enjoyed this place. Â I came here on a Monday night and avoided any wait times. This is probably the best ramen I've had, though I feel like it's a bit expensive for what it is. Â I had the shoyu ramen and it was really good. Â The broth was flavorful, the pork was great, and the egg was cooked perfectly (slightly runny, yet firm). Â  The pork buns here are amazing. Â The pork is delicious and fatty and goes well the peking duck style buns. Â  Overall, a great meal and probably the best bowl of ramen you'll find around.

I've been here a few times over the past ten years, often with long stretches of time in between visits. It hasn't changed. It's a village staple. The food is pretty good--the specials are usually the way to go--and the energy is all its own. I love the nights when people spill out on to the sidewalk, sipping their BYOs over bites of food and conversation. Many people dislike/complain about the table service, but I think it's just part of the package. It's basically a French cafe taken as is and transplanted in NY. But I get it, we're in NY, not France. I just don't mind it.

I can only say good things about Cafe Condesa. It is so reasonably priced for the quality of food, and the location, it's hard to believe. It's tiny, but not uncomfortably so. Everything going on is visible, there is no doors to anywhere other than the bathroom. Open kitchen, and even where they wash dishes is in sight. But it gives it an authentic, cozy feel. Definitely make a reservation! About 10 minutes after we arrived, every seat was taken. And there can't be more than 30 seats. I went on a Thursday night with 3 other people. Our waitress was very friendly and really sweet. BTW free glass of wine with check in on yelp! It says house wine, but they let you pick from any of the wines available by glass. They serve soda in an ice cold can, with a glass of ice...which was awesome. For starters we had artichoke ravioli, crab tortellini, and baked brie. Everything was delicious and very good portions. The sauce for both the ravioli and tortellini were delicious. I am not crazy about brie but everyone was raving about it. Our table ended up getting the same entrees, the steak and the scallops. Extra side of brussel sprouts, and mashed potatoes. The scallops were DELICIOUS, seared beautifully and I loved the cauliflower puree it came with, amazing! I don't eat meat but the guys loved their steaks, I saw they were cooked perfectly (medium rare), I tried the baked potato and guacamole it came with, yummy. Dessert was very good as well, the chocolate creme brulee is decadent, you must like chocolate a lot if you order it. The berry crisp was probably my favorite. There was also a chai cake, that we weren't particularly crazy about. But we were all so full that it didn't matter. Coffee and cappuccinos are incredible!
The only reason this places will lose a star is the wait to eat. It took over 2 hours to get a table. Other then that the food was amazing. I will be coming back to this place as much as i can.
all i can say is GREAT ! 5 star all day!

Good homemade food in a small, family owned Italian joint. I got the baked ziti with meatballs that was well seasoned although meatballs were a bit dry. My friend for the meat lasagna which looked amazing but tasted too bland to me as I appreciate spices. Canollis are made fresh, which I appreciate, but the filling had a weird consistency and not the typical canolli type. Service is sweet, big menu.

My 2 girlfriends and I had an outstanding dinner on a Wednesday evening at Bobby Flay's new restaurant, Gato. Â We were met at the door by friendly hostesses who made us feel welcomed and immediately sat us at our table. Â We were then greeted by our fabulous server, Corey, who helped guide us through our gastronomic feast. The menu while not long can at first seem overwhelming, but through Corey's knowledge of the food and its components (the descriptions on the menu do not do the food justice) helped us decide on our choices. Â He was as excited for us to eat as we were. Â We decided we wanted to taste as much as we possibly could eat, while of course saving room for dessert. Â To start we ordered from the bar menu, which there is a choice of 13 large one bite appetizers, you choose 3. Â If you are with a large crowd definitely order one of each. The eggplant was definitely a standout. We also ordered from the appetizer section the roasted octopus, which melted in your mouth, charred tomato salad and scrambled eggs. After you eat these scrambled eggs you will never want to make them from home again. Â They are to die for (and I am sure if you ate enough you will have to go to a cardiologist). For our main course we had the kale and wild mushroom paella, which is unlike any paella I have ever eaten and the Orata, along with the charred carrots and roasted cauliflower. For dessert we shared the blackberry crostata and fromage blanc cheesecake. Both were spectacular! Our server surprisingly presented us with a cordial and a plate filled with mini biscotti. To add to our excitement, Bobby Flay himself was in the restaurant cooking and walking around talking to diners and even helped the table next to us choose from the menu. Overall this was a great meal and we once again have to thank our server, Corey.

Incredible. I almost feel a little guilty posting this review, as A) I am a tourist in NYC and Â  B) I don't want this to turn into yet another tourist spot... Because it's not. And it's *awesome*. I'm not exactly sure how we lucked in to finding this place. We were wandering down an alley, and my fiance joked: "We're either about to get mugged, or we're about to stumble on something amazing". Sure enough, we rounded a corner, and The Jeffrey was there. Amazing it was. The Caveats: -It's really crowded. Really noisy. Absolutely packed. (New Yorkers clearly know a good thing) I *hate* crowds. But it was totally worth it, once seated at a communal high-table in the back. -It's totally a Hipster Menu: Craft Brews, Pickled everything, Charcuterie, Pulled Pork... BUT IT'S FREAKING DELICIOUS And while the menu and staff veer toward hipster, the clientele, interestingly, did not. Mostly 30-somethings after work. And the decor is nice. The Good: -The Happy hour prices... Great deals on a selection of beer from their menu & a few other beverages The Better: -The beer list... Not as extensive as some, but well-chosen & thought-out, and definitely long enough. The ones that we sampled were terrific, particularly the Goeze. If you're into Goeze. The Oh-My-Gosh-This-Is-The-Best: -The food! It's only "bites" but *everything* we had was sooooo good. So good. So good. *Pulled Pork Tacos (The best!) *The fantastic small Charcuterie & Cheese Board was a steal at $15.00 *Kale Salad *Meatballs *Pickle Jar The portions were really generous & every dish tasted phenomenal! The Shocking (In a good way): -The Bill We walked out stuffed, and satiated for $82.00 (tax & tip included). In New York City. Safe to say we'll be back.

First off, don't come into Fish expecting a waft of cool air to escape the city heat. Â Fish isn't HOT, but it's the food and drinks that'll (hopefully) cool ya down. Â Great food and drinks, at that. Â My clams were well shucked and the house white wine ain't so bad. Â I can't wait to come back and try out more items on their menu!
I just want to add after a series of bad meals and a bad call on the hostess/waiters part we will not go back to this place.
I've been here 4 times now and every time has been amazing. Possibly my favorite place in Manhattan.

This place was very busy in its Williamsburg location on a Saturday evening. What was I expecting? The wait was worthwhile though for its great arepas. Although the arepa appeared to be small, it was more filling than I have imagined.

Both of the prior two reviews seem weird to me. Look, I came in b/c of the write-up in Serious Eats. Counter guy recommended the roast pork, smoked mozzarella, and wild mushroom sandwich (on foccacia). I get chills just thinking about that sandwich - I can't remember a better sandwich. Looks like a typical Italian deli, except for the blocks of cheese on top of the case, and the prepared food (looks better than the usual). The cheese seems to be well priced, but I'm no cheesemonger. I can tell you that sandwich was amazing, and I'll be back.
This place has some seriously tasty buffalo chicken wings. So good! I only wish they offered milkshakes to wash it all down.

Loved it here, our waitress made us feel so comfortable. Â Not at all touristy and she was great with the kids and parents. Â Short rib sliders were a great start and the garlic shrimp with polenta was filling even for an appetizer. Â Veggie soup of the day was very good per the 12.year old critic with us. Â Close to theaters though that was not our criteria. Â I felt at home here, like dinner at your favorite aunt's house.

Whole in the wall restaurant that everyone should try whether you're local or a tourist. While waiting I enjoy watching the workers making dumplings in the kitchen. It's always constant moving and never stopping. I've been here a few times and I love their $1 dumplings and never regret getting them. Perfect to dip and must eat fresh. The value is amazing and you get a good amount to enjoy, I believe you are able to order them to go. The one order I have regretted so far is the soup dumpling, there wasn't much flavor in the broth or dumpling. I ordered thinking that this dumpling was like the famous soup dumpling at din tai fung. The place was small and cramped so there was barely any room to try and enjoy the food. Don't expect great customer service, the woman gave me an order that wasn't mine and once I realized it I went to give it back. The man that took my order scolded me asking why I would touch somebody else's food making me feel like I was in the wrong and incompetent -____-. I love coming here when I'm in the city. :-)

Overpriced. I was disappointed when I ordered the turkey, avocado sandwich. For $10- I got a sandwich that literally had two very thin slices of deli meat on it, with greens and bit of avocado on it. Also, the time I waited for this sandwich doesn't make sense, considering there wasn't much to it.

Whoa, delish hand made dumplings, 5 for a buck and they are big! I prefer the 4 fried pork buns for 1.00. I've also tried the wonton soup which is a whopping 1.75. You can also buy them frozen for take away! There is very limited seating, tiny tiny. This is the place on Eldridge with the upside neon open sign and the dirty windows. I think they keep the prices so low by using slave labor... They are constantly yelling around those girls in the back screaming them to keep making dumplings. But you know what, that's fine with me because these dumplings are truly delicious, and truly inexpensive.

I came here for dinner on a Friday night - and the place was packed, with an approximate half an hour wait. Â Cold soba nicely complements a warm (almost hot) Spring night. Â I had a light meal with the avocado tuna tartare to start, followed by the tororo soba. Â The soba was fresh and cool - just the way I liked it! Â I eyed and ulimately passed on the dessert menu, but going back would probably try the milk pudding with strawberry. I really liked the lighting and the lights - they were authentically pretty.

Supreme Pizza was perfect - just the right balance of flavors and sauce with a airy and crispy crust. Spinach Campanelle was pretty flawless as well. Lightly sauced with the perfect amount of garlic and cheese. Not too impressed with the bloody mary though - very heavily seasoned. Otherwise really really good.

I had the "package set" which allows you to order one appetizer and 3 different types of pasta. While great for saving money (as you are allow to refill), I was like meh. But again, like a i said, it's a great deal. The Panna Cotta was DROP.DEAD.AMAZING -- this is a must order! Perhaps when I have the chance to come back I should order their main course and see if it'd actually be way better.

Our waiter was Great...the Food however was Not. Â We had the Veal Marsala which had absolutely Zero flavor. This place is great. Â I'm almost afraid to review because it seems kind of under the radar and hasn't become completely overcrowded. Â The atmosphere is cozy, with nice, dim light. Â The food is really, really solid. Â  Though everything was good, these were the standouts: Â the broccoli rabe, burrata, polenta, patatas bravas I definitely want to check out the brunch soon.

My girlfriend and I had dinner here with friends while in NYC for the US Open. S+P has a great atmosphere...not stuck up or super trendy. Â Meat & cheese starter was great, especially the liver mousse. Â Our waiter was very helpful with wine selections. Â Great oyster selection as well. The place is the size of a closet in NYC. But that still won't stop me from coming here. Their pizzas look old, but the other stuff that they have are pretty good! I love their pasta and grilled ham & cheese sandwiches. The people are friendly...always wanting to chat you up...
Why go here when you can go to big wong across the street? The atmosphere here is grosser than the fast paced big wong. Â The food and waiters pale in comparison. Â Just cross the street.

My son wanted to eat in Chinatown- google search gave us this suggestion. Food was cheap! Considering what tourists like us shell out - family of five ate for $10. Overrated. I got the shawarma platter. I was expecting this to be the best thing I have ever tasted (based on the reviews). Yes it was good, but not fantastic. The lamb was good but not succulent. Was edible but I would not go out of my way to eat here. On a side note...I ate this in WA Square Park. The squirrels are PSYCHO!! So I realized very quickly this place is not ideal for pescatarians, but since my significant other is an avid carnivore, I made it work. I just went here for the second time, a few weeks ago, but instead of trying lunch again, we went with my work team for dinner. The dinner was far better than the lunch. We ate at the restaurant in the way back of the store. It was the best Italian food I've eaten outside of Italy. I had ravioli with ricotta and spinach. They were delicious. Great late night dining place. One of the few places open 24 hours in Astoria. Awesome beer and wine list. Had a great brekkie here that I could not finish. Â The place was popular with several people waiting for them to open their doors at 8 a.m. Monday morning. This place is awesome. Yes, a tad pricy for lunch but the sandwiches are amazing and big enough for 2 people. Â Meats are sliced right in front of you and bread is super fresh. Â  Owners are very Italian but that's ok, I am too

I usually reserve my five stars for fine dining experiences, if they live up to my expectations, but I will make an exception for this rustic little italian restaurant tucked a few blocks away from Union Square. Â  I don't think I've had such good pasta since I was in Italy. Â My dining partner and I, got there a bit before 9pm on a Thursday night. I really really want to give Eataly more than three stars but the crowds and the disjointed layout kind of killed my buzz. Sure, the selection is incredible. I got the most delicious cheeses and salami here to take home for Easter. My family (the lucky recipients) and I loved every morsel. But having to elbow people just to get a hunk of parmigiano reggiano was a little stressful. Also pricey. I allowed myself to splurge since I was on vacation, and in the end it's not much more expensive than Zingerman's, but I doubt I would be shopping there on the regular if I lived in NYC. The dry goods, pasta, and bread selection were all equally amazing looking. I was meeting a friend for lunch so I didn't indulge in any onsite eating but I was insanely jealous of all the delicious looking sandwiches and trays of meats and cheeses people had before them. But on the flip-side I was also really relieved to not have to be juggling a plate on top of my basket. Seating here is just as rare as a parking spot in NYC. If you were brave enough to wait for a table (I overheard one couple as they discussed their time) it would take over an hour to get seated. For a casual marketplace? Hello no! I know this is Mario Batali and all (and I worship the ground his orange crocs walk on) but good grief! I got nervous and itchy just looking at all the people crammed up against each other. But at least they looked happy in the throws of culinary ecstasy, so I guess they had that going for them. There are a number of different stations that I found to be pretty confusing to identify amid the throngs of people and I'm having trouble remembering them all. I remember the sandwiches, the gelato, some amazingly fresh looking seafood.....I just felt turned around an overwhelmed most of the time because of the crowd that kept the place from flowing well. I grabbed my stuff, a cooler bag (so smart! made transporting it home on the plane a breeze), and got the hell outta dodge. You can tell that Batali and the other planners of Eataly tried to make this as organized as possible. There are plenty of signs, and the check out process is a breeze. You can only enter in one door and the exit is situated further from the entrance. They attempted to keep it open and airy and fluid. It's just kind of hard to maintain any sort of order when the place is so mobbed. I can't fault Eataly for being popular but I do reserve the right to get claustrophobic when I pop in for some fresh farfalle.

Fantastic!!!

Bobby Flay's newest restaurant. Â I love the layout of the place. Â There is an open kitchen to the left, and the bar is in the middle of the restaurant. Â If I go again, I will order more of the bar options; they are very small portions but very well thought out and prepared!

Good place w good environment but the fish was so bad that i couldn't even believe they served it. Also i asked for pasta to go and waiter said the chef does not take pasta to go. Whyy i asked? mmmmmm. Â joe shanghai. Â the restaurant that first instroduced me to the hot steaming savory soup of porky goodness all wrapped up in a dumpling bun... mmmmmmm. So happy this place opened! Tons of options and even though it's essentially a food court it feels nice, upscale,and clean. The only downfall is some of the employees at nam pang are unprofessional and seem like they don't want to be yhere. But everywhere else I've eaten have been A++

Pretty solid Thai food, the portions are huge, service is generally very snappy (once you are seated), the decor is pretty nice and modern. It's that fucking good. Â Let me begin with that. Â What is? Â Trattoria L'Incontro is. Â I've heard about it for years and it's sat gathering dust on my list of restaurants to visit. Â This is mainly because it's in Queens, and I'm a Brooklyn guy. Â I have no big impetus to come up here. Â However, the other weekend the girl was out of town, and I wanted to go have a great meal somewhere new. Â With Rosario's as a good place to pick up a sandwich for work on Monday, La Guli nearby to pick up dessert after, and the subway a block away, L'Incontro came out on top. Â The place is a lot larger than I expected. Â High ceilings, big open dining area, and a lot of tables. Â Regardless, the place was bustling by 6:30. Â Some people had special occasions, others didn't, some young, some old; it was a good mix. Â I grabbed a table right in front, which was good for people watching. Â I didn't realize it at first, but it reminded me of Italy more so than 9/10 other Italian restaurants--especially those that play up kitchy decor. Â In the back, the chef, Rocco Sacramone, was not just schmoozing people but making sure that the operation was running well. Â My waiter, Carlos, was excellent. Â He was friendly, unpatronizing, and even putting the recitation of the 20 item specials menu aside, he was knowledgeable as well. Â One of the best waiters I've seen in quite some time, and that's coming from an ex-waiter. Â That's a lot of good things to list about a restaurant, and luckily for me, the food was even better. Â  For a starter I got the wild game meatballs special, which are ostrich and venison in a sauce with mushrooms and truffle oil. Â I hadn't had either meat before so it took a little bit to disseminate the different flavors, but I thoroughly enjoyed this dish. Â The ostrich tastes mostly like beef, with the venison adding a slight gaminess and oily aftertaste. Â The mushrooms were delicious, as was the sauce with added a earthiness to complemented the meat well. Â I was a bit disappointed that I only got two balls, but from a pacing perspective it worked. Â This dish paired well with the Nero D'Avola I got by the glass. Â For a pasta, I got the much talked about mezzaluna ravioli, which are stuffed with mascarpone and pesto, and come in a brandy and walnut sauce with shaved asparagus. Â This was an excellent dish! Â The pasta tasted homemade as it was, and had the perfect amount of bite to it. Â The filling was rich, creamy and flavorful, and contrasted well with the nutty flavors of the asparagus and sauce. Â Thank you Yelpers for the recommendation here. Â For my main, I got a red snapper special which came in a chickpea puree with spinach and chantarelle mushrooms. Â  The fish was absolutely delicious and cooked perfectly. Â The sauce was very simple; the chickpea sauce acted as a slightly creamy, salty contrast to the rich flavor of the fish, with the spinach and mushrooms adding in a little variety. Â I thought the mushrooms could've stood out more, but it was still an excellent dish. Â I was too full for dessert, but got an espresso and sambuca. Â It was just like what I'd had in Italy; full of rich flavor. Â I did not bother using the sambuca on the coffee, as it wasn't needed. Excellent meal at an excellent restaurant. Â I saw one reviewer compare the owner, Rocco Sacramone, to Mario Batali. Â I would consider that a downgrade; Batali is happy just to rake in the money, and only once have I been bowled over by a dish at one of his restaurants (Manzo). Â Rocco is doing it the right way, as he was omnipresent in the back of the room, making sure that the everything was going perfectly. Â More importantly he was succeeding, as there weren't many holes to poke into this dining experience. Â Most importantly, all of his dishes were nuanced, wowed in different ways, and were worth the money. Â By the way, while the pricing isn't low by any means, it's very fair for what you get. Â Going all out, this dinner cost a little under $80 without tip; you could easily do $50-60pp if you're more conservative. Â I love old school Italian, but sometimes a change in pace is needed. Â L'Incontro earns its reputation as one of the best Italian restaurants in NYC.

I don't understand what the fuss is about. This place is mediocre at best. The food was pretty bland, had to salt everything. The only thing that was outstanding was the octopus. For good greek food there are much better choices in Astoria....like MP and Agnandi.

Have come here many times the last few years. The food here is really excellent, always consistently good. The service is also excellent. Always order the specials as the menu is quite underwhelming to read. We had a guest last time who said this was the best meal she ever had. The atmosphere is also very romantic and the place has the feeling of a "special" night out. BUT ....since the last visit they have hung a gigantic TV on the back wall and it really turned me off. I CANNOT IMAGINE WHY THEY WOULD DO THIS. There was football on TV. Its hard to imagine making one change that would change the environment so much. I dont think I want to go back...its that off putting to me. But the food is fantastic......please get rid of the freakin TV Rocco !!!!

I can understand how maybe like 30 or even 20 years ago, Lombardi's would have been considered amazing because I'm sure there would have been nothing like it. But now, seriously? Really? I'm with Lizz K. on this one -- I just don't get it. Nowadays, it's easy to find good pizza. The thin crust is too thick and also too bland (along with the sauce). I ordered a small sausage and wild mushroom pizza. I don't know what was wild about the ubiquitous ordinary white button mushroom that you find in any grocery store, unless they were gang banging mushrooms. The pizza was delivered to my table soggy. The raspberry Italian soda was watered down and the soda water was already half flat. I had the privilege of paying $33 for this terrible meal. Listen, if I'm laying out this kind of money for food, then it better be good, or at the very least decent. Lombardi, the sun has long set on you. Go along now and let another more worthwhile establishment take your place.

Based on food alone, this place is a 4. Throw in price and it goes to 3.5 stars. Throw in the fact that they couldn't serve alcohol when I was there on Saturday, that drops the gastropub down to a 3. But since I didn't want a drink, I didn't care so back to 3.5 stars. Add 0.5 stars for the boobs I stared at during dinner and we're back to 4. Bone marrow appetizer. I'd order just this and maybe a fried egg for extra awesome and be happy all day long. Chori burger: $17 for a beef & longanisa patty, yam fries and $2 extra for one egg? Pricey! Oh well, wasn't my money we were spending so I ate the burger and maybe 1/3 of the fries. The burger is pretty damn tasty w/ that hit of sweet longanisa cut by the pickled veg (might've been atchara). The bun holds all this deliciousness together, but couldn't contain the runny yolk, but that's what dipping is for. The kamote fries are sweet and tasty and DENSE! That's why I could only eat 1/3 of them. That and the previously enjoyed bone marrow w/ sinangag. Kalamansi & seltzer: tastes just like sweetened kalamansi juice and seltzer. Refreshing! Bonus: the waitress touched my bum. Not glancingly either.

Do it. Great place to take friends or a casual date. Nice and cozy decor, relaxed vibe, tasty food, and surprisingly inexpensive considering the portion sizes. If you live in the area (as I do), this will definitely be one of your go-to neighborhood spots. I recommend the chicken empanadas as an appetizer. Great flavor, nice size, and only $2! As far as the rest of the menu, I've eaten here on several occasions and ordered something different each time...I've yet to be disappointed :)

One of the best burgers in the city--if not the best. Â Went there for brunch with some friends from Greenpoint. Â They all got egg-y brunch things (which were fantastic), but I'm not gonna lie, my burger may have been the strongest order (fried pineapple ring, pickled beets, harissa chili mayo, sunnyside up egg...like whoa). Bloody mary was delicious, too. Â Wish I could have had more time to explore the cocktail menu (looked quite creative).

How is this not rated the best pizza in NY? It beats Grimalidi's by a mile, and that crappy tourist joint Lombari's. Here's the deal. This is about Pizza. Not salad, aps, dessert, side of fries, whatever you're used to getting. Just Pizza. I theorize that since they focus on the pizza, they can perfect that and not worry about the rest. The servers are all these tough talking chicks who don't take shit from anyone, but you've got to respect that. They get the job done and fast. The owner is the one back there making each pie with love in candle light. My only complaint is they are always playing cheesy italian-american music. One time I went in and they had some old school opera which was much much better for such a romantic and sophisticated atmosphere. So they don't take reservations in advance so show up early or wait.
Fantastic authentic food and Sabrina the bartender is wonderful, pleasant and knowledgeable! You MUST try the sweet n' sour chili sauce!

Okay, fine. I'm another one of those people totally smitten by Roberta's. It's a little overpriced but worth it for the outstanding food and fun log-cabin-esque vibe. Added bonus: the hipster waiters are not the mean kind. Kind of strange, I know. But the only thing now is that they're too popular for their own good. The last couple times I've been, I've had to wait for over an hour. The back patio bar where you wait for a table is definitely their saving grace. One time my friend and I sat next to the NY Times food reviewers who ordered literally one of each thing on the menu and kept giving us tastes of everything. Of course it was all delicious. Saw their stellar review like a week later.

It took us a little bit to find the place of America's first pizza but we were very happy with our choice! The location is quaint and historic and you know if the walls could talk there would be millions of stories! We enjoyed our pizza very much - would have liked a bit more sauce and our crust was more burned than we would have preferred but it still tasted very good!
Always great food, great service and long lines.

I had a list of dishes I was craving, and have to come back again to try them all. What upset me was that Saturday afternoon that I went, they said they did not have the lambshank with orzo available. It looked so good from Yelpers' pictures. We did get the octopus chickpea salad, and the octopus was soft, with a bite (some like it slightly crisp and chewy, but here, it was as if it were massaged and beaten to obtain such tenderness). We then got the scallops that came with capers, spinach, and dried cherries. This was an excellent pairing of flavors, but it would've been perfect if they seared the scallop in the brown butter a tad longer. Then came the Greek paella with shellfish, spicy lamb sausage, and orzo. Don't expect this paella to have the crispy layer of toasted rice on the bottom. It is orzo, after all (so it's more like a seafood pasta than a paella). It was rather like a cioppino/bouillabaisse. Overall, service was excellent, and the room was comfortable. I want to come back for the rabbit dumplings (even though I've had them at Kefi in the UWS).

One of the must-go in St. Marks if you can get a spot. The food is Japanese but with a western twist that makes it interesting and unexpected. They also have a wide selection of Japanese tea. Plus, the desserts are very tasty as well (again with a somewhat western twist). The atmosphere is also very well, a good place to come with a small group of friends while drinking tea and catching up on life. Definitely one of my favorite places to go to in town.

I'd have to say mediocre at best. Â Came with my parents for my mom's birthday and ordered: Mushroom Crunch, Pork Butt, Papaya salad, and Chicken wraps for appetizers and Green Curry with Shrimp, SK Vegetable with Tofu, Pad Thai with Chicken and crab fried rice. Â  It was just eh. Â flavor profiles fell flat and I've had far better thai in the city....

What do the following have in common? -"Spartans! Ready your breakfast and eat hearty... For tonight, we dine in hell! " -"Just who are the people are we designing this car for? Â Sportsmen.*" -A perfect game in bowling They are, respectively: -Line from the movie "300" -Ad for the Chrysler 300 -A score of 300 What does this mean? Â Then went for a trio of dips with pita: -Whipped Spicy Feta- delicious with extra virgin olive oil, lemon, crushed red pepper Â  -Romesco-my favorite, with red peppers, almonds, garlic Â  -And finally, traditional tzatziki-spectacular For meals, my two friends had the salad with shrimp. This place is adorable. The BBQ chicken salad is Delicous!!!! Cornbread croutons, soooooooooo good.
Hole in the wall. Worth the price, go with the classic--green. The spicy one was good, but not as good as the classic.

Story: The legendary place where "Friends with Benefits" was filmed...Oh! And where there's Cuban food too! Exploring around Nolita, I took a break to check this hyped place out. The break was definitely worth it. Ambiance: The setup is really like a cafe/diner feel. Very compact and intimate. There are actually two rooms, one to eat and one to go. It probably can fit Â 20-30 people. With the decorations, music, and smell of the food you'll immediately feel like you're away from the concrete jungle but in some diner in Cuba. Food: Corn (Recommended) Freshly made corn with chili powder, lime & cotija cheese. Served hot and juicy. Additional seasoning is provided. A great on the go meal Limeade (Recommended) Appropriately sour with every sip. I would just ask to easy up on the ice so I would have more to drink. Customer Service: The service was fairly fast. I guess they know how that their corn is pretty popular. Overall: I give this place 4.5 stars. The wait wasn't too long, the food was served fresh, and the feel was pleasant. A great place to take a quick break but my next visit, I hope to lunch in and try their entrees. Advice: -Beat the rush hours, this small place can get packed. -If it's on the go, go to their to-go site right next door.
4.5 stars. Best ramen ever!!! Minus 1/2 star for the 50 minute wait.
pizza is pretty good however the place is a dark sh**hole. but best pizza your gonna get that late in Cali

REALLY good mediterranean food - very authentic and delicious. Â The Kafte Kabob was delicious and the platter was very beautiful and colorful and served a huge helping of hummus, baba ghanouh, salad and amazing mediterranean rice. Â Also had the Lamb pizza which was beyond words - SO delicious. They gave us dessert on the house which was very sweet. The outdoor seating is a nice touch in the front. Â I definitely recommend if you are tired of the run of the mill hipster joints in Williamsburg. Coming from a mediterranean background myself, this place does a great job.

Just opened in the beloved Gascogne space, this French feeling spot with a garden in back is back. The menu has classics and updated classics which are quite enticing. The restaurant was getting ready at opening time and putting finishing touches before service started. Â  Bread is from Sullivan St. bakery.- yum. Â A little amuse bouche of scallop & pistachio was delish. Ate: Skate w/savoy cabbage with mustard seeds- $26 Potatoes souffle- $10 Also got to try the potatoes gasconaise with foie gras. The food came out pretty quickly usually a red flag, but all was quite good. Especially enjoyed the cabbage- winey and mustardy. The souffle potatoes with goat cheese are light airy fried potatoes- prettty amazing...........More to try and already Chelsea has embraced this newbie!

I recommend the Classic -- (ask for it spicy) with an ice coffee to be had while sitting on the window facing table/stool, watching east village passes by. Pick a day, any day, it will be a good day for a banh mi.

It's hard for me to give any noodle joint in Chinatown more than 3 stars. For one, the service is always served with a bit of grumpiness. And two, the bathrooms are never clean. That being said, there are maybe 100 wonton noodle joints in Chinatown. I've been to many, but the one I always come back to is this one. Mind you I've been coming here since I was a kid, maybe at least before I turned 10. I'm touching the edge of 40 now so you can imagine how long this restaurant has been here. The quality has gone down over the years, but Â it has been very consistent. The Good: - Wonton / Shanghai Dumpling / Noodle Soup - Beef Innards Noodle Soup - Shredded Pork and Fermented Egg Congee - Pork Potsickers - Steamed Pork Buns - Price The Bad: - A huge attraction for tourists. - Idiots who order beef and broccoli in a restaurant with the word "Wonton" in the name. - It's in Chinatown (see above for explanation)

Visited Sweet Science for my friend's birthday this weekend for the first time. Service was ON Â POINT... whilst we just had buffet style appetisers- Â It was deeeeelish. Loved the venue, loved the art, loved our Irish server, absolute superstar. Can't wait to come back. Slainte!
Wait is not really worth it. Â Pizza is ok. Â There are others that are better.
Super crowded. But with that being said, it is a great brunch place.

My favorite ramen place in the city! The ramen is a bit expensive ($15+) but they are large bowls and one order comes with more than enough food to be split with two people. I also recommend the pork buns, which are the best pork buns I have ever had (and that's saying a lot because I don't even like pork buns!) and the chicken wings on the appetizer menu. The only reason I could not give them four stars is because it is a bit expensive and I HATE the fact that they don't take reservations! We always end up waiting 1 hour plus to eat here, but the fact that we (and so many others) do just tells you how good this place is!

The green bean and asparagus apps/small plates are good. Salmon is crisp and cooked perfectly. My seabass had a bone in it that did a small number on the roof of my mouth. It was the only bone in it but truthfully I didn't finish it because of it. The service is very nice and polite and the food is fresh which still makes it 4 stars for me. It's small so not ideal for very large groups.

Although the specials list is ridiculously overwhelming, the food is absolutely superb. Great for date nights and fancy dinners. The waiter was extremely welcoming, friendly, and knowledgeable. I have no idea how he remembers the list of 18763478 specials...

Above and beyond the best chicken gyro I've ever had in my life. The fries are no slouch though, and the jalapeÃ±o and [white] cheddar dip esta muy delicioso. It's a small place, with two tables and four bar stools. The door also stubbornly refuses to stay shut, which is a problem when it's single digits outside. But the staff are super friendly and the whole presentation is done with aplomb. $9.50 for a chicken gyro with fries, or $7.50 for most other sandwiches.

Ugh.. Yelp must be deleting unfavorable reviews because I reviewed this spot ages ago. The namesake of this restaurant really got my mouth watering, but after much anticipation it was quite the let down. Yea.. its one of the 'nicer' and more 'hip(ster)' restaurants in the hood, but the portions are TINY, the service is slow, it is not very vegetarian friendly and the whole experience left something to be desired. The restaurant is sit down and 'nicer' than most Sunnyside establishments, but its still a little tacky. Looks like it was converted from an old school Italian restaurant, and its not sure what kind of restaurant it wants to be. Bacon popcorn - they should offer a non-bacon alternative for vegetarians. Garlic or caramel? Something easy and cheap. BF does eat bacon but wasn't going to town on the popcorn so I took that as a sign it wasn't anything too special. Oxtail - my poor bf, this thing was ITTY BITTY and unimpressive. He said it was pretty good but definitely did not live up to the hype it gets. Parpadelle Pasta - Almost flavorless and again TINY. Prices would be fine if portions weren't so small. You really have to order at least 3 dishes a person here, and though its not crazy expensive, it adds up pretty quick. Lychee Panna Cotta - I was super excited about this from all the pictures and reviews. I love everything Lychee! I did not love this. Super underwhelming. Sorbet trio - pretty mediocre quality sorbet. Not a fan of the texture. Come here if you love meat and small portions.

What a drastic difference and disappointment. After my last visit to Gramercy Tavern, I absolutely could not WAIT until I could come back for another meal. Â I wanted to show off what NYC had to offer, I wanted to treat someone special to a truly unique and memorable experience, and based on what I experienced last time, I thought Gramercy was definitely the place to make that happen. Unfortunately, I was wrong. Again, we were in the dining room: Â the service this time was polite and well timed, but otherwise nothing like the hospitality we had received at our last visit (unfortunately Solomon was NOT our server this time). Â It lacked that same personal touch that captured our hearts the last time we were here, and instead we felt like we were at any other restaurant with well mannered staff and good lighting. The food was also less impressive. Â Rather than have the three course menu like we did last time, we decided to splurge with our out-of-town guests and treat ourselves to the seasonal tasting menu. Â The food was just not as impressive this time around. Â The execution of each dish was precise and on point as one might expect, but the food was missing the depth and complexity of flavours that had caught my attention the first time around. Â The squid ink tagliatelle, for example: Â sounds amazing on paper, but ultimately tasting very much like a simple pasta dish that did nothing to capitalize on the several exciting elements that were there. Seasoning was marginal on a few plates, but what ultimately let me down was a lack lustre finish with the apricot panna cotta and tapioca pudding dessert. Â Served simply in a small glass cup, it just seemed far too pedestrian, bordering on "made ahead of time", for a place like Gramercy. Â If there was something redeeming in the flavours or textures, I could care less about the presentation - but there was not. Â  Needless to say, this was not the "knock your socks off" meal that I had hoped for my guests, both with regard to service and food. Â And even after 5 courses and a dessert, we still ended up going out for hot dogs and nachos afterwards because sadly, we were simply just not satisfied.

Great! Food was even better than the rip off places that charge you $20 for Daeji Bulgogi! I like the self serve deal - and you definitely get great quality! Lots of Korean people in there - so it obviously is good. Must try if you're in NYC and want some Korean food!

I've been here on two separate occasions and on both I have experienced delicious food and drinks. The first time I came I dont remember what I ordered exactly, it was a pasta with mushrooms I believe. It was delicious and the wine was great as well. The service was perfect as well, the waitress came around not too many times but was available when we needed her. The second time I had a salmon dish with vegatables. The salmon was delicious!! Moist, flavorful and plenty. I had the white sangria with this dish and it was delicious! The only cons, which I won't substract stars because they are not the establisment's fault would be: - It's on avuenue B, so quiet a walk from an train. - Crazy girl loud group that spilled their pitcher of sangria near us and kept interrupting another party's grandmother's birthday party!

So, my husband wanted a greek salad. Â He was at the point of "starvation" so compromising wasnt in his vocabulary. I conned him into Wafa's by telling him he would be able to get what he wanted. Â He wasnt happy. Â I ordered right away some fried cauliflower and things started to look better. Â It was DE-lish. Â There was no denying it. Â Next came the meats and the baba-g. Mouth watering --- Â we chowed down. Â The food was so damn good that by the end of our meal my husband was planning our return trip and who we were bringing with us. Â  The food, the "family" aka staff was all fantastic. The reviews are right. Â FANTASTIC!
Every now and then I eat somewhere that reminds me why Anthony Bourdain has the best job in the world. Â This is one of those places.

Is Momo Sushi Shack the best Sushi spot in the Five Bouroughs? Maybe. It is definitely the place to bring people to when they visit the neighborhood. I strongly recommend the Ramo Roll (vegetables, cilantro and spicy tofu mousse) -- even if you are an omnivore. It's a little pricier than most Sushi places, but you get what you pay for.

had a pleasant meal here. sidewalk dining was great for people watching. waiter was a little inattentive. tuna burger was univentive and lacking in flavor. despite this i would go back and give odeon another try.

This place is fantastic... Â a hidden gem in the heart of midtown. They have a wide variety of noodle dishes, which are super tasty.They have an even wider variety of sake. But the best item on their menu is definitely their chocolate cake!! Best I have ever eaten in my life!! I cannot give them the fifth star though, because of the lack of gluten free items in their menu (wish they would offer some more sushi...)

Wifey took me out for a birthday date that included basketball and dinner aftwerwards. Â It was an eary afternoon game so she decided to go with an early dinner afterwards. Â After we walked over from MSG, we found ourselves at a very quiet Lulu & Me. Â We were greeted very nicely and were told to not mind their staff running around because they had a party later in the evening. Â He told us that it didn't mean that we should rush. Â He was really nice and made us feel welcomed. For appetizers we went with the ricotta dsh and the shrimp& cod cakes. Â A+ for both of them. Â The ricotta dish came with some pieces of bread to scoop up the cheesy goodness. Â We also had an excellent Cab Sau (it paired better with my meal, sorry to my wife). Â For our main course she had the sea scallops and loved them, especially the red quinoa. Â My dish was the skirt steak and it was cooked a perfect medium. Â We were pretty stuffed (the game included a few beers) so dessert was not going to happen. Â However, we were treated to a glass of wine by the restaurant (I wish I could remember the type). We were lucky to have the place to our own, but even if we didn't the food itself stands on its own. Â It truly felt like a private party for two and the staff could not have been any better. Â What a wonderful birthday.

Dear Umami Burger: Welcome to NYC, where people actually WORK. Â WE are not trust fund babies who have all the time in the world to sit and eat at a restaurant. Â If we are lucky enough to even run out to get lunch, you better believe it will be to go. Â Walked in today only to be told the place doesn't do "to go" orders. Â Seriously?! Â IT'S A BURGER JOINT!! Â I guess all the hype about this place is overdone. Â I haven't tried it, and never will cause I don't have the time to sit around in a restaurant. Â If I do have time, I'll be going to a restaurant nicer than a burger joint. Â At least we have Shake Shack with delicious burgers and an understanding of NYC life.

Penelope I was encouraged to visit this midtown brunch staple from a friend of mine. Â @Penelope welcomed me with a Â 25 minute wait at 215p on this Super Bowl Sunday - ouch. Â I was seated swiftly though (under wait time) and the host took care of some linger gals who wanted to stand behind me at the bar, whew! Â  Crowd is midtown yuppies and you've invited them over to your grandmothers kitchen for an intimate brunch. Â Great old cabinets and antique coat/ hat hooks I appreciated. Â Enjoyed the coffee station while you waited for a table, great touch. Â  Bloody Mary - served in a white wine glass and made with sake. Â Yes sake. Â No condiments yet very spicey and tasty. Â The one complaint I have about the cocktail - too much horseradish, kept getting caught in the straw. For brunch, went with recommendation of salmon wrapped fresh farm poached eggs with a side of chicken apple sausage. Â Good presentation. Â Chicken sausage was fairly bland - not a fan. Â Mixed green salad served with eggs with these interesting raisins. Â The forementioned fruit was not on the menu and for friends who know me, you know this is a major pet peeve of mine - identify the fruit!! Â  Salmon wrapped eggs very good...nothing super unique about them but well poached. The music playlist seemed to support the struggle the restaurant has -- one minute Fleet wood Mac/ Steve Miller Band (thank you), next two songs dance club mixes. Â Fun quirky logo ( and good merchandise line) yet nothing "wow" about this menu. Penelope gets a 6 on the #brunchbelle scale - I'd come back., its a solid meal but nothing to write home about.
Even though we arrived a few minutes late....they sat us. Guys are Friendly and the food (had the Ropa Vieja) was especially god. This place is the real deal. Will return when in Corona.

As a Californian, I can say with utter conviction that this is one of the best taco trucks in NYC. The meat is seasoned so well, the staff is very friendly and the food is priced like California. The best part is that they deliver! One of my friends lives down the street from this truck, which was how I heard of it and thank God for her. This past 4/20 this same friend hosted a kick it party at her place, and of course we all had to order from Tacos El Bronco for the main course. I think we ordered about 80 tacos (I'm not kidding) for delivery, and they were even nice enough to throw in some extras! Without a doubt every taco was devoured, and every tummy was satisfied. I have a special place in my heart for Tacos El Bronco. Eating their food makes me feel like I'm back at home. :)

When I first ate at this place I said, hey its cramped and people are waiting outside after putting their names on an imaginary list, these people done lost their minds. Then I discovered the to go place next door. Â Mexican Corn? Â I was like, yo my man, is that mayo on that corn? Â wtf? Â Are you serious. Â Nah, no thanks. Â Then eventually I relented. Â Rite of Passage. Â Seriously. Â It is amazing. Â I sometimes drive to this place just to get the corn (dont do so during the week before 7 cause you will get an expensive ticket, take my word for it.) Â  Steak sandwich has a sauce and is decent. Â Could use a little more steak, but hey. Â The place isnt expensive but for the amount of steak in the sandwich, it leaves you scratching your head. Â  However, the real deal is the CORN!!! Â Go there, get the corn. Â Take a friend and get a couple. Â Dont let them wrap it in the foil cause u lose the cheese (yes i said cheese). Â take those ears and sit outside. Â enjoy the day and your corn. Â You will be glad you did!

Fantastic experience all around, I highly recommend this place. I went with a colleague, we sat at the Chef's Counter (which was very cool.) It was a great experience all around: -Creative menu -Good food -Friendly and attentive staff -Nice ambiance and decor Standard West Village pricing for the fare, no complaints there. I tried the special appetizer which was spaghetti squash (and somethiat If the weather permits check out the back garden!

This place is fantastic! And it is BYOB which I always appreciate. At least if the wine is bad it is my fault :) Everything tasted good. Slightly untraditional take on the escargots but beautiful. And you have to try the Tournedos Rossini. It might be one of the best things I've ever eaten.
This is my happy place! The food is great, the drinks are great, and the staff is about the friendliest bunch of people you can know! My husband and I go there at least once a month.

Was here with a bunch of friends and family on a Thursday night for some random drinks after dinner. It's a really cute place, not too intimate not too large, and plays great music. If you're deciding on a venue to celebrate a birthday with friends and still want to be able to talk to them, hang out, listen to music, Ugly Kitchen will be a great place.

I must say I was a little bit skeptical before trying Totto Ramen. I was like yeah, a ramen is a ramen you know, noodles and soup, so why is everybody so crazy about this place. Now I admit: I was wrong. Maybe it's due to the 5 min wait when we were expecting more like 2+ hours but still: it was amazing. And I will be happy to wait 2 hours to eat another of these delicious ramen. What an incredible experience!!
yummy!

This is what I think - if you didn't rate them 5 stars, you either visited them at a real bad time, pissed some of the staff off, lost your appetite after waiting 50 minutes, or I don't know...you were having a piss-poor day. These guys ROCK. Â Lamb platter, chicken platter, combination platter, they are all equally awesome and indescribably satisfying considering you just spent $6. Â Falafels - I don't dig their falafels. Â These cart boys are not known for falafels. Â If you went there for falafels, you're probably dining at many other restaurants and ordering the wrong stuff. Â They probably offer falafels on the menu for the girlfriends who were dragged there by their boyfriends and never dreamed of eating what initially may appear to be very insanitary and borderline in violation of all health department codes. Â  Yes, their hot sauce can be too hot. Â At times, it gets so darn hot that my eardrums and head actually start to feel funny. Â But that's ok. Â It's all part of the 53rd & 6th experience. The meat/rice platters are so good that some of my ibanker friends that work in the area eat late night snacks here 3 times a week. Â Of course, they all make $500,000 a year and can afford to walk down a block to Del Frisco's and eat their porterhouse three meals a day...but they don't. Â They rely on the cart to satiate their hunger. Now, health related concerns. Â I'm sure the place can modify a few things here and there to improve the perception by those that haven't had their platters. Â However, I don't think it's all too bad. Â I personally feel fine eating here than going to Taco Bell that's had rodent issues for the past 4 years. Â One thing though....I hope the cashier guy doesn't handle the food though. Â It does make me lose my appetite for the 30 seconds during the interaction. Â Of course, my appetite runs full-steam as soon as he hands over the food. Â  Anyone visiting NYC really should try the place out. Â It's cheap, not too slow if you visit during non-peak hours, and most importantly, the food is addictively delicious.
Great tasting Â dumplings! Cheap and yummy! Â Great for snacks

This is the one of the best Sushi Restaurant in NYC!! Service is ok (to be honest not that good) but Sushi is superior. I do not need to go back to Japan for great Sushi. If you are sushi lover you should come and try!! It is worth paying. I paid about $120/person with one drink. Â 2 hour limitation is not comfortable however if you want to have Sushi for affordable price, this is the place you should come.

This review might be premature, because my friends and I didn't end up sitting down for entrees. We were about to, but the computer system messed up our reservation, making us wait too long for our table, so we left. While we were waiting, though, we tried the: Guacamole - pretty good. Needed more lime. Flautas de pollo - delicious. Tostadas de carne - FRIGGIN AMAZING. Like WHOA. Tiacoyo con hongos - interesting taste. Get if you like mushrooms. Atmosphere is super hip and fun. Loved the decor. Go with friends or on a date. Go for your birthday dinner. Go for a fun weekend dinner.

The pizza is awesome here. The slices are huge! One is probably enough per person although while you are eating it you are craving the next slice already. Artichoke is the one to get. Although theres crab and also regular (margarita) and sicilian. But seems like if u got Artichoke i was plenty happy with. Only knock on this place is there's no where to sit and its basically a hole in the wall. And on a cold day it prob drives away some biz but i guess that's great for people willing to freeze and eat in the cold. If this place was bigger and had seating, would probably get more 5 stars.
One of the coolest spots I have been to. The Pork Betty may be the best bite I have ever had. The Lotus Root is awesome.So is the sushi. Great vibe, chill area..great value!!!

The service is usually fine but the food is subpar. I've been to the restaurant a few times and most of the food is dry and/or tasteless. The one and only reason to go there is the amazing cheesecake. Skip the dinner and visit just for dessert.

First confession: This review is about a year old but Dom doesnt change too much so I wouldnt worry Second confession: I don't like pizza. I mean it's ok and I will eat it but it's not the passion that some Yelpers have for it and argue points over it. Just not my fave dish. Â So that being said I wanted to try the famous Difara's simply because it's a NY legend. Now I have tried the hyped pizzas of Grimaldis and Totonnos and hated them. I cant stand that burnt bottom taste. To me I would eat a slice of freaking Papa John over those gourmet crap pies that Yelpers do cartwheels over. So that being said I didnt expect much from Di Fara as me and a coworker set out across Brooklyn on a weekday late afternoon. I guess this is the time to come because on a wednsday at 3pm there wasnt many people and we waited about 15 minutes or so. The whole time my buddy was griping "oh I cant believe we have to wait, this is bull I can go to that pizza place on the corner and get a slice in a minute" this went on the entire wait as we watched Dom, oblivious to the people around him make his pies. Putting his hands right in the hot oven, cutting the fresh basil, shaving the Parmesan, drizzling the olive oil. Â One thing I love is food ceremony, craft.This is why I love Japanese food so much, the artistry of it and Dom is an artist. Â So we get 2 slices each. My complaining friend takes a bite, pauses, swallows, looks at me and says "you know what...this is effing good pizza". He literally ate his words and we both ate the slices pretty fast. I loved it as it wasnt all burnt and tasted so fresh, i love basil (grow my own) and olive oil so this made it taste far better than any other slice I had before. Â  A year later and I sadly have not returned because it's in freaking Midwood and I wont travel that far for Pizza, Any pizza but alas Â the memory remains...

Ok, so, when I checked the menu after a friend picked this place for brunch, I was scared, and pissed at myself for not checking the menu sooner and vetoing the spot. I don't do strange foods well, and Filipino food definitely fell into this realm for me. BUT MY GOD was I surprised with all of the deliciousness. The servers were helpful and attentive, and the decor was fun and cute. No one made you feel dumb for not knowing what things on the menu were. I had the iLog breakfast with tapsilog - I figured with steak and eggs I couldn't go wrong, but I went beyond not wrong and into very very tasty. The steak was perfectly marinated and cooked, and the egg over the garlic rice was divine. My friend had the chicken and waffles - I tried a bite of each and they were uh-mayzing, and I don't have any shame so I will admit that whatever syrup comes with the waffles, I was eating it with a freaking spoon out of it's little jug. It wasn't like maple syrup or waffle syrup but it was so, so good. Super, excellent meal. I'll be back to try other things.

Came here with my work team, I think it is hard to get a reservation, and the place isn't that big; however, the food was excellent, service is good, and prices are reasonable for NYC. Â Will definitely return. Â Its kinda in a touristy area, but the atmosphere is nice and they have a list of different wines for $25 a bottle which is great.

Go here. Has the best prime rib sandwich on earth . I'd rather eat this than a philly cheese in Philly. Marketplace is the best. Also dined upstairs at the rooftop beer garden ... had the $90 sample for 5. Still thought the prime rib was the best. Can't stop thinking of it.... total fat talk !

Zutto restored my faith in ramen. Â I've always held a deep hatred for Ippudo (yeah, I said it) because they pour at least half a pound of salt into their ramen bowls and their noodles are sub par at best. Â I've always felt like an outsider since that place has 1000+ top notch reviews and I'm the only one who thinks they deserve two stars max. Â But it looks like I've finally found my happy place! Space is vast, and they have outdoor dining too with tables and chairs so you can eat and people-watch passing the neighborhood. Â We walked in during late afternoon and it was pretty empty, so our waitress was super attentive. Â Maybe a little too attentive. Â It got to the point where she kept staring at us and we started getting nervous. Â Anyway! -Pork Belly Buns: Â Ughhhh, so good. Â We were tempted to try the exotic options with kobe beef and whatnot, but I stuck to my guns and went along with the pork belly buns with miso mayo. Â They did NOT disappoint. Â The pork Â was done perfectly, and it was so soft. Â Definitely one of the best pork buns I've ever eaten. Â The bun was sooo chewy and the miso mayo is an awesome sauce to go with it. Â I could see why people go crazy for it. Â We finished it up in 2 seconds! -They do honor the free Asahi draft with your Yelp check in (and cheerfully so) so don't forget! -Spicy Miso Ramen: Â I was afraid this one might come out super salty, as it usually is with ramen restaurants, so I braced myself. Â But thank God it wasn't. Â The spiciness was to a decent degree so I wasn't drinking water every 5 seconds. Â Noodles were perfect, and I could definitely taste the fresh ginger in my ramen. Â I also tried his Tonkotsu ramen, and the pork belly literally falls off the bone because it's so tender. Â It also wasn't as salty and milky as I feared it would be. Â  We were still fishing up the baby noodles at the bottom of our bowl towards the end, so we decided to do a kaedama for two. Â That was a big (and awesome) mistake. Â They bring out an extra bowl of noodles, and it's literally another bowl of ramen when you dump it into your soup. Â It's ridiculous. Â I almost passed out. Â We couldn't order dessert, let alone even look at the menu. One negative thing. Â When the check came out, I saw that my miso ramen came out to $15. Â It's actually $12, so I told the waitress and she apologized and fixed it for me. Â Otherwise i would've paid an extra $3 (hard times?). Â Always scrutinize your bill. All in all, it's a highly recommended place to get your ramen fix! Â I'll definitely be coming back, I just wish it wasn't located so far from me :(
The food is quite homey. Nothing fancy or imaginative but really satisfying.
Amazing authentic food. Makes me really miss China with its fantastic flavors. Also has some great beers on tap.

Recommended by our hotel concierge and was pleasantly surprised by the reception, friendly bartender from Miami and the personal touch by the wine connoisseur. Â  We got there around 4:15 just in time for the 1/2 price Happy Hour (Wine / Beer) and then was seated at a nice table near the fireplace. Â  Food was outstanding as well as the service. Â  We will be back the next time we're in NY.

This place looks like it could be in Tokyo, and that's also what my Japanese friend said about it. "I feel like I'm in Tokyo!". The service is friendly (as it should be, given the Japanese "customer is god" idea). They have a great variety of teas, interesting pastries, everything is made there (as can be seen by the huge kitchen in the back), and they also serve savory foods, which looked delicious although we didn't try them. Â  I wish they were open for lunch!

Tasting menu was impeccably presented and flavors were complex and fresh. Â The service was on par with quality and beauty of food. Â We were a party of four - two of which did the tasting and two who ordered entree's and appetizers. Â Due to theater times we dined at 5:15 and arrived a few minutes early upon which all staff readied themselves for our party. Â We also had to rush at the end to which we accommodated quickly and graciously. Â Well worth the $$$$

To start, I have two complaints: (1) the divine little falafel balls at are just too damn small, there's no crunch on the outside, it's all just a single simple texture, entirely eliminating one of my favorite components of the dish (2) they really need to expand, there are only a few seats, and even if you're one of the select few lucky enough to wait ten or fifteen minutes to score a chair, both the employees and the customers are constantly rude. Also, I think there's some room for improvement when it comes to the "Hummus," the "Green Falafel," the "Red Falafel," the "Tabouli," the "Israeli Salad," and the "Babaganoush" -- all of which, in my opinion, are unfortunately underwhelming. Now for the accolades and superlatives: (1) The "Harissa" Falafel is outstanding. (2) The "Sabich" Sandwich has pretty much the best eggplant I've ever eaten at a fast food restaurant, and the accompanying hard-boiled egg is prepared to absolute perfection. (3) I'm addicted to their "Tahini," it's wonderfully sharp and rich and comforting. (4) The "Morrocan Carrots" are incredible, simultaneously crunchy and tender. (5) The "Eggplant Salad" with roasted red pepper and tomato is like to crack to me, it's so amazingly good. (6) The "Zahatar Pita," whole wheat is my preference, is terrific. (7) The "Marinated Red Beets," a personal favorite, are always really good.

This may be biased, but it's truthful. I ate here a few weeks ago, with a visiting family member. The food was very good, the (very attractive) staff was insanely nice, and the ambiance was both disarming and interesting. But when I left my birthday card, which inside held a $100 bill, ON THE BAR over night, I was sure it would be gone the next day. In the face of my skepticism, my out-of-town-brother said "who knows, they seemed really nice." To which I replied "they were nice, but this is New York City, dude." The $100 bill was still in the OPENED envelope and the (hopefully single) staff was once again sincerely welcoming, not taking the easy opportunity to make me feel forgetful. Call me old fashioned, but with so many restaurants and bars to choose from in northern Brooklyn, it goes a LONG way to feel a sincerity and warmth from an establishment. Especially one that has so much else going for it.
I am very happy when I come here their service is amazing and I love coming here for brunch. Overall very pleased with the service
I would recommend it def!

I can't believe 53rd and 6th halal has its own review thingamajig. A part of me doesn't want to rave about how good it is because I don't want the line getting any longer than it already is. But I won't be selfish. Go for the combo and their hot sauce is HOT.

My favorite restaurant in the hood. Â Nice atmosphere. Â Seriously, some of the best pizza I've had in NYC. Period. Â Perfect crust, cheese, and sauce proportions. Â The pasta dishes are a hit or miss for me though. Â Save yourself some heartache and make reservations!!! Â The wait can be as long as 2 hours.

All I can say is that you better be starving when coming here because the portions are huge and you will want to finish every bite! Had the burger and it was one of the best I've ever had. It was enormous but I was determined to finish it, it was that good. Cute little place inside and friendly waiters. Love living close to this place.

Came here for dinner on a Thursday night. Place was PACKED and we had to wait around 30 min. Service is kinda slow and tables are packed a bit close together in certain areas but you can't really complain since the prices are so good. Let's get right to the food: - Crispy Chinese watercress salad w/ shrimp, squid & chicken ~ 3 stars Watercress was fried well and very crisp. The dressing was very fresh, tangy, and vibrant with a nice minty undertone. Didn't care so much for the watercress - it was reminiscent of vegetable tempura - and the meats were just ok. The dressing was what really made the dish for me. - Tom Yum soup w/ shrimp and mushroom ~ 3 stars A tiny bit on the sour side. Other than that it was quite flavorful and delightfully light for a hot and sour soup. - Fried soft shell crab w/ shredded green mango sauce ~ 2 stars It was fried well, and you could taste the crab, but much of the flavor of the crab was lost in frying it. The mango sauce was also nothing to write home about. I think my general disdain for fried foods coupled with my high expectation of this dish ruined it for me. - Fried fish topped w/ curry sauce ~ 3 1/2 stars Wonderful. The curry sauce had some vivid citrusy spring flavors - the initial taste on my tongue was a tad too sweet but it had a nice depth of flavor. A bit spicy though. A fire will take place in your mouth if you consume too much of this. - Massaman Curry w/ beef ~ 3 stars Curry didn't taste much different than what you would find at other Thai places. It tastes pretty much as you would expect it to. The beef however, was cooked well - nice and tender. - Coconut Green Curry w/ chicken ~ 4 stars Wow! This curry had clean, crisp, and distinct flavors. It tasted very fresh and you could clearly differentiate the flavors of all the ingredients; this is a very well balanced dish. Chicken was tender and didn't taste too mushy - this made me happy. - SautÃ© Chinese broccoli w/ garlic sauce ~ 1 1/2 stars Since I'm Chinese, I eat sauteed vegetables all the time. This was incredibly blase. Do not order this. - Seafood medley of shrimp, mussel, and squid ~ 1 star I didn't try the shrimp or squid. Â I had a mussel and it didn't taste fresh - bad texture and lacking in flavor. Disgusting. Someone commented the shrimp tasted funny. This dish was so awful, I should have picked it up and thrown it in the trash. Verdict: If I was in the mood for really good curry, I would come here again but depending on the dishes you order, it can be a real hit or miss. I can see why it's so popular though. The food is not bad and the prices are quite good.

not bad... but could be better. went here for both brunch and dinner with groups of friends. they have a wide selection of drinks, if that's what you're looking for. from what i've heard, the raspberry beer is pretty tasty. i had the waffles for brunch (they ran out of the special waffles). also had a chocolate croissant. both good, fresh, but nothing to go out of my way to get. for dinner, i got the salmon so my son could have some. after all the apps we've ordered, we hardly had room for the salmon. managed to eat just the fish, the cous cous was actually pretty terrible. the staff is nice, food is decent, it's family friendly, extensive beer selection and good for groups. so if that's what you're looking for, go for it.
Great food. Reasonable prices. Nice staff. Great neighborhood feel. Loved it and would certainly come back.

I'm not a fan of chain restaurants... but I have to admit Houston's has one of the best Spinach Dips and ribs. Â Ribs so good that they practically fall of the bone. Â Just for the dip and ribs I'm going to have to give it 4 stars.
I like this place, but not for the food. But I love Artichoke dip with bread.

Great food and service from this now classic space in Williamsburg. Here's a a restaurant that cares about good produce. The food is simple but very good. The service matches the food. Highly recommended for brunch and dinner.

Love this place! Â Great food, strong margaritas and cheap beers. Free movies on Sundays, though tough to find seats. It loses Â a star for being so crowded sometimes. It's understandable, I just wish I Had it all to myself.

This place is amazing. That's all I can say. Everything, absolutely everything is over the top beautiful in this restaurant, in every way imaginable. It has to be the most cozy, cute French crepe place outside of Paris. And the food is definitely some of the best I've had. Brunch crepes are $9 at brunch and they'll definitely fill you up. Actually haven't tried any sweet crepes but all of the savory ones are amazing. And at dinner the prices are only a few bucks higher, which makes it well worth it to visit for any meal.
Best Soul Food I've tasted outside of my mother's kitchen! Chicken & Waffles are superb.

Stopped by on a Tuesday night after a couple friends (who don't know each other, and on separate occasions) recommended the place for the good food and good portions. It did not disappoint. We had the tzitziki, broiled scallops, and baby shark. The tzitziki was delicious, the scallops succulent, and shark well-flavored. All if them were large portions. In fact we had to pack some of the scallops and shark bc we couldn't finish. Then they rolled out the complementary dessert - a delicious pudding that I couldn't stop eating even though I was already full. I would highly recommend this restaurant to anyone who enjoys simple good seafood that will also fill you up. (Making a note to self to also explore the non-seafood menu on my next visit.)

With over a 1000 reviews, it's hard to add anything new, but here it goes... By Sir Rennet's well-known "Cheese and Butter theorem", first derived in 1547 by a French mathematician, which states that: Deliciousness Quotient = sqrt(cheesiness + butteriness) * 2.7, its no surprise that the corn on the cob at Cafe Habana was Finger-lickin good. The heaping mound of cheesy butter loaded onto each cob makes it inevitable. (Of course, this corn was also exhibit A for the Gordon Ramsay Rule: "the unhealthiness of the dish is inversely proportional to the deliciousness of the dish). Aside from the corn, the cuban sandwich is pretty darn good and if you're feeling like you should order something "healthy" (which obviously makes no sense), then the portobello goat cheese burrito is also really good. One warning, it may seem like a good idea at the time, but if you go solo in taking down a cuban sandwich, two corn on the cobs, a plate of fried plantains, and a portobello goat cheese burrito, you WILL feel a little sick. In a good way. Not that I'd recommend it though...

Tuk Tuk is pretty good. Thai food for a good price, can't really go wrong with the thai ice tea too. Do careful with the spicy option. Now i might not have the highest spice tolerance, but it's pretty up there. I'm convinced the chef adds pure capsaicin to the food if you ask for spicy, or at least the distilled fire from eruption of Mt. Vesuvius. Really evaluate how much spice you can handle before you blindly say "ya, i'll take that spicy please" Your tongue might spontaneously burst into flames.

GET TAKE OUT AND ALL PROBLEMS ARE RESOLVED! This place only gets five stars because the Blueberry Pancakes are PERFECT. Cakey texture, perfect amount of sweetness, and the additional maple butter doesn't hurt either. The wait is dreadful, I'd suggest take-out, usually takes about 10-15 minutes, this way you don't have to wait two hours.
An excellent brunch place, the egg benedict tasted really good. I didn't enjoy smelling secondhand smoke from another customer sitting at the table next to me though

i love thier pork skewers, they have wonderful service and it is always authentic. It's good to drink iced green tea especially when everything you eat will be grilled. They only take reservations over 5 people I believe.
I love this place the arepas are fresh and the Mami arepa is my favorite, you guys must try.

Though by no means exceptional, Ugly Kitchen is a fun spot, and can be a great beginning to a night out in the east village. It straddles the line between restaurant and bar admirably. Ugly kitchen features a nice (albeit limited) menu with such delights as spicy tomato bruschetta, buffalo wings, pork buns and a variety of entrees presented in a quiet and vast back area. Slightly classier than your typical bar menu, and executed more than satisfactorily. In contrast to many of its neighbors, Ugly Kitchen is cavernous and spacious, and more than accommodating for large groups (of which mine was one of many on the night I was there). The transformation from restaurant to bar is gradual but definite. The lively conversations that marked the start of the meal was replaced by dancing in our seats and yelling at neighbors. Reasonably priced drinks courtesy of a till 9PM happy hour certainly helped grease the wheels and turned our dinner into a party. Of course this is great Â if youre in the mood, but obviously can be annoying if you were looking for a quiet night out or catch up session. If youre looking for a hybrid meal / night out then Ugly Kitchen is fine enough, but make sure you know what youre getting yourself into...

Although they do not take reservations normally, Cafecito will accommodate larger parties. Which is why 8 of us were able to enjoy a wonderful little dinner on a Saturday, with no wait and minimal hassle. We split two of the Saborcito appetizer platters, which is essentially a plate full of fried goodness. Definitely a good start, and a steal at $11. Entree-wise, I think at least half of our party ordered the Churrasco, which is so hard to resist. It's delicious skirt steak cooked to order, served with Chimichurri, rice, beans, and tostones. I get maduros every time, because 9 times out of 10, they are infinitely better than tostones. (That one time is only when you eat at your friend's house in Miami, and her mom is an AMAZING cook.)
