I also got the chance to try the old clothes (Ropa Vieja), and the Pollo Cafecito. Both are stellar, and the latter is SO MUCH more delicious than it looks. Seriously, it looks like thin, dry grilled chicken, but it packs a juicy, flavorful punch. After letting me try some, my friend asked, "Can you yelp about this chicken?" Yes, yes I can.* The best thing about Cafecito is how affordable it is. We had multiple pitchers of sangria, appetizers and entrees, and it was only about $30 a head, with gratuity included. ________ *I also promised to yelp about the techno song that seemed to be on repeat the entire time. That, and the fish sandwich were the only downsides to this meal. It's not bad, just not as stellar as the rest of the food.

was leaving nyc and wanted to try the 1st pizza place. my experience fast to come out... cheese was freshly made but not very flavorful or enough on the pizza sauce was san marzano but had better flavor elsewhere crust was nyc thin style nothing special for the price I would get Di Fara pizza and would never look anywhere else

I've tried this place twice - once in the restaurant and once through delivery. Funny enough, it was my delivery experience that made me a fan of Ngam. The restaurant itself is really cute and cozy. I came here for dinner one night with some friends. It was a weekend, but I think it might've been a Sunday (can't remember) as the place wasn't too crowded and we were immediately seated (4 people). I ordered the zucchini noodle pad thai (I really can't even remember. I ordered one version of the pad thai anyway!). I remember it was tasty, but I've yet to try a pad thai I haven't liked. The portion was quite large, but the dish was a bit pricier than at other Thai restaurants. All in all, I was happy with the experience but a bit let down as this place seemed rather hyped. Fast forward some weeks or months, and I order the Crispy "Laab" with Sesame Sticky Rice (which I can't seem to find on their website menu, but it is listed on delivery.com It exists, I swear.) because I'm craving some Southeast Asian flavors (fish sauce is basically my comfort food). OMG this dish is so good. I had pork and it was so flavorful and tender and didn't remind me of any pork I'd ever had before, but it was fantastic. It's spicy and tart from the lime juice and definitely fish saucey. It comes with a side of sticky rice mixed with black sesame seeds and I assume coconut milk, which is the perfect foil to the spicy, salty pork. I'm still thinking about this dish months later. I even looked up how to make it. Obsessed.
Great, historic burger joint in the heart if least west village. Has Mc Sorley's on tap. The beauty of it is it's simplicity - burgers and beers delivered on plastic plates.

I love the decor in Tuk Tuk, It really sets the mood - fresh, pleseant, elegant, Â casual, peaceful and modern. The food is always delightful and very reasonably priced. Lots of vegetarian options. Lots for everyone. I've taken a few different groups there and everyone has really enjoyed it - which in my experience is quite unusual!

I went here for a family get together, and really enjoyed the food. Â It wasn't THE BEST Italian food I have ever had, but it was definitely very good! Â It's a really nice style place for a large group, we had about 10 people and they sat us at a round table and we shared - just like if we were at home. Â The one thing that was great was the round table! Have you ever been to a restaurant with a large group and all they have is long tables? Â You basically have to play musical chairs or you're stuck talking to 2 people all night!
This place is a whole in the wall..but the food is yummy. Â We had the roti canai and the laksa noodles..so good on a cold day..

Round 2: This time, a friend and I went back for dinner, and there were no seats for the next three hours, so we just seated ourselves at the bar. Â There, we ordered the Salad Nicoise with fresh seared tuna, $24.00, while my friend ordered the stake frites with bÃ©arnaise Â sauce, $34. Â It was no surprise that both dishes were delights to the mouth. Â My salad, which consisted of green beans, hard boiled eggs, tomatos, arugula, anchovies, and a few other ingredients I cannot remember, was topped up with tuna well done and seared in no oil (because I asked for it to be done that way, and they were kind enough to follow my somewhat outrageous health conscious request). Â Despite this, I enjoyed my salad, as the tuna was sushi grade tuna (after having canned tuna for so many years, I could easily tell the difference), and the saltiness of the anchovies blended well with the rest of the salad. Â I felt so French. Â I felt so classy. The steak frites was simply amazing. Â My friend got it done medium rare, and I took a few pieces of her steak dipped in bÃ©arnaise sauce. Â The steak was good quality steak, perfectly juicy, plump, and flavorful. Â I especially liked the sauce; it was well mixed and not overpowering, and the tarragon vinegar was just enough to round off the combination of other ingredients (there was definitely butter and egg yolks). Â Rich and sour and creamy. Â Sooo good. But the highlight of the meal was nothing more than the fries. Â After I told my boss (a huge foodie as well) at work that I had gone to Batharzar and loved it, she recommended that I try the fries. Â And the fries were phenomenal. Â I don't even know why they were so good, but here is a brief description: extremely thin and crispy, with a slight chewiness. Â And quite short as far as how long the fries were. Â And not too greasy. Â I wish I were in New York right now, so I can go back and order those fries again, and figure out exactly what made them so good, what made them my favorite fries in the world. Â Now on to the search for best Chicago fries. Â I heard there were duck fat fries at Sepia near Jefferson Street. Â Time to go there tomorrow...

Ippudo, you have won me over. I never thought something so elementary as ramen noodles could taste so delicious! I had arrived here with a friend on a Friday night around 9 PM. We were expected to wait for 2 to 3 hours until we were seated. With St. Marks just two streets down, I opted to spend my time wisely... by drinking, of course! I returned after two hours and only had to wait 10 minutes before I was seated. We started off the night with Hirata Pork Buns. These are absolutely amazing. The pork is perfectly braised in a tangy spicy sauce. The succulent pork is served on a freshly steamed bun. The Shinomaru Hakata Classic Ramen was a smart decision! Â This is a pork base soup that is simmered with cabbage, mushrooms, scallions, miso, and garlic. The ramen noodles are very dense and pleasantly filling. The shredded pink pickled ginger complimented the soup well. Expect a flavorful and silky soup. My friend ordered the Akamaru Modern with braised pork belly and preserved egg. The Akamaru has a pork base as well, but it tasted a lot differently from the Hakata Classic. The soup is a lot heavier and much saltier. I am not a big fan of the Akamaru and I am hesitant to recommend this dish. Service was spotless throughout the night. Â From the moment we walked in the door, we were greeted in unison by the entire staff with warm hellos in Japanese. We were constantly being taken care of by attentive staff. We did not have to wait that long for our dishes despite that there was a full-house. The interior was embellished with many Japanese accents. Lighting was dim and pleasantly romantic. I would highly recommend Ippudo for date-nights and even casual hangouts.

Upon first glance, this place screams TOURIST TRAP!! Â After all, it's right smack in the ultimate place where tourists congregate in the city. Â But I'm a fair guy and I must say just because it's in Times Square doesn't mean they skimp on the food quality. Here's what's worth grabbing: DELI STUFF: As you'd expect, the pastrami, corned beef et al sandwiches here are pretty solid. Â I actually fancy their pastrami sandwiches because they really do carry a good deal of flavor and the meat is quite tender. Â Pastrami and corned beef combo is also worth checking out, along with the reuben sandwiches. Â Bonus points for also having good pickles, cole slaw and beets on the side for free! Â Their matzo ball soup is also worth checking out. Â It's great on a cold day! BURGERS: Here is where the nice surprise was. Â Their burgers here are tasty, juicy and they are even better when you throw some sauteed onions in the mix. Â Try a bacon cheeseburger here with sauteed onions and you'll know what I'm talking about. Â The steak fries here are also great and are a nice complement to your meal. ENTREES: I'm mixed about this one. Â The portions here are gargantuan, which is good or bad depending on your dietary habits. Â Personally I thought the fried fish is pretty decent here, and so are the fried shrimps. Â But they are on the costly side. Â The beef stew was also good, though again, the portions are insane. Â The lunch portions are more manageable, but again, it's also pretty big relatively speaking. CHEESECAKE: Yep, the cheesecake here is pretty fucking good. Â It's creamy, rich and dreamy. Â I second what some folks say about adding too many frills like syrup on their cheesecakes, but honestly, it's pretty darn good. Â If you're going to eat here, you should definitely save room for dessert. Â I know it's hard with the huge portions they serve here, so plan on either sharing an entree or sharing the cheesecake if you don't have a huge appetite. Conclusion? Â This ain't no tourist trap. Â It's a bona-fide solid place to eat, just be prepared to be stuffed. Â The prices here are also reasonable. Â It's not cheap, but whaddaya expect if you're in Times Square??? Note: The wait here can get absolutely crazy, especially around 6pm. Â Come early if you want to avoid sitting or standing for a long time in the middle of a huge crowd.

Had a good first impression when I came here a couple of years ago. Good food and atmosphere with live music that time. Have been back recently a couple of times and both times have been pretty disappointing. Once was for brunch. The menu was pretty much uninteresting except for like one thing (the huevos Cubanos), which everybody at the table got (and the neighboring table too). It was ok. Certainly not mind blowing or anything. The other time was for dinner. Had the lechon Cubano and the ceviche. Both were pretty mediocre. Especially the lechon given how much they were charging for it. Granted, we might've had a better time if it was late night rather than dinner time if the atmosphere were to pick up, but I'm not really too inclined to try again. Certainly will never take my out-of-town friends here again. Pretty embarrassing actually.

Came here for Restaurant Week last week with a large group of people (8 people) and it was fantastic! Â  We had a slight problem with the reservation so they gave us all complimentary pink campaign (that's the way to my heart!). Â Also, they sat us at a round table which is great for a large party. The views are amazing on the river which makes for a cool atmosphere. Â  The Restaurant Week deal was phenomenal b/c you can order off the full menu (with a surcharge on certain items) but this allows for many more choices than offered at most RW restaurants! The portions were also larger than most restaurant's RW deal. Â I had the burrata cheese appetizer which was delicious and large! And the tomato pasta which was a little al dente but really tasty and fresh as well!! The service was also great. Â They did not rush us along at all which was perfect for a group of friends getting together to catch up and enjoy each others company. Â I really enjoyed the relaxed pace. Overall a wonderful experience - especially for Restaurant Week!! I would highly recommend it!

Didn't like it at all! Too much grease for nothing, no taste at all in that pork belly ramen I got ! Â decor - awful. In any case, not worth even 15min wait, not to mention hours and hours that seem to be a standard wait time here. Will definitely avoid this place .

Went here for a date and it was actually quite a fun place with decently priced drinks - $6 for a jack and coke. Not too crowded just the right amount of people. There's plenty to do with darts, pool, deer hunter, and a variety of board games, it provides a lot more fun than most bars. Also pretty easy to meet new friends for the night and just hang out. Definitely recommend it if you're in Williamsburg. The hipster scene wasn't too overwhelming either which was a plus to me.

I love this place. Â Love the vibe. Â The people who work there seem to really love working there and making sure customers have a great experience. Â The food and ambiance are fun and eclectic, but not so "in your face" in the morning at breakfast. Â Love this place. Â Can't wait to go back!

After reading the reviews on Yelp, I decided to try this place. Â Well, it is as good as all the others had said. Â The sandwiches here are fantastic. Â I only tried the roast beef sandwich (Mr Moses) and it was fabulous. Â The roast beef was nice and tender, the coleslaw were the perfect compliment together with the melted cheese. Also, Johny actually works there, he's the guy that cooks your meal and takes your bill, and kinda funny too, will definitely go back.

Ordered the Black Forest Ham crepe a few times when I worked in the area. It was nice to be able to see who makes your food when picking it up, as the kitchen is right by the door. The crepe itself was great, a solid 3.5-4 stars. Something that would really set it off, in my opinion, is some gruyere, which is found elsewhere on the menu. Overall, a great crepe if you're in the area.

Up front, I will say I don't quite get the Shake Shack hype. To add to this, when the Tribeca location first opened across the street from me, I was stoked - and utterly disappointed. First burger ever was - charred to bits, the re-try was ok but then malt was messed up. Those are common problems when you open a new place but at the price point - and the hype - I would have expected flawless opening..or some trial runs (many restaurants will offer free food to attract test diners). To be fair, they've gotten into a groove since then and I like their bird dog and the shake stack. The corndog remains a salty mess of grease and I'd steer clear of it. Also, lines are ridiculously long at times - for what you get/pay for. If you have a dog..get the dog treat - it's a nice touch.

Ward III was a second choice Happy Hour gathering when our first choice turned my team away because the room they set aside wasn't ready. Â That's ok, because we had a great time at Ward III. Â The hostess was super friendly and just super cool. Â She even got us a table without us having to ask, but then again our group of 10 wasn't taking up way too much space around the bar, so extra points to her for taking charge of the situation. Â My cocktail of choice was the Angel Zahir, refreshing but nothing spectacular. Â And for the boys? They are more simple, they were happy with their Blue Moons. Â But the star of the night for me was the tomato soup and brioche grilled cheese. Â Hands down the best grilled cheese I've had to date! Â Who would have thought that I would have my best grilled cheese at a bar/lounge? Â I was teased to no end by the boys for ordering the soup and cheese amongst the other bar food spread, but I didn't care this just meant that they wouldn't want any of it which = more for me! Â I wonder if I could just go back, hide in a little corner and have a soup and grilled cheese or take it to go? (Yes, it was THAT good!) I also love the fact that they have house rules posted on their site and storefront :) Thank you, much appreciated!
very Japanese environment curry is ok

Holy cuteness. Bianca is an absolutely adorable find for a quick, romantic, well-priced Italian meal. It would make a phenomenal spot for a first date, or for a nice and intimate dinner to catch up before a movie or show. Â  The service is very quick and efficient, though I wouldn't say friendly, as they are a very busy little place and seem to turn tables over fairly quickly. I guess that's the trade-off for having such an affordable little dinner spot. I did notice, though, that they can definitely accommodate larger tables; there was a table of 8 seated right behind us who seemed to be having a lovely time. Just don't expect to be sitting there discussing philosophy for hours. You can do that at the Yippie Cafe next door. For reference, we highly recommend the Lasagnette de Verdure for an appetizer, which is basically like a mini veggie lasagne, and as usual, the Tagliolini ai Frutti de Mare for a main course; you can taste that the pasta is home-made and the seafood is fresh and succulent. I also ordered the ravioli with ricotta, butter, and sage and although I enjoyed it, I think next time I'll go for something a little bit more filling and interesting.

Really enjoyed this place. We went on a Sat morning at about 11. It was empty but the staff was very welcoming. I came with my boyfriend and baby. They were amazing to us. The fresh squeezed orange juice was refreshingly sweet and nice. The shrimp and grits and the breakfast burger were deliciousness!!! The grits were nice and light, fluffy even. The shrimp was coated in a spicy sauce that was soo good! The burger was nice and juicy. It came with an egg and bacon and clod slaw and roasted potatoes. Yummy!! My boyfriend doesn't like eggs so the waitress offered it to me; I was able to just get egg whites which were cooked perfectly. I didn't drink but my bf did. He got a traditional margarita and enjoyed it. It was one of the best brunch experiences ever because everything over all was just great! But by the time we left it started to get crowded. Â FYI- This would not be a good place for a baby on a crowded day.
Got off the megabus and was starving. Kobeyaki definitely came through and bonus for having alcohol. Not a place to go out of your way to eat but good to know its around!

This is truly a hidden gem. Â Came here last night for dinner with the girls. Â The place is a little hard to find because it's not on street-level, but it's right next to Remedy Diner. Â We made a reservation for 4 and when we got here, our table was waiting for us - YAY! Â (Yes, apparently you can make a reservation on Saturdays too) This is a simple, no-frills place that looks more like a cafe (oh wait, it IS a cafe!) than a full-fledged restaurant. Â  It's BYOB with no cork fee. Â Unfortunately we didn't coordinate very well, so we ended up with three bottles of random wine and sake. Â I generally eat at home before going out for dinner, to avoid looking like the fatty that I am. Thinking that this would be more tapas style (since it's a cafe), I had prepared myself a pre-dinner meal at home of a pint-sized glass of protein shake and a giant egg roll (don't judge!). Â I really wish I hadn't done this, because then I would've had more room for all the yummy pasta dishes. The portion is not big but satisfying. The antipasto for two was just enough of an appetizer for the four of us. Â We had the spinach and ricotta gnocchi with fresh tomato sauce. Â Unlike your typical gnocchi, this giant gnocchi is stuffed with spinach so it is light and fluffy. Â The tomato sauce is like crack, my friends proceeded to spoon out every drop of it. Â We also ordered something from the specials (written on the board by the cashier's, where you place your order). Â I don't remember what it was called. Â It was a fettuccine dish with olive oil, lemon, artichoke and some sort of cheese (of course). Â Like all the dishes we've tried so far, this is very simple but flavorful with a lemon zest in every bite. I love this dish and hope it makes its way into the regular menu. Â  The total bill came to about Â $40 after tax and tips. Â Mind = blown. Â That's $10 per person for dinner! Â Great food, fresh ingredients, friendly staff, no wait and BYOB! Â We'll definitely be back to try more pasta dishes. Â Make a reservation and order from the specials. Â I think they're only open until 10pm on the weekends, but they were still really busy when we left a little after 10.

Love this place! Restaurant isn't extremely big but good size with a bar. Cozy, inviting and romantic without being over the top. The service is superb. The owner is always walking around asking how things are. We had a large group of people and honestly every dish we tried from appetizer to entree was delicious. Came on a Saturday night and the place is packed with people. They had live music playing (guitar, saxophone, cello) Â from 8pm-11pm. Â I would recommend this for a nice or romantic occasion but also appropriate for family. People were dressed mostly business casual.

Went there because we saw that the scallop dish was one of the best dishes of the year according to a GQ article. Of course, that dish had run out by the time we got there. The best things we tried were the crab toast (OMG) and the wood roasted lobster. Def need to come back for that raw scallop dish and more crab toast!

BEST thai food i've ever had in NY! My friend is Thai and she only comes here for her comfort food. The 2 of us ordered 2 appetizers (BBQ pork and papaya salad), 2 main dishes (green curry noodles and pork noodle soup), sticky rice, thai iced tea AND 2 desserts --- we managed to finish everyhing!! it was SO delicious!!! warning: the papaya salad is very spicy. i normally eat very spicy food and my tongue and cheeks were burning up!! i will definitely go out of my way for this restaurant again.

Two stars for ambiance, one star for the spaetzle. Â The restaurant/bar itself is cozy and charming, the waiter that day was cute, and the area is a hip part of Park Slope with many other restaurants and stores. Â We came after running a 5K so we were particularly hungry and glad we found a place open on a early Sunday morning. Â Based on other Yelp reviews, I ordered the chicken paprika with spaetzle. Â The chicken itself is completely lackluster; its just simple boiled chicken with paprika. Â The spaetzle was different--soft and chewy little irregular balls of dough that soaked up the flavored chicken juices. Â This was my first time having Austrian food and I must say, the flavors were bland and unimpressive. Â Perhaps this is just how Eastern European food is.
I go here mainly for the soupy buns - Shanghai style. Â Other dishes are alright but not as great as the soupy buns. Â The dumplings are good too. Â And I like the crispy fish skin.

The Jerk Chicken ($12 for large order, comes with three pieces of chicken and lots of rice and cabbage) was incredible. I love spicy everything and can usually handle anything but holy shit, I couldn't eat any more after the second piece. There I was in Prospect Park screaming my ass off--I shit you not, it was that spicy. If you order to go, ask for LOTS of napkins. They gave me one napkin and it got smothered in grease in the to-go bag. Poor Levi's...
Awesome place, loove the ambience.. n the foods great too !! Will definitely go again !!

Four of us ordered 6 appetizers. Absolutely delicious - vivid flavors and the sides were near perfect accompaniment. The wild mushroom in phyllo dough 'tart' came with shoestring fennel in remoulade sauce - WOW! Giving 4 stars for: no liquor license, cash only., a bit cramped inside.
Charming and intimate. Â Less is definitely more both in decor and menu offerings. Â The Pork Belly Bun is a fave. Â A delightful find in the area.

Best sushi I've had in the city. I had the Prix Fixe Chirashi Ume and it was absolutely delicious. Fish was super fresh and melted in your mouth. I decided to go with the Chriashi so I could really taste the fish becuase when it's a maki roll, you don't get as much fish. My friend and I started with the fried prawns as an appetizer which were just okay. I would skip on the prawns. I'm not a huge fan of the atmosphere. It feels very sterile but I understand that they're trying to be very minimalist. The prices were not too bad considering the quality of the fish. I couldn't believe that tipping is not accepted at this restaurant! I made a 6:00 reservation for a Tuesday and made it just a few hours before and was able to be seated right away. However, it seemed to get very busy just shortly after we were seated. This was my second visit and I'd love to come back.

What is the perfect noodle? I came to Super Taste after having read numerous reviews about it on Yelp. Having lived in China for a good amount of time, I am no stranger to Lan Zhou La Mian - a specific type of noodle that is hand pulled in a specific way. The noodles here are just as good as any you will find in China. They have just the right amount of "bounce" to it, the perfect amount of give when you bite into each strand. I ordered the house special which seems to come with a little bit of everything, braised pork, beef tendons, ox tail, tripe, a fried egg and a few leaves of spinach for garnish. It was delicious. You could tell that the broth had likely been simmering for hours because of the strong beef flavor that permeated it. The toppings were plentiful but some were rather bland as they hadn't had enough time to soak up the tasty broth. The place was somewhat empty when I showed up at 730PM, which was great for me as the space is not big and I am. Around the time I finished my meal, 8-830PM, people were filling up the seats. Most appeared to be locals dining alone, people coming off work or students exhausted after a long after-school study session. It was 100% Chinese patrons, which is not a bad thing depending on how you look at it. They probably do most of their business by delivery I would imagine, since the cashier seemed to be taking a lot of delivery orders while I was there. I hear that Lam Zhou Handmade Noodle gives this place a run for their money. I will have to confirm this for myself some time in the future. What is the perfect noodle? The search continues...

I've already left a review for the other Piccolo in the Gramercy area, but I had to write a review about their new brunch specials. AMAZING!!! BEST brunch deal ever. I got the lobster and avocado with poached eggs on a croissant. The lobster serving was very generous for the price and it even came with a side of delicious salad. Don't forget the free mimosa! All for a price of $12. Also remember to stamp your coffee and meal cards for more free goodies from this steal of an Italian gem. Piccolo ma grande!

The King of Falafel & Shawarma, What a fitting name! I recently paid a visit to this popular food court err I meant cart and the kings certainly live up to their name! You will find their cart on 30th and Broadway, not far from the N & Q Broadway station. As with all good carts, you can always spot them with the line of hungry people. The best part about waiting in line is that they give you a free falafel as you wait to order. This was by far one of the best falafels I've had in a long time. So fresh! The menu is posted on a railing opposite of the line and food cart. Â The prices are $3-$4 more than most chicken and rice carts but the Kings of Falafel give you a TON of quality delicious food. Wraps and kebobs are about average prices. The men are friendly and open to prepare your plate just the way you like. I ordered the Omar platter and asked for kinda spicy but not volcanic which came with a salad and 2 more falafels!!! Like most foodies, I quickly paid for my meal and raced back to my apartment to enjoy the meal. Everything was delicious and cooked just right. Not sure how but I managed to not eat it all in one sitting and saved half fo lunch the next day. Â Highly recommend The Kings and look forward to returning for more but mostly the falafels. Check it out if you're in the area. It's definitely worth it!

There has got to be some sanity in the review section. I went to Do or Dine on Valentines Day with my girlfriend, after a long hard day of busting my ass. First thing I asked for was a cup of coffee, and honest to god, the waitress told me "we don't serve beverages here." To put it plainly, I was furious. I don't drink alcohol so there was nothing for me to drink but water. The entire meal, they were playing music I actually like, but playing it ironically(I know that sounds weird but you could tell if you were there), which [pissed me off even more. I ordered steak, and they didn't ask me how I wanted it cooked. When it came, it actually was a delicious flavor, but the meat was tough and chewy(it was supposed to be flank), which frustrated me. And there was no salt anywhere. My girlfriend is a vegetarian, and she basically was presented with a 15$plate of leaves, all arranged very nicely, and flavorful, but vastly insubstantial. The general vibe I got was that the maintenance of their hip atmosphere was far more important than satisfying the customer. Apparently, at Do or Dine, the old addage "the customer is always right" does not apply. If not for the beauty and grace of my date, I would have a. lost my cool and b. had a terrible time. That I had a great dinner was in no way contributed to by the restaurant, service, atmosphere, or food. I will say the appetizers were fantastic, I can't lie. When the check came, I slapped a one hundred dollar bill on top of it and waited about 20 minutes in the emptying restaurant for the waitress to come pick it up, as though they had somehow forgotten me? I don't understand why that took so damn long. So, they get 2 stars, rather than one, for the following reasons. 1. They are competent food-wise. 2. There probably are some people who want to be abused in the way that we were when we went there, who would see it as a validation of their hipsterness. 3.Its not my taste, I guess, but they clearly have got something specific going there and are very accurately achieving it, even though I think it's bullsh*t.

The noodles are delicious - so fresh. You can see them making the dough in the kitchen. Two of us ordered fried dumplings, two entree noodle dishes and a beer, and it cost $20. The restaurant itself is non-descript and a little divey, but the food is a treasure.

super yummy little shop. Â they had a special the day i went--a beef brisket sandwich with onions and horseradish sauce....OMFG it was so good. Â they should definitely make it a permanent menu item. Â the tomato soup leaves something to be desired, but it's good to dip your sandwich in. Â seriously this place is so good...we went on a rainy night and it was find to sit inside. Â the sandwiches are delicious. Â and the staff is friendly.

Man oh man, do I love this place. They have this machine in the back that goes back in time once they get your order and starts making it 10 minutes before you sit down. The Pho is fantastic, assuming you like good things like ample meat, richly flavored broth, and plenty of it. I recommend the Vietnamese French Dip for two: get a Banh Mi and 2 bowls of Pho, and dip your half of the best Vietnamese sandwich in NYC into the best Pho in NYC, smiling at your partner while the juices drip embarrassingly down your face. Oh, and it's super inexpensive and the staff is really nice, although very quick about things. To be honest, I've had better in other places, but I've never had better in New York, and I don't think I've ever had better for this price. Love it!

Pulled pork sliders were amazing, I still need to try their drinks. We didn't order any because we were quite satisfied at our previous drinking locations by the time we got here. Sliders have a few sauces on the side to choose from, chipotle, ketchup, etc. The pulled pork was great as it was not over or undercooked, it was the perfect level of tenderness balanced with flavor and pork texture. I didn't like the seating arrangements as the tables were quite small and the small square seats often caused lots of people bumping into each other.

My boyfriend and I stumbled upon this place for lunch while we were visiting the city and it was so good we came back for the Sunday brunch! Â For lunch we split an onion soup and then the portobello sandwich for me and a chicken sandwich for him. Â Both were amazing- all of the ingredients were fresh, flavorful, and well presented on the sandwich (I hate when you get served a sandwich that is humanely impossible to eat as a sandwich). Â My boyfriend said it might be his favorite sandwich he's ever eaten. We came back for the Sunday brunch and it was just as amazing as we expected it to be! Â I loved that my salmon gravlox came with both greens and fries. Â The restaurant itself is small but charmingly decorated with French posters and a very comfortable environment. Â Staff is great. Â We were so happy to have found this place and will definitely return when we are back!

The eggplant was bar none the best I've ever had...I have to go back to try it again. It was light and airy and good flavor. Octopus was cooked on point. Flavors linger and are well developed. I will definitely go back to explore the menu.

This is my 2nd time at Almond. First for dinner and now for brunch. This review is for both times. This is a solid establishment from service to food. The food is not overly inventive but it is executed well and good. In the first visit, it was for my friend's birthday and the service was excellent! The waitress was friendly, attentive but not overbearing...which is just right the right balance. Â We had a good girl celebration---appetizer--Shared Steam Mussels (fresh and yummy!) Entree: I ordered roast chicken and my friend had the lamb shank. Both dish was good. I especially enjoy the chicken which was moist and done well. Sorbets for dessert! Yummy, good time! The 2nd time, I went with friends for brunch. Group of 6 and you can make reservations! Awesome! My friend and I arrived first and was seated without the entire party! Great! It was already a good start. One of my friend was half an hour late, no problem and no pressure to order. It was again another good time spend with friends. There was a good selection for brunch especially with one of the requirement was to find a Â restaurant with salad choices! Brunch was again solid! I ordered the Almond hash which is done with duck confit. It was good. So, if you are in this neighborhood and want to find a good place to spend time with your friends, a place that offers good food options, accepts reservations (even for brunch!- say goodbye to waiting 30-40 mins) then this is a place for you to try!

Had a lovely brunch with my friend. We sat outside of the restaurant where the sun was shining on us. The first table that we sat was super wobbly and unstable then we moved to the corner table by an apartment staircase. Boy, outside seating was pretty cramped with small round tables. Note: You are allow to grab any table when you choose to sit outside. Me and my friend ordered from the Brunch Special which includes 2 drinks. As we were ordering, our waitress let us know that they 88 the French Toast. How could you run out a popular brunch dish...you know! I got the Eggs Benedict with OJ and Cappuccino and my friend got the Eggs Norwegian with OJ and Latte! My first time having Eggs Benedict and it was very delicious and also I love the yummy homefries. Overall my friend and I really enjoyed ourselves. Definitely a recommended brunch spots even though they don't take reservations but the hostess rocks at seating all the parties down!

BEST PIZZA I HAVE EVER HAD! Got here right before the dinner crowd and was seated right away. The atmosphere was just how I pictured a typical Brooklyn pizzeria; busy, loud, and wonderful. If you want the best pizza NY has to offer, come here! oh and p.s. if you're coming from the city, take a subway to Brooklyn and walk the Brooklyn Bridge back to NYC after dinner for a romantic stroll and breathtaking views.

The 5-star review has little to do with the food. Â The food is actually pretty good, which is why I'm not penalizing it. Â But the reason to come here is to enjoy a sunny day, have a beer, eat some grub and forget that you live in the concrete jungle. The Boat Basin can't hold a candle to this place when it comes to atmosphere, staff, food, or crowd. Â  Pier 1 is just what the doctor ordered at the end of a long NYC day.

typical bad service from a chinese establishment. i also thought it was weird that they seated us at a large sharing table with others (hostess didn't mention it to us prior to seating us - as we would have enjoyed having our own table). service was bad, they pretty much ignored us. the pork soup dumplings were nothing special, i've tasted better

Love this place! Â The reviews are true. Very very small! Â But worth it. Â The service was great. They were very nice and helpful. The atmosphere was cute and fun. The sangria was good and the food was enjoyable. Will def come back to this place!

10-word summary: Dry-aged beef for two definitely worth it; cocktails are great. The steak is prepared with two huge bone-fuls of marrow and in a great dark sauce. It's unlike any kind of steak you'd get at a steakhouse. For two people, the steak and one appetizer or side is probably enough food. Only other piece of advice is to try the cocktails - the Copperhead is good for people who like strong, dark drinks.

I'm with the other negative reviewers on this one. Don't understand the hype. I've given this place three tries, and each time failed to impress me. First time we were really hungry and waited almost an hour to be seated. Decided we couldn't wait anymore and just ordered to go. Even that took 20 minutes. Ordered the square. Nothing to see here people! All they did was switch the order of the cheese and tomato sauce so sauce is on top, cheese on the bottom. Had a pasta dish that was meh, but hefty portions. Another time, an out of town friend visited me and insisted on trying it. Originally wanted the lobster salad but they said it wasn't available! Shame on them for not stocking their kitchen better. She ordered the seafood salad instead. Not impressed! Hardly any expensive seafood. Mostly calamari tossed in with mussels. Already wanting to leave, my friend suggested we order a dessert. Big mistake. We ordered a tiramisu to share. It took them literally 20 minutes to bring to us, and it wasn't even busy. By that time, there were only a handful of tables occupied. The server was nowhere to be found - probably on her cigarette break?! I mean, all she had to do was slice a piece and bring it over. I could not wait to get out of this over-hyped greasy joint. Never again!

Great place for a quick bite. I went here with a friend who is a vegetarian and she approves of the vegetarian options. Great quality but unsatisfying portion, I left the place still hungry after two gyros.

No Yak! You have to call and make sure they get their Yak Shipment which happens in the Summer and vanishes within a couple of weeks. So call call call call! OTHERWISE, their food is so fun to eat. There is a great vegetarian selection.

Coffee=5 Service=5 Decor=5 Great little hidden gem in a busy commercial area. Excellent Cappuccinos very smooth... And yes I may be a sucker for the artwork in the froth but it's also an indicator of attention to detail. Once you've had a Cappuccino like this it gives you a greater appreciation and point of reference when compared to the mass-produced, production line, factory - coffee places. French press nicely done. The staff is very friendly and even if you've only been there your second time they make you feel as if you're a long time regular. They make it a point to remember you and your drink preference. Although seating is limited, the rustic decor is inviting and well done. The only thing that could make the coffee better would be an organic option.

Loved this place so much I came twice on this trip! Â Perfect for a late night snack after a little night of bar hopping. Â The make your own omelet is phenomenal and the cocktails are amazing. Â The Truffle Oil Mac n Cheese is to die for.

Absolutely to die for. Had a chicken over rice two nights ago and I've found myself craving it ever since. It is also very filling. I eat a lot and I didn't even manage to finish it, saved some for later and it even tastes great the next day. For $6, you can't go wrong. The halal guys is a must! Highly recommended.

I stopped by to make an outdoor reservation for my friends and myself for 4pm for their happy hour because it was a beautiful day. A woman took my reservation, and an hour later I went back to confirm it. Then an hour after that I got a call from the manager that they apparently do NOT take outdoor reservations and I explained to him I had confirmed it..so I assumed he would help us out. I arrived 15 minutes early just in case. After about 45 MINUTES OF WAITING I saw a table open up and I asked the manager if I could sit down to which he told me "theres a waitlist"...I thought "obviously...Im on it...." Â Then after AN HOUR another table opened up and my boyfriend asked the manager if we could sit down and he asked my boyfriend "who are you?"....I was dumbfounded. We are the people who've been WAITING OUTSIDE FOR AN HOUR. Once we did get a table we had poor service. Drinks would take up to 15 minutes to get. The only redeeming quality of this place is the outdoor space.

Love this place! Had the pleasure of being their first lunch customer today and got to meet with the owner who is lovely. I had recently noticed that Ramen opened when I walked past it to my office and had an opportunity to step in. The spicy pork miso hit the spot. Has he perfect amount of heat and so much flavor. The gyoza were delicious and so delicate that you can tell they were made with care. I also never skip on adding an egg to anything as it makes a great accent to the dish. I am a fan and with winter coming I am delighted at the thought of coming back for more. Need to work on the owner to accept cards though since cash-only is tough - I never like to carry cash.
Make the Sunday brunch your business to attend...my friends and I are never disappointed (even with the long a$$ wait)...nuff said!

Took a chance on this little place last weekend to get food for a dinner party. Wow what a wonderful surprise this place was! Ordered just about everything on the menu and we loved it all. The hummus and merguez were particularly amazing. On top of that the owners were just so super nice, crediting their mom for the various recipes and insisting I try the hummus right on the spot. They claim great hummus is a sign of everything else being great. Think they are right!

I was very surprised that the ramen here tasted as good as it did. This place is more of a Japanese restaurant for white people. Other than being located in a prime spot for white people traffic, it also employs very hip decor such as the very Brooklynesque communal wooden dining table. The management here chooses to cast aside the traditional uniforms and allows their hip young Asian waitresses to wear whatever strikes their fancy. The tonkatsu ramen was the most impressive thing we ordered. The broth was surprisingly complex and tasted like it had been cooked for hours. The Zutto pork belly buns were good but nothing mind-blowing. Check-in here for a free 12oz. Asahi! Other than the ramen, everything else on the menu I could probably get elsewhere either better or cheaper. This place is really more for the ambience, although even that isn't particularly impressive. If you have women-folk in your group, they will probably enjoy this place.

Went last night and was very, very happy with my experience. What a bang for the buck!! A small cafe with excellent, fresh (noticeably fresh) food- and offerings a little more sophisticated and wide ranging than I expected! A lovely staff, casual environment, and bustling with customers. Parking was do-able even though it was a nasty, rainy night! Totally great place- I will be back soon for sure!

If you live in the Heights this is a must go to restaurant. Â If you dont its worth the trip. Â The service is nice. Â The chef really knows how to mix flavors. Â Have the smoked trout with almond salad its fantastic.

Being from Atlanta, I'm not usually spoilt for a choice in Ramen. However, on my recent trip to NY, I decided to try out the highly decorated Ippudo. I was warned that I will be expected to wait about 2-3 hours before I get seated. So I put my name down, and headed for the nearest bar. I was called by the hostess to let me know my table was ready even before I was able to order my first drink! Not bad at all! When you are walked to your table, the entire staff welcomes and greets you. The dining space feels crowded and loud when you enter, bu when we were seated, although it was a bit of a communal table, it strangely didn't feel so. We were able to chat without shouting, and quite fairly private. And then came the food. WOW! I think the nearly 2 billion reviews for this place cover all aspects of it, so I'm not going to get into details. However, the flavors, or should I say the balance of flavors. The experience of drinking the broth was like drinking an excellent aged whiskey - the flavors, the lingering after tastes, the tingling of sense. Must also add their alcohol list is extensive and very well curated. Definite must go - the place is packed for a reason, and not douchy at all - something I have come to expect from most NY places with lines 2 mile long.
Went there for brunch, Food was awesome! Loved my server. She made special shots for my friend and I. What a great way to end the weekend! Plus watching the world cup on a project! Holy Hanna!

Say hello to the next Roberta's / Momofuku. Â Go there now before the enthusiastic 2-star NYT review, because that will happen and the lines will make the Roberta's wait look measly. Â  Reason why? Â Easy. Â This is dining a la now - comfort-ish food served in a playful attitude environment using high-end ingredients and unique concoctions. Â Nestled on a rapidly-gentrifying block of Bed-Stuy (the wine bar, Sud, down the street being the dead giveaway), Do or Dine, like the places I compared it to, brings all the components of a winning formula together without it seeming like a formula at all. Â  Per the chef owner, when recommending dishes: "Some of our dishes are just really satisfying. Â The others are ... really interesting. Â Depends which end of the spectrum you fall on [as to what to pick]". Â  And so roll the dice with "interesting" and you get a serious chunk of head cheese served with an extra-tangy mole mustard, deviled eggs with fried baby octopus sticking out of the top, whole; a grilled caesar salad, served as a single giant grilled chunk of romaine on a butcher's block with a knife jammed in it ("Et tu Brute" is the name of the dish; get it?); a chilled corn soup, studded with caramel corn; and an explosive, perfectly cooked sliced duck breast, with an ample, steak-like char, tender inside. Â  The menu is playful, often hilarious. Â "District 9" was the name of a new prawn dish; if you've seen the movie, most of it is spent with the main character saying "f--king prawns!" over and over and over again. Â See the aforementioned "Et tu Brute". Â This place is zero-attitude and all game. Â  They are also BYOB for now; they'll keep your beers cold in the back, and open your wine for you. One of the chef owners saw me using my phone right before we ordered and said, "You Yelping?" Â No - I was actually trying to figure out what artichoke escabeche was (didn't try it, but sounded great). Â But I had already planned to politely do him the honors after the meal - even if I'm going to hate the 60-min wait the next time I go...

I had a fantastic late lunch with my son after a freezing couple of hours at Chelsea Piers a few blocks away hacking balls over the Hudson River. The tapas were the absolute most authentic and best I've had in this country - no holes barred on the rich, robust seasonings and ample doses of garlic. Â The top of the list was the bocadillo de buttifara - a sandwich on crusty bread of catalan pork sausage, carmalized onions, tetilla cheese, and mustard ... And the selection of sherrys by the glass over the top especially the super sweet special reserve (can't recall the name) which was like raisin syrup.. Ended with an equally syruppy double espresso. Great way to spend a very cold afternoon in the city. Â Looking forward to returning in the evening sometime and revisit the friendly and professional staff.

I came here and had the Arepas benedictos (without meat) which was an amazing poached egg, with cilantro hollandaise on a corn cake. The corn cake was SUCH a great idea and the dish was absolutely delish!! LOVED IT :D

First visited Joya on a date. Â Soon after I started working not to far and it's become a staple in my life. lol I get pretty much the same meals from Thai restaurants - Pad Thai & Pad See Ewe. Â Both never disappoint. The restaurant can get pretty loud during lunch, so I recommend after hours.
Good service. Have always passed the place but never went in. Food was good. Glad we went.
Great authentic Greek food with really friendly, professional, accommodating service. A gem.

I am very picky about my food and I have a lot of food allergies. Â Not only was the staff completely patient and willing to work with me but the food tasted amazing. Â Also they really know their wines and how to pair them with exactly what you are eatting. Â I can't say enough good things about this place but put it this way - I was in midtown on the East side and I made the trek there to meet friends and it was totally worth it. Â DO IT!

I was here on a Sat. night bad choice. The wait like any good restaurant that doesn't take reservation was over 2hrs. So I put my name down and went to the bar around the area because the restaurant bar area was full too. Went back after they called to say my table was ready, had 2 serving of DELICIOUS ramen. Get the pork bun appetizer. Would wait all over again ..

Considering the other soup options in the immediate vicinity, it's a mystery why I don't go to the Soup Spot more often. But there are a couple things about it that keep me from being a regular. 1. Â Yes, the place is small and there is probably very low overhead, but you have to line up outside and that really sucks when it's below freezing. I really want that soup on a cold day, but I must suffer for it first. 2. It's really convenient if you work by Penn Station. But even though it's only a half block from my work, I still have to put on my coat to go there because see #1. 3. For the price ($4.50 for a large, $6.50 with a half sammy), it's a good deal because you also get bread and a piece of fruit. But the bread tastes funny and the apples are often not that great. Why no option to pay less and get no sides? But look, the soups ARE really good and they are not made with MSG nor do they leave a funny taste in your mouth like the ones at ABP or the salad/sandwich/pizza/soup places nearby.
I love love love Fette Sau. Â Expect longish lines, but it's worth it for the food. Â Great BBQ, as well as good drinks. Â No frills - paper towels at benches - but it's great. Â Good stuff. Â Enjoy.

With the glorious twin pillars of the Dan Dan Noodles and Dry Pepper Wings, Han Dynasty is without doubt one excellent Neo Szechuan import from Philly. While some of the other dishes I had just kind of tasted like the best Chinese takeout I've ever had rather than the best Szechuan, I wouldn't say Han is the end all be all for this type of food in this area. When it comes to mains my favorite by far are Dry Pot Style and Long Hot Pepper Style. In my humble opinion nether is really mouth-destroyingly spicy, but both pack a decent amount of heat. The three most beloved dishes here, and I agree they rule, are: 1) The Dan Dan Noodles 2) Wonton in Chili Oil and 3) Dry Pepper Wings. All of this food is pretty intensely greasy and heavy but the above dishes display some really masterful taste that makes it worth it. Definitely come here at some point and brave the wait for this stuff. Â However, beyond these dishes Han kind of fell flat for me. For instance, the Dry Pepper Style shrimp were nauseatingly greasy with a pretty tasteless breaded and deep fried shell over which was poured a kind of half-hearted and bland chili oil. Â I didn't really dig the Three Cup Chicken either, which could have used A LOT more heat. So yeah, no real problems here. Definitely give this spot a try. Just please do not come here expecting hands down the best Szechuan, or even general Neo-Chinese fare in the city
The original teochow soup noodle joint on Bayard Street. Beef stew here is super tasty. No frills, kinda dirty but food is still the best. Â Price as always is great.

This is a great neighborhood restaurant. Â The food is consistently fantastic, the price is perfect, the service is spot-on, and I'm always happy to eat there. Â It's no wonder why they have security guards, food this good could cause a riot. Â Havana Outpost has done something really incredible and I hope they stay here in Ft. Greene for many years to come. Â If all you have is the beans and rice, you'll be in for a real treat, it's the best I've ever had.
Cute place - decent food

My husband and I found this Korean food restaurant. Â We love it. Â Food is fresh. Â They also have samples of salad, smoothies, and desserts. Â They also have different kind of fried rice, soups and noodles. I order beef bibimbap. Â They also have chicken and tofu bibimbap and you get to choose either white or brown rice. The have the containers ready for to go orders but if u tell them its for dining, they'll give a tray. Â My husband had beef bulgogi over rice, fish cake and squid. Â Then, we order shrimp tempura since we do love sushi :). Overall, its a pleasant experience. Â We will come back next time when we are in midtown. Â The place was packed even though they had additional seats downstairs so I'd suggest trying to go off busy hours. Â We were there at noon so of course finding a seat is a challenge. Â We were lucky that a couple left while we searched for a table.

i went once when it first opened and it was unbelievable how good the pizza was. Â Unfortunately, it has been discovered so the wait is pretty long, BUT they are VERY accommodating with takeout. Â If you call for an order, they will call you back when the pizza is going IN the oven! Â That's quality service.

I love this cafe! I came here with a friend for a weekday brunch and we arrived around 11:30 when it was relatively empty. We requested to sit outside because it was extremely nice out for that week, around 60 degrees First off, our waiter was extremely professional and polite. Secondly, this cafe is so well decorated and bigger than you'd initially expect! The back room has a fire place and art deco pieces that make me feel like I just stepped into someone's home. The food was perfect! I ordered the eggs and a side of fries, which were perfectly crispy and salted and a big enough portion to share. My friend ordered the eggs Benedict which they raved about in between bites. It was a wonderful meal and not extremely expensive! Both of our meals came to around $20! I will definitely be back!

Went for a late brunch on Sunday around 4pm, that's the least busy time for most restaurants. However, there was a line for this place. Ordered Cold Antipasto, Grilled Quails, and a grilled fish. the tzatziki is sooooo fresh HOME-MADE. Griled Quails are very tasty I loved it a lot. That fish cost $28 supposed to be shipped from Greek but it tasted like local farm raised. Saw a lot of people ordered Grilled Octopus, looked really good. Overall, that's a good brunch for about 70 dollars with tips.

I love their dumplings! A little much on the ginger but delicious and great for the price 12/$3. Their fried dumplings are my favorites whenever I go. The noodles are delicious and slightly chewy; they also give you plenty of noodles. There's a few pieces of meat (beef, pork, etc) but I feel that they can throw in a few more veggies. Can't go wrong for the price though (~5) for some noodles. Definitely a small place, very informal: you eat to the sounds of the chefs slapping the dough to make the noodles. Make sure you stop by for some cheap and filling food.

I came here for the first time this past week for a friend's Birthday happy hour. If you're a fan of rum-based cocktails this might just be the place for you. For a Monday evening the bar seemed lively and crowded, with white wall interiors and a back area past the bar equipped with large wooden tables for customers to gather round and lounge at. While the beverage menu seemed to consist of island resort specialties one might find at such tropical venues as 'Painkillers' I found the interior a bit of an odd balance in conjunction. The food menu I will say looked delicious and I will absolutely be returning to try the burger and the grilled cheese. The staff looked a little overwhelmed and the main bartender who took my order seemed to be constantly getting mine as well as other customer's orders wrong (at least one mistake resulted in receiving a $13 specialty drink Â for the happy hour price of $8.) Overall a fun atmosphere but the staff left a bit to be desired. Do try the flaming cocktail, however!

Since my first 1-star review for Artichoke, I've gone here three more times - I wanted to give this place one more chance to make up for their earlier attempts, EACH TIME AFTER THAT IT WAS THE SAME TERRIBLE OVER-BURNED CRAP. Even at its freshest, it wasn't great at all. I understand pizza; I know how burned pizzas can be, I absolutely love pizza from places like Di Fara's and Lucali's, known for the crispy/crunchy crusts, but every time I go to Artichoke, the pizza chef puts old pizza and leaves it in the oven for much longer than necessary, and it literally comes out CHARRED. BLACK. UN-EATABLE. I had told the chef that it was way too burned, and he scoffed at me, almost raising his voice at me telling me "that's how pizza is supposed to be, get over it." Complete jerk about it. I asked him to give me a fresher slice, and he did resentfully. Â Even the fresh margarita slice he'd given me was "OK" at best, but to go through all that trouble for an overpriced $4.50 slice of pizza that's overhyped - what's the point? This has happened 3 out the 4 times that I've gone there. You're better off getting a slice from dollar pizza.

I'd like to start off by saying I don't ever write reviews on restaurants because everyone's taste usually vary so greatly. But I had such an amazing dinner here I wanted to write one. See when we got to Eataly my party and I were amazed at the market and atmosphere of BIRRERIA, but were very very worried when we saw how limited the menu was. We were just going to get drinks and some cheeses but decided to stick it out and give it a try. I'm so very happy we did. I got the pork dish, and I'm not a huge pork lover, and it was the best thing I think I have ever eaten. We were so pleased we stayed. So if you look at the menu and think you won't like it, give it a try, because it was truly AMAZING!!!
Best. Pancakes. Ever.

After overdosing on tzatziki sauce this past summer, I had not been in the mood to enjoy Greek food. I pass Pylos on my way too and from the subway station everyday, though, and it always looks popular and smells good. Then I checked its reviews on Yelp and read very good things. I decided to try it on a Friday night on a whim without a reservation (I had heard about a community table that doesn't require a reservation). My friend and I checked in by 8:30pm and were seated by 9pm or so--not bad at all! Even better, the community table was a pleasure! While I was expecting to be crammed elbow to elbow with fellow diners, my friend and I sat comfortably at the end of the table with plenty of room to hold our conversation and put our multiple-course meal. Furthermore, the restaurant is decorated so well. I loved the ceiling (you'll know what I mean when you go!). The food provided an even more pleasurable experience. My friend and I shared octopus, a lamb shank and pastitsio. The octopus was delicious--not at all like chewy and squiggly calamari that I was expecting it to resemble. The lamb shank was another A+, and the pastitsio was to die for. I would HIGHLY recommend all three dishes without the faintest hesitation whether or not they'd be fully enjoyed. Who knew Greek food had so much more to offer than tzatziki sauce and hummus?! Just kidding, I'm not that naive...but really, I was so impressed by the offerings! I cannot wait to go back and try more!

My go-to after a late night. One slice will hit the spot! I love pizza and can eat multiple slices in one sitting, but this is all you'll need! It is delicious, creamy, amazing comfort food. Don't expect the healthiest option, but once you step in, you immediately know what kind of food this place serves. I absolutely love this pizza, and missing it is probably one of the most difficult things for me right now!

Cowgirl is great! I love their half price happy hour and am a huge fan of taco tuesdays. The service can be slow and a bit ditzy but they kind of own it and most of the time it's comical. The food is worth it!

OH LAWRD!! Â  Perfect, Perfect and Perfect! Â Have you ever had the Persian chicken wings? Â Oh, me neither! Â I am vegetarian, so I've never had the experience that everyone seem to talk about all the time there. Â Anyways, the White pizza is my favorite and the drinks are consistently made with real Brooklyn prices. All these edge Brooklyn places think they are on Park Ave or something. Just saying... I never knew how many people really used Yelp. I never thought my opinion mattered and really it doesn't in the grand schema of things. If by chance it does to you, go check it out for yourself. Â I think you'll have nearly the same opinion as I, even if it doesn't really matter. Good job Bijan!
Grimaldi's, Totonno's, Spumoni L&B, and Di Fara's - these are as good as pizza gets!

If you are on a low cholesterol diet, this place is not for you. I listened to all of you Yelpers and tried the most recommended items and was not disappointed. The burger was perfectly prepared and the pile of shoe string fries were so garlicy and delicious! The chicken liver toast was more oily and heavy than I'd have expected but still, I thought it was really unique and yummy. I've eaten a million deviled eggs, but there was something that set these ones apart, a slightly acidic taste? I'm not sure, regardless they were great (my friend thought they had a funny aftertaste, pshh). My only half complaint is that if you are going for a bloody mary you might mention to go light on the horseradish if you don't love huge blobs of it coming through your straw. The atmosphere is chill and cozy which fits into the whole country theme and our service was great!

would have been a fan had the service been better. Â too many chefs in the kitchen so to speak. Â the male owner is thoughtful and sincere, he gets it. Â the female however is less so. Â  nobody greeted us, we sat at the bar next to the register and were overlooked for a bit until i asked for menus. Â the crowd built up behind the register as something had been missing, a bill, the cash, something. Â someone from another table was looking for his sandwich and that he had been waiting 30 minutes, they delivered. our food was up, but sat there while three people who passed it, looked at it and kept going. Â meanwhile the girl is trying to become part of each conversation but doing nothing. Â finally we asked for our food and pointed. Â there were a few other oversights but you probably get the point.

I lived here around the block for 20 years and been eating his pizza . Domenick puts his heart and soul into making each pie. This pizza is just amazing it melts in your mouth . Yes the slices are thin but that's how Italian pizza should be. The best pizza in New York

Great place to be when you're with group of friends. servers were very friendly and the serves was attentive. they literally refilled our glass of water right when they heard the ice cling, Tofu was great, Kalbi was delicious, and the presentation was good enough for my taste. will definiately come back!
Can't get enough of the banh mi's and vietnamese iced coffee. Super cheat eats, fast and delicious. Cash only.

Emily may be the best pizza I've had. Ever. If not, it's definitely top 5. Their pies are inventive and some of them are unlike anything I've seen elsewhere. And they're actually surprisingly big. I came here for lunch and split two pies with a friend. It was a lot of food, but it was so good that I kept eating until I hated myself (I do that a lot). For the sake of variety, we went with one red and one white. The red was The Colony, which came with pepperoni, pickled chili and honey. The chilis were amazing - not too spicy, and gave it just the right amount of kick. The honey was subtle, and not overpowering. Every bite was a combination of salty (pepperoni), spicy (chilis), sweet (honey), or all three. You really need to try this one. Our second pie was the eponymous Emily. This one was definitely sweeter (we were warned beforehand when ordering). I've never had crushed pistachio on a pizza, but it works. Really well, in fact. It also had truffle cheese and a generous honey glaze. Since it was sans sauce, this one was baked a little crispier, which made it that much more amazing. Between the pistacchios and the truffles, there was a nice balance of savory to go along with the sweet. They also have good beers on tap and whiskey! But it was 12:30 in the afternoon (that means I only had a beer). Our server was super friendly. She provided us with wonderful recommendations/conversation, and kept the indie tunes playing on the stereo. The decor of the place is also great. It has elements of cute (signs pointing you to the bathroom, handwritten notes in the bathroom, wine served in lab beakers), but also a cultured feel (an old map of New York and a wooden mandolin slicer on the wall). I will gladly come back to Emily until I have tried all of their pies.

Holy smokes a 1 hour wait?! The take out and dine in line are the same. Kind of odd but that's how they do it here. Straight to the point. My comrades and I were seated upstairs and handed some menus. The place was packed! I guess there was a bit of confusion who are server was because it took roughly 20-25 min until I had to get up and ask who our server was. One must try is their Brooklyn sodas. I had the root beer and sure enough it was def a root beer I haven't tasted before. Between 4 people we ordered a sausage, pep, mushroom pie. You can't order slices here. But the large pizza was perfect for each of us to have 2 slices. The cheese is super cheesy and fresh. I loved the basil aroma. The pizza itself and crust is super thin. I like thin crust pizza but I wish it were more crisp with a crunch. I gotta admit, it was certainly an experience coming to Brooklyn for some pizza but I can't say it was the best I've ever had. I guess my heart lies with Cali for Pizza My Heart which by the way sells pizza by the slice.

I'm going to start off by admitting my rating may be influenced by the fact that I have to go way out of my way to get to this place. So I might be judging it more harshly because I expect it to be better given the effort to get there. Service is great. Everyone in the cozy restaurant is very friendly and helpful when it comes to suggestions of what to order. The place is probably best for a quiet lunch date as it is cramped. I definitely wouldn't come with a group of kids or girlfriends during a shopping excursion. I find the lamb sandwich incredibly overpriced (around $11) and definitely not worth it. It was pretty darn small and stingily filled. It has a lot of flavor while being flavorless. That is, I feel like the actual ingredients are kind of flavorless, the lamb, the vegetables, etc. but all the seasoning is an overpowering mishmash of tastes so you end up with something indistinct. The spanakopitakia are tiny little triangles of yummy, flaky, buttery, spinach-y goodness. They might be a little rich for some but I love them. Definitely great as an appetizer or as a light snack on their own. The baklava is good. Not spectacular but everyone has their own preferences when it comes to baklava. I find the layers a bit too dry and I wish the flavor was a little more nutty and less dependent on spices for taste. Overall, I'm not sure if I'll be back but it's a nice place to stop in if you're in the area. I will say that the times I've been in I've seen people ordering salads which looked delicious so maybe that's their specialty.

An immediate must-try once I heard of its existence. It's not like I'm an obsessed bacon fan like the entire Internet, but any place that does both a meat and beer sampler is key to my appetite. Saturday afternoon- PACKED. Luckily was able to find my way into a seat at the bar. Was able to order the bacon and beer sampler within 10min For $20: 4 5oz beer samples, 6-8ish pieces of mixed bacon. Even though you can choose your own beers, the draft list is severely lacking. They do have several crafts, but considering the plethora of beer bars opening in Hell's Kitchen, this craft list left a lot to be desired. Bacon came at a good variety, but they don't match the bacon with the beer for you. So really it's just ordering two separate samplers. Great idea, okay execution. Good for bacon lovers regardless I suppose.
willing to try

Buffet? At a Michelin-starred restaurant? This sounded too good to be true, but it really was as excellent as you would expect from a Michael White restaurant. When you come for Sunday Brunch, you get live music, an unlimited buffet of tons of breads, pastries and other foods, and an entire entree, for just $64. Yes, that is a lot of money, but considering all that you get, it's not too bad at all. Located on the second floor of a hotel, with large windows overlooking the street, this is a really beautiful place. From the moment you step in to the warm greetings, you can tell why this is a Michelin-starred restaurant. They escorted us to our table in the luxurious, spacious dining room. It's refreshing and surprising to see such a large, wide open restaurant in NYC. The closest tables were far enough away that we weren't forced to listen to some annoying conversations. We ordered pretty quickly, eager to head over to the buffet. This was a buffet like none other I've ever seen, as everything was of the highest quality. It's a beautiful presentation of some really excellent food. I easily ate more than $64 worth alone in croissants, chocolate croissants, muffins, smoked salmon, and a bunch of other Italian meats and other stuff. Once I was officially way too full, the entrees arrived. Unbelievably, they have all of the great dishes they are known for including in this menu. For one of them, we tried the Rigatoni ala Carbonara, which was really great. The pasta was perfectly al dente and chewy, and the sauce was so creamy and rich. What looks like a small portion is actually very satisfying given how much flavor and richness it packs. For the other entree, we of course went with the White Label Burger, which has been praised several times over the past few years as being one of the best burgers in NY. This was a seriously intense burger: an 8 oz. prime patty with bacon marmalade, Nueske's bacon, American Cheese and a perfect fried egg on top. It's a large burger that's tough to manage without really getting your hands dirty, mostly due to the runny egg oozing all over, but it's totally worth the mess, and it really is one of the best burgers I've had. It's also served with a side of pommes dauphine, which were so creamy and rich that they really sent me over the edge. This was an incredibly delicious and overwhelming entree. Even though we were absolutely stuffed, we of course had to make a final trip (or two) back to the buffet to check out the dessert selections. I was again shocked to see how much high quality stuff was included: there was fresh fruit, a fruit tart, Vanilla Mille Feuille, Almond Brioche, and the popular Olive Oil Cake. The few bites of everything I tried was really great, especially the soft, tasty Olive Oil Cake and the Almond Brioche. As mentioned above, service was perfect too. I don't know what the normal lunch/dinner is like here, but if you like both quality and quantity, the Sunday Brunch can't be beat.

The place was pretty empty on a Wed night. Â The prices were high and the food was only so-so. Â Rice cracker crusted tuna was great. Â Pea soup was so-so. Â Buffala cheese was too soft inside and came with a hard as rock piece of bread. Â I came for the prix fix dinner but it ends at 6pm!

Loved the selections on menu. Creative but tasty, plentiful but not too much. It's kind of an expensive place ($ 35 + drinks + tax+ tip) but prices are justified. Moussaka and Arnabeet Mekle was my favorite so far. But fish in Entree was great. After eating the priz fixe food I was too full to enjoy desert but all the guilt of eating so much food is totally worth it.

Very good! Wonderful service and an incredibly diverse tapas menu (with pretty generous portions--everything is definitely shareable). The Brussel sprouts are pretty amazing, as are the bacon-wrapped figs and olives. The polenta is very good. My son had the falafel which he said was the best he ever had. The goat cheese has a very strong grassy flavor, which is a good thing depending on your preference. Very flavorful lamb tagine. Wonderful chocolate lava cake. Would definitely go back again. I solidly recommend it!

This place never ceases to amaze me. Â Working in the "Club" business, I've been coming to Sanfords after work at 4am for the past 6 months, 4 days a week at the least. Â And just when I think I'm going to get tired/fed-up with the menu the chefs seems to be able to keep everything refreshing. Â  As I write this the Sanford's Waffle has got to be the best Damn Waffle I've ever had. Â I hate waffles btw and much prefer pancakes or french toast. Â But this Waffle that Sanford's has is literally batter with Crack. Â  I'm also hooked on the Turkey Bacon and most of the Salads they offer as well. Â  Everything is consistently fresh and up to par. Â Remember this is a 24 hour Diner. Â 24 hours.

I've been going to Rincon Criollo with my family since I was a little girl. Â When my dad arrived from Cuba, this place was here. Â The owners haven't changed and the wait staff is always friendly and amazing. Nothing can ever beat my grandma's home style Cuban cooking, but if there is going to be a second, it would be Rincon Criollo. Â The masitas de puerco are amazing, and they will bring out a whole bunch of sides. Â Black beans, some platanos, and your main dish... yum yum. Â And, for a ridiculous price (compared to the city). Â Gotta love the Christmas lights decoration and disco ball too. Â This place is a classic: Â if you're looking for authentic Cuban, come here.
Tasty at first. Nice orange puffy rice. Â  Not sure if the orange color was saffron spice or something else, but the rest of the large portion was just ok.

Went on a Tuesday night (7p reservation) for dinner with another couple. Â Asthetically, this place is a homerun. Â The whole front of the house opens on to a quiet street with some tables al fresco. Â Nice bar with some hightop farm tables. Â Lots of wood and warm colors. Â Very inviting. The staff was very attentive. Â Both the waiter and somlier had REALLY bad breath issues, but what can ya do??? Â They both made excellent recommendations on food and wine. We decided to share a few different things and ended up with the Gnocchi (I usually find gnocchi too heavy, but this was extremely light and tastey), Lobster (cooked perfectly with a really nice, spicy chili broth), Pigs Ears (ehh - tastey, but I'm not down with chomping on cartiliage) and another that is slipping my mind. For entres we tried the Halibut special (amazing flavor) and The Steak - now here is where I deducted stars. Â This is a $76 dollar steak, which is just obnoxious, but they claim that this is THE BEST cut of meat in the country. Â I'm a steak guy so I had to give it a shot. Â I have been to every steakhouse in the city and plenty more around the country, and this steak doesn't even crack my top 5. Â It wasn't terrible, it just wasn't at all delicious. Â I was told that you really need to eat one of the heirloom tomatos WITH the piece of steak to get the most out of it. Â For 76 bucks, this steak should dance on to my fork and do a backflip into my mouth. All in all - this place is thumbs up.

We just got back from a trip to the city and our son, who lives there, Â told us this was the best Italian food he had eaten. Â We went to Italy last year and this was as good as the best we had there. Â Try the cabbage salad with spicy olives and don't miss the panini. Â Not fancy but authentic and delicious.

Came here for brunch. Â After all the hype about the Black Label burger, I had to try it. Â I won't say it was the best burger I ever had, as some people do, but it definitely delivered and I left satisfied. Â I actually appreciated that it wasn't too big and didn't make me feel like I wanted to be rolled out of the place after devouring the burger and plate of fries (which were also delicious). Â Easily in the top tier for burgers, but $26 is just too much. Â If it were clearly the best one I'd ever had I'd say fine, but there are a lot of great burgers for much less. Â And the service also wasn't the best. Â So 5 stars for taste, and minus 1 for value and service.

I've gotten takeout from here many times, and the food is pretty good, but after today I am never going there again. Â Why? Â One time, several months ago, I found a long black hair in my takeout container. Â I gave the place another try and didn't find anything like that again for a while. Â Last month I found a staple in my tabbouleh. Â I gave Turco a third try. Â Guess what I found in my tabbouleh again today? Â Another staple. Â Boo. Â Disgusting.
Popped in here knowing nothing beforehand and was pleasantly surprised! Delish. Â Don't find myself in this neighborhood often but will stop by again.

I've always thought Scott Conant was a harsh critic on TV, but now I know he's just holding other chefs to his high standards. DInner at Scarpetta was a simple, wonderful, delicious meal. Bread Basket - I'm not a huge fan of the bread basket at most restaurants, but the bread here was so wonderfully fresh and yummy, I had a couple of pieces. I can't remember all the different types of bread offered, but all the ones I ate were good. The best one was definitely the stromboli, stuffed with smoked mozzarella, salami, basil, and cherry tomato. I wish more restaurants served bread like this! I slathered the rest of the bread in olive oil, eggplant caponata and mascarpone butter. I could eat this bread basket every day! Braised short ribs of beef w/ vegetable and farro risotto - The short ribs were so tender, no knife was needed. The risotto w/ the sauce was rich, wonderful and oh so tasty. Creamy polenta w/ fricassee of truffled mushrooms - A touch salty, but Â a perfect marriage of the smooth, creamy polenta and the rich, flavorful mushrooms.
