The truffle oil really highlights the earthy flavor of the mushrooms and takes this dish from good to great. Spaghetti w/ tomato and basil - I have never had spaghetti like this before. I've read the rave reviews of this dish, but was always a bit skeptical - how good can a simple spaghetti dish be? Apparently, really, really good. The perfect tomato sauce paired with perfectly al dente noodles, need I say more? Duck and foie gras ravioli w/ marsala reduction - The ravioli filling is creamy and delicious. although there isn't a strong flavor of duck. The marsala reduction is good and doesn't overwhelm the rest of the dish. Black tagliolini w/ mixed seafood, sea urchin and minted bread crumbs - This is one of the best black pastas I've ever had. This is the first time I"ve had black pasta with uni and I have to say, I really loved it. Seafood was cooked well and not chewy, but my fave part of the dish was the minted bread crumbs. Beautiful restaurant, great food, fast service, I'll definitely be coming back again.

A friend and I were walking around one night trying to find a good new place to eat. It looked cute and the menu sounded good so we gave it a shot. We were not sorry. The dinner was fantastic. I had the duck and it's some of the best I've ever had. I've since gone back many times for dinner. Brunch on the other hand, was a little too common for me. It wasn't anything special and would direct you to Bacchus for a French Bistro brunch.

Love it here! Â Bartenders are great. Â Popular night spot. Â The pickle back shots are my new favorite thing! It's a great dependable place to go for nights when I don't feel like trekking into Manhattan.

During the new years I had some time off, and my friend told me we have to try re.union. We went there for breakfast, and couldn't be happier. I had the Shakshuka which was so tasty! The sauce was great, the eggs were cooked exactly as they should be and the bread was fresh and crunchy. Easily one of the best I've had. My friend tried the grilled cheese sandwich, the fancy one. It looked so yummy, with tons of bacon and cheese. I had to taste it, and even though I loved the Shakshuka, next time I'll definitely get the sandwich.

Oysters weren't good as Colonie's (Atlantic ave) & Seafood Stew was OK, but not for $17. The service was also odd. The server was more noticeably attentive to my husband, while he barely made eye contact with me. Feeling snubbed, I am not sure I want to go back, but I hear cocktails rock here and the Dry-aged strip loin my partner had was very delicious. Don't bother with dessert though. Sad choice between chocolate ginger cake & buttermilk pie. Quite boring. I prefer Prime Meats on Court st (amazing food & impeccable service).

Sometimes I forget about genuinely perfected high end Italian cuisine. I'm not sure if it's the price point or the atmosphere that generally keeps me away, but I need to reconsider my strategy. We came in for a quick bite that confirmed that my attempts to a make pasta at home are somewhere between insulting and embarrassing. Quick thoughts: - Spaghetti in tomato & basil sauce - sounds simple & boring? I'd come back just for this. - Cavatelli w/ rabbit, porcini mushrooms & arugala - very good, but I would explore more of the menu before reordering. - Great service
been going here for years always great and my go to except when the line is long

Came here for lunch on Saturday. A friend recommend the place. Made a last min reso Â they still made us wait a little bit. We had the tuna burger that was really good almost raw but it wasn't. Salmon avocado tuna tartar it was delicious so smooth. The Benedict jane. Crab and crawfish it was so good. It was fried but wasn't too fried.

Ok here it goes... Ricotta cheese on grilled bread perfect Arugala salad very tasty- nice touches lamb sliders, Joey Campanaro watch your step these might be better - the goat cheese & roll takes ti over the top Ravioli with the robiola cheese is one great noodle which is stuffed perfectly, not too much , not too little. The Malati or whatever the uneven flat pasta with the pesto is called is seriously a great pasta & light, but flavorful pesto. Porchetta is tender, fatty, ande flavorful...pure peasant delight..the lightly dressed radichio & arugala goes well to cut the fattyness... The side of potaoes is not to be missed...toasted, fried with garlic oil..whatever...really special/ The focaccia is the lightest with a hint of tomato sauce on top is great for scapping up the sauces. The wine list is varied & priced gentle. The cake with the raspberry & pistaccio was moist, light & worked with a buttermilk gelati Illy coffee Nice staff & professional Only con: The bus staff tends to want to grab stuff off the table too fast. The wait staff does not rush you, but they do want to & at these price points, need to turn tables. We recommend & we will be back

Great atmosphere....nice cocktails (Happy Hour is pretty solid - you can only get them at the bar area, downstairs.). Food was excellent - try the hummus w/ jalapenos, brussels sprouts and falafel apps.

If you come here and only eat one thing - you can't go wrong with their famous Bash Burger. Â The meat is tender, succulent and perfectly cooked. Â The bacon onion jam works perfectly with the yummy cheese and meaty goodness. Â The size is also just right - no too big, not too small. Â I also can't say enough about the two onion rings that come with the burger. Â Perfectly fried, crispy and just all around good. Â The fries on the side were also nice, thanks to the perfect texture and the slender, yet steak fries feel. Â If that's all you're gonna get, you'll do fine with that. Of course they serve other items. Â We gave the shrimp scampi starter a try. Â It was definitely good, but for the high price tag and tiny portions, I think you're better off going with the burger. Â The fish tacos starter dish was definitely better for the price you pay. Â The sauce that goes with the tacos was divine and I think this works better as either a sharing dish or a small entree for folks with small appetites. The ambiance of this place is great - dark but quaint and definitely bustling nearly the bar area. Â The service was also top notch. Â It's a good place to catch up with friends or even for date night. Â  We didn't get a chance to try out the wine selection but the beers on tap were excellent. Â No complaints on that front. Â In short, this is a nice all-around place to grab a bite or drinks with friends and loved ones.

I'm going to give it 3 stars since I'm not a HUGE macaroon fan and can't tell the difference between a "cheap" one and the real deal. Â  The flavor variety is insane....rose petal macaroon-whoa! I like the creativity. I tried the lemon, raspberry, and salted carmel--the lemon was definitely my fave. For me personally, I just can't justify paying $2.70 for one tiny macaroon....but hey to each its own. Â I will say I felt incredibly rich as I ate them walking down Madison Ave. window shoppin

Best Indian food in NY hands down! The chicken and lamb dishes are absolutely superb! Great atmosphere, music, food and drinks you just can't wrong. UES has been craving for a restaurant/bar like this for years! It is now my regular.

had an intimate dining experience here the other day...with the guy sitting at the next table. never mind that we were with other peope, im sure he enjoyed my conversation with my friend as much as i loved hearing about his job, his hobbies and how his day really sucked. i can't remember what else he was talking about, but i was distracted by my divine dessert. also, the waitress kept squeezing in the small space between us so it was hard to stay focused. tartine is lovely, charming and i am a sucker for french fries and warm blueberry cobbler with ice cream (love, love, love) so i really cannot give it less than 4 stars, but don't expect an easy dining experience- it's cramped, crowded, and busyy.yyyy.

Never a disappointment. Â Always happy to see there menu change up seasonally. Â I tend to like the starters and sides a bit more than the entrees. Â Always end up with a table full of plates. Â Artichoke Dip, Deviled Eggs, Mashed Potatoes, Caesar Salad... Also a great place for raw bar.

The first time I came here was great. Had a wonderful time with Garrett Â (bartender) at the bar. So good I brought 7 more friends with me the next time. had a good time then. Then I tried to have a date at the "dining room" as a walk in. From then on, it turned horrible. With an empty dining room, we were sat at the bar tables, that lovingly view all the sitting patrons at the bar butts, and crowded cause the bar is usually crowded. Our server was inexperienced and brought us the wrong drinks. we asked for another table away from the bar, We were REFUSED with the excuse that "though we don't seem busy, we have reservations), my first date with this guy so far has turned bad when I suggested this place to meet, so I'm not happy We got offered to move tables when we got our entrees, after appetizers, because those "reservations" never showed and they are still empty. By that time we just gave up and sat at the horrible table while viewing numerous empty tables across the floor from us. I complained to the manager, she did take some drinks off and replied with "I hope you try us again" So I did, this past Saturday. I had work till 5 in Grand Central, after me and my friend decided to meet half way to each other, I recommended Maysville, BIG MISTAKE!!!!!!. I call ahead of time to ask if we arrive in 20 minutes, can we have a table for two. The hostess says yes. So, I get there early, get a drink at the bar after I put my name down with the hostess. That this point there are only two tables in the entire dining room. Garrett is bartending, which I didn't know if he remembered me, so I didn't say anything but just ordered a drink. My friend arrives, we ask for a table. and guess WHAT? SAME THING. we get sat at one table away from the other horrible table I perviously sat at the last time I was there, the bar tables. My friend asks if we can sit at other side, the guy goes back to the hostess to ask, she comes over again and the same EXCUSE!!! "Though it seems we are empty, we have a lot of reservations coming" I just say forget it, lets go somewhere else. The hostess gives us the saddest fake emotions of "I'm sorry, MAYBE YOU CAN TRY AGAIN" I turn around pissed and say "OR NEVER" I ask Garrett to close out my check, and he quickly starts to be like "Hey, you were here last time, you wrote that great review about me and my manager read it" I said " Yeah that was awhile ago" cause I was surprised at the fact he remembered. IT was a long time ago, Then Garrett says, don't worry illl take care of your drink.... once again Garrett goes up and beyond my expectations of service, I really think he is a great employee and to be honest, he is the only reason I keep coming back to this place because all the other experiences I have been here were just horrible. Then later my friend tells me the hostess mumbled underneath her breathe when we wanted a DECENT table "Well maybe next time you'll have a reservation" I call later to complain, speak to a manger Named Talia? (could be wrong) "Try us again, we want you to come back, we want you to have a good time, I really want to turn this around for you" The statement is nice but do I trust it, not necessarily, I've been told that before from a manger there. Overall I'm very upset over the whole experience in total. If I want to go back alone to enjoy the bar if Garrett is working, I think I will. Its embarrassing to try to bring people to a this restaurant as a first date or for a friend you rarely get to see, twice in a row, being rejected. Its just very damaging, I know its NYC and there are thousands of restaurants, but to have the same restaurant treat me so poorly when I'm referring their business to by trying to experience their service, i just can't explain how upsetting it is. But I have brought several people to this restaurant, dates, friends, colleagues, and out of three times, only 1 was great, and its because we sat at the bar. The other two were a disaster because we tried to sit at the dining room. I have worked in hospitality (food) for over 5 years in NYC and been manger, opened places, and done every job imaginable. I have never been to a restaurant so blind business sense and inexperienced in customer service. Its really insulting to be refused a table twice now. So I am relying the message to everyone else, if you have a reservation, good luck. If the bar is open, GO THERE!

The owner was basically the host. I'm from California and if this is the best pizza I've ever had, I'm a little shocked. Staff was absolutely great tho. Too bad you can't get a 1/2 n 1/2 specialty pizza which is what we wanted. But after a walk over the brooklyn bridge, great stop for pizza. The best? Send me a message and i'll give you my personal opinion.
Nom Nom NOM!!!!

We've eaten at two of the four restaurants in eataly, and were wonderfully surprised by both. Â The meat restaurant is wonderful, as is the fish. Â The food was terrific, and the service was excellent. Â We're an italian family, and love great food - we drove two hours to wait for a spot at the bar, but it was well worth it. Only problem were the crowds.

There is a reason everyone talks about the pancakes. They are GREAT. Crispy on the outside in a way you wouldn't expect... fluffy on the inside the way you would. Eggs florentine left a little to be desired. Something about the proportion of spinach/oil was off. On the flip side, the salmon/scallion/egg scramble was very flavorful. Service was attentive and pleasant. We'll definitely return here.

Why have I never been here before now? This place is so cute! The vibe is trendy, the music is at the perfect volume, the decor is simple + clean & lighting perfectly dim. The staff is so friendly, I almost want to be friends with all of them. The menu is sooooo perfect! Salty & sweet, veggie & meats! How do I chose? Not to mention everything is organic & locally grown. Karen, the talented, young sue chef sent out lots of dishes to try. Everything was amazing! I was literally licking my fingers! The proscutto fig pizza was heavenly, the spinach quinoa salad was Devine & the kabucha squash toast was the best thing I have ever eaten! I can't wait to come back because the menu is seasonal, so only the freshest veggies make it onto your plate & it is always something new!

I might be giving this just a little extra boost due to nostalgia, but god damn do I love Lombardi's Pizza! Every time I go to NYC with my family we hit up this spot. What's not to like? Yes it's a bit touristy but sometimes you've gotta just grin and bear it. The decorations and whatnot are cool in my book. I've had the white pies here and they're great, but I think the original margherita is the best. This time we got it with pepperoni and mushrooms. Killer choice! The pepperoni is small but spread generously over the whole area of the pizza, and each one is perfectly crisp. The mushrooms add an earthy flavor that actually complements the rest of the ingredients quite nicely. A large fed three people very, very nicely. It's cash only so bring some greenbacks.

Con: We wait about 45 minutes after our reservation for 2 seats. Pros: The staff really took care of us. They sat us down around the corner and offered us two glasses of champagne and an app as way of apology. They had some fun wines to try out and the tasting menu was a nice treat to see some great takes on a lot of interesting different tapas with a twist.
Went here while in NY, food was decent. Our server was horrible. Didn't want to give any refills. Took forever to get food. Very unfriendly. Don't recommend.

I'd like to start by saying I'm a big fan of Bobby Flay (his TV shows and his other restaurants...miss you Mesa Grill). I had high hopes for our Saturday night reservation, but ultimately left not overly impressed. Space is beautiful...did a great job. Â That was the highlight of the evening (along with dessert). Started out with a watered down martini at the bar (was a short pour that the bartender tried to fix by adding more vodka to the ice-water slush left in the shaker). The menu has a lot to offer at surprisingly reasonable prices for a celebrity NYC restaurant (especially the entrees). Started with: Eleven Layer Potato Caramelized Shallots, fried sage Garrotxa Quince Horseradish Bread Salad. Eggplant, Manchego, oregano, balsamic. All were pretty much Meh. Â The eleven layer potato was the best of the three, but was basically potatoes au gratin. GATO Salad- Greens & Reds, Asparagus, Ricotta Salata, Tomato, Crunch Wheat - just ok, overly dressed. For main course: Porterhouse Pork Chop, tomato pan juices, romesco polenta - had good flavor, but the pork was pretty tough. Not sure if this is a purveyor or kitchen issue. During the meal, I wanted to order a glass of red wine and asked for a taste of the Pinot Noir. The waitress returned and poured the whole glass. Â When I tried to stop her indicating that I wanted to taste the wine first, the response (albeit apologetically) was that they are not allowed to pour a taste. Â Whaaaat?? Â  I'm not asking for a 1/2 glass, just enough to decide if I like the wine. The waitress was accommodating, but the the experience left a bad taste in my mouth that was not from the wine. Wine preference is extremely subjective and everyone's palate is different. I've never encountered a restaurant of this caliber in NYC that prohibited giving patrons a taste of the wine they are about to order. We finished with: Espresso soaked bread pudding with Mascarpone Crema and bittersweet chocolate- Â Was delicious and the culinary high point of the meal. All in all disappointing. Â Could have been my high hopes. Â I'm not sure if all the great reviews are from star-struck food network groupies (the emperors new clothes) or if I just caught Gato on an off night.

I had Hu Kitchen cater a client lunch today. Â WOW - their food really is that good . Â We had the Rotisserie Chicken, the Chicken Tenders, Tuna Salad, Quinoa Salad, Miso Kale Salad, Cauliflower Puree, and an assortment of cookies and juices/teas. Â Everything was truly delicious - super flavorful and not at all salty; very fresh and clearly made same-day; and absolutely satisfying and filling without leaving you feeling lethargic and bloated. Â We had an assortment of people in the meeting and even the 'least healthy' among us was blown away and wished he could 'eat that food every day.' Â Oh, and my personal favorite for dessert were their macaroons - better than any bakery I've tried... and I shamefully know my NYC baked goods. Â Jessica, one of the owners, was a delight to work with as well. Â I will definitely recommend Hu Kitchen to others for catering needs and can't wait to go to their restaurant with friends. Â Thanks for an awesome addition to the city!

SO SO worth it to make the trek into the heart of Chinatown, outside of the touristy Chinatown, to eat here. Â The pork dumplings are amazing and the sesame pancake with anything in it is incredible. Â I had mine with egg which comes with cilantro and carrots. Â My mouth is watering just thinking about it. Â My husband and I walked to the Brooklyn Bridge and ate our dinner in the middle of the bridge with a view of the city. Perfect!

I came to this place while I'm in New York because its highly tauted. Â The look of the diner looked unchanged and very classic. Â I did what seemed to be the only way to go, I had a Bistro burger and a McSorley 's Ale. The beer was good for being a beer and the burger was very tasty. Â I'd say it was a notch above a restaurant burger, like a TGIF Jack Daniel's burger for instance, its a notch above that. Â It's not the best burger I ever have, i'm from California and we have In N Out, enough said. Â Corner Bistro is the total package, from the look of the place to the taste of the burger, I vouch for it.

My girlfriend and I have been to Giovanni's "Brooklyn Eats" twice now and both of us agree that this is most likely the worst sit down Italian restaurant in Park Slope. Where in the world are all these 4 and 5 star reviews coming from? Our first visit was, for lack of a more creative description, pretty crappy. I can't really speak much on the specifics since this was almost a year ago at this point, but suffice it to say nothing about our dinner stood out. In fact I would say the one thing that made an impression on us was probably how incredibly bland both our pastas were. Very disappointing. Regardless, we decided to make the same mistake twice last night and the results weren't any different. We both ordered the hanger steak medium rare which, while tender, somehow tasted like nothing. Seriously, how do you manage to suck all of the flavor out of something as simple as a steak? Do they have some kind of special machine in the back that does this? The salad we started with was equally weak, and was one of the saddest looking Â dishes i've ever seen. It was basically a pile of wilted lettuce with way too much dressing and some random pieces of meat and cheese scattered around the bottom of the plate. At $9.00 it was a total ripoff. Bread was tough. Wine was sour. Silverware was dirty, and the dining room is lit kinda weirdly. The list goes on. I'm starting to wonder if everyone else on Yelp is getting high before they come to eat here.

Like it very much :) A little small and can get a bit loud depending on who's sitting around you, but still maintains an intimate feel (Tuesday night). The service was good and the bottle of wine we brought was gladly opened and poured at no charge! (Big, big plus) Ordered two appetizers: the classic mussels and the goat cheese tart. Mussels were perfectly cooked, in a white wine sauce, and not one mussel was empty. Goat cheese and aged Swiss cheese tart was extremely flavorful and coupled with some mixed greens to calm your mouth down. The quail dish was, again, perfectly cooked and seasoned; a healthy portion as well. The duck breast was also extremely flavorful and the meat was tender and very well prepared. It did seem, to me at least, that the meat was a bit overwhelmed by the sauce it was covered with, not in terms of flavor but quantity. The sauce was a port and red wine sauce. Desert was the Choux puff pastry filled with vanilla whipped cream and fine sugar. I didn't know so I asked what Choux pastry was like and the waitress said "it's just like a puff pastry". That was already in the menu but it doesn't really answer my question...I guess the answer I was looking for was: It's a pastry baked without a rising agent. The high moisture content in the dough becomes steam and puffs the pastry during the baking process giving it its light attribute. But it's all good...and so was the espresso. Overall, the place is good, the service is good, food is very good, price is good, BYOB is great, cash only is OK.

It's strange for me to not be in the West Village on the weekends brunching. I made an exception to come here on a Sunday morning since it was super close to my apartment. The wait wasn't too bad, 20 minutes for two. The roomie and I ordered blood marys while we were waiting around. They were freakin delicious - super spicy, just the way I like my BMs. The crowd here is pretty upscale...Chanel and D&G donned customers eating brunch and hanging out by the bar. I had the Turkish Eggs and a side of Quinoa Hash Browns. The eggs were definitely interesting. I wouldn't recommend it if you aren't into Greek yogurt. The hash browns came out in a cube-like form; they were cooked spot on - crispy and not a soggy mess. I wasn't a big fan of the quinoa taste though. Not a big fan of the brunch menu, but I'd give this place a shot for dinner. I'm guessing the Michelin judge person didn't come here for brunch since it was only mediocre at best.

Decided to stop in here for a quick lunch on a Friday afternoon. Â Sat at the bar and decided to indulge myself in the grilled cheese sandwich. Now, I've eaten grilled cheese sandwiches before, and I wasn't expecting much anything different. This sandwich, on the other hand, was hands down the best grilled cheese sandwich I'll ever have. Â No doubt about it. In fact, to call it a grilled cheese sandwich is to do it injustice. Â Two huge pieces of bread that are covered in some type of crispy/fried cheese, and a melted guyere cheese on the inside. I'm not even sure what the ingredients were, I just remember it was heavenly. Atmosphere: Awesome place to grab a beer and a bite. Â Casual, cordial, homey, and outright awesome. Â I'll be going back many, many times to come, considering its two blocks away.

Excellent pizza, insulting service. My party made the mistake of ordering dessert (a passable cannoli) after we had finished our pizza. What happens if you linger, for any reason, after they have arrogantly whisked your plates away is that you are immediately of no use to them as clients. Grimaldi's business model is: get them in, get them fed, get them out. So after about 2 minutes into our cannoli, our (Serbian?) waiter shoved new place settings and silverware in front of us as if the next party was already seated. Their tables are small so there isn't a whole lot of room to maneuver at this point. A minute later, he dropped our check in front of us. We were miffed but were intent on enjoying dessert. A minute after that he dropped 2 large menus in front of us. At this point there is no room whatsoever. We reluctantly gave him a credit card at this point but made it known to the manager that the service was a joke. I live here. I am used to rushed service but Grimaldi's is ridiculous.

Meh. I have ordered from here a few times for delivery and recently tried out the brunch. Â When ordering I got basic pasta dishes, which were good. Â Fresh ingredients and not too heavy. Â  Brunch was not nice. Â Our server was a little bizarre, and both my friend and I were disappointed with our food. Â It bummed us out because she was up visiting and we barely see each other... just crazy how much of a damper a weird meal can be on a visit. Â She ordered the french toast and it came smothered in canned mandarin oranges - juice and all. Â It was really gross and her meal was totally soggy. Â The oranges were not on the menu so it was disappointing. Â We didn't complain but we got out of there ASAP. I'll also add that their unlimited Bloody Marys and Mimosas both come from a pitcher, that the server fills at your table. Â That turns me off majorly.. I like a drink to be freshly made with fresh ice or something considerate! I had two Bloody's and must also add that I got zero buzz off of it. Â On an empty belly! I never trust pitcher poured alcoholic beverages...

I've been here a few times. Â It's basic udon noodle shop, nothing fancy but it is satisfying if that's what you're in the mood for. Â I usually get the fried fish cake udon and gyoza. Â The gyoza is usually stuck together and slightly burnt on the bottom, but they are juicy and flavorful. One order is on the small side, with 6 to an order. Â The fish cake is a round one that's cut into 4 pieces, and it is tasty with good texture when you bite into it. Â The udon soup base has a strong msg taste, which I don't mind since I love to drink soup full of msg. Â The noodle was soft and chewy, like udon. The prices are very reasonable for midtown, and they tend to open late.

Old fashioned old fashions - served perfect without calling them so. A brunch visit in early May allowed us to sample several plates. Rye Benedict was not as impressive as may be desired. Tiny pieces of pork belly on tiny muffins. My best guess also says that the hollandaise was whipped with a beater? Scotch eggs prepared as expected with a thick cheese sauce atop bacon. A bit dry, the sausage is fried for too long. Pork belly itself!! Thick luscious slices of marbled heaven. Wow. And more manhattans.

Let me tell you- I dont even like seafood. But the generous helpings, coupled with delicious taste has made me a fan. Go with a group. This place is best enjoyed where there are at least 4 of you- you cannot eat an entree by yourself- at least if you dont wanna be sick later. My experience- 5 of us, Jalea, Avocado salad, a plate of sausage and fries, and a pitcher of Sangria- 74 dollars!! We were full and still had money to go drink.

This place is an oasis in a sleepy neighborhood dining wasteland. After an obsolete Yelp review steered me to a closed venue, we hiked up here and had a very good meal with awesome beers. They had me at grilled local squid (with fingerling potatoes, spicy-chili tapenade, and lemon). The pulled-pork sandwich was good as well, though I kind of wished there were more options on the sandwich menu. But what's there is good. Service was slow but friendly. It was the mid-afternoon doldrums between brunch and dinner and I think we all felt it--patrons and staff. Nice, relaxing stop.

Taim does not serve the best falafel I've ever eaten but it IS good and the crispy shoestring fries made with aoili oil are even better. I just had to try their famous banana/date smoothie and I was so disappointed I will not order that item from their menu again. The date part of the smoothie was undetected and the frozen bananas were water logged/icy. The cost of this smoothie did not justify the overall experience. I'm a little put off at street food costing so much, a falafel and a side of fries costs 12 dollars not including tip, Â ( to be fair the sandwich is huge and loaded with vegetables and hummus). I also like the staff here. They are courteous and professional even when while being harassed by the drunks who stumble in from the local bars who are so twisted it takes them several hours reading the menu and even longer placing an order!
The food as always was excellent. The lemon Meringue pie is just crazy.

I am writing this review strictly for Seahorse's BRUNCH. I have visited Seahorse over 6 times now for brunch and still have yet to disappoint. The reason I've frequented there so often for brunch is because they have one of the largest brunch menus available (2 large pages). Â I love it. Â You can find anything from eggs and grits, to eggs Benedict over crab cakes, to Cap'n Crunch french toast (which I still have yet to try), to pork chops, and of course fish tacos. The atmosphere is cutely decorated with a marine theme. Â The last 3 times I've went I noticed a lot of families dining there, and more kids then normal, but it was cool. Their food is reasonably priced. Â Mason jar Bloody Mary's and fresh lemonade are great, the mimosas are served in flute champagne glasses and are yummy, but a little pricey for the size. Every time I leave I always say to myself, I have to come back for Happy Hour or dinner....Got to make that happen soon! ;)
Cheap and delicious. pork steamed soup dumplings and scallion pancakes are a must. $20 got me really full

First of all I have not had the most perfect experience here but I still cannot give it less than 4 stars. Â I am beating myself up over this. I have to be honest right? Been twice and had two very different experiences. Â  You come here for a reason. Whether it be the beer or pigs head, lamb belly, or the craft beer you have your reasons. I have tried a ton of menu items here and been ticked to no end when the things I want are not available (happens a lot so get here early). Â I get even more ticked about the fact that our seats weren't available for an additional 40 minutes from when I was told on my second visit) . My conflicted emotions surround the fact that I cannot argue is how damn good their food is. Â Even though I Â  Everything here is incredible. Last time they did not have the lamb belly (still waiting to try this) or the pigs head (eat the eyeball if you dare). It costs $65 and fine for 4 people if getting other menu items. While it may be the house novelty, its delicious, and you will leave the restaurant feeling like you ate a pigs head...not pretty but you will be full). As neither pigs head and lamb belly the two things are the menu features, we were upset. We ended up with the ribeye at twice the price ($120) of the other two. Yes it was the best steak I ever had, but still not happy that I didn't have my options for a lower costing item. Â If it wasn't so good you can be sure I would have raised hell. Â  Other menu items that are a must buy are lamb tartare and the ham board (3 piles of ham with delicious biscuit and honey). For a buyer beware protip - Thursday, Friday, Saturday could be dangerous. You might end up shortchanged with your wait time and menu choices once seated unless you are super early. Your best bet is a Sunday or Monday night to have quick seating and a full menu at your fingertips. Another option is to plan a private event (10 or more people). I suggest giving them a call and exploring that option. Seemed like a great option when I was discussing it with the manager.

We ordered Chicken Kebab platter, it came with salad, rice, pita humus and 2 souses. waiting for food takes a bit of time but it worth waiting. The cost of the lunch will surprise you, it's only 8,5$ for this much food. Everything is very tasty, u can literally just point on something in the menu and won't regret you'r choice. Stuff is also really nice and friendly. Place is never get's crazy busy, so there is no waiting in the line to seat. has a TV to watch some sport. Coming back every morning.

quite possibly the most overrated restaurant ive ever been to. its really cheap, and i think that makes people like the food more than they should. honestly, i think the chain lemongrass is better even though its a chain. i think ppl also like it more than they should b/c of the clubby decor... thai food in park slope just kinda sucks in general compared to hell's kitchen

Wonderfull restaurant!! Â Food is excellent, and atmosphere is inspired. Â Owner is a great guy, but the rotating grandmother chefs are the secret ingredient. Â  Service was a bit slow, but food is very authentic and any wait is well worth your time. Â Just order another glass of wine!

I've been here many times for dinner here with friends for catching up and it's always been pleasant. Granted, these were mostly weeknights so service maybe more attentive and friendlier than brunch madness. Water was always refilled and when it's AYCE mussels, the shell bucket would be replaced when full. Fries aren't as great as Frites in EVillage, but they're not bad either. AYCE mussels are first served in the broth/flavor of your choice in 2lbs portion and subsequently u can switch it up or continue with 1 lb buckets. Other options such as meatballs pasta, chicken pot pie, steak, and burgers have all been solid. Haven't actually tried anything bad really. Decor walking in has the bistro feel, there's posters and books of The Little Prince and TinTin. There's also an enclosed patio seating in the back. The tables are placed more tight than I'd like, but the food will keep me coming back.

I went for dinner at around 8.30/9ish and there was no wait. The staff at the bar/kitchen area directly to the left were super friendly, they all had really big smiles and all that. I was pretty excited because they support local farms and I'm all for that but I was expecting a significantly lower price point (I think I was probably thinking of the lunch menu which seems like a great deal-$9 for soup or salad and a main). They had a lobster pad thai special that was tempting but at $26, was not an amount I was willing to spend on a restaurant that I was completely new to. I went with the "authentic old-school pad thai" and my friend got the pad see ewe. We also got a free cocktail ("Fall in Love") for checking in on yelp! The pad thai was very sweet, there was way too much sauce. The pad see ewe considerably better in terms of balanced flavor but was incredibly greasy. The cocktail was yummy. It was very refreshing, tasted like real pear (grainy bits and all), and didn't have that overbearing taste of alcohol. Also, our server was all like "WRITE A NICE COMMENT" before putting in our drink order so. yeah.

Great Restaurant. Great menu. My girlfriend and I ventured down last night (a friday) and waited less than ten minutes for a table. We had two glasses of wine and four courses and paid less than 100 dollars. To start we had the frogs legs They were super juicy and the sauce that accompanied them was perfectly spicy and worked splendidly with the frogs legs. Then the Foie Doughnut What a beautiful combination. This was the best Foie prep I have ever had! Everything about it was awesome. Then the steak The protein was perfectly cooked and seasoned. With it came avocado, kimchi, and roasted potatoes all Â of which paired brilliantly. Then Oh MY God!! Then the LAMB Two pieces of lamb belly and colantro! That was it but it was incredible! Thanks for a great meal we will be back soon

Horrible service...waited 30+min for our food, just to get the wrong order! Â Food was just mediocre at best....AND they add in the tip!!! We were only a party of 2!! No wonder service sucks!! Won't be coming back here anytime soon!

I adore Habana Outpost and am so glad that it is in Ft. Greene and EXPANDING! What more can you ask for on a lovely spring/summer/fall day? *great drinks *yummy snacks and such *cool and diverse crowd *ample space either covered or out in the open If you are a fan of dining outdoors as I am, you should def check this place out. It is not award winning food or cocktails, but they get the job done in a fun and laid back manner. PLEASE don't leave without a frozen margarita!
I came here for the seafood. Everything was fresh. I didnt like the setup of the seating that much, seemed crowded but that is just me!

Hearth is a must! The salad with white anchovies is the perfect summer appetizer. The Duck breast with confit is delicious! The fois gras dish provides the perfect balance of tart, sweet, buttery, and bitter, between all its accouterments. And the pork loin is truly satisfying, served with yummy sweetbreads. The deserts are good. But nothing out of this world. Overall I would say that Hearth is a master at combining flavors and textures. Everything is a joy to eat.

How unexpecting to find this sandwich shop inside a typical Korean market. My friend lives around the corner so we came and got the PHO REAL sandwich and guess what it does really taste like you're eating PHO except without the soup and plus avocados. I only wrote about this bc it was something I've never seen this concept before and was not disappointed at all!

I really our weekend dinner. Â I was a bit worried when I heard everyone talk about "small plates." Â However, from what we ordered, they were not small at all. Â Plenty of food for a single plate per person. Â While it gets busy on the weekends, the servers were working hard to ensure everyone had a great experience. Â Will be back.

I am relatively new to Mediterranean food and I have little experience in the cuisine. I cannot say that this place is better or worse than other places, but it was an amazing dining experience for me. The food was amazingly good. I can comfortably recommend this restaurant to anyone who is uncomfortable with trying out new ethnic food. One downside is that this place is quite pricey and the portions are very small, which could make the bill jump quite high without really realizing it. All of the dishes are relatively low priced, but the portions are very small and you end up ordering more than what you originally planned and the final bill can be a surprise. Considering that for the same price, you could be dining at one of the more finer restaurants in the Michelin Star tier, this is a bummer. However, the food is excellent and the service is decent. I like the lighting and the interior. It is quite comfortable and warming with respect to the dim lighting and the reflection on the walls. From the appetizers, we ordered Hommus, Tabbouleh, Warm Eggplant with Pita bread and they were amazing. Warm eggplant in particular was outstanding. From the Meat section, we ordered the Chicken Shish Taouk, Kafta, Lamb Kebab, and they were all decent. The Chicken Shish Taouk was very bland and plain and I couldn't see why it has been so overly written among the Yelp reviews. Kafta was better in my opinion and Chicken Shish Taouk was an overhype. In general, I felt that this place has its forte in the meat section, so try to talk to the waiter/waitress for more details on the dishes. Everyone has mentioned Candy Bar as a must, but I feel that there is nothing Lebanese, or Mediterranean about the Candy Bar. It tastes like any chocolate infused desserts in any other restaurants or bakeries. A more ethnic and delightful experience in my humble opinion is Mixed Baklava, which is a traditional Lebanese pastry. It is excellent and more representative of Ilili. Candy Bar is a chocolate cake that simply cannot go wrong, but it's very American, rather than Mediterranean. All in all, dining at Ilili was a pleasant experience. I recommend!

For most of my life in NYC I have been on a quest to find the best Californian-style burrito. Chipotle did satisfy that urge for quite a while, but then I stumbled upon Dos Toros. This place has the same exact format as Chipotle, it's fast and very fresh. However, the thing that makes this place stick out is that everything they serve is edible heaven. From the carnitas that are divinely juicy and so tender that you can basically eat it with a spoon to the chicken that is grilled to perfection to the steak that is tiny chunks of everything I could ask for in a meat to the guacamole which is creamy and exploding with beautiful flavor. Â It doesn't matter what you order here because EVERYTHING is pure amazingness. Go to Dos Toros if you really want to know what a great burrito should taste like.

What took me so long to review BLB? I don't know... It's one of my favorite spots in the neighborhood. After enjoying yet another delicious dinner this week, I had to YELP. Even if I haven't YELPED in a long time. There were 6 of us and we did some damage. All of the empanadas were excellent. Â The Bandeja Paisa rocks each and every time we order it. Colombian style Arroz con Pollo was perfect. Grilled Salmon with fruit salsa was delicious and sexy (hey at least it was for me OK) Â Patacon con Todo drenched in that Aji sauce. Mmmm.... My sister's diet consists of 90% chicken SO of course she ordered the Colombian fried chicken special w/ honey to drizzle on, jalapeno mac & cheese and ensalada rusa. That moist fried chicken, well seasoned and crunchyr? and a side of honey? Oh yeah! Big Big Jug of Sangria. Delicious! Â Mojitos? My aging mother licked the empty glass. No, she doesn't have a drinking problem. It was just that good. Oh, and our waiter, Javier K. is the best! Buen provecho!

Finally came here for their famous burger when my friends were in town! I read an article before I came here, claiming the BL burger here to be the #2 burger in USA. Maybe the expectations were set too high... the burger was good.. but for $26? I expect more. The burger was done just the way we wanted - medium rare but I find something missing from the flavor. My friend had the monk fish and it was very good! I had a cocktail called Rhubarb Sophie and it was really refreshing and tasty. I would come back again, but to try other items on the menu instead of the burger - but if you have never been here before, order 1 to share among your friends just to say 'I've had it before!!'

My buddy had been talking this place up, so I knew I had to make the trip. His advice - Cuban corn. Oh my god. Roasted Corn covered in a spicy mayo and cheese with a lime zest garnish. I never knew that corn could be so filling until eating here today - and it was cheap! Maybe $6 before tip for two massive pieces. My only regret is that I didn't get a chance to explore the menu a bit more, but judging by the smiles on everyone's faces, I'd say it's a hit. Pro Tip: If you're solo, grab a seat at the counter. Guaranteed to atary

We were in the city for business and randomly ended up at Woodrow's. The bar has a great atmosphere and a fantastic staff. My group mingled with the regulars who were very fun and welcoming. I had the spicy shrimp which was killer. The owner came over to us and greeted us. She has an incredible warmth and sincerity. It was a really great night for my group. We've been back since and it was another fun time. It makes me wish I had a Woodrow's down the street from my place. Thank you Erin - you make us feel at home. Sean

Corner Bistor is an unaffected neighborhood spot with amazing burgers that are a bargain! It's great for late night munchies after going out in the west village or meat packing district. I have to say that the burgers are probably the best I've had for the price and I will be going here from now on instead of Pastis for my late night outings in the neighborhood.

The best barbecue New York City by far. Â It's a nice walk across the Williamsburg Bridge to this little spot in Williamsburg. It's a block away from the entrance to the bridge. We ordered the brisket, hotlinks, pulled pork, wedge salad, some sides(mac & cheese, chili, potato salad). The brisket was the best I've ever tasted in the city. The rest of the food was pretty good also. But the brisket was the star of the show. Next time I'm just going to order 2 pounds of brisket and sit back and relax. 4 only because it was a bit pricey.

I was looking for a new brunch place yesterday. Decided to try Sanford's due to the 400+ reviews. It's nice inside, diner like but a bit trendy. Small though and no waiting area. We were squished in between the hostess stand and front door waiting for a table. I ordered the Croque- Madame and my bf ordered the Western Â Quesadilla. From all the raving reviews, I expected better food. My Croque Madame was not flavorful at all. This is one of my favorite breakfast meals so I know what it's supposed to taste like. This was lightly toasted bread, dry, no salt, no flavor. It tasted like dry toast with an egg slapped on top. Very disappointing. I tried my bf's Western Quesdailla and it Â wasn't great. He wasn't thrilled with it either. Â Everything was underwhelming. I would have rather gone to Jackson Hole or just a regular diner and had better cheaper food. After we ate, his stomach was bothering him. My stomach has also been bothering me since I ate there yesterday at 2:30pm and got worse throughout the day. I 99% sure I'm sick from the food, I even had to call out of work today. Â  I won't Â be returning here. Maybe other items are on the menu are great, but I'd rather not take the chance.
get a flight of bud
This is a small place but the atmosphere is so nice. the food is superb! Will be a new go to spot!

How in the world has this place escaped me????? Â Seriously one of the BEST places I can remember eating at. Â I was just there last night and I SOOOO plan on being there this week again. Beef carapcio- not my thing- AMAZING you MUST get the bronzino- that's the fish I eat all the time- this was the BEST I ever had gnocci- perfect broccoli rabe raviolis- WOW pork chop- sick!!!! you have NEVER had potatoes like this in your life- I can not explain the perfection of the outside lightly crisp and the perfect inside- I don't like potatoes but these- I COULD NOT EAT ENOUGH- the broccoli rabe is awesome- def a major kick but I don't think they can make a bad anything. Â  This is now my new gem- and if you read my reviews you will see I am a PAIN IN THE ASS to please- this is a wow wow wow- GO NOW

Somehow lucked out and immediately got a table for two around 4pm on a Tuesday. The ramen here is good, but not outstanding. I ordered the Chicken Paitan Ramen, but the noodles were slightly undercooked and pretty chewy. The chicken itself would have been dry had it not been swimming in the broth. I enjoyed the broth; it was a simple salty and oniony concoction that's incredibly satisfying on a chilly day. If you've never been to Totto Ramen before, please keep in mind that the place is TINY. It's essentially a narrow hallway in a basement. No joke. Don't dare bring a group here. The place is CASH ONLY, so leave your cards in your wallet and hit up the ATM. Despite my less-than-spectacular experience here, I would actually go again, and hope that I can once again slip in without waiting.

After reading all the wonderful reviews, I went to Jadis with three girl friends. I was not disappointed! We got there early around 830pm, so we got a table right away. It was snowing out, but inside the place was toasty! We ordered appetizers and a bottle of wine. The bill came out very reasonable! Such a good find on the not-so-busy block of LES. The food was delicious and the waitress was knowledgeable and attentive. I will definitely go back!

Love: the ridiculously cheap $15 butcher steak (hangar steak) which is always perfectly done - a beautiful medium rare is sometimes hard to find. The $6 side of thick-cut bacon is also pretty awesome. Hate: the wait. First time was 45 minutes, 2nd was an hour. They should just take reservations at least on weekdays so I don't have to always pop into another restaurant and have pre-dinner appetizers (which I've done both times). If I could plan it out, I would end up eating way more there. In summary: awesome grilled steak for the cheapest I've ever paid.. If you don't mind the unpredictable and usually longgggg wait.

Food was amazing, tried just about everything, the pork belly? ridiculous, the ribs ? they fall off the bone . The pulled chicken and pork wasn't bad either. The sweet/spicy sauce had a sweet subtle kick. oh and Kathy was awesome!!!. Came from long island to try this place because I'm on a grass fed beef kick....I will be back...

Yeah, yeah. Â You think I must be a tourist. Â You think I must not be a local because I like this place. But that's completely untrue. Â I lived in New York for many years and ate out almost every single day. Â There's a reason this place has 2000+ reviews and maintains a good rating. Â Just because people know about it doesn't make it bad pizza. Â I've been to Patsy's, multiple Ray's, 2 Bros, Di Fara's, Artichoke Basille, Grimaldi's, etc. etc. Â New York has a million pizza spots and everyone has their own opinion on how they like it. Lombardi's was the original, uses coal, makes a beautiful thin crust charred pizza and uses quality toppings. Â The best way to get it is to get the original Margherita pizza unadulterated. Â That way you get thin slices, that just burst with flavor and aren't too soggy. Â Only when you add tons of toppings, the slices get sloppy as a thin crust pizza folds underneath the weight. Â Eat it original and don't complain.

Popular by terms of limited seating. Lovely place. Even lovelier breakfast. Even if you think it is annoying when people do it, you will probably grab your iphone and take a snapshot at the early morning meal you order at Clinton. Very often there seems to be a 2 hr wait. Go shop in SOHO while you wait. I liked everything about this place.

My go to for dessert after dinner at one of the countless restaurants in TriBeCa - it's the best way to cap off your night. I recommend their hot cocoa and pb&j cookies, and can't forget the homemade apple pie with a generous serving of vanilla ice cream for that perfect bite. Also great for brunch - super generous portions. Love their eggs Benedict, healthy veggie/fruit smoothies, and plantains as a side. Wait can be a bit longer if you go at peak times but rarely longer than 30min - the place is huge!

the first time i came here it was on a week day at around lunch time. Â there was a wait but luckly it was just the two us so we waited for about 15 minutes before we were seated. Â the place is quite small and long. Â it's a cozy ambiance that is perfect for eating ramen on a rainy day or during the fall and winter months. Â the service was quick and efficient just the way i like it. Â the cooks were all japanese which got me really excited because i was sure that we were going to taste some authentic ramen. Â I'm telling you they did not disappoint. Â i had the spicy ramen and it was heaven in my mouth. Â warmed me up very quickly. Â i had a side of avocado with it just to give it a cool refreshing twist. Â my friend is japanese and he told me this was one of the best ramen he's ever tasted so that just confirmed my taste buds right there. second time i went here i tried to come early, it opens at 11am and i arrived at 1040am. i thought i was going to be too early, it being a thursday and all but i was surprised to see there was already a bunch of people waiting. Â again the service was quick and the food was still very yummy...I stuck to the spicy ramen with the side of avocado...its my staple dish now whenever i go there. be prepared to wait, it is quite a tiny place but the ramen is quite worth it!

Even as busy as it was for a Saturday brunch, the service was decent and the food was excellent! I feel in love with the Sam I Am eggs (asparagus and feta in the scrambled eggs) and even recreated the dish when I got back home to Miami!!! I will definitely make time to visit again when I back in NYC!
the best thai food in nyc

let's just keep this short and sweet: ONE OF THE BEST MEALS OF MY LIFE!! 1.Pork Buns: Do believe the hype! 2. Cured Hamachi: Elegant, bright, and complex. Lots of flavor going on for such a simple dish. 3. Soft Boiled Egg: w/Summer Beans and bacon. Again, simple ingredients but you're in FLAVOR COUNTRY! Not something I would usually order but I'm glad we did. 4.Crispy Pig's Head: came looking like a crab cake, tasted like fatty delicious pig. Genius! 5. ...and we had one more thing but i started to get drunk at this point. wish i hadn't however. great for parties of 6, for the minimum 6 person bo ssam of course, but if you can't get that many friends to go, just order a la carte. i had a MIND BLOWING experience and will definitely be back!
Yummy! Especially the New Orleans milk drink. Also shared the pancake dish, which was incredibly filling. Be sure to head down the street to try the Red Hook Lobster Pound too.
This is the most delicious piece of Pizza I have ever experienced in my entire life.

What a wonderful place to eat and have some friendly conversation with Sara. Â She made me feel right at home even giving me a sample of the freshly roasted nuts that had just come out of the oven. Â Delicious! I had the poached egg with thick asparagus. Â It came with a side of some fancy greens with s slight balsamic dressing. Â In town for a few days and will be back to try something for dinner.

Margarita pizza was amazing love the fact that they use real fresh mozzarella. Takes a bit of time to get our food to our table. But hey it's fresh pizza I was fine with the wait. Next time I will try with different toppings.

Unfortunately, I was overall disappointed with my experience here. The food was below mediocre. The soup "specials" were bland and served at room temperature. The decor of the restaurant is far superior to the kitchen's product. Â I definitely expected more.
This is amongst the best Thai food in the city. Authentic. Lots of specials every night. Not that expensive. Only issue is the size relative to the number of diners. Long waits are common.

A small and cozy bar where they have a variety of rice wine. The ambiance was nice with jazz music and good for small group of 2-3 friends to hang out. Â We came in to grab a drink while waiting for our table for the next door restaurant. They have some Japanese bar snacks for you to choose from to go with the drinks. If you are up for adventurous food, takowasa (wasabi marinated raw octopus) is pretty good with rice wine!

Just came here last night for dinner with two other guest. Â I happily sat at the bar enjoying the happy hour special which was delicious. Â I'm personally not a huge fan of oysters but I did enjoy them especially the west coast ones. Â I also received a brilliant explanation from the bartender regarding the different types of oysters which was helpful for someone like myself. Â The bartender was also very helpful in assisting me with getting a table for my party of 3 since most tables are for 2. Â She was always asking if my party was ready when a table opened up which I appreciated instead of passing my name just because they weren't physically present yet. Â  The overall meal was delicious as well. Â Ordered the cured salmon and squid to start as well as several more oysters for the table. Â Not a huge fan of cured salmon more of a squid type of person but I thought the salmon was exceptional. Â Personally I thought the squid tasted a little too much like the grill and lacked seasoning or salt. Â I have not complaints about the grill flavor but I just think there should have been some more salt but with that being said I'm no chef. Â  For the main plates we shared four mains between us and there were no complaints. Â However the highlight was definitely the clam fettuccine which is a must. The service was also amazing and this place definitely does live up to the hype on yelp. Â I was afraid I would be disappointed because of all the high praise but i will definitely be coming again soon. I also love how the establishment takes an interest in the voice of their customers.
over priced, the salad is fresh but something you can put together at home easily. Coffee is really plain.

I've been coming down here since I was a kid with my mom, who used to go down with her dad who worked down on the docks back in the day. Â Thank God that nothing has changed. If you make the trip (which you absolutely should, and as soon as you can), there's only one sandwich you should bother yourself with: the potato and egg. It's pretty much the only one I ever order, and it is without question a pilgrimage-worthy sandwich. Ask for it with just a bit of ketchup for sweetness.
really good pizza, annoying line and tourists

from a recommendation, we took our parents to joe's shanghai to eat the infamous dumplings. honestly, it was just ok. it wasn't a horrible experience and the food was okay--i just don't think the food was so amazing that it warranted the almost hour wait. the crispy beef however was quite delicious!

Came for brunch recently and I had the Eggs Bella Donna... Poached eggs atop polenta with sauteed spinach and portobello mushrooms with pancetta and a tomato sauce. Â This may be one of the best breakfast dishes I've had! Â Great french bistro ambiance, not too loud, but bustling! Â The bread was good with room temperature butter, that wasn't too hard to spread! Our server was attentive without being intrusive... We will definitely come again on our next visit to Soho!

The line here is often out the door. Â But the place is tiny, so if there's like 3 people, the line is out the door. Â  The cones of frites are greasy goodness, but they fry/season in small batches so it's not super quick. Â True to Belgian form, they offer lots of mayo-bases sauces. Â Frites sauce (essentially mayo) and the especial (mayo, ketchup and chopped onion...a little strange) are free. Â Others you have to pay, but they have a 3 sauce combo which is good. Â I got basil mayo, horseradish mayo and curry ketchup. Â All the sauces were fine, maybe a little weak. Â I could have really gone for some pilli-pilli sauce. Â  It's not quite Brussels, but the major elements are there.

The food were awesome which topped with great coffee (unlimited amount. Step aside Starbucks, Â I wish Freda has many sisters who can open stores all over NYC.:-). All four entrees were great Â and service made it this an outstanding Sunday morning experience. Â  Go early if you don't to wait.

Pylos has become the benchmark for quality Greek cuisine in NYC. Â All aspects of the dining experience are superlative: food, decor and service. Â However, Pylos is still able to maintain an ambiance of casual elegance. Â I cannot say enough about the wonderfully prepared meals that have been served on several visits, over a year's time.

Every time I ventured around this place, there was always a long line outside. After so many attempts at eating there, it was eventually decided to order it to go, the wait was about a half hr or so. The pizza smelled sooo delicious, I couldn't wait to get home to eat it. The drive was about 20 minutes, but by the time it got home, the pizza was already cold (it was around winter time) and had to be reheated in the oven. Although the pizza was good, it could have been better. I had high expectations considering how famous Grimaldi's is and also due to the pizza's initial tantalizing scent. I suspect it's better to eat the pizza right there and then at the restaurant. I had a much better experience at Lombardi's.

This place is VERY unique! I loved the way its made. The Zen looking Backyard is very very cool looking and very pleasant to sit in. The food choices are very limited and the place is understaffed. But over all a very positive experience!

We had cold pea soup (very refreshing) and a salad of fava beans and pecorino cheese, dressed with yummy olive oil. Â For the main course, we had the lamb papardelli (hearty, meaty sauce spiked with olives) and roast duck breast with tangy rhubarb. Â The wines by the glass were really exceptional. Â We had half-glass tastes of a number of them (I don't think you can go wrong with any of their reds, though some of their whites were not great). But it was the dessert that blew my mind: I had buttermilk panna cotta with big chunks of juicy grapefruit and spicy peppercorns. Â The sweet and spicy and tangy flavors all came together blissfully. Â Consumed along with a cup of their spiced chai tea, it was a sublime experience. I can't wait to go back!
Food was good, waiters were friendly! I especially loved the brunch! Would definitely go back.
Cheap. Solid italian cuisine. Nice atmosphere without tourists.

Anyone big upping this place as the greatest banh mi in NYC is in serious need of a reality check. I recently relocated from 41st to 60th, leaving behind my beloved Ba Xuyen only to find Brooklyn's "other" banh mi spot a block away from the new digs. Â Salvation, or so I thought. After a dozen visits I can say with complete certainty that Thanh Da does not measure up. Â The bread is always dry, the nem nuong is overcooked and way too sweet, and the durian they make shakes with here is frozen even in the summertime: bland and all onion. Don't get me wrong, the fare here is passable, comparable to the stuff you can find in Manhattan. Â But after hearing for so long that this place was IT, I can't help but feel betrayed. Â Twenty blocks is a bit of a hike for a banh mi and some Horlicks, but I guess I could use the exercise.

THIS PLACE IS RIDICULOUS. YOU SHOULD SUE. You can get better chicaron at Manila Oriental or Pacific Super. What is there to "halo" in the Halo-Halo? ..its basically milk & ice! Also, the waiters/waitresses don't have any knowledge as to what filipino food really is. At lastly, the plates look like it's from chinatown which doesn't make the food any more appealing.

Zutto. You can get sushi, pork buns, and french fries all in the same meal. Just for that, I'm a fan. This is not a place to go when you're hungry and want to slam multiple sushi rolls in your face. The $9 Tribeca Roll is essentially a spicy tuna roll (with avocado and caviar in their defense) smashed into a triangle. Their special rolls also only come with 6 pieces: what?! That was a delicious and expensive disappointment. The pork buns are the bomb. Pork belly & short ribs, so good, with flavored mayos and various accompanying slaws that really compliment well. I heard from friends that the vegetarian bun (portobello) and the Kobe beef bun were worth trying too. The service was acceptable. The waiter messed up our various orders of buns (we were a big party with a yearning for massive amounts of buns), but was polite when we asked them to be returned and exchanged for the correct ones. An older guy, who I can only imagine was the manager, kept his watchful eye on the server after this error and made sure he checked himself before he wrecked himself. Zutto. Worth a stop in if you're in Tribeca. Not worth traveling for.

I love Hanco's and usually order the rice vermicelli with tofu -- it's the perfect light meal and the tofu has a nice honey sweetness to it. I'm also a fan of the tofu sandwich, everything about is so fresh and delicious. My biggest problem with Hanco's is that they consistently mess up orders! I really wish they were on seamless, it would make life so much easier.

Was there for the grand opening and had an amazing time! There were a ton of people there but it never felt to crowded. They had several specialty cocktails available that were delicious. I was also able to try a few different food items that were very good as well. The great service and fun crowd created an extremely pleasant atmosphere!

We always end up here for brunch at least twice a month. It's nearby and we can be domestic and do our shopping after, it's cheap and byob, and the have outdoor seating. Â I usually get a the croque monsieur or eggs benedict and he always gets an omelet. Â The potatoes are covered in the hollandaise sauce which is delish. Â And oj and coffee is included which is a pretty good deal. Â There is usually a wait, so bring along the NY Times are make your boy wait in line while you pop in some stores real quick

I'm baffled by this place I really am. On taste alone this would get a comfortable 4/5. Reasonably priced, large portions and free sample tastings of the sauce. Open late to soothe the post binge drinking hunger pains too. So, whats the problem?? For a place claiming to sell 'authentic Belgian fries' it is utterly laughable. I live in Lille on the French/Belgian border and have made trips to Brussels and Bruges pretty often to have their tasty fries. These taste NOTHING like authentic Pommes Frites. In fact they taste like really good chips that you'd get in a British chippy. Mis-shapen, quite thick, pretty greasy but most of all tasty. Let me paint you a picture. You like beer. you open a bar selling only Belgian beer and you call 'American beer experience'. Yey, everyone loves the beer....but wheres the connection?? If you like this place then never go to Belgium for their fries it's that simple. Rant over. If you see me in there tonight its coz they taste good ok!
Interesting decor with friendly service

What is there to say that hasn't already been said? First of all, while there are plenty of vegetarian options on the normal menu, there is also a vegetarian menu that they only give you if you ask for it. I've known many vegetarians who've been going there for ages and didn't know this. My personal favorite dish is super simple, it's the garlic and pepper seasoned pork over rice, I think it's O-7. It tastes like candy.

I have to say that I was very excited when I heard that Momofuku Ssam was opening up in my 'hood. Â I'm always on the look out for good Korean (or at the least, Korean-inspired) food. Â I was also super excited about the addition of the term ssam, umlauts and all, into the American vernacular. Â  The food? Â It's a very limited menu of either rice bowls ($13) or Asian burritos ($9), with a choice of berkshire pork/chicken/shitake mushroom. Â There's a couple of bun options as well. Â I got the shitake mushroom rice bowl w/ hoisin sauce. Â I think you need to ask for sauce, otherwise you don't get any and it's a bit bland. In that manner, they're different from Subway/Chipotle/whatever other cafeteria style restaurant you compare it to. Â The assembly process is pretty opaque. Â They don't tell you if you have the ability to customize at all and choice of sauces, etc, which defeats the purpose of preparing it in an assembly line in front of you, in my opinion. Â  That said, I really enjoyed my rice bowl. Â I did wish I could have asked for extra kimchi in mine, but it was very tasty. Â Was it $13 tasty? Â That's a tough call. Â I went to Ktown last night and for $14 all-in, I shared grilled mackerel, soft tofu stew, and dolsot bibimbop, plus all the banchan. Â Ktown is a much better deal. However, for a quick local fix... MSB may do the trick. Â One other suggestion is to get some other beer than OB!! I love the Korean loyalty, but if you can use fancy Bibb lettuce, you can get better beer!!

I know about tapas...I hit up Barcelona, Spain, on the regular tip. Â Me and the Catalan peeps kick it like no other. The interior reminds me of a house in Sevilla, Spain...totally legit decor. Â Dark, candle-lit, romantic, cozy, an upstairs area for intimate dinner dates...**PLUS you can look down a big-tittay'd chick's dress from up there**...Jus sayin Tore up some octopus, goat cheese balls, avocado salad, scallops (don't pronounce it like you're from Massachusetts), grilled eggplant...and lots of Estrella Damm (this is the preferred beer of the Spaniards). This spot is uber-dope because its not easy to find and the opening is small...but once you enter....its like the Disney World of tapas delights. I hope ya gotz a fat gangster roll like me or have Amex...otherwise, you'll be washing dishes there for a year. Â It ain't cheap.

Alright, I went back and tried it one more time. I was SO pleased!!! I took the owners advice and actually told the server that I wanted my pizza 'very crispy'. It was amazing. We started w/ the roasted pepper and burrata cheese. Very, very good! Then I went with a dryer pizza, since now I know that the neapolitan pizza is actually meant to be "auntenthically wet"... So, I opted for the Arugula. Delicious. Perfect! Will definitely come back now. Service: The staff was very accomodating to us. We had a big group which was very slowly trickling in (and I know that gets annoying if an entire party isn't there yet). So, I was shocked at their patience and amazing casualness of it all. Very Very good! Always give a second chance. -n

Had the single worst dining experience I've ever had the other night. Â When ordering our food, my girlfriend asked about red meat or fish options that were mild and ordered one of said choices. Â It turned out to be moderately spicy and she brought it to the attention of our waitress. Â The waitress breaks major NYC attitude, yells at my girlfriend "This is an Indian restaurant, It's supposed to be spicy, what were you expecting"? While the ambiance was nice and my cocktail was decent, the food was pretty standard with small portions that are heavy on the oil and a side of burnt naan. Â  Â With so many options in the area with great cocktails (The Auction House, Jbird) and solid Indian food (OM), you can't have your waitstaff behaving in this manner and expect to stay in business!
Very noisy bar & restaurant area in the front. Ask for the back room. Nice garden ambience. Wonderful wait staff. Food good. Overall pleasant dining experience.

Great atmosphere with a local feel even the wood chairs which look uncomfortable aren't. Service is good and smart as well as their knowledge of wines. Branzino delicious as was the Vongole and Fettuccine Funghi even Calamari appetizer was tasty . Pricey yes but unlike many joints this place is worthy. People love the patio I don't it can be made to be more inviting and comfortable. My Gamberoni appetizer was good not great. All in all I'll be back eventually.

I just discovered this awesome Thai spot right around the corner. Inside seems very chic and modern, so it's ideal for lunch dates. Prices are decent, especially good for this being in the city. I ordered the red curry chicken which could have had a little thicker curry though still tasted very good. Their Thai iced tea is on the sweeter side compared to others I've had but it's definitely a fix.

Tucked away on the 9th street, Cha An is a little oasis in the busy New York city. Â Straight up the fleet of stairs, behind those fabric curtains is a tea bar. Â I like their $10 daily special. Â On Mondays it's Chicken Soboro (minced chicken with fresh herbs and rice), a side dish of chicken simmered in broth, some pickles, and genmai (brown rice green) tea. Â  Black sesame pudding is as good as everyone mentioned, topped with black sesame ice-cream and a piece of honey glazed thin pastry. Â The $16 special A on the multi-grain porridge was however not so impressive. Â It did came with a delicious chestnut cream tea roll with berries though. Â  We've also attended their tea ceremony ($15/person), lasted about 30 min that includes only 2 pieces of plain mochi and a taste of Matcha. Â It was a very very brief intro on tea ceremony, and the hostess even dressed up formally for us. Â I thought it was interesting but didn't really worth $15 for that though. Â Then again, I'd love to come back again for their delicious dessert and tea!

Every famous place can't keep their quality of food, I guess... I wish I can be here when they just grand opened..so I can taste how great they were, and give them a better rate...I'm sorry I need to say their food made me very disappointed, their coffee r weak.. Nth to recommend. Plus Not comfortable at all...rush rush and rush...I only stayed here for half hr because ppl here rush and gave us a bad attitude...

This tiny place offers very good empanadas. Â Tried 6 different versions, plus a dessert, and while I don't remember each one specifically, I can say they are all very good, and I have no regrets trying the other ones the next time I go.

One of the best New York meals I've had in a long time! I've been meaning to try this spot for quite sometime and since my roommate works next door he hooked me and my family up with a reservation. To start we had the bone marrow and cheese plate. Cheese plate was wonderful but that Bone Marrow is where it's at! Some restaurants give you very little marrow but Saxon serves it with seasoning and bread crumbs with plenty of marrow to share. As an entree, I ordered the duck breast. I tend to suffer from Food Envy so I was happy to feel that I had the best Entree at the table. Other entrees at our table were the Gnudi, Porkchop and Hanger Steak. Everyone was VERY pleased. The service was perfect, the ambiance is divine and I can't wait to go back again for the lovely cocktails and MORE FOOD.

We waited around 50 minutes for brunch on a Sunday, and it was totally worth it. The blueberry pancakes with maple syrup, needless to say, was absolutely amazing. Â The pancakes were fluffy and the syrup was delicious. Â They have samples for people to try while waiting for a table. Â They were really good. Â  We also ordered the Southern Breakfast. Â It was also delicious. Â Portion is huge. Â Flavors were great. Â Whole dish was perfect. Â The cheese was not too heavy and it was a great addition. The buttermilk biscuit wasn't so good. Â I had a bite and passed up on it. Â Rather save my appetite for the pancakes and eggs ;) I really wish the wait is not as horrible so I can come here all the time! Â Would probably try to order delivery from them to see how it holds up.

5 stars no questions asked. These guys ARE different. I ended up eating here when I wasn't able to eat at 5 guys around the corner because it was after 10. Well, am I ever glad my original plan didn't work out. Got the gyro over rice. Filling and delicious and inexpensive. Perfect late night NY street food.
Hole in the wall, cash only, 3 burners in the kitchen kind of place. Country blues playing. Strong coffee, fast, good food, no frills. Classic neighborhood breakfast place.

Anella is, put simply, a special place. Someone has put a lot of thought and care into creating this experience, and it's enough to make me want to basically marry the place. Which I may look into. No matter what time you go, the menu will be small. If you like having a lot of options, this won't be a positive for you. However. The limitations allow the kitchen staff to coax the dishes they DO serve into perfection. And who doesn't love that? Dinner hour visits are rewarded with some of the best complimentary bread you'll ever have. It may have nicotine in it, and I think I'm alright with that. Â I recommend the Stoic Sage and one of the pasta dishes (so far, the octopus one is my favorite). Brunch is a transcendent experience. Coffee comes in a freaking BOWL. The French Toast rivals that of the Black Swan, and their Bloody Mary showed me the light that is tomato juice and vodka in the morning. The sandwiches are damn good, too. I've yet to go for lunch, because I have one of those jobs with normal hours. Feh. I'm sure it's glorious, just like any other meal they serve. But I will tell you this: go to Anella. Seriously. You'll be doing yourself a big favor.
Good stuff. It's a safe place to take just about anyone. The decor works better when the place is packed, so for aesthetics sake, go!

I'm sorry, I love Popeye's and all, much more than I should in fact, but what's with all the reviews here saying their chicken is the "best"? Am I missing some kind of small-scale meme or are you people legitimately insane? Popeye's isn't the "best" anything, unless we're talking about "best" purely in terms of the category of weirdest, grossest place I've ever seen an Internet cafe installed into. (Yum yum, nothing like eating a bucket of coronary then checking IMDB on a public keyboard covered in the crumbs and grease of ten thousand fat strangers in an establishment that actively encourages finger-licking! Where do I insert my dollar for ten minutes?) I mean, Pies 'n' Thighs isn't perfect, neither, but comparing it to Popeye's in any way/shape/form is ludicrous. In fact, let's get my biggest complaints about this place out of the way: I hate Williamsburg, I hate hipsters, and chances are, I probably hate you. I hate how ridiculous it is getting to/from here unless you already live here or near the JMZ, which as far as I'm concerned, may as well go to fucking Narnia. I also hate how inadequately air-conditioned it was in here, though I'm not totally sure that's a hipster thing, but it sure seems like it is: "Eeeeeuuugh, look at me, I don't need comfortable, artificially conditioned air, not when I have my MUSIC" Okay, I just wanted to get all my unreasonable/tangential complaints out of the way, and clarify that I am not deducting a star for any of them. Although I really want to. So anyway, yeah, fried chicken! Here, it is delicious. I mean really really good. I had to think about it a while, but in the end, I put just slightly under the chicken I've had at Brooklyn Bowl (which has the edge in juiciness, and is the best I've ever had). Rest assured though, the chicken here is wonderfully seasoned and fried, and yes, kicks the ever-loving shit out of Popeye's. This is one of those meals that immediately makes everyone you're eating with totally stupid and silent, partly from sheer paralytic unhealthiness and partly because you're all so amazed/grateful at all the wonderful things going on in your mouth that it requires your full attention. Unfortunately, at least in comparison to the chicken, the sides didn't quite hold up their end of the bargain. My mac 'n' cheese was lukewarm, bordering on cold, a cardinal sin that disqualifies it from consideration. And the biscuits, similarly, were just okay.
