I like my biscuits soft and a bit warm, and these were not, though serving it with honey butter helps. The fries, for their part, were certainly fries. As for the "Pies" part , the apple pie we had (which had a generous dollop of whipped cream on the side, and, interestingly, a thick slice of cheddar underneath), was pretty tasty, though not quite occupying the same space on the "worth going out of your way for" scale as the chicken. It is safe to say that I probably would've appreciated it even more had my stomach not already been exploding with chicken grease, however. All in all, though, a pretty great meal that I will almost assuredly never have again unless someone literally kidnaps me and takes me there. That's right, screw you, your bowties, your male short-shorts, AND your tasty, tasty fried chicken, entire subsection of Brooklyn!
Amazing eggs Benedict! probably the best brunch place I've been to in east coast. Nuf said.

This restaurant's Kangkung belachan is the best! Â  I've tried the ones at Pinang & a few other Malaysian restaurants & they are nothing compared to Taste Good restaurant's. Â Their version is not soggy and soupy. Â The belachan sauce is rich and flavorful. Â  I would rather do a take out than to dine in, because the dining area is small. Â I get a bit cranky and claustrophobic in very confined areas. Â I'd appreciate it if they would expand the place or perhaps, move to a bigger location somewhere nearby.

I'm not sure if I'm just really good at picking times to come to Grimaldi's, but I've never had to wait more than 15-20 min for a table, and it's always been worth it. Â One of my favorite places to meet up with my Brooklyn friends to catch up over a couple of pies.

Great place. Had brunch there recently and had a really good time. Seated promptly at our reservation time, had a great server and all around good atmosphere. Didn't love my salad but would definitely come back and try something else. Definitely recommend making reservations for brunch- it gets jam packed!
great vibe great spicy noodles with shrimp crazy good mohitos.... thumbs up very busy -good thing my cuz knew the host...

I gave this place 3 stars only because I didn't taste anything mind crazy good. It was good, but nothing that blew my mind. F cancelled on V and I again, so we decided to save Korean BBQ for another day. I picked Ngam, only because it was new and I just saw something online raving about their chicken wings. Andrew was our waiter - cute and sassy. I was a bit apprehensive on ordering a cocktail here - all of their cocktails are soju based. As memory serves me - I don't do well with soju, but Andrew insisted that the soju were fine. I got the Below the Root - it was ginger flavour, but I didn't taste that much ginger. Perhaps because I expected my drink to be overly gingerly, since Andrew advised this cocktail was for extreme ginger lovers. V got the Mojito one - I liked V's better. We shared the following items: Crabcake - it was the special for the day and it was really good, but I felt it could have used a bit more acidic. Raw Oysters - Yums! Chicken Wings - ummm, underwhelmed. There shouldn't have been an article written about these chicken wings. It was just okay, nothing spectacular. It was moist, but just not seasoned well enough. Mushroom Spring rolls - these were good. Love the light flaky shell. Mussels on the Beach - really yummy coconut milk based curry. We ordered too much for two people and we were stuffed to the core. I would come back if I was in the hood, but not trek all the way up here with V with V's bike in hand and I would skip out on the chicken wings.

I dunno.... $150 for four people to eat and have a drink.. which doesn't include the $50++ we spent on raw food waiting for our table at the bar.. and I don't feel 'full'. Â This meal definitely wasn't worth the money. Â  The food was ok... kinda good at moments, but not really outstanding. Â  It weirded me out that our server kept saying how much she coveted dishes and wished she could try them. Â YO... feed your servers your food so they know what the heck they are talking about. Â Our waitress went on and on about how everything looked... but she hadn't tried anything yet. Â Don't these people get a staff meal? Â She also asked if everything was ok like six times... whatever, let us eat. Â  We were smart enough to go on a rainy night, so the wait wasn't too bad, nothing like what the others are describing. Â  The ambiance is awesome, you're eating on a roof top on the water, statue of liberty in the distance... come on... super cool. Â  Aesthetically, it's pretty spot on, rustic fish shack feel. Â But... the prices? Â Holy mother of EXPENSIVE! Â and the portions.. meh... if you're gonna charge $25++ for fish.. it should be a piece much larger than what my poor friend ordered. Â I got a 1.5 lb lobster that ... didn't quite seem 1.5 lbs to me. Â The deal of the night was the Snow Crabs... clearly that's where you get some bang for your buck. Maybe because they are labor intensive but it took my friend who ordered them a little more time to eat. I'm ok with paying extra for sides, and frankly, the ones we got were pretty delish. Â  So...Raw Oysters.. really small! and I got the special ones that were supposed to be 'bigger' from Canada. The green condiment that came with them was yummy. Lobster, grilled, fine, priced ok for a 1.5 lb lobster... Fish special, really small portion Scallops were just ok (which the waitress raved that she wished she could try them because every time she takes them out of the kitchen they look so good, FYI... grooooooosss kale that came with it made all of us wince yuck), also a small portion Snow crabs... deal of the night. Potatoes Gratin, yum, Snow peas special, yum, mac and cheese, alright. Drinks $10 for a drink made with well-vodka? yikes. Â  The whole chaos at the 'waiting area' bar was wack. Â Cash only? Â Guys yelling out my name to find me to give me food? Â I can see where this really sucks when the place gets far busier. Â  When my friend asked for water, the waitress explained that it was self-serve, and we had to get up and get our water ourselves. Â SERIOUSLY? Â For what we were paying for our meal, we needed to get up and get our own water? Â COME ON. I know they are new... but they are run by a local restauranteur with 10 years under his belt. Â  It's really ... a theme restaurant folks. Â Of course there should be a seafood funky joint in Red Hook, that makes total sense.... but the prices? for that? Â meh, I'd say they are pulling a Times Square themed restaurant scam on NYCers looking for a cool dining experience. Â  The food was ok... rave that it was amazing? Â Nah, can't go there. Â Why 3 stars... the ambiance, vibe and decor and aesthetic festiveness of the joint made it fun... although the pain I"m feeling in my wallet is gonna suck for a while. Â  Next time I'm in Red Hook and I have $75 to throw at a meal.. I'm heading to the Good Fork or Fort Defiance or Home/Made... and I'll have some spare change for a few drinks after.

Excellent price for delicious sandwiches, everything is so fresh! Â My first time here was last week, and its so close to work, I will def come again to try out so much more of their varied menu. This time i had the french cheese sandwich and it was a great treat. I am sure I need to come here more often to try out the rest of the menu, and I Will repair my review depending on that :)

So, I came here during my last New York visit, and while I wasn't impressed with the service I kinda expected it. Allow me to re-count the tale. Imagine: you go to Times Square (which is only appealing to tourists because of the the bright lights. Hm...maybe, when you become a tourist you become like a confused animal; attracted to bright lights?) In any case, after being horribly disappointed to find that Spamalot didn't have a Sunday evening show, my friend and I wandered for a bit. We got hungry, apparently, right around their closing time. Which is why they hesitatingly sat us and our server wasn't the happiest man on Earth, and I wouldn't be either. The prices are expected for Times Square. I mean, honestly, my fellow Yelpers, Times Square is expensive; some one has to pay for those bright lights and the fact there's a Ruby Tuesday there. With that said, the food wasn't stellar, but you do get a ton of it. As for the cheesecake; I've had better, but not in New York. Here's my advice: go well before their closing hours having already eaten dinner somewhere else. (There's a ton of places to eat in New York). And, finally, go with some one else and just order the cheesecake. Trust me, one order is enough to split between two people. (As for finding an alternative dinner restaurant in New York; if you can't think of one, send me or another fellow Yelper a message. I know, anyone on this site would be more than willing to share eateries.)

I've frequented this place often with friends and bring my sister over here when she's in town. Last time I was in I sat at the bar with a friend and noticed the record they were playing was the instrumental to Nas' Illmatic. Can't hate a place that represents.

mehhhh The portions are small.. I live right next to moo burger and they offer a better portion for almost the same price. The burger was good though.. no complaints about that... I don't know if I will be making the trip to two 8 two anytime soon...

This place has some extremely good Italian food! Â First of all, I was surprised that they even sat me on time, (7:00 reservation) seeing how busy the place was. Â Once I sat down, the waiter explained to my party and me the "family-style" dining this place offers, which is similar to that of Joey and Eddie's in San Francisco. Â We decided to go with calamari to start, Spaghetti and Meatballs, and Chicken Parmesan. Â The appetizer and both entrees were fantastic, and we devoured every bit of the food. Â For dessert, we ordered tiramisu, which was also great. Â I will surely be going back here when I return to NYC! Mama mia, that's Italian!

So good! I recommend you go with a lot of people who are open to sharing - that way, you can try a bunch of things at once. It won't be very cheap, but it will definitely be worth it. The host was kind of a jerk the last time we went, but we stayed anyway because the food is so good, if that's any sign of quality.
Very cute. Campari, Cocque au Vin (very tender), Caprese, Pesto Nociola (delicious and unique). Small portions.

I've had much better street meat at three other carts and a truck. Â I don't get the hype. Â  Seeing a food cart with 4k+ reviews and 4.5 stars - last night, when cold after seeing an awesome concert, I had to give Halal Guys a try. Â No line, quick and easy to get the food. Eating at home though, you can barely tell it's meat. Â No texture, it's chopped up crap. Â Tastes maybe half a level higher than Taco Bell. Â  And the hot sauce. Â Sorry, no. Â Just too frikkin hot. Â Brutal. Â No reason to be that hot, no reason to soak into your skin like that and then when tired try to take out your contact and feel pain for an hour while trying to sleep. Â That all is my fault, but still. Â No. Uncle Gussy's food truck is about 15x better, same price, and at the corner of 51st and Park. Â I'm heading there today to get the taste of Halal Guys out of my mouth.
Believe the hype. This is the best. Great service, delicious pizza, and cant get more authentic nyc pizza than this!

This place continues to blow my mind. My boyfriend and I moved to the neighborhood in October, and first happened upon this after passing their storefront and seeing a sign for happy hour oysters and $2 tacos. I live for oysters and also work at an oyster restaurant, so I had to check it out. Patio was wonderful, the place was surprisingly near empty. I guess on weekdays in Park Slope happy hour is a bit barren most places. The place had a wildly delicious looking menu, so we decided to come here for my birthday at the end of October. The place was very quiet, but the staff was wonderfully attentive and accommodating. This is when we met Ermira. She is unbelievably sweet, knowledgeable, and all around a great server. And this is coming from someone who's served for around ten years. She heard it was my birthday, and we got a complimentary amuse, and a dessert with port! Such a treat. We left high on food and great vibes. We came back for brunch with my family from Jersey, and while she wasn't there, the service was great. We made sure to make reservations a week in advance, since there were seven of us for Saturday brunch. GREAT brunch food. But really, nothing compares to their service and food at dinner time. We THEN had to come back for my boyfriend's birthday, and she remembered us! Again, there were few tables in the place, and we sat in our same spot. Same treatment as last time, she hooked us UP. This is why I always say, treat your servers very well, and they will return the favor. It's not that hard of a concept to understand, but so few in this city get it. Just last week we came again because my sister and her fiance were in town. She remembered our names, was her super cheerful, effervescent self, and my family loved her. THEN, with all of us just having happy hour oysters, tacos, and a couple appetizers with a couple drinks, she STILL hooks us up with an amuse and a dessert. Â I have never left this place feeling anything less than elated. Ermira is amazing. The food is SENSATIONAL, and easily one of our favorite restaurants in the city right now, but I find myself thinking; if not for her infectious attitude and amazing service, would I still think this is one of the best spots? Who knows, but I will not stop coming here for as long as she works here. :]

I love the fact that such a place exists to get such good food late at night in NYC. Great for layovers. The sauce and tender vegetables that come with the escargot were amazing. The Shrimp Provencal was delicious. I loved the tender ravioli. The chocolate Bruno flourless chocolate cake was very good. Can't wait to return.

The first time I went here was on a Friday night, needless to say it was packed and I had no reservation. The hostess was really sweet and offered us the bar after a few people were seated at their table. We were a party of 2 looking for a great bottle of wine and a few apps, so the bar was perfect. They have a nice wine list and the food is great! always interesting specials and if you're splitting apps, they split them for you! We had a lamb pappardelle and scallops, they split them so we both had our own plate. Oh yes also try the oysters if they have them, they usually have a great mignonette with them! I like the atmosphere here; big windows, dim lighting, lots of movement and typical restaurant noise. Staff was very nice and accommodating. I'll definitely make it a Â regular spot until they give me a reason otherwise.

We came here by chance as the bar down the street was crowded. I'm glad we did. We are started with their special orange gin cocktails which were refreshing and smooth. It needed slightly more oomph, maybe mint or a hint of ginger to waken it up. We shared an order of broccoli rabe with anchovies, Parmesan cheese and boiled egg. OMG. This was the bomb. So tasty! We were told it was essentially broccoli rabe with Caesar salad dressing. I could eat a big bowl film of this stuff! Patatas bravas with mayo and sriracha were also good but definitely less memorable. A really nice spot with lovely staff and excellent service. It's a little on the pricey side but worth it!

The Meatball Shop puts my Italian mother's meatballs to shame. Â The first thing was ordering. Â The laminated menus are filled out by the customers with erasable markers. Â No room for error there-great idea. Â The restaurant is decorated with black and white old photos and we sat at a long table with other patrons on ether side of. Â A little tight but when our balls came, that didn't matter. Â I ordered the special which was Buffalo chicken meatballs in a bleu cheese and hot sauce topping. Â As a chicken freak and a lover of all things hot and spicy, I practically licked the bowl. Â I can't wait to go back. Â I love balls!!! Â Also, on the weekends, they have a bar in the basement called "under balls" where you can either wait for a table or just hang out.

I would just stick to the ramen and avoid any of the appetizers. Â I had the gyoza starter which was mediocre, it needed to cooked on a grill and not within a pan in order to get more of a char on the gyoza. Â Anyway the pork based soy sauce flavor broth ramen was good; the noodles were great and full of flavor, the pork was amazing (they use high grade pork belly) but the broth was a bit lacking. Â Overall some of the best ramen in New York.

I trusted the reviews and was not disappointed. The bartender whipped up amazing cocktails and was charming on top of that. My roommate and I went for 4 dishes all unbelievable. I appreciated the kindness of the waitstaff and the cooks cooking right behind the bar. I could of sat and indulged all night.
Mmmmm fries, with special sauces, enough said! Â Minus one star for lack of seating, especially when it's cold out.

**Only ordered sushi and sashimi** Definitely not Yasuda, but at $3 per piece, i'm not gonna complain. The sashimi serving was very generous (2 thick pieces) and surprisingly fresh for being 8pm on a Sunday. I'm still in search of the best price:freshness joint out there, but until then Zest will do. Did i mention they deliver? Uni to my door in 15 mins... winter will be busy for them. muahahhaha.

Amazing amazing amazing!!!! That's why there's always a loooooong wait. I looooooove me some good meatballs! Spicy pork with the mushroom gravy is the absolute best, the gravy is so thick it coats your tongue and the flavor lingers just enough that there's a hint of mushroom and gravy when the spicyness of the pork kicks in, about 30 seconds after you've started chomping away at the meatball. I love that at first bite the spicy pork meatball just tastes like a pork meatball and the kick settles in after a couple chews.

Had their chicken katsu curry with a side of fukuzinzuke (red pickles). It was pretty tasty, but talk about being stingy with the curry sauce! I've never had such a thin layer of curry sauce. Thankfully it was salty (and delicious) for the amount of rice they gave, but still..I like my rice Â COVERED in curry. I also didn't like how I had to pay $1 for a side of fukuzinzuke when I'm used to getting it for free in Japan and Hawaii. Yes, I'm spoiled. Apparently you can get a free side if you go on the 5th, 15th, or 25th of each month. I'll be sure to check it out again on one of those days.

One of my favorite memories of a recent New York trip was Â gobbling down the pork belly asian pear sandwich as pork belly fat dripped down my forearms. Thank goodness I carry around handiwipes in my purse. The lemonade was freakishly sour and not refreshing. The ginger apple cider was amaaaaazing - hot sweet and perfect, with 5-6 one-inch cubes of apple floating in it. a post-drink treat to eat.

The Charred Octopus is a good! The first time I had it, it was made perfectly. The 2nd time I had it, the texture/flavor/crunch was somewhat off. (From the first experience) On the initial bite, the octopus was perfectly crispy with a pinch of salty taste. As you bite into it, it becomes so soft and tender that it melts in your mouth. I had the Wild Skate fish, and it is more on the sour side. It was delicious and the potato foam was a great complement. Had the chocolate mousse and ended dinner there. Portions are small. Service was great!!! The waitress did not mind at all taking her time to answer all our curious questions about the food.

I came here after fellow Yelpers raved about the corn and fellow Yelpers were right. Grilled corn with the mayonnaise and chile powder and lime and cheese was nothing short of stupendous. The corn was so superior to the cactus tacos I had corn will be all I will order here. $4.25 gets you two huge ears. Trust me--you will say it is too much and then eat both and want more. The cactus tacos came two to a plate on freshly fried tortillas. The cactus was crunchy and tossed with onions but did not have any great punch. The small side of beans and rice was flavorful. This place is packed at the night so get here early lif you don't want a 30 minute wait for corn. Table space is tight so do the counter in a pinch. Oh a nice young man I chatted with told me the corn here is far better than the one at Habana Outpost on Brooklyn. CORN GETS 5 STARS!

Very cute, large restaurant hidden away down a few steps from the street. We got to sit on the second floor by the window, so got a great view of lovely West 10th St. It involved walking through the kitchen too, so got to sneak a peek into there. So many wonderful tapas choices that I think I could come back time and again (a little on the pricey side, so that's what will rein me in...). My biggest impression was just that I felt... surprised by each dish. There was just something about the ingredients or the way that they prepared every dish that was creative and pleasantly unexpected from what I had imagined. Also, fair warning: really strong sangria!

This was my first time ever having Thai curry, so I don't have anything to compare it to. That being said, I thought it was excellent! I had the green curry with brown rice, and the portion was just right Â (but I was hungry at the time and would have eaten anything...) The curry was creamy and spicy, but not too spicy. I got a little overwhelmed by the coconut at the end, but overall delicious! The atmosphere is also very romantic, it would be perfect for date night or a girl's night out.

Easily found a late-night table for two at The Smith this past Wednesday evening. Even at the hour, there was a lively crowd and a pleasant buzz in the restaurant, making if feel as if the night were still young for my date and I. Being an after-dinner sit down, we only selected from the bar menu - the quality of what found though would be enough to drive me to a full entree order though, had I the appetite. DEFINITELY order the beer battered green beans. They were heavenly. With a very light batter and a generous amount of salt, they tasted as good as they could on their own. The serving comes with a side of ranch dip, but unless you are a fiend for the dressing, leave it alone. My fascination with the beans was backed up in it's clarity when the waiter told me that the beans were the staff favorite too, and that they'd often take a plate at a time between the crew - everyone taking handfuls as they came in and out of the back. Did that bother me? Not at all. I understood the appeal.

A friend and I went here for some great wine and cheese. You walk in to a great decor and ambiance. We ordered a bottle of wine and 6 cheeses, that the staff chose for us according to our wine pick. The staff was courteous and knowledgeable. We will definitely go back and try out the other small plates.

Amazing chicken sandwich, chicken biscuit also so good. Â Staff was really friendly and helpful. Place is pretty small and beautiful. chicken was definitely the best and most creative and it was looking great. Fried chicken was spot on... flavorful, crispy and aromatic.

This review is a little late, so I don't remember all the details of what we ate, but I remember leaving this restaurant very happy. The decor and ambiance were wonderful, our waitress was extremely friendly and knowledgeable and our food and drinks were delicious! I do remember the portions being a little small and the prices a little high in comparison, but overall, it was a great night at this restaurant.
We got the tapas in order to sample more. We especially loved the fig tapas and grilled octopus tapas. Drank yummy moscato. Eat here.

4.5 Yay! Â While walking in Soho, discovered another Cocoron opened up. Â I loved their stamina dip at the other location. Â Here I tried the Mera (think it is called Mera Mera)..cold soba noodles with hot broth.. It was pretty delicious. Â Unfortunately my bf's choice he didn't think was nearly as good/flavorful (not sure which one, but it had chicken meatballs). Great service. Â Nice space. Â  $12 each for a large. Â  Portion I felt was quite small. Â But then again aside from the fact we both like to eat too much and we walked to/from Brooklyn that day, maybe the portions are just fine for most normal people. Â  Â  Definitely worth a return visit!
I currently hold the world record (unofficial) for putting down a slice of cheesecake here. CRUSHED IT.
Every bite was delish! highly recommended!

Tried a few things of the menu and the only thing I fell in love w/ was the cuban arepa. It was uber delicious! Also had the pernil empanada which although was overly stuffed with pernil, was yummy! The other items I tried like the empanada wih feta and spinach and broccoli and cheese were just ok. It's a whole in the wall type of place, w/ small tables right next to each other but the prices are not bad.

Good food at good prices. Â I had the chicken and waffles, while good I don't think it lived up to all the hype. The Arnold Palmer (not sure what they called it... half lemonade/sweet tea) was good and I definitely recommend but I was a little disappointed that I didn't get to try the red velvet cake (ran out/didn't have any that day) overall a good kinda hole in the wall spot

Not having had authentic Chinese food in quite a while, my girlfriend and I opted to venture down here for dinner on a Monday night. We'd just come out of seeing Jiro Dreams of Sushi, but it was a tad bit chilly, so why not some good and warming soup? Having said that, neither of us ended up having soup. Arriving around 8pm, there was no wait and we were immediately seated. My gf had the Soy Sauce Noodles and I had the combo platter of Roast Pork, Roast Duck and Barbecued Pig. We also shared the Chinese Vegetables in Oyster Sauce. All dishes were really yummy and the portions were generous. The highlight were the Soy Sauce Noodles. You could really taste the fire of the wok in the noodles. The roast meats were succulent and juicy, and the vegetables were fresh, crisp and complemented nicely by the oyster sauce. While the seating here is rather tight, the prices are also extremely reasonable... probably ridiculously reasonable. The first time I look at the menu, I was convinced that I needed to have my eyes examined. My combo platter, which was also served on a huge bed of rice, was only $6.75. Our total bill, with tip, came to $21. As for the service, it's always quick and polite. If you're in Chinatown and looking for good, quick and cheap eats, look no further. I look forward to returning and trying some of their soups. Just bear in mind that the four stars doesn't warrant gourmet food. For yummy, quick and cheap Chinese food, this place warrants four stars.

Mexican sucks in New York. It's a cliche for a reason. Â Dos Toros aims for the OMG SF crowd, a crowd that quite conveniently passes through Union Square with some frequency. The convenience of this place can't really be underrated. It's a few steps from Union Square on the way toward everywhere cool further downtown. So that gets points. The real question here isn't whether this place is as good as your favorite mythical burrito shop in San Francisco. Â That comparison is pointless in this context. Going to California every time I desire a burrito is not an option. It's more useful to consider Value Over Replacement Burrito (VORB). In this case, the Replacement Burrito, the baseline, fungible, standard burrito Â is, of course, Chipolte. Â  So, my verdict is that Dos Toros is marginally better than Chipolte. Â The meat is superior, I prefer the rice, and there are more options. Also inconsideration is the not insubstantial psychic benefit of supporting a local business. I don't think this place is quite as good as NYT would have you believe, but I would still stop by here again if hungry for something quick and filling in the Union Square area.

I live on 7th street and love this little place. It is a great addition to my neighborhood, a place i have lived for over thirty years! Not only are their little plates delicious and surprising but the staff is friendly and attentive. It is clean with a lovely decor and it is not expensive! A gold star in my book.

I really dig their lobster. Cheaper than you can imagine, and just as good as they could ever be. Yet, the atmosphere and service is almost beyond dislike...LOL. Same as other restaurants, they prefer pay by cash.

Had reservations here on a Saturday at 5:30pm. I would've preferred having dinner a little later around 7pm but it was probably my fault for making reservations so last minute. But anyway, as for the food, everything was soooo goooood. I ordered the spicy duck meatballs for my appetizer and my friend got the ceviche of bay scallops, I'm not a big fan of seafood (let alone anything raw) but I tried the scallops and they weren't bad at all! For our entrees, I ordered the Grilled Prime Creekstone Hanger Steak.. medium well- sooo yumms. My friend got the Crisphy Hampshire Pork Belly which was great too. And lastly, for dessert I got the toasted almost ricotta cake which was okay.. and my friend got the take five sundae which was good. oh and their ginger ale tastes real fresh and different which was cool. Overall, a great experience and worth the $$$$ :)
Pretty good traditional sandwich! I thought the amount of carrot mix was just right and there was good medium spice. I'd order it again!
Totally recommended! Yummy, not expensive, great staff, and totally satisfying!! You will enjoy their food at any time of day!

This is a solid addition to the Brooklyn Heights culinary scene and something which fills a really needed vacancy. Aside from Henry's End and Noodle Pudding, Brooklyn Heights lacks a solid representation of neighborhood restaurants where the food is good and the experience great. The food at Jack the Horse is really solid American fare, with a great burger that is always a go-to, a very delicious, smoky macaroni and cheese, and some great salads that change from week to week. Nothing on the menu stands out as unique or amazing, but the restaurant seems happy to stand by the classics and just have a solid all-around menu. Despite the great comfort of their food, the service is somewhat less than impressive. They are very welcoming at the door and seem to be trying their best, but certain things fall through at the table that are somewhat inexcusable. Several times, they have forgotten drinks that were ordered, and they also are very inattentive in terms of replenishing bread and water. Despite these faults, Jack the Horse is a solid neighborhood standby that the Heights can seriously benefit from.

Now these guys know how to cook the classic thin crust pizza. I am not a big pizza guy but you know when you eat a great slice of pizza. The pizza's are cooked in charcoal oven which add to the taste. The place is pretty cheap but don't forget to get cash these guys don't accept card. The place is not too big for the no of people who turn up everyday. Its just filled up with chairs and table everywhere. The thing that i hate about the place for which is deducted the 1 start is the huge line they attract everyday. You usually have to wait for 30 mins to get in . But its worth the wait. I would suggest to get some ice-cream from the Brooklyn ice cream factory which is just meters away from this place and the Manhattan view from this area is amazing ..another reason to visit this place.

What can I say? From the discrete rear entrance to the killer Manhattans, 4 cherries, put together by the friendly bartender, it was easy to overlook the snippiness of the maitre'd who wanted to put us at a 2 person table when one of our foursome dropped out. Salads were Divine, crispy duck was perfect and olive oil cake was simply delish. Good wine list too. Great funky little find for a light summer dinner.
I had lunch here. Â It was awesome! Â Eggplant and zucchini on flat bread with some kind of spread and veggie mix, with a bottle of water. Â $8.00 Wow!

INFESTED WITH ROACHES We had little roaches crawling on our table. Â  I wasn't expecting a lot from this place and for what it's worth the food was actually pretty good. Â Unfortunately, they had no beef dishes at all available when we went. Â Apparently they ran out? Â They brought our food out completely in the wrong order, but that wasn't a huge deal. Â It was the fact that we had roaches on our table. Â Mid-dinner and all of a sudden we had them crawling on our table. Â I killed the roach we saw first and handed the napkin to our waiter and he just acted like nothing happened. Â When I started fussing he took the napkin to the manager. Â The manager asked if he could offer us drinks or dessert...why would we want any more food from your kitchen when you have a roach problem? Â Then he offered to give us a voucher for our next visit. Â AGAIN WHY WOULD I COME HERE AGAIN WHEN I KNOW YOU HAVE A ROACH PROBLEM? Â Then he offered a discount...of 10%. Â Our tab was 43.50. Tax was 3.98. Â 10% of our 4.35. Â So he saved us 37 cents??? After he threw away over half of our food and we had a roach on our table? Â He finally gave us a 50% discount but truly the tab should have been on the house. Â I've never been anywhere in my life where a roach crawled on the table! Â So filthy.

I was craving a salami sandwich for whatever reason and La Panineria fit the bill perfectly. It's a tiny place with one table and a couple of stools; great if you want a quick and quiet lunch or dinner. I got the DiamantÃ© panini, which had spicy salami and provolone cheese on a baguette. I added their fig mustard which was outstanding and gave some extra kick. At $10 for a sandwich and drink, it's a little pricey for such a simple sandwich that doesn't load on the toppings but the guys here clearly care about their craft and the quality shows in the ingredients so I'd gladly get my salami fix here again.

So the eight of us had the bo ssam at 5:00 p.m. on Saturday. Â My expectations were muted due to the mixed reviews from fellow yelpers and elsewhere. Â Boy, was I pleasantly surprised. Â Let me just say that this early dinner was a most unique ssam experience. Â And this is coming from an experienced meat and ssam eater. Yes, the oysters were fresh and good. Â The pork butt (shoulder) was fatty and juicy. Â But two items really made the dining experience over the top: Â 1) the boston lettuce (rather than the typical redleaf) and 2) the oyster-kimchee puree (used in conjunction with or in place of the ssam jang). Â These two items really made the dining experience unforgettable. The noise and the ambiance, however, have much left to be desired. Â The ambient music was being played too loud. Â Coupled with the background noice generated from the massive crowd, you feel like you are dining at a nightclub. Â It was difficult to converse (conversate- current day usage?) with anyone without having to quasi-yell. Â And the short bar stools serving as dining chairs- what's up with that. The food makes up for it, however. Â Mind you, this place is not cheap.

Despite having to wait almost 40 minutes for a table (even with reservations and at 2pm), my friends and I enjoyed the food. I ordered the Mexican brunch dish, which was good but not as good as the eggs benedict my friends ordered. (Doh! Should have gone with my first instinct!) The fresh pressed grapefruit juice was also a winner. If you don't mind waiting awhile for brunch, then it's worth checking out.

This is a great place to grab cheap food quickly, especially on a college budget! The place recently renovated and it looks A LOT better than it did before. They carry snacks and have a lot of drinks as well (including alcohol). It can get really crowded on weekend nights and they open late. You can grab food from the buffet or grab the cooked meals on the shelves. The food isn't amazing, but hey it's cheap! I come here often when I'm in NYC and recommend it if you're on a budget!

Usually the first stop on our cheap LES dates. Dumplings and scallion pancakes here, followed by drinks at Local 138 and then sharing an ice cream sandwich from Melt. What can I say that hasn't already been said? Nothing, cheap delicious dumplings. Sometimes we buy the big bag of frozen dumplings and make them at home but it's not the same.

Dumprings! I love me some dumprings! After a 20min wait, we sat down and ordered the pork dumplings, green onion pancake, green beans, and drunken chicken. These XLB's are some of the juiciest I've ever had, but the skin could've been thinner. They tasted so meaty, I almost thought they were beef for a minute. 8 large dumprings for $4.95 vs. 10 small dumprings for $10.95 at Din Tai Fung. Just a completely different dining experience. Joe's is grungy, bustling, and they churn out some delightful soupy morsels.

Knockout Ramen, great environment. The secret to a table (if you live or work in the neighborhood): drop by in the late morning or at lunch and request a table for that evening, enabling you to avoid a 2-hr wait.

I sat at the corner of the wide bar with a friend. I had the daily fixed price three course lunch. It was delicious and very well presented and good value. The food is sophisticated without being pretentious. The portions aren't large but I find that most New York restaurants give you far too much food. My friend chose off the a la carte menu which is significantly more expensive. The restaurant is well decorated; large and airy. The barman doubled up as our watier and was very helpful and solicitous. I will definitely come again.

It's good, but is it worth 2000+ reviews 4 stars good? Maybe not. I'd give it 3.5 stars. The portions are big, but for fries it's not really that cheap. The flavors they have for dipping sauces are pretty interesting. I'd definitely introduce people to it, but if there's a line out the door I might as well skip it.

I didn't actually have any catfish there but the shrimp cocktail was well seasoned and delicious. The drinks were good, I can't remember the name of my drink but it came in a champagne flute and had london dry gin in it I believe. My point is this place is a great addition to the neighborhood, great drinks, good food, and the ambiance is nice. I'd definitely return and should I don't doubt that the catfish will be exemplary and I'll up the review to 5 stars.

insanley good!!! I have tried to the Brisket - amazingly soft the ribs - sooo tasty and also soft the burnt end beans - i could eat this everyday until i die edemame pea salad - soooo good, i was so full i took it home and ate it the next day If you like meat that has been prepared and cooked by people who know what theyre doing then go here! such reasonable prices and really good quality food too. the flavours of everything are perfect. The staff are also excellent and helpful and they have a great selection of beers on tap! It can get a bit busy with lines out the door but it moves pretty quick :)
Surprise and amazement from entering the door to finishing the meal!!!!
Crowded and not the best service at all. But all and all it's a nice experience with truly original Italian flavors, plus the mix with little shops and the market makes it something unique.
Best decision I've ever made. Sandwiches good. Customer service awesome. Only thing not going for them is space but that can be upgraded later. Din is AMAZING!

Good ramen, but lordy are the staff rude. I understand it's a popular spot and that they're busy, but it's pretty frustrating that ever single time I've tried to get a table there, I've been spoken to like I'm an idiot for even trying or an annoyance for being there. Go to Zuzu instead.

I am, humbly might I add, what some call a taste maker. as a nationally recognized style expert on E! / VH-1 amongst others, people look to what I say as the newest thing, since I seem to have a knack for knowing the newest thing. this past month was my birthday and as I usually like to do, I put together a fun lil' cocktail party. my good friend (also a taste maker) paul sado invited me to throw the get-together at the bar he was DJing at in tribeca. enter WARD III. Â it is a sexy space. dark, simple but still full of class and style. the bartenders are extremely welcoming, accommodating (and hot) and while they own the joint, they still get their hands dirty behind the bar, mixing up stiff drinks and creative concoctions. there were a ton of fun people in the mix making for a great vibe and crowd. not too busy that it was bothersome just perfectly filled for a good time. sado spun hot tunes that had us dancing past closing. this has become my new fave spot. wanna make it yours?
Great when I feel like eating take out. Even better when I'm broke and still want something delicious. Â Might actually like this one better than the one in sunset park

This place is sexy. Â Not ultra-modern, pretentious, W lounge sexy. I'm talking exposed-brick, vintage-chandeliers, deep-cherry-wood, wine-cellar sexy. I have yet to eat or drink something that didn't make me swoon. A thoughtful wine list and some of the most amazing small plates I've ever had. Procsuitto mac and cheese, tuna and salmon tartare, margherita pizza. All perfect. My favorite part, beyond the food and wine, is how inviting the service is. We were as warmly welcomed when we stopped by just to feed our mac and cheese craving as we were when we ordered dinner and bottles of wine.
Many D8s, Less light, YUm oyster, beautiful survice.

Hadn't been here in years, since the pre-kids days, but it's one of the more kid-friendly places on the UWS so we went back one Friday night. The food has maintained its high quality level. The octopus and cod appetizers were particularly good. And it's good for kids for two reasons -- (1) the sound level is high enough that you won't be mortified if your kid screeches or something, and (2) the "small plates" at Greek places are mostly never made to order, so you don't have to sit around entertaining them while their dishes are prepared. (We were seated downstairs, away from the more date-friendly upstairs area, but it's perfectly nice down their and doesn't feel like a "family ghetto".)

The service depends on who's working, but the food never disappoints. Best Key Lime pie when it's in season and burgers better than any you can get anywhere else. Really also recommend the spinach dip. Love the live Jazz music too. A great after work or date place.

Hand down the best xiao long bao I've never had. I'm willing to wait in line for this place. But it's super small and the tables are crammed against each other. The meat inside is decent sized. The dough isn't too thick to chew and not too thin where it'll pop when you pick it up.

Great atmosphere and food.The market lettuce salad is the best salad I've had in awhile. I'm a vegetarian and they have a few vegetarian items but not the extensive list that I thought. The service is incredible. They made vegetarian tacos that weren't on the menu (you should put it on guys) and also ran to get soy milk for my latte as they didn't serve that either. So well accommodated and very pleased.

First of all I am not a great fan of small dishes like Tapas and Meze simply because in Manhattan Â it's usually the biggest scam since the $40.00 hamburger. I am however happy to eat my words and just about every thing that comes out of the tiny kitchen at Tia Pol.40 minutes for a table? no problem, I'll have the fried garbanzo beans to start and a glass of Cava. Tight seating on backless stools?not an issue, the excellent lamb skewers,bacalau croquettes,patatas bravas,lengua,serrano ham platter,blistered peppers and the cockles and razor clams is actually worth the crick in my back . I like this place and it's laid back vibe,the wait staff are efficient ,friendly and knowledgeable about their wine list. Very well done.

My friend and I wanted a nice quiet place to warm up after a long walk in the cold and we were excited to find a Japanese teahouse. We ordered some dim sum (small snacks for tea) and two pots of tea. We rather enjoyed our tea, but the dim sum dishes left much to be desired. The teahouse had a nice ambience and was ideal for chatting.

The only Panamanian restaurant in NYC, and it is very good! Â There are no frills here, just authentically prepared food served at a leisurely pace. Â Brush up on your Spanish, because you just might need it here. Natasha ordered everything for me creating quite the feast for us, but I took notes: Â  - Carimanolas. Â Tubes of yucca root filled with lightly spiced ground meat. Â With the appearance of a Twinkie, this was actually a savory delight. Â Great start. - Patacones. Â That is how they refer to them in Panama, you may know them better as Tostones. Â Twice fried green plantains served with a hot sauce. Â Though heavy, these are addictive. Â I am surprised these haven't taken off in the U.S. Â  - Oxtail. Â So tender, lightly adhering to the bone. Â I love how they stewed this. Â Matched with peas and rice as well as sweet plantain, this was a true delight. Â I am known for being a slow eater, but I readily abandoned my fussiness and just went at this dish. Â This was great comfort food, Panamanian style. Â I really recommend trying this dish. Â  -Sorell. Â This is known as bissap in west Africa. Â A lovely drink with a kick; it is made by boiling hibiscus leaves. Overall, there was not a single miss in the bunch. Â Everything was just great. Â The preparations are simple but effective. Â The ambience is low key, and the decor is understated with Panamanian kitsch on the walls. Â The service is very slow and almost nonexistent. Â But Panamanians know this place, and they trek long and far to come here. Â If it meets their approval, it should meet ours too. Â  Five stars because I know of no other place like this.

Fantastic. Pure and simple, fantastic is the one word that sums up Adrienne's Pizza Bar. Great location, great service, great space, all complemented by even greater food. My wife and I LOVED our meal here. From our drinks to our dessert, everything was A+. I am a big caipirinha fan, and I just had to try Adrienne's Sicilian spin on a Brazlian mainstay...I did not regret it. Maybe it was because I hadn't eaten anything up to that point, but two sips and I was already catching a buzz. The drink was awesome, but the free bread that came before our meal was also superb. When our pizza arrived, I was suprised at how big it was. I'm typically not a fan of thing crust pizzas, but this was pizza was absolutely perfect. The thin, almost crispy pepperoni was divine and the crust was niether gooey nor flaky, it was just right. The pizza was really good, but I also enjoyed the chicken parm sandwich I split with my wife; they stuck to the script and produced a great sandwich. As if the drinks and entrees weren't enough, we just had to try the Nutella cake. It should be against the law to eat at Adrienne's and skip out on the Nutella cake, enough said. Definitely check this place out if you're in the mood for a great meal at a great price.

This is literally the best brunch I have ever had. Definitely recommend any of their Tartes FlambÃ©s, specifically the Munster. The mimosas are expertly made, and the service was among the best I've received in New York. Big thanks to GÃ©rard, for the incredible experience. Will definitely come back soon!

An hour wait, but worth it, at least the first time. This is a tasty piece of pizza. The mozzarella cheese compliments the chewy dough and the amazing tomato sauce. Brooklyn made sodas available too. The atmosphere is low key and has a family atmosphere. Warning, there are a lot of tourists that go here.

My favorite bar/restaurant in Park Slope. The owners know their food and drink and though the choices are limited, everything here is interesting and delicious. And as others have said, the best burger I've ever had, really amazing.

I've lived 2 blocks away from this place for 6 years and never knew it existed. It's small and virtually hidden next to the Chinese restaurant. We found it on Yelp and I'm so happy we did. It will be my new go to restaurant for delicious, fresh, healthy food. I had the amazing special grilled tofu salad and my boyfriend had the mouthwatering salmon filet salad. Both were flavorful and filling. The vegetables were perfectly ripe and the dressing paired perfectly with the taste sensations of the ingredients. The service was so nice too. The owner even gave a us a fresh guava to take with us that just arrived.

The empenadas were 3 diffrent kinds, so u have your choice of meat poultry vegy, very good..the service was a bit slow, and since I am originally from NYC, the atmosphere was comfortable, but for sunday brunch I dont want to sit next to drunk people, that was the only down fall...I will try it again

GO out of my way to come here once a week. Reminds me of the Oaxaca fare we enjoyed at home in our parent's restaurant with our Mexican coworkers. The tacos al pastor is my jam and the salsas they serve them with are homemade and incredible. I've eaten at the food truck and the restaurant. Both are awesome. Oh and they give you a little caramelized green onion to bite on between taco bites and radishes. Super authentic. Plus Mexican Coke. Best Mexican I've had on the east coast!

Good food, heaping portions, very affordable -- what more can you ask for? Stumbled upon Il Corallo while exploring the NYU area with some friends, and stopped in after yelping neighborhood lunch places and seeing their incredible lunch specials. $9.95 for a pizza and a house salad -- I may have been starving but the house salad (really just a regular salad) tasted fabulous and was lightly dressed (per my preference), and I was surprised that the pizza was a whole pizza. I was expecting maybe a slice or two. But no.... it was an entire Med. sized pizza for one person - perfectly chewy thin crust and great tomato sauce to cheese ratio. Needless to say, I had to take half of it home. A delicious meal for a great price. My dining companions had different pasta dishes and enjoyed their food immensely as well.

Cute little place with excellent selection of great Italian dishes. Ordered several items to taste, fried calamari, Penne, salad, polenta, and a few others. Â All fantastic, reasonably priced, rustic look and feel, warm, cozy, and inviting. Â Can't wait to try again but unfortunately located in the middle of nowhere. A world away but most certainly worth the trek. Â Service a bit slow but was properly apologetic and had great attitude and since prices were reasonable, easily forgivable.

I'm a huge fan of palatschinken. Â There needs to be more of it. Â Funny thing is, I wasted months of not eating palatschinken back when I was living over yonder because I thought it was some kind of pork dish (Schinken = pork in German). Â D'oh! Â Nope. Â It's a crepe. Â Wonderful, delicious crepe-a-palooza. Â So, in the effort to make up for lost time, I abide by the maxim, always get the palatschinken. Â  Cafe Sabarsky's got a trout palatschinken. It's good. Â Yes, it's a bit on the small side. Â Sabarsky is nothing if not authentically European, meaning, kind of expensive, kind of small portions, etc. Â But no one will bat an eye if you get wine at lunch. So that's a good trade off. Â And then you can order cake. Â And coffee. Â And as long as you ignore the damage being done to your wallet, it's all good. Â There are far more mediocre places in New York for the same price. Â I mean, have you seen how much the Olive Garden charges these days? Â Well, I haven't, but whenever I'm in the midwest and end up at those chain places, I'm always surprised that they are not actually so cheap. Â At least the Cafe Sabarsky is charming and good. Â  Sabarsky's Sacher Torte is more Demel-y than Sacher-y. Sorry. I will elaborate, borrowing an explanation from a friend of mine. Â In her words, Sacher Tortes are like day old Ding Dongs. Â And that, my friends, is why there's Schlag on the side. Because Austrian cakes are dry. Â Now, Demel's Sacher Tortes have always been slightly moister than Sacher's Sacher. And Sabarsky seems to have borrowed the Demel recipe (although the chocolate is not as rich). Â In other words, the Sabarsky Sacher Torte is kind of like a half-a-day old Ding Dong. Â It's still good, though. Â But, honestly, not as good as Demel's, whose branch here closed a few months ago. I'm still very sad about that. Oh, as an aside, many reviews complain that the cakes here are on the dry side. Â Willkommen in Ã–sterreich! Â Seriously. Â Austrian cakes tend toward the dry side. Â Sabarksy's very authentic on that front. As an aside, if what you're interested in is Austrian food, and you're not beholden to the UES location or proximity to the Met, may I suggest you head downtown to Cafe Katja? Â The spaetzle's better. Â It's cozy and has a great wine list, and it's much cheaper. Â Just a suggestion.

Because I love this place, I took my mom there this afternoon. What started out as a disaster led to a wonderful lunch. I ordered the vegan hot dogs as I usually do. My mom got the salmon sandwich. I bit into my hot dog and spit it out immediately upon realizing that it was beef. I'm a vegetarian. Uh oh. I notified the waitress, she apologized and my food was brought out. It was delicious as usual, but I was pretty upset by the experience because it was my first bad experience of any kind at Westville and I was definitely let down. She offers my mom and I a complimentary dessert. I thought this was the extent of the apology but was still gracious. We ordered an apple pie and I got a coffee. Then, she brought us the check. We were only charged for my mom's sandwich. The total was twelve dollars. I was shell shocked. What would have been a meal costing over thirty dollars, was twelve dollars. I thanked the waitress so much because I was genuinely happy to know that the business really cared about its reputation and its relationship with its customers. I commended her on her professionalism and her graciousness. I wish I caught her name but I can attribute the gestures of apology only to the business as a whole. I was honestly doubting whether I would back into the restaurant after being served a beef dog after clearly ordering a vegan one, but now I know that I don't have to fear mistakes because they will take care of business.

I usually order the same thing whenever I come here: grilled skirt steak with rice, beans, and a side order of tostones. I've never been let down. Last night, however, I went back and decided to try something new. I ALWAYS start with the grilled corn mexican style (chili powder, lime, and cojita cheese). Honestly, there's no point in going to this place if you're not going to get this dish. It's the staple and a MUST have. That being said, probably not the best idea to come here on a first date - you'll spend about 10 minutes after picking your teeth and that's obviously not that attractive. Anyway, this corn is messy, delicious, and overall incredible. I decided to order the Pollo Mirador (sauteed chicken breast with roasted garlic sauce, spicy spinach & white rice) this time. I have to say that I was a little surprised at just how much garlic was in this dish. It was also mixed with a lot of lemon, which made the sauce incredibly strong and tangy. If you're into those types of flavors, then great! Me, not so much. The spicy spinach was pretty delicious and the rice was just your standard white rice. I do recommend ordering a side of tostones with any dish. It makes the meal complete. I wouldn't order the chicken again but the grilled skirt steak is bomb. Get there on the earlier side if you don't want to wait a long time for a table.

Very nice of them which is why I would give them 4 stars instead of 3. All my previous visits though I had were about the same with service. Â I'll always come back for the pizza.

They take reservations here but not from 8pm-10pm (very odd, since that IS prime time) I made reservations for 7:30pm on a Friday. K and I sat at the beautiful seafood bar right by the front door. I was surprised by how quiet the room was, but I was comfortable when I sat down amongst the other guests that were already seated. Japanese salt is the star of the show here. The seafood is very fresh, the beef is tender, the vegetables seemed like there were just picked from the soil, everything is sprinkled lightly with the mild but tasty salt from Japan. Some of the dishes we ordered were, sashimi to start, grilled sea urchin, grilled asparagus (this literally arrived 2 short asparagus cut in 3 pcs for $6), grilled whole rock fish (this was a small fish slightly smaller than my hand), grilled dark meat chicken. (every dish we ordered was TINY). The cooks serve the food and drinks on a long wooden paddle to the guests seated at the bar, it was pretty cool to watch. I especially loved that when an order placed they would jump on the ice bar to pick out the ingredients. The food was good, but very pricey for the actual amount that was served($350 for 2 people). For big eaters like K and I, we found ourselves hungry after 20 min leaving the place.... I'd definitely go again IF someone else was paying. :) Enjoy!

I've been here about 5 or 6 times since my last review and I have always been pleased, bordering on orgasmic. Some recommendations: 1) talk to your server about the oyster selections in detail--I had some that I never would have tried (from Virginia!) and they were sensational 2) maybe you think you don't want the meatballs, but YOU DO 3) if you are hungry, the fried chicken is huge and every bite is heavenly 4) the escarole salad is still among my favorite salads on the planet 5) the french fries may only be french fries but they are outstanding 6) yes, deviled eggs! 7) sazerac! Â Once, they wanted to give our table to some other folks, so they bought us a round in exchange for moving to the bar--yes! Â  Count me among Walter's' biggest fans.
pork belly buns !!! perfect place for a pre-dinner ;)

I think I had my expectations way too high for this place. Most of that is due to me being a Negril fan. This being the sister restaurant kinda had me expecting alot more First..the decor was dope. It did the job. Nothing really to write home about though. But it was nice The Dj was the Dj from Negril village that always played well. Now let's get to the drinks. Sangria was weak. Overall, I'm going to give soco another go round. Cool place. Just don't go expecting to be wowed. Â All different everything next time.

Went to cafe Habana tonight bec Bianca around the corner had a 45 min wait. The yelp reviews were great and I love cuban/mexican food and caprinias on a Friday evening looked like a winner. We were a party of three and got seated immediately in a corner table in the back. I've been ordering the miso glazed salmon from mooncakes for years now. It is soo delish and one of my favorite things to order from here. My ordering experience has always been great, even when I do it online and have to put in specific things that I want, it is always correct. The steak sandwich is also very tasty, a little tough but good. The mango lobster rolls are amazing!! This place always seems to amaze me.

Situated in chelsea market you'll find this taco shack which offers up authentic tacos. Affordable price and quick service. Reminds me of the taco shacks in Mexico City. Place your order and bring the receipt to the counter for one of the attendants to make your taco. You get a choice with the flour or corn tortillas which is great. I went with the corn tortillas for the al pastor and the pork taco. Both were flavorful, grilled well on the flat top, and had a nice kick to them. Make sure to add on the spicey sauces, green, red, and radishes on the counter that accompanies the tacos well. Also their Horchata drink is a standout as well. Sweet and refreshing.

I'm a biker, I love to ride. Â But I also happen to like eating. That's why Pier i is so awesome. Â Tucked away under the west side highway is this little oasis of goodness. Â Great food, great views, it's a welcome respite from the hustle and bustle of the city. Â What I love is how the food here is decent (solid burgers, great lobster rolls, really tasty fries) - and the beer offerings here are solid. Best of all this is right by a bike path - the perfect place to stop for an outdoor pit stop. Â Here you won't feel like an asshole if you park your bike by your table (unlike many other annoying "outdoor" restaurants in the city that give you shit for leaving your bike by your table). Â As much as I like the Frying Pan downtown, I like this place even better because there are less pretentious fucktards who show up here and it's a far more chillaxed place. I just came back from Thailand a week ago and this place is ok. There are better places in the city for thai food. The line is not worth the wait. I'm not a 100% positive, but I think they cheat (pre made can ingredients) on how they make Â their chicken soup or tum ka gai. Maybe on a less busy night the food would be better.

3.25 stars. Â There are those who will say that this is the best burger in New York City. Â And they very well may be right. Â It's a decent burger, and quite frankly, I haven't tried too many burgers in this city. Â Having said that, from a burger perspective, this place doesn't hold a candle to the great burger spots of Texas (I've even had a better burger in DC), and I'll tell you why. First, the quality of the meat left something to be desired. Â For example, a truly awesome burger may feature meat that is aged in-house (Ray's Hell Burger in Washington DC), grass-fed (Hut's Hamburgers in Austin TX), or simply USDA prime (Beck's Prime in Houston TX). Â The burger at Spotted Pig is none of these. Second, often there would be at least some variety left to the consumer in order to make their burger. Â Very few places can get away with singular options (Arnolds Burger in Amarillo TX quickly comes to mind as an exception). Â I like a place that doesn't just give me fancy Roquefort cheese burger as my singular option. Third, the actual burger provided at Spotted Pig, while tasty, went overboard on the Roquefort cheese. Â  The pungent bitterness may have meshed better with the burger if it was balanced with chantrelles, but this was simply not an option given to the consumer. Â It was basically good (but not great) quality meat with good cheese. Â  Okay, I know that might come off as overly harsh, and it doesn't change the FACT that the burger at Spotted Pig is very good. Â I just think that it might be hyperbole to call it the best in the city, and if it is, I would suggest that NYC is not the destination for burgers in the first place. What Spotted Pig DOES do especially well is eggs. Â We had the deviled eggs appetizer, and we were delighted by their consistenty, taste, and balance of flavors. Â I saw some tantalizing eggs delivered with another plate and instantly wished that I had ordered something outside of the burger. Â I also ate a Cubano sandwich which was tasty, but I would have liked a bit more balance between the prosciutto (substituted for the traditional ham) and the pulled pork (which was a bit overpowering). Â The tiny pickles meshed well with that particular order. Also, I want to give props to the atmosphere at Spotted Pig. Â This place is genuinely awesome. Â  From the spotted pig with rainbow colored boots adorning the front of the restaurant to the restaurant layout to the staff, this place exudes a level of awesomeness that cannot be fully explained. Â  In short, this is a nice spot to check out, but I simply wouldn't call it a destination spot for burgers. Â Try out some of their other cuisine (and definitely try some of their more brunch-friendly items), and you will leave this place happy.

I had to come here because of the reviews I've seen, ranking Totto Ramen among the best ramen shops in NYC, even hitting the #1 spot on a few lists I've encountered. My top two had always been Hide Chan and Ippudo. I'd been meaning to come here for over a year to see if it matched, but I just never found myself out in this area. Plus, I heard the waits can be pretty tough. I finally made it. My top two are still Hide Chan and Ippudo. Totto falls in the top 5, maybe even clinching the 3rd spot, but a distant 3rd. I came on a Tuesday at 7pm, and the line was only 20 minutes. Not bad, so chalk that up as a win as compared to Ippudo where I've never seen less than an hour wait at most normal eating hours. I ordered the char siu pork, the spicy ramen, had a kaedama (extra noodle), and then ordered the chicken ramen as well. Yes, I'm serious. You'd think that was because the food was so delicious I couldn't stop eating, but overall it was good, but not the best. The pork was interesting; they used a blow torch to put the final touches on it. It was tasty, but I wouldn't shy away from a bit more fat on it. Also, the slices were cut a bit thin and I think this may have made them taste a bit dry to me. Also, they presented it on a slice of lettuce with some bean sprouts. I don't know what to think of that. The spicy ramen broth was interesting. I optimize for porkiness in my ramen broth, which is why I love Hide Chan and Ippudo. There was definitely pork flavor, but more striking was the spicy flavor they added. It was garlicky, peppery, and spicy, although a bit overpowering. Tasty, but I prefer stronger pork flavor. The chicken ramen was okay. I liked the strong chicken flavor, but the chicken itself was dry which I suppose is expected. But the part that really brings them down a notch to me is the ramen consistency. At my top 2, I get perfect noodles every time. At Totto, each of my noodle servings was slightly different consistency, ranging from slightly mushy to slightly too al dente (don't forget I got 3 servings between 2 bowls + kaedama). This is something a top ramen shop has to get right. I'd come back here again, but only if I was in the area - which is rare - and the line was less than 30 minutes. Like I said: it's a top 5 ramen shop, but I've got my top 2 already.

So, I'll start off by saying I live in Texas and that I eat tacos a couple of times a week. These guys cook amazing food. I highly recommend that you stop in. I had a cantaloupe agua fresca. It was made perfectly. Not too much sugar. Paired with a Chilorio Beef Brisket Taco & a Kale & Potato Taco. Both blew me mind. Go now! Located in the Essex st market.

how far the mighty have fallen... i ate here many times the year it opened. this May, back in the nabe, we stopped in again. honestly it was like eating at Chili's. oversalted, too sweet, dumbed down and disappointing. done.

I visited this place after hearing rave reviews. Â We got there around 3 PM and the place was packed...good sign! Â Once we were seated the service was very slow. Â We were actually unsure if we had a server assigned to our table. Â I completely understand being busy, but after spending 12 years in the food service industry, I know the value of just acknowledging the guests. Â If you're busy, we totally understand, we just want to know that we will eventually be served. Â Once we ordered, the pizza actually came out pretty quickly. Â It was large enough for a table of four to split, and really delicious! Keep in mind that this place is cash only. Â They have an ATM there, so just make sure you bring cash or an ATM card!
Love this bar. Great decor. Great cocktail. Great food. Also, the bathroom is very clean and smells like mango. All around great experience!

Ok ... we always love Cafeteria, but add Nicole as your waitress and you are guaranteed a GREAT, fun time. Â Service is hit or miss with some of the waiters, but Nicole is ALWAYS on, provides the best service and is a BLAST .... and thanks for getting us film info!

This place is really cute!! I love the bar area in the front. Give me a chalkboard any day and i will fall in love with the place. The selections for you were scribbled in white over one side of the walls. I loved how the wines were presented above the bar with a walkway. Very show..and i like that as well...gave it an industrial edge. The bartender, hello friendly. He was more than happy to open a few bottles and allow you to take a taste to see if it was to your liking. The cheese pairings were good as well but i enjoyed them more over at Casellula. The ice cream sandwich though at the end tied it all together for me. I think that it is in a bit of an odd location but surely it will kick off in the coming years. The whole 10th and 11th ave above 45 is trying really hard to transform and i am just not sure if there is the demand for chic/trendy places yet in the area. I hope it survives though cause i really enjoyed myself!

I think I'm giving it so few stars because it was so raved about by everyone and I was pretty disappointed. There was a tolerable wait on a Saturday afternoon. Â Like many Manhattan eateries, the seating was a bit cramped. Â  My chilaquiles were salty and not very delicious, and the black beans that came with my dish were also not very good. Â My friend's steak and eggs were so-so. Â  I guess the upside is that it's cheap. Â I won't be going back.
One Of My Hotspots In NYC. Love Everything About This Place! Wish I Own It! They Have Never Let Me Down! Great Food.

There aren't many vegetarian options which was a total bummer for me. The only entre that was vegetarian was the beet ravioli but I went with the salad the 1st time we went. The salad was crisp and fresh and very tasty. The flash fried oysters are TO DIE FOR!! I don't like oysters so the fact that I love this says a lot. We actually decided to go back just for the fried oysters and I decided to get the ravioli. These were probably the most decadent, smooth ravioli I've ever had. I just wish I could go there and try different things, everything else is heavy on meat so this is all I could have. Either way it was amazing though.

This spot is most definitely on point. Soup dumplings do not usually amaze me to any degree, but the ones at this place blew my mind. So soupy and delicious! Came during odd afternoon hours so we got seated right away, but the place was still rather packed. Can't imagine what it's like during peak hours. We also had the hot and sour soup which was good but didn't stand out (it hasn't anywhere for me it's just comforting) and some scallion cakes I think. The cakes were good too.

Probably the most authentic Korean restaurant in the NYC tri-state area that comes closest to tasting like food you would eat in Korea. The interior design has the feel of a restaurant you might encounter in Seoul's Insadong district. The fact that there is always a line (both Korean and non-Korean customers) is a testament to its reputation as a great Korean restaurant. The banchan (side dishes) always taste fresh and the servers are more than happy to refill upon request. The soondooboo (soft tofu) is fresh and there is no hint of any MSG in the food. Everything I have had has never disappointed and I tell my friends that although this restaurant isn't the typical Korean bbq place with the grill attached to the table, this is really the place with the best tasting and most authentic food. That may mean little to others but it goes a long way with me. I have heard from others that they use ingredients directly imported from Korea but I have no way of corroborating whether there is truth to that. The place is a bit cramped and sitting near the front will mean you are likely to have waiting diners in close proximity (my only complaint about the place). Again that is just the consequence of doing what they do pretty well: providing good food at a decent price.

Yes, five but I'm boycotting it. Â Lets see how long before my craving for the most amazing pizza ever makes me punk out and cave in. Â 5 dollars a slice, ok we pay that for coffee in NYC but the wait, OMG the wait. Â Over an hour and a half for a pie. Â With that delicious smell and hot bubbly pizza coming out of the oven and staring you in the face. Â  Ok I can even handle that, it's the fact that there is no rhyme or reason to how the orders are placed and who gets their slice/pie first. Â  If you are a germaphobe skip the place the tables are always gross!

The chocolate cake is amazing. Seriously--amazing. I'm slightly concerned that it might have had some sort of euphoria-inducing drug baked inside. Very fun, unique place, & a great spot for a date. It is very crowded though--I hope you're in the mood to make new friends because you'll be sitting three inches away from another couple. There is a semi-outdoor courtyard in the back, but I assume it requires a reservation (& possibly a large group).

Defonte's has great sandwiches, as all the reviewers point out. Â the egg and potato and egg and pepper heros have a special place in my heart. Â I used to live a half block from Defonte's, and there was no better breakfast than a Defonte's egg and potato on a bench in Red Hook Park. Defonte's does double-duty as a good place for coffee on your way to work, and they've got basic provisions in case you run out of milk, eggs, or bread. The only down side of this place is the hours! Â I would have gone much more if they were open when I got out of work. Nice work, ladies and gentlemen!

I really, really like it here. I've had several great meals here and its a good place to take my vegan friends to. When I heard there was a new menu, I was excited to try it out. When I ordered my favorite thing on the menu (kangaroo sliders) I was disappointed. I miss the goat cheese and pineapple salsa that they previously came with. Now, its served with a chipotle aioli and carmelized onions that doesn't really compliment it so I miss the old sliders! On a different note, I'm always impressed with how many specials they have and it seems like some of the older specials made it on to the new menu which I'm happy about (corn and jalapeno fritters, stuffed calamari).
Cheap and good food. Made the mistake of eating in and all my clothes and bag smelled like grease and oil. Next time i'll take my food to go.

Outstanding brunch on Labor Day weekend. Â We arrived just as they opened and were seated immediately. Â Based on Yelp reviews, we chose the Short Rib Hash and Eggs and the Hangtown Fry. Â Both were excellent, although we liked the Hangtown Fry just slightly better. Â Restaurant was lovely, service was great, overall a fun way to spend a Sunday morning.

Don't get the burger. I Had been there two other times, thought it was decent, fun. Â But this time,oh my word, two of us (out of four) got the burger. Â The meat couldn't have been worse, it was the lowest quality I've ever encountered. Â Neither one of us could eat it, one or two bites each and we realized the meat was just bad. Â I didn't realize Hamburger meat could be so chewy, and this had stringy things. Â We Should've retuned it, but I feel awkward about that. Â I just can't understand how they served it, it was really, really bad.

I talk about the Walter Foods shrimp cocktail. A lot. I don't even like shrimp--mostly just cocktail sauce--but these shrimp are always particularly plump and fresh in a way that makes me feel oddly naughty. And you know, I also don't like filet mignon. It's a lean cut and not what you'd call robustly flavored. But here? It is of the gods. Best I've ever had. And my parents loved them some filet mignon when I was growing up. The cocktails are pretty decent, too, and the cute, overall atmosphere makes it one of the more prime spots in Williamsburg. In my opinion. I will say that I've never been exactly thrilled by the desserts. But I'm usually full after my DIY surf and turf anyway.

Amazing food. Â I have never used these words: "the tastes are so subtle;the foamy amuse bouche is popping in my mouth; tasting sweet and salty and loving it". Â The food was astoundingly great and inventive. Â The duck confit croquettes special appetizer was outstanding followed by several other appetizers which were equally delicious. Â Seared Scallop appetizer had 2 generous scallops atop pureed cauliflower with fabulous flavors. Â 6 mini pulled pork tacos in polenta taco were delicious. Â Homemade gelatos fabulous especially chartreuse chocolate and salted caramel. Â Service was excellent with very attentive mature waitstaff making sure we were happy. Â Prices are typically New York mid high, but worth every penny. Â Certainly much less expensive than many of the other midtown restaurants.

I want to start out saying that I love authentic Thai food and I haven't found a great Thai restaurant in NY until I came here, and I was excited to eat here. I loved most of the dishes we ordered. The highlights were the papaya salad, larb, and red curry. I totally judge a Thai restaurant by those 3 dishes and they were absolutely fantastic. The soft shell crab was amazing too. Now why didn't I give this place 5 stars? Well, it's because I'm torn. These dishes were great, but the restaurant served us sour yellow curry. It wasn't a little sour, but very sour. Everyone in my party had a good scoop and at first, I was skeptical of the sour yellow curry as the yellow curry I've eaten in the past didn't taste like this, but I still ate the portion on my plate as everyone else seemed okay. Boy was I right about the sourness because needless to say, I got sick afterwards. The waitress was super sweet and kind after we asked if the curry should be sour. She looked confused and said it shouldn't be and brought it back. She took it off the bill and made a new batch for my table. The manager however tried to defend their yellow curry saying it should be a little sour and that they make it at the beginning of the week and freeze it for the week. I must have gotten a bad batch, but honestly, he should have left it alone. So I'm torn because I had some amazing dishes. Then the restaurant served us food that went sour. Just be careful if you go. But definitely one of the better Thai restaurants in NY.

Awesome new place that's totally going to liven up a somewhat 'eh' neighborhood. Â Beautiful decor (super trendy), specialty cocktails (try the Westside Mule, delicious) and yummy menu (truffle fries, hellooooo). Has a great upstairs space for private events that overlooks the bar. Â  Best part of the place? OUTLETS UNDER THE BAR TO PLUG IN YOUR PHONE. genius.

I am officially addicted to Grimaldi's pizza! Â If anyone even mentions the name of this restaurant, my mouth begins to water. Â My boyfriend and I always order a large pie to split...and we never have any leftovers. Â I recommend going right when they open, especially during the summer, because it gets crowded quickly and you will have to wait in line outside. Â You can also order take-out...another great possibility (especially if you are already in DUMBO). Â Just a note: they only accept CASH!

Depending on what time you go there is usually a long wait to get seated but once you do - boy is the food worth it! I've been here over 6-7 times and the food is always on point. My favorite are the kebabs and the peasant salad. The fried and grilled calamari, grilled chicken, and seafood pasta are amazing too.
