My bf made me try octopus for the first time here and with much hesitation, I tried it, and it tasted great actually - kind of like chicken. Not sure if I would have it again though - I'm not that bold. The lemon potatoes are unbelievably delicious. The olive bread with drizzled olive oil that they give you in the beginning is yummy and you can even ask them to substitute that for warm pita bread if you want to be 'healthy'. Sometimes they'll give you a free dessert at the end of your meal. Even if you have to wait to be seated, the food quality and decent price is well worth it. It's great for a date, or with friends, or with family - casual but nice, busy ambiance. Luckily, my bf and I have been here enough to go when there is either no wait or no more than a 5-10 min wait. We'll be back for sure! ;)

Marc Forgione would be amazing for a first date or a group meal. Â The space is approachable but impressive. Â I took my boyfriend out for his birthday - and luckily had the code from Blackboard Eats for a much appreciated discount! Â (pretty pricey) Started off the meal with amuse bouche from the kitchen - pea soup shooter and some sort of tatar. Â Strangely, they only gave us 1 spoonful of each (for 2) but we both wanted to try it! Â So we awkwardly tried to split pea soup with our forks... not an easy feat. For appetizer, we ordered the Veal Cheeks Milanese. Â Tender and flavorful, the only complaint is that it left this weird coating of fat or butter feeling in my mouth. Â Not the best mouthfeel in the world. For entrees, I ordered the hanger steak. Â It was tasty but over cooked (I asked for medium rare/closer to rare. Â It was more like medium) Â - what I DID find spectacular was the bone marrow that came with it! Â HUGE fan of bone marrow and I didn't realize it came with that so was pleasantly surprised. Â  My boyfriend ordered the Whole Red Snapper. Â It was his fault he ordered it, b/c it did state that it was whole - but that fish came out and it was SUPER bony. Â He had such a hard time eating it that he stopped after less than 1/2 the fish was done. Â I tried the fish (I love whole fish) and I also struggled eating the fish without getting bones in each bite. Â Maybe we just got an extra spiny fish - not sure. Â I honestly can't even tell you what this dish tasted like because the bones dominated the dish so much that I don't think I even concentrated on the taste of the fish! Â For my bf, the picky eater, on his birthday dinner - I felt bad that he ordered this. Â Especially since he ended up cooking another meal when we got home b/c he wasn't full from his entree!!! For dessert, we got the hazlenut ice cream sundae - it was great. Â Not too sweet at all. Â They then gave us 2 complimentary brownie bites wth the check, now THOSE were amazing. Â If I knew those were coming, I may have skipped the ice cream sundae! All in all, the experience was decent. Â I'd go back and NOT get the fish or the steak - I have a feeling that the other dishes are better and have less issues with the prep or doneness. Â Solid restaurant, although it made me question the validity of what it means to have "1 Michelin Star"... i've been to many more restaurants I thought were more deserving.

The Akamaru Modern broth is perfect! Flavors are rich and complex. It is probably one of my favorite broths. Noodles were cooked well but I like slightly thicker/chewier noodles. Just a taste preference. Tori Karaage Fried Chicken was tasty but really..when is fried chicken not tasty? Hirata Buns (Pork) were okay. Meat was not that tender but flavor was alright Yamitsuki Goma Kyuri Cucumbers are so good. Love the crispness and the tasty sesame oil dressing The waiting area is small and the wait is usually long. There also are only a few chairs in the waiting area. I have gone here at 9pm and at like 130 or 2pm and there always seems to be a pretty decently long wait.

This is my favorite Jean-Georges restaurant. The food. The ambience. The service. Even the plates. I love every little detail. ABC kitchen blew me away the first time I ate there. It was one of the first nice restaurants my girlfriend and I went to when we started dating. Now, it's been a year and ABC just brings back good memories. I Â never thought I would like Chicken Liver, but thanks to them I do. We ordered the Lamb Shank once and the bone sticks up off the plate. So, when everyone was done eating I grabbed the huge bone in my hand and started chomping away at the meat. Jean-Georges walks over and says " I like your style of eating. It is very medieval." I tried to reply, but I had a mouthful of lamb so all that came out was "raff flabb thraw blrooo" . A little embarrassing, especially because Katie Holmes was sitting at the next table and laughed with us at the whole situation. ABC Kitchen is growing in popularity, so plan on making a reservation weeks in advance. It is an unforgettable experience and I hate leaving that Â place. The decor just cheers me up and makes me feel as I'm in Â a fairytale forest. Can't wait to go back!
Yeah, still as good as ever. I had the pork buns and Karaka Men ramen...if this was my last meal ever, I'd be alright with that. Yeah...it's that good.

I am definitely a regular. They are open late nights. Â Prices are cheap for alcohol & food. Everything is great. They always try to accomadate groups of any size. Attentive and quick staff. My favorite izakaya! Â Food tips: sashimi salad, mentai pasta, chicken meatballs & shishito peppers. Yum.

Score! Â I'm so glad I tried this local Lebanese restaurant in my neighborhood. Â It's gonna be a new favorite! Â The lamb was tender and perfectly spiced and cooked. Â The homemade rice and lentils with onion atop was fluffy and tasty. Â The homemade unsweetened iced tea was perfect with the touch of mint. Â I can see why they earned a Michelin star!
Loved the chicken fried steak and the patty melt.

Not bad, but not special. At the edge of the world, no wait, it's just Ave C.. There lives Royale. What looks to be a pretty standard nyc bar (i.e., not super dive-y but definitely not swanky either) serves up a solid burger and beer. The meat and cheese--aka the most important parts--juicy and melty. Good job. Two little and pleasant surprises? The toasted sesame seed bun and bibb lettuce leaf. All right. Not too shabby. The bartender/waitress was nice. Other patrons kept to themselves. BBall was on. ::shrug:: Didn't wow me so no 5. It did hit the spot messy burger + beer wise with no silly waiting for a table, so you'd think it'd be a 4. But the fries weren't very good, and they got a C sanitation rating. Eh... that just seems lazy. 3, it is. Tip: Â Download the scoutmob app for 50% off coupon on dinner.

Often times, we try to find one or two things we like about a restaurant. We focus on those as reasons to dine in or recommend to others. Other times, you'll be lucky enough stumble upon an establishment where there is nothing NOT to like. You find every reason to recommend it and visit them over and over again. Ilili is one of those places. It is an ideal spot to enjoy delicious Lebanese food, strong cocktails, great service, and terrific ambiance. Better yet, none of these are mutually exclusive. With a cavernous interior that has a bi-level space which separates itself into lounges and dining areas, Ilili works wonderfully for group dinners and celebrations as well as intimate dinner dates for two. Coming in for just a drink or two at the bar is just as fun with friendly bartenders and strong cocktails. Speaking of cocktails, lovers of fruit-fruit flavors and hard-hitting drinks seem to enjoy From Beirut with Passion with mint infused vodka and passion fruit. If one desires to balance a strong drink with a lighter, refreshing choice, the Fresh Medow (with gin and cucumber) is perfect. The food menu boasts a combination of typical Lebanese fare along with some novel creations. The memorable, yet typical, include Hommus (pine nuts), Warm Eggplant, and Bone Marrow. The amazing Saffron Tripe is the winner for creativity. Even tripe haters will be converted by this dish. Two drinking-and-dining experiences at Ilili only fuel the desire to come back for more. A glutton like myself will prefer to share more food with less people, but Laura A's awesome review (yelp.com/biz/ilili-new-yâ€¦) best encapsulates the group experience. The Mezza Kbire and Candy Bar are at the top of the list for the next visit!

This is probably my favorite bar in the city. You walk in and the energy picks you up, makes you want to let loose and socialize. Yes, probably 50% of the crowd is average West Village--bankers and girls working in fashion--but I've met people here from around the world, artists, chefs, etc. Plus they continue to allow me in wearing a cheap Uniqlo shirt, jeans and chukkas, despite all the well-dressed gentleman inside. Drinks are awesome but expensive. Come on weeknights for a more interesting and smaller crowd.
Yuk! Duck soup pic showed thick juicy slices of duck breast over steaming broth. What came was a bowl of bones, fat and grizzle. Â Beware.

Well its settled. Mariella is my absolute favorite restaurant in Park Slope. It has never failed me and my family has no celebrated three different birthdays here. The food is amazing, the service so fantastic and personal and the specials... oh the specials are always above and beyond the usual incredible menu. My favorites: fettucine bolognese & their lobster risotto special We've also had brunch here. This seems to be the only non-swamped, roomy brunch spot in Park Slope. I almost don't want to tell anyone its so rare. The ricotta pancakes are the best I've ever had. I got the short rib hash, actually, which was delish, but my sister got the pancakes and I couldn't stop eating them. Last year, my family and I walked the Teal Walk for ovarian cancer research in Prospect Park and brought 20 people in for a Saturday brunch afterwards. The owners and the staff were so well prepared for our arrival, we've already made another reservation for this year. I probably should stop writing about my Mariella love, because I'm getting really hungry. See you at brunch this Saturday!

Probably one of the best restaurants in NYC....HANDS DOWN. I went for my 30th birthday and it couldn't have been a better experience or meal. Obviously, you have to pay for that type of experience...but it's worth it. amazing staff and incredible food.

Once upon a time, I was nervous about picking a restaurant for a date. I had all these parameters; it was supposed to be in this certain neighborhood, it could only be these types of food, etc. I asked a friend* who said, "What are you, an amateur? Forget all that. Just take her to Las Ramblas. Eat some tapas, drink some sangria, and you're in like Flynn." This is good advice. The food is always good (she'll be impressed), the tables small (you can get close), and the sangria is boozy and delicious (she might even find you attractive after a pitcher or two). If you live in the West Village, then she will probably be impressed enough to walk home with you. If you don't, then the walk's long enough that she'll realize she's out of your league before you make it to your place. So take a cab. _________ *This is clearly not a good friend, as my close friends are not cool enough to say things like "in like Flynn," nor can they put together grammatically correct sentences.

I had the New England Lobster & CT Lobster Roll & the fish and chips. It was all melt in my mouth and it was so delicious. Not a fan of fries in general but I ate all their chips and fries. Loved their lemonade. Their service was attentive and polite and most importantly, not over bearing... I am seriously craving another Lobster roll right about now, wish Lobster Joint wasn't so far from work/home. The place is modern and their are things only available for happy hour. Must find time to go try them.

Ive been here 3x already (2 dinner and 1 brunch) and once for take out. Remember to make reservations if you want to eat here for dinner. I absolutely love the chef and his food. Altho, sometimes it gets really oily and heavy. The foie gras and fresh pasta is to die for! Always leave room for the coffee ice cream/doughnut dessert. Everything on the menu is amazing and so much flavor and love! You can tell the chef loves his work because he would always comes out during dinner service to talk to his patrons with a huge smile. The only gripe I have about this place is spacing and that its CASH ONLY. It can only fit 10 customers max. It does get very claustrophobic in there. The restaurant is amazing but it really is a very small bistro. If you dont make reservations, the wait can be anywhere between 30 mins- 45mins. And make sure to bring CASH! Pricing is between $15-$25 for entree. If you throw in some appetizers and the dessert for 2 people dining, your check is about $70-$100. Its very affordable especially for the quality French food in NYC. oh and btw - the restroom is in the kitchen. Make sure to ask the hostess first.

It was good pizza. NOT great. Not the same pizza you get in Italy. It was definitely NY Style pizza. I went on a Tuesday which is ideal, because I would not be happy if I waited an hour on Saturday night. I once had pizza from Harry's Big Tomato or Luna in CT, and these were both far better. Try Lombardi's in Manhattan.

Even though it is listed in the Michelin Guide NY, in my opinion it is overrated, and overpriced. Â  The Ramen was good, but not that great . Â It was not worth the price and the wait. Â I would not come back. I prefer Daikokuya in LA (the taste, and decor). Â Ippudo does not feel like a traditional cozy Ramen house in Japan. Â The decor here is modern, and use of communal tables like in Le Pain Quotidien. I think that communal tables are more common in NYC than LA. Â  By the way, there is no to go, and doggy bag. Â Either you finish it, or it goes all to waste. Â But the portion is not large.

Last night was my first time dining at Buttermilk Channel. It had been recommended to me by a friend for its "really good" fried chicken. The prices are up there. The service was good as my waiter was able to accommodate my mock-tail order with ease. There are no mock-tails on the menu. I guess the place was somewhat full, but not really packed. We ended up having to wait longer than I expected for our main entree to arrive. I ordered the duck meatloaf and was really happy with it. It was a small - regular portion which was fine with me. It was moist and interesting, but in a good way. My guest ordered the fried chicken, but was unfortunately, underwhelmed with it. The texture was good enough (juicy inside and crunchy outside), but it wasn't seasoned very well, if at all. I tried a small piece of the chicken and totally agreed with her. I honestly don't get what all the rave reviews over the chicken are for. I recommend the duck meatloaf and would go back for that, but I'll stick to getting fried chicken elsewhere.

Come here alone or in a small group, come here to eat happily and leave. I don't recommend this for a long sitting party situation -- that's not how you do it. Best things to try: - Beef & Tripe (hottest rating on the menu with #10) - Wontons in Chili Oil - Dry Fry Szechuan Beef If your plates aren't red, you're doing it wrong!

Cute place for brunching over comfort food with few friends. Â  We waited for more than 40 minutes before we got seated but what do you expect 1pm on a Sunday? Â The restaurant's L shape set up opens up at the back, where the best area for dining is. We were pleasantly surprised with the shabby chic, charming feel, creme fireplace and outside patio that is just waiting to be used once the weather permits. Â  My open face croque monsieur was delish, in fact, I think it was the best part of the meal. Â Think thick fluffy white bread pan fried in GruyÃ¨re cheese with ham and sunny side up egg on top accompanied with mesclun salad. Â  My friend's salmon burger was tasty but slightly salty but the tuna sandwich was mediocre. Â We couldn't leave without trying their popular waffles and can I say Â we couldn't have asked for a better ending? Â Their waffles are so light with that 'just right' sweetness, you can easily eat one on your own without feeling overwhelmed or heavy. Â BTW, if that's all your heart desires, I'd recommend having a side dish with it. Definitely want to come back to try their mussels and wine and burger and beer.
Always a wonderful time. Try to score a seat at the bar.
This one is much bigger than the one in Union Square - good service and drinks.

Il Bambino is my new obsession. I came here on valentines day because my bf and I were fed up with overpriced, pretentious Manhattan restaurants and their stupid valentine's day menus. We wanted to find a quiet, affordable place off the beaten path and we did. Everything on the menu is delicious. I highly recommend the cheese plate...it comes with a great assortment of different cheeses (and our waitress was really knowledgeable about the different kinds). Â The crostinis were crunchy and delicious (especially the garlic butter crostini). Â The paninis are also really good. Â They have a wide enough assortment that whoever you go with will definitely be able to find something that they like. And for dessert, the brownie was so amazing that I saved a little piece, wrapped it up and brought it back to the city with me (I'm a loser). Â  This place is "the great bambino". Great food, great atmosphere, great service. And with the BYOB, it's amazingly affordable. Â A great place for a date or a dinner with friends. Â It's really a gem and I find myself craving it all the time.

The food here is delicious and very affordable. Ive only just recently tried arepas and i have to say that I love them. I had one with chorizo which was very yummy and a michelada that was so so good! I would definitely come back here again, and its great for brunch!

This place is amazing! A great find in the SoHo/Nolita neighborhood! This is a great spot for salad and some pizza. Their pasta dishes are also really great. This place was very low-key and the service is great. All of the people are really laid back and attentive. The place is a little small but it is certainly worth it. It is very cozy inside and feels "homey" Tip: Make a reservation or call ahead. This place is swamped during lunch and dinner hours. My personal favorites are the Rubirosa salad and the Rubirosa supreme pizza. The salad is arugula, homemade mozzarella balls , shaved parmegiano cheese and homemade balsamic dressing. Everything is so fresh and authentic! This is by far my favorite salad in SoHo. The Rubirosa supreme is so great as well. Its your basic pizza with a pepperoni, meatball and garlic zing! The pizza here is thin crust and it is more then enough to share a large with about 4 people. The pizza is so tasty and flavorful. A salad runs about $12 and the pizza is anywhere from $16-$24 but it is well worth it for pizza and salad!

Breakroom NY: Manhattan: China Town 12pm Wednesday 5th November 2014 Four Stars I stopped in for lunch after court. I ordered a Beer and the Breakroom Burger ($8.45 a la carte) at the back counter. There are only like 10 seats in this place. Â The Bun was pedestrian but soaked up the abundance of flavor from everything else. Â The patty was thick and tasted like angus beef. Â The crispy yet fatty confit-cooked Pork Belly did not disappoint. The Runny Egg helped sauce the burger. Â The Fried Onion half added the necessary crunch. Â The use of Iceberg Lettuce didn't scream gourmet to me but the tomato and pickles were good. Â Overall, it was an enjoyable meal.

Out of all the things I ate on my recent trip to New York, this definitely was one of the most memorable. Â It's a ton of food for $6 and it hits the spot. Â The white sauce is like if ranch, yogurt, and mayo had a child, and for some reason when you mix it all together with a little bit of hot sauce it's just really satisfying. Â We waited in a bit of a line, but I thoroughly enjoyed it. Â I got the chicken and rice, and I would recommend getting extra pita bread, the combination is really good.

Yelp turned me onto this spot. I've been meaning to try the location since I moved to the area but never found a good opportunity-- this prior weekend, I was finally able to hit it for brunch. I rolled in on the early afternoon-ish period on Sunday and found that there was plenty of ample seating! There were only a few parties here-- and the restaurant has a fairly admirable selection of seating available, both indoors and outside, so this definitely chalks up as a potential "on-the-go" brunch spot. Service was great! The one girl that was waiting on our table was friendly and attentive. Orders came out in fairly good time; I didn't feel the duress of a long wait (one issue I've had with grabbing brunch in this area is that I feel like it takes 10yrs to get my orders sometimes). I opted for the buttermilk pancakes, which were pretty phenomenal. Prepared just right and with all the usual suspects (syrup, strawberries, blueberries). My selection was pretty satisfying and hit the spot. My friend went for the country breakfast which is an impressive assortment of food (biscuits, scrambled eggs, bacon, sausage) and all of it tasted fantastic! If anything stood out to me, I'd have to vote on the biscuits-- super tasty! I skipped on the drinks and had their iced coffee instead, which I had no complaints with. I would recommend this for brunch if you're in the area. I've yet to sample it for drinks, but one of these nights I'll definitely make that happen.

I love this place! Â On Tuesday nights, all apps are 1/2 priced. Yea! Â Try the coconut mojito and opt for the flakes on top - absolutely delicious and dangerous at the same time. Â The fish tacos are amazing and so are the ribs. Â Try the chips, guac & salsa basket - they give you a variety of different chips and the guac is some of the best I've ever had! Â  Strong drinks, solid food.
A taco joint that succeeded in eschewing the one grand redeeming quality of all Mexican restaurants: festivity.

Initial impression of Public is one of simplistic awe. The decor is minimal yet it catches your attention in so many ways. From the red brick walls to the asian style plants, I was unable to tell what kind of cuisine this place was really trying to get across. I guess the "food without borders" tagline that Public presents is really true. After my inital glance of the menu there were american style salads, asian influences, indian spices and much more. We started with the steamed edamame which was sprinkled with small strips of sea salt as well as some melted butter. The butter on the edame caught me off guard right away as the sweet and the salty flavor combination was not one that I usually associate with edamame. I found myself eating the ones on the outside of the bowl which had less butter on them which is similar to what I do at a movie theater when a friend orders popcorn with that faux butter. I guess that analogy is somewhat telling of my feelings toward it. Â  For my appetizer I ordered the grilled scallops which had a sweet chili sauce and some plantains to accompany the scallops. My initial bite of the scallop was one of confusion. It had a nice grilled outside and seemed cooked throughout yet had a mild fishy flavor which was something I could definitely taste but didn't detract me from eating on. The 2nd scallop didn't have this flavor at all and tasted wonderful. Also, the creme fraiche and sweet chili added some nice flavors when dipping the scallops in. For my main course I ordered the roast lamb over goat cheese polenta. The roasted lamb was cooked to perfection and when you add the crispyness of the goat cheese polenta, the texture of the crunchy and tender was a perfect combination. I would recommend this restaurant to those on dates as the drink list is full of fun cocktails as well as an efficient staff. Although my waiter was a tad rude, he got us our food in time, took away our plates when finished and made sure the meal flowed smoothly. I would definitely go back.

We went on a rainy Sunday evening, so there was no wait. Also no corking fee on Sundays - go there then! We got the grilled saucisson for an appetizer, the pissaladiere (basically a pizza on puff pastry), and the bouchee a la reine (chicken, mushrooms, quenelles,and cream sauce in a puff). Generally speaking, the food was okay. Good enough, but not amazing. The new potatoes that came with the grilled saucisson were heavenly though-sweet, lemony, buttery, with a perfect texture. Felt kind of rushed by the service (definitely the opposite of France) but, altogether, a cute spot for a date in the West Village - maybe brunch is better.
Yes. It IS crowded, expensive, overwhelming. But it is also amazing, having everything you could ask for, and more. A feast for the senses and the belly.

I like their food, the ingredient is fresh and good. Â But extremely overprice!! Â Two of us girls, only order one soda each, no special wagyu beef or live seafood, except regular shrimps, the bill comes out to be $110!! Â I usually go to Flushing for hotpot, even Little lamb or Little sheep only cost about $40 ppl. (no alcohol). Â For the extreme high price, I expect a lot more. Â  Also, the place is really small, and you will probably bump into someone you know if you live in Bklyn. Â And that makes no privacy if you want to talk to your friends. Â I guess this is one of the very popular place in Bklyn, therefore you will need a reservation for Fri and wkd. Â  Just to be fair, the food is good, just the pricing and lack of privacy is something that turns me off.

florence fabricant put it best: Do or Dine, or Don't. We weren't allowed to bring in beer on Monday, I guess they got raided over the weekend. Â  The best thing we ate was the nippon nachos, easily duplicated at home. I resent the self conception that this place seems to have, that they're so audacious and irreverent that it doesn't actually have to be... delicious? Â For example, there were arbitrary black sesame seeds in our otherwise normal root beer floats. Â The texture was really annoying and they contributed nothing to the flavor. Â Why not take the conception of this dish ONE logical step further, and use black sesame ice cream? Â That would be totally delicious, you could buy the ice cream from the Chinatown ice Cream Factory, which everyone adores, easy, a fun twist on a classic dessert drink. Â But their execution, in this case and others, wasn't pushed far enough, and the results were sloppy. Â  the space was cute, but even if it was byob again, i can't imagine going back.

One of my favorite restaurant's in the city! Â Indoor/outdoor garden is beautiful. Â Food is lovely. Â A hidden gem in the heart of the Villge. Â I've been eating here for years and it remains one of my all time favorites. Â My personal favorites- the Lamb chops or the homemade Gnocchi. They recently added a new place next door called Aperitivo...just as quaint and comfortable- here you can get tasty bites and wine out of beautiful etched glasses. Â  I feel like I'm at home every time I visit.

this place makes you want to be Caulky MacCaucasian--all Cape Cod-dy, white pants, silver coffee mug, fleece, volvo, loafers/new balance, and mayonaise to put on everything including the family labrador! this place is blue, not as in depressed like the little paxil cloud. the interior is pale blue. it's a small space not a ton of tables. it has a very warm/coolish-by-the-ocean feel to it. the food is comforting without being overly heavily. it very much has a pacifying feel to it but not in one of those con artist Â holistic mumbo jumbo ways. this is the real deal. i have had dinner and brunch here a bunch. chicken meatballs, mac-n-cheese (white cheese, i believe--nothing like the chester cheetos ORANGE about this pasta and fromage), artichoke dip, etc. are in perfect portions and very delicious, especially the chicken meatballs with pesto! the curry chicken salad is badass, but may not be everyone's cup of chai tea. grilled cheese, the BLT, and the chicken meatball sub on a baguette is rockin'. the red velvet cake and cookies-n-milk are nice ways to sweeten the ending moments of your dinner. this place is good for a light dinner date and it can accomodate a fairly large group of 6 people at some tables. the theme to this restaurant should be: "Blue his house With a blue little window And a blue corvette And everything is blue for him And his self And everybody around 'Cause he ain't got nobody to listen... I'm blue, da ba de, da ba die Da ba de, da ba die"
I absolutely love the atmosphere here and even though there was a wait it was so worth it. So many great options to choose from but any choice is a good one!

Have you ever had a secret desire to have a nice meal served to you and then when you are finished you go into the next room and join 500 people for a top-rated Broadway show? Â Well, that is pretty close to what you get at Trattoria Trecolori, assuming that the Brooks Atkinson theater next door (literally) is running a show you want to see. At present, the play happens to be "After Midnight," but this is a restaurant review so let's get back to the subject at hand. Trattoria Trecolori has the look and feel of a neighborhood restaurant despite being set in the heart of the tourist-heavy Broadway theatre district. Â We arrived at 6:30 PM on a Friday night and the the place was packed. The first level was boisterous with a happy crowd at the bar in the front and diners at all of the tables in the back. Reservations are a really good idea but don't look for any of the fancy internet tools. This place is old school. You call, they take your name, time, number of diners and that's it. Â You show up and the guy who meets you has a little notepad with a list of names written down. We were whisked upstairs to the second floor dining area--noise level moderate here-and a waiter arrived almost immediately to take drink orders. Â Service at this establishment was superb. Â There was no delay at any point. Water glasses constantly filled, requests handled promptly, friendly attitude, Â everything you could ask for. Â And even though you are not constantly bothered by a staff person asking if everything is OK, the waiter seemed able to be there whenever you needed something. They had no specials, which is fine. Â We were looking for a nice Â meal, nothing extraordinary. Â They have all of the Classic Italian dishes you would expect. Â I ordered the veal piccata and my wife had chicken parmesan. Â The included side order of vegetables were fresh and very good as were both entrees. Â We shared a mixed green salad--also good--and the house Sauvignon blanc by the glass which had a nice fresh, crisp taste. Â The portions were generous so we skipped dessert and ended with a cappuccino and espresso. In sum, an enjoyable dinner, superb service, and reasonable (in New York City) prices.

Came here for a nice lunch, came out with a question mark over my head. The portions were so small that I left hungry. I ordered the market fish (sea bass special, seared filet) and it came with a sad plate of wilted greens. I recommend ordering the whole fish because you get more for the price! Next time I should stick to the pastas. The only cool bonus was that Mario Batali was filming in the back of the restaurant with a few Top Chef folks and I got to make eye contact with him, haha.

I can't say enough good things about BarBacon! We found this place while heading to another, but when you see a place with BACON in the name you stop and go in! I enjoyed everything about BarBacon...they encourage you to upload your pics to instagram using their hashtag #BarBacon (which to me shows they are confident in the quality of what they are serving b/c they are telling you to post it), they are trendy but not too much so that you feel out of place (it's very comfortable and inviting inside) and the service was great (the bartender was informative about the beer selections they had and the bacon options available). Yep they not only offer food with bacon, they also have options where bacon is the star! We were instantly drawn to the flight option - $20 for 4 5oz pours of beer and 4 (2 slices each) types of bacon (we had applewood, pecan smoked, peppered and jalapeno)!!!! Trust me when I say you will not be disappointed when trying out this place, even if it's just for a quick pop in like us!

I die. Yes, this place is crazy busy. If you don't like large crowds of loud, happy people enjoying every kind of imported Italian good you never imagined, then don't come here; stay in your cave. I would love to do my regular shopping here, and you technically could, because they have all the basics a regular grocery store does. However, seeing as I am less than fabulously wealthy, I come mostly to have a snack, browse, or buy things like bread (try the semolina baguette), meat for special occasion meals, harder-to-find items, and good quality olive oil (they have a great selection with a range of prices). You'll also find amazing fresh and dry pasta, cheeses (don't buy it here unle$$ you can't find it elsewhere), chocolates, beverages, cookbooks, and housewares. There are niche restaurants (each focuses on a different item, like fish, vegetables, etc.) nestled in various nooks, as well as a few in the center of everything. Great place for a third date; too noisy for a 1st or 2nd.
Not much to say... it doesn't get cheaper or better than this. Â 5 dumplings for a buck. Â Walk in, order your dumplings and get out.

I rarely use yelp,but my experience was pretty jarring. This hurts to write, but it's too gross to ignore. Five Leaves food is pretty good I will say that. Here's what happened- I was sitting in the big booth near the back and as I got up after eating I saw a bedbug crawling along the seat. I tried to quietly summon a server but they were all too busy, and I didn't want to make a big deal and freak everyone out. I know there are some things that you can't control, but they need to clean up a little better or something. I don't want to end up with bedbugs burrowing into my jacket and then bring them into my apartment from eating at what I'd assumed was a clean restaurant. As a precaution I washed and dried everything i was wearing including my jacket. I suggest eating outside to be safe.

Such a great place for an after-work happy hour. The drinks are cheap (beers are $4, specialty drinks maybe $6). The bartender is really nice and you can tell it's just the kind of place locals come year round.

Generous portions. Nice ambience. Clean bathroom. Service was fine though we had to ask the waitress several times to be seated. Once seated things moved great. I am not a fine taster of sushi, so all I can say was that the salmon, tuna, and spicy tuna all tasted different. And I was full on the Triple Roll option 3x8 pieces for $12).

Tia Pol is very wonderful in small ways...other than the big wait. Our party of four arrived at 6:30 and was told it would be a 45 minute wait. Â This turned into an hour wait and we were finally seated after an hour and 10 minutes. Â Other than that, this restaurant is great for small groups. Â The tapas is absolutely amazing and tasty as was the pitcher of sangria. Â We ordered the spicy rough cut potatoes (so good that we ordered a second round afterwards), the sherry chorizo (again, second round), the skirt steak special, monk fish cheek special, the tomacat trio dip with baguettes, and ham croquettes. All were delicious -- recommendations are the croquettes, chorizo and potatoes.. as evident by our second orders. Â The wine list is long and obviously Spanish themed. Â The bartender and waiter were attentive as could be. Â  The space is romantic and dark, perfect for date night. Â There is a room in the back of the restaurant with two long bench tables if for larger parties but other than that, most of the tables are 2 or 3 tops. Â Ensure you come early to avoid the wait! Â Just come hungry.

THIS GUY IS A LEGEND!!!! Â This place is a tiny whole in the wall, and when you arrive be prepared to wait at least 2 hours for a pie. But you can not be restless waiting... each pie is perfection and one of his masterpieces, so do not rush the artist, because it's his kitchen and you are just welcome to watch and admire true passion and perfection. This was a MUST on our Brooklyn day, and we are so happy we made it there!!!

Just have to say that if you're aching for some Japanese curry and you want the real thing... this is a great place to get it. Â I walked in, was out with my bowl of katsu-curry in five minutes, and have loved every bite of it. The store has an amazing katsudon smell, too. Â  Katsu-hama gave me just what I needed! A teeny bit pricy for what it is, though.

Came here for dinner after work on a Friday night. Â THey had a nice jazz band setting up in the bar area and generally the place had a lovely dark, intimate feel to it. Â  I ordereded the fish special of the day (branzini) which came with an excellent red cabbage and goat cheese special. Â  Â  The food was pretty good - and the wine was excellent. Â  Great place to catch up with a friend or have a date. Â Ambiance is really nice. Â I would go back just to have drinks by the bar area.

Honestly Anthony & Son never fails to dissapoint ! Their maspeth location has tables and some of the best pastries. The Matt and Steve special is out of this world and highly reccomend you give it a shot

They really deserve five stars but it came down one star after last night. My roomie and I dined here last night. We were both really hungry and ordered with our eyes like usual. We had delicious fried oysters on a shell with a bed of cole slaw. We also tried the fried calamari with homemade marinara. I liked it a lot but the sauce was missing an ingredient I couldn't quiet point out. I ordered a New England clam chowder which was creamy and not too rich which I enjoyed. She ordered the Lobster Mac and Cheese. She only enjoyed the lobster from it, but the mac and cheese part had a little too much flour to cheese ratio so it made it really sticky and not pleasant. I should have stopped after all that food but I had to try their famous Connecticut style lobster rolls. The bartender or kitchen Â brought over the New England which I would have and should have gladly devoured. Ended up waiting 20 mins for them to boil a new lobster and by the time I received it, it tasted rubbery like they boiled it too long. The salad on the side tasted fishy. I really didn't want to complain or make them fix my order again so I just ate it. Kinda felt ill after I did that. Even if it was cooked properly I don't think I can enjoy eating a warm/hot fleshy lobster roll. I'll stick with Luke's Lobster Rolls forever. So far nothing has beat the authenticity of those! Glad I tried this place though. It's close enough proximity to me ill be back!

Crepes were delicious! I had the chicken asparagus crepe and the chicks was very nicely flavored. My fiancÃ© had the banana Nutella crepe and loved it. The coffee had a nice taste as well. It is a cute restaurant and service was very fast. Very close to the Staten Island ferry terminal. Will like to visit again next time we are in town.

Mark's slider is second to Minetta Tavern's Black Label Burger because I broke a 1 year bet on this burger. I lasted seven months without meat burgers and broke my fast on this baby. I'm not quite sure if that should be sadness or happiness but I'll sway to the latter. Big thanks to Philip N for screening and approving all of my St. Mark's bites this evening. He really knows his food and will not disappoint you. I am happy to have such great friends IRL and it's nice when they cross over into Yelp. The shakes at Mark sound good. Salted Caramel or Strawberry your thing? Yes, mine too. Then again, I rarely decline a shake. Cheap but really decent beer is on the menu. It's St. Mark's! This street will not rip you off! All orders should also include fries. They are perfectly crispy without going hollow in the middle. Best part of Mark other than the sliders? Spicy dipping sauces!! Hello!
Great food.

This place lives up to its good ratings. The well done burger I had with Cheddar cheese was delicious. The place was really nice inside. The waiter was attentive and pleasant. The German beer I had was perfect. My friend and I went for a late lunch on a weekday so I am not sure how they handle crowds. I would definitely come back.
Outstanding food and service, but a bit pretentious in the way that really good restaurants shouldn't be. Â Not overly pompous, but just a shade precious. But the food itself is amazing.

Love how a nonna is making my meal, with her family recipes!... sure Staten Island is out of the way, but the ferry ride is pleasant and this place is soooo worth it. I had nonna Adelena's food the other night, made us want to walk over and give her a big hug and kiss! my friend said he wants to marry someone who can cook like her! LOL good luck to him. There are 6 different nonnas cooking on dif nights. Food is great and prices are very reasonable. Plus you get complimentary homemande focaccia. Go sit down at nonna's table and have an amazing meal will ya!?... for more reviews, please visit my blog,

Belgian beer bar with a questionable croque monsieur -- the bread not toasty enough, the bechamel too lightly applied -- but spot-on moules frites. Six or so different mussels preps, but it's hard to go wrong with the classic white wine broth. And very good fries, too, which show up in another satisfying take on a classic, steak frites. The meat could be more tender, but it bursts with beefy flavor. A nice low-key option for brunch or dinner. Probability of return within 1 year: 60% (this capsule review is courtesy of my July "short and sweet in the summer" initiative)

Nice place. I came here with a friend on a Sunday around 7pm and the place was busy but not crowded. We ordered the Thai Curry Lobster Tortellini and it was soooo good. You only get 4 for $12, but it is lobster so that's not really shocking. The curry isn't particularly strong or Thai, but the whole thing is delicious nonetheless. The burgers were also delicious. Flavorful and perfectly cooked, with crispy bacon and tasty fries. The craft beer selection is awesome. I fell in love with this smoked wheat beer, Barrier le Pete. The space is really big for a bar in NYC. The bar is double sided, separated by a wall, with a back room and possibly a downstairs or upstairs room, maybe for events. I will definitely be back :)

Ate: Gambas, Cod wrapped with potato, pork loin, chorizo Drank: Sangria Liked: Gambas were good. Â Cute space and very authentic. Disliked: Music was too loud and we were trying to talk. Â Not their fault, but wasn't our speed. Sangria was weak. Chicken: None! Â Chicken haters would love this place! Would mom like it?: Â Mom would go up and try to dance with them to all of our embarrassment. Would I go back: Yes, on a night without the live music. Recommend: Gambas Al Ajillo. Â That's like the calamri of Tapas places. Â And I love it.

Just as cute and cozy and teensy and romantic as you would have imagined and hoped for. There's something about the scale and pace of Wallflower that serves as an antidote to daily life in the city. It's everything not coming at you, not pulling you and pushing you, not overwhelming you or assaulting your senses. Just letting you be. Letting you enjoy a cocktail, a low volume, a warm space, a nice meal, and the person you're with.

Authentic and spicy Thai. Not the cheapest but won't break the bank. Lots of fresh ingredients (herbs, etc). Seems to have lost a 1/2 step in the years I've been going there but maybe this is just me getting finicky. You must try the soft shell crab w green mango salad and drunken noodles with ground pork (eat this immediately as the pork get's more and more chewy the more it cools). Oh, and the service is definitely a bit sketchy but not too bad.

This place stinks up my end of Red Hook with nasty fried seafood and boiled crabs smells. The owners should be fined for not putting in a better exhaust system. The smell is downright offensive sometimes. Additionally, it's totally overpriced. The food is completely mediocre, and the decor is so cheesy. I can't believe people still flock to this place.
cant ask for anything more incredible food, amazing and talented creator, perfect ambience

Amazing new restaurant! We held a company party there in december - was just awesome. Really tasty food, great wine and drinks - and we love the feeling in the space. Beautiful decorations - many of which the owners made themselves. We loved the zinc bar and the hand made doors to the wine cave upstairs. Highly recommend.

1 red white and blue special, 1/4 lb shrimp cocktail, king crab app, 2 11/4 lb lobsters, corn on the cob, mashed potato's covered in lobster bisque, 3 glasses of wine and 3 stella's. $117. Â 2 very happy people.

I absolutely love this place! It's fresh and puts ANY other fried chicken to shame. Â I had never eaten organic, healthy and chemical free chicken until I went to Soco and its a huge difference compared to that greasy fast food. Â Can't wait to go there again! mmmmmm
Absolutely amazing meal. We had the papaya salad, lamb curry and the avacado semifreddo with macademia nuts. This is easily my favorite place in the neighborhood. Also, a great spot for date night!

Being a Filipino myself, I would always be critical of a Filipino-style restaurant and luckily for Ugly Kitchen, I can say this a great spot to eat and hangout! Â  The place itself isn't too big, but there is a bar in the middle that takes up a decent amount of the place. Â Even though the place isn't big, I felt content being inside, and they also had a good variety of music playing. As for the food, I tried the spicy pork buns and ugly dumplings appetizers. Â I personally like the ugly dumplings (inside has cheese and tomatoes) more due to the crispiness and even though the pork buns were good, I am spoiled by trying pork buns from other places. For the main course, I got the Sizzling Tuna Belly. Â I feel you get a nice generous portion so if you are craving tuna, this is a definitely win. Â What I'll say though is that I tried bits and pieces of food from other friends in my party and felt they were much better. Â Their sizzling sisig was very good (contains minced pork belly, liver, and cheek with onions, soy sauce and topped with an egg that they mix). Â I also liked their Fried Isaw platter, which is just fried pork ruffle with soy sauce and vinegar, a classic way Filipinos eat pork. Â I couldn't go wrong eating the Lechon Kawali too (cripsy pork belly). Â I'll say though that I KNOW eating all this pork is not good for my health, but hey, it tastes GOOD! Overall, I liked the atmosphere here and would definitely come back to try their other dishes like their beef platters and of course.. their Cripsy Pata, which is pretty much fried pork.. and heart attack waiting to happen!
Some of the best family style Italian food I have ever had. Â You have to try the lemon butter chicken!

I will preface this by saying we went for restaurant week. Â Perhaps going to this restaurant for lunch during restaurant week had something to do with the less than lackluster service and meal we received. Â I reviewed the menu before making the reservation. Â I am a vegetarian and assumed that this restaurant offers a veggie option -- as most do and went. Service -- upon asking the waitress for a veggie option she shared that they really don't have anything on the restaurant week menu and that i could order from the regular menu. Â After a bit of back and forth -- that I thought was absolutely unnecessary -- she finally asked if there was a veggie dish avail. Â Once she confirmed there was -- I went with the prix fixe meal. Â The mushroom soup was a nice way to start the meal -- it was flavorful, good texture etc. Â The 2nd course was pasta + sauce. Â A less-than inspired rendition of chef boyardee. Â What I received could've been done Â with Prego and noodles at home. Â Finally the dessert -- Â Tiramisu -- m'eh. If you're in the neighborhood and want to take advantage of restaurant week -- go elsewhere.
service was very nice i dont know if the price and quality were worth it I will give them one more chance for brunch

Stumbled in with the boy one morning (2pm) on a whim (okay, we were tired of walking and trying to decide on a place to eat). It looked okay. Another average city eatery. Ordered one of the "Fancy Cocktails", the Hungry Teacher (a strange drink to have to order out loud) and it was very good. The food came and I was pleasantly surprised. Very good. I had breakfast, he had a sandwich, both were just as good as the other. As I read through these reviews I keep seeing "consistent" come up over and over again. I couldn't agree more. We came back a few weeks later, both ordered different things off the menu, and again were impressed. This place isn't trying to be anything more than it is. It's an American, no frills, comfortable restaurant, but it does what it does very well. Decent price, really tasty food, great drinks, totally worth checking out.

This place is amazing. Me and boyfriend come here literally 1-2 every week. Either for brunch or lunch. It delicious! The food here is always fresh. The market sides and salads are always great, but if you come here on a weekend brunch def try to breakfast burrito! And their pumpkin pie is to die for. Although I think they only have it in the fall.

Not much I can add...delicious food (had the Cioppino and Corn/Crab Chowder) served by a friendly, helpful staff in cozy locale to boot. They have whole fish here; that is, you get a whole damn fish (!) then filet it yourself. C'est magnifique.

I took my family here for my graduation dinner and out of all the restaurants we went to during their stay in NYC (La Sirene, Caracas Arepas Bar, Alta, & Balaboosta) this was by far their favorite. They kept ranting about how good the hangar steak was. I, on the other hand, trusted yelp and ordered the gnocchi...which was ok. It's not Lupa. I just now know I'm not a big gnocchi person. (It tastes kind of like an Italian "mien ge da.") BUT they did have the BEST panna cotta I've ever eaten in my life! Delicate and flavorful. GO. And good luck with reservations.

I ordered wonton lo mein and congee with preserved egg. The congee was really good but I couldn't say the same for the lo mein. The wontons by themselves were marvelous but the lo mein was just noodles that tasted like it was bathed in chlorine. Plus, I was expecting the lo mein to be actual lo mein not just plain yellow noodles with a little sprinkle of sauce. I could NOT take another bite. On an earlier day, I ordered wonton noodle soup and it was horrendous. The soup was a whole separate taste aside from the noodles. If I compare the wonton lo mein and the wonton noodle soup, the lo mein was the exact same thing just without the soup. Never ordering noodles from this place ever again. It was not good for my tastebuds nor my stomach. I am very displeased. I have yet tried their other dishes but two out of two experiences were bad so no thanks.

I read the review in TONY a while back and decided I had to get there ASAP. It was worth the trek to and fro on the Williamsburg Bridge. The size alone is worth the venture. You get a mouthful of delicious steamy goodness with each one, whether it be the pork or the steamed vegetable. It's a good place to stop by when courting any out-of-towners looking for a cheap spot to eat. At 5 dumplings for $1, it's the best deal you're going to get.

I love this place. Food is great. Wine is inexpensive. Service is fabulous. It is tiny, you may share a table with others and you have to squeeze behind the cook to get to the bathroom: I think those things make me love this place even more. Food here is for sharing, flavor full and interesting: Delicious!

Try CDG. You won't go back to BCD tofu. The side dishes here are amazing. It's a bit off the beaten path of korean restaurants (on 35th instead of 32nd) but definitely a hidden gem with little to no wait times.

You seriously question several times where the eff you are, but as soon as that sweet saucy, hidden cheesy, 12 slices of heavenly Sicilian style pie comes out, at first bite, you're planning your return visit. And order that big ass dessert thing with all the shit. They will totally know what you're talking about when you order it that way. Don't eat the blue stuff! Dig right on to the Spumoni center tower.

Indian cuisine is not an area I would consider myself even close to knowledgable in, but when Pippali quietly opened in the Flatiron, "Curry Hill" area of Manhattan, the consistent positive feedback eventually led to further research on the restaurant. Pippali opened under the oversight of Chef Peter Beck, who spent time at Benares and Michelin-starred Tamarind, before he decided to open a place of his own. And when a restaurant is named after a pepper (also known as Javanese, the "Indian long pepper"), how could I not make a visit? The four of us arrived at the restaurant on a weekday evening after work, and were seated at a four-top towards the back of the dining room. The entire venue is pretty enclosed as it's situated underground, but is adequately spaced with several rows of tables to keep the room organized. Although it was only half full at that time, every table was filled by the end of the night, making for a clamorous dining environment. It's far from the ideal location for an intimate conversation, so be prepared or arrive at an earlier hour to avoid the crowds. One of my friends was more familiar with the cuisine so we defaulted most of the decision making to her, as well as the choice to serve everything family style. In due time, our appetizers made our way over. The Sungta Kismuri, a dish comprised of pan-grilled shrimp served over a lentil-rice pancake. The shrimp were plump and juicy, cooked to just the right tenderness, and seasoned well. They were complimented by the masala-onion sauce, but the slight soggyness of the pancake was the one thing that detracted from the overall execution. The Gose Sadhi, presented almost like a soup, was a complex layering of coconut, chili, and garlic flavors, while the cabbage and black-eyed peas added some much-needed texture to the dish. The choice of entrees at Pippali is even more vast, so we had a harder time narrowing it down to two dishes. The Subz Tikka Masala featured submerged slices of tandoor-grilled soya (a meat substitute) in the familiar fenugreek tomato sauce. The flavors were spot-on, a balance of savory, sweet and acidic, with just a hint of spice and the addition of cauliflower, broccoli, and bell peppers helped amplify the dish. The Bihari Gohst, on the other hand, was a carnivore's delight: an entire lamb shank braised in a rich, full-bodied curry sauce. The lamb, fall-off-the-bone tender, had a faint edge of gameyness and had soaked in plenty of flavor from the curry. With the addition of onion and tomato chunks, it made for one of the most satisfying and aromatic plates of the night. While I can claim nothing about the authenticity of the food served at Pippali (besides what my Indian coworker assures me is as close to the original that's she's had), from what I've tried, everything served here demonstrates a great deal of care and attention to detail put into each plate. Portions are generous and prices are more than reasonable, making it a viable option to put on regular rotation. I'd return to try an even greater variety of dishes and to see just how generous the kitchen can be with the spice; after all, why else would you name a restaurant after one?

I've never had a bad meal or a bad time here. The place puts just right the spin on hip. You always feel like you're just where you want to be when you're here. The service is professional, friendly, on point. The food is straightforwardly American and really really good. The burger, fried chicken, fried green beans are all done to a turn. The crab artichoke dip will have you fighting over who gets to lick the bowl. I just really like this place.

Good solid food for the price. The Calamari appetizer was a bit chewy for my taste, but the opening bread basket, complimentary Caesar salad, and excellent service were all components of providing a great value. My sea bass entree was very good, and the cheese cake was great.

Catered a casual supper for 45 people, Fried chicken, greens, mac and cheese and peach cobbler. Â Sharon in the catering department was amazingly helpful with the menu and planning. Â The food was a HUGE hit. Â The chicken delightfully crisp and tender, the greens flavorful, the mac an cheese addicting and the cobbler sweet and delicious. Â We are new to the neighborhood and will be regular customers.

The Italians don't "Just do it" - they do it with style, flair, and imagination. They have the ability to transform the mundane into something that makes you sit up and take notice. I usually read with interest all the listings under 'Hot on Yelp', even though in this regard, I personally am a manifestation of what the economists call the Free rider problem. How so? Well, Neanderthal that I am, I don't believe in having bookmarks. That's right! I don't have a SINGLE bookmark on yelp (gasp). Hey! I still believe in exercising the mental faculties of storage and retrieval, you know :) Honestly, when I saw Via Quadronno as one of yelp's top picks and skimmed all the rave reviews about "life changing Panini", I merely yawned at the hyperbole. But once "East Side hater" Sam P added to the chorus that he could consider moving (!!!) to the UES "just to be in walking distance", I HAD to see for myself what the fuss was all about. I'll admit that it took me some time to understand the menu of options, for there were cuts and cheeses that I had never even heard of! But, dear lord, this Milanese Paninoteca (with other locations in Tokyo, Hong Kong, and Florida) undoubtedly serves the best Panini in the city. How they are able to bring together six different ingredients masterfully, while accentuating the amazing bread, is something that blows me away each and every time. Though, I must warn the vegetarians that ham appears to be the area of expertise and available options outside of this remain few. Nevertheless for Panini aficionados, this place is pure bliss. As I relax and savor the experience, my mind's eye is transported to the magic of Italia. One can't help but marvel how the simple sandwich, which is an ode to convenience and speed at your corner deli, is elevated here to a gastronomical delight. VQ also serves one of the best cups of cappuccino in New York, with as much foamy goodness as one can expect. Even though I prefer thicker crema than that at VQ, I do appreciate the quality of the espresso with beans sourced from Antica Tostatura Triestina which has a proud heritage of exporting roasted coffee worldwide. VQ has earlier been awarded many accolades for their coffee ("Best Espresso in NYC") and while the honor probably now belongs to Ninth Street Espresso, VQ deserves honorable mention in the premier NYC exponents of this art. Sadly, I haven't been as impressed with the desserts in terms of both quality and selection. The traditional Tiramisu is as tired a version as one can find in the city, and once the novelty of the deconstructed Tiramisu di San Dona wears off, the menu has little to offer. I wasn't impressed with any of the cakes I tried: Campagnola (rustic cake with Apple and Raisin) or Coffee. While the 28 flavors of gelato are highly touted, I have been unable to sample any of them in my three visits here. I could care less about the crowd. During the day you have the share of Madison Avenue power brokers, ladies who lunch, European tourists, as well as the Gossip Girls. Yes, Snooties! I heard you the first time when you mentioned that you spent ONLY $3,500 on that fab dress you're going to wear for that boring wedding. Now, if only wit, charm, and intelligence came with a price tag!!
Great food and atmosphere at this place. Highly recommended if you need a good cup of coffee and to get some work done in a quiet atmosphere!

PROS: Food was Awesome!!! With a capital "A." Spicy chili tofu and bean noodles were ordered (two different dishes) and both were great. The food is definitely 5+ starts. Also, the chai is outstanding!! GET IT! CONS: It was a little small and had a health rating of B. I am a vegetarian so this did not concern me as much...but it is a bit of a con. To be fair, many chains get a B like subway, but still. Also, the service was only three stars. When thinking about this food, imagine Chinese mixed with Indian. If you like this concept, go for it!

I love Eataly. I actually didn't know that it was a Batali partner owned eatery/market, but now that I know, it makes sense. The reason I'm not giving it a full 5 stars is because I haven't tried the pasta/seafood eats here. I've only eaten at the meat bar, where I've had the freshest and most delightful prosciutto de parma that my mouth has ever had the pleasure of tasting. It is quite unbelievable. My favorite thing is to get the formaggi e salumi platter, which is $22, and comes with a variety of 4-5 cheeses, and 4-5 cured meats. It is great for sharing, and pairs well with a crisp and chilled glass of Flor prosecco. The bread is fresh and thick, and the special platter comes with honey, marmalade, and another sweet complement. The parmesan reggiano is lovely, and the ricotta is smooth and mild. I come here often to satisfy my prosciutto craving, and I recommend it to anyone looking for a great meal in an interesting setting. Highly recommended. Weekends are very crowded, I'd come here on the weekdays. Service is is kind and good. Will be back again and again.

I read a bunch of reviews about Grimaldi's and finally got the chance to go. Located under the Brooklyn Bridge sits the famous pizza place. Â This is a pretty awesome site to see and I recommend anyone visiting the are to go here just to be down by the Brooklyn Bridge and see this area. Â It is very cool. Â Grimaldi's isn't very big, but they have packed a ton of tables into this place so everyone is packed in. The pizza was fantastic, it was fresh and had great flavor. Â This is some of the best pizza I have had in NYC and it is at the top of a lot of "top pizza in the country" lists and such. This is a must visit, and I am glad I was able to go to the famous Grimaldi's pizza.

One of the few eating establishments in the NYC area that can be truly considered a "panty dropper". Seriously, if you want to score some serious "smush time" points make sure you take your date to Traif to wine and dine her or him. After an amazing meal here if you can't "get some" then you would have a hard time scoring in a whorehouse with a fist full of hundreds. It has been a while since we dined at this wonderful restaurant but I just realized I never reviewed it, so here we are at #1900, and it's truly fitting for a milestone review! What I remember most is, um, let me think.......EVERYTHING!!! Totally amazing food, top notch service, delicious cocktails - it's the total package! Five stars all the way. Throughout the night even the 80's new wave music was on point. I was in awe as everything that I placed in my ravenous mouth was just perfect. Started with a cocktail - the violet beauregard - blueberry infused bourbon (Whoa!), beet salad (YUM!), meaty juicy strawberry cinnamon glazed ribs (OMG!), succulent BBQ braised short rib sliders with sweet potato fries (YOWZA!), and bacon donuts with ice cream (NOM!!!) were all just ridiculous. Traif straddles the line between casual and upscale. It's a perfect spot to impress a hot date, special event, or for some friends to get together and enjoy conversation over a fantastic meal and cocktails. The staff are friendly, competent, knowledgeable, and go out of their way to make sure you have a truly enjoyable dining experience here. Even the prices are reasonable and affordable for the quality of food and service you receive. The menu is eclectic with something for everyone's palate. Even though small the cocktail list and craft beer selection are terrific. How can anyone not like this place? If you can't enjoy a night out at Traif then you might need to check your pulse, and your taste buds. Boom-chicka-bow-wow!

This place hits the nail on the head for food, service and price! I came here on a Monday night and luckily two people were just leaving the bar so my boyfriend and I were seated immediately. I recommend sitting at the bar since the bartenders will help you pick the perfect beer with sampling and suggestions! We ordered a dozen oysters and all were tasty. The Long Island jumbos were seriously jumbo. We couldn't eat one because it was so huge. I'll pick a different oyster next time! We also had the crab cakes which were perfectly fried and paired with a tangy arugula salad. It was nice they weren't doused in mayo which is the norm. Also had the salmon tartar--highly recommend this! It came with toasted baguette slices and was dressed in a mustardy Asian sauce--sauce was very light. For the entree we split the scallop and shrimp dish. There were only two scallops and one shrimp which is a bit small for an entree but with three starters we were pretty full. When we left we said we want to come back here more often. Next on the list is the clams and pasta and the squid salad! I think the way to go here is to share everything-that way you can try it all!

Completely addicted to everything here. I have to have their orange at least once a month and my boyfriend has religiously eaten the tender muscles for 20 years. Love the pork n shrimp dumpling. Nice smokey taste. Staff us friendly and honestly just there to do their job. They may not smile often but attentive for the most part. We are regulars so we have maybe grown on them and they joke around with my kids.

I would probably give 3.5 stars. This place has a cute vibe and the service was fantastic. Â That being said, for the 40 minute wait, I wish the food had been a bit better. It was definitely tasty, but nothing spectacular. (perhaps just too bland?)

Went here during a quick biz trip to NYC. Service was attentive and the food was decent. It was the first time I had Venezuelan food of this type. I went in not knowing what arepas were and found out it's like a South American version of our burger...well sorta. Friends also ordered steak, and varias small dishes ranging from their cold octopus to grilled shrimp. Oh and they started us off with some dried banana chips and bean sauce. The sauce was awesome and they gave us more on request. There portions are a bit small for my liking, but I think it's quality food. If prices were a bit lower they'd get a 5.

Mark meets the mark on St. Mark's Pl. Â Totally catching the party vibe of the neighborhood, the interior is cute if not a bit intimate, although it's basically a burger and beer joint. Â But, even the "sliders" are relatively high play, and don't be fooled, their "sliders" are more like the size of a small burger... Â I way over-ordered. Â  The beer comes in overflowing pils glasses for not a lot of money. Â The skin-on fries had a surprisingly delicate quality for this more rustic preparation. Â And the 4 condiments including BBQ and jalapeno, were a great pairing. Â The chef was quite fun to chat with and clearly loved what he was doing. On my list for next time is the pecan pie and the Guinness milk shake... Â totally wild and creative idea. Â Burgers and fries aren't my usual fair, but this place made it feel worth it... Â so did our waitress Donna.

Whenever I'm not in the mood to try anything new that may disappoint me, I go to Big Wong. Â I love this place because their food quality can always be trusted upon. Â I can always count on Big Wong for a decent meal. Â It's also not too pricey here. Â  Although the food is good and the price is decent, their service is prettyyyy bad! Â I went to this place with about 6 friends (asian) and we shared a table with 3 non-asians (tourists). Â OMG, the waitress was UNBELIEVABLE! Â She came over to our table complimenting how 'handsome' the tourist couple's son looks and blah blah. Â We're just like ok... awkward.. And them she comes over to refill our cups.. or should I say THEIR CUPS. Â They filled up each and every cup of the tourists and left our cups empty. Â She looked at our cups and walked away! Â We got so pissed and decided to give them a crappy tip. Â Those waitresses there are so unfair and racist to their own people!

Holy truffle fries! Soo the bestie was in town, and wanted to get something "light" to eat after a long weekend of cocktail annihilation. So we decided to find something in Brooklyn and stumbled upon this place on yelp. I ordered the mushroom toast and the bestie got the granola with fruit and we split a plate of truffle fries...because it only makes sense, duh. The mushroom toast was good... however the cut of the toast was too thick (clearly I was too hungover to register that I DID order a toast dish, what the hell did I expect??) Soo yeah that was my own mistake. However, the dish overall was tasty but I wish there were more slices of mushroom in the sauce... but still good nonetheless. I tried the granola and that was amazing! They had a light and airy tasting whipped yogurt with a crunchy and not-too-chewy granola mix. It was perfect and very refreshing with the fruit on top. The truffle fries were perfectly fried.. with the right amount of truffle oil tossed to taste. Service was great, great atmosphere and very much enjoyed the food. Â I look forward to coming back to try the five leaves burger and the brunch menu on the weekends.

This place doesn't live up to the hype. I've had lots of different things on the menu. Went here with two other people and we shared appetizers, entrees and desserts. And while it's all very interesting and fun, you're over it after a couple of bites and ready to move on. Good food to me means loving the dish from start to finish. I like trying new things, but if the novelty wears off that fast and you have no desire to finish eating it, it's a thumbs down. That being said, all of their pork buns are great, so whenever I get a change to stop by for those, I certainly will. But as for a sit down dinner, I think we were all secretly wishing we had gone to a good old italian restaurant.

Employees Only makes fantastic cocktails. Best Pimm's Cup in NYC. Best drinks ever. I love this place, speakeasy schtick and all. I didn't think the drinks were any pricier than other lounge-type bars in the city - 13 or 15 bucks each? Pretty typical for Manhattan.

Excellent coffee, great french toast and at sandwich I'll be talking about for a long time (The penny breakfast sandwich). The pesto on it really does something! Atmosphere was very quant and had a great feel to it. Wait staff was very friendly and engaging! A spot to check out for sure!

Likes... The outdoor patio is nice for the summer Brooklyn nights. The atmosphere is social, lots of laughs, drinks and CORN!!! The food is descent... The drinks are great... Dislikes... Very small and seems to always be crowded... Can be a bit too noisey for me... The ordering process will take getting used to... Tables could've been cleaned better... The idea of security being there concerns me but I guess it's ok. Weekends are jammed packed, try and come as early as possible. Â Weekdays are crowded too, just with more families (tots & strollers)

I've never in my life had Ethiopian food before, so I had no idea what to expect or what to order. It was a bunch of us and we sat at this cozy big round table. Thank Jesus my friends ordered two huge plates, that I suppose had every dish on the menu, like a sample platter. We tried everything and there was not one dish that we haven't enjoyed. Everything was cooked and seasoned to perfection, and the injera bread kept on coming. Honey wine was like angel's nectar. The desserts almost killed us. That apple pie! OMG! The chocolate Creme BrÃ»lÃ©e! OMG! YUMMY YUMMY YUMMY Oh and the Ethiopian girl with the towel on her head (who served us) was stunning and so sweet. MUST GO!

One of my favorite places in NYC. Definitely worth the wait every time! Somehow, by the grace of God, we got a table for 4 on a Friday night at 7pm without a wait. Unreal! That is definitely not normal (I have gotten there before 6pm on a weekend and still waiting almost 2 hrs). Â There is an Irish bar around the street that you can go to if you want to wait. Anyway, the food is great. The pork buns are AMAZING, the samurai ribs are good, and all the ramen noodles are delicious. Â I have had the Miso Ramen and Akamaru Modern ramen - both very tasty and not too salty, which ramen noodles tend to be.

Second the bad bartender review. It's become abhorrently bad. One of them is just an outright nasty man. He'd be better off at Farrel's across the street. He just hates being there and hates everyone.
Laid back place with an unique williamsburg decor. Â Brisket, pullet pork, sausage are delisious but the pork belly is to die for. best bbq in brooklyn hands down.

You get no points for the bread, you only bought it. You get no points for The pork is "wet," not "moist" -- like eating tuna from a can without draining first. It's a good thing that it's small, or I'd feel worse about having to throw half of it away -- I had to wash my hands twice and chew three sticks of gum to get rid of the taste and smell of this thing. Maybe the other options are better; I'm not holding my breath (nor holding out my wallet).

I found the Hourglass Tavern online while looking for a place to have a work dinner that included some Vegan friendly menu items. I met with Beth and was very impressed by her dedication to our group and her attention to details. It made our evening a fabulous success! We felt like VIPs and everyone enjoyed their meal and the charming atmosphere. Our server and bartender, Scott, was wonderful. Thank you Beth and Scott, The Hourglass Tavern is certainly on my list of favorite places!

My husband and I ate here on Tuesday night of Thanksgiving week. We chose this restaurant based solely on Yelp Reviews. So, what can I say... Rather pedestrian is how I would describe our experience. My lamb chop was rather tasteless and barely warm. Glenn had the pasta special which he enjoyed but it hardly was a show-stopper. Service was satisfactory, wine was reasonable, the location very convenient. Would we go back... NO... too many other options to choose from..

A recent 10-day stint in Williamsburg had us dining at The Grand 3 times. Pretty damn good to get us back. Tuesday Taco Night did the deal. Smoked rabbit one Tuesday and duck confit the next. These were the best tacos I'd had in years - and good portion size. Other things that rock: Great service, oysters, Kotzritzer on tap, excellent pork ribs and mighty tasty Brussels sprouts. I did order a steak one night. It was underdone the first time around, sent back, another brought out but as with the first, it was tough and pretty tasteless. To their credit I was not charged (however; they did not ask what the problem was).

This place rocks! Their Quinoa and Summer Vegetable salad is awesome - totally filling and refreshing. My partner always gets the Panko Chicken Tenders, and the quality of the meat is really good. And the garlic mashed potatoes - to die for! And their customer service is fantastic - I had to work out a delivery issue, and they were totally accommodating. I will certainly continue ordering delivery from them and go to the restaurant. The delivery biker was sweet too and because of their wonderful service I felt more than happy to give an extra big tip.
If you ever leave anything behind (which was my sweater in this case), they tend to "throw it out" the next day. That was what I was told; that they found it but threw it out

Two gyros for $7 is pretty hard to beat, especially when they're this tasty! They aren't the best I've ever had, but the price makes up for that. One gyro filled me up, but if I were hungrier I'd definitely need one of the delicious looking sides. I'll definitely be back for more!

Most people who have read the reviews realize this pizza is hit-or-miss... not in their delivery, which is always fresh and hot, but whether the consumer likes white sauce and artichoke. Â The sauce is so rich and thick that it can be overpowering. Â Definitely worth taking a visitor to the NYC, but I don't go out of my way to get it.

5 stars. Easily. The guys here are really helpful despite the small space and large number of unknowing customers. Their menu is extensive, but you're really coming here for the $3 slices. Highly recommend the broccoli or spinach slices. They're made with fresh mozzarella that you can absolutely taste along with the veggies, that could perhaps be very fresh based on how they taste. If you're into toppings, the sun-dried tomato slice is pretty damn good, but if you're into just the regular cheese, go for it. I know most NY pizza is about a thin-slice, utility cheese, but anything with toppings here is pretty damn good. There's nowhere really to sit here, so grab your stuff to go.

It's good. Â I ordered too much based on other reviews - it turned out that the portions were fine, especially because they gave me an extra bruschetta for no apparent reason. Â The atmosphere is very nice, though the music, while good, was pretty loud. Â But the food is solid - nice flavors and well prepared, including some tasty pickled veggies with the panini and bruschetta that appeared to be made in house. Â Definitely worth a visit.

Hip Hop And The Fedora Gang Meet In Chelsea. The Joseph Leonard team takes on Chelsea. After dropping hotspots all over the West Village (Perla, Joseph Leonard, Chez Sardine...) the Little Wisco team has just expanded into Reasonably Large Chelsea with Montmartre, a narrow, Parisian-hill-inspired two-story alley of a townhouse with a bar up front and a window in back overlooking their garden. French classics meet Asian fusion perfectly here.

The food is 4 stars, but the service makes the overall experience less enjoyable. The fish tacos and the grilled octopus appetizers were grilled perfectly and seasoned well. For the main dish, we had the rib eye steak and fish. They were good, but nothing to really rave about. Now to the service. In our case, it wasn't that the service was that bad... it was just that the waitress didn't care. She didn't bother to tell us about the specials. She didn't come by often and generally seemed aloof. She just didn't seem like she wanted to be serving food. This place is hit or miss. If you are blessed with a waitress who cares and brings the food on time, you might have a 4 or 5 star experience.

Yayayayayay! So glad we found this place! Went to the Whitney with my folks, and you know how hungry Vito Acconci can make you when he's sitting in a dark room slapping his palm with a crowbar saying he wants to be alone on a low quality VHS. Couldn't be happier right now. I had jeed jard, a tom yum base soup with chicken, BBQ pork, bok Choy, and a hard boiled egg. Fresh ingredients, fresh spices, each component of the dish cooked to perfection.
