My mom said of her pok tak, "Thai bouillabaisse," that it was the best meal she could remember having for a good long time. Â It was fragrant with galangal and fish sauce, tender squid, perfect mussels, and salmon as well. She also said of the menu that she wished she lived in the neighborhood so that she could sample even a small fraction of the dishes. Dad got an egg noodle soup with a massaman base, chicken, and pickled mustard greens. Such a pleasant coconut-turmeric-chili oil combination. The staff is lovely. The prices are great for the upper east side and it's byob. Really, what more can one ask for in this life? Thank you, up Thai for making our night!

first off, i was def looking forward to eating here. Â my gf spoke highly of the place (she had their brunch before) and so i was excited to experience it. Â the decor and vibe inside is very simple and welcoming. Â when we walked in, a gentleman (who looked like he was a manager or owner) told us that it would be a few moments before we could get a table for 2.. but what was weird is there were definitely a few tables open. Â we sat there for about 5 minutes and then came back and seated us at one of the open tables that was already open when we walked in. Â (felt weird having to sit around for what appeared no reason but no big deal.. and it did seem he was doing it to every patron that walked in the door..not sure why?). Â  Anyway, the menu looked great. Â My gf ordered their french press coffee which she enjoyed and she ordered the huevos rancheros which she inhaled. Â it looked great too. Â looking at other customers dishes, everything looked great. Â  i ordered an OJ.. which was fresh.. but tasted a bit watered down, which was surprising. Â I opted to order a lunch item.. their Mac 'n Cheese which i was told was spectacular. Â I LOVE mac 'n cheese dishes.. anytime i see a place that makes it, i have to try it and see what they do with it. Â Dumont in williamsburg makes a killer mac 'n cheese, S'mac in the east village, even Van Horn in Cobble Hill... and Brook-Vin in park slope among others make great mac 'n cheese dishes. Â  Anyway, Juvenito totally let me down because first off, my dish was only lukewarm when i got. Â  Presentation wise, it was pretty weak too. Â It looked/tasted like a watery white cheese sauce tossed with macaroni and was served in a bowl with 3 slices of tomatoes on top (i would've preferred diced) with breadcrumbs. Â It really felt/tastedlike a cheap little dish that was just whipped together. Â  And more importantly, the flavor just didn't do it for me. Â Sad part is i felt like i could've cooked something tastier at home... as i even would've preferred a bowl of Annie's boxed mac 'n cheese to this. Â Anyway, maybe i can revise this review next time when i get to have one of their other dishes but this is all i have to base it on right now. Â (again, they have a very appealing menu, and i'm sure they have much better stuff)... but shouldn't everything on their menu be fairly awesome? Â Anyway, that being said, it may take a while for me to want to take another chance with Juvenito, and get this sub-par mac 'n cheese off my taste palette.
The falafel with israeli salad is the closest thing as to have it in Tel Aviv... or so I remember...

Great Old looking bar with good prices especially in comparison to the neighborhood places like Brinkley Station. Â Gets a good happy hour crowd. Â They have a good lunch special which includes a beer and entree. Â Food is good and the atmosphere is victorian. Â Wonderful location by Bloomingdale's.

I kind of don't get it when people complain about food being messy. Have you ever had really great barbecue? Haven't you noticed that (a rather large) part of what makes the experience of having really great barbecue so uniquely thrilling and pleasurable IS the mess? Throw care to the wind people, it's food the way it's meant to be. This is one fine sandwich. The chili mayo and the meat juices and the sriracha blend together and everything squirts out the back a little, and then you get to pick up the pieces of meat that fell out with your hands and shove them in your mouth like a heathen. I found that the toasty French bun held together just great and was crispy to the last bite..but maybe that's just me. Cilantro-haters beware, the stuff is stacked on there like lettuce. Definitely recommend the skirt steak, pulled pork, and peppercorn encrusted catfish, holy crap yum.

Yum. Finally got over here and had a delicious lunch. Silky butternut squash soup and a delicious sandwich (the aioli! the crusty bread! the amazing smoky-but-not-salty bacon!) was actually reasonably priced. I will certainly go back and try brunch -- although my dining companion wasn't super-impressed with his omelette, the short rib has sounded AMAZING. Service here was excellent, too. Speedy, attentive... and well-timed coffee refills (key!).

This place is definitely worth the wait. I would suggest visiting at off peak hours as some others have also suggested to avoid the wait, but if you must you must. You just can't get this kind of pizza taste without the coal oven! The pizza is so fresh and tasty - I'm getting hungry just thinking about it. A must try for New Yorkers. I also love the Italian sodas.
In the price range, which is $15-20 entrees and $10-15 pastas, this is as good as it gets in Manhattan. They do straightforward, traditional Italian food, and they consistently nail it.

Clearly a very popular place. Â As of when I read the comment last, the wait time was non existent at this new location but I think people are beginning to find out this place. Between pork buns and karaka (spicy) noodle which is what I ate, If I can just eat one, I probably would choose the pork buns although noodles are very good too. Â For a ramen noodle shop, I say this is a tad expensive but I suppose you get what you pay for. Place is very clean, waiters are very friendly and food is good. Â Midtown west has a relatively limited selection of good Japanese food (cheap or expensive) so this addition is a much welcome one.

I loved the cheesy thai pop music. Head bopping, cutesy, Asian fun! That aside, the food was pretty good too. We started with the steamed veggie dumplings. Very tasty although not freshly made and overcooked as they were falling apart. Â I has the krabi 'not for novices' seafood soup. Great spicy heat although I must fall in the novice camp because I has a slight coughing fit from the spiciness! Â It also came with a certain fungus that I'd only had in my Chinese grandmother's cooking so not for novices indeed!! Overall, good meal with good service.
Affordable domestic pitchers and extremely affable staff. Can't vouch for the food

Great food in a small diner atmosphere. They were open later on Saturday to accommodate the St. George theater goers. We were going to eat at Besos Â but the two-hour wait would have made us late for the show. Â  Next time I will go directly to Gavel grill. The service is very good and they don't rush the diners.
the spaghetti was undercooked. The tomato sauce was tasteless. There were only two shrimps in the dish tho it was called 'seafood pasta'.

I went there for brunch and although my friends enjoyed what they had, I have to say that I was a little disappointed. Â I had the steak and eggs and first off was not asked how I wanted the eggs so they turned up scrambled. Â No biggie on that but I was slightly pissed off at having to cut a good half of the steak away for being very fatty. Â However, the bellini's were scrumptious, the seasoned potatoes were to die for and the server's were lovely so I will try this place again.
Fresh fish, great ambience, and they allow you to bring your own wine. No cork fee for first bottle. Great prices, and yummy flavors.

+1 to the Smoked Gouda + Bacon Mac and Cheese - It's good .......like reallll good. It comes in a small dish they serve Creme Brulee in, so if you were thinking of sharing ......DON'T - it may lead to you lunging across the table at your company and clawing they're fork adorned with a tiny cheddar cheese wrapped bacon sprinkled noodle out of their poor horror stricken hand -Thus ending your friendship permanently......because your a Â psycho. But who will blame you? Cafeteria just serves up goodness all around. I couldn't finish my chicken and waffles, but I put up a good fight until my little belly threw in the towel. Of course I had my usual Lychee Martini.......only this time it was a Lavender Lychee Martini ( Warning - Do Not eat the lavender jelly .......it taste like soap....or just glycerin....either way it's bad) and the wild berry mojito had me contemplating theft. Yes I love those trashy menu's it's a fact : Â I'll be back for more - and soon...........
Great experience with helpful and friendly staff, exciting atmosphere and above all top notch food.

Poutine! Tastes like mashed potatoes, but it's a lot more fun to eat! The dipping sauces here are excellent, as well. I had my first taste of poutine here; I've had it elsewhere only to be disappointed. We stopped by late-night, but Pomme Frites is a must-have anytime of the day.
Closed Wednesdays? WTF?

This was my second time dining at little owl. Both times we were a party of 5, so made reservations well in advance. The first time was a summer evening a few years ago. I can distinctly remember the soft shell crabs and heirloom tomato salad as well as the pork chop and crispy chicken. Everything was perfect. The second time, last night, we shared the meatball sliders and the gnocchi special (with goat cheese/ratatouille) to start. The meatball sliders are just as good as you expect them to be. I ordered the whole, grilled branzino special which came with lobster risotto. The fish was cooked simply, but the flavors were delicate and delicious. Lobster risotto surprised me as it had a tomato taste. I also tasted the halibut, lamb shank and skate. All prepared nicely but didn't wow me like my first time here. The atmosphere and service are both great. All in all a solid place. Love the location.

Being so in love with dinner I decided I'd give brunch at this small restaurant a try. Unfortunately, my rating had to be brought down a notch due to lazy, inattentive service, as well as a menu that was tasty but not as well-rounded as I'd hope for. My brunch partner and I decided to get the spicy duck burger and the blueberry buckwheat pancakes, as well as a side of kirby pickles on a whim. The duck burger was extremely tasty and indeed spicy, but I was surprised by the paltry amount of fries that accompanied it. The four pancakes were pretty good but not life-changing. The butter was quite delicious though, and the vanilla bourbon syrup good enough to eat with a spoon, but I would much rather my fellow foodies head over to Shopsin's for a true pancake experience. Not planning on dessert, we were given dessert menus and of course HAD to order some because, quite frankly, the portions were too small to fill us up! Having decided on our sweet endings, it took forever to be acknowledged by our waiter, who seemed to be more intent on avoiding our stares than ever glancing in our direction. Finally, the hostess of all people asked us what we'd like to have, and the orders were made. My partner had the beignets with chocolate and lemon ganaches. Considering I hadn't had a piece of fried and sugar-dusted dough in ages, this was quite a treat, and the two dipping sauces, both thick and rich, were perfect foils for the light, puffy pillows of crispiness. We also shared the strawberry rhubarb parfait with jicama and mint syrup..a refreshing change from the beignets. The fact that I have little to say about it, however, reflects my relative lack of enthusiasm for it. Oh well, the meal was tasty overall, but I think I'll stick to dinner.

Best pork buns I've ever tasted! In addition, I'm not a big fan of ramen as I often opt for dry noodles wherever I can (I'm a big fan of pan-fried noodles), but this is the one place I will finish my bowl of ramen. Sometimes I'm not very adventurous when ordering so the Shiromaru Hakata Classic suites me just fine every time I order it!
SOUP DUMPLINGS are so delicious. The restaurant is a little bit hard to find. Inside is really crowded, slightly dirty and the service isn't great but the deliciousness makes up for it.

I went to Rye a week ago with my boyfriend, using a 30% off coupon we got from Blackboard Eats. Â I'd recently read a review of the place in NY Mag, and wanted to give it a try. Â After nearly walking past the front door due to its austere dark wood and frosted glass front, we stepped inside for an early dinner. Â The decor reminds me of the simple, scrubbed and charming interior of a dining room in the only hotel in town in a old Western film -- there's a different set of antique salt and pepper shakers and mixed silverware on the tables, and everything is pretty much dark brown woods and white linens. Â  We were greeted and seated immediately (we were some of the first to arrive for dinner that night, but even as the place filled up, I never saw people ignored at the door), and thus began one of the best dining experiences we've had in a while. Â Our waiter was extremely friendly and knowledgable about the menu, and gave his recommendations based on his personal dining experience when we asked. Â I ordered a special of the night: lime-cured and then grilled ceviche with citrus, and my boyfriend had a braised short rib sandwich and the handcut fries. Â We also split two plates (12 in all) of eastcoast oysters, and sampled 2 cocktails each from Rye's creative cocktail list. Â All was scrumptious! Â For dessert we ordered the donuts (a nice old fashioned cake donut) with vanilla ice cream, and a Brandy Milk Punch to go with it. Â Really delicious, and perfect for a hot summer night. Â  All in all, I don't have a bad thing to say about Rye, and my boyfriend and I have vowed to go back enough times to try everything on the menu.

Atmosphere: Williamsburg cool with the air of Japanese mannerisms Food: Yummy Price: Affordable. Cash only. Portions: Standard Udon bowl Wait time: Varies. But typically it's crowded and there is a wait. This is probably in my top five in Williamsburg. The wait sometimes turns me away, but the food is always solid and hits the spot. I mainly go for: Kinoko Tsukejil Udon (mushrooms) and the Black Sesame Ice Cream (which is AMAZING) to close, but all the Udon is good, just depends what you're in the mood for :].

I am in love with Rye's brunch! I had the Rye Benedict which is basically eggs benedict but on a delicious buttermilk biscuit and with pork belly. It was amazing! My wife had the Rye Slam which has your basics, you know....eggs, bacon, potatoes and Ridiculously delicious french toast! And with how amazing the food is i am surprised it is not really that expensive.

This the kind of hipster-cool type place that normally tends to offend my sensibilities. But the pizza was wonderful, delicious sauce and cheese and a light airy crust. The service was also excellent. Â The bibb lettuce salad is delicious with an interesting dressing. Â Overall a fine lunch!

whoa. Â okay, so i went there for dinner on friday night. Â we got there and the line was out the door and the wait was 2 hours. Â 2 HOURS! Â refusing to accept defeat, my friend and i bundled ourselves up good and proper and asked to be seated outside. Â in 40 degree weather. Â was it worth it? Â for these meatballs, YES! Â the food was a revelation. Â it was so good, in fact, that when another friend came to meet us a few hours later, we went back and sat outside AGAIN for a 2nd helping. Â i had the spicy pork meat balls with spicy meat sauce over mashed potatoes. Â he had a side of risotto with sliders of varying meatballs the first go-round. Â the second time we diversified our portfolios and got the "special" sliders- mediterranean lamb, another side of risotto (a fave) and the sauteed broccoli. Â there wasn't one thing that hit the table that wasn't 100% delectable. Â no regrets! Â sometimes you have to suffer for greatness.

Loved it here! This place is much better than Slyvia's. The service was on point-- the staff are very friendly. The wait wasn't as bad as it could have been. The tables are a bit squished together, but it works. The fried chicken was juicy, the greens were great. The candied yams were bomb! My friend liked the mac n cheese. The cornbread was a bit lame, but this is a great restaurant overall.
This place rules! Â The food is amazing!!!! The beer selection is awesome!!! And the staff super nice! Â Yum yum yum

Supposedly this is the place where New York chefs go for dinner after their own restaurants close. Legend or not, this rumor was enough to raise my expectations to lofty heights, and Blue Ribbon got 5 stars from me! The subtle service was charming, and I'm still talking about the food with friends a week later. I shared the bone marrow appetizer with my favorite aunt and had trouble eating my smoked trout salad afterwards, I was so full. A perfect night owl dinner spot, albeit pricey.

My husband and I had the absolute best experience here. We are both foodies and he is a born and raised Queens guy who is insanely picky about his Italian food, but this place to rocks. We originally were turned off because it seemed to be very touristy but wow did we have an awesome meal. My chicken picatta was delicious, my husband's veal chop was to die for, and the wine that our server recommended was so good that we had 3 bottles. With all that said ... we WILL be back!

Fun place. I definitely enjoyed the experience and the fries, but I personally don't love all the sauces. Considering fries are their "staple" they could've been better. Nevertheless they still were super tasty! I liked the mango one and sweet chilli best!
mmmmmm fresh mozzarella...crusty bread..... arugula....

Great wine bar! Â I love that they have small bites that I can nibble on, while I sip on wine and gab away. Â They also have walnuts and a cracker at the counter. We actually came here after finishing dinner at Gusto Ristorante e Bar Americano. Â It was one of my friends birthday and we all weren't ready to call it a night. Â Lo and behold, this place was just a few stores down! Service is pretty good, minus the one chick that worked that night. Â We were just having fun, but I guess we weren't "classy" enough and she kept shooting us disgusted/annoyed looks. Â Whatever. Â I would definitely still return. FYI: Â It's a small, cozy place and not ideal for groups of more than four, we had 6.

Just perfect. SERVICE Flawless at every stage. I entered with luggage, a briefcase, and a blazer and they graciously checked all three immediately. As I waited for my date, they offered me a drink at their slick bar. When I raced out of the restaurant to go find my date (who was lost), they didn't bat an eye. When they noticed we were on a date, they seated us at an intimate corner table. The staff were consistently friendly, professional, and informative, without being too chatty or intrusive. The pace of the meal was perfect; we never felt like we were waiting for anything, yet also never felt rushed. FOOD While I adore Korean food, I don't normally associate it with fine dining, and was admittedly skeptical. Unnecessarily. Jungsik (pronounced "Chongshik") does an excellent job at toeing the line between traditional Korean and modern culinary trends. We opted for the tasting menu and were not disappointed; each dish was beautifully presented and prepared to perfection. The only items that fell below "excellent" were the petit fours served at the end. Our green tea confection was too bitter, and the others were underwhelming. But at that point we were so full, I'm not sure it would have been possible to satisfy us. In addition to our food, we also ordered two cocktails each, and were again very impressed. Their house martini (a Korean take on a dirty martini) was the standout for me. All said and done, the damage was a bit over $500, and it was worth every penny.

This place has great selection of beer and meat dishes. We got the steak tartare on special sauce and small English muffin was delicious, bone marrow melts in your mouth and Choc-cutarie for dessert was so yummy. The commuter table in the garden area is nice for groups and the ambiance was casual and relax. A good hang out place that I would recommend!

I might have a new favourite meal - sha balep. They are Tibetan beef patties. It is somewhat similar to a samosa or an uzbek mantu. It is essentially ground beef with spices, encased in dough and fried. What's not to like? The dish comes with 3 different sauces. Big portion too, and I ate all of it.

WOW!!! Â Understated, minimalistic but comfy setting...Well worth the 30 minute wait (even with reservations) for "Sunday Supper"...The menu offerings rotate...The food is very good to exceptional in a Southern Style sorta way...Sunday Supper was three courses for $25 and to me a New York deal...The restaurant is small, kinda cramped but hey; it's NYC...An East Village Gem!!!
Great value for lunch specials. $7 includes tea, soup, and an entree. The food was good, and the decor was nice for this price point.
I'm sort of addicted to cafe orlin. Â Food is fresh and amazing. Â Love the goat cheese salad ... Yummy brunch ... Great dinner. Â You can't go wrong with anything you order!

The food and atmosphere were great, however the waiter was a total jerk. When asked what he would recommend off the menu he rudely said he "could not recommend dishes since every palette is different." When asked what are the most popular dishes, he said he "could not say." Â He had a horrible attitude and was not helpful in the least. This will be the last time I go back to Kilos.

We ordered. For our first executive board meeting, we were supposed to have a home cooked meal, but instead we had Lombardi's delivered. And delivered it was. This is some good pizza. Light, thin crust, that had me coming back for multiple slices of plain and mushroom. Yum-o.

The place can get chaotic: Â The waitresses can seem rude, but they're really not: they're just super busy and are terse with the interaction. Â Don't take it out on them, they're working very hard. All the chaos is WORTH IT. The noodles are super fresh, and the soup is very light. Â The dumplings were also fresh; we know because we peeked into the kitchen and watched as they were made.

Holy god damn shit Jane, I am in love. Â I think this place could alone justify rent in SOHO. Â All you need to know is that every brunch entree comes with an awesome complementary cocktail and two people can feast and drink for under $40 after tip. Â Need I say more? Okay I will, Benedict Johnny, take your standard eggs benedict and make it anything but with corn pancakes, roasted tomato hollandaise and house made maple chicken sausage. Â K, that should do. Go.
it wasn't the best shanghai dumplings i ever had, but they were pretty big and tasty. the green onion pancakes were my fav! yummy!!!!
this place is awesome, we get delivery from this place regularly and it never dissapoints, breakroom burger and fries is the way to go

Why is it that purveyors of such good food can't also be keen businessmen? The pizza here is good. So good that it deserves the chance to be consumed in a more comfortable setting. Yes, I think it was always meant to be a takeout stand, but that just doesn't work for pizza. That "fresh from the oven" quality that is missing by putting the pizza in a box and reheating it in the microwave a few hours later. I could have walked over to union square and eaten it on a park bench, but it was raining that day, so I insisted on having my pizza on a narrow counter attached to the wall, right in the middle of everything. I tried to be as positive as I could, but this was just in no way a comfortable eating experience. Furthermore, I asked, and was told that they had been open for about a month and a half. Now, I am aware that that is not very long, and that many things still need to get ironed out. But, the lack of stable business hours or a menu on the wall are not little kinks and probably should be taken care off by now. Hell, they were able to put a sign for a draft beer on the store front, and thats not even available yet, which is perhaps another thing that was not thought through very well. How are you gonna have draft beer if people can barely fit inside the store? Can't really drink it outside Now, despite those draw backs, the food was terrific, which is why they get four stars. I was planning to try all three different offerings, but after seeing the size of the artichoke slice, I got that and a regular (Neopolitan) slice. The artichoke was tasty and unique, but now that I've tried it I don't think ill get it again. The regular on the other hand was just terrific. Its true, it may just be the best accessible slice in Manhattan (Patsy's East Harlem is in the middle of nowhere, and I'm not a big fan of Joe's.) So, my concluding thought is that while things will run more smoothly when they hire more staff, the shop will still be limited by its size.Hopefully in the future, people will be able to get their slice quickly and go. I'll always keep it in mind as a pizza option whenever I'm in the area.

I've been wanting to try these marshmallows for a long time, and then I found them a at Food Cellar in LIC. And what can I say, Sweet & Sara marshmallows are great! They're light and fluffy, sweet but not too sweet, and totally vegan!I There are a few flavors to choose from, strawberry, coconut, and vanilla, with strawberry being my favorite. I looked up them online and they also make smores! I can't wait to try this! Hoping they open up their very own store soon.

Overall this place lived up to its expectations. Â The food was delicious, and the environment is great. Â Not to mention they have a great selection of whiskeys and beer. Â A little expensive, but i promise you wont leave hungry.

We ordered the escargot, the kasulet, and the filet mignon. The sauce for the escargot was rich and flavorful and went well with the escargot itself and the bread. Make sure you ask for extra bread to scoop up all the leftover sauce! :) The kasulet was hearty and definitely filling as a "warrior's meal." Get ready to feel super stuffed after eating it. As someone with only a moderate sized tummy capacity, this dish was a little overwhelming, so bring a buddy to share it with or prepare yourself for leftovers. The filet mignon itself wasn't quite filling enough, especially not for the price, so it missed the mark a bit. However the touch of foie gras and shallots did help bring the dish together. Overall, it was a cute, cozy spot. It was a bit pricey but it made for a good date night. :)

Great food, but for the money, I think I'd rather venture elsewhere, not sure it is much different cost wise as a BLT joint. Â  The waits were long both times I've been here, but the hostess was very accurate on how long the wait would be. Â Waiting at the bar is not a bad option, and the kitchen can get the tasty (but pricey) spinach dip out with time to spare before your table is ready. The food is good. Â I had a good seared tuna, that was rather disappointingly served with a tomato salad, which is exactly what you think it is, a tomato... Â The tuna was good. Â Second time around, went with a nice dry aged steak, served with a baked potato, much much better. Â The Hawaiian steak is also tasty, not overpoweringly sweet, but a nice balance of sweet & savory. A solid option, but not a spectacular one.
Corner Bistro is on my top five burger list. Â You often have to wait in line and the place is a bit rough, but it's got character and I like that.
I think for those who know of this masterpiece would kill for it!

OMG! with so much hype, i was afraid i was doomed for some disappointment. We headed to this cart after my beloved A's beat the Mets at Citifield. We were both hungry but saved our appetites for the halal cart. We shared the chicken over rice, and it was enough to leave us both satisfied. Great serving size for just $6! The white sauce is off the hook...and be forewarned....the red sauce is SUPER spicey....so use with caution. The Mr. absolutely loved this dish. I can see now why they are so popular. We lucked out and only waited a few minutes in line. Make sure you look for the guys in the yellow shirts, and long lines, as there are many different halal carts out there. We will certainly make another trip back to this cart the next time we're in NYC!

Generally I use fries as an excuse to eat more ketchup... At Pommes Frites, I use fries as an excuse to eat more pineapple mayo... and I use pineapple mayo as an excuse to eat more fries... It's a vicious cycle. Tip for the broke: Â Ask for as many free samples as possible. Â Then, when they get annoyed that you're not ordering, just pretend you're with someone else who already ordered. Works like a charm ; )

My friends had reservations they could not make and I was looking for a brunch spot to take my boyfriend for his birthday so we used their reservation. We had an absolutely amazing Brunch here. I suggest making reservations as I saw plenty of people waiting while we walked right in. My Boyfriend had the Vaca Frita and I had the Latin Benedict. Both were absolutely amazing! The steak was perfect, the eggs were perfect. The sauces were perfect. Can you tell I'm a fan yet? The service was also perfect. Perfect Sangria too. Overall perfect experience and I shall be returning very soon!

They certainly know what they're doing when it comes to meet. All the main items I've tried are delicious. Brisket, pulled pork as well as pork belly. The sides however have not been as impressive. They seem like fast food sides a bit. However, I will definitely be going back several times just so that I can try all the different proteins! Meat lovers dream for sure.

Great wine selection. Took myself out on a date and got the Bambino appetizer and cheese plate. Absolutely delicious. I'm gluten-free so I can't have the paninis. But they sounds delicious. Great for small parties. Will be back soon.

I just had to speak up in defense of what is truly a neighborhood gem, because i really don't know why even when people seem to love the food, they still seem to have such problems with hurdles that comes from such a small places being so popular. First off, on our recent visit, they could not have been nicer. Yes, even though we got there only ten minutes after opening, the wait for a table of two was already approximately 90 minutes. (we took a chance on a Saturday) We decided just to order a pie to go, as did a few others, and we all got our pies in about ten minutes. While we waited, we watched the proprietor bring out glasses for and open the bottles of wine brought by people who chose to wait seated on the benches outside, which on such a beautiful evening seemed like a decent way to pass some time. We also listened as he suggested alternatives to some tourists visiting from Iowa who did not want to wait the two hours for a table for four they required, and then he proceeded to call over to the restaurant he recommended to help secure them a table there. Very hospitable. Most importantly, the pizza is exceptional. simply way above average -- crisp, lightly charred crust, perfect sauce and quality flavorful cheese. the addition of garlic and fresh basil is free, and definitely recommended, as are the portobello mushrooms topping -- sliced thin so the cook perfectly in the time the pizza cooks. they make their own ricotta, so, you just have to try a calzone too! the atmosphere of the tiny dining room is also absolutely charming. My advice to anyone making the trek over, bring extra bottles of wine, so you can enjoy a glass on the benches while you wait for your table, or, take your order to go, and if the weather is nice, walk it up to Carroll Park up the block and enjoy it al fresco (there are even benches with tables in the middle section of the park that are perfect for such an impromptu outdoor meal)
Excellent food and drinks! Just a little sad about the gentrification of the neighborhood...

Homophobic and bigoted. Went in there on a Saturday night. Said they were closed because we were two gay men but then took orders from others. I called them and they said they were open. But when I went again they said they were closed. I wouldn't want to go somewhere that serves hate and refuses to serve a gay person. Also the food is kinda gross.

How can I put this succinctly? I. Love. This. Place. Seriously. It's so hard to find a go-to spot that's consistent with both service and food in NYC and especially in the Lower East Side, which has become overrun with Bridge-and-Tunnel (read: the button-ups/jeans/hard-bottoms/Bebe-attired) & frat boys lately. YB manages to stay welcoming, fun, and mature with the proper food & drinks to accompany the atmosphere. Drinks: you can seriously do no wrong here. I'm not a gin fan. One of my favorites drinks: Poquito Picante. Spicy. Flavorful. Light. And gin based. Go figure. And if you don't know what you are in the mood for, their bartenders are more than adept at helping you figure it out. Pisco. Mezcal. Rum. Tequila. Cachaca. It's all good. Food: consistently amazing. Small bites can go as light as a deconstructed salmon ceviche to a picada (assorted fried goodness). Then of course there's always the fan fave: chicharron de calamar. Entrees include some of the most tender short ribs I've ever had, never-dry lechÃ³n, and a steak for 2 that can probably feed 4 if it weren't so damn good (& I so greedy). Best. Churros. EVER. Service: just look for Gio or Angel. They'll take good care of you.

Amazing atmosphere, although it's more modern than truly Lebanese. Â The food is fantastic (and reasonable prices) and the staff are all great. Highly recommended if you're in the mood for some Lebanese.

WHAT I ORDERED: *Appetizer: Â Mussels with chorizo sauce. Â  Â  Â  Â -Mussels tasted fresh and were very tasty. Â  *Main course: Rib eye and creamed spinach. Â  Â  Â  -Steak was a solid choice, but, as expected, not to the caliber of a Â  Â  traditional steakhouses like Ruth's or Morton's. Â Definitely many steps above a steak at some chain restaurant like Outback though. Â Wouldn't hesitate to order it again. Â  -Creamed spinach wasn't bad, but also not as flavorful as other creamed spinaches I've tried in the past. Â  *Dessert: Â Tiramisu and vanilla ice cream cone Â  Â  -Both were really delicious and tasted freshly made, instead of something that they had stored in a freezer for a while. Â  Â  PROS: *The restaurant had a very modern decor and a nice vibe. *Very diverse menu, offering everything from seafood to meat dishes. Good place to bring people who have different tastes and can't decide what they want to eat. Â Everything on the menu will be a solid choice and of good quality and taste. Â  Â  Â *Good service and they even remembered to bring the birthday girl a cotton candy cake with a candle on top! CONS: *The AC didn't seem to be working, because I was sweating during my entire meal, but what can you expect for summer time in NYC?? Â  *May be slightly overpriced for the food. OVERALL: I would go back there the next time I wasn't craving anything in particular, because of their eclectic menu and the fact that I knew that I wouldn't have to "stay away" from any items on the menu because they weren't known for some particular dishes. Â  Definitely wouldn't hesitate to go back.

Pro Tip: A Yelp check-in gets a free drink with ordering an entree. Not everything is an entree though, so you might want to strategize with friends. Also, there is no limit per table - three of us checked-in, and we got three free drinks.The white wine, however, is nothing to write home about. Reservations: Recommended. Easy to come by on Opentable. Seating: Not my favorite. The stools have no backs. Actually pretty Thai authentic, as I think half my meals in Thailand were backless, but this is NYC, I walked around all day and such, and my back hurt. Chiang Mai Fries: Nobody's favorite in our party. Fried sweet potato, in bigger chunks than sweet potato fries. Meh. Spring rolls: OK. Lobster Khao Soi: Very good, but too spicy. They did not ask me what level of spice I wanted, and this came out too spicy. However, it was delicious. Any restaurant with khao soi is noteworthy.

Went here last night with some buddies. Â Their main focus is the pasta, with all the plates/bowls being about $10 on average. Â Let me tell you, its amazing. Â I have the Fusilli with Lamb, and it was great. Â The pasta is a little thicker, and al dente, but delicious. Â I highly recommend this place and hope to go back soon.

oh traif. Â  i don't remember every dish of what seemed like an endless tasting course. Â but, the entire meal was delicious from start to finish. Â the most memorable dishes for me were the prawns, scallops, pomegranate glazed baby back ribs and the bacon glazed donuts. Â  just as a heads up. Â to do the $40 tasting course i am describing up above.. you need a minimum of 3 people. Â yes, $40 tasting course. Â probably the cheapest tasting course you will ever have in the state of new york for 13-15 courses. Â  they take reservations now, so take advantage of it! don't be one of the dummies waiting forever outside. Â because there is really nothing within a 2 block radius to do around here.
the vibe is very hip and the waiters was very helpful and friendly. there are very good dishes but for the price that we have paid the portion was too less. Not ideal for groups.
The buffalo gyro/pita is tasty. Â Not too big on cucumbers, though. Â They put cucumbers in everything!

Waited 2 hours for a table. When presented with the menu at the table, found out that all the bowls contained pork products (I have a pork sensitivity). Had the vegetarian option. The $15 I paid must have gone to the ambiance because I cannot think of what else it could have paid for. Ramen: water, salt, noodles, and meat is optional.
the pizza was sooooo good words cant explain, my mouth wanted to keep eating but my stomach wouldnt let me!! :'(

My date and I went to Salinas last night and had nothing short of a lovely experience. Â Everyone from our server down to the coat check girl was very professional and friendly. Â The space itself is romantic and clean and presents itself as chic but not overstated. Â I feel like it is definitely a good date spot, especially in the back garden area, which is simply gorgeous. The menu is all tapas, with a few entree options sprinkled in. Â One must order was the brussel sprouts and cauliflower app that was dusted in some sort of spice and served with a yogurt sauce. Â It was divine! Â The "Spanish Pasta" dish we ordered was very flavorful, if not a little strange as far as texture, but full of vegetables and topped with a poached egg. Â It was definitely different and stood out as good choice. Â We also ordered one of the fish specials of the day and it came baked and topped with chickpeas, and was spiced perfectly. Overall, we were very pleased with the flavors and portions of everything we ordered. Â We topped dinner off with the flan, which I thought was a little too vanilla-ey, but it came accompanied with Â a mango foam and cookie crumbs which made it fancy and surprise tasty. I also love that the restaurant is right next to Bathtub Gin, and super easy to get to from the subway. Â I will be back!
Great food. Great atmosphere. Great service! Nice wait staff. Live acoustic music. Think "Triplets of Belleville". A must. Get the Date Cake for dessert! Awesome!!! Love this place.
Wonderful atmosphere, service, and food. Filet was tender and seafood was fresh. Best yet....2 for $12 martinis! I recommend the lychee.

LOVE this place. Â I'm a vegetarian who likes to pretend she's vegan sometimes, so this place is perfect. Â Delicious and healthy - can't be beat. Â I've had most of their sushi rolls and have liked all of them (spicy mango is really good). Â I recently had the sweet angel wrap and wasn't blown away by it (although I split it with my mom and she really liked it) - we got the large wrap and one roll of sushi to split and I felt satisfied. Â you really can't go wrong at this place. I've been to both their Union Square and Chelsea Market locations - it's true their small, but it really doesn't affect the quality or enjoyment of the food itself.

One word: perogies. Get 'em fried, with onions, and leave happy. Low key spot around the corner for my apartment that satisfies all my potato dumpling needs. B&H across the street feels cleaner and the guys there are more friendly, but I can't argue with Stage's perfectly caramelized onions, pan-fried perogies and the quick and efficient counter here.

This place is great! Comfy dive bar type feel -- the pulled pork sandwiches are so. damn. good. Holy. Just get two for $5 and you're set! I didn't drink tonight (gasp!) but friends had a wide variety of beers that they seemed to enjoy! Also, there's a TON of board & trivia games -- lots of fun trying to figure out the pop culture quiz stuff. Would definitely make the trek out to Red Hook again!

I thought the sandwiches were quite excellent. Lots of selections, and at very good prices. The atmosphere inside is quaint, cafeish, but not in a bad way. There's also a lot of delicious looking cupcakey things in the case inside. I didn't have any, but how could they be bad? I had to take some stars away because the service was fairly poor. They forgot to bring one of our Crostinis and the sandwiches came out in staggered waves. but I enjoyed my sandwich enough that I would definitely go back again. Â and just hope the service is a bit better.

My favorite quick meal at a affordable price. Unda chicken(egg chicken) and aaloo roll are my favorite.meat well marinated amd cooked well..the reason for one star less service,staff Is rude .when u go to eat somewhere u want someone to give u a welcoming smile not who looks at u like oh god now I have to work cause of u!

Ugh, this place is so tasty it's obscene. Awesome beers on tap, friendly staff and EAT THE MEAT! No joke, I usually go for the Kasekraner with cheese inside, but if I want to dump that lovely der kommisauce they have on something it's most definitely the weisswurst. Gives is a nice tangy kick to a relatively mild sausage. I live upstairs, still not sick of the food here. Beer is great here, and their house white wine has something to be said, its quite decent if you're not a big beer drinker. They also have the ONLY proper selection of shnapps I've seen in park slope, they're small pours but still really fun to have for a cheers at the end of your sausage nosh.

Went there on a Sunday night for the $44 three-course supper. Everything was spot on and a great deal for $44 based on the quality of the meal. I had the special app, a fluke tartare with avocado.. the highlight of my meal. Super fresh and light. I had the Red Snapper with carrot juice and Lior's spice blend. I really enjoyed this, particularly the spices which had a hint of curry in there. He had the agnolotti with sunchokes and ricotta, a winner. We also tried the gnocchi bolongese app, wow. I could have just eaten a big bowl of this. The sauce was delicous. For entree, he had the ribeye, this carried a $6 supplement, but well worth it. Dessert as the pecan bread pudding for me, excellent, and the orange torta for him, really light and delicous. On a Sunday, every table was taken. Highly recommended.

Crabs you want crabs you get. This is a place that practically is a whole in the wall and gives many established so call crab restaurants a run for their customers. The food is very flavorful. It's not expensive. Menu is very simple you are not overwhelmed by a extensive menu. The place is small so seating may be a little wait. I had the alaskan snow crabs with broccoli and corn. I should have gotten another order to go. Will revisit.

We had a 10pm reservation here on a Saturday. Â The first thing that hits you is how intimate (small) the space really is. Â Our group of four was originally seated in the middle of the bar, but by the time dinner started we were moved to the corner of the bar, which is definitely the best experience you can have with a group larger than two. I was determined to eat at this place upon getting some recommendations, so I failed to consider the fact that I was going to dinner with an observant jew, muslim and pescetarian. Â This fact was an issue because, as advertised, Degustation is a Spanish tapas place and almost everything includes meat (particularly pork). Â But we asked the chef to prepare us a five-course tasting menu that would not cause anyone to break any rules, whether moral or religious. Â He was a little skeptical and surprised we had even showed up, but in the end he helped us out big time. I cannot be the guy to talk about the actual tasting menu because it was definitely modified for our convictions, but I can say that what was served was amazing. Â Every course was better than the last. Â The wine list is also great. My favorite aspect of Degustation, though, is the ambiance. Â It is so comfortable and quiet, with Bob Marley playing softly in the background. Â And who can complain when they are watching a team of chefs prepare every course right in front of you?

BCD got rave reviews from other users so I decided to check it out myself. Â I also wanted to try the spicy raw crab, can't seem to find it on a lot of menus. Â In we go on a Tuesday night at about 5:30P, there's a good crowd in there already. Â There are still some tables open toward the back and I noticed that there's a second floor as well. Â The servers were all very courteous and we didn't have any problems. Â The menu seems abrupt, not a whole lot of choices. Â We ordered the seafood pancake, seafood soondubu, kalbi (short ribs), and the gejang (spicy raw crab). Â The banchan spread was just okay, seems like everything was too sweet. Â I did like the fried whole fish a lot and it's cool that everyone gets their own. Â The pancake is one of the better ones I've had, nice and crisp. Â The seafood soondudu was good, but it's quite pricey here and it's not any better than any of the other restaurants around this area. Â The short ribs were pretty good, they are on the sweeter side. Â I find that the crab was smothered in too much sauce, but I think that's how it's served. Â I still enjoyed it, the crab is sweet on its own. Â I'm glad that the sharp spikes were removed so that was good. Â By the time we left, it got pretty crowded and there's a small wait by the door. Â  The place was good, but it's not great. Â Limited menu could be a good thing when you can't decide, but sometimes you just want a few more choices. Â The place is a bit pricier than the other places around, but the food is the same. Â Not sure if I'd be excited to go back.

Creative, but well within the neo-Neapolitan pizza mainstream. Â Dynamite crust baked in a proper wood-fired brick oven, but it will be better once they can sell you wine with your meal. Â I'd also prefer a slightly larger menu, like an app or two per night, as well as a pasta or two. Â  Go try this place for yourself, it'll be worth it.

You see a lot of these carts around NYC. I was skeptical about the food at first, but it's actually that good! I ordered a chicken plate with pita bread and the white sauce they added on to it enhanced the entire meal. I just wished there were more options when we went, but it was still far from a disappointment.

Fun neighborhood restaurant with great food and service. Love sitting outside in the summer to people watch. Â The oysters are heavenly. Salads are so fresh and tasty. Unbelievable burgers. The paprika chicken and pork chops are my favorites. Comfort food at its best. Â Yum!
Porcini Flan is awesome, nice gin cocktails as well. The bread cart is amazing and almost ruined my appetite! The wine paring was a tad lacking, but still worth it.
The pork belly and pulled pork is amazing, but the best is the baked beans. When they cut the meat, the take the scraps and put it in the beans. Oh my god, it's just too good.

Great and fresh food for a very good price. Â If you're craving fried dumplings and noodle soup, definitely hit up this place. Â The beef stew noodle soup have cubed beef and beef tendon pieces while the beef noodle soup have sliced beef. Â The decor is next to none but the food makes up for it. Â  Be warned, the hui xiang dumplings take awhile (~8 minutes) to steam and contain dill and a lot of it.

A little scary looking on the outside but don't be afraid to go in! Food is incredible I've already gotten it two nights in a row and I don't even dine in there! Only a few tables all bunched together but I make a 15 minute walk just to get it taken out. SO GOOD. The penne vodka is my favorite and the guys that work there are really nice
Wafa is definitely a great labanese spot. Their chicken shwarma is great. The hummus is really good also.

When I told my co-worker I was going to New York, he recommended I eat at Katsu-Hama. Â He makes regular tonkatsu-filled visits to Japan, but he always stops by Katsu-Hama when he's in the city. Â Thank you Tom, for the delicious tip. I went with a few co-workers for a work day lunch, and the place was packed. Â Luckily, it was an efficient operation built to accommodate New York's hordes of salarymen. Â Our party of four got seated at a counter, where we were presented with menus and a set of green tea, Japanese pickles, and sesame seeds with a pestle, almost as soon as we sat down. The food was fantastic. Â I ordered the katsu lunch, which came with white rice, miso soup, cabbage salad, and two beautiful golden brown cutlets of breaded and fried pork, all for $11. Â The tonkatsu was some of the best I've ever had, moist and meaty, with crispy, flavorful breading that didn't feel heavy in the least. Â The katsu didn't need much else, but the tonkatsu sauce poured over ground sesame seeds was wonderful, hearty with a light tang, and a smear of yellow mustard paste added a little wasabi heat to the mix. Â The rice and miso soup were great, and I even liked the shredded cabbage, though it was the only thing left on my plate when I was through. Â The katsu lunch was a good amount of food, but if you're very hungry, you can upgrade to a $16 "surprise" katsu lunch. Â It sounds better in Japanese - all it means is "supersized." I loved my tonkatsu, and I'll keep it on my short list for places to come back to in New York. Â Tom said the last person he recommended Katsu-Hama to went three times in a week-long trip. Â I had a mediocre lunch the day after my visit, and I rued the missed opportunity to go back for another meal of deep fried pork (I would have loved to try the katsu curry). Â A great quick lunch is surprisingly hard to find in midtown, but you can always swing by Katsu-Hama for destination tonkatsu.

My roommate had been telling me to try this place as a great delivery option for some time now. Â  I ordered the skirt steak and the corn (my roommate told me that 1 sandwich and an appetizer would be more than enough, but he forgot that I require more to fill my stomach now that I have become yelp elite). Â It was delicious! Â  The steak was remarkable quality for a delivery sandwich place and the chili mayo is fantastic! Â I love the cucumber and cilantro in the sandwich, and now get pissed at subway for not having those as options. Â  The downside is that they take too long for delivery (especially since I live a few blocks away), they only take cash, and they don't allow any substitutions.
Â¡Taco fantastico!

Pros: - Food is good: I enjoyed the blueberry pancakes. Â Not mind-blowing but definitely solid - Service is good - Space is nice Cons: - Cash only, which is ridiculous for the price point of this restaurant. Â They should be investigated by the IRS as I'm sure saving on credit card fees is not the only motivation for this policy - The complimentary biscuits and jam are no longer offered - Extremely overpriced: they charge $17 for pancakes which costs them about $0.50 to make - Pricing doesn't make sense. Â Order the regular pancakes? $15 Â Order the blueberry pancakes? $17 Â Order a short stack of regular pancakes and add blueberries? Â One would expect an additional charge of $2 (or even $1 since it's a short stack), but no, an additional $3 was charged when we got our bill

I thought everything was really good! You get so much food and it is really good. My boyfriend and I went kind of crazy and wanted to try everything. We got regular pickles (yum!) and fried pickles (also yum). He orders a beer float (I wasn't the biggest fan but he liked it). Â  For the meal I got the BBQ jack chicken sandwich. So yummy! It comes on a biscuit, the BBQ was great (I don't usually like BBQ all that much but this was kind of light and tasty). It had way too much cheese on it for me but my boyfriend ate what I couldn't. It was also easy to take off any cheese I didn't want. It also came with cheese grits -pretty decent (I usually like my grits with a little butter and a little salt) but these were definitely tasty. Â  For dessert we got the fried Oreos-yum! I missed those things. The service was good! But the wait!...oh man-it was pretty long. But the great thing was they had a great system where they text you within 10 minutes of your table being ready and ask if you want to hold your spot or not. This was great. We were able to walk around the UWS until our table was ready. So be prepared to wait on the weekend-but at least there's other things to do in the area including a quick trip to Barnes & Noble (nerd alert). Haha Anyway, definitely a good spot!

Before we get to the meat (and oh yes, there was meat. Â Lots of it.), let us discuss the bar. Â This is an important first talking point, because you should expect to get to know this place quite well, as members of your party will be traveling to it to re-up on booze as you wait on line. Â And yes, there is almost always quite a long line - but it's easily tempered by hooking yourself up with a GALLON of beer. Â Yes. Â Gallon. Â Beer. Â  They have a great selection of local breweries, gushing out of taps with knives on them. Â Knife taps? Â Oh yes. Â Lets not forget. Â They may sell beer by the gallon, but this is a meat lover's heaven. Â  So after you wait on line, go through two or three gallons of beer (it's remarkable really), dispatch friends to fight for a seat, and order up a heaping portion of meat by the pound, you're in business. Â The pulled pork and the brisket is outstanding. Â The sausage that they had that day was disappointing, but the old standbys were in top form. Â The sides compliment the meal perfectly, and the beer never stops flowing. The inconvenience of finding a place to sit, and waiting on that line is part of the fun. Â The other part is the food.

After having dinner at Little Owl years ago and loving it, I've been wanting to try their brunch for quite some time. I've feared the crowd I've seen gathered outside this place on summer days, however when I finally made it out on a snowy Saturday morning, there was no wait at all. Â In fact, no line formed the entire time my friend and I were there. There's one good thing about snow! The restaurant is quaint and cozy, situated on an ideal corner in the West Village with perfect, open people-watching windows. Staff are great - helpful and observant without being intrusive. The Foodnalysis: - Coffee - Average, not good nor bad. - Whole Wheat Pancakes - Had to try this after hearing how much Alton Brown loves them. They did impress! Whole wheat pancakes didn't sound particularly appealing to me (perhaps because of the higher likelihood of them being dry/dense), however these were incredibly well prepared. Simple, fluffy, moist, not as rich or heavy as typical pancakes. Wished there were more berries (these were just served with a sprinkling of strawberry slices and blueberries), but still an excellent choice. - Cheese Grits - Surprisingly good. Had a more watery consistency than I'm used to, but was a nice savory balance to the pancakes. cheese grits - surprisingly good. more watery than grits i've had in the past, but a nice savory balance to the pancakes. The Bottom Line: A great brunch option with short lines on snowy days! Â Try the whole wheat pancakes -- solid, simple fare.

It's a bit confusing to arrive at this quaint Japanese restaurant, but once you do, it's worth the "trek." Dishes: - Onsen Tamago - Fluke Carpaccio - Buta Kakuni - Chawanmushi - SPECIAL: Oven-baked rice dish with lobster meat, crab meat, etc. Would order all of them again expect the special - the rice was a bit too dry for me and the dish was quite bland overall. Can't comment on the sake - we decided to abstain from alcohol that night. Would definitely come back.
Best Greek restaurant in manhattan. Will definitely visit again soon.

I think geographically this is the closest bar to my apartment which makes it my "local." Â I don't come here often because the crowd during the day resembles an AA meeting after party and the crowd at night is a track-bike hipster fiasco but they have good beer and yummy snacks. Â You can't deny a bowl of cheese balls and how eloquently it pairs with a jack&coke. Â They also have lots of board games though most of them only have half of the pieces you need to play.

My now husband and I have been regulars at Joya's since 2002 when we first met... Â  We have always been huge fans of this restaurant/ lounge and regulars (eating there at least once every two weeks.... at times once a week), great food, great drinks, very reasonable price, awesome service and very small wait time. I will say that our last visits have not been the best, the waiters who are usually very pleasant and attending were rushing this time around. Â The wait was much longer than usual and the place really didn't have the feel it has for me in the past. Â I always noticed the owners at the location, but for the past two or three years it hasn't been that way and it obvious its affecting the great feel i loved about Joya's. However the food still remains to be amazing and my favorites still are the apple martini and the chicken Pad Se Yu. Â And ofcourse...no one makes a better calimari in my opinion! Â I absolutely love the spice rack (which i have to admit my husband got me into). Â I love the place and what i like the most about it is that you can be a couple, a group of friends or a family with children and still each one of these different groups will find the place to be very enjoyable and the food to be amazing!

I am in love with Perry St! Jean George just never fails to impress me. From the service to the decor and especially to the food, the entire experience was top notch. We arrived a little late and was told we would have to wait. We sat by the bar and had a round of drinks.. after a good 20 minutes later, one of the maitre d's came by and insisted on buying us another round while we continued to wait! What a gesture! We accepted the offer and kept munching on their delicious bar treats until our table was ready. First and foremost, I am so pleased at how flexible they are with how you decide to order - especially since we came during restaurant week. Most restaurants make it mandatory that the whole table participates in the RW menu, but not here. We were able to order 2 RW menu's and 1 of the 'Taste of Perry St' tasings between 4 people! This way we were able to try everything on both tasting menus. Additionally we added the fried chicken since we heard such good things. Everything was delicious! Some of my favorites were the: Rice Cracker Crusted Tuna: love the crunch of the rice cracker with every bite of the fresh tuna.. the sriracha-citrus emulsion added the perfect kick. Slow cooked Salmon: definitely slow cooked. this was the most tender piece of salmon I've ever tasted in my mouth.. melted like chocolate. Market Beets and Pears: Love the pairing of beets with pears.. with a hint of sweet from the honey and a punch of citrus from the lime.. so whimsical and tasty. Superb service and modern decor- the C-shaped booths were comfortable and roomy.. our whole party had an amazing time and will be back for more!

this review is only for the lentil soup. the price is $4.75 now! pretty pricey for just lentil soup. nothing special about it. very plain. it comes with a pita which was nice and soft but still nothing I would crave. I tried the soup cuz of the other yelpers mentioning it. it's a boring lentil soup. save ur $$ for smtg else. I will try smtg else next time and hopefully that will meet my expectations?!
Always a good choice. Line moves quickly and they give you a ridiculous amount of food for only 6 bucks. Even if the rice can be a little over cooked sometimes.

What great service! The waitress brought me second round of side dishes (free) when she saw I finished two of them. After they serve you rice from a big bowl, they add water into the bowl so later they would come back and serve you rice soup. Thought that's really funny. Food is awesome too! I ordered a seafood soup and it was great!

I fail to understand the hype about this place, except for its location in a particular corner of Brownstone Brooklyn where is admittedly a dearth of fine dining options. I found the atmosphere at Jack the Horse pleasant and the food good enough, but with Noodle Pudding and Henry's End just around the corner, I'm not banging down the door to be seated here, especially given the rather steep pricing. Service was a bit frosty as well. I hope Jack the Horse can elevate its game as it could be a wonderful addition to a beautiful neighborhood.
I can see why this place gets so many great reviews. Very tasty crepes, great hot chocolate, and the woman who made the crepes was so sweet and thoughtful. I will DEFINITELY return again and again.

I was running around the East Village the other day doing some Christmas shopping, and needed fuel, so I stopped at Taqueria Diana. It's a narrow spot, with seats for about 8 people in the back, and a bench out front. Takeout is probably your best bet, though eating in is not impossible on a weeknight. The staff is sorta gruff, sorta hipster, sorta beardo, and all dudes. You order at the register at the left, then they bring your food out at the end of the counter on the right (near all the salsas). I got the chicken quesadilla, and it was hands down AMAZING. The chicken had Mexican seasoning all over it, which blended with all the cheese. The portion was huge, and a more restrained person would have gotten 2 meals out of the thing. The side of guacamole was really good too, and there is an assortment of freebie salsas you can try. Taqueria Diana is 100% down and dirty, sloppy Tex-Mex, and I love it.

Brunch review only. There are much better brunch places around. I'd be curious to try their dinner from looking at the reviews, but I'm not sure I'll be back. I really had high hopes based on the other reviews and an awesome menu. However, the food was mediocre. We ordered: Norwegian Benedict - terrible hollandaise destroyed this dish, eggs were slightly overdone, and the salmon was tasteless and dry. Home fries were okay but were littered with peppers. Zero seasoning on anything. Scrambled Bruschetta - lacked any flavor and was just "meh." Oatmeal - fine, no complaints. Coffee - fine, nothing to write home about. Service was nice but we could barely understand the guy (one of my friends is bilingual in French - this was a mumbling issue) - and he disappeared for LONG periods of time. It took like 10 minutes to get salt and pepper, and more than 30 to get the check. They did leave us alone to visit and chat, which was nice. It was clear, however, why the place was more than half empty on a Sunday morning when other brunch spots had lines out the door. Edit: I got a message from the owner and hope to try their dinner in the future. Props to owners who acknowledge unhappy customers and try to remedy the issues.

I have been here a few time and can honestly say this place is one of the best brunch places I have ever been to! Everyone I have taken there has said the same thing! It's reasonably priced and all their dishes are perfectly made!

The burger destruction tour of NYC makes a pit stop at Corner Bistro... -tasty burgers NOM -nice staff and bar tenders- for such a crowded place you can only expect so much speed but I appreciate the manners and politeness! -Great beer specials -Don't be fooled by the size of the bar- more seats in the back but certainly not spacious. Came in with a large group and waited about 5 minutes before we were seated. Tables turnover quickly here! I dig!
Fantastic. Â Consistently fantastic. Good for eating in (atmos = hip/casual) or taking out. Can't go wrong with shrimp pad thai!

I organized my girl friend's birthday party here last weekend. Open table didn't allow me a reservation at this place for a party of 14, not sure why. But, I had no problem getting a reservation on the phone two weeks in advance. It was one of those rainy New York days with no cabs and heavy traffic, none of us were on time. They had a lot of people waiting for a table, still the owner was kind enough to understand our situation and hold the table for us for 40 extra minutes. Considering that they were losing business by doing so, that was nothing but great customer service. We were very pleased with our server as well. She handled the group so large without any panic or hesitation. She was on top of things throughout, gave us some great wine and food recommendations. We ordered few bottles of wine for the table, the Argentinian Malbec was spot on. Definitely ordering a couple of bottles for home. Similarly we ordered few appetizers to share. The African Mussels were my favorite. For entree, I went with 'Poisson Yassa', I have never had branzino so delicious in my life. Trust me, I eat quite a lot of branzino when I go out. The fish was cooked just right, there was so much flavor in the fish and in the topping. I highly recommend it. Another popular item from the menu was my husband's Lamb Tagine. After he had a bite of it, he was a happy man. More than he ate, he probably shared most to the rest of us cause he wanted to show what a great choice he had made. :) We had brought a cake for the birthday girl from Paris Baguette. Ponty Bistro charged us absolutely no fee to cut it and serve it. Also, unlike most restaurants do it, they didn't include gratuity in our final bill. We paid with 7 Credit Cards and remaining cash, there was no difficulty. Overall, it was a great night and an amazing experience.

I enjoyed the majority of the dishes that my group tried here, especially the salmon and ceviche. Be warned they only accept cash here. I knocked off stars because their kitchen staff were highly unprofessional - I can honestly say I've never been to a nice restaurant where I've left this frustrated! I had a really pretty girl in the group that I went with to dinner, and the guys in the kitchen literally kept standing together openly gawking at her, laughing etc, it made for a really uncomfortable atmosphere considering the place fits about ten tables. They were practically leaning over the counter to stare at her, it's like guys get a f****** grip. The server had the nerve to give my friend a piece of paper with one of the chef's phone numbers on it saying "call me maybe". Such a joke considering the amount of money we had just spent at what was supposed to be a classy place, it felt like we'd just walked out of a bar with some drunken idiots trying their luck. Won't return.

Friendly, quick, plenty of seating at prime dinner time. The whole staff was concerned that we were comfortable and enjoying our food. Like everyone else who's reviewed it, I had the mango chicken. Was not expecting such a wonderful presentation, and both the look and taste of the tofu could've fooled any self-righteous carnivore. Only reason this didn't get 5 stars was the price: $12 for tofu, mangos, and a bowl of rice. It's certainly a reasonable price, especially for Brooklyn, but the restaurant itself is more of a take-out seating area than sit-down. If things were quieter and away from the street, I'd be here every day.

I've eaten at this cart many times and loved it. Last night, however, this was not the case. I got my chicken and rice to go, so I got my sauces on the side. First, I tasted the food without sauce and something tasted "off" but I determined it was just the lack of sauce. Today (since 8am, now 5pm), I've been suffering from food poisoning and about to go to urgent care. Beware.

Best pizza in New York....the cheese oozes from the pizza and crust has that nice crunch to it. The downfall of this place is the ambiance and the wait. Â I'm pretty sure making the money they do they can at least open up a bigger place, instead of bumping elbows with everybody. Â The ambiance is pretty garbage. Â They really need to step and get someone to modernize that place. Â The wait sucks balls. Really if you valued your customers and want more money......help your customers out by again opening a bigger place and not having them wait for hours in the cold. Just Saying. Bottom line: Great Pizza, Horrible wait
Heaven on a pizza. Â Sadly has ruined most other pizza for me.

This was the first NY pizza place that i went to when i visited NY back in like 2007? We had to wait in line for the place. From what i can remember it wasn't too long. maybe like 30 min. or so. The place is small and crowded. when you sit down at a table, the next table is pretty much attached to you. The pizza portions were good. It's not TOO expensive, but it's a well known NY pizza place so it's a little more expensive then a normal pizza place. i would recommend visitors to try this place out when you're in NY or even people how live in NY and have never tried this place out. We just got the supreme pizza and it was delicious. Â :) GO GO GO!

I celebrated my graduation at Gato along my family who traveled from Mexico... we all LOVED IT! there was no dish we didnt like, and my family's experience in NYC reached a new standard. All is excellent: the grilled octopus, the scrambled egg, the paella.... Just go! You can see Bobby Flay working the kitchen! flawless! Service was EXCELLENT!

Great dessert The apple pie ravioli with maple walnut Ice cream. Â The :pasta' is made of very thinly sliced apples, stuffed with apple pie filling. The maple walnut ice cream is served on a great short bread. Very innovative. Loved it.

What a great little find. Â I had the penne with vodka sauce. Â Simple dish, but done right. Â Not really that much sitting room, but if you don't mind getting a little close to a stranger and maybe sharing the parmesian shaker, its fine. The skinny: Â The food gets a decent 3.5 - 4 stars. Â Not bad at all, not astounding either. Â Overall though, given the great price and the rapid speed at which the food came out, Pepe Rosso gets 5 stars.
Just go there, take my word for it. Â It is worth the wait. Â We stood in line for approximately 45 minutes and were glad we did. Â Excellent BBQ. Â Authentic, good stuff.

This place is VERY good - and I didn't even get a beef burger. As a pescovegetarian who also opts for the "flexitarian" term when it comes to bacon (oops), I ordered the Manly Burger but with portobello in place of the meat. So delicious. The bacon lardon on it - wow. Good enough to force me to overcome an inherent dislike of the word lardon. My boyfriend had the B.U.B. and was similarly pleased with his choice. We also split an order of onion rings. Seven rings came in the order, but given their size, definitely enough for two people. Crisp, fried deliciousness, and I was pleased that the onions themselves were thick enough not to be drowned out by the fried exterior. Calorie counts are posted for most menu options, though not all. Not exactly sure why some items are exempt. Anyway, the calories are plus/minus/neutral depending on you and your company, but worth noting. This is the only reminder that Umami is, in fact, a chain (locations in CA, NY, NV, and IL) -- thankfully, nothing else about the restaurant gives a hint of the mass production vibe. A final note: I found the prices very reasonable for a restaurant in this area. Burgers are $12-$15, beers around $8, and cocktails for $12. Not cheap, but you're probably hard-pressed to find a better price for this quality. We aren't often in this area, but will definitely consider returning to Umami next time - or even making the trip just for Umami!

I did the 3 course prix fix for $16.95 and I thought it was worth it. The food was very tasty and filling. The vegetable samosa was delicious and in an amazing sauce. The chicken tikka masala was served with white rice was very solid. The kheer was the perfect way to top off the meal. Its texture was very nice. I recommend checking this place out.

So regardless of my negative reaction from Joe's Shanghai a couple years ago. I decided to take the plunge and risk the being of my digestive system. I was craving for shanghai soup dumplings. I got it for take out and it was ready to go in 15 minutes. I must say, compared to Full House, the quality was much better. I had the crab meat soup dumplings. The wrapping didn't break and it came through after my first bite. Compared with Full House, it has a different taste to it but not a bad taste. Both are good in their own ways but I think I'd prefer Joe's over anywhere else. Definitely trying their wontons next week! Stay tuned!

Fun place, decent food. But they have some absurd policies. For example, they have a brunch dish- poached eggs and chicken sausage. I ordered that, ans asked if I could have the eggs scrambled. They said no- they can't substitute the eggs. Scrambled eggs! So, I ordered the "eggs any style" which is served with bacon, and asked if I could switch the bacon for chicken sausage. They said yes! So basically I had to do this stupid little dance to get the dish I wanted, when they serve it anyway. What could possibly be the reason for not letting someone switch poached eggs for scrambled?? Additionally I was there for a bday party recently, and we brought in a $40 cake. They charged a $2.50pp cake fee! That was $17.50 for them to bring out the cake with candles in it. It's ok, but there are better places that care about customer service.
Centrally located, great ambience and amazing wines for a good afterwork drink or meet-up or date. Â  You have to politely edge for real estate at the bar but it's well worth it once you have a seat.

Surprisingly delicious, if artery clogging. I ordered the chicken and waffle, dark meat smothered. Skin was crispy, meat was tender, and gravy and syrup is an unexpectedly wonderful combination. Mac 'n cheese was a little lumpy and congealed though, hence the minus one star. Next time I want to try the peach cobbler and sweet potato pie!
Overall, it's the most authentic Malaysian food I've had in NY!!!!

This is some luxury snack! I mean, it is $2.80 a bite (macaroon). But, it is worth it. Lucky for me, it is half day on Friday before Labor day, figured I'll get myself some treats. Walked in around 3:30pm, line wasn't too long, but gave me some time to figure out what flavor I want. When it was my turn, I walked up happily requesting 6 macaroons. I opted for the paper bag (cost extra few bucks for a nice box and paper bag) and ordered a rose petal, pistacio, ghana chocolate, melon, salted caramel, coconut and i dont remember the 7th(yes, i said 6 at first, but got 7). I love all the flavors especially rose and pistacio. BF loved the chocolate one.Amazing! Worth coming back for more, but only if I feel like treating myself because honestly for $2.80 a bite, it better be a special occasion!

Really enjoyed myself! I'm allergic to shellfish but still felt there were plenty of yummy options. My group took a while to get behind the sharing bit cause we all really liked what we ordered. But highlights for me were the patatas bravas and the patatas in alioli (sp) as well as the meatballs in brandy sauce! Don't let them fool you into thinking the patatas bravas are hot- they were just tasty. I could have eaten just potatoes and meatballs and been perfectly happy. The drinks looked good too-though I wasn't partaking this particular evening. Service was very friendly and they described anything we had questions about as well as letting two of my friends try two different wines and then decide what they wanted. I feel like a lot of places don't do that anymore. We made a reservation so our party of 5 had no problems getting in. I'd suggest making one if you know you want to head there-it did fill up pretty quickly once we were seated around 730. Definitely seems like a later night dinner kind of place. I think it would be fun for a group or for a nice date!
Loved the Kale mac and cheese. The service was great and all the food was tasty. A great place for a group to share!

I could add to the positive patter here instead I'll focus on the place's nice wine list and the bacon-wrapped dates. Â Once more: bacon-wrapped dates. Â I had four tapas, including them, and everything was faultless.

So good, I can't imagine what I could say that hasn't been said 800+ times already. So just a quick recap of what we went with: Large cone, three sauces, comes out to $8.75. Best $8.75 worth of potatoes I've ever bought. Sauces were, in order of favorite: Parmesan Peppercorn, Mango Chutney Mayo, War Sauce. The Peppercorn was amazing; the War Sauce combo of Frite Sauce and Peanut Satay didn't seem to mix as well as it sounded like it would. The girlfriend, fresh off a trip to Vancouver, picked up a small poutine, which is potatoes smothered in cheese and gravy. Also delicious. After a hard day's night, we hightailed it back via the 6 to eat our potatoes in the comfort of the hotel room. Fifteen minutes of pure olfactory temptation before pigging out in the comfort of our heavenly bed at the W.

Super cute and cozy spot for wraps. They have seats that swing facing the front window. I mean its always fun to do while eating. The loaded tater tots and wraps were amazing. Good amount of meat, flavors, and calories in one bite and it was probably one of the best things I've ever eaten when I was in my drunken state.

I've been here about 10 times in the past year. I'm consistently blown away by Donny and his attentive staff. If you want to feel taken care of, appreciated as a diner, and have one of the best meals of your life, give Pelligrinos a try!

Given: - Ethan likes spinach - Ethan likes artichoke - Ethan likes pizza Theorem: - Ethan likes spinach and artichoke pizza. Proof: - Slice was bought, devoured, and enjoyed in peaceful food coma. Therefore, Ethan likes spinach and artichoke pizza because it induces coma.

My friend and i decided to give this place a chance since it was raining hard outside and my friend didn't have an umbrella and didn't feel like getting out of Macy's. Â We went here for dinner. First the service was subpar, they did not even give us bread until we asked for it. When we got the two slices of bread it was stale, tough and old. Yes only two slices, not a whole basket of bread and we only got two slices cause we asked for one of each type of bread otherwise they were only gonna give us one slice. Very cheap on the bread.
