Secondly, the food was small portions and cost over $20 a dish for pasta. A super small bowl of soup was $10. Totally not worth it. I ordered the prescuttio salami salad and the chicken soup and my friend got the cuttlefish twist ink pasta and our bill came out to be $30 per person (include tax and tips). Basically if you want good Italian food, Don't go here. You will not get full and food is over price. I recommend Tony di Napoli or Buca di Peppo in Times square for authentic Italian food with big portions at a reasonable price. Side note: It seems this restaurant is more of a novelty and probably for tourist. By the way, the male wait staff at this place was quite attractive but our server/waitress was female.

I'm almost scared to give these guy's all 5 stars, for fear that they may get complacent. I know my middle-eastern food( Kuwait, Born and Raised). First-off, its old school making fresh pitas right in the restaurant..that makes this place special right out of the gate..the falafel is crispy crunchy and not greasy, the baba ganoush you can actually taste the eggplant. I haven't strayed too far from the sandwich part of the menu which at about five bucks is a steal...oh yeah try the lentil soup as an appetizer if you're really hungry..really garlicky and lemony!

Wonderful. We headed over here on a Friday night for a quick bite (3 of us), it was full so we sat at the bar. The bartender was great with service, the environment was great, we didn't really notice an inconvenience with sitting at the bar (which is not easy). I ordered the beef carpaccio (includes fries), which was literally happiness in my mouth. I then ordered, the skate (I think) with the sweet corn. I can't even explained how delighted I was. I'm very picky with seafood. This is just a sure 10. Each of us had ordered a appetizer, entree and a desert and we ended up paying a little under 40 dollars each. It really was spectacular. Romantic or cozy for date or small intimate group. Go!

When here for brunch on a Sunday with a group of friends. We did have reservations and were seated immediately. We did the boozy brunch for $29 per person. They are fast to fill your glass with the choice of Bellini, mimosa, bloody mary, or screwdriver. I chose the Bellini which was really good. The food we order all came in at once and was really good. I recommend the French toast and the spicy fennel sausage. The server was very attentive, can't remember his name I think Carlos, he was always making sure our glasses weren't empty and very friendly. I will definitely recommend this place for brunch. One thing, be careful going in with an empty stomach cause you could get very typsy before the food comes out. Speaking from experience

Speedy service, cash only. The chicken wings were a bit bland, despite being covered in sauce. The Massaman chicken on pad thai noodles special was good, with flavorful sauce. My friend loved her spicy pork and pineapple fried rice but complained that there wasn't much pineapple to speak of. I wasn't as impressed as I had expected to be.

Great casual place to come eat and drink. I ordered the chicken diablo sandwich which was nice and spicy (even though I like it more spicy and added hot sauce). My girlfriend had the chicken Plato which had great flavor to the beans, rice, and chicken. We also ordered the grilled corn and it was the perfect "appetizer". The main attraction however, were the margaritas. These icy beverages fool you; they will rush up to your head and make you feel dizzy in no time.
Best $6 you'll spend for food, especially in the city. Get the combo with extra white sauce. Beware of the hot sauce!!!
You can not beat a family run place where everything is homemade. Â  Don't miss out on the best grilled cheese in Queens!

Meh.... According too my sister it's hit or miss They missed when I stopped by. Maybe my standards for noodles is different from everyone else but when all 3 members of my party walks out with sad disappointed faces I know it's not just me... Got seated before the dinner rush and they got all our noodles orders wrong...

I was born and raised in Brooklyn, so I know great pizza when I taste it and L&B doesn't have it. Â Maybe I went on an off night, but the pizza here is way over-hyped. Â Go to Elegante Pizzeria in Bay Ridge if you want slices and sicilians that are authentic, fresh and tasty. The tomato sauce was excellent however the dough had a funky texture and taste to it. Â  I won't be going back. -------------------- *Update: Â I went back and it was a lot better. Â Their Sicilians are really good. Â Must have been a bad batch the first time!
Best Burrito in NYC. My favorite burrito is the BBQ Chicken Burrito. Get it, you'll love it!

If you are craving a delectable burger, unbelievable fries/onion rings, unique dipping sauces, and fresh ingredients, look no further. Â Bareburger is the perfect addition to the million restaurants in Murray Hill. I would highly recommend the bison burger. Â The meat was juicy and cooked to perfection. Â My friends had the turkey burger and beef burger and were impressed with their choices. Â You can't pass up the fries for the dipping sauces alone. Â They use creative mixes to add a nice compliment to plain ketchup. Â The special sauce is my favorite! Â We also tried a spicy relish type sauce that added the best bit of punch. Â  One of the owners, Matt, could not have been more attentive and excited to have my girlfriends and I try everything. Â After a delicious meal, he served us the most amazing fresh crisp mint chocolate chip ice cream. Â The perfect top off to the meal. Â  It will be great to have a cold beer with a burger once they get their liquor license, but for now the food is enough for me to keep going back!

I have been going to this place for a few years now. Never a complaint and always satisfied. The service is very friendly and warm. The food is excellent! I've had the salads, pastas, pizzas and wine and they are all fantastic. The prices are super affordable and a lot of variety. It can get a little crazy space wise, since it gets very busy at peak dinner times. I try to go either earlier on a later time so I don't feel too overwhelmed since the space is a bit cramped. Definitely a gem..
Okay food horrible service...

Followed the reviews and went to lunch. It was surprisingly light (yeah, really) as the portions weren't huge and the food was nice and fresh. Beware the candied yams - you can have it instead of a derest, they're so sweet....
Fantastic food. Â Expensive, but well worth it. Â I can see why it has sooo many great reviews...

Went in here on a whim and was pleasantly surprised. Really tasty food and pleasant service! Our waitress was really nice. We had the short ribs, bacon mac & cheese, seafood & chips, and the lobster roll and everything was flavorful, for the most part. The lobster roll was the only underwhelming part of the meal. It wasn't horrible, but it wasn't worth the price either. Overall, I would go back there again to try some other things from the menu.

When I looked trough the reviews I should have noticed they were about the bar and not about the food. Â The kale chips and brussel sprouts were ok but the rest our meals were not good. Â None of us finished a dish. Â These included: Mushroom/spinach quesadilla, chick pea fritters, mixed seafood grill and turkey sliders. Â I haven't written reviews before but wanted to warn anyone who might think the high star rating has anything to do with food.

I tried to get a reservation via email, and Nicole replied back to tell me that there were no tables available that weekend, without even offering me a spot for the following weekend. I emailed back to ask when the next availability was, and she never replied. Good luck making it in the hospitality industry...too bad since I was really looking forward to having some good Filipino food in Manhattan that isn't served in a joint that has TFC blaring in the background.
Food is always very good. Very clean and good customer service. What more can you ask for! I always get the pastrami. Soft fresh bread. I would def go back and recommend this place.

Another great date place. They don't serve alcohol - its BYOB of wine, but if you forget and show up empty-handed -tada! They have a phone number of a nearby liquor store who will deliver your bottle of red or white in 10 mins for free! Was pretty sweet when that happened. Food was delicious and authentic, and overall an excellent time in a cute neighborhood.

This place is gorgeous. Love the fact that we can watch the game in a place that is fun and laid back but still beautiful and trendy at the same time. It's right in the middle of Midtown so you don't have to go far our out of the way if you're visiting. Â I counted 11 Big screens on the wall.. No squinting up at tiny tv's here. Had the truffle fries.. Delicious! Prices were really reasonable. The staff was so friendly and went out of their way for us. Â We're from out of town and they accommodated us by putting our game on, even though it wasn't demand. Â Thanks for making it a great Sunday away from home!

Compared to Halal Guys at 53th St, this guys really need to up their game A LOT. However, for the price and effort, I suppose you guys can scrape 2.5 stars. Rounded to 3 stars. Meat is in chunks but not savoury like Halal guys.

Hubby took me here for my birthday. Food was alright. I had the vegetarian paella which was decent. Drinks could've been a bit better. The view from the table we sat in was great. The atmosphere of the whole place was nice too. Definitely expected way more out of this place though.

This place was fantastic. I was just here, and I'm not kidding, it totally lifted my whole mood. The music is great, the tablecloths are bright and cheery, and most importantly the food was delicious and well priced. I ordered an arepa that was made with love. I swear you could taste it. The proportions of salty meat with sweet plantain and delicious cojita cheese sprinkled on top. Total perfection. I also ordered the lemonade which had a delicious, almost maple-y flavor. It was lunch so the arepa came with a side of soup, salad, or yucca fries. I went with the salad, which was fine, but I regret not giving the soup or fries a try. I'm so happy to have found this spot. Go check it out!

I used to LOVE applewood brunch. The grits were specatular, moist, almost runny and the omlettes were creative (who puts corn or roasted carrots in an omlette??). I was not only willing, but eager, to shell out $20//pp min for brunch, on a bi monthly basis---BUT things have changed my friend, things have changed. The last 4-5 times I've gone there for brunch the grits have been awful, bordering on inedible. They're now dry, flavorless pillows of what more resembles polenta, and with the grits my enjoyment of their food as dried up as well. Please Applewood, go back to your august 2011 recipe for your grits. What you are selling now is actually worse than the 5 min quick grits I keep in my closet. That is problematic. The grits are probably 70% of what I come for-- and I've noticed other patrons' disappointment as well. It's for your own good. Going backwards is sometimes the best step forward.

Rocco is by far one of the best chef's in the city. WOW is an understatement for how our meal was. Flavor explosions in our mouths. I don't think you could go wrong with anything on this menu. The waitstaff was attentive and professional. Worth every penny. I'll be back.

This place is in a great location and is probably why the stars are inflated to an overall 4 star rating (as of this point). Right off of Herald square, it's great to go into this mysterious basement restaurant with a "tumbling E eyechart" sign spelling out MEW. Â The restaurant is a decent size inside and maintains an intimate, intellectual feel with low lighting and dark wood paneling. The waitress kept talking to my husband in korean - beware. This is a Korean run Japanese Izakaya. This was reflected in the food, where the korean food was actually better. Our group of 5 ordered the: - okonomiyaki. Japenese savory pancakes, which were not as good as the places off st marks. - deep friend takoyaki balls. I liked this more than hubby. It felt more unique because while I've had takoyaki, I've never had them as fritters! Crunchy outside, gooey inside, great flavor. Came with about 8 balls. - age tofu. Disappointing. I love this dish but they don't do a good job with it here. - chicken kara age. Similar to the tofu, this Japanese fried chicken was not up to scratch - Yakitori set A AND B. BIGGEST RIP OFF EVER. Do NOT get this. Each one is $12 and comes with 5 grilled skewers - two of which are vegetable skewers. (seriously?? You're going to give me a skewer one one roasted onion cut in half???) This alone makes this place not worthy of 4 stars. - buta kimchi: sauteed pork with kimchee and veggies. Simple, with not enough pork. - omu soba. Best bang for your buck. Only $8 and it's a huge yakisoba noodle dish within an egg omelet - spam oshizushi. Surprisingly tasty! - Light broth with different fish cakes and sausages and veggies inside. Delicious! My favorite dish of the night. I can't recall the name, but it was great! You can get it for 2 or for 4. They take reservations. Great option for those in the area! Just don't order the yakitori sets!!

This is beautiful little French restaurant along Atlantic Ave in Brooklyn Heights. They have a casual yet romantic vibe with dim lighting and superb service. Prices hover in the mid 20s for entrees so it's not cheap but it's affordable if you're looking for nice night out. To start I got the French onion soup ($7), the broth was addictive and the abundance of perfectly caramelized onions was great. They skimped on the bread only having put a small slice of the same hearty bread provided at the table (which they continually refill), and there wasn't a ton of cheese either. Regardless it was a delicious soup. For entrees me and my friend shared two of our top pics. The classic steak frites and the fish special of the day (striped bass fillet with fingerling potatoes and asparagus). The steak was supposed to be a New York Strip cooked medium rare. I found the steak to be disappointingly thin (especially as other Yelp photos of the dish showed a much thicker cut of meat). It was also cooked medium, almost medium well. The fries were average at best, no seasoning or features or flavors that made them stick out. The fish dish was very good. The fish portion was modest but it was cooked very well and had a night crispy skin on it. It was sitting in a buttery sauce which had great flavor but could have used a little more seasoning. Overall I was happy with the dish. As mentioned before the service was amazing and the restaurant overall was nice, the food I'd say is 3.5 stars but this place definitely deserves a solid 4 stars with all things considered.

Cheap-ass food for your big-ass stomachs and whiny wallets. They have all the staples here for a reasonable price. Love the forever-flowing coffee, but sad they don't have splenda, but that can be easily overlooked by the forever-flowing coffee. Don't complain about too much salt. It's called Jimmy's Diner- what do you expect? That name should immediately imply too much salt and too much butter, so come in with reasonable expectations, people.

Ambiance: Tiny, about 20 tables. Â Dimly lit, intimate, some booth tables, conveniently open 24/7 Food: FANTASTIC! Order seared peppered yellofinned tuna (spicy), pesto polenta, cafeteria burger with pepperjack aged provolone, fried egg and avocado Service: Very busy and order takes forever to come in but waiters are awesome Bon Apetit!
Incredibly disorganized front-of-house makes for a bad start to the meal. Â However, the food is very good.
The halal is soooo amazing that this cart. It is totally worth the wait!

i got here around 6 pm with my boyfriend and i had to wait 1.5 hours. i waited because this place had such good reviews. I really liked the way that had everything. we both ordered ramen. i got the Spicy Ramen (i forget the name) and my boyfriend ordered the Akamaru modern. Both were okay but i prefered the Akamaru modern. maybe it was becuase we overhyped it for ourselves, but it was not that great. i guess i was just expecting like a WOW.

If you're going for the Sunday brunch get there early as it gets packed pretty quickly. Â But that makes sense because the food is amazingly good. Â I had the cactus omelette (can't remember the menu name for this) which I'm glad I took the chance on. Â The service is really good too, which is extremely important to me, as is the decor and atmosphere. Â And odd is it sounds, the bathroom is dope! Â LOL Â  I'm looking forward to going there for dinner one day as others had lunch entrees that looked fantastic. Â  It seems very accomodating to families as all the yuppies (and there are A LOT) in the area definitely congregate there. The drinks look pretty good too. Â Maybe next happy hour? Â Will let you all know. Â Meanwhile, check out Chavela's folks.

Oh my god!! I had the most awesome lunch here last weekend, I still cannot forget it! So I had the vegetable tortellini with pesto sauce and walnuts. It was that day's special. It was soo delicious. My friends also tried from my plate and agreed with me :) Everybody stayed pleased with their food. I recommend this place 100%. Their food is awesome.

If I'm ever on death row, I want my last meal to be a slice of their pepperoni sicilian pizza. I would write more about how delicious it is, but I honest to God have a leftover slice of it sitting next to me and I need to finish eating. Best pizza in New York. Go now. Or when they're open.

Ok, so I made it my mission in life to finally get out there to try the famous square pie. Â I like that you can buy full pies or half pies. Â The pizza was really good. Â Good sauce, good crust, good all around. Â There is always a line here and the staff kind of has an attitude of heightened self-importance, so minus 1 star. Â I also had their Spumoni gelato, which I was a little disappointed in. Â I've had better at Ferrara's in Little Italy or even De Robertis Pasticceria in the East Village. Â Overall good place, I would definitely stop by if I was in the area, but I'm not sure it's worth a trip out there just to get their pizza.

Great ambiance (lots of open air coming in when its warm) and incredible drinks + food. If you're looking to relax and just talk to whoever is around you, this is definitely an ideal location to do so. Seriously, the drink selection is impressive and the food is far from shabby. My single complaint is the lack of credit card acceptance, but when I have cash, this is where I want to spend it.

I only have the best things to say about this restaurant. It is a great date night place - very intimate and cozy with a super cool vibe. The cocktail menu is great - most cost ~11$, but are worth it for the range of ingredients and quantity of liquor that goes in. There is also a fairly extensive list of aperatifs and digestifs. The menu is at first glance small but truly fantastic. I would have eaten anything on it. My partner ordered the lamb shank - delicious. Though, a slightly small portion. I ordered the duck breast with lentils - insanely amazing. Perhaps my favorite duck dish I have ever had, and I order duck everywhere. The portion was insanely large. Four slices of breast and a leg/thigh portion. To cap it off, we couldn't say no to the date pudding with il labortorio vanilla gelato - perfection again. Tip - if looking for a quiet night, ask for the table in the back. We loved it.

Went for dinner and it was amazing! Little french cafe with amazing food hidden in Murray hill. The chicken is to die for and so is the pork. We tried the apple tartin na dthat is the only thing that could be better...Would def come again!
Had to get there early for lunch to beat the crowd.

It's simple: the barbecue here is insanely good. They smoke their brisket over two kinds of oak for 23 hours, slice it thick, and sprinkle Maldon sea salt on it before handing it to you with a soft, golden bun the size of a grizzly bear's paw. You then pick a craft beer, pay them a pittance, and dump an irresponsible amount of the delectable house barbecue sauce onto your sandwich and try not to pass out from the dopamine overload. If you haven't eaten here yet, you're wrong.

So I've been to Kefi several times now, for Brunch, Dinner, and Lunch. Â They are close to a friends apartment, and so we've ended up there a few times when we want to go out for a good meal. Â  The food here is great - particularly the sheeps milk ravioli. The salads are large and flavorful, the olive oil they use is super delicious, and the cocktails are really spot on. Â The Angourri (with cucumber vodka) is my favorite. To balance the good food, the staff have always been very polite, and I can't recall a single bad waiter. The only thing about this place that drives me nuts is the acoustics - it gets crazy loud in here. Â It is fine on off hours or less busy days, but during dinner on a weekend, the noise reflects off of everything. Â I took my father here once with some other people, and he spent the whole evening asking us to repeat things, and later told me he couldn't hear anything that was said. Â  I have mostly come here at odd hours or with a reservation, so I haven't had a problem with getting seated, but the place definitely makes use of all of its tables.

Nice ambiance but food is just okay. Came here because it was supposed to be the best pretzel in the city. I don't think so. Got a bunch of veggie sides and they were TINY for $8. Only good value here is the bratwurst with sauerkraut. Wont be returning.

i remember somebody said that it's like a disneyland of italian food. Italian goods everywhere! They have everything from fresh pastas to cured meat. I was in Cheese Heaven too! Anyway, there food is good but you have to know what you want to eat. Pasta, Seafood, Meat, veggies etc. It was my first time there, I didn't know what to expect and I ended up ordering something I didn't like too much. I was thankful for what my Â boyfriend ordered. We ate at Il Pesce. I had the sea urchin crostini and fritto misto for my main entree. It was ok but my boyfriend had the seared flounder with mixed nuts and grilled peach and It was the best! I will definetly go back and try there pasta and pizzzaaa :)

From the beautiful interior to the attentive staff, topped off by exceptional food and you have a great restaurant. Try the Brussel Sprouts and Atayef & Veal Bacon which are our favorites each time we go. The wait staff is very good with recommendations. I suggest going with the small plates so you can experience a variety of great Mediterranean food. Excellent wines as well. I highly recommend ilili!

Nothing special about this restaurant, the food was tasteless and not filling plus the portions are small and bad quality. The only enjoyable thing here was the atmosphere, the views, and we had a great waiter. The setting 4 Stars The service 4 Stars The Food 1 star
You can taste the love. Luscious. Fresh, local, organic real food. Refreshing. Yes, go.

4.5 Stars Wow Scarpetta, I will be having dreams about you for a long time. I am a huge Chopped fan and was hoping to casually run into the chef Scott Conant but sadly did not. I am going to just go out and say it now. I think Scarpetta may be better than L'Artusi when it comes to pastas. (Although I'll have to go back to L'Artusi to make sure). The meal started out with these delicious breads. My favorite bread was one that had ham and cheese in it! The dips it came with was olive oil, an eggplant spread, and a mascarpone butter. Yum! My boyfriend and I shared two pastas - a black tagliatelle with seafood and a short rib and bone marrow ravioli. I couldn't decided which I liked more. I wish we had gotten three pastas and no entree. For entree, we shared the halibut which I didn't love. Although it was prepared well, I didn't care for the tomato/caper sauce. On a separate occasion, we had the polenta and it was the best polenta that I've ever had! For dessert, we had the chocolate cake which came with a caramel gelato which was delicious as well. I cannot wait to come back!

I had no idea this was a Cuban+Mexican place. Â I hadn't checked Yelp before going so I was surprised by all the Mexican choices on the menu. Â Not a big deal, I like both cuisines, I was just not prepared for it. Â But now I know that the place is meant to be a mix of both. Â  I'm Cuban and I was looking for a place with more Cuban options on the specific day I went. Â Anyways... Apart from that, the Roast Pork dish I had was melt in your mouth tender and flavored well. Â Portions were great, not too much like typical Cuban places and not too little. My Michelada was good. Â I didn't try the corn which everyone seems to be raving about. Â  The crowd was pretty and trendy Soho like all the restaurants in that area (which I like). Â  Would I go back? Â sure why not. Â  Would I rave about this place? Â eh.. Â  For pure Cuban I'd rather go down to Sophie's on Chambers St yelp.com/biz/sophies-cubâ€¦ for Mexican I'd rather go just a few doors down to Tacombi. (yelp.com/biz/tacombi-newâ€¦)

First off, to get the negatives out of the way - the restaurant is small, can feel a bit cramped at times, and it is hard to get a reservation when the sun isnt still up. Looking past that, it was one of the best dining experiences ive had in the city. The tagliatelle appetizer is sublime as were the gravy meatball sliders. The pork chop was the best ive ever had and my husband loved the arctic char. Finished it off with root beer float and some light spooning for the perfect evening.
Best pizza and calzones period. Â I know this place has a little bit of a wait most nights but it is well worth it. Â This is a must if you are in or around Carroll Gardens

We came during Labor Day weekend and had no wait. Â Between the two of us, we had the Classic burger and the off-menu Five Spice Duck Burger, the truffle fries, and the fried pickles. Â Overall we thoroughly enjoyed the meal. Classic Burger: I could definitely taste the umami flavors in this burger. Â I loved that the bun was perfectly toasted, how the parmesan crisp was perfectly salty and gave a nice crunchy texture, and the complementary flavors brought by the house ketchup. Â The patty was also moist and a perfect medium rare. Duck Burger: Â This Asian-flavored burger may have been better than the classic. Â The flavor was spot-on and the patty was juicy, and I loved the duck cracklings on top. Truffle fries: Â Perfectly crispy and thin, smothered with a gooey, truffly cheese sauce. Â Great flavors that were pronounced but not overpowering. Fried pickles: Â I don't know what was in the batter but it was light and flavorful. Â And the sprinkling of cheese over the entire dish was the perfect complementary touch. I will be back! Â Next time, I will try the truffle burger, and of course another duck burger!

Awesome 100% vegan veggie burger and fries for only $10. If you're not 100% vegan, choose from a half dozen cheese options to mix your burger up a bit. Great cocktails and mocktails. My acai berry pineapple punch was fantastic and my friend loved her wildberry mojito. The restaurant was packed but we waited only fifteen minutes for a table on a weekday evening. House music is pretty loud but adds to the fun, clubby vibe.

As I have said in my recent review, I would come back for the brunch that everyone raves about, and that I did. Stopped in for new year's day brunch with the bf to a surprise it was jam packed! Lucky for us as soon as we walked in we got a table for two right in front. Score! Looking over the brunch menu I decided on the "burekas" which came with an Israeli salad, labane cheese, eggs and some pita. The bf ordered the "Israeli breakfast" that consisted of eggs, labane cheese, Israeli salad, potatoes and pita. Basically same as mine lol. We also ordered a side of their blueberry pancakes that came with fresh fruit. When I got my dish, I wasn't too pleased. First of all I ordered burekas, what I got was they smallest little puff pastry. I atleast thought I would get two! However, it was decent, filled with feta and olives. The eggs were good and the salad as well. I enjoyed the cheese and pita the most. Same goes for the bf's dish. The pancakes were really good on the other hand. The fruit was super fresh and juicy and the pancakes were made well. I was a little disappointed with their brunch but their menu was also large, so I still have some hope that the other options will be better. I will come back to try some other dishes. Sidenote: brunch was a little pricey!

Awesome food and ambiance! Upon first entrance, the cozy decor and nearby tables give the restaurant a very inviting feeling. The friendly staff only adds to this feeling! I have come for both brunch and for dinner, and both were very good. For brunch, I ordered the shrimp and grits (normally I don't indulge this much, but it was so worth it). The nicely-sized bowl was finished in minutes! A few months later, I came back and ordered salmon with sides of zucchini gratin and their kale/quinoa/Israeli couscous blend. It was served in quick pace and was delicious, but also very balanced and healthy! Overall, the Brindle Room is an excellent mix of a comforting environment and a modern interpretation to homestyle classics!

Ahh, if I lived in NYC - I would frequent here often. Ambiance- Â loved it. Â It was a sexy- cool- dimly lit. Dinner consisted of Coles y Coliflor, Lubina Balear, y Ensalada Nevat. The open roof area in the back is so nice. I love Spanish food and this place definitely left me impressed.
food was good, waitress was great. beer is a little $$$ They need to put a little HAPPY in their HOUR!
So good we came back again 3 days later. Awesome, authentic Italian food. The polo di vitello alla piccata is great!!

I'm on the fence about this place. Â Conceptually, it's awesome - everything potato! Toppings! But the service in this joint left a little to be desired. Â They kept me waiting for no good reason, when the very thing I ordered, they all made it a point to say that it's good because it's made right in front of you (mashed potato pie). Â I sat there holding my dick until they were like - oh, you ordered? Â no I'm standing here for my health. Â Also a source of confusion was what I ordered. Â They don't give receipts either, or at least didn't ask me if I wanted one. Â That kinda bothered me. But that's not to say I didn't like it. Â I loooooved my mash pie - I got with bacon,scallions, sour cream and ranch sauce with melted cheddar. Â OMG it was so good and for less than $10 I was STUFFED for my movie night (so no snacks, which saved me $$). Â I'm looking forward to getting back there to try some other delightful tater stuff, but the staff leaves a lot to be desired. There is also not a lot of space to sit and eat.
Excellent food and reasonably priced drinks of a decent selection. It gets loud in the evening, but overall a fun night out. Highly recommend splitting a bunch of the small plates--they're delicious.

One of my favorite restaurants in NY! Had the duck shepherd's pie for dinner and friend had the skate. The profiteroles was amazing for dessert especially with the Â freezing vanilla ice cream sandwiched in between the two hot breaded pastries dipped in hot oozing chocolate. Brunch here is great too especially the egg meringue.
Nice place; several great hard to find dishes and very low prices.
Good. Japanese feel but a bit expensive and not enough ramen. No wait on weekday

God bless you, Yelp. Always helping me find the local spots that are off the grid, affordable, wonderful and all of the in-between. Of course I consulted my handy Yelp app when searching for a great place to eat in the midst of my brief 24 hour stay in NYC. We were on our way (on foot) to the Trade Center memorial from Manhattan and this was along the way. The inside is itty bitty (like many things in NYC) but you sacrifice very little in comparison of the quality, service and value you get here. The perfect date spot in my opinion! Very dim and uber romantic. The menu is a spanish/Mexican fusion with everything from pork chops to enchiladas. Since I was in the mood for a little Mexican, I went for the enchiladas. As our amazing server mentioned, they were indeed "just enchiladas" but they were still satisfying (and a huge proportion.) If I can make one huge recommendation, it's get the portobella salad. Just do it. A warm portobella mushroom topped with melted cheese on a bed of greens with nuts, sprouts and goat cheese. Dear god, it was fantastic! I want to replicate it at home! Overall this place was one of the highlights of my brief trip! Â More "tourists" should give this place a go (locals, too, of course.) :) Hell, if I could give five stars for the Yelp app check-in offer aloneI would: A free glass of their house red or white wine. Saved us $20 alone! Just go.

All in all this place was pretty good, they had several other items on the menu but we stuck to the empanadas and Guacamole (which is prob one of the best next to Dos Caminos) The empanada's were better than expected...best one was the Brazil one, it had ground beef with potatoes which was steller cuz it was semi spicy, very flavorful and the outside was not too think but still had a crispness to it...the greek sausage one was yum as well.... the 5 thumbs down ones were: Steak and cheese - Tastes like Hot Pockets Chicken - Dry and flavorless Desert empanadas were stellar...so good: Fig, cheese, cArmel : so yum! esp with icecream on the side Plantain and cheese - uber yum!!! so perfectly sweet and the cheese just amped up the natural sweetness of the fruit! Wrap up: Go here for cheap eats, if you love love love empanadas
Amazing falafel and very fresh ingredients. Love the green and Harissa falafel, as well as the Greek Salad.

Located in the heart of SoHo, we came here for a Sunday brunch during a day of window shopping and I was pretty amazed at what I saw after I stepped in. The space is pretty massive with high ceilings and tables spread out everywhere; it was definitely very spacious and comfortable, although the noise level is above average considering the sheer number of people that were dining there at the time (packed house). I was also impressed by the fact that Balthazar has their very own running bakery next door; that led me to believe the bread must be pretty awesome here. Â Therefore, we ended up getting the "Le Panier" - which is basically a basket of their baked breads and pastries. Â Everything was very fresh and pretty good. For the main entree, I've tried the eggs benedict (my favorite) as well as the brioche french toast. Â Overall, the quality of the food was very good and the eggs were properly cooked (you'd be surprised how many restaurants can't make a proper benedict). This place would be perfect for larger groups since they had plenty of larger tables and there's plenty of space wherever you sit. Â From what I can remember, the service was fine and we had an enjoyable experience here. I would be curious to come back again to try some of their other main entrees on their brunch menu, as well as their raw oysters!
Love the food and the restaurant. Â Gotta come grab a bite if you happen to be in the Soho area.

I love this restaurant. Â It's great for special occasions and so far I've been very impressed with both brunch and dinner. Â It's beautiful inside, and it's nice and spacious because of the TriBeCa neighborhood. Â The menu changes seasonally but also keeps some of the winners always on. Â The sheeps milk riccota is a must order, along with one of the pastas. Â It's a little difficult to get a reservation, but I've most enjoyed my experiences for an early brunch or weeknight dinner before the crowds get too intense.

If i can make it 100 stars, I would! I can't get over the taste and freshness of the food. My mother and I went to hopefully get some decent chinese food in china town during our stay in Manhattan so we went in here. From start to finish, EVERYTHING was delish! We had their steamed dumplings, pork fried rice, sweet and sour chicken and general tos chicken. OMG everything oyu bite into, you know it's fresh, just made with a ton of flavor! This resturante was by far the best food in new york, florida (where we live) and pretty much almost everywhere I've been. This place is a must go to!

Dark, cozy, intimate atmosphere, but be warned some of the tables are awfully close to each other. Not much of vegetarian selection, but heeyyy its a burger joint! What I did have was really good and made up for the lack of options. Â  I had the polenta, which was super thick, rich and creamy! Amazing. Perfect dipping sauce for the thick crispy fries! I was a little disappointed to see my only entree option was a simple penne pasta that I could make at home for a fraction of the $19 price tag. It was pricey, especially for the neighborhood, but I have to say it was unexpectedly good. Hard to go wrong with simple quality ingredients served hot and fresh. yum. My friend tried the burger and enjoyed it, but she didn't say it was the best burger she's ever had or anything like that. Four dudes were sitting next to us and looked a little ridiculous woofing down the burgers and licking their fingers in business suits. Based on that observation.. it must be good :) Â  Free donut holes at the end of the meal! OMG incredible! Not just because they were free, I would definitely pay for those little bites of joy! Its a pretty tiny restaurant, so I would avoid it peak meal hours.
The reason I really love Habana Outpost is because of all their sustainable practices. However, the food is spectacular as well! Perfect place to eat out with friends on a sunny summer day.

I think it was an off day but I have to say the meats were all overcooked. I give them points for delivering on flavor and great value. All the food of the hot buffet and salad bar looked fresh. Don't ask for chimmichurri, they will look at you as if you are crazy.
Good food but I need More Bukowski references! Step up your Lit game. (b)

Jackson Hole has become my go-to place for hungover brunch. They have awesome breakfast specials that include, like, everything. I've yet to try one of their legendary burgers, but they look amazing and I can't wait. Service is always efficient, atmosphere is interesting.

I'm going to get caned for giving Minca 3 stars but I like Ippudo better. Â Why? They have shishito peppers, pork buns and enough liquor to pacify an alcoholic. Minca is pretty small however the service is great. They treat you well and understand what you're saying even if you're not speaking Engrish. The waitress asked if I wanted Coke or Diet Coke...I responded with Shorke (sure and coke mashed together). Their tables also have a sticky coating on them. Â Alternative fly trap perhaps? Or to prevent one of these where your elbow slips and your face falls flat on the table? Not cute. I ordered the pork and chicken soup base ramen. Â More pork belly please. It only comes with one stinkin' piece! :| For $10 a bowl it's not bad. Â Minca is comparable to Menkui Tei. It can get packed since it's so small but when we went on a Saturday night around 9 PM we were able to grab seats with the quickness. In the words of Arnold, "I'll be bach."

The. Best. Pizza. I've. Ever. Had. This came as a recommendation from a native New Yorker and I could have sent him flowers right there on the spot. Â  The pizza was so authentic and so fabulously tasty that I am drooling thinking about it right now! Â I had the pleasure of visiting twice during our brief NYC tour and savored every spicy, chewy bite. Â  The smaller size is plenty for two and if you are dining alone, they wrap each slice in foil so you can actually keep traveling by Subway. Â I cannot WAIT to go back!!

I live about 10 blocks from this place, and I come here at least once a week to eat their scrumptious breakfast specials, drink their excellent lattes and borrow their wifi to get some work done. It is a perfect, friendly escape from my home office. The wait staff is sweet - attentive but not overly so. The weekend brunch is lovely - live music in a backyard patio? What else could you want on a sunny Saturday?

Really yummy Belgium fries. Now I am boring and just use regular ketchup or the frites sauce--but friends of mine have gone mad with some of their other sauces. Maybe I'll venture out and try some others ...well unless garlic or onion is listed as one of the ingredients--yuck !(some Italian I am)

Nice spot but like some of the other reviewers said, a little pricey for the portion size. Â The food was pretty good though. Â Seating isn't that comfortable... Made a 7:45 reservation but still had to wait for 20 - 30 minutes but hostess was nice enough to buy us drinks.

I was really excited about this place given they're related to Stanton Social and I love the Strawberry Fields drink at SS (well, I pretty much like any drink with strawberries). Anyway, reminded me that Stanton Social itself isn't that great. Both BarBacon and Stanton Social are like higher concept Cheesecake Factorys, but not necessarily with better food. I got the Bacon Torta here, which was basically a salad atop guac atop two slabs of bacon atop two corn cakes. Literally...it was like a savory trifle or an open-faced sandwich. I was not in love. We also got the mac 'n cheese, which I didn't try, and the bacon pork sandwich, which I thought tasted heavy and like a bad sloppy joe. Crowded, noisy, and not great. I'm disappointed.

Mario and Pierina make this place feel like their home, and you're the guest. All the food is homemade and everything from the wine to the antipasto are straight from Italy! Pasta was made al dente, and the chop special was to die for. Have the homemade pannacotta for dessert, and and espresso to wash it all down. 95st and Corona avenue, you can't miss it.

Literally on of the best thai places I have ever been to in NYC (and I love me some Thai...). I got their Pineapple Fried Rice, it was only 9$ and it was the best Pinapple Fried Rice I have ever had! The bacon was fantastic, the ground pork was interesting and flavorful, and the pineapple was ridiculously sweet. The decor is adorable and very appropriate to the name. I would recommend Noodies to anyone, and will definitely go again.

The Gramercy Tavern is a great place to eat. Â We were lucky to snag an open table in the bar area on a Wednesday night, reservations are highly recommended. Â The bar was full as well as the dining room. The service was very good, offering drinks just as we sat down. Â Several people inquired upon us throughout the evening. The menu is short but the food is delicious. Â I had the pork chop, thick and juicy prepared in the open kitchen next to our table. The only drawback was when we didn't order a second round of pricey drinks instead of the dessert menu we received out check. Â So we went somewhere else for dessert. Â Dinner for two with one round of drinks and tip came to $100. Â Plan on spending some money if you are there with several people getting drinks, apps, meals and desserts.

GREAT addition to the Indian food landscape in the West Village. Indian food is my favorite and I hadn't yet found a place that I loved since moving here a year ago. So you can imagine my excitement when I got my seamless order last night and it was delicious and fresh and felt healthy (not greasy at all). Â QUALITY ingredients. I had the malai kofta (creamy yellow sauce and hearty veggie dumplings), chicken tikka masala (slighty spicy to the perfect "heat" and tender chicken) and samosas (veg and chicken) that were maybe the best I've ever had. Portions are huge - I got three gigantic rices to go with my 3 entrees and will now have rice to eat for ages :) Highly recommend!

Been three times. Always super solid food, which is why it gets the four-star. Seating without a resy has seemed pretentious each and every time. Maybe the maitre'd staff was imported from Marea and thats why they are like that, or maybe its just the neighborhood. Whatever the case, I have no problems spending the money to eat there whenever in the area. Also, its been busy every time I've been there, but they could certainly stand to lose a few tables to ensure better guest comfort.

I really like Mighty Quiinn's BBQ! It is a self-serve restaurant and is great new addition to East Village. We tried a few things here and my favorite is definitely their beef brisket sandwich. They are tender, juicy and come in a huge pile. It also comes with side dishes. I tried the snow peas salad and it was great! My husband got the pulled pork sandwich and it was very delicious too. The portion is generous and he was very stuffed afterwards. The trick here is you have to find your own seats because there is no waiter service. So come early to get a table. Otherwise, you have to wait a long time.

Dined at Becco before a show. Great meal good value considering it is on restaurant row in the middle of tourist town. Very nice atmosphere a little tight and loud but it was part of the charm.Food was very fresh well prepared and served piping hot in a timely well paced manor. 4 in our group ordered 2 pasta specials which consist of 3 different pastas spaghetti marinara , pasta pesto and lobster canaloni Â all very good.The fish special was a whole fish baked brought out to your table whole then returned to kitchen and filleted and plated with potato and shaved fennel very good ,the broiled steak dusted with porcini mushroom served with garlic mashed and sautÃ© brcolirabe.We also had appetizers fried calamari , and hot antipasto which consisted of baked clams , broiled shrimp, stuffed mushrooms and egg plant rolitinie which all were excellent . Beware the portions are large (we ordered way to much) Excellent wine list and there are several selections for 25.00 . Service was profesional Â attentive but not over bearing .
. the food was fantastic and the service was exactly as it should be. it was a bit expensive but it was worth every penny . I will be going back soon!

ok,... *exhaling* this is my second time here and the first time eating. the drinks? Â 'meh' on both occasions. Â HOWEVER the service the first time from the bartender was awesome. Â this time? Â *crickets* Â it's not that busy in here and it takes 15 minutes to get the second round we ordered? Â  the food is good. the service this time? Â sucks greater than a black hole. oh! Â we asked if there were specials. we were handed a menu. Â the menu says the prix fixe is offered "daily." one person told us the prix fixe is offered "mon through thu." Â a different person told us "mon through friday" because they're not open on mondays. Â the PRINTED menu reads "daily prix fixe menu" and they don't honor what's in writing? Â *side eye* oh, the bartender? Â clearly (she is still) overwhelmed. ok, still here at the restaurant. let me finish my food before it gets colder.iI'll update this later...

As good as this food was going down, it was not awesome an hour later. I think it is important to remember that this is "street meat", and you can not base your experience on the aftermath. The Halal Guys are actually awesome. Â I got the lamb and rice with extra white sauce no hot sauce. Â They give you huge portions and have cute matching outfits. I see a lot on here about bad attitudes, but I have not experienced that with them. Â  If you are standing in an awful spot for them because you are trying to eat your food, then they might say something. Â Remember they are extremely busy making food for everyone and their moms all day so it is OK for them to be cranky. There is usually a huge line for these guys, so try to not go during food "rush hour." Â With this said, I have never had to wait more than 15 minutes for my food. Â  There is limited space to eat around the truck so plan on a place to bring it ahead of time. Â Most importantly, enjoy your street meat!

I've never had pizza quite like the square slice here at LB Spumoni Gardens. Yes, I have had "sicilian" style pizza. Yes, I have had thick crust and Chicago deep dish. Yes, I have had every type of artisinal and neapolitan pizza. And every interpretation of utility pizza and new age vegan pies. All put on traditional, sourdough, pita, cracker, you-name-it-I've-had it crusts. And yes, I have had the square pie at DiFara (still one of my all time favorites). This pizza achieves two things right off the bat. It is light and fluffly and its chewy gooey. All within a light crisp crust. Unlike DiFara square, the crust is not heavily fattened up and takes only a light crisping in the oven, versus a deep crisp texture. The dough however, grows to monsterous height. Like a good slice of Texas toast. But instead of meeting with a slice of cheddar, this dough melts....no FUSES, mozz cheese straight into itself. It does this so well that one cannot tell when dough stops and cheese starts. And just as your jaw is fusing the crust/dough/cheese together the sauce comes in with a hit of acidity. POW, keeping each bite seperated. Otherwise you'd be lost in a cheese/dough dream. I appreciate all types of pizza. My favorite being more thin crust and neapolitan wood-fired types. But I also love a well made slice that carries with it neighborhood pride and a good deal of history. If I grew up in the Bay Ridge area I could easily see this being my feeling of home. A warm and doughy comfort food perfect for sharing with the family, friends, and loved ones.

Tourist Trap! Tourist Trap! I ordered the eggs benedict and the bread was stale, and hollandaise sauce was too overwhelming - it took over the entire dish. it was spicy and unpleasant. My wife took the blueberry pancakes and they serve with it a ridiculously small portion of buttered-maple that is enough for half a pancake. when you ask for more - they charge $2 for an extra portion - we asked for plain maple syrup and still - $2 charge. I highly suggest going over to cornerstone cafe - at the corner of 2nd street and B Avenue and ordering the pancakes - you get fresh fruit with it, a jug of maple syrup, whipped cream and butter - generosity! hospitality! The people at Clinton St. Baking Company forgot that their clients are people, and not just wallets. Tourist Trap!!!

Came here at 9PM on a Sunday night and there was no wait. Â Came because I was craving blueberry pancakes and this place is supposed to be the best. Ordered blueberry pancakes with a side of sugar coated bacon. Â It should've been amazing but it wasn't. Â I don't think they use buttermilk in their pancake recipe so they were pretty bland. Â Nothing special at all. Â Did not like the warm maple butter. Â Would've preferred plain maple syrup. Â Sugar coated bacon was just OK. Â Not worth the price or the hype. Â  The blueberry pancakes at Joe Jr's restaurant on 3rd ave are much better and half the price.
great soup. very long line. definitely felt like i was on seinfeld.

Total middle of the road place. Burger was great but the fries came out cold. Â Asked for new ones, got the same batch refried. Bartender was completely unattentive to boot. Not worth $25 for burger, beer, and fries

Not sure why I feel so differently than most of the other reviewers. Â It might be that most of the patrons seemed to be from out of the neighborhood and I live just a few blocks away. On this note, it does seem that this is a destination place and not a local place which I usually prefer. The front of the house is nice enough and the place, though not my taste, is ok. I had the mushroom pizza, which was ok when i removed the mushrooms. Â My gf had the seafood pasta which was, honestly, very bad. Â The pasta was both overcooked and watery which I never experienced before. The drinks, which were heavy pushed on us by the waiter, were not really that good . Â I expected more because they promote their mixology and all but they just were good tries that missed the mark. Â The gin and tonic was good as it should be. Maybe my gf and I arent the market for this place but I really can name 20 places in a 5 block radius that is much better, not to mention healthier. Like I said, not sure why my impressions are different than the posts but I would say this place is average at its best.

Their indian pancake with eggs were good as was the herbal soup. The braised duck was slightly below average and expectation. Service was strange - with a seemingly an abundant amount of servers, our table was not cleared of emply dishes. We even caught them glimpsing over and looking at it then proceeded to walk away. Giving the small table they provided us, there was a dire need for tablespace.

Oh. My. Goomba. The falafel. The shawarma. The hummus. The red cabbage slaw. The BABA GANOUJ. (And I haaate baba ganouj.) Amazeballs, top to bottom. And friendly as can be. We entered and immediately were greeted by friendly faces offering us samples. And they did. Big honkin' sample cups of their falafel and shawarma, with promises that they would woo our taste buds. Indeed, they did. We were wooed, and damn if I didn't want to put a ring on it.
I work next door and make sure to get my Halal fix at least once-a-week. Lamb w/ rice, white sauce, hot sauce and grilled onion in the BBQ sauce = the perfect last meal. All for just $5.

Best roast pork in town! I will travel from queens to chinatown just to wait in line to get some. This place is one of those hole in the wall places that you would often walk by and not even think twice about. Like any other chinese restaurants, there are roast duck and pig hanging by the window. The interior is a bit runned down but who cares, theres really no space to sit anyways. Â The small roast pork is only $3.50 but the amount of food is enormous. The first time i ever came here, i was watching the guy chop up the meat for my $3.50 pork over rice and thought to myself when is he ever going to stop. He just kept piling it on and the lid could barely hold it down. There are so many different cuts of roast pork and he gives you a bit of all of them. The roast pork here is not dry at all and its coated with this super amazing sweet tasty sauce. Every piece is glistening (i drooled a litle writing this). This roast pork reminds me of the roast pork at the end of the movie of God of Cookery, the perfect dish. Dont be fooled though, even though theres 3 or 4 people ahead of you in line, the wait could be 15 minutes long.
The artichoke salad is ridiculously good

Went here for a bit of a midnight snack when I first got into NYC... Got the trio of Mac n Cheeses... Cheddar and fontina, smoked gouda and bacon, and my favorite... truffle oil... Truffle fries with parmesan... yes please... Anything with truffle oil... yes, yes, and yes...

I think this is my new fave neighborhood spot. I'm a sucker for convenience and accessibility and it's on the street I live on so they already won in my book lol Mad at myself for taking so long to check it out though. The $1 empanadas and $5 happy hour cocktails make me happy. Taste and quality are not sacrificed which is how it should be. These were some of the best empanadas I've ever had. Tres leches was also a hit and I love the red sangria. Hostess was especially polite and greeted me with a warm welcome and the bartender was attentive. Pretty sure I'll be frequenting.

Went for Sunday dinner the restaurant was full but we were seated in 5 min. The food was delish!!!! I got the ludacris which is straight up fried chicken wings was so good my friend had the smothered chicken with the gravy which was just delicious and my other friend had the chicken with waffles... The waffles were fluffy warm and sweet the perfect partner to the fried chicken. Sides were Mac n cheese (ok) corn (better) and fried okra which was surprisingly really good with hot sauce. And the best part of my meal was the cornbread warm and sweet! This place is a must!

The "Oxcart" is a little gem of a restaurant serving delicious food and wine at reasonable prices. It is small but comfortable with a friendly staff. This corner place looks as if it got lost on its way from Paris and had the dreadful fortune to land on Newkirk Avenue. Newkirk is like an old suicide scar running along the top end of Ditmas Park. The ugly haunted buildings lining this street are only surpassed by the overall Transylvanian darkness of this part of Brooklyn. It's like "Silent Hill" except the siren sound never came to return the place to the light. Somewhere deep below street level there must a 100 year coal fire burning. The street snakes from Ocean Parkway across Flatbush then succumbs to a bitter forgotten death at Brooklyn Avenue. It has the unpleasant task of Crossing Newkirk Plaza the miserable low rent strip mall that sits up-top the Newkirk Subway Station Home of the Q Local and B Express. I am sure that these two lines have etched on their sides "Abandon all hope ye who enter here." This mall has comfortable benches and is a perfect setting for wrist-cutting.

We heard of the crazy wait time, so made an effort to get there at 10:45am, but there was already a long line! The decor was hip/mordern, and I was surprised to see how big the interior was. We ordered the Classic Hakata Ramen($15), Akamaru Modern with extra egg($17), sizzling spicy tofu($10) and Mille CrÃªpes cake($10) for dessert. Over all, the soup was flavorful and the noodle were cooked al dente, the best part is definitely the egg, it was cooked perfectly, the egg yolk was creamy and just a little bit runny. The spicy sizzling tofu tasted similar to mapo-tofu, served in a small stone pot. The most exciting part had to be the Mille CrÃªpes cake, it's a 20 paper thin, hand-made crÃªpes layered with ethereally light and creamy custard, my favorite dessert while visiting Japan! Ippudo is definitely a great place to hang out and have good food. But for the prices, I can find much better ramen restaurants for cheaper in L.A.
If you like Chipotle, you'll love Dos Toros. Â The experience is like ordering a cheese steak in Philly: fast and rude. Â The food is nothing like what I ate growing up in Cali.

I've been looking for a place like this all across the country. Simply fantastic and inexpensive -- I could easily eat 50 dumplings / potstickers. Not really a sit-down place, but four of us just chilled in the Â middle of the sidewalk with soysauce dripping down our mouths.

my friend and i had dinner at cabana the other night. service was good, the food was excellent! the portions were large, perfect for sharing and so delicious!!!!!!!! Â i look forward to my next dining experience.
get extra cheese on the pizza, otherwise its delicious.

I live a block away from this restaurant and I'm ashamed to say that I have only been there twice. Â But twice I left the restaurant wanting more. It is a rather large place in a neighborhood like Woodside. Â They have outdoor seating and a large indoor seating area. Â The decor is nice and is pretty comfortable. Â It was jammed pack with customers and it was already 8:30 at night. Â They only accept cash. Â It is definitely more of a family place, so if you want a quiet romantic place for dinner, this might not be a good place. The wait can be rather long for dinner, so if you don't want to wait and want to try out their food, I suggest going for lunch. Â I went with a rather large party for dinner so we waited around 15 minutes for a table. Â We had to split into two tables due to our party size. Â The menu is huge, they have beer and wine menu, a vegetarian menu and regular menu. Â The whole menu consist about 30 pages! Â It took us a long time just to browse through everything to see what we wanted to order. For my table, we ordered the beef satay, fried calamari with sweet chili sauce, fried fish cake, shrimp fried rice, Nur-Sub noodles, and yellow (karee) curry with chicken. The waiters were friendly and very patient. Â We didn't have to wait long for the food. Â The appetizers came first. Â The fried calamari were crispy and delicious. Â It had a great crunch and the sweet chili sauce was great. Â the fried fishcakes were about the size of a silver dollar pancake. Â It came with a sweet peanut sauce which was great on the spicy fishcakes. Â As for the beef satay, it came with a sweet peanuty sauce and a side of pickled vegetable sauce. Â The satay were tender and delicious. As we finished with the appetizers, the waiter brought out the entrees. Â The portion for the entrees were a little small, but they were all very good. Â One thing they like to do a lot is add cherry tomatoes in all of the dishes for garnish, which was a little bit weird for me. Â The Nur-sub noodles, which tasted exactly like beef chow fun with black bean sauce, was a little too saucey for me and they used ground beef instead of beef slices. Â The shrimp fried rice was a hit and everyone loved it. Â The yellow curry with chicken was delicious. Â It had a hit of coconut milk which is why I love curry so much. Â The chicken chunks were a little too big. Â The only thing I don't understand is you have to order rice separately, I think it would be better if they would give the first bowl of rice free and charge for additional bowls, because with the size of the curry, one bowl of rice is definitely not enough. Overall, Sripraphai is definitely one of the more authentic Thai restaurants I've visited. Â They have a great wait staff, great food, and it is a good place to wind down and have a good meal with good friends.
The cubano with green sauce. oh my...dat GREEN SAUCE doe!!!

they have a really great wine selection (and good prices) and the service is awesome. I ordered 3 small plates which were all really interesting and I also ordered a cheese which was a disappointing portion size for $6. It was literally just a thin slice. I ordered the rabbit for my main dish and it was one of the best things I have ever tasted. Only other con to this place is they need to work on the exhaust in the kitchen which is right in the middle of the place. I sat outside and its lovely out there but I have a feeling that if we sat inside we would leave smelling like dinner.

Food here is top-notch, especially for the neighborhood. However, the staff working the counter seem to be under the influence of very strong marijuana and spaced out. Perhaps a touch of Williamsburg-itus. I would love for this place to succeed but they need to get the line moving and the orders right. D

I have wanted to go to Pio Pio couple of times but it was always full. Finally it was ok when I went there with friend on Monday early evening. We all like the decor of the restaurant. We picked the most popular item, madator combo. The waitress only said the potion is big enough for 3 people and allowed us to order it. The potion was for more than 4 people! I really felt embarrassed when our table was full of plates of food. OMG! I wish the waitress had suggested us some other food. The food was really nothing special. The cocktail was delicious though. I will definitely go back to try some other food.
Love this spot and super lucky it's across the street from me!

Good to try, wouldn't go back. Kind of a hike to get there. Service was fine. Ambience- very sleek and modern. Food was hit or miss. 2 plates and a dessert for about 26 bucks. Not bad for a top rated restaurant. Unfortunately we were there late day and they were out of the options I wanted on the tasting menu....Always annoying. Â  Didn't get to try the calamari. Yellowfin tuna burger -very good and delicious mayo spread. We all agreed it was the best dish of the meal. Shrimp - nothing special. Omelete- Â Could make one just as good at home. Rice bowl with poached egg- very good sashimi - small portion but very fresh/good. Desserts- some sort of chocolate pudding- nothing too great and was expecting the molten choco cake with ice cream to be better. A good tasting experience to try once if you've got the cash. for dessert we had warm Valhrona Chocolate Cake with vanilla ice cream and some sort of banana shortcake. Â both were good - but it's hard to go wrong with dessert. :) the decor is really simple and clean. TONS of windows and it was a beautiful day so all the sunlight made me happy. :) it's a bit of a trek to walk there - FAR west side.

Great Ukrainian restaurant in Soho. Good food and great atmosphere. Love their authentic outfits. And you can't beat their tradition of doing a free shot of vodka with you as you leave the front door.

woohoo! I just wannt go there for brunch EVERYDAY! I went with 3 other friends at 12pm. It was super crowded. Thanks to our reservation we got seated soon. I ordered the benedict with crab meat and my friends ordered french toast and classic benedict. All dishes were amazing. I'm not gonna comment on the dishes since there's so many people reviewing. I'm just gonna say if you are looking for a brunch place, Jane is the place to go. (make sure you make a reservation!!!)

Totally killer pizza. Â The yuppie hipster vibe is 500% worth dealing with. Â  I went with 3 other folks, and we tried a little bit of everything. Â We started with a cheese plate and a meat plate (with meats cured by the restaurant itself). Â Both were stellar. Â  The main event were the pies though. Â We tried the special pie which they were serving, which was called a Spanish pie. Â Truth be told I dont really remember what the Spanish pie was. Â It was good, but the menu'd pies were where its at. Â We ordered the Specken Wolf, The RPS, and my favorite, the Guanciale and Egg---pigs' cheek and fried egg on a pizza!!! Â I was a bit skeptical before we ate that the gimmicks would outweigh the actual quality and taste of the dishes, but not at all. Â Great crust, pizzas cooked perfectly, and the meats are absolutely delicious. Â  I will absolutely be returning.

This tiny place is perfect for a quick lunch break or an informal meeting. It has very good sandwiches and soups with seasonal, always fresh ingredients. They also have home made cookies and offer all kind of coffees/teas. If you order a lemonade they will prepare it at the moment, squeezing the lemons right there in front of you. I love the fact that the price you see in the menu is tax included, and the staff is very nice and amiable. My only remark is the tables could be bigger, they're so small it seems hard to fit more than a dish and a cup.

This has become my go-to Chinese noodle house in Chinatown, where, in case you are not aware, is in no shortage of any noodle houses. I'm trying to do lose weight and keep fit that kinda sh*t and I would restrain myself from eating carbs unless it's REALLY worth it. This noodle house well survived on my craving list, even though it's full of carbs lol. First off, order the knife cut instead of hand pull. Anyone can pull, any restaurant can pull, but knife cut is another story. It's really hard to cut it just right, not too thick that makes it hard to cook but just thin enough to keep that chewing texture. This place, nailed it. Next comes to the dumpling. Can't miss!! During my feeling-good-so-not-too-strict-on-diet period, I would order one to eat there and order a bag of 50 to go. Unbelievably CHEAP! So good... so good... And if you still have space in stomach (which I highly doubt), go for the oxtail soup. Soup is ok but oxtail is done its justice. This is a sketchy noodle house in a somewhat sketchy location. But for foodie like me, who cares =P
The other reviews have said it all, 4 golden fried dumplings for $1?! Â Eat them while they are hot and enjoy this little sinful delight.

It felt very strange to have lunch in such a Â nice place inside Macy's. Nevertheless, the experience was a positive one. The eatery is airy, bright, and vast. The staff is beyond courteous, and the food is delicious and interesting (we had the noodle-less lasagna and cuttlefish ink pasta..neither tasted like what we expected) although pricey for a setting like Macy's. I understand that Macy's is undergoing a landmark facelift, but the rest of the department store has yet to catch up with a place like Stella 34 (with the exception of the first floor and shoe zone). Not sure if I would come back here for a meal, but I am interested to try their gelato to go.

This is definitely the happening Cuban spot in all of Fort Greene. This is not your normal restaurant build...you know the Hollywood gag props that have a pair of legs sticking out from a building or a backside of a NYC taxi two stories up. Habana is the real thing with a taco druck wedged between the inside and outside patio portions of the establishment. When you first walk in (from the restaurant side), there are two lines: #1 is for everything while #2 is only for corn and drinks. I assume this is to speed up the process of ordering. The top portion of the receipt goes to the truck outside if you ordered any food. The server shots out names of ready orders. Let's begin with the Famous CORN, dare I say it rivals the corn on the cob from Smoke Joint right down the street? Yes. It is nicely charred, a little dry, topped with butter sauce , queso, seasoning, and a lime. Next up is the Cuban Sandwich voted best in NY, was it? It very well could be with roasted pork, ham, swiss cheese all finely sliced with pickles and chipotle mayo. A split crispy toasted hero delivers the meaty goodness to your mouth...is that tuna I taste? The Mexican Grilled Cheese is what we would call a cheese quesadilla made with a commercial flat-iron press. What makes the one at Habana special is the green and white sauce that they generously drown the thing in. Yum. It comes in two large pieces. I washed everything down with a small yet flavorful cup of the ginger pineapple lemonade whilst sitting outside with a hayload of patrons. It was an ideal scene for this warm summer night. I did consider the $8 for a frozen mojito steep, but I will be back one day looking for refreshment.

Good ramen, yes. Overpriced, yes. We arrived early (right before 11, when they open) & it was a Friday, so there was no wait at all. We wanted to get here early because of the ridiculous stories we've heard about the lines. Glad we did, or else I might not have liked this place as much! Food-wise, it really is pretty good. I'm not entirely sure that it was worth the money, but I would say that you should try it at least once. When in NY, right?

The line to get in here on weekend is probably worse then the line at Lavo on a Friday night. The food is great but I would rather go across the street where the food is just as great and the line is non-existant.

First off, anywhere that has custom ice cream cookie sandwiches is 5 stars in my book. My fav combo was one choc chip cookie & one choc choc cookie. The meatballs are great too - never knew a vegetarian meatball could be so good. They have a unique way of ordering food by using dry-erase markers which adds to the charm of the place. The wait can be super long and they don't take reservations, but it's definitely worth the wait.

I live in the neighborhood and was meeting my childhood friend for our weekly get together dinner, so I thought we could try it out. Â Boy, am I glad I did! We ate outside and surprisingly, it was very quiet and chill. Â The service was excellent and the food was scrumptious to say the least. Â I ordered the calamari salad and it was divine. Â My friend ordered the ratatouille and it was to die for. Â The cocktails are very original and they were also excellent. Â For dessert we shared a frozen lemon mousse which was finger-licking good. I also like the fact that it's a quiet and chill environment. Â No loud music, no loud noises. Â Just a nice, quiet West Village restaurant. The only regret I have is that I wasn't hungrier. Â Next time, I plan to get there very hungry and try the entrees.

Definitely quality pizzas. Brick oven joints are so much better then regular pizzerias. I would have given them 5 stars if I didn't have to wait so long. I guess they just have a hard time keeping up with the orders. I could under a little after tasting their goods.

Rudest service ever. Â I tipped a snippy little server Â just under 20% and she actually chased me down in the street because I guess she thought she deserved more. Â Had to ask for water, had to ask for cream twice, had to ask for a corkscrew and nobody even asked how our meal was. Â I don't know about you but eating out is a treat and I expect to be treated like I treat my dinner guests. Â The food was so so. Â My rating is based on terrible service. Â If you expect a smile and kind service, Â eat somewhere else.

Brunch review only. Menu egg offerings are many variations of poached eggs, poached eggs and more poached eggs. Sides are a whopping $5. Yet if you want to substitute bacon for kale in your meal it's an extra charge despite them each being the same price as sides - weird math if you ask me. Music was blaring so loud we had to ask them to turn it down. Coffee was offered in a paper cup?? Kale salad was good. Conclusion: Too many issues to make it worth going back.

Grape Kool Aid and Southern Fried Chicken FOR THE WIN!!! There is nothing like walking into Amy Ruth's and finding out that the Kool Aid of the day is grape! There is also nothing like biting into a thick and juicy fried chicken breast smothered in crispy goodness and real sugary sweet maple syrup on top of a thick fluffy malty Belgian waffle. Southern fried FOOD-GAZM!!! Yeah, you can say I'm a fan of this place, especially when I want to get my southern food grub on. Have been here a few times over the years and it's always pretty consistent. Great service, terrific flavorful chicken, delicious sides, and kool aid! The chicken is not greasy at all, and the waffle has a wonderful malty flavor. Syrup is the real deal - not that fake stuff. Baked mac & cheese is pretty good with a nice crust on the edges, and the collard greens are some of the best I have tasted (made with a turkey stock we were told). Plus, the fresh hot basket of cornbread they put on your table is a nice touch. YUM! The Rev. Al Sharpton - chicken and waffle for $9.75. Large glass of Kool Aid Â for $2.50. Sides go for $4.50 each. Free basket of cornbread. Not bad overall and you get a lot to eat. Our waitress here last week was funny, friendly, and awesome. Each time we have been here we always notice how nice and well mannered the staff is. Smaller dining area on main floor and larger room upstairs. Bathrooms are clean, and everyone says goodbye when leaving. Seriously, if you are the type that gives this place less then four stars go back to eating fast food KFC. Southern fried charm and goodness for sure.

I was happy to see that Greenwich had added banh mi to its collection on MacDougal, but unfortunately, this place did not stand up. I ordered the spicy brisket sandwich and it did not remind me of a banh mi at all. The bread was soft and chewy like a hoagie, instead of having the crunch of French baguette. The beef was bland and had a boring tone of spiciness with no other flavors. The vegetables were off. In the end, the sandwich tasted more like a Philly cheese steak (with no cheese of course) than a real banh mi. Disappointing. I would stick the Baoguette and Banh Mi Zon in the East Village.
great food and wine, nice intimate atmosphere. went with a variety of appetizers and some mulled wine - very happy, would come back. good pre-barclay's spot.

I've been to Toby's a few times... the food is consistently great. Pizza's are always cooked perfectly and the menu changes every few months. Salads are awesome and they have a solid beer selection. So glad that this place is a few blocks from my apartment!

I have been here only twice, and that is far from enough. Both times we had the tasting menu, once on the weekend with a group of 10 or so and once on a weeknight with a group of 4. Â Both times the service was friendly and attentive, and the food and drinks never took too long. The drinks are great. The food is ridiculously good and plentiful, especially considering the low price of the tasting menu. Both times it got to the point where we really could not eat anymore, but more was coming, -so no worries that the tasting menu is going to leave you hungry. I personally was not too impressed with Traif, but this place is excellent.

Jack The Horse is simply the best. Â I awaited the opening of this place some 5/6 years ago...I have been a devoted customer ever since. Â The decor is simply lovely. The food consistently spectacular. Â Whether you have the fried oysters, the soup of the day their steak or sokota burger, you can rest assured there are no bad choices on this menu. Whatever your proclivity, it will be met. Tim, the owner, remembers you and is very thoughtful with his devotees and Â  first time patrons alike, that Â only adds to the experience. Like all restaurants they have had lousy servers but even that is remedied by your next visit. Â Brooklyn heights has added quite a few eateries as of late and that's great, but this place will be an institution... I have to mention their Brunch, whether you need your egg poached to perfection or you rather the brioche French toast or pancakes with sausage this is also a worthy experience.. Full bar....

Saw Junior's on Travel Channel's 50 best places to eat or something and Junior's was on the list for authentic New York Cheesecake. Having a soft spot for cheesecake, I had to try. Started with a slice of strawberry cheese cake take out. It's really cramped inside and hard to tell where the line was. But of course, the cheesecake was delish! So creamy and rich. I just wish they didn't add that strawberry syrup on top. Came back for brunch the next day and it was crowded but wait was not long at all. Our waiter was all smiles and provided wonderful friendly service. I usually don't like griddle cakes (pancakes), but theirs was so fluffy and buttery. The turkey sausage links were crisp, though a little salty, complimented the pancakes perfectly. They were very generous with the bacon, they gave me like 5-6 strips. This was by far the best breakfast meal I've ever had!

As a middle eastern eating kabob is like breathing air but I'm very picky with the food I eat and the way its made and I believe that the Kabob Shack really just went the whole nine yards. Not only is it affordable, it's probably one of the best kabobs I've eaten in a long time. You cant go wrong ordering the chicken or the beef kabobs and slapping on some of that good white sauce and the fries with what they call the "kicker" sauce really takes it to another level. Usually when you eat things like fries and kabob you have this heavy feeling and you just want to go home and sleep. I have to say after eating it was a nice full. Not to heavy not to light, it's a nice place to go before you go party in the city or if you just need that place to go to if you had a long night at the bar or the club. The staff is very friendly and when you're there you really feel welcomed. You have conversation with the people there not like most restaurants where the mission for the establishment is to get you in and get you out as quick as possible. It's a very "home" style environment. I say check it out but to everyone at the Kabob Shack I say keep it up and you'll definitely see me soon.
