You've heard it before, but crispy on the outside and soft on the inside with 30+ dipping sauces (some 0.75 extra) is a good thing. Â  Zillions of calories and g of fat keep me from going there more often. Â  Note that even the regular (the smallest size) has more carb and fat calories then an adult needs. It is a very good splurge.

It has been a few weeks since my first trip to Buttermilk Channel. Yelp, was the reason I had been dyeing to stop in and man was it everything I had hoped for. I brought my grandparents and mom while they were visiting. We went for an early dinner on a Sunday night and had no problem getting a table. Our bread service was popovers with honey and salt, light and absolutely delicious. My meal was already off to a great start. When it came to ordering, my grandmother and I decided on the Sunday night special (I have a weakness for specials). When we were told it would take 40 minutes to make I was not discouraged. I started with the grilled kale and endive salad (highly recommend), anxiously awaiting my 40 minute chicken. When it came I was overly eager for the first bite. Let me say that it was delicious, no BEYOND delicious. This might be the best chicken I have ever had. It was juicy and tender with greens and bread soaked in light yummy gravy. I devoured every bit of that meal and have been meaning to go back ever since. Next up brunch.

Came here on a recommendation for good Thai food in the area. Cute little hole in the wall. Literally, blink and you'll miss it. Adorably decorated with all the kitchen action front and center. If you sit at the bar you can watch the chefs at work while you dine. They advertise being Thai comfort food, but the only recognizable items on the menu are the classic pad Thai and veggie spring rolls everything else is pretty artisan. And most if the menu ingredients are locally grown and or sourced. I ordered the pad Thai with chicken. The flavor of the Thai sauce was incredible. The noodles were perfectly cooked with the flavors of ginger and garlic jumping off the plate at you. The fresh bean sprouts and peanuts gave the dish the perfect crunch and texture. But the chicken, was very over cooked and chewy and the tofu was surprisingly tough. I also tried the Thai ice tea which was delicious for being $5...just wish it came in a bigger portion. I sat at the bar on a busy Sunday night. The waits for tables were quite long. Don't expect the greatest service at the bar though. They pretty much leave you on your own unless you wave them down. I will probably be back when I have my next craving in the area or Until I find a better spot.

I had been dying to check out a place with a $1 oyster happy hour. Â I finally pulled the trigger on this cute little place. Â It's a combination fish market and restaurant, with a small bar and a few tables. Â I was the only customer when I arrived. Â  The server/bartender was a nice guy. Â Besides excellent Malpeque and Bluepoint oysters, there were $4 beers and $6 glasses of wine. Â The bar was a great place to zone out, eat some oysters and contemplate the world (or not). Â I'll definitely be back.

Parked on the corner of 30th Street and Broadway, the King of Falafel & Shawarma makes the entire intersection smell so great you'll want to stop and eat something, even if you just ate something else. The King's food has received well-deserved accolades, including a Vendy Award, but the Astoria locals lined up at the cart at any hour of the day seem like the true measure of its success. Try the extraordinarily crispy falafel, of course, but don't miss the perfectly seasoned chicken of rice (and say "yes" to the salad of pickled veggies on the side). Â On days when I am super hungry, I go for the "Freddy's Junior," chicken and kefta doused in tahini (hot sauce optional, but recommended by the King). Don't miss this place, Astoria.
This place has some wonderful food and I highly recommend it. The steak with the tasting sides is amazing. The staff also makes the dining experience great.

Not sure why I haven't reviewed this place yet - I've been 3 times and enjoyed it. Love the beer selection. Don't try and order a Bud Light here. I think you might be kicked out. I like hefeweizens and they have a nice selection. They feature different breweries throughout the month with specials and it's a fun way to try new things. Crowd isn't necessarily my thing but I've always had fun with whatever group I was with. One time came on a quiet Sunday for lunch and enjoyed having the place practically to ourselves. Burger and fries were yummy and washed down with a perfect Allegash White. Prices aren't too out of control (Lunch for 2 with 1 drink each was $50 with tip) but some of the more fancy/unique beers can add up.
Get some cheesecake!!! You won't be sorry for these calories!

Passed by on a beautiful Sunday afternoon, took a chance and grabbed an available table in the back . Warm and cozy, great service all around and an awesome, cooked to perfection medium rare burger. Meh on the fries. But what will forever stand out in my memory will be the pickle....oh man, what a great pickle.

I think the majority of my reason for giving this place 3 stars is because of the location. Â If I'm on St. Marks, I'm not going to get a slider... unless I'm here just to try it. Â The sliders were bigger than your normal slider, with a soft bun and thin slivers of onion. Â For some, it might be considered too much onion. Â Also, my friend told me that the onions were sliced differently when he came a few days earlier. Â Sometimes they are mandolin thin and other times thicker. Â The buger was tasty. Â The shoestring fries were over cooked and nothing special. Â They were merely a vehicle for trasporting the sauces from the little serving dish to the mouth.

The selection for breakfast is a bit limited, eggs in different styles mostly, but the food was delicious, the atmosphere is great, and the service was friendly. Perfect for a late breakfast with the in-laws. My only criticism is that the service could have been a little more attentive.

Crepes in New York are usually cheap replicas of what a crepe is meant to be. Typically you get an ultra thin pancake topped with the merest layer of nutella and underripe strawberries, folded into quarters. And then they shake the powdered sugar thing and say "voila - dat'll be $6.00" Check that preconceived notion at the door sil vou plait. A friend and I were hunting for dessert. Financier was closed so we wandered. And like any good New Yorker, we found another alternative. And struck GOLD. The menu was posted outside, the place was cute (maybe a smidge pretentious) and we wanted sugar. We were seated promptly at one of their maybe six tables and had a more than lovely waitress. He had a nutella crepe with bananas, and I thwarted the bikini gods and got my own crepe - raspberries and nutella. Both come with ice cream btw. The ambiance is perfect for a low key but elegant date (think tall dark and handsome with a side of espresso). And the crepes (savory and sweet) are as elegant and well thought out as the mood lighting. The crepes were to die for. Slightly crispy at the edges, paper thin. Filled with ripe fruit, covered with just enough, but not swimming, in our favorite chocolate hazelnut spread. Topped with a perfect globe of vanilla ice cream. And for $9, its cheaper than Chikalicious, you get a seat where they don't hassle you out the door, and you get a large portion. One side note - Management? Please get your own business cards. I'm hooked and I want to share the love!
It takes me back to my childhood when we would go to Casa Â Moneo to buy Â products from Spain for Chrismas Eve. At Despana I find the wonderful treats and warm staff.

A night here with a few friends, a few pitchers of whatever beer is on special, and a round of Bonnie's wonderful catfish burgers is a great time. Â Rotating art installations add a creative atmosphere, and while Bonnie's may be popular, it's always worth the wait.

After Madison Square Eats goes away for the year at the end of May, pretty much all of the vendors move 10 blocks north and set up shop here at Broadway Bites. While most of the vendors are the same, the layout here isn't as good. It's much more narrow and stretched out over a few more blocks. That means it's much harder to just browse around and find something you like before committing, because you would need to walk back a few blocks through the crowds if you skip something that you realize you want later. Space issues aside, you can get a ton of great food here. The omnipresent Melt Bakery is always a good choice, and is located right at the beginning of the south entrance. If you've had all those flavors though and still want an ice cream sandwich, try the big Macaron ice cream sandwiches from Macaron Parlour. However, if you are in the mood for something sweet that's really amazing, you absolutely must stop by the Breads Bakery booth and get the Chocolate Babka ($12). It's that expensive because it's pretty huge, and probably not meant to eat on the spot, but it's so good two people can easily finish it. The addition of this vendor this year is definitely the best thing about Broadway Bites now. All the other usual suspects are here too to provide you with a ton of great savory options. You can get pizza, Korean, Mexican, Thai, you name it. Try a bunch of stuff, since the majority of the vendors are really great, and then save a little room for Breads Bakery to leave here really happy and satisfied.
Excellent Texas meat market style BBQ. There's often a line at times near 8, so if you want to avoid the wait, try to go before 6pm or after 9pm.

A great spot for a quick and reasonable lunch, and a welcome addition to the flatiron lunch scene. Â The place does turn into a more refined fine dining establishment for dinner service, but the great food and reasonable prices remain. Â We stumbled in late night and were fed like royalty, and enjoyed a vast selection of draft beers.

Honestly kind of surprising. Â We have eaten here a lot over the years. Â Tonight we were going to Chelsea Market for lobster and decided to come here instead. Â It used to be pretty darn good. Â The lobster tonight tasted as though it was precooked and heated up. Â Really tasteless, just really mushy and horrible. Â The only saving grace of the meal was the scallop ceviche, could have had more scallop but can't complain. Â I doubt we will eat here again, not that it was expensive, just not good.

the old location was a jewelry store with bahn mi in the back and the new location is really all about the bahn mi. while the hilarious allure is somewhat subdued its still really fresh, flavorful, quality bahn mi for soooo cheap. $3.75 for a pork sandwich! Â sweet/salty pork, fresh cilantro, carrot, cucumber and crusty bread made a tasty lunch and can be split with another for a really wonderful snack.

Excellent tapas. Braised octopus, mussels, fried goat cheese, scallops and pulled pork empaÃ±adas. All delicious. JalapeÃ±o margarita was the best I ever had. And the service was impeccable. Possibly the best service I've ever received at a restaurant.

The place from the outside looks already so inviting. The maitre D' greeted us and sat us promptly, friendly yet professional. The service was a little slow, but the place was buzzing. We had the perfect arugula salad, fresh, simple, and the dressing was yummy and had the perfect amount in it. We also shared the beet salad...a little too cold to my taste, but still fresh. the pizza was great, the crust was thin and crusty. The burger was cooked perfectly well, and very good, same for the steak and tomatoes. If you have a cocktail, try Le Boulevardier.... I'll go back.

That was a good pizza. Â Is it worth $20 for the small, apparently as there was a line of people willing to pay, for me it was a very good pizza, one of the best I've ever had. Â For $20, it's just a very good pizza, price that bad boy around 15, and you got yourself a 5 star.
The soba lunch is amazing Â  Â and the bites for dinner are delicious Â  Â every meal is different

Brunch Review. We came in right before the crazy brunch rush, the wait was only about 20minutes, which was fine since this is across from the Highline. Once we got seated, we started out w/one of their fancy bloody marys. SO many different kinds of bloody marys to choose from, it made me indecisive! We went with: -CORONA MARY: Espolon Tequila, chipotle & fresh lime -HAMPTON SHORE MARY :Citrus Â vodka, Cape May clam juice, fresh oyster & lemon Both were tasty and STRONG, just how I like it! The best part is they actually give you a whole-size celery stick in your bloody mary!! At $12 a pop, these bloody marys are kinda pricy, so you better drink it all up. For brunch entrees we got: -Huevos Rancheros $15 three baked eggs, black beans, ranchero sauce, Monterey jack cheese, lime creme fraiche, crispy tortillas, pickled jalapeno -Fried Egg Sandwich $13 two fried eggs, house-made Italian sausage, aged cheddar cheese, sesame seed roll -Finger Lakes Farm Grass Fed Burger $18 applewood bacon, white cheddar, pickled red onion, sesame seed roll, fries, chipotle ketchup We all shared so that we got to taste everything. The fries that came w/the burger were delicious, until we found a piece of glass stuck to one of the fries :X We told the waiter and he quickly got us another order and also replaced our burger as well. The fried egg sammich was great, since they left the yolk running. The huevos rancheros was really good and the size of the portion was huge!! This is a great brunch spot, if you dont mind the wait!
I want an Woorijip on my college campus so badly, it's not even funny. It's convenient and cheap, and the food is good. Perfect for a Korean food fix.

Normally my palate is a bit overwhelmed by Brooklyn's Jamaican/Caribbean Â food offerings. Normally the heavy use of seasonings leaves me choking for air or a careening into my kitchen for more water if I come across an especially bad cook who (all to often) tend to rely on pepper Â to mask a horror show of a meal - but not today. Having made my commute in one piece I decided I was a bit too lazy to cook . I had passed The Islands on many a hot night , shamefully ducking my thrifty ass in the neighboring Chinese food store, but today with my twenty in hand I nervously entered and ordered some Curry Chicken with Plantains. The woman who ran the shop was friendly in that particularly Caribbean way ; that is, she is very kind but ultimately disinterested with strangers until they become regular faces I'm guessing . Used to Caribbean portions, I noticed my meal had a little bit of extra poundage on it; a definite sign of quality rice. My arm almost got tired carrying it and I got a small!The rice was nicely balanced by the meat, and everything was lush and frag rent. I was skeptical but after I put the first bite into my mouth all I could do was dance..dance and moan in delight!! The heat in the curry was just right, the rice was lighter then I expected and the chicken fell off the bone fresh! Anyone can make chicken fall off the bone, but a place that can do that FRESH at $8 while keeping that level of spice and quality they have is rare! I'm too new to give advice, but if you want standard Caribean fare at great prices, I'll meet you in The Islands,

My friend and I tried the hotpot only, but we will come back for hotpot and korean bbq soon. The price was reasonable , the hotpot was great. I am usually picky on the cleanliness, it was comfortable enough for me to stay. The service was great! The waitstaff made sure the A/C was on the right temp for us. I hope this restaurant will continue the level of food quality and service, i highly recommend this restaurant to all!
Go there for the steamed mini soup buns, but stay for nothing else. Â For true, edible Shanghai fare, there are a couple other places in chinatown I would recommend over this place.

Came here with a friend on Saturday late afternoon. Â The place is small, and we shared a table with three other people. Â Spicy miso ramen is approximately $13, but it comes in a big bowl and will fill you up completely. Â It's not really spicy at all (if you like Sriracha, this is even less spicy than that). The pork slices were a little too fatty (one slice was pretty much all fat), but the noodles are good, and the broth is extremely rich, so I didn't get to finish the whole thing. Â Ask for hot tea, which is complimentary, and water. Â You're going to need it because the meal is quite savory. Â Service is fast and friendly.

This restaurant is so good! I tryed ravioli al fromaggio, it was really delicious :) It's quite noisy but if you want to be sure to eat something good, I recommend you this restaurant! The only problem is that we can't pay by card, only cash!

Food is ok , but there are so many other places in Midtown that are so much better (Aburiya Kinnosuke, Sakagura, Donburiya, Onya, Soba Totto) that I wouldn't waste my money here again. In addition, service is horrible. Â I've placed an order for pickup twice, and they've messed it up both times. Â The first time they prepared the wrong order and refused to make it right until I threatened to leave. Â The second time they didn't prepare the order at all and I had to wait 15+ additional minutes for them to make it. To make matters worse, they refused to let me use the restroom as they said it's only for "dine-in" customers, not "takeout", which is ridiculous.
Go into the city oftern and can't keep out of this place for lunch or dinner! Â Prices are fair and portions are enormous.....quality is there completely.

Chef's table was more than a dinner to me. Â It was like watching a live art show where you see the artist painting live on a blank canvas. Â With only 18 seats (I believe) and serving half the seats at a time, there is detail and love put into every bite sized dish. Â  When I walked in, I was blinded by the squeaky clean shine the kitchen exuded. Â All stainless steel including the horse shoe shaped counter us patriots dinned on. I had heard there are about 18 to 20 bite sized portions served. Â This made me a be skeptical as to, if I'd need to stop by the near by McDonalds and super size my Fish'O filet to be satisfied. Â Like Golielocks said, "it was just rite!" Â I wouldn't want any more or less. Â  Each bite was an explosion of favors. Â Trying to detect what each taste was is part of the fun! Â The sorbet that prepped my palate for the next course was green and reminded me of sushi. Â Why did this sweet sorbet remind me of sushi? Â Ahhhh, the Shiso leaf I sometimes wrap my sashimi in was in play! Â Who woulda thunk that green leaf would make such an awesome sorbet?! My favorite dish and I mean favorite!! Â I'm still have dreams about it... was brioche topped with uni and (drum roll).... shaved black truffle. Â I peed in my seat with excitement!! Â Spectacular!!! Â I was trying to scheme up a plan to get the other diners bite size as well. Chef's Table is not to be missed. Â Yes you may get carpal tunnel from hitting redial button trying to get that impossible reservation, but its worth it!! Â I've dinned all over the world and have never had such an avant garde dinning experience as this. Â Don't miss out!
I wanted pork belly S but Â it was already sold out so i got bulgogi S. It was pretty nice not that spicy with juicy pork and fluent toppings awesome.

This place has some of the best ambiance and decor of any restaurant in NYC. The food was equally remarkable. Â We started with the scallop appetizer -- soooo delicious. The scallops were grilled and topped with this slightly sweet compote and a little creme fraiche with a drizzle of balsamic vinegar around the plate, then topped with some arugula and crispy plantain. Â Perfectly balanced bites! Â  I had the pork belly dish in dashi with a poached egg on top and my gf had the venison - both very good too. The venison is quite a hearty dish, served on a rich helping of mashed potatoes. Our server Delano was awesome too and really knew all the details of each item on the menu. A new top 5 for me based on the beautiful restaurant and amazing food and stellar service

I came to ilili last night (weekday night) for restaurant week and upon walking in, I was really excited. The decor is intimate and classy, and the place was packed! My friends and I got a drink by the bar until our table was ready...which was also packed. We finally got out table and our menus. You get to choose 2 apps, 1 entree, and 1 dessert. There are some dishes that you can pay a supplement for. Since I was with a big group, we tried many apps. The best thing that was on the table was probably the falafel...and the pita bread that's served with the appetizers. The tuna belly was not what we expected. We thought it was going to be served raw but it was cooked out dry. The avocado sauce on the tuna was amazing, though. The steak tartar was compressed and creamy, but not in a good way. It was tasteless. Their only saving grace was the dessert. The candy bar and cheesecake (I got to try both!) were awesome and I want more now just thinking about it.
A west village bar! Why not! The location itself qualifies it to visit - besides it helps that they serve up some nice cocktails!

Came here for $2.50 pork & rice baby! Decor: 2.5/5 -only 1 table with 1 chair -Be prepared to wait Service: 3/5 -service can be slow but that's cause there are only 1 main worker and his wife(?) Food Presentation: 4/5 Taste Buds Say: 4/5 -Roast Pork & Rice: A classic and favorite of many. Definitely get this if you can't decide. -Crispy Pork & Rice: REALLY good yet really FATTY. I felt sick after eating this.. It was that good I couldn't stop eating. -Chicken & Rice: not the halal. The chicken has bones and was a pain to eat. -See the photos, the food is ridiculously packed into a small container. Wah Fung 1, Halal 0. TIP: Don't get the large $3.50, he just gives you alot of rice and a tad bit more meat. $2.50 is the best bang for the buck!

Early on in the school year, my roommate and I decided to make the epic journey from Manhattan to Brooklyn, in search of the Holy Grail of Pizza, aka Di Fara's. It was a long, exhausting journey filled with lots of reading and crowding on the train, and by the time we actually got to Brooklyn, there was a small, hand-scrawled sign on the door: "no more dough, will open again at 7:30pm". We had arrived at 6:30pm. Any shopping malls or book stores to lounge around in and wait? Nope. After walking around aimlessly for an hour, we returned only to discover a large and rapidly growing line in front of the small door. Waited about another hour to get our pizza. It was 8:30 by the time we retrieved our beloved prize, and by that time my stomach was already eating itself. Therefore, I'm not really sure if the great flavor of the pizza was due to the fact that I was severely hungry or from the pizza itself, but the buffalo mozzarella and the fresh basil were awesome. The pizza was a little on the greasy side, but nothing a little napkin dabbing can't fix. Holy Grail? Maybe. Worth $5 a slice? Questionable, at best. But unless I move to Brooklyn, this was probably a once in a lifetime journey.

I am not an expert on Korean food whatsoever but I do got a good palate. This is not much of restaurant it's more like a eat-and-go kind of "deli" that it's mostly used by employees of local businesses. The food is nonetheless good. The buffet is limited which is a good thing because you are not overwhelm with choices.

We arrived to NYC late on a Friday night from LA and needed some good food. Â This place is always open late...always open! Â The place was vibing with cool music, and interesting people just having a great time in NYC. Â The hostess was very cool and friendly. Â The waiter was OK, but not great. Â The bus boys stood around making small talk with each other too much. Â However, we had fun. Â The Fresh Fig and mixed Greens salad with crispy proscuitto and balsamic dressing was Freaking Fabulous! Â You know what else, the Atlantic Salmon over plantains with asparagus was insanely delicious, and the Veggie Burger might have been the best beef-substitute EVER. Wow. I have been here before in prior years, and don't remember the food being super-fantastic like it was in Friday night. Â So, buyer beware, maybe only these menu items are 5-star. Â But this place is too cool, and I love it! Â Have a drink, have a salad, have a meal, and have a flippin' fabulous time in Manhattan. Â Please.

Jane has great music and the brunch menu offers a good variety. Server was prompt with drinks and after we ordered our food was able to upsell us some 'starters'. We ordered biscuits and cheddar grits - biscuits came out, but grits did not. Followed up with the server and she said she thought we wanted it with our meals - but we wanted it as a starter. Food took a bit of time (half hour) and arrived cool, fries were cold. A bit disappointing because of the wait... Had higher expectations because of the wait time and reviews.. I think service could also use an extra person when it's this busy, as tables could use more attention.

I live a few blocks away from Bar Bruno. Â Since they opened, I have walked by and admired the renovation, but the menu always seemed mediocre and uninspired. Â I finally tucked in with a friend this morning for a late Columbus Day breakfast thinking maybe I was missing something and the food tasted better than it looked on the menu. Â  The atmosphere IS great - a welcome addition to the neighborhood -- intimate, great decor (vintage European Cafe). Â with full bar, nice music. Unfortunately, the food is just as uninspired and mediocre as the menu looks. Â I doubt I will ever come back. Â There are way too many other choices in the neighborhood for great, fresh tasting food and this is not one of them. Â It's a shame. Nothing about the meal was tasty. Â I had the asparagus and goat cheese omelette. Â My friend had the egg sandwich. Â The egg sandwich was on toasted whole wheat. Â Not particularly good bread. Â The omelette was slightly overdone, the asparagus over-cooked. Tasted like something you'd get in a diner. Side salads were made with tasteless mixed green with soggy mediocre dressing. If they could take just a few notches up on the food, this place could be great. Â I wish the menu and food matched the extraordinary effort and vision that went into the space. Get a decent chef and you guys will have a loyal Cobble Hill foodie crowd in no time!

HIGHLIGHTS: PORK BELLY APPETIZER BIBIMBAP OK: Prime Beef Shabu My New York friends know me as a shabu connoisseur (or would that be, shabu addict?) so on a recent visit, we ate here. Â It started to get busier around 8, so I'm glad we were early and had a reservation. The prime beef shabu was decent - our table of 6 shared one hot pot to cook everything in. Â My shabu spots on the west coast are one hot pot per person, but I do appreciate that we are at one table, sharing, it becomes a more social experience that way. Â There was no shortage of veggies. Â The goma (sesame) sauce was good, the quality of the meat was solid, but I wasn't blown away.

i loved my brunch experience here at abc kitchen! i had my birthday brunch here with one of my best friends, and the food was pretty amazing and fresh. Â bc our food took awhile to prepare, we were offered a fresh tomato and mozzarella salad (delicious). Â following our complimentary salad, we split the tomato toast (like bruschetta) which was perfectly salted (and almost pizza like). i had the eggs benedict and hot chamomile tea as well. Â everything i thought was perfect (it was my birthday after all) and even the decor was pleasing to the eye.
On point! Ordered the pulled pork and its one of the best pulled pork I had anywhere. I'm gotta admit I'm really surprised considering the area. I will order it again to see if they are consistent.

I went here last week for a late dinner, and had the best enchiladas that I've had so far in NYC. As for the decor/resaturant, the place is fairly small and the tables are very close together. We were sat literally right next to the door, and there was another couple 2 feet away from us. If you want your own space, this restaurant is not for you. That being said, the wait staff does a good job getting you in/out. Apparently they don't take reservations either, so be prepared to wait, especially if you have a group of more than 2. The prices were pretty reasonable, and with a laid back atmosphere, you can have a few drinks with friends while you wait for your food, or after you scarf down your plate (portion size is good too).

I really like Ootoya. Whether it is the very mid-range chain outlets in Tokyo or this absolutely superb outpost in NYC, the food is always great. The kurozu or black vinegar preparations are each one a delight. The salted grilled Saba or mackerel is succulent and laden with taste in every salty bite (if you like fish, of course!), and the onion and daikon salads with bonito flakes are yet to let me down. I liked the Hokke yuen though the fish tastes better just grilled with salt, and have also enjoyed a couple of the tonkatsu choices. Also excellent is the Yakitori - and the oyako don. Not big on pork belly, and they won't budge on substitutions so the hot pots remain untried. And not big on sashimi either so that shall remain forever untried. Get the set meals. Avoid the raw egg topping! And eat big when you do get in (no reservations, and long waits always) - they don't serve dessert so real estate reservations are unwarranted.

Don't try this truck!!!! Â I dont usually do reviews but after reading such high reviews, and driving an hour drive in traffic, I felt I must review this food. Â The food was horrible. The chicken was too spicy with an after taste. They served regular white rice with a slight yellow tint instead of basmati yellow rice and the white sauce taste like mayonnaise. I love Halal chicken and I was greatly disappointed. I've had better food from the trucks near Jamaica ave.

Living in Williamsburg for over 6yrs, it's hard to keep up with the restaurant boom and all the new places popping up. I'm glad we ventured out to this place because what a gem! It was a quaint and lovely restaurant. As someone who loves fried chicken, I decided to try new foods that I've never had before and I was glad that I did! Fried green tomato with remoulade sauce (which was unreal) was a great starter! My meal consisted of chicken fried steak with grits, 2 sunny side up eggs, biscuit, and strawberry jam. The problem with this meal is that it has now set the bar extremely high if I decide to have chicken fried steak somewhere else! Everything was so flavorful that we can't wait to go back and try everything else. Usually when you land on a dish you love, you end up getting it over and over, but with Beehive, it seems like every table ordered something different because it's the kind of place where you really can't go wrong. The owner was friendly and involved. I'm sure beehive will prosper because of such great cooking and customer service. We look forward to coming back many times and eventually making it to their delicious lookin desserts.
Small, so make a reservation if it's more than 2 of you. All the food is great but the Txakolina wine is the best part!

Wow finally!!! Shopping Monday in soho and ventured off the path a bit.. Came upon this place and found out it was it's first day open. I'm so glad I wasn't the last to know about this gem. First of all the staff was extremely friendly and knowledgable about their products. They carefully explained their menu and gave me great recommendations on what I should order. The prices were good and the food was even better. I recommend this place to everyone and I advise you not to leave without having an espresso! You won't regret it. Thanks La Panineria and welcome to the neighborhood.

There are so many great things to say about this place. First off, it seems like it's packed every time but magically there have always been one or two tables open, never had to wait. The menu has so many types of pasta to choose from it's really overwhelming and so far they have all been good. It's like what grandma would have made if she was Italian. Good quality, always fresh. I have to reinforce what people have been saying here, this restaurant is one of the BEST values in Manhattan. It would probably cost more Â to make this food at home (unless you have a big family). Good place to bring your out of town friends too :-)

We met old friends here the other night, and I only chose this place due to its location. Â Our food and drinks were Â excellent. Â The cauliflower and the arugula salad and flank steak were exceptional. Â The deviled eggs were not exactly my personal fave style, but the eggs were cooked to perfection - no over boiled blue eggs here. Â I forget the cocktail I had, which prompted a second one. Â Our server was delightful

Came here with my lady friend on a Saturday before a broadway show. Â Awesome cocktails and delicious food. Â I had the lamb and she had the chitarra. Â Both were terrific. Â We were too early for a busy dinner crowd but it was still a cool atmosphere. Â Would highly recommend...

Went back again for lunch. Had the grilled cheese with swiss, fontina, and white american on sourdough with fries ($8.50). The combination of cheeses was alright, but it was not completely melted throughout the entire sandwich. Was looking forward to the fries since I had heard they were really good. They were alright. It was an average sandwich with average fries. Even during weekday lunch, it's crowded and noisy here.

The only complaint I have about this place is that they refuse to take reservations for parties of 6 or more! Come on! Use a credit card to hold the reservation....oh wait, they are too cheap to take credit cards. You would be 5 stars if you corrected this stuff Bianca! More importantly though? The food is amazing!! And so very reasonable! All the pasta is handmade and homemade! Do NOT MISS the Lasagne or the Gorgonzola Gnocchi! Typically good as gnocchi is? It is usually like lead balls in the tummy. NOT HERE!! light as a feather! There is actually too much in the portions to finish. Truly the best kept Italian food secret in Manhattan! The soup with a broth and parmesana cheese and the spaetzle like noodles? A meal in itself!! I have dined here 3 times now. Totally consistent. Once was a party of 11! EVERYONE enjoyed their food! And basically NO ONE could finish! We're a foodie supper club to boot! I am headed back with some friends in a few days. Can't wait!!

LOVE THIS PLACE. Their artichoke and margherita pizza are really good. I've heard the crab is a hit or miss though. Their slices are HUGE. Pies are HUGE. Such a good place for a late night snack. The only thing that sucks is that it's tiny and the line can get reallyyyy long, but so worth it. There's always a few benches outside where you can sit while waiting. Too bad there's no place to eat. Either stand at the counter or outside, or eat while walking home. (:

Great staff and good food, I only have the boiling crab in Vegas to compare it to but I liked this place much better because it wasn't as spicy and you could taste all the flavors better. Â The waitress was very eager to help, cause I guess they just opened, so water refills were happening about every 8 minutes and napkins were being taken away every 10. Â They take the orders using iPhones and give you the receipt using an Ipad mini so that was pretty cool. Â The absolute best part of the meal was dessert, it was a flan they call a "creme caramel", thought it was a little pricey at $4 since it looks exactly the same as the flan you get at Vietnamese bakeries in Chinatown, but the flavor and consistency was absolutely amazing. Â Definitely recommended! Â Tip: if you don't eat that much, share a combo with someone and order a side of carbs each, it would be too salty if you ate it on it's own. Â It's a lot of food!
Slightly expensive, but desert here was good.

We were looking for an Italian restaurant in the area, found "ToJ". Â Its a very cozy little tavern. Â Very comfy and warm feeling. Â The peeps are friendly. Â We had the mussels which were out of this world. I had the shrimp pizza yummy! I guess that's the Italian part. We would definitely go back to this place even though its not an Italian restaurant! Definitely comfort food from grandma's kitchen!

The bread and falafels are great, the hummus is mild. If you order the falafel platter, make sure you share with someone, because it's big. The space is relatively tiny, but enough for the neighborhood. We five people had to share a four people table.
this place has a good selection of beers and really yummy apple bread pudding... Will be back to check out brunch

Very kid friendly environment. Â I highly recommend the blackened fish tacos. Warm and inviting ecclectic atmosphere will make you want to stay for a while to enjoy a second or third mojito, which you may need if you have a lot of children.

PD does it again, amazes me, for $2.25. Today, I ordered the fried pork dumplings (#4) and sesame pancake w/ vegetables (#21). I figured it was a good day to go, with a snow storm, so that I could get a seat and eat my food as fresh as possible. The fried dumplings, I thought, were as good, if not better than the boiled dumplings. Such flavorful meat in these tiny dumplings, and the two sauces they provide at the shop go perfect with it (hot chili sauce and a brown sauce). The sesame pancake is what I regretted not getting last time, so I was left with extreme curiosity. It was awesome. Amazingly soft dough, flavored with the vegetables and plenty of sesame seeds, and only $1.25. It's getting to the point where I almost feel bad paying THIS little for THAT much food. They might as well be paying me to come in and eat. But, I'll take it.
the food equivalent of cocaine in a foil tray.....theres a reason theres a line for this place every day..! $6 well spend....be warned....you will want it every day!

The pizza is authentic and the pepperoni and meatballs were a good choice for toppings. Â Service was as good as the food which came out in a timely fashion. Â I'd go back if I was ever in Brooklyn again.

I had dinner at Almonds about 2 weeks ago. I brought a friend in because I live in the neighborhood and the food is great. I hyped up the place a lot. We sat down and put in our order, the server was very nice, attractive Latin guy, can't remember his name but he was great. After we received our food and began to eat, I stopped because I saw a mouse run across the dining room. I was mortified, but not 100% sure. So I told my friend. After about a minute we both saw it run across the room. I was absolutely disgusted. Earlier in the summer I had a similar experience at Almonds, only this time it was cockroaches. I disregarded it because I figured it was the heat. But after seeing a mouse...I just can't . It sucks because I'm a very picky eater and Almonds has a great selection of food and wine. But it's obviously not a clean restaurant.
best ramen in the city (so far), better than the places on 1st ave. they make it right in front of you and they have the best pork out of any ramen place.

Is it wrong that I only want to eat here again for the delicious, tangy naan and smile of the guy who runs the place? They're open 24 hours (I'm almost certain), and tons of guys were standing around at 11pm eating, listening to music, and chatting with the owner. I saw a taxi idling outside. There's nowhere to sit, but if you like standing, that'll work. Don't be afraid to ask what everything is, because he'll tell you happily. Get as much naan as you feel comfortable ordering. Don't expect this to be a formal affair. The food is really good for the price (cheap as hell), but nothing is gourmet, and it's microwaved for you. It's kind of ramshackle and rundown and has a lot of charm because you know people come here twice a day. They even sell weird Indian films on a shelf behind you.

Love this place!!!!!! Â Beautifully designed, superbly staffed, and an amazing beer selection! The vibe in The Jeffrey is laid-back, welcoming, sexy and sophisticated. An absolute must-visit while in NYC.

YUM, YUM AND MORE YUM!!! I have been hearing about Belgian fries for years being the best in the world but never tried them thinking I needed to go to Belgium to get the real thing. Â Enter, Â Pommes Frites on a Sunday afternoon after a long walk around the city and you've got yourself the most mouthwatering snack you've ever imagined. I never thought I would like mayonaise and ketchup mixed together, but my friend (who visited Belgium) and I devoured the fries with the "especial" sauce and were talking about for days. Â If you're looking for authentic and heavenly Belgian fries, Â you must go to Pommes Frites.

This is my first time at a Spanish grocer. Can't say that I know what authentic Spanish food tastes like but I definitely know what a good sandwich tastes like! I had the Picante and it was delicious. The bread was so crispy, just the way I like it! After ordering, there's seatings on the side where we settled and enjoyed our food. There's complimentary olive oil on the table; I dropped some on the sandwich bread for taste and it was so good. Prices are very reasonable for soho area ($8.50 for a sandwich), definitely plan on being back here some other time.

La Goulette is the best addition to Grand St! The food is fresh, healthy, and every dish I've had, I think I've tried everything on the menu, is incredible. Can't go wrong. The owners/brothers, Karim and Anise, make it an experience - they're friendly, helpful, and passionate about their food. Only issue is, I can't stop eating here.

I guess I don't know what British fare really is, I'm ashamed to say.. For a pub on a Friday, Cock & Bull was quite empty. We were sat upstairs but since we'd be the only table, moved down to a pub table. Started with the sausage rolls. Sausage wrapped in puff pastry is always going to be delicious, and these did not disappoint. I had the beef and ale pie, which I guess is their specialty. I wish I had gone with the chicken pot pie as I didn't live the beer broth. Good service though, and, from what I can tell, good traditional British food.

My boyfriend took me to Five Leaves while I was in town this past week, and it was a perfect date night. We arrived there around 8pm on a Friday night, and he let me know that there would likely be a wait, but there was a bar. Indeed, there was a 30 minute wait, but we kept ourselves happy with drinks at the bar. If you don't have patience for tight space, I would say don't go on a weekend, but for me, the ambiance (despite the packed house) was worth it. The specialty drinks were incredible! I suggest the Foxtail. The bar was a bit awkward and cramped, but I would have done that over waiting outside in the cold, for sure. I filled myself up with the INCREDIBLE cheese plate and salad, I was so thankful my boyfriend and I decided to share an entrÃ©e, the pork chops. The entire meal was cooked to perfection, but I still can't stop thinking about the cheese. The entire plate was amazing! The entire experience was perfect for a date night on a Friday, and I highly recommend it!

I stopped into Jimmy's Diner for breakfast on a rainy Saturday morning. I sat at the counter. I was impressed with the service (a fellow with facial hair). The waiter was quick, ready to crack a joke and seemed to know what my order was going to be before I said it. Â  My coffee came with a little doughnut treat. My huevos rancheros was delicious - hearty and just the right size. I will definitely at Jimmy's again.
The best Italian food you will get anywhere besides Italy. :) I would recommend this place for any occasion.

I love, love, love this place. The shoestring Â fries, the cheese plate, the steak, all perfect. I had rosÃ© and a different sparkling drink both were good. You must go here. Go with a friend that lives close so you can put your name down and them go hang out until they call you. Yes the wait is long, but this place is worth it!

Fantastic brunch spot with the girls! Â Had dinner here over a year ago and was equally satisfied this visit. Â I think we ordered just about everything on the menu. Â Loved our server, he was friendly and kind enough to explain the menu to us. Â Oh and most importantly, they had the BEST Bloody Mary's I had all week in the city and by Saturday we needed it!

The boy and I decided to take a leisurely Friday night stroll all the way from Hell's Kitchen to the Lower East Side in search of the city's best meatballs. I'm spotting a distinct trend in our activities: we will go to the ends of the earth on foot for a delicious meal!!! Everyone's been raving about Meatball Shop, so naturally, we had to try it.. when we got there, there was a 2-hour wait for a table inside. But having trekked all the way across the city for a mouthful of meat, we were not prepared to wait and opted to sit at one of the tables outside. Despite the chillier temperatures. To mitigate the cold, I ordered some tea. I was determined to have my meatballs right away. Anyway... we ordered two heroes -- one with spicy pork meatballs and spicy meat sauce and the other with beef meatballs and the mushroom sauce. At $9 apiece, I would definitely bulk The Meatball Shop in with the city's best food deals. The food arrived fairly quickly, and we promptly proceeded to stuff our faces. I started with the beef meatballs/mushroom sauce. Something was just NOT right about this hero... instead of mushroom, the sauce tasted like some sort of candy? My boyfriend had the same reaction! Vaguely reminiscent of Good & Plenty...? I was wholly confused... and not in a good way. On the other hand, the spicy pork/spicy meat sauce combo hit the spot! Very satisfying, pretty large (although not as big as a foot-long at Subway, as my man felt the need to point out), and great soft texture. Long story short... was this place life-changing? No. Would I trek across the city to fill my mouth at Meatball Shop? Probably not. But would I grab a hero on my way back from Fat Baby at 1am? Absolutely. By the way, the service was absolutely perfect in every way. Despite being seated outdoors in the cold, we were repeatedly checked on by multiple servers. We did not feel in the least bit abandoned. On the other hand, we were a little confused when not one but two bar tables became and remained empty during our meal (as we saw through the window). Why couldn't we eat in the warmth?!?

BECCO. ..OMFG LOBSTER RISOTTO. ..if you need a warm & salty fix, get this. This joint was crowded ..(Saturday night) Aside from some crazy drunk lady asking me my age and getting wine on me.. I recommend trying this spot at least once... it's good if you just saw something on Broadway, or went to the discovery museum, or you're near times square and in the mood for decent Italian. The servers are soooooooo effin NICE. Our waitress opened new bottles of wine for us to just taste and see if which one we preferred, she totally didn't have to do that. 3 bottles later we found our winners. We ordered so much food, so fat. Egh god so fat that night. But hey I think it's nice the food is good, only thing I didnt care for was the Cappuccino, (the espresso tasted burnt and weak), and the pesto pasta, that was very blah.

Like they even need another review to say how awesome they area. EVERYTHING is good here. The staff, drinks, food, brunch, lunch, you can not go wrong. Just go. Deal with the wait that is there every Sat/Sun morning to eat here. It's worth it. Sometimes I'll go alone and find a spot in the bar area pretty quick. Okay I talked myself into it, I'm crawling out of bed and on my way now. 945AM on a Saturday morning... Robertas here I come.

Oishi Des!! I've had ramen everywhere from Kyoto station to dowtown LA, and Totto Ramen is truly something special. This tucked away little secret embodies everything ramen should be. From the tiny kitchen with huge stock pots to the eat-and-run vibe, this place is straight outta legitville. I had the original chicken ramen, so perfect. The broth was lightly seasoned with deep flavors, and not to greasy. The noodles deliciously chewy. I got mine with an seasoned egg. YUM. I went early, 6:30 on a Monday night and the place was packed! Be prepared to wait... but it's SO worth it. There isn't much else on the menu besides ramen, but really, why would you come here for anything else?

The wait here is usually about an hour plus on the weeknights/weekends but it is totally worth the wait. Their ramen is really fresh and their soup base is delicious. My favorite here is the spicy ramen. Their appetizers such as raw octopus is good too ... it's octopus chopped up into small little bite size pieces marinaded in wasabi. Oh and of course their pork buns are to die for! This is a must have when you come here :)

Chargrilled burger and shoestring fries are on point. The burger has a nice full meaty flavor and the cheese makes it a very dense bite. At times the flavors are almost too rich as it seems to be with every dish in this place often bordering on too salty when earn together. The gnocchi plate is among the best offerings here tasting very smooth and buttery and the chicken liver toast is also a delightful dish. The seating is a bit cramped but the atmosphere is definitely very hip and I saw Anja Rubik dining upstairs so don't be surprised to see supermodels dining here. It was packed even on a Monday night. Get here before 7 and you won't have to wait for a table. Also a bit of a pain of the ass to get here since there's no subway stops nearby.

DELICIOUS! Â This is a review for the brunch at Cafe Condesa and it is DELICIOUS! Â This is a small neighborhood cafe in the heart of the West Village - no scene here on a weekend morning/afternoon - people coming from the gym, meeting up with friends, handling a hangover with the tasty and headache curing muddled fruit mimosa - whatever one needs, Cafe Condesa has it. Popular with the brazilian crowd and usually has soccer (real football as some would say), on the television if a game is on. Â Small and quaint, can't accommodate parties larger then 6. Â Perfect for couples or a small group of friends.
A little pricey but good food. I had the steak and garlic potatoes - it was great! Good enough for a meal if you dont want it as an appetizer

Great restaurant week, the portions wore just perfect I love the taste of the entrana and my fiance love the chicken The fish tacos wore amazing and the chifa ceviche as well Â  I wasn't to crazy about dessert but they wore good I will return again But do way get the wine special $25 dollars battles.

Yay to a new and nice lookin' food court! Â This place has little muenster for yummy grilled cheese sandwiches, num pang with their awesome banh mi, the umami burger, sprinkles, skinny pizza (isn't that contradictory?), dos toros, chop't, etc. There's plenty of seating throughout this place and it's super clean! Â It's also at a good location and on the second floor, fyi!

I was looking for a good lunch spot with parents in Chelsea and even though we were over on 7th, a friend recommended hiking over to 10th for Cookshop. Â I'm very glad we did. Â Having a friend you can always rely on to give great recommendations is such a luxury. Â Oh wait, that's why we Yelp. The food is farm-fresh ("haute barnyard"), seasonal New American fare. Â The lunch menu has a lot of healthy and non-greasy options. Â I opted for the chef's salad which had huge, spicy dandelion greens, beautiful slices of smoked ham, long fingers of patÃ©, and both fava and butter beans. Â Definitely not your typical chef salad. Â The real winner was my dad's bluefish pate, which while listed under the "salads" was really more like an amazing version of bagels and lox. Â The plate came with a jar filled with really incredibly good bluefish patÃ© (one of the best uses of bluefish, really), a home-baked bagel (or pseudo-bagel, I'm not quite sure), and a pile of sweet caramelized onions. Â Definitely order it: it's delicious but not something that immediately jumps out at you. Sitting in this airy, bright, air conditioned restaurant you can even watch the little people, sweating away on the High Line.
Ordered the bash burger. It was fine. I guess I just don't have taste for american burger..

heaven in my mouth! got the spreads (tsatziki, taramosalata, melintzanosaata, revithia), grilled octopus & bean salad (octapodi stin scara, revithia, fasolia, tomates liastes), arugula & chicory, dried cherry, apricot, walnuts, manouri, raspberry-thyme-honey viaigrette. and the highlight of it all: the grilled branzino, potato, olive, tomato. the spreads are ok, but other than that twas delish~ everything was light, full-bodied in flavor, and made me extremely happy. between two people we had all of this & it felt good. the service is fine, the food is good, i will be back.

There is so much to love about Bohemian... from the dark rum mojito to the artfully prepared seafood and other additions like the mac and cheese and wagu beef-- everything is cooked to perfection. The best way to experience Bohemian, in my opinion, is to order in a "tapas style" so that you can share a bit of everything. The rib eye is my favorite cut of meat they offer, and you cannot skip on the mac even if you think a Japanese restaurant is not the place for such an order. It's hidden, we walked past the door five times before finally finding the entrance our first time here. The secret phone number and speakeasy atmosphere add to the delight of dining in such a special place. The restaurant used to be Andy Warhol's apartment-- I mean, how much cooler does it get? Go to the bathroom while you're here and test out the Japanese toilet with the water jets and heated seat. I've sat at the bar for the most part, the tables seem too far away from the chairs in a living room couch to coffee table type of way, but I guess that adds to the charm. The staff is incredibly helpful and friendly. I'm coming back soon.

We went to this little restaurant before heading to a broadway show and the staff were really friendly and happy to help! They ensured the food was brought out swiftly in order for us to get to our show on time. The menu had excellent vegan options (try the curry, the chickpea burger, the beets and the roasted sweet potatoes) but also the salmon cakes were delicious! The roasted cauliflower and the zucchini stuffed with quinoa lacked some serious flavor which was unfortunate. But give the juices a go! If you want to have a delicious, healthy meal with some options for vegans this is the place to go. The setting was nice - make sure you get the table facing onto the street for people watching.

I've read all the other reviews and it pains me to do this but I'm going to have to stick with 3 stars. Â When I first heard the concept of italian grandmas preparing a custom menu every night I was sold. Â But I knew there'd be a hitch - it's on staten island. With that out of the way if there is any place worth a trip it certainly is this. Â Getting there for a non-native such as myself was a cinch. Â The staten island ferry is free and in the current beautiful weather - a bit of fun as well. Â Once off the ferry it's a short walk (~5-7min) to the restaurant. We had a reservation and a great table near the door. Â The space is small but doesn't feel cramped. Â It's like you're in someone's house (or perhaps basement with the exposed brick and industrial lighting) and their grandma is slaving away to bring you some home cooked goodness. Â  Going into menu detail would probably be a waste of time since it changes daily but I'll say the appetizers were pretty good. Â Fried oysters were one of our favorites. Â Our server was a bit scatterbrained and continued to be a source of anguish during our meal. The owner was there and everyone was extremely friendly. Â I just wished the food was BETTER. Â I'm not a real food critic but I did grow up in an italian household and can easily tell good pasta from bad. Â None of us could believe how mediocre the pasta/rice dishes ended up tasting. Â  I'd really have expected a better selection of pastas and really utilizing the specific talents of the nights chef. Â  I loved the place, I loved the trip, I loved most of the people, I just wish I could say I loved the food. Â I really didn't. Â I'm hoping I caught them on a bad night. Â I'd still recommend people go try this place but just dial down your expectations a bit. Â I'll probably go back in a few months to give them another shot. And no matter what they tell you there is NOT an 11:30pm ferry back to Manhattan :(

Stopped in here after reading so many positive reviews on Yelp. I got the squid ink linguine (Linguine Neri alla Monsignore)- the portion was huge, so much seafood on top I thought they'd brought the wrong order! Â The food was served promptly, and was excellent. I ate alone, but it would be an excellent place to take a date or eat with friends. One thing stopped me short of 5 stars- I ordered diet coke with my meal. Â The waiters asked each time between courses if I wanted another. When the bill came, I was charged for all three, at $2.50 each! Most restaurants will comp your refills if you're drinking Soda. Â Frankly, most restaurants wouldn't charge $2.50 for a bottomless diet coke. That was my only complaint about an otherwise excellent meal.
Great food, cool atmosphere reasonable prices. I had the enchiladas which were very tasty. Â Guac was solid although needed some salt, cool bar too. Â Great addition to LIC

Great place! They were out of the mussels, so I chose the hamburger. It was definitely one of the best burgers I've had. Very fresh and cooked perfectly to order. Â They had a great beer selection as well. I had Resignation Brewing Company's KCCO Black Lager (Chive on!) which was awesome. The service was great too. Quick and attentive.

Not so much a House as it is a hole in the wall, but I'll take it. Â It's dirt cheap for good food. Â My friends swear by the fried dumplings but you definitely get more bang for your buck with the boiled shrimp dumplings. Â They were savory and soft, just like they should be. Â We also got the duck sandwich, which was good, but some hot sauce is definitely needed to add some pazazz to the food. Â But $5 for dumplings and a sandwich is absolutely perfect for my broke ass. Â Also, you should just go (if you haven't already which I'm sure you have) just because it's fun to battle over the limited amount of seating. Â It's a battle to the death and I refuse to loose!

This place is weird. They serve pretty good food (pork belly and the chicken come to mind) but the atmosphere is confusing. There's enough room in the center of the room to dance. There's also a bar and a standing area. So on a Friday or Saturday night if you come here for dinner your table may be flanked by people dancing or standing around and drinking. It's also really loud so definitely do not come here on a date (unless you don't want to listen to each other). The good part about this place is their kitchen is open late, so mcdonalds, pizza, and hot dogs aren't your only option past 1am.

Upon arriving, you see that the restaurant will be a charming experience from the beautiful wood door entrance that leads into a foyer/cellar of apples with an overpowering apple aroma (I don't know if this aptly explains the experience, but if you go you will understand - very unique!) The restaurant is exceptional. The service upon arrival is tremendous. The staff is very gracious and welcoming, moving at a relaxed and comfortable pace, which is a little different from the traditional hustled pace that I felt at other NYC restaurants. The food was absolutely magnificent and delicious. Overall, a wonderful experience. I can see why Bouley has multiple Michelin stars! Â If you want the very best and want a charming experience, this is it.

We went there for brunch on Sunday, starving because we spent an hour trying to find some place where we could have a table without a 45 minutes wait... We finally sat there and shared a very good cheeseburger followed by an enormous albeit not very fresh waffle with strawberries and cream. Â It was too early to test it, but it seems that the place has an extensive choice of Belgian beers. I also loved the decoration, with posters depicting excerpts of Tintin, and a wall reminiscent of a train wagon. An overall charming impression!
Flat out awesome! Whenever I'm in Midtown I have to stop at this place. For the price and the amount of food you cant beat it. Fills me up and there's usually a wait but it's so worth it.

Loved the food. French toast were not overpowering- just right. Very yummy. The cucumber ginger ale is worth trying - at least once. The shrimp ranchero with avocado is very filling & scrumptious. Definitely one of the better satisfying brunch places. However, Service during seating is a little slow :(

Carne asada burrito was closest to SF/mission style I've come across in the city! Â Meat could be a bit more grilled ie charred (as opposed to just cooked through) but that's a preference of chargrilled taste over a softer texture. Nonetheless, solid.

Just too overrated, too crowded, too pricey, I'm not gonna lie you have a good pork bun which exactly the same thing as what my mom cooks for me at home. Besides that you are just an ordinary ramen place which quickly became another food chain business. I have tried you twice which mean I gave you 2 chances to impress me but you are just okay. I like the staffs though, they work hard and they deserve recognition.

People are probably giving this place good reviews because of the river side location, but for me, I don't think so. IT is always crowded, long lines for the tables. The food is terrible. It is frozen or mass produced, soggy bread for pizza and burgers. frozen fries. Salad was romaine lettuce and tomatoes that's it. And I'm definitely not a high maintenance person, but yuck. The drinks are watered down. Yes if you want to go and have a pitcher of beer it is nice once, but don't ever eat there please.

This just opened in the neighhborhood. They're all so nice! I tried the Terri Berry and the Green Power smoothie...It's a vegan/organic shop but you wouldn't know it by the taste of the food...Both were great! I'll be back for sure.

3 Stars- "A-OK" This place gets a 3 star rating because it 'does the trick,' in terms of thai food in general. Its also 3 stars because I'm from the west coast, and out there the basil, cilantro, and mint are clearly distinguishable from Â cardboard. Aside from Brown Sugar in Boston- my general view on eating thai on the east coast is that its not unlike listening to music with the bass & mids and no hi's. That being said, if there was no west coast- or Thailand for that matter, then Sripraphai would be as amazing as the NY Times describes!
Yummy!!

all you hear inside oasis is "falafel sandwich" over and over again. I don't know if it's because it's super cheap, delicious, and vegetarian, but that's what 90% of people seem to order. I myself Â go for the "vegetarian platter" with the unbeatable trifecta of hummus, tabbouleh, and falafel for 6$. I can't not have all 3, they're all amazing. my bf gets the meat sandwiches, and he loves them, so branch out, people! also, when my family was in town from NC we went there to get take out for 8 people. they were quick, generous and cheap... everybody was stuffed for like 45$!!!!

First time I visited this place with one of my friends I fell in love-usually I'll go to a place maybe a second time or even a third to make sure but this place I didn't even need to do that. I tried their "fish burrito" and I honestly thought I was eating the real fish, it smelled like the real thing and tasted-Pheww! But not only I enjoyed what I love (fish) but the healthy way (you can say). My friend had the breakfast platter which included the turkey bacon, home fries, wheat toasts, eggs-I tasted some of her food-lets just say I wanted to order the same thing after I had my food ha! I like where the place is located, in Williamsburg and coincidently my yoga studio is not too far from it-now you know I'm happy about that. So before/after my yoga on the weekends I can go grab a smoothie-perfect. Like I posted on foursquare (tip)- even if you're a vegan, vegetarian, pescatarian whatever you'll like this place, you'll enjoy the good, environment and where it's located. They accept cash/credit :-) Most importantly there's a big "A" on that door from the health department-awesome!
Best food in Chinatown. Â Order the wonton mein soup. Â Roast pork and duck are favorites along with young chow fried rice. Ask for the ginger and hot sauce.

Like a Chipotle version of Mediterranean food but slightly higher quality and price. The hummus and whole wheat pita were delish. Falafel was flavorful and not dry with a slight kick (tried Harissa flavor). Large quantity of food, definitely a meal and a half for me.
Stopped in recently for lunch for two. Chicken curry and meatball banh mi sandwiches. It would be pretty challenging to find a better sandwich in NYC for less than five bucks.

I have tried many Halal carts in NYC from Brooklyn, Manhattan and Queens with the highest rating. I have to say, this place tops all of them. The meat and rice just compliment each other and is not blend like many other places that need their sauce to create taste (like 53rd in Manhattan). I certainly recommend!!

A nice place for dinner. Great freshly made iced coffee, made personally by the server, Adam. He recommended the whole wheat penne with salmon. When he heard that I didn't like fish, he immediately said that it can be made with chicken. The meal was delicious. The chicken was grilled & the pasta was marinated in pesto sauce. Thank you Adam for your service. :)
The pizza here is delicious and the service is wonderful. I've been here two times and both times I have been impressed. If you want grub after going to Ulysses, hop on next door!

OK we went to the Brindle Room for lunch today. It's a little small but big on the flavors. MY wife had the five herbed chicken with sauteed kale, roasted garlic and horseradish, I must say a Great combination. I had the burger which they are famous for, and I can agree with that. It was approx six ounce burger very tasty made from the Deckle cut of the rib-eye cut. It was 80/20 mix, cooked med-rare, unbelievable taste, juicy and perfectly cooked. It was accompanied by had cut fresh french fries, crispy on the outside creamy on the inside. The burger is So rich that anything more that what was served would have been a waste. Def going back for another crack at that burger.....

This is my favorite wine bar in the city. I love to catch up with friends or grab drinks before an evening out here. I love the cosy atmosphere and the wine list is extensive. Best for small snacks and lots of wine. It's very chic so remember, those 2 $ signs only cover your drink.

We were in the mood for Italian food...this place popped up so we gave it a chance. The food, atmosphere and service was 5 star. Really great. The Papardelle with short rib ragu was outstanding. We had 4 other dishes and each was equally impressive. A must visit. You won't be disappointed.

Thank you thank you thank you. Â To a great company with great food and the best service. Â They catered my wife's baby shower and everything was absolutely perfect!!! Â From the presentation, quality of food and flexibility they are the best.

I really wanted to like Ippudo, but alas, the ramen is overpriced and mediocre compared to anything they have in California. I've been to the one in east village as well, but the only thing they have to offer is their broth. I got the shiromaru hakata classic and there was nothing special about their meat or toppings. The lunch special with the eel was also badly proportioned as well. The buns were good, but again, nothing I would come back for. Love their service, but for the wait time I would go somewhere else.
Not sure why people rave about this place. Â I'm not saying it's not good, it's just that there are plenty of places that are as good if not better. Â Not a place I would go out of my way to eat at.

I got food poisoning from them. Abdominal cramps, diarrhea, fever and chills, nausea and vomiting Â - all within 3 hours of eating there. Vomiting lasted for 6 hours and now i have severe dehydration and even a subconjunctival hemorrhage due to the vomiting. Still nauseous. No food is worth that.

I love living on the Upper West Side but the major downside is the lack of interesting restaurant choices in comparison to our neighbors downtown. Â I read early reviews of Kefi each more flowering than the next so I was excited to finally try it. Â Kefi definitely lived up to its hype. Â I have gone a few times now for lunch, and on each visit I found the food fresh & Â full flavor. Â I highly recommend the White Bean Soup special if they happen to have it available. Â Its a subtle blend of white bean, tomato, spinach, spring onion, dill and lemon.....I think. Â (I am determined to crack this recipe b/c I really want to make it at home). Â  Having just returned from Greece I was a bit hesitant to order the Greek Cobb Salad but what an amazing new interpretation on the old standard, twisting it up with shredded lettuce, lounza (smoked pork loin - yum!), graviera (greek cheese), sun dried tomatoes and yogurt dressing. Also worth trying is the Kefi burger, and their grilled octopus. Â  If there is any downside to Kefi I would say in my experience the service was inconsistent. Â On each occasion a host or waiter failed to greet us and we were searching for anyone to help seat us. Â The waiters are pleasant enough but when we needed service our waiters went a.w.o.l and we were left begging the busboy for another drink, the check, etc. Â Nonetheless, Kefi is definitely a standout of the UWS. Â Their portions are generous, the prices are modest and it is well worth a visit.

I thought the food was solid. I would like to give this place 4 starts but I can't for a couple reasons. THE GOOD: Bartender was very nice. We had to wait about 10 minutes to get a table so we went to the bar and had a drink. The girlfriend ordered the Red White and Blue special, it was a good value. We were seated pretty much right when the hostess told us we would be which was good. Our food came out in average time. It was good, the portion sizes were what I hoped we would get for the money. THE BAD-ish: Service was just average. A little slow to take our order. Slow to pre-bus our table and never really checked on us during the meal. Also, the downstairs area for the bathrooms smells.....strong. The soap dispenser in the bathroom I used didn't work and everything just felt dirty. I just didn't feel the restaurant was as clean as I would have hoped. Food presentation was lacking a little. When they dropped off certain items, they had the oyster crackers just sitting on top of the sauce; not what I would like to see as a patron or a server. Wrappers on top of my food seems a little out of place when you're paying over $20 for an app. Overall I liked the food and the atmosphere but I won't be rushing back there anytime soon.

Really one of the best meals I've had in the city. It's a local neighborhood spot for us, but tend to consider it a "treat" to go. The breakfast/brunch is great to tuck into especially during the weekdays if you have time. I love the eggs served with small fresh tortillas and homemade guacamole. The pork quesadillas were excellent to. We finally made it and sat at the bar for the tasting menu and splurged that night and got the wine pairing too ($32, I believe but well worth it if you can drink a ton of wine, they'll keep pouring it). The chef and sommelier really pay attention to what they're serving and work together on "pairings" checking in on the next course's ingredients vs. the grape. Each dish was better than the next--the chef is careful to listen to your likes/dislikes. We told him to serve up anything. He started us out with delightful seafood dishes and graduated to heartier meats, etc. before finishing us off with a light salad and dessert. A couple sat down next to us mid way through our meal and he began serving them an entirely separate menu which shows he really takes pride in offering Â these "tastings".

My mouth is still watering thinking about this place. We had an absolutely fabulous experience here. Food, service, and ambiance was all top notch. My favorite part of the meal was the cole slaw. Usually, I refuse to eat it because I don't really like the way it tastes, but here I was literally licking the bowl clean. I wish they could ship some of it to California. My pastrami sandwich was one of the best I've ever had as well. And don't get me started on the cheesecake. The chocolate mousse one had me licking my fork in a less-than-ladylike way. Our server, who I wish I could remember his name, was wonderful. We were in a large party of loud, obnoxious women, and he put up with us. Never had to wait for a refill or flag anyone down. We took care of him handsomely, but he deserved it. The decor was very Brooklyn, with a Brooklyn Dodgers mural on one wall. I loved the vibe. I will definitely be back here next time I'm in NYC, and in the meantime I will dream about that cole slaw and cheesecake.

Cozy little dining room that transport you to a lobster shack in main with a hip feel. All the meal options come with choice of beer or soda. I had the taste of Maine which was a half of each roll. The half size is comparable to one of a slider but it is a good sample platter for first timers. After trying the three, I decided that I prefer either the lobster or the crab. Each roll is buttered and toasted while the meat is cold but juicy and tasty. The crab roll was soft and flavorful while the lobster roll provided the same experience with a more substantial texture.

Oh, Sweet, sweet Falafel Gods!!!!!! I'm in tears thinking about how I must go to NYC again for the best falafel. That's right, THE BEST FALAFEL in the world!! I didnt think a place would exist that could master such a simple dish... but it does! and it's name is Mamoun's!!!!! *Insert "STELLA!!!!"-like Scream here* You cant get good falafel on the west coast, so it was an extra special treat. I came here on a recommendation, and it was truly one of the best places I ate in New York. 3 bucks for a falafel sandwich that is tasty, light but filling, and totally satisfying. Their tzatziki is nothing like Ive ever had. Wonderful and flavorful. Their veggies they use are fresh, their bread is warm, the falafel is light, crunchy, moist, and flavorful. Truly the best Ive ever had! The hot sauce they have on the table is the hottest freakin' hot sauce Ive ever encountered in a middle eastern/Mediterranean restaurant. It is potent and can ruin your sandwich if you put too much on, be careful with that shit, people! You have to come here! Just look at the awesome reviews!

You don't have to like the pizza (you must have faulty taste buds) but don't hate on DOM because he's the man. (you must have no heart). The wait is certainly ridiculous when you consider the fact that you can't really wait inside the place (it's tiny, crowded, and it will make you smell kinda greasy/smoky) and the fact that there's immense traffic on Avenue J. BTW, those of you who complain about the location (you wimpy Manhattanites who don't know what a daily commute to work is like), stay home and order Dominos then. There's plenty of us that don't mind that it's in a residential/local business/not much to do area. BUUUT since this is just a hole in the wall pizzeria, you should not expect much of an atmosphere anyway. Which is fine by me because the pizza here is unbelievably freakin amazing. I couldn't stop thinking about it days after I ate it so I got some last night and yes, went through the ridiculous wait again but all is forgiven when you see Dom (that's his name right?) hard at work on your dough..removing a perfect pie from the oven and putting in the box, drizzling it with olive oil (watch that baby bubble!) and scissor-cut a bushel of fresh basil onto it..and don't forget the perfectly salty cheese. It's heavenly..it's tantalizing, it's unforgettable, and worth the wait. Granted, some parts of the crust can get burnt but that's what adds to its genuine, hand-made with love and CRAZY SKILLS charm. p.s. Dom and the chick who takes the orders actually smiled at me this time. I know it doesn't count for much but for Di Fara's standoffish attitude, it's service with a smile.

Well let's just say the beers are cheap and the meat is yummy! Went to this local corner dive for a burger and beer on a Sunday night, and it took almost an hour to get a table...but if you go, WAAAIIITT and get a table. The burger is pretty delicious and while you might get a delicious bacon cheese, feta, mushroom, egg, everything else you can think of burger elsewhere BUT the meat in this patty is better than most other places...and overall enjoyable!

I love this place, the gluten free breadsticks are so awesome and I'm not even gluten intolerant. The risotto and pizzettes likewise are both delicious, the taste are always on point. I also have to give a special shout out to Josh B. who always has a smile on his face and gives me quick, accurate and fun service every time. Â The only thing I would suggest to management is better pricing on their wine bottles.

We stumbled upon Root & Bone by accident. We were down in this hood because I had a groupon for a place nearby. In my infinite wisdom I didn't see what time that place opened...which was 5pm...not 1pm when we were there. womp womp...Well Yelp to the rescue. This came up at the top with 4 stars. And well, we were standing right next to it. Anyway, it's a southern joint in the East Village so it's not really "southern" inside, it's more East Village inside. The waitress was excellent, and asked if we'd been there and explained the menu. It's small almost tapas style but with the option for a full plate on many of the menu items. We opted to split and try multiple things. We got the chicken and waffles, brisket meatloaf and just regular biscuits. All were absolutely excellent! The biscuits, while not amazing were very good and the sauce that comes with them was great. I think these could be lowered in price a buck or 2 though. The brisket meatloaf was not like we expected (which is good), it isn't a heavy "loaf" it is pulled brisket and it was great, could have been a bit warmer but still great! The chicken inside the chicken and waffles...wow. just wow. I will go back to get just the fried chicken, it was outstanding!!!! And they give you maple syrup. The drinks were good, we only got one each because we weren't in the drinking mood or spending lots of money mood. But, they were very good and had a punch. Of course the one I ordered came in a dainty tea cup...man card revoked. But it was good nonetheless. I will give this place a go if I'm back over here!

It seems this spot is probably a better choice for dinner - my friend and I had brunch here and just thought it was ok and nothing that stood out as amazing.
