The brunch menu is rather limited, and what we did end up getting lacked taste. The enchiladas were bland, as was everything else. On a more positive note, the cocktails are very reasonably priced, and are by no means weak. The bloody mary was good, but could have used more heat.

This place is without a doubt one of the best ramen places I've ever been to. The broth with the extra spicy added to it was fantastic! Noodles were very fresh and with the pork and egg additions made it all a great meal. I also had the pork bun, which was a great small dish to lead me into my ramen meal. Also, the service at this restaurant we phenomenal! Never have I experienced this type of service at a not so expensive place. 5/5 food & service

Wanted to like this place. Service was terrible. Sat an hr after our reservation. After finally bring sat we ordered. The food took over an hour to come. It was very tasty but super delayed. Only getting 1 store for the music. That was the only decent thing about this place besides the view.
Pizza in new york is difficult to rate but this place does a pretty good job and saving its reputation. A lot better then you two brothers pizza for $1.
Great place to hang out with friends! Awesome sangrias.

Food was really tasty. I had the pate to start (special), which was very good and a very generous portion. The rigatoni bolognese was excellent. The bolognese sauce was very light but seasoned perfectly. The service was friendly and attentive. The decor is really nice, kind of rustic and the light fixtures are really nice. They look like old milk bottles!

I've been going to the 53rd Kati roll for quite some time, I will write a review here and there. Both places have a very busy customer line but this location was sampling out tiny shots of masala tea. The tea wasn't fancy at all, no spices in it, just simple chai and milk. Hmm, they need to try harder on that for sure if they want a following. As for the roll themselves, they deserve 5 stars of course. Juicy, kick in your mouth spicy but dies down quickly to taste the other spices. The naan is neat and not too buttery/oily. Highly recommend it
This is place is really good. Â The curry chicken katsu was really yummy. Â Miso soup was so so.

In a word; disappointing. It's no wonder to me how this place has fallen from one of NYC's hot spots to where it is now. The service is fine not great, our 7pm table was not ready for us until 7:15 which also took me having to speak with the manager to get seated. The food was Â between ok and good, certainly nothing special, Especially for the price. Insalata salad and the guinea hen were very good, the veal was poorly prepared, a true sign of an a restaurant that does not belong in the upper echelon...we won't be going back.

I went for dinner with a few colleagues from work and had such a good time. This place has lovely ambiance and excellent service. Very good selection of wine and beer as well. For starters, we had the 'Chevre claud' tartes flambees (goat cheese, honey, creme fraiche and bacon).....freakin unreal, a must try! I had the 'nemrod spatzle' and Jeremy (the owner) suggested I tried it with bacon, I am so happy I listened to him. The spatzle had a lot of flavor, creamy and delicious. The bacon really took it up a notch. A few of friends had the "le burger a la strasbourgeoise" and loved it, I will be sure to return and try that next time. When you come here, don't hold back on the desserts they are fantastic. We had apple crumble, creme brulee, chocolate mousse and a tarte flambÃ©e Â apple w/caramel & grand marnier--- yes, we pigged out and it was so worth it. Over all experience is a full 10. This place is so cute and intimate, I will most definitely come back!

Top Ten Reasons to Eat at Joe's Shanghai: 1. Soup Dumplings 2. Soup Dumplings 3. Soup Dumplings 4. Soup Dumplings 5. Soup Dumplings 6. Soup Dumplings 7. Soup Dumplings 8. Soup Dumplings 9. Soup Dumplings 10. Everything else you can thank me later.
Sanfords is AMAZING. My favorite is the pecan crusted chicken salad. Their burgers are great as well.

I went once a couple months ago, and loved it so much that I went back another 3 times since. Â I also brought my friends (who are getting married) to try it out, and they liked it so much, they asked if they would cater their wedding! Â The brussels sprouts are delicious (like everyone says), and I really like their French Onion soup. Â My girlfriend (who's a very picky eater, and now my fiancee) loved everything so much that she tried everything! Â I mean, she even tried my fish...and she doesn't do seafood. Â She hates onions and soggy bread, but really likes the Onion Soup as well (although she leaves all the onions and bread behind). Â Overall, a great experience every time. Â Also, the staff has always been really friendly.

The entrees took a long time to come out, around 15-20min, but luckily we had ordered the calamari appetizer. The calamari is seasoned well and comes with a garlic yogurt sauce for dipping. The complimentary Turkish bread that came is fine, nothing spectacular, so we didn't bother filling up on it. The Kofte kebab comes with 4 big flavorful meatballs. The swordfish is charred and has a great meaty flavor. Both dishes came with pilaf rice, salad, and carrots. The servings are huge here. The service is attentive and polite. The menu isn't large but they do a great job on each dish. The dishes are about $15 each and the portions are worth the price. The crowd eating here is a bit older and it's quiet place to have a low key chat.

I finally stopped by in here for lunch and I am a happy camper. The place is nice and clean and the staff is friendly and attentive. The menu features a brunch theme in addition to salads and burgers. I ordered the angus beef burger, I was so hungry that I was praying that it would not let me down, but it was really tasty. I Â ordered it with swiss cheese on a wheat bun, which was perfect. I saw that they also had cocktails on the menu which looked interesting. Only drawback is that it's cash only but the prices are reasonable that it's ok, unless you are drinking a ton. I will definitely be back here for lunch, I am sorry that I waited so long to try it out. I have been missing out on a good place in a neighborhood that lacks good places to eat!

Oh the hype the hype... It's hard to get a table at market table.... So one day I was passing by and craving a burger I ordered one to go. After waiting a while at the bar, where patrons enjoy a meal as well as at tables, I got a huge brown bag to go and paid ($20! - after tax+tip)...well it was not what I dreamed about....it was small, a little dry too (I ordered medium), and much less juicer than its cousin at The little Owl... I don't like the design / atmosphere inside; it's clean and simple and yet missing something.... I did have brunch there that was nice / eggs Benedict , but it was not amazing...

I've been a fan of Momofuku Noodle Bar since they opened, as they have "appeased" the vegetarians with Ginger Scallion Noodles and Shiitake Pork Bun for a while now. Momofuku SsÃ¤m does not follow suit, and I was pretty disappointed with their offerring. It was a little humiliating to have the waitress tell me "well, you can eat the pickles and some bread." I'm aware of David Chang's meat-centric style, having even bought the cookbook at one point, so I wasn't expecting much on the meat-free spectrum. One dish would have sufficed. Even a side dish. There were several dishes that seemed vegetarian friendly, with generally one Â seafood-based ingredient, but they didn't offer to adjust the dish. So I had a nice bottle of Bruce Cost's Ginger Ale while my friends tried several dishes. They liked the pork buns and a scallop dish best, and didn't like the sea urchin/tapioca/whipped tofu.
Steak was amazing!

Haute Cuisine Mexican! Fantastic!! So wonderful to have some place so authentic in in the shadow of Caliente Cab and all those terribly inauthentic Seventh Avenue horror shows. Small place, tight quarters. Make a reservation. Very much a "joint". Great menu, amazing food, great drinks (super margarita) and solid service. Its the first time I've eaten cactus. Delicious! We cannot wait to go back!
Simply everything that I had was delicious! Â One of those places that I will remember and come back to!

Simply cannot be beat. Trattoria L'incontro is easily one of the best italian restaurants in New York. Â The service is impeccable and the food is so well-prepared and tasty. Your server will rattle off 30 or so specials of the day (pay attention!) and at the end of this impressive recital, you will pretty much want to order everything. Â I recommend asking him any questions you may have and he will delve into even more detail. The service is really top-notch, and your courses will be spaced out perfectly so that you really get to enjoy the meal. Â  The bread with the sun-dried tomato tapenade was so addicting and delicious. Â Definitely try it, but remember to save room for the rest of the food. We were a large group. Â We started with fried zucchini flowers, fried calamari, and house salad. Â Each was delicious. Â The flowers, although small in quantity, packed a large punch of flavor. Â The fried calamari was some of the best I've had anywhere. Â The salad was good---it had a really good balsamic. The brick oven pizzas looked too good to ignore, so we had them next. Â The cheese pizza with prosciutto, arugula, and truffle oil was one of the best things all night. Â Such a great combination of flavors and you really taste the truffle. Â  Each entree was delicious and different. Â From the veal parmigiana to the pasta with chunks of lobster. Â You can't really go wrong here. We didn't really have room for dessert but we ordered anyway. Â The cannoli is one of the best you'll have, and I've had cannolis from pretty well-known italian pastry shops. Â The nutella pizza with hazelnut ice cream was a perfect way to finish up the amazing meal. Â  This was quite an experience and I cannot wait to return!

I live on the Upper West Side and I WANT UPPER WESTVILLE! This is one of Manhattan's best restaurants in that the food is extremely tasty, healthy, attractive, and pretty inexpensive--which applies to home delivery, too. I discovered Westville while dating a woman in Chelsea. Now that she no longer lives there, I am praying that this brilliant chain will bring its imaginative veggies-and-protein-wth-few-carbs formula higher up in Manhattan. Whenever I need to grab a meal in Chelsea, this is where i'll be. The staff never lies about the wait time for a table and they move diners along without pressing them, so the wait can be miraculously brief. Please expand northward.

Honestly, to date, ABC Kitchen has been one of my favorite dining experiences in NYC. JG really lays it down from beginning to finish. The decor is beautiful and sets the tone for a casual dinner without the casual service. It all is cohesive from beginning to finish: the elegance of the food really says a lot for the sustainable practices supported by the restaurant. Definitely would come back.
Great ambience, the wait was a manageable 20 minutes. Fantastic French Toast! Must order!

Loved the lasagna; the beet ravioli in a butter sauce was a bit heavy for our taste - but I guess that's what we should have expected from a butter sauce. Â I know little about wine - waiter recommended one that I really liked. Â We came early so place was not crowded. Â Service was excellent. Price reasonable I think.

+1 for the quirky and fun decor (I especially liked the train set) +1 for the attentive waiters and busboys +1 for the unique and extensive menu +1 for the Daisy's Eggs, Coconut French Toast, Tortilla Soup +1 for the food coma that quickly set in... *yawn* 5 happy customers that said they'd be back

Pretty good steaks, still doesn't beat Keen's or Luger's. Â Awesomely addictive fries. Excellent dessert - cant expect less from the French. Excellent service - rare feeling of a server actually making us feel welcome and that they enjoyed being there even if there was a crazy wait. Â Zero feeling of being rushed out of our seat. Excellent atmosphere - great looking people and lively vibe with great lighting.

My friends and I were wandering around SoHo in search of some good eats. NoLita House and Cafe Habana happened to be closed that day, so we turned to yelp and found Cafe Gitane. The cafe was super hip and had a great relaxed atmosphere. We endured the heat and waited about 20 minutes to be seated. This was my first time trying Moroccan fare, so I wasn't sure what to expect. The sandwiches were delicious and healthy. The chicken was a bit dry for my taste, but the extras made up for that. Next time I will definitely venture out and try the couscous dishes. They looked awesome! If you're in SoHo and are looking for a healthy, cozy cafe to dine at, Cafe Gitane is your spot.
Brunch is excellent. Great bar!
Phenomenal and approachable Italian cuisine. Very close to what my mom makes. Pork belly, Jewish artichokes were both incredible.

Was visiting nyc for the first time and wanted to splurge a bit on good sushi...so i made my reservation 1 week ahead and came here on a Thursday for lunch. We had a la cart sashimis. I think my fav was the scallop. Everything else weren't very impressive. Portions are tiny...for the price paid I could've gotten much bigger and fresher (in my opinion) pieces at my fav sushi restaurant in the bay area. I wonder if I should've just opted for the bento boxes.

I LOVE Nyonya. This spot is good, but my loyalty lies with the Brooklyn location, where I used to go with my family as a tyke. I always get the Seafood Scramble here, which is a great big serving of fried noodles, squid, shrimp, scallops and veggies in a mysteriously delicious gravy. Cash only here! The restaurant's pretty, though it gets quite busy and cramped because of how the tables are spaced. But unless you're getting up a lot it shouldn't matter: just sit ya butt down and have some Scramble or any other tasty dishes off the fried noodle menu.

This is a cute little spot not too far from my apartment. We came into Saleya to grab a bite to eat before a movie on a Friday night. I've tried coming in before around happy hour but it was way too crowded. Not so much this time since we missed happy hour by a few minutes. The downstairs bar area is small and cramped. It's difficult to maneuver through the tables when coming and going no matter which way you go. I had the spicy shrimp pizza and the salmon. I really enjoyed the pizza, great combination of flavors. The salmon was good, not great. The service was decent. I think the guy was the only person for the entire downstairs area. I'd stop in again for an inexpensive bite to eat or maybe to check out their happy hour. Not sure I'll be a frequent diner considering all the other options in the area.
There's usually a wait, but it's worth it. If you don't have a large party, try your luck at the bar for an open spot.

I was really looking forward to having dinner here with my beau while escaping one city for another, but unfortunately that wasn't so. Â Our waitress rushed us into ordering after coming over to us about 5 times within 5 minutes. Â Without any time to discuss what we would like to order to share a la family style, we blindly ordered uni over soba noodles w/uni broth (special for the evening), seaweed salad w/sesame dressing, maguro yamakake, jidori shioraki, buta kakuni and ended with the black sesame creme brulee. Â The uni soba noodles were fantastic, but then again, uni on anything makes it 500x better, even if it were ice cream. The other dishes were well prepared but didn't make me have a "when I'm back in NYC, I have to come back here" moment.
The lamb meatballs, so good! Really all the food was excellent, kitchen is open late, friendly bar staff and tasty drinks. Strong recommend for a healthy late night bite to eat.

Outside of the normal wait, probably the best ramen in NYC. Â Little pricy but worth it. Â My favorite is the Akamaru Modern (Tonkatsu noodle soup). Â Appetizers are hit and miss. Â Nice Sake selection.
Such an amazing place... with amazing mac & cheese!
best french food for the best price. tiny restaurant even by nyc standards. filet mignon with foie gras, heart attack worthy. it's perfect for an intimate date, not a first date and not for groups.

I had very high expectations of this place being that they market themselves as a "gastropub". For a gastropub, the service was very good. We are used to a long wait and spotty service, but our waiter made himself available to is despite how busy it was. My wife started off with the ring of fire which was amazing and i went with a beer flight, three of the four beers were fantastic. Started our meal off with a bacon sampler, which consisted of a pair of 4 different types of bacon. Â The jalepeno bacon left much to be desired and the best tasting one was the peppered bacon. We then had an order of their hot wings and bacon infused blue cheese dressing. Hot wings were crispy and they used something along the lines of franks red hot to dress them. If you like that style wing... Order them! For the mains, I had the lobster roll and my wife went with the lobster Mac n cheese(on the specials menu). The lobster roll was nice, the bread was OK but the chips were a bit overcooked for my tastes. The lobster Mac and cheese had a strange "grease" smell to it. It wasn't really a lobster Mac, it was more like a bacon infused Mac n cheese garnished with some lobster on top. For dessert we had the bread pudding topped with ice cream, hardened chocolate and bacon brittle. This was decent but not an epic dessert by any means. It probably would've been better if it wasn't served on a bed of low quality chocolate syrup. All said and done, we were both left a bit disappointed after all the hype, but we will definitely come back here just for the bar situation... They know how to mix a cocktail and pick quality beers.
Excellent sushi and excellent prices, especially for New York. I had the sushi lunch and the eel was amazing! I highly recommend.
This is the ramen by which I measure all other ramen.
food.. Â ok service.. friendly and attendant price.. ok nothing special but not a bad place to go

If you're able to purchase through Gilt, Bakehouse is worth it purely on value. Not worth spending full price on dinner though. Has a chain feel, with a menu that sounds a whole lot better than it really is. Nothing is horrible, but has a 'bro crowd' feel to it. Nothing on the menu was memorable. Service is however better than expected, our waiter was very attentive and friendly.

Let's start with the ugly. I've been living in the neighborhood for about 2.5 years now and found this gem one night when my bf and I went walking around the block. On a slow night you will get the great service with witty/funny waiters and a nice hostess. On a busy night (which seems to be every night now due to it's word of mouth popularity and when the weather is amazing) you will encounter a hostess who is rude, lies, and waiters who are condescending and also lie. Going back to the lying, I have called before and made reservations for 2 in the past and for some reason now they do not take reservations for 4 and below. As i walked up with a group of 3 I was quoted a 45 minute wait. Having worked in a restaurant setting that was constantly busy I knew the wait time would be less than what I was quoted because I observed 3-4 tables near the end of their meal. I had no preference of inside or outside, but to my surprise once some tables were available my group of 3 gets pointed towards a table that is small in space while a couple gets a table with more space (this table in particular was occupied by a group of 3 so it would've been a no brainer to seat us there). When I make this observation I let the hostess know if she could switch us since the smaller space would be more suitable for 2 rather than 3 and she responds with telling me that this other couple had made a reservation. OH really?? Now you're taking reservations for parties of 3 and under? I was pretty annoyed and let her know and some other waiter who was trying to explain to me that that was my only option or I could wait 20 more minutes. Pssssh thanks for being so accommodating. Now the good: the grilled calamari and Spinach Gnocchi: MUAH! Yummy yummy yummy!!! Although I will point out that this last time they served the calamari on a bed of mixed greens instead of the usual arugula and please note: GO BACK to the ARUGULA. The bite and bitterness of it suits the calamari better than the mixed greens. To wrap this long review up, I would recommend the manager to hire hostesses who are confident managing the front desk. I would also recommend you go back to allowing parties of 2 to make reservations, and learn to make exceptions depending on the situation (placing smaller people in tighter corners, etc). My bf and I always bring our out of state visitors to dinner about 1-2 times a month and Â year round and we recommend this place to anyone who asks' us where they can get decent Italian food. We want to continue to support our neighbors and their establishments, but teach your employees to cut the attitude and teach them about customer appreciation. I am sure they wish they could work a more glamorous job, but until then smile and interact with the guests who are putting money in your pocket. Buon Appetito!

This place is amazing. The good rocks the service is stellar and I'll be coming back time and time again. If you're looking for a great Italian restaurant in Park slope this is the place to go to. Highly recommended!!!

I came here last year and loved loved loved the freedom I had as a gluten free eater. I'm planning a trip to New York in a few weeks, and I think there is a possibility that I am more excited to come here than i am to see my friends and family. Pizza-Gluten free. Beer-Gluten free. Stomach-ache free.

what the heck happened to mamoun's? for $3.50, a falafel sandwich that was absolutely awful. falafel pressed flat, dry like cardboard. pita stale. half as much sauce as was needed. something's up with this place. there's better falafels at any street cart anywhere in town. i won't be back.

Let me just start by saying, I have heard amazing things about this restaurant. While the food was pretty good, the service was pretty bad. I really want to give this place 2.5 stars, but that's not possible, and after I wrote this review, I rounded down... Ultimately the food was pretty good, I got a pasta and my boyfriend got the branzino. Both were pretty tasty and filling. We also got the kale salad to start, which was pretty good, but also pretty heavy on the onions. The problem is we asked for sauce on the side. My boyfriend ordered the fish and asked specifically if the olive oil that's poured on at the end could be withheld. The waiter said, so I'll give you the sauce on the side? My boyfriend then repeated that he wanted the olive oil withheld. They somehow came to a weird agreement about sauce on the side. The dish shows up, with you guessed it, completely drenched in olive oil. The guy who dropped off the food couldn't have cared less and it the waiter never checked in on us. My bf actually got up to go get him. Then he wouldn't even acknowledge that the olive oil was all over the fish. I'm not talking about how the fish is cooked in a little olive oil. Its clearly added after and decoratively around he plate. It's an aggressive amount of oil. Honestly, it was so uncomfortable. The waiter couldn't even acknowledge the olive oil on the plate or that they had a 2 minute conversation about how the sauce would be on the side. He was impressively stupid. But who hired him? Kefi's did.

I am not Thai, nor have I ever been to Thailand, but I know when food taste how it's supposed to. This place gets 4 stars because the hip interior, friendly atmosphere, service, and complimentary green tea mo-chi desert. We ordered Pai See Ew, Pineapple Fried Rice, and noodles with chicken broth(blend). The place is tiny, only 5-6 tables. The food has relatively smaller portion, and it's missing a tiny bit of authenticity. It would fit most people's palette, but it didn't satisfy my Thai cravings. :( If you have a blend palette and Â just want a small bite in a cute place, this is the place to go.

I would go again. the lasagna was great. I would not order the spaghetti and meatballs though. As i pointed out to my party of 6, sitting at table fit for 4, it kind of tasted like the mushed up dog food in a can. Everything else worked for me though. Price, amount of food, and service.

Quaint is a cute little place in Sunnyside. Came here last Friday and inside was dim and more like a bar. We were seated at a booth table, which was cool since it was by the open kitchen where you can watch them cook. For appetizers, we had the calamari and the mac & cheese. Both were really good. However, the calamari was a bit on the salty side, but was perfect with the marinara sauce. I just didn't like the fact that the marinara sauce was cold. The mac & cheese was made with small pasta shells and had little pieces of bacon in it. I ordered the burger and french fries. It was really big and juicy and comes with all the toppings. I believe he had ordered the chicken breast, not sure...lol. Anyways, overall, it was a good experience and the waiter was attentive. It wasn't packed when we went on a Friday evening at 6PM. And it wasn't packed when we were leaving. I guess it depends on the crowd and time. They seem to have a really good brunch menu for Saturdays and Sundays. I would like to come back here for brunch on the weekend sometime.

After dining at SHO with two stars, was excited to come here. No problem getting a resy for an earlier dinner on Friday. There are two dining areas, each seating 20ish, separated from the bar area by the hotel entrance. We were in the inner room, which was pretty quiet. We went with the 4 course. Bread choices are between normal or olive mini baguettes with soft butter and this olive spread. There was an array of amuse bouche - I was a big fan of the warm truffle potato. For starters, the live scallop was amazing..buttery and sweet. The gnocchi with peekytoe crab was creamy and delicious. The egg and tiny bit of uni upped the savoriness. For fish, the peas added a sweet tinge to the halibut. I preferred the bass, which was perfectly cooked and on the vinegary side. For meats, I really liked the morel mushrooms and mushroom broth with the nicely done veal tenderloin. I preferred the rabbit, which was tender and came with an assortment of young carrots. For desserts, the chocolate with jasmine was good, but I liked the mango ricotta more. I loved the green tea macadamia from the petit fours. Overall great food, great presentation, great service, though the dÃ©cor could use some color. The portions are definitely on the smaller size, and it's pretty pricey for how much food you get, but each dish has a lot of depth.
no one needs to hear from me about how good the spotted pig is. Â i love it just as much as everyone else. Â don't skip the deviled eggs.

I went to Le P'tit Paris for the first time a few nights ago. Â I used to frequent the Italian Resaturant that used to occupy this space, so I thought I would give this a try as well. The atmosphere was nice. Â Cute little tables, soft glow lighting, and waitstaff that actually speaks french. Â There was almost no one else in the restaurant on the Thursday night was there, but I imagine those cute little tables would start to feel cramped if the place was full. Â Our waiter was very funny and personable. Â The service was great, though I would have been shocked if we were not well attended to, since there were more waiters than customers. Â Even so, this guy was terrific... I wish I remembered his name. We started with the French Onion Soup, which was pretty good. Â My date and I both ordered the Hangar Steak, which came with salad and fries. Â Salad = great. Â Fries = salty deliciousness. Â The steak = waaay underdone. Â My date ordered his steak medium well, and it came as a perfect medium rare. Â My medium rare was very rare. Â Because everything was so well seasoned and presented, I was shocked that they didn't know how to cook a piece of meat. Â I mean, not even close to what we ordered. I think this place has a few kinks to work out in their kitchen, but it is a very sweet little place that would be nice to take your date or go out for a nice quiet evening. Â Worth a shot anyway.

My dorm room for school was only a few blocks away from here. About a month into living in my dorms, another student introduced me to this place... and I still can't thank them enough! It's definitely one of those tiny hole in the wall places you would be unsure of, especially if you are just visiting the city, but I assure you that you need to try it. Perfect budget meal if you are trying to save a few bucks and great for college students! If I can remember correctly, it was $2 for an order of dumplings... TWO DOLLARS! That never happens in Manhattan! Also, did I mention perfect hangover food? Yes, they could be using less than 'quality' meats/produce in order to be able to sell it so cheap, but I don't think it could be any worse than the frozen dumplings at the grocery store or Micky D's for that matter. I now live in Charleston, SC, but when I do visit the city this place is definitely on my list of go to's!

Stopped in on a cold November Saturday night just after historic Pier A opened to the public. The space is beautiful, the staff is super nice, the view is fantastic (be sure to walk around the deck area). My only issue was the cost, which was high, around $8 for a pint. But, it's to be expected. This is not a neighborhood bar to grab a beer with friends; it's a spot to grab tourists who've just finished their Statue cruises. But it works if you want to pay a little extra to enjoy the scenery. Personally, I can't wait till the fancy cocktail lounge on the 2nd floor opens up. The area in front is weird because it's not well lit and if you don't know there's a restaurant there, there's nothing outside to indicate it. Either way, well worth a stop until April or May when this place gets insanely crowded.

I really enjoyed dining at Room Service. Anytime I can get a filling meal at a clean and romantic restaurant with great service and not spend a lot I'm a happy man. The styling here is gorgeous, even the staff is dressed extremely well. Entrees are mostly $9-14, apps are $4-6 as are the desserts. In fact two people getting 3 courses each after tax and tip came out to $55. For a starter I got the Shrimp Parcels (about $6) which were five shrimp with a layer of chicken fried up and served with plum sake dipping sauce. I couldn't really taste or see much chicken but it was a tasty app. My entree was the Roadside Noodles with chicken (about $9). This was steamed rice noodles (also available with egg noodles) with scallions, bean sprouts, crushed peanuts, and a black bean sauce. The portion was big and the dish was delicious. The chicken wasn't overcooked and though the dish was a tad on the sweet side, I'd definitely order it again. To finish I got the Kaffir Lime Pie ($5) served with a berry sauce. I could have done without the berry sauce but the pie was delicious. It was much more dense than a regular Key Lime Pie, it was a little firmer than cheesecake. Either way it was tasty. I also got to try the Thai Pumpkin Flan. Keeping in mind Thai Pumpkin isn't the same as regular pumpkin it was still good. I wouldn't really call this dish flan though. It was a textured custard in a paper cup inside a bowl sitting on a plate with a chocolate drizzle. Not sure how you were supposed to incorporate the chocolate while eating the dessert but it had nice warm spiced fall flavors that went well with the season.

I typically don't get excited about BBQ because I think people get to hyped about it for nothing. But there have been two times I thought it was worth the hype: once in Kansas City at a spot called Bryant's (TRUTH!), and the other here. My fiance had the ribs, I had the chicken. Both superb. Rib meat was perfect. Tender, smoked just right, delicious. Half chicken was just as good. The chef brought out some wings for us to try as well, and those were awesome. Well sauced, great spices. Â Delicious. Fries were terrific, just right, some of the best I've had. Â Prices were very good for the portions we got. Â Food came out really fast. Overall, best barbecue I've had since KC. Bryant's ribs were more saucy, I might prefer that. Here sauce is on the side. Â But the side dishes here destroy Bryant's. Â Best BBQ I've had on the east coast.

This new Italian spot that feels like it could have been used to shoot scenes in Goodfellas (minus the animal figures adorning the wallpaper) is serving up some really excellent pastas and pretty good pizzas. We arrived quite early at around 6 PM, so it was still empty and we were able to score a sweet, large round booth table. The place was pretty much packed by the time we left at around 7:30 PM, after a very satisfying meal: - Beet, Orange, Bufala, Basil Salad ($12) Looking for something lighter since we were about to have pure carbs and cheese, we were very happy with this light, refreshing choice. It's not really a salad like you would think of with greens and leaves, but rather consists of just beets, orange slices, bufala mozzarella and plenty of hazelnuts (mostly like the name suggests). It sounds like it might be a strange combo, but it works well, especially delicious from the added crunch of the hazelnuts. - Calabria Pizza ($15) The pizza came out next, and was of a decent size, not particularly large or small. This one was topped with some deliciously salty salami along with chili flakes that added a good amount of spiciness. The pie was light on cheese and heavier on sauce, which is a ratio I typically don't favor, but it happened to be delicious. I'm definitely interested in trying the other pies after enjoying this one so much. - Chitarra Pesto ($13) The pasta is where it's really at here. This excellent bowl intrigued me once I read the description and saw that it was topped with shoestring fries. I always like my starch topped with even more starch. The pesto sauce was slightly bland for me, but the pasta was nice and al dente and had an excellent texture. The dish as a whole was quite tasty, aided by the fun factor and crispiness provided by the shoestring fries. I would definitely recommend trying this, especially if you like pesto. - Maccheroni Dome ($16) This was the clear MVP of the meal. Another very unique pasta creation, this consisted of a large mass of macaroni, meatballs, ham, tomatoes and bechamel sauce, all baked and encased in a delicious shell (the dome). It's hard to explain exactly how impressive and delicious this was, but just look at the picture, in which you can still see the steam coming out of the piping hot interior (yelp.com/biz_photos/antoâ€¦). This is a definite must try. - Tiramisu ($9) For a perfect end to the meal, you must try the excellent Tiramisu. It's a very sizable piece, with a strong, coffee flavor and is really milky smooth. It's definitely up there with the best I've tried. Service throughout the meal was pretty good, though it did get a bit tough to get attention once it started getting crowded toward the end. Still, the food was good enough that I would definitely return to try some of the entrees and more of the great pastas.

the newest and worst of jean georges' places - ambience whiffs of a once-cool spot that has now gone bridge and tunnel. and it hasn't even been open that long. they made a good mojito, but the first bite of food, our appetizer, black pepper crab dumplings were so bad that they rendered my palate useless, seriously, and we had to cut our dinner short and wash our mouths out with soap

Food is consistent. Â Great value for the quality and ambience. Â Lobster has a great sauce. Â Rib-eye is well charred. Â Squash du jour Â tart with brown butter and ricotta is freaking awesome- Lamb salad- great dressing and crispy capers add a nice textural contrast..Sundae is Â great way to finish off a meal! Brunch is really not anything special BUT you wont be disappointed...

Amazing BBQ, great down-home scene, but I wish it wasn't so pricey. Â If it was cheaper or if I made more money, I'd come hear much more frequently. Â In any event, if you're looking for great BBQ, look no further.

Not anything special and the coffee was lukewarm and tasted bland like a dunkin' donuts. The eggs and toast with home fries were very ordinary needing salt and the toast was underdone and had almost no flavor. Expensive for very little.

If you're gluten-free and want italian style thin gourmet pizza, this is the spot The long thin baguette style (gluten-free) bread sticks are awesome, brought to the table and great dunked in olive oil The large size salad is perfect to share. My fave pizza is pesto with goat cheese, feta and arugula. And though I try to avoid sugar, one night i took home a NY black and white style gluten-free cookie. The risottos are very good - but I come for the pizza. Â And there are great prices on wine. The downside - no reservations are taken and the line of gluten-free foodies is often out the door. Also the tables are tightly packed and it is very loud. No lingering here, once you're done eating, they get you out the door.

Two words: buttermilk pancakes. They were fluffy and delicious. Might even be better than those at Clinton street baking company. As reservations are not taken for Sunday brunch, my friends and I trekked to brooklyn early. We arrived around 10:45am and luckily there were three seats together at the bar. I love the chilled out and friendly, unpretentious atmosphere. I also tried the fried porkchop and cheddar waffle, which was underwhelming. The pork chop was tough and hard to cut through. Portion was large though. It was a poor choice on my part, I want to come back and try one of their egg dishes.
Brunch was amazing. I will definitely visit this spot again. Customer service was great and it didn't take long to receive my food.

Freshly made Soba! Upon entering, you can see your noodles being made. What a treat. We took a seat at the bar, our server was very friendly and attentive. Employees here are sweet. Love that the restroom is so clean and they were burning incense inside. At the beginning of your meal, a hot towel is provided. That was a wonderful way to freshen up. I appreciate that our water and tea cups were always full. They serve excellent matcha green tea and it's complimentary. Presentation of dishes are beautiful. The Soy Cured Tuna and Salmon Sashimi were really fresh, cool, and smooth. Simply melts in your mouth. The Cold Soba was lovely. Nice chew and fresh. The dipping sauce it comes with was a bit too salty for us. Towards the end of our meal, we were given a pot of hot water. We were told to pour it into our dipping sauce and drink the mixture as soup. We had a delicious meal here. Everything was light and flavorful. Quality ingredients used. Their lunch boxes are great. The restaurant gets filled up quick for lunch during weekends. Come early.

Pizza... Whenever I hear the word, I think of a thick, chewy dough with a layer of greasy cheese on it. Usually, my answer is the same: No, thanks. Visiting Posto semi-regularly after moving to the next block has exponentially increased my cravings for this common food item. The best part about Posto is, you can create your own heavenly pizza on their crunchy thin crust (I recommend the regular crust). Their truffle oil is really really good. I would recommend adding some truffle oil into any pizza that you make from here- believe me, you won't regret it. The roasted garlic that you can also add to your pizza is creamy and sweet, and melts in your mouth. Also, before the season is over, taste their delicously thick gazpacho. I took away one star because I didn't think the waitstaff is fast/friendly enough. Other than that, incredible!

Rating: 3.5 Walked over from Museum of Moving Image and it was farther than we thought...thanks hopstop! We got there at 5:44pm and some dude behind the counter yelled that they don't open till 6pm. Good thing there were chairs outside so we sat and counted down the minutes. Grey clouds were rolling around Steinway St. Me and my friends arrived there first but was seated last...smh!! Drink: Orange Fanta (Mexican Soda) nothing special because it tastes like a regular one Food: My friend got the Voodoo Queen w/fries...portion size was huge but the fries were lacking, soft texture and bland. I got the Chicken & Waffles and absolutely love the Tabasco glaze. At least I crossed this off my list but the commute is too far for me if you live back Steinway St or Astoria definitely stop by! Remember CASH ONLY!

This place is great! WINNER: Churrasco steak and truffle fries... if this were in my neighborhood, I'd be in real trouble, haha. Cocktails, yes! Caramelized Banana and chocolate crepes, ughh, delish! Environment also great for intimate evening get togethers, especially a romantic date (pretty dark, which I personally enjoy). Service was also great. Try it out!!

This place reminds me of that clip from Portlandia about the "Dream of the 90s:" youtu.be/FE_9CzLCbkY The atmosphere/ambiance of this place is definitely turn of the century but with a modern twist. I think the interior design and branding is what I really liked most about Boulton & Watt. It's pretty loud when its crowded, but thats typical of a bar in the LES. Nice spot right on the corner. The windows can open completely, which lets a nice breeze in. They have a decent food selection, including an entire section of pickled items in jars. The way that was worded makes it sound gross, but it actually looked pretty good from what I saw. There's pickled carrots, cucumbers, peppers, etc. I got the veggie burger with tzatziki sauce and sprouts, which was delicious. The fries were AMAZING. My bf got the regular burger but we thought the brioche bun on both burgers was a bit much. I literally can't wait to eat my left over fries. The drink menu is pretty big. I can't remember if they had cocktails or not, but they definitely have wines and beer. We actually ordered another round after our first, but never got our drinks, so that kind of sucked. Besides the missing drinks, the staff was great. Fast & very nice. I can't wait to come back here and try the fish & chips on the menu :)

byob and good good food! A super-tiny place a few steps east of the corner of first and first. We went vegetarian and were not disappointed. Among the three of us, we ordered one appetizer and three main dishes. Everyone walked away with full stomachs (even my friend whose appetite mimics that of a garbage disposal) and this only set us back about $35. The service was speedy and friendly. The place, as previously mentioned, is small. A few decorative pillows and paintings make for the "Himalayan" experience. Not that I was expecting desolate, snow-capped mountain tops or anything. Bring some good wine, a small group of friends and you will be satisfied!
Stopped in for a late lunch. Terrible service. Crap oysters. Lousy, cold, under-seasoned steak with no char whatsoever. At these prices there are far better options. Pass. Seriously, pass.

People come here for the amazing selection of beer but I submit that they need to stay for the incredible craft cocktails. Jacob, the mixologist, is incredibly friendly and welcoming. Be it his immense knowledge of spirits, bitters and various house made tinctures or his epic beard (which just screams wisdom), he will craft you a perfect cocktail catered to your taste. Whether you're feeling classic or more adventurous in your imbibing, you will leave satisfied. The Jeffrey is a desperately needed bar is a neighborhood that has long been deprived of great craft beer and cocktails. They also double as a coffee shop during the day too, enough said!

This place was absolutely amazing!!! Food was delicious, seasoned well and not under or over cooked, staff was pleasant and courteous. Pulled my chair out whenever I got up from the table or returned, never left our drinks empty and checked on us constantly making sure we were satisfied and not in need of anything. Tried watermelon fries for the first time and they were to die for!! Also had the croquetas and yuca, also delicious!!! I have no complaints. Restaurant is a little small but it gives it a personal intimate feeling which I love without other patrons being on top of us. Will definitely go back!!

DiFara's is in a class by itself. Â I first read about it on the cover of the Village Voice in 2003 as being the best pizza in the city (no one had ever heard of the place and all the food critics went stampeding out to Midwood - I read review after review after that). Â Unfortunately, I waited 6 years to go there and finally made it out this Summer (and then went back every other weekend until now). Â I cannot stop kicking myself that I have missed out on 6 additional years of DiFara's heavenly pizza. Some people say that Mark (Marc?) at Lucali's learned how to make pizza by watching Dom and asking questions. Â  I'd say that he has the basics down but Lucali's is a step down from DiFara's. On my most recent visit there, I brought a friend who kept pestering me by saying, "What's so special about the pizza?" Â I said, "Just taste it and you'll see." Â She was skeptical. Â We waited the usual time and got our first slice. Â I let her have the first bite and she exclaimed, "Oh dear baby Jesus!" Â I'm not sure what that means but the next plaintive words out of her mouth were, "Why did we only order 2 slices??!" Â (They let us order more.) I went with my mom on Labor Day weekend. Â We spent the usual 2 hours at DiFara's - 1 hour to order, 1 hour to get the pizza. Â My mother and I ended chatting with a Brooklyn native who was like the ringmaster for everyone waiting. Â He was funny and charming and, because of him, everyone ended up talking to everyone while watching Dom make pies. Â My mother was completely fascinated and entertained watching Dom do his magic. Â It was one of the best, most bicker-free times I've had with my mom. I met someone recently who said she hated DiFara's pizza and that L&B Spumoni Gardens was much better. Â I instantly knew her judgment was bad and that we wouldn't be friends. Â ;-)

Cafe Gitane at the Jane Hotel is the perfect spot for a casual walk-in dinner on a week night. Â Went for the second time the other night for a friends birthday (no reservation) and a large group of us were seated immediately. Â The service is generally lackluster, but for some reason it feels appropriate in a French themed restaurant. Â The wine and food are well priced AND delicious, and at any given point in the night, you can expect an array of models, hipsters and scruffy haired west villagers parading themselves through the space. Three stars for the disappointing service, but must try the avocado toast!!

This is a wonderful restaurant with a great atmosphere. Â It is cozy and romantic, yet not too quiet. Â The service was great and we all enjoyed our meals, although I cannot say we loved them, hence the four stars. Â We tried the fried feta cheese, stuffed grape leaves, and meatballs which were all good. My NYC friends who joined us were really pleased with the everything. Â Prices were reasonable for a good NYC meal.
I got sick after

While Patsy's Pizza is good, Lombardi's is awesome. Â Even if you just sorta, kinda like pizza, make time to visit. Like Patsy's, they use a coal oven at Lombardi's. Â Like Patsy's, Lombardi's has been around a long time. Â But the comparison really needs to stop there. Â Lombardi's is in Little Italy. Â The ambience is incredible. Â And the place is packed. Â Even at an early hour the tables were crowded. Â By the time we left the line outside was long. The pizza was light, the crust was crisp and the toppings were incredible. Â This was pizza as it is supposed to be - and for good reason. Â This is the birthplace of American pizza places. Â In 1905, Lombardi's was the first place - ever - licensed as a pizzeria. Â Over 100 years later and it's still well worth a visit.

Outstanding barbecue. If you're coming here, order the Brisket, some Pulled Pork, and the baked beans. These products are truly outstanding - the brisket and pork are juicy and smoky, and the baked beans will literally make you cry they're so good. Also had the wings which were very good - however, given that there are a plethora of amazing wings in the city right now, I was underwhelmed. The TEXTURE of the wings was gosh-darned perfect. Smoked for 2 hours then fried, they were some of the best textured wings I've ever had. The way the dress them, however, could be better. Â They claim chili and scallion and lime and some other things (I think?) which could be awesome, but I found them to be so spicy that the spice drowned out the other flavors rather than complement them. I'm aware this is super picky, but I'm rather a wing snob. I will definitely be returning for the brisket, pulled pork and those amazing baked beans!!

I go here all the time for BRUNCH and its ridiculously delicious!! I always go for the Short Rib Hash and Eggs: braised short rib, eggs any style... and OHHH MANNNN!! that shit is ridiculous. i can't even explain how good it is and it's the perfect portion. It fills me right up and it makes me feel all good and happy inside. I also suggest trying the Stone Park BLT: pork belly, vine tomatoes, bibb lettuce, garlic aioli... Cus ME LIKEY PORK BELLY!! yesh you heard me... I'm all about that. So if you're in the area around brunch time i suggest you stop in and get yourself something delicious to eat and some great alcoholic beverage :)

Visited for the first time this week and had the egg and chive pancake and the mixed fresh veggie pancake, which were from two different parts of the menu. The fresh veggie pancake had a thicker crust and was fine, but the egg and chive pancake was more like a crepe, and at $1.50 a real value...no need for soy sauce or any other condiments. It was wonderful and also nutritious.

I dined there multitude of times and udon was oishi! I especially like the waves of irasshaimasse! when you just poke your head through the entrance. Their combination sets are plentiful, I especially like their gyudon and curry sets. Did I mentioned it's BYOB? If you are too lazy to bring anything anyway, you can ask them and they'll run close by to get you few cold ones!
Great chicken and waffles. Small space though.

Ootoya is one of those restaurants that I hesitate to review for fear it gets too popular and loses some of its original charm. Â :) It is by far one of the best places I've tried in NY and one that I will definitely make a trip out to again. Â Their homemade tofu and pork belly is exceptional and what really makes Ootoya unique for me is its attention to detail, the exquisite simplicity of the dishes, and how well it does non-traditional Japanese food (at least what you see in the states). Highly recommended!

Price/Food - Came here at 4 in the morning after a long night out some friends. We ordered the chicken and rice and the combo with chicken and lamb. The chicken was decent but the special white sauce tasted like crack! Nothing too special but they are very generous with portions. $6 for chicken/lamb and rice?! Can't go wrong with it. Definitely good drunk food! Service/Location - We went at 4 in the morning and surprisingly there wasn't a wait! - 6th and 53rd!! Don't go to any other one! Recommendation - Chicken and rice with lots of special white sauce. Everyone at the cart was telling me to get the white sauce. WHITE SAUCE FTW!!! - Always a line but they open till 5AM on the weekends so this is a great place to come to after a night of drinking.
TaÃ¯m's falafel is unmatched anywhere else. Perfectly spiced and never dry, with all the toppings & sides. The red falafel is my fave, but all are yummy. Excellent smoothies, too!
Went there last Saturday to celebrate friend's birthday. Â Excellent food. Got short ribs, the best ever got. Also tried friend's order - trout, fresh and delicious. Love bread as well.

Love this place! I wanted to try everything. I came here for a weekday brunch and was seated in 10 mins. I ordered the duck confit hash, it was delicious! The french toast was also awesome with crispy edges. I want to come here again to try other brunch items.

This place reminds me of a restaurant in Seattle. Â The place was packed, but we did not have to wait at all. Â They seemed very well organized there. Â The restaurant seemed a little upscale, but I'd say it was more trendy. Â The wait staff we're mostly in nice dark jeans and collared shirts which was nice to see. Â Some friends recommended this place to us and we came for the food. Â They use a lot of organic/local vegies etc. Â It was great to see that for a NYC restaurant. Who knew...... Â Unfortunately I was not that hungry that evening so we ate light. Â We started with 2 different types of salads. Â THey were both very different, but very delicious. Â One contained beets & pears and the other was mainly greens. Â  I usually do not order Chicken, but I did that night and was really glad I did. Â Good portion and paired with purple potatoes which were grilled. Â My partner ordered the lamb. Â It was sort of a sampler and paired with polenta. Â For dessert we shared the ice cream. I forgot to mention the cocktails were good and also had a nice mix of wines.

I've been going here since the beginning, since the very first week they opened. I have had at least 10+ visits here. At that time, they ran a really tight operation. The food was excellent, the service attentive, and the location was convenient, hip and cozy. Tim, the Maitre'D apparent informed me that it was a new venture by one of the owners of Le Barricou, an exceptional French restaurant, and one of my personal favorites a stone's throw away in Williamsburg. He claimed that they "were better than Le Barricou". It was a bold claim, yes, but I felt like they might actually have been able to back it up. It was to me, at least, without a doubt a 5 star yelp experience. Unfortunately since that time, it seems to have wavered in quality. One of the most frequent problems I experience here is the lack of attentive service. Most of my recent visits have started with a 20 minute wait for a drink, or even water. I get the distinct impression that there is a culture of disinterest among the staff, whom seem far more interested in socializing with each other or their friends at the bar, than actually catering to their customers. Â It has the effect of making the average customer feel like they aren't part of the club. I wish I could say it was any other way, but it's an experience I've had multiple times. The french onion soup is excellent, the burgers, pasta and fish are extremely good, and the steak is pretty good, as well. The Beef Bourginon and Coq Au Vin are pretty good, but not at the level of Le Barricou. The cocktails are ok but lack the polish and imagination of nearby mainstays like Miles and Dear Bushwick. The flourless chocolate cake is on another level of excellence. I have insisted to visitors that we dine here just so it can be experienced! Over time though, the portion size has shrunken somewhat disappointingly. It still ought not to be missed though. Like other reviewers on here, I am extremely torn about this place. I desperately want it to become "Le Barricou East" but it seems like the requisite discipline is missing that would put it on a higher level. If they can't reach that level, it will merely be another in the long line of decent but disappointingly aloof New York City dining establishments.

The food is authentic and fresh and expertly prepared. All the pasta dishes were great! Homemade, al dente, and clung onto every bit of sauce. Food is excellent all around, only complaint is that the list of specials is outrageously long, so long that you forget what they started with! The staff is mainly Italian speaking and it is so impressive how they recite the dozens of specials with their authentic accents. The service was amazing, absolutely on point from start to finish.

The burgers are good and it is not expensive. However the ambient is below average. I can understand that it is cash only, they need to increase their margin and that the space is limited to the tables are way too close to each other. But there is no excuse for the awful service they have here, the waiter refuses to utter a word and everyone looks as miserable as if the house puppy had just died.
Great food, even for vegetarians!

I normally shy away from Williamsburg for Sunday brunch, but based on a tip "no hipsters each brunch before noon" we arrived at Rye at 11 am for brunchies. Bottom line: YUM. We started with their homemade "donuts" (more like donut holes). Crispy on the outside, tender and spicy on the inside, I wish we'd saved these for dessert. They were served with a side of whip cream, which I thought didn't add anything, but... *shrug*. We also had a duck rillette. Kind of a duck pate, and some "sourdough." I say "sourdough" because sorry, as much as we might try, proper sourdough cannot be made outside of San Francisco. But the rillette was quite tasty as well. For my entree, I tried the Meatloaf Sandwich I'd heard so many raves about. And it was worth it. A combination of duck, veal, and beef, it was rich and delicious. I am STILL FULL 8 hours later it was so good. One thing: too much bread. The meatloaf PLUS the giant roll is too much. It would be excellent as an open-face sandwich or heck, ALONE on a plate, with some fried onions on top. It is seriously solid enough to stand alone. While some have complained about the service, ours was great. The waitress was attentive, and our water and coffee were constantly being topped off. The decor is very turn of the century (whether it's real or just made to look that way I'm not sure...) with tin ceilings, old wood floors, old silver used everywhere (mismatched cutlery, old coffee urns, and the check plate). All in all we were very pleased with our brunch. We lingered till around 12:30 pm, when all the hipsters started trickling in.

We had the day off of work today so we booked a reservation at this New York Institution of a restaurant and both ordered the 5-course lunch tasting menu. Â  First thing, when you walk into the restaurant, its beautifully decorated for fall. Â Bright orange mini pumpkins and matching flowers fill the space and the air smells like thanksgiving. Â We were walked pass the chefs doing plating and my appetite was whetted. Â  The first course was a lobster salad. Â This dish was my husband's favorite of the day. Â It was beautifully bright - the red acidity of the beets complimented by a wasabi cream topped with lucious lobster. Â Licked the plate clean, which is difficult to do in a classy institution but we were that committed. Â  Second course was scallops over cauliflower. Â This dish was deliciously salty but a bit gritty actually. The first main was the sea bass. Â Amazing. Â A squash puree plus tangy fennel with a perfectly cooked fillet made this dish a perfect one for fall. Â  Finally the duck course. Â This was the big disappointment for me. Â Duck is amazing. Â Seriously, how did they mess this up? Â I still have trouble explaining it. Â Basically the duck wasn't quite as crispy as you'd expect and it was topped with a seared salsa of carrots, peppers, and onions which just added a mushy texture. Â I just think it didn't do the duck the justice it deserves. Â  Finally - we had dessert. Â If not for the dessert this meal would get 3 stars. Â We had a banana and chocolate cake with praline with a side of salted cashew ice cream. Â I would kill my mother for more of this dessert. It was actually heaven. Â When I'm in heaven I expect to eat this dessert, calorie-free, for every meal. Â We also had an apple tart. Â It was good but like the democrats at midterms, it was crushed by the competition. Yay for days off.

Super cheap and satisfying meal. Â The restaurant doesn't seat too many people and there was a line to the door at about 7pm on just any regular weekday. Â Service is a tad bit on the slow side and food takes a little while to come out. For a place called "Spicy Village"... theres not really that many spicy items to choose from on the menu... I'm quite the adventurous eater and I love parts of animals that aren't usually eaten.... so of course I ordered the lamb innards hui mei (not sure what hui mei translates to... must be a dialect I don't know?). Â I opted for the large size and it was the perfect amount for me (I'm small...) The freshly made noodles remind of those from Xian Famous Foods - same texture, taste, etc. Â The broth is white. Â I still can't figure out what makes the broth white.... as long as it tastes good right? Â It's just a basic meaty broth - the lamb innards doesn't come spicy so I added the hot oil. Â In addition to lamb innards aka intestines, the noodles also came with wood ear mushroom and these long vegetable things that my mom usually ties in a knot... I couldn't tell you for the life of me what they are called. Â It was, in my opinion, a pretty decent and tasty meal for a whole 6 dollars. While this was a satisfying and filling meal, I was hungry about 4 hours later. Â Just FYI.

Food is always good here, the broiled scallops are awesome, the stuffed shrimp, the stuffed clams, the baked clams, the swordfish kabob, the chicken kabob (which was juicy), the lemon potatoes are yums and so are the fried potatoes. It can definitely get cramped at busy hours and a long wait on weekends and night. Service is basic. It's good to go in a group so you can order a lot and try different dishes.

This is the best Banh Mi place I've experienced in NYC. I live a few blocks and an avenue away and I come here about once a week if I can help it. And every time I do I am reminded why Brooklyn is such a great place to live: unmatched quality in authentic ethnic foods and low prices! It is inexpensive and they have the best Vietnamese sandwiches in the city. I've tried other places in Brooklyn that were good, too, but this place really tops them all with their authentic flavors, [tasty] variations on the traditional banh mi, and their unmatchable baguettes! It has been mentioned before: the baguettes that they use for the sandwiches are amazing. They are perfectly crunchy, flaky, fluffy, and always fresh. I don't know where they get them, but the man who works there once announced 'you don't get this bread in grocery store!' Which is true. The atmosphere is very casual, take-out style. The ladies who work there are very nice and welcoming (though sometimes they talk about customers in Vietnamese haha, but you'll never know...) Always a plus. Oh, and they have good egg rolls, too. Now let's talk about the milkshakes. They make an avocado milkshake here that is smooth, creamy, and refreshing. I was so curious at first, and now I don't know why I was ever skeptical. Some people don't care for the texture, but I love the subtletly of the flavor. I've also tried their jackfruit, lychee, and strawberry milkshakes. The strawberry was pretty ordinary, though still very good; the lychee and jackfruit were very sweet, so if you want a more sugary yum yum flavor, those two are for you. I love vietnamese iced coffee as well, and theirs is top notch. Credentials: I'm from Seattle, which has a large Vietnamese population and large amount of very authentic and very good Vietnamese food. My roommate is Vietnamese (and also from Seattle). In the end, the verdict is Ba Xuyen has some of the best Banh Mi out there, and certainly the best in NYC. When we have friends visit, this place is always on the 'must eat' list. So there's my rating: 'Must eat.'

There is literally not a negative thing that I can say about this place. Even the 90min wait wasn't a downside, because Upstate handles it in the best way possible. The hostess took our number so our group could go to a nearby bar (where we enjoyed happy hour) and the she shot us a text when our table was ready. Amongst our table we started with the crabcakes and the tuna tartar, then for entrees moved on to the fettuccine with clams, scallops of the day, and the fish of the day. I don't particularly care for fettuccine or clams...yet somehow I thoroughly enjoyed the dish. I will be back to try the Happy Hour for sure!

Woohoo! As good as it gets! best V-sandwich i've found YET and amazing cheap price! better than Saigon Vietnamese Sandwich Deli stick to the pork b/c the chicken can be little fatty. the others aren't that interesting -we tried them all. the veggy/budah has lots of cold gluten and beancurd-skin -which is pretty good if you eat it apart or out of the sandwhich first. when you ask for "hot" they give you a slice of chili pepper, lol. wonder what "extra hot" gets you? [ask for "no mayo" if you want to skip the western ver] can almost last the next day but the pickle vegges make the bread soggy if you don;t take it apart when you get home.

I've lived in New York almost all my life, just a couple of blocks away from this joint, and though I've heard the hype, I've never tried it....perhaps because I have an aversion to hyped up joints. Â Anywayy.... I got a falafel and a side of hummus ($4.25 in total) and it was amazing, if maybe a tad bit soggy. Â The optional hot sauce on the falafel was a definite plus -- it had a lot of real flavor to it, it wasn't just HOT. Â The hummus was great and creamy without tasting fatty like a lot of supermarket hummus. Â The counter person was very friendly. This hole-in-the-wall is obviously not the place you want to take a first date, but if you like falafel then I suggest you come here. Â If you're broke and looking for semi-healthy food, I also suggest you come here. Â  Woop.

LOVE the burritos here! Dare I say it's better than Chipotle? Burritos are about a buck cheaper than Chipotle (though veggie doesn't include free guac like Chipotle so there's that...) The people are really nice and the space is pretty cute. You can also get cheap beer while there so that's a plus (though I wouldn't take a date here). Burritos are very very tasty and HUGE and you will be way full after finishing it in like 3 minutes. I suggest sneaking one into the Regal movie theater next door so you don't have to pay the insane popcorn prices.

Native New Yorker here. And let me tell you: This pizza is incredible. Granted, I live nearby, but I pretty much fiend for it and go back once a week. The crust is chewy and smoky and unlike anything else in NYC. Also great: the decor. Romantic all throughout, amazing garden in the back, good for parties or couples or solo. The wines, desserts and espresso are also great, and the olive oil for the bread is amazing. The non-pizza entrees are good, but can't compare to the pizza. Two big complaints, however: First off, the service. They're generally nice, but they are guaranteed to forget about you at some point, usually when its time to bring the check. They may or not bring bread, and they may forget your drink. I can forgive them somewhat because almost the entire staff is Italian, and that's how the service is over there as well. So, I guess you could call it "authentic." Second complaint, and I'm sure it's gonna cause some controversy. Please, PLEASE hire some local folks. It's pretty unacceptable for a Â successful restaurant in the middle of Bed-Stuy to not have ONE black person on staff. I understand that you guys are new, and you're from Italy. But please, bring in some local folks so the community can benefit from your restaurant, because most of the people who live here can't afford it, and your very presence is a harbinger of high rents to come. This would be a great neighborhood restaurant--but it doesn't feel like it's part of the neighborhood.

The smoothie was spectacular and the ability to charge my phone was to die for. Actually though, best power outlet in nyc 2k14. I wish more restaurants would follow in Taim's footsteps with their exceptional standards for charging capabilities. Temperature was a little cold, but overall nice environment

On a rainy night, after a documentary screening at IFC, the BF and I were headed to Fish and Grom, two favorites. As we trodded through the moonlight and rain, we happened upon Pagani, and decided to give it a try. We were tucked into a booth table by a friendly hostess, who hung up our umbrellas and briefcases. Service was friendly, attentive, but not over-bearing. We ordered a cocktail while we perused the menu. Great drinks, nicely blended flavors. We couldn't decide between the stuffed calimari and the grilled so we got one of each. The grilled was far better. For entrees he had the scallops, which were divine; fat, seared on the outside and juicy and fleshy on the inside, served atop crisp bacon. I had the monkfish with seared sweet onions, grape tomatoes, spinach and halved fingerlings. It was also great. Honestly, we could have split an entree. Though not large in size, the food is nicely platted with the appropriate amount of time between appetizers and entrees so that your tummy has time to realize it is getting full. The BF has a sweet tooth, so we split the Amalfi cake. It's basically a lava cake with some fresh vanilla bean ice cream and fresh, ripe strawberry slices. The berry was the best part for me. The cake was okay but I feel like I've tasted this same cake a lot in the past several years. Overall I would definitely come back. There's a nice, private room in the back, so this looks like a solid bet for a work or friend/special event location.

BYOB, BYOC* and BYOA** for a pure fish experience. Â This is not fussy food but rather pure presentation of delicious ingredients and plate that lets the food speak for itself- and this food doesn't just speak - it sings.*** Â Ask for bread, the dipping sauce is like crack and the waitress doesn't always remember to bring it. Oh yeah, and don't come here if you have something private to discuss the tables are close. *Bring your own cash, they don't take credit cards **Bring your own appetite, the portions are large. ***When I say the food sings, I don't mean how I sing, I mean it sings well.

The search for the greatest food in all of NYC is over. Â I have found it here at Caracas! Seriously, the BEST MEAL OF MY LIFE. Â And trust me, I've eaten out a lot in the past year in NYC. Went with my two best friends on a Saturday night, arrived at 10:30 pm. We were seated at the bar, but right after our server took the order, a table opened up and we were seated promptly. Â The ambiance is very cozy (but not in a cramped way) and very representative of the gregariousness of the Williamsburg area (but not in a hipster, bad way). Â  Guac and chips: Guac is so creamy and savory and just awesome. Â The chips are homemade and mixed in with plaintain chips which I adore. Ensalada Fresca: so good, i don't exactly remember what was in it, but it was freaking great. La Mulata (arepa): so so so savory and i just didn't want to stop eating it...go plaintains with little bits of jalapeno and black beans! All three of these dishes go so well together. Â I"m vegetarian btw, and this place is super veg-friendly (e.g., they can substitute baked tofu for any meat and have many simply veg options). Â For the meat-eaters, don't worry, they have chorizo, shredded beef etc., which my friends got. Live your life to the fullest--HURRY UP AND GO TO CARACAS!

It was my first korean brunch in 2013, i like westernized korean fusion. that was great combination. Food was nice and very catching eye balls, Taste was phenomenal. Service was great!!! Highly recommend!!

Friends brought me here for the first time, and I must say it was a lot of hype. I didn't want to spoil their moment in grace after waiting 40mins to be seated, but Ippudo does make some damn good ramen. The interior decor is nice, even from the bar sitting infront of the entrance, all the way to the packed tables in the back. The servers and waiters we're cool, but I'm just going to judge based on the food... The ramen was good, and pork buns were awesome, but expect to pay for what you ordered. I believe a majority of the ramen bowls we're around $17+? kinda on the pricey side, but definitely didn't matter since we came here completely hungover from the night (morning) just a few hours earlier.

Maybe it's good if you're drunk and from out of state, but if you know want to know what's really good chicken and rice, head over to Sammy's halal. Beware of the hot sauce and know what you order before they ask you.

This place is fun! It's probably one of the better sports bars in the midtown west/theater district area. They have TVs in abundance and their beer list is above average. I love that they put on the sound for big games and do not try to imitate a suave lounge/club by playing top 40s music. They're a sports bar first and that's refreshing in some ways. Three Monkeys is a modern sports bar with multiple flat screens and a huge projector to be viewed from the second floor. There's plenty of seating and the TVs are logically placed throughout the bar. However, it can get very crowded here especially on the ground floor. The bar fare is decent here. The chicken nachos are a good appetizer to share with friends. It's a large dish and quite delicious. My friends were a bit disappointed in the wings which have more batter than meat. Anyhow, most people don't come to Sports bars for their food. The atmosphere here for viewing games is great and that's important.

Most of the food on the menu is pretty good although overpriced. I eat there frequently due to the fact that I live several buildings over. The quesadilla is delish! My biggest complaints lie with the staff. They are always extremely friendly but seem to regard their place of employment as a place for their own entertainment. In a restaurant like Grey Dog where you wait in line to order at a counter, I'd rather efficiency over excessive chit-chat. Friendliness is great but keep that 20-person-deep line moving! Also, does Grey Dog only hire smokers? The staff is constantly clogging up the sidewalk, and even sitting on neighboring stoops, smoking cigarettes. As a neighbor I hate it. The sidewalk is always littered with butts and getting to my apartment requires walking through a smoke-cloud. Patrons be warned that now that the weather is nice, sitting by the large open windows is akin to sitting in a smoking section. My third complaint is that the high-top tables are reserved solely for the staff. Not sure if it's officially so or not. Regardless, they are permanently parked there on rotation. (Even when they are not, their sweatshirts and half-eaten meals are.) When the place is packed they should offer those tables to customers wishing to sit. Bottom line - great food; fun atmosphere but a predominantly young hipster staff who would rather hang out with each other than work efficiently.

They have the best corn I have ever had. I went to NY in May 2008. I'm still telling people how wonderful the corn is at Cafe Habana. Â It has the best flavor. I went to a lot of places to eat while in NY, but this was by far my fav. I can't stop thinking about it. It's very yummy, and addictive.

I went here last weekend with my boyfriend and it was awesome! The weather was nice so we got a table outside and were served right away. The waiters were all super friendly and offered excellent service. We shared the orientale as an appetizer which was good. Then I had the ravioli and my boyfriend had the salmon pasta which were both really good. For desert we had the choco coco crepe which is coconut, chocolate and ice cream drizzled on a crepe, it was soooo good! I would come back here any time!

Still my favorite brunch place in the city (essex is a close second). many reviewers are not a fan of the new location (in a hotel) and the fact that it is no longer self serve sangria. i was a little skeptical whether this new situation would be comparable to the original, and i was pleasantly surprised. The food is the same and still good - i've tried the breakfast burrito, chicken quesadilla, and most recently the flank steak. nothing amazing, but all solid choices. one loss was at the old location they also had a taco truck that went around the dining room serving chicken, steak, or pork tacos to start the meal. they also still have 'unlimited' sangria during your meal. Â they start serving you when you sit down and will continue as long as you are eating. there are approx 4 white and 4 red types to choose from (and you can switch your choice each time). we were concerned that a potential downside could be slow service (meaning less drinks during brunch) but our server was fantastic. turns out i actually prefer not having to get up and get my own drink since he did such a good job. this is a great way to kick off the weekend. though i would recommend you visit on saturday so you have sunday to recover from all the fun you will likely have during and after you finish brunch!
The first of a handful of nearby tapas bars, and still the best. Patatas Bravas and Pimientos de Padron are amazing, as are many other dishes.

These people make bank on selling flour and sugar. I got the throwdown wafel while in Central Park and it was very good. It seemed to be a combination of wafel, whipped cream, and some sort of peanut butter. The throwdown is $6, and add-ons (i.e. strawberries, ice cream, etc) would have further made this an unreasonably priced wafel. Definitely try it for the experience, but the price is a little high for return visits.

Pretty good meal here. My boyfriend and I got a table in the back garden. It is really cute back there! The sangria was really good. We ordered: -Toro Con Palta: tuna belly tartar with avocado mousse, capers and soy-lime sauce -Avocado salad -EntraÃ±a: grilled skirt steak with chimichurri sauce -Mussels with garlic, bacon, cilantro, tomatoes, scallions and white wine huacatay sauce The skirt steak was the star of the show. It was tasty, juicy, delicious and perfectly cooked. It's making my mouth water right now just thinking about it! Everything else was average. Nothing blew me away.

This place is for people who aren't bothered by crowds and love Italian food. It is a cool concept with a cheesy amusement park feel. There are arrows pointing where each seciton is and a line to follow. There are wheels of cheese stacked up and meat hanging like a clothesline. It's more than just pizza and pasta, so can have some vino or get some gelato.

We started with an appetizer of avocados and tortillas. Who would have thought that something as simple as that could be so delicious! I ordered the slow cooked heritage pork, which was tender and the perfect portion size. The sides weren't memorable. They had some interesting fusion dishes on the menu that I will have to try next time.
Much better than the other carts I've frequented. Â Big fan!

Excellent hearty brunch, you will not go away hungry. The dining room has larger communal tables, so it was perfect for our party of 5 people. If you go with a smaller group you would have to share.
