Â  I had the haluski hash with sausage, peppers and pickled vegetables. The haluski reminded me of spatzel not tremendously flavorful on its own, but it bound the meal together. The sausage balls were extremely well seasoned and flavorful. A couple fried eggs on top and you have an amazing meal perfect "gut bond" to cure a hangover. It was a little greasy, definitely not the place to count calories. Thoroughly enjoyed the thick country bread and homemade hot sauce , which I believe contained sweet roasted peppers. All in all an excellent meal, with plenty of good quality coffee. i want to come back to the the excellent draft beer selection which featured several I pilsners and lagers.

I really want to give this place 5 stars but there were a couple of dishes that made me cringe. Inside is dark, romantic, and a bit on the louder end. MAKE RESERVATIONS. This place is ALWAYS packed and I've only gone on weekdays. Let's start with what went right: - black iron shrimp - my drink. I think it was called Strait from Beirut. Everything inside sounded like a mojito but it tasted nothing like it. It was sweet and delicious. - lebanese rice (UHH-MAZING). WARNING! They ask if you want rice (I thought it came with our meal but they actually charged us $8?) - DUCK SHAWARMA. oh man. I DREAM of this almost daily - warm date cake Things that made me gag: - mouhamara (walnuts, sundried peppers, pomegranate molasses). What IS this? cold spread? The waiter told us to order this and my friend and both did NOT like it. - lebanese snowball (dessert). I'm big on dessert and was really pissed at this plate. Â I mean seriously, I was PISSED at the food for not tasting good. It was THE worst dessert I've ever put in my mouth. Bitter, small portions, and just wrong. At least I know better and won't make the same mistake next time.

Probably one of the most expensive bowls of spaghetti I've ever had, but Â also one of the best I've ever had. Nice bite, perfectly coated with simple basil marinara. Don't let the portions fool you, you can taste buttery deliciousness in every bite and the stromboli basket for the table is a meal in itself. burrata appetizer - very fresh and delicious creamy polenta mushrooms - overrated foie gras ravioli - way too salty black tagliolini - amazing taste of the sea chocolate vanilla parfait - heaven obviously some items are hit or miss, personally I'd stick with the pastas and dessert. too bad the place felt a little 'stuffy' with business meetings, froufrou 'meatpacking' area with wait staff faking an accent. if you can zone these out, and enjoy your meal it's still worth a visit.

The food is good, not great. It's tiny and cramped. You leave smelling like the daily catch. Â But there is something about this place that makes it irresistible. I think it's because it has the romance of what I imagine a New York dining experience should be like: intimate, personal, out of the way, full of personality and character. It's a small adventure finding and dining at Cafe Condesa (it has no sign), but it's a rewarding adventure none the less. A great place for dates or any time you're looking for intimacy over glitz, character over style.

Came here for dinner, around 6:30pm, luckily we beat the dinner crowd. The place is tiny without being overbearing. Lighting is a bit dim, but we were still able to read the menu. The staff was very attentive and friendly, but not the point where we wanted to kick them for constantly checking up on us. They were able to give good recommendations and we weren't disappointed with the food either. On top of that, the owner dropped by the table and offered a complimentary edamame. Their edamame was seasoned differently, a slight spiciness to it as well. The table got the zutto pork belly bun, slightly spicy, but it was very good. There was a good meat to bun ratio, and the bun was very soft and chewy. We also ordered the calamari, which is okay as far as calamari goes, and there was another plate, the peppers, I think, I don't remember, but I just knew it was spicy and I don't really eat spicy food. The main course was the ramen. I got the well known tonkatsu ramen. It was very savory and filling. It didn't leave a bad msg taste I would get from other ramen places, so I take that as a good sign haha. Someone ordered the seafood ramen at the table and it looked amazing, well worth the money. The shrimps were huge and not what I expected at all.
Great brunch spot. Â Delicious eggs benedict.

Heaven in a sushi bar, Chef Yasuda is the man. Â If you go, you have to sit at the sushi bar and get the omakase. Â stand outs were the giant clam and the squid face, which usually isn't on the menu. Â GO! Â You won't be disappointed.

all american fare in Tribeca. gf got the pulled pork entree. i got the cobb salad. it's traditional american. food is ok. nothing to write home about. the biscuits they bring out pre-meal is pretty tasty (esp cheddar/bacon ones). it's waaaaaay too much food. they should lessen the price, and the portions as well. prob wouldn't come back.

shabby chic atmosphere in the style of havana's barrio chino except the food is mexican (and very decent fresh mexican at that )in the spirit of La Izquina or Zarela. Â it gets an extra star for the ambiance, great drinks and easy going, competent staff. Â After 3 visits the food is closer to 3 stars meaning it's really good but not super memorable. Â Do have the guacamole, however, it was delicious...cheers!

As the other reviews highlight, the food at Purbird is incredible. I'd be remiss, however, if I did not highlight the delivery service. It was raining heavily tonight and our food arrived perfectly warm (all the way out in Prospect Heights). The delivery man was soaked with a smile. I can't thank him enough.

Incredible sushi! Â Super fresh fish, well cut, and the rice is perfect. Â Additionally, we sat at the sushi bar and the chefs were nice and put up with our ordering individual pieces at a time. The prices are insane, and so I can't really imagine coming back with any frequency. Â When you you're paying $3-4 for a single bite, it adds up quickly. I would rather come back here for a business dinner.
Terrible food and service, bad atmosphere. Go elsewhere.

My 1st 5 stars! It was that good! My friend took me here yesterday [Thursday night] The service was great. Waiter was very kind & friendly. Made sure we were content without being too intrusive. Even as we left, we had 2 "good byes & thank you" from workers/cashier/boss maybe? Now the FOOD. Granted I was hungry, but still. I ordered a Salmon burger because yelpers recommended it. Wow!! I inhaled it & finished it quickly. I couldn't stop eating it. I finished my plate clean. No crumbs anything remaining haha. The salmon was soft w/ a unique fried texture. The salad w/ it was fresh. The bun was soft but not soggy. The avocado & mayo made the dish fabulous & tasteful. Especially the mayo. I was really contemplating on taking one home to eat again, but I stopped myself =) Never knew healthy / organic food could taste so good. I was shocked. We also ordered kale w/ garlic, also good. My friends ordered the chicken soup & chicken cutlet hero, which they enjoyed also. The dessert was not that great though, so skip that.

I loved this place! They are hands down the best pancakes in the city. Advertising & hype comes true for this place. I came on Friday at 11:30am and there was an hour & a half wait for a table, but they do the cool 'text you when it's ready' thing which is nice. Luckily I was by myself so I was able to score 1 of 2 bar seats to eat a quick lunch before work. I ordered the banana walnut pancakes which were SOOO good! I was not able to finish it so it's definitely a hearty portion. And the syrup they give you is a specialty as well w/ butter already mixed in. Be warned though - they give you a TINY amount and then charge you $2 when you ask for more (which is pretty lame in my opinion). Can't wait to bring fellow pancake-lovers back to this joint!

The whole experience, from beginning to end, was absolutely amazing. Sat in the main dining area, with the skylight fully retracted overhead. The bread basket offered a couple of different choices, all extremely good, especially the one with rolled up salami(?) inside. I'd just be reiterating everything that everyone else had said so I will just generally state: Mushroom polenta. Spaghetti with tomato and basil. Go. The spaghetti almost literally brought tears to my eyes. The first bite transported me back to Italy. No pasta in the US has ever made me feel this way.
The veggie burrito is incredible! I love the free chips and salsa! The prices are great! I wish they were open later, it would be great after going to a bar/club.

Definitely my favorite chicken and rice cart in the city. Â  I constantly crave it now that I'm not in the city anymore. Â I remember my college days, where we would take a cab 40 blocks north to get chicken and rice at 2am and cab it back just to fulfill our craving. Â The combination of the pita, the rice, the white sauce, the hot sauce just can't be beat. I love that I can get this practically any time of day - so consistent and reliable.

Although the B rating and cleanliness leaves much to be desired. Dom makes the best pizza I have ever had. I mean ever in my life!! That amazing slice is worth the wait. 3 cheese and fresh basil and olive oil to top it all off. A true gem in brooklyn NY!!
Food was overpriced (expected in Time Square) and greasy. Â Service was alright and seating was quick. Â Essentially, it is everything you expect from a restaurant in time square.

OK, I don't typically review a place after visiting just once, I prefer to get an average overall impression if possible, but this place made such a vivid first impression that I've already made up my mind about it. If JoJu is anything to go by, Vietnam might be the best thing to happen to sandwiches since, well, sliced bread. Up front, we ordered the original sandwich, a lemongrass chicken sandwich, and the bahn mi fries. Â They were all winners. The biggest thing I've noticed is that the vegetables don't just sit there and be vegetable-y like in many sandwiches. Â You know what I'm talking about, the lettuce serves as tasteless filler texture, bell peppers contribute a mild sweetness, tomatoes grace us with their watery crunch, but without the meat and cheese it would just be a sad salad sandwich. Â Here, the pickled carrots, daikon and cilantro are what make it special, the vanguard of an unrelenting assault on your tastebuds. Â That's not to say the meat just takes that lying down, at least not the lemongrass chicken. Â I was delighted to see them use thigh meat (dark meat!), and it's a juicy counterpoint the the tang of the veggies. Â I didn't add the fried egg, as I wanted to get a base impression before building on it; I'll save the egg for the inevitable Next Time. Â They also gave me spicy mayo on the side to put on it, but the sandwich itself was just so tasty I couldn't bring myself to add to it. Â Again, there will be a Next Time. However, the spicy mayo DID play a standout role in the bahn mi fries. Â The french fries themselves were double-fried and thick-cut, which is my ideal, as it means a solid crunch on the outside and a warm, soft interior that reminds you that, yes, this is a potato you're eating. Â Don't get me wrong, the barely-recognizable-as-potato sticks and the did-you-actually-fry-it-or-just-nuke-it softer thick cut fries have their place, but I'll take these over those any day. Â Drizzled with spicy mayo and piled with the same veggie mix as on the sandwiches, the bahn-mi fries are a serious contender against poutine and chili-cheese fries as my favorite fry-based food dish. Â The side of spicy mayo I got with the sandwich also happened to make a handy dipping sauce when I reached the oft-neglected underbelly of under-adorned fries. Best of all, this place is cheap as hell and in my neighborhood, so I can visit often and anytime. Â That I didn't notice it earlier is a mistake I fully mean to rectify. 5/5, see you again soon JoJu XOXO

The staff was nice but honestly I was not impressed with the food at all. It's a family style venue (meaning big servings) Â so if your looking to bring your kids to get chicken fingers and fries this is not your kind of place. They are very overpriced in my opinion. We got the baked clams appetizer, bake ravioli, chicken cutlet and shrimp parmigiana. The bill came to $140. The sauce was very garlicky and I have tasted better and expected better about this restaurant. We also wanted to order mozzarella sticks something that most Italian restaurants have, not this one, they don't have them. Basically no traditional finger style food. Just make sure you ask your server before ordering about the size and portion. I think this would be a great place to go with a group, not a family of four.

Overhyped, in my opinion. We were disappointed with our visit here, much like with Bareburger. Hubby was craving ribs, so we came here with high expectations. He ordered a full rack, with the slaw and mac and cheese as sides. I ordered a turkey burger with mac and cheese. The ribs looked great when they came out, but when hubby took a bite his face showed the disappointment. I tried a rib and although it wasn't bad, we couldn't see what all the hype is about. The slaw was regular slaw, mac and cheese was bland. The little corncakes were good. My turkey burger was tiny, dry and bland. Waitress was very nice. Now, I understand the premise of the shop and I fully support it. Organic, grass fed meat from local farmers is the way to go. And the meats in the butcher part of the store looked divine. Next time I will pick up some meats to make at home. But I can't justify spending $60 on a meal that left us feeling disappointed.

One of the best brunch spots in Brooklyn! My friends were in town visiting for my birthday and wanted to take me to brunch. I told them we had to come to SoCo! We each got something different based on all my favorites. We tried each other's food and everyone was pleased. We also did the endless mimosas. The shrimp and grits is my favorite, the red velvet waffle w/ fried chicken is a close second! Good food. Good drink. My kind of Saturday afternoon!
* Very good place to eat, the service is good, but very expensive.

If I could eat at Fitzcarraldo every night for dinner - I would. Â Although the restaurant is a well kept secret - it deserves to become a neighborhood staple as well as a destination restaurant. The menu appears limited - but don't let that fool you. Â I am a vegetarian and the chef is so talented and flexible, I have seriously had two of the best meals ever at Fitzcarraldo. Â After eating there twice - once with a large group for the tasting menu and the second time with a smaller group for their a la carte dinner- it is no exaggeration to say that the family style tasting menu was amazing and for the price - a steal. Â Both the tasting menu and a la carte dinners were individualized to accommodate all dietary requests. The service is attentive and wonderful. Â Other reviews cover all of the amazing aspects of this restaurant so no need for redundancy. Â I really can't say enough about Fitzcarraldo. Â Just thinking about the food is inspiring another visit.

Enter at 11:10 PM, a table of 5 patrons in the back corner trying to figure out their check. Â Staff cleaning up and preparing to close for the night. They close at 11:30 on Saturday nights and they'll remind you nicely. 20 mins to order and eat. I got the Pork & Chicken mixed broth with Kambi (soy sauce flavor). Â Maybe it's because I was sick and my sore throat was just going away but it was too salty for me. Â The pork however was delicious! Â Best pork I've ever tasted in my Ramen. Â So I cherished my pieces of pork with each spoon of Ramen. Â  My BF had the spicy basic ramen which looked creamy and slightly pink. Â It wasn't as spicy as we expected but just right. Â I'd actually be able to finish a bowl of that spicy ramen without getting swollen lips. Â  Next time I'll try the Soy bean sauce Miso ramen. Â  I ate it so fast I burned my tongue but it was worth it.
Love the feeling of doing bbq by your self. Food is also very good. Don't forget to order their desert!

What with all the ultra-positive reviews, I was expecting a life-changing experience. Â It didn't change my life, but the fish was extremely fresh and tasty. Â The prix-fixe is a very good deal, so go for that. Â I have to say, though, that even though the portions are satisfying, they could be a bit bigger. I chose tamago, orange (?) clam and Spanish mackerel. Â The tamago was excellent. Â I could have eaten 20 pieces of it alone! Â The other tastes kind of blended into each other, and I wasn't very impressed, but it was really good, just because it was so fresh! Â For dessert, we got our ice cream mochi. Â The sad part was that we just got one...... The place is very nice, very minimal decor, modern, etc. Â But I was a little disappointed that they didn't have the fun toilets. Â The bathrooms were clean, but could have used better decor. Â The service was pretty great and snappy. A great experience, yes, and I'll most definitely go there again.

My boyfriend an I used to frequent Basso Est back when it was on Orchard St. down in the LES and we became very friendly with Alex (the owner) over time - I'm sure it also helped that Mr. Boyfriend speaks Italian...but, either way, still a great place. It's been over a year since we've tasted Basso fare so, we went to Basso 56 for the first time since its location move and everything was still as we remembered it, absolutely fantastic. Â We received complimentary glasses of Prosecco after Alex recognized us from the days of yore. Â Yummy! My boyfriend had the Cornish hen special, which he said was really good. Â I had the osso bucco special, so delicious. Â It tasted just like how my grandmother used to make it! The menu really hasn't changed with the location moves and we've always been extremely satisfied with everything off it that we've sampled...that would be pretty much the entire menu. The staff - excellent. Â I will honestly say that the service we receive at this place is some of the best I've ever received at a resonably priced restaurant in Manhattan! Well worth a try!

Moto is hands-down my favorite restaurant in Williamsburg. And that's saying ALOT....the ambiance is so low-key and romantic and these guys basically invented the old-timey look. The live music on weeknights alone is enough reason to go {be ready for crowds + avoid weekends completely}, but then they whip out small plates like swiss fondue {best I've ever had!} and lentils with fig jam & queso blanco on toast...mmm. oh, and the dessert wine is divine. just go...
No pretention, great music, $4 beer-and-tequila specials, vegan sloppy joes, a pool, table, board games, and unlimited cheese balls? I'm not sure what more anyone might want in a bar!
Great food , great vibe ! Make sure to SHAREEEEE plates are huge. Waiter was Â overall experience great

Classy little spot attached to Madam Geneva that has fancy, $13-15 drinks. Very speakeasy-like. I really enjoy places like this. No frat-like behavior going on, just adults talking and being chill with each other. I approve.
Not sure what the hype about the food is about. Â  Service is great, and attentive though.
Delicious coal fire pizza, quick service. If you are looking for the 'authentic' New York slice, this isn't it, but in my opinion, it's better. Cash only & gets really crowded.
Love the falafel!

I can't speak for other dumpling houses in NYC, because this is the only one I've been to. But when I can feed myself well beyond capacity for $3, I am officially impressed. Vanessa's Dumpling House is easy to miss and truth be told, it feels like the kind of place that only gets customers because they're referred or brought there by friends. I was brought here by my friend L, who knew I was in need of some seriously good budget eats. I looked over the menu and figured that if an item only cost $1, it would be tiny, in the way that the value fries are usually not too filling when you order them from a (insert your chosen fast food burger joint here). However, L warned me not to buy too many things. "This stuff will fill you up!" she said, but I scoffed and ordered a vegetable sesame pancake AND a veggie dumpling. That might sound like absolutely nothing but rest assured, no matter how hard I tried to stuff my face, I could NOT eat all of it. The veggie bun was alright. A little bland for my taste but a super bargain for $1. I want to say the sesame pancake was also $1 or so. It was bigger than my hand and stuffed to the brim with slivers of carrot and zucchini in some sort of tasty sauce. It was a welcome lunch that carried well over to dinner. The place itself is cramped and seating is hard to come by. You're usually best having one person stand in line to order and another hovering over tables waiting to swoop in for a seat. Try to know what you're ordering before it's your turn as the ladies here are quick to ask and seem as though they'd be even quicker to get annoyed if you're still unsure of what to get. All in all, a tasty place for a cheap meal. Will definitely be making a return visit next time I find myself in NYC! PS. This place gets $5 for being absolutely delicious and affordable for what you get. This is no way indicates that this would be a place to go to daily or that it is in any way an example of fine dining. I couldn't imagine how much weight you'd gain from such a diet. But if someone's willing to try it, let me know. I'm curious. Any wanna-be Morgan Spurlocks out there? PSS. Sriracha fans will be pleased to find giant bottles of the stuff on the wooden tables!

I don't know what it is about this place but I freakin love it. The bar was salvaged from an antiques dealer from the Bronx. Nice simple menu, old fashion drinks, and 80s rock. I mean could you ask for more?

The first time I had Artichoke pizza was at about 5 am and all I remember was that it was an explosion of yumminess in my drunken mouth! I have been back since while sober and it is still just as good!!! The artichoke and spinach slice is what I always get (I've tried the crab slice too but it's not as good) and all I can say about it is that it's delicious! I think this place is getting more and more popular since I first went, so now there is usually a line out the door (which isn't really saying much anyway because the place is so small). But, expect to wait. Also expect the wait to be worth it. YUM

Farm to table good eats. Â Get the korzo burger, meat or beet, truly addictive. Â Also, the beet salad is amazing. Â It gets crowded quickly, be prepared to wait, or get there early. Â Also, AC is not yet up to speed for the summer, but it seems they've fixed the heating problem for the winter by attaching a shelter to the front.

This is the place to go! Â Go to this place and experience their great food, drink, and service. Â Best mediterranean place in NYC...in fact, one of the best restaurants I've been to anywhere...period. Â  These people are masters of the spice rack, grill, and mixed drink/alcohol. Â You see and taste their attention to detail in every dish and drink (we had). COCKTAILS: great balance and delicious; best cocktails i've had to date in NYC. Not a cocktail type of person and had 2! Must try the refreshing Fresh Meadow and tasty seasonal option Cedar Cider (served cold or hot; opted for cold). MEZZAS: Brussel sprouts!...uniquely prepared and assembled. A perfect marriage of sweet and savory; is very light but you feel guilty cuz it tastes decadent. Just try it and you won't be disappointed. Shrimp hommus (that's how they spell it): so very creamy; must get with shrimp Octopus: perfectly tender (very difficult to do with THICK cuts) with yum lamb pastrami and a citrus vinaigrette dressed greens to cut the richness of the pastrami. Grape leaves: subtle tomato based bite sized snacks similar in size to vienna sausages (vs. the overly lemony versions at many other places) ENTREE: Mixed grill (for 2): 2 perfectly black and blue kafta lamb chops (as requested) served over herb roasted tomatoes, chicken shish taouk (juicy and tender), lamb kebab, and the unassuming yet very tasty ratatouille. Â Served with garlic whip trio each specifically made for each of the meats. DESSERT: Get the huckleberry cheesecake and candy bar. Â Cheesecake went oh so well with a glass (ahem...2 glasses) of their spanish Moscatel WINE: A bottle of Grgich Hills Zinfandel...yum Last but not least: SERVICE: Great, very knowledgeable and attentive staff....and they gave us some complimentary lip smackingly good passion fruit cocktail and a strained yogurt dish. :)

Thursday at 11 am -- about a 10 minute wait in a cramped line. The bonus? We got to peep what other people were eating and a waiter came by with some orange slices while we waited. Once seated, the hubs and I got some mediocre coffees. I ordered the much-talked-about Dutch pancakes (lemon, ricotta, and blueberries), our daughter ordered chocolate chip pancakes, and the husband ordered huevos rancheros on our server's suggestion. We also ordered a side of bacon and cheese grits (you know, health foods) to round out our indulgent meal. In the end, we had an ungodly amount of food. The pancakes are thick and dense (I usually prefer a thinner batter). There was little difference between the Dutch pancakes and the chocolate chip -- I could detect a slight lemony flavor, but the ricotta didn't seem to do anything for the taste or consistency. The flavored butters that came with the pancakes were interesting, but only alright tasting to me, and syrup was regular diner fare. Same goes for the huevos rancheros and sides -- all were pretty typical diner food. Nothing bad, but definitely nothing special. Our bill came to $44 -- reasonable for the amount of food we ordered. Service was excellent. Attentive, friendly, and helpful. All in all, I don't think we'll return to Tom's. There are plenty of places to get similar food, and I can cook a better, cheaper breakfast at home.

Just enjoyed a superbly crafted Dominican dinner with the family. My little guy had the ox tail stew which I was fortunate to sample. The gravy was savory perfection and the Ox tail melted in my mouth. I had the pork mofongo which was garlicky scrumptiousness with just the right amount if tasty pork crackling. My big guy had uthe bistec encebollado with white rice & red beans . The steak was flavorful & tender, again dressed in a delicious gravy /sauce that complimented the rice perfectly. My hubby had the chicharon de pollo with yellow rice & black beans . Best black beans I've ever tasted and I love my habichuelas guisadas . These black beans had just the right amount of tangy vinegar taste , I could have eaten them by themselves. We topped off our meal by sharing a flan with guava sauce and a cafe con leche. The service was five star , attentive , patient with my husband changing his mind 5x Â and friendly. The food is off the charts , the prices are reasonable. & the portions healthy but not overly so. We were here Â a year and a half ago after we attended a party in the neighborhood and Â when contemplating dinner options this evening after our visit to Brooklyn Puerto Viejo was an easy pick as we had waited too long to re-experience this delicious food. Everything was memorable from the empanada apps, to the sangria. I would eat here again and again, but alas we live in Jersey so until the next time Puerto Viejo.
Very nice place with helpful staff. Meatballs/fricadells is handmade in the kitchen at the place. Create your own dish and be happy

Quite a nice find here in downtown Brooklyn. Pretty much identical to the famous Prosperity Dumplings in LES if you know that place. Although I have to admit the wait seems to be less here but the place is smaller as well. But during your first visit best to just get the dumplings to go to avoid having to fight for a spot to sit down. They do seem to offer more noodle selections though but this being my first visit of course I went for dumplings and sesame pancakes. The dumplings were definitely well worth the price and tasted very freshly made. I had more expectation out of the sesame pancakes however I felt it was pretty dry and lacked sauce that Prosperity would add in their version. But for the price you pay $3.5 for 10 boiled dumplings they're still worth it despite they raised the price it seems sometime earlier this year. If you have a chance definitely give this place a try. I do think it gets pretty crowded though so definitely be ready for some wait especially during lunch time.

Plus: - great for boozy brunch for LADIES; There were 5 different groups celebrating birthdays; All women, all beautiful - Excellent price point for unlimited drinks - Restaurant does not try to rush you out after you've finished your meal. Our group of 13 was there from 2:00pm-4:30pm drinking and laughing. I noticed the groups around us lingering and having a jolly time after their meal as well - Bright! There's a skylight in the main dining area. -Roomy: A lot of places pack in people and tables - our server was very attentive and did an amazing job of refilling our drinks and dealing with our rowdiness. At one point two of my friends were hanging out underneath the table Cons: - LOUD- you have to shout to the person next to you. It's a very open space where noise echoes and bounces off the concrete floor and walls. The music is blasted at an almost unbearable level (although 20 somethings might not have any issues with it). - only one bathroom each for each sex Our entire party ordered the pre-fix, unlimited drinks in addition to two pastas. I enjoyed the pasta dishes better than the tapas and sides. The pizzas also looked divine. I would definitely choose the pizza options over the tapas the next time I go. Do NOT go there on a brunch date or with your family. Do go with a group to have a great time and to get drunk.

A fantastic patio where you can sit outside surrounded by a variety of fruit trees, a diverse and well priced menu, excellent service, and you get to BYOB? Taqueria Kermes is nothing short of perfect and each every experience here has been superb. Whether you're on a date, a meet up with friends, or a large group gathering, this establishment can and does deliver on multiple levels. The food here is delicious, fresh, and very well priced. The nachos are a great starter and perfect for sharing, these are definitely some of the best nachos I've had. The wide variety of tacos are unique and two are enough to fill you up since they're really generous with the fillings. Suprisingly, one of the best items on the menu is the rodeo burger...full of flavor and good until the last bite. I would highly recommend this place for any occasion and any time of day!

I used to love this place but not anymore. Last time I was here I realized that the product is lower in quality. As I was eating the chicken n' rice their was a lot of yucky ligaments and bones in the food. I cannot recommend this place anymore although I used to be a big fan.

SMALL! Â Don't make plans to come here for dinner... it's not that kind of place. What kind of place is it? A perfect place for a bottle of wine and a snack. Or an esspresso and a sandwich. The food is great but when they say small plates they mean small plates. There are only a couple of tables for four and a long bar for six. Not the spot to go with a group.

I've been here several times with large groups of friends. I can't remember if they take reservations but I know for sure that they won't seat you until everyone in your party has arrived. Their bar is ALWAYS packed and it gets more packed as the night goes, especially in the summer. This place is fun and energetic. Their crab meat guacamole is the best when they have that on their special menu. I actually like everything on their menu and it's a good portion size.

I expected more frm this place especially w all the good reviews on here but after abt an hour of waiting, this place was only ok. I've had better pizzas without this long wait. ehhhhh....i'm sorry to say, i would have been much happier eatting a greasssyyyy yummy $2 pizza from costco than wasting my time here...but now i know better. :P whatever, now i can say 'i've been here, tried it and it's off my list.' :P

OK...so I came because of all the 5 star reviews. Sorry to burst everyone's bubble but for me this place is not sensationally amazing. I think it's decent, along the lines of Chavelas, but not OMG authentic Mexican food is here, or something I would walk a mile for. I did think the fish tacos were really good, but pretty much everything there was undersalted. I'd order from here and carry over to Washington Commons across the street, where there is alcohol.

I have to say we were all very happy and satisfied with our experience at Dino BK. We arrived for our res on time and were seated after about five minutes. The place was extremely busy as it was opening night. The restaurant is decorated very nicely in full blown BBQ/industrial Brooklyn style. We ordered the Swag sampler for two, honey BBQ wings and breakfast all day for starters. The swag sampler was nice and presented well. It comes with deviled eggs, boiled shrimp, fried green tomatoes and chicken wings. Everything on the swag was pretty good not great but definitely enjoyable. The wings were very nice. The breakfast all day which is smoked brisket hash with an egg on top was delicious! It comes with two sides. We chose turkey neck greens and cole slaw, both were nice. We all had combos for entrees. The brisket was excellent! The ribs were very good but i could only eat one because we ordered a ton of food. The pulled pork was delicious and the sausage my brother ordered was very good. The combos come with two sides. We tried beans, potato salad and all had mac and cheese. The mac and cheese stood out as the favorite. It was cheesey as hell!!! The combos also come with a little cornbread muffin style that was delicious. Everything was very good and it felt like they were very much on top of things for the launch and that was good to see. The drink selection is very nice as well. Service was quick, attentive and pleasant. They have a ton of different options and should be able to satisfy just about anyone. Yes there will be families and kids and i would suggest making a reservation. This is a BBQ restaurant that is for everybody. People who have tried plenty of BBQ will not be blown away by it but the difference is you can just sit down, relax and be SERVED some very solid BBQ. Well done by Dinosaur on opening night!

Went this week for my birthday with my girlfriend. Very nice place; kinda NE farmhouse feel to it. Cozy and nice. The wait staff was very friendly and attentive and overall, the experience was great. Now, onto the food. I tried the tasting menu which consisted of: *Olive oil poached big eye tuna - Really well done. Light and flavorful. A really nice start *Duck Bolognese with Gnocchi - REALLY nice. small plate so the flavor had to pop. Â Had a really nice saltyness to it; which would have been too much in a large plate but in a small plate, worked perfectly. *Steak (I forget the cut) over carrot puree with roasted garlic - Again, REALLY nice. Perfectly cooked and the carrot puree was great. Small cheese plate - Very nice selection including Cato farms Bloomsday; which I always like Dessert - Rasberry bread pudding with marscapone ice cream -delish! My girlfriend had: *Sauted lobster with champagne braised napa cabbage, warm quince soup - The quince soup was really well done. REALLY nice balance of flavors. The lobster was a tad overcooked. Still really nice but we're being hypercritical here. *Pan roasted striped bass caramelized shallots, red cabbage, creamy polenta - HOLY CRAP!!!!! This was the TITS! Definitely the nights big winner. The skin of the bass was crispy and incredible. The polenta was out of control. Flavors all balanced and working well together. As my lady said, "it's hard to talk about this dish without cursing" BIG WINNER. Overall, our experience was great. Highly recommended.
Smile across my face just thinking of how delicious the fried chicken was. Â Definitely worth another visit in the near future...

This place is a great place for anyone and everyone! Â The food is really authentic Viet. Â I went on a Sunday evening, and it was rather busy, but I only had to wait 10 minutes. Â I ordered the sautÃ©ed beef cubes over rice, classic banh mi, papaya & mango salad, and spring rolls. Â Everything was delicious! Â Lots of green and orange. Â All items on the menu are cheap, too! Â The only reason I wouldn't give a full 5 stars is because it took awhile for our order to be taken and the banh mi wasn't my favorite. Â Other than that, I can't wait to come back to try the pho!

Came here for lunch with a coworker and it was a decent meal. Cool ambiance with plenty to look at and a pretty extensive menu. I had a fish and a cactus taco and shared the chicken sopes with my friend. The fish taco was the favorite of the meal but overall everything was a bit dry and bland. Also when I asked for some hot sauce on the side to add more flavor, they brought a bowl and charged me a $1 at the end. I mean, a simple bottle of tabasco or cholula would have sufficed. Anyway, I am glad I tried it once, but not sure if I would go back.

This place was a pleasure to visit, even for me, just a tourist from California. This is the first place I've ever seen to actually serve the corn covered with the spicy mayo and cheese. Around where I grew up, there used to be these guys that would walk around with shopping carts holding all the essentials of a mini restaurant, and sell the corn on the streets. I love the atmosphere of this place also. It's so colorful. It almost feels like you dived right into the heart of Cuba the minute you step into this place. The outside area is nice to just sit back and relax with a frozen margarita or one of their other drinks.

We were at Roberta's for a birthday party this past weekend... and it was great! At first we were very confused by the address. We drove from south Brooklyn, as as we passed by more and more projects we were a bit dumbfounded that such a highly regarded pizza place would in the middle of Bushwick. The pizzas were all great: Fresh ingredients, just the right amounts of spice/sauce. The salads were yummy (and we saw their lettuce garden on top of their building) and satisfying.

Simply a great burger. Â Definitely one of the tastiest in New York - everything is spiced just right; super flavorful. Friendly, very low-key, casual staff. Good service, but make sure to come at the right times, because it can get a bit on the crowded side. Â Definitely not the place to sit and hang out casually, because they always have people waiting for tables. All in all, super great food, great vibe.

OUR FAVORITE NY PIZZA! Â This is easily pilgrimage pizza. There were people in there from Minnesota just for the pizza. I truly love to watch Dom DeMarco make the pies. I like to stand at the counter and just watch him work. A true artisan. He makes each one himself for 11 hours a day. He works nonstop creating each pie and has flour all over his shoes. His daughter was working at his side and even dealt with a heckler at the window with ease. Seriously, a pizza heckler? Anyway, to me there are two main types of pizza in NYC. First you have the type with the big bubbly crust, the fresh mozzarella, and basil...I guess it's the margherita pizza type. Second, would be what I call NY style pizza with the thin crust and tangy sauce which is duplicated mostly in every little town and city. Then you have Di Fara which to me is in a league all of its own and leaves them all behind. It is gooey, cheesy, tangy sauce with random chunks of tomato, the basil is fresh and yet not overpowering somehow. Quality ingredients, three types of cheese. I love how he drizzles olive oil before he puts it in the oven. We seriously love this place. Our favorite pizza. The pizza dreams are made of. The pizza that is "last meal" worthy. We want to move closer to this pizza. Pack up and live on Avenue J in Brooklyn. It's that good.

Rule 1: Do not let your taste buds experience a dish that has not already received rabid hype on Yelp. Rule 2: Don't order anything off the menu. We ordered a simple Chinese watercress spinach plate (off menu), and it was $14. For that amount, I expect my spinach to sing and dance. At other restaurants, it would cost around $7-8, and of course, the waiter will not expend any additional effort to tell you how much it costs unless you ask. I assume. Every bowl of rice costs $1.25, fyi, and the Cantonese seafood crunchy noodles were overstarched and the vegetables in it sour! Ah, another $14 down the drain. So don't order ANYTHING OTHER THAN WHAT IS PRINTED ON THAT LARGE ZAGAT EMBLAZONED POSTER, unless you like to donate to this place. And the bathrooms...be careful not to slip into toddler piss.

Scott Conant does his Italian food well... Always a great pick of mine if I am ever in the area but either you have a reservation or expect to be seated at 5pm or 10pm on any given day. We did an assortment of the octopus, mozzarella in carozza and braised rib and farro to start which were all excellent. Â Fish was tender, mozzarella was light and creamy and the rib was so light and perfectly cooked. Pastas are a must - we did the spaghetti with basil and san marzano tomatoes (his call to fame) and agnolotti Â with rib and bone marrow which was excellent. Â  Capretto to finish off the meal with some spinach was phenom - I would highly recommend this to anyone. Service was great and so was the atmosphere, especially being in the meat packing district. Buon appetito
delicious. always a long wait, so plan ahead. basic family friendly environment

It is all about the people here, ask for Jeff or Luis, the best. Â Jeff will keep you entertained during your time spent there! Â The buzz is great, it is a hopping place with the best pizza and check out the antipasta bar or Jeff/Luis will tell Â you what to get. Â  Those two are the reason to go there.

just 3 weeks young. fresca was a welcome find while waiting for the lirr. Â new, clean, with a sweetly decorated euro theme. Â great small menu. i had the omelet crepe. Â flavorful with just the right amount of 'shrooms, onions and ham. Â she dresses the edge of the crepe with a rich swiss that is half in/half out of the crepe allowing for a crunchy skirt to form. Â can skirts be crunchy? Â :) Â this one was and mmm-mmm-good. the menu doesn't contain the newly added milk smoothies of bananas and berries. Â all good stuff.

3 1/2 stars. I came with Sally and John and we ordered the duck prosciutto, a double garlic pizza, another pizza with duck meat on it, the Bee Sting and then a couple desserts with dessert wines. The duck prosciutto was really good except cut needed to be but wider. A little too much duck fat with the think strip of duck with it. The pizza here is really good. The dough is very similar to naan bread and the menu is constantly changing. We all agreed that the biggest issue with the pizza is that the dough is soft. Not crunchy at all. The best one hands down is the Bee Sting. The other pizzas we liked but didn't think were really amazing. The Bee Sting is pretty awesome. And you can order pizzas off the menu so you can always order this one. It's similar to a pepperoni with honey on top. It's damn good and this would be the choice pizza to order every time. Desserts are solid though the dessert wines they chose for us really matched up well. Finally, like everyone else had stated, this place really is very hipster. Not a little, a lot. Yep, I'm one of those guys that really can't stand hipsters, but despite this it didn't really color my eating experience. Just letting everyone know that it's hipster here.

I LOVE GOOD BEER! Â This place has good beer! Â Therefore: Â I love Rattle 'N' Hum!!! Ok let's get serious: Â there are A LOT of beers to choose from and I can only drink so much. Â I'll be honest I cannot remember the names of the all the beer I drank - but I can recall drinking a stout that is a life changer (I believe it might have been the Southern Tier Mokah Stout) and an excellent blonde. Â They have all their beers listed on the website so check that out. Â The drafts range in price from $7-$10, but the bottle range from $7 to $25ish (but these are 22ozes). Â The food is your typical pub food. Â  Warning - I went with a party of 12 and we really struggled to fit. Â This is not the place for big parties. Â Even though we were loud and annoying the wait staff was excellant, put up with all our seperate checks, and was surprisingly speedy. Â  For those of you who prefer a PBR, Natty light, or the like.... this is not the place for you.

Talk about pretty high end Gourmet Greek cuisine. Let's start with the grilled octopus, it's a must have. Very tender and full of flavor, served with garbanzo beans which adds a unique but good flavor. The arugula and spinach salad is Â perfect. Let me back up to the bread that is served with olives and Greek cheese. I could have had that for dinner and skipped the main course. We ordered the short ribs and halibut for dinner. I'm sure everything is good. For dessert you must try the lavender mousse. Enough said. Service is really on par. Any time a cup of water was empty or drink was done they were always there to provide a refill. Love this place!

Came here a while back for brunch and got the huevos divorciados and a few sides. Â Great service and nice atmosphere.. a little modern trendy with a hint of tropical Mexico vibes. Â Get the brunch menu and also finish it with a tres leches. Â You will thank me later!

I am not sure how the burger is still considered secret since it seems to be posted on the specials board every day, but it is great. As is the food and service. This is my neighborhood restaurant, and when faced with limited options elsewhere I often go hungry and save the money and calories until I can eat here.
This place is amazing. Delicious food.

Echoing what everyone's already said, this place has incredible service. Â I mean, seriously. Â I have never met waiters who are more on-top of their game. Â I think they all went to etiquette school. Â It's unreal. Â  Food is fantastic if you're into the whole New American thing. Â They go a little too heavy on the odd meats for my taste. Â If I were into this genre of food, I'd probably be giving Gramercy Tavern 5 stars. Â I'm just not into it, but that's just me. The service, though, is divine. Â I can't say it enough.

I came here for brunch on a drizzly Sunday and had a lovely time. It's a tiny little place with maybe six tables. Had the huevas con chorizo, which came with a salad and some fries - a good, delicious amount of food. I was a little hesitant to take my girlfriend from Mexico here as NY Mexican has disappointed me many a time, but she said her green enchiladas were phenomenal. Prices were just right - it ended up being $16 for my food and a cappuccino.

I want to cry writing this review, because alas, this was my favorite go-to restaurant when I lived in Brooklyn, and I miss it so, so much. I don't know what it is about this place. Despite the sometimes unfriendly Hipster waitstaff, and the almost unbearable Hipster clientele that make up 95% of the Diner scene, I simply could not get enough of this place. At 6'3", 240 pounds, I'd manage to bend my body in half and squeeze my giant frame through the tiny door of this original, barely-refurbished 1927 diner, week after week, just for the privilege of eating their amazing food. (How's that for an intro to a 5-star restaurant?) Vapid Hipsters aside, I know EXACTLY what it is about this place: The food. There's no real menu at Diner, save for the burger and steaks which are always available. You learn the menu at Diner when your server sits down with you and writes it out on the parchment-like paper that serves as a tablecloth. The menu can change almost daily, though the theme of ingredients used will typically last through a month or so. Pay attention -- for the whole writing-on-the-table thing is a useless gimmick. For example, as the server describes to you the most amazing salad with 20 ingredients grown fresh from their local farm, all they write on the table is "SALAD." Not too helpful when you need to recall the 11 or 12 extremely verbose items they just finished reading to you. The food at Diner is simply amazing. When I moved to Brooklyn, I ate, like 4 or 5 different things, and generally refused to try anything new. I never believed I would try so many new foods until I came to Diner. Diner was my breakthrough. Every single thing I ever got talked into trying here (hello, rabbit?) I ended up not just liking, but LOVING. Diner's food is so fresh and so well prepared that I will pretty much try anything they serve up here. But when it's all said and done, what's the most standout, special thing Diner serves? The burger. Raised from cows on their own farm, and ground to order, Diner makes a burger that must have crack in it, because its amazingness defies reality. I have never, ever had a burger this good. No matter how you order it, it will come out rare-to-barely medium rare. Meaning, it will still be twitching and bleeding when it arrives on your plate. And that's the crack, I think. I used to eat burgers medium-to-medium well, but Diner converted me and showed me what I was missing out on. Perhaps I'm a vampire, I dunno. But you haven't lived until you've eaten a burger from Diner. The fries are amazing too. As is the homemade mayo. DO NOT PUT KETSCHUP ON YOUR BURGER OR FRIES HERE. It's mayo or nothing. Oh, how I miss you Diner. You're like that ex-girlfriend I wish I could bang again.

One of my favorite to go spots!! They're reasonably cheap and haven't disappointed me yet. They have a decent variety of Korean food, my favorite would be their spicy rice cakes since I'm a loser for spicy food. Def worth the stop!

Please do me a favor and do not come here. This is a neighborhood gem and I would like it to stay that way. Whether it be breakfast, lunch, or dinner, La Taza does it right. Here are some of the highlights: Your time - In and out in less than 15 mins or stay and relax for hours. This place lets your eat at your own pace. Original - Don't be scared when you see Octopus Salad and Tripe Soup on the menu. While this place boasts Puerto Rican originals, it has items for all to enjoy. For the timid, try the Spanish Bean Soup, or the Roasted Chicken. Portions - Come hungry! These guys make an art our of piling an unimaginable amount of food on tiny 50 cent plates. If you take your time and breath you should be able to finish all. Price - You could probably buy an entree at Taza with the spare change you find in your couch. With just about every item on the menu coming up under 10 dollars this place is probably less expensive than shopping at your local NYC grocer. The Verdict - This place is great. Do our neighborhood a favor and find some other place to eat. The last thing I want is to have to wait in line to eat at this place. -Andrew ------------------------------ Recommendations: Breakfast - Bacon Egg and Cheese Lunch - Spanish Soup Dinner - Roasted Chicken or Fried Pork Dessert - Flan my man!

We went to Gramercy Tavern on Easter Sunday for my husband's 30th birthday and I would really recommend this restaurant for a special treat. We don't usually go to this kind of place but found it really friendly and welcoming - the service was excellent. The food was really great but it was the little extras that made all the difference - like the extra bits of food they brought between every course and the fact that they put a second table cloth down when the wine waiter had spilled a drop of wine on our table! If you are visiting New York and looking for an upmarket but unpretentious meal out - choose the Gramercy Tavern (main dining room).

I've been here *two times*. I strongly recommend the shrimp and calamari. They season the shrimp very well and they have a little special sauce that is so delicious! Â  Â  I loved it backyard it's very peaceful! They put a fan which I really appreciate... and there is stones everywhere...the first time it was perfect...the second time the neighbors next door were doing construction it was very loud. Â  Â  The actual lobster roll is not my fav. The first time i had it ...it was a lunch special and they put coleslaw on it and I hate coldslaw. I thought that was very odd. But honestly its about preference maybe you like coleslaw. Other than that it's very delicious. Its hard to find really good lobster but this place is worth checking out.

They are Gluten-Free! They have the Celiac seal of approval! The restaurant is small yet inviting. The set up was incredibly comfortable. The staff is attentive and friendly. The food is yummy! I have to eat Gluten-Free and usually don't have much in the way of choices. Sometimes gluten-free food is tasteless. Not here, I could even eat the bread sticks! The staff offered us bread sticks as we waited for our table, they could see how famished we were. The pizza was so perfect my moth is watering as I write this review. They have gluten free cupcakes: red velvet, carrot, vanilla, Â chocolate peanut butter, and fudge. Don't forget to ask them about their Winkies! Their answer to the gluten-free twinkie! If I lived in NY I would be there once a month at the very least! All the baked goodies are made fresh! The manager is Albert, he is not only great to look at, he is attentive, and runs a friendly restaurant. They cannot accommodate more than a party of 6 and don't take reservations. I have included their website if you have more questions. risotteria.com Â  Â  Â  Â 212-924-6664

I got a full veggie sandwich on sesame bread, a red bean bun, and a coke for less than FOUR F*CKING DOLLARS. FOUR. Aaaaand it was delicious. But PLEASE be waiting for your number. The women that work there are SERIOUS. Right, there's no seating, and no one who works there is nice, so don't go there to impress a special someone. Go there because you need a meal that costs less than the change you found on the street that day.

I had the best meal at Calle Ocho tonight. Â I am in from out of town and went to Calle Ocho because I read that they had some gluten free options. Â I ordered the grilled steak but didn't realize that "carabas" is blue cheese and attempted to scrape it off when my dinner arrived. The bartender and manager quickly arrived and insisted on replacing the meal despite the fact that it was my fault.. When my meal arrived it was one of the best meals I have had in a long time, The food, manager and bartender made this a great meal. I hear that they have a great brunch including bottomless sangria. I definitely will have to check out.

Terrible place for parents with kids. We tried at the early evening hours since that's just what we do when we go with kids. Â Although there were open tables, we got told that it'd be a 45 minute wait not once, not twice, but three different times. Â The final time that we swung by there were over half of the tables completely open, they had just open, and nobody waiting to be seated, and yet it would be a 45 minute wait for us, a party of four! Â  Staff was rude and unapologetic until we walked out the door with a quick 'so sorry'. Â We're never going back.

Located on the 2nd floor. Food: Raw octopus with wasabi - chewy but good. I wish the octopus wasn't cut up into such tiny pieces though. It has hard to eat this Fermented salmon - good Agedashi tofu - very good but same as other places Yakitori: Chicken heart - delicious Chicken neck - tastes like regular chicken breast/thigh Chicken thigh - plain Japanese fried chicken - needs more seasoning? Beef tongue - too chunky - prefer thinner more marinated slices Beef short rib - OK Chicken meatball covered with rice - pretty good Frozen banana with coconut milk and tapioca - best dish of the night Yakitori Oh Taisho is still my favorite
Great service, great food (with big portions), great drinks and decent wine list (both of which rare for Thai restaurants), AMAZING decor. Can't complain at all about this place.

best banh mi in the city (for the price). there are other places that are fancier, but they charge double so im giving the crown to ba xuyen. i like to walk over to sunset park to eat mine... pretty good view of manhattan from there
Not as good as everyone is saying..... Good yes, but not WOW, and certainly not worth the wait in line and travel time it took to get there.

I went here with my family before going to a Billy Joel concert. For appetizers we ordered the lobster ravioli which was amazing. For the main course, I ordered a margarita pie which was also excellent. The one issue I had was that they rushed us to get out. Then again, it was a Friday night and they had reservations to meet. if I am ever in the area I will go there again, but not on a Friday night or a weekend!

Undeniably, Ippudo is one of the most famous chain stores in Japan. But will it ever occur to me as the best ramenya in Japan? I doubt so. On the other hand, it can be seen as an outstanding ramen restaurant in NYC. Still, I do not think the ramen is the best one in the city. The reason I am giving Ippudo a four star is that I consider ramen as cheap and filling, and that was not the image I got from Ippudo. Interesting points are that Ippudo's tonsoku (pork leg bones) soup has a very strong flavor and its noodles are unconventionally thin. And what the f is wrong with all the ramen restaurants in NYC that do not serve gyoza??

Food: delicious and well priced given the presentation and ambiance. The cocktails: superb. Huge variety ranging from your most basic to your most imaginative and everything in between. The service: impeccable. Delightful wait staff who are attendant but not overly aggressive. This place is a class act. Great for a date, a casual post show bite and beverage, or anytime you want to find yourself in a cozy little speakeasy with at least a few fedoras roaming around. Easily my favorite bar in midtown.

Food: Awesome Cost Per Person: $15-$30 What we got: Roasted Chicken Salad and Benedict Jane Meal: Brunch Pay & Stay or Grab & Go: Pay & Stay Dress Code: Casual Bring: Anyone Good to Know: Go early or make reservations for weekend brunch

The wine selection is spectacular and food is absolutely incredible! I been here a few times now and everything I've tried has been amazing. ASPARAGI GRATINATI, CALAMARI (seriously the best I ever had), LINGUINE ALLE VONGOLE, COSTOLETTE D'AGNELLO etc...alll soooo good! I'd recommend it all! Â  The waiters are very knowledgeable and although the place is kind of small and gets busy, the service is flawless. Â Also, the place plays real good music and it has a gorgeous garden in the summer. Â  I can't wait to go back there!

This is just for the drinks part of the menu as I went only for drinks. The place is loud, fun, and gets packed on the weekend. The drinks are good, but there isn't anything new about the menu. The DJ was good the night I was there. Overall a fun place to go, dance, and hang out.

This place is amazing. It's such a unique but chill brunch spot. The menu is an interesting and contemporary twist on Filipino food. So much was happening with my taste buds! Seriously, the seasoning was on point. Potatoes were magical. Banana ketchup? Yup. Sangria? Big and strong. And I had two jumbo prawns with their twist on eggs florentine. My boyfriend had tasty spam with his benedict. The people next to us had sides (some type of sausage skillet and long spring rolls), which made us want to order more food, but we resisted. The chicken and waffles and french toast looked BOMB.COM. The atmosphere was chill and there was a forest theme with moss on the walls. Never been for dinner, but DEF go for brunch.

Ate Thanksgiving meal here. This place tries awfully hard to reflect a cozy, rustic hide-a-way. This attempt masks an overpriced, pretentious venue with marginal food. The pork schnitzel was overcooked and relatively flavorless. The pickled vegetables consisted of what seemed like a Vlasic dill pickle and a spoonful of canned caraway sauerkraut. The desserts were extraordinarily forgettable - if not bad. We were stuck with a $350 bill for four and walked away wishing we'd never seen "Edi and the Wolf" - on-line or in person. Skip it. NYC has too many good restaurants to waste your time and money here.
Amazing, friendly service delicious food wonderful decor fab wine list whats not to love? ill def be back

This is my hands down favorite place in NYC for pizza. Â  My boyfriend and I split an "Old Fashioned ($20)" with pepperoni (+$3) and Kalamta Olives ($3) with a side of Meatballs ($10). Â I literally was stuffed by the end of it, it was AMAZING! (And we have leftovers) The pizza was perfectly made and the meatballs were so great! Oh and when you are seated inside (which was more quiet than outside on Stone Street) they gave us each a piece of bread and oil+Balsamic which was also perfect. Â  I am bringing everyone I know here. Â I am in love!

This place is fantastique! In the city, food this good would be twice this much. They haven't raised their prices in all the time that I have eaten there. Which is unusual in ny. This is the way felafel is meant to taste (for all those of you not in the know). If it tastes any other way it's due to budget set backs. All their other salads and stuff are also worth trying.

Looking for "New York Pizza"? You'll find it here. So there are usually lines outside the door at this place - it's for a reason. Grimaldi's in Brooklyn is one of the well-known, guide-tapped landmarks of New York. They have some pretty awesome pizza when you eat it fresh from the oven, especially on a semi-chilly day. The warm, gooey cheese and coal brick fired dough has no other match in the area. My favorite is the white pizza with extra garlic. On a really nice day, order take out and trot over to one of the nearby parks (Empire Fulton or Brooklyn Bridge)...

The first time I came to Bubby's was super late on a Friday night and I was pretty drunk so everything tasted amazing! The second time was for a Sunday brunch and I was less drunk (came after a wine tasting class), and it was still pretty good, so yay for Bubbys! It's a cute place, looks like a country diner or something. There's a plastic cow outside and a bunch of benches that rock back and forth, which can be pretty exciting when they are masquerading as regular benches. The burger was delicious. I also had their watermelon lemonade and asked for vodka in it and that was very refreshing. They had the most amazing and fluffy sour cream pancakes with strawberries on top. Awesome. I want to go back for the pancakes!! However, I felt like the prices were high and this review makes me sound like a lush!

Wow, I'm definitely singing Song's praises! I have to say this is the first time in my life where I'm not left crestfallen by the hype....seriously! Â Song very well might be my go-to Thai place from now on. If you read nothing else read this: for 5 entrees, 1 glass of wine, 1 thai iced tea, Â 2 summer roll appetizers, 1 small calamari appetizer = $67.50 (tax included)!! ( Don't know about you but I can easily spend that for a 2 person dinner in the city). We arrived a little after 8pm on Saturday night. We waited 45 minutes or so to be seated; partly because we were a party of 5 and partly because it was so nice out ( for winter) and people were out in droves. With so many people and no proper waiting area ( unless you count the sliver of narrow space behind the bar that extends from the front door to the dining area) the wait was a little frustrating, but I'm happy we waited! Once seated, our waitress was attentive enough, friendly, and great about keeping the table clear. The calamari appetizer was a little under fried and floury for my taste, but the summer roll was tasty. Everyone was satisfied with their entrees ( fried seabass in coconut-curry w/ veggies, beef in chili basil w/ tons of veggies, tofu pad see ew, chicken and string beans in red curry, and chicken in garlic reduction w/ tons of veggies). The portions, as mentioned by all other yelpers, are more than generous (I mean even the pad see ew noodles were bigger than I'm used to). Amassing everyone's leftovers I can comfortably say I have lunch for 3 days or so : ) More impressive than the portions, their ability to retain each dish's flavor. There was a DJ "spinning" in the dining room, the music was good, not too overwhelming and my parents ( both 50+) were definitely enjoying it. All in all a great night!

Who is giving the restaurant all these high ratings??? I went here 3 times... months apart. I kept going based on the strength of the ratings. Each time I felt the rice was cheap quality and overly soggy and the meat (I had oxtail, curry goat and curry chicken), was poorly seasoned. My family is from the Caribbean and we know how good island food should taste. This is not it.

So while I give Taim credit for their creative 'falafel balls', I despise being asked if I'd like some "Israeli salad" with it. No offense, but that cucumber, onion, tomato- olive oil Â combo has been a Mediterranean delicacy for thousands of years, and Israel is a fairly new country of European Jews (85%) who have only been introduced to the cuisine in 1948. Where is the Jewish flavor or contribution? Suddenly falafel is Jewish? Did the French call Morocco's couscous 'French'-- I think not. Â  The staff seems so programmed to always call it 'Israeli' salad, which is simply weird and mildly offensive. Secondly, tabbouli is not supposed to have more bulger grain than parsley. Either the cooks don't want to spend the day chopping parsley--or the grain is cheaper. All in all, the hot sauce is great, the pitas a bit thicker than I'd like -- and I'm impressed that they have Omba, (origin- Iraq).
The bar is small so it can get very crowded and very loud. If you're bar hopping start here a little earlier in the night and get a mojito! They're served with fresh cut sugar cane. So good!

This place is so so bomb. The hubs and I have had a lot of sub par and down right awful mexican food in NYC! That was until we stepped into the creatively decorated establishment. Their chorizo burritos are no joke and neither is my loyalty for this place. Only Mexican place I will ever go to in this city! Viva la Taqueria !!

Absolute top notch service. The best manager coupled with beyond amazing food on top. Ribs are RIDICULOUS fall off the bone with a very original sauce. Desserts are pretty unbelievable between the Carmel cheesecake and the apple tart. You really can't go wrong dessert wise and the hangar stack and the ribs are on point. No complaints

Left feeling full but a little underwhelmed. Â Everything I tried (pomegranate berry sangria, lobster puff pastry, duck, albondigas) was delicious, but just not the best I've ever had. Â The seating was also very crowded, I almost felt like I was a part of each of the two dates going on to my left. Â It's definitely an intimate space that would be great for date night. Â If you ever see a duck special on the menu, give it a try... that was my favorite bite of the night!

Another great gem in the heart of NYC's China town...25 Â¢ hand made dumplings need I say more? This isn't a place to go have a sit down meal in, but it's a good place to grab a quick lunch while on your way to your next meeting or 15 min lunch break. This place is the epitome of hole in the wall. Tiny place with 20 Asians crammed in a little tiny kitchen, working hard to make you the most tastiest and cheapest dumplings china town has to offer. The most delicate, delicious, perfect dumplings that I've ever tried. They come in various fillings. I had the pork with cabbage dumpling and the shrimp with cabbage. The shrimp dumplings had whole shrimp inside not that blended seafood stuff you get in traditional shrimp dumplings at your local Chinese/sushi joint. The pork dumplings were def better than the shrimp. Stick with the classic. I also had the sesame pancake, which is sooooo good. I got it with chicken and the chickens was crispy and so flavorful. 4.5 stars, and worry every ounce of it.

Rocked a sunday brunch here over the summer. Nice to get a Mimosa or screwdriver with morning food and sunshine. The grub portion a bit on the small side so you always order something to thicken you up.

These are awesome sandwiches! What really stands out here though is the bread, crusty little loaves of deliciousness. I've only tried two of the flavors so far, but I will gladly go back and work through both the regular menu and the special menu.
Great food and service.

It's your typical Texas barbecue joint, or what I imagine one to be. A bit loud, and at least 7 TV's tuned to sports. Supposedly anything with Creekstone Farms listed on the menu is halal, and they have pretty good sides with all the meals. The mac and cheese is good, but not the "best I've ever had" as some people are claiming.

I came here with my wife on a Wednesday night and ordered to go. We got two orders of the lomo saltado and an order of the rotisserie chicken. I've been to many Peruvian restaurants and this one is by far the worst one. The lomo saltado was awful the meat was dry and not juicy at all. The meat looked recooked and burned. I think we got left overs from the day before.This is the last time I set foot in this place.

I never understand why Korean food is so expensive (maybe someone can explain it to me). But thanks to Woorijip, I'm allowed to enjoy the flavor of Korean cuisine, without having to fork over an arm, a leg or even my wallet. After some serious shopping, I decided to take a quick break to grab something good to eat. Without any hesitation, I decided to go to Woorijip because here, their foods are always fresh, the selections are good, and there are always enough seats to go around. Being that Woorijip is also a buffet ($6.99/lb), I usually like to try a little bit of everything when I'm there. Their food is never disappointing; in fact, some of them taste pretty interesting yet always yummy. If buffet is not your style, Woorijip also offer pre-packaged food for you to grab and go (perfect for microwave dinners or the office) and if that still doesn't fancy your interest, well then you can order food from their in-house kitchen, which I have yet to try.
Wasabi mayo is my personal favorite. Â This place may be the only reason for a Jersey kid like me to go into the city.

$6 for a big bowl of noodles with 11 dumplings for $3. The noodles are hand made, stretchy, and flavorful. The soup is pretty generic, but it is delicious. If I could eat here every day, I would. Sadly I'm not from New York where I can get delicious noodles at an extremely cheap price.

HOLY Austere gimme some more of that POlENTA!!!!! Ok so maybe it's not something you'd normally order but I urge you to just do it, you will fall in love. The decor is nice and dim, the tables are long and wooden and can accommodate abou 8 people so it's good for groups. The bar is nice and wide. The music is great - well it's Alternative Rock (Kings of Leon, Phoenix, Coldplay, etc.) so if you expect to hear something else maybe you can ask the lovely owner, she was always very helpful whenever we asked questions about the food, drinks or anything really. The drinks are good, haven't had the wine but the beers are awesome! The food: Okay, I read some of the reviews that kept complaining that the portions are too small..no, it's not that, it's the fact that we're used to always getting these gynormous (yeah it's a word or it will be, I'm using it get off my case :) portions which most times we don't even finish and then we take the leftovers home but they end up getting thrown out a week later because we forgot to eat them - that my friends is a waste. The portions are small for some orders, for others they are just adequate, if you want a big arse platter then go to Applebees or something of the sort to satisfy that big belly! Â The delivery is quite nice too, food comes on these chopping blocks, it's simple but tasteful. Also...every single time I was there, we were always offered to try various dishes on the house, I don't know many places that do that very often...do you? The bathroom is nice and clean, the reason why I mention it is because on the wall they had the following: "employees must wash hands, customers are encouraged to follow suit!" That is great, customers should wash their hands dang it!! Haha. Now go get off Yelp and get that polenta! :)

I went to Lombardi's with two friends who had recently moved to NY. After seeing Lombardi's on Food Network, I was anxious to go. BT and I got there early (about 11:30 AM on a Sat), so we waited for my friend BS at the bar. Starting off with some nice Bloody Mary's. BS arrived about 10 minutes later, and we were seated almost immediately. We saw our server sparingly , once for drinks, and once food, and to drop of the bill. He was nice enough, but not very attentive. The pizza arrived, a large pepperoni and sausage. The pizza was a little smaller than I though It would be, and more greasy. Still a pretty good pie. Nice cheese, great crusts. A little expensive for the size, but a nice and memorable meal.

It's a little ways out, but it's worth the trek! Though dinner reservations were made and confirmed, our names somehow didn't make the list. Sad face. Even still, our hostess was beyond gracious and more than accommodating, seating us promptly at 8PM. Yay! ATMOSPHERE: The interior was both elegant and cozy, with velvety booths, dim lighting, and a very welcoming staff. What I loved most was their semi-private back room/garden space with a retractable roof for the summer months and a beautiful wood-burning fireplace for the winter months. This space can be reserved for private parties and events or as an extended open dining area, when the crowds come in droves. A very unassuming exterior, with an amazingly lush interior and oh-so romantic vibe, Salinas is perfect for an intimate gathering with friends/family and also great for a date night. SERVICE: Our waiter was most helpful! While introducing us to the dinner menu and providing cocktail suggestions, we received complimentary croquettes and crudite from the kitchen. He also ran through the specials for the evening and answered all of our questions and dietary concerns. Dietary, you ask? Yep...we took Meatless March through April. On this note, both our waiter and the kitchen accommodated beautifully! FOOD: We started with tapa plates of roasted brussel sprouts and green cauliflower and grilled octopus. We loved the citrus yogurt dressing that came with the brussel sprouts and cauliflower and the octopus was cooked perfectly! For my entree of sea bass, the Chef kindly offered to serve up more than expected, adding cockles, mussels, and shrimp...don't mind if I do! Rich in flavor, yet light in appetite, I was happy as a clam through every last bite! DRINKS: With a savory meal on the way, my waiter recommended their Cava Blanca cocktail, of muddled grapes, vodka, fresh lemon, agave nectar, topped off with a cava float. Not-too-sweet and incredibly refreshing, it was the perfect pairing to my meal. After a wonderful 2 courses, I wished we ended up staying for something sweet...but alas, a feverish boyfriend was in desperate need of sleep. Oh wells...we'll just have to return in the not-too-distant future!

Heavenly comfort food. Perfect for soaking up all that alcohol in your stomach. I ordered to go, the pulled pork, chicken and waffles, tater tots, and of course the chicken biscuit. Everything was cooked to perfection. But the pulled pork was a bit disappointing. Otherwise The staff was nice and helpful!

Mmmm yum.. amazing amazing amazing pasta! It is SO yummy. All the food is incredible and the presentation really adds to it. Great service, drink selection, and service. The only reason I give 3 stars instead of 5 is the portion sizes. They are SUPER tiny, especially for the prices.
The lines here are loooong. But, for good reason. There is nothing you can get here that won't be the best you've had. Awesome food, awesome smoothies. I'm a fan!

Duck breast was top-notch and cooked perfectly--seared crispy fat on the outside, nice and medium rare on the inside. Very rich and flavorful. Get it! Steak tartare needs a minor adjustment--there was a sweet flavor in there...perhaps a sweet tomato gave it a ketchupy taste. Comes with fries that are vaguely reminiscent of McDonalds, but I actually mean that in a good way. I normally think house cocktails are a scam--usually a way for a resto to achieve some scale, but there's a reason the classics exist. Howe'er, in this case, they're quite solid, and reasonably priced. Kronenbourg is a nice simple lager, good and crisp on a hot night. Boston Bibb salad was good but slightly overdressed. Escargot were excellent. Atmosphere is pretty good--admittedly, the clientele are biased to stuffy white Brooklyn Heights people, but the music is good, and many of the other touches give it a decidedly authentic feel.

This is my 1st 5 star rating. Â They deserve it. Â Fantastic, authentic, fresh middle eastern food. Â Everything is good here, even if you think you don't like something from the way it sounds. Â I've been thoroughly satisfied every time I eat here. Â Plus it's not expensive, at all! Â It's all good. Â It's all inside. Â JCPenney... or Bedouin Tent, rather.

Returned on a snowy Saturday night to be welcomed by this amazing little 3-piece band. Luck was on our side as we got the last table... Food was equally as wonderful this time -- different soups, different entrees for both boyfriend and I. Neither of us was disappointed. This time, we got a bottle of red (forget what we chose now, but it was great). Per the suggestion of the waitress, we tried the date cake for dessert -- WOW. It was heavenly. A perfect, perfect Saturday night...

Love it when a place can make you feel completely transposed to somewhere tranquil and relaxing.. Rabbithold did exactly Â that for me on a Sunday brunch. Super-cozy place with its exposed brick, tall ceilings and wooden floor. Â I appreciated all the little details in the decor such as, the monkey chandelier, old eyeglass chart. Staff was very considerate by letting us know beforehand that the only seat in the back was directly under the sun. We then decided to sit by the "privacy door", w/ a great view of Â the lovely outside garden. Ordered the egg Benedict, which came out fabulous and tasty. Just perfect! My companion really enjoyed his French toast. Brunch here ranks among the best in Brooklyn. Tempted to return try the brunch/dinner menu

I came here for happy hour a couple weeks ago for the first time and it's a really neat joint. Â I love the underground feel and lack of tourists. Â It's mainly just finance people and asian people, haha. The place is really discreet and before someone told me about it, I must've walked by here at least 30 times without ever seeing it.
