Â  That being said, the atmosphere is great, the finger food, cheap and delicious like wasabi shu mai? and grilled squid. Â Beer, at $12 a pitcher was a great deal. Â I will definitely be back soon! ****

This was another stop along the Insomnia Tour (my birthday in NYC). Amy Ruth's is so cute inside...I love the murals on the wall!!!! Great service....really good food, I enjoyed something from just about everyone's plate, salmon patties, catfish, greens, cornbread, mac & cheese....oh and red kool-aid! Ya just gotta try it!

We went here starving and all four of us left without finishing our food. My son's chicken tacos were full of bones. My shrimp taco was luke warm and chicken wings were rubbery. Everything tasted like it had been sitting around for a while then stuck into the microwave. How does this place stay in business? Seriously, it was worse than fast food on the NJ Turnpike.

Mulberry & Vine is just what this block and neighborhood needed. Â Healthy prepared foods without the grocery store feel of Whole Foods Market. Â  I am sure their selection of salads, sandwiches and soups will get refined over time. Â But for now, I will enjoy their quinoa black bean chili, tofu sliders and Luli Tonix juices. Â It is hard to disagree with "real foods, big flavor, no dieting", although I think they are overdoing their message of healthfulness, especially in a neighborhood that doesn't need the goading. Over time, I am hoping they stay open during weekends and offer breakfast choices. Â Great start though!

I do not know what the 4-star hype is about this place. Just because its in TriBeCa doesn't mean it's automatically delicious. I went here for lunch when I had jury duty as it was right across the street from the court house. I was highly disappointed. First, everything on the menu is super expensive for what it is, which is basically an "upscale" diner. I had the Mac and cheese, which tasted like it came from a box, and the chicken salad sandwich, which was basically diced chicken covered in mayo. My crappy office cafeteria makes better chicken salad for a quarter of the cost. Maybe I just ordered the wrong things, but I will not be going back to try anything else. There is much better in the area, like the Subway restaurant two blocks down.

Really one of my favorite restaurants in New York. I've sampled a good majority of the menu items here and am consistently wowed by the food. Â The prices are more than reasonable and the portions are just right-- no skimpy tiny plates and nothing obnoxiously huge. Â  I highly recommend starting off with the "selection of spreads" appetizer-- while all 4 are great, the eggplant and chickpea spreads really stood out to me-- lots of great, fresh flavor. Â We wanted to make sure we wiped every last bit out from the bowl so we asked for extra pita bread, brought over to us free of charge. A favorite is the chicken souvlaki -- tender chicken with creamy tzatziki sauce wrapped in a warm, chewy pita. Â Served with extra thin, crispy herb sweet potato fries and a classic greek salad, this dish makes for a great lunch or dinner. Â The sheep's milk ravioli or dumplings are two other standout dishes-- tender handmade pasta which tastes like something my non-existent greek grandmother would make for me. Â  The wine selection is also plentiful with a wide range of prices. Â  The waiters are helpful and eager to share their knowledge, but service can be very, very slow. Â Even during a weekday lunch when there were no crowds, it took me a while to get water, give my order and receive my check. Â Waiting isn't too painful though since the decor is a beautiful, calming white and blue. Â I absolutely adore the mosaic in the back by the stairwell leading to the bottom floor! Kefi, just pick up the service a notch to match the level of the food. Â In the meantime, I'll continue spreading the word about how amazing this place really is.

Love this place. Location is convenient, prices are just right, cozy, can hear each other speak. It does not have a fancy or trendy vibe, but a perfect place to catch up with a friend on a rainy or snowy day and not feel pressured to get kicked out. Also, the very reasonable prices and incredibly homey pastas and food make you feel very relaxed. The service was excellent - when my friend couldn't decide between two wines they automatically offered her a sample to try. Two thumbs up, great job.

Proclaiming a restaurant as the "Best Place to Eat Hamburgers" in the WORLD (as per UK Guardian newspaper) is like a triple-dog dare to check it out. Â Who can resist? The Little Owl bacon cheeseburger really is fantastic. Â Who can ever really say if it's "best in the world", but it is an outstanding competitor amongst a strong pack of contenders in New York. Â If it makes any sense, I'd describe it as a feat of "balanced succulence". There are so many fantastic components in this burger, but I think what is great is that despite the lush and fulsome nature of each part, they all manage to complement and enhance one other, rather than overwhelm or muddle each bite. The 8 oz brisket and short rib patty is delicious, with great depth of flavor and really, really juicy throughout. Â The single slice of American cheese and solitary piece of apple wood smoked bacon doesn't make you feel like more fat is being added, but rather additional subtle nuances of flavor and texture. Â I'm also impressed with the bun, which does a fantastic job of reining in the abundance of juices so you don't miss a single drop. Â Plus, they are the perfect texture and size, and does not distract from everything else that is going on between the buns. I'm also a big fan of their fries. Â Seasoned nicely with curry, cayenne and parsley, it has a nice bite to the NON-MCDONALD-ESQUE fries that were crisp and fresh. More, please! How would I compare to other burgers in the city? As much as I love Shake Shack's patties and potato rolls, 8 oz of goodness will overshadow 4 oz of goodness any day. Â Stand and Burger Joint have good burgers, but they can't compare in depth of flavor and just the number of "taste buds that light up" with each bite. Â 5 Napkin can lay claim to burgers of comparable sumptuousness, but seem to require quite a bit more grease and oil to get there, Â and admittedly, sometimes I do leave with a heavy, sodden feeling and a sudden desire to run 10 miles after eating there. Â Gus & Gabriel's also have big, lush burgers that I really like, but I just keep getting the one with a fried egg so I don't think I can really compare (fried egg makes EVERYTHING better!). Nick's and Pier 1 Cafe have hardy, juicy burgers that hit the spot, but just lack similar finesse in composition. Â  Best in the world? Who knows. Â Best you'll ever have? Â Try to beat the crowds (VERY small restaurant!) and find out for yourself!

OMG. Expensive? Yes, I would say that ~$15 for a burger is expensive. Â Was it worth it? YES OMG YES. I got here around 6:10pm on a Friday night and there was a slight wait, but really not too long of a wait. Â My bf ordered the truffle burger (OMG LOVED IT SO MUCH IT WAS SO RICH AND JUICY) and I ordered the regular burger, which was also good, but I preferred his truffle burger. Â We also ordered the teeny tiny french fries, which they were meh. I don't like teeny tiny fries, you can't pick up any sauce with them! I did enjoy the random spoonfuls of garlic aioli, etc so that was great. Â Would I come back? HELL TO THE YES.
I had the Trofie Nero and it was very good. Delicious pastas and excellent service.

The good: - the portions are big enough to take the leftovers home and eat them for lunch the next day - the food is gooooooooood. i mean, i didn't go to heaven every time i took a bite, but it's better than a lot of thai food i've had - it's cheap. 8 bucks an entree? yes please. The bad: - the service. other people have mentioned it, and i don't think it's awful, but it's not really good. we mostly got ignored, but we got our food/drinks/check in a timely manner The it-depends-on-your-taste: - it's a bit loud... many tables in a small space, bad acoustics. this happens to be a pet peeve of mine, but most people don't care. - atmosphere: the place feels like it's trying to be hip... and it apparently thinks that poor lighting is really hip. but again, it wasn't that bad, and a lot of people like that kind of thing. Bottom line: it's cheap, it's plentiful, it's delicious, and if you can deal with a quiet waiter it's definitely worth it.

My go-to dinner place. I've gone here countless of times for both dinner & brunch. Â I love it!! Dinner: portions are perfect. Â I feel like NYC has this problem either dinner plates are teeny tiny, and you have to eat a cheeseburger after you leave (i.e. stanton social) or plates are soo big you need someone to roll you out on a stretcher (i.e. acme bar & grille) but not this place. Â Perfect sized portions, never any leftovers, never craving more. I brought my parents here, my mother (typical italian mom) never orders italian food anywhere we go, and if she does she only complains during the meal "you know, i can make this better!" but this was the first time she actually enjoyed her meal. Â I also convinced her to try the mussels (which she refused to try for 56 years of life) Â and SHE LOVED THEM! Â Fact is, if I can make my mother a believer, that should be more than enough proof that this place is a gem. Definitely underrated, and a part of me loves it more because there isn't some long line standing in the way of me and pure bliss. OH and brunch is a deal $12-- coffee, alcoholic bev, and entree try the eggs benedict- the cured meat and their french bread... Magnifique! Â Also their apple pancakes! Â WOW! a lb of fruit toppled on these beautiful fluffy pancakes.

My friend, who I shall refer to as SCJ (aka "I. Die."/that girl) [I am told that going by three initials is the epitome of bourgeois/state prison noise band] and I worked together in Copenhagen at a job so easy that we spent most of our time planning where to have brunch (no, really). Woefully, we are both now living back Stateside but have (for some reason) chosen to maintain our assiduous effort in finding the perfect brunch spot. This is complicated further by the fact that SCJ (for some reason) doesn't live in New York, so when her chopper does land here, we must make the most of our rare and coveted brunch opportunities. We went back and forth all week (from iPhone to Blackberry, I'm sure) about where to brunch. The criteria were stringent and our gratuitously snobby outlook made the decision-making even more difficult. It should provide outdoor seating so that we could people watch and "be seen" (we are after all, self-diagnosed celebrities), basic but well-prepared brunch fare and, most importantly, not be dim sum. The time had finally come and as we sat awake the night before discussing the origin of "Huevos Rancheros" and speculating on their unexplained popularity/origin as a "Hispanic breakfast food," I recalled Extra Virgin. At last, we could sleep with ease (and the help of much gin) in looking forward to our brunch visit the following morning. We diligently arrived at 11:00am as they opened for brunch. The paparazzi fortunately did not see us as we were the first customers to arrive like those awkward first guests at a party unsure of where to stand and what to say. We were promptly seated at Extra Virgin's outdoor seating deck (facing West 4th Street) which is a step above the sidewalk making it even more stage-like than a couple of faux celebrities like ourselves could have asked for. Within minutes, all of the outdoor seats had been filled and people began to sit inside as well. The waitress arrived promptly to take our order and it arrived about 10 minutes later (impressively fast, I say). I had the chevre and scallion omelet which was served with french fries (I would order the side salad next time since they were only OK). The omelet itself looked like it was made using approximately six eggs and large amounts of chevre - Well done. SCJ ordered the salmon eggs benedict with the side salad which she raved about almost as much as she does the added benefit of having a driver. We completed our meal with a couple of mimosas each and enjoyed this great setting as we people watched for a while and enjoyed taking in the enviable West Village scenery. The crowd continued to grow and it is apparent that Extra Virgin, with its friendly service, decent prices, large portions and excellent location made a great place to brunch . Alas, SCJ's chopper has taken her back to far-off lands, but when the chopper does return, we must come back to try that french toast everyone keeps raving about. Highly recommended.

This place is NOT a tourist trap. Â Yes, the service is a bit rough around the edges, but the food, and the soup dumplings in particular are excellent. Â The dumplings are quite simply one of the best things I've ever had. Â They are rich and delicate at the same time, they are soft and softer, which leads me desiring something crunchy. Â Despite the textural neutrality, these are just amazing little dumplings. Â Not sure if I prefer the pork or the crab versions, they are both excellent . Â  One piece of advice, do not order 2 orders at once, because they will stack the steamed containers on top of each other, and by the time you are finished with the top order, the bottom layer have had time to cool a bit and perhaps deflate. Â Order one at a time. Â Occasionally they will put a few too close together, so when you grab one, it rips and looses its wonderful broth. Â Its a real bummer, you can watch the disappointment around the table when it happens. Â Eating them is a bit complicated, but after a few orders I think i have it down, and it adds a bit of fun to the meal. Â Take a small bite, then a small sip, but leave enough broth for the big bite with the filling, perhaps add some of the pungent black vinegar/soy/ginger mixture on the table that I happen to think is fantastic, or the red peppers in oil which is great but not hot enough. Â  After that soft hot course perhaps follow up with the scallion pancakes for that needed crunch. Â Also very good, hot and crunchy but not too oily. Â Or change it up with a cold course. Â We had the Fried tofo, which was surprisingly spongy, although packed, or should i say soaked with flavor so I enjoyed it. Â The Singapore noodles were the best dish aside from the dumplings, they rival Udon for the thickest noodles I've ever had and i think they win. Â Great chewy noodles with a few nice greens, another fulling and tasty dish, although as expected a bit oily. Â  I can't give this place 5 stars, because every time I go, there seems to be some issue at the circular communal tables with strangers talking too loud about either their sex life or their inability to pay the bill not realizing Joe's Shanghai only accepts cash, welcome to chinatown. Â  I understand that sitting at these tables is the price we pay for such amazing food and its just part of the experience, unless you are the lucky enough couple to get the table for 2 by the door (you are MINE next time!), so I wont dock them too many stars for that, but it does dampen the dining experience a bit. Â If you have 7 people and can get an entire table by yourself, I suggest ordering a bunch of dishes, most importantly the soup dumplings and share it all. Â Very highly recommended, if you can stand the awkwardness of the communal table and the mediocre and sometimes rushed service. Â I look forward to returning to try the Razor Clams.

First off, let me preface this by saying my yelp grading criteria are as follows: 1 star (would never go back, unless paid to); 2 stars (one time experience is enough); 3 stars (average quality of food/ambience); 4 stars (great quality/service/ambience); 5 stars (reserved for the best). Yelp reviews have been inflated with "foodies" thinking that 4**** food consist of average presentation and "hip" places to eat. Â Herd mentality, me thinks, is at work here. Â And so I am here to say to "foodies" go take your herd mentality elsewhere. Â This review is for those wanting the review of someone who believes that instagram photos of food says more about the individual taking the picture than the actual food. Â Peasants please stop reading, others please continue. Service: Reservations were not made, but we only waited 13 minutes when arriving at 8:10 pm on a Thursday night. Â The wait is made easier by the electronic system which sends a text when your table is ready so that you can walk around EV. Â I will say though the hostess told me there would be a 40 min wait, and obviously severely overestimated the wait. Â So don't be discouraged by the initial time quoted. The waiters on the other hand were very nice, but to tell you the truth, many looked pretty casual. Â Ok you caught me they looked like west coast surfer bros, and I come from Newport/Laguna beach territory. Â So while this is normal for me, I don't want these people giving me my food suggestions. Â At the very least, you can dress up and pretend you work at a restaurant charging $30-$40 a meal. Â This is NYC not Bro lets check out those swells. (4/5) Food: Pork Buns: Â Started off with this Momofuku staple. Â I would say less impressive than Ippudo's heavenly pork buns, but a good experience overall (4/5). Â This was probably the best part of the meal unfortunately. Â The pork is tender and fatty, while the sriacha like hotsauce adds and kick to the bun. Â I love the fact the pork bun is simple with a hoison like sauce, without the mayo/heaviness accompanied with some pork buns (Totto). (3/5) Chuwanmushi: For those of you unfamiliar, this is a traditional japanese egg custard usually steamed and served in a small tea cup. Â This dish was served in a large bowl with mushrooms on top. Â David Chang the owner of the Momofuku chain, for those of your unfamiliar, is korean by ethnicity, but has lived in Japan. Â I believe if he tasted this dish, even he would agree this is not authentic or even good by any standards. Â Bland, tasteless, and quite forgettable. Â This oftentimes delicate dish was turned into a Frankenlike fusion monstrosity. Â (1/5) Quail: WTF is this shit. Â Never had quail before, but the presentation alone looked like a 7 yr olds abstract painting. Â Watermelon radish? Â Great idea, but then I would think the radish is somehow pickled in watermelon. Â Instead it just tasted/looked like it was cut up to look like miniature watermelons. Â For $20 you get one quail, prepared by neanderthals cooked over a fire. Â The meat was dry and bland. Â Take your money elsewhere. Â Honestly kinda looked like rat meat. (1/5) Spicy pork sausage with rice cakes: Â Asked the waiter if this was good, he said it was a favorite. Â Whenever I am told this by a waiter, I ask but do "you" like it. Â I trust waiters who eat the food often more than the people who dine only at a restuarant once in a while. Â Unfortunately, in this case, I was misled by both. Â This is a korean like dish. Â Kimchi style sauce dressed on top of korean rice cakes that are pan fried. Â SAUSAGES?!?!? No where to be found, more like ground pork put into the sauce. Â Extremely disappointed, but very filling. (2/5) Overall: Though I did not try to duck bo ssaam, which I regret, I do think that a great restaurant only needs 5-7 dishes that are amazing that change seasonally. Â All the dishes at Momofuku tasted like a forced fusion of Asian/modern American flavors and it fails miserably. Â For me, Momofuku has been quite disappointing to say the least, and I would think that for David Chang, having lived in Tokyo, there is some regret at not honoring the authenticity and culture behind the dishes he is trying to bring to NYC's masses. Â On the other hand, go across the street to Milk, for some Blueberries and Cream cookies (tastes like you are eating blueberry clouds).

Cute local place with great food. Burgers are really good, love the fries. fish and chips is really good. The pretzel app with cheese and mustard sauce is really yummy! nice selection of beers makes this place even better!

One of the few restaurants I keep returning to. Huge fan of their Akamaru Modern and their spicy Karaka Men ramen. It's worth the wait.... but not 3hrs of waiting. If you're a fan of thick, wavy noodles, be sure to ask. Â Their Akamaru Modern comes with thin, flat noodles, which is still good.
Great food, great wait staff, especially the Australian woman. Food was promptly, great for guys who like football too.
Food is good and great price!

A buddy of mine stumbled upon this place while waiting for our friend to finish the 2013 Marathon. Â We were looking for a nice place with a good beer selection and tasty brunch items to help us pass the time. Â This place fits the bill to a T. I had the pork belly, lamb and beef slider sampler and enjoyed every I was able to chow down on them. Â It wasn't very long, as I was hungry and they went fast. Â The beer selection is expansive with numerous items on tap and a good selection of craft and specialty beers. The prices were good for the area and there wasn't too much of a crowd. Â Most of the tables in the back had a few patrons, but the majority looked as though they were chatting and basking in the afterglow of a satisfying brunch. The bartender was a very pleasant Aussie, who was very knowledgeable about cocktails and craft beers and even let us try a new brunch cocktail she was trying to perfect. All in all, this outpost is better than its Manhattan original.

I'm on a mission to check out all of the best pizza places in the city. Â Boyfriend and I checked out Luzzo's on Sunday afternoon and we're so glad we did. We split a Bufala pie. Â The sauce was simple and delicious. Â The crust was soft and fluffy yet also crisp. Â The only thing I would've changed was a little more basil but other than that, it was a truly superb pizza. We'll definitely be going back. Â I'm already craving it!

I adore Scarpetta. Â The decor is chic and comfortable, the menu is full of delectable things and the overall experience was relaxing and blissful. Â  I expected it to be a lot more casual and more of a "scene." Instead it was a very refined place with a long bar, casual front seating area and a main dining room with a massive glass enclosed ceiling that let the light in. Â We sat in a caddy corner booth perfect for two. Â i didnt see anything interested on the cocktail menu so I went with a glass of champagne (my old standby) and my husband had red wine. Â The menu was difficult to navigate only because everything looked SO good. Â From the traditional mozzarella in corozza to the new American fish carpaccio and soft shell crab appetizer (which I had, delicious.) Â The entrees were a page full of pasta like duck and foie gras ravioli (amazing, and a very nice portion!), cavatelli with rabbit, black tagliatelle and good old fashioned spaghetti to meat entrees like steak, goat and fish. Â I can't complain about any of the food, it was all absolutely delicious. Â I went with the more exotic flavors (soft shell crab and duck and foie gras ravioli) while my husband went the more traditional route with the mozzarella and spaghetti (as usual.) Â I even had trouble deciding on the Â dessert menu so I got two (white chocolate semi freddo and chocolate and vanilla parfait) but they also had cake, fruit tarts and panna cotta. It's pricey so not a casual place but I'll definitely go back for another date night or special occasion.
A lovely gem in the neighborhood that's cozy with a great wine selection and delicious food. Great for dates or catching up with a friend.

God, I love this place. Great selection of drinks, coozies on the PBRs, a decent jukebox, cheesepuffs, and Jenga. Not to mention my poison of choice, the Texas Two Step - A bottle of Lonestar and a shot of crappy (but in a good way?) tequila for $5. Top it all off with a Frito Pie and I'm in alcohol-soaked, artery-clogged heaven. An unpretentious bar with a great back story (look up Kokie's), I usually try to steer the group I'm with to the Levee during Williamsburg drinking nights.

I never gave 5 stars but I say I need to be more generous. Food was great, wine was reasonably priced. Great, homey atmosphere... I'd definitely go back again and again. Not super fancy but if I had this first impression, I've decided this deserves 5 stars.

You know how all "Indian" food in New York starts tasting the same? How you walk into a restaurant in Curry Hill & expect something almost, but not quite, slightly better than Seamless-ordered chicken tikka-- or at least, you think so because you're sitting in a restaurant & paying a heftier tip? Yeah, no. This is *actually* better. Group of 3, came in around 8:45 and were seated without fanfare in the last available table (though people started wrapping up, such that by 10 we were one of the last tables still there). We had a hard time picking entrees but went with 3 for the whole table. The Bihari Gohst was flavorful & still moist; the meat fell straight off the pretty big bone it came on, and was enough meat for all. The Jaipuri Kofta had great flavor, and the sauce was wiped up to the very last drop, but the dumplings were a bit small and didn't hold their integrity together as well as I might have liked. Subz Tikka Masala was good to counterbalance the heaviness of the lamb, but the tomato sauce was a little too front-and-center. The variety of options & the nuance in the dishes we had was refreshing, and leaps & bounds above most Indian food I've had in New York. They were all executed pretty decently. I'm a fan, and not just because I wasn't eating it on my couch!
Really good Italian pies are served here. The service was nothing to write home about, but the pizza was very authentic and tasty. 4 stars.

The service is impeccable, Japanese style, friendly, attentive, making you feel welcome. Tiny seating area (6 ppl for bar, 26 ppl for table) yet comfortable and intimate. Definitely order one hot pot to share and a few options from appetizer menu!

Even though this place has some history (for a restaurant in NYC), it's still quite pathetic as a restaurant, since it should be about food. The menu choices are so limited that I was compelled to just leave. I ended up ordering chicken with fries, which was nothing special (both of them), and offensively overpriced ($27 for Â a small piece of chicken?!) As a side note, I found some hair in fries (tasty, huh?)

My husband and I have been here several times and its totally worth the trip into NYC and the $8 toll. The service is always excellent and the seasonal menu is always changing and always good. Â I love the shrimp and grits on the brunch menu.

1/8- Had to update my rating to 5 stars after having the garlic and artichoke dip again this last sunday. Â It was delicious and paired so well with their Barata wine. Â The service is consistently good here, definatley my favorite spot in all of queens. My favorite spot Â in Forrest Hills! They have a great selection of wine and beer, the bartenders and staff are amazing, very friendly and attentive. The salmon burgers are delicious, the location is great, it has a very homely, cozy feel to it. Â I also tried the garlic and artichoke dip that they make daily...its super tasty.

I had an enjoyable lunch here yesterday, and smiles all around :) I made my sammie order half sized which was a generous portion and great value for the quality! Â The fried chicken and kimchee is unique and perfect level of spice. Â During my time there, a stream of regulars came in, a good thing to see for being a new restaurant. Â Service was excellent too! I couldn't have asked for more, I will be back!

I've had nothing but good experiences with The Spotted Pig. Lovely place for an intimate dinner with friends. Have yet to try the much-hyped burger, but trust me, I will soon enough. I can't go here without ordering the gnudi, which are so incredibly soft and rich and delicious you could forget your own name. Expensive, but worth it.

Late night eats have never steered me wrong here. They're open till 4 am. The menu rarely goes over $10. Try the Beef Pan Fried Noodles. The beef is tender, the chinese broccoli... crisp, and of course, the noodles. Slurp.

Went there with 2 girlfriends at around 10pm, because we heard there are short lines after 10:30. Â We just couldn't wait that long, and were happy to see that the wait was about 10-15 min. Â They still had pizza in the oven (!) and service was very friendly. Â I got the famous artichoke pizza. Â It's just heavenly. Â A MUST for everybody who loves good food, even with the long lines.

This place is awesome! Â The food is cheap and delicious, and the selection of beers on tap is good and also reasonably priced. Â The garden has lots of seating room, so it doesn't feel crowded even though it looks like a lot of people are there. Â Will definitely return for more clam rolls, fries, and the delicious dogfish head!

You must visit Cafe Habana and try their GRILLED CORN (5+ stars for the corn)! Â It's a must. Before visiting I asked my friends where the best eats in NYC are. The one place everyone had on their lists was the corn here. Grilled to perfection with some type of cheese (someone said cotija cheese), chili powder and lime. We were staying in the area so I actually came back here 3 days in a row for their corn. I was obsessed. Yummm! The Cuban sandwich was packed and pretty good...but I corn steals the show! The photos don't really do it justice. Big tip is that if the main restaurant is busy just go for the take-out line next door...by the time you get your order, a seat may open up! There are a few tables and counter seats. One other day we went quite early Â and got counter spot in the restaurant side right away. Be prepared for a wait if you're coming around lunchtime it's gonna be busy!
One of my favorite restaurants in the city. Â The service is always good. Â I recommend the fried chicken and avocado and carrot salad.

Four of us had dinner on a weekday evening. Â The place was packed although you would not know it from the outside on Macdougal Street. Â We dined outside and had a variety of appetizers including the Pomodoro e Basilico and Pate con Cippolla plus three pizzas, salad and a bottle of Sangiovese. The food was excellent as was the service. Â The outside garden dining area is very small and very dark. Â Good luck if you happen to drop anything under your table or chair. Â You will never find it without a flashlight. Â Service was prompt and pretty regular considering the number of people in the restaurant.

Cool new addition to Bay Ridge! Love the outside seating area with heat lamps, hung out there comfortably Mid-November. Good beer selections, very friendly service, good pub food (although the garlic pesto fries had me choked up in tears) and not terribly pricy.

We've enjoyed two dinners here recently. The service from reception to farewell was excellent, highly professional w. a certain warmth. The room itself is one of my very favorite in NYC. However, David Bouley needs to return to creating cuisine. His menu is somewhat tired and for a one star Michelin & Â he is out pricing himself w. the $175 tasting menu. Desserts need to be changed...Also there is no bar to relax at pre dinner.

I'm sure that this place gets plenty hoppin at night once the lights get dark Â but we were looking for a place to enjoy a nice cocktail on the early side before dinner and Employees Only was the perfect place. Got there right as it opened - had the place to ourselves for a little while - and it was just what we wanted. I suffered from a lack of imagination and got a custom drink that while thoroughly enjoyed - wasn't my favorite custom drink I've had at a speakeasy by far. It was what I like to call a 'spa-drink' - cucumber, vodka (so shoot me because I don't LOVE gin), lemon, some fizzy water and simple syrup maybe? I mean... that's not QUITE what you go to a speakeasy for but my boyfriend's dad was just downing his old-fashioned which he said was "muddled to perfection". THAT's what you go to a speakeasy for.

Loved this place. Â Very good and very cheap korean and japanese bbq for manhattan. Â Went with a group, and we all got a different lunch meal (times square set, broadway set, manager's special, hell's kitchen set) and grilled it up in the middle of our table (standard for bbq restuarants). Â We all love our meats! Would love to go back for happy hour and bring more of our friends!
Favorite brunch place of all times. I take my friend here and no one ever disappoints except the fact that you have to wait so long.... fluffy pancake is just the best. You will get addicted to it!

Authentic! My Father is as Greek as they come. This place mirrors his ingredients and yummy flavor combinations. When I eat the Greek Salad (Cucumber, Feta, Onion, Tomato, Olive Oil, Oregeno, Etc) I am transported to my backyard as a kid - eating summer dinner with the family. It is very tiny & Cash Only. I find it easy to go here right after work to get a table w/ friends. You will not be dissapointed. I would go as far to say best Greek food in Manhattan.

A 3 buck meal- ten dumplings and a container of hot and sour soup. Â Outside of New York this would be a bargain and in New York, it's a steal. Â Some may hate on the hole-in-the-wall nature of this place, but I'd like to note a few benefits to the cramped location- you get a front-row view of the workers making the dumplings as you order and you can meet some of the other Prosperity Dumpling patrons- and Prosperity certainly draws a diverse crowd. The sesame pancake here is the thick, bread-like kind rather than the thin tortilla-like variety I'm more partial to. Â If you like bargains and dumplings, this is a can't-miss in New York.
Very trendy the energy is good, food was fresh, not too heave and very tasty. Service was great. I would recommend everyone to visit this location.

Very Nice Diner feeling and Staff!!!! Chicken is pretty good but unfortunately not better then (Peaches Hot house chicken) but definitely 2ND best... Only 2 downfalls...Mac/Cheese was too soupy for me and the coleslaw taste like KFC, other then that everything else was good. dessert Are GREAT!!!!! S'mores Pie is Delish!

The food and culture were great... but I don't think I really understand the hype. For some reason I was picturing the menu to have 25 different types of soup dumplings... and all different kinda of weird dishes. The menu is pretty much like most other chinese restaurants, and there are only two different choices of soup dumplings: Pork and Crab. We ordered crispy duck, pork noodles, and both dim sum options. The pork dumplings were really good; neither of us cared for the crab. The duck was good, as were the pork noodles. I was excited to come here, and no I'm not disappointed, but I wish they had more options for the dim sum... be creative!
One of the best small restaurant in New York. Elmhurst, queens" The lemongrass chicken it's so freaking good. Good job guys! Â I'LL BE BACK!!

Is it authentic? ...NO Â  Is it organic and/or family owned heritage breed animals, smoked to succulent perfection using utterly mouthwatering dry rubs ? you better bet your ass Pork Shoulder, Ribs, Brisket, Pastrami (if you're lucky enough to catch them on a pastrami day) and Pork Belly are all on some next-level-shit. Â Each bite melts in your mouth.....intoxicating you like some sort of animal flesh derived crack rock. Â  Ordering by the pound means you can try a little bit of everything. Â KEY for an indecisive person like myself, faced with the TUFFEST lineup of meats I've ever seen in my life. Â  All of the sides are great, but listen carefully now.....if you go to Fette Sau and do not order the baked beans - you've seriously got some life-evaluation to do. Â They cook the baked beans with huge pieces of burnt ends. Â These baked beans are seriously GANGSTER. Â Most batches include huge chunks of SEVERAL meats. Â I could go and make a meal out of just the baked beans alone. Â  -Mini Martins potato rolls to make little sandwiches with. -Dozens upon Dozens of different Whiskeys. Â  -5 different BBQ sauces on the table to compliment your food. -Incredibly cool atmosphere including diagrams of the different cuts of meats on the walls and a yuletide log burning on a giant flatscreen tv. -they usually have old cowboy music playing. The only downside is that you will wait a while for a table most nights of the week......but you can always bring it home! Â Enjoy!
good food for a great price - brunch special with cocktail for $15. food was pretty great, as was ambiance

We went to buy sunglasses on Time Square and asked the Caribbean expat salesman to help us find a non-touristy, New Yorker's secret, lunch spot. Â He not only told us about Margon, but walked us there because he needed a break. Â He was right. Â This place is outstanding! It's a whole-in-the-wall (I know I wrote "whole", because it is the whole package). Â  Â First off, it's Cuban fare. Â All of the workers speak Spanish, though most speak English too. Â It has a small bar, several tables, and a few booths, but is one of these narrow little alley-like places where you line up, order, pay at the till and sit if there's room. Â Everyone was very friendly, and pretty good looking to boot. Â I bantered in Spanish with the crew and jested about finding rich men on Wall Street. Â Turns out some of the ladies here wouldn't mind being whisked away by a broker if there are any banker types looking for love. Â  Â  My daughter asked the young man at the counter to give her his favorite thing. Â It turned out to be a heaping plate of yellow rice, black beans, and pepper steak. Â I ordered the Cuban. Â Within 5 minutes my Cuban was ready and brought to my table. Â I almost fell out of my chair when I tasted this bad-ass sandwich! Â It is seriously the best Cuban I've ever had (hey people, I'm talking about sandwiches here). Â I was content to suck down my Cuban but had to try a taste of the pepper steak too. Â It was delicious! Â Then, the enchanting Margon food wizards gave us a couple free pieces of chicken. Â I died and went to food heaven. Â I can only begin to express how good this place is. Â If you need any more proof, know that I waddled out of the restaurant from being so stuffed.

I am deducting stars mainly for the service. I had a bad feeling from the moment we sat down that something was off. We checked out the menu and we quickly decided what we wanted. And then we waited....and waited....and waited. Finally I waved down what I thought to be our server. The woman came over and asked if we needed something, I said we wanted to order which seemed to surprise her. She said she wasn't our server but she would take our order. My husband's soup came out fast (faster than our drinks actually). And then the waiting began again. Our food took forever! When it finally came out it was delicious but we were frustrated. After we finished our meal we waited again. We were headed to the 92Y Tribeca and had to leave BEFORE PIE! That was the whole point of coming here! The whole time we were there I don't think we ever saw the same waitstaff twice so I couldn't tell you if our server ever actually spoke to us. Needless to say his tip sucked and that's a shame because I am a really good tipper.
Good stuff, I always ask for extra pate.

This is a great place to come on a date with a food/meat loving dude. Their portions are large, the ambiance casual but also funky, and the servers are all very friendly. I would absolutely recommend a few things: - The butcher bar salad with BBQ chicken. I know, it seems lame to order a salad at a place known for it's meat, but seriously, it's one of the best salads I have ever had. Greens, blue cheese, walnuts, cranberries AND meat. You don't even need dressing, it's that good. Plus, it's huge. - ALL the sides! We ordered the baked beans, mac n cheese and the corncakes with honey butter and I would order all of them again, The beans had so much flavor (bacon, so good), the mac and cheese was not too soggy or too fake-cheesy and the corncakes were the perfect blend of salty-sweet. - The burger: part brisket, part beef, all quality. So juicy and tender without being overwhelming. Plus, in the 1 1/2 hour we were there, we heard 4 different covers of Seven Nation Army. That is not a complaint. That song rocks and so does this place.

My wife, Judy, & I went for a romantic meal to remind us we could be a couple from time to time (we have a 4 year old son). The night was rainy but landing at La Sirene was a fine way to stay dry for a couple hours & enjoy an excellent meal. My wife ordered the duck liver salad appetizer which was easily enough for an entree...FOR ME! I ordered the roasted trio of cheese (brie,blue, goat) salad with garlic crouton. The salads were both truly excellent with fresh greens & light dressings. I had the steamed mussels with curry, diced apples and light cream (Moules Rochelaises) as an entree. My wife ordered the sea bass special that evening served with pureed carrots, sauteed zucchinni & potatoe salad in 3 small baking dishes. The mussels were small but the serving abundant...and I still could have eaten more! The broth was terrific with the fresh French bread. Judy's bass was cooked perfectly & had a nice flavor with a hint of garlic (I prefer shallots with fish but no objection here with this dish.) Judy couldn't resist the chocolate lava cake with coconut ice cream & I had the French stlye zabaliogne with mangoes, blackberries & rasberries. I believe I won that contest. I did taste the coconut ice cream though & it was very nice. I look forward to my next visit ...which will be soon! My only objection would be that the space is not particularly conducive to quiet conversation, but that could have been due to the noisy party of 6 next to us that seemed to be talking over one another. NOTE: IT IS A BYOB RESTAURANT SO DON'T FORGET TO BYOB!

We all loved it! The service was excellent, and the food was delicious. My braised octopus appetizer was one of the best things I ever ate! The pasta was perfect. My only complaints were the over-priced cocktails and the volume of the noise - the background music made conversation difficult.

I've eaten the pasta I devoured a gelato, or two, or three. I've had the pizza, And drank the wine and noshed on the cheese plates, I even browsed the book section and shopped for groceries. Â  I've done most of the things you can do at Eataly, aside from the beer garden and the fancy schmancy dining areas (the fish!), and it's been enjoyable every time. Â I love browsing through the grocery sections, marveling at the imported milk and cheeses and hand made pastas and salted meats and wanting to buy everything. Â There's plenty to see and plenty to do, what a great a place to be.

3.5 stars, but that's temporary. I'd have to try it one more time because the review below is somewhat mixed. Saturday dinner at 8;30. We had a reservation, but didn't need one. There were a bunch of tables full, but still plenty empty. Pad Krapraw (Basil) - thai chili, string beans, onion, bell pepper, and basil leaves Pad Kratiam (Garlic) - minced garlic, onion, scallions, and assorted vegetables. Cons: - inconsistent quality: the basil stir-fry had no flavor and definitely not a basil flavor, but the garlic stir-fry was delicious - Asked for light oil/sauce - definitely did not listen - Asked for extra spicy - was definitely not spicy enough and this is usually not a problem at other thai restaurants when you emphasize it as much as I do. Not sure why they didn't want to make it spicy enough - when you get assorted veggies in your stir-fry, they are not finely chopped. there were entire chunks (think 3 inches) of carrots and zucchini in there. this is not normal for thai stir-fries. it's usually very thin and much easier to eat. chunky veggies belong in curries, not in stir-frys. - two dollars extra for each additional side of white rice and trust me you need more rice because their portions are so small. we got 2 extra servings of tiny rice bowls, so we paid four more dollars Pros: - beautiful, spacious ambiance - nicely decorated, dimly lit - they bring 4 different spicy sauces to the table to complement the dish - a vinegar, a sour hot sauce, sriracha, and chili flakes - servers are attentive and pleasant - some of their dishes are hits (see first one under cons)

Cafe Himalaya has long been sitting in my bookmarks, one of its elders if you will. We had not sought it out when we came across the opportunity to dine there and took advantage of a day that beckoned the coming of Spring. CH is a very unassuming place. Its wooden seats and benches are utterly devoid of any comfort Â and the cafe itself, save for a few posters mostly of stupas in the Kathmandu Valley, is largely missing any embellishment or deliberate flourishes inviting the diner to fully enjoy the experience. I had hoped that these two cosmetic and functional issues would be offset by the best Himalayan food the City has to offer. I had certainly hoped so after refreshing my memory by going through many yelp reviews. Their menu, as well as their suggestion board, offered many vegetarian options. My husband loves momos and so do I. So we settled on the 8 piece Shogok Momo Takpa pan fried dumplings stuffed with potato & herb served with dry cabbage salad. They were AOK. I have had better, in Queens, and worse, on the trail in Nepal which gave my GI tract quite the workout! ;))) CH's were a very happy medium. #15, Thukpa, a traditional Tibetan noodle soup topped with sauteed fresh green vegetables, was my choice. It looked nice and was hot when presented but it was very bland and the noodles' texture was odd. I do not think they were made in house but I cannot place them either. Kind of rough and yellowy. I did enjoy the thick slices of tofu and the greens which were not overly cooked and still retained their beautiful green color and flavor. The broth though could have had more depth and it was a little oily but not in a good (spicy oil) way. I only ate half and I love me a bowl of vegetarian Asian soup! After seeing after the fact all the positivity for the Chili Dofu I think I may have ordered wrongly and should have tried that. Perhaps next time. :))) The L. ordered the Tsel Phing bean thread noodles sauteed with cabbage, carrot, peas & spinach served with paratha bread which was #20. I did not try it but he managed to finish all of his. My beverage was just a plain iced tea unsweetened. I had noticed butter tea on the menu but was not in the mood though their Thai Iced Teas and Smoothies seemed like an ideal refreshment for the warm day. The L. had a mango lassi which we could see the gentleman making behind the counter at the front of their open kitchen where the chefs were busily preparing our dishes and those of the other diners which grew in number as we ate. It was a gorgeous day and everyone was in good spirits. I even thought I had a Paul H sighting, but alas it was not he. ;))) And the facility really is not my thing, including walking down the steep stairs to use the restie. Calling it a cafe denotes something which I do not believe they offer. There are seats, very uncomfortable, and table service but no ambiance (Justin Bieber music on the radio, scary I would know that). I do not like to be less than supportive of the Tibetans and Nepalese as I very much respect, admire and am interested in their culture but this meal sadly did not offer me any more knowledge than I already have. I am happy that so many others love Cafe Himalaya and will patronize them. We wish them all the best and namaste. youtube.com/watch?v=fSiwâ€¦

The good part about eating in Carmines is that they serve HUGE portions. One order is for 2-4 people. For reservations, all guest must be present before seated. And they are really strict with this policy. The restroom was on the 2nd floor in addition to this I wondered how does disabled and senior Â citizens get accommodated when they need to use the restroom...im not sure if they have one on ground level. In regards to our evening,we had shared the dishes between 6 adults and a kid...we ordered calamari, antipasto and Pasta seafood special... The calamari was crunchy but the sauce was in the salty side. The antipasto appetizer was a platter with a portion of mussels, Â wrapped asparagus, sauteed spinach, spagetthi,baked salmon...it was pretty decent and the salmon was my favorite. For the linguine pasta seafood special, the mussels were phenomenal and delicous...shrimps was average and the sauce itself was too much olive oil. The water glass were small probably the reason behind that was so that a customer wont get filled with water and have more appetite eating than drinking...so people can chowdown The bill was a bit pricey though...we had to split for each adult for $25 with the aforementioned 3 Â dishes. And that was with eating with a consevative appetite.

I visited NY the first time in my entire life this past weekend and my goodness, New York, you are amazing. So an acquaintance of mine (who shall not be named) and his fiancee introduced me to this magical food cart called Halal. He ordered three mixed plates. The 20 minute line was definitely worth it. He suggested the oh so amazing white sauce. As a fan of hot, I wanted to try it, but I was warned that it was super spicy. The meat in this plate were super delicious and juicy, and the white sauce just adds so much more flavor! (My gosh this sounds oddly wrong...) Anyways, I highly recommend this, but remember, don't add TOO much white sauce(:

Food was excellent - pork belly was perfect. The rolls are delicious - ask for extra! They were more than happy to accommodate a couple of minor dietary requests for the table. The waitress had a great wine knowledge. The service was great overall but they did seem a little too hasty in asking if we were done w dishes/drinks so I felt like they interrupted a tad too often. Dessert was impeccable - Stumptown coffee ice cream!! Was excited to see Stumptown coffee in NYC. Parting favor was a house made zucchini muffin for each of us - adorable and unexpected. It's pricey but I'd go again for a special occasion.

i love you minca!!! best ramen in the city (i'm not counting ippudo because who the hell actually has time to wait 2 hours for ramen-- i love it but it's impractical). Â i don't understand the haters... the minca sio is sooo damn good...love the roasted garlic flava and al dente noodles. Â also most incredible gingery dumplings.

Came here just for coffee and drinks after shopping in ABC Carpet, but was blown away. The atmosphere is unbeatable. Very comfortable, high quality, and creatively executed. Oddly romantic, and loud enough that you have to lean in, but not too loud. Great wine selection, mostly organic, like the food, I am assuming. The bar area was very cozy, and the wait staff very friendly and attentive. The news of its opening a few months ago received a warm welcome, and it was highly deserving of it. Jean George made the culinary decisions, so I have to go back for dinner VERY soon.

When I first walked in there, I expected your everyday local diner. Â I was already excited that it was 24 hours and only a stones throw from my apartment, but then started to get a little skeptical when I saw things like "tuna tartar" and "portabella mushroom" I was scared that this diner was going to be trying too hard. Â I simply went w/a buffalo chicken wrap and fries to be safe. Boy did they prove me wrong. Â It was all really good, right down to the french fries, that I actually crave and miss having! Â All their food is really fresh and top line (shocking for a diner) and decent prices. Â I couldn't get enough of their panko breaded chicken fingers. Â  It's so nice to have a variety of things to choose from, that aren't just your average diner menu items. Â Great, quality food at "diner" prices! Other things to note: -they do deliver (and our pretty efficient) -bring cash, no credit cards accepted -they have an awesome brunch on the weekends for only $9.99! -there's also a bar there w/wines and beer and I can't remember if there's cocktails as well, but I've never had one
Hands down the best macarons in NYC, particularly the rose and coffee flavors, though I have had better in Paris. Be careful of eating too much though or you'll get sick!

Went to Balthazar for the first time recently for Sunday brunch. It was packed, I got shoved around a few times because it was so crowded inside. The bright side is the food was absolutely amazing, I had the eggs benedict and I also tried a few other dishes my friends had gotten, all great! The reason for the 4 stars is the service, it was extremely poor. My waitress was awful, she was rude, and pushy. My friend asked for toast on the side and she almost bit his head off saying we don't serve toast on the side. Nevertheless I can judge too poorly on Balthazar for one waitress. I shall return again soon.
Came here again with a different friend and we ordered the mac attack again. Â Why not give it a 2nd chance? Â Glad we did because it was much better than the first time. Â Now I get it!

I want to give this place 2.5 stars but will be generous and round it UP to 3. Â I was excited to finally make it to Corner bistro but honestly it was just "ok". Â NOthing really special. Â My bf and I both had the bistro burger and an order of fries. The burgers were tasty especially due to the bacons but it wasn't anything out of this world or different. Â The fries were disappointing. Â McDonald's fries are better. Â enough said. Â Kinda underwhelming experience overall.

Came here in the summer during cherry blossom time to visit Brooklyn Botanical Garden and the Brooklyn Museum as it's just a block away and since we biked here we were all starving for some good eats to re-energize us up. Definitely go for the Jerk chicken which was full of flavor and jerk spices. The pigeon peas and rice were also full of flavor and was the right accompaniment with the chicken. Â Nice sides of veggies and a salad as well. Huge portions and a great lemonade to accompany the lunch. The restaurant is no frills with the kitchen on the bottom and a small cramped sitting area on a steep staircase upstairs that didn't have A/C in the middle of summer but the place is great for takeout and sitting in the park to eat.

WOW. Â As a neighbor of Kiwiana, I'm excited to have acquired an uber-local restaurant that joins the ranks of Rosewater and Palo Santo. We stopped in for dinner on opening night, but (impressively) the only hint of prematurity was the lack of libations, which we purchased from around the corner upon sitting down (they held the table - bonus points!). The manuka (an herb) and Marmite-braised baby-back ribs are aMAzing. They arrive falling off the bone, bursting with flavor, and deliciously accompanied by a sweet squash puree. The New Zealand snapper was absolutely delicious, but admittedly only won its praise after we'd licked the ribs' plate clean. Â The tomato and chili sauce is delicately complex, the braised fennel subtly brined, the snapper skin lightly crisped, and everything perfectly seasoned. Fear not, drinkers, I think Kiwiana fully opens with a selection of wine and beers in just a few days. Â  We'll definitely be going back soon. Â For sure. Â YUM.
Great place, great staff, what's wrong with the crowd. .. I guess there's nothing you can do about that anymore in Manhattan.
Need my cheese fix

Solid dumplings. The chives pancake was a bit too greasy for my taste, but the dumplings more than made up for it. I also love the fact that there are a total of four seats in the place. Â They mean business, so get your dumplings, shut up and eat. Â Don't worry, once you start eating these dumplings you'll forget about whatever you were talking about.

I hate to use such a trite expression, but it fits here: this place is a gem! In college, I studied abroad in Spain for a quarter and lived off of eggs. You see, Spanish food doesn't really have many veggie options- so my confused host mother would feed me eggs with every meal for protein. Eggs in my lentil soup, eggs in my salad, eggs in my pasta, eggs in my sandwiches- you name it, she egg'd it. I couldn't eat them for a year after that. 4 years later, I found myself reading reviews for Despana on Yelp. And I started craving tortilla espanol. I dashed here after work and satisfied my craving with a tortilla bocadillo. And man it hit the spot. The bread was so good, the tortilla was just as I remembered it. There's another vegetarian bocadillo with grilled veggies that I have to try. I also had the blueberry cheesecake and it was AMAZING. I've never had anything like it. I'm normally not a huge cheesecake fan, but this cake is not your typical fluffy cake- it's more dense and is made with a different type of cheese. I don't even know how to describe it, but try it. Note: there isn't much seating here- a few stools and a table in a corner of the store. The rest of the place is a specialty goods store with all kinds of Spanish imports, such as membrillo (quince) jam and Valor chocolate.

We went there for breakfast today. We loved it!!! Â It was clean, food was delicious and atmosphere was comfortable. Â We did not have any small kids with us but there was a large presence of kids but you did not hear them at all. There was a small Â playroom that kept the kids contained while the parents enjoyed their meal. I will definately return for lunch or dinner. Â I was very surprised to see how much I enjoyed this place as I normally like my usual places and this is far out of my way but wanted to try it.

The food is absolutely amazon here. As a not so picky eater, I have to say that I wouldn't like to have breakfast at any other place after trying out their red pepper quiche and scrambled eggs on puff pastry. Orange juice/champagne ratio in mimosas was not satisfying; however they made it up to me with their delicious food.

By all appearances, "sparse and unappetizing," would be a polite way to describe Le Grainne's bread basket. Pale and Keebler Elf sized, their slices look severely under baked and texture-less - - you know, the kind that remains uneaten on airline and hospital trays. But who were we to pass up free carbs and the cheap serotonin high? Twelve minutes later... What in the name of Paula Deen possessed us (butter) to eat two FULL baskets of bread (butter) in record time? Special yeast? (butter) Imported water from France? (beurre) Secret recipe? (butt-uh!) Perhaps it was the butter...? (crack butter) Slathering 2 inches (gold butter) like it was Nutella is not normal. (embalm me in this!) My food was equally awesome. I ordered the dinner omelette ($10) filled with turkey, ratatouille, and mushrooms. Don't hold me to this but I have consumed 4,231 omelettes in my lifetime, so trust me when I say this tasted delicious and homemade. Not surprisingly, this too was bathed in butter. My dining companion opted for their ($18) tilapia "en papillote" (in parchment) with mashed potatoes and asparagus spears. (Note to self: To score a taste, the creepy prolonged stare is just as effective as puppy dog eyes. Who knew!) By end, we were too full to even read the dessert menu thanks to their evil, will make you fat bread & butter. Why do we do this to ourselves? Note: Service is comical. e.g. 1) waiting waiting waiting...2) floating chunk of cork in glass of white wine 3) when we were ready to pay, the waiter tried to take our appetizer order But seriously, this was the richest butter I've ever had from an inexpensive, casual sit-down restaurant. While normally a jam packed brunch spot, it's worthwhile to check out for dinner. Butter!

Saigon Shack is one of my all-time favorite places in the Village, and I regularly take friends here. It is cash only, which can be annoying, but the food is excellent and the service is quick (if a bit inattentive at times). It is important to avoid the lunch rush, as with most places around the NYU campus. The place gets slammed around 1200 and clears up around 200. I don't know how bad it is at dinner, though I'd imagine it gets pretty crazy during the school year. Everything on the menu is solid, though I'm particularly fond of the pho, because it is the best I've been able to find anywhere in the City.

Tried to get lunch here Saturday noonish. LOTS of people waiting out front. We stick our heads in the door and we're told 25 minutes. We usually prefer to sit and eat at the bar anyway, but we're told they don't serve food at the bar. Odd. We pass for lunch but plan to return. Smaller crowd around dinner time so we stop in again. This time I tell them I write for Yelp! and I'm told they have a table ready for us. For real.. they walk us back, and back... thru the kitchen, around the corner and to our table. Our waiter. Honestly, I think he was a good waiter. I think he was a good waiter who was in over his head. We got very little attention from him. He seemed to be behind the 8 ball even with his other tables. That being said we got what we ordered in a timely fashion and if you want to put a spin on it... with very little server interruptions. Pizza... not my taste. It was good. But not the type of pizza I like. Maybe as a tourist I've gotten used to mass produced food and can't enjoy the fresh home made stuff? The GF loved hers, and she is a fan of more traditional flat crust pizza. I will say the half that had mushrooms got soggy really quick.

Have never met such a friendly staff. Priscilla was one of the nicest and most attentive bartenders I have ever encountered. If I owned a bar I would totally steal her. Food was also very good, and the ambiance was cool. definitely would go again.

My friend and I were sobering up so at around 4:30am on a Monday we headed here. It was surprisingly crowded at that hour. We were made to wait outside for a little while. Many people inside were dressed in a very try-hard manner. I had a cobb salad. It was ok. They took forever to bring the check. I would not go here unless it was late at night and I really wanted a sit down restaurant experience. ps. We saw Amanda Lepore at the bar

How quaint. How cute. How adorable. And how tasty. The wait is LONG, but when we were walked in, there were so many open tables in the back. And not that many people left before we came in. Odd. The french toast, french onion soup, and croque madame were amazing. My favorite was the french toast with the caramelized sugar. It gave the french toast a nice crunch and, with the confectioner sugar, it is enough sweetness without the need for maple syrup. I could have done for more fruit though. Like 3x more fruit. The egg on the croque madame was perfect with just a little bit of runniness to provide for a clean meal. The french fries were amazing! They're so skinny, I devoured them all without feeling weighed down by the carbs. I'm feeling it now though... I must return for the pancakes. We were told that they had run out of pans so any order of pancakes would have taken at least an hour. We noticed it was more like 30 minutes as the couple beside us decided to take the plunge. Gosh darn it, if only we had! Oh well, another time.

beef bulgogi banh mi $5.00 +tax Checked in for the free egg, well done. Ordered and saved for lunch the next day. Â After being in a super cold fridge, I took a bite and sandwich was still tasting good. Then decided to heat it backup, tasted fresh like it was made the same day. Â Microwave for about 40 seconds or so. Any longer, it would probably dry out the bread. Location can be hard to find at night if you dont look closely at the signs, street gets pretty dark and the street lights dont help much.

It was a Wednesday night, 7:10 pm. I arrive at Freeman's and put my name in, "Table for 2 please." They tell me, "About 30min." Ok, fine. My boyfriend arrives at 7:35, I let them know he's here and they tell me, a few more minutes. We are sat at 8:30. And, fyi, they only take reservations for parties of 6 or more. This is definately a scene, which is annoying to me. A couple groups walked in before us because they "knew someone", including a group of 5 girls who were laughing at their friend, yelling something about how she knows everyone and has all these connections, making it clear that they were seated so quickly because of her. The drinks were great, $12 each, but great. The waitress was wonderful. The food, mediocre. I got the filet mignon and started with the heirloom tomatoes, my boyfriend got the fried chicken and we split a side of mac 'n cheese. The chicken was so fatty that he had to pull off the skin and only eat the meat (why else order fried chicken if you can't eat the skin?!). The mac 'n cheese was good. My filet was ok, the creamy horseradish sauce that it was served with was good. I was dissappointed. It was so loud inside. Again, a Wednesday night! I do like the european feel as we walked down the alley toward the restuarant, but that is the biggest draw for me. I much preferred National (right around the corner on Rivington).

What a great experience! I won't repeat all of the wonderful compliments that several other reviewers have already stated, but I'll share a few tips for you newbies who need an orientation to this place. The guys behind the bar are incredibly helpful, laid back, and really hospitable. They gave us all kinds of advice on what to order. Yes, the place is loud, but we were too distracted by the good food, so the noise didn't bother us. Meatballs come in a few varieties: beef, spicy pork, chicken and veggie. You can pair them with an array of sauces (tomato, spicy tomato, mushroom, parmesan, etc). You can order meatballs in a sandwich form, or you can order them as "naked balls" which is a set of 4 identical meatballs (you can't mix and match the meat varieties) that you can pair with sauces and a starch (like pasta, risotto, mashed potatoes, chickpeas). We had no reference point, so we started out with sliders so we could try a variety of the meatballs. I loved the sliders. We decided we loved the spicy pork meatballs the most (really tender and flavorful), and then we proceeded to order the naked spicy pork balls with spicy meat sauce. It was the ultimate comfort food, love at first bite. The prices are reasonable, as a matter of fact, the meatball orders will cost less than a glass of wine there. Save room for dessert! The ice cream sandwiches are divine. You can choose the type of cookie and pair it with their different choices of ice cream.
I love this place. Very comfy and homey. The crepes are fantastic. I felt really relaxed here.

I've been here a few times, and most of those times required a 45minute to 1:30hour wait. I went here on July 4 for brunch, knowing that I'd be waiting quite a while for a table for two. I saw a couple walk out of the restaurant warning us that the wait was too long. Another couple in front of us asking for a table for two decided they didn't want to wait either after they were told hold long it'd take to get a seat. So then it was our turn to ask for a table for two, and they responded 'The wait is a little long right now at 25 minutes.' TWENTY FIVE MINUTES?! THAT'S NOTHING!!!! Wow.. the people who opted to leave either are not from New York or they're just darn impatient. Don't they know that walking to another less-than-spectacular restaurant and getting a table there will probably take at least 25 minutes? After four minutes of waiting, another couple walks in and asks for a table for two. They are told it will be a 10 minute wait, but they are also impatient and leave. Thirty seconds later, we get our table. A total wait of four and a half minutes. As we sit down, the table next to us is cleared and could have sat the impatient couple immediately. A shame for them. They could have had the most amazing brunch of their life.

I added a star for the nice server. On to the food... I had the worst grilled cheese ever! Â To add insult to injury the gross thing was $15!! Â The sandwich came open style on a huge piece of bread. The cheese hardened quickly to the point my fork and knife struggled to break me off a piece. I asked for pickles, which I love, and they even sucked. Had a weird after taste. Â Anyway, I won't visit here again.

Locavore meet Manhattan. Three of us dined at ABC recently. The food was delicious...fresh, pure and assembled with a deft hand. It is a perfect spot if you like fresh ingredients served in a way to showcase their pure flavors. Bold tastes....no! Intricate constructions...no! 14 ingredients per dish...no! Fresh ingredients...sort of! Sparkling fresh ingredients that seemed like they just were pick off the vine...YES!!!! For those of us that like food the way mother nature meant it to be but improved by a gentle hand of man, ABC is perfect. The space is a bit raucous, but comfortable. You can talk if at tones a bit above normal. The wait staff was professional, helpful and unobtrusive. I will go back, maybe tonight....
Lamb Massaman. Fuck yeah. Best I've ever had.
The noodle there is a little bit thick than ippudo, and the line is longer. I love the spicy one.

Had the blueberry pancakes, salmon eggs benedict, rosemary sausages, smoked bacon & bellini's. The blueberry pancakes were amazing itself but add the warm maple syrup and it tastes even better! The salmon benedict was yummy as well.. the biscuit was light and the hollandaise sauce was delicious! As for the service.. took a bit longer for the waiter to bring us our water and we had to flag down the waitress to take our order. I guess thats expected when this place is packed and so busy all the time?

The moment I walked into this place I knew I was going to love it. Decorated like a Japanese courtyard yet with jazz piano filtering across the open space, the atmosphere is very welcoming and relaxing. Came for lunch on a weekend and there was no wait, though the place did get more crowded as I finished my meal. I don't know whether this is only for lunch or for dinner as well, but there was a miniature buffet of boiled eggs and pickled vegetables, which I found went splendidly with my salad (miso dressing, my favorite!). I ordered the first item on the lunch menu, the Gomoku Kamameshi, which takes 20 minutes to prepare. When it came, I was impressed by the depth of the pot. It looked really small in the picture, but it was tons of food especially for the price. I'll admit I think this dish was a little bland, but it was very satisfying and heathy. Service was extremely friendly, and I just got a sense of authenticity. I lived in Japan for a bit, and this place definitely reminded me of restaurants in Tokyo. Will absolutely be back.

After trying an authentic Liege Belgian Waffle in Amsterdam, I have been on the permanent search for restaurants that can simulate their sweet, crunchy, delicateness. After reading about Petite Abeille's waffles on Yelp, I came in for Saturday brunch, and it was definitely worth the visit. I ended up also ordering another waffle afterwards to eat for breakfast the next day (and naturally finished it within the hour). Their Croque Monsieurs are also also pretty good-- the cheese is nicely grilled on top, and the fries that come on the side are crispy and savory. Food was pretty authentic overall. I also enjoyed how the restaurant looks completely unassuming from the outside, but is nicely decorated and bustling once you step inside. There's even a little patio with lights in the back; try to sit there if you can! Petite Abeille is a cute brunch destination to come with friends or family, and I will probably be back.

Stumbled upon this place one night in NYC because a restaurant we wanted to eat at was an hour wait. Place is really nice and spacious, the decor is different but in a good way. Our waitress was really nice and patient with us because we couldn't make up our mind on what to eat. Eventually when we did figure out what we wanted for dinner, we got the shrimp scampi plate to share, a glass of moscato for me, beer for the bf and a double shot of Grey goose for the both of us (to keep warm). Prices are reasonable for the amount of food and service and the shrimp scampi was excellent! Perfect amount of sauce and shrimp to satisfy us.

I liked this place until I got my Alta salad with salmon. I usually order my salad with salmon. This piece was chewy and about four square inches. Not worth it at all. My friends liked their food. Fun place. They must have run out of salmon!

Just plain excellent! Who knew vegetarian sushi would be extraordinary! It's a work of art the way these guys make these rolls. I like meat, and I was super skeptical on trying it out, but after I got a taste. Wow! I was in my happy place. Lol. I'd go vegetarian if I could eat here every day!

Ate here Monday night and was blown away by the service, the attention, the cocktails and of course the food. Bartender prepared one of the best manhattans I've ever had. Enjoyed drinks with friends and people watched a bit. Then got into the wine and dinner. Mozzarella in carozza were perfectly cooked, baked clams were again some of the best I've had. Â Sweet and tender broccoli rabe with shells. Stuffed veal chop was fork tender and very flavorful. The meatballs. Shocking. I must have them again. Also heard great things about their seafood salad. Hope to get the table again someday soon.

All wine bottles are $25 which makes drinking here so affordable. Â The food is also good but I don't think it was a life-changing experience like some other reviews make it out to be. Â The space is really small and you will be sharing a table with others which can be a down-side since the others at the table will be listening to your conversation. Â The service though deserves 10 stars - it's not just friendly, it's WARM and KIND - definitely obvious it's a family-run joint. The food: Â hummus pizza was just ok - i got it after reading some good reviews here but I wouldn't recommend it. Â the "dough" was plain and you can't taste the hummus - the only thing you can taste is the wasabi peas on top. Â the foie gras with raspberry is worth getting - i don't even like foie gras and I liked it. Â the duck is fantastic - best dish of the night so definitely would recommend. Â the pork buns are not very good and weren't memorable - nothing compared to momofuku. Â the strawberry almond truffle dessert was tasty but again, not life-changing.

This place is as good as the reviews say! Had the vegetable dumplings for $3. They were very flavorful and really hot. We opened the box and the steam just wafted out. We also tried the scallion pancake. It was so fluffy and so good. Have had the scallion pancake at a couple of other places but this place really nails it. And its just a $!
We were in from Philadelphia and Â had a wonderful dinner! The pizza was out of this world. Great service and wine selection with a down home feel. Fresh home made food.
Eggs Benedict = delicious. Â good coffee. Â reasonably priced brunch. Wait staff had no issue with us having a 3 hour brunch

I had walked by Extra Virgin on a leisurely West Village stroll on a Sunday afternoon. The patrons eating outdoors looked pleased, and the restaurant seemed like a good fit with the quaint neighborhood around 4th and Perry. Making a mental note of its name, I decided that I would have to try it out soon after. A few weeks later I did try it out, and I was glad I did. I went for brunch at about 11:30. As a party of 2, we did not have to wait. However, I might attribute this to the dreary weather and the "early" time-an hour later the line looked never-ending. The restaurant's ambiance was great-simple, but with a touch of West Village chic. The crowd seemed down to earth-various people at the tables around me seemed like regulars, downing their coffee while reading the Sunday Times. I ordered the Virgin Fritatta-which has goat cheese, pesto, arugula, and roasted tomato. DELICIOUS! The coffee was also fresh and strong. I also recommend this place because of its prices. Brunch in the city tends to be expensive, especially in the West Village, but I paid $17 for entree, coffee, and tip. I can't wait to come back for dinner!

I came here with my boyfriend and ordered the two most popular dishes according to Yelp - the French toast and Benedict Jane. The French toast was delicious! Three hefty pieces of brioche soaked in their vanilla creme brulee batter - dear god... this was sooo good!!! But I do wish they would sell a "half order" of this because the serving was was wayyy too big! The Benedict Jane sounded perfect on paper but fell through. The crab and crawfish cakes had a seafood essence to it but lacked any large, discernible chunks of seafood. Â We also ordered a side of the rosemary fries due to some good reviews about it but they were nothing amazing. Service was ok, nothing special. Save yourself the hour plus wait for weekend brunch by making reservations. Although, we did have to wait 10 minutes for our table. Ten minutes is better than an hour! The French toast was amazing but the rest of our meal didn't live up to our expectations. 3.5 stars

Simply the best ramen in NYC! Ippudo has been disappointing for me because of the over-hype, but despite the high expectation my friend has given about this place, I simply cannot find fault about this place! The chicken paitan ramen (the original) has absolutely the best broth I've ever had; and the torched pork was wondeful, it's thick cut but tender with the perfect proportion of fat and meat, which I much prefer than the ippudo's thin-cut lean pork slices. And the off menu unidon (yes, uni as in sea urchin, not unagi) was delightful as well! Oh, and the obligatory note: yes, it's a long wait but it's worth it.

adventure. i'm always up for adventure. a small group ventured from our comfortable brooklyn existence to travel to the wilds of queens. and at the end of our journey we were rewarded with amazing delicious german food and tasty cold german beers. this place is one part VFW lodge, one part banquet hall and one part restaurant in rhienlander, wi. those are all very good things. and so are adventures. i plan on making this adventure regularly.

Had brunch there. French toast is too ricotta-y and you only get one piece. Husby liked his eggs but said everything could use more salt. Fried green tomatoes need an accompanying sauce. Service was friendly and prices are reasonable With a few tweaks, could be four stars

I dined here on February 16th with my girlfriend and had a pleasant experience. All the food was excellent and the presentation matched. A beautiful, black and white theme extends through the restaurant, graced by photographs and sharply dressed staff. Our server, Jonathan, was informed and attentive, explaining enough of each dish to shape our decision, but leaving enough out so that the food was still a surprise. Despite the busy night, he still had enough time to converse at length and made us feel welcome. I never got to experience Chef Cardoz's cuisine at Table, so I'm thrilled that the city can once again partake of his talent.

First time. Had dinner with a friend 2 nights ago. Place is cute, modern, clean design. Has a very comfortable vibe. Sinatra was singing softly in the background.
