Bread and flavored olive oil and menus came quickly. We each had a specialty drink. My was vodka. Nice flavor and perfect strength. Cold night. I had the mushroom soup***** stars! Wanted to lick the bowl. My friend enjoyed her salmon tarter. Next I had the roasted chicken. Perfect juicy and seasoned beautifully. It was served with garlic mash and veggies. Mussels with fennel sauce was my friends choice. She raved. Was too full for dessert, but they looked great. Service throughout was warm and friendly. Like we'd been there before. Kind of place you could come by yourself. Sit at the bar and enjoy your drink and meal and enjoy the people. Welcome to the neighborhood.! Will definitely return.

I really wanted to like this place - I really did. I love empanadas, and I was even a little.... ahem... inebriated when I arrived at 11:00pm to get some delicious Latin food. However, the place disappointed after the hype that I had seen here. The empanada that I got for $3 was really small. I got a pizza empanada, and to my dismay, it barely had any filling. Half of it was just air and the other half was a bit of cheese and a spoonful of tomato sauce. The boyfriend really seemed to enjoy his though (the spicy chicken, I think). The service took entirely too long for two take-out empanadas and was brusk with us. A sit-down table managed to come and go in the time it took for us to get ours. In the end, the only redeeming factors at this restaurant are it's 24/7 availability and the fact that you can get food (of any sort) for $3 in Hell's Kitchen.
Place was awesome - they gave a date and I Mac n cheese bites and 2 shots that were unbelievable. Â Definitely going back!

Must preface this with the fact that I did not in the end even get to eat here - Just wanted to send a message - When you walk in, there is no clear access to tables, or employees - there is no take out menu to be seen, and standing in the lobby for 5 minutes with a confused look on my face Â (twice within the space of one hour no less) does not produce any help from the employees (are there any?) I think front of the house stuff like this is essential for any new business - I really wanted to eat there today - I live a block away - But it was essentially impossible , and it wasn't even crowded in there. Â here's hoping that they figure this stuff out...

This is one of those places where the service is absolute shit but the food completely makes up for it. I don't know why but the staff always seems to remind me of those scenes in a movie where everyone wakes up with a hangover and barely wants to move. You pretty much have to wave them in with red flags like you're landing an airplane if you want some service. HOWEVER, despite all that...their food is delicious. Not just delicious, but cheap and delicious. I've had quite a few things here but I usually end up getting duck noodle soup and wontons. I usually refrain from getting wontons at most "chinese" restaurants. (I put chinese in quotations because many chinese resturaunts in america are anything but chinese) but this place does know how to make them right.

I have been looking forward to going here for some time due to the Yelp reviews and it was well worth it. Â We had a 7 pm reservation for 5 and were sat immediately upon entry in a big booth with lots of rooms. Â The restaurant is very open and not crammed like so many NYC places. Â Our waiter JP was unbelievable, friendly and knowledgeable. Â The food was great. Â My one complaint was too much meat on an app and not enough corn cake, and that is hardly a complaint in most people's eyes. Â I could have dined on the delicious filling apps alone, but the steak was to die for so I am glad I did not miss out. Â Cannot wait to go back here!! Â Oh, and the sangria was the bomb and they were very pleasant about my free Yelp glass of sangria :)
positively delicious! Â The best panini I've ever head, luscious risotto, and a great cheap bottle of wine! We thoroughly enjoyed the food and the service, the location and the decoration.
Love getting food here after a night out! Love the lamb with white sauce. Super cheap and you're given a huge portion. Worth waiting in that long line!

It's really good place to chill when it's not so busy. Â I had a lovely birthday brunch here. Â The only downside was it was a bit crammed for a group of 14. Â You must order a churro and is pure decadent.

This place is much cozier than I expected. Today's weather was nice, but the four of us opted to sit inside as the sun was too much for our hangovers. We sat in a room off to the side, pleasant and just dark enough, and there were large windows open to the breeze, which felt nice. Our poor waiter. Every time he asked (terribly difficult) questions such as, "What can I get you to drink?" or, "Did you decide on food yet?" he was met with a chorus of "Huhh.. mmm?" (again, the hangovers). He was cool and friendly though, laughed at us, and waited patiently. Three of us had the huevos rancheros, which was very satisfying. In retrospect, it was a senseless thing to order at place with a Middle Eastern flair, but I guess we can't resist the Mexican grub. When we asked for hot sauce, we got ramekins full of some yummy homemade-looking hot salsa with an actual kick to it. I also liked that the dish came with a fresh side-salad with a tasty mustard-y dressing. The potatoes had excellent flavor but could have been far crispier. The fourth member of our party got a bagel & eggs, and judging by sight alone, I would say stay far away from the bagels. I didn't try it though. There are tons of options here for the vegetarians, which I like. The best thing I tasted here was the coffee. If you order a cup you will receive an incredibly hot and delicious Americano. It seems they will take FOREVER to deliver it to you, but it's worth it. By the time we left, newcomers were in for a long wait. I will be back next time I can make it early enough to miss the brunch rush. It's a perfect atmosphere to gently ease yourself back to reality after an awesome weekend night, over yummy, affordable noms and perfect coffee.

I found out something incredible the food was amazing the churrasco was incredible Delicious and paella was incompatible new York opened a great spot also the drinks blew my head off especially blame them not me come try it and you would be happy and satisfied I promise and the bartender sharmaine is so friendly and hooks up the best drinks you can imagine the service is amazing I invite new York city and the world to come and confess your sins on the black board Â  sexy beautiful self I dare you and you won't be disappointed the atmosphere is crazy the music will awake everybody with happiness and joy i will invite you come over and see for yourself

So I just threw up after eating here, because I ordered too much food and tried to finish all of it. Â I really thought the portions would be a bit smaller. Â Two orders of dumplings and hand pulled noodle soup, way too much for one person. Â I had to throw away half the soup and store four of the dumplings. Â I really tried to finish all of the dumplings because they really don't store very well, kinda like trying to put McDonalds in the fridge. Â I kinda thought the dumplings would be like the ones at the bank across the street, tiny and not filled, WRONG! Â They were more like the ones at the construction site down the street and filled to the brim. Â  My one issue with the place, and the reason I wish you could give half stars, is because the fried dumpling skin was a little too thick for my taste. Â However, I know some people like it like that so I won't punish them for my own personal tastes. Â All in all, for roughly ten dollars total, this was quite a bit of food, probably could have filled two people.

Just so you know, there are two "Tacos El Bronco" in Sunset Park. One is a truck, usually parked on 5th, always has a ton of people outside it. The other is a restaurant down on 4th. I haven't been to the truck, but the restaurant is good. Clean, with reasonable tacos. Not the best tacos I've ever had, but having lived in LA and Albuquerque, I have tough standards, and these were yummy.

Excellent place. Â Love the vibe and the crowd. Â Great attentive and informative service. Â Menu was excellent, as were the fries, the salmon, and the chopped salad. Â I was very happy with the wine list too. Â Very ecclectic, many small winery offerings I've never seen before, and I'm a wine afficionado. Â I will visit again when back in NY. Â High five I wish all spots could be as good as this. Â Great work.

I had always wondered about Market Table. Every time I was in the neighborhood, I peered into the floor to ceiling tiled windows and promised myself to give it a shot! Food was INCREDIBLE. I'm salivating thinking of the gnocci with shortribs--wasn't too heavy and shortribs deliciously tender--and my boyfriends bacon-wrapped scallops were also wonderful. He had lamb shank which comes with gratin potatoes that are so out of this world that I devoured most of them off his plate, and I had the flank steak which was generously sized and perfectly cooked. Great wine list too. Service is a bit slower and food does take a while but it's nice to sit back, relax, and enjoy a slower pace once in a while, especially in NYC.
Small menu but everything I've had was excellent.

Got the regular 8-piece box set for $21.60, so $2.70 a piece. Selected 8 flavors: rose petal, caramel with salted butter, orange blossom, blackcurrant & violet, lime & basil, chocolate from Ghana, green apple, and raspberry. Verdict: rose petal, caramel, orange blossom, blackburrant, and lime are my preferred flavors. Rose was very fragrant, delicately soft on the inside, and simply delicious. I love how the fragrant stays in your mouth after your first bite. I love pairing Laduree macarons with a hot cup of cappuccino especially on a rainy day like today!

Came here around midnight when I was visiting NYC and stayed in Chelsea. Nice ambiance and chatty atmosphere. Food took a while but it's late and they were switching staff. Â Smoked salmon benedict was great. Large helping of smoked salmon. The eggs were firm though, which was fine for me. I'd rather they overcook than under. My friend's mojito was on the weak side.

Went here for a date and it was fantastic. Â I had the sugar freak special po' boy sandwich, mac n cheese and fried chicken! so delicious. Â The food wasn't greasy and the portions are huge. Â The decor is different from anything in astoria. Â it is a real gem

Holy crap. I apologize for cursing but I will do it again... Holy guacamole crap! I am not a breakfast for dinner person but it was pancake month and sometimes you just gotta live a little. I usually don't like weird mixes in my pancakes but these pancakes were AMAZING. It's been over a week and I find myself zoning out to thoughts about these pancakes - kumquat, toasted coconut, and only God knows what was in the syrup. The pancake had so much depth and that perfect crispy outer ring that you only get with homemade pancakes or ones made with love. We also had the buttermilk fried chicken which was also equally good. To put the cherry on top, although the place was packed and busy, our waitress was no less than awesome.
As other reviewers have noted, always great on any day, at any hour. And SUPER cheap! Falafel and Shwarma sandwichs are both excellent. I really love that pickles are included as topping.
Awesome fries and sandwiches! Used to go all the down to Mott Street Downtown but now I go here for those crazy cravings!!! Love 'em!

A great ramen joint in midtown. Â The wait can be at Ippudo standards but with good company it can go by quickly. Â The wait is tough in the cold weather but if you manage to get in the enclosed hut with the 15 other people waiting then all that body heat makes the wait bearable. The soup is flavorful, not too heavy and noodles are perfectly al dente. I can't remember which soups I've tried but I do know that they were all delicious and hearty. If I were to compare this to other Ramen places in the city - its superior to Ramen Setagaya and Menchanko tei, couple of ranks above Rai Rai Ken and the overrated Ippudo and a baby step below Kambi/Minca. Â Totto Ramen has made its way into one of my top ramen places. Â The only thing that stinks is the wait but well worth it when you're in midtown and have a hankering for it.
The Thai Tea is pretty good!

This place is all about offal, and they make zero attempt to cater to those who don't eat it. The hot dog was quite lackluster, and came with *nothing* on it, for $4.50. Friends enjoyed the heart, but the $10 price tag on that is rather high, considering how incredibly cheap it is to buy heart. The $6 dessert tarts were *terrible*, worse than what you'd expect out of some random greasy spoon in the midwest. All in all, if I want meat, I'll go next door to Fette Sau. If I want a deep fried hotdog, I can go Crif Dog (where they are significantly better and cheaper), and there are a million options for sausages. This place needs some work.

The food was okay. I think the place was a bit small. There was only one bathroom. They ran out of a lot of the cocktails on the menu. The 2 I wanted they didn't have which was a bit disappointing. They let you sit down as long you have half your party here and they don't really count each person like other restaurant do.
We sat at the bar and had cheesecake and coffee and a few drinks. Â  Wonderful atmosphere, great service going back again. Â Good prices.

Expected a bit more from all the five stars. It was pretty delightful though. We tried most of the meats and found them generally to be delicious and very fresh. The al pastor was the real highlight here as it is carved off of a giant spit gyro style. The salsas taste homemade and are excellent. The price is also right.

Amazing Greek food. The only problem is that you have to wait for your table. It's very crowded it. The best time to go.,It's between 2pm and 5pm. Â It's worth it. Fresh fish and seafood, affordable prices.

I ADORE this place! They have such a romantic rustic decor. Its really pretty and makes you feel like your on the French Countryside. The food is absolutely delicious! I had the chicken, my roommates had the signature burger and the charles pizza. Everything was flavorful and satisfying. We were stuffed half-way through the meal but not having desert was not an option. I got the Chocolate Moelleux and my roommates shared the Profiteroles. The Chocolate Moelleux was dangerously yummy, and the Profiteroles was also really good but large potion, so ideal for sharing. I would love to frequent this place more. Its a bit of a walk from the train station but totally worth it. The service and food are impeccable! Plus! If you check-in on yelp you get a free glass of wine ;)

Fast service. Â Not a place for privacy. Â There are few table up close and chatty personal. Â The lady at the table next to me kept kicking us in the shins. Â But it started a fun conversation. Â Sweetbreads were amazing. Â Pulpo & fennel lovely. Â Bone marrow super tasty and heart attack rich. Â Oxtails with peppers spicy and good. Â There's the bar jamon around the corner where you can sip and wait for your table if you have one. Â They will come and get you and caddy your drink over for you. Â Olive oil ice cream - do it!

Came here because Pizza by Certe didn't have any pizzas with mushrooms on it. Â Decided to take a walk a block down and found My Pie. They import their flour from Italy! Â WTF - definitely caught my attention. Decided to buy pizza for the whole office. Mushrooms in truffle oil - amazing Margherita - amazing Plain Cheese Slize - to die for :) Everything was very good, highly recommend you try it out if you're in the Midtown area.

Watermelon mimosas? Avocado toast? Um, hello, the sound of those is amazing, and you're in luck, because they taste even better than they sound. And you get to enjoy them in an adorable cafe that makes you feel like you've stepped into another world. It makes you want to wear a slinky dress and lounge at the bar with a dirty martini and make eyes at one of the gorgeous waiters. But, you should stuff your face instead because the brunch is amazing. I opted for the baked eggs with tomato, basil, and cream as my entree, and they were perfect- not too oily, which happens often with baked eggs. I can't remember what anyone else ordered because I was busy dying, but before we placed our orders we were (pretty rudely) staring at other people's plates, trying to figure out what they ordered and salivating at all the options. They probably thought we were tourists, however, because I think we were too busy eating to even talk. It's that good. I'm starting to drift off into a food coma thinking about it, so we'll stop here.

After living and working in Tokyo for 2 years a decade ago, I truly felt as if I were right back in Japan at Sakagura. The decor and food is traditional...and real, homemade soba like this is nearly impossible to find in the states. The sashimi was possibly among the best I have ever had. Service impeccable, just what you would expect from a traditional Japanese restaurant. It wasn't just lunch...it was an experience. Highly recommend!!!
I kind of don't understand the hype. 4.5 stars? Â Really? I'd give it a solid 3, at best.

I hate to be a downer... but this is maybe my least favorite Pizza experience in NYC. Server was as attentive as she could be... while handling ten other tables during lunch rush. Prices are steep. Pizza is... OK. Actually, maybe a little worse than OK. And I got the Margherita. If you're in this area, do yourself a favor and go to L'asso! Way better atmosphere, service, AND FOOD FOR THE PRICE!

At first glance, it is easy to miss this restaurant as the first floor is long and narrow. The main dinning area is on the bottom floor. The restaurant is trendy, hip, and modern. I can't say that for the food. The food is meant to be shared family - style. For groups, I would definitely suggest : 1) Ceviche - we ordered two ceviches and that was good for a group of 6. I preferred the Ceviche Lemino vs the Mixto because i did like the texture of the chunks of fish. 2) Chicken - Each order of the chicken is cut into 4 pieces (two whites, and two darks). 1-2 pieces are usually good per person. We ordered the matador combo which comes with the additional sides. Others we had were : 1) Picante de Camarones - shrimp sauteed with yellow rice. My one compliant is that there wasn't a lot of shrimp that came with the dish. 2) Papa Rellena - they only gave you 3 pieces. The sangria was deliciously strong. This could be a spot where I just come just for the sangria.

Grabbed The Journal sandwich for $7.62 and enjoyed it, but would certainly guess that the meat-oriented sandwiches are more of a hit, given that this was kinda sloppy, and not in that guilty-pleasure-deli-hero kinda way (plus I didn't meet the $10 minimum for plastic despite a substantial charge). Tiny bodega aisles so beware during the rushes.

Had the pleasure of eating here a week ago, only made better by it being a work event so the bill wasn't coming my way. Very modern decor (exact opposite of my other Jean-Georges experience @ Piccholine), little dark but in general a warm and inviting layout. Â As expected, staff was very attentive, friendly, and helpful in suggesting cocktails and dishes. For food we got a bit of everything, what stood out on the appetizer front was the burata, pulpo, and some type of truffle sweet potato concoction (the best, however the portion could only make a mouse full) - also got the tuna but it did not stand out. Â Main course was the lamb, which was fantastic. Â We also got the fried chicken for the table which didn't blow me away (and I had a few drinks in me, so was salivating for some good friend chicken). I would highly recommend Perry St, keep your orders to the classics and you will not be disapointed.

So as everyone knows, Mamouns is a great place to get cheap falafel. Â It fills you up, and is less than $5. Â I have had very good experience EVERY time I have been to the one on St. Mark's. Â This one however, disappointed me. Â Not because it wasn't delicious, but because the guy at the counter basically charged me and gave me something I didn't order. I just order a "falafel sandwich" and was charged $3. Â I told him I just wanted the falafel sandwich, and he said that "all sandwiches that come with falafel is $3." Â It clearly stated that a falafel sandwich was $2 and that the hummus sandwich was $3. After paying $3, and after biting into it, there was hummus in the sandwich. Â This is not what I ordered. Â What if I was allergic to something in the hummus? Â Totally not cool. Â What was worse, was that when my friend ordered a falafel, he was charged $2.50 and got Â a sandwich that didn't have any hummus in it. Â In the end, I believe that he just made this sandwich earlier, didn't want to throw it away, and made up some story to sell the sandwich. Â I will never go to this Mamoun's again. Â I didn't really care about the extra money he charged, but he basically decides what my order is, rather than the reverse. Â Go across the street for a falafel sandwich instead....at least for this location!
I traveled more than 7 times in NYC and It's an obligated place for me when I travel to NYC.

The food was exquisite (for what it is), a New York City Thai restaurant. Highlights include the Toam Zab (spicy lemongrass soup), Pad Pred Proam (mock veggie duck), and the Pad See Ew. We were veggie eaters and accidentally ordered real duck, hoping for some eggplant. Luckily they were nice and took the dish away and didn't charge us for it, but make sure to read the menu carefully. Love the BYOB, and the service was good. If you forget about the BYOB, there is a decent liquor store 3 doors down. The atmosphere isn't amazing and I wish they had a few more veggie options. I definitely plan to eat here again, and you should plan to here too, especially if you like Thai food.

A must go every time I go to that area. The corn is absolutely my love. BEST corn in the world. Also tried the sloppy joe's sandwich the other day. Very Very spicy! but delicious!!! There's always a lot of people whenever you go. So prepare to wait a bit ;) It's worth it! There isn't a lot of tables in the restaurant. Many times I just wait outside (sometimes I eat my corn outside haha) there's a bench. So I would suggest to go there when it's not too cold... Also, pretty good price ;)

Came for dinner last Friday night with my girl friend. Â I mainly wanted to try it because it has such a great view of the city. Â Didn't have a reservation but figured, hey we can have a drink at the bar. Â It was very busy and we put our names down to wait for a table, the girl said it would be 30-45 minutes wait time. Â We had margaritas at the bar and waited and waited and waited. Over an hour had gone by and they still did not call us even that we saw empty tables available. Â I went to ask what was happening and was answered by the manager " we are really busy on Friday and its over an hour wait now... ( no apology at all and with an attitude) Â I said you should have told me that when i came in?. Â They were really rude but we decided to wait since we had been there so long. Â Checked back again and they looked at me like i was crazy..We were finally seated after an hour half of waiting and $60 bar tab for 4 margaritas, to one of the tables that were empty for at least 40 minutes... Â They could have at least bought us a round, but that would make them wrong.. The food was really sub-par and portions were small. Guacamole was good but tiny portion, Â I had the sea bass, tasted very well done and my girl friend had the steak. it was just a small steak with rice and beans. Â  Also they play a very annoying trancey salsa music beat, it's fun at first but it never changes and gets on your nerves after an hour. Â  Probably the best part of the night was the views and the Margaritas.. I will not be coming back here any time soon.. Â Too bad, because I love hanging out in LIC

A very welcome addition to Clinton Hill! Â  Great!: I've been here twice and am a huge fan of their shrimp, lobster and grits! Â Great flavors and very adequate portion of lobster & shrimp. Â Caramel Martini was fantastic and served topped with a pierced roasted marshmallow balancing just above the luscious caramel liquor - great presentation! Â  We began with appetizers: crawfish dumplings and BBQ short ribs. Â The dumplings were very good, but the short ribs - fantastic! Â Spicy, sweet, tender and juicy. Â They can expand THAT appetizer to a main course! Â The watermelon lemonade cocktail was very good and Â the blueberry bourbon sour (verklempt! - TO DIE FOR - if you like bourbon drinks) NO, I didn't drink all that in one night! Â lol, I was with my partner and mom. Â We all tasted each other's food to get more of a cross-section of what SoCo could do well. Â The Salmon was well seasoned and cooked just right - tender, juicy yet slightly firm. Â The service was impeccable! Â Very friendly/outgoing staff that was a pleasure! OK: The smoked pumpkin ravioli was OK. Â Cooked al-dente, but I didn't really taste any "smoke" flavor. Â The cornbread was too cake-like (moist) and a bit sweeter than I like. Â I'm into the more grainy, slightly drier and less sweet cornbread to go with food. Â And for $4 extra (I think?) that was too expensive for the portion we were given. Â The mussels tasted fantastic but a few were under-steamed (very mushy texture)...not sure how that happened but for the few that we got, the portion was large and the broth was fantastic, so I'll give them another shot next time. Not so good: Noise level inside. Â I don't like nor frequent loud crowded restaurants, but, if the weather is nice (like it was both time I went) then opt for the backyard seating where you can actually have a conversation without shouting "what?!" throughout your meal. Â :-) Overall, my experience was very favorable and will definitely be back! "Chow" (Ciao!) for now! Â :-)

Amazing burger! Bacon was delicious. Wonderful specialty drinks-bloodys and spiked cider. Cute ambiance. Definitely not a place to run and quickly grab a bite being the service was slow. They take their time but the food is that much better for it. Salads are delicious but very small. This restaurant is perfectly simple.

I had this potato dish as an appetizer. It was very flavorful. For entrÃ©e I had this stir-fry beef with peppers and onions. It came with a choice of rice or bread. I chose the bread. The flavors were amazing but the beef was a little over cooked. I would still come back and try other things on the menu. Surprisingly this place has mango lassi an Indian drink, which I order. It's a favorite drink of mine.

The tiny restaurant was packed, but we were squished into a table for two amongst masses of other customers chatting and laughing. It had a really atmosphere, music and chatting. The food was ordered quickly, arrived quickly and paid for quickly which is great when you want something for lunch in btwn shopping and sightseeing. I'd definitely go again.

A fun place to enjoy a burger and a beer. A good solid honest burger but there is nothing particularly outstanding about it. Not worth waiting in a long line, so go at an off hour. The place is old school and unfortunately dirty. The bathroom is similar to what you would find in a truck stop. The prices are reasonable given its popularity. This is a check the box type of place for burger aficionados.

Nice little place in Greenwich village. I can't comment on the entrees, but the happy hour wine flights were great, the cheeses were excellent, and the servers were all fantastic. Will definitely come back here.

Enjoyed a delightful meal in their outdoor space. Â Goat cheese salad, fried chicken and lobster rolls were all excellent. Â French fries and potato salad were perfectly prepared. Â Desert of chocolate mousse cake was a great finisher. Drinks were strong. Â Wait staff was all smiles and helpful. Â I highly recommend this restaurant.

Found this by Urban Spoon rec, and man, it was awesome. This tiny restaurant was kind enough to open their doors early for us, to get us out of the cold moring air. Once seated we were treated to an amazing old-school cappuccino - no drizzled syrup on this badboy! the scrambled with salmon and spinach, served with mashed potatos, tinged slightly red from a tomato infusion, were whipped to perfection. True warm, cozy, comfort food on a chilly fall morn. Beware, seating is extremely limited, so you may have to wait. Say "hey" to Ramon when you get there...colorful server with an intersting music background...enjoy!

Yummy! Not much more to say about this place; look at the number of reviews here and the avg of stars. The fries are amazingly delicious and there are a variety of sauces to choose from. Good on a cold day because eating these fresh off the fryer will leave you warm and fuzzy. Goes good with beer.

Although in general I find it pretty difficult to mess up shabu shabu, Shabu Tatsu is the only place I've encountered thus far that leaves me satisfied! Â Attentive staff, cozy atmosphere, fresh meat & veggies, and the more delicious smell of all of it cooking, make this place a shabu shabu mainstay. For 20 bucks you can get a set shabu shabu meal complete with app & dessert. Â It's the perfect amount of food for the semi-starved appetite, and wont' leave you feeling groggy and overstuffed! Of course, like everyone else says, the soup is the best part! Â And even better, they DO NOT use MSG in their soup cups! Â It's just salt and pepper! Also I found the pitchers of Sapporo, a first encounter for me, to be absolutely clutch!

When we were in NYC, this was the first place we hit up because it was right next to our hotel in downtown. I guess the prices caught us off guard because NY food prices are a little more than LA prices so I can't hold that against them. My review will be based on taste. On to the food. We saw a bunch of 4-5 star reviews on Yelp, which is the main driving force for us to eat here. Maybe the anticipation was a little high, but I would rate the food just OK. It wasn't great and it was for sure not bad. I ordered the waffles and it didn't give me the 'wow' factor. I would recommend Penelope, but if you have another restaurant in mind, I'd go there first.

The Scratcher is kind of hidden down in a basement area of a brownstone on 5th Street. Â It's a real gem if you can find it. Â It's a low key and casual hang out, where you can go to read a book at the bar and indulge yourself in a nice mug of beer, or you can meet up with some friends after work and just relax in a home-like environment.
You probably won't have to wait as long if you're just a couple people; it's easier for them to squeeze you in somewhere. Pizza is marvelous. Sauce was a little runny, but tasted great.
Pure Deliciousness! Love me some meatballs-- and these are PERFECT! Some serious Guido balls. YUM.

EXCELLENT FOOD, DRINKS AND SERVICE. I came here for my birthday and it was amazing. I was a bit skeptical at first because you can't make reservations and its a cash only place but it was all totally worth it. When we got there we were told that there was an hour wait but we only waited about 15 minutes before being seated. The service was great, our waitress and the porters were very attentive. I would definitely come back to this spot. I recommend the king crab legs with all the special mixed sauce, spicy! (My boyfriend had the lobster, it was also excellent!) Seafood heaven!!! Â I was there on 7/12/14.
Awesome coffee. Awesome avo-toast. Awesome service. My only gripe is that the place is pretty tight space-wise, but we were still able to get seats by the window.
Udon and dumplings were great. Â The atmosphere was good too.

I loved this place. Â It was busy but not too loud, swanky hip but not snooty, the service was excellent without being overbearing, drinks were interesting and tasty, and the food was delicious AND beautiful. Â 5 whole-hearted stars.

After 2400 reviews I'm pretty sure people get the point - this place is solid. Have had the spicy and the original. Â Both are great. Â (The spicy can be a bit too salty though). The pork buns are also excellent. Â The wings good. Consistently a long wait - but worth it.

One of the best Indian restaurants I've ever experienced. We stuck with the basics: garlic naan, chicken masala, and vegetable sides of dal and chana masala. All dishes were amazing. Bottles of wine are in the $30-$40 range, which seemed reasonable for NYC. The place was busy, but we were seated within 5 minutes. Booths and tables are spacious, so you can relax after a day of walking (unlike many local places that are small, cramped, or don't have a dining area). Service was very good & friendly as well. 5 stars!
This place rocks, fast service, great atmosphere, EXCELLENT FOOD!

DO NOT COME HERE. Save your money and your time. I read the reviews here expecting a fantastic seafood restaurant and great, friendly service but experienced none of the above. This just seems like a place for downing beers and eating oysters. The restaurant is a dive bar... The washroom is disgusting (a gas station's is better) and the atmosphere is loud and rowdy. We came to eat dinner and ordered 2 Fish & Chips, 1 Fried Chicken sandwich, and 1 Grilled Salmon. The bill would be $60 plus tax and tip. The waitress was absolutely terrible. She never came to serve us our food (she let another server bring it to us while she took shots with a few male customers), she never asked us how our meals were, and she seemed less than enthusiastic when we asked if she could kindly give us a bottle of much-needed ketchup for the bland fish. She even spilled some oil on my brother's pants as she took away our empty plates and she didn't apologize or seem to notice. Our food was ridiculously overpriced ($15 for 1 measly piece of fried fish and a small side of fries). My grilled salmon came on one plate while the mashed potatoes (more like flavourless liquid potato soup) arrived on another plate. The fish was supposed to come with mixed vegetables so when we asked where they were, the waitress seemed a little surprised and disappointed as she reluctantly went behind the bar and grabbed a handful of mixed greens from a plastic bag then plopped it in a bowl and passed it to me. When I asked what varieties of potato were offered with my grilled salmon, she said she didn't know and had to go to the kitchen and ask. A waitress who works at the restaurant but doesn't know the menu? Great. Everyone else in my group had their meals arrive 10 minutes before mine and the bell in the kitchen rang a few times to indicate my meal was ready before the waitress finally acknowledged it (the noise level in the place had skyrocketed by then). The fish & chips was very small. The fish was 1 thin cod fillet split in half to make "two" fish fillets. When we told the owner, Jeff, that the fish was smaller than we expected, he said: "Well, it's one piece of fish. That's how we do it here." Then he walked away. This is definitely not a place for high-quality food and definitely not family-friendly. The only slightly redeeming quality of our experience was that the owner removed the cost of 1 Fish & Chips order from our bill after we complained though he didn't inform us about it. Needless to say, I do not recommend this place and I won't be relying on Yelp for "highly recommended" restaurants anymore.

I would revist NY just to go here. Â Their food is amazing not to mention their staff is super friendly and know their stuff. Â  Went to celebrate my parents' 40th anniv here w/ the family. Â Got several appetizers and drinks. Â My dinner was the stuffed trout (sorry don't know the correct name) it was the special of the night and boy was it special. Â Probably one of the best meals I have ever had. Â  Will definitely come back when I'm in town. Â A must if you want some incredible Cuban food, great drinks and an overall great experience.

I love Trattoria L'incontro so much, I had my wedding rehearsal dinner here! Â This is by far my favorite Italian restaurant in New York City. Â Rocco is a tremendously talented chef and his impressive list of specials (memorized and recited by the superb waitstaff) is proof. Â Don't even bother to open the menu. Â Stick to the specials. Â The food is authentic but creative and will make happy diners of even the most discriminating of food snobs. Â And for dessert? Â Hazelnut (nutella) pizza. Â Trattoria L'incontro is practically perfect in every way. Â Hot damn, this is why I love Queens.

Corn corn corn corn corn!!!!! So delicious, oh so fresh, just perfectly grilled, and perfect for a post shopping snack. Confession: I don't actually love the cheese or mayo, but it somehow works with the corn!! Yum! I'll have to come back and try some of their other food (the tortas look and sound delicious), but for now, I'm content grabbing a corn on the cob and chowing down under the little trees outside.

This is more of a 3.5. I really enjoyed the stuffed mushrooms. They were fabulous! I asked for a recommendation for pasta and the waiter suggested the "pasta special". It was a red sauce with sausages, tomatoes, mushrooms. Delicious! Portions are HUGE!!! Seriously, the more the merrier. The lack of stars comes with the service. Our waiter took a super long time to bring us drinks and things that we asked for. They didn't come to check on us at all so it was difficult getting our the bill and refills on drinks. Otherwise, I would definitely come back just for the food and choice of breads! I guess it's just so popular!! Even though we came early (5pm for dinner) it was still an hour wait!

I really hold a high standard when it comes to barbecue. By far Brisket Town went above them. Having been to barbecue greats such as The Salt Lick, in Texas, this is as close as it gets. The service here is amazing to say the least, always ready to answer questions, recommend food, and are pleasant to be around overall. This is easily a new favorite.

Holy Crap! This place is NO JOKE! Thank you so much Yelp for guiding me Â a new go to inexpensive DELICIOUS spot. Boyfriend and I had the falafal and chicken pita sandwich (forget what it was called) and babaganoush. The food is delicious and that's what the 5 stars are for. Â When we came it was crowded and service was slow (one waiter for the whole place, plus the owner helps out but I also thinks she cooks?) I really dont care when the food is that delicious, I cant wait to come back and try everything on the menu!

We stopped in Nook for lunch earlier this week with a couple of friends. Â No problem getting a table on a weekday, but (as previous posts mentioned) it is small in there. Â My friends had really enjoyed breakfast/brunch at this spot before, but I found lunch to be.. lunch. We all ordered soup and sandwiches. Â The mushroom soup of the day was decent, but I thought the sandwiches were pretty skimpy. Â My chicken and avocado sandwich had maybe 1/3 of a chicken breast that had been thinly sliced and about 1/4 of an avocado- all on a piece of thick crusty bread. Â It tasted ok, but seemed really stingy and could have used a lot more volume. Â The rosemary fries were good. Drinks were odd. Â Each table was given a large bottle of water to serve ourselves. Â There was no ice and the water was room temperature. Â We ordered sodas and were presented with a glass and whatever was left of a can- still no ice. Â $3 for a can of soda, but we had to drink it warm... very European. Service was slow and gruff. Â CASH ONLY. Â So Nook was a disappointment. Â I'll try somewhere else next time!

This place is classic....obviously, if it's the first pizzeria in the United States. But I digress. This is great, brick oven style pizza, so don't expect it to be your typical NYC slice that you can buy on the corner. The cheese and sauce melt together pretty well with the toppings, the crust is crispy (some parts are burnt, but then again, it's brick oven). The service is pretty fast, and they are all friendly enough. I recommend this place if you're going on a pizza tour, if you're with a group of friends, or if you're out on a date. There's nothing wrong at all by going to this classic in the heart of Little Italy.

3.5 stars. Â I should first point out, I'm originally from the 305 (Miami) so I grew up eating this stuff as a kid so I am a bit more critical. Â  (yea, the asian with a spanish taste bud). Â Every time I come back from Miami, I always miss its cuban food. So, I was glad when Rachel A organized a Cuban dinner in Queens. Call me loco but for cuban food, I'd trek 1 hour of my commute to try some comidas Cubano. The place is friendly and casual yet the waiters Â are "suited-up." Â  It does add a sense of "class" and service is attentive. Â  Started with appetizers: ham croquettes, cuban tamale with pork, yucca con mojo, chorizo, and codfish fritters, plantains, and a pitcher of red sangria. Â  Free sliced (hard pressed) bread was provided as well. Â The sangria was a tad sweeter than I would have liked but that's more of a personal preference thing. It tasted more like fruit juice than wine. Â Again, depends on your taste. The bread was average- yes it's free but it seemed a bit dried. A little butter could have helped. Â  The appetizers were good: cuban tamale had the right amount of corn consistency and pork filling; the yuca was well-cooked, soft and non-starchy. Â However, the mojo was a little lacking; it could have had more of a garlic and citrus flavor. Â The plantains were sweet and served right-no complaints. Â The rice and beans were a little bit of a dissapointment though. Â Generally, rice and beans are a staple of a cuban meal and it just didn't have the "oomph" I was looking for. Â I was looking for a salty, zesty, well- seasoned black beans and rice. Â What I got unfortunately, was bland rice and beans with little taste. Perhaps my most favorite of the dishes we've sampled were the ropa vieja, oxtails, Â and lechon asado. Â Now we're talking-these dishes hit home in the 305 and made me want to jump on a plane and head down back to Miami for more cravings of cuban food. Â The meats were all succulent and seasoned well. Â Note- these portions are not really big enough for family style; you're better eating the plate on your own. Ever had a guayaba con queso pastry? Â Think of pastries stuffed with guava paste and cream cheese (sweet, savory, tangy all in one). Â Well, Rincon Criollo's version is a "deconstructed" version, without the pastry. Â You get whole pieces of guavas and a tub of cream cheese. Interesting concept, and while good, i do miss the pastry version. They also do birthdays, complete with flashing lights, a jingle, and a dance, and a flan. Â Do embarrass your friends by telling the staffs it's their bday. Overall, this place is good for a cuban fixing. Â However, I do feel it's easier for me to travel down to Miami than to queens (it's so far!). Â But, if you're close or in the area, this place will satisfy your palate for cuban cuisine.

I don't like pizza. There, I said it. I don't say this to be contrarian. I genuinely don't like pizza. I'll eat it, but I usually find the same dull combination of white bread, processed mozzarella cheese, and tomato sauce incredibly boring, and usually too salty. If I even have a slice, it's usually because there's nothing else to eat. And pour on the veggies please (processed meat like the kind they use on pizza really does make me want to be ill). OK, OK, so if I hate pizza so much, why do I give Artichoke Basille's 4 stars? Because IT'S THAT GOOD. Their signature slice (the Artichoke slice) has no tomato sauce (yay!). It is a thick soft-crust slice topped with a half-inch (1.25 cm) of deliciously cheesy creamy sauce that can only be described as something that reminds me of alfredo sauce, but *way* better. And then they add artichokes, and some other green vegetable that I can't be bothered to remember. And the slice is HUGE. I am easily satisfied with just half a slice, but I will eat a whole one just for the taste experience. They won't sell you half a slice, but they will cut a slice in half so you can share it with your family, friend, or frenemy whom you are not-so-secretly hoping will gain enough wait to make you look thin by comparison (recommended strategery: each of you order your own slice, have them slice yours in half, then offer the frenemy half of your slice in addition to the one they already consumed). They have only 2 other varieties of pizza: the margherita and the crab meat slice. I've had both. Meh. The margarita slice looks fancy, but in reality is nothing special. The crab meat slice is loaded with crab meat, but is way too salty for my taste. I don't particularly like salty food, so you might want to take that description with a grain of salt, so to speak. Their locations in Manhattan on Macdougal and on 14th St seat *maybe* 6 people each, so be prepared to take the slice to go. If you want to sit down, visit the one on 10th Ave and W 17th St. I just noticed they opened a couple of locations in Queens and Berkeley, CA, but I haven't been to those, so I can't comment. Last word: Artichoke Basille's is great for late-night snacking just before you go home, and showing a visitor to NYC a weird yet awesome version of pizza that they cannot get outside of NYC. Except Berkeley, apparently.

Great food for the price. You may have to endure a long line though but it is definitely worth it. My recommendation is to try the lamb gyro over rice. You can also share with a friend. The serving is quite big. This is my favorite spot to go to for a cheap and quick bite after work.

This ish rules. The burgers embody everything I love about meat. Everything is awesome. Especially the onion rings. ESPECIALLY the bloody marys, which I come in for all the time, day and night. People dissing the bloody marys here are straight fools. Fools, I say! If you want to see god, order the bacon royale.

This place is fantastic, such a great find! Very good made-on-premesis contemporary Italian dishes at a very unNYC price, as in affordable! Their staff has always been very friendly, their menu selection interesting and compelling, and just-right portions (for me/friends) in terms of just enough to fill you up but not so much you're walking around with a doggie box, which personally I can't stand. The wines are even affordable (for NYC) too. The ambiance is nice whether you're seated just inside or in their garden courtyard in the back. A bit funky flair to go with the bit funky flair of the place and it's charm. So if you're looking for an affordable meal in Chelsea over by the High Line Park.
Pretty Solid meatballs. Â Spicy Pork is my favorite, and the Pesto was really good too. Â Then again, I was pretty drunk..

This place makes me remember how much I love breakfast. The space is very well-designed and modern, and the staff is helpful and courteous. We grabbed seats in the empty downstairs area to enjoy the comfy couches. The chocolate croissant was flaky with the right amount of chew, just the way I like it. Unfortunately. they were out of the regular baguettes and we had the buckwheat version, but it was still very good. We ordered the grilled cheese with bacon and the mackerel sandwich. Â The sandwiches were ok, but I wouldn't do this again. It just didn't hit the spot. I'll definitely be back for the egg sandwich, baguette, and more chocolate croissant though!

My favorite Thai place to go to. It's in a good area, cheap, cozy and the food is very good, but not excellent as sometimes it's overdone. If you order pad thai, ask for less sprouts or half of the plate will be sprouts. I have no idea why they do it this way but they do. Drinks are $10. The staff might rush you if they are getting too busy so don't be afraid to push back. But usually staff is nice. Still come early. After 7 pm on Friday it is packed. Bring cash, as credit cards are not accepted.
flipping love it

Really really awesome. Â I love the location of this place, at the end of an alley removed from the hubbub of the city. Â Once you go inside, it's an amazing maze of an old building as well, beautiful all around. Â I went here for brunch on my birthday, and everything we got was delicious - fresh, quality ingredients. Â I had the poached eggs with roasted tomato, cheddar cheese grits and toast. Â I highly recommend this is you're feeling something savory! Â Planning to go back for my graduation celebration - this place is definitely too pricey for a regular old evening out, but totally reasonable for a special occasion.
this is the best of Korean Deli place in NYC. you can choose and take all of you want. if you cant eat spicy food, it's fine; you can enjoy not spicy Korean food!

Ok, so I have not had pizza because I am terrible at trying to make a gluten-free crust, and the other places just didn't cut it. I haven't had breadsticks forever (15 years??), avoid risotto, and have not had cake since I was 5 because it wasn't worth risking to see if I would have a bad reaction or a reaction that I could deal with. Here comes Risotteria. My close friends convinced me to meet them down there (I never go further south than Penn Station if I can avoid it). We had the shrimp risotto and calamari salad, they was fine. Nothing too special. And the breadsticks? I think I have 9 of them. And so light! One friend couldn't get over that it was GF (he LOVES bread). I got sausage pizza; it was four slices and we each had one, but it was yummy. I do wish it was bigger, but I suppose then the crust will fall apart because it is GF. Then The Tres Leches cake. Yes. It is capitalized. I even took a picture of it so I can remind myself to go back. So good! It was so moist! I waited expectantly for my throat to start itching and close and waited for a sharp pain in my stomach.... nothing! I ate that thing. I don't care if I stuffed myself! I went to rehearsal in a food comatose. And can't wait to get another Tres Leches cake.

new way to eat fries, who doesn't like tasty fries. Good spot for after party because they open til 3 I believe, but don't go too late, their fries are too popular and it will be out before u get there.

This place is really good. I like the way the restaurant is setup. makes me feel like im not in the city. Â you ahve to go early though or else theres a long wait. the food is simple but really good. good place to take a date or a friend.

I guess Japanese ramen is not for me. I couldn't have more than 2 bites. I ordered miso chicken soup (?). I didn't like my first bite, tried to like it having 2nd bite, then gave up. I failed three attempts before my first visit due to 1+hr wait each time; so I went around 3pm expecting no wait, and got a seat after only 15minute wait. What a disappointment. I thought I would like ramen since I love Japanese sushi/sashimi, and Izakaya foods; well, I will try at least one more place for ramen.

*Updated: Eliminating the table service they initially had was a GREAT move. Placing orders are now much easier and faster, bumping my rating up to 5 stars. Extensive beer selection, very good food, nice social environment.

Went on a weeknight, and the place was packed. We lucked out as a group witha Â reservation had not shown up, so we got their table. Place has kind of an intimate vibe. Crowd was eclectic. Music wasn't loud (ie. could actually hear the person across the table) The wait staff was extremely helpful and courteous. As soon as we sat down, we were each individually given an in-house made bread roll 2 of us had the Buttermilk fried chicken (not going say much other than, TRY IT) 1 of us had the Lemon Pappardelle The chicken batter was rich tasting, and crunchy. The chicken itself was moist. The cornbread was moist, and salad was great. I think the entrees are a wee bit on the pricey side for what you get, not extremely overpriced, jus a wee bit, especially since the portions are pretty big. Right before leaving we were given individually wrapped homemade oatmeal choc chip cookies, which were yum yum. Not sure it's a place I'll be coming over and over. Don't want to break the bank. But all in all, a great first time dinner spot.

I love this restaurant. It's charming, dark, cozy, warm, intimate with a simple euro feel. There are about 5 tiny tables, an open kitchen and one waitperson. It was the perfect place to stop in after a long night of shopping in the bitter cold. A friend and I were hungry and started trolling for restuarants; when we walked by Cafe Condesa, we had to stop. The Â mix of aromas just draws you in. We ordered a salad, sweet potato ravioli (AMAZING) and two orders of the same salmon dish. Everything was divine...I don't often expect much from the sides but the mashed potatoes and asparagus were noticably good. I wish that we hadn't ordered the same meal so I could have sampled a different dish. The scallops were ordered at a neighboring table and looked extremely tempting. The dessert menu also looked pretty good but we didn't give in. The portions are perfect and the prices were pretty reasonable. There was a small line of people waiting outside by the time we were ready to leave. This tiny litle place obviously has a few dedicated fans and I am now one of them. I plan to go back soon.

What a great little place in Manhattan! Great service. Food is solid and well made classic French (except for a few Italianish dishes). The escargots are absolutely delicious as was the tartare. My wife has mussels which were huge and tasty in a great curry sauce. Big fan! Note to owners: the music- um no. French children's music mixed with Cindy Lauper? Qu'est que c'est??

I came here to celebrate my friends birthday and I have to say...what an amazing experience! Â From the moment we arrived everyone was friendly and courteous. Â Our server Alex went above and beyond. She was knowledgeable about the menu and even made suggestions. The food was delicious!! We ordered the Churrascos and the Branzino...omg! We'll definitely be back! Â By the way....the birthday card is a great touch! Keep up the great work!

I walked into Minetta Tavern on a Monday night with my boyfriend and a friend. Â It was packed and the bar was full. Â When I told the hostess we did not have a reservation, she promptly ignored me. Â When I tried to ask her how long the wait would be she walked away. Â I was very disappointed and extremely angry, seeing as I am a cook and a former foh staff member, that she completely ignored us. Â I will not go back, if your hostess can't be bothered what does that say about the rest of the restaurant?

On my most recent visit I had the lamb and truffle toast with sauteed broccoli rabe and portabello mushrooms. YOU MUST ORDER THESE 2 DISHES. The truffle toast is probably my favorite dish there next to the bacon donuts!

Bonnie's is a small place with about 4-5 small tables in the back and 2 in the front. Theres also seating by the cooking area where you get to see all the things that go into making the food. The burgers here are fantastic, and for the price they can't be beat. Its a nice black angus burger with a lot of free toppings as well as choices to add other things on. Usually I come here for that and Buffalo Wings which is another must have at Bonnie's. There hasn't been a time where I've gone to Bonnies and not eaten those two things. The burger and wings are some of the best in Brooklyn to me. Theres also a nice selection of craft beers as well. Great food, nice vintage decor in a small spot. Get here early during dinner time as it tends to get packed. And it should be packed, because the food is great.

Woorijip is my savior when I'm in the mood for cheap, convenient, comforting Korean food. Whenever I'm feeling under the weather, nothing clears up my stuffy nose than something with Korean spice. Found deep in the hustle of K-Town, between other Korean BBQ places and Karaoke bars, Woorijip is perfect for a grab-and-go meal. This place is always packed with customers and the atmosphere is similar to a fast-casual dining place. Along the left side is the hot buffet items which rotate regularly and always offer a wide assortment of classic Korean dishes. Nearer to the back are pre-portioned entrees and soups. My favorite is always the Korean sushi, which makes a great snack. In addition to their selection of hot food, there's also a wide selection of sodas, juices, beer, and spirits. The Korean juices are always interesting and worth a try. The prices are fairly comparable but if you're not careful the weight-based pricing can turn around to bite you. However, the pre-portioned containers run at 3 for $12 and is more than enough for one person. But if you want a wide selection, Woorijip is perfect. I will definitely be back when I'm craving Korean again.
Waited three hours for a table. Saw famous people. Ate disappointing sandwich. All in all, not a great experience.

I have been coming here for the past few months, each visit just gets better. The beer list is awesome, changes every day and there is always something new to try. Had friends in from out of town a few weeks ago, who are big beer lovers. And it was craft beer week. So they had a bunch of beer events on. I had the Dogfish 120 minute which is my favorite. We ordered some app's for our table(Sliders, Nachos and Guacamole) were delicious. Staff were very Knowledgeable and attentive. Always a couple of Irish lassie's around. Love the accent!! Music was cool, classic rock, good buzz if you want to show some tourist/beer lovers a good night out or just in midtown, it's right by penn station. They also have a happy hour on sat nights and $5 special Kick the kegs on sundays. I know where i will be at the weekends.! All round it's a cool place to chill and drink good craft beer!

Came here on a sunday just right after they opened. It was reasonably easy and service was nice and helpful. The overall experience was OK, not worthy of the overall hype based on my lunch experience. We tried the steamed pork buns, the fried duck dumplings, the o.g. momofoku ssam, and the duck over rice. The pork buns were a standout, the duck dumplings were underwhelming (the fried aspect overpowered any resemblence of duck and tasted like a ball of fried batter), the o.g. momofoku ssam was way too overpowering (extremely sweet, messy, and not very creative) and the duck over rice was just that. It would be a place I would try again only if someone pushed me hard and I would get different items (would get the pork buns again though).

Today my girlfriend and I decided to eat Malaysian food. We were very pleased with the service and the dimmed lighting of the place. Definitely recommend others to come here for dinner. We ordered Curried Chicken over rice and Hanian Chicken over rice (delicious). This deserves a 4 star review because the portions of the meals were very small and some of the chicken were dry.

I love Martha. It's one of the most beautiful restaurants in town-- fantastic ambiance, original and inspired meals and drinks, genuinely friendly, warm, and attentive staff, and never so busy that you can't get a table or have to scream across the table to be heard. I would have given it five stars except for this reason, and I hope that the owners are listening: I understand their reasoning behind changing from Brooklyn Sandwich Society, but I truly miss BKSS. I think it was a better restaurant then, for brunch anwyay. And Martha is a better restaurant at night. As a compromise, I would love it if at least the brunch had a better sandwich option than the "breakfast cheeseburger" or whatever it is. It's just a little overboard, and too large and too messy and greasy to enjoy as a sandwich anyway. It tastes good, but for breakfast, I'm just not really into it. At least do something else-- there used to be this merguez breakfast sandwich with scrambled egg on a delightful brioche bun and I could never get enough of that thing. Also, I miss the picked jalapeÃ±os that came standard with every table. Now you have to ask for them and I'm not even sure if they always have them anymore. And lastly, their menu has changed to almost be a menu of nothing but dishes inspired from China, Japan, Thailand, Vietnam. I like that they borrow ideas and techniques from those cuisines, but their menu is almost becoming a fancy Chinese restaurant more than anything. I miss some of the more New American options they once had on the menu; at least to have some variety. If I want Chinese food, I'd rather just go to a nice Chinese restaurant. Seems like they are going through a slight identity crisis and I am not sure what I think about it because, admittedly the food is still excellent. I just miss the stuff New American that used to be on the menu that they did really, REALLY well. But, all things considered, I highly recommend this place, especially for dinner. It's a really special spot and would make for a unique date place.

Avocado toast: Â YUM. Â I looooove avocado so you really can't go wrong with it for me. Â Strong on the lemon flavoring and the red pepper flakes added just a tinge of spicy. Â  Cous cous w/chicken: Â I felt like the cous cous itself was a bit bland and dry. Â It tasted a lot better if eaten together with lots of hummus and the green sauce (no idea what that was) that it comes with. Unfortunately, there was not enough hummus and sauce to accompany every bite of cous cous, so I was left with some dry and bland "rice" at the end. Bottom line: Â I would still come back just for the avocado toast. Â YUM!
Do not go here if you are a vegetarian or into carbs. Â It's all meat! Â There isn't even any pasta here. Â It's awesome, though, and I loved the rooftop dining.

I came in on a weekday with a few people and the service was really good and the atmosphere was relaxing. The food was well made and crafted nicely. This little gem is something not usually found in this neighborhood which was a pleasant surprise! :)

I've been to Cafe Henri a couple of times for take out and sit down meals. Generally the food has been pretty good (esp the brunch and crepe items), making this an especially popular spot in restaurant starved LIC. The service on the other hand is a whole other story. I generally just focus on food at restaurants and don't really complain about if the service is less than stellar. But the past weekend when I went, the service was so rude and disrespectful it actually made me angry! I went with my younger sister and boyfriend here for brunch the past Sunday. My sister wasn't hungry and just ordered the chocolate croissant. My bf ordered the egg and sausage platter and I got the orange, caramel crepe. The chocolate croissant came out after a few minutes, and then nothing else came. It was a busy morning and we just assumed they're backed up with orders. After 30mins we saw people who arrived after us getting their food and when we hailed the waitress over to our table she asked us if we wanted anything else. Basically she totally forgot about the rest of the order and never put it into the kitchen! Afterward, there was no apology no indication of when our food was going to arrive. She just casually walked away. Then after our food arrived, we asked for salt and pepper since we were one of the few tables without a condiments set. She took one from an empty table and angrily set it down. Halfway through the meal another table asked for salt and pepper and instead of taking the shakers from the empty table next to us the waitress comes over to our table takes ours without a word! This whole experience let me with a really bad taste in my mouth and I think it'll be a while before I come back here. The only redeeming quality about the whole experience was the food. The scrambled eggs were perfectly cooked, not too runny and not overly browned. The home fries were really tasty with just the right amount of seasoning. The crepe was also very good. Soft and thin with just right amount of fruit and caramel filling. Maybe I'll just do takeout from now on...

Fonda is by far my favorite bottomless brunch in the city! I've tried pretty much everything on their brunch menu, and every single item was delicious. The drinks are great too, and they will keep them coming the whole time you're there! I'll be back again soon...
So cultural taste it is. I tried the mixed platter this time including three sauces. The green one impressed me with its spicy flavor.

Mighty Quinn's operates like the chipotle of BBQ. I had really high expectations after trying their brisket sandwich at Smorgasburg this summer. The brisket I had there was not fatty at all and super tender. They also topped it with pickles, hot peppers and a generous amount of BBQ sauce. YUM. I remember it being the perfect bite. Still thinking about it now..yum! 2 of the guys in our group ordered ribs, I ordered the brisket again and another friend got a pulled pork sandwich. You line up and tell them your order aswell as the sides you like, we tried the beans which were amazing , the broccoli salad and the sweet potato with maple pecans. You also get a bunch of free add-ons such as coleslaw, pickles and peppers. Everyone LOVED the sweet potato side but it's more of a dessert than anything, very sweet and tastes strongly of caramel. We all also ordered beers because you gotta have a beer with BBQ. It's overall a fun and laid back place to go but I wasn't as impressed with the brisket as I was before.The pieces they cut for me were extremely fatty this time around. Some people will also probably like that the BBQ sauce is on the table but it's not fun when your friends are hogging it and your brisket sandwich is dry. Wish I could go back to the perfection of that Smorgasburg brisket Sammy right now. Mighty Quinn's is still a top choice for some good meat and much easier when you have a large group since you never have to worry about splitting bills. The prices are also decent at about $9.25 a serving and sides for about 4 dollars. If you're looking for a less fatty cut I suggest telling the guys behind the counter because otherwise you might be disappointed Â like I was.
Can't say anything about the food but good happy hour drinks nice atmosphere awesome bartender

Got delivery. Ordered the beef platter. Smallest portions of mediocre beef and sides I have ever payed $20 for. The food was OK but for that price and the small portions I need to be entirely blown away. Probably my last time eating from this place. I'll spend the same amount for better quality meats and larger portions at bare burger EDIT----------------------------------------------Â­--------------------------------------------------Â­---- So I can't discourage take out or delivery enough. But the dine in experience was really solid. The wait staff was very friendly and sweet and I always like BYOB even if they charge a small (corkage? but also for beer, so I don't know what to call it) fee. Sandwiches were all really good especially the pblt. Outdoor seating is really the highlight of the restaurant. Â Portions are still a little underwhelming but I think they get away with it since it is all local and grass fed. Â Probably the best cole slaw I've had since moving from home. More like 3/12 stars but I'm rounding down because the check presenter said Â SERVICE NOT INCLUDED and CASH TIPS APPRECIATED. I am a server I know how nice it would be to put this on cash presenters. But you are selling 20-25 dollar entrees and 12- 16 dollar sandwiches. Don't insult customers with that stuff. Unless you want to be a diner and have diner prices and service. Still 2 stars for delivery. Don't do it.

Ok, so I don't usually write reviews on here, and a part of me almost doesn't want to write a review on yelp about this place because I want it all for myself. But after going here tonight I had to. The food and drinks are insanely good (I had the black bean burger) and the bartender is beautiful! Definitely planning on getting back to this place ASAP. Highly recommended.

What a phenomenal place! Seriously - I rarely care enough to write more than a two-liner, but this place is so so so worthy. Amazingly tasty Thai food combined with a beautiful and unique decor. On top of all that, it is so reasonably priced that i actually consider it irrational not to return... Unlike other places where something you order always turns out to be a dud, not a single dish that our party of six ate was anything less than magnificent. We started with the delicious Golden Triangle which was pure fried heaven served with a fantastic plum saki sauce. Had this along with the calamari which was damn good also. Â  For my meal I had a dish i could not even have imaged in my wildest dreams - the Lychee Siamese Duck with lychee fruit, pineapples, cherry tomatoes and basil.

Yes this is a chain, no not all locations are created equal. Dim, Swanky, Comfy Seats, Plenty of Â "Professional types" eating at the bar during lunch. Â GREAT HAPPY HOUR CROWD, drinks are still the same price, but good time to people watch. Romance Factor: Â 8 Hobnob Potential: Â 8 Destination Rating: Â 8 **This LOCATION HAS A BAND DURING HAPPY HOUR Can get a little on the noisy side which is great if you do not want someone overhearing your conversation. Strong Suggestions: Knife and Fork (Ribs), Great Dip, Tortilla Chicken Soup (very filling) Great Burgers

Brunch today. Â LOUD! Â Something of a scene. Â Delicious Dandelion salad and grits. Â Fritata a little tough--maybe serving it in a cast iron skillet is cute, but leads to overcooking? Â Our waiter? Very charming.

Unquestionably, two of the best meals I've ever had have been here at Colicchio and Sons during the Summer 2012 Restaurant Week. Â From the availability of the full menu to the attentiveness of the waitstaff and maitre d', this is clearly a restaurant that highly values every customer and wishes to create a completely engaging dining experience. Â Service was perfection - courteous, friendly, informative. Â The food was astounding - every dish so delicious I feel a little guilty listing them by name since the rotating menu means many of them won't be available for long. Â The TC Burger is definitely a can't-miss menu staple - perfectly cooked and simply dressed. Â Likewise, the zeppolis on the dessert menu are complete heaven - light and sweet and served with delectably rich chocolate sauce. Â Also, for those of you who prefer not to drink with dinner, but want something beyond sodas and iced tea, they have a great selection of varietal grape juices and other non-alcoholic beverages. Â All-in-all, my favorite restaurant in New York, bar none.

FAMILY SIZED PORTIONS- LOVE! WARM SERVICE- LOVE! CLEAN, HOME-Y ATMOSPHERE- LOVE! the location is great and the restaurant has a friendly vibe. great for a date or a family dinner. every time that i've gone, my waiter has always been accomodating, welcoming and attentive. =) my favorite dish? mussels fra diavolo

I stopped at the bar this afternoon. Â I had noticed the sign yesterday and was thinking of trying it for lunch next week. No beer on tap so I went with a Prosecco instead. Lighting directly over the bar looks modern. Â Lighting in the back dining room uses mason jars arranged in a chandelier pattern. I wanted to go to some bars that had mixologist, and Employees Only was one of the places I wanted to go to. Â  Great bartenders!! Looking forward to returning for more drinks and some food

I rang in the new year with some friends at Buvette, and it turned out to be a great idea. The food and wine list get a solid five stars, but the service seemed to try too hard to emulate French stereotypes, hence the four-star rating. While the wines are definitely the most expensive items on the menu, they were solid and fairly reasonable by the bottle (for NYC standards). As I was with a larger group, we were able to try about half the dishes on the small menu, and all were astounding. Particular shout-outs go to: - Cassoulet: incredibly rich and warming for a winter night. - Brandade de Morue - melt-in-your-mouth salt cod, perfect on their toast - Oxtail Marmalade - a must-have! - Mousse de Foie de Volaille - their homemade chicken liver mousse was the perfect balance of salty and creamy. - Tarte Tatin - the perfect way to end a meal, the apples deliciously caramelized While the plates initially seem small, they pack such a rich and hearty punch that you won't go away still hungry. Whether you're trying to find a place for a romantic date, a way to impress your out-of-town guests, or just a pick me up on a dreary day, look no further than Buvette.

OKAY SO this place delivered this weekend. Sunday night we went out to dinner at Freeman's, intent on an hour and half or so meal. We left almost four hours later. I can truly say these things: 1.) This is by far the best hot artichoke dip I have ever had in my entire life. 2.) The chicken entree is possibly the best I have ever had, definitely top two. 3.) I don't know what is in the cocktail, "The Freeman", but it is fantastic as well. 4.) I LOVE my friends on the waitstaff. HI ANDY!! Additionally, having the entire couch area in the upstairs lounge was excellent, and I felt like a character from Dead Poet's Society, only with booze.

For this review I will be co-opting the vocabulary of another Yelper: Rolled up in dis dope resto wit my boyz Evan R.eFlex and Garrett "Tha General" P for some serious hoggin and not like da kind a hoggin you do when you lose a bet. The colada was off the muhfuggin hookunut so I ordered two of em. Pork jowl was fresh ta def and we crushed tha cumin-spiced lamb ribs with the yogurt and flatbreads like the bow-legged chick with tha extra toe at last call at a JC bar.

Been here twice - once just for drinks at the bar and once for dinner. Both times the staff was amazing. Â Music - not what I want - usually led zepplin or something similar - why? It's so gorgeous in there keep up the ambiance! Love the setting it's so intimate and I always enjoy exposed wood. Anyway - drinks were great - the food is AWESOME My husband and I shared their salad with the walnuts appetizer - that was flippin awesome awesome so awesome! I got regular pasta and pomodoro (can't really mess that up) but my husband got the truffle ravioli and he is still talking about it. Â In fact I wish he would shut up!
