Ootoya, as others have mentioned, is a chain in Japan known for teishoku, or set meals. Neither the interior nor the prices look like they're part of a chain, but what do I know? That said, the atmosphere feels nice and classy, and the presentation equally so. My party of two were seated at the counter in front of the yakitori grill, but sadly we weren't feeling up to yakitori that night. I ordered a yuzu-infused sake and the hamburg entree with a side of white rice (as compared to a set meal) and my total was about $30. It looked small, but was immensely filling. She was also satisfied with her gyutan entree. Our server was unobtrusive and stopped by only thrice - to take our order, check on our food, and then seeing if we wanted anything more or just the check. Since we were engaged in conversation with each other, though, that was fine by us. Do be prepared for a wait, though. My friend and I dropped by a bit before 9PM and waited about 20 minutes to be seated; there were 4 parties before us, and yet more people coming in after. We'll still probably come back to try more dishes off their menu.

i was just walking by just after lunch and grabbed a pork sandwich to go, i am currently trying to fake a work emergency so i can go back and get another, shame i don't work in the area as i would eat here all the time!

Had a disappointing experience here prompting me to post a very rare Yelp review. Â Called in advance to make a dinner reservation with my wife's family. Â When I called, I told them we would have a small, well-behaved baby with us in a car seat. Â I said I wanted to make sure that was alright. Â The guy I spoke to was very nice and took the reservation for 7:30. Â He said he would make a note of the baby so they could accommodate us at an appropriately-sized table. At 3:30 the day of the reservation I got a call from the hostess saying there had been a "mistake" with their reservation system and they could only seat us at 6 pm or 9 pm. Â Of course neither of those worked, so she cancelled our reservation. Â Surprisingly, she wasn't particularly apologetic about the cancellation. Â She seemed to regard it as our fault for not being prepared to accept the offer of a 6 pm dinner reservation. Â (Who gets home from work by 6 pm?) The odd thing is that a few weeks before, I stopped by in person and asked the hostess about making a reservation on a different night, also mentioning we would have a small baby. Â At the time she also told me they could accommodate us only at 6 pm or 9 pm. It's perfectly fine if the restaurant isn't kid friendly. Â (Although maybe a bit surprising, since Jack the Horse bills itself as a neighborhood institution in a neighborhood that is full of families with young kids.) Â I certainly don't think all New York restaurants have an obligation to be kid friendly. Â And I don't mind if they have a policy of trying to seat parties with kids before the dinner rush (or after it). Â But taking a reservation with full knowledge that it includes a kid, then calling back to cancel a few hours before dinner strikes me as very poor form. Try Sociale instead. Â The food is better, the staff more accommodating, and you don't have to worry about the restaurant drumming up a phony excuse to cancel on you a few hours before your reservation.

Only 15-20 min. wait for Sunday brunch (no reservations taken for weekend brunches), but slow service and we were very thirsty as our drinks were never once refilled, even towards the end of brunch when it wasn't that busy anymore. Â  The free bread basket comes with 1 slice of moist, delicious banana bread, 3 slices of forgettable raisin bread, and pink butter. Â I mistakenly thought the pink butter was whipped strawberry cream cheese and took a big ole bite. Â Big mistake!! Â Bleh - it's just pink butter - no unique flavoring. Â Just colored, whipped butter. We ordered the Waffle with Berries and Peach Waffle Â - the only 2 waffle options on the menu. Â (No pancake options, but a whole bunch of egg/omelette dishes for brunch.) Â The waffles were good, but nothing special. Â They're both plain waffles topped with fruit. Â The berry waffle was better than the peach waffle, however, because it had fresh fruit, as opposed to canned peaches. Â  If I come back, I'm trying the chocolate bag for dessert! Â (Not on the brunch menu, but they serve it throughout the day/night if you ask for it.)

This place has the best HOT HOT HOT wings. I always go to this place with my friends & we spend a lot of times there. They also have good burger n beer collection. I wish this place was little more bigger. If u r looking for HOT HOT HOT wings then I would highly recommend this place to u. Best wings in the town.!!!

This restaurant sums up everything that is good about New York City. Â In what other city can you get fabulous, exciting food until 4 a.m.? And eat it off white tablecloths? I ended up here at 2:30 a.m. on a Wednesday Â and still had to wait for a table. Luckily, the wait wasn't long. My friend and I had been dreaming of the marrow and oxtail marmalade for like, forever. It did not disappoint, even after a combined three years of wanting to try it. That's pretty incredible, if you ask me. 24 hours later, I swear I could still taste it. It sounds like a weird dish but it's really out of this world. Next time you're sitting around the apartment at 2 a.m., wondering what to order from the diner ... get your butt in a cab and go to Blue Ribbon. Your wallet will be considerably lighter but your tummy will love you.

My first time here was kind of a blur because we were a large group and ordered about 8 different pizzas and they were all so good that we pretty much blacked out and inhaled everything. So I came back again recently and was blown away again. I just...can't. My favorite: Cherry mother-effing Jones. Feel like bacon love was also amazing. greenpointer is great if you love arugula like i do. even just a plain regina (mozz, tomato, basil) is amazing. If you're like me and get hangry, come at least an hour before you know you'll be hungry. Just go. Let it happen.
I went here about a month ago for lunch and was so charmed. Lovely spot!
Wonderful owner who makes nearly everything on the menu from scratch off his age old family menu. Let's keep this joint alive and make it thrive in the neighborhood.
Wonderful romantic dinner spot with an amazing seasonal menu and robust wine list. The polenta was some of the best I have ever had - but you can't go wrong. Everything is amazing.

So, its my friend's birthday weekend and I missed out on the previous night's drinking festivities... Clinton St. Bakery Company was part of the agenda for the post-birthday celebration. Looking through the menu, I really wanted to try EVERYTHING, but I settled for the Spiked Hot Chocolate, Banana Walnut Pancakes, side of Sugar Cubed Bacon, and side Biscuit. The Spiked Hot Chocolate came out first and it was delicious... who doesn't like alcohol hidden in sweet drinks? The Banana Walnut Pancakes were surprisingly huge!... and when you add that warm maple butter--ohhh lawwd! bomb! The bacon was great... but then again who doesn't love sweet salty baconnzz! Lastly, the biscuit was sweet and rich with a nice softness to its interior.... delicious as expected. I wanna eat here every weekend for brunch. That is all.

I'm currently living in Florence, Italy, where there is no good Asian food, and I've been dreaming about this place. When I lived in NYC I would frequent their buffet any time I was in the area, and sometimes make special trips just for their kimchee, kale, and shrimp pancakes. The food is delicious and cheap and they usually have a wide selection of stuff at the buffet. The ambiance isn't so great but it's best for a quick meal or take-out. Definitely try all varieties of the pancakes they have at the buffet! This will be one of my first food stops when I'm back in town.

I went to a birthday party here and I thought the family style platters would never end. Here is what we had 1. Garlic Bread - Super Crazy Awesome 2. Cold Antipasti - Delicious 3. Veal Scallopine Marsala - Awesome 4. Chicken Parmigiana - Delicious 5. Shrimp Scampi - Mutha-fuckin' Super Crazy Awesome Delicious 6. Marinara- Delicious 7. Ragu (Assorted Meats) - Seriously Grubbin' 8. Titanic - Magically Delicious (or Tragically Delicious if you happen to have a victims family member within earshot). 9. Huge Platter of fruit & Assorted Desserts - Totally worth the insulin dependency that may result due to consumption. 10. House wine - House Wine Delicious I think we may have had a few more things but I began to lose consciousness. I also hear they deliver.

Good value but the food is not as good as in the past. Of the 3 pasta dishes in the pasta dinner special only 1 was really good, the Swiss chard ravioli. If you want fantastic Italian try somewhere else.

SALMONELLA POISONING!!! Â Just got the results from my doctor after I ate the chicken meatballs here. Â I did not eat anything else 8 hours beforehand and couldn't eat for days after, so it absolutely was from Penelope!!! Â Don't go.

Horrible slow Â service, indifferent bordering on rude. Average food. That's what I had been told, and it was accurate. Probably wont survive unless they replace the entire staff with people who care.

Mama ooooooooo didnt mean to make you cry, if I'm not back again this time tomorrow oooooooo, its because this place is too delicious and if I ate here every day I'd be 400 lbs. I love you too much Empanada Mama. The quickest way to my heart is to deep fry something. Add some spice and some cheese and I'm a goner. Mix that with a 24 hr sign and a $3.00 price tag, you have to literally pry me off the door step. Plus I love rhyming (and Queen) so this place is perfect. I love a restaurant that has a clearly defined sense of itself, does one thing extremely well (and in this case in a multitude of ways), and has a quirky ambiance that is fun and unpretentious. As a rule, I tend to shy away from chicken at restaurants, but I highly recommend the spicy chicken empanadas. The reggeton is also delish. Im not too down with the "fusion" ones, but once I try them (which I inevitably will) Â I solemnly vow to update.

I love brunch, so I prefer to try a place for a first time for brunch if they have some sort of unique menu. After reading rave reviews on Maharlika, their brunch items sounded very unusual, and I had to try it! I like the vibe of Maharlika, and the wait staff are wonderful in explaining what each dish is, and how it should be eaten. Many of their brunch items sound enticing to me, I ended up choosing the Sizzling Sisig with the garlic rice. Unfortunately, I was sort of disappointed, it wasn't as tasty as I would've liked it to be, and the portion was small for $16, I was still hungry after eating this dish (okay, maybe I have a big appetite for a slim girl). I wasn't ready to write Maharlika off, I wanted to give it another chance, and I decided I would go back for dinner. A few weeks ago I went with a group of friends, the NY Ethnic Food meetup. Tulfer, one of our servers was great, he explained everything in detail in with a lot of enthusiasm, and was very nice and patient with our groups disorderly Â table/seating at the beginning. I had the Balut (fertilized duck embryo), which was an interesting experience in the way you eat it, and I liked it! For my entree I ordered Kare Kare (with oxtail), it was very tasty, and filling. I'm happy I gave them another shot, and now I'm a fan of Maharlika too!

What a great, cute, charming little place. My wife and I live a couple of blocks away and were meaning to try it out when it first opened. It looked so cozy inside especially on a cold night. We did stop in and were really pleasantly surprised. Everything was great. Their duck was incredible, the dessert was amazing, wines were delicious, and everything was reasonably priced. They have this price fixe that was super cheap for the quality of the food. The waitstaff is very friendly, the place is extremely romantic but it's tiny. It's not the type of place you want to roll up to with eight of your college buddies to get some beers. I strongly recommend it. You will not be dissapointed.

The atmosphere is a bit cheesy (seriously, do we need the waiters to yell Itadakimasu every 5 minutes?) and the wait on any given day is long and frankly unnecessary, but the food is fantastic. Putting aside the ramen (which you have to eat), I highly recommend the pork buns and the wasabi octopus. Â The pork buns are bit different than Momofuku: less meaty, but less fat, and more sauce. Â They really provide different spins on the same dish. Â In terms of the wasabi octopus, make sure you have it with a glass of the draft lager they have on tap. Â It really brings out the flavors in a way you can't experience simply by having the dish alone.

I came here on a thursday around 2PM and there was no line, although there was still very limited seating. Â I was able to snag a small table with one chair, which was fine cause i was alone. Â I ordered a cheese pie, waited about 20 minutes, then devoured 5 slices (could've had more but I had to save some for my wife) of some of the best pizza i've ever had. Â The 2 and a half hours on the subway was totally worth it. I wouldn't hesitate to do it again.

We ordered the traditional margarita pizza and bruschetta. The bruschetta had tomatoes right from the fridge (super cold) and the breah was soggy and cold. We asked the waitress and she was kind enough to change it for us but it was the exact same thing again. The pizza had some sort of weird taste on 1 side (as if wine got poured on it) and smelled funny too. Overall the pizza was just OK and wouldn't recommend the long wait lines to get into this place to anyone!

The Little Owl is a West Village neighborhood restaurant on the corner of Bedford and Grove. Â Although only a block from touristy Bleecker, it seems miles away. Â The restaurant vibe is lively, but very relaxed, and not too noisy. Â The decor was rustic and cozy - a great place to spend a cold, gray January Sunday. Â The service was very good too. Â Upon entering the door, we were given a warm greeting as if we were being welcomed into their home. Â We sat at the bar as there were no tables but as soon as one opened up, we asked to move, and were promptly moved without any eye-rolling "I guess sooo" dirty looks. Â Our drinks were promptly refilled and the food came to the table in a timely manner. Â  On the food! Â We split a side of Italian sausage, which was quite good and not greasy at all. Â I got the cheeseburger as I heard it was amazing. Â Yup, it was amazing. Â It is a thick burger, and I ordered it medium. Â It came out perfectly cooked and very juicy. Â The cheese was tasty and the thick slice of bacon just sent me over the edge - pure burger bliss. Â The bread was also very high quality too, it held up nicely from the burger+cheese+bacon grease onslaught. Â Oh yeah the herbed fries were great too, but I was too busy destroying that amazing burger to really notice the fries. Â Wife got the whole wheat pancakes with fresh berries. Â The fact that they had whole wheat pancakes is a huge plus as very few places have it and my wife quit white flour. Â The pancakes were excellent and weren't a foot in diameter like at some diners. I highly recommend the Little Owl, just go at a slightly off-peak time as it is a very small restaurant.
It's a cute and inexpensive spot for a romantic date. Just amazing. The food is great. The pizza is crusty and so good. The desserts and ice creams are delicious too.

Clinton Street Baking Company is a small restaurant that serves up some of the best comfort food I have ever tasted. Â  Space is tight and limited but...Oh my GOD! Â If you taste the blueberry pancakes you will forget about all else. Â There are 3 layers of fluffy goodness with a blueberry compote that has these beautiful blueberries topping off the pancakes. Â On the side is a small ramekin with this warm maple butter that completes this plate and makes it the dynamic duo. Â I also tried the sugar bacon strips and they were nice and thick, crispy and utterly yummy. Â  A perfect salty and sweet combo. Â  I took home a slice of chocolate banana cream pie but that had to wait for next day's consumption. Â  When you are eating these pancakes, they feel so light and fluffy that you don't know that exactly how filling they can be. Â I couldn't eat another bite for the whole day and reserved my pie for the next day. Â The pie was equally delicious. Â It has a thick Â inch crust. Â The flavors are big and bold and this one fills the tummy with satisfaction. Â  You can taste the fresh bananas and big banana flavor, chocolate pudding, butter and maybe nuts in the pie crust. Â I know it can't be a straight graham cracker crust. Â It didn't taste like it. Â It tasted like there was more to it. Â  Yelpers were right on the money about the lines of people waiting to get a table. Â Don't come around brunch time or you will find yourself outside like me. Â I waited 20-25 minutes and I have to say, I would do it all again just to taste the yummy goodness inside the Clinton Street Baking Company. Â The waitress and hostess are nice and friendly. Â The hostess does a really good job in placing people and trying to minimize wait time. Â She is also right on the money when she told me a 20 minute wait. Â The price is not cheap, I paid $26 with tax and tip, but you are really getting good food for your money. Â It is well worth it. Â I can taste the butter in the crust of the pie. Â I can taste and puncture the small little blueberries on my pancakes. Â I can taste the flavors of the butter maple syrup. Â My small one complaint is the comfort of the high chair I sat on. Â It was a bit uncomfortable. Â I had a view of the street. Â I stared straight at the lines of waiting people. Â I saw anguished faces of those who wanted a table and then I saw salivating tongues as I munched on the blueberry pancakes. Â Can't say I blame them, because I did the same thing when I was waiting. Â I even gave the thumbs up to one eager patron waiting for her table outside and use hand signals to convey my total satisfaction for those lovely blueberry pancakes. Clinton Baking Company has menu has a lot of comfort style breakfast plates. Â  Some of their signature breakfast plates are available even for dinner. Â  This is a cash only establishment so come with lots of $$$. Â When I left I vowed to come back soon. Â  Can't wait to go for round two, Eggs Benedict. Â I've also been inspired to buy their cookbook.

Nice friendly place to hang out with the family and friends. Solid, tasty basics, like omelettes, salads, burgers, hanger steak. Standouts for me are the red flannel hash and bloody mary. Can you tell I go there on Sunday mornings alot? It's hit or miss with the more adventurous dinner specials though. But the vibe is always cool, as in welcoming.

Amazing food!!! Best Lebanese food I've had in a very long time and Wafa (owner) is a sweet heart. I had the Kefta kebab with tomato bulgar and hummus, delicious. The restaurant itself is very cozy and the service was on point. This restaurant is definitely going to be my go to spot for traditional Lebanese food. Highly recommended.
Great service! Red Velvet cheese cake was amazing!!!! Â I have also ordered Â cheesecake online and had it delivered and it was still amazing!!!

Met up with a friend there for dinner last night, after being away for so long! To keep it short - saw 2 roaches, one midway through appetizers, and one midway through our entree....crawling right next to me on the slat bench. Â The waitress was really nice and apologized up and down and moved us to the bar. Â Wasn't her fault. Â She said there was construction going on next door, and well.... you know...it IS NYC. Â Needless to say, we both stopped eating. They comped us everything, which I thought was superb customer service, but I felt bad about it since we did finish up the wine (it was a corked bottle so figured we were safe). Â We left a healthy tip to make up for it, and chalked it up to taking your chances in the EV. Â All was well...until my friend emailed me this morning and said he woke up in the middle of the night, feeling ill from what he surmises is the gnocchi from dinner. Â I think NSC is removed from my dinner spots for a while. Â So sad since it was so good, and the staff is so nice :(. Â Maybe when construction finishes, I'll give it a try again.
The rotisserie chicken and fried rice is worth the slight trek to woodside just for some take out.

2 Pizzas: Â 1)sausage, red sauce, olives, tomatoes. Â 2) prosciutto, olive based sauce, goat cheese, tomatoes. Delish. Â The sausage was mildly spicy. Maybe too much for a 4 year old. Great for everyone else.

4.5 stars Second time to MIster Hotpot. FIrst time was during the winter and the second time was in late July. The place really reminds me of mainland China, with the look and feel of the place. I do enjoy hotpot and this place has many options with fresh meats and vegetables. I'll preface by saying i'm not a big "spicy" eater anymore...but if you do love spicy (heat spicy and hot spicy), the sichuan pepper corn will F your mouth and taste buds up! BOth times i went, we opted for 50/50 half spicy/half house . We did take out most of the spices in the spicy broth side but it Â still had enough spice. The fried tofu skins are banging, but they sell out real quick. And the waitress suggested we make a reservation and ask them to make it so we have an order in place. We went with the beef combo, $25 i think. It was a big platter of nicely cut and presented beef. the lettuce underneath could also be used in the hotpot. There are some a la carte options. The live shrimp is difficult to cook but delicious. Me and my cousins looked inexperience on our first few attempts cooking it (the shrimp would splash us with broth). So the waitress did eventually show us a tip on how to cook it. I can't give it a full 5 stars because during my first time there, the waitress was pretty rude, even for a chinese restaurant. I will say it was kinda busy that night and it was our first time there, so we weren't sure about the serving sizes so we debated on how many a la carte things to order. HOWEVER, the crazy thing is, the same waitress served me my second time there and she was really nice! ps, takes credit card, clean interior, clean bathrooms.
SO delicious, cheap and friendly. My favorite lunch spot in the LES. I recommend the Siciliano panino (eggplant!)

My friend had wanted to meet up for dinner, so we decided to try this place out. To start, we ordered the empanadas. We thought there might be one with shark meat... we were intrigued. But as we opened the empandas, we only saw chicken, beef, cheese, and... another chicken. What happened to the shark? Our disappointment was short-lived as our arepas came out. My friend ordered arepas with chicken and steak; I had a pork one and the other was just the white cheese. In hindsight, we should have just gotten one each because these arepas were big and packed with a ton of the fillings and flavor. I also added the green sauce because that was amazing. It was like crack. I just couldn't get enough of it. Anyway, the meal itself was mostly good. I would have awarded another star, but the service was kind of slow. It took a while to get our check in the end. Also, I checked in using Yelp and there was a special (50% off!) but they didn't honor it! They said it expired a while ago.

Went here on Halloween night for dinner with two of my friends. The wait time was okay. Read a lot about this place here on Yelp, it has got 4 stars. But, my experience was just 'awful'. Food Experience: I think it's clearly over hyped from my personal experience and my friends agree with me on this. We ordered ROASTED CHICKEN BREAST,HOMEMADE SHRIMP LINGUINE and PAN-ROASTED ORGANIC SALMON. The first two dishes were okay. Nothing special, nothing great. But, the the Salmon dish had two cubes of some meat(may be smoked bacon or ham) mixed with brussels sprouts, toasted pecans and roasted apples, so we called the waiter and told him the same, he wouldn't agree and insist that it's only the fruit. Then the manager comes, explains it wasn't other meat at all and it could be a harder part of salmon itself, which I completely disagree. However, got the dish replaced with a fresh one. Overall, my take on this place is Over Hyped, Super expensive and under par with mediocre service.
this place is fantastic! And as a quick update, if you work within a block or two he will give you free drinks to keep you coming back...what a businessperson!
Yum!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!! That's all for now.

Always a great lunch spot. Cozy up to the bar counter as there are plenty of seats during the lunch hour. Fresh veggie ingredients, great service, and a killer milkshake. I'm a fan of the corn on the cob which has some nice mexican cheese and spices and their field greens go well as a side with the mains. I've had the tomato soup which works well on a cold day and the steak and field greens salad. Filling and healthy. Sandwiches are great as well on their rustic bread which goes with a choice of sweet potato fries. Yum.

It's a rare occurrence when I I decide I will make a return visit, midway through a meal. Friendly staff (always a big win for me), thoughtful timing for when the dishes came out and some amazing food! Â  What we ordered: Deez nutz (complimentary, thank you!) I would never have thought to order this on its own, but man this stuff is addictive. I can see myself ordering this with a few beers. Cashews, spice dusted died cherries and bacon bits with a touch of brown sugar and heat. I was so sad I couldn't finish them because I was so full. Crispy pig ears Crunchy. Very crunchy, and porky. Theres a sweet and vinegary slaw, I think raspberry vingarette. On butter lettuce leaves. This was good, but forgettable for me. A touch sweeter than I would have liked. Smoked boudin noir I adore blood sausage, and they did a bang up job here. There's nothing in the way of fillers so the sausage crumbles (this made me happy). There's bread, honey Dijon mustard, and pickled onions on the side. A piece of sausage on a slice of bread with a bit of the pickles...so awesome. Chicken wings These aren't baby wings (my stomach rejoiced), they're grown up wings that were perfectly juicy and crispy on the outside. It ess finished in some sort of spice/very light dressing that was great, but wish it was slightly stronger. Ribs Tender, smoked dry rub ribs. I will definitely order this again, and not share. I was unabashedly eating with my hands and licking my fingers. I had stars in my eyes. Beignets These were good, but I won't order then again. The coffee/dark chocolate syrup was tasty. The beignets themselves were not what I expected. They were hollow....and I was sad. Otherwise, they were crispy, non greasy and very light. I think I just had different expectations. Bottle of syrah Get this syrah of you like fruit forward, juicy reds. It's called the big mouth. Thank you for a lovely dinner!

Too many other good eats in Chinatown that I wouldn't bother coming back here. Â I had the "crispy" pan-fried noodles w/ beef, and the dish didn't come out as expected. a neighborhood gem...Delicious grilled calimari, fresh salads, Â perfectly prepared risotto, flavorful and balanced pastas, thoughtful and carefully selected wine list at modest prices, and richly chocolate dolci. Cheap food and good, the duck is great.

I like Joy D's review and I agree with her: pro: Â  good food - I especially enjoyed the oysters at the raw bar and the bone marrow dish everyone raves about. My absolute favorite restaurant without question. I discovered this place about a year ago on my first trip to NYC. Marc doesn't screw around, he knows great food. One of the best italian restaurants in all of Manhattan. Fairly resonably priced, it's not super cheap but you won't have to sacrifice rent next month to get a delicious dinner. They have a ton of different pasta choices and their pesto sauce is out of this world!

Good Latin Fusion food, nice portions as well. Â Last time I went there I had to lay on the floor on my back afterwards to digest. Â they have great drinks naturally like the Mojitos etc... Molto bene! Â Outstanding chicken parm. Â I've had it three times now and it's consistently excellent. Â Highly recommend - atmosphere is pleasant, energy feels good - everyone hustles! Â My wife and I LOVE this restaurant.

Delicious!!!!! harira soup - amazing start of meal the tomato and lime opens up the appetite Seafood bastilla - savory puff pastry stuffed with shrimp and squid mouth watering!!! There is always a line outside and a wait. Good thing there is a bar across the street. They will text you when the table is ready. The appetizers is EVERYTHING here. What can I say I love this place. The food is always good . Even if it sounds strange I say try it because nothing they make is bad. never a long wait fantastic service Â Defiantly a place I will be going to for a long time Just be advised it is cash only and in the summer get a peach sangria :-)

Oh, how I missed late night runs to the taco truck in my native Los Angeles, but Brooklyn you've managed to spoiled me yet again. - cheap and delicious!! my two favorites.. so flavorful.. - every few days i try to go without eating meat for a day, which is really hard because i loove my meat... this food defintely satiates my cravings.. - tastes even better than the other place i used to go to.. i will go here instead..

GREAT spot ... the cannibal dogs were above expectations.... the chinese mustard they used was killer, a little like wasabi in terms of the flavor, heat, and nasal sensation. Â  Â Tripe chili and the fried onions & scallions really made this unique. I also had the smoked kielbasa which definitely had a smokey flavor. Â  Really good. The biggest compliment I can give is that I ordered 3 things (broccoli rabe was the 3rd) thinking I would sample a little bit of everything but not finish it all. Â  That didn't happen. Â  I stuffed myself and ate it all because it was so good. The only thing that was disappointing was that the pig face cuban wasn't available for lunch.

long anti-locanda just because i wanted to sneer at another "celeb" (DeNiro) cum-restauranteur, i been holding out to come here for so long and finally did- twice in the space of a week! once for dinner, once for a late afternoon sunday brunch. Â i was very impressed. Â fun, warm, bustling, casual atmosphere. Â service at dinner was terrific, service at brunch not bad but not great. Â i think my experiences amount more to unadulterated satisfaction as opposed to just being surprised that i was not let down... for dinner, we had the crostini wit blue crab, jalepeno and tomato-- delish! the piglet in me just wished there was more to savor than two small pieces to split with my companion for $10. Â  small servings, or at least smaller than most other restaurants, or at least most other italian restaurants, seemed to be a common theme here for every dish but our dessert for two (more on that in a second). Â a serving of pasta at locanda might equal 1/2, or even 1/3 of a dish at il mulino, scalini fideli, or roberto. Â this is not a bad thing (hello, portion control is cool in 2010!!) but just be forewarned! upon my request, our server steered me to try the pasta special for dinner- a classic take on linguini with clams. Â it was fantastic and simple-- fantastic because it was simple. Â the clams were incredibly fresh and wonderful. the dish was mild by design and buttery and light at the same time. we also tried the stuffed mountain trout with castelluccio lentils, and pancetta for $26. Â this is one of the menu's staples and it was fantastic. Â i could definitely eat this again. the trout is cooked but served in a sushi roll style, over what my humble palate will describe as BBQ lentils (always a good thing!). Â this was just wonderful and left us scraping the sauce off the bottom of the plate with the house bread-- buttery focaccia that is puffed lightly and sweet, sparingly garnished with dried rosemary fronds. Â  the only misstep of our dinner (and our server's recommendations, perhaps) was the "chocolate fantasia for two" (a/k/a la fantasia di cioccolata for two --chocolate gelato, marsala gelato, tartufo di cioccolata, marsala caramel, candied chestnuts-- for $16). Â This was delicious and was a chocolate lover's delight, but was simply too much of one thing and became a bit monotonous. Â if interested in two desserts, rather than just splitting one, i would recommend a single serving of this and trying another dessert altogether. Â if getting a single dessert to split, go for the one-serving version, not the "for two" style. for brunch, we again noticed the small portions... not because we wanted larger but because it is unusual in this day and age, it seems to get servings that are the appropriate (and healthy) size. Â  Â Many things sounded (and looked, by roving our eyes to our neighbors' plates) wonderful. Â we settled upon 2 poached egg dishes-- the uovo modenese with cottechino hash, spinach and tomato hollandaise($16) and the "scampi and grits" with organic polenta, tomato, sausage and coddled eggs($17). Â both were just wonderful. Â the hash was flavorful and exhibited complexity in subtle fashion-- was that a touch of cinnamon in it? yum. Â the scampi and grits was lightly doused in a tomato sauce speckled with niblets of sausage bits. the small shrimp were cooked to perfection and had that unmistakable "snap" of off-the-boat freshness, with every bite. Â  the lemon muffin from the pastry menu was out of this world. many other things looked delicious, but we fared well on our first outings! Â i know it has been around, but this is a new favorite place for me now that i've finally gotten on the train!
Genuinely enjoyed the Ramen. The quality and service are great. Be ware of the long wait.

best. ramen. in brooklyn

Perfect,Cute,Amazing Food,Fantastic Bellini's, Great Service,Cute Back Patio=We'll be back, ALL THE TIME!

Been meaning to write this review for some time now. Been there twice. Once for fathers day brunch and another time for birthday dinner. I preferred the brunch. 75% Very good Roquefort cheese-burger ***Short Review Came here for a late lunch in Dec '11 The Chargrilled Roquefort Cheeseburger is solid. The bun, imo, is the best part, but the beef is also great. I think the blue cheese was a bit overpowering. It is strange & inconveniencing that they only serve the burger after 3pm on weekdays. Chicken liver toast is a must, although not for those squeamish about chicken liver. Creme caramel dessert wasn't bad, although not entirely essential. Value is reasonable & prices are moderate. Service was good. Ambiance is charming, but a bit cramped & the acoustics are loud. I don't feel it's the most comfortable dining environment. ***Detailed Review + Chargrilled Burger with Roquefort Cheese & Shoestrings $ 17 (Dish Rating, 78%) Â  yelp.com/user_local_photâ€¦ yelp.com/user_local_photâ€¦ Very good burger overall. Â The burger bun is exceptional. Â The beef patty, and seasoning are very good. Â I loved the thin shoestring fries. Â I felt the Roquefort blue cheese was a bit over-powering, but then again I'm not the biggest fan of blue cheese in general, when used as the only cheese in a burger. Â  The beef patty worked great here. Â The meat is sourced from the excellent 'Pat La Frieda' butcher. Â I wasn't able to find out what meats were used from my otherwise very helpful and attentive waitress. Â However, I doing some research, many have suspect it's a blend of sirloin, chuck, and short-rib. Â I think the meat is grilled. I requested the burger be cooked 'rare' and it seems to have come out that way pretty well. Â The meat is consistently cooked rare, and there is some nice char on the outside. Â Juice levels are at the lower end of moderate. Â It doesn't flood with juices, but the meat is very moist, and I feel the juices certainly lend to some flavor. Â The meat is overall moderately fatty. Â  Flavor-wise, I didn't feel the beef itself had an 'explode in your mouth' level of flavor. Â I think the meat, while very delicious, worked great in a more subtle manner, while having a very balanced level of seasoning. Â It's really something I best enjoyed while savored more slowly. Â Texture of the meat is moderately soft. Â The meat has a nice chewier texture to it, being neither mushy nor difficult to chew. I wasn't a fan of the Roquefort blue cheese. Â On some levels, it worked great. Â It certainly was a very good cheese that I enjoyed, even though blue isn't my typical favorite. Â The cheese was melted very nicely into the patty, almost forming something akin to a butter, and lending the patty a more buttery texture. Â  Some level of restraint was used in terms of the amount of cheese used, and that is a good thing because the flavor of the cheese is quite powerful. Â I felt the blue cheese was already a bit over-powering in flavor, and was the my least favorite part of the burger. Â If the meat was more robustly flavored, or if there were less blue cheese, or even a milder cheese/cheese blend, I think the balance in flavors of this burger would have been more effective for me. Â Then again, this only reflect my bias against blue cheese, and other may feel different depending on how they like the Roquefort. Â For me, the burger worked best when I reduced a bit, around a third, of the blue cheese. The bun is my favorite part. Â It's a brioche bun, toasted on both ends with a prominent char. Â It's a sweeter brioche, and the toasting gives it very prominent char, that lends additional flavor to the overall burger. Â Of course, char on the bread isn't quite the same as char on the meat, but I feel it certainly helps a lot. Â The bread is light, and compresses well. Â It holds the juices nicely without falling apart. Â The dough is quite light, moderately doughy inside. Â The bread to protein ratio is fairly spot on. Â Eating the bread by itself is very enjoyable. Â The chef does an excellent job with any dish that uses bread imo (have enjoyed their chicken liver toast & grilled cheese sandwich a lot in the past). At times I felt as if the burger was also lacking in more sweet flavors to balance out the aggressive blue cheese. Â I felt using a bit of ketchup, also in restraint, helped a lot. Portion size of the burger is about the same as other gourmet burgers, but I felt is was quite heavy and filling. Â  Shoe-string fries are great. Â The cut is very slim (I understand this is also a preference, but I enjoy mine that way), seasoned slightly a tad too aggressive, along with some rosemary herbs. Â They were slightly greasy, but not overwhelmingly so. Â Even though a generous portion was given, I did not feel they were too heavy. Â They're served at a nicely hotter temperature. Â I enjoyed them very much and had no trouble finishing it. Â  Â  Overall a very solid burger, and it's easy to understand why this is one of NY's most acclaimed burgers. Recommend

Food is good but the service is terrible. Â The lady is an Italian wannabe soup nazi and it just doesn't suit her or the ambiance. She's downright rude (not just to me but to most customers) and though the food is good, Â there are so many good Italian options with good service that I won't be back.
