Went here during my recent "Pizza discovery tour " of New York. Â We were in the neighborhood on a Saturday and frankly, there wasn't a lot of open restaurants in the area. Â  By the way it was freezing outside and we didn't want to walk too far. Â Luckily we ducked in here and it was plenty warm from the wood burning oven. Â The staff was wonderful about greeting us and making it authentic in Italian. Due persone, I said and got one of the many available tables for two. Â So they specialize in Pizza and Panini so we tried one of each to share. The food was ok, as my readers know I'm into finding good values. This was good food at full retail price. Â So the food was good, the service excellent the place was warm inside on a cold day outside. Â Only losing one point for not falling into my value category. Â I think the bill came to about just over $32 for two. no drinks.

Finally a restaurant that delivers the goods in Harlem (ok, it's the second one after Cecil, but still I'm legitimately excited since all the other restaurants in this part of town are super sucky - including Red Rooster and the like). BLVD does it with a sweeeeet upgrade on soul food, across the board: the smoked chicken was crunchy on the outside and tender on the inside without being greasy; the ribs were just mouth-meltingly juicy and flavorful (my fav). The creole ketchup for the fried okra was a tad over-salted, but that's piddling. Their wine selection is great too - my pinot noir was top notch. Just one note: consider sitting inside, there may be unwanted guests cramping your style in the outdoors space.

So, so, so, so happy I was finally able to try this place. Â The sushi is a piece of art... prettier than "regular" sushi and the two handrolls I tried were very tasty AND very healthy! Â The flavor combos are creative and unique. Â My only minor complaint is that my mushroom handroll had a bit too much sauce in it that overwhelmed everything else. Â I would like to come back and try all the other stuff though.

This is the spot for those late night cravings when intoxicated. Yep something greasy and good for the stomach. For a taco truck they sure give you good quality that I can still recognize even if I am little drunk, so that says a lot. Love all the toppings and horchata too.

After hydrating with strong happy hour drinks, one gets quite famished for substance of the edible kind. I've passed by this place all the time and have always mentally noted to try it out though I always had the impression it was a wine bar which it obviously is not (they do have a nice wine selection). Everything here was amazing. The food, the service, the atmosphere. We got there on the earlier end of a Tuesday evening so it wasn't busy. I have a gluten allergy and the waiter asked beforehand and totally got it. This is what I got: Heirloom Tomato Salad - The mozzarella on this was so delicious. One of the best we've ever had. Tuna and Hamachi Crudo - This was also really delicious and I absolutely devoured it. This place will not let you down.

ilili is the best mediterranean so far in NY. I was born and rasied in Astoria and their food is nothing I've ever had. What! the brussel sprouts were the highlight of all the dishes we had that night. I rememer as kid how brussel sprouts tasted and never touch them again until now. Wow, I will go back just to have them. And, yes ilili is a beautiful place chic.

I have been here for brunch and dinner many times and the food, service and wine selection are great. Â And the atmosphere is really fabulous . . . there are tall ceilings and open expanses of windows. Â It is especially nice to sit at one of the tall tables facing out of the windows . . . if you get really lucky you may even see the pigeon trainer's pigeons flying (he lives diagonally across the street).

A friend told me that there was only one word to describe Umami Burger. And that word was HYPE. She was 100% on point. Good thing we only waited about 10 minutes for our table of four (it was a Thursday at around 6:30). Not long after we ordered, there was a long line outside. I had the Truffle Burger. To give you a general idea of just how greasy this burger was, think - the oil of five Shake Shack burgers squeezed into this one Umami Burger. (Okay, maybe I'm exaggerating a tad but I think you get the picture). We also ordered the truffle fries, cheesy tots (not on the menu) and the smashed potatoes. CARBS GALORE! Truffle fries were good. Cheesy tots were okay but it only comes with eight dinky pieces so it wasn't really worth it. The smashed potato is literally just a smashed potato. Flavorless and looks like somebody sat on it. If you're in the area and you don't have to wait more than 15 minutes, I would say give it a shot. Anything more than 15 minutes would just be wasting your time.
We've been going to Marc Forgione for over 2 years now. Â The food is consistently delicious. Â The ingredients are so fresh and amazing. Â I could eat there every night. Â A must!!

What a great find! Thank you fellow Yelp members. This is an ideal spot for anyone commuting out of Grand Central Station. A 5 minute walk brings you into another world. It is a bit tricky to find. I was looking for a basement entrance from the street. I ordered a dish of duck with scallions. I am no expert on Japanese cuisine but the flavor of that duck was.....well it's all it's quacked up to be! The small serving size was not what I' m accustomed to so I had to savor every bite. They have a huge sake selection but unfortunately I also have some serious driving ahead of me. Hopefully next time I'll be able to try some sake. So glad I found Sakagura!

I was so excited to brunch here. Usually, it ends up being Frankie's 457 for brunch, since they open a little later (at 11) and the prices are more reasonable. And hey-- Frankie's never lets me down. But one morning, my parents were in town, so I met them + my brother and his wife at Buttermilk Channel for brunch. And we got a table immediately, because we were extra timely. And again-- I was so excited for this food. Everyone talked it up /so/ much. And it just wasn't that great. The French Toast was sickeningly too sweet, like couldn't eat it too sweet... And we love french toast. The pancakes were just okay. The corned beef hash was just okay. Here's what was really interesting, was when my boo ordered a cappuccino... And the waitress brought him what I could only describe as a shot of poorly-tamped espresso made in an older, imperfectly cleaned/maintained machine, and then with positively scorched milk just lumped on top. That's not a cappuccino. But we would've let that slide-- especially since, upon hearing the milk burning in the tin, we both turned around, and saw that our server was preparing the drink; not a real barista. But no.... Because when the server brought it over, she didn't just set it down in front of him, and sheepishly sulk away, embarrassed by the steaming cup of crap she'd just placed before a guest. She actually had the nerve/ disillusionment to loudly proclaim upon serving the drink "This is like the best cappuccino I've ever made, it's sooo good!!!" .... My boo just laughed, and I flatly said, "Really? Because it's definitely not a cappuccino." And the server just kinda seemed confused and smiled and walked away. HIRE A BARISTA IF YOU'RE GOING TO CHARGE SO MUCH FOR POORLY PREPARED ESPRESSO DRINKS, AND YOUR SERVER IS GOING TO TRY AND RECEIVE ACCLAMATION FOR SAID-CRAPPY DRINKS. In the meantime, we will leave the ridiculousness for the masses and stick to Frankie's 457!

Easily my new favorite bar in Bushwick. Avoid the art douchery of tandem, the tropical vomit spewage of Bossa Nova Civic Club. Get some well thought-out cocktails, or no frills drinks in a cozy setting, and enjoy ridiculously delicious cajun food while you do it. Seriously. I had the shrimp sliders w/ tarragon..outrageous. And you can never go wrong with the Boudin Balls. Tchoup Shop knows where it's at.

We ordered 2 vegetarian platters and they gave us one piece of bread. We kindly asked the waiter for another piece of bread to go along with the other platter and he refused! We called the manager over and he said, "I don't care if you order one hundred platters, we will not give you another one!" What kind of service is this? To make a statement like that when each platter is supposed to be accompanied by one piece of bread is ridiculous. Terrible service, terrible attitude.
Cool place wit a great, but limited brunch. The coffee is killer and the eggs are cooked perfectly. Our large party of 8 - all newbie, local New Yorkers - said we would definitely come here again!

Don't you hate when you have to contradict your best friends on tasteful choices? SORRY, ANTHONY!!! I went out o a limb to try this place for the first time, courtesy of my mother (yes, my mother, knowing full well this place has been reviewed by my mid-twenties to early thirties friends) who was craving a burger so badly that she was willing to walk from Sunnyside Skillman to 30th Avenue Astoria, competing with the other nouveau chic choices surrounding us (Bare Burger, for one, is only a block away from Sweet Afton). Let's put it this way- It was so damned good that I just got in the house but 5 minutes ago, threw off my shoes, and flipped open my laptop to jot down these essentials before they wither away in my thought-crazy mind: To address but only ONE negative, if you order the burger and you like medium rare, try to order it rare because the cook over-estimated the cook time. Other than that, she had a gruyere burger with butterlicious rolls, and Brooklyn Bomb Brand McClure's Pickles Â which made me not want ketchup. UH, what!? A burger without ketchup is like a pb and j without the Jam- kinda empty unless you have a great base. I had the salt& pepper spare ribs with emat that fell off the bone when I picked it up. This is exactly what I look for in my ribs. Coleslaw was also interesting and tasty. Note, I hate mayonnaise, so since it was made of vinegar, mustard seeds, coriander, and some kind of unidentifiable spicy aftertaste, I was very pleased. Ambiance: Perfectly dim lit with a "Date" section in the back, I'd like to say, and the "see and be seen" popular front. Â Music was not too loud and was mellow enough without putting me to sleep. Decors was rustic and the benches and booths were simple but comfortable. Service: Just right. People: Not pretentious. Not raunchy. Not gauche. Conversational, good looking, and my neighborhood friendly. I am definitely returning... with people I can have about 5 Lagunitas Pilsners with. OH YEH! Not a wide selection of booze, but they were all my top-choice wines, drafts, interesting cocktail concoction,and HOME MADE ROOT BEEER!! DELICIOUS. Sweet Afton, thank you for making my Sunday night a sweet delight.

The french toast was one of the best I had in the city. and my friend who was visiting fell in love, and now she wants to go back all the time! the service was friendly, attentive, and overall a wonderful experience.

Cannot imagine this place being any better. In fact, cannot imagine a better restaurant, period. I (finally) got onto the Top Chef train a few months ago, and started watching the first season. My boyfriend made dinner reservations for us as a Christmas gift for that reason...and I was not disappointed. Service was remarkable, from the moment we walked in until we had finished our last bite and were out the door. Friendly, accommodating, perfectly attentive and helpful without being overbearing. ...And the food. We split the garganelli and the mustard green salad appetizer. The pasta was incredible, but the salad arguably more so, simply because we were so surprised at how fantastic and articulate a salad could taste. We were sad to finish the plates. For entrees, I had the cod and he had the kingfish...both fantastic, simple, but complex flavors. I can't even describe; you just need to try them. Dessert was apple panna cotta and a chocolate peanut butter mousse. Again, phenomenal. After finishing this meal, we made an agreement -- cook more at home and eat out less during the week, so that we can afford to eat at Perilla (or other restaurants this good) more often. Consider this my New Year's resolution. Thank you, Perilla, for a truly exceptional meal.

I was not overly impressed with this place. The rotating cocktail menus are pretty cool, but there was only a selection of four when I got here. Yea, they were pretty good tasting, but nothing special. The wine in a water glass was a little weird, guys could have classed it up a little for that, wine glasses are like six for $2.99 at IKEA. The place does get very loud, but I think its pretty decent if you are in the area with a few people and want to hang out for a bit. Have not tried the food, but would come back to give it another shot.

One thing I had to try was the classic New York cheesecake and Junior's was ranked as one of the top dogs for it! We decided to come here for a late night dinner after we watched Phantom of the Opera down the block. My friend and I ordered a Rueben, a Steakburger, and a slice of the original cheesecake. In general, the food was pretty good. The meat in my burger tasted slightly bland, but the mushrooms were very flavorful so it offset the blandness of the steak. Onion rings were too dough-y also. Food is not that amazing...but the real reason we came here, was for the cheesecake. Â The strawberry cheesecake got really really good reviews, but we opted for the original. It was good. I'd definitely have to try the other flavors next time I come back. Staff was super friendly, too (as I have encountered way too many rude people during my stay in the Big Apple....) So props to them!

Went last night (Saturday) and although told 1/2 hour wait it was quicker. Â We ordered our food really hot and were not disappointed. Â Started with the Pork/Crab roll - I liked the crunchy fried outside but the pork overwhelmed the crab to the point that they should have left the crab out. Â We had some beef dish, can't remember the name that was so tasty and delicious. Â Then red snapper with basil chili sauce - so often this sauce is just too sweet but this was a delectable crispy fish with a sauce that wasn't cloyingly sweet. Â  I didn't experience bad service but I am also not a diner that needs my waiter to come sing me kumbaya. Â The guy brought our drinks right away and the food came out lighting fast. Â Our water was refilled - which was mandatory with the hot hot food. Â So nothing to complain about there. Â  I actually didn't mind taking the 7 out to Queens.

I went to Ward III thanks to a handy little app called Urban Daddy. I was staying at the Millenium Hilton with my boyfriend in the Financial District and needed to find a place that was relatively close so that I would not have to deal with the intense thunderstorm of this ridiculously windy, wet night. Ward III. "Sounds a lot like Drink in Boston," I thought. Said boyfriend and I hailed a cab and went on our way. I was relieved to see that it wasn't some gaudy and pretentious looking bar, but a small little venue that would be easily missed had we not kept our eyes peeled. The place was a little too loud for my taste, as I was just looking to go to a place where I could drink and canoodle (in a socially appropriate way) with my boo. But Ward III was poppin' and I couldn't hate on that. When it's good, the folks will flock. The place had a nice ambiance that seems typical of most bars like this: low, pale yellow lights, hints of red (throw in a brick wall in there and you're good to go) and dark wood, dark corners and odd looking, sometimes abstract pieces of art hanging somewhere. I ordered the Tortuga and was instantly in heaven. Nothing like ginger, citrus and rum to get my heart pumping! I then dared to see what kind of concoction they would come up with when I asked for "something bubbly, something cinnamony and nutmegy, yet something that goes down smooth. I want something that warms me up inside (that's what she said), and cools me off. Oh, and throw in some apple." I was waiting for the bartender to look at me and say, "no, you picky betch," but he nodded sweetly and served me something that had it all. When a bar can cater to my particular needs and make my taste buds tingle with joy, I'm all about it. I'm a bit disappointed in myself that I didn't try the food. Maybe next time I'm in the city. :)

I live in California and the whole farm to table thing is big here. It is nice to see it in New York too. I do wonder where these farms that operate in the dead of winter are. Anyway, the food was excellent. The french fries were the best every. Our vegetable appetizers were also exceptionally good. Our server was helpful and prompt, although the hostess seemed to take longer than a "few minutes" to seat us. We waited about 45 minutes on a Monday night for a table of three around 8:30. Be prepared to wait. The wine list was also extensive and even though I didn't get to try any of the cocktails they looked very intriguing. It was a bit pricey and I wonder what percentage of families in the neighborhood would be able to afford eating at such an establishment. It would be cool to see a place like this bring their food philosophy into the community by giving back some how.

not sure how this particular cart became so much more popular than the rest of the other dozens of halal food carts..but hey, im not complaining..there's a certain novelty to lining up at 3am behind 20 other people for a solid foil plate of rice+chicken+white sauce goodness. I'm usually not a fan of street food Â but there's just somethng about this place!

This is the place to go for great pizza Napoletana. Â Being a NY area native that lived for a bit in Italy, I don't say that lightly! Â The calzones are also delicious. Â We were able to split one large pie and one calzone between three people for an early dinner. You can tell the ingredients are fresh and the service was attentive and prompt. Â The atmosphere inside is lovely- very nicely done in a casual way. Â Also, there is unlimited iced coffee refills, a rarity in NY!
Please do yourself a great favor. Ask for Brooks. An amazing server. Makes a great Martini. His suggestions where on the money. Thank you for our Brooktinis.

This review is based off the VEGGIE DUMPLINGS ONLY, 8 for $2. um, well.. I hate to say this, Vanessa's are better but a buck more. These dumplings had some type of undefinable cabbage type substance within, whereas Vanessa's filling is cooked and definable. Â This place is a 10x10 hole with 5 stools. Not bad, I do agree with Elle P, the dumplings are a 3* but the shear cheapness of it all bucks it up a star. I'm gonna go back for the Veggie Pancake.

This place is amazing. They have the best buns around. When we went in the fall they had duck buns, served with little pickled cucumbers and homemade sauce. Also, we had fried duck wings, served with this mango compote I believe. SO delish. Everything we have had here is so good- full of flavor, beautiful plating and delish. We always go in the morning right when they open so we never have to worry about the crowd.

Spritzenhaus is a large north Williamsburg beer hall, similar to the south Williamsburg beer hall Radegast. There is not much different between the two; both have a selection of brats and creative sausages, long bench seating, and a decent selection of beer, wine, and spirits. However, Spritzenhaus has that fantastic central fireplace, and on a raw October evening, there is nothing more cozy than sipping some wine, chomping some double-fried French fries, and smelling the wood burning in the night.

The paratha was so light and crispy, I loved it. The whole kati roll itself? I've had better, but that's not to say these aren't good. The achari paneer roll was great. The unda roll was actually kind of cold when served, and the eggs were slightly overdone. The amount of chutney made the rolls a little soggy. I still loved the chutney itself, the flavors of both rolls were delicious, and the portion size was perfect. I recommend getting two rolls; they have deals for ordering in twos. The line was to the door, but it moved quickly. Although there's limited seating, people here eat and go, so a table will probably free up while you wait in line. The service was super friendly. I'll still miss my Spice End kati rolls in Philly, but these will definitely do while in NY.
Busiest restaurant during afternoon. I used to work at the midtown manhattan, this is the cheapest place for lunch break and good tasty food!

Made our way to the back of the bar at 6pm on a Friday and there were two stools waiting for us. The bartender made me a lovely, close to perfect negroni and hubby had a manhattan. Two cocktails and a standard hamburger later we tried to close our and the new bartender was real pissed we didn't already have a tab open. We left an otherwise fun couple of hours with a bad taste in our mouths from his attitude. Maybe it was part of the Old NY era Irish swag, but it'll be awhile before I venture back.

What a jem to have in the neighborhood! Tried the cabbage, collards, cornbread, traditional fried wings, yams, and mac and cheese and everything was delish! The potato salad and sweet potato pie were my favs, hands down. It's so good, I've been there twice this week. And Mrs. Napoleon is a sweetie. #adownhomespot

Four of us went to Barbuto on Tuesday night. Â The restaurant was busy and full of excitement. Â It created a fun atmosphere for us. Â The menu was very interesting and provided a variety of options. Â Two of us had the cauliflower salad (Crudi), which was heavenly. Â It is hard to tell how they are able to transform a cauliflower into a tasteful work of art. The flavors of the ingredients mixed together perfectly and the portion was very generous. Â One member of our group had the risotto which was prepared with ramps and asparagus. The serving was also very generous and provided plenty to pass around the table. Â For our main course we ordered, gemellicon salsiccia, jw chicken, cod (merluzzo arrosto), and pork loin (filletto di maiale). Â All of the courses were wonderful with the filletto di maiale and the merluzzo arrosto being standouts. We felt no rush during dinner and our server was attentive and knowledgable about the menu. We would definitely recommend this restaurant to others.

Every year, I go on two double dates to celebrate my dearest friends' birthdays at New York's great new eateries. In February, we celebrated Amber C. and myself at Battersby. In April, we celebrated Maddie O. and Kyle L. at Xixa. Perhaps the best double double date of all time. I highly recommend the tasting menu, which is a great deal at $40 for the number of courses, range of ingredients and fantastic flavors. The cocktail list is fun and sectioned off by famous ladies throughout history. I ordered a Cleopatra cuz we're both the shit.

Food is DELICIOUS. Drinks are very strong and the ambiance is a good mix between a bar and trendy lounge. Our waitress was super nice so was the guy behind the bar. Portions however leave a lot to be desired (especially for the price); which is why I'm giving it a 3. If you're starving, I'd suggest going somewhere else. What I ordered: -Spring Rolls: good, but again tiny portions (one spring roll was the size of my pinky) -Pork Tenderloin: so good; juicy and very flavorful. I wish they'd given more of it. Cabbage + sauce+ pork create a really good blend.

Great late night fast Korean food. Â Tried the beef noodles and it was really good. Â Haven't tried the Korean fried rice but will another time. Â Great prices especially when many places are closed. Â Open till 3 a.m.

Go on Saturday so you can get the Lamb Shortribs. SO YUMM!!!! We started with the Prosciutto, Coppa Cotta, Broccoli Rabe and Octopus. I NEVER like broccoli rabe because it's so bitter, but it's done really well here and prepared nicely to take away the bitterness. All other starters were tasty too, though the octopus was kind of tuna-y. As for the main course, we got the Pork Shoulder, Market Fish (Stripe Bass that night), Gnocchi, Oxtail and the fatty, juicy, delicious Lamb. Overall, it was a tasty meal with really great wine and such a great atmosphere. I LOVE LOVE Babbo, but it can be a little stuffy there. Lupa is much more laid back and lively with a more favorable bar area... and CHEAPER! :o)
The service wasn't great but the food was reasonably cheap.

I LOVE this place. The food, vibe, drinks just the ambiance- all awesome. Never disappoints. The chefs selection for appetizers is really good. Keeps you wanting more. The portions are a good size. I usually order the skirt steak. Rice, steak, fried egg on top and sweet plantain. Delicious! My fiancÃ© usually orders the paella and loves it. The only thing is that they could use a wider selection of tequilas. It's a Spanish spot but other than that always a good time. Also has a lounge area with comfy sofa/seats.

Sweet Afton is the bar that dreams are made of. They have a very small menu but this is for good reason as all of your choices are unbelievable. The staff is awesome here, real cool folks. I had the brunch burger which was top of my list for anywhere and the fried pickles were amazing. The macaroni and cheese was the real deal but share it with a friend it's got some intense cheese action happening. I also got a ommegang witte cocktail which had gin witte beer, OJ and ginger. I could have drank a million of these and after I left here tipsy and full, I Â think I might have. Can't wait to come back to NYC just to hit up Sweet Afton again!

On one of my many trips to Bonnie's I was completely blown away by my meal. Usually my girlfriend and I stick to the usual awesome wings but this time something on the Specials Menu just caught my eye. The Wild Boar was perfectly seasoned and just so flavorful with every single bite. The waiter recommended a draft Four Point Toasted Pilsner which complimented the sandwich well. Â After wiping the plate clean I could not wipe the Smile off my face!

Hand pulled noodle was very decent. Â This place may have the best hand pulled noodle in NYC. Â Dumpling wasn't as good as I expected, or more like it wasn't my favorite kind of dumpling with thin skin and a lot of leek. Â Very good spot to stop by if you are in the area

I figured while I was in the land of Yelp yelping for place in NYC I had to mention this one. My esthetician said her sis took her here, and when I looked it up on Yelp it had good enough reviews to try it out. It may be tiny as all sh*t and the lines are hella long, but the pizza is drool over, orgasmically, good. Now being born and raised in Los Angeles, maybe I don't hold pizza to a high standard, but what the hell is wrong with all you yelpers saying this place is 3 stars? DO YOU EAT PIZZA? Geez. All NY pizza is good to me, but this place is worth the wait in line during a snow storm. Â It also is nice that is is right by the rice pudding place. Mmmm I want the stuff now! Gooey. Crusty. Mmmm...
had a great dinner there with friends. Â just go there and you will not be disapointed

My boyfriend and I come here all the time. The owner is great and the wine/beer is all amazing. They have seasonal beer to try and a great happy hour. The food is possibly a bit lacking, but that's maybe to be expected. The ambience is really cozy and wonderful too.

This place was not at all worth it. We waited on line for a table for over an hour and were seated by the meanest, most impatient man who made our entire experience really terrible. He actually yelled at us multiple times for no reason. The pizza was good--but that's the great thing about New York--we actually have good pizza at lots of places. And I can tell you at most other places the host doesn't make patrons feel like crap. This place is totally skipable.

Oh schnap is the hot sauce hot hot hot! I only put one tiny drop on my falafel sandwich and my mouth was burning during the rest of my dinner. ...and they offer a bottle of that for purchase...idk if that's just death or what. Either way, if you're one of those people who find regular hot sauce a breeze through the park and are on the search for the sauce that will compromise your taste buds, here ya go. You have been warned. Regarding the falafel, I have to say it was pretty good! However, it's on par (but not better) than Falafel's Drive In in San Jose, CA. I also love how on the menu, they describe what's in each of the menu items, makes it clear for those with allergies or for those who simply didn't know what falafels are made of (but now I know!). I tried their baklava, and it's one of the best ones I've tried! The honey oozes out in every bite, and each layer is so flaky and yummy mmmm. Def worth a stop when on Macdougal. It's easy to miss when trying to spot it, but hard to miss as it is open til 5 AM, so chances are it will be open when you want to head over and try it. Makes me feel bad for that other falafel store right across the street...that place had no customers!

I've been to Dos Toros twice. The first time I went was right when they opened and I was so completely underwhelmed. Really? A slice of cheese pressed onto the tortilla? Guac from a squeeze tube? For the same price as Chipotle, I was not impressed. But everyone ranted and raved about how good it was and I thought, maybe they just didn't get all the kinks worked out. So I stood on the line, out the door, and gave the basic burrito another shot. This time I was way impressed! Maybe not the best burrito I've ever had, but definitely tasty. I also very much appreciate their attempts at being earth-friendly - compostable utensils and greenware cups (I think that's what they are called)! But then today I read a terrible article - the rice is actually made with chicken stock! It's a vegetarian faux pas! And in the article, the owner is quoted as saying, "at least we tell people, some people don't" - but the menu (I double checked on their website) specifically says "no meat" next to the basic rice and beans option. So Dos Toros - you could have had the chance to become one of my favorite spots, but now I literally can't come back. Le sigh.
Please oh please oh please come to the uws pretttttty please!

In my opinion, this place is one of the worst sushi/Japanese experience of my life. It's not a place where I would visit again. Surprisingly though, it was packed when we dined last night. Sorry, it's just 2** s for you.

Cheap, delicious, and filling. We ordered the beef stew and big wonton soup with shanghai noodles (I'd recommend getting the shanghai noodles if you want a thicker noodle) and the roasted duck with wonton noodle soup. The wontons were very good, flavorful and huge. The beef stew was tender and came with a generous portion of beef chunks. The duck was good as well. Load it up with some hot sauce and you've got yourself a delicious meal. We paid $17 after tip and tax.. so cheap! The service was meh.. we didn't have any problems because we spoke canto and didn't as any questions but I did see a waiter raise his voice at and act pushy to a Caucasian lady who sat near us. If that happened to me, I'd drop my rating to a 3.

I've been here a few times.Try Sliders, steak and sea bass. It's good for people who are not that hungry because everything comes in smaller portions of three. But if you order sliders, that's enough for one person *:) Â Try their special popcorn prior to your order (something they give you before your meal). That's a must try snack! *:) Â Enjoy!

this place is awesome. Â food is super tasty and what a fun menu! Â we have gone here every week since they have opened. Â honestly everything i have tried here is great...all stars include the fried pickles, chicken sandwich with honey and pickles, biscuits with two types of gravy and the mac and cheese is delicious. Â although the menu is all about comfort, the food is not soaked in oil and you don't leave here feeling guilty about the meal you just had. Â the only thing i do wish for is for them to put a side of something green on the menu...side salad or steamed brocoli with my fried chicken and fried pickles would round out every amazing meal i have had here!

Brooklyn pizza at its finest! I love this place, Â the service is always good and the food is even better! My favorite is the zucchini and eggplant pizza so delicious! Its thin crust pizza with so much flavour from the dough to the tomato sauce to the toppings. Also, a must try is the nutella dessert! Warm and damn good! Love this spot! There's a bar, dinning room and outdoor seating for any type of night you decide to have :) Enjoy!

This just might be one of the best meals I've ever had for 6 bucks. Â I ordered the mixed platter of chicken and lamb over rice without the lettuce. Â Extra white sauce which is delicious as most have mentioned in the other reviews. Â I was only in town for 2 days and I made the walk to this location twice. Â  It's that good! Â  They are fast as far as service. Â The food is just divine. Â The red sauce they give on the side is pretty hot and tastes great in small amounts. The dish it self tasted amazing. Â The chicken is shredded and mixes really well with the lamb meat crushed up like ground beef. Â Mix that in with the white sauce and rice , is just amazing! Â  Will come back every time I'm in NYC.

a great example of how service can make a 4 star place a 5 star place. Â came here for brunch the weekend. Â we were seated immediately (first to arrive at 10 am!) and within minutes we had steaming hot coffee at the table. Â  our orders were taken quickly and the food was brought out steaming hot- chicken and waffles for my plus one and the pulled pork with eggs and home fries for me. both were delicious. we ordered the pecan bourbon pie for dessert and it was absolutely amazing. Â when our waiter dropped off our bill, he placed a small take out container on our table. Â turns out they gave us a piece of their pumpkin pie, complete with a side of whipped cream just because. we can't wait to come back and try the chicken and biscuit with a side of cheese grits. Â a true neighborhood gem.

The only trouble here is having to make a decision on their extensive menu. Â While huge, it offers so many different, flavorful dishes. Â While they vary in size, you're never wrong to get at least 2 a person and share EVERYTHING. Their scallops and steak (rare, thank you very much) are my favorites. Â Most of their other dishes are a close follow up, like the brussel sprouts. Â  The ambience is nice, though the third floor (yes, it's hidden away) was quite warm compared to the other dining area. Â The staff is cordial, and relatively quick. Â You don't wait too long for your food, and while you DO wait, you've got some great red sangria in your hand, so who cares! Â  Great tapas place with its own signature in every dish!
Delish says it all
Deeeeericious

BEST BAR-B-QUE IN NEW YORK CITY! I use to go to their one 125th street location constantly when I was a kid. It was always super packed, and it took hours to get a table, with good reason this place has the best Bar-B-Que i've ever tasted. I recently came back to Dino BBQ but this time I visited their new location in Gawanus and the food was the so smoky, Â so flavored, so perfect! I ordered the BBQ brisket chopped melt with the side order of Mac and Cheese, and my friend ordered the BBQ brisket BBS. Both orders were delicious. We immediately fell in love with the Mac and Cheese, it was cream, cheesy, and of course a bit spicy! It reminded us of our favorite Mac and Cheese, and we considered this one a better candidate. New favorite Mac and Cheese! The BBQ brisket chopped melt tasted great, I love the combination of the sweet with the smokey brisket, the meet was perfectly tender. The blue cheese on the BBS was amazing, it gave it a different flavor but was still a perfect fit for the dish. I can't explain how great these tasty sandwiches feel on your taste buds! Going back to union to avoid the long line on 125th even though i live closer to that one! This place deserves more then 5 stars :)

Just a great, special little place in the East Village. Really reasonably priced tasting menus are fun and varied. I don't love communal tables, but when I've gone it hasn't been packed. Mood is good, staff is very friendly and laid back. If you are looking to spend $50-70/head and have a cute date where you'll really like the food this is my suggestion. Another good option that is comparable is Monument Lane in the West Village.
Amazing delicious food and cool atmosphere. Cheapest food and amazing portions. Live musuc on Sundays make it a great date spot too.

It was super-easy to get a reservation via yelp, and we were seated right away. What I didn't count on was my friend not really being interested in anything I wanted to order and vice versa - since everything is family-style and intended for 2-3 people, we could only order one dish. We settled on penne with broccoli, olive oil and garlic. It arrived very quickly, pretty much covered in a layer of broccoli with very little olive oil, garlicky, and al dente, just the way I like it. It was too bland for my friend ... but oh well. You can't please everyone. The order was huge and it broke our heart to leave so much on the plate, but we couldn't take away leftovers. I let her choose the dessert and she opted for the tiramisu, which was wonderfully creamy. I'd definitely come here again, except with a larger party (at least 4).
Nothing is better on earth than dinner at FISH. I love my oyster special with beer. I go to this place so often, i'm afraid soon they'll ask me to pay rent Â :) ha ha!!

Love this place! Actually have never been there for brunch, but always love to hide away for a quiet dinner. Â Everything is always perfect. We were actually inspired last year after a conversation with the owner to return to Paris for New Years! We had enough good wine and conversation that we went straight home and booked the trip. We will definitely try the brunch when the spring comes:)
Yummy clay pot fried rice! It was a hit for our first visit here. Nice staff and decor. For the second visit, still felt the same thing for the service, the duck isn't ideal.

What a unique spot. First time I have ever been offered a bound book full of drink choices. I loved the taste of punch we were offered upon being seated at the bar upstairs. Ours was lemony, jenever based. I couldn't quote the other ingredients except to say there were at least five more of them. From there, my friend and I each had three more drinks each (I think?). The only one that wasn't to my taste was Hunter--for me it tasted too strongly of anise, but that's just one person's opinion. We also had some delicious bar snacks: sausage roll, Scotch eggs and miniature shepherd's pie. Around 8 on a Saturday night, a pianist started playing ragtime tunes which added greatly to the sense that we were in another time and place.

I like Bobby Flay and was really looking forward to dining at his newest restaurant Gato. Unfortunately I was a bit disappointed in my dinner here. I tried a number of dishes however nothing was all that memorable or remarkable. To start we ordered some bar bites which included the burrata, eggplant, and lamb. Of the three, the eggplant was the best however was a bit undercooked and slimy in consistency.The burrata was nice and served chilled with a touch of balsamic vinegar but an extremely small portion. The lamb was also a tiny portion and though tender it was nothing exciting. Appetizer wise we ordered the scrambled eggs and the octopus.The octopus was cooked perfectly however the flavors were a bit mild for my taste. The scrambled eggs that were raved about in reviews were good but didn't live up to the hype. For entrÃ©es I had the kale and mushroom and artichoke paella. This dish was also highly recommended but I was not a fan. It was quite greasy, the artichokes felt a bit out of place, and the amount of rice was too sparse in comparison to the vegetables. Overall the meal was not bad per se, but nothing stood out that made me want to try anything else on the menu. The space is very pretty though and service is friendly, knowledgeable, and attentive. Nice to sit and enjoy the scene but the food does not live up to expectations.

Good food, mediocre service. I came here for brunch and was pleasantly surprised by their smoked salmon omelette. It was pretty much like a lox bagel, but in omelette form. Eggs and smoked salmon covered in cream cheese? I'm a fan! Be sure to grab a glass of their freshly squeezed orange juice to kick off your morning.
The food may be ok but the staff are rude and arrogant.
Had one of the best meals in many years here. Tried a few things on the menu. The lemongrass tofu, shaking beef, and the eggplant were stellar. The Napa cabbage was also amazing!
Great service from Doris, she was super friendly and helpful! The food was incredible--especially the goat cheese empanada and the arroz com pollo. Delicious mango margarita as well!

Was in the mood for tacos tonight. Decided to try this place out finally. Brought 1 steak and 1 pork taco plus the Mexican corn. The meat for both of the tacos were very tender, fall apart in your mouth tender. The tortillas soft and flavorful. Each taco was topped with a cilantro, onion guacamole Â mixture. The take out box holding the tacos had a slice of lime for extra flavoring. That was all the flavoring that was required for me. Hot sauce wasn't Â needed and if you ask me that is what makes a great taco. The Mexican Â street corn was rather tasty Â the only thing I would probably Â change is the amount of mayo that they Â slather on the corn before adding the cheese. As well as sprinkling the entire cob with chili powder so that it isn't Â lumped into just one section. The corn also comes with a lime wedge. Overall I enjoyed my food. For 10$ hunger was completely satiated. I will return to try the spiked lemonade!

This review is for a Tavern dining experience, since we didn't have time to do the full tasting menu. It's a gorgeous space, with clearly a lot of attention to the details of decor. The bartender was friendly, attentive and helpful. She suggested the Orange Blossom which was nice. $14 nice, I don't know, but otherwise nice. My favorite item ordered was probably the duck liver mousse with the pickled vegetables and grilled bread appetizer--every bite was perfect and the bitterness of the vegetables and crunch of the bread was a great contrast to the rich mousse. It was actually more enjoyable than my entree, the arctic char (dry) with lentils, parsnips and and brussel sprouts (all just average). Dessert was rather forgettable too...I think it was a crumble. I'll have to update this if I ever come back for the full tasting menu. I think it might be a more representative picture of why this place is so highly rated.
Went here for Sunday brunch. Great food, coffee and the service was top notch. Perfect little spot that I will definitely come back to.

This is one of my favorite places to go with friends and eat yummy food. You can taste the care that is placed into every single component of a dish. It is the atmosphere and the food that makes me want to go again and again. The uni linguini and the margarita pizza with and eggs are both outstanding! Don't be nervous non-brooklynites about the neighborhood when you get off the l, you are going to be just fine. Also in the winter Roberta's sets up tents out back and serve spiced wine and cider. It feels like a tiny cozy ski lodge. Go immediately!

AMAZEBALLS 2013. This is the best restaurant in New York City. Maybe the world. They take your allergies very seriously and do not cross-contaminate in the kitchen. The gluten free bread, pizza and pasta is so ridiculously awesome that my friends/family who are fortunate to be able to experience the food spectrum in its entirety say it's better than its gluteny counterpart. The sans-cheese artichoke and spinach pizza is basically like the flavor Olympics in your mouth. Gold medalist. Try the mango margarita, tuna avocado salad and every single desert. All of them. Have two apple pies then chug down a snifter of port. FAAAAAAT KIIIIIIID. You're welcome.

I honestly preferred Kefi's former digs on West 79th, in a cozy little townhouse with a lovely wine-bar upfront. I realize that the move to the current location on Columbus was due to high demand and endless waits at the former location, and I'm happy that in this economy they were able to prosper. The wine list offers a refreshing selection and the nouvelle Greek food is appealing and reasonably priced. For those who prefer to sip ouzo (I don't get it), there's a pretty decent selection. I really like their spin on the Greek salad, and the trio of spreads is a delicious starter. The sheep milk ravioli with brown butter and sage is delicious, their rendition of mac and cheese in its moat-size dish Â was very rich and filling and and my husband thought the pork was bursting with flavor.

My favorite spot in Nyc, my nephew put me on to Pio Pio family style dining. I make a point of going here at least once a month. Best Calamari in the city, order the red Sangria by the pitcher, one glass is not enough. Seafood is great, I make sure I order the Matador Combo and another dish. Inexpensive and classy at the same time. Great staff and great atmosphere. And don't forget to order desert!

I love Shabu Shabu. It is a fun way of sharing food with friends - I enjoy cooking the food while having conversation with people. Moved from San Francisco, I was looking for a place in the City where you can get decent Shabu Shabu. My Japanese hairdresser recommended Shabu Tatsu to me. I decided to give this place a try after reading all the good reviews on Yelp. I made a reservation for a party of four for dinner. This place doesn't give you your own pot, the four of us had to share the same pot . The food is fresh and the service is good, but quite pricey given the small portion. Also, I didn't like the dipping sauce that much. The overall experience is good but I think it is over-priced. Maybe I will try this place for lunch next time as the lunch is supposed to be cheaper.

Is there any way to post a Yelp review of the BQE? God save me in this traffic. Dining at La Sirene reproduces the supreme elegance of dining in the home of a good friend who has impeccable taste in food and tacky marine-themed chachkies. The overtly unpretentious poster art balances the care put into each dish. The goat cheese tart with truffles for example... I wasn't sure if I should eat it, or pet it, it was so adorable. The escargot was begging to be devoured with chunks of fresh french bread. Simply put - this must be one of the quaintest french restaurants in the city. My applause master chef!

This place is pretty hit or miss. On the upside, the falafels are pretty good, as are most of the sides I've tried. Unfortunately that is where the positives end. The hummus is completely bland and the pitas taste like they came from the grocery store. Not particularly friendly service in my experience. There are better alternatives in the area...

I went to visit NY last year, and everyone and their mommas told me about this halal cart. SPECIFICALLY THE ONE ON 53rd and 6th! Hands down they are the best Halal Food cart in NYC. I know this because during my stay in NY, I had those drunk "I need food" after the bar cravings. I went to some of those other Halal carts to try it and also because I felt sorry for them, so I thought I'd give them some business. So I gave the other carts a try but I'm sorry I still feel the same way towards the 53rd and 6th Halal cart! Ooh yeah extra extra white sauce please YUM!
Best in the neighborhood. Not over priced, relaxed and amazing food. I would eat here every night if I could.

This place is well documented so I'm not sure what I'm going to add that 1,500+ haven't already said. The buns and rotisserie duck were on point. Their pickle game was decent also. Only qualm was the backless chair... I'm a sloucher and need that support.
nothing to say. good food at a good price.
I had dinner with the girls on a Saturday night for my birthday. I LOVE the atmosphere! EXCELLENT FOOD, DRINKS AND SERVICE!! Adding this to my list of FAVS!

WE LOVE GAIA!!! We stopped in randomly on a Saturday when she first opened and we have been back multiple times a week ever since. It is by far the best sandwich place in the city and the CHEAPEST! $5 for a sandwich with fresh bread that she bakes there, are you serious?! It's less expensive than fast food and everything is fresh, imported, just amazing. I haven't gotten anything there that I haven't liked, and I have tried pretty much everything on the menu. I'm partial to the Elegante and the Delicioso, but both the meat and vegetable lasagna are delicious as well. I will say though, do not come here if you're in a rush. There's a small staff and the place is constantly crowded, and even if you're getting your food to go it can take upwards of 15 minutes for them to make it.

Came here for Sunday Brunch, arrived around 11:35 (they open at 11:3o) and was the second table to be seated. People continued to come in within the next half hour, and pretty soon the place was filled up. We sat outside in the back, which is enclosed but also has heat lamps - chairs are not particularly comfortable outside, but the natural lighting makes up for it. We shared three of the top dishes I read about on yelp: 1. Chicken n Biscuits with Crispy Apples - a bit disappointing. The chicken was perfectly fried and moist inside, but lacked flavor. Â It came with a nice sauce though that was quite good. Apples were indeed crispy and sweet 2. Blueberry Pancakes - wow. Thick, yet somehow still fluffy with the perfect amount of syrup on top? Corners were crisp. 3. Egg-Cheese-Pork Belly Sliders - OMG. Heaven. Heaven. Heaven. The orange juice was very delicious, and they do unlimited coffee refills. Now preferably you show up later than 11:30am so I don't have to wait in line. Thanks. And thanks J. for driving me out to Williamsburg for this delicious meal.

being a little hung over from last night and having friends staying in w'burg made it the perfect opportunity to try Marlow and Sons for late breakfast/lunch. i had a damn good bloody mary (why does the hair of the dog work, anyway?). Â we also ordered the basket of sweets and the scone was a little dry but the jelly on top made it delish. the sticky bun was good too. i think i tried the donut and i think it was good. then i had the pannini of cheese and raddichio which was really hot and kinda greasy, but it was kinda just what i needed since i woke up a tad slow and stupid. the service was nice and friendly, the place was so hip it hurts. and band of horses was playing on the stereo. which is kinda funny cause of the spot and all.

Apparently, I live under a rock because I had never heard about Di Fara before and I've been in New York for almost five years. Â  My friend lives close by and she kept insisting that we had pizza. In all honesty, I wasn't really in the mood for mediocre pizza and I wanted to sit down for dinner, but somehow he convinced me. From the outside, it looks like any other pizza place and I wasn't too empresses. After five minutes of waiting in line and finally shutting my mouth, it hit me "Wait, why are we in line?? Â There is no one inside!!". The man in front of me and my friend quickly filled me in about the place while waiting in line. Truth be told, I was relieved to find out that this place had really great pizza and it wasn't your average place. We finally got in and I realized that they only take cash and the slices were $5 each. In all honesty, it's pointless to just have one slice. Definitely go for the pie and bring some cash. In the end, it will be cheaper and you'll have more. I had one cheese slice and I wolfed it in seconds! The crust was just the right size and tomato sauce didn't taste like can! Also, I noticed the pizza wasn't overly greasy like most of the pizzas in NY. The combination of the cheese was delicious. Overall, it was great freaking pizza! The only down side is that if you are planning to sit down here, it will most likely NOT happen. It's really small and barely has any sitting area. I plan on visiting again but to pick up a couple of pies and pick up some beer and bring it up to my friends place.

Damn you for preying on my drunk ass last night. Â I don't know what's in that white sauce (crack, possibly?), but the combination of everything on my plate was a party in my mouth. Unfortunately, the party turned into an all-out brawl in my stomach, but still TOTALLY WORTH IT.

Don't be fooled by the title -- this isn't actually a diner. Rather, it's a more upscale take on traditional diner food, and thus, the prices are higher than you'd expect from your typical greasy spoon. We made that mistake, but the staff was so welcoming and genuinely happy to seat us that we couldn't bring ourselves to leave. If you're a dirty martini fan, you've absolutely got to try their jalapeÃ±o dirty martini, made with vegetable pickle brine. I went the boring route and ordered their burger, which was cooked exactly how I ordered it, but I'd be interested in giving their other items a try next time I'm in the area.
Love the cheesecake! Burgers are great too but the onion ring suck... Big portion size.

The service at this place was amazing. I threw a bday dinner party there and they were very accommodating. I showed up 30 minutes late and with about half of my reservation and they sat us immediately. The food was awesome. We ordered all appetizers and the entrees were delish. I had the suckling pig which was to good but I also taste the beef ribs which were outstanding. Our waiter started out a little on the rough side but he warned up to our table quickly. At the end, the owner gave our party a glass of champagne to celebrate. This place set the mood for an awesome night. Thank you so much.

Who knew ramen could be $12 a bowl? (Lucky for me I didn't pay.) I like how they put us in the cozy, cozy couple seats though we were not a cozy, cozy couple. Way to make assumptions! Mmm. Wait... where did the pork belly go?

Came here with friends (party of 5) on Friday night. the place was packed highly recommended: Vietnamese Ice coffee, already sweet without the sweetener. Crispy pork belly appetizer, it has a crispy skin and juicy inside. Seafood Pad Ped, very delicious! Pad Thai and Basi fried rice were okay, not as unique as the appetizers. service was good. price was reasonable. if you don't make a reservation, be ready to wait, though.

I met friends at ilili last night at 8 PM and it was crowded... a testament to their food and service. There are several rooms and two floors full of tables... the low lit, high ceilings, and warm decor provide the perfect ambiance for a group dinner or date. The eggplant appetizer and brussel sprouts with grapes are both must have starters. I am always a fan of the duck schwarma, the meat melts in your mouth-- don't be deceived that it's served in a paper-wrapped pita cone and meant to be eaten with your hands, well worth it. The wait staff were attentive and helpful. I've been many times and can't wait to go back!

I came here with a party of 6 for a friend's birthday. We had a great time and the food was excellent. I am drooling thinking about it. The meat and cheese plates are delicious, though a little pricey. The steak tartare is awesome. I got the wild boar pasta and loved every bite. Is it gauche to lick the bowl? We wracked up a giant bill (I am talking over 500 bucks ACK!) but we got about three appetizers, 6 entrees and a ton of drinks. The cocktails are a steep 10-13 bucks each, but if you aren't a bunch of drunks like we are you probably won't get into the same predicament.

I want to give this place 4 stars but the last time I ate there where so many flies in there I couldn't finish my food. Â I do not know how a place could operate under health codes with so many flies. Â It was just beyond anything I had ever seen at any place with indoor or outdoor seating. Â There is no possible way that they could keep them out of the kitchen. gross

i've visited this place 2 times during my last few visits to nyc. i have to admit, this is one of the best rustic italian places i've been to. Â prices are reasonable, good service, and excellent meat dishes. Â  favorite dishes: mortadella with pistachios and paprika (i've been searching for something comparable here in sf), bucatini, and fried polenta. Â  i do appreciate how they put a glossary of the obscure food terms (like tripe and such) on the back of the menu. Â i wish they did the same for their obscure wine list.

Good service....attentive. Â Both had the Bar Steak medium...cooked perfectly....but we both thought it needed salt even with the garlic butter. Â Fries were perfect as usual. Â No hassle as we had a business meeting and stayed there for over 1 hour. Â Would def go back.

Tried their brunch. Nice options for $10. Space is a little cramped, but the service was good, and I enjoyed the Eggs Benedict, which come in three varieties: Canadian bacon, salmon, or Florentine. I got the Canadian bacon, which was tasty, and my friend raved about the salmon. Didn't love the potatoes, but their Hollandaise sauce was top notch. I'd definitely go back.

Really tasty and cheap Thai food! Loved that it wasn't the normal curry/spring rolls Thai food. I got the Pad Ped Proam and it was delish but REALLY spicy. It was a veggie duck over rice, which was really good, though I definitely needed like 6 glasses of water to finish it. Maybe next time I'd get it and tell them to make it a bit less spicy. Place is real cute and the service was good! Will be back if I'm looking for Thai in HK. YUM!

Stumbled upon this place when my friend and I didn't want to wait in the brunch line at Westville. The space is clean, cozy and nicely decorated with dark wood. The coffee is strong and come in big mugs. We ended up splitting an order of the shrimp and grits and french toast w/nutella. Both dishes were great, but we loved the shrimp and grits more. Super rich and creamy with parmesan cheese, topped with very fresh shrimp cooked in garlic-buttery goodness. Came back with another friend and we had to order the shrimp and grits (again) and biscuits w/sausage gravy. It was pretty empty and the waiter was watching the world cup game on his laptop, so we joined him at the bar. Recognizing me from my last visit, he gave us complimentary sangria. I will definitely come back here for dinner.

I was desperately looking for a place to grab dinner with a friend. So I set out on my online mission to find a restaurant that will fulfill the foodie in me while still trying to be on the healthy side. Â Not only to my surprise did I find something practically in my back yard, but it was exactly what I was looking for! The waitress and waiters were extremely friendly and helpful. When i go somewhere new, I love picking their brains for food suggestions. They were more than happy to help out and recommend anything from appetizers, entrees to the wine. We tried; Sweet potato fries, Kabocha Squash Tart, Brussel sprouts w/ Parm and these buckwheat noodle that I cant remember the name of, sorry... They change up their menu based on what's in season and what is locally available. Which is pretty exciting! I can't wait to come back here when the weather warms up to see what other deliciousness has been added to their menu!

5 stars across the board. Authenticity Originality Atmosphere And most importantly taste. Friend and I came here for an early dinner. The food is fantastic. You can literally taste every Spanish spice in the dishes. It's hearty and filling and makes you feel like you've just had a great home cooked meal. Overall a great experience. When you get here try the sangria and make sure you get the tacu tacu. The risotto is to die for

This place could get 5 stars for the chicken biscuit alone! The unassuming storefront of Cheeky Sandwiches is pretty easy to miss and anything but cheeky. Once inside my girlfriend and I were greeted by the chef and some jacked Spanish dude at the register. Think James Vega from Mass Effect 3 for my gamers out there. There isn't much space, a single table by the window and a standing bar to eat along the adjacent wall. I'm not sure what to make of the decor, I think it's kind of cool and a little divey. From what I understand the owner is originally from Louisiana and I can see some of that reflected in the decor. We ordered two chicken biscuits each and we wanted to split an Oyster Po'Boy. They were out of Strawberry Soda so we opted for the Ginger Soda instead. After about 10 minutes we got our food and... Man let me tell you about the Chicken Biscuit: Perfectly seasoned and freshly fried chicken- juicy on the inside, crispy on the outside. Rich southern gravy. Fresh, crisp, zesty slaw. All sandwiched between a freshly baked warm biscuit? Yes please. Why didn't I get two? This thing is amazing. The slaw is so amazing because it's the perfect contrast to an otherwise extremely rich sandwich. My only complaint is that the sandwich sort of deconstructs midway through. The biscuit gets a little soggy, some pieces of chicken fall out, and some of the slaw slides out. I would love to come here on the crowded days just to see other people picking at the fallen scraps of their sandwich. I was completely shameless eating this bad boy. (In hindsight I should have asked for a fork.) 5 stars all day for the Chicken Biscuit. If you're appetite is anything like mine, the sandwiches will seem pretty small. 1 will satisfy, but not fill you up. Luckily we had that Oyster Po'Boy to split. My girlfriend was full from her biscuit so the Po'Boy was all mine. For anyone wondering why Oyster, it's simply because I'm allergic to shrimp. I have no doubt that the shrimp (or even the half oyster/half shrimp) is the superior option for Po'Boy. It was a solid sandwich, the bread was a little tough, but the fried oysters tasted great! Pickles, lettuce, and mayo gave it character, but that hot sauce gave it soul! I usually eat my oysters raw, but I can totally get behind some more fried oysters one day- especially if it's anything like Cheeky Sandwiches. A quick note on service, these guys are really down to earth. Halfway into my Oyster Po'Boy the chef started chatting with me about it. He mentioned it's one of the least ordered items and he wanted some feedback from me. Also, on our way out the jacked dude hands us two piping hot fresh beignets. SCORE! I've never had beignets but they're sort of like the zeppolis and the funnel cakes of the world. I liked them a lot. I recommend this place to anyone in the area to check out. Actually, even if you're not in the area, come try it at least once. I know I'll be back soon.
