One of my faves in NYC and probably the first one to carry my favorite coffee beans.

I definitely have never had a pizza like the artichoke pizza. You MUST get it. Creamy and delicious. Super thick crust, that has the perfect thickness to equal the deliciousness that is on top of this pizza. $4.50 for a slice, a little steep you may say, but you will only need 1 slice to fill you up. Definitely planning on coming back asap.
Just amazing, best to go across the street, its the same food/company/cooks (they alternate), just without the lines

Four dollars. Â That's how much my filling lunch at Dumpling House (now Vanessa's Dumplings) cost. Â It's also how much I spent just getting to Chinatown for my cheapo dumplings, but hey, it's worth it. Â While you might find better dumplings elsewhere, you sure as hell aren't going to find cheaper ones. Â Fried right in front of you on the other side of the take away counter, Vanessa's Dumplings arrive hot on your styrofoam plate within minutes. Â Not only can you see them fry, but if you peer toward the back of the restaurant, you can see several cooks diligently making dumpling after dumpling behind the glass window. Â But how do the $1 dumplings taste? Â Well, like dumplings I guess. Â Frankly, I was too hungry to discriminate much on taste. Â The cheap eats don't end with the dumplings. Â $2 sesame pancake sandwiches swaddle tender roast pork, cilantro and shaved carrots. Â The fried pork buns looked pillowy and delicious as well, and I had a hard time keeping my fork away from my coworker's plate (I figured that was out of bounds). Â $4 and a stomach full of carbs later, I can happily report that I'll be back next time I feel the urge for a midday field trip. Â Thank you, (Vanessa's) Dumpling (House).

Great food, very unique Mexican fusion. I had the rabbit enchiladas and my wife had some shrimp with fried jamÅn. Both were delicious! The fried cactus side was interesting. Wife liked it, I thought it had a weird texture... But it's cactus. :) Huge selection of tequila drinks. DÃ©cor: really nice and trendy! I recommend making reservations.
YUM. I always saved room to have a slice of Artichoke for dessert.

I still dream about the meal I had here last year... We ordered the Phaparko Dhendo - a delicious and spicy assortment of curries served with the traditional Tibetan dhendo. Â I had no idea what dhendo was before eating this meal. On it's own, it plain and mushy, but dipped with curry, it's delicious. Â  I have been looking everywhere for a more authentic restaurant but this is the real deal. Â Our servers were very sweet and explained everything on the menu, and we enjoyed the traditional Indian tea that was served to close the meal. Â  Cute decor, intimate feeling but I would go here for lunch or dinner alone without feeling out of place. Â Check this place out!

Best french toast I've ever had. Â The baked eggs were also amazing. Â On a Sunday morning at 11:30 we sailed in. Â I've always seen a wait here. Â I think it was that many people were distracted by the gay pride parade- got hit on by two lesbians that day-score! Â Go to extra virgin, the prices are totally reasonable and then head to the highline and walk to chelsea. Â God I love the Highline and french toast!

Good empanadas but after the initial few bites, it just goes from yummy to I'm tired of eating this. Don't get me wrong, the crust is flaky and soft, the inside whether you ordered a sweet or savory one is good, but the taste does get tiresome quick. I ordered the Romeo & Juliet dessert one, along with a banana & ice cream one. Definitely liked Romero's guava & Juliet's cream cheese filling or is it the other way around? Also tasted the spicy chicken, shredded beef one, and spinach & cheese (best one in my opinion). For the savory ones, I definitely recommend you stock up on their green salsa/sauce. Dowse your empanadas in it, it will make the empanadas more enjoyable. But since I feel like the sauce should be a secondary thing with the empanada as the star, I feel like i must take away 2 stars since it is called Empanada Mama and not Sauce Boss Mama.

While the patatas bravos and torilla were delish I found myself angry at the fact that the "divers scallops" was in fact, a lone scallop. For $13. I would have complained to the manager but the yummy white sangria made me forget... I guess there is a price to pay for trendy-ness.

Tucked in the Gramercy Park Hotel, Maialino is a fitting gem of Gramercy. It's encapsulates the feel of the neighborhood--class, comfort, and history. Get on that flatbread!!! CAROTE--REFRESHING NON-ALCOHOLIC drink choice for brunch. It had an extra kick from the GINGER but I loved it. SUPPLI AL TELEFONO--GOURMET MOZZARELLA-TYPE STICKS? This appetizer brought out my inner fat girl who's always craving a combination of crispy, saucy, cheesy, and a bit of starchy goodness. I couldn't get enough!! PORCHETTA--HUGE FOOTLONG ROAST PORK SANDWICH. I SHARED this with a friend so the portion was just right. The EGG was RUNNY and the PORK was COOKED PERFECTLY but LACKED SOME FLAVOR. Overall, it was a good sandwich but it DIDN'T KNOCK MY SOCKS OFF. I also wasn't a fan of the bread. **if you want something CHEESY, order the CACIO E PEPE TORTA DI OLIO D'OLIVA--SO GOOD!! Olive oil, what olive oil? It didn't cross my mind at all because this MOIST ANGEL OF A DESSERT overcame me. Top it off with vanilla bean marscapone and I was in heaven. PANNA COTTA--BEST panna cotta I've had in NYC. The consistency was SO SMOOTH and SILKY and it paired very well with the rhubarb, surprisingly. Decor is very warm and comforting. It's not screaming bougie but it does feel more upscale than your typical trattoria. Turn the corner from the hostess stand and you'll be blown away by the amount of space and seating. It's bustling, vibrant, and when the sunshine comes in, it's such a pretty and simple space. **Something that really attracted me to their MENU is VARIETY. Even though it's menu has quite the selection (all the dishes sound appealing), it STILL HELD IT'S INTEGRITY and QUALITY OF FOOD. They serve ALL MEAL TIMES and even serve LATE NIGHT SNACKS! I can't wait to try that. I'll be coming back for sure. FYI MAKE A RESERVATION

My husband might drag me back here because he pronounced his warm lamb salad 'genius' but my pork chops and cheddar waffles were as bland as the sterile dining room. The pork was indistinguishable in its flavor and texture from the innards of a chicken cutlet from your standard pizza store and the coating was like Â too much Shake N Bake from your mom's in Cleveland. The waffle was lukewarm and only had a cheddar aftertaste that reminded me of Cheese Nibs. Even the accompanying syrup was bland and tasted like water-down agave. The not-Stumptown coffee was good and I liked the lightly pulped orange juice. I was depressed at having to pay $15 for this meal, so great in conception and so flavorless in execution. Meanwhile, my SO was babbling happily about 'delicious jus' this and 'incredibly tender meat' that in between lusty bites so if you are going to Buttermilk Channel, consider that a lamb salad endorsement.

OK, I know this is a tourist trap, but I don't care. Â I love Carmine's! Â My dad also loves Carmine's.. so when my parents come into the city to see a show they always want to take us to Carmine's (which I've never complained about). Â I've tried to take my dad to other spots in Restaurant Row or on 9th Avenue, but he wants nothing to do with them. Â The portions are enourmous here, so come ready to eat your heart out.

I'm crying because I live all the way in Boston and I miss this little gem. As if this cart needs any more reviews. No matter where I am in NYC, I always make my way here to get some lamb/chicken combo with the famous white sauce. I love you 53rd & 6th Halal Cart.

Was hanging out in Times Square after work and decided to visit the much talked about Junior's which is famous for their cheesecakes. I picked up the Strawberry Cheesecake, a chocolate cookie (for hubby to take to work as snack ... heh heh) and a Sugar Free Low Carb Plain for myself but I find it overpriced cos it cost me $6.50 for a tiny slice! The service was cool, easy location so I am not gonna complain too much. LOL!

This place is good for a casual get together with friends, coworkers, etc. The vibe is pretty energetic with a large space that fills up around 8pm. Lots of groups, but not a lot of dates. I sat downstairs. We ordered a bunch of small plates and doner kebab. Everything, except the kebab, was very good. The hummus hit the spot - warm, yummy and perfect with their fluffy bread. The crab cakes were also good. We also had the feta, wrapped in phyllo and deep fried. Can't really go wrong with that. Service at the table was good, but they had lots of problems with the reservations (they should really switch to open table). The soda was also a little flat. Prices were very reasonable, especially for the area. Overall, I liked this place and will definitely go back, but will probably call twice to confirm a reservation.

Get your Thai fix here! This little place serves up big flavor Thai food. All served hot and quick for such a small place. A genuine wonder. Pad Thai with the rib,spring rolls and satay apps. to start. Outstanding, not available at home like this at any price.

Came here on a Saturday at 11 for brunch, it's a really cute place with outdoor seating that's great for the summer. They have Stumptown coffee, which my friend really loved. I got the Green Shakshuka, which I'd heard was really good. It was decent, but honestly it kind of just tasted like hot green salsa over baked eggs, so not that big of a deal. My friend got the Poached Eggs with Haloumi, kind of like an Eggs Benedict with Haloumi and Tomatoes. She liked it a lot. Both dishes came with a side of perfectly baked sourdough bread. We also got the House Cured Duck Bacon to share. This was really good, and we're definitely going back for more. Think what makes this place a 4 and not a 3.5 would really be the service and ambience though. It's not over-populated by the brunch crowd yet, so it's still a good mix of busy but relaxing at the same time. The waitstaff is really friendly and nice, and portions are not too big but it's a nice, suitable amount for a filling brunch without making you want to pass out from a food coma after.

My journey to find a great sit-down in Little Italy continues. This place looked good, just going through the Yelp pictures. Had to secure an early lunch reservation (it gets crowded) because the menu turned pre-fixe around 1pm. Good service with waiters coming back every 10 or so minutes. Got the Mini Rice ball appetizer ($11) and Meatball sliders($12). Menu options for lunch aren't the same as dinner turns out, but I wanted to try these. Mini rice balls themselves were good, but the marinara sauce it came with was thin. Meatball sliders were juicy and cheesy - very good. Better if you reserve, a little pricey ($12 for small cocktails), but attentive service. Not really a spot I'd feel the need to go back to.
Love it. good service, fresh and creative dishes. highly recommend it

I dragged the bf here since I was on an elotes (grilled corn) crave after having it for the first time at la esquina. The place is tiny, the tables were tiny, you'll be able to hear the conversation from the next tables over since you're practically sitting only inches apart. The wait was about 15 mins for 2 on a Tuesday night at 7:30pm. However, for this night none of it really bothered me. We ordered the grilled corn (a-duh). It was cheaper than la esquina. (here it was $4.25 for 2, la esquina charges $4 per corn.) But for some reason I think i enjoyed the ones at Â la esquina more. they were bigger, juicier, had a nicer grilled corn taste. Don't get me wrong these were still pretty good ! I would have liked for the spice to be lightly dusted all around instead of just concentrated on the top though. Shrimp Tacos (2 tacos plus rice & beans for about $13)- pretty pricey since im paying $13 for two tacos, im sure majority of people hardly touch the filler rice & beans. However, the BF did try the rice and he said it tasted like they added butter and that it was good. The grilled shrimp had that nice grilled flavor that i like, like it just came fresh off a grill. They were perfectly cooked and juicy too. BF ordered the chicken mole enchilada- i took a bite and it was ok. Ordered a limeade and it was wayyy sour. Â Didn't finish it. Â Should have gotten one of those yummy looking mojitos next time :( If I come back, I would order the corn again, mojitos, shrimp tacos, and maybe something new to try. Worth visiting.

Yes this pizza is good, yes this pizza is famous, but what is all the hype? Tourists come to the area just to eat here and is spoken of all over, yet I can't exactly differentiate the difference between frank peeps and Lombardis. I already feel the virtual stoning from the colt following this place has, and my response to them is look above.. I gave it 4 stars. Thin crust, delicious sauce, and old school dining atmosphere.
Good and a great deal
Great food, great service from everyone (Kimberly our waitress was very knowledgeable and outgoing) and this is a GREAT restaurant! Â We will be back soon!

Great spot. Very good selection of fish and simple dishes. The space is cozy, if not extremely small, making some of Manhattan's smallest restaurants look downright spacious. Prices are a bit on the higher end, but the fish does not disappoint. I definitely plan to go back regularly.

my experience was not the best. I asked for a table because I was alone - i do not have problems sitting on the bar but the bar was full. So, after wait 20 minutes they asked me to sit on the bar. Ok, no problem, but why they dont asked before? I was starving. After all, ate good pizza and they also have good drinks. My tip is: dont go alone if you need food. Its kind of impossible eat if you are sitting on the bar.
I can't even begin to describe how much I love this place. Get the Modern with a soft boiled egg and hot paste on the side. Sublime.

Great place for breakfast. Plenty of options for vegos and traditional breakfast eaters alike. Our group was happy with the granola, oatmeal and fruit salad presented. Coffee is passable and available in sizes small to extreme buckets. Staff are friendly enough, the atmosphere is friendly. Grab your own cutlery, condiments and water.

Seriously the best seafood boil I've had in this town minus the heafty price. Service was awesome and quick, food was just so yummy. Â Bring your purse filled with cash bc they don't take cards. They also have a full bar and awesome drink selection. I'm sold!!

To all the DiFara lovers, youre going to hate me but here goes...I love pizza. DiFara's Â was ok-tasty Â because of the fresh herbs he grows on his window sill in the front of the store Â and natural Buffalo mozzarella. Thats how pizza should be made... but Â its very greasy and sloppy.,their crust is very thin and mushy. I -2 people Â can eat an entire pie by themselves thats how thin and light it is. Seriously people! not worth an hour wait or a ride on the subway from the city! READ ON...For many years the place was Â in Â serious need of a Â gut and refurbishing job. So what, you say?....I was told they also offered dishes such as a minestone or vegetable soup/ which he made on some Â occasions for certain people on a whim, if you asked .So I ordered a vegetable soup as my husband waited for his pizza. BUT, I made the mistake (or should I say was lucky to witness with my own eyes by ) asking to use their bathroom (after all we were waiting for over an hour !) and was shocked at the over-all conditions of the kitchen behind that door. Everything was older than ancient ! It was disgusting, really!. Besides everything being so ancient (cant be cleaned properly),it was a grimy Â roach smorgasborg back there..Sorry to break it to you ! .And as I Â squeezed my way passed his VERY surprised son preparing what looked like it could be my vegetable soup- I noticed he was using leftover scraps from other dishes they had prepared, yuck! He was scooping up stuff from what looked like a garbage bin into a pot on the stove! But I thought NOooo, I must SURELY Â be mistaken. What am I thinking?! ..When I finally got my soup, a thick stew like meal in a deep bowl- I was sooo disappointed to discover scraps of nothing but vegetable skins Â with their stems still on and a few even with their labels intact! My heart sunk. Looking at the long line of people waiting for Â their orders- I felt disgusted at what was just served to me, Â and ashamed to say anything to this old man who was an icon to these people.Then I was offended. Did they think I wouldnt notice what was in my bowl? ...What happened to Difara's? How can they continue under these conditions and in this manner? What about the health department and inspections? Â Needless to say, I have not gone back in 3 years and dont intend to. Has anything changed in this establishment? Please tell me it has, because every time I read rave reviews on this place I get chills down my spine. Wake up people!!..There, I Â finally said it.!! So crucify me...

The food was good! Had the chicken enchiladas and they were good but I've had better. Â The guac was yummy but we ordered it with medium spice and it was super spicy so be careful if you're not into that. Â The drinks were okay, a little too sweet for my taste. I would go back.

Get the sticky buns, you wont regret it. I don't understand all the negative reviews for waiting time, I'm a frequent here (as I work down the block), and all hours of the day I never see any lines, or when I do, everyone is served quickly. Really good on the wallet as well, when it came time to assess the damage done to me, came out to $15 for a really filling meal. Would definitely recommend.

I don't normally like Irish coffee but my friend said I had to try it. I'm glad I did- it was perfect. Hot perfectly done coffee with fresh cold cream on top, and freshly grated nutmeg. I've never had a drink like that, and I wish I lived in NYC so I could come back and have that more often. Bartender was very friendly.

Worst service and experience ever. I came here a couple of years ago with my family which included my elderly grandmother who was in a wheelchair. Apparently she was in the middle of the way and needed to move. This situation could have been handled in an appropriate way by kindly asking us to move, but instead the host just told me that "she's in the way and needs to move" in such a rude and disrespectful way. Because of this I have never stepped back into this restaurant. The food isn't even that good. If you want real Italian go to the various other restaurants in the city.
i have always loved this place. best squares on earth. now i live on the island i have to schlepp back to bklyn when i have my pizza fit

What a fun place to dine... Most were hipsters but there were a fair amount on non-hipsters... Like me. Â Liked the feel of the dining area and the eclectic music made it better. Â AC/DC, Al Green, the stones all were represented. Â The food was outstanding! Had the pot appetizers (which are seasonally rotating) and they were a mousse (portabello mushroom was one) roasted marrow and razor clam "egg salad" all of which were outstanding. Â I had the pork chop with goat cheese polenta and maple glazed Apple...to cook a thick chop takes work and they did it very well! Had the cheese cake with mango ice cream...odd mix but it worked! I would have like to see more wine selections but what they had was quality.

Been coming here since soon after it opened have been for both lunch and dinner, I usually have the steak and eggs at lunch time and a side of blood sausage and take advantage of the half price wine option at lunch , I have eaten most things on the menu and they are great had an awesome steak with truffle butter one night as a special , the service is good and the owner is usually there and friendly , a great spot it only seems to get better

i'm not even a sliders type of gal but man, these sliders sure are good! who would have thought that such a small burger could taste so good! it is just a slider with cheese and grilled onions but its so delicious and not dry, or greasy!! i had 2 regular sliders and split an order of cheese fries! and it was more than enough for me. the ambiance is nothing fancy but a long narrow hole in the wall, along with a couple of tables in the front and the service is good, no complaints! if you're in the mood for sliders and in the area, this is definitely a great spot to try!

best oriental breakfast and soups in the NYC area. don't be mistaken by the looks of the place. its not fancy and actually they only hace a. ounter for 4 maybe 6 people to eat on the site. but dumplis, soup, breakfast are just amazing

As other Yelpers have recommended, I ordered the squid ink. WOW. I want to go to there again and eat at it again. Oh, we had the best waiter. My wife and friend ordered the Salad Caprese. Not being Italian, they always ate it with just some salt/pepper. The waiter sees this, and calls them out. "That's not the way you're supposed to eat that! Here, let me show you." He proceed to dump olive oil and balsamic vinegar all over their salads. I'm lol'ing, my wife is horrified, but he says "It's too bland without it. Try it now, it's better. If you don't like it, I'll get you a new one." Okay, so no risk there. Well, my wife takes her Caprese with oil/vinger now, thanks to our waiter. A+ Oh, the Tiramisu was delicious! Made in-house. Get it!

For now.

A real let down!! Â You are definitely paying for the name. Â Saw Lombardie's Pizza on one of the local food shows and couldn't wait to try it out during our first visit to NYC. Â To begin with, a plain large pizza, with Â 8 slices runs $20.50. Â It's 3 bucks a topping on top of that. We ordered a garden salad ($7.50) that came from a bag; it had 2 cherry tomatoes, onions and a sprinkle of sliced mushrooms.... very disappointing. On top of that, they don't accept credit cards; very inconvenient for us, as we don't travel with much cash. So how'd they earn their stars? Â 1-seated us quickly. 2- not a long wait for our food, and it was hot. 3-fresh veggies on our pizza. Â Overall, an okay experience, but I've had better tasting pizza for less.

Today is La Panineria's second day open. I found that out when I stopped by for lunch today and had to know how long I had been missing out on their incredible sandwiches (I can live with not having known about it for one day). The small, unassuming storefront gives way to a tiny interior, one lunch counter and one large, communal table, and the back kitchen where the proprietors make their sandwich magic. I had the Parma on ciabatta ("prosciutto di Parma DOP 14 months - fresh Robiola Nonno Nanni") and my buddy had their special of the day on a baguette (salami and cheese). They may just be meat and cheese sandwiches, but the best things are usually the simplest, and the ingredients they used were outstanding. The cheese was rich, the bread was crusty and chewy and basically perfect, the meat was equally impressive. The sandwich/soda "start up special" may have cost $10, but that's a small price to pay for reaching sandwich NirvÄna. On our way out of the store a man, who I will assume was the proud owner, asked us how we enjoyed our sandwiches. We told him we would be back soon. That was not a lie.

OH Yeah ~ Having brunch at Jane is MmMmm GOOD. My aunt and I shared the vanilla bean french toast, seared tuna salad, and Lobster Benedict. Where do I begin? I absolutely loved the vanilla bean french toast! The toast here is done RIGHT. We were served three large pieces of toast. As I broke tore off a piece of the toast in my hands, I could see how the bread softly came apart. The toast is soft and just melted in my mouth. I told my aunt how impressed I was with the Lobster Benedict. The lobster in it is fresh! The potatoes on the side were crispy - just the way I like it! I ate some of the seared tuna and had it to go. A nice bonus, is that each entree comes with a free drink! I tried the apple champagne and the white peach Bellini. Tip: They don't serve starters during lunch. Come for dinner for that! They also serve one free drink per entree for Sunday Brunch!
My first Ramen-slurping experience. The wait was worth it. It's not cheap for a bowl of noodles, but it's dang good and they give you enough to feed two.

et's put it this way: I had hyped up how good dinner would be in my head for weeks before finally eating here. And it was still amazing. Then, I hyped up how good brunch and dinner a second time would be despite knowing how dangerous overhyping food is. And again, still amazing. There is nothing that Andrew Carmellini, pastry chef Karen DeMasco, and all those LV bartenders can cook/bake/concoct that is short of utterly delicious. Since you definitely want to try everything on the menu (food and cocktail alike), I recommend going with a larger group (despite having to wait a couple of weeks for your reservation) so that you can taste everything. Or you can do what I do and compulsively go back every other week, pretending like I can afford it. But can you really put a price on a meal that could allow you to die happily? Ok, this may be a slight exaggeration but the point is, the food is Good. Real Good. appetizers: - ricotta - a Carmellini classic that you definitely want to try. Even the toast itself is stupidly perfect. - lamb sliders - only two per order, but eat this. entrees: - grandmother's ravioli - not your ordinary ravioli. this guy's grandma knows what's up. - orechiette - the broccoli rabe lends a really nice crunchy texture and vegetable element that most of the other pasta dishes lack - gigatone - mixed into a hearty, deeply satisfying ragu - papardelle - lamb bolognese topped with ricotta. great stuff. - porchetta sandwich - infinitely superior to Porchetta's version, constructed from thin cuts of juicy, well-seasoned porchetta and gooey melted provolone. - chicken dinner - must come back to try this. I hear it's a winner. desserts: - lemon tart - nicely textured filling with a rich lemony taste - almond semifreddo - the best thing ever. - panna cotta - heavenly. - fantasia di cioccolato - it's delicious gelato, but nothing particularly worth trying. right. So, I generally don't condone absurdly long reviews but I've made an exception because I simply can't contain how much I love this place. Do yourself a favor; eat here.

We went there last night. It is a bit out of way but the food is excellent and highly recommended. The beet salad is amazing and spiced lamb is to die for. Very good selection of wine too. Overall highly recommended,

Some friends and I were out on a Wednesday night. We wanted to find a bar. Not a bar where we could sit quietly and have meaningful conversations. We wanted a "bar" bar. We walked into a few other places in the neighborhood and struck out. Then we stumbled across Scratchers and knew we had found our destination. We walked in and there were 10-15 people in the back playing amazing and upbeat music on string instruments! I don't think this was something that Scratchers coordinated, but it was awesome! We walked up to the bartender and said, "We want to drink cheap tonight." His reaction? "I got you." $3 PBRs all night. Just what we were looking for. I'm not sure what this place is like on a typical Wednesday night. I think a group of people playing Irish music could make any bar pretty cool. But we were there until 2am and I can't wait to go back. Side note - we had just gotten done seeing a concert, and guess who shows up at this bar? The cellist from the concert. With her cello. And yeah, she freestyled and got in on it. Epic.

I had heard good things about this place, and read great reviews about the place. Started off with the Samurai Ribs - these were tasty and tender. A pretty good way to start things off actually. After that I ordered the Shiromaru Hakata Classic ramen. The first thing I noticed was that the soup was flavored more on the mild side - In other words it wasn't a strong flavor - more subdued. I prefer a stronger more flavorful soup base but I suppose mild is the "safe" approach to feed the masses.. The one thing that stuck out to me was their use of the pork loin. Unlike the normal sliced chashu that is present in other versions of tonkotsu ramen that I've had, these guys do not slice it, and instead just put the entire chunk of pork belly in there.. Mine was very tender - slow cooker tender and was very good. Â All in all it was a good bowl, however I've had better ramen for cheaper, and didn't have a ridiculous wait to deal with.. If I were to judge this place based off the ramen alone, it would get a solid 3 stars.. However since the overall experience was so poor, it has to come down to a 2 which is really a shame since they were issues that could be fixed with better management. Every party including ours were told the wait would be approximately 2 hours.. Really? for ramen? The sad truth was that it ended up being a 3hr wait, and this ramen is NOT worth a 3hr wait.. It's not even worth a 2hr wait... A 1hr wait? maybe.. We ended up spending a lot of time (and a whole lot more money) at the bar with drinks and bar foods just so we wouldn't go crazy. At one point we left and walked several blocks to search for other potential dinner spots - we managed to get a few finger foods from hole in the wall places and returned with still an hour to go from the impatient hostess. This is a 2-star restaurant that tries to act and pass itself off as a 5-star restaurant when its not. Their food needs to justify their attitude and swagger; unfortunately it does not. In case you're wondering why our party waited the 3hrs, I was a guest in town and my gracious hosts wanted to show me what "great ramen" in NY was all about. There is so much other good food waiting to be experienced in New York that this place will not be a priority the next time I come to town..

Why are all the best Japanese restaurants in basements of office buildings? Â We were reminded of our search for Mizutani in Tokyo (one of the best, if not THE best sushi bar in Tokyo) as we were directed down to the basement of this office building by the evening security guard. Â  We were not very warmly welcomed, as the maitre'd pointed out to us that we were more than 15 minutes late for our reservation, and asked us to wait a minute while she figured out where to put us as she apparently had given our table away. Â I was particularly annoyed by the welcome when I was led into the dining room and saw that there were plenty of available tables to be had. Â  That being said, the actual dinner service was quite good, and the food was as good as advertised. Â Our favorites were the beef tongue (so tender and flavorful), the tori tsukune (chicken meatballs), and the jaga dango (light, just slightly sweet, mashed potato donuts, essentially). Â Yes, you can find tsukune at any izakaya or yakitori place, but these were maybe the best I've ever tried. Â The jaga dango was simply like nothing I've ever tried before. The gindara yuan yaki (soy marinated cod) and jidori shioyaki (grilled organic free range chicken) were other standout dishes. Â With so much talk about how small the dishes were, we definitely went overboard, and ended up with too much food. Â We were actually quite surprised at the healthy portions of jidori shioyaki and beef tongue that were served. Â  Oh well, you can do much worse than leftover tori tsukune for breakfast the next day.

The great burger crusade continues. This month's entry was the grilled roquefort burger and shoestring fries at spotted pig. I LOVED it. Meat was excellent, and the roquefort cheese provided a welcome bite. Only negative was the amount of bread, which, while deliciously toasted, slightly overpowered the burger itself. The fries were amazing though. Not a single negative, and if hadn't been 90 degrees out today, I probably would have cleaned the plate. Service was superb. Not rushed and very friendly. There isn't a huge beer selection on tap, and I would caution against ordering the spotted pig bitter. It was really unpleasant. Also of note, the bathroom is VERY cramped, which leads to some awkward side-stepping while you stare pointedly at the ground to avoid the glance of the man or woman who was just making those god awful noises in the stall you were necessarily leaning against while using the sink. On the up, the bergamot hand soap smells amazing. I went to the bathroom twice just to lather up. Overall, a very satisfactory dining experience. I would love to order something else off the menu if I came back to see what else the chef has to offer.

we sat on the rooftop dining area, and WTF-no pasta? Â how can we eat an an "eataly" place and not get italian pasta? Â anyhoo, their charcuterie and cheese plate made me forget that. Â the pork shoulder was as overpriced as it was juicy. Â  come early so you can have time to check out all the stands.

Wow, everything about this place is amazing. The ambiance is really cool. Not necessarily "Japanese" but very classy, but not so classy that you can't dress casually. It's a relaxed vibe. The overlooking second story tables is pretty cool. We sat at the bar. The service is top notch. The servers were very nice, always filling our tea and very attentive to our needs. The food is excellent. My friend and I both got the tonkatsu. To. Die. For. Very tender and juicy pork. The whole dish was huge. It was the perfect amount of good though. There was an egg custard type of dish that came with it. I've never had it before but it was pretty good. For appetizers we got the salted tofu and natto. Both very good. And for dessert, mochi and vanilla ice cream. Oh yes, and we got the Gold sake which was so smooth. With all this food and drink the whole bill came out to only $100, that's including the tip. What a deal. All in all this was an excellent find on Yelp. I will definitely be coming back here again.

They offered flat water and carbonated water which was nice to have that option and they were free! It was a great time with the right people. Mussels: 9/10 - There was sand in some of the mussels. Came with fresh fries! The sauce is a killer!!!!! Use the table bread to dip it!! Chicken Pot Pie - 8/10 - It was nice comfort food. I wished the pie crust would be more flaky instead of a soggy and chewy. Lamb Milanese - 9/10 - Â It was a interesting dish. The fried lamb was underneath an arugula salad. Lamb was super crispy. Mac and Cheese appetizer - 9/10 - It was a nice cheesy start to the meal. It came in a little skillet dish. Mediterranean Salad appetizer - 7/10 - I don't like olives but this salad had peppers, feta cheese, chickpeas, raw red onion and lettuce. It was a nice refreshing blend. Whole wheat spaghetti - 8/10 - Pasta was good and it came with plentiful of mushrooms.

We made a reservation here for Sunday brunch but unexpectedly woke up a little late, but still wanted to see if we had a shot since it's just the 2 of us. Lo and behold, we arrived an hour after our reservation and the wait for 2 would be an hour and 45 minutes to two hours. Craaaaaaaazy. We were about to leave because we were starving and it was our own fault, but then the hostess told us that the bar is first come first serve and I think it was our lucky Sunday because there were only 2 seats left!! Score!!!!! The Sunday brunch items all sounded so yummy, I decided on the Benedict Johnny. My other choice was the french toast, but I wanted something more savory. I enjoyed my meal and loved my complimentary freshly squeezed grapefruit juice. The home fries are DELICIOUS! We didn't even need any extra pepper or any ketchup! My boyfriend had the Benedict Jane, which i surprisingly liked more than my Johnny. He told me he liked his white peach Bellini very much too. It was nice sitting at the bar and watched just how much vodka the bartender poured into his little shaker every time. And it was alot. Side note, They have more seating downstairs where the restrooms are. I will DEFINITELY come back for the french toast and Jane. On time. With a reservation.

Chicken is really easy to cook, but few things are as satisfying as an expertly cooked chicken. Purbird does it pretty well. I've ordered from here about a dozen times. Only once was the chicken not up to par. Other times, it's terrific. The mac and cheese is delicious as well. Probably the most delicious mac and cheese I've ever had that uses whole grain pasta. Although, after leaving leftovers in the fridge it's pretty clear why- it's SUPER cheesy and greasy. But that's not a complaint. The chicken pie in phyllo is also surprisingly tasty. But 90% of the time I just get the flame grilled chicken. Can't go wrong with that.

Just took my girlfriend for her first slice of New York pizza. Had a cheese and a pepperoni.. The owner was incredibly friendly and even threw in one of their square Sicilian pieces for free. Â Absolutely incredible, and the kitchen was actually staffed with Italians.

a hip cozy corner pizza/italian spot worth the trip if you live nearby. Small and thoughtful. a very nice house red at $6 a glass (thankyou!). i shared a salad, Capocollo pizza, and a plate of meatballs for dinner. Â plenty of doughy springy bread and grassy olive oil (infused with red pepper flakes??) to get you started as you look over the little clipboard menu. Â The pizza is Â thin crust and crisp though a wedge can't stand straight out on it's own. Â This is a pie that cooks in about 7 minutes! Â But there is a nice tear and chew that isn't flat or doughy and the mozz is fresh, no shredded cheese blankets here. There is a room in front where the pizza oven is and also a larger room in the back, we sat in the back at a small 2 top table. Â The decor is a mix match of furniture and home stuffs and it all fits in well. Â Very nice. I will return to try more items. Cash only

I love this place!!! You feel like you left NYC and went to Italy. I ate at the pizza and pasta place and ordered the short rib tagliatelle handmade pasta. It was beyond amazing! Waiter suggested a wine pairing and it was perfect! Pretty affordable for the amount of food and quality of ingredients! Ended the evening with tiramisu gelato. Perfect meal!

What happened to this place?!?! Â It used to be spot on with service and food...the food was mediocore at best and the craptastical service...w.t.f.?! Sitting there waiting a good 20 minutes and no one, NOT ONE, of the so call wait staff stopped at our table to ask if we were ready to order or bring water or anthing. Â FInally I flagged one down and he just looks at me...like deer in headlights..so I ask if he can take our order and it literally felt like he was contemplating whether or not to. Â Chicken curry puffs was good but then the rest of the meal went quickly down hill from there. Â The pad thai we ordered, the noodles were actually gummy...like as if this dish was cooked beforehand and just sat out or something...I asked for everything mild because my dinner date can't handle and the request was totally disregarded. Â There are plenty of other great thai places to choose from especially in queens but sad that this one has fallen off.

Came here for the first time last June 28th. It was suggested to just walk-in around the time they just opened for dinner (5p) because dinner reservations for 7p or 8p are quite hard to get. Successfully, we got a table for 2 parallel to the bar. Walking in, I loved the rustic, elegant, vintage-y feel to the place. In a word, I described the decor as "reclaimed". The mirrors lining the wall, the chandeliers, the china were very organic. To start, the dipping olive oil was amazing. You can distinctly taste the freshly squeezed green olives. Â  The salad of the day which was a bed of arugula mixed with mint leaves, strawberries and cubed goat cheese was just exquisite. The combination of the mild saltiness of the cheese with the distinct sweetness of the strawberries is complimented by the bitterness of the arugula and refreshing mint leaves. I definitely recommend the thin-crust whole wheat pizza with clam, mint, parsley and chilies. The combination itself sounds unexpected but the taste is a wonderful surprise. I love how the clams were cooked perfectly, it has the buttery texture to it so u can distinctly taste the clam. In every bite, you get an explosion of tangy and spicy which is grounded by the whole wheat crust. Unfortunately, the entree was quite disappointing. When we were ordering, I initially wanted the sea bass but was swayed into getting the halibut. The adventurer in me decided to leap and try the halibut on a bed of snap pea in corn broth. According to our waitress, it is one of their new entrees and it still is not part of the menu. I am glad it was not part of the menu because only on my first bite, I was already taken aback. The halibut was quite overcooked. The sea salt was too distinct that you can feel the grains on your tongue. The sauteed onion was very overpowering that the dish almost tasted like corn soup and the corn broth was just too salty. The entree was just a huge mistake. For the sweet finale, the vanilla chip ice cream cake saved the day (or night). It was served as a log with vanilla sauce, sliced almonds and topped with orange sorbet. I loved the combination of the sweetness of the vanilla ice cream with chocolate chips and the refreshing orange sorbet. Overall, I highly recommend this restaurant. I will have to go back to try the sea bass next time.
Great brunch place with tapas style dishes. Do try the chorizo here.

Honestly I'm a HUGE ramen fan and I think this place is pretty overrated... The upside: - the bbq pork bun is delicious. It has the Ippudo spicy sauce and the pork is super tender (read fatty). - black cod smelled fishy but super moist and tender - $2 noodles refill if you have broth leftover in your bowl - the cute decor with the variety of ramen bowls on the walls with the red lanterns, the nice seating arrangement, the dried ramen noodles bar and place setting. - Ramen broth was tasty but oily. - Friendly staff and great service The downside: - 1 hour wait to get seated. It's a PITA to keep your excitement after 1 hour wait when it's 40 degrees outside... burrr. - the stringy ramen noodles (I like my noodles chewy and curly) - hard boiled egg (the soft boil eggs are a must for good ramen combo) - expensive for ramen I had better ramen in Japan and other places in the Bay Area... Anyways it's still good but not super like everyone says...

Came a with a friend this morning to grab some brunch before catching our movies. Â The restaurant was cute. Â I liked the decorations and the feel. Â  I ordered crepes with bacon, onion and Swiss cheese. Â I usually love anything with either Swiss cheese or bacon and in this case, both. Â Unfortunately, the crepes was not that great. Â The onion was cut a little too big and was not cooked enough to bring out the sweetness. Â The bacon, on the other hand, was cut into too small pieces which didn't allow the flavor to come out. Â Well, the cheese...I love Swiss cheese so that's hard to go wrong. Â  Overall, the food was not too bad but could have been a lot better. Â I really like the look and feel of the restaurant. Â I would probably give it another try if I'm ever around the area and wanted to meet a friend for brunch.
wow so amazing, beautiful intimate and delicious. you pay for what you get!

We had a lovely meal at Caffe Linda on our last night in New York. Â The owner came to talk to us to answer any questions about the menu and the staff were attentive and friendly. Â The food was good quality and just the right quantities for us (unlike the unnecessarily enormous portions we have had at other American restaurants). Â A lovely cosy place and we easily got a table before 7pm but I suspect it would be much busier later in the evening.
Love the atmosphere and the food is amazing.

*Disclaimer* I went to Arepas on August 8th, which was a while ago, but I wasn't able to write this review until now. Even though it wasn't recent, I have to make sure people know why they should avoid this place like the plague. At first glance, Arepas Cafe is a quaint and cozy Venezuelan restaurant. My girlfriend and I were looking for a new spot to enjoy in Queens, and a quick Yelp search led us to Arepas. I'm very particular about my food, so I don't really waste time on restaurants below 4 stars. Arepas had really great reviews and according to my fellow Yelpers the food was top notch. After seeing a few pictures on their page, I was sold and we decided to try it out. We were greeted by a friendly waitress and after looking over the menu, we started with the mini empanadas appetizers (chicken and shark). They wouldn't honor their sangria deal on Yelp but no big deal. For the main course, Â I decided to order the Reina Pepiada arepas (chicken with avocado and mayo) and my girlfriend got the Pollo Mechado (shredded chicken). This is where the disaster began. Â The food came out in a decent amount of time and the empanadas were pretty good. Nothing to write home about, but pretty good. At this point, we started to notice that our waitress wasn't very good. She kind of just disappeared after our main dishes came. Once they did come, I wasn't too impressed. My Reina Pepiada arepas had WAY too much avocado. It was basically like eating a plain avocado sandwich. I couldn't stomach it. It was so overdone I ended up ordering the baby shark/stewed chicken and cheese arepas. My girlfriend decided to take the remainder of Â my avocado one home to hook it up a little. Her shredded chicken arepas was okay but average. We ate, we paid, we left. Where's the disaster you may ask?? The night of/day after, me and my girlfriend both started having severe stomach issues. This place actually gave us FOOD POISONING. We can't be sure what it was, but my guess was the shark or the avocado they served us. For a total of THREE days both of our stomachs were messed up. It ruined our entire weekend. We tried to call the restaurant and speak to the manager but we could never reach him. It's an absolute shame because we probably would have come back, but after this experience I'll never set foot in this place again !To solidify this deserved 1 star rating, the manager was reached out to several times immediately following the disaster and was never there... Atleast according to the people that answered the phone.

I would highly recommend the country-bread French toast with maple whipped cream and candied pecans. Crunchy and sweet! I personally like a savory and sweet breakfast so I usually try to share with someone else. Â I would also recommend getting the house-made biscuits and jam, delicious! The Chicken and Egg Sandwich was just 'okay'. The ingredients tasted very fresh, but it was messy and mostly bread and very little chicken. The place is small so it's not a good place for big groups; I think 2 to 4 people would be ideal. The tables are really close to each other so it's hard to move around. Also, the staff isn't particularly friendly or accommodating. I wouldn't recommend: - Coffee Seltzer with Ice Cream: not very tasty - Northern Spy Apple Pie - also nothing amazing, the only good part Â  Â  Â was the small scoop of ice cream on the side.

They're pricey for tacos. I went through the yelp photos and have seen the steady price increase from $2.50 to the now $3.50 price. I'm used to paying a max of $3 per taco (no tax). This is the only reason why i knocked off a star. The ordering is a bit weird. You pay and you get a ticket. YOU have to hand the ticket to the cooks so they can prepare your order. The staff is friendly and got my taco ready to go in no time, but that's a Â super confusing process. I ordered the adobada taco which is marinated pork, which is more of a minced texture. Some success on top, which i didn't really ask about because i was taco excited. I dabbed on a half spoonful of the spicy salsa and ate the thing. The corn tortilla is thicker than typical corn tortillas, but they make them in house. It's almost pillowy with a slight chew. I would be most unhappy if i opted for the flour tortilla when there's such an awesome alternative. The filling was flavorful and juicy, but really, the highlight is the tortilla.
Fun speakeasy that is easy to get into, decent food options as well

Did you know that I walked by here the other night, and no-joke - there was a line out the door and all the way to the giant intersection a block away. Â Come on - what are you people even waiting for? There are a half dozen small, dirty, CHEAP, hole-in-the-wall ramen bars less than as many blocks away serving ramen that's orders of magnitude more delicious than what Ippudo will happily charge you $20 for. Â  You know, this is your basic supply/demand at work. Â BECAUSE you wait in line for hours to get expensive, mediocre ramen, Ippudo can charge an arm and a leg for mediocre ramen. Â We've created a monster, perhaps. Â Unfortunately, it's like voting: mine alone doesn't matter, and nothing short of a mass-exodus will bring this food-relationship back to parity. So, first thing: let's talk ramen. Â Sure, the general, base ramen costs around $15 or so....more expensive than other places but not egregious. Â However, if you want basically ANYTHING in your bowl, it's an extra $2-3 per item. Â That adds up quickly. Â What I noticed was that the broth, itself, was a bit bland, so we splurged extra for the pork belly and some other items, which made the bowl too rich to consume. Â Can't win, i suppose. Â Perhaps if you go this route and "build" your perfect bowl, go easy on the add-ins. Â your belly and wallet will thank you. So what, then, are you paying for? Â Well the ambience, My Pretty. Â Every dark, classy, shi-shi atmosphere comes with a pricetag. Â Personally, I don't love the idea of eating ramen at a fancy-looking restaurant (regardless of how laid-back they try to make their classy-ness look), because ramen should be consumed on a stool, at a counter, next to a vat of boiling water and noodles, as the steam fogs up your glasses and you wonder if that A-grade health rating posted on the window was earned or purchased. Â You know, as God intended. Â However, the team at Ippudo likely worked very hard to create the dark, sexy, ramen den you will be eating your noodles in. Â  Saving grace? Always. Â Though there is a lot about Ippudo that I do not like, they did give me one wonderful, precious thing very dear to my heart: Â They introduced me to unfiltered sake. And I've never gone back since. Â Seriously - you want the best deal in this joint? Get a large carafe of unfiltered sake - guaranteed to get you and your date (even if he's a big man) a little tipsy for the bargain price of $18. Why? 1. it's just tastier and more interesting than regular sake 2. you can actually get nearly the same deal if you bought it at the liquor store and consumed it at home, which is basically unheard of when you're buying drinks at a restaurant. Â Good value? Check. Done.

Yes - it is true, sometimes, food does live up to the hype in the press. Â I refused to go at lunch time with all of the sheeple (ok, I am being rude, but lines down the block freak me out - unless the people are in vintage Star Wars costumes). Â So, I waited until the week after opening and got a coconut tiger shrimp sandwich to take home for dinner. A short wait, where I watched the tall, cute owner/chef talk to the staff and customers. Â This guy really likes his job, and likes to promote his good, fresh food. Â I really hope that they sustain that outlook, their great ingredients, and that this little hole in the wall stays in the neighborhood for a long long time. Â Yes, $8.00+ is a bit much for a 6" sandwich, but this ain't Subway. Â You are paying for quality and taste. Three days later... WOW! Â On a whim, I ordered the grilled corn with chili mayo, coconut flakes and chili powder. It was amazing. Â I can only wonder how it will blow my socks off when corn is in season. Â I will try it again in July and you may hear my screams of joy echoing through the tri-state area. And the catfish is great as well. Â Well seasoned, slightly spicy, moist, juicy with the home made sweet soy sauce. Â Get used to these updates, because I am going to eat my way through the menu over the next month or so. Â My only criticism - get the corn to eat in. Â Having it wrapped in paper to go makes it really embarrassing when you are sitting at your desk and licking the foil - just to get that last drop, and some one walks into your office... Â (take it from one who has been there!) Next, I'll try their big restaurant, Kampuchea. A month later... I am in shock, because I just paid $15.25 for a sandwich. Â Their new Lump Crab meat Sandwich was advertised on the chalkboard on the side walk, and I missed the 1 in front to the five in the $15.00 sandwich.... Â Verdict - the sandwich is GREAT - but I am still kicking myself for paying $15.25. Â Shudder... The only reason I am not docking them a star is because the sandwich is good, and it was my fault for not reading carefully.
Lovelovelove their pizza!!! Delicioso!!! Give it a try-you'll be hooked!!!

I live within proximity of Bocca Lupo and have been an avid fan since it opened up. I was also pleasantly surprised to have discovered the location in one of the episodes of Damages. It appears that the show does a lot of shooting in Carroll Gardens, sorry, I am way behind on my TV watching, maybe by years. That said, Bocca Lupo is an outstanding little restaurant with a lot to offer, it's got a terrific corner location in prime Carroll Gardens, the restaurant space in my opinion would benefit from noise dampening ceiling tiles. As when the restaurant is near capacity which can happen at any night, conversations over the 2'x2' ft tables can turn into near shouting matches. But regardless of this inconvenience, the food at Bocca Lupo is fun, and spirited. Their paninis are superb, can't go wrong with any of them, as per many reviews on this site. The staff is attentive and over the years have done their best to accommodate late comers, as they don't take reservations.
sesame cream brulee soooooo amazing

One of the most delicious fried foods!! yum, yum.... fries with the largest variety of dipping sauces. we tried the frite sauce, sweet mango chutney mayo and roasted garlic mayo. the belgium fries were fried to perfection... the variety of sauces made it completely unique.... a perfect snack after walking and shopping through east village!!

My experience took place sometime after 11 o'clock on a Saturday night, and it was awesome! If you are trying this for the first time, I strongly recommend the chicken & lamb with rice plate. Just add white sauce, mix and you are in heaven. Warning: the red sauce has a pretty good burn so don't go crazy with it if you are a fan of spicy.

Eating extremely spicy food is akin to a religious experience. Order dan dan noodles with a side of spicy cucumbers. Redolent in chili oil, the pair makes for a solid start - days later, I'm still delirious from the stuff. Be sure to request an appropriate heat level from your server, just in case you want things turned up a notch (or not). Chef Han Chiang consistently delivers, replicating his success at multiple Philly locations, finally branching out to NYC's East Village. If you're familiar with his restaurants down south, you won't be disappointed here. If you love Sichuan food, it's party time at Han Dynasty. There's room for a crowd, so bring friends.

I've eaten here many times in Brooklyn and Harlem. Overall the BBQ is above average however I come here primarily for the wings. Â As usual they did not disappoint. The hoisin are a welcome change from the usual buffalo or BBQ wings served elsewhere.
Just not crazy about the setup, glad we checked it out, just not into it.

I was in the city for the weekend, visiting some friends, when they told me that we'd be going to the bar just across the street that Friday night. "We're just going across the street? But I'm only here for the weekend!" "That's such a Miami-attitude. You'll see." And I did see. This place was AMAZING, and now I'm extremely jealous that its right across from their buildings front door. We went pretty late so I didn't get to try their food, but everyone around us was drinking anyways. I found that the bar was fully-stocked, the service was friendly, and the prices were fair. The crowd was an interesting mix and the place had an extremely laid back vibe. It's a MUST-STOP for anyone in the neighborhood.

Cool place. I went for the oyster happy hour and happily got there as soon as it opened - because an hour later it was packed. We ordered off the happy hour oyster menu because we wanted to try the others, and I was happy we did. That being said, the happy hour makes it too crowded! I'd go back .
Favorite place ever! Â Do the chefs table, you will thank me :)

My standby breakfast and luncheon place in the hood. Their omelettes are elite. Goat cheese, brie, scallion, chorizo is my normal rotation of mixers. And I must get this out of the way: the bacon. In a day where we have bacon cookies and Baconators, it could seem the pig to be an abused, neglected, even overshadowed art. Condessa, though, is bringing bacon back. It is an orgasm of fat and flavor in my mouth, which I can honestly say is the only thing to hold that noble distinction. And of course, it's a pleasing, unassumingly cool place. It channels some of that chic Bohemian vibe, without being that 3rd rate Bohemian we all too often see in the city. Their salads are also really, really, ridiculously good looking. Seriously, I've only ever oggled them (aside from the house side salads, which are pretty great).
The food was hearty and flavorful, the service was prompt and friendly, and the atmosphere was tasteful and quiet. Yes, you CAN visit Cuba legally, and you should.

I'm not Italian, but love Italian food, so what do I know? Â We dropped in during our visit to NYC to try it out and except for the loudness, we loved the food. Â Had individual portions of Tony's chicken and the escarole served with it, which we'd never eaten, was great. Â We loved to place and plan to visit again when we return to NYC.

I think this place is getting such high reviews due to how out of the way it is for everyone. It's good don't get me wrong but it's by far not the best of any category. It would get an other star from me if their savings in rent was displayed in the pricing of the food. It's small leading to long waits and the staff seems to be overwhelmed at times. I will be back and see if the food earns them an other star.
Solid takeout at a great price. Would highly recommend for a quick bite or casual delivery.
Breakfast , Dinner Â great, Dessert

The ambience is much nicer than most standard ramen places with darker lighting and a cherry blossom centerpiece. The ramen is delicious with perfect noodle thickness and there were several flavors to choose from (as opposed to Setagaya). I tried the Modern which was flavorful but not spicy but I prefer the original- Shiromaru. The side of roast pork over rice is also very tasty. Â I usually get the extra pork belly and egg which make the rameneven better! Â I don't understand the reviewers saying they weren't full- how could you not be full after a whole bowl of ramen- regardless of the taste. Â  I was here for the opening and Japanese TV was filming and asked to interview people about their experience and what they thought about the price. I think a few dollars more for better quality meat and a nicer ambience is definitely worth it. Service is generally quick and efficient- Â once you're at the table, sometimes there's a long wait depending on the time. Â I sometimes venture out to other ramen places, especially in the East Village like Rai Rai Ken, Setagaya, etc but Ippudo is so far my favorite.

This is my new favorite restaurant on Staten Island. From the decor to the dessert, I'm in love. Adorable outdoor eating area, exposed brick, PERFECT music all greet you upon walking in. Comfortable sized tables and super high ceilings. Getting to the important stuff, the food. Party of 5 ordered 3 appetizers: Mac and cheese : perfect. Calamari : capers and jalapeÃ±os?! Oh my goodness... French onion soup that you could tell was expertly made. Entrees we ordered: seafood risotto : gigantic portion. A little rich for my taste, but delicious. Short ribs : recommended by our waiter and we're incredibly tender with layers and layers of flavor. Duck breast : again, layers of flavor and tenderness (outstanding chutney on top too. Mmm). Prime rib : rivals the hardcore steakhouses on the island. Add on the exceptional service and delicious desserts (and watermelon sangria!!!), absolutely do not miss this gem. To long time islanders: the chef is formerly of the American Grill on forest avenue. No wonder it's fabulous. GO GO GO!!!!!

This place is amazing! I have been wanting to come here for years and finally the opportunity presented itself! Â I'm so glad that it did. I work at PUBLIC Restaurant and in comparison this place does a great job in educating their servers. Â Our server was Jeremy. While he was young he was very knowledgeable and attentive but not overly so. Â We had 4 courses and got out for less than $200!! Â That's a steal if you ask me! Â I can't tell you how happy I am that we live so close and can walk there! Â The drinks at the bar are also awesome to watch being made and the bartender (while busy) was still very pleasant! Â I don't know if they can do a better job next time! Â I challenge them :)

Ippudo had a two and a half hour wait, so we tried Momofuku. We were seated right away by a courteous hostess. Our waiter was also very friendly. We ordered the ever popular steamed buns, roast duck, spicy sausage and scallops. While tasty, for $23 we got three (3)!! Three scallops!! The roast duck was tasty and had slightly more on the plate compared to the scallops. The steamed buns were good (i love pork, especially the fatty part) but at $10 for two (2) it was pricey. The Spicy sausage was unremarkable at $19. My bill came to $105 for three people and left me completely unfulfilled. I won't be going back. Ever.

Oh bubbys. You've got a photobooth and celebrity sightings but that has zero to do with your charm. Maybe it's the homemade pies or homey vibe of your food...whatever it is, id brunch here every weekend if possible.
Came for brunch. Contemporary nyc style restaurant serving cafeteria food. Â Crowded all the time. Great selection. Great portion size esp the salad. Make sure the servers are around you.

I've been to Walter's for drinks twice. The first time was great--perfectly mixed drink and super friendly bartender. The second time it was another bartender, he was not friendly, the drink tasted off and then he seemed to try and gip me out of 10 bucks. Â After trying to get his attention for a while--I asked for my receipt back since something seemed up with my change and instead of doing so he handed me another 10 dollars. No apology or anything. Awkward. The hostess here is always sweet and the food looks great but I will bypass sitting at the bar if I see bartender #2's workin.
One day I'll come here and the food will actually be warm.

I loved this place, a true Austrian gem in the city. We got there around 6 p.m. on a Tuesday, it was almost empty. By 7 p.m., every table was busy and there was hardly room to stand. So get there early! The food is delicious. Although packed with butter, everything tastes light. Awesome selection of beer - definitely enjoyed the Grossen (sp?). Also, this was some of the best and warmest service I've ever received in a NYC restaurant. If for nothing else, go for the Spaetzle! Sooo good. Can't wait to return.
Very traditional Korean cuisine, awesome food! No wonder the place is also busy pack with people. There is always a wait, but it is worth!

UPDATED I went back here, and they have really gotten it together. They are now changing the menu regularly, and the bartender Damon is quite the mixologist - fans of little branch, etc will enjoy drinking here. It's much calmer than Henry St. Ale House, which is nice - I had a delicious hangar steak (though a tad undercooked), and the chicken liver schmeer w/ cranberry compote. Yum! They have excellent steak, chicken, burgers, and many other good dishes, red snapper, lamb loin. I crave the steak though.The service is warm and personable, and the manager once bought us drinks because we sat at the bar and chatted about sports, which we'd all enjoyed.

I came here several times after a recommendation from a friend. It's a great dessert place and tea house, one of my favorites. The only con is that it is really small and you're basically elbow to elbow with the party over on the next table (unless you go during down-time). They have a wide selection of teas and desserts as well. I can never decide what I want, therefore, every time, me and my friend pick the "Chef's Selection Dessert Sampler," which the chef caters a surprise dessert menu to your tea selection. I have yet to be disappointed from the selection (since they give you many samples). My only wish is that they would be more informative on the samples, since some of them are so good, I would like to order the full-sized dessert. Overall, this is a great place. Highly recommended.
DELICIOUS. Pizza was on point, chewy crust and proportionally laid out ingredients that made me get all hot and bothered at the restaurant.

Spent quite a few hours here the other night, a lot of traffic but not too crowded early on..as the night when on that changed drastically Awesome bluegrass band on saturday afternoons And they have a bag of warm croutons as a bar snack..yum!

I came here with my two friends earlier today. The food was very delicious and the envioment was friendly. It may be small but it is worth it. It's also very affordable which is a big plus. I would like to visit again. *If you collect 15 cupons from them you get a free meal!* ^_^

I always come to this place for duck and today was a great disappointment, I order the duck leg w noodle as always; however, after have way of eating the noodle and while I was chewing the noodle, I felt something hard and found a silver piece steel. I almost swallow it, fortunately, it just scratch the inside of my mouth.... It will be a long time for me before I order food from here...

Terribly slow, inattentive service, pretty empty, and in a bad location (unless you're coming from the theatre). Â The waitress served one in our party the wrong beer (even after she questioned it). Â Overall, nothing special enough to go back to.
Besides de decor being so beautiful, our cheeseburger and fries were amazing! The mayo/herb sauce was delicious! I highly recommend this restaurant! The waiter was really nice too! Make reservations.

Literally a hole-in-the-wall Came here for dinner with a couple of friends for dinner. We were looking for something tasty, quick, and inexpensive and this place fit the bill. Seating is pretty limited, but we were lucky to get a table right when we walked in. The paper menus are fairly extensive for the size of the place, offering multiple types of noodles and appetizers. We all ended up ordering the same thing, the spicy beef noodle soup, except we switched up the types of noodles, alternating between hand drawn and shaved noodles. The noodles are served in plastic bowls and they came out fairly quickly. The quick lowdown: the broth was tasty, although sometimes the spiciness hit the wrong part of my throat and burned in a way I don't really like. I ordered shaved noodles and while they were good for the first five minutes, they started to fall apart and I was struggling to pick them up with my chopsticks. The beef was nothing to rave about. The meat was not the best cut and a little tough, but hey, it at least gave its flavor. Overall, a mediocre dining experience. Honestly, not my favorite bowl of beef noodle soup and while cheaper than most places, beef noodle soup isn't that expensive to begin with, so price isn't usually an issue. I might stop by again if I'm in the area again (which honestly, I probably won't be. The restaurant is so far out of the way). However, I won't be making a crosstown trip to grab a bowl of noodles.

Ate lunch here and was very happy! Had the beach salad and added shrimp. Don't like onion and they had no problem subbing more mango. Great portion and I loved it. Being from Memphis, all the Elvis memorabilia was fun to see. Quirky, fun place, a little hard to find at the end of the street.

This might be my favorite ramen place so far... I've had at least 3 different ramen soups and all were delicious. I had the Akamaru Modern, the spicy pork, and most recently their seasonal Shoyu Ramen, or as they call it their "1980s-style" ramen. I was worried that it wouldn't be as good as the first two, but it was even better! I also LOVE their pork/chicken buns. I think I prefer it with pork but both are good. It is amazingly soft and tender-both the bread and meat. And I like the spicy mayo and lettuce they put on it. Unusual, but heavenly. Also I love the decor of their interior. The only reason I didn't give them 5 stars is that their staff can be hit-and-miss; sometimes they're very kind but other times they can be rather stand-offish, maybe because they're so busy. I recommend going at lunchtime; usually it's too long of a wait when I've gone for dinner.

This is a place to return to since the menu changes almost daily. Food is fantastic and not your every day fare. First came with my wife and split a striped bass. Came back a second time with friends and split some of the appetizers - pig croquettes,

I made two trips to Williamsburg this weekend and this was stop one. Â I am not much of a brisket connoisseur, but everything about this place led to a great evening. Â The brisket tasted fantastic, the beers were ice cold (and went down with ease w/ the brisket) and we even saved room for slice pie between 3 friends. Â I'd perhaps pass on the pie if I went again, but everything else was great. Obviously the brisket is the star, but don't pass up the side dishes, like potato salad!.

This place has an amazing lunch special for $7 that includes a couple of appetizers. Comes out quick too. They deliver. One thing is that t he service here is not great, but it also isn't bad. Atmosphere is really cool and they have a cool bathroom lol. Not that I should be reviewing their bathroom. Anyway, I recommend this place.

My friends took me here for a late birthday dinner and I have to say I was quite impressed. Â I love the decor. Â Very romantic setting, great for dates. Â The staff was friendly and helpful. Â We had the Crab toast with lemon aioli to start. Â It was amazing!!!! Â The Pretzel dusted Calamari was good too. Â We also ordered the squash blossom pizza which was divine. Â You could taste the freshness and quality of the ingredients. Â  Â Definitely a must go!

I had a delicious brunch here last month, although the waiter was Extremely rude. Last night I tried their dinner and was very disappointed. The Hanger Steak was tough and uninspired. The Shepherd's Pie was thrown together. Our appetizers were better (fried oyster special and the white bean/anchovy mush). What saved the experience was our incredibly friendly waitress, which I was not expecting to find. This may be a good place for a snack and a glass of wine but not much else.

A group of came here and we made it in time for Happy Hour. Most of us drank the Caracas? - some mango drink with rum. It tasted like juice, but it was strong and still good. I had a good helping. The complimentary crispy flat chips - they were pretty heavy handed with the salt and it wasn't only me that thought this, but the whole group agreed that they were beyond salty. We didn't have any entrees, but just small bites and we had the following. French Fries, Beef Aioli - this was H and I's favourite dish of the night Shrimp Toast au Jus - this didn't do anything for me. It was cute to look at it. Brisket "Tots", Potato, Mustard - this was good, but the beef aioli with the fries....gosh, who needs ketchup? I actually was coming here for dinner, but had to cancel due to a change of plans, but I definitely will come here to try a full meal.

Awesome service great food and amazing decorum. I get to be picky though because I'm Lebanese and the Lebanese dishes were a bit of a fusion which is what the restaurant is going for... Brussel Sprouts though,,,,,,GET THEM!

Usually I love this place. My parents ask to come here every time they are in NYC. However be careful of their hours. Yelp and google list that it opens at 11am M-Sun and sadly it doesn't. We arrived Mon morning at 11:30 to a man waving us away. We are still unclear if it was going to even be open on Monday. Nook if you read this, please take the time to update your hours on the necessary web pages as to not disappoint your patrons. Cheers

The bread is to die for!!! I had the shrimp and grits which was amazing as well as the trout my friend had! We shared the pecan pie and that was also amazing! Great place if you want good southern soul food
Solid Option. This institution is super reliable. Love the live music. Definitely an older man crowd. Apparently the veggie burger is to die for - will get that next time.

Nice vibe. Waiter Matt was friendly & knowledgeable about their beer selections. Food: -Oysters were very fresh and very gooooood -Bouillabaisse had fresh fish and seafood but though it needs more herbs and seasoning for a clear broth. Overall nice! -Cod was really nice prepared. -Crab cakes were good. Service: Good Beers: Good This is a great seafood place. Go there you'll be very happy!
The reviews are true. This was seriously the best "Chinese" food I've had in manhattan. Family friendly. Awesome.

Nice place. Good atmosphere, though space is a little tight. I had the venison with pesto and it was pretty good. The brussel sprouts were great, I'd definitely order those again. I wasn't amazed by the food, but the nice atmosphere, quick service, and decent prices made for an overall solid dinner.

Everything about this place is down right great! From the customer service right down too the check.. I went here with my girlfriend and her best friend after church and I must say from the outside I was prejudice but as soon as you get to the backyard and sit to eat, it is an experience! Lucky for us it was a lovely day and the right temperature! I would imaging what the night ambiance is like! We started off with an appetizer (munch) which was a glorified powdered jelly donut but this wasn't any donut.. They added a special purÃ©e sauce which is referenced in the dish below and the donut is warm.. Once again it may not sound like much but trust me you will not be disappointed!! Now to the dishes: I ordered the chicken and waffles and it was amazing! There is this special purÃ©e sauce that they add to the dish that gives it an extra kick.. The waffles were the right size and the chicken is baked to perfection.. My girlfriend had the duck and this was my first time tasting it.. Can't really complain, enjoyed it for what it was but then again I'm not sure what duck is suppose to taste like! All I can say is that it was succulent and every bite was as good as the next one! Our mutual friend ordered the fish and chips, which may not sound like much but it blew me away! I was expecting fried fish battered and breaded but they actually bought a whole fish and baked it with French fries! (LIFE CHANGING) haha.. Overall I rate this place a 5 out of 5! Great for a social gathering or first date.. For all 3 of us the bill came up to $131.00.. Which I think is reasonable! And that is NOT including tip! Paying the bill too me is what set it over the top for me.. For my AMEX card holders, there is an app (if you are not already aware) called "cover". Basically you register with your name and your card and the waiter rings it up at the register by pulling up your check in name.. I thought that was pretty cool and quick!!

After waiting 6 months (anxiously) to find time to go to LadurÃ©e, I finally went today! Waiting in line just killed me. The lady in front of me bought box upon box upon box of macarons. It was as if she was made of money. Judging from the shopping bags she was carrying, (Louis Vuitton, Juicy Couture, and Gucci), she probably was made of money. After waiting about forever, I finally got to order! 1. 2 Rose Petals- Thought it was okay. I like the FranÃ§ois Payard's Rose Lychee one more. 2. 2 Blackcurrant & Violet- Sour, bit like jam. Tastes heavenly after a heavy, super sweet macaron, like the Vanilla or Coffee. 3. Orange Blossom- My FAVE! Sweet, and light. Tasted a hint of... jasmine? 4. Coffee- Eh. I liked it, but maybe I need to buy more to ... "taste" again. 5. Vanilla- Amazing. So good. Better than Bouchon's. The cream is so thick, and the shell compliments it so well. 6. Lemon- Tart... but balanced perfectly with the sweet shell. They ran out of chocolate and pistachio. Disappointed... Their boxes are to die for though... Hello Kitty boxes! SO CUTE

In all fairness, the pizza is good. Â But is it worth the wait? Â No. Â Juliana's down the street is the same pizza without the wait, and if you are willing to venture a little farther into Brooklyn, places like Lucali and Giuseppina's are even better. Â However, if you have friends who come into town and they are desperate to go to Grimaldi's, you will not leave hungry.
This place is amazing the food is excellent. The staff is awesome. Highly recommend it.

You have to come here to try the Crab dumpling. They are know for this. Â It is soo good. At first I order one order of the Crab dumpling and didn't realize how good it was. Â After I midway finish the 1st order I had to order another because it was that good. I also order a few other dishes here but it was ok. The food tends to be a little greasy but that's your typical chinese food. The restaurant is small and a little dirty but they are very busy. If you don't have a large party be prepare to share a table if your seated in one of the bigger tables. It's how' your typical asian restaurants are run if you came from Hong Kong. They have a lot of servers here so the service is quick. No matter what time you come here there is always a lot of people.
The tavern room now offers a $35 three-course prix fixe dinner.

This is the Place to BE! It be Poppin! We arrived around 7pm on a Sat and the tables were all full. But luckily it was still the dinner crowd to the turn around time is quick. We grabbed a table and send some people on line. At this point the line was only just by the awning about 4ft from the Garage door. I would say it was about 40-50 ft from the actual ordering counter. We were on line for an hour, an HOUR! The BBQ is DELICIOUS but a bit on the dry side in terms of cooking and sauce. We ordered a little of everything. One guy helped us weigh our food and he moved... at... a... snails.... pace... actually - I think the snail just passed him. You order by the lb and you watch him add on 2oz at a time.
