Just grab a heaping portion my man! The beers are served in cool mason jars. Don't be surprised if strangers ask to join you at your table. Although there are no smoking signs on the tables outside, people smoke. One poor pregnant lady had to keep moving around. Yes this place screams beer garden but please - keep in mind this is a restaurant and they close at 11, have consideration for other patrons. I like the place but given that you have to wait 1-2 hrs to get food, I'd rather head over to Radegast.

Eataly is a fun stop so long as you are not claustrophobic and don't mind the energetic and chaotic shopping scene. The space itself is beautiful and organized, all little markets within a market with narrow passageways designed to maximize the opportunity to herd visitors through all the little specialty shops for fish, meat, gelato, vegetables, bakery, coffee, etc. It's a place where you can buy anything you might need for your Italian home or commercial kitchen, from a biscotti pan to a beautiful blood orange to rows upon rows of olive oil to selections of $300+ 3 ounce bottles of aged balsamic vinegar. I especially enjoyed the double espresso and macchiato I had at the standup espresso bar Caffe Vergnano, which has a gorgeous Elektra Belle Epoque espresso machine. If you want to visit when it's less packed, try visiting around teatime to miss the lunchtime rush and accompanying lines.

Have been to Fette a few times. Great location and environs. The inside seating space fills up fast and there is often a wait for a seat either at the tables or the bar. Similarly, the food line can go out the door, but that just attests to how yummy the food is. You can easily empty your wallet though if you eat with your eyes, which is totally understandable! Brisket, various ribs are always good. The beans are amazing, and the sauces (especially the vinegar-based one) are perfect.

Great tasting korean food! They offer hot and cold buffet options weighed by the pound, and pre-packed hot and ready to go boxes/bentos of food. Usually very busy during most times of the day, especially during lunch time! It's fairly priced for NYC. They don't always serve the same things, they change it up and keep the foods varied, but they take into account which foods sell the most and keep it around for a long while. I think it's a great strategy for their type of restaurant. The staff are super friendly and even though the lines are usually long, they keep things moving smoothly. The only complaint I have is that it gets really hot and steamy in there. It's a small restaurant, and there's a lot of hot food and throw in crowds of people and it gets quite claustrophobic and sweaty. More often than not you won't find seats if you're in a group, although if you're by yourself, you have a better chance to sit and eat your food in peace. I highly recommend for lunch, for pick ups to go and take home, to stay and hang out with friends, and for exploring the Korean Cuisine without having to go to an expensive restaurant. Definitely have to try at least once, happy eating folks! :)

More like 3.5 stars. The place is small, it feels cramped. And it is very loud. We ordered the pork special, but when it arrived we realized it had 1 ounce of meat and 4 ounces of pure fat. They told us that there was no mistake: the Chef expects us to eat the fat too (and die of a heart attack before dessert, apparently). But they were gracious about offering to take the dishes away and bring us something else. So we played it safe and ordered their chicken dish, which turned out to be piping hot (don't know how they get a chicken to be this hot. We could not touch it for several minutes), huge, and pretty good. It was supposed to be served with some sort of risotto, which was not really one (not creamy), but it was still enjoyable. Overall, it was an OK dinner, but not memorable.

Amazing restaurant. Has a great vibe and its difficult to get reservations. The margaritas hit the spot! The vegetarian food was terrific. We had their Mexican corn on the cob and guacamole. The mushroom tacos were great as well. The restaurant does get noisy but in a nice way. I would certainly go back again.

7/23/14 Food: 3 stars Mega ramen- the mega ramen wasn't bad, it just wasn't good. The char siu was burnt and the ramen cook's sweat was in my ramen. I only know this because the hostess seated us at the counter, which is located 5 feet away from the hot stoves and pots cooking your ramen. The restaurant is not air conditioned and only has a few small fans to circulate the air, so it felt like 100 degrees to me. For the chefs, it must have been even hotter being closer to the stoves. This caused the chef to sweat profusely. Every 10-15 minutes he'd use his gloves to grab a paper towel to wipe his sweat from his face, then continue to place the contents of your ramen inside their respective bowls using the same gloves that he used to wipe the sweat from his face. Service: 1 star The ramen was more expensive and less tasty than what I expected, so I gave our server the cash for our meal and a 10% cash tip. After all, we were underwhelmed with our experience. She returned with the cash we had left as tip for her and whispered into my wife's ear "this doesn't include tip". As we got up to leave she said "wait", she literally jumped in front of me, blocking my exit from the restaurant, counted the cash tip we had left her right in front of my wife, then said "Was there a problem with the service?". I didn't see her count our tip and didn't hear her tell my wife that our money didn't include tip, so I didn't realize she wanted more money. So, I politely told her that "There wasn't a problem with the service, we just didn't care for the ramen". Looking bemused, she repeated "so there wasn't a problem"? Â I repeated "No". She looked upset and out of ideas to guilt us into leaving more money for her. I can overlook the chef having an off night burning our food, but the server having the gall to confront us about leaving a tip which reflected our experience is the reason I won't be giving them another chance.

Awesome little joint in BK. With a friend, we split a green pizza, which was okay, nice and cheesy. We also split the chickpea salad, which was fine, but cold, and contrasted with the rest of our meal in that way. We also each got the falafel sandwich, which was incredible, filling but not too much so, just great. I just wish da place served booze.

Wow, what a surprise. Went here for brunch and shared the Mediterranean sampler an order of the Shashouska w/meurguez. Everything was tasty and fresh. The staff was super helpful with recommendations and have to say, I was happy with her decisions. Would def recommend coming her with a friend or two who like sharing!

I Have eaten here twice, once for lunch and once take out. Place is really cute and the food it great. Looks like it might get busy after Â work, and your might not be able to get a seat. The messed up my to go order and the I was fine with it, but the boss would not have it corrected it right away. The place lost a point on the size and comfort factor.

Went last week, just ok, the happy hour deal is a good deal, waited 40 mins and was still able to order one round. Â The mussels had sand in it and the rest of the food wasn't very flavorful. Â Oysters were good, but I've definitely had better at aquagrill, mermaid, and grand central amongst others. Â Staff were hit or miss, some really friendly ones and some with attitude.
You have to get that Fisherman's bowl.

I really give this place 3.5 stars. Â My friend and I came for brunch this weekend; we shared the baked eggs and the basque scramble, along with the fries that come with Gorgonzola fondue (aka small dish of melted cheese). Â I would describe the food as good enough to finish the rather large portions you get, but not so overwhelming that I would rave about it to other people. Â If you sit outside, it's a very nice ambiance, and a relaxing way to spend your Sunday morning if you're in the west village. Â Yet the tables are too close together and the ice coffees are too small. Â I've had better, and most likely you've had better too.

Have had only take out and just the four meat lasagna on several occasions. Â If that is any indication of the remainder of the menu, then I absolutely can't wait until I make an actual physical trip to the establishment. Â Maybe for their weekend brunch, as I have heard absolute great things about it!

O...M...G... this burrito is sooo hitting the spot! I wish i would've taken a picture of the size of this monster b/c it truly was huge . Â ...that's right, i said "was". Â I took me two attempts, but i was finally able to finish this puppy off! Â Luckily for me, i'm expecting twins so no one dares make a comment at the amount of food i'm eating or how many lunches i need to have :) I got the grilled steak burrito with a side of guac & order of salsa & chips. Â YUM!!! A couple of my coworkers got the chili con carne burrito and were equally as pleased. Â The chilli in this case, means the chilli peppers and not chilli meat. Â They said their burrito had the perfect amount of heat and sauce inside. I take one star away b/c i feel the guac is a bit overpriced: Â $1.10 for a "jello-shot" of guac... why are they not as generous in this as they are with their humongo burritos? oh well, guac aside - this place is def the shiz when in the mood for a burrito.

I have been coming here for years. They used to be just a regular cart on the streets of Chinatown until they finally opened their own store a few years ago. I was so happy when I saw this lovely husband and wife couple dishing out quality chinese food for such an affordable price. Although most people rave about the value of their bbq meats over rice, my review is more for the rice noodle rolls smothered in soy sauce and peanut butter sauce. It is soooo addicting!! The noodles are pretty standard and yes other carts in Chinatown serve the exact same "churng fun", but there is something in their sauce that keeps me coming back. I always have them add extra peanut butter sauce because i feel like it brings the taste to a whole new level.And don't forget the fish balls Â :) Best of all is the price... You get soo many noodles for an amazing cost. If you buy the small, white styrofoam containers, it's only $1.50!! Problem with that is, when they put the sauce in, it leaks everywhere in the bag and causes a big mess. SOLUTION: pay 50 cents more and get it in the small plastic containers. You get a little more noodle anyway. Go and try this place! But beware, the lines are usually long but if you're just getting the churng fun, walk right past the bbq line into the little store. You'll be thanking me when you try it for the first time.

Went here to meet some co-workers, so was already going into the evening with low expectations--but it ended up being way less terrible than I thought! The place was pretty quiet, but it was snowing like crazy out, so I'm sure that had something to do with it--but it was nice having the place to ourselves. The bartender was warm and attentive, and answered all my annoying questions without seeming annoyed. The menu's pretty standard bar food, but they did have a deal where you can get a burger, fries, and a beer for $10. I didn't get that but a few other people did and the burgers were HUGE and looked legit. My friend had the black bean burger and said it was the best veggie burger he's had in years. I didn't eat any of it, but did have some of his fries, which were so good, like I would go and just order fries (if I was the kind of person that did that) I ended up just splitting some quesadillas with a friend, which were ok, not wonderful, but that's my fault for getting quesadillas in an Irish pub-type place, Next time I'll just get the burger and fries and deal with the emotional consequences of eating so many calories. Also the music was great, song after song came on that I loved and felt like I hadn't heard in forever...also set at that perfect volume where you can enjoy it but don't have to strain to hear whatever dumb story your friend is telling. I don't know if it was the bartender's personal playlist or what, but I dug it. My co-worker complained at one point when "Streets of Philadelphia" came on because he didn't want to think about Tom Hanks dying while he was out drinking, but think that was just his attempt to be funny. It wasn't really.

This place is more of a 3.5 stars place, but I'll just be generous and round up. HK Wonton Garden is one of the best places to get a nice and filling bowl of wonton soup in NYC (that I've found so far). Prices are incredibly low and service is decent enough. It's a nice little hole in the wall, usually filled with a mixture of locals and tourists. All of the waiters wear Hawaiian shirts which is kind of strange, but endearing. I've had the beef stew wonton soup and the pork and chive dumpling soup. Both were fantastic and satisfying. I haven't tried the other dishes on their menu, but would recommend skipping out on the dim sum (which I have tried here) as it's just subpar here and you will find much better fare at many other places in Chinatown. My only gripe with HK Wonton Garden is the fact that they tack on a "service charge" on the bill. Prices are low enough so you may not even notice it on the bill, but do take a closer look and you will see that they add tax and then another mysterious charge. When we inquired about this, the waiter gruffly told us it was a 'service charge'....meaning they just add the tip onto the bill. I was pretty thrown off by this and I assume it's because they've had people skip out on tip before? Either way, it's not something I was very fond of as it wasn't labeled at all and if we hadn't asked, we would've added tip on top of this charge. I'll come back if I'm ever in the area and need a quick bite to eat, but will definitely be more conscious of the bill and other charges in the future.

So I decided to brave the blizzard and trek back over to Roberta's to sample another pizza. Since I had the Margarita pizza the last time I decided to add some meat into the mix and get the R.P.G. pizza. I'm just happy that I didn't pay for it, cause the pizza was meeehhh at best. While the dough/crust was great the actual toppings/seasonings were lackluster.

Was here recently and enjoyed it. I spent nearly a year in Belgium, so it was nice to go to a Belgian establishment. There were three of us and we were sat quickly. We ordered our beers and were complimented on our proper pronunciation. That was nice. They have a good selection of the usual Belgian beers on tap and in bottles. The food was fine, but I've had better in Belgium. When I was there they didn't have one of my favorites: stoemp. I need to go back for the mussels and steak frites. The atmosphere was nice. Relaxed and such.

We went here after wedding and had a great time. Â It is a 30-40 yo something crowd with excellent food, drink and ambiance. It is a bar with lots of tables and good food. Â Very casual. Â Great decorations and lots of history. Â The wait staff is very friendly. Â  We had steamed mussels and a spicy shrimp dish to start. Â  I had a burger which was excellent. Â Others at our table had linguini with shrimp in a lobster sauce, and steaks. Â The linguini dish was exceptional. Â The steaks ok, but needed seasoning. Â The prices are excellent with most dishes $12 or less!!!!! I know I should know this but I think it is an English pub. Â  It is a great place to take a group of friends. Â We will go back.

What better way to spend a day with someone you care a lot about than perusing Williamsburg for food and entertainment? My cousin and I have always been very close because we have so many things in common - one of which, is our love of food. When she suggested Le Barricou for Sunday brunch, I was eager to try it, having read many glowing Yelp reviews. Off we went, to Williamsburg, to eat, drink, and catch up. I am a sucker for quaint little towns. Le Barricou is situated on your quintessential old-Brooklyn-type block - many of the storefronts still look a bit old-fashioned. Yuppies galore. Street parking was ample. The wait was about an hour, but well worth it. The restaurant was bustling with people having drinks and conversations. Yuppies and hipsters crowded the storefront, waiting for a table inside. The bar inside and the decor on the walls was beautiful and indicative of the old-world vibe. The tables and chairs were simple. My only complaint is that the seating was a bit cramped, but, promotes conversation with perfect strangers, some of which are very nice. To our left, two girls from the area who complimented my spiked flats from Bakers. To our right, a father and daughter who seemed to be arguing the entire meal (you can't win them all, right?) He told the waitress to lower the music on three separate occasions - yes, that kind of annoying. The meal was great - spinach and goat cheese croissant. The croissant was tasty, the goat cheese was high quality, and the side of fries complimented well. Iced coffee in mason jars was a nice touch. My one complaint - if you have to use their bathroom, it's in the back through the doors. There was a crowd by the bathroom when we got there because it's a one-room deal, no communal bathrooms. A plus: at one point, it got so crazy, that no one really cared if you used the men's or women's bathroom. Adjacent to the bathrooms is an ATM - always convenient. It also looked like they had an outdoor patio area, but it was very small. I can't wait to go back.

I was one of their first customers, initially they started as a pop up at the same location they are now, then I guess secured the lease and are now in there permanently. Back then they were BYOB, those were the days... However, Brisket Town is still one of the best bbq spots in the city. Both eat in and take out are exceptional. They sent us a pre made meal for xmas with mains and sides that just needed to be put in the oven, everything was perfect. The brisket and smoked turkey is also ideal leftover food, and remains in my fridge to this day. A little on the expensive side, but so is every BBQ place in the city worth eating at. I will Â continue to recommend Brisket Town to anyone listening.
one word amazing

Lan Zhou is a tiny noodle outpost in the thick of Chinatown. Enter the small quarters and you'll be greeted with a food + show experience. You'll see a man tossing up handmade noodles much like the old pizza parlours of days past. You'll also see dumplings being hand rolled. In this joint, authenticity rules the day - I haven't tasted beef noodle soup like this since my childhood visits to Taiwan. The broth is savory, not too oily or salty - refreshing change from the increasingly "touristy" joints that surround busy Canal street. Lan Zhou is not for the reticent...not for the timid tourist. Go here for the grub, not for the service. As you enter - take a quick look at the menu posted on the wall and simply shout out your order. If you sit idely waiting for someone to take your order...you will sit there forever. My recommendations are the classic beef noodle soup and for the more adventurous- the beef tendon soup. At $4.75 a pop this has got to be the best deal in town! Even in Chinatown. Finally, an order of fried dumplings are also a must-have - and make sure to take home a bag of dumplings - $8 bucks for a bag of freshly made pork dumplings.

Great food, decent service. Had the steak, which was excellent, though not the best i've had in my life. Latin music in the background but not a single cuban song. The mojito was small and full of ice, didn't really amount to the restaurant's name :) Since it's located at a hotel's lobby, the happy hour party, drinking in the afternoon, looked like a real HAPPENING. it was good, but i probably won't be back here again until i go to all the other restaurants in the city.

This is sexy vietnamese food. It's cheap. It's tasty. It's fast. Usually, vietnamese food shouldn't take very long to prepare. But even when this place gets really crowded, they're still fast. I'm almost sure that they have a time machine. Pork summer rolls? Yes. My clothes are coming off. The lemongrass chicken over vermicelli (or rice) really gets me going. It's tender, perfectly charred, and delicious. I get too excited when I eat this. When I finish, I gently slip into a food coma. The Banh Mi. So yum. When I eat it, I hear it speaking to my soul. Pho. Phorreals so good. Whenever I'm freezing around campus, I eat this hot loving goodness and it's like all my childhood dreams are being fulfilled.
i waited for over an hour for a table and then got way over charged on my bill. all together the food was not worth the hassle.

Spaghetti, tomato, basil. Â That's it. Â That's the description on the menu. To put it as simply as that: Â it's the best we've ever had. Â Period. Â Here, Italy, Little Italy, wherever. Â And it's indicative of the place. Â Simple, tasteful, delicious. Â Polenta with truffled mushrooms? Â Richer than Bernie Madoff used to be, but for real. Â The Agnolotti is a confluence of tastes that evince smiles. Â The turbot makes you think Le Berna-where? Â  Â  Â The wine list is comprehensive without being arrogantly overwhelming and features plenty of reasonably priced offerings. Â Our bottle of 2004 Amarone was a happy result of a few minutes of discussion with our server. Â  Â  The bar scene is alive and fun before or after dinner. Â The service is helpful but not cloying, condescending or annoying. Â The room is comfortable. Â  Â Put down that can of tomato sauce & run to Scarpetta. Â No, seriously, do it.
So.good. We all finished every last bit of our food. The risotto and bolognese were soooooo delicious. I had amaretto gelato that was so good I would go back just for that! Great neighborhood gem!

If you are from the school that a cocktail is just a cocktail, this place will educate you in the creation of well-mixed, perfectly blended drinx. Â A friend of a friend said this was her favorite place in all of NYC. Â I believe her. Â One cocktail turned into four, because I wanted to taste them all. Â I started with the Pimm's Cup and then I had the West Side. Â Yummy. Â You can't taste the alcohol in the Long and Fancy works of art with alcohol. Â Henry one of the men who make this place what it s stood behind the bar and made his own recommendations- he even made me a custom drink that was soooooooooooo delicious. I didn't even ask what he put in it. Â The drinks are magical and reason enough to come by EO. Â The speakeasy that makes drinkin' easy.

As a Californian, I never understood why New Yorkers went on and on about how great their pizza was until I finally tried the pizza at Patzeria Perfect Pizza. Perfect is an understatement... I have cast my official vote for my favorite NYC pizza and so far and this is it. Don't worry... I will keep an open mind to trying some other places if other yelpers swear that there is a place that is the end all be all, God or Goddess of NYC pizza. However, be forewarned, I've already acquired a huge bias for this place already, just like I'm sure you have for your own neighborhood joint. I only order by the slice here. I'm not sure how the big pies are but I do know that the slices are thin crusted and crunchy, not at all soggy, just the way I like it. The toppings are fresh and their sauce has the perfect amount of garlic. So... In closing, if you're in the area, I definitely recommend stopping in for a slice. And the lasagna is not too shabby either!

If you grew up in the New York metro area during the 50s and 60s - and miss your local Italian restaurant - by all means visit Benito One. The food is excellent, and the service superb. The produce used in the bruschetta and salads is fresh, and the home-made pasta dishes are great. The afternoon maitre d', Joe, will take good care of you!

Fantastic service! Host was incredibly welcoming, waiter was friendly and on point. They gave us extra complimentary olives and arugula for the 3 vegetable mix appetizer, chocolate at the end of the meal, and limoncello to end the night. Atmosphere made us feel like we were in the 1940s, loud chatter but enjoyable. Decor was quirky with pastel mint, coral, ochre walls decorated with oversized sculpture reliefs of parts of the body. We ordered the spaghetti of the night-white wine spaghetti with clams, the veal scallopine piccata, and the tordello bolognese. Unfortunately, everything was too salty for our taste! ***The service was amazing***

The food was great! Wait was kinda long an hour and a half. I had a brunch special chocolate chip banana biscuit french toast. It was delicious. My friend had a biscuit with a sunny side egg and cheese and on the side potatoes. He also had the spicy margarita. One of the best parts was the endless coffee!

Sakagura is a classic, upscale Japanese restaurant that is NOT sushi-oriented. Read: no california rolls or spider hand rolls here. If you're used to very Americanized Japanese food, this place is going to surprise and confuse you. We had the tofu salad, which pleased a vegetarian and a non-vegetarian. I loved the eggplant served with 3 kinds of miso, very diverse flavor palate. My friend had the fresh salmon sashimi don, which was very good as well due to fresh and well sliced sashimi (it's a skill!). The only thing I wasn't super impressed by was the dessert. We got earl grey ice cream and sesame ice cream. I'm a huge fan of sesame ice cream, but this one just tasted like vanilla ice cream with pieces of sesame in it. Lame sauce. The atmosphere is super Japanese. Clean and orderly and efficient. Service was fine, but I'm used to getting impeccable service at Japanese restaurants so the service level here was actually below my expectations.

I've always said you know it's good chicken when you get past the skin and the meat is still flavorful. Pio Pio got it right. I heard about this place and their green sauce from a number of people. When my boyfriend said someone mentioned it to him, I thought, we have to go here we're missing out on something. Boy, were we. I was in awe the moment I walked in. This location is huge, and I love the creative eco-friendly design. I felt like I was in a medieval Peruvian castle sitting in the big wooden chairs upstairs overlooking a huge dining area down below. But enough about the decor. We ordered the Matador Combo to share. A whole rotisserie chicken, rice and beans, avocado salad, fried plantains, french fries with salchipapas and that infamous green sauce all for $30.00 (feeds two or even three if you're a light eater) you can't beat that - OK maybe you can but I haven't seen it yet. We ate and ate and asked for a doggie bag when we couldn't eat anymore. We went here on a Monday night; it was pretty empty which was good because I was licking my fingers and smacking my lips like I was at a back yard BBQ. We also ordered a half pitcher of Sangria, which was the only thing that I was not impressed by. It was really sweet and tasted like a syrup mix. I should have ordered one of the drink specials that our waitress recommended. I would definitely recommend this place for a group event (I'm thinking about having my birthday dinner here), the space is huge, the food is good, the portions are large and the price it right.
Love! Wish there were more options like this out there. So cool to have the paleo spin. Also, there is yummy treats and take homes to bring into the kitchen at home!!

Situated a few blocks away from the noisy and overpriced Stone Street drinking area, this bar's interior resembles that of a bar in a mountainous small town and would be perfect for filming a sequel to "The Shining". However, the bartender was very friendly, as long as you did not make derogatory comments about "soccer" and the Irish national team (at which point, she makes threats about closing you out of the bar). While their other customers mostly kept to themselves, some were sleeping on shaky bar-stools and would wake up to ask for another round of beer, but concerns about personal safety never surfaced. Overall, drinks are very cheap for the area, especially the 5$ beer+shot special for those who had a tough day at work hopping from one wild-goose chase to another. Definitely a recommended area.

It was just A-OK. Nothing awesome. They were good fries. I'm assuming slightly bit healthier as well, even if it's fried in all that glorious oil. Pricing's not that bad. It's a specialized little street food, and the cost to keep that hole in the wall running, with workers, fresh potatoes, and vast amounts of sauces, it's reasonable. Pricing for a small cone of fries - $4.50, which can easily be lunch or split between two people. The thing that makes this place special is the vast variety in dipping sauce (20-30 kinds), all of which are $1.00. Coming as a group definitely helps in getting to try more sauces. The fries themselves were not all that salty, but I don't know. Feels like just alright fries. Lets get real: It's a hole in the wall. If you're expecting service, pay up and go to a restaurant. The guys here will do their job: 1) ask you what you want, 2) Do it as soon as possible and efficiently. It gets a little busy sometimes, so if they mess up, be cool and they'll make a change for you. Tip them ONLY if you feel they've done a little more than that. There's a small seating area in the back (fitting maybe 8-13 people), if you're lucky to get a seat and sit down to do nothing. Would I go back here desperately to try the fries? No. Only other time this place would come into my head would be probably as an appetizer before dinner/lunch, or something to eat before a night at the bar (and there are SO many bars around--it makes sense). Minus two stars because: -Nothing special. It was okay. -The sight of all that fresh oil sorta makes me ehhhh... -Yea, it's street food, it's a whole in the wall, but still. Looks of a place can sometimes bring scores down.

Maialino was good but not as awesome as I expected. The wine and wine steward were amazing. She presented me with 4 wines to taste and we discussed each one. Her recommendations were spot on. The food portions were adequate but the flavors were not as robust and complex as I expected. The next time I'm in NYC and craving Italian, I will try Lupa.

Sicillian Pizza huh? FANTASTIC. I never had pizza with the tomato sauce on top of the cheese instead of Â under but I learned to never say never and try this awesome pizza. WARNING: The flavor is addictive and you might lose count of how many slices you devoured due to the great taste. It's like the tomato sauce and the palate go hand-in-hand. Every slice I ate stirred up the neurons and taste buds to create a blissful harmony. By the way, if you still have room, make a quick stop to the Spumoni ice cream stand next door for some great dessert.

i came here a few weeks back, the waitress on a thursday evening was very lovely and welcoming. i had ordered a pasta dish, she was nice enough to split the portion for two. Â above and beyond for service. very unique style thin pizza. Â loved it.

This place is secretive and makes a point to be so. I must admit that NYers love this sort of thing and totally seek out the hard-to-find destinations. In order to get the number at Bohemian you either need to obtain it from a friend who has it or email them directly. They don't accept walk-ins, only phone reservations. My date and I shared a few dishes. We started with the fresh vegetable platter with a fondue sauce. All of the veggies were super fresh and delicious and the presentation was gorgeous. Next we had the uni mushroom croquettes then fish egg/uni and rice and finished with the garlic shrimp. Everything was well done, but in the end I actually expected more. For a restaurant which makes itself out to be so exclusive, their product didn't match my expectations. I expected spectacular, but only got good. I wasn't blown away by any of the dishes and for the price I honestly would rather take my money to another high end NY establishment. Sorry Bohemian, the atmosphere sure is cool, but the food wouldn't bring me back.

My friends and I were visiting NY for the first time and wanted a true "Chinatown" experience, and that's exactly what we got! I've never had hand-pulled noodles, and I'm already craving more! I, personally, had the #2 (Beef in hot & spicy soup) and it was delish! I also had an order of the dumplings which were to die for! My group also had the #23 and the #14 and they both loved it! Â  The only cons I would have would be the size of the restaurant, it has very limited seating, and that its cash only. Bring a couple bucks and you're good to go! Wonderful food, wonderful experience! Will definitely stop by again when in NY.

A bit overrated and not all that impressive. Best dish was the gnocchi. Um, if that was the best dish this place could offer, then I would suggest others to look elsewhere. Fish was bland and tasteless and the salad was a basic salad. I have had better salads at Chop't. It's expensive for mediocre food and mediocre service.

This is my first Yelp review, and I'm not a pro. It's worth noting, I'm not here to shill for Anella, either. Â I'm giving three stars, described by Yelp as "A-OK", though, I think, for the sake of accuracy the "A" should be left out. Rather, I'd say this place is just "OK" at best. Anella is a C student on the Brooklyn/Queens restaurant scene, and I'll tell you why. Anella has all the pretense and menu-source hyperbole of a so-called world class neighborhood joint, but on my visit for brunch there was all of the price and none of the quirky ingredients and spot on prep. To start, I ordered a glass of orange juice. I swear I was served some kind of consumer variety Tropicana. To be fair, the menu didn't boast fresh juice, but it was $3, and the rest of the menu indicated attention to fresh and local. I feel like if a place is going to cut corners, or break consistency, it should at least be proud of the fact. I don't want a rooftop grown salad on my plate and jug OJ in my glass! For whatever reason, I decided to order the burger. I suppose a burger is something of my litmus test for whether a place is going to thrive. I ordered my burger medium rare, another test of whether service is adequate. I asked for cheese and was given two options: blue and fontina. I opted for fontina, though it's not my first choice for burger topping. After a long wait, after other diners had arrived, ordered and been served, my burger arrived, cooked nearly well done. After all the waiting I certainly wasn't going to send it back. I asked for mayo and ketchup. I was given ketchup and an apology instead of mayo. I persisted. I took my first bite of burger, and, to my surprise, it wasn't half bad! I'm not saying there is any excuse under the sun for serving an overcooked burger, it's not rocket science, but it tasted pretty decent. The menu said something about an "angus blend" which I assume means they're careful to control the fat content of the patty. It was fat content that saved this burger. Had it been 90 percent lean, no amount of non-existent mayo would have saved it. As it turned out, it was still juicy and flavorful, despite being poorly cooked and kinda hard. Loved the bun (toasted brioche) and actually loved the fontina. I wasn't impressed with the accompanying mixed greens, they were of the gourmet deli variety, common to all middle-class New Yorkers, though, they weren't offensive. Worth noting, greens arrived well seasoned. I was initially told the burger was served with lettuce/tomato/onion which wasn't the case. My burger was served with a few leaves of salad mesclun over the top and a couple of slices of uninspiring tomato on the plate. All this for $13, not an uncommon price in greater New York City, but no bargain for what I got. My wife ordered the caprese sandwich. According to the menu it's made with house made fresh mozzarella. If the mozzarella is indeed house made, they should give it up. By no means was it fresher than so many other mozzarellas. Certainly wasn't more tasty. So, the question is, would I go back? I suppose I would. I wasn't impressed, and I kinda think this place is DOA, but I wasn't offended. I just think they don't get it. They need a lesson in details and consistency. If my friends suggested this place, I'd tag along. I sense all the 5 star reviews are bogus somehow, but whatever, I'd eat there again. This is as honest a review I can think to write about a place. Will it make the Yelp cut? Remains to be seen. Hope so, cause it's the truth as I see it.

I've been "lucky" enough to go to St. Anselm 4 times now... why not more? Usually it's a 2 hour wait (maybe longer). The last time I tried to get in, they said to try again at 10pm because their wait list was full. It's the best place for a $15 hanger steak that's flavorful and not tough. It's comparable to Peter Lugers. The sides are great as well, but it changes on occasion. The truffled mashed potatoes are a must have. Also the anchovies are incredible. One note: Sometimes the food is inconsistent with the amount of salt that they put. Sometimes it's too salty.

What a great healthy option in this part of town! Â The food is terrific! Â The restaurant is fresh and bright! Â Loved everything we got (Basque shrimp; lemon chicken; steak and fig salad). Â Looking forward to returning and trying other dishes (had a bite of the "eggplant provie" sandwich and was happily surprised at how flavorful it was - I'm not a big fan of eggplant)!

Was excited to come here for a couple of reasons - 1) having a friend who was a Tabla alum, and 2) a new restaurant that was within a 5 minute walk of my apartment is always a boon. Â  The service is excellent without being overly obtrusive; the waitstaff moved effortlessly from the kitchen to the table, and while you could see the army of people in the kitchen, the activity was far from chaotic - extremely well choreographed. Â  We began with the Cod Throats MeuniÃ©re (recommended by our host), the Orange Ricotta with Beets and Grilled Bread, and the Pumpkin Crab Soup. Â Since there were 4 of us, my friend requested that we share the soup, which they graciously did. Â My other friend ordered the Grilled Sardines with FrisÃ©e aux Lardons (which I decided to avoid, since I am not a fan of sardines). Â The soup was brought in 4 espresso sized cups, well, technically, the room-temperature crab was brought out, and then the soup was poured over the crab, and the small spoons allowed us to savor every rich creamy bite, with a hint of warmth (perhaps ginger?). Â The ricotta and beets were tender and flavorful, and were excellent served on top of the grilled bread (multi-grain from Sullivan Street Bakery, grilled with a touch of olive oil). Â I could have made a meal from the shared appetizers alone; a lovely balance of rich, yet light enough not to make me feel sluggish. Â The Cod Throats were the most decadent of the appetizers, and I only needed a few bites to taste - excellent sauce to accompany the cornmeal-breaded fish. Â  My friends shared the Bacon-Shrimp Burger with Spice-Dusted Fries, "BPC" Melt - Bacon, Pear and Cheddar Toast with Arugula Salad, and I ordered the Seared Diver Scallops with Cauliflower. Â The scallops were glazed with a sauce that had a sweet/tangy tamarind base, and the cauliflower had a slight taste of cumin (presumably a throwback to Tabla). Â  The Â entree was perfectly portioned, and filled me up, which made me skip dessert, which was my only regret, since my friends ordered the Chocolate Pecan Layer Cake with Pecan-Chocolate Chip Ice Cream and the Butterscotch Pot de CrÃ¨me with Chocolate Streusel and Single "Maltmallows" . Â They favored the Pot de CrÃ¨me, even though one of my girlfriends commented that the sauce looked like cheese *grin* Â  I have to say I forgot the name of the cocktail (non-alcoholic) I had with the meal, but it was a cucumber-based drink with a slight bite of pepper at the end of each sip. Â Very refreshing, and honestly, even if they were to serve it non-virgin, I would still order it without booze. Â The lemon verbena tea is also a nice lunch option. Looking forward to coming back and tasting the desserts (interesting combination of sorbets - in particular the grapefruit-tarragon).

I come here when I want some delicious hazelnut ice cream, slightly melted on top of a sugar crepe. Â  I try to have a meal before going straight to dessert, and it's usually the mussels and smoked salmon salad or sandwich -- depending on how healthy I want to be that day. Â Both dishes are delicious and healthy, so don't feel bad about the dessert. I recently noticed that they changed their name from Le Gamin, but I have been coming here for over a decade and the quality has not changed despite the name change.

Had a great meal here. Â The chicken and waffles were delicious. Â One of the best waffles I've had. Â Crispy but also soft and delicate. Â Mac and Cheese was crazy good. Â Liked how they used shells. Â Pork Belly with pickled watermelon was really good as well.

had the Grand Slam to try a bit of everything. We shared it between two people. If a bigger guy or eat a lot, one can finish it. I enjoyed the curry and chicken katsu the most. The pork and sausage was ok...maybe 3 stars. But any future visits would consist of chicken curry. You go here for the curry if you couldn't tell by the name...that's basically what they have. Chose a meat with the curry. The curry is tasty in my opinion. Will be real nice in the winter. It is hot in the restaurant in the summer. See a list of my favorite restaurants in NY newyorkcityreviews.wordpâ€¦
the best falafel ever.

My favorite Mexican food on the East Coast! Fresh, cheap, wayyy better than Chipotle (and I do love Chipotle.) Their carnitas tacos are my favorite, but you get more food for your $$ if you order a plato. Always get the guac.

Stopped in here on our way back to the subway station after a very long, cold day of touring. Â It was warm and cozy.. just what the doctor ordered. Â Our server was super friendly and knowledgeable about the wines and cheeses. Â We both got a glass of wine and shared some cheese. Â We just got one piece of cheese which comes with toasted baguette, fig compote, grapes and walnuts. Â The amount of cheese for $9 was also generous. Great little spot!

Went to this place during the middle of the weekday so there was no long wait and service was very attentive. I never been to a restaurant dedicated solely to ramen but gave it a chance since noodles are such a comfort food to me. Strolled into this place with my mother who ordered the classical pork version while I ordered the spicy. The classical version had a rich broth with the most tender pork on this side of town. My spicy version was very balanced with pork bits floating on top of the noodles. All in all a very rich and comforting meal. It was the first time for me having Japanese style ramen and the broth had a salty rich taste which I'm usually not accustomed to since I'm so used to Chinese soup noodles. Although the broth was a little saltier than expected, it had a lot of depth and definitely had no msg since my mouth did not feel like a dry sock.

Our dinner at Little Owl Â was incedible!!! Â Fabulous food, great service and hospitality. Â The co owner/host treated us like we were highly important folks who frequented the restaurant often. Â It was our first time. Â The pork chop was the best we have ever had. Â Lamb raviolis, Â halibut, and dessert strudel were equally wonderful. Â A neighborhood Â place with a homely feel and far from the hustle/bustle of Manhatten. Â Our waitress delivered super advice and Â superb service! Â Can't wait to go back. Â Hard to get reserviations but eating early helped.

After one visit: Â The atmosphere is friendly and trendy, and the wait staff was efficient. Â The food was just OK. We started with the shrimp and grits app which was a bit watery and lacked flavor despite the bacon and paprika. Â The shrimp were tiny - the size you find in cup 'o soup ramen, but without the flavor. For entree, I had the smoked prime brisket and it was decent but not thrilling. Â I limit my red meat consumpion and felt like I squandered my ration here. My guest had the ravioli with caramelized cauliflower and blood oranges which she enjoyed, and noted the unique flavors of this dish. Â I had a ravioli and enjoyed it. Â We haven't seen this ravioli anywhere else, so TWR gets points for originality. Overall TRW was OK. Â I may give The Writing Room another shot myself but would not recommend to others yet.

Had dinner with a bunch of co workers and tried the Chicken Parm, Eggplant Parm, and ravioli which was delicious. Prices are steep considering. Once in a blue not a bad option. Definitely better in my opinion than Carmines. If you can make it to dessert Tiramisu and Cheesecake are great.

Came here for the third year in a row to pick up a cheesecake to take back home for Thanksgiving. Â The cheesecake is always a hit, and I win over new fans to Junior's every year. Â This place is great and has become a tradition. Â Unfortunately, I know nothing about anything else they sell, as I can never get past the cheesecake!
hot ramen, pork buns, cold beer...yum~ will be returning soon. great happy hour drink special. go early..avoid lines..

This is hands down one of my favorite restaurants in the city. The food is great, the staff is friendly and the sparkling strawberry sangria is perfect for a summer day. We come here so much that the waiters know us by name. It is very small, and they don't take reservations, but we've never had to wait too long for a table. My recommendation is to put your name in with the hostess, get a buzzer, then go next door to Tio Pepe for some guacamole and sangria while you wait. As for food, definitely get the lamb chops if they have them that night. They are usually on the specials menu. The gambas, chorizo, and patatas bravas are also very good.

Great place - I came here for a bday party and got a very cozy table for 8 in the back. Food is expensive Â - but well worth it. I had the fish, which was really flavourful and delicious! I will def go back....but get ready to spend spend spend.

Not that you need to read ANOTHER review on Balthazar, but in case you're curious, I had a nice time, thank you. Ever since I first started shopping in SoHo as a tween, I've been wondering what that quaint restaurant on Spring Street w/crowds of people around it was all about. Over a decade later, I finally got to see for myself. It's bustling, it's big, it's warm, and somewhat rustic. The reservation staff was kind, the waiters, hostesses, and busboys were all on top of their game, and the crowd consisted mainly of middle-aged families with their 20-something sons and daughters out for a belated Mothers' Day dinner. We had the octopus salad appetizer--how do they get the octopus SO tender? The flavor was light and mixed well w/ the grilled flavor but I for one prefer my octopus with a bit of chewiness, although my family enjoyed it very much. Also had duck confit for the first time (what a delicious combo having it with wild mushrooms, caramelized onions, and crisps) and was very satisfied by the generous portion..Mom had the pork cheek served on top of baby carrots and polenta which was very savory but is it supposed to have the consistency of meat stew? Brother got the bar steak with frites, just-the-right-size portion cooked exactly medium-rare, and a side of good frites. All and all, it was a great family dinner. French food isn't something I get cravings for, but if I did, I'd come back here or Les Halles. Both around the same level in my book, but Balthazar probably wins on location.

Ok this is hands down the best bang for your $1 in NYC. I have had $1 pizza. But this is more special. It has more meat than carbs. For $1 you get 5 pan fried dumplings. Walk up hand your $1 and The Dumpling Man hands you a box of dumplings. No fuss. If you are thirsty get hot sour soup for $1 or my favorite, soy bean milk for $1 as well. Don't judge this place for its location, cleanliness, or service with a smile. Stick to the protocol and you will be satisfied. On my way out I ordered 10 boiled dumplings to take home for $2 they were just as good. Seriously its cheaper than a pack of frozen dumplings at the Chinese market.

Lawrence - actually we waited for a good half hour because we came at 12:15 on a Friday. Had we come 20 minutes earlier there would have been no wait at all. Â Not much of a wait any other day of the week either. Â  I work right across the street from here and come at least twice a month. Everyone I've brought here from work and from out of town has loved the pizza. The old fashioned will feed about 4 people. The caesar salad is excellent and I crave it possibly more than the pizza itself, but the pizza never ever disappoints and I sit there saying 'this is so good' everytime. I once sat at the bar inside and when I went back to my cube I kept smelling something the whole afternoon realizing it was the smoke from the ovens that sunk into my shirt so be careful sitting at the bar. Any of the tables inside are fine, and if you sit outside with less than a party of 5 you will probably be seated at a picnic style table with other diners at the same table to conserve time and space!

We knew the deal - it was going to be a long ass wait for our table of 8. Â We had a very crabby and forgetful waitress, but like every other good Greek restaurant in the area, you put up with terrible service for the fresh & delicious food! Â So my advice is to put in your name as early as possible and get a drink at 718 while you wait the hour. Â They'll call you on your cell when your table is ready (which is convenient). Â Fantastic Greek salad (that feta was a little slice of heaven)! Â The cold spreads were below average, surprisingly. Â The quail was very hard to eat with any amount of grace - I should have ordered something that doesn't require an anatomy lesson to consume! Â The truly outstanding dish for me was the grilled calamari appetizer - it was phenomenal. Â I'll definitely go back to this restaurant again and order seafood instead - everyone's fish dishes were remarkable. Â Yay for Astorian food!
The chicken biscuit Â sandwich was excellent and it was only like 5 dollars! I am craving it right now! Â Go try it yourself. You will not be disappointed. Highly recommended!

Honestly, you come here for the dipping sauces. The fries themselves are good, fresh, big, and come in a huge quantity. In reality, you just come to experience the sauce and my favorite was the wasabi one. They have a huge list so you can try many for your liking, but just know this is the main reason why you come. Also be aware that there are limited seating. Place is small so you will most likely take this on the go.

I really have nothing bad to say about this place! Â  We went here for a coworker's birthday since he really liked the bar. Â He went here before at about 1AM and made friends with the bartender, leaving at 6am! Â  I heard about this place through nymag since I was trying to find a nice place that has a fancier style of frahd chicken and this was one of the top choices so I had to go here. Â  When we got to redhead at 7ish we immediately were seated (yay!). Â We then each got a beer ($5 dollars norm, $3 dollar PBR, $10 cocktails) and decided to start with the mushroom flatbread. Â Wowww delicious. Â It had all the stuff I loved on it..mascarpone cheese, onions, and fragrant mushrooms. Â The bread it was on was savory and crispy. Â SO good. Â Then we threw around the idea of doing family style but then one of us was sick and didn't want to spread their germs so she got the one-eyed caesar salad and the cuban corn (corn with creme fraiche, spices, lime) and the rest of us got...the frahd chicken!!! Â When the salad came out I kinda felt bad for my friend because it was one round flat biscuit with an egg in the middle on top of lettuce leaves but she tends to eat small meals constantly so she was fine with it and said the biscuit was really good. Â The cuban corn was alright compared to other places I've been (cafe habana). Â However, when the boys and I got our frahd chicken platters woaaah woahh wooooahhh! Â Two huge pieces of chicken, a big side of strawberry/spicy almond spinach salad and a nice piece of cornbread. Â We all assumed the pieces of chicken came from some steroid pumped chicken because they were huge!! Â niceeee. Â  We bit into the pieces of chicken and juices and steam came out right away. Â This is probably one of the best pieces of fried chicken I've had in a long time and my family fries damn good overnight brined chicken. Â It was not dry at all, the skin was crispy and flavorful all around, it was steaming hot Â and extremely filling. Â I ate a million calories that night..couldn't stop after one bite. Â The salad was excellent as well, and I thought the cornbread was really good even though it was a sweet cornbread. Â Kinda wish I had mash potatoes too, but I was satisfied with what I had in front of me. Â  After another round of beers and singing happy birthday to the bday boy as he received his beautiful strawberry shortcake and a candle (more like a sweet scone but sooo good and pretty light with the mint, ice cream and creme fraiche), we declared the evening a success! Â  The service overall was excellent. Â They were all pretty attentive whenever we needed anything. Â Nothing bad happened. Â The environment was great. Â I didn't think the place was too small. Â It was more intimate and a nice place to go with a group of friends. Â Nice amount of lighting (not too dark or too bright) and it was noisy enough to feel "bumpin" but not "ahhh turn it down." Â  Loved the place and will definitely come back again to drink cocktails, hang out and get some good quality grub. The impact? Â After 2 rounds of beers, birthday cake, 3 fried chicken platters, corn on the cob, salad, and a flatbread appetizer we paid about 144$ Â (with tax/tip).

Super popular trendy joint, loud thumping music, scruffiness, etc. so tried Saturday brunch. Was given the WORST seat I have ever had (and that's saying a lot) in a restaurant; right next to the kitchen and toilet on a super-busy morning. And an egress right behind me. Think last row of a packed plane, near toilet and galley. With the window open. Asked to be moved, but no luck. The waitress was very gracious and handled the situation very well. The food? Alas, sounded better than it tasted. Had the pork belly sandwich. Too much belly, too little pork. Lots of crunchy. rather than melt-in-your-mouth fat. No no no. Had to chop off the fat to be able to eat it. From now on, will stick to pork belly in Asia (the continent). Salad was overdressed. Cappuccino a luke warm afterthought. All in all, wouldn't go back, especially on a packed Saturday. May go again on a weekday to see what the fuss is all about.
Really nice, home made food feeling about this place..... Really big servings and the waitress Robyn was very nice.... We had an awesome time and have left overs for the next 2 days....!!

Got 6 plates, 3 were amazing, and 3 were OK at best. Wait staff was OK, except that it seemed like i was inconveniencing him every time i wanted to order another place. The upside was how cute the place was. Â Perfect lighting and feel, great for dates (just make sure to read the other reviews first, and figure out what dishes will be to your liking )
Avocado shake and a #1 is the way to go. Best banh mi I've had around. And cheap too.

A nice setting with some great arts pieces. The drinks were decent. The lychee cocktail was better than a mango cocktail I ordered. I don't recommend the assorted fritters. Drunken noodles were pretty tasty but just a tad too much on the oil. Overall good experience for a good price. I'll probably visit again to try some of the spicy entrees or the curry dishes.
Authentic Nepali food with live music. Must haves - choila, sekuwa. The momos are good too. The music is bollywood plus nepali. All in all a grea evening guaranteed.

Tiny place that reminds me of Japan - lol Honestly I don't remember what we ordered since it's been two months, but we did order several dishes, all of which were a small portion. Food was good in general:) I tried a glass of Burgandy since I like Pinot. It was ok... I like an ambiance though..

my first thai experience... loved the coconut rice and the sweet rice with ripe mangos but what what threw me off is the service....waiter goes, " you're not gonna want your change are you?" what a dbag... he did somethin else too but forget about it.... i was gonna give 4 stars but service deserves only 1 1/2 star...

One of my favorite all-around restaurants in Brooklyn. The food never disappoints, the service is always helpful and friendly, and the atmosphere is warm and congenial. The Sullivan Farm Chicken is always a good bet - moist, flavorful and more than you'd like to admit you're able to eat. However, the duck is hands down my entree of choice. Great desserts as well - but I hope they bring back the salted chocolate tart!

I moved to NYC roughly a year ago, and as luck would have it, my apartment at the time was just around the corner from Ugly Kitchen. The combination of delicious food (I'm a big fan of the porkbelly), good drinks, friendly staff, and overall lack of pretentiousness has turned me into a regular. Every time I get visitors in town, I always take them here, and I've never gotten a negative review! The only (minor) issue I have with Ugly is that it's not too great for dancing at times, despite there being a live DJ who spins (mostly Top 40 and Hip Hop... my cup of tea) every weekend. Nevertheless, I have been here on nights where people do get their groove on, but it really all depends on the crowd on that particular night. Overall, it's still an awesome place and definitely my go-to bar in the city!

Solid brunch place, I would say that the pancakes and waffles here are the two standout items on the item. They take a while to seat you even when tables are available, but otherwise service was pretty prompt and the ambiance is beautiful, well lit, good for group conversations

Ok... So this was absolutely delicious but holy &@$â‚¬ was the portion large... I guess I'm not used to American portions just yet haha not a place to miss if your in the neighbourhood. Ordered a side of pickles that where absolutely delicious, their variety made it hard to pick... If I could I would try and taste them all. I'm a big eater and it was tough, small portion eaters, you might want to split one of their sandwiches haha if you finish it order a second!

I have been here over a dozen times now and have yet to come across anything I didn't like. One of my favorite combos is chicken meatballs, pesto sauce, mozzarella and a side of the risotto of the day (if they have the mushroom risotto you NEED to order it). I love love love all of the food ive had from there the only reason I am giving this 4 stars is because the wait is typically longer than they say.

Good god, you thought to yourself. 439 other people have already written about Grimaldi's, what in God's green earth could you possibly add? Sweat starts to drip down your forehead. You start to get a lump in your throat and drink a glass of water. Your brain starts to go into hyper-drive. You start to remember that you and T came on a very sunny, Monday afternoon. You both thank god that your friend's apartment, where T was staying, is only three blocks away. When you arrive at Grimaldi's, both of you are a little perplexed because there are only three people standing outside. This couldn't possibly be, could it? No line for Grimaldi's? No, there was no line. And within two minutes, you are already sitting at a table. You recall ordering an extra cheese and mushroom pie. As you're looking around, seeing all the Frank Sinatra memorabilia, you start to wonder if maybe Grimaldi's is a front for the Mob. HA HA HA HA - of course it isn't (and if anyone from the Gambino family is reading, you have absolutely nothing against them. They are strictly businessmen). When the pie comes, you both start to eat a bit of the fresh basil. And then you both start eating the slices. And you both think to yourselves, "yes, we believe that we have now found the best pizza in New York." Â Even the tourists from California who are sitting next to you agree with you. You all laugh when the woman from California explains that she's originally from Brooklyn and that California wishes they had pizza as good as this. And you all laugh, at California's lack of good pizza. Walking out, stomachs about to burst, you and T just look at each other, in utter amazement that you both finished the pie. Yes, a walk across the Brooklyn Bridge was most needed right about then. "Wait," T yelled out, "isn't there a place called Jacques Torres around the corner?" Intrigued, your eyebrow goes up, a la The Rock, because you know what The Jacques is cooking.

i've had the Cambodian noodle soup and the country duck with mushroom noodle soup. both very good in flavor of the broth, solid egg noodles, decent amount of meat and veg. The accoutrements are where it's at. The spicy sweet pickled chopped up peppers are really good. I can't dump enough of it into the broth. I've also had the pork chop rice and it wasn't that good. thinly sliced chops with kind of rubbery meat. definitely skip to noodle soups only.

I had the Sukiyaki here, which I would recommend over the shabu shabu. Delicious broth, and enough food to leave you satisfied. Although, if you are used to American portions, do order a few appetizers. I would definitely return here with my friends!
Really friendly staff, excellent tortas. Just keep an eye on the ingredients (onions, pineapple) when placing an order. Free Wifi + authentic fountain drinks include jamaica.

I've been married for 6 months and I love my wife; but after visiting Momofuku and indulging on a steamed pork bun passed down by the hand of God I'm starting to worry that I may slowly falling I love with pork - Â yes, Pork, you heard me right. Â  We started steamed pork buns (see previous paragraph) and then moved on to the special of the night fried shrimp heads - crunchy greatness. Â The uni with the beet tapioca and whipped tofu was good, but frankly subpar compared to ham & chicken liver terrine sandwich - stupendous. Â To add some more substance to the dinner we added the spicy pork sausage and rice cakes which was great, but left me longing for the terrine sandwich. Â Some have a drink to conclude a great meal, I ordered more Pork Buns.

i am a huge pizza snob. Â the priority list for good pie is as follows: 1. oven 2. dough 3. sauce 4. cheese 5. atmosphere 6. toppings the oven is not great. the dough is not great. Â the sauce, cheese and toppings are, however, the best (they are all imported from the old country). Â the atmosphere is great. Â the problem is the pseudo sadist pie trower who will make you salivate for 2 hours before you get to bite down on something. Â this is a bit of a trick, making the pie taste better because you have to work your patience for it. Â Patsy's is still #1

I love Nolita. Â This place has a great vibe and reminds me of some places in Trastevere in Rome... Â Great food, service was ok, but I think it's just because our server was new and she messed up on our cheese tapas order, but the Pizza was great. Â Winde selection is good and prices are quite reasonable. Â I prefer the front area to the back. Â But if you want a quiter vibe, head to the back.

Little did we know how cold it really was. 37 degrees? Nah, that's nothing, we assumed. Try walking across the Brooklyn Bridge on a cold winter's night with NO hat and NO gloves. Actually don't -- P and I DO NOT recommend it. But alas, the things we do to get to Grimaldi's in Brooklyn for a little taste of their infamous NY pizza. Verdict: Good deal & good pizza... I really liked the fresh mozzarella cheese and basil they used! Their house wine was super cheap too! See that pizza in my profile picture? Grimaldi's! We got there early for dinner (6pm?) so we didn't have to wait. We were lucky indeed because right after, people were piling in! My friend, who recommended this place, had to wait an HOUR + to eat here. I must confess: I only ate 1.5 slices because I was SUPER full from the late lunch I had earlier. Don't shoot me! But P made up for it -- he pretty much inhaled the whole pizza, with the exception of two slices (which we saved for our late night snack later ;)). Only grief -- one cook almost killed P when he was in the back getting out of the bathroom. They almost hit him with a shovel....and then another cook yelled at him for taking pictures of the pizza dough. We told the nice owner and he said "I know" as if it was something that was normal and unchangeable. Oh dear! SO EAT AT YOUR OWN RISK. Ok, just kidding... Well this was one item to check off our list... Go here for a taste of NY pizza!!

I could not be happier that taverna has come to manhattan. I had travelled to queens just to try the food at the original restaurant a year ago and never forgot it. The food was so good I would have travelled to Greece if I had to. Their manhattan post is managed by the same team and the quality and prices are similar. Like the original, they do not take reservations. That is perhaps the one thing I wish they had changed. I shouldn't complain. At least, I can easily cab it to dinner here.

There's a lot to love about Maimonide. I love that they give you a comic book that tells the Maimonide story. I love the huge, communal tables. I love the salty kale chips that they always provide at no charge. I love the excellent, eclectic music they play. I love that the MOBs and the back wall are both shaped like the arches of the Bridge. I love that each MOB has a healthy virtue. I LOVE the burger. I love that the Glowing Skin is tasty, but my natural beauty renders it unnecessary. I love that the Belly Charmer is so satisfying I don't realize it's vegetarian. I love that it doesn't look anything like any other restaurant you've ever been in. I love that one wall is full of gravestones for fruit and veggies.* I love that the other wall has an American flag...of sorts. I love Lindsey, who is unfailingly nice and helpful. I love that it is an affordable and more importantly, delicious vegetarian option that I can walk to. I love Maimonide, a New (York) hero. __________ *For instance, a pepper will be on the wall, and it will read, "Mr. Pepper died for fajitas."

The food is absolutely delicious and unlike any place we have been. The rabbit was fantastic . However, the experience was not fun. It is very dark and loud. Our server was so unfriendly and made us feel like we were in her way. We waited a long time between courses. It just made us feel bad.. It was my husband's birthday and he did not want to wait for dessert. We just had to leave.
inexpensive tasty noodle soup! my fav! i love trying out new dishes here too!

We had dinner tonight and were not terribly impressed with Pepe Giallo. The atmosphere was pleasant and the staff was friendly. The food, however, was mediocre. We started with grilled calamari, which was actually the best part of the meal. Nicely grilled with a light lemon dressing over arugula, which was fresh. Problem was with the main dishes. My wife got fettucini alfredo sauce with chicken and mushrooms. The pasta was undercooked: it was chewy and less than tasty. The chicken was cold and tasted as if it was boiled a long time ago, refrigerated and then thrown into the hot cream sauce....My rigatoni with basil and eggplant was ok, just nothing that would make me want it again. A bit too much garlic for my taste. Overall, although the atmosphere was nice, we couldn't recommend it to anyone, and wouldn't return for another meal.

It might seem ironic that my most fulfilling New York dining experience as of yet comes from a street meat vendor. Until you realize that the dude who makes it all possible is not only the King of Falafel and Shawarma, but the award-winning King of NYC steet vending. For less than $4, you can enjoy an amazingly huge, mouthwatering chicken pita wrap. Or, for two bucks more, try the lamb and beef combo. The chicken plate is just as good as any other choice, and the King who makes all this happen is just about the nicest, funniest guy to be doing this kind of job. At The King, it's not just taste that you're getting. Not just the perfect price. You're getting the humblest delicacy that tastes better than any overpriced, complicated dish you can find around the neighborhood. Sometimes simpler is better--and with King's artistry, tastier, too.

Right across from my house. We have been waiting for like a year for this place to open. It was totally worth the wait! The only bad thing is I would have loved to have access to this patio all summer!! They are still in previews but the bar staff was on point and good to go. One of the owners/managers stopped by to make sure we were having fun. This is glam inside and laid back outside....sure to be bushwicks go to.

This was a definite experience. Â The smokey smell of bacon greeted me upon arrival. Yum! I got there on a Friday and was told that the wait was 90 minutes, which was kind of expected. Â Even the bar area was crowded. Â Luckily the rest of my party had arrived in the next 10 minutes and the hostess was able to squeeze us in. Â Lucky us. :) Â Kudos to her as that is great customer service! For starters we got the bacon tasting and Brussels sprouts. Â Honestly, the bacon tasting was just 'okay', but it was nice to try all of the different varieties of bacon. Â For the price, I would have expected nice thick slabs of bacon, but these were thin like you would find at a common diner; there were 2 slices each of 4 varieties. The Brussels sprouts on the other hand. Â WOW! Â These fresh sprouts were mixed in some sort of light tasty yogurt sauce with cubed bacon. Â This was definitely one of the highlights! For the entree, I got the bacon Reuben. Â This was actually not a sandwich, but two halves of an open-faced sandwich. Â Again, nothing really special about it, but it was tasty and filling. My friend got the Barbacon Banh Mi, which was quite tasty and very unique tasting. Â Imagine a regular Vietnamese sandwich... on steroids. My wife got the Lobster Mac n' Cheese. Â This was definitely something to write home about. Â Even though they put the lobster meat on top, it was almost like the pasta was cooked in lobster water and absorbed the taste. Â (This is a good thing). For dessert we all split a brownie and a bread pudding. Â These were okay, but a nice touch for the end of the meal. The waitress Lindsey was a hoot! Â Being very knowledgeable about all of the selections, giving us a laugh, and quick service, I had to give her a shout out!! Pros - Good service, bacon, more bacon Cons - Crowded, more for experience Suggestions - Despite the drink selection was great, they should have a choice of a smoky or bacon beer with the meals which would pair nicely.
Great Bloody Marys and Hand Crafted Beers! Â Excellent Burgers and Salads! Â Located in trendy SOHO across from NYU. Â Definitely going back if in the area

Cha-an is good, but overall, it is overrated. The desserts here are standard, good Japanese desserts. I ordered the matcha latte which was very good. However, I was disappointed to learn that it was made from powder. If you are charging over $5 for a latte, it should not be made just out of powder! I tried the black sesame creme brulee. The taste was subtly sweet, and really interesting. I would highly recommend that if you do drop by. The decor is not particularly impressive. I know some people might think this place has really nice decor, but I just saw some Asian looking screens here and there. This place takes only cash, which is annoying. Food 4/5 Decor 3/5 Service 3/5

I am not one to ever eat from a cart or wait in line, but I make an exception here. Sometimes when you had a long night out in NYC and you're hungry but don't want to go eat at a 24 hour place this is the go to place. This cart is always packed so yes it is that good. The chicken and lamb gyro over rice with lettuce and pita is so delicious especially if you drench it in their white sauce and hot sauce on top! Another big plus here is that it's always very clean and the food is super fresh!
Definitely visit this great park slope diner for some buffalo wings and turkey or vegan burger

This is fun place with a very welcoming atmosphere. We had the flavored vodkas and they were really tasty, you hardly noticed their potency. The borscht, of course is what most people went for near us and we were no different, both of us ordering it. We stuck to the old reliables. Vodka and borscht. It's like we were in Fiddler on the Roof or something. I recommend KTB for an authentic experience, although I can't be 100% certain it is true to Ukrainian culture but it certainly feels like it is. I will be going back for more fun and more vodka too.

Ate here in 2010. Food was pretty good for the price, but the wait was significant and because they were understaffed, someone tried jumping in front of us. I recommend their soups for a plain but soothing flavor. Also, it looks like they took the couch out. bummer

Song started off as 4 stars and unfortunately has been bumped down to 3. My first experience with Song was eating in the restaurant. Upon entering, I found the staff a little bit rude as no one acknowledged me until I asked if I could be seated. The lady said "Oh, I thought you were waiting to pick up food." (Even so, I should have been acknowledged, no?) I was meeting a friend there so I asked for a table of 2. The dining room was literally empty, however I was told I needed to wait for my "whole party" to be seated. Despite the annoying start, the rest of the time was near perfect. Service was fast, the waitress was friendly, and the food was delicious. The pad thai was one of the best I've had in awhile. The dressing on the mango salad was so good that I wanted to lick the plate. For 2 appetizers, & 3 entrees (I got some pad thai to go for my boyfriend) the entire meal was under $30 with tip. My takeout experience was not as great. When I went in to order, I was again greeted by the rude host(?) manager(?) who seemed annoyed to take my order. The pad thai was clumpy and greasy - it actually tasted like Â completely different dish than the first one. The rice that came with my chicken and veggies was so overcooked it was like one big mush. The garlic chicken and veggie dish however, was very good. The mango salad was not as good as the first time because the lettuce was wilted and soggy. I added some of my own lettuce though and it made it a little bit better. I probably will order from Song again in hopes to get the quality of food I had the first time.

Dining at the Crescent Grill in Long Island City made for an extraordinary experience. The reviews made it all sound quite good, but not until we walked in did we discover the owners are from our town in SW PA. Â We would like to think this is how they acquired their work ethic. The welcome was warm; but so it was for everyone who came in. Â  The tasteful decor and a Gallery full of the works of regional artists (for sale at affordable prices) lures you right into a formal but unpretentious dining area. Â What the efficient staff brings to the table are examples of amazingly Â beautiful and delicious cuisine. Â  Crescent Grill is a destination restaurant. Â Prepare yourself for a special meal, prepared and served with you in mind.

I really love the feeling and cool look of this place. Don't expect to speed through, its the sort of place that you should go to when you just want to enjoy the Japanese atmosphere and unique coffee. I believe the owner also runs the noodle shop a few doors down.
Service was great! Drinks were even better and my "Picada" was so delish! I totally recommend this place for those who want to try tasty latin food & remember its all about QUALITY not QUANITY!!

Yum yum yum. Ever since I had the Belgian fries in Amsterdam I have been searching for a place in America. Saw Pommes frites while walking through the area and I knew I had to have some. Needless to say they were YUM. Even though I'm pretty sure they are better in Holland I can't deny the fact that I love this place. Had the curry ketchup, it was magical. Makes me want to try all the sauces. The regular size is more than enough for two people if you want a quick snack.
After hearing so many people talk about this place for years, I finally got to try it last week. It definitely lived up to all the hype. I wish there was a place in LA that serves this.

I LOVE this place! Â I work just a few blocks away so when I heard that it was coming I was super excited. Â The owner is so nice, he is very involved with everything, introducing himself , asking how everything is, making suggestions etc. Â I am vegetarian so I obviously can't talk about a lot of the dishes, but all my friends rave about everything. Â I always get the tofu salad, it is my favorite thing on the menu. Â The tofu in it is some of the best tofu that I have had, the texture just melts in your mouth. Â The carrot soup is super good as well, I just wish the miso didn't have fish in it so that I can eat it, but hey can't fault them for that... I also like that pretty much everything on the menu is like an appetizer so you and your friends can just order a bunch of different things and get to try everything without running up a super high tab! Â Just a great restaurant all around!

Adrienne's Pizza Bar delivers the finest quality pizza in lower Manhattan. However, they don't always deliver on time...dun dun dunnnnn. On a particularly hungry and snowy day pizza was ordered, in advance, for 12-1230, we had confirmation from the friendly and knowledgeable pizza lady and me and my coworker's sat and waited for noon to enjoy our pies. Apologies for the run on sentences I am experiencing hunger delirium. Any who we called at 1:30 asking "Where the eff is our pizza?!" The pizza lady, realizing the error, deep discounts (I'm talkin 30%) and bread. She ensured us the pizza will be there in 20-30 minutes. It is now 2:30 and we are all starving. I fear some team members may opt for outright mutiny. There better be extra pepperoni. The moral - switch to generic or dollar pizza and avoid mayhem like Adriennes.

I stopped in here on a Saturday afternoon to wait on my escort, Brigitte D. Upon her arrival (as she was a couple drinks ahead of me) we immediately ordered shots of Jameson and some solid onion rings with a side salad. Both the shots/food were wonderful choices for 7:15 in the evening. This place has a hip vibe. Good people watching. Young crowd. Essentially - the best the EV has to offer. Throw in the back garden area and we have a winner here at Royale.

Considering how much I loved it the first time, and the fact that the more I think about it, the closer I get to declaring Traif one of if not THE best dining experiences of my life, it should be of no surprise to anyone that a return trip was all but assured.
