Â  I wound up ordering many of the same dishes, and they were even better than I could have possibly remembered. Especially the seared foie and egg. That dish alone can make a grown man weep openly with joy. But also sadness at knowing he cannot eat it continuously for the rest of his life. The short rib sliders were perfection yet again, and the litany of other small plates delivered were all various degrees of outstanding. But the reason for writing this update is not to sing the praises of dishes already drooled over. No friend, I'm here to talk about the bacon donuts. If you read my previous review (and you should - hell, it should be required in lit curricula around the world) you can see that we were "too full" last time. Pathetic. If only we knew just. How. God. Damn. Good. These little balls of bacon infused heaven clouds could possibly be. Â Don't let yourself wuss out. Â You will gorge, you will smile, and then your perfect meal will have a perfect ending with these amazing treats.

Food is so, so good. Service was so, so bad. We had a reservation for a friends birthday at 9:30, they close at 11:30 on Â Saturdays so we figured no problem. When we got there the waitress in the front was a little abrupt but no big deal, she passed us off to someone else got us seated fine. Once we were seated out waitress asked us quite quickly if we were ready to order. I asked her for a few minutes, we hadn't had a chance to review the menu yet. She said no problem, came back about a minute later, I said we still weren't quite there (we hadn't had a chance to really take a look it was so quick) I asked her for another "90 seconds" she said fine, walked away, and it was literally the last time we saw her for the night. After waiting ten minutes for her to return we were a little confused, then I looked up and saw her grab a to-go bad and her purse and walk out the door. Her shift had ended and she literally walked out the door without giving us an update, introducing us to our new waitress, whatever. A few minutes later (it was a LONG wait altogether, we drained our drinks in the process) a new waitress showed up. She made no explanation for the change (she didn't know we had seen the first waitress leave) and just said "do you know what you want yet). We ordered some appetizers (meatballs, goat cheese and fried cauliflower, which were all beyond delicious) and our meals all at once for fear that we wouldn't see her again. The food came out (not delivered by her) and was great. Between us all we tried shawarma, schnitzel and couscous and it was all perfectly prepared and so good. Out water glasses remained empty for a majority of the meal and we had to ask random employees to refresh our drinks. Finally, as we were celebrating a friends birthday we wanted dessert. She came to clear our table asking only "you done" to which we said yes, but would like to see a dessert menu. She walked away without a word and brought us THE CHECK instead! Ok fine. (Mind you, it was 11 o'clock now, half an hour from closing, there were plenty of other people in the place, and it wouldn't have been so late in the first place if the service was at all decent). We decided just to cut our losses and pay since we weren't feeling very welcome. We put our check out to be collected and then we waited. We looked around to see where our waitress had gone and noticed that they were having a staff meal in the restaurant (I actually think this is sweet. .. but you still have to you know. . . do your job). I tried to make eye contact, no avail. We waited some more. One of my friends got annoyed and stood up to go confront her because we had waited so long. . . I talked her out of it (maybe I shouldn't have) we waited some more. Finally she takes the check. Â Brings it back promptly. On the way out she mutters "later" under her breath. . .not good bye, not have a good evening "later". Â It's not a cheap place, and the atmosphere, which is lovely, doesn't lend itself to such crappy service. Really disappointed!

My boyfriend and I came here yesterday and we enjoyed it very much. The food was really good. I had a cheese burger with mozzarella. No bun with sweet potato fries plus a mixed green salad. My boyfriend ate a cheddar bacon burger with sweet potato fries and we shared bbq wings. Everything was delicious. Really nice spot. The register was pretty interesting. Very antique and vintage. I believe he was the owner, very nice guy, said it was made in the 1920s. Loved this place

I did like this place, it can get crowded in a hurry but If you are not in a rush try it. The service can be much better if only they were just a tad bit more attentive. I think the service focuses so much on the front where the bar is located that they forget about us hungry heads in the rear. I came here just for a plain and simple burger with cheese and that's what I got. The burger was good, a little on the small side and needed just more seasoning but I could not complain because it is filling, unlike other places which gore you to death with food for 10! The sides are good and i enjoyed the sweet potato fries. Start off with a drink the bar mixes them well. if will definitely come here again.

Pros: Friendly service, great food (my experience: lentils, rabbit pot pie, croque monsieur). The richness of almost every dish makes up for its size, which upon first glance may be disappointing to those who aren't sure just how small a "small plate" is. Â  Cons: When you're hungry, one small plate does not constitute a meal. Obviously, a spread of various dishes (at least $8 or more a plate) quickly adds up, so unless you're gainfully employed and financially comfortable (in Manhattan terms), this is a "special occasion" type of place. The restaurant itself is small ("quaint," but undeniably tiny) and consequently busy, so after a lengthy wait, you'll be in close proximity to neighbors and will probably hear every word they say. Will be back, but not before something big happens around paycheck time.

I've eaten here twice and both times I have really liked the food. I always get the octopus, which is cooked perfectly here, and the Mexican corn - I'm a sucker for Mexican corn. Last time I got the pan roasted market fish with artichoke, which was cooked well but underseasoned - nothing a little lemon and salt/pepper didn't help, though. The restaurant is tiny, but there's a little bit of a larger back room, even in here you'll be squeezed in like sardines. It doesn't really matter when you're eating but it's awkward getting out. The service is not great, a little blunt, rushed, not too much hospitality, but I find that a lot of places in Brooklyn are that way.
Amazing coffee (pour over, espresso drinks, whatever you fancy!) and a PB&J to die for. Don't let the small - sometimes packed - space scare you away. Best place that's opened in the area in years!
This has to get 5 stars, but I still think the best pizza in the country is Pepe's in New Haven. That being said this is right up there and it's worth the wait in line.

if you miss paris and san francisco, this is a good place. it's my neighborhood spot, the only "wood-style" cafe in the area. Â casual and unpretentious, you can stay as long as you want with just a coffee if you want to. food is fabulous most of the time (not always--it's a cafe after all) in an authentic french cafe style. moist omelettes, crepes in meal-style or dessert, croque monsieurs, tartines on light toasted baguettes with heavenly butter and jams, and warm merguez sausage on a baguette. just about everything comes with a side mesclun salad on the plate. it used to be Le Gamin, but changed hands about two years ago although it remained pretty much the same. good quality, inexpensive, great vibe. haven't had dinners here except a risotto once that was great. mussels are a specialty. good wine list. it has a buzzy atmosphere with a mix of arties, tourists, locals, the occasional celeb hiding out in their home territory in normalcy, a little business meeting once in a while, and no pomposity or attitude, and once in a while it falls apart and customers get mad. especially because of the laid back service. or it just gets too busy and they can't keep up. in short, a cafe as it should be. if you want robot waitstaff, go to an upscale restaurant. although it is not as laid back as it used to be. for a rush meal you should go somewhere else. it's really best to roll out of bed and wander in for wakeup rituals, before greeting the full impact of nyc and the rest of the day. in fact, i think i'll go there right now.

The roasted garlic sauce is to live for. And the fries are fresh and crispy. The inside of the restaurant doesn't have much seating but they have holes in the table so you can set your fries in incase you do dine in. Awesomeness. You can't go wrong with this place.

You are in NYC . You want goats neck. What? You want a place where you can go with some friends and breathe the NYC fresh air in a table by the front. What? Just stop by, understand where you are for what you want, and enjoy. It is fine, it is tasty, there will be some nights when it is more hits than misses, so relax and have a drink while you think how lucky you are to be here.
Best Peruvian place to eat. The Jaela is deilous and please don't forget to have there sangria. Anything on the menu is on point. Great for all occasions. It could get pretty packed on weekends.

Simply the best,,, you look at the food before you order, cook is just excellent. Whole chickens are just too cheap in price, high quality. Joe's gotta charge more than the others! Prices all reasonable!

I really like the food here (I got a bison/buffalo entre, and the artichoke appetizer) and the atmosphere is great. It's reminiscent of a country-style Vermont restaurant, albeit with louder music. However the service is absolutely atrocious. The first time we ate here the host gave us a sarcastic "oh, great" response when we informed him our entire party had arrived. The second time I was told that we could wait an hour for a table, but the kitchen may or may not be open by the time we would finally be seated. I don't get why so many restaurants in the city treat their customers like a burden, and Freeman's is no exception.

This place is amazing, get the greek salad and roasted chicken, you cant go wrong. I live right near the place and go at least once every week or two. Its not cheap but well worth the price, i recommend it as a staple to the area, Greek food galore!!!

The bar is cool with lots of character, in a gas punk kind of way. I believe this was a former bike shop. The beer taps come from bike equipment left over from the former bike shop. My brother found this gem whilst walking from his part of Williamsburg to my area. The food is good and the atmosphere is even better. We came here for a Sunday brunch this winter. There was a jazz trio playing and the vibe was quite cool. If you want to stop in for a fast one, or, enjoy a hearty meal then saddle up to the bar. I enjoyed the intimate space and great lighting.

new spot - same great sandwiches! a favorite take out joint in the neighborhood. great for lunch or dinner (and one of the few cheap options left in a neighborhood who has a barneys and rag and bone in a few block radius) - i had had every sandwich on the menu, along with every bubble tea and can vouch for them all. i don't think Hancos are doing anything spesh just serving good, plentiful ingredients on a decent bun. what more do you need?

I've been going to Snack ever since it opened, over 8 years ago. It's teeny tiny, so odds are that you will have to wait on a bench outside for a table. Â The food used to be amazing and has gotten a little unpredictable, but in general I would recommend the Avolegdomo (perfect if you have a cold), lemon chicken soup with orzo. it's tasteful and tangy. Â The Spanikopitika (spinach triangles) are delicious in a flaky filo dough. Salads - go with the butter bean salad. Â For entree, the shrimp with orzo is really good.

Delicious NY style pizza! With 2,000+ reviews here there really isn't much I can add other than it's delicious and worth the wait!! Without the wait I would give this place 5 stars, but due to my hatred of standing in lines and crowds I'm giving it 4 stars.

Yep, Yelp's pretty accurate on this one. Just so, so delicious. The service is a little wonky, but more on that later. This one's a keeper. I had just eaten at Sushi Nakazawa a week prior, which itself was really good, so I was worried it would color my expectations of Sushi Yasuda. Yasuda had nothing to worry about. The two have very different styles, with Yasuda focusing more on simplicity and minimalism, and I think Yasuda knocked it out of the park. Â We both got omakase, and the fish was served fresh and plump, with no to little saucing (I want to say none at all, but my memory fails for the later pieces). Admittedly, the first wave of nigiri was by far our most favorite, and if I could do it again, I'd just ask them to keep repeating our first round, which was comprised of mackerels, yellowtails, and tuna, but we were curious and wanted to try other fishes, which were good, but not nearly as good. Overall, the meal was not as expensive as I thought it would be, thankfully. Service in the restaurant is excellent. However, securing a reservation is a bit of a headache. You must call to acquire one, and the person that responds is curt on the verge of rude; simultaneously, he speaks so quickly I had trouble understanding him at times, and before I could realize what was what, he had hung up on me. But thicken your skin and do not give up. I called again. This time he advised I call again at 4pm in case there were any cancellations. I called a third time at 4pm. "Whattime?" "Um, 7-ish?" "Sorrynoneavailablegoodbye." "WAIT!" "Yes?" "There's nothing available, at all?" "Oh, there's one at 9:30." "I'll take it!" Of course I'll take it. Come on. Next time, I'll call well in advance.

Snuck in here for lunch on the weekend since we saw that quite a few others were doing the same. Â The restaurant is cafeteria/buffet style. Â Take a tray, load up hot/cold foods, some prepackaged options, a drink and pay. Â It was $8 a pound for the hot/cold food bar, which wasn't bad considering how many options you had to choose from. Â  They also had nice prepackaged food options - maybe this might be nice for bringing home to the family one night instead of cooking yourself? Â Prices were reasonable. Flavor wise, a few dishes were really great, but some were so-so - similar to what you would find at a deli pay by the pound. Â Overall I thought it was pretty basic, good, homestyle cooking. Â  Seating - quite a few seats! Â If you had a group of 8-10 you could probably come early to grab some seats. Â Then each person could get what they wanted from the deli bar, and some beer/soju (!!!).

Yelp said that it was the best spaghetti in NYC, my wife will disagree. Â She spent the remainder of the night feeling ill. Â I ordered the top sirloin, someone needs to inform the kitchen that when a piece of meat is cooked properly there is no need to drip some kind of sauce on it. Â I have had $44 steaks at Flemings, Morton's, McCormick and Schmick's and this was not a $44 steak. I don't know if the regular chef had the weekend off, but I could've received this "steak" from Sizzler for half the price. Â Waiting 2 months was not worth it.

Judging by the perennial line outside, you'd think there is something otherworldly about this place, or that it's the only place to eat brunch in Prospect Heights. Unfortunately, neither are true - it's just a good ol' diner with lots of flair and smiley service. They're famous for their pancakes, which have some pretty exciting flavors (lemon ricotta anyone?) but otherwise are just GOOD. My huevos rancheros was big and hot but also nothing to write yelp about. Their signature chipotle mayo was amazing on the fries the waiter brought around to the shivering hordes outside, but maybe I was just delirious with hunger because it didn't do much to liven up my eggs, etc once inside. The walls are covered with old-timey kitsch and the servers are friendly and inquisitive *almost* to the point of being patronizing. For a quicker brunch with booze and (in my opinion) more local color, head two doors down to Shane's.

Unfortunately like many food carts, this one is not vegetarian friendly :( But, my boyfriend loves it and I always bring or send visiting friends here & they universally love it. Â  My last roommate used to order extra sides of both sauces and bring it home for me so I could make my own vegetarian version lol. So all I can say is the sauces are good and that all my friends love it. Around normal eating hours the line is always long but I've seen it with no line during off hours before. Always long lines late weekend nights too. Great sobering up food! I've been told the one directly across the street is the same company/same food but never attracts as long of lines (people are creatures of habit and/or skeptical) This is a great place for a quick, filling and affordable meal a midst a sea overpriced mediocracy in midtown.
amazing, simply. and super sexy.

Seriously overrated! 4 stars for this place? I hail from cow state and we have better Latin American food than this establishment. Â People in Brooklyn must have different expectations. I guess the concept of garden dining automatically makes an establishment trendy. For starters the place was way too hot and dark. I guess it's supposed to be romantic but I just can't imagine staring into the eyes of my beloved with sweat dripping down the side of my face. Definitely not a fan. I'm not used to restaurants that don't have AC. I'm from an area where dining areas are equipped with AC or mist systems. Services was okay. I was with a group and there was a baby there with us. Service wasn't that at tentative. Â The menu was a lengthy menu. To be honest way too long!! Â I don't think anything really jumped out at me. I ordered the organic chicken because I don't normally buy chicken myself. My meal was decent but not amazing. Others got steak and fish. I dabbled at their meals and won't be running back anytime soon to have dinner here.

I really don't know how to go about writing a review on the horrible experience we had here. The food was better than average, I was happy with what I ordered. It was not the best pizza I've ever had and there are plenty of other places in Brooklyn that do it better. The deal breaker for me was the service and the blatant disrespectful treatment from our waitress. I no longer work in the food service industry but, I've spent more than my fair share of time as a server, bartender, and manager that I know when a server has stepped waaaaaaaay over the line. And then have the OWNER overhear the whole thing and do nothing to intervene. We had a group of 15 of us having our usual Wed night outing. We had been having a great time, a couple of drinks for "some of us" (explanation on why I include this in a moment) before we decided on Paulie Gee's to eat. We had heard some decent reviews so we decided to try it out. The food arrived in respectable amount of time, although the rest of the table had finished eating by time my Greenpointer pizza came out. But, it was tasty enough to overlook the wait. As the establishment doesn't have a license to serve alcohol, I politely asked the waitress if it was okay for byob and she said yes. I poured a couple of members at the table a drink (I had bottle of Jameson shared by 3-4 of us during our weekly wiffle ball game earlier). It comes down to the point to pay and everyone starts breaking out cards and cash. Now here is where the night went south very quickly. I respect any establishments' policy to not split checks for groups of various sizes, that is not my gripe. The complaint arises on the way the wait staff handles the issue when it arises. Our waitress failed epically. Rather than stating up front when taking orders that splitting checks was an issue, like any server worth their salt would do, she proceeded to tell the group at the end of the meal while everyone had clearly started spitting what they owed. That alone isn't even an issue, we're all grownups and can find our way to an ATM. Things happen, people are fallible, servers forget. I can give anyone the benefit of a doubt. Â  What I can't let go is when the same server throws a condescending glare and has the gall to ask a group of adults, and Brooklynites - several of which live in the neighborhood, "Have you ever eaten out at a restaurant before?" like we were children out on prom night. Needless to say this didn't go over to well with people who were about to spend a couple of hundred dollars on pizza. And if she does read this - the answer is yes we have, quite often. I think she would be suprised at the amount of restaurants who have no issue splitting checks. Needless to say, displeasure was voiced and the waitress stormed off to the wait station where she proceeded to talk about the table loudly enough to hear. I am paraphrasing here but, she basically called a table where half of the people there hadn't touched a drink a bunch of drunks. The owner of the establishment overheard the whole thing and did nothing to mitigate the issue. This, in my mind, shows a systemic lack of regard for customer service. I promptly left the premises and let others deal with the fallout because I have zero tolerance for disrespectful servers. I spent too long as one. One bad apple does spoil the bunch. And do remember every person that enjoys your establishment will tell another person, every person who has a bad experience will tell ten. They lost a few thousand dollars in directly recurring business from our group, not even factoring in referral business. I will make sure to tell everyone I know to avoid this place like the plague. I also know about 14 others who will as well.

Rude, rude, rude. Wanted to kick us out before we were even done. Brought us the check to make us leave when we were about to order more drinks. They have no respect for their customers. I would not recommend this spot. Beware of Steven (by far the rudest waiter there).

Finally made it to the original Ippudo in the city. Everyone tells me this location is better than the west side location. Well, they are right. We ordered the spicy ramen and pork buns. Wow, the flavor and taste was off the charts. I felt the west side location watered down the broth. But here the broth was perfect. Rich taste but not overpowering. Wait time was a bit long but we had a party of 6, so that is not surprising. Will be back.

This place is pricey and schmancy, however the experience is pretty authentic. It feels quite Italian with lots of gourmet treats like snacks, cheeses, meats/deli, and homemade pastas. Â I had lunch there at Il Panini and though i don't remember the name of the sandwich, I remember the bread being so heavenly. Â Their raw ingredients are great: excellent meat and savory cheese.

Pretty much a bad experience overall. The oysters were served in a pie plate and when we asked for salt for the mussels, the waitress brought them to the wrong table and didn't realize it until 10 minutes later when we asked about it again. In addition, the 2nd entree we ordered (the mussels being one) never came. All in all, with drinks, the meal of a few oysters, a few mussels and a few drinks cost us $60 and we weren't even close to satisfied when we left.
I feel like this place is way over hyped, the food is okay but not worth the long wait. If you are interested in checking it out try a weekday the wait should be under an hour.
The breakfast was actually better than lunch and dinner here! My favorite is the vegan tacos - best item on the menu!

I left here with a ridiculously full belly and dreams of what my life would be like if I were Italian and had family style meals like this all the time. Grant it, I would be 500lbs. because I wouldn't be able to control myself but boy would I be happy. Â This was my first visit to Carmine's and I was a little nervous because the wait was pretty long even at 10pm! Â While this annoyed me, it also intrigued me. Â Any place that people are standing in a line or braving a ridiculous wait (see Georgetown Cupcake and Pasta Mia reviews) I need to know about it. Â All good things come to those who wait, right? Â Defintely right in this case. Portions are enormous! Everything is served family style and the menu is on a chalkboard. Â So bring a big family and make sure you have at least one person with good vision. The shrimp parm was to die for. Â Actually, I am quite ashamed to admit this in public but I went there in May and it is now August and I have been thinking about their shrimp parm ever since I left. Â I mean I even thought about a quick Chinatown bus trip up there for another taste. Ok not seriously but it could work. My dining companions also enjoyed the salad (huge) and some delicious Moscato that I have been searching for ever since. Â This place is a must do. Â We also ordered the chicken masala which I avoided as mushrooms are evil, but that only received so-so reviews from my fellow dinners. This place is great. Â Imagine my sheer elation when I found out that there is a new location opened right here in DC. Â I have been stalking them and now they are open. I am on a mission.
As good as it gets! Everything is delicious! Super fast. Lines 'round the block!

This is a very trendy place with lots of good looking customers, handsome bartenders and waiters. It was a pleasant start just by looking at them :) Â I've been told this place always has a long wait, but we got there on Tuesday night around 7:30, got seated right away. We started off with the Crab Bechamel Bruschetta, very tasty with a good amount of crab meat. Recommended! We ordered duck breast and their famous hanger steak for entree. Â Steak was average, the duck breast tasted much better. Â Definitely order the sauteed mushroom on the side. A little disappointed with their butternut squash cake dessert, basically it's just 3 slices of the regular butternut cake with some pistachio, not that good.

My wife and I have eaten her countless times. We used to order several times a week, but since they opened their second location in Gowanus, the owner has disappeared and there's been a marked decline in the quality, quantity, and service. It's worth trying once, o. We strongly suggest dining in vs. taking out. Not because it's a wonderful dining experience, but because the food doesn't travel well and they tend to be really stingy or get things wrong on to-go orders. Makes sense when you consider this is food truck cuisine, meant to be consumed immediately. Favorites: falafel, chicken soup, pizza, pulled chicken tostada. Nachos look good too. Just be aware that the spicy is really spicy! Sadly, we crossed this off our go-to list for the reasons mentioned above.
Amazing!!!! One of the best Thai foodi've ever had in nyc... Decor is superb!! Service is very fast and attractive staffs Â +++ luv this place def coming back

pleasir! magnifique! After being in Cannes for a week and not eating ANY real crepes or REAL french food with one acception... this was a nice reminder of a glorious week. I almost wanted to pay in my leftover euros. YUM. I had the Savory CrÃªpes Forestierie which was amazing. The fresh squeezed orange juice @ the perfect temperature..mmm... delicious. And for the sweet: CrÃªpes aux banana & nutella.... all that topped with a cup of coffee all for 10 dollars, you can't lose. I'll be back. Yum. Happy Birthday America....

blergh. just had dinner at CM last night. don't want to waste words/time/$ on this. if you're going to do 'fancy tapas' and get all creative, then do a good job. this was just not delicious. it wasn't even not tasty. it was just overworked, oversalted and overpriced. and it was $200 for tapas. retarded. save your money. p.s. i miss xunta

Did they change the recipe or something? A new chef???? Me and my gf each had the Shake Shack Burger (with fries and a coke zero, which we shared :D) - The Shake Shack Burger being just a single burger with cheese, lettuce, tomato and some of their special sauce (a light orange/yellow sauce). But we both thought the burger didn't taste as good as we remembered. I hadn't had Shake Shack in around 6 months, and it was at this same location, but I remember it tasting better than this!??? The burger was still good, but average.., and it seemed kind of small. The fries were plain; dull.. On the good side, this location does not have as long a line as the other locations. So, I'd still give this place another chance.. Just to order something else.. maybe the double stack or one of their hot dogs I remember being very good. No fries.

Absolutely love this halal stand. One thing that I did not like --they weren't able to tell me if they had a mixture of beef and lamb, or just lamb. The man working was honest that he didn't know. However, they should know what they are selling considering they are so famous. I have been coming to this stand for years. Definitely top notch halal food.

A tiny but well organized noodle shop with a friendly staff. I got off work a half hour early by myself and arrived at about 5pm. There was already a long queue but luckily I only waited 30 minutes because I was by myself (I got in before 3 parties of 2 that signed up before me hehe). I started off with the avo tuna appetizer, which is torched tuna sashimi with avocado. Normally I don't spend 6 dollars on a few pieces of fish but I just got my paycheck and I'm so glad I indulged because it was delicious. A MUST try. My miso ramen was also quite good. The yolk in the hardboiled egg was the perfect texture and the soup had just the right amount of flavor. Not too salty, not too bland. The pork was cooked perfectly as well. I can see where the hype comes from. Though it was certainly not worth the whole 11-12 bucks, this bowl of ramen was a great experience.

Please do not compare them to Katz's K is not in the same league.More comparable to 2nd ave Deli. They have the greatest in Jewish style meat sandwiches in New York City and so does Dave's. Love the scruffy ambiance of the place although i have taken to take home for my food. A bit pricey but its worthwhile for the best. I personally ear the pastrami which can be a bit greasy elsewhere but not here. Problem lately in that they occasionally run out of food. Hope that will not happen tomorrow when i have a big order for them. Like the young guys behind the counter. They are friendly and pretty efficient.

Have tried the macarons at the original Laduree store in Paris, and it was the best macarons I have ever eaten. Â  Some macarons sold here did not taste the same as the ones sold in Paris, but still better than many of the other macaron shops around NYC. Because Laduree is a well recognized macaron brand, prices are a bit on the high side. And, I wish Laduree was easier to travel to, as it is located in the UWS.

We were so fortunate to stop into Crescent Grill on a Saturday night... For starters, our bartender Ryan was the friendliest guy I've ever met. Â The "bread" is actually melt-in-your-mouth biscuits that are served with a honey/butter mix, and the food was incredible! Â We had such a great time here, and definitely looking forward to coming back soon!

The big huge seafood pot here is really good and fun to eat. Â I bring friends here that come in from out of town and they all love it. The live octopus is something everyone has to try because of the novelty. Â They literally take it out of a tank and cut it up and put it on a plate. Â The tentacles are all still moving around when you eat it. Â Food and alcohol are all reasonably priced. Â  I would recommend this place as a fun place to go with friends.

A Solid Dinner and Evening out, I will definitely be coming back! The reservations are a little tricky but I was able to snag one for a group of 5 a little last minute and when we were running a few minutes late (actually one person in our party was 30 minutes) they were extremely nice about it and didn't make us give up our table. The crowd and atmosphere are reason enough to come back, lots of energy and bustle, a good New York feel to it. And surprisingly the noise level didn't prohibit conversation which I appreciated since I have trouble hearing! The food was well-prepared and good. A little bit on the pricier side but overall everyone was happy. While I know it is sacraligece to not get the burger here I went with the cod in parchment and was very satisfied, it was very tasty and a generous sized filet. My boyfriend did have the black label burger though and so I got to sample. It was good, not the best burger I have ever had (he enjoyed it more than I did), I know its crazy but I think the part I didn't like was the blend of the 45 day aged beef. Perhaps next time I would go with the Minetta Burger and not the Black Label... Definitely will be heading back!

I will keep coming here for as long as it exists. Â The traditional Japanese decor is truly relaxing, and the wonderful smells that greet you when you walk in let you know you're in the right place. Â  I never get the udon; I always go for the handmade soba noodles. (You can watch them roll and cut the noodles as you're waiting for a table.) It doesn't matter if you get a hot bowl or a cold bowl; they are delicious. Â I've also had the unagi and tuna bowls...both are outstanding, bursting with flavor. Â The unlimited green tea refills are soothing to the soul. Â It's the kind of place where you just want to hang out, even after you've finished your delicious meal.

Pretty amazing place. All the italian ingredients one could as for. Ate at the seafood section. Â The seafood salad is really frickin good. Had gelato on the way out. Â Will go back to try pasta pizza sections. And if I ever want to make an Italian feast at home, I know where to go to get the goods.

Filling out a section in my profile reminded me of my visit here over the Summer. I'm sure this place gets packed most of the time, but luckily we caught it when it was relatively empty on an in between lunch/dinner time. We walked into it, not knowing it's story but rather just because it had a strange name and were curious. They sat us upstairs in the corner room on this awkward tiny table since the olympics were playing (some stupid random event) and they figured we wanted to watch it. After sitting there for 15 mins (after the appetizers came but before the meal) we moved to the corner chairs/table because we couldn't handle the strange seating. We both ordered the burger with the shoe string fries. Let me tell you, that burgers/fries combo was so good I am still thinking about it months later. Yummmmmmmm That's all I'm going to say. I can't guarantee that you'll have good service when this place is packed, or that you'll have a good table but all I'll say is try to go on an off time and definitely try the burger.

I have been here several times as my sister works very close to District and this is their designated happy hour destination. Â Staff is very friendly and take care of their regulars. Â Happy hour prices are good. I am a fan.

So this restaurant used to be a really good restaurant that served up some scrumpdiliocious jerk chicken but it inevitably closed. Â When I saw the "Brick Oven Pizza" sign posted for months I turned up my nose and continued to walk down Franklin Ave. Â  We stopped by tonight with 2 bottles of wine thinking that it was BYOB but apparently they were cited recently and had to shut that down. Â I guess sippin' on water would do. Â We started off with the Salumi Board which was really good, however I wish that they had a mix board with both meats and cheeses. Â We then moved on and had the Sopressata Picante and the four cheese with pepperoni pizzas which were both really good. Â I love Neapolitan Pizza and I was very impressed by the soft/crunchy dough and the really good sauce and cheeses. Â  They don't have a liquor license yet but apparently it's coming soon. Â The interior is super warm, inviting and rustic. Â Perfect place for a 'lil date if you don't mind your breath hummin' like garlic. Â I'm sure it will be even better once you can pair your pizzas with a good red wine. It will be interesting how the pizza wars will be played out since there are now 3 pizza shops within a few blocks of each other on Franklin Ave now.

Not worth the time. I called this place to order and they answered and upon asking for delivery they stated they were then closed. Apparently they closed 15 minutes earlier. So why answer the phone and ask how you can help if your closed? Very unprofessional especially when holiday hours were posted as open until 1130pm. Plenty of other Thai places to go.

My favorite Japanese Ramen in the city so far. Â I've had Ramen at 4 other places in the city and this can be considered my favorite place. Â I've never been the biggest fan of Japanese Ramen but Ippudo made me think otherwise. Â I was a little hesitant at first because of the hype but it didn't seem to disappoint me. I've been here twice and both times we had to wait for about an hour. Â No biggie since there were awesome happy hour deals going on at the bar ($3 sapporo light drafts). Â So waiting at the bar while sipping on some yum cold beer right after work with your friends made that hour fly by. Â  I personally liked the open kitchen and the huge cheesy tree hovering over the tables. Â I liked the cheesiness of the servers yelling "ilashiamaseh" every time someone new walked into the dining area. Â I liked their pork buns althought they were frozen, premade and heated up before serving. Â I liked their version of the pork tofu dish that was biting off the Korean stew "soondooboo". Â And overall.. I LOVED their original ramen. Â DEEEE-lish. Â  Been here twice and will go back.. especially for their Sapporo light deals and a pork bun.

Easily the best falafel in Astoria and maybe even New York City. The food is cheap, delicious, and service is fast and friendly. The sandwich melts in your mouth and, after one bite, you will be addicted to the point where you will salivate like a dog every time you pass by the cart. In fact, just thinking about their falafel will induce a euphoric and primal state within you. The other day, the most wonderful thing happened: King of Falafel and Shawarma opened a new location on 30th avenue and 33rd street, in my neighborhood! Oh! I'm so excited! What a wonderful world we live in! I'm going to run over and buy a falafel sandwich now! brb

One of the best meals I've ever had. Every course, from the appetizer to the main dish to the dessert was incredible. (Note: the chocolate souffle and cinnamon gelato for dessert was probably the best dessert I've EVER had. Really fantastic.) I don't have enough great things to say about this restaurant. I went here for my birthday and had a truly special meal. I should note that this place is very small, so I would definitely recommend making a reservation.

A friend and I walked in here at 11:30a on a Saturday, waited 10 minutes and were soon seated in the little outdoor garden behind the restaurant. A 10 min wait for weekend brunch is rare in Manhattan. We ordered an omelet and waffles to split. The garden veggie/goat cheese omelet was delish. Â The waffle, though, was in a league of its own. Â Bananas, chocolate sauce, and vanilla ice cream on top. Â I also had a lychee belini with my breakfast...refreshing and surprisingly strong. Â  I have tasted heaven, and it is marvelous. Â  I will be back - oh yes, I will be back.
I've ordered from here a few times, their delivery time is fast and I live a bit far from it. Great for breakfast :)

The bartender who took my order more that doubled my tip AFTER I signed my credit card receipt. Â I tipped $4. Â It was changed to $9. Â My 4's are ridged and open ended. Â One could never be mistaken for a 9. Â In light of the discovery on my credit card statement, anything good about this pace is now overshadowed with mistrust. Â It is such a small amount but I still feel violated.

WOW.... just WOW. I got the spicy pork meatballs with mushroom gravy. I could take a bath in that gravy. Mashed potatoes were great too. The focaccia bread wasn't that great but whatever-- it's the meatballs I'm here for. The place was really crowded for 3AM but I guess that's a good sign.

We came here right on the dot at 10:30 am on a Sunday so we were able to avoid any lines or what not for brunch. Â A bit early for brunch in New York, but had a busy day ahead of me. Â They do have this cute elevated waiting area that seats a few I noticed and also a bar area for those waiting for their other party. Â You really can't miss this place. Â It is brick red on the corner of Bedford and Grove in the West Village. I had the eggs benedict like dish, the poached organic eggs, being the brunch traditionalist I am and it was very good, though I did notice they had substituted sausage for ham. Â That's as much deviation I like for my brunch. Â My friend had the mini kale and potato fritatti which comes out in four little pieces with salmon on top. Â We both felt like we had eaten without being full, if that makes any sense. Overall, the food was good, but unremarkable. Â Service was really good, from start to finish and they don't rush you in the least, which as two girls who were catching up, we appreciated.

The sheer quantity and quality of food stuff here garners this place a solid 4-star rating. It definitely seems overbearing the first time you step through its doors, but after a few minutes, I was able to get into the groove of things fairly easily. Â In a sense, Eataly reminds me of a high-end night market -- busy, crowded, clean. The markets are split into treasure troves of items from all over Italy - from dried goods, fresh pasta and bread, to fresh groceries and truffles by the ounce. Â There are even sections for alcohol and kitchen appliances. All of this is interspersed with dining areas, some seated, some standing. Â My biggest draws were the areas where you can sample some of the fresh crudo and wines (most conveniently sold next door). I would definitely be back to find some fresh cheese and aged prosciutto for my next party! Â "Delciious? Â Yes, I brought this back from Italy!"
Best $6.50 you can spend in nyc. Amazing sandwiches.
the place is amazing, went with friend on Christmas eve. love the vodka pizza ;)

The fact that the Bao Shoppe opened up right across the street from me is a huge problem since their food is really amazing. Great space, delicious food and they seem to support local artists by hanging up art for sale on the walls. Definitely check it out!

Don't read... JUST GO. If you must... Once you make it through the street-level labyrinth to this basement gem, everything is divine! Sophisticated ambiance, fantastic sake list, and the food--every dish was exquisite, but the assorted eggplant was quite a treat! And do not skip dessert. We had the pear and the black sesame creme brulee. The pear was good, but the creme brulee will send you straight to heaven.

I like that I know my butcher's by name and that they are trying to source responsible meat. Friendly, knowledgeable, and prepared meats you don't find anywhere else. The Pathan sausages were really good.

This was a block from our hotel so we went there a couple of times. The white sangria is delicious! They a had all the windows open when we were there so there was a nice summer breeze. Good music was playing, the bartenders were all very nice and we even received a complimentary appetizer on our 2nd trip there. My absolutely only complaint (minor one) is that I had to salt the food both times we went. We'll definitely be back.
Food was really good but service was horrible. Took a long time to have our drinks.

OK Nick. so what. 5 stars for a wrap place? Â Next thing I know you'll be 5 starring chipotle and halal trucks. Well I'm not but I will consider it in the future now. Wraps. Swingy chairs. 2 for one blue moons after 10pm. Â tater tots. Although I don't care much for blue moon, I love swingy chairs. Â Now there are only three of them. But people watching just went to the next level. Now the food. Â The wrap flavor combinations are delicious! Â So much so that I had to call my brother 7 states away just to talk about this as I was eating one. Â Howling nights, as you can see from the other reviews is impressively creative and delicious. Â There wraps are made there, and are not flour, whole wheat or radioactive looking green "spinach tortilla. (you don't fool me food service industry...) I spent 2 wake less nights tossing and turning that I did not engorge myself with there wolf attack tater tots, however my magic 8 ball says that I will be buying that for myself in the near future. Â Like the VERY near future (I've got a custom magic 8 ball so that's why it delivers such long messages) 2 recommendations. Â Obviously sit in a swingy chair. and 2. try these wraps. Â I was going to get one of the wraps without melon and the melon ended up being my favorite part of the wrap. Â Another wrap that had plantain chips in it provided that much needed texture switch-up with complimentary sweet/salty flavors in the wrap. I apologize for not giving the names of the wrap, but I'm confident that they know what the hell they're doing. I have gushed about this to strangers on the street, and will continue to do so until they let me down (which I'm hoping is never) Also reasonably priced, and again the flavor combinations are not typical ones that I've seen at wrap places. Â If Â you're looking for turkey Swiss on a flour tortilla this is not the place for you. Â Otherwise, stop reading this and get on your nearest subway or taxi down here.
Guys, this is a restaurant in little italy - MANHATTAN ! Half of the reviews are about some rstn in brooklyn ?!!!!!!

The restaurant was packed and this surprised me because it was a Tuesday night. Â I soon learned that the great food and service is probably the reason this is one of the most popular Mexican restaurants in the West Village. Â Our waiter, Orlando, was excellent and friendly. Â One of the best things on the menu is their homemade tortilla chips, which are thick and delicious. Â Everyone enjoyed their meal as well as our many margaritas. Â Will be back soon!

This place was great. The ambience is intimate and laid back. It was so different from most sushi places, but in a very good way. Not much to add, just that it's great. Â Fresh, unique, great service.

I love me some Shack! Even though I cheated on them for 4 years with In N Out (don't tell them) - nothing compares to SS. My first time at this location, as I usually go to the Madison Square Park. There's just something I love about eating Shake Shack in the middle of the park or at night with string lights, but this location was actually a ton less crowded which is a plus. Also my first time having their hot dog. Amazing! Split in the middle and nice and griddled just as it should be. Their relish is absolutely amazing. Truly. And I love relish. It's the perfect amount of sweetness - and I'm not even a fan of sweet relish. My husband got the Bird Dog, and it's incredible. I was kind of jealous, honestly. Even with relish being an extra .50, $3.50 was a steal for such a good hotdog. We decided we were going to be fat and got burgers, too. But we justified it by not getting cheese sauce on our fries and just getting regular fries. We toyed with the notion that maybe we wouldn't get fries at all, but come on. Shake Shack has the best fries - that's definitely something they hands-down got In N Out on! With our Victory Summer Ale beers and a cramped corner seat, we were uncomfortable but oh so very happy. And I just realized that Brooklyn makes SS their own beer... is it any good? Gotta try that next. Also got the custard of the day made into a concrete: Buttery Caramel and Cocoa Nib, with my choice of malted marshmallow topping mixed in. Try it and thank me later.

yums! So rather than waiting for 20-30 mins at Caracas, this place is small, but not packed. Â Comparatively, the arepas offered here are similar to the ones at Caracas. Â This isn't really the best date place since the atmosphere is lacking, but it's great for a quick bite. Â It's cheap, delicious and filling.
Best ramen in town!!!! Â But prepare for the wait!! It might took an hour to seat but it worth for wait. My favorite is spicy ramen. They make the dish just perfect.

If we're going by the food only, then this is a 4. Â My friend had the Gouda, and I tried it - very unique and a good mix of sweet, spicy, and salty. Â I didn't try her salad but she said it was great. Â I had the Gruyere, which isn't something I would normally get because of the onions. Â Thankfully they were caramelized enough that they tasted just fine and the mustard really added something special to the sandwich. Â The slaw was a little strange for me, as the caraway seeds were whole and plentiful, and kept getting stuck in my teeth. I knocked off a star because our food took over 45 minutes to come out. Â There were multiple servers and the woman gave our meals to the girls next to us. Â So, I got some recycled and late food. Â Uncool! Â Not a dealbreaker, though. Â  I'd go back - but not when anyone else is there, so maybe service would be quicker. Â This time, I would probably try the mac and cheese everyone is raving about, though. Â Mmmm. Â Mac and cheese...

My office team is interesting. We have on person who is vegetarian and another who can only eat gluten-free. The solution? Hu Kitchen First off, the savory food here is delicious. It's good for you, and because it's gluten-free, okay for everyone to eat. I'm not a big fan of veggies or anything healthy (sue me), but I can eat the savory food here up like it's a steak covered in butter. Unfortunately, that's the only great thing about Hu. The desserts aren't good, and they have a very weird texture. Dislike. And the price. Holy crap is it expensive. I once purchased a tiny cup of mashed sweet potatoes, and a tiny cup of pudding. It came out to $19. What? So come here if you have an expansive amount of expendable income and want some delicious savory food. Otherwise, there's Wendy's down the street. Those chicken nuggets are calling.

Holy Khao, tapas that I don't hate! Was here on a recent Friday night. Â The hostess was nice and let us order some beers while we waited for a table. Â Definitely appreciated the beer prices ($3-$6). Â The server was helpful in giving us an idea on how many plates a table of 4 guys should be ordering (4-6 small plates plus 1 big plate). Â The plates came at perfect intervals as we were never left waiting forever for the next plate to come (as can happen at some tapas places). Â The portions were pretty decent for being small plates and was enough for 4 guys to get enough of each plate. My favorite dish had to be the sizzling sisig (pork head). Â 2nd was probably the pork jowls or the mussels (with chicken sausage, I think). Â Great food all around. Â And the banana dessert was pretty good. Â All in all, a great experience.

The blueberry pancakes are to die for. Thick but fluffy. Sweetened just right but drizzle it with their lovely maple syrup anyway. It was so good that I paid extra for another serving of the maple syrup. Well worth the wait in the cold. Service was good too. We asked for a cup of hot water and were warming our hands when one of the waitresses offered us another cup so we didn't have to share. A small gesture, but nonetheless it was one that both impressed and touched us.

Came here with a date on a Friday night, about 20 minutes late for our reservation but they accommodated us regardless. It's a nice cozy restaurant with dim lighting and dark wood tables. Tables were on the smaller side but the staff placed cups/plates comfortably. We started off with a sparkling red wine off the $25 bottle list, which is a great deal; I would recommend it. Upon sitting, they served a bread/stick/hummus/olive box which was very good. There was a variety of everything and the hummus was a nice touch. I started off with the seafood antipasto and pasta deal. I would recommend the antipasto, giving you a tasting of everything if you're open minded to trying new things. I don't remember all the different pastas they served except for the clam linguine which was very good. The rest was overly drenched over a salty tomato sauce. My date had the Â veal(?) I believe, I remember enjoying his dish. Overall, I enjoyed the experiences. I definitely would not get the pasta deal again, the service was not up to par with refilling the linguine which really was all i wanted. Everything else was perfect and I enjoyed the wine and restaurant itself. I would come back to try different specialty dishes and definitely for their olives/bread/wine! Besides the slack with the pasta refills, everyone was extremely helpful, attentive and friendly.

The food was awesome and the drinks was amazing, I definitely will come back again. The salmon is amazing if your looking for seafood. I tried the mac & cheese which is also good as a appetizer. I came from happy hour and the drinks weren't bad. The view by the water was spectacular. The service was great & music was very good

We came here last night for my sister's birthday and I have to say it was a GREAT experience! Â Let me start by saying that it's quaint little restaurant in Williamsburg BK so if your looking for a huge extravagant city restaurant this won't be for you. Â If you are looking for good music, nice atmosphere, and awesome food and drinks then you'll love Cubana Social. Â Our server was friendly, attentive, and sweet. Â She suggested drinks and offered her opinion on what she thought was best on the menu. Â The drinks, oh man they were good...All I'm saying is do not come here without having a Celia Cruz (So Tasty and STRONG) Â I had 2 and left feeling "Whoa" lol Â The food was great, the empanadas were tasty (I had 3: chicken, pulled pork, and egg / cheese) Â all very good. Â My main course was awesome! Â The chicken a la plancha with rice and avocado was to die for! Â I loved it! Â They put it together so well and the taste and flavor was out of this world. Â I definitely recommend this place to anyone who wants good cuban food and awesome drinks. Â  NOTE: it can get expensive when ordering lots of drinks but the drinks are worth every penny.

Love the food but the service attitude still has ALOT of room for improvement. Â The dude answering the phone taking orders for delivery needs to improve on his basic conversational courtesies. Â I would gladly train the staff free of charge just cuz i love the food(was a flight attendant with a top ranked 5 star airline for 5 years + my folks used to be in the F&B/restaurant business for over 30years) and its such a shame to see the place run by people who don't know better. Â Good service and good food goes hand-in-hand and thats what make you a good restaurant.

We chose to do the 4 course price fixe menu and it was wonderful. We walked out satisfied with the quantity of food, many times with price fixe menu we are not. The food was delicious especially the marrow bone with scallops, a very unique dish. The food is a blend of mainly Italian with Mediterranean influences. The service was impeccable. Decor was simple but elegant.

All and all - meh, so meh. Went here for a late brunch with a group of friends. There were 7 of us, and thankfully after a not so long wait we were seated in an outdoor table under umbrellas - quite nice since it was a beautiful day. Food - meh. I shared a plate with the lady and we got the salmon burger and an omelette. The salmon burger was WAY too tiny for its price - it really was more of a slightly bigger slider than a full blown burger. Served with just plain old Belgian fries (the only food item here worth mentioning - didn't try the waffles). The omelette was decent Â and served its purpose - but wasn't really memorable except for the mashed potatoes. Service - less than mediocre. It takes a long time to flag a waiter down to get your check, check on the food, etc. One of friends didn't like the waffles and requested to replace with a burger. They kindly did so and took it off the bill. All and all - there are better places Â around the area that provide more: more service, more food, more flavah.

I wish I had more stomach room for my dinner at Swine, because the menu is such a carnivore's delight and I was one happy and delighted carnivore post-dinner at Swine. The restaurant itself has two floors - a top floor and a basement where some of the cookery transpires. We were led to the basement, which has some bench seating and a communal table in the middle as well. The selection of homemade charcuterie was pretty wide, and I had a hard time narrowing down my choices to the duck prosciutto, foie gras torchon and the speck. Everything was really delicious, actually. I loved the melt-in-your-mouth duck fat that accompanied each slice of duck prosciutto, the complex savoriness of the foie gras torchon and the woody, alpine taste of the speck. Our 3-selection board came with some whole-seed mustard and we were offered more bread when we had finished the first batch. I also tried the pork chop, which was unfortunately a little bit more meh. The sauce was a bit too thick and sticky to really provide a nice contrast to the pork, and the pork itself was not evenly caramelized. I definitely would want to come back here to try more of their other homemade charcuterie. All that came up to $25 per head.

It was okkkkkkk. Certainly didn't live up to the hype of life surrounding it (though I'm aware that it's an NYC institution). I've been twice (one time in the middle of the snowstorm of LIFE so I was tearing into it off the strength of being hungry LOL) and on both occasions, I still felt like there was more to be desired... For those contemplating standing in line (suckasss): DON'T! Just call ahead of time, place your order, stroll in and move on with the rest of your day! You also have the dine in option but the ambiance is nothing special. With these things in mind, come here if you HAPPEN to already be in the area and want to take some slices over to the Brooklyn Bridge Park to pass the day on a sunny afternoon or check out the Dumbo architecture, etc.

OMGTHISISTHEBESTRICOTTAIHAVEEVERHAD. ...and I've had homemade from my family and from Italian deli's in NJ and NY but for some reason this sheep's milk ricotta was just sooo friggin good!! I think the way they use sea salt and a little bit of olive oil helps bring out the flavors of the cheese. Â The bread that comes with it is standard Italian bread so the cheese is the main event. Â  Anyway, I had a ricotta flashback, I've composed myself now. Â Went with a friend for brunch/lunch and had a great experience! Â I wish it were summer so we could have sat outside but the place was decorated very pretty for the holidays and it was so cozy inside! Â I had the lamb sandwhich and it was delicious. Â Very Greek tastes to it and the lamb was soooo tender. Â The lamb had so much flavor to it, it didn't need anything else but the sauce on it was very good and the bread it came had great flavor that complimented the meat well. We got the gingerbread for dessert and could have had 3 plates of it if they would have let us. Â It was nothing fancy, just a basic dessert of gingerbread came with sauteed apples and a marscapone gelato but the flavors were so delicious and strong. Â I wish there were more apples though because that may have been my favorite part. Didn't try any drinks because we were still finishing up our coffee (which btw they let us bring inside with us, very nice of them, I don't think most places would let you do that) but the drinks did look good and the bar area was packed. Had reservations but there wasn't a table ready for us yet - no biggie though, it happens and it was worth the extra wait. Â Would love to enjoy this place outside in the summer!

The food and brunch service were fantastic. Â Enjoyed and shared amongst two other light eaters the ricotta pancakes as well as the Big Breakkie. Â Definitely a great place to showcase Greenpoint's vibe.

I have been to this restaurant a few times in the past year and every thing has been really delicious interesting seasonal food. I have been very happy with everything I have eaten Â and the service is decent as well. Here is my picky comment... Redecorate!!!! Food this sophisticated deserves a better setting. While I love that it is a cozy spot in red hook and there have Â been some interesting architectural details added there are way too many cheesey chotzkas. Lose the Christmas lights , this is not a dorm room, and the bad art reproductions have got to go. Last time I was there I was seated in the little back room . It's tar paper like walls made it dark and I found the ugly Christmas decorations distracting. The space is small and a little cramped, but worth sitting in for the wonderful food. A careful editing of the Â decor and some investment in good lighting could make you feel like you are in the excellent restaurant that you are instead of feeling like you are seated in grandmas basement.
Great lunch if you are craving homemade Italian specialties. The bolognese sauce with Â pasta was superb. Grazie mille.

Ordered the artichoke pie at their sit-down area and we were overwhelmed with the size! We dug into it quickly (we were starving) but it was still drippy and gooey (not necessarily a bad thing but it was difficult to eat). Note to self: let it cool a minute so as to not burn my mouth and not have cream and cheese all over my hands. DELICIOUS! We ate 2 slices and took the rest home. Vinny (the owner?) was really cool and gave me a free beer because the PBR I ordered wasn't cold. $28 for a small artichoke pie & 2 PBR's for two people.

My friend asked me to go to Momofuku as a part of her "must eat" list in NYC before she went abroad for a year. Frankly I wish we had celebrated her last day at a different restaurant. My experience was practically the opposite of everyone else's review. The wait-staff was very nice and accommodating - getting us drinks at Milk before our entire party had arrived, and then promptly seating us. Beyond the waitstaff though, the food doesn't didn't live up to the hype - end of story. The portion size was completely unbalanced - and made it impossibly to really sample the food unless you ordered 4-5 dishes per person. The sardines were uninventive and entirely under-proportioned, the blue fish sandwich had so much spices on it I had to actually open the sandwich to see if there was actually any blue fish in it - give that blue fish is a pretty oily fish - that is a first for me. the quail eggs and mushrooms were overseasoned, and then the pork....everyone raved about the pork....was just mediocre. May I remind everyone that pork has such a high fat content that it is in its very nature absolutely delicious. Somehow, they managed to make it worse. The pig head turrine consisted of a micron-thin spread of salty gelatinous mess...devoid of any real flavor. The pork shoulder, apart from appearing undercooked, was as salty and flavorless as the other dishes. The pork buns...everyone raved about the pork buns...I don't get it. The 3 people at my table ordered 8 dishes, and at the end we were still hungry but too discouraged to even venture at another dish. Trust me...save your money and go to China Town or Korea Town for some authentic food, and skip this place.

We spent nearly $800 on our tab here and the bar was good until someone stole my brand new pants - just paid $215 and they were still in the shopping bag. Â Not a good crowd obviously!! Â Be careful of your property here!

Boyfriend and I always get takeout from Kimchi Taco when we want something hearty but healthy (in comparison to other takeout places) and delicious and cheap. It's so good that writing this review is making me crave it! I suggest the spicy chicken kimchi bowl and the pulled chicken tostada. So so good!

This place has rocked for years. The drinks are great, the lighting makes everyone look hot. They have delicious sauteed collard greens and the best sparkling water ever. I stay away from the overly sweet chicken appetizer, but the oysters, the seafood, whole garlic, the bread are all quite yum. Â They are open quite late which is the best part.
It's sure is tiny in there. The food is great. I would recommend the famous corn. Good quality and a nice change of pace from the other restaurants around the area.

My husband and I went here for dinner on a weeknight. We didn't have a reservation so we ended up sitting on the chef's bar area. We watched the chef's make all the dishes for the restaurant so it was pretty entertaining. The chef and staff were very clean. For appetizer we orders pork rinds and sisig, for entrÃ©e we had BBQ ribs and crispy pata with a side of coconut rice. The pork rinds came out right away which they should have since they tasted like they came out of a bag I could have purchased at a bodega lol. The ribs came out next - they were ok and had an overwhelming taste of fish sauce. Next came the crispy pata which was very tasty. I've had crispy pata all my life and this was one of the best ones I've ever had. It came with papaya coleslaw which is traditionally served with this dish. The sisig came out last. The waitress forgot but it's ok since she was nice. The sisig was a bit overdone and it didn't have the bite a traditional sisig should have (I was looking for a crunchy/chewing texture). We were too stuffed to have dessert there so I asked for halo-halo to go. Since we were sitting at the chef's table we heard the chef yell at the waitress about not encouraging to-go orders since they don't have plastic utensils. I had the halo-halo the next day (out of my freezer) and it was delicious.

A friend and I stumbled in here one night as we were waiting for a dinner reservation at another restaurant. We figured we'd just sit at the bar and enjoy a glass of wine while we wait. As our wait was an hour long, we decided we'd order an appetizer to hold us over. We asked our female bartender whether she would recommend the hummus. She kind of looked at us funny and said kind of rudely to us: "it's hummus". Eggplant bruchetta it is then! About 20 minutes pass and we're kind of wondering where our food is, when the waiter brings us our... hummus? The hummus was so light and creamy, and it was served with the warmest most delicious pita bread I have ever tasted. We had gone through half of the hummus before we realized - wait, we didn't order the hummus. I don't think we cared at that point - the hummus and the pita bread were just that good. No, female bartender, this was not just "hummus." When she realized she had placed the wrong order (maybe in her weird way, she had actually thought she had recommended the hummus), she was actually very nice about it. She ordered us the eggplant bruschetta on the house, which was also very good. However, on a chilly night (or really, any night), I say stick with the warm pita bread. You won't be disappointed.

This place was worth every second to millisecond of my time. I can't put it in any simpler terms! Food is DELICIOUS and reasonably priced plus it's easily accessible by many transportation mediums. Must try to experience it, give your taste buds a treat!!

**Free Harney and Sons iced green tea with Yelp check in!** When you work around Rockefeller Center, lunch gets real boring, real fast. Â Then I found out about Reviver and ventured a bit further out than I usually go. Â Best "healthy" food I have had in Midtown. Options at Reviver is flavorful and filling, despite the seemingly "small" portion size. Â I say small because I could probably eat two of these portions and be happy. Â Reviver, if you read their website, is all about food density, nutrition, and making "every calorie count" - so, small meal, but packs a big punch. Â For a quick and affordable Midtown lunch option though, Reviver is one of my new top choices. Â With Dig Inn Seasonal Market and Natureworks not terribly far away, Reviver wins the healthy food race. Before I get into the entrees, I have to mention that that free iced green tea I got was probably some of the best iced green tea I've had in a long, long while. Â I didn't even put any sugar in it. Â Harney and Sons is becoming quite mainstream in my opinion when it comes to teas, but Reviver must put crack in it because it's amazing and refreshing here. I had some referral credit on Seamless, so I used it to order two entrees to cover both lunch and dinner for the day - Carolina BBQ (after reading many rave reviews) and Lemon Chicken. Long story short - Carolina BBQ is my preference over the more boring, less flavorful lemon chicken. Â Something about the semi-spicy and sweet house made BBQ sauce and the perfect mixture of ingredients (love red quinoa!) come together to make quite the satisfying healthy lunch. Â The chicken is not dry here, but I wouldn't call it juicy either. Â It's not actually that flavorful, but with the sauce and the rest of the ingredients in the Carolina BBQ, it's perfect. Â Lemon chicken is quite boring and a bit tasteless compared to the BBQ... it's not why I gave Reviver five stars....nothing much to say here. Â However, I would still consider the lemon chicken a front runner compared to other healthy shops. As I was walking back to work, I noticed that Reviver had a tent with samples set up on a corner on Broadway... looks like they're trying to promote. Â No need though, as I'm sure Reviver will have regular clientele very, very soon if they keep up the good work.
Very nice Vietnamese place. quite a few vegetarian options in the menu and a very tasty food in general! will be back!

My favorite pizza in the city, hands down! their artichoke slices are large enough that one slice will fill you up pretty nicely. If you love cheese then you'll love the artichoke pizza b/c it's the perfect blend of artichokes + cheese... the crust is just crispy enough so everything tastes amazing! Plus, they're open til the early hours of the morning, making this one of the best drunk foods to get after a night of partying!

Awesome place to hang out - Great decor and cool staff. Good vibes all around. - I don't get what all the fuss is about when it comes to the food though, and the food and drink are way overpriced IMO.

The worst restaurant. I'm a regular and i ordered an order to go. Not only did I not get servcice they threw my out of then restaurant sober when I started to ask where my food was. TERRIBLE SERVICE. over 30 minute wait for greasy unhealthy empanadas,
Nice place for a good pizza!

THE BEST Thai Restaurant I've been to so far! I've tried about 8 Pad Kee Maos from 8 different restaurants over the country. This is the finest I have ever tasted (though the quantity is bit on the less side). Between 51 and 52 on 8th ave, It's a small restaurant in between two brighter ones so it was easy to miss. it's right between a bar and apt entrance, if you got to 52 then you passed. Cozy restaurant will a fast turn around. Waitress were pretty friendly, menu was simple. I ordered pad kee mao, my favorite thai dish that i order at every thai restaurant. i substituted calamari (original menu) for chicken, spicy level was "spicy". the texture of the wide noodles were soft and bit chewy, sauce had a light hint of peanut, not too sweet. the balance of the taste was just right. The only downside is that i wish they gave me more for $11. Anyhow, 4.7/5.0 stars. Definitely a must try if youre looking for dinner after a long day shopping or broadway show!
Delicious, super authentic Thai food. Incredible flavors and a variety of dishes. A must try if you've been to Thailand and want to really revisit the incredible cuisine.

YUM!!!!! with 5 exclamation marks. Â We had a 30 minute wait, but it gave us enough time to walk over to Doughnut Plant, buy MegaMillion tickets for the 640mil drawing, and walk right back with the hostess calling our name. Â The blueberry pancakes here are TO. DIE. FOR. Â I am not the biggest fan of blueberry but I ordered it because I heard it was theeeee best and it sure was. Â They were so fluffy and delicious but not overly sweet. Â The maple butter syrup was a great compliment to them as well. Â We also ordered the Buttermilk Biscuit Sandwich with bacon, and it was delish too. Â The homeade tomato jam added a good flavor to it and the sugar cured bacon was a good sweet and savory combo. Â The service was very friendly throughout our whole stay. Â The place is tiny and packed.

A friend steered us here when we were in NYC in May not too long after Minetta opened (so it wasn't too hard to get a reservation). The food was quite good but not quite up to the expectations set by the glowing NY Times review that appeared the same week. Especially, the steak I had was good but not quite worthy of the "better than any steakhouse you've been to" hype. Good drinks.

thought it was good, but I went on a food tour a while back and i had the best falafel...but unfortunately i think the place is closed now, but i still compare all NYC falafels to that one. I didn't love this place, but I didn't hate it either. I guess it wasn't quite what I was looking for on my falafel quest. If you are in the neighborhood and you have a craving, give it a whirl, but I wouldn't go out of my way for it.

Absolutely love the savory crepes ESPECIALLY the goat cheese, fig, rosemary and onion. Had the sweet crepes too but those aren't as special since its available at every other crepe place. Small place, great food so be prepare to wait unless you make reservations. Cute & Friendly staff who speaks French but not snobby (the female ones at least). Will def return and taste every one of the crepes.

Tisserie 55 is by far my favorite coffee shop in Manhattan to get work done while enjoying a delicious beverage. After visiting numerous coffee shops since moving here in August, I've determined that Tisserie fits my criteria for a perfect coffee shop to do work. 1. Drinks - Mocha has the perfect mix of strong coffee flavor with smooth chocolate finish. 2. Price - 3.50 for a small mocha in a mug. For NYC crazy cheap. 3. Internet - free and unlimited. Even when down no problem because you can snatch the signal from the Starbucks next door. 4. Seating - plentiful Even have card where you get your 10th drink of your choice for free. Does it get any better than this? If so, I'd love to know about it.

Beef Bulgogi Bahn Mi with spicy mayo minus the jalapenos, Â almost perfect. Â You will not be disapointed. Â My wife had the pork one and is was very good. Â Fast service, good price and great food. Â They win the trifecta.

I went here at night after dinner and got steamed milk with almonds. Â I love the scent of almonds in my drinks and this drink did not disappoint at all. Â I also got this chocolate cake with chocolate liquid in the middle and my friend orgasmed over it. keeeding. Â but it was just sooooooooooo decadent!! Â  Our waitress was also very very nice. Â I went here at around 9 ish and it's not as packed. Â A very great place to just sit down and catch up with friends!

It was good but I dont think it was truly great. Many of the dishes seemed a bit to disparate - tons of different ingredients thrown together and not always working in total harmony. The dishes were properly cooked and served in a timely fashion, the drinks were outstanding and the service was good. I just think they reach a bit too high and dont let the signature ingredients speak for themselves as much as they should. Overall I liked it but I dont think its quite 4 stars, but Im glad I tried it and its definitely one of the better restaurants in the area.

Came here on a Sunday night with another friend. The place is small so it is extremely hard to get a reservation. I made this reservation probably 3 weeks in advance. The place is underground so it is a bit hard to find, but the food is absolutely yummy. We had their Washu Beef Tataki, their deep fried marinated chicken and their Sake Oyakodon. Everything was spectacular. For dessert, we had the pear dessert and it was unbelievable. It isn't too sweet, which I like, but it might not be for everyone. Their dishes are like tapas style, so definitely order to share with friends.

A group of four of us enjoyed a delicious dinner on the last evening of Restaurant Week. Two of ordered off the pri-fixe menu, the other two off the normal dinner fare. The special mushroom soup was tasty but a bit salty, though the standar butternut squash soup was perfection. The porkchop and salmon specials were delicious (they're even thinking of adding the salmon as a regular dish it's been so popular), while the standard menu orderers seemed just as happy with their choices of skirt steak and pasta. All the portions were generous, but save room for dessert!

This place is great.what I really like about it Â that his food is very different from others and every item he has at his restaurant is unique so if you ever Â around give this guy a try and you won't be disappointed .

came here tonight for an anniv. dinner w/ my bf thx to yelp. I couldn't get reservations but was told they reserved tables for walk in's so we decided to try our luck. got here at about 6pm on a Fri. and didn't have to wait at all. the place was so cute, nice and cozy, just perfect. I was tempted to get the lobster soup but chose the meatball sliders instead, yummy. Stan got the scallops which were delicious. I did taste the anchovy which I didn't care for but it didn't overpower the dish. we also tried the oysters from nova Scotia they had this evening which was heaven, we should've got more. for entree I got the crispy chicken and he got the lamb - everything was yummy, I cant complain, and that's hard for me :-) unfortunately we got so full not only could we not finish our entree, but no room for dessert :-( damn, and I really wanted to try the pear crisp. I'll be back. oh yea, and the service was very good. the busboy was on point and the food came out very fast

Mmm a $6 meal in midtown NYC? I'm so there. The line looks kind of crazy when you get there - but it moves really fast! I'm a huge fan of the white sauce. Its a great place to bring out of town friends because I'm pretty sure they heard of this cart. Only downside is finding somewhere to sit and enjoy this meal. (bring some water --- you'll be thirsty after!)

Great atmosphere- very trendy and interesting decor. We had the burger with fried egg which was beyond delicious, the beets and burrata, and the crispy brussels sprouts with a chili-caramel glaze, also amazing! All portions were decently sized, and the burger came with a pile of fries, as well. Service was very attentive. Overall, great experience here and will be coming back.

The first time i was introduced to Empanadas Cafe my cousin brought a bag to work for everyone to try. Â They were great. Â I quickly took a drive by to the store to see what else they had. Â  i love the corn and whole grain Empanadas. Â They are to many to mention as which one is my favorite. Â Only negative is that they are small but I just order more and sample a little of everything.
