Came here for brunch with my wife and enjoyed a chicken sausage scramble and a side of hash browns. The scramble was great but i kind of hoped for a bigger portion. The hash browns were nice and crispy on the outside and a bit gooey on the inside. The place is nice and clean. It's little small and the place was packed but we got the last open table so we didn't have to wait. The service was great and the food came out quickly. Would have given it a 5 if I had a bigger portion of the scramble for the price.

Love this place. We come here often for early dinner with our young child. The backyard area is big and open. Lots of high chairs available. It's covered so if the weather is fantastic it's not as nice as a real garden but if it's a little rainy or cold then it's great. All dishes I've had are delicious. For kids get the side order of mac n cheese for $5 (or 3 sides for $12 and throw in a veggie and their amazing onion rings!) This place isn't cheap but it's not super expensive either. Great value.

There are a few things you should know before going to Lucali. First, you will most likely have to wait a while. You may leave and they will call you when your table is ready, but the wait might be long. I believe I waited for an hour and a half on my last visit. Second, it's cash only so make sure you are prepared for that. Third, you can bring your own bottle (they will gladly open it for you) and, from what I hear, dessert. Once in, your waiter/waitress will fire off a list of toppings you can get on your pizza and you can order to your liking. I believe a pie starts at $24 and goes up depending on which toppings you get. They also serve calzones. Overall, the pizza is good but I'm not so sure it's worth waiting a couple of hours for. The curst is OK but, as others have mentioned, it can be large and super thin/crispy. That being said, it's definitely good pizza and worth trying at least once.

I went here because my friend recommended me to try out. I went on a sunday for brunch, the wait wasn't that long even though the place was full, the servers were quick and very on to point and moving fast. I tried the La Sultan which was very tasty, while my partner tried the banana with neutella (well, this on can't go wrong) The presentation was great and made me want to try other savory crepes as well. I am glad I tried it out and can't wait to go back again!

Stopped in for MLB baseball... Calamari was on point & sweet potato fries are necessary!!! Check in on Yelp for a free drink (mixed/draft beer/whatever)! Â Bartenders are hilarious and full of energy. Â I was expecting a huge bill & it was surprisingly realistic. Â I'll be back & send friend's!

Best Manhattan hands down I ever had, for this reason alone Char No.4 is a must. I made reservations through open table and my group got there in 3 parts but they let us sit down and wait for our party instead of making us wait by the crowded bar, huge plus. Â  It was a Wednesday in January and they were holding a steak potatoes and Manhattan special for $28.00 great deal, the steak was perfectly seasoned and cooked. Â However since the Manhattans were so good you had to order another (or two) and since everyone raves about this place you have to order appetizers (worth it!) So you walk out spending $70 a person easy. Oh and I can't forget about the delicious key lime pie, again just perfect. Every bite or sip was worth the price tag, can't wait to go back!

This place is my SPOT. It's just so inexpensive and delicious. My ideal order would be a pork sandwich (#20 on the menu) with an order of pork and chives dumplings (#1) and a soy milk drink. Grand total: $4.50, and I am fully content. I love that it's right near the Grand Street station, and the place is usually bustling, which is why the wait for the pork sandwich takes a bit longer than it should. It's well worth the wait though. They also have bubble tea, noodles, and buns that are pretty decent as well. I come back here over and over again for that pork sandwich though, I'm about to turn into one!

The best place to get your drunken all-shrimp wonton, roast duck breast noodle soup fix! Do I hate myself after I finish eating cause I'm so damn full and it's 3 in the fucking morning?! Yes, but if I didn't get it, it would be on my mind all day the next day. So just go get the damn bowl of noodles. The service is, as always, curt but effective. Just let them bring you whatever's ready first even if everything else is not. That's just how we do!
Terrible service. Â But the food is just good enough to make up for it. Â  Freaks and weirdos abound. Â Bad place to take kids. Â But it is the best Thai food I've had in Brooklyn.

I may have to make this my new go to spot in the area. This place is perfect for a quick bite, or something on the fancier / classier end. You can get your $10 Pad Thai and Pho's or go for some nice Michelin recommended dishes. We did a family style assortment of the spare ribs on sugar cane skewer, curry, red snapper and spring rolls and nothing was disappointing. I can't wait to go back and try more of the michelin dishes!

LOVE IT !! try the blueberry Muddle Shut up! You don't make them at home! Delicious cocktails that are truly unique and delicious. I love going out for either: food I cannot get anywhere else or for the atmosphere. They have wonderful deep fried battered pickles, gourmet creamy mac n cheese and real burgers. The ingredients are top of the line, boutique liquor, Murray Cheeses and a great butcher! If you appreciate great meat rare try this burger. The crowd here is a loud weird bunch of 40 sumthin drunks. Dont ask how I know.....Go for the food and beverages and bring yer own friends. Servers are friendly service is slow but its about the quality of the end product.

Fun atmosphere and great deals on most days and for happy hour. Â I came on a Sunday and got pretty delicious $8 margaritas. Â Quesadillas and taquitos were also half price although I didn't take advantage of that. Â My friend I had the mussels, arepa con carne, the guacamole, and some kind of shrimp in a well-seasoned sauce. Â All of it was tasty, not necessarily authentic and a bit overpriced, but I probably would only go back during one of the specials.

If you like Greek food & you've NEVER been here...you are missing out big time! The food here is absolutely delicious & fairly priced.. For appetizers, we had the Greek salad which was so fresh, so healthy & so good.. For the main course, I had the chicken souvlaki (which was fantastic) & even though I'm not a big fan of lamb or any type of red meat, my bf forces me to try the leg of lamb he ordered & wow.. it was amazing so no doubt about it, this place is worth 5 stars!!

I definitely think this place is way over-rated. We made sure to get here early on a Friday evening (7:30 pm), and the host said it would be 2 1/2 hours for 3 people. We decided to stay and have drinks in the bar, and alas, the wait ended up being only an hour. The bartenders were nice and actually put alcohol in the drinks - that was the highlight of my dining experience here. As for the meal, we split the: - Deviled Eggs - Prunes Wrapped in Bacon - Burger and Fries -Skate (think it was a special?) Overall, the food was meh. We asked for the burger med-rare, but it came out beyond rare. The bf still ate it, but I was completely repulsed. Having been my first dining experience here after lots of rave reviews, I'm not sure that I'll be returning.

I'm sorry folks. Â This place is a bit overrated. Â Had big hopes from this place from all the great YELP comments. Â I was just a bit disappointed. Â The place is narrow, dark, crowded, obviously greasy, and has no public bathroom. Â Very limited seating. Â What I found most interesting was the large holes they drill into the table so you have a place to insert the wax paper cone the fries come in. Very good selection of sauces to choose from. Â In fact too many to choose from. Â The sauces range from traditional, simple, and exotic combinations. Â Then you're rushed by the people standing in line behind you, the person taking your order is giving you this look of, "Hurry up and make up your mind!" Â  The fries are nice and crunchy obviously from being double fried...which makes them Belgium. Â A little less salt might be a suggestion. Â I should have asked for no salt. The pricing is a bit high. Â I could buy 20lbs of potatoes for what they charge for a double order. Was really lucky to show up because they will be remodeling in mid June of 2008.

No wonder this place is empty. Yech. Ordered the nasty korean taco and chicken mole taco. Both were way too sweet, though there was a ton of meat piled on. My stomach was not happy after I had a few bites of each taco. The black beans are boring as hell, tasted like they were straight from a can. Chips aren't homemade and are too salty. This is NOT Mexican food. This is a hip chain that draws you in with its cool, casual atmosphere and chases you out with its awful food. The cashier/server was very helpful and sweet, though.

My friends and I wanted to find a yummy Asian restaurant to eat at so of course, we used Yelp to help us with our search. Decided to try out this place a few weeks ago and I'm glad we did. The atmosphere is super cozy and I loved the decor with the wood. We ate here on a Saturday so it was pretty busy. We decided to share a table with four other dudes but it wasn't as awkward as you thought it would be. The thai pop music in the background made for a great dinner. We ordered the spare ribs (comes with 8) to share between us three girls. They were deliciously sweet and spicy (a little too spicy for my taste) and the meat fell right off the bone. As a main course, I order the wok ginger curry with chicken that came with a side of rice. The aroma of this dish was so fresh and enticing plus it tasted even better! Everything in the dish worked together so well. I got mine with no spice (you can order mild, medium or hot) although, I was told certain dishes can't be made "not spicy" Warning: When they tell you it will be "spicy" and you think you can handle it, it probably is too hot. My friend got medium spicy and the dish was barely edible for her :(.

As you know with this restaurant, the only option is the $55 tasting menu. But let's be honest, you're ordering the bread ($3), and probably going to get the additional menu item of the night ($15), and you're getting wine... Meal was definitely pricier than expected. Went with a group of 4 last night and was very impressed. Quality of food is outstanding, decor is minimalistic with a focus on the food. Even though the menu changes basically daily, here's what we had: Butternut Squash w/ cashews, ricotta and crispy pigs ears (Amazing) Monkfish w/ cabbage and mussel foam (Super buttery and lobstery tasting) Chicken Legs w/ green chili sauce (Additional menu item, amazing) Beef, Beet and Eggplant (Amazing for a hangar steak, and I don't even like beets) 2 Desert Courses Only two qualms were: Pacing was too slow between dishes, i understand spacing a meal out, but you never want customers to keep looking to the kitchen to see when their next dish is coming, some dishes were like 20-25 minutes between courses. Additionally: we sent 1 bottle of wine back, didn't love their wine options and quite pricey. All in all, great meal, cool staff and good time. Absolutely recommend going.

looks nice from the outside but that is it.. Came in one night, because of the interesting decor Â to be confronted with a showering of cheap glass chandeliers Â Like someone took a gigantic chandeliers and put it in this placed it in the middle of the restaurant. So it's actually looked pretty cool , if overstimulating. You can gaze upon the enchanting chandelier or interesting art works on the wall but what good is a place if the food and service doesn't match the wonderful decor? It's at least different and not another restaurant (at least from the outside). The food and drink prices are reasonably price by NYC standards, it's can get a bit loud and when I was in there, The tables are so close that it feels like I was packed in like a bunch of sardines. The service was down right poor... the waiters just don't care. Â Food was okay just edible and filling. Â Oh yes did I mention it got a "C" health grade rating outside. Â Gross! Â  This restaurant is very similar to QI in midtown... maybe the same owner/chef. Â  . Don't be fooled by the posh decor and enchanting chandelier. Â Quality/Cleaniness/taste of the food and service is much more important than the decor. Not so memorable experience go elsewhere if you can..

People are mean and have too much to say. You either like this place or don't. Prices are fine. If you go before 7pm mon-fri its happy hour, so you get a dollar off every taco you order and beer is $3! Nachos? Stfu! They are amazing! Margaritas?! Amazing!? Oh and hey! Its a bar so you can't take them to go so people stop doing it. And yes there may be "hipsters" eating here a lot but let's face the facts, it doesn't matter who eats where. All that matters is that the fried shrimp taco is omgosh amazing! And if you are allergic to anything you should always ALWAYS tell the people while you are ordering not after so that they can accommodate your needs. Just like you would anywhere else you might eat. Yo shout out to the girl who had blue hair, because she always knew to switch up my tortillas after the 80th time or so of giving her my same order everyday. Now! It may take long sometimes for my order to come out but if you look with your EYES you can see that there is only one grill in this place and one fryer. So! I'm going to assume if there are at least 10 orders placed before my own that I will have to wait a little. But then again I have common sense. Anyway! Awesome place! :)

The interior and overall decor are nothing to write home about. While it's definitely sexy enough for a hot date and candid enough for a beginning to a legendary night out, it doesn't really stand out from a lot of the other establishments that surround it. In fact, I would say it (alone) is pretty forgettable relative to the rating it's received on here. The service is excellent. You won't have to play "Where's Waldo" with your waiter. While I have nothing to add about the deliciousness of the ramen served here (though I wouldn't slap my mother over it), I highly suggest getting the tako wasabi. It's a great conversation starter and will help make your 60+ minute wait a lot shorter while making new friends! This place is okay, though I wouldn't hop on a plane to NYC just to try it. (If you do wish to do that, go to Momofuku instead. The nearly-religious raving over it is completely warranted.)
made 11am reservations on sunday, was seated promptly. got jane and johnny benedicts, both were delicious. my friend said that the bloody mary and peach bellini were disgusting though.

Favorite. Fun with a group, though I prefer to go alone or with one other person, so I don't have to hold anyone's hand to try something new. The bartender always makes good suggestions when I'm being indecisive. I think what I love about RnH is that it isn't trying to be something. It's a beer bar. Outstanding beer bar. With great food. I haven't seen any pretention, nor any schtick. I walk in, take a seat at the bar or a table and get down to drinking delicious beer. What more can I ask for.

The lady and I had a 10:30pm reservation, but was a little late because our flight into New York was delayed. Â However when we arrived, the Maitre d was very courteous and lead us to our table. Â From start to finish the people at Bouley made my girlfriend and I feel like a million bucks even though we did not buy the Prix Fixe dinner meal. Â For our meal we shared an appetizer, each had an entree (duck and lobster) and ordered a dessert. Â I won't go into the details of the meal as they were all fabulous and already described by others. Â But simply put it was to die for. Â  However what really made this experience delightful was the unexpected soup before the entire meal, the fluffy and flavorful mashed potatoes, and the pre-dessert which was not expected with our meals. Â After our entrees, we ordered one dessert, but to our delight they gave us a second dessert courtesy of the chef. Â  All the little intricacies of our meal were things I have never knew was possible in a dinner. Â As I've never had this type of service at an expensive upscale steakhouse or restaurant in Los Angeles/Orange County. Â There is a reason why this restaurant received a Michelin star, and I will say having eaten at other Michelin star restaurants, this place is a step above others in the same class. You gotta go here when you are in New York!

Hands down my favourite Italian joint ever! The home made food by the lovely owner is all about substance over style. The hot dishes are prepared in the oven and given to you in the rugged tin pot, sizzling hot. The perfect place to take your beautiful date :) Buenisimo!

A great family style Italian restaurant. Ambiance is casual but warm & energetic, great for group dining with family and/or friends. Kid friendly. Friendly & efficient staff. Entrees are served family style, love their stuffed mushroom appetizer & risotto. Hard to pick favorites from the pasta dishes, they are all so yummy. Mid town location does get a bit touristy, that is why I used to prefer the UES location, but that seems to have closed down. Great spot for Â holiday dinner, work events etc.

Solid stuff. When you're white and they hand you the American menu (particularly the lunch one), hand it back. You'll know it's the American one when you see General Tsao's chicken, etc. Okay, now that you have the real menu, get some wonton noodle soup. Or pea shoots. But really, the wonton stuff. Stick with Hong Kong style food, and you'll have a great meal. And it's super reasonable.

Love this place. Â Their lunch special is amazing. You get a beer off their lunch menu with a filling sandwich for cheaper than you would without a beer. Â No brainer. Â I've tried many of the sandwiches on the menu, none of which have disappointed. Â The truffle popcorn is good, but small for the price.

They had 54 SPECIALS... Â yes 54 - and the waiter recited them all from memory. Â  Each of the specials (most of them local) had me salivating-- Â wild boar Meatballs, fiddle head salad, rabbit stew, fish ragu with white beans, wild game sausage made in house... Â  It's pricey, but worth it!
The best family style Italian restaurant in the New York Metropolitan area. Note: This restaurant is a cash only business.

Ippudo lives up to their reputation for having tasty ramen, but after having been to a few other places in the area, the price tag makes it seem just mediocre. I always get the house ramen and pork hirata buns. Â The wait makes the food more delicious, but besides all the hype, the ramen is good, but not amazing. Â I heard that Ippudo in Japan is considered a cheap alternative to some of the better places to get ramen. If you're one of the first customers to be served at Ippudo, they will give you complimentary hot tea!

Make a reservation! ....and order the Grilled Shrimp and Jalapeno Grits. They are to die for! The scene is loud, but not too crazy! Perfect for groups or a table for 2! My friend lives in NYC, and this is one of her favorite spots..... it's definitely the best meal I had when I was visiting. Deviled Eggs for our appetizer: you don't see these on Texas menus, but they were the best I've ever had Entree: Grilled Shrimp & Jalapeno Grits Drinks: French 75 (Champagne, Gin, and Lemon Juice) We stayed at the bar afterwards for a few more cocktails! Fun place and great food! :)

Two stars because the space is really nice in the evening for sunset...but the food was such a profound disappointment. Â Fried clams and oysters are coated in way too much batter - can't even taste the seafood. Â Like eating fried dough. Â Gross.

Came here for the first time tonight for my birthday celebration with a reservation for 6pm. My party, save for one person, arrived nearly half an hour early. The hostess (who wore a nifty little hat) showed us to our table without a problem though. It was situated to one side of the giant chandelier in the middle of the restaurant. The piece itself looks nice and fancy but with a small space like this, is it practical? Not really. A waitress came by not too long afterwards to ask if we wanted to order any drinks to start. My friends and I felt that we'd like to wait until our last person shows up before ordering, which she said ok to and walked away. Some time later, she comes back to ask the same question. We give her the same answer, but she gives us this face and says with an attitude "...ok?" I mean, yes we were early and it did feel kind of awkward sitting around waiting and not ordering, but it wasn't busy at the time and there was no need to give us an attitude. Nevertheless, we decided that we'd order some Thai Iced Teas and apps the next time someone came around, whether or not our friend showed up. The same waitress passes our table again later but doesn't stop to ask us again, which was fine for me because I didn't like her very much anyway. A different waitress comes to take our order and we get the drinks plus the Golden Triangles and Curry Puffs. (Our friend arrived shortly after). Both were quite good, especially with the sauces they came with. The Thai Iced Tea was good but could've been stronger in flavor and a bigger serving, but for $2.50, not bad. As for the entrees, based on Yelp reviews, it seemed like the Room Service Pad Thai was the best thing to try here so four of us got it. I liked that it was wrapped in the egg whites, making it unique. I've had Pad Thai before at many other places and while this Room Service Pad Thai was good, I certainly felt it wasn't great. This is probably a personal preference thing but I definitely prefer the thicker noodles used in most Pad Thai dishes. The one at Room Service used very thin glass noodles, which isn't bad but made it feel like there wasn't much substance. My friend kept saying "Where are the noodles?" lol. They did give a lot of seafood though. All in all, I had a decent time here. Service was good after that first waitress. I probably wouldn't come back for dinner as I felt it was a little too pricey, but may come here for their lunch specials some time.

Orale! That's it, NYC. Give a GRILLED chicken option to those of us who love a chicken taco. Â Love the simple, fresh pico de gallo. Ya'll make me a little less homesick for CA taquerias and my favorite taco trucks in the Mission. Removing a star because, well, the chips are so-so. I know ya'll know Dona Thomas in Berkeley. Now that's a chip--don't worry I won't hold you to their mole.

Went there for brunch today & here's what I thought.... Pros: Delicious pain au chocolat & croissant while you wait for your food! (the pain au chocolat is one of the best I've had!) Fantastic music! Great ambiance! French toast = perfect balance between soft & crunchy, just the right amount of sweetness too with wonderful fruit on top Delicious home fries that were perfectly cooked & seasoned Cons: My only con was the wild mushroom omelet - I didn't find it to have much flavor on its own & added salt and some ketchup...maybe some fine herbes would spruce it up a bit? Oh, the other con, no cream or half & half for coffee! Â I find this to be a problem at most restaurants....I just don't really enjoy coffee without REAL cream, but that's a small con :) Overall, loved the space, the music, and other than the omelet, really loved the food!

not much of a choice for vegetarians other than the split pea ravioli and salads. and i'm sorry, i haven't got the salary to drop 18 bucks on a salad. if i'm paying that much money, it better be for something that'll sit good n heavy in my belly. the wine list was alright, but the choices were more with bottles rather than by the glass. went here for a friend's bday/farewell party so didn't really have a choice in the venue. the split pea ravioli was yummy, but the unending bread basket was the only way i actually walked away with a full stomach. i don't think the food was worth the price. the atmosphere was energetic, but got too loud towards the end, to a point where i would rather have stayed quiet than try to participate in the conversation over the din around us. the main reason they have 3 stars is the waitress. she had the most annoying attitude. i wanted to tell her, honey, you don't own the place, you work here, so let's not forget that i pay your rent and bring your nose back down
Amazing food, amazing drinks, charming atmosphere, great service! Â I want to eat here every day basically.

literally just got back from this place, and read so many good reviews on here so i wanted to try it... well since it was sat we expected a wait. we were told 15 min it was more like an hour. but I'm in the food industry so it's understandable. we had the portabella appetizer and the center of the polenta/gorgonzola was cold. but it was still very tasty. i had gotten the pesto with calamari risotto. now risotto is a fickle thing to make and so is calamari so I'm not sure what i was thinking when i ordered it but it was awful. the risotto was mush and the calamari was so rubbery and hard i deemed it inedible. the waiter didn't even stop at the table to see if we liked our food, because if he had it would've got sent back. Â my boyfriend had the veal ravioli's and he said it was really good. maybe I'll give this place another chance when it isn't Saturday but I'll definitely steer clear of the risotto.

Intense flavors, many with cream fillings. Â yes, they are good but does not come close the the macaroons at Le Maison Du Chocolat a few blocks north at 1018 Madison and 79. Â Their macaroons are filled with the most delectable delicious chocolate ganache. Â blows these macaroons away.

Came here for lunch after work one day and was blown away by the fried chicken and waffles. The entire place smells like butter and syrup and I practically had to be rolled out. The service was excellent and I strongly recommend it to anyone looking for a top notch place to try the most crispy and flavorful chicken and waffles.

Just the best you can have anywher in the US. Due to my job, I travel a lot and I always love the spices, that's' why I have to eat mideastern food at least twice a week. When I am in Brooklyn, I basically come to this place almost every day. The food is as fresh as it can be. You are looking at it being made in front of you. The staff is very friendly. My son is 3 years now and he basically loves the hummus and the lentil soup. While pregnant, my wife consistly ordered delivery from there. Unfortunatly I moved from Brooklyn and we can only get this great food when we travel there over the weekend. I hope this spot will be here for a long time as it is already here over 20 years now.

I've been to many restaurants in Chinatown, I've definitely had better dishes else where. I ordered chicken with ginger & black bean sauce, it's a simple dish. What I cannot understand is the dish has sweet source in it which made the taste quite bizarre. I've tried the same dish in 3 other restaurants, none of which offered the sweet flavor as this dish is supposed to be salty and a bit spicy. Portion wise, it's not that great either, only a few chicken slices, most of the dish is onion and hot pepper.
The nuts

Another conquest of the HH group -- $10 for 3 flights of wine, $6 for escargot or a questionable large ball of goat cheese... This place wasn't too packed at 6pm a Thursday, which was great since I hate shouting across the table to have a conversation. Â Decor involved those velvety flippy chairs that you find in old theaters - not conducive to adding seats, so I wasn't really a fan To be honest, I like wine, but I am no connoisseur. Â I must've tried 6 glasses of reds and whites, and the only one I can recommend is the riesling - sweet and smooth without the awkward taste that you get from moscatos and cheap whites.

This place is my new addiction. Spanish cured meat is so delicious. I recommend coming in on Wednesdays when all sandwiches are only $1. I also really like the mix cured meat from Spain platter. They give you a little bit of everything and it comes with warm, toasty bread. You wrap the cured meat with the warm bread and it's amazing. They make really good french fries too! Their fries are crispy and potato-y. Get them with the ali oli and the brava sauce!

When I moved to the neighborhood I was eager to try Peaches Hothouse since I had already been to Peaches before moving nearby. The chicken here is out of control! I ordered the Hot Chicken and I would advise anyone thinking about ordering something else on the menu to not. If you don't order the hot chicken you will be sorry. It's too good not to have and enjoy! The cocktails look good but I was more keen on the beer they have on tap! Good selection and it only seems right to pair a Hot Chicken with a cold beer. The service here was not the best but okay. It was busy and they were orders going in and out but for a small establishment I was expecting a more personable experience.

Went to dinner at Benito One for the first time this past Wednesday night with a group of 12. Â The staff welcomed us as we trickled in and arranged the tables for us. Â Service was immediate, professional and very welcoming. Â Bread was brought out immediately and was plentiful and delicious. Drink orders taken and delivered right away. The waiter suggested a couple bottles of wine, both of which were very good. Â The menu selection was exceptional. Â My favorite dish is veal parmagean. Â I travel quite a bit and look for places that serve this dish so I ordered it. Â It was off the chart good as were the breaded clams I ordered as an appetizer. Â If you love veal parm like I do, pounded out thin, nice seasoned breaded and pan fried just so the breading is almost crisp then served with plenty of bubbling slightly browned mozzarella so tender you can cut it with the side of your fork, this is the place. Â My first time there. Â I will go back next time I am in NYC.

I've heard so much good things about this place. The wait was about 1.5 hours, so we decided to order and just eat outside a nearby park. I've had other famous pizza places to compare to (apizza sholls, portland & cheeseboard, berkely are my tops) and this one failed to come close. We ordered the pepperoni and sausage. I could tell that the ingredients were good, but the pizza was a bit sloppy. The crust and bottom wasn't baked to a good "crisp". Overall this pizza is above average, but one of the best? not in my opinion. Grimaldi's or Lombardi's ... I guess it's just your preference but I haven't had Grimaldi's yet.

Went to Maialino with a friend last Saturday afternoon. Â Very cute, fitting for the gramercy park hotel but less over the top, more clean / country feeling. Â They were all booked but had some availability at the center bar area, so we were seated without much of a wait. Â The staff was very friendly from the start - I've gone to many brunch places that express disdain that you had even entertained a hope that you might get a seat on the weekend - Maialino had none of that, everyone was very warm. My friend and I went a little over overboard - three entrees and two sides and split everything. Â Everything came out all at once: cacio e pepe strapazzato (scrambled eggs with pepper and pecorino), ricotta pancakes, and raviolo al uovo (ricotta, brown butter and egg yolk) plus our thick cut pancetta al pepe nero (black pepper bacon), salsiccia di cacio e spinaci (spinach, pecorino and pork sausage). Â I went for the scrambled eggs at first. Â They were rich with a bit of bite from the pepper and cheese, moist without being runny. Â A bit hit after the first bite, but a little monotonous after a while, though the little crackers they served with it offered a nice texture contrast. Â The raviolo was perhaps even richer - one big singular raviolo that oozed egg yolk and cheese when prodded. Â Couldn't linger too long, because I was saving room for the ricotta pancakes, one of my favorite pancake variations. Â Was a little disappointed - the pancakes weren't as flavorful as I'd hoped, were a little less crisp on the outside than expected, and I didn't find the dollop of ricotta or the peach compote particularly compelling (though I guess I should admit I'm spoiled by my neighborhood Clinton St Baking Co). Â Still, not a bad pancake by any means. The sides - sausage and bacon - were both good, though the sausage was perhaps my favorite (the bacon was similar, but didn't quite measure up, to the thick slabs of bacon served at steakhouses like Peter Luger's, Wolfgang's, etc around the city). Â It was packed with flavor and little bursts of pecorino cheese - really delicious. Would definitely go back to Maialino. Â Not the best brunch I've had in the city, but right up there, especially when you consider the ambiance and ease of getting a table when just dropping in on the weekends.

Lunch Special blew my mind. I was the only one in the place. Chicken panini tasted like it was cooked over open flames (mmmm!) and the white bean soup in a tomato broth was incredible... and don't even get me started on the home made chips! So Delish!
NYC brunch staple!

Okay. Â I want to give you the most important fact up front: THIS IS THE BEST PATTY MELT I'VE EVER HAD IN MY ENTIRE LIFE. This is no hyperbole. Â This is cold, hard fact, like Newton's laws or the Electoral College. Â I love being the skeptic, so the fact that this place has stolen that from me and replaced it with a perfectly pair of perfectly toasted rye slices, between them some delicately sauteed onions and a tender, yet robust patty of beef, makes me simply irate. Â So irate that I'll probably just eat my feelings with this DELICIOUS PATTY MELT. Okay, the fawning has stopped. Â Its just a damn good burg, and the fries are like old fast food french fries. Â Really, really, really good. Besides the Sandwich That Shall Not Be Named, there are plenty of other reasons to love The Narrows. Â During the winter, when the sun has all but abandoned us, The Narrows kindly serves up hot toddies and warm ciders to thaw our weary souls. During the summertime, we can delight ourselves with $1 oysters and $6 tecate/tequila shots (or bud/whiskey) during their gracious Happy Hour, I believe 4-7. Â The food has ALWAYS satisfied and I've brought a few crews here for some late night eats. There is only one thing that is sort of a bummer, and a very important note to anyone coming to The Narrows, and that is they are a CASH ONLY ESTABLISHMENT. Â They have an ATM on premises but you might want to just have some handy. Cheap Booze. Good Food. Easy Vibe. CASH ONLY. C U Thar.

Been meaning to go here for a while for brunch and will now have to make this my regular spot I got a few things to try and all were equally amazing: Fisherman's egg: 4 stars, hollandaise was perfect and eggs and fish were great farmers breakfast: 5 stars, the toast, eggs and potatoes all came together perfectly...the potatoes left me speechless French toast: 5 Stars, hands down one of the best i have ever tried, crispy on the outside bread pudding like on the inside, with fresh strawberries mimosa was strong and good prices are extremely reasonable will be coming here very often

Listen I still have not found the HOLY CRAP of all NYC pizza but L &B gets 4 stars for having everything plus good pizza. Â I lived in Brooklyn for 2 months Â and I was at this place almost every week. Â The sauce is great so go with the sicilian not the round you will not regret it if sauce is your thing.
love it

Cheers to an aesthetically pleasing bar on the Upper West. Going downtown is such a hassle and this is right in our backyard. The rosemary lemonade was delicious. And it comes served in a jar. Yes, very hipster, but nothing off-putting. Music was lacking but they are really nice about being accommodating with it, i.e. putting on something better at request. Plus Jacob himself seems like a cool guy. Great place for drinks with a few friends. Try a pickle!

I'm torn - somewhere in between 3-4 stars for me. The burritos were really good - but in a very "opposite of Chipotle" kind of way (and I love Chipotle). Â I was extremely full afterwards and could not eat for the rest of the day. Â I guess that's good?
Very retro, loved the ambience. All the waiters speak French. Great wine selection and for a cozy night in!

Never fails to impress me during brunch! Unfortunately a few of their locations have closed down, so me and some friends trotted over to the near-union-square location. We were seats within 30 minutes. Our waitress was super patient with us and we ordered the berry waffle to share. Def get a waffle dish if you love belgium waffles -fluffly, light and goes great with their light cream. I had the croque madam. The eggs are done sunny side up and isn't liquify, so no massive egg yolk gets over your sandwich. The bread is soft and is great with the ham. They don't rush you and it leaves you full but not to the food-coma fullness. Cant wait to go back for more waffles!

Decor and ambiance adorbale. Service and food just so-so. Prices okay. We came here for brunch one Sunday afternoon and ordered egg white frittas. It was decent, not super tasty but filling. I wish it had come with something, though. They could have thrown in some hash browns or a salad like a lot of their other egg dishes.

Stellar banh mi, well deserving of the high marks its received. I've tried a few sandwiches, and one or two of the apps (appetizers not essential here). They have traditional bahn mi, but it's my opinion that where they excel is their originals. Specifically the Kakuni Pork Belly bahn mi is a must, I'm not sure what crack is like, but the experience must be similar ("Got that cr'nack, yeah, I got cr'nack" 2 Chainz). Â On every visit I'm always amazed at how delicious this sandwich is, the union of fresh vegetable and marinated pork belly is a real win. Extra points for good value, the sandwich comes in at just $5.25. Worth the hype, and the trip if you don't live in queens!

Went here tonight for dinner. The food was delicious, and the price was excellent for what you get. Stepping inside the restaurant, the cashier is immediately to your right. If you want take-out, continue a bit farther down to either the sandwich or the platter line, choose the food you want, and then pay at the cashier. If you want to eat in, continue to the very back of the restaurant, where there is table service. That's where my friend and I ate. We both ordered the shredded beef stew special ($9), which comes with two sides. I probably wouldn't have ordered it if I hadn't seen it in the serving area at the front of the restaurant, but it looked so appetizing, I couldn't resist it. My eyes didn't deceive me--it was delicious and tasted about how I'd imagined it. The beef was a little tough, but not overly so, and the blend of flavors from the peppers more than made up for it. I tried a little of the green sauce since I'd read so much about it. It was good, but not really necessary for my meal. I'll have to try it next time with something else. As I mentioned, the main dish came with two sides. I chose black beans and sweet plantains. The black beans were slightly spicy--better than average. The sweet plantains were a nice change from the rice I usually get. The serving sizes were pretty large, too. I hadn't eaten all day since the bowl of cereal I had for breakfast, but I was pleasantly full at the end of the meal. My friend couldn't even finish hers. The atmosphere is kind of cafeteria-like, but it doesn't really matter since the food is so great and the price fits the setting. The staff was nice enough. Our server wasn't very conversational (I don't think he said a single word to us) and he was always in a rush, but we got him to smile a bit, and it was easy enough to get the check. He didn't refill our water regularly, but he seemed happy to do so when I asked him to. By the way, tip is automatically added to the bill. Overall, I had a great experience, and I'm looking forward to going back soon!
Great service Small but nice decor, clean Food was a little bland, even after Â I added the house chili sauce.

Food was great, but the service was not. Took about 15 minutes to greet us, and another 15 to bring us our coffee and tea, and it was not a busy time of the day.. We ordered similar items; the ham and cheddar cheese croissant and the spinach and gruyere croissant, with a side of home-fries. All of the food was absolutely delicious from beginning to end, but super heavy. Overall I liked it (was my second time there), but its the kind of place where you eat allot and go home and take a nap, rather than attacking the day...
Correction

Cafe Orlin could use some more light inside, with its heavy wood accented interior. It makes for a somewhat depressing brunch spot, especially so on a cold and blustery day. HOWEVER, the food was bursting with flavor! My date and I both ordered an omelette, me the mushroom with carmelized onions and him the fontina and tomatoes. Upon the arrival of our plates, the smell of butter wafted into the air. Where was it coming from? Why, the eggs of course! Its buttery goodness (and I suspect with a touch of cream or milk) lent our blanket of eggs the perfect fluffiness. The eggs came with a light salad and its heavy counterpart, roasted (more like fried) potatoes. Four triangles of rye toast with butter were part of the deal too. Delish! We shared the hummus plate, which came with one (only one?) thick and chewy pita for dipping. Generous portions of olive oil covered our hummus, as well as a few olives and fresh tomatoes. A side note: Orlin doesn't serve coffee. Only espresso.

I just discovered Mezetto, and it's one of my new favorites. I've tried a number of different things including the hummus, the falafel buns, the avocado salad, the Brussels sprouts, and the striped bass. Every dish has been delicious, and the portions are generous, considering they are small plates. The staff is welcoming, friendly, and attentive, and the location is great: right on the corner of Houston and Allen. When it's warm, all of the windows are open, and it's great people watching. Plus, there is live music on Tuesday and Thursday nights. I highly recommend this place for it's warm, casual vibe, interesting menu, and great food. Check it out.

The food is good and the prices are very reasonable, although I thought the portions were a bit small. In reality, I probably could have eaten another whole breakfast when I was done. If you're in the area and want a no-frills breakfast/lunch, this is a great place to go to. On the grand scale of luncheonettes, Johny's has a long way to go before it's Cup & Saucer.

What happened Joe Shanghai? This place was delicious in the past but right now I feel like it's greasy chinese food. My crab meat soup dumplings came out cold and it's not as flavorful as it used to be. I prefer my options in Flushing now. My chicken lo mein was VERY OILY and you might as well rename it and called it veggie noodles with extra oil as a topping. I was having trouble finding the chicken pieces. I bumpped into an old friend and decided to have lunch here but now I know to steer clear from this place next time we have a reunion.

I'd been here a few times before, and always had to wait for a table, so I was prepared for that. What I wasn't prepared for was being handed menus, bread, and water, then left to sit for 20+ minutes while everyone who was seated after us was served. It was to the point that these tables had food brought out before anyone even considered taking our order. Being excited to introduce my boyfriend to a restaurant I had enjoyed immensely in the past, I was trying to stick it out, but I couldn't get the attention of the waiter (owner?), so I politely asked the busser if it would be possible to order, thinking he would tell him we were ready. Instead, he went over and talked to another table for a few minutes, and we still weren't acknowledged. We ended up just walking out and picking a different restaurant in the neighborhood. I honestly don't even know why we waited as long as we did to leave. Never again.

The food here is great. An excellent addition to our neighborhood choices. Everything seems authentic, and the prices are very reasonable, but at the same time a number of options are special, with better than average ingredients and flavors...
This place was delicious!! The table bread was amazing, the gnocchi, the pasta, everything. Really great atmosphere and location as well. And the prices are quite good... particularly the Prix Fixe.
My husband and I love it here. Good food, good service and the brunches on the weekends are a-m-a-z-ing. We're a fan. Love this place.
Despite the crowds the food is so delicious I always go back. Everything seems really fresh, the tacos are such a good deal, and the trio of salsas are amazing!

I never write reviews but I was so excited about eating at this place that I just had to write about it. This place is as authentic as it gets. Me and my husband are both from Russia so we are very serious about our food and this place felt like eating at granmas! This restaurant is all over Ukraine and is a place we visited on our travels back home so i was soooo excited to see this place open here in the city! The decor is traditional Ukrainian and very cozy. The place just opened so they let us try their infused vodka on the house. We tried the bacon vodka which was recommended by the waiter, I was unsure but after we tried it.. I was intrigued, this is the only place in the city I have ever even seen this on the menu.. Also tried strawberry infused vodka which was amazing. Â We started with the pork sausage appetizer and Blueberry mors which was very refreshing (its a traditional russian berry drink). Ofcourse we had to have the pirogi or pirashki which were to die for and just as good as grandma made. I ordered the Â Salmon Moscow style which is basically salmon cooked in creamy cavier sauce. Loved it and cant beat the $22 price for caviar anything. My husband had the mushroom and potato vareniki which are basically Russian version of dumplings and they were out of this world. We both ordered the sorrel borsht which is something even if we haven't had before and my taste buds were singing. The sever was very attentive and the manager checked in on us from time to time to make sure we had everything we needed. I will def be coming back with my family!

DUdeS: what's up with complaining about chaotic grocery shopping?! YOU LIVE IN NEW YORK HOW IS EATALY LESS CRAZY THAN WHOLE FOODS OR THE-APOCALYPSE-IS-COMING-BUY-ALL-THE-CORN-IN-Â­MANHATTAN DEATH LINE OF TRADER JOE'S?! But ok: one star off for prices. Yes, it is expensive. But, nice things often are! If you want your additives and dollar menu, go elsewhere. Ok: another star off because there is the slight smell of snobbery. I go: oh hey, which is a good fish? You know, what do you you like, fish guy? And he's all: this is Eataly. It's all good fish. No, it is all GREAT fish. C'mon and get off the PR high horse, I just wanna know which salmon filet to get because there are SEVEN DIFFERENT KINDS. But I like it. If you like food, you will enjoy it.

I only came here to pregame before hopping to another spot for a Yelp Event, but I have to say its a pretty solid place. It made me feel like I was in a 1950's diner, maybe because the paint scheme was similar to the feeling you get looking at Edward Hopper's Nighthawks. The vibe is just that cool. I went with simple and got a bowl of some tasty salted french fries and a beer with a shot of whiskey on the side for under $10. so this place was a win.

4.5 really- The star is the big tray chicken. Insanely flavorful chicken and sauce is served in a large pan family style. It's gussied up with some nicely braised potatoes and finished with a handful of chopped cilantro leaves. YOU MUST get the noodles as an add-on- fantastic home-made versions that cling to the sauce like long lost lovers. We had a couple pork pancakes- FANTASTIC with the table sauce which resembles chili oil mixed with butter. BYOB for those that want to bring a couple bottles of scotch. Prices are very reasonable. Eat here.
Hands down the best ramen place in the east coast. But didnt really find the humor of the mexican dude ( who was calling out your name ) funny. he was actually quite annoying.

This is one of the most popular places on the planet. I used to live a few blocks away and, when I walked by, the line could sometimes be a block long. You get a lot of freshly cooked, tasty food for a low price. It is definitely a step above the other food carts. They now have at least four carts, so if the line at the original one is too long, you can go to the one across the street or down the block. Just make sure it says, Halal Guys. One tip, the hot sauce is too much even if you like spicy food. Best if you take just a few drops of the hot sauce and mix it with the container of the white sauce, then pour the mixture on your food. That will give you enough fire without burning a hole in your stomach! Enjoy!
This place's whiskey selection is inspiring me to move to Cobble Hill when my lease runs in the spring. Â I'm not even kidding.
Great Pizza Big servings Our waitress was super nice Free soda refills Simple, but excellent! Will Definitely come back.
Awesome cozy Japanese tea house with lots of interesting options on the menu. Strongly recommend trying their high-end matcha green tea.
good food. if you order for delivery is seems to come really overly salted. i suggest you eat in the restaurant.

Honestly, a great meal from beginning to end. Â Great atmosphere and ambience for this new Bobby Flay restaurant. Â Top recommendations: Â the eggplant, the tarragon chicken, the kale paella and the cauliflower. Â Will go back to try more....

The two brothers who started this business are from SF-yay to CA! The burritos are delicious, and I like how the tortilla is thinner (less calories) and have cheese melted onto them! Pros-delicious, filled burrito; great guacamole (only ~$0.94 versus the $2 at chipotle), friendly workers Cons-a bit of a smaller joint but you can take your burritos to go; extra charge for cheese (that really made me sad!!) Overall-yummy burrito that competes with Qdoba and Chipotle. Â Btw, all three have similar prices considering I just went to all three this past week!

Wasn't quiet sure what to expect when I was told we were going to eat Himalayan. Â The place is tiny inside, and two of us had to sit on the couch. But my friend knew exactly what to order and gave us all suggestions! Now ive eaten here like 5 times since my first visit! Start with Avocado salad, you like a little spicyness! Its beyond! Soups are supposedly really yummy too. I am vegetarian so I've had some of the veggie entrees. Chili Dofu, Tsel Shesha, and the Tsel Khowa are all amazing! My friend gets the same thing everytime... Casha Shamdey.. its a chicken dish and the sause it "heavnly" according to her. Really good food, once i asked him to spice my plate up a bit because I love really spicy foods. And this guy was not fooling around. It was so hot Â I was practically sweating! Anything you get is bound to be yummy!

This place is DELICIOUS. I am vegetarian but strangely love sushi even though I never have too many options really - so I was ecstatic to hear about this spot. The rolls are delicious, innovative, healthy, complex, beautifully presented and flavorful. The spot is tiny but they play great hip hop music & has a fun energy to it. You leave feeling satisfied but light n healthy. Love it - highly recommended.

My go-to place for banh mi sandwiches. The perfectly marinated pork is pillowed between a freshly baked hero and topped with tangy carrot and daikon salad and cucumber and hot pepper slices. It is a fairly basic operation, approach the counter and the ladies crank out the sandwiches. You can adjust to taste - I don't like parsley but do like it spicy - and a warm sandwich is in your hands in mere minutes. There are counter seating lined up against both walls so you can dig in right away. And today I saw they added some warm/hot appetizers like spring rolls and pancakes. Looks good and I might partake next time since they were only a dollar or two. The place can be easy to miss since there is scaffolding in the building next door and it's located on the very busy Grand Street. But do yourself a favor and bookmark this place!

Had dinner at this new spot last night. The staff is great and the food was good. The best of the food were the oysters, flat bread, and skirt steak. The cocktails were outstanding. Â The ceviche left me wanting something more flavorful. I will definitely be returning here to sample some other items.

yum yum yum yum yum $3?! yum yum yum yum yum However. I have to agree that the falafel sandwich isn't as good as it used to be. Even a year ago you count on heaps of fresh cabbage and lettuce, but I ate there twice last week and both times were slightly less than awesome. Still great for $3, but not as fresh as it used to be.

As an avid bacon fan, I came here super excited but was sorely disappointed. The bacon was just a hard flat thing.. not juicy or anything. Like yelp says... meh, I've experienced better. Sorry BarBacon, I had high hopes for you. You failed me. :(
Delicious Pad Thai Tofu! Modest environment but the food is delicious. :) Â Lunch specials for under $10.

Really really really good pastrami on decent rye bread with just OK coleslaw. Pastrami...just the right amount of fat and spice. Shared a large ($13) sandwich...enough to satisfy the craving...but I so wanted more!. Bread was decent but crust was softer than I'd like. Coleslaw lacked personality. Pickles....tiny little slivers of sour pickles...were tasty but unsatisfying in such tiny pieces. Walkable (about 20 minutes) from Brooklyn Museum/Botanical Gardens. A little further (about 30 minutes) from the Barclay Center.
True italian and most authentic in nyc. you will leave full and happy. Ask for Rocco!

Great place to start the morning with! We had to wait 10 minutes on the street because it was too crowed inside, which was a bit odd... ( this is only the reason why we scored it as 4 stars and not 5). The dishes were great! Really tasty!!! Defiantly a place to come back too. Tip: come after 10:00 if you don't want to stand in the line and to wait.
Awesome place to grab a bourbon/scotch/gin.

This place is pure perfection when it comes to panini's. I have loved every sandwich I have gotten here (with the exception of the Fontina because I don't like truffle oil, but that's my own fault for ordering it and thinking they'd go light on the oil). My favorite will always be the roast chicken with mozzarella, arugula and spicy mayo. Eating at this restaurant is great as you can sit indoors or outdoors in their garden and the wait staff is pleasant. Ordering is also great as their delivery is pretty quick and the food has always arrived hot. The only "wish" I can think of is that I wish I was able to get chips or a side with my sandwich. However, their portions are always generous so they can stand alone as far as filling you up goes. All in all an awesome spot, and a must visit if you're in Astoria and craving a panini.

Nice spot! I came here on a date & really enjoyed myself. A Moroccan themed spot that is focused on healthy foods as well. It was small, but cozy. Casual, with a SLIGHT smidge of intimate. The aura is like this since people don't know about this place. Heck, I didn't even know about it. Staff is so genuine & hardworking. I really enjoyed myself here. I'll eventually go back. Maybe :)

Breakfast dishes themselves are ok. I think food could be better somewhere else. But they serve you cookies, coffee, and other small breakfast items that makes waiting less boring. The decor inside is pretty wild also. It could be fun, but I wouldn't go out of my way to try it out again.

i like this place. Â its usually pretty crowded though. Â good breakfast, and good drinks, haven't had anything else. Â  they have an open area outside where local merchants sell jewelry, etc. Â  and its solar powered!

Little Collins is an extremely small coffee shop, it's even smaller when the entire shop is seated with patrons. It was really difficult to place an order on a hot summer day since there's no lines or indication of where you should order. The set up of the coffee shop was very much like a bar. I ordered an iced coffee which was just average, I personally wasn't a fan of the dark burnt smokiness of the bean they used. I might just give Little Collins another try but it's not my first choice for coffee in the city.
we had lots of appetizers and pasta entrees. Everything was REALLY salty. I had to wash it all down with pitchers of water and coke...
Great Food. Great Service. 'Nuff said. Only negative, a little too dim for my liking.

This place does not take reservation, and has no order as to who is next. We went to this place, and gave my name to the hostess. Â Then a couple just walk up to the front and cut the line while we were waiting. (I thought they just want to gave their names to the hostess), and the hostess actually sit them first because those guys were just blocking the front. Â  The couple who should be next was yelling how come they got seated ? Those jerks already got seated and the hostess told them they will be next. After that couple is seated, we should be next. Â The hostess did not check her list nor call names, but just seated whoever is standing at the entrance. When we confront the hostess, she sounded very annoyed and said, "ok, ok. You are next." Sorry, that completely ruined my appetite. Â Will never go there again. For anyone who wants to go there: just make sure you bypass everyone and walk up to the front and stand there and the hostess will seat you first. Â Or you can give your name and wait there forever. Sorry, Not my kind of place.

Oh, Ashbox. I love you. I have been working right around the corner for over a year now and this is my go-to spot for lunch. I love this cafe so much that when I think about moving away, Ashbox comes to mind, and I realize how much I would miss it. I normally get the Tofu salad- it's a mix of greens, homemade tofu (which is super soft!), grape tomatoes, cucumber, kelp, sunflower seeds, and this amazing homemade lemon miso vinaigrette. delicious. Pair this with a Spicy Salmon Mayo Onigiri (rice ball) which is my fave of them all and I've got my perfect lunch. The miso soup with fried tofu is also great. My mom's japanese, I've lived in Japan and know what good miso tastes like and this is pretty comparable. It's perfect for those cold winter days. This place is always nice and toasty as well (a nice escape from my cold office). When I'm feeling like I need something a little heartier, I go for the Turkey or Egg Salad sandwich on ciabatta bread. You can't go wrong. The staff are always very friendly and polite. I've gotten some free drinks and cookies here with my to-go orders before (I think because 1. I'm a regular 2. I tip them every time 3. They love me). It can get a little crowded after noon, but there are usually plenty of seats. If you come after 3 on a weekday you'll dodge the lunch crowd.

Just moved to NYC so friends brought me here tonight for a taste of Brooklyn. The food at Roberta's is unbelievably good. Had the clam pasta and a magherita pizza. The pasta was spectacular. Flavorful, cooked to perfection. Didn't have a res so had drinks in the bar tent out back while we waited. It was about an hour but it flew by. Full-on hipster crowd and totally casual, kind of grimy vibe but in a good way. The staff was super eclectic-- tattoos, hoodies, piercings, etc. Host, bartender, server were all really kind. The only downside is the bathroom. Wish it were recessed from the dining room, instead of being smack on top of it.

Beers are so overpriced. Food is lackluster. Clientele is douchey. There's a cute backyard but it's always so crowded, why bother. I've tried this place three times, and i really wanted to like it as it's right near my house and SHOULD be cute. Instead, it's just lame.

Food (5/5) Â  Decor (1/5) Â  Service (1/5) That doesn't actually average to 4 stars, but it's a bit hard to overlook the fact that the dumplings here are REALLY good. Â This isn't a place you go on a date. Â It's not a place you take your parents (as they might be appalled by the sanitation). Â And it might not even be a place you would take your friends from out of town (unless they're super cheap and love dumplings). Â It's a place you go to take out (yes, take out as eating in the cramped 10ft x 10ft space filled with hungry people waiting for their dumplings is not a very enjoyable experience) delicious, mouth watering dumplings to eat elsewhere--maybe on the street a couple blocks over where it doesn't smell quite as bad. Â So forget the fact that the guy at the counter isn't exactly patient (though speaking Chinese helps) and that the restaurant looks like a hole in the wall transplanted directly from Mother China. Â The dumplings are really good and come at the dirt cheap price of 4 for $1. Â These are not your mother's dumplings either. Â These are jumbo dumplings and 8 is a pretty large meal for me. Â Or better yet, buy their frozen dumplings at the even cheaper price of 50 for $9. Â Take them home and cook/eat them at your leisure in the comfort of your own apartment.

I tried the crab and the artichoke pizza slices. The crust is thin yet crispy. The toppings are flavorful, the slices are huge, and the price is decent. Perhaps not the best from a traditional pizza perspective like grimaldi's but definately a goood slice of pizza.
The best Chinese I've ever had. They aren't kidding when they say white meat. Everything is fresh and delicious. Â Worth paying the additional price you pay for the quality.

Went for dinner here last night, as I have been wanting to try this place for quite some time. Â The restaurant is very small, but really cozy-feeling. The tables are very close together, so you can almost brush elbows with the next table, however. Â  Got there at 5 (the only reservation we could get) and was seated at the "prime table" next to the window. Â As it's on the corner of two streets, this provided a great view and as a bonus, we were sitting right next to the heating element, which was great on a cold day. Â The host (Chris?) was extremely accomodating and allowed me to sit at the table for 15 minutes while waiting for my companion. Â  Wine list is small but the reds, at least, were very tasty and they offer a generous pour. Â Few beer choices were offered, but they did have a Maine and a couple Massachusetts brews, which automatically made me want to give them 5 stars. Apps: Lobster soup Â - the broth was flavorful but not too thick that it was heavy like a bisque. Â It is made either with light cream or no cream. Â It came with a few large chuncks of lobster, though they were pretty chewy and seemed overcooked. Â This dish is about 3-stars because, while it was good, it wasn't close to the best i've had. Asparagus risotto - they use large asparagus in the risotto, which I thought lacked flavor and were a bit tough, so the dish was really missing the asparagus flavor. Â The risotto was creamy but not too heavy (they do not use cream, just cheese), but the risotto itself was undercooked and therefore chewy. Â Had the risotto been cooked a bit longer, this would have been a 4-star dish, but it was only a 2.5 for me. Entrees: Cod with green bean salad and parsnip puree - The parsnip puree was the best part of this dish. It was creamy and sweet and had great flavor and texture. Â The green beans were cooked slightly so they were still bright green and crunchy, which I liked, and they were tossed with some sort of greens, perhaps pea shoots or some kind of sprouts. Â The cod was cooked well and flaked off in pieces. Â It was not dry at all. Â The dish was covered in some sort of lemon/olive oil dressing and gave a nice acidity to what would have been a sweet dish due to the puree's sweetness. Â This was a 4-star dish but not because of the cod - rather, because of the deliciousness of the puree and green bean salad the cod laid on. Crispy Chicken with asparagus and potatoes - I never get chicken at a restaurant, but the waitress told me it was one of the two best dishes at the restaurant so I gave it a shot. Â It tasted like a fine-dining establishment's answer to fried chicken. Â It was salty, fatty, and buttery, and had a good taste the first few bites. Â The chicken was not dry, and the skin on top was very crunchy rather than slimy or rubbery. Â The asparagus and potatoes it came with were also cooked well and had a nice flavor. Â However, after more than a couple bites, the chicken tasted a bit one-note, and I wasn't wowed when I continued eating. It starts strong but sort of peters out as you finish the dish. Â I would give this dish 3 stars. The standout of the meal was definitely the cod dish, and I would order it again, though I would probably not order any of the others again. Â  The waitress was helpful and friendly, and when asked for her recommendations as to what is "the best" to order, she surprisingly pointed out some of the cheapest menu options on both apps and entrees, leading me to believe that she sincerely did think these were the best and was not trying to up-sell us. Â I really liked that about her, and was impressed with the service because of it. The host was also incredibly friendly and chatted with me about restaurants in Boston, beers, and complimented my outfit while I waited for my date. Â He was fantastic and really makes the place friendly and home-y. I would say overall that the food deserves a 3-star rating on average, but the ambiance is so romantic and cozy, and the waitstaff was so friendly and accommodating, that I am bumping it up to 4 stars.

This italian restaurant has a great fine dinning look with the welcoming ambiance of a family italian. Â  Elegant with a great buzz. Â  The food was delicious and I think the fried breaded veal was excellent.

My BF and I enjoyed this place. It's small but has a good vibe. I was told that the cheese fondue is great there. Not big fan. But other than that, everything what we order (Pork rib and some today's special veal cutlet) was excellent. Great live music. I'd definitely go back there!

i didn't believe my husband when he said it would be worth the trip. (hey, i grew up a few blocks from sunrise deli and yumma's in sf!) Â i was wrong. so wrong that after i polished off my falafel i marched my butt right back in line for one to take back to the hotel :)

yeah... not much to be said that already hasn't been said.... this place is pretty much flawless. Â Except the bartender that broke a bottle of WHAT?! lol..oh good, it wasn't our bottle of rose..... while, i did not dine the full tasting menu here... a gf and i just rolled up to sit at the tavern bar for some drinks and light appetizers. Â a whole bottle of rose, some sweetbreads, grilled octopus AND a rhubarb bread pudding dessert later.... we were full. Â the food was fantastic, as was the attentive service. Â i love the casual "tavern" dining atmosphere that separates the actual fine dining room. Â  Â  if this is just the amuse bouche to their tasting menu...then i am more than delighted and amp'ed to come back, tavern or the main dining room. Â though i am wondering if there is any difference in terms of quality & taste b/t the two?

Really good, reasonably priced Mediterranean food. Â I usually get the Kruveet or the Zuchinni cakes and recently tried the cookies (all of which are are delicious). Â I stop by a couple of times a week and do schoolwork here and the staff is very warm and polite. Â Great place!

On my sole visit here, a couple I was with ordered 4 apps for their meal--what a good way to go. Â I had a pork loin, which was also very good. Â There's a decent list of beers, and the atmosphere is lovely. Â For a delightful evening I'd recommend taking a stroll along the promenade and hitting the Horse for a late night meal.

Came by since I was in the area and was blown away by the quality of both food and service. Wasn't busy since it was just after the brunch rush but am definitely interested in coming back for lunch/brunch. Will definitely tell friends to stop by.

Had been meaning to go for some time!? However, most of the dishes were really very unexceptional. My poor daughters burger should have been sent back but we were afraid to do so. The service was friendly and attentive at all times. We sat at the very first table so of course were being watch by what I can only image is the grandmother owner. My pancakes were the only dish I would recommend and it came with favored butters as well. I ended up sharing with no problem my pancakes with my poor (sans burger) daughter. Â  I have no real proof for what I am about to report so draw your own conclusions. Four of us got sick within less than 12 ours of eating. I was bedridden unable to look at food. Unfortunately, this place has the strength of being a diner but along with this all the negatives of a diner as well. Example: when using the washroom I noticed that when I entered the room my hands felt wet. After completing my assignment I realized the connection. There were no hand towels and the only way to dry was a slight breeze coming out from what I would have a hard time to call a hand dryer. I have always had problems with food places that do not have hot water or proper ways to dry your hands. I really don't want to shake hands with people with wet hands when I am eating out. So buyer beware. I hope Tom's that truly is a neighborhood favorite reads this and reacts to right an easy to fix wrong. It's a fun place but we certainly will never return after this experience. Sorry

Maman is a great addition to the area between soho and nolita. The case of sweet and savory items is beautifully displayed as is the layout of the rest of the coffee shop. Â I especially like the grilled leeks quiche. Great selection of teas and the service is welcoming, friendly. My one point of contention- why carry all compostable utensils and not have a compost bin?
We have been coming here for over 10 years. Â The food is consistently good and the staff is very friendly. Â It is also a good place for families with kids.

Met two friends here on a Friday night for a birthday dinner. Drinks were good ($10 cocktails). We ordered the peanut bacon brittle and oyster pot pie for starters. Both very tasty. I ordered the duck gumbo which was good. However, I asked if it was spicy. Like any spice level at all. And the waiter shook his head with an emphatic, "no, not at all." Of course, it was spicy. Too spicy for me really to enjoy. (Admittedly I am a spice wimp, but that's why I asked!) Also, It was served over rice and the rice was not fully cooked. That was a bummer. The meal cost me over $50 dollars so I was pretty disappointed. That said, the appetizers were good, drinks were good, and my friends' meals were good. So I might give it a second shot.
Food is fabulous! The owner/chef came out to greet us. Sunday brunch is pack. Please make sure to make reservations. I will recommend to ALL.

Wow! Â This place is amazing. The goat cheese tart is the best thing I've ever had! Â I also really enjoyed my filet and the foie gras on top was amazing. Â I wasn't a huge fan of the dessert however (maybe because i was so full already). Â The servers are so friendly and really make you feel welcome. Â And to top it all off, for 2 entrees 2 appetizers, and dessert, with tax and tip the bill came out to just over 150 dollars. Â A great experience, I can't wait to go back!

Came around 4pm on Thursday and waited only 5 minutes. The staff is really friendly. Location is really crowded, especially the bathroom.. But on to the food review Ramen was so flavorful and new since I've never had a chicken broth ramen before. The pork was amazing and melted in your mouth. And the noodles! So good. Only downfall was that I felt super sick afterwards.. I think it was the oil but I still enjoyed it! Overall, I think it's better than Ippudo but not better than ramen dojo in Cali.
Great pizza with chewy crust that reminds me of naan bread at Indian restaurants. Buratta was delicious. Great atmosphere and service.

I recently had a "girls brunch" at the Writing Room. The Writing Room is a cute restaurant on the Upper East Side. I loved the atmosphere, especially the back room that has a library like feel. However, I found the food to be overpriced and underwhelming. The cornbread was dry, and the salmon eggs benedict tasted too fishy. The bakery items seemed better than the other brunch options. If I returned I would probably stick to the cinnamon rolls. They have a decent tea selection of high quality teas, but the mimosas and cocktails were far too pricey. My mimosa had hardly any champagne....and paying 13 dollars for a glass of orange juice is a bit ridiculous. While I liked the location and the decor, there are much better brunch options in the area.
Try the bone marrow appetizer....DELICIOUS!

Came in late night on a Tuesday. Went for the de facto signature dishes: butcher's steak and spinach gratin. They lived up to the hype ... except the steak was over seasoned with salt. Still, a great place.

I came around 7:30 and was able to get a table for 4 no problem (though the wait got longer as the night went on). Great service, and AMAZING food. Our table shared a variety of pasta dishes that were all delicious--perfectly cooked meats and excellent portions (filling but not over the top). Very neat ambiance (it looks like your Grandma's kitchen late at night) but be prepared for NOISE! It is packed inside. I didn't mind it, and thought it added to the scene. The puffed gnocchi with mozzarella were delicious.

This place is overrated but I enjoyed it. (I almost gave it a 4) First of all, the address is wrong cause its hidden in an alley - part of the charm. It was ice cold outside so thank goodness we had reservations and were not part of the long ass brunch line outside. (good but not worth frostbite people!) Atmosphere is quaint, service was very friendly. Artichoke dip is very good although I dont think people realize how easy this stuff is to make cause its pretty overpriced. I liked my friend's pork sandwich a lot, and the smoked trout was good but not my preference. I loved the cheddar cheese grits. The one thing I did not like: my dish. bummer. Probably why I knocked the review down. Dont call it beef brisket hash and serve something more like stew. Or at least warn people it is large chunks of beef and potato stewed in a sweet beef broth... anyways...its a little overpriced but most of the food is good so I'd go back

We were visiting Staten Island and not sure where to go for breakfast this morning. This small diner was a great find for inexpensive, standard breakfast fare. Eggs and belgian waffle were yummy. We're used to crispy and greasy potatoes, so we found these to be a bit dry. Staff was friendly, waitress was attentive especially with coffee refills. Didn't feel rushed after our meal was over. Customers included NYPD, hard-hat-wearing construction workers, and business suits. Parking was difficult, but apparently thats the norm in the area. Overall, a pleasant experience. Will return next time we're in town.

This is the best kept secret on manhattan. Order everything and when you are done with that order everything again. The sliders are melt in your mouth, juicy, perfect flavor balance and textures of meats. It is the best slider I have ever had. Â Only problem is that you get 3 to and order. And you can not just eat 1. Â So Order 2 per person ~ they will add on a few extras if you ask. Â Or be decadent and get 3 to yourself. There are so many other options to try . Seriously everything is good here. Â Joey is a dessert king and master with all his foods. Salads are heavenly. If you are lucky you will go during white summer truffle season and have a pasta with hefty shavings of the freshest truffles in the city. Staff is super pleasant, knowledgable, and attentive. We Can't wait to return soon!
osewaninattemasu

I dedicate my 300th review to Lamazou because it is THAT good and has actually taken me THIS long to write it because I just didn't know how to put my love into words. Let me try: We love it so much, we have formed a very exclusive Sandwich Club. See Jane K.'s review and you will understand that we are very picky about membership. In fact, her application is still under review thanks to her last minute switch up to the Manou (Buffalo chicken and gouda) instead of the Black Forest (prosciutto, havarti and roasted peppers) and the fact she revealed that one must go early to beat the rush. The only reason she is still in the running is because she shared her peanut butter chocolate gelato bomb with me. I respond well to bribery. When visiting Lamazou, the Lamoretti (roast beef, cornichons and cheddar with horseradish) must ALWAYS be ordered. No questions asked. It is the very best and I'm started to get choked up just thinking about how delicious it is. I've also enjoyed the Butterfly, Smart Duck and Mirabella. You must also always order your sandwich on ciabatta. I haven't tasted their other bread but you know what? I don't want to. This ciabatta is homemade, delicious and just the right amount of crunch on the outside and doughiness on the inside. Why mess with perfection? At this point, don't forget to ask them to slice it in half or if Jane K. is tagging along, into 3s. They will be very accommodating and thanks to their knowing looks, I have a feeling we're not the only Sandwich Club in town. Finally, I just really like the people. The owners pitch in and take orders and make sandwiches when the shop starts to get hopping. They clearly know what they're doing in the sandwich world, and I just might be their biggest fan (even if I do pay in Sacajaweas, Peter D.)

OK, I'll give it to everyone; their ramen is pretty tasty, but having to wait not 1 ... but TWO & A HALF HOURS just to grab a table on a cold Friday evening is RI.DIC.UL.OUS. I actually came at 5pm on a Friday to put my name on their waitlist and the line itself was about 20 minutes (seemed like no big deal) but in order to be seated, all parties must show up. Needless to say, I had to come back when all of my party was able to show up. Fast forward 2 hours later (7pm), we come back to put our name on the list again and we're bombarded with 2 pages of names. The restaurant itself was super small already and the line out the door definitely was greater than what the restaurant could accommodate. My NY friends really wanted me to try this since it's so popular; I abided. I don't mind waiting if it's amaze-balls, but factor in long lines outside on a cold cold night does not make for a good impression.
