We didn't get our seats til about 9:30pm, but what made me really furious was when the guy SKIPPED our name on the list & seated another party of 3 ahead of us (the nerve! well, turns out he placed our names on the top of a new page but forgot it.... argh!) FOOD - yes, their ramen was good. I enjoyed the "niku ramen" I ordered (lots of pork meat & favorful broth) but they do not serve any hot tea ... just cold water (on a cold night... thanks) Overall, the ramen was good, but I'm still left with a bad memory of this place. If I ever return & have to wait even an hour to get seated, I'm out. It's totally NOT WORTH the wait!

This place is absolutely delicious comfort food, from the seasonal salads, to the chicken biscuit, and the boxes. Â Everything is super delicious, and the wait staff is nice. It does get a bit packed, and I prefer sitting in the back room, but overall a solid experience. Â Limited space for big groups. It's cash only, but there's an ATM outside.

I'm ALMOST tempted to give HC 5 stars, my experience last night was that great but I don't just dole out 5 stars willy nilly. We walked in on a Tuesday night around 7:00 with a reservation at the chef's counter. It was a nice night, if a bit chilly, and a few brave souls were enjoying cocktails out in the front garden. The atmosphere of this place is so freaking adorable. We were able to score a small table for two down by the bar so we grabbed it. We were kind of in the way of the servers trying to place drink orders but they were very gracious about it. I only have a few tiny little complaints. The wine by the glass offering could be a bit stronger and I wish they had better stemware. We had had some wine at Lela Bar across the street so we didn't want to do a bottle, although the bottle list is not bad. I started with the Valdo prosecco and it was very mediocre to below average. My date chose the Chateau Lagrezette Malbec but then changed it to the Johnson Family Â Cabernet instead, I wasn't a huge fan of either. I realize the proper pour is 5 oz but when you have a Â small glass and only pour up to a proper amount it doesn't equal 5 oz, just sayin. Our waiter was very attentive as were all the people working there. The amuse bouche was sublime, a slice of grapefruit with fennel and mint, I wish they had that as an appetizer! We decided to split a bunch of things so here's the rundown: 1. warm red quinoa, black kale, swiss chard, almonds, confit pear, manchego - uhmmm a MUST order, I could be satisfied eating this every day. 2. braised lamb shank, mint spÃ¤tzle, carrot, broccoli, parmesan cream, tarragon - another winner, the use of mint in a lot of the dishes was so fresh and springlike I could almost taste summer on the way! 3. DUCK BREAST & CONFIT LEG fava beans, english peas, chantarelle mushrooms, grape tomato, pattypan squash duck jus - the duck was absolutely perfect, crispy skin, moist meat with the leg being insanely tasty. 4. green & white asparagus, smoked ricotta, pea tendrils, lemon vinaigrette - this wasn't my choice, I mean asparagus is asparagus but this was definitely one of the better sides I've had. AWFUL TERRIBLE SERVICE. Which is a shame because the food is really good. We went for a friend's birthday (there were 8 of us) and made a reservation for 12:30p on a Saturday. I arrived with one other friend first and were told we'd have to wait for our entire party to arrive before we were seated. Ok, not a problem! My friend and I gladly grabbed a drink from the bar. The rest of our party arrived about 10 minutes before our reservation. We were told they were getting our table ready. Around 1pm they finally seat us. That's 30 minutes PAST our reservation, at least a 45 minute wait. We received the wrong food that we ordered, drinks didn't come in a timely manner (and when I mean timely I mean we had to remind our servers about them twice), and the servers were rude! With the exception of the one waiter that was very nice and apologetic, everyone else was just mean. No customer service/hospitality skills whatsoever. We asked if we could split the charges among cards and they said that wouldn't be a problem. They charge one of my friends the full amount (almost $300) and only charged some of us the split amount. You would think when you're spending $300 in a place you could expect decent service. This was not the case. The food is good, but I wouldn't go back there if my life depended on it. There are plenty of other great places to eat in the city; don't waste your time or money on this hell hole.

In a field of many Toby's does a pretty nice job. It really is a science to get that perfected Neopolitan pie, and Toby's isn't the best. It is very tasty with more crunch than chew, but a nice assortment of toppings however. The place is very small and kind of hectic, but if you need a beer and a pie before 6pm it's a good standby.

This is my favorite thai restaurant in Long Island City. Their food is delicious and very inexpensive. The ambience, service, staff everything is great. I have been going to tuk tuk for 3 years now, i have taken many friends here and haven't dissapointed everyone. My favorite from them: Drink: Thai Iced Tea Appetizer: Curry Puff Papaya Salad Entree: Green Curry with Tofu Drunken Noodle with Shrimp Dessert: Mango with Sticky Rice (Seasonal)
great food. cheap and really well kept place
GREAT CORN! Came here on a late Monday night and was one of the last customers. I was very pleased that the waitress didn't try to rush us out.

This place is the best had a reservation for my mother bday dinner an of course the world runs on her time so she shows up an hour later I thought Â we lost the reservation but they waited an kept a four person table ready for just me an my mother an their was a lot of ppl waiting to be seated before us had an fantastic time great food great music will be back very soon.

I wish I had come across this restaurant sooner. Having always been a fan of malatesta and not realizing there was a sister restaurant, my boyfriend and I stumbled upon malaparte and decided to give it a try. Not only was the food off the chart, the service was impeccable. I have to say that the service as malatesta has gone seriously down hill which is why we were on the look out for a new italian favorite. My boyfriend and I enjoyed a wonderful meal and kept it mind for the next time we wanted a low key evening with great food and wine. Fast forward 2 weeks. My family came to visit, which included my parents, 2 brothers in their early twenties and one of their girlfriends. May I also mention that my father is extremely impatient and we had a diverse group of tastes. After the wonderful service, reasonable prices and great food we had the last time we were there, we decided to take the group to malaparte. The wait staff made the night our most enjoyable meal of the visit. The staff was attentive, made sure the group always had drinks and the wide range of food, came out quickly, done to perfection and no one was waiting for their dish. Additionally, when paying the bill we did not notice that gratuity had been included (due to the extremely reasonable prices) and tipped on top of it. The staff immediately pointed it out to us and returned the extra money. I can not say enough I impressed I was by the staff. Thank you for such a wonderful evening, it went off without a hitch and the family couldn't have enjoyed it more! (also failed to mention, this is my first yelp review, joined just to post on this restaurant!)

Lillie's please make your restaurant wheelchair accessible. Â I called to make a reservation, and asked if it was wheelchair accessible. Â The host said yes, then she said well, all the chairs are high (barstool style). Barstool height chairs are not wheelchair accessible. What a lost opportunity.
Love this place. Ordered online and went to pick up the same day. Sara is very sweet. I ordered a lot of marshmallows for our camping trip and Oh man they are delish.

Mmmm mmm - who doesn't love Ramen? Even if it is in the middle of the summer and the wait is 20-30 minutes? I went to Ippudo for lunch on Sunday and while I thought I was getting up earlier than most New Yorkers (noon), the place was still packed. The tables are shared, but they don't feel cramped, but the service is a bit hectic. It took us awhile to flag down our waiter. I ordered the Akamaru Modern which was unbelievably good. The broth is always what does it for me at a ramen place, and Ippudo was no exception. It had a really rich flavor and when I stirred in the special sauce, the broth became even tastier. The pork was really super tender and the noodles were cooked perfectly. I was definitely lovin' life as I slurped down my lunch. I would definitely come back here again - I wish they did take out though. I would love to eat that ramen while watching Top Chef in my underwear at home.

This place needs some work. Quite generic in everything they offer, but then again, prices are low. I may have ordered the wrong things. Don't eat grilled chicken here... it will be very... very dry. You'd probably safe with hummus or other simple things. I was disappointed but it's clearly a very popular spot. I imagine nothing is truly made from scratch.

Food here was delicious and beautifully presented, and the service was friendly. The decor was trendy and the menu prices are very reasonable. They obviously make their money on the drinks, which are way overpriced. Another downside was that the place was super loud (even at 11pm). That's to be expected in New York, though.

you wouldn't imagine sitting on a stoop facing mounds of garbage bags heaped on the side of the street with piping hot artichoke cheese and cream oozing through your fingers on a humid, sweaty, sooty-skinned nyc day a welcome experience..but it is!!! this place is CHARMING and DELICIOUS! many characterize the first few bites as 'heavenly'--and they are! its like eating cream of artichoke soup atop cheese and a perfectly baked crust (again..not something you'd imagine would be enjoyable on a hot summer day...but somehow its so perfectly tasty and savory it doesn't matter that its 90 degrees out and your fingers are dancing to balance the burning fresh out of the oven pizza crust collapsing in massive artichoke topping goodness). there is only a tiny bench outside for seating...and standing room at an outdoor plank/makeshift bar for a few more folks...as i mentioned it faces the street and LOTSA garbage bags...but the pizza hits the spot...and you feel happy and even kind of smug as literally EVERY passerby comments on Artichoke as they pass by... "o man! i've always wanted to try this place..there is is always such a long line" "i've heard of this place...it's supposed to be really good/" and the most common: "OMG this place is AMAZING!--lets get cash and get a slice" i suggest you do the same :)

My fiance and I had dinner here on a Friday night. Â In general the food was pretty good and the staff was attentive - though it would be hard not to be in a place so small with no real kitchen to hide in. Â What really killed it for me was the looong wait and cramped interior. Â 45+ minutes milling about outside on the sidewalk. We ordered the patatas bravas (spicy potatoes). Â The potatoes were delicious - chunky, crunchy and salty. Â However, the 'spicy aoili' that was drizzled over them was basically like creamy mayo or something, which was different than what I am used to when it comes to patatas bravas. Â We ended up ordering a second batch with the sauce on the side and a side order of sriracha. Â That was awesome. :) ham croquettes - seriously a waste. Â There was no ham to be found in them. They were just fried balls filled with some sort of soft cheese. Â It reminded me of something you could get at a drive in (like Sonic) and be disappointed by. chorizo - At first I wasn't terribly excited by these but they grew on me. Â I would definitely get them again. peppers? - some sort of Spanish pepper sauteed and sprinkled with sea salt. Yum! Good Sangria. Â I also had a light, easy to drink glass of red wine that the waiter recommended. Â I think the wine list should definitely include way more wines by the glass than it does. Â This is a tapas restaurant after all - Â the idea being to enjoy small portions of food with a glass of wine. Â But I guess this is America as well, so the authenticity isn't as important as the overall experience. In summary, not a bad place, but not terribly special. Â I'd probably rather trek to Brooklyn for Zipi Zape Tapas Bar for the more spacious seating (indoor or outdoor), local, owner run feeling, and way more variety.

I had pancakes, which I saw photos of first. First let me say it is rare to get food that looks like the photo. Judging from all the photos, they are pretty consistent. The pancakes were buttery, hot and fluffy. I feel sorry for those going to chain pancake places. The omelet was really good as well. I will be back
Love this place. Â The pizza is awesome! Stone street is a great place to socialize as well.

I read the previous reviews and can totally see where some people are coming from. Yes this place it VERY snug and tiny- Yes the service can be snarky- Â but all in all it has become one of my go to spots in the neighborhood. Their food is pretty good- do NOT get the baked clams- but DO get the lobster risotto and anything that is served with buratta. Wines are pricey but it is what it is. The bartender does not want to be your friend- but he will pour you a glass of vino....when he gets around to it.

Ah, Srapraphai you STILL got it. Â Shoo to the naysayers that say this authentic famed Thai restaurant has gone downhill. Â Came here for lunch back in the day, and returned this past weekend only to find it is simply the BEST, highest quality and freshest Thai there is in NYC, Hail Woodside, Queens (where all the true Asian food is). Â  This place is spacious, clean and pretty festive actually given it's Queens; when I came last weekend there was a big family birthday bash going on. Â On both times I've come for lunch around 1, I didn't have to wait and was promptly seated. Â Service can use some work, but the food and value are so good, I didn't have the heart to dock a star. Â The servers were polite and friendly, and made fine recommendations but they were slow in getting us proper silverware (we were missing knives and forks and what not), needed our waters refilled and other blips (they didn't give us chopsticks right away, how wude!) No one can deny the cheap prices; most apps, soups and entree are at $10 at the most, and a whole fish can be just a whopping $20. Â Not to mention you really get never, before-seen Thai dishes that are authentically Thai. Â In the 212, you get your usual Pad Thai, drunken noodles and green curries... all run by the Chinese. There is trully no where that can compare ('cept maybe Rhong Tiam before they went take-out only). There are some Chinese-oriented dishes, true but here is the run-down on what you should get: 1. Start off with a soup. Â Either th Tom Yum (traditional), or Tom Gha Ga- I happen to like the latter. It's a creamy, coconut milk based galanga soup with chicken .. which is creamy, sour, and really rich in that zingy galanga flavor. Some might find it a little too herbal? A little medicinal, but I swear it's an interesting spice that blends really well with the sourness of the soup. They have the Tom Yum version with cornish hen too, hen! 2. Papaya salad- hands down, the BEST papaya salad I've ever had. Â So fresh and crispy- like it was right from da garden! Not only is the chilli/ lime juice dressing so delicious (I swear there is fish sauce in here!), this salad is tossed in with dried shrimp! (In Burmese we called this Belachong.. not sure what the Thai call it) Sounds nasty but it adds a great crunchy texture and salty flavor. 3. The Fried Bean Curd- a simple fried tofu; there wasn't anything too specical about this. I've actually had better "golden" tofu (more battered), so this might have been my least fav. It was fried in such a way where the shell tastsed like paper (and I do not believe in tasteless tofu)....and was a bit dry ( of course then, not greasy, so pick and choose your battles!). Â The side sauce of sweet peanut dipping sauce was complimentary though. I think next time I will opt for the curry puff (typical but tasty), or "golden bag" (this recognizable puff looked good next door) 4. Pad Thai- traditional Pad Thai always hits the spot. No frills, just peanuts, egg and clear noodles. Â  Not too greasy...delicious. They also seemed to have good, traditonal drunken noddles along with some Chinese of flavorings: soy sauce noodles. 5. There were a lot of good looking "over rice "dishes, but since we had our Carb fixed already, we went for a main, a la carte. We were going to go for a curry but my sister didn't want one that was made with coconut milk and the only one that does not was the Jungle Curry and that's kind of watery and not fun. We ordered the Saute Duck, came with the usual chilli and basil spices... this was ok; a little TOO saucy. The flavor was good but it was just a little tough. Conversely, the veggies were a little soggy. I'd wish we gone for a cripsy fish option or the soft shell crab (yum yum). In addition to the duck, we got a side of coconut, brown and chicken rice. Â Each was so rich in flavor, especially the chicken!! Â It was so tasty- I could have ate it alone. Even the brown had a nice nutty flavor- I'm sure they used all top notch ingredients. (An anecdote, my sister asked for green tea and got a really special brand which they only sell in Chinatown!) We were so stuffed, we took some food home. Â I had no room for dessert but there seemed to have been quite an extensive dessert menu; sticky rice and other sweet little things (which you can get via the take-out fridge near the door). The total bill came to $60 or something but we ordered a lot of food. I don't ever regret trekking here (though admittedly, I came via car both times wah wah but if I must the 7 train will suffice). Sripraphai is simply the BEST Thai and anyone who says otherwise.... well they must be from the motherland themselves! P.S. Cash Only

i go to cafeteria when its late and i want real food and even if i have to wait in a line around the block for 30 min like a club, its worth it. the food is yummy they have a vegan burger the fries are so tasty!! its a party in there. loud dj. celebs always. good for anytime, any occasion! loove

It is easy to overlook Rose Water, on the corner of a residential street but you would be wise to stop in. I've been for brunch - which I had no complaints but after dinner, last night, I can say that this is one of my favorite restaurants in the neighborhood. As a vegetarian, it is often a struggle to find a solid , delicious entree other than your standard veggie plate. Rose Water has succeeded. The Baked Polenta was absolutely delicious as were the brussel sprouts and chantarelle mushrooms on the side. The staff/service was attentive and personal. I highly recommend and cannot wait to go back.

Oh man did I like this place. Took a minute to find, it's not incredibly obvious from the outside. Met some friends on a Monday night, about a dozen of us seated in the back. Had a couple of Peronis to warm up as we were early. EVERYTHING I tried was excellent. Had the carpaccio salad, don't miss this one if you go, worth the trip all by itself. The flat bread and prosciutto plate was also killer. I had the seafood soup, don't remember the name but it was fabulous. This is my go-to order whenever I travel around, they make some variant of it in basically every country I've ever been to. This version was very rich, generous with the seafood and had a rosemary overtone that knocked it out of the park. Great atmosphere, reasonable prices, highly recommended. Gotta take the wife here on date night, it's that good.

Difficult to get in, and those terra-cotta pots on the ceiling look like might fall...but food so good. Â Appetizers more interesting than entrees-but isn't that always the case? Â I love the beet napolean thing in particular.

This weekend I dined at Ngam... my second time there. I enjoyed the atmosphere: communal, hip and young. My family and I ordered their chiang mai fries as an appetizer. The idea and complimenting sauces were great. However, it felt like I was eating straight batter when it came to the main component of the dish. For our entrees, we ordered the curry duck, zuchinni pad thai, pad see ew, and lamb. My family loves to share our meals, so I got to try each dish. The curry duck was my favorite. Duck was crispy and well cooked. I recommend getting the coconut rice on the side because their jasmine rice (that comes with the curry) is too dry and lukewarm at best... Â The zuchinni pad thai was a great concept, but was overflowing with tofu and was lacking in" zuchinni noodles", which I was most excited for. I wish it was less of a tofu dish and more representative of a pad thai that the menu promised. My sister's favorite dish was the pad see ew (very traditional and well executed). Lastly, the lamb was plated beautifully, and I appreciated the work that went into the dish. It also had good flavors, but may have been, at times, overpowered by the red pepper/chilli flakes sprinkled on top. Overall, I liked the menu options and flavors. I would give Ngam a 4 star for the food, but for the two times I have visited Ngam, my waiter/waitress was non-existent.

Came here with 5 people on a Saturday night, and while it was crowded, it didn't take long to get a table. Â I wasn't crazy about the company, so I was eager to drink. Â The Lychee martini was excellent. Â I had a few and suddenly the company didn't seem so bad (and one of the couples left, but whatever). Â It was noisy which, for my purposes, was a plus. Â Not all that memorable, but not bad. Â Also, I am pretty sure it wasn't all that expensive which is nice.

Loved this restaurant! Â I don't really like pizza, but the pizza here was really delicious and only around $15 for a pie. Â Some of my fave appetizers here are: mozzarella and tomatoes dish and the peekytoe crab. Â I had the halibut for my entree; it was good, but I was so full from the appetizers and pizza that I couldn't appreciate it. Â The only issue I had with this place was that the bass had a lot of dill in it, and the menu did not mention that fact.
Best thai in New York City. Nice and spicy. Great service. Delivery sometimes not as hot as it should be, and can take long, but worth it.

I gotta say, I love this place! Its a cozy little place that offers great service, great cocktails, and beautiful design. The cocktails are between $8-$12 and are worth it. Delicious and refreshing. Im a fan.

the portions are generous as they were intended on family style eats. the tugboat was a monster--I'm somewhat afraid of what the titanic looks like..the amount of ice cream fruit nuts and whipped cream was such taht 4 people split and still couldnt finish... to be fair though the ginormous amount of food that came out slowed us down xD the carmine salad was pretty good, the diced bits of meat and cheese definitely was a yummy surprise (co-worker ordered it and i just said ok) the veal parm was a little disappointing as the meat was a but tough--almost seems as if it was sitting to cool for too long (the cheese seemed a touch dry and lukewarm... all in all wasn't a bad meal...but wasn't particularly amazed by it either

beer. burger. Â nonsense. Â none. Â  I requested rare and although there is a limit to the rareness I would prefer, I was impressed that they gave me a real rare burger. Â ppl are so paranoid these days. Â  it was late and we piled into a booth while 1 or 2 ppl missed chunks of the conversation because they fell asleep sitting up. Â we stole their fries. Â what's not to like?

Terroir Tribeca is a little hipster-y and it isn't quite as cozy of a venue as I normally like in a wine bar, but it's a very cool spot and was busy. I know why it was busy too; they have great happy hour specials! They have a selection of about 10 to 12 wines that are all $6 per glass between 4 and 6pm. The regular prices of the same glasses are between $9 and $13. This is a great reason to come in early. The service was great and my waitress was happy to make some suggestions along with very good descriptions of the wine. This summer has been declared The Summer of Riesling at Terroir, so all of the white wines by the glass are Riesling. Luckily, Riesling can be either dry or sweet, so if you're a white wine drinker, you're sure to find something that will suit your taste. I recommend the 2009 Hermann J Weimer Late Harvest Riesling...it's like drinking heaven. Awesome place with a fun vibe. Go there this summer, especially if you're a Riesling fan!

Ok, here's the breakdown: 1 star for the service and 3 stars for the food. My server, Jesse, was very nice and polite but extremely slow and unattentive. After he gave us a glass of water each, took our order, & served our food, he never checked up on us. It was quite annoying because our glasses were empty for a good 15 minutes - we were so parched from walking around in all that heat yesterday! He finally appeared, only to greet the peeps sitting at the table next to ours. I was also searching for him not only because I was thirsty and needed a refill, but because my grilled turkey burger was very pink on the inside (more on the food next). Anyway, I patiently waited for Jesse to take their order and I was hoping he would turn around and ask how everything was going. But he did not, so I had to reach out and grab his arm as he practically ran away. I showed him my pink turkey burger and he actually asked "where is it pink?". WHAT?! oh no he didn't. He took it back to get grilled again. Â What really annoyed me was when he looked at our empty glasses and asked "do you need refills?" hmmm...no shit. My turkey burger (with lettuce, tomato, avocado, & cranberry aioli sauce) was OK. It would have been great if it weren't practically red in the middle. After Jesse took my burger back to the kitchen (scary), the chef brought it back out. He explained that their turkey meat was always a little pink, but that he "still went ahead and grilled it for you all the way through." Um, I didn't understand how he was able to grill it completely yet tell me their burgers are usually a little pink?? Anyway, it looked like I had a fresh new plate and burger, but I took the bun off to inspect the burger and HAH - the chef gave me a brand new bun and toppings but my bitten burger was still on the bread! Maybe I'm wrong but I thought they should replace the entire thing if they left it half raw! My cousin said her hamburger was delicious though, so that's a good thing. Our neighbors got the breakfast croissant and it looked delicious! I don't live in NYC but the next time I visit I would like to come back and try the breakfast - I will just avoid the turkey burger. Also, the place is very cute and simple. Â Lovin the color scheme!

I have live in LIC for 2 months and this is definitely the bright spot of the restaurant scene. You can't go wrong with any noodle dish although Â Pad Kee Mao is my personal favorite. The prices are very reasonable. I will probably give into their lunch special in another hour or so.

Bullet points: Everything I've tried on the tiny menu is tasty and well-made No liquor license as of last visit, so byob Super-nice, unpretentious people waiting tables and behind the bar It's a refreshing break from the over-hypedness that can sometimes get too much in Williamsburg. Â Sometimes I don't want artisanally produced greens/water/air and excruciatingly designed everything else. Â That said, I've got mixed feelings about the room; once in a while it feels too bare, even though it's small, and at other times the sparse decoration feels soothing. Wanted to review it because more people should try it. Â It's almost always uncrowded probably because of the lack of a liquor license, not because it's not good. Â Ack, I hate double negatives.

This place is so awesome from the ambiance to their signature dishes. Â The tempura butternut squash is to die for as well as the seafood Frito Misto!!! Â I loved it so much I requested to speak with the chef. Â To my astonishment he took the time out to make sure all was well. Â I'll definitely recommend this place to anyone and everyone. Â Thanks Chef Bustillo!!!

Num Pang doesn't need another glowing review here, but I gotta give them some love regardless. ILU, NP! Â I love the way your amazing bread (and my face) gets soaked through with delicious porky grease. Â You are the best, the best!
I felt kinda nasty after leaving and found the soup dumplings here to be a little on the gelatinous side. They were ok, but I'm not going back since the wait is out of hand.

I had been wanting to go here for a while but was put off by the no reservation policy, however I needn't have worried - you just give your name and number to the staff and they'll call you to come back when the table is ready, meaning you can go elsewhere for a drink while you wait. We went on a Sunday evening and didn't have to wait more than 45 minutes. The ramen, as I'd heard, were amazing, some of the best I've had outside of Japan. I will definitely be back!

This place is a repeater for me. Â I moved down the street and have really made this a staple due to its reasonable prices, delicious fare, and laid back attitude. Â I love the fresh food at decent prices, especially for this 'hood. Â I also like the BYOB policy which saves you a pretty penny. Â I find the menu and fresh ingredients very tasty in a restrained way -- not too many heavy sauces, not the kitchen sink on your plate. Â I feel clean and healthy when I leave here and will continue to come here. Â They also make delicious iced coffee, so I get one to go almost every day int his heat wave. Â Just remember to bring cash.

The cool thing about starting a new job in a new neighborhood is that you get to explore and learn where all the good places to eat are. I recently discovered Hanamizuki, which sells Japanese rice balls. It's right smack in the middle of wholesale clothing and jewelry stores so it's easy to miss if you're not looking! They do an Omusbi Plate combo for $9.50 and you get your choice of 2 rice balls and miso soup combined with their appetizer of the day and Japanese pickles. There are 8 rice ball choices and 4 miso soup choices - all of them sound super delicious! I went with the Hawaiian, which had spam, dried tomato, chili and nori - seaweed, and the Sweet Potato, which had Japanese sweet potato, hijiki-seaweed, deep fried tofu and black sesame. For my miso soup, I went with the Gnocchi, which had tofu-gnocchi, arugula, black peppers and extra-virgin olive oil. I really liked the miso soup - the gnocchi was very moist and chewy. The arugula was also made the soup very fresh and light. The rice balls were a bit on the small side but they're pretty filling once you get through eating both of them! I thought the Hawaiian wasn't as good as some other spam musubis I've had but it was pretty tasty. I really liked the Sweet Potato rice ball because it was sweet and salty at the same time. The workers were very friendly and I hear the desserts are coming in soon so that's definitely something to look forward to. They also serve Columbe coffee!

While the food is some of the best Thai food I've had in NYC, their service is appalling. For a restaurant of this level, it's embarrassing how poorly trained their staff are at handling simple tasks. We had such a poor restaurant experience - we arrived prior to our reservation but still waited 45(!!!) mins to be seated and the food takes a good 60 - 75 mins to arrive after you've ordered = don't come hungry. The server barely checked in on us and took 30 mins to bring my glass of wine. We enjoyed the food, so we agreed never to come back there - only get takeout or delivery. Well - I just had to call 4 times because the first person who would answer transferred me to someone else who then put me on hold, picked up and hung up. This happened 4 times before I finally spoke to someone and they said I lived 2 blocks outside of the delivery zone. What? I've had your food delivered here numerous times... seriously? You can't come 2 more blocks for an $80 delivery order? In NYC you can get great food and great service combined. Those who don't provide both will not survive as we can all just spend our money elsewhere.

How have I not written a review for this yet??? Ridiculousness as I've probably been to this Pio Pio location like 8 times. This is by far my favorite location of all the Pio Pios. It is chic and the space is massive - perfect for birthdays and groups. They do not seat you until your entire party is there - so make sure you tell your friends to arrive 30min before the reservations if your friends are anything like mine. We always do pitchers of sangria, the matador, lomo saltado and occasionally some seafood themed dish. Although everyone raves about the chicken...I actually enjoy the lomo saltado more! It's strips of tender beef sauteed with peppers and onions on a bed of french fries. Bangin'. I also strangely enough like the avocado salad that comes with the matador combo. And the green sauce. Sigh. Solid 5 stars!! P.S. they also do take out!

My favorite tapas in the city. Best to go early in the evening or late right before the regular menu stops. The second floor overlooking the main room is the place to be. The Smoked Eggplant And Lebne Dip, Crispy Brussels Sprouts, Grilled Gulf Shrimp & Chorizo Skewer, and Avocado Relleno are regular favorites, tho they used to do a smoked mozzarella in a kataif-like cup that was the coup de grÃ¢ce.

I am sorry Sanford's. Â Like most amazing things in my life, no one has ever heard me talk about you. Â The most prized, amazing & cherished things in my life, I keep to myself. Â Some people brag. Â I brag about things. Â However, I choose to brag about things I don't care to lose. Â The other stuff, I keep close, and under stealth. I love Sanford's. Â The secret is out now that Yelp has a Queens site and community and it has been profiled. Â Ironically, putting the word out has DECREASED the traffic a little bit, not cause crazier lines like I once thought. So like any jealous guy, I hope you stay the hell out of this amazing brunch spot. Â Sometimes I sit at the tables, sometimes I sit at the bar. Â I love the bloody marys and the brunch menu is really amazing. Â I get hot chocolate with it, and it kills some of the heat. Â  I believe brunch is everyday now. Â Call to find out for sure.

This is becoming a go-to when we're in this part of Astoria. I like the approach in that MP Taverna offers a number of familiar flavors, but sometimes with little twists. But the twists never come off as pretentious. The overall vibe of the place is nice, straddling that line between casual and a little Â more upscale well. On two visits, our servers were friendly and helpful. One word, though. If you can, get a table upstairs. The sound Â there is more conducive to conversation with the folks at your table. If your taste in beverages runs to more potent potables, they have plenty of options. I've had a cocktail, the exact name escapes me, that was basically their take on the mojito that was effectively refreshing. Now, as to the food. This will focus more on our visit last night and touch back to one at the end of May. In the two visits, there was only one disappointing dish -- the calamari appetizer. The calamari itself avoided the texture woes, but was curiously lacking in flavor. While this place generally excels at not getting too fussy, this was one instance of erring too far on the side of simplicity. With that out of the way, on to last night. We had three items as apps -- the Octopus with Mediterranean chickpea salad, Grandma's meatballs and the bulgur salad. The Octopus -- Oh. My. Goodness. It is the best octopus dish I've ever had. The texture was perfect, not the slightest bit of rubberiness, with a nice char on the outside. It went very well with the salad, with the pairing of the chickpeas and the octopus proving a great choice. The bulgur salad was a refreshing balance of sweet and salty, soft and crunch. Pomegranates and dates, almonds and olives, red onions and pine nuts. The meatballs came with wedges of soft pita bread, tzatziki sauce and lemon. The texture was more creamy than dense and meaty, but it was solid, if unspectacular. These three were all well portioned apps, as opposed to the sausage one from the first visit, which was tasty, but seemed skimpy by comparison. The mains -- Roasted lemon chicken, grilled dourade, dumplings. I can speak most about the dumplings. Made with ricotta, they managed the nice trick of being pillowy without becoming gluey or overly glutenized. The sauce was a perfect vehicle -- acidity from the tomato (regular and sun-dried), a little funky edge from the feta, spicy kick from garlic and pieces of lamb sausage. My dining companions enjoyed their entrees. The one who had the chicken isn't as big a garlic fan as us, but still enjoyed it, in particular showing appreciation for the crunchy, flavorful skin. The one who had the dourade it was very clean, a fresh grilled fish that met her expectations to the letter. I can't pass without noting an entree from the first visit -- the Greek paella. It is another good option, as they didn't skimp on the seafood. Orzo pasta subs for the rice and the sauce was quite flavorful, resembling nothing so much as a diavolo sauce. Desserts: Baklava apple napoleon and galakataboureko creme brulee The napoleon is a good example of offering familiar flavors in a well-executed, different fashion. Layers of baklava with apple compote inside and a spiked ice cream on the side. It is sort of an apple pie flavor profile, but with the crunchy phyllo and honey, it adds a different dimension. Or, if you prefer, the apple adds a little bit of flavor to cut into what can sometimes be cloying sweetness in a baklava. Oh, and the ice cream was pretty darn good, too. The creme brulee is something we've enjoyed on both visits. The fresh berries cut into it. The crunch from the shredded phyllo set it off. It's not an "OMG, amazing dessert!", but it's pretty darn good. One final note, this place is not a "cheap eats dive", BUT the prices are a good value. Similar dishes would be higher-priced in Manhattan. For example, I highly doubt the dumpling dish would only be $15. All in all, it's a worthy addition to Astoria and well worth the trip for others outside of Queens Â (it's a short walk off the last stop on the N and Q lines).

yes! pricey for queens but worth it for a nice date or special occasion, or even just a mid week pick me up (forgive me, people who use their money wisely). the new salmon dish is awesome. it would be great if they had more veggie options but still...good stuff. The way Japanese to keep their tradition and culture is very respectful. Â Sushi Yasuda is one that deserves your respect. To taste sushi better, I recommend you order one or two pieces at a time. inexpensive, fast service (sub 30 second wait time during peak), satiates any craving you may not even have had.

This was easily one of the top 10 best meals I've ever had! Now, separately, the meals would not have been so great. Â If you come here, you should agree amongst your fellow diners on appetizers to share, because the combination of flavors is killer. My friends and I shared the Phoenician fries, the Riz, and the Mouhamara. Â I could've done without the Riz, it was just rice, a bit bland, but the other two were wonderful. Perfect hole in the wall-you won't have this at home-snack spot. Â I came here after while I was in NYC for my birthday weekend. Â A friend recommended this spot and it was just right. Â  They give you a paper cone of pommes frites (basically just belgian fries) and you pick a sauce (or more) and you're good to go.

Came here with 3 coworkers - sat caddy corner at the bar. After reading a Serious Eats "Best Grilled Cheese of NYC" where they named Westvilles' one of em, I had to try. Family style, we started out with baked clams, fried calamari, caesar salad, a bottle of house chianti, chicken parmagiana, sausage and meatballs, rigatoni alla vodka with mushrooms, and sautÃ©ed broccoli rabe. The food as always not fancy but consistently good. Â Had friends in town with their twin daughters for the first time needed a good consistent Italian restaurant in the theater district. Â It was very busy, lots of large groups, several birthdays we could tell by the number of times they were singing "Happy Birthday." Just an informational update that while the downstairs bar is now only open on Fridays and Saturdays; you can rest assured that they'll still take care of you. Â The 9-part Salt & Ash is still delicious, but if you are very lucky you may be able to score a Fernet-Sling (shwing!).

My boo and I had a great time at Swine! Between the two of us, we had a 5-choice board of gravlax, duck prosciutto, foie gras torchon, country pate, and speck. Everything was tasty and I loved the idea of trying something new (duck prosciutto). The whole grain mustard that came with it was DIVINE and the waiter said it was locally made in Brooklyn. The dessert, the Swine Sundae, was eh. the added chocolate-covered bacon was too overwhelmingly salty.
Great brunch place without the hellacious wait of other, more popular places. Get a seat outside if it's nice.

My staple when studying till late at the Bobst library (with plenty of drunk people for entertainment)!

my my my, hard to find but, so worth it! this little place is a gem. i don't think i would look anywhere else for traditional japanese. it takes a while to get seated (it seems as if there is always a packed house) but its definitely worth the wait. the vibe is very cool, casual, and friendly. definitely a go. :3

The best middle eastern platters, the rest are imitations. Watch out for the looooong lines though specially late at night or early in the morning depending on how you look at it. All the drunk clubbers standing in line for 45 minutes to get their fix ;). Good times!
The truffle burger with truffle glaze is out of this world. Couple that with one of their selected beers and it will be a very satisfying meal.

Definitely a 3.5 star place, especially with all the hype, it's a lot better if you go in expecting it for what it is: a long wait for what is ultimately good (not great) Ramen, great pork (and subsequently pork buns) I would probably never come back if the pork wasn't as tender and succulent as it is. It's small and intimate, which makes it great for when you're eating, but this, compounded by the hype, causes the long lines.

I'm not so much a fan of the food as I am of the service. Â The food is mediocre at best. Â Two items that do stand out are the chili cheese omelette and the corned beef. Â  Getting back to the service. Â It's one of the best examples of how a restaurant should treat its clientele. Â Gus, the owner is all smiles and greets everyone who walks through the door. This place has great food and is one of the few places in Brooklyn to accept bitcoin!

This was my favorite Turkish place until......looks like some renovations are underway. That's a good thing. But they renovated the prices as well. The mix plate chicken/lamb has gone up to $17.20 from $13. Â At 13 the price was fair but at 17 I think they will have shot them self in the foot. I will certainly not be back and nor will my co-workers. Â We will miss this gem but I guess it's time to move on.

Pizzas are no ordinary slices. Great ingredients and great attention to detail. The owner is originally from Brooklyn which is refreshing since Brooklyn has become a haven for people "finding themselves" with a stupid haircut via Wisconsin. The owner is super friendly and very well knowledged on whiskey and bourbons. Would totally recommend and go back!
Great food, decent prices Mac and cheese and chicken pot pie were as good as it gets

I currently switched jobs and the closest soup place is Hale and Hearty. The Soup Spot is hands down the best soup place I have ever been to in NYC. The soups are made fresh daily; they will fax you a list of the soups upon request. I have never had a bad soup there. The line gets pretty long, so I usually try to arrive at noon or before. They are extremely efficient and if you know what you want, you can be in and out in 2 minutes. Â I miss this place so much.

This. Place. Was. The. BOMB DIGGITY. Its usually really packed but I went wheb there werebt many people there. I got shrimp gumbo and afterwards I got the B56 sliders I think, so good! The food had so much style to it and I enjoyed myself. Can't wait to go back.

No matter how others will recommend other Tofu houses in the K-town, I have to say this: I just love this place. From the appetizers, the little yellow fish is awesome. Rice cake is Â delicious as always. Tofu pots: seafood or beef.

I really don't understand what's the hype with this place. I came here on a random weekday, like a Wednesday or Thursday night and the wait was an hour long. I was fine with the wait, wondered around St Marks and came back in an hour. There was literally no sense of customer service with the waitress quickly coming to you to get your order and never to be seen again. The ramen was slightly better than average, but not really worth the wait time or the price. The pork buns were good, but again, nothing outstanding. The whole time I felt like it was a food court rather than a restaurant due to the lack of service and at the same time it felt like they were eyeing you to leave because of everyone else waiting outside.

My husband always insists that we eat at BIG WONG for lunch when we go to Chinatown. Â The congee there is my favorite, it is the best within the tri-states. Roast pork is good but now-a-days you can find many places that serve up good roast pork. Â The place is always packed during lunch so be parpared for only elbow room or sharing tables with other patrons. I always found it quite interesting that a lot of Americans eat there and they all seemed to have been there before and are accustomed to the hustle and bustle of the wait staff and seemed to really enjoy the food. Â I also see different generations of Chinese folks who enjoy eating there. Â BIG WONG has been there for a long long time and sure it's one that would be in the history book for NYC Chinatown.

Having recently started a new job in the neighborhood, I took it upon my cuisine-crazed self to explore all of the restaurants within a 4-block radius. This is the best. One afternoon around 1PM, I walked by and couldn't help but notice the swarm of lunch-breakers lined up at the entrance. I popped in to inquire about the food and wait. Ramen and a long-ass time. "I'll come back." I told the friendly hostess. The next day I took lunch at 11:45. Arrived at noon and still had a 10 minute wait! The place is huge, but the good food keeps it packed all day. I ordered the Akamaru Modern ramen as per the countless Foursquare/Yelp fans' recommendations. Kinda Expensive. Real delicious. Treat yoself.

Just to be candid, we were ready to walk out of this SoHo place immediately after being seated. Â We waited over 30 minutes to seat a party of four. Â We were eventually seated at what consisted of two small cocktail tables pushed together. Â It was so near the restrooms that my wife had to sit perpendicular to the rest of us so people could get by. Â We were constantly being bumped as other customers had to squeeze behind us to get into and out of the bathrooms. Â When we first sat down, two booths were also empty, and we asked if we could switch. Â The hostess and waitress unceremoniously said "No!" Â Those are for big parties and we were a party of four. Â They then sat two parties of four in the booths. Â We asked if we could change with them (we were there for a family celebration) and we were in line before them. They again said "No! Â The hostess makes the final seating arrangements." The only reason that we didn't leave is that we were starving and it was getting late. Now, the reason that they I am not giving them a one star review: Â the food was very good and the waitress that served us was nice and friendly. Â We took Yelp's advice and ordered the corn. Â It was spicy and cheesy and amazing. Â We also got the fried plantains, which were not too greasy and cut fairly thick. Â The Huevos Rancheros with steak were awesome, and the corn maza boat stuffed with feta and beans was the dish of the night. Don't get me wrong. Â This place is EXTREMELY noisy and packed. Â At one point, 1980's Axel-F dance music was blaring so loud that we had to stop talking for a few minutes. Â My son felt his braces coming loose from the vibrations! Â Its like they are a wanna be Dance Club or something? However, the food is really great. Â We aren't sure if we will be going back, but the horrible seating arrangement was surpassed by the corn and maza.

Casual dining, but not a huge menu. I went for brunch and there wasn't a wide range of items. Brunch champagne drinks were thirteen dollars so I decided to skip that. My hubby got a burger that I sampled and that was really, really good. I got the goat cheese quiche and that was good too...but the place just doesn't blow my mind. It's overpriced for what it is. It was a little too busy, resulting in slower service-good food, but overall just not deserving 4 stars.

I am so impressed by the beautiful, spacious outdoor garden here...I didn't notice it on my first visit, so it was a really nice surprise when I returned! Â What I did take note of during my inaugural meal was that medium spice level = HOT. Â Unfortunately, I didn't recollect this and struggled through my meal once again. Â Nevertheless, from what I tasted of the tom yum soup through gulps of water & sips of the best thai iced tea I've ever tasted, it was fantastically flavorful and the drunken noodle dish was very good as well. Â The panang tofu curry did not strike the right chord with me; it seemed too strong and let's just say it proved difficult to digest. Â  As others have mentioned, this place is very well-maintained, esp. the bathrooms. Â Be sure to take your regular election of spice level down one notch, dine al fresco, and enjoy :) ps: seems to cater well to any group size

The ambiance here is great. I love the woodwork. The food is pretty good, rather standard fare, sandwiches, salads, etc. It's great for a quick lunch with friends. The baked goods are quite scrumptious, especially the marble brownie with cream cheese. I almost got a sugar coma from just half, but it would have been worth it. I am serious about my brownies. The crowd and staff are very nice and pretty quiet. Great coffee too.

If I could choose one word to describe this restaurant it would be lively. Balthazar has found a way to pack a large number of people (comfortably) into a small space adorned with many many bottles of bottles lining the walls. We were seated quickly by a very friendly waitstaff. Unfortunately it took a while for our waiter to return to get our drinks and even longer for him to get our orders. As a group we got the escargot appetizers, the steak frites, filet mignon, lamb shank and duck shepherds pie. The escargot was the first to arrive. And it was just beautiful, not only were the escargot large in size but they were swimming in a pool of decadent butter and herbs. Each bite was flavorful and they even took the effort to add sauce within each snail to enhance the flavor. Along with our appetizer was the bread basket, nothing too amazing I was just a little confused about the rock hard butter. It was almost impossible to scrape any out of the bowl without stabbing the small container. Unfortunately it was a while after we finished our appetizer before our entrees finally came. I am sad to say that my steak was utterly overlooked. I ordered a rare and it came out looking more closely to medium well. I didn't want to have to wait another 40 minutes to get my food so I ended up eating it anyway. It came accompanied with two sauces, an herb butter infusion and a bernaise sauce. I favored the butter, I found that the bernaise was too overpowering and took away from the taste of the steak. The fries were delicious and arrived crisp and delicious. My friend who had ordered the filet mignon had the same issue with her steak being overcooked as well. She had asked for medium but instead received her steak well done. Her dish came accompanied with a side of fried, spinach and a peppercorn sauce. I didn't care too much for the sauce I found it a bit bland in flavor. On the other hand the lamb shank was absolutely delicious, the meat literally fell off the bones and was seasoned beautifully. When the shepherds pie arrived we all had the same look thought, "that's it?" It was tiny, about 6 inches in diameter. But what it lacked in size it made up in flavor and heartiness. They didn't skimp on the duck however it wasn't heavy.

BEST. GLUTEN. FREE.PIZZA.EVER. I have eaten at tons of gluten free pizzerias and this is far the best. You cannot even tell the pizza is gf. My husband had the pesto risotto and it was on the dry side but still tasty. Highly recommended! Oh nit every kid friendly because it is a small place and no high chairs - for a heads up.

Simply the best.. And vegan.. Can't believe how good they are..I've tried countless of vegan treats and with the exception of lulas ice cream on 6th street .. Â This is the best vegan treat you can get.. And now stores like Duane reade carry them.. awesome..

Very reliable Park Slope standby that I've been to fairly regularly in the last few yrs for dinner, once for brunch. Â Simple, classic interior and friendly, attentive staff. Â Bar at entrance and a few tables, more tables further in down a few steps. Â Food doesn't usually wow me, but its consistently good and enjoyable; likewise the menu doesn't overflow with fancy descriptions and pairings, just consistently solid combinations. Â Marrow bones available in the winter are savory and a standout. Â Weekday prix fix is a very good deal. Â Otherwise, prices are moderate.

After spending new years day (I'm so behind with my reviews! Ah well, a chance to relive my awesome holiday) keeping my hungover sister company, I managed to coerce her out into the cool new air of 2014 to join me for dinner. We ended up at Marietta after surveying the other nearby local restaurants--the menu and the sweet fairy lights sealed the deal for us. We went pretty early so the place was near empty but the service was tops and at least we could eat our way through the menu without fearing judgment from other diners. There were enough awesome things on the list of appetisers that we ended up just getting the whole dang charcuterie board. The winner from the board was definitely the brown jam. (I feel weird just typing that and knowing that I'm talking about pork shoulder. It was a rillette, I think? It was delicious, I know.) I made the mistake of adding a pork shoulder appetiser to a pork shoulder main and as delicious as it was I was well and truly pork shouldered OUT. But this was my mistake, not Marietta's. (Don't make the same mistake I did. Get the fried chicken, by the sounds of it...) The drinks were also delicious, and Ginuary was kicked off well with a special from the bartender called the Black Tie Affair. It was essentially a French 75 with vermouth and I'm willing to accept that name because I felt Fancy. I felt so Fancy, I had two.

A perfect cozy cafe in the heart of the Village, this place is both romantic and casual at the same time. Â The menu is varied in options and the food is very reasonably priced. Â We visited La Lanterna for a late night snack/dinner. Â We sat in the garden, which was open, airy, romantic, and cozy. Â Our service was friendly and efficient. Â Between the two of us, we ordered the soup and the caprese salad. Â I really liked my mozarrella cheese, basil, tomato, and balsamic sauce. Â Wow. Â What an enjoyable experience! Â I will certainly visit again when I am in New York City in the future.

Very welcome addition to the neighborhood. Â We've tried a fair bit of the menu, some highlights are the brussel sprout starter, lasagna, the pizzas are very good and the Baby Jesus cake is outstanding (and I am not at all a dessert person). Â Staff is super friendly and I've heard the brunch is outstanding so we'll be trying that soon.

This place could benefit from good management. Our waiter was surly, spent time texting at the bar (it is unconscionable that a manager would permit cell phone use on the floor), and was inefficient at processing payment. (He used the "drop and run" method for our bill--any good server knows that when people are ready to pay and leave, they are ready to GO.. and thus, one should take two steps back, especially if one sees a credit card..he went to go check his text messages instead of quickly processing payment). There is a mix of friendliness and detachment that servers at a place like this should cultivate-- none of the TGI Friday "Hiii! I'm here to take care of you! Lemme sit down next to you!" but alas, no need to screw up your face in distaste, walk away with a tetchy attitude. Food was good, drinks strong. Overall a good experience.

went for the bottomless bellini brunch today- the food, service and drinks were amazing!! Can't recommend this place enough- The burger was the best I've had in NYC!! The owner Alon was attentive, charming and sent a complimentary Halvah desert that was really delicous, Making reservations for next weekend and bringing Â friends. Â Cudo's to Danielle the bartender who kept the drinks flowing!!

Open Late, which is wonderful for people in the food and entertainment industry ! really accessible experience and great meatballs, a super fun concept. I went on the recommendation of a co-worker and was totally impressed.
I was not interested in grabbing something here, but dang I'm glad we did. Our falafel was super tasty with that hot sauce of theirs. Real good.

Ordered my usual ZEN Salad and the portions of the avocado and portobello mushrooms seem to be less and less each time . Love this place but the salads aren't as good as they use to be. Presentation is a big part and the rolls still look and taste good but can't say the same for the salads.

My husband and I love this place. I've lived in Europe 3 times and it always makes me feel like I've traveled into a Parisian oasis. There are amazing high ceilings and an older 1930's look to the restaurant. All the waitresses have adorable white half aprons with scalloped edges. I absolutely love it here. One time we came for my birthday brunch and the quiche was incredible. I felt like I had never had a real quiche before I came to Balthazar. I was in love! And my husband knows I'm a total sucker for creme brulee. He surprised me when I returned from the restroom. And it was a delicious surprise. If you are looking to woo someone for brunch or dinner, this is the place. I warn you that you will want to keep coming after your first experience here.

I went to this place a year or so ago, but didn't really recognize it until now. Â The burger I had was decent, not really noteworthy though unless you consider the sad state of NYC's burger scene (edible gold goes not make a good burger). Â I like the nostalgic look of the place a lot, and if you're a burger nut , live nearby, or love old school diners I might reccomend this, but otherwise don't worry about it

Great place for class and quality! We made a reservation for 15 people four days beforehand and the private dining team was very accommodating to make sure we were all set for that evening. Christine C. assisted with logistics, answered my questions, and helped me pick out the course menu for the evening. That evening, we had customized printed menus for all the guests. For appetizers, we chose Insalata di Astice (lobster salad) and Torchon (foie gras). For entrees, we chose Tortelli (cheese ravioli), Marubini (pork shoulder ravioli), and Tagliata (prime strip loin). For desserts, we choose Budino di Limone (lemon custard) and Mille Feuille (dark chocolate cake). All the foods were presented in a spectacular way and tasted delicious. Special shout out to the Tagliata, which was prepared medium rare without us saying anything.

To be quite honest, I don't think I'll ever come back to the restaurant again. There are quite a few pros of going to this restaurant. They include: - Location is nice. Quick access from the trains (less than a 5 minute walk) - Food is served in a timely manner - The decor of this restaurant is so pretty - The price is reasonable - The pomme frites are tasty. They have maple syrup on them. So why does Gabi A. only give two stars for this seemingly charming brunch spot? - I felt SO sick after eating the food here. They put WAY too much butter when they cook. Don't get me wrong, I am a strong believer and lover of this much scorned dairy product (I cook with butter all the time...SHHH!! Don't let anybody know...) they don't use butter, they ABUSE it. Beyond Paula Deen use of butter. My croque madame was a beautiful sandwich of gruyere and ham topped with an egg. It was delicious upon first bite but that was about it. The combo of excess gruyere + untasty ham + my bread dripping in butter was just too heavy for me. The food has so much fat content here that I had stomach upset for the next 2 days. Thanks Le Barricou. - My significant other ordered the duck confit hash that almost had a medicinal taste and quality to it. I would pass on this. - The waitress was a snob-ka-bob. She had this strange accent that I think she was using on purpose and got offended when I asked her if the food was French-Canadian. ***Insert weird faux-French accent here*** "No. No. No. The food we serve here is French! It is not Canadian." Well lady, I've been to France, and I've been to Canada and I must say your portions size and flavors are more Canadian than anything.

After reading the reviews, I had too high expectations for this place. People said there was a strawberry cream cheese that came with the bread but all I got was plain bread. The burger was good but not in my top 3. It just tasted like any burger with cheese lettuce tomato. The sauce didn't do much but I liked the bread though. The French toast was good but not amazing. The crust was too hard and the center was too soft. Unless that's how a French toast is supposed to be like? My friend said the chicken sandwich was good, though I wasn't sure if she was impressed by it. I really wanted to try the jane/ Johnny Benedict but only the classic was available, which is lame and boring. The experience was good over all though. Our waiter kept refilling our water for us even though he put a glass bottle if water on our table, which was nice since I drink a lot.
Amazing. Good food. Great decor. Excellent price.

the bbq craze might not seem like much of a big thing these days, but fette sau still serves up some very taste bbq. Â i'm not a big ribs person (too messy with meat bits always stuck in your teeth), but i love their pulled pork and brisket. Â i have, however, witnessed at least two rib-offs (fastest & cleanest to the bone wins) among my friends, and they seemed to like the food well enough, judging by the meatless bone discards laid out before them (or maybe they're just really competitive?).

The falafel balls are tasty, the toppings are o..k chopped lettuce/tomatoes, the tahini sauce seemed spliced with mayo, or just kinda bland. I'm spoiled, I've eaten falafels in the middle east, Â where pitas are warmer, toppings are more varied. But it really is a deal in this neighborhood, and the island at large.
Been to this location and the one on 3rd ave and I liked this one a lot better. It is much more trendy and hipster. Loved their happy hour specials. Will def return when I am cravin for jap BBQ!

We were a group of 6 that arrived around 7pm on a Tuesday to a 30 minute wait for a table. It was rather crowded. We had the seafood pancake to start and the fried whole fish. The seafood pancake is mostly pancake and scallions, I was able to pick out the tiny bits of seafood in it- one whole small shrimp and a few pieces of Â squid or octopus tentatcle. I ordered the Soon Tofu beef/pork dumpling/nild spicy and it was exactly what I expected. And it was very good.. I wasn't able to eat my entire meal- the offering was large. There were about 3 dumplings in my soup plus the egg you drop in. I loved the experience there, but a larger person or very hungry person could .Two others from the party ordered the Bibimbop and said it was extremely good. Â I would definitely recommend this restaurant. I honestly felt like I was a tourist on vacation in Korea.
Poor service. Food is not tasting. Seafood salad with poor dressing. Strongly not recommended to dine there again.
All around mediocre food/service/everything. Very forgetful.

Yesterday, we mistakenly had the Brontasuarus Rib, the Pulled Pork, the Brisket, fries and 2 beers. Outrageous total was over $60! The beers were crisp and cold and then it was ALL down hill from there. They charged us for 2 fries and brought 3 to the table so that was annoying but then they refunded the mistake plus a bit more so that was helpful. HOWEVER: When we ordered the Brontasaurus Rib they said it was 1 pound of meat though really, like the brisket, it was 1 pound of slimy FAT. The pulled pork was tasty, though also admittedly fatty. After we picked what we could from the fat pile (I have a photo) we got very sick (we both puked once each from this meal). The rib was under-cooked and along with the slimy fat did us in. Needless to say I do not recommend eating here if you value your time, money, stomach, and intestines.
Great food, great music, great service. What else do we want in a bistro?

Right up to the top of my list - an interesting blend - espresso bar to the left beer bar to the right table and TVs out back with several tables and outdoor area with a tent and the worst view ever in NYC - nice yard of trash and other hoarded equipment to view over the fence along with the 59th street overpass. Â Real dumpy area for this place by the bridge but it's a gem - hope it holds! I may be slightly biased because they had beer tasting event outside with a real tasty whole pig being served. Â Beers were great and pork was mmmmmm yea. I'll be back to try the everyday menu but if they have this event every Saturday I'll be a regular

Second time's the charm! The first time I went was a year ago. My friends and I were about to go on a Paris trip, so it seemed appropriate. Unfortunately my bouilabaisse was blah, but the service was great and the servers gave us travel tips. Â BTW, to the funny waiter who said I'd hate London and should stay the entire trip in Paris - you were wrong. So wrong. Had another opportunity to come here for a belated birthday dinner. This time, I ordered the filet mignon (medium rare) and was impressed. The filet was cooked PERFECTLY. Warm, juicy, pink, my knife cut effortlessly through that piece of meat. It has a bacon pepper glaze that gave just the right amount of seasoning. The price for this dish was also quite reasonable, considering the ridiculously high markup NYC has on cow meat (Why is steak so exorbitantly expensive in NYC? Why??). Of course there's no sides or anything, so we ordered some truffle fries to share. Which were awesome by the way. Perfectly plump and crispy and the fragrant truffle oil was lovely. The service was great as before. The waiters are super charming. Â One of them even provided some helpful tips for my friend, who couldn't decide whether she wanted her filet medium or medium well. He (smartly) advised her to go with medium.

The shawarma is my favorite, falafel also good, the chicken kabob is basically like a chicken sharwarma. Always love the baklava. And the on-going middle eastern music is fun background filler. Great way to introduce the food to kids/adults. There is more variety than I have described here.

Popped over here after the BK Night Bazaar. I was happy to see they are open late as we were getting dinner after 10PM. I love the ingredients they use and the flavors coming out of the kitchen are delicious! I had the duck confit with arugula and my boyfriend had the lamb tagine. When we're in the area again we would go back in a heartbeat.

Yakitori Totto proves that as long as ingredients are utterly supreme, even a simple preparation like grilled skewers can get diners yearning for such things as an animal's tongue, heart or liver. Omnivore's non-dilemma. If you arrive on a weeknight a few minutes before 6 p.m., you should have no trouble getting a table.

It's street meat. Cheap, fast, greasy food that is utterly delicious and probably not the most sanitary. I had chicken and lamb over rice, and it was great. I ate a little bit of the hot sauce and wanted to cut my tongue off. Still, it was good food. The line was about 4 people deep when we stopped by for a weekday lunch, but it moved fast.

This was initially a super long essay review, now just normal long ;) Â REALLY like the food here. -Alta boasts a charming exterior, so charming in fact, we walked right by it the first time.. It looks like an entrance you'd find to a home in a lil alleyway in England--covered with lots of flowers and vines (and a private little two top), so look out for it. Â  -Once inside, a narrow bar space leads into a rustic, manor-like dining room, with a fireplace in back and a second floor that looks down onto the main room. Â We were shown to the sweetest table on the floor--right in front of the fireplace--and I was really stoked they took my request for a 'special table' seriously, as you never really know with the person taking your reservation. Â Brother's 40th and mom-meeting-new-girlfriend celebration, so definitely pleased. Â Would be nice to dine on the upper level balcony next time.. -The meal was *GREAT. Â The cocktails and wine list superb as well, with Ewa de Provence such a winner, I've been craving it badly ever since... -A quick rundown of what we ordered, and what I'll order again when I return, which I will, and soon: //Goat cheese puffs. Crisp on the outside, smooth & rich on the inside. Â Light for deep-fried cheese! Â (And four pieces!) Â The lavender honey was the proverbial cherry, and so so good, we snuck in finger dips when (we thought) no one was looking. Â Would buy this by the jar if I could. //Paella. Yes and yes. Â Plenty of shellfish atop rice in a delicious squid-ink sauce. Â ORDER IT. //Brussel sprouts. Delivered. Â I love it when the outer leaves are crisp, and the sprouts were moist and flavorful down to the center. Â (The ones at momofuku are also very good.) //Lamb meatballs. Good flavor, but just a little too gummy (I'd try them again, though, to see if it was just an over-mixed batch that time). Â The butternut squash puree went perfect with them, however, and again, four portions. //Braised octopus salad. Good, and the meat tender, but not too memorable. Â Fresh ingredients. //Truffle surprise. Could have been a miss, but it was a straight yum. Â Yes and yes. Â If you love truffles, ORDER IT. //Enormous shrimp. Got em out of curiosity. Â Never seen anything like it! Â They're the size of lobster tails. Two to a plate. Â Good, but not great. Â But pretty rad looking (they come from Madagascar, I think?). //Smoked foie gras mousse. Foie is tricky, but this was good. Â Refreshing, almost, if you can picture.. //Catalana mousse. Mmmm! Â Decadently light and flavorful. Â The standout of the three desserts. Â Would order again. Â For takeout please ;) //Chocolate souffle cake. I've had better, but there was nothing wrong with this. Â Delicate and creamy. //And the third--a special birthday plate--served in those great little spoons: Something delicious that I can't remember. Â (It's been two weeks since we dined, sorry!) Â  Portions for tapas are usually skimpy at restaurants, and the menu predictable, but these were almost generous, and the variety exciting. Â We even wondered if the four pieces that came on certain dishes were the chef's special touch, as there were four of us (and three is usually the norm). Â Can't wait to try more! Â These are some tasty bites. --------- (ps.. I'd have given this place five stars were it not for our server. Â She was the wet blanket on what could have been a stellar dining experience (though this one busser with his over-enthusiastic dish announcements sort of softened her inattentive attitude lol.) Â She did not believe us when the second glass of wine ordered was different from the first (we'd answered 'yes, same please'), and blamed us for the table being unbalanced and rickety (it was like that when we sat down). Â She barely let us finish our sentences and did not check on us during the first four rounds of food. Â By the end, she warmed up a little, but what a sour grape. Â In the interest of full disclosure, I will say that we were late. Â We called fifteen minutes prior to our reservation and let them know we were running behind, which ended up being twenty. Â Our fault, but out of our control, and I felt bad. Â I hate being late for reservations. Â She did nothing to make us feel relaxed and welcome once we arrived, however. Â We were told there was a reservation one and a half hours after us, so we did our best to eat as swiftly as possible and told her it wouldn't be a problem for us not to have dessert. Â The party after us most likely ran late as well, because we ended up ordering dessert and an extra round of cocktails, by which time she cracked a half-smile.)

History: I work right around the corner from this place and have been coming here for Wednesday lunches for a few months now. I also used to live around the other corner from this place and have been coming here since before the renovation they had some time ago. Keep in mind this is a pay-by-the-pound buffet style restaurant w/ open seating. No wait staff. This is neither a pro or a con. Just is. Great for lunch, since it's quick. Though you can certainly eat your dinner here, feel free to consider this place not a dinner destination, but somewhere to pick up loads of prepared meats to have for dinner at home. Onto the rating! Pros: They have, at various times of the day and/or week: flank steak, sirloin, top sirloin, chicken hearts, pork and chicken sausages, beef ribs, turkey wrapped in bacon and other various things one could expect from a regular Brazilian type place. You go up to the counter, and ask the man what he has. Also, he'll give you as much as you want, don't be shy to ask for more. Tip this man! Cons: The not-meat-on-a-sword bar can be hit or miss. It can also be very random. Expect raisins in the fried rice. Though I suppose this is normal. It could also require a triple-take to figure out which is breaded chicken and which is fried fish. Neither are bad, they just look the same to my carnivorous eyes. Deal Breaker? Deal Maker! This place is dirt cheap. A giant plate of food and a can of Coke is like, 10 bucks. If I were to compare and grade the meat available here to the same available options at some place in Manhattan, it's a solid B to their A. It's the price that just puts it over the top. Tip: Things get heavy! Remember, you the price you pay for 1 lb. of meat is the same that you pay for 1 lb. of rice or pasta.

Excited to have this cafe open. I've met both owners who were very accommodating and friendly. Nice to have some variety in coffee flavors and can't wait until they start having sandwiches! Very happy to support this local business
We love their Mami and veggie arepas. Lovely staff too!

Very typical American menu, the portions are substantial and my favorites would be the spinach artichoke dip and the fork and knife ribs. The decor is very modern and it looks very inviting as you enter the citigroup entrance. The best part about this place is the after hours environment. The bar is packed with the after work crowd and the live jazz band is what I'm usually there for.

Prosperity does not disappoint! Â Lunch today was $6.75 - 18 dumplings, 4 pork baos, 5 pot stickers, and a diet coke. Â My boyfriend is Chinese and says that the dumplings are a little doughy on the sides; I'm just a white girl so I thought they were delicious. Â We both agree it's a great value for solid dumplings and friendly service. Â The store is tight; go to the park on the corner of Hester and eat al fresco.

I always get excited for Dine in Brooklyn, the restaurant choices are great and it's not overrated like NYC-RW. I picked Kiwiana as I heard good things about them. It's a low-key, cutely decorated restaurant on Union St. Not surprised that it was a full house even on a weeknight. Their Dine in Brooklyn menu offered great choices, it included the famous baby back ribs and fried chicken so that's exactly what we ordered as our entrees. For appetizers, we shared the squash soup, roasted beets and mixed greens salad - all delicious with the salad being light, simple and the best. Chef Simmons added a special touch by bringing out all the entrees himself. The entrees were great and he did not skim on portion size. The skin of my fried chicken was very flavorful though I would've preferred it crispier and the food hotter. Finally, we shared a bread pudding and raspberry lamington as desserts. It's a solid 4 star restaurant, we glanced over their regular menu and everything was reasonably priced. Will likely return and recommend.
Thank god places like corner bistro still exist. A sloppy down to earth burger with a mug of beer. Because, America. And because not everything in the WV has to be shi shi.

We had made a reservation for 4 for our guests from out of town as we live in this neighborhood and thought we would try something new from our usual spots Blossom, Gascogne and Cookshop. Well, almost upon our arrival there was trouble in paradise. We had an 8:30 reservation and were told to wait til our table cleared-this took well Â over 40 minutes, and had us do a lot of jostling at the bar while we did so. Not a problem, we thought , friday evening , busy New York dinner crowd, we could deal with that. When we finally got our table, the service went from marginal to worrisome to terrible. We not only had a long wait for our appetizers but were never offered any drinks or wine until we ask for it. Then when it was about to be served, ( we had ordered a glass of white and one of rose) another waiter bumped into ours and I was drenched with half the bottle of rose. Â The offending waiter didn't apologized he merely asked in an abrupt manner " if I was ok" I replied that I was not and retreated to the restroom to clean myself off. When I came out the manager was there having now been informed of the accident but as I was still furious at having not only my clothes drenched but having a waiter give me an attitude about it, I was seeking some kind of an apology from her. Daria Conley Albert was somewhat understanding however, her lack of empathy that I could possibly be upset by the fact that I was DRIPPING with wine from my underpinning to my outer clothes, somehow evaded her Â and what she offered was to dry clean my clothes and a weak apology.
