While I can appreciate accidents do happen, what I don't appreciate is being made to feel awkward or seeing indifference from the wait staff at said accident, especially when it involves a customer. Â I sat through the remainder of our meal with damp, stained clothes and we have vowed never to return to this place. While the food was fine, the abysmal service made it a down market experience. With so many excellent eateries in Chelsea, The Red Cat is perfect example of all looks and no substance and should be skipped by anyone who wants a great culinary experience. This one should have been named the Red Herring!

BEST MEXICAN FOOD IVE EVER HAD!!! and I'm a mexican food junkie! i LOOOVE THEIR CARNITA NACHOS! this place is a mazing! and the guy at the register was very nice and friendly! I would definitely be coming here often since i work a few blocks away

A local highly recommended this place to me. While I've only been once, my dinning experience was suboptimal. The place has a cool retro feel to it and like Jason P. mentioned in his review, it definitely has an old chophouse/speakeasy feel to it. I think the all white attire of the waitstaff complete with bow-tie helped with that. I started with a caesar salad that was tasty, but not amazing. Really though, how amazing can a caesar be? It was my birthday dinner so I went all out and ordered the surf and turf for the main course, dressed with vegetables. The giant prawns were delicious as giant prawns usually are, yet I was severely let down by the filet mignon. The taste of filet mignon should blow you head back like sticking your head out of a Ferrari at 150mph. This tasted more like....well, like a minivan stuck in traffic. Functional, yet dismal at best. It was covered in peppercorns, so the taste was overwhelmed with spice rather than the delicious, tender filet. Above all was the horrible soundtrack. I'm not sure if some employee turned on their Sony Walkman through the PA, but the music did not suit the setting. Excuse me, but who wants to listen to the Beastie Boys and Social Distortion while attempting to enjoy a nice dinner. Don't get me wrong, there is a time and a place for Social D and the rapping white trio, but neither should be at Walter Foods. Try their tasty drink menu, but hold off on the surf and turf.

The whiskey cocktails are great, but the hidden gem: the pulled pork sandwich. Good heavens, that was the best pulled pork sandwich I have ever had in my entire life. Words don't do it justice. Seriously, come to Post Office and order their pulled pork sandwich: you'll understand what I mean.
Truffle burger was awesome.

Meant to write a review here since all the good reviews have already said it all. But, might as well write something now than never. Another good reviews doesn't make a difference, right? lol But, my 5 friends and I went there during lunch when we visit New York. We are from Southern California and we went to New York around late March-early April 2014. When we got there, it was a long wait time: about an hour wait, which is the only downside. The food made up for it. The place is really small, we didn't care. As long as we got our ramen in the cold New York day. The food was really really good. We all ordered ramen dish and loved it. We also order the Avo Tuna ($7) which is a torched tuna sashimi w/ avocado marinated in special yuzu garlic sauce. Very very good. it only serve 5 pieces for 6 of us. Good thing one of us does not eat fish. :P Would recommend going here. Just be prepared to wait awhile during busy hours because the place is small like any place in New York. :D

I was looking forward to this place for a long time since I saw some recommendation of it and the first time when I came here the average waiting time is 2 hours. Of course I quitted and made a reservation. However, I was disappointed tonight. Their sauces are limited and it is not convenient for you to refill. They give everyone one sauce, which is basically Â soy sauce....I mean who needs soy sauce for hotpot?? Everything you order is extremely tiny. So tiny that you need to order lots of them to get stuffed. Also the hotpot base is not authentic... We got free ice creams since we checked in here with Yelp. All in all, I will NOT recommend this place to my friends.

Best cous cous in NYC. Though I must confess that my goto with Chef Samir is the lemon chicken over rice which is perfectly priced at $7. I don't think there's a better bargain. What is also a bonus is the variety of sauces - which goes beyond the white and spicy. You can get a mint (my favorite) and another spicy variety. Also lately, they have been offering free hot moroccan mint tea which hit the spot during this cold spell.

Went here for lunch with my wife and we were blown away with the quality of food and the taste of the burgers. Â They were amazing, needed many napkins and the Truffle fries were AMAZING! Will definitely come back here when craving a burger.

FIRST OFF: RESERVATION get one. It's worth it. If I could give Employees Only 6 stars, I would. We ate here for our 14th anniversary. It was busy and noisy in the bar area. That means that there are good drinks. The wait staff was exceptional, attentive and on top of things even though it was crazy busy. I had the La Mikana and the Fraise Sauvage for drinks. The La Mikana was my favorite. It was grapefruit cordial, gin and champagne garnished with rosemary. SECONDLY: It's busy and noisy because it has amazing food! We had the Marrow Poppers and the Charcuterie. The chicken liver patÃ© was the best I have ever eaten, velvety, smooth and creamy without the gritty dirty taste some chicken liver patÃ©s can have. My husband got the Porterhouse Pork Chop with Black-Eyed Peas & Savoy Cabbage. The pork was tender and the chop was almost 2" thick. The side was black eyed peas that were also savory and the best companion to the pork. I had the Â Elk Loin Wild Rice, Winter Squash, & Parsnip. It was excellent! It came with elk marrow, which I could only eat a few small fork fulls since the portion of food was generous. The waiter suggested the cheesecake for desert. We are not really cheesecake people, but we figured we'd try it. It was smooth and creamy. Not the pasty cheescake with graham cracker crust that is everywhere. Our meal and experience was above and beyond. Those are the only words to describe.

This took awhile, but finally got in! It was our lucky day and my gf and I walked in to an hour wait for the bar. Not bad since it's very difficult to get reservations here... but somehow within 2 mins the hostess came over and said they had a table for us since a table decided to leave. LUCKY us!!!! I'm a huge fan of the restaurant, everything was white, cute decor and lighting. We had the mushroom/oregano/egg pizza which was my top two favorites tonight. The oregano worked well with the pizza. We also ordered the roast suckling pig for an entree which is also my top two. Can't decide which I enjoyed more. The waiter recommended a pasta dish which I forgot what it was, but it had blue cheese in it. Good, but didn't stand out. Fries were also delicious here. For dessert we had the butterscotch pudding, loved that it wasn't too sweet. Can't go wrong with Jean George's restaurants especially this one.

The food was tasty but the service by one waitress was the worst and I will never patron this establishment again. They start their business at 5:00PM. My party was the first group of customers of the night at 5:30. The waitress bumped my shoulder with the plates and left without a second glance, did not ask if we were done with our meal before she brought the check, and flipped open the bill booklet to see if there was anything inside at my table instead of taking it back to the cash register. She yelled at us for eating macarons purchased at a nearby bakery when she could have simply asked us to put them away. Beware: there is a mandatory drink purchase required per person. After I ordered the food, I asked for water and was informed that I had to buy a drink. I paid $3.99 for a non-refillable cup of oolong tea. I can't believe I did that! Never again! Their serving sizes are microscopic. The photos in the menu make the food appear Â a lot bigger. I had the tuna and avocado carpaccio to start and it had 5 small pieces. I also had the salmon roe donabe-gohan. Once again, the photo made the serving look much bigger than the actual size.
Get the spaghetti and savor every bite. You will not be disappointed. Also must mention the bread basket is phenom.

Stopped in for lunch today (Tuesday) - it was pretty empty, but that's expected mid-week. Â The wait staff was very friendly and not overly attentive, even though there were few other patrons to be busy with. Â It was just two of us, so we ordered the beet and ricotta salad and the chicken salad with tarragon to split between the two of us. Â Both dishes were fantastic - the beets weren't too tangy from the vinaigrette, the ricotta was fluffy and light, and the sandwich was perfect. Â The chicken salad had specks of orange zest that, combined with the tarragon, made for a very fresh and not-heavy-at-all sandwich. Â Great ambiance in the place, too. I'll definitely be back to try out the dinner menu sometime soon!

Came here on a Wednesday night around 6pm and in order to have a table you needed to make a reservation. Really? Rude hostess' at the door went inside anyway and the place was empty. Sat at the bar and tried a few items. All which were super delicious. Had the Mac and cheese and sliders. Bartender was super cool and the chefs are cooking right in front of you. Would I go again? Doubt it. Overrated.

Such a great Brooklyn Diner experience, my sweet potato pancakes with strawberries and root beer float were glorious... I love the service here, while waiting in line we were even offered slices of orange, ginger biscuits and water. AND I saw the Suzanne Vega lyrics and autograph on the wall, is it really THE Tom's Diner?

What could I possibly add to the 200 other gushing reviews? Just this. Â If we want to continue to insist that this country is advanced and humane while we still have the death penalty, then every man on death row should be given La Sirene's filet mignon with foie gras as part of his last meal. Â That is what a proper society would do.

Tiny, cramped, and very claustrophobic. A friend suggested coming here, so my mother and I gave it a shot. The waitresses pull the tables out for whoever sits at the window booth. It would have been a really enjoyable experience if the staff handled the table next to us a little better. The group had a party of four, but only two people were there, so the waitress sat those two people at the table next to us. Then the wife of one of the men came and they shoved their table over so it was right on ours. The guy sitting next to me was on my lap. If I moved even the slightest, I'd elbow him. He was loud, nosy, and when my dish came, he almost stuck his nose into my plate--I'm not even kidding. The woman at the table was sitting at/outside the door, but it was better than making her climb to the booth and having her sit on top of my mother. Both men kept trying to talk to us which I found to be really annoying, and you could tell that I was no longer happy sitting in there because the girls on our other side kept giving me worried looks and my mother kept asking me what was wrong. What should have been a peaceful lunch where my mom and I could spend the time chatting was spent with me trying not to tell the guy next to me to move the f@ck over before I punched him. I usually don't care about loud and annoying people (much), but it was so cramped and they were eavesdropping on our conversation that I felt uncomfortable. To top it off, the waitress never even apologized or offered to move the trio to the bar. Everyone there just assumed things were okay and that everyone was comfortable on top of each other and went on with their day. So service? Meh, nice, but I was not happy about that. Now for the food: Breadsticks are like large, chewy puffs of clouds with a hint of cheese. They're gluten free to boot. I loved dunking bits and pieces into my risotto and then eating it that way. I ordered the spinach, goat cheese, and roasted red pepper risotto. It was a bit on the looser, watery side, but was still good and filling. I wish there was more spinach and peppers, though. The amount you get in the risotto is hardly worth the price (17 dollars and change). Would I rush back here to get risotto again? No, not really. I prefer the risotto I make over theirs, and while the breadsticks were yummy and unique, they weren't like some other breadsticks I've been addicted to. Maybe my experience with the customers next to us colored my perception of this place, but I wasn't really willing to come back here anytime soon to try it again. The same friend who told me to try Risotteria told me to get the pizzette next time if we ever go again, so maybe I will to see if it's worth it.

Okay, so the restaurant is cramped and crowded. Â I like to see it more as cute and cosy, but if you don't like being in small cramped restaurants you might have an issue. Â However, the food here is probably the best italian food I've ever had (don't tell my mom). Â I had the tagliolini ai frutti di mare and it was delicious, and the price is ridiculously cheap. Â The service was great as well; the manager was very nice and friendly to us while we were waiting and our waitress was nice as well. Â  We also got our food very quickly which is always a plus. Â If you love italian food, you have to try Bianca.

Oh hey, its a ssam bar but you can't really get the good ssam unless you preorder with a bunch of people. Â Great. Â It's like an IHOP that doesn't sell pancakes. And yes, I know they have a fish ssam but everyone knows fish is basically a vegetable. I've been to several of David Chang's establishments and I have to say I was sorely disappointed by this one. Â  What we ate: -- kimchi was good, unique -- I would never have thought to put apples into it. Â  -- rice cake with pork sauce was good, delicious. Â but its a pretty basic and simple korean dish that's really difficult to do poorly. -- pork belly bun was good but really nothing all that special. Â when you're cooking with all that pork fat, it is damn hard to screw it up. Â a restaurant (with a reputation like momofuku's) really should do a little more than serve up a slab of pork fat and call it a day. Â it's a little lazy to be honest. -- seafood stew was terrible, awful, very bad, gross. Â i had a flavor i couldn't really put my finger on and i don't really care to try to. The only reason I think this restaurant has four stars is because most other non-Japanese/Thai Asian restaurants in Manhatten are pretty terrible.

Great tapas spot with really warm and atmospheric dining and bar areas. Â All the plates we had were spot-on, especially the octopus and brussel sprouts. Â Our waiter took time to answer all questions thoroughly and the wine list was very much up to the task of pairing with very different kinds of dishes. Â Terrific earthy and pleasantly tannic Rioja went well with everything.

This was probably the best ramen I've ever tasted. The food was great. Â However, 3-stars due to our over 1 hour wait on a weekday night when the hostess told us 30-45 minutes. The ramen is good, but don't know if I'd wait over 1 hour for it again. The hostess with the long brown wavy hair was also extremely rude after we checked on the status of our table after 30 mins had passed. She gave us a huge attitude which was very unprofessional.
Heavenly! Delicious, SPICY (we got 'hot') fried chicken with a touch of sweet, tangy greens, and the tasty little cornbread wedge. YES.

We can't resist shopping here on our last day of our visits to NYC. Always start with a meal. Â I enjoyed the ravioli and got the recipe from the waiter. Then we shop for the most wonderful and usually hard to find items and leave with a ribeye poboy for the flight home. Perfect ending.

Now open on Sunday! Oh boy! You should go here for brunch with your out-of-town buddies for some classic Brooklyn. However, if your friends are expecting a Sex and the City type brunch, tell them that Carrie's house is on Perry Street and point them toward the subway while you chow down at Tom's and make some new friends. I went on a blustery Sunday and they were so nice to serve us hot coffee, strawberries and cream, orange slices, and bread with honey while we waited outside. Service was a definite win. Like many others, I agree, the food is definitely decent and consistent though not otherwordly. BUT it has some of the most reasonable prices of any establishment in this town. Also, its not trying to be too cool or too hip. Its got a million signs telling you about their abundant specials and cherry lime drinks. It has kitsch all over the place. But not TGIFriday's kitsch, but dollar store christmas garland and fall leave garland kitsch. Awesome.

Wow, this place has absolutely the BEST perfumes I have ever smelled. Â Forget Sephora, come here if you need to pick up something for your sig other. Â The perfumed candles I can tell are also big sellers here, as they seem to be constantly replenished by beautiful French workers buzzing around the store (Take that Yankee Candle!). The line doesn't deter me however, because the quality of the packaging they use just can't be beat. Â I know of no other outfit that takes boxing their wares into such an art form. What I don't understand is why they offer these little soft cookies with flavored cream inside them. Â It doesn't look like they are well stocked of them, because when I'm here there the trays are hardly ever full. Â How do they expect to sell any of them when they are almost $3 a pop? Â When I bite into one, I just don't see the appeal and I chase it down with a hefty dose of fun dip in order to cover up the taste. Please note that the above paragraph was written on opposite day. Â Read accordingly.

Admittedly, the first time I walked into Sanford's, I was expecting average diner food. It turns out the food was excellent and very reasonably priced. Â I have been there 4 times this month. Overall, the portions are very large...one dish is almost enough for 2 people to share! Â The 3 mushroom risotto and 3 mushroom ravior were full of flavor and cooked perfectly, The shrimp and calamari risotto was also very good with a healthy portion of fresh jumbo shrimp and calamari. Farfalle Genovese was also very tasty, again cooked perfectly with good flavor. Â The servers were very friendly and attentive but not too intrusive. The only downside is that lighting is very dim and the menu is printed in very small print making it hard to read. Â Other than that, Sanford's is truly one the few good restaurants in Astoria that I can trust for good food.

Came here for lunch with a friend and the place was packed; the wait was not long though. Â While we were waiting I was concerned about the seating... they had one longgg cushioned seat against the wall with many tables but there didn't seem like a lot of space between the tables. Â I was thinking how am I going to sit inside without putting my butt on the other customer's table?! Â Then the waitress walked us to our table and dragged the table out, my friend slipped in and she pulled the table back and then I was like ohhh. Â It felt a bit like communal seating only there were gaps between the tables. Â  We ordered the old fashioned pizza with sausage and prosciutto. Â I would not recommend this unless you're one for salty stuff. Â The prosciutto was really salty. Â Anyway, Adrienne's were not cheap with their toppings and filled our pizza nicely. Â I really liked that their sausage were sausage crumbles instead of the regular sliced sausage. Â Sadly, I was not able to taste much of it... maybe it was the seasoning or maybe the prosciutto took over. Â However, the pizza was crispy/ crunchy and I LOVE that. Â I also tried it with sausage and mushrooms and it was much better. Â Nice thin crust pizza.

Okay, you know how your friend has that one friend and she is kind of super awesome and great and has never done anything bad to you ever but you kinda don't like her at all but you can't tell anyone? Â If that person turned into a restaurant, for me, it would be Public. Â  I think the brunch here is great. Â I think dinner here is great too! Â The atmosphere is good and I've never had bad service. Â But for some reason, Public leaves me cold and unenthusiastic. Â Though, to be fair, we'll undoubtedly be hanging together soon.

I wanted to like this place. Â After all getting Italy all in one place how can you beat that. Well...oh where do I start.. Firstly, the concept is great but who designed this place seriously. It is confusing, seemingly unorganized and looks liked it was just slapped together last minute. Â As a designer, it is a bad start when you need a map to figure out how things are. While the overall idea is great. I love the wine, coffee, fresh meats and seafood selection, pasta all showcasing the Italian culinary tour de force. The overly priced food and small portions but hey they have to pay the rent right? The restaurants and tables to grab a class of wine, cheese etc with friends is fun if you can snag a seat. It is like trying to find a lawn space for the Bryant Film festival. The quality of the food is first rate and so is the pricing. I think I was paying Euro prices...but hasn't the Euro dropped against the dollar?!? It is clearly meant for the trust fund kids, yuppies who can afford to live around the area and the bankers across the park. Would I come back...sure. It is a great idea and maybe once the dust settles after the opening honeymoon period.

Came here with two friends. Wait is about an hour depending on when you come. This place was on my dumpling roadmap so while we waited we walked over to try Nice Green Bo. Between the two, I would have to pick Joe's Shanghai. When you first enter Joe's, they greet you and give you a ticket. They call out ticket numbers whenever a table is available. Really busy on a weekend morning/afternoon. I ordered the pork soup buns and the crab soup buns. I like the texture of the dumpling wrap. It's not as thick as Nice Green Bo. But the soup buns are pretty salty. I probably chugged a glass of water for every 4 buns I ate. If I have to choose between the pork or crab soup buns, I would pick the pork one all the time. P.S. BE CAREFUL TO NOT BURN YOURSELF BY STUFFING THE WHOLE THING IN YOUR MOUTH! Definitely be coming back again.

Best ever...omg. We went for New Year's Eve so they had a 3 course prix fixe menu... So good. Â The foie GRAS was really melt in your mouth delicios; it had onion and raisins which complemented it nicely. Â Also had potato salad with truffles and caviar; it was the best potato salad of my life and normally I'm not a potato salad girl. Â For my baby's appetizer he had gnocchi with mushrooms, I think the gnocci was rice rather than potato and it was on point. Next was the main course. Â Yum! Â I had veal with prosciutto and brussel sprouts....3 of my favorite things. Â Also there were fried battered sweetbreads on my plate with a spicy aoli sauce. Â I was scared to try the sweetbreads but they just tasted like fried anything. Â The veal was perfect. Â So tender. Â Best. Â My baby had snapper which was pretty good too but nothing to rave about. Dessert was my favorite part maybe, because it was the best thing I ate the entire year. Â Nougat which tasted like cheesecake with chocolate nougat on the bottom, chesnuts, and pomegranate sorbet. Â Didn't try my baby's desert because it had oranges ew. Atmosphere is nice, service wad good, I want to go back every day for the rest of my life.

Weirdly, I like the sides a lot better than the meatballs but I order the same things every time I'm in here: 1. Naked pork meatballs with spicy pork meat sauce and mozzarella on top 2. Polenta- best polenta I've EVER had 3. Broccoli 4. Cream soda It's small so it fills up fast and can be a very long wait at dinner time and on the weekends so plan accordingly.

Good, not great. Ordered a medium chicken katsu with extra curry and a sliced boiled egg - apparently extra curry means the to-go box is DROWNING in curry. Which is okay by me, because curry + rice is only good when there's enough curry to soak every grain of rice. The chicken cutlet is nice and large, even sliced, and it's juicy and tender, too. No complaints! 3 stars because it was good, and if I worked in the area, I'd probably go there a lot for lunch, but it's nothing to get worked up over.
food was typical japanese, good sashimi
Close to the park, we grabbed a couple of traditional bahn mi sandwiches. Â They are tasty and cheap and quick. Â You can't go wrong!

The most horrendous peruvian food I have ever tried, It used yo be ok, but now, its quality decreased, its horrible, it greasy, i got a ceviche and the fish was still frozen on my plate, then I order a creamy rocoto tiradito and the cream was diluted with water, the pisco sour didn't have lemon and was all wattery...simply disgusting, horrible service, they make you wait for ever and they are dirty, the tamale my mom order was spoiled and rotten. The piononos are always old and the alfajores are not alfajores anymore, they filled it with some tipe of lousy unflavored chocola mouse, that's not an alfajor... sorry guys, thats not the way the peruvian food taste.

Had my birthday dinner here and it was the best service I had ever received. If you want to have a nice, peaceful, calm dinner atmosphere with delicious drinks and food, this is where you need to go. Our server was delightful, and very polite. The food was so delicious, I kept eating til I could not eat anymore. Plus our awesome server gave us a yummy dessert to take home & enjoy on the house!

Mooncake is hit or miss, depending on what you order. I'm always cautious with Asian Fusion places, and rightfully so. Sometimes fusion tastes like what people THINK should be in a certain item to make it seem cool and trendy, rather than what combination actually makes the food delicious. Vietnamese Summer Rolls: skip. They were super tiny and not at all tasty. Miso Glazed Salmon: Most yelpers recommended this and I'll agree here - this was a good choice. The salmon is cooked right and very flavorful (yet healthy tasting... take that as you will). Grilled Pork Chops: good, but a step below the Salmon (I'm normally a huge pork chop fan!) While I don't adore Mooncake Foods, they do have a decent amount of good dishes. I'd swing by if I was close, but I would not go out of my way.

I have given this place multiple tries and hopped around the menu. It is not very good. Everything is grossly over salted and/or over spicy. The truffle fries were ok the first time i got them, absolutely horrible the second. Sometimes the sauces are appetizing, and other times they look/smell/taste funky as hell. And delivery literally around the corner has taken an hour or more on a couple occasions. One star for effort because i love the idea of a specialty chicken finger joint, and one star for the super nice delivery kid who always apologizes profusely for how long it takes.

Oh, boo. We were so disappointed by our visit to Cha-An. Yes, the sesame creme brulee is very good, but if you've ever had black sesame in any sort of dessert, you'll know it isn't THEIR version that's special - it's just this particular ingredient. So many of the other items of interest on the menu were "sold out" (I put this in quotes because the stickers look like they'd been sold out since 1999), so there were few remaining items that really called to us. Correction: there were some lovely sounding items, had it been the middle of summer, but serving strawberries in February doesn't really appeal. The Matcha latte was super chalky and a little bitter, so I believe the water was too hot when it was prepared, and our server mistook our question about one item and brought us three. We explained we'd only ordered two, and he offered to take it back. Â We demurred, feeling bad, and to his discredit, he left it on the bill. Â The right thing to do in that situation would have been to leave the dish but not charge us for it. Â The tea also took FOREVER for him to bring, and he never offered more water for my white tea. Â The service doesn't factor heavily on my review, but it did put a damper on our evening overall. Overall, i expected better. The quality of their green tea roll cake could have been found for $2 or less at any standard Japanese bakery, the creme brulee was nice, and our remaining special dessert (a warm red bean soup) just didn't inspire. We will not return.

Really, really disappointing. I've lived in the neighborhood for years and have always wanted to come here. I brought the husband and my friend from out of town. I ordered a chicken dish, yawn. Had little to no seasoning, not delicious at all. My husband ordered a steak and the cut of meat was complete garbage. Knowing that they butcher their own meats and own a butcher shop themselves, he thought this would be a great bet, not so. Tough, gristly, really disappointing. My girlfriend's pasta dish was drowned in rosemary, I could tell she hated it. I think the thing that was so awful was that in this economy, we go out to eat so rarely these days. To spend $100 on this meal was really heartbreaking.

We walked into Tink's on a warm Wednesday evening, right after a non-eventful workday. My girlfriend had been there for brunch before and recommended the place. We walked in and the place was pretty empty for the start of dinner service. We were greeted by this inked up chick who was very nice and accommodating, I think her name was Roxy.. She sat us down and shortly after brought us a complimentary tomato soup on a big ass spoon topped with a crouton, it was quite nice. We ordered a bottle of wine and took forever to figure out what we wanted, simply because the menu was extensive and everything looked great. We finally decided on four small plates and chilled with our wine until our food came. We ordered some kind of tater tots dish that was topped with duck gravy and it was fucking insane! We couldn't keep our hands off that shit! We also shared the grilled cheese which was also phenomenal; it was served with a kilimanjaro of fries. Next came the nachos, they were just okay, but for some reason we couldn't stop eating them. Lastly came the gnocchi dish, which looked like it was 50 shades of grey, not the prettiest dish, but it was the tastiest gnocchi we've ever had. It was a nuclear bomb of garlic goodness. We enjoyed every thing we ordered and were completely satisfied. We were so focused on our meal that we didn't even notice how packed the place got till after we were done. Our waitress did a great job and provided us with excellent service even when the place got crazy busy. Big shout to Roxy and the restaurant itself for having some bomb ass food. Go to Tink's!

This is one of my favorite restaurants in NYC. Â The menu was not unusual, but the food is some of the best for the price. Â Service was also excellent. The night we were there, the kitchen had accidentally screwed up our main course (brought the wrong ones). Â The server apologized and brought us an extra app (we already order apps) while we were waiting for the main course to be prepared. Â It was nice. Â On top of that, they also brought us dessert on the house. The food is excellent here and I would eat here again when I'm in NYC.

My husband & I visit this restaurant for the first time back in August Â in surge of authentic Cuban food well we found it. we travel all the way from the height "manhattan" to queens and let me say it's worth the trip. Â We ordered ropa vieja, filete de cerdo, arroz moro, yucca and desert delicious flan and mini churros what a feast. We went back in September for my hubby's birthday and second time around was even better. the staff do make you feel at home. One of the staff members I don't recall his name but he's the best there he puts on a wonderful Â mini party for the birthday customer, wares a hat w/lights,cheers you on and dance floor moves. Â We had an enjoyable dinner Â and a every nice time at Rincon Criollo. Come November and December our family celebrates more birthdays which means back to Queens. Â Love this Restaurant.

Came here for oysters and clams after a stroll through the New Amsterdam Market. Oysters and clams were fresh. Service was polite but very slow. Atmosphere is lots and lots of football on different screens (so take that for what it is). We were pleasantly surprised to see that the oysters were each $1 instead of $2 and the clams were on special for $9 / dozen (around 2 pm on a Sunday). We probably would've ordered more if we hadn't gotten the check already. Solid option for raw seafood in the seaport area.

I've heard many things about this legendary halal cart, and had intentions of going the last time I visited NYC. Â However, sadly that did not happen. Â I did not want to make the same mistake twice, so I came here with some great friends on my last night in NYC. Â  Food (9.0/10) = Chicken, Lamb, and Rice for $6.00...OOOOOOOHHHHHHH YEAAAAAAAAAAA! ("Macho Man" Randy Savage). I was fortunate that the line was not long when I came here. Â But after tasting the deliciousness of this "street meat," I would line up for this stuff even if the line started at the end of the block. Â Man... I don't even know how to describe the food. Â The chicken and lamb were seasoned well and surprisingly not dry. Â They add plenty of cheese too. Â Meat and cheese baby...oh yea! Â I added the white sauce and the red sauce. Â I don't remember what they were, but it made the food so much better. Â Note: I wasn't drunk. Ambiance (?/10) = it's a food cart. Â I witnessed a turf battle between two homeless men though, haha. Â The dominant beggar spent most of his time near the food, asking for the change people received after they paid. Â Lurking in the back of the line that night was another man collecting change. Â It was entertaining to see the dominant beggar go after the lurker, and how some of the regulars in line encouraged him to protect his income, haha. Service (7.5/10) = Service was fast. Â These guys really know how to keep the line moving. Overall Opinion = I don't know why you just read my review. Â This is the 1758th review, and they've average 4.5 Yelp stars. Â What more do you need to know to convince you to visit this epic joint on 53rd and 6th? Â  Â Go get your chicken and rice, and maybe a free show - "The 53rd and 6th Halal Cart beggar vs. the Lurker."

My husband and I live around the corner from Little Dokebi, and watched its gradual transformation from the former Turkish restaurant that occupied that spot to this cozy-looking bar, serving up Korean street food specialties. For some crazy reason, we waited this long to visit, but WOW will we be going back!! We came with a friend, and each ordered a different meal. My husband's pork kimchi fried rice was delicious, my tacos (I got greedy and ordered three types: beef, pork, and white fish) were fantastic, and my friend seemed very happy with her bibimbap. Â We also ordered the steamed pork gyoza to start, and a seaweed salad. I know this is strange to say, but their seaweed salad might have been the star of dinner (at least for me). I could eat that stuff by the bucket, as well as the white seaweed salad banchan our waitress described as "Korean coleslaw." Utterly refreshing, creamy perfection. And on a warm Saturday night, we easily got a great corner table right by the window - service was great, our waitress was wonderful. So, yes. Go here. You won't regret it.

This place is cool. Its small and tight but plays the best old school 80s movies. The tacos are very good and at 3.00 a pop you can taste an array off of their menu.. but wait!!!!!!!!! let me tell you about that GUAC..... man slap yo momma because the stuff is so dayum tasty! the only thing I can say that I don't like that they do, is make it seem like the Guac comes with the meal. But it's only $7 and so worth it (as well as that hot sauce. Please don't get me started on those flavors! ha). OKAY and I personally like a flavored margaritas, However these classics are very good. I like mine with salt, please and thank you. Just wish the place was a tad bit bigger. I mean the bathroom has more space than the seats and tables. But other than that its a nice place to go and eat before or after the bar.

I highly recommend splitting the taste of Maine with someone -- go big or go home. Â You get 1/2 lobster roll, 1/2 shrimp roll, 1/2 crab roll, 1 bag of chips, 1 soda & 2 crab claws + a pickle. There's a ton of butter on the toasted bread and in all the seafood too -- so don't get this on a day you're on a "diet." You really can't go wrong ordering here - everything is delicious! They have all these specialty drinks -- the ginger soda was delicious and had quite the kick.

Had to have some pizza while in the Big Apple so tonight's dinner was dedicated to Lombardi's. There was less than a 5 minute wait for our party of 3 tonight...and that was at prime dinner eating time. We were led through the innards of Lombardi's and I was surprised at actually how big it is. We decided on a large with homemade meatballs, sausage and mushrooms ($23) as well as an appetizer of bruschetta ($9). The bruschetta was okay, 4 big squares with fresh tomatoes on top. The pie overall was okay. The best topping out of the 3 we ordered was definitely the homemade meatballs which was soft and tender and didn't taste artificial like those Costco frozen ones. They use fresh mozzarella and there's a thin cover of sauce on the pie. The dough is super thin but I found it tasted rather salty. As the pie gets cold, it gets harder to cut and is pretty chewy. It's a popular place, don't get me wrong. Lots of old school pictures on the walls add a definite local feel. I'm glad I got my pizza in NYC...now on to having a hot dog.

I love milk & honey, this it's definitely my go to place.The food is fresh and tasty. they have great coffee and tea. it's in a good location and they have Â Free Wi-Fi but the only downside is cash only. N I'm also obsessed with their peanut butter cookies.

Worst place ever. The manager is an incompetent pompous individual who treats customers like dirt. I have never had a more infuriating experience at a restaurant in my life. I can't wait for flat top to go out of business. That manager brings Shame to the whole neighborhood. If I could I would rate it 0

For what it is, I think Paprika definitely deserves five stars. Â It's head and shoulders above similar restaurants in the neighborhood. Â It has a very nice ambiance, service is well-informed and friendly without being overly familiar and the food is really good. Â In fact, really really good. Â On top of all this, it is incredibly well priced, particularly for food of this quality. Â There is nothing to fault, so five stars it is!

Outstanding food. Â Went in during happy hour. Â Tried one of the special beers. Â Amber was a great waitress, Â very attentive! We had the spinach avocado dip to start followed by the burger with the aioli and truffle fries were outstanding! Beer selection was very extensive and menu had beer pairing with all the dishes. Â Again, Â truffle fries...

I had been looking forward to this dinner for over a month as I planned a visit to NYC. Perhaps I set my expectations too high leading me to be feel underwhelmed with my meal and service. I will say, the maitre d' was extremely kind and I enjoyed speaking with the sommelier who came over to discuss the wine list. However, our server was quite mediocre and the timing between plates was incredibly slow (not the server's fault per se). As for the food, I am the ultimate pasta lover, carbonara being one of my favorites, but at Maialino, I couldn't even finish half of my plate. Â The guanciale overpowered the pasta with smokiness, making it taste like a one note dish. I definitely think my homemade carbonara (from Cook's Illustrated) blows the Maialino version out of the water. I also ordered the chittarra pasta, described as Spicy Tomato, Braised Pork Skin, Pecorino & Oregano, but to me this tasted like spaghetti doused in a four dollar bottle of arrabiata sauce. My friend's Bucatini all'Amatriciana was the best dish of pasta on the table, but again, was nothing to write home about. My favorite part of the meal had to be the generous portion of crisp, succulent brussels spouts, we enjoyed as a side. I absolutely love Danny Meyer's restaurants but I don't think I'll return to Maialino.
Top shelf. Save this one for a special occasion.

This was my first time eating Filipino food. I came here for lunch and ordered the sausage (longisi??) $12 lunch special. It included: -2 sausages (tasted like the Chinese garlic sausage) -a small cucumber & onion salad -some sour soup that I loved -rice -a fried egg that was half soggy and half cooked Overall the meal was filling and delicious. My friend got the chicken which was very tender and flavorful. We also shared a halo halo $10 which had: -purple ice cream (reviewers say taro, but I have no clue what flavor it was) -condensed milk -pudding (or was it flan?) -shaved ice -jelly on the bottom The dessert was delicious. Except the ice chunks were a bit hard I was also looking forward to ordering the "jeepney" drink bc a friend has recommended it. But I was very disappointed to hear for whatever reason they stopped serving it along with many other drinks on the menu. Overall the server was nice and it was quiet in the restaurant on a weekday afternoon. I might return to try other dishes since I rarely eat Filipino food. They also had a outdoor space but it was too hot that day to eat outside.

Don't get me wrong, Hagi is still a great place. But lately I began to notice that the food doesn't taste as good as it used to. More like, the food is a lot more bland than what I've had before. I am already aware of the fact that most Japanese dishes tend to be bland. But hear me out, I've been to Hagi before. I've tasted their dishes before. And I'm telling you that last Saturday's meal I've had was even more bland that what I was used to. I've gotten over the fact that they serve small portions because they were still tasty as hell. But now that there is less taste and still small portions, BAH! -1 star!

I had just returned home after an 8 hour flight overseas. Â I was meeting up with my girlfriends for food, fun and the usual girl talk. Â From the outside the placed looked okay. Â Once inside we were escorted to the back table that is perched higher than the other tables. Â I guess it's a pseudo VIP area without being VIP. Â It just seemed odd. Â The pseudo VIP area is near the patio. Â I spent most of the night rubbing my hands together because of the draft from the patio doors. Â Can someone insulate that please! Â  Our waitress was decent but then there was the guy serving water and then the other guy putting the napkins down. Â Please! Â It's not that deep for all the production, you are not a 5-star restaurant. Â  I had two margaritas and felt as though I was drinking Mike's Hard Lemonade. For dinner I had the fried chicken with the red velvet waffle. Â Now I just got back from Brussels Â and I will gladly gift the chef my airline miles so he can see how waffles should be made and taste!!!. Â The chicken was decent. Â The desert menu left a lot to be desired and the lack of variety of drinks left things at a stand still for the moment. Â And keep the drink titles simple! All these fancy names for overpriced drinks add more to silliness and pretentiousness. Â  Because my girlfriends and I don't see each other often, when we get together we enjoy our dining experience. Â Well as we were enjoying our experience, one of the managers came to our table. Â We thought he was introducing himself to us and maybe offering us comp drinks since we did spend a sizeable amount that night. Â Or simply say hello. Â No instead he recommends that we sit at the bar. Â Translation. GET UP!! Â We were all floored!! Â It wasn't crowded, there wasn't any parties waiting to be seated, we are very mindful of that when going out. What he should have done was recommend a drink or try to sway us on the desert, don't just tell us to get up!! Â What made things worse was that there was no room at the bar. Â With that we went home. Â I was just in Europe dining with a group of friends where we sat for a long time without being disturbed. Â I'm not saying our intention was sit at the table all night, but it was unnecessary for the manager to tell us to move when it wasn't that crowded. Â  Basically his attitude reflected that he didn't care if we came back or not... So I won't. Â  It's so sad when wanna be pseudo restaurants spoil an experience.

Love the ambiance. Feels like old French cafe. The bar is classic, mirrors, tons of booze. The tables are narrow. The back room is large with more tables and some benches around the stove. Good service. They were very kind to bring me vinegar, lemon, honey and hot water for my sore throat. Our party ordered the apple gruyere omelette, spinach mushroom omelette, Benedict, and spinach goat cheese croissant. All were excellent. The fruit bowl side was also very nice. Crispy potatoes were perfect and the side salad fresh (ps. I really like East coast bunch serves a small salad with the entree; makes the meal so balanced and I feel healthier for it). Oh yeah, coffee so excellent I could drink it black. I would return for more delicious things on the menu. PÃ¢tÃ© sandwich, I'll get you next time.

I wanna be a billionaire so freaking bad, Buy all of the meals I never had, I wanna be on the cover of Food & Wine magazine, Smiling next to Oprah and the Queen Oh every time I close my eyes, I see my name in shining lights yeah, A different Michael White restaurant every night, all right, I swear, the world better prepare, For when I'm a billionaire. If I was a billionaire, I would eat here 8 nights a week. Â Michael White is a pasta magician: Convivio (when it closed, a part of my heart closed), Marea, and Ai Fiori. Â Service was so impeccable that they brought us a box of Kleenex on a silver tray because we had tears in our eyes. Â I went with the following 4 course $89 prix fixe (along with a bottle of Sancerre Le Mont - you can't go wrong with Sancerre): - Vellutata: the personification of fine dining - pieces of lobster bathed in a velvety bisque. It was good, but I had to restrain myself from ordering the Animelle (sweetbreads) to pace myself. Â  - Trofie Nero: words cannot describe how amazing this dish is. Â Squid ink pasta seems cliche and overdone, but this dish is a religious experience. Â This was the best pasta dish I have ever had (and will ever have). Â The pasta is home made, the minced scallops are as fresh as can be, mouth watering acid is present somewhere (subtle hint of vinegar or lemon) , and the spicy breadcrumbs give the dish a crunchy complex texture. Â You will mourn when the plate is empty. Â  Â  - Agnello: this dish makes me want to buy a sous vide machine. Â Imagine lamb chops wrapped in a flat rich sausage. Â This was a mind blowing follow up to the trofie nero. - Dessert: how could I be expected to remember what I had for dessert after those two mind erasing courses!?

Came here prior to heading over to an event and it was good but not super great. Got the last available table outside and personally I think that is the only way to do happy hour/dinner/lunch/brunch in the city when it's nice out so that was great. Ordered the Lobster PLT with sweet potato fries as that's what everyone raved about. There were a lot of chunks of lobster so that was good but I have to say the lobster salad itself was not that flavorful. The Pork Belly portion of the sandwich was perfectly done and I was impressed they were using Amy's bread for the sandwich though I think it was toasted just a hair too hard for my own personal preferences as I cut the roof of my mouth. Overall I think it's about 3.5 stars but I wasn't wowed by anything.

My friend lives in the neighborhood and you can only imagine my excitment when she mentioned that a restaurant devoted solely to meatballs was opening! Â So, we decided to try it out on a Saturday, not long after it opened. The restaurant was busy, and we had places to go so we opted for take-out. Â The woman taking our order was less than friendly, but she appeared capable. Â There were 6 of us ordering - so I understand the logistical nightmare - but we figured that with worksheets and all, she should be able to get it right. Well, when it came time to pick up the food, shenanigans ensued. Â The staff couldn't seem to figure out what we ordered and it was unclear what exactly they were trying to give us. Â To the restaurant's credit, they handled the situation quite well. Â After going looking through a few of the take-out containers, they returned most of our bill and sent us packing with nearly everything we had ordered. Â Kudos. The food was quite good - with one exception that I will touch on later. Â As a connoisseur of delicious meats, I have to say that the spicy pork meatball with the spicy meat sauce was incredible. Â The beef meatball with classic tomato sauce was good, but failed to reach the same epic status as the spicy pork. Â Now, that exception I mentioned earlier was the salmon meatball. Â I'm not sure how they make these salmon meatballs, but I would advise avoiding them at all costs. While the service wasn't great, I have to imagine it was partly due to the fact that the restaurant just opened. Â The food was good enough, for the most part, that I would definitely give this place another try. Â Not for take-out though.

Food is really good cute small place only for 2 people is perfect. Â The dessert crepes were great not too sweet but just enough sweetness for great dessert. The escargot was savory and makes ya want more. Definitely a place to go barck to for more. can't wait to try this place for dinner

Great food. Service is a little slow but the quality of the food makes up for it. I love all the food from the salad, pasta, to the dessert. This is a must-go restaurant in NYC! Also perfect for a date night! Do note that they only take cash and don't do reservation.

I don't like to go out on holidays as service is rushed and food is mediocre.Mother's Day. 2014 was different. we had no reservations but the hostess went out of her way to find a table of four.The servers were quick and pleasant. All our drinks,appetizers and mains arrived promptly.Food was delicious and that legendary green sauce keeps getting better. Thank you for a wonderful evening!!

This grimaldi is overrated. Â It was so not worth the 1 and half hours wait. Â Compared to the manhattan one, this grimaldi is cheap about their toppings and they do not taste as good. Â It was super dry with too little cheese. Â I saw more crust than I did of cheese. Â It was the worse experience ever. Â I was hungry and I expected more than just horrible pizza. Â  I can't wait to try Juliana that is opening next to them. Â The Grimaldi family is back in the pizza business!

Love this place. Great service, great food, great atmosphere. Had capresse salad, fried calamari for appetizers; ravioli, pizza and gluten free pasta for dinner and gelato and banana bread pudding with gelato for dessert. My teenagers are loving it. That says a lot. Did I mention service is amazing? It is.

The reviews were right, there's definitely going to be a wait to cram you somewhere in the room, but once you're in it feels like you're part of a big family that is ready for some breakfast. Came here with some friends on a Sunday for brunch and we all ordered egg dishes which were humongous. Was there anything crazy special about the eggs? Not really, but you could tell that it was made right there and that it was fresh. Would definitely come back!

Had a late lunch on Sunday, 8/30 and probably would've given 3 or 4 stars: food was good for the price, service friendly and attentive and a patio was a plus. However, I was double charged - called 17th st location first, was told to call 20th st. Spoke to several people, everyone was very friendly; they took down my contact info, receipt number, etc etc. and ...nothing. I've been told that the records already been transferred somewhere. I don't understand why it is so difficult to find a record of a transaction that occured day before! At this point I would like to reverse the tip as well - I've alread spent couple of hours for a $30-something overcharge - contacting PETITE ABEILLE, my credit card co, looking for receipts... I'm a business owner myself and it would probably take me about 5-10 minutes to pull any record, recent or old.

My crew stopped by Casablanca when we saw that it had opened. Â We used to frequent the Moroccan place by the Bay Ridge Ave stop until it closed. Â I forgot how much I missed tagines and Casablanca makes them delicious. Â The service was also great, they were very attentive and friendly.

Best Indian I've ever had. Â And, service was amazing. Â We came early with our four year old who was nearing the end of her rope, and the wait staff was wonderfully attentive and friendly. Â The food is fresh and subtle in texture and flavor. Â Can not recommend this place enough!

Who needs to impress your Valentine with fancy French / New American food on Valentine's Day when you can take her to a Scottish Gastropub that serves FRULI strawberry beer?!?! Talk about surprising your Valentine! LOL!!! Here's how the surprise went down: Beer: + Fruli. They are getting an extra star rating from me for the sole fact that they carry the best beer to person-kind IMO and that's Fruli, strawberry beer. ORDER IT. Cocktails: + Sweet Ginger Brown. Goslings Dark Rum,Muddled Lime, Ginger and Brown Sugar. $12. This is their signature drink and I suggest you order it - it's absolutely fantastic. The ginger with muddles lime combo and rum is exquisite. DO IT. - Iona Abbey. Espolon Reposado,Lime, St. Germain, Cucumber. $12. This cocktail was meh - I wouldn't order it again. The lime got lost with the elderflower liquer (St. Germain) along with the cucumber that was just kinda there. This drink sounded really cool though not executed well :(. Food: - & + Fresh blue crab on Toast - Crabandprawn meat, fresh chili, garlic andmascarpone aioli. $12. It was very good - however it was a little to mayo-ey for me and I love mayo. I dip my French fries in mayo and mayo makes almost everything better though in this case it kind of gave this overly creamy consistency that really didn't augment the fresh blue crab and in fact, you lost a bit of the crabbyness which was sad. Still fairly good though... + Meat Plate - Pear and lemon chutney, haggis bread. $16. This was good - it was meat on a board, with chutneys and bread that complemented it quite well. It was simple, yummy and delicious. Easy. + Scottish salmon - cauliflower and fennel puree, roasted cauliflower, rocket. $25. We asked for it rare and they did it rare. The fennel puree was damn good and the roasted cauliflower was crispy yet firm and succulent. Nice job on the dish guys - the salmon was a hearty portion and seasoned quite well. Service: - Now, here's why they get 3 Yelps. They rushed us completely and wouldn't let us order as we went along. WE HAD to order the entrees at the same time as the appetizers (I HATE THIS and they clearly didn't want you there for more than an hour) in addition to the fact that tables that were coming in kept getting shuffled around and/or they wouldn't accommodate a table for 2 asking for a different table even though it was empty (still for 2) perhaps not against the wall or against the window or vice versa. We were in and out in 1 hour and 10 minutes...I am NOT a fan of this. I like to take my time and hang out...And because of the huge rush that you forced upon us, I will probably not be coming back. Too bad because I like your place and your food is good... THIS has been a review by Gaurav

DEAD ANIMALS ABOUND. There, I summed up what you'll remember about Freemans. Did your girlfriend vote for Obama? Does that cutie you asked out from the next cubicle never seem to wear leather around the office? DO NOT CHANCE IT. If you do, you might be paying for brunch with a side of pissy diatribe and no way you're getting lucky after that.

Minetta Tavern is a cozy restaurant with lots of character and great, flavorful food. My party of four tried to call in for reservations last Saturday for the same Saturday evening. The hostess replied that they only had a 11pm reservation left. She advised us to call back at 4:30pm for any cancellations - luckily, we were able to snag a table at 7pm! The interior of the restaurant is very charming - I felt like I was transported to a different decade entirely. There is dim lighting with lots of warm colored furniture and loud caricatures on the walls. I split the tavern steak ($26) with one friend, and the other two tried the za za pasta ($19) and the famous black label burger ($26). Cooked to a nice medium rare, the tavern steak was very, very flavorful. It was delicious. My only gripe was that it was quite hard to cut through, even with a steak knife. I kept pushing the fries that came with it off the plate by accident. I sampled the za za pasta, which was also tasty, but I far preferred the steak. Our waitress was excellent - she was the epitome of friendly, knowledgeable, and accommodating. There wasn't an iota of pretentiousness about her. When my friend noted that her drink tasted a little too strong, she quickly took it back to the bar to add more of the nonalcoholic soda. It was the best service I've received at a restaurant in awhile. I was very impressed with Minetta's charm and its food. It's a great place for a date night or dinner with a small party of friends - I wouldn't recommend it for large parties, as it's pretty small. I was very pleased with my dining experience here.

I'm not sure why I have never yelped this place. I guess because I frequent it so often. But sitting in the open window with the breeze in my hair has inspired me. My favorite local gem for sure. My go-to place to take visitors. Very authentic. Much more than Caracas in this neighborhood. Not to mention it is a full sitdown restaurant with a beautiful ambience and open windows. I start with the ensalada tropical, and usually have the Guayanes arepa filled with Guayanes cheese, Â kabocha squash and avocado. If you haven't stopped by, you're missing out. I hope they never leave

Buttermilk Channel often has long waits but I will say that it's one of those places that's totally worth it. Â Your best bet is to go early-- right when they open for brunch or right when they start their dinner service. Â  I've been here a bunch of times & nothing is ever bad. Â Some highlights are the pecan pie french toast (rich & decadent but SO GOOD) & the fried chicken & cheddar waffle. Â Their homemade breakfast sausage is both sweet & spicy & incredibly delicious. Â For dinner I've gotten a great fried pork chop with the cheddar waffle. Â But my favorite meal was their duck meatloaf with a Huckleberry sauce & a big golden onion ring on top. Â Good lord. Â It wasn't just my favorite meal at Buttermilk Channel, but one of the best I've had in the city!! Â And I'm not even THAT big a duck fan. Â  Definitely give this place a shot-- just go early or else prepare to wait a while. Â (The pay-off is worth it though!)

went to minetta tavern for brunch (with a reservation of course, otherwise it'd be hopeless), and got the latkes and the black label burger. Â the latkes was pretty good, but the black label burger was truly amazing. Â we were a bit skeptical at first when the waiter refused to add cheese, but when the burger arrived.. oh. wow. Â it was thick, tender, juicy, and simply phenomenal! Â  also got a latte during brunch, and that was pretty yummy with perfect foam-espresso ratio. Â next time, will have to come back to try the steak and bone marrow! ps - the service was there too~
The food is usually good. It seems like this place has become too popular for its own good -- the waiters seem to feel that they are doing you a favor.

I loved it. Went there for a corporate dinner and was impressed. The atmosphere is cozy and trendy, laid-back, but on a classy side. The staff was attentive and knowledgeable without being too reserved or too chatty. Big plus. What I remember the most is the kangaroo meat appetizer. I'm pretty conservative in my food tastes, but this was so flavorful and unique and I'd probably try it again. The other dish I tried (raviolli) was good too, but Â I wish the portion was just a tad big bigger. The selection of wine was huge and the dinner made a great impression. A definite recommend.

This place is really off the charts. I've been several times since the chef and menu changed and it's been such a vast improvement! The fish entrees are cooked to perfection and the sauce and veggie parings rock the house. The yogurt sauce with curry is to die for. The spiced hush puppies have the best blend of seasonings that I've tried in a long time and the roasted Brussels sprouts are the kind of dish I wish I was capable of making at home. Run, don't walk!

Horrible service. We were going to a show and it took 30 plus min for our food to come. My fish tasted exactly like fish.. Ick I think it was frozen. And my aunt found loads of egg shells in her pasta ;( Anyway the manager came and said 'how is everything?' I assume he thought it was great... When we said we were late for our show he argued with us and said we had at least 20 min! Imagine the luxury of of running to the theater, like actually running! Anyway rather than acknowledge our unhappiness he walked away checking his phone.... Totally disrespectful, the waiter said they were short staffed and I understand that. I felt bad for him but there is no excuse for the manager.

I expected a lot more from this restaurant. Â My wife and I are foodies and went here because of DDD and the other reviews. Â Unfortunately, it did not live up to our expectations. The wait staff and environment were very friendly, the meal was moderately priced, but the meal was just OK. The pretzel was quite good, but the cheese sauce was just OK. The Caesar salad was good, but the caviar hush puppies were not great (not worth the calories). The fried chicken was cooked perfectly, nice and moist with a good crust, but no flavor. Â The sauce that comes with it is quite good and I enjoyed the biscuit. Â However, the Amish Country fried chicken is way better. The shrimp/andouille sausage/grits entree was good, not great. The shrimp were medium size and not a lot of sausage. Â The flavor was good. We took a bag of the peanut bacon brittle to go - mostly just peanuts, not much brittle or bacon. Â I thought it was OK, my wife did not care for it. Overall, it was a pleasant experience, a unique menu, but just OK in the execution.

I same here for dinner with my girlfriend on a Thursday night. Since I am not usually in the city, I rely heavily on reviews to find a good place to eat and this place sounded great. We shared the "Picada" to start and was satisfied with the choice nothing spectacular. She had the Arroz con Pollo and I chose the Lechon Confitado. Â Both entree's were AMAZING! Â I never really thought I could say that about Arroz con Pollo but it was. I dont even know how to describe the Lechon dish, the flavoring was at the same time familiar and yet it was fresh and new. The only reason I can not give 5 stars is because I think giving any restaurant that favorable a review on 3 dishes is unrealistic so I will have to go back and try some more. The staff was super friendly and attentive. Â The only downsides: its a bit small but if you have a reservation and are not going with a large group, I guess that does not matter, and the menu was limited. Â But again worth another trip next time I have dinner plans in the city!

What can I say about Champs? it's a divey little diner with loud "musak" and vegan junk food. I think that sums it up perfectly actually. It doesn't look like much, but if you give the (very reasonably priced) food a chance, you might be pleasantly surprised. The Tuno Melt is a personal favorite, although I have yet to be informed of the ingredients. Â Again though, this is junk food - lots of fried tofu, seitan, and carbs-galore. They do have like maybe one or two raw salads and some macro plate that you can get with tempeh, but it's quite limited. On a nice sunny day, it's a great place to have a snack and people watch whilst admiring their tattoos. Â The service while incredibly sweet is also aloof, often forgetting anything from your order to utensils. On a side note, one that wasn't obvious enough for aloof me, is that they are CASH ONLY! Â Surprisingly for 2014 where everything is now swiped at the table with a tiny hand held device.

I've walked by this area so many times have never seen Bodhi Tree. Two nights ago, a group of us decided to give it a shot. I loved the atmosphere--dark with lots of candles and thai decorations. The menu was very extensive and the waiters were alright. The food was authentic, but I personally like the twist Cafetasia and Spice put on their dishes so it wasn't the best for me. I started off with the avocado roll, which was absolutely perfect. It tasted fresh and healthy, just how I like it. My friend got the duck roll and liked it so much he ordered a second. Others got the fried calamari, which was nothing spectacular. The grilled chicken skewers with sauce were good though. Â For an entree I got the tofu pad thai which was good except that it was way too salty. Also, there was baby corn, squash, and broccoli in them which really confused me. One of my friends got the fish and pumpkin soup. The fish was completely burnt on the bottom so she sent it back for another one. It got out fast but the dish wasn't very good. The drunk en noodles were very much like Spice's. Thai iced tea was spectacular, much better than Cafetasia's. Overall the food was good but a little over priced I'd say. You can get the same stuff much, much cheaper at Spice and Cafetasia.

The best sandwiches you can get hands down and course the price is right. Â You can't go wrong and one sandwich is enough to fill your belly if you are really can put them away, heck order 2 so you have a back up. Â It is tasty and a really quick meal on the go. Â No thrills but I can assure you that you will not be disappointed in the taste, flavor and value. The standard sandwich has sweet, sour, crunchy, freshness and just plain fantastic. Â I really haven't tried anything else but from just experiencing the sandwiches, you really can't go wrong. Â Great to grab a copule for your friends for poker night, a game on the tube. Â The sandwiches just are perfect for yourself or for a group. Â Simple yet it just hits the spot!
I still have dreams about the grilled kale salad....

Forgot to post this review back in August...Not wanting to wait a long time (one time, I stopped by on a weekday at 2:30pm, thinking there should be no wait, for one, but boy, was I wrong), we decided to go 11:15am on a Sunday and guess what, the strategy worked. Â By the time we finished, the wait was 2 hours!!! Â Ok, ramen was good but not 2-hour-wait good!! Â Glad we went though - pork buns were good. Â More spicy than those at Momofuku Ssam Bar and instead of cucumbers, the pork buns here had lettuce :-( Â  Buns were nice and pillowy-soft so made up for the lettuce. Â Had the Akamaru Modern (hey, Ippudo, fix the price of your ramen on your website - says $14 for the Modern but your menu on Sunday said $15!) which was pretty good. Â Broth was rich and flavorful. Â Hubby had to order extra noodles 'cause the ones that came with the order wasn't enough. Â Shared the mille crepe cake for dessert - tasted like it was in the frig with other stuff. Â I didn't give Ippudo 5 stars because of the mille crepe cake and the noise - really, why must you announce every single bowl of ramen coming out of the kitchen! Â Actually, I don't know what you are yelling. Â For all I know, you could be saying "we are 2-hour-wait good, y'all"!!

I have to admit I love this place. The location is hidden. Hard to find the place if you are visiting for the first time. The price is not very reasonable. But still, this is my favorite place. This place used to be a private house, so when you go there, you feel like you are visiting friend's house.

BEST 6 BUCKS I'VE EVER SPENT!!! I initially feared that the Halal Guys would be overrated but I was proven wrong--IT WAS AMAZING. The meat combination plate we ordered had bold flavors and various textures from the meat rice lettuce and cheese, which were made even better with excellent red and white sauces. Some say it's greasy but it really wasn't in my opinion. The portions were a plenty and enough for you to save for another meal... so win win! Be sure to go to the correct stand. There's 3 Halal stands in that same corner but only 2 of them were the real Halal Guys. It's pretty much the ones with the longest lines. Don't worry about the line--it moves really quick! Oh yeah--cash only! Really wish we had this in CA.

I usually like to reserve the 5 stars for places that cost me too much $, but are worth every penny. Â Who knew that a freekin' sandwich could be so good? I've eaten Vietnamese sandwiches in at least 6 other places in NYC, these are SO MUCH BETTER than any other I've had, it's like their made on another planet. Â I mean it's impossible to even write this right now. Â I'm getting juicy just thinking about that sandwich. Â Gotta go!

It's a bright cute little cafe on the corner. It was a great place for brunch. I had the open face steak sandwich. I was expecting something a lot less fancy, but the dish was still really delicious. The steak was cooked really well and it went well with the fried egg on top. Yum!
#1 food in bushwick!!! i eat here almost everyday and have no complaints! top picks: -crab cakes -special soups -escobar -special salads -devil eggs

I love that they use chicken broth instead of pork! I ordered the Totto Extra Spicy Ramen with char siu chicken and a seasoned boiled egg. The chili oil comes on the side, which is perfect for those who can't handle super spicy foods so you can decide how much or how little to add. Personally I added all of the chili oil at once and it actually wasn't too spicy at all. I can't say the ramen here is better than that other popular ramen spot that everyone goes to in East Village... but it's pretty close! We came here on a rainy Friday night at around 10 pm and waited only about 30 minutes to be seated which wasn't too bad, considering there were many of us waiting. They get the food out quick so customers are also in and out of the restaurant really quickly! Although the ramen was really good, my favorite part of my dining experience was actually watching the chefs! The seating is bar style so you can watch them have fun as they cook and prepare your food. Not only are they friendly and comical towards customers, they are with each other too and you can tell they really love what they do! Ultimately a great experience and a perfect end to our rainy Friday night.

Came here on a Saturday night around 6pm, we were seated quickly and there was only two couples in the restaurant. I started with the Arugula Salad, Pears, Walnuts, Goat Cheese and Balsamic Vinegar it was AMAZING! The ingredients and flavors were married perfectly together and the goat cheese was so creamy & rich. Perfection! For my entree I ordered the Risotto with Roasted Butternut Squash and Sage. It was creamy and tasty. I would've liked more butternut squash in the dish but it was still delicious!
Really cool eat in LES with delicious southern-style seafood. The sauce is delicious and overwhelming. I actually think the crab is a lot better than the crawfish. The sides are all good too.

To be honest, sometimes I'm skeptical about price-fix menus. Yes, the food comes at a slight smaller portion. But that's to be expected. In past experiences, sometimes even the quality/flavor lacks that luster that you would find in their regular dishes. Not here. No way, no how. Bengal Tiger Indian Food packs quite a punch when it comes to their cuisine. Located on the 2nd floor, Bengal Tiger is a cozy, bright little space. There's not much seating to go around so if you plan on coming for a bite... arrive before that dinner rush. They have beautiful artwork/phrases from wall to wall with those classic warm as well as jewel tones... very inviting. I was meeting my friend after work and we got there JUST in time. We managed to snag the last spot since a portion of the restaurant was conquered by a meetup group. Although a tight space, we sat comfortably. Vegetarians, have no fear. You have options here! (Rhyme not intended.) My friend had plenty of meatless options which was great. For the price of $16.95, you get an appetizer, entree and dessert. Not bad IMO. App/Veggie Samosa: Phenomenal. The outside is crispy and the inside was generously seasoned filled with potato and peas. And it was on top of a green & red sauce that had quite the kick. Let's just say I asked for a personal pitcher of water. Entree/Chicken TIkka Masala: Had to go with the classic choice, of course Indian spicy. (Go big or go home!) The chicken was extremely tender and there was just the right amount of sauce to meat ratio. The layers and depth of earthiness and savory flavors were on par. Dessert/Kheer: I'm a rice pudding lover. Add cashews? Spices? Home run. All in all, I highly recommend Bengal Tiger. There's unlimited basmati rice and their Naan is superb. The prices won't burn a hole in your wallet and they don't sacrifice on the spice. Staff was incredibly friendly and my water glass was never empty. This is a fantastic little spot to satisfy all your Indian Food cravings.
Cash-only tasty Thai in very loud, unimpressive open dining room. All dishes inexpensive and delicious; cheap, good wine too.
The food is pretty overpriced. Â It is a casual restaurant but prices reflect more of an upscale place. Â It would be a nice place to grab a casual quick meal if it weren't so pricey.

This place was yummy and fun! Plus amazing service! We had gazpacho which was more cucumber and mango than tomato... Which we loved. The papas rellenas had THE BEST dipping sauce. Some delicious plantains... And the Vaca Frita which amazed us! We had a mojito and a caipirinha. Her mojito was gone pretty quickly... My caipirinha was too strong so they remixed for me! Then dark chocolate. Cake dessert! Go here!

the good: ambience, service, price, roast pork with rice and black beans. the not-so-good, overhyped: I expected Cuban food at a place called Cafe Habana, but most of the menu is Mexican dishes. Elotes (grilled corn) I have tried elotes in Mexico City several times, and these are not that great. The seasoning is good but they fail at the star - good succulent corn. I felt like all I ate was a thick layer of mayo and cheese on top a charred young corn. I would come back and give it one more try, but this is the last time I take the 'best thing I ate on a stick' recommendation of a TV chef seriously ( yea, Tyler, I'm talking about you)
I don't know what's this guys secret but he shouldn't change a thing. I get about ten plates every time i go to NYC and bring it back to Chicago for the family. Simple, cheap, tasty.

Ordered the tuna burger and got food poisoning. Was in the NYU ER very shortly after eating their food. I called to warn the tuna was bad and was assured my dinner charges would be reversed. Â I was also told the GM or owner would call me. THEY DID NEITHER OF THE ABOVE. Don't patron such a poorly run establishment.
Fantasic delivery service and excellent salads. Â My favorite arugula salad is from Penelope.
Pretty good lunch food near the Intrepid Museum

Came here after dinner to grab a midnight snack with a few friends! We weren't too hungry, so we ordered the "regular fries" which was still a pretty good size to share for about $4.50. We were about to pick two sauces when the guy behind the counter said that if you buy 2 sauces, you get 1 free. The sauces are about $1 a piece, but sooo worth it! We decided on the black peppercorn, mango chutney and roasted garlic. I really liked the black peppercorn sauce which basically tasted like grounded black peppers with mayo or something, a little spicy kick to it and still very flavorful. I could totally imagine this sauce as a spread on a sandwich. All of us really liked this sauce, so I would definitely recommend it! As for the mango chutney, this was my second favorite. It was a little sweet, but not too sweet, so it tasted very good with the hot fries. I can't explain the flavor, but I would recommend this sauce if you are a mango person. As for the roasted garlic, I didn't try it since I'm not a big garlic fan, but from what I heard, it wasn't that great. So I would try my luck with something else. Once you get your fries and dipping sauces, this place has a few tables and counter tops where you can chill and enjoy the fries. They even how these cute little french fry holders in the tables (which are little circle cut outs in the tables/counter tops). I thought that was very creative idea! I would recommend coming to this place to grab a snack, since they offer a large variety of sauces will probably satisfy anyone's taste buds! The fries here are also very fresh and served right off the frying pan! Yummy :)

Came here on a Sunday afternoon as part of what turned into a Brooklyn/Queens bar crawl and thoroughly enjoyed myself. Cheap beer, good eats, tons of outdoor seating, not crowded at all. The bathrooms are slightly odd since you feel like you're inside a metal trash can, but other than that, fabulous place. And kudos on the eco-friendly practices, big fan.

If service is king, this place is royalty. Â We were just looking for a quick bite and the menu posted outside looked great. Â We walked in and asked about the soup of the day and the person behind the host stand told us that they don't do soup for brunch but he could arrange it for us. Â Great! Â I am getting over a cold and just wanted some soup. Â The same person came by our table as we were looking at the menu and offered more good advice and was extremely helpful and friendly. Â When our waiter came by, we mentioned the soup and he said he'd have to ask but we pointed to the person who seated us and he said 'Oh, that's the owner! Â If he says it's ok, then it's ok!' Â My husband got the veggie burger. Â Both were great. Â The soup (potato leek) was creamy and tasty. Â The veggie burger was so good that my husband informed me about how much he was enjoying it after every bite. Â We also got fries. Â Man... These fries are great. Â  Â Perfect. Â I'll probably dream about them tonight. Â The owner came by to make sure we were enjoying our food and was sure to tell us to come back. Â In case I didn't convey how great the service was, just go and see for yourself. Â What you'll also find is a creative menu, tasty food and a comfy atmosphere.

Degustation shares the same building and address as Jewel Bako (Jack Lamb being the owner of both restaurants).
