Â Degustation's cuisine can be considered expensive, fancy tapas (which seems a bit ironic considering tapas are traditionally cheap eats). Â That being said, the menu consists of several a la carte items and a chef's 5 course tasting menu ($50) and chef's 10 course tasting menu for $75. I really enjoyed the setup of the restaurant, which is basically an open kitchen with a 16 seat bar surrounding the kitchen. Â It's very compact and expect to feel a bit squished with your neighbors (and probably hear their conversation). Â The cool thing is that you're also within 3 feet of the chefs who are making the dishes you will be eating. We went with the 10 course tasting menu (which is basically like a tapas omakase). Â Because I went here in November last year, I can't quite recall all the ingredients or subtle nuances of every dish. Â Some dishes I do recall were: uni gelee served in a martini glass (interesting presentation, the uni and gelee wasn't overly fishy/briney, and the stick of veggie -jicama I think- helped break up the mushy texture), a very bland fried eggplant with fresh mozzarella and basil was disappointing (I wished it had some salt, and I am not one to prefer overly salty foods), egg dish with bacon presented in a hollowed out eggshell atop a mound of salt (very cool presentation but I accidentally broke the eggshell - oops), and lastly, the dessert of caramelized torija. Â The caramelized torija was the only thing I can remember with more detail. Â It has a harder, caramelized outside (learned that it is a torched bread), with a soft warm center. Â The only thing I could compare it to would be bread pudding. Â In that respect, it would be like the best bread pudding I've ever had. I felt full but not completely satisfied. Â Yes, for $75, 10 courses is a great deal, but the journey from the first to the last dish had too many highs and lows. Â It just wasn't consistently good or delicious; quite unmemorable. Â In fact, the only thing I would readily order again would have been the torjia. Â Actually scratch that. Â If I'm presented with a 10 course menu from them again, I would like 5 of those courses to be the torjia. Our server was nice and the ambiance was intimate yet also exciting since you could see the kitchen creations and interact with the chefs. I also noticed that a lot of other reviews that were posted around Nov '10 were in the 2-3 star range. Â Maybe it wasn't a good month for them? Â Anyway, it was a nice experience, but not a great dinner.

If you asked me what the best Diner in Queens is, from those I've tried, I would definitely say the Jackson Hole! But, to review it as an overall restaurant, it gets a 3. Â My favorite things there are the waffles, the biali's, their burgers, vanilla egg creams and their omelets are good most days. You really can't go wrong, it's not glamorous food, but the waitstaff are amazing, attentive and fast and it's just a fun atmosphere because you are somewhat transported a bit back into a more happy go lucky time. If we are looking for breakfast in Queens, this is where we go because we can always depend on a great waffle!

Stopped in for a quick gelato as I winded down my day. Â Went with pistachio. Â Sweet, very tasty with whole pistachios in it. Â Server was friendly. Can't wait to go back for lunch or for another gelato. Â They all look appetizing.
About five years ago, I tried falafel here for the first time and ever since, it's been a standard that is hard to beat.

Had their Miso Totto Ramen. Apparently it's the best thing they serve according to a friend who frequents there. The wait was about 30 minutes since I came alone. For others who came as a pair++, the wait was longer. Once you enter, you proceed to put your name on the sign up sheet and they will call you out as the customers trickle out. I had the privilege of sitting at the counter and had the fun of watching the chefs doing their magic making the wonderful ramens. The music playing was upbeat and Â it was clean. The ramen was excellent. The pork broth was savory and not excessively oily, the noodles were thin and cooked to perfection, the buta slices was juicy with just the right amount of fat. I remember just smiling after eating the half boiled egg as I haven't eaten a half boiled egg in so long or a ramen to this standard. I usually don't go for miso ramen, but I'm glad I did here--it's no where near the diluted miso soup flavor. The servers were really nice, all smiled, and they never rushed anyone despite the crowd outside. The waitress even prepared the spoon and napkin for me during the wait time even though I was planning on doing it myself once the bowl of goodness arrived. So glad to have finally visited this landmark :) Thanks Totto for bringing back happy memories and for being up to standards!

Pretty decent Flip food. I always love the calamansi juice (key lime lemonade). Â Chicken adobo - classic goodness. Better prices here than Bayan cafe, but I still think Bayan's food tastes slightly better.

Our food was great, especially the breakfast quesadilla with its well-cooked eggs. My sister-in-law can't eat gluten and there were actually quite a number of options for her, which thrilled her. For example: two types of gluten-free cookies, gluten-free muffins, and gluten-free toast (which looked like real bread, not just crackers). The staff was amazing friendly. I can't believe people could be so happy working on a Sunday morning.

Went here for a Pre-show dinner with a friend. Very crowded, but we were seated within 5 minutes from walking in. services was OK, nothing special. I had the lasagna which was very large serving (i didnt finish). Pricing was as expected for being in the city. I would come here again.

the food was a 5, the service was a 1... so I guess that averages out to a 3? whatever, i was never good at math. the pizza was delicious and trust me... it wasn't just good because I was starving. Â After my 3rd slice, I kept going for more and even when I couldn't eat anymore... I just wanted to keep going. Our server was a complete douche, not helpful in any way and everytime he came by, I swear he just wanted to kill himself. We weren't needy and shit, even if we were.. he should be wanting to help us since it's in his job description. Luckily for him, I too work in a restaurant and can't bring myself to ever leave no tip, but damn... I really wanted to because he looked like he did not give a flying fuck about us.

this is a nice place, it is very small and dining areas are tight. Â We were 8 minutes late for our reservation and the waitress/ manager gave us a hard time about it. Â Asked us if we wanted to sit outside at 6pm on a hot sticky New York evening, the answer was no. Â Made us wait 15 minutes and then brought us to a table on the 3rd floor, where many table were open. Â Food was decent, nothing over the top the waitress was pleasant and service levels were average. Â You can do much worse in the theater district that is for sure

The fried chicken here? Alright but definitely not even close to the tastiest I've had. Biscuits are great- super tall and fluffy and buttery. Hush puppies are crisp on the outside and surprisingly light. I thought my chicken biscuit was pretty good, larger than others that I've had, but would've liked something extra in the sandwich to balance out the hot sauce--it seemed rather one-note. The fried brussels sprouts & squash salad was really good! I'd recommend that if you want some veggies with your meal. The space is super tight. I had a table that was pretty much next to the table on my left and with just enough space on the right to squeeze into the banquette. Service is surprisingly bad considering this is a rather hip, mid-range priced place, where our water wasn't refilled even once. The table next to us had to ask for more water and the waiter gave them more but didn't bother noticing that the other tables around had run out as well. So, bottom line: chicken unexceptional, service couldn't care less, go if you're craving biscuits but don't go out of your way for this place.

I stumbled upon this place while I was in the neighborhood with my friend. I got the shrimp teriyaki balls ($6/6pcs), it was different from the ones that I had. Instead of bonito flakes, it had corn flakes on top and it had teriyaki sauce instead of okonomiyaki sauce that usually comes with it. I've had alot better at other places but it's worth a try.

Char No. 4 is my go to place for whiskey. The food is well prepared, properly seasoned, and comes to the table hot. Â Burgers are juicy and flavorful, in particular. Â The staff are pleasant and knowledgable about their products. There are 2 real stand-outs here, though. 1. Key Lime Pie. Â Seriously. Â It is slap-your-grandma fantastic. 2. the bar staff. The bartenders are all extremely well educated with the entire selection of whiskeys Char offers. Â They are exceptionally congenial and eager to help, taking the time to listen and talk about what they are serving. The bar offers a booklet of some few hundred whiskeys they offer from Scotch to bourbon and rye, to blended whiskeys, and small batch and artisan bottles. But truly, the best way is simply to tell one of the bartenders what you are in the mood for...smoky, sweet, sharp, peaty, simple, complex, long or short finish. Â They will bring a couple options and offer their opinions, then let you decide. Â  To their credit, even when this place gets packed, the bar staff always take the time to be attentive and relaxed with their customers. Char No. 4 is, beyond a doubt, a true gem for whiskey lovers.

Really cute place with friendly staff and great service. But I thought the food was terribly bland. Had the mushroom pizza and artichoke pizza, plate of sausages and something else I can't even remember. The pizzas weren't very good at all. Sausage pretty good. Had a great time but I wouldn't return.

So, I'm going to go out on a limb here and say.... "meh...." Don't know if it was the hype that got my expectations up and Ippudo just didn't seem to deliver or what but I'm just going to have to go with "It was okay." I think there are plenty of hyped up restaurants that are well deserved of the hype, but Ippudo isn't it...at least not for me. We got to Ippudo at around 11:50 on a Sunday morning and there was only about a 15 min wait. By the time we got out at 1:30 however, there was a crowd of people and we overheard the wait was up to an hour by then. I've had friends tell me that they've waited over 2 hours for Ippudo before, and that baffles me. My disclaimer though, is that I find myself drawn more to Sapporo style miso ramen or Tokyo style shoyu ramen with the curly yellow noodles over Hakata tonkotsu ramen with the thinner straight noodles. Yes, the broth of the tonkotsu ramen is good but I kind of find it a tad overwhelming. So if you're into tonkotsu style hakata ramen maybe this is the place for you. So let's break it down: We got seated and the waitress was very nice and energetic. We got our waters but then waited around for almost 15 minutes before the waitress came by again to take our orders. She was apologetic and the restaurant was busy, so it's understandable. Plus, gave us more time to look over the menu... not that you need it though because there are like 7 options for ramen... you have more trouble deciding among all the varieties of appetizers, in my opinion. I got the Shiromaru Hakata Classic... because I like the tried and true varieties. This was supposedly the "orginal" version of what started it all. It was good, decent amount of noodles, a half of a soft broiled egg, but my gripe with this ramen (and the other ramens we got at the table), was that it wasn't hot enough (not like spicy hot, but temperature wise, it wasn't hot enough). Â Maybe it's just me, but when I eat ramen, I like the kind that's nice, hot, and steamy...the kind that would fog up your glasses if you wore glasses, ya know? We also had a Akamaru Modern, this was nice and different and had an interesting kick, with the garlic and hot oil...once again though...not hot enough. My other friend tried their special ramen which had monkfish liver pate mixed in...and this one I thought was pretty delicious and different from any ramen I've tried before. I'd come back for this ramen (but not if wait was more than 15 minutes). The pork belly buns got a big "MEHH" because I've had much, much better on the streets in Taiwan, land where pork belly buns originated so yeah. And the pork belly in the buns wasn't even fatty, either! It was lean pork as far as I could tell. They did seem to have lots of other options for appetizers though. Overall the three of us each had a bowl of ramen and split 1 order of pork belly buns and paid $22 each...definitely NOT cheap for ramen, even for Tokyo standards! So to wrap it up, Ippudo gets points for creativity in the monkfish liver pate ramen, friendly service, a really clean bathroom, and nice atmosphere. Â Their ramens need to be served HOT and overall taste was just okay...and the wait (if there is one) and price is not justified for me. All in all, I'd go somewhere else for ramen because I'm sure there exist places that are just as tasty, not as expensive... perhaps just not as well known and hyped up as Ippudo.

Came here on a date with my boyfriend through HowAboutWe. The date included an appetizer to share, two entrees, a dessert to share, and a round of drinks. For the drinks, we each ordered a glass of wine. About halfway through the meal, a bug flew into my glass, so I received a new glass. The meal here was pretty good. We shared the kale salad (due to all the glowing reviews on Yelp!), my boyfriend had the lamb, and I had the sirloin special. We shared the blueberry financier. The kale salad was good, although my boyfriend didn't like it too much. It is a big serving (can be a main dish!), so we had lots leftover, which I was able to bring home. My boyfriend preferred his lamb dish to my sirloin, but I enjoyed both. The sirloin came with some grilled green beans and roasted corn. Both dishes were decently portioned, however the dessert was a bit tiny. This restaurant is small, and quaint. The tables are really right next to each other, and it seemed to be a pretty popular spot. However, the prices were a bit high, and it wasn't that cool inside the restaurant (more like, warm/comfortable).

Fitting for Tres Carnes to be compared to Chipotle, as it is in some comments, because for all its' hype it is no more worthy of a visit. The meat tastes better. And the extra $ you pay cancels that out. There are awesome burrito places in nyc, don't get suckered by a mediocre one.

Great food. Great music. Enjoyed the atmosphere and everything else that goes with it. The taste of the food was about a 4/5 star. I wouldn't say that i haven't eaten anything similar around the area, but you would definitely want to try this restaurant. :)

Got a last minute reservation for 6:30 on a Friday night a few weeks ago. Good thing I did. The places was quite popular even at that time. Very quaint and surpisingly somewhat Parisian. Make note though, the place is tight quarters. I sat at a table that when I left 2 people at tables on either side of me had to move so that I could get out, and I'm not a big person. The service was friendly and attentive. I had the pumpkin ravioli that was very good (not as good as Union Cafe's butternut squash ravioli) and the lamb chops. I would go back. The menu had quite a bit to choose from and the wine list was nice as well. The atmophere was fun and festive. Right off the 6 to boot.

Overrated. I really don't get the hype. Difaras continues to be the best in Brooklyn in my opinion... has been for almost a decade now. Certainly not worth the wait, even though it's local I don't even bother.

Another great spot in the Lower East Side. Â Tucked away in an alley, and it almost feels like you are eating in someone's home. Â Funky and cool decor. Â I have only come in for drinks, but the food looked good too.

This a really great place for sandwiches most of which have lots of mozzarella in them. The sandwich (panini) menu is huge and they can customize anything on the menu to your liking. One of these sandwiches is big enough to fill you up for dinner. I would definitely come back here again. 1 star off for being out of chorizo when I tried ordering a sandwich with it.

I ordered from here last night and it was outstanding! I've never had better delivery pizza! Â Get the spec and arugula pizza you will not regret it particularly if you get the table 87 salad on the side.
Go for the burritos and skip the tacos. Â Tacos were terrible, very dry.

At long last, Hudson Eats is finally up and running. First: A little background. I started working at Brookfield Place (f/k/a World Financial Center) exactly two years ago. Even then, much of the building was under construction and as time went on, store by store shut down in preparation for the renovation. For far too many months, the dining options consisted of only Financier Patisserie, Devon and Blakely, and the dreaded corporate cafeteria. But, at long last, and not without a few delays, Hudson Eats opened in the first weekend of June. Layout-wise, it resembles an upscale food court, similar to the likes of Gotham West Market. Each restaurant/shop has its own area and visitors and customers are free to wander between them. There's a good amount of communal seating available as well, but it's probably not the best place to hold a business meeting. While the full line up of vendors has yet to open (one more day!), most were open for service a day in advance; Dig Inn Seasonal Market, Mighty Quinn's, Skinny Pizza, Dos Toros, Tartinery, Sprinkles Cupcakes, Chopt, and Num Pang appear prepared to serve the public. The options and variety of cuisines available are pretty impressive, encompassing salads, barbeque, pizza, Mexican, and even Cambodian sandwiches. Lines during lunch the first day were pretty lengthy, but I imagine with a little more time, it won't require a solid 20-30 minutes to order and recieve food. Time will tell if Hudson Eats can live up to the pent-up hype as well as the sizable crowds that are sure to form - but it's a promising start.

4.5 stars. I love the hidden nature of this place, the ambiance is perfect and the service is great. I'd say 85% of the food is great too. Came with 2 friends for a 7 PM reservation on a Wednesday. Loved the decor and intimate nature of the space, and the mid-century feel of the room (hello Don Draper's apartment!) We tried: --Fisherman's Salad (skip this, it's fine but not amazing) --Fried Sweet Potato (AMAZING, do not miss) --Uni Croquette (yum) --Sliders (delicious) --Miso Cod (perfection in a dish, the cod was like BUTTER, I don't understand how they cook it that way..) --Pork Loin (good, but not the best we had) --Various cocktails (all were good) Overall, Bohemian is a very cool place that I would definitely come back to. Not a meal I can afford everyday (total was $70 ish per person) but definitely a fun place to take out of town guests or go for a special dinner or occasion.

OMG! this place is just regular fries and different dipping sauce. Not worth it. I like my fries a little on the crispier side and these were regular wedge cut fries and soggy. I thought they were going to be a nice and crispy since they were a nice golden brown color. So disappointing. Â We got the regular pommes frites sauce...pft! it's just mayonnaise. Maybe I'll have to try them with a different sauce, but I don't know if that will make a difference since these are just fries. I went to a Belgian place in DC that has frites too and although they are just regular fries too they were at least nice and crispy. Â Unfortuantely, this place is not worth it especially since it is a little ways from the subway (like most places in this area).

Whoever gave you that half-boiled piece of meat on a bone with sauce on it under the name "BBQ" is an asshole. Give it to the nearest dog and leave. Now you're gonna get on the B61 bus to Beard/Van Brunt St in Red Hook or take an Uber if you have $20 burning a hole in your credit card. When you get there you'll see a building called "Hometown Bar-B-Que" and you're gonna go inside. Your taste buds are about to be rearranged in the best way possible. What's good? Everything. Everything? Everything. "But I heard..." SHUSH! Everything is good. The lamb belly? Fat-glistened and amazing. The beef ribs? Big enough to flip over Fred Flinstone's car. The brisket? Call your momma. The beans? A meal in itself. The kale? The reason kale ain't played out yet. The cornbread? Fuck your carb intake. Get it. The sausage? Order it and take home the rest for tomorrow's morning hash. Since it took you a while to get here plan to spend at least a couple hours here if not more on a busy night. The line can range anywhere from five minutes to an hour on a nice day. If you get there before 7 you should be good. After 8PM all bets are off BUT you can spend that line time getting toasted on whiskey and Shiner Bock while the nutty smokiness in the air tells you stories of meat and oak.

Heard so many good things about this place. We decided to check it out on our stroll through Union Square. The service was blah. Cashier was a little rude. It took little to no time for the food to come out which was nice. Seating was skimpy w only 3 or 4 tables. We got the carnitas burrito. It was merely above average. We both decided it was just a small upgrade from Chipotle. Difference is that this burrito cost $11. Definitely not worth the price. Don't think we will be coming back.

I have had brunch, lunch, and dinner at this restaurant. And I enjoyed all three. I liked brunch the best. I thought it was a nice selection of entrees and all for a fair price. I wish the wait wasn't so long, but it really is one of the best places in the neighborhood.

Very Very well made noodles (both kinds). The wait was pretty long, and the heat was getting to me a little (No AC where I was. I think they had it more in the back because I was seated near the entrance). Other then those two things, it was totally worth it to try this place out. I got the miso ramen, and I loved it. The soup was not too oily or salty, and the staff was very very nice to us. It's pretty small though, but you KNOW that if a place is a hole-in-the-wall place and there is STILL a long line of people waiting outside in the summer heat, you KNOW that the food has to be great.

I'm a huge Landhaus fan. They've been around for a while with their tent at Smorgasburg, but this location at the Woods with a larger menu is even better. Their grilled corn is the bomb (seriously, it's my favorite), jalapeno cheddar hush puppies were fluffy and flavorful, great shrimp burger, and crab rangoon...I've loved everything I've tried. A couple weeks ago they had a ramen special that was absolutely delicious - perfect in this chilly weather. I also dig the outdoor seating. It's a nice place to chill in the summer, and in the winter they put up panels and get the heaters going. Cozyyyy. And don't forget the bacon on a stick, y'all. ;) In conclusion: highly recommended and definitely worth checking out. Come for the drinks, stay for the food. Or just come for the food.
I waited about 45 minutes for a roll that I finished in 45 seconds.

Since the move this place has definitely took a landslide for the worst. The customer service always sucked. But the food always superseded that. So I dealt with it. Flash forward to today. It moved to a more spacious, 2 floor mansion as opposed to its former matchstick box location. The customer service has stayed the same, they know people come here no matter what so they don't care. But the pizza sure has taken a toll. My last experience was pretty lame. I came here because my relatives from Puerto Rico love this place. So I got invited. They came with an entourage of about 8 plus me and 1 more. Can you believe they seated us in the cramped corner on the first floor just so that they won't have to open the more spacious 2nd floor? Really! Even the table behind me stood in awe at the face of discontent we had. This should never have had happened. Welcome to NYC!, know that New Yorkers rarely eat here now.

The pizza that my friend and I got were a bit off. It was way too thin. There was not enough cheese :( Â Unfortunately for us, the owner had to make about 5-6 pizza pies while I was there. He was probably in a hurry. So I figured this is why he wasn't up to his best. (But $5 for a super thin slice?!) The positive side is I do LOVE the taste of the pizza for the most part. I still love you Di Fara!

This used to be my favorite burger joint.. That is until they changed their fries. Can someone please explain why? Was it to cut costs? If it was I know a heap of people who wouldn't buy the fries because quite frankly they taste like crap. So there goes some of your sales shake shack. Your crinkle fries were so good and set you apart from all the other burger places in New York. If you were going to make the change at least do it for the better. Not to replace them with soggy, tasteless run of the mill fries. I'll also say that the girl at the register didn't smile/say hello or barely acknowledged us. When the burger came out they didn't have onion like I'd asked and the wrong one had pickle on it. Also mine looked like it had been squashed. QUALITY SLIPPING PEOPLE! Shame on you shake shack for being so cheap. You've lost a customer and I guarantee I'm not the first..

There is no doubt that this Toscano is authentic. I cannot say enough good things about this restaurant. We have had just about everything on the menu, but my favorite is the short ribs with polenta. It is quite possibly the best short rib that I have ever had. The two negative reviews here please disregard- I do not see any issues with the qualitative aspects of their food, or the qualitative. The service has always been spot on (but as in this business, things do not always run smoothly)- this is one restaurant that hopefully will stick around. Heading their again this evening!

A nice little gem for a weekend brunch. Â The eggs benedict and croque monsieur were very satisfying but fairly straightforward. Â I really enjoyed the potatoes with the hollandaise sauce. Â I wish we would've have gotten refills on the coffee or orange juice. Â It kind of seemed a few dollars overpriced. Â Overall, delicious brunch options in a cute neighborhood joint.

Great pre theater dinner spot. Â Superb service, and nice timing to ensure we enjoy dinner and get to show in plenty of time. Â Fabulous pizza, crunchy light crust and fresh toppings. Â Seafood pasta wonderful earthy flavor. Â Canolli to die for. Two things, easily corrected, keep them from a 5. Â Specialty fried artichokes were oily, underseasoned, and had too many inedible chewy leaves. Â Bread for table one piece was fresh baked and amazing flavor of olive oil and rosemary. Â Other pieces were day old cold chewy. Would still keep them my first choice for pre theater dining in the area.

This place was on my restaurant "to do" list, so it was a lovely surprise to stumble across it on our recent walkabout in the Lower East Side. We we're pretty hungry when we got there, and we were treated to a great assortment of German food. Actually, they say it's Austrian, but it was quite German to me. Let's say "Germanic". Appetizers - We started out with a mixed platter of cured meat which came with pickled vegetables (onions, carrots, cucumbers) and gorgeous, fresh black bread. Good time to start a reduced starch diet! The highlight of the apps was the pork belly (I think that's what it is) looks just like uncooked bacon and tastes great. The only trick is that the flavor (for me at least) is much more present when eaten on the rich dark bread. It needs that context. By itself a bit too fatty and lost, if you ask me. The smoked hard salami assortment was very good too, as was the capicola. One thing that I wasn't crazy about was the blood sausage, a bit too sweet and soft. Finally, we had a choice of 2 spreads on the side, a lovely light cheese and liverwurst, both very flavorful. Entree - We decided to split an entree and went with the Emmentalerwurst (basically a light-cheese wurst), white cabbage, and polenta dumplings. Everything went great together, was extremely flavorful, and most importantly, tasted fresh. This is in direct comparison to the another German joint we went to on the west side, where the entree felt a bit overcooked and old. I also loved how all the elements went so well together. The cabbage, the cheese and wurst felt like they were perfectly intertwined in my mouth. And, though I didn't have much of the dumpling, I must acknowledge it was very good for sopping up the cheese that was leftover from the Emmenalerwurst. Even though we split a big app and an entree I was amazingly full and totally satisfied. Great meal, and it's also great that the placed I wanted to go to for so long turned out to be quite a joy. Non food things...service was pleasant and quick, and the decor was great, wonderful lighting, very airy, felt clean and new. As I mentioned to my girl, it's like we were guests there, rather than the feeling I get in a lot of Manhattan places which is that we are intruding on their private cunty wannabe sophisticated syndicate. In the end, great place. Definitely would love to go back to check out the other stuff!

I've been in this neighborhood now for more than 15 years. This is my new favorite spot. There. I said it. The secret is out. I go for the food (great for sharing with a small group of 2-5 in my opinion so you can order one of everything and try more!), the funky and chill atmosphere, the quality sourced ingredients (I did the research!) and the friendliness of the staff. I went when it first opened and have been back more than 6 times (trying to taste everything and I STILL have things to try!) Tonight I had my go-to Seared Cauliflower- I'm ADDICTED- and the salmon sandwich. Delicious. Every time! I guess I was holding off writing this review in part because I don't want it too become TOO popular.... especially come summer with the backyard outdoor picnic tables, but..... secrets this good aren't meant to be kept! Plus I want the owners to be successful and stick around.
Very good falafels.. But I wish they had more spicy options!

great spot for a quick & cheap bite. Â always come hear right before catching a movie at the AMC theatre. Â I enjoy the simplicity of the menu...pick the meat and how you want it prepared. Â I always get the CARNE ASADA soft taco...so juicy! Â If you like spicy, the red hot sauce has an awesome kick to it! Â down it with some good 'ol fountain soda...you'll say, "AHhhhh~" afterwards. Â never tried the burritos but they seem to be a bit hit and look fulfilling!

Love this place! Even the bread and black beans are amazing. The restaurant is nice and big and u don't feel cramped. The service is good and the atmosphere is great too. The portions are big and the groupon is a great deal. I would go again if I was on the Upper West Side. I had the surf and turf after being sick and the meal hit the spot!

Great deal for lunch! Beatiful decor & excellent service. The menu is easy to understand with detailed description of sauces. I was confident ordering & very happy with my selection, shrimp in basil sauce jasmine rice, and rolls. I cant wait to go back & try other dishes.

For the love of balls! MMM MMM MMM ! Their meatballs are really good! I got their spicy pork with pesto sauce and mozzarella cheese. I thought this was good until I had my boyfriends portion of his meal. He had the spicy pork with spicy meat sauce and it was sooooo goood!!!!! Found my go to ball and sauce :) Will be getting that when I come here next time! Their mash potato sides here is really good too. Best mash ever ! Must must get. The wait here is ridiculously long. I would come here when it first opens to avoid that wait.

I wanted to like this place more, because they had so many gluten free options for my husband. Â He thought his gluten free raviloi was so-so... my food was so-so... however, we both thought the dessert was fabulous!! They had all kinds of gf options many places don't. Â My husband has the GF carrot cake and loved it. Â They also had GF red velevet and key lie pie. Â I had a dessert from the specials menu... a hazelnut tort... not GF very yum. Â We will give this place another try each ordering different dishes most likely.

Okay.... so I'm kind of stuck with this place. The concept is cool... 24 hr diner that serve cuban food. Except I think it's cuban by concept but not really cuban. I don't know, maybe I ordered the wrong things. I love breakfast food all throughout the day so I tried their breakfast. It's a small place and very loud and busy. Â  Good: their drinks are pretty interesting and good. strong too. Bad: I don't like their bathroom. I can see the shadows! Overall... hummm... maybe i'll give it another try.

Went to Fish last night, after a brisk walk around Washington Square as the sun was setting...Fish has the illusion of looking much smaller and cramped from the outside, but once we were in, we realized how much less cramped it was than we had thought. Â We grabbed the only 2 open seats at the bar and enjoyed a fruity Pinot Noir that hit the spot. Â We started with a shellfish tower that came with 3 types of oysters, King crab legs, and shrimp, and since I have to try the crabcakes at every restaurant that I go to, I gave the appetizer a shot. Â The crabcake was amazing, lightly breaded on the outside with plenty of lump crab meat and a hint of dijon. Â My petit gf destroyed the King crabs in the shellfish tower, and I was impressed by 2 of the 3 types of oysters. Â For dinner, she had a salad topped with grilled tuna steak strips, which were cooked to perfection. Â I had Chilean Sea Bass in a soup with stewed tomatoes and potatoes, which was unbelievable. Â I have walked by this place for years on Bleecker St, but it was usually too crowded to get in...I am glad to have finally gotten to eat here, and I was far from disappointed. Â We will defiantly be going back..

Reviews are stellar and the ambiance is good. But how does a place with such a reputation serve processed American cheese on its grilled cheese? They should be serving the ultimate grilled cheese and instead, it's oily plastic.

Very tasty! Â  Not from Brooklyn but would come back. Â Price wasn't cheap but definitely worth it if you like sea food. Â  Could see the statue of liberty from my rood top seat! Â Over all pretty cool place.

Traif review 2/13/2014 This was my second visit to Traif. Besides braving the weather again after going to the Knave in the Parker Meridian for coffee and hot chocolate, we were also venturing into Brooklyn. We took the M train and walked around the corner, which in nice weather seems very fast but the rivers that the streets had become really made this more like fording creeks on the Oregon trail. After walking by Shiksa and realizing their favorite waitress was working there that night, we made our way to Traif. We started the evening with cocktails. I had a Red Pearl (or 3), which is chili infused vodka muddled with Thai basil, kiwi and citrus sour. One of the best drinks I have ever had. My friend had the Rude Little Pig which is lapsang infused tequila with orange liqueur, pomegranate and a bacon rim. I have had this before and for me the bacon rims tastes a little too much like artificial liquid smoke. Her boyfriend had the Dacker Adirondack Ale which was great. Becca, our waitress was phenomenal, letting us order our plates a little at a time because we prefer having only 1-2 at a time. While we were waiting the staff greeted us with an amuse of the bacon broth. I don't quite remember the order of dishes but we started with a few salads. The Macintosh, pomegranate, cranberries, greens with bacon and blue cheese was light and delicate. The cheese was grated into a fine dust instead of hunky which my friend's boyfriend enjoyed. We also has the tricolore salad with grapefruit, clementines, currants, carbs al vino, and sunflower seeds, this was very bright and fresh but I think I preferred the first. The burrata with roasted beets, raspberries, pomegranate yogurt and mint was my least favorite dish of the evening. Way too sweet, it was like eating dessert. Burrata doesn't have enough salt to stand up to the sweetness of both beets and fruit. Eternally on the menu, we had two orders of the spicy big eyed tuna tartare on top of little tempura Japanese eggplant rounds with kecap manis. Still one of my favorites. It warrants saying that my friend is picky about meat products due to animal rights so many of the dishes are off limits. We did get to have the braised escargot with pork sausage, roasted wine mushrooms in a red wine sauce that came with two thick toasts for sopping up the sauce. She did not try the snail but it was her boyfriend's first time so I bullied them into ordering it. Could have been a little more flavorful but it was nice and light which escargot don't have s a tendency to be due to the butter that people use with them. The salt and pepper shrimp with pineapple, roasted yam, snow peas and sweet spicy Thai vin were another highlight of the meal. So much better than the shrimp at ABC cocina. Sadly most of the other pork, duck, foie gras, beef, sweetbreads dishes were off limits for ordering but I saw them all go by and I really wanted one of everything. Supposedly the last menu at Traif was even better. Although I wasn't a proponent of ordering it, the baked muenster cheese with smoked chorizo, golden apples and crostini was another stand out dish of the evening. Perhaps another bite of apple or crostino would have helped the amount of cheese but it was not excessive, being served only in a small ramekin. Our final two dishes included the sautÃ©ed broccoli rabe with portobello mushrooms, truffle toast, fried egg and aged asiago and skate cheeks "New England chowder" braised bacon, spinach, potato and leeks. The egg on the broccoli rabe would have been better if we had eaten it right away but it over cooked and became hard boiled. I partially blame my friend who turned it over so it would drain into the bread but didn't pierce it enough. Not at good as I remember. The skate cheeks were like a chowder but large pieces instead of incorporated. Buttery texture and a nice light taste, they were another highlight for me. We decided to order the bacon doughnuts because we thought they only came two to an order. They brought us four, along with panda cotta on the house and sweet vermouth after dinner drinks. Another fabulous meal. I specifically complemented Becca on her impeccable service, aside from the little freebies (they also bring a piece of pineapple to refresh you at the end), they were wonderful and attentive, water always in the glass and the drinks just kept coming (by request of course).

What more can i say about this place! i read a couple of the reviews and atfirst i was apprehensive about coming! But i can tell you that I am glad i took the chance. The feel of soco alone was enough to make me come back. It was totally Brooklyn Chic..I tried the famous chicken and waffles which was good, but the Pecan Crusted Pork Chop was soo good. I enjoyed the texture and the different flavors, it was a new feel but one that felt oh so good! I must admit im in love..we tried the mac and cheese and that alone shouldve had its own menu! It was delicious, with a nice crust and soft on the inside. Rob (the server) suggested that i try the mardi gras which tasted like a rum punch from the south!! Where do they do that at?? SoCO thats where! I love this place and would definitely come back with my business partners at first chance!! Brooklyn we have a gem!!
Best tequila drinks around. Â It's tight inside but if you want good Mexican food accompanied by a jalapeÃ±o margarita then this is where to go.

I love the atmosphere of this place! It's loud and busy but very trendy and fun. All of the food is outstanding. I went with a bunch of girls and we all tried different combination of the meat platters and sides. Everything was delicious. I personally had the pulled pork and bbq chicken with the mac & cheese and coleslaw. It was one of the best mac & cheeses I've ever had. My friends tried the sausage, ribs, and other sides, no complaints with anything. The only downside was that we were seated at a high top table in the bar and it got very crowded. At one point we felt like we were on a date with these two guys standing just a few inches away from our table. I've also been to the Harlem location a couple years back and it was equally good.

Had a really nice dinner here - the yellow tail appetizer was tasty but small, the duck and fois gras ravioli was excellent, and the spaghetti was great (but not excellent). I'd definitely go back though.

So I'm going to write a more befitting essay on this subject in the future, but this place has an AWESOME burger. Sorry about the capitalization, but the burger is "that" obnoxiously good. The fries leave something for the imagination. Great atmosphere, and there is a Barnes and Noble is right upstairs. Great place to enjoy that new novel.

This is an excellent spot in little Italy for delicious family style Italian food. Â My favorite dish that we ordered was the Gnocchi. Â The pizza was good as well but I preferred the pasta. Â The wine we ordered was by recommendation of our server and was also very good. Â I definitely recommend this place if you're looking for some real Italian food.

Yes. My very first five-star review for a Brooklyn restaurant, given here for so many reasons. For creating a true destination spot in Red Hook, and staying after Hurricane Sandy no doubt made your first winter harder than you ever could have planned. For designing a place that looks like it's been there for years, with bars and rooms and games and spirit where the tourists feel like locals, and the locals feel like family. For a bar where, when you ask for a margarita without mix, you are told they don't even HAVE the sweetened crap. For the most light, fresh and generous order of fried oysters I've ever had, with a tomato bacon aoli that was nothing short of inspired. For littlenecks fresh enough to introduce themselves, with cocktail sauce spicy enough for the diner to actually stop eating long enough to praise (and this guy NEVER stops eating long enough to praise!). For the full assortment of appropriate tools for eating a king crab - especially the Zeecut (best thing for the task). The crab. The crab. The crab. For dropping a little bit of Fire Island into the middle of one of the last affordable neighborhoods in Brooklyn, more Williamsburg than Williamsburg and a community with a true spirit that is nothing short of infectious. I'll be back - many many times. I'll take the bus - it's only a block away. I'll go on weeknights for your FABULOUS looking happy hours, and hope to see many other Yelpers there. Thank you.

My favorite Smorgasburg folks have set up shop in the East Village. Showed up on a Sunday night with a few friends. Â The line was long and the place was packed at 8:30 pm. Â  We managed to wolf down some brisket, sausage, a giant brontosaurus rib and some pulled pork. Â The rib was clearly everyone's favorite. Â The sweet potatoes are not to be missed as well. Â  Looking forward to many returns.

French fries are my all time favorite. These were very good. My group tried the pesto mayo and the roasted garlic mayo. The roasted garlic was the favorite. I think the small is around $4ish and the sauces are $1 each. I crave these.

I ran into these guys at a pop-up by Madison Square Park and had their fried chicken sittin' pretty in a generously buttered up, fresh out of the oven buttermilk biscuit. It was insanity, so I got a second one, which says something because they baked the biscuits as they went so each one takes anywhere from 5-15 minutes to make, depending on their inventory. It might not be the same sitch at the brick and mortar.

This place is a historical landmark, one of the few original buildings in NYC. Â Fraunces Tavern is an Irish bar serving up Irish bar food in an old building that has been around for hundreds of years. Â I definitely enjoyed the historical location and seeing how much of the original structure still remained and think about the people who have been through here. Â I had the pot pie here and I must say it was a very good meal. Â The service from the kitchen was pretty fast and they have a great selection of beers. Â I would definitely mark this place down as a place to try brunch.

5 stars for taste and 3 stars for price/value = 4 stars. Ippudo is slightly overrated. Â And VERY overpriced. Â But yes, their ramen is very delicious (at least the modern ramen was). Â Soup is very rich and comes out hot, and the ramen noodles are of perfect consistency. Â If you like spicy you HAVE to pay the extra $2 and get the spicy paste. Â Just don't put too much or you'll regret it and not be able to taste the goodness of the original broth. But still, really? $20 for a bowl of ramen is kind of crazy.
Duh-licious, I liked both the standard slice and the big slices. Everyone on here has a long review, I'll just say that I agree with it. Love the oreo-vanilla icing.
soup dumplings. soup dumplings - - -

The wait is agonizing but the reward for the wait is worth it. First time I ever got fried chicken and waffles was here, and I have to say, it's been pretty tough to beat. I've had it at Pies N Thighs, and while both are extremely sickeningly delicious, I thought this place's chicken had it down better. The gravy with the maple syrup - I have to stop, because I am about to drool. I've had the hangar steak and eggs here too. So so so good. Also the buttermilk pie. Service is friendly, obviously it can be slow because everyone and their mother comes here. It's become a well-known spot. Very hipster-y. Seriously though.... don't sleep on the chicken and waffles.

Such a cool atmosphere and amazing space. The drinks and food are pretty cheap for what you're getting. I would have given it 4 stars easily, but my food was just mediocre. I think I'll do more drinking and less eating here in the future. But maybe I'll give the food another try. Overall I would definitely recommend this place. A great place for a group of friends on a nice night.
it's good.

Tiny, very cozy n intimate spot. Very welcoming and professional service... a tad too attentive. Thai chef cooking French-Asian fusion. Roasted squid legs: tasty sauce and interesting combo of ingredients, but the squid itself was low quality... it tasted old and fishy. Sparkling baby back ribs: very good. Seared duck breast noodle ramen: not crazy about this dish as much as everybody else. It's just an average ramen, not even particularly flavorful. Underwhelming. Baked cod with mushroom risotto: very tasty and delicate, but the mushroom flavor was totally hidden by everything else. Hanger steak: good, but not particularly inspiring. Cheesy truffle fries: fine. Mediocre red wine by the glass... only 1 choice available. Overall, a good choice and surely well priced. You can tell they're as excited as everybody else at the beginning of their business, but fell short in a few recipes. They have plenty of time to improve, though, and their ideas are without a doubt valuable. Cash only. Uncomfortable seats and "tables".

A friend recommended this restaurant and I'm sure glad she did. The ambiance is great; the servers are friendly, good-looking and great with suggestions; there was no pressure to order more or drink more; and the good was a great mix of local-organic-rustic-americana: - Ordered the clams based on my friend's recommendation...big fan. Simple but delectable - Mixed greens special salad was simple, light and tasty - Split the steak .... the chimichurri sauce (that creates a smokiness) may not be for everyone, but I was a fan...and the steak itself was basically butter. - We ordered the lemon bar and dark chocolate ganache dessert. The lemon bar was a real standout. The dark chocolate was good, but perhaps a bit intense. - Oh yeah, the Lolita cocktail was refreshing and a great apertif. - On the per-glass, the malbec went great with the steak, we were 50-50 on the pinot noir, but the grenache was simple and yummy All-in-all, a really good experience and would go definitely go back.
Excellent food, service and atmosphere. Â Veggie burger and tabbouleh were outstanding. Â Don't miss this one
Beef Udon is great! Great prices and service is super quick even during the midtown lunch hours.
Best Mexican food in town! Love the drinks and atmosphere as well as the service, although it is usually a long wait for a table.

A very typical Chinatown eatery that serves cheap, fast and good food with very minimal service. Â I love their roast duck here, and it's the dish that keeps me coming back here. Â I also like the roast pig as well, but it's definitely not as good as the ones you can get in Hong Kong. Â I usually get a combination of roast duck and roast pig over rice. Â My wife likes the wonton noodles here as well.

I went here for lunch on a Friday for the outdoor seating :) The service was pretty terrible..we waited at least 40 minutes for sandwiches to arrive. Luckily they were good, although i'm not sure if i'll be back for lunch during the week. I had the roast beef sandwich with melted swiss on ciabatta. My friend ordered the hot breaded eggplant with pesto on ciabatta and it looked pretty incredible.
Best dumplings ever. The location might scare some tourists but don't let it. Be prepared to set with other people and don't forget they don't take credit cards so bring your cash

Came here for an event-- the octopus salad was soooo good. loved it. the lasagna was good, but nothing special. but my friends chicken milanese was really good! i did try the fettuccine w/ pesto though and it was no bueno haha. the chocolate gelato and panna cotta was AMAZING!!

Best brunch ever! Thanks to my dear friend who came to wait in front of the restaurant at 8:45am on a Sunday morning, we were able to sit in at 10:00am. The French roast, omelet, the sandwich, everything classic brunch item was just amazing! We also got free drinks and juice/coffee.

Ever since I moved away from NYC, this is the one of the few restaurants from home that I truly miss. Â Vanessa's Dumpling House is always one of the first places that I stop by when I go home every time. Â You can't find any other place in Chinatown that ha better dumplings. Â The dough is not too thick and the inside is not too oily. Â Many dumplings in Chinatown have those two problems. Â The dumplings at Vanessa's are perfect. Â A perfect dumpling with the perfect amount of crisp to it. Â Besides the dumplings, they offer sesame pancake sandwiches and noodles (soup and stir-fry). Â The sesame pancake sandwiches are amazing and they have several selections (ham, duck, pork, roast beef) and makes the perfect compliment to some dumplings. Â (My favorite is the roast beef sandwich). Â Looking at the menu, there is not one thing that I don't like, there is not one thing I don't like and none of the items are going to empty your wallet. Â For about $4, you can get a nice tasty sesame pancake sandwich with a side of dumplings and a drink. Â You can't beat that anywhere else. Â Just one con about Vanessa's is that it is always crowded and hard to get seats if you want to eat there. Â But Â I would just take the risk since this place is definitely a must visit if you're in the neighborhood.
Cheap and delicious dumplings. Cash only. There's usually a line but they churn food out quickly.

Pretty bad overall experience. Service was very slow and inattentive. We ordered pork katsu and beef udon soup. Both dishes were 20 minutes apart, greasy and pretty bland. To make things worse both my mom and I got sick afterwards. Would not recommend this place.

Was here for brunch in Summer '12. Amazing food and atmosphere. Service could b a little more attentive but thats no fault of the staff, they just need to hire more people. No drink special otherwise it would be 5 stars. There is no brunch like a boozy brunch

My fiance took me here for my birthday last year. The food was AWESOME. We shared the duck meatballs which were quite tasty. No one else comes close to their risotto, LOVED IT. I wish I could come here for dinner every day!

You don't have to be from Texas to know good barbecue. It's all about the meat, about the care and preparation and finally the rubs. Fette Sau succeeds at all three. The pork belly is moist, fatty, good balance of salty and meat flavor. As long as you're not recovering from quadruple duple bypass, I think it's safe to indulge. By far, my favorite cut was the brisket, followed by pork belly and finally the pork ribs. (Next on my list to try are the beef ribs and pork sausages) Where I'll say I wasn't as impressed would be on the sides. German potato salad was nothing to write back home to Germany about. Lastly, the rustic decor, communal seating and dark lighting set the mood to chow down with your fellow bbq enthusiasts. The meat will always serve as great conversation with the group sitting aside. Did I mention I smelled like bbq smoke the whole way home? Get here as early as possible if you want to beat the lines and sit comfortably indoors or outdoors. After 7pm on a weekday and I'd say good luck. Hipster line out the door for sure. You'd swear there was a salvation army drive.

This one time I spent a semester in Paris and I also hopped around other countries. Ever since then, I've been trying to relive my eurotrip without hopping over the pond. I'm always starting sentences like, oh god, this place I went to in Paris/Madrid/Rome etc. had this thing that was to die for. Is it obnoxious? Yes. But have I ever claimed to be something I am not? No, I keeps it too real. So this Saturday, I tried to kick it Spanish style and came to Boqueria for tapas and sangria. BEST COMBO EVER. Unfortunately, it was too early and they were still serving brunch. Not that this means it's too early for sangria. We had the rose sangria, which was the bomb. As far as recreating Madrid for me, the sangria was on point. The meat and cheese platter was good, but frankly, unremarkable. It's just a variation of the antipasti platter, you know, get thee to a Trader Joe's and DIY. Points for the freshness and quality of the cheeses, meat, bread and the pairing though, it was a pretty popular choice. The Spanish brunch choice was underwhelming. It sounded dandy on the menu, rock shrimp scramble on brioche with a side of Spanish style home fries. The flavors were flat. The potatoes were good, but everything is yummy when seasoned with Sazon [a speculation]. The one tapas we tried -- quail eggs over chorizon on toast points -- was delightful, but $6 dollars for 2 cracker sized pieces? Can I just book my ticket to Madrid right now? Â Plus, something about the food here just feels...unauthentic. But that's me being obnox, right? Oh, but shouts to the host for giving us the BEST BOOTH in the house. I'd come back just to sit there and try all four kinds of sangria.

I was looking for a new brunch place to check out and based off of the yelp reviews I expected more. Â (Maybe my expectations were too high?) I love the feel and ambience of Sweet Afton--the mason jar with flowers, the candle, the low-lighting (though they didn't dim the lights until we'd been there for over an hour, which I thought was just weird timing) It was a relaxing, chill place and I LOVE that it's locally sourced food/ingredients! :-) Now to the food/drinks. Â I ordered the Blueberry Muddle (gin, blueberries, mint, lemon juice) is was DELISH-- but note: Â VERY strong on the fresh mint!!! I appreciated it, very fresh and reminds me of summer but it could be just a tiny bit less mint and more lemon juice/gin. My bf ordered the Bloody Mary and it was very good! (I took a little sip) Â It was very spicy and has pickle juice ---it was very good!! We ordered the fried pickles because we heard you HAVE to order them. Â And let's face it, anything fried--my bf and I will love. Â They were not what we expected, but in a good way. Â They are fluffy and flavorful--good, but didn't blow my mind like others said... Â  ALSO, they brought it out WITH OUR entrees .... which we waited quite a while for--we didn't mind the wait but would have preferred to have the appetizer BEFORE our meal. Now, we really wanted to try the mac n' cheese but feared brunch time would not have it--alas, no mac n' cheese... so we both got Grilled Cheese with Gruyere cheese (there were a lot of yelpers suggesting it) and I have to say I was disappointed. Â It was just alright and pretty plain. Â Nothing amazing (as others have said) and I would not order it again. If coming for brunch get there early--we arrived around 11:15 right after they opened and basically had our choice of seats but around 12:15 the only seats available were at the bar. Â  Overall: - Grilled Cheese--just okay, would not order again. - Fried pickles--pretty good, but not sure if I would order them again. - Ambience and friendly staff-- awesome & loved!! - Probably would come back again, but maybe only at night to try the mac n' cheese and some more drinks.

This place is yummy! My friend made a reservation here for 7. Seated immediately when we were all present. Brunch here is yummy and a very good hangover cure haha. I was slightly hungover when I came but that disappeared after eating the food. I got the sisig which was the Pig ears, snout, cheek, belly (cooked 3 times--boiled, grilled, sautÃ©ed), with sibuyas, garlic and lemon. I really liked it. Not going to lie I originally was expecting an actual pig snout sitting squarely in the center of my dish, which would have left me baffled as to how to to eat it. It wasn't that erotic though and the dish came in a sizzling stone plate with all the ingredients nicely diced and chopped. My friends got the fried chicken with Taro waffles which was delicious as well...I am really curious how the hell they fry it without flour...genius... Overall a great brunch experience and is a bit of a nice twist to your traditional NYC brunches. Great for groups and the wait staff is SUPER friendly which was nice!

Simply the BEST Italian Restaurant in NYC compered to any other doesn't matter upscale, rustic... whatever! GAIA is the BEST! try if you are lucky her spcial fresh pasta with truffle sauce, and the Siciliano panini, she bakes the focaccia herself! what else can we ask! She is absolutley devoted to quality and love for food! and her strong character only makes it better ;) I take all my friends who come and visit NY there. The first thing they say when they get back home... I miss Gaia! not even NY... just Gaia food. I love to see her complaining at people who is in a rush to calm down, or even telling them she will not take their order if they don't have time to wait... she is the maximum standard of Slow Food! a real one! Tip: don't go at rush lunch hour... go soon at 12pm or later than 2pm your experience will be way better.

It's a great Malaysian restaurant. Â I always order the curry crispy pancake to start--always good. The first time I came here, my friend had order for me. Everything was good except for the taro plate desserts, Â just not my kind of dessert. The cold chicken and fried rice plate was good. Second time, the special Malaysian noodle plate was okay. There was a Malaysian restaurant near the police station that was mediocre, but they closed down. Nyonya is good, try the food. Malayasian food is a influence by Chinese, Thai, Indonesian, and other cuisines. For such a popular place, it's cash only place.
Still the best pizza I have ever eaten in my entire life. Â When I get my urge to eat some pizza this is the only place than stands up to my MVP tastes. Best in New York, hands down.
Consistently good. Â Great beer, decent service, good atmosphere, good age mix. Â Not a real pickup scene, not a dive, not a sports bar, not an Irish pub (no Celtic fonts, thank you very much).
THE BEST OF THE BEST VENEZUELAN RESTAURANTS IN NYC! COMPLETE MENU, GOOD PRICES AND VERY SPACIOUS. REALLY RECOMMENDED IT! The food is excellent!!!! Much better than Caracas Arepa Bar.

Fantastic flavors and attentive service make this a great restaurant in NY. Â Cosy 2nd floor room features tasting menus and fine wines, but you can order a la carte. Each item was perfectly prepared and the flavor and quality was superb. Â I do agree with some of the reviewers that individual items are small portions, but the 7 course tasking menu makes up for it. Prices are high, but what you expect for 5-Star dining

Plain and simply, I love this place. I hadn't been here in a while and it was as fantastic as I remember. I went with the Tuesday special, which was delicious. If it weren't for the unnecessarily loud group of girls next ot us, it would have been absolutely perfect. We got seated immediately, as they don't take reservations unless your have a group of 8....or know somebody. Service is always friendly and personable.

Great food, but service has really gone down. The last few times we were there, the servers were completely overwhelmed. They clearly need more staff. Unfortunate, because it's a great menu and has a great selection of wines.

I tried this place on a whim and OMG, it was delicious! I love thai and this place definitely satisfied all my cravings! The calamari appetizer along with the spring rolls were fresh and wonderful. We ordered the "special" pad thai which was a refreshing new take on the traditional one and it was out of this world! The prices were not bad at all and if I lived in NY, I'd definitely come back! Give it a try :)

Two years ago, my son and I travelled to New York for a vacation. Our main reason was for me to take him to a Yankees game before The Stadium was torn down. Fortunately we were able to do that. Unfortunately, the Yankees didn't make the playoffs! But besides seeing the game, Spamalot!, and other attractions the highlight of our one week stay was Patzeria Perfect Pizza! Every night we'd buy a slice or two, take them back to our room and watch Sportscenter as we ate the best pizza in the city (or anywhere else for that matter)! Since we were staying at the Hotel Edison, it was easy to simply walk out the 46th street exit, make a right turn and walk a few steps to Patzeria Perfect Pizza. My only complaint is that I can't get them to FedEx a couple pizzas with dry ice to California. I'm considering a trip back next summer for the pizza alone! It is THAT good! I'd give them ten stars if I could!

Cocktails were great. Atmosphere & decor is wonderful--and unexpectedly hip, for the UWS. Biscuits were amazing, as were our starters. Pickles were ok, but being in NYC, I've had FAR better. My friends enjoyed their entrees, but I'd ordered the $14 mushroom mac & cheese, & was really disappointed. I can't believe I'm even saying this, but there was too much cheese in this dish. (Is too much cheese even possible? When it completely overwhelms the dish & you wind up feeling like you're choking down a vat of sizzling hot salty cheese, then yes.) I prefer to be able to taste the macaroni in my mac & cheese. And couldn't taste the mushrooms, either. Had about 5 bites & was thoroughly cheesed-out--leaving a MASSIVE plate of food, which my friend took home. Hope she can get through it better than I could!...Other things to note: This is one of those kids-in-the-bar kind of places, so if you hate that, beware. Also, a bit of a wait to sit. The prices are a bit steep, but not outrageous. I wish there were more vegetarian entrees--some sort of vegetarian biscuit sandwich, at least. Next time, I'll stick to the starters & sides. Worth going back at least once more, to see if I can walk away without feeling like my entree was trying to give me a coronary.

I think I am a bit of a snob when it comes to certain cuisines, and Thai is one of them. I experienced the real deal in Thailand and ever since have not found anything comparable. Therefore, any review of a Thai restaurant is going to be amazingly biased! But I shall continue to strive for near objectiveness. I've walked by Room Service numerous times but never made the journey to a table. Decided the time had come. A friend from overseas requested Thai food, so I took a shot in the dark and brought us to Room Service. The decor and ambiance is great, half night club, half wanna be sex party. It has all the nuances of a trendy restaurant in Chelsea. But it's also unique in the fact that it dives head first into the idea that you are eating at a hotel. Cool digs. The food was in fact. Damn good! Ordered some Pad Sai Eew and Pad Thai, as well as, a few other appetizer items, including dumplings. Once they arrived I was shocked. The pad thai was HUGE overpowering the plate and delicious too! Everything was hot and nicely prepared. Not too much peanut and not too much spice. It was definitely some one of the best Thai I had in NY. But not THE best. Overall, I'd definitely recommend it someone looking for a fun and trendy place to grab Thai in Chelsea.

Want market price eggs? Look no further than Tia Pol. I had no idea that eggs were seasonal, but I heard that chicken is - thank you, Stone Barns. I think I was too bemused to ask where the eggs came from, but I won't be shy next time. I was here for brunch today and spent a total of $13.50, tax and tip included. What a deal! I was afraid that the market price eggs would be some obscene price, which would make me want them more, but luckily they were $8.50. I had the market price poached egg, which was served on a bed of lentils and sausage. I was happy as a clam, lapping up the sandy green edges of my bowl with big spoon. My friend ordered the market price scrambled eggs with salt cod, which was also delicious, and two others ordered the pork and roasted bell pepper sandwich. Yum. I'm not sure what vegetarians or vegans would do here - there are always the potatoes I suppose. I'll definitely be back, but I might bring my own coffee cup next time because I always feel unnerved when I can't fit my finger through the handle.
Salad decent, pot pie good, duck good, bass good, amuse bush free but a waste. Â Lesbians making out at the bar. Â Need I say more?

This place is definitely a bit overpriced ($5 for one taco), but I do believe that it is worth it. I didn't realize that it was within the market, so I was that freak pacing back and forth on the street until I saw a sign that said it was within. It's a tiny booth/shack thing and the guy working was friendly, though juggling orders at the same time. I opted for the Chipotle'd Chicken Taco and it was made right on the spot in front of me. There are three chairs along a bar top where you can eat and after squeezing lime and taking my first bite, the flavors came through in my mouth. The chicken was tender and had a nice spice to it, and the lime definitely helped bring all those flavors out as well too. He also put in the perfect amount of meat, so that it wasn't skimped, but also not falling out in a huge load, which I appreciate. Would I come back for a taco? Yes. Do I still think that it's worth it? Yes. Is it expensive? Yes Yet, I really don't see an issue with paying for good food.

The food was good but the main ramen attraction was not the best and not worth the 1 hour+ wait. Ippudo'a ramen was good but i did not find it to be amazing or anything special, however their appetizer did leave a really good impression. The Hirata Buns are definitly a must have.

Absolute favorite place in NYC! Service and food are equally impeccable. My friend and I were splitting a side and also wanted to make a substitution to her entree. With out asking - the server told us how to order to make it the most economical. The place smells like butter, the food is sublime. I would go here every night if I could.

Call a spot Brooklyn anything and the masses will come and so will their children and more kids and more. First Saturday open this place was PACKed.....with teeming and screaming toddlers. Â Ambitious in nature and hitting some marks and missing others. BLT- $8 with maple glazed ham and tomato jam on grilled country white with avocado. A few light pieces of steamed yellow wax beans plus some taro chips complete the plate. Â Sounds good right? Â Tasty except for mealy, unripe tomatoes- on a BLT kinda ruins the sandy. $1.50 for two little cookies from Amy's cookies not house baked and just ok. *************** $2.50 Â HOT Chocolate with house mixed chocolate is not to be missed. Rich and dark and super chocolatey- this made up for alot. Some nice packaged goods that look like they were made in house. Â Breads are from TomCat and Orwashers- I would have preferred a local Brooklyn baker as there are so many. Â Corner space with side seating and one communal table is quite nice though the crowd particularly the Windsor Terrace toddlers were daunting.

I rarely go to restaurants that won't accept reservations since there are so many excellent restaurants that do. Â I decided to try Battersby to celebrate my friend's birthday given the restaurant's reviews and the availability of reservations when ordering the tasting menu. I have contacted the restaurant twice by email and twice by phone (recorded message since no one ever answers the phone) without a response. Â This restaurant may be the best in Brooklyn but it will never receive my business. The poor customer service exhibited by this establishment does not bode well for its' future, regardless of the quality of its food.

A FIVE?! Yes - at worst, it's a 4.5 (and please note this is based on a singular brunch experience, but given that this heaven is a block from where my best friend now lives, will probably be visiting much much more). The pair of us came here for Sunday brunch, and Astoria was well represented by this cute, hip spot, that is apparently open 24/7! For $12, you get your bottomless coffee, one of any several brunch (both breakfast and lunch) entrees (three versions of eggs benedict, fritatas, salads, burger, etc.), and your choice of brunch must beverage - mimosa/champagne/bloody mary/wine with one refill. Â  I got the eggs benedict over crab cake and was definitely not disappointed. Â The eggs were huge, perfectly poached, and the hollandaise very complementary and not at all overwhelming. Â The crab cakes - again, really couldn't get much better. Â Gorgeous slices of homestyle bread, mimosa with the fresh squeezed OJ in a generously sized flute! Am in brunch heaven? I'll admit a few things that could be improved in my book: (1) get one of those curtain thingies for that door that is going to open frequently with new customers - it helps with the wind in winter, and (2) don't pre-butter my toast - especially when you put so much -- but that's pretty much it! Other than that, everything was tops (food, service, pricing!!). I'll admit, I can be stingy with the stars, but a near perfect brunch experience at a mere $12? While that may make me appear easy to appease, let me tell you how hard it is to achieve this! Bravo Sanford's - I hope to revisit you for other meals soon enough!

YUMMM wonderful breakfast, great people there, full and make sure you use open table so you don't need to wait on a sunday. With anything from the brunch menu you are given a free drink and there is also a lunch menu with salads,burgers, etc. My friend loves the french toast there. They also have 2 types of omlettes that you can't go wrong with. She ended up getting the egg benedict which had home fries, fruit, and etc. I got the chicken sandwich after seeing another girl have it. There was roasted red peppers, pesto, chicken, wonderful bread, and TONS of amazing fries. Some of the best fries I've had. The coffee is also very good there. The portions are huge and I regret trying to finish mine..which led to an afternoon of shopping in soho and east village to walk off the food coma. The bread basket had 4 types of bread..a raisin one, french soft bread, and some crispy chiplike bread with a strawberry butter or etc? The raisin nut bread was amazing! It is a wonderful place to go with friends or family from outta town in general. I think the food came out to be about $13-15 and with tax and tip etc it was $20/person. Def worth it and I want to go again every time I'm in NYC for a sunday brunch!

I really like this place. Â The atmosphere and service are top-notch, and the promise of celebrity sightings alone may have swayed me to try this place. Â (While I didn't rub any A-list shoulders, I don't hold that against the restaurant.) Â However, the food did leave more to be desired. I started with the hamachi tartare, which was excellent - no complaints there. Â Our party also got some cheeses to share, which we asked the wait staff to recommend. Â While one was universally enjoyed, we didn't touch the other 2 much after the first bite. Â I may not be a cheese connoisseur, but I have had cheese courses that were much better. Â For my main course I had the orecchiette. While the pasta and meat were good, it was incredibly oversalted. I probably downed 5-6 glasses of water (and corresponding trips to the men's room) and still felt thirsty afterward. Â Overall, the food was a mixed bag, and it just wasn't at the level of the rest of my dinner experience.

In a neighborhood that has no short supply of Thai restaurants, Room Service is a standout. Their drunken noodle is my personal favorite - the rice noodles they use are fresh & chewy and the spicy sauce is full of basil flavor. Starting at 6.90 for an appetizer & entree, the lunch special can't be beat. Â I order from here regularly on Seamless and the food arrives in a jiffy and the entrees are still steaming hot. On occasion, the lunch appetizers may still be cold in the middle (e.g. the chicken and shrimp steamed dumpling). Â But for the cheap price, c'mon you can't really complain too much...

In a few words: trendy, sexy, a cr@p ton of liquor bottles lining the bar walls. Big red velvet curtains hide the entrance My friend suggested we meet up for cocktails on an early weeknight eve. My first impression was the exclusive title. I got there around 5:30, but the place didn't open until 6. This place literally serves to employees ONLY because 1) they aren't open during the day and 2) you must be on a yearly salary based position to dine or drink here. ($$$$). We popped in 30 minutes into opening. It was already packed! Not one seat at the bar, and it was Tuesday. This was fine with me---I thought the atmosphere and crowd gave it a very fun, and speak-easy type feeling, which I love as an appreciator of said era. Upscale, high class hipster crowd. Handle bar mustaches, Supreme hats, girls in silky work dresses in PR. Don't come if you dont have trendy glasses, read pitchfork on your Ipad3 or work at a coffee shop. Come for the mixed drinks, stay for the food, and leave for the price tab. I got the ginger smash chocktail. Absolutely delicious. Not so strong though. I was expecting more. But the actual pieces of crushed pineapple and ginger made it worth my while. So fruity they got stuck in my teeth. Â My friend and I ordered the potato gnocci portobello plate, which I severely enjoyed. Perfectly firm wheat gnocci in a really rich, buttery yet non-creamy mushroom sauce. Tender speared asparagus and real portobello steamed mushrooms also delighted the dish. It was perfect. I wanted to lick the plate. Cant wait to come back! I loved the washer's closet dÃ©cor, full of 1920's flapper photographs. And, awesome graphic design on the bar's logo.

It's a good thing that I don't live in NYC because I'd be broke from coming here all the time! A friend suggested several places to have dinner while I was visiting the city on vacation. Boy, did I ever make the right decision! We ordered the tasting menu and asked them to give each of us different dishes so that we could have a wider variety of dishes to taste. You sit watching them prepare your dishes right in front of you. We had fun trying to guess if it was our dish they were preparing. The presentation is top notch. Beautifully done to accentuate the dish's flavor. And each dish was flavorful and unique. I was happy to see a good friend and my stomach was happy with delicious food. BTW, you can pretty much walk by the place and not know it. It's an unassuming door next to or a couple doors down from a bar.

The bar is very nice and the beer selection has something for everyone. Â The food is very good but I would suggest just splitting an entree as an appetizer because it is just too overpriced. Â Upon the arrival of a large group of loud children we quickly finished our beers and took our business over to the Dram Shop.

Awesome Authentic Mexican food I havent tried everything yet but i will def be back to try more. Had no complaints about anything friendly atmosphere great food my favorite would be the spicy pork def worth a try if you havent already.

This is by far the best sushi i have every tried and i have been tried many. Not sure how their regular rolls are but their special rolls are amazing. Yellow Dragon roll is my favorite here as well as spicy tuna dumpling

This place is one of the rare gems in NYC that will have you staring at the menu for a good15 minutes. Though I no longer live in Queens, it is still a spot I frequent and crave. A crostini and panini makes the perfect lunch. And their brunch pain is are fantastic!

Very good food and the service is very nice the staff is very professional and friendly Try their pancakes and the smoke salmon platter Also everything on the breakfast menu comes with a free juice OJ or cranberry

Great rustic Italian spot located in the Greenwich hotel. Â Arrived right before dinner service began at 5:20 pm. Â So we took a look see around the hotel lobby and spa area. Â The place is really understated but very nice. Â Then we went back into the restaurant and were seated promptly at 5:30 with the rest of the Early Bird Special Crowd. Â  My fiance and I shared the blue crab crostini with apple and jalapeno. Â This was a delicious little 2 bite starter but packed with flavor. Â Then we got a full on amazing dish: LAMB MEATBALLS! Â WOW, go here just for these little wonderful balls...yes wonderful balls. Â Then we topped off this experience with the scallops which were cooked perfectly. Â  I do have to give an honorable mention to the chicken. Â This couple across from us got the chicken and we were both enthralled with the wonderful smell and portion that you get for $22 a head. Â  Well done Locanda Verde....see you again soon.

The Little Owl has a burger that has quickly moved up the ranks to #1 burger spot in my heart (and replaced the Spotted Pig burger which WAS #1). It's a true fatty pants burger. A very rich cut of ground meat - this is have it for brunch and eat lettuce for dinner kind of burger. The burger is topped with a thick slab of bacon and melted cheddar. No condiments needed. The best part of the burger scenario at Little Owl is that the bun is made of pizza dough. Had no problems getting a table for 2 at 1:00 on a Sunday.
Great Food! Great Environment! Spectacular Mac & Cheese and Amazing BBQ!
