The broth is salty and the menn (noodles) is mushy. Al dente is not just for pasta, it applies to soba too. I've been here four times and not once finished an entire bowl. However I did walk across the street to fill up on takoyaki as soon as I paid my check. All four times. If you're looking for good soba, there's a great place in SoHo that begins with the letter H. the end

For a place that seems to specializes in waffles for breakfast, I expect the waffle to be damn good. Major problems with the meal: waffle was lukewarm and it seemed like they used store-bought (?) whipped cream. Not a horrible place to grab a waffle if you're craving it, but not worth taking a trip to there specifically.
Food was good..For vegetarian there are only couple of choices unless you are picky you will be OK. However the customer service and wine selection was great!!!

food was delicious, the service was really strong and the chef came out to bring us free goodies and chat a few times throughout our meal. Â i would definitely reccomend to just about anyone. Â only caveat being that it is pretty pricey and, to be fair, it isnt the first place i would send someone in carroll gardens. Â that being said, my wife and i really enjoyed the meal and experience, we will be back.

I took a star off only because their ridiculous wait times! Visited at 2pm and 9pm on a Friday and Saturday. Both times, over 25 minutes of wait time to get take out. Annoying! Everyone was complaining. Overheard a girl say that she'd been waiting so long, she would have taken anything they had given her, at that point. However, the food? The food is worth the wait! I tried the shrimp, chicken, chick pea and cheese roll. Everything is spicy. There's no mild or medium because the proteins or veggies are already marinated. Luckily, I love spicy food so this was mild for me. The shrimp roti was the best, by faaaar. There were quite a few shrimp there, definitely didn't skimp. I wish I had ordered more than one! Chana masala (chickpea) had the authentic flavour but needed just a bit more salt. The cheese roll was decent enough, Â definitely worth a try though. Chicken tikka roll (no egg) was second best! All rolls comes with coriander chutney inside which gives it the spiciness. Unless you want more heat, no need to buy extra chutney for $0.25. Downside: small portions so you do need 2 rolls to fill you up. Masala chai tea and mango lassi are decent. I see why people can eat this stuff every day. It's perfect on the go food. A lot of south Asian people can be seen ordering, so it must be good!

Blueberry pancakes were just as delicious as everyone says they are. On weekdays, it starts getting really crowded at 9 am. (They won't seat you until your whole part is present.) I tried my friends' savory dishes and those were alright. The biscuit that comes with one of the dishes is gigantic!
My favorite neighborhood restaurant. Â Great atmosphere, awesome staff. Â  I love the wooden bar and rustic decor. Â Get the cast-iron kale and the crab bolognese. Â It's to die for.

Where do New Yorkers go when they are threatened by a fast approaching hurricane and need to do emergency grocery shopping? Â Why, the pricey and extremely crowded Eataly, obviously! I had a flight to catch Sunday night before the hurricane so I went to Eataly to grab a sandwich since there's nothing delicious to eat at the Delta Shuttle terminal. Â Eataly was a mix of frantic pasta and sausage purchasing, calm wine drinkers and workers putting stools up on bars since the place was shutting down. I stood in the panini line and ordered a cold prosciutto/cheese/balsamic jam sandwich. Â I'm telling you, that sandwich was the highlight and savior while I waited to see if my flight would actually take off (it did.) Â  Day-um that sando was good! Â It's a simple sandwich and I was afraid that the jam would soak into the bread since I waited to eat it but all ingredients were evenly flavored and complimentary of one another. Â It was $9 which was a little pricey. Â I would have liked to spend more time at Eataly but everyone was acting crazy and most of the bars were closed. Â I think one empty-handed Brit summed it up best on the way out: "I'm glad I saw it, it's a beautiful space but I think I'm going to head over to Whole Foods now."

It really takes one good place to open the path to exploring more. Before Yuca, I hated sweet plaintains, plaintains, banana you get the idea. My friend took me to yuca bar 2 years ago. I had to order the Platano Relleno, Pull pork... i just had to. It was so good from then on I love sweet plaintains. This is one of my favorite restaurants been there maybe ten or more times. I'm trying to make new friends so i can brag about this place over a plate of paella or puerquito cubano *drool*. Â I never come here to eat alone. There is so many great choices, you'll want to bring someone else along so you can eat some of theirs too. Sharing is caring, i stress this fact whenever i'm at Yuca Â one less star for the noise. I love to eat, I love to talk just as much. So thats the only downside for me.

A 24-7 (or almost so) food market by which there's a bit of seating, but food by the pound here at the buffet-style tables where you can get whatever you feel like eating. Pre-packaged meals to the side and back, and also a few drinks in a cooler to the side. Good for a snack or a lunch pack to go, but if you're in the mood for hotter (temperature) food or freshly done food, look elsewheres.
Food here in new york is different from California i just miss latin food from new York not the same here in sac

Great service, didn't have to wait to long during lunchtime. Â Lots of locals, always a good sign. Â The waffles were just okay, I was hoping they would be a little sweeter without dousing them in maple syrup. Â The half and half was frighteningly sweet so I would just share it with someone. Â The staff was very polite and gave us lots of to go boxes for our leftovers. Â Service can be slow, our food came out right away but the tables who came after us waited a pretty long time. Â Portions are huge, I would definitely recommend getting the fried chicken meal since it comes with two sides which are usually $4.50 extra each. Â I also enjoyed the layout of the restaurant, feels like a secret hideout!

Bogota, I've had it up to HERE with you. Your food is excellent, but your service is shit. If I make a reservation I don't expect to wait an hour while the hostess makes 2001 excuses. How about, Sorry this really sucks! Here are some drinks while you wait AN HOUR FOR YOUR TABLE. Not rolling your eyes at me and saying you "want to say it's going to be 15 more minutes" every time I ask. Or if I come for brunch I don't think it should take a server 20 minutes to even notice that five of us are seated at her table. There shouldn't be disparities in when the food comes for large groups. Get your act together. Your food is, as I heard one woman say when she was told there was an hour wait (and she didn't have a reservation -- I did and waited that long), fucking phenomenal. But I can't stand for the service and the lack of acknowledgment that your service sucks has me at the end of my rope. It will be awhile before I come back.

Awesome spin on home cooking! Portions will definitely NOT let you down. Â I've been here twice now, and both times everything has been excellent. Â Dishes of note: bowl of mussels (gigantic - see my photo); chicken and pancakes (has bacon...mmmm... and the syrup is divine); and the beer floats for dessert. Did I mention it's a $h!T load of food?

Ordered a small pizza... verdict: it was OK. I can say I've had better pizza and I can say I've had much worse pizza. The middle of the pizza was very soggy and had no stability, which is a major letdown for me when it comes to my pizza but the pepperoni was probably the best I've ever had, super fresh and crispy. Overall, I think the hype of the place is what makes it a staple in Brooklyn, rather than actually having really good pizza. I'm wondering now if I made a huge mistake, by not stopping next door and grabbing a pie at Juliana's instead. I guess I know for next time. Notes: ONLY SELL PIES, NO SLICES! CASH ONLY!

went here for dinner on a saturday night. the happy hour for drinks only consist of one special cocktail (which was described as medicinal - my mistake for ordering it even after that) and 1 beer (palm ale). the oysters are $1 on sat from 2-8pm but they're not good, not bad. the best thing about our dinner was the small plates which we got 5 of for $30 (2 cheese, 1 meat, 2 appetizers). we have the stemmed mushroom crostini and the asparagus crostini, which were probably the best thing there. i was very disappointed with my entree. i ordered the tagliatelle and it was one of the smallest pasta dishes i've ever seen. i don't expect a large dish but this was smaller than average so i was left unsatisfied. on top of that, most of my sugar snap peas were not fully cooked so i couldn't eat those. lastly we had the bread pudding. this was dense but because they made a mistake on our order, we were comped for it so i guess i can't complain? overall, the food isn't bad but it isn't great. it's fair but i would not go back considering the prices were more expensive than should have been for the quality. the wait staff was nice though.

Very Good Burgers They make a good burger that about as good as In-N-Out. The meat is still a little pink. The thousand island dressing makes the burger complete. It's not as good a steak burger at Steak & Shake though, because it doesn't have the crispy crust surrounding the juicy meat. The custard ice cream was very rich, therefore delicious. A single was enough for me. The store was packed despite having a shorter line than most. While I wouldn't wait in line for 20 minutes to have this, I wouldn't mind getting it again. I also like that they sell wine.

One of my favorite bars. Definitely not for the faint of heart. Everyone has an average of 3 tattoos. They serve free cheeseballs and twizzlers. Ask for the fresh-squeezed margaritas! They're to die for

Loved it! It's a cute place that's both an Italian market and a collection of restaurants. We went to "la pizza and la pasta". Very very good food- the fresh pasta with lamb shank ragu was soo fresh and delicious. My friend got the gnocchi which omg was so light and fluffy and the truffle sauce was so rich and aromatic. We also got the sauvignon blanc which is very smooth and refreshing. def a must go! And all the deserts look so good but the gelato is amazing and a little expensive.

This could be the best restaurant in the west village. My girlfriend and I have been unable to get in here because it is packed every sunday night. Â We finally made a reservation and it was definitely worth the wait. The place is very cute and straightforward. Â It is a family owned and operated joint that you can get some excellent red-sauce style Italian dishes. Â The garlic bread was superb, hot and fresh. Â The mozzarella was way better than in most places in the area. Â As far as mains we got: fettuccine bolognese, chicken parmigiana, linguini with olive oil and garlic, and shrimp fra diavolo. Â We were only four people but we literally devoured everything and even had to ask for a second helping of linguini. Â This was not because the dishes were small by any means. Â Everything was so good we had to try dessert. Had a cannoli and chocolate cake and it was worth feeling absolutely stuffed and having to unbutton my pants. Also - this place gets extra points because it was someone's birthday and they hit the lights and played a birthday song. Â The whole place was into it and clapping. Â That might not be your cup of tea but we really had fun. Â  Don't sleep!

Eggs benedict over short rib hash? AMAZING! Rarely is such a good meat made into hash. The hot chocolate is pretty good too. Everything tastes amazing, and the prices are not bad either. Except the drinks. A small hot chocolate, however good, is quite pricey - $5. The servers are amazing. One of my friends complained that she never got pumpkin pie over Thanksgiving, and when I mentioned it wasn't on the menu, a server passed by and said that it was available! Yay!

Food was good, friendly service, accepts credit card, outdoor seating available. Had the: 1) Pork adobo over rice- flavorful, tender meat, but on the salty side. 2) Lumpiang shanghai - springrolls - a MUST get appetitzer. 3) Pancit canton - DO NOT recommend. Noodle dish with choice of meat or vege. The noodles had a very artificial taste, the shrimp was the pre-packaged frozen food type.

To be honest, right now, not a huge fan of Mediterranean cuisine. Â (Maybe I've had it too much lately) Â Overall, I really enjoyed this place. Â We were in the upstairs dining area which was not really crowded and though noisy, it didn't have any issues with having to shout to be heard, we could carry on normal conversation without raising our voices. We were here with a group of 7 people and they were able to seat us with only 3 people that arrived. Â We ordered and shared several mezes, a salad, and two entrees. Â Everything was fresh, properly seasoned/dressed and flavors were all well-balanced and harmonious. Â Probably one of the best experiences for this style of food. Â  I LOVE cacik and their rendition was quite good. Â We also had the calf liver and a few other standard meze. The donner kebab wasn't as intricately spiced as some of the better ones I had but it was still very good. Â The chicken was also quite good. Â  I have to agree with other reviewers that the rice pilaf they include was top-notch. Â  The desserts... all of them were good. Â One of the few places where they got the baklava right! Â Not too sweet, plenty of pistachio flavor. Nevermind the strange name, they've got good food in a good lively atmosphere and good service at a good reasonable price. Â I want to rename it Beyogood.

This place is and always was one of my favorites. I read through the reviews, especially the bad ones and would just like to add my two cents: 1. Risotto is supposed to be served al dente. The wonderful thing about this place is how authentically Italian it is from the quality of the ingredients to the way they are prepared and paired. Â  2. You can choose gluten free or not. I started eating at Risotteria long before they served gluten-free alternatives. Whether or not you have gluten issues, you should try this place because the food is delicious! 3. Yes, the main attraction is the risotto, but their pannini are wonderful. Again, the best ingredients and put together in a truly authentically Italian manner. For example, they slice their meat to order- not at the beginning of the shift. They are extremely detail oriented. This spells quality! 4. If you had a bad experience with a waiter, that's too bad, but not a reason to stay away. Waiters come and go. To me, a much better indication of the quality of a restaurant is the kitchen staff. From the beginning, this place has had many of the same guys in their kitchen. That speaks volumes in a city where kitchen staffs change as often as baby diapers!
it's just really, really, really, really, really, really good ramen. (and with no line, large dining spaces, and real japanese servers, it was a step up from the ippudo visited in tokyo!)
It's consistently good but the quantity decreased and the priced increased.

We were trying to decide what to do for our anniversary dinner. We looked all over and decided to stay local. Â  After reading many of the yelp reviews we made a 9:30 reservation. Took about 30 minutes to get a seat. Well worth the wait. The atmosphere was great. The service amazing, and the food out of this world. Â  Don't miss out on this place. An absolute gem!

So good! Casual but with terrific, polite, friendly service. Food is super good: spatzle, sausages but also lighter fare like the awesome beet salad and herring appetizer. Â Deserts are amazing but change so often that I am afraid to get too attached to any one dish. Such a great addition to the neighborhood.

Prompted to come to their Soho location because during Googa Mooga I tried their amazing fried chicken. Â And it only tastes better in their store. Â Its a great date night spot as well as the ambiance is very intimate. Â We were lucky to walk in on a Saturday night without any wait. Â  We started with an order of the Kushi oysters which were delicious accompanied by an assortment of sauces sure to please all different palettes. Definitely order the fried chicken, the skin is perfect and you can dip it with the honey. We also tried the lobster dish which they can deshell for you in the kitchen. The lobster comes with a side of corn. Will definitely be back for more of that fried chicken (And I'm not even a fan of fried chicken)!

It's like a Chipotle, but with potatoes. If you think the pictures look amazing, it's even better in person. The mashed potatoes, homemade chips and sweet potato fries are the best in my opinion. What you put on them is your discretion, but whatever you do, DON'T SKIP OUT ON THE SAUCES. Deciding which sauce is the hardest choice you'll have to make while you're there...choose wisely. (The Garlic Aioli, Parmo and Truffle are my favorite) Apart from the amazing potatoes, the staff is always super friendly and energetic.

So good. So fresh. Somehow 5 people managed to eat 3 large pizza's... and we were all on "diets." I thought I was waiting in line at an amusement park. As frustrating as it may be, bring someone ahead of time to hold your hand and make sure you don't leave and remember me saying it's so worth the wait. This sign there says something like we are not responsible if you choke on seeds or pits? I thought this was a joke. That's the greeting I get after standing here like a jack a$$ all day? I'll translate it ahead of time.... OUR INGREDIENTS ARE SO FRESH THE PITS ARE STILL IN OUR OLIVES. Fresh mozzarella like you've never had before. That sign has really put a damper on all my other pizza experiences because now I search and search for it and understand why no where else can get away with it.
Love this place! Great italian food, nice and warm atmosphere & people.

I'll try not to be biased, but boy was this place a huge disappointment and I'm not hard to please. I gave it 2 stars instead of 1 just in case of partial ignorance lol. This place is small, and by small, I mean tiny. If you wanna come here, make a reservation for sure if you can. Walked in and was asked if I had a reservation. I replied no at which point they said "ok, please wait over there." There, being the 3' x 3' waiting area at the entrance where there is hardly any room to "wait" as it was way too cold to be standing outside. It's like a human puzzle game when other people are entering/exiting as you have to shift to just the right positions to allow movement due to how their doors open and close and how confined it was. In addition, when they told us the waiting time we inquired about if we needed to put our names down on a list. The answer was no and that we have to be there at the time they think they will have seats available. Mind you, there were several empty tables which we ended up waiting for to sit at in the end anyway. On to the food.... What we ordered: Monkfish Liver - this was surprisingly pretty good. It's garnished with thinly sliced pork collagen (i think), scallion and black colored roe (don't know from what) in a mildly sweet sauce. Without the garnishes, the liver had a taste resembling that of tuna fish. This wasn't the case the other times I have tried this else where but I enjoyed it despite not normally liking items like this. Atlantic Salmon Carpaccio - Â hard to describe the flavors because I can't recall all the ingredients but it was fairly light and appetizing overall. About 8 pieces of salmon with the larger roe eggs atop each, marinating in a puddle of the dressing. No complaints here. Snow Crab Croquette - wasn't really sure what to expect with this one but I wasn't a fan. It had a nice crispy outer layer which tasted pretty good but past that it was downhill. The inside filling resembled watery mash potatoes and had a mild sweetness to it. I don't know if it was my taste buds but I was wondering where the "crab" part of this dish came into play as I tasted nothing close to that. Hakata Tonton Hotpot - this was the biggest disappoint of all. Maybe I wasn't prepared for what to expect but this was certainly nothing close to what I imagined for a hotpot. I was starving and this version consisted of 90% cabbage and chives, 1 maybe 2? dumplings, 1 or 2 slices of pork sirloin, a couple pieces of tofu and a few pieces of pork belly and tonsoku. If you love cabbage and chives then this is the dish for you because that is what you will be filling up on lol. It got old very fast. The broth was pretty good with a bit of spice to it though, i'll give it that. Had to order several more additional meats to get any where close to being fully satisfied. Service was ok. They tend to you well, when they find the time to do so. They will pour your drinks when they see a glass any less than full and assist you in prepping your hotpot. They'll even scoop it into the bowls for you. I'm sure some of their other dishes may be fantastic but from my experience, I doubt I would come here again. Or at the least, not have a high expectation in terms of their hotpot.

It's easy to get hung up on the Korean or not-Korean delineation of Jungsik; I'd say that it's definitely more of a French restaurant with some Korean influence. The food was mostly good, but the ones that didn't impress were heavily sauced and left us bloated/rolling out the door. Fried oyster: Certainly interesting due to the black crust, though the aioli was a bit heavy. Recommended if you're into oysters (sadly I am not). Sea urchin: YUM! (If you like sea urchin.) The flavors basically imitated that of a sea urchin sushi, with the seaweed and rice flavors. Anyway it was delicious. Royal bibimbap: Obviously very rich and filling, what with the truffles and risotto. Couldn't eat more than a couple of bites, but it was okay. Crispy red snapper: Tasted great with the salsa. Very refreshing! Tribeca lobster: Two hunks of perfectly extracted lobster meat, yum. The downside was that it was drowning in this unnecessary pool of sauce -- would've been better with just a few dribbles of the sauce to let the actual lobster shine. Galbi: Loved the sweet, marinated Korean flavors. Meat was quite tender, though we were already stuffed by this course and couldn't finish it all! Duck: The most disappointing dish. Flavors were just flat and unmemorable. Sweet potato tart: I was so determined to get this (even though we were about to explode) because it sounded intriguing and I love sweet potato. It turned out to be a very interesting long, rectangular thing with little balls of candied sweet potato on top. The tart itself was somewhat mediocre (crust had no flavor at all) but the presentation was cute and I enjoyed the milk sherbet.

Hm...not sure what all the hype is about. =/ Maybe I had too high of expectations, but I thought the ramen was average and overpriced. We came here on a Wednesday for lunch around 12:30pm and thankfully there was no wait and we were seated immediately at a communal table (I honestly can't imagine waiting 2+ hours for this!) Akamaru Modern ($14 + $4 for Braised Pork Belly + $2 for soft boiled egg): This is the original silky "Tonkotsu" (pork) soup noodles topped with Ippudo's secret "Umami Dama" miso paste, pork chasu, cabbage, sesame Â kikuarage mushrooms, scallions, and garlic oil. With all the additional items I got, the grand total was $20 for a bowl of ramen...the most expensive bowl of ramen I've had, but definitely not the best. I liked the noodles and the broth (flavorful and not too oily) but it wasn't anything amazing. The most disappointing part was the meat. The pork chasu slices were way too tough and dry. Also, why did I only get 3 very small pieces of braised pork belly when I paid 4 extra dollars for it?? They were also pretty tough and did not melt in my mouth like how normal pork belly should. I also got the ramen with the lunch special (which includes a side salad and chasu bowl) for an extra $3. The salad was literally like 5 pieces of leaves...at least the dressing was good I guess....The chasu bowl was not impressive and came with a lot of rice and not a lot of meat. Â  Overall, I liked the trendy ambiance and the service was great, but the ramen was just average... I'm glad I got to try this place, but unfortunately I won't be back.
Very good food , and relaxing vibe . I love their shawarma plate , very authentic . Will defiantly come again.

Great place to have a group dinners (6-8 people). I highly recommend getting a soup, which I rarely do when eating out. The soups have a lovely spicy & sour broth. There was plenty of starter mini-dishes too, which is common at most Korean restaurants.

While I haven't been to the restaurant proper, I did get to eat Roberta's pizza at their booth at Madison Square Eats when I was visiting a friend in NYC. The beesting pizza may be the best pizza I have ever eaten in my life and that is NO small feat to accomplish. Drizzled with honey, chili oil and red pepper flakes over the fresh mozzarella and soppressata, I swear this is the most surprising yet delectable combinations of flavors you'll ever find on a pizza. This pizza is honestly a good reason to move to NYC in itself. Â Can't wait to go back specifically to try their other pizzas!

Outstanding! Â The food will absolutely not disappoint - tasting menu plus wine pairing was $260 pp so it's a splurge.... But I can now say I've had the best meal of my life... Â Waygu tartar, truffle risotto.... Amazing!!!! And - visit the bathroom - Japanese style toilets are delightful - haha

I came here for the 3rd time and it was terrific like my first two visits. I always get the Rev. Al Sharpton-- chicken and waffles (fried) I went there in the afternoon and I was full for the ENTIRE day. I only had to eat that one meal! The sweet iced tea is delicious and i finally tried the mac and cheese today. Pretty yummy!! The service is quick, the staff is friendly, and the food is fabulous! Â The only downfall is that sometimes there is a line, but it's worth the wait!! :-) It's super close to the 2 and 3 line, so it's convenient to get there! There's no excuse not to go, so definitely give it a try!!

Fantastic! I see I'm not the only one transplanted from the Bay Area looking for some good comida mexicana. I walked by this place yesterday, saw tacos on the menu, and decided I'd give it a try. Had a great chat with the owner, who is actually from the Bay Area and wanted to bring good Mexican food to New York. Two soft tacos with carne asada were some of the best I've ever had. They come with salsa (freshly made), cheese (melted onto the tortilla), sour cream (out of a squirt bottle, so not chunky), and hot sauce (not too hot, green chiles). Guacamole (also freshly made) is $1 extra, but definitely necessary and totally worth it. I wish the carne asada had been cut into smaller pieces, but it was still tender and flavorful. Went back today and had one soft taco with carnitas, also amazing and tender. I love that the tortillas are steamed and the cheese is already melted into the taco. Tacos were well wrapped so that everything didn't fall out the back. You can see tons of people in back preparing meats and other things, so it's obviously fresh, and Dos Toros is also environmentally friendly with their silverware and cups, both biodegradable. Overall, very friendly staff, AWESOME prices, and delicious Mexican food. I'm already a regular customer!

Like many other hyped New York pizza places, this one simply fails to deliver. Â Crust was okay but the cheese to sauce ratio was a little off. Â Overall the pie was tasteless and bland. Â I enjoyed the space and setting and appreciated the history but in the end it was simply not that good. Â That being said be sure and try is for yourselves. Â I might have been there when they were having an off day and have not been back. Â I would probably give it another go but am rarely in the area.

I am not sure what took us so long to find this place but we finally decided to try Peppino's after living in the neighborhood for almost two years. I could kick myself now that I know what we have been missing. They have perfected the pizza here. There is no comparison with other pizza by the slice joints in the area. The wood burning, brick oven makes all the difference. The pizza was fantastic but more than that, the service was above and beyond. Our server, Vito, was such a sweet guy!!! I never realized since we headed home after our meal but I left my wallet at Peppino's. It was hand delivered to our door by an employee at Peppino's. Everything was in it's place. Thank you so much Peppino's. You have two more loyal customers!
What an amazing meal! Â You just don't get better than this in NYC.

AMAZING margaritas, yummy food, adequate service, ridiculously snobby staff. Â Also, they brought my table of 7 the check about 1 hr 45 min into our meal and told us the wait list was too long and we had to leave. Â Don't think I'll go back unless it's to sit at the bar.

My husband and I finally got a chance to try SONG. The plus: Portions- were huge- & we got a big bank for the buck. The cons: In their pad thai- had virtually nothing other than noodles in it. Â No eggs, vegs, or peanuts to speak of.. but it was really crazy busy so perhaps we will stop again. Curries- good- not overly sweet, which I hate in Thai food. Fried Calamari- eh- ok- not light & crisp, but rather heavy and doughy,. So unsure- I'd have to try again, but I'd probably check out somewhere else first. Loud- really loud-, but I expect that @ dinner time in most NYC restaurants.

Everything about this place is great. Â The only reason I did not give it 5 stars is because of the wait times of an hour or more, but you know what, it's worth it. The tapas are Â make my mouth water as I write this. Â The atmosphere is cozy Â and tight with a great young crowd. Highly recommend this diamond in the rough!!!!

Pros: The food here is really good. We ordered the Fettuccini Provencale & the Parisienne crepe for our entrees. Oh & they're absolutely delicious! As for our dessert, we got the sweet crepes (Suzette & Belle Helene) & oh my God, they're so fantastic! The service was great. Friendly waiter. The place was pretty cozy. We like the decor. Very homey feeling. Great outdoor seating! Two entrees & two desserts, we spent about $40. Cons: Now this is a tough one. We really can't think of anything bad about this place other than maybe a bigger portion? Just stop by at this place. You won't be disappointed. Definitely will put a smile on your face... Â  =D

Great pizza, pitchers of beer, but go for lunch. Â This place was overcrowded with tourists and kids at 9:00pm on a Saturday. Â I know, bad time to go anywhere, but I think its more of a lunchtime place.

The ambiance within this place is great and the food is excellent! The courses that I tried had many spices and were very flavorful; they gave a kick to Thai food. One thing that I was unsatisfied with was the lighting. It was way too dark and I saw several people using the light on their phones to look at the menu. Other than that, I am very pleased about the food and decent price of the place.

In the last two years, I've probably been to Verlaine's about 20-30 times. Â Its one of those places where you just can't go wrong. Â For starters, happy hour Â is until 10pm every Â night! The happy hour drink menu, although not super extensive, is pretty good and you can't go wrong with their signature Lychee martinis. Â Not the strongest drinks in the world but if you have enough they can take you to your "happy place". Â They also serve a nice assortment of asian fusion tapas. Â Personally I've tried the shrimp, chicken dumplings, chicken satay, and ginger wings and all were seasoned well and flavorful. Â Not to mention the food comes out fairly quickly and is always hot. Â  For a LES bar it isn't as divey as you would expect (although I would hate to see it in natural light) and while itts definitely not a fancy bar its a step above some of the other grungier bars in the area. Â  Be warned - it gets VERY crowded as people filter in for drinks after happy hour at other bars has ended. Â There is pretty much one hostess who also waits tables but somehow she manages to turn tables and make sure you get seated. Â Service isn't stellar but they get the Â job done. Â There is a DJ who plays decent music and although it can be a little loud at times, its not unbearable. All in all, if you're looking for a happy hour bar where you can eat, drink and be Â merry, Verlaine is definitely a good option!

SOLID casual taqueria w/ a super sweet staff that always enhances my experience!! i've always ordered the $2.95 tacos so i can try the variety of meat fillings! FISH, SHRIMP, & CARNITAS are my favorite so far. FYI tacos are served on corn tortillas ---fish taco (ensenada style): YUM.. hot & crispy the first time i had it but not as crispy the 2nd & 3rd time around ---shrimp taco: spicy! they don't use quality shrimp but I overlook that fact because it's so flavorful! ---carnitas taco: delicious w/ a nice char & served w/ guacamole! ---al pastor: odd this one is served w/ pineapple.... SKIP ---vegetarian taco: nothing to rave about but it has corn LOVE the spicy habanero sauce & green tomatillo sauce they bring to the table with your food! NOTE: use the belly loyalty program to get free chips after 2 check-ins & yelp check-in gets you a free jarritos & free mexican gum at the door Thanks PayPal app for the freebies!

This little restaurant is worthy of its acclaim. The food is great, the prices are more than fair, and the staff is welcoming. As I work nearby, I was happy that the positive reviews on yelp were not unfounded. I had the pork belly sandwich, which was tender, salty, and sweet; pickled onions added a nice tartness, and a runny egg put it over the top. It was generous, with two thick slices of pork belly. I also had the signature Breakroom fries that should be experienced rather than described, but I'll try. Addictive. Almost a meal in itself. The apotheosis of overkill gone right. What's not to like? Runny Egg? GOOD. Cheese? GOOD. Bacon? GOOD. Pork Belly? GOOD. Oh, and there are crispy fries somewhere under there. Will be returning soon to try a burger (I was coveting the Breakroom burger next to me). Keep up the great food!

I am really torn as I write this review. On one hand, I see many of my fellow Yelp friends and Elites gushing about this place. On the other hand, I just did not think the meatballs were all that amazing as most everyone here describes. So please don't attack me with pitchforks and other blunt instruments when I say this - OVER HYPED!!!! Maybe my taste buds for meatballs are spoiled because I have an Italian mom who cooked the most amazing meatballs. My grandma and sister are just as good if even better. I always ate great tasting meatballs the way they should be made, simmering in a pot of wonderful sauce all day on a low flame, and sneaking into the kitchen to swipe one on a fork. Those were the days. I mean, don't get me wrong, Meatball Shop's balls were ok, but not worthy of five star ratings. Just good. I dropped in here for lunch and was lucky enough to grab a spot at the bar after a ten minute wait. The place itself is small and cramped, and you can wait a long time for a seat if there are two or more of you. Service was ok, but not overly attentive. Not once did anyone ask me if I was ok, or if my meal was good. It does have a nice down home type decor, with old pictures and tools hanging on the walls, and a pretty nice wine selection in view. A few beers on tap too including PBR and Sixpoint. I ordered the special meatball of the day for my meal. Today it was the steak, bacon, and cheddar ball with a mushroom sauce. Also had a side house salad and mint lemonade. To me the meatballs had little taste and the sauce was bland. There was no "oomph" in this plate or anything that made it stand out. Sure, it has a nice presentation in the bowl topped with a thin bread slice, but I did not experience the flavor explosion that so many here have raved about. Plus, the portion is on the small side. The salad was covered in a guacamole type dressing and also had kernels of corn in it. The greens were fresh and crispy, but were overpowered by an overabundance of dressing poured all over it. The dressing was tasty, and had chunks of guacamole in it, but it was too much overkill. The mint lemonade was a nice cool refreshing drink on a humid day. Cost for all this came out to $14 before tax and tip, so it is not too pricey. Again, I just feel that this place is a bit over hyped. It's not bad, but definitely not all that fantastic either. Maybe I have to come back here again and try something else. I don't know. Maybe I am just one of the lucky ones who know what fantastic meatballs should taste like since I grew up eating them. 3.5 stars is what I would give this place if I could.

I was very excited when I heard from my fried that BCD tofu house in Manhattan was going to reopen soon. I have been waiting for long and finally I and my friend came around 11pm on Friday. I was so surprised cuz there were still a lot of people at that late night. The interior was bright, which I loved, and it was clean. I ordered PORK SOON TOFU. It was spicy but very delicious. I like pork soon tofu so much but I never tasted like this delicious before. Also, there was fried fish came with other side dishes. Wow! I loved it. I just became a big fan of BCD. Waitresses were nice but I couldn't get good service at the beginning cuz too many people. Â but the manager came and listened & accepted all my complains. He redirected them and they just came and apologized. They brought additional side dishes and checked on us Â often if we need something. Delicious food, excellent service, clean and well organized interior! I just liked to come again soon. I strongly recommend you to come and enjoy delicious food here. You will love it. Had a really, really great dinner here. 4.5 stars. Went w/wife and another couple. The portions are small, but our waitress was helpful in mentioning that up front and helping us determine the size of our order. We started with a homemade ricotta, which came w/a fig jam and olive oil. Light and delicious. A great start. For the second portion, we ordered about 6 dishes. This included the scallops w/sea salt (good but too small a portion for 4), escarole salad (really good), potato gnocchi (which was a split vote...I loved, 2 others not a favorite), garganelli w/a mushroom ragu (excellent). My personal favorite here was a roasted mushroom dish with fried egg, ricotta and pancetta. Could have had a few portions of just that and gone home a very happy man. We all each ordered a meat/fish course individually. Two went for the Branzino, which seemed great, I went for the Tagliatelle bologense (white), which was fantastic. Not sure I was ready for another pasta, but glad I went for it. My wife ordered the hangar steak w/crispy potatoes. To me, this was the only semi-miss dish. She asked for it medium rare, and a good portion of it was rare/B&B. Tasted fine, but with so much outrageous steak in the city, you have to bring it a little stronger. A note about a good portion of the dishes at L'Artusi is that they are covered in cheese. This includes the mushroom dish, the brussel sprouts, all pastas. If you are not down, or have lactose issues, something to note before you order. Finished w/the gelati (serviceable), olive oil cake (good) and dark chocolate terrine (very good) along w/ a very fine cup of coffee. All of this, along with two moderately priced bottles of Piedmont, came to about $200 a couple all in. For the quality food, scene, and service, a great dining experience in NYC. Right now, L'Artusi and Convivio are my two favorite Italian restaurants in NYC.

Extremely fresh, home-made pasta and yummy desserts. Great spot for a date or dinner with family. I had the Fettuccine Di Zafferano and loved it - perfect ratio of veggies and sauce to pasta. The waitress was very attentive and friendly, and was happy to make suggestions/answer questions. She even let my mom make a small change to her meal despite the menu advising against it! ;) The manager asked us about our visit and thanked us for coming as we were leaving -- nice touch.

Nice atmosphere, Staff is really nice, fast and helpful Reasonably priced. Food is ok, not outstanding but good. Four stars becasue the drinks were actually pretty good (Otherwise for the food would go to three stars)

Authentic Japanese curry with fairly large portions. They have great curry and katsu but thats pretty much all the choices you have. I definitely make this place one of my stops when I go to New York.

I like being able to sit outside and the Rose Water has nice patio seating. The menu with the food/wine pairings was very well done and was also a good value. Service was very good with a minute taken with each wine to explain it without a long essay. I will go there again.

Been there a couple of times. Food pretty good, but the noise is eardrum-piercing loud, to the point of pain. Could NOT have even a perfunctory conversation, could NOT hear my tablemates. Ouch. Â (Try Hibino up Henry Street instead for great food, great service, and a warm but serene ambiance for a conversation with friends.)

I was a bit skeptical when I told my friend I wanted to get some tea, and he made me go to this place. I was like "what's the point of paying so much for tea, I could just go to Starbucks"...but it's worth it! :) They have a variety of teas to choose from. I honestly can't even recall the tea that I ordered (so many different names, and I am definitely not a tea-connoisseur) However, they bring your cup of tea (of course) and then a pot of the tea.. So I guess it's worth the 5 or more bucks that you spend on it! The place itself is really cute! I loved the bathrooms...so high tech! I guess it's the Japanese techy-part of it! :) There are private rooms that you can get for like 20-40 a person, depending if you want food or just dessert, which I think would be so awesome to utilize if you want a really romantic date! I like this place, and will be back!
Just OK place. Nothing memorable. Didn't think the restaurant week price was a great deal for the average price of a dish in this restaurant.

The ambiance was magic. The outdoor space in particular is really special. The food. Excellent. Flavorful. Well prepared. Thoughtfully plated. The tuna ceviche and patatas bravas were particular standouts. The combination of food, ambiance and service makes this restaurant a success. It

Oh, park slope you're like the super nice guy i never went out with but I am always reminded how great you are when we have that once a year run in at a party. Went to Pur Bird for lunch w a friend and being a new place we took it upon ourselves to order as much as possible to get the full effect. Portions are perfect for splitting, so keep that in mind. Plus, price point is around 6 bucks so if you order 3 things you're pretty gold and makes it about 10 bucks per head. We had the JalapeÃ±o infused mash potatoes...shut your dirty mouth they were tasty....also, the home made chicken soup, great as well, and not too salty. My favorite hands down was the mac and cheese. I loved that it had thick cheese on top but underneath was my favorite runny almost soupy cheese....YES PLEASE. We also had the chicken pot pie, which I really didn't care for, but I generally don't like pot pies anyway. It was more like a hot pocket pot pie though. The counter staff was AMAZING, Super sweet and checking in on how we liked the food-love that about a new place....it's always smart to make an effort and take notice of the customer. The place was clean and plenty of seating. Also love that you don't have to bother with a waiter aka no BS or tip to deal with. And they take Credit card. It's great food for a cold day!
The best pizza I've had in a very long time. Really friendly staff. Romantic setting. Going back tonight. 5 stars if it had a liquor license!

I live around the corner, as well, and and have never written a Yelp review, but just feel compelled to say how in love with this place I am! From the ambiance (just what the upper UES needs) to the service to the food (fresh baked bread, homemade pastas, etc.) this place combines big-restaurant feel -- aka a place you could feel comfortable to go for a drink with your iPad or a first date -- with high quality and a neighborhoody feel. Also, a mix of ages -- very sophisticated, hip, yet not uptight (but not the Penrose crowd, which has started to feel fratty). I have now been twice (including tonight), and am planning a third expedition tomorrow eve! Can't wait till they start serving brunch on January 25th, 2014.
This place is absolutely awesome! So chill. The eggs are great. People working are really nice. I'll be back :)

How can a place name Bubby's (Jewish for grandmother) have it's menu literally packed with bacon and pork?? Poor Bubby is spinning in her grave. Even the freeking biscuits have bacon fat in them, for christ's sake! It looks as if management decided, "wow, lets make the menu southern comfort food" (perhaps they mistook BUBBY for BUBBA?) and then got a guy (maybe a car mechanic?) from Jersey to cook it. My friend this stuff is simply awful! My husband said the food was so greasy he could not eat it. I ordered fried chicken, green beans and mac/cheese (only veggies that did not contain bacon or pork fat.). If you guys wanna go southern, then at least learn to make the dishes. This was AWFUL! Modern Southern cuisine has nixed the pork grease for flavour. The chicken was a favourless, greasy mess. No herbs, no spice... just greasy crunch... and EXTREMELY salty. They brag about brining (really called Koshering) the chicken; guess they don't do a second soaking in plain water, as you should (before preparing) to remove excess salt. The atmosphere is so loud we could not have a conversation without shouting across the table. The beer was warm, so was the water they brought on a 95 degree day. When I asked for ice, they offered to get me a iced lemonade at 5 bucks (!!) a glass. I know they have a captive audience down there in Tribeca. But I gotta tell you this place sucks so badly, I'd walk needed blocks in the 95 degree heat (or freezing cold) to find something else.

I grew up in San Diego, so I'd like to think I know a thing or 2 about Mexican food! Nothing on the east coast can compare to SD or Texas Mex, but Los Tacos is pretty dang amazing. I had the cactus taco and chicken. So Yumm. Their drinks are pretty amazing too. I was stoked to see Tamarindo Â (water infused with tamarind), a San Diego taco shack staple.

This rating is mostly based on the food. The ambience is comfy and relaxing; a good place to grab a drink and then go. The food is very bland - pretty mediocre overall. I came here for the $5.95 lunch special (sounded like a great deal!) and ordered the cheese/jalapeno tamale and chicken taco...nothing seemed very seasoned and there was a complete lack of spice throughout each item. My boyfriend tried the quesadilla which was deep fried (odd) and oily. Margaritas are tasty but can't really taste the booze in it; maybe that's a good thing? You be the judge.

Tutto Ramen v. Ippudo Or so it seems - the main ramen rivalry! And my friend picked Tutto Ramen. Why? "The noodles don't get soggy as quick!" How quick? I didn't ask - I was too busy eating their addicting char siu pork with the ramen. Oh, and by the way, get extra pork. It's really so good, and the ramen too. Best I've ever had, to date! And I'm not so sure if I can find better - their noodles are just ... firm, thick, strong, good-looking, mouth-drooling... Remember, I'm talking about them tasty noodles. They're SOOO GOOD! TIPS: - Go on an off-hour. During peak hours, you may have to wait an hour for a seat. And they don't take reservations.

I first discovered this gem of a restaurant in March '11. Fast forward to my next trip to NYC, and I decided I just HAD to return. Yes, it lived up to all my expectations. Liverwurst platter, beer, austrian meatballs, mmmmmmmmmm. Very affordably priced.

Paprika, you are my Manhattan version of Brucie, Noodle Pudding, and Fragole put together. Â Affordable. Â Cute. Â Homemade pastas. Â Good wine list. Â I truly do consider Paprika to be among the best Italian places in Manhattan. Â If you want your scene and have a penchant for overrated pasta, go to Osteria Morini. Â But if you want pasta that is honestly better without the frills, Paprika is your place. I had a veal ragu pasta that was a daily special. Â The pasta was absolutely delicious and definitely had the whole "homemade" taste to it. Â And veal ragu? Â Well what's not to love? Â It reminded me a lot of the ragu that I would get at Fragole. Â Mmmm. Â The bistecca or steak or whatever was on the menu (I forgot) was also very delicious. Â  I will definitely return here when I'm looking for an Italian place in the East Village.

When we arrived there we discovered that we had to order in one place and then bring the food to the dining room next door. That could be a cool concept if the dining room is nice and has a killer view, like many of the seafood shacks in Cape Cod. Red Hook Lobster Pond has a fairly small cafeteria style dining room with long wooden picnic tables and benches. The only windows are by the entrance leading to the street outside. No veranda, no garden, no backyard, no water view. Just a very loud, cavernous dining room. The place where orders are taken is also very loud. The cashier kept asking us to repeat ourselves and still left something off the order. The prices are pretty high for a semi-self-service place. Full service places in Sheepshead Bay have comparable prices. So, I don't get why this place is so popular. The food is decent, I must say. The lobster is super fresh! We ordered a lobster bisque, which was tasty but very spicy -- something that the menu does not mention. The lobster rolls were really tiny. The one called Cape Cod didn't really taste like the ones we had in Cape Cod, and we had many. It was almost unseasoned. However, the other rolls were quite delicious. All in all, the next time I'm craving lobster I will not be heading to Red Hook.

Honestly. Food was good but not the greatest. I feel the ribs were undercooked and the jalepino cornbread, well. But the sauce was good and the pecan ice cream with bourbon was boss. Nice atmosphere. Would go back. Pricey.

Excellent place. I would have made the trip from Manhattan (yay!) to Astoria (uch) sooner had my fiancÃ© explained this restaurant better. She called it a "diner." Yes- it's 24 hours. Yes- it's fairly inexpensive. Yes- it's owned by Greeks. But that's really it. The menu should probably be categorized as "diner inspired fare." The menu is also far more streamlined and condensed than the average diner. It doesn't even look much like a diner. I recommend ordering the way we did last night- order a bunch of appetizers to share. Everything was a winner with the Fried Ravioli and Crunchy Ranch (Chicken) Quesadilla standing out a bit. Pretty good service, too. We'll return, for sure.

The context: It was around 2pm on a Saturday, I was trolling around central park south after brunch with a friend who I saw first time in 10 years, and we were looking for a boozy spot to continue the catch-up session. Â Who would have thought that most bars don't open till later in the afternoon on a Saturday? Â After a few searches and a call, we walked in Riposo 72. It is very clean-cut, simple layout, small and comfortable. Â There was only one other table having brunch when we arrived. Â We ordered the $5 Mimosa to start with. Â It was made a little too sweet for my liking. Â For second round, I had a Bellini and my friend ordered $5 Bloody Mary, and they were both tasty. Â We were there for a good 2.5 hours, chatting, laughing and catching up on the last 10 years of our lives. Â Our server was attentive at first but zoned out towards the end. I checked out the other's table's brunch and they looked fantastic. Â With $5 drinks, I will be back to test this place as a brunch choice.

Went here yesterday for lunch with friends. I was really in the mood for some tasty bbq and convinced my friends to try it. Although the service was great and our server Gina was very knowledgeable and helpful in helping us decide what to get I was just a tad disappointed, Â My two friends ordered the Philly cheese sandwich and i ordered a platter (forgot the name) but it was the one that you choose any three meats from the carving board and you also get two sides and coleslaw and pickles. My two friends each ordered sides separately because their sandwich only came with coleslaw. Anyway, below I will list the different food items and what I thought about each one Burnt ends- Not really charred at all, not much flavor and a lot of fat that wasn't properly rendered. Brisket- No flavor and very dry Ribs- They had no color looked almost steamed and although they were small they weren't fall off the bone tender and no flavor Philly Cheese sandwich- This was very tasty. They coat the meat in the cheese sauce that they use for their mac and cheese and top with grilled caramelized onions. Mac & Cheese- very good, tasty, creamy cheese sauce Baked beans- good flavor- however, the beans were a little hard needed to be cooked down more corn cakes- hard and dry mashed potatoes- buttery but they have the skins in them, not a fan I can't comment on the sweet potato wedges because I didn't try them. I'd also like to say that the portions were way to small for the price and not really enough to share like the Gina suggested. we did share but we also ordered a lot of food. My dish was listed at $27 but if you wanted ribs and burnt ends you had to pay an extra $2. I didn't think that should be extra money. Also they never offered us the complimentary apple cake at the end of our meal and we spent quite a bit of money for lunch and we were sitting there and heard the server offer this one guy the complimentary apple cake so my outspoken friend called her over and asked about it and she was trying to get us to buy a cake but then mentioned the complimentary slice. She wound up bring it to us and it wasn't good. It was dry and had no taste of apple whatsoever. I'd also like to point out that their sauces aren't really good. They have a sweet and spicy an original flavor and habanero. Nothing special about them, The habanero is just straight up HOT!! Â the original just tastes like regular bbq sauce from the supermarket and the sweet and spicy is watery. I'm such a foodie and I was expecting so much more. I was craving good bbq because I got a taste of some at an event the Friday before, but this didn't satisfy my craving. But, nice people I do have to say. I wouldn't go back though. I'm giving an extra star because of the service

What more can you ask for? Â Their appetizers and entrees are unique and delicious - their razor clams are wonderful and the three entrees I've had there has been top notch. Â Also have been there for drinks and finger food, and the (heaping) raw bar and flatbread are among the best I've had. All of this combined with a spacious setting and great decoration is just what the neighborhood needed. Â Will be back many times more.
wow~! really good~! taste~ really gooooooooooooooooooood!! i will go again~! see ya!!!

Staff were great, very kind and friendly. The place is pretty and the music was great. Only problem was the food was really less than average in my opinion. We had the pad-see-eu (sp?), massamam curry with roti appetizer and one of the specialty chicken dishes from the back of the menu. The roti was really good, but everything else was super sweet. The food was sweet to the point where I no longer wanted to order dessert and could barely finish my food (and the dessert was mango sticky rice, my favorite!). I definitely won't be going back. Sorry Tuk Tuk!
Excellent service, Â nice atmosphere, Â  friendly staff. Â  Full bar. Â  Excellent 3 cheese ravioli in bolognese sauce.

I was pretty disappointed with my first experience at this reknowned restaurant. First off, after how many lists I've seen Minetta on, proclaiming that it has one of the best burgers in the city, I can say, it just tasted like an ordinary burger to me. The preparation of the meat was spot-on, but the taste was nothing special. Now onto the service. The waiter literally dropped the ball and forgot about me and my friend. It took us literally an hour to get our burgers, meanwhile the 2 tables to the left and right, both of whom were seated about 30 mins after us, got theirs within 15 mins after they placed their order. When we finally got our burgers, no explanation or apology was offered. And to "top it off", no puns intended here, the waiter asked if I wanted to refill my glass of wine. I normally don't do so (even if I intend to get another glass) until I finish what I have in my glass, but since she poured for my friend and was right there, I agreed. I still had about 1/3 of a glass of wine left. The waiter finished pouring what was left in that bottle and my glass of wine was as the same level as my friend who just got a fresh pour. She walked behind our table, about10 feet away, to open a new bottle, looked at me, but did not top me off. The waitress even looked at me while she was opening the new bottle, she knew what she did, but she just walked to another table. Overall, my dining experience was very disappointing, especially the service.

I had the worst service ever here. Â After my friend and I were seated, we waited 40 minutes before someone came to take our order. Â  Just when we were about Â to leave, the waitress comes, takes our order. Â Another 20 minutes past before the food comes. Â  When the food arrives, my friend tried to flag our waitress down for a spoon and she gives him the "one second" finger and walks away. Â  I enjoyed the gnocchi I ordered, I'll give them credit for that. But after waiting for my food for approx. 1.5 hours, I think anything would have been good at that point. Worst service ever. Â Have not gone back since then.

Okay you guys.... I was at a tug of war on the amount of stars this place deserves but after much thought I feel the 4th star is rightfully deserved. Here's the scoop: I foolishly thought I could pull a party of 6 with no reservations on a Saturday night at the prime time of 7pm (in my defense it was snowing and raining all day who'da thought I wasn't the only fiend tryna get my fancy grub on) My total wait time for a table was a whopping 3 hours and although I may have a flair for the dramatics this is no tall tale, this is real life home slice. I literally waited 3 hours to be seated. So be warned you last minute yelpers who tryna gauge the severity of not having a reservation and just showing up: The gauge is real--- real upsetting when your hungry! I was upset that I was waiting so long and thought about what I would do if a customer of mine was waiting this long to be seated and thought, well damn I'd at least get them a free drink and voila with a Yelp check in you get just that. Check! Then whenever I kept approaching the host stand to get updates I always felt assured that they were taking care of me, giving me the update on the table (i.e. their on dessert, they're getting the check.. etc) I mean even if it was all BS the dude was so empathetic and personable it was hard to be mad. Another check for the quality of host. After what seemed like a millennium of waiting when we were finally seated it took a moment for the waitress to come over but once she checked in with us she made sure to stay in constant contact with us, she was engaging and efficient. Check again for good waitstaff! The food was simply great, seriously no need for a lengthy description-- it was delicious! Get the picture? Another check mark! Last but not least when we were waiting for valet to pull up our cars the guy that accepted the keys/tickets from you was such a nice guy! I had to wait a bit for the car and in my time standing by him he made sure to greet and say goodbye to each patron-- offering funny jokes and keeping those who were waiting informed on wait time. Can you say CHECK, CHECK, CHECK AND CHECK? It's hard to be mad at this place, I kinda felt like that Rhianna Meme where she's got this crazy satisfied look on her face and the caption reads, "When you throwing random mood swings at your man but he's handling them really well" That was totally me, and my boyfriend was Blend on the Water totally handing my mood swings well... Touche Blend, touche!

This place is so sweet! The decor is very Williamsburg, with black and white checkered tile, a tin roof, and a dark wood bar. The service was super friendly. We got seated right away despite the restaurant being full around 2pm on a Sunday. The chicken and waffles was some of the best I've had in Brooklyn -- delicious syrup, hot sauce, and crispy piping hot chicken. Prices are average -- brunch ranges between $8 and $15. Bloody Mary was good but not amazing, and definitely on the spicy side. I'll be back!

I've been here a handful of times and I would classify the food as pretty good. Mac and cheese is food and cornbread that they give free with your first yelp check-in is amazing. Â At the bar try their sidecar. Where SoCo loses points for me is sadly in the crowd. It rings phony. It's like every Real Housewives and Love and Hip Hop wannabe must eat here. Â It's a platform to stunt and front. This culminated in a shootout that the establishment did an excellent job of keeping under wraps. When I go out I wanna just chill, eat a great meal and sip on some good drinks. Â SoCo has the elements but I'm concerned someone's lace front weave, fake eyelashes or Lee press on nails might end up in my plate. It's a shame because the clientele has hijacked an otherwise great restaurant.

I think it's the best slice in the city. Â I actually prefer the regular, plain slice. Â The Di Fara special is very good, but I think the plain slice with the fresh basil and olive oil is terrific. Â I think it's fresh mozzarella paired with grated parmesan. Â It's fantastic. Â Been twice and haven't waited in line. Â It takes a bit to get the food because everything is cooked fresh.

Just held my sister's bridal shower here. Kathy was great to work with in helping to answer questions in days leading up to the event and her staff was very attentive in attending to our guests. They were very accommodating even when guests arrived extra early and lingered after the event. In a few instances, Kathy also served as my ear to the ground to help keep me posted on an our guests and their needs and providing recommendations. The food was served family style and everything was delicious. There's also a wide range with what is available. As they just opened the private space up, I'd be curious to see how their menu might evolve. Not to say there wasn't several options to choose from! Something I think would be great to see in a catering menu moving forward would be a brunch menu. The space is rustic which is perfect for DIY-ers and folks who want to be creative (of course, within reason--I would not ask a business with a new space to let me tape things up to their newly painted walls, etc.!). Suffice to say, its'a great backdrop for your Pinterst Party dreams. Bottom line is if you are looking to host a casual private event for a small or mid-sized party in Queens with good food, check out Butcher Bar. Parking in Astoria can definitely be a pain but there is a parking lot right next door to help alleviate some of those pain points. I would definitely consider having a party here again!!

I am by no means a Lobster Roll connoisseur, but have heard rave reviews of this place and was having lunch with a friend who lives in Battery Park and I owed her lunch. What a treat! First off, the guys here are awesome, friendly, funny and nice! Then the lobster roll.. I have had Eds, Pearl, Mary's.. and they are good, but I am not a fan of mayo and too much of it, and Luke's is perfectly about the lobster itself. The chowder was tempting, but the lobster roll was what I came for. Don't miss it!! It's no frills and just about the lobster roll :)

I live right around the corner from this restaurant and i have walked past it for months until i decided to try it out last night. It honestly is one of the best Japanese restaurants i have tried in NYC. The food is fresh, authentic and it tastes SOOO good!

Room Service is a solid Thai spot with a central location on 9th Ave. For the modern, sleek ambiance and the price, it's a tremendous value. The mojitos with fresh mint were delicious, as was the decent selection of $5 Southeast Asian beers. The food won't blow your mind, Â as the menu is pretty standard American Thai, but they'll nail your favorite delivery-night dishes. I had the Spicy Basil Noodles which were tasty but they weren't spicy as the name implied. Also sampled the red curry and pad thai, which were about as standard-goodish as I was expecting. If you want to feel like you're going out without raping the wallet, this is probably one of the better options for Thai in Midtown west.

Cool little local joint with excellent thin crust pizza. Their sauce is on the sweeter side and they use a good amount of cheese on their pizza. Go with the 18" pizza - it's easy to plow through several slices since the crust is so thin.

What I loved about this truck is the amount of food for the price. For about 6-7 dollars you get a whole bowl of food with some bread. The white sauce is what makes the meal. That sauce is like heaven in your mouth. And the spicy sauce is SPICY!!! I can usually handle the spice but this sauce was hot. I think this place lives up to all its hype and is worth it if your in the New York area. I want to go back.

Never again. I went to PÃ¢tÃ©s Et Traditions yesterday with a group of 7 people for my friends going away brunch and had the most horrible experience. We ordered food and it took forever but that's understandable for a brunch so no real complaint there. The portions were small and the lack of side dishes on the brunch menu didn't allow to compensate for that. However, both those things I can get over. The real issue was when we had to wait for 20 minutes for 4 beers and 2 mimosas. This kept happening all through brunch so that we all only had 2 drinks in the span of about 2 and a half hours. Don't know about you but part of my brunch experience is drinking and if I have to wait 20 minutes every time I ask for a drink then that's a problem.They also never came over to ask how we were doing. When the check came we paid and left what we felt the server deserved for a tip. Let me just say I've worked in service and my boyfriend works in service now. I'm well aware of what a good/bad tip can do and none of us felt our server deserved more than what we left. So, we left the restaurant and this is when it gets bad. The owner FOLLOWED us half way down the block to lecture us on tipping. We spent 15 minutes arguing with her about how we didn't think our server deserved a bigger tip and when we finally all tried to give her more money she wouldn't take it! She kept saying it was the principle and that "next time" we should give a bigger tip. Did she really think there would be a next time after what she did? seriously lady. I don't usually write reviews but I thought everyone should hear about how insane this was. She kept saying that for parties of 6 or more a 20% tip is mandatory...umm, is it? You really expect a 20% tip for bad service? and if that's the case then add it to the bill because if you don't then there's no reason why you should be following me down the block demanding a larger tip! It's a shame because the food is decent and the place is cute but there are a million other places in BK that have better food and much better service.

Excellent Royale Burger with cheese tonight - and 5 stars for the Take Out service. On the phone, they told me it would be ready in "8 minutes." And they weren't kidding. I walked there in about 6 minutes...then they took 2 minutes to take my credit card and to give me a free glass of water to wait. Then my food came right out. I live two blocks away, and the whole process took less than 15. One low point was that the onion rings were just put down in a paper bag without any other container. The crispy coatings fell off, leaving tasty - but naked - onions. I kept having to dig out the crispy stuff. Ah, burger craving satisfied!

We had the cheong fun with shrimp, the cheong fun with fried ceuellers, pork and egg porridge, roast BBQ pork, roast duck and fried won ton noodles and it was super yummy. Every dish did not disappoint :) The food arrived pretty quickly and they were able to provide us with additional stuff as we ordered them pretty efficiently. Highly recommend for a quick yum totally worth your money meal!!

Not sure why the website says it's closed, but when we called, they said they were open all day today (no break) on Sunday, 8/31/14. Â We hustled down there in a light shower, and were seated in 10 minutes (the lady on the phone said 45-60min). Guess we got there earlier than expected! :) Pork buns - not as good this time, like they missed some sweet sugar/honey. The tako wasabi was good, as always, though smaller portion than before. The Akamaru Modern was great; much better than their plain Tonkatsus. They had some kind of special "Italian-style" hybrid ramen, but we went with the classic and were not disappointed.

The food is incredible! And the price is right ... not often those two thoughts go together in NYC. We arrived at 6 on a Tuesday and were the second table seated. By the time we left around 6.45ish, the joint was 90% full. The service was friendly. The salsas were plentiful and delicious. My only complaint is the chips were a little thick and heavy for me, and you pay $3 for them. You get the salsa's with your meals anyway. I had the Camarones Borrachos, which was incredible!!! Big serving of shrimp, green rice, sliced avocado, tiny corn tortillas, and the mole (i think it was mole) was what turned a good dish into something special. My friend had the Arrachera Taco, which he said was also incredible. Maybe even slightly better than the expensive one he had at La Palapa. I'd love to back and try the drinks and really draw out my meal. Though when crowded it must be a little insane there. If you go on weekend, or during prime-time hours, which I would do under the right circumstances, prepare to wait ... but sitting in a bar around the corner would be worth it!! This review is brought to you by the word Incredible!!!
This place is awful. Â Super unprofessional. Â Completly unorganized. Â Food is mediocre. Â Do not waste your time, or your money.

Legendary Black Label Burger was just as I imagined it...glorious. We decided to go have a special Sunday evening dinner completely at random this winter. Â We called Minetta and checked out any cancellations. Â They had us call back a little later in the afternoon maybe after 2 or 3. Â When we call the second time we scored a 7:30 rezzy. Â Burger gods were on our side. Â Don't think you will ever get this lucky. Â As with all great well known restaurants, look to book 4 weeks in advance. Had some beers and cocktails to start, the usual. Â Service was fine nothing crazy good or bad. Â Ambiance is great, you feel special there. We had a Mesclun Salad w/goat cheese and some Bone Marrow to start which I ended up slurping most of on some great texas toast. Â The bone marrow is super manly, try it at least once. Â I won't go into further details and let it be a surprise if you have never tried marrow. I had the Black Label burger and my GF had the bone in strip. Â The burger was absolutely delicious and her steak was amazing too. Â She thought it was on par with Lugers and the rest of the NY steak houses if not the best. I am actually craving Minetta Tavern now and may have to call for a reservation after I click post.
Absolutely delicious food. Skirt steak with plantains, rice and beans was amazing! Tres Leches! Sandia! Always busy, so I'm not the only one that loves this place.

Surprisingly good service for a place this busy. Â We ordered the meatballs and octopus as appetizers. Â They were both OK, but not incredible: the meatballs were pretty standard, and the octopus tasted like very moist chicken with a char on the outside. Â For the mains we ordered the lamb shank and the branzino. Â Lamb shank was very tender, but I didn't really like the orzo that came with it. Â The branzino was great, and came with nicely seasoned potatoes and cherry tomatoes. Â We split a chocolate mousse for dessert. Â This came with a scoop of sesame ice cream which was a little weird, but definitely interesting. Â The mousse itself was rich and delicious, although not quite as airy as most mousses I've had. Â Great place, and I'm looking forward to going back to try out the kefi salad and the sheep's milk ravioli.

BarBossa - ele e o melhor! Â Here's why: Drink - I had the Strawberry Mojito and it was clearly sweet from the berries and not just loaded with simple syrup. Â However, there was not nearly enough rum. Â Both my roommate and I agreed the drinks were WEAK & SUGARY though delicious. Ambiance - tiny, Nolitan, perfect Service - efficient FOOD - The food was so SAVORY! Â I enjoyed the Crab & Garlic dip that came with 5 crostinis. Â It was filled to the brim with crab, and the garlic was not strong at all. Â I am all about extra garlic, but the crab was so good, I forgot the garlic was a bit absent. Â For my entree I had the Tuna Tartare Salad with Ricotta Toast and a fresh greens salad. Â For the first time in NYC, I found an inexpensive ($14) entree with LOADS OF TUNA TARTARE! Â Finally, a place that serves the portion you pay for. Â It was heavenly. Â I was so full that I enjoyed only a bite of the ricotta toast, but it was also delicious. Â The salad included arugula and cilantro with a light dressing I am kicking myself for not coming here sooner!!!
Intimate seating and the food was good. However, I can't remember my favorite dish - that may be a sign??

4 of us came for the very last 40 minutes of service on Sunday night. The service was excellent, the food was amazing. Some of the best Yakitori I've had in NYC, and especially for the area. Egg plant, chicken meatball, chicken heart yakitori is not to be missed. The non bbq dishes were great as well. Can't wait to go back and try more of the menu. Check out there menu online before going, online menu is a much better way of getting a good idea of what you're in for if you've never done yakitori.

Love. Three Letters was just fantastic. We had a big group for a recent dinner. Â Lots of wine, appetizers, entrees and desserts. Â I started writing this review in March right after I had been there. Â Unfortunately I forgot about it but didn't want to pass up giving them some love Yelp style.

Awesome bottomless brunch!!!!! My friends and I were looking for a fun place to go have brunch before a matinee at the theater, and we came across Mezetto. Â  The restaurant is located in the East Village and is nestled in a corner. Since it was summer, all its windows were open, which made it great for people watching. Â The place itself is nothing special, but the service was great and the brunch delicious. Â Not to mention the delicious mimosas (pomegranate, peach, orange, pineapple, and passion fruit).

Hands down some of the best Middle Eastern food I've ever tasted. Â The food is absolutely fabulous - tasty, well-portioned, and easy to share in groups of people. Â This is a place to go to have a great time with friends or to impress a date. Seven of us shared the Mezza Royale, Mezza Vegetarian and Mixed Grill, and supplemented the meal with an order of brussel sprouts, lamb ribs, and duck shawarma. Â We then squeezed in a couple of fantastic desserts. Â This was a lot of food but we seemed to scrape every morsel off the plates. Everything we had was fantastic but I have to say the brussel sprouts and the duck shawarma really did it for me. Â I highly recommend these. The only thing that wasn't so fantastic was the wine list. Â If you're a fussy wine drinker, choose something you're more familiar with on their menu.
Tiny Tapas bar open to street had good service and some great dishes. Rabbit and chickpea stew was good; chorizo fava was excellent; shrimp dish was outstanding.

I've heard many good things about this place and finally came to see what all the fuss was about. First of all, farm to table is my thing. I can't say enough about how much I love the concept. So when I walked in to find the farms and what they contributed to the restaurant on the chalkboard, I was basically sold. When it comes to the seating, the tables are set up like picnic tables. 3 long booths in a "railroad style" layout. This means that if it gets crowded, you will be seated next to some random food lovin' stranger. Ok on to the food. My 2 friends and I shared the bacon wrapped dates. There were 5 so we had to fight for the last one. The bacon was crisp and all the flavors were unbelievably delicious. I mean really. It's bacon and dates and cheese. What can go wrong? Nothing. Then 2 of us shared The Beet salad. It was a good mix of beet, candied walnuts, carrots and cheese. I didn't like the dressing which was some sort of mayo type situation. Then again I don't typically like dressing and I really don't like mayo. So I may not be the best person to ask about that. Anyway, my friends also ordered the pulled pork sandwich and the burger. I didn't try either, but they made a lot of satisfied noises for me to know that they enjoyed their dishes. This place is pretty awesome. I'd definitely come back. Oh, the bathroom. Just an fyi, the light in there is really dim. So if you're planning on checking to see if you have spinach in your teeth, you may want to bring a flashlight.
Love this place. Amazing sangria and great customer service! I love coming here for mojito madness. Its the only reason i love Mondays

A cute and easy place to go out for dinner and drink after work. Â Love the outdoor seating area. Â I had tuna tartare for appetizer, and it was okay -- not that impressive. Â For entrees, I tried chicken and sea bass, and they were delicious. Â The sauces on both dishes seemed a bit heavy, but the flavors were great. Â Food portion was good for the price.
always delish and they make you feel like family!

Come here for the cool setting and cheap prices. Â As for the food, not so good. I get better Pad Thai off a street cart (not even close actually). Service is basically clueless. The health inspection recently went from a C up to an A so that's a positive.

best ramen around. rich chicken stock broth. pork is done deliciously and tastes heavenly in or out of the bowl. Â spicy sauce is unusual and well matched to broth flavor. Â there is typically a wait for this popular place but it is well worth it.
