This is Manhattan, after all. Â No matter where you turn, walk, stand, sit, or spit, there are thousands of others around you. Â One wonders how any of us keep our wits about in such madness. Â Speaking from the point of view of lowly tourist, I'd say the best way to stay sane is to find little nooks, like Nook, where you can have a pleasant conversation over some pleasant, yummy food. I came for breakfast with one local and two other Manhattan visitors. Â  Together we had: Mocha-chinos Baguette with cheese and organic jam (on appetizer menu) Egg Scramble (cheese, tomato, bacon, chives) Eggs Benedict Potato Pancakes Yes, Nook is ubber-small. Yeah, there is a solitary man taking care of all customers. But the food was beyond good. Â I loved the baguette with cheese and jam appetizer; it sounded like a curious combination but it arrived beautifully plated and was easily devoured by all. Â My scramble was great, the potato pancakes on par, and the Benedict good. Â  Overall everyone was pleased with the experience at Nook. Â Just mind your neighbors and come with the time to sit and enjoy. Â If you're in a hurry, as so many Manhattanites seem to be, consider some place else for the time being.

The pizza was soggy and absolute crap. Â The service was poor, the hostess was rude and refused to put a to go order in but five minutes after we sat down at the crummy little bar a guy walked in to pick up his to go order! Â WTH? Â Lord, how is this rated so high? Â I will never eat here again. Â Crap service, crap food.

This is an amazing neighborhood gem- trendy decoration, friendly staff, and delicious Thai food! This is exactly what UES needs - an above standard Thai restaurant. Lunch special is mostly $9 and $10, and only duck for $16. A lunch set comes with an appetizer, an entree and soup or salad. For appetizer, the net-rolls are crispy and tasty, dumplings look like hand-made and tasted very good. For entree, We have tried beef pad Thai, beef pad se-ew, and chicken red curry. All were satisfying. Entree comes with good quantity and much less greasy than most of the Americanized Thai restaurants in the city. Thai ice tea is just about right, rich but not too sweet.

Apparently I came on an off day. I dined with a friend who loves this place, and the reviews seem to be great, but I was not pleased at all. Although the waiter was very friendly, we had to ask for bread- once they brought it out we had to ask again for small plates, and then again for some butter. His lentil soup was good but could have used some more seasoning. I ordered the fettuccine pescatore- the pasta was way too hard, it could have easily used another 2 minutes. I hate soft pasta, I like it a little firm, but this was just plain ol hard. The lobster meat and clams in it did not taste fresh at all. The scallops were tiny but good. I would be willing to give this place one more shot, but only because I have heard so many good things about it- this must have been a one time miss. The prices were low but the service was off and I was very disappointed with my entree. Sure, I'm picky about Italian restaurants, however I don't think its being too picky to want your pasta al dente.

I don't know, either the food is going a bit south, or my hangovers are coming on earlier than they used to. Lately, when i've tried to retrieve some lucidity by having a falafel at Oasis after partying, it has only made me feel drunker and more nauseated. I used to long for that falafel while pretending to be engaged in conversation with whomever was boring me in Williamsburg at the time, but now not so much; the hipster-spiel doesn't get filtered through the falafel dream and I am forced to observe my own tedium while listening to complaints about the derivative band that sounds like Can, or the Â details of getting a ticket for riding a Â fixed gear bike through Grand Central Station (actually, that didn't bore me), or someone whine about Â having to move to Los Angeles or Korea because the art scene sucks in NY. I do appreciate Â how complicated the falafel is at Oasis, with sauerkraut and pickles, and onions and whatever else they wanna toss in there. Â Maybe I should be staying off all the acidic ingredients when I've been drinking. Okay, so it isn't Oasis' fault at all, though I think the pita could do with some warmth.
Very good Southern Fried Wings, but the Guinness -- even by Midtown standards -- seemed overpriced at $9.

Went back to Cafe Orlin for breakfast, this time during the week and can still report that the food is outstanding but the service still sucks. Servers seem dis-interested in the customers often spending too much time at the bar and not caring to see if their tables needed anything or were even enjoying their meal.

Extraordinarily good Greek food in the East Village -- this place is not to be missed! Â My first choice for lunch apparently did not serve lunch, so my Yelp app guided me here instead. Â Apparently that app is useful! The ambience is wonderful. Â The ceiling is quite striking being lined with terra cotta pots. Â The main seating area is along a narrow corridor that is buttressed by a bar at the far end with more seating area in the back. Â The music was tranquil, yet modern, decidedly Greek in a way that I felt like I could have been having his meal in Athens. Â  The menu is rather limited for lunch, but I opted for the Pastitsio. Â Often, in less capable establishments, this can be dismissed as Greek lasagna. Â Here, however, the dish stands alone strongly showcasing wonderful Greek tastes. Â The first thing that strikes you about this dish is how aromatic it is. Â It made me pause for a moment, lovely. Â Presentation, was monolithic, with a feature rich surface, adorned on the side with fresh rosemary and a lone cherry tomato. Â The noodles were perfectly cooked. Â The bechamel sauce was really quite good. Â The flavors were so balanced, every forkful was identical. Â And it was so flavorful, and it was not heavy at all. Â I really enjoyed this dish. Â I was rather surprised by the skilled execution of the chef. Â Well done. Â The dish was accompanied with complimentary pita which was fresh and delicious as well. Â  My thoughts are that this would make a wonderful place to take a date. Â It also should be substituted immediately for one of the more lackluster selections on the 1 Michelin star list for New York. Â I can easily think of three restaurants on that list that fall well short of this place. Â Bravo. Â Come one, come all.
Nice Laid back vibe on prince street . Drinks are good . The enchilada was burnt due to the charcoaling .
The condiments are all fresh and delicious. I had the pork and chicken tacos both were delicious but I liked the pork slightly better because of the flavor
I practically live here over the summer. The most amazing Sicilian pizza and spumoni. Period. Case closed. End of story.

Found this place by accident, I did not expect such a gem in this area but I am glad it exists! Had dinner here the first time and the food was wonderful! The portions are plentiful and the service was great, my waitress was Grace and I kinda loved her! I went back months later for lunch and was not disappointed, they were very busy but managed to get a table right way. The grilled cheese with soup was perfect!

I am officially hooked on the Pork Sliders!!! The spot is nice and cozy and prices seem reasonable. However, the service although very nice couldn't keep our tabs in order or sometimes forgot a few orders, but in the end we got what we ordered just took a while. I don't understand the whole lighting in the bathroom. One room had red lighting and the other green and no mirrors, so not sure what's going on there. Music was pretty mixed, but got better into the night. It is a must to return if only for the pork sliders!!

Great place to go for brunch! Â Expect a wait during peak weekend hours, but the food is worth it. Â Has a shabby chic/cutesy country farm vibe, with mismatching chairs and even a church pew for seating. Â  What I get: I love the Nutella French Toast (but then again, you could slather Nutella on a shoe and I'd eat it...) or Veggie Burger. Â My bf raves about the Penny Egg sandwich on a croissant and the omlette. Pros: Yummy, soul-fulfilling food, great waiters and hostess Cons: Long wait, cash only, crawling with annoying 20-something girls.

My husband and I went for dinner here because we saw it on Diners, Drive-Ins and Dives the other day. Guy Fieri spoke very highly of it and we wanted to experience it also. It's a small place, so don't look for spaciousness. The waiter/host was very friendly the entire time. The wait for the food wasn't long. The food itself was delicious. The burger was better tasting and I think the best I've had in years! We could have had seasoned fries for a couple dollars more, but we stuck to the regular fries. We plan to return another day to try out other items on the menu.

I am obsessed with macarons and this place was like heaven for me! Once I got inside, there was a line but not very long (I was there in the middle of a weekday. Â There were little towers of macarons and pretty pastel decor. Â They had a lot of different flavors to choose from! I got orange blossom, rose, violet, chocolate, and salted caramel macarons which was around $20. Â Pretty pricey but I felt I needed to go here while in New York and on the past 3 trips to NYC, never had time to pop in here so for me it was definitely worth it! You can tell when you bite into these little guys that they are fresh made daily. Â Moist but still with that little crunchy crack when you first bite in. I saved half of my macarons to devour on the plane back home! A must try place in my book.

Well-prepared, if unimaginitive food, but the service is quite slow and inattentive. The good came out at the right time but water glasses and coffee mugs went un-refilled for most of the meal and only a verbal flare gun got their attention, including when it was time to pay. On a final note, what does this place have to do with New Zealand? Likely will not return.

Cool blacked out store but uncool backed up staff; Loyalty only applies for purchases of $10+. The menu "applies Chinese, Taiwanese and even Japanese flavors to a hoagie that was already French-Vietnamese", but I was in a rush and had just eaten but couldn't resist the Black Sesame Milkshake w/ whipped cream ($4.36). Would consider returning with a carnivorous sandwich-eating accomplice for a bubble tea an the chiller (yes I know). Hopefully they don't take as long to emerge as the shale... Wifi PW jelly22 at time of purchase

We had our pre-Valentines dinner here. Things that were good: space is lovely Chicken livers were GREAT. I would go back just for them. Wine list was interesting. The Lebanese wines were very good. The red i had was wonderfully smokey and rich. Crowd was young and fun. Front staff was efficient and pleasant. Desserts are great, if a bit on the over sweet and cloying side. Things that were bad: its really dark and noisy. To the point of being silly and unpleasant. Service was horrible. They seemed to be completely understaffed and overwhelmed, which for a resto open this long is pretty unacceptable. Plates were really hit or miss, Nothing seemed to match or blend well, which is not so good at a small plates place. We had a good time, and appreciated that our waitress apologized for the slow service, but it was not really exceptional. I think that with this type of food, you really have to go above and beyond. Otherwise, ethnic food just becomes street food served in a fancy place.
one of the best pizza ever
Came back and had the truffle burger and fiancÃ© had the moko loko which has to be eaten with a fork and knife. Sweet potato fries and fried pickles are tasty.

I ordered from Zen for the first time today. SO PLEASED. I don't know about everyone else, but I'm always scared to try vegetarian food because I know how badly it can go wrong haha. BUT I ordered for delivery; the service was fast, the food was AMAZING, and the delivery guy was really nice (even though my dog barked him down) the prices are really reasonable. I'd recommend the deep fried wontons,they're amazing. the veggie dumpling aren't as great, and the sauce included. I thought it wold be better, but with the mango chicken and the wontons, I DONT CARE! sorry if my review is super long and spastic, but this is my new place to order from. Plus they wrap everything so so cute.

Cool new little spot with fancy sandwiches in a noodle and dumpling part of town. I had the tuna melt and I liked it quite a bit. The tuna wasn't too rich either and the cheese went well with the whole experience. My only issue was usually with a tuna melt you griddle the bread or something to make it crispy, sadly mine was ungriddled. They're still finding their rhythm which is typical of a new business. I have no doubt that they will, and once they do they'll churn out some tasty sandwiches for all the court workers nearby.

This place is unbelievable!! A true gem in the heart of LIC!! I feel so lucky to live in this neighbourhood!! We had great experience getting same day reservation when I called. We waited only 5 minutes to be seated. Menu is wonderful!! And the food AMAZING!!!!!!! A must go. The decor is super cozy and warm too! Love love love the place. We will definetely go back!

Five of us ate at Basso56 last night expecting a more than decent meal as a result of reviews on yelp, chowhound and even Zagat. Â Our experience was profoundly disappointing and confusing. Â In fact disillusioned. Â Some did warn us that is was a tourist place not worthy of true foodies. Â I should have listened. Â My first clue that this was not going to be what I expected was when the waiter, a perfectly gracious guy, asked where we were from and was taken aback a bit when we said UWS and the Village. Â So here goes. Â The drinks were quite good. the barata tasty. Â Except for one main dish, a special wild mushroom ravioli, the food was disappointing at any price. Â Some inedible. If you want good pasta go to Â  Lupa, Cacio e pepe, Apiary, Gotham just to name a few.

We got some rolls at at Saturday flea market and they were delicious. My chipotle mayo BLT lobster roll was served with warm, soft, buttery bread. The bacon was a thick slice and the saltiness gave flavor to the tomato slices and iceberg lettuce. The mayo had a touch of spice that added a little zing. Oh, but the large hunks of succulent lobster claws were the stars of the show. Portion size wasn't very large, but this was only $10. DH got the Connecticut style roll ($16) with melted butter. He says, "It was very fresh. The buttered bread and buttered lobster were a delicious combo." However, he wished they put some chopped celery in it instead of the chives.

This is my " go to " neighborhood place if I feel like being " uppity". Â This is an upscale restaurant if you want to take a special friend or loved one out for a nice meal, and is also good for clients if you work across the street like I do. It's not cheap, but sure is good! Â It's farm to table so the menu constantly changes and goes according to season. Recos; Cheese plate Grilled Octopus App Salmon over corn chowder with shishito Â peppers or any other salmon fish on the menu Seared Branzino Steak tartar Any dessert!

So I was told that this is the best Thai restaurant in Queens. Was here for Mother's Day dinner with my BF and his family. We arrived around 6:00pm and there was a wait. Luckily, we didn't have to wait too long. The menu was so extensive that I was overwhelmed. The only thing I was able to decide on was my drink-Thai Iced Tea. There was a lot of food on the table for the 8 of us. Tom Yum soup was good but I was told that the broth should be creamier/thicker. The Pad Thai was alright. A little too sweet for my liking. The steamed stripe bass with garlic, chili and lime was spot on. The crispy pork and grilled beef were equally tasty. Enjoyed the experience and would definitely be back to try all the different desserts they have.
Great and amazing Mexican food for a cheap price!!! Friendly and kind staff!! Only bad thing about this place is the location its very small. Who cares when your eating great food?

Their sandwich collection is great. Definitely better than sandwich shops such as Pret a manger or Potbelly. Clean, fresh, well seasoned and great tasting sandwiches for a reasonable price. I would definitely recommend this place for lunch.

threekitcheneers.com The Three Kitcheneers went to Tia Pol!!! This is a teeny tiny tapas restaurant in Chelsea. Very cozy and warm - a quintessential downtown feel. I ate so much food here it's just ridiculous. To be honest, I can't even remember everything I ate. But what I do remember, I can't stop thinking about. The Patatas Bravas, a classic tapa of potatoes with a slightly spicy aioli, was the absolute best I've ever had. The potatoes were so crispy on the outside and creamy in the center, like gigantic french fries. F*ck. I want them right now. I'm embarrassed to say that this was my first experience with Pimientos Estilo Gernika - holy crap - these should be on every menu, I don't care if it's an Amish Bakery, these should be mandatory. They're finger sized crispy green peppers sprinkled generously with sea salt. So simple. So amazing. threekitcheneers.com threekitcheneers.com/bloâ€¦
Mascarpone and Corn Risotto Aranchini Balls, Tomato PurÃ©e - excellent Handmade Pappardelle with Braised Oxtail Ragu - excellent. Seabass with mushrooms and italian brocolli - good.

This place was awesome , cozy , chill vied , and most off all reasonable and so affordable . The waiter I had was friendly and so was the owner . They both were very attentive but not over whelming . The food ( THE BURGER ) and the cajun fries were orgasmic , I recently just started eating meat again and they have shown me what I've been missing . AND ITS BYOBBBB , I live in jersey but I'm so making this a place that I come to frequently and often :)

I never knew this was Austrian place - I always thought this was just a bar of some sorts. I came here with S, of course this was S's suggestion since S is from here. We ended up sharing the following: home made liverwurst w/red onion jam - I wasn't too into the liverwurst here. It had too much mineral after taste. However, S gobbled it up without a problem. S actually finished the whole plate and I had one bite. landjÃ¤ger / home-made pickles / liptauer - S was explaining this to me and it didn't sound too appetizing the way S was describing it, but I actually loved this dish. austrian meatballs / roasted vegetables / potato puree - this was good, but gosh, I wish it was more spicy or some sort of heat. We ended up dipping our meatballs in the homemade mustard. Really good mustard in such a cute little pot. Katja's Margarita mit hollunderbluten - I can either like or dislike elderflower, but this Margarita contain the perfect amount of elderflower. S just got a beer and Marillen (Apricot) Reisetbauer, Austria - damn strong. I couldn't do a Schnapps. It's not fruity and you can't even tell it's Apricot and S knew Schnapps would be too much for me. Cute place, I would definitely come back here to try more things, but I would order landjÃ¤ger / home-made pickles / liptauer again.

Pies n Thighs is a magical place where you can get succulent pieces of chicken with a crispy coat of fried goodness, a buttermilk biscuit peelable layer by layer and a side for just $13. I'd imagine a plate of fried chicken this good would cost closer to $20+ as it does in other restaurants, but it doesn't! Each piece of chicken had a light and crunchy crisp to it while the meat inside, dark or white, juiced ever so slightly as you took a bite out of it. Â The biscuits were fantastic- thick and chewy but peelable in thin layers if you'd like. Â Both the chicken and biscuits taste great with honey. The sides were OK. Â The hush puppies are fried corn bread; they're good but a little too much fried food on top of the chicken. Â The mac and cheese is just mac and cheese. The fries looked pretty standard- my friend got them but I didn't try them. Aside from the sides, the chicken and biscuits are the main reasons to try this place out. The Chicken Box is the way to go. Next time I want to try their pies, which I hear are amazing as well.

I've been coming here since the beginning and love it more every time I go ..the food is super tasty, the flamenco is tons of fun and the staff is friendly and attentive even when they are packed. champagne sangria is my drink of choice (although they Â all are delish) and you can't go wrong with any of the tapas. Â One of my favorite places to eat and drink in the city. :)

Nyonya takeout is a monthly thing for me. Â The beef rendang, curried beef, roti cani, & peanut dessert are savory! Â On the other hand I'm not a picky eater, I once ordered the Asam Laksa and nearly gagged. Â Don't do it

This is the perfect date spot. The ambiance is romantic, intimate, and just the right amount of dressy, and the food is delicious!!! I had the Linguine Alla Vongolle (linguine with clams) with white sauce and it was so good!! The clams were small, but delicious. My boyfriend had the rigatoni with sausage in pesto sauce and he couldn't get enough of it. We chose this place because we were looking for a good place to eat dinner during our one-week trip to NYC and found this place because of it's 4-star rating with a high number of reviews and close proximity to Times Square, and boy, we quickly found out that when NYC rates a place 4-stars on Yelp, they really mean it! Definitely recommend!

I had the good fortune to visit this quaint and friendly neighborhood restaurant. Upon entering, the ambience is obvious. The chicken torta sandwich, stuffed with avocado, with chioce of fresh salad or skinny fries, was deliciously prepared. Lentil soup is filled with chunky veggies and just the right consistency. The coffee is high quality and refills are forthcoming. Moderate price, friendly staff, delicious food....did I mention the outdoor garden area? A great and very welcome addition to Sunset Park!

This place is excellent overall. I had to wait 2 hours for just a 2 top but I am very glad that I did. The ambiance is very nice. It's very cool that the kitchen is completely open. I liked that you can see the chefs doing their work. I had a side of bacon and some sort of potatoes. They were both excellent. The bacon is super thick and full of flavor! Really not bad for 7 bucks. The potatoes were great too! For our main course we had the hanger steak and salmon. They were both cooked to perfection and seasoned well. Wine was nice too. This place just really has their shit together!

This is NOT a coffee shop- its for stuffy stuck up upper east side old ladies who want to drink over priced weak coffee that's "ooo la la it's Italian!" So basically if you're looking for any kind of latte type drink, turn around.

Google Neil Ganic, Â it's no surprise that this Venetian Empire-born-Croat's reputation is well deserved both in and out of the kitchen. I had dinner here last night just as it was opening and my delicious meal was supplemented by his tales of the NYC culinary world of the 80's (a real treat for those that have read Anthony Bourdain's "Kitchen Confidential"). I had originally stopped by for lunch, but was dismayed to find it closed despite the restaurant hour signs in front. It turns out that it's usually closed on Monday afternoons because he's off at the fishmonger's, so yelpers beware! When I returned for dinner with a Â friend, it was just opening up (5:15ish). As we got accustomed to our cozy little corner and opening our my first bottle of Sierra Nevada (BYOB), he came out of nowhere recommending that we try the special of the day, the spicy seafood combo. It was essentially the regular cioppino (pronounced "cho-pee-no"; shrimp, lobster, mussels, & scallops), but served in a spicy tomato-ey base instead. It was very reminiscent of the Japanese dish Champon or Korean Jjampong without the noodles. The only thing keeping me from noisily slurping down the broth to the last drop was pausing to meet Neil's kids who would casually walk in & out the place to hang out with their dad. Neil might seem like a stoic man, but he's incredibly friendly and kind. Oh and these musicians came in asking to sample the sound of the old timey cash register for some of their songs. Talk about the full Brooklyn experience! As others have mentioned this is a fantastic date spot. Once done and wiping bits of the ocean off your satisfied face, head off to Ferdinando's across the street for some Sicilian homemade sweets and cappucino. Your date will love you.
Good cocktails. Reasonable prices: $12 drink. Very loud music at night so not great for conversation but a fun place for a tasty drink! Glad to see a place like this in the neighborhood.

I have to give this three stars despite the food being really good. I went here last summer with some co-workers since it is in the midtown area. When we first walked in (during lunch rush) the place was packed and we were told we would have to wait for a table. We didn't mind since we really wanted to try the place out. We were given menus to look at while we waited. Half an hour later we were finally seated and a server came to clean our table while we sat. Nonetheless, after ordering an appetizer of fried plantain chips, a couple of empanadas, and rice with chicken we still had to wait for about another 20 minutes to finally get our food. The food was really good, however, the service was horrible. To top it off after all the waiting and horrible service we paid our bill and left the rude waitress no tip (the blonde one - not sure if she works there still), which is when she decided to follow us as we left and say "we work on tip and if you don't like the service you should say so". Needless to say I haven't been there since even though the food was amazing.
LOVELOVE Great traditional decor Great fresh fish meal Great service gogogo~

if you're looking for rich french comfort food, then this place is great! Â the place is small, but really cozy, so make sure to book a reservation in advance. Â The food was wonderful! Â  We had the curry mussels and the goat cheese tart for appetizers...wonderful! Â The goat cheese was beautifully tart and creamy, and the curry sauce was great, not too heavy or spicy. Â For entree we had the filet mignon with fois gras and the moulard duck breast...again...wonderful! Â The steak was cooked exactly how i asked and the duck was rich with a great sauce. Â Oh, and the BYOB thing, major plus! Â When i went for my birthday, the ice machine wasnt working, so thank goodness we didnt get champagne, but I would assume if u needed a bottle chilled, they can help with that as well. Â oh, the dark lava chocolate cake...DIVINE!! Â for anyone who loves chocolate cake, and i loooooooooooooooooooooove chocolate cake, this was heaven! Â An amazing end to an already amazing meal. Â  The onlt drawback i had, was that we were seated right infront of the kitchen where the food comes out. Â Maybe when you book a reservation, ask NOT to be seated infront of the kitchen if possible because then you leave smelling pretty strongly of food. Â Not to mention its always louder infront of the kitchen.
Service was excellent. The mixed seafood platter (grilled shrimp, mussels, fried calamari and clams) was really good.

Apparently they have a lunch break between 4PM and 5ish. So I guess people working at a restaurant do eat lunch and are actually people meaning they make mistakes. We did get here at 4 PM. after a short conversation and misunderstanding, we sit there for a good hour enjoying tea and their tart cake which is REALLY good. going for $7 a piece, they better be good. There's around 6 two seat table outside and many more inside. Do sit on the quiet side of the block with lower traffic and car. Â  After a hour, the waitress gave us a bottle opener which we pass along to our fellow diners. The rest of the experience is just great. We order a beet salad which is well dressed and really good. They grilled it for the warm feeling. The entrees are great as well. I will definitely come back just for byob and their tarts.

I've been to this place a few times. They give you a good portion with their lunch specials. However, at $9-$10 for their typical lunch items, you pay for that extra portion (whether you can finish it or not). Their menu boast some really interesting homestyle items. They are dishes that you won't typically find in the surrounding vicinity (for this price). I would love to try all of their lunch specials some day, especially their oxtail stew. I've tried their chilli over rice & beans lunch special. It was a bit salty for my tastes. Another time, I went for their cuban sandwich. Now the cuban sandwich was very good. It wasn't the best I've ever had. And, I wish it was a bit more juicy. However, it was still a very good cuban sandwich. Even my friends who have never tried a cuban sandwich beforehand had good things to say about it. During lunch hours this place packs up with customers pretty quickly, customers ranging from office workers to construction workers, and everything in between.

I love, love, love The Melt Shop! Every single grilled cheese sandwich is hot, delicious, not-too-greasy, and satisfying. The tator tots and their dipping sauce are to die for. I could eat here every day!

(JalapeÃ±o infused) Vodka and lemonade was delicious. Gravy topped roasted chicken was good. Chocolate mousse was good. Jamaalaya is pretty good, and the cornbread is pretty good. But the atmosphere is terrible. Very loud for such a tiny space. The music is loud. The customers, even louder. There is a table in the middle with a terribly obnoxious crowd that had not been asked once to calm down. These guys are yelling and laughing louder than the rest of the place. The menu on the wall is nice, but give me one that Ivan read without having to get up and squint. I'll go back to Delta Grill.

Normally I would expect a large diner like this to just be another lousy diner experience, especially being so close to Times Sq and endless theaters and tourists. Â Ive been in here a few times now for late breakfast and brunch, and have no complaints! Â For the amount of people inside and out, the place is a well-oiled machine. Â Even the mens room is clean which is unheard of in a place with volume like this. Â The food has been solid and the bloody mary's and mimosas are some of the best Ive had in quite a while!

I cam here the Sunday night of fourth of July weekend with my boyfriend to the start of a little night on the town since we took the next day off. I read so many pleasant things about this place on Yelp that I had to see for myself. The decor was thoughtful, I felt like I walked into a classic Indian establishment. The lighting is on the low side which I enjoy. On the TV abvoe the bar some bollywood movies were being played. There's something to be said for the atmosphere, I could tell all of the other diners and bar patrons were having a nice night. The menu is quite nice. It has a variety of traditional Indian dishes with a twist. To start we had the fried okra which was tasty. Something I'd try to recreate on my own but I doubt I can execute it as nicely as the chefs. For entrees we had the lamb byrani and chicken tikka masala. At first we thought the portions looked small but they ended up being perfectly sized, we ate the entire thing. The flavors were delightful, meat was cooked nicely. Unfortunately I do have some criticisms for the restaurant surrounding the pricing. The low hanging fruit here is the plates are expensive and you don't get the bang for your buck as far as the meat. (Read: Stingy with the chicken and lamb in my entrees). If there's one thing I can't stand, it's paying $15 for a cocktail with a small amount of booze. This place does that. I'm cool with an expensive drink but I expect a good amount of liquor and Â for it to arrive quickly. On to my next point that we ordered a second round to have a cocktail with our entree and 20 minutes had gone by before we decided to cancel it with the server. She said she had to check with the bartender to make sure he could cancel it. Thankfully it wasn't and issue but I find it unacceptable that we would have to wait 20 minutes for a cocktail on SUNDAY NIGHT when there were maybe 5 people at the bar. I think what was going on was the bartender was training the hostess and there's nothing wrong with that but it's not okay to let patrons wait that long for drinks. It was obvious that they weren't focused on training, more like hanging out behind the bar. I won't be back. I feel it's a tad overpriced.

4 dumplings for $1.00?! You won't find a deal like that anywhere else! I recommend the fried pork and chives dumplings. What makes these dumplings the best in NY is that they are not greasy/oily, unlike those you would find in many other restaurants. They are perfectly fried till golden brown on the bottom in this big pan that seems to hold up to 60+ dumplings all at once. They don't seem to add much oil but their method gets the job done! Dip it in their vinegar-y soy sauce ( the vinegar adds an extra kick) and you'll see what the rave is all about. I would recommend trying one dumpling without any sauce or condiments, just so you experience the flavorful filling that the dumplings have as they are. It's always packed when I go, so be prepared to wait a bit. Also, anticipate your order to be to-go because all the limited tables are always taken. This place has grown tremendously in 10 years. I remember when it was a hole in the wall just trying to establish itself in Chinatown and now it's a top destination for many visiting tourists!

While this place is good, it's definitely not as good as Ippudo. The wait isn't as bad as Ippudo. I definitely have to say that eating at Ippudo is more comfortable than eating at Totto. But the thing is, when eating at Totto, it feels more authentic, as if you were in a ramen shop/stand in Japan. The chefs were really nice and really cool to talk to. Don't dismiss this place. Have both places and see which you prefer. I'm just an individual that prefers Ippudo over this place but I don't discount this place at all. It's good fresh ramen - good broth - and overall a very enjoyable experience. I would definitely recommend to ramen / noodle / carb lovers.

The mediocre soul food is not worth the shitty service my friends and I received today. Mac n cheese was microwaved as well as the meatloaf in a "tomato sauce" which was ketchup salted and peppered. Worst dining experience in a long while. With an empty restaurant you'd expect the service to at least be mildly okay. Wrong. Awful experience, total disappointment will not be returning.

You know that saying, "save the best for last"? Well, that just sums up my experience here at Ippudo. I've tried SO many ramen places here in the city (faves to name a few are Hide-Chan, Kambi, Miso Ramen) but I was holding out on trying Ippudo. I've heard so many people and have read the reviews saying the wait's super long.. and well, my hunger doesn't have time for that. Especially in a city where ramen shops come in abundance. With that said, I took the smart route... I went solo. I walked in a noticed a crowd of people in the front waiting for the table, but since I was by myself, I was seated immediately. Pretty damn nice. Ambiance - it's interesting - very upbeat and trendy. They greet you as soon as you walk in the main dining area. What I mean by greet...the staff actually shouts something in Japanese at you... which I'm assuming means Welcome. (again, I may be totally wrong) But it was kind of nice - got me in the mood...for a beer. But I resisted doing so (gotta watch my figure...LOL) ... anyway you get my point. Seating - along the perimeter, they had the traditional booths for large parties. However the center dining area was where the action was at. The best way to describe it is that it's similar to a biergarten-like setup where there were huge picnic-looking tables.. so basically you're sharing this with other strangers. Meh, I don't mind that. Food - Since it was my first time.. I wanted to get the full experience and was only going to order the classics. So I got an order of the pork buns ($9) to start...Overall they were amazing! I wish there was more of that sauce in the bun but it's okay. It was still good. The lettuce gave a nice textural value to the bun, adding a good crunch for every bite devoured. The pork was cooked perfectly and soo tender. Great appetizer. For the ramen, I ordered the Akamaru Modern ($15) with Nitamago ($2, seasoned soft boiled egg) on top. Similar to Momofoku (but not nearly as good as Ippudo) ...their ramen is priced pretty high... however it was definitely worth it. Seriously, this is the best ramen I've ever had... I don't know why I was holding out for this long to try it!! The service was spectacular.. they were really quick at refilling my drink and checked in just enough, but not to the point where it became annoying. Overall, this place lived up to my expectations and more. To avoid the long lines... just go solo. Trust me, I won't judge you.

my boyfriend just moved into the neighborhood and as we were exploring the other day, we stumbled upon taiyo foods, aka my new favorite japanese grocer. it's small and cute, and they carry every japanese item i love/use on a regular basis (shiseido shampoo/conditioner, my brand of udon, pocari sweat, onion rings, etc.). they even have assorted japanese kitkats! so, i wound up buying a 2L bottle of pocari sweat, panapp ice cream, and vanilla bean kitkats, all of which were super yummy. the service is very friendly, too! they are patient and willing to take the time to help you find whatever you need. i will definitely be coming back for more!

The outside of the cafe was the shop front for Friends!!! We ordered the pork chop and the fish- the pork chop was huge!!! The combination of the fennel with the butter beans made this meal the star! The fish sat on top of some sort of sweet corn and pesto salad which my friend thoroughly enjoyed, the fish was average:not bad/not great. Great ambience-go for the recommendations- the meatball sliders are meant to be legendary so that would be my tip!

Came here and sat down because I'm on jury doodie. Â Otherwise no reason to sit as its a to go spot with Asian stuff on the flat screen which was way too big and far more advanced than anything in this "haven't changed since the 80s to go spot". But was surprised that they took credit cards. Ok Austin F (I assume F is for Farts - because your review for this place was full of them) I relied solely on your review of the shanghai noodle beef and wonton soup "being the best soup you have taste period". Â This soup deserved a 5 out of 10 but it was cheap. Â Meat was too fatty, broth plain, wontons good, noodles good too - broth needs work since it's the base of the soup. Â Austin gets instant Yelp review ejection for such a bold unsubstantiated statement. Â Austin Farts if you get smashed in the face by a snowball in February 2013 it was probably Bramfy B. On the other hand the pork buns were good - drier and doughier than I'm used too but I like. Service is funny here - old dudes seem pissed at you for sitting down and eating but they somehow still provide good service - just in a old man "get the F outta here" kinda way. Doneski

This place is 150 years old! And when it opened, there was no 12th ave, so it was right on the river. It retains an old world charm, and the bartender will make you a fantastic martini. And it's not crowded - perhaps because it's on 11th ave, and so a bit off the beaten track.

Beer selection was great. It was really cute inside and spacey. The servers were always on point with checking in on us! Wasn't too impressed with the food...it lacked flavor. Maybe it was just that specific plate I got (the macaroni and cheese). I'd definitely come back though, that beer!!

It is always hard to find places that do vegetarian ramen, so I went here with a carniverous friend of mine so we could both get our fill. I really enjoyed the one vegetarian option they had. Â A ton of food with lots of flavor. Â Will definitely go back

We went there for brunch today. Overall, the food, service, ambiance, and crowd were all good. I would have given it 4 stars, but I've decided to deduct one star due to the following minor problems: 1. The coffee that I ordered was stale. 2. My Tajarin (pasta Carbonara) was a bit too salty for my taste. Maybe it was because the chef was generous with the prosciutto. 3. My husband's L'Artusi scrambled eggs with sausage and crispy potato was also too salty. 4. They didn't serve desserts for brunch, so I didn't get to taste the olive oil cake. The winner of the brunch was the orange and macadamia nut scone that we ordered as a starter.

Caracas is super tasty. Â I've been there several times for both brunch and dinner. Get the fried plantains and the "popular" arepas tasting platter. Â  If I'm going for it, I get a bottle coke or a milkshake. Last night for dinner I had the mixed berry juice which was delicious. Staff is cool but definitely "relaxed". Â If you need something, say something! I would say ignore the haters below with the 1-3 stars. They are stupid and probably don't know how to either make dinner conversation or flag a waiter down. This ain't the Ritz people!

Here's the sitch: Their food is really good. like really really good. They use the best products to get you that food, so that's why it's "over-priced" for bushwick, in williamsburg or manhattan that is cheap. But my god, their service is terrible, I've had many instances with their service: Last summer when my table ordered coffee as a pre meal (because coffee and pizza? not a great combination on a warm summer evening) and he acted like he forgot about it and then brought it to us after our pizza, it was 3 cups of coffee, and they weren't crazy busy. 2nd: rude waitresses.. all the time I've never had a pleasant one. 3rd: I was there with my boyfriend getting brunch and we asked for extra sugar for our coffee and the waitress gave us 1 more packet.. acted like she was doing us a favor. then made a stink when family members came to join us, when the whole place was empty. 4th: you always have to get their attention to give you the check, and they are always leaning against the bar as you are trying to do it. 5th: after all this i still love the food and i flipped to ordering delivery when i have a craving for the zaaa. but the lady they have working the phones is so rude when she first answered i laughed a little, because it was just so jarring, and then she proceeded to have a really inappropriate conversation with me over the telephone before taking my order. .. I've worked in the food industry and usually this is a problem with management. They hire the people they'd like to fuck and not the people that are the best. I think the owners are really cool and they have a great product and i commend them for doing it in bushwick. It shows real vision. I just think they need to fix a few things, and it looks like im not the only person that thinks so...

I live on the block and while the crowd of people obstructing me from reaching my apartment gets annoying, I understand why they are there. Orlin is the best. Reasonably priced, delicious brunch that doesn't feel too decadent (but probably is). The service is nothing spectacular but I can't stay away. Literally, I walk by at least five times a day. Their dinner is really good too.
awesome veg sushi. Â great addition to the neighborhood and is my go-to healthy lunch spot.

I finally went to Sweet Afton after hearing about it so long from friends and from trying it at Summer Stunner. My two companions and I went after a long afternoon of Old Fashioneds and Sopressata at Bateman's so bear with me since my memory is a bit fuzzy. Actually my memory is just plain awful in general so bear with me even more. The three of us came around 7 pm on a Saturday night to find a slightly crowded establishment. We decided to sit at the bar itself and were immediately addressed by a waitress for our beverages for the evening. I left my drink choice up to the bartender since I had no interest in choosing. Sometimes a lady just wants things decided for her. In the end I received a Coconut Lime Rickey. The good news: it was strong. The bad news: I'm not the biggest lover of coconut. Still, I give them props as it was very well crafted. The men had Modelos Especiales which is a can of Modelo with salt, a wedge of lime, and Tabasco sauce around the opening of the can. In hindsight, that's kind of gross that you lick/drink the hot sauce off the lid of the can. I feel like there was a 20/20 special on this. Oh well, I'm alive for now. Although one really comes to Sweet Afton for the drinks, there are some really tasty eats to have as well. As soon as I found out SA had fried pickles I just HAD to have them! Fried pickles are probably my favorite fried vegetable in the Fried World... along with sweet potato fries, french fries, onion rings, fried eggplant, and fried zucchini. Oh and fried mushrooms. I think that's it. These babies came out piping hot and I do mean ugh-did-I-really-just-burn-my-tongue-on-fried-Â­pickles hot. The Beer Battered Fried McClure's Brooklyn Pickles with smokey sauce are a little different than your usual fried pickle. Instead of just deep fried pickle chips with a light coating of batter, these pickles were just enveloped in a fluffy dough pillow. One might almost think they're about to eat a donut hole or something comparable. Still, they were good even though I think it's just a little too much bread going on. Next time I am definitely trying the Portabella Burger and the Mac & Cheese. I had my eyes (or is it my stomach?) on those two. Overall, Sweet Afton is a great local bar to hangout to nab a bite, a cocktail, a beer, and/or a sexy girl from Queens.

Had an amazing birthday dinner here during the holidays. My bday was the weekend before Christmas so I was lucky to get a table but Gramercy Tavern handles it well. Our own personal hostess seated us for the first dinner seating and I noticed immediately how much space and privacy we had in the restaurant. You can tell they are very particular about not crowding folks which was definitely appreciated. We ordered off the 3 course prix fixe which offered a wide array of options. I might have preferred a few more but realized quickly that because everything is made so fresh they can tweak and change whatever you'd need in case you have dietary restrictions. We do not eat pork and our waiter noted the lamb sausage which came in one of the entrees and even confirmed the casing wasn't pork. Really impressed with this attention to detail. Food was delicious. Beef tartare, snapper in peanut sauce (with insanely fresh, seasonal veggies - yum!), apple cake as a dessert and the most delicious and beautiful coconut cake as a surprise for my birthday. They didn't skimp a bit and we were happily stuffed at the end of our meal. Also worth noting is when we were originally sitting down my husband nicked his finger on his chair. We found a small screw sticking out of the chair, so he simply asked if it could be replaced. The staff were so apologetic and word got out to the manager, who apologized personally and offered us a free round of drinks. We hadn't said a thing, and had moved on from the encounter, but they were so polite. What great service!

Great brunch deal but really just wanted to mention that the waiter was insanely nice. I noticed it throughout brunch but didn't say anything and as we were leaving my girlfriend noted the same thing. Very good food, excellent service, great brunch deal. Go!

awesome dumplings.. but you already know that.:) interesting family style where you end up sitting with another family.. if you dont like that - get a large group. The family did recommend a few dishes for me any my friend. Would go there again soon!

We ordered the ribs, pasta with rabbit and pesto, and steak and melon. Wasn't too fond of the pasta, but everything was great. They weren't kidding with the sweet and savory theme. For dessert, we ordered the bacon doughnuts! They were delicious.

Made reservations for my 24th birthday and I got there and it was sooo beautiful/intimate inside despite how the outside looks. My party say outside in there lovely garden area. The food was awesome. It had an authentic Italian taste. Overall I would recommend this place yo everyone.

A magical restaurant tucked away in a fairytale setting. The cocktails, wine & negronis exceed expectations. Quiet enough to actually heard your date or friends talk. A friend is an investor in this place but that doesn't stop me from really enjoying this adorable place. There are rumors of setting up a CSA for a local school.

Que Rico que Riko opened in my 'hood. Love Peruvian since back in the day when Coco Roco opened in Park Slope the first Peruvian in my old Â nabe...Peruvians are the culinary masters of South America and known for rotisserie chicken. Opened in a former Thai, Pio offers a daily meal of a quarter chicken, rice and beans or salad and fries for $6.50. Bravo that someone with culinary vision opened in a part of Chelsea near Penn Station that is forlorn of good/cheap eats save for Supreme Pizza and MoonCake Foods so welcome Pio Pio Riko.

On the advice of a friend I split the bicol express (a big chop) and the pancit and liked both a great deal. Also the portions are pretty substantial and splitting two entrees left quite a bit of leftovers. The chop was super tender and the brown sauce it came slathered with made a nice accompaniment for the garlic rice. The pancit had more going on than you could shake a stick at. I'll definitely come back.

I was looking for a new brunch spot and went here after reading good reviews and seeing rose water waffles and green shakshuka on the menu. Â It is in a great hood and is a nice looking spot but there is definitely nothing special about decor. Â Waited about 5 minutes for a table for two. Â Once we were seated the waiter took a while to come over and take our order. Â  Â We then had to wait forever for our food to come out. Â The hostess came over to apologize but it seriously took forever to come. Â My shakshuka was cold and the waffle tasted kinda like matzo. Â I can see waiting a while for food when a place is crowded at diner but not during brunch when you are making eggs and waffles. Â Seriously, how long does it take to make a waffle?! Â  With so many other great spots around, I will definitely not be back.

Been coming here since 1997 when they actually had Belgians working the front. That job's now been outsourced to Filipinos so it feels a little like home. Fries are still awesome, and usually rotate between the roasted eggplant mayo, mango chutney & parmesan peppercorn, depending on how sweet or savory i feel that day.

Very lively, great food and good music. I usually order the arroz con pollo, empanadas, churros and the french toast with fruits for my daughter! It's so delicious!!!! I love this place! I love to go here for brunch!

Hailing from LA, this is my new favorite taco spot! Came on a Thursday night and boy this place was poppin but my bf and I were able to get seated pretty quickly. Reasons to come: 1. This place is LA themed, so as a Lakers fan, this place is on point 2. Tacos are delish! I ordered the chorizo, steak, and chicken tacos 3. Good service. We were kept waiting for a bit on drinks and ordering of the food, so the waiter comped us our first round of drinks 4. Location. It's in the heart of the LES so barhopping after this spot is a must Needless to say, I'll be back quite often to satisfy my taco cravings. :)

This place is amazing. Â Full stop. Â Wandered in here last night for an early dinner with some friends. Â The staff was incredibly friendly and knowledgeable and the decor is super cute. Â Add in the fact that it is BYO and you cannot beat this place.

From Columbus Circle, getting here feels like a hike sometimes, despite what Google Maps might deceive you to believe. And this place is almost always overpacked around lunch hour. But wow are these burritos awesome. Plentiful, flavorful, and a ton of variety in what you put in it.

Will keep my review short and simple. Everything that can be said has been said. Â Went to Little Owl for a late lunch. Â Forgot my camera! Sorry no pictures. We love is place. Â Quality food and friendly service. Will go back to try other dishes. Cheers to good food and friendly service!

First and foremost the Bartender had the best playlist in a restaurant I've ever heard outside of a lounge setting; was there for brunch after an intense morning workout and napping in an Apple Soho's amphitheater. All I wanted was a good ole fashion American menu aka real pancake. Â In my Yelp search, Bubbys' menu was the only thing resembling my craving between Soho to TriBeCa area. The environment is farm kitchen cozy. Â Friendly server. Â I ordered the griddle special: sourdough pancakes, eggs and chicken sausage. Â The portion size was authentic. Â I received stack of two almost plate size fluffy golden brown pancake, overlaying the eggs and sausage. As I enjoyed every bite, engaged in caught up chatter with my pal, Â while simultaneously appreciating Al Green blurring in the sound waves.

That place is nice and the food is delicious! We had blood pudding (which was amazing) with apple mustard (the highlight of the meal, so sweet and sour, so subtle, really delicious) and cabbage with pancetta. Then a salad with spanish ham, curry and endives (and croutons and roasted almonds), very flavorful. For dessert, we shared the famous black forest charlotte and it lived up to its reputation, a real treat! However, it is sold for 2 but would be more appropriate for 4, which means that we took half home. Anyway, it was my only (minor) regret and it was as delicious when we had it that same night. Service was extremely kind and nice and while I'm not small (but not the tallest either) I had no problem fitting in the school tables, and liked the atmosphere of the place very much (and the great music).

Not worth the hype, in my opinion. My friends and I came here in a party of 3 and we were told that the wait time would be about 2 hours. We walked around until there were only 7 parties ahead of us. Skip ahead, and we are seated.. In a table that was meant for 2. We were all clumped together and we weren't allowed to change seats because of the amount of people that were waiting. I ordered the chocolate chunk pancakes and I thought it was way too sweet. My friend ordered the banana walnut pancake and said it could've been sweeter. My other friend ordered the omelette and thought it was okay. In the end, we all paid $22 each, with gratuity included in the bill automatically. This place is good as a one time experience but I wouldn't come back here. Maybe when they renovate the place to be bigger and fit larger parties, then I would venture back here but until then, it was a good experience.

The food and the cocktails here are super good. We had all appetizers - the yogurt with garlic and cucumbers, humus and the eggplant. We also had the calamari and Â a greek salad. The bread was fresh and delicious, but they aren't overly generous with it. Â Since our meal was all dipping sauces we needed a lot of bread. When asked for it, we got some attitude from our waitress. She also started giving us the hairy eyeball at 10:15 because she wanted us to leave, even though they didn't need the table and there were several other parties there. Prices were great. Would definitely go back in spite of the service.

This place is very good, I had the Vanilla Bean French Toast. They use 3 huge slices of bread, and surprisingly I had to stop before I can touch the 3rd slice. My girlfriend loves this place. She even became Mayor on Foursquare during our visit. I do recommend. Its an easy 4 stars but I didn't have a WOW factor

Great waitstaff, comfy and cozy without being cramped, good prices, and good food! Â I had the eggs benedict for a Sunday brunch, and it was great. Â Came with tea (or coffee) and orange juice, not to mention a pile of homefries. Â I got their homemade chili paste, which is worth a try.

I like this place, and have been several times, but be warned, their curries can be hot, I mean, incredibly, painfully hot, particularly the green curry which I would avoid altogether. I love hot and spicy food, but when you can't taste anything because your mouth is scalding, that is just silly. My friend ordered the green curry and I thought she was just being a wimp, then she had me taste some and it was ridiculous. She ended up sending it back. They were actually nice about it, and she ordered something else without fuss. Â So I'd just advise caution on their spicy/hot items - they border on sadistic. But they have a huge tome of a menu with plenty of choices so don't worry. They also have a lovely garden seating area in the back which is a lovely oasis in the summer time. The service isn't friendly but it's respectful, so overall I'd say it is a good experience.

The Malagueta Restaurant is an absolute GEM hidden in LIC. I have been dining at Malagueta since it first opened. The owners are both truly wonderful, kind, and honest people who REALLY know how to cook an amazing meal. The decor is very simple, Brazilian chic with the fabulous screaming Carmen Miranda painting on the wall. I highly recommend this restaurant, especially since the prices are and have always been VERY REASONABLE! Enjoy the fried yucca with Brazilian sausage appetizer, and anything from the dinner menu is DELICIOUS, but you must DEFINITELY not pass up on the Passion Fruit Mousse! :)

Went here last night and can't stop thinking about it..... Queens, why must you be so far away? I tried Tibetan butter tea for the first time and had vegetable momo (dumplings), spinach/radish thenthuk and aloo dum, all of which are recommended. The sauces here are off the charts- sinus clearing but not too spicy.. just enough for a heady gastronomic euphoria. Â Now I'm just counting down the days till I can go again ;)

I don't understand how this place can get so many 4-5 star reviews. The food here is less than average especially for tapas in NYC. I Â did not think the sangria was good and the decor was nothing special. The service also did not impress me. I will definitely not be returning here.

Their food is really good, but overpriced for "Vietnamese" cuisine. Maybe it's because I'm a chinese girl that usually gets her Viet fix in delish traditional Vietnamese joints in Chinatown. Is the price because they're a tad "fusion"? Maybe. But I personally feel like bunker is cashing in on the hipsters. Sorry, yes, I said it. Hipstahs. Cause Pho for $9+? Spring rolls at $7.50? By no means is a meal for $9 expensive, but a bowl of Pho for $9 is when you compare it to others. Awesome++ pork chops though.

There are no words to accurately describe the experience. 1) Know that you are going to wait a good long while. 2) Know that you are going to spend more money on pizza here than anywhere else and you will know it was a bargain. 3) Know that no other pizza will have a chance to be your favorite. 4) Know that you will leave very happy and return very often. See you in line!!

I don't give many 5 star recommendations but Le Parisien met my expectations fully. I found this cafe thanks to my fellow Yelpers by searching restaurants in Murray Hill and sorting by most stars. French food can be hit or miss but, to me and my wife, this is a hit. It's a small place between that seats about 30 people. The owner was our waiter and he's from Paris. Our dinners were authentic and perfectly prepared and the prices seemed reasonable. We came on a Monday night around 8:30 and had no trouble getting in but I'd suggest making a reservation on any other night.

Can this place please expand? This place doesn't have many seats, but then again it will be harder to maintain quality control of the food if it does expand. I love the house wine prices. It is very good! My gf took me here after Maison Premiere because she knows i love my beef. We shared scallops & clams as an app. For entree we shared the ax-handle ribeye for 2 - med rare, and it was cooked to perfection. It was a tad over-seasoned but it was yummy. Â A bit fatty for my taste but that's because I'm not a fan of ribeyes in general and prefer strips. However, that's where all the flavor is. We shared grilled bacon and pan fried mashed potatoes as a side. The bacon was ehhh. I had better at other places. The pan fried mashed potatoes were yummy though because it had a hint of truffle oil and it was crispy yet mushy at the same time. A great complexity with textures. For dessert we shared the cheesecake. However, i was a bit tipsy from the cocktails at Maison Premiere, Larry Lawrence, and the carafe of red wine during dinner that I do not remember how it tasted. I had the ill food coma by the end of the night all thanks to my gf who likes to reward my gluttony.

I love me some Bambino. I've probably been over 20 times since moving to Astoria. Favorite panini is the prosciutto with gorgonzola and fig spread. Soup is good too. I try to go to new places but end up here a lot!

Great neighborhood spot! Â I was staying at the TRYP hotel around the corner on West 35th and wanted a restaurant that was close to the hotel. Â I found Tavola on Yelp, and we had a great meal. Â The restaurant was completely full on a Tuesday night. Â It was a little on the loud side but not uncomfortably so. Â There is a short list of very fairly priced wines by the glass ($9-13); I had an Italian rose that was very nice. Â I had a Caesar salad to start that was tasty although somewhat over-dressed. Â My daughter had the rice balls (arancini), which were large (tennis-ball sized) and delicious. Â For mains, I had pappardelle with veal ragu that was one of the best pasta dishes I've ever had. Â Too bad I was too full to eat all of it. Â My daughter had a margherita pizza. Â We didn't try the desserts as we didn't have room. Â Service was friendly and prompt but not rushed. Â I would definitely go back if I'm in this part of NY again.

I'll give EV 4.5 overall. We've been there for both dinner and brunch, and both were great meals. Love the surrounding neighborhood, which seems to be well-represented in the many I'm-too-sexy-for-my-skinny-jeans types that populate the place. It's good people-watching. And it's good for a reasonable-for-Manhattan dinner with drinks or liquid brunch. Can't remember everything we've had there, but I can vouch for the fabulosity of the bloody marys, margaritas, Moroccan scramble, shrimp cobb salad, chicken sandwich, and pancakes. Even better: the Â prices aren't bad at all. We had to wait for a table for maybe 30-45 minutes during both visits, but these minutes passed pleasantly at the bar with drinks. The hostess was friendly and attentive; I remember she checked in on us while we were waiting. The place seems constantly busy but not packed to the gills. For the brunch visit, our waitress was something of a too-cool-for-school space case who shruggingly decreed some of the dishes "okay" when asked for recs and got my friend's order wrong, though the problem was corrected quickly.

Came in after a long cold day at storm king, the hostess and staff were super warm which was great cause i was frozen solid! It was a big group of us we sat up at the communal table by the bar, we all had different cocktails and they were all different and unique and very tasty everyone loved them. as for the food everything was on point nothing crazy just solid comfort couldn't ask for anything more. will definitely be back for more of those truffle fries and the katniss everdeen.

I went here on a Dine in Brooklyn deal, but I checked the prices afterwards and it's still not a bad deal. Â The place is not a fancy restaurant, but go in thinking casual seafood place with good food. Â The view is great and there's outside seating which looks like it'll be cool during the warmer weather. Â If you want to check out their menu, their website is outdated but their facebook is current. It has a nice very casual seafood joint feel, which I like since seafood is expensive to begin with,so Â why pay a premium for cloth napkins. Â The staff was very friendly and attentive, quick to clear any finished bowls and plates. Â The food was delicious. Â I ordered the peel and eat spicy shrimp as an app, the jumbo crabcake and apple pie. Â The spicy shrimp was awesome - seasoned perfectly, good size, good portion and cooked well. Â The crabcake was delicious, there was a lot of crabmeat and the sauce complimented it very well. The apple pie was warm, but left a little to be desired as it was a little dry - not terrible though. Â But hey, we're talking about apple pie at a casual seafood joint. Overall, I'd definitely say check this place out. Â I was reading the other reviews and went in with really low expectations, but in hindsight I have no idea where these people were basing them on. One big complaint was the prices. All i can say to this is that this is fresh fish, on the waterfront in New York City - This is NOT red lobster. Â Eat up and enjoy.

The hype is real! The chicken & rice bowl were amazingly delicious! Get the hot sauce on the side! It's super spicy! I love spicy foods and could barely handle the flamin' red sauce. One is big enough to share amongst two people. Beware, there are plenty of trucks in NY claiming to be The Halal Guys. You must look for the cart that says "The Halal Guys"

This is a nice airy brunch spot that is great on a sunny day. The restaurant has a very unique decor that I suppose is a cross between French and Moroccan (though I've never been to Morocco. The atmosphere is nice and the high ceilings make the space seem extra spacious. I'm told this place can get quite crowded during the prime brunch hours, but we go there early and were seated promptly. Another way to brunch this spot without any trouble is to make a reservation. They're well known for their avocado toast so we opted to try that and I can confirm that it is indeed very good. I'd recommend getting it if you go there. I had the baked eggs for my entree and it was decent! It wasn't the most filling meal, but it did the trick. In summary the atmosphere is great, the wait can be deceivingly long and the food is a-okay! Visit here when the weather is nice - it'll be worth the walk through the West Village

I'm sorry but glasses-girl has got to go! She practically begged us not to tip her. She mistakenly thought we were just ordering drinks and wanted to kick us out, forgot to bring items ordered and menus requested, never checked on us, EVER, and then asked if I wanted to take my untouched mulled wine to go (didn't drink it for a reason) since she needed the table. Again, she asked if I wanted to take my ALCOHOLIC BEVERAGE TO GO since she "needed the table." Um...... I mean WHAT?!?!?! It's just really sad because the food we tried, Grilled Eggplant with pesto, olive tapenade and goat cheese and the Chicken Cous-Cous were sooooo delicious. Plus, it's super cute! Damn.

Mm good cheap down-to-earth/homey Polish food. I tried the mushroom barley soup. Yum. Really creamy without being too heavy. Also had their polish platter. It's perfect if you're not sure what you'd like. Really liked the stuffed cabbage and the pierogies. The sauerkraut and mushroom pierogies again is delicious!
Great place, fantastic wine list, and a great staff. Â What's not to like?

I haven't been to SF in a long time, so I'm not even going to wade in to that whole raging burrito debate. Â But as an aficionado of Mexican eats, here's what I got to say. I almost walked right past Dos Toros. Â Literally a hole in the wall, I don't think they have any outdoor signage. Â My initial impression was not great; it's clearly a fast food style venue, with a few wooden tables. Â Conceptually, it's rather like a Chipotle: burritos, tacos, or a bread-free "plato," made with your choice of grilled steak, grilled chicken, or shredded pork, with similar pricing. Â But the flavors definitely put Dos Toros a notch above. Â I particularly liked the rice and the hard tacos, which are served in a freshly fried, semi-crisp yet chewy corn tortilla. Â The tacos are sold individually so you can mix and match to your heart's content, but the pricing seems a little off. Â They're about a third the size of the burrito, but half the price. All in all, not worth a special trip, but if you find yourself near Union Square, check it out.

Great place to go with a friend and saddle up at the bar for some drinks. Â Ducks tends to be less crowded than other east village places, so I haven't had an issue with getting a spot. Â Not much in the way of lighting, so if you'd like to take pictures, either bring a good camera or be prepared to flash away at your own risk. Â The house cocktails are all fabulous. Â I'd recommend the mint julep!

I came here last Thursday with two other people right at 6pm, and they were able to seat us within a few minutes. Â This was both good and bad, as the happy hour (2 for 1 Kirin and Sapporo) is only good at the bar until 8pm, and they can't transfer checks from the bar to your table. Â So we were all double-fisting on the way to our seats... quite an impression to make! Â It's ok though - the hostess was really nice about waiting for us to pay our tab. Â In general, the people who worked at Ippudo were fantastic - really friendly and welcoming. The food was also pretty great. Â I got the Akamaru Modern with the soft-boiled egg. Â I think if I'd ordered the extra pork it would have been too much... as it was, with the two beers and the brothy noodles, plus the (excellent!) pork buns and edamame (with delicious salt for sprinkling on top) we got for the table, I can't remember being so full in my life. Â My friend had ordered a side of spicy sauce, and I dumped some of that in my noodles, which added a great kick. Â I think I might have gotten sick of the broth if it weren't for the extra spiciness though. Â Also, my egg was hard-boiled, which was disappointing... I love soft-boiled eggs so I was particularly looking forward to it, and you'd think they'd get the cooking level right when it's an added extra thing you have to request and pay for. Â  I do think the prices are ridiculous - I ended up paying $16 for a bowl of noodles and egg and broth. Â But hey, there are tons of people willing to pay, as evidenced by the long wait times, and congratulations to them for doing so well in a city where it's tough to create a viable business out of a restaurant. Â I'll definitely go back, especially in cold winters.
Great pre-night out joint to stop in and grab a tasty Falafel!! Yum...had a great dinner.

One of my go-to brunch spots, I have been here dozens of times since moving to the neighborhood. I almost always get the goat cheese/tomato omelette and am always happy. I've also tried the duck hash and the huevos rancheros and enjoyed both. Honestly, though, my two favorite things about this place aren't even on the menu -- I LOVE the complimentary biscuits/jam they give you when you sit down (I could eat those all day every day), and the side of potatoes they give you with your eggs are so well favored and well cooked, I find myself scarfing those down before I even get to the eggs!

GREAT FOOD! Having said that... I don't know where they placed our coats (4 of them and a scarf). Two of the coats came back wet and stained. Cleaners kind of stain. Both are very good quality coats. The scarf...missing. SHAME ON YOU!

I've been going to Fish for seafood dishes but also because I want to try the AYCE blue crabs, today was my lucky day. I had AYCE blue crabs and I ate a lot..may be 16. They were well seasoned but too small & didn't have a lot of meat. I thought it would cost$21.95 but they recently increased the price to $24.95. I would say it was good but not great, will probably go back for seafood dishes but not the crabs...

Had the priveledge of trying the artichoke and spinach slice the other day in a quick stop in. It was wonderfully creamy and not overly heavy like some say. I really enjoyed the twist on the classic pizza and the namesake slice. Next time I looked forward to sampling the rest as the sicilian, margherita, and crab looked great too.

This review is just for the bread, which is among the best I've had from any artisan bakery in Brooklyn or elsewhere. Baguettes, buckwheat baguettes, Bolzano miche (a giant sourdough round with some seasonings)--all are amazing and affordable, perhaps unsurprising given that the guy in charge of the bread program used to work at Thomas Keller's Bouchon. $2.50 for a baguette; these guys, like the French, understand that bread is a basic human right. Okay, I'm joking a bit, but seriously... buy a loaf. Oh: and they bake multiple times a day, so it's usually fresh. Unbelievable.

Great brunch place. Nice Latin inspired creations. Attentive service. Pleasantly surprised by complimentary buttermilk biscuit, prosciutto and mole sauce aperitif. Rustic decor with cool ambiance (Sinatra and Louis Armstrong overhead). Highly recommend.

The first The best Mamoun used to make you a sandwich with a smiling "I make you like" He was right I always have a bottle of his hot sauce laying around Great to cook with Felafel/ Baba combo Lotsa tahini Salam, my friend
Make reservations! fills up quickly and for good reason. Excellent food, service, and atmosphere. Will become a favourite when visiting East Village.

It is a very clean with soothing organic energy restaurant. The owner self is a chef checking his customers with his smile ;) Â My boyfriend ordered parmesan chicken pasta Â and I ordered seafood pasta. Wow it was so delicious! And the best part of the finale was the dessert treated from the owner for my boyfriend's B-day. We only ordered two delicious pastas though, the owner's kindness gave us a happy moment and at home mood. Thank you. We marked your restaurant as the best year 2013.
So Good! It's, in my opinion, the best of the affordable Mexican cuisine spots in Manhattan.

i really love this place, but the tables tend to be cramped and ling waits to get in, i tend to go during they day to get my fix The arepas are like smallish I usually buy two to fill me up, it can be a bit much at like 16 for two basic ones but its way Â cheaper to make! and if you live in Williamsburg all of the ingredients are at the supermarket on Havemeyer I made the secret sauce at home its pretty close cilantro, parsley, e.v olive oil, cup vinegar, yellow peppers, mango I posted the full recipe with instructions on my blog, Â I also included a full recipe on how to make the pabellon Enjoy! cheekystitch.com

Amalfl The tuna sandwich was really good and delicious as at buonitalia in the Chelsea Market. That tuna changed my mind about tuna in a can or jar. The cherry tomato in the sandwich was a clever choice. I don't like a pale tomato that usually in a sandwich. The texture and sweetness of sliced cherry tomato made the sandwich fresh taste but the sandwich was rather dry, adding EVO helped. Paestum The quality prosciutto and a creamy-milky mozzarella were so simple and delicious. . The morning special (croissant and coffee) $3.50 is a steal.

Not so great. Â The place itself is pretty cool, though, dark and old and with lots of character. Â We got a seat right away, and ordered a few burgers, fries and a grilled cheese. Well, the fries were marginal, the burgers were raw and the grilled cheese wasn't even melted all the way through. Â No sign of cheddar even, just plain old American chz. Disappointing.

Great rustic atmosphere and attentive service. The polenta defines the standard. Brochettes with ricotta. Black truffle oil and honey a delicate and well executed balancing act. The fish/shellfish in a light tomato sauce with small octopus an amazing value. Great fairly priced wine list. It is very busy after 7pm. We got there at 6 and it was perfect. Everything done to perfection

Great place for a bite when you are bar hppping in the village. The falafel is great. Also love the Â Shawarma kabab. Narrow with limited sitting places. Best is to a take-out and sit on one on the apartment steps close by and dine with your date :)
too salty, too much oil and the wait is not worthwhile.
BEST tasing menu of 2014! take my word or not. I'd rather you maintain some doubt, so next time i want to make an RSVP ther would still be an open seat :P

Each visit I make to Manhattan is packed with awesome friends sharing perfect nights out. Dinner at Blue Ribbon Brasserie didn't disappoint! I was staying in SoHo and was happy to be able to walk to dinner. I met a friend at the bar for a drink while we waited for the rest of our party to show up. I have to say, the only reason why I'm giving this place 4 stars instead of all 5 is due to neither of our cocktails being well made. My dirty martini was cleaner than if I had ordered it with a twist and I was in desperate need of a 7 o'clock cocktail after such a terrible flight. The host/manager was charming and provided us with just the right balance of attention and space. He left us alone while we waited but seated us in a flash as the two girlfriends we were waiting for met us at the bar. He and our server visited often enough to keep our wine and water glasses full. The four of us started out with a dozen oysters and the vegetable basket. The table agreed, these were possibly the best oysters we have ever had. I ordered the Shrimp Provencal. The cheese ravioli was sinfully, melt in your mouth good and went surprisingly well with the bottle of malbec we shared. There were two steak orders and a duck entree and zero bites left by the time our plates were cleared. When our server asked if we'd like dessert I explained that I was only in town for a few nights and wanted to roam around SoHo for a drink at lounge and dessert elsewhere so we could hit three spots in a night. Instead of pushing the menu, he laughed and told us to have fun tonight. When we asked for his favorite places in walking distance, he sent us to a truly perfect choice two blocks away. Thank you! Since I always end up staying in SoHo, I will definitely revisit.

My downstairs coffee bar. A go-to every morning, great prices and coffee that actually tastes like coffee. The service is fantastic, quick and the baristas are cheerful early in the morning. When coffee isn't your fix, they have local ice cream sandwiches that can make any hot summer day more bearable. Overall, this little coffee shop in a quiet part of Â the street is a great place to stop in and recharge your batteries.
Delicious!!!! Loved lunch deals omg guasacaca lol best sauce ever!
Food was amazing, I really enjoyed the clam pasta dish. It was a lot of food that I was not able to finish my meal. Def would go back if I am in the area.

The food here is absolutely delicious. I ordered the grand slam and wasn't disappointed. The katsu is fried until crunchy, the sausages taste like hotdogs but with a crispy skin, and the curry was very tasty.

I have a confession to make. I'm actually a vegetarian.
