We headed to the closest place we could see from the Brooklyn Museum, and I could smell the jerk and it smelled so good, and then someone walked past with plates full of jerk chicken, so I decided to have jerk lamb, but they were out, so I slid all the way to the bottom of the vegetarian totem pole and ordered the chicken. It is the first time I have had chicken in years and it was totally worth it. And, well, if you're gonna cheat, you might as well cheat with the finest. Good god, it was delicious. I'm not ashamed. I may even have wept a little bit.
I could eat an entire meal of just the yellow rice and red beans. Rotisserie chicken and steak with onions are both excellent

This is actually a five star review. Champs is a conveniently placed location for me to entertain clients, being situated literally around the corner makes it an amazing place to host meetings, in a great contemporary lively environment. Â The food is always delicious, even when they sell out of popular items, it is a positive, as they were obviously so busy that day selling delicious food. Even though I am not a vegan, the food here is just so good that insist clients to try it out, most leave shocked at the quality. Â  After visiting Champs many times to take a coffee meeting, the amazing staff being super accommodating people they are keep a dairy milk stash in one of the refrigerators, I could enjoy my coffee the way that I liked. Â With real dairy milk! Â It was like having an 'in'. No more! Â Apparently there have been a number of complaints that an innocuous carton of milk was spoiling the dining pleasure of the more austere vegans that frequent the establishment, voicing their displeasure has forced the management to remove this sneaky little opulence. Best coffee in the neighborhood, just got spoiled for me, I am sad.

I've been going to this place for years for special occasions with my wife. Â It is our FAVORITE restaurant - period. Â This title is bestowed across all genre's of cuisine. Â The first time there was for a pre-fixe valentines dinner and we've been going back for all special occasions. Â When that wasn't enough we started going for somewhat special occasions and at this point we just go. Â No need to even look at the menu as the waiters will give you the extensive specials list. Â The food is always delicious. Â Blue Marlin carpaccio appetizer and caramelized onions on steak are two dishes we love but we always try something new on the specials list each time we go. Â Service is always superb and when someone asks for a new restaurant this is the place we send them.
yummy, humongous portions however, the wait took forever.. i came for my birthday in mid-december and we waited about an hour
The best BBQ I've had in NYC. The BBQ sauce is delicious, just the right blend of sweet and spicy. The meat is tender and juicy. Pro tip: Order the cornbread.

We were looking for a cheap late dinner (10:30pm) option which was still open on a Monday in SoHo and found Mooncake had great reviews on Yelp and reasonably priced dishes. I ordered the Pork Chops and my girlfriend had the Sliced Steak. The pork chops were good, while the Sliced Steak was sub-par - meat was just too chewy. The menu didn't mention anything but the rice that came with my pork chops was very very spicy, something which I don't like. Overall, I found the restaurant reasonably priced and decent, but it's definitely overrated here on Yelp. You probably won't regret if you go there, but you probably also won't have fond memories for too long, either. It's an honest and cheap place to eat.

Walk through an unmarked entrance with a psychic sign and pass into Employees Only. Â A speakeasy-esque bar in the quaint West Village that sure carries itself some swagger. Â There is actually a fortune teller working there every night of the week, so after a drink you can even get your fortune read. Â  This place is pretty awesome. Â Went here on a week-night date here and was lucky enough to try a variety of drinks. Â The bartenders make all of the drinks with great care and your cocktail will be perfectly. Â The Lazy Lover and the Ginger Snap were the most tasty drinks I sampled, but really with any cocktail you can't go wrong. Â Drinks are pricy though, $16 a pop, so be warned. Â  Weeknights are probably the best nights to visit this hot-spot since the bar is rather small and it fills up quite quickly. Â There is ample seating and I can just see this as a miserable place to be if there is no place to sit and enjoy your cocktail.

So many places in Chinatown, so few that you will go back to 5+ times. Â Spicy Village deserves a spot in your Chinatown dining list for a bunch of reasons but hey ... I'll talk about the friendly and tasty ones. The small restaurant is really unassuming from the outside and when you go in you just have to find yourself a table and sit. Â The owners will come out to ask what you want with a sweet smile and make you feel like your one of their longtime friends visiting. Â Seriously - I always get a nice smile and no attitude at all. The whole menu looks satisfying however I've consumed A LOT of the pork pancakes (for a mere $2.50) on my quick walks through Chinatown that could be a small meal. Â The bun that gets stuffed is toasted to order and stuffed with sweet and smoky shredded roasted pork. Â There is some cilantro in there and some sort of sauce situation too - in case cilantro is a deal breaker. Spicy Village serves up a huge fulfilling meal with their Spicy Big Tray Chicken: an enormous platter of chicken with mouth numbing Sichuan peppercorns. What you'll get is ... you guessed it .. a big sizzling tray of spicy chicken, potatoes, and veggies in hot chili oil that you are going to eat every last bit of. Â You can easily split this amongst 3 or 4 friends. Get going .. you have something spicy to order!

I'm so incredibly happy I stopped in here for dinner last night. Can we talk about the guacamole being the most freaking amazing I've ever had? The service is killer! You rarely get treated so well in New York. The atmosphere is casual yet the food is just perfect. Will return often!

This review is only for their cheesecakes. I came here on a Sat night after a nice dinner somewhere else. They have a separate entrance for the bakery/cheesecakes and another entrance for the restaurant. The bakery section wasn't crowded. They have all the cheesecakes displayed and packed. The size of the cheesecakes are pretty big and less than $10 each. I got two different types of cheesecakes. One is the cheesecake with strawberries and another is the strawberry short cheesecake. Both were $7.25 each. cheesecake with strawberries - 7/10- Â The cheesecake part was amazing! But once you get to the strawberries, jam, and gram cracker pieces it ruins the taste as a whole. The strawberries tasted really old, the jam tasted funky like there is this strong vinegar or alcohol taste in the jam and the gram cracker pieces didn't taste like gram crackers at all. Overall it felt like I should have paid for a regular plain cheesecake because that was the best part out of everything else. Strawberry short cheesecake- 8/10- This is a combination of a strawberry shortcake and a cheesecake together, hence the name. It tasted like eating a yellow birthday cake with strawberry cheese filling in the middle and in between two layers of strawberry jam with strawberries and whip cream all around. Presentation is nice and it does taste great. Nothing tasted wrong or old and the sweetness level is just perfect. I did not give it a 10 because I was sad that I tasted more of the cake than actually the cheesecake. I actually liked the cheesecake above but without the strawberries stuff. Overall I would come back here for a regular slice of cheesecake and their milkshakes. I saw a few people ordering milkshakes at the restaurant and it looks amazing and yummy. There are limited seating for those who only want to purchase from their bakery section. It is a good place to have dessert after a meal with friends or partner. It is away from the busy parts of Manhattan so it is not too noisy.

I received an apology from the Service Manager at Perilla, and I like that they took the time to check and see what made the service not on par with the meal. Â It may only be my experience, but the fact that they want to address the issues is important to me. Â Thanks for checking in Perilla! Â I will return.

Ambiance = 4. The seating arrangements make this restaruant feel a lightly cramped, especially for the UES, but this does lend itself to a cozy and unpretentious atmosphere (think, good option for date #2 or dinner with your parents). Â  Service = definite 5. Very attentive and polite servers who did not rush. Food however, is just a 3. The tomato/burrato dish the best part of the meal, but by no means outstanding. I also ordered the eggplant/ricotta dish and the pesto cavatelli, neither of which felt appropriately seasoned and therefore lacked any excitement. Â  If you come here with a date, stick to the wine and some of the simpler small plates and cheese selections. Other than the quality of the service, this was not a very memorable meal I probably won't be back, there are too many other better Italian options in NYC.

Awesome BBQ brisket sandwich! Choice beer. Swank ambience. And not touristy/hokey like Dallas BBQ. On par with Fette Sau with a step above Chipotle feel. What more could you want? Come here if you're hungry and not vegetarian. You will not be dissatisfied.

I only recently moved to Astoria, but I've been here a few times since and even before the move. The vibe is very relaxing (during the week, weekends are a bit crazy) and the dim lighting can actually make it a great spot for grabbing drinks on a first date or getting together with a few friends. There's an eclectic mix of people that come here, from hipsters to locals to... umm just normal folks. They have a pretty good beer selection.. but you won't find Bud Light, Coors, Miller, etc. Their simplest light beer is Amstel Light. I haven't tried any of the cocktails yet either but I'm not reviewing how their drinks are since you can get the same drinks anywhere if you wanted to. The bartenders work pretty quickly too, so you're not waiting forever to grab a drink. There is a fair amount of seating, but it's usually hit or miss if you can grab a table or seat. No big deal, either way. The atmosphere and coziness of this place makes it a good spot. Hmm, I really don't have that much more to say, except for the fact that I really like this place. To sum it up: Sweet Afton is the perfect mix of sexy, rustic, and modern vintage.

On my first real trip to new york with my girlfriend and randomly stopped in on a Saturday. Wasn't dissapointed at all. Good food, good atmosphere, and good service. Would definitely come catch a game and grab some food here in the future.

Fantastic meal and service. Â Pizza was very good and the Lasagna was phenominal. Â I also tasted the Veal Scaloppine Piccata and it was excellent. Â Even the selection of bread was great. Â Our waiter was very attentive and timed the meal perfectly since we were seeing a show afterwards. Â Very impressive restaurant.

So after an afternoon on the high line, my girlfriend and I went here during a hankering for tapas. No reservations on a saturday so we sat in the lounge area. We ordered some Â tapas to start: octopus, pork belly, patata bravas, and razor clams. All were very good but those razor clams were freaking awesome. Feeling we could stuff our faces with a bit more we ordered shrimp and foie gras dish. By then, we felt that service was a bit slow, but considering how busy it was, it was understandable. The shrimp came out and then nothing. A full 30 minute wait nothing. Then another 5 of waiting to see where our waitress was before finally spotting her to flag her down (who had not really showed up in the last 15 min before either). And yet another 10 for it to come out. Although annoyed at the wait, we let it go as soon as we took a bite. The foie gras was the one of the best foie gras dishes I've had. And I've had it at Per Se. But then... the third bite. Foie gras should be mouth temperature at the coolest. It should never be... "did this just come out of the fridge?" cool. We waited for the the waitress to come around, and let her know about the dish. We received a replacement in 10 (so pretty sure they forgot about the dish the 1st time around). Cooked perfectly. Excellent dish. Overall, it was excellent food, but total dining time was almost 3 hours. When other tables were in and out in 2, service was lacking, but I'm thinking it's because we sat in the lounge area. As for the 4 star rating, despite the service, I would return for the food, and that's not something I would typically do.

Better bang for your buck than Vanessa's at 5/$1. Â Tried the pork n chive and it tasted just like Vanessa's Dumpling House on Eldridge ...and was just as greasy. Â Anyone that yelps the ability to taste a difference either has the palate of Tony Bourdain or is a fibbin' tool. Â Enjoy them both - Â to go - since neither place has "ambience" or "seating".

Went here for the first time yesterday and I can see why everyone is into the hype. It's a great space with a really friendly waitstaff. They played Nirvana's whole discography which was pretty awesome. Not much for vegan folks though.
Great food, nice people, It was not expensive and the place was clean. Great choice for an informal place with great indian food. It is not a pretty restaurant but it is very good
Had chicken risotto with olive and pepper. It's an ok place and you can find better food places for this price in the hood. I don't know why there is so much hype.

The pizza was tasty and the Italian soda was even better! Â Definitely go when you have time to wait and aren't starving. Â  I had a wonderful creamy beer they had on tap, worth a try if they still have it.

Barbuto was delicious. The wine director was extremely helpful, our server was less so, but we had a great time and the food was wonderful-I would recommend it to anyone. I want to make sure to mention that the support staff (runners, bussers) were outstanding. We never needed water, and never had to look far to ask for something. Our server didn't help us navigate the menu well, and wasn't very present. He talked around the menu ("nothing is necessarily better than anything else, it's just different") and didn't give any helpful descriptions of anything when we asked about particular dishes. That aside, we loved what we did order. Here is what we ate: Appetizers: Marinates olives salumi (a meat plate with some crostini which was delicious, like every meat plate) duck liver pate (really unbelievable) Â  Pasta Course: Spicy Sausage Ragu (absolutely delicious) Gnocchi (so good) Entree: -Pollo Al Forno (so delicious, this is what this place is known for-it's a must) -The Steak (really outstanding, this place is known for chicken but the steak is out of this world, perfectly prepared and so delicious) -Swordfish (most disappointing thing I ate all night. The fish wasn't fresh and was overcooked, it came recommended by the server (as I mentioned earlier wasn't as helpful as he should have been)) Â  Sides: Greens and potatoes (both outstanding) Â  Dessert: Chocolate Bundino (amazing, there's a reason everyone recommends this thing) Â  Initially I was worried dining here, because places that are trendy usually end up with mediocre food and service, and it was not at all the case with Barbuto. The food lived up to the hype, and I would happily eat here again.

A fun neighborhood spot, always inviting, shabby looks with wood chips on the floor and a real wood fireplace burning in the cold months (yep, quite a fire hazard). The staff is nice, the atmosphere is lively (this place is never empty). Beers are basic but good. The Fish & Chips are our favorite thing on the menu; they are as good as the stuff you get at the other side of the big pond. The hamburgers are really nice too. The Shepherd's Pie is actually a Cottage Pie (it's made of beef, not lamb or mutton) isn't as great as one would expect which is a shame. I do not suggest it. The portions are quite generous and for a $3 charge they will split it for you onto two plates for two people. Just a proper and solid enjoyable neighborhood gem we love.

We ordered Salmon and Gluten Free eggplant pasta. It was without a doubt the best gluten free vegetarian pasta ever, I have been to a lot of Italian places for this perfect flavor. I was delighted and so was my husband, he said his Salmon was very flavorful.

I love this restaurant, and this type of Filipino packaged in a setting like this is a long time coming. The menu is amazing from a selection standpoint. There are usual suspects (Longonisa, Adobo, etc.) and also unique items I had never heard of (even as a Filipina having grown up in a Filipino food household), like this wonderful smokey eggplant appetizer. Also great from an atmosphere perspective. Impressed all around.

We really like coming here because it has 3 of our favorite dishes - mango chicken, roti canai and the crispy golden fried squid. We wished their portions were a little bigger compared to Penang nearby. Also, their mango chicken is not as good as Penang's because their mangos are usually not ripe enough and are a little hard and sour. At Penang's, their mangos are softer and sweeter. It is a lot cleaner here than at Penang though!

If you are looking for a quality pizza place around this area.. this is your place. Â  Little Italy is filled with tourist traps and this maybe one of them. Â But the food is actually good. Â Where else are you going to get authentic NY pizza (thin crust) pizza? Â  Â Plus the beer selection is delicious. Only complaint I have is because the pizza is so thin if you don't eat it fast enough the center kind of gets soggy :( Hint: if you are going for lunch get there at 12 and there is always a spot.

Worth the wait it takes to get your food. Everything is made fresh to order, and you can tell. The bread is crispy and delicious and the coffee is tasty. The place itself is tiny but spotlessly clean.
Best milkshakes in Brooklyn!

I always come here for happy hour whenever I'm in the Les. They definitely have one of the longest running happy hours in town, until 10 pm. The best happy hour drink to order here is the lychee martini. It is pretty strong and only $5. Definitely cheaper than Tao's. However, I have tried the other happy hour drinks and they are kind of weird. The sangria is kind of chunky with weird fruit in it. The Vietnamese bloody mary you should definitely stay away from. I ordered it for the first time last Thursday and it definitely isn't your run of the mill bloody mary. I think they try to mix it up by adding serracha hot sauce and there is definitely chunks of ginger in there. I felt like my mouth was on fire and I was choking on ginger. You also kind of feel like a vampire when you drink in here because it is very dimly lit inside, so in the summer time I prefer to go somewhere with an outdoor area as well.

Had a great time here with a small group on saturday night--got there early to catch dinner before some other plans and the line was minimal. The staff was great! I was worried about the "no substitutions" on the menu, but the waitress confirmed that all my choices were ok with my food concerns! I had the ropa vieja-- DELISH. Nothing more annoying than ordering ropa vieja and getting a giant bowl of peppers and onions with two or three little chunks of meat. this was almost all meat!!! FANTASTIC! Also really dug the sangritas :) would love to come back when it's warmer to try and sit in the back!

(Having been only once, I'll give this place 4 stars for now.) If you enjoy Chinese pancakes, noodles, buns, fried or soupy dumpling goodness, you've come to the right place. If you've got less than 5 bucks in your pocket and looking to roll out of an establishment, you've come to the perfect place. At Vanessa's, you can get 4 delectable dumplings for $1! I recommend the pork and chive fried dumpling. Don't forget to dip them in spicy soy sauce! Â Mmmmm....quick, anyone have a dollar?

I didn't particularly like being stuffed into a tight corner table in the back when the restaurant was rather empty. $25 wine menu is very reasonable and has some decent Â wines, however the soiled cork that I noticed on the final glass was disappointing. We had the all you can eat three pastas and found them rather good. The antipasto appetizer that it came with was terrible (we should have choose the other option which was a caesar salad). The server said the chilled seafood on the antipasto was swordfish and it turned out to be not fresh tuna. The antipasto portion was tiny and seemed to be pre-plated and straight from a jar or can. Service was decent and far from great.

Love their happy hour would probably only come for the happy hour. The staff were nice and patience since we sat at a table for 4 and it took our friend 30 minutes to arrive. We did order food as we sat. I would only come for happy hour because the portions are pretty big for happy hour prices. I thought since it was cheap they'll cut back the portions like most places. I also ordered sushi off the happy hour menu, prices weren't too bad but the quality of the fish wasn't top grade. But hey you get what you paid for. I usually go to Jins for happy hour sushi but I think I found my new spot when I'm in town.

Five star lunch joint. The ladies and gentlemen at Tina's serve up some mean rice and beans (come mon,wed,fri for the black beans) with a meat of your choice. Great Pollo al Horno, Better Pernil, Amazing Ropa Vieja and I wish I could just stuff my face in the tray of maduros---what?

Seafood lovers rejoice. There is a place with great value, reasonably priced seafood, and with preparation so delicious I came here twice in a week. The Boil does seafood done Cajun style..you choose your seafood, which is sold by the pound, then your sauce, then a level of spice. Sauces are dry, lemon pepper, garlic butter, and ol bay. The Boil special spice is all of the above and the one I recommend..what you get, be forewarned, is enough garlic to fill a bowl with. The best values are the combos because you get corn, potatoes and sausage with them if you are a meat eater. Two lbs of anything gets you corn and potatoes. The boil has it down pat so they save on washing and you are guaranteed hygiene. You get your boil in a plastic bag, along with plastic gloves, and a plastic apron. Appetizers are in paper containers. Your waste bucket is a steel bucket lined with plastics. Super easy cleanup! The first time we ordered the catfish basket...the fish was cooked to tender perfection and lightly breaded and the Cajun fries excellent. A huge portion, I was getting slightly full from it. Then we had the 2 lb combo of Crayfish and shrimp. And what tasty, tender, jumbo shrimp they were! Such a pleasant surprise from the smallish shrimp we were expecting. .And tons of crayfish..it was a heaping bag. And coated with millions of bits of garlic(so if you don't like garlic, ask them to scale down). We ordered medium and it came spicy. On the second outing my party ordered Â oyster sliders(delicious,and plump and delicate) and clams and more shrimp.Again the food was cooked to perfection. the clams tender and so juicy and plump and what is becoming a standby the Boil special sauce for it along with the shrimp. This time, we ordered medium spice again and strangely enough, it was not as spicy as the first time(which was only two days prior). Kitchen standards! The Boil is dark(we chose to sit in comfort at the tables in the back) and has a lively bar scene up front. Do the aprons and the gloves unless you want garlic all over your fingers. Our waitress the first time was exceptionally friendly, the second time another waitress serves us and was sweet. The bartenders however are intimidating...boys.. when guests come through the door you don't stare, you SMILE. Hence 4 stars instead of 5. Still , The Boil is a place I'd return to over and over again. Oh, just a note..it is CASH only. Also, don't go during prime dinner time. Try to get there by 6 or before. Skip lunch, it's that good.

Lunch was onion soup (presaged by that unmistakable waft of gruyere -- it nearly knocked me over), a decent beet salad with remarkably soft bunches of mache, and a Chimay Red. Â Then I went shopping in my woozy beef broth & trappist ale stupor. Â Best day ever!

A dinner at the Dumpling House is a stressful affair: first you have to stand in the long line to be barely acknowledged by the counter person, then try and get a table hungrily awaiting for your number to be called. The competition for space can get intense: expect to be snapped at or to snap at that unconscionable person who grabs an empty table right before you sit down. But the food is divine, addiction-inducing, cheap, and worth being elbowed, pushed, shoved, and given dirty looks to. Sesame pancakes are a must.

I tried the pizza, bagels, delis in NYC and this cart was my favorite meal. Â I had to come back on my last night to get it again. Â I tried the mixed platter the first time and found that I liked the lamb better so returned for the lamb platter on the second night. The wait was about 30 minutes in the freezing cold. Â It comes with two packets of white sauce and one small hot sauce. Â I mixed it all in for a good sauce to meat and rice ratio. Â I wish there was one in my town. Â  There's another cart trying to copy this one - not sure if it is as good but I'm guessing not since the line here was way longer than the other one. Â The real deal is on the southwest corner.

Great Pizza!! Got pepperoni and pruscuttio. The pizza had great flavor and it was nice and hot when it arrived at our table. It was a nice Friday afternoon so the servers were bussling in and out and didn't give us much attention at the bar. I refilled my own water and had to cancel my order for my salad with the bus boy because I never saw the person who took our order. It is pricey so I would expect a little better service than what I'd get from papa gino's.

Dekalb restaurant is amazing! Really great food and a relaxed atmosphere. Eat the lamb, the Gnocchi, the Polenta fries (!!!!), the brussel sprouts and probably anything else on the menu because it all seems great! Even better, Dekalb is BYOB for the moment so you can get out of there for very cheap. There is a well stocked corner store practically next door with some pretty good beer. Eat here, I promise you will love the food!
The booths ROCK! Super comfy! Staff was nice and drinks were pretty good. I cant wait for summer here, the windows are to die for! And the horse w the balls....(youve gotta be there to understand)

The pork katsu curry is their specialty. Â Normally I get the medium size and it's more than enough for me. Â Please don't get the home-run special unless you are sharing it. Â Eating it alone will probably give you a heart attack after because it's a really hefty portion =) The katsu curry comes with rice and a side portion of cabbage, along with a meat based curry sauce. Â The pork katsu is crispy, tasty and tender. Â Pork chops are normally quite chewy in the US, but they make it just right here. This is not bad choice for lunch, it's only $8 and change. Â  The place is a bit old though, they should renovate it. 1 star off for this. Also, on numerous occasions, they over-fry the pork chop, as a result, it becomes dry and dark, so another star off for this.

If you want to try some authentic Dosas you've come to the right place. The food is cheap and tastes super fresh. The samosas are also fantastic.I waited almost 20 minutes for the food, which I don't mind at all. The food there are fulfilling. The guy that is making the dosas is so friendly. The sambar is alright, not too crazy about it. Overall, I would come there once in a while to satisfy my cravings.

After seeing thousands of reviews for a single restaurant, I set my expectation for this place sky-high and really want to know how good this place is compared to the godly Ichiran Ramen in Tokyo. I went there Monday 12.00 pm and didn't have to wait at all. Pork bun was excellent but ramen was very disappointed. I had their black-tonkatsu ramen and the first thing I noticed was how thin the chashu was. It was paper thin. A lot thinner than the pork that came with pork bun. The soup was generic so I didn't want to slurp it bottom up. The worst thing about this place is the price. Two bowls of noodles and 2 buns costed me almost $50. Not really worth it. I don't know if Ippundo is the best ramen in NYC but the quality is not even close to many generic ramen shops you can find in Japan.

I don't get why this place is such a huge deal. First of all, this restaurant fails as a ramen place. It's more like udon. The broth is good but they definitely skimp on the toppings. Pork buns are also average. I'm just saying, for the quality and taste of the dishes the prices and wait time is not even close to worth eating here. Especially since NYC is full of far superior ramen places.

We stopped by on a Saturday and they quoted us a 1.5 hour wait. Â That day, instead, we chose to go to Frankies (on the same block across the street), which was amazing (read my review). Â Anyways, we went back on a weekday to Clinton St. and only waited a half hour. Â We ordered the blueberry pancakes with maple butter, biscuits with Â homemade raspberry jam and sugar cured bacon. Â You HAVE to try their bacon. Â It is incredible.
Best desserts in the city!

I always think of my wonderful Armenian grandfather kicking from his grave when I go to a "Turkish" establishment. But it's New York City in the 2000's, my angel. And anyway, just for you, I'll describe Beyoglu as "Mediterranean / Middle Eastern." Delicious hummus and pita. I can't even call it pita. It's better than pita. It's soft white fluffy-but-crisp goodness with sesame seeds. Also deserving of a shout-out: the cacik, dolma, and phyllo + feta. Friends have raved about the branzino, but since I don't eat fishies I can't comment personally. I'm always a sucker for a Greek salad; Beyoglu's is nice, pretty standard. Service is usually attentive and helpful. On my most recent visit, the waiter was the sweetest thing. But I've also been sneered at in the past. All up, same as most Manhattan restaurants, I guess -- every waitperson/host/etc has good days and bad. It's quite cozy inside in the winter, and in the warmer weather it's a lovely place to sit outside. Finally, my eloquent assessment of Beyoglu's wines by the glass: they suck.

This place is super popular and hard to get into. Both times I have been here the hostess told me it was a 1 hour wait - yet suddenly we were seated within 5-10 minutes! Don't be discouraged if they tell you it's a long wait...it's not. The food is excellent and so are the drinks. The empanadas are my favorite - especially the goat cheese and the guava. They have an extensive drink menu and they make some of their own liquor too!

Was I hiding under a rock? Election night- 2/2009 (yes, I know I am a bit behind here) So much energy in the city. My college friend and I stopped at Ara for wine. We were contemplating where to go to dinner when the bartender insisted, "You must go to Scarpetta!" Loved it! Getting back to the rock- while watching Top Chef, one of the guest judges just happened to be Scott Conant. Little did I know Â when I was under the boulder that we were in the company of greatness. We arrived at Scarpetta without a reservation and were kindly offered one of the high tables in the bar. I actually believe it is one of the best tables in the house, more casual than the dining room but a great vantage point for viewing the incoming and outgoing scene. Our Russian waitress was a doll face. Her wine reccomendation was outstanding. We also were fortunate enough to have the maitre d looking out for us. Incredible food and Super service!

The standards for Mexican food in NYC are not that high! When I am in NY I lower my standards for Chinese, Mexican and a few other cuisines. This is authentic but authentic doesn't always mean good. Not bad just average. The chips were cold not fresh and the tacos were authentic but average. The meat was dry. Â For NYC it gets a 3 for authenticity. Outside of NY it would get a 2. We have a large Mexican community but diners here do not demand good food and when you get used to eating mediocre food you get all excited when it is mediocre and authentic. Not much else to say really. If you live in the neighborhood it is fine but it doesn't warrant a special trip. It is better than Tacos Matamoros in Sunset Park. That was too sloppy. Not really sloppy aesthetically. But how it tastes. This is more to the point crisper flavors. But not as good as Tacos Al Suadero in Queens. But if you live in the neighborhood it is fine for an inexpensive meal.
The driest roast chicken I have ever had. But the escargot and salad are good and our server is amazing! Quite pricey place concerning the food quality though.

Excellent ambience, very comfortable. Sat by a window seat on a sunny afternoon and enjoyed the street view. Service was excellent and attentive. The portions were small for the price though and was a little bit disappointed at that. Dessert was a chocolate molten cake with ice cream for my birthday, which was quite decadent and wonderful. All in all a mixed experience.

This place is classy! Not pretentious-classy, but definitely the classiest place in the neighborhood. The fusion of french american cuisine makes my mouth water. They cut all the meat themselves on the premises! The chef(Joe) is a master of his craft and you can tell by the taste of the food and by talking to him that he is passionate about cooking. Overall the staff was amazing, engaging , and happy. Had a burger and fries last time I was there and it knocked my socks off!( The fries come in a little bucket!)
The best Malaysian food from the truck . Delicious curry dishes and pleasant customer service experience. Â  Â  Â  Â  Â  Â  Â  Â  Â  Â  Â  Mamak A food truck gold mine!!!!!!!

Very good, perfect flavors. Nicely cooked, not too well done or dry! This place can get busy so be ready to order when it's your turn. Can be a bit tough to find seating when it's crowded but do not let this small detail turn you away since it really is worth a visit!

I should start by saying I absolutely love this place and have been eating here for nearly 10yrs. Â I live in the neighborhood luckily, but when I didnt, it was still my go to place. Â I really enjoy the cool and relaxed ambiance, the friendly staff and the food is consistently good...not to mention a great value! My one gripe about this place, the reason for not giving this place 5 stars is the wine menu... I wish they would get a new one, one I can understand. Â Its a good thing that I know what I want (I generally get the same thing!) because theres no point in trying to decipher all the animal pictures or read the small font. Â I wanna come in a restaurant, look at the menu and easily hone in on what I'd like to drink. Go Yankees!

Went to Locanda Verde for brunch after moving downtown and I've been looking forward to this for a while now since I'm usually too lazy to travel for food. So here's what I thought: Reservation: I called a day prior, they only had a 2 pm brunch reservation available on Sat. So I took it, but when I asked about possibly walking in earlier, I was informed by the hostess that if I was interested in an earlier walk-in, she'd much rather give my reservation to someone else who would really appreciate it. Not rude, but left a weird taste in my mouth. I also asked about a standard wait time for walk-ins on weekends, the hostess said she would not know, so 2 pm it is. Seating: Showed up right on time and we were starving, and was seated promptly by one of the three hostesses. Staff was professional if not overly friendly. Pros: food taste great, well thought out and service was fast if not super attentive. Bloody mary was amazing and so was the sheep's milk ricotta to start. The warm garlic focaccia was to die for. Cons: EntrÃ©e execution was borderline terrible. The poached Uovo Modenese had one poached correctly and the other cooked all the way through. Similar scenario with my Wood-fired Uova Al Forno. One side of my dish was cooked through, the middle was runny, and on the other side, the egg was pretty much raw: when I put my fork in, the egg white popped and ran all over my dish, a little unappetizing. Not sure that's how food is supposed to be served but we both ate half of our entrees, disappointing. Overall: After spending over $120 on brunch for 2, we were expecting a whoa moment. Locanda almost got us there, but not quite.

The atmosphere is a bit stuffy and boujie but the food makes up for it. Monkey Bread: I was so impressed by the bread--in fact, I'm impressed that I can be impressed by bread. You might be wondering what's so special about bread but it was SO good. I loved the two side butters, especially the seaweed butter. Definitely a must try. BBQ Octopus: This was well done but not my cup of tea. Perhaps I'm not a big enough BBQ or octopus fan. Rohan Duck: This dish was elegance at its finest. I typically order the duck if it's an option and it is without a doubt the best duck dish I've ever had. It was cooked perfectly with a beautiful red center. The sauce was delicious and, as strange as it sounds, I was actually really surprised by how good the farro was. Who would have thought that a grain could be so tasty?

This place may have one of the best Pork Katsus in town. Serves generally high quality and delicious curry dishes including pork and chicken katsu, shrimp tempura, all atop white rice covered in Japanese Curry. Also on the menu is the "home run" and the "grand slam" which is a combination of their pork, chicken, shrimp, and sausage. Would recommend against their sausage as that is the least appetizing of their choices. As for the location - its nothing special. It mostly operates like a fast food joint where water is self service and you bring back your plate to the front after you're done eating. The seating is limited so not good for large parties and can be very crowded at lunch. The best parts about the restaurant are that its fast and delicious. They also deliver but on grubhub and unfortunately not seamless. They definitely deliver good value on money spent in terms of portions but mostly deliciousness. The food is inexpensive - especially by Japanese standards - and a worthwhile place to visit regularly.

This is actually as good as it gets. The wait is killer... the fact that everyone keeps waiting several years down the road is a statement in itself. I've been coming to Five Leaves for about 4 years. The food is 100% every time. I must have had about 80 brunches and a few dozen dinners here and I've never had a miss, NEVER in nearly one hundred meals. And the staff is amazingly professional, hip and beautiful but still extremely friendly. The ricotta pancakes can't be passed up (order for the table to share on top of your meals) and the yogurt is shockingly large with the best assortment of fruit I've had anywhere. Their eggs are amazing so big brekkie if you're hungry or the sage panini for light days... and always get a side of avocado, so fresh and perfectly ripe - I'm from Cali so I know. They make it all look so easy, I always leave wanting to come right back :)

Definitely worth the dollar signs, if you're looking for drink where all of its delicious elements are perfectly mixed/combined. Have been there with 1 person on a week night and on a Saturday night (during July 4th) with a party of 8. Always went upstairs, and service was excellent each time. Each waiter/waitress took care of whatever we needed, was patient, and did a good job remembering the orders. I had the Black and Blue, and the Fugitive. Loved the Fugitive, but the Black and Blue was too gingery for me. Nonetheless, I can tell that all the drinks were mixed by professionals! Have to try the Taproom next time!

i really liked everything i had at the smith. it was the biggest restaurant that i went to in NY, so i didnt expect much but the drinks were delicious, the salads and the steaks were all great and fairly priced.
A tasty, fresh meal in a casual atmosphere with good friends. Â What more could you ask for on a lovely fall evening?

I will say this about Carmine's, Don't order your own plate! Â This is family style, which means they bring enough food for the whole table. Â The Cesear salad is great and the service is not bad. Â Make reservations as you can't just walk in. Â  When you make reservations, it should be at least a few weeks in advance. Â If you have no plans on day of dinner you can call in and probably get a table or not! but worth the effort.

This was my next stop on my NYC ramen tour. Â This review is for the miso ramen. Pros: Broth was fantastic. Very flavorful and rich. Definitely compares to broths I've had in Japan. Cons: The noodles were slightly under. I wonder if rushed and just pulled them too quickly. Â The pork was just OK. Much better at other places. If you haven't figured it out- this place gets busy. Just go by yourself to get in and out quickly. I will say the spicy ramen looked great too and was very popular. I'm glad that I got the miso though- since it was so flavorful and didnt need any extra spice etc. Overall still ranks pretty high- as I feel the broth is the most important. Â Also pretty good value.
Philly cheese steaks to die for! What a pleasant surprise. I have traveled from Manhattan on the subway Â twice now ( and its a pain in the butt ) just to get the sandwich!

WOOOOHOOOO Very first pizza joint in America!!!! Â I absolutely love this place and have for many years. Â I make it a point to always come here when I visit. Â  Pizza is very good not the best I have had but all in all love this place!
Love this place. Â great quality healthy and delicious food and def one of the best coffee and dessert spots in the city.
Got the meatloaf sandwich and shared the brussel sprouts and mac-n-chese with my family. The biscuits were great too. Was an awesome dinner! Cool atmosphere as well.

Foods were okay but I'm giving 1 star only because of their dishonest service. We were party of 4 people and they automatically charged 20% service fee on check. I asked why and was told that it is automatic since they are in Theater district and there are so many tourists. I asked them to remove 20% and they took if off from my check. I normally leave generous tip (20-25%) but was so upset that they were trying to rip me off so just left $20 (total bill was $280). Manager followed me as I was leaving and his explanation was even worse. He told me that they charge automatic 20% to tourist and care less for them since they are not coming back. He said he wants local customers like us to come back. So, is it okay for a restaurant to discriminate customers if they are tourists? I would never come back to this restaurant. WARNING: Please review your bill carefully if there is any unexpected charges.

Came in just for a banana and fig smoothie, and o m g thats as good as it gets! Not too thick not too thin, not too sweet but not too bitter, by far the best smoothies in town! I wish they a location closer to work but ugh, will definitely make the trip back to try another smoothie!

Great food, nice staff, and cool atmosphere...what more could you ask for. Â The coconut tempura calamari is amazing. Â Pad thai and Streetside Noodles are also really good. Â Best Thai I've had anywhere in Midtown.

When I begin a a review with "Forgive me father for I have sinned" I am in food heaven. It has everything for everyone and is in an excellent location. My favorite was the make your own pasta bar. This was my first time, but not my last.

One thing you'll always find in my freezer is a bag (or two or three) of dumplings from Prosperity. You get 50 for only $8, and they're great to have on hand for dinner appetizers, late night snacks, or if friends drop in unexpectedly.

Loved the dumplings here and it may be my new favorite dumpling spot in Chinatown. 11 dumplings for 3$ and 7 for 2$ you can't really go wrong. The skin is perfectly thin and the amount of filling is perfect. Bursting with porky flavor and plenty of chives... It's just wonderful. They have plenty of condiments on the table such as siracha, soy sauce with crushed garlic mixed in, chili oil and crushed chilis, and vinegar so you have a lot of options to choose from to mix and match. It's a pretty small place with two tables and some wall-side seating. You're not coming here for the ambiance so just find a place to sit and enjoy the delicious dumplings

Beija Flor is the best introduction the Brazilian food and live music. Visiting Brazil is on my to do list & one visit to Beija Flor will make you want to apply for your visa right there! I visited the quaint LIC restaurant this past Saturday to see a live samba band performance. Â Staff immediately greeted us and were able to accomadate our big group. Â Our waitress kindly explained our menu options and even warned of large portion sizes especially the meat platters! (This is carnivore heaven - Carne del Sol appetizer all the way =D) We reviewed the wine list and realized wait we are in Brazil & ordered a round of caipirinhas. Â They were tasty and full of sugar but I think they went easy on us. As the band started, a couple people casually samba dance around their tables and with others. Â Don't worry this is a judge free zone and anyone who knows anything Brazilian samba can be as lively or lazy as you want. Just have fun. Â The musicians then began to give the audience instruments to play and we all made nice additions to band. Â  Needless to say we had a fantastic time at Beija Flor, Great people (patrons & staff), lively music, delicious food and drinks and warm, cozy atmosphere. Â Beija Flor is more than a restuarant; it's a great tourism advertisement for Brazil. If you can't get to Brazil this year, check out Beija Flor. This is as good as it gets! Keep it up :)

Do you like eating family style? I do~ Do you like Italian food? Me too~~ What about family style Italian? Me...Not so much and I hate it.... SIKE~! I LIKE IT.....I LIKE IT A LOT~! I've been dining at Carmine's since 1994, or so, and i never get tired of it. Although it's not the best Italian where you can brag to your frenemies about, it's very TASTY and their humongous portions are a serious VALUE. But even more important is the whole family style dining experience where friends and said frenemies (if you couldn't ditch them) declare a truce for a few hours to decide what to eat and are forced to share throughout the night like....A HAPPY FAMILY~!!!. Oh yes...peace on earth can exist at Carmine's.... Anyways, i like most of the menu and here's some of the highlights: 1) linguine with white clam sauce: chunks and chunks of fresh clams 2) fried calamari: very soft/fresh and they give you the tentacles which is like the best part! The batter is somewhat on the heavy side though... 3) penne alla vodka 4) shrimp fra diavolo: best sauce with chunks of tomatoes. 5) salmon with lemon and butter?: real good for all you pescatarians out there. 6) baked clams: good stuffing. Wish the clams were a bit bigger though. Here's what I don't really like: 1) free bread: it's always hard and not easy to eat. But you'll still eat it because you need bread to mop up the sauces from the entrees 2) garlic bread: like eating a brick and not enjoyable at all. You can try dunking it in some entree sauce to soften it up, but then you could have used the free bread, right? 3) chicken scarpariello: I've been told this is a signature Carmine's dish, but i didn't think it was that great. Disclaimer: I'm really not feeling chicken as of late. So my opinion might have downward bias even though I'm trying to be fair. Summary: Carmine's is a great place to dine, but the wait can be horrible. I really have to check out the Upper West Side location one day.... P.S. - I have to declare a....VALUE ALERT!!! WOOT~!!!

I only came here because I was getting hangry. The bf gets scared when I'm that way so I picked the place and in we went. Very modern and cozy. The waitstaff were all young looking men who were quite helpful. Food was simple, mostly tasty and proper portions. Bf got the grilled bison sirloin that was OK.. on red tomato polenta - which was delicious. I got the pan seared salmon that was plain, but the risotto it was on, was tasty. I like huge portions and I knew I'd be hungry later, but I knew I wouldn't feel disgusting after the last bite. I took off a star because the prices were on the high end for the amount of food served. Maybe it's due to what they boast as farm to table.

What a wonderful dining experience from start to finish! That's why I gave this place 5 stars. The food was very good but really is was the entire experience that makes this place 5 stars. First off, I called thinking we would be late...they said, no problem, great. Then, we weren't late, still no problem and seated us within 5 mins. Amazing. After being seated, we finally noticed just how adorable and cozy this place is. Our host, waiter and owner was warm, inviting and friendly. After a few moments, he grabbed us some delicious cocktails and told us about the specials and one particularly stuck out, the octupus. As the waiter said "If you love octopus, you must get this dish", I was all ready to order it. It didn't matter how it was prepared so we did. Additionally, we ended up with goose liver pate with malbec marinated white grapes (wow), goat cheese and anchiovie bruschetta, crispy blood sausage over polenta and a cheese plate. All the food was great from start to finish. If you're looking for a great dining experience from start to finish that won't break the bank, absolutely check this place out!

My friends and I went on a Saturday night. Â It was a lot of our first times with Brazilian food so we knew it would be a lot of meat but not much else. Â Being the resident flexi-vegan within the group, I stuck to the veggies and rice offerings in the buffet line, but I can't say there was much taste/texture there. Â From what my friends were saying, the best stuff came from the window where you order different types of meat (pork, beef, chicken) and cuts (different types of steak, for example). Â  Â They serve it to you fresh from the grill so you really can't go wrong there. Â Everyone's bill came out to ~$7-8 and left waddling so it's not a bad deal if you're hurtin' for some serious carnivorous time.
Pricey Â ... and worth EVERY PENNY. Â If you're serious about bourbon (or whiskey in general), this place is an absolute can't-miss.

Perhaps because I had read so many favorable reviews over the years, I came to Num Pang with high expectations. Â However, in the end I thought that the sandwich here was just OK. Overall, there Pulled Duroc Pork sandwich was like other Banh Mi sandwiches I'd eaten elsewhere, but somehow there's was not quite as tasty. The pulled pork, although flavorful and really very well seasoned was just a little too greasy for me. Â The sliced cucumbers, pickled carrots, and chili mayo sauce that dressed the sandwich was good though. So, if you like sloppy BBQ Pulled Pork sandwiches, or grilled Philly Cheese Steaks that you can get at New York street fairs, you will love the sandwiches here. Â Since I placed my order and the sandwich was ready in about a minute, I would call this more of a fast food place than the artful hand-crafted sandwich shop they call themselves. Â To each his own, though.

I am a huge fan of falafel and this place did not disappoint! I stopped in after hitting the bars all day and this was just what I needed. Inexpensive and super tasty, however the hot sauce it super intense! My buddy warned me that it was hot, but being that I enjoy spicy and hot food I brushed it off. Big mistake. After putting a good amount of it on, I was in tears, nose running, and mouth on fire just after 2 bites. Next time when I am back, I will definitely use less.

Dropped in here yesterday with some guys from work and we had breakfast. I decided to get the longsilog with fried garlic rice and egg. It took awhile to come which was odd because I was first to order and I got my food last. Oh well food was okay I have to come back to try other dishes.

I went to Almond last night with a friend, per the suggestion of BlackboardEats. First and most unfortunately given the heat wave that is currently pounding New York, the restaurant didn't seem to have its air conditioning on. As a result, just sitting in the stifling restaurant resulted in an uncomfortable meal. For drinks, we each ordered a craft summer ale (apparently their only beers on draft are local craft beers--which is a rather nice touch). While I love trying new microbrews, the beer was a bit tasteless... I ordered the ravioli for dinner. The dish was good and had a nice summery feel but it was not something that I would crave in the future. I'm glad that I gave Almond the try but considering the high prices and average food, it's not a place that I will go back to anytime soon.

Walked in and thought, oh I guess the power went out. Nope, they just don't believe in lights. Once our eyes adjusted, we perused the extensive beer list and continued to try some different beers. We were a party of 4 and scored a bench seat in the back of the bar. Really liked the cool, laid back vibe but missed the great music they allegedly have. Upon inquiry learned that the neighbors have been complaining about the noise. Bummer, and not really their fault. Bathrooms were disgusting, though. Clean it up people. Saw a couple in the front corner making out to the point I thought they were gonna go at it right there. Besides those negatives, still a cool crowd, cool bartenders, and fantastic beer selection.

The fireflies cocktail is gross. Too much cinnamon. Cute place and good location, ideal for drinks and people watching. Food is whatevers. They're charging people Â like $6 for two slices of watermelon, couldn't help laughing at the people that did order it. What a joke.
Excellent food and service! The only reason I didn't give this place 5 stars is because the seating is cramped, especially during weekend brunch.

Good food but I expected memorable given Scott is a celebrity chef. Soft polenta with mushrooms - best thing I had, earthy mushrooms, rich sauce, creamy polenta Crudo - other than the sea salt, not much flavor Spaghetti with tomato and basil - their signature dish, it was good Duck and foie gras ravioli - tender pasta, cooked perfectly but a little rich and I thought it needed more sauce Short rib agnolotti - very good Wine list was pretty good Service was good and the ambience was nice Overall good food, just not to die for, perhaps my expectations were too high

Normally I would say this is 4-star drunk food, but the fact that I eat it sober on occasions warrants the 5th star. I usually get the mix (half lamb, half chicken) with both white sauce and red sauce, but be careful. A little bit of the red sauce goes a long way to spicetown. Both the original food cart and the new Union Square storefront are great.

Had a very nice dinner here. Â As others have stated, the crudo and the duck are the way to go. Â The affogado dessert was too bitter, or this would have been a 5 star review. Â I highly recommend this Vitae for a nice dinner.

Not that this pizza needs another review on Yelp for you to try it but Im gonna offer my two cents anyway. We ordered to-go and it was very easy and fast. Watching your pizza being made was great. We sort of just hung out int he back in front of the oven and nobody told us we were in the way :) Super nice staff, great friendly environment (Not like Grimaldis), and just a nice family feel. I would love to come here with a big group for some cozy comfort pizza the next time Im in NY. The only downer...of course...the price was $22 for a medium with pepperoni and mushrooms :( Worth it though.

Really great happy hour, everyone knows how good their $5 Lychee Martinis are - but the place is narrow & gets so crowded & extra loud so quickly, it's almost impossible to hear what your friends are saying - or get over to that cute guy at the bar (or for him to make it over to you). Â But the food isn't bad and you'll definitely have fun when you get the spot up front blocked off for a group of your friends... I think I liked it a lot more when I was a bit younger, but now there are too many other places in the neighborhood I'd rather go to that aren't so pretentious or packed to the walls.

Bring your appetite and your wallet to Scarpetta as you'll need both in spades. Taking a friend to dinner here will ensure fond memories of delectable Italian bites, top notch service, and some extra sweets to mark the occasion. For our gal's 30th, we had 2 rounds of prosecco and the braised octopus, special of the day burrata and heirloom, braised short ribs, and tagliolini to share. As we are 3 petite ladies and 1 vegetarian, the plates were more than sufficient given the richness of the plates. The bread basket, which I had seen reviewed well, was not all that interesting save for the bacon strips in some pieces. Otherwise they were actually a bit tough to chew. The octopus was perfectly tender and wonderfully smoky with excellent texture points for the bed of ceci beans and olives. Burrata was creamy goodness but the heirloom was poorly cut, merely prepared in eighths, which is hardly elegant, and the one stain on an otherwise gorgeous presentation. The short ribs were thoroughly braised and unbelievably soft on a stage of farro risotto, and the tagliolini was a star amongst overlooked calarmari, artichokes, and olives. The pasta here is not to be missed. We topped off the birthday girl's fete with the amedei chocolate cake which turned me onto butterscotch like I'd never known. It came with a plate of various petit fours and a candle for wishing. Would be back without a second thought for a future special event.

Okay. Â Seriously...$13 for a bowl of ramen?!?! Â Are you seriously serious?! Â With tax and tip, one bowl of ramen cost me $16. Â And that bowl of ramen was not big either. Â For that kind of money, I can get TWO decent bowls of ramen! Ippudo serves only one type of broth--tonkatsu. Â I have to admit the broth is really good. Â It scored major brownie points when I saw that there weren't many fatty floaties, like many tonkatsu broths do. Â But I'm not a fan of their noodles. Â They use thin angel-hair-like noodles, rather than the thicker, somewhat curly-type of ramen noodles I'm used to seeing. Â I didn't like the thin noodles. Â Their stewed Berkshire pork was fatty and literally melted in my mouth. Â But the portions are too small. Â I was not satisfied when I left, so I got myself a falafel sandwich (such a fatso, I know). The interior and decor is really chic and modern. Â I came around noontime on a Wednesday and it was not crowded at all. Â I thought the place was closed because there was no long line in sight, as I had anticipated. Â Overall, albeit the tonkatsu broth was really good, I don't think this ramen was worth my $16.
Lunch special was delicious! I loved the soba noodles, shrimp tempura was cooked well, and the presentation was excellent.

The hot & sour soup is smooth and sharp and simply wonderful. Pork dumplings, fried or steamed: very good. Â But it was the prawns with a snazzy chili sauce that really made me say, hey that was a nice taste sensation. Bravo! The service is pleasant and very talented, too.

My friend took me here after she was craving their "Chige Nabe Udon," which is udon in a spicy broth with kimchee, marinated beef and raw egg. Omg...it was so good. Maybe I'm biased because I'm Korean and love everything spicy, but this was legit. The broth was really flavorful, slightly tart from the kimchee. I regret not getting it, because I got the squid tempura udon and while it was delicious, it wasn't anything special. The place is reallyyyy tiny, so I would not recommend going with a big group. I think their largest table fits like, 4 people. Anyway, I would definitely come back here if I am craving some udon on a cold day.

Came here on a Saturday night. Â Place was full but we were lucky to get a table outdoors immediately. Â Table is quite small so the nice waitress brought out each dish individually one after another. Â We were not rushed and were able to enjoy each dish leisurely. Â Love the crispy pig ears. Â But the bone marrow was exceptional Â I've tried plenty bone marrow dishes in the city and this has to be one of my favorite.

Love this places charm and now with their soccer theme World Cup in Full effect! Â Wow they have gone to next level. All day drink specials. Â Excellent apps including famous spicy wings. For mains you can't go wrong with any of the tacos(chicken, fish etc). Or a wonderful pulled pork sandwich. Don't miss the Mexican corn!

Melissa is very personable and I love her restaurant. Â Short ribs are great. Â Best dollar oysters for happy hour. Staropramen Czech pilsner on tap. Â Nice wines and drinks. Â One of this place that I regret not going to often enough because there so much great food and drink in the EV and LES.
Very nice here, good for a date, prices are decent based in the course of what is being served. Definitely will come back again

Boy do I love me a place where I am surrounded by a whole bunch of other gays. But man do I not love it when the place needs a good clean up and less laziness with the food not to mention the slowness of service. Â Harsh I know especially when I am surrounded by a whole lot of raving reviews. Â  This place can completely be lovely with some French countryside feel to it but it's not there, it took a wrong turn somewhere. Â I'm not crazy about it. Â Conversations around us were more interesting than the food. Â NYers love their brunch and you just can't get it wrong. Â I am not paying that price for something mediocre.
I changed my review because you were big enough to contact me to make it right. I will be leaving so I cannot take you up on your offer but I appreciate it. Cheers
Biscuits and gravy! Yesss. This place is tiny, so come early!

IF you are looking for an AUTHENTIC Gourmet Spanish Shop, this is it! Many kinds of chorizo, manchego, olive oils, canned peppers, etc. They also allow you to taste some of the food before you buy. Gourmet sandwiches and drinks can be purchased here as well. Must get: Chorizo, Manchego. Olive Oil

my favorite go to place when i can't decide where to go. Â their menu is huge! the food is fresh and i've never had a bad meal, from mussels to burger. Â our waitress is great. she's so friendly and warm to our children. Â finally, the apple pie.....damn good!

The wings are decent, similar to wings you would get at hooters or buffalo wild wings. The burgers however, were one of the worst I've had in recent memory. They grill the burger to smithereens, leaving you with a charred cancer burger. We ordered the burgers medium, but it still came out very well done. My friends couldn't even finish their burgers since it was so burnt. The restaurant is pretty small and has a diner vibe to it. Service was ok, but nothing to rave about, esp for a small place. I'll stick with bareburger next time im in the neighborhood.

Yea so this place....is the ALL STAR of Brooklyn. Seriously, I am blown away. Hubs and I found ourselves in Williamsburg last Saturday and thanks to yelp mobile were able to find this GEM. Â It was early 6pm...but we we hungry and had our choice of seats. Â There's a happy hour between 5 and 7 which is awesome. Â We shared the chorizo as an app (divine!) and I dined on the Chivito Completo- filet mignon with bacon, fried egg, onions, lettuce and tomato. Â My heart cried a little but it was amazing. Hubby had the Churrasco- skirt steak with baked potatoe and salad. Â  Dessert....yes we had dessert after all that! Â I tried the dark chocolate cake with a cortadito and he had the dulce de leche flan. We sat there after we finished and talked about what had just happened. Â We had just shared one of the greatest meals in one the greatest restaurants we've ever been in..and we travel TONS. Â So this is saying alot. Â The service was STELLAR, vibe was freakin' awesome- sexy decor, HOT eclectic music. Â PERFECT date spot. Â  I can't wait to go back and applaud the staff on a job WELL DONE!
The classic ramen was ok. The broth was excellent. I did not appreciate the pickled ginger in my ramen. The pork was super thin , dry, and bland. The ramen was al dente.

Have been going here for years. Food is always fresh The grilled calamari and octopus have always been consistently good. The portions are huge! Service is attentive and fast. My favorite Greek restaurant in Astoria.

Delicious food. Prepare for your taste buds to get clobbered with flavor. But between the heavily fried foods and the meats, expect to shave a day or two off your lifespan after eating here. And double up on the blood pressure meds since all dishes are salted by the dump truck full. I loved the miso cauliflower, a wonderful flavor combination that never occurred to me. The crispy brussels sprouts were drenched in a fish sauce vinaigrette and bacon and I ate every salty bite. Two of our party ordered the winter soup and that is one tasty bisque with a few chunks of poached lobster floating in a cauliflower purÃ©e. My son ordered the vaunted country fried duck and waffles which didn't do much for me. The roasted porgy filet was a breaded fish that tasted like a fish fry and was forgettable. All in all, the word that comes to mind in describing the food is "garish". They're determined to wow your palate even if it kills you. Plan a good cleansing fast the next day.

What a great place! Great food, good service and awesome decor! The only thing that was weird was in the middle of our meal 3 ladies walked in for lunch and were coldly turned away by the host who informed them that they would be switching the kitchen over from lunch to dinner soon and so they could not be served. The ladies informed the hostess that they had traveled very far to come to this specific restaurant but she still turned them away. Considering my boyfriend and I along with one other couple were the only people in the restaurant, I didn't see why they wouldn't just let the women stay?! The women were so upset and we felt bad for them and even a little uncomfortable considering this happened right next to our table. ...Very awkward

Up there among the best falafel I've had. Â The falafel flavors aren't very different from each other, so I always get the green. Â Eat in for good presentation. Â Friendly staff, fresh food, convenient location. Â I wouldn't mind it being a bit cheaper though.

This is my favorite brunch spot despite the fact that I live on the upper east side. I just keep coming back. The siracha bloody marys and the pomegranate mimosas are great! I think my favorite meal is somewhere between the Thai tea french toast and the Thai burger. Two things you should do when you go: Order fries for the table and for dessert definitely get the goat cheese cheesecake it may sound weird but is so creamy and delicious Â and definitely enough for 2+ to share. Only reason not a 5 is because I have been there a bunch of times and the service can be slow. BUT it gives me more time to enjoy my unlimited drinks!

Came here for a birthday dinner after searching Yelp for an Italian place in the East Village. This is a nice casual, but not too casual spot. It's kinda like those pair of jeans that can be dressed up or dressed down. Either way it works. Got the risotto balls and polenta as appetizers and both were great. The other main dishes however, were just ok, except for the risotto which was really good. The artichoke ravioli were also very good, but I didn't order that. I ordered the fettucine, which was a bit bland, and not impressive. They should really consider putting that on a bigger plate, b/c it just looks like you are getting a side salad. Anyhoo, prices were reasonable and food, depending on what you ordered, were above average.

Came here with family to celebrate a special occasion and it did not disappoint!!! Here's a list of the things that were my favorites: - Bacon wrapped dates and olives - Wok seared "taglierini" of calamari - braised occtopus, carrot and rainbow radish salad - Steak tartare (OUT OF THIS WORLD - almost contemplated ordering another one just for myself) - Spaghetti Pepperoncini - Braised short rib of beef - Roasted pork belly confit (OMG...I'd come back for this and the steak tartare every single day if I could) My only complaint about this place was how ridiculously loud it was that we all had to yell. I understand it's busy and popular but it was really the most amount of noise I've heard in any restaurant. If it were quieter, it'd be the perfect romantic place for a date. But it isn't, so I'd say this is a place for the casual hangout with family, a group of friends, etc.

I prefer smaller soup dumplings... things were ginormous. Still tasty. Also ordered the shanghai noodles, which were good. The fried quail appetizer was bland. Was seated at a table with another tourist, which turned out to be good conversation. Fast, no-nonsense service.

SoCal kid in NY and when I heard "Halal cart" I was like wtf?! The reviews were off the charts so I said F*&$ it.. we doin this! WHOA the food was DELICIOSO!!! I'm not even playin, it was the most memorable street food I had in NY and NY has an amazing array of street food. I had the combo plate which includes chicken, lamb, pita, and rice all sauced up in spicy goodness. It's fast, cheap and super filling. I have 1 bone to pick with "The Halal Guys".. These dudes could not stop looking at my girls culo. It's like they never saw a beautiful girl in their lives!! Anyway the food was so good I took it as a compliment just next time I'm gonna put my girl in a Burka. Peace

Pio pio was very nice. It is a beautiful restaurant which kinda makes me feel like I'm in a birds nest??!?! The atmosphere was nice even though it was very loins and very dark. My favorite thing was the appetizer we had which was the seviche. It is a plate of seafood which is very hard too explain how it is but in one word AMAZING. The chicken was rotisserie and we absolutely delicious. I would defiantly recommend this restaurant if you want to try Peruvian for a change.
Delicious and cheap, enough said.

An upscale Olive Garden is a pretty apt description. We were a party of 10 and ate family style, I'd recommend this if you can do it. We got caesar salad and appetizers to start which were a little different than usual (honey ricotta and peas, anti-pasta), they were good, not great. Pastas came next, ravioli were good, linguine with clams was ok and pasta with tomato basil was something I could make better at home. If I had gotten those with the all-you-can-eat pasta, this would be a two star review. The meats were all good, steak with corn stuffing was very good, salmon and potatoes were very good, the chicken parm was good/ok. Desserts were also ok/good. Service was quality (my picky grandpa had no complaints, which is rare) and I enjoyed the experience, though having to deal with Times Square crowds wasn't great. You likely won't be upset about going to Becco, but with all the 4+ star reviews, you may be a little underwhelmed, especially if you're used to good Italian food. There are better places, but Becco is a solid good, not great.
The Miso smoked salmon plate is amazingly tasty. The seating is little crowded Â though.

The food at Scarpetta will not whisk you away to a land beyond your dinner table or change your beliefs about what should be. What it will do, and does do, is satisfy with competent, sometimes creative, and extremely tasty spins on classic northern Italian cuisine, with some regionally-inspired dishes thrown in for good measure. We came here at the recommendation of one of my cookbook-writing friends, who told me that the food had been well-received. Since I trust Mindy, I made the reservation a month in advance - this was to be the location of my pre-40th dinner. What I hadn't counted on was my bafflingly stupid behavior the night before - Halloween - something that Scarpetta takes no responsibility for. I had gotten absurdly drunk, failed to take care of my inebriation with an equal dosing of water, and woke up to catch my flight to NY still drunk and very dizzy. I shook like an addict as I waited for my flight, thinking, "oh, I'm going to have to cancel dinner tonight, because there's no way I'm going to keep it down" - this after I threw up a stomach-full of water, pepto-bismol, and dramamine in a garbage can in concourse B. After two naps, several tylenol, and water, I felt much better, but I was concerned that Scarpetta might not agree with my fragile, hungover self. Â To test this, I choked down a cracker - my first solid food of the day - and, after not throwing it up, realized I was actually going to be able to eat dinner. Which turned out to be a very good thing. Our table enjoyed our food - we ordered the polenta (it really soothed my belly), the tuna tartare, the beet and La Tur salad and the pumpkin ravioli (whoah, almost more dessert than pasta course), the duck (incredible, perfectly-cooked, really delicious), and the black cod. We splurged on the chocolate cake, the carrot budino, and the semifreddo for dessert. We loved every course and left not a bite. Sauces were quite good - classical reductions and glaces that were not too salty and were not used with a heavy hand. Because I was hungover, Â my critical capacities were compromised. Usually I'm a much more critical and picky restaurant goer. But the upscale comfort food offered up by Scarpetta caught me off-guard - none of my critical neurons were firing and I loved bite after bite. And I was thrilled that the room had stopped spinning and my nausea was gone. I'd definitely consider Scarpetta for a business dinner or a casual bite at the bar. It wasn't quite what I had in mind for my birthday, but given the circumstances of the prior 24 hours, it was the perfect place to dine.

Celebrated my 31st birthday here with my Friends.I so glad. The food was excellent. The place was packed and noisy but fun. The yuca fries were also incredible, My favorite part of the meal was the Empanadas..Loco Tuesday Â half-priced tapas and happy hour drinks. Consistently exceptional service and food from this place, Our waiter was really good with checking up on us.I don't remenber his name,but I know his from Brazil. I got a Caipirinha, Brazilian drink it's amazing also yucajito really good. The drinks are great, stick with the sangria and Caipirinha and you can't go wrong. The food was excellent. We loved everything we ordered . we had a great time .we will go back. recommend this place

We came during lunch for the pre-fixe menu. Â It was decent but the pork buns didn't live up the hype. Â My girlfriend loved them but she didn't try the ones over at Ippuddo. Â  Granted, this place is good but not nearly as good as everyone says it is.
Not bad for Astoria. This place is basically a dinner with a tweaked menu and some nicer decor. In the wasteland that is Broadway it stands out. Take a star away if you have a car.

The food was delicious! So many vegetarian options - I had the cauliflower mezze and tried a friend's eggplant. Also, we made it in time for their happy hour, which was a nice perk. I had something called From Beirut with Passion - but all you really need to know is that the drink was nice and strong. Another nice perk was the service - from the bar area to the dining area to the restrooms even. One of my friends thought the service was almost too attentive but I will happily take overly attentive servers over most of what you find in NYC! I also liked that the place had a decently sized lounge area where I could have as pleasant a wait as possible prior to my friends' arrival. The only negative for me was that the place seems to attract some nearby corporate types in suits for happy hours/early dinners. To be expected but the atmosphere was not too stuffy regardless.

Nothing to say. It's 5 stars. It's the best pizza I've ever had in my life. Yes I've been to Italy but couldn't find better pizza. Some ppl are complain about the wait but come on, why not enjoy it? Yes it is more expensive than other pizza spot but it's really worth it.

The food here is sooooooo good! A bit pricey, but the service makes up for it! We ordered the mussels with curry & apple sauce (awesome!), escargots (gives you 6 of them but the yummy taste just stays in your mouth) hanger steak (best steak I ever ate), duck (burst with flavor), filet mignon (perfectly cooked), skate fish (good), the Profiteroles (ice cream with a Â unique pastry topped over it and chocolate (bit overpriced though)), creme brulee (won't fill you up but recommend it if you never had). We had 5 people break the bill and paid about $46 each, gratuity included. Would probably go back for the pre-fixe some day.

I wanted to love Empanada Mama. Really I did. I love empanadas. And I love mamas. But somehow this didn't quite work out. I ordered a ton of food here (at least a dozen different empanadas, some guacamole, a tamale, an arepa, etc.) And to be fair, some it was quite good (the arepa, the corn flour rice-and-bean empanada, the vegetarian empanadas), some of it was okay (the Brazilian empanada) and some of it was downright gross (the tamale, the guacamole). I might go back and order carefully and selectively. Then again, maybe I'll just find a better place to go.

Pros: Quick take-out. Scallion pancakes. Cons: Greasy, 'made too far in advanced' tasting food. Canned mushrooms and imitation crab. Requested vegetable spring rolls. Actual rolls had pork and shrimp. Cash only. Run down /tired space. Tossed the leftovers. Sad I wasted one of my precious NY meals here.

I made a special trip here after seeing there was Â a new Terri location in the FiDi. I got my favorite, the garbanzo salad melt, and scarfed it down on the way to the train. I also got a cupcake for later and a donut for tomorrow's breakfast. The place is clean, spacious--but I was the only customer in the place on a Saturday afternoon--and service was lightning-quick. I put the cupcake in the freezer when i got it home. I noticed they have an iPad register system--"Yeah, we're making some changes from the 23rd street Terri"--but still no restroom. (Really? What were they thinking?) You can go to Chipotle around the corner, which is public access, but still, it's sad to see all the food establishments that somehow forgot to include plumbing in their plans. (Okay, okay--I know they don't own the building or anything, but they provide a restroom for their employees, don't they?) To be fair, most of the lunchtime customers are probably going to take the food back to their desks, or even eat at a nearby park. I was able to share that the Cinnamon Snail truck parks on Water and Wall every Tuesday--just a few blocks away. This neighborhood is cookin'!
