A girl my age should've known better if martini is her enemy, it will always be her enemy!! but sometimes you just can't help it! Â Lychee martini was the culprit to my otherwise healthy body! Â That is not to say Lychee martini is not delicious, and i'm sure the same bartender had master his skills in making god knows how many of them since my last review was written. Â I came on a week night recently, always love to sit by the bar, it was nice and quite which was to our advantages cos we just wanna catch up over drinks! Â I just love the casual, easy going ambiance of this place, esp the bar, it's long and comfortable enough to fit everyone in! btw, the sangria is just as good!

Not bad...but please it's NOT In-N-Out so stop comparing shake shack to it! The line was out the door and we waited about 20 min which isn't that bad. First off, the bun...it's a bit sweet so if you like sweet bread...you may like this burger. The meat patty was a bit greasy but it's a burger so what do you expect? The crinkle cut fries totally Â reminded me of my cafeteria fries from elementary school! Â Hubby ordered the caramel shake which tasted like just a plain vanilla shake but he still liked it since it was creamy and not that sweet. Overall, if you've never tried it, it's worth trying but don't expect In-N-Out prices since it is on the pricier side and expect long lines during weekend/peak lunch/dinner hours!

The food is always divine, which is excellent! Their only flaw is that waiting for a table can be a drain, especially one the host tends to seat her friends first! Tisk tisk, however the staff is very friendly & the dj who isn't amazing tends to play good jams. Best nights to go, are Fri & Sat. be prepared for at least a 45-min wait though. Eeeek!
This place is great. The "host" staff or method used for seating guests is the only thing off.

If there is a Laduree within a ten mile radius, you better believe I'm going. Yes they are pricey, but these are among the BEST macarons on the planet. We got a half dozen box on our last day (because I like to be fancy and eat macarons at the airport. Laduree macarons stay fresh longer than most and don't get gross and flakey.

Friend and I went here for dinner last night, and wow. Just wow. The food was outstanding--creative, flavorful, and nicely presented. The service was attentive without being overbearing. I liked the simple yet cozy ambiance--a bit cramped, but it did not really bother me, as I was too distracted by the amazing food! Friend and I had the sticky pork buns and fried green tomatoes as starters--both outstanding. For my main, I had the pork tenderloin with black-eyed peas and collared greens special, which was heavenly. The pork had been brined to perfection. Friend had the fluke--while she thought the fish itself was a bit bland, she found the accompanying ingredients (which was kind of a pistou of cranberry beans, dill, and something else I can't recall) to be outstanding. I will be dreaming about this place until the next time...
I normally am not a big fan of pizzas... Yes, I know I must be weird. But sweet Jesus, what do they put in their pizza? Crack? One bite of their Artichoke & Spinach and it was simply heaven.

Great dinner spot after the movies (which are a few blocks away) So many healthy, tasty options. Â Well priced. I had the quinoa burger with salad and loved it. Def want to go back and get a ton of the veggie sides! The crowd is very 20's/30's hipster and attractive. I guess the quinoa burger lovers can be a certain "type"?!

I take down tacos at this spot at least once a week, sometimes twice. A lot of NYC spots pursue cool -- and that can def come off cheezy contrived. This place tho has a genuine cool vibe. Like Jeter or John Mayer Live in LA. Place fills up but you don't feel crowded. Great volume control on the music. They played a couple songs from the late 90s, early 00s that I liked. Highly recommend the Tecate. Get 3.

I could eat that light green sauce with a spoon. What is it? Sangria is heaven. You can get an entire chicken and french fries. But its kinda expensive. Great place for large parties, but it didn't feel original after seeing 4 birthdays in one night. Overall, its a beautiful space and fun atmosphere. The food is good, drinks are good, somewhat overpriced.

The service was really great. We initially sat on the patio in the back, which is super cute. But the bugs were biting, and we moved inside. The waiter was very nice about it and didn't appear bothered by the inconvenience. The dollar oysters were good, but not the best I've had. We ordered two entrees and shared. I got the catfish po'boy, which was delicious. My friend got Le Chalet, a salad with blue cheese, pecans, and cranberries. It was good, but much too sweet for me. The cornbread was amazing. Their hurricane cocktail was extremely potent. I don't normally drink rum, but I really liked this drink. The portions were generous, and we ended up bringing leftovers home. Definitely recommend this place.

I got there on Thursday around 10pm, hoping there is no line since it's pretty late. When I got there, there were still many people overflowed from the restaurant. As a party of 1, I waited probably like 15 mins, not too bad compare to 2.5 hr wait that they usually have. I had Chicken Paitan Ramen... it's the ramen heaven! Perfectly matching firm noodle and creamy soup. They serve really quick, within 5 minutes after you are seated. People at Totto are very friendly and I like their vibes. Also, don't forget it's "CASH ONLY". I know it's ridiculous to wait 2+ hr to have a bowl of ramen.. but just get there when it's not too busy (later than 10pm) and try it. You will not regret.
It's different from ippudo...lighter because of he chicken stock versus pork/mixed stock at ippudo. But it's still very good. Get the spicy ramen but it's really really spicy!

Disney World comes to the UES! Â A little TOO themed and manufactured and TURN DOWN the lights. Â On the plus side a round table for 6 and quiet enough to carry on a conversation. Â The prix fixe food was good as were the cocktails. Â Our waiter was a little rough at the edges. The ladies who took care of us were great!

i just can't understand how they can sell dumplings for sooooo cheap?!?! this place and vanessa's dumpling house, just north a couple blocks are the best deals you can find in chinatown!! i will have to say that this place has better flavor and you get 5 for a dollar instead of the four you get at vanessa's. however, there's hardly a spot to sit at prosperity while vanessa's has a couple more to accommodate the crowds. i also ordered a sesame pancake with beef, but didn't seem to find any beef in it, what's that about?! i think i got a regular pancake on mistake. it's cool though, i can't really complain because the flavors just made my buds as happy as can be and my stomach satisfied. my friends and i shared 10 fried and 10 boiled dumplings. with the prices so low, i thought we should order another 10, but we hardly finished this batch, haha. the fried dumplings have a great texture and the boiled are the best dumplings you'll ever find. i could no sooner chose between the two types than if i had to chose between keeping my right or left hand. they are just that delish!! beware when biting into a boiled one, the juices will be dripping down the side of your mouth, onto your clothes if not bitten with utmost care. all this and i just spent 3 bucks. where else are you gonna find good flavor for so cheap?! this is one hell of a bang for your buck!!! you really should stop by here when you're nearby, i'd consider it a sin if you didn't.

I'm a huge brunch person and I've been to many brunch places in the city. Â This by far, hands down is one of the best brunch places. Â  YOU MUST TRY THE ARTICHOKE DIP. Â It is the BEST artichoke dip i've ever had. Â aside from that my bloody mary was delicious and my pulled pork sandwich was awesome. Â My friend had the poached eggs and cheddar cheese gritz and she couldn't stop telling me that good it was. Â In her words "its the best breakfast I've had in ages." Â I took half of it home and my boyfriend devoured it. The restaurant itself is very cute and quaint. Â It is a bit hard to find. Â The place is on rivington NOT CHRISTIE. Â On rivington, there's an alley next to a coffee shop and Freeman's is at the end of the alley. I definitely want to go back and try the other dishes.

A NYC must! I always get the elote and the shrimp tacos. The wait is totally worth it, so definitely wait it out if you must. It may seem a little cramped inside, but it definitely is an experience go eat elbow to elbow with a complete stranger :) a part of New York charm! The workers are a bit sensitive with the waiting list, so just be patient; your time will come.
Miriam is a warm and cozy restaurant. For vegans, there are few options, unfortunately and the portion sizes are miniscule (unless perhaps, you order a meat entree).
food is great and you even get a cigar at the end of your meal!

I had a day off and always wanted to get breakfast and spend the day walking around NYC. My expectations were high based on the impression I saw on a TV show, I think Â it was on a segment of 'Best thing I ever ate' on the food channel. I was disappointed that the honey buns are only served on weekends. I visited on a Monday :( I ordered a coffee and the smoked salmon. The portions was very small to my liking. The smoked salmon tasted like the amce smoked salmon I bought from Costco which is pretty good. The english muffin tasted like Thomas's and the poached eggs tasted like you what.... The plate also came with some pickled onion thing which was blah and a dab of butter. The sum of each component tasted like what it supposed to which lead to my disappointment. I have to agree with other reviewers that I could have made this if wasn't so lazy. Starting my day off here coming from Jersey and dropping $21 (tax and tip) for breakfast and leaving hungry was a big let down. I can't blame them for such average food but I took stars away because of the price ($3 for a cup of coffee), small portion, and they did away with soft boiled eggs. I paid in cash but would flipped out if this place was cash-only.

I have never waited for more than 15 minutes to get in here, but then again I live in BK and I guess if I ever saw the 2 hour line I would come back another day. About the food: Fabulous. I traveled Italy for a few weeks and haven't had better pizza. Honest it is delicious and flavorful. Absolutely a perfect treat.

Love, love, love this place. I love drinks and apps and sharing and this place meets all my needs. Get the meat skewers and the pomegranate mojitos. Also, get the plantain stuffed with spicy beef. Skip the crab cakes and the fried calamari. Great for dinner, drinks and warm summer nights with friends.

I used to love coming here but now there is always an insane wait! I am tempted to buy my own pot and do Shabu at home! I agree, the food here is very expensive. And I am certain with their continued popularity that it won't get cheaper. That said, the food is good and the experience is worth it. If you have the patience. Maybe someday the hype will die down and I won't have to go eat Indian on 6th street instead.

Mimi & Coco is one of my favorite regular restaurants in NYC. It's definitely comfort food that I wouldn't even mind walking in the cold or snow to get to! The girls and guy who work here are so sweet, very polite and of course make the most amazing food. You won't go wrong eating here if you want some delicious rice, burdock, chicken, steak, seaweed, curry, whatever! Bottom line: try this place out and it'll become a regular food haunt for you!

The food may be good but the service is HORRENDOUS. I dined here with friends recently and we made a reservation. We showed up to find that making a reservation is useless. They had no table for us and asked if we would mind squeezing onto a two-top with the assurance that they would move us to a larger table as soon as one became available. We agreed, reluctantly. We ordered and before any of our food came out another table emptied. We asked if we were going to be able to move to that table and were told no because they had to save it for an incoming reservation. We reminded them that we were an incoming reservation as well but they said they needed to save that particular table because it was the only one they were able to fit 5 people at. We were once again assured we would be moved when another table became available (yet another lie). Between our apps and the main course another table did become available and when the server went to seat another party there we reminded him that we were still waiting to be moved (as he had promised us we would be). The waiter became belligerent with us. He said you are eating at a place called Nook - what did you expect? It's going to be crowded. We ask people to squeeze into smaller tables all the time. We reminded him that we only agreed to do so because he promised us that he would move us as soon as he could. He said he had no intention of moving us ever cause he needed all the tables he had for incoming reservations (again we reminded him we were one of those incoming reservations). Turns out he was saving the new table for when his buddies arrived for dinner (based on the big hello he gave them when we set them). While all this is going on he continued to take new reservations for tables he knew he could not seat and then the poor people would show up and be told that could not be accommodated. I understand that this is a small space with limited seating but why then take reservations at all. Just have it be first come/first served. Why also would you seat parties who were not all there? During our visit that was a 4-top that had only 2 people sitting at it not ordering anything for almost 45 minutes until the rest of their party arrived. I will never be back to Nook. There are too many other amazing places in this neighborhood to put up with such poor service and disrespect.
Good pizza. Not the best I've had and didn't leave a very strong impression. Pretty cool that it's a historic landmark and what not. Worth a trip.

It's a toss up between Red Hook Lobster Pound and Luke's Lobster for best lobster roll. This place is definitely out of the way though, so it's not as easy for the mass NYC crowds to get to, but if you can make it over, it's worth the trek. Â Definitely fresh and delicious, and what's great is that there is a picnic style seating area next door where you can enjoy your meal. Â At Luke's, unless you're one of the lucky 6 people who get a seat, you're still eating over a counter, and not at a table. Â For a big groups, try to make it here. The lobster roll comes in 2 ways: Maine and Connecticut. Â The Maine style is your typical lobster roll, served cold in a bun. Â I opted for the Connecticut style, which is served hot w/o mayo. Â I loved it, but unless you eat it fast, the bread can get kinda soggy. Â I didn't have really have a problem with that, as I scarfed mine up in like 2 minutes. And the people working here are so friendly! Â No matter how great food tastes, if I get bad service, the most I'll give is 4 stars, but the extra friendly service is worth .5 in my book :)

On a cold evening in a hip part of town, the Shabu Shabu is just the ticket. Thumbs up on all aspects, of food, service, atmosphere and value. Even on an early Tuesday evening the place was busy. Looking around I think I was the only non Japanese patron. Must say something about this place. While I was on a date, I could see this place as a lot of fun with a group of friends and the right sake selection. Next time definitely.

WOW. This charming little French cafe is going to be my new hang from now on. Mindblowing crepes, good wine, beautiful men all over the neighborhood (even if a lot of them don't swing my way), good-looking waitstaff with solid recommendations...I could go on and on, but that would spoil the surprise for you. Just go there.

Very cool place, I like the ambiance there and the service was on point. Â I had the chicken and waffles and it was delicious, I also got to try the jambalaya and it was to die for. I def recommend this place and will come back

Let me start by saying the service here is VERY good and the decor has a homely and inviting feel to it. Â  Drinks were pretty good and the food was decent but I expected a bit more. Â I had the linguine with shrimps, cheese, and clams which was not bad but will add it was nothing to cry over. Â I'll return in the near future and try something different. Â MAYBE.

Everything from the atmosphere to the food, makes this a great brunch spot. Aita has a very intriguing menu that features some great dishes. My Â personal favorite is the smoked pastrami salmon benedict. Its served on fried green tomatoes with a side of delicious potatoes and a flavorful little salad. The only reason I am giving 4 stars instead of 5 is that the dessert menu is lacking. I had the chocolate fondente and was less than impressed. The berry gelato was fine but it really didn't do much for me. A simple panna cotta with berries or a canoli on the menu would be a great addition!

Just opened, went for the first time a few days ago. Had a bunch of snacks and beer. Everything I had to eat was very high quality. Walked to the back and noticed a spectacular rotating oven. Clearly these guys are into what they're putting out. The wine list looks like someone did some thinking, by the glass as well as by the bottle. The homemade hummus and bread was some of the best I have had. Looking forward to my next visit and if they are consistent (which I expect by the way everything was being tended to by the staff), I will immediately change my rating to 5 stars.

Taking that "special someone" to dinner? Try taking them to breakfast! I've heard of this place for a while now, so I had to go and see if these blueberry pancakes were really as good as they say... Well, it was! This was the first time I have ever salivated over a fluffy blueberry pancakes! Â We also had the Eggs Benedict (the hollandaise sauce was perfect) , and the potato pancakes w/ applesauce and sour cream. The best breakfast in NYC? So far, yes. We got there when they opened and the place filled up very quickly. The aroma was intoxicating which put the crowded place in a very happy mood.
I don't mean this in a bad way but this is a total parent spot. Since opening I've been here with my mom and girlfriends parents and both meals were great.
Crazy long wait on the weekends and overpriced but otherwise its a pleasant experience with pretty good food.

Finally decided to check this place out after walking by it twice a day to and from the train. I'd read the reviews, I kind of knew (or thought I knew) what to expect: I was blown away! The list of specials was daunting, the service was impeccable, the wine list was well-rounded, the food was flawless. Highlights of the night included a carmelized fig salad with pecorino romano, and chestnut /sausage stuffed ravioli. We had a bottle of Montepulciano with our meal that was so good I'll probably visit their wine bar next door just to enjoy it again. What was originally meant to be a quick meal turned into a several hour dining experience that made an ordinary night really special. I really look forward to going there again, but I can't even imagine being able to try stuff that's actually on the menu.. not with all those glorious specials!

Ruby's is really good. I think it''s an excellent spot for lunch with a friend. It's pretty small compared to other restaurants, so probably not the best choice if you're in a large group. However, seating is adequate and the food is really good. Order the amazing Australian Bronte Burger! Trust me, it will not disappoint. They also give generous portions of food so it shouldn't disappoint from that aspect either. I'd highly recommend stopping in for a burger, pasta or one of their large salads.

My husband and I had a great meal at Cuba on a recent trip to NY. My Hemmingway mojito (made with ginger infused rum) was tasty as was my entree, a braised skirt steak. On the other hand, my husband ordered the pork, which was not super flavorful, but still cooked well. The wait staff was speedy and kind. Overall, enjoyable meal. I'd would go back!

We arrived early for lunch and were greeted by some very grouchy waiters, but so what, the pizza was delicious! Â We ordered the antipasto and it was fresh and yummy, then we ordered two pizzas, one meaty and the other veggie. Â They brought one and we were eating it without question and then they brought 2 other pizzas and we realized that the yummy pizza we are eating was one we didn't order. Â It was ok because they didn't charge us for it and we just ate the other two pizzas. Â After awhile they started to all taste the same. Â Don't get me wrong they tasted GREAT! Â We came here because we saw it on Food Wars and wanted to check it out!

Earlier this month on a trip to NYC, my cousin introduced me to this amazing place. According to him, there would be minivans from New Jersey that would pull up and whole families would order up and eat in their cars. We saw a whole slew of cars lined up up on 56th between 6th and 7th with people eating in their cars. If anything, that is a good indication of great food! Earlier in the week, after being let down with dinners at Momofuku and Gramercy Tavern, I was determined to eat something good. My cousin who lives up on 57th said that I had to try this cart out. After ditching my germ-phobic sister, who would not allow me to eat off of a street cart, I went off looking for this cart. What I found at midnight on a Monday night was a cart with a line of 20 people. The line was very fast and I got the combo. Damn, it was gooooood. And only $6!!! The yogurt sauce is tasty and the hot sauce was nuclear. Not sure why it's called a Halal cart, I mean I've never seen a Kosher cart. But whatever, it's good. I only wish we had something like this in LA.
RUDE manager, host.... Will take bribes to get you seated but will make you wait for two hours take the bribe money and NEVER seat you.... Never going again! If I could give them a zero, I would.

i'm happy to report that i had an experience that is also not consistent with the other reviews which hopefully means this place is getting its act together (or that it wasnt that bad in the first place). we went with 12 people on a saturday night at 7pm. we were told, by a very nice server, there would be at least an hour wait but the bar was open and very convivial and reminded us all (southerners and australians mostly) of lovely and relaxed beach restaurants with broad views and horizontal sunlight. and it was hot as hell outside but the fans were on full blast and we were drinking pitchers of coronitas for 11 bucks, on ice, with limes, pure fun. we ordered some very good raw oysters and spicy shrimps to snack on and chilled out with our friends. a little over an hour into our wait they brought us to our tables on the deck, open air, cooler breeze by this point, string lights overhead, with a view of the harbor and the statue. we ordered more buckets of coronitas from our man alex, who was great, then the northeastern steam pot, a million blue crabs, fish and chips, fried scallops, fried oysters, mac and cheese, all of which was cooked very well and super delicious. the fried oysters and scallops were a giant hit and the crabs and lobsters were perfectly steamed and all was very reasonably priced. we were there from 7 to 11 and had an absolutely great time. we'll go back again and probably soon and probably once a month forever. there is not a place in new york like this place where you can sit outside at picnic, eat fried oysters and crabs that are brilliant and dont cost one million dollars, watch the sun set, chill out. a bunch of the red hook crowd is already hating on it, yelpers are clearly piling on, but i think this place deserves a visit.
Noodles were great and you get loads, staff are awesome, cheaply priced. Say no more.

The greatest trick the Devil ever pulled was convincing the world that he didn't exist. Danny Meyer is not a restaurateur; he's a master of the dark arts. There is no other rational explanation for the inevitable, often inexplicable experience that you'll have dining in one of his restaurants. This is particularly the case with Gramercy Tavern. No matter who you are, who you're with, where you're from, or what you're doing, the minute you step foot into Gramercy Tavern, you're Danny's. and he won't let go until you pry yourself back out of the doorway. Dining at Gramercy Tavern is like stepping into an early scene of "The Devil's Advocate", when everything is going just a little too right. Backwaiters just happen to enter the restroom seconds after you do, smiling warmly as they ask you quite unexpectedly, 'Is this your first time here, sir? We hope you come back to visit us." Bartenders at the perfectly-packed bar anticipate your arrival, guiding you to a seat that didn't appear to be there five minutes beforehand. Mysterious strangers who have been coming there for eternity charm their way into your conversations, no matter how determined you are to be left alone, and you'll eventually thank them for it. Have I mentioned the food? Try picturing the most fantastically roasted, tender sweetbreads you've ever had, delicately garnished with razor thin pear slices and bits of walnut. Try picturing an elegant fish filet doused in mushroom broth and bok choy, with a dusting of oats to boot. And try not to worry; because Gramercy Tavern won't let you. Gramercy Tavern will distract you at every turn. Gramercy Tavern will hypnotize you with Â its worn-in bar, its seasoned staff and its towering floral bouquets. Gramercy Tavern will force you to stare out of its dramatic windows; it will lure you into the trance of its veteran operation, and you won't stand a chance trying to find something wrong. Danny Meyer is determined to convince you that Gramercy Tavern is one of the best restaurants in New York. Maybe you'll find a way to prove him otherwise. I couldn't.

i don't go anywhere else in nyc for bbq because i'm afraid to have a bad experience and eat bad bbq. the line is always out the door but it's worth the wait. you end up spending the entire waiting time thinking about what to order (and you will still over order). great atmosphere inside. the table situation is a little nerve-wracking. it's one of those places where you order your food, pay at the register, and find a seat. i've been seat-lucky and got seats immediately the two times i visited. i've ordered the same three meats (listed in order of deliciousness): - brisket: so tender/melts in your mouth; was a little fatty this time around - burnt ends: tad salty and little tough this time around but still very good - spare ribs: great flavor in every bite for the sides - i've tried: - pomme frites: nothing special. save your money/appetite and order the other sides - sweet potato casserole: good. but think it has too much maple for my liking. i'm not a fan of sweets so i might be biased. - burnt end baked beans: very good but always a tad salty - broccoli salad: delicious and you will feel less guilty because it's probably the only green on your plate the free add-ons are all good. i finished all my cucumbers and not even the meal itself. the bbq tastes just as good the next day so don't worry about over ordering! also do they sell the bbq sauce??! so freaking good. i want to use it as my new salad dressing.

Vibe- NYC Cowboy BBQ Price- astronomical Service- Cafeteria style Greeting- none Table bread- plastic bag rolls Food: Brisket is amazing Berkshire pork ribs are excellent beef ribs are dry Shredded pork is dry Beans burnt ends are excellent Sausage is forgettable Potato salad is not good WIGB? Only if you are buying. I have to say this is some of the best BBQ I have ever eaten. But the prices are so high for what we ate. We could have gone to Per Se with the price we were charged for what we ate. I thought a mistake was made when we got the billl. Everything here is by the pound. Those heavy bones add up fast. The food is the best, but not worth the price. Hard call, but someone has to call it like it is. If a Texan ate here and saw the bill he would laugh at us yankees!
Long wait, lots of hype. Crazy amounts of tourists. Pizza was 3/5 compared to others I've had. No where near as good as the $2 slice on my block...

The food is amazing. One of my favorite Malaysian restaurant in Manhattan. The portion isn't too much, but the flavor is there. I love the Indian pancake and the curry sauce that you dip with it goes so well together. (****) Everything is good on the menu. You can probably close your eyes and point with you finger when you order. I usually get their Singapore Rice Noodles and this dish with the Fried Taro nest. Each dish have it's own unique flavor and taste. Trust me, you won't be disappointed. (****) Place is super packed (which means this place is good) Service is quick. I was fascinated by how skilled the waiters are. He was able to clear my table in one shot and I had serving of 7 people, so you can only imagine how many plates I had. Seems like he was playing Tetris or something. (****)

Great vietnamese sandwiches, pork belly sandwich is amazing. Kimchee fries are awesome. Â However avoid busy times. Quality definately suffers when they are really busy. I noticed my sandwhich was cold and didn't taste as fresh as previous orders. Even at that, they are hands down the best place for viet sandwhiches within a 20 mile radius.

Haven't been to Pelligrino's in about 2 years and since we happen to be in the area, we decided to try our once favorite Italian restaurant in NY. All I want to know is.. What the F%#K HAPPENED?? The food was disgusting. We will never eat in this place again. The Food, when it finally did arrive was cold, no presentation whatsoever, bland and I made it known to our Waiter that we were very unhappy. Needless to say after a $125 check (for 2 people), we left hungry. That Menzo finoquo that greets everyone at the tables will not ever see me or my family there again.

I'm so excited for this place! This is my "go-to" breakfast spot from now on! Cute lil cafe down in alphabet city. The brunch/breakfast Â menu is not overwhelming, but the food is great! I started w/the "2 eggs any style, potatoes, mixed greens & toast" for $4!! Yes you heard me, 4 buckaroos!! It really doesnt get any better than that... so I thought. I continued w/the "belgian waffles w/fresh fruits (blueberries, strawberries, bananas), whipped cream and orange blossom syrup". The fruits came plentiful on my waffles. The orange blossom syrup was delicious, not too sweet. The place gets pretty busy for brunch, so be prepared to wait a bit. As busy as they were the waitresses were super attentive. There are so many great things on their menu, and all with very reasonable prices. Â I can't wait to go back and try their french toast!!

rolled through for a work dinner, definitely needed a classy joint that didn't exude stuffy rich but young rich....ai fiori did me justice. Â  drink was good, not great. Â salad was bleh but rarely do i ever get an amazing salad. Â entree was out of this world, i had the ravioli and was a bit confused when i only saw 2...i could tell they really put their weight into making each one, absolutely amazing. Â i will definitely be back... on a work tab ;) or a celebration, prices are up there. Â what i did appreciate was the space, it wasn't cramped and stuffed like you had to weasel through tables. Â my colleague (rich young buck from singapore) said his plate was great but he wouldn't rank it up as the one of the best in NYC.....

After a long wait, we were greeted very enthusiastically by the waitstaff. Â We ordered the akamaru modern (what everyone says is the best ramen) and pork buns. Â The ramen was good, but not what I had oped, especially for the $14 price. Â The pork buns, however, were delicious (but overpriced @ $9 for 2 as well). Â Overall, Ippudo is an experience and everyone should try it, but I'll probably not be coming back. (+) pork buns, service (-) value, LONG wait, a bit overhyped

Went here today with a really good friend for a post-shopping meal and it was a great experience. I ordered the Orange Tulipes cocktail which was really nice and refreshing. It was a lovely day and we indoor seats but right by the entrance so we could feel a cool breeze. I ordered the tuna tartare and it was great. The fish was fresh and the light olive oil and pepper seasoning was great. The fresh bread was a huge plus (just out of the oven!). My friend ordered the halibut as per many yelpers' recommendations (thanks guys!) and it was AWESOME. The smoky flavor made the fish taste very different. She also ordered a side of fries which were super tasty (I mean WHO can say no to fries!). Our server was super nice- very attentive and gave us great recommendations. Bottomline: sure, it's a TAD pricey but the food was so tasty that it's worth a small premium! Definitely returning here :)

I have to give this place 2 star for slow service, and mediocre shake.(come on, the place wasn't crowded) The Sliders were decent, nicely seasoned with onions and potato bread buns. As for the Guinness Shakes, well i can barely taste the guinness syrup.(huge letdown since that sucker cost 6$) The service was okay in the beginning, but the waitress was nowhere to be found when i wanted to pay my tab. Apparently she Â was on the other side of the narrow hall and 2 workers are blocking the way.(of course she was chatting to one of her co-worker, go figures.) I can't really expect much from a place that sell 2$ sliders. then again, the 123 Burger Shot offer more selection for better price.(like 3 Sliders for 3$ and 3$ for a choice of Â Waffle Fries, French Fries, Potato Wedges, Sweet Potato Fries, Fried Cheese Ravioli,and Yucca Fries.) i'll remember to hop to 123 Burger Shot, the next time i have the craving for sliders.

slick vietnamese lounge/restaurant that caters to after work crowds and beyond with a sick happy hour and a little different vibe than some of the nearby bars in the immediate block. That's the great thing about the LES nowadays, there's loads of variety. This place wasn't my particular cup of tea, but it was close, the high ceilings and orange give a warm, large feel without it actually being that big. The front has a great racetrack couch lining for a larger group or two, and the bar was filled with couples, a couple singles, and the like. The music was actually a bit loud, kind of the serene beat/electronic heavy loungy type stuff which got boring after a while. The floor was REALLY STICKY. I'm really not sure why, it didn't matter where you were standing. But at least it's a good sign that people are drinking too many lychee martinis here. If you haven't had lychee anything, I urge you to try, they are unique and a terrific combination of a deep sweet while retaining a fruity surface.

Had a great time eating here while in NYC...the waitress named Tasha was great and entertaining which helps since as with the south soul food is cooked slowly...that wasn't a problem though, once we got the food all of us struggled to finish our plates because it was that much and that good...I had the Rev Al Sharpton as its called (smothered chicken breast with waffle an Mac and Cheese) excellent is all I can say...the half and half I had was great tasting but I wish i could have finished it...if ever you are near Harlem on any type of trip, make it a point to get here for good service ask for Tasha and excellent food...even the on-duty manager walked around asking of everything was ok...this place is on point

I've only been here for the open sangria bar brunches, but I've been enough times I think I've sampled half the menu. First of all, the open sangria bar: it's awesome. They offer around 6-8 different sangrias in pitchers and you go up and help yourself (after being carded at your table, that is). The only problem is the line sometimes gets a little long and sometimes they run out of glasses. So hold on to your glasses and be a little patient - it's unlimited free booze for christssake, calm down and wait three minutes. Secondly, the food: It's good, but not great. I can tell that's the case because, despite going to brunch here about once a month for the last 6 months, I can't really recall a single dish that I loved. But nothing was ever bad, save for the cachapa de salmon (though that could be just a bad ordering decision for me since eggs and salmon are not really my thing). Thirdly, taco dude: There's a guy who comes around dispensing taquitos out of a little cart with all kinds of fixings. I think it costs like $8 or so per order. Trust me on this: one order of taquitos per every 2-3 people is more than enough, unless you want to get so full you feel like the baby alien from Alien is going to burst out of your tummy, and you're ok with that alien being made entirely of taquitos. Also really difficult to get a decent buzz going that way, even with free sangria. Lastly, desserts: If you are not so full you need to be rolled out of the restaurant just yet, the desserts are awesome, especially the bombas (South American donuts). Oh, I almost forgot about the bread. The yummy yummy bread and the delicious strawberry butter they give you with it. So, if you want to eat so much and drink so much you'll be full for days on $20 a person, Calle Ocho is your dream come true.

I went here on a Sunday afternoon with my girl and must say I was impressed by the food, especially the Mac and cheese and the ambiance if the place. The staff was courteous and service was prompt. There is a dress code, which I found out the hard way, no tank tops, but it was no biggie, I changed and went right back because if how nicely the staff relayed the dress code to me.

Tried to have brunch here last weekend. Â We were greeted at the door and told their was no chef, only juices and drinks were available. Â What? Â No explanation. Â We traveled quite a distance to enjoy the start of a great weekend. Â Very disappointed.

Food was great and the owner was warm and gracious. I wanted a certain appetizer but it wasn't available so he offered me an alternative. It was different from anything I had ever had but I was enjoying the other dishes more and couldn't finish it. He offered to take it off the tab since I didn't enjoy it as much. I appreciated the gesture which shows he cares about people truly liking the food. Speaking of which, the vegetable grill bread and chicken wings were fantastic! Also, the fireplace adds a cozy feel to the whole space that is perfect on a chilly night. My friend and I hung out there a little longer than we should have but never felt rushed or pressured to leave. Excellent meal and great hospitality!

I went to Room Service this past Friday night for my friends bachelorette party. I can not say enough about how great it was. I made a reservation for 13, when we got there we sat at the bar and waited maybe 10 mins, while having great drinks made by the super sweet bartenders (girls), we were seated and the service was excellent. They were so kind to a large and I'm sure obnoxious bachelorette party group. If ur looking for a very beautiful posh restaurant this is ur place. the ambiance was very elegant. Yes the place it tight but it's NYC what do u expect. I will absolutely be back.

So I'm a big soup dumpling person. Big fan. I finally made my way down the sketchy alley to Joe's. After throwing my name on the wait list, crossing my fingers it really was 15 minutes, my buddy and I were shuffled in to sit with some other slightly baffled diners. Sat down, before drink orders were taken 'Dumplings?!' Ah! Lucky for me, I'm a quick reactor-pork please! A few beers and some spicy chicken were added. Place was noisy, busy and a little crazy. Then the dumplings. I am in love. I would walk from Brooklyn for these dumplings. The restaurant is amazing, because of these dumplings. I came back three days later, with another friend who wanted Sunday Chinese, for these dumplings. Go. Now. It's getting cold in NYC. For $5, 8 soup dumplings?! Win.

One Word: Yum I was on a first date last night who took me to Grimaldi's under the Brooklyn Bridge. I've been to the Hoboken, NJ Grimaldi's before, but never the original. It was seriously delicious. We ordered a pepperoni pie to go, sprinkled extra cheese and red pepper flakes on top, and took a walk to the river. Sitting and eating the a Grimaldi's pie by the water was a fabulous first date! Loved every minute ... and every bite.
This place kinda sucks.

Let me just sum it up because Cafeteria does not even deserve a review: -Horrible hostesses On a Tuesday night, we waited 30 minutes to be seated although there were plenty of empty tables. -Terrible food Atlantic Salmon with pumpkin was nothing special Special of the day: Sweet Potato and fig ravioli tasted like crap Passion Fruit Palmer - sour -Atmosphere Loud, dark, and pretentious Cafeteria, with it's terrible service with overpriced food, is not recommended!
Pretty place. Food portions so small!! Â Steak dish wasn't even 4 oz!! Fish dry. Wouldn't go back
I'm Korean. I've seen my fair share of "weird foods". The live octopus topped anything I've ever seen. Nice service. Good food. Interesting decor. Try the live octopus. LOL!

First time in this location - I've only ever gone to the one near Astor place. I'm deducting a star because the price keeps climbing up ($3 now). But the falafel is still delicious, the veggies fresh, and the hot sauce deadly. A little hole in the wall - pick up your food and go eat it at Washington Square Park!

superbly impressed with food, ambiance and the experience in general. i just couldn't agree with the city of new york and their alcohol laws: Â no serving of any kind of alcoholic beverages before noon, on sundays. Â  WHAT ??? Â my brunch experience was ruined. Â not really !!! Â my seafood tower -- literally, was nicely enjoyed without having to get too out of control. Â our reservation was for ten thirty and finished every gram of sea food by twelve; Â at which point, we were able to order our mimosas. Â timing couldn't be better, anyways. Â our option was to have a glass of champagne instead and a chocolate and pear tart. Â amazing !!! initially, we were seated by the window at a tiny tiny table ... not so fast in feeling disappointed. Â we were eventually moved to a larger table and had a better chance to enjoy everything; Â including the view. Â true. Â people watching at balthazar is big component of the experience.

I don't even know where this is originally from, what's in it, or what the name is... all I remember is jotting this down on my blackberry so that I come again for another taste. JUICY + TEXTURE= perfection I'll be returning with my Californian friends to showoff the east coast eateries.

I came here for dinner on a Saturday night a few weeks back when a friend was in town and we were not disappointed. We made reservations, but I'm sure we really even needed them. The place was pretty full, but did have some open tabkles. The whole menu looked delicious, it took a while to decide what to order, but the servers were extremely nice and patient. When we finally decided, we started with the chips and guacamole, which you could tell were fresh, You could taste the avocado in the guacamole and I'd be shocked if they didn't make the chips there daily. For our entrees I got the Chile Reanos and my friend got a shrimp dish. We were both extremely pleased with our meals. My meal, had just the right amout of spice and the filling was perfectly complemented by just a bit of blue cheese. My only complaint was that it was too dark, so it made it hard to see the menu and such. I will definitely be back here!

I would've given 4 stars b/c honestly the food was good and the decor is nice too. We didn't wait long on a Sunday evening and overall it was cool. The only thing that put a damp on this place and probably affected my decision to return is the fact that egg shells were found in my honey pineapple fried rice. That's an absolute NO NO!. We told the server and she brought out a fresh new plate(maybe) LOL, but that's just not cool.

Around the corner from my office. Â It's an after work bar for me, meaning that I will only go here when I'm not buying the drinks. Â But hey, we're within a stone's throw of Times Square and if you want to overcharge the tourists I totally get it. We do come here semi-occasionally for office get-togethers. Â And on these occasions, I have noted that they have an amazingly large beer selection. Â It's kind of redic. Â And the food is decent too. Another reason for the 2 stars: them people that work there be RUDE. Â Like, come on, you're already overcharging me to drinks, not need to have attitude. Â We're often on the second floor, and they rent it out to 2 parties at the same time sometimes, and they put up a velvet rope to divide the two, and are very aggressive about us not crossing the line (and by they I mean the bar people, not the other party...)

Sometimes it's better not to read too many reviews because it might create unrealistic expectations; and that happened to me. We ordered the cold seaweed w. garlic as appetizer and that's one remarkable dish because you literally see it make to order in front of you by your server/cashier right at her cashier counter. The taste was ok but this is a dish best served cold instead of at room temperature. Â  We had the house special with knife peeled noodles and mixed Beef with "normal" hand pulled noodles. House special means mixed beef + fried eggs + noodles. Half of my knife peeled noodles sticked together and formed into big chunks, which I think could be normal because the noodles were cut fresh from a big dough without adding extra flour to separate them. The texture of the noodle was good, a bit chewy but not tough. The regular size noodles had similar texture, I'd prefer this over the chunky doughs. I'm glad the broth wasn't salty because that tends to happen in most places. Â  A good place for a quick and reasonably priced meal; order noodles and skip the rest of the menu.

Aurora Soho is a seemingly solid choice for those looking to stray from the Euro-fab fare of Cipriani or the down and dirty pub food of Broome Street Bar. Â That said, the service, decor, wine list and food were all just okay. Â  The place has promise - offering some lovely specials including a soft shell crab salad and a tomato/cucumber gazpacho that were quite tasty. Â  Â If you're in the area, I guess it's worth a shot.

Damn it... I knew this spot before all you guys discovered it. I used to be able to stroll in on a Sunday afternoon and get any table I wanted and never wait for sangria. My fave is the Harlem but sigh... why did all the rest of New York have to know about this place!?! Why couldn't it have just been mine, all to myself. The unassuming entrance, the wonderful strawberry butter and rolls, the mole sauce. Now I have to share it with the rest of the NYC peasants. sigh.

Have not had their prepared food. Have no doubt that it is spectacular, as their main ingredient (no pun intended) is superb. Thanks to RHLP my family has had two exquisite holiday dinner celebrations with their lobster. Thanks to RHLP for being there, will see you again & again. Will definitely try the rolls or bisque on next run to redhook.

I was really excited about trying this place. I went on a Sunday and they were packed but we only waited about 20-25 minutes which I thought wasn't that bad because it gave us time to look at the menu. Whilr we waited though we were by the bar and i noticed the bar tender was using his bare hands to tear mint leaves and to put ice in cups. Kinda rubbbed me the wrong way but maybe I'm just a germaphob anyway When we sat our waiter introduced himself right away and told us he would be with us in a few minutes which he was. We ordered the tomato soup for an appetizer and it took a half an hour to come out. But it was delicious! It took another 30 minutes after we were done with the soup for our food which I thought was a little long. My husband ordered a burger with their parmesan fries and I got the Mac attack. Out of all that, the fries were the only good thing. The burger was pretty average and the Mac and cheese was salty and bland. We then ordered the fried Oreos which was really good. It came with a shot of chocolate milk and a little bit of espresso ice cream. I think I would go back and try something else since their apps and desserts were good.

Great joint for some Japanese curry!!! Their champion platter is one of the bigger curry latter I have seen in my live LoL the only down side about this curry house is the high price for a small little bowl of extra rice is almost 1/3 of price of a regular platter lol but Â the free water makes up for it ;)

I've visited Cafeteria a few times with friends and once on a date and all of my experiences have been consistently good. Â The restaurant is a decent size with both indoor and outdoor seating as well as a lower level. Â The decor is cool and modern but has a slight ikea-ish feel but still very fun, particularly for groups and it can get loud at night. Â The outdoor seating is also heated so you can still dine outside (with very cool heated lamps) when it gets a little chilly. Â Now mind you this is chelsea so be prepared to see lots of Â fabulous gay men on so if this isn't your scene, Cafeteria may not be for you. Â The service can be hit or miss as I've had a range of experiennces but it's never been horrible. Â Food and drinks are pretty good as well especially the mac and cheese. Â I also personally recommend the blueberry mojito as its probably the tastiest mojito I've ever had! Â Definitely a cool spot for lounging with friends! Â Kudos Cafeteria!

AWESOME! One of the best places I've been to! I'm quite the critic when it comes to sushi, especially veg sushi... The varieties of veg, rices and sauces were perfection. Prices were right on... worth every second of the wait for a table. I will for sure be back next time I'm in New York. Favorite: the February roll of the month was something with beets and absolutely amazing. Best veg roll I've ever had no doubt.

Walked in and was greeted and seated promptly. Within seconds, a glass of water and utensils were placed in front of me. I looked through the menu and flipped it front to back at least a dozen times. I thought how could there be such little selection. No creativity just plane sushi and kitchen orders. Honestly it was a let down from the better reviews. It is a cozy little restaurant that fills up fast. My waitress didn't seem to want to answer anyone's questions. She was frank and pretty much just served me food and charged me. The salmon was probably the only good thing I can say I digested. Soggy rice and soup was below par. Can't say I'd recommend it.

Damn that was good. Â Almost the best Vietnamese Banh Mi sandwich I've ever had. Â They really do it a disservice by serving it cold (at 6pm), but for $4.25, I'll take it home and microwave and toast it. Â Is it better than Baoguette? Â Baoguette's seems to have a bit more meat and bit more of that gooey stick-icky and therefore more decadent in my opinion. Â But at this 4.25 price point, I'll definitely come back here just to be sure.

Really great food and friendly as can be staff. Yes, it's a tad on the pricey side compared to other quick middle eastern joints but that's because they use much better quality ingredients, and you can really taste this. I would definitely come back.

One of the best run restaurants in the Brooklyn, food, service and vibe are all right every time I have been there...with the exception of Restaurant week (don't go on that week). They have basic Latin American fare that taster fresh and seasoned right...not over done like some other places. One complaint I have is that they put way to much ice in the pitcher of Sangria...next time I will ask for no ice. Â Been here at least 10 time and will be back :)

Jadis is a lovely little/a little bigger than little, wine bar with delicious food, and a great atmosphere. They know all about the wines they serve, and they have a nice selection of beers as well. No liquor though... By far the thing I love most about Jadis is the staff. I had my birthday party here and they were so accommodating and patient with our large group. I called ahead to reserve a spot; the owner is such a pleasant and helpful person. Â I chose Jadis because they weren't strict about everyone arriving at once to eat, and they were cool with the group getting bigger throughout the night, as long as we stayed in our large section or by the bar. They saved us a great loungey area in the back with several couches and a large coffee table for food and drinks. The waitress was attentive all night, and didn't mind if people helped themselves to drinks at the bar. Everyone mentioned how it was a great location for a not-so-rowdy birthday party. I just went to Jadis for a second time a few weeks ago, but this time we did not have a reservation, yet we were a large group of 12 people, who trickled in at different times. Again the owner was so kind and accommodating and the waitress as well. We had the table for 2 hours before people who had a 9pm reservation arrived. They allowed us to add more chairs as more people arrived and they were very cool about latecomers ordering food 20 minutes before we had to leave. Overall I think Jadis is a great place for large groups and the tables upfront are cozy and romantic, so imagine it's a good place for a small group as well. Definitely go!

Il Bambino may have the best panini in all of New York. I live a ten minute walk from Il Bambino in Astoria, so needless to say I go more often than I should. It's just so darn tasty! They have a large menu of paninis and crostinis, as well as a seasonal soup and a few other items. I go all the time with my boyfriend and share a panini, crostini, and soup. There's really no way to go wrong here. They have a brunch menu Friday- Sunday with egg-based fillings in the paninis. All the meats and cheeses are from local shops and the spreads are killer. There usually is not a long wait, and when the weather is nice they have a backyard patio seating area that is great! Prices are good, food is great. Go try and become an addict.

This place was a total let down, definitely over hyped. Went there with a group and half liked the food while the other half was disappointed. The chicken was nothing to rave about, was average. The worst dish was by far the gnocchi, it was the seasonal dish with spicy sausage. It was nothing special to look at, appeared as if it could have just been dumped out of a can and the taste, ugh was like a soggy sausage pizza. Because most of the gnocchi had burnt bottoms, combine that with marinara sauce and sausage equals awful. The only good dishes were the swordfish & side of potatoes. But still would not recommend, there's much better places around.

Loved this place! Â Went there to celebrate my roommate's birthday. Â  they printed up custom menus for our large party, and the service was great. Â Quality Greek cuisine; everything was fresh and delicious, including dessert. Â Our group had many vegetarians and everyone loved the food, I will definitely be going back!

Was so excited to try this and couldn't believe how great it tasted! I've had kimchi in Korea before and this definitely tastes a lot alike! I had the Seared Pork Bowl and my boyfriend had the kimchi fried fish- he loved it! This is his first time eating Korean food so he was hesitant about it but now he can't stop talking about it! Would definitely come back.

Want to know the best bargain dinner ever? Â Go to dumpling house and order 1 order of dumplings and a beef sesame pancake. Â It's $2.50, and so good! Â  Â The cilantro and sauce on the sandwich...yum. Â One of the other works as a good lunch. Edited to add: Â They have remodeled and added seating and a few new menu items. Â The only one I have tried is the peking duck sesame pancake sandwich. Â It was yummy!

Cute, little town like place for brunch! Fabulous music, packed with people and calm atmosphere. We ordered: 1. The steamed eggs with sundried tomatoes - 5/5. A little on the salty side but a great meal 2. Steamed eggs with the salmon - Also great- really good portion of eggs and salmon. Compared to other places with this dish-this place had great presentation and taste! 5/5 3. Nutella crepes - nothing particularly special about it. Better off getting the eggs Cappuccino was also really good. Will definitely revisit. Account for waiting time though!

WOW! Â Upon coming to this location (very windy during wintry days), it seem so barren from the outside. Â It was in a neighborhood that is probably still being developed. Â But when you walk into the dining area, all the seats were FILLED! Â Luckily I made an apptmt for my party of 15, but still! Â It fooled us but in a good way. Â  This place does get pretty noisy but it was alright. Â I think to enjoy the sunset and view, the best time to come would be during the summer time when the rooftop is exposed. Â I mean, during the colder weather days, they have an indoor heating system, which is fine. Â I just did not like that they keep opening the side doors for the dishes to be carried out :(. Other than that, it was a good experience. Â The seafood was decent. Â I enjoyed my soups and sides. Â If you check the website, I think there are some periodic shuttles that run from the station to this restaurant, not bad at all!

Hidden down in the basement level of an office building, with great izakaya and a tremendous selection of sake. Loved the Beef Back Ribs, Sashimi and the Siu Mai, as well as the Black Sesame Creme Brulee. I'm not a sake expert, but the wait staff was extremely helpful in explaining and recommending a fantastic sake.

In addition to having had a fantastic lunch at Gramercy Tavern in the past, we also held a small lunch reception in their private dining room after our wedding ceremony at the Marriage Bureau. Darlene, their events coordinator, could not have been more helpful and accommodating, and was brilliant at answering all of our questions (and there were a lot!) as quickly as possible. The private dining room itself was amazing! We had the option for additional floral decorations, but the standard decor was absolutely gorgeous--lots of seasonal greenery and a succulent centerpiece. The room holds up to 22 people, but some of the leaves were removed from the table to accommodate our party of 13. It was the perfect amount of intimacy--not too cramped, but we didn't need to shout across the table either. The waitstaff were totally attentive and professional as well (I think we had our own "crew" waiting on us), and it just totally enhanced the atmosphere of our special event. And the food--THE FOOD! It goes without saying that our guests were RANTING about how fabulous the food was. We opted for hors d'oeuvres before the meal, which were chosen by the chef, and each one that came out was better than the last (the fried oysters were a huge hit with even the most passionate of seafood haters). The meal itself exceeded expectations and the portions were generous. I had the Peanut Butter Semifreddo for dessert and it. was. INCREDIBLE!!!!!!!!! At the end we were surprised with trays of tiny treats (mini macarons, chocolates, mini chocolate tarts with meringue) that were worth feeling overstuffed. Overall, our meal at the Gramercy Tavern was the absolute highlight of an already unforgettable day. I wish I could get married every week so I could keep coming back again and again!

I've been meaning to go to the Brooklyn location for a while, but the one in the city just seamed a little more convenient. I went with a few friends and we shared everything. The place doesn't seem like a Southern place, it has a Brooklyn hipster vibe. The thing to get, of course, is chicken and waffles, the white meat was surprisingly juicy but I do wish there was a dark meat option. The waffles were all light, airy and crispy. The food: Crawfish Hush Puppies- Remoulade sauce. The hush puppies were nice, it was fried well and not greasy. The remoulade was a tad spicy and it went well with the hush puppies. But if I didn't know there was crawfish in the dish, I would have never have guessed. yelp.com/user_local_photâ€¦ Mac and Cheese- gruyere, fontina, aged white cheddar, Ritz cracker crust. The mac didn't really have enough of a cheesy taste, it seemed more like an Alfredo sauce. The dish didn't seem seasoned and the pasta shells didn't have any taste. yelp.com/user_local_photâ€¦ Chicken and rosemary+mushroom waffle- Rosemary was my fav waffle. Had a nice aggressive rosemary taste, the chicken was nice and crunchy and didn't feel greasy at all. It was tender and juicy for white meat. yelp.com/user_local_photâ€¦ Fried Chicken Parmesan- tomato sauce, mozzarella, sundried tomato and basil waffle. This sounds odd as hell, but it was surprisingly good. The idea of putting tomato sauce sounds disgusting, but it worked nicely. The cheese was a non factor but the chicken picked up the tomato sauce nicely and it went well with the waffle. yelp.com/user_local_photâ€¦ The General- fried chicken with General Tso's sauce, rice and broccoli waffle. I actually heard a lot of good things about this one, but sadly, this was my least favorite. The General just tasted odd, it didn't seem like General tso's at all and it was uber sweet to boot. The broccoli in the waffle was weird as hell, especially since the broccoli was over cooked and it had that weird over cooked broccoli taste. yelp.com/user_local_photâ€¦ Coconut rice pudding- whipped cream, black sesame cookies, toasted coconut. Ick, I was not a fan. It was too loose for rice pudding, it was like coconut soup but then it was also chunky like cold New England clam chowder. yelp.com/user_local_photâ€¦

I've been to Barcelona. Â I've been to Las Ramblas. Â I've been to this resto on a date. Resto 411: - Tiny spot, overall...I'm not even sure if they have a bathroom?!! - Real tiny bar...like 5 feet long and 2 feet deep - Packed as ish with beautiful peeps..and Castillians could be found habla-ing, drinking, eating and reminiscing about their homeland's deelish tapas - Estrella Damm beer on draft...mmmmmm Tapas we smashed up: - grilled octopus over Mediterranean salad w/purple potatoes - shrimp in garlic, white wine & lemon - Prince Edward mussels in a tomato sherry wine sauce - Grilled sardinas over marinated peppers & onions - Sauted mushrooms w/almonds & sherry wine - Giant langoustines Sucking the guts outta the giant langoustine heads while my date stared in horror was quite entertaining. Â Silly American chicks need to eat like the Spaniards when eating tapas.

AH! They're open late and my room-mate and I stumbled in because we were starved. What a treasure we found.. clichÃ© Chinatown hole in the wall experience with solid food at a bargain price. I spoke to the waiter in my choppy Mandarin and it seemed to give us more respect sine I was the only white guy in the place... and my room-mate's Korean. Â  Can't remember what I ordered but it was flavorful and satisfying. The bok choy was ok (needed soy) and the duck in my noodle soup had a lot of tiny bones and not all that much meat... but it was cheap, so I can hang. **Only reason I didn't give the place 4 stars is that we may have been overcharged (we weren't in the mindset to dispute it)... and -more importantly- later that night, I got one of the worst migraines I've had in over a year and couldn't figure out why. Upon reading some other reviews... it seems that they use MSG.. which may not be a big deal for most people (won't kill you), but it is certainly a trigger for me. :( That alone may deter me (personally) from returning... but a fond memory no less.

The best Katsu I have had in NYC. It was a slow day at work in Midtown and I had a craving for Japanese Curry Katsu. Luckily Go Go Curry is only a 10 minute walk from my work place. For around $10 I got the Home Run plate which came with Katsu, Shrimp , Sausage and a boiled egg. I left satisfyed with a tummy full of carbs and protein. The Katsu has a nice crispy crunchy outside and warm juicy pork inside. The curry goes well with the rice and Katsu. For me its a perfect match! The Home Run Plate is good for those who can't decide what to get because it has a little bit of everything! :)

Underwhelming. Was very excited to eat here, ( really enjoyed eating at Bozu!!! ) BUT i was kind of disappointed. Most of all by the service. Bad service puts a BAD taste in my mouth. We were served by a woman dressed in overalls who just didn't seem to care at all. Had to ask three times for a glass, had to ask twice to see the menu again....etc etc. Portions were skimpy...my eel and avocado sushi tacos had tiny scraps of eel. The spicy bukkake udon was quite good as was the seafood udon special. Would not return here.

Best panini I've ever eaten. I love the owner. She's so authentic and is super blunt but I love that about her. Everything is AMAZING and super fresh. They know what they're doing here and the prices are incredible. My mom, dad, and I all ate for $30 and got multiple dishes.

I love this place. I actually venture here sometime 1 or 2x a week. The food is always solid, the service is good. Â They have a really good happy hour special and their backroom is gorgeous for brunch.

The best Italian in Little Italy! Â We've been to Pellegrino's several times over the past few years and it always delivers. Â The pasta, veal sorrentino and ricotta cake are delicious. Â We always leave with a smile. Â Great service and reasonable NYC prices. Â NOT a tourist trap ( maybe the only one left!) 5 stars from me and my picky husband!
Great comfort food

I have run by here so many times on the weekend as I would head towards the water. And every time i would pass the benches outside would be full of people and the inside looked bustling as well. However every time I would get home I would forget where it was until recently. I was on vacation and made a special effort to track down this place for bunch and I was not let down. Â From the service to the decor to the food everything was fantastic! I know you say to yourself..but really how can someone mess up brunch its so easy... well yes but it can be messed up ... trust me and everything here was fantastic.

Perfection arrives on a prada-esque plate here at Sushi Yasuda. Their decor is emulated by their food; clean, perfect, simple, elegant. I don't know where else to recommend someone to go more than here as long as you don't mind that there are no crunchy California rolls and no loud banging techno music. And trust me, I love that scene too, I love my Blowfish Sushi and my Blue Ribbon, but this is sushi in it's perfect state: raw. My girlfriend had a plethora of eel to choose from, couldn't make a decision, and so tried five different types. The smile on her face as she gulped down her baby tako was of sheer pleasure. It was light, buttery, and had a wonderful texture. We hadn't had better tako elsewhere (although Sushi Roku's baby tako special sashimi was excellent in Vegas as well and comes in at a close second). The seabass soup was incredibly fragrant, the fish flaky and wasn't dry in the interior at all. The sake we had (and much of it we drank that night I must confess) was amazing. We don't usually drink cold clear sake, just nigori which is an unfiltered sweet sake that is white, and our server picked the perfect one to accompany our meal. Four bottles later we were ready to put our Manhattan coats on and bear the cold as we walked through Midtown in awe and in love of the city I fantasize about as home. Although not cheap, Sushi Yasuda is worth every dollar. I would have paid three times the bill and still had been satisfied. My miso did really taste better there. And to me that's the question that I always ask myself, "Where is the miso better, and is it just a figment of my imagination that it is?" No, it was better here, along with everything else. Everytime I go to my beloved NYC I always hit up Yasuda. You'll see us, bundled in the corner, with hands wrapped around our tea and sake, eyes wide, just waiting for the freshness to drop on the table.

Big Thai place in Â Long Island City. Nice service, friendly staff. Not very cozy. I ate here twice, the food is so-so... Price is very in-expensive like in most Thai places... If you have tried Dee's in Sunnyside or Shri pa pa in Woodside on 65st (sorry I am not spelling this name right, I know) you will see what I mean. Tuk Tuk is the main stream Thai food nothing special or very authentic here.. Descent, good food yes, Authentic Thai, that's debatable... Hugs

Don't be fooled by this easy to miss restaurant - the food is amazing, whether you are getting take out or eating in. Â I've seen the chef from Ngam Thai, Chef Hong, (who was on Iron Chef) eating here. Â If you live in or near Hell's Kitchen, this is a must try! Veggies - Try the avacado papaya salad and pad ped proam: delicious!!

Extremely disappointing. They advertise all you can eat blue crabs from 12-4PM. We showed up at 12:20pm on a Saturday and the place was empty. There may have been 4 people eating crabs. Â We were informed that they were already out of crabs 20 minutes into the deal! Â They shouldn't advertise this deal on their website if they only have 40 crabs for the entire day.
I tried a lot of BBQ in the city (Fette Say, Blue Smoke, Hill Country) and here is my review on Mighty Quinn's BBQ compared to the others: l-homme.us/lhomme/mightyâ€¦

I ordered delivery while staying in NY and the dishes were bland and uninspired. Â Can't comment on the atmosphere or presentation as I had delivery but the Satay had 4 skewers of meat and about 1 Tablespoon of dipping sauce. Â The Pad Thai was as bland as plain pasta. Soup and Ahi were okay but Calamari appetizer was chewy.

A lot of people don't get the hype behind ramen, pork buns etc. but this place has hands down the best ramen in the city. My go-to is the Akamaru Modern and I add pork belly or a soft boiled egg. Also, line can be long... very long. Best bet is to come at an off hour as to not wait 1.5+ hours.

The crepes here are phenomenal! It is made with buckwheat flour and a lot of butter. I've had the ones with apricot jam and chocolate sauce. Both are amazing! I've also tried the escargot. They served it out of the shell. It was buttery, garlic-y and yummy! The bread it came with could be better though. I will keep coming back to this place. It is very small so try not to come on a Saturday night, like we did. We ended up sitting at the "bar". It's not actually a bar. We sat on bar stools facing their very tiny kitchen. It was pretty cool watching the chef make crepes but it was too hot.

What a unique, wonderful place! Truly a destination for adventurous eaters! And only 15 minutes from Grand Central, I can even get my Manhattan friends to go! Order the live lobster and squid stew. Not only is it fascinating, but very, very tasty. Not for the faint of heart though! Also don't forget to use the squid ink, it adds a whole new dimension to the dish. This is NOT a good place for one or two people. You need to go in a group of a miniumum four as dishes are HUGE - they are served family style. Also it helps if you have a Korean friend familiar with the dishes of course! I adore this place, its one of my best excuses to get my friends to take the 7 to Queens :-)

This post is a few weeks late, but I'm writing it anyways. Â I'm not a fan of meatballs, but this place was amazing! Â My opinion might be borderline skewed because we were starving at 2am, but it Â was nonetheless, extremely satisfying, and I'll definitely go again. Â Plus, you just can't beat the price! My suggestion: meatball smash with a side of alfredo sauce and the original tomato sauce. Â Then pour a little of each over the meatballs.

The brunch at L.P.P. was super disappointing. Â The seating was too cramped - they tried to seat a party of 5 adults (including 3 grownass men) at a table for 3. Â Finally we crammed into a booth for 4. Â For some reason, there was no heat, and the place didn't warm up until about 1pm when it got crowded. Â I guess body heat is better than none? The ham and swiss crepe with green salad, the croque monsieur with amazing fries, and the eggs benedict were all very tasty. Â The "pancakes" = giant salad plate-sized cake of corn muffin consistency, super sweet...and the "fruit salad" was MAYBE 1/2 cup of chopped strawberries. Â The brioche french toast was 6 teeeeeeny pieces and some "fruit salad", causing my 6'1"/200 lb little brother to alternate between laughing and shaking his head over his "brunch". Skip the brunch!!! Â The price ($10 with coffee, juice, or tea) is nice, but for 12.95 you could have a big ole plattah with a free mimosa at Windsor Cafe.

Yet another new Mediterranean/falafel joint in the city. Â Perhaps it all started with the street carts, monitored and executed by immigrants trying to make a living. Â Then someone recognized that there's a needy market out there for this grab-and-eat sandwich, so brick and mortar places started to pop up like daisies. Â Once upon a time, you could score a falafel sandwich for just $1.50, but now with all these organic and sustainable messages, you might have to pay $8 and upward nowadays for a decent sandwich. Â While there will always be the 'cheap' rendition of the fried chickpea mash and sliced, marinaded meat, if you need a sit down place, you're never far from one. Â Hence we have another hummus location. Â Well, the title said 'hummus', but unlike the Hummus Place, the star IMHO is the meat. Â There are gyro, shawarma, chicken, steak, and taboon (chicken/steak from taboon oven) and only a slight mention of hummus on the menu. Â Nevertheless, this place is great for vegans/vegetarians because of all the interesting fill-ins, which unlike Maoz, is assembled by the busy staff behind the counter. Â Though they did not go cheap with the fillings. Â They really try to stuff the pocket of pita or lavash wrap to the fullness. Â Oh and the bread, of course. Everything is baked in house in their taboon oven, roaring continuous to leaven up the doughy casing for your protein. So glad there's even whole wheat pita available! Love that. Â I even bought an extra pita (50 cents). There are lots of spaces for eat in. Â As they just opened last week, everything looked brand new and clean. Â The staff is still learning the rope around the kitchen and not all menu items are available yet. The meal won't be as cheap as the dollar pizza joint a block away, but everything is freshly made, spacious area to dine inside, and just glad it is not another fast food or chain restaurant opened in this space. I look forward to return and try the hummus, but not as an afterthought, but as my main dish. Â Hint hint. Â Please include a hummus plate option on your menu!

This what I imagine a Korean home style dinner to be like. The 6.95 buffet was tasty and had a lot of variety from warm to cold to firey foods to choose from. Even a noodle bar in the back of the place. I liked every dish I had and I cannot even tell the names of the dishes I had. I do remember loving the chicken stew, that tasted like home and my mom cooked Peruvian food, so go figure.

If you're looking for a cozy, comfortable, and delicious place to enjoy food and wine then Grey Dog is the place to go. Always have welcoming staff who will accommodate you and make you feel at home. Do not leave without trying their sweet potato fries. Awesome happy hour with 1/2 bottles of wine!

Came here with a friend on a sunday at 5pm because i had a living social deal. Brought a few months back, used it two weeks ago. Apparently the establishment is under new management and the place was emptttyyyy! Food was wack and the only bartender there was also our waitress Â and dj. Gets two stars for their lychee martinis!

I just ordered from this place and feel highly motivated to write a review. The food here is awesome. I had the Kale Salad, the Late Night BLT, and 2 cookies. The Kale Salad was light, lemony, and flavorful. The Late Night BLT had thick cut turkey and a slightly hot/spicy kick that was on the money. Cookies were bangin' It's a bit pricey at ~$20, but well worth it.
AMAZING. Sushi is out of this world. I love sushi. 1. make reservations by the bar. 2. try the tasting menu and let he chef surprise you. 3. you will fall in love with sushi if you're not a fan.

A nice, hidden understated spot. If you come with just one buddy, you can sit at the tea bar (if there's space) without waiting for a table. * Black sesame creme brulee - 4 stars yelp.com/biz_photos/5QgBâ€¦ (with black sesame ice cream) This could easily have been black sesame overkill, as the creme brulee was topped with a black sesame crisp AND black sesame ice cream. But somehow they avoided overkill as all the flavors and textures were slightly different, enough to complement each other. Any single one of these elements would have been really underwhelming by itself, especially the creme brulee (I would say its texture was a little too soft for my preference. I like it a little more firm. Also it was served at room temperature - I'm not sure what's proper for creme brulee, but I like it cold with a freshly flamed crisp top layer). But put all three together and they just go together really well as a dessert.

Once you see this place from the street you just can't turn it down. There's a cute covered outdoor patio area along the sidewalk perfect for people-watching (I once saw Natalie Portman stroll by). It's the perfect kind of place for a late breakfast/early lunch and their brunch items are unique. Recently I ordered the Israeli eggs, which is just a plate of 2 eggs however you like, salad, hummus, and couscous... sounds weird but makes a great combination. Their coffee is excellent and some dishes come with a little glass of fresh-squeezed orange juice. The service is very friendly and responsible. Cheap and delish breakfast hang.

Apparently, there are two spots right next to each other. Â The spot on the corner of Prince & Elizabeth is for dine-in while the one further north on Elizabeth is more for to-go orders. Â If you're shopping on Broadway, make it a point to stop here for a break! We only stopped by for a snack...the grilled corn Mexican style. Â Pretty damn good so get one for yourself and don't share! Â The cayenne pepper puts it all over the top.

My "greenest" friend wanted to catch up and so I was not surprised when she picked Northern Spy Food since they focus on local and sustainable ingredients. We both weren't that hungry so she ordered the winter squash soup, which was hearty but wasn't out of the ordinary, while I ordered the kale salad with squash, almond, sharp pecorino and lemon dressing. The kale salad was well balanced in flavor and in texture, but it also wasn't amazing. The cod we shared was great; crispy skin with tender, fragrant meat. The freekeh risotto with zucchini, kabocha and mascarpone is on my list of what to get next time I go.
