The star of the meal was definitely the chocolate caramel cheesecake which was decadent but not overly sweet; it was perfect. The service, however, was far from perfect. Our waiter wasn't mean but inattentive. I literally had to walk up to the cashier to get his attention when he charged me for a different table's check ($40 more than our check). I admire their focus on their earth-friendly ingredients (+1) but their service and food left me wondering if it is worth coming back to. I will try their brunch though, since I'm always on the hunt for great spots to eat my favorite meal of the week.

I've heard some mixed things about this place from friends who live the area. First of all it reminds you of being in Little Italy with the hawking from non-other than Mr. Grimaldi himself. Well, that a nice impression of what's to come. All I can write is this: The number 1 was almost indelible. The pancetta had a really strange odor to it and we felt that it was well cooked. Plus our soup taste like warmed over water. And table service is nothing to talk about but just take the order and walk away... not all too friendly. All you have is the very disheveled looking Patsy the pizza master play the game of small talk with you. On the bright side dessert was the only good point I can make about Juliana's. Some of my friends that are long time residents of dumbo call both Grimald's and Juliana's tourist traps.

I LOVE THIS PLACE! Â There are a few reasons: 1. the Chef/Owner! Â He's crazy! Â But such a nice man. Funny, warm, caring, etc. Â 2. The place is so small, but wonderful for intemate dinner with a group of friends and/or clients. Â 3. the menu is diverse, well thought out and always excellent. Â Although, as a creature of habit, I'm taken with the hanger steak - its always pretty amazing. Finally, 4, its BYOB, so it make the great food all the more affordable, when you can rock it with your own amazing wine. Â Just make sure to bring enough for the crazy owner to share a glass! ;)

Love this place-inexpensive and delicious. Â I bring all my friends and family here who come to visit, and now my Dad insists I take him there anytime he visits. Â Their soup dumplings are awesome and I also really love their chicken and cucumber with red pepper. Â The wait can be ridiculous, so I usually try to get there for right when they're about to open-if not, prepare to stand around for a long time (especially if you have a group of more than 4). Â They seat you with random people but that's never bothered me at all, but I do tend to talk a lot. Â Definitely an experience.

I grew up with Junior's, and it was always a yummy way to go... Maybe because I was a kid I thought it was the hottest coolest spot... Unfortunately for this location,the menu is "meh" (BLT best way to go), the lunch portions are big and sloppy, c'mon pasta on the plate that runneth over, negative on the food Â presentation and I think the quality is lacking... I think that the cheesecake itself is still stuck in an era prior to pastries becoming influential... Don't dislike it, but don't like it either... I give it a 3 because for others it's a cool place... As for it being called "Jewish Food", seriously NOT.... Check out Katz's or Second Avenue Deli, Zabars.....then you will know what a party in your mouth is...
Golden fishball noodle soup. That's all you need to know. You're welcome.

Perfection. Really there isn't much else to say about this place from the wine to the desert it is perfect. Started with the salmon and steak Tatar and had a perfect zucchini pasta and spiced lamp for our meals. Finish the ideal date with the guilt and gluten free tart.

4.5 stars! I really loved this place and will, without a doubt, be returning. Everyone says great things so I'm going to use this Yelp Review as a reminder for what I can't miss next time. So, future self, please get: - Fluke Carpaccio with Miso (so fresh) - Washu Beef (one of the specials - hopefully it's still there) - Beef Tongue (seriously tender) - Jaga Dango (donut outside, potato-paste inside - mashed potatoes, the consistency of red bean mocha) - Sake Oyake Don (salmon was great, roe was great - rice was just rice) - Chocolate Souffle with raspberry sauce (gooey and delicious) It's ok to skip: - Miso Yaki Onigiri (wasn't really crispy rice - this is better at Yakitori Totto (NYC) and Gochi (Mountain View)) - Buckwheat noodle with soy dipping sauce (my friend loved this, but perhaps I just don't care for the cold noodles) - Pork Belly (super fatty, very tasty - just not as good as the beef tongue) Looking forward to my next visit!!

This is a great place! Â I love the cozy, intimate, trendy atmosphere. Â The food and specialty cocktails were both great. Â I had shrimp and grits. Â They gave us blondies with our check which was a nice surprise and delight! Â Worth checking out.
Amazing!

Clearly the best burger place ever! I ordered the Truffle Especiale, and my friend ordered the Manly burger. The Truffle Especiale was mouth watering!!! The fried egg was a nice touch to the burger. The fries were really good too. We left completely satisfied. One downside: We had to wait for half an hour to get a table. But believe me folks, that wait is totally worth it! I will be back :D

Wow two BBQ places in Astoria now and that's awesome. While John Brown's Smokehouse is decent bbq, this place takes the pig. First off the place is setup like both a restaurant and butcher shop, the latter means a glass window with ready to cook meats mostly from their menu available for purchase by the lb. Ambiance is great, nice wood panels, tables and chairs / benches to be expected for bbq fare. Service was excellent, yes this as opening week but it was very nice that one of the owners came to our table and gave us an extra side dish during dinner and then a piece of pie to take home on the house. Probably shouldn't expect this every time but there obviously is a focus on good service here due to way the waitress handled our table, mention of relevant questionnaire at end of the meal, and then we were asked to like them on Facebook and yelp if we enjoyed ourselves. I dont mind at all when someone is trying to get their business promoted by providing good service and a good product. Food was great, first served muffins with amazing honey butter which was ridiculous. Sampled lots of meats, to be honest the burnt ends were mostly fatty and the turkey was nothing special but slathered with their two delicious home made bbq sauces I was very happy. Pulled pork was terrific, next time ill focus on that and ribs, brisket, sausages, and other stuff I missed. I also like how they use organic and fair animal treatment meats, healthy food makes tasty bbq. Although we had water, I noticed no coca cola or pepsi products, only natural organic soft drinks which is cool. I think I overheard they may have beer soon to and that would be a big plus. Not gonna lie though at some point we smelled windex, while cleaning is nice if your going to clean so close to food and serving area during open hours maybe check into some natural less chemically products. Anyways, this place rocks. Great BBQ in Astoria is a very good thing, hope its here to stay. Will be coming back to eat, maybe takeout, and definitely buying more prepared raw meat to bring home to my own sweet patio propane paradise by the park.
Fantastic Salmon Nicoise salad! Â Was super busy and yet service was flawless! Â Moderately priced~ Â Highly recommend

Great atmosphere, great for groups (downstairs) or for a date (upstairs area, overlooking the first floor). I came here with 9 other people and ordered the Whole Shebang - one of everything on the menu excluding the cheese plates and dessert, all for $420. We did the calculation and it turns out to be a $13 savings compares to ordering all the same items a la carte. Not a big savings overall but it took out the complexity of deciding what to order. Overall I really enjoyed the food. Â Given the size of some of the plates I didn't get to have a lot of each thing, probably about a bite or two, but they were flavorful bites. Â Not everything was great - the octopus ceviches was tough and chewy, the oysters were small and nothing special, as were the shrimp & chorizo skewer and the coca with mushrooms, ricotta and truffles cheese. Â Most other things were pretty good but the winners of the night were the smoked mozzarella skewer, crab ravioli, sea urchin risotto, and the braised short rib with beet pasta. Even though I only had a bite of each thing (and not even everything), I was very full by the end of the meal and was glad when we finally got the last plate, as I knew I would be tempted to try anything new they brought out. Â We didn't have room for dessert so I can't comment on it but they had some pretty interesting choices. Great place - I will be back.

3.5 stars. I really love the decor, the back garden adds a casual romantic vibe to the restaurant. Since I went with a group of people I got to try several dishes including masaman curry, Penang curry, curry puffs, salmon, short ribs, and calamari. My advice if you are thinking of ordering any of these dishes skip everything, but the curry and curry puffs, everything else was disappointing. The price however was very reasonable and the service was on point.

My GF and I visited here recently because of yelp. Â Wow, you reviewers are right, food was great! Â The French Onion soup is the best that I can remember having! Â Seriously, the best! We shared two flambees, the biquette and a blackened chicken one with goat chess. Soooo Good! Â Food was priced right as well. Â The service was great, mostly family and straight from France. Â Our waiter was friendly and funny. Â The owner made a point to thank us as well. Â It can get cramped but thats a fact of life in manhattan. Â  Definitely will be back.
Cuban sandwich is the best ever! Must try along with (of course) the grilled corn on the cob! They are so delicious!
one of the best chives and pork fried dumplings around!!!

The soup dumplings are to die for. Food is all round outstanding. Bring your own bottle is a nice option. Service can be hit or miss - but the food more than makes up for it. Ahhhhhh those soup dumplings!
Food was well seasoned. it's a hot spot and Â so expect a lot of chitter chatter. I could not hear my own voice. The wait is too long. !, exceptional staff,

If you crave sicilian pizza... this is the place to eat!!! Although it's a bit out of the way to get to... it's worth the time and drive... and adventure to get here!!! Plus they have Italiam ice and soft serve ice cream (get the orange cream swirl!!!) that's surprisingly good and tastey too~! It's best when you take some home... and reheat it in the toaster oven... and let the crust get a bit more crispier than normal... but just to hear that first crunch when you bite into it... it's to DIE for~!

I've heard about Eataly for a few months from a foodie coworker. Â Although I am not a huge fan of Mr. Batali's, I am certainly now a fanatic of his eatery EATALY!!! Â WOW!!! There are so many nooks and crannies in this place all mixed with fresh, fragrant, and delicious groceries (how can anyone choose just one brand of chocolate?) that it all seems somewhat overwhelming. Â One turn and you end up in tapas, another turn and it's the coffee/gelato house, another turn and you've got the pesce restaurant... We decided to eat first in the Pesce restaurant in order to avoid the over-indulgent shopping that laid ahead. Â We started off with delicious white wines from the region of Umbria. Â One was light and fruity while the other was dry and full bodied. Â We then had the tuna tar tar on crostini appetizers. Â YUM......... Our main course consisted of fish (IL PESCE Restaurant) Â  I ordered the "CHAR" which I had never had before on a bed of lentils with a fusion of fennel...amazing. Â Char is a fish similar to Salmon and it was cooked to perfection. Â Quite flavorful and rich. I think the best part of the evening was of course dessert. Â I have had gelato before and liked it. Â Now, I am a FANATIC and am afraid that I will have to open my own special charge account at EATALY just for my daily consumption of "il gelato" in Pistacio flavor. Mario Batali, thank you, you make my heart sing!

We live in the neighborhood and have been eating there for a quite a while. We just tried to order today like we always - even if it takes time lately since Guy passed by - and we've been advised by the manager that we were not allowed anymore. The employee says that we "cursed" at the staff and we need to "behave" since it's a family business. I never cursed any employee or delivery man in my life, i work in the industry...i've never even heard something like that. I explained the manager it must be a mistake and the guy didn't even try to explain the facts, when it had happen, just decided to back his staff. When we explained this never happened with us, the employee asked if we still wanted to order... Obviously not. I don't understand this behavior, so anti-customer and disrespectful, especially since we've been supporting this place a long time. Very, very disappointed and not hungry anymore...

Really super cute spot my friend Bee too me to. It's so quaint and the mood is just right in there. Thumbs up. It is dimly lit but not too dark. They got it right. We shared hummus and the eggplant for apps. I had the lamb with apricot and prunes for my entree. I had the peach martini. Good but not great (meaning, I like it strong), however the presentation was nice and the flavor was right. Â The only thumb down was that our waitress gave us the wrong bill (undercharged us) then another waitress chased us down two blocks (we didn't even notice!) to come back. She was very nice even though that was weird. Â I've never had that happen before. Overall yes I'd go back if I'm in the area (I came from Queens to meet my friend). Â  I think there's an outdoor part also in the back.

I'm sure it's boring to read a review for a pretty solidly reviewed place, but I've been here so many times I feel I owe it to Yelpers. Â  Do's: Â 1. Get there early-ish for dinner (like by 8 p.m.), especially if it's a Thursday-Saturday and you want a table and you have more than two people. Â 2. Order the Captain Lawrence Liquid Gold if it's on tap. Â 3. Order any of the panini or the AMAZING mac & cheese, but if you order the lamb chops make sure you specify how you want them cooked; they can be a little too rare. Â  Dont's: Â 1. If you don't have kids or don't like kids, maybe stay away from brunch hours. Â They have a kids menu and it tends to attract...well, you know. Â 2. Â Don't order a mojito. Â They just don't know how to make them. Â  The service here is always good and friendly. Â We've actually never had a problem. Â The 3 stars is due to one-too-many undercooked lamb chop incidents and overcrowding (the wait and the close-together tables) at peak hours.

tight area and the waiter was rushing and it was hard to get her attention to order drinks or food but the food was really really good and it came out fast but its a little pricey............ i won't go back but it was a cool experience

Walked by this place a few times and were always intrigued by the older gentleman cooking at the front of the house. The man just looks like he knows what he is doing. We had a couple of soups here a few days ago. We'll definitely be back for more. We also got some house special fried greens which were over-priced compared to the rest of the menu, too greasy and wilted. The soup was top notch however.

More like 2.5 stars. I could take it or leave it. Loud at,osphere, generic decor, and a teeny tiny menu posted on the walls. Our server was hating his life big time and was pretty crotchety. The nightly special food was great while everything else was pretty mass produced---- Don't even ask if they have fettuccine Alfredo or you'll get a serious serving of sass mouth. I couldn't help but wish we had gone down to little Italy to have a different commercialized Italian experience.

Amazing food, great atmosphere...I will absolutely be coming back! Started the meal off with the roasted cauliflower soup. Was perfect for a fall night and just the right consistency. I had the braised lamb shank for my main entree and it literally fell off of the bone. Every bite was better than the last. All local seasonal ingredients used which truly makes a difference in taste and quality. Be sure to ask about the local wine and spirits they have.

Came here for dinner date last week and the place was perfect for a first date. Â It is intimate and quiet enough for you to actually hear the person next to you. Â The lighting was also perfect so you don't feel like you are under a police interrogation light. Â The waitresses who work there were super friendly and seemed to know my date well so he is probably a regular there. Â  Overall, the food was pretty good and the portions were big for a restaurant in the west village. Â I had the snapper which came on top of a bed of rice and vegetables and had this nice slightly spicy tomato based sauce on top. Â I really wished the restaurant offered bread for the table so I could soak up the sauce. Â  The place only takes cash so bring cash if you eat here. Â Thank goodness I had some on me because my date actually made me split the bill. Â Needless to say I don't think there will be a second one! Â Hah
The best food ever!! When the food is this good, you kinda don't have the right words to describe it. The platter sells for just $6 but tastes like a million bucks!!

Make a reservation early, and arrive on time. Food is made with great care, using fresh ingredients and interesting combinations. Slow down, enjoy the atmosphere which feels a little like an indoor garden scene from a Murakami novel. Really delicious, unique meal--order a variety and eat it family-style.

I kept hearing all the buzz about Amy Ruth's so I thought I'd give it a try. I was looking into the different soul food restaurants of Harlem because I'm having a Â party coming up and was looking into getting it catered. Â It was a huge disappointment. The menu is definitely overpriced. I ordered The Ludacris (Fried Chicken Wings with Mac N Cheese and Candied Yams). It was definitely a huge let down. I definitely cook my own soul food at least 5 times better than what I tasted. The chicken had absolutely no flavor to it; it wasn't seasoned at all. The Mac N Cheese looked liked a layer of shredded cheese just sitting on top of it. And the candied yams just tasted like something was missing. I would not recommend coming here. I only had one dish but first impressions obviously will not keep me coming back regardless of the other dishes that might be good.

The grilled corn-YUMMM!! This place is smaller, but it does not disappoint! I went while I was visiting NY, with a friend whom had found it on Yelp and we were both very satisfied! The pulled pork is also a must-have! Prices are great and you get a great street view of SoHo! Love it!!

We stopped in late-night for a drink and some deviled eggs. The eggs were really good - I wish I could have them again, but for brunch. The french fries were matchstick-thin and delicious, with fried garlic and rosemary and LOADS of salt. So much salt, I felt pruney. The place is expensive but I'm told to go back for the burgers. I'll definitely try again as long as the wait isn't too long.

Very good food and excellent service. My friends and I visited this restaurant and thought the food was very good. The prices are reasonable, and the beer menu is very extensive. I thought the staff was more than courteous, and I enjoyed my steak tartar. I will definitely be back.

Now that I have read some of these reviews, I am upset that I did not try the date cake. Â Outside of the apparently unparalleled experience of the cake, however, I can speak of the rest of the experience. Â First of all, this restaurant is relatively hard to find given that it has no sign (Brooklyn contains a number of restaurants covered in steel bars with no outward indications that an eating establishment is indeed kept inside). Â Moto had lively music (although the flute player was slightly overpowering for my taste), delightful food (including an artichoke dish served with delicious saffron mayo sauce), and a surprisingly bustling crowd. Â It makes for a wonderful place to take a date. Â I certainly appreciated the introduction to this slightly hidden restaurant in the Brooklyn area, and I definitely want to take my girlfriend so I will have an excuse to try the "date cake". Â :)

They have an amazing salad bar with generous portions, large choice of good quality ingredients, and all for a really reasonable price for a midtown location. The food buffet is pretty good too (both hot and cold). That's all I've tried but they also have ramen/noodles/sushis/sandwiches. Bonus: nice upstairs seating area in the back.

One of the best restaurants I've been to in a while. I usually try to recommend dishes, but to be honest, I've been there 4 times and everything is unworldly good. The collard salad and cavatelli are must haves. The burger, wings and ribeye are can't miss. Seriously, come here before the wait is 2 hours.

I am a fan of hand pulled noodles, especially when you're able to watch him pull the noodles right after you've ordered them. The beef noodle soup was delicious, though i needed to consume a gallon of water afterwards. It's also hard to pass up $0.25 dumplings, so we didn't.
My first time here greatly enjoyed the sandwiches we had everything was just as expected after reading the yelp reviews

Been here many times already. Still an great authentic Japanese restaurant. Â I am not a fan of soba in general so cannot comment much on the soba noodles. Â The udon however, is delicious. Â I suggest the chirashi if you are hungry (too much rice) and also the special monkfish liver pate.

I was meeting a friend that I hadn't seen in a year. She hails from Astoria, so I figured she knew her Greek restaurants pretty well. I needed advice for my upcoming step 1 exam and she had plenty of advice to give, so we sat for over an hour catching up over good food. When I think Greek, I usually think of gyros and pita bread. The fact that I could bearly pronounce anything on the menu lent an air of authenticity. I enjoyed the decor - interesting ceiling concept. We ordered appetizers and shared a salad. I would recommend doing the same if you're in the mood for a light dinner or if you're saving yourself for dessert (or in my case dinner part II) elsewhere.

Went for dinner while in town for a visit, and this place was great. The bar was small and crowded, but the drinks (had The Orchard) were delicious. At dinner the grilled octopus appetizer was AMAZING (I had not had octopus before and thought it would be like squid, but this was hearty and not rubbery). Also had the salmon-avocado tartare which was good, but better with the wonton crisps as they provided a textural element (and the soy-wasabi sauce didn't do much for it, not spicy at all). I had the filet mignon which was cooked to perfection and came with delicious mushrooms and a potato waffle (yum) in a flavorful chimichurri sauce. My friend had the salmon over a bed of spinach with hollandaise, and it came with three friend lentil balls which were unique but definitely good. She said her dish was great. We ended the night with the profiteroles. It was just ok - the ice cream was good but the profiteroles were dry and therefore didn't taste fresh and flaky. Our server was great (Brianna). She was attentive, efficient and friendly. I know this is supposed to be an amazing brunch spot, but I would highly recommend that people try it for dinner as well!
FReally awsome!! and im picky, delish crisp crust, basil so fresh ..it was def just cut, perfect amt of cheeze..really awful wait evan at 10 pm at night we waaited an hr...byob

My favorite Thai restaurant in UES. Â Hidden gem in the region of the 2nd Ave construction. Â Completely unassuming from the outside but beautiful inside. Â Great lunch menu. Â Beef pad see yew and shrimp pad Thai are favorites. Â Their lychee martini can be addicting. Â Thai tea or coffee can be great sobering alternatives. Â Make sure you ask for the chili and tegu will bring out a set if 4 types of special sauces. Great price.

Invited coworkers for a Friday night dinner. They have a good selection of drink cocktails and wine. The crab salad and grilled octopus is highly Â recommended. The duck with risotto and huckleberry sauce was very tasty. The only thing was the place was pretty vacant for a Friday night. I suppose it's Â because it's all the way located Westside of Manhattan at the Ink Hotel and not that many frequent around the area.

We're visitors from the Left Coast and complete foodies! Found out about Totto Ramen on Yelp. Read the WSJ and NYT reviews so we had to try it. Arrived about 9:30 pm on Monday night. About a dozen people waiting ahead of us. Despite the light rain falling, our party of four decided to sign-in on the clipboard and wait. About an hour later, we got in. It's a very small place. About room for 20. Two tables for 4, 1 table for two, and about 10 stools at the counter. Initially, we split up. Two at the counter, two at a table. Then two adjacent seats opened up at the counter. Asked the waitress if we could all sit together. She was cool, very accomodating. Our wait was deliciously rewarded. Our party ordered 2 spicy ramens, 1 miso ramen, and 1 mega-ramen. Bowls came out steaming hot and as far as a simple bowl of noodles are concerned, visually appealing. Absolutely delicious. Rich, savory broth, noodles al dente with just enough "teeth." Char siu pieces with just the right balance of fat to lean. Scallions just mild enough, not too much "bite." Adds to the play on textures. Miso color and taste just right. Spicy ramen had just enough heat without overpowering the noodles and broth. Mega-ramen had a little too much garlic. Liked that we "porked it up" Â though. Still, earns 5 stars. If you have the time and don't mind the wait, you'll be rewarded. If you're starving, you can go to Lucky Burger next door and nosh on an order of fries. Just save your appetite. It'll be worth it.

After five months of hype I figured it was time to visit Ippudo and see what all the fuss was about. Before I start crying about how good the ramen is, believe me there were tears, I want to talk about the things which weren't so great. As has been pointed out previously, this is a chain, albeit a very good chain, the starters however are ordinary. Having eaten there twice in a week, I have sampled my share. Fried Shishito peppers - These short, sweet and slightly spicy green peppers, were unfortunately deep fried. They are served with a piece of lemon and some rather suspicious yellow salt - AKA chicken salt. My plutonium(MSG) radar was ticking. Karaage (Japanese fried chicken) - The chicken wasn't particularly crispy or really that tasty and was almost a little dry, I would have murdered some mayonnaise. Shrimp fritters - Deep fried shrimp, a greasy batter with a decent mayo/soy dressing. Pork Buns - I am a big fan of pork belly, when the fat soaks into my arteries and flows out of my pores, I lose it a little. Despite this I will try and do my best to remain objective - tasty but not as tender as Baohaus or Momofuku. At about $9 each you may as well skip them as they will be the last thing you remember about the meal, onto the ramen (around $14 each). Please don't mess around with chicken or duck, order the kakuni(braised pork belly) and if in a hedonistic mood, pay the $4 for extra kakuni (one piece). A large bowl of noodles with two fatty pieces of kakuni, kikurage (Mushroom), red pickled ginger, menma (pickled bamboo shoo), 1/2 hard boiled egg, sesame and scallions, drawn together by the most incredibly deep, rich and creamy broth, god damn, I didn't leave a drop. Is it wrong to want to bathe in it? Notes for the first timer: - If you go there prior to opening at about 4:45, and don't mind copping the incredulous stares of passers by not familiar with the Ippudo cult, you can join the line which will form rapidly. Otherwise expect a 45 minute or greater wait. No reservations. - Allow a good six hours mandatory food coma recovery time if you are going the kakuni. No tight dresses or skinny man jeans should be worn after. - The soup spoon comes seated inside a bigger spoon, which at first I thought was simply there to hold the soup spoon while not in use. However after watching a few fellow eaters, I think the bigger spoon is used to assist in the transportation of noodle to mouth. TBA. - Did anyone find it suspicious that they fill your water up so frequently? MSG radar. Tick. Tick. Tick. Both times I have been dehydrated for hours after. It could just be excessive salt. Â  - Did someone say the hostesses were pretty? An MSG foil?
Oh man Kamayan night. Thanks for letting me feel like a lost boy but eat like a king. Hands only, vegetarians beware. The food is awesome plus it's so fucking fun.

Surprisingly underwhelming. After standing in line for a good hour and glancing at exiting patrons with extremely satisfied reactions, we had super high hopes for this place. Unfortunately, the food came out really salty and the service was par at best. I really wanted it to be my favorite go-to ramen place, but I'll need to look elsewhere. I heard Ippudo was pretty good so that may be my next stop. Overall - worth a try, but meh.

The West Village is probably my favorite area of the city, and Extra Virgin is in my top, if not at the top, places to eat in the neighborhood. The countless raving reviews of the french toast does not come unwarranted, it really is that good--not overly sweet and perfectly creamy beneath the layer of toasty crust. If you haven't tried it yet, I highly recommend you find some time on a sunny spring/summer day, grab a seat outside and enjoy yourself some Extra Virgin.
One of the best cocktail bars in tribeca. Great kale salad, love the chicken wings, cocktails are excellent. Some of the portions are a bit small for the price but pretty standard for NYC

This place reminds me of a Japanese style tapas restaurant. Â They had all these different small portions of cooked food. Â I ordered the anchovy salad, dumplings, katsu don, fried calamari, smoke fish and Sapporo beer since it was Â half off on the weekends. Â After all that food and beer I was still hungry so I ordered the Udon with shrimp tempura (since it was a udon restaurant). Â The udon was very good as it was nice and chewy. Â  Then for dessert, I tried sesame ice cream since it was recommend by a fellow yelper. Â It was good and very unique as I have never heard or tried it before. Â It reminded me of Chinese black sesame paste with milk/cream. It was definitely a meal and didn't break the bank. Â My bill came out to $30 + tip. Â Not too bad for all that food and beer.

This is a great place to go for brunch. They offer FREE (yes, FREE) sangria to go with your meal, and they've got all kinds of varieties to choose from, both white and red. The food is very good, too. I've had the Latin Benedict, eggs Benedict made with arepas instead of English muffins and the Ropa Vieja con Huevos. It's all good. The only negative is that the service is a bit slow, but that has a lot to do with the fact that this place is always packed at brunch time. So be sure to show up when you have plenty of time to sit and savor the food and FREE drink.

I am pretty big fan of MP Taverna. Â It is top notch greek food and isn't crazy pricey to boot! Â The grilled octopus and meatballs are to die for. Â The service is kinda ehhh, but quick to make things right.

A lot of places in New York claim to serve "authentic' Italian style pizza, but I have yet to find one that gets as close as Piacere. Â The ingredients here have the freshness you usually only get in the motherland, plus the spicy olive oil was out of this world. I was also pleasantly surprised by the wine selection here: the chianti we ordered was great and totally reasonably priced. Will def be coming back any time I get a craving for pizza all'italiana.

Came here the other night with some friends after a long day of drinking and horse betting (Belmont Stakes anyone?). The first thing my friends and I noticed was how reasonable the prices seemed. $11 or $12 for most of their entrÃ©e dishes. I started off with the Insalata di Rucola con Pere, Noci e Caprino, which was very good. That goes without saying though as I love anything with goat cheese. Some friends shared the Polenta alla Griglia con Fonduta di Formaggio, which I was fortunate enough to try. The cheese fondue sauce that accompanies the polenta was delicious and we proceeded to mop it up with the bread once polenta had run out. Next up for myself was the Gnocchi di Patate con Prosciutto e Salvia al Pomodoro, which was a very good gnocchi in my opinion. I especially liked the addition of prosciutto as it gave the dish a nice bit of crunchiness to it. The portions were very reasonable and most everyone at our table was stuffed before they could even finish their dish entirely. Overall the atmosphere is very warm and dimly lit. I didn't notice outside seating, but they did have the big windows up front opened up. I also recommend the brunch here and while I don't quite remember what I ate, I do remember having a good time and enjoying the food.

I ate so much that I got sick, because everything was delicious and I couldn't stop eating. I think that pretty much sums up my review but... Complimentary popcorn with bacon- ADDICTING. I actually nearly demolished the whole thing while waiting for my friend to show up. scallops with roasted carrot puree, truffled corn salsa, capers- soft grilled to perfection. good with and without the puree. the bed of corn it was on, was surprisingly flavorful as well and not just there for decor. yellowtail tartare with yuzu gel, scallions, cassava chips- listen to the chef's recommendation of mixing it all up. delicious. crispy pork trotter with spicy mayo, slow cooked egg, and scallion- pulled pork is hard to make since it can become a bunch of stringy, dry pieces of ...string. not in this case! fried chicken with pickled daikon and herb ranch sauce- what is this witchcraft? WHITE MEAT CHICKEN THAT ISN'T DRY AT ALL? marshmallow ice cream with rice krispies treats- okay, where else have you even heard of marshmallow flavored ice cream? it will transport you back to childhood smores... unless you missed out on childhood and never had smores.

What do you order at a Shanghai Restaurant? Of course, SOUP DUMPLINGS!! Â  You MUST order the CRAB and/or PORK MEAT SOUP DUMPLINGS when you go to Joe's Shanghai!! Â Trust me, if you are here with a group of friends and family, you'd want to order more because 1 order only comes in 8. Â Before you know it, 8 of them will disappear into everyone's tummy. Â Anyhow, back to the soup dumplings. Â The meat and soup are mixed incredibly well inside the thin layered dumpling. Â To top it off, the dumplings taste even more scrumptious after dipping 'em in some ginger/vinager soy sauce. Â I just love it!!

A slice of Artichoke pizza is like eating a whole pie anywhere else. The slices are very flavorful albeit greasy. I was happy to try Artichoke (I ordered the namesake Artichoke slice), but prefer more typical thin-crust New York Style pizza. This is kinda like a heart attack on a plate, and there's much better pizza to be had in EVil.

This place sounded better than it actually is. It's a little hole in the wall in the middle of NYC's Chinatown, and sure, it does have handmade noodles, and sure, you can see them handmaking the noodles, but it was kind of disappointing. Nothing bad, but I think I was just expecting more from it. I've had handmade noodles in China, in Boston, and in the Chinese markets of LA and San Diego, and all of those were better than these. I think a large part of it was the way it was cooked- it was very greasy (the stir-fried ones) and the soup noodles were nothing spectacular.

The only meat I would recommend is the turkey bacon.... Everything is very dry. The food is very heavy, even the salads that they offer is full of mayo. Not very diet friendly. Quite inexpensive, a full plate of food would take you back less than $10.

Amazing fresh seafood with French influences, accompanied by a laid back slow dining atmosphere. Â Come here with friends and a couple bottles of wine, because you can stretch this meal out for a while and Neil the owner/chef-one-man-show in the kitchen has yet to disappoint.

I would give it more stars if the service was better and they allowed delivery and pick-up. I've been a regular there for quite some time and they don't care about repeat guests. They're always crowded. Reasonably priced good food, but I've had better dining experiences in Manhattan. I would recommend going there on a slow day.
I love this place. Rolls of paper towels on the benches. 1/2 pints of microbrews. Weighing your massive tray of meat and paying by the pound. I love this place.
Great place to grab a drink, a bite to eat, and catch a game on one of the several flat screen's!!!
Best damn BBQ ever! Brother-in-law and sister brought us here... Said it was great but its better than that!!! Country band, JD Patch play'n now... Having a blast!!! Love this joint.

This is a very good place for dumpling, old school dumpling and made with real crab meat :) the flavors are rich and the soup dumpling was soupy ! You are here for dumplings and dumplings only please, lol Don't even care about service, please:) Ugly place, no service, bad location. Who cares, they have good dumplings:)

One of the reasons I love Yelp is discovering little gems like this place. I honestly would have never found Joya if I was just walking around, or even consulted a restaurant guide or concierge. It's one of those places that you have to actively search for, since it is a bit off the beaten track. However, I really think it is worth going out of your way to try. When you walk down Court Street to find this place, you may have to do a double take. I had to walk up and down the street a bit and actively look in every building to find this place. The only advertising on the outside is a simple paper sign that says "Joya". No banner or anything else, just the basic sign. I actually thought for a moment that Yelp was fooling me, and that it closed and was long gone. But nope, it was there. I went with a friend, and I got the lunch special. It was two fried spring rolls and chicken Pad Thai, all for only 8.95. A very good deal for New York standards. My friend went with another noodle dish that came out to only 7.95, and again, very nice deal. Only problem was that it was a cash-only establishment. So please remember to bring cash, and there are a few ATM's in the neighborhood. The spring rolls were alright, though I felt they didn't contain quite enough roughage inside. Mostly just noodles, and that's it. Luckily no human teeth (like a previous poster mentioned). The Pad Thai, on the other hand, was delicious. The noodles were nice and tender, not too soft and mushy. Chicken was pretty limited, but it was a nice compliment with the dish. Just enough spiciness and flavor too, so it wasn't overwhelming. Service was friendly, and my water glass never went empty. Got our food in less than ten minutes, which is very good for a sit-down restaurant. Everyone there was friendly and helpful. Restrooms were clean and well stocked also, though a bit awkwardly placed (right in the middle of the restaurant, facing the seating area). Overall, I had a great experience here, and would definitely come back. What I like the best is that while coming here, I discovered the neighborhood (which I'd never been to before), and a few other restaurants that looked good. So not only will I come back here, but also to the neighborhood.

Verlaine is amazing. The place has a nice interior, a young, professional crowd, and lots and lots of lychee martinis for $5 during a five-hour happy hour. The place can get crowded, especially on weekends, but this is New York, so what do you expect? The food is small plates, so if you're really hungry, eat before coming here. Otherwise, enjoy the drinks and make some new friends :)

The best thing about these sandwiches is the bread. Â It's crusty and toasted but actually CHEWABLE and fresh. Â It doesn't scrape the roof my mouth when I bite into it, nor do I feel like my front teeth are going to fall out. Â Definitely messy eating, however, but they provide moist towelettes for you to wipe your fingers. We had the beef brisket and pork belly sandwiches, both of which were extremely tender and flavorful, but the beef brisket in my opinion just slightly outshines the pork belly. Â The lemonade was also quite good--you can tell it was freshly squeezed. Â  I was a little annoyed because I asked them to cut the sandwiches in half but they said they won't. Â Hm. Â Beware that there isn't that much seating here. Â The seats are upstairs and are bar-style.
This is my 3rd visiting. It's getting salty and salty....

I came here for dinner around 8pm on fri after a day of thunderstorms (perfect timing for noodle soups!) and the place was filled, but no wait! i ordered the marinated beef and kimchee udon while my companion ordered the chicken curry udon. my broth was delicious! the noodles Â were soft but tough enough to chew - very different from other udon i've had which were more tough and solid. the chicken curry broth tasted good but i didn't sit well w/ my brain- i have this notion that curry should be thick! ALSO, TRY THE BLACK SESAME ICE CREAM!!! it was AMAZING. we ended up getting another scoop on top of the scoop we had already. THIS place should be a part of the recession special ppt that's been floating around! total cost of meal w/ dessert and edame: 27$

While Freemans may no longer be the top of the Manhattan speakeasies, it certainly maintains it's decorative charm, fervent crowds and insouciant attitude. Lead by co-owner / downtown fixture Taavo Somer, expect the smattering of art stars, celebrities and models tucked into dimly lit nooks, gaily noshing gastropub fare under the watchful, wall-mounted glass-eyed taxidermies scowling overhead. The clipboardrix at the door plays guard against out-of-town gawkers. One whiff of intimidation, and expect her to utter a strategically dispatched "2 hour wait."
My current fav panini: Mortadella, garlic roasted potatoes, truffle aioli, pecorino romano
OMG, Jeff the owner has to be the nicest restaurant owner EVER! Fabulous food, friendly servers. Â Made my birthday one of the most memorable in 47 years. You can't go wrong here. I will be back.

New York, let's get this out of the way. We, and by we I mean Los Angeles, do ramen better. I know, I know, this can be a big blow so let me soften it with a few concessions. No doubt about it, New York is the center of the universe. There's an incredible feeling I get anytime I come to this fine city. Walkability is great. And often, you've got the edge on food, especially the higher end stuff. But just like I doubt I could find better Dominican food in LA, or better Mexican food in New York, I've come to realize that for much the same reason, we've got you beat on ramen: Proximity. I know, Japan is still far from LA you say, but we are the Pacific Pan Handle, and outside of Honolulu, we've got the biggest Japanese population. And thank God, I think that proximity and the awesome Japanese population we've got on the West Coast makes its presence known in the culinary arena. Apart from going to Japan to get the real deal, you can find some great ramen in Honolulu and LA! So I say all of this to say that while LA ramen has my heart, I've also been mightily impressed with New York ramen. You're not at LA levels, but you've got some good stuff going on here. And I've been weighing this all day, but I believe Ippudo just edges out Momofuku in my book on account of the ramen alone. Ippudo was bomb. The pork buns were good, but it's the Akamaru Modern ramen that really grabbed my attention. The noodles were the perfect texture, and the flavor of the broth was complex but to make it easy: downright tasty. The serving size was just right and the speed at which that stuff came out was awesome! The vibe inside I'm mixed on. I like the size of the place, as I didn't wait at all in line for lunch. But it's a bit too hipster for my taste. Totto has Ippudo beat there. I also struggle with the price as $15 for a bowl of ramen is a bit much. But you get what you pay for, and this stuff was good. The green tea with the receipt was a nice added touch and the service in here was top notch! I'm excited to try other ramen joints on a future visit, but for now I'd say Ippudo is worth a try!
Just ok. Cash only which is obnoxious for the volume they do. Over priced. The server rushed us in an out. Just as good if not better pizza elsewhere in the city. Don't make a special trip.

This place is the reason I started writing reviews on Yelp. Had friends in town and was trying to decide on a fun place for dinner. Chose this place without realizing I've been here several times. DUH! Â Anyhow...there must be a reason I keep coming back. Food, drinks, ambiance and prices are all good.
Honestly good was great. . .but it seemed a little salty. Everything did. Could have been me.

Not the Nicks of old. Not fantastic I was quite disappointed a lot of money for the type of sandwich. The sandwich bread was ok the meat was ok not enough for the price they charge. I ordered the eggplant, provolone with roasted peppers. Peppers were jared and not fresh roasted as I'm used to growing up in an Italian culture. I'm not sure if the cold cuts were boars head, I don't think they were. If you want a real hero there quite a few places that put this DiFontes to shame.

My wife and I went for lunch during Restaurant Week. Â The space was very modern with plenty of light coming in. Â We sat near a window with views of the Hudson. Â The service was slow at first as we had to flag down our server to take our orders. Â  We were pleasantly surprised with the selections: we had 5 choices for an appetizer and 5 choices for an entree. My wife selected the heirloom tomato salad as the appetizer, steamed skate as the entree and molten chocolate cake for dessert. Â I ordered the ginger rice bowl as an appetizer (as recommended by our server), fried chicken as the entree, and berry soup as the dessert. Â  We were first provided with a slice of rustic bread but was a little disappointed in the quality. Â  Then we received the amuse bouche, which was corn fritters. Â Even though my wife doesn't like fried foods, she did enjoy them as they were very light. Â  Next came our appetizers. Â We were stunned at the large portions and quality. The heirloom tomato salad was served warm with a light vinagrette dressing and berries. Â The ginger rice bowl contained sliced avocados, panko-breaded lightly-poached egg, pickled ginger, and scallions on top of a bed of seasoned steam jasmine rice. Â My wife was full after eating a large majority of our dishes. The entrees were delicious, but not as good as the appetizers. Â The steamed skate was lightly flavored with romesco sauce on the bottom and sliced fennel on top. Â The fried chicken was boneless and was served with a side of corn relish and a spicy scotch bonnet pepper sauce. Â My wife wanted to save room for dessert so I ate most of our entrees. The desserts were spectacular. Â The molten chocolate cake was the best I've ever had and came with a scoop of vanilla ice cream (not a spoonful like most restaurants). Â The cake was rich and really gooey on the inside. Â The berry soup was almost as good and topped with fromage blanc ice cream (French frozen yogurt) and a sweet biscuit that you can dip the soup. The waitstaff didn't rush us so we stayed for about 2 hours. Overall, we were really satisfied with the service and quality. Â Well worth the money, although we did pay Restaurant Week prices.

I love this place, the atmosphere is fantastic go there at the wrong hour and you will run into a long line. The food is great, but seating is limited due to the fact that it gets packed there pretty fast. I haven't there in a while and I miss it, perhaps before summer is over I'll go back.
I ordered take out from De Mole. It's a small and cozy atmosphere. The waiter that took my order was friendly. I had the chicken taquitos. They were yummy. I'll have to go back to try more dishes.

Have to say the place is a good place to go on the weekdays for a nice chill atmosphere but forget trying to come here on the weekends. Full of the bridge and tunnel "scene" crowd. Drinks are solid bartenders know what they're doing. Food is good.
One of my favorite restaurants in New York.

I am a thai food aficionado. Been to thailand over 20+ times and this place is as close as you can get to local thai cuisine in Bangkok. For lunch, I always Â go for the Wok Basil With Chicken ($9 tax not included). I love how the layout/atmosphere is suppose to depict a local street in Bangkok (though so much cleaner ;)). For lunch this is definitely worth it.

I'm not sure why a restaurant with over a thousand reviews needs another one, but perhaps I am the minority viewpoint of this place. We came in on a Sunday evening after seeing a play. Open table didn't have any reservations until the next month, but we decided to give it a chance. Â Put our name on the list and expected to wait an hour. Â After sitting down at the shelf bar and people watching, we decided to order and eat it on the shelf. Â Well, do yourself a favor, don't do that. First you have to order your food at the bar, and yes it was a busy weekend night, and "Brew" Â was very nice to take our order, set us up with plates , water and bread. You need to realize that the food here is served FAMILY STYLE. Â One dish can feed a minimum of 4 people. $38 for the chicken parmigiana, $10 for pasta. Â And you still have left overs. The food was ............eh. Â I have had better chicken parmigiana elsewhere. The greeter calling out names was so ineffective, anyone could have taken our table. Â  The noise level is insane, but for the most part people were friendly and we got into conversations with people waiting for their name to be called. Next time I'm looking somewhere else. Â This is not a relaxing place.

Had breakfast here Sunday morning as a tourist. The plan was to go to the Hell's Kitchen Flea Market and my maps showed it to be around the corner (incorrect). Well we ended up stopping here and the food and service was excellent. Kids had the silver dollar pancakes with Chantilly cream and fresh fruit (they passed the fruit to dad). Other meals were oatmeal very good, awesome croissant sandwich loaded with great ingredients and a simple scrambled and turkey bacon all tasty. If I had to find something only the Busboy was too quick trying remove plates, some of us still eating one of our kids felt he needed to give up his plate. I'd recommend the place very Â clean and the bathrooms were cool. Felt the prices in line with quality of food and were reasonable.
Best square in nyc

Modern Filipino Food in NYC. Went here a few months ago to have a cousin dinner in the city. We anxiously awaited the 4:30PM opening and were promptly seated towards the back of the restaurant. Our server greeted us and talked about the history of Marhalika and some of the items on their menu. He was helpful and sincere. Here's what we ordered: Garlic fried rice - Delish Chicken and Waffles (!!!) - A twist on a classic Southern dish. They served their fried chicken with Ube waffles, drizzled with a coconutty syrup... Freaking amazing! Sizzling Sisig - all of the pig's parts Trio of Vegetables (Long beans, puqui puqui, and mustard greens) Fried Chicken Spam Fries - only in NYC, of course! I heard that they were tasty. Ice cream trio I don't eat meat and Filipino Food does not have any true Vegetarian dishes, so I ordered the vegetable trio. I loved all of those veggies, except for the mustard greens; they were super bitter. The portions were small, but a perfect size for each of us. The decor of the restaurant was modernly decorated, small, but accommodates enough people. It has a welcoming, intimate feel to it. The bathroom was clean and modern. We ended our meal with dessert, a trio a ube ice cream, cheese/corn, and avocado. I know these sound like odd flavors/combinations, but they were delish. Filipinos love mixing salty and sweet. I really enjoyed eating at Marhalika. They did a great job modernizing Filipino Food. Hopefully other people can enjoy Filipino Food as much as they enjoy Thai or Vietnamese, or Sushi. Mabuhay!

Atmosphere was very rustic, beautiful 1920's era cash register (Bring Cash) behind the bar (BYOB). Staff was very friendly, food was absolutely awesome. Great BBQ Wings, Pulled Pork to die for. Great Price! Well Done Juniper, Well Done!

To me, this place was like "hipsters play restaurant." Â I promise I'm not hating on their success and I'm glad everyone else is so entranced by it. Â They seem to have Â mastered the art of good restaurant, over which they are extremely pleased with themselves. That's not to say it wasn't decent food or that the service wasn't pleasant. Â However, I'm pretty sure the reverance is due to equal parts hype and limited supply met with competence. Â I've been to Market Table a few times, which is supposedly from the same group of people and had a similar impression. I guess I can see why people like this place. Â It's tiny so it seems exclusive and desirable. Â The ceiling and the full walls of windows are cool and the food is good...not great, good. Â The focus of the meals are style, not substance. Â The wine list is okay and it looks quaint enough to film a rom-com fall-in-love dinner scene in this joint. Â If you like when Hugh Grant falls in love with Jennifer Lopez or when a ruggedly handsome Hugh Jackman pirate travels through time to fall in love with modern day Jennifer Aniston (who's playing a pediatric oncology veterinarian nurse), you will love Little Owl. If I walked into this place with no expectations, I'd say "solid three and a half stars, rounded up to four." Â However, with all the hype and the hoopla getting a table here, I found myself waiting for something memorable or amazing and it just never happened. Â This could be a solid usual spot, but they are way too hip and way, way, way too oversolicited to ever come back on my own time and dime.

My friend recommended this place to me and I must say the food was quite good. Â I'm not an expert on Cuban cuisine but I thought everything I tried was tasty. Â The ambience is nice. Â You can have a nice date there or even go for a family event. Â It's definitely on the pricey side so be warned. Â I would recommend it for anyone who has the urge to splurge.
My wife and I thought this pizza was amazing. However, we were hammered. The artichoke pizza with Alfredo is memorable. Would go back here sober just to make sure it was THAT good.

We have been to Cielo several times when it was located on 8th Ave. it was great. Â Tonight we went there (at the Mayfair Hotel) for dinner-BIG MISTAKE! The food was mediocre and the service was TERRIBLE! The waitress was rude, slammed the dishes on the table, not attentive, and tried to rush us out from the very beginning of the meal. I was embarrassed in front of friends that had joined us for dinner. You know what they say--"Screw me once shame on you-screw me twice shame on me". We won't be going back!

Came for a Sunday brunch. Â This place is very crowded. The food was an ok. Â I had the smoked salmon and egg salad sandwich with fries (don't remember the fancy name for it). Â I also had a bite of my friend's waffle with whipped cream (more of a big bite of whipped cream, and it was mm mmm good). Â The fries are just ok as well, and they don't taste like home cut fries. THe decor was very relaxing and I think the back seating area is very cozy. Â BUT did the 5 of us had a relaxed brunch? Â NO! Â Again, because it was toooooo crowded!!!

Pylos is delicious! Our waiter was awesome and he helped us make a solid wine choice since my friend and I were not very familiar with Greek wine. We shared a few appetizers, including the octopus which was really tasty and soup with chicken and orzo. Overall everything was fantastic. I will definitely go back. The atmosphere alone is well worth the trip. Make sure to make reservations, it was packed!

Loved the wine flight! This place was great for a night to catch up with a friend. I docked a star because the servers were so beyond busy/stressed that the service wasn't too great. Â They didn't even let us pick all of our wines in the flight because they were "too busy." However, I can't complain too much because they gave us the happy hour price past happy hour. I also visited the location in San Francisco and it was absolutely delightful (almost identical in appearance). I will return... Oh, and get the honey goat cheese ball...delish!
Best falafel and hummus I've had in the US. Great restaurant!!

Not super great, but best in near distance. Overpriced, pretty oridinary taste and preparation, and we all thought coffee was terrible. Not worth the 30min wait or $15 fixed price for Sunday brunch. Disappointing, but the area provides little else.

This place is great. Â Luckily was able to walk in and get a nice table after I heard some buzz about long waits, etc. Braised lamb shoulder = could have been a bit juicier but a great dish There was also a "special" ploenta which was the best dish on the table. Also, be sure to ask about the caramels.. I don't believe they are on the menu for dessert but there is an interesting selection and they are really good. Good atmosphere although a bit loud at times but that's the sound of people enjoying themselves! 4 out of 5 on this one... would definitely return & recommend
Good hand-cut fries in the East Village. I'm a purist when it comes to fries (i.e., vinegar and ketchup), but they have too many special dipping sauces to count.

This place is great! Went here in the summertime and had a beer while sitting out front on the sidewalk, then moved inside and got some appetizers once our friends arrived. The food was all tasty and the beer selection was decent. It was very crowded, but not in a bad way. It's quite cozy, it feels like everyone knows one another. The paper covered tables + crayons raise it to a five star....come on, who doesn't like coloring and drinking??

It's good. I'm not going to lie. But the wait is just ridiculous. I mean, listen, I'm all for great ramen and stuff. But I just really don't care much for waiting an hour or more for ramen. In any case, I got the one with all the different types of pork in it (the $15 one). Definitely couldn't finish it because they don't skimp out on the meat. But I knew my husband would be able to finish his and still be hungry, so I opted for this huge ramen. In any case, it was pretty good. No huge complaints, but i've definitely tasted better soup base (ippudo anyone?) than this one. But I have to admit that the different types of pork cuts were one of the best I've tasted. I liked that they didn't skimp out on the meat here. 5-6 huge chunks of pork and you've got yourself a pretty full customer almost forgetting she waited forever to eat in a really cramped table with two other people who were actually pretty nice at least. Almost. I'm all about the experience of it all, but at least I can have some of my own little space at some other unnamed ramen places. In any case, this is a pretty good ramen place. Go for the experience and then you will either love it, or if you're like me, know that at least you tried it and it wasn't too bad, but will probably for elsewhere later.

My boyfriend and I had dinner here last night before going to Sleep No More. The food was totally yummy and the staff was very helpful. We decided to share everything, which was the perfect way to get a little bit of everything! We started with the Empanadas and Tuna Tartar. The empandas were really yummy, baked and full of exotic flavors. My favorite was the beef and I also enjoyed the corn, skip the spinach as it wasn't great. The tuna was served over guacamole with toasted baguettes. The bread was a little bit salty, but the tuna was amazing! Then we moved on to the special salad which happened to be baby spinach with beets, ricotta cheese, and toasted walnuts. It was absolutely perfect! The dressing was very light, the beets were sweet and tender, and the walnuts were tasty. For our entree we ordered the flank steak which was rolled with veggies, egg, and some yummy herbs. It was served with the perfect potatoes- not too crispy and a little bit spicy. You could cut the meat with your fork. It came with a really delicious sauce. We finished with two different desserts- the bread pudding and the sweet potatoes. The bread pudding was perfect and served with a scope of dulce de leche gelato. I did not love the sweet potato, although it could be the rosemary-line gelato that turned me off. To top of the amazing meal the staff brought over two glasses of dessert wine (mascato) which was the perfect was to finish the evening. I will definitely visit here again soon. I would have given 5 stars, but I felt that it was a little expensive.
I love the brussel sprouts, calamari and burgers were perfect after a day outside.
So gooood!

There is not one bad thing I can say about this place. Â The food is incredible, always fresh, large portions good enough to share, and so tasty. The service is always on point. Â The restaurant is always packed, you will most likely always wait on line but even the wait is pleasant ... they bring you wine on the house while you wait! Â  The octopus is a must try. Â I can never get tired of the food here!

Came here for brunch on a Saturday in August, hoping to soak up another final outdoor dining experience of the summer. Unfortunately you're overlooking (and hearing) the East Side Highway, but if you can get past the noise (and the funk/fun of neighboring Bellevue) this is a solid outdoor brunch option. Food is reasonably priced and well executed - got the avocado toast which I wanted to essentially bathe in (gross, I know) and some mediocre lamb sausages. The boyfriend got a brisket and egg type deal that was pretty fabulous and I kind of wanted for myself. For dessert, go with the roasted caramelized bananas, which are actually listed as a side with brunch, not on the dessert menu. Phenom. Great service and friendly waiters are the icing on this fancy cake. Er, dining experience. Go!

Honestly, I had this place on my list because I thought it had the cutest little alleyway leading up to it. After reading reviews, I was excited to try the food, too. I went for brunch with a few friends today, and I narrowed it down to the 5 Cheese Macaroni & Cheese and the Raised Waffle with Banana, and upon my waiter's recommendation, I ended up ordering the waffle. It was good, but I wish I had ordered the macaroni & cheese instead. Both of my friends enjoyed their meals. One had the skillet, and the other had the poached eggs over grits with a side of fries. They mentioned that they weren't as filling as they would have liked them to be, but they had great flavor to them. It was such a cute place and the staff was very friendly, so I'd come back to try the macaroni and cheese if I ever get a chance.

Had to wait about 15 minutes before our group of 3 were seated. It was my first time there, and I was overwhelmed by how crowded and loud it was. The waitress was very friendly though, and remembered our request for a table, even through the crowd of dark jackets. My two friends were set on having a drink here because of the happy hour prices and the lychee martini. I don't normally drink lychee martini's, but I was open to trying the fruity drink because of its rave reviews. I found it to be strong yet delightful, and definitely addicting. With the alcohol settling and the candles glowing, the crowd was much less of an annoyance and it made for a great night.

I walk past Uncle Gussy's to and from client meetings all the time, but it's always 4PM and I'm full. Â Since it was nice out I decided to venture a few extra blocks for lunch today and I'm so super glad I did! The like looked long...like REALLY long...but it moved super fast and I had my partner-in-lunch-time-crime with me to pass the time. Â  I had the Greek salad (I like to pretend to be healthy sometimes) with lamb gyro, tzazaki, and a side of pita. Â The lamb gyro was amazing! Â There's no other way to describe it - perfectly seasoned, crispy on the outside and moist and tender on the inside. Â Yummy feta and grape leaves too! Â They definitely did not skimp on the tzazaki - there was enough to dip the ridiculously ridiculously good pita in at the end. Â  Will definitely be back again, and again, and again =)

I was in a mood for some Corned Beef Hash and Eggs for breaskfast so I called and ordered for my coworkers and myself from Los Papi's. What a disappiontment, they sent us old Hash (being a lover of Hash, I know the difference) and wheat toast that seemed to be stale (no bread delivery this morning?) We should have sent it all back, instead we tossed it out and ordered from somewhere else. Â  Â  Â  Â  Â  Â Papi What Happened?! This isn't the like you, Getting the orders wrong 9 out of 10 times I can deal with, but old food.........No Good!

Really solid food at an incredible price. Â Especially for this neighborhood, you really can't beat the price. Â The menu variety is fantastic too, with so many pastas, entrees and apps to offer. Â Very casual atmosphere, nothing fancy about the ambience so don't expect a romantic meal. Â  Service was prompt, and pre-meal bread was good too with nice olive oil on the table. I recommend this for an affordable delicious meal out.

I came here for brunch with my girlfriends yesterday to celebrate my birthday, and we could not have had a better time. When the manager found out it was my birthday, he didn't just mix us a free cocktail - he gave us an entire bottle of white lambrusco and a trio of fruit purees. With a birthday candle. We didn't even have a reservation, but they treated us like royalty. The food was absolutely spectacular - we had baked eggs, gorditas and steak and eggs, and everything Â was perfect. Can't say enough good things about the baked eggs, holy cow. The lettuce on top was the best part - lightly dressed, very lightly cooked, so delicious. Coffee was tasty too. In short, Juventino went out of their way to make our day special, and we will be back. Highly, highly, highly recommend.

Any place that can convert me to a Hush Puppy fan is a fan of mine... This place is great... Thanks to the new fresh-produce/organic/non-steroid tainted food craze, this restaurant pumped out some good eats for me a week ago. I met two of my girlfriends there and was blessed with a minimal, but intimate setting and felt not a single wave of guilt come over us as we were clothed in thrift tees, jeans, and old clunky boots. At ease and with great experienced help, we were brought a fantastic Reisling. We ordered and our food came out shortly after... We got the hush puppies with brown sugar butter (originally a side, but requested for an appetizer) and they were just a true delight - perfectly brown and golden, but warm and soft on the inside with creamy butter that had been perfectly touched with brown sugar. Â We also ordered the heirloom and red onion salad which was de-lish. The tomatoes were sweet, juicy (in season) and the red onion was perfectly sliced thin and the vinaigrette was light and satisfying with fresh ground coarse pepper corns. For the third appetizer (keep in mind we shared everything), we ordered the short rib gnocchi with broccoli rabe in a parmesan broth. Â The gnocchi was so tender it felt like they had just been rolled out and plopped in boiling water. The short rib was lacking, but did not take away from the dish as a whole (I just like short rib). Â The parmesan broth was light, but held true to the cheese's natural flavors and the rabe... well, it was there and it was good, but who cares at that point?! For mains, we split the swordfish and the lamb shank. Preferrably, I like my swordfish seared, which I emphasized at the time of ordering and it came out as I wished. Â It was placed on top of a corn, tomato, Â avocado and frissee salad which was a nice compliment and resembles one that I Â prepare myself with swordfish, as well. The lamb shank was fall off the bone perfection... It was properly braised and stewed in a red wine broth and even still had the little morcel of marrow that I sucked out of the bone at the end. We had nothing left in us for a hefty dessert, so we ordered the berries with fresh yogurt and honey. Â I fantastic little sweet treat without the guilt (and calories!!) The bill?? Practically non-existent... 160 was the totaly. Highly recommend this place... relaxed, casual, and fantastic honest food! Enjoy!
Amazing black bean burger! wish i couldve gotten it with falafel but this tastes amazing. Â Its like super healthy nachos on a burger! Â great location, great service, clean establishment!

New York offers so many different restaurants, how is one to choose. Â I want to eat at them all! Â Somehow I think "all" is almost impossible, especially since I'm not a local. Â With that said, I'm sure going to try for "all"! Â A girls gotta have goals after all. My first night in New York and BF treated me to a night out at Gramercy Tavern. Â I knew reservations were full since I did my research the week or so before. Â I was pleasantly surprised that around 6:30 on Friday night we were able to snag one of the last tables on the Tavern side. Â  We started with cocktails and I opted to start with the Jalisco Pear with Herradura Blanco Tequila, Pear Liqueur, Allspice Dram, and lemon. Â It was perfectly balanced and had the right amount of sweetness that kept me craving sip after sip. We were on the East Coast so I couldn't resist the oysters, and we had to try both preparations, two iced and two roasted. Â Both preparations were exquisite, the iced ones were served with a flavorful mignonette that I wanted to drink as a single shot. Â The other two oysters were lightly roasted and were served warm with a pesto like sauce that made each one sensational. Next was the Fluke Tartare with radish, kumquat and trout roe. Â Since we were sharing all the dishes for the evening they split the dish for us, a nice touch if you ask me. Â The Fluke had a wonderful citrus essence throughout and was complimented by the thinly sliced radish and trout roe. Â  We kept on going with the appetizers and shared the Duck Liver Mousse with pickled vegetables and grilled bread. Â We received a generous portion of creamy duck liver mousse with crispy grilled bread. Â We enjoyed each bite as we slowly spread each piece of bread with the luscious mousse and varied each bite with a different pickled vegetable. Â  We kept the evening moving and made our way to entrees. Â We opted to share the Cobia with king trumpet mushrooms an oat risotto and bok choy. Â I was curious about the nontraditional use of oats to make a risotto and how the whole dish would come together. Â The Cobia was flaky and moist and the king trumpet mushrooms added an earthy note. Â The oat risotto was a stand out and was a wonderful vessel for the entire dish. Â The whole dish was well thought out and executed with every detail in mind. We couldn't end the evening without dessert and thankfully we both eyed the same dessert on the menu, the Lemon Pudding Cake with pinenut nougatine, yogurt and rosemary. Â I want and need this recipe so badly, the Lemon Pudding Cake had a moist cake texture with a rich lemon flavor. Â The pinenut nougatine added superb texture to the entire dish. Â I cannot emphasize enough how tantalizing this dish was. Â We scraped the plate clean wanting to find every last morsel of cake. The menu and the food are sensational and that alone would keep me coming back here for years to come. Â The service was impeccable with everyone working in unison and taking care of each patron as if they were part of large family.

I saw that most of the reviews were for brunch, but they seemed mostly positive. We had dinner at CafÃ© Gitane on Tuesday 12/30/2014 at 6:30pm My experience was lukewarm, but perhaps I need to go back for brunch, as that seems to be better put together. First, the room, hotel and hotel bar are beautiful. I'm definitely going back JUST for the hotel bar, stunning. We arrived at 6:20pm and the place had only a few filled tables, still we waited at the door for several minutes as waiters walked by and there wasn't a host/tess to acknowledge us. Actually, 2 men arrived after us and were greeted first. Hostess was icy at best. Does she know how to smile? Waiter with the green hair was also simply doing his job, with no welcoming gracious attitude. He didn't technically do anything wrong, but he wasn't very warm either. Half-way through another waiter took over who was very polite and warm, long brown hair and comforting smile. I complimented him on the way out. The table was actually quite small, all of your plates/drinks couldn't quite fit. The chef should be aware of the plate sizes that he/she are ordering. They may look great in the kitchen, but they don't fit on the small tables. I ordered the iced mint tea, but was brought the hot tea instead. I didn't complain We started with the baked feta with capers, olives and chopped tomatoes. Quite flavorful and a good start. They were out of the chicken sandwich that my companion ordered, but the waiter offered another choice that was decent. I had the couscous with chicken. It was a tower of couscous, quite delicious with a smear of cold hummus on top and a ring of pesto on the plate. Quite satisfying, flavorful and nicely portioned. We skipped dessert, but I definitely wanted to have the chocolate bread pudding..mmmm, next visit if offered at brunch.

I'm not a big ramen fan. Â I've never understood why people crave it so much. Â  But I'll admit that Ippudo was good. Â The broth and noodle texture was really tasty. Â I ordered something that came with pork which made the broth a bit greasy for my liking but nonetheless delicious. Â  Ippudo's decor is gorgeous, I especially love the bowls in the front of restaurant. Â Servers are tentative and friendly, always a plus. I'm unsure if I would go back though, unless I'm having a carb-attack . Â But that's because I'm not a noodle person!

My date took me here over Valentine's Day weekend and we were seated immediately, thanks to a well connected friend of his, instead of having to wait 30 mins for a table on a busy weekend. Our waitress (sorry forgot your name but you're hot!) was friendly and informative, giving us the rundown of the specials and offered suggestions for first timers. Service was on point; drinks and food arrived without us having to flag them down, they refilled our glasses with water when it was at the halfway mark, they collected our plates and gave us extra napkins, and they did all this with superb customer service! As for the meatballs...ONOM NOM NOM NOM!!! I ordered the "everything except the kitchen sink" which came with 4 mouthwatering meatballs, on top of a bed of well seasoned greens, a side of chickpeas, beans, and broccoli. Everything was well seasoned and complimented each other, playing upon the palate. Top it off with one of their ice cream sandwiches and you couldn't ask for a more perfect meal! My date went with mint ice cream tucked in between 2 huge chocolate chip cookies (mind you I HATE mint with chocolate chip) and I nearly devoured the whole thing!!! Everyone needs to check this place out! And bring your friends! So you can finally say Â "balls in your mouth!"

This was the worst experience that I can recall in my entire life! I loved the food there, almost each time, and I went there a lot. Â Only one lazy Sunday late afternoon to encounter very unpleasant episode there with management. Â They refused to serve my friend a glass of wine who was just meeting me there at the point when I had desert. Â So I said please give ME another glass, and they told me that I can't have it since I already ordered desert! (apparently that's a cut off right there). Â They follow a corporate policy of not serving alcohol to non-dining patrons so diligently that even at 5pm with three tables occupied they still had to follow a policy as if it was a Burger King, not to mention in a very rude way. Â I actually came back AGAIN and brought this up to the female owner of the place and she was just as arrogant as the Sunday manager and told me that "it was always their policy". Â  All in all there are hundreds of trattorias in this city and dozens are just as good (food-wise), but being treated in this manner is unacceptable. Â I shouldn't have to go spend my money and beg for something on the menu like a food stamp beneficiary. Â Pizza and non pasta dishes btw are nothing special at all. Â And decor must have been picked by the owners themselves at some unflattering flee market. Â So good luck but don't even dream of any substitutions and avoid at all cost any arguments because they will only make you feel like a beggar or may just kick you out.
Great place. Great food, I especially enjoyed the kitchen sink salad. Great, friendly service. Hint: get a growler and fill it with iced coffee or cider.

I'm crazy for dim sum, and this a great place to go to without going to Chinatown. I've been twice with my husband and we loved it. The decor is muted but not in a boring manner, the place still has character, with a major focus on a long, roughly-designed wooden dining table near the center of the restaurant and it is lovely. The food is flavorful, fun and delicious but also affordable. If you want to try various foods at a lower price and without giant portions, the lunch special is great for that. It's not a large place but it isn't a hole in the wall. So far we have tried the following dishes: Kung Fu Xiao Long Bao, Sesame Chicken, Scallion Pancake with Sliced Beef, Beef with Scallions, Pan-Fried Dumpling, Orange Chicken, and Vegetable Spring Rolls. I really hope that this place can withstand the New York pressure and not become a jaded, distant memory of a place.
Outstanding! Â I have never had a better macaron!

Last of its kind. Unexploited by hipster irony, unimpeded by regulation, and an unwavering menu, you need to put this place high up on the list. You go to a place like this more for its kitsch than its nuanced food, I will say that. It's a cultural artifact, what with the jukeboxes, the homey, "hair-in-the-face" kind of waitresses, and its 50s throwback feel. I've had a few romantic, post-coital breakfasts here, and let me tell you, it's an intimate place. It's not in the heart of Park Slope, it's off a highway; it's not gluten-free, but greasy; it's got immense charm. Write your novel here, bring the family here after church -- even if you have to wait to get into this hidden shoebox of a place, you'll be happy you did.

I have eaten at Halal Guys for years and have watched them expand from one cart to the many that they now have.
