Whether they are the best halal cart in NYC is a constant debate that I do not have the answer to yet. There are still many carts left that I want to try. But as far as Halal Guys go, I do consider them at least one of the best. The big selling point here is the value. You are getting a plateful, and I mean plateful, for $6. This is an unbelievable value anywhere, let alone NYC where a bottle of water will cost you $2 on a good day. I always get the mixed over rice with plenty of white sauce and hot sauce. Like many have already warned, the hot sauce is no joke; I would definitely try a couple of drops to sample first. The lamb is delicious, but on the saltier side, so the chicken and rice help balance it out. The pita is nice to have when the hot sauce becomes too spicy. There is great science to this meal! From a longtime fan, I still believe this cart is going strong and am excited to see how far their popularity extends.

In ten years and probably twenty visits I've ordered this. Tsingtao Beef chow fun (with and without black bean sauce (prefer without) Char siu (to go, once). That's it, plus tea. I've tried bites of other people's food and it's always good. I know that's very narrow, but it's one of those goldilocks moments, infinitely satisfying and affordable food from a place that's open late. Â It's uncomplicated food and an honest mix of people.

I popped into this cute little bar yesterday for Sunday brunch with friends. The menu seems small but the food is really tasty. I ordered the fried Catfish Po' Boy and Â a biscuit on the side and was so pleased! The fish was well seasoned and I loved the pickled veggies on top. Great place.

I was in NYC for business for a few weeks and one of the our customers suggested we go to Cafe Habana. WOW! I'm from Houston and we have great Tex Mex. The BBQ here is legit!! My go-to options are brisket (best in NY) and the dry-rub spare ribs. Both are so tender and full of flavor. The sauces are delicious but I barely use them cause the meat is so good on its own. Side options are okay. Coleslaw is good, mac and cheese is okay (liquid queso), and corn bread is hit or miss. Service is cafeteria style. Lines for food can get pretty long but the bar is always quick. Tons of tables, great for big groups. There are bunch of big screen TVs that are good for sports and the back room has a stage so check their calendar for live bands.

The food is definitely good but nothing out of this world. I do think that the hummus is delicious, but be aware it is sun dried tomato flavored. The souvlaki platters are pretty good but hard to eat. Overall, if you are craving Greek, I think this place is definitely the best in the area. I am Jealous! I am jealous of Laduree pastry chefs for their inarguable talent. I was hopeful of this place, because the neighborhood could use a new restaurant, but I won't be coming back here anytime soon. After blowing $300 on food and drinks for a party of 4, my friends and I were still starving!! The food was good, but the portions are way too tiny. Despite the prices seeming reasonable, they really weren't for how little you get. This is a great place to take your anorexic girlfriend, but don't come here expecting to be full if you're a normal person. I will return to this restaurant when it starts living up to its awesome name and providing their diners with healthy portions. Then, I'd love to give this place Â a 5-star rating all the way.
Hands down the best sandwich spot in the East Village. Been coming here for years.

great restaurant with amazing service and food. I would recommend the tuna tartar which is to die for. Have a nice selection of wines at good prices. A great place to dine with friends.

This is not your everyday Thai restaurant, because they have their own styles First, let's talk about the location, located on 9th Ave between 47th and 48th Street I personally don't like going that way, because the closes train only stop on 8th Ave, so if you want to go some where from 9th Ave to 12th Ave, you have to do some walking, and in the winter = No Fun! lol But this restaurant is not that far, you can take the blue line which is A, C or E trains and stop at 50th Street and walk few blocks to this restaurant If you not sure where to catch the blue line, just take your train to Times Square stop, and connected from there, and I'm sure most of you, your trains stop at Times Square. I have a meeting with one of my friend for lunch, and since I never been, I have to looked around when I arrived in the area, it was during day time and sunny, and I gotta tell you, once I arrived at the front of the restaurant, I thought it was out of business. lol Because the sign of this restaurant not really stand out, the front of the building is Gray color, and the name of the restaurant is chrome and is small If someone once told me about this restaurant and I happen to be in the area, and I walk by, I will never thought this is the same restaurant someone once told me, unless you are going there because of this restaurant Once I walked inside, just like I told you before, this is not your everyday Thai restaurant, beside the 1 buddha sitting on the wall, you will not have any idea this is a Thai restaurant, is very modern, black and white is their color, you see the bar on your right hand side, tables and chairs on the left, and it goes all the way through the end of the restaurant, I'm thinking this place can probably held about 80 for sit down dinner and standing maybe 130-150 people, probably good for Christmas party They seated us kinda in the middle where the swanky chandelier, and next to it is a table, since I'm sitting on the left hand side facing the wall, and the other table in the middle with 2 chairs on each side facing each other, that's mean one of the chair back is facing my back, and is no walking space in between, so every time someone walk by, I have to move my chair, and often people kicked my chair by accident, very uncomfortable, luckily is not busy during that time, or else I will probably yell at someone. For the food Once again, they have their own Room Service Thai Style I ordered the Fried Coconut Calamari, never have them before, I had Fried Coconut Shrimp, but not the Calamari I gotta tell you boyz and girlz, you GOTTA try it when you decide to dine here, it was so....good, not only is was hot and crispy, is also very tasty because they added the coconut in it, so different My friend and I both ordered the Pad Thai (I know right, seem like that's all everybody order when they goes to the Thai restaurant) lol But not in this case, because my friend and I read over the menu, and they was writing on the bottom of the menu explaining how their Pad Thai are so different from the others, and they called it the Room Service Pad Thai If you clicked on some of the pictures on here, someone actually posted on here, is Seafood Pah Thai covering by egg white, is very nice, and is also tasted very good The presentation is really good and I like it a lot Last but not least, the server She came by and took our orders, didn't say much, never did stop by and check how we are doing and asking about how was the food etc My glass did almost went empty one time, but someone else saw it and refilled for me Overall, 4 stars I will recommend this to my friends that's for sure.

A group of 12 of met here last night.. It was a mixed group of people.. Miss A's cousin wanted us all to meet here.. Among the group were three kids and two adults who didn't like spicy food.. The twelve of us fit very comfortably in the back circular table with the lazy susan.. Â I would say, 12 is the limit for that back table. I took the reigns and ordered the first round for the table.. I ordered 2 orders of the Cold Sichuan Noodles, one order of the Sesame Noodles, Â one order of Beef Lo Mein for the Children, 1 Cold Sichuan Rabbit, 1 Cold Pork Belly with Garlic, 2 Orders of Chicken Wings, 2 Orders of Pan Fried Dumplings, 1 order of spicy cucumber. They had a Korean Batter to them and then tossed with Chinese peppers. Â  Miss A ordered the next round of food.. .She ordered the cumin lamb, dry pepper style chicken, the three cup chicken. some sliced fish and cabbage, some more lo mein, chinese broccoli, kung pao and string beans with pork.. Â The cumin lamb too sweet, the kung pao again suffered the same fate.. It was almost like they were all the same dish with slightly changes besides the forward sweetness.. Â I also didn't really enjoy the string beans.. Chinese Broccoli was good. Â  The dried pepper chicken was good too, however, it seemed incredibly bland when faced off against the intensely sweet options on the table. Â  I would have been happy if the meal ended at appetizers. Â  Service was on point.. Friendly, the left pitchers of water, refilled tea, brought forks and soy sauce for people, filled extra rice, cleared plates in between cold and hot offerings.. Dinner with tip worked out to 35 an adult.. I feel like this place is a good mix of sichuan dishes and food court dishes to make everyone happy. Â  If I go back, I would have no problem finding things to enjoy. Â I would definitely order those wings again.

Â We ordered the kangaroo tacos (yum) and the lamb lollies which we've decreed are the BEST lamb chops in Astoria, the land of many Greek people. Â This is saying something since you really cannot go anyplace in Astoria that does not pride itself on its lamb offerings. Â The lollies also came with a divine arugula salad with pomegranate seeds and a light vinaigrette which could have been a stand alone dish. Â  I decided that I didn't want to commit to a full kangaroo filet and had the salmon which was sublime, along with a kind of sweet potato mash unlike any I've had before. Â Andrew did commit to the kangaroo and, while it was cooked perfectly, he thought it was a touch gamey. Â We also ordered the beet slaw which was tasty, but to my mind, could have had a touch more vinegar to give it a tangy bite. Â If those are the only two critiques of the Koala.... When leaving, Christina, the manager, came over and apologized for not coming over sooner, and kindly gave us a 10% off coupon for our return visit, which is definitely around the pike. Â  Last...Yay! Coopers Ale in Astoria! Â Yes, I was thirsty!

My fav Banh Mi place--ever! I've eaten Banh Mi all over the place in NYC and Canada and I always come back to this place. The ingredients are fresh, the bread is crusty, and the price is CHEAP. You really can't go wrong with this. I just wouldnt carry this onto the train because it is pretty garlicky and you may get jumped. I have one complaint though. I went to their new location today. I was a tad disappointed at how little of the cripsy pork bits they put into the sandwich. The last time I had it was a while ago so I will have to agree with some of the other posters that the quality may have gone down slightly. I would rather that they raised the price a little than to start skimping on the ingredients. I paid $3.75 for the sandwich and I would have gladly paid $4.50 if there was more pork!

This place has excellent authentic Mexican food (not that Spanish Harlem doesn't), but for a whole-in-the-wall place it's amazingly good. The tacos or quesadillas chicas with Oaxacan cheese is a favourite. Take-away always seems quicker than dining in, and no delivery.

This place is like Milo Ventimiglia's abs in season 1 of Heroes - if you don't know what you're looking for, you're going to miss it. Tiny, cute little falafel place snuggled deep in the heart of Chelsea, from afar it looks like just another brown stone, but you'd be a big fat loser not to check it out - ESPECIALLY now that I have told you about it. Falafel wraps, salads, pittas etc with hummus, and then a delicious smoothie selection (recommendation - get with coconut milk - urgh heaven). You can walk away with a hearty, healthy meal to go, as guilt free as belting out a couple of verses of R.E.S.P.E.C.T in a sound proof shower. Lovely.
I feel as though there's nothing more to be said other than the seats at the counter are the best seats there....hands down.

Having not called in for years, we were quite excited to go back and visit one of the saucy 'grande dames' of Downtown Manhattan. I confess to being left a bit disappointed. The decor hasn't changed and it still feels comfortably close to a real Parisian brasserie; the service and the food were average; we are always on the lookout for good steak tartare, and this one was dry; the chicken was indifferent; the wine list, on the other hand, is extensive and interesting; some tables were quite noisy; I am afraid that this place has lost most of its attraction whilst maintaining high prices. I am waiting impatiently for Pastis to re-open.

My friend used to work as a cook here and told me of the high quality products they produce, so me and a buddy went to check it out. I found the overall experience cute, but hardly top-notch. Everything about the place is new age hipster, from the staff right down to the way you order. The interior decor felt very family style/cafeteria. There were several 2 seat tables surrounding a large 12-16 seat table in the center. The decor was pretty chic, but the wall behind the bar was lavish while the opposite felt out of place. It was just solid color paint with old pictures hanging on it. The way you order your food was even more new age. You don't even tell the server what you want, you write on the laminated menu with a dry-erase marker and hand it to them. I was a fan of the gimmick. It makes sense for a place that sells only a handful of plates, but each with a large range of customization. It must expedite the process of ordering and decrease errors. The food was simply alright according to my tastes. The meatballs were very much Italian in style. They were very heavy on the spice, almost its detriment. I had the chicken meatballs with mushroom gravy atop rigatoni. The sauce with the rigatoni was awesome, albeit scarce. I would have liked more in my order, however there were 4 meatballs. You may dismiss 4 meatballs as petty, but I assure you these meatballs are quite large (I'd say 30% larger than a golf ball). After 4 meatballs and a tiny amount of sauce and pasta, I was stuffed. Overall, I was not much impressed by The Meatball Shop. It was just "OK". Those meatballs really need to be eased off spice.

I had their Green Papaya Salad and Ratchaburi Crab & Pork Dry Noodles for a take-out dinner recently. The papaya salad was lovely. Strands of crunchy green papaya swimming in a pleasantly funky-sour-spicy-sweet dressing, with a hefty sprinkle of dried shrimp, grape tomatoes and long beans. It was deceptively spicy and I was quite surprised since most Thai places I've eaten at are sissies when it comes to spicy food. Â It hurt, but it was good kind of pain :D The noodles themselves in the Crab & Pork dish were outstanding - springy, tender egg noodles! I was perched right in front of the counter where they prepare the noodle dishes and watched as the woman swirled a bunch of noodles in hot water to heat them up; then she plucked them out of the water and, while still hot, tossed the noodles with what appeared to be: sugar, MYSTERIOUS SEASONING, and sesame oil. Â I understand why they were served dry now - I could eat bowls and bowls of those noodles, because they were dressed sooooo perfectly. Delicately eggy, sweet, and savory! They were stingy with the crab meat however. $10 a bowl should've garnered more than a itty spoonful of shredded crab! The roast pork was nothing to write home about, a rather dry, lean version of Chinese Char-Sui.

We had a 2:30pm reservation for brunch on a Sunday in late January. Â We were seated promptly. Â After that that was the only thing that occurred promptly. Â  While the food was phenomenal, particularly the suckling pig ragu and the bombolotti all'Amatriciana (Spicy Tomato & Guanciale)--the service was seriously lacking. We asked for the wine list and then waited 20 minutes for the list to arrive. Â We ordered, and then waited another 20 minutes for our drinks to be served. Â We also ordered some pastries and they too took over twenty minutes to be served. Â  Our entries arrived another 20 minutes later. It was over 40 minutes after we were seated, that our drinks and pastries were served and an hour before our main dishes were served. Â Fortunately the crowd in the restaurant started thinning and Â our coffee and dessert arrived in a reasonable amount of time. Â In trying to give a little slack to the wait staff, the restaurant was packed when we arrived and it was near the end of the shift for them. Â But in end, there is no excuse, the.service was egregious In summary, food was a 5 star, and service was, at best, a one star, thus my 3 star rating. The waiter realized how bad the service had been during our meal and offered an unsolicited Â apology at the end of our brunch, but unfortunately that could not make up for what happened during the course of our meal. .

I love this place... but only when I'm really drunk or haven't eaten for a day or two.... namely bc its so rich. The sicilian and artichoke are my favorite... it's definitly worth the wait (theres ususally a line) The only down side is probably the calories you ingest with one slice... but it's soooo worth it. I promise!

The service was horrible. We were seated for 10 minutes before the waiter came by with the menu and water. They gave us such an attitude when we wanted to share the crepe. This place is cash only. I will probably not come here again.

I am a big fan of simple menus that offer the option to combine ingredients in complex ways. Â Burritos, tacos, quesadillas, platos and chips -- how much more simple can it be? Â But can I have a crispy (not soft) taco, with pinto (not black) beans, minus the guacamole, light on the rice, heavy on the cheese and salsa, plus the hot sauce? Dos Toros is conveniently located close to the Union Square subway station. Â Seating is at a premium in this hipster-friendly joint where the NYU crowd rules--the same crowd that one sees in the long and winding lines at Trader Joe's. Â The line at Dos Toros moves at a snail's pace though--that's the price to pay for the underlying complexity. Â Service is friendly even if a little hurried. I find the food to be tastier, and the ingredients more healthful, than at Chipotle's or Qdoba. Â Everything with the exception of the guacamole tasted fresh. Â That said, this simply cannot compare equal to 'California Mexican', that defies definition even after my recent trip to California.

This is my go-to neighborhood tapas spot. Â Very cute decor, cool menu, not too hard to grab a reservation. Â I adore the goat cheese and honey, the brussel sprouts and this sashimi type dish they have. Â You need to know, though, that I don't eat red meat, and this may be why I like this place. Â Unlike other tapas restaurants, there are options for people like me. Â So this probably isn't the place for "authentic" Spanish fare. Â They also don't take credit cards, so that's a little annoying. Â The acoustics are such that the place gets quite loud, so maybe not the best first date spot if talking to your date is important to you. Â Over all, though, I think it's tasty and cute, definitely worth a drop in for a more casual dinner.

I was meeting up with a friend who lives in NYC and is vegan, and she suggested this place for breakfast. Â I'm not vegan or vegetarian but was open to trying Champs since we don't have many vegan restaurants in Hawaii. Â I'm glad my friend brought me here. Â Everything was so delicious! Loved the pancakes, soysage, and tempeh bacon thing...although everything was vegan, it tasted just like the real thing except less oily. Â The baked goods looked yummy but I was too full to order anything else. Â I would definitely return here the next time I visit NYC. Â Laid-back atmosphere, healthy food, and friendly staff makes Champs a solid choice if you are ever in the mood for a nutritious breakfast.

I see what they're trying to do but it's not working, at least not for me. Â This tiny (I mean, really tiny) tapas restaurant has some good things going for it. Â Good ingredients, authentic intentions but it is way overpriced and the plates vary in size so much that it's impossible to gauge how much to order. Â I ordered three dishes and it was too much. Â I ordered the huge order of bacalau croquettes which were delish, however, drowning in mayo. Â I also ordered the pork belly which was essentially three chunks of pork fat on top of some vinegary salad. - there was only fat - no meat anywhere on the plate, which, for $15, I found really disappointing. Â The skirt steak was overwhelmed with more vinegary onions and some roasted pepper salsa. Â My girlfriend ordered the fried sardines (these were excellent), the foie gras (superb) and the cod cheeks (microscopic) Â and I shared a $19 glass of wine. Â I left unimpressed and $140 poorer.

The food is good. But I wanted more food! The menu is short and sweet. I love a small menu because I hate going to a restaurant and not being able to pick what you want especially when you are hungry. My gf and I had the platter. She had the lamb, salad, and fried cauliflower. She liked it but mentioned she wouldn't travel all the way to metropolitan ave for Wafa's. She said the lamb was cooked perfectly. The down side was...too little food. I had the chicken schawarma, fried cauliflower, and the baba ganoush. It was yummy. Despite the portions, we were both excited to try another dish. Unfortunately, it was the spinach pie. I am a big fan of spinach pie and Wafa's version did not do me justice. It was tiny (thank god it was, because I don't think I would have attempted to finish it). I'm not sure why there was a strong flavor of onion and herbs. It was overwhelming from the usual spinach pie I get. I wouldn't recommend it.

Sotto 13 is on a quiet part of 13th Street. Â  Nice ambience both in front (casual) and in back (sit down dining). Â  Â The food was actually quite good, especially the pizzas, and the service was better than average. My low rating here is solely due to a billing error that the restaurant has not corrected despite two calls to their manager, Giuseppe, in the last month. Â  I had dinner there with two friends on December 18, 2013 and I have yet to gain resolution for a mistake on the bill. Â  My portion of the bill was $45, for which I tipped 20% ot $9, for a total bill of $54 for me. Â  However, my Amex was charged $93. Â  Â Sotto 13's manager, despite two calls with him within a week of dining there, has not credited me back the amount due. Sadly, if it were not for the billing dispute, I would rate this as a pretty good place in the West Village. Â  Â Given the lack of resolution for my bill, I will not be going back there again.

There are no words to describe the pleasure that is Ippudo NY. Ordered the Akamaru Ramen... It was unbelievably divine. If I could pick one meal to have in NYC, it would be here at Ippudo NY. I wish I could try everything on their menu. I also ordered the Hirata Buns, which was also amazing. Mmmm. Luckily, my friends and I didn't have to wait that long. Only 20 minutes for a large table and it was more than worth it.

a great stop over if youre in brooklyn. the place is minimal. but the pizza and the people make up for it. the pizza is always just coming out of the oven, since there's such a huge turnover with so many people ordering. one way to guarantee you get your slice faster then some, ask for a topping, dominic puts it on a slice while the pie's still baking, so when it comes out you don't have to wonder if you'll be the lucky few who'll get a slice or have to wait for a new pie. the best topping is extra cheese, fresh mozzarella pieces put right on the slice.
Everything we tried was delicious. Â Nuestra Paella & Pollo Al Carbon Y Vinagre Forum were both great. Â Romantic restaurant with tons of fresh flowers everywhere! Â It was beautifully decorated.

So I was in NYC for a friend's birthday. He and 5 mates had come over from London to check out the Big Apple, although I had warned them that New York in July might not be the best time! We spent time in Williams burg exploring and we ended up drinking and hanging out at the Lucky Dog Bar on Bedford. Â After mentioning to some folks we were going to try Pies 'N' Thighs, the locals all raved about it. My friends, the Brits, said good soul food was non existent in London, so we were excited and hungry. Â  We walked to the small looking store front and when we entered, the site of the home baked pies was enough for me, but it was very warm in the small eating area. The host said since we were such a larger group we could sit in the back. We were lead to what felt like a basement garage, which in the summer heat felt nice, cool, and a touch damp...much more comfortable. Â  We order a bottle of red (my friends are definitely wine folks.) and checked out the wonder of the menu. I had to describe some of the items, since they didn't know what collard greens or hush puppies were. They were also curious about catfish. I really wanted fried chicken and waffles, but the BBQ pork ribs won me over. One of my friends got the chicken plate and we said we would share. The wine arrived, and we tasted it but it had been corked. We told the waiter and he immediately apologized and got us a new bottle of a grenache, which was very good. Â  The portions are good sized. I had BBQ pork ribs with cornbread, a pickled vegetable salad and grilled corn on the cob with cotija cheese, and I also ordered hush puppies for the table. My friends had pulled pork sandwich, another had fried chicken, and we ordered collard greens to share. The ribs feel off the bone, very tasty. The corn on the cob was sweet and just enough seasoning. The fried chicken was fantastic. Juicy and crunchy but not greasy. My only complaint was I tried a biscuit from one of my friend's chicken dish and it was a little dense, not light and fluffy...it actually seemed like it might have been around for a while. It was just ok, not bad, but as a baker I think it could have been better. We didn't get dessert, way too stuffed! Also would like to go back and try the mac and cheese, and the chicken and waffles! Â  The service was very good, the waiter was attentive and around when we had a question or concern. I can't wait to get back to NYC and to Brooklyn to eat here again!

This small but cozy wine bar is a welcome addition to Hell's Kitchen. Great atmosphere/staff and the food is good but could still be improved. I'm a fan and rooting for them! -Narrow, cozy, dimly lit room with few tables and a small bar -Friendly, helpful, likable staff -Nice, affordable wine selection -Food was all good but several dishes could use a little improvement. Keep experimenting! -Crab bolognese was a creatively flavored dish Â (presentation could use a update though) Suggestions/Critique: -The crab bolognese has great flavor (mint? or something is a nice touch) but the presentation needs work. Too beige... get some color in there -Beet salad would improve with more thinly sliced beets and better cheese -Last time I went there was a 20 minute wait and when I asked to put my name down was told you don't take names. Maybe you don't want to worry about taking phone numbers or tell people to stay close by but it's a little weird to be told "we don't take names." All in all I'm a fan and will be back but hope they can make some tweaks to join Adesia and Caselula as a premier Hell's Kitchen wine bar.

Sure, I'd love to be one of the (over) 400 people to review Cafeteria -- really, how often do you get to write "excellent meatloaf" in a review without also mentioning someone's mother or grandmother? Â Our table had the chicken & waffles, cobb salad and meatloaf with mashed potatoes -- served quickly, by a lovely and handsome human being and without any attitude (which seems to come up in other reviews -- I didn't see it). Â I think I would enjoy eating here much more at 4am rather than on a busy Sunday night, even with immediate seating -- way too loud to enjoy the company of the people I was visiting. Â They were also out of almost every beer choice -- our server said "Sundays are always bad" -- okay, but if that's the case, plan ahead, have the beer. Â Regardless, we'll be back the next time we're in town.

My wife and I went here this past Saturday night, after watching the space develop over the last year as we live very close by. We loved Trading Post though it was not very crowded, it being a weekend in FiDi and the first week Trading Post was open. It is a gorgeous bar with a very warm atmosphere given the dark wood and great lighting and good music. The dinner was quite good and we even had a couple great bourbons in the whiskey bar downstairs. A great addition to the neighborhood!
Good Korean food for the fraction of the cost. Doesn't get any better than that! It gets really busy around lunch time, but the line does move really fast.

I can understand the long wait, but I'm not quite sure I myself would do it. Don't get me wrong, I thought the cuban sandwich was delicious and certainly worth a re-order on a return trip. It's meaty, salty, tasty, filling. Everything you want out of a sandwich. The moscow mule was refreshing and delicious, as well. It's worthy of 4 stars on food alone. But, the space is way too cozy for comfort (as in patrons are packed in like sardines) and it gets ridiculously warm since there's no A/C. Servers walk around like bumper cars and can't get you out of there fast enough to keep up with the line outside. I mean, the restaurant itself has it's own charm to it, with almost kitschy decor. But it's certainly not a relaxing meal by any means. If by chance it's empty on off-hours, it's worth a stop for the cuban sandwich and a drink.

Decent service, fairly quick seating, food was cold when it came out and the chai latte was more tea than latte. Was expecting better everything with the 4 stars and over 300 reviews. Food wasn't too bad but not the best either.
Great for brunch.
Brussel sprouts, squid ink paella, wine, fire place....that's all you need to know!

to my surprise, this place absolutely lived up to the hype. Â i would consider junior's a MUST-EAT when visiting the city. the 'original new york cheesecake' was the best i ever had. Â so much thicker, denser, more wonderful than other cheesecakes. Â we did the little take out booth, not the restaurant. Â service was incredibly quick. Â i also grabbed a snicker cookie on my way out- it was so heavy, so soft, so chocolaty! Â roll the dice and try something else if you want to- but i can confidently vouch for the original cheesecake and snicker cookie.

What a great find. We were walking to our hotel when my husband spotted this gem. It's a complete hole in the wall, but it was crowded. Must be good, right? RIGHT. We went for breakfast the next morning. They know their regulars by name, deliver to local businesses, and have GREAT FOOD. Plus, it's a father/son combo running the place. You can't go wrong. Great diner good, great prices, and excellent service. We wanted to go back 1 more time but didn't have a chance to! We love Johny's!
Fresh, flavorful and delicious. The place was super cute and everything was so great. Â The short ribs were really amazing, so rich and the portion was large.

unlimited sangria bar?! umm.. that's an automatic 5 stars in my book. I loved my experience here, even tho we got here when the kitchen was about to be closed and we were only able to get 2 sangrias in. Their brunch is decent and with the unlimited sangria it was perfect. Did I mention there's unlimited sangria with every meal? They don't take reservations so get here early! Then you can get back in line as many times as you want to try each and every one of their 5-10 flavors of sangria (I kept losing count of how many flavors there were with every giggle causing sip I had of the yummy liquid stuff). Granted only two of the sangrias were legitimately flavored and the rest were fruity juices, regardless they were all delicious

If you work anywhere near Soho this amazing restaurant MUST become part of your lunch rotation. Â Why? 1. It's delicious and healthy! Â A different spin on salads and sandwiches. 2. There is crack in the salad dressing. 3. The owner, cooks and waitstaff are warm, friendly, gracious and talented. 4. If you like pulled pork (and I do!!) you will dream about the pulled pork sandwich.

Looking for waffles and wanting to go skating at bryant park, this popped up in yelp. CONS FIRST One. Hour. Wait. at 11 am Saturday. for a party of 2. ugh Food takes a while to come out when packed Not the cheapest option, but hey! NYC! Pros! Nice decor, nice place, nice servers, good service! Good food! We had chicken and cheddar waffles, a custom made omelet, bacon and the best of all this AMAZING green tea lime thing that was just delicious. ( The name escapes me, i have it somewhere. i know i could probably buy it online, but its here that we found out what it was!) Good portions! (I mean, you pay for it... but at some places its measly) Chicken was good. Juicy, tasty, overall was just awesome. Waffles were ok too! I liked the cheddar. They had a tabasco honey maple syrup which I was not the biggest fan of... i should of just asked for regular maple syrup. Maybe if you like tabasco you'll like it, I dont. Omelette was really good, this bread with apple butter that came with it was delicious too. They seem to rotate specials. I wish i could try them all alas my budget is not infinite. Overall great place for brunch... just be prepared for the wait!

Pio Pio is one of my top fave restaurants. Fantastic mixed drinks, well seasoned food and giant portions to share with tu amigos y familia (friends and family;) I was introduced to this wonderful chain in 2008 at the Queens location and was love at first bite. Imagine my excitement when I learned that there was a gorgeous location not far from me in Manhattan! I had my birthday dinner here a year ago which was a big hit with everyone there. This is a perfect choice provided the people you hang out with love food! Matador Combo and Arroz con Mariscos are crowd pleasers. These 2 dishes + sangria, tostones and avocado salad all lead to a happy tummies and lots of laughs with friends. Most of the tables here are designed for big crowds so I highly recommend it for a ravenous bunch. The place could be noisy so I do not recommend for the early dates. The bar section isn't a bad choice for quick drinks and smaller feast. Decor is beautiful, modern and clean. Service is always on point and never experienced any rude employees or long wait time for food. Pio Pio is defintely doing it right!
I set up an account to give this restaurant 5 star. Amazing price and taste made me feel like at home. I'm sure I will come back tomorrow despite of waiting.

We met friends here on a sunny Sunday afternoon, seated at the bar our friends had the hamburgers which they said was huge and really good. Â We only had drinks but their Bloody Marys are made with great care, using fresh grated horseradish, classy and bang on. Â The atmosphere is bustling and it's the kinda place where it is really easy to interact with fellow diners. Â We were seated at the bar, getting a table seems to be a waiting game so, if your like me and enjoy eating at the bar, this may be how to try it, beware however as they serve a limited menu for bar customers. Â The decor is great and you have lots to keep the eye busy, service is friendly prices are moderately expensive but well worth the atmosphere and the portions are big.

This is a place you only need to try once. I made the mistake of going twice. My first visit to Jimmy's Diner I ordered chicken and waffles which was ok but I stuffed myself silly and felt guilty the rest of the day. That's my fault because I have a disorder where I have to eat everything that's in front of my face. Â If I'm hankering for some fried chicken for brunch, I'm better off going to Peels in the East Village and nooshing on the fried chicken biscuit, which is the perfect portion. But then again, Jimmy's is a diner and for diner fare, it does ok. My second visit to Jimmy's Diner the service was deplorable. I ordered the Elvis waffles, which again, was a portion too big for one person. You would think I would have learned my lesson from my first Jimmy's visit but alas, I ate myself silly again. It wasn't mind blowingly delicious; It was just in front of me and I was bored. Definitely go during a weekday when there aren't any crowds or wait time.

Do or Dine has some delectable options...granted they ever make it to your table. The one time I decided to eat at a table rather than at the bar, my partner and I ordered three things: the lamb (usually delicious) the duck and the vegan appetizer. The lamb arrived first, quickly and lukewarm. Mostly fat. Whatever. We let it slide. And then, then we waited forty minutes. The server hid meekly near the service window. The vegan appetizer was piping hot, super tasty kale and cashew (?) cream situation but the duck entree right after it arrived cold and tough. To top off our long, mediocre dinner, the server offered us a free dessert: a frozen snickers bar she admitted could be bought at any corner store. Wow. You guys are killing it.

The price is as good as it gets in this are for lunch, and the cilantro ginger sauce is delicious. I made this place my lunch mainstay until I had one not so good chicken buckwheat noodle salad, but I would still come back here. The steak plate is also great, although slightly chewy. What I like least off the menu are the wonton and noodle soups - they taste sorta gamey. Better off taking the walk to Chinatown for authentic wonton noodle soup.

I am giving this 5 stars based on the Red White and blue alone. I've had other food there and it was alright, usually very fresh -- but all of it's a footnote for the fact that you can get 6 oysters and an alcoholic beverage for $8. That's cheaper than doing it yourself. I tell everybody about this place.
Love this place! It has a buffet bar! Can't beat that. Also, who can complain about a place with abundant and cheap korean food?

Ate here for the first time today and had the Carne Asada and Pollo Asado tacos. These tacos are super authentic! Â I was transported straight back to Mexico with that first bite. Super fresh, handmade tortillas and made to order just the way you like it. Definitely my new fave spot in Chelsea Market.
Tiny, but great date spot. Â Typical cute wine bar with a very warm and friendly vibe. Â It can get crowed since it's small, so be sure to go on an off time/day to get a table. Â Great wines/cheeses.

Glad we found this restaurant. Unique dÃ©cor is comfortable, eclectic and elegant. Wait staff friendly and attentive. Food original and delicious. Fried brussel sprouts were incredible. Rockfish in artichoke broth was wonderful. Can't wait to return.
I really love this place - the food is amazing and the people are lovely. Â Definitely try.

I stopped into this bristling little bistro on a whim, the pristine minimalist decor inside giving off an almost infectious warmth. Sat at the bar for a beer and hors d'oeuvre (the deviled eggs are fantastic! whipped light and airy with a rich profile of pickled accoutrements), and was pleasantly surprised by the amount of attention I received from the waitstaff who were clearly busy with the other tables at full. Oftentimes in a situation such as this I find it easy for a single patron to get lost in the hustle and bustle of larger parties and good-looking table dates, but in no time at all was checked on by the pleasantly outgoing bartender. They had a small but lively list of wines and beers on draught, reasonably priced, and a unique menu of plates I'm looking forward to going back and trying, especially the fish curry and beef rendang, both of which I almost snatched off a tray exiting the kitchen. All in all a pleasant experience I am looking forward to repeating. Next time I plan on bringing friends!

Sex is like pizza. When it's good, it's really good. When it's bad, it's still pretty good. I like pizza. I really like Di Fara pizza. It's definitely some of the best pizza I've ever had. But, at the end of the day, it's dough, sauce, and cheese. I, thankfully, had access to a car so was able to avoid the long subway ride, and, encountered no wait when I arrived around 7 PM on Â Sunday. From the other reviews, it seems like no wait is a rarity so maybe Sunday night is a safe bet. Di Fara may be a quintessential NY pizza pilgrimage. Fresh pizza hand rolled by an Italian man and his sons. Pay attention to the hours of operation, though-it closes early!

I have been coming here for the past few years and every time my experience has been great but recently I was very disappointed in the service. Â After my sister and I placed our order, the waitress tells us 25 minutes later that neither of our entrees were available. So I decided on another entree and ten minutes later the waitress brings only my side orders (salad & avocado). The waitress then disappeared for some which I became really annoyed, subsequently the owner saw that I was visibly upset and apologized on behalf of the waitress which comes to find out left for the night. Since the waitress didn't relate to the cook my complete order, the owner Â offered to give me anything I wanted on the house but after sitting there starving for an hour, my sister and I decided to leave. In addition, the staff appeared unorganized and the establishment gets smaller and smaller. I won't be coming back here anymore.

This restaurant is located on the second level of the Setai hotel. Â You ascend to the second level by walking up a long staircase and walk into the bar area. The bar area has a longish bar directly in front of the entrance and a few tables and sitting areas. Â The bar is attractive and exudes a calming feel. Â We waited in the bar for the rest of our group to show up. Â The dining room is large and open and windows abound. Â Tables are spaced far enough apart that you aren't required to be (an unwilling) participant in other tables' conversations. The food is Italian-inspired, but utilizes what I think are fresh ingredients that are combined in interesting flavorful ways. Â There is a tasting menu that allows the diner to select any item on the menu for an appetizer, main course and dessert. Â The portions were not large, but, the tasting menu appeared to afford value. Â  The olive oil "pound" cake was an outstanding dessert. Â The beef cheeks were very good and offered a lot of flavor. The wine list is extensive. We enjoyed a Chateauneuf du Pape and a Brunello. Â  Service was efficient (though there seemed to be somewhat of a lag between ordering the dessert and the time the dessert arrived).

Food is great, 85% of the staff too. Â The hour and a half wait for a table that happens occasionally and the other 15% of the staff... not so good. Â Tiki disco party every other Sunday in the summer... 10 stars!

The ambiance was great. Live jazz band over brunch? Who wouldn't enjoy that? Ordered the salmon omelette with potatoes and a fruit bowl on the side. Big thumbs up!! I would definitely come back here again!

The people who own, work at, and run this restaurant all seem super nice, and they are obviously putting a huge effort into putting an original, and may I say healthy, spin on Mexican food, in an upscale, Carroll Gardens-y sort of way. Â  However, I personally prefer $2.50 tacos in Sunset Park with a bowl of chips and guacamole, and no part of me really craves upscale Mexican food with a twist. Â However, if this is your thing, then you will dig this place.

Great wine bar in the sea of nothingness that is Midtown-East. Â Had a double date here and had the crudo pizza, cheese pizza, olives, meatballs and focaccia. Â Nice selection of wine as you would expect. Â Nice intimate spot perfect for couples or a double date scenario.

The ciabatta, sweet chili sauce, and medium rare beef is what makes the Bronte Burger so perfect. Best meal I've had in a long time! The sauce adds sweetness but doesn't overpower it to make it taste like a Thai Asian sauce dish. The ciabatta is hearty and so much better than a typical burger bun. The cheese is melted really well and the tomato is a fresh bite. The pumpkin salad plus chicken was so delicious as well. A simple vinaigrette, crisp spinach, creamy goat cheese, and soft pumpkin. 1 burger + 1 salad was a lot of food for the two of us. Definitely coming back to try the pastas and Australian drinks!

The best way I can describe this place is that the food does not match the dÃ©cor or location. Â It is located all the way at what seems to be the end of the island and the dÃ©cor was a blend of a tacky Applebee's and a grandmothers house. Â The food however was great. Â I absolutely love southern food to begin with but I was beyond pleased with the quality of the food. Â The portions are also huge. Â By far the most memorable thing I had there was the Hurricane Nachos. Â It truly was a perfect storm of chips and meats.

The food is great. However the service is horrible we are sitting here for an hour and we are getting one plate every 10 minutes. Not only did the waitress get the order wrong but now she is giving us an attitude for asking for our correct order. Time to look for a New Mexican restaurant.

Our best find this year. A low key lovely dining room to wile away the hours nibbling at delicacies of Iberia. With Spanish beers in the cooler and a whole wine store next door, you can complement your croquetas with uncommon cervezas and vinos.
Great soup dumplings and cumin lamb... Very happy this place opened in the area with the recent decline in quality at Grand Sichuan

friday night, no reservation, waited for 10 mins for a table, the waitress was really nice got to try their thai iced tea, came up in a super cute jar, very refreshing~~ we tried their noodle soup, flat noodle, and dry noodles with duck. everything was tasty, except the dry noodles are super sweet, don't like it. also tried papaya salad with raw crab, the raw crab made the whole dish fishy...i should have thought about it, but gave it a try since i heard wonderful things from wondee siam's same dish. well, not gonna order again here, maybe still will give wondee siam's a try~~ in a word, nice cute thai restaurant, authentic place, reasonable price ( portion is a little bit small, i finished my dish in no time~~ scared my friend...).

They couldn't even get a basic Turkey Club right. The turkey was way too "rare" and there was there was Serviced with a handful of oil-soggy tasteless chip. Our waistress was at the bar doing shots with the other staff members. When she did come to our table, the music was too loud for her to hear us. Comical, in hindsight, I guess. I won't be back.

I ordered the roast pork and roast duck rice dish, and a side of seasonal vegetable green in oyster sauce. Â Such a simple and nutritious dinner - Â I thoroughly enjoyed it. Service was good too. Will definitely be back in the future.

Casa Mono is the kind of place where you want to keep going back until you've tried everything on the menu. Decorwise, it's so cute. Â Dark wood, smaller and intimate with an open kitchen and optional sushi bar style seating that puts you right where the cooking action is. Â  I love the food here. Â Hudson Valley Pork Croquettes (a little taste of heaven), razor clams, Charcuterie de la casa, Â  mussels, skirt steak and gamba w/black rice....all my favs so far. Â  Good but not amazzzing...pan tomate, ensalada mono..each as uninspiring as the name, calamares fritos decent but not $15 worth. The great thing about Casa Mono is that dish feels like a thrilling discovery..... good or bad. Â I had no idea this was a Batali restaurant until I had raved about it to friends.

Chef owned restaurant with a creative menu served with class. We went for lunch after opting out of our regular first day in NYC lunch spot due to UN week craziness. Very knowledgeable waitstaff as to the menu and wine list. Was so impressed we bought our recently relocated friend from Luxembourg a restaurant gift certificate for her birthday. This place will be part of our dinner rotation along with the Modern and Le Bernardin in our twice yearly trips to NYC.

My mom's new fave noodle place has enchanted me. I've been here three times already and have to say they make some of the best steamed rice noodles with special sauce. One order with tea makes a meal. Come with a group, order that as an appetizer(or order two) and then some noodles. On one day, Â I had the seafood noodle dish, mom had some dumpling soup and my sister had the chicken rice casserole--more expensive but large enough to share with two more people. The food here is tasty and supposedly, the food has no msg.It's also cleaner than many of Chinatown's noodle shops. Just a note for vegetarians...the shrimp dumpling have meat mixed in them, so buyer beware. It's Chinatown, and usually seafood dumplings are mixed with meat.

Stumbled upon this place while looking around 5th ave to get lunch with a friend on a Friday afternoon. The bartender had us sit at the table by the window, and with the door open it provided just the right amount of outdoor vibe without actually being outdoors. He was also very attentive to get our order in. My friend and I split the original "fried" burger as well as the apple-raisin potato latkes. Both were very hearty and delicious. The burger was extremely juicy (and this is coming from someone who opts to never use the word "juicy," but in this case it's necessary) and the fried crispy outside was a great alternative to the typical burger bun. We also felt obligated to accompany the meal with some beers... I went with the Palm Amber Ale, which I thought went nicely with the rest of the food. (And it came in a huge mug that looked aesthetically pleasing.) All-in-all, great place! Food took a little while to come out, but it was well-worth the wait. I'll definitely be coming back here!

I've been about ten times and it's never disappointed. I had lunch here yesterday and it was delicious. The goat cheese salad and the butternut squash ravioli were superb. The servers have always been great and there's a decent bar too.

Loved this place but Yikes! the prices have gone up so much! Â I appreciate that they want to make money but what are they doing here??? Â This is cafe fare but that's all...nothing more. Â  Â I can go to Balthazar and pay $10.50 for onion soup or Â to Bergdorfs with a breathtaking view of the park for scallops less than the price of pasta here. Â Food is still good just a little pricey for this place (in my opinion).
I went there with 3 friends, and we ordered a hot pot. The hot pot is super big, which can serve more than 6 girls I guess. But the soup in the hot pot is not spicy enough. Generally, it's OK.

i've never been here before since my mom is the one who picks them up for me (my mommy is so good to me!!), but they are still fresh and yummy by the time i get home. my mom was born and raised in vietnam and she only buys her banh mi here. so that's saying something!"

A day in soho is not complete without at least a drink at Balthazar. Â  Always packed so prepare to stand if you want a drink, unless you we one of the lucky ones who finds a seat or two. Â The place is vibrant and service is of high quality. Â If you have time or want to eat... The food for brunch, lunch, and dinner are all fabulous, as well as a great and extensive raw bar. Â Tables are very booked so make a reservation! complaint: Rudest coat check girl I have ever met when we were there on Saturday this week.... She brought our stroller up... Which they requested I check... Totally fine... I had my daughter in my arms who was getting hungry and needed to be changed and the place is always packed so I had just a few things going on ... I planned on tipping her but I needed to get to a side so I could get situated... She followed me and then stood there annoyed as I tried get things in order and help my 5month old... She then rudely loudly stated "you know... We recommend at least one dollar tip for the check service".... Again, I planned on tipping as soon as I could get to. My purse but my priority was my daughter and this women was so rude... And then when I was waiting for a little old women to get up the stairs from the bathroom so I could walk down, she bumped me and cut me off and went down the stairs in front of me... I was obviously waiting to go down but had an. Â Infant in my arms so was waiting for the other women coming up the stairs since it is a narrow stairwell. She really was rude and if she had been a bigger part of my experience, I would not return based on horrible rudeness. Also, They have attendants in the bathroom. Â Normally this would be fine but the one in the ladies room, each time I have been there, is quite rude when I don't have a dollar to tip. Â I do not always take money to the bathroom, nor do I have cash often. Â I do appreciate the service but it makes me have an unwanted stress when I have to leave without tipping. Â Also, there are only three stalls so if you are alone, you are never alone alone :) and it is small enough that it feels like your being watched or listened to. Â I know that is weird but just a personal feeling.

They say the best way to get over an ex is to find someone new, and thankfully, my love affair with Sripraphai followed hot on the heels of my break-up with Pam Real Thai. Sure, the service leaves something to be desired and the decor looks like it was done by an interior designer with some sort of multiple personality disorder, but that's not the point. The point is the food and what delicious food it is! My absolute favorite dish at Sripraphai is the green curry with roasted duck. I always make sure to ask for it "Thai spicy" so that it's numb-my-mouth-and-make-me-sweat level of spicy. The duck is really tender and the pineapple adds a touch of sweet to balance out the spiciness of the curry. Completely SPOT ON. **FYI Sripraphai is closed Wednesdays. I learned that the hard way.

I went on friday night right after the big snowstorm, and the restaurant had a bunch of tables open, so that perplexed me at first. Â While waiting for our table we saw these small guanciale and parmesan rolls, so we ordered those as an addition to the wonderful foccacia on the table. Â We started with a prosciutto from Iowa which was great and quite peppery and wonderful bay scallops with a light clementine and chili dressing. Â Both were delicious. Â Our entrees were the spaghetti carbonara and the pasta with suckling pig and arugula. Â The carbonara was very peppery and creamy with some nice crisp guanciale. Â The pig in the other pasta was very tasty. Â For dessert we shared a wild berry pie that had a wonderful crust and tasty berries. Â The service was very attentive even though we were ticked back in a corner.

Love this place! Hubby and I got a single to share as a snack, and were even able to sit down inside. Tried 3 sauces- the Curry Especial, Sambal-Olek, and Dill Lemon Mayo. Love the dill mayo, and the curry. The sambal is just straight Sriracha sauce, but it's good to mix in with the others if you like things spicy. Love this little place.

Probably one of the best margherita pizzas I've had! There were so many pizzerias I wanted to try in New York but I knew I had to try "America's First Pizzeria" and it did not disappoint! I was worried about the wait, but the restaurant was actually pretty big so we were seated immediately. Margherita Pizza ($19.99): The two of us shared the 14" small pizza (3 big slices each) and it was the perfect amount for two hungry people. I enjoyed the thin crust, which was very crispy but not too burnt. I really liked the fact that it wasn't too greasy like a lot of thin crust pizzas I've had where the bottom would get soggy from the oil. The crust stayed perfectly crispy throughout the entire meal. The mozzarella cheese and basil were also very fresh and tasty. My favorite part of the pizza though has to be the delicious tomato sauce. Usually I don't really pay close attention to the sauce on pizzas, but this was so good!! I loved the fresh tomato taste with just the perfect amount of sweetness. OVERALL: Pizza was delicious. Service was great. And no wait?? I'm definitely coming back next time I visit!

This place is amazing! Â Love the location and the strange but fun decor. Â Its so unique and the food just fits. Â There is a great attention to detail here in the food and decor. Â I have recommended it to many people and its always been a hit. Â I don't know if they have dinner but I've only had brunch here. Â Highly recommend it.

I'll add to the cheer here. Â Was in The Village one night with a buddy, and we needed a new bar. Â My brother, who lives in LA, knows all the good bars in Manhattan and he recommended it. You'd never know there was a bar this far down on Perry Street, but keep walking and there it is. Â What a great place. The beer is very good - quite a selection, and at prices you would not believe (for good beer in Manhattan). It is crowded as folks here say, but that should not deter you. Â Check the place out - go early and get a table, or go late and stand. Â You won't be disappointed. I'll only give it 4 stars, though, since the crowd can be a pain sometimes - hard to get a drink, and to hear yourself think.

I never got to try any of their food, just because I am always getting their late, but it is a very nice place to go and grab a drink after work. The atmosphere there is always nice, and people very friendly. However, late at night this place get pretty crowded and loud. Â I would recommend going there between 9 and 11.

Wow I'm in the middle of eating the Catalan sandwich and its so good I had to make sure I Yelped this place before I forget. The staff was very friendly and helpful and its actually decently priced for what you get. The bread is a great mix of chewy/crunchy and the ingredients are very flavorful. I'll have to start coming in here more often for my lunchbreak.

I'm so torn about this place, because while the food is really good, my friend and I had a really bad experience with a rude-as-McEnroe waiter during dinner a few weeks back. We get there at about 5:30 for an early dinner, and we're the only people in the restaurant. My friend brings a half bottle of wine from home because it's BYOB. She orders an 8 dollar salad, I order 15 dollar chicken kebabs. The waiter snaps "You know you need to spend 15 dollars a person to drink your wine." We were kind of shocked. Nowhere on the menu did it mention that. We're the only people there, for goodness sake we only have half a bottle of wine, just let us drink it. We don't listen to him and just keep drinking it. He left us alone after that, but we couldn't believe how rude he was. The food got to our table pretty quickly, and it was delicious. We were venting as we savored the perfect yogurt sauce on my place (she kept dipping bread into it) about how we wanted to hate this place because of the rude waiter, but the food was too good for us to hate it. So, I guess make sure to spend at least fifteen dollars a person if you want to split half a bottle of wine over dinner, and enjoy the food.
Freemans i s charming, warm and yummy! But its impossible to get into with out a reso - def a great place to bring friends for birthday or event of some kind, kinda pricy, but worth it!

Came with my family (party of 5 + 2 kids) on Saturday around 12:30PM and luckily got seated right away after some tetris-ing of moving another party that just arrived to another table by the super nice host/waiter/owner(?). We ordered a whole bunch of things - the crab spring rolls, crab chips, garlic-tomato fried rice, fish banh mi, short rib banh mi, bobo chicken, pork loin, and beef cubes and everything we had was really good. We also decided to try the tapioca dessert at the end, which I'm not a big fan of but the artichoke iced tea is really delicious and refreshing! This is definitely not your typical Brooklyn or Queens traditional Vietnamese restaurant so don't come here if you just want a bowl of pho. If you do want to try good food with a twist and really nice service, it's worth the trek. It wasn't until the end of our meal that we realized everyone was ordering the Banh Xeo so unfortunately we didn't get to try that but I will next time if I ever venture this far out again.

K and I walked down here after work (8pm) and there was a 10 min line outside of this small pizza joint. They serve beer but no place inside to drink it and no bathrooms for us to use so I didn't order any. We ordered 3 slices, artichoke & spinach, margarita and crab. Being Asian having crab/seafood on pizza is not too weird in fact I liked it! the crust was thin and crispy, very good. Margarita pizza was good not mind-blowing though. The artichoke pizza was like spinach dip on crusty bread, yumm! Very good and will surely be back for more. One complaint though is that I thought the crust was a bit too thick my taste but it isn't a deal breaker. Can't wait for my next visit! Enjoy!

My fave NYC pizza place. Perfectly crisp, thin crust pizza. Robust sauce. And tasty toppings. I love the atmosphere here too. It's laid back & fun. Decent bar. Even though the place is out of my way, I go the distance because I've yet to be disappointed with the quality of the pizza. The only area in which this place falls short is customer service as the staff is not very inviting, but I don't care. When I go here, I go for great pizza and beer with friends, not for small chit-chat with strangers.

Last time I went here, I remembered the breadsticks. They were very yummy and we couldn't get enough of it. There was this seasoning which went well with the riosottos. I'm definitely going back there and buy it and enjoy more riosotto. The last riosotto I had from here, had a plastic piece, and I took it out and continued eating. I just hope it has an A rating from the NYC Dept of Health.

Nice atmosphere, great coffee, and cordial efficient service. Â The steak sammie was delicious with the exception of the the arugula which was clearly old and rather limp. Â The fries were okay could have been crisper and seasoned. The tiramsu was fabulous. Â The prices are reasonable including those for the wines and specialty drinks. Â Looking forward to their dinner service which is to start in March.

If you are looking for a good sports bar with amazing food Manhattan Proper should be at the top of your list. I visit MP regularly and keep coming back for more. I don't think I have ever had better bar food. They mushroom truffle burger is probably top 3 out of anything I have ever eaten, and I personally do not like red meat with the exception of MP's burger! It is seriously so good. And their fries are also amazing. If you don't get the burger than definitely get the truffle fries, your mouth will explode. If you want to eat healthy they also have a really good salad, the pear and gorgonzola. But get it with chicken because it adds a lot more flavor. I seriously love this place; its decently priced, they always have specials on the food and drinks and its a good crowd!

It was our first night in NYC and I had heard so many things about Jr's on the Food Network that we decided to try it. Man was the place packed. Surprisingly, it didn't take long to get seated. I had been superstoked about trying this place for weeks prior to arriving in NY so I couldn't wait to dive in. I loved how they made BLT's out of various salad sandwiches including egg salad and tuna salad so I opted for the egg salad BLT and an order of their onion rings. The hubby went with the full rack of ribs, creamy coleslaw, and steak fries. We also decided to try some of their pickled beets and regular oil based slaw which was complimentary. Kinda strange that they chose those items to be complimentary but I will admit that the beets were very tasty (though I have had tasty pickled beets from a can). My meal was ok, the egg salad was kinda bland and the batter on the onion rings was a bit strange. They should have used beer batter rather than tempura batter as some of the onion rings batter tasty cakey rather than crispy. The hub said his ribs were decent, fries were ok, and the slaw was ok as well. However, he said there was nothing memorable about any of it and I agreed. I couldn't go to Jr's and not try what they are famous for: CHEESECAKE! So we opted for one of their best sellers, the devils food cheesecake. Out came a huge brick of cheesecake! While being good (how bad can chocolate cheesecake be?), it was very very rich and heavy so we didn't eat much of it. To be honest, it didn't knock our socks off like I thought it would. In the end, the meal was a bit overpriced, but that was just the beginning of what to expect for meal costs in NYC. Everything there in TimeSquare is overpriced for sure! While the service was good and I can't think of anything bad about this place other than the price, there was also nothing memorable about it which for an 80.00 price tag, I felt there should be!

It was such a relief to find this place in a sea of corporate blah. I had to stay in the area for work and was so happy that I didn't have to go very far to get good beer. Plus, in a hood where hotel bars are charging you $10 for a Heineken, these beers are a downright bargain. The food was also well priced for the neighborhood though not really special.

Enjoyed a late night dinner here with my brother after just arriving in NYC. Â It was 1am and the joint was quite busy with diners (not just drinkers) giving credence to the notion that this city never sleeps. Â Great pub atmosphere with exposed brick and a nice warm, charming feel. After slight sticker shock at the $17 price tag on the burger (this is NY after all) I proceeded to relax and enjoy the experience of America's first Gastropub. Â This was quite possibly the very best burger I have ever had and was nicely accompanied by shoestring fries that were just fantastic with their subtle taste of garlic & rosemary. Â All of this washed down with a properly poured pint of Guinness. Â The only drawback was the beer selection...I was expecting just a little more in this department as I was hoping to try an east coast craft brew that I'm unable to get my hands on in the Northwest where I am from. Overall I would highly recommend.
a little spicy

Gorgeous, colorful, veganized sushi rolls! Great concept, great execution = healthy AND delish! Small, bright space tucked away near union square, around three tables. The place could seat about 15 ppl. My friend and I have been wanting to try this place since it first opened and finally went last night. It's a small space tucked away near union square. The place has only three tables and could seat about 15 people. We shared the roll of the month (pumpkin/squash flavored), the mighty mushroom and the green machine. I really enjoyed the roll of the month - twas savory and slightly sweet. Mushroom roll was also great b/c it tasted strongly of mushrooms and I'm a big fan of the fungi. Best description for green roll was that it tasted really fresh and well, green. We also got the spicy shroom wrap, which I could've done without. The rice wrapper was chewy, so it was hard to take a bite. The flavors were bland and there was a vague sliminess to it - not sure if it was from the wrapper or the mushrooms. Overall, really happy with the food here and I'll def be back to try the other rolls. Minor complaint about sanitary conditions - there was a bug/fly constantly buzzing around our food while we ate, so that was annoying/distracting.
Went back and the gambas was excellent, but other dishes were just ok.

Went with my boyfriend and mother and had a delicious dinner! We ordered a carefe of white sangria, which was delicious and came with fresh fruit and sugarcane. Â Then, we had the yucca fries, guacomole with taro and plantain chips and the shrimp and garlic appetizer. Â All wonderful! Then, for our entrees we ordered the jardin arepa, full of tasty veggies and cheese, a shrimp arepa, and an amazing salad filled with mango, avocado, onion, pumpkin seeds all in a wonderful ginger carrot dressing . Â Lastly, dessert was the flan and the sponge cake which tasted delightful! all in all, this place is WONDERFUL! we will most certainly be coming back! Carmen is the best!

Had reservation for 7:45, still not seated at 9! Â Kept getting different stories about how long the wait was. Obviously they don't care about their customer's time, so don't waste any by coming here.

Was drawn to DoD after watching Justin Warner win Next Food Network Star. OVERALL: Gourmet, creative food without pretension or high price. Started our meal with the steak tatare and thoroughly enjoyed it. First time having it, wasn't sure what to expect, but it was good. For our main meal we went family style and got the Fish & Chips and Salmon. The Fish and Chips, though good was hard to eat. The fish of choice was Chilean Sea Bass, but instead of being cut into nuggets or strips, it was fried whole, which meant picking through bones and other inedibles. Some of the included fries were a bit overcooked, but were good overall. When I asked for vinegar for the chips, there was none, but the astute server returned and suggested mild tabasco instead. More vinegar than heat in the flavor department. Â Emblematic of the service overall. Very personalized. Also had the salmon, which was amazing. Charred on the outside, and amazingly flakey and moist on the inside, served with a Mediterranean style assortment of mashed potatoes, olives, asparagus and tomatoes. Had a fois gras donut for dessert. Never thought I'd be able to stomach liver, but I did. Craving more sweets, we visited nearby Dough afterward. Definitely going back to Do or Dine.

One of my favorite brunch spots with amazing food and salads and LARGE cups of cofffeeee. :) Love the half Sandwhich and salad option. Generous portions and fresh ingredients. The country salad is probably one of the best salads I've ever had! Â Ambiance reminds me of San Francisco.. Very down to earth and casual. Club Sandwhich, cheese and bacon croissant, and the rueben au jus are my favorites.

Moderate at best, I don't understand what's the hype is all about. I had much better pizza in my life. We're a party of three and queued for about an hour. When we were first in line, the manager skipped TWICE on us, just because we're a party of three, he prefers party of four to fill up the table. When we asked for the check, the waiter included TIPS in the total amount. For a party of three ? I can understand if we're a big party, but for a party of three ? That's illegal by law. When we asked why he included the tips in the amount, he said he has to be "harsh" and thought that we're tourists. The waiter was rude and unapologetic.

Brunch started off with the kind of fresh baked bread that you scarf up even though you know it will fill you up. The apple pancakes were delicious as was the savory cheddar burger and rosemary fries. My only regret is I didn't have the mushroom soup! Coffee and water was kept filled to the brim by our attentive server. The place is small but the seating is comfortable and it's great people watching. Looking forward to going back.

I am relieved that the DW has come to the sleepy sweet neighborhood of Windsor Terrace as it is the antithesis of every other ( the two other ) bars in walkable distance. Â  The beer selection was very generous and the decor--smattered with old shop relics, horseshoe bar, and honeycomb-tile floor--rounded out the ambiance. Â This being said, there are still a few quirks they need to work out. Â Seating was a bit of an issue because there are more 4-top tables than any other option. Â A good part of my time there involved staking out parties who looked like they were leaving. Â Also the air conditioning was on full-blast for the entire evening. Â I have no idea what this was about, bu it seemed out of place on a chilly December evening. In all, I think this is a great place with a few naive kinks to work out and I will definitely be going back. UPDATE: I went back this afternoon for a drink with a friend and although the crowd was SIGNIFICANTLY smaller than a usual evening, it was almost impossible to get the bartender's attention. Â After sitting at the bar for 10 minutes and not once being asked if I needed a drink, I managed to catch the eye of the bartender who was having a conversation with a bunch of guys at the end of the bar. Â I get it it was a slow night, but seriously come on. Â I still love you, DW, but please take note of this serious but easily remedied issue.

I called to make a reservation because we thought it would be packed - there's reason why this place was not packed and it's not because of the food. It's the people that work there. Firstly when I called, I was greeted by a condensing guy who asked me to repeat myself when I asked if he took reservations for tonight. Then he had to ask me 3 times if I wanted it for a hour from now. I had to say yes three times to confirm- which was a little obnoxious (first impressions are always on point) We came here with a friend who we haven't seen in a year to catch up, needless to say, were talking so much we didn't even look at the menu when it was placed in front of us - 5 mins later, abruptly, the waitress asked us if were ready. Obviously we were not ready. She set the mood for the rest of the dinner - constantly interrupting our conversation to ask if we want this or that - never politely waiting for a pause to interrupt us (like in nicer restaurants) but just rudely state her question. We had the Volk and Pepe pizza and the beet salad. Our friend had the Gorgonzola Dolce & Spring Onion pizza. Both pizzas were tasty but I was underwhelmed with the $5 beet salad which I didn't finish, and i LOVE beets! The rose I had was very dry and warm when served, so all you tasted was pure alcohol, I had to add ice to it to make drinkable. Maybe it's because they don't have AC - and the wine became warm instantly. Honestly we were all sweating after a hour! Thank goodness the weather got cooler that evening and they opened the windows! We ending the night with baby jesus cake which was the best part of the dinner. Really. What made it bearable was the bus person who was very nice and kept filling up our waters and greeted us nicely when we left. We did over tip hoping that it would go to him and not the rude waitress. Unfortunately, it's a very nice place with decent food but terrible waitstaff and bartender. IF they can fix that then the place will be packed with more guests. There's a thousand amazing Italian restaurants in the city which is only 15 mins away that has nicer service and amazing food. Too bad the one nearest us have to be subpar because of the service. Especially for the prices they charge! Would not recommend this place - Go to Turkish Grill or Takesushi for the same prices and quality of food, but at least the people working there cares Â about their customer's experience and makes it our go to spot for Sunnyside!

We were around Times Square and had a craving for halal truck and went to the renowned original Halal Guys. The line was intimidating, although you're through very quickly. I tried the mixed gyro and chicken over rice bowl and it was delicious!!! For $4 and $6 you CANNOT go wrong. Wanted to try the falafel but I was incredibly full. Careful, the red sauce is spicy and the aftermath can be lethal [in the bathroom]. A must try in NY!

This was one of my first "fine dining" experiences in NYC! Â Came for a work lunch during restaurant week (I think they only participate for lunch) and it was top-notch. Â Hard to get to by public transit, right on the West Side highway, but worth the journey. Â The food, service and modern decor were impeccable and would definitely recommend for a business lunch/dinner or a special occasion.

After 3 visits, Becco has left me happier every time. First off, I recommened making a reservation and if it is more than 2 people you will probably not want to sit in the bar area. There are basically 4 completely different dining rooms at Becco. First time, it was just me and my boyfriend and we sat in the bar area which was fine for two people. Second time, party of 4 in the skylight room, really pretty especially if you are there when it is still light out. Third time, upstairs, which may have been my favorite. The food here is delicious. The prices are reasonable, and they make sure that you get a great experience. The $25 wine list is wonderful! I think it is awesome that they offer this..had the one of the Dolcetto's. Amazing. They usually have a long list of specials going on, so listen carefully when they tell you because there are a lot, and you'll probably want them all. Must do the pasta, it can be added to your entree for $9 and shared with the table if someone does not want to get it as their actual meal. Top Picks: *The mussels...I don't know what is in that broth but it is addicting and delicious, and just thinking about it makes my mouth water. Possibly the best mussels I have ever had. *Unlimited pasta...self explanatory. Served table-side, unlimited. My favorite ever was the mushroom truffle ravioli! *Cheesecake... Overall, a great place to come with the family. There is something for everyone.
The brisket was good but the piece we were served was very fatty. The baked beans were good. Â The beef ribs were simply amazing. Can't wait to come back for more.

Great buzz/hum in the restaurant, always packed! Love being able to see the chefs in action! Everything was scrumptious and great service. We had the bucatini, branzino, and roasted quail.. everything was elegant and tasty. YUM.

One of my new favorite places to eat and hang out in NYC! Â Been to the city so many times, and just recently had the opportunity (thanks to Yelp!) to try this out. Â It is a little difficult to find (thus the basis of its appeal), but once you head down the stairs, you will see what a popular place this is to those who enjoy great food! Â LOVE LOVE LOVE the sparkling sake that they have on the menu (can't seem to find it anywhere now, even online). Â The best way to enjoy this place is just to have an open mind and an appetite! Â Order a few items, try them out, and then order some more! Â Have fun with it! Â Would completely recommend this to those traveling into the city that want something DIFFERENT!

It was a nice experience. Â I don't have a ton to say either way. Â A bit cramped. Â Service was great though and the food was lovely. Â My girlfriend was very happy - which is always a plus. Â Wine, food, really pleasant service. Â Good stuff. Sorry - don't have a ton more to say. Â Prolly why it isn't a 5

SEASAME PANCAKE WITH PORK! - juicy well marinated meat, with pickled carrots and cilantro, all in a crispy seasame fried dough of goodness - its like a spin on a vietnamese sandwich - it sure tasted a lot like one the pork one is better than the duck one the dumplings are alright...the pork dumplings were better than the veggie dumplings but i wouldnt get the dumplings here despite the name.
