I almost forgot!! They have the best tasting Scallion Pancakes I have ever tasted! and with that chili oil all over it just makes it crazy good!!
This restaurant is a true Italian treasure! Their Alfredo sauce is the best I have ever had.

Their creations are creative and yummy but my favorite thing about this place is the service! I have a lot of allergies and they were incredibly accommodating. They went out of their way to prepare a feast for me and I couldn't be more grateful!

Went to Balthazar last week with friends and family. I loved it from the minute I walked in. The atmosphere was wonderful...it is a wide open space with columns and service stations with fresh crusty bread arranged, waiting to be served. It can be a bit loud so perfect for groups that like to talk and laugh! The service great...our waitress made some wonderful suggestions, was pleasant and knowledgeable. The food spectacular -Appetiezer - warm goat cheese and carmalized onion tort...spectacular! The main courses ordered - grilled chicken paillard, grilled brook trout salad, duck confit - all wonderful. The desserts exceptional - we tried the creme brulee and the Profiteroles - a perfect finish. The wine...lovely! I can't wait to go back! Note: lunch is a bit pricey....do not miss the experience...save and go to enjoy an afternoon in France!

I came here after reading the Yelp reviews that stated that it was "great for vegetarians!" You'll notice that I put the exclamation point within the quotations. I wholeheartedly disagree. So my girlfriend and I gave up meat for lent, and we were looking for a place to eat in the area. We decided on Ippudo, and I was quite surprised to find that they only really have one ramen on the menu for vegetarians. We both ordered it, but my girl ordered it without the wasabi flavoring because she can't handle spicy foods (lucky for me, she can handle spicy guys!). The whole time we were there, we couldn't stop staring at all the delicious meat around us. Sigh. But anyway, the ramen was just okay. And the ramen without wasabi was almost inedible. It was so flavorless that my girlfriend couldn't even finish it. But I can't fault the restaurant for that, so my review is solely based upon my ramen. If I had to sum Ippudo up into one word, it would be, "meh." On a positive note, I loved the music. I don't know what the genre is, but it's just like the opening theme to samurai champloo. But they played it loudly, and they screamed at each other in Japanese all over the restaurant, so the ambiance was kind of.. loud. I understand that the yelling is traditional, but it amused me to see clearly un-Japanese people screaming in Japanese. hehehehe

lovee their corn!!! simply amazingg and cheap too, 2 for $4.50! the place is really small tho so it's best to go with just 1 friend, you'll get seats faster that way. It's packed most of the time and you'll notice you sit right next to a stranger while you're eating (you wont have much room to move around). Will definitely go back for their corn, plus a friend recommended their hangover soup so I'll be trying that next time I go!

Delicious!!! Â The restaurant is beautiful. Â I love the rustic/modern vibe. I ordered a pulled pork sandwich with the best cole slaw I ever had! The staff was courteous and despite being really crowded, we were able to easily grab a seat. Â I loved the bbq bottles on each table. What a great place!!

I went here on a set up thing by a magazine. I've walked by the place a thousand times and never went in. It was a quiet Tuesday night. Waitress was great. Very knowledgeable, good recommendations. They do some pretty cool stuff with their tater tots, which you wouldn't expect, but it's definitely worth it. The snap peas are very fresh and a great spring/summer dish. I had the Red Jacket Barley as my entree. There were over a dozen vegetables cooked in to it with a creme fraiche topping that melted in to the barley perfectly and thickened in to the entire dish. After eating I got to meet the chef, Joey, and he was a warm, wonderful person, who put together some pretty great plates. I would recommend heading over here and sitting in the back patio. Wonderful staff, great chef, and some delightful food.

My college roomie was in town and after a long weekend we needed a Sunday brunch spot. We also needed to find a place that opened before 11 or noon and Sanfords was our spot being it's 24 hours! When we arrived, we were seated right away. There was some older couple and families in the restaurant seeing as how it was 9:30 the hungover crowd was still fast asleep. The breakfast/brunch menu is quite extensive and on Sunday's they don't serve booze til 12 which was fine because we drank more than enough!! But with that being said for $14 you can get a nice pre fixe meal which is really worth doing. We ordered off the breakfast menu instead. I got the organic frittata Â zucchini, ricotta, cherry tomato, pesto (8.5) and my friend got the build your own omelet which she filled with tomatoes, broc and cheddar. Both the omelet and frittata were a nice size, more than enough food. They were also served with home fries which made it a well rounded breakfast meal. We also got a fruit salad to split between the two of us. The frittata was just okay, I wasn't wowed by it. The veggies were a little soggy and there was just doll ups of ricotta in a few random areas. I did do all egg whites and the home fries were delicious! The fruit salad again was just meh, I felt like the fruit could have been a little fresher. My friends omelet looks delicious!! And she said she really enjoyed it. We were in and out there basically but not rushed. The bill came to about 25 bucks which I didn't think was too bad for the amount of food we got. Service was attentive and helpful with making menu selections.

My boyfriend, who is French, came to NYC for a weekend. He's your typical baguette lover, with a pride for all things a la francaise- so when I told him we were going out for a real American breakfast, he was doubtful. To sum up our breakfast at Clinton St. Baking Company America- 1. France- 0. We started lining up at 8:30 AM. They open at 9. We waited 30 min to get in the door, BUT they had no space (this place seats only like 40), so we waited another 30 min ... total wait was an hour and we were early. But the waiting is notorious. Its worth it if you're willing to be patient. Go around for a stroll in LES, take a coffee, or two or three. Its worth it. We had the French toasts in banana caramel sauce which was to die for. We also ordered the Spicy Chorizo omelette breakfast. It was excellent, but nothing out of this world. And for the grand finale- IF YOU GO HERE, YOU MUST ORDER THE SUGAR CURED BACON. Im no bacon fan, but this stuff is heavenly. Its crispy-sweet and crunchy like candy. but if you're turned off by the sweet-savory enigma, have no fear- becuase this combo works perfectly well. I don't know how to explain it ... for that, you'll have to ask God. We walked away with full stomachs, and I had the satisfaction of telling the Frenchie that we Americans can do breakfast better anyday (some days). We also walked out 2000 calories into our day.

Today woke up craving for Yuji's mazemen ramen... Drove to Manhattan, parked and realized that the place is now closed not only in WholeFoods Gowanus but also in East Houston... So, hungry like little bears, we start yelping to find another place making the mazemen (dry) ramen and we found none... Incredible, you would say. Yes. At least, I couldn't find nothing. If you have any tip, please let me know! So, drove back to Brooklyn, to CHUKO, which we wanted to visit as some friends say it's very good and yelp reviews are very good too. Ready to have a good but classic ramen with broth.... BUT the special of the day was a mazemen ramen!!! LUCKY US. Named Mentaiko ramen, it is made like a carbonara but much fresher and with scallion, and little crunchy bacon strips. Delicious! So happy. Te place is small and nice, service very kind and efficient. Everything was good from the shrimps bun to the pork gyoza to the shishito peppers. Next time I will try a classic ramen, I am sure those are delicious too. Just, to have broth, you need to be in the mood!
Green sauce is life. Big Sangria. Brasil, Reggaeton, Spicy Chicken, Viagra, Cuban, Plantains and Guac. Open 24/7 and delivery! Yes, yes,yes.

My dumpling place used to be Fried Dumpling at 99 allen until they closed. The dumplings were also 5 for a dollar, and a little better than prosperity. but prosperity is the best around now. just try not to offend anyones dai lo on eldridge street

Every time I come here I seem to lose my memory by the time I get out. The first time I came here with my friend and we decided it was a good idea to drink an entire bottle of sake between the two of us. The 2nd time, I was already drunk. It's a semi hole in the wall and definitely only accessible if you knew about it beforehand. The specials changes. If you're lucky enough to be there during the uni special day, then count your blessings and eat it! If not, well then, that's unfortunate. Some things are good, some not so much. Overall it's a nice, authentic Japanese place and one worth checking out.

- actually 3.5 (4 for pizza, 3 for pasta/unfriendly waiters) - I don't understand why this place is so popular among people. probably because of its great location -- on the 23rd st and just in front of the madison square park? - this place is just like a grocery market where some of its space is allocated for dining tables. As a grocery store, it's really amazing, full of various kinds of pastas, sauce, meat, cheese, seafood, etc. As a restaurant, it's awful: seating tables are too dense one another, and the area is somewhat noisy. - Pizza was really nice! Its dough was the most chewy or tasty that i've ever had! We chose one with eggplant/zucchini toppings, and these toppings went perfect with this amazing dough. - As for pasta, it was so-so. Especially, out waiter got a wrong order; we ordered a meat-filled pasta with meat sauce but he brought ravioli with pesto sauce to our table. We told him that you brought us a wrong one, but he insisted that we ordered the ravioli. oh god. we had a terrible experience here. I would never dine-in at eataly again; but I'm willing to have its pizza again as to-go.

Went here this evening after a few months of meaning to go. The food selection looks really good, and after some deliberation, my brother and I decided to try dinner another time and went the dessert and drink route. What we had: Apple Strudel, Marzipan Ring Cake, Green Tea and Hot Chocolate. I'm a Marzipan-aholic, so the ring cake was all my idea. My bro had spent a semester in Vienna a couple of years ago and hadn't had the chance to get Apple Strudel since, so that was a must order. The strudel was delicious! The apples were perfectly tart and the pastry was yummy and crispy. The ring cake was not something I would get again. It really didn't taste a lot like Marzipan and was really dry and generally boring. The tea was really good and the hot chocolate was okay. The ambiance was upscale and pretty and seemed to emulate a Viennese coffee house. We didn't have a chance to go into the Gallery but the Alfred Kubin drawings on exhibit are really cool: dark and nightmare fantasy. This is how the Neue Galerie describes the collection: "Collectively they envision a world that is the opposite of that of modern science and technology: one that is driven by human irrationality, animal instincts and supernatural forces".

The portions are very small for the price, but on the other hand, the nutritional content of most plates is basically equivalent to a glob of Crisco of approximately the same size, so I'm not sure that bigger portions would make any sense. Basically, this is a novelty place, but apparently a lot of people like that sort of thing and it does attract repeat customers, otherwise it would never have lasted in this location. Conveniently located near a 24-hour drugstore--you'll be needing some Pepto action afterward.

A pleasant surprise! I'd walked by many times but never really meant to try this place, it looked pretty standard. One night I wanted a vegetable based meal for an affordable price after 9 0 clock in the east village, and this seemed to be one of the only places that fit the bill. I walked in and immediately realized I'd been missing out. It was packed...on a Thursday! The atmosphere was cozy and authentic East Village. And the food! The food was reasonably priced, healthy, varied, and really delicious. Not at all just another asian fusion spot...really specific flavors and styles. It's unassuming but worth even a trip all the way into Manhattan for you Brooklynites out there. So gooood.

I love Ootoya. The NYC location is a branch I the Tokyo-based chain. Good service, great food- they take Japanese comfort food and elevate it to a whole new level. You can get very fresh sushi and sashimi, if that's what you want, but they also offer many pork, chicken and beef dishes, as well as grilled fish. Their yakitori is fantastic. You can get something very simple, like pork tonkatsu, or you can be adventurous and get the raw tuna with grated yam and fermented soybeans. I like the Ikura-don set: salmon roe on top of rice, accompanied by pickles, rice, miso soup and wonderfully soothing chawanmushi . Extra fun- sit upstairs overlooking the open kitchen, and watch the bonito-shaving machine do its thing. Cool!

This is one of those great little finds in the middle of Little Italy/Chinatown. Â I'm a local and love a good breakfast place that I can eat at once or twice a week. The food is excellent and reasonably priced for the area. The reason why am not giving it five stars is that the service was so painful this morning that it nearly ruined my appetite. Â  I walked up to the counter to order and the gentleman standing there, a blonde Australian guy, Â said to me "can you hold on a second." Â I said "sure." ...And then to my surprise right in front of me on the counter he was pulling his one dollar tips from the jar. Â  Five one dollar bills at a time and replacing it with a five dollar bill. Â Then he did it again and again till there was 4 five dollar bills at the top of the tip jar. Â I found it a bit strange or shall say I poor taste, but I thought okay.... maybe finally has a chance to do that. Â  I sat down and waited for my breakfast and notice three or four tables were piled high with dirty empty plates. One of them even had a tip on the table. Â I did see the sign "bus your own table" but not everybody follows that and the sign is ONLY in the back. Â Meanwhile the entire restaurant has dirty tables all over the place. Â Customers we're coming in and wanting to sit down but there was dirty tables everywhere. Â Even the table I was at was super sticky. Â  Then when my amazing food showed up and the same blonde Ozzie said "do you need anything else"? Â I looked in the little silver bucket on the table and said "there's no fork here" and he said "oh you can get it over there." Â  I cannot believe how lazy this person is! Â  Half the tables are missing them. Â  It's a service business and he works for tips! Â What a joke! It put a bad taste in my mouth. Â Then I asked the guy across the table from me "is it just me or is the service here really bad." Â  He said, "I had the same experience with silverware." Â  I walked up to the counter and said "the knife table in the bucket is dirty." Â Response he got was "you can get a new knife over there." Â I've waitress for 10 years. Â My response would've been "oh my gosh I'm so sorry " and walked 3 feet to hand a new knife. Now I'm willing to come back here because I'm a local and love Two Hands food. Â Maybe the manager or the owner had a talk with the staff or got a new staff. Â I hate to blame one or two bad experiences cause of one or two poorly hired choices. Â One more time Two Hands And if I have another bad experience service I'll bring my breakfast appetite elsewhere.

This place really does deserve 5 stars. It has never disappointed. I had teh pork chop last night and found myself licking the flavor off the bone. I know its sound gross...but trust me when I say it was heaven. The food is bomb and the ambiance isn't too shaby either.
It is the best! Love the sauce and hot sauce, but be careful not to put too much hot sauce.

My sister, friend and I stopped by Gila's for a quick lunch on our first day in the city. The food was awesome but the service alone made it worth the trip. Gila's warm, welcoming and quirky personality is infectious and she made us feel immediately at home - worrying about our warmth, getting us situated at a table and giving us advice on the menu. The food was affordable and delicious, particularly the grilled eggplant and hummus. Thanks for a great first experience in New York, Gila!
I have only good things to say about my experience here. Five plus stars. Â Welcoming friendly service, perfect mixology, delicious and creative food.
This place is amazing. Couldn't be happier. Crispy crust, amazing and fresh toppings, awesome wood fired pizza.

I came in on a mission to take down the Black Label burger. Â I found a great seat at the bar and dug in. Â I ordered a tasty tap beer ($8) and struck up a conversation with the bartender. Â Out came the burger - cooked to a perfect medium rare. Â My first bite flooded my taste buds with a rich beef flavor that lingered on my palate. Â The burger is not heavy, nor is it greasy. Â It is quite rich. Â There is no mistaking the fact that this is a luxury burger. Â It went down too easy and too fast. Â I honestly savored every single juicy bite. Â At $26 I won't be eating this very often but it was worth the splurge tonight. Â Oh, and the fries were pretty righteous too.

After reading the glowing reviews for BentOn Cafe, I decided I'd take a break from burritos and check it out for lunch today. I lived in Japan for a year or so, so I frequently get cravings for home-style Japanese food (katsu-don, temakizushi, karaage, etc.) and I also have fairly high standards for Japanese food (no sickly-sweet teriyaki for me). When I walked into BentOn Cafe, i was struck by the number of Japanese speakers I heard/saw in the small space (not really a cafe, so plan to grab-and-go) - they must be doing something right! I scanned the pre-made bento selection and decided on a katsu-don as I've been craving heapig mounds of Japanese rice lately and some fried pork never hurts ;). I also grabbed a bottle of nice cold green tea, paid (credit card - $9.75 total), and walked back to the office. They have a microwave for customer's to heat up their bento, but mine was fairly warm already so I skipped it. When I get back to my desk and opened the bento, I was impressed by how fresh and crisp everything looked (veggie weren't soggy, they included a few ripe cherry tomatoes for variety) and my first bite didn't disappoint! I can't get over how crisp and crunchy the tonkatsu is! That makes me think that they both: 1. Take pride in their product and 2. Make these bentos frequently, so nothing is sitting around for a long time. Moreover, they used just the right amount of tonkatsu sauce, such that you get that wonderful worcestershire flavor, but it doesn't mask the pork flavor or soak through all of that lovely, fluffy rice! Overall, I am very impressed with BentOn and will be back soon to try more! i'm especially interested in their desserts, as it's been far too long since I had some Japanese baked-goods :)

Although the no-reservations practice can make for a long on-site wait, the food is truly delicious. For an appetizer we tried the Suzuki Hakusai, seabass steamed in nappa cabbage and wrapped in a torched yuba tofu skin. Â Instead of the usual ramen entree, I tried the Shojin ramen which is vegan and served cold. This was a revelation, it actually felt restorative on a hot summer night. Â Will definitely go again, as long as we have enough time to wait in line.

For this price range, it's hard to ask for more. Â The ambiance is very relaxed and intimate in this dim-lit brazilian nook. Â I found it to be the perfect place to have a conversation, while the noise level is high enough that others won't be listening to your conversation, it was never loud enough to the point where you have to make an effort to hear the other person. Â This is an ideal to take somebody on a casual date. While the locale is small and constantly full, I have never had to wait more than 10 to 15 minutes for a table which has been very convenient. When it comes to the food, this place continues to surprise me. Â I have had the pleasure of tasting 5 of the main courses on the menu and I have liked each and every one of them, considerably. Â When you take in to account that they are from the 12 to 17 dollars range, you are pleasantly surprised at what you are getting. The service is fast and attentive and the food comes out quick enough so that you are not complaining about your ravenous hunger, but not too fast where you feel you are being rushed to eat and leave so that other people can sit. One thing that was a bit strange and another that has always been annoying to me, though. The strange one is the soup in the bathroom... Â Instead of having liquid or foam soap, they have this strange bar that looks like a small melon or zucchini (depends on how much it's been worn down) and is drilled to the wall. Â Kind of feels like your giving the soup a hand-job just to clean your hands. Â The annoying one is that this place is cash only which is always a pain considering that in this day and age less and less people carry cash with them. All-in-all, this place is a great little spot and I recommend it to anybody that want to have a nice relaxed night with good food and brings good company. Â I highly recommend the Rice Bolognese Al Forno.

We went to Kefi after reading all the great reviews and had an enjoyable meal. The place was packed and we were told it was about a half an hour wait. We sat down at the bar, ordered the pomegranate margarita and LOVED it! We were at the bar for no more than 10 minutes before our name was called and we were sat. We had a small table in the middle of the back room, quieter than the front of the restaurant for sure. Our server was very well spoken, knew the menu inside and out, and was very accommodating to my food allergies (I'm gluten and dairy intolerant). I ordered the seared striped bass and it was really quite good. I don't tend to go for striped bass as it can be kind of fatty, but the filet was a perfect size and the sides were seasoned really well. My boyfriend ordered the chicken which was good (he was expecting a breast, but it was bone-in), but he still enjoyed it. I'm not sure we would go back there again, but if you're looking for good, decently priced Greek food on the Upper West Side, this is the place for you!

i definitely agree with its adorableness. a very long wait. nothing too special but the food was certainly good. Â i had a vegetarian sandwich. Â michael had a really good muffin, i don't remember what kind but it was good. edit: Â their mac and cheese is delish. Â THAT is what i recommend.

Do not go here. Very rude and unprofessional servers and bartenders. Very pretentious, and stuck up. They also charge $2 for an ice cube. Meaning if you order a drink on the rocks, they will put an ice cube in it and charge you $2. Is it a magic ice cube? Will this ice cube make me a better person? I don't understand the science of mixology? I don't care. Do yourself a favor and go to the White Horse Tavern around the corner. $3 Pints all day everyday - Where the real finance professionals go to get drunk.

So, I love Westville. I love the formula, I love the food - it works for me. No wonder I was soooper psyched to see that it was opening a new location right near my house. It looks great from the inside - it's spacious, airy, light, and a nice, clean design with a bar. Love the bar. And there's a (very small) outdoor seating possibility. They had to build a kitchen in this space, so it took them a loooong time to open. Unfortunately, it still seems to have some kitchen issues. The first time I went, I ordered take-out, and took a seat at the bar. 40 (!!!) minutes later, I finally got my food. They kept on saying "it was coming", but really, a turkey burger shouldn't need to take 40 minutes. Also, it seemed like diners were getting their food before me. The second time I came with a group and we were seated quickly and service was much better. The food took a little while to come, but definitely not 40 minutes. I'll keep on dining here, just because I love Westville and its veggies... but I hope they sort out their issues soon. Three stars for now, but I might give more stars at a later time. Some favorites: Market Veggie plate (try the brussel sprouts... seriously, so damn good, even though I used to hate brussel sprouts!) The sandwiches on special - last time I had a fishcake, mmm! Salmon over baby spinach with lemon-dill vinaigrette (don't know what they put in that but it's dee-lish!). Anyway, just go, and try it out. You won't be disappointed.
great beers on tap and bottles and great food. Moule frites: pick your own sauce.. i went for the bacon and cream sauce. it's a mixed crowd for dinner vs. drinks. interesting..
Fried Chicken and soul!!! Â An authentic hoot. Â Don't come here if you are keeping on diet.
I'm very late in writing this review. I ate here during summer of '08 and ever since then I regularly dream about their margherita pizza. It was simply the best pizza I ever had.

If I'm on death row, my last meal would be steak and junior's cheesecake. Cheesecake is my favorite dessert, and I've had my share. Junior's have the bessttt! My personal favorite is the raspberry swirl. Their red velvet cheesecake is great too, better than most bakeries that offer this variety. Ive had their strawberry shortcake a couple of times and the chocolate mousse once. Ive always sticked to the classic raspberry swirl. So creamy and perfect balance of the sweet and tart. Plus i like the fact that they used sponge cake for the crust instead of graham. If u eat at the restaurant, grab a seat at the bar so u dont have to wait long. And make sure u order their Brooklyn buffalo Â wings. The besssttt...

Been here many times and never wrote a review! So here's my opinion...Lincontro is a specialty food restaurant, so when the waiter asks if you want to hear the specials, always say YES! I think I ordered from the menu once...every other time has been a special and I haven't opened a menu since..not that the menu is bad but the specials are incredible...try the cold lobster salad, the buffalo mozzarella with prosciutto! these are delicious. Also the general manager is a delight! he makes everyone feel as if lincontro is their home...if you're a picky eater he will even try to make a special just for you..

I don't know why I do this...I go to a place that gets yelped for their dumplings and I order the beef noodle soup. Idiot. But you know what I realized? I may be the idiot for ordering it, but why in the world would you play such a cruel trick on me, Mr. Prosperity Dumpling? It's because YOU are the fool, doing what every single Chinese eating establishment before you has done to give the impression of how skilled they are, how luxurious they can be, or how you can grasp tightly the antiquated dining traditions---add superfluous menu items. Not only does it cost you more to stock the perishable ingredients needed to make the superfluous dishes (bok choy, rice noodles, braised beef), it takes time to prepare those ingredients and that time prevents you from focusing on what you're already good at!. It is very clear to me that you do one thing right--make guotie. Your guotie have skins that fry well, resist falling apart, the pork and chive filling is seasoned perfectly, the ratio of fat/gelatin to filling is perfect such that no dumpling is ever dry, and you get a great crisp on the bottom because you've had so many years of experience cooking them in that enormous pan of yours. So why do anything but that when your noodles absolutely suck!? Argh, and why make the noodles the most expensive thing on your menu? My thought was that I would get the item that the place is most known for and then try and get their most expensive item (at $3, the noodles were not that expensive at all, but still). The noodles didn't seem fresh; they were the processed type you'd get dry at a supermarket and rehydrate. Consequently they didn't have good resistance and just crumbled in your mouth. The broth was not well filtered and I found multitudinous scum coagulates floating on top of the bowl. The broth wasn't well seasoned either, tasting just a little saltier than canned Swanson's chicken/beef stock. The beef tasted boiled and didn't have the essence of anise/5-spice that you would expect from a dish like this. The highlight was probably the boiled bok choy included in the soup. I couldn't finish it. In Asian culture you're threatened as a kid when you don't finish your food with parents saying stuff like, "Every rice grain you don't finish is going to be a pock mark on your face." After leaving those noodles, I'm running to Duane Reade for some Neutrogena. **They have sesame pancake sandwiches here too, but they're much better at Vanessa's where the pancakes are made fresh to order. These are just sitting in a stainless steel catering bin. ***Incidentally (not that I care, but you might) I noticed an enormous 50lb bag of Ajinomoto MSG in their kitchen. Maybe it's why their dumplings are so damn good. You'd better believe it. If that makes your ears ring, that's really too bad. But also realize that it's what has made this place as good as it is. Don't ask them to change that, you're lucky they didn't use some shady rural Chinese MSG manufacturer.

I just remember it being served in huge portions, way too much for four of us to eat. Â It was okay, just nothing special. Â The service on the other hand was great! Thankfully, eating at 3:30 PM meant there were only a few other patrons and we could enjoy our meal at one of the tables. My sis and I decided to each get a Combo 2 (2 rolls, 2 individual pieces) and share it, along with an order of the edamame. Â We both tried the Strawberry kiwi yuzu juice which was sweet but very refreshing. Â  The edamame came from the cold case next to the register and weren't anything special. Â On the menu they are listed as having Himalayan sea salt on them but I really couldn't taste it. The 2 pieces I picked were the Baked Tofu and the special piece of the month (black rice, braised okra, heirloom tomato, and preserved lemon). Anyone who says it is not as good as it was years ago is a miserable person that should not post! It is just as good as my first visit 32 years ago! Don Peppe's is like Sunday dinner made by the most talented family with Grandma supervising everything. No rectangular plates, no drizzled nonsense, no ingredients that nobody heard of until the last few years. Just amazing real food for real people. Tonight I had baked clams and chicken scapriello. Unbelievable!!!!*****

This is excellent beyond belief. It seems simple cramming rice, chicken (or lamb), and lettuce into a tin plate, but they do it right. Their white sauce is to die for and if you're in the mood to spice it up, they have a good spicy sauce too (which you should be careful about). Sometimes I am tempted to fly from LA, just to eat here. If there is one place I recommend to go eat in NY, this is it. NOTE: Do not get chicken and rice at any other cart besides this one. They're simply the best.
Some of the best pad Thai I've had. Pho Bo broth is very tasty with anise and a little jalapeÃ±o.

I've been here many times and always order the soup dumplings. The soup is so tasty and it is fun to eat. I also had the double cooked pork, sweet and spicy! Must try. Always crowded, mix of tourists and regular New Yorkers. You know it's a good place when it can attract both groups. Took off one star because we had to share a table with 4 other parties. I have never experienced such an attitude from a restaurant service ever.... He showed his displeasure at the fact that my friend did not order anything ... When we started to order and I let him know that I have nut and soy allergy, which normally is not a problem even in very casual restaurants, it looked like it was a major issue for him.... The pizza slice we had was pretty good. I prefer other pizzerias in Brooklyn though.
10 stars for the all you can eat mussels with a Stella for $22. Six different preps. I love the Thai curry. Only place in NYC with Gulden Draak on tap. Arguably the best strong ale in the world!

I am a big fan of Viet food and have been searching for a replacement for my previous favorite in the EV. My go to on 2nd Ave btwn 4th and 5th decided one day that they were Thai now and I hadn't found a place since that satisfied my Viet cravings. Enter Xe May. I went there this week for dinner and was impressed. I have a "no sandwich for dinner" rule so I went for my go to - grilled pork vermicelli. I was really hungry so I threw in a grilled meatball taco for fun. Food was prepared fresh and we ate in the restaurant. Vermicelli bowl was plentiful and the grilled pork on top was delicious. Well seasoned...juicy...not too fatty. I was pleasantly surprised by the moist and delectable meatball taco. They steam the meatball and crisp it on the grill top which gives it a great texture. I tried some of the shrimp and papaya salad as well as the green papaya salad and both were delicious too. The ginger dressing on these was quite good. Overall, delicious food and hospitable service that makes me want to go back again soon. Highly recommended. I think I heard that they are open late night too.

As a decent fan of Lil' Frankies I was pretty excited to hit up Supper, but upon arrival we were asked to wait at their bar next door where Prince was pumping so loudly overhead that I almost considered rounding the troops and running out. However, after being recommended a remarkable glass of an Italian white wine blend, my patience slowly came back. Luckily, our wait wasn't too terrible and were corralled into our table next door where the music and setting was much more conducive to a peaceful gathering. The food: the white bean dip that's served at the start was excellent; the fennel salad was good, albeit forgettable; but the pasta dishes, naturally, were perfect. All three of us ordered specials that night :I ordered a simple rigatoni with meatballs (which were some of my favorite I've had in pasta - I feel like the secret ingredient has to be lemon zest or something lemon) and fresh tomato sauce; my friend ordered the special tagliatelle with mint and fresh herbs in butter and parmesan (a great, simple departure for a pasta dish); and my other friend ordered the slow-braised short ribs, which were actually disappointing. I don't attribute this to the restaurant, I just simply attribute it to the fact that anything slow-braised that's not pork - whether it be a lamb shank or short rib or whatever - never really is something to write home about. In general, dinner was great. Our waitress could have afforded more Â attentiveness, but in general, I'll return to Supper. Next time, however, I'll make sure everyone sticks to the pastas and that I have the balls to request that the Â music be turned down a bit at the bar next door while waiting for a table.

Mahmoun's is a wonderful place for good, cheap falafel. Â Don't be afraid to splash out on a cup of Lentil Soup. Â Especially on a cold wintery day, it hits the spot as you share a tiny space with NYU students and cheery drunks wandering through on their way out (or way home) in the West Village.

Really good, inexpensive Korean. For $3-$8, depending on how hungry you are, you can get one or a few delicious items. Lunchtime runs like a well-oiled machine - hot buffet and pre-mades to the right, cold pre-mades to the left. Get 'em and go. We haven't stayed to eat in the place, so don't even know if they have a sit-down menu, but if they do, I'd imagine it's just as good as what they lay out for lunch.

Simply amazing! This hidden gem in the heart of Brooklyn not easily found. I guess that's a good thing because the place isn't so big. Came here with a friend who lives conveniently in the neighboring town of Flatbush. Cool little joint with delicious burgers and soccer games on TV . I had a good time here, staff was pleasant. They were a bit short handed but after I ate the food it made me forget. I ordered the 'Good ol Boy' Not too many sandwiches can fill me up but I felt pretty fulfilled that night.The Alamo Burger with the fried egg is crazy! Love the Crab cake sliders too, very delicious! To wash down this amazing meal I was hoping for some choices of shakes and/or smoothies. Other than Alcohol and bar juices there weren't really any choices. Desert looks great but was too full to order any. Next time will do

Dined here twice during RW Summer 2012. First, great space. Open, relaxed, but still very nice. Service - great! However, I have high expectations for this place given that TC came from a Danny Meyer restaurant which focuses on hospitality. Food - it's great b/c they offer everything on the menu for RW. The menu changed from the first time we went to the second. But the pork belly was on it both times. Wonderful! The use of the grill is great and you should order something that is finished/made on the grill. I don't think you can really go wrong with any of the apps/entrees here. However, the desserts are definitely less exciting. The chocolate souffle is def on the drier side. Although I really like this place, it's a bit far out there. I would not go out of my way to come here on a normal basis, but can see myself here time to time. If you are in the 'hood, this is a def a great option!

I recently came here on a Friday night around 6 PM and there was no line. We were seated immediately. The place was full after we sat down and I was happy I didn't need to wait. The restaurant is really small and it looks like it can seat no more than 20 people. We sat at the bar table facing the kitchen, since the regular tables were all taken. We ordered the shrimp gyoza ($6) for 5 pieces and each piece had one whole shrimp in it and it was delicious. It was crispy on the bottom just how I like it. For ramen I had the spicy miso ramen with the wavy noodles ($13). I like the noodles, but I didn't like the broth that much. It was just a little spicy, which is fine. But it was missing that flavor. The ramen came with 2 char pork, it wasn't all that great either. Again, I thought the pork could use some more flavor. I liked the gyoza more than the ramen. This place is CASH ONLY!
Cheap and delicious ! I only gave three stars because there is no where to eat you can just carry out BUT the food is GREAT. Definitely going there again.

I am a bit reluctant to give a review to this place. La Sirene is so perfect that I just don't want to share it with anyone. Â I love the fact that it is BYOB. Â It is tiny, so definitely make a reservation before you go. Â The food is delicious. Â I had the seafood pie, and it was creamy, hearty and fresh- perfect for a drizzly day in New York. Â Service is wonderful. Â We stayed long after we finished our dinner, and we never had to once asked our waitress for anything. Â She didn't rush us to leave either, and we only got our bill when we requested for it. Â I can go on, but the point is that La Sirene is definitely worth your visit, but promise me you won't share it with too many people.

Every time I'm in NY/Brooklyn I can't resist visiting Roberta's. Love the pizza, atmosphere, even the tiki bar which is very nicely heated while waiting for a table. On our most recent visit, a Saturday around 2 pm - was full, as always but hot toddys and beer make it go by quickly. Once we grabbed a table I got the The Bee Sting pizza - honey and chillis - unique but super tasty. Husband ordered a very gluttonous breakfast. Essentially eggs Benny on a toasted croissant. While he enjoyed it - pizza is definitely the best bet. Overall great beer and cocktails - awesome pizza, chill, affordable. What more can you ask for.

Came here Saturday for dinner with the lady and 4 friends. Getting in: - Walked in and requested a spot outside, and got one Atmosphere: - Cool Mexican resto - I liked the vibe - On a quiet picturesque block Service: - Very good and friendly Food: - Guac was amazing - Shishito peppers were great - We got all the tacos. Â Our favorite were the fish, pork and steak. Â 3 tacos to an order! - PRICES ARE FANTASTIC Drinks: - Got some beer and some margs. Â Very good all around Other: - Great neighborhood place - Finally found an excellent Mexican spot in the neighborhood (we were missing Taco Taco from when we were in the UES) - Will be back soon and often - Prices make this a go too spot as well
Amazing service! Just make sure to make reservations! And the food was delicious as well as the complimentary drink to go with the brunch. :)

Came to dinner at this place in a party of four after hearing great things about the food and ambiance. The food I'd say is a solid 4 stars due to uniqueness - I don't think I've ever encountered a restaurant in the city that serves this variety of food - and for the ambiance. The service however, is horrendous. This was by far the worst service experience I've ever had in NYC and it's a shame given how nice the food and ambiance is. Food - flavorful, unique food that's served in generous portions. Also great for groups since the four of us only had to order two items and we were fully covered. Any of the chicken dishes should be good, as our chicken was extremely tender and flavorful. The food quality is solid, and the sauces that come with the sides (e.g. plantains, fries + sausages, etc) add panache Ambiance - really interesting interior and great decor. Gives off a this amazonian vibe that adds to the food experience. A bit dark in the inside, but spacious seating especially given the area. Service - extremely terrible service. We weren't assigned a waiter and none of them spoke English properly (not a big deal) but they couldn't understand anything we asked for and required us to repeat orders multiple times in the already loud restaurant. Something that really annoyed our group was that when the restaurant undercharged us by 50% - we told the waiter, but he didn't express any sign of gratitude and it took him 25 minutes to reissue the check, which delayed our Friday night plans. We were extremely upset after all this wait and the waiter didn't apologize, and said the manager was away. Finally we demanded some form of compensation for the lost time, and the waiter gave us a dessert, in which he made the four of us split it, which was a super cheap and disappointing move. Extremely sub-par/below average relative to NYC service standards that ruined my Friday night and I would never make me want to come here again.

Really liked this place a lot. Went yesterday with around 7 of my friends. We were seated right away in the back--long wooden table right next to the wine room. Pasta dishes are really good (I had this whole wheat dish but I also sampled the raviolini, and gnocci--both great) and everything seems fairly priced. The Tuscan Panzanella (a salad with bread, tomatoes, olive oil, red wine vinegar, capers, garlic) was delicious and this is coming from somebody that hates garlic more than anything in this world and not that fond of tomatoes (nice Italian I am -huh?)! It's small, a little tight (but not too bad), and I love the lighting (intimate) and the chandeliers... Service was also very good--friendly wait staff... I'll be back without a doubt :)

Visiting NYC with 14 people. With all the good reviews of this place. We were looking forward to have some great ramen. A couple of us were quite disappointed with it. Others were saying its just okay. Not really that good. Sure the place looks good. Stuffs are polite. And the bowls, and the presentation of the food are very pretty. But really not the taste. And certainly not worth the over pricing. The wasabi ramen tastes like what I Â got from supermarket's $1 instant noodle..

Cookshop has always been on my running path with it being close to the Hudson and next to the High Line. It always looks so cute but I never went in because the sweaty flushed look isn't a good one for eating out. I finally had the chance when a sushi restaurant I was going to go to was closed and this was close by so I was very happy at this serendipitous turn of events. It definitely paid off. From what I can tell, the menu changes frequently which makes each experience very fresh and unique. This can also be bad if the things you love aren't on the menu the next time you go. When I went, I fell in love with some of the small bites like tacos and oyster sliders. I could have eaten 5 oyster sliders and been happy that that was my dinner. But we ventured to try the charcuterie platter, which wasn't as good as others I've had like at the Breslin. We also got the scallops and steak option, which were ok as well. The only memorable thing that night was the oyster sliders, which wasn't on the menu anymore when I last checked but I think that Cookshop will still be an option that I will keep in mind given that the frequent menu changes for better or worse will always give me the option of trying something new.

As a healthy eater, the name already tells me to avoid Salt & Fat at all costs. Â However, if there is one restaurant that can make me relapse, it would be S&F. Â Despite the artery-clogging food choices, the food is simply unforgettable. While there some seasonal changes to the menu here and there, it is a simple and stable menu that boasts signature dishes from the first appetizer on the last entree on the list. I have never tried "shaved" foie gras until having it here. Â Between the bacon, mandarin oranges, and foie gras, we have an absolute roller-coaster of textures and flavors for the taste buds. Â The Pork,Duck,Chicken is a hilarious name for a dish. Â It is a bit too fat for my taste, but the flavor and texture as amazing as expected. Â The same goes for the oxtail terrine, but fortunately it is compensated by being a small portion. Â Without doubt, the scallops is my top dish. Â Tender, juicy, fatty, succulent, mesmerizing, add-in-your-own-adjective-here, holy crap great. There is undeniable pride to have a restaurant with such acclaim situated right in the middle of the Sunnyside neighborhood. Â It is a pride and joy for the community and all of its residents. Â Queens is becoming more of a destination for comfort food, and there is no better vanguard than Salt & Fat to pioneer the concept of chic, modern, yet affordable American-style comfort food.

This place is AWESOME. The food is so good that will put a big smile on your face. I order from Fabio at least twice a week and he never disappoints me. Â Tonight I had the 'special' dish of trofie pasta with pesto sauce made with arugula, cherry tomatoes and burrata and then lamb chops with broccoli rabe. THIS GUY IS A GENIUS!! I very seldom write reviews, but the food tonight was so good that pushed me to finally leave a feedback... Ordering from the regular menu is a good choice, ordering among the Specials' Fabio creates every day is a MUST! Cozy place, friendly service, casual atmosphere, reasonsble prices given the high quality of ingredients. HIGHLY RECOMMENDED!! CHAPEAU!

When I came to Northeastern for Orientation Week I had to participate in a myriad of ice breakers - all equally as stupid and mind numbing. Everyone goes around and says their name and where they're from and what they're majoring in... sometimes the questions get creative and you get to say what your favorite food is. Well, unbeknown to me, the answer "meat" is deemed as inappropriate and not funny. Well it is my favorite food. I love meat. I LOVE MEAT, EVERYONE. Oh. I get it. That's why the guys were smirking at me. They thought I was referring to their "meat." Oh that's just gross. That being said, the meat here - in the form of hamburgers - is spectacular. Even though the top bun ripped and I had to hold onto the meat (for dear life, everyone), well spit on my neck and hit me in the crotch - that burger was mighty good. I had no idea what to do with myself while I waited for my lunch partner. I wasn't offered any menus which I found strange until I realized that there was a menu plastered to the wall. Not much was done to that menu.. except maybe prices have changed. Yup, most definitely. If I was of age, I'd get drunk here. First on hamburgers, then on the beers. And then I'd break out my colored pens and I'd carve my initials into the table because DAMN IT I HAVE NEEDS TOO. Then I would pass out because I ate too many french fries. But all would be okay with the world. PS I hate the small plastic plates. They made me feel a little claustrophobic.

Adrienne brings pizza to a fine dining level. Â I've been to this restaurant quite a few times during the work lunch rush hour and never reviewed it. Â Last night, I was there err romantically, and was surprised by the serenity and class that Adrienne offers to a Sunday night Pizza dinner. Â While me and my date ordered a salad and shared a pie, one couple to my left popped open a bottle of wine and had pellegrino with their pizza in a dim-lighted setting. Â  A college frat boy to my right chowed down an entire large tray alone (sans 3 squares he took to go) in what I assumed to be a munchie-binge. Â In any event, the pizza is thin-crusted and tasty and doesn't make you feel too heavy at the end. Â The versatility this restaurant has to offer is quite impressive (sans for the 10 oz sized soda bottles!). Â 5 stars for Adrienne's!

Really really good. After a grueling day of Christmas NYC crowds, this place was a highlight. Tiny space and it was crowded, but we didn't wait long. White pizza hot out of the oven was amazing, and the boyfriend raved about the margherita pizza. It was warm enough that we ate on the leaning counter out front. Crispy, hot, big slices. And not too expensive -- three slices and one big water bottle for a little over $15.

My sister-in-law booked this restaurant for lunch and am really grateful she did. Â Benjamin was our waiter and he couldn't have provided better service even if he tried. Â He gave us wonderful recommendations of: Â chicken parm w/pepperoni, pesto ravioli, spaghetti carbonara, tagliolini al forno and the pesto ravioli alla brando. Â The other dishes at the table (the nicoise salad with fresh tuna and the shrimp salad with fava beans) looked delicious, as well. Â The chicken parm is the size of the plate - perfectly crisp on the outside but very moist. Â  Benjamin knew we were first-timers (my sister noted on her reservation) and brought us a delicious sampler of antipasti. Â After lunch, we were completely stuffed but they brought us warm parmesan and prosciutto poppers. Â We declined dessert although I was totally disappointed because all of the cakes/tarts looked delicious. Â We had tickets to the Moma and had stayed at lunch for hours. Â Warm chocolate chip cookies were brought, as well as dark chocolate bark with almonds before our bill. I originally went based on the antipasti menu, so will have to go back and try it. Â Food was great & customer service was amazing. Â Looked like a good mix of locals and visitors. Â Will definitely go back when I'm in NY.

The food is great, and the affordable wine list is extensive. Â But the service is miserable. Â Try to go during a non-theater rush time or expect to have your waiter pour half your bottle of wine on the table because he's rushing so much.

Look I'd give it four stars because when this place first opened I had a delicious puttanesca there, but when I was back (after having lived in Rome for a couple of years) they had changed the chef and the puttanesca was either not so good or not on the menu. I can't remember which. I don't know. Perhaps it was a seasonal thing, perhaps I was jaded from Rome, either way I was disappointed...so three stars.

Super awesome sandwiches for a very low price ($5-6) with a good selection of vegetarian and chicken options. Service is fast and there are bar stools to sit on. Wish they had some plum sauce to go with the sriracha!
Great food- good service- overall top notch!
Excellent food, excellent menu, excellent service, great atmosphere - just a fabulous place. Particularly if you want to go for a stroll along the Hudson before or after.
