Wow. I had such a great meal here last night with my dad. He works in Newark and I work in the FiDi and we decided that we are going to start getting dinner on weekday nights a few times a month (He will take the PATH train in) I am so happy for this, but know it will be a challenge given my dad's parameters--can't be more than a 10 minute walk away (or he will get lost), can't be too loud, can't be too crowded, can't be sushi every time (I wish). I will have a tough time finding more restaurants that compare to this gem and am certain we will return again soon. To start, my dad had the Â  salad of kale, spelt, pine nuts and apple. It was really uniquely prepared and very flavorful. I decided to go with two apps and started with tuna tartar. It was served with a fried quail egg and crispy shallots. Scrumptious. As an entree, my dad got the red snapper and I got the whole wheat reginetti with rock shrimp and mushrooms served in a coconut sauce. This was the best pasta dish I have ever had in my life. The flavors were amazing and the pasta was cooked perfectly al dente. It's been a long time since I wanted more of a dish as much as I wanted more of this dish. It was exceptional. For dessert, we split the German chocolate cake with milk chocolate coconut ice cream. Â Extremely good. I got a cappuccino and my dad got a coffee. Our server was very attentive and the ambiance was just right. I truly look forward to coming back here.

We really enjoyed our brunch at Jane. The food was delicious and the staff was nice. Our waitress kept our cups of coffee and glasses of water full. She made great suggestions for appetizers and dessert. I was able to appreciate her more after we were finished with our food. Why? Because I didn't feel rushed to leave the table--and they were super busy. My party and I were able to enjoy to continue our chat after brunch for a few more minutes. Try Benedict Johnny and their French Toast...Mmmm!! Deliciousness....

Super divey place with an unexpectedly delicious, high quality burger on a paper plate for $7. Beers are cheap and they have McSorley's ale and dark ale for just $3. A great place to eat and drink well on a budget but if you're looking for frills this place has none. If you're sitting in the back, you basically have to give a hairy eye to the server just to get his attention.

Pretty good, but you have to stick to the more traditional pork and hoisin buns than the more adventurous stuff, which I didn't think was that great. There are better buns in NYC but this one isn't bad.

I had dinner with my family at Marietta this past Saturday. It was a last minute second choice since the first restaurant we planned on going to was unable to accommodate our group of 8. Â This was the happiest I've ever been after a rejection. The food was amazing, the salmon dish was one of the best I've had. I sampled some of my nephew's fried chicken which was crispy and delicious. Everyone enjoyed their dish from the steak to the mussels. The atmosphere was great. The old school reggae playing in the background was a nice touch along with the candlelit tables. Makes you feel like you're in a different place and not this quiet unassuming block in Brooklyn.

Love this spot! Â Amazing cocktail menu and wine list (love the Greek Sauv Blanc)! Â Oysters are divine as are the brussels sprouts. Â  Every time we come here we end up having our meal at the bar because we love the setting with the large windows. Â The staff is awesome - great and attentive. Â The bartenders make killer drinks and have time for recommendations even when it's packed. Â  The cocktail of the month club is divine as well - definitely well worth it and great reason to make multiple visits! Â :) Having a personalized concoction stored away for your own private use = amazing!

Sooooo gooooood. Had the seafood pasta special. I had to try hard to be polite to my company by not scarfing down the food. The waiter had a thick Italian accent and was very helpful in making my decision with my meal and wine. This is a nice place, and I will definitely go again. Probably alone next time so I don have to watch my manners.
Great home-style food and wonderful service....Norma A. NYc

I am impressed on my first visit! My friends and I decided to try out this spot for New Years Eve. As most of you know, NYC restaurants are always jam packed on NYE. I walked in (2 minutes) before our reservation. Unfortunately, some of my friends were running late. We immediately were told that if everyone is not on time, we would lose our reservation and would be placed on the waiting list. Luckily, our table was still available after a few minutes. The service was great. Our server, (sorry can't remember her name) was very friendly and was so upbeat. The entire staff was quick to refill our water and sangria's everytime our glasses would run out. Everything was very organized and you can tell that this establishment was run by a professional! Everything was in order. Food came on time and was made to perfection!

Oh my my my my my. La Tarte Flambee. How could you have so little reviews? This might just be the best place on the UES for an afternoon snack, dinner, lunch, or any meal. A combination of pizza and crepe: what could possibly go wrong? It also helps that the service is friendly and they'll explain everything on the menu in an authentic French accent. We got two savory flammies: the top two on the menu which I couldn't pronounce and had to point and nod. After that, we decided to get another mushroom one and add cheese to it. The banana split flambee comes with 2 full dollops of whipped cream and homemade chocolate sauce (or nutella if you ask for it). Thin, crispy crust. Warm, gooey cheese. Heavenly ham and honey. I'm in louvre.

Efficient service, good food and friendly staff. The downside is that prices are higher than you'd expect for Harlem and they don't take credit cards. When you arrive, don't be too scared by the crowd of people waiting outside. They have more seating upstairs, so the wait is usually pretty short. It seems that they seat parties of 3-4 faster than parties of 2. Service is extremely efficient; they had water, utensils, and complimentary cornbread (which was hot and fluffy) on the table . We got the honey fried chicken, which was absolutely smothered in honey and may be too sweet for some people. The collard greens were very tasty and the mac & cheese was good, but not overly impressive. We also got a waffle, which was good, but a bit expensive at $8.

My girlfriend and I went here for Valentine's day and it was an excellent experience. I would highly recommend it to anyone else (for v-day or any other day). Let me start by describing the space. The main dining room is in what feels like an industrial garage that is mostly unfinished. This may sound unappealing but it the way it is presented is actually very comfortable and sexy. The "australiasian" menu is very interesting, and the dishes themselves do not dissappoint. I ordered the Wild Boar (something I had never had nor seen before) and it was very good (tasted like kind of a cross between beef and pork, which makes sense). On Valentines day, they had hundreds of candles all over the restarant, and they gave us a CD with all of the songs that were playing that night (very nice). I want to go back in the summer, becuase it looked like the 'garage door' on the main dining room opened up. That would make it even better. You should check it out.

Great price on dumplings if you want to get full without spending too much money. The fried pork and chive dumplings are tasty. They're not my favorite, but they're cheap. I even bought the frozen pack of 50 to take home and cook on nights when I don't really have time to cook. It's definitely a bargain.

I went back for breakfast, and we were the first ones in. Oh my goodness. The brunch is so good; I decided to go for Southern fare and had the beignets and the cheese grits. The beignets beat the one's in Cafe Du Monde ANYDAY. They don't look like carnival food and are very hearty. The grits? Wow. I've had grits in Charleston, Savannah, and Atlanta, and these definitely do compare. They are quite possibly better. Little Owl will never disappoint. Never.

Very good barbecue. In the winter, there's limited seating inside and can feel a bit cramped. In the summer, there's outdoor seating but more patrons. Ribs are great. The moist brisket is slightly better at Hill Country.

Convenient healthy Korean food to-go or dine-in alone. I love their buffet to eat at the spot and then buying take-home bento boxes afterwards, like bibimpbap and chicken. Pricing point is simply unbeatable. All bento boxes come with soup and rice. Tons of fresh rice cakes (The rainbow flavor is the classic, but the pumpkin flavor was omg so good.) Woorjip is awesome. This is one of a kind- I have immense appreciation for its existence to us lazy office workers.

Love the ambiance. We sat upstairs on the balcony and it felt like I was in some sort of intimate library. Perfect romantic date spot. The menu is really extensive and varied. We had a hard time picking from all the choices so we asked for some recommendations and the waiter was very helpful. I was a big fan of the squid ink paella and braised short rib of beef. It's on the pricier side compared to other tapas restaurants but the service, food and decor justify the price.

Must haves: pollo al forno and insalata cavolo (best kale salad ever)!! The chicken is tender and the chicken skin + sauce is so tasty! The risotto frutti di mare pasta was pretty delish too. The place has an open kitchen which is pretty cool - if you get seated in the back area you can watch as the chefs prepare the dishes. The service here is excellent even when they are busy and staff is friendly - definite plus in my book. Once I came on a Sunday night around 7pm and had to wait around 40 minutes for a table, and another time I went around 6pm on a Thursday and there was no wait. Definitely come with reservations or come during the weekday to avoid waiting. Lastly, did I mention this place has the cutest logo of a shaggy dog?

Was funnelled into this place before a Letterman taping by the staff. Didn't really appreciate that, but it did seem like a nice place. Wasn't my thing -- not a casual enough spot to grab drinks with friends. The lunch (happy hour?) specials didn't look bad at all! Might need to give it a second chance.

We loved introducing Beth to the Moscow Mule. May have been the first one she ever made but it was dang perfect. Leaving a touch of Pittsburgh at the Bettie Bar leaves us feeling all special and stuff. We plan on being a regular for years to come.

I think it's excellent, there's just no room for variety. Once you've had it, you've had it. There's no secret menu (a la in'n'out), there's no monthly specials, its just the 4 permutations of what you can buy. And... that's it. To be clear - those 4 permutations are all excellent. My favorite is the lamb/chicken combo over rice. And, for Jesus' sake, be careful with that red sauce. It will mess up your next day otherwise.

went for it here! we basically ordered everything off the brunch menu and shared it. highlights: cheddar waffles (although the rest of the table weren't that big of fans) hash browns (SO BANGING) scrambles doughnuts best meal award goes to: pecan pie french toast. (lucky for everyone at the table, it really isn't something a person should eat alone so we all got to dig in) low lights: bacon (while i didn't have it, the table was a bit bummed on it, too fatty) pancakes (apparently the recipe is meh, and not very buttermilky) orange juice (tastes fine, but next time put a blindfold on us, so tiny and so expensive) worst part of the meal: the biscuits. yes i said it. they weren't that great in taste AND we found a huge piece of plastic in one. After trying to flag the waiter down for 10 minutes (after the 55 minute wait) he asked if we wanted to send them back.... the wait is bad, the food is delish. make sure someone gets the pecan waffles. seriously.

1. REAL TALK If you don't mind having your conversation casually overheard by the people sitting next to you, then proceed to sit at small cute rectangle table. 2. CORNY You get to select from Oven-baked Wheat, Fried Wheat, or Fried Corn Flour-based Empananas. I prefer the Corn flour empanadas because they have a slightly thicker crunch on the outside. 3. HOT POCKETS I tried to avoid any flavor that sounded like it would taste like a hot pocket. That meant no pizza, americano, ham & cheese, or broccoli & cheese for me. 4. TIPSY The medium-pitcher sangria will probably get two people tipsy for $24. We got 8 or 9 glasses from it. We chose the red wine sangria because we thought it'd go along with the mainly savory empanadas. 5. PICKING FAVORITES Fig, caramel, cheese: impressive dessert empanada: A++ Beef Corn-Flour Empanada: original beef flavor is delicious: A Chili Beef: Not just a beef bias, beef is just excellent here: A Brasil: beef, olive, onions, potato: A Chorizo: pork sausage with latin spices: A Cuban: pulled roast pork, ham with mozz cheese, sofrito sauce (pretty good but the arepa is better): B+ Viagra: shrimp, scallop, crab meat: B Reggaetown: pulled roast pork, rice, peas. didn't love the rice in it; B Mushrooms: I usually love mushrooms but this was mushy and didn't do anything for me: C+

Five Leaves is pretty dope. Â Sometimes you walk into a place that is hipster-infested and wonder if it's all for show, and sometimes you walk into a place that is the reason hipsters began to copy the genuine article in the first place. Â Five Leaves falls into the second category. Â The records they have stacked behind the bar are ACTUALLY playing, the tattooed bartenders ACTUALLY know how to mix a drink, and the service is ACTUALLY genuinely friendly and competent. Five Leaves is a fairly small, laid back, relaxing place to go with a date or to catch up with some friends without having to shout over the din - all while eating some truly quality food and quaffing some inventive cocktails. Â There is a bar area that is good for waiting for people but I would recommend trying to get a table if you're eating, since because the area is pretty narrow and you may find yourself being unintentionally brushed against more than a few times as people pass by. Â  I began my night there with a Red Rider (bourbon based with cherries - but check their menu to see the full details - they use some pretty obscure, house-made ingredients in their drinks [Guinness syrup!] which sets them apart from the crowd) and the Devils on Horseback served with a tangy mustard (Sweet/Savory/Spicy = delicious). Â Since it was a cold night and I'd be walking to the Brewery for Storyteller Night, I decided to go with their hearty Shepherd's Pie. Â Although it came out piping hot (shepherds must have mouths lined with asbestos), after breaking the mashed potato topping with my fork and the homey semi-spicy, semi-sweet smell wafted up, I decided the risk of 2nd degree burns in my mouth were worth it and dug right in. Â The ground-lamb they used was cooked perfectly and matched well with the sweeter vegetables - the proportions of ingredients was perfect. Â For a guy who rarely finishes his entire plate, I faced this belly-busting-dish head on - not because of some inner machismo (ok, well maybe a little) but because this was SO damn good! Â  I understand they also have a pretty banging brunch.

Absolutely love the brisket..tender and juicy, falls apart with a fork..Portion look small but it fills me up.. The 'homemade' bottled ginger ale is absolutely delicious.. I never get a sandwich.. never waste calories or empty tummy filler on bread. Never use the sauce.. My one 'gripe'.. not enough cukes and coleslaw..

I feel like Lombardi's is one of those places, kind of like Ippudo and Shake Shack, that suffer from waytoomuchfuckinghype syndrome. This is usually characterized by justifiably good food, but a disproportionately long wait due to tourists who have ZOMG seen it on __(insert food-related TV program)__ or OMFG read about it in __(insert magazine name)__ or !!!!!! heard about it from a __(insert social or familial connection)__ and are soooooooo stoked to have their authentic New York pizza experience!! Fuck that. The pizza here is good--as everyone else has said, it has a just slightly charred thin crust that is the right amount of chewiness. They let you pick your own toppings and will gladly do a half/half pizza for you. Service is nothing exceptionally good or horrendous, and seating is better on the ground floor over the basement. It's got the whole New Yorky exposed brick really warm lighting thing going on, but something about it doesn't quite match up to the ambience of lets say Minetta Tavern (which is also hyped but I'll give credit to for having a nice, more authentic New Yorky feel to it). I guess the hoards of shopped-out tourists diminish the feeling of this place a bit. And the wait doesn't help. But I'm still giving this four stars for actually pretty good pizza and sentimental value, because this is the first legit restaurant I went to for dinner the first summer I spent in New York, after almost getting arrested for piggybacking in the subway (long story) and blatantly ignoring the undercover cop whom I assumed to be a drug dealer and then charming my way out of trouble with my gorgeous Dutch friend (who was 16) and learning for the first time how convenient it is to be a girl in New York. Oh and this was also when I was seventeen and poor/spent all my money on clothes and not food. Oh how times have changed.

They blow away all the competition in the West Village. For the price of two L'Artusi fried eggs, you can instead order Piccolo's Steak Pizzaiola and be blown away by the incredible flavors. Skip the unsatisfying Frankie's Spuntino sauce and order Piccolo's lobster cannoli a la vodka instead - then you'll realize the difference between tasty and bland. Hands down, the best Italian joint in the West Village. The atmosphere is welcoming. The pastas are delicious. The house wine flows. No frills. Just perfect food.

I really enjoyed my meal here. Everyone in our decent-sized group had something different and not a single one of us left disappointed. I had the Trancio di Salmone, and although the salmon was nice, it was the roasted brussel sprouts that really stood out. My daughter had the Galletto al Forno (chicken over green beans and cous cous in a broth), and because she's only five I was lucky enough to be able to nibble off her plate as well. I thought the chicken was great and I perhaps enjoyed it even more than my salmon. The meat was juicy and the skin was nice and crisp, just the way I like it. Others at our table went with the Peperoni Ripieni (meat-stuffed peppers), the Porterhouse (served medium-rare and cooked to perfection), Sable fish (a daily special), and the Sinfonia di Paste (three daily pasta preparations). And as I mentioned before, I didn't hear a negative thing about a single dish. Perhaps the lone improvement could have been with the free items served when you initially sit - namely the bread. Both types could have been better, although the dipping sauce was very enjoyable and the assortment of olives that they served were all quite good. The space is large and kind of crazy, but the service was attentive and friendly. I wouldn't hesitate to go back.

You know at my age I shouldn't be eating two dinners a night or having a huge snack at 2 in the am....but it's NY so F it!!! These halal carts are everywhere but this particular one has a boat load of good reviews, it was next to my hotel and like of 5 my yelp friends all reviewed it. Â This was my 1st halal cart experience and my wife and I went back 4 out of 7 nights in NY. Â Sooo good. The lamb & chicken pita for $6 is the cheapest most satisfying meal you're going to find over here. Â Who knows how this stuff tastes in the sobering light of daytime but I don't care...I'm on vacation in NY and I'm gonna grind this stuff like I'm on death row!!

Wow. This place is truly delicious and fresh. I've been there twice with my boyfriend and, each time, we have marveled at the unique selection of fish (tilefish, bluefish, etc.) and not just that, but also the creative concoctions upon which they are served. The chef clearly puts one-of-a-kind thought into his masterpieces. Oh, and the spreads served with the bread before dinner (pate, French butter, etc.) -- awesome. Ambience - check! It's adorable and has that cozy B&B feeling. Dessert - we've only had one, but it (bread pudding) was amazing. The service is delightful (except ONE time that I was starving and it seemed like an eternity until the bread arrived), but the pro's definitely outweigh the cons by a long-shot. I will be back over and over again.

This is a most stop and eating destination. Make sure you come here on an empty stomach because there is so much to try. I wish there was a place like this by us in Los Angeles. It is a warehouse of nothing put amazing Italy goods, coffee, groceries, places to eat The kicker for that day, Mario Batali happen to be there for Â a book signing

Having been a longtime customer of Joe's, I felt I've had enough meals there over the years to notice a downward trend. the chef who makes the soup dumplings must have left recently (within the past 2 years) because the flavor of the broth and the wrapper of the dumplings are significantly different. The wrapper texture is now thicker and puckers more out of the steamer. And the crab meat dumplings -- something is seriously wrong with it. Not even the vinegar and ginger could save it. In our most recent meal, we got the subgum rice cakes. It was OK -- not much different from any of the other Shanghai places in Chinatown or Flushing. I agree with other reviewers: The Joe's in Flushing is about 25% percent better. At least I don't have to share tables or get charged an automatic 15% tip there.

At first their $18 lunch "special" didn't seem like such an awesome deal, but then I remembered I was in NY. Â And yes, $18 for lunch is a deal in The Big Apple. It did turn out to be quite a bit of food... A falafel sandwich Side of hummus served with a basket of soft pita bread And some pretty uh-mazing french fries I gobbled it all up since, afterall, I'm eating for 2 these days. The service was attentive and speedy- there was even time for a dessert stop at Pinkberry before heading back to work. Perhaps this wouldn't be a deal back in Chicago, but it was a pretty special NY lunch!

Had Lombardi's for the first time last week, and that it was good. Not great, but good. The pizza seemed a little bit undercooked, so maybe that was the issue. A lot of flavor and great sauce, but the crust was a little gummy. I'll definitely try it again, and maybe ask for the crust to be well done.

LOVE everything about this place. The decor is cool, the prices are right and the food is excellent! The only drink I've had there is the lychee Mojito but it's awesome and I really have no interest in ordering anything else. The tuna tar tar is probably my favorite appetizer, so good & only $7? Every time I visit nyc, I'll definitely be stopping by room service :)
Grandma's slice is amazing. Great little place. Very friendly. Tomato basil and Cheesecake were very good also. Actual location is between 7th and 8th on 46th.

Margon is a special little cuban kitchen in midtown packed during lunch hour with midtowners in the know, but they don't serve dinner. The food is tremendous if you like cuban specialties like roasted pig, fried yuca, seasoned fish or steak and of course rice and beans. The cuban coffee is both extremely good and extremely strong, which is a perfect way to end the meal before shuttling back to work. Don't let the extremely casual, almost fast food decor fool you. This is one of the great lunch restaurant treasures in midtown.

Unknown passerby in front of Meatball shop: Do these guys have good food? Me coming out of the shop: They sell mysterious orbs of meat made from a central kitchen in Brooklyn. They also offer various market sides and desserts! Passerby: Hmm, well I need to feed a few of my friends some decent food for not mucho dinero. Me: Ahh then perhaps this place will please your friends. *hands over a menu* Take this object but beware it comes with a lot of hype. The food is bland, tastes mushy, does not hold up a candle to most Nonna's and is often served lukewarm. And, the service well, it can come across as haphazard and rushed during the worst of times. Passerby: Oooh! That's bad. Me: But you can get outta there without spending too much and it's a known crowd pleaser for most folks. Passerby: That's good! Me: But the waits can stretch upwards of an hour on most days..... Passerby: :( That's bad. Me: However, they have several locations spread across the city now so you don't have to constrain yourself to this location! Passerby: That's good.... Me: But I'd only eat here on a whim with a group that's easily pleased. Passerby: O_O Me: That's okay. You could do worse; It's just pleasingly mediocre that's all. youtube.com/watch?v=r_pqâ€¦

The pizza was great. The staff was very nice but not super attentive. In all fairness I Â came here with a large group on a busy night. Everything was great except we did have to keep stopping the waiter to ask for things. They could have definitely benefited from having another waiter working. They forgot to bring us the second to bottle of wine we ordered. It wasn't a big issue just something to note. I had a great meal and enjoyable evening otherwise. If you aren't going to be a high maintenance group I think you wouldn't have any problems.

I did a favor for a friend and she wanted to thank me by buying me some dinner. We were in the Union Sqaure area and after a short walk we ended up at this adorable little place. It was a tuesday night and we were seated in the very busy patio area. Since the wine was half price we started with a bottle of wine. My sugar mama suggested I get the mussels but i ignored her and went for the salad. It was warm out. I didnt want to be drenched in sweat because wine makes me hot (twss) and a hot pot of mussels would surely melt me. I ordered a salad. a HUGH JASS salad. It was amazing. There was bacon in it. What isnt amazing with bacon??? and Im not much of a salad girl... so for me to love this salad was a big deal. Then we had a great idea. we split the salad AND the mussels with white wine sauce. It was great. I was really grateful for the meal and will def go back (if i can avoid he ridic wait time!) The location in tribeca is my GO TO P.A. Go on Mussels night!!!! (the rattatouie ones are my fave)

This place is great. It's fresh food and a lot of it. Definitely recommend going with at LEAST 3 people. Â The lemon potatoes are a must try as are the grilled octopus for appetizer. Â Don't let their freshly baked bread ruin your appetite and be sure to get there are least 30 mins before you intend to eat because there is always a wait. Â This is a must go to with out of town guests!

I really enjoy Rucola. Â I have been 6 or 7 times to date and have always enjoyed my time there. Â The food is pretty outstanding - always fresh and well prepared. The standouts for me have been the fish dishes, the duck and the home made rigatoni is amazing. Â All the appetizers are great for sharing and I particularly like the fresh summer salad and the heirloom tomatoe salad. A great place to eat dinner with a small group of friends!

One of my favorite restaurants in the city, and didn't hurt that it's one block from my former apartment on Minetta Street. Burgers are phenomenal, always cooked at perfect temperature, fantastic soft shell crab, innovative dishes. The sauces, whether is be on pasta or over mussels, are something special and i'm always interested in trying a new one. Deserving of a Michelin Star. Go eat here.

Blessed with a 2 hour lunch break during jury duty, I decided to explore the streets of chinatown. Yelp led me to Big Wong, and I was ushered to the "single" table, hilariously filled with other jury duty attendees. Sadly, I wasn't that impressed with the food. I was pressured to get the roasted pork (but I normally don't eat pork). So I got the chicken with mixed vegetables, thinking Chinatown would make a generic dish taste magical and amazing. Well, it tasted like chicken with mixed vegetables... except the sauce tasted more like the gravy you pour on thanksgiving turkey, and the "mixed vegetables" were just spinach. Did I order something wrong? The wonton soup (beef & shrimp) was really good. I didn't order with noodles but I WISH I did. Lots of people around me were also eating steaming yummy looking noodle dishes, which appeared way better than mine. All my food was under $9 and was ordered, served, and cleaned up within 30 minutes.

My girlfriend and I were meeting some friends here on 12/1 and as soon as we walk in, we bump into John Mayer, who was also eating at Freemans that night. Â Unfortunately for us, he got sat immediately, while we had a 2 hour wait. Â Actually there are about 2 different wait lists here which is indicative of the restaurant's popularity. Â  After the star-gazing was over and my girlfriend's panic attack subsided, we sat down at the bar with my friends and ordered a couple of the house cocktails appropriately named.....Freemans. Â The bartender, Frank, could not be any better. Â He's attentive and knows precisely when you need another drink. Â We ordered the artichoke dip to start, which was amazing and the booze started flowing; then onto the house-made hunter sausage with beer braised cabbage & prune stout mustard. Â The girlfriend got the roasted beet & apple salad with watercress and Riesling dressing, both of which were outstanding. Â We ordered a bottle of syrah, which was amazing and well priced. Â  We both ordered the seared filet with sweet & sour onions, mashed potatoes and horse radish cream. Â I should have mentioned that we just got too hungry to wait for a table and sat at the bar in the corner. Â If we hadn't been in the corner, it would've been to overwhelming to eat and deal with other customers ordering drinks over your shoulder since the bar is pretty small. Â  Overall the food was a 3.5/5 and the atmosphere, bartender and drinks give it an extra .5. Â  Enjoy
very nice, amazing
The Popeye Delight falafel is amazing as is their mint lemonade. It gets very busy here during lunch I recommend take out.

This is by far one of the best restaurants I have been to in recent memory. A close friend and I went to Piora based on rave reviews from both friends and Eater magazine (currently the hottest restaurant in NYC). We were not let down! After we ordered our first drinks, the Leaves Falling (not on the website, gin, calvados, apple, maple syrup, tea and lemon) was my choice. It tasted like fall. DELICIOUS. Get in my mouth! My friend ordered Wear and Tear, a twist on an old-fashioned, made with rye, aperol, chartreuse, cinzano and angostura. The chef brought out an interesting amuse. It was made with infused apples and something else. Tasty and refreshing. Based off of the reviews and recommendations, we started with the Monkey Bread. How do you not order warm, buttery, salty bread with delicious buttery spreads? It is served with whipped lardo (fancy term for pork fat) and seaweed butter. For our entree, we split the Bucatini (made with squid ink and black garlic and topped with crab), the Duck (absolutely divine, the breast was cooked perfectly), and the Halibut (perfectly cooked as well!). We each ordered a glass of wine with our meal. I got the Veltliner (a dry, crisp white) and my friend got the Burgundy). I should mention that our server, Elle, was fantastic! She was very knowledgeable and sweet. The owner, Simon, came by to check on us. I mentioned that they carried a whisky that I love, Brenne. This led to a discussion that we were both MBA students but wanted to enjoy a lovely dinner. When we ordered our desserts, I noticed that two came! Elle shared that Simon gave us a complimentary chocolate raspberry tarte (fantastic!) in addition to the ice cream (chocolate, salted caramel (the best!) and vanilla) that we ordered. My friend also ordered a glass of Port. Before we left, I was introduced to Kyle, the Sommelier. It was nice to have a conversation with him, as we hope to have a school event at the restaurant. Piora is clearly not a "cheap" place, but I would offer that it is an incredible value for the quality of drinks, quality/size of portions and the incredible level of service. Between each course, the service team cleaned the table and constantly refilled our water glasses. I never had to ask for anything. This is rare, even in restaurants where plates are $20+. I HIGHLY recommend stopping by Piora, especially before it becomes impossible to get a table. They take reservations, so get it while you can!

My husband and I took a bus in from New Jersey and we hustled, as fast as we could, over to Tony's. We'd never been here before but his best friend, a native New Yorker, reccommended this place. We decided to share a baked Ziti and almost hurt ourselves trying to finish it off! I've been to Italy and ate everything I could while I was there. My grandmother is Italian and I NEVER pass up the chance to eat her food, but I have to admit, this was one of my best meals ever, simple as it was. The flavors came together in a way that made me sad that we couldn't finish it off. Like with other restaurants on our tip back east I was upset that it'll probably be a few years before I can eat that again. Overall, the service was great, we didn't feel out of place in our grungy tourist clothes and we got our food quickly.

Awesome place, it's a once a week treat my coworkers and I look forward to. My personal favorite is the fried pork chop special with moro rice and beans though the consensus favorite seems to be the breaded chicken. Make sure you ask for lots and lots of GREEN SAUCE. It's magic. Also the guava cheese patties are great to top off meal.

Chelsea neighborhood stalwart doling out good breakfast/brunch to neighborhood regulars, visitors, and sundry lady groups. It was already packed at 11 am on the weekend (that's when it opens!). If you want a seat on the sidewalk, come earlier. Typical cafe/bistro fare, good service, and atmospheric in that older French cafe mold of a place like Bar Tabac in Brooklyn. It's pretty bright and unpretentious. Seating is fairly close together. The breakfast dishes are pretty simple (we had an omelette and a poached egg with goat cheese, respectively), though there is a penchant for ratatouille here--you can get find it in several dishes. Good way to get the weekend started. To boot, a couple of nice girls from out-of-town gave us their partially used Metro Cards on the way out.

Have been here a number of times already and it has become one of our favorite spots in the neighborhood. First of all, the staff is very friendly and accommodating. Â Have been there with a bunch of friends (6 adults), 2 toddlers and an infant, and they were able to sit us all comfortably. Â They also have a goodie bag for kids with crayons, little planes and toys (which I feel the adults enjoyed even more than the kids). Really like the decor, a bistro with a retro, soccer theme to it. The menu is not too ample, but it is solid and the food is fresh and tasty. Â The appetizers are really nice (loved the ceviche and the morcilla with avocado) bur maybe a bit on the small side, but then, if you are going to order a sandwich, you don't really need too much of a appetizer, as the sandwiches are huge. Â We have ordered different sandwiches and they are all fresh, delicious and come with a side of either French fries, salad or Israeli cous-cous. Â As I mentioned, the sandwiches are huge and I always end up bringing home half of mine (not a complaint!! just a comment). As far as desserts go, the flan is creamy and rich and we also had the maple ice cream, which was delicious. Right now they are open only for dinner (and until late!!),but they will be opening for breakfast, brunch and lunch soon. Really hope that they keep up with the quality, prices and friendliness.

Went here for brunch with high anticipations considering the reviews this place garners. The setting is a bit railroad-esque with I believe, a bit more spacious area in the back. Considering this was the first time having Filipino food, I wasn't quite sure what was good (probably why I left not as satisfied as I would have liked). Unfortunately, the meal itself was not very memorable at all and the only thing that stuck with me was the odd banana ketchup condiment that is on every table. I did see a good amount of other diners ordering a sizzling rice dish (for brunch?) that seemed popular though.

This place is turning into a weekly pleasure for me and my wife. Â It reminds me of my mom's home cooking that I can have daily if I wanted. Â The food is excellent, with plenty of selection and variety. Â The price is very reasonable and I was very satisfied with the amount of food. Â In their Teishoku, you order a main dish which comes with rice, pickles, soup and egg custard, all of which are delicious. Â  The chawan-mushi (egg custard) is cooked perfectly and is excellent. Â So far we've been there the past two weekends for lunch and plan to go this weekend as well. Â My only gripe is that we went late for lunch and they ran out of most of their desserts - but I guess that's a reason to get there early!

Best burgers we have found. A Â completely non-discript bar but fantastic burgers ( even the veggie burger is good) and the onion rings and blue cheese wedge are also a must. We have spoken to the owner, he gets best ingredients from different place s ( Ie: pickles for LES, burgers from Tom Kats etc) and the effort shows.

**Disclaimer** I just returned from brunch at Calle Ocho ...so if the following makes zero sense...it's becauase I am a bit intoxicated;) So I decided to throw caution to the wind and attempt the unthinkable...brunch at calle ocho WITHOUT a reservation....with FOUR people...crazy? Yes, I know...but that's how I roll... So here's the secret, and yes, I might regret sharing this in the morning, but something tells me with this buzz it's not the only thing I will regret... So, the bar is first some, first served...so, If you go early..I'm talking 11:30, they will let Â you in to snag a table. They do not open until noon, so, you will sit... and you will wait but ALL U CAN DRINK... it's worth it.... The food is okay, I mean, it's brunch, and I never really expect much out of a brunch, what I expect is a full glass of the hair of the dog...and something to soak it all up...lets jut say they delivered!! The sangria bar alone is worth the visit, self serve, 8 kinds= GOOD TIMES. And the basket of bread to kick things off is, how should I say...fan-freakin-tastc....I have no idea what the culinary word for these little bits of heaven are, but I can tell you that I have never been more excited about a piece of bread...ever... Why not five stars? Well, I wasn;t as excited about the rest of the menu as the bread, and I am a bit drunk so I am trying to avoid the inevitable "I love you man" feeling that comes with the buzz!! In conclusion, GO! Make a rezzie of you have the option, if not, take one for the team and show up early for a bar table..oh yeah...and don't plan on being productive after....that would just ruin everything....;)
This place is great, best soup dumplings for now. Be careful, they are hot, and you might burn your lips. Also like the beef lo mein as well.

This place has been on my radar for some time. So when my boyfriend and I flew back to NY one night and trying to figure out dinner plans, I immediately suggested Applewood since it's so close to where we live. What I liked about the food was that you can order small plates or entrees. The small plates can be appetizers or you can order 2 and make it to a meal - which is exactly what I did. I ordered the grilled octopus with microgreens and Garlic scapes with pork belly topped with a poached egg. My boyfriend got the fluke entree dish. My dishes were definitely on the lighter side but did not skim out on the flavor . My boyfriend's dish was a little more substantial with the beans and grilled vegetables. If I were to dine again at Applewood, I would definitely keep to the small plates and try all of them!

I loved, loved, loved dinner at Salt & Fat. This is a hidden treasure. Every dish was inspired and well executed. We ordered the shaved foie, and I was impressed by how the components of the dish fit together and the quality of the ingredients... It had the most delicious mandarin orange I've ever tasted! The pork trotter was fantastic as was the Artic char. I really loved the Rice Krispies dessert... Fun take on a childhood favorite! I would absolutely recommend this restaurant to adventurous eaters... Nothing is ordinary and everything is delicious!

Solid 4 Stars--no doubt. I always get their burritos (shocking, I know) and I am never disappointed. Â I wouldn't recommend going here if you are in the mood for Mexican, because it is a far cry from authentic cuisine, but it is super yummy. My 2 favorites are the veggie burrito and the grilled chicken burrito. Â Both of them have cucumber, carrot, mesclun and sprouts. The veggie has avocado and vinaigrette, while the chicken has chipotle mayo. Â They are always fresh, and my absolute favorite thing about their chicken is that it tastes like chicken and has the consistency that chicken is supposed to have. No mystery meat here, or VERY convincing mystery meat anyway. They also give you a side of fresh tortilla chips and salsa. The downsides are that the place is tiny, and there are high tops inconveniently placed in the "dining room" which makes it awkward to maneuver even from door to counter. Â Also, they a touch on the pricey side for me, but I guess that's just because I am a Brooklyn girl living in Manhattan's world. Â And finally, their fresh salsa has a lovely flavor that is unnecessarily mauled by spice. Â The heat totally ruins what could easily be light and delicious...yet it doesn't stop me from eating it.... Give it a try, I bet you'll like it. Â I know I'll be back for more.

Love love the quality of the food and the what they stand for. Very pleased with the preparation of the food and how it is served. Excellent wine list for a small joint... and pretty amazing cocktails! Interior setting is very appealing to me for dining it. I do not give five stars out much, but this has earned everyone!

My wife and I were pretty impressed with the ambiance of Bouley when walked in the door. The rest of the night went downhill from there. While the staff was relatively attentive, polite, and friendly, there's simply no excuse for a prix fixe dinner for two taking three and a half hours. It could have bearable if the food was amazing, but every dish was at best boring. We went for thirty minutes at a time with no food other than bread on the table. Add to that the fact that the couple sitting right next to us arrived thirty minutes after we did and finished twenty minutes before us even though they ordered the same seven course meal with wine pairing. Skip this place and head to Le Bernardin.
Order something off every part of the menu -- appetizers, salads, sushi and hot appetizer/entree. SO DELICIOUS. Even save room for some fried ice cream. the wait is daunting

Contrary to its name, there's nothing French or poetic about Verlaine. Actually, despite cushy seating, it reads more like a bar than a lounge. Come here to get a lil toasty on cheap drinks. The lychee martini is not legendary because it's shockingly delicious (it's fine), but more because it's $5 during the generous happy hour, 5-10pm. The mixed drinks are a little weak but served by a friendly bartender. The orangey lighting is annoying. The second time I was here, it was for Miss Puja P's birthday thing. No one had picked up the phone the several times she called beforehand to ask about reserving space for a large group. It worked out okay in the end, since when we informed the initially unhelpful waitress of our unreturned calls, she miraculously found us a few tables fast (stunning feat since it was SO crowded). Verlaine is an easy go-to. Unfortunately, everyone else is thinking the same thing, so it's usually insanely crowded and awful. When it isn't crowded, the space feels a little ragged and depressing (and still unrelentingly orange). I don't dislike Verlaine at all, but if past efforts are any indication, I'm not sure if I'll ever be back in here for longer than it takes to sigh and walk back out.

Saw the recommendation on Thrillist for brunch and decided to give it a try. $26 for sharing plates, entree, bottomless coffee or one of their drinks was well worth it. It's no wonder why it's called "Feast" because there was an ample amount of food. Their "Beery" Mary was good. As the waitress explained, it is more like a michelada, if you're into that. And THAT, I am into! That wasn't my drink though. I ordered the bottomless coffee because it's...bottomless. Sharing plates included zucchini bread, parfait, this watermelon emulsion, crab meat and scones. For the entree, I ordered the smoked salmon and boyfriend ordered the wild mushroom puff pastry and a side of bacon. I never thought I would say this, but they give A LOT of smoked salmon. The bread was nice and crispy and the salmon contrasted well with the beets and added to the absence of the salt on the potatoes. This might have been better as a sharing plate. I tried his mushroom puff pastry and really liked it a lot. Also, the side of bacon came with over 6 pieces of bacon! Not a complaint. However, bacon was more chewy than crispy. Unfortunately, I'm a crispy bacon type of person. In terms of price, quantity, quality and environment, I really do like this place a lot. It's definitely balanced in that aspect and yes, of course they have the Edison light bulbs, mason jars, wood and metal combo going on. Auto win! If I could, I would give it 4.5 stars. By the way, try to come at least by 1PM for brunch. That way, they're not all just cleaning up and preparing to close until dinner and become slower with service.

I discovered this place on a night where they had an awesome one-man band. He sang tons of great covers and the bar was packed and jumping. Was truly surprised. Thought this was more of a sports bar (they have TVs in the booths), but it seems like it's a hybrid. I imagine this bar will be great when football season is back, but for now it's a cool place to meet after work get good beers, steak tidbits and maybe hear the one-man band. I am going back this week.

I mean its pizza right...NO its more then that. Artichoke was a experience. I've never had more unhealtier pizza. 1600 calories per slice !!!. Sure its fattening but how often am i gonna eat this stuff. This pizza was amazing. Soft crush loaded with cheese and god know. But basically loaded with freshness and something to make your taste buds go insane. I'm not a pizza enthusiast but this pizza is amazing, compares to lorenzos in philly

I just go for the bubble (tea) coffee...the iced vietnamese coffee with extra bubbles is amazing! If I'm spending $4.50 I'd take this over a frappuchino anyday. Bubbles are usually pretty good, but on the oversweetened side, so you might want to tell them to hold the sugar until you taste it. My only complaint? They don't have splenda or artificial sweetner, so if you're not a sugar fan there are no options. Small cute place, better for takeout than hangout.

Open face mushroom sandwich and polenta & eggs were delicious! They said wait was 25 mins but we were seated within 5 on a Sunday at 11. Â Politely asked us to move to another table to accommodate party of 8 and gave us free homemade candies as thank you. Def going back!

4 stars for brunch.... I checked out this place after a friend spotted the restaurant featured in one of dailycandy's weekend updates for brunch. the location of almond has been home to many restaurants over the few years. Â seems like a great location but the tenant turnover seems to be historically high! Â  the host was very nice- seated me and got my drink order. Â the ambiance and decor is very nice and they played classical music! Â so if you are a classical music geek like myself, you'll enjoy your time there! Â they played mostly music from boroque and classical periods.... ok so they bring out these hot rolls/biscuits....SO GOOD. Â they give you 3 different types of butter- whipped, honey and apple butter. Â oh the bread is so yummy!!!! Â  the entrees on the brunch menu er on the pricier side ($14-$16). Â we ordered the following: Almond Hash duck confit, roasted onions, potatoes, duck cracklings, poached egg w/ a side of toast: Â YUMMY. Â a bit salty...but scrumptious!! Â  Special omelette of the day: Â i forgot what was in it but i didn't like it too much. Â bc i liked my almond hash better. Service was friendly and attentive and there are hooks around the restaurant to hang your coat! Â I will definitely go back for brunch again!

Even after having a full meal, we had to make room for a snack at pommes frites, a fry haven with perfectly cooked Belgian style fries and a variety of sauces to fit any personality. Our group of four was lucky enough to get in right before the fry rush hour, around 5:30pm and even luckier to score ourselves a table in the closet sized establishment. Deciding on a large order of fries and a side of the eggplant mayo (chef recommended), we took a load of our feet and enjoyed some good conversation over some freshly fried, crispy heaven. As good as the fries are, its really all about the sauce. The eggplant mayo was an unexpected surprise that I would order time and time again. Sounds kind of weird, but just give it a try Â - it won't disappoint.

came on a company dinner, so since everything was free, i was more pleased than before. but really, not stellar food. good food only. not worth the hype or the price, but this time, dinner was decent. - raw oysters: good, 3 stars - pumpkin ravioli: 4 stars - balathazar salad: 2 stars, dressing was gross, no flavor, just oil - monkfish: good, 3 - salmond: good, 3 - choc pot de creme: decent, 2.5, chocolately, served cold. pudding like, maybe i'm not a fan of pudding - creme brulee: 3 - banana tart: 3 service was too quick, always pouncing to take away your food

Shrimp wonton noodle soup and roast pork chow fun. Â Both were pretty good. Â Didn't like that a waiter came to the table and removed all the condiments off the table (while we were in the middle of eating, AND using those same condiments). Â Portions are on the small side, but nevertheless, not a bad meal. Â Don't take out the plastic, because they only accept ca$h...........and they also close at 9 P.M.......no me gusta!
The best Greek in Astoria!

Yes The food is good but not that good when you get sick! If your celiac, or gluten intolorant STAY AWAY!!!! So I made reservations there and I called first to ask if they have gluten free options, they say "yes we do, we also make homemade pasta, and can accommodate allergies!" Clearly they do not know the meaning of allergies!! So I go and dine, I have a salad and then The Â pasta, since the waiter and the person I had called before coming to the restaurant had confirmed "we make gluten free pasta" So I decide so have the pasta..... Ok well immediately after a couples of hours I start feeling sick! Typical reaction of when I ingest gluten. Well Thanks to Hearth, the waiter and the person who answered the phone when I made the reservation Â I've been in bed and and sick all night and day...because I ingested gluten and the ignorance of the staff in not taking serious allergies! So I called the restaurant a day later to check again how they make their gluten free pasta, and I was told, "we make it on the same machine we make our regular pasta" I'm like what?????? I'm confused I called and asked for gluten free and NO ONE including the waiter told me that you make it on same machine, which means cross contamination!!! Wow, they really take it serious here!! Thanks for getting me sick!!! So please read again!!! If your celiac stay away!! IT IS NOT GLUTEN FREE!! Even though they call it gluten free! It is not safe to eat!! They misinterprate the term gluten free without considering people allergie!!!!. And please restaurant read the guidelines to call something gluten free!!! If you call it gluten free then you must know, it's prepared in a separate area where there's no cross contamination!!! Or if you can't do that, call your fake gluten free pasta, rice pasta since its made of rice!!! But please in no circumstance call it gluten free!!! Inform all of your staff!!! You can only call something gluten free if you take precaution not to have cross contamination!!!! Everybody knows that!!! So disappointed!! That's why I keep eating in the same restaurants that take gluten free serious! They are also small restaurant and they make it happen!! It's all about how well informed you are!

i *heart* the meatballs and everything else here! this is one of the places i wish i could bring back with me to san francisco and boy would it do a killing if they had an outpost there! this was the last meal we had during a recent trip to nyc, which was unfortunate because i probably could have been pretty happy with another visit! my boyfriend and i kept it simple, ordering the "everything but the kitchen sink" salad with spicy pork meatballs and classic tomato sauce, 1 slider with the daily special that day (mediterranean lamb--da bomb!) with pesto sauce, a root beer and an ice cream sandwich with the special banana walnut chocolate chip and homemade honey ice cream. everything was ridiculously, ridiculously good. and did i mention the price? so reasonable, even cheap, for the quality of food you get. love! love! love! big props to the staff as well--they forgot to put in our ice cream sandwich order and without any hesitation they comped it for us. extra points for that!

Very disappointed. I had important guest from foreign country and we decided to go to Degustation. First, we got there on time, but we needed to wait almost 1 hour. After we waited for that long they told us to sit in the next sushi restaurant where connected with Degustation inside of the restaurant. We ordered tapas tasting course. One dish is tiny, you can eat with one bite. It took way too long to bring one dish. We seriously fell asleep waiting for next dish comes. we finished dinner after midnight with our reservation was 8:30pm. Â After I told server to bring food quicker, his attitude was not great. He also brought a wrong dish. I was so regret that I picked this restaurant on such an important day. We all exhausted when we leave this restaurant. Taste was ok. Overpriced. I would never come back.

I came here using a Gilt City offer - which consisted of a 4 course prix fixe meal, glass of prosecco, and after dinner drink for two. Â First I have to say there was no attitude when we mentioned the offer, like some other restaurants might give you, which was a relief. First course was a cream of cauliflower soup w Parmesan crisp, and it was AMAZING. Â I'm pretty sure there was some truffle oil on there too. Â Second course was lobster risotto and was pretty good. Â There was something that tasted a bit off in a couple of the bites - I'm not sure if it was the greens or something else - but the rest of Â it was creamy and it came with a decent amount of lobster. Â The next course of lamb chops was small, but very delicious. Â I could have eaten another plate of those to be honest. Â I'm a short girl so overall it was enough food for me, but probably wouldn't be for a larger guy. Â Last course was dessert was a cheesecake spring roll. Â I know what you're thinking - Â fried cheesecake - not anything special. Â But this wasn't your normal dense cheesecake - it was so light and airy and rich all at the same time! Â For our after dinner drinks we were able to pick any cocktail on their cocktail menu - again a pleasant surprise for using an offer of some sort. Now when the bill came they rang up the full amount, added gratuity, and then took off the value of all of the food/drink. Â Personally I have no issue with this because you should be tipping on the full amount anyway, and it actually made it easier for us to calculate tip. Â If you're the type that would take issue with this though - you've been warned. The only "miss" Â was the lobster risotto and it was still pretty good. It still gets 5 stars because 1) service was excellent and 2) it could just be my tastes re: the risotto.
Decor was nice, food wasn't bad, but won't go back!

Just wrote a much longer review which was lost on the yelp app. Â Lucky for me my experience at Friedman's was a billion times better. Â Gotta try the lamb burger - one of the best burgers I've ever had. Â Matzo ball soup, seasoned fries and kale salad were all just incredible. Â And the service was awesome - we got a super friendly and funny waitress and it just rounded out a fantastic meal. Â We are goin back to try the dessert, which sounded great, but we were stuffed. Â A must-go.

This is the real deal. Without a doubt, the best salumeria in Manhattan. Eataly can eff right off. The place is small and there are only a few tables, so if you are in a rush or on your lunch hour, to-go is probably the best option. It's sad that while here earlier today, I realized how completely foreign a real salumeria is to most Americans. Overhead while in line: "I thought paninis were grilled sandwiches? Where are the regular Italian sandwiches? Can I ask for one of these ungrilled?" and "What are those big rice ball things?" Better to learn late than never, I guess! Anyway, on to the food. Get the Marche panini, which is fresh salami, VERY fresh mozz, marinated artichokes and arugula on crusty bread. The combination of the peppery salami and the creamy mozzarella is spot on. Â And the sandwiches are so substantial that you can save half or split with a friend. They also a have a pretty nice selection of other items: cheeses, antipasti and pastas. Yum. Let all of the tourists go to that overpriced, overstuffed, overhyped place near the Flatiron. If you want delicious, fresh and authentic Italian deli in Manhattan, this is the place to go.

things i look for when lunching in midtown: 1. clean restaurant 2. speedy service 3. somewhat healthy food choices 4. deliciously fresh tasting food 5. cheap woorjip meets them all. you have to try the clear noodle with veggie. it's only $3 and is a filling lunch meal. also the try kimbap/chicken combo.. it's $5.50 and will probably last you through tomorrow's lunch as well. my only complaint is there is always TONS of people here at lunch.... its the kind of crowd that has no problem bumping into you Â or cutting you off as you choose your Â meal, slightly annoying but worth it for the good cheap eat.

my first time here and CANNOT STOP RAVING about the generous and courteous waiter and ambience! I ordered the Tunisian Eggs and they were absolutely DELISH- pita cooked to perfection and my friend ordered the Middle Eastern eggs and gobbled the whole thing up. DESSERT WAS ON THE HOUSE. We had the gelato and sorbet combo: bloody orange, vanilla and blackberry cabarnet- so so tasty.Couldn't have been a better brunch. Thank you!
There's Something addictive about the ketchup spaghetti dish. Other great dishes are the pan seared tofu mozzarella dish, and cabbage pork belly

was here for lunch and had the crispy chicken with arugula. i stole some fries from my friends who had the burger. was delicious! nice decor and friendly service. would love to try their dinner one day.

This is my new favorite restaurant in Brooklyn...which is pretty significant since there are some pretty fantastic places in this borough. My friend and I went on a Friday evening around 8pm and were seated immediately. I love the decor of the restaurant, with the bartenders situated behind a long dark bar...dim lighting. It feels like the 1920's prohibition era. I started with the French 75 cocktail - a gin, prosecco and lemon concoction. My friend had the Jack Rose, which was a mix of apple brandy, grenadine and lime juice. Both were excellent. To start we had the fried brussel sprouts....AMAZING. Hands down best brussel sprouts in NYC. 10x better than the infamous sprouts at Momofuku, Dubuque and Brucie. Â They came piled high in a ramekin, tossed in a lemon vinaigrette with capers and TONS of pecorino cheese. I would go back to that place just for those cruciferous morsels. For dinner I had the meatloaf sandwich which was incredible. Perhaps because it was made with duck, making it moist and super flavorful. My friend had the crabcake appetizer for her meal and she said it was just "OK" Dessert- even though we were stuffed we opted to get dessert and chose the Warm Chocolate Cake. Why Rye...why would you even attempt to serve any other dessert at your establishment when you have this gem on your menu! It was the best molten chocolate cake I have ever had. A light as air, gooey chocolate cake topped with a salty caramel sauce and came with pistachio ice cream. Also there were ground of pieces or biscotti or amaretti cookies I think beneath it. The combination of flavors and textures was just awesome. I don't think I could try another dessert there again, knowing that I would be missing out on this! Service was very good. Our waitress was very nice and knowledgeable. I usually don't pay attention to reviews on here which focus on service since I am more interested in the actual food than the people serving it. But our waitress was great so I am just throwing that out there. This is sure to be a place that I will go to often. And until then I will dream about those brusel sprouts and warm chocolate cake.

Me: "I'm going to Room Service for lunch. You want to come?" Coworker: "Uhhh... is that a hotel that charges by the hour?" The name can be slightly misleading, case in point. So what is it? Room Service is a trendy Thai restaurant in Hell's Kitchen on 9th Avenue, NOT a hotel or establishment that gives happy endings. I'm really just reviewing the cheap lunch here since that's the only time of day I get around to this place. Most of the lunch specials are under $10 and you get a really nice bang for your buck. I always get the chicken pad Thai which comes with a choice of appetizer (choices: Crispy Tofu, Vegetable Dumplings, Steamed Chicken & Shrimp Dumplings, Chicken Satay, Spring Rolls, Green Salad With Peanut Sauce Dressing, Fried Chicken & Shrimp Dumplings, Chicken Tom Yum Soup). I've had both the chicken satay and the dumplings as appetizer choices. Try to dine in to take advantage of the pretty scenery. I do so love the giant encased chandelier in the front. If you must do delivery, give it 45 minutes. They take a while. Is it legit Thai? Probably not, but it's a good portion, tasty and easy on the wallet... what else do I need during a weekday work lunch.

Want to get transported to Cuba? Go over to Cuba in NYC, with a reservation of course. We had a party of 10 so reservations were a must. The actual venue isn't that big.. maybe 30-40 people at a time? On the night we went, there was an elderly man rolling cuban cigars in the corner (Though told they were complimentary for dinners, a friend went to pick one up afterwards and was told that tip was required.. a $20 tip. So much for being "complimentary"). We were right next to the live band so yes, while it added to the ambience, a wave of relief came over us when they took their breaks so we could actually hear each other during dinner. While the vegetarian options are limited, we were able to make a family style full meal. We shared the 2 salads, plantains, mushrooms, basically anything that was veg-friendly. There were 6 of sharing. The waiter told us the veg paella was meant for 1 but each easily fed 3 of us because of the sides we had gotten. Oh well. Drinks were amazing. One of the best drinks I had all weekend. The bar tender was shakin' it to the band's music. Very entertaining :) Definitely make reservations and if possible ask for the back room.

My hubby and I stumbled across this little bar on a recent outing to Williamsburg. What a great find! We stopped there before dinner and after. Located a few blocks Â from the Marcy Avenue stop on the J, this cozy little spot is the perfect place to enjoy a libation on a cold winter day. While I only enjoyed Nut Brown Ale's, I did take a peek at the food menu which featured a small selection of comfort food. I'd definitely return.

Came here for a Saturday brunch at 12:30 without a wait for a party of 2. Banana french toast: fantastic! 4 thick french toast halves soaked in caramel syrup with caramelized bananas and a few strawberries. The french toast was very soft with a crispy crust - perfection. The marzipan added a delicious compliment. Overall an excellent entry. My date got the basque scamble (pepperonata, polenta, salsa, avocado puree, chorizo), an interesting cornucopia of different flavors. Bottomline: an excellent brunch, will be returning to try out the dinner.

Oh my goodness! For some reason I have never gotten into Greek cuisine, but after one dinner here, consider me among the converted. This place made me think past feta cheese and gyros and opened up a world of delicate, delicious Greek delicacies. Portions are surprisingly big -- after just two appetizers I was forcing myself to finish my entree. The place is TINY, so get there early (even on a weeknight), because it fills up fast.

Maybe my expectations were too high.. The wait wasn't too long and the hostess/server was super nice. The oysters were good but it was only served with cocktail sauce, no mignonette. The beers were great, I especially like my summer ale that had a hint of dried flowers. As for the food, the octopus salad was just okay. Nothing mind blowing. The clam pasta was garlic city. Maybe even garlic country, and it was good but very one dimensional. My boyfriend got the fish and that was decent as well. Atmosphere is cute and the service was great, just didn't think the food was as awesome as everyone claimed.

With an 8pm reservation, my party was still not seated at 8:45 pm. We told the hostess we were leaving and she shrugged her shoulders. I hear the food is good, but I obviously can't comment on that part. Poor restaurant management, and a disappointing waste of a Friday evening spent waiting to eat.

Went to the bar area, not the restaurant. Great ambience, cozy and really cool vibe. Perfect for a casual date. They have a good happy hour too! The bar menu has a good selection of crostinis, and appetizers. We had some crostinis and meatballs. Everything was delicious and service was great

We ate here as my husband is gluten intolerant and enjoyed a lovely pizza and risotto. Â They have really mastered the bread sticks and the apple pie for dessert was to die for. Â We shared our meals and dessert and it was not overly expensive. The service was friendly and prompt. It was certainly crowded and everyone was sat almost like a school mess table so not the place you would go if you want some privacy and intimacy. The place had some cool music playing in the background. We enjoyed ourselves and our meals! Would definately go back if we lived in New York!

Bay Ridge has its new hipster mecca. It's no surprise the neighborhood is gentrifying, but at some point, the NIMBY's should throw in the towel. Because what they've done with the space is nothing short of amazing and Lock Yard is here to stay! Let's break down the name: Lock Yard. Lock because the space was formerly a neighborhood locksmith. Yard because they have the best backyard in the neighborhood (and perhaps all of South Brooklyn). It has a retractable roof, so it'll be open in the winter too, which is a big plus. As someone who did a fair amount of underage drinking in Bay Ridge years ago, the most welcome addition that Lock Yard brings (other than a touch of class) is its good beer and food selection. It's run by the same owners as Kettle Black and Ho Brah Taco Joint. They don't serve wings at Lock Yard since that's Kettle Black's claim to fame. But their menu is loaded with tons of sausage options. I had the CBR (chicken and broccoli rabe), and it was delicious. Also tried the sweet potato tots, a concept I didn't know existed. Definitely worth trying. I also can't speak enough about how friendly and helpful the staff is. They offered beer recommendations, samples, and joked around with us during their off time. One of the bartenders is a Phillies fan though, but he knew he sucked. They also have trivia night on Wednesdays (with a monthly tournament) and movie night outside on Tuesdays. There is literally no reason not to come here if you're in the neighborhood!
Their non-pork options are incredibly limited. In fact, limited to one soup option. It was just okay.

My favorite new restaurant in NYC, and I sure hope no one finds out because I want it to be "my place." I live in the neighborhood, and Hell's Kitchen badly needed this farm to table locally sourced restaurant to add to its many offerings. It is now the one place I take everyone who visits me because it's that good, and no one has been disappointed. The atmosphere is industrial and Williamsburg / hipster inspired. I love the brunch with fritatas, omelets, and fresh bacon. The drinks also are excellent and substantial. The happy hour cocktails are unique and a good deal. But dinner- wow. Everything I've had here blew me away, and I'll keep coming back for more. The chocolate sundae dessert with homemade vanilla ice cream is basic but perfect. I love everything about The Marshal. You will too. And don't forget to check in on Yelp because you may find a nice surprise.

Waiting in line at Grimaldi's reminded me a bit like the soup nazi experience in Seinfeld, mixed in with some of the Godfather. The older gentleman at the door was strictly business. You get the feeling with him, that it was an honor and privilege to be eating his pizza. If you don't pick up your pizza when they call out your to-go order outside? Fuhgeddaboudit. No pizza for you! Of course, I jest. You get your pizza, he'll just give you a hard time about it, saying the pizza will get cold. Just listen to the man. That first slice I had was absolute pizza bliss. After a half hour of walking across the bridge, then another 45 minutes of waiting outside perspiring profusely in the heat, it was well worth it all. I'm a huge fan of NY-style pizza. I could probably eat it every day. I like my crust thin and crispy and my toppings minimal, even the cheese melted a certain way. That coal-fired brick oven at the back of the kitchen looked like it had been there for hundreds of years. Yet, it looked alive and well, churning out pizzas left and right. I just couldn't understand how people could eat this pizza with a knife and fork. It's all about the fold-and-tuck when eating NY pizza. The menu is simple. Small or large, then choose your toppings for extra. No medium or personal-sized or slices. We ordered 2 smalls and it was enough for 3 hungry people. The crust had that perfectly burnt, smokey flavor, slightly chewy on the inside and crispy on the outside. The wilted basil on top gives the pie a nice hint of flavor. You can taste the fresh mozzarella, melted and gooey, with a slight dairy flavor. Just make sure to eat it fast, as that cheese hardens quickly and becomes a bit chewy and rubbery to digest. The pepperoni were quarter-sized and thicker than the typical big flat ones. My favorite would be the white pizza, sauceless and with garlic. Yes, service is virtually non-existent, but if there's no line, I'll return the next time I'm in the city.

Love this place. Every couple of months I find myself craving their goat cheese tart, hanger steak, and profiteroles so my boyfriend and I bring a bottle of wine from our mini collection. The only problem is that their wine glasses are tiny and not entirely appropriate for Cabernet so don't bother bringing an incredible bottle of wine since you won't be able to enjoy it fully.

I want to start by saying that the main reason for returning here will be the wait staff which is excellent and of course the location. Â On this sunday brunch our food was brought almost instantly and was presented well...the taste was average, nothing to write home about--so staff in front doing their job, staff in back needs some work. Â One pet peeve was we ordred just plain pancakes for our daughter..no frills...and they charged us $17.00, guess we have another place under the pain of Manhattan rents?
really good French place, the best I've had in New York.

Wow! I went for dinner with a group of friends and everything from start to finish was awesome. As an appetizer we had oysters, the charcuterie platter and lamb chops. For our main dishes we had the Black Bass, Skate, Elk and the Porterhouse Chop. Everything was fresh, cooked and seasoned to perfection and accompanied by delicious sauces. All the meats literally melted in your mouth. Dessert didn't disappoint either, we had the Butterscotch and Mascarpone Cheesecake which was to die for. I didn't try any cocktails, because I was having red wine, which by the way, was really good too, but a lot of them sounded very appealing on the menu. Our main server, and everyone else, were attentive, friendly and efficient. Even the bouncer was sweet and funny. The place is small, but the decoration is pretty cool. My only complaint would be the lack of restrooms, there's only one, but if you're having dinner, your server will take you downstairs where there's no line, and you also get to see the kitchen, where all the magic takes place. This is not a cheap restaurant, but given the quality of the food and nice portions, it is absolutely worth it. Being a lounge, I didn't have high expectations for the food, but boy was I wrong! I really can't wait to go back to this amazing place!

My colleague and I randomly Yelped this restaurant for a business meeting. We were seated promptly upon arrival and the waitstaff was attentive to our needs. Very welcoming atmosphere, clean and well-lit. Service was excellent and I appreciated all the little things--putting our sake bottle in a shallow dish of ice, the warm hand towels in the beginning, the humble mannerisms of the waitstaff and the complimentary green tea at the end If you order sashimi or sushi (as I imagine most would) it comes out very quickly. Granted, we were there past peak hours (close to 8:45 pm) but the restaurant was still probably about 80% capacity and quite busy. The portions of sushi, while not voluminous, were generous and delicious. Very appropriately priced for what you get. If ever you are in this neighborhood and would like quality Japanese food at a sit-down place with comfortable ambiance, I would definitely recommend Wajima.

I had the spicy pork with mushroom sauce, and beef ruth spicy sauce sliders. the spicy pork was recommended by some man sitting next to us. but I personally thought the beef with spicy sauce was really flavorful. Â Really good! It was quite small for 3 bucks. this place is definitely recommended though.

Great ramen place - very solid. The chashu has a nice grilled taste to it and is also nice and fatty. Just like in Tokyo. Miso broth is slightly thick but not greasy. The spicy is particularly good, and has a decent kick to it. The noodles really shine! Nice service and the staff are all super friendly.

I had family in town and we met some other family who came to town down here for a nice dinner. Â It exceeded my expectations. Â First of all the place is tiny, yet they accommodated our group of 7 with a smile on their face. Â Plus I had my young daughter with us and that was fine with them too. Â The service was GREAT and the food was DELICIOUS!!! Â Everyone at the table ordered something different, including drinks and we really enjoyed it all. Â I will definitely be back here at some point. Â Plus it's right around the corner from The High Line which is awesome.

This place is amazing. Â The food is always very fresh, and never disappoints. Â They also always have interesting wines and a variety of fresh oysters. Â  One downside is that they have no liquor license, but they have awesome wines and a great rum cake dessert that are absolutely awesome!

I have been looking for a Peruvian restaurant for a while and this is the real deal! I travel quite a bit to Peru for work and have enjoyed Peruvian Cuisine for years and this place definitely didn't disappoint!great atmosphere, huge portions and exquisite flavors of Peru! Highly recommended!

Even if this is true, a bowl of ramen broth should not be ice cold or he should have offered to reheat the dish. Chunky double-fried pieces of potato. Several dipping sauces are available. Â The small size is large enough for one person to feel they've had too many fries. dark, intimate, neighborhoody and friendly. i've only been here for the drinks and appetizers, but they have never failed to disappoint. the best thing about g&g is the atmosphere - it's a small space, the bartenders are always extremely friendly, and the woody/smoky feel to the entire place. My favorite place for bbq hands D! Go with a group so you can order everything on their menu so you can try it all, that's what we did. Brisket was amazing due to the fat/meat distribution. This place has the most mouthwatering, delicious pancakes in Manhattan. Â Unfortunately, due to its popularity, the line is always long and there will always be at least a 45 minute wait. Loved this place! Definitely worth the wait. The pork buns are as good as everyone says, they are DELICIOUS. I got the akamaru modern ramen, which was also amazing.
