Despite the fact that Queens is a hefty hike for me nowadays, I still love visiting the borough because of the sheer culinary diversity that's offered within its borders. I'd heard of Taste Good Malaysian Cuisine in several instances, but it wasn't until recently that I was able to make a visit to the restaurant. It's not a "destination" spot, in the traditional sense of the word; the interior is pretty bare-bones and tables get turned over fairly quickly. But as I'd yet to expand my knowledge of Malaysian cuisine, I was looking forward to making a trip here for dinner. I left the ordering to my two other friends who had been here previously, and in due time, our menus were taken away and the plates started arriving from the kitchen. First, the Roti Canai, an Indian-influenced dish that features a flatbread with a curry sauce on the side. The version at Taste Good has one of the stretchier and denser (albeit more oily) iterations, which makes pulling it apart and dipping it into the curry sauce an even more enjoyable activity. We also got an order of the Hainanese Chicken, a plate that I'm not typically fond of, but is also another signature Malaysian dish. The white meat was very tender and the skin delightfully plump and chewy; the flavor was overall on the milder end, even when submerged in a chili-ginger sauce, so an extra helping of cilantro would have come in handy. The disappointment of the night had to be the Kari Laksa, one of the most lauded dishes at Taste Good. This Singaporean coconut curry noodle soup was impressive at first glance, with an opaque, red-tinted broth and toppings of shrimp, fried tofu, chicken, fish cakes, and bean sprouts. Unfortunately, it didn't carry through on taste thanks to the overabundance of coconut milk that had been added to the broth; even the chewy, perfectly cooked noodles couldn't save the laksa from the heaviness that overpowered any nuance in flavor. It was slightly ameliorated by the Sizzling Bean Curd, a dish featuring blocks of pan-fried tofu served with a thick, gravy-like sauce cooked with ground pork, shrimp, carrots, onions, and scallions. It's a pretty monotonous dish in flavor, in hindsight, but the combination of all the savory ingredients was delicious, especially when paired with a bowl of white rice. I wonder if, over time, the intensity and quality in dishes at Taste Good has declined, especially given the strong positive reviews from earlier years. For the most part, the meal was satisfactory, although the highs and lows were across the board. For those in the area, it's a viable lunch or dinner alternative, especially given the reasonable prices. I'd consider returning to try a different selection of dishes, although given the lengthy trek, it doesn't seem worth making a special trip out for.
I must admit, the pizza was delicious! The service left something to be desired. Maybe we came on a bad day..
Hostess was SO MEAN. My parents were visiting from Tokyo and we had a reso but we were so put off by the attitude of the hostess that we decided not to bother going in.
Yummie. Better than the biriyani cart down the street. Great greasy Cuban sandwich made on dangerous looking equipment. Enjoy!
Great cheeseburger with fries! Struggled to find anywhere to sit and so we ended up standing. Can get very very busy at times.

Mamoun's is the best place for a late-night snack if you've been at a bar in the Village. Â The falafel is so good and SO! cheap. Â The line can be brutal at times, but it's worth it if you want to save $2-$3 off of the typical prices from other similar venues downtown.

Looks like Manhattan just got a new tourist destination. Â Eataly is a mega food market for Italian specialties. Â The selection is WOW but not budget-friendly. Great place! Absolutely gorgeous menu, very original combinations!

Two stars bc I have eaten here before and all was fine, but feel terrible this time around.

We went here for a date night and the experience was absolutely delightful. Â The food was really good from the oysters to the fish entrees. Â The yellow fin tuna and scallops are definitely worth going for. Â Interesting wines, well paired with the dishes. Â Service was impeccable. Â Apart from Le Bernadin, this is the best seafood restaurant I've tried in New York.
Ive been here 2x. The seafood dishes are yummy. The salads are Good. The muddled berry mimosa is delicious!

I had a good time last weekend at Sweet Afton drinking with my friends. I was most impressed by one of the waitresses, who worked really hard to seek out a table for us. She told us that she had just given a check to a specific table so it would be a good time to hover, and we did indeed catch that table! I did not eat any food, though my friends did and thoroughly enjoyed their meals. I only ordered one drink, the Afton Fizz, but I was impressed by it. Quirky and strange, pretty sour, but tasty, I drank it slow to let the flavors last. I look forward to coming back to Sweet Afton in the future - while it was very crowded on Saturday (and surprisingly so because it was still pretty early), I at least know the wait staff looks out for its customers and the drinks are quite tasty!

came in tonight to test run the spot for a work dinner i had planned for next month. Â the staff were uber friendly and amiable. checked in our coats and straight to our table. Â the event manager had booked the table for me. Â  we started with cocktails. Â my brit boss went with a cosmo and the waiter asked if we liked ginger. Â i said why yes i do. Â apparently they have a signature ginger cosmo that no longer is on the menu, but the bartender would make upon request. Â it was delish thought not spicy as i was expecting. Â it's ginger infused vodka, triple sec, and white cranberry juice. the waiter brought us an amuse bouche of a tiny sunchoke and celeriac with a soy marshmellow. Â playful and tasty. started with the scallops which were perfectly seared and more sweet than spicy. Â i had a bit of the lentil salad from my dining companion. Â it was quite a portion for a starter. Â veggies would love it. Â the pecans bring out the nuttiness of the lentils. Â  before the main, we received another amuse bouche of mushroom ceviche on aubergine miso and ginger ponzo sauce. Â the sauce packs a tart punch. Â i had the tofu porcini gnocchi, which was an interesting texture of crispy gnocchi. Â the dashi sauce was packed more heat than i expected. Â my boss had the lamb which looked divine. Â i'm not much of a lamb person, but she seemed to enjoyed to its last morsel. i had the key lime tart for dessert and my boss went for the hokey pokey Â ice cream. Â it's a new zealand treat with honeycomb broken into vanilla ice cream. Â my tart was a nice refreshing end to a delightful meal. Â can't wait for round two in a few weeks. on an event planner view, kim has been a pleasure to work with. Â got back to me quickly and had contracts prepared. Â open to dietary substitutions.

YUM! i came here on a night adventure and was craving asian food on this vacation. I ordered the Shanghai Wonton Noodle Soup and couldn't believe what I got for $5. I got a bowl full of noodles and four huge wontons. The soup was great and I got to tel you, if your soup isn't right, everything else falls down with it. The wonton were a little overcooked for my liking but still good overall.
Delicious. Definitely coming back.

Solid brunch spot. Â I arrived just before noon on a Sunday and didn't have to deal with a ridiculous wait. Â In fact, once my dining companion arrived we were seated within about 10 minutes. I like the look the place; kind of like dining in an old house from last century, it reminded me of something out of Gangs of New York, but without the all the violence, bloodshed, and overacting. Â The only thing bloody around here was my Bloody Mary, which was quite tasty. Â Eggs and grits! Â With origins in Texas, I love me some grits, and these were respectable. Perhaps my only gripe is they pack the tables in tight like sardines. Â I guess I would be left waiting longer for a table if they didn't, but I don't like people all up in my face so early in the day. Do it.

BEST FALAFELS EVER!!!! I am NOT a falafel fan at all. I've had it at multiple locations from Hawaii to Australia and I've always gotten nothing but dried burnt ball of blended up chickpeas. So when my dear friend told me I HAD to try this place, I knew I had to as she's had the same experience as me when it comes to falafels. I"m not sure what she ordered for us to share, but I think it was the trio of falafel platter. they all tasted delicious. and my favorite part was the massive scoop of hummus they offered. Oh do I love my hummus. Everything went so well with each other. Besides the amazing pizza NY had to offer this Hawaii girl, the falafels here came in a very close second. The place is small with bar style seating around the place but it was kept very clean. The servers seemed to be very nice, although I only went there to ask for extra plates and to return my fully demolished plate.

I can see why this restaurant is packed at 6 pm on a Wednesday. My table split a bunch plates so that we could get a taste of everything. I've ranked the dishes from favorite to least favorite. 1) Crab Toast - I can see why everyone raves about this. A must have! 2) Lobster w/Lemon-Chili Vinaigrette - Best lobster I have ever had. Tons of flavor. 3) Cavatelli w/Shrimp - Cooked with these amazing chili breadcrumbs. Complex flavor for a seemingly simple dish. 4) Corn w/Manchego, Jalapeno, Lime - An amazing side dish. So fresh and unique. 5) Peach Cobbler w/Blueberry Ice Cream - The perfect combination of sweet & tart. 6) Chicken & Pork Sausage - The sausage was out of this world. But, it was served on a bed of dressed parsley. It needed actual mixed greens. 7) Baked Halibut w/Summer Squash - Pretty bland. Skip it. 8) Rasberry Linzer Torte - Not what I expected. The torte tasted like gingerbread. Combined with ginger ice cream, I was on ginger overload. Overall, a great experience. We had the food above plus 6 cocktails/wine for a total of $250. Definitely not a place to go for an inxpensive meal.

This place is the epitome of hipster brunch. Yeah, there's long waits, especially if you insist on dining with more than one other person on a weekend. However, it's completely worth it if you don't fall into the category of having to avoid this spot on general principle (I've met 'em). The food is delicious and definitely a few rungs above standard. The coffee is great also. There's a little coffee window if you're just passing by. I have to say, it's rather sensibly priced also: I went here on say a Friday, and to the glossy, huge neon diner by the Metropolitan stop on say a Sunday, and couldn't help but notice how competitive the prices at 5L were and how superior it all really was.

I had the blue cheese tomato quiche. It came with salad and it was delicious. The place is lovely. But what I like the most is the staff. The guy behind the counter is very friendly and smiles all the time.

I've been here a couple of times and to be honest, Lombardi's lost it. Their pizza just isn't the same as it used to be. All the NYC tourists get a kick out of it though...I hate tourists. Anyways, if you want to get amazing, authentic thin crust pizza, I suggest John's Pizzeria on Bleecker street.

The happy hour is really great, I suggest coming for it. But just because it's happy hour doesn't mean it'll be dirt cheap. If you ONLY get meat and booze like we did, you might end up paying over $40 a person still -- of course, you would be totally and deliriously gorged. But that's what happened to us. No regrets... but maybe next time, we will order a rice dish or two to fill us up before we get to the $40/person mark. Get the beef intestines and set yo' grill on fire!!

Yes this place can be a bit pricey but it's definitely a foodie's heaven on earth. Â There's gelato, there's a mini restaurant inside using the fresh ingredients they carry, fresh meat market and seafood market, fresh pasta and sauces, etc. etc. I seriously had ADD walking in here. Â  On my random trip here with my friend we got squid ink pasta, scallops, pasta sauce, speck, and ate gelato while we shopped. Â This place is so adorable and I can be here for awhile just taking in all the gourmet treats. Â Again, yes, it's pricey but it's quality ingredients and a one stop place.

$89 rib eye in communal seating. Really? Not that i was foolish enough to get that. Alas, nothing good can be said. Â Overall just sad. If these people are indeed from the South, they should be ashamed. Â Bland and frozen. Don't bother.

Ok if I ever wind up on death row and they offer me my choice of last meal, please send the chicken liver mousse from Northern Spy. I had the fish which was excellent. Also the beet salad came with beet sorbet which I haven't seen before. I tend to steer clear of French Fries, but the duck fat fries were worth making an exception. However the yogurt dipping sauce was too thin to stick to the fries. The lilett drink was refreshing, but didn't have enough booze to justify the price. All in all a pretty amazing fresh spot, good for taking out of town guests or a special night out.
Best couple of bites of yummy goodness I had all week in NYC.... Seriously! Had the s'more special of the day... Freakishly tasty.

I needed a quick bite to eat between Dr. appointments and this place popped up on the Yelp app. I took a quick gander through the photos and decided to give it a shot. The pictures alone looked too good to pass up As other Yelpers have said, this place is totally unassuming. Â I never would have thought to go in had it not been for their listing on Yelp. Â Right away the 'Smart Duck' caught my eye. Â I love duck, but never have I even dreamed of having it on a sandwich. Â The man at the counter gave me the last push I needed to make my decision. Smoked duck breast, brie AND cornichons... Â Sold! Â When asked if I wanted anything else on it, Â I just asked that he prepare it as he would for himself. I sat down, took the first bite and felt all my cares just melt away. This is the best sandwich I have ever had with it's unique combination of flavors and textures that meld together in perfect harmony. 2o minutes or so later when I found myself back near Lamazou, I was tempted to walk back in just to tell them how great the sandwich was. I decided not to be a stage 5 creeper and just head home to relish in Smart Duck wonder.

Jay-Z goes here. Â Beyonce goes here. Â I go here. Â Need I say more? Yeah, probably. In a quaint Brooklyn neighborhood, Lucali sits amongst residences. Â Early diners line up before the door opens, even though, they have a reservation. Â It's one of those places. Â I didn't have a res for my party of 2wo, but that didn't seem to be a problem. Â But, that was also because we arrived early. Service is good. Â Food is better. Â The menu is scrawled in chalk on the wall, and Lucali's keeps it simple: the usual suspects for toppings. Â The kitchen is wide open and you can see the pizzaiolo's exercising their craft. Â It's dimly lit, wooden everything, only one bathroom, and the restaurant is fairly small. Â  Lucali's is a gem in NYC, unadulterated by the Brooklyn Bridge crossing masses looking for Grimaldi's. Â Luckily, Lucali's is a bit further away for tired tourist legs. Â I would definitely say that Luc's is a great date spot, because it's intimate and surrounding conversation chatter is not too loud. Â There aren't many distractions except the pizza, and hopefully your good looking significant other.

heard the lively crowd and awesome music down the block as i was wandering down orchard with the man-friend. Â if a place is packed after 10pm on a sunday night when everything else on the block is dead, there has to be something good going on inside, right? Â yep. delicious, fun margaritas. Â MF ordered the fresh grapefruit/habanero (half spicy) and grapefruit/jalapeno and they were both quite hot! Â def not for the meek or weak. Â i didn't love the habanero since it was too much fire and not enough taste for my liking but the jalapeno was fantastic and savory, paired with the refreshing sweetness of the grapefruit. Â i want to go back and try the dark ginger mojito. in terms of the drinks and food, what stood out most was the freshness and simplicity of the ingredients. Â the service was amazing, very friendly and unpretentious, and the atmosphere was low-key and intimate, great tunes and asian-inspired decor to go with the name. Â love this spot.
OVERRATED!!! Â OVERPRICED!!! We decided to give it a try because we got a Groupon and the other reviews were good. Will never come back!

Scallops and octopus to die for. Melon with fresh ham was cool, refreshing and delicious. Mixed baby greens salad was wonderful. We shared six oysters that came from both coasts. Â They were fresh, briny and so so good. Service was very attentive. So why not five stars? Really really small portions and very dear pricing. That being said, I would very much recommend Prospect.

When you hear about famous New York pizza you usually don't hear this place mentioned.. but no late night drunken experience in New York would be worse off with a visit here. The artichoke pizza is literally spinach artichoke dip put onto a pizza. Â That's all you need to know; it's rich, creamy, and delicious.

Their broth is extraordinary! Noodles aren't the best I've had...so I'm not huge on the hype. Pork buns are delish, but again, don't think I'd wait too long on line for them. I've had their special once- the squid ink noodles and it was the most delicious ramen I've ever had in my life! If this item were permanently on their menu, THEN I'd be willing to actually wait with all the other ramen-hungry stubborn folks.

This is the best ramen places I've ever been to, including a few in Tokyo. I am a ramen aficionado. it is my favorite dish. The diverse elements that go into the complex taste of ramen have to be balanced well; otherwise, the one element that stands out even slightly will overpower and define the entire dish. In most cases, it's the saltiness that is overpowering (ex. Momofuku Ramen). At Ippudo, they have found the right balance between the noodles, soup, and toppings. only downside is that it's so popular that you will always have a wait.

I've been eating at Pellegrino's for years - a trip to NY includes a trip to Little Italy and Pellegrino's for lunch. I was incredibly disappointed this trip and will not return. I don't enjoy spending $200 for lunch to be treated rudely and as if I don't belong. Particularly in a mostly empty restaurant. To Pellegrino's - if your gnocchi is gummy, maybe you should check the batch made that day instead of telling your patron it's because she's used to frozen gnocchi and fresh gnocchi has a different texture. I've never eaten frozen gnocchi in my life and in fact know what properly made gnocchi should taste like. And I certainly didn't need to hear about my frozen gnocchi palate from the server four times. Food was meh, service was rude and curt. Thank you for encouraging me to branch out and create new NY traditions.
I really enjoy the service and atmosphere here. Like the drinks, they are cheap as well. Try the burger and fries yum! Definitely good times. Thumbs up

Mulligatawny soup-good, light, yellow lentil variety, Mild, fresh Masala dosa with idly-good execution, crispy and delicious, orange-red sauce is something I haven't had before, good for dipping Palak Paneer--fresh spinach, light, tastes more homemade than others (not overly salted or oily), tip: drizzle white sauce on top. Masala tea (Chai)-standard, good for after dinner on a cold day. What to improve: Service was pleasant but a little slow and scattered. Place is pretty new, though. I'll give them the benefit of the doubt. I imagine they'll figure out a more efficient system. Overall: one of the top indian places in Jackson Heights. Deli Heights has the advantage in flavor, but this place has better value...and it has Dosas. Worth routine visits.

Went there a few months ago and the food was excellent. Â This time, just OK. Â Soup dumplings were delicious. Â Pork with garlic sauce was very good. Â Chicken with garlic sauce was just good. Â Son's beef Lo Mein was bland. Â Daughter's Sesame Chicken was huge globs of fried breading surrounding a speck of chicken. Â Bill for 4 was $70, a little pricey for Chinese. Â Also...no liquor license so BYOB. Â Went on a cold night and people are CONSTANTLY opening the door since there are no reservations and it's always packed. Â May seem minor but really unpleasant if you are sitting at the front part of the restaurant.
Loved this place! Went for brunch and had the best French toast I have ever had! Also had the omelette which came with a salad and potatoes, really good as well! Highly recommended

My co-worker highly recommended Salt & Fat, so I decided to take my sister and FiancÃ© for a try one day. Â  The menu is condensed and very limited. Â This means that each dish listed should be fantastic since they only have a handful of dishes to make. And waalaa, YES, the food was, indeed, outstanding! Â We loved the food!!! Â Think a few food items are Korean-inspired. We ordered a few dishes to share amongst the 3 of us: ~Prince Edward Island Mussels (thai oyster dashi, chinese sausage) ~Crispy Pork Trotter (spicy mayo, slow cooked egg, scallion "mu-chim") ~Korean BBQ Wraps (marinated hanger steak, pickled daikon, miso) ~Fried Chicken (pickled daikon, herb ranch) ~Lastly, we had the lovely soft ***Lychee Panna Cotta*** with plum vinegar gastrique, and yuzu buttermilk sorbet A few observations: Unique Nice decor Candlelit dinner Small place Light fixture Has character Menu changes Complementary baconFAT popcorn to start! Soothing base instrumental music playing in the background Noise level is good.. Not overpowering Excellent service. Nice and friendly Finish off with a complementary yogurt smoothie! Worth the wait in every way YUM YUM YUM - I just can't wait to go back to try more of the menu! TIP: NO reservations taken... Arrive early for a table! Note: Parties of 6 or more will be charged 20% graduity.

Salt and Fat feels out of place in the midst of the rumbling trains and take out restaurants in Sunnyside. Â  The menu really falls in line with its name. Â  Bacon fat popcorn as a light snack as we looked through the menu was fantastic. Â  I wanted more and was thinking... why didn't orville redenbacher come up with this one? The menu is simple and reasonably priced. Â  We had . . . Lobster Salad Yellowtail Scallops Braised Pork Belly Tacos BLT Buns Fried Chicken The top 5 i would definitely have again but the Fried Chicken. . . . that was horrible. . . Â seriously... no flavor but the first 5 i would definitely try again. Â  Since the menu is so small i'll try the other half of the menu next time. Service seems slow but this place has a lot of traffic. 3.5 stars... 4 stars if service was better.....

Great place for large groups. Â Make sure you make reservations, otherwise expect a very long wait. Â Very touristy, so it's very casual and loud. Â Family-style eating is great for bringing people together. Â Try their veal dishes. Â If you have a large group, get the large hot appetizer which has a little bit of everything -- an Italian version of a pu pu platter.

This place is a really great local spot, located in the heart of Carroll Gardens. My family and I went last night for dinner after some relatives came into town who are vegetarians and can be tough customers to please. We ordered great wine and were extremely happy with our dishes: the lemon fettuccine with vegetable bolognese, eggplant marinara, meatball sandwich, and the pasta special. All of our meals were delicious: tasty, warm and just what we needed. There were excellent options for the vegetarians among us and everyone left very full and happy. Highly recommend although go early to avoid a line!

Well, you cannot argue with the price:dinner for four came to $110 , including wine and gratuities for a meal of four appys, four entrees and wine. Service was terrific and caring. The con: geez, the noise level was really horrendous!! Impossible not to shout, and for heavens sake, they added music to the mix around ten p.m. Maybe they equate noise with a good time, but it is a serious flaw. Also, tables were so small they gave the four of us a table usually reserved for two. Food was good, not great. The owner is trying sooooooooo hard, so will I. I'll return and try more selections-but NOT on a Saturday night.

The food is good, fresh and with good variety. However, it could pack a greater punch in the spice department. The guac is solid, but if you're looking for an amazing appetizer before your burrito or tacos, get the elote. It's worth every piece of guilt and self loathing that follows, believe me. Where Carino's goes from 3 to 4 stars for me is the service. The staff is willing and able to answer any of your questions about the food, but most importantly the tequila. I learned quite a bit about this spirit by talking to the bartender and trying the tequilas that he suggested. At the end of the night, he had an on-the-house nightcap with us. Couldn't have been a nicer guy.

We went to this place while visiting family in Brooklyn. After nearly 10 miles of walking/shopping this was our last stop of the day and we waited a full hour and a half to be seated in this approximate ten table establishment lit by pillar candles - rustic doesn't even begin to describe it. The aroma as you're sitting outside waiting is torture in itself. The kitchen is completely visible in the darkness with the glory of a woodfire oven. No menus and minimal toppings - simple is better. We ordered two pizzas and a small calzone , which was not small by a longshot. The crust was light as air with a sauce from heaven and the toppings were fresh and delish! The whole experience was likened to a popular speakeasy for foodies. After a certain time they turned away customers for takeout. Â Customers brought their own beer and wine but they served a variety of canned soft-drinks. Obviously I'm a fan and recommend this experience to the masses!

To wait over an hour in line for pizza that can best be described as "meh"? Not worth it. We got half white, have margherita and we weren't particularly pleased with either. On the white side of the pizza, the cheese and garlic congealed into a sort of gluey paste with a similar texture to hardened fluff. Texture aside, the flavor wasn't there either. It was bland and flat. The margherita side was substantially better, but still mediocre. It would have been ok, but the sauce let it down a little. It was just too sweet. It was rich and bold in very good ways, but I couldn't get over the sweetness. It was as if they dumped a cup of sugar into it instead of salt. The crust was the best part. Crunchy on the charred edges, but also had the right amount of chew. The restaurant itself is bustling and brimming to the point of chaos, but not quite. They've definitely done it enough that they are able to stay Â relatively controlled, but barely. Long story short, never gonna be my first choice for pizza.
the pita bread was perfect, everything else needs a lot of work... the service was extremely slow and the food wasn't very good. I'm hoping they'll improve over time.

I went there today but my experience wasn't as Â tasty as i anticipated . I will not come back for the ramen. The ramen I had was the kimchi miso ramen and my son the chicken, both Â broth were bland, not tasty at all ( I didn't eat it , neither my son). However I will go back just for the noodles,pork and service.

I don't care if you're full: get the ricotta and nutella calzone. Just be aware that it'll burn the living lord out of your hard palate if you are too eager. We had 14 people, and the service was still excellent. Our server was very attentive and rather saucy, which worked for her. We got about 10 pizzas for our big group -- I tried the speck (perfectly complemented by arugula) and the fig (awesome if you love salty & sweet together) as well as the tartufata, which was a little oily for my taste, but the truffle flavor was delish. We debated dessert, but I am so glad we gave in, because the dessert calzone was really to die for. I left with confectioner's sugar all over my face and clothes, but I didn't give a hoot because my belly was so, so happy.

Elegantly rustic, gorgeous venue on the bottom floor of the Greenwich hotel. We sat in the open cafÃ© area of the restaurant, where tables spill out onto the sidewalk of a bustling but quaint TriBeCa street corner. With the al fresco vibe and ample people watching opportunities, lunch here on a breezy, mild afternoon was an absolute delight! The 2 of us ordered and shared the following dishes: Scampi ravioli: one of the best pasta dishes I've ever had. The ravioli stuffing is actually whitefish - never had fish-stuffed pasta before, but the fish was so tender and buttery-tasting that I didn't miss the typical cheese stuffing at all. The herbaceous scampi was brimming with fresh calamari and butterflied shrimp, which were cooked to perfect doneness. They weren't rubbery or overcooked in the way scampi tends to be at all, which indicated how fresh the food was. English pea ravioli: slightly more traditional than the preceding ravioli, stuffed with ricotta and a scant pea purÃ©e. Inexplicably, our clueless waitress claimed there was no sauce or garnish on the pasta other than grated lemon zest, but the raviolis were served on top of an oily bed of cream with some marinated roasted tomatoes on top. I think I would've preferred it served her way instead to make the bright springiness of the peas pop. Still a very fresh and tasty pasta dish nonetheless. Broccoli rabe sausage grinder: this sandwich was kind of confusing - it was like a semi-awkward fusion of a classic sausage n pepper hoagie with their ricotta appetizer. I actually didn't eat the sausage because it was so greasy and I was pretty stuffed at that point, but the sandwich bread with just the cheese and the pepper/broccoli rabe sautÃ©e was SO yummy! The bread was great - thin but extremely crispy crust encasing an uber fluffy and soft interior. The ricotta was so sweet and flavorful - I can definitely understand why the appetizer featuring it is so popular! Tip: come during lunch (M-F), when the menu features some of their dinner entrees at a nicely discounted price in addition to some of their standout lunch/brunch-only items. The scampi ravioli in particular, which isn't on the dine menu, is definitely not to be missed. The food here is definitely on the heavier side - the pasta noodle itself is denser, thicker, and chewier than others I've had, and the dishes are quite rich. Still, I found Chef Andrew Carmellini's acclaim to be well-deserved, and between the food's freshness and execution and the lovely ambience of the restaurant, a meal here is certainly worth the indulgence!

On the rare Friday off, my husband and I decided to try something different for lunch. We are usually both in Manhattan, but since we live around the corner, why not? It's a welcoming place: fresh-tasting, healthy-looking food. I have no complaints about the food, though it's a bit pricey for 'prepared' food. Our original plan was to take it home, but the staff, who are friendly, asked if we wanted to eat-in. We decided to do just that - except there were no seats available. We waited for our sandwiches + kale crisps, and it appeared some mothers with their babies and prams were leaving, but they re-adjusted and sat back down. We were offered a table with miniature chairs by the washroom (yuck), which looked like a child's play station. We politely declined and asked to take-away our food. I think the waitstaff were trying to be good hosts, and suggested we wait, but no one was going anywhere, and we were hungry. Perhaps the restaurant should introduce a policy where they can turn the tables over during peak times, especially if people are just sitting there and are long finished with their meals. Â We had to leave with our food (happily so - I prefer my house over a crowded little cafÃ©), when there were people parked at tables not eating. Something to consider, Stocked.
Fun place to spend a day on vacation from Los Angeles! Bartender was patient and friendly with me choosing my beers! Clean bar that I wish I could go back to!

Excellent Brunch place. Â  Came here with a party of 6 and a Gilt City voucher in hand. Â You never know how these vouchers are going to pan out, but this time was nearly flawless. Â We got 3 pitchers of Sangria, which was more than enough for 6 of us. Â It was a nice touch that they put the ice in the glasses instead of the pitcher (giving more bang for the buck). Â The guacamole was good, but interesting. Â Had a different flavor than most guacamole that I've had (maybe adobo and chipotle in it?). Â  I ordered the steak and eggs rancheros (fighting the urge to always order huevos rancheros) which was pretty good. Â The steak was a little tough and cooked a little too long (ordered it "medium") but had good flavor. Â The egg was also cooked a little too long, as I like it to be a little runny in a dish like that. Everybody else enjoyed their dishes. Â The tuna sandwich seemed to be a big hit. Â The service was good, and I liked the look of the place. Â Everyone in my party said I did a good job of picking the place (when all I really did was get a Gilt City email). Â Would definitely come back!

Eataly was an amazing experience. Part market, part cafeteria. (See my pictures) My friends and I ate in the seafood restaurant, Il Pesce. I had the black fish filet on lentils. It was delicious! One friend had the scallops and the other had the smoked trout. Both were just as good. Word of warning, there were no pasta dishes in this restaurant. If you want pasta, you would have to eat at La Pizza & Pasta nearby. The wait was long, but that's to be expected on a Saturday night. I would love to come back here to try more.

Tiny little place that packs a big punch. Great selection of Â oysters and beer. Crab cakes fresh made from Â lump crabmeat were moist and the habanero honey glaze was delish. Â Service was great. Â Our new favorite spot.

Tried this place for the first time y'day for brunch. Really nice atmosphere and decor, nice crowd and I appreciate a place where you're not sitting on top of each other (they're hard to find) and you're seated quickly (10 minutes without reservation for Sunday brunch ... good stuff!) Food was delicious! All the ingredients were clearly super fresh and the egg yolks were the brightest yellow and absolutely delicious (happy chickens=fabulous eggs). It took awhile for our food to come out eventhough the place had thinned down by the time we were seated, so I'd likely steer clear if in a situation where I was pressed for time. Thankfully, we had a lazy afternoon ahead of us so it was nice to sit and chat over coffee. Our waitress was apparently a part of some inergalactic student exchange program as it took us 4 tries to get sugar on our table although she had ample time to just wander around aimlessly. Again, food was great so would definitely come back

This place is awesome! Â New owners, new chef, new menu, all changes for the better. Â Food was delicious, drinks were awesome and innovative (umm, homemade sweet tea with a prosecco topper?? Â yes, please!), wine list was very affordable given the quality of the bottles. Â Can't wait to go back!

Its always crowded here, but luckily I found two open seats at the bar when my mom was in town the other night. Great wines and they will let you taste anything before you buy. We ended up staying until the closed and had such a great time people watching. The bartender Leo is amazing, so welcoming and fun.

No judgment, only regret. This was the solemn vow 5 girls took while looking over the menu. Â  When all was said and done the damage was 8 plates. Â  8 full meals. Â  For five relatively smaller people. Â We promised no judgment from each other, but as I type this I'm realizing -- this was TOTALLY judgment-worthy. Â  We each had our own egg based dish and split the blueberry pancakes, pear vanilla waffles, and sugar cured bacon. Â  Best guaranteed-regret decision ever. Â  This is crack bacon. Â  This is the bacon of your dreams that you think you'll never meet in real life. Â  Sugar and salt were meant to be, and they find a happy conduit in Clinton Street's bacon. Â Amazing. Â End bacon ode. All of the egg dishes pleased -- I had the Spanish scramble, which would rival an egg based creation at any brunch spot. Â The chorizo bits were in each bite. Â I'm starting to think chorizo is as essential an ingredient in breakfast eggs as ketchup and salt & pepper. There was great anticipation over the blueberry pancakes, so it was a no brainer to share an order. Â General consensus was that these were very good pancakes. Â But I have to say the waffles stole the show. Â  Those waffles with golden crispy edges with some kind of poached tart fruit (rhubarb or peaches) had me at first bite. Â I might have moaned a little. Â It was a little gross to type that word out. Â But I can't really describe the inarticulate noises we made as a table upon trying the waffles. Â  I almost forgot - there was some ridiculous maple butter they brought out with the pancakes (or maybe it was the toast) that was addictive. Â They tried taking it away at some point. Â They failed. Â  To be fair I am more of a waffle person than pancakes. Â And really, neither of those because when it comes to brunch, I much prefer eggs. Â  Â Though Clinton St Baking Co is known for its pancakes, it more than satisfied for the egg and waffle lovers. Â  Something for every bruncher here.
Perfectly fried chicken/pork, flavorful curry, great meal. Â Chicken or Katsu Curry are the way to go and a single is a surprisingly large portion.

Pretty good, but nothing great. I have had better in Chinatown. The plus is that it was really cheap. Â Got the lobster ginger and scallion special (2 lobsters for 20$) and that was good. Â The chicken lo mein and the wonton soup Â was ehh... try something else...

The restaurant does not serve the most traditional Thai cuisine but there are many things that make this place endearing. Â First, while the place is pretty small and can be a cramped (but what else is new in NY restaurants), the decor is modern and clean. Â Second, as everyone agrees, the Thai iced tea with the frozen Thai iced tea cubes is quite delectable and the whole presentation of the tea with its milk , syrup and the the cubes is a real eye candy. Â The idea of frozen ice tea cubes is just genius- they preserve the flavor of the tea throughout the meal and are also pretty to look at. Our entrees- green curry and the PCU noodles were tasty and also surprisingly large, considering this place at first glance seem like another one of those frou frou restaurants that serves tiny portions of food. Â The fries with the chili mayo sauce were also very good,,with the mayo sauce not being too spicy and with just the right flavor of tanginess. Â The servers were polite and attentive but were not overbearing. Â On top of all these great qualities, the bill came out to be quite reasonable. Â We left the restaurant pretty happy. Â It satisfies the girl's liking for ambience, presentation, and taste and also makes the ever so practical guy happy with its value and quality.

Japan is the best place to get clean and tasty food Quoted by my British friend who lived in Japan for a couple of years. I got to agree with him. Â I have NOT yet made a trip to there yet, but here and there I have tried Japanese food in the States, and they are absolutely great food. It is sad to see that so many east Asians pretend to be Japanese ones and destroy the authenticity of this fine cuisine. This place is 100% Japanese. Â How do I know? Because of their beautiful yet sleek decor and nice staffs.

Had a late lunch at BXL and was pleasantly surprised. Â The menu is mostly Belgian with a few deviations. Â My companion and I split the mussels in white wine which were plump and juicy and cooked to perfection. Â They came with a large side of crispy fries. For our entree my companion had the burger which said was juicy and cooked perfectly. Â I decided to try an Italian pasta dish, spaghetti carbonara. Â Here is where I have to lodge my only complaint. Â While the pasta was cooked al dente and the portion substantial, Â  The dish lacked flavor and was drowning in too much heavy cream. Â It could also have used some peas, which is the traditional way to make carbonara. Â My criticism may be a bit harsh, but Â I recently returned from Italy where I had outstanding Carbonara. The decor is cute, although a little 50's kitsch, but the service was professional and just friendly enough without being overly familiar, Â  All in all BXL is a welcome addition to Flatiron dining and we will definitely return. Food: Â overall very good Service: good Atmosphere: cozy
3.5 stars. Quality food. Quality drinks. Reasonably priced for the city, but moderately overpriced for what you get. Great location and atmosphere with good but not mind blowing food or drinks.

Joe knows how to make the magic happen. He knows what he's doing. Three beautiful, intellectual women shared a table with me, discussing how their husbands are oh-so-very close to publishing a book. They laugh, they toast to refreshing sesame noodles and delicious soup dumplings- happily giggling while they say, "Sorry I keep squirting on you!" STOP. You are dirty if you thought otherwise. (That's what she said) Joe's a popular guy; ladies, food, beer. Who wouldn't want to be him? He has a line all the time waiting to experience his savory dishes. That pickled cabbage- oh man! Tangy and simple. The portions are just right too. It's more than the amount served for tapas/dim sum, but less than a traditional Chinese restaurant portions. This is awesome because you can try a variety of foods without having to force feed yourself and feel fat when you go shopping after (hint: do not try on clothing after lunch). To give you a better picture, 4 people ordered 8 dishes and the total was roughly $70-80. That's including tax and tip! Joe... You da man.

I wanted to like this place, but they made it hard for me to like it from the moment I stepped inside. Â They sat us in the back garden where we had the heater blowing directly at us, but we were forewarned that it would be hot. Â I hadn't really eaten that day, so I was really looking forward to sitting down and eating a great meal. Â How was I to know that every single dish would have banana or mango in them (I am allergic to both) and that everyone around us would be served and it would take a good 45 minutes for us to get our meals? I had ordered the corn-crusted salmon and my friends had ordered other dishes. Â Yet mine came out a good 10 minutes after they had been served (this is in addition to our 45-minute wait for our food). Â The medium salmon was oddly cooked, with the top half being overcooked and the bottom half was basically sashimi and lacked any kind of flavor. Â The "cilantro mashed potatoes" was not great either, in that it was a weird color of green and basically tasted like mashed potatoes that came out of a box. We were given free flan for sitting at the crappy table in the back; however, even that wasn't very good. Â  I think it might be that Brooklyn hates me, but I'm never coming back to this place.
Great vibe and fantastic food! Â Perfect place to go if you are meeting a few friends for drinks or having dinner with a date. Â Loved it. Â Can't wait to go back.

extra stars for decor, wonderful back patio, koi pond, friendly and fast bartender. Food was good, the guy was in the worst mood ever when I ordered but maybe cheered up by pick up time at the window. the food was good but not nearly as cheap as advertised. I think the prices have gone up substantially from what I see on older reviews, but still good. 2 seafood sammies, 2 cocktails, 2 beers was about $70.
Almost 4 dollars for a taco that could only feed a Keebler Elf. Are you guys serious? Their shakes are good, however.

I've heard a lot of great things about this place from others so I decided to give it a try. Maybe I went on an off-night but I must say that I was slightly underwhelmed with dinner here. Especially considering the $100 cost per person (we each got a couple of drinks too). Don't get me wrong - the space itself and the vibe were both very cool. The food and service, however, were just alright. I definitely expected something better, especially given its association to Top Chef. Some of the better items we ordered were the gnocci, sausage pasta with ricotta, and the JW chicken. The calamari was alright, nothing special. As a heads up, I would avoid the cod. My friend who ordered it essentially noted that it was nothing more than a glorified fishstick. Would I give this place another shot? Maybe. But considering how much money we ended dropping here, I think you can do much better elsewhere.

I'm not usually a fan of Mediterranean, but several friends have been and raved about ilili so I had to see what all of the fuss was about. Dinner was delicious, but the desserts were absolutely amazing. Everyone on staff was friendly and helpful, really taking the time to understand my likes and dislikes before making any recommendations. I've been back several times now and have had the same great experience every time!

I was torn whether I should even write a review because I like this place so much and, selfishly, I almost don't want other people to discover it. But, it's too good to keep all to myself. Best combination of food and drink - seriously, it will redefine how you feel about both beer and grilled cheese. First, as other reviews mention, the bottled beer list is extensive and from countries you never expected to churn out delicious beers. The draft list is usually only 4-5 long, but Â if you're still having trouble deciding ask the waiter/waitress and they'll not only tell you their favorite but let you sample as many as you like. Also, they rotate out their drafts on a weekly basis (maybe even more frequently than that?) so if you like something, get a lot, or go back soon! Second, as an adventurous eater and a cheese lover I was bound to love these grilled cheeses. To date I have had the Gouda sandwich (black bean hummus, guava jam on brioche) and the Fontina (mushrooms on foccacia). Personally, I preferred the Gouda as it was more manageable and the parts blended incredibly well together - and that's saying something because I HATE guava. I have made it my personal mission to try every sandwich on the menu so I'm sure I'll have updates to make! Third, the vibe. Spacious. Wooden tables. Klunky decor. Did I mention SPACIOUS? Fourth, great value! The portions aren't huge but every sandwich comes with a small salad so you're covering all your food groups there. Honestly, if this place was in Manhattan or even WIlliamsburg it would be crowded all the time and at least $5 more per item. It's that good. Overall, great great place to kick back (hence the name?) enjoy a few beers, lighter food, and the company of friends. They're open starting at 7 in the morning and have WiFi available until 6pm so if you're in the area and looking for a good place to study/work in peace come here!

I was in New York for the weekend and this was one of the last meals I had. It was a beautiful day, (hot by my standards, but that's what happens when you live in the Bay Area for 5 years) so we decided to sit outside in the back patio . Food: I got the bluefish cakes that came with Â celery root slaw and poached eggs. She got the shrimp and grits. The bluefish cakes were pretty damn good, flaky and moist. I feel any place that serves bluefish is confident in their cooking and it showed in the food. The celery root slaw successfully balanced the bitterness from the root and the creaminess of the dressing. Poached eggs: perfect. The accompanying hollandaise sauce didn't overpower the dish. Her shrimp and grits was what shrimp and grits should be: satisfying and rich. I've had shrimp and grits probably 3 times in my life, and this was the best of out the 3. Needless to say, I'm not an expert on it but it's a solid choice. Get it on a chilly day, and you won't be disappointed. Service was attentive and friendly. Enough said. Minus 1 star just because for the price, the portions were a tad small. This place is charming in its simplicity. The menu simple and straightforward, the interior decor is understated and tasteful. I like a place that does simple food well. It was a memorable brunch. Lovely neighborhood, lovely food, and Â lovely company.

We had a reservation for two on Friday night. Â We had a bit of a wait for my taste. Â Over 40 minutes spent at the bar for drinks and once we were seated the tables were very CLOSE together. Â I know - its New York and space is limited but I would like to know the person I hit elbows with at dinner. Once the food arrived - solid options. Â We started with the warm goat cheese salad - fantastic fresh mix of greens and pine nuts. Â Followed by the Steak Frites. Â Cooked to perfection and good flavor. Â A bit pricey for salads and steaks, however walking distance in my neighborhood makes it worthwhile. Cons - the wait, overall crowded and prices Pros - the food, location and service.

I held my daughter's baby shower here yesterday and I couldn't be happier with how it turned out. The place looked lovely, there was plenty of waitstaff who were all very nice and efficient, and the food was good. I had the chef bake her cake, and it was delicious! Everyone raved about it. The cost was very reasonable. No one rushed us, even though we were there longer than the agreed upon 2.5 hours. All in all, a great experience.

5 stars for spaghetti - I have inappropriate dreams about this dish. Â So simple yet so amazing. Â Must have crack in it. 3.5 stars for creamy polenta. Been there, done that. 4.5 stars for the bread with the meat and cheese baked into it. Â A meal in itself! 0 stars for the hostesses looking my mom and I up and down (my mom is not in the best of health) and trying to seat us at the drafty small table in the front of the bar room even though we had a reservation. Â  3.25 average rating, which is a shame because the food is worth it, the staff is not.

Delicious AND cheap. Lived in SFfor past 6 years, had great Indian food everywhere. This is the best Indian food I have had so far in NYC and way cheaper than other Indian restaurants with good food. He has great sauces that come with whatever you order. On a sunny day grab some food and then a grassy spot in Washington Square park.
Love the food, the atmosphere, they're always pleasant and you can show up on a Friday night and not have to wait too long. One of my favorite spots for udon!

I'm torn between a three and a four. A four would be for the service, ambiance, and the drinks. But the food was only okay this time. Everyone is going nuts for the elote. While I'm sure if you've never had it fresh from a crappy vendor in East Los Angeles, it's very good, but I've had it fresh from a crappy vendor in East Los Angeles. The sopesitos were hard and not too tasty. I am still giving them a four because we slid in at the end of the night and that could account for the discrepancy from all the fantastic things I've heard from my friends. On another note... damn that daiquiri is strong and delicious! Major plus points!

Love Greek food and also love seafood dishes. Did my research and found this place on Yelp. I was amazed with all the good reviews here and high average star rating. Was expecting a great dinner at Taverna Kyclades. However I was a bit dissapoited with this place. I was surprised with the food, it had no taste or flavor. Worst I had in long time. I couldn't even finish half of my main course. The service was great, the waiters here are nice and professional, and know their menu well. However the food sucks and it is very overpriced. I got: - Octopodi for $18 - Horiatiki salad for $15 - Sea Scallops for $30

Walked by it while visiting Brooklyn and it lured us in. Love the energy in this place. As the sun set, the interior only seemed to get warmer, with their perfect lighting, candles and such. The food is absolutely delicious! We ordered spaghetti with marinara sauce for my friend's five year old son - but this was definitely not your ordinary pasta and sauce. Not the typically the most enthusiastic of eaters, he savored every bite, almost finishing the entire (generous) portion (we helped him! We couldn't help it). We didn't hear a squeak from him the whole time! He was in spaghetti heaven. Also ordered the lovely fennel salad. So fresh. And the Sicilian tuna sandwich - absolutely delectable. Their organic beer hit the spot too!

From the very rude hostess to the mute bartenders who never uttered a sentence to me the entire time I seated in their section at the bar, the horrible service ruined my first and last experience at this restaurant. Â  I don't think the hostess saying "yeah yeah, whatever" and turning your back to a customer while they are speaking to is very professional or inviting! My meal was just ok and with so many other awesome restaurants (Prime Meats, Wing Bar, Clover Club, Frankies, Henry Republic) in the Carroll Gardens/Cobble Hill area (which I've lived in for 3.5 years), I don't feel like I am missing out if I never ate at this restaurant again.

I would give this place 2 thumbs up if my hands weren't so busy eating the free sampler pancakes and cookies Tom's wait staff gave us as we waited in line for a table! The line was out the door for a Saturday morning ~10:30am, but it was relatively quick, around 15 minutes. But the wait went by quick as the service while we were waiting was wonderful. When my company and I got seated, I ordered the Pumpkin Walnut pancakes and my company got an omelette with fries. The first bite of my pancakes was heaven. So fluffy, not too sweet, great texture. I ate my first pancake with ease and euphoria, but I had trouble eating the other 2 pancakes as I couldn't handle the build up of sugar. (Though I think this is just a personal problem of preferring savoury foods in the morning vs. sweet foods, so I'm not blaming this on Tom's at all). My company's fries were really good too. Even though there was a constant line out the door during our meal, I didn't feel rushed at all to finish our food and leave. Great service, great food. Two thumbs up!

Two stars for outside patio. It is great and a nice escape from the hustle and bustle of the city. The food is not tasty at all. We had the calamari which was not crispy. It wasn't soggy but it was like rubber, it was thick and Â hard to chew. The carpaccio was ok but not recommended. Gnocchi or duck breast were not recommended either. To sum up not recommended.

My husband and I made a New Year's Resolution to try all the restaurants on Fulton street. We spotted Prospect and headed in for Sunday brunch. The service was nice, the seating was a bit tight.. but the atmosphere was cozy. He ordered the meatloaf sandwich and I got the Prospect benedict with pork belly!!! His was delicious and moist. He kept saying throughout the meal that it was the best meatloaf he had ever had. Mine was a huge disappointment. I am always sold when I see pork belly, but the small quarter size piece was over cooked and dried out. Also I'm pretty sure there was supposed to be spinach under the eggs, but there was only 2 leaves of arugula. I was raised to not complain about my food, so I tried to be thankful...and then I found a hair in my potatoes.... I glanced up and could see that 3 of the cooks had beards. My mother would be disappointed, I couldn't finish it. Don't get me wrong, I love a man with a beard, just not in my food!

Had serious doubts about this place even before stepping foot in it. A sports bar...in the middle of the theatre district. Being a native NY'er, I was afraid it would be wall-to-wall tourists, however I was pleasantly suprise to see it was it cool hang out, with great bartenders and some pretty good bar food. We made it in right before the happy hour rush and at one point, it was somewhat crowded. Our group kept the drinks following well into the night lol and had some appetizers as well, which were suprisingly good! I didn't even encounter nor did it seem like the place was infested with tourists. I won't be itching to come back here, just cause its your typical, run of the mill sports bar...but it's not as bad as I thought!

Nom nom nom...only one thing to remember to do here, ORDER THE CHICKEN SAUSAGE. I never would have imagined that I'd dream about free basing chicken sausage, but I did...and I would...except that it'd then bypass my taste buds.

Let's start with the end of the evening and work backwards... Check: $65 (!!) Rigatoni with eggplant, mozzarella, tomato and basil - Very good. Fusilli with crumbled sausage and mushroom in a creamy-ish truffle-tasting sauce - Delicious. Mixed organic greans topped with apples and goat cheese - BIG salad, fresh and tasty. Â Generous goat cheese portion. Bottle of Sicilian red wine - Good, especially for the price. Â  Ambiance and staff upon walking in...Warm, welcoming, friendly. I don't know but if you ask me, I wouldn't have expected to find such an affordable and charming place in Chelsea (charming, yes, affordable, no). Â Pepe Giallo is a great find.

What's wrong with Williamsburg - it's places like this. Hipster hell. Pretentious people, douchish bartenders, everyone trying WAY too hard. If you're looking for real people, Brooklyn Ale House is the move. Unless you're a regular at Levee. If you are, please stay there.

After reading all these wonderful reviews and food blog posts on Piora, perhaps I hyped it up too much for myself, because I left feeling, for the most part, rather unimpressed. I made a reservation on Opentable almost a month in advance in order to get a table that wasn't at either 5pm or 9pm. My friend and I ended up coming for dinner at 6:30pm on a Monday night (Veterans Day), and I immediately liked the rustic, yet modern feel of the restaurant. There are a few tables and counters by the door, a hallway that stretches along the bar, and the main dining area in the back. We were seated in the back along the wall, and I absolutely loved the view out the back window of a very vibrant looking garden. To start, we were presented with an amuse-bouche: sunchoke chips with mustard and violet. Interesting combination, and I thought it was delicious. From the menu, my friend and I ordered the monkey bread and the scallop to share as appetizers. The monkey bread was every bit as wonderful as I had read, and well worth the $6. It came out of the kitchen piping hot, and the bread was soft and doughy. It was presented with whipped lardo and seaweed butter on the side. The lardo basically tasted like a fluffy, half-melted butter, and it was delicious with the bread. The seaweed butter was a novel idea, and I enjoyed that as well. The scallop came out soon after our monkey bread. The dish consisted of three scallops presented nicely with sweet corn, a creamy sauce, chanterelles, and crispy chicken skin . I thought the scallops were seared well but not particularly memorable; the sweet corn was better, and the chanterelles were, as my friend put it, "divine" and had a wonderfully rich flavor. I ordered the bucatini as my next course, and this is where my impression started to go downhill. The bucatini - served with garlic, Dungeness crab, maitake mushrooms, scallions, and slivers of red pepper - tasted vaguely like lo mein, and I enjoyed the first few bites. I did find it on the salty side, though. As I started to finish off the noodles and reach the bottom of the bowl, it started to get oilier and oilier until I was left trying to get the last few pieces of crab and mushroom from the very oily sauce at the bottom. My friend had the rigatoni, which he also found very oily. Additionally, he had ordered a side of spigarello, which our server described as similar to kale and broccoli rabe. It was so incredibly salty that neither of us could finish it (which made us both very sad, because we really wanted to eat it!) Over-salted food aside, it was clear that Piora was trying hard to make a good impression through the level of their service. Our servers were incredibly attentive; our orders were taken and our plates cleared promptly, the table was scraped of crumbs after each course, and we received helpful answers to our questions. Unfortunately (and I almost feel bad saying this because everyone there was so nice), the level of food just wasn't as good as I had expected, and neither my friend nor I are particularly eager to go back soon.

This place is despicable. Â Nothing says "there goes the neighborhood" like the arrival of a massive megabucks multi-investor-driven drinking establishment like this place. Â At least TGI Friday's is honest about what it is. Â This place pays lip service to the now-trendy notion of the beer hall while preserving none of its integrity. Â The beer menu has many predictable German selections, yet no respect is paid to the traditional method of serving the different styles in the proper glasses. Â At $7 a beer, I would expect more. Â KÃ¶lsch is not to be served in a stein. Â Neither is Hefeweizen. Â I'm not even German, and I know that. Â There is supposedly German fare to eat, but I saw oysters and brick oven pizzas (!) Â I felt sorry for the inefficient and overextended waitstaff, though they definitely did not match the beer hall premise either. Â I don't think a single member of the cacophonous mass of people drinking here lived in the neighborhood. Â This is for over-privileged suburban transplants looking to get rowdy on someone else's turf. Â It's a real stretch to call this place a beer hall, but please, don't call it a beer garden. Â It has to be outside to be one of those, fyi. Â Also, hefeweizen is a style of beer, not a brand.

I went here last night for the 1st time and I'm very happy that I did. Although the place is a little small, it's beautiful and charming. The staff is very friendly and the older woman who greeted us had such a warm and welcoming smile! The place wasn't too loud or too quiet. My date and I first sat outside but since it was a little too humid we took the table by the window. It was like we were in our own little world. It was so comfy. They gave us chips and dips as starters, which were amazing! My date almost ate it all without sharing lol!! He had the Cordero (lamb shank) & I had the Lomo Saltado (rib eye stir-fry). I'm not big on food, usually I just inhale my food lol but my Lomo Saltado was soooooo good, I found myself savoring every bite. My date liked my dish more than his! The Cordero was pretty good but the Lomo was even better. To drink he had Blue Moon beer and I had a Peruvian amber beer. I'm not a beer drinker but I wanted the whole Peruvian experience and I'm glad I ordered it. It was delicious!! I gave Surfish 4 stars and not 5 for two reasons- the place was a little small and the Cordero wasn't as great as my date had expected. Peruvian food is one of his favorites. All in all I was very pleased and will definitely go back, even if to get Lomo Saltado to go.

So far so good, no mega crazy lines, and they move amazingly quick! Â This by far beats out the madison square location and I hope the lines stay as reasonable as they have been. Â The burgers are juicy and yum, cheese fries were delicious, and the shakes are true treat! Â I also really like the downtown butter brown. I hope this location stays a low key location so this place can remain uncrowded! Â And don't get me wrong there is a good amount of people here, however the line moves fairly quickly since the service is fast. Â But this may change if the lines become the size of the madison square park lines.

Let's see if I can accurately recollect my experiences at Sakagura. Â Ok, so it is a hidden away in the basement of an office building, but that just adds to the ambience of the place. Â I've been lucky to have had three good dining experiences here (only for dinner though). Â I agree that it is a bit pricey but if you have a good reason to celebrate and kick back in a quiet, subdued and charming environment, then come to Sakagura. Â They have an extensive sake and drinks menu, though as a light weight, I couldn't really enjoy it all that much. Â I did try the plum-flavored sake, which was really sweet. Â The small plates are also quite good if you're open to sharing with your group. My memory's a bit hazy, but here's what I can remember trying: jidori shioyaki (chicken, a bit salty but good), chawanmushi (sucker for steamed egg filled with little treats), agedashi tofu (can't go wrong with this), onigiri rice balls (salmon toppings, just ok), soba noodles (refreshing!) and surumeika yaki (squid = yum). Â While I didn't have the opportunity to try everything, I made sure to take a stab at the dessert. Â I picked the black sesame creme brulee, which was amazing! Â I would come back again and be a little more adventurous with the sake selections.
Amazing pizza....with AMAZING lines!!

Tabare was my first venture into Uruguayan food and it has made me an avid lover. We arrived at 6pm and was given our pick of seats. We opted for the table-for-two by the window. They have Happy Hour daily from 5pm-7pm and it features 50% off or Buy-One-Get-One-Free cocktails and select wines. Their tequila with lime and smoked paprika was delicious! Their sangrias are also super yummy. But the star of the night wasn't the drinks - it was the food. The empanadas were delicious and the chorizo was super sweet and spiced just perfectly. The raviolis of the day, stuffed with buffalo mozzarella, roasted potatoes and rainbow chard, was phenomenal. The steak, which was cooked to perfection, was super juicy and the chimichurri, which was a bit more sour than others I have tasted, complimented it very well. Dessert was blueberry ice cream and their homemade cookies - the cookies were a bit hard to eat with a spoon since it was so hard but the ice cream was amazing. I've never had blueberry ice cream before!

This place is hands down one of my favorite trips in the city. I had heard about this place from a fellow gluten-free pal and I was not let down. If you like risotto, this is your spot. The pizzas are quite delicious, too, albeit gluten-free. What I always enjoy as well are the breadsticks. I could eat those all day long! The impeccable service is what makes this place stand out from all the others. The waitstaff is quite fun, knowledgeable and entertaining, and even though it's often quite crowded and you have to wait, they offer drinks from the bar to keep you happy. I love you, you're perfect, NEVER change.
I AM IN A JOY COMA due to the chicken n' biscuit. like, maybe i am going to die?

This place is such a cute Victorian restaurant. I love the decorations! They have your usual British pub fare like fish and chips, cottage pie etc. Good drink menu too. We wen right after Sandy so the kitchen ran out of food, and they were short of manpower. They had no more bread left, so we ended up ordering a bunch of appetizers instead. The flat bread with figs was good, minus the figs, I hate figs. I really liked the pigs in a blanket. We also had the croquettes which was basically mashed potato breaded and deep fried. The food was blah, I would come back for drinks again though.

Mediocre food but convenient and friendly. Â Polpetone and spinach gnocchi drowning in too much sauce. Too much bread filler in the meatballs. Special avocado and tuna salad very good. Reasonable service. Busy and lively. Seems kinda silly for a restaurant this popular not to take credit cards for 3.5% fee.

You sit at a table with a bunch of people, and if you're in a small party you will definitely be seated with strangers. The food makes it all worth it--shanghainese soup dumplings are worth the wait and the slight discomfort of being seated across from people you've never seen before. Then again, that's pretty much the beauty of Chinatown. It is CASH ONLY. so make sure you stop at an ATM beforehand--it's cheap so $40 should definitely have you covered--possibly even $20 if you're not ordering much more than the soup dumplings. Also, try the radish buns.

I took my friend and boyfriend on Saturday night to Junior's to eat the most fabulous cheesecake. Â My friend had just arrived from New Zealand, for her first visit to the United States, and I told her she had to try Junior's cheesecake. Â We entered and were told it would be about a 20 minute wait. Â I said we were 3 people, and the name was Teresa (my friend from New Zealand's name, as people struggle with my name). Â We stand there and watch everyone around us be seated, and we stand there patiently for over 30 minutes. Â I go up to the male hostess and asked if we are coming up soon. Â He says we aren't on the list so we must have been called already. Â He makes it very clear as he goes through the lists and won't show them to me, that he never wrote my (my friend's) name down, but then he tells me repeatedly that it is my fault, that he must have called our name and we didn't come when called. Â That is not possible, as we didn't talk and were listening closely for our name the whole time we stood there. Â Then another hostess, female, says she is really sorry and that we will get the next table no matter what size it is. Â Then about 3 minutes later, she calls Andrea party of 3. Â I look at her dumbfounded as she walks off to seat another party...she had just told me that we would get the next table no matter what. Â Now I am absolutely more fuming than I have been in years, and the male hostess just shrugs and says, "not my fault". Â The female hostess didn't seem to care that she had messed up either when she returned to the stand. Â At this point I'm torn because we have been waiting 45 minutes for a table, and my NZ friend is horrified at the service and we haven't even sat down yet, I don't know if we should stay or if we should go. Â But we had waited so long at this point and the restaurant had emptied out and I just wanted to sit down and eat some cheesecake. Â So we stood there for another few minutes until someone finally sat us down. Â I asked the person who seated us (not the hostess) in a striped shirt if he was the manager, and he said he wasn't. Â Our time at the restaurant was ruined because my boyfriend and friend just kept saying how awful the hosts were, we should have left, how could they have been so unprofessional and rude, etc. etc. I have been to Junior's a number of times and have never been treated so rudely or dealt with such highly unprofessional people. Â My friend kept remarking how awful the experience was all day Sunday and this morning. Â I love how I wanted her to try Junior's cheesecake and now she will have lasting memories of terrible service in her time visiting the United States. Â  You all need to seriously have a discussion with your host and hostess and make sure this does not happen to other people in the future. I will definitely never take first time visitors to NYC to your restaurant ever again.

Hi everyone! So we headed here about 7pm and the wait in line for dinner was about 45 min. Â So if you come here super hungry you might want to grab a little snack to help hold you off until you get seated. Oh and it gets kind of tight in the waiting area. For my 1st time going to this place I was pretty satisfied. Â Of course I went here to try their soup dumplings that they are known for and everyone seems to talk about. I wanted to see if it was actually as good as people have been saying. And I have to say I wasn't let down. We had gotten the Crab and Pork ones and we ate every single one! They came out hot with the steam coming out of the bamboo container w/ a soy mixture on the side. You bite into them and the broth just bursts into your mouth. They must be popular because before we were even able get settled into our seats, the waiter was already asking us which dumplings we wanted to order. 1st tip! - You got to eat them while they're hot, because as soon as they start to get hot the broth inside them starts to get thick and its not as great. 2nd tip - WATCH YOUR SHIRT! LOL We also ordered the spicy eggplant with pork and the beef tendon soup. Which were both pretty typical but I liked the Eggplant dish more than the soup. A must try in Chinatown for Soup Dumplings!

Broadway bites has a variety of cuisines and choices for lunch, dinner or even a snack. You can sample things from different places or just eat what your stomach is telling you. I was only sampled/ate from Bangkok Bar. I got the curry rice bowl. It was good, very aromatic and a little bit of a spicy kick. I also got their Thai Iced Tea, which was average. Ah~ I wish I got to try other places, but I'm sure i'll be able to find them in the Union Square Holiday Market that's coming up soon. Or their return to Broadway Bites. Broadway Bites is at a great location in a busy shopping area. Also it's great to sample or to see what restaurants have to offer from around the city. So if you like what they have, you can probably track them down in their main locations.

I've been living in the neighborhood for many years and wasn't able to try this place out because of the ridiculous weekend crowds. I finally remembered to check it out during the week when I had a day off and it definitely lived up to its reputation. The menu has a great mix of sweet and savory options for brunch from pancakes to every kind of egg dish imaginable. Â I had the potato pancakes, friend green tomatoes and the Spanish chorizo omelet. Â The tomatoes were friend to perfections with just the right amount of seasoning in the breading. The potato pancakes were light and flavorful and the addition of smoked salmon and a hard-boiled egg on top was perfection. Â The omelet seemed to be one of the weaker choices on the menu. It had too much cheese for my liking and nothing that made it stand it out from the rest. Ps. don't miss the fresh orange juice or raspberry lemonade: so yum! So refreshing!

I'm from Texas, and this might be my favorite BBQ place I have ever been to. Â My girlfriend got the brisket sandwich and I got the pork. Â we also got sides of fries, baked beans, and sweet potato casserole. Â Everything was amazing, especially the sweet potatoes. Â Everyone says the Brisket is incredible and they are right. Â Will be back many times.

One of the cheapest Chinese place I've every been. Consider me a fan! The food here is very simple and authentic. This doesn't mean it's bad. On the contrary, the food here is very good! Just don't expect to be wowed by the presentation. The dishes here are usually about $5-$6 and that's very reasonable as one dish will probably fill you up. Yum! Cash only!

One of the better meals I have had in a while from a purely taste standpoint. I ordered a chicken sandwich with chipotle mayo and roasted tomatoes which came on a perfectly toasted baguette. The dish was accompanied with a salad-- the dressing's sweetness complimented the sandwich very nicely. Â  I also tried the fresh cucumber juice, which had a beautiful deep green color. It was refreshing, and I'd definitely recommend trying it if the other interesting drinks don't appeal to you. On the whole, I'd say Cafe Gitane's simple presentation and perfectly executed food is great for lunch or brunch-- it was bustling today, but in a friendly way, and has an overall positive energy that makes for a pleasant outing.

This is the go-to place when my bf and I are indecisive about where to eat. Hasn't let us down yet, reasonably priced, Â better-than-diner-food. There has been an incident though, a "micky" sighting incident. Haven't been back since then....

So my last review criticized wafa's delivery system and I'm happy to say it's on point now, no more "delivery when convenient" which is incredibly appreciated and respected. As for the food well, consistently awesome as always.

we come here for special occasions as it has that old school dinning experience. Â nothing is flash just traditionally beautiful. Â the food and service are phenomenal. Â they always have stunning flora arrangements and the cheese is to die for.

I felt I needed to write a positive review after the ludicrous one written about the homeless guy situation on 10/25. Â Really? Â You blame the restaurant for the actions of a random homeless guy? Â  Anyway, the food here is very good with fast, courteous service. Great NYC "counter" atmosphere, small and bustling, just like you would expect. Hopefully the Cally people have returned home. Buh, bye.

Cheap Thai food. The lunch specials are amazing. 2 appetizers and a main course for less than $10! The catch is that the portions aren't that huge. Since I was having a cold and needed to eat spicy foods (it helps, trust me), I had the spicy tom yum soup, which was pretty good. I also had the spicy fish cake, which was ok. And the spicy basil chicken. The spicy basil chicken was a little bit too spicy for me and I felt like crying. Service was ok.

I can't believe I can actually move right now. This place is absolutely great! I'm not gonna lie -- my friend and I both missed the restaurant and walked straight up to the to-go bar -- that's never going to happen again! Anyways, since my friend and I were waiting for our other friend, we were asked to sit and wait at the bar. The bartender is extremely nice! We didn't order anything at the bar, but the bartender kept checking up on us and making sure if we needed anything or not. Once our friend came, we immediately ordered the Grilled Corn Mexican Style. YUM! I don't even like cheese, which was put on the corn with the chili powder, and it was still amazing. There are two corn that come with each order!! Overall, I had a GREAT experience! The waitresses were nice, but as other people have mentioned, the restaurant is a bit tight -- however, the bathroom is not as dark as everyone is saying it is. It's like a club bathroom - enough to do what you need to do and get out. Aside from that, it's a cute place around SoHo and a good place to relax after a full day of shopping! Your first time? I got you covered. Cailin's Recommendations - Appetizer: THE CORN!!!! AND/OR Ensalada de Espanica y Manzana: slices of apples and grapefruit on top of spinach -- I didn't order this, but I saw this woman next to me eat it and it looked tasty!! ($8.25) Cuban Sandwich: Citrus pork/Ham combo sandwich -- apparently voted #1 in NYC ($9.25) OR Grilled Shrimp Tacos - these 2 tacos look so small, but they are so filling!!! ($11.95) PS: order the white sangria -- SO GOOD. You're welcome, you're welcome, you're welcome!
Crazy good avocado toast.
Pork noodle soup is too sour! Thai tea is just like your ordinary tea.

Great food. It was my first time eating Tibetan/Nepali cuisine, but it was very tasty. Kind of like Indian food but slightly different. The place is small and was fairly full on a Sunday evening. Super reasonable prices, with every dish on the menu at $11 or less. Note they no longer do BYOB.
