this is my favorite spot on st. marks pl. Â i eat hear a couple of times a week. Â i literally CRAVE their veggie tacos. Â they are the best i've ever had - and the gauc is amazing. Â very friendly - great looking place - just the best! Â highly HIGHLY recommended.

The service is terrible!!! The guy in charge skipped some people when they stand in the line waiting to be served. I think the staff there think they are the GOD. Customer has to worship them. Soup is very very salty. Bad bad experience. We will never come again.

Casa Mono is a unique place. It is both neighborhood place and destination dining spot. Small with a open kitchen, bar and very small loose tables in tight "shoe box" Plan on waiting for table or sit at the counter overlooking the kitchen. If you plan ahead make a reservation. It is a fun place where you order a bunch of tapas and drink a lot of wine for a night out. I have had everything on the menu sine dined here four times now. I do prefer ordering the tapas items over the larger dinner items. All of it is good. One favorite is the Red Snapper Crudo which is awesome. It is very difficult to go with a group unless you have reservations. Great place for a date and to hang with a friend or two. Also go next door to Bar Jamon which they own also for a drink while waiting The decor is very nice for a small place.

I have been meaning to check this place out for Â a while. I walked in with my friend without a reservation and we were told by the host that the restaurant was full, even though it wasn't, but we could eat at the bar. The bartender greeted us and asked if we'd like a drink and I asked if he could recommend wines to go along with what we would order. We ordered fried olives, fried cauliflower, fluke ceviche, lamb shank and a grouper dish, each one more unbelievable than the next. As each course arrived, the barman poured our wines giving an enlightening explanation why each wine matched each particular dish. Such a great night I can't wait to go back with friends. My advice, skip the reservation and sit at the bar!

If Helen of Troy was the face that launched a thousand ships, then The Grocery was the restaurant that launched this yelp account. I have to say, it was honestly one of the most underwhelming meals I've ever had in my life. I'm not sure what happened to The Grocery, but it seems like the glory days are long gone. We looked at the photos online, read some reviews and were expecting to be blown away. Sadly that wasn't the case. The food was trite and the prices inflated, the atmosphere, lackluster to say the least. At $25, the halibut was the smallest piece of fish to ever grace a plate outside of Manhattan. I would have sent it back but was too embarrassed to make a scene. The tables are right on top of each other and I didn't feel like including the neighbors in my plight. Sadly, I ate the fish, all two bites of him, while wondering what kind of pizza I was going to have for desert. The bill was $160 including tip. We had 1 beer and 1 glass of wine each. I also find it suspect that all the negative reviews have been "Not Recommended" by the Yelp moderator (and therefore not factored into the overall rating). Clearly, 30+ people have shared a similar experience but Yelp has silenced them by relegating their opinions to the fine print. Shame on you Yelp.

One of my favorite soba places I've had! Setting: small little area, but worth the crunch. The service isn't too bad, they are pretty fast in serving you depending on were you sit. My first time I was in the back, it took them a while to take our order, however in the front we got service right away. Raw octopus: I thought at first.. Weird... But omg after having it at other places, this was my favorite place to have it at. Kimchi pork dip: must have/try! It may seem very salty, but that's the point of the dip...DONT drink the broth until the end when they give you water to add to it. It's a perfect amount of spice so that you can still taste the food well. Warm nameko oroshi soba: this one was ok compared to the kimchi dip. I think it needed meet. Chicken rice balls: one of my favorite appetizers. It's nice and steamy when you get it and a bit of a wait but worth it. They warn you ahead of time it's about 10-15 min, but they bring it out once you have your soba so your not fully waiting ok food. I'm not a chicken person (personally hate chicken except dark meat) but I enjoyed this dish a lot. Meat was tender and juicy while the rice surrounding it was perfectly moist. Overall: I would come here again and again.

I had dinner here the other night before a show. Â It was average diner food, too expensive for the food. Â However, the service is fast, and that's a plus. If you want an expensive, fast, average meal, this is the place to go. I did have a piece of cheesecake on another occasion, and it was good, better than average.

Don't get ahead of yourself here and go crazy for all those delicious sounding wings, salad with kale croutons, pork and shrimp buns and fill up before you get to the delicious ramen. Â  You really want to save room for the ramen. Â As others have stated, go with the pork in the vegetable broth. Â Seriously, the combo is heavenly. Â Ok, get the salad with the crunchy kale too. Â If you're a fatty mcfatterson like me, stuff a bun or two down your gullet. Â  This soup warms the soul. Â Be prepared to wait. Â Super friendly staff is able to answer all your questions about the cuisine. Don't forget to get a few beers to help wash down all this grub.

Brunch review Been here twice and I can't help but get the benedicts. They come with a complimentary cocktail. It is always a ridiculous long wait for brunch so be prepared to starve. The Benedict Johnny was delightful. I really enjoyed the roasted tomato hollandaise- added a bit of a kick to eggs benedict. I liked the idea of having corn bread instead of an english muffin, but it was REALLY heavy because it was sweet. I would suggest you sub your homefries for greens if you choose this dish. The classic benedict was much more mild and basically classic. The eggs were not the best nor freshest eggs I've had, but still acceptable. The buttermilk biscuit was yummy!!! It was large, so you should share it unless you are a little piggy. Service is average. Nothing bad to say.

We've been going to "Spicy Village" since its earlier incarnation as "Henan Village." Â Then, the food was quite tasty, but the menu was limited--principally good for lunch. Â Now that the menu's been expanded, it's a great place for an affordable, unusual and delicious dinner. Â The owner/waitress, Wendy, is warm, personable and attentive. Â Every once in a while her rambunctious young daughter shows up and adds a rambunctious, family-feel to this charming hole-in-the-wall echo of the way New York used to be..

Went for breakfast with my boyfriend, had the lentil soup which was very good all natural and fresh. Fresh baked bread and strong Mamosas. My boyfriend had the Fritata with mushrooms and potatoes which was my only dislike.. Noting special but not bad. We would def go again if parking wasn't so hard to find and the wait to be seated I would of gave it 5 stars...maybe next time buddy

As a vegan, I was so pleasantly surprised to come across Terri while attending a 3-day training in the Financial District recently. I ended up visiting them all 3 days: Day 1 for a vegan brownie, Day 2 for a meatball sub, and Day 3 for a buffalo sandwich. (Can you tell I was in the mood for comfort food?) The meatball sub was excellent -- the sauce and bread really made it. There's tons to choose from, including much healthier options than what I happened to choose. I'll definitely return if my travels bring me back to FiDi at lunch time!

The best service I've experienced in NYC or really at all - super friendly and service minded staff! The food (French) was delicious, as was the cocktails! They have a SUPER cozy/nice garden that is everything you could ask for! Perfect for a date

If you think getting quality, authentic BBQ in NYC is impossible, then Mighty Quinn's is an absolute must try. Â I could smell the smoke from a block away as I approached the restaurant. Â Real BBQ comes from the burning of actual wood, so smelling the intoxicating smoky goodness from that far away was a great first sign. Â The second was seeing how packed it was. Â Luckily my friends were already there and had a table reserved. Â  The line for food was pretty long, but it does move quickly. Â Standing near stacks of wood at the read of the line, you can see large slabs of meat being expertly butchered in the back. Â Then, as you move closer, you can see the finished product being cut, portioned and served. Â This is also where I saw what that days special was: smoked pig cheeks. Â Although I had already decided to get brisket and pulled pork, I also knew I need to try some of those cheeks. Â For sides, I kinda had a bit of a brainfart and failed to order the burnt end baked beans, which my friends were raving about. Â Instead, I had a hankering for some fries and cornbread. Â Choice of slaw is an automatic side, and I opted for the creamy version. While both the pulled pork and brisket were excellent (the brisket was a tiny bit too fatty, though), those smoked pig cheeks were the single best thing I ate that day and maybe for quite a few days before and since. Â Since the cheeks obviously get a lot of work from pigs chewing, they were just loaded with flavor. Â I can't even imagine how long they had to be smoked for to break down the muscle. Mighty Quinn's has a nice selection of craft beers to complement their outstanding BBQ. Â I will most certainly be back next time I'm in NYC.

This place has the most flavorful Thai dishes I have ever had. I was starting to get over the whole Thai craze until I started frequenting this places. The curries are so fresh and robust but the Panang beef pobably stands out the most. The service is efficient and somewhat friendly although when they start getting really busy you may have to do alot of flagging down.
Pork buns. 'Nuff said. Ramen is overpriced.

Gramercy Tavern is one of my favorite places to go in the city. Â Whenever I dine here Â I always feel great and relaxed at the comfortable atmosphere. Â The food and Â service Â is great all around. I absolutely recommend this place for special special occasion.

one of my go-to spots in Williamsberg all the bartenders are really nice and friendly the bar has a nice open space with plenty of seating the crowd is usually good can come for the wide variety of beers, to sit back and play some jenga, or to try the bratwurst/sausage(I had the chicken one- it was real good!), chorizo chilli, or a hot pretzel even the bathrooms are good. There's never a line or they're reasonably clean -well, they don't stink, dunno about for a #2

Review number 200! Woo hoo! I'm glad I get to honor this precious spot with a great review for a great restaurant. I believe it's darn near impossible to get a reservation here for dinner, so we stopped in for lunch hoping to catch a table. Success! A table right by the window was waiting for us. It's a pretty small place, about 15 tables, with a small bar and partially-open kitchen. I ordered the sunflower seed salad which was one of the most tasty dishes I've had in a while! Also, got the pasta fagioli soup and a side of french fries with garlic aioli. Superb! The service could have been a touch faster but we weren't in any rush. While we were eating we actually saw two tour groups go by to look at the "Friends" apartment building located above the restaurant. So cool!
I don't get the hype. It's just another Chipotle. Everything tastes boring, from the salsa to the rice to the meats~

Orlando is the best bar tender in all of the West Village. As a local, I can assure his mixology is second to none! He is amazing. Ofrenda is amazing!! The guac is delicious. Ask Orlando for the drink Jess and Vicky had. It's a special mix only Orlando can make with "passion"

Great Italian food, and decent prices all things considered. Many of their primi pastas can be had for $10 and they're actually substantial enough to suffice as a meal. But my wife and I are evidently pigs, so we shared a primi and each ordered a secondi. Their Branzino is pretty good, but I actually had food envy this meal and enjoyed my wife's braised short ribs more. They give you the option of cooking the Branzino with bones in or out. Bones in is definitely tastier, but it is a bit tedious to pick them out of the filets. So if you'd rather not deal with that experience I wouldn't blame you for getting the bones out. The braised short ribs were succulent and sweet. They come with a side of polenta making the dish very hearty and filling. I also got to try some of my friend's baked eggplant antipasti. It was coated in Parmesan Reggiano which is just fine by me. The atmosphere here is casual and relaxed. We ate at our leisure and didn't feel any pressure to rush. I'm a fan of this place - it's a solid Italian option in the West Village

This place definitively has the best roast duck, as well as congee. The duck wasn't too salty but with a hint of sweetness. I guess it's the honey and soy sauce mix. They also used high quality duck, which didn't have just fat. You could tell that they spent a lot of time roasting the ducks. Also, cooking the congee. I had the thousand year old egg congee with salty pork. The salty pork had a lot of flavor, unlike some other places just had salt or some of them didn't even put salt. I had to take away one star because I bought a whole duck yesterday and brought it home. My husband mentioned the duck wasn't as meaty as the one we had last time, but rather very boney.

Very clean and nice atmosphere. I loved their choice of soft music. Our waiter was super nice. The vegetarian chili bowl was a disappointment because it was more a soup than a chili. The 'canera' vegetarian sandwich was great especially with the spicy fish dip.

I tried the gyro platter or gyro over rice yesterday after all the hoopla. The best parts are that the platter is only $6 in one of the priciest tourist places in NYC and the hot sauce is so good and spicy. It is really really hot like the reviews say. The bad parts are the white sauce is not tahini sauce! I can spot mayo easily and so when I tasted it, I knew it was mayo! It really had no spice or flavor in it aside from mayo. Â I doubt it even have yogurt mixed into it! Also, the yellow rice they use are kinda hard. Not soft and plumb like rice is supposed to be. Maybe their food use to be better before all the buzz?

YAAAAAAAAAAAASSSSSS!!!! I took my boyfriend here because I read the reviews and I'm new to the Buswick/Williamsburg area. We went on a night that was pretty packed so waited for a couple minutes. NBD, they asked us if we wanted to put in a drink order so I ordered a Dark and Stormy while the boyfriend ordered the Old Fashioned... FIRST OF ALL- This place puts so much care into their drinks, you can imagine how much care they put into their food. Their D&S is bottled and carbonated on site, their Campari is aged in a french oak barrel. These things make such a difference in the taste and experience of drinks and I wish more people cared this much. Needless to say, we didn't order just one of these delicious drinks... we ordered... several. Everything here is made for sharing, which makes it an amazing date spot or a place for 3-5 friends to gather. Since it's a little more intimate, I think anymore than 5 is uncomfortable. Oh, I should also mention that we went back exactly a week after our date with some friends. I just HAD to. On to the meal(s)- Brocoli Rabe- This was something everyone told us we could not miss. The rabe was accompanied by anchovies, parmesean, and eggs. The combination sounds odd but the bitter rabe, with the salty anchovies and parmesean, was perfectly balanced with the creaminess of a medium boiled egg. This is the dish that has me coming back because I feel like I'm eating something relatively healthy but incredibly delicious at the same time. Patatas Bravas- We went to Barcelona and enjoyed several versions of this dish- It's basically fried potatoes with Mayo and Sriracha, although in Barcelona we wished it was this spicy. As delicious as it was, it was my least favorite because I kept accidentally eating the paper that was on the bottom...WHAT!? It looked like potato skin... -_- Creamy Polenta- And creamy indeed it is. I don't think it needed the pork ragu at all. Both were amazing together, but they would have definitely help up on their own. We licked the bowls clean and wished we had more. Grilled Octopus- The boyfriend and I had some delicious Octopus in Europe and we were taken back to those amazing moments once we tasted this one. Although it was a pretty small portion for the price, the meat was tender and there was a great char to it. Another dish I wish we had more of. Steamed Mussels- Spicy, tangy, garlicky, aMAHzingness- that's all I remember of that but it was yummy. Try it! Tagliatelle- My friends thought it was a bit salty but I love that so I didn't mind. For some of these items we got them from a tasting menu. I think I would have chosen to order it anyways. I wish that the noodles were handmade because I think that a fresh pasta would have held up better to the flavorful sauce. Roasted Organic Chicken- This was another thing off the tasting menu. I don't typically order Chicken because it's something I make a lot of at home. However, this chicken was such comfort food. The garlic jus it came with was a game changer. It was tender, moist, and well seasoned. Something I would easily order again. Tiramisu- Have you ever had a dessert that just blew your mind? (cue explosion sound effects). How can something be so decadent yet light, satisfying yet not heavy? Please meet TSA's Tiramisu. It has all the elements of boring tiramisu with a twist. I think the most important element of their tiramisu was the Espresso Granita. Instead of soaking the lady fingers in that, they top the dessert with this and it makes it cool, light, and refreshing. It's the perfect thing to end a meal with. I should know because I had it end my meals twice. Summary- Go there. You won't be disappointed. If you take a girl there, you will definitely score some points. Get the drinks, get the broccoli rabe, get the tiramisu. You won't be disappointed.

After looking at all the reviews, and the recommendations of so many people and places, we decided to go there yesterday after seeing a show. Â Gotta say, I wasn't too impressed. We started off with the deep fried Octopus ball entree/appetizer. Â Good but not great. Â Felt like we were tasting more ball/breading, and I couldn't really taste any octopus. Â Next up was the single order BBQ and the BBQ Squid. Â Had one lamb, one duck, one waishu beef, and one asparagus bacon. Â All GREAT, as was the squid. Â Last, we chose one of the hot plate pancake dishes (can't remember which one, but it had pork on top), and the Yaki udon. Â The pancake was good, but the bbq sauce on top overpowered it a little. Â The Yaki Udon was just not good. Â It tasted like the they just threw the sauce that was on the pancake onto the Yaki Udon. Â They both tasted exactly the same, which didn't make it any better as a whole. Â It ended up tasting very very salty. Unfortunately, I'm not drinking right now, so I wasn't able to have any sake with my meal. Â But maybe that's the trick, right? Â Alcohol might make everything taste better?? Â Overall, just for the food, some good, some great, one bad. Â Very hit or miss (but with bbq being a definite HIT), with other places offering better overall tastes. Â I would've given it 3 stars, but with all the recommendations, I was just a little more disappointed...

Cafe Orlin was rated as one of the best brunches to visit so we made plans to eat there. They do not take reservations for brunch and we waited for over an hour to be seated. Yum! Â I really liked everything that we got. Â We started off with: Â Beef skewers (SO GOOD!) - it comes in 4, and it's a tad spicy. Always crowded ... Â A fun spot for good comfort food ... Soooo many good pies... A great place to people watch !

Good for what you get. Â Randomly chose this place based on the sheer number of bodies inside, most of whom looked Chinese, which I generally take to be a good sign. Â We ordered some the lychee duck (mainly because my friend and I were curious what that exactly entailed), a seafood stir fry dish, beef and broccoli, and salted fish and chicken fried rice. Laduree is by far the best place to go for macarons. The place itself is beautiful and once you enter the store, the smell surrounds you. My favorite flavors are pistachio, salted caramel, and rose. The only problems I have are the long lines and price.
small cozy and romantic restaurant. Top notch service. Was pleased with service and dishes.
I was in town for an hour, went to Udon West on Yelp recommendations and was sick until the net day. Â Salty nasty food. Â  They do have great service, I will give them that. Â Bad Yelp!!!!

Get the bouillabaisse. our waitress was awesome -- she's austrian and we just happened to be going to austria the week after so she gave us lots of fun(ny) commentary/advice. it's BYO! the restaurant/tables are small so be prepared to get intimate with your party and the other parties.

Of course, Junior's cheesecake is the best, as the original Brooklyn restaurant became known for. Â Order the regular- it's creamy and smooth, but is enough for two people. Pizza bagels are amazing, and cheap ($2)! Best drunk food ever.

Lucked out and ventured in after some horrible winter weather so seating wasn't a problem at this usually busy spot. Although I'm still struggling to discern the difference between Korean and Japanese BBQ, I will say the team at this restaurant do an unbelievable job in educating diners on how to enjoy Japanese BBQ. The dessert we went with (Green Tea Mille CrÃªpe) was suggested to us by our server, Guillermo, and it didn't disappoint. A great experience all around!

I came here this past Sunday for Brunch with two of my friends from Brearley. We made a reservation and the wait was only about 10 minutes. Not bad at all. My friend actually reminded me that we had been there once before for a private birthday party on the bottom level so I guess this is my second visit! Anyway, I ordered the Benedict Johnny and a lemonade. I was drawn to the description of the dish which included maple chicken sausage and corn pancakes - SOLD. I never had an eggs Benedict meal before so the poached egg was definitely a memorable experience. I think that may be the first and the last poached egg I'll ever have. Not that it was good, please, don't get me wrong the meal was great. However, I prefer all my foods well cooked. I cannot stand runny eggs! My friends enjoyed their meals as well. After a long search for venues, the Counting Room (1) had lots of space and looked great inside, (2) offered us a lot of options on food/drinks, and (3) was very reasonably priced. Drinks were great (including the house punch they made for us), food was delicious, and event went smoothly. Comfortably fit our group of 60 or so.

The ramen was absolutely delicious! I got the basic pork broth with thin noodles. Â The portion was huge! The broth was amazing and the noodles perfectly cooked. Â Went for dinner a little after 9:00 PM and only had to wait 15 minutes. Â I definitely recommend Minca!

Yo! You can come here for breakfast and get a short stack of DELICIOUS pancakes with a free alcoholic breakfast drink of your choice for $6! That right there is the best deal in the the neighborhood. I didn't have the pancakes but my friend did and they were good. I got the french toast and it was equally as amazing. To wash it all down we got bellinis and mimosas. If someone gives Don Pepe's less than 4 stars, they should have all reviews removed from Yelp and should be banished from reviewing anything - even non-food related things - for life. great experience to shop, see, and eat Italian food products. Their gelato is so good (had pistachio and salted caramel). Yes it pricey, their gourmet products, but it's just Â a fun experience to try.

Solid place for drinks and apps. I came here for dinner with some friends on a Thursday night and the place was pretty packed and "bumpin" as the kids say. Cheap and tasty soups and congee. I just wish they would open up a spot in DC :D Will be back.

So i was visiting NYC with some friends from Europe.our hotel recommended Pylos, as high end place.the place is very elegant, food was great ,(though u feel like you are rushed through the meal, which makes it feel commercial)the experience was very Â pleasant !!!!!

Cafe Luluc is a solid spot for a cheap, casual breakfast/brunch, but by no means is it destination-worthy in my opinion. The menu is also quite comprehensive, with everything spanning from your breakfast staples, sandwiches and salads, to other more French entrees. So now on to the less than great... The bf ordered their grilled vegetable panini with goat cheese (very much against his usual habits, I know) which he asked to be served with fries. The sandwich was pretty simple and tasted good, but nothing too special just judging from the bite I took. The fries were surprisingly good though, nicely crispy without any unnecessary grease. I just can't shake the perception of Cafe Luluc as a hip French diner. My experience was fine, though I can't say I would return just because there are so many other more interesting options in the area.

one of my favorite ramen experiences ever! Â the broth was perfection. milky, frothy, tasty, heaven. Â the meat was excellent, the noodles perfectly cooked.

It is surprisingly tasty, even on the rolls with chocolate chips in them. Apparently black bean dip goes with everything. Who knew. This is a perfect place for brunch with your ladies (and boys- it was a pretty equal mix). It's HUGE, so there's plenty of room for groups (though the booth was a tad squished and not the most convenient for hopping up and down for refills at the sangria bar). The decor is big and bold, lending it a Vegas-y feel, which makes even more conducive to sitting around and stuffing your face. And, best of all, they didn't rush us out- we sat there for a good hour after we finished our food, just nursing our delicious sangrias. That was a definite bonus. I get the feeling that you could sit there all day and they wouldn't give you shit. I will definitely be back.

In the restaurant obsessed landscape of New York City, fads come and go. Certain ingredients become staples on every menu; identical tattoos pop up on the forearms of drones of waiters, bartenders and kitchen staffers alike. Everyone prints their menus on the same type of paper, using the same fonts and pricing schemes - giving you a bargain on this, overcharging you for that. Like the fads themselves, these restaurants come and go, fizzling out into the darkness like thousands of other forgettable restaurants before them. The exception to this trend is the restaurant that gets better with age. It takes a lot to make a restaurant get better with age: location, focus, discipline, dedication, hard work, love... and arguably a number of other intangible factors that defy explanation. Roberta's has all of those things, and has steadily become better over the years because of them. Roberta's is a convent of food culture. It has a uniquely branded identity that extends to every aspect of the place. For the staff, one gets the impression that they don't want to be anywhere else; as if Â Roberta's has become a refuge from their everyday lives. They cling to - and ensure the vitality of - this dreamscape by providing you with a rather amazing restaurant experience. From the built-in radio station, to the rooftop garden (where genetic cross-mutations are the every day norm), to the tiki bar out back, Roberta's has built a compound to protect its diners from reality, all tucked behind a nondescript door in the middle of industrial Bushwick. The food, beverages and pizzas are all top-notch, too. Roberta's is one of the more unique restaurants in the U.S. Not because it's trendy (which it is), but because it's different. And good. And special. And fun. Go and see for yourself.

Char-Siew Sook Sook and his Lo Pou are in the house! (Otherwise known as Uncle BBQ Roasted Pork and his wife- just a little nickname my friend and I gave them.) The best square pizza in town.

Went here on a Friday. Â In scenary and ambiance- a great NY hotspot. Â Typical people-watching, atmosphere, typical expensive cocktails, typical busy-ness! Â It's wise to make reservations well in advance to snag a table, but sitting at the bar is just fine- as long as you're aggressive enough to pounce on the next empty seat. Â  The restaurant has conveniently decided to ignore seating people at the bar, so you're on your own- so beware. Â  Though I ate at the bar, I'd recommend making a reservation for table so you can experience the rustic decor, dim candlelights and shield yourself from the cold! Â  This place is actually much bigger than Tia Pol (my other tapas lover), and is quite the date spot with his homey, cozy feel. ALRIGHT: What to order. Â The menu here is really eclectic I think for tapas, finding not the typical Spanish fare (I didn't seen an ounce of chorizo, which admittedly was disappointing, at least when I went- and no patatas bravas!) - pulling from mainly a lot of South American (cornish hen), italian (crab cake risotto), and Greek (fried goat cheese? Well I guess that could be Spanish) influences. Â  Below is a list of what we had and there were worth every mouthwatering bite! 1. People have raved about this and it's true- the Brussel Sprouts are one of the best things I ever tasted (and you know that the sprouts are not well known for their good taste)- the pistachio undertones is the real treat here. Â I even MAYBE considered a second order- wowee. 2. The Fried Goat Cheese- NOT OILY! You'd never be able to tell it was in the deep fryer; they're so clean cut and refreshing. (Yes fried cheese-refreshing!) Especially dipped in honey :) 3. The Cornish Hen- overlooked as tapas item, and it WAS good. The meat was very tender, not gamey at all. However, I'd say the winner was the chili dipping sauce soaked within the hen. Â Beware, though this dish is SPICY. (which for me, is usually no problem and I thought it was HOT)- as it's sort of laced with jalapenos. 4. The Crab Cake Risotto- passable; good, very rich but the lumps of crab were meager and it tasted more soupy than like risotto. 5. The Charred baby octopus- This was OFF THE HOOK! I love me a good octopus, very Italian style, perfectly seasoned with aioli on the side and spicy potatoes. YUM YUM YUM 6. The Squid Ink Paella- The rice has squid ink in it! Â Not unusual for tapas but had never seen this infused in rice. AND the rice was totally non mushy, it was a bit crunchy! Â The other seafood was typical- clams, mussels, shrimps- I didn't care for those. Â I really liked the rice though. The bill came to about $75, a little on the higher side but I thought it well worth it. Â I'd say for sure do your reading of your (yelp!) reviews because when I asked the waiter what to get, he recommended everything most expensive on the menu. Only an unsuspecting tourist would fall for that!!
extra friendly service! Â  Â  lobster rolls are off the hook too.

This is my favorite place on the Upper East Side. My boyfriend and I decided to stumble in early one Saturday and ended up staying until way past our bed time. It's now a part of our weekend routine. The prices are more than reasonable. It's intimate, but not uncomfortable or loud. When the weather is nice, they'll open up the glass sliders which is quite lovely. I've eaten about half of their menu. The kale salad is amazing for those watching their waists, but for anyone else, they have the best wings I've ever had. Let me repeat, THE BEST WINGS I'VE EVER HAD. They're hot, but not unmanageable. Smokey, but not overpowering. Always cooked perfectly. Eat them. Love them. Rejoice. The beers are constantly changing, which is great if you like to try things, but kind of a bummer if you fall in love with something and they rotate it out. They always have an abundance of choices though. You'd be hard pressed not to find something you like. The bartenders are a really good resource for picking something good out. Love Cassie. She's good people. Basically, go. Eat wings. Drink beer. Or if you're a classier fellow, try some of their awesome old school bourbon. Be happy.

Extra Virgin is a little pricey but worth every penny. Every single food item we had was delicious (and we ate a lot). The squash raviolis I had for dinner were divine. I wholeheartedly recommend this place.

I love fries, so I thought I would try the new La Frite. I got the skinny fries, even thought I think I ordered the signature, thicker fries. However, the service was very friendly and helpful. The sauces were also very good - I think I had the rosemary aioli, but I thought they were a tad expensive per sauce. For a cheap price, you get a cornucopia full of fries (enough for perhaps 3 people) hot and made-to-order. The only thing I would recommend is more seating, but I understand that is a constraint of the space. I'm excited to see La Frite grow as a business in the future.

From the good folks at Resto comes this fascinating butcher shop slash general store slash beer bar named for Belgian cycling legend Eddy Merckx. Vaguely reminiscent of the 19th century, when you'd drink a beer at your local grocer and take some home in a bucket with your other provisions. There's a lot to love here: the massive selection of brew, the laid back vibe, the good music, quality meat, good people, dry goods. Â The prices don't seem out of line to me, but people gonna hate. But for those of us who get it, it's good. Rock on.

Not worth the hype, came here for their Wednesday promotion where all the items on the menu are $1, sangria $2, beers $3. Nothing was good, mostly just BREAD with tiny portions of either shrimp/meatballs/pulled pork/chicken/whichever other filling. Save your money and go somewhere else for happy hour.

This place is a bit pricey for me, as only a single burger with no sides costs almost $9. But if you're trying to escape from a potential hurricane/all the garbage on NYC whacking you in every direction, the closest establishment will do. Rundown: Spicy Tuna Burger - B+ Chicken Teriyaki Burger - B Tempura Sweet Potato Fries - A I really wish they gave their patrons a larger portion of Tempura Sweet Potato Fries. They are finger lickin' good, especially with Wasabi Mayo. Good service and good assortment of specialty condiments. The lighting is a bit dark, which affects the ambience of the place IMO.

Have eaten dinner here multiple times and loved it... Today I went for brunch and was totally blown away. We had a fruit plate and the scones to start. I eat the biscuits in a sausage gravy which were to die for! I thought the pricing was very very reasonable as well --- I will be back for brunch!

Ordered two chicken platters which arrived quickly. The food arrived hot and was very tasty. Portions were large and offered at a fair price ($11). I'd say it was tastier than Tahini, Chickpea or Pita Joe.

I've only been here for lunch and not brunch/happy hour/late night drinks but I've gotta say, after my two visits I'd definitely come back! A restaurant/bar like this is not something that anyone ever travels for, but I will say that if you're ever in the midtown west/hell's kitchen place and you want a drink or food, you could do FAR worse than Alfie's. The service was attentive and polite. The guy (assuming manager) was very welcoming the two times that I've been there. Alfie's has a pretty decent beer list (didn't try any mixed drinks) of both drafts as well as bottled beers. Our server was able to explain the beers also, which was really helpful for my friend who doesn't drink beer often enough to know what she likes. The food was pretty on point. Again, nothing gourmet, but when you're expecting just regular bar food, Alfie's blows that idea out of the water.

i've always heard resounding praise for perilla, the little restaurant that could, courtesy of top chef alum harold dieterle. it's nice to know that a reality show contestant is truly talented, and committed to his craft. so kudos to harold for opening a successful restaurant in manhattan. the location is wonderful once you get there. it's a funny thing that from quiet, calm, quaint jones street, there is saturday madness and tourist-infestation a half block in either direction. but perilla keeps it's doors open and all we heard were chirping birds. drinks: worth a mention. i ordered a bellini - passion fruit was the flavor du jour - and it DE-LISH. totally refreshing and clearly made with fresh fruit. it went down very easily. M ordered a "smoky bloody mary," named because of the inclusion of barbeque sauce. that worked very very well. it was spicy but cut with a sweet smokiness. i immediately regretted ordering my bellini. main course: first, the server lays a plate of small lemon pound cakes - roughly the size of golf balls - on the table. i wanted to ask if i could just have a slice of that stuff with some yogurt. really tasty. instead, i ordered poached eggs and smoked salmon on an english muffin, hold the hollandaise {shush. that stuff freaks me out. sorry.} and a side of fresh fruit salad. the egg dish was nice - nothing nutso and something i could have easily made at home - but good nonetheless. the fruit salad was actually the winner. most places have a fruit salad option that, pardon me, is LAME. this fruit salad was serious: thick cut pieces of banana, mango, pineapple, plum {plums!!}, and a handful of black grapes {my favorite}. no weird syrups or sauces, just good fresh fruit. M got the spicy duck burger. it was intense. the fries are beautiful and thick and slightly spicy, not too spicy. the burger itself is not for the faint of heart: piled high with a spicy duck patty, avocado, jack cheese, and all the fixin's, it's a challenge to get through. the duck meat is very rich and very good. i had two bites of that mammoth and felt like i had a meal. bottom line: Â perilla offers a very pleasant, reasonably priced brunch. there are options for everyone {we spotted some pretty awesome looking/smelling french toast on the way out} and the food is well prepared. we remained full and happy well past dinner time, which is a sign of a good brunch. i'll certainly be back to perilla for dinner.

My first time at Uva on the Upper East Side with a group of close friends. Ordinarily I only take dates to restaurants with dimly lit, electronic candle light but this place had a certain buzz about it. We eagerly waited about 25 minutes for our table with our mouths watering as we watched patrons Â eat. We were seated in the back of the restaurant which had a nice ambiance overall. Contrary to other reviews I've read, Uva was not Â overwhelmingly loud. If you are going out to dinner in New York City and Â expect peace and quiet then do it in the confines of your own closet apartment. Otherwise, Â enjoy the incredible food and people that NYC has to offer. I ordered bacon-wrapped scallops. The scallops were perfectly cooked but a little under-seasoned. I would rate my plate overall 3 stars, but my friend's tagliatelle pasta was extraordinary topped with a bolognese sauce. Dessert is what pushed me to 4 stars. We had the special 7 layer crepe cake. Absolutely fantastic. Made the meal hands down. My friends ordered an almond cake which was so-so. The verdict: you can't go wrong with Uva. If you need a date spot, this is your place. And what woman doesn't like a good pasta dish? Not any woman i'm taking to dinner!

Friend and I were going to a show on the UWS @ The Beacon and needed a quick place to eat before we went to the show. Asked an UWSider where we should go and she immediately said Kefi so we made a rez. We arrived at the restaurant and they brought us downstairs. I was really confused at first because there were SO many tables upstairs but then I realized how big the space was downstairs. We were seated at a cute table, great room. Waiter was very young but nice. We decided to do a lot of sharesies. The menu was inconsistent with its writing - one page would say "chickpea" and the other page would say "hummus" and both were hummus. I felt like I was back in Israel with non-native English speakers. We ordered a potato and brussel sprout salad which was delicious. Then shared a falafel that was big and yummy - a little mushy for me. The spreads were tasty and they were accommodating by letting us substitute some fishy spread for more hummus. The pita and the bread they had were great but of course we asked for more and then got stuffed on bread. We had goat cheese ravioli that was excellent. I can't even explain how full I was. I was in pain from overeating bread. The total bill was $60 including tip which was totally reasonable for 3 people. I look forward to going back non-rushed and less bread. When we left, we noticed EVERY table but about 5 were filled. Massive restaurant.

Just brilliant sushi. Â Fantastic selection from basic sushi / sashimi all the way to Torro. Â All the food was super fresh, perfectly prepared and delicious. Â Best sushi in Manhattan so far - for my money way better than Sasabune (the paint wasn't peeling off the wall at Yasuda). Â Stand outs were the oysters, eel (so I'm told) and Torro. DÃ©cor was pleasant, waiter wasn't. Â Make sure you ask for the other menu where u can make up your own sushi selection - way cheaper.

I don't know what it is but there is really something special about this place that you can feel when you walk in. The service was great and very friendly. We ordered the Pork Belly with Brussels Sprout & Onion Panzanella, and Niman Ranch Top Sirloin with Tuscan Kale & Bone Marrow Butter. Both were excellent! The pork belly was so crispy and tasty - definitely a dish you want done well if you're in-taking all those calories! The sirloin was perfectly cooked - which is always upsetting when you get your steak and realize it's cooked wrong. It was a really relaxing but also lively night out. I'm really impressed with Colicchio's restaurants I've tried so far!

Prix fixe was only $15 here. The food was amazing! (no booze drinks included or even available). Friend and I went halvzies so I had the roast Chicken sandwich and she had the apple pancakes and we split them. Â Both meals were great. The service was a bit glacial... Took forever to get our coffee and juice while the table next to us got their drinks almost immediately (we ordered at the same time with the same waitress). Â However we got our meals first and they wait a long time for their meal.... Fair enough, bitches! Â Great food, slightly slow service, nice atmosphere, and lots of cute gays.

The female server with long dark hair totally talked crap about me in Spanish. While I was standing right there. Sorry, but this place just ain't worth THAT. To the barista in question: People understand more than you think they do. THANKS.

It was OK overall. It's the trendy AND EXPENSIVE Upper West Side. Crowded with people. The service is *excellent* and the staff is *excellent* and super, super friendly, helpful, and gracious. They have to squeeze in between crowded tables and they were great at getting to us and delivering good, more water, and updates to us. I was pushed up against a brick wall during the whole dinner because it was so crowded, so I was eating with my shoulder pushed into my neck. The food was...OK. I ordered a plate of pickles as an appetizer, and they were disappointing. I was expecting something fresher and firmer, and they were limp like store-bought, glass-bottled, cooked pickles. Not terrible, but meh. Not nearly as spicy as advertised. I also ordered two beers after the waitstaff let me try samples of a few, and the beers were excellent--cold and poured into a flute glass. The hamburger was good--the meat especially--and smothered with pickles, but it was un-eatable as-is. I ended up just cutting it all up into small bits so I could at least eat without having the burger explode in my hands it was stacked so high--easily six inches tall. Not a huge burger, but it was small, firm, and oval/rounded, not flat like a typical burger. Good flavor, but difficult to eat. They load up a large metal bowl with french fries, which were adequate. Other meals I saw people eat there included fried chicken smothered in mushroom or sausage gravy, grilled sausages on a bed of french fries, and other southern-style foods. I also tasted the fried green tomatoes, which were OK, but very, very bland. The chicken and the sausage platters were piled with food. The hamburger, two beers, and the pickles, including tax and tip, came to around $55. Â  On the plus side--great staff, good food, great location On the negative side--high prices, crowded seating

Loved everything about this place--the decor, atmosphere, fresh bread, and meals were delicious. The braised short ribs and bolognese were excellent. The service was quick & made us feel at home. Perfect place to carb load before the Marathon!

Great place to go for a intimate date without the stuffiness based on the backyard decor/setting. The menu was minimal which eliminates the general issue of being overwhelmed with too many options. We were disappointed that they ran out of the bread because the description on the menu was enough to make this carbivore's mouth water. We ended up ordering the carrot salad, duck breast, and black sea bass. The flavoring for each dish like a taste bud rave!! The only downside for me personally is that I'm a big eater and the portions was not sufficient for me (I have a really serious appetite to be the point of being offensive); but if portions isn't an issue to you and you're a pure taste enthusiast then I highly recommend trying to this place out. I still need to come back here for the Saturday Pho!

Came in to no line (which I'm told is rare). The 2 of us were seated at a table of 8 but luckily friendly people. We ordered pork dumplings and fried noodle. Way too much food for 2. The price was decent but I felt you there were better options nearby from a pricing perspective. The dumplings were good. I had in my mind they would be excellent and maybe my expectations were too high. The fried noodle was average and there was plenty of it. It comes out hot and freshly cooked. Â  Overall a good experience but I think I had the bar set too high.
fresh lobsters by the pound.

We are first time visitors to NY, and had a wonderful meal at Le Parisien. A small restaurant, with a very friendly vibe. Coq au Vin was excellent, as was everything else, including the nice conversation with the folks at the next table (one of the pleasures of a small restaurant).

This place should be called "Cheryl's Global BITCH". Never in my life have I ever interacted with a woman SO rude and SO condescending in my life. I'm assuming she is the owner, because she just acted like it. Really? Do you just not want us to eat here at all??? I would have walked out, but it was my friend's idea to go here and she was starving. We arrived a few minutes before 4pm, and before we could even say "Table for 2" - this woman basically started yelling at us that we only had 3 minutes to order food. When we asked about Happy Hour options (which stated right on their sign board that it started at 4pm) she screamed at us again "I TOLD YOU THE FOOD ENDS AT 4pm!" She didn't really stop there, she then talked to us like we were children explaining the whole time slot = meal option break down. Not really sure how to react, we just sort of nodded and started heading to the backyard part of the restaurant. Cheryl then scream "Hey! I'm not done with you. Did YOU hear what I said? If you want food you need to order it NOW!" Thankfully I wasn't eating, because why would I even want to waste my time with food from a woman who obviously doesn't give a damn about customer service. My friend ended up ordering a sandwich and we both got lemonades. I don't even care how any it tasted, as far as I'm concerned I will never go back here, and I regret whole-heartedly that I didn't say so to her face. Hopefully this will make a difference. PS. When we left the restaurant, the sign board was now changed to dinner options, which said right underneath it "Dinner: 4pm-10pm". Also, the waitstaff was HORRIBLE as well, really pushy and acted like we needed to leave ASAP.
The pulled pork melts in your mouth and the baked potato was perfect. Â As was the lemonade.

Sketchy entrance into an office building. Downstairs in a dungeon. Authentic decor. Feels like I'm in Japan. Don't expect rolls. Awesome food. I'm not even going to give you suggestion. Just ask the waiter some recommendations. Amazing! Best Japanese in NY.

I hadn't been to Miriam for months - my last experience was great and the second visit didn't disappoint! My friend and I split the burkekas - flaky and creamy - and the babaganoush - nice and smokey with a swirl of good olive oil - while waiting for our other friend. Â We hung out at the bar with a fantastic bartender, whose name I wish I had caught. Â He pointed out that mezes were half off and beer and wine was two for one during happy hour from 5-8 p. Â When I declined a drink and opted to stick to water, he kindly whipped up a raspberry lemonade from scratch, complete with muddled raspberries and a splash of seltzer. Â It was tangy and such a nice, personal touch that you don't often see. We split the mesclun greens with poached pear, spicy calamari, zucchini cakes (delicious yogurt sauce!), hummus, and kadaif wrapped shrimp (crunchy and delicious). Â My friend got the chicken shawarma, which was a ridiculously generous portion. Â  Zucchini cakes, babaganoush and shrimp - and the awesome bartender! - were the highlight of the meal.

I am always a pushover for eating near the waterfront and I love Red Hook, so a visit to Brooklyn Crab was in order. Went there this afternoon soon after they opened for business. Lovely late afternoon sun on the 2nd floor patio. We order a dozen Barcat oysters and the fried oyster and fried whole belly clam sandwiches, plus a glass of rose wine and a limeade with rosemary vodka cocktail. It was early and the staff was attentive. The oysters were plump and tasty. Sandwiches were good and the french fries were well prepared and nicely salty. Undersalted french fries are a pet peeve for me. The space is casual. I passed by on fri night and could see that it was a mob scene and that the staff was overwhelmed. If you are smart go to Brooklyn Crab earlier in the afternoon. I agree that the prices could be more reasonable. Â It is a good location and has potential.

1.Crostini A. Mozzarella, basil pesto, chili oil - Â  Â I am a sucka for mozzarella. Â When mozzarella and bread are making love in my mouth, it's like Donny Hathaway and Roberta Flack. You don't know what I mean? Â Go YouTube, ya lazy ass. B. Piquillo peppers, olive spread, anchovy - Â  My Latina friend said, "This is the best anchovy ever I've EVER tasted!" I didn't think it's exaggerated. Their anchovy is really less-salty, fishy taste and fresh. Â Amazing. 2. Jelu, San Juan, Argentina 2009 Â  100% Torrontes. Honeysuckle and flowers with some mineral on the Â  Â  Â  Â  Â  Â palate. Perfectly balanced by its level of acidity. I only sip a bit since I don't really drink, but this white wine is smooth as Barry White's voice. Â Now you really gotta go to YouTube, huh. 3. Vanilla bean panna cotta with strawberry sauce and chocolate corn flake cluster ASK THEM because they don't have this on their menu. I love this too much I have been peeing in my pants. Â As soon as I cracked this joke, my friend told this cute waitress that I love this too much and I peed (Ya know I made this shit up, right?) It's hands down the best Panna Cotta. Â I mean, if you have tried the better one, message me.

Don't let the size turn you way! Ruby's is the perfect place to stop at when in Soho. The host/waiter was very welcoming and genuine, the atmosphere(music, decor , people) was cool(Australian vibe) and the food was amazing! Together with a friend we ordered the Bronte burger, creamy chicken pasta, and shrimp and avocado salad which were all delicious($40 pre-tip)! Just thinking about my experience here makes me smile and I most definitely recommend Ruby's!

Great authentic Japanese Izakaya in midtown. I recommend their crab cream croquet. Cream croquets from other places are usually filled with too much cream and not enough crab, but their croquet has a lot of crab meat, so it's very flavorable. Reservation is a must because it's always busy at night.

Too much food!!! The portions here are so big and exaggerated that it made me feel like i was full just by looking at it. The gravy is too heavy and after a few bites it made me feel sick. If you are a conscious eater then i suggest you don't come here.

Had a late brunch here on Sunday. We were sat quickly, got our drinks, ordered, then waited for almost 30 minutes to get our food. All the tables around us, including some that sat after us, finished eating before we got our food. I ordered the duck hash. It had delicious chunks of savory duck mixed with salty potato deliciousness. The whole has was rounded out with a earthy nutmeg or a bit of cinnamon. If you don't like a bit of sweetness to your hash, I wouldn't order this. Other diners with me had the pancakes and an omelet. They were pretty standard and nothing to truly write home about. I'm planning to check out the dinner in the near future, as I have heard it is pretty stellar.
The food was awesome and reasonably priced. Loved the short rib sandwich and the Coq Au Vin was likewise delicious. Pleasant atmosphere, good music friendly service. Highly recommend this place.

This is some of the best and most affordable italian in the city. I enjoyed my meal here far more than other popular Italian places downtown like Porsena. These pastas are fresh and taste like they were made for you. The olive oil that is brought out onto the table sets the dining experience as a rich and flavorful meal. The salad to start was excellent- the greens were fresh and the balsamic glaze was sweet and tangy. My pasta dish was exactly what you would want from a classic Italian place downtown- rich, cozy, but also a little innovative in flavor. The ravioli was a pillow of heaven in my mouth- I will be coming back soon. Also- prices are extremely reasonable!

am i the only hater for traif? i really like the setting with the little piglet logo but i was kind of astonished by their high requirements. Luckily we had a party of 7 or else it was mandatory for each of us to have the $40 per person chef special. A friend of mine brought a drink from starbucks and they told her that she was not allowed in with that drink. the waitress told her its because they didnt want to a large company like that to ruin their ambiance. i understand if they didnt want her to drink it while she was attending this great dining event but this was no outside beverage at all. she just bought it before she came so she didnt want to leave it outside and she had to gulp it all down before she sat. I had to tell a friend not to come eat because it was mandatory to have the $40 per person course if there were 8 people or more. we ordered chicken wings, hamburger sliders, spare ribs, tuna eggplant kecap, softshell crab, italian pasta, and fingerlings. spare ribs were a little too sugary and so was the chicken wings. the sliders were good but not for the price. the softshell crab was great too but not for the price. i loved their serving style, it was very family oriented because it came slowly. a small portion of everything but that was also the downfall, the portions were way too small for the price. i expected a lot more from a trendy up and coming area. i believe the bill was about 240. none of the 7 people that went that night went home full after the dining experience. the tip was a mandatory 19.5%, more than a lot of manhattan areas i have ate at.
Maybe the best noodle / soup spot in Chinatown

Agree with everyone else...not much ambiance, but great, cheap, authentic dumplings. Â Make sure you also try the sesame pancakes/flatbreads (a couple of other reviewers have mentioned it as well) too, stuffed or unstuffed. Â THAT is what makes me go out of my way to swing by this spot. Â Mmm. Â Carb gluttony! Â :)

Nice music, friendly . waitress. Really good food. We tried the soup of the day which was fine Mussels a la provencale was fresh and the sauce was fine but a little too milky. The grilled cheese was great so was the beet salad.' That was my second dinner of the night so I ordered grilled pulpo, a second appetizer instead of a main course. Grilled pulpo were good too. Also tasted the filet mignon sandwiches at the table. Was ok but the French fries were average. The hanger steak was delicious Ordered a couple of glasses of Uruguayan wine (the Syrah), but it was really not good. The chocolate cake and the flan were really good. I recommend the place because of the food and the friendly people that run the place

I wish I was back in New York so I can have a slice of their yummy, delicious, gooey ricotta cheese pizza! Add a ton of garlic and oh my goodness, you'll win my heart! They have a couple locations but when we're in NY we usually frequent here. I love that they're open so late! It's the best thing to eat when you're getting out of the club at 3am. New Yorkers eat pizza at 3am! San Diegans eat mexican food at 3am! Since you guys don't have carne asada burritos on demand like we do, pizza will have to do ;)

The dumplings and noodles here are on point. Nicely tucked away from the overly crowded Vanessa's and Prosperity dumpling spots, it's always a quick pick up here in comparison. It's been one of my go to places for a quick bite or late evening snack after going to the bars (beware, drunk ordering can be dangerous!).

While the food was just OK and the rose was subpar, Â the service and attitude of the staff needs to be revamped. Â We had to ask our server twice for drinks that were not delivered, and at one point, he spilled an entire glass of water on me and into my pocketbook. Â I understand that accidents happen, and I received many "I'm so sorry", but they (I saw him talking to what appeared to be management about the mishap) didn't even offer to buy me a glass of wine. That shows a complete lack of regard for the patrons. Â Needless to say, Â we will never be returning to this establishment.

Great find - amazing price, amazing food, amazing atmosphere. Amazing all around. The employees are pretty cool too. I will definitely be back here (a lot) and I will continue to recommend it to friends. PS: it's BYOB!

Cute little place for a quick and delicious lunch. I got the arepa with cheese, avocado, and plantain... hubby got the shredded beef. Both were delicious! Very flavorful, good lunch portions, and super tasty sauces on the table (one spicy/sweet and one cilantro cream). The arepas were just the right thickness (not crispy, not doughy) and not at all greasy. Passion fruit juice was delicious, too. What a great find! I also noticed that they do happy hour.

Tacos are small affordable and full of flavor. They give u guac sauce and hot sauce perfect compliment. The service is horrible be prepared to wait bit if u ask me its worth it. My second best taco spot.
my plate stunck! like some put they penis and the corn muffing was so dry. Â the food was not so great like the food network emphesizes.

Sips & Bites catered our wedding reception and it couldn't have gone better. We are both so grateful to the staff for helping the event go so smoothly! Nicole, the catering manager was beyond friendly and always quick to respond to changes and questions throughout the entire process. At the party, the chef was so organized and helpful. She was also just plain nice. I got a glass of red wine knocked all down the front of my dress (it came out no problem), and the chef ran to the bathroom to help and to ask if she should send a staff member for club soda. So, so, so great. My friends RAVED about the food, the waitstaff (besides being some of the best-looking people I've ever seen) were ON POINT. Constantly with a tray of amazing food and worked the room with a smile. HIRE THESE FOLKS!!!

Inside Bianca the decor is understated and the tables are tight.. the food is memorable. Started with fried artichoke - never heard of it before so we went for it. It's kind of an earthy/ woody taste. It didnt do much for me, but my friend liked it. When i said memorable, I was referring to the lasagna and tiramisu (although now that i think about it, the fried artichoke was pretty memorable just not in the best way). The lasagna is a huge portion but delicious nonetheless. It's got tons of meat and many many layers. So good - i want one right now! The tiramisu is probably one of the best i've ever had. Super creamy and light. I want that too!! Definitely will be returning with CASH because it's CASH ONLY.

The most satisfying dinner of the past few months. Â Pull out $20 from the ATM, grab a buddy and a sixer of Modelo from the bodego next door, then pop in for some mofongo. Â You're gonna want to use the extra $4 for a tip, if only to say it was the best 20 bucks you ever spent. Sure, the food didn't make me cream my jeans, but it did help me overcome my fear of mofongo, perhaps the least dignified of national delicacies -- Â a sticky, starchy lump of plantains and fried pork chunks that is usually so dry it takes a whole pitcher of gravy to allow a fork to pass through it. Â Casa Adela's was perfectly moist and came with an awesome garlic butter sauce, full of all sorts of spices -- I got monfongo'd. The biggest sell, though, is the atmosphere -- it's an authentic neighborhood dirty spoon, the cooks standing at the counter drinking beer and cracking jokes between orders. Â English is a second language here, which is fine because I love going to restaurants where I can practice my Spanish and not feel like a prick. Â BYOB, pay at the register, and hairnets is my gold standard from now on, assuming there's also some rice and beans floating around the room.

Simplicity, appropriate volume, reasonably priced wine & variety of pleasing menu in cozy atmosphere. FOOD - refreshing poached egg green salad w/ pine nuts, mussels w/ herbs + wine was cooked properly and served at right temperature in a crafty pot that the cover served as empty shell dish. Â The crunchy fries was mouth watering. ATMOSPHERE - simplicity, bare bone decor style of table setup is appealing. Hard for a Gunner to cheer for PSG, but we can overlook the fact. Â Dining in the restaurant gives you the feeling of being transported to a nostalgic French small town. Â Efficient service and hospitable. LOGISTICS - easy to get to at 3rd Ave & 33rd St in Murray Hill area. CREATIVITY - for future evaluation.
Food was tasty, great prices

Delicious food and good service. Pleasant ambiance- a diamond in the rough on an otherwise unimpressive midtown street. A good alternative to the midtown standards when looking for lunch or cocktails after work in the east 40s.
Disgusting burger that tasted like gasoline. Low quality meat. Terrible service. Took a long time and mixed up our order. Can't imagine how this place gets four stars.

Forge gets an A+ for atmosphere. Â It's a great space that is well-designed. Â If you are there with good friends and order some good wine, you are sure to have a delightful time. Forge gets a C+ for food. Â For the prices, it was, sadly, nothing to write home about. Â My "halibut en croute" should have been called "hunk of bland whitefish". Â The foie-gras came with five different kinds of salt-why would I want to put volcanic salt on something that is already so rich, three of us had trouble finishing it? Â The best thing we had all night was the pumpkin creme brulee-a great mix of innovation and taste. Overall, I'd give it a B+. Â Great location, great space, good (not great) food, a little too pricey.

From the moment they started construction on this place, I was eager to check it out. Two Hands has that specific hipster vibe where you just know from looking at it that good coffee is to be found inside. Finally got my chance to check it out yesterday, and while the coffee did not disappoint, everything else did. During my 15-minute wait in line, I decided on an iced coffee and the baked egg roll, only to be told they were sold out of the latter. At 10am. On a Saturday. At a breakfast establishment. I settled for the avo toast. As a lifelong New Yorker, "NYC prices" rarely faze me, but $7 for mashed avocado on a piece of bread the size of an iPhone is ridiculous. They can probably get away with charging these prices since there's nothing else like this place in the neighborhood, but I prefer not to feel like I've been robbed first thing in the morning. Next time I'm in the neighborhood, I'll hit up Baz or Nolita Mart instead. Their decor and coffee is on par with Two Hands', but blessedly come without such a pretentious crowd.

I went to robertas for brunch. Â It was a disaster. Â I waited over 90 minutes for a table, and when I finally sat down, it was another 45 minutes before any food hit the table. Â I felt that it may have been because I went at a peak time, so the following tuesday, I ordered pizza for delivery. Â Yet again, it was a 2 hour wait. Â When the pizza finally arrived, it was cold, the cheese was hard, and the crust was tasteless. Â I was thoroughly disappointed with the quality as well as the service.

Dropped in for a late dinner. We were in the neighborhood and decided to take advantage of a Scoutmob deal, intrigued by the African/French headline. We were pleasantly surprised. A great place for an intimate dinner. Cozy and quaint and the tables have the feel of a dark (but not too dark) corner. We noticed quite a few French-speaking patrons (a sign of authenticity?). In the mood for seafood, we ordered two dishes. The Lobster BLT wasn't bad but the highlight of our meal was the 5 Stars Seafood Risotto, creamy and flavorful, with generous portions of lobster, shrimp, mussels, scallops and calamari in perfectly cooked rice. Great texture and taste, and more than adequate for sharing. Mouth-watering, really. Would recommend this place to all my friends who love seafood, spices and strong flavors.
Great selection of emapnada's very creative choices, small place though. Â Always seems like there is a line so get there early. Â Good prices for food.

buttermilk is at the end of my street which makes me a very lucky man. Â my wife and i go often and usually get the following: - pickles, grilled flatbread, soup (sweat potato and pumpkin in the fall was just as outstanding as the current cauliflower and apple), kale salad, pasta or grilled vegetable platter for the vegetarian mrs and usually the hake or lobster special for myself, and i can easily knock back 4 (or more) of the gentian sling, i would have been more particular about each plate but doug changes the menu based on what is seasonal yes, we eat a lot but the food is that good and fresh that we easily finish it up without feeing regret. Â i try to leave room for the pecan sundae or the salted caramel sweatbread but its not easy. we have been over 20 times at this point and i have tried everything on the menu minus the pork products. Â i would recommend it all. to me, this is one of those places that all new yorkers who enjoy a good night out should try at somepoint, it is a true gem.

to be honest, i think baltahzar is one of those places where the hype has gotten to it ... everyone has heard of it before they even come to NYC, and maybe it's because of that you expect too much, but i do not think it lives up to it. it's crowded, you sit way too close to the other table, and there's always a line out the door for weekend brunch. i think the food itself has that cafeteria assembly line feel ... they sit you down, pour you water, take your order, serve you food, clean it up, and get your bill to you so fast that you just feel it's all very impersonal. probably because they are trying to get you in and out so they can serve all the people still waiting. i didn't think the food was that great and can think of so many better places to eat brunch in nyc, even if you are looking for a trendy atmosphere.

This weekend we decided to venture out of the safety of Fort Greene (we love you, Black Iris!), and we ended up at Runner & Stone. Â After we got done poking at the interestingly textured wall (determining that it was smooth but not soft), we turned our attention to the menus. I immediately zeroed in on the South Brooklyn on the drink menu (rittenhouse, dry vermouth, maraschino, saint-germain, bitters? Â um, yes.), and it was even better than I imagined. Â I like a drink that's strong but doesn't feel as though I'm lighting my esophagus on fire, and this more than fit the bill. We started with the grappa-cured striped bass with fennel, which was delicious. Â (Actually, we started with the bread basket, which shouldn't get short shrift - this being a bakery and all.) Â The boyfriend had the campanelle which had duck confit, olives, artichokes, and preserved lemon (and was pretty much fantastic), and I had the fish (which was monkfish that day and also fantastic). Â We pretty much licked our plates clean. Honestly, I would go back on the strength of that cocktail alone.

This place SUCKS!!! Â I don't get it. Â I really don't. Â There's a line at this place pretty much everynight (I pass by it everyday), and the other yelpers recommend it highly, but the food and service is just awful. The first time I ate here I thought the food was dry and bland so I never went back. Â Just recently, I decided to try it again because it must be good if the place is packed day in and day out. Â WRONG!! Â I ordered the red snapper grilled with beets on the side. Â It took 1 hr for me to get my food, the waitress never gave me the beets (I had to request it twice), she never filled my water, and the fish was over cooked and dry AGAIN. My friend fared no better. Â Her dish was absolutely disgusting. Â She ordered the Greek Style Shrimp which basically includes 4 large shrimp DROWNED by a disgusting tomato sauce with Feta cheese. Â UGHHHH!!! So gross. Â She coulnd't even eat it. The only good things were the beets and the free dessert, otherwise this has to be one of the worst restaurants I've ever been too. Â The service was horrible and so was the food. DEF DON'T RECOMMEND IT!!
Gramercy Tavern does tasting menus right. Everything was made expertly and the drinks were poured perfectly to accompany our meal.

Check in at FourSquare and get free beer? That's 2 stars quickly added. Zutto breathes great service, good food, and a fresh environment. They serve a variety of different ramens including wasabi broth and seafood broth. I opted for the seafood ($16) one cause you know what they say when it burns going in... The noodles were perfectly cooked, broth was rich and flavorful and they really give you a good amount of sides and if it wasn't enough you're welcomed to order extra of everything. Let's just hope it lives up to its name.

Ok this is my new favorite Indian takeout! Ha the mulltawny soup which was delish and the chicken tikka masala. Everything was fresh. The jasmine rice is so buttery and you can eat it alone. I take away one star since i called once at 4:05 and they said they were closed until 5 then I called later and it took 45 min. Â I was starving but it was worth it.
Nice bar with an East Village feel. Â Too bad the crowd is super-douche/wannabe douche especially on the weekends. Â Plus, management does not know how to handle drunks.

Went here for dinner last evening with out of town guests who wanted to experience something different. Â From the moment we walked in Roman greeted us like we were family and showed us to our lovely table and continued to treat us as if we were guests in her home throughout the evening. Â Never once did we have to ask for anything. Â Water was refilled throughout the meal and full attention paid to us. Â The food was delicious and met every expectation and even those Roman recommended were as good as she promised. Â Fabulous experience, great decor, great food, great service!

Happened to be hungry and searching the area for something different and luckily came upon Ba'al. Â I had the hummus platter, which comes with two sides. Â The zaatar fries were awesome. Â For $7 bucks, an entire platter of tasty, filling food is a rarity in NYC. Â I will definitely return.

It was an awesome experience from the minute we sat down until just before we got the check. Â That part hurt a little but totally worth it. Â It was nice to see Korean food showcased with so much artistry.

I have eaten here 4 or 5 times since it opened. The calm fettucini is like heaven. The burger is one of the best in Brooklyn. Great cocktails--The Bees Knees is dangerous and delicious. Oyster are always good. Friendly staff and nice owners. This is my favorite new place.

I LOVED IT! Had the combo 1/4 chicken and pulled pork! Really good! Had the greens- THAT ROCKED!!!! The mac n cheese was good, tho I was slightly disappointed. I also had the Donkey Punch- YES, YES, YES! The service was definitely 5- star. I can't wait to go back again. So many other things to try!

An indisputable 5 stars for the price. The food is harder to rate. Quality and taste varies from dish to dish. Here are the best dishes I've tried (and the only ones I would recommend): -pork and chive dumplings. The only good dumplings they have are fried, and the only fried dumplings have pork. -sesame sandwich with vegetables: probably more calories than a bagel or donut combined, but cheap and filling -tofu soup with duck bone-marrow broth: oily but flavorful and filling -wonton soup: a good start, but hot sauce and soy sauce required -steamed vegetable bun: good value + generous amount of veggies To avoid: -any type of steamed dumplings (borderline gross and not tasty) -fish ball soup (as bland as it gets. soy sauce won't save it) -sesame with egg: it really tastes like the egg was cooked in pork fat. -most of their soups are bland. I wouldn't recommend ordering them unless you are not that picky.
You will love the burger and service! The Irish Waiter is a sweetheart:-)

Hands down, my first time trying Filipino food set a very high standard for the above this cuisine. I do not want to create a proclamation statement over here but YOU HAVE TO TRY Kaldereta and Laing. Their mustard rice also hit the spot. Our server was very cool and helped us with choices. Come here with a group of people or by yourself...no one should distract you from Kalangitan Â (Heaven) ;)

Holy crap! I cannot believe how delicious and cheap this place is. I paid $3 for a hummus and tabouleh sandwich that was truly amazing. I had the pleasure of eating here last week after catching a show at the Comedy Cellar. It was a perfect ending to a great night. This is the perfect midnight (or later) snack after a night out!

Came here one day with the roommate for dinner. Â We were both pretty hungry so we ordered a decent amount of food. Â The place is BYOB so that's pretty cool. Â I came here awhile back so I was looking at the menu to refresh my memory, but I don't see the wings on there. Â Hopefully they didn't remove it because those were some of the best wings I've ever had. Â Not your typical buffalo style wings drenched in hot sauce. Â This was a deep fried wing with more of tempura batter topped with a sweet soy sauce mixture and sriacha. Â Just a great combo. Â We split an order of the fried chicken sandwich (humongous), and the animal burger. Â We also ordered mac & cheese but I'm pretty sure it wasn't the bacon/scallion that's currently on their menu and not the regular one. Â Oh well, I just remember it was delicious! I've been hoping to make another trip but not before getting some exercise in. Â The name of the place is perfect because it's serving comfort food. Â Mmmmmmm

The pork bone ramen here is outstanding. The pork belly, eggs, noodles, and veg were all top notch and the broth was truly flavorful. I also had the kale salad, which was also excellent (if maybe a tad over-dressed). The reason this is a 3-star review and not a 4-star or more review is that I just think it's exceedingly tacky to have a cash-only restaurant that has an ATM that charges $2.25 and only dispenses up to $140. The McDonalds across the street has a .99c ATM that I can get $200 from. Â I know this sounds petty, but little stuff like this drives me crazy.

Welcome to the LES!! Welcome to the Orchard Street family!! The pork taco, margarita GREAT!!! They really are the real deal.. GO NOW~!!! before word gets out and you can't get a seat or a meal!! hurry...

I dream about this kind of pizza. Thin crust with sweet tomato sauce and just the right amount of cheese. They have a wood fired pizza oven, and it really makes a difference. There are a few seats in this take-out spot. Quick service from old timey pizza guys. Wish they would open another location uptown!

This is just a straight up divey bar that serves a mean burger. Â For the price, this is the best burger you'll get in the city. Â I like to describe it as a really good homemade burger. Â Besides having some of the best burgers, this place has cheap beer, and McSorley's on tap.

If you want Italian food that is cooked by a nice grandmother - come here! The menu changes with the cook so there is always something new to try. The appetizers were great as well as all the main dishes. The wine selection they have is great and pretty big and reasonable. Â The trek to Staten Island is worth it, and its really close to the ferry so its more of an adventure to get there then a trek!

Visited the Park Avenue Tavern a couple of nights while staying nearby. I didn't partake of the food...but the beer selection was great. However, the highlight of both visits was Richard. Richard is crazy. I don't know if he's like that all the time, or if he'd just had too much caffeine, but man, that dude was insane. It definitely made for a memorable experience!
This place serves good crust pizza. Also they have italian cusine. I like their spinach and pancetta salad. If you are finding pizza in Chelsea, This would be a good option.

Really fresh food, ambience is good. Cozy little place. Good location. Loved their falafel along with their hummus. Just enough seasonings. Spicy falafel was my favorite. Little falafels were easy to eat. Very good smoothies. Great for take out. Nice people. Everything is in great balance. No complains.
I went on a Friday night. Great service great food and great wine. If you are looking for a nice meal and laid back servers this is your place. I will be coming back very soon.

For the west Villiage this restaurant is a hidden jewel. Â The prices are very reasonable, including the wine list,mthe food fresh and very tasty, plus the service is excellent.
