Â It is a warm and cozy place, we went on a Saturday night around 6:30 and within 10 minutes after we were seated, the restaurant was full.

So, you're looking for a great steak and don't want to break the bank. Â Well, Landmarc is your place. Â Whether you're craving hangar or strip -- and an incredible glass of wine to match-- Landmarc can offer the variety and know how you want from this kind of place. Â The appetizers -- from calamari to bone marrow-- are amazing. Â The desserts are even better. Â And, best of all, the wine list affordable, offering choices by glass and half bottle to allow access to a variety of options. Â Try the Ridge vineyards wines - they are truly my favorite. That said, I just ate at their new restaurant Ditch Plains, and it makes me think twice about recommending this place. Â  I hope that the service there isn't an indication that this place is going downhill.
OMG had the Cajin crawfish. I'm addicted!!! Going back with friends for more and to try their other dishes. Can't wait!

EXTREMELY delicious food. I had the Caprese salad and the spicy sausage pizza, both of which tasted as good as, and if not better than, Italian food in Italy. The mozzarella in the caprese was almost a religious experience and the pizza was SUPERB. I was still experiencing lovely aftertaste a few hours later. The service was great, the guy seemed genuinely excited to be working there, the outdoor seating area is nice, and I just loved eating here. This is about as high-quality as it gets for Italian food!

Not just for brunch. Went for lunch and was pleased with the food and service. A kielbasa and kale soup was savory and attractively presented in a large bowl. This was followed by a lamb sandwich with a nice portion of fries. The lamb was well seasoned, and presented with grilled onions in pita, harissa on the side. My companion's vegetarian plate featured good portions of Â hummus and tabbouleh , both savory and well-prepared. I believe there was baba ghanouj as well but the plate was swiftly dispatched. The ambiance was casual and well worn, and suitable to the terroir. Look forward to a return visit.
Very nice pork buns!!

Love love love this place! I'm a weird lacto-intolerant gal who can have goat chees for some strange reason... They have a goat Gouda wih bacon, avocado & chÃ¨vre that is to do die for. First legit (non-gross soy "fake cheese) grilled cheese in over a decade. I am one happy grateful camper.

i've been here twice and neither time participated in the actual choosing and ordering of items (if a menu is more than 2 pages long i tend to get overwhelmed), but it was pretty good the first time and the second time i got punched in the face with deliciousness! definitely get the sarang burong, which is all sorts of meat and veggies in a taro basket. Â  what's a taro basket? a fried basket of mashed tasty-ness made of a strange root vegetable, that's what. it's been a few days since i've been here but i keep dreaming about the sarang burong. Â mmmm...... went with 4 friends and everyone was stuffed to the gills and even had a beer each, and the total came out to a measly $25/person including a generous tip.

Cute little place with little chairs and tables with holes in them that you can put your fries through :) And the ladies who work there were very friendly. The fries were good, very substantial and filling. I'm a fan of the wasabi mayo ^.^ A regular size is more than enough for two people.

Had a great dinner at Becco. Tatiana our waitress was amazing. Â If you are not going to a show let them know so you can take your time. I had the Branzino and my wife had the Beal Piccata. Â Also great wine list for only $25.

Years ago I used to LOVE Jack the Horse Tavern. Over the last year, however, I have noticed a discrete change in its quality of service. I have returned dishes to the kitchen each and every time I have been there over the last year because they were either cold or undercooked. It seems as if the kitchen is suffering from quite a bit of mismanagement, and unfortunately there are lots of timing mishaps as a result. It is sad because the cooks are obviously putting quite a bit of effort into food prep, only to have the staff to ruin the meal with poor execution.
One of the best sandwiches I ever had - but they are to small :)
even my white friend likes it! haha..the place is hard to find, but I look for it everytime i am in new york

Went back today with my boyfriend! He got the shrimp and grits and I got the jambalaya with the biscuits with sausage gravy....my boyfriend loves the biscuits. My jambalaya was nice and spicy and filled with shrimp and chicken, they definitely wasn't cheap with that. We didn't even break $50. Our server was super funny and very nice!! Definitely a permanent spot for me I'M SOLD!!!

Hooray for Panino Rustico!! My coworkers and I often order delivery from here because their paninis are fresh, plentiful, and delicious. They always get our orders right and delivery is quick and efficient!

Had my birthday here this year . Party of just over 20 and we had the tasting menu . Everything that was brought out was delicious . The scallops and lamb meatballs were some of my favorites. Drinks were awesome . This place is on point . Would recommend and would go back . Traif is next on my list to try!
Tasty, different, and classy. Nice little wine and pizza place located in a pretty random spot close to the river. Will be back!

I liked Alfie's a lot. Â it's a cool beer bar with above average bar food. Â I came here on a Sunday night for dinner with a friend and we really enjoyed everything. Â Our waitress was very sweet and super attentive; couldn't have asked for better. Â Ambiance was also nice and they play really good music. Â Would definitely return.

I love this place. Â It's a simple restaurant in Sunnyside with friendly service. Â The food is incredibly delicious, and seasoned to perfection. Â The dining experience starts with complimentary bacon fat popcorn. Â From the menu, I recommend the Fried Brussel Sprouts, Fried Chicken, and Striped Bass. Â The meal ends with a complimentary shot of a Korean yogurt for dessert. Â All in all, Salt & Fat makes for a great meal, and a great place to eat with friends or a date.

This place is a literally a hole-in-the-wall...space is quite limited. But, if you can land a spot, you're in for a treat. We tried the octopus (special), lamb chops, steak tagliatelle (special), and tuna tartar. The octopus dish was amazing...probably the best I've ever had. The lamb was very nicely cooked and quite flavorful. The tuna tartar was fresh and was well-complemented with avocado. The steak tagliatelle a classic take on bolognese and very tasty as well. We had a 2011 cabernet sauvignon (forget the vineyard), but paired with our small plates very nicely. For dessert, we had the ricotta cheesecake, which was not too heavily and went well with a solid cappuccino. Best worth a return trip, with many likely to follow.

I ate here almost two months ago and I'm disappointed that its taken me this long to write a review. Osteria Morini is very worthy of high praise as one of the best Italian restaurants in the city. Now I can't remember exactly what I ordered, but I do remember everything being top notch good. I believe we started with a selection of 3 meats and cheeses to share and maybe one other appetizer for the table. Everything was excellent and the service did a great job helping us pick out the meat and cheeses and explaining them when it arrived. For entree's we all went with pasta and nobody regretted that decision. The pasta was extraordinarily succulent. So soft and airy you can tell it was made in house. I literally enjoyed every bite until my dish was completely wiped clean. The whole meal was delicious. With 2 bottles of wine the bill came to about $100 a person for a party of four. Yes, on the pricier side but sometimes you have to spend a little to get a little.

Not only do they have one of the best falafel sandwiches in America, with fabulous pickled cabbage, fresh egyptian falafels, and a perfect bouquet of flavors, but it's only $3 and the guys are really nice. They've been my favorite fast food in NY since '04, when I first came to town. And I met my wife on the Subway because I stopped to get a falafel sandwich here 4 years ago, on the way to Central Park. Now that's good service!

Clinton St. Baking Company is one of those brunch places in NYC that gets a lot of press. Â Everyone says, "You HAVE try their pancakes." Â However, after yet another visit to a place that everyone raves about, I left completely underwhelmed. Â The blueberry pancakes were tasty, but they were not the best pancakes I have ever had. Â They were not light an airy, but thick and left me feeling overly full. Â  If you are a foodie like me who has to try this place despite my review, make sure you visit on a weekday rather than a weekend when you will have to wait over an hour to eat.

Seated at the bar and receiving excellent service from Courtney our anniversary dinner was a pleasure to be enjoyed. Â This smallish village establishment has a well deserved reputation based on their delicious food - great service - cool ambiance. Â A decent, although short and pricy, wine list rounds out the dining experience. A bit pricy but worth it for a special occasion or merely a stop after a hectic day at the office - We will return again!

Considering i live in jersey and i drive out there ...pay 8 dollars for toll and deal with city traffic and angry taxi cab drivers JUST to grab a platter ...at least once or twice a week...i say its GOOD!....However if u're looking for quality over quantity, this is not the place for u...its a lot of food..and dont get me wrong, its good food but its still street food and its exposed to new york city pollution....but when u' ve spent a couple of hours drinking and u need to grab a bite at 4am....THIS IS THE PLACE!

$1 for 5 dumplings, enough said. I was visiting NY and my friend recommended this place. So glad I stopped in, the dumplings are cooked right before your eyes. No frills, super cheap and really delicious. Reminded me of the night market street vendor food in Taiwan with a price to match. The place is tiny, so you have to get your food to go. Pan fried or boiled, can't go wrong. Better yet, get 5 of both.

This review is solely for the drinks because I HATE the food. Mix the Sangria and Margarita and BOOM you have a nice drink. The atmosphere is very friendly - you have people with dogs outside, along with mothers and fathers and strollers. Inside you have an island to eat at (uncomfortable at times because the line gets long and you find yourself struggling to eat) Â They also have booths (not many) Either way, I have gone to this place a handful of times and enjoy the drinks and nice atmosphere outside! CASH ONLY PLACE - Please remember that!

Best bahn mi I've had in a very long time. Â Steaming hot!! Â I forgot to request the whole wheat baguette because I didn't see it listed on the menu. Â I only knew about it from reading Yelp reviews. Â Next time...if I'm ever in the area again. Â Made a stop here for quick lunch before going to Brooklyn Bead Box down the street. Â I ordered the shredded chicken but they gave me grilled instead. Â No prob because it was freak'n fantastic!!! Â I'm normally a white meat only kind of gal but the dark meat wasn't overly greasy and didn't have that "meaty" taste to it. Â I ordered mine Medium spicy which was in fact medium spicy. Â No extra condiments needed. Â I loved how the bread was oh so warm...crunchy on the outside, super soft on the inside. Â A very good amount of meat and carrot/daikon mix. Â I also got a small Taro Bubble Tea to wash it all down. Â That was fantastic as well. It wasn't overly sweet and was actually refreshing. Â I'm just sad that I live in Queens and rarely make my way to BK. Â I highly recommend this spot for a quick lunch. Â Super popular. Â 1:30pm on a Sunday and it was packed with a continuous flow of customers. Â A very good sign. Â Yum!

i've been here twice. the first time a few years ago, and the later recently. i didn't consider the pancakes to be necessarily fluffy or all that tasty. I really didn't care for the butter maple syrup which was like lard. this place has a lot of tourists

My favorite lunch spot in the entire city. Sophie's is the perfect place for a to-go lunch in FiDi, quick and delicious, with huge serving sizes and fair prices. As a summer intern working in the WTC, I found myself at Sophie's at least twice a week. The killer combination is their spicy chicken with beans and rice, but really their entire menu is gold. Highest recommendation.
Great food. Â Wait for food was a bit long but worth it. Â Wish they had a larger space. Â Great Italian good in Park Slope does exist! Â Definitely going back.

Came in from Texas at the recommendation of a native New Yorker .... Totally worth the train ride! Ordered the Lil Stinker and my sister ordered the cheeseburger .... Both cooked to perfection. The pizza had so much flavor, and the drinks were sufficiently loaded. I'd recommend to anyone visiting

I'd received a couple of recommendations for Market Table, so as part of the food safari my husband and I are on, I thought we'd give it a try. Â You know what? Â It was a disappointment for us. Â While my pan-roasted chicken was very good -- I think it's about as good as chicken gets - oddly, the halibut ordered by my husband was unremarkable. Â I say 'oddly' because it is one of the more expensive items on the menu, and Â it really fell short Â (description: Â "flavorless"...) We began the meal with the beet salad, and I have to say that was excellent but not a real differentiator -- we're running into equally good or better beet salads in just about every decent eating establishment in the City. Â  So that wouldn't be enough to bring us back in. I might be convinced to give it another try if it weren't for this: when we left, every inch of us smelled like we'd been working in the kitchen - clothes, hair, even my handbag. Â  Ick. Â It smells good when you're going to eat it, but not when you're having to wear it for the rest of the night. Â Glad we skipped the dessert so we could pay the dry cleaning bill. Â  This one doesn't make my all star list, sorry.

I work downtown and had never tried Adrienne's Pizza Bar although I heard great reviews from several people in the office. Â I went to dinner with my sister on a Friday night and it was very crowded, but we were seated right away. Â The seating at the restaurant is very, very, VERY close to your neighbors, a point that I will refer to later on. We both ordered drinks from the bar and they were fine and reasonably priced. For our meal we ordered a pepperoni pizza. Â The pizza itself was delicious! Â Although somewhere between bread and the pizza the couple next to us began arguing about each our infidelities. Â My sister and I were basically sitting in the fighting couple's lap. Â I'm not joking; I was literally only a few inches from the man in the couple. Â Suffice to say, glasses were knocked off tables and food tossed across the table. Â We felt like we were on Punked or some other stupid game show, but it wasn't a joke. Â Clearly any proximity to this would have been horrific, but even if they had been whispering, I would have still heard every word. All in all, for dinner and show, the price was reasonable. Â The food was great and the atmosphere (sans crazy couple) would have been great had there been a few more inches, feet between neighboring parties. Â Ah, well, I will definitely be back.
Great friendly service. Thin crust pizza is awesome. I had the spicy sopressatta & buffalo mozzarella pie and it was perfect!

We were just here earlier today for our anniversary date, we were at the main dining toom. I just have to give three stars and i will explain why. First, the three stars is actually for the attentive service, warm decor, very kind comp as the anniversary gift. If it weren't for the service I really don't think gramercy would get the three stars. Second, to me when you are dining out at a place like Gramercy Tavern- I would rather see a well executed dish than all other things. I think the food should be the center of everything, i would rather recieve an okay service but awesome food and not the other way around. First course: squid ink pasta with whatever it was- it was just okay there was nothing special. Ruby red shrimp-the shrimp was cooked perfectly but it was just bleh..it's coated in sesame and some peas puree. I was disappointed. Second course: sea bass with peanut curry sauce. I appreciate the freshness and a perfectly cooked bass but come on...the curry just killed the whole dish. Lamb was good but it could use a little bit more component-i have to say that i enjoyed the tatsoi and hen of the wood mushroom. Maybe it was just a fluke that I had to experienced, i hope it was since its coming from one michelin star restaurant, at least get the food right. I would probably be back to try the tavern menu, hopefully it's not as disappointing as the main dining room.
Absolutely delicious brunch. Not the largest portions but fabulous food. (We had the scones, pancakes, beef hash and omelet). Yummy.

Japanese comfort food in tiny no frills eatery. The food arrives quickly. I love their curry sauce, it's mild and goes so well with the fried chicken. I prefer the chicken to their shrimp. Even though they are large, you only get two shrimp. Nothing fancy, but a great place for a cheap and quick lunch.
Everything is delectable here, especially the gnocci! I love bringing friends here for their first time. The location is great and the food wonderful.

Being a small little joint situated in a side street around the Garment District, Go Go Curry is one of those hidden gems in NYC. I had heard only good things about this place prior to coming here, and with a hankering for some Japanese curry, I decided to stop by here on a Sunday afternoon with a friend. The place is a shrine to baseball, and most notably, Hideki "Godzilla" Matsui, and being an ardent baseball fan, I felt right at home. Although the cleanliness of the place was somewhat questionable, it was a very rainy day and I could give it a pass. I ended up ordering their Grand Slam meal (you can find it in the pictures below), which included a combination of all their katsus. For less than $15, I received a gigantic meal that when I started out, wasn't all that hungry, but ended up finishing all of it anyways. The katsu wasn't all that oily and the curry was just right, not too sweet or spicy. Overall, I was very satisfied with my meal and would definitely come here again. Inexpensive meal, great food, and fast service (at least when I went). Unless you have quite the stomach and appetite, I'd recommend coming here to split the Grand Slam with another person because I ended up not eating anything else for the day afterwards.

This place is awesome! Â Make sure to get in line early and think before you order ALL the food in the world. Â Go with friends! Â The only draw back to this place is it gives me severe anxiety everytime I try to sit down. Â There are just a bunch of benches and a ton of people saving seats. Â It has always worked out but I can't help it, I wish it were a little easier. Â I'm not going to take too many points away for that because the BBQ is probably the best in NYC. Â Before you go hating on NYC BBQ, let me remind you that this is one of the culinary centers of the World, so there are probably a few others that can stack up against this in the city as well and I bet those can go toe to toe with any other place in the country. Â So at least try it before you judge it. Â Enjoy!

i was denied last week after a 1 1/2 hour wait was insurmountable for my hunger. Â so i came back much earlier (before) 6:30 and walked straight in and plopped myself at the bar. Â ordered up a session while waiting for my friend to arrive. Â i went with everything but the kitchen sink. Â classic balls and tomato sauce. Â the house veg for the night was beets, hummus, cucumber and rocket. Â enjoyed the veg more than the balls. Â the meatballs were still good. Â nice and moist. Â okay this is sounding a little dirty. Â but i'll be back for some more. Â maybe a slider or smash. Â more sides and dessert next time around.

A solid 3. It's good, but not nearly good enough to be worth the wait (and I definitely don't mind waiting hours for ish if it's worth it). Your soup base choices are either chicken or vegetable, which results in a lighter broth compared to the heavier pork-based broths at other joints. That's not necessarily a bad thing. I thought the difference was refreshing. Overall, a tasty bowl of ramen - noodles were perfectly al dente as advertised. However, is it so different and tasty from its competitors that it's worth a 1 to 1.5 hour wait? Hell no. It's worth at most 30 minutes of waiting.
Hands down best place for happy hour and appetizers in Downtown Brooklyn! Great atmosphere, a breath of fresh air in comparison to Fulton street. 2 for 1 happy hour. Rena and Alex are amazing!!

On a recent food truck lunch hunt near the office, I came across this interesting little mobile eatery and was pleasantly surprised. The menu spans across some tasty flavor combos from lemon chicken over cous cous to kofta sandwiches, and the price point settles around $10 for a meal. Chef Samir greets everyone with a warm smile and definitely seems to enjoy his gig, making the experience extra pleasant. My lemon chicken with creamy mayo sauce over couscous had a healthy helping of veggies and was crazy filling, definitely enough to share for two people. The dish itself is not all to dissimilar to halal cart meals I've had, perhaps a bit healthier, but definitely still savory decadent. I'll have to come back to try their sandwiches!

IF YOU ARE HERE FOR THE CORN...GO AROUND THE CORNER!! Please don't wait on the silly line for a table... you can just walk around the corner and there's an older Cafe Habana selling the same corn without a line. Â  The Grilled Mexican Corn is a deal at $2 a pop. Â It delish and one of the most delicious things I've ever ate. Â Srsly.

Called ahead on a Friday night to make sure I had a table for a second date(I wanted a nice night of relaxed conversation) . We walked in and it felt like they we're grateful for the call ahead because we were seated at what seems to be the best spot in the house, a comfortable couch with pillows to match and perfectly sized tables. I could tell within 2 minutes of walking in that it would be a great night, everything seemed just right. Il Baretto did not disappoint from the ambiance to the food/wine pairings and the service. Our waitress was brand new so she seemed a bit nervous, but attentive and thoughtful nonetheless. The friendly owner went around to chat with anyone and everyone in this small wine bar (max capacity is ~30), you could tell he cared about his patrons. The menu isn't overwhelming, has something for everyone, and can best be described as an Italian twist on tapas. Smaller plates for sharing with your friends or date, as a fun and interesting take on your typical Italian eatery. Ordering pizza, salad, pasta, and scallops all to share with my lady friend each dish impressed us both with their quality and originality. We ordered a bottle of wine at the suggestion of the waitress, as neither of us knew much about wine, but we both really enjoyed her choice. Overall, Il Baretto is a fresh, new wine bar with an intriguing combination of small Italian plates and wine pairings at very reason prices ($10-12 per plate). Guys, if you want to impress a girl on a date bring her and I guarantee the night will go as planned... [5/5]
Really good seafood. The spices that are put in the seafood is what I liked most. Waitstaff is fast and very friendly. Make a reservation or you will be waiting a long time.

This is my go-to Udon place near work if I want sit down service. Â If I want to grab and go or something more casual, I usually head to Onya down the block. Great service. Great food. Â An excellent selection of a variety of Udon's and other dishes (curry, teriyaki, etc.). Â All of the dishes I've tried are good and consistent... and an excellent portion. Â I usually start of my lunch with gyoza followed by the karaage udon (fried chicken) or the fish cake udon. Â  Haven't come for happy hour, but I do want to try it given their happy hour pitcher and beer specials. The only gripe is that for ATT customers, phone service in the back of the restaurant sucks big time. Â So be aware of that if you are expecting a call from someone you are meeting up with!

This place is just a fun place to go for lunch or a late afternoon snack. Â The food is very good, but the desserts are wonderful. My wife and some of my friends had the type of very rich desserts which the Viennese are justly famous for. Â As I have to be a little careful, I had the apfel strudel, which was also wonderful. Â If you plan to come for lunch, you should check to make sure the museum is also open that day, as they have a very good collection of early 20th century Austrian art, especially the paintings by Gustav Klimt.
Great service, great food, no complaints. I got the salmon dish. Â It was big and great.

When it's good, it can be very good. The problem is that it's not always good. Â The first couple of times I came here, I was blown away by the food, especially that "secret sauce" they put on the table. Â I love that stuff! Â The shrimp dish I ordered was also great - perfectly cooked, pleasing to the eye, and well spiced. Â Unfortunately, on a couple of return trips, I have found a lack of consistency which has resulted in some disappointment. Â I'm not ready to give up quite yet (it's the sauce), but be forewarned: you pays your money, you takes your chances.

This place is literally a hole in the wall with the best freshly made Rice Rolls (Churng Fun) i've ever had. The rice flour batter is made from scratch and you add whatever toppings you ask for into it. Â The taste and texture is simply amazing and unlimited sauces you can add from the bottles on the counter. Â After Sun Hing Lung I never went back to regular churng fun. unfortunately Â there are no tables or chairs so in order to fully appreciate it you'll to eat on the sidewalk ...LOL.

Oh wow, another five-star review, how terribly original. Sorry. Â Actually, sorry that I'm not sorry. Â This review isn't gunning for original or insightful or poetic or any other literature 101 concepts. Â This is about how good Il Bambino is when it comes to what matters: putting food on a plate, enticing you to put said food in your mouth, and the subsequent yummy sounds you make as you eat the aforementioned food. I've been there twice in the past three days, including the days immediately proceeding and following Thanksgiving, a day notorious for food and such. Â Thanksgiving Eve was a dinner trip with my fiancee: baby string beans, fingerling potato salad, artichoke panini, roast mushroom panini. Â To say the food was good is to say that a lake is damp. My taste buds were in full-on humbuggery mode throughout Thanksgiving, since it wasn't food from Il Bambino--so we went back for brunch on Friday morning (and really, any place that offers a Friday brunch is obviously the best ever). Â If you've never had a breakfast-y panini, you are basically a caveperson, but a fairly uncultured one at that. Â You know the kind, they have a favorite rock, but it's the same old rock everybody has, and never really tries other types of rock for whatever silly reasons. I love my fiancee, but I would leave her for the peanut butter hot chocolate. Â There. Â I said it. Eat at Il Bambino or go fall off a cliff. Â Those are your options.

ONE OF THE BEST RESTAURANTS I HAVE EVER EATEN AT. Also...it sh*ts on Traif ( see my review for that place) Innovative, delicious dishes with amazing service. Aside from the fact that they were pumping 90's hiphop throw backs, our server was one of the coolest chicks ever. I love unpretentious hipsters, they don't come around often but this place with full of them. We didn't dine on any of the entrees but that shall come soon, I just moved around the corner, Nippon Nachos- unbelievable. wonton nachos? heaven on earth. Steak Tartar- Yes, please. Shishito Peppers-- ehhh I didn't hate them but it didn't blow me out of the water. I like a little char on my peppers and the selection of salts were a little strange? Deviled Eggs- YOU'VE GOT TO BE KIDDING ME. I could eat these all day, err day. Tacos- Â Baby Octopus Taco I believe it was.. I didn't have one but my bf loved it. Seriously...EAT HERE.

Here's the trick: DON'T have high hopes for this place. Forget that Yelp is more-or-less urging you to go there. Â That's what we did, and we ended up loving it. We went for a brunch on a Saturday in June. Â I was expecting lines - I thought I read that is was a super popular place in Park Slope - but there was no one at the bar, and only about 8 tables seated inside. Â We were told outside was full, but we came to the conclusion later that they were probably just trying to fill up the inside a little. I was sick, so was not drinking, and our waitress wasn't too pleased about that. Â Too bad she had to let it be known. Â =( BUT, then the food started coming. Â Oh, man, this place is really good. Â I saw another table with the fish tacos, and asked if the order included 1 or 2. Â It came with 2 and a side of surprising salad (you'll see), and plantain bites. Â The tacos were SO good, and very light and fresh despite containing fried fish. Â My wife got the Columbian breakfast. Â HUGE. Â Huge plate full of probably 5 or 6 eggs, and good rice, along with 2 ho-hum empty arepas. The Flan, sadly, is NOT flan as you'd expect. Â It's more like a boring bread-like sweet dessert. Â But the tres leches! Â Oh my God, the tres leches. Â If you love almond flavor (think marzipan), you'll be in heaven! The atmosphere is great in there, too. Â Really, fun, and modern, mixed with local-slice-of-life stuff on the walls. Â And plenty of room. Â I'm so glad to find a restaurant that isn't cramming 100 seats in a space for 60. We'll be back again and again. Â I'm sure.
I use to come here often for lunch. It's better then Veselka! They just need to work on their pizzas..

My food twin is kinda famous on yelp, so when he says, let's go to Traif, you go to Traif. After a bit of a hike and a broken flip flop later, we arrived at an unassuming little space where a little wooden pig with a heart shape on its belly beckoned us to enter. Sitting at the bar, waiting for our table, our bartender recommended we try some refreshing specials. I don't even know what was in my drink but it tasted peachy and minty and went straight to my head. Ten points for you hot tattooed bartender! It was a warm, slightly muggy evening and we were escorted to the back where we had a lovely view of the vines entangling the ceiling and the little garden, an absolute oasis in the middle of Brooklyn. The thing about Traif is that while it reminded me a lot of Animal in Los Angeles in terms of the menu, it definitely had its own New York charm. It was obvious that a lot of thought had gone into the menu and there were some interesting combinations I hadn't seen before. Standouts were the broccoli rabe. The twin is a huge advocate of having something green on his dinner table (something both our mothers have stressed to us time and time again) and it was the perfect choice because it appeases our mothers and was so tender and flavourful I was picking off his plate (much to his dismay). Then came the razor clams. I really don't know why they don't do razor clams at more restaurants in New York. They're so succulent and whatever they did to it at Traif made them a bajillion times (excuse my kiddy talk) better than they normally are. I suggest that you don't skip out on the foie gras. It comes with fluffy/crispy fingerling potatoes that you won't want to miss out. And who can say no to maple syrup yes? I have to say my only disappointment was the lamb meatballs. They tasted just like regular meatballs and I'm not even a fan of pulverised meat. Oh and if you have room for dessert, run, don't walk to get the brown sugar budino. Chocolate at its very best my friends. The bacon donuts were decent too - not your average New York City policeman's donuts I tell you. If you're looking for a sinfully delightful, absolutely un-kosher meal, I suggest you head to Traif immediately and keep going back for more.
Awesome brunch! We loved the brisket hash and the biscuits with gravy. Between the 2 the hash is more flavorful and the biscuits more subtle but both were delicious!

3.5 stars really. I love empanadas (partial to Filipino style empanadas) and so was drawn into this place. The restaurant is on the cramped side but I did see a group dining at the outside tables so, maybe if there was nice weather out and I had a group I would opt for that but inside it can get pretty packed. I came in for lunch at noon yesterday and my fiancÃ© and I were the only other diners inside other than a couple with two kids. Still, service was a lot slower than expected. Didn't get refills on water throughout our entire time there (though we watched the diners next to us get refills). My fiancÃ© had to flag the waiter down several times when they forgot to bring out the empanada he ordered with his burger and when I wanted to order something else. Our waiter also never checked on us after the food was brought out. I ordered 3 empanadas to start-- the brazil, chorizo, and the beef (baked) and the passion fruit shake. Of all three, I liked the brazil the most. The meat was nicely seasoned and I only used the red and green salsa sauces provided out of curiosity. The other two I had to use the sauces on every bite out of necessity. The corn shell was crispy and I actually enjoyed the shell more than I thought I would but the chorizo meat was dry and bland. The ground beef empanada was the worst of the three.. regrettable and forgettable. :\ I wasn't quite full yet and intrigued by the chicharrÃ³nes under the tapas section, ordered them. Fried pork belly with tostones? Yes, please! (I love lechon kawali, fried pork belly Filipino style) While we were waiting for it, the place got really packed and a long line at the counter formed. It got so loud, both parties on both sides of us were practically yelling into our ears. My initial excitement soon faded, replaced by a migraine, and I just wanted to get out of there. By the time the chicharrÃ³nes came, I just took a few bites and asked for a to go box. The need to leave aside, the dish was good and seasoned well. Four chunks on a bed of tostones. Hard to mess up fried pork belly! It was supposed to come with a round of red and green salsa but we didn't get any. Still not sure if I'd come back. At under $3 an empanada, sure it's cheap.. for NYC. But I feel you could get just as good quality for less elsewhere. That said, I do like that they offer a ton of options making it easier to customize your meal and you can walk away from this place sufficiently stuffed for a decent price. If I did return, I'd try out the more frequently ordered empanadas.

Glad I read the reviews before so we were able to quickly find the door (second green door on the right on Morton!). Food was delicious and fresh. Â Between four of us we shared: - Butter clams - Duck leg confit - Lentil Salad - Grilled hanger steak - Cured pork belly - Potato-Cauliflower gratin - Brussel sprouts - Dark Chocolate & Cherry Ganache Everything was yummy but the stand-outs were the duck leg confit, the cured pork belly & the brussel sprouts. Â Yum! Service was great. Â Will definitely be back again!

Went there last Saturday night for my boyfriend's birthday dinner. Â Had made reservations in advance for 9:30pm so we could take advantage of the 4 course menu for $38. Â There was a significant delay in getting seated at our table and our group of four ended up waiting for an hour to get seated. Fortunately, we were in no rush, and they appeased us with a round of free champagne. Once we were seated, things ran smoothly. The food was delicious (i had the salad with bacon and goat cheese, perfectly cooked shrimp, excellent hanger steak, and an amazing chocolate lava cake. Service was excellent. Wine was amazing. I would definitely recommend this place; however, wouldn't come too hungry since you may have to wait a while for your table.

Been going to Distilled since it opened and every time it is consistently (1) amazing and detailed service with a big smile and also (2) delicious mouth watering food and drinks, (3) lively casual sophisticated ambiance. Â What else can you ask for?! Don't miss: - Wings: Â extra crispy on the outside and juicy in the inside. Â Fried wings with a Korean twist. Â Even comes in two size orders so you can get it every time and still save room for trying other plates - Â I order it every time - Popcorn: Â yes it is addictive and it's free! Â Just save room for.... - Duck and Waffles: Â Chef Shane Lyons' creativity shines with this plate. Â Lightly fried duck over melt in your mouth French toast waffles come together with a drizzle of the homemade jalapeÃ±o maple syrup and Thai basil leaves. Â The combination of these is to die for. Â I want to bottle the maple syrup and take it home with me! - Â Cauliflower: Â one of my favorite sides here. Â If you don't like veggies, this will change your mind. Â Same with the mushrooms. - Â Herb and Sprout salad: Â I am not a salad fan but this I get this salad every visit. Â It is a nice light salad to balance the other plates in the meal. Also the candied lemon rinds help too! - Â Tuna Crudo: Â yum! Delicious and light. - Â Desserts: Â chocolate pudding has so many texture and flavors (not what you expect by the name!), s'mores dessert you just can't go wrong. Â  - Cocktails: I am not a huge cocktail fan but Sheldon and Benjamin are so creative. Â They will make anything you want or just pick from the creative menu. This is a great destination restaurant if you don't live in Tribeca or downtown, but a much needed neighborhood spot that you can grab a drink and bite with co-workers, stroll in for a dinner with friends, or go to dinner for a date. The price is right for NYC, the neighborhood, and most importantly the quality service and good. They will cater to your every need unlike many pretentious restaurants. I plan to keep coming back and even host a holiday party or work dinner here soon since they can block off a section of the restaurant. Can't wait to try brunch soon! I should have written this review a long time ago!

This place was very good. The food was great, the service prompt and friendly. The atmosphere here is amazing. While you can order delivery from here, I'd recommend coming in and enjoying the ambiance.

came here about an hour before our show we had to attend about a block away in the theater district. we needed a very nice restaurant to go to for my 30th birthday but in decent time so we couldn't be late for our show. it was just before the dinner time rush and it wasn't as busy as i thought it would be. nothing to really complain about. the food was good. menu had enough to choose from and fast service. i asked to put a rush on the food, but i didn't really have to as it seemed everyone else got their food fast as well.

I was pretty disappointed. I ordered arroz con pollo and the chicken was really overcooked and dry. One of my friends ordered the same thing and his was overcooked too. Â The service was friendly at first, but I I had to ask for a soda like five times, and they started to give me attitude before finally bringing it.

I feel like I have been giving a lot of 5 star reviews lately, but I seem to have hit a string of really good dining experiences. Tried Gyu-Kaku a few weeks back with my cousin and some of her friends. I once went to a traditional Japanese BBQ like this in Japan, but that was years ago and haven't been since. Â It was on a Friday, later in the evening, around 730/8 so there was about a 45 min wait for a table. But when my cousin's friends decided to join us last min they were very accommodating in upgrading our reservation. Another factor eased the wait... HALF PRICE HAPPY HOUR ALL DAY! I have yet to find another place in NY where you can have a draft Japanese import beer AND a lychee martini for a combined price of $8. The drinks are good too so this becomes dangerous. Once we did get seated and the food started arriving, it was at the cyclic rate... I can't even remember there was so much. We ordered the BBQ special for 4 and it came with Soup, Salad, Rice, Noodles, Sashimi, BiBimBop, and those were just the apps. Then the cook it yourself portion of veggies, lobster, chicken, duck, NY strip, scallops, skirt steak, some other cut of steak, it is a legit 16 course meal. And it is fun because it is interactive... They were out of the two Kobe beef dishes, so we didn't receive those but they adjusted our bill -$40 as a result which was fine by me. Desert was included, a sweet red bean paster waffle and s'mores. it was a ton of fun, cheap cheap drinks, and after the reduction on the bill, it was $140 split 4 ways... $30 each for a 16 course meal! The service was friendly and respectful, as are most traditional Japanese restaurants, and it's just a fun atmosphere for a group or first date. Will Definitely return, worth it for drink prices alone!

Always a popular soho spot, the mexicorn here is a thing of legend. I love the shrimp tacos with shredded cabbage, guacamole all wrapped in a corn tortilla. The drinks were a little lackluster and I may just grab a Pacifico next time. Be prepared for a wait...drop your name and hit the shops nearby.

After a rocky start with putting together a reserved table for 12 for my birthday, I had low expectations of what my experience was going to be. For $29 you can have an all-you-can-drink brunch but the fine print is that everyone has to participate at the table. Â That turned into an issue as I, and a few others, do not imbibe but some at our table do. Â So they waived that for us on the trust factor that we wouldn't share drinks. But as the brunch went on (and the alcohol was consumed) everyone's rainy day crankiness melted away and we were able to enjoy some very delightful and yummy fare. On the menu - These are the highlights because we ordered a million things: "The Forager" Â - wild mushroom, truffle oil, ricotta, chives wood-fire pizza - SUPER DELISH Margharita and White Pizzas - everyone loved Crostini with prosciutto and mozz - LOVE IT Fried Calamari with Basil Aioli - I'm not a fan of aioli but this aioli ROCKED Chickpea Fries - Pretty Good, not as good as other apps Sausages with Peppers and Onions - Also DELISH Baked Crepes with Spinach, Ricotta, Tomato Sauce - An unexpected favorite Things you can skip: French Toast - the children liked it but it was nothing mind-blowing Fried Donut Holes - eh, skip it Overall, I would totally come back here for another boozy brunch even if I don't drink. Â I had a great time. Â The food was good. Â The atmosphere trendy but chill.

Service: Attentive, personable, accommodating Decor: Cool, enchanting, laid-back Food: Phenomenal, addictive, delicious In a word: Amazing! Anytime I wanted to ask for something, BOOM: there it was before I could finish turning my head! A napkin, more bread, water. Amazing! Both times I've been over the past few months the staff has been exceptional. We tried all different items the two times we've been (expect for the Pollo al Aljillo - WOW!!!) and almost everything was mouthwateringly delicious.

I have been around New York and I must say Anthony and Son Panini Shoppe is my absolute favorite place to dine in, there food is AMAZINGGGGGGGGG the absolute best! I love their staff they always greet everyone with a smile and it's just overall good vibes in this place. Their nutella milkshake is wonderful! Delivery is always on time, never late and the food always arrives hot. The owner Sabino is great he is such an easy guy to start a good conversation with, I have never had one negative thing to say about this place. I will always turn to this shop when I want good food around maspeth and brooklyn. On top of the food being amazing I had ask the owner about the meaning of the FDNY sandwich I think it's so kind that this shop dedicates one of their famous sandwiches on the heros of NY. Their is literally no other panini shop better than Anthony and Son Panini Shoppe, I recently found out they cater also, I might even think of having them host one of my company parties, thats how amazing they are I wouldn't turn to any other place but them, forget subways, quality food is at the panini shoppe.

Rubirosa is another wonderful pizza joint! I must confess to you that Â pizza is my weakness. Â I am an addict I cannot imagine my life without pizza. Â With that being said.... I am lucky to be in the best city for pizza. Anyhow, I have always wanted to try Rubirosa but did not want to wait 1.5 to 2 hours to get a seat.... Â on some random evening..we lucked out and found someone who dropped their reservation. Â Whoohoo! We were filled with excitement..,.. finally we get to try: Rubirosa. Let me tell you...no disappointment here... Â We snatched a 8pm reservation and got there 15 min late. Â Thankfully they did not give away our table. Â , underestimating how long New York block are we walked for what seemed like 45 minutes to get to this place, This place was packed to the brim. Â  I ordered a side salad and we ordered the pizza with mozzarella, basil, sausage, and onions. I liked the salad although it did has too much balsamic dressing. Then the pizza came, it looked so beautiful. First off I could see the balls of fresh mozzarella that had melted right onto the pizza. I took one bite and I was in heaven. Everything from the crust, to the cheese, and basil was so fresh - the flavors were so rich. I loved every single bite of that pizza. We ate the whole thing no problem. My mouth was salivating over the warm finely cooked crust and heavenly morsels of mozzarella... Â I had dreams about this so I had to write a review...my mouth was watering for more.... Tip: Trust me...Make a reservation...Waiting sucks!

A great addition to the Upper East Side. As a Falafel fan, I have tasted bad, good and great falafel. Though, cliche' I regard Taim's falafel to be one of the best that I have tasted in NYC. The environment of this place is great. Clean, well organized with a super friendly and helpful staff. The space itself is nice with lots of seating available. I had the falafel pita which was very good. A nice dark crunch on the outside and soft, greenish chickpea mix on the inside. Everything seemed fresh and there was a good variety of toppings/sides, all of which looked great. This place is very new and doesn't have a website or online ordering available yet, though I am sure both will follow. Prices are on par for the area. A falafel pita was $6.95 while the platter was $10ish....
Hand over them pork buns because they are delicious! :) - oh and definitely be ready for a LONG wait for dinner...but it'll be all worth it in the end!
I recommend this place. Fish is fresh. Gets busy and I had to wait for a table for more than 45 min. But it was worth it. Staff was friendly and I liked the beer.
Delish! I had the smoked turkey ruben, and I was very pleased. Yummy slaw, melt sauce, buttered rye toast ... Wash it down with an Arnold Palmer and you're good to go!

Coming to Moto for the first time is like discovering the hidden jewel of Brooklyn. Â The neighborhood is so quiet and bleak, but behind the rusted door and drapes is the hustle and bustle of hipsters in what looks to be the like set of a romantic, sort of steampunk-ish movie. Â The space is so oddly narrow , but no one seems to mind, including me. Â It's unique and cozy, like most popular New York restaurants are. Â  Even on a Monday evening, the wait was about fifteen minutes, but that was fine with us. Â We waited at the bar where I ordered a Black Velvet, which consisted of Guinness and Champagne. Â It sounded like a strange mix, but I was definitely curious. Â And it was actually quite good; the champagne didn't destroy the flavor of the Guinness. Â It was still rich with a nice bubble to it. After squeezing into a table, my friends ordered the artichoke with the saffron mayonnaise. Â I don't particularly like mayonnaise, but the saffron oil made it taste like a light butter. Â Now, I think this is the only way to eat an artichoke. Â Our main courses came shortly after; I ordered the vegetable risotto. Â When ordering this, I was skeptical and I prepared myself to be disappointed with the amount/quality of vegetables or the texture of the risotto (I think I am pretty picky when it comes to risotto). Â But this was cooked perfectly; it wasn't too mushy/saucy or undercooked. Â The spices were light and fresh and it was filled with large strips of colorful vegetables (though mostly peppers). Â I think this could be the best risotto that I have ever had? Â For dessert, we ordered the date cake, of course. Â From previous yelpers, you know that's really the only dessert you get here. Â And you can believe the hype on that.

Food was delicious; very flavorful and authentic. Only thing wrong was there was a bathroom smell that you smelled as soon as you walked in. Kind of ruined the experience a bit. Other customers were affected too.

$4 will get you 2 eggs, potatoes, and greens. That's a deal. (5/5) We also got Steak and egg (4/5). Hard to cut steak with a butter knife. Only downside....long wait. But if it's sunny out, not a problem. You will build up a huge appetite...

Went here after being referred by the barista from Zibetto as having authentic Italian pizza and can't agree with him more. Â Started off with the eggplant pargmigian and it was enough for two, perhaps three. Â  As for the neopolitan pizza...the crust was crispy thin yet so supple. Â Yes, so supple, I could chew on that crust all day long. Â The bufala mozzarella really does have a unique flavor that comes together with the spicy salami that we orered on the Ripieno. Â Though the pizza was good, I couldn't give it five stars, because when compared, Grimaldi's is in another league of its own.

Just stumbled upon this spot on the UWS... Delicious!! Attentive and friendly staff. The special cocktails were both inventive and delicious, and the food was great! My friend and I were just having a light bite to eat, so she had hummus and I had the hummus bowl with chicken. The hummus and accompanying bread was fantastic, and the chicken was perfectly spiced and moist. A great find!
Great food and awesome service we had clams and of course LOBSTER MAC ~n~ Cheese
Favorite food to eat while in the city, they never fail to disappoint. I'd sit out in the blistering cold just to enjoy one of these! I don't know any halal that's better in the city.

I can't tell you how many times this place saved me during my Midtown lunch hour, especially when I needed a break from the Pret-Chipotle-Cosi rut. Cubano sandwiches are pressed by a crusty old timer who'll strike up a conversation with you in Spanish. Ask for black bean or plantains on the side. And the Morir Sonando drink is like an Orange Julius times twenty - frothy condensed milk and citrus. Wow!

awesome food came here as a celebration after my shsat and simply amazing food. it was a very quaint and simply delightful atmosphere. the waiter was above average and we had good service. I had the pekin duck breast which was amazing and my father had the steak and eggs, also amazing . My dish was a little better but the steak and eggs is a much better bang for ur buck, the serving is HUGE, so next time id do the steak and eggs, but once again both were delicious. My sister is a picky eater and orders the chicken everywhere, but the free range chicken was absolutely divine, best chicken I've ever had. The caramelized vegetables,I'm not sure what it was called was very good but the dumplings are a better choice, start off with that. Finally, the waiter was very knowledgable concerning wine and helped my parents pick the perfect wine to pair with their meals. Just very expensive, I feel prices could have been lower by a couple dollars on each dish.

Came here a while back for a friend's birthday with a group of 20 people on a Saturday.. one word - INSANE! The establishment can get a bit over crowded, being that its a tourist spot and everyone assumes its the most authentic food. On the plus side, the food was good for what it was and the portions of course were very large. I think its a bit pricey for the quality but I can see this being a spot to eat before catching a shower in the theater district.

Sauce was delicious. Sat outside and the atmosphere was great. Service was fast and staff were friendly. I got the linguine with eggplant Parmesan and my boyfriend had spaghetti with meatballs. Both dishes were delicious and I was really impressed with the sauce!
Beef meatballs, marinara sauce, on top of brussels sprouts with figs, along with a pomegranate lemonade. Â Outstanding. Â Service is really good.

It's a nice cozy Italian restaurant. I came here for lunch with my brother, first time at the restaurant for the both of us. I'll call it cozy because the restaurant only seats 28 people in a pretty tight space. They did have one table of ten if you want to bring a group of friends but it's mostly tables of 2 and 4. We walked in about noon time on a Wednesday; there were about 8 others in the restaurant at the time. The menu comes in a binder, lots of options here. I went the familiar route, Veal Parmigiana ($21.85). Two large cutlets with fresh vegetables (carrots, broccoli, string beans and potatoes). I was a little surprised not to have a side of pasta for that price. The waiter didn't ask if I even wanted pasta which was really surprising to me. Price wise $21.85 is a little steep compared to other restaurants on the block, this dish averages between $19 and $20. The bread on the table seems like average Italian bread, a little on the dry side. I did appreciate the carafe of ice water on the table. My brother had the Veal Marsala ($21.85) also a generous portion on meat along with the vegetables. We used a $25 gift certificate from Restaurant.com which helped offset the prices on the menu. They do have a fixed price lunch deal for $12, it looks like a good deal. I will say the quality of the food here was outstanding. I loved the sauce on the veal and the vegetables were prepared very nicely. That's a large part of my reasoning for the 4-star rating. As for the atmosphere I was a little on the loud side. Surprising given the cozy atmosphere at this place. Unfortunately we were seated next to a table of gentlemen carrying on with their cell phones during their meal. Apparently one of them just lost a contract for work and was very upset on the phone. This detracted from my overall dining experience. In a small restaurant such a Benito it's hard not to overhead the conversations at the table next to you. We waited 30 minutes for our food to reach the table, a little surprising given the fact there were only eight other people in the restaurant at the time. Other than the wait the service at Benito was very attentive, good job.

GREAT food here, BUT... I went last night (Saturday night) for dinner. Dinner was delicious, but we were rushed rushed rushed through our meal. It was very uncomfortable. Â  We got the meatballs and the gnocchi. We ate at a regular pace, not at all slow. While we were very much still actively sopping up sauce with our bread, and had a couple pieces of bread and lots of sauce left, the waitress came by and scooped up all three plates and walked away. Â I'm not sure why we didn't say anything ( like wait, stop!) But we didn't. Then, as we sat with full drinks, the waitress came by and dropped the check. We paid, left a 20 percent tip, and then continued to chat while finishing our drinks. After only about three minutes, someone came by and asked if we wanted anything else. We said no (we had already paid). It was clear the only reason for their asking this question was to usher us out. Â I repeat, we had mostly full drinks, and had only a few minutes earlier wrapped up dinner. Then, a minute or two after that, they came by and CLEARED OUR WATER GLASSES. Come on Northern Spy - you guys are classier than that. I've worked in a restaurant. I know when you want to turn a table, and the customers are dawdling. But we weren't doing that. Do you really want your customers to feel rushed and unappreciated when they leave? So you make 20 bucks less at the end of the night...isn't what's more important that we leave happy, and keep coming back?
Good and cheap! But the Corned Beef can be a bit fatty. Yummy hash
pretentious dickweeds go here. but once they're here they eat pretty delicious Moroccan inspired French fare. my apologies if you're a pretentious dickweed.

Love this shanghai restaurant. This one and the one on Elizabeth St. The Shanghai Lo Mein is good. Soy Sauced just enough. I ate in here before and the service was good. The crab meat soup buns are yummy too. Plus the scallion pancake. Â The Take Out is in the back of the restaurant, it's an easy transaction. Staffs are friendly, nothing to complaint about.

Whole rotisserie duck lunch. Holy moly. I'm not sure how I can go back to duck dishes anywhere else after this amazing experience. The 4 of us shared pretty much the world's biggest, juiciest duck done 3 ways, with different ways to eat it- naan, gorgeous butter lettuce, rice and a duck soup that will change your life. I've been thinking of this dish for months and still can't get over how amazing it was
black beans very bland.. chicken in the salad ..very bland.. steak salad very very small.
Wow awesome. Â If the dishes on the menu seem appetizing before you go, you'll love it.
Stopped in without a reservation and they were very accommodating. Had a wonderful meal and some fine drinks. Would recommend to anybody.

Took notice of a bustling bar, in what appeared to be a tastefully-assembled venue. Â I ended up sticking to a liquid (largely digestif) diet, after taking a look at what was a seemingly divine menu. Â The raw bar, in particular, piqued my interest and appetite, alike; regrettably, it was a chance drop-in where my time was too limited to try anything. Bar side, a range of liqueurs and old world vino are at the tenders' disposal to potentially prime your palate. Â I appreciated the variety of Italian liqueurs and after-dinner juices, but felt the wine list, on the aggregate, to be narrow in scope and exceptionally over-priced (and YES, I do understand location breeds such). Â Staff was knowledgeable and seemed to be having a good time; the clientele a blend of ages with a uniform felicity.. Â Didn't feel there would be much of a dress code to stress as long as you can somewhat put yourself together. Â Will return in the future

I really love the live band. Def makes the ambiance fun. My boyfriend had the cuban sandwich and I had the lechon asado. I'm a big cuban sandwich person, so when I had a bite of his sandwich...i thought to myself, is that a cucumber? Don't tell me you replaced the pickles with cucumbers. The sandwich overall wasn't bad though. My meal was pretty good, little bit on the sweet side with the lechon. The rice and beans was good. I decided to take my chocolate rum cake to go....i ordered that because it said lava cake...might as well go to chilis for a lava cake because it's alot better. The service was really good, the waitress was really nice and attentive. So hence thats why they got for stars.

Ramen....Yummm.... drooling thinking about Totto's spicy Ramen. Â It's the same as the Totto Chicken Paitan Ramen, but with a large scoop of spicy sauce on top of the ramen. Â  The spice scoop on the side gives you a chance to taste the brooth, and then mix in the peppers as you like. Â  The noodles are nice and springy, and the chashu are awesome. Â Like most of ramen places, you can also add side items, like additional egg, or spicy bamboo (very spicy). Â We also the tuna tartar, pretty good, but not great. Â  The place is pretty small, and there's always a line. Â Best time to go: Weekday - Mon-Thursday, at around 4:30 -5 PM. Â This is when most people are still at work. Â We go there first, and then go back to work afterwards. Â No lines Otherwise take a late lunch - around 1 PM Don't try over the weekend.

3 stars Soba-ya has been one of the few japanese restaurants that consistently has been in my rotation ever since it opened. Â I average 2-4 meals at Soba-ya a month and have had virtually everything on the menu. It has time and time again provide to be a good value. Â  The portions are smaller given what they used to serve but I think its consistent with what your seeing across the city given the rise in food costs. As far as apps go: My fav is the Â yuba sashimi, which is tofu wrapped in yuba raw bean curd. I know of no other restaurant at this price level that would even think about giving you real wasabi with a $6.50 app. Â Kudos for real fresh minced wasabi root. Moving on to entrees: The Soba noodles are made in house and you can witness it first hand as there is generally a fellow making them for all to see in the main dining room. I prefer taking my soba the good ole fashion way which is cold with a little wasabi and dipped in the sauce that they provide. Otherwise I really enjoy the various sashimi "Dons" aka sashimi over rice bowl. The top Don in my humble opinion is the Salmon Oyako which is fresh salmon sashimi and salmon roe and of course real wasabi. #2 on my list is the Tuna Steak with garlic sauce over rice. Â I think of it more as butter sauce because it taste like butta! #3 Is the fresh Tuna Sashimi over rice. #4 The Bara sashimi, think of it as a minced Chirashi over rice that includes Tuna, Salmon, Amberjack, eel, shrimp,squid,omelette, cucumber and shitake mushrooms. Last but not least, one of the most simple desserts that tastes great is the Milk Tofu, its a cross between Tofu custard and jello. i would say there best value is the lunch menu during the week and on Sundays. Â  Expect to spend about $30 bucks with tip if you go for entree and app.

My favorite brick oven pizza in NYC. Â My fiancee and I go there whenever we're in the mood for pizza. Â We LOVE the portobello pizza with caramelized onions. Absolutely delicious. Â I wish the tables were a drop bigger, but it still works for a local neighborhood place. Â Really great spot during the summer when the outdoor picnic tables are out. Â I like their salads too.

Came here 5 or so more times since previous review. food is always incredible. house eggs with a creamy tomato sauce for brunch is spec-fucking-tacular. i could literally put that sauce on wood chips and be content.

Food was slow in coming but worth the wait. Â I had a white bean and kale soup which was great. And a well-portioned pulled pork sandwich which didn't disappoint. Â Nice ambiance. Polite, attentive staff. Â I'd go back...

I have been to Kilo for dinner on several occasions. Â I have found that not much on the menu grabbed me, but actually I have enjoyed nearly every dish I've had there. Â I highly recommend Kilo to all foodies, as both quality and presentation are top notch. Â Try the octopus on the current menu, which has chickpeas and chorizo! Â Whereas some options change weekly, I was told that the octopus will be on for awhile. Â  I appreciate that many of the staff here are highly knowledgeable of the food and drinks available and are very passionate about what they are serving.
This place makes my heart sing! sooo darn good
Many happy things are happening at the espresso counter in front. Â The food is also good.
service was horrible but food was outstanding

I would give this place 5 stars for food. It's really really good. I can't stop getting the squid tacos because it's quite uncommon and it makes me eat my own fingers. They have great concepts for margarita flavors. I am in love with the idea of habenero infused grapefruit...they warn you that it is spicy. I eat things REALLY spicy. So of course I'm like bring it. At times - its perfect albeit it does give me heartburn as I am drinking it and I think heartburn makes for a faster buzz. However, there have been other occasions when drinking it is just unpleasant. I've never had to water anything down. I've been in Thailand countless times. I was eating live chilis at the age of 6. But really, ridiculously spicy alcoholic beverages isn't ideal. Also- the 1 missing star is for the influx of annoying bridge and tunnel or financial people that hang out in the Lower East Side. I live in the immediate neighborhood. It's a drag to show up at this place at 7 on a Tuesday night for dinner and have it be packed and packed by people who act with that sense of entitlement. Give me a break and go back to the upper east side or Long Island.
Great Sangria, delicious tapas, the wait staff is great! Â It can be a lil overwhelming when crowded but they make it cozy and comfortable for everyone :)
Great restaurant in the theatre district! The meatballs were spectacular. My mom tried the three pasta special which was really nice. I had the salmon which I highly recommend!

Happy hour until 10 o clock- sold! Their happy hour drink menu consists of: lychee martinis, white and red sangria, and $4 glasses of wine, among other things. Â  The appetizers are not on sale, they're around $8-12, and really delicious. I recommend the shrimp spring rolls with peanut sauce (they're thick here, not skinny like some places), curry puffs (REALLY spicy!), ginger chicken wings and the chicken sticks with jasmine rice. Probably everything on the menu is good. We're usually standing at the bar, but if you sit down, the waitress service is suprisingly efficient, considering how crowded it gets. Enjoy!
This is one of our favorite places for a last minute dinner. Their pickles are excellent, the soul food is hearty and their Â Kentucky Porch Sipper is a Bourbon cocktail done right.

Good but not great. It's a shame that I had num pang's bahn mi because I will now compare all others to that perfection. Saigon Shack's bahn mi was just ok. I did however love the summer rolls. You can't really mess those up. I tried the beef ball pho which was great until I had a huge piece of gristle in the first beef ball. It's game over once I get gristle. That was my first time trying it. Maybe gristle is standard in beef ball pho? Â I hope not, but the broth and noodles at Saigon Shack were very good. The service was good, but I will probably just try other places for pho next time. Â The vermicelli bowls looked good. Â Perhaps I ordered the wrong thing.

Even though this place is pretty pricey for a graduate student, I still bring my friends who love chicken and waffles to this place. I love love the chicken and red velvet waffles. The last time I went was during New Years Eve, and I had the fried oyster appetizer--can you say freakin amazing? I was surprised it wasn't completely packed, but that was good for us since we didn't have a reservation. The live music (violinist) in addition to the music was great. I can't get enough of this place!

I did the pre fix wine pairing lunch. First the service and decor and ambiance is terrific.The food was overrated and was expensive to say the least. The chef still uses a lot of foam in their presentations which I was never a fan of. If I go back again I will order off the menu as opposed to the tasting menu . I just spent a weekend at the Inn In Little Washington and the food was spectacular and dwarfed my experience at Bouley.

Delicious food! Fast service! Well priced! Â At a non standard meal time the restaurant was full when (with lots of locals as well as tourists) every other restaurant within 5 blocks had no more then 3 tables. One thing to note is it is cash only, and a little hard to find.

I was told this place was really good so I visited it on my last trip to NY. We ordered several dishes and they were all good. We ordered for wine, Gruner Svenlitner, which was perfect pairing with our food selection. Next time I would like to order the Peking Duck if I go with a group of friends. It looked delicious. Service was good and ambiance is casual.

A super cute spot in Park Slope! Came here for brunch around noon and barely missed the mad brunch rush. Brunch for prix fixe $14 was very reasonable. I recommend the Spring Frittata and the rose water lemonade, which was very refreshing on a warm summer day. Tried this place for the first time during Brooklyn Restaurant Week, and ordered their roast chicken - delicious and moist! You can't really go wrong with any of their dishes. Service was slow but friendly.

So far, the best meal I've had in 2014 has been the tasting menu at Traif. So good that after I finished typing that first sentence a few seconds ago, I had to take a deep breath and close my eyes to take in the memory of the delicious bites we had here on our last trip to NYC. For $45 (each), we had it all. And then some. I'm struggling to remember every dish we had, but the highlights were the tuna tartare on tempura Japanese eggplant, salty seared scallops, strawberry-cinnamon glazed ribs, short rib sliders and the "bagels and lox". I don't even like salmon but I devoured the "everything bagel" focaccia and smoked salmon. It was just one dish after another of deliciousness. Our party of 5 was just loving all of it. ESPECIALLY those bacon donuts. I mean come on. Fried dough and bacon. Our server was the best. I don't remember her name -- but she was so fun and we bonded immediately over being single, not having kids and not caring a bit! She made sure our drinks were always full, our plates were cleared and silverware refreshed. I'd come back here in a heartbeat. The place is on the small side so if you're going -- make a reservation (and add a +1 for me). It's a must.

An amazing small locally owned and operated French restaurant. They have wine specials during the week. Beautifully decorated by mostly hand made art. Do yourself a favor and go here as soon as possible.

See no evil (tourists), Hear no evil (tourists), Speak no evil (tourists!!!) Definitely one of the more "normal" bars in the Theater District that isn't swarming with those damn tourists. I like that. Two floors and two bars plus an outside patio to get your drink on. Decent beer selection and pretty good bar food. They play top 40 songs which is such a relief. I have a feeling I'll be frequenting The Three Monkeys more often now as an escape from all the crappy places I'm surrounded by at my current office.

Apparently the white sauce is all the hype. It did live up. On this 53rd and 6th block, there were 3 carts with signs and guys saying they were the Halal Guys....okay. Confusing. We decided to go to the one with the longest line. A Halal guy came up to us insisting that they were the originals and the others were copy-cats. Okay okay, take it easy.... The line went quick, got the mixed combo of lamb and chicken. A take out container of lettuce, rice and meats topped off with this magic sauce and bam!! You got yourself a delicious meal. Only $6!!! Sweet! Tasty sauce. Meat was a tad dry but you can't beat the price!

The only thing getting in the way of Traif's excellence, is the uber high standard they have set for themselves! Â Their food is really amazing and despite the fact that their chef Jason didn't win Chopped, he was clearly the most talented chef on the episode and totally should have won (although we didn't get to see what he would've made on the dessert round, but I just think he would've taken it). Â  I've been to Traif on date nights and with friends, and both experiences are equally amazing. Â Not too good for large groups due to the space, but four people is great so you can order a ton of the food and share. Â  Traif have a lot of small plates that are great for sharing (except some portions leave you wanting a little more) and they also have larger entree plates as well. Â What I love to do, actually almost anywhere I eat, is to SHARE! Â If I go with someone, I like to get like 3-4 small plates and an entree (if you read my reviews, you know I love to eat a lot)! I've eaten a good number of their dishes and the standouts to me are as follows (note: Â their menu changes somewhat regularly): -lamb tenderloin medallions were perfectly cooked, succulent and juicy, with i think a pistachio crust or something that gave it a great texture and crunch, along with a hummus puree or something, and a fruit compote on top...this is an aphrodisiac. Â If you want to score on a date, order two of these dishes and watch the magic happen. Â It is that good. -seared foie gras: Â I feel bad for the goose that get overfed to stuff their liver for our guilty little pleasure, but OMG, this is soo good. Â Perfectly seared and served with a great mix of hot and sweet, with an egg...this is delicious! I just realized that I could go on and on writing about how much I love so many of their dishes, but what I would encourage you to do, is GO, look at the menu, see what you like, and order liberally. Â The food is amazing! Â  Their drinks are also masterfully crafted, so don't skip the drink menu either. Â  The ambiance is somewhat dark and moody, usually with lively banter in the background from the packed house (I've never seen it empty), and the best part - they have an open kitchen where you can watch the chefs do their art. Â I sat at the bar once and was amazed at what all they could do in the space they had, and I think one night I softly applauded as their dishes went by me. Â  And last of all, the wait staff are extremely attentive and courteous, and they will be more than glad to make suggestions and answer any questions about the dishes they serve so feel free to ask them. Please enjoy!

Finally a place that breaks away from the grecian choke hold that is 30th ave. The ribs Â and mac&cheese were great along with organic soda, I Â almost forgot I was in Astoria. Good food, cool staff can't wait for delivery to be available

Yes yes yes- you are going to have to wait for an hour and half BUT WORTH IT! Here is my tip- go put your name in- Walk over to Russ and Daughers and get a salmon lox sandwich there and split it with someone to curve your appetite then go walk the Williamsburg bridge to work off the calories that you are about to eat. At that point, your table should be ready. They are connected to a link where you can see how many people are ahead of you so you have a roundabout idea when to get back to the area and they will text you Ok now about the food- I LOVE IT! Pure and simple. We tried the fried green tomatoes b/c you cant get that everywhere. It came with this avocado/sour cream type sauce that complemented it perfectly. I could have eaten that spread solo. The tomatoes had a perfect crisp with great flavor. Now the blueberry pancakes-- soooo friggin good. Moist beyond belief! Blueberries on top, blueberries in the middle, blueberries everywhere! They serve it with a small dish of maple butter syrup AKA Crack syrup- so delish! I also love that once you are inside, its very relaxed and they are not rushing you out. I don't mind waiting since once i'm inside its calm and a great treat! It is worth the wait!

Where do I even begin? I came here during the holiday season for the first time while hosting two of my dearest friends who flew to NY for holiday. We got there at around 7 and they didn't take a reservation so we have to wait. The hostess said that the wait would be more than 2 hours as they are extremely packed. We were waiting for a few other people to come and meet us up at Ippudo and we are a group of 6 people so we were hoping that the bigger tables will clear up fast since most patrons come in a group of 2 or 3. Surprisingly, 20 minutes in, we got a table! YAY! The noodles was really really good! Perfect amount of chewiness in every bite. The broth was outstanding and for $2 I can get an extra bowl of ramen which is really a good deal. Just remember to never finish the broth if you plan on getting a second serving of ramen for $2. It's totally worth getting bloated and fat! Definitely coming back in the near future!

The food was awesome the staff was helpful a little preoccupied at times but good service all in all. I could see if you were with a group how you may have to wait because it's kind of small but I sat at the bar no wait at all The fries were killer ! And the music thou loud if you weren't in the mood was great stones mostly but fun ! I really like the atmosphere for a lounging kind of day because it no one was in a crazy hurry it seemed

The place is very cool. Huge, actually. Dark and hip. We had the ceviche mixto (very good) the cause (incredible), the jalea (which was too big because the portion was a whole one and not a half like it should correspond for two people). The yuca was very hard and not edible, though. Aside from that, fast service and nice staff.

This is one of the few restaurants in the West Village that's open past 11PM, and yet every single time that I stumble in at midnight there is consistently a 20 minute wait. Totes worth it. My must-orders include the ricotta gnudi, chicken liver toast, and of course the burger. On any given night the tables around me are laden with the burgers: toasty bun, juicy beef, strong tangy roquefort. And those shoestring fries, so deceptively light, easy, fun to eat with the best-tasting ketchup and mustard accompaniment. The decor: pure kitsch. I love it. There is a pig motif everywhere you turn and hearkens me back to my third grade class and crazy Mrs. Mudra, whose classroom was an unbridled homage to our school mascot, The Bullfrogs. There are few restaurants in NYC that I consistently return to. Fear of commitment: there is just too much in the NYC dining scene to sample. But The Spotted Pig brings me back every time: always open, always delicious, always a good time.

BBQ as Disney would imagine it. This is pretty much a theme restaurant that serves BBQ. The meat was better than the sides. Portions were needlessly gigantic. Â Service was friendly and the decor was interesting: I liked the bottle chandelier. The restaurant seems made for the Barclay's crowd.

This location is CASH ONLY. Never was a big soba fan until I tried Cocoron. WOW. They really know how to make their broths. I've tried both the dip and soup version and both are great. I would say the dip is a cooler way to eat the soba noodles but the broth runs out more likely than if you are to get the soup verison. They will refill your bowl with hot water to keep the broth going. Recommendations: Warm Japanese Curry Soba - very thick Kimchi Dip Soba - spicy & lots of flavor
pretty loud on a sat night hard to have conversation but food was delicious!!!!! and fast would definitely recommend to arepa lovers

Oh the irony, the ssams are the least interesting things on the menu. Â They are pretty much starchy, spicy Korean burritos. Â Thankfully, the chef brought over his sinfully fatty and luscious steamed pork buns from Momofuku. Â The veal head terrine is also a revelation for fans of snout to tail cooking.
