The fish is poached in a flavour packed broth, but the portion is small. Â So, really just order anything with pork, pork, or pork since that is where the chef's passions lie. Â They are usually accompanied by seasonal, local vegetables like sweet corn, okra, sugar snap peas, etc. Â Come early, or bring a snack for the wait... The space is wheelchair accessible in the sense that one can easily wheel in, but someone in a wheelchair will have a difficult time enjoying a meal with friends. The space when crowded gets too cramped for easily access. Â The tables are either too low or the counter too high for level dining.
This place has excellent food. Everything I have had-- mainly burgers, soup, salad, BLTs-- is first rate. And it's also a historic bar, quite worth a visit even if all you want is a beer.

Have you ever seen the face of god? I have and I can tell you it looks like pulled duck lettuce wraps with banana puree. You ever wonder what the point of the Large Hadron Collider is? Well, it makes Pork cheek and pork belly meatloaf. I fucking love this place so much. If you like Traif, then just think of this as its older hotter sister. If you want to make out with some of your friends' hot older sisters, then just bring them here. Prices are extremely reasonable. $5-$22(Venison). We had 7 dishes + 2 desserts the first night. $6 Roasted Carrots $9 Fricca-dilla(Asiago cheese, potatoes, fried egg, and salsa verde) $11 Korean short ribs with Guacamole $11 Pulled duck lettuce wraps with banana puree $15 Crab Flan(not a fan) $7 Spring Onions $14 Pork cheek and pork belly meatloaf (Prices are fairly accurate, I was drunk, give me a break) We went back the next night to get dessert because it was that damn good. Churros with Jalepeno Cranberry Sorbet are solid, as well as the Sundae. Make sure to try the Agave. Ask for the side of Blood Oranges and coke lines of sesame salt, etc.

Again, came here around 10pm. Â The kimchee fried rice was good! Â As was the spicy tofu soup. Â Both hit the spot for the weather. Â Again, selection was minimal. Â But some days all you really want is some cheap food and booze to wash it down with. Â For that, this place hit the spot.

The host was cold and impersonal as we waited for him to print out (?) where we were to be seated in the almost empty restaurant. Our party of 2 got seated at a 5 seater table which was awkward in itself, but the staff didn't even bother to clear the rest of the unnecessary place settings. We had been told great things about the Brussels sprouts but they were so rich and sweet they were almost inedible. The babaganoush was overpowered with the smokey flavor, the tabbouleh salad was wwwaaayyyy too lemony/vinegary - we didn't really enjoy it. The lamb balls were great, as were their pita breads. Terrible coffee.

Ippudo NY ramen was good. It was great. And coming from someone who lives in Los Angeles and the San Gabriel Valley area, where awesome ramen is a dime a dozen, that means something. In fact, I'll tell you quick and simple. The only reason that Ippudo isn't sitting on a 5-star review is the absurd wait times. Eating at Ippudo is probably one of the hardest things to do in New York City. Â The wait is insane, and even when you are finallyseated, it feels like you're always being rushed and service takes way too long. If you can get past feeling like you're in a crowded subway train though, the food is all amazing, and the prices really aren't bad at all and all worth it. I personally ordered the Akamaru Modern ramen, essentially just a flavor-supercharged version of their tonkotsu ramen, and also got to try just about all their appetizers. Â The Ramen was perfect, and although I usually like my ramen really strong, I feel like it's just the right amount of flavor that anyone could enjoy it. If you have a chance, I would definitely say swing by Ippudo and give it a try!

Came here on a Wednesday night and we ended up waiting 1.5 hours! Â That's crazy... I'm scared to think how busy this place is on a Friday or Saturday. Â Totally knock off a star just for the wait. The ~1800 reviews should clue you in that the ramen is superb. Â Best ramen I've had in the USA. Â Like everyone else I had the Akamaru Modern Ramen. Â I added an egg and pork belly. Â Heavenly. Thank you Grace C. for getting us the free Pork belly buns ;-) Â The pork belly was very very tender. Â It's prepared similar to peking duck buns. Quick Tip: Â If you have broth leftover, for $2 you can get extra noodles

I ate several times at the original restaurant before they moved to PS1 and have to say I was a little disappointed with this spot. Physically the restaurant is incredibly loud and the tables (which are school tables) aren't good for parties of more than 2. The bone marrow had too much butter and instead of the baguette they now serve toasted bread that is way to rich with egg to compliment the marrow. The bone isn't sliced lengthwise so you feel like a neanderthal trying to scoop it out. The blood pudding was very good, though the smear of mustard sauce on the plate makes the presentation look awful. Green beans and mushrooms where too oily and very few mushrooms. Service was ok. I'll be back because you can't get this type of food in many places for a reasonable price, but the quality isn't what it was before.

I have a man crush on David Chang. Besides a bad batch of rice cakes at Momo Noodle one time (which I was reimbursed for), I have enjoyed every single thing I ever ordered at one of his creative restaurants. I don't even ask what something is when I don't know; I just trust that it's going to be awesome. And it always is. The buns (pork, shrimp, oyster, whatever they feel like!) never fail to give my mouth an orgasm but don't be afraid to leave your comfort zone. You are in good hands. The wait may attempt to scare you away but don't let it. It's never as long as they say and you can always grab a drink at schoolbred's next door. They'll text you when a table opens up.

This is kind of our go to place when we don't know where else to go. Â They always have a good selection of wines to go with their cheeses and paninis. Â The service is very friendly and is able to make good recommendations upon request. Â The decor is fun and kind of funky, it's really great in warm weather because the back patio is really nice. Â Head here if you're in the mood for cheese and bread.

BEST PIZZA IN NYC.. Simple as that! Â  I'm sorry you have to be a hater not to LOVE this place. Â Hint of advice: Artichoke and Crab are great but... try the Sicilian (the squared one)! Â then you will know that does guys really know there stuff! No fancy ingredients and still .. one of the best pizzas I had in my life (and trust me, I am half Italian, I had plenty of pizza in my life )

Food is full of flavor and texture it's beyond belief. Went here because of their yelp reviews and their veggie pho because I'm vegetarian. It was amazing and tasteful. The only thing I would recommend is more mock meat in their soup only had literally 3 small pieces of "meat." Space is small very right but they have a high turn around because they're always busy. We had 3 couples ahead of us and got seated within 15 min, not too bad. Food came out fairly quickly and staff was friendly and refilled our waters 3 times! Great staff!

Been there 3 times by now (twice for dinner and once for brunch) and have tried most of the items on the menu. Def need to make reservations especially for dinner. I must admit, I am more impressed by their concept than their food. They recommended the burger but I found the jalapenos to be too overpowering- I could not even taste the meat. There was also a special, the truffle pizza, and it was all cheese- even too cheesy for someone who loves cheese. However, there are quite a few great items worth mentioning. Their pana cotta is absolutely delicious. You can taste the purity of the cream. It's light and fluffy, unlike most panna cottas I've tried, and not too sweet. The mushroom pizza with farm egg is great to try as well. Overall, ABC is a great place to try, especially for a work night, since its less crowded, but probably won't be a place I will go time after time.

We decided to go to Beyoglu for a Saturday night dinner, after we read the positive reviews about this place. At 9.30pm they ran out of iskender and doner kebab, which were the reasons why we decided to go there. We had hummus, taboule, sucuk izgara, falafel. As to the main course, we got the chicken tavuk izgara. Beyoglu, as declared also by the owner, is not a Turkish restaurant. Despite his name, this place lacks of a clear gastronomic identity. The food we tried was mediocre, the service ok but somehow invasive. The place is a crossover of a bistro, middle-eastern resto with bad pop music playing in the background.
Our brunch today was delicious, the service was great, the space lovely. The only thing negative to say is the servings were small for the price. But we will go back.

I have only been once and wasn't too impressed but good enough that I would give it at least another try. Â Comes highly recommended from Greek friends as classy but not as pricey as other nice greek places like Avra or Milos. Can not add to the effusive praise of Christos as i did not meet him.

$8 prix fixe lunch - three courses in a nice modern Thai bistro? Such a deal. I really love how they serve their iced tea...make sure you order it! It's not 100% authentic Thai, but it works in a pinch for a quick lunch meal. Nice atmosphere. Love sitting in the front window for a slightly Â intimate lunch.

Lets put is this way... About 15 years ago, when I was 12 years old, my aunt and uncle made reservations and took me here. I was SO impressed I memorized the name, the cross streets, and its location in the Village! My uncle bet me that I would eventually forget. I have not since been back there, but I still remember this dining experience like it was yesterday. The atmosphere, the service, the smell, the food, and this was all before I knew anything about running a restaurant or working int the culinary field. It just had this aura about it. It was a super tiny, cozy, family run, authentic Italian place that served me a monster plate of spaghetti topped with 2 mouth watering meatballs the size of baseballs, no joke, that I could not even finish. That is a feat within itself. At that age I could devour a house if you let me, and I couldn't finish that plate. I cannot wait to get back there, I am so glad it is still there. I don't know how much it has changed since then, or how relavent this review is to now, but I will always remember, Piccolo Angolo, corner of Jane and Hudson, West Village. Highly Recommended.

This is a typically nice looking Thai place. Service is fast and food is good. Tuna tartare was ridic! Spicy fred rice was as advertised. i did not have the drinks but they looked fancy and moderately priced.

I actually wasn't that impressed. Â The sushi was just alright and the BYOB rules were quite complicated. Â Your first bottle of wine is free but then you pay if you don't order a certain amount and no beer or sake. Â There is another BYOB sushi place (that I won't mention because I don't want any of you making it even harder to get in to) that has better sushi, and uncomplicated rules. On the plus side the staff was really nice, but quick to rush us out at the end of our meal.

Simply delicious. I had heard a lot about this place being rated the best Italian food in the entire city and I had been dying to try it for a while. My fiancÃ© took me for my birthday recently and it was just as good as I had hoped. I had the mezza Luna ravioli and it was to die for, melted right in your mouth. The pasta was so fresh and light and the filling was amazing, almost as good a the sauce on top. My fiancÃ© ordered the filet mignon and finished every bite. He is the type of eater who puts salt and pepper on everything he eats before even trying it, but he never once reached for the shakers at this restaurant. We split a tiramisu for dessert and I wasn't big on that, but it was my first time trying it and I think it just wasn't for me. My fiancÃ© ate every last bit of it and said it was one of the best he'd ever had. The atmosphere is great also, staff is very friendly and the chef and manager frequently come out to check that everyone is doing fine. The one negative I have to say is that for such a pricy menu, the portion sizes are somewhat small. We definitely didn't leave there full. Overall it was really great. I can't wait to come back here and try something else.

these people do not need my review, but still I need to let them that they are doing a great job for 6$ even though it is not a very clean way to make your gyro sandwich! if you a picky you might have an issue eating there

I absolutely hate crowds and the claustrophobic feelings that I associate with them, and the moment I walked into Eataly I was ready to turn around (although the line of people just waiting to get out of the store would have prevented me from doing so). We made our way past a dizzying array of meats, cheeses, accoutrements, various market counters, casual eateries, a bottle shop area and hundreds of people just to get to the elevator that would catapult us to a more serene Birreria. After our lunch, we fought our way upstream to get back to the doors, but not without taking a quick break for some gelato. There were several enticing flavors but I eventually decided on a cone with chocolate chip and chocolate. I can easily say that despite the holiday shopping crowds and overall sensory overload, that gelato could get me back to Eataly without any hesitation. Smooth and delicious, the chocolate was great but the chocolate chip? Other-worldly. It tasted like cold fresh milk with semi-sweet dark chocolate slates pierced throughout. I will definitely be back the next time I'm in New York - hopefully on a day warm enough to take my gelato outside.

My malaysian friend invited us to this restaurant for a malaysian style new year dinner ( the new year date is the same as chinese new year). So the restaurant has a new year's menu ( serve only until the 15th day of the chinese new year), and one of the special dish is sth like "low chai". It has crispy noodles and all sorts of vegitables. Then some old lady came to our table and pour a dish of salmon on top of it, then opened two red envelopes containing some spices. She sprinkled these spices on the top while saying that they represented silver and gold. then she said some other words wishing us good luck and have a good year. Â after all these, everyone on the table had to pick up our chopsticks and started stiring the whole dish, it was a fun chopstick fight. Finally we could eat it. It tasted a bit sweet and sour as most malaysian dishes do... but the crispy noodles added so much texture, love it. then we had oil rice and coconut rice, i prefer oil rice though. don't remember other dishes they ordered, but one of it has a taro smashed and shaped like a bowl and fried, taste really good. the crab is good too. For the desert, we tried several, mostly are good. do not order ABC, some kind of shaved ice. and mango pudding is just ok. Do try the fresh coconut pudding, it's huge and comes in a whole real coconut shell~

truffle fries...best fries i've ever had. devils on horseback were great, but i wouldn't order the octopuse again...seemed to get lost in the sauce..sounded good in theory, but lacked any pop. place is very nice as well.

This place is good. I was pretty hesitant to come here, because I've been to a lot of restaurants back home in San Francisco that aren't as good as what my parents cook, except one or two. It sounds bias, but I'm pretty sure my dad cooks some bomb ass Filipino food, because when my friends come over who don't really have Filipino food too often, they kind of get blown away. But when I came to Jeepney, I was pretty impressed. All the dishes are not all traditional Filipino dishes, some of them have a really cool twist to them. For example, Arroz Caldo (rice porridge) with fried tripe! Holy crappola. Best idea ever. Longanisa in a hot dog bun with bagoong (shrimp paste) mayo is another awesome idea. Good stuff Jeepney! Â I'm happy that I came to this place. I wish they had Filipino restaurants with this kind of style in California.
very nice place. small and quaint and cozt. quail was very good. nice wine list. will def return

I have waiting years for a place to open up in our neighborhood outside of Farell's. Â I must say the beer selection, happy hour, and new hot beef sandwich are awesome. Â I met one of the owners a while back, when I forgot my yankees, great guy! He sat with my brother and I and we chatted about families. Â Great overall welcome. I was there the other day and asked Nick the bartender Â for the owners name as I wanted to write a personal letter to ownership on a job well done. I told him I come here often. Â With wife and a toddler once a week is often to me! Instead of telling me that it is against policy to do so or anything of that nature which I would have totally understood... Nick stated that he works there 6 days per week and has never seen me before. Â That was his response to me...Literally insinuated that I was lying. about ever being there before..I was not impressed by his lack of customer service in his response. I explained why I was asking, he cut me off. Â  I asked him is this how you should treat your customers? His response was to me was to calm down. Â I was speaking in a very civil tone...instead of diffusing a situation he was stand offish and really didnt care what I was asking him. I went from Yay-I am in Fan to A-OK. Â He pretty much turned me off to being a patron there for the short term maybe long term. Â  Afterall, a customer only remembers their last visit. He really burned me up!

Went for brunch and the space is beautiful and the food was excellent! I practically licked my plate to get every last bit of my duck confit, side salad and sunny side eggs. However as great as everything else was, the service was just so spotty it can't warrant more stars. Our server (and everyone's) talked so fast we had to keep having her repeat herself, she was rushing our menu choices and it took 20-minutes for her to realize that she had swapped out check with other patrons.
My number 1 go to place when having a group dinner in NYC. Salads, pastas and calamari (my fav) are the best!
Doesnt get better
Yes, these are the guys that will hook you up with the best Halal food in NYC.
bar seat. beer. bread. burger mussels fries.

Tried many of the items.. BRISKET IS THE BEST! Â  Â ANYWHERE. EVER. Â  Ambiance is cool as a hell....the way its positioned right next to a garage and how it can be a bit difficult to find. Â  dig it.. I'm a fan.. but only for the Brisket. Â The baked beans were a different take, my girl liked it b/c it was saucy but it was just a tad too salty for me.

Love this place!! I had the shrimp po boy yesterday...Amazing!! Before that I had the chicken sandwich...loved it! Â Very casual, welcoming, unpretentious. Great service. I loved the bathroom too lol. If you are in the area please stop in and give a taste you won't regret it.

my friend and i shared a carafe of white wine, pumpkin ravioli, fries w garlic mayo, and a warm goat cheese with caramelized onion tart. the fries were the shoestring version and quite nice, esp with the garlic mayo. the pumpkin ravioli was cooked perfectly and tasted delish. now to the creme de la creme: our tart was the best thing we had all weekend. the side salad and tapenade were a poifect touch to the creamy, tangy, sweet, and savory tart. i wish i had one right in front of me so i can enjoy that tasty experience again!!!

the eggs are STILL GROSSLY UNDER DONE. Â  Took my bf here and joked about my prior experience, but assured him that if he got the eggs benedict, they've probably fixed it by now. Â Being so confident, we both ordered it (we are eggs benedict addicts on Sunday). Â  It came TRANSLUCENT, and no different from the last time I came, we could literally run our forks through the murky lumps of egg whites that jiggled on our plates. I love marc forgione otherwise - have gone there for dinner, and drinks, but this poached eggs situation is just bizarre. Â Does Marc Forgione have a firm belief that this is the way poached eggs should be served? Â  I'm all for the runny yolk, but NOT for runny egg white.

After living in NYC for almost quarter of my life, I finally visited this historic pizzeria. And no wonder they are so popular! Pizza is soooo good. And, I did not expect the place to look the way it does. The interior is more of a diner. Not a con, but a bit surprising.

Why, when this place already has +180 reviews, do I need to add another one for La Sirene? It is just that good. My mom was coming into the city for her bday, along with my aunt, and I was torn about where to take them for dinner. I wanted some place that they would not forget, with wonderful food, ambiance, and service. And since they're both big wine drinkers I knew that could get pricey. I could not have picked a better place to take them. It was a late Wednesday night dinner that ended up lasting past midnight, and all they could talk about on the cab to their hotel was how wonderful La Sirene was. The place, as everyone has stated, is small and intimate. I wasn't uncomfortable at all and it was actually bigger than I imagined after reading all the reviews. We walked in and were promptly seated by two delightful servers. The smell coming from the kitchen was wonderful and we couldn't wait to eat! For apps we had French onion soup, escargot, and the mussels in curry sauce. The mussels in curry were TO DIE FOR. My sister and I went through almost three bread bowls soaking up every bit of the sauce because it was so delicious. That is the number one reason I will return, I can't wait to have more. My mother has been eating escargot for 50 years, so if she says they were the best she's ever had, they must have been amazing. My aunt raved about the soup as well. For dinner they both had the goat cheese app since they were already getting full. I didn't try it, I think because I was still working on the curry sauce, but once again, they couldn't stop saying how good it was. I was torn between two fish entrees and Didier recommended the seared pompano fish fillet, a French take on a Floridian recipe. I loved it. The cherry port sauce complimented the fish perfectly, the flavor was not sweet, not too fishy, it was just outstanding. I was thankful for the recommendation. My sister had the seafood shepherds pie since she was especially hungry. Nothing but good things to say about that as well, the vegetables were very fresh and seafood was savory. For dessert we wanted something we could all share since we were stuffed. We had the profiteroles - Didier let us know this was more of a "fun" option on the menu. They were sweet but not too sugary, had ice cream inside, topped with chocolate callebaut. We were full and extremely pleased with everything. And the four bottles of wine had us all warm, singing, and smiling ear to ear. Aside from the food, what really made the experience wonderful was the staff and Didier. I was nervous that we would be rushed since we had the latest reservation possible, but we weren't at all, we stayed for hours without ever feeling like they were waiting for us to leave. The waitresses were awesome- we talked with them throughout the night, drank some wine with them, and one even sang some opera- I forget her name but I loved her!! And it really completed the French bistro feel. And Didier- he is the MAN. He simply will not accept a meal below his expectations. If there was anything we weren't happy with, all we needed was to say the word and he let us know it wouldn't be on the bill. But of course we were thrilled with everything. He was so friendly, and when he speaks about food you can see and hear his passion for French cuisine. Yes I'm gushing. But I loved this place. I can't help it. Lastly, one review said this place is mediocre. I think that review is garbage! Take it down!! PS... Hi Didier :) Thanks again for giving my mom such a great bday dinner experience!

JOYA BANGS!!! Period!!! I actually just recently went back for the second time and go totally different dishes and they too were AMAZING!!! Spicy Mussles, Pad Thai Noodles (ClichÃ© thai but amazing here), Coconut Curry YUM YUM YUM!!! Wow...so good...and this place stays PACKED!!! The prices are really amazing and the service is quick! But the most important part is this is the BEST THAI IVE EVER HAD...SERIOUSLY!

I was initially disappointed at the prospect of sitting in the wine cellar downstairs but it turned out to be a nice setting for a date. Â The waitress we had was quite nice and the mixed seafood dish I ordered exceeded my expectations in terms of quality and size. Â I'd definitely come back to try some of the other dishes.

The lasagna here is beyond. Â It is an amazing, unsurpassed, bechamel lasagna unlike any other fresh, meaty little piece of homemade Italian food I've had. Â I clearly can not come to Bianca's without having this lasagna, but also tend to split another pasta dish as an app so that they all get there fair chance. Â  Can't say as much for the meat entrees since I'm stuck on the fresh pasta. Thus far the bolognese was good, but I may have been disappointed in it as an entree...especially with that lasagna there for the choosing. Â The gnocchi in blue cheese sauce is rich and delicious and the ravioli with butter and sage is always tasty, but again I prefer it as an appetizer. Â Have yet to sample the basic spaghetti marinara, but it looks excellent and I have spoken to other people that come just for that. So many of the best Italian restaurants are cash only, Bianca's included. Â I've never waited too long, even on a weekend night. Â As others have said the bar next door is a great place to wait and you can bring your drink over if you're seated. Â Love this place.
Unreal pizza & salads The best ever, we loved it The place smells like no other restaurant thanks to the coal fired oven THANX

I've got pride, and I've got a little bit of an ego. Because of those two things, I get inordinately cranky when I feel like a) someone is trying to dupe me or b) I am successfully duped. This is how I feel about Fette Sau - or as I call it, "Home of the Well-Fed Hipster." Every time I've gone there, I've asked for maybe 1/4 pound of meat, a sausage link, one side and a beer. This never fails to cost me more than $20. The fact that I find the food seriously mediocre pisses me off even more. (The fact that I've gone to Fette Sau three times despite being disappointed each and every time qualifies me as a complete sucker.) The meat is never, EVER as good as it should be. I've had the pork butt, brisket, ribs, and two kinds of sausage - the only one I'd ever opt for again is one of the kinds of sausage. The meat is generally bland, in my opinion - sometimes even a little dry. The sides are "eh," and overpriced. I liked the baked beans - the cole slaw is blech. The rolls are pathetic, and the house red wine taste like vinegar swirled around in a public toilet bowl. The fact that I'm one of very few people to rag on this place gives me pause, but what are you gonna do? All I know is that I really, really don't like this place. Sorry, Fette Sau. I wanted to love you.

This is the jewel of Brooklyn pizza, the pride of Avenue J and beyond. A few steps away from a rambling subway station lies the ramshackle little Midwood pizzeria that is Di Fara and the Italian hero himself, Dom Demarco. Luckily upon my last visit, I didn't have to endure the fabled waits that this place is known for. Just get there early and beat the lunch rush and you can snag a seat and glare over all of Dom's collected newspaper bits and numerous accolades and awards. The pizza however is a hallmark of deliciousness. Fresh basil, San Marzano tomatos, buffalo mozzarella, a nice helping of olive oil, and a crisp perfectly charred crust that I've yet to find elsewhere. Each pie is handmade, one by one and only by Dom. Every bite is truly a memory in it's own right. You can't say you've ever had real Brooklyn pizza until you've been to Di Fara's. Sure, there's all the other bigshots like Grimaldi's and Lucali's but nobody has the charm and hole in the wall goodness that is this little chunk of Brooklyn.

Ramen-Ya will be my new go to spot in the West Village for Ramen. The quality and flavors aren't up to the Ippudo's or the Totto's of the world, but solid ramen none the less. This would have been have 4 stars, but all of my pork was grizzly/tasteless and the broth and noodles needed to over compensate for the overall dish.

I want to know why no one ever goes to the second Halal stand? I really find it hard to believe that the one spot everyone seems to hog and make Â this enormous line, is a lot better then the other stand which barley has as many people and it's the same company! I'm not trying to offend anyone but I would really like to know the answer? I don't see the difference, i've ate from both. Well, here's my review in general of the famous Halal Guys, I think their food is good. I guess they are better then most other Halal spots around the area (this does not count the second cart on the same street) and it seems the give a bigger portion then most. Sadly portion isn't important, because the fact I can't finish it, sort of means i waste it. So instead I get a new spoon and fork and go looking for homeless people to offer them my left overs, because trust me my left overs are big enough to feed another person. For six dollars, it's a pretty good deal, and plus i get to do my good deed of the day. I like putting the white sauce, don't really like the hot sauce. I like lamb over rice, it's Halal food that makes the perfect lamb, so therefore their is no other option in my book. It's the best sort of plate when you're really going all out for a meal, and I hope you're planning to walk around after that, cause you will end with a full tummy in the end.

Yum yum! Cheap good thai food and cool atmosphere! I had the thai iced tea which was very interesting and the chicken curry panang, which was really tasty! I would definitely go back again to try more dishes. It's a great option with friends or your boyfriend!

Fette Sau is a meat paradise, with decor and atmosphere that accurately reflect the surrounding neighborhood. It gets busy, but with a little bit of hunting, we were able to get ~8 seats together for our group. Be prepared to wait, though, as since everything is carved to order, it can take a while.

I get hungry just thinking about this place! One of my favorite places to eat in the city. Fun atmosphere, friendly staff, DELICIOUS menu... oh yeah and the ice cream sandwiches are amazing. Be prepared for a wait, but it's worth every minute of it.
This place is delicious and well-prized. the Merguez platter is a must!
I am definitely down with japanese food and no body does it better than Ippudo!!!!!!

One word...SQUARES!!! This place use to be 5 stars but recently went under Â new management and kinda slid off. But with that being said the pizza squares are amazing, the regular slices not so much. Best pizza in NYC hands down!!! Need i say more? They also have a family restaurant next door that serves pretty good food. They also have a take out part which you could basically get anything to go. Before you go you must head to the ice cream stand and get spumoni . Parking can be a pain, small lot and street parking. Gets very crowded in the summer and on the weekends.

Great ambiance! Gotta love the history at this place! Â We went on a Saturday night and there was a live music. Music was great! Played everything from Irish music to classic rock. Bartenders are awesome!

Had two different kinds of experiences here. What they had in common: Fantastic Pizza (the Quattro Signorie, spelling?), inexpensive beer, and lively fun clientele. The pizza is fantastic - Â easily in the Top 5 of Brooklyn. Â  What they didn't have in common: the service. Bam, the bartender during our first visit is incredible - knowledgeable, friendly, attentive. The gent we had on our second visit was - not Bam-like. Every answer was a "yeah, sure" or "yeah." Very detached, and even seemed a bit annoyed by how busy it was getting (it was a random Sunday afternoon). We'll certainly be back (again and again), but we'll hope Bam's behind the bar.

My husband and I frequent the Williamsburg location. So far, this location might be better. Â Sometimes we get screwed with super tiny portions of chicken or vegetarian chicken in Williamsburg. Â Here, our portions were the largest we've ever gotten. We are piggies. Â We care about portion size. Â I think that the portion size we received warrants the price. Â The super pretty and very tall hostess was also very helpful with service. I have tried almost all of the specials in the Williamsburg location. Â I had the Hawaiian special here and it was almost perfect. The pineapple waffles just needed a little more pineapple. Â I had to really look hard to see the pineapple. We were happy to see that Â the buffalo chicken and the duck with the cranberry waffles made it to the menu. Â They are specials at the Williamsburg location. Our only gripe is that we ordered sauteed kale and received a bowl of peas and carrots. Â As much as I love being reminded of one of my favorite movies, Â Forrest Gump, peas and carrots do not equal kale. Â  Our server asked the kitchen about the peas and carrots and he returned saying that was what the sauteed kale dish was supposed to look like. Â It had a few greens in it that seemed to be spinach. Â This makes no sense at alll. Â We said that we liked the carrots, but the server took the dish away.

Overly hyped. The hot sauce is like the devil's saliva. Couldnt breathe after a bite of it.. & I rly do like hot sauce): Ordered a lamb & chicken combo.. the meat came out shredded like tuna. Literally tuna. Great location, though.

Cheap drinks. This was a local bar that had a line on a Tuesday at 7pm. Â The food wasn't the greatest. If you're a local that's looking for a good bar (meaning cheap drinks) and want to grab a bite then go here. The party next to us said the bar was featured on Food network. If this was true then it definitely contributed to the bars popularity.
Excellent pie!! This is what i had in mind when searching for a perfect pizza. Sauce, toppings and crust was perfect. I highly recommend stopping in and having the Boscaiola

This restaurant has been on my list of places to visit for a while. So when I had the opportunity of venturing to Brooklyn n dine at the world renowned "Lambardi's" I felt like a kid on Christmas morning. Â As we entered the establishment I was amazed at how big the place was. Granted there wasn't one big room but rather several tiny/ narrow rooms. I loved how the hostess walked us through the kitchen n past many other rooms to take us to our table. It certainly added to the ambiance (old school Italian eateries). I was so excited to finally be sitting in front of a table, at a restaurant I'd never thought I get to visit. However, that excitement turned to shear disappointment when the food arrived. We ordered the meatballs n bruschetta as apps n they were great, but the pizzas margarita & a pizza with mushrooms left something to be desired. While the crust (texture n flavor) were good the rest of it was lacking salt, cheese, flavor, flavor, and more flavor. I must say I have had much better pizza in the past at other pizzerias. I was in disbelief n for a while thought I had read the wrong reviews and/or come to the wrong place. Prices were reasonable but the waitstaff was not attentive and did nothing to make me or my guest feel special (waited 15 min for check after asking 3 times and no one offered un replenishments our drinks) . I got the impression that the reputation spoke for it self, rather than the food & service providing a reputation for the business. Â Perhaps they had an off day, but I will never be back to find out. If you want to visit this famous joint to say u have eaten here great but if your in the mood for excellent quality pizza n service there's much better pizzerias out there to be discovered. Service: Below average Food: Average

Oops ... I drank too much at the bar waiting for a table. Â Something that you will likely do too at this trendy ramen spot... but for good reason, as it is worth the wait. If stuck, the bar selection of Sake and Shochu is good .. too good ... and I sampled a good deal of them. So much so, I didn't hear the waitress call my name for our table... repeatedly. Hey, I finally had a spot at the bar and, anyway, I wasn't going anywhere ... too cold outside. OK... on to business ... so this was like my 10th visit to Ippudo, but only the 3rd time that I actually ate a meal as the wait can be too daunting. Â But I did say that the wait was worth it and it is. The ramen are truly great and it is entirely because of the wonderful broths that are prepared here by the wizards in the kitchen. Â These are not heavily prepared with thick seasoning. Â These both have a nice complexity and refinement to them that I have not experienced at other noodle establishments. Â  Their appetizers and main dishes are also of a high caliber (flavorful pork buns, salmon carpaccio sprinkled with Parmesan). I do like the layout of the restaurant, but I wish that they found a few ways to squeeze in a few more tables so that I might have more of a chance to come back. Well, there is always the bar.

I have been planning on giving this place a try for a very long time and I finally did about two weeks ago. Since then I have eaten at this place twice more, not so much because I fell in love with it right away, but more because I felt like I had to try three different sauces in order to give this place a fair review. The place itself is adorable, as you can tell from the photos it has three tall wooden chairs in front of it which are usually taken. Once you enter it, the place is really narrow and you stand by a counter, usually in a somewhat long line, where you order from. There are two tables in the back which fit about 4-5 people each and a bar which could fit about as many. The wooden tables have holes in them that are meant for the cones, I think that is both cute and a brilliant idea. The service is pretty quick and efficient and I would say for the amount of fries you get that they are not overpriced. Also, they do not have a bathroom that is available for customers from what I could tell. First time I came here I ordered the Frites sauce because it just seemed appropriate. I didn't plan for this to be my full meal, more like a "snack" so I shared the regular size with another person and for a "snack" it was really filling. The fries themselves were thick, mostly soft yet crunchy at times. They were not too salty which was good they actually had just the right amount of salt, however I cant say they were extraordinary. The sauce on the other hand was pretty good. My second time here I tried the Sweet Mango Chutney Mayo with my friend and I absolutely loved this sauce, you can barely taste the mayo and the sweetness is really subtle, definitely recommended for people who are not much of mayo fans. Third time I decided that these regular sized frites are going to be my actual lunch and for the most part I had them all to myself. The result was that I could not finish them, when combined with the sauce it is pretty filling. That time I tried the Roasted Garlic Mayo which I had my eye on for some time but unfortunately it was a disappointment, I cant put my finger on what exactly I didn't like about it, but at some point I just gave up on the sauce and ate those fries with ketchup. All in all, this place is worth a visit if only to try as many different sauces as you can handle, but if you come here expecting to try fries that will blow your mind, I suggest lowering your expectations or looking for another place. I personally will be back.

Just returned from spending a week in NYC. Â My son who lives in Brooklyn wanted us to try this place. Â It was crowded, very small space. Â We did have to wait a while, but the very friendly staff checked in with us every few minutes assuring us that they would seat us as soon as possible. Â It was worth the wait, the food was fantastic. Â The food is southern, comfort style food that your grandma (if she was from the south) would cook. Â Order the Fried Green Tomatos with bacon and arugula, you won't regret it. Â Next time I'm in NYC I will go there again.
Bad service. There're apparently training & communication problems. Sat down and waited about forty mins before someone came to take our orders. Food only ok even though we were starving.

Even though I live in Queens, NY I had a recent craving for lobster roll and I remember the Lobster Pound in Red Hook. Â So I just had to make a trip down there. Â I had the connecticut style lobster roll with chips and a lemon lime soda, OH MAN EVERYTHING WAS SO GOOD! Â Generous delicious pieces of lobster in the rolls and just worth the trip if you don't live close.

gorgeous hapsburg style decor delicious and surprisingly not super expensive food SACHERTORTE ($8 a slice but i'd pay double because it's fucking SACHERTORTE) ummm yeah also the bread basket they give you is literally overflowing and this isn't cheesecake factory bread, hunny bunnies. i can't say enough good things about cafe sabarsky. my favorite place to eat in nyc by far.

I am still not sure which cart this is - there are two. One that say "The Halal Guys" and the other have the apples on their shirts. I am reviewing The Halal Guys - and they were great. I got the combo over rice. White sauce was amazing, meat was great. Nothing wrong here! I've had NYC food carts in the past with less than stellar results. I'd love to go back and try both carts - to compare!

Great coffee and pastries! I tried out this place because of Cups. They use Verve coffee from California and the espresso drinks are fantastic. Bonus points for having these cute little notes on their coffee cups I have since dubbed 'daily coffee wisdom'. I also really like their boreks.. Wish they have galaktoboureko or custard pie..

My new home away from home! Great Coffee....If you love Grilled Cheese sandwiches this is your spot. Â They are the Grilled Cheese connoisseur. Wine and beer as well. The atmosphere is what I am in love with.... I don't feel like I am in Queens. The music and service is wonderful:)

Few weeks ago, I bookmarked this place to give it a try. Bought the falafel platter, it tastes amaze balls! it includes israeli salad, tabbouleh, three sauces, seven small pieces of falafel and the famous hummus. For how the other plates of their menu look like, I guess that they should taste delicious and fresh as well. I didn't know that this place was extremely small. More than 4 people can't fit at this place, so just go in, and take your order to go.

3.5 Stars really. Â The butternut squash soup was tasty and had a real earthy tone given the walnuts. Â My NZ venison was cooked perfectly, spinach seasoned well, and sesame potatoes were interesting. Â What topped the meal was a NZ type of dessert with fruit, cream, and a light cookie thingy on the bottom. Â What's not so great was flat/ expired diet coke from a 2-liter bottle, the table setting (tiny place and I was stuffed in the back), and the noise level was extremely high - table to the left had middle aged men and women discussing orgies and table to my right had a woman talking about hours of make out sessions and slutting it out. Â Classy, but I suppose it was better entertainment than dining with an ex. If you follow Top Chef alum Mark Simmons go for it, but this "mediocre" review is totally for the poor front of the house execution.

Definitely one of the best French restaurants I've been to. Ambience: -Small, quaint, mood lighting = ON! Great for date nights or casual dinner with your girls (or your boys or both). Â  Service: -Attentive and eager to recommend dishes that fits your taste/preference. Food: -It's aright. I mean, if you like that French thing. J/K. Delicious! Must tries: -Homemade pate -Escargots -Sauteed octopus -Foie gras -Mussels in red wine (has bacon!!) -Duck cassoulet -Filet mignon (it's topped with foie gras - hell yeah!) Tips: -Reservations are encouraged. But because it is a small restaurant, reservations for 6+ on Friday & Saturdays aren't accepted. You can try though - they sometimes make exceptions if you try for earlier in the evening. -BYOB spot w/ no corkage fee. Plus, there is a wine & spirits close by that delivers for free. La Sirene is open to accepting wine deliveries for your dinner. -Offers 4 different veggies dishes for the table to share when you order entrees. The veggies are seasonal and are bottomless so don't be shy to request for more!

Bistango Bistango Bistango... I don't know what to say... My friend in the area, who is a regular in the place, swears by it... I have had my share of meals from them, by delivery, and going there. Â I'd say my taste buds are screwed up... but while the wait staff is very attentive and friendly, and more so to regulars, and the place is very welcoming and nicely decorated and organized... i have a problem with the food. Texture and preparation wise its fresh and well prepared. The wine list is very good too... but... i find no flavor on their food. I might be spoiled by other places that use more spices and seasonings on their food, but this place is expecting you to either find the subtleties in the the pasta and water used to boil it, or the natural taste of tomatoes and basil, which i like but come on! u need more than that, its Italian food for gods sake! Every food joint in Rome had more tasty plates than this! Any ways... if its any consolation.. their prosciutto and mozzarella and basil salad is good, they might be using Prosciutto De Parma i guess. Well hope it gets better, but I've had much from them, and usually the same experience... it might be me in the end, but this is my experience. Â Sigh.. i like Italian...

i give this place props for having a line out the door in the freezing cold at 4am. beautiful decor, quality american food. the cornmeal breaded calamari was tender and yummy, and the mac and cheese was really tasty. the bleu cheese one was waaayyy too strong for my taste though. overall a good experience, i would probably come back

Best Thai in Park Slope for sure! Cash only, which is a bummer but otherwise it's a great place. The delivery is fast (but you have to call them - no online ordering service) and the restaurant itself is a modern, cozy place - good for a date or dinner with friends. The draw back at the restaurant is, because the food is good & relatively inexpensive, there's often a long wait on weekends and evenings.

Finally made it to Pommes Frites! Only 15 minutes after eating a big brunch, we stumbled upon this little famous hole in the wall and were drawn in. We got small fries with 3 dipping sauces: War Sauce (yummy), Pesto (pretty good), and Irish Curry (AWESOME). Split among 4 of us, this small portion was plenty to go around. Definitely a great place for a snack, any time of day.

Great pizza! Since moving into the neighborhood, came here, went to Lucali's, and came here again. I don't really taste a difference in the pizza, which is great news to me. I will not have to visit Lucali's anymore and wait long for a table. Another difference is, this place is not BYOB and has a wine and beer. The staff is very nice! You can also get takeout but nothing beats eating it fresh out of their oven. A pie is $22 and toppings are $3 each except for their specialty toppings like artichoke hearts and sausage. We usually get pepperoni, portobello mushroom and spicy peppers. The crust is so thin and crispy at the edge and chewy in the center. Their sauce is delicious. Every ingredient is top notch. Also free garlic and basil!

Waited for about 20 min on a thurs afternoon for lunch here. Definitely worth the wait. The restaurant looks like an old cottage - cozy and inviting. Perfect setting for drinks with good friends. Food was great, especially the chicken meatballs which is offered on a salad, in a sandwich or by itself as an appetizer. I say skip the filler and just get it as an app. The chicken pot pie was sooo good. Lots of veggies (that actually have crunch to them) and chicken, although it seemed like the whole thing wasn't heated all the way through - it really didn't matter to me. Surprisingly good beer selection and wines by glass.
Great service..

I think the ramen here is pretty good BUT not worth the hype of worth waiting hours for. Thursday night before 630 didn't have a wait and so that was nice. The bar seating was actually not too bad, aside from the fact that the tall chairs are inconveniently tall for short people like me to hop on (5'1). I didn't feel like i was any more in other people's personal space than when sitting at a table...but YMMV. The servers are nice but really don't do that much--they seat you at this U shaped bar for a reason (easier for them to serve!) Had the classic. If you're familiar with Korean food the soup tastes like seollungtang - which is a good thing btw! Haha. I thought it was fine but got a lot saltier towards the middle. I personally love strong flavors but this was a little too much. Oh yeah and the pork buns. Pretty good actually...! Good when fresh but a little greasy (it's fatty pork, so expected). Anyways. Docking a star because it's 1) hard to find 2) pricey 3) overhyped and 4) the shouting and yelling of the servers drives me insane! Can't keep a conversation in there without hearing some loud shouting.

The only thing that I don't love about this wonderful french restaurant is it gets too touristy and not enough of the tourists speak French. Â Pick the off hours and you might be surprised at who pops in.
broke da mouth Excellent representation of my home state, better than anything in my home town, has Hawaiian sun, just wish I lived closer or it was in Manhattan. Can't wait for brunch to start
Pork belly +1!!!
We had been to Lidia's in Kansas City and were expecting something similar. The food was good and the atmosphere nice but it was not what we were expecting.

24 hours you can't beat that.... especially when you have the cafeteria cosmo to order. The price is reasonable and the atmosphere is great very chic and modern. A good place to go after a hard night of partying cause you can get breakfast all day... my kind of place. Service is wonderful always end up over tipping the waiters. You definitely need to check this place out.
Excellent sushi and service. Â The prix fixe is an incredible bargain.

Highly recommend if you want to try something off the beaten path and have some rich wholesome food. Went here last night for dinner with my friend and we each ordered the hummus to start and mac n' cheese for dinner (which they offer in about 4 different ways). The food was AMAZING and the ambiance was really cool. The place is cozy and relaxing. Best to go when looking for a table for two. They even have games you can play while waiting for your food.

Outstanding restaurant! A 5 star rating here is a no-brainer. Each and every dish my group tried was amazing at Market Table. The vegetable sides are big enough to share. Make sure to have the Corn off the Cob and the Black Kale. We tried a real variety on entrees: duck, pork, fish. The waitress strongly recommended the Duck, which was outstanding! Its served with both sliced breast and confit. Fall off the bone delicious! The Whole Pig of the Day special (a daily cut) was a deliciously fatty (and totally edible) Pork Belly with grits and a home-made pork rind. The Sea Bass was also very good. One thing I found strange was that they didn't have any of the popular whiskeys: Maker's Mark, Bulliet, Jack Daniels Market table would be a very good date spot. Great ambience.

Been here twice, years apart. Both times the menu, wine selection, and service were fabulous. Â The decor inside is not much to look at (meaning: blank walls, white tablecloths). Even outside, which is lovely in warm weather, is not much fancier than some metal tables and chairs. But the food and wine make up for the lack of scenery. I've tried: octopus salad, a rabbit entree, duck risotto, a duck entree. All fabulous.

*Sicilian slice (yummy!!! Large square slice with sauce on top; the crust was bready and wonderful, the cheese wasn't overwhelming, loved this pizza!!! Would definitely have it again but I want to try it with toppings or their other pizzas) *eggplant sicilian (eggplant with penne, romano, bread crumbs and mozzarella; pretty good; very cheesy though; the eggplant was very drenched in sauce so it was super soft, I would have preferred less sauce and a crispier eggplant, regardless, it wasn't bad) *garlic bread (this was legit, haha, loved this bread! crispy, garlicy, and perfect) *broccoli rabe and sausage (it was ok, not my favorite dish, kind of plain) *chicken parmagiana (nothing amazing haha, tastes like chicken parm) *arugala salad (yes! very good, the argula was fresh and nicely dressed) The quality of food from this place is good, definitely want to dine in one day and try their ices, other pizzas and croquettes

I usually stop by one thin crust pizza place when I visit NYC and so have I've alternated between Grimaldi's and Lombardi's. Â I think both are really good, but have to say Grimaldi's in Brooklyn is still my favorite. The mozzarella is the key and is very good, but the crust is just decent (too crispy for me, parts were just too hard). Â I got the mushroom and pepperoni, which were fine, but didn't enjoy the sauce this time around. Â A little more basil would be good too. Â Also this place is Cash only. Â  I used to think only NY had the good thin crust pizzas, but I think places in SF are catching up.

This little restaurant is truly a Hole in the Wall. The interior is small and might not look that pleasing, the kitchen is open and whenever someone enters the restaurant the cold wind blows in.... but wait until you have their food! I had a beef noodle soup with a couple of baos. The soup was perfect for this cold weather. The noodles were soft, the meat tender, and the broth was excellent. Â When a soup is good we Asians like to express in this way: refreshing. The baos were delicious as well. When u r in Chinatown (Manhattan) definitely check it out!

I love this tiny place! I ate here for the first time about 8 years ago and it still rocks! Falafel platter & sandwiches always amazing; Baba ghanoush is excellent. Â Take it easy on the hot sauce, it's good but blazing hot! Â Oh and the Baklava is also excellent. Â Mamoun's has one of the best tasting AND best priced falafels in the country!

Lombardi's pizza is delicious. Â It's one of the best examples of NY style pizza. Â But keep in mind, the line to get in is insane (at any time of day or night). Â They only sell pizza by the pie (not by the slice). Â But if given a choice I go with Grimaldi's.
The food was fantastic and the service was just right. Definitely a place to which I will return.

Best pizza I had with my visit to NYC! There was more mozzarella on this pizza then anywhere else. Waited in line for about 35 minutes and it was totally worth it. Ordered a large for me and my gf and ate or leftovers later in the day while touring the city! Very good cold pizza! I was come to Grimaldi's every time in visit NYC!

Really large portions just like mama used to make (if your mama was a big Italian mama!). Â Nice friendly service. Â Think Buca Di Beppo for you West Coast people but a little less commercial. Â All you need is literally one pasta dish...
Love the drinks and the freshness of the vegetables and Fish!!! And the the servers are excellent

My second time there, was very disappointed , plus overpriced and not worth my money , 3 people, we had 3 glasses of wines and 6 plates , we ended up with $250, including the tip. Tabouli was very dry and tomatoes were scarce. Chicken taouk skewers (kebab) $23 had no flavor . Kefta, lamb meat tasted like hospital food. Batata harra, was oily and horrible. Duck shawarma was nothing special . Would love to say otherwise about ilili but this overpriced place is nowhere close to a real Lebanese Â cooking.

Really? The best pancakes ever? The reviewers must have never had seriously good pancakes....and for $14 plus, they are only mediocre and certainly didn't look anything like in the photos.. I cook a 10 X better pancake at home. Had the crunchy banana with cinnamon chilli chocolate sauce - the best part was the bananas, but $14 for a crunchy banana? Any kind of sauce must be asked for and butter came in typical, diner style wrapped-pats. We shared several dishes and besides the food being nowhere near expectations, the interior decor was boring, and the service was rude and not deserving the tip that was automatically added to the bill - good thing because I would not have left much of a tip. $23 bucks each for a disappointing meal and experience.

I'm actually inspired to write this review. This place rates a very strong $$$ experience on the restaurant scale. The food is superb. Value is ridiculous. No need to pay and wait for Locanda Verde or Gradisca. Much(!) better than Malatesta. Shrimp tomato risotto blew me away. My friend took a bite and did a freeze frame with her eyes shockingly widened. It has a depth of flavor that sticks to your palette. Not sure how they did the stock but it hits your umami tastebud. Like the kind of rich bone marrow beef broth that burrows into your tongue - but seafood style. The octopus salad was divine. It was different because the octopus was amazingly soft and sweet. They must have marinated it in a softening agent. That or they massaged it for 2 hours like 3 star Michelin sushi chef Jiro. The assortment of sauces was light but very flavorful. I am the type who would not miss wine if i never had another sip. I do not crave wine. However, my wine was absolutely delicious. The Cannoneau. The nose is spectacular. I think it has Grenache because it had the sophisticated perfume/cologne smell that French blends have. I was afraid it would overpower like a merlot but it was a hybrid between a Pinot noir and Cabernet. Perfection. Â A glass is $9 but would run you $13 in tribeca. The waiter automatically pours everyone a bump to try first. My friend had a great white wine. Big Sauvignon blanc fan. Service is efficient, prompt, and lightning fast. I think it's one waiter and bartender duo. Think casino dealer efficiency with a French accent. How they cook such wonderful food in that tiny little kitchen is unbeknownst to me.
Uva is a great place for a first date. The atmosphere is extremely romantic. For a more detailed review, please click the link below: halsteadproperty.tumblr.â€¦

I went to Le Grainne on a monday around 7 with a friend. As soon as we entered a charming french musician bowed his head to greet us as he was singing and playing "la boheme", lovely! We shared a cheese plate, I had the risotto de Mario and my friend had the preciutto mozzarella pesto sandwich. The cheese plate was simply BEAUTIFUL! I'm already crazy for cheese but my eyes were also eating this generous collection of soft and strong cheeses. My risotto was simply delicious, my friend says his sandwich was a delight. The food, the wine, the music, all were agents to produce a wonderfull experience, a genuine french atmosphere, for a very reasonable price. My friend Â and I are coming again soon!
went there for late night drinks. great music, lovely seating and ambiance, and drinks that are not overpriced. it wins!

Excellent meal. Service was also very friendly and attentive. Â Started with the torchon which was creamy and really good. Â They paired it with some dried fruit and nuts, and purÃ©ed something...it all meshed very well together. Â Then had the Trofie Nero dish. Â I see why it's so popular! Â It was fantastic. Â This will be on my list of places to come back to when I'm back in NY.

Awesome fun and friendly staff, beautiful decor and the food is delicious - especially like this place as a brunch option. Best shakshuka ever - the cowshuka is awesome with marguez in it and the falafel was incredible with delicious sauces on top. Hummus was amazing - they just don't offer wholewheat pita which was a bit disappointing. Highly recommended!

I was visiting New York and tried this place. It was unbelievable how good the lasagna was. A lady sitting next to me recommended it and it was stellar. They will not sit you until everyone in your party is there. Excellent food and I highly recommend.
Brilliant. I'm not even half as addicted as my friend to their macarons but I'll always be willing to shell out $3 each for these guys. The salted caramel, vanilla and coconut are all fabulous.
Delicious~~! must try when you are around~!

Came here last night and it went along way to overcome my Â disappointment in the collapse of my beloved mets to the lowly pirates...anyway, I digress. Started with a duo of salads, one the typical roasted beats, goat cheese, arugula and really yummy cherry tomatoes(both red and yellow). The other was a burrata with really interesting and quite juicy purple heirloom tomatoes. The tomatoes were truly wonderful in both, though the burrata could have had a little olive oil drizzled over it but all in all refreshing and nice. Then I was urged to try and the lasagna bolognese and it did not disappoint. Nothing too kinky, but it was really exceptional bolognese in a healthy sized portion. Really a solid place, though I will say the service was subpar. Still for under $25 a person, I truly enjoyed...... p.s. I had the prime rib the first time I went here and it was also very enjoyable but that bolgnese was pretty addictive!!!

This place has a nice vibe and good food - my only complaint being when I was there last (a party of 7) they automatically added the tip to the bill, then didn't say anything when we tipped on top of that not realizing that the tip had been added to the bill. Â So, our waitress (who wasn't completely attentive) got two tips for our table. Â  The food is good, filling and simple. Â I'll go back, but will be more careful next time with a large party.

I loved everything about this place. The waitress was amazing always with a smile on her face. The food was perfect in every aspect and the decor was also great. Can't wait to try some other things on their menu. Porkies is definitely worth the calories.

Thelma on Clinton is a must if you are on Clinton street. Firstly, the staff is super nice and friendly. The owner is always on premises touching tables and making sure that customers are happy with everything. The food is tasty and well done. The house smokes stuff is the way to go! I really enjoyed. Will be back for sure!

Restaurants like this make me almost wish I lived in a place that was more "hipster" or Nolita/LES. Â I guess I am just happy to get to visit, whether it is for my live indie music or to eat at places like this. Â This area has so much character and locals get to go to hang out at these quaint places like all the time. Â It was the casual ambience that got me. Â I'm probably too corporate and preppy for a place like this normally. Â ;P I had the Mediterranean couscous with chicken and my date had the spicy tomato meatballs. Â I left the meal kinda wishing I had ordered his dish which was much better. Â I'm rather fond of bread dipped in warm tomato sauce. Â The Mediterranean couscous I had was a tad bit too dry and bland and this is coming from a girl who has cooked couscous at home with what was to me was a more palatable result. Â  Don't get me wrong. Â The presentation was beautiful and the hummus on top helped with the dryness, and like I said my date's dish was delicious, but the couscous needed to be fluffier and the chicken moister. Â I think it could have benefited from being soaked in chicken stock. Â It tasted like a vegetarian couscous with the chicken added on as an afterthought.

I had brunch here a few hours ago and it was delish. I've been wanting to try this place out since it opened a few months ago. I stopped in today, sat at the bar, and ordered. I had "leas breakfast" which consists of toast, sausage, scrambled egg with kale, and a crispy potato. Sooooo yummy! With a ton of herbs. The decor is beautiful - wood tables, chandeliers, and coat hooks! I loved it and will be back!

Had the miso ramen with roast pork. Super salty! Like way too salty, salty. Pretty much all I tasted in the broth was salt, no complex flavors that you normally expect from a good broth. The pork was ok, nothing special and they definitely didn't sear it or anything. The skin looked kind of just melted and it didn't have a pretty color, to say the least. On the plus side, the noodles were good. A nice al dente texture throughout the whole time I ate. And the hostess has the time estimates and seating system down, which is great in terms of efficiency.

This place is probably older than I am but its still probably one of the best places to eat around the neighborhood. The chicken and ribs are really good and for an low and affordable price. They take orders fairly quick and the lines move fast. Sometimes the place is really packed depending on the time of day. There are seating here but it is not really cozy and I usually take mine to go.

You don't wine and dine someone you just met, but you can supply them with one of the best slices of their life for the price of a beer. Want to know if that ladddddy you are talking to is worth it? Offer to take her to Artichoke, if she balks onto the next one. Artichoke works on any level between CM Punk sober to David Hasselhoff on the bathroom floor.

yum yum. no new york trip is complete or authentic without a stop by this cart. as everyone else says, love the white sauce- its what makes their dish. they also give you a ton of food. what's not to love?

For a minute I thought I was home, and by home I mean Portmore, Jamaica. Â Yes Gladys is that good. Â It deh pan par (translation: can hang) with any West Indian restaurant in Brooklyn. Â The flavors taste like somebody's granny in the kitchen. Yeah man, jerk pork is on point they just need some more 'skin' pieces, jerk chicken is relish and the didn't. Â Rumor has it the owner went to Jamaica to research and he got it right. Â I will def be back. Â The only reason it's 4 and not 5 stars is because I haven't tasted the goat or oxtail yet. Â Btw the festival a tek life!!!! (Translation; is on point)

I came here on a summer Saturday night with my mom and sister. We were told that there would be a 45 minute wait but it ended up being much shorter. I got the chicken biscuit and it was really really good. The corn on the cob (seasonal side) was amazing. For dessert (have to get a pie, right?) I ordered the apple pie with graft on cheddar was quite amazing as well. I would totally recommend for a chill Saturday meal.

This is my favorite dumpling place! Hands down! For all the Vanessa lovers out there, the difference between these two dumpling place are Prosperity has more meat in their dumplings and Vanessa has more vegetables. So depending on what you like more of, that would factor your decision. For me, it's meat :) and yes I did a test run between these two dumpling houses. Sometimes I question what meat was used, 5 dumplings for $1??!! But I learned to stop asking questions a long time ago, especially when it relates to food.
This place is literally over rated.

Just got there the night before Valentine's day. We walked in at 9:10PM and we got a table rather quickly - the host came twice at the bar to apologize that it took longer that he told us - very nice; and the girl at the bar was also super sweet. Food was very good. We got Lamb and Cod, it was perfect. Service was nice too. My only small complain is that it looks very cozy from the outside, but it tends to be a bit loud inside. But, still a great place in the area!

Best sangria ever the food is amazing I love this place the service is great plan ahead and make reservations. Â The flamenco show is awesome tho the guitarist is kind of freaky but he can play is A$$ off. Â The food is amazing except the squid on its own ink that's just not for me but everything else is great. Â GO!!!!!!

Well yelp is right about one thing the pancakes are really good! This establishment has a nice setting, a good crowd and they serve you plenty of food. If you choose to eat there for brunch, arriving early is a must as the line can get long however they do move pretty quickly. Â To add to any meal, a must is the Cajun Bloody Mary, this drink will surely pop you out of any hang over from the night before.

For cheap roast meats and noodle soup, Noodletown (not to be confused with Noodles Town on Mott) is the place to beat. Whether you're here late at night or just for a cheap lunch, the value here cannot be beat. Service here is actually pretty rude and getting your water refilled is incredibly difficult, but for some reason I've learned to accept and tolerate that here. Seems like the waiters/owners here won't really change their ways anyway, and given the crowds that come here during the meal hours and late at night, there's no reason why they would need to change. Obviously, this isn't the only place to get noodles and roast meat, but the price here is just hard to beat. Baby pig and the roast duck are probably my favorites, and the wonton noodle soups are done fairly decently. My friends and I are contemplating getting a roast pig from here, but just have to find the right occasion. Overall, the food and value here is amazing for late night eats and greasy hangover recovery, but don't come here expecting amazing service or ambiance.

Only went here for a drink but loved the atmosphere! My gf and I sat at the bar and Â the bartender Patrick was beyond kind! I wasnt sure what kind of wine I wanted so he let me have a little taste of one. Ended up getting a great glass of wine and just loved the experience.

I love this place. I had ordered a chicken and waffle dish which I forgot the name of but the chicken was drizzled with honey and my waffles had mushroom and rosemary SO DELICIOUS. Reminded me or Hash House in Vegas which I love. The chicken was nice and crispy and very tasty, and the waffles were to die for.. I am definitely coming back for more.

Cutie Patroller report This place is one of the first eateries to start the Gastropub trend that started in New York. Â Freemans has now become a Downtown LES classic. Which other restaurant in New York City is located at the end of a non-descript dark alley ? ( I think Commerce at Greenwich village is on a unique street but they're not on an alley ). An absolutely must- order dish is the Artichoke Dip (believe me, it is worth making a trip just to taste this! ) Some of their dishes change by season, but the Beer Braised Pork Shank that I had there last time was soooo yummy -if you see it on the menu Cutie Patroller highly recommends you Â order it! The atmosphere inside is hip & cool and they are always busy. Â The space is dim and decorated with dark woods and stuffed taxidermy (eek!) Â but it has a very vintage feel to it, almost like an English country club in the middle of NYC. Â Currently, they now have an open upstairs area (^_^). by Cutie Patroller
Amazing mixed drinks. Great backyard. That is all.

Best vegan and vegetarian options for a sushi lover. Extremely convenient, affordable, FRESH and fast. Service is always pleasant. Sort of solves the problem of going out for Japanese with a vegan. I wish they were open until 2AM because it would hit the spot after a night of drinking, but other than that they're tops.

Bianca's restaurant was recommended by a NY native, so i knew it had a very good chance to be my favorite new spot. As soon as my friend an I got there it seemed to be packed, but fotunately we got a table right away. We were greeted by a very friendly italian man, and he sat us right away. We sat down and the first thing i noticed, was that it was like sitting at an italian grandmother's country side kitchen. The place is a hole in the wall but very accomodating, its stimulating in all sense of the word. The fragrant smell of food coming form the tables next to you which are literally inches away from yours, the sight of a romantic yet nostalgic mood of everyone talking (it can get to be a little loud, so not recommended for a quiet dinner) and the catching up and laughter you hear around you which makes you feel at home. We started with the eggplant parmigian, which opened my taste buds for the rest to come right away, accompanied by a glass of chianti. Then on to the main dish my friend got the taggliatelle with salcchich (pasta with a saussage tomato sauce) but it compared nothing to my lasagna. Oh if I could only describe how good it was! Im sorry for those who commented that it had no taste and should have more ricotta (the frozen dinner lasagna is right up your alley) they obviously have never had good italian fresh-made pasta. This lasagna was so fresh and had the right touch of ricotta cheese that it made me not want to finish the whole thing and keep some for later! the two tables next to me, ordered the same thing just from looking at mine. All in all, it was a wonderful experience, which is made up of all three: delicious food, good ambiance and great wine selection. For those of you who will complain about how crowded it is, how they dont have mozzarella sticks, or a varied selection of cocktails, just go to your local bar. This is a place for those who enjoy fresh italian recipes, wine and loud but cozy atmosphere.

Came here for dinner and was just okay. I'm visiting from out of town and was a little bummed that I spent one of the nights for a meal on the pizza here, because there are so many amazing places to eat in the city, and this is unfortunately not one of them. The atmosphere of the restaurant itself was nice; not too loud. They also have 1/2 price wine from 4 - 6:30 pm, so that was a plus in my book. Between my friend and I, we had the margherita pizza, brussel sprouts, and the arugula salad with grilled artichokes. The salad was good, nothing mind-blowing. The grilled artichokes were a nice touch, the dressing was not too lemony, but the arugula was a bit large and tough. The brussel sprouts were great, they come with pancetta which makes the dish a bit salty, so you may want them to go light on the pancetta or request it without. The pizza was disappointing. I've had wood-fired pizza many, many times and this crust was just soggy. I don't know how else to describe it. The outside crust was fine, the tomato sauce was fine, and there wasn't much cheese. It was a fail in my book. Sorry, won't be back. I recommend taking a cab over to the West Village or East Village and eating somewhere there.

Made the mistake of getting my black label burger cooked medium well the first time around. Â I like my burger pink and juicy, but lately when I order medium at other places, i get a half mushy burger, and i'm sick of it. I had to go back a 2nd time to order medium given the great overall reviews. Â $26 for a burger and fries is still overpriced, but it's definitely one of the best burgers i've ever had. Â The grilled onions have an excellent, somewhat sweet flavor. Â Only complaint is that it was a bit salty overall. Â Always a good sign when you don't need cheese to make a burger, though. The fries are standard crispy thin fries. Â They give you a ton, so at the least, it's a filling meal. Â I much prefer these to soggy steak fries. Â Nothing special, though. If you don't want to wait, go late on a Sunday night (say 9 PM). Â Had no trouble getting a table. Â On any week night, you'll either wait around 45 min for a table, or have to settle for the cramped bar. Â As others have said, they do take reservations. The service is decent, and they have a nice drink menu. Â Atmosphere definitely takes you back in time to a jazz club-like setting in the late 50s / early 60s. Â Worth trying at least once, and going back if you get a craving.

never had a chance to try chicken & waffles, im soo glad my first time was here! we had a group of 10, so it kinda sucked that we had to wait a lil while, and the host actually left, so i had to go inside and make sure we were still on the list. Â the host that took over, told us that it would be hard to seat us together, so i just told him it was fine spillting us up, IF he had too (i was hungry, lol) but as long as we stayed in same room. I was hoping that he would try to keep our group together, but nope, 2 tables, same room. oh well. other then that, the service was good and quick. they only got one order wrong. but the food... AWESOME! i would def go again, but probably not a big group like that.
Went as a treat for my Brother's birthday. Incredible. Creative menu, great service. People dress up a little bit.

According to my "picky" Korean friend, good Korean food is not in Manhattan but New Jersey and Queens. Her favorite place in K-town though, is Cho Dang Gol, and she said that this restaurant has the best soon tofu of the area. Of course I needed to go and see. Thus, she organized a little expedition there with some coworkers and friends. We started with the seafood pajeon (pancake) and it was good but just a little bit oily. The side-dishes came, and most were pretty standard. The mackerel was cooked in a spicy sauce instead of fried, and it was delicious. The kimchi was one of the most spicy I've had in the area, though I still prefer Hanbat's more. I ordered the kimchi soon tofu, and it was very good. The tofu was silky and tasty. How does it compare to the other ones like BCD or Seoul Garden? I'd say it's a little better, but I wouldn't be able to think of specifics unless I had them all in front of me at once. I did think that the flavor of the stew was stronger and thus I liked it more. A couple of the other friends got the seafood soon tofu, and I tried theirs. I thought the seafood's broth tasted fresher and the kimchi's tasted sour (but in a good way), as expected... I slightly preferred the seafood's flavor over the kimchi though so I'll probably order that next time. One person ordered the bulgogi stew, and it was yummy. The flavor of the marinate dominated the soup and went very well with the rice. The rice was also different from other places. They cooked it with some black rice, and thus the color was slightly gray, but it didn't look, or taste, unappetizing at all.

Not much to say what's already been said. This place is great to try different types of tea and their desserts are superb! Black sesame creme brulee is ridiculously delicious, I am certainly addicted! They do require one order of tea minimum per person, which is fine, since you can just add hot water and drink tea like a lunatic! I refilled until my tea was pretty much water.

OMG this place is amazing finally a tasty seafood place in NYC. The seafood was so fresh and I love the romantic yet down to earth atmosphere of the restaurant. The waitresses were quick and friendly. For food I would recommend the clams with the lemon pepper sauce its to die for.
