We also had the chicken tenders which were so fresh and crispy I was shocked for a seafood place. DO NOT leave without a side of Cajun fries you will regret it. Definitely going back cant wait to try the lobster!

Good atmosphere. Interesting menu - ok wine selection, menu items add up fast. Decent portions for tapas. Flavor and prep could improve (our "crispy rice cake" was mushy risotto with charred mushrooms). Food went right through us (we made it to hotel-60 Thompson-just on time). Â Good atmosphere, wish the food was better.

Food, drinks and service were great! When you get a chance, sit at the bar and watch them make cocktails. Quite impressive. : Highly recommend monkey bread, octopus and suckling pig. : Desserts (strawberry and chocolate) were okay.

All in all it was a great place. My bf really loves their soba so I've been here a few times. However, the udon curry katsu noodles on their special menu was awful. I don't think it's a good idea to mix Japanese curry (gravy like consistency) with udon noodles and add chicken katsu. I felt like I was eating gravy noodles. I really liked everything else I've ordered here before, so 4 stars, but don't get that udon curry thing. They have really fresh tofu for appetizers, and the price isn't too bad. The soba noodles are the best, and I loved their tempura.
Love love love! Went for Valentine's Day dinner and the food, service and atmosphere rocked. Def a new go to for me!

Walking into Robataya is a trip. You fall in love with the place right of the bat.... A few things. First of all the food WAS AMAZING...BUT, our server had no clue what he was doing. It took him 15 minutes just to greet us. No one came to talk to us. He finally came looking rushed and disheveled and was frustrated when we gave him a drink order. He came back with a missing beer and 1 water for 4 of us. We were so excited to try this place! But our server was not clear on how to order so we ended up ordering not enough food when we had asked him how much to order. it was very frustrating. The food was delish. The Salmon and Salmon Roe earthenware pot was so fresh and yummy. The Robataya LI duck and New Zealand lamb were tender and perfectly cooked. The vegetables were fresh and perfectly seasoned. Soft Shell crab was perfection! The lightly fried asparagus wrapped in fish paste, pine nuts and rice cracker crumbs were amazing and like nothing I've ever had (which were on the house due to our servers lack of intelligence). We also loved the hot Udon noodles. i will absolutely return and eat there again!
I've been there twice and love the food! The bartender was kind of a dick to one of my friends.
This place should be added to everybody's go-to brunch spots. Friendly service and phenomenal/interesting dishes. Nice back garden, but its quite small.

The misspelling in the name of the restaurant bothers me since it suggests that it's not authentic in some way, but the food is fantastic and the service is superb. I recommend the sweet plantains to share. Kale omelette was delicious. (As for the misspelling, it's just an unnecessary accent mark over the i (see photo), a mistake that a Cuban person would never make.)

Beware - this restaurant does NOT take credit cards, CASH ONLY. The restaurant itself is small but intimate, decor is dated but clean. In the summer months they provide seating outside, where you can bring your dog, which is nice. To review our dinner experience, the mozzarella and tomato salad appetizer was tasty and the beet and goats cheese was OK, the beets were a little dry and slightly passed their best but not to bad. I asked for a little more french bread to go with my tomato salad as it had a lot of dressing on it but was told they were out which was odd as the table next to us was shortly served with french bread! I ordered the fish special but would not recommend it. They presented it to me first and it looked great in the pan, I thought for an instance they were going to prepare it at the table but it was taken away and then served to me over 10 mins later. By the time it arrived it was cold at the tail-end (stone cold, like it had been chilled) and lukewarm at the head. When I told the waiter he strongly disagreed with me and told me that the fish was not cold, then walked away. He came back to our table and offered to cook it again when he noticed I wasn't eating. The fish already had the flavor that it had been reheated so I declined to reheat it again, by that point I was done with the dish anyway as the vegetables they served with it were also old, over cooked, cold and again had a flavor that they'd been reheated. I understand kitchens prep food in advance but seriously it doesn't take much to serve fresh food and have a little quality control. That said, my husband really enjoyed his shrimp pasta dish, it was hot and tasty. Pasta was cooked well and lots of shrimp. For dessert we had tiramisu it was tasty and a good size to share. When we received the bill we immediately handed over a credit card and were told they didn't accept cards. As we didn't have cash my husband left and walked to a nearby ATM. While he was gone the waiter came by, took the bill and as he walked away told me they had forgotten something. I thought at first that they might comp the dessert or something like that as the main dish had been bad but no, they actually added a few items they'd forgotten and charged us in full for everything. Not good customer service in my opinion for a badly cooked and expensive meal. The staff were pleasant and the waiter as we were leaving attempted an overdue apology but by then it really was too late! It's possible we would come back for salad and pasta if we were desperate but then again there are LOTS of other restaurants to eat those dishes. I am sincerely disappointed as I would liked to have added this restaurant to our list of local and walkable places to eat but sadly no!

I was really, really hoping I would like it here more. The pizza was good. Great...not so much. I was definitely able to tell the ingredients were fresh though. But it didn't blow me away. We ordered outside and ate outside. The counter person was nice enough. They really keep the line moving. The customers are TERRIBLE! After being asked if we were in line by a man, the same man proceeded to cut us in line anyway(and the 10 people behind us!). Then I went to get a table while my husband waited for the pizza. A couple left and I sat down at the table to wait. This woman, her husband, her friend, and three kids just sit down at my table and the woman claimed I took her table after she put down the pizza. They do have a parking lot, but good luck. Street parking is pretty easy. Spumoni was...good enough. Worth a try...just once. I give three stars because the ingredients really are very fresh and prices are decent.

How dare you call yourself Petite? If you think for a minute that I believe you when you say that it's because of your size you are wrong beau mon cher.... You are French you sexy little thing you; you lure me, trap me with your pastel colors, with your flare and arrangements; you display your breads and croissants and pastries with impunity... then you give me the most amazing omelettes, sweet delicious and gigantic waffles with cream strawberries; good coffee, outside seating, delicious crab cakes, mussels and half price Belgian beer on a Tuesday afternoon... You have it all played out with your motif of Tintin; bring me back to those streets on the Blvd. de St. Germain and make me feel as though I was transported to a neutral oasis of giddy and delicious leisure, relaxation and mental ga-ga.... Â you know who-WHAT you are but you name yourself Petite because you are.... a coquette. Â Donc j'aime votre petit dejeuner Et tu.

We have been here a couple of times. Â Extraordinary NYC vibe. Â The bartenders all rock the house! Â Very Hipster but exciting energy as a result. Â The Bone Marrow Poppers should come with a disclaimer "Warning Highly Addictive!" Â  Â Crazy good! Â  Again, it's all about the bartenders! I almost don't want to say anything because it is already mad crowded but this place is too good to not acknowledge.

A star for free beer with a check-in. A star for delish ramen Monday special. A star for fresh spicy tuna roll. A star for an interesting spin of "coffee and donuts" dessert. It's just kinda far from everything.

The mozzarella on my caprese was remarkable. The tomato and the basil...not so much. Proportion wise, they didn't make sense. The tomato slices were far too thick and the basil tasted old and not freshly picked so I ended up pushing that to the side. My chicken parm was pretty good considering I am an Italian food snob. It's very hard for me to find a chix parm at a restaurant that I do like and this one was pretty respectable which they should consider quite an honor. Dessert was mediocre. The waiter clearly thought it was God's gift to desserts and called it 'heaven on earth' and actually ridiculed me for not finishing it OR eating it the right way (starting from the back)....I'll eat the darn mousse however I see fit, thank you! Fin.....

After 6 years in NYC I finally made it to Grimaldi's in Dumbo, Brooklyn. Â We went with a small group of 5 visiting from CA so we had to show them what NY pizza was all about. Â They were down to wait no matter the how long so that was a huge factor. Â It was 30's out and windy but our wait wasn't too bad at 3pm got in within 30 mins. We ordered two pizzas: 1) Margherita with Garlic and 2) Pepperoni, Sausage, and Garlic Both were a hit and extremely delicious. Â We loved the crust and the sauce flavored very good. Â No one complained and usually my girl from CA loves to complain so this was very impressive!!!!!

Disappointed with the service we received from the hostess. The food and waitress made up for it though. The eggs Benedict and hash browns were delicious (made with tarragon which I love). Â We also got the hummus and bf got the blueberry pancakes. Overall, the food was very good and we'll be back.

All right, y'all. Times are Tough 2009 continues its theme. It's almost been two weeks since I've written a review. I've been crippled by a work project, a dwindling bank account, and exhaustion, so I've barely ventured beyond the compounds of work and home. I have a draft saved for a review of the Union Square Wendy's. And I was giving it three stars.* WHAT IS GOING ON?! So when Preeti B asked me out to brunch on Sunday, I jumped at the opportunity. Anything to avoid leftover pizza, am I right?** Plus, I've been meaning to check out Buttermilk Channel for a while. We were extremely lucky to have beautiful weather on the day we went because it's true that there will always be a wait. "Thirty minutes, but be generous with me, please," said the hostess. Of course, of course. Half an hour later we were seated outside, a romantic table for two. Here's where Buttermilk gains my respect: Your brunch includes your choice of tea or coffee, as well as your choice of orange juice, mimosa, bloody mary, or champagne. THANK YOU. Never make me choose between a mimosa and coffee. I'll skip the caffeine for a buzz in most cases, but I will be Grump McGrumperson regardless. I ordered the scrambles with mushrooms, goat cheese, and spinach. Dee-lish! I was mainly in it for the additional sides: hash browns, two pieces of toast, and a little salad. It beat paying $4 for an extra side. Preeti, on the other hand, ordered the Pecan Pie French Toast, and after tasting it, I was left slack-jawed. Then we got into it about which is better: Cake or Pie? To which I replied, "Pie!" and Preeti said, "Well, you are from Pennsylvania." Props to my Society of Friends! The inside layout was a little cramped, and there's only one bathroom (albeit, a lovely perfumed one!) so don't hold it in. Buttermilk may not be a total home run for me (the food was good but I could probably make what I ordered at home), but the ambiance and prices make it worth it. And heck, it beats Wendy's. __________ * The review started out as a joke until I realized I was actually reviewing it. Listen, I love me some Wendy's. THERE I SAID IT. ** Let it be known, I still think cold pizza for breakfast is delicious.

Most everything in NYC was closed the day after the Great Blizzard of 2010. Frantically calling restaurants around town, phones just rang endlessly, disappointing me at every turn (can you accomodate a group of 9?), but Brindle Room came through in the clutch. I guess it's not surprising, since chef and owner Jeremy Spector apparently lives above his cozy East Village spot. Lucky for us. We ended up taking nearly half the seats in the narrow restaurant. Steve accidentally called it "The Bindle Room," which sounds like a secret hobo hangout, but it's actually very nice inside-- dark wood dominates, with two rows of hightops leading up to a long bar in the back of the restaurant. That day burgers were very good. Sure, there were some minor issues, but for obvious reasons I was in a forgiving mood. Even so, I was floored by how much complex, dry aged flavor was packed into the beef, which dominated in a way that seemed even more pure than the infamous Minetta Tavern Black Label Burger (and at $13, for at half the price). However, I had some minor issues with the cheese selection (no American?) and the fries were nothing special. According to Jeremy, he uses the trimmings from his partner at Sebastian's Steak House in Morristown, NJ, where the steak is dry aged on premises. The blend itself is a combination of a bunch of cuts, that can apparently change based on what's available. From his explanation, he was clearly excited about the quality of beef used in the burger. A few weeks later, even after eating a slew of incredible burgers, the Brindle Room's burger still haunted me. So last week I stopped by for a late lunch (the burger is only served at lunch) and eagerly ordered a burger. To my sincere delight, they now have American cheese. As good as the first was, the second burger was even better: cooked to a perfect medium rare and sporting an incredible sear which gave way to loosely packed meat leaking aged beef juice, each bite coating my mouth in complex, fatty flavor. This time, the onions were far more caramelized and the fries look much, much better (and there's about 3x as many). I've eaten a lot of great burgers recently, and lately my preferences have leaned towards thin, griddled patties, but this may have been the best of the lot. As I said, it's only available for lunch, so I recommend finding an excuse to skip out on work ASAP. In the meantime, I'll be fighting my own cravings (and returning to try the rest of the menu for dinner). Pics: flickr.com/photos/lawandâ€¦

I visited this wonderful place last Saturday night with a friend, who had been raving about it for a few months. To start, the place is tiny which struck me the minute I walked in. Â However, a charming greeting by the bartendar and skillful attentive service by the server Rafael, immediately calmed my nerves. Â I cannot say enough about the service. Â Efficient, friendly, but just enough without being intrusive. Â We began our meal around 7:30 and left after midnight. Â  We had almost everything on the menu. Â Some standouts included the heirloom tomatoes, brandade, sundried tomato tartine, and the duck rillette. Â I would also say the cheeses are of a nice selection, even if they were all American which I did not expect to see here. Â It was nice to see this and even nicer to sample them. The wine selection was impressive as well. Â The options were numerous enough to always invite another glass, but without being too overwhelming. Â Their quirky map on the wall was a nice touch. I realize the cutlery is small (ok, very small), but it adds to the charm of the place. Â The food is well worth the price. Â I would highly recommend this place for a romantic evening who someone you actually enjoy talking to or catching up with a close friend.

Very trendy Peruvian restaurant! Â The Matador is awesome you get chicken, wiener fries, avocado salad, fried garlic plantains, and rice'n beans all for $36!!! Â It was only two of us but that meal is really meant for 4ppl I think. Â The pitcher of Sangria was delicious and strong. Â LOVE Pio Pio 8!!!

What a cute little French place! And great for brunch. The food was delicious awesome. Here's what we ordered: La Savoyarde - camembert cheese, bacon, potatoes, swiss cheese, white wine, onions & garlic Le Croque Monsieur - toasted sandwich with ham, emmenthal cheese & salad side Both dishes were amazingly great! The dessert crepes looks amazing too, but I was just so full. I'm definitely going back. It's a totally different places than the crepes places in the LES, which is also good, but this place is a mini French cafe. You get the feel too!
Moved to the area in July and I've been here 4 times already. One of the best! Brunch is good and so is dinner. Even nice for just a quick drink!
You know, great place to kick back with a small group on a Thursday night, but they rejected my yelp coupon! Told me it wasn't a legit coupon and they didn't have a deal with yelp. Disappointing.
If you are really hungry, it is a fine choice. But I would save the calories. I didn't like any of the hot sauces either.

My friend and I came at 7:40ish on a Wednesday night. I had to make a quick run to the nearest Chase for some cash because I didn't realize until I got to the front door that Jeepney is cash only! It was already pretty busy inside and no tables were available, so we settled in at the bar. It was comfy and spacious, though we were subject to chilly breezes from the door once in a while. Chori Burger: The price of the burger might seem off-putting to some (the $17 price tag sure threw me off at first), but it's SO WORTH IT. In fact, one order, which comes with a generous portion of fries, is enough to satisfy two people of moderate appetites. Our bartender-cum-waiter recommended that we get the burger cooked no more than medium, so we got ours cooked medium. The patty is very thick, but the bread and meat hold together quite well so it wasn't too difficult to eat. The burger is sooo juicy, yet it wasn't overly greasy and didn't leave me feeling disgusting afterward. Plus, the condiment (banana ketchup? bbq sauce?) complements the meat's flavors perfectly. And the fries. Oh, man. They're pretty thick cut, which I prefer, with a satisfying crispy exterior and soft interior. I don't know if they're made of regular or sweet potatoes; they looked regular and pale but tasted sweet. What sorcery is this?! The accompanying sauce (some sort of mixed mayo) was good, but I liked the fries on their own. Bicol Express: Pork shoulder with chili peppers (yum), two little things of bok choy and a bowl of rice. The pork is quite tender and on the salty side; there's a lot of yummy fat, but the flavors aren't very complex. I liked it but I think it got kind of overshadowed by the burger, haha.

Happy our 'til 10pm EVERYDAY, what can be better than that?!?! Â And the drinks are sooooo good! Â The lychee martini is not too sweet and just strong enough. Â The food is really good also, and the service is always great with very friendly and helpful bartenders. Â  The ambiance is the perfect vibe of trendy and chill. Â A great spot if you're looking to meet cool people outside of the super trendy or super dive setting.

mmmm soon dubu. really great lunch specials. nothing cures a hangover like a piping hot and spicy bowl of tofu soup. I usually get the seafood one. they have a good assortment of apps that come with the meal. it varies but typically it'll always come with salted fried fish and kimchi and a raw egg to put in your soup (if you feel like it.) it comes with rice in a clay pot and then they add water to make a broth. to be honest the rice broth is pretty gross. completely unnecessary. just throw it out. you'll thank me later. it is kinda pricey for lunch but you do live in New York, right? get used to it. treat yourself to a spicy bowl on a freezing winter (or freezing spring) day. thumbs up. will definitely be back.

Joya has an amazing ambiance as you walk in it is very romantically lit up. Â Additionally, they have a very cozy seating area outside as well. Â On top of that their service was great as my friend and I played musical chairs as we could not find the perfect spot to sit. When it came to food, I ordered the Kang Gai sliced chicken with eggplant, bamboo shoots, peppers and carrots in a red coconut curry sauce. The dish was so savory and the vegetables tasted amazing in the red coconut curry sauce! Delicious!! I downed it with a nice cold Brooklyn lager on draft. Will definitely come back to try other dishes!

I loved that the big bowl of Saigon pho and some spring rolls were sufficient for me and my boyfriend - who were both starving at that time. There's nothing better than some good pho on a nippy February night! Anyway, I also ordered Grilled Pork Chops, Shrimps with spring rolls and rice to go. Very flavorful and satisfying. The only downside was when my boyfriend went out to withdraw some cash, the waiter kept staring at me like, "Come on, order something already!!!!" He kept glancing at me, approaching me and asking if I wanted anything even though I told him I'll just wait for my boyfriend cause I'm not sure what he wants. So meh, I just ordered the things I usually eat so he could stop bugging me. I know you want my butt out of there so you could seat more customers but chill out, it's not as if we were going to sit there for an hour. But whatever, I'm still a fan!

Stumbled on Saraghina with a few friends after finding the restaurant we meant to visit was closed. Very glad we did! The service, atmosphere and food were all fantastic. We shared gnocco fritto, a pizza di Napoli, and a pizza con carciufo. We sat in the back room, by the pizza oven, and the smell of the wood oven was a severe temptation until our food arrived. The staff were very friendly; it seemed like everyone who worked there thanked us on our way out.

woohooooooooooooooooooooooooooooooooo! i'm so giddy. i didn't mind the walk over to the 41st street location. but now, having a new store so close just makes me want to say it again... woohooooooooooooooooooooooooooooooooo!
Great food and wines....we sat at the "bar" overlooking the kitchen area and enjoyed watching our meals being prepared. Loved our food and the wine suggested by our waitress.

I've been here twice and have always enjoyed it. They don't take reservations and you can expect to wait thirty minutes, but it is definitely worth the wait! The staff is amicable and Penelope's has a really down to earth feel. Both times we went for brunch. Once I ordered the waffles and the other time I ordered the farmer's omellete. Both were fantastic!

I love this place because it's really casual and cute. The moules and frites are great. I've tried the Marinieres, Jamaicaines and the Grand-Mere. The Jamaicaines was my least favorite of the three. It wasn't bad or anything, just not my favorite. The other two are amazing. They give you so much, I could barely finish my portion. Their weekly specials are great too. Half price beers on Mondays (all night!) are hard to beat, and a great way to start a week. The servers are really friendly too, very charming.
Awesome value - the chef is incredible, generous with portions, and even offer delivery. Â I frequent as much as I can.

5 stars based on drinks alone. You will not have a better drink anywhere. Will not! And i'm talking about the upstairs bar, NOT downstairs. When you are upstairs at the Dead Rabbit, just know that you are in the best bar in all of the United States, and most likely anywhere in the world (from a mixed drink standpoint).
So, now I have a BBQ problem.

The place is mediocre. The service was as bad as it gets! The guy at the register yells at you to place your order, and wants you to get out of his face as soon as you pay. I have tasted a lot of falafel in my life, and this was the worst ever. It was a lettuce sandwich with less than four falafel balls. Didn't fill me up at all and ended up crossing the street to Chipotle to get a burrito. I truly have no idea why it is rated so high here.

Made a last minute Open Table reservation for dinner on Friday night. Â The bar was buzzing and packed, but we were still seated right away. Â Our server was really helpful with the menu and answering any questions about the margaritas and was very helpful getting us in and out so we could still make it to a UCB down the street on time. Â  The guac was as good as advertised (it's written up on a bunch of blogs, Yelp, Zagat...). Â I love d the warm soft tortillas served in addition to chips. Â Spicy mushroom soup was an interesting special (didn't love the masa dumplings, did love the mushrooms), 3 skirt steak taquitos and 2 chicken flautas were tasty, satisfying, and a value at $8 ea, and the beet salad was loaded and delicious (as were the 5 big shrimp served on the side). Â  Will def be back for dinner and $10 margaritas!
Always freash always hot!!! oh yea it melts in your mouth & every where else.

It doesn't get any better than this! Â The Prince Perfection and Margherita Pizza was the best. Â The tomato sauce was fresh. Â  During our visit to NY we met the owners son Dominick at Prince Street Pizza. Â What a wonderful young man who was passionate about his pizza! Â Thank you Dominick what a great dining experience.
Overrated overpriced

Chillin and spontaneously came in here because of the Wednesday deal--$1 dollar sandwiches and $2 for sangria--albeit with orange soda added to it. Hey, it's a place to come to when you're starving, watching your pennies or you're with a fun group. It's not a foodie's destination, but it does the job.

Totally great place for an expensive feast. Â I took my girlfriend and her mom here as an attempt to get our relationship in a better place. Â I recommend the chef's 10-course tasting. Â It certainly impressed the gold-digging mom who watches a lot of Food Network shows, but it was for naught since the girl had her sights on another fellow all along.

AMAZING sandwiches but they are racist. I walked in here to pick up an order and was ignored...my white friend walks in and suddenly gets service for my order. As good a friend he is, he goes in on them and they suddenly see me. They apologized and gave us the food for free but the scars are still there. Mannnnn, the looks I got when i walked in that store. Smh.

Went for the first time this past Monday. I have spent 3 of the past 5 years living in northern Japan, and have eaten a lot of ramen. This also makes me totally biased towards the type of ramen I am used to (namely, ramen from Sapporo and Asahikawa) Broth: 3 I ordered the "Minca" ramen, which was a shoyu base. It was fairly hefty, cloudy, and very garlicky. It tasted good, but just wasn't my style. Noodles: 2 I had a momentary lapse of reason and ordered the futomen as opposed to the chijire-men (wavy noodles on their menu). Once again, not my style, and since I really don't know what *good* futomen should taste like, I can't really judge them. I ordered an extra serving of the wavy noodles, which were too chewy/doughy for me. I tend to like them very eggy, with an almost transparent quality to them; I also really like my noodles to have a lot of "spring" to them. These noodles were not what I was looking for. Toppings:3 There was nothing out of the ordinary. The charshu was pretty good, but it was COLD at first! Big pet-peeve of mine. Gyoza: 3 The gyoza were good, but I was bummed that I couldn't make my own sauce. The dish of sauce I was given was so deep and so full that whenever I dipped a dumpling into it, it ended up overflowing. All in everything was average; not bad, but not really matching my tastes. I will try the lighter broths the next time I go.
Thin Crust! the place is very cozy, true meaning of ny pizzza

For such a popular place, I'm pleasantly surprised at how fast I was seated for brunch on a Saturday. The food was delicious but the biscuit was pretty dry. Their coffee wasn't that strong either but I had a pleasant experience.

This place is decent but not worthy of the praise bestowed on it by Yelpers. Â Here's some advice - even if you've been to the one in Japan why don't you wait until you've been to the one in New York before posting a review. Â Can you people please relax? Overall it is a cool restaurant and the food was good. Â It is not the best ramen restaurant in New York, not even close. Â Setagaya and Momofuku ramen blows this ramen away. Â However, the staff was cool and the food wasn't bad. Â It's more of a normal restaurant than a ramen shop. I'm starting to believe you can't believe everything you read on Yelp.

I have no idea why I've never written a review for this place! It was one of my first fave restaurants when I moved to NY and it truly is cozy. I spent many a winter morning snuggled up drinking tea. I've only come for brunch and my personal favorite is the brioche French toast with the chantilly cream. ORALGASMIC AF!!!! The place gets pretty packed on Sats & Suns for brunch. Once there was almost a two hour wait but it was more than worth it. At one point in time I was in here multiple times a week but this is my first visit in months and I still love it just the same. I'd like to address something, a gentleman came in as I was eating and sat himself at a table. A party of 8 walked in after him. He did not make his presence known and I'm pretty sure the staff overlooked him with the big party coming in. He left upset and made sure to let everyone know he would leave a yelp post about not being brought a menu. While I understand where he's coming from, and this is a piece of advice for anyone, if you seat yourself without making eye contact with a staff member it's your responsibility to make your presence known. It's best to wait to be seated or at least make someone aware of your intention to dine. Yes, the staff could've and should've been aware of him but I believe in being proactive and if I were him I would have done more than stomp out like a toddler throwing a tantrum. If ever an experience is not to your liking in a restaurant, communicate effectively. Offer a solution. We are adults and we are human. People will drop the ball. It's fine to let them know respectively. Anywho, I love Cheryl's! Go eat and be merry.
Great service, great food, great price - can't beat a BYOB with the food and service to match.

We made a reservation for 4 for a noon brunch on a Saturday nearly a month in advance, and despite a member of our party arriving nearly half an hour late, we were able to still sit at our table without any issue, which was nice. It's a fairly spacious area but is loud enough to create a busy vibe. I ordered the mushroom paella, which was pretty good, and I found the food to be decent quality but not too crazily priced. I tried some of the salmon crepe and the skirt steak, which were just alright. Obviously, the main draw of the brunch is the bottomless sangria, which is pretty good and is fairly free flowing. The desserts we split were the tres leches cake and the caramel flan, which were also not bad. All together, I had a great time with friends over decent food and would gladly recommend it to others.

This is a the place that my native Hong Kong friends recommend time after time. Â  The roast duck and pork are unbeatable, and better than what they found on the streets of the HK. Must be the water. I have been there countless times, and the meal is consistently great. I would not expect it to be otherwise Why would so many Boston students hop on the "5 Buck" buses " Â for biweekly refills of duck , pork and ribs Â at Bing Wong's? To read more stories about the place check out my short review at : bit.ly/nsgfe5 or lovearoundtheisland.com Gan Bei !

The food here is great and that's why my wife and I continue to return. Â However, (and it's a big HOWEVER) the owner/hostess who mans the seating area is awfully rude. Â Being a business owner myself, I get that you need to assert control and keep things moving but she can attempt to fulfill such duties with a bit more courtesy-especially with the patrons. Â After all, she is in the SERVICE industry. Â To be fair, the pricing is competitive. Â If you are looking for a good Italian place and don't mind a lack of manners, this is the place for you. Â Otherwise, I would recommend Frank instead.

Fun, young and great lychee martinis!!!!!!!!! Some of the reasons why I love Yelp is the honesty of the reviewers. I needed to find a new hot spot for the girls and I to goto. After searching around on yelp. Verlaine looked very appealing. I made sure to make reservations for 8 to secure a table ( smart idea Â if you don't want to be stuck by the bar all night) Nice and comfortable venue, a little loud but manageable enough to hear your company speak. I loved the chicken wings. They were fresh, hot and the right combo of sweet and salty. A decent Happy Hour Spot!

I wasted ten dollars eating from this place. It was my first time eating from Lombardi's after seeing how popular it is. It even said "BEST REVIEWED" on the side of a banner so my friends and I thought it might be a good place to eat. We got into the store and we were guided by a waitress who placed us in the waaaaaaaayyyyyyyy back corner of the store where the other exit was. The waiter who arrived moments after we were seated, was smiley and nice. We ordered the 18" pizza with four toppings. It took about 30 minutes for the pizza to come out and it looked delicious. We each ate 2 slices...and as I ate my second slice, I tasted this bitter flavor which I thought was from the red onions. I then turned the pizza over and it was COMPLETELY BLACK and BURNT. I told my friends to flip their's over and theirs' were burnt too. I called over the waiter to tell him that we were eating COMPLETELY burnt pizza. He looked at us with a "so.....what?" look. I also asked him if all pizzas are supposed to be burnt like this. He then tells me, "have you ever tried a pizza before? They're usually cooked in traditional coal ovens that have no temperature control, so they come out different every time." I was a little mad about him questioning me if I ever tried a pizza and told him how carelessly prepared the pizza was. He then tells me "Oh, you're supposed to tell us to cook it lightly or do you want it harshly cooked." He NEVER offered such an option to us, so instead of asking for the manager to report this waiter's ignorance and rudeness, I just told him "okay." He walked away quickly. If this waiter was not rude and annoying, I would say that the pizza was okay. It was not the best pizza I've ever tried. The meatball topping is a must get.
Hooray for upstate and Utica signs hanging! Go for happy hour. So happy this bar/restaurant is in the EV when you need a seafood comfort food fix. People are really friendly.

So it's not often that I eat an approximately 2000 calorie dinner. Â Two thousand calories. Â To put that in perspective, I would have to run almost 14 miles to burn off 2,000 calories. Â  It would be worth all 14 miles. Â Every. single. one. Â  I think this is my 3rd or 4th visit to "The Shack". Â My wife and I discovered them by accident on a trip in 2009 and every chance I get to visit New York, I'll try my best to visit. Â It's been a while since my last visit though (I think I last visited in June 2010) and I'm glad to see there are more locations including one within walking distance of my hotel. I actually think Shake Shack has replaced In-And-Out Burger as my favorite "fast food" burger. Â Everything was absolutely perfect. Â The burger, the fries, the root beer float ... everything.... perfect. Â  I should have picked up a replacement t-shirt as the one I have from 2009 is getting a bit old ... oh well, maybe next time.
Amazing taste!!!! I love it!!! Thanks, guys, for a great dinner!!!

Great wine and tapas. Â Exceptional location. Â Had glasses of the Zinfandel blend and the Tempranillo. Â Excellent. Â Also ordered the olives and Margherita pizza with arugula. Â Everything was great and we loved the ambiance,
The wait is close to eternal Â & the price is expensive but the Pizza is a must try at least once!

Coppelia is AMAZING! First of all, it served some of the best Latin/ Mexican/ South American food I have ever Â had!!! I ordered the Quesadilla and a beef empanada. My date ordered the Burger. Food was AMAZING. Oh, and we also finished off our dinners with an AMAZING milk shake! Secondly, the food is so affordable! Prices range from $6-$17 on the menu... AMAZING! Thirdly, and lastly, it's open 24/7...AMAZING! Enough said. Enjoy ;)

It's loud and always busy but we'll worth it. Â Try to get a booth in the back it's slightly quieter. . The beer menu is amazing. Â 50 tap beers plus over 100 bottles/cans in addition to the tap. Â Food is also very good. Â The mussels are my favorite, a little spicy but great with a cold beer. Â Would suggest they sell desserts. Something sweet to round out all the great flavors.

My fave pie in the slope. The service is great and the food amazing. Their dessert calzone regularly visits my dreams where I'm surround by these amazing pockets or nutella and ricotta. A dream where I can eat as many as i want and not gain a single pound. A great spot to come with a small group so you can split a pie and share a large calzone, but believe me, when it comes to dessert, you'll want your own.
One of my favorate Japanese restaurants... authentic and specialized in food selection. I highly recommend the salmon roe with sea urchin.

Public has yet to let me down. It's one of my favorite restaurants in NYC. Ya heard me! FAVORITE. The service is great, the food is fantastic, and the bar staff is just lovely. It's a great place to grab a drink with friends, have a dinner date with your boo or can be accommodating enough for a 8 person birthday party on Saturday night. They even let us bring in our own cupcakes, and waived the plating fee. Small things like this, set them apart from the bougie and stuffy places. 've tried everything, but my favorite is the pork belly and kangaroo. I know something cute sounding as a kangaroo shouldn't be eaten. But i did, and i liked it. And i'll do it again. Cheers.

Came here a couple years ago and I don't remember specifically what I got but I remember everything was delicious. The tapas and the entrees my party got were all outstanding. Would definitely go back.

This is a top of the line sushi place. I don't believe there is anything like sushi yasuda. I'm a big fan for several reasons. The interior looks like it should be on a poster for japanese minimalism. Made entirely out of wood, the interior is boxy, and big. It's truly unique. It's worth popping your head in just to see what it looks like inside. TIP: make your reservation ahead of time, and ask to be seated at the bar. It's a table level bar, and the chef's serve you your freshly made sushi. The sushi is realy high quality. So is the green tea (seriously, you must order green tea while you're there. It looks ilke you're sipping duck weed. And it's free!) They have a price fixe option for dinner that hovers around $20. That's an awesome deal. Add an extra $3 for dessert. Sweet. So why only 4 stars? The portions were a little smaller than I would have liked. Still, you can't beat this deal anywhere. Great way to impress a date.
Great hole in the wall spot! Lots of options and service is quick and friendly. This is a good option for folks that want a delicious bowl of ramen but can't stand the wait at ippudo.

Khao Kang is a fairly new addition to this Bermuda Triangle of Thai restaurants on Woodside ave. Going in, I got a lot of mixed feedback from several people. The place is small and cozy, it's basically a Thai version of a cafeteria that you find ALL over Thailand. The setup, it's either you are to staying or to going. You have the option for two or three items, but for an extra .50 cents you could get the three options. So to start off, they give a shit ton of rice. After the rice is plated, you pick out items that are placed on top of your plate of white rice. The food: I ordered stir fried cabbage with shrimp, "pa low" which is a soup of tofu, whole boiled eggs and pork belly, and lastly, "moo pot prik king." For me, I thought the portions were a tad small, but at the end of the day, the food was very Thai. It was authentic since the food was not as sweet and definitely more spicy than I was expecting. The mostly Thai clientele was also another good indication of how Thai it was. This place is a good, quick place to get authentic Thai food, but it is a tad pricey for Queens. I also finished my meal with the black sticky rice with coconut milk. I have always liked black sticky rice since I was a little kid. The one here also has coconut shavings and I think it's chunks of taro, it's worth a try.

Cosi little place to enjoy a couple of drinks with small plates with friends. Cheeses were good, nothing amazing though... And the wine offering was interesting. I found it a but pricy for what I had in my plate though.. Friendly service

When I think of Lombardi's, I think of clam pie. Their regular pizza is great, but their signature clam pie is out of this world. That's what sets Lombardi's apart from other great pizza places the the city. I had a friend who was skeptical of clam pie, but I took him there last week and he became a true believer.... Order the clam pie. You will not be disappointed!

The elusive search for the perfect birthday dinner spot lead me to new local spot, Saxon+Parole, with it's perfect combination of an upbeat, fun atmosphere and tasty food/drinks, all while allowing my girls and I to catch up over a leisurely dinner. Â  The decor was fantastic, with a large open bar space, secluded dining areas which kept the noise level reasonable, and a subtle equestrian theme. Â The celery gimlet was the perfect refreshing, delicious cocktail to kick off the birthday celebration. Â We were seated quickly at a spacious table in the back (although the reservation was for 7 people, only 6 chairs were at the table... a deficit that was quickly remedied!). Â A bottle of champagne (courtesy of my best friend, currently residing in London) was sent over and glasses filled! Â I am already in love. Â  And next, the food. Â We opted for a big share, especially seeing how the rave reviews were focused on the first courses over the main entrees. Â Here's how we fared: Seafood tower (medium): Â oysters, mussels (delicious, smoky flavor), steamed clams, shrimp, salmon tartare. Â A great selection which allowed us all to try a bit of everything. Â  Mousse pot: we got 2 orders of the mushroom pot, a perfect amount for our group. Â Extra bread was promptly provided as we scraped every delicious morsel from the pot. Beet salad: a tasty, light salad. Exactly what you expect and everything you want. Grilled pork chop: this was fantastic. Perfectly cooked and great portion. Guinness Short ribs: I must say, I've never met a short rib I didn't like, and this was no exception. Huge portion, falling off of the bone. Â Amazing. Sweet potato, miso tortellini: very yummy, but a small portion compared to the heft of the meat dishes. Cauliflower gratin, brussels sprouts, french fries: all perfect sides although the portion of the brussels sprouts could have been a little bigger--they went fast. Oh,and more blue cheese mayo, please? Dessert: Chocolate souffle! Yay! A hit (as was the birthday song that came with it...by my friends, not the wait staff. This isn't Chili's). Apple almond cake, warm cinnamon donuts, and creme caramel rounded out the meal perfectly. Â  Overall, I couldn't have asked for a better meal, atmosphere, or service. Â Thanks S+P, for making my birthday dinner, everything I hoped it could be, plus champagne!

This place is 24 hrs. Â So if you want a nice place to take a date after a late night of drinks and dancing then this is a good place to take them for munchies. But on regular times of the day, this place is still really good. The mac and cheese is pretty good. The pork chop is pretty darn good. The drink to get though...definitely the white grape martini. Strongest drink on the menu, according to the waiters. Â Good stuff.

I've only been here once but my experience was awesome! Great outdoor seating. Affordable happy hour & delicious chips & guac. Definitely check it out if you're in the west village craving mexican food.
The best pizza I've ever had! Getting the pizza is a pain in the ass but well worth the hassle. I would eat this every day if i could!

Used to have Public on my 'Red Hot List', a 'greatest hits' list compiled from Adam Platt's annual 'Hot Lists' over 4-5 years. However: (1) tasteless, watery cocktails, mostly ice; (2) appetizers dominated by sicky-sweet accents; (3) main courses served cold; (4) side-dish not served at all; (5) silly wine list, with a couple of token selections $50-70 in each group, and everything else triple-figures; (6) desserts that couldn't be bad (sticky toffee pudding) but were and; (7) lame, cheesey Euro-disco music at peak volume. Geez...what a fall from grace, and all for $250 per couple!!! Someone here must have photos on the Michelin guys.

In a city that has countless Italian eateries, Malatesta has definately become an official favourite Italian restaurant on my list! I am always worried that restaurants that label themselves as ''Italian'' are in reality ''pseudo Italian'''(translate to: overdosing the cheese, creamy heavy to digest lasagnas and pizzas with 20 different ingredients) . The focus here is on the food- fresh, tasty, simple, humble, satisfying, just the way Italian food should be. The tomatoes taste like tomatoes, the pasta is genuinely al dente, the waiters are proper Italian. Â Having extensively travelled in Italy (north to south) I appreciated that the food brought back memories of delicious cities such as Napoli or Palermo. The handwritten menus and simple warm decor brings a lot of charm to this place. All in all, eating at Malatesta is about enjoying serious Italian food, first and foremost.

Honestly some of the best cocktails I've ever had in my life! Oysters and Drinks were Amazing. Staff and environment were fantastic. Try the bell pepper infused drink! I highly highly recommend this place, you will not be disappointed.
Quiet, lovely, delicious. Staff is super friendly and nice. Amazing coffee, which, really, is all I want in life.

Loved the gigantic beef rib. It was a juicy tender short rib that I didn't want to share. The rub used is a touch spicy but so good with the fat from the rib. I know everyone loves the moist brisket here, and man it was mighty flavorful but I was very surprised that the brisket wasn't really fatty. Maybe I'm just used to hillcountry's overly fatty brisket. Â  The cornbread with peppers and honey butter is a must have. Mac and cheese, as well as the beans were ok, but clearly not the star of dinner (for me at least). I came on a Sat night, and found the service to be incredibly friendly but the hostess hard to find. Then I realized she was doubling as waitservice. For a place this busy, they should have a dedicated hostess. Overall, a fantastic very affordable and delicious bbq. Sorry hillcountry, I think I have a new bbq love.

Soooo good! Â I had the Room Service Pad Thai. Â It was fairly cheap at $14 and a generous portion size. Â It was Pad Thai with assorted seafoods wrapped in egg whites. Â The flavors all came together in the most perfect way. Â Delicious and filling! The ambiance of the place was really nice too. Â Very chic with a huge chandelier in the middle. Â Tables are close together, but it was never too noisy. Servers were friendly and polite. Â Food came out really fast.

This is a classic NYC pizza place with a long heritage. Â I always come here when my friends want the tourist NYC place but I still want a good pizza. Â Four stars only because there has been a lot of competition that has emerged in the pizza category and a lot of them just have a little bit more.

With some friends, we walked into this proverbial hole-in-the-wall on Bayard recently, and were happy we did. Despite the dismal decor and the bathroom that should best be approached with eyes closed, the experience was quite good, starting (and ending) with the food. (If you're looking for anything but the most perfunctory service, look elsewhere). Â On a busy Sunday, there were several tables open, indicating that many a tourist has yet to discover the place, or perhaps they don't know what to make of the menu, which features mainly large soup and noodle bowls, rather than the more familiar main courses. I don't know, but their ignorance was our reward. We had, in no particular order, seafood noodle soup (a "small" bowel was quite enough to share), the country-style duck-- superb-- , Chinese broccoli in oyster sauce, Â a wonderful curried chicken on rice, mixed seafood, and a couple of spring roll Â and "shrimp ball" dishes. All were good or better, and the price is right here. The four of us escaped with full bellies and were only 30 dollars per couple poorer. (Note, they add a 15% tip to the bill, so you shouldn't too).
Pro: oyster happy hour! $1.50. Fresh seafood. Great bread spread - white fish spread. Â Mussels are really tasty!! Waitress was attentive. Con: a lil pricy.

Came to happy hour here on a Monday and got some oysters and drinks. Everything is pretty standard stuff, but what was nice was just how cheap things were for happy hour. Oysters were $1 each and drinks were $4. The quality was OK, but considering it was so cheap, it was worth it (although I don't know if it would've been worth the money had it been regular time). I've never really tried oysters before, but it was decent although the size of the oyster was pretty small. Anyway, will be back to check out the rest of the menu. I love the ambiance here - it's literally a hole in the wall, and sort of reminds me of a speakeasy because the entrance is difficult to notice and easy to miss. It's nice and cozy inside, and the staff is pretty personable.

update: you have to try their summer special, Reisei Gayu, set (rice served in cold bonito broth): 1 pot of tea +1 soup + 1 rice bowl + 6 appetizers + 1 desert = $17!!! Cha-An toast with azuki and whipped cream + Jasmin ice cream: Â OMG!!! it's simply AWESOME! ================================================= my grandma, mom's side, was a Japaneses - Korean, and she'd visited us many times when I was little. at that time, my everyday wish was.. This place is amazing. Â Very small place with awesome breakfast food. Â Johnny was really nice, and the food came out super fast. Â My wife(borat voice) and I had eggs, bacon, homefries, and toast. Â So good. Â Its was only 15 bucks for the 2 of us. Â Try to squeeze in and grab some breakfast nextime you are in the area.
the best falafel sandwich i've ever tasted in the history of my life--fairly priced and very very good

Lobster rolls have somewhat become a delicacy for me, the main reason is because of their high price tag. But it's summer time, and a cold lobster roll is both refreshing and seems to hit the spot. So down came Red Hook Lobster Pound, fairly reputable in the metropolitan New York area. Red Hook offers two types of lobster rolls ($16.00 each): the Maine style served cold with celery, spices, and a touch of homemade may; or the Connecticut style roll for warm lobster smothered in melted butter. Both are served on a J.J. Nissen split-top bun. I opted for the Maine style. When I received it, I was amazed at how many chunks of lobster meat were stuffed in the bun. But soon after biting into it, I noticed the bottom half of the bun contained all slaw and celery. It was somewhat disappointed for getting my initial hypes up and then feeling somewhat deceived. As for the lobster roll, I wasn't at all amazed. Yes, the lobster was fresh, but all it tasted like was cold lobster, mayo, some slaw in a roll. It tasted like the simple components that they were, integrating together nicely, however it didn't really get me as excited as I was hoping. It was at best average, and I would have figured I could have made a lobster roll at home, with the exception of some homemade slaw, for a fraction of the price. With lobsters selling at one of the all-time lowest price of about $4.00 per pound (and if you travel to the Northeast, you can get lucky enough to score lobster for $2.50 pound), I wonder why local places like these don't adjust their prices accordingly. $16.00 for a lobster roll is somewhat overprice and not worth it at all. It's sort of insulting considering that hamburger meat and other meats sell for more than lobster at the marketplace. Red Hook Lobster Pound, I really tried to like you, but you just didn't cut it for me. Moving on...

I don't normally get pangs of hunger for Italian, only because I make it better at home than most of the joints near my office. Â A coworker brought me to Pepe and I gotta say, I can't make lasagna this good. Â It had that slightly singed edge that made the outer layer of cheese crispy, but without burning it. Â That's like the precision bomb of lasagna-making. Â There was also this other green pasta dish I tried which I can't remember the name of, but let's just put it this way, five of us got five different things, and no one had a single complaint. Well, the bread they gave out was a little too squishy, but hey, you can't complain when it's free. Â You cannot go wrong with eating here, unless you try to come smack dab in the middle of lunch, because then you'll fight for limited seating space. Â Yea, some random dude sat down at our table. Â I was gonna say something, but instead I just jacked a piece of his squishy bread while he was looking away. Â Win.
Love, love, LOVE the red velvet waffle and chicken. This is a cool spot to hang. This is one of my faves in BK!
Travel to eat here You won't be disappointed Best vegan brunch food

Oh artichoke pizza, you're definitely outstanding. Â If you stop by here, make sure to try out each of the slices. Â My favorite slices are in this order: Artichoke and Spinach Vodka Crab Margarita Any combination of two of these slices will leave you stuffed on your couch! Â YUM! When you drop by, no matter what time it is after 5pm, you'll be greeted with a line out the door! Â Sure, the indoor area is a little small.. but still, the line says a lot!

joe's shanghai is probably one of the better XLB places i've eaten at...although nanxiang in flushing is better (thinner dumpling skin and better flavor)... but you cannot beat joe's for the price...my dining partner and i had one order of the pork XLB yelp.com/biz_photos/0CjKâ€¦ yelp.com/user_local_photâ€¦, one order of pork/crab XLB yelp.com/user_local_photâ€¦, scallion pancakes, and the shanghai noodles with shrimp yelp.com/biz_photos/0CjKâ€¦... the XLBs were very juicy, the scallion pancake was crispy with a fair amounts of scallions yelp.com/user_local_photâ€¦, and the noodles were packed with shrimp...*drool* i think i need a large bore IV started so i can get a XLB broth infusion... NB: Â make sure you go inside and grab a number and not waste any time waiting outside...
I love this place and the food but the experience with the service is poor. The last two times that I went there I had two different waitress and both were not too good.

Recommendations for the Dan Dan Noodles, scallion pancakes and dumplings in chili oil were all on targets. Great taste and loved the heat. I love south Florida but our selection of awesome Chinese food is limited. Great lunch! Will definitely return on my next visit to NYC.

Yum! Get the frozen 50-dumpling pack for $9 and store it up. It makes a quick and scrumptious lunch/dinner. Prosperity dumpling is fantastic. There is always a line (the restaurant is truly a hole in the wall) but it moves fast and don't be intimidated by all the yelling that goes on.

Excellent seafood. Great prices. Expect to wait if you miss the first seating. It's worth the wait for sure, but there you're limited on where you can hang out. If Fish is busy, you can bet Blind Tiger across the street is too - but between the two, we found beverages to wait it out. The lobster specials were amazing. The oysters were big and excellent (Spinneys), but the clams had even better flavor. My only suggestion would be to work on the shucking process - a bit too much sand and shell bits - but otherwise lovely. We found that the staff worked really hard to take care of everyone, but the restaurant gets very busy and noisy so patience and a bit more wine goes a long way in insuring you'll have a great evening.

What a lovely, quaint, and delicious place for brunch! Left this cafe feeling full and very satisfied. The food wasn't too heavy or salty -- the tastes were so complementary and subtle yet lively, and just a joy to feast on. I ordered the salmon pot pie, and avocado toast to share with my friend. She ordered baked eggs. I also had a mocha. Everything was delicious. The salmon pot pie was so beautiful! I did not expect the plate to be like a work of art. By the way, the lighting at this restaurant (at least in the day) is amazing with the sun shining through the cafe's large windows so that foodies can take pretty photos. Haha. The salmon inside the pie was overall tender and flaky. There were also generous amounts of spinach, sitting at the inside-bottom of the pie. I usually prefer not to eat olives, but I tried the olives that were sprinkled on the top of the pie. They really provided a flavorful punch to each bite, and weren't overwhelming. I tried a bite of my friend's egg dish (which had cream and potatoes) -- and it was surprisingly not too heavy. Nice and light! The eggs were cooked perfectly with a bit of yoke running so that the tastes blended and it could be used as a dipping sauce for the bread they provide on the side. The avocado toast was nicely presented as well. Such a simple dish that you could make at home with quality ingredients, but nevertheless very tasty and addicting. There was a generous amount of avocado, and the crushed red chilli peppers and lemon juice were very complementary (and also generous). Get your taste buds going! I also enjoyed my mocha, which was legitimate mocha -- not just chocolate, sugar, and milk. It was a pleasant, perfect balance of bitterness and sweetness. Also so adorable that the cocoa is shaped into pawprints -- that made me quite happy. The drink also comes with a square piece of wrapped chocolate candy, which also had a paw print on it. I didn't expect a piece of chocolate as well so that was a nice surprise and at $3-$4 for a pretty small cup (although not too bad), I was glad there were those extra details. The service was decent, nothing out of the ordinary. A lot of the waiters look very much identical -- all quite tall with dark hair and light eyes and nautical-inspired, striped shirts. So it took some effort to remember who our waiter was -- but it didn't necessarily seem like we got assigned one waiter in particular. I had an awkward encounter about the restroom since...silly me could not get the toilet to flush. A few people waited outside. I had to break what appeared to be a laugh-out-loud conversation between two waiters. One of them was polite enough, saying that he would check. He came back out seconds later, saying that the toliet works and asking if I had "tried flushing." I indeed did, but that was that. I must have flushed in the wrong direction. Anyhow, the matter got settled so that was that. Hah. A lot of the visitors seemed to be tourists and travelers living in the Jane Hotel. Overall, it's a bit out of my way to get to, but I would love to come back. Chill ambience and delicious, quality food.

We have been here twice and absolutely love this place. Â They've expanded the seating which really makes a big difference. Â The service is good and the food is more than worth it. Â The wiener schnitzel is so worth it and can even be split between two people. Â Don't miss out on some amazing authentic Austrian food. Â The cocktails are great too.

It makes me sad to write this review but there was no opportunity to get our point across at Farm yesterday so I'm left with no choice. Farm on Adderley has always been a favorite in my family-both for food and service. Â However yesterday's (Mother's Day) experience was unbelievable shocking. Â We arrived (three adults, one two year old) for brunch right when they opened. Â The restaurant filled quickly and clearly they were not at all prepared. Â We ordered two egg dishes, a burger and a side of scrambled eggs and toast-didn't seem complicated. Â The food took over ONE HOUR to come-that is no exaggeration. Â The waitress didn't even try to offer anything (bread, some fruit for our child, water...) and just kept blaming the kitchen. Â Apparently "the burger takes longer." Â We have a $50 grill at home and you can cook a burger in 15 minutes. Â We were not the only extremely dissatisfied customers (some bordered irate and left, went to CT Muffin, got coffee and muffins and came back and their food STILL was not out). Â I've been a waitress-stuff happens in the kitchen you can't control but how about saying "let me Â warn you our burgers take a long time" when someone orders it. Â Or at least make sure you keep their water glass full! Â FYI-the food came out lukewarm at best, the eggs were runny and my husband's burger was sub-par at best, not even served Â on the english muffin that was advertised! Â Argh! Â Luckily it was a very happy mother's day despite the lousy food and service!
getting a burrito from here after a heavy night of drinking prevented a next day hangover. this place is a miracle worker. it should be studied by scientists to discover its magical properties.

A lovely place! Â I had lunch here and all of us in my party agreed that we would be back! We each ordered something different and everything was superb. Loved the space, the waiter was sweet, warm, and professional. This is my new favorite place.

i stopped in alone one morning recently and had a good experience. the place is super cute and filled with nice light. it was pretty quiet inside and had a good vibe. i ordered the corned beef hash with poached eggs, which was not quite what i expected, but even better. the hash was juicy cubes of beef cured perfectly -not the typical kind of greasy friend hash most places serve up. the eggs were cooked just right...overall the dish was a home run. i would definitely go back.

I went here for dinner on Saturday night. A friend recommended it, I called at 5pm for a reservation for 4, and was able to get an 8pm seating for that same night. Sweet. Four things stood out: - 3 tasty microbrews on tap. I had two of them, the IPA and toasted lager. - Ricotta gnocchi appetizer. Rich creamy sauce, and perfect texture - not mushy at all. - Grilled pork chop. Juicy, seasoned, and served with a great smoked chili sauce (don't worry, it's not spicy). - Bacon mac'n'cheese (side dish that came with the pork chop). Great service and great music selection too (we heard some Michael Jackson, White Stripes, Led Zeppelin).

Kyclades is an authentic Greek restaurants, with great Greek food, run by Greeks. That said: it gets busy, it's loud, and it's run the Greek way so be patient. Food wise it's as fresh as it gets and as tasty as it gets! (really cheap too!)

One of my Top 10 fav places in NYC. I recommend this for groups too. Just call ahead to reserve the front sofa area. We always come back. Why? Best Lychee Martini's ever and only $5 (2 for the price of 1) until 10pm weeknights. This place does not dissapoint. It's our starting point before we move on to the partying/dancing in the area. I have also had the food back when they had 2 for 1 apps. Good food too, easy asian-fusion: spring rolls, wings, calamari... If you are looking for a low-key, easy going, no frills, cheap happy hour - this is your place. 5 stars for $5 Martini's. Note: be carefull what you wish for. after 2 rounds, you may find yourself a little happy, if you go for the next few rounds, be prepared to call out sick the next morning. They are potent. Disguisingly so.

The dumplings are always great and even if there is a line, it moves fast. I am not sure why the price raise though, so I have started going to other local dumpling places instead. It's still cheap here though.

Some of these reviews about not getting seats are annoying, you need to claim a seat then have one person go up and order for you. The place is busy because it's good so deal with it, it's not a fine dining establishment where a hostess is going to kiss your a** and push your seats in for you, come on, get real. It's a self serve delicious BBQ restaurant. Anyway, I loved it. I had been "fiending" for some true BBQ and Mighty Quinn's hit the spot. I had the brisket, my girlfriend had the ribs and we had the pickles and cole slaw all of which was great. My favorite part beyond the slow cooked meats was the beans, so much flavor. I will be going back and like I said if you see open seats grab them, have your friend/lover/husband/cousin go and place the orders. The line moves quick so do it right!

Great ambiance. Delicious, savory, interesting (you must try the dates stuffed with almonds wrapped in bacon. Scrumptious!) menu. The wait staff was a little wacky, but if you want really delicious Mediterranean cuisine, Olea is the place to go.
AWESOME !!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!! Get the square, get the antipasto salad 0 good to go

Sicilian Slice and Spumoni with or without chocolate (only in the paper cup) --- THE BEST. Â Wasn't crazy about the pasta dishes, but this place is just a restaurant I will always look forward to visiting.

Really excellent brunch. Â Started out w/ the salmon rillette [like a salmon spread served in a cute little mason jar] with everything-bagel-chips. Â My cousin got strawberry rhubarb pancakes with pistachio butter and some warm honey cream served on top - totally delicious. Â I was really tempted by the biscuits & gravy, beef hash, and their burger, all of which sounded great. And there was no wait at 1pm on a Sunday! Â Definitely going to come back here to try dinner.

Great brunch spot. Eggs Benedict was delicious and all brunch entrees come with a cocktail (mimosa or Bloody Mary) included for a very reasonable price (around $20). The Bloody Mary was pretty spicey so not for the mild palate. Good service, clean, modern and nicely decorated. Gets very busy for brunch so definitely make a reservation or expect a 45 minute or longer wait.

Hi I recently went to eat at this place and honestly have loved the burgers. What Â I didn't Â like was that I had ordered a burger well done and then the waitress brings my burger raw that i seriously saw blood coming out of it when I took my first bite. The waitress was also not very attentive as the other waiters. I honestly would give it a better rating but it was just not one of my best experience.
Roasted corn and a black bean sandwich after a late night out. Â Hells Yeah! Â I have to stop at Cafe Habana when I'm in NYC. Â Try it! Â Now.

This place is awesome food. I have been eating here for years. The Chicken with Rice is amazingly delicious. The white sauce and the red sauce certainly are the secret recipe add that makes this place incredible experience. Every time I go to eat there is always a line of people waiting which is a great sign that food is still served with quality. Great place to eat.

While walking into the establishment I see a butcher table the middle and an extensive aisle of beer - I knew then that they mean business. Sat at the bar with a friend while watching Kill Bill Vol 1 and 2 ... We decided to split the Lamb Belly. The Lamb Belly was the fattiest thing ever .. we didn't finish it, but it was delicious. A very laid back place with friendly service. The restroom has very cute decor and it was super clean. Meat and beer lovers should try this place out.

OK, so I know this place doesn't need any more reviews, but i LOVED my lunch experience here a few weeks ago and had to yelp about it. I'm typically not a fancy person, but a coworker invited me to join her quarterly lunch bunch and I said TOTALLY. Apparently if people in your party don't show, you get penalized $50! this place is serious. Make sure everyone shows up. I thought this was going to be a 4 course prix fixe, but it was more like 5 or 6! with the amuse bouche, specific breads per course, and dessert tray, I was stuffed to the brim. But not in a gross way. Everything was so delicious and artfully prepared. It was like each of us had our own waiter. I definitely felt fancy. final note: Chocolate Frivolous - definitely not to be misse! OMG, this was 6 different chocolate desserts on one plate - some cold some hot, all super delicious. I want to eat here everyday.

Bone marrow revelation... Been to this place a couple of times and I've never left disappointed. Â The raw bar is a great place to stop by right after work to grab a couple pints of beer and down a couple tasty oysters. Â  For starters I love the bread that they serve. Â It's like a peasant loaf with just the right amount of crusty outside and soft chewy inside. Â Plus, it doesn't hurt your mouth when you eat it. Â  The main reason I had to post up a review was to simply evangelize the masses on the goodness of their beef bone marrow appetizer. Â I just had it last night and have not been able to stop thinking about it ever since. Â For that alone I'm giving this place 5 stars. Â It's beefy, fatty, melt in your mouth goodness is only made better with the accompanying sea salt and marmalade. Â When you scoop it out from the bone it just about falls apart onto the toast provided. Â After finishing it I was giddy and felt almost guilty about eating something that decadent. Â I'm sure my heart could have done without the excess fat, but definitely a must try if you only go to this place once.

Ok, here's what I think: Â The last time I was in Manhattan, took the train to Brooklyn twice to eat at Grimaldi's. Â It's that good. Â Maybe at the times that I went, there were no lines, or hardly a wait, and the pizza was phenomenal. Â Keep it simple: Â plain cheese; pepperoni with mushrooms; sausage, peppers and onions.
