I usually prefer crispy fries, but these were a bit too much, bordering on too dry because they were in the fryer way too long. The sauce was decent. although I wish I could've tasted a bit more of the garlic. Would go back and try more sauces, and hopefully less overcooked fries.

Feel free to add a star or two if you enjoy misanthropy; the scowling here would certainly impress the "authentic" crew over on Chowhound. I got the Cantonese style lo mein with roast duck and roast pork, C32. I was expected the noodles to play a passive starch role but they were good on their own. The duck was great; the pork was pretty good but some pieces were too swine-ish. The two hot sauces on the table weren't meant for C32 but were quite impressive - one was orange and the other was heavier and darker. The service was unacceptably gruff. I don't expect "welcome" or "would you like to hear our specials?" but some variant of hello would be cool. The ordering and serving of the food was fast, but getting the check wasn't.
mamoun's falafel is to falafel in san francisco what sex with a real woman is to sex with a real doll(tm).

Why of course I had to check out this place when I'm in NYC. After all, 6000ish review... We ordered: - Hirata Chicken Wings = crispy with glazed pepper sauce. Typical. - Hirata Buns = I'm all about pork buns. Yummio! Get it. - Akamaru Modern = well-balanced broth, too bad I'm not fond of the thin noodles. - Shiromaru Hakata Classic = simple classic bowl of ramen. Delicious broth that is not overly salty. Great ambiance, great service, and great comfort food. I hope you give this place a try. Cheers!
great comfort food - the place is adorable and in a cool location

I've been there a twice. Ate at the pesce restaurant by myself. Very good, but small portions for the price. Smaller than much better, similar restaurants such as Le Bernardin. Ate at the pasta restaurant last night with my significant other, an Italian and native New Yorker. We went to the King Tut exhibit and dropped in at around 9:30 for dinner. I wanted to pick up a few things, and while we waited for our food I grabbed a few items and took them to the check-out and rushed back to my table. Didn't realize until we got home that I was overcharged. I bought a 4-pack of Italian soda, and was charged for 2 when I only purchased one. Considering that overcharging seems to happen frequently here, according to some other reviews here and elsewhere, I can't help but wonder if there isn't some employee scamming going on. I tried to buy some fresh pasta, but the woman behind the pasta counter was too busy putting up the pasta 45 minutes before closing, and flirting some guy on the other side of the counter. "I can tell you're a very real person," he was telling her as I desperately tried to get her attention and was summarily ignored as she batted her eyelashes back at him. So, I gave up and moved on. We left after dinner and about 20 minutes before closing. On the way out the door, some employees were lingering near the door. One said to the other, "I can't wait to get the f*ck out of here!" very loudly as I walked passed him. Nice way to send a customer on her way. We spent over $200 there (would have gotten more from me if the employees didn't decide to stop waiting on customers during business hours), with dinner and the items I purchased. Between being overcharged and the less-than-pleasant attitude of the staff, I think I'll take my business to one of the hundreds of other Italian restaurants and specialty food stores in NYC from now on -- ones that don't overcharge me, ignore me, and then send me on my way with obscenities.

Hip place on 9th. Fast, efficient service. The green papaya salad was fine, more than fine but not exceptional. However, it's the Pad Chili with chicken that was one of the single most textured and layered Thai dishes I've had. I prefer brown rice but either would do. Warning: it's spicy. Don't be a baby.

Food is tasty, but this place is overrated. Long lines and the doorman comes off wayyyy to strong. He keeps asking everyone, "what are you bringing to the picnic?" It's completely hypothetical and for his personal amusement that's not entertaining nor funny. The same guy also is "also offering free jokes, spicy or mild?" (Rated R and PG-13 respectively). Really? Jokes are ok, but should you really be saying such things to a compete stranger you just met? I suppose if you've already had a few drinks, you could maybe enjoy the atmosphere, but in the light of day with a clear head it's just odd and uncomfortable. Are we at a comedy club or a restaurant? The music is way too LOUD, you have to shout to be heard. Please turn it down! I can't imagine working here. Warning: there's a table right near the front entrance and 1 very specific seat underneath a vent that drips water! It's generally a shared table, but DON'T take this seat! Why should you pay to have possibly dirty water dripping on you while you eat? Asked to be moved, it's perfectly ok! Overall, tasty food, ok portions, uncomfortable seating, really loud music, and long lines, ok service, and weird doorman/bouncer. Worth the wait? You decide. Personally, there are plenty of other places with much more comfortable seating, yummier food, shorter lines and reasonable music that I'd much rather patronize. Worth noting CASH only! What year is this? The 1800s?
went here again recently, and again...AMAZING...just wanted to share! love you barbuto

I was lucky enough to get a table on an early saturday dinner at Char No.4. Everytime i walk by, it's packed. So i'm curious to see what this place is all about. The food is yummy, to read more about it, see beeneatingaround.blogspoâ€¦

What a great find! Very fancy style of pub food and I just love it. The second I entered this place and saw and smelled all the food I loved it right away. Their house rolls are just amazing I literally couldn't put it down. We ordered the peanut brittle with bacon which everyone raved about and they were good but nothing out of the ordinary. Second we got the pretzels with cheese to share which were perfect if I had ( drank) beer. Our final appetizer was the big eye cesar salad which was delicious and came with a yummy fried bread with egg! For my entree I obviously had the fried chicken which was outstanding and the salad it came with was even better WOW what a great dish! I will definitely be back when I'm in the mood to pig out!
Excellent quality at an excellent price. The place is cute. The only drawback is that the menu is slightly limited as the name suggests.

The pizza was decent but nothing special, especially not worth the 40 minute wait on line and another 40 minutes waiting for the pizza after placing the order. I would've given it a 4 star rating if it doesn't for the lack of service. Â If the service was better and the food came out quicker I would definitely change my rating to a 4 star.

We were a party of three for my daughter's 25th birthday. As it happens, we got the only table which affords the opportunity for private conversation, other than the two or three booths toward the back. It was nice to have the ability to talk by ourselves. Now the food. Â It was wonderful! We all had the Sunday Supper, an incredible bargain of three courses for $24. On thus Sunday it was a lovely refreshing salad with shaved root vegetables, a lovely cutlet of breaded, crispy pork, and a yummy pumpkin bread pudding. Everything was delicious. Don't miss the chicken liver mousse, it is to die for. Also, get the pork sticky buns, another don't-miss. Unusual and delicious. I had the celery tonic cocktail, Â which I found refreshing and inventive. Definitely going back, I am thinking about brunch...

I live half a block from this place. It's fantastic. Every time I walk by, whether on my way to catch the bus or walking the dog, I always peek in the windows to get a glimpse of what people are eating and drinking. Heavenly smells are always wafting out the doors. Yum. I've been here for everything they have to offer: lazy Saturday brunch, dinner date, or just a glass of wine at the end of a crazy day. The prices are perfectly reasonable for both drinks and food, the ambience complements the menu, the music is always great, and the servers are sweet and attentive. The last time I had brunch here I had the Warm Bankie and a Bloody Mary... Yum. I've had a solid variety of things from their dinner menu and nothing has ever disappointed me. I'm a particular fan of the potato pancetta pizza and that ever-awesome Baby Jesus Cake! A half-carafe of pretty much any wine they offer is the perfect addition for a meal for two. The first everyone I ever came here, one of the owners happened to be behind the bar. I sat down on a stool and ordered a glass of wine, content with my intention to delve into my book for a while... only to find myself engrossed in conversation with said owner and couple of other patrons at the bar for almost two hours. It's that kind of place. Yay Astoria!

One word can only describe this place. FANTASTIC!! Â Had the meatball sandwich with pesto and mozzarella and arugula on a brioche bun. The side salad it came with was a nice compliment. Cocktail of choice Moscow Mule served in a copper mug.

I had heard such positive things about Eataly that I was set up for disappointment. Â What I found was a hodgepodge of "Italian" food purveyors. Â None of the food purveyors was particularly special or interesting. Â The shopping experience a crowded, disorganized, frustrating shopping experience. Â There were some excellent individual Â stations, but it was less than the sum of its parts. One could get most of the Italian items at Whole Foods with a fraction of the pretense and effort.

I am IN LOVE with this place! I can't believe I lived right around the corner from it for so long and it took me until this week to discover. Since I did, I've been here 3 times! It's this super cute Japanese coffee shop (fits around 12) with amaaazing coffee and a few really yummy food items - serving breakfast, lunch and dinner. From the moment you walk in, the entire experience is very different... I've never seen coffee being brewed the way it is in Hi-Collar. The menu lists 3 different brewing methods (I recommend the Siphon) and a selection of coffee beans with different blends and strengths. I love the fact that you are able to see the entire process.... To top it off, they have a great friendly staff and extremely decent prices! Definitely my new coffee spot.

On the good side: - It used to be nice once - The wolves that raised the wait staff did a great job On the bad side: - The food is absolutely vile. Avoid the chicken caeser salad, the tomato soup and the tuna burger - You may be condescended to, feel ill-served by and have an existential crisis as you wonder whether your purpose there is actually to please the waiters, and not the other way around - If the food makes you retch, be a man about it and don't complain. They will not apologize for it or take it off your bill. But, you may get a moderately amusing sarcastic comment about what you just tried to do
Their bean salad, tomato soup and avocado chicken panini is delicious..

Absolutely amazing food and service! I have gone here twice and plan to go back again soon. Their brunch menu is to die for...I recommend the avocado bread to start, followed by the frittata. For dinner, I would recommend the mushroom consomme, and everything off the pasta menu. They grow their own produce right outside the restaurant on their balcony so everything is fresh. Day or night, the ambiance is an added plus.

After all these years, baby, you're still The One. It had been several years since my last visit to Blue Ribbon -- NYC was a different world back then. But recently I came here for a late night snack after a concert downtown. It's amazing how busy this place gets in the wee hours of the morning -- not surprisingly it's a well-known hangout for the city's restaurant staff and food royalty. Our meal consisted of oysters on the half shell (from Nova Scotia and Northern Cal), served with lemons and three different types of sauce, including vinegar. Simply perfection. We're talking orgasms in the mouth. I wanted the Matzoh Ball Soup but was afraid I wouldn't be able to fit the main course -- fried chicken -- into my stomach if I did imbibe. Â  Knowing that my accomplice and I wanted to split the bird, our waiter offered to serve it on separate plates. A nice touch, especially considering I'm not a fan of splitting food off the same plate (Just a weird little thing about me that seems to annoy people.) You really can't go wrong with anything on the menu here. For my money, BR is still one of the best restaurants in the city. It's consistent, fresh and delicious, and it serves up a healthy dose of cosmopolitan cool. The rye whiskeys were also very nice. Next time I'm trying those matzoh balls.
like they said, only more so. Â especially the veggie pomegranate goats cheese thing Â and bbq beef taco was almost as good.

Where do I begin... I went to Pies 'n' Thighs because a friend recommended it (not sure if she'll be a friend after that experience)... We went on Tuesday, July 27th. Â When I walked in, I was disturbed by the decor. Â It looked like a late 70's early 80's garage sale gone wrong. Â Mix matched chairs and tables, which looked extremely dirty as opposed to vintage which I think is what they were going for. Â Anyway, since the food recommendation was good, I decided to give it a try anyway... BIG MISTAKE... The waitress who looked like she just rolled out of bed in her dingy tank top, dirty converse sneakers and head full of dripping sweat was a complete turn off. Â She was nice though. Â She gave us all glasses of water, but to my surprise, the cup was dirty because the water looked to have grease floating on top. Again, another sign that I should leave, but I didnt. Â I ordered the chicken box, which comes w/ 3 pieces of chicken, a biscuit and 1 side. HA! I asked for a breast, leg and wing. Â What I received, i'm not sure. Â The only piece that I was able to identify was a thigh (thus the name pies n thighs I guess). Â The chicken was disgusting... and luke warm @ best. I mean for a small establishment, such as this, you would think that you could get fresh out of the oil hot fried chicken. I could have gotten fresher, tastier fried chicken at the local halal chicken spot. Â Hell I could have gotten better fried chicken at the local chinese restaurant. Â The biscuit that I received was COLD, HARD and UNAPPEALING! The collard greens, were a scam, nothing southern about them, and there was hot sauce poured all over them, which I did not ask for. Â My friends Mac and cheese had hot sauce poured all over it as well, maybe they put the hot sauce on to mask the bad taste. Â Who knows. Â However, even with the bad food, there was one highlight.... THE LEMONADE!!! Yummy and refreshing. Â I was tempted to try the pies, to see if there would be a saving grace for this place, but they all looked super stale and definitely not appetizing. Â All in all, I spent $15 and went home hungry and with an aching belly. Â This place does not scream "southern cuisine" and if all you're looking for is some good fried chicken, take your $11 and go to Popeye's where you can get 10 pcs of hot, tasty fried chicken for $10.99.

I've only tried their Maine style lobster roll but I'm eager to try the Connecticut style roll and the Shrimp roll. Their lobster rolls are to die for! The buns are so moist and chewy. Lobster is fresh, cooked just right and simply delicious. I was devouring every bite. You get cape cod potato chips to compliment your roll. They also have Maine soda's and root beer. This place is in the middle of nowhere but it's well worth the drive or walk. Pricey but will definitely go again.

It's mostly busy during brunch/breakfast time. Mostly, if you don't have a reservation, you probably would have to wait a bit. Most of the food items are fairly decent to good, although I wouldn't go crazy over it with one exception. Those damn vanilla bean french toast. It's totally orgasmic. I keep going back for those damn french toast. fluffy, warm, sweet (but not overly) and the damn vanilla aroma. gahhhh!!! French Toast!!!!

Fort Defiance. Â  Â It is so nice to be able to get a GREAT cup of coffee in Red Hook. Â Not only do they have great coffee, but their sandwiches are oh so tasty. Â I have tried the muffaletta which is HUGE and the vietnamese sandwich, which is a nice variation on the classic with bigger badder veggies and rather than a smear of of pate' its like chunk oh pate'. Â  Â I have yet to try their cocktails, but am looking forward to a nice midsummer refreshment very very soon.

I love this place. This is sort of a special spot for my girlfriend and I. The cheese Lasagna is absolutely amazing. I have had good lasagna in my day, but la lanterna di Vittorio makes the absolute BEST lasagna, period. If you told me there was better, I wouldn't believe you, outright lies! The atmosphere is classy yet informal, the ambiance is warm and inviting. The wait staff has been friendly, punctual and competent each time I've visited. Vittorio himself is a gentleman. I would recommend La Lanterna di Vittorio to anyone but my worst of enemies. If some one is too snobby to appreciate this hidden gem, then it is probably for the best, as you should keep better company. This is not an upscale restaurant but it is a classy bistro. As for dates, my girlfriend Â still asks to go back there after three years, so it can't be bad. This is definitely our kind of place. The dim lighting gives a warm and comfortable atmosphere which perfectly accentuates the delicious food. It is absolutely refreshing to enjoy such quality without the pretentiousness that so often accompanies excellence.

OK with the bazillion reviews here, everyone agrees that Ippudo has really good Ramen. However, I do not think it is worth the 1 hr and 45 mins wait for dinner. Either come for lunch, or grab a snack and eat a late dinner. My friends and I gave up the first time and came back around 10pm the next night and there was still a half an hour wait, but thats Nothing! We hung out at the bar and had a very delicious lychee martini. The place is really loud and fun. When you walk into the dining room with the hostess, she makes a small announcement and all the cooks, waiter screams some greeting at you. I couldn't help but smile. Also, if you're with a small party, you sit at these communal tables with other people. They have really good ramen and the soup is amazing. I do not think the pork buns everyone talk about it that great. The bun itself is soft. But it is kind-of bland. Also, I do not like that all ramen is served with pork.

Tried their appetiter. It's delicious. I had the pork belly(3 pieces of steamed pork belly, some cut asparagus, with shredded green onions), and a shrimp soup. My colleagues had skew(mediocre) and rolls(which looked very fresh). Price is reasonable considering it's in Midtown. Food quality definitely is impressive.

Totally old-skool fancy... the place is bathed in this red-orange light that burnishes the hard edges... so, if nothing else, everyone and everything looks very pretty. Macdougal Street is one of my favorite parts of the city, I was in the mood to experience a New York restaurant as one would have in the 40s or 50s. This place definitely fit that bill (in a good way). The Black Label burger was perhaps the smallest $26 burger I've ever had in my life, but it was excellent. I can't say that it was the most amazing burger on the face of the earth, but it was very, very good and worth the price. I should have also gotten the asparagus salad special -- it looked very good -- but instead I had 25 percent of my fries and left the place feeling full.
Good service, tasty tapas, and great wine... Tia Pole is still my favorite tapas bar but this place is up there. Restaurant is tiny so groups wouldn't work.
Just didn't think it was very good. Been there twice. Service wasn't professional and the food terrible especially the fries. What is that?

The food was excellent. Worth a trip to Staten Island. The front-of-house staff seems to have no idea how to run a restaurant, though. I sat for half an hour before my drink order was taken, and the host asked for my name on the reservation after I was already seated. Even more rigamarole than I usually have to put up with to dine out in New York.

My husband and I came here on a Saturday night looking for a good neighborhood spot. We've had quite a few disappointing and completely mediocre dining experiences in LIC, but Open Door was NOT one of them! It was definitely a laid back environment, but our server was prompt and attentive. The beer selection was great and we enjoyed everything we ordered. The honey butter is AMAZING - our only problem was the too small amount of bread they give you. We ordered a bunch of small plates - the dip trio (homemade eggplant chips are the best!), croquettes, fried chicken bites, tartare trio, and the steak entree. To top it off, I got the pumpkin pie...I don't even like pumpkin and this was delicious! My husband ate the carrot cake whoopie pie and barely shared, so I know he loved it. :) All in all, a really good dining experience - we will be coming back soon!

It's pretty good, but also think it's a bit over-hyped. Sorry! The ice coffee is excellent, we tried the pepperoni pizza and the egg sandwich. the pizza was amazing...the egg sandwich was okay. we also tried a pecan roll, which we didn't like. also, to be quite fair, it's pricey and there's no where to sit. so either the food better be outstanding, melting my face because it's so good or get some tables. it was okay, but my husband and i prefer bergen bagels.

First of all...how many waiters do you have to flag down before you can get waters for the table. Read: four. Second, I haven't gotten the food yet but the aforementioned incident angered me enough to write an inflammatory review on yelp. Hey guys quick update, food was great - rating up to two stars. Still no water. Also not a fan of their rose wine. Vinay out.
Phenomenal experience! Â Not only was the fish as fresh and rich as the best sushi joints in Manhattan, but the service was incredibly kind and thoughtful.
The food was delicious, I had the guyere, shitake and spinach risotto, a ceasar salad and breadsticks. Great flavor and the service was sweet! 99% Gluten free menu!

Favorite brunch place in the city. During the summer, lines can be expected at 12 noon on a Sunday, in the winter the waiting times are less acute. Â  The brunch fare is really tasty and filling, and a great deal. Ithink the omelettes are fantastic. particularly the salmon and the cheese/spinnach omelettes. I hear good things about the Eggs Benedict also. Coffee is delicious. Service is friendly, fast and efficient, but they seem to have a high turnover of staff. A beautiful, chic crowd with very little attitude. For New Jerseyans, it is about a 15-20 minute walk across from the 9th street PATH, which makes it quite acessible.

Have walked past this place for a number of years and never knew what I was evidently missing. Â Neighbor suggested we try their Sunday night mussel special. Â So we did and we were very glad we did. Â There are a variety of mussels to choose from and we sampled three...marinieres, provencal and marocain. Â All were very good, down to the last dip of bread in the juice. Â The accompanying frites were served hot and cooked just perfect. Â A neighboring table was served an order of the Belgium Style Spare Ribs and the tower of ribs gave me food envy. Â The way they devoured them indicates envy they deserved. Â Apparently they have a Saturday night special for the ribs so you know where I'll be on Saturday night soon. Â The range of reasonably priced salads and dishes we noticed being served elsewhere all looked plentiful and worthy of a try. Â The service was attentive and friendly. Â For those in the mood for fine Belgian fare and a wide selection of cold beer BXL will meet your expectations.

Okay...so it took me a while to try what i thought of as "that place where the pet food store used to be." Â I guess the idea kinda freaked me out. Â But once i tried it...why did i wait!??? The falafel is really good, but the babaganough is the true prize winner. If you have a buddy with you, splurge on the vegetarian platter, which is more than enough to share. Â You will get every single veggie salad they have (i really like the roast carrot one) as well as hummus, baba, falafel and some dolma. Â  Get gingerale to wash it down. Â If its afternoon, take your feast to mccarren park. Â If its late night...scarf it down in the brightly lit shop and peoplewatch the others who are getting their falafel or donner fix after a wee-hour L voyage.

Waited to write this review because every time I thought of this place, my mouth begins to water. My cousins and I had just finished eating brunch, got some cannellonis from Little Italy, got some boba and ice cream in Chinatown.......and then decided to come here to eat. Yeah I know, we're pigs. I just couldn't bear the thought of passing this place up to try! The waiters must have thought we were the cheapest Asians ever. We were a party of 6 but got 2 bowls of noodles: Â The Roast Duck Noodles and The BBQ Pork Noodles with Won Tons. We were so full from everything else and needed to leave room for dinner after this meal too.... Take a look and see the vibrant, thick cut, juicy meat in the bowls of noodles: Roast Duck Noodles: yelp.com/biz_photos/big-â€¦ They're definitely not stingy on the meat portions here. The roast duck was nice and salty. It tasted even better when the duck was soaking in their juicy broth! My favorite part of the duck is the thigh. OmFg that piece of meat was so tender. BBQ Pork Noodles with Won Tons: yelp.com/user_local_photâ€¦ BBQ Pork is one of my favorite things to eat because it is so sweet and pink in color. There was tons of meat in this little bowl to go around for all of us to have too! You could tell they make their own won tons as well. Extra brownie points! Some places I have been too, actually buy frozen ones and just feed them to you. I am sure these were frozen, but my point is they actually roll the won tons up themselves! The noodles in both bowls were average, but the meat and the broth were so tasty, it surpassed the need for better noodles. My cousin also told me that they have deals here occasionally for lobsters! 2 for $20? Awesome! I wish I had more days to come back and eat here because their rice dishes also looked salivating! I must mention, the food is REALLY cheap here. #authenticchinesefood #bomb #iloveNYC
Great food .. I order from them all the time .. love it !!

I don't really venture uptown as much so I was very surprised to find such a legit place like Jeffreys. One side of the bar focuses on craft beer and the othern side focuses on spirits and cocktails. Naturally, my palate has always landed me on the spirit side but it is still so convenient that I can meet up at this spot with both spirit and beer enthusiasts. The food is also ridiculously good for it's reasonable prices. Favorites are the burger, sigmund pretzel, devils on horseback, and the happy hour $1 oysters. The bartenders are all very friendly and knowledgable about their beers and cocktails and the environment is fun and hip without taking itself too seriously. Definitely one of my favorite last night spots!

I read a good review of this place in a local publication. In the mood for some comfort food, I came here last sunday eager to see what all the buzz was about and I left somewhat disappointed. The service was decent. Our food came rather quickly. I got the pulled pork box and sampled some of the fried chicken box. The mac n cheese was nothing to write home about. Maybe its because I think baked macaroni is the perfect companion to fried chicken and theirs was not too far removed from stouffer's frozen mac n cheese. The chicken was properly battered and fried but lacked in the flavor department. The pulled pork sandwich came on a soggy bun and was impossible to pick up and eat. The meat in the sandwich itself was bland and could never hold a candle to the roast pork shoulder that my family makes. The most redeeming part of the meal was the biscuit. I would definitely give this place another chance and check out their breakfast/brunch fare but I'm definitely not returning for dinner.
Love their garlic fries! Tiny dining area, but worth the wait!

Great for a lunch date! Great ambiance! Â If I had to describe this place, it will be as if Latin food and Soul Food had a baby this would be it. We tried the following because we JUST had to try A LOT: Paella Marinera Valencia?: liked the paella, BUT sad to say I've had better, this one almost tastes like jambalaya =/ Pollo al Ajillo: the chicken was dry, but on the bright side the dish tastes really healthy! Pollo Jamaiquina: this was probably the best of the 3! Â It was moist and dripping with jerk bbq sauce! The place deserves four stars because our waiter was so attentive and sweet and the bus boys kept filling our drinks up before it ever went down an inch! Â It was amusing to see the mute, old couple next to us stare at us and listen to our conversation, because HEY when you're old I guess you have nothing else to talk to each other about??

What a great hole in the wall! Had my usual diner breakfast, 2 eggs scrambled, bacon, home fries and toast. All done to perfection. Decaf coffee washed it all down. Place is clean and service is fast, prices reasonable ($5.50 for a full belly) and the menu is deep for anyone wanting more than just eggs. It's small like everyone else has said but I don't see how making it bigger would make it better. My new home base when I'm in the city early.

I have only lived in New York for a short while, and I have made it a point to explore the culinary side of the city. Â That being said, I always manage to find my way back to Sergimmo. Â Even though it is not that convenient for me to get to, I still take the time out of my day at least once a week to go enjoy what I can only describe as the greatest italian sandwich in the city (and possibly, the world). Â It isn't just one sandwich either... I have tried 20 of the 25 or so sandwiches on the menu plus at least 5 of the daily specials. Â Every single one is mind blowing. Â The bread is always fresh, as it is brought in out of necessity rather than bought in bulk, the meat is always succulent, and the mozzarella... oh man the mozzarella... The mozz is made fresh... every 2 hours or so. Â If you are lucky, you will show up just when a batch is getting finished up. Â If you are really lucky, you will get a sample straight out of the bowl with the mozz still warm and milky. Â But who am I kidding... with the cheese made so often there isn't ever really a time where it isn't still warm and milky. Every sandwich comes with olive oil and a balsamic glaze that accentuates the flavors of the italian cured meats and mozzarella, creating a harmony of deliciousness in every bite. Â The menu is essentially a giant suggestion, as you can make a sandwich with anything you please. Â Arugula and hot/sweet peppers are a personal favorite, as well as artichoke hearts or sun-dreid tomatoes, but really you can't go wrong with any combination. Â However, if you happen to show up on a day where the special is a Roast Pork panini (I think it is usually on Wednesdays), forgo the menu and just go with that. Â I have had plenty of philly-style roast pork sandwiches in my day, in and out of Philadelphia, but this one tops them all. Â Crunchy, yet not too bitter, broccoli rabe and sharp provolone sitting on top of succulent roast pork... Alright, gotta stop before I work myself into a frenzy. Traditional Italian pastas are available, from homemade lasagna to pasta with pesto or a la vodka, making it a nice place for dinner as well. Â I usually don't do desserts, but the cannoli is absolutely divine. Â The homemade ricotta filling is perfectly sweet and creamy and it leaves nothing to be desired. Everything is available by the pound, making it not only a great sandwich shop but also a great deli. Â There is a fantastic antipasto selection including, a personal favorite, octopus and calamari salad marinating in olive oil and lemon. Â  Any time I have friends or family in from out of town, this is my first stop. Â Any time they return, with or without me, Sergimmos becomes their first stop as well. Â Hearty portions and a familial atmosphere define what seems is becoming less the best kept secret in Hell's Kitchen and more notoriously the best sandwich shop in Manhattan. If you are in the area, by which I obviously mean the Tri-State area, a visit to Sergimmo is a must!

Was very excited to get a really nice looking 24 hour place right next to where I live! However, the service IS slow, as others have commented on. The food is okay. I think they try and cut corners a little too much. Â Example- no cream only skim milk with coffee or cheap bun with the eggs benedict with brunch. The muffins they bring out with brunch are sub par. I will say that the decor and the place looks great. Really tasteful looking restaurant and gorgeous marble countertops.

I used to come here for the coffee, desserts and free Wi-Fi--all of which are solid offerings--but now I know the brunch is great. I will definitely be spending more weekend mornings in Manhattan. I had the salmon brunch special (don't remember the exact name), which was salmon and eggs over and english muffin. The special was more than filling and came with potatoes, OJ and a choice of coffee or cappuccino, all for $11. My friend had eggs with their fried dough, which was really good too. Wait time isn't long.

Most amazing bar ever. Craig is so hot. The best bartender. They should wear the black tight shirts that they used to wear. Craig is probably the most amazing person ever. And he makes the best drinks.

After a good night of drinking in the city, I always find myself standing on line for a combo platter. For $6, it is totally worth the wait and stands up to the hype. I was never into lamb meat but after trying it from this place, I was instantly hooked! The combo platter constant of chicken, lamb mixed, pita bread and a little bit of lettuce. To enrich the flavor, you MUST smother your platter with their white sauce!! *drooooling* The more the better! If you want a spicy kick to it, they do have hot sauce but be warned that their hot sauce is outrageously HOTTTTT so do give it a small taste before you pour it all over your food.
Drinks are great, homemade potato chips are delicious, but the pasta is bland and tasteless. It's pretty hard to screw up pasta with cream sauce and bacon, but they somehow managed.

ohhhhh i am so disappointed that I am only giving this place 2 stars...i had such high hopes! The food was average at best. I ordered the suckling pork sandwich arrangement which cam overflowing with crisps and salad. The million different grated apple varieties were nice..but just OK. Probably the best thing about the place was it interesting clientele (i was seated next to some famous artist that the waiter was gushing over and on the other side some gorgeous looking interior designer that the Times is about to profile..i wasn't eavesdropping really, its just the tables are so close together it is hard not to hear!)

I am very picky about my pizza. Â The crust has to be crispy and paper thin. Â The cheese better be fresh mozarella, NOT the stringy polly-o stuff. Â Anything less goes in the garbage. This place surpassed expectations. Â The ingredients were fresh, delicately chopped. Â The pizza is exactly the way I like it, the crust is one of the thinnest and crispiest I have tried in this town. The ambiance was really nice, a casual, local pub feel. Â The worn leather booths with slate or wooden tables, embossed tin ceilings, classic look to the bar. Â  Beer and wine available, and some comfort-food classic desserts like apple pie, cheesecake and chocolate chip cookie.

Even though Balthazar is a Parisian-style bistro, the restaurant itself is practically an NYC institution. It's huge, rustic and seemingly very popular with the young and the beautiful, the well-heeled and the well-traveled (read: tourists). There are daily specials but I'm preferential to the Balthazar bar steak, which is essentially steak-frites served with a bearnaise. Ordered medium-rare, it comes out nearly perfect with a slight char on the exterior. The french fries are pretty standard, which is to say, great. My friend ordered the duck confit, which came out crispy and well seasoned, although a little dry. His escargots were better in my opinion, simple and served in a very garlicky butter. A cote du rhone suggested by our waiter paired nicely with the meal and was reasonably priced at just over $30. Ultimately the food and the experience at Balthazar is everything that it should be in a bistro/brasserie: solid and reliable. The caveat is that nearly everything is also a little pricier than it probably should be. The service, however, is impeccable, which is made more impressive by the cramped, packed-in layout of the dining area that ensures everyone gets jostled at least a dozen times during their meal. The wine list is a sizeable selection from France (of course) with an emphasis on Bordeaux.

After thorough research, I decided to come here to try the ramen. It was past ten and the wait was still 40 minutes (on a monday night). Well it's worth the wait, tables are communal so better be friendly. Â I wanted to get extra noodles but realized that it's too much. But if I wasnt that then i'll definitely get more!

I really wanted to love this. Pork, Asians, East Village...what's not to like? But it was just okay. And at $100 for two, you really want it to be more than okay. We ordered a glass of wine for each of us, oysters with kimchi, the brussel sprouts, pork buns, and the sausage with rice cake. The oysters apparently don't come with actual kimchi....they come with a dollop of kimchi foam. Yes, I said kimchi foam. I have no idea what it is. It just tasted like sriracha-esque chili sauce. Pretty standard. The pork buns were good quality but bland. These aren't like the cha siu bao you get at dim sum. It's more like what you get with peking duck - rice flour bun with yum pieces of meat, sauce, scallions, and cucumber. The only thing missing was the crispy piece of fatty skin...tho this was definitely fatty enough. I liked the brussel sprouts, but my friend wasn't thrilled with how burned they were. The ground sausage with rice cake was tasty, especially the crispy parts of the rice cake. But it looked and tasted like something an average cook familiar with Korean ingredients could've made at home. It definitely wasn't as spectacular as I was hoping an entree from Ssam would be. We both agreed that neither of us would probably come back. [sad face]
Love Bogota. The staff are lovely and always make us feel very welcome which just adds to the fantastic experience. The food is absolutely excellent too. We keep on coming back.

I was in town for Business and my co-worker said this was a must visit for Dinner so i walked over to check it out. I chose the Seafood bar and sat at the 'chefs table' since the Chef was standing in front of my area. He was very helpful w/ the menu suggestions and helped pick out a great meal. I had the shrimp salad which was great and then had the grilled Scallops which was excellent. The service and vibe was good, i recommend to check it out ! Bonus- upstairs there is a Beer/Restr on the roof which has a great view of the NYC skyline at night ;)

Came here with my friend Blake on a random night. We weren't looking for anything big, but sat down and saw the option for a 10 course tasting... and couldn't really help ourselves. We seemed to have the best seat in the house; right at the outside corner of the bar, where the pass is so we could see each dish being finished. I've gotta say that they take their food seriously here; the tiny open kitchen was packed tight with young chefs concentrating pretty damn hard on each dish and I would be hard pressed to find a staff that knew more about each item. I would definitely suggest putting yourself in their hands and just opting for a tasting. The portion sizes here lend themselves to being eaten en masse, cause they're small and I'm big. Food isn't anything that'll blow you away, I found most things to be pretty subtlety flavored but its nice being to see each dish prepared in such close quarters. This would be a great place for a long casual meal with friends or a date.

Milk & Roses. At first I didn't get the mix and thought that having "Milk" in the name is some kind of trend these days not even having a single drop of Milk in it. What? You didn't get it? Well.... Milk & Honey, momofuku Milk Bar, Buttermilk Bar, Milk Lounge and etc? Still didn't get it? Yelp it. Â Anyways, Peter D* loved Milk & Honey (the speakeasy bar) in his review while I wasn't so crazy about. So I told him that I would prefer actual Milk & Honey mix and also suggested that Milk and Apple Juice is a good alternative. He told me I was sick. I retaliated that, Milk & OJ was also good, introduced by Alton Brown on FoodNetwork... Â Ohhhhh, I am sorry. How did I drift so away from yelping Milk & Roses to babbling about my sick and obsessive love for Milk? It is unknown. Anyways, I was only trying to say that, in that sense Milk & Roses mix confused me at hello. But also want to say I like this place to the degree of putting that much thought in it. We were intended to go to Ashbox for a brunch on Sunday but it was closed... then I wanted to go to Acapulco diner a block away. Again it was closed. darn.. God, are you punishing me for not going to church on Sunday? Now, I've decided to go to Champion Cafe (1108 Manhattan Ave) BUT, I found Milk & Roses (1110 Manhattan Ave) instead. There is no sign for this place but I knew it was new. I wasn't sure if they serve meals. They just looked like a coffee and tea place. I love mysterious places but I was quite starving at the moment so wasn't sure if I was able to make it to Champion Cafe.... So we walked right to the counter. One girl and a guy gave us a full face to face attention having their elbows bent side by side on the counter. What a greeting. Cute as hell and nice as devil who lost his evil nature in dazed manner(?)...maybe misunderstood that they are supposed to be sweet. Wow I am sick. **shaking heads** They handed us the full menu and told us they even had a Lasagna daily special. The decor, thru and thru, and then went around a couple of blocks times I liked it. When you walk in the place, on your right there is a ceiling high book shelf filled with old books. The original painted tin ceiling and the exposed brick wall/wooden beams, marble french/italian cafe tables along the walls. Very rugged but hip. Then a grand piano at the end of the open space which hinted me a live music. Jazzy music in the background. This place is used to be a second-hand thrift store. Maybe that is where they acquire all of these old books from. Only three month old the guy said. Anyways, what a nice change! You did the right thing. You... nice guy. We had a regular coffee, an iced coffee, lasagna and two eggs with proscuitto and cheese($5). prices are very modest considering the ambiance. My cup of coffee was espresso latted, not diner American, in a Big cup! Â Really good. coffee priced $2-3. My two egg sandwich was served in a good panini and huge. My friend's home made Lasagna looked good and I was offered to try but by the time I raised my fork, it was all gone. It was that good. My friend said. I guess, rolling my eyes. Crowd wise, locals of course. laptop people, bookworms & grown up hipsters. The guy who served us - I think he is the owner - had a debatable accent. I said Australian but my friend says Italian. Well I guess Italian by the look of the place and the menu. Otherwise, I would see some crocodile Dundee things going on as the guy kind of carried that kind of casual air. He was really nice enough that he brought us a dollar back to our table saying we somehow overpaid him. Jesus... that was a good deed done on a Sunday. What a find. New and Hip, Opens on Sunday. almost dirt cheap. Nice people. And I also like the name Milk and Roses a lot which rhymes like Guns 'n Roses but much less violent so that God wouldn't hate me so much for going there on Sunday instead of church**. P.S. Since many asked... * I am not affiliated with Peter D foundation, corporation or any kind of Â  Peter D business, not bloody-related nor romantically involved. But Â  I have to admit that he is a such a great person to yelp with. ** Sadly(?) I don't go to church regularly. Though, God in my head Â  Â said that drinking Milk and smelling Roses are pretty much equal Â  Â to going church in this universe, as long as I believe in him/her.

Another home run, and our New Years Eve savior after a horrible experience at MP Taverna. The pimms lemonade cocktail is wildly refreshing and the burrata is like eating a piece of heaven. Love the staff -- super welcoming and caring. Local favorite for sure.

What a wonderful place for good American comfort food. Â Very seasonal menu and well executed. Â I went for the Sunday supper which is the perfect way to get a variety of dishes for $25. Â What a deal. I am giving 5 stars because this restaurant did everything I would expect for a great meal. Â They didn't try to hard or deconstuct a dish for the sake of deconstructing a dish. Â They just executed perfectly. Â We had pork shnitzel which came out piping hot on the inside and ultra crispy on the outside. Â It was seasoned perfectly and with the depth of flavor from the oil, you can tell it was fried stove top rather than a deep frier. Â The sides were braised cabbage which was a nice tart and crunchy compliment to the schnitzel. Â The other course was an herb spaetzle which added a wonderful taste of autumn. Â The chef used a wonderful blend of fall herbs which pulled the meal together. Â Everything was seasoned perfectly. Â The first course was a simple but well made fall greens and herb salad with beets and dessert was a warm apple cider cake. Â  Overall, the meal was well balanced and delivered on flavor, texture and temperature. Â The service was warm and attentive and the restaurant provided a good amount of room, so you dont have to be jammed together (as in most NYC restaurants). Â At the moment, I cannot think of anything I would have changed. It is a bit out of the way, but worth the trip. Â 5 stars.
Great breakfast! Â Gave 3 stars because I immediately saw a hair in my scrambled eggs when the plate was brought out.

This was fantastic, order a combo plate with extra white sauce and a cup of hot sauce. Â You can't go wrong with tasty "lamb" and chicken on top of the bright yellow rice! Â  We came here and picked up lunch after the Macy's parade and I'm finding myself still craving the creamy gravy tzaziki-like sauce and the spicy kick the red sauce gives!

Never had falafel? Try Taim and it will def set the bar. I prefer the green one, it's a bit spicier than the other flavors. I highly recommend their falafel sandwich. Great for lunch. Â Their platters are great for dinner, the mediterranean style sides are super healthy but doesn't taste so :)

I have had Shabu-shabu at home for years so when I was told that I am having dinner there, I wasn't that thrilled. Â Besides, I always thought it was just eh. Â Nothing special and nothing really tasty. Â  And nothing really has changed after having dinner there. Â It's just meat and veggie with two types of sauce (one tasted like mustard and the other seemed soy-based). Â But then again, I guess it's the same with sushi. Anyway, it was good but I just am not a big fan of it. Â Compared to other shabu shabu places I have been to (pho32 in ktown and one of mott st near hop kee), I have to say this probably was the best of all three. Â Then again, my sample size is laughable.

Go Fish!! Â Not the card game--the small sort of hole-in-the-wall restaurant on bleeker. Â Sort of a dime a dozen type place in coastal New England or the Jersey Shore-but a nice stop in the Village. The $8 special has been duly reviewed-i Mix half oyster and clams and enjoy the chard--not a PBR type guy. Â I have had about half the appetizers and have never been disappointed. Â I prefer the chowder to the gumbo. Â I felt the gumbo would have been better over a bit of rice or with some crawfish--though tasty--the chowder is better. I feel the entrees are a tiny pricy for the type of place--and I have gotten fish filets to go--(they have a small take-out/seafood market type place up front) and I thought the prices were a bit high. Â  Â Service is always spot on and the waits are never terrible. Notes--share the desserts. Â They are sort of unmemorable-but way too big for one-and only $6. Â  The blue crab special seems great-but only in the afternoon. Â Great spot to do tapas or just drop in for some apps.

My girlfriend and I went to eat at Carino the other night. We went based on all the rave reviews on Yelp and had high hopes for the place. I asked the waitress what was most popular on the menu and she recommended the fish tacos, which I ordered. My girlfriend ordered the pork enchiladas and we also got the tamale app and guacamole. The guacamole was pretty good but did not come with enough chips (you have to order chips al la carte for an additional three dollars.) But the guac turned out to be the best part of the meal. The tamale was dry and flavorless, not to mention cold. In fact everything that we were served was luke warm to cold. We ended up having to send the enchiladas back to be warmed up (which we never do, we both wait tables and try our best to be easy customers when we go out) They came back a few degrees warmer than they had first come but still not satisfyingly warm. Plus they were drenched in this weird orange sauce, ick. My fish tacos were also cold and generally flavorless, plus I only got two for a staggering 12 dollars or something insane. Beans and rice you have to order al la carte to help supplement the hunger that you will be feeling after eating such small and dull portions. I ordered a tequila and grapefruit cocktail which was not bad but did not take the edge off having to reach in to my wallet and shell out sixty bucks for an extremely unsatisfying meal. I would never recommend this place to anyone. You can get better mexican food from a truck.

We came here and loved the food. We had the fattoosh salad, the appetizer combo plate and the lamb kabob. Everything was wonderful and the service was quick and friendly. By the way, the enterier is roomy and very nicely decorated. They had arabic Â music on the whole time which we enjoyed. It was a mix of traditional and modern.

Rarely do you find delicious made-to-order food that comes out quick. Johnny's serves it up fresh and fast--not fast food fast, but fast. I give it a 5/5 for a few reasons: * Good atmosphere. When you step into this 13-seat railroad style hole in the wall it seems like nothing has changed in over a decade or two, and it's wonderful! * Menu selection is well rounded without being overwhelming. I suggest the Big Man Breakfast (it's similar to IHOP's or Denny's "2x2x2" option). * Staff is friendly and on point. Though you don't necessarily have one server, all the hands on deck are aware of what's going on. I'll be coming back and so will you!

What we ate: soup dumplings (both kinds), green onion cakes, mu shu pork, shanghai flat noodles, fried shimp. Yum! Â  I live in San Francisco and I'm used to being disappointed by Chinese food there, so the first time I ate at Joe's I wasn't expecting much. However, both times that I've eaten here I've been very happy. The dumplings were soft and delicious, but it was the green onion cakes that got me really excited. You wouldn't think they'd be so hard to make but a lot places screw them up. Joe's version was perfect. Everything else we ate was good and the prices were really cheap. Service: typical noisy, frenetic Chinese restaurant where the food gets pretty much thrown at you. An intimate, quiet dinner this is not.

I found a deal for this place on Amazon Local and figured that I'd give it a try. Â It gave me an excuse to venture out to another Queens neighborhood. Â  I was not sure what to expect, but it was a nice surprise when we walked through the door. Â This place has a really nice atmosphere. Â It was a bit busy, so we sat at the bar while they prepared a table for us. They have a great selection of Nepali and Tibetan food. Â We ordered the vegetable Momos, which were awesome. Â They were just the right amount of fried and tasted delicious. Â They came with a few sauces which they paired nicely with. We also got the Tsp Phing, which is noodle soup with vegetables and potatoes. Â This was also very delicious. Â I also got the Cheley with beef. Â I really wanted to get it with Yak, but they were out of it. Â This was pretty disappointing. Â However, the beef was very good and made up for it. Â It was nice and spicy. Â Just the way I like it. Each of the dishes came with bread, which was the only disappointment. Â It was kind of bland. Â However, it was nice to dip in the sauces for the momos. Give this place a shot. Â You will not Â be sorry.

Mostly went here for the history, as being the first pizzeria in America. Â The layout of the space is interesting, after having our name called we were lead through the dining area, through the kitchen where the pizza ovens are, and into a secondary dining area - it was interesting in a good way, kind of neat. Â Started with a salad and then had a pizza. Â Nothing extraordinary but a satisfying meal with nice ambiance. Almost forgot, one thing to note. Â The waitress was nice but didn't return with my change after I payed the bill - pretty sure it was intentional - the amount I gave was close but slightly higher than meal+tip - but I didn't set an expectation that she should pocket it. Â Other than this incident things were great.

A very delicious Irish/English brunch on Saturdays and Sundays from 11-4. The food is excellent and you will yearn for it for the entire week. The place can get very busy and in those times, the service isn't very good, but life is hard and it could be worse and you should just deal with it. Go there hungry, not starving. And the happy hour is excellent, though the prices are always good, and they even have happy hour on weekends (11-8). Great draft selection. Beautiful atmosphere.

It's a pub nothing more nothing less. Â Great bartender I believe his name was Rob (Irish to the core- just what I would expect in a pub). Why do I say it is just a pub -well the food lacked luster however in their defense the kitchen isn't really a kitchen.... Â The fries were cooked in a oven, yes that's to mean not fried (I don't go to a pub to be healthy). Â They reminded me of cardboard and those french fry chips they once sold in the supermarket. Â The sliders were dated- tasted old, like when you defrost a well seasoned burger and let it sit in your fridge for 4 days before serving it up. All the above was however forgotten following the great music played by the Irish band! Â They Rocked and we drank the night away! So will I go back? Yes Will I eat before I go? Absolutely Do I recommend it ? Â Yes on a Tuesday that's when the band was there

When I learned I was coming to NYC for my birthday weekend, I was beyond excited. A huge part of that excitement was due to the food - Chicago is an amazing food city, however, they have several food 'voids'. One of those food voids is honest-to-goodness ramen. I wanted the real deal in New York, so my husband and I hunted down the top two Ramen joints in NYC - Ippudo and Totto. Totto was closer to our hotel, so once arrived in Manhattan (and checked in) we marched straight over to Totto. Even though it was the butt end of lunch hour, it was still about a 30 minute wait. NO MATTER. WE WERE ON A RAMEN-ESQUE MISSION. Once our name was finally called, we sat at the bar and were given all of 90 seconds to decide what we wanted. It's not a huge menu, so there's not a ton of deliberation involved. We both chose the Totto Spicy Ramen. My husband got a side of corn and I got a side of seasoned avocado. The chefs work in front of you, and once our order was put in they hit the ground running. They piled fresh ramen noodles, savory meaty broth, spicy sesame oil, scallions, char siu pork, bean sprouts, nori and the avocado. It Was Divine The broth was fragrant, meaty and spicy, the noodles were cooked al-dente (perfect!!), the avocado was savory and the vegetables added a nice crunch. The pork was fatty and tender with a nice char - this was definitely a highlight. It's a richer cut of pork, for those who are curious. I was absolutely blown away by this soup, we both left stuffed and extremely impressed. I highly recommend this place to anyone jonesin' for noodle soup. Cash Only.

We stumbled into this place late on a Saturday night- right around 11:30pm. We were happy to find that they were still serving food. The bar is definitely divey so if you're looking for an upscale place- this won't be it. There were only a handful of people in there that seemed to all know each other. The bartender was SUPER friendly. Â The drinks were strong, the dartboard was free and the fish 'n chips were the best I've ever had. So glad we randomly found this spot.

This little slice of Italy just so happened to be located a few blocks away from the Trump SoHo Hotel were I was staying. Within walking distance for sure. It was overflowing with people when I arrived and since I didn't have a reservation there was only one spot left at the bar, so I took it. PRO: --The inside was very warm and cozy when I dined, in the evening hours. --I started with the meatballs and had the spinach ravioli as the main course, both dishes were perfect in size and tasted absolutely AMAZING. --The bartender served a perfect bitter Manhattan. I could have had a few hundred if possible. --The service was very prompt, polite and friendly. No complaints CONS: Very Busy and not much room inside... but its nothing to dock a star for. Just be sure to make a reservation. I WILL eat here again for future work trips to NYC.

I have always heard of the NY cheesecake -- the origin of the delicious, so fluffy I'm going to die slice of diabetes. I had a hard time choosing what flavor I waned. After a indecisive wait, I went with the original. I went to the bakery instead of the restaurant itself since I only wanted dessert. The outdoor seating was kinda ratchet... there were pigeons everywhere. So my friend and I went to the red stairs and enjoyed the pretty lights of Time Square while devouring the most delicious cheesecake I've ever eaten. Cheesecake Factory you just got served! I shared one with a friend since the slice was quite big and a little bit decadent. If I am in NY again, this is a must. Maybe a different flavor next time. Something fruity, so the tart of the fruit can mellow out the cream cheese.

There is a full-on Ramen war going on, with Totto being the latest to join in the fray. (Reminder to self, go eat there). It took me awhile to get to Ippudo and now I understand the wait outside and the $14 bowls of peasant food. While definitely more expensive than your average bowl of Ramen (lose 1 star), it really does distinguish itself from other Ramen places with its rich creamy broth. So rich you can see a layer of oil (or fat?) floating on top of the soup base. Order the extra noodles cuz it's certainly not enough with what they give you. I'm a fan and will come back but I'm going to search around for something comparable in taste but lighter on my wallet. And perhaps lighter in fat too. Now that would be 5 stars. Hey, eating healthy is always a bonus.

I teetered between 4 and 5 stars for this one, but I settled on four because I felt like it. Â I'll be back to this joint, so take that for what it's worth. Â  A very sexy special someone and I shared the following: -Pumpkin and Goat Cheese Croquetas: anything pumpkin would please both of us, so this was a big win. -Calamares Fritos: yum. -Mussels: double yum. -Dorada w/ Sunchoke Gazpacho: the gazpacho was killer. Â  -Goat with Saffron Honey: to die for. Top this all off with a great, and highly-recommended bottle of tempranillo, and this place is a winner. Â I'm moving to Spain immediately. Â Or at least Mario Batali's Spain.

Meh. In 14 minutes you could walk from Testo to Il Passatore. Â The menu & underwhelming food would be the same at both places. The Caprese con Mozzarella di Bufala ($10) was really disappointing. Â The tomato wasn't ripe, the cheese was dry & the garnish was ONE basil leaf. Â The plate needed a healthy drizzle of olive oil. Â Where was the waiter to bring this? Â Outside, smoking. Â Rip off. The entrees were fine. Â The handmade pasta in the ragu was great. Â The sauce itself was thin & kinda like the sauce in Chef Boyardee. Â Once upon a time, Chef Boyardee was a great champion of Italian cuisine. I wasn't surprised that my steak was overcooked. Â The poor thing was dry & gristle-pocked, but the garnishes made it more enjoyable. Â The caramelized onions atop the steak were the best part of my meal, really delicious. The small space & atmosphere are charming, i expect to see a lot of traffic here. Â Though i walked away feeling "meh" about my meal, if you stick to the pasta selections you won't have completely wasted your time & money. Cash Only. Â No alcohol, no BYOB. No AC. PS, AVOID the seafood pasta unless you like the taste of freezer burn

This place is CHEAP. In a good way. It just boggled our minds! Our entire dinner, for 2, came to the grand total of $6.50. AND we had leftovers! This is the breakdown of what we ordered: - two orders (4 pieces) of the fried dumplings at $1 per order - one sesame pancake - one order of the boiled dumplings (9 per order) The dumplings were good, dense, and of healthy size. My husband wasn't too fond of the thicker skin, but I thought it made it feel more homecooked. Plus, depending on the region of China, not all dumpling skins are meant to be thin. Also, please note that this place is NOT fancy. It's a tiny hole in the wall, disorganized, crowded, hot, takes cash only, and you have to be diligent in checking up on your order, because they may or may not remember your order. In summary, I loved it there. The reason why I didn't give 5 stars is because of the thicker skin, which I acknowledge people may not like, and the fact that its crazy inside that restaurant. But some people might love it that way! Just check it out - it will be an experience, and a cheap one at that!
Horrible! I ended up with the same food from a competitor's cart, and it was WAAAAAAY better than this one. Way over hyped. Don't fall into the trap!
Great Salads and sandwiches. Comfortable decor, WiFi and the staff is friendly. They also serve a nice selection of beer & wine. Best for lunch & dinner.
great customer service & fresh seafood. appropriate portion sizes. loved: soft shell crab, lobster roll and oysters. don't leave without having a slice of their key lime pie!
If I could give 10 stars for falafel it would go to Taim. This gem is amazing. Too small inside, but food is DELISH!!!

Living in the area, this is a place I head to quite frequently. Â Downstairs is pretty relaxed, but can get very busy, has a good drink selection. Â Upstairs there is normally a wait for (infact pretty much every time), but when you get up there they do a good job at keeping it not busy. Â Drinks are fantastic.

What other place can make you wait 2 hours and you still leave smiling! Â and then hankering for your next visit! Â  Broth is awesome. Ramen is good. Broth is awesome. Sake is good! Broth is awesome. Great service. ahhh, you get the picture... nice artwork all over the restaurant this is for the females -- 2 restrooms for us! Â compared to the one room the guys get. Â ^_^ Â  Shiromaru Hakata Classic was decent. I enjoyed the special Ramen they had tonight better. Â I think the special changes every time you go...so the name is useless. Shoyu Ramen contains a very salty broth. Â But if you like salt...that's the one to try. Tori Karaage was pretty good...however it came with 5-6 tiny pieces. Edamame came with this peppery-salty dip - decent. Chilled Sake comes with a glass in a wooden box. Â Heard that it's tradition to drink it out of the box instead of the glass during celebrations. Worth a visit! Â What have you got to lose except 2 hours and about $20 for a bowl of Ramen. Â at least you'll walk out with a yelp review to write. Â =)

This review is for drinks & music, unfortunately haven't had a chance to try dinner here. Â I absolutely love this place. The decor is definitely 1920's speakeasy. Â When you enter the bellhop greets you & takes you to the restaurant. Â I came here for a friends birthday & we went over to listen to the heathen's perform. Â The music was GREAT, the artists here are talented. Â Also when they switched to the DJ, I really appreciated the 90's music. Â I had a great night here & will definitely be coming here again.

Yes: Delicious grilled shrimp special with rice & beans and pico de gallo; yummi corn. No: Super small portions (specially for the price); bad frozen margueritas... not tasty at all! Plus, they have this weird policy of not serving the shrimp dish for lunch.

If you love bubble tea, this is the place to drink it up! Â I have gotten the classic bubble tea twice now and it has done nothing to disappoint. Â They put a fair amount of tapioca pearls and the flavor has just the right amount of sweet to this afternoon treat. They even give you a rewards card, so that when you buy ten you get one free. Â How great is that right?! I still need to try one of their sandwiches, but I have a feeling it will be quite a grand experience. I hope this place stays open and remains a staple here in East Williamsburg. Â I also hope that more cute storefronts open up like this along Montrose.

This place is pretty good. I liked it a little more just b/c when I got here there was no lines. I actually liked this place a lot more than Lombardi's. But prior to this I wasn't really a pizza fan, but this made me like pizza a little more. Also it's right next to the Brooklyn Bridge, so it's a nice walk to walk off all that carb.

At first glance this place seems to be a hot spot with people coming to this venue frequently. Once you sit down and receive your entree that seems they tried to put a little creativity into it the food has to be the worst tasting Cuban food i've tasted for the price they are charging. I have a problem with the previous reviews it seemed as if they wrote themselves because for one sure thing the food really sux!!! With the exception of the free bread that's given to you. Overpriced food that's mediocre!

Delicious brunch. We got the traditional irish breakfast (with beans - so good), the steak + eggs, and the corned beef hash. I'd never had corned beef hash, Â and really enjoyed theirs. I had never been to an Irish pub and was glad to get to go to Molly's. My friends often go, and I can see why! Delicious brunch.

This is a counter place with very, very limited seating. The pizza is delicious and fairly priced for the quality. I ate there as a vegetarian and as a vegan and even their vegan pizza is delicious and has generous toppings. It's pretty quick, too, though it can get a little crowded sometimes in the tiny space. The pizza is pretty rich/heavy, even the vegan stuff, so be ready!

What can I say? Ippudo is insanely addictive. I love the Karaka Men -- spicy red Ramen -- with egg. The steamed pork buns are sinful. The shishito are served hot and sizzling -- fantastic. Five stars on the food. Only drawback is the ridiculous typical wait time. If you're eating alone, though, you can usually get seated at a big table; can be a lovely lunch.

Awesome! Great, simple wine selection by the glass. The (small) dishes were hard to beat. I had a ceviche with grapefruit & mint, and my friend had grilled octopus with pork belly. I want to go back again and again and try everything on the menu.
They added an extra room next door. So this should help the late night lines and the Sunday church crowd.

Great first impression. I loved almost everything. I love the ease and simplicity of ordering (writing on the laminated menu) and of course, the food was excellent. I had two meatball sliders (beef meatball with tomato sauce, chicken meatball with parmesan cheese sauce) and a vanilla ice cream sandwich with chocolate chip cookies. The sliders were delicious! Both "balls" and sauces. You can tell they use high-quality ingredients. I wish I had ordered one more, but I knew I wanted to try their ice cream and I didn't feel like pigging out. House-made ice cream was also very good, though I thought the cookies were merely okay. Too hard and crispy, though I know some people like their cookies that way. I like them chewy and a bit doughy, especially if it's gonna be for an ice cream cookie. All very affordable too, by the way. I can't wait to return and try more items on the menu. Thumbs up from me!
GREAT!

This place is huge and romanticaly colorful. Specially when you eat their Lasagna and salad most of my favorite, worth it place and services. although you will wait for the orders to serve and its worthly enough because of the surroundings Nice for a group of friends and even romantic date with your love ones. Great and perfect place to take your relaxing mode. Your eyes will never get tired while watching those waiters refillings empty glasses in every table. Most of all my very enjoyable part when im looking at there tables mostly have this what we called "cheesecake", Honestly speaking I dont like cheese its makes me vomit. But over all the food here are delicious and worth it.

the pastel dumplings are awesome!! i could eat them all night long. i've tried the ribeye steak and the mackerel. the steak was very tender and the mackerel was also full of flavor! i would definitely check this place out again to try the other things on the menu.

My girlfriend and I like treat ourselves to brunch at Cafe Ghia on the weekend. Ghia serves very good food, but not quite enough to satisfy on a late weekend morning, though the bottomless coffee is comforting to grasp onto for the duration. The breakfast sandwich and vegetable scrambles (vegan or not) are my favorites .I like the idea of their biscuits & gravy, but the dish is too salty. Go early, the place gets filled pretty quickly. Also, Ghia had a mushroom and wheatberry soup special for dinner recently that was outta this world!

Do you want the best pizza in the city? THEN THIS IS YOUR PLACE! It can be a little pricey since you pay for the pizza not the slice and each topping is extra $$, but don't be cheap, its worth every penny. I also really enjoy their Bruchetta, its a staple for each visit. KEEP IN MIND, this is a very well known restaurant and tends to be busy during peek hours so plan ahead, either call for a reservation or wait time, or dont come starving and be prepared to wait a bit (only during peak hours). Also this is a cash only establishment, but there is an ATM located right outside the door! ENJOY!
Great service, amazing food. I will definitely be back.

Food is great, but definitely check your receipts. My bill came out to $40.72. I provided a 17% tip of $7.00. I discovered that Shanghai Asian Manor decided to add an additional $1.00 when I looked at my credit card statement. That is just shady! I will eat there again, but I will absolutely under-tip them next time. It's about principle, not $1.00.

I wanted to give 3.5 stars, but had to round and decided to round up. I went with a group of five for my birthday and we shared the beef brisket, pork ribs, and the special which was a pork belly and sauerkraut creation, with sides of mac and cheese, collard greens, potato salad, and cornbread. The moist brisket was both moist and tender, though not very fatty. The rub was a bit too strong for me and took away from the amazing flavor and texture of the meat. Just a touch lighter on the pepper and it would be absolute perfection. The pork ribs used the exact same rub to the same effect. They were perfectly moist and the meat was great if you scraped off the rub. The BBQ sauce was delicious, though I never use much because my favorite part of BBQ is the meat. The mac and cheese wasn't bad, it just wasn't good. It needs... something. The collard greens were great, perfect flavor. The potato salad was nothing to write home about but it went well with the BBQ which is its job so I would definitely order it again. The cornbread is delicious, especially with the butter. And we ended our meal with the maple bourbon pecan pie and ice cream, which really stole the show. The atmosphere is nice and not too crowded. The staff are all very friendly and helpful, and the service is amazing. The food came out quickly and everyone enjoyed their drinks. I grew up in Texas and miss easy access to incredible BBQ and have started my search for the best I can get in New York. This was tasty, but just not close enough to become my go to BBQ joint in Brooklyn.
Food was pricey however the ambiance was great and so was the food.

Jury duty in the cold NYC winter meant only one thing - I could finally grab a cheap weekday lunch in Chinatown! Entrees here sell for as cheap as $5 a bowl for the basic vegetable & egg noodle soup. I ordered the #1 House Special Noodle Soup, only $7.25 for a delicious bowl of knife cut noodles, ox tail, beef tendon, tripe, beef slices, and a fried egg. I wish the egg was more over-easy, but the tendon and beef slices were great. The noodles were also too soft for my liking, but I think that's a matter of preference. The older generation of Chinese people just really like their noodles soft, but I need that al dente texture. The noodle shop keeps a container of cilantro on every table, and I was not shy about shoveling spoonfuls and spoonfuls of the herb into my beef broth. The broth is on the lighter side and one of the better broths I've had in Chinatown. When you order, you have the option to get hand-pulled, knife cut, or rice noodles. Definitely try the knife cut noodles - I love the irregular length and texture of the noodles. If you sit near the kitchen you can see the chef slapping the dough against the table and pulling the dough into long noodle strands. What's the secret ingredient to making that springy, chewy Chinese noodles? "Jian shui" ("kan sui in Canto), aka lye water, is high in alkaline and gives the dough that yellow, chewy texture. It toughens up the dough and gives it that nice firmness. If you make noodles at home though and decide to add in lye water, be careful!! Lye, depending on the concentration, can cause severe burning or blindness. An easier alternative is to use dehydrated baking soda instead of lye. I had no idea they had seating downstairs until I saw a group of 10 magically disappear behind me. Next time I'm trying the pan fried noodles.

Went to the Brooklyn Star this past weekend with moderate expectations. Â We ordered about half of the items on the menu (far too much btw). Â Overall it was just OK. Â Let me break it down a bit. Wings - Good, not great. Â I would have preferred spicier Cornbread - Very good. Â I recommend this one Summer squash casserole -- no good. Â Strange consistency. Â A bit runny. Weak flavor Green bean casserole -- One of the highlights. Â If debating between the squash and green bean casserole DEFINITELY choose this one Dr. Pepper ribs -- eh. Â OK. Not that tender and the flavor just wasn't that great Meatloaf sandwich -- Mixed feelings across the table, but this was one of my favorites. Â This is a meal in itself. Mac and cheese -- I thought it was very good with a little hot sauce. Â Feeling was not matched across the entire table as some thought the flavor was a bit strange. Chicken fried steak -- By this time I was really too full to even eat much of this. Â I took a taste. Â The mashed potatoes were pretty good. Â The chicken fried steak was average. Â By this time I wanted to go home and do some jumping jacks though. In general this place is just OK, and in a neighborhood where there are so many excellent options I won't finding myself going back. Â If you want the best southern food go to Pies and Thighs (although the menu is much more limited there).

I just spent a good 4 hours here chatting and drinking tea. I ordered the Honey Phoenix (Oolong) and the Makinohara Sencha (Green) along with Cha-an dessert set. Everything tasted scrumptious and the tea was excellent. Our bill came out to $100--what a splurge at a teahouse haha. My friends and I were having profound conversations and I hope we didn't disturb the other patrons when we got a wee bit excited. Random: The bathroom is gorgeous! I had to go multiple times thanks to all the tea I drank. I even went into the mens room because the woman was taking way too long in there. The womens bathroom is much nicer and the toilet is high tech (mwahaha) :) Important: Cash only.

Good Thai food, and at a price point you really can't beat (especially in the w village). Pad Thai is awesome, dumplings are great, and they have really awesome lunch specials during the week. Downsides: Staff can be a bit odd at times and the place is very small. If you can get a table and are in the mood for Thai, I would definitely recommend Pinto.

Really wanted to love this place after tons of hype from my gf. Walked in around 6 on a Friday and asked if they could get us a table for 7:30. Maitre d' called us and let us know ten minutes in advance it was ready. We wandered over to Bleeker for some wine meanwhile. So that was great :) Mains: the skate was delicious but I was a bit disappointed by the lamb shank which was gigantic but almost horrifically so. After having good wine before the meal, when we ordered the wine by the glass at the top of the list here, we were also a bit disappointed by its lack of any interesting character. My favorite part of the meal was dessert. The chocolate souffle w/ gelato was simply to die for.

Really lovely place for both brunch and dinner. I especially enjoyed their lox club sandwich, it's enormous and you feel good for getting your money's worth. I think what really made the place stand out for me (because let's face it, this isn't the first cute French brunch place in the hood) is the personable staff. They make sure you're comfortable (the place is baby friendly!) and have no qualms about recommending their favorites as well as joking around with the patrons.

Very nice little Tapas joint in the lower east side. Â The food and drinks were delicious and reasonably priced, especially when you buy drinks by the pitcher. Â The service was good and friendly for the most part, barring the guy who tried to pinch my fiancÃ©e and I in between the window and the table, and was kind of rude about it when my fiancÃ©e asked him to pull the table back out a little bit so that we could breathe a little.
