Â We understand that space was limited, but that was a little ridiculous. Â Aside from that minor blunder, we had a fantastic time. Â You absolutely MUST try the Crispy Pork Pizza , probably one of the best things I've ever eaten. Â Definitely would have given 5 stars to this place had it been purely based on food and drinks.
Over priced for what you get. We wouldn't rush back here again.
Went here for brunch and got the Eggs Benedict. The service was slow and they overcooked my egg. The Bloody Mary was good and the bacon servings were very generous.

Ended my last week with the visiting of this place -at first got huge open space for dealing with the parking. One of the amazing place though a bit simple before this never tried at here. Seemed a bit pricy from the other when first saw it for the ordering. As the first time before coming here knew a bit from the review done by others-ordered for their tacos that good really tasty. Also the meat here yummy -had only three tacos, meat and the sope------so delicious.

Excellent, excellent, excellent...the food is amazing, the service is superb (never expected this level of service in any restaurants in east village to be honest) and the atmosphere is really romantic. They did a nice job on the ceiling with clay pots, liked how unlike it was to the other Greek restaurants out there mostly themed of Santorini, with white and blue. I took my boyfriend here and we both loved it - became our favorite Greek spot.
Reasonable price with great food & service. We have never been disappointed going here...

I love this place! Came here after we found out how long the wait was over at clinton st bakery. My party of 7 only had to wait like 10 minutes for a table for sunday brunch. Things were already off to a good start. We look down at the menus and back up to each other in disbelief at how affordable everything is. Two eggs, plus potatoes and mixed greens for only $4??? Are you kidding me? Yes please. Â  And they waitress was kind enough to sub out the greens for fresh fruit. So one would assume the food wouldn't actually taste that well considering the price but not here folks. Everything was really good. The fresh squeezed lemonade was also great. Our waitress kept coming back to check in on us and refill our drinks. Top notch service + great food + low prices = easy 5 stars from me. This will continue to be my go-to-spot for breakfast in the city.

I fell in love with Maialino the first time I visited, and have been back countless times since. Â The food is consistently excellent. Â We always start with the lightly fried artichokes, which are perfectly cooked - not mushy, not too crispy. Â Last time, we ordered the Maialino "suckling pig" for 2, and it was succulent and flavorful, with an incredible crispy skin. Â We also had the carbonara a few times, and each time the pasta was perfectly al dente, and the sauce light and silky, just as carbonara should be. Â  The best dessert of all time is the Torta della Nonna, or "Grandmother Cake," which is a lemon pastry cream in a tart shell, covered in pine nuts, dusted in powdered sugar, and served with a lemon caramel sauce. Â Former pastry chef Jenn made it best, but the new chef is doing it justice - maybe the sauce was just a bit too acidic - but the overall dessert still delicious. Â  Maialino brunch is great as well - the lemon ricotta pancakes are light and sweet, and the homemade doughnuts served warm - so delicious!

It was great once upon a time. Then the prices started to rise. The beer menu was surpassed by others and we realized how much a drink was going for. Fighting over table space is never a joy either. The BBQ is still good, but I guess it's not worth either the hassle or the price anymore, esp in the summer months when we can do it ourselves at how. Pork belly is still a joy though!

Still craving more puerto rican food from my last experience at "Pasteles y algo mas", I decided to try casa adela since it was closer to me. Yelp, I love you, but sometimes the reviews for these Â restaurants are on crack! I absolutely did not see what the big fuss was about this restaurant! Â I get better spanish food from the cuchifritos or even the grocery store sometimes! It smelled good upon walking it, but lacked authenticity. Â I ordered the chicharron de pollo with yellow rice and red beans and a side order of potato salad. Â The chicken was okay, I liked the the crust it had on it but wasn't made the traditional way. It was like they had dipped it into a batter as opposed to just frying it. The rice was normal and so were the beans. The potato salad killed me! I had high expectations that fell flat to the floor and got ran over by a truck. Absolutely nooooooo flavor whatsoever! Â I was tempted to add salt, but I just left it. The bf ordered a sancocho soup, which he said was okay and a pernil sandwich. The poor pernil sandwich was dryer than the sahara. We asked for a mojo (garlic sauce) which they seemed to forget about. They had rotisserie chickens cooking which seemed to be popular, Â but I don't know there's a thin line between jui y and dry when doing rotisserie. The waiter was really nice however, but search for puerto rican food in nyc continues.

This is probably some of the best higher end pizza I've had in a long time. My friend and I split a duck hunt and a banana boat pizza. Both were really amazing. There is not much more that I can do to elaborate, its a very subjective experience. But really good stuff. Normally I would just give this place a 5 for the food, but some things were a bit off. We waited for almost 2 hours. Not bad, I do understand that the place is popular. We waited in the bar area and ended up spending a lot on drinks. Again, not the worst thing in the world. The problem is that they then try to squeeze you into the communal tables and you may end up sitting next to someone who is either sloshed, or you are sloshed yourself sitting next to someone that isn't. Plus I have all kind of issues with personal space when eating. We also didn't care much for the wine we had, but I don't think that's the restaurant's fault.
Have to come for Happy Hour. The appetizers and desserts were so good. We can have more. Service was excellent. Have to go back again! Soon!

The pancakes are perfect. Maple butter is out of this world- although, I really think its too little for 4 huge pancakes. It's a tiny bowl! WHY. *Can I have some more please?* Also, I had the bluberry muffin and it was seriously SO BAD. So hard and brittle- it tasted like cardboard! Starbucks make a better muffin than the one I had here. WTH- they're supposed to be a baking company and they get the basics like muffins wrong! Also, the waitress here was a real bitch. We tipped 12% and she asked for a 20% tip! I mean, 20% tip is only when the service is impeccable! The service was OK mainly coz the waiters and waitresses are such hustlers and so loud and just ruin the laid back breakfast experience.

just a quick update on my original review....really nice experience and good meal but no idea why they cook with such a heavy hand on the salt shaker? each person in our party of 4 were taken aback how or why every dish we had was so seasoned. The pizza appetizer was very nice and my steak entree was good...far from exceptional. Fun place, good service and good food that could rise to another level with more inventive seasonings other than salt.
A true dive bar. Super cheap beer and deals. Decided to go in after we came out of the beer garden across the street. Not much to choose from tap but they have a lot bottle selection.

Overall wonderful experience. Saw the restaurant/bar on yelp and decided to check it out with my mom and brother, what a spectacular decision! Don't walk in expecting the Ritz, but if you want that "I'm a regular" feel, this. is. your. place. Stopped in to have some drinks and dinner and were greeted by an exceptional owner and waitress. By following the suggestions of our waitress we ordered the Drunk fish soup (amazing), garlic shrimp, fried rice with shrimp (ooooh I'm dreaming of it), and the pork belly dish. No complains heard. The service was impeccable. Rarely in New York will you get a waitress, let a lone an owner who really connects and wants to welcome you to their "home." Go and try this place, dressed in your jeans and t-shirt ready to take some shots and have a margarita (or a beer from their hefty list) and enjoy this dive bar with amazing food! You won't regret it! Thanks again, we'll be back!!

I was going to start this review by unloading my arsenal of pho puns (e.g., best pho, pho-sho; unpho-gettable pho pho-nomenal), but I feel like doing so would just trivialize the love and respect that I have for Saigon Shack. Â Summer rolls are fresh and consistently good. Â I won't claim to be an expert on authentic Pho, but the Classic Beef Pho is delicious and complex and super flavorful. Â The meat is really tender, but kind of bland. Â My partnah always orders the catfish and rice. Â It's a nice mix of flavors and always fresh. There are so many other menu options that I want to try, but I can't seem to break away from my standard order. Service is good, but it does get really busy. There is usually a wait but tables turn over quickly and orders appear like BAM, within a few minutes. The servers don't snuggle you or stare into your eyes and tell you how pretty you are, or anything like that, but they are always polite and responsive. I visit a few times a month and they are not the type of people to spill food on anyone intentionally, so sorry for the poster below me who was sad she didn't have an Eleven Madison Park-length meal or experience because of the "Asian chick" at a small Vietnamese restaurant.

The pizza was great & the staff friendly. Everything was great till just about the end, when two people from our group went out to smoke. The owner asked us if we were ordering anything & I ordered dessert. He asked if the two people had left & we said no they were outside. A few minutes later he comes back & takes the two empty chairs away. Then asks us to move to a smaller table. Two of us had to eat dessert standing... All of this because there was a big party that needed chairs. We almost got tossed out because the owner wanted more business. Loved the pizza but will not go back.

Delicious and flavorful food. I couldn't decide what to order, as the menu had so many appealing options. I settled on the cavatelli. It is perhaps one of my favorite pasta dishes I have ever had. My mother enjoyed her frittata, and the bread pudding made a great end to our lunch. A bit pricey...but I wasn't paying.
Best pizza in NYC!
so delicious! had lunch here and I know I'll be back. you can't go wrong with anything on the menu. friendly staff and food is ready fast.
best chicken in woodside. period

I was very excited to try this place, but I left disappointed. The service was bizarre - granted our waitress was 'in training' but she was super weird - staring at us, awkward silences - and the food was not great. The space, however, is very nice and I could see it being a good place to go for drinks and maybe appetizers but I will not come back to eat again. Don't get me wrong, the food is edible, but there are much much better options available within walking distance. If you must eat here, avoid the super bland sandwiches. I really hope they get it together and improve the food, the place has a lot of potential and would be a great addition to the neighborhood...
I recently ordered pizza for my work crew from here. Â We got a few plain pizzas and picked them up. Â Definitely one of the better slices I've had in a while.

I like this place, but it's still a little too new. I had their tonkatsu, which was delicious, albeit pricey ($10!) for my SF standards. I came here for lunch, and I was super excited about their takoyaki, which they...didn't have ready. (I guess they get more people asking for it for dinner?) My friend was looking for chicken katsu, which I understand not having, but then my friend asked for a cup of ice to drink with her coke, and there wasn't any ice. (Really???) The tonkatsu is still good though, and it was a little more than enough for me. Make the takoyaki available for lunch, serve some beer, and I'll be here more often.

My family and I used to meet other family members at Carmine's but my daughter and her boyfriend came here one day and recommended it highly. Â So glad we tried it. Â This is our new go-to place in NYC!!! Love love love it!!! The food is amazing! The staff is wonderful! They can't do enough for you! Â This restaurant is truly the best Italian in the city.

Trying to figure out which of the four near-identical halal carts on this intersection was THE famous 53rd & 6th halal cart caused us a great deal of anguish. We finally decided that this one near the statue/fountain must be the one as it had the longest queue and didn't open until 7.30 pm. I still don't really know if the other carts are affiliated with this one or are just shameless imitators. We ordered the mix chicken and gyro plate and loved it. I agree with all positive comments above and below.
Off the hook. Flavorful. Great portions. Good atmosphere.

After reading so many great YELP reviews on this truck, I''d figure this would be the most orgasmic thing I would eat and gave it a shot. I went to the truck on Park during my lunch hour. The guys on the truck were really nice and sweet and suggested the "Maine Lobster Roll" which I agreed too. Considering they aren't fishing for the lobster in their trucking, boiling it, and then cooking it to make this lobster roll, I thought $16 was a bit steep for the size of what would be equal to a 6in sub at SUBWAYS . From the first bite, this roll lacked flavor. It was suppose to be tossed in a lemon mayo and I tasted no lemon whatsoever. For me, it was just lobster, with lettuce and a sprinkle of Â paprika on top. Â I was waiting for the kick of flavor but that never came thru. I was truly disappointed in not only the roll, but the fact that now i am $16 poorer. Frankly I don't know why this place has so many great reviews. I like food with a lot of depth and flavor and this place just didn't deliver. I will give 2 stars though, because the bread was awesome as well as the workers' attitude ( and they were cute).

If this place were closer to my work, I'd have dumplings everyday and no doubt turn into one sooner or later. Â It's cheap and it hits the spot. Â Without fail I always eat with my eyes here and end up getting an order of the spicy wontons and the pork scallion pancake sandwich thing on the menu. Sometimes I may even add a seaweed salad to make me feel like I'm eating a little healthy. This isn't a place you come for the atmosphere. Â It's a place you go to for cheap, fast, delicious Chinese food. The place is tiny so if it's packed so you'll have to act like a vulture once you place your order at the counter in order to snag a spot. Â Not a recommended place to take a first date, but if you want a spot to sit, it's always easier when one person places and waits for the order while the other looks keeps an eye out for a table.

Great ramen and pretty quick service once you are inside, but that's the problem. Totto has maybe 10 seats at the bar and 10 regular seats, so the lines outside can be huge. We came one night when it was not too crowded and waited maybe 20 minutes. The cooks are blowtorching the pork slices as you wait, and the added items are fine. A great place but you have to wait.

Ambiance: cute hipster neighborhood place, old and new school rap/r&b pumping through the air... Unexpected but comforting. Â Rustic tables and ceiling. Think the random disco ball spinning in the ceiling is a funny little touch. Â It's a small quaint restaurant. Â You won't have to worry about 50 tables because the area is far too small for that, but a comfortable small. For starters I had the nacho which was different but delicious. Â It was more of a hollow wonton with cheese diced pico de gallo along with the deep fried deviled eggs. I thought the deviled eggs with bacon was good although it could've used salt and I actually didn't find my bacon until the very last last bite... Still good but would've been on point with a dash or two of salt. I tasted the doughnut with fois however I want it to be known I was told the jelly wasn't great so I just ate a piece of the outside with powdered sugar... It was really good. Main course: Chicken and waffles I was not a big fan of the maple syrup with blood orange mixed in... But the Cornish hen was the bomb!!! Waffles weren't bad but the Cornish hen was seriously on point. Â There was some type of greens in with the waffle and chicken which... I guess was a weird to add in but I saved it for later to just eat with the chicken. Dessert: Frozen snickers was really good, just as you expect. All and all I'll be back!

We waited about 10 minutes at 12:30 on Monday, but when we left, the line was probably an hour long. Â Great pizza, but probably not worth the wait. Â I prefer Il Fornaio in Little Italy - but they only serve pizza at lunch. Friendly inside. Â Fast, bustling, no frills.

In the past 18 months since I have lived in New York, I think I've eaten at this restaurant more than any other in the city. The place reminds me of my great grandmother's house in every possible way: drop ceilings, mismatched lamps, mounted deer heads, and hoards of people cramming in to eat Polish food. The stuffed cabbage is delicious, as are all of the versions of breaded cutlet. The kielbasa isn't the best I've ever had, but it's up there. The pierogi are stellar, in every variety, the potato pancakes are awesome, and the pickled vegetables are perfect. And BYOB means that dinner for 4, (not including a bottle of Zubrowka purchased from the liquor store next door) will probably run under $50. The place gets crowded on Fridays and Saturdays, which can mean a wait (at the door, to place your order, to get your food, to get your check, etc.), especially because they usually only have one person serving. But once you sit down, they are in no hurry to rush you out the door, so you can linger over your nalesniki and vodka until you're good and ready. Minus one star because the waiting can be stressful if you are unprepared, and the lack of waitstaff makes me anxious when people around me starting getting annoyed, but seriously one of my top choices in NYC.

Group of five in for a mid-aft snack on the holiday weekend. I had the cheese burger -- was great. The fries come with a great spiced mayo (you may want a spoon...). Seating is great, open concept building with really interesting architecture. Had the locally-brewed lager too -- a great summer beer.
Spicy tropical chicken with black eye pea long grain rice and pineapple mango salsa and sangria ! Â The chicken was seasoned with spices and the rice was a perfect complement

I was NOT on board with the whole fancy pizza thing-- UNTIL I CAME TO PAULIE GEE'S! This place is the best. Amazing pizza, quality service. And Paulie himself is Â almost always there, talking to the guests, being friendly, funny and welcoming. My only complaint is that I wish I lived closer to it!
Good lord. Still as fattening and delish as I remember from 2 years ago. I love you. The one across the street IS THE EXACT SAME. You noobs.

Curry Soba noodles!!! I don't live in NYC but I will definitely be coming to this place first when I go back to visit my friends in NY. I dream about their curry noodles and wish we had something similar here in SF (there probably is, I just haven't stumbled upon it yet). I love places that specialize in certain types of foods which is why it's no surprise that this place is very good at what they do - soba noodles. Everytime I eat here, I feel like I'm in a Miyazaki film eating delicious animated Japanese food. I really need to find a soba noodle place here in SF because I always go through withdrawals whenever I think about this place. Excuse me.......**shivers in a corner**.......ok, I'm back. I'm ok. I'm ok.........................WHY!?!?!?!...... ::ahem:: Ok, I'm ok now. I promise. Anyway, come here. Yummy food!

Nice little unpretentious Mexican restaurant with a cafe feel to it - small tables, plastic cutlery (but nothing else plastic), newspaper to read, delicious spicy hot chocolate. And lots of vegetarian options! Yey for carnivorous places that make the effort. Much easier than Spanish Harlem where my sucky monolingualism and their lack of clearly vegetarian dishes results in confusion. Vegetarian options include nopales (grilled cactus) burritos and tacos, huitacoche and flor de calabaza 'traditional' quesadillas, cheese or garlic spinach quesadillas, seitan fajita etc. I haven't tried them all yet, but it's a challenge I'm willing to take on. So far nice flavors and nothing nastily greasy. I enjoyed the casual atmosphere. Service was really slow but that just made me feel welcome to hang out and read.

A gem of a discovery in Bay Ridge! This is the kind of French Food-faire you'd expect in some hoighty-toighty (sp?) location in the city but nope, it's safely tucked away in neighborly mom n'pop Bay Ridge, Brooklyn and I am A-OK with that. Â I hope Petit Oven is here to stay! This is the perfect place for a grown adult (child) to: 1) Partake in a romantic date with your significant other. 2) Get treated to a fancy-pants drunkie dinner with your middle-aged parents who will most certainly foot the bill. Â (I picked this one!) The restaurant recommends you make a reservation ahead of time and from my guess it's because it operates true to its name -- it's a small establishment that fills up quick in its peak hours. Â I came at 6:30 to an empty restaurant and left when it was filling up. Â They also have Happy Hour $1 oysters until 7 so we (my grown-ass self and my parents who footed the bill, yay!) took full advantage of that. I'm under the impression that the restaurant offerings are seasonal and that's cool if you like variety and if you don't, go to McDonald's, you philistine! Â Our server was knowledgable with her wine recommendations and giving us the lowdown on what goes down on the daily (chef goes to the market during the day, picks out some cool ingredients and really just improvises a fantastic flavorful menu), I can't complain about talent like that and you get what you pay for...culinary GENIUS. Menu items worth writing home about: 1) Escargot = Holy shit, when you're done eating the snails, sop up the leftover HERBY GARLIC OIL SAUCE, with more bread. 2) Proteins (Duck and Steak) = Cooked to perfection. Â Duck had crispy skin, Steak was moist and delish. 3) Bread Pudding = Because. Bread. Pudding. A bit on the pricier side but we had an undeniably great time. Â  Great service, great food -- Would definitely come back with my folks or the bf if we felt like splurging and enjoying a relaxing night out without the fuss of heading into the city.
My favorite restaurant in BK..

Today I met someone for a business luncheon and ate at The Smith for the first time. I am sorry to report that I would not recommend this fancy over priced place. The bathrooms are coed which weirded me out too. I ordered the Mediterranean salad. I have never tasted anything so salty and over peppered in my life. The person I was meeting ordered a roasted tomato cheese soup. She said it was good. For a soup, salad and a cup of coffee it was $36.00. WAY too much money for food I would rather eat in a Diner. Thanks but no thanks...

Visiting NYC from San Francisco and our hotel pointed us in this direction. I ordered the Breakroom Burger and fell in love with the first bite. I will be back to try the tacos before I leave..... May be back twice before I leave.

This place RULES. And it's near the Comedy Cellar, a great comedy joint. The cracked out white girls that hang around here are cool, the emo-dopes and just plain trashy babes that wander this block, with the restaurants and bars nearby makes a great environment to pick up a falafel sandwich with white sauce and spice. The meat is just right too - that thing, whatever it is, whatever part of whatever animal it comes from is just moist to the mouth and bangin'. The hummus, babbagonoush and all the other delicacies are on point. Whoever tries to mess with these people and act the fool, will get stomped on personally by me. That's how much I love the employees and food here. The only one who can go in there and make fun of these savages and their smelly selfs, is ME!
Gueros is amazing. Â Definitely a bit of a wait if you're eating there. Â The fried avocado and jalapeno tacos are my fave. Â Nachos or chips with queso are also amazing.

I love ramen and I really like this restaurant! We came in on a Thursday around 1PM. The atmosphere and decor of the place was really nice, and the food comes out pipping hot in the bowl. It stays hot even to your very last bite of noodles or your very last sip of soup. I got the miso ramen ($15) with a side of egg ($2). It's actually pretty pricey for ramen. I've had just as good ramen in Los Angeles (and they give you more pork meat with a side of egg) for $10, but this isn't Los Angeles it's New York City. Tea is given after your meal. Every time a group gets seated or ramen is being served to someone, the whole staff just starts shouting something in Japanese- or so you think it's Japanese. My friend speaks Japanese and it's just funny when she tells me that some of them are actually saying something in Japanese while others are just shouting something in gibberish. Haha... My friend had a bad experience with the service here when she came with a group of people on a Saturday. I'm glad she decided to give this place a 2nd try when I came to town.
worth a visit. ilke a high end grocery store with a rest inside. the food was creative.
Probably one of the best panini's i've had...great ratio and awesome bread...the soup is delicious as well.....if in the area don't hesitate to stop in.

Surprise Surprise! My Japanese (true-bred Japanese) New Yorker friend brought me and his girlfriend to this Ramen place - described by them both as their favourite ramen place in the city. I have tried Totto Ramen and am quite disappointed. Am keen to try Ippudo but am too lazy to wait in line. I was really excited to find out if Minca could triumph my Totto Ramen experience! He highly recommended the Toroniku Ramen - slow cooked pork belly with fresh cabbage in shoyu soup base. It was WOW! The soup base was very savoury, not too salty. However, it was slightly oily ... but I really could not blame them for the greasiness. Because the 4 large chunks of pork belly meat (from which the oil oozed out from) were so succulent, tender and delicious. The fresh and crunchy chopped cabbage 'dressing' the ramen dish gave a 'light and healthy' touch to the soup and meat. The ramen noodles were springy and chewy! The quantity totally triumphed Totto. I was so full after the meal. Japanese friend said that Ippudo did not leave much of an impression on him. We went there at around half-12 on a Sunday - it was not too busy - there were a few empty tables. The place is really small so avoid coming in large groups.

After searching other reviews to find a place to take my mom for her birthday, this looked like the best bet to actually be able to comfortably sit down and enjoy a relaxing meal. We had relatively earty reservations, so we got a nice table by the window, and started out with the guacamole. It didn't disappoint, and was even pretty filling when using the mini tortillas instead of just chips. The smoky chipotle sauce was a perfect add-on, giving it a kick. We went with a couple different drinks off the specialty menu, and they were each strong enough to give you your money's worth for NYC. As for the food, we got a skirt steak, some pork shoulder, and the uber-cheesy chorizo/cheese appetizer. All three were done to perfection, and it was a big hit with my mom (who seldom ventures into the city from the boonies in NJ). Two cocktails, two entrees and two apps for $80 is hard to beat for the quality of food we had, and all of us left stuffed to the gills! Would certainly come back here again.

definitely one of the best xiao long paos in manhattan. Â better than joe's. Â the skin is not thick, for sure and the meat is very flavorful. Â have eaten there 5 times and it's been pretty consistent so far. Â the classic pork xiao long pao is better than the pork with crabmeat. Â  Â  also, it's one of the cleaner restaurants in chinatown. Â can't give this place a perfect 5 because have not found the other dishes they are good at.

the place is ok...porterhouse was good and chorizo and morcilla as well... appetizers are kinda of TOO small...the ceviche was just TINY and 14$...and honestly..pretty bad..."spanish" style octopus (i add the quoations bc i am from spain and had never eaten pulpo like that..) was ok...just an ok place...fine quality meat but that is it...i dont think i will go back...but you never know

pro: Dinner: this is my default place to go to when i want comfort food and a drink, which is always. get: fried green beans, mac and cheese and mussels. they have a pretty mean burger special on sundays that come with a beer. I always get their pink pussy cat sundae. (red velvet cake, homemade strawberry ice cream, strawberries and whipped cream!) Brunch: its been a while since i went for brunch but i remember having a really good eggs benedict with spinach and smoked salmon. they also have a cocktail special. unlimited refills for a set price. there's also a photobooth downstairs and you'll find a surprise next to the bathroom stalls.if you peek through the holes in the walls pretty solid service too. con: LOUD. the white tiles in the place makes noise bounce everywhere.

4.5 This place is as good as its reputation.. We arrived on a rainy Monday night at 5:47. Â We open the door and are greeted by a crew of people.. "I'm sorry but, we do not open to six.." they said "That's ok, do you mind if we just sit at a table and order a bottle of wine and wait for you to open" I replied "We do not serve alcohol, If you would like to walk three blocks down the street, you can purchase a bottle of wine" So, we were on our way down the block to pick up a bottle of wine.. If you are a wine drinker, I would highly suggest you bring a bottle from home.. There were very few decent choices at the local shop.. We arrive back at Lucali's at 5:58... Still, they open at 6 and in Lucali's world, 5:58 is clearly not 6.. 6 o'clock comes and it is now time to enter.. We enter the restaurant with 5 other tables.. Mainly families with kids. Â The place is really very charming, very comfortable and rustic.. I am pretty sure that candles and the raging swirling fire coming from the forno, were the only light sources in the restaurant.. Â It's romantic.. The smell of wood, the tin ceilings, the treated yellow walls, the old wood furniture.. It reminds me of a cross between Peasant and Il Buco.. Very rustic.. The pace is smooth.. The pizzaiola, though, in no rush, is steadily producing pizzas and calzones. Â One thing I found surprising was that the pizza doughs are essentially pre-rolled and are stretch out just a little more prior to being topped and fired. Â  We order from the "menu".. You either can order a calzone or a pizza.. All limited to a handful of toppings.. First we received the calzone.. Light and airy, with a golden brown outside, it had the perfect filling of ricotta, mozzarella, and sliced artichokes.. Â Served with a side of bright and vibrant tomato sauce.. It was just amazing.. The sauce, was a perfectly drinkable red sauce.. We could have easily stopped at the calzone.. But, we trekked on.. Plus, we had some much wine leftover and the wine would have been so lonely without food.. It was our duty.. The pizza.. We ordered a classic pie.. The sauce to cheese ratio was perfect.. Not too saucy, lots of wonderful milky mozzarella..Though, I am pretty sure there was a blend of cheese passed the topping of the aged parm. Â Often times at these high end or Neapolitan style restaurants, you receive a burned crust and they tell you "it's traditional".Here, no excuses had to be made.. It was just an amazing pie.. Great place.. For a few years the crowds have kept me away.. It's was not as bad as everyone makes it out to be.. By the time we left at 7:15, the place had still not filled up..
Decent but nothing outstanding, will give 3.5 if I can

3.5 stars. We got there just before it opened at 11:30am on a Friday, and there were already several groups in line before us. Â However, we got seated in the first round of people (whew!). Â Otherwise, the wait can be pretty long. The pizza here is fine, but I don't think it's so special that I'd wait in line for it. Â I guess it's one of those places that you just have to try once if you're a tourist. Â  We got a small pizza (has 6 slices) with sausage - this was a good size for 2 moderate-appetite people to share. Another table's pizza was pretty black and burnt on the bottom, but thankfully ours wasn't charred like that. If you're visiting NYC/Brooklyn, note that Grimaldi's is a 5-10 min walk to the Brooklyn Bridge - You could eat at Grimaldi's & then walk across the bridge to Manhattan afterwards.

If you're looking for a good dining option in the UWS during peak hours and don't want to get stuck in an hour long wait, check out Kefi's. Kefi's is a spacious restaurant (rarity in NYC) with plenty of seating. Our party of eight had no trouble getting seated during a Sunday lunch. Here's a short rundown of some of the lunch items: Mac n Cheese - It was good, but wasn't a standout. I prefer the the mac n cheese @ the Yardhouse. Ravoli - Excellent flavoring, better than the mac n cheese. Salad - Spinach salad with bacon bits, boiled eggs, sun-dried tomatoes was fresh and very good - I'm trying to figure out what ingredients they used in the dressing so I can make this salad at home. If Kefi's start selling their salad dressings by the bottle I'd be first in line. Meat Burger - I only had one bite and it was pure deliciousness. This is what I will order next time I return to Kefi's. Chicken Soulvaki - heathier and almost as tasty alternative to the burger. In addition the reasonable prices, charming atmosphere, and good service makes for an enjoyable dining experience. 3.5 stars rounding up!

Alone on Christmas Eve, I got a call from a friend, "We're going Â to Rolf's, come join us." Well just before I left my place, I got another call, "Rolf's is closed, we're at Molly's." UGH...ok...When I got there, I was confused because the door is unmarked, Â super small and I am not (New Yorkers know that if you open the wrong door, you will be in an apartment building if you don't pay attention)... I finally squeezed in an noticed the filthy floor, OH, that's sawdust...ummm ok... I spotted my friends and had a seat, directly in front of the fireplace. Thank goodness I was chilly and required thawing. Â I wasn't hungry, but my friend had a shephards pie that I tried. Â It was very tasty! The servers were all very nice and the drinks are unremarkable...its whiskey, ok, great.... I must say that they were playing decent music. Â I will try this place again, once I lose 80lbs so that I may easily fit through the door. Â That is, if I can find the door again...

A bunch of mixed reviews on here (really high and low) Pros: 1. Â Eaten here twice, lunch and dinner on travels. Â Both times I thought the food was awesome. Â I stuck with the large plates, apparently people have some bad vibes on the small stuff. 2. Â Bar/wine selection is solid if you want to try new things you can get a few things to enjoy. 3. Â Staff is super friendly. Â Both times people talked, made suggestions, etc... Â  Cons: 1. Â Wait staff is pretty laid back. Â Common thing I get in french places run by french people. Â If you wave someone down they don't seem to have a problem but they always appear busy and not running to tables like at a normal place. Â I wouldn't go here in a bind for time.
Excellent drinks and chicken and waffles! The other stuff I've tried was just meh, especially the po boy. So dry and flavorless!
Amazing Pizza. Very fast line also.

I have to say I could just sit down and eat a million of those pork buns, but I am not a huge fan of the Momofuku noodles. They were kind of bland and bulky (in a sense that it was just carblicious (and this from someone who LOVES carb). In fact, I would say stick to the appetizers and order a bunch of them. My husband got something that involved either sweetbreads or some other kind of intestines in a chile-like soup, and that was pretty awesome too.

3.5 This place will most likely continue to do good business despite my review so if nothing else, I'll just use this platform to get a few things off my chest. Â  Food was worth the money. Â Really delicious. Â It arrived super prompt and impecable even on a busy Friday. Â  Atmosphere was lively, laid back, and slick. Â There was a little wait for a table so the host took our # and texted when our table was ready. Â  Nice. Â  This far, I'd be back. Â However; The bad part: Â Our server, Loren. Â I hate calling out people but this guy rubbed us pretty wrong. Â Maybe an off night for the dude but it seemed his zest for his work had long ago departed. Â The bar tender directly in front of us put more TLC into his JOB on a bad day. Â We are not demanding people. Â I'm a server myself. Â We don't need or want anyone coddling us however a simple follow up to how any of our 4 dishes taste is service 101. Â Especially for an nicer place. Â We started to make eye contact with him to invite a interaction. Â Nothing. Â Also, no words spoken when he dropped off the check. Â Just plopped it down. Â Maybe thats the 'tude the place allows or encourages or thats just his personal style but when we drop good money for dinner, we need the whole package. Â Will we be back? Â Maybe. Â Probably not. Â NYC = Tons of options.

I liked this place. Cocktails were good, maracuja one was awesome with Tequila. Fresh juice was used. Food was fine too. No complains. I had the duck dish and I thought it tasted great. Red snapper cooked up/fried in plantains was dope too.

I'm a Prospect Heights native and a huge foodie with high expectations. I too was one that eagerly awaited Morimoto vet Jamison Blackenships creation and I have to tell everyone that it was worth the wait. Do try the fried oysters which are as succulent and tasty as the sauce. Also, the pork ramen in pork broth-is divine too fine a word? I'll just write delicious. Also, the pork gyoza were light yet full bodied in flavor, quite savory. Â My friend tried the chicken ramen dish with corn which I also tasted and you know what? I could feel the love that the chef put in to shaving the corn from the cob, it was sweet and crisp and just awesome. By the way, the decor is beautiful, its clean and refined and a compliment to the staff who may be many but are equally refined and friendly. Claire was especially outgoing and informative. Welcome to the neighborhood Chuko!

This review is almost entirely based on the service. The food was fine, but it was not nearly enough to overcome the service issues. First, we asked to sit in the back. When the host went to check for seats, we heard the waiter who was working the front section tell the host to lie and say there were no seats. Then we heard the waiter complain about how everyone wanted to sit in the back, and we were his only table. But somehow, despite having only one table, he still managed to total ignore us. I had to actually standup and waive my arms around like an idiot to get him to come over so we could order. This place must be fine normally based on all the other reviews, but if you walk in and happen to have a lanky guy with saggy jeans wait on you, just leave. He's bad enough that it will definitely ruin your experience.

Went here for brunch the other day and it was such a let down. The food was only so so and the service was even worse. The oyster appatizers was good but hard to eat. The eggs benidict was not great and while all the pictures show home fries it comes with salad (without dressing). The bill for two people was over $90 and i could have gotten the same bad food and worse service at a diner for $20. To be fair the atmosphere was cute and nothing was horrible, it just wasnt very good either.

I was there with a group of girlfriends. The big draw to this place is the big portions, which is great for sharing with friends. Do not get the frozen bellini, we did not think it had any alcohol. The staff was extremely friendly, the food is not great, but it's not bad neither.

I've walked by this place so many times and always see people waiting outside for seats. My girlfriend and I decided to try it out to see what all the hype was about. It's not a big restaurant, there are ~15-20 tables. We got here at 6:30pm and no wait for us, hooray!! I noticed that the line started shortly after we were seated though. We looked around to see what other people ordered and opted for the Prime rib-eye dinner - looks like that was the most popular dish. It comes with assorted vegetables which we both liked. We also had ice cream as desserts. The food was fresh and we enjoyed our meal. This place is cute and I guess there are not a lot of good shabu-shabu joints in the neighborhood, hence it's a hot spot - especially when it's cold out. My friend and I both felt that it's a tad overpriced, as we can go to Chinese hot pot for the same price with more food varieties. I may come back again if invited with friends to go.
Love it. Â Great, cheap, authentic pasta. Â Don't bother with anything in Little Italy.

A bit of a goat rodeo, but the old school feel and the fast service makes it totally worth navigating the crowds. I've been here a couple of times; the food is good overall...but the pancakes are amazing. So many varieties, and the three buttery sides make every bite an adventure. When friends are in town, we hit Tom's for good food, good value, good service and great atmosphere
Went back a 2nd time, better than the first. Â Cant get enough of that sauce.

Came here for a quick dinner before the opera. Â Staff was very nice to accommodate to our time constraint. Â Great atmosphere, cozy and fantastic food. Â Oysters were fresh and priced reasonably. Â New York strip was cooked perfectly and generously portioned. Â Striped bass was slightly overcooked. Â We had to skip on dessert. Â Great wine selection. Would definitely come back.

At 6 o'clock this place gets packed -- real fast. We ordered a variety of seafood to taste - clams, shrimp, lobster, crab, crawfish. The combo deals are the best because you also get the potatoes, corn and sausage. We've tried the Garlic Butter Sauce and O'Bay. I prefer the lighter garlic butter sauce. The clams in the garlic butter was delish! The catfish basket was great - juicy and tender. The cajun fries were okay, we got most of the burnt ends. It was good until you've had too much... the garlic taste just reeks in your mouth for days and looking back it just makes me nauseous. Your clothes will also smell for days, so beware! Service was a little disjointed, but that goes away when you start at your food. The place was modern and chill. I probably won't be back because of the high price tag for what it is worth. I was still hungry after all the food we ordered for 4 people.

A perfect late night eats spot. Open 24 hours, conveniently located, good food. We stopped in one night pretty late to get a snack before calling it a night. There is only enough room for maybe 15 people to sit comfortably inside but people are constantly coming and going for to go orders. It is very intimate, with dim lighting and flowers on each of the tables. We ordered: Plantain chips: I would take these over chips and salsa any day! The two sauces that come for everything is so so so tasty! The green sauce tasted like a spicy avocado sauce and the red was also spicy but with a tang. MMMMM YUM. Desayuno Colombiano: a breakfast one but served all day. Colombian sausage, cheddar cheese, eggs and Spanish onion. Super delicious and perfect with the green sauce. Hawaiian: pieces of ham with sautÃ©ed pineapples and mozzarella cheese, different but still good. The sweetness of the pineapple was nice. Cuban: slowly roasted pork, ham with mozzarella cheese and sofrito sauce. The favorite! Each empanada was around $3. I would say a tad on the expensive side because if you were really hungry, you might need like 5 of them. The menu has lots of other full entrees like stews, tamales, and meat and rice. Service was A-OK. They were very busy! All in all I would come back.

One of the best shabu places I've ever been to. Â The homemade gyoza had a great chewy texture which translated to fun and deliciousness. We had the pork tonsoku hotpot for 3 people. Â I don't even want to describe it...just go!

Best thai in the neighborhood! There's typically a wait and they don't take reservations, but it's worth the wait! Â Everything I've had there had been great! The food is not too heavy. The fried rice with lump crab meat and wok cashew nuts with shrimp were both tasty. It's definitely small, but totally worth sitting close to a few strangers for good food!
Meat in a ball, who would have thought. Â There is 4 per order but they are huge.

A lot has been written about Little Owl's food (which was great) so I would just like to add that what I really appreciated most about Little Owl was the lovely service and homey feel to the place. We'd been given an hour wait, so the girls and I walked around the neighborhood for a bit. Just as we were about to walk in and tell the maitre'd that he needn't call my cell as we'd be hanging out at the (cute!) bench out the door, maitre'd comes out and addresses me by name to tell me that we would be seated shortly. Granted it was a Monday night and it seemed quiet, but I didn't think he'd remember exactly who was waiting for the next table. He also gave us the option of squeezing in a 2-top, or wait for the 4-top, but the party in the 4-top apparently tends to linger. I think it says a lot about the place that they know their frequent visitors so well! Oh, and the arctic char and the halibut were great- well seasoned. The asparagus risotto was nice and light, great for an app, and my only complaint about the calamari was that I would have liked to have more of it. Mildly disappointed to discover they don't have the burger on the dinner menu, though. Truth be told, I had my heart set on it all day. Can't wait to go back! I'd love to have brunch here, too.

Despite wanting to offer 5 stars for the perfectly GF meal, the wide variety on the menu, the excellent ervice and the lovely room, this restaurant can be a heartbreaking experience for a celiac and I'd like to warn my fellow celiacs so none of them suffers the same kind of birthday disappointment I had this January. That's because, since Bistango bills itself as a certified GF restaurant and not just a restaurant with a GF menu, I assumed that I was going to a place where I would be able to eat everything on the menu. Not so. It's not just the fact that glutened items are available on the menu - that is good because it attracts non-GF friends and family. It was the fact that Â some of the most special menu items (black pasta, cavatelli) were available only to gluten eaters. I almost cried when I realized that if I wanted certain of the sauces, I'd have to forgo the black pasta and cavatelli for the same old GF penne readily available these days even at budget hotels. It stung that here were special old favorites offered only to gluten eaters here at "my" "gluten-free restaurant." Why couldn't they simply offer the same kind of gluten pasta -- penne -- to the "regular" eaters if they couldn't make it available to GF customers? Another disappointment was the extra two-dollar charge for a second teeny-tiny serving of unbelievably delicious GF bread when there was no charge for a second extra-large serving of regular gluten bread, and the higher prices on some menu items if you wanted it gluten-free (huh?). At the very least, they should set a "normal" menu price and "market" the gluten products as "available at a discount." I guess I was "being a baby," but I almost cried when I saw the $2 charge and that the main menu items were only available with penne. The only glitch in the service was the host, who was awkward with us (a brusque "Can I help you," as if he thought we'd wandered into the wrong joint when in fact we had reservations) and neglected to offer to hang our coats -- we struggled with them at the table thinking there was no coat check, and later we saw coats being brought out from the back.

A quite little place that I happened into on a lonely, rainy Saturday afternoon whilst wandering Williamsburg. I was pleased at how friendly the server was, and I suspect he may be the owner. He greeted another customer by name, which always warms my opinion of an establishment. I ordered a chai - non-sugary - and a muffin. The muffin was beautiful; it was dainty, moist, healthy and delicious. Seriously wonderful.
Abigail's margarita is insane. Their burger is great too. The vibe here is perfect.

I don't know why it took my friend from California to take ME here! I was glad she did. The food was amazing! The burger was SO good. And the shoestring fries! We also had the oysters and the devil's on horseback. The waiter was really good at making recommendations. Only went the one time for a late dinner but it was a good time. It was a little crowded, noisy and dark but other than that...super fun time. I don't drink so maybe I could not appreciate the alcohol part of it. Definitely worth checking out.

My boyfriend and I came here the other night, this is restaurant #2 on our quest for NY's best BBQ... cue epic music... The restaurant was much smaller than I expected and the signage was either discreet or non-existent as I hadn't realized we had arrived until I peeked through the front door. So pay attention to your Google Maps. There was a small bucket of beer in the front holding Shiner Bock, of which I am a fan. Though I think with the weather and the ice melting rapidly I noticed my first couple sips being room temp before getting to the icy cold part. A strange sensation and a mere minor offense. We decided to order: 1/2 lb. lean brisket, 1/2 lb. fatty brisket, 1/2 lb. pork ribs, coleslaw, bbq beans, and mac n cheese. When the platter arrived, it truly was a thing to behold. The mac n cheese blew me away, the jalapeÃ±o flavor was distinct and such a wonderful addition, I couldn't help myself and ate more than my share. Definitely some of the best mac n cheese I've ever had. The coleslaw was a beautiful purple color with shredded carrots atop. I thought it was lovely and really wish I'd enjoyed it, but unfortunately I'm just not a fan of mint in savory dishes. It tasted rather prominent to me and just makes me think of what it's like when you eat just after brushing your teeth. The beans were quite good. Pretty standard fare. Not stellar, but by all means not half bad either. They were tasty and filling, but a bit forgettable. The ribs though... the heavens parted and the angels sang and a light shined upon them. They were other-worldly!! The bark was crisp, the smoke ring was dense, the meat was tender. Definitely the star of the show, despite the restaurant name. The brisket was delicious and you could clearly see the smoke ring deep into the meat. I think we'd definitely ordered too much though and we're unable to eat it all. The meat was sliced thick and so tender it was a challenge to even pick it up with a fork! I think for my personal taste though, the lean brisket was better than the fatty. Normally I prefer fatty brisket, but when the meat is cut as thick as this the fat becomes too much for me. I wish I could've reviewed a dessert, but alas we stuffed ourselves so full we couldn't even attempt it! I think a pound of meat for 2 people next time will be plenty. All in all, I think it was a phenomenal meal. Even the sliced white bread served with dinner was more complex than it appeared and flavorful. I was totally shocked that by 9pm the place had pretty well cleared out and the restaurant was left with only a few tables. A place like this definitely warrants a packed house We'll DEFINITELY be back for the ribs (!!!), lean brisket, and the mac n cheese. So far this is my favorite BBQ in NY, though it will be interesting to see how it holds its place as we visit the next contender. (I'm taking this NYC BBQ trial very seriously.)

I went there for brunch recently after hearing they had a new chef and was very pleasantly surprised. We were welcomed and did not have to wait long at all (unusual in the Village) despite the great atmosphere and -- as it turns out -- excellent food (and Bloody Mary's!). Â I had a perfect New York restaurant moment, and I plan on being a regular.

After a long night of partying and debauchery, I awoke around 2.30 pm with friends at my apartment and growling stomachs. Â Rather than make anything, we decided to try out Wolfnights. Â It was amazing. The wrap I had, the Brothers Grimm, was a fabulous concoction on a fabulous fresh wrap. Â I loved the plantain chips that were inside - added a great crunch! Â Everything is apparently 100% natural, and I'm now quite glad I have a good-for-you alternative to visit at around 4:30pm. Â I can't say for sure about the other wraps, but my friend said the Teen Wolf was falafel at a high point. Â Try a Wolf Attack. Â Just do it. It looks somewhat like halal, but tastes a million times better. Wishing I could have eaten on one of those swinging chairs. Â It's a tight fit for this joint (15 seats in the whole place, max!), but it's so worth it. Can't wait to make this a weekly thing!

Ok this place is simply amazing. Â A co-worker suggested this place and said it was some of the best spaghetti she had had in NYC. Â It's a great location in the middle of the meatpacking district and the interior was pretty nice. Â It's a good thing we came early as the main dining room was for reservations only. Every single item we had was great to AMAZING; Heirloom tomatoes & burratta - So creamy and delicious. Spaghetti - Simple but perfectly prepared. Â I don't think you can get a better bowl of this outside Italy. Duck & Foie Gras Ravioli - So rich and decadent. Â The sauce and fillings are both so tasty - I highly recommend. Coconut Panna Cotta - OMFG!! Â WTF!!! Â As awesome as dinner was, this dessert was easily the best dish of the night. Â Note: Â I don't like sweets! Â I don't eat dessert! Â My friend ordered this and insisted I taste it. Â Seriously it's effing AMAZING! Â I would come back here and just order this, it's that good. Easily 5 stars considering every dish we had was stellar.

Still don't understand why people won't go to the third cart.... I asked the guys at the cart why there was no line at their cart, and they simply said, "that one was the original." Â Fine by me! Â I'd rather not wait in a long line for good quality food!

I went here for dinner a couple weeks ago and loved it! Upon arriving, the host said there would be a 20 min wait. However, our party of 3 was seated only about 5 mins later. The menu had a lot of interesting burger options, such as ostrich, wild hog, and buffalo. However, we all opted for the more traditional meats: beef and turkey. The burger I had was fantastic, to say the least. I also really enjoyed the fries. Overall, it was a delicious and reasonably priced dinner. I will definitely be back!

Was here two times about a month and a half ago and there was a manager speaking in a really uncomfortable way to a staff member both times. Couldn't tell what it was about but she was killing the vibe--which is decent but not great. Above average food but drinks so-so. Decent place to go if it's not busy but unprofessional staff interactions are not the highbrow ambience this place is looking for.

What a great find! Thank you Yelpers! Cute and Cozy. Food is Delicious!! Portions are grand, french fries will definitely linger on your plate after. The menu is full of variety, but not at all overwhelming. Service was fast and friendly. Prices are unbeatable for this area and the quality! I went with the yelp reviews and ordered the turkey burger on a Portuguese roll, which was very tasty! The only drawback was the seating which was a little tight when getting into a chair, once you were seated it was fine, and comfortable. The restaurant was busy for a Friday afternoon. I'm going back to try more dishes soon and the minty lemonade!

Personally, the food is not that great. Now when i go there i only order the bbq fries and some wings. Also, I find the bruncht menu pricey, considering the portion size. The staff there is very friendly however the service is very slow.

It's the best neighborhood diner I could have ever asked for. Â Genuinely friendly waitresses, delicious, fresh-tasting food, and extremely reasonable prices made this a spot to go alone late on a weeknight, or with friends on the weekend. Â Don't disappoint yourself and try and go on a Sunday, though...they're closed. Â I really miss Mooncake Foods now that I've moved away :(

Stopped at the Brickyard for a quick bite and a drink last Friday night before seeing Cabaret. Â Happy hour was going on in the front bar, but there was plenty of room in the back dining room area. Â Very friendly and accommodating staff (we were on a time constraint). Decent beer selection, but nothing on tap that would be considered a rare beer. Â We ordered the Philly Cheesesteak Spring rolls and the Steak Frites. Â The Cheesesteak Spring Rolls were some of the best I've had, and I always order them when they are on the menu. Â We also ordered a Caesar salad which was WAY over dressed, picture drenched soggy lettuce. Overall, great for a quick bite. Â Stay away from the salad or else order dressing on the side. Â If you are looking for rare beers, you might want to try another place. Â Overall, we enjoyed our experience,

it has been almost a year since my return to saigon shack. but the restaurant has remained the same with their service and food. i think one of the best joys in my life is when i share delicious food with others, in addition to their happy reactions to the foods i introduce them to. pho is good any day, but especially on a cold day (or a rainy day..or a sunny day..) got the saigon pho (thinly sliced beef, beef balls, brisket, flat noodles, cilantro, basil, scallions, bean sprout, hoisin sauce) for $8-9, which comes with another small dish with lemon, lime, bean sprouts, basil, and peppers as toppings to add to your liking. other pho restaurants also have large portions and good prices, but i prefer saigon shack b/c the broth is much clearer and less oily than other pho restaurants. the noodle doesn't take up the entire space of the bowl- there is plenty of meat! the warm, perfectly seasoned broth warms your whole body and you feel stronger to withstand against this cold winter! i have to try their banh mi sandwiches. soooooooon.
TWO SNAPS UP! Sweet and sassy blue collar boys running this joint, they are adorbs! ...and the pizza is delish!

Just had Peppino's for the first time, I'm ashamed to say. I've lived right next door to the place and have never been over there until tonight, but it was really good pizza. I had a pizza with tomato sauce, garlic, basil and capers (no cheese) and it was awesome.. can't wait to try the others. I got the small, which is 6 slices and I usually can put away a lot of food (see photo) but only ate half, all for $10. I will be stopping in for a full dinner one of these nights instead of just getting to go food - looked cool inside and a great neighborhood spot.

Love this place. Â Also helps that I only live 2 minutes away. Â This place is open at 7:30 AM.. which also means that I have to take lunch orders from the crew in the morning. Â "2 #1's, 3 #8's, 1 #11, 10 spring rolls, 5 coconut juice..." Â yea... it gets that crazy. Â Cheap and delish. Â Beats paying the midtown $$ for Ma Pache.

Thumbs up if you are considering this early in the morning. Â But if you're going during peek hours, I would think twice in the extreme winter. Nook is very small, but it is that perfectly cute type of place that appeals to NYCers. Â There is really only enough room for the diners and the waiter to walk through the tables. Â When they are at capacity, you must wait outside. Â  The service is delightful. Â I am amazed that this one guy can service nearly 10 tables. He definitely has a very specific system and it works marvelously. Â I think it's pretty amazing that they are so busy and capable that they will even recommend to folks with large groups a restaurant down the street, rather than rudely have them wait forever. Â  As for the food, you can't go wrong. Â We had the eggs Benedict and one of the popular scrambles. Â Both were perfect brunch type fair. Â  All and all an enjoyable experience.

Becco is my go-to theater district spot. It's fairly reliable to get a reservation as long as you call a day or two in advance and they have something for everyone. The $25 bottles of wine are a great deal. I've discovered some great wines that I otherwise wouldn't have ordered. The all you can eat pasta is a real crowd-pleaser. They always have three different types of pasta and the servers come around with pans of each one every few minutes offering you more. It also comes with either a great Cesar salad or antipasti appetizer. Only issue is that it attracts some loud out-of-towners, but that's to be expected in this neck of the woods. If you're seeing a show, this is a great spot!

Yes, this place is technically "closed" because they don't offer a sit-down service and they only do take-out through seamless. HOWEVER. Don't let that stop you from ordering on seamless. Their sandwiches are delicious and are familiar yet innovative at the same time. The Classic Roast Beef Panini was amazing, with homemade horseradish, muenster, and cilantro. My friend had the Cubano, which had banana peppers and (also) cilantro. They were both amazing. Also, the staff are extremely friendly and pleasant. So, no, you can't walk in, order off a menu, pay with cash, and sit down. BUT, you can pull up seamless on your food, order there, and take this fantastic food outside to the many parks, benches, etc., in Fi-Di and enjoy some awesome sandwiches.

Life in the east village can be fun, but many of the restaurants in the area are appealing to people who've come to drink, date, or party. That is to say, if the food is good, it's salty, expensive, and served in the sort of place you don't feel like you belong sitting there eating on your own. And the places where you do feel ok flying solo tend to have very unhealthy food. So I have been searching for a while to find a low key place that serves delicious food at a reasonable price. Gaia is an excellent choice. On the south side of Houston street, it's a little tricky to find; you have to go down a set of stairs into a small, bright, cozy place.. There are recent magazines visible under the half dozen glass topped tables. It's the kind of place you might go to meet a friend or to eat on your own. If it's busy, you may end up sharing a table. I had the lasagna and a fresh pear juice. The pasta comes in a vintage steel tin to keep the food warm. Nicely spiced, filling without being overwhelming, and so comforting. This is simple, delicious, nourishing food and it feels like you're eating at the house of a friend. The decor is nothing special, but the relaxed and friendly vibe of the owner and waitress more than make up for it. You will feel very welcome here. Finally, the prices are very reasonable. $7 will get you lasagna that you could easily pay $15 for a few blocks away at Pulino's. It tastes better and is likely better for you at Gaia. Highly recommended.

I have been avoiding this place like the plague. I hate crowds -- especially when that crowd is the only thing between me and thin crust pizza. My friend wanted to eat here for lunch on the Sunday of NYE weekend. Great. But it was surprisingly/ridiculously empty! Tip: Come before 1PM if you want to have a chance of no lines. When we left, the line was out of the door. Is 12PM not a realistic lunch time? I don't understand people. We were ravenous so we ordered two whole pies. The waitress was a little wary -- considering we're two small Asian girls. But we finished it. It definitely was a struggle, though. I recommend getting both the white pizza and the original - they balance each other out quite well. Italian sausage and panchetta toppings were legit.

I've been to just about very Smith location and can't think of a single time that I've been disappointed with food or service. Â Always very solid on both fronts. Â Noise level is the only thing I would point to but I have never seen it as overly problematic. Â This is my standard go-to for lunch and dinner with friends.

Huge place! We were able to get a table for 8 on a Friday night. Great service and delicious food and drinks. The wings which everyone has raved about here were not all that but the chicken liver pate was fantastic. The duck n waffles were incredible and so were the ribs. The Franklin burger, although uninventive and pretty standard, was cooked to perfection. The desserts didn't sound as great, so we skipped them.

I was super excited to try this place after hearing about their "secret menu" item and this place somewhat met my expectations although I have to say that their portions are pretty small for the prices the restaurant is charging. Â Due to the hype that this restaurant has gotten, expect to wait for your table even if you have a reservation and once you get to your table, also expect to wait for your food because of their "small kitchen." Â  The good: this restaurant has pretty awesome food made with the freshest of ingredients and cooked to utmost perfection. Â The chef and his staff pay a great deal of attention to the way the food is prepared and presented and the chef does amazingly different things with the same ingredient in 1 dish to show you how many different ways the ingredient can be cooked,which showcases the many facets of the ingredient itself. Â For example, we had the tuna appetizer and in it, the chef prepared beets in 3 or 4 different ways and each method that was used to prepare the beet made it taste wonderfully different from the others. Â The pickled beets were of course sour and savory while the dried beets sprinkled on top were surprisingly sweet. Â This is done with several dishes throughout the menu. Â  The monkey bread is definitely a must (and this is coming from a person who hates bread). Â It was warm and soft and super buttery. Â We also had the scallops which were pretty tasty too but nothing that struck me as wow that was amazing. Â I enjoyed the tuna more than the scallops. Â Now for what we really came here for, the Dry Aged CÃ´te de Boeuf. Â This dish was amazing!!! Â Even though this place isn't a steak house, it beats many of the steak houses I've been to in this city. Â My Dry Aged CÃ´te de Boeuf was waaaay better than the steak I had at Peter Lugers. Â The chef made this steak a delicious piece of heave. Â I was thoroughly happy with this dish, although it was the priciest steak I've ever eaten. Â Also the little potato balls that accompanied the steak were so delicious that I couldn't stop eating them even though I was painfully full from the steak. Â The little balls of golden joy were seasoned perfected and more importantly cooked perfectly. Â I couldn't have asked for anything better. So after my heavenly steak, why did I give this place only a 4? Â Well other than the over-pricing of the dishes, I was pretty disappointed with their wine selection. Â If you're going to offer this incredibly up-scale dining experience, you should at least have the wine to accompany the outstanding food. Â When I asked for a Shiraz like wine or a Cab like wine, I was really disappointed when the waiter came back with a dry red that was far from what I asked for. Â It was either that or a full-bodied red, which I thought was very strange. Â Other than that, this place definitely impressed.

One of my favorite brunch places here in nyc hands down. I usually come here just for the delicious Chicken and Ube Waffles. However, recently they have added a variation of dishes to their brunch menu. Between four people we had the Sisig, Eggs Benigno, Chicken and Ube Waffle, and the Mango Stuffed French Toast. Everything was amazing, my favorite dishes has to be the Sisig and Chicken and Ube Waffles. I love the hip ambiance of this place and the wait staff t-shirts with sayings like "My Bestfriend is Filipino" too cute. I'll be back next time I'm in nyc again!

Always busy and there's usually a wait, but the food is worth it. Â I love the pollo mirador. Â It's a limey garlicky chicken concoction served with yellow rice and spinach. Â The corn also never disappoints. My boyfriend loves the Cuban sandwich. Â Actually, the thought of how delicious the food is supercedes my need to hibernate during this frigid New York winter and motivates me to make the trek to Nolita. Â  I am putting on shoes and puffy jacket to head down now!

This place is the classiest, most elegant Korean restaurant you will find in NYC, no question. We came here to celebrate a birthday, and they made it a point to acknowledge it on multiple occasions and in multiple ways. You have the choice here of doing either a tasting menu, or creating your own tasting a la carte, which is what we opted for. They started us off with an amuse bouche plate of a clam soup, an eel cigar, some Korean fried chicken, and an oyster purÃ©e of sorts. The clam foam soup was really nice. Little smokey, little clammy, and light and creamy. The eel cigar was light and crunchy, but very neutral. The fried chicken was crispy and light, and served on a dollop of a spicy aioli. The oyster purÃ©ed was good, and neutral as well. Nice start to the meal. From there we went on to the octopus and the fried oyster. The octopus was tender and tasty, and came along with another aioli. Fried oysters were a little on the fishy side, and I wasn't wild about them. They were very crispy and, like the octopus and the chicken, came on an aioli. It is a heavy dish to be sure. At this point, we've seen the aioli show up a few times, and this becomes the theme of the night. T! we did the yellowtail rice and the pork belly rice. The yellowtail was seared a little more than I cared for, but the dish was very fragrant. The pork belly rice came doused in, you guessed it, aioli! There was plenty of delicious, tender pork belly, but between the pork and the aioli, it was almost too heavy to eat. The next dish was the red snapper with crispy scales. This dish was a solid piece, with the exceptions of the dollops of green aioli on it! The broth is clean and light, and the fish, perfectly cooked. As a special birthday treat, they brought out their take on a Korean porridge dish that is eaten on a persons birthday, which was a really nice touch. For our meats, we went with the duck and the jungsik steak. The duck was nice, but nothing you haven't had elsewhere. No, the steak... Of the steak. Best steak I have had anywhere, hands down. You pay $50 for maybe 4 ounces of meat, and it is worth every penny. It is super flavorful and melty, yet meaty. Amazing. Get this if you come here. If you don't, you might as well not bother coming. This is the best thing here. If you couldn't tell, I liked it. To end the night, we were given a copy of the menu with a special birthday message on it, a very nice touch. Overall, the meal came out to about $250ish before tip. Overall, I found most of the meal to be very heavy, and the aioli is way overused. That being said, the place is super elegant, service is really impeccable, and the steak was insanely good. I do recommend it for an occasion, but be warned of the heavy dishes.
This place has done everything right. Food is very tasty without being laden with truffle oil. I can tell everything is fresh. The staff is on point. Great atmosphere. Favorite NYC spot so far.

If it weren't for that new Cooking Channel, I may not have ever heard of Fette Sau. Â Luckily for me, I did see a show that profiled the restaurant, and my friend happened to see the same show and mentioned going there since she lived kind of close. I don't really hang out too often in Williamsburg-- so I didn't know where I was going. Â Good thing I had that Yelp app on my phone to tell me how to get there. Â Yeah, i just plugged the Yelp app... and what? Â But I may not have needed it because while walking down Metropolitan Avenue, I took a few sniffs of the air (a la Wolverine from X-men) and I just followed the scent. Â  Anyway, we met up around 5:30 because it opens at 5 and (1) we wanted to beat the crowd; (2) we had somewhere to be later that night so it worked out. Â I'm glad we got there as early as we did. Â Not only do we get some of the freshest cuts of the day, it's all communal seating--first come, first serve-- so it can be tough to get a seat. Â  But it also helps to know what to expect once you get there. The first thing you should do when you walk in is check out the menu and see what delicious cut of meat they have because they only feature six types per day. Once you've made your decision, the butcher will ask you what you'd like and he'll lay down this metal tray on a scale, almost precisely pile on what you wanted and that tray becomes your plate. Â Knowing this will at least shave off a few precious minutes and the people behind you on line may appreciate it. Well, now on to the juicy stuff-- the food! Â O. M. G. Â The barbecue is some of the best I've ever had. Â I love the dry rub on the meat--not only does it add a ton of flavor, but it also adds a really nice crisp, unlike some of the wet rubs. Â The brisket was so tender, the pulled pork was good, but my favorite was the pork belly. Â It was like heaven in my mouth. Â We also got the potato salad, which was more vinegar-based-- i prefer the mayonnaise-based salad-- but it was still pretty good. Next time I plan on making my way down to Fette Sau, I'm going to call in advance to see what they have on the menu. Â I was really looking forward to trying the cheeks, but I was disappointed that they weren't serving those on the day i went. Â I also want to try to the beer next time-- those glasses looked pretty cool and the taps using kitchen utensils was unique. Â I can't wait for next time now.

The broth for the beef noodle soup was watery and lacking in heartiness. The noodles had the needed qq bounce. The meat that was in the noodles was tender and flavored just right. The fujianese wonton soup had this light but hearty broth. The umami flavor was delicious and just warmed you right up. The dumplings were heavy handed on the chives and skin is thinner compared to other dumpling places. They are also sweeter.
Fun atmosphere. Great service. Amazing food. Get the kimchi pancake. You won't regret it!
There is nothing new for me to say that hasn't been said already. Everything about this place is amazing!

We were visiting the East Side Tenement museum and we were there way early before out tour started & we asked where was a good place for breakfast. Â Dudleys was less than a block away. Nice little place, a bit more than a handful of tables. Â We were there late morning and wanted something to hold us over before lunch. There were only a few customers and the wait staff was friendly & super attentive. Â  We had: Buttered Avocado on toast, tomato's & fried egg - 10 - this dish rocked. Â You wouldn't think Avocado on toast with some tomato's would be much to rave about (especially for 10 bucks) but it was. Â Awesome bread, fresh veggies and the egg on top came together perfectly. Â More than a few bite snack and less than a lunch - just what we were looking for. Wild mushrooms, home made ricotta & roasted mushrooms, lemons & herbs - 10 - again, this dish rocked. Â Bread - home/artisan made I would suspect, the homemade ricotta & roasted mushrooms - awesome! Â  Recommend - yes. Â Its unfortunate that we won't be able to check this place out again for lunch or dinner on our trip.

TimeOut Shortlist New York 2012 recommended this restaurant, so we had brunch on Father's Day. Â It's MICHELIN guide 2011 Recommended so our expectations were appropriately based. Â The wait staff at our table had no idea how to interact with customers apparently, because we were treated as if we were peasants who had no idea of what the simple menu items were. Â This person overstepped the boundaries of a waitperson and even patted me on the back on one point! Â The food is WAY over priced and severely lacked sophistication. Â Lastly, it's almost impossible to have a conversation with the deafening level of noise with sound with everyone's voices reverberating off all the hard services. If you're in the mood for French food, do yourself a favor and visit Artisanal Fromagerie and Bistro in NYC instead.

Full disclosure: I watched Harold's run through Top Chef and have been following his trails to get here since that season ended. So we came here for a birthday dinner (it was at 6pm, I got reservations way to close to the day, but that is my fault), it was a nice day outside so the front doors were open and the fans were on, it was very comfortable inside. Â There are only about 20 tables in the restaurant, with a few of them being 'booths'. Â There is no fu-fu garnish in any of the dishes, your plates should go back totally empty. The menu is very refined (8 first courses and 8 main courses), and everything was very well presented. Â The waiter was very good, attentive and laid back. Â On previous recommendations we got the spicy duck meatballs and the sea scallops, they knew we were sharing them, so they brought them out on 2 plates which was nice. Â The meatballs were fantastic, and the scallops cooked very well, the meatballs win though. Â Maybe because there were more, maybe because I have been talking about them since I left, not sure. For the main courses there was a John Dory special that was very nice, and a wild boar chop. Â The fish was cooked perfectly, and the sauces was delightful, and the portions were very good. Â The wild boar was roughly 10" circle of boar on the bone. Â There was a very good breading, panko and good flavor, with greens on the top. Â The vinegarette soaked into the boar and made it even better. Â This is a hard choice, but I go with the boar, no the fish, I can not decide, they were both good. Now there are carnivores, omnivores, but I think that I am a desertavore myself. Â I really do love desert. Â So we had the apple and raisin crisp, served in the pan, and the dark chocolate tart. Â The tart was good, rich, deep, refreshing, very easy to eat despite the amount already consumed; but the apple crisp was amazing. Â I don't know how something that simple could be that good. Â We really enjoyed it. Â A lot. Â The peppermint ice cream was divine, as well as the vanilla, very strong flavors in a small little package.
