This was a very good birthday meal, I would give it my full endorsement. Â I watched as everybody's food as it came out, and it all looked good. Â It is expensive, but what do you expect. The restrooms are two little private rooms in the back, decor carried through them, clean and stocked. Â Sinks difficult to use a bit, but an overall good experience, 4.25 Flushes

Ate here in the dining room in early December with a friend. Food was good. Not the best I've had for that price range but still enjoyable. Service was perfect, never without bread or water. Ambiance is what you would expect from this kind of restaurant, couples and business professionals, not too loud not quiet, and nice but fun. Lighting was good, I didn't have a flash on my camera but was still able to take pretty decent pictures of my food. (what do you expect? I'm asian, that's what we do!) My favorite dish was the smoked trout. The rest was good to okay, but if I can't remember them then were they really that good? In any case, the experience was nice and I think next time I would do the bar so I can just order one good dish instead of the 5 course.
Always first place we bring people when we visit. Service is top notch and the food is just as good. Whether it's pizza, calzone or the dessert calzone it's always delicious.

yum! I love me some bbq! Â We sampled most of the meats. Â We had the end piece of the St. Louis ribs and it was overly charred and dry. Â Pulled pork was eh. Â But the boneless beef ribs and brisket was delicious. Â Moist and seasoned, but not salty.
awesome brunch place in west village.

Five dumplings for $1- not much to complain about. Â I tried to do a mini taste test in the surrounding blocks between the dumpling places- I lined these ones up next to the ones from fried Dumpling on Allen Street and I have to say I prefer the ones from Â Prosperity. Â Fresh although a bit oily. Â I did get stomach cramps once but maybe that's because I gobbled down 15 in a matter of minutes... I don't think the place looks that clean and it's not very inviting nor convenient. Â But if you're on the LES and want a good deal on dumplings I would recommend this spot in a heartbeat.

Jamon Serrano was served cold when it's much better at room temp. The quality was also not very good. Â Polpo was tasty though. Â Not bad overall but vie had much better tapas in NYC for much less money

I've been here twice for lunch in the past month. The first time it took over 2 HOURS to get my food. I wouldn't believe it if it didn't happen to me. The second time it took 45 minutes to get a burger. Awful.

Atmosphere is great for a date. Tables are a little too close together but there's always a wait so it would just be worst if they weren't. No place for waiting so probably good idea to make a reservation.

Went to Cha-An on a whim after getting some okonomiyaki next door. My boyfriend and I went for tea and dessert. You go upstairs and suddenly you are in Japan. The decor it very traditional and calming, but also very chic. They have a very extensive tea list as well as some very upscale food items and desserts. They have a daily creme brulee. It was Earl Grey Â the day I went but we ended up getting something else. It took 5-10 min for a server to come and actually give us a menu to look at. But once we got our tea the service picked up. They offered us more hot water for our tea pot twice. Oh also there is an awesome electric Japanese toilet in the Â girls bathroom. Love it! Overall Cha-An was a lovely experience. Domo Arigatou Gozaimasu!

We ventured to the shake shack mid afternoon for some lunch. The smokeshack burger was awesome. The cheese fries were ok. Seemed like an out of the jar cheese than what I'd prefer. We each had a shake, the mr. had the Wall Street shake which he said was good, not great. I had the lower east side which was really good. We ended up sitting outside and waited a bit for our food. Overall, would eat there again.
Great dinner with great service. Party of eleven and everyone loved what they ordered. It was one of the best Pad Thai's I've had in a long time. Will defiantly go there again.

There is always a long line for brunch at Cafe Orlin, which is overly hyped, in my opinion. The food is decent, but it's definitely not worth the 30+ minute wait on a Sunday morning/afternoon when you are hungry and just want some food in your stomach. The first and last time I was here, I got their famous Pumpkin pancakes topped with cinnamon yogurt. The first couple bites were delicious, although it needed a bit more pumpkin flavors. After a while, though, the pancakes tasted slightly undercooked and I felt a bit nauseous. The texture was a little off too - some bites were wet, while others were overly fluffy. My mom got the Brunch Specials of Eggs Norwegian, which included fresh orange juice (tasted good) and a choice of coffee or tea. The eggs benedict, topped with smoked salmon, poached eggs, and hollandaise sauce on top of English muffin, was nothing special. Just tasted like any other Eggs Benedict.
Cheap? Yes. Tasty? No. Many better options in surrounding area. Don't believe the hype.

Had reservations for 6 on a Saturday got there about 20 mins early and got seated right away because the restaurant was empty. Next thing I know I look up from the menu and it was packed. I ordered a special which was technically an app but asked if I could have it as an entree and it wasn't a problem. It was spinach and ricotta gnudi (which is almost like gnocchi but no potatoes figure it's like the stuffing of a ravioli) it was served in a sage butter sauce and topped with parmesan cheese. It was so yummy, it was rich from the cheese and also salty (in a good way) I sopped up the rest of the sauce with the bread from the table. The portions here are satisfying but not a lot don't expect to be asking for a doggy bag because I guarantee you'll finish everything. The branzino was good but very very boney(even after they took out the bones) so if you don't feel like digging around in your mouth with your fingers to take out the bones I would suggest you get something else like maybe the short ribs. I got the chocolate cake for dessert with ice cream it was ok. The cheesecake was killer it was ricotta cheesecake but was super creamy and tasted more like a New York style cheesecake so if you are looking for a traditional Italian style don't get it BUT if you like any kind of cheesecake get it !! Decent size slice too. Waitress was very friendly and explained everything on the menu well. Bathroom was clean also. Minus one star for the restaurant being extremely dark, tight seating and noise level.

Came here for Summer 2013 restaurant week. Service is just ok. Our waitress refused to split the check even we told her we will have three bills in the really beginning. the tip is granted for 20% automatically - Â we have 6 people. So instead of that we have to calculate how much on each bill, and she didn't even say sorry about that. The dinning room is dark, loud and really crowed. They don't serve any bread/chips and the portion is really little. Hard to get full. We had following stuff: -Fish Tacos -Sea Bass Chorillana -Skirt steak -Paella -Tuna tartar -Beef short ribs -Orange Crepas -Lemongrass Flan There are not too many choices for restaurant week menu. So we end up ordering from the regular menu. Â I like the fish tacos and the Paella.

One of the best croque madames i've ever had (Paris included!). The bread is crispy enough for the egg to not render it as pulp, and the cheese was flavorful without being terribly overwhelming. I've been a couple of times now, once for a late breakfast and the other for lunch. The first time I came I got the french toast, which was thick and delicious though a bit sweet. I kind of take the blame for that last one though as I definitely poured too much syrup. When I asked if they had a syringe for the syrup so I could inject it right into my veins they looked at me strangely. Four stars for the service being a bit spotty... in such a small space you'd expect to get noticed every once in a while.
I had the chicken liver toast and the delicious burger medium well. The food and drinks were delicious. The customer service can use some improvement.

Terrific ambiance, friendly and welcoming service, and all the drinks and appetizers we had at our table of 6 were excellent. We especially liked the empanadas and lobster taquitos, but everything was very enjoyable. We'll be back!
Best coffee shop and smoothie bar in the neighborhood.

After a lackluster experience at the Nacional, we headed over to Las Ramblas to kick things up. Â Amazingly, we were able to get 10 people into the bar (I guess good fortune going on the 4th weekend)... Â We ordered about 10 porrons (you got to get a porron - it looks like a bong but is for sharing wine/cava/etc in a crazy messy fun way) and all kinds of great flavors - the pear and strawberry definitely were huge hits. Â The food as usual was delicious, and the service is with these tremendous smles. Â  My wife was trying out the various sherries, and the bartender who was being super helpful for being so busy, even comp'd her when he recommended one she didnt like. Â Speaking of comps, they threw in 2 free dessert porrons at the end of the night - at which point I did a double :) If they opened up in a bigger spot, I would DEFINITELY be there more often with big groups. Â So much fun! PS - a hint, if you go for the porron (oh you got to!), you may not want to be wearing something that wine stains will ruin. Â Almost certainly you'll spill a little until you get the hang of it.

I was looking forward to dining here for a while. Â I have heard only the best things about this place. Â  PROS: Â  Hostess was very welcoming and super helpful - she was great! Â  The Upstairs Bartender & Raw Bar Chef were extremely friendly and knowledgeable - very impressed with those two. The Mulled Wine was out of this world!!! The Bussers had a great attitude and were friendly! Decor strikes an interesting balance between super cute and hipster grandma kitch. Great Beer selection as well! This place is a very cool spot - the ambiance was very cool and crowded. CONS: Manager was extremely busy, hence the dismissive attitude is to be expected? Our waiter had a polite disdain for us. Â  The food was decent but not amazing - Â as we had expected for the price of the menu. Apparently here the price does not equal quality. The bread was burned...when we asked for some more it was also burnt Â - Â is that a "thing" now? Also - be prepared to wait a loooong time unless you come during off times.
Best brunch spot around. Be prepared to wait if you go on peak hangover recovery time as the place gets super crowded. Once you get in you will see why they love it. Go here it's worth it.

5 because i don't know any place that tops this one. Â I know Bourdain came here, but who cares, they didn't need him to get the official "it's great." Â Actually he didn't do me a favor by coming here...Now it's always packed!! Â Seriously though - Bourdain is the man! Â I'm a fan of him too! Â  Ok back to the review, has high quality food, great variety, great selection of alcohol, decent wait staff (defensive), and decent value (you are close to times square, it's supposed to be expensive).

I recently traveled around Spain, but had yet to experience an authentic tapas experience in the US...until I visited Boqueria that is. Â Upon entering the relaxed tapas bar, I looked to my left and noticed that the long hostess counter was adorned to look like a mini tapas bar displaying platters of tortillas and other traditional dishes. Â I began oohhing and aahing with excitement as my Spanish memories came flooding back to me. Â I pulled my tongue back into my mouth and joined my coworkers at one of the high tables overlooking the open the kitchen. Â We had a tough time deciding what to share, because everything coming out of the kitchen looked amazingly authentic. Â  We finally decided on the paella and several smaller plates. Â The Espinacas a la Catalana was a plate of sautÃ©ed spinach, garbanzo beans, pine nuts, garlic, and raisins. Â The mix was definitely Mediterranean - something I would have expected to find on a Greek menu more than a Spanish one. Â I am not usually a spinach fan, but the garlic and raisins added such contrasting and interesting flavors to this leafy green. Â It was love at first bite. Â The Brandada de Bacalao was in true tapas style, meaning there were round pieces of toasted baguette topped with the whipped cod. Â Most tapas tastings around Spain include something over a slice of bread, which helps fill you up before you gouge yourself sampling the entire spread (well, at least it does most of the time, lol). Â The Bikini de Tres Quesos was a delectably greasy grilled cheese panini filled with MahÃ³n , IdiazÃ¡bal and Manchego cheeses and marinated tomatoes. Â The crisp multi-grain sandwich was served with a small portion of spiced Patatas Bravas (roasted potatoes with garlic and chili oil) and a side salad. Â I absolutely love the Basque IdiazÃ¡bal cheese, which is rarely on menus here, so this was a thrill for me. Â Lastly, the Paella Valenciana was the traditionally large crisp pot of rice, prawns, mussels, clams, cockles, chorizo, and shredded chicken. Â The chicken was extremely tender, the chorizo packed with flavorful spice, and the shellfish bursting with freshness. Â The dish itself was a bit oily or buttery or something, but I still enjoyed it. Â I have been to several Spanish restaurants were I have suffered through dry rice, so I definitely preferred this. We were all satisfied with the reasonable prices and friendly service. Â  I cannot wait to return and sample the rest of the menu.

inconsistency at its best. Â Sometimes 5 stars; sometimes 0. Â Put some meat on your stuff that says it has meat. Â Atleast try to send it warm. Â Order somewhere else in desperation, this place is ok if youre willing to roll the dice.

Came here with my family to celebrate my birthday and boy was I happy that we did! I have to admit that this was our second choice for a restaurant. Our first choice had a one hour and 45 minute wait. Sunday night at 6:30... really?? Oh well. So the five of us walk into Miriam's and no wait for a table. Yeah! Pleasant and happy servers greet us with smiles. Even the bartender nodded. We got a great both in the back corner and loved the adorable ambiance throughout! We were all totally happy with what we ordered. I loved my pear salad! It was large enough for two to share. I don't agree with some of the other reviews that said the food was tasteless. I ordered the four small plates for $12 and felt as though each one was perfect and complimented each other with just the right spices and flavors. Overall, I was thrilled! I was a great dining experience and I will definitely be coming back!!

Excellent service. We called to make a reservation, but were told no tables were available all night. But, we were told to check back at 5 p.m. to see if there was a cancellation. Sure enough, we got a table at 9:30 and proceeded to have the most bitchin roast chicken ever. The atmosphere is great and lively, and the table staff are real professionals. I'm just sad we don't live closer so I could dine here more often!

i have been going to Natureworks since they first openes and I've always enjoyed the service and their food. Almost everyone who I work with that goes to the gym eats here. Â The evas omelete starts off my day full of energy and I end it with a high protein vegetarian salad with a side of Â my favorite sauce tahini! I will continue to order from this place, I'm always completely satisfied with everything.

Bummer. Â I returned this past weekend to show some out-of-towners a great time, but unfortunately, Fukurou has changed since its openings. First, fried chicken gizzards are no longer on the menu. Â Was not happy with that because they are simply not easy to come by in the village. Â There were a few other changes from the original menu but this was the biggest loss for me. Second, and this one is egregious, Fukurou is now imposing a minimum drink order. Â What?! Â Is this an entry fee to eat? Â Has my lovely little neighborhood gem turned into a pretentious NYC nightclub? Â The worst part is that the cocktails were not the least bit impressive, and non-alcoholic beverages in tiny little cups were $4 apiece. Â It's not so unusual for me to have a cocktail or beverage with dinner, but a mandatory drink is pretty ridiculous. Â Sure, I'd stop by for the mackerel roll or the yellowtail and daikon again, and maybe try more items on the menu, but not if I have to put up with subpar and overpriced drinks forced on me. Whomp whomp.

This is by far the best panini place in the neighboorhood, I've tried a couple of other places but they just are not as good as Panino Rustico. I too thought that it wasn't going to last long due to the fact that it's on a corner in a quiet neighborhood but was surprised when I came for lunch during the day over the summer and the place was buzzing! I recently went back over the weekend and again the place was filled. The food is absolutley delicious, from the paninis to the desserts just yum, the decor and seating is quant, the staff is freindly and attentive and the prices are great. I will definetly be coming back here again and again :)
waiter excellent food and service great !

NOT VEG FRIENDLY (for brunch at least) more on that later.... Really great atmosphere and pretty good food and drinks. I went for breakfast and had the pollack cakes. They were good but a very small portion. I was really impressed with the side of mixed greens. It wasn't much but the light dressing (some kind of olive oil concoction?) was amazing! The mimosas were delicious and strong-got pretty tipsy off of 2. The service was friendly. Besides all that, my friends and I did have a pretty negative experience. The Farm is not at all accommodating. Two of my friends were vegetarian and vegan and had a hard time with the menu. One of my friends decided not to get anything. The Farm refuses to do substitutions, and if you remove things from the item they also don't reduce the price. I don't understand why this policy and snooty attitude exists in Brooklyn.

First time eating here, I read some of the review here in Yelp, but still had some doubts if it was a good place to eat. Boy was I wrong. From our waitress explaining the menu and food to the quick service and Amazing food, I recommend this place 100%. I had the 5 course tasting menu that give me 4 savory dishes and 1 dessert. Â off all the dishes I had the two the stood out is the Rib eye with the potato Leek hash brown with creamed spinach. the meat is cooked medium rare with this jus that pulls everything together. it almost melts in your mouth. And then I had the Caramelized Torija. Its this bread pudding, flan tasting awesome looking thing of Â a dessert served with a grape fruit section. Will definitely go back and try the 10 course tasting menu.

Despite it's location in Times Square and the perpetual influx of tourists - Carmine's still succeeds in being an enjoyable dining experience. We went with a group of people, which seems to be the best way to take advantage of their family style portions and large menu. No, the food doesn't push culinary boundaries - but they do do simple, flavorful dining best. The wait was not nearly as long as expected given the fact that it was Friday night - I think we had to wait twenty minutes at most (Amazing). Our waiter was charming (not something you can say often) and informative and his recommendations were spot on. All in all, a pleasant experience. Note: Make sure you leave room for dessert!

When I ate at Butcher Bar last year. the food literally blew me off my chair! OMG i had THE best burnt ends ever! I decided to come back this year and bring my friends (who know their BBQ) and experienced THE worst service ever! We waited 45 minutes for our food (which clearly had gone forgotten) and the food was not good. The burnt ends were neither burnt nor even hot! The string beans had absolutely no flavor, the smoked turkey looked like it came directly from boar's head, it had absolutely no flavor and the sweet potatoes were overcooked. We had to get their attention and as an apology we were served huge donuts that were cold, old and tasted like rubber. Went from my most favorite BBQ place to my least favorite.

I crave these when I'm back in Toronto. It's the first thing I eat when I land in NYC. These fries are like no other. I refuse to even eat other places 'belgian fries' because I just get disappointed. I usually get a regular (regular is BIG!) with frite sauce (free), but last time went for the truffle mayo (1.75). It was really rich, but so delicious. Hint: Get the sauce on the side. Sometimes they put way too much on when you get it in the cone - the fries get totally saturated and lose their amazingness.

Does Harold Dieterle's restraurant live up to the hype? Decidedly so. We started with the calamari on a bed of crispy watercress and the spicy duck meatballs. The calamari was out of this world and easily the best execution of any calamri dish I've ever had. The duck meatballs, although tasty, lacked a certain depth and sharpness I expected out of such an esteemed chef. Did this really win him Top Chef? Perhaps a hint of citrus would have helped... In either case, the calamari dish was so good that I'm willing to give the appetizers a perfect score. For the entree I had the seared duck breast with starfruit and a dill pollen glaze. The duck, as expected from a quality restaurant, was cooked perfectly and the cut was perfect. The glaze was very flavorful without being overpowering and the incorporation of starfruit added a slightly sweet yet generally neutral contribution to the flavor. I wish the starfruit wasn't so separated from the rest of the dish though... it would have lent its flavor nicely had it been pureed or something. All in all, the execution couldn't have been much better. My party also had a snapper dish and a dorade dish. Both fish fillets were pleasantly executed with great sauces but... there just wasn't all that much originality there. All in all, although the entrÃ©es are great I urge you to come here and try the calamari appetizer. Really, it's the best thing of its kind in NYC. I'm giving it five stars. Is it something you MUST try before you die? Well...no. It's simply a fresh execution of some classical flavors. There's nothing incredibly original going on. However, perfect execution counts for a lot.

I'm not sure why this place got an average of four stars. Â My lunch buddy and I were a bit disappointed. Â We both agreed we wouldn't come back, that we had hundreds of other restaurants we could try in the downtown area. We both started off with the roti cani. Â We both admit it was tasty. Â We also enjoyed the soup that came with the meal, which was simply a clear broth with chicken, mushrooms, carrots and cabbage. Â While we started drinking our soup, the roti canai came out along with my lunch special. Â By the time I finished drinking my soup and eating my roti canai, my lunch was cold. Â  I ordered the beef masak. Â There was so little there, I could scoop it all up and hold it in one hand. Â The beef was really chewy. Â The sauce was good, but what difference would that make if the beef wasn't tender. My lunch buddy had the Malaysian style spareribs. Â They were pretty tastey, but there was so little to eat. Â I think they took two spareribs and cut it up into five pieces. Â If we didn't share our lunch specials, she definitely would not have had enough to eat. Â  The service wasn't the greatest either. Â After we finished our soup and appetizer, they didn't even take our plates away. Â We were sitting at a table for two didn't have much room. Â We had to stack our plates together and put them aside. I definitely would not recommend this place. Â The only thing decent about this place was the decor.

This is a busy hotspot in the West Village. Â Make reservations, but don't be surprised if you have to wait. Â The Meatball appetizer is a must order. Â It comes with 2 MASSIVE meatballs that are at least a pound each and the size of grapefruits. Â They Â were cooked perfectly, with just the right amount of moisture, and were served piping hot even through the center. Â We also tried a pork braciole. Â (thin pounded pork rolled up around cheese). Â Oh so good. Â The ziti with vodka sauce was also a winner! Â There are so many great choices in NYC for Italian, but Piccolo will be worth a second trip.

MMM...I finally tried out the happy hour and it was lovely! Can't go wrong with $3 beer and pile-loads of comfort food. We had the calamari for appetizer, he got the pollo con arroz and I got the fish tacos w/ sweet plantains and quinoa. Mannn the food was amazing. "This is the best chicken and rice I've ever had!" he said. Amen dude. Had the Aguila and Xingu, they were very different from other beers I've had, def thicker and more flavor. I will def come back :)
I ordered a mama gyro. It was super delicious. Service was awesome. Not much seating area though but it was very clean and trendy. Best for a quick tasty bite on a low budget.

I used to be a big fan of Ippudo and endured many a long wait to slurp their undeniably superior broth. The last few trips though, I walked away feeling like the food has gone a little downhill, and that, combined with the long wait and crowded atmosphere, drives Ippudo into the overrated category. The service is no-nonsense and quick, but at the same time you feel a little rushed. It's loud and crowded, and you are frequently crammed in next to strangers. The pork buns are delicious, but the ramen is average.

I have eaten here for Dinner on the weekend but this past weekend it was my first time having brunch. Â I went with 5 other girls with not wait Â time we had a table. Â There was a decent amount of people there and we asked so many questions about the menu but the server was soooooo polite. Â We pretty much each ordered something different. Â I had the breakfast po' boy with a side of fried oysters (that i put in my sandwich) and i was in heaven. Â The table was real quiet for about 7 minutes while we all ate which is saying something, the food was so good that we didn't want to stop to talk. Â I also tasted the shrimp and grits (amazing) as well as the bananas foster french toast (sinful). Â I am coming back soon!

Loved this place!!! The food is extremely fresh and delicious, great service and cozy atmosphere... Truffle fries is everything its made to to be!!! In one word "Delicious"!! the warm baby beet& romanesco salad, was Â also great Great place for am intimate dinner. Â Enjoy
The Hatch Burger the best burger I have ever consumed.

Hi surprise sandwich shop near Penn Station. Sergimmo Salumeria is one of those places that confused me initially when I walked in because there were no order here and pay here signs and it wasn't super self explanatory. However, it has a feel like the Soho Alidoro in midtown. There is seating and the sandwiches are pretty tasty. I had something with chicken, roasted red peppers, balsamic and arugula. Definitely go. I will be back for sure.

I really love this place for the great price and the great food! I came here for a friends birthday dinner and was pleasantly surprised and the amount of food we received for pre-fixe and how good everything was. We had unlimited wine and beer for 15$ a person as well. My favorite was the bruschetta, polenta with mushrooms and the pasta. I would definitely come here again maybe even for my own birthday.

Very good food and nice atmosphere. The sweet & sour chicken liver appetiser is to die for. Entrees are quality, the pork chop is huge and crispy, and the cod tasted great with a side of herbed french fries. Very good experience overall.

From start to finish, everything was excellent. Outstanding service. Beautiful ambiance, and everything my wife and I ordered came out tasting delicious. After ordering a few appetizers, and snacks, she ordered the grass-fed steak, and I had the scallops. We went back and forth, eating off of each others plates. YUM! The steak had a little char on the outside, and medium on the inside. It really doesn't get any better than that. Delicious!. The scallops were equally tasty. Enough said. Don't miss this one.

If you gave this place less than 5 stars, go shoot yourself. So far, this has been the best dining experience of my life. Aside from its exclusiveness, this place really delivered. Granted the service and decor may not be stiffy/fancy like those at michelin starred restaurants, it was just right amount of warmth in both aspects where I felt like I was at my friend's apartment. The food is spectacular. When I say spectacular, I mean one of the best executed food I've tried so far. Listen to your fellow yelpers and go with the a la carte instead of the pre fixe. 1) Uni croquette- was full of flavor. The croquette itself had the crunchy exterior with perfect creamy/steamy interior. The flavors worked incredibly well in a way I did not expect. Highly recommend. 2) Foie Gras Soba- seriously delicious. In many ways, this goes against the traditional soba where the purpose is to deliver a clean-tasting meal which will keep the palate clean. The foie adds the fatty and earthy Â goodness to the broth which, when mixed with the traditional broth, enhances so much flavor in itself. The noodle was perfectly cooked. The foie was amazing. And all those three ingredients worked incredibly well. 3) Wagyu Beef Slider- holy moly. This place is known for its prime Japanese beef as its located behind a Japanese meat shop. The quality of the meat in this slider is so good and perfect, and I could honestly say it was the best "burger" I've had in my life despite the size. Could have 3 servings of this by myself. I'd ask for the ketchup on the side next time though. 4) Mac-and-Cheese - only "just great" dish of the night. Incredibly cheesy, and the toasted bread with tomato spread worked really well with mac and cheese. But in the end, it was a very good mac and cheese and flavor didn't stay with me for too long. 5) Branzino- wow. If you didn't like this dish, what the fuck is wrong with you. Dish came out sizzling with the perfectly cooked fish along with farmer's vegetables seasoned after they were cooked. My sister claims those were the best vegetables she's ever had not to mention the fish itself. Definitely a hearty meal. Ridiculous. Can't wait to go back in the near future and try out all their other appealing choices. 5 stars.

BEST Greek Food I've had since I lived in Europe! This place has the atmosphere, great service, and awesome prizes!!! I would definitely send any and all friends there!! Not to mention go again whenever chance (and economy) permits!!!
Amazing. And this from a guy who is 40 years past hipster

Definitely want to see this place succeed but it's got a ways to go. Â We came for a late afternoon lunch. Â They might have been slammed by a heavy brunch crowd earlier in the day, which explains why they were out of a few items. But that doesn't excuse some of the mistakes. First, the positives: 1. Friendly and efficient service 2. Clean and inviting atmosphere. The only misstep on the decor is a sectional painting that looked like it was more suited to a mid-level chain hotel restaurant. If they hung some black and white photographs it would be much nicer. 3. My sparkling rose was crisp and dry and I imagine their other options are good too. Second, the neutrals: The smoked eggplant appetizer was fine. Nothing special. Lastly, the negatives: 1. Â The Coke. My wife and I have developed a theory that when a restaurant's colas are bad, the meal invariably disappoints. Â We keep hoping for a case that disproves the connection but so far no luck. Her coke arrived lacking in both syrup and carbonation. Â We sent it back and it returned all syrup and even less carbonation. Undrinkable. I'm not saying a restaurant should focus on its sodas, but non-alcohol drinkers should be taken care of too. 2. The bread. Instead of fresh bread we were served thick slices of toast with olive oil for dipping. Â The toasting may have been a way to mask stale bread. Or toasting may be their standard practice. Either way it's a bad idea. Toast cries out for butter, not olive oil. Olive oil works with fresh bread, not toast. 3. The frisee salad. The poached egg on top was cooked until the yoke was completely hard. This defeats the biggest pleasure for me of a frisee salad, which is breaking the yoke and having it run and mix with the dressing and the bacon. Also, the frisee itself was not fresh--it tasted old. At the end of the meal we were presented with a check where we were billed for a bottle, not a glass, of the sparkling rose. I know mistakes happen, and it was promptly rectified, but it still felt like the cherry on top of a bad meal.

Come hungry! If you get the full dinner set, you'll get refills of cabbage, miso soup and rice. The chicken katsu is yummy and I like mixing the sauce myself and how your meal consists of so many little courses. Some of the staff is very nice (the guy who seems like the manager), while others are a little cold. Overall, it's a great dining experience if you haven't eaten lunch and are looking to go home in a coma and watch Netflix for the rest of your life.
This place is an experience! The wine and food is wonderful. The service is great! Try the mac n cheese the avocado salad the lobster risotto and the deserts!! I will be going back here!!

Foods not that great and the service is worse. No one checked to see if our food was alright and that wouldn't have bothered me except my wine glass was empty before my food arrived and remained empty the entire meal. We had to ask for the check 3 times and I won't be coming back here. Skip it.
Yum yum! Cheap price but very delicious ! I gave 5 stars. My friend recommend this place and I am so happy. I definitely will come back to tried more !

The appetizers are pricey, but worth it for the quality. The burger was incredible and a complete contrast to the huge greasy stack of meat from the Corner Bistro nearby. Â The meat was remarkably light and fluffy, like a marshmallow. Â I don't know how they do it, but it's an impressive technique. Â You have to try it to understand. Â This burger will truly blow you away. The Cuban sandwich that's only available at lunchtime is worth a trip in the middle of the day, it's the most amazing version of a pork sandwich you'll ever taste. Thumbs down on the Spotted Pig cask ale though, it tasted something like a 50/50 blend of PBR with Saranac ale. Â Maybe it is a deliberate blend of lowbrow meets middle class (ironically, in an extravagantly priced neighborhood) that they are going for? Â I expected a bit more from the draft selection. Update: Â Months later, and I've moved to the left coast, and I have dreams about eating here. They can't make a burger like this anywhere in LA, not even Father's Office. Oh how I miss SP! If I had time for only one meal in all of Manhattan, I am pretty sure I'd be here.

This place really is as good as it gets. Went here for brunch on a Sunday and had the absolute best experience. Our waiter was so pleasant, not pushy but helpful. Not enough kind words can be said about the bartender, too. He knows his way around a bloody mary. Our table had the baked eggs, the burger, and the Mangalista dish, which was basically eggs benedict. Everything was amazing, and seriously, ask your waiter about where your food came from. The beef in the burger goes through some intricate process before it reaches your plate, the ham in the benny has a similar experience, probably the eggs too, for cryin' out loud I have no idea. The breakfast bread basket was incredibly satisfying as well. Best homemade bagel our whole table had ever tasted, same goes for the scone. The jalapeno cornbread was insane. Jalapeno cornbread? Yup. The trio of treats came with an assortment of spreads, including vanilla butter. For pete's sake, just go here, please. You won't be disappointed!

Mediocre food, terrible service. I've been here three times, the third was my last. The food was mediocre the first two times and the third time I never even had a chance to order. I ended up being seated towards the back in a really crowded space, which was not ideal in the first place. Then to make matters worse the manager made a scene about our table being in the way. We ended up leaving before we even ordered. I wasn't disappointed because the food isn't great and there are so many amazing places right around the corner. We had a great dinner at Cafe Gitane instead!
So gave it another go but still baffled by a place where it's impossible to quickly grab a sandwich for lunch??!! I still call it "Confusion". Short of the coffee/ice cream bar, the layout is a mess.

Writing this review because I am seriously fiending for some chicken over rice. Â It's almost been a year since I've last had it and I thought I could go on not writing or thinking about it, but it skitters across my mind every now and then, but just right now, it's overwhelming. I'm not sure why it's so good because it's just chicken and rice, but I really LOVE chicken. They call me the chicken mastah! Sometimes. Anyway, like everyone has said, take heed with the red sauce, my friend slathered it on his food thinking it was going to be like siracha, but man, he was crying. He said it was soo good that he couldn't stop eating it, even while crying through the red sauce. Â The white sauce couldn't even save him, damage was done. Definitely load up on the white sauce because I got up 3 or 4 times to refill. So if you want to continuously shovel food, generously slather on the white. Gluttony rules!

This is by far the best Thai restaurant I've been to so far in New York City. Â The food there is delicious! Â Service is also good. Â Although the restaurant is always packed, I never have to wait too long for seats.

What has happened to Char. No. 4? This was easily my favorite restaurant in Brooklyn by a mile for several years. In the past 12 months though, it has really gone down hill. Obviously there is a great bar and drink menu. But the service has really taken a hit. And the food too is just not what it used to be. Here's hoping this amazing institution gets some of it's magic back. I miss the old Char 4.

A great restaurant, the likes of which are seldom found on the UES. Â The food was good and the service was amazing. Â This is the perfect neighborhood joint. Â Cozy and inviting, I can see myself here on many a night.

I don't even like NY style pizza and I couldn't stop eating the meat lover pizza. Love the crispy crust and the balance of sauce and cheese. Ended up with only two slices, could easly see myself eating at least half a large pie. Best pizza I've had so far while visiting NY, but pricey and doesn't really fill me up.

I went there on a Friday after work and did not find the wait to be too long. Â I am not a seafood eater but I found the catfish sandwich to be very tasty. Â I also had the shrimp tempura which was good. Â Service was okay. Â We were a party of 3 and were seated at the table right by the kitchen. Â I did not like this table because the two seater table was attached to ours; making it a table for five which left us with no privacy. I probably will not return unless my friends wanted to because they loved their meals of red snapper and grits.
We were in the area and a bit lazy to walk to 3rd ave so we decided to eat here... To our surprise the food was very very good, every dish that came to our 4 people table was great!

This is some serious falafel. Growing up and being raised by an Israeli woman, it has made me somewhat of a falafel snob. I rarely order it out. But, I found myself wandering TribeCa while my fiancÃ© was busy and I thought, hmm why not? I loved the variety of falafel flavors and different sandwich offerings. I went with the Popeye. Spinach and mushroom falafel in a fluffy whole wheat pita (the way it should be) with hummus, tahini, fresh spinach, and red cabbage. It was a little more expensive than I'm used to but honestly it was worth the price. I loved it. Perfectly cooked and delicious falafel, tons of fresh spinach soaking up the delicious tahini. I'm drooling just thinking about it. The food is clearly authentic as I heard the owners heavy Israeli accent speaking fluent hebrew. Everyone was very friendly and the food was fresh. Â Nothing is more unappealing that a sad soggy falafel ball. They had me wait for a fresh batch which I very much appreciate. I look forward to trying their jachnun and shakshuka!

We stumbled upon Market Table after our original brunch plans were thwarted by large crowds and a lack of tables at our first destination. Overall, the experience was definitely well above average, though not perfect. Market Table was busy for a weekend mid-day, but not too noisy or overwhelming. The ambiance was quaint and rustic, but tables were fairly close together and caused some inconvenience when being seated with large jackets and bags (I guess that's NYC in the winter time, though). I went for the Poached Eggs (buttermilk biscuit, grilled ham, & hollandaise.... errr perhaps they should call it Eggs Benedict?). The dish was, by far, the best eggs Benedict I have had in NYC, or anywhere for that matter! The biscuit rivaled the buttermilk biscuits at Cookshop (though Cookshop still has a better biscuit), the ham was great, the eggs were perfectly done, and the hollandaise was delectable! It came with a side salad, which was also very good. However, I was craving some OJ with my brunch and when it arrived I was surprised to see that it was literally only about the size of a shot. I know it was probably fresh squeezed, but that was a let down. As for the service, our waitress was efficient but not intrusive and we definitely enjoyed our brunch!

The falafels are probably the best I've ever had. The reason why I'm giving 3 stars is because of the intangibles. First off the place needs to better serve it's customers. If you are about to order and a phone order comes in for 40 falafel sandwiches, the entire staff will work on the 40 sandwiches before your order gets made. I understand it's a big order but having experience in the food service industry I also understand that you shouldn't dedicate 100% of your staff on one order. This creates a log jam in the restaurant, with lines going out the door for no reason. I'm not sure if the owner knows this is happening but I have yet to spend less than 15 minutes in the place, even if there is no one in front of me. Today I was there at 11:45 am, no one else was in line, it still took 20 minutes because of a phone order. Break off a few of your staff to serve the customers in line, very simple. Also while the falafel is delicious, perfectly fried, moist and full of flavor, they ruin it by putting it together into the pita very sloppy. I know a falafel in a pita isn't exactly the neatest thing to eat, but the pita breaks every time, hummus and salad comes pouring out of the top, it's just not a very well made sandwich, but that can be fixed very easily. That being said I still really enjoy it and it's a new place so I'll give them another few months, and update my review. I'm sure they'll get their act together and start pumping out the best falafel sandwiches in NYC.

Have Renje G. to thank for finding this great place This place is a good introduction to what a great Vietnamese Â sandwich should taste like. Their Banh mi is awesome. Â I had the grilled pork served in a crispy baguette and topped with cilantro, cucumber slices and daikon. Whatever sauce they used had a perfect blend of spices. Add the avocado shake and you got yourself a perfect lunch.
This place is busy but worth the wait.
old school aweseome
Great food. Serving size small. Tables are intimate. Take only your closest friends! =o)

I came here for brunch and had the soft eggs with a mimosa. The food was pretty underwhelming, the eggs came out soggy and the home fries were cold. I didn't get a sense of freshness from the meal. That said, the place is cute and the service was good. I wouldn't come back for breakfast but would definitely Â give lunch a shot.

Nothing extraordinary about this place. I had the mussels, Caesars salad, swordfish and panna cotta. Mussels were great, generous portions. Salad was horrible. Swordfish was good but vegetables unedible. Panna cotta was good. Price was reasonable. Very average.

The Gyro-Spiced Beef Sliders blew my mind AND my tastebuds. Wow. They come three to a plate with a side of homemade chips with yogurt sauce and an incredible hot feta dip. The appetizer is big enough to be a meal for one person. I may get just that with a drink if I go back to enjoy their bar! We also had the corn soup which was very good but small. Our entrÃ©e was a feta and spinach stuffed sole on rice, which was very good and in a big portion. We ordered too much food, but it was so good that we ate all of it. Dessert? A variant of baklava that was super sweet. Really liked it, Â but can't imagine how a single person could eat the whole thing! It was large. Very friendly, attentive staff when we went there on Â a Monday night. Sat at a sidewalk table and shared a half bottle of wine. Very cool, quiet and romantic environment for a dinner date with my handsome husband. Would love to try them out again and see what the upstairs dining room is like. We were quite pleased with our visit. But, yeah. The Gyro sliders? Amazeballs.

This is a great place for brunch, the wait can be a bit long, but they will take your phone number and call you when the table is ready and there are a few interesting boutiques nearby to distract you while you wait. I don't want to say that the food is typical Brooklyn Fare, but more restaurants seem to be trending towards new and upscale classic American. These guys just do it right, the quality exceed the price. I highly recommend the pork chops, and the sour cream doughnut which comes out warm and covered in powdered sugar (yeah!) and Brunch includes a alcoholic bev, I recommend the bloody mary, if your into them because they do it well.

Get that spicy fries coated with canjun spicky goodness! The pulled pork sandwich was OK but the roasted bun was superb! Â I tasted the Mac and cheese and that is a def must order from the menu. This place is cash only though so that's just an fyu

One of my favorite brunch places! There's always a crowd waiting on Sundays. Make a reservation! Even then sometimes there's a wait. The bread basket is delicious! I heard the bread is from Balthazar. The strawberry butter is yum! I got the Benedict Jane which was cooked nicely, loved the home fries. You get a complimentary drink with your brunch order, definitely a plus! The food doesn't disappoint if there weren't such huge crowds so often I think I'd come here more often.

I have been eating at this place for a long while now and let me tell you, these guys are great!!!! I would eat here every day if I could! The food is delicious, inexpensive, the portions are big and you don't feel guilty afterwards. Honestly the best and most consistent vegetarian food in Brooklyn.
BYOB - makes this a great place to bring a six pack and stuff your face with delicious foods.

Eat brunch here. We have been a few times.. It is always busy when we go, the service is pretty good.. But the food is great. Brunch comes with a free mimosa/sangria/bloody mary AND coffee.. The red sangria is the best around.. and the home fries are a mixture of sweet potatoes and regular potatoes. Delicious.
Stopped by here for a chocolate bag and a couple of drinks during lunchtime - and it was FANTASTIC. Â Sat outside, there were little heaters and the service was great. Highly recommend that dessert!

This place is amazing. The pizza is delicious. I had the marinara and I ate it all. The staff is super nice and accommodating. The owners are friendly and the place has a great vibe. It was a fantastic evening out and I can't wait to do it again! A+!
Amazing on all fronts, I just wish Â the menu offered more things, but well worth.

Had dinner with friends here a few weeks ago and wasn't blown away by the food but I really enjoyed the decor and atmosphere. It's a bit Euro, nautical, rustic all mixed in. Dimly lit lamps/lighting created a nice warm vibe. We split some mussels which were good, standard. I had the onion soup and a salad, also just ok nothing spectacular. My friends had different dishes - Chicken, Steak tartar, salads...all were good. The fries were the best part! I did enjoy a great glass of red and everyone else seemed to pick great wines as well. Overall, the service and food were fine, no complaints. I'd come back to have drinks at the bar next since the vibe is very cool and everyone at the bar was enjoying themselves.

Graffiti is one of the most unique restaurants I've ever been to, and now among my favorites in NYC. Chef Jehangir Mehta specializes in International tapas style cuisine with Indian undertones. With only four tables, the space is crowded to say the least and we were squeezed onto a table with other random customers. Despite having my back pushed against the wall exactly one foot away from the kitchen, there was something very charming and honest about the restaurant setup. It was cozy and I think we were actually lucky to be smelling all the different aromas coming from the kitchen. Another aspect that contributed to the honest quality of the restaurant was the fact that Chef Mehta walked around and was very involved in restaurant operations and making sure guests were satisfied. It only makes sense for a chef to be involved in ongoing restaurant activities, but unfortunately not many take the effort. That is why I can appreciate Chef Mehta's courtesy and dedication to the restaurant and customer satisfaction much more! There's so much to say about the food. First, I'd like to point out that the waiters bring each dish out one at a time, which allows you to really focus on the medley of flavors that each dish provides (also it would be tough to fit more than one plate on the table!). The waiters are incredibly knowledgeable about the dishes and painstakingly explain the components of each dish as they arrive.

Nice place but I won't eat there again. They got a "C" on the health inspection but you won't find their grade in the window because they don't want u to know instead of making improvements they took finds because they were scared the "C" grade would turn people away

SO excited for this Luke's Lobster location in FiDi. Â It seems the lunch option expansion in this neighborhood continues to grow, and in the right direction with quality places like Luke's, adding to the infamy of downtown Manhattan, and not just for Wall Street (good or bad), but for amazing, new places to eat! Â (Step aside Midtown, it's time to share the spotlight)... Â  This is the first and only Luke's I've been to, and from what I've experienced, it's clear they know how to work a winning formula. Â This location has got a lot of the seaside-harbor, New England charm to it with its smart decor of nautical props and objects, to its lobster patterned fabric chairs (I loved this touch), all within a tightly compact space. Â There are some tables and chairs to eat inside, but the heat from the kitchen that stifles up the place should seriously change your mind from enjoying your meal indoors. Â On a nice day, it's better to eat outside in a public atrium or park that you might find nearby. I'm not used to paying $15 (lobster roll only) or $17 (lobster roll, soda, chips and a pickle) for lunch, but for a meaty and delicious lobster roll from Luke's, it is worth the occasional splurge! Â My sandwich was incredible. Â The split-top bun was lightly grilled and buttery without being greasy, and the lobster meat was served Maine style with huge morsels of chilled, fresh and tender lobster with a touch of mayo, lemon butter and Luke's special seasoning blend. Â Barely much seasoning on it, but all the while amazing in texture and flavor, it truly was a delicately simple, yet unforgettably perfect sandwich. Â  Their menu does offer a trio of seafood staples, from the namesake lobster roll, to either a shrimp roll, or even a crab roll. Â I'm excited to come back and try these Â other options that I haven't had. Â They also carry New England Clam Chowder and a "soup of the day" that you can pair along with a half roll. Â For those looking for something sweet to end your meal, you have the option of either a classic or blueberry whoopie pie. Â I went with the classic, and it was pretty substantial (heavy and decadent) and a bit on the sweet side, but enjoyable nonetheless. 4 stars instead of 5 since they only offer one style of lobster roll (Maine), whereas it may have been a great idea to also provide Connecticut style rolls for those who enjoy that version (warm lobster with butter). Â I myself will always love the Maine style version, but it's nice to have a choice like they do at Brooklyn's Red Hook Lobster Pound.

SPACE: 4 stars Nice space with typical Williamsburg feel. Â Small, probably seats about 40 when maxed out. Â You can sit at small tables, the main food bar (which is more of a "chef's table" type setting) Â or the cocktail bar in the back. COCKTAILS: 5 stars Top notch. Â We had 6 different cocktails paired with our food (as suggested by the chef) and they were all on point. Â Whether opaque and shaken or clear and stirred the bartender got everything right. FOOD: 5 stars Ok, for all who insist on being technically accurate, much of what is served here isn't true ceviche, though some is. Â Most of what is not, is more of a sashimi on steroids. Â Don't get me wrong, it's not "overdone" for the sake of look or outrageous ingredients. Â It is however, incredible. Â Little hints of spice, citrus, ginger, heat or crunch on every bite. Â All the while, the flavor of the fish comes through. Â Ever bite of every dish we had was perfection. SERVICE: 5 stars Our waitress was kind, attentive and knowledgable. Â We never wanted for water, drinks or food. Â She was on top of everything. We sat at the main bar in front of chef. Â He politely asked if we were going to have dinner or just snack. Â We said dinner. Â He asked if we would mind putting ourselves in his hands and "let me just take care of you. Â You won't be disappointed." Â He couldn't have been more correct. Â Great experience in every facet.

Good food but I think they need more waitstaff for busy season.. Robin was as lovely as ever but seemed under pressure! Love the food especially their meatballs. Its a great spot near Times Square but don't go for that Cacciatore-too many bones!

I've been here several times and I love IT! Â  I'm not crazy about shabu shabu, but I love the barbecue. Â The meat was so delicious that it melted in my mouth. Â The large bottle of Sapporo was the perfect complement.

I love places like this - hidden nooks that have great food and if you didn't know they were there (or had Yelp to direct you) you'd walk right by and miss out. The bulgogi and bibimbap were great. I can't want to come back and try some other things off the menu. Sure they have wraps, burgers and sandwiches, but if I want some basic American fare I'd go elsewhere. Be adventurous and try some Korean dishes. Each dish came with miso soup and a side of kim chi. All of that and it's hiding in the lobby of an office building. That's what makes NYC so fun.

I just got back from having brunch at Penelope. Since moving to Gramercy, I've heard great reviews about this restaurant. I arrived at 10am for brunch (Sunday) and it was about a 20 minutes wait for 2 people. They had complimentary coffee for everyone waiting which was a nice touch. I got the "sam-I-am" which is pretty simple - scrambled eggs with asparagus and feta. It was good and what I expected. The 7grain bread on the side was delicious and the fries were crispy...just how I like them. Only downside was the fake bacon. EWWWW! Not like the kind bought in the grocery. Penelope uses seitan and it doesn't taste right. Besides that, service was friendly and accommodating. Don't be fooled though, the food is not worth more than a half hour wait.

Oh my god. Deliciousness! I went with a large group last night (12 people) and everyone was happy with their food. Drinks were strong and tasty... my friend actually started gnawing on the piece of sugar cane they put in her drink (it was something with pineapple... I forget which one exactly). I ordered the Puerquito Cubano, which was monstrously huge! It was like, a gigantic slab of pork over mashed plantains and it was freaking insane. So good!! FFJKDEIOJAISDJALWIDLAIL! Minus a star because they screwed up our reservations (got the time and number of people wrong) and we got a bit of a 'tude from the workers... I guess because we were so big. It was a tight squeeze... the place was packed.

Lombardi's pizza is Mario in Mario Kart. Â Yeah, he doesn't have the bulk of Bowser or the acceleration of Toad, but he is well-rounded in every way that they are not. Â Still with me on this parallel? Â Good. The pizza here is great because it really has no weaknesses. Â The crust, sauce, and cheese are all excellent. Â That being said, none of them individually steal the show as the reason to come here. Â The flavor is a great jack-of-all-trades-master-of-none balance. Â The onions, red peppers, and mushroom toppings were very fresh. Put simply, this is tasty pizza with really fresh toppings for an appropriate Manhattan price.

Had dinner in the garden out back which is completely lovely. you'll Â totally forget that you're in the epicenter of the bustle of the burg. I was really looking forward to trying this place after reading some of the reviews and the photos are extremely appetizing. I don't mind sending a bit of cash for a decent meal, that's for sure, but $15 for a tea cup saucer size portion of civiche misto that quite possibly came out of a can is just outrageous! The shishito peppers aren't the first thing that comes to mind when you think Argentinian food but they were seasoned perfectly and the portion was enough for four people to share. Their truffle fries are perfectly crispy with sufficient truffle essence; they are obviously not hand cut but for their texture and taste it's excusable. Â The grilled corn is tasty but its kinda hard to mess that up considering were in the height of the corn season, grill it up, slap on some butter, cheese and lemon; done! I did have a bite of the blood sausage, that shizzz was delicious!!! The casing had the snap you expect in a sausage and the filling was perfectly smooth and rich... This would have been a three star review except that our food took 1.5hrs to reach the table. Everything came out at once even the canned civiche and fries that could came out as apps... While waiting for the restroom overheard a table cancel their order cause they were waiting for over an hour to which the waiter responded "are you sure? it should only be another 15mins or so."... haha! We split the check between cash and credit and out server added another $60 on the credit cards (honest mistake but still).

Occasion: Friday dinner for Restaurant Week (A) Food (4.0 out of 5): What we ate: 1) Stake Tartar - Unique, rich flavor, well complemented with hot pepper and onion 2) Falafel - Very crispy (almost hard) but soft inside - if you're used to traditional falafel, we may skip this dish as appetizer! 3) Moujadara - sweet, full of rich texture 4) Hommus - my favorite!! Must!! Served with warm (feels like just baked out of oven), fresh pita bread (funny - we even ended up asking for more bread with big big smile!) As main dish, we had 1) lamb chop (super tender, good quality meat with sauteed green sauce), and 2) vegetarian risotto (a bit disappointing part of our dinner, a bit too salty and the sauce was a bit blend, would recommend trying out other dishes) Drum rolls, please. For our dessert, we got 1) candy bar, and 2) sweet cheese tart (would recommend this, don't worry, it's not too cheesy and the best part of this dessert is, orange blossom syrup! also very big portion so expect to bring something back home!!) (B) Ambience (4.0 out of 5): We were seated in a side room full of couples - enough space between each table (I even ran into another friendly couple sitting next to us, ended up sharing my review/recommendation on the dessert menu.) It feels quite cozy but romantic with the high ceiling, and dim lighting. The whole restaurant is very spacious, great for both group, bar scene and romantic dinner for couples! Â  (C) Service (4.0 out of 5): Our waiter was nice, considerate - well-informed about the menu. The food came in a timely manner and careful to details. He also had a great recommendation for us (without much experience in Lebanese food) (D) Value (3 out of 5): Decent value for $$ (wish they have more signature dishes on their restaurant week menu)

I love this place! My girlfriend and I have been a few times. The food is always amazing, I love the ambiance, and the staff is friendly and awesome. I love that the owner is always so calm and engages with customers. I also enjoy the hostess and the charm that she brings to the restaurant. One of my favorite places to enjoy a delicious Southern meal!
If you like a hipster ambiance, a unique, ever-changing menu, good drinks and live music, this is the place to go. Brought my boyfriend here and we both were floored. So, so good.

I developed a new appreciation for pizza when I tried Lombardi's wild mushroom, onion and panchetta pizza for lunch. I'm normally not big on pizza but, it was the food of choice for a lunch meeting so I went for the most exciting pie. Thin crust brick oven pizza topped with perfectly thin slices panchetta blend perfectly with the mushroom and onion flavors on each slice. My one qualm, the tip end of the crust can get a little soggy and droopy so 1 less star for bad slice structure BUT, this pie made up for that with flavor. Â 4 stars for tasty pizza and prompt delivery.
Amazing beer selection.

So my friends and I Got together one afternoon and all tried the Black Label Burger and the thing was amazing. Â Not willing to pay the price on a regular basis, but certainly was a treat. Â Other than that, the service and atmosphere were great. Â Hope this is a new tradition for us.

If you're looking for a quick bowl of ramen for a cheap price, this is definitely a great place to go to! Finding this place maybe troublesome for people who don't frequently travel to Chinatown, but with that said, it provides a certain charm to it; it adds to the low-key restaurant feel that's provided. The place itself is pretty small and compact- probably fits at most 15 people. If you go with friends, travel in a group of 2-4 people (including yourself). When you order water, it's given to you in a pitcher and you have to drink out of styrofoam cups. I wasn't particularly bothered by it, but for those who are, here is your warning. It's better to just purchase a bottle of snapple or a can of soda. The menu features a pretty good variety of ramen. I purchased the beef with the wide hand pulled noodles. My friend purchased the duck with the rice hand pulled noodles, and my other friend ordered the chicken and shrimp with the regular hand pulled noodles. I didn't wait that long- probably about 8-10 minutes before I got my food. The bowl my ramen was held in was a pretty standard size for a ramen house (if you're an avid ramen eater). My ramen also came with some bok choy. The ratio of noodles to beef and bok choy was pretty even. Not too much bok choy to overwhelm the ramen, there was enough beef so I didn't feel cheated, and enough ramen to fill up my appetite. The texture of the noodles was great. It was soft, but also strong enough to withstand being pulled by my chopsticks (I've visited a ramen house where the noodles would literally break when held between my chopsticks; a very bad experience). The quantity of noodles was great, considering that you only pay $6.25 for a bowl. The beef was cooked just right; not undercooked where it becomes too chewy, and not overcooked where it becomes to unbearable to eat. It was just right to eat. The bok choy was pretty standard, not much to say about it. Overall, I was greatly satisfied. I have a huge appetite, but I actually wasn't able to completely finish my bowl! I got to about 4/5ths of it before I couldn't eat anymore. I don't think you're going to find a place that sells better ramen for this price. My only complaint is the beverage options. They were very limited to what they have; just a couple of beers, between one and three different snapple options and a couple of different soda cans (I don't drink soda so i was even more limited). Really it all comes down to a few factors: location, price, and the quality of food. If you can overlook the beverage choices and the small space, this is a great place to get your ramen!

Done Peppes, what can i say but amazing place! Traditional family New York style Italian dinning. Great Service, all right off the boat, put on a great show. Although I am a New Yorker ended up finding out about this place from friends of mine when our flights were canceled at JFK. They took me to a local place Don Peppes which they have been to before, this made the night. Foods is served in huge assortments for the whole family in the center and everyone is served on their own plates. Prices are great for the amount of food you get, really cant beat em. No menus, a large chalk board displays the selections and prices. Perfect al-dente pasta and some of the most tender veal you will ever see, the waiter cut the veal with a spoon it was so tender,! Remember cash only, otherwise you will pay up at this place believe me! Great place to bring a large group and perfect spot to impress a date. Top of the dinner with dessert with classic spumoni. Great italian food, love it, this is a must go.

From the outside, the signage and setup looked intriguing. Â I was disappointed with the wine (and selection).. the waitress was French speaking but seemed like she really had better things to do.. the biggest surprise were the crepes.. they were doughy, poorly seasoned and for anyone who have had good French crepes, I would suggest finding another place to spend your money. Â To be fair, we did not have the deserts that others rave about.

Totally amazing understated new place down on Myrtle near the subway! We have come here so many times I've lost count and have now tried everything on the menu at least once. Once they get their liquor license I sure hope more people will come and give it a try because the staff is amazingly friendly and the music is THE BEST, I personally love some old soul and blues music so having Otis Redding soundtrack my meals there is a great little perk. Service is fast and the food is delicious. HIGHLY RECOMMEND.

Ommegang and porchetta (with arugula and blue cheese)... yeeesssssss. Â I'm so glad I came here. I read a bunch "best of" yelp reviews and decided to hop onto my bike and ride on over. The ride itself was only 6 mins from my house, so that's a major plus. Upon entering, I was immediately seated. Another plus. I opted for the counter instead. Took out my laptop and immediately tried to go online. No dice. This place has no WiFi, which immediately means one star off. However the panini (porchetta with arugula and blue cheese) And beer (ommegang) was great -fantastic flavor for both. Wish the panini had a bit more pork, but whatever. I'm not usually a beer lady, but ommegang was fantastic. The counter guy is really chill, quick to serve and personable. Yes this place is a bit hipster, but the food is awesome. Slightly pricey for a panini and beer, but other reviewers are right when they say that this may be the best panini you've ever had. I'm definitely coming back.

This is a great spot in Astoria for some good ol' comfort food. If you're looking for a light and/or super healthy dinner, this probably isn't the place for you. This is the place for fried chicken, fantastic mac and cheese, and po' boys galore. It's also adorable inside, very fun design. Great pudding desserts as well. Recommended.
great happy hour! great lychee martinis!

This little Brooklyn Heights gem is the best Italian that I have had in NY. I visited this restaurant on several occasions, and have been pleased every time. This restaurant reminds me of a restaurant in Connecticut owned by good friends of mine, because it is simple, fresh italian. Don't mistake simple for red sauce and pasta- these are mostly authentic italian dishes. The dishes are just usually very elemental, created to highlight good quality components, rather than smother poor quality ingredients. My favorite dish is a special that is frequently featured- mussels in a light seafood sauce made with lobster. There is something about this sauce that is just sublime and amazing... and I can taste it as I sit here typing at my desk. The mussels that Noodle Pudding uses are large, clean, and plump, and absorb the flavor wonderfully. I also have tried and can recommend the beet ravioli, the venison ragu, and the buffalo mozzarella. That last item, the buffalo Mozzarella, is another favorite of mine, a creamy, silky cheese that perfectly compliments the drizzle of house olive oil that they pour over it. While the service at times has been curt and a little spotty, these were during very busy times, and was never rude or lacking enough to formally complain about. It is also pleasant to not have overly doting service when trying to enjoy good conversation and good food.

This place has the most amazing food. My absolute favorite place to eat in NYC. The artichoke appetizer is manifique, and so is the Chicken Parm and the soft shell crabs. I haven't even started on dessert, but if you're not full afterwards, I would recommend it. Great atmosphere and great food. Make sure you get to know the Maitre d', Brandon, he'll take good care of you. I wholeheartedly endorse the caprese appetizer, thin crust pizza, filet mignon, and chocolate cheesecake (to. die. for.)

We went here the first time just a day or two after it opened. We had a great time discussing the menu with the owner, who at that point had time to spend in the nearly empty place. That has changed now, and we are happy that this restaurant bermuda triangle has finally found a keeper. The moules and the truffles mac are the best thing on the menu, IMO. Brunch is also good here, and the space is really relaxed.
Amazing. Staff is always warm and friendly and very knowledgable! Great wine, great good. I live a few blocks away and will def be back many, many times.

One word: INSTITUTION. Â This is THE place to order middle eastern fare in a casual setting in NYC. Â There is no seating room to speak of but if it's a nice day its a short trek to WSQ Park and you can sit and eat your delicious Shawarma or Falafel right there.

I think it was because I was with wonderful people at the moment and it was the perfect timing and it was a good day and I was ready to watch Phantom of the Opera (which was really good!), I loved my experience at Juniors. The wait wasn't too ridiculous .. and rather fast. It amazed me since I was in Times Square. I had a Cobb Salad and for $15 dollars .. that salad was really something. It was ginormous and absolutely delicious and satisfying. It had everything in it and their balsamic vinaigrette was awesome. My boyfriend and his cousin liked their dishes as well and for dessert, we ordered a strawberry cheesecake. I have always been a fan so this was no need for words. Yum. Our waitress was also really friendly and on task. Our food came in godsend speed and I noticed although she was handling a big number of tables and customers, she remembered our wants too. Will probably try the one at Dekalb, just for comparison.
It's on the water. The burger is not bad.
The noodles are always delicious. I've gone here quite a few times & the roasted duck noodle soup is my favorite.

I don't know about you, but I like my Sangria ingredients to spend some time to get to know each other...hang out together...play a little bit....a menage a quatre if you will. But it's hard to be impressed when the bartender makes it in front of you with some fruit juice, simple syrup, a few slices of pear, and red wine out of a jug. I have a personal addiction to sangria fruit, because I can get drunk off those delicious suckers without ever having to pour liquid down my throat. The fruit should be fully marinated in the goodness - not plopped into the mix 5 seconds before you stir it together. Am I right or am I right? On another note, this restaurant is the size of a closet. How they cram so many people in there is magic itself. But not comfortable magic, because you are constantly nudged and elbowed while people pass by. I came on a busy Friday night, and was told that my wait would be 45 minutes for my party of 3. Unfortunately, 45 minutes later, the wait was still another 45 minutes. However, we were lucky enough to be able to sit at the "bar" and got in a lil sooner. I say "bar" because it's about 4 feet long and 1.5 feet wide. It's a counter space that can sit 4, where the bartender makes his drinks on top of a fridge due to lack of space. The food is decent, but it doesn't make my eyes roll to the back of my head. I don't remember hearing any moaning during the stuffage either - which to me indicates that it was A-OK but not amazing.. The Lowdown on Food: -Red Pear Sangria: a pretty good mix, but nothing you can't make at home in a few minutes -Grilled Octopus: good amount, but a little chewy and not as tasty as other grilled octopus (try Casa Mono or Bocca di Bacco) -Baby Lamp Chops: tasty, pretty tender and no overbearing "Hello, I'm LAMB" smell -Seared Ahi Tuna: well seared and seasoned -Chicken Empanadas: pretty good but nothing spectacular -Egg Noodle Paella: Don't think Asian style "egg noodle" - it looks like skinny Macaroni. Not bad paella though. -Mushroom/Setas: It's ok -Patatas Bravas: not bad -Grilled Prawns: pretty good grilled flavor to it...but a lot of their dishes have a grilled flavor... All in all, a decent tapas joint for a date or a small party. If you have some lady friend that you want to get close to, but haven't gotten the chance, this cramped space will allow you to make a move w/o being obvious. You can play the "Oh I'm sorry, I didn't mean to touch you there...someone pushed by behind me" card You can thank me for that little piece of advice later :)

Way way way overrated. Had lamb shawerma. You wouldn't even know it's lamb. Almost no flavor. Definitely no flavor of lamb. DUH. What's the point? Bland, borrrrring. The bulgar the same. Another big nothin' in sleepy Forest Hills, the world's capital of Big Nothin' restaurants and pubs. Some of 'em get raves...they don't deserve 'em. It's just that they're in Forest Hills...where everyone's desperate. Try food like this elsewhere...where it has, y'know...flavor. Was really looking forward to a lamb dish. How is it possible to eradicate all flavor of lamb? Forest Hills is the worst for food. Service was okay...food was meh. Won't be coming back. Don't believe the hype just because you're desperate to go out in Forest Hills.

Delicious thin crust, Naples style pizza in a delightful environment. Â I came here with a Yelp friend and we split a 16'' pizza with mozzerella cheese, basil, and truffle oil. Â The pizza ($23) was a enough for 2 people and definitely left us fully satisfied. Â  The decor is adorable and I loved the details such as the upside down chair and table. Â It is a small pizza parlor so it does get very crowded on weekends. Â There is also a bar area with some chairs where you can sit and eat or order a glass of vino while you are waiting for your table. Â  The waitstaff was great! Our pizza came out so quickly and our waiter was constantly filling up our water glasses. Â  Notes: Cash only. Come on a weeknight so you don't have to fight the crowds.

Great place to grab a quick lunch or a light dinner. Their sandwiches are fresh and tasty. Tons of ingredients and combinations. Their pho sandwhich is a yummy american twist on Viatnamese Pho. Haven't tried any breakfast sandwiches yet though. This is a staple in my diet when I'm on the go.

Food: LOVE LOVE LOVE THE BASH BURGER!!! Absolutely the best burger I've ever had! Cooked to perfection, both taste and texture. Goes perfect with the sweet potato or waffle fries! YUM! Can't wait to go back! Service: Our waitress was pretty attentive and was knowledgeable about the menu. Water was constantly refilled without being asked.
This place was on point. Meat falling off the bone, buckets for the bones, awesome Mac n cheese. Definatly a keeper. Will be going back

Where do I start? Practically the only reason I walked in is because all other restaurants in the area were packed. Upon arrival I had to specify several times to three different people that "yes, it is just me" - I guess a female dining alone during lunch hour is something unheard of. And if you are hoping for a table - bring company. All of you solo losers will be seated at the bar or at a communal table facing kitchen. I actually wanted a table as I was planning on reading a magazine and having a few of my gadgets around. I didn't make it into the dining room and tried to fit my ipad on the tiny space sitting on something resembling bar stool. Now the food: it was a chilly day and I ordered oyster and clam stew to start. Look, I am not spoiled. I was hungry and would totally settle for a mediocre hot soup. In addition to weird taste, I ended up with severe stomach ache later. Considering it happened about 3 hours after my meal and this was the only food I had, it is pretty accurate to state that this was the reason. My next dish was Fricassee of wild mushrooms with polenta. Damn, how I wish I ordered a sandwich instead. There was one on the menu, but I decided to step away from typical lunch meal and try something new, considering this place's reputation. Polenta was over salted and mushrooms were tasteless. I live in the neighborhood and this lunch experience scratched this place of my dinner plans map. I am kinda sad Â - wanted to try their burger and "next plate" on my communal table fries did look good.
Came here for a date, and was completely amazed by the service, food, and atmosphere. I had 5 courses and all were to perfection!

I am lucky enough to work a few blocks from this location!! Pinto is a great Thai place; it has a nice cozy and cool vibe about it. I can confidently say that their pad thai here is one of the best, if not THE best, pad thais I've ever eaten. With an $8 lunch special that comes with a salad, your choice of appetizer and entree - what's not to love?? Seriously, you are kidding yourself if you think you can find a cheaper lunch spot in the West Village that comes with all that food (and if you do, can you please share the info?!). My usual order is the fried potatoes with mayo sauce as an appetizer (mayo sauce = YUM!!), and shrimp pad thai for the entree.
