I'd say I've eaten pad thai from lots of places, and so many of these places make it too sour/greasy to the point where it's not appetizing... Pinto is NOT one of these places. AND if you love shrimp like me, you'll know that places usu charge more for shrimp as your choice of meat --- but Pinto does not!! Shout out to the thai iced tea there!! It's super cute how they serve it: a cup of tea ice cubes, and condensed milk and syrup on the side so it *feels* like you're making it yourself. It's also delicious. A+ !! The service is great too! The waiters are very respectful and attentive. Tip: if you order to go, call in ahead of time; I had to wait 15 min once when I didn't. I have been back and will keep going back.

one of my favorite restaurants in the city. it is so hard to find a place that has great food, ambiance, good for a date or for a group of friends, and all at a reasonable price... but this is it! there is always a wait so get there before you are starving. the bar next door is a pleasant enough waiting spot, though it also gets crowded with all of the other people waiting for their bianca table. you can get bottles of wine starting at ~$40 to ease the wait time. once you finally get your table at bianca, the servers are very efficient. note that i did not say charming, caring, or even necessarily nice. but they are efficient. some of my favorite menu items are the fried artichokes, seafood tagliolini (they put in a lot of seafood!), lasagna, and fritto misto (which i usually get as an appetizer to share). they also frequently have dinner specials which sound too delicious to pass up. every time i go, i am ready to go back again immediately.
Awesome Pizza!! White pie is great with lots of garlic. Yum~~getting hungry just thinking about it! Â + +

Little Owl is THE BEST. Delicious food, cozy atmosphere, excellent service. The bad news is also the good news: so tiny! The small size makes for an intimate experience, but also means it's tough to get a table, If you're regular, they remember you, though. If you have to wait, it's lovely to wait in the little elevated love seat if you can get it. Very romantic.
Excellent food. Friendly service. Small menu, but all the dishes are the chef's specialties.

I love this place, one of my favorite places to go for a delicious meal at a fantastic price. Â The French menu is short, simple, and delicious. Â Staples like French onion soup, salad with goat cheese, and meat and chicken dishes populate the menu. Â The place is really small and cozy, not for big groups, but perfext for great conversation with a friend over a bottle fo wine (BYOB, no corking fee, clutch). Â The waitstaff is accomodating and efficient. Â They let you take time to enjoy your meal rather than rushing you, even though there is always a line at the door of people waiting to be seated. Â Come with a bottle of wine and your best friend and you will be sure to have a lovely experience.
You are looking for Roast pig with rice? They have it. Roast pig with noodle? They have it. Roast pig noodle soup? They have it. Whole Roast pig or baby pig? They have it
I love Bonnie's. The burger is great, the wings are hot, and the fries are perfect. I'm glad they started delivering, although if you can wait for a table, the atmosphere is relaxed and inviting.
Delicious noodles and duck. Cons: cash only and not very clean looking.

The best thing about this place is the Mac Attack, IMHO. Came here a bit early for dinner last Friday and we split the Mac Attack and each got a salad. The best mac was the Truffle (big surprise), then Bacon-Gouda then the 3 Cheese one. I had the kale salad with mint which I loved and my companion had the spinach salad and said it was delish. I was pretty disappointed with my glass of Pinot Noir, but I guess I am a little picky. The atmosphere is modern/sterile and cool but not really my style. However, they do have great outdoor seating which was a game-changer this past weekend. The waitstaff definitely fit in with the Chelsea vibe, if you catch my drift, and were super nice, especially when we knocked over a wine glass. Fortunately it was empty because spilled wine is NOT cool! Apparently this place is open 24 hours, in which case it would make a fantastic late night dining spot. Truffle mac & cheese at 4am? Yes please.

This is a great new addition to the neighborhood. So far everything I've had is delicious. Great brunch! The eggs florentine were perfectly done and the french toast was superb. La Gigogne is also nice for dinner. Salads are fresh and flavorful, spatzle terrific. I haven't tried the tartes flambees yet but they look pretty tasty. The atmosphere is welcoming and the service is friendly and attentive. Eat here!

My husband and I love this place. There's not a lot of good restaurants around the area and the food is delicious and fancy enough to make up for the cheesy decor and bad music. Faves - mussels in garlic/white wine sauce, special veal chop, steak au poivre, special risotto, banana pancakes, the crispy bacon the brunch dishes come with, good coffee, steak frites lunch, Kronenbourg on tap, and the free chocolate truffle that comes with the check. We have had bad waiters, but we have also had great waiters. As mentioned above, the decor isn't the best, and the bad music can be loud. But the FOOD is mostly excellent and the price is right. Windsor Terrace is all the better for having such an establishment. P.S. The "L'Petit" instead of "Le Petit" used to bother me too. But the food is too good, I got over it.

My brother likes coming here, so I usually oblige when he visits Manhattan. The atmosphere is fun (it's a great spot to hang out with friends), and the food is decent. My favorite dish here is their brussel sprouts with yogurt and bacon. As the restaurant is so named, one should probably order a dish with bacon here. The dishes here are quite simple- nothing too intricate- but what can one expect with bacon.

This place was definitely not what I was expecting when I came here with my girlfriend. This was more of a family style Italian dish restaurant but the food was still great. My girlfriend and I nearly finished the penne a la vodka which was delicious. The mixed drinks were pretty strong and not too overpriced for a midtown spot. I'd come back again sometime but probably not without a bunch of people.

Go in a large group, then you can try more things on the menu. Â But do make reservations way ahead of time. Â  The place is slightly below street level and kind of hidden. Â Easy to walk pass it by accident. Get the brussel sprouts, preferably 2 orders of it if you're in a group. Â I don't normally eat brussel sprouts, but I'll eat it here. Â It's savory with the right amount of crisp on the outside. Â I also liked the bacon wrapped dates and braised short rib. Â  Ambience can be a bit loud at times, but tolerable.

The food was really excellent.The produce was very fresh and the food was very clean tasting but also flavorful. My water cress salad and vegetable pasta dish both had very unique flavors that were unlike anything I'd tasted before. I would like to say that I wish there were more vegetarian options. I've heard such great things about the burgers, so I'd love to see a unique veggie burger. I also found that the wait staff could not give me a clear answer on the ingredients in the dishes I asked about, which is of great concern to me as a vegetarian and a person with food allergies. I would recommend Crescent Grill to a friend but until there are more vegetarian options on the menu that I can be sure I can eat because I know the ingredients, I don't see this as a place I would return again and again, which is a shame because I did enjoy my meal.
Good drinks, good food and good prices! Â I will definitely come back. I loved the Capirinha drink, beef tacos, calamari, mussels. Â Would definitely come back!

I didn't understand anything that I read about Eataly. Â I just, like.... didn't get it. Having a free day to do whatever I wanted (which happened to be my birthday!), I endeavored to figure out what this mythical grocery store/restaurant/wine bar was all about. It was pure pleasure from the moment I got through the doors. I felt like I was in a tiny, bustling, indoor Italian town piazza, complete with a market, specialty food shops and restaurants. Â Everyone enjoying Eataly could have been Italian, as far as I'm concerned. It was all the things I love, right in front of me, behind me, over my shoulder, to the left, to the right, across the room... everywhere. ADD in the best way possible. The sexiest way possible. I smelled the cheese counter, I saw link ropes of sausage draped across the meat counter. Â I heard a sizzle of something being cooked in a hot pan. Â The aroma of wine made circles around my nose as I passed through the center, where people were standing at high tables, indulging in midafternoon vino. Â I saw a million different pastas, and touched a huge wheel of Parmesan cheese that reminded me of an experience I had in Rome. Pasta and cheese. If I could eat it for every meal, I would. Deciding that it was perfectly acceptable to eat a full pasta dish at 3:30 or 4:00 pm (hey, dinner wasn't 'til 9:30!), we immediately got a table for two at the pasta restaurant at the back. Â Cacio e pepe. The intense pleasure I derive from this simple dish was exacerbated by the al dente spaghetti, the most perfect simple sauce and hints of cheese therein, and the fresh cracked pepper. Â I wanted it all for myself. Eataly = gluttony? I don't care. It's my birthday, after all. Â Cacio e pepe for me, per piacere! Sensory overload in that moment, almost exactly a week ago, has prevented me from writing a clear, organized review. Â I guess I didn't understand anything I read about Eataly because it was too good to believe, too wonderful to conceptualize. But having seen it for myself... I get it. It might not be perfect for everyone, but for me, it was heavenly.

This is the place I recommend to friends for Thai. The food is incendiary, reasonably priced and closer to real Thai than any place in Manhattan. I usually love and can handle spicy food; here, I have to order medium spicy or else I'm guzzling the Thai ice tea with my chow. I love the diffrent range of curries--sour fish, jungle curry.Interestingly enough, I don't love the Pad Thai here--thought it lacked something. Stick to the curries if you come. Oh, it's a an easy trek from Midtown if you take the E/F to Jackson Heights and then walk. The Woodside station has always confused me.
The best in New York , definitely worth the wait.
We visited Eataly in January and ate at the restaurant Manzo

I couldn't be happier that this place exists, especially so close to me!! A huge fan of cute, sweet, little places and an even bigger fan of crepes, I was THRILLED to doscover that they make them it of buckwheat! I'm a bit sensitive to white flour and usually, have some nagging feeling when I have a crepe that it's not in my interests..that is, until I saw this place. It was love at first sight. And, not only are the crepes amazing and somewhat healthy, they are huge and will deflnately fill you up. And, the salads are also generous and perfectly dressed with a homemade dressing. I always get a crepe when I am there and think it is the best place to eat in NYC as far as French food and crepes go. My waitress and chef are from Belgium and they are so kind and down to earth and approachable Couldn't be happier with this gem. Do yourself a favor amd check it out. You won't be disappointed.

Went to dinner with a friend on Friday night, and was pleasantly surprised. The food ranged from solid to excellent, and overall, we really enjoyed our meal. Despite the uber-modern, we're-trying-really-hard-to-look-Miami-esque decor, the service was prompt and pleasant. Highlights food-wise: + Deep fried poached eggs with caviar and creme fraiche appetizer. Um. Yah. Need I say more? + Glazed short ribs with parsnip puree. Our server told us it was the best dish on the menu. I don't doubt him. I almost licked the plate. + Crispy sea bass with portabello "fries" -- so good. The not-so-highlights: + Chili crab dumplings app was mediocre, and compared to the deep fried poached eggs, basically non-existent flavour-wise. + The dessert menu. Lackluster options, including a molten chocolate cake. Seriously? The petits-fours green tea chocolate cake that they gave us, though, however, was excellent. I would have paid for a full-sized portion of that as a dessert. All in all, a wonderful dining experience. It wasn't obscenely priced, and in fact, they have a very reasonable tasting menu ($68) and an even more ridiculously priced spring promo for $38 (or maybe it was $36) if you get there before 6pm on weekends. I would definitely go back to this restaurant for another meal.

I'd like to state upfront that it is definitely not worth the wait. We went during a weekday and arrived around 11:50AM, and was told by the hostess (a very lovely girl) that the wait would be 1.5 hours! Usually, they like to pad themselves but really we did wait that long. Thank God for the app they have otherwise I would have bored myself with the wait since there isn't a lot to do nearby. I will admit that I ordered something I wouldn't have liked so I can't fault them for my poor choices in ordering. My friend ordered the eggs benedict with salmon and it was OK. It wasn't bad but I'd rather have my eggs benedict on an english muffin. My issue is with the texture. With the salmon and the eggs/sauce over the biscuit - it's just a mouth full of MUSH. Plus, I prefer my yolk a little more runny. The pancakes on the other hand, OMG, they were amazing and delicious!!! Stick to ordering that if you ever go. Overall, the food just doesn't justify the wait time. I won't be going again so I'll be stuck trying to perfect my own pancakes at home. At least now I know to mix my maple syrup with butter and warm that up.

Nothing but great things to say about Hillstone on 53rd. You run a class act - everything is exactly what you would want it to be. You arrive down the stairs from the lobby of the Citi building, the place is always buzzing and full - when you are told there is a wait, do not fret - turnaround is quick in this place, so step to the bar, order a Negroni, listen to the live Jazz band, watch the views. The hostess then collects you and whisks you off to your table - none Â of this normal NY approach, if you haven't paid your drinks tab, they just transfer it to your table - very nice touch. I know the menu so well now that the whole explanation from the server is not necessary, but want to say that the staff are fantastic all around. Always attentive, always fast. The room is a moody, hip space filled with booths that you sink into, privacy between other diners ... you could spent the whole evening here. A final shout out to the front desk staff - despite the absolute hundreds of people that flow through the doors, you remember who we are after a little while. A complete surprise, but yet another of the reasons we keep coming back. My favorite dinner, the artichoke dip and the California burger . Simple, but perfect.

I first tried Grimaldi's midweek at 3 pm on a warm summer day. I expected two things...a short off hours line and to find out that the pizza was over-hyped. Neither was true! Â There was a 45 minute wait and the pizza was incredible! Since I was alone, I beat the line by getting a pizza to go, then walking it over to a nearby park where I ate more than half the pizza! Â The rest made it to about 9 pm that night :-) If you like good pizza, this is the place to go!

This review is just for the strawberry cheesecake :). Â I went into their Bakery which is adjacent to the restaurant and really just a cheesecake take out place. The strawberry cheesecake is a big, thick slice with lots of strawberries and syrup on top. Â But the syrup is not overwhelmingly sweet. Â Instead it nicely complements the full body goodness of the cheesecake. Â Junior's cheesecake is so light and fluffy yet still creamy - so by the time I'm done I still feel like I have room for more! I need to branch out and explore other flavors but the strawberry one is just sooo good!

i lived 300 feet away from this place and my habitual menu is: raw artichokes for appetizer carafe of montepulciano spaghetti di chitara chicken cutlet you put that all together and and I'll ignore the ok service don't forget your cash (only)

My wife and I attended Joe's Shanghai on a Friday night and was greeted with a long line out the door. Â After our long wait the soup dumplings were worth the wait. Â In addition the sesame chicken was delicious. Â Absolutely worth the trip!

Great new spot in the neighborhood. I had the escarole salad to start, which was absolutely to die for, and the hangar steak...perfectly cooked! My friend had the panzanella and duck soup (so different, creative & delicious!) definitely a must try!

The fries were delicious and unlike any I have had before. I am not sure how they got them like that, but they were great! I wasnt sure of which sauces to try as I planned on getting the trio, and the guy behind the counter saw my hesitation and asked if I would like to try a sample so I asked which he recommends and he gave me 4 to taste. I tasted the Mango Chutney Mayo first and Wow! My decision was made. I tried the other 3, only 1 of which I remember was honey mustard, they were all so-so. Â I knew I Â wanted hot crispy fries dipped only in that sweet succulent sauce, which had a bit of a spice and tang to it! I am a huge fan of dipping sauces and thiswas one of my all time favorites I have ever had. The fries were perfectly golden and crispy on the outside with a warm potato mush inside. I saved the big ones for my husband to eat as I picked through and devoured all the small crunchies, double dipping every single fry. The place is small and there was a line out the door, which isnt very long since it is so small. They had mellow music playing inside, and the 2 guys behind the counter had a very calming effect on me, as they seamlessy helped the customers. We scored the best table there which was right out side of the door. Anyways, the fries were awesome and that sauce..ohhhh that sauce!!! I dont regret not trying any others, and when (not if) we go back I dont think I would even have the urge to try a different one.
Absolutely lovely dining experience. There is not a bad seat in the restaurant and the service is impeccable. The empanadas were fantastic, as was their amazing take on fried chicken.

Perfect in every way. We had: duck meatballs - yes, as good as everyone says. My husband is asking me to re-create them. (yeah, right) watermelon "prosciutto" - i love me some fish sauce & citrus so this was perfect for me. I wanted to lick the plate. On the fence about the asparagus ice cream, kind of wierd but kind of good. slow poached salmon - perfect, loved the lychees hangar steak (husband's) - this topped his previous favorite hangar steak roasted peach sundae - ginger ice cream was delicious, not overpowering at all. Honestly, the rest of the dessert was pretty forgettable. If we lived in NYC, we'd definetely visit this place often. LOVED. IT. Sad we didn't have enough time to get to Kin Shop...maybe next time!

Great pizza. Nice little hole in the wall ambience. Limited menu but clearly you only come here for the pizza, and watching mark make it. If you're lucky, he just might make you his special nutella desert pie.
Good Service, Have to make reservations first, otherwise it would be a lonnng wait!! French Toast and Johnny are my favorite... the roasted tomato hollandaise is sooo good!!!!!!
Great food...nice atmosphere and the Punta Cana sangria was unbelievable....decent prices....great service...never had to ask for anything....
Great Brunch
Great food! Will put you to sleep!
Get the Gyu-Don (thinly sliced beef over rice) it's the best- for a great price too! Also they have pretty good drink deals and udon. Fast and friendly service.

The cheesecake = 5 stars. Tried both the strawberry cheesecake and devil's food cheesecake. I love whatever recipe they use for their cheesecake filling; so smooth and creamy, cannot get enough! This is being picky of me (I say picky because I will eat anything that resembles a donut cookie cake brownie pie muffin and love it) but I really wish they used a graham cracker crust versus a regular pie-type crust! Maybe they just want to stick to the original? But, that would have put it above and beyond for me. I recommend getting an original cheesecake or an original with a berry topping (blueberry, strawberry, etc.) if it's your first time here so you can experience the cheesecake amazingness full throttle. The food = 3 stars. Nothing special, pretty fresh, expensive for what you get. My boyfriend got the turkey/pastrami on rye and was charged extra to add tomatoes and onions so his sandwich, sans any sides, ended up being $15+ (dry turkey to boot). My house salad with feta added was $10+ (lots of fresh veggies though which was nice). Not quite worth the moola if you ask me. This location is busy (obviously!) but the service was great. Our waitress, Grace, was extremely patient and on top of her game. I'd average everything out and give Junior's 4 stars. Bottom line, come here for dessert with Grace! You won't regret it.

Traditional in many ways: Service, food, and ambiance. Â  We waited at least a half hour past our reservation and the manager was kind enough to offer us a drink from the bar. Â  Dining with four? Â Split a Black Label Burger as an appetizer. Â You will NOT regret this. Â The only thing you may regret is having to share the burger with the rest of your party. Â BUT... this will allow you to leave room to share a larger and more magnificent piece of meat... the Dry Aged CÃ´te de Boeuf. Â Yesssssssss. Â I just don't see myself becoming a vegetarian any time soon. Â  Note: I'm not a big fan of the desserts here.

Thank god they opened a Mexican restaurant on my block. I was getting tired of Chinese and Brazilian. Lol! This place just opened and the decor is fabulous. I ordered the guacamole and chips and it was yummy. Also, I ordered the chicken taco and it was flavorful. Overall, I recommend this place and I hope it does well.

Hip atmosphere. I recommend the fried sweet potato and squash served with a tangy vinegar sauce. Â Although I found the green sauced coconut rice with pork ribs delicious; I was disappointed because I was expecting the pork ribs to be grilled. Â It turned out, it's braised pork ribs. Â I told them that they should describe the pork ribs as braised as I usually associate pork ribs with grilling. Â I also recommend the brussel sprouts with bacon. Â Hopefully, it didn't have sodium nitrite. Â They couldn't answer me if it did or not. I like this place because it's not the usual Thai food that's predictable. It's almost too dark for me. Â It's very hard to read the menu or one's bill!

Yeah, I did it. Â I stood in line for 40 minutes to get into Grimaldi's. Â I slurped down half a large pizza with pepperoni and mushrooms, then ordered a second. Â And I am not ashamed. Expect a wait, but I'm not telling you anything you haven't heard before.

Oh Junior's, like a bottle service only Manhattan party girl turned Jersey housewife, you've let yourself go!!! Â The strawberry cheesecake used to be my favorite, but it's been stank the last few times I've tried it. Â It's great that you use fresh strawberries rather than canned goo, but you need to be more sensitive above its shelf life. Â Nothing can ruin a cheesecake experience like a huge partially rotten strawberry. Â The actual cheesecake itself is still creamy and delectable, but the toppings have consistently gone so far downhill. Â You'd think with all their tourist turnover their fruit toppings wouldn't have time to spoil!!!

So my boyfriend and I were in New York on vacation. Â It being New York, we wanted to find the best pizza, not necessarily New York - style, but just the best, and Artichoke's was mentioned around when we were Googling. Â It was a little walk from the subway, but absolutely worth it! Â This place is so astonishingly small, but these stars are all for the food. Â We had 2 artichoke's and a slice of sicilian between the 2 of us. Â And the slices were large! Â The artichoke slice was absolutely amazing. Â It melted in my mouth and it was so creamy. Â I just kept eating it. Â The sicilian was good too, but I remember the artichoke one the most because I think it was that good. Â After we were done, we were waddling out of there because our bellies were so full. Â One slice is seriously REALLY large!! Â Each and every time someone says they're going to New York, I ALWAYS recommend going here for pizza. Â I can't wait to go back to New York for this pizza. Â I've been craving it so much.

Went to The Spotted Pig on a Sunday afternoon. I loved it....the deviled eggs were amazing and the bartender made an awesome Pimm's Cup. My husband and I split the Burger with Roquefort Cheese, it's plenty for two people. The burger was just ok, Â but the fries were some of the best fries I have ever had. They were so light and yummy with little Â bits of fried rosemary throughout. My only complaint, is that the service was terribly slow that day. I live Dallas but travel to NYC often, I definitely will return.

as it states in my profile, if i was able to have one last meal before getting the electric chair, it would be lombardi's... Â the all white pizza is literally a slice of heaven, but so is just the regular cheese... Â  let me put it to you this way, after leaving the east coast to be implanted in the west, i have done it a couple times where i catch the red eye out, grab a couple of pies from lombardi's, inhale them, and then catch the red eye back to LA... Â insanity?? Â maybe, but once you have a lombardi's, you will understand...

Stopped in for our first welcome back to Brooklyn meal and pretty impressed. Â The hot chicken was good, loved the kale, but I must say the coleslaw was to killer. Overall though, my favorite thing was the Tennessee Jam Jar. Â  Wait staff was nice and attentive. Â Only downfall, the space is tight. Â Otherwise, cocktails looked reasonable, beer selection was above average. Â I look forward to stopping by again.
Great staff and apps. Â Not the best ramen, ZuZu on 4th is much better. Â If you want apps definitely get their chicken, potstickers, shushito peppers, and their friend brussel sprouts (when avail).

Great sicilian pizza! Love the amounts of sauce and cheese on their squares. Pkus the dough is so chewy which I love. Minus the one star because sometimes their sauce on the pizza can come out overly salty. It really depends which pizza are you getting your slices from.

My wife and I were visiting in the neighborhood last week and stopped by Caffe Linda based on quite a few good reviews on Yelp. Frankly, I don't understand the high reviews. The food wasn't bad, but it certainly wasn't anything special. Pretty mediocre, really. I had chicken piccata and I enjoyed it. But I've had better many, many times, including at home. I don't remember what my wife had, but her reaction was the same. We had a good bottle of wine, an OK dinner, and an overall good experience, though with a hefty total bill. But, mostly, it was a good evening because it's a comfortable place with a friendly staff. If their food was better, they could be a real winner.

I got their teen wolf, which is their falafel wrapped in a fig and pomegranate dough. I loved how they took raw dough and cooked the wrap right in front of me. soo cool. BUT their falafel itself was TOO SALTY and a bit undercooked and mushy in the middle. no good. Â  and despite how cool the concept is, the dough flavored dough did little to elevate the entire wrap. maybe it's because the falafel's saltiness was overwhelming. hoping the saltiness was a one time oversight. i might come back again and try their other veg option with cauliflower. it might also make a difference if you eat your wrap right away. i got mine to go and ate it an hour later.

Service is good and the staff is nice and personable but I'm Italian and this is not even close to the Italian pizza. It's good food don't get me wrong, but it's not Italian style. So all in al it is fair but not worthy the long wait.
best pizza in new york. nothing more to say.
Great food for an extremely low price! It would be 5 but the only problem is that its to small and hard to get a seat.
Breakfast and lunch at this cafe is wonderful. Â I can't say enough wonderful things about their menu. Â Service is good, average. Â Atmosphere is so-so. Â But I come here for the food period.

We came here for dinner twice and the food was superb both times. The staff was very friendly and attentive and the atmosphere was great. The owner, Dan, came over to greet us and was so well-spoken and gracious. I can't wait to try their brunch menu!
the juke box is good and underrated.

Best pizza I have ever eaten. If I were to make a list of pizza places to visit this would be #1 FOREVER. This restaurant alone is a good reason to come to NY. Only drawback is due to it's super goodness and off the chart out of this world deliciousness AKA taste-bud stroke inducing capabilities its really popular. So if you come here a bit too late (around 6) you will wait in line for a long time. I waited for about an hour ........... ANNNDDDD it was worth it. Skip to this part if you don't want to fry your brain with useless made up words depicting how good this place is. Basically if you like come here. If you don't like pizza come here. If you don't live in NY fly to NY then come here. If you're too young to fly to NY wait until you get old enough then come here. If you're too old to fly here threaten to take away their allowance and get them to bring you here. Skip to this part if you're actually trying to get something useful out of this review. This place is awesome just go try it then marry it.

Bistango is a solid italian/pasta shop, with quality ingredients and interesting combinations. It can get really busy, and the space can get a little overwhelming if you go during the weekend. I can vouch for the pappardelle with short rib ragu - if that appeals to you, go for it. Supposedly the chicken is good as well, although I haven't tried it personally. For those of you that have allergies, this place might be your savior - the waitress firsts asks what everyone's allergies are, and I think many of the options are (or can be) gluten free.
Great coffee, good ambiance, no kitchen (bad food, microwaved eggs). If only they had good food...
It's summer and I cannot stress more the importance of outdoor seating! Â 5 minute wait, great date, a crusty goat cheese sandwich and some sparkling raspberry lemonade. Â Great place for brunch.

I came here with my boyfriend for his 30th birthday dinner and had an amazing time. Â We had been following Chef Forgione on The Next Iron Chef, so was bowled over when he came out to personally wish my boyfriend a happy 30th. The staff were really friendly and encouraging towards all the menu choices that we made. Â For appetizers, we ordered the chili lobster in a sriracha sauce with Texas toast and the crab cake special. Â My boyfriend thought the crab cake was the best that he had ever had. Â This was followed by Casco Bay cod (medley of seafood) and LI duck Elvis Presley for entrees, finishing with Lady Ashton's chocolate cake and pecan pie bread pudding for dessert. The food was amazingly good and included mini compliments from the chef, in the form of a spoonful of pumpkin soup, one potato chip with dip and a shot of green tea sorbet. Â My boyfriend thought his duck was phenomenal, but I thought my Casco Bay seafood ensemble was a bit peculiar, consisting of one shrimp, a couple of scallops, clams, mussels and a piece of cod. Â I would definitely come back again, but wouldn't order the Casco Bay cod in future. This is a great place for a romantic dinner, date or even to come with a group of friends. Â Even the bar area looks like a fun place to have a couple of drinks.

Cool vibe and awesome bartenders! Cannot wait to go back for the summer months since they seem to have a spacious backyard. Cool lighting and very clean, crisp feel which is a nice change of pace compared to some of the dive bars I have gone to.

A friend of mine who has lived in NYC his whole said I have to eat pizza at Lombardi's. Â I am a food snob and my wife is a pizza snob so it is hard to impress us... Â This place was AWESOME!!! Â When we walked up to it there were people waiting all over the place and all around the place so we were very worried. Â We only waited about 30 minutes so we thought that was impressive. Â It is hard to decide what you want as you walk through the place and see all kinds of interesting pizza's. Â I read one review on Yelp before we came and the person said order extra mozzarella and this person could not be more right. Â Order extra mozzarella!!! Â  We got one large pizza and half was pepperoni and the other was meatball with basil and mushrooms. Â A large is easy to split as the crust is thin and amazing. Â We also had great and friendly service!!! Many people around us had the clam and seafood pizza and they were eating it like crazy. Â Next time we go we are going to try that pizza for sure. Get off your couch and go see the world!!! Â Go to NYC and get a real slice of New York Pie!!! Enjoy what you eat and enjoy your life!!!

I know that not everyong out there is a fan of jane but I am! I've eaten brunch here several times and I really enjoy the ambiance (not too loud, pretty laid back, and generally a nice, comfortable place to eat a nice meal) and the food has always been consistent for me. of course the dilemma with brunch is whether you should get sweet or salty and my recs for both are the following: challah french toast for sweet - which is REALLY huge, rich and sweet, if you're not into rich and sweet, I'd say avoid this; and benedict johnny (or jane... whichever one consists of the corn patty on the bottom) for salty - I love corn, eggs and hollendaise sauce and putting all these things together makes me TOTALLY love this dish. I've eaten dinner here before as well and the steak is pretty good!

I loved their dumplings. So much that I ate them near constantly for months. Now, I can barely look at dumplings without wanting to puke. That's not their fault, though, and their dumplings remain delicious and cheap. They are pork and chives boiled in thin skins. You can get 12 for $3 or 8 for $2--doesn't get better than that. You can also get 50 frozen dumplings for only $9. Their other food is so-so, in my opinion. I've tried their rice noodles with beef in broth, and it was extremely plain, and the noodles in peanut sauce just tasted like peanut butter. Not my thing.

My friends all love it. Grilled snails are so good that we ordered 4 plates. Quiche is very nice, especially the one with bacon and onion. Small plates are good and really small! If you have a group over 4 ppl, better double the order. Sandwich is good for hungry guys. Menu is short, for large group, you can try all the dishes on the paper. It's funny that another group of people holding their pre-halloween party in this tiny place. It gets crowded and noisy. But not annoying as the place provides the right mood for that. Service is sweet... but they are super busy sometimes you cannot find the right one to take the orders.
Luzzo's is THE pizza in New York. It rocks!
One of the best dates I have ever been on! Their Valentines day menu was amazing, and the wine pairing was great too. I love the decor, and the service is excellent. I would love to go back!

GREAT location, so-so pizza. Sorry, Grimaldi's. I wanted to like you, I really did. It was on my list of places to try on the East Coast and sadly, the experience just didn't measure up. The pizza was all right, decent but not memorable in the slightest. Forgot about it as soon as we walked out, in fact. Waiters + service was great, though. Cute and accommodating, just how I like 'em.

My favorite burger spot in New York, but I can't go too often because I order too much every single time I come here. It's just so good it's hard to help yourself. The bacon sliders are my favorite and the Guinness shake is really good, though I've never been able to finish it by myself. Even the Candied Bacon shake was surprisingly good. It can be super crowded on the weekends, but it's totally worth it.

This is our third time in this incredible place, and it never fails. The quality of food compared to the price is ridiculous- one of the best places to get your steak on! Plus outside garden, great music and atmosphere, and to top this: an incredibly sweet and respectful waiter that always offers us a shot of grappa even though we refuse to have dessert. We love PT!

Blue Ribbon, for me at least, reminds me of a better, nicer, and more expensive version of La Folia. Â A bit of an obscure restaurant, it does a nice job of flying under the radar for most of the public while being a staple for serious foodies in NYC. Â The secretive location helps to achieve this, as well as the intimate setting of the restaurant itself. Â Lastly, and perhaps most importantly, they do not take reservations. Â While 90% of the time this is super annoying, it serves to make this restaurant accessible to anyone who is down to wait long enough or to eat at an obscure time. Â I think certain restaurants (Otto comes to mind quite quickly) suffer from the fact that after word got out of the good food at reasonable prices, it became pretty difficult to get a table due to the hordes of tourists fighting for a seat. Â Now, I subscribe to the philosophy that anyone should be entitled to experience fantastic, progressive cuisine-whether you were born on the Upper East Side and have been on the cutting edge of food your entire life, or if you are from Iowa and in NYC for a weekend, where permeating the boundaries of your own food comfort zone is ordering a steak medium. Â Although it makes it annoying to get a table at some of the great restaurants, we should all take solace in the fact that fabulous cuisine is accessible to anyone-even if it does mean we have to call 2 weeks in advance to get a table for two at 7pm on the weekend. Â Blue Ribbon, then, serves to remedy that by their no-reservation policy. Â  Now, as for the food itself, it was stupendous. Â The highlight of the meal was definitely the buttery, succulent bone marrow. Â Everyone else had some type of fish, I had catfish atop perfectly cooked spinach. Â The toasted bread that the bone marrow was served on served as an interesting contrast to the richness of the marrow, and ultimately, having huge bones show up at your table looks carnal and awesome. Â  The service was great, and my only compliant were the drinks. Â The three of us started off with a bottle of wine which we finished off before we got to the entrees, at which point we ordered some cocktails to accompany the food. Â In short, all three were awful. Â My cocktail was least-awful, in the sense that the leathery taste of it wasn't completely vomit-inducing, so I sucked it down. Â My friends were not as fortunate as I-their $15 cocktails were set aside after a sip. It was fairly pricey-about $100/person for a shared appetizer, an entrÃ©e, a bottle of wine split between three of us, tax, and tip.

I have not been DISAPPOINTED in awhile and even more so because I've been wanting to try this place for awhile after reading the good reviews. First off my annoyance was I tried to make reservations on Open Table to get points but it said all the tables were booked so we walk in for brunch and the whole place was empty. What's up with that?? Then the waitress was clearly new and very unprofessional (as in flirting with the other waiter and then standing there staring at us for awhile...uhh awkward) so that made things unpleasant throughout the whole meal. Two of us ordered hot and cold coffee and it was BAD. Â Their explanation was the coffee was from Colombia and its just strong but believe me I've had Colombian and Italian coffee and this weird taste was not because it was "strong." So I didnt drink mine at all. Then my friend ordered the steak and the waitress explained the dish wrong so when she changed her order, the waitress made it seem like it was impossible to changer the order. The food was ok and the portions were not that big. Of course the waitress dropped the silverware on me when she cleared the table, got our check wrong by forgetting to take off the steak (and the nice thing to do would have been to take off the coffee) and acted like it was so difficult to correct HER mistake of charging us for more. Also why is the menu so unclear and why did it say AMEX only when it's not? The only upside of the place was that I liked the decor. I think the waitress ruined our whole meal and experience at Yerba, who knows maybe if we had someone else it would have been at least OK.

Amazing food, large portions (for ostensibly mezze), beautiful decor, lovely service. I wish I lived here just so I could come back. Prices seemed a bit high, but given the actual amount of food per plate, were actually reasonable. The lamb gyro was good and twice as big as I expected, the the eggplant-pomegranate-syrup dish was FANTABULOUS. Spiced fries were also good. I was still full from lunch and couldn't finish my food, and couldn't take it with me to a Broadway show... very sad. I wanted the rest of that eggplant, dammit.

Warning: you may get addicted to their guacamole! Its simply amazing. The restaurant itself is so tiny, can only fit 10-20 people at most. The food here is not bad, not the best Mexican restaurant in the city, but not bad at all. I have enjoyed the meal we had here with my brothers. Its a great place to come and have lunch or branch. For a dinner however, you might need to wait for an hour to find a seat, so I'm not sure if this will be worth it. They have a good bar, friendly barman, and great margaritas - so fresh. Great tequila list! I have tried their: Arrachera- taco with steak with avocado (4/5) Calamari - squid with avacodo salsa (4/5) Ensalada De Mango - salad (mango, mixed greens, shrimp and you guessed it - avacado) (3/5)

Ah Westville, sweet sweet Westville. You never let me down. Westville is a neighborhood spot. It's not swanky or glamorous but it's definitely not lame either. Westville is just no frills, it's usually for people who live in the neighborhood and want some good, fairly healthy food that tastes like Mom made it, thus the need for the many locations. Westville is less of a destination and more of a comfort. Don't get me wrong though. I do actually go out of my way for Westville simply because: 1. I live in Brooklyn and we don't have one and 2. it is incredibly consistent. The food is always good, the sides rotate depending on the in season greens, and there is never an astronomically long wait. It's my go to spot if we want to have a good impromptu dinner on a busy weekend night. Westville is not necessarily good for big groups though. Despite multiple locations, each restaurant tends to be on the smaller side, with close seating. This is more of a 4 person or less, casually catch up with your friends, kind of place. Menu breakdown: theunitedstatesofk.wordpâ€¦

Went here for brunch today. Avoided the 20 min wait by taking seats at the bar. Enjoyed the coziness and charm of this place, as previous reviewers have already described. The "pumpkin" waffles were very good. Full of flavor, and moist. WARNING: "fakin bacon" doesn't even come close. It's very tempeh like and not so bacon like. I say go for the real deal or none at all. Cappuccino is worthy, but have a double cause the cups are small. Overall, a little pricey, but worth it for the homemadeness and real maple syrup.

As a regular diner at this place I will be honest with you- Robertas is mad cool. The long low wooden tables are just my taste, I like a place with awesome food and not a lot of show. The selections of beer and wine are nice, they have super expanded their seating in the back and outside where there is another bar... and then they have events they are super fun and cool. Again, cool. Everyone who works here and eats here looks so cool. Sometimes its a bit annoying and people are putting on airs everywhere, but I can deal with it, because the food is AWESOME. The food is $$$, dont get me wrong, but so many items are local/fresh/grown BY ROBERTAS that I think it's worth it. Simple dishes with tons of flavor. The cuttlefish and the scallops are perennial favorites, and all the pizzas are good- order 3 with a group of 4 and get a lot of awesomeness for cheapish. The service has never been 100% on point but the place is usually mobbed by all the wealthy artists in the area with no where else to go (yet) that is as cool as they are. There is often a wait by the bar which is cramped but again, I can deal, because this place is just so cool.

My sister recommended this new spot in my old neighborhood. She raved about their pulled pork sandwich. I love me some pulled pork, but I've had it in some of the best places in the Carolina's and Arkansas, so I was skeptical. I gotta say, pretty damn good!! Best pulled pork north of the Mason-Dixon Line!!! Oh and their iced coffee is off the hook!!!

We stopped in for a to-go order before heading back to the apartment. Upon taking a gander at the menu, the cool, casual setting, and the happy-looking patrons, we instantly wished we'd made time & plans to eat here. Next time! We opted for the same thing: pork chop banh mi ($7 each.) I love vietnamese sandwiches -- the crusty french bread, pickled veggies, often time a mayo-loaded dressing -- but the meat is always a downer for me. So not the case at Saigon Shack; I was pleasantly surprised to find the thin, salty pork chop the star of the show! It had very little fat or oiliness. Looking forward to eating this again...with a bowl of pho! Cash only.

OMG. I don't know about the rest of the menu but of what we ordered - both were to DIE for! Vanilla Bean French Toast: Hands down, this is the best french toast I have ever had in my entire life. I don't know how they make it so fluffy inside but it is amazing. Roasted Shrimp Ranchero: the black bean sauce and the cheese and eggs and avocados just melted in my mouth and exploded with flavor

This place is okay. The pizza dough was the best thing about the restaurant. The pizza was rather small, rather expensive, and didn't have any of the pop I expected from reading the reviews. The mozzarella wasn't adequately salted and thus tasted very plain. The tomatoes tasted like greenhouse tomatoes, none of that grown-in-the-sun flavor. I think that a 15 dollar pizza in the summer in the the NY/NJ area better have some freaking amazing tomato action (I mean we have awesome tomatoes in this area in the summer) Not sure if this was a mistake but our Arugula salad came undressed, when we asked for dressing just olive oil was dropped at the table, after a second request we got balsamic vinegar. Arugula salad is a pretty basic summer salad and is classically paired with parmesan, balsamic, and EVOO. Anyways this place wasn't bad, I was satisfied, my Â GF was not (she thought if she could ever get her family to visit NYC that her Italian uncle would have given the chef an earful in his broken italian-english) My summary is this place wasn't worth the money or the time considering the other proximal options. I would probably come back here for a drink as it had a sort of cool vibe.
Great food and service!! I have been here so many times and they have never upset me. Yes, to be honest, maybe a little expensive, but hey, it's a nice Japanese restaurant. Aren't they all?

Only been here once but when we went, the food was great. Â It was mussels night and each serving included at least two dozen mussels in a wonderful broth. The accompanying French fries were delicious. Â Will be back although we live in AZ!

On the hunt for a great mid-week breakfast, I stumbled upon Maialino. It was the perfect fit. My friends and I enjoyed a delicious and seasonal breakfast along with house-baked pastries. Everything was really reasonably priced! The location can't be beat, right by Gramercy Park. As expected at a Danny Meyer restaurant, the service here is great, and if the food isn't enough of a draw for you, the potential of being seated at a table next to Danny Meyer himself should be an added bonus. I felt very lucky at my breakfast! While in the presence of greatness, I dined on delicious eggs and pastries. What could be better? I would definitely revisit in the future, whether it's for breakfast, lunch or dinner.
Love this thai place long wait coz its pack most of the times but worth it! Love the shoft shell crab salad n the pork belly. This place will not disappoint you!

I miss Palo Santo. First, great dinners. I remember when it first opened and the chef/owner served up AMAZING chef's menu dinners. Everything was always perfect. Meats were cooked perfectly, savory, and never over-seasoned. Get the chicken offal grilled on skewers. Perfect latin street food! But the BRUNCH is TO DIE FOR. Every time I went, I always left stuffed. I loved the various fish (soft shell crab, even!) on grits, and the oh-so-delicious hash. The potato hash is also amazing, as is the whole baked plantain, served with sour cream topped with brown sugar. Mmmm!!! The decor is a little funny, with the knick knacks in the tables. They look too shiny when compared with the rustic decor.

The first time i went to Lombardis I could not for the life of me understand what all the hype was... Then I went with my absolute favorite new york person JC! JC introduced me to this special concoction pizza: Pepperonni, Pancetta, Roasted Peppers, and extra sauce! Holy mother of pizza, what a flavorful explosion on my tastebuds! Now, i get it... now i get why i have to wait an hour for a table here! Ok.. also... a very under rated item here is the salad! It has this special purple dressing and is so yummy! Get the salad people, vegetable are good for you.. and who knew they could taste so gooood!

I had wanted to go here, but then it completely slipped my mind when I was in the area. Â Luckily after my friend and I tried to go to the meatball shop and there was a half hour wait (Monday night 8:00) he remembered the Empire Diner was only an avenue away! Â We walked over, were greeted by the friendly host, and then seated right away. Â It is really cool inside, you feel like you're in an old fashioned diner. Â In an effort to try a bunch of things my friend and I decided we'd share everything. Â We started off with the French onion soup with the bagel bread pudding croutons.. amazing! Â No complaints here! Â Also as someone who loves cheese I find that French onion soup at times can actually be too cheesy, and that was not the case here. Â I thought it was a very good amount. Â  Next up we got the loaded potatoes and happy waitress. Â Both soo good! Â Seriously though, nothing we ate was bad. Â The potatoes had foie gras, bacon bits and jalapenos on top, and sour cream on the bottom, but it tasted much better than any sour cream I've ever had. Â The happy waitress was a poached egg sitting on a piece of taylor ham and something that seemed like a corn cake. Â Again, both were very good. Â Our main dish was the Lemon chicken. Â As someone who really isn't a huge fan of chicken this was great! Â It was very flavorful and kind of light, if that makes sense. Â It had ricotta on the side with some baby carrots and a giant piece of crispy skin. Finally we couldn't pass up dessert. Â Our waiter told us the pies they had and any other specials for the night, and we settled on apple pie with ice cream. Â So good, we finished it all! I was certainly stuffed after that meal! Â I really had no complaints though; everything we had was so good! Â And there were so many more items I wanted to try! Â I'm definitely planning on going back.

This place is great. I've lived in this neighborhood for 9 years and this is the first place I've Â felt was needed. I hear their chef is from from the south, he has made an amazing menu for sure! I can't wait to come back for more! Get here fast!

After visiting Japan, I never thought I would find another bowl of ramen that would be able to stand up to the likes of the mom and pop shops just outside of Tokyo. Well, I stand corrected. Now, there are plenty of places in LA that I frequent that have good ramen as well, but Ippudo is definitely the one and only spot in Manhattan that I enjoy getting my ramen from. Not only is the ramen perfectly cooked, the broth seems to have had a lot of attention and love put into it. And you can't visit Ippudo without ordering their pork belly buns. If you've gone here, and passed up on the buns, consider yourself unfortunate. I think the only problem I could potentially have about Ippudo is their pricing point. I mean, $16 for a bowl of ramen to most people who KNOW ramen, is absolutely ridiculous. But keeping everything else in mind, especially the locale and Manhattan's premiere foodie scene, it's to be expected.

so happy they opened another store in downtown! got the pork katsu curry for $7-9, which came with cole slaw on the side! the curry was not too sweet or too mild, had just a hint of spiciness. the pork katsu was crispy and well-portioned, but the rice was a bit dry, and needed more sauce to be soaked in...the place is small, but has about 10 seats, with a friendly staff and fun wall posting to look at! :)

Let me preface this by saying I went to their food truck at Pier 13 in Hoboken. I've been wanting to try a cheesesteak from Shorty's for the longest time, so I couldn't resist when I saw their truck in Hoboken. I got the buffalo chicken cheesesteak and it was OK. Nothing spectacular, but it hit the spot. Let's put it this way: I wouldn't be against eating another one. I do want to point out that the staff was on-point though. The guy who took my order was super friendly, as was the cook. While I was waiting for my food, another customer returned her sandwich... because it was too spicy. To me, that's ridiculous... you ordered it, you have to deal with it. But the guy took it back without any questions and made the lady a new sandwich. That's great customer service right there.

Not your typical ramen joint - there is actually walking and eating space. I didn't mind the long wait ... came here expecting really good ramen. Turned out the service was phenomenal, wait staff where very attentive and they made sure that our glass were never empty. However, I was only here like I said to judge the ramen; it wasn't mind blowing awesome ... it was okay, a tad pricy I feel - I had better. I will give it another try in the near future.

Awesome BBQ and mac and cheese here! As someone who goes to school in NC I very much enjoyed the ribs, fatty brisket, and pulled pork (their BBQ sauce is excellent as well). Also some really cool mac and cheese flavors (we had the original but still great) and a good variety of sides/desserts. Pecan pie was also delicious!
Wonderful place! Everyone who works there is so friendly and welcoming. I got a sangria and a tortilla espaÃ±ola. Super yummy! The tortilla tasted just like the ones I miss back in Spain :)
Warning: this spot gets packed!!!! Really good food and drinks. We sat at the bar and our bartender was charming and friendly. Bacon wrapped dates are a must!

Lamb, fish, cactus, and steak tacos were consumed. Lamb - delish. Fish - excellent. Cactus - interesting. Worth trying. Steak - spicy as hell. Watch out. They warn you, but take heed! Chips and salsa were ok. It's completely liquid salsa, so if you prefer the chunky style you may not be satisfied. Great prices, but it's pretty loud inside. Nice servers. I'd go back.

It's tough to beat a tasty falafel pita that doesn't cost more than the spare change in your pocket. It's tasty, it's filling, and it's cheap. Those three things aren't so easy to find in Manhattan, so I'll keep coming back to Mamoun's when I'm in the neighborhood. Just be warned, you're going to make a mess. Get extra napkins. Especially if you're a couple beers into your night.

Small yet beautiful dining area that is very charming amidst the chaotic 2nd avenue Subway work. The staff was very helpful, patient and engaged with providing a good dining experience. The Tarte Flambee's that we tried were delicious and filling. Can't wait to try some more and take advantage of the all you can eat special :)

4 years ago I moved to the neighborhood and tried this place out and was not impressed. 4 years later some girlfriends wanted to eat Vietnamese close to my apt so I said let's try this place. I AM VERY IMPRESSED!!!! Â  We order the fried spring rolls. Â DELICIOUS Peking Duck Banh Mi - WOW AWESOME Pho Special - EXCELLENT We had the pulled pork Banh Mi and that belongs at Dallas BBQ so we couldn't see it fitting in here. Give it a try. Â It gets packed during prime time but the wait is no longer than 30 mins

I wanted to love this place .... I am constantly going to Broadway shows and always need a new place to eat before (or after) the show. The food was okay -- but the service and customer relations was HORRIBLE. I don't ask for a lot ... but a few things .... Let's start when we walk in: It was about 6:30pm on a Saturday night. Â The place was empty. Â The hostess asks if we have a reservation - we didn't. Â She then does the typical NYC hostess thing where it looks like we're inconveniencing her because we don't have a reservation. Â  Anyway - she seats us, but while doing so, she informs us that someone else has a reservation for the table (in the empty dining room) at 8:30 and we have to be clear by then. Â I was speechless. Â Who says that? Â Really? Â Shocked. After being ignored for a while, our waiter finally shows up. Â We order our beers and they take forever to appear. Â I'm now joking with my girlfriend that we're gonna miss the cut-off because their service was slow, not because we were. We get out appetizers, delicious. Â But, before we were even halfway through them, our entrees show up. Â This is my biggest pet peeve in the world. Â At a restaurant that demands reservations and says they're going to kick you out of you're not done in time -- they should know how to time food service properly. Â  The our waiter disappears again. Â Throughout our whole meal he never comes by to ask our it is (my salmon is way over cooked, by the way) or refill our beers. Â We were finally able to flag down a bus boy to help us --- by the way -- the dinning room is still far from full! Meanwhile, the hostess shows up and tells the nice old people next to us (who had literally JUST paid) that they need to leave so that they can clear up the table .... Â  Finally we get our check and leave. Â  I know you're a theatre district restaurant, but seriously -- you can try a bit harder with the service, no?

I came here for my birthday dinner and had a great time! We reserved for a super early... 5:30PM dinner on a Friday. We had the restaurant all to ourselves. The large windows flood the dining room with an amazing and modern warmth that I'm sure is quite welcome on any wintry day. The bar is the centerpiece of the dining room, with exposed brick and high ceilings. The food was excellent and came out very promptly. Waiter service was attentive but not pushy, informative but not pretentious. I really think this place is just perfect for having a date, a hangout with a long-time dear friend, or for some straight up good food in a comfortable environment . I was super happy with my grilled arctic char. Char is this very buttery, smooth fish. The sweet corn was a great accompaniment. We also got the quinoa hushpuppies as a side, and they were great hot.

I cant believe I waited this long to go here! Their steamed buns are delicious! Its not that oily and the soup inside is really good. Its much better than Joe's Shanghai for about the same price. I also recommend their stir fried noodles, seasoning was perfect and it wasnt soggy nor too dry. There was also the preserved vegetables and chicken noodle soup- that I always get at a shanghai restaurant - but it was mediocre. Overall I enjoyed my meal and their service was not bad. and being a relatively new restaurant the decor is pretty. PLEASE... dont get just some fried rice and general taos chicken like the tourists I saw that day. *facepalm

I took a walk to Woodside today in hopes of exploring the neighborhood. I tried this place out and the lady was super friendly there. She was a one man show cooking, cleaning, and taking orders. The savory omelette crepe was very good too.

This place makes enormous banh mi, and if there were ever a banh mi size competition, Saigon would win, no question. I like that their pork is barbecued, but I find their sandwiches difficult to eat. They are so overstuffed that you can't get a bite that combines all of the salty, tangy, sweet, spicy and crunchy elements together, and when I eat banh mi, I want all of those flavors dancing simultaneously in my mouth.

Food: 4 Stars Service: 4 Stars This place is authentic Japanese cuisine. You can see it in their menu, their food, and the staff. I came here with a couple of friends for a weeknight dinner. We were in midtown and looking for something light and this hit the spot. Looking at their menu, they have a lot of interesting options that are definitely not typical offerings. I ordered a chicken katsu that was amazing. Huge portions with amazingly moist and chewy rice, crisp and fresh chicken and great egg within as well. Honestly the best chicken katsu I've ever had. I also ordered an appetizer of small japanese hotdogs. The waiter had recommended it given the uniqueness and me wanting some sort of appetizer to add to our meal. It was indeed interesting and cute. I can't say the taste was amazing, but I'm really glad that we tried something new at this restaurant. Service is great and the waiter was very patient and helpful. It seems to be a place where a lot of Japanese locals come to eat!
Yes. Please. More of this.

i live in california but when i went to visit my friends who live in brooklyn, i asked them if they had found any places yet that satiated their california mexican cravings. they took me to gueros to eat. i tried the fried avocado and jalopeno taco and the al pastor taco, both which were pretty tasty and a good portion for me (although the pineapple in the al pastor taco was...weird). my only complaint with the tacos were why only one tortilla to hold everything together? the standard should be TWO tortillas, otherwise everything tends to fall apart and get soggy. my consensus: not bad for NY mexican fare since all other mexican food out here SUCKS. if i was still living here, i'd come here to get my mexican fix. just add a 2nd tortilla to the tacos and we'll be okay.

I had the roquefort burger and shoestring fries when I was here. I loved the shoestring fries, and the burger was decent. It wasn't oh-my-god good, but you can only do so much with a bleu cheese burger. It's not a novel concept, but the ingredients were fresh and it was nicely done. Twenty bucks for burger and fries is a more than I normally pay, but this is a Michelin star restaurant in NYC, so it's priced for the location and circumstances. In Arkansas, we have burger places that will run you close to $15 for burger and fries. As long as the line isn't ridiculous, I wouldn't hesitate to return here for lunch with a friend. The chicken livers are calling my name.

Everything that there is to say about DiFara has been said and yes, it's as amazing as you've heard everyone say. let me confirm a few facts for you. -yes, it takes forever. watching the master at work makes the time ease by though. -yes, it's worth the trek, no matter what the distance is. -no, there is not any a/c, so beware of what days you decide to venture to the venue. (first time i ever went it was about 100 degrees out. very poor decision on my part.) -yes, the square pies will catch fire & fill the room up with smoke. i suggest taking breaks for fresh air outside. -go plain. i'm a purist & think its the only way to go. so do it. -DO NOT go here expecting to "pop in for a slice". it will more than likely take longer than you expect it to. -you're a fool for ordering a slice here anyway. your supposed to order pies. duh. -if you go for a slice, it will more than likely take 2x as long because Dom isn't so quick to keep the slices ready to dish out. there's a list. and an order. learn that. and if you INSIST on ordering a slice, order two. because you WILL want more than one after you finish it. -come before opening. line up. the pizza tour will jump in front of you any way you cut it, so be smart and show up before doors open after their mid-afternoon break. -never, ever, ever complain. you are LUCKY to be at DiFara. you are being given the privilege of eating the best pizza on the face of the earth. give the man a little respect. -if you have low sugar or act like a jerk when you're starving, bring a snack. -be polite. don't bug the man or his family when your order will be ready, because they don't want to hear it. take a peek at the list yourself and see how many names before yours have yet to be crossed off. this means: stay near the counter. -don't forget to say please and thank you and give him a sincere smile. he deserves much more than that, so don't be a jerk. you dear patron, are not any better than any other body walking in through that door. -also be sure to check their facebook to find out if they are open. they have been closed on Mondays & Tuesdays randomly and it would sure be a pity to travel all the way out there only to find out that they are closed.

If you can't make it right when they open aim to arrive about 1 hour afterwards so that you get seated in the second wave after the initial seating. At 8:40am we only waited for 20 mins before getting seated. Not bad at all. By the time we left at 10 the wait was MUCH longer. Yes - blueberry pancakes and the bacon are amazing. The biscuit disappointed all of us. It was as dry as what everyone said. Tons of Japanese tourists now taking selfies. Just an observation.

This place has the best brunch. The huevos rancheros is out of this world (and I don't usually even like that dish to begin with). The Irish coffee is also the best I've ever had anywhere. Laid back feel and friendly staff. Worth the hike to red hook!
Place is cute, but the pizza not so great. The crust was extremely soggy.

Best Brunch in Brooklyn!! Amazeballs! The line is no problem. Put your name on the list and then take a walk around the neighborhood. They will call you when your table is ready and all is good. Let me just say that the entire staff of Buttermilk Channel is a shining example of what excellent and caring customer service should look and feel like! While having brunch on a very busy Sunday, we brought an 11 month old child who was the center of attention. She was treated with the most amazing love and affection by so many of the servers and management. If you can find mgr Michael, he will make sure you are given the very best of what Buttermilk has to offer. Next, if you can request Chelsea as your server, she is truly fantastic. She will lead you through an exceptional dining experience. Â Warm, friendly, and caring. I truly could go on and on about how well we were treated here... Now for the food-- it's straight up Delish!!! No joke, the reason the line and wait are long is because the food rocks. We had a brunch feast and each item was perfectly seasoned. Portions were large, and so yummmmm. First off we were given a plate of sweet baked treats that satisfied every flavor sense. The scrambles were so tasty and fresh!! Every item we ordered was hot out of the kitchen and made to perfection. Even the prices are really fair for how high quality everything menu item is. Try a spicy Bloody Mary and you'll be having seconds for sure. Even the hash browns are crispy perfection. This place is fun, the vibe is pure and so incredibly inviting. From the music to the smiles, I am going to be craving this spot until my next visit to Brooklyn. Well done. Thank you for the remarkable experience!!
Had never had an arepa before coming to Caracas. Â I take all my Latin friends here and they love it. Â This is a really great restaurant .... Priced right so it is a regular hangout

Sincerely has to be one of the worst pizza experiences of my life... First of all, the prices per slice range between 4-5 dollars and pies between 24-30 dollars! The pizza did not taste good, crust was burnt, hard and stale, I'm actually surprised that they actually make it there and that it's not pre-made. Yet again another pizza place that does not live up to it's hype and the outer boroughs still prevail in having vastly superior pizza. Yes, that means the one in your neighborhood and still at an affordable price. The only pros of this place is if you're tired of the regular flavors of pizza they have an interesting combination of flavors, I just didn't like it. I had a margarita slice that was burnt and a artichoke slice that was very weird, to a point that when i threw away my garbage there were two more slices that only had several bites and then discarded. Beware

It's like a huge Italian shopping mall, full of Italian stuff. Â Pricey 'tho. Â You can get a box of Barilla pasta for $1.88 or less at Safeway, even $1 on sale, they sell it here for $ 2. Â But, they have all sorts of dried pasta from Italy, brands I've never seen before. Â Extremely hard to get a seat to eat during the lunch hour, full of people. Â We walked to several dining areas in here and they were all full. We waited for a long time for gelato because they only had one server. Â A medium cup was $5.90 and you can get 2 flavors, so we got chocolate and coconut but there was not an equal amt of coconut (less), so I felt cheated while hubby enjoyed his choc.

Here's my gripe about Lombardi's. Â The last time I went there with a group of six, we were escorted to the uh..."upper deck." Â Walk past all the nice people eating their italian whatnots. Â Go through the kitchen. Â up a narrow flight of stairs and there you will be seated in a "dining room" with about 6 tables outfitted with cheap red checkered tables and metal folding chairs. Â VERY LAME! Â Honestly I would rather be turned away than brought up there again. Pizza-wise, its just okay. Â Nothing to write home about. "Dear Mother, I've experienced PIZZA..!" Â  meh. 3 stars. Â Even my Peroni didn't taste as good as it usually does! Â And you know I looooooooove my Peroni.

Capri Cafe is a great option for a homemade quick bite. The tables are close together and it can get loud, but the quality of the food definitely makes up for it. The waiter and owner adds to the authentic feel of the restaurant. I would recommend any of their dishes. Don't be turned off by the subway rattling your plates as it passes underneath the restaurant. Capri Cafe is a great place to dine with locals for a quality meal.

Being from DC, I have to say I'm sadly underwhelmed. Came on a Tuesday afternoon close to 4pm; figured I could beat the lines since it was pretty off-time. Nope. Still waited a good 20 minutes (party of three). We were seated at a bar-style table; there's a small ledge to put your bags under the table and hooks on the side for jackets. Very cramped. Maybe seats 15 total. Staff was friendly and I guess everyone spoke Japanese, so I knew it was authentic which was a plus. Got the Miso Ramen; came with an egg, bean sprouts, green onion, and pork (can choose between pork & chicken). Honestly didn't know what to expect... They add a dollop of miso in the middle which makes the broth really thick once it's dissolved. Also, there was a definitive alcohol taste in there (probably sake) which was a little too strong for my liking. Everything else was average, but for me it's really the broth that makes or breaks it. Probably won't be going back whenever I come back to NY. Still like the local places around here better.
One time I had a meal here that was one of the best I'd ever had. Two other times, it was pretty good. That's what you get with tapas I guess.
All the good things said about this restaurant are true! Â Absolutely delicious! Â Everything was delicious! Â The pasta melts in your mouth!!

My mother's workplace is near this restaurant so we headed over for lunch. Pros: Very yummy Pork and Crab Xiao Long Baos. They taste the same as Joe's Shanghai dumplings. Shanghai Stir Fried Noodles is a must-try! I usually don't eat noodles of this thickness but the sauce they cook it with makes it worth trying. Wine Chicken is not that bad although I wish it was less oily. It is a decent portion considering some of the other places I've been to. Cons: Since the space is very small, be aware that you will have to wait if you're going during peak times such as noontime. It can get noisy but my mother and I chose a window seat near the front so it wasn't that bad (if I remembered correctly, this is the only window seat there). Overall, it's not the best place for shanghai food but it's still a good place to stop by

Good selection, fresh produce, good beers. Oysters were great and competitively priced. They are on ly a wine and beer place so too bad for you martini drinkers. Happy hour from open to 7pm. The cooked menu is limited and like to see more variety like fish or shrimp etc... Also like the temp of the oysters to be colder but overall a close second to Balthazar.
for 5.00 the lamb and rice is great this is a staple in ny. the lines are always long
Great food and service - a real NYC experience.

I was totally a beer person before I met a girl. She introduced me to the world of wine (I am not saying I am an expert by any means... I just become more appreciative of wine in general...^^) and Gottino. Although she is just a distant memory now, I still remember and visit Gottino. It is a small and cute wine bar that offers a lot of Italian wine. There is an outdoor garden, nothing fancy though. The waiters really know their wine and I have never been disappointed with the wine they recommended. More of a place to enjoy a quiet evening with drink a glass of wine or two. Definitely not flashy, but very charming. They do serve small plates, but I don't remember any of them being worth mentioning.

The MOST amazing Valentines Day was spent here. While my husband is a total catch, it wasn't him that made this holiday special.....it was Bistango! The gluten free bread warmed my soul. The dipping sauce, perfection. The wine, perfection. The service was perfection, topped with the owner greeting us and sitting down to ask us about our meal and my journey being gluten-free. I will tell everyone I know, GF or not, visit Bistango! AND if you take a girl here for a date, bonus points. It is very romantic.

Pastrami Butter. Car Bomb Hit Chocolate. Fried Chicken. Shrimp and Grits. Vanilla Chai Doughnut holes. Duck Gumbo. All amazing! Â Our group managed to order almost everything on the menu tonight and there was NOTHING left in any dish! Â This comfy place doesn't have a lot of seating, but it feels cozy, the food is incredible, the service was friendly and swift. Could not have asked for anything more. Â Put this place on your list!
Loved the omelette that was stuffed with bacon and cheese and the cheese blintzes were incredible. Didn't love out table as a draft was blowing on us entire time. But great breakfast place.
Not bad Â specially Cali rolls , but litle pricey .

I did it a couple times, survived the line for some excellent food. Yes on weekend the line is long, yes you are sometimes outside in the rain or sun. But its worth it. Yes Tom's is an original, zagat rated and famous. It is worth it. The pancakes are famous and so are waffles. Now the Huevo Ranchero are favorite. The Cherry Lime Ricky best I have ever had. So suck it up wait in line and enjoy!
Awesome food and quick service. Spicy option is not 'burn your mouth off' spicy so if you like a little heat, go for it.

I had great expectations for this place, after seeing it on food network and mtv (p.diddy loves it). My bf being a cheesecake connoisseur wasnt impressed, yes it was good cheesecake but we both agreed cheesecake factory is better. his cheesecake didnt really have a crust. Some delights very innovative like the " strawberry shortcake cheesecake" Â was alright, but i felt it couldve been executed better. -the strawberries in the cheesecake didnt taste fresh, it was like preserved strawberry jelly mush in the cheesecake.

Frankenstein tourist ramen that eats more like a fusion hotpot. Â This is mini mall style ramen in hungry man portions. Â The quantity is enormous. Â But the pork chashu is too big and chewy, eats almost like a pork roast or pork chop, or dare I say Korean samgyupsal. Â The broth is odd looking, a weird grey hue across the board. Â The consistency of the broth is even weirder, it is super thick and it's not a rich fatty kinda thick, more approaching something reminiscent of a Korean jigae stew to a cornstarchy sauce. Â I ordered both a Spicy miso and Toroniku. Â  Where's my pork cheek meat? Â They just add a very rubbery piece of Chashu. Â Waiter said it's Toroniku broth. Â Whatever. Â You get the picture. Â Any place that serves a "Kimchi ramen" isn't Japanese ramen. Â My guess is it's Korean interpretation of Japanese ramen, as I see side dishes of Kimchi and banchan style bean sprouts. Â I give it two stars because if it wasn't sold as ramen, I would not be comparing it to something that it claims to be. Â Not horrible. Â Not good.

Four of us went here for Thanksgiving and had the prix fixe menu. Â The food was wonderful, but what really made our night was our excellent waiter. Â He was truly passionate about the food and made great suggestions about what to order. Â He made sure we got to try a little of everything on the menu, and was so proud of the food he was serving. Â I'd love to go back here for a meal off the regular menu.

Great, well considered food in a comfortable setting. The location means it's probably overlooked, but we've had two meals here and both were EXCELLENT. I don't agree with the review that calls it expensive. It's completely commensurate with a restaurant of its quality in Manhattan. My wife and I actually were surprised by how little we paid. Today we shared a starter, didn't hold back on the mains, and both got a drink -- the bill was under $100, including tax. Our only real complaint is that the bar has let down the quality of the food -- our drinks have been 'just OK' and not worth their cost. Thoughtful drinks improperly or lazily made. Still... There are tons of great options in Manhattan, but we'll definitely be coming back.

Myself and a colleague went here off online recommendations on how this was the best cheesecake in New York. We both agreed it was a disappointment. Cheesecake was incredibly heavy and on the dry side. I've had better homemade and at the Cheesecake Factory, and from my grocer's frozen section. It was however the best part of the experience.
