I had a brisket that must have been pure fat. It was not good at all. I literally could eat very little with trying to work my way through it to find any actual meat. Potato pancakes and matzoh soup were okay, but nothing that blew me away. Onion rings were awful. No flavor whatsoever. My colleague ordered a roast beef sandwich and it was awfully dry. They really need to step up their game. I imagine most of their clientele are one time tourists who do not return. I would never go back here and could not recommend it to any of my friends to waste their time on a New York eating experience.

I'm a concierge at a hotel and a Hell's Kitchen resident. I've recommended this place to so many of my clients and friends and after speaking to one of my chef pals felt like a little bacon fix. I've worked for the likes of Thomas Keller, so I know a thing or two about food. I ordered the grilled cheese as I had many times before. What makes this sandwich so special is the bread and the toasted bread and bacon combo with the tartness of the cheese meeting the sweetness of the bread . I love this sandwich and was craving it after work. What I got was a stale white bread sandwich , fatty bacon , and cheese. The cheese was melted but it looked like it went through a toaster oven with the bacon on top, some of the bacon came out undercooked . Definitely not the food I raved about since this place opened. Seriously disappointed. The soup was so so I basically could have had Campbell's soup chicken corn chowder and fared better, actually miss the tomato soup. Definitely changed my review of BarBacon... And any future clients I send over .

by far my favorite slice in the city! Â the only bad thing about this place is the line that it generates, and the slightly inefficent way they handle orders, but i cut them a lot of slack, because the crowd is insane and for good reason! Â the pizza is amazing. they offer four slices: crab, margarhita, scilian, and of course, artichoke. Â the first ive never had, i loathe seafood, and hot crab dip on pizza sounds revolting to me - BUT - Â ive heard from many friends that it is really good; the margarhita is wonderful, your traditional ny large triangular slice with fresh tomatoe, basis, and cheese; the artichoke is basically spinach artichoke dip on pizza crust, and is every bit as wonderful as youd expect. Â the best slice, however, is the scilian, a square and therefore crispier version of the margahita slice. Â it can be a little oily, but they use only EVOO that is drizzled on after it comes out of the oven, and that is also when they add the fresh basil (otherwise, the basil would burn in the brick oven, so smart!) and where else can you get a slice this good for only $3.50 nand a $5 big gulp of bud or budlight? in a convienent to go cup that no one will ever suspect is beer expect to wait in a long line, no matter the time or weather; ive made the mistake of taking several out of town guests here, and on return trips, i am forced to wait in line regardless of circumstance: yes, liz, im refferring to the time you made me wait for a slice at 5am in the rain for over an hour...but ultimately, it WAS worth it ;) the owners have expanded to a new zeppole and ice cream place next door, and also are opening a roast beef sandwich shop nearby, the empire building begins.....

I came with my family on Sunday to have a good brunch in a place with basically "good reviews " After waiting 20 min outside , we were waiting 20 more min to get what we ordered : 2 omelets , granola yogurt Â and pancake... The value of our money for the small plates ( accept for the pancakes ) Was not worth it.... Definitely we will not return here.. A Tip for the waiters : if you are packed it's not the costumers faults , try and keep on smiling...

Frankie's 457 has really yummy comfort food. The dishes are big and delicious. I have had the eggplant parmesan and the brown butter pasta with sausage. Both dishes are great and I would recommend them. Overall Frankie's 457 is a really good Italian restaurant!

This place is a good time... not only do you get to eat some delicious food, but there is some good hipster watchin' action as well. The food was great. I would highly recommend the brisket and the sausage. Both were perfect. The ribs were good. The pulled pork was kinda what ever. But the real reason you should go here is the bourbon... the selection is fantastic, and the prices are somewhat reasonable, and on top of that they have the best ice cube in Brooklyn (those of you that have been here know what I'm talking about). The only complaints I have are the above mentioned what ever pulled pork, and the face that the bar tender did not know any thing about bourbon... If I'm going to a place that claims to have one of the best bourbon selections in Brooklyn I would appreciate a little direction from the person who's serving me.....

Okay, so I read the reviews and they were excellent so I said let me try it. Horrible Idea! The food had no flavor and by the way I got the oxtail. It was an extremely small portion. I guess the people that reviewed this place were skinny people that do not like food that has flavor in it. I personally like a food that is well seasoned, has flavor and is reasonable in size. This place had none of those. Horrible and never ever will I get anything from them again.

So, I was brought here by a friend when we needed a place to sit, talk and eat some good food and I've been back every two weeks. The grilled cheese is bomb (you definitely should add bacon) , tater tots to die for and you must get tomato soup to dunk everything in. The atmosphere is very chill. They usually have sports on and change it to the game of your choice if you ask so I was able to watch the Knicks lose again. The staff is extremely friendly and fun to talk to. I like how they change the name of those tip jar. Basically if you are looking to eat good food, chill environment and a couple of laughs, you should check this place out.
nice setting and very good food. Â portions are small so eat an apple before you leave home! Â service was very attentive. Â will prob go back.

So I went here with a friend who lives nearby and I can't say it was the highlight of my week. Â The fabled artichoke and spinach pizza is essentially spinach-artichoke dip poured over a pizza crust. Â It was pretty darn tasty for about half a slice, but then it just gets to be too much and a couple of slices would just make you sick. Â We also tried the margherita and the sicilian. Â Both were just average and a little burnt. This is a take out place with no place to sit down, though they do sell draft beer. Â The crust here is thick and doughy, more like a foccacia, not crisp yet chewy like a good pizza crust should be. Â There were only a couple of people there when we went in on a Wednesday night and we waited just a couple of minutes, so I'm glad I didn't stand on the line others have complained about. Â So, overall, I won't be hustling down to 14th Street for this stuff, but I've had a lot worse.

A great place to order lunch on Seamless Web! Â Too bad their $20 minimum for delivery means I will not likely be a regular though. Â Oh well. I went with a small "hot and soup soup" (their spelling) ($1.75) and the shrimp with Szechuan chili sauce ($14.95). Â The hot and sour soup as it were was just functional and did not stand out with its flavors in any way. Â I would have preferred more piquancy at the least. Â The shrimp entree was considerably better though. Â I was surprised to see jumbo shrimp and so many of them at that. Â Better yet, they were perfectly prepared making them tender to the bite and full of flavor. Â Flavor really abounded here as the shrimp were literally engulfed in a more than generous serving of the sauce. Â All around it was a solid dish that my rice sopped up wonderfully. Â The clear slight here was that sauce was not really spicy in any way, a typically lament for Seamless Web orders. Â A great value, and I would be sure to order this dish again and try a few others. Â The high minimum order price tag will prevent me from doing that when I have to order for one though. Â However, I will check them out in person.

after a long wait of 12 years, i finally made it to the halal cart Â (next to hilton) on this trip to NYC. we (my 2 friends and I) waited in a long line on a cold windy night (around 8pm). bought 2 meat shawarmas, 1 chicken shawarma and 1 meat biryani (with rice). costed us 22$. the food was ok, nothing compared to my earlier experience. in fact, i had to lie to my friends by saying that the food was great, Â cuz i made them wait and eat in the cold weather. the only saving grace was their hot sauce. maybe it was an off-day ... but i guess my craze for their food is over... next!

I would have to say that this place is pretty bad when comparing it to other BBQ joints in the NYC area. My boyfriend got the brisket and burnt ends. they were lacking in moisture and when I went to snag a bite I did not want another. I'm usually a big fan of brisket. I got the brisket Philly cheesesteak which was again lacking in moisture and drowned in cheese sauce. The music was too horrible (pop punk) to ignore, also no alcohol! The macaroni and cheese was pretty bad and mash potatoes were cold. Not going back.
Happy hour the only way to go! Chunky guacamole, thin tortilla chips, and other hh samplers really good. Regular menu pricey.

My palate is ridiculously small. Â The list of things that I won't eat is way bigger than what I will eat. Â If any protein besides beef, pork, chicken or fish is put in front of me, I tend to pass it to my always more adventurous dining partners. Â That being said, I prefer dives rather than "tasting menu" restaurants like Atera. Â If I feel out of place because I'm wearing jeans and a golf shirt, I get uncomfortable, no matter how good the food is. However, my friend wanted to take me here for my birthday and I figured WNYOLO (Why Not You Only Live Once). Â I'm glad I came because as I look at the tasting log that they hand you at the end of the meal (in expensive paper stock) I thoroughly enjoyed myself. Â I ate things that I would never have dreamt up in an acid trip. Â Fried lichen chips. Â Squid ink sauce. Â  Sea urchin. Â Beer foam macarons. Â There was quite a bit of sophisticated molecular gastronomy going on here, and almost everything tasted good to great. Â There were 1 or 2 things that I didn't care for too much, but batting a thousand out of 20 tries is an impossible thing to ask out of any restaurant. The service was impeccable. Â The servers are all men, and good looking men at that, so eye candy alert for the ladies. Â Your meal will be about three hours long, and they handhold very well. Â Making good small talk, eye contact, and attentiveness. Â These guys probably have day jobs at Bergdorf's. Â Expect the check to be in line with Bergdorf's, as a peek at the check came out to about $150 per person. One of the fun things about the place is finding it. Â There is no sign outside the entrance that says "Atera". Â A kind employee will come out to get you if you have the befuddled look standing in the street.
You can eat a massive meal and get completely drunk for under 10 dollars. Do you have any idea what you're eating or drinking? Maybe not. But it's tasty. Who cares?
Manhattanites took the subway into Brooklyn and were wowed by the excellent food, service and ambiance of Stone Park Cafe. Â Will be back! Â Everything was fresh, well-prepared and delicious.

This was my first experience with Grey Dogs on 16th. Â Who knew there were three fabulous locations. Â Grey dogs is always my favorite brunch in the city, but the lines are usually so long no one will wait in them with me. Â This location is maybe 3 times larger than the union square location yet the lines seem even longer. Â I got there five minutes after my friend and the line moves quickly, so we only had to wait a few minutes. Â Just like at the other locations, they promise that when your food is ready you'll have a place to sit. Â The difference with this location is they dont shoo you out, so we lingered for an extra hour. Â Free refills on coffee, no additional cost for swapping out homefries for mixed fruit salad, and your "customizable best brunch ever" is always less than $15 bucks. Â Love at first bite. Â I"m still full from yesterdays brunch binge.

Comparison word tests for you summer-school kids: Cowgirl Sea Horse is to nachos what John Wayne was to Western Movies. Cowgirl Sea Horse is to margaritas what Johnny Cash was to 20th Century Musicians. Cowgirl Sea Horse is to ambiance, simplicity and amazingness what Chuck Norris was to Pop Culture jokes. Done.

There are so many thai restaurants in NYC, specifically in Hell's Kitchen, that it can become very difficult to differentiate one from another. Luckily, Pure Thai Cookhouse manages to stand out with some of the better thai food I have tried in the city. It's a very small restaurant, and we ended up having to wait in the very confined space for about 30 minutes, but it was worth it. We started with the chicken curry puffs, which were really good. Small, but fluffy and delicious. I also got the grilled spicy beef salad. It was excellent. I got the medium spicy level and that was just spicy enough for me. It was the perfect amount of salty and spicy, I could have easily ordered that as my entree. I decided to go with the chicken pad thai since it's usually what I order and I would be able to compare it against other thai restaurants. Pure's pad thai was definitely one of the best, it had a much stronger flavor than the typical pad thai and it was absolutely scorching when it came out of the kitchen. Add in a couple singhas and I am a very happy camper. I would return to Pure Thai Cookhouse without a moment of hesitation.

Right off the bat we had reservations for 8pm and were told rather rudely by the hostess/waiter/owner Mario we might have to wait about 20-30 minutes I was not happy I asked if we could wait at the bar and was no it was occupied with someone eating there. This restaurant is really small and we had to wait by the front door the alternative was waiting outside in the freezing cold. Mario came back about 10 minutes later and offered a small table by the bar that had become available we accepted just to get out of the front door. We were offered the specials but never asked if we wanted drinks so I had to flag someone down to place a drink order. I ordered the stuff clams and for the entree the fruiti di mare which were good my fiancÃ©e ordered the mozzarella and the pasta with sausage and broccoli which she really didn't Â care for. We needed to flag someone down for just about everything drinks, desserts and the check so overall the food was ok but not worth the hassle of having to grab someone just to get basic service. This establishment would be served with just hiring a real waiter and letting Mario go to an office hopefully off site and let someone who knows what they are doing to manage the front of the house.

The service here was excellent, water always filled and very friendly staff. Scallops were delicious, the braised short rib on the risotto was heavenly, the duck and foie gras ravioli is a sin, SO FREAKING GOOD, and the spaghetti reminded me of a delicious margarita pizza in pasta form. YUMMY. I'll be back

I went here for a lovely Sunday brunch. Go early-- we got there right at 12 and didn't have to wait. When we left at about 1:15, there was quite a line. All four of us had the $12 prixe fixe and felt it was well worth it. Â  I had the eggs benedict which was great. My friends had the yogurt/granola, the apple pancakes, and the goat cheese/spinach omelette. Everyone was pleased. If you are looking for "authentic Italian" this is not your place. But if you are looking for a great, bright, cheery, no-fuss brunch spot, check this place out.
Great food and excellent beer selection. Â The octopus is delicious.

Maybe we hit Chef's Table on a good night, but I found the food, atmosphere and service to be impeccable and our meal was one of the best, although incredibly rich, meals I've had in a long time. Definitely arrive promptly for your reservation - two of the diners in our seating arrived late and the chef started without them. Â We arrived with a 15 minute buffer so had plenty of time to sit, peruse the wine list and take it all in. Â We went with the 4 wine pairing (you can also do a 9 wine pairing) and happily the sommelier promised to email us all of the wines we drank after dinner so we could revisit the ones we liked. We ate 20+ dishes, including about 6 fish-based one-bite courses at the beginning. Â T and I have had a number of tasting menus before at other NYC spots but this one takes the cake. Â Each dish seemed almost better than the last with the flavors slowly building up in intensity. Â The flavor combinations were fresh and kept my palate interested - it's hard to remember every detail but there were hints of Asian influence in several of the dishes with a strong presence of seafood in all of our savory courses (just the last savory course was non-seafood, a perfect couple of pieces of squab). Â My definite favorite was the uber-decadent uni and truffle dish. Â Amazing. Â It makes my mouth water just thinking about it. The dishes do come at a pretty fast pace but it's amazing to sit, slowly chewing and tasting each course, while watching the chef and his staff carefully construct each dish. We also had an amazing cheese course (paired with nuts, honey and preserves, it was mind blowingly good) a sorbet course, a pastry course and chocolates at the end. Â These were all paired with a lovely sweet wine. Service was impeccable, our sommelier was friendly and the chef even chatted a bit with our side of the table in between courses, which was a nice extra touch. While it is terribly difficult to get a reservation and it's very formal and it's VERY expensive, I would recommend Chef's Table to any foodie and hope to come here again for another special occasion.

This place is average but the seating view tops it off. Across the street from Fairway, sitting on the patio and eating seafood. It doesn't get any better than that. They also have miniture golf downstairs in the back for a little entertainment. We ordered Fried calm strips which were breaded a little to much. The crab roll was amazing and let me craving more. Ordered crab royale which is combined with a load of seafood and it was filling and good. Can't really mess up putting seafood into boiling water. It was a little pricey for lunch but good overall.

Superb selection of food. Â Six plates are great for two people. Â You MUST try the infamous bacon doughnuts! Â I believe the menu is seasonal so what is on their website may not reflect what they are currently serving (at least in my case). Â I should have ordered everything on the menu because the chef has a way of incorporating unconventional ingredients (i.e. Strawberry-Cinnamon Baby Back Ribs) that send your taste buds on a journey.
Friendly staff, hearty food, reasonable prices, and a warm atmosphere. Can't complain.

I would have left this place zero star if I could cuz it's two words - rip-off. Burgers looked nothing like ones i saw in reviews AND their own menu - they were small and unstuffed. I had a pitifully tiny piece of tomato stuck inbetween the paddy and bread, which I had not noticed until I asked the waiter and he pointed it out. I could not help but laugh, and made the waiter feel a bit embarrassed. I bet you would feel embarrassed working for a rip off place...then there was one piece of lettuce, and when I don't discover the onions and many more extras that were in the menu, I brought my question to the waiter, who says he would bring me some extra sides. Holy lawd, I got another eye-sized tomato and one piece of lettuce. WHERE WAS MY ONIONS DOE?? I didn't bother anymore, and left no tip. Terrible experience, totally cheated me off my money.

I had an 8:15 reservation on 12/14 and kept being told it would be 5 minutes until a table was ready. At 8:50 we still hadn't been seated and had a show to be at by 10. The waiter/host was rude and made no effort to apologize for the wait, offer us a drink or just be honest and say it'd probably be best to leave so we could at least fit in a meal somewhere else before the 10 o'clock deadline. Would not go back here again.

Pier I is just like boat basin. same concept. by the water. gorgeous views. mediocre bar food and just a place to sit and drink. The location is really nice, although you have to seat yourself and literally have to hound and stalk people for a table. The food a meh. just your typical stuff of burgers, chicken fingers, etc. but I think they have a couple pasta dishes. There's also random fireworks sometimes, I think it comes from the jersey side which was a really nice touch especially if the weather is good. Great ambience, good date place as well, and you can stay and stare at the water and the view as long as you like. Nice place to hang out with good friends on warm summer nights.
Pretty good brunch. Â I recommend the pancakes and the steak sandwich.

Chic Organic Eats -- Fantastic Flavor If you haven't been this is a MUST TRY. Love the quality of the food and amount of thought that goes into each dish. Had a fantastic time with friends and was able to try many dishes. Cannot say which was my favorite as they were all delicious. The atmosphere is clean and warm, and I've been told their brunch is also equally as fantastic. Date Rating: 9 Pick up Scale: 3 Strong Suggestion: come hungry.

Clinton Street Baking Co is probably one of the most highly reviewed places in Manhattan. Â  They say that the wait is crazy. Â  I circumvented the wait by arriving right as it opened on Friday morning. Â  I came and I ordered Banana nut pancakes with a biscuit on the side. Â The pancake was good and it came with a delicious maple butter. Â Their orange juice is freshly squeezed and their pulp is refreshingly sweet. Â  Their breakfasts are great and when you order their pancakes, their maple butter steals the show. Â  Everything is really well-prepared and I enjoyed my meal, but I can't really say that I'd go out of my way to come back. Â  But if you do come for breakfast, do come early.

I was a virgin to these types of sandwiches (Banh mi) , although I've long loved pho and other Vietnamese foods. Â I echo everyone's review here - very very good sandwich on all levels...crusty bread on outside, chewy on inside...fresh veggies. Â The pork caught me a little off guard though....it's some morph of bacon and normal pork. Â Also bizarre that it shares space with a jeweler. Â Option for spicy which I recommend. Â The spring rolls look good too. Â There's only benches to sit but cram it if you want to eat it while it's warm. Â So flavorful...party in my mouth and it keeps going well after I'm done...must have raised prices recently to $3.25 - $3.75, but I'm not complaining. Â  Update - had the chicken finally and it was awesome! Â Dark meat and very moist.

In over twenty five years of eating and drinking in NYC I had the really disappointing experience of being "cut off" Â for the first time last night at Char - and yes, this by the same ringlet haired bartender mentioned by T.K. in his review. As someone who has held two NYC liquor licenses myself I'm pretty aware of this is supposed to work. And three middle aged people averaging a drink an hour talking quietly amongst themselves does not match any criteria that I can imagine for refusing patrons drink. The bartender is really reserved and lacking completely in personality but that was fine until after three hours of us eating and drinking he announces that "for our own good" he's cutting us off. Two of us had had three drinks and one of us had one! It was so lame and while I've enjoyed Char on two previous visits I would never go back to this establishment.

I've been here a couple times now. The schnapp + beer combo is a must. The food isn't outstanding, but good, and reasonably priced- although the sausage options should be more like $10 IMO. The service has been good and the ambience is nice. I recommend the Wiener schnitzel. Worth visiting.

My friend said the lobster roll here rivals the famous Hamptons lobster rolls. Â I have not been impressed with NYC lobster rolls in general. Â This place rocks! Â I have been back three times and can't bring myself to have anything but the lobster roll. Â WHAT is the sauce?? Â I also asked for extra lobster the first time and there was an extra charge but I appreciate them giving me what I want. Â However, I no longer order extra because there are whole pieces of lobster and plenty. I also order the butter lettuce salad every time, this is a simple but flavorful salad and they consistently have used the best part of the lettuce, which is unheard of for NY. Please don't take this off the menu!

Oh, Public. I had such high hopes for you with your trendy facade, and steel and concrete decor, and buzzing sparkly crowd. Unfortunately the whole night was a service fumble - although extremely apologetically so. -Unannounced server switch mid-appetizers -Forgotten drinks (2x) -Forgotten side order -Oops forgot you are allergic to gluten... -Exploding pen whilst signing credit card slips The food was fine to somewhat tasty but everything was just not quite on pitch that night. Mushroom ceviche was creative but over miso'd, duck was well cooked but over glazed, asparagus was zesty with lemon but slightly over grilled. The sommelier was very friendly and knowledgeable though and we still had fun. Ultimo grade: "meh" face.
Great food but as many have commented before the wait times are long. Â We waited almost 3 hours for a party of 3 to get in. Â The pancakes were delicious.

i love how they decorated for Christmas. It was romantic, and cozy mood for couple to have Christmas dinner date. I loved the food. Their lobster salad, and squid black ink pasta was sooooo good! Their steak was little too tough to chew, but potato on the side were perfect! Their lamb was very tender and tasty. Desserts were also wonderful. Their food display were okay. It wasn't the best but pretty enough to have one star. Their service was little disappointing, At first, they forgot to bring balsamic vinegar we asked for. Later when they brought our first dish which was appetizer, they did not even explain about the dishes. When we asked, they explained about the dish. Sommelier was very good actually. He recommended very nice wine which went very well with our main dishes. It was not even on the menu. Well, I would go to Ai Fiori again, but not any time soon.

Came here after a show on a Monday night. It's another speakeasy style bar where the entrance looks like a Psychic place from the window. Totally threw me off, but then you step inside and go behind the curtain where voila! you are now in one of Manhattan's coolest bars. The bar is split in two parts where you can either sit and actually have dinner with your cocktails or Â just hangout by the bar itself. We decided to sit down since we were a bit hungry and ordered Bone Marrow poppers, potato gnocchi, and spaghetti to share. It's a bit pricey here and smaller portions so I would say don't come here starving. Bone Marrow poppers were pretty good, but I was kind of whatever about the potato gnocchi. I didn't really like the consistency of it 'cause it tasted it a bit more mushy(?) I like gnocchi to be more of that sticky/doughy consistency. Spaghetti wasn't with tomato sauce and had a nice kick to it. For cocktails I got the Lazy Lover which had a very unique taste since it was jalapeno infused. Think it took a few sips to get used b/c of the slight jalapeno taste to but I liked it overall. My friends got the Fraise Sauvage and the Manhattan Cocktail which I liked as well. Great Food. Great Staff. Cacio e Pepe was amazing!!!
With an amazing new waitstaff, this restaurant trumps everything on Smith Street. Kudos to the best meal and best service anywhere in the neighborhood!

As a Chicagoan, my friends and I were looking for some good NYC pizza to compare to our beloved Lou Malnati's deep dish. amazing white.

The food selection is excellent, although not many options for vegetarians. The highlight is the chicken, rubbed in some super miracle oil, that makes it so tasty. Le Parisien: quaint restaurant with great service and food that's simply delicious. Â  They greeted us with complimentary wine while we waited for our table!

This place was delicious and had such a friendly atmosphere! The cheese was soooo fresh and the tomato sauce was delicious. Garlic. Yum. Definitely sit at the bar so you can watch the dudes sling dough all over the place and make amazing looking pizzas. But seriously --Â the pizza was amazing.

This is the kind of pizza I love. While New York pizza is unique and whatnot, Paulie Gee's has amazing creations that I crave. I recommend the Hell-boy and the Greenpointer. The mozzarella variety they use is unusual for pizza and soooo melty delicious!

Lovely neighborhood Italian joint offering surprisingly authentic and dirt-cheap grub in a homey chic space. Da Marcella is part of my initiative to try more neighborhood places, and I got a chance to try it when I needed a pasta place before a recent half-marathon. I made reservations for three on Friday night, and we got our table arriving early. Later arrivals without rezzies had to wait a bit, but the staff brought them comp drinks (belissimo!). The hostess was super-friendly, personable, and accommodating. She kisses several regulars on the cheek when they arrived. She was also bold with recommendations, a quality I strongly respect. The food was very good to excellent: salmon tartare special (recommended) was delizioso and the house special tagliatelle (with classic bolognese ragÃ¹ slowly cooked for 8 hours) was spot on. I will most definitely become a regular here, if I have anything to say about it (and I do).

The food here is really amazing. Â I've had the pork chop - very large, super moist and with tons of flavor and the pan friend chicken - worth the wait and served with amazing, flavorful collards and really good potato salad. Â And there's the biscuits....oh, the biscuits!

I absolutely love this place! The food is amazing and I love that they import all their ingredients from Spain. Pretty good but overpriced, especially considering what you are paying for. The falafel is a bit bland and nothing to write home about. The humus is good. The place itself is nice and offers a lot of room to sit and eat.

first time i ever had an arepa. i tried three different kinds, don't remember the names. hella good though, all bursting with flavor. will definitely be back for more of that chimichurri. Â we ordered to-go, minimal wait. Â gotta teach myself how to make arepas like these.

I spent a year living in Asia. I have been back to Asia several summers in a row for months at a time. And you know what? This ramen was heavenly!! Memories and goodness and happiness in a bowl and a bun. This will be a regular on my New York circuit from here on out.

Hands down, one of the BEST BURGERS I've ever had. So effing juicy.. and those FRIES! Every other Tuesday they have FREE stand-up comedy in the back room..called "The Grand Stand". Pretty awesome to enjoy dinner/drinks and get some free laughs from great comedians!

The balaboosta of this charming establishment knows how to do things right -- our evening was perfecto!

Awesome food in a cool old building. My bud and I split orders so i had the french toast and an omelet Â with ham, spinach and onion. A great savory and sweet combo. Food was served extraordinarily fast, too. We got there a little before they opened at 8am and there were three other groups waiting. My husband and I went to Bogota as a last minute birthday dinner for him. Â Right from the start we knew this was a great place. Â The atmosphere is warm and inviting. Never tried an arepa before, now I love them, you always find a very friendly host here, I recomend this place 100 percent

I have eaten empanadas before but once I came here a few months ago I have not been able to eat empanadas from another place. Came here awhile back since I've heard wait time at this place is ridiculous. After an hour and change, we got our table and looked at the menu. I really like my New York Style pizza and I would definitely not consider Adrienne's a New York Style slice...However, the pizza pans are OK. Not very adventurous but I know what I like!

This place was seriously hard to find, but all good things are. We ordered the sausage sampler, meatballs, ruben sandwich, creamed spinach/egg/veggies plate and the pretzel. Everything was fantastic. We enjoyed the cheesy dumplings, perfectly moist meatballs, warm ruben with mustard, delicious brussel sprouts and sauerkraut. Great food and friendly staff. Impressed with the freshly baked Pita and Laffa bread!!! Looking forward to another visit soon!

Ippudo is the trendiest little ramen joint in town. I used to think that I had to go to a homey hole-in-the-wall ramen place to get authentic ramen but Ippudo proves that ramen can be trendy AND delicious. But be prepared to wait for a table because they don't take reservations and Ippudo is pop-u-lar (duh, 1400+ reviews?!). Appetizers... ...hirata buns with pork - OMG so delicious! I think this may be my favorite thing at Ippudo. The pork was tender with the perfect amount of fat and the (mildly) spicy sauce is heavenly. ...hotate ponzu scallops - These bite size morsels were delicious. I really enjoyed the fresh jalepeno pepper slice with the scallop. ...duck with balsamic sauce - Pretty tasty but I think the hirata buns and scallops are better appetizer options. Ippudo has 5 kinds of ramen to choose from here, plus a daily special ramen... ...shiromaru hakata classic ramen - First of all, I LOVE tonkotsu soup and any ramen place that offers tonkotsu soup based ramen has already gotten on my good side. The classic didn't disappoint~ the noodles were toothy, the pork slices were well seasoned and fatty, the bamboo shoots were crunchy, the seasoned egg soaked in the soup was softened just right, and the sesame seeds added the perfect finishing touches. ...akamaru modern ramen - They add a fragrant garlic oil sauce to the tonkotsu soup that gives the whole bowl of ramen a really smoky, heavy flavor. This is good if you want to try a less traditional ramen. ...tan tan ramen - The shiromaru hakata classic is my ramen of choice at Ippudo, but when the special ramen of the day is the the tan tan ramen, I always get it because it's Ippudo's spicy ramen. Though it's not extremely spicy, I really like the thin ramen noodle and the addition of the cilantro and peanut flavor. Overall, I really like the ramen at Ippudo and they definitely know their pork. My only minor complaint with their ramen is that the soup is a little too salty and heavy to drink after finishing the noodles. Since it's such a heavy meal, I think it's really thoughtful of them to give a complimentary cup of hot tea at the end of the meal. While Ippudo isn't my absolute favorite ramen place in NYC (I prefer Minca), I love bringing friends who are visiting NYC and have never been to Ippudo.
Perfect when I'm in the mood for healthy great food! There are a lot of options and the market plates are the best.

Really great food in reasonable price. Nice people. The place has NO ambiance and super casual, and it is crowded so you may have to wait--just to know before you bring a fancy date.

You know when you're at dinner, and not one of your party of six can come up with that name, that song, that character from that movie...and it's driving you all crazy? Your waitress at Palo Santo, she knows it. And it's Richard Dawson. And everyone will collectively shout, "YES!!!!" And then she'll bring you each a taste of a cloyingly sweet dessert wine that, although disgusting, you will drink because it was a nice gesture, and you're not rude. And you will overtip her, as a result. And it will be a nice end to a meal that consisted of highs and lows that average out to be just A-OK. The highest of the high was the simple mini-tortillas served with the perfectly seasoned, fresh avocado, with the juicy ribeye a close second. The lowest of the low was the anticuchos platter that I was actually quite excited for. I believe it was rabbit liver, kidney and heart. I have enjoyed liver in many forms, so I am not sure if this was a one-time issue, but I was honestly disgusted by these little offal skewers. The taste was offensive. And yes, I kept eating because I was futilely hoping the next bite would be better than the last. Falling somewhere in the middle were my decent, but inexplicably cold Mahi Mahi, the hearty and comforting turkey and dumplings, the refreshing jicama salad, and the intriguing mushroom mole, all washed down with Imperial, Brooklyn Winter, and a good selection of wines. We topped off the meal with some well-executed desserts including a nice key lime pie, a predictably wonderful apple crumble, and a creme brÃ»lÃ©e fired close enough to the table that the blowtorch warmed the room. Palo Santo did not rock my world the way I hoped it would; but it's relaxed, sexy atmosphere, coupled with brief flashes of culinary excellence, ensures that I'll return to give it another shot.

loved their soba noodles. Â Their lunch box set is a great value - so much food. even more in love with their desserts - green tea and black sesame ice cream - not too sweet, perfect. Â the wasabi honey was not my favorite. Â the mini don's are a great option if you want a taste. Â i'm a fan.

It was a rainy, gloomy Friday afternoon, (lots of those going around this summer, no?) and I was desperate for sunshine and a cocktail. Â Fortunately by 5:15 p.m. the clouds parted and I busted out of the office to Nolita for BarBossa's killer Happy Hour -- $5 select cocktails, including their famed caipirihnas. My reviews occasionally extend past the drinks themselves and include a bit of dish for the ladies about the boys behind the bar. Â Well guys, here's one for you -- BarBossa's Simone (pronounced Sih-moan-ay) is fresh from Brazil herself and an undeniable knockout (not a term I bestow lightly). Â Ladies, don't hate -- she's also super sweet / knowledgeable when it comes to Brazilian booze. Â We even "collaborated" on changing up things for my last round, adding passion fruit to temper a spicy jalepeno selection. Â I'm a big fan of their overall cocktail philosophy. Â They don't claim to offer every drink under the sun, or that their bartenders have years of formal training, but they specialize in simple, regional cocktails and what they do, they do well -- and at reasonable prices. Â NYC nightlife, is that really so much to ask? On the food side, Simone graciously offered some free, crunchy mini-pizza bites for snacking (just another reason to always sit at the bar -- happy liver AND happy tummy). Â We didn't opt for a full meal but everything looked and smelled great. Â Sandwiches / paninis are under $10, and main plates mostly under $15. Â They have an intimate back room near the bathrooms that could be perfect for dinner parties. If you're looking for a delightful, casual place to wile away the hours, soak up Elizabeth St. people-watching or -- let's face it -- gawk at the gorgeous girl givin' you shugah (with your drink, of course), BarBossa's spot-on.

The staff was very friendly and accommodating and a refreshing change from the presumptuous places around the neighborhood. We sat out in the back garden for dinner which was a great way to enjoy a wonderful meal, then on our way out sat at the inside bar for a night cap, we just didn't want to leave. 5 stars - highly recommend.

I LOVE this place! Both the food and the ambiance are a delightful blend of elegant and informal; gourmet and down to earth. The service was fantastic and the drinks were original and not too sweet. The whole evening was wonderful on so many levels. The absolute must-order dish is the crispy pork belly with pickled watermelon. The deeply flavored meat paired with the refreshing fruit was inspired. Veal ricotta sliders, orrechiette with lamb, pork tacos were superb. The only miss was the fettucine with tomatoes. The risotto is not a classic Italian one- but that's so hard to find in NYC. Finally, our dessert was great but the dessert list is eclectic - if you must have chocolate, you may be disappointed. We felt that mixed drinks were a more appropriate accompaniment to our dishes than wine. The Single Buck with rum, bitters, and pineapple juice was refreshing and not too sweet. Rather than having just one waiter, we were served by a variety of people - all of whom knew the menu and answered our questions enthusiastically. More importantly, never once in the course of the meal did I have to ask to have our water glasses filled. One more thing - the waiter immediately let us know that they could accommodate all food sensitivities and dietary restrictions. When we told him of our two allergies, he quickly let us know which dishes would work and how they could change some of the others. Their positive attitude about food issues is a welcome change to the way many well-heeled restaurants treat people with food allergies.

Having lived and loved Beechers in Seattle I was disappointed with this experience, it was nothing to do with the food, that was great!
