Best burgers! Love this place. And they have yummy cocktails too

Huuuge, messy burger.. crispy shoestring fries and a nice cold beer. What more can you ask for? The burger is really juicy, and lightly seasoned. I love the fact that I can walk away and not DIE right after eating all of that. It's my favorite kind of "full". It can get pretty busy during lunch, so know "that" before goin in. You will be standing in line in the middle of everyone eating burgers. Its pretty small in there, too. I love the booth seating though. I think they have chili. .Never tried it.

There are lots of reviews for this place so I'll just throw out some of the highlights: -Wine flights. Even at $16 (the non-happy hour price), I felt this was a good deal. And its just fun to get a variety. -Ambience - it was really buzzing with happy energy, and the dim lighting created a fun atmosphere. -Charcuterie/cheese options are well priced.

Pizza is one of those super touchy foods, not only in New York, but around the world. Â Everyone has an opinion on what constitutes the ideal pizza. Â Admittedly, Saraghina checks a lot of the "yes" boxes on my pizza grading rubric. For starters, I've never had to wait for a table here. Â I'm always seated promptly and my order is taken down within a reasonable period of time. Â The servers seem to lack the pretentious attitude of the other "hot" pizza spots in Brooklyn and the food really speaks for itself. Â The crowds here are pretty friendly and I always feel right at home, whether dining inside or out. My friends and I are all big on the house wine and like to kick things off with a market salad. Â I'm always hankering for the coppa & carciofi, my girlfriend likes the bufala, and you can never go wrong with the prosciutto & funghi. Â The pizza here is made by hand, so don't be afraid to eat them with your hands. Â For those of you with proper table manners, the pizza can be eaten with a fork and knife, but you'd be better off with the standard crust pinch. Â The slices hold up, without sagging or cracking; the definitive mark of an excellent pie. Sometimes, depending on how they're staffed on that particular day, the food can be a bit slow, but I have always found the service to be exceptional. Â Attentive servers, willing to bring you water or whatever else you may need while the pizza gods are busy creating something truly remarkable. Â It's a bit far from where I currently live, but I think that's one of the nice things about Saraghina; it brings you to a neighborhood you might not normally visit.

2.5 Stars Was it good? I think so. After hearing the people next to me obnoxiously gushing and guffawing about the pizza, after reading nearly every article from Time Out, Bon Appetit, The NY Times, etc posted on the place's walls, after making the trek down to boondock Brooklyn, after waiting over two hours for the pizza, I honestly don't remember. I do remember it being edible food and satiable enough for my stomach. I was so hungry while I waited for the hyped up pizza that I wanted to steal a slice from the obnoxious group's table and run out of there yelling, "Suck it!" Â I wanted to eat a frozen Tombstone pizza and feel just as satisfied. I can chop some basil and pour some olive oil over that frozen crud. It didn't matter to me. By the time the venerable pie was placed in front of me, Â all of the dazzle was lost and it tasted like any other pizza to me. Don't go when you're hungry, and prepare to wait a long time.

I have traveled bridges upon bridges to get to Grimaldis. Across the Williamsburg,through China town, over the Brooklyn Bridge, because I refuse to pay for a metro card, but I'll pay for an entire pie (what is logic). Of course there's a long line, but then all good places have one. Unless you're a hole in the wall, but that's usually because they don't receive enough publicity for there awesome food, but now I'm getting off topic..... Theres a beautiful area by the water where you can take your pizza to go and eat it there. I would prefer to eat outside then inside the place. It is a bit crammed, but if you want the full experience go for it! Â Pizza's still amazing no matter where you have it :)

I *DO* love this place. And I'm reviewing mostly on the food. Top ramen and pork bun for sure. This is very authentic ramen and the broth is really savory! The pork belly is outright DELICIOUS and smoky tasting. I found the dark broth to be too salty and strong, but in the lighter broth, it's wonderful. However, the wait is a HUGE deterrent to making this a regular place. The space is large, and I know very popular, but I have never gone there where they didn't say there was an hour or more wait. Since they don't take reservations (unless you go in the middle of the day and they will then give you a reservation for 11pm), it makes it next to impossible to ever get a seat. And I'm not *that* much of a fan. I cannot tell you the number of times friends and I have wanted to go here and could not get a table. That's fine I guess, because it allows me to savor the many other excellent ramen, soba places nearby anywhere in the east village. So while I love their ramen, and it *is* worth eventually getting a reservation there early for late in the evening, it's not something you want to deal with when hungry. It's a beautiful place, but I wish they would make it a little easier to get a table. Maybe it makes them look highly sought after, but after this many years later, I am not as willing to play the game and more than happy to go to other places that are quieter and have just as tasty noodles. This is why it doesn't get 5 stars from me.

Simply one of my favorite places in the city. Â Good for large gatherings of 10 or for dates; Jadis is pure genius. Â It's a little out of the way for me, but I will never complain about making the trip! To summarize: - Great, fresh ingredients, simply combined. Â  - Lovely wines, offered at a reasonable prices and served by a courteous staff. (Note: don't go here for cocktails or a bar scene. Additionally, they only have one beer on tap.) - The decor is comfortable, almost library like. Â In fact, they even have a Webster's Dictionary in one of the bookshelves! I won't actually tell you to go here, as you might ruin it for me, but I do recommend Jadis to friends. Â And for those with like mind and similar palate, go and enjoy.

Stopped in with daughters before we went to see "Once" on Broadway. The Victorian atmosphere and Irish influenced menu was a perfect fit. We had the Shepherds pie, Irish Stew and Roasted chicken dishes. All tasted good and the portions were generous. Â I was pleased withe service and the prices were moderate for a NY restaurant near Times Square.
Some weird things on the menu, but overall solidly declicious.

I love this place...... when they have food. I have gone there a couple times for lunch and they were out of literally everything but 3 items on the menu. 3! That was not good. But if you go for dinner, the food is simple but exceptional. Everything is truly local and the place has a decidedly LES vibe.

Fette Sau is totally worth whatever pain-in-the-ass line you have to wait in to order your food. Â And whatever crazy-stalker-esque behavior you have to engage in while attempting to grab enough seats for you and your friends to chow down on some delicious smoked meat. I'd bookmarked this place long ago, and was super-psyched that I finally had the chance to give it a try on a recent trip to NYC. Â We got here pretty late (after 10pm) on a Saturday, and the place was pretty crowded. Â The line wasn't as long as I'd feared, and we were able to snag seats, drinks, and a huge platter of smoked meat within about an hour of getting there. I think we tried just about everything on the menu - ribs, pulled pork, spicy sausage, brisket, pork belly, baked beans, and German potato salad. Â The only thing we wanted that they were out of were the pickles. Â Everything was outstanding. Â The pork belly, brisket, and ribs have to be my stand-out faves - each of these practically melted in my mouth. There were a variety of sauces on the table, but my favorite had to be the original. Â The mustard-vinegar version reminded me a little too much of Chinese mustard, which wasn't the look I was going for with my bbq. Dining is family-style, so don't be shy about asking your neighbor to pass you that roll of paper towels - you'll totally need 'em! One criticism, the mason jars the drinks were served in tasted way too strongly of the bleach they use to clean them. Â Definitely a turn off from my otherwise pretty tasty cider.

We only came here after being deterred by loud music at a nearby favorite German place. Â This place was still pretty loud. Â They should not consider their menu a "Dinner" menu since you can't really eat a proper meal there. Â It is definitely bar food style. Â The kale salad was pretty unique, but I wouldn't come back if I was looking for a substantial meal. Â It is a very "hip" bar hangout for those who don't mind noise.

At it's core, Penelope is a neighborhood diner. Â I have been here for both brunch - where, on my first try, my friend and I lucked out and didn't have to wait at all since there were no other parties of two waiting in the crowd outside (sorry group brunchers, sometimes it's better to leave the entourage behind!) - and dinner. I've always had really good service here, even when it's hopping - waiters are friendly, busboys are quick to remove plates/utensils, and my water glass is always refilled appropriately. Â Yet none of this attention is intrusive or overdone. Â Surprising. They do a solid brunch. Â The French fries that come with most mains are addictive. Â Golden and crunchy on the outside and soft inside. Â I tried stealing a few off my pal's plate and nearly lost a finger to his fork. Â All the egg dishes are tasty and cooked to your preference. Â However, I have yet to find a place that knows how to do eggs "over medium" to my liking (i.e. the whites are solid and the yolks just to the very point of not being runny. Â Yum.) Dinner here is fine, except would it kill them to turn the lights up a little? Â My eyes are young and healthy, but when I have to lift a tea candle to my menu to read it, that's a sign it's time to invest in a higher wattage bulb. Â  Actually, my main problem with dinner here is that the atmosphere seems to aspire to "dark, cozy bistro with quiet conversation and candlelight" when truly it's a nice diner dinner in a really dark room with a lot of loud people (me included). The dinner and lunch menu here are pretty much the same. Â The same addictive French fries that come with brunch also come with some of the dinner dishes. Â Their chicken meatballs are very good - moist, maybe a little too moist, but flavorful and won't leave you feeling too full. Â The pesto mayo is herby, fatty and delicious, but I usually ask for it on the side because they slather on a lot - and because I'm such a girl. I feel compelled to warn you about the cinnamon buns. Â WORST CINNAMON BUN EVER. Â It was very dry and the sugary glaze on top cracked and fell to the plate in bits when I cut into it. Â That ain't right. Â It looked and tasted like it had been left over from the day before. Â Just gross.
Great food that reinvents asian cuisine with french and american flare.
Best shanghai buns I have ever eaten so far! :D They come out hot! The flavors of the soup and the meat are perfect. If you want to see them for yourself, feel free to watch my video!

Best Malaysian Restaurant in town hands down!!!! lived in the city all my life and am big fan of Malaysian curry, i have tried literally almost every single malaysian restaurant in town. when i first starting going here i always order the curry chicken rice. later i realize if you order them separately, is a little pricey but you get your money more worth it. especially if you're a big eater like me.
Ridiculous pizza. The end.

4.5 Stars. Great atmosphere and friendly service. A perfect place to shelter from the blizzard in the winter, or probably shelter from the heat/humidity in the summer. Beet cocktail was surprisingly AMAZING. Order it. The fried plantains with salty cheese were really good- but I was a little surprised when "salty cheese" just meant Parmesan, I was expecting some kind of soft cheese and was a little disappointed. Yum none the less. I got the special arepa, but my friends swear by the De Pabellon (shredded beef, black beans, salty cheese- Parm thingy again- and sweet plantains) and the Los Muchachos (grilled chorizo, spicy white cheese, jalapenos, and sauteed peppers). Both have said that they are a little bit disappointed when they order anything else because the De Pabellon and Los Muchachos are so amazing. However, the special arepa that evening was F**KING INCREDIBLE. Pork shoulder, soft cheese, plantains, jalapenos, and cilantro. Stuffed to perfection in a perfectly crispy arepa. So-freakin-good. The arepas are filling and if you share an appetizer you probably don't need more than one, but if you're starving you can probably get through two. Definitely recommend!
best chile rellenos anywhere! and i've been around the world. Â surprisingly great hole in the wall! easy st pkg. pleasant neighborhood.

The food was really good..it gets packed as it should..we live a block away Â and we didn't know about this place because it's hidden but we are glad we found it through my happy cow app I have turned to a vegan recently and this place makes it so much easier..the place needs ventilation I smell like food when I got out

3 stars (I wish I could give more) I'm not going to jump on the bandwagon here and laud this place as the next big thing. Â Don't get me wrong, it's a great little spot tucked away somewhere in the middle of...oops...not supposed to give it away. :) Â I did have some issues with the food and the slow service from the kitchen. Â It was nothing major but sort of annoying. Â  Our party of three sat at the bar. Â I'm glad we did because I don't think the tables would've been better. Â Some, if not most, of them were glass coffee tables surrounded by sofas and lazy chairs. Â That's not how I want to eat. Â The diners were sitting sort of funny and all had to lean forward so that they could talk to each other. Â  We ordered the $55 tasting menu and a plate of sashimi. Â The sashimi was three slices of kanpachi and some other white fish. Â Both were very good. Â I love kanpachi which is a variant of the more fatty hamachi - my favorite. Â  Like others have wrote, the tasting menu consisted of an organic vegetable fondue (big deal); mushroom croquette topped with uni (very good); roasted branzino w/ veggies (very good); chorizo/salami/beef tongue? (didn't like the tongue); wagyu burger / ikura over rice (burger was tasty but too rare for me; the SINGLE potato wedge was too oily; the ikura was okay); and finally the sake panna cotta (edible but not a fan). Â For $55, I thought it was reasonable. Â My gripe is how long it took for everything to come out. Â 2 HOURS and 15 minutes!!! Â That's just too long. Â If the meal was 7 or 9 courses, that's fine. Â But for 5? Â The panna cotta literally took over 15 minutes to come out. Â I asked for the check thinking that we were finished with the courses since we already had five. Â But, just as I was asking for the check, the waitress said our dessert was coming out. Â And it did. I think if the kitchen was on top of things and didn't make us wait, It may have gotten four or four and a half. Â I may have to try it again and not order the tasting menu. BTW: The bathroom is no big deal. Â I don't know why so many yelpers are raving about it. Â I was expecting some magical room with fancy lights and a robot that roams around cleaning the toilet and sink. Â It's a freaking bidet, people!!! Â So what? Â All middle-class households in East Asia have them. Â They realized that wiping your fecal-smeared butt with harsh paper is too barbaric. Â Too bad North America is still okay with that... And I got the reservation by calling them on the same day!!! Â Their phone number is not hard to find!!!
Love the burgers. The bun and burger beat In & Out by far!

When a restaurant has the word Yak to describe it, you would assume that there would be more yak dishes to choose from. I was kind of disappointed that there was only 3 dishes that contained yak in it out of the whole menu, the yak momo, the yak tongue (Cheley), and sauteed yak slices (Shapta). We had a groupon and they said that the yak slices were not included in the deal (even though we offered to pay the difference) and they were out of tongue for the day. So we settled for the yak momo's. Yak Momo ($12.95) - Tibetan dumplings that is similar to a Chinese Xiao Long Bao. Inside was seasoned yak meat which was strong in ginger and cilantro taste and the best part was the bit of soup that gushed out when bitten into. The dumpling skin was a little thick and almost bun like. Eating this, you would have thought it was beef. (8/10) yelp.com/biz_photos/himaâ€¦ Gyuma ($9.95) - A sausage filled with beef blood and ground beef. At first look it might seem a little gross. That's the thought I had when I laid eyes on this dark matter. Taste wise, it wasn't as bold as it looked as it was lacking seasoning but it did have a bloody taste. It was very burger like. When out of the casing, the meat fell apart. (6.5/10) yelp.com/biz_photos/himaâ€¦ Goat Thali ($12.95) - This was more like a sampler platter of condiments than an entree. The thali only had one small cup of goat meat curry. The other 3 cups consisted of a rice pudding, a chili like dip, and another kind of bean dip. Also they give you some rice and a small piece of crispy bread. Overall not much to eat but you get to try out a palate of flavors. (8/10) yelp.com/biz_photos/himaâ€¦ This was my first time eating yak not in jerky form and I kind of expected more from it. Maybe I would have enjoyed it more if it wasn't grounded. I did enjoy this cuisine as the food had influences and flavors from cuisines all over Asia. But in the end, it just wasn't something I wanted to have seconds of.

So I actually made the reservations on yelp for Sunday brunch (for 2) and surprisingly, they had a little issue with that. Â I guess there's a little bit of a disconnect between them and opentable.com because they said they couldn't find my name on the reservation list. So I was told to wait which I didn't have a problem with especially since it was such a long walk from the train; but literally 2 minutes later, the host called us over and gave us a table! Nonetheless, we get seated and our waiter is really sweet! She even gives us suggestions for the drinks which I really appreciated! For drinks I had the Red Lemonade which had the right amount of alcohol while still being fruity just how I like it! For our meals, I had the Bourbon St. Eggs Benedict and my friend had the red-velvet Chicken & Waffles. Â But although I really enjoyed my eggs benedict, I wish I had gotten the chicken & waffles! It really is that good guys, there's no hype here! Â We also ordered a side of Mac & Cheese and SCRUMPTIOUS is just an understatement! So Cheesy and moist and flavorful and filling! We didn't finish everything of course. When leaving, the host actually nicely apologized for the confusion about our reservations in the beginning which is basically what gives them the 5 stars lol. Â I guess to avoid any confusion, I wouldn't suggest making reservations through opentable.com. And when you do go there do not leave with out ordering a side of Mac & Cheese! Overall the ambiance was great; good music! The food was great! The service was great! I will definitely be paying SoCO another visit!

this place was great. Â I've tried about every taco, even the specialty tacos, which sound weird but are delicious. Â This place could definitely be compared to some good taco shops in Arizona and California. Â The prices are very reasonable. Â I would definitely go back.
Best Pancakes Ever! Â Love this cafe!
Great experience on a business trip. Â Service was great even though I was the only member of my party. Â Food was awesome, definitely recommend.

Green eggs and Lamb is probably one of my most favorite breakfasts. The eggs are "green" because of cilantro. Food is based on Turkish cuisine with lots of lamb, fresh spices (like cilantro) and tomatoes and potatoes done creatively with lots of salad to balance out the starch. Plates are large and service is great. Even the decor is wonderful. Turkish tiles and large gilded mirrors hang on the walls giving this high ceiling restaurant a warm and inviting feeling. We went on a Sunday and made a reservation which helped us to be seated faster. I am surprised there are not more reviews about this Fort Greene wonder as the place was packed and there was a line of folks waiting to get in as well.

Get to the Chase: Pros: 1) Fantastic morsels of awesome! 2) Simple, delicious, affordable and quick 3) $3-$4/soft taco for the quality of food is outstanding 5) In Chelsea Market you'll easily spend $25+ per meal, whereas you can get fresh guacamole, grilled meats and flour/corn tacos! MMM 6) Great service (pleasant staff) Cons: 1) The cooler looks a bit iffy...rusted edges with a vat of water holding some bottles of soda (opt for the fridge that they have instead of the cooler) 2) Can get quite busy/packed by meal time 3) No seating

OH MY GOSH! I was blown away by this beautiful restaurant which was right in my own backyard. My friend and I were starving after exploring the art exhibits during Target First Saturday at the Brooklyn Museum. We quickly searched Yelp for nearby restaurants which had a decent menu as well as dessert options. That is how we stumbled upon Mayfield. We were not prepared for the experience we had that evening. I ordered the burger since I wasn't interested with the other menu items due to my dietary restrictions. According to our server, it was the best burger in the City, so I was anxious to see whether it would live up to the hype. I have eaten at a quite a few burger joints as you will tell from the list I have in my profile, but my palette and my mind were pleasantly surprised by the symphony of flavors. First of all, the $15 Mayfield burger is HUGE. I had to figure out how to dig in, but when I did it was DELICIOUS. The ingredients included an egg? What on earth I thought, but it worked. The individual portion was crazy and it came with fries. Our appetite was more than satisfied and we somehow managed to make room for dessert since that was our original motive for dining at this establishment. I loved the space, great for couples, large groups, happy hour with colleagues, or to catch the game.
Very good place love to food
One of the best burgers I've ever had. Its a great local bar with friendly staff and good food in general. Outdoor space with a huge TV. Get the burger!

Went with my lady and another couple the other night for dinner. Totally charming spot and nearby us too, which is a score. I had a blueberry mojito before dinner -- it was terrific and unusual. Â We ordered the mixed cheese and mixed meat plates to start off with -- I recommend. Â A nice assortment and all really good -- not huge portions, but normal (some places in the 'hood pile on the meats for a group of four.) Â The rest was shared small plates -- the meatballs and the macaroni and cheese are def. worth trying/sharing. Â I will def. return and check out brunch. Â The waitress was nice -- informed, prompt...and exceedingly cute!

I was visiting a friend and she suggested we go for dinner to this place. What a great choice! We both ordered the sea bass which was just divine! Buttery, melt in your mouth delicious! Our friend ordered the meatballs which were GIGANTIC! Everyone was pleased with their meal and our wine was good too. The ambiance is a bit romantic, the service was great, and the place is dark but in a good way.

Best pizza ever. We choose to sit and eat, there's a window you can order pizza by the slice. We tried the Sicilian pizza (this was our first time trying Sicilian and NYC pizza). And oh my god was it the best pizza ever! We were still hungry so we got a slice of there artichoke pizza, not my favorite but it is unique and different so I can tell why it's so popular. It was a bit pricey but sooo worth it! Would love love love to go again!!

Decor is awful, food was bland. I started with the Mexican shrimp cocktail , sauce was out of a jar with a few pieces of diced avacado, served with saltine crackers! Really?? I ordered the enchiladas don Blanca., pretty bland in taste. Sangria was delicious but a bit on the small side. Â Service was ok, wouldn't go back or recommend .

I'm honestly not sure what all the hype is about The Spotted Pig. The staff was pleasant enough, but it felt like I was waiting for my food for years. Ages. Millennia. Who knows, maybe they were having an off night but after having to wait for a table it just felt ridiculous. The food was pretty good, but there are plenty of other places that somehow manage numbers and timing more gracefully.

Would have gave this 5 stars but we showed up 1 person short and they made us wait an extra 40 minutes!!!!!!!!!!!! food was awesome, service was excellent. really enjoyed the apps. Will definitely be back.

Stumbled across the malt house for a drink and some food and I was not disapointed!!! Great drink selection, good food, good atmosphere. Guy serving us was really helpful when choosing drinks & food! Quality place would certainly recommend it!!!

Out of town Arizona visitors. Stopped by to warm up. Gracious hospitality, quality beers and good food. Enjoyed the soup of the day, Shepard's Pie and chips. Nice place. Jack our bartender steered us straight. Recommended.

Oh my cappuccino!!! The best coffee in Manhattan. If you are in town, I would highly recommend you don't miss out on their outstanding coffee and delicious pastries, quiches, empanadas, and sandwiches. That's all.

It a sweet weekday lunch-hour (uncrowded) when V and I met G-Money for sushi lunch at Yasuda. The name precedes the actual experience. I used to work around 44th and 5th so I was surprised because I had walked into the venue several months back because of the sushi bar ambiance - expensive, clean, simple with a Japanese wood panel theme. A great experience and recommended for any sushi-lover. For the Omakase from great sushi chefs, you have an option 8-10-12. I was opting for 12--if I am getting the best sushi in NY, I want the most of it. G was the guest of honor and she chose 10, 7 different sushi pieces and 3 rolls which was a great amount. They were all delicious. Next time, I want to choose my own, keeping a few that I tasted... The sushi keepers: Toro King Salmon Uni Our table got to talking about flavors, this king salmon is tastier than that salmon, the spanish mackerel is tougher than the (reg) mackerel. The cooked shrimp (also topped with rock salt) was nothing compared to the sweet honey taste of the cooked eel/unagi. G and I attempted to give Uni another try (10+ past attempts for both of us). The uni was topped with a pinch of rock salt, it also tasted slightly torched to give it a brulee flavor. We could just never fully grasp its popularity and flavor...until now... I really don't know what did me in, I usually understand why something taste good or bad. Â I felt like I was playing a game of 20 questions. And then it hit me...as sea urchin roe, uni has a funny taste--almost something familiar...a flavor that most adults will eventually encounter...a body part with many other names...what is better known, for lack of better names, as 'vag' or for some 'lesbo'. I like sushi at all times and all forms..but uni is a taste too close to home...the fishiness...claminess...the sliminess...the textures...all seem similar to the female sexual organ pre-wet on top of a piece of sushi rice. Now you have something to think about the next time you have a piece of uni sushi. And like great sex, Yasuda had great uni. A perfect place for sushi purists, Yasuda's name is out and well-known. Uni will be your and my dirty little secret.

I have been wanting to try this place for years!! It's seems impossible to get brunch reservations.. Simply because it's so cheap (less than 20 dollars an entree and you get to enjoy unlimited sangria).. How can you say no to a LAZY SUNDAY!! I guess it's because i came with my fav peeps in NYC!!! My fav girl, fav roommate, and my date (all my loves ones).. We were starving and started "inhaling" all the bread in the bread basket and order another one immediately. Have I said that they have one of the best breakfast?? Especially the "cheesy bread".. My roommate is 25% Latino so he told me the name of the bread but I forgot.. I guess it's because of the sangria.. The corn bread and the chocolate bread were amazing as well.. The chocolate bread was crispy and also semi-sweet made it perfect. I think I had a total of 5-6 breads.. We also finished the strawberry butter and the waiter brought us another "bowl" of strawberry butter.. I was kinda glad that we had the room with a bigger table all the way in.. We started "salsa-ing".. I guess everyone around us thought we were really drunk but we only had a glass of sangria.. enough of my story.. let's head to the food.. 4 of us ordered - Quesidillas de el salvador.. It;s just quesidillas with chicken in it and top with avocado.. A nice mixture with some sour cream on top.. you have a really confusing taste.. sweet, slightly spicy, and mushy taste.. The chipotle chicken was so tender.. not my favorite dish but it's good - vaca frita.. The steak was so perfect.. perfect mexican food for brunch if you want a slightly heavier portion - burrito sucio.. MY FAV DISH!! It's like an omelet cover with beans avocado... PERFECT FOR BRUNCH if you want eggs.. it's like an american + spanish combination.. SANGRIA!! It's totally depends on your taste.. my favorite is the spanish harlem and tropical.. SERVICE!! Best service in MANHATTAN!! The waiter came and talked to us a couple times and brought us extra bread + Sangria.. he told us not to worry about the house rules and we can start TABLE DANCING!! lol.. My parties surprised me with the dominos cake since my bd is approaching.. LOVE YOU GUYS!! The dominos cake was really good if you are a chocolate lover.. too bad I am so full to enjoy!! I will def come back to calle ocho again.. MAKE YOUR RESERVATIONS A MONTH AHEAD!!

FANTASTIC!!! We showed up without a reservation and although the place was packed, my wife and I were seated instantly. The waitstaff here moves quickly, but are quick to remind you that there's no rush and relaxing after a hearty Italian meal is important! The waiter was friendly and engaging, and the kitchen was more than accommodating for us to try several menu items (they let us order 1/2 orders so we could do a variety). The pasta was homemade and all the ingredients tasted marvelously fresh. The wine selection was great and the desserts were some of the best we've bad in NYC - I'm particularly fond of the many non-chocolate dishes they served. I can't find another restaurant in Little Italy that I'd rather eat at - this IS the place to go, you won't regret it!
BEST lunchie idea ever! I can't wait to go back! I had the mixed veggies and chicken tikka rolls and they were PERFECT!

Nice ambiance, good wine selection, the waiter was very attentive about what kind of wine i wanted, though we ended up ordering for the table by the bottle so the eventual selection was good. Food was good, though i have had better, so nothing 'too' exciting. However, i had gone for a friend's bday party & we were in a very large group, the staff took good care of us & my wine glass was never empty. So overall, not a bad evening ;)
I really loved the Ramen....one of the best ones in NYC The enviroment of the restaurant reminds me of an authentic japanese restaurant. Although the long wait was very crazy....I still recommend it

I really enjoyed my dining experience here.. Thanks to a dear friend who brought me here, I got to experience the funnest, coolest, delicious quality food here. Love the fact we sat at the main ingredient table with the chefs right in front of us and cooking what we picked right there and then. Â Love the fact they put a selected amount of veggies and meats on ice in front of you and use it til it's sold out. Â So fresh and local. The chefs are pretty amazing other than cooking delicious plates Sitting the whollllllle time inside their circle not moving!! Â Wow. Â impressive. Â  They hand all dishes to you off their wooden tool, which at the end of night: please do not forget to tip (on that wooden tool)!!! Â  Creative dining at its best.

I wanted to get away from the city for the weekend, but wasn't able to get on a bus or train anywhere far away, for various reasons. Freemans was a pretty damn good alternative. Walking down the alleyway off Rivington St, I suddenly felt like I was somewhere else entirely. What you read is true: it's a fantastic space, definitely worth checking out if you are visiting the city or if you're a veritable New Yorker. The toast was overly toasted (more like crispy croutons), and they forgot to bring out my coffee, but it was nevertheless a gem of an experience. Great service and undeniably tasty food (oh, those perfectly poached eggs!) I will be back to try the famed artichoke dip.

Went here on Saturday . Hard to find no sign on the location but found it. The Cashier not so welcoming. I was super excited to go here because of the reviews. The biscuits are amazing. I would advise to get with honey! The Chicken and Biscuit was delish! I got 2 Chicken and Biscuit Â and 2 biscuits and wow very good! I left one for Sunday morning and it taste even better then the day before! The guy cooking super nice but the Cashier was lacking a smile and a hi ! However, I would go here again because mmm mmm it is divine food!!!

Burrata appetizer was good, and the $25 bottles of wine are a great deal! However, they make it all back with the high-margin unlimited pasta trio. There is no other way to order pasta there. It tasted typical (that is to say, OK), and there's no way someone could have more than one plate.

okay, mediterranean isn't exactly at the top of my list of favorite cuisines. not at the bottom either, just doesn't really do anything for me. met a friend in tribeca for lunch while walking up west broadway, decided we couldn't pass up this "cute little blue place." it just looked so... homey. :) short 'n simple, food - great. service, excellent. it was just one level but the waiter told us there was an upstairs lounge under construction. i'm hardly ever in this neighborhood, but honest to goodness i will be back. tomato basil pizza. yes. grilled chicken sandwich. yes. (dat aioli!) harira. oh god, yes. very happy to know this place exists.

Nestled in brownstone on park slope block between 2 residential building this semi secret restaurant boasts a wonderful $25 prix fixe menu. Palo Santo is a cool a restaurant, from a stylistic steel cut sign above the front door to the exposed kitchen as you step in to the renovated brownstone. In the back you will find a south American tropical experience. The food is always amazing, especially if you are a meat eater. I love the chicken liver app and steak for dinner! There chimichurri is excellent as well. This is a great restaurant for date or friends, especially friends from out of town! I am sure the popularity of this place is truly based on great food, good atmosphere, and a unpretentious environment! Plus being sort of off the usual park slope beaten path helps.

This place is awesome drunk or sober. It's best at night though imo and when the temperature is below room temperature. The decor is awesomely antiquarian (did I just say that?). I have to go here every time I go to NYC. I think I've tried most of the sauces. or maybe that's what Rai told me since I was wasted. What do they have? Fries. Frittes. Whatever. It's good. Read the other reviews for the meticulous description. But I can't really elaborate too much. They are potatoes that are fried. That is all. And it's good! You. Go. Now!
Still great after all these years. The service is so excellent. Â Try Le Grand from the raw bar.

Yum. Just got back from a really wonderful, satisfying meal here. Perfect heart warming dinner for a cold and rainy October day! My friend and I got here at 5:30 on a Sunday and we waited 1.5 hrs in line for a table. The wait was pretty painful, it would be hard to come back here again with such a long wait, but the food was really fantastic and cheap. We shared an (side) appetizer of the Char Siu Mayo Don- WOW. Such an interesting mix of flavors. I really enjoyed it, as much if not more than the Ramen. My friend and I both ordered the Totto Spicy Ramen. I really loved the spicy sesame oil. YUM. We were super full by the end of the meal and could barely finish our Ramen! Next time I would avoid the long wait times by putting my name down before they open! Also, FYI they don't have to-go containers, so bring either a large appetite or bring your own! Cash ONLY.

I consider myself more of a purist when it comes to Japanese - no "funky dunky" rolls (as my bf calls them), and no fusion... ....so I love that this place has amazing variety for sushi/sashimi. I wouldn't say it's the "best" I've ever had - some pieces were straight up misses (esp disappointed with the toro today)... but stick with the chef's recommendations (the ones circled in red each day) - they were all pretty solid. Also would add that the sushi rice here reminded me a bit of the sushi places I used to frequent in Tokyo, i.e., it's done right. I loved that I could taste each grain of rice. I realized when I got the bill that yes, this place IS expensive. My bf and I got 26 pieces, miso soup, green tea, and an yebisu for lunch today and the bill came out to $190 with tip and tax... and honestly, we were still a bit hungry. P.S. Forgot to mention that I LOVE the simplistic decor of the place...

My wife and I were in the area and went for dinner after reading the great reviews on Yelp and we were not disappointed. We had the bacon-wrapped stuffed dates to start and they were the perfect combination of sweet, salty, and crispy. Â For main courses, we shared the plantain-crusted talapia and the "vaca frita" skirt steak. Â The talapia was very flavorful and the skirt steak, which is usually a tougher cut, was so tender it was as though it had been made by your Jewish grandmother. Calle Ocho also gets bonus points for having great drinks and a fun, lively atmosphere. Â We will definitely be back!
Pretty neat place. Crowd friendly. The staff there is really really nice! I really love their mini burgers and wings! Would definitely come back here when out late with friends.

Lucky, lucky me! The executive sous chef is a dear friend of mine.. therefore I get Â extra small plate presents ... and what is to hate about a restaurant that starts you off with a bag of popcorn that had been popped in bacon fat? Light, crispy and full of bacon flavor. I started off my fantastic dinner with the Chili shrimp with a refreshing combination of watermelon. Simple but the bomb! This is the BEST small plate to start with. And my significant other's favorite. While I had two of the three Chili shrimp. I believe my significant other had the lobster. Which I cannot recall how it taste since I believe I didn't get a chance to taste it. :( Next was the braised pork belly tacos. Delightfully sinful for my arteries but oh so good on my tastebuds. You have melt in your mouth pork belly topped with kimchi, pico de gallo and queso fresco. The perfect marriage of mexican and korean. Then the famous "Crack & Cheese!" FRIED potato gnocchi (which had me thinking, this is what gourmet tater tots must taste like) with cheese, cheese, and bacon and bacon. If you thought the pork belly I had was seriously unhealthy, wait until you've tried the Crack & Cheese. Seriously delicious. And right before we were expecting to have our branzino.. we were hit with 3 surprises that were going to put our stomach over the edge with bloated and happiness. First gifted to us was the mussels, so savory with bits of chinese sausage all over. My boyfriend, a big fan of chinese sausage, hoarding all the chinese sausage while I am aggressively stuffing each of those succulent delights into my face. Talk about a gluttonous couple. Then we had the crispy pork. to me, this was my favorite present small dish. This had me seriously nostalgic for my grandma's pork cooking. Crispy on the outside but a soft and tender inside. Topped with a runny egg and spicy mayo. Before this dish came I was already worried how I was going to eat the branzino, but after the first bite of this,I really didn't care how I was going to fit the branzino in my stomach anymore. Then came our branzino! One of my favorite fish, deboned and lightly nutty and flaky. Comes with a small side of mixed greens and small orange slices. Perfect combination for this type of fish! The perfect fish for seafood lovers and non-lovers alike. I seriously cannot believe nobody has written a review for the branzino. It disturbs me. How can all you foodies not order the branzino? What is wrong with you? Order the branzino next time. Then the dinner was ended with a yummy lime panna cotta with avocado ice team. I had asked our server Lightening to *surprise me* Â for dessert in the beginning of ordering. And thank god he chose the panna cotta. The panna cotta was perfect after this feast because it was creamy and, to me a much better option since it was definitely not overwhelming. And the best part is avocado ice cream! Taste like super smooth avocado lightly sweetened. Very nice. :) And at last our bill came. With mini yoghurt probiotics that called Yakult that I've had throughout my entire childhood. And thank god I've had it before cause I was so over stuffed. Even though it is suppose to help with the digestion of my food. I wasn't able to drink until the next day. I left the place wobbling out the door and holding my stomach but with the happiness smile on my face. It has been awhile since I had a meal where I enjoyed it from start to finish.

Honestly, this pizza was nothing special. I really didn't even want to eat here, but I was hungry and there it was. I would have much rather eaten at Grimaldi's, but that wasn't an option. The wait is tremendously long and its not worth it at all. I've had much better pizza in a million different places all across the country.
The best the best the best!!! Ä° had a dinner here couple of days ago with my friend. And the steak I had was amazing. Beautiful romantic atmosphere. Friendly servers. Love it.

This restaurant is a udon west IZAKAYA, unlike my favorite little hole in the wall on St. Marks. I was in the neighborhood and decided to give it a try. I was greeted promptly by staff. Sitting at the bar, I ordered agedashi tofu and nabeyaki udon with a sansei udon to go on a drizzling Monday night. The staff was friendly and attentive; the chefs made eye contacts and smiled. The restaurant was half empty and the vibe was inviting. (1 star) The wait staff was not rushed, neither did they make me wait for long to order. (1 star) They serve the nabeyaki udon first - no biggie except the soup was not rolling boil and the filling was very little. Chicken was not grilled before hand like the other Udon West in St Mark's, and there was no spinach in my nabeyaki udon. The tempura batter on the shrimp was too thick to soak up the soup and fall out. The soup tasted ok. The noodle was satisfactory; not too stiff and definitely not your Chinese grocery udon noodle. (1 star) However, when I finished eating the fish cake, I tasted something funky which reminded me of scaling the fish, and Â my stomach started to hurt. Then came the agedashi tofu. I like how they laid the tofu flat on a small plate to make it easy to eat with a spoon. However, the sauce was way too sweet with not enough daikon radish and the serving was very small. The sweetness was sickening. While sitting at the bar, I kept getting my back bumped or slid by wait staff and patrons which was a bit annoying. I think I will come back here to try their sashimi and other izakaya item to be fair. I really want to like this place because the staff was very attentive and I was happy with the service. However, the food which made my stomach ache and was seasoned wrong simply does not make sense to return to. Perhaps I was unlucky on a October Monday night.
Beef lo me in awesome Pork buns awesome Spring rolls awesome Chicken fried rice amazing

If you haven't been to Eataly, then i insist you go immediately. Even if it involves a plane ticket.... just charge it to me - you need to see this place! It is a huge warehouse in some of the most expensive real estate in the world, so it's pricey. But that's ok, because although you will greatly admire the tiny, but beautiful Alessi milk jug, you will not pay $360 for it. The space is divided into several sections. Depending on which entrance you use, you will feel like it is a supermarket full of fresh produce, or a bustling coffee shop with gorgeous patisserie, or you will get shouted at for going 'in through the out door' if you try to enter on 23rd street by the registers. There are several restaurant/bar areas too - I was trying to think of my favourite space, but they all serve wine, so I like them all. The Pizza/Pasta area located in the middle of the 'dried goods' section of the supermarket is always very very crowded with a wait of an hour or more. Luckily you can put your name down and visit the bar area which has fantastically comfortable bar stools - I know because I once spent several hours on one sampling all the different red wine. You could also spend the time looking through the mouth watering selection of cheeses, vegetables, freshly made pasta, cook books, kitchenware that you desperately need but will never use, or..... you could visit the charcuterie section in the middle of the whole thing. Maybe that's my favourite place... the only downside is that it is based on small bars with no seating. Which means that you have to stay at least sober enough to keep standing up. Not my ideal evening, but hey, my liver sometimes deserves a night off. It does get really busy - weekends and anytime that's acceptable to be drinking an aperol spritz are crazy. It's part of the fun, go with it. The nice thing is that anyone shopping in this (let's face it) overpriced speciality Italian supermarket is probably middle class, nice and educated enough to control their temper. And if they're not, just stuff a cannoli in their mouth - they'll soon forget whatever gripe they had!

yes! Great decor (lots of lights...) and fun environment... A little too noisy with two groups around us, but after they left, it was much more bearable... The Indian beer was AWESOME!!! I'll be back!

Oooooohhhh it was soooooo gooooooood. Had to wait about an hour, but it was worth it. I had the Spicy Vegetarian Ramen, my husband had the Spicy Ramen (regular, with pork), we both got extra noodles as was recommended by another reviewer. Everything was so fresh, noodles had a perfect texture. Really wish they did take out!!!
The food was amazing and the service was great! My only negative comment is that the seating area was a little crumby.
Good atmosphere and had Sessions on tap, so all pluses in my book. Â They services was a bit slow and the food solid, but nothing spectacular or dishes that stood out. Â Overall good.

Love their spumoni and the pasta dishes. I had penne a la vodka with chicken and it was delicious! I wasn't impressed with the fried calamari, but their vodka sauce sure is good. Â  Good service as well. Â The waiter never failed to ask if we needed anything and the food came in decent time.

First off Service is Super friendly, Mike will remember your name after your first visit. Plus they have Doughnuts from Dough (oh how I love that place). Food is pretty tasty and fresh another huge pro, its right down the block from my house. I will say the only con is it is a Little bit pricey. Spent about 30 for breakfast for 2 with tip. I love the food though so I will be back!

Great place in alphabet city! Real mexican food that is delicious and staff that is friendly and attentive! It is my go-to mexican spot in NYC for things other than your run-of-the-mill tacos and burritos. Great margarita options and their happy hour also has appetizer specials in addition to drink specials (note: at the bar only)

It's not often a food joint earns 5 Stars for both its food and its generosity. Yes, generosity. While dining here today with my 4 year old daughter and enjoying a great meal in a cool atmosphere, we notice a bedraggled man walking in. Out of place among the hipsters and TriBeCa Mom fashionistas, I realized this man was homeless and assumed he would be promptly shown the exit. Instead, Shia, working behind the counter, respectfully asked him what he needed and initiated giving him a large bowl of their delicious split pea soup. I am sure the best meal that man has had in ages. Dine here for the food but come back frequently to show that good deeds and being a member of the whole community are the restaurants that we want in our neighborhood.

Went last week with friends and we had a great time. We ordered family style and all the meats tasted delicious. My favorite was the smoked pork... yum! The sauces were phenomenal and added just the right amount of kick. Tried a lager and I wish I could remember the name because it paired very well with our meal. Â I will definitely return!

Located underground, this small and cozy Pub is absolutely perfect. The name itself won a star in my book. You walk down a ramp to enter through the front door and there, welcomed by a very friendly worker. To the left we have the restaurant side, and to the right we have the bar. The interior design is epic and I am a big fan of how they did the whole place. It's beautiful. Our waitress, Sarah, was such a pleasure. She was so kind and she is the reason for the extra star on my initially four stars review. Me and Veronica got the salmon burger ($18 each) and James got the house blend burger ($19). My salmon burger was good yet a bit dry but nothing that a little ketchup and hot sauce couldn't fix. The chips that came on the side were perfect and I finished those way too soon. The fries that came with the house blend burger were absolutely delicious as well! They were perfectly salted and I kept stealing some from James. For drinks, I got the Juliet's Pimms Punch which contained Pimm's, chambord, and homemade lemonade, with a bit of mint and a cucumber slice. The taste starts off really sweet and fruity and then becomes more strong towards the end. The Shakespeare is definitely a place I would come back to!
Nice addition to the neighborhood

pros: cheap. cheap. cheap. delicious! i usually come here whenever i need to take the chinatown bus down to dc. got a spare $1 bill? yup---just trade it in for four Â tasty pan-fried dumplings...add you own sauce, and WALA...eat away. cons: small shack...and pretty dirty, but hey...the food trumps. (that's ny for the most part anyways...)

Sometimes it's hard for me to decide if any given restaurant deserves a 4 or 5 star review. Â But if any restaurant serves me something that is "close your eyes and savor the moment" delicious, it's an easy call. Here it was the french onion soup. Â The flavor explosion of my first bite absolutely rocked my socks. Let me back up a bit. Â We were seated relatively quickly around 8:30 on a Thursday night, but with a place this small, I can see it being hit or miss. Â The waitress was Â funny and helpful, and even had a little bit of a french accent to lend the experience a little extra dash of authenticity. I ordered the bistro steak frites and my fiance got the salmon. Â Both were delicious, but our excitement was a little tempered because we were still recovering from the appetizers and their mind blowing deliciousness. Â I mentioned that the french onion soup almost made cry, and she couldn't stop talking about how her roasted artichoke salad was the "most delicious thing she ever put in her mouth." We also had dessert, but I can't remember what it was called. Â It's a shame, because that was delicious too. Put it all together with a reasonably priced bottle of wine, and it was an excellent dining experience.

I have been wanting to try La Follia for some time now. Â We finally went there for dinner tonight and it did not disappoint. Â The Papardelle is to die for! Â Outstanding! Â It was served with a lot of shredded pork. Â I'd like to try their other dishes, but their Papardelle is so good, I might have to order it again! My partner had the Bolognese special which was very tasty. Â And we started with the fried calamari with peppers. Â The calamari was nice and tender with light breading. Â The peppers added a nice kick! They have some good wines by the glass, carafe, and bottle. Â We ordered the Sangiovese -- one of my favorite reds. The waiter was attentive and the service was very good... even with a full house. I will definitely go back again.

The lobster rolls and lobster bloody marys are so great that I'm willing to travel from Bushwick to Greenpoint to get it. Â BUT nothing is worse than a having my mouth water in anticipation for lobster the whole way only to get there on a monday and have it be closed!

Omg. It's love at first sight. A love which deepened upon first sip, then bite... A great bottled craft beer list, an array of fancy grilled cheese sandwiches, Â and coffee done with reverence. It will be hard to stay away.

Went here for dinner on a Saturday night around 7:00 - no reservation. Â They seated us quickly, and though we were pretty close to the people next to us, it wasn't bad. Â The music was good and the speakers were good quality. They have a great beer menu, though the one I ordered had a lot of foam. Â I ordered the ham-wrapped endive, and my wife got the meatballs with frites for dinner. Â Both were decent, but not incredible. I'd say the best part was the dessert. Â We shared the chocolate mousse. Â I am not a big dessert person, but the mousse was better than I thought it would be, and for only $7. It's a nice little restaurant, and I'd recommend it if you're in the area. Â Next time I'd probably go back and have a drink at the bar first as well.

Met a friend for drinks and appetizers! Â It was delicious. Â Definitely a great destination for us since we live close by BUT I recommend it to anyone who enjoys great food at an optimum price point. Â The fried panko-crusted oysters are delicate, while the salmon tartare was simply dressed with powerful flavors; just like the decor. Â Simple, powerful and comfortable. Â Enjoy NYC and all those who discover this neighborhood gem!

Super oily and completely lacking in flavor. I'm bot sure what all of you see in this place but it is completely sub par compared to everywhere else I've been in China Town. My mouth tastes like msg. Bathroom had hand sanitizer in the soap dispenser.
This is by far one of the best hidden gems in the city. I was born and raised in NYC and this is a top 5 spot. Go early to sit in the garden.

This is a brunch review so for now i'll give it just 4 stars. Â Friend and myself went in around 1:30pm on a Sunday, the place is very cozy and not extremely packed but there was a constant coming and going of people. Â I ordered the hangover pizza which is a big hit in the reviews and from word of mouth. Â My friend ordered the L'Italiano poached eggs; grilled Italian bread, hot sopressata & ricotta. Â The pizza is large enough for 2-4 people maybe even more as it's about the size of a small pizza cut into 8 peices. Â It was delicious, wow, it had just the right about of spiciness from the sausage and the potatoes on top gave it this breakfasty feel. Â Would definitely order again but with a larger party. Â I was sad to have left overs and couldnt take them with me because of where i was going afterwards. Â My friends dish, the L'italiano, just as good if not better, it was a perfect portion and will definitely order it as well next time. Â The sopressata and ricotta with the poached eggs was a wonderful combination. Â She got a side of home fries which were perfect compliment a side salad could of been just as good. Â  Â I forget the wine she ordered but it was a white and was crisp and refreshing, great for brunch. Â I ordered the Vesta punch, which in my personal opinion was just ok, will not be ordering it again as it just didnt agree with me and I was expecting to taste the fruit flavors more. Â Our server was attentive but not overbearing, always with a smile which was genuine, you could see he was happy to help and answer any questions we had about the dishes and drinks, very helpful. Â  Â Definitely a great spot for any occasion or people. Â Date, family, kids, friends. Â Highly recommend and will be going back again to try all the brunch dishes. Â I'll update this review when I have something new to add.

I only get the spicy vegetarian. Â It is great, good level of spice, lots of veggies and chewy noodles. Â the wait is long- try to come on an off time. Â The downside is the annoying people on line. Â Stand to the side. Â Wait your turn or leave. Â Stop making a big deal. Â Also come with one or 2 other people, not your 3 kids, your baby stroller, your luggage. Â Eat, enjoy, leave.

Oh sweet baby J another decent restaurant in Sunnyside! What's next more than two good bars? I kid, I kid, no for real it's amazing sunnyside is coming into it's own and starting to attract some winners. The name itself is enough to get anyone in the door. Who doesn't love salt and fat? The other thing that sold me were the dishes. Creative plays on classic favorites. Starting from the moment you sit down with popcorn, but wait is that bacon grease? Oh, yes it's cooked in bacon grease, my friends. My lovely date and I choose the crack and cheese and the pork tacos. I have to say I could have done without the bacon in the crack and cheese it was just a little too much. The tacos were amazing! I will say I love small dishes, as you can try more things, and three dishes was perfect for us. We finished with the marshmallow ice cream, yes yes yes. A few tips, they're only open for dinner, tear. Only take cash. Lots of seating!

I love it here! Â We started with a few cheeses from the cheese menu that were complimented with an awesome Tuscan red that the waiter suggested. Â We shared an heirloom tomato salad that just exploded with unique taste. Â Dinner was superb - both the fish special and the steak. Â And, the service could not have been better.
Everything(including other food, service, and the environment) besides the Xiao Long Bao is horrible.

Honestly, this will be my first time giving a place 4 stars based mainly on ambiance and service. I think it would be hard not to enjoy a meal at Ippudo. First their organization in spite of the fact that the wait time is hours long for a table is on point. They dont play. Secondly, when you are seated there are a flurry of american japanese yelling waiters at your service. Dirty your napkin? BAM new one in ten seconds. Out of water? LIES, that never happens there. The food was nice, the pork bun is hands down best one I've tried, the meat is chock full of flava' and they have some special sauce action going on in there. The ramen itself is nice, I appreciated the kae dama ( more noodles for 2 bucks) option since I found the noodles a bit thin. The chashu pork was good no complaints there. Still I feel like if you are going to charge 13 bucks for ramen which is essentially street food in Japan from what ive heard, you better be doing something special with it. I didnt feel like Ippudos ramen on its own was a game changer, but I can definitely get behind this restaurant as a whole experience.
Excellent spot for late night dining -grilled calamari is a favorite.

We hopped in and there was a 45 minutes wait, but the hostess took our phone number down and texted us when our table was ready, which was super cool. The place is super loud and crowded but the food is PHE-NO-ME-NAL. Fresh OJ and Nutella French Toast were to die for. The pumkin waffles were good as well. Will definitely go back!

From the old school but very commercial Hip hop and R&B to the deliciously strong cocktails and interesting fare, Cubana Social held my interest from the moment I walked through its doors. The decor is reminiscent of pre-Castro Cuba, complete with palm trees, simple lines of hanging lights, and small performance stage. But I must've went on movie night--a projection of a classic film was my main entertainment. Perfect for someone in love with vintage everything. The menu, though, is a unique approach to Latin cuisine, fusing the old with the new by using locally grown and organic ingredients in traditional and non traditional dishes. I love that it also incorporates gluten-free and vegetarian options. Like the won-my-heart avocado tempura. Fish tacos were delicious, spicy, and pretty on the plate. I didn't really care for the "taco" part, made of plantain. An interesting idea but too thick and potatoe-y to work. I'll definitely come back for the Celia Cruz, refreshing and sweet, like my experience at Cubana Social overall.

** 1,000 review ** Everything about Tia Pol is a-ok to good. It was some of the better tapas I've had in New York City at New York City price and portions. At first, I was excited that my group of five was seated in the back, for there's more space. However, we were seated at a long table, and by being at the end, I missed about Â of the conversation. That's also because the music was playing on the louder side. I was also not impressed with the lack of dÃ©cor. When I think of tapas, I think of "fun fare" and expected a little bit more on the walls. My friends and I ordered so many yummy dishes. You have to get the artichoke salad. The dressing is heavy, but it's lemony goodness. (Maybe ask to go light on the dressing?) The fried chickpeas were also unique and worth checking out. I also liked the squid ink dish, but there weren't many pieces of squid, and the pieces were on the smaller side. (But, yummm, ink!) The fava bean spread was nice and subtle as well. Lastly, we also got the almond cake and custard ball desserts. Both were pretty good, but I wasn't totally blown away by either of them. I'd recommend the custard balls (4 in a order) over the almond cake, I think. Unfortunately, the evening ended with my friend's Tia Pol gift card not being accepted because it incorrectly came up as having no balance. (You'd think that if the card had already been used that the restaurant would have kept the card, right?) The manager was apologetic, but the event unavoidably soured the experience. Then again, the price wasn't too bad in the end even without the discount.

Totto hits the spot like no other food joint in the city... When I go to Totto, I don't eat breakfast or lunch because not being able to finish the amazingly tasty ingredients put into every single culturally crafted bowl of blissfulness would do dishonor to the ramen gods. There is no doubt in my mind that this is the best bang for your buck in NYC... the appetizers and entrees are as cheap as they come, and the service is quick and alert. When I go, I get the Totto Chicken Paitan Ramen, with the Char Siu Pork, Kikurage Mushroom, Seasoned Boiled Egg, and the rayu sauce for some kick. The flavor combos work really well together... I do wish they had a poached egg option though. If they offer the grilled sea urchin special ($4.50) order it. While it is difficult to declare a clear winner of 'who has the best ramen in NYC' Totto gives Ippudo a run for their money. Ippudo doesn't have as much culture and soul as Totto, but has a more diversified and pricier menu... Bottom Line: Go to Totto, wait on the line, and brace yourself for an exploration the likes of which your mouth has never experienced. When you sit down in this restaurant you are no longer in America... you are in ramen country...

Had high hopes for this restaurant, but was greatly let down. I came here with a friend and we ordered the avocado toast- I'm an avocado lover and this was extremely bland and I didn't even want to finish it! I then had the chicken and waffles- or shall I say raw meat and bread. The chicken was significantly undercooked with visible blood, which made it inedible. Highly do not recommend!

If I worked in Midtown East, I'd be having lunch at Piccolo Cafe on the regular. Â I stumbled upon this cafe and chose the roasted italian peppers, arugula, dijon mustard, bufala mozarella, and chicken panini, which comes with a mesculun green side salad ($10). Â It was very good and very satisfying. There are six small tables in this cafe and the walls are lined with old Italian newspapers, which gives it a cozy atmosphere. Â  To sum it up: good food, fast and friendly service, affordable prices, and a cozy atmosphere. Â What more do you want from a lunch spot?
I have been on a search for the best Bahn Mi in Jersey City, NYC and Brooklyn. Â This is the winner!
Went for brunch with 5 other friends. We were seated within 15 minutes. Service was great and food was nice and fresh. Not the best I've had but I'll definitely be back.
Super bland food and way over priced!

Just had brunch with my girlfriend, and I would say that the food is a 3.5 the Chill-a-Killers were really tasty, the poached eggs in the benedict were overcooked, the standout was the homemade chicken breakfast sausage that was a 5. Â The staff was nice, personable and attentive, the mimosas were ok (the cucumber one wasn't for me but my girlfriend loved it), the coffee was good, overall I would give it another chance.

My first gluten-free dining experience was a good one. I don't have any gluten issues, but my girlfriend was recently forced into a very restrictive diet, and I don't want to be that jerk eating delicious things in front of her, so off we went to Risotteria. The place is very small and cramped, but for some reason, it didn't bother us, and it normally would. The servers were extremely friendly, and give you the most awesome GF breadsticks to snack on. And I have to reveal some shame: Not only was this my first GF dining experience, but it was also my first time trying risotto, GF or otherwise. Despite having a great menu selection (both G and GF), we both went with the classic risotto, which were delicious! The prices were just right too. I can't wait to return next time I'm in NYC.

Best Ethiopian Food in NYC (and I know my Ethiopian food after having lived in DC for 3.5 years). Great service, great prices, and amazing portions. I loved all of my food and will definitely be back.

Atmosphere 4/5 - A little bit more dimly lit, making it a great date spot. Service 4/5 - As we had an extremely large table, the wait was a little hefty but the service was very good. The check was divided by SEAT to make things easier at the end of the night (to do so is godly in NYC) Food 5/5 - I had the Kaisen don & set which came with a sort of fluffy egg soup, salad, and miso soup. The dish I had was assorted seafood on top of perfectly cooked sushi rice. I used to live in Japan for a while in undergraduate so I am particular with my food... but this was quite good. Not too pricey either.

Nobody should gets 5 stars, there is always room for improvement but I don't see how this place can get any better. Excellent food that is priced below what one expects to pay for N.Y. and 1/2 price bottles of wine on Wednesdays. We camped out on the porch and enjoyed the fire place,lunch, our wines while watching the rain drizzle outside on a small outdoor dining section Â closed for the winter. The server was friendly and competent without the pretentious air I've come to expect in a lot of this neighborhoods eatery's.I also received a warm greeting from the manager and her bar staff. This facility is a go to place when on this side of town.

This rating is based on the venue which is immaculate, service which is friendly, and people which are sociable. If the food adds up to the hype all i can say is SOCO FTW! SOCO has definitely started on the right path to success. Now were is the food I'm starving drooling over your entree pics online! :)

The food was actually very good. Â My complaint is the Union Square portions and prices. Â My lady and I were hungry after our entrees and had to order more food. Â And she's a toothpick! Â Does the owner realize he's in Bed Stuy?
I went again and I must reiterate, it just doesn't get any better than a $6.75 bacon cheeseburger and a $3 Yuengling draught.. Best burger for the buck in NYC.
The only way to end the night out in NYC. Enjoy.

Reminiscent of the markets and streets of Italy. Everything is a little scattered and the huge place is much more pretentious than Whole Foods. I WILL be back to Eataly for products such as breads, meats, wine, etc.

Helloooo sauces! Â I'm obsessed with sauces in general. This place has a gazillion choices. Fries are good but I'd eat anything dipped in those sauces. So many choices. I feel pressured when I'm there and always walk out feeling like I shouldve gotten the other one. But always happy with whatever I get.

Let me start off by saying that I tend to be very picky when it comes to Colombian food. As a Latina, I'm always trying all sorts of cuisines but in particular Latin food. I loved this place! The red sangria was made just the way I like it. They definitely put the time and effort into their food/drinks and service. I fell in love with their Arepa de Chocolo with shredded queso blanco. I can't wait to return and try other menu choices. I liked the comfort and casual-ness of this place as well. Nice decorations :)

Didn't know what to expect but the place exceeded expectations. 5 Reasons to go: 1. The trout is exceptional and the accompanying garnish and veggies are wonderful. 2. The meatloaf sandwich is an A++ 3. The jalapeno bacon cornbread is tasty as hell. This coming from someone who generally despises cornbread. 4. Excellent service plus fairly reasonable prices. 5. The orgasmic chocolate bread pudding. I've been trying to hit most of the top restaurants in Williamsburg and this place is one of the best. All five of us who came for dinner loved the food.

They do not take reservations except for parties of 8, sure no problem, I will wait. Got there at 8:30 pm, table for 5? Guy at the door who would benefit from some anxiety pills FYI, says it will be wait about 2 hours. Wait, he would be benefit from some ginkgo for concentration as well. Â So we go grab drinks in the hood, come back in hour and half, and he informs us Â it will be another hour to two. Well sure, will go get another drink somewhere else. Table opens up in the place around the corner with the same flare, and we end up there. Â Two hours later no phone call, we passed by the place just so I can give a handful to that guy and he is not there, few tables empty! Have not tried the food, but based on their disorganization and lack of proper customer etiquette I would pass this place big time!

I've not yet checked this place at night but judging from the bar and what's on tap that might be the time to come. Instead, since this place is stumbling distance away, I went here for brunch, but I'll be stumbling further on down fifth in the future. First of all, we stopped by about 3 minutes before they open on Sunday and we're turned away. When we came back a little later we were escorted to the back room although the more appealing front area was entirely empty. The back room decor definitely would look better in low light. With the lights on the horrible chipped-up paint job, worse wall art and general clutter were all left exposed and gave the place a dumpy atmosphere. Our waiter, although competent, had a unique serving style that was maybe aiming for unobtrusive but came off as strange and inattentive. Our coffee was european strong in a good sized cup, but our food was not impressive. The latka entree was small, the polenta (raved about here) made me wonder what previous yelpers were talking about, and the flatbread was a big puff of sweet overload. I've travelled extensively through eastern Europe, lived in EE enclaves in the states, and love the cuisine, but I'm sure any native eating here would have a few words for the chef. And maybe this is a more general gripe, but calling breakfast brunch doesn't warrant a $6 markup per plate.
Went on a saturday night, and had a wonderful time. The food was creative and delicious. The staff were friendly, attentive, and knowledgable. We will certainly be back.

I love coming to Queens Kickshaw -- it's always a great place whether for coffee, dinner or just late night drinks or dessert. Lovely place to come and get some work done, catch up on reading, or grab a bite with a group of friends. The coffee is great, but their hot chocolate and hard ciders is what I usually go for when I'm not there to eat. From the food menu my favorites are the gouda and guava jam grilled cheese sandwich and their mac and cheese with green beans and caramelized onions --- best ever!! The meal portions can seem a little small for the price, but I don't think it's that much pricier compared to most places around. Their brunch is also good, but it's not my favorite, especially given there's always a pretty long wait for brunch on weekends. They used to have a pear compote french toast and omelette with fried parmesan that's no longer on the brunch menu anymore, sadly. Â  I've never experienced bad service here and the place is super cute, so all in all I would give this place a solid five star. :)
Just had drinks at the bar downstairs. Cosy bar with encapsulating grandpa chairs - yes please! I'd definitely go back for drinks, and perhaps even eat the next time round.

I LOVE Blue Ribbon Brasserie! Every time I've been, the food and service have been outstanding. You can't go wrong with anything you get, but if you need a recommendation I would say start with the oysters and get the fried chicken. Â If you're with a big group, try the seafood tower. The service is always top notch and the ambiance is warm in cozy. The only issue is they don't take reservations for parties of 6 or less, so you'll have to wait. Â And the bar area is tiny, so waiting inside is a little tight.

Grape and Grain is bursting with charm. I loved the secret drawer filled with napkin scrawled notes in the antique tables we dined on. The shrimp and grits and bacon satiated my post-Friday night malaise and filled me up. I loved the simple charm of the spot--unpretentious yet lovely, hip, yet not annoyingly hipster-esque for brunch. I was dazzled by the gorgeous antique tea sets and cutlery with floral engravings on some of the spoons. Our food was served by a laid-back server with a pleasant presence and soft smile. I will be returning. It is a special spot. Love!

This was certainly the most luxurious meal I have ever had! My girls and I hit the redial button nonstop to get reservations. Just as I was giving up, my friend got through. This was her first time ever calling and SCORE! we got a reservation. Pure luck...should have also bought a lottery ticket that day! I tried keeping track of how many dishes were served, but I lost count quickly. There was uni, caviar, duck, fish that I have never heard of. Every dish was amazing and the service was spotless. Â  If you can get a reservation and stomach the cost, go for it...it will be an absolute unforgettable experience.
Stella 34 Trattoria has some of the most unique Italian dishes in New York! Great view from the 6th fl of Macy's too.

The day sanfords decided they were too faux high class to serve coleslaw and pickles with a burger was the day I stopped going. Sanfords was GREAT when we first moved to the neighborhood 7 years ago, a nice super high quality diner that served booze. Then there was the the fire and it seemed like it was a steady decline from there. I guess they wanted to change the direction of the restaurant but it just didn't work for us. The last few times we went the quality was just poor, chewy steak, pancakes weren't fully cooked, bacon soggy, burnt omelet. They do get two stars for the fries though, those have always been nice and crispy. I hope these last few times were just a fluke but unfortunately we won't be going back until i hear they are serving pickles and coleslaw again. This is officially a pickle protest.

24-48 hours later, I'm still thinking about this meal. *Love* it. I'd go back in a heartbeat. In short, the food was outstanding. 4 meat-heavy dishes (plus bread & butter, which we requested) were shared between the 2 of us: 1) Sea urchin with bacon on focaccia. 4 delicious (yet small) bites. Total flavor explosion. I don't recommend sharing. 2) Agave Glazed Chicken Wings. How do you elevate the chicken wing? Like this. Loved the blue cheese emulsion. 3) Braised Short Rib of Beef. Does it get any better than this? (Answer: NO.) The short rib was so tender. Paired well with taglierini pasta (and somehow Not a textural disaster)! Portions were very generous. 4) Roasted Pork Belly Confit. They had me at pork belly. Yes, the menu is a bit visually overwhelming. 40+ plates described on 40+ single-spaced lines. Take your time, and ask the knowledgeable and friendly wait staff for recommendations. Great atmosphere. Loft-like space. 2 levels of seating. Dim lighting. And a nice date place (but gets noisy during peak hours). FYI: Only cash and American Express accepted.

Ippudo was nice. But with all the hype, I expected much better. I guess it's because I had their pork buns first. Those were amazing. I could eat those every day. No wonder people pay $8 for two small buns. The ramen was alright, although I wish they gave more meat. I only had two slices of pork in mine. They did ask if I wanted extra noodles with my left over soup however. I guess that's a plus. It's also expensive, so I'm not sure if it's really worth the money. I'll go when I need to take people somewhere nice to eat.

I love this place. It's exactly what you would want from shabu shabu. We often go with a group of 5-8, and always with a reservation. It's often pretty full so make sure you call ahead (even a couple days). They also only have one large table in the corner that can comfortable accommodate 8+ (has 2 table stoves). But let's get to the food -- it's so good that we always order the same -- the prime meat. The meal comes with a small starter salad that has an amazing peanut dressing. I hate salad but it's like candy, so I enjoy it. Then the stove is turned on and everyone starts dropping in the vegetables (mushrooms, carrots, cabbage.. even tofu). Once the water soaks up the flavor we drop in the meat (high quality and A LOT of it). I've typically come with groups, but it's also a good date spot (food is great, with good company and a little teamwork on the cooking - pretty awesome.) The food is good and the act of helping make your meal is a nice addition for most of us cooking inept ny'ers. The meal finishes off with a scoop of ice cream (chocolate, vanilla, red bean, green tea). Do your table a favor and get a pitcher of beer to help it all go down too.
