Noodle Soup was okay, a bit salty. Â The Pork bun is a must. Â Be prepare comfortable shoes while waiting for seat. Â It took at least an hour if pass 6:30pm. Â I longest I waited was 1 1/2 hours.
! Wonderful place, the food is great, and it brings me back to Korea :). The people are very friendly and it has a comfortable atmosphere that makes you feel like everyone is together :).

We have been here before and enjoyed it. It is loud, but manageable, the service is fast, and the burgers amazing. Tonight was a disaster. It was unbearably loud. Our server told us that the music was set and that was that - there was nothing he could do about it. We waited 40 minutes for our burgers, and they were not cooked. All in all, a ruined evening.

Omg I have found the number one fried chicken spot in NYC, yes I said NYC. Silvia's use to good, then there's Amy Ruth, good but pies and thighs ohhhhh my. I thought my grandma was in their kitchen and it was Sunday dinner. If you're longing for real southern style collared greens fried chicken and cornbread I urge you to take a trip to pies and thigh really good food

Really phenomenal and so crazy charming! I've walked by this place for years never having gone in. Me and the boyfriend went in on a whim the other day because (we both had a craving for Muscles) and it was insanely good. The prices are so reasonable and the food tastes so fresh. We got the Muscles & Frites as an appetizer along with a cheese plate and the I got the Coq Au Vin he got the Steak Hache . So crazy good and rich with flavor. Very romantic ambiance too. Heading back soon.

Scored a table for a random Saturday brunch, and the place did live up to it's outstanding reputation. There is some kind of mood that lives in there, it's an energy. The service was decent and the ambiance was energetic. I felt like I was getting an experience and a meal, not just a meal. We had the Steak Frites, Eggs Benedict and Mac and Cheese.The Eggs Benedict was outstanding, I was expecting a little more from the Steak Frites but I am spoiled by steakhouses I guess. The mac and cheese kind of stood by itself, it was quite tasty but not the best I have ever had. We then ordered a bottle of wine, after the meal for some reason, the wine list was outstanding by the way. I feasted on the Caramelized Banana Ricotta Tart for dessert, it was delightful. I will say again with much fanfare, it was an experience as much as it was a meal. The place is a cathedral of dining in New York City. Keith McNally should run for mayor, he has my vote.

came here memorial day sunday for brunch and it was dead! woohoo! i think it gets pretty busy on a normal weekend though, bc i overheard a regular say its really quiet. it is a nice place for brunch outside since its on a quiet sidewalk, however, not very good for people watching. they didnt rush us out since there were very few ppl there, but not sure if thats the case on a regular weekend and the service was very friendly. the food was very reasonably priced, and it was fresh. i had the proscuitto sandwich, which was very filling, and a delicious iced coffee - very strong for an iced coffee. my bf had a grilled cheese sandwich with tomato, he loved it, but it was too greasy for me. i'd come back to try more.

Nothing about BUVETTE can make me understand its popularity and why there is an hour wait for Sunday brunch. *Garden seating is cramped; table for 2 is hardly big enough for one, and the chairs are tiny and very uncomfortable. *Portions are small; prices are high and food is just fair. *Service is slow. *I couldn't wait to leave, wondering what the fuss is all about. I just don't get it.

Popped in for a quick dinner after some Flatiron shopping on a Saturday night. Â Great escape from the cold in the back room with a fireplace! Â Definitely coming back for their weekday specials. Â All you can eat mussels and a Stella for $24!

Make sure to request a table upstairs by the live music/cigar rolling or you will miss it downstairs. The drinks are strong and the mojitos are traditional; SURPRISE: you can order pitchers for the table! It's loud, fun and a great place to have a big birthday bash. The food is tasty, and when ordering entrees, I'd recommend sticking with chicken. Food to get: -Ceviche -Any chicken dish especially Â Chicken Breast: Sweet Plantain. Mozzarella. Mushrooms. Zucchini. White Wine Sauce Don't get the Mahi Mahi in cachucha pepper sauce. It looks like an orange sea of floating fish (appearance distracts from the taste here). I loved the lively atmosphere, authentic staff accents and friendly culture. Come here for a guaranteed, entertaining time! P.S. Cigars are complimentary ***Tip: Every Monday night = $5 drinks and appetizers
Everything is great on the menu....... Â Even the salads are addictive. Â I love eating here often.

Dumplings are tasty and cheap! Can also buy them frozen in a bag! Owner is nice and gives you instructions how to fry them properly. He even gave us one of the sauces for free. Sesame pancakes are simple and delicious. Noodles are fine. Can walk away with a full stomach with just $5!

Corn on a cob...or shall I say CRACK on a cob?! It's definitely their signature. GET IT! It's always SO busy here, so you should almost always expect a wait! And the seats are TINY! If you're okay with being half an arm's length to the table besides you, then sure, come for dinner. Actually, the food really isn't all that bad, but the experience had been so RUSHED, it took the fun outta it.

I have nothing bad to say about this place, other than it's not closer to where I live.(Long Island City) Coming from San Diego, I usually stay away from Mexican restaurants because they just can't seem to get it right in NYC, but this place went beyond my expectations. I had the guacamole and elote for appetizer, and then a chicken torta. But I got the feeling that whatever I ordered would have been fantastic. Great atmosphere, very friendly service, and good cocktails. My friend had a tequila based cocktail that was served in a small terracotta cup which was really good. If you like tequila, and the recession hasn't bit you, treat yourself to the Don Julio 1942. Best tequila I've had, and Carino carries it. I will definitely go back to this place when I'm in Williamsburg again. Â Great spot!!

Decided to check this place out for brunch with a few of my girlfriends today and honestly, I think people hyped up this place too much. In addition, the waitress made the smoked salmon frittata sound exponentially better than how it really tasted. The "omelette" like dish was bland with a one dimensional taste of "egg" while the texture parallels to a solidified airy omelette. Shoot, if I knew, I would have stayed home and made myself a more exciting omelette! The price was decent for the okay food that they served. Although, the waitstaff was very attentive, it was questionable if either they wanted to wait on us or if they were just trying to rush us out but it seem more of the latter. It was just okay.

I burned my mouth really bad on a bowl of searing hot soup here. They warned me it was hot but I was so thirsty I just started guzzling it down and paid the price - I haven't been able to feel my mouth for a week - I can hardly swallow lol. Somebody left there bread at the table so I got some free bread out of the deal and was able to save some for later. The manager even brought me some ice from around the counter - CAUTION SOUP IS HOT LOL

The bf looked up a place around the neighborhood that had brunch and we came here. They have a brunch menu as well as cold cuts, sandwiches and some baked desserts. I got the eggs Benedict which came with bacon which I thought was better than ham and he got an omelette. He really enjoyed it and both came with fries that were dusted in Parmesan and delicious! The waitress was very nice and the place was cozy. I would come again :)

I have been here 4 times in the last 4 months. Â I would come here more often but I live in FiDi and this place is in Hell's Kitchen. Â Woe is me Â :( If this was in my neighborhood, I believe I would eat here at least 3-4 times a week. Â Is the food THAT good? Â No, but it is better than most. Â I LOVE spicy spicy food and this place gives my spice a kick! This that I always love is the Papaya salad, the chicken curry puffs, Pad Kee Mao. Â I have tried almost every dish on that menu (yes, even though I have been there only 4 times, I order a Sh*t ton of food). Â All are fair to excellent. Â  It is the best Thai food I have had in NYC thus far. Â Any other places that I should try?

Romantic, dimly lit, Italian den with friendly and courteous service! We came in with family friends who had two kids under 4 and although they were a little rowdy (we came in early- at 6pm) then service never faltered for a second.

Request that bowl of chicken skin. Â The pieces are huge fried swatches of crispy skin. Â How are the pieces so big? Â Let's just put it in our mouths and not think too much about it. Â Man. Â It's got mega crunch. Â It's free too - what? Â Free fried skin. Â That's so rad. Sizzling sisig of pork ears and pork fat was good. Â Greasy greasy, and the vinegar helps add good acid. Â There's no wonder why Filipino people are so thick. Â I have one Filipino friend who has a literal bowling ball for a head. Â He says there is more of him to love. Â Gross. Â  I tried them out at the meatpacking pop-up, so I need to check out their new location soon or somethin'.

Simple, decent, delicious. Nothing mindblowing. I tried their salt&pepper shrimp and their scallion noodles. Too salty on the scallion noodles but I didn't really mix up the sauce like I was supposed to.

Being Chinese and in New York. My inner FOB was compelled to visit my roots and semi-motherland..*que oriental music*..Chinatown! btw I HATE the word oriental. I miss Chinese Food. I miss it more than anything. I think I miss it more than SEX! eh...I take that back...I could go without Chinese food for a bit. But anyways Chinese food at Joe's Shanghai sound like the NYC version of "Panda Express" but this place puts the A in authentic. The funny thing is that you'll never find anyone named Joe serving you. Â In fact, when my non chinese speaking friend tried to order, the waiters formed a football style huddle to determine which one was most likely to understand our order in English/ChingElish. The Goods: Crab Meat Steamed Bun static.px.yelp.com/bphotâ€¦ Yea. How I imagined. The Skin was a bit thick but that helped keep all the juice from not EXPLODING before it gets into your mouth. The Soup was good and damn nearly burnt off all my taste buds! Onion Pancake static.px.yelp.com/bphotâ€¦ Onion lovers unite. I love Onion Pancake! Eggplant with Garlic Sauce w/ Â Pork static.px.yelp.com/bphotâ€¦ This Dish was spicy!! I was hurting the next day.. Pan Fried Noodles Â w/ Beef static.px.yelp.com/bphotâ€¦ One of my favorite dishes. Can't go wrong with this choice. What I didn't like is that you have to "Dap Toi" = share table with complete strangers and try not to steal there food! You might sit with total strangers and have that awkward silence or try not to act too much of a fool. The four of us tried to spread ourselves around a table that would seat a family of 8...heh the waiter wasn't having any of that.

stopped in because we were looking for a good little place to have brunch. The burgers are amazing, so much flavor and taste so fresh. I ordered the shrimp chili pasta and it was out of this world! I would 100% recommend this place and I am definitely coming back!

This is a small but comfortable restaurant on the LES. Â This staff is friendly, attentive and professional. Â They have a Â limited menu but everything on it is recognizable and good. Â They also have great cocktails. I went there because we were heading to PDT at 9pm after and i was pleasantly surprised. Â i would definitely go back.

I came here with Lori N. and had a delightful, authentic-Italian dinner. Their lunch specials are stellar: we got the potato leek soup and vegetable panini for $9.50 (that's with tax). The potato leek soup was a different type than I've ever had -- a bit chunky. Needed some salt but was tasty. The panini was very hearty. The bread was stellar. Be sure to get some of their delectable olive oil from the shelf, too. There's only enough seating for, like, 6 or 8 people, but stay if you can. The vibe is wonderful.

Ahh so much food I don't remember it all. Focus was more on the conversation, and that's what this place is all about. But these are all good: Creamy cod roe spaghetti, croquettes, beef tongue, pork belly, fish jaw, chicken meat balls, a mess of yakitori, fried pork fat, black sesame ice cream with mochi--all good. Wide range, and all of it is tasty. Better than Kenka, by a mile. Also more exp.

Would gladly give a 4.5 if I could. A clean and delightful dining experience. Girlfriend and I were looking for a new place to go and happened upon this one based upon the reviews. It did not disappoint at all. We both had the prix fixe and it was delicious. My pumpkin soup was super and the char was perfect. I was stuffed for dessert but had no problem enjoying it all. Enjoy!

Insanely overrated. I sat at the bar and was served by the bartender. The girl never stopped moving, I have to give her props. The Mexican Firing Squad she made me was okay. Not sure there was any "homemade grenadine" in it and I'm pretty certain she put hot sauce in there instead of orange bitters, but whatever, it was drinkable. Got the corn, which is covered in mayo (ew), cheese and chili powder. When the chili powder and greens on the bottom of the plate are the redeeming factors, you know it's not very impressive. Also, I could see the chefs grilling the corn and they grill it, and then throw it into a huge bin, so no wonder my corn was lukewarm when I got it. Also, there are 2 cobs in an order, surprise! I also had the roast pork, black beans and yellow rice. The roast pork was insanely juicy, but lacked much flavor. The yellow rice was good. I had to douse it all with hot sauce to give it a taste. The service was good. The bartender let me charge my phone and all of the servers were pleasant. This place has been on my list of must-gos for so long now and I am pretty bummed it didn't live up to expectations. I mean, mayo on corn...what the fuck was I thinking?

I'm a fan because of the specials and the place is pretty cute. I went last night with the bf, roomie, and brother (whose visiting from San Diego). Â My bro was like very cool little french spot nice, the decor was awesome. Â The service was poor but not in an unfriendly or bad way just unorganized - they must asked us how many for a table about 10 times. Â  We went on unlimited moules night, which none of us did. We did start with moules - which was delicious... yummy. Â I split the burger with the roomie - to be honest it was alright. The fries were good. Â We also ordered a salad with carmelized brie and pears - yeah we are fatties so what ... and it was aight, actually no it was mediocre. The ambiance was right and it was pretty inexpensive as dining goes. Â Its a nice option for my hood and would probably go again.

The burgers here are pretty tasty. I had both the truffle burger and the duck burger (not on the menu). Splitting with a friend, I think the truffle burger was more to my liking. Also ordered the fries. I personally think it would've taste better without cheese and a little less salt. The service is good and the waiters were friendly. My friends and I waited for 1.5 hours and came back to stand outside the restaurant and wait another half an hour. Burger is good, too long of a wait is not. I think it's been hyped up too much, hence the long wait.

I am originally from Kolkata, India where kati rolls are the iconic street food. All I can say is that the rolls served here are really close to authentic, except in Kolkata you will not find a shrimp roll. Our go to option is the Unda Shammi, and for those in the know this is very close to what is served at the Dhabha at Ballygunge Phari at Kolkata. We prefer this location to the one at MacDougal street since it is more spacious.
totally delicious and fun dining experience
awesome yakitori! :) -premium beef -chicken skin -chicken oyster nice service. good selection of sake.

Visited Perry St last night for dinner. The meal was fantastic, everything tasted incredible from appetizers, entrees to the drinks. However, the service was dreadful. After taking our order, we did not see our waiter for the rest of the night. It was as if he disappeared. Turns out after asking about him, he had left during the shift and passed our table on to another waiter. Which is fine, but this was never communicated to us by either waiter and we were basically ignored for the duration of the meal. Again, we were very pleased with the quality of the food/drinks but for such a highly regarded (and expensive) restaurant the service was poor enough that we will be skipping on Perry St the next time we look for a high end dinner.

Great place! Â We came in a bit early (12pm'ish) and there was only brisket available (as far as meat was concerned) so we had that while there. Â They were nice and there was sides such as potato salad which is delicious especially topped with scallions that they out on top. Â I didn't taste the collared greens but the chili was good, (very spicy) but good. Â We waited until around 1:30pm for the ribs to be bought in and man were they worth the wait. Â It seems (and maybe I'm wrong) that the peppery brisket rub was mixed with sugar and used on the ribs. Â They have beef and pork but since we had the brisket we got the pork ribs. Â Its family friendly and can accommodate a couple of large groups (not more than 6-10 people I would say). Â  Todd (the guy that served us slices of meat heaven) was just awesome! Â He was so accommodating, generous and just all around helpful and sweet. I like how everything seemed strategically placed and decorated. Â I would definitely eat here again with no problem. Â A bit pricey but not too bad considering the quality and what other places are charging. Â Really good grub with a nice little $3 beer happy hour (12-6pm)

First I must say, either make a reservation or get there at opening. We got there at opening with 5 people and all tables were reserved, we had to squish into a booth. We ordered everything under Shabu menu: pork, chicken, prime beef, beef, and shrimp. They also bring a heaping plate of cabbage, mushrooms, noodles, tofu, carrots, etc. One of the most fun way I've eaten. You take your chop sticks and your thin cut of meat and you swish it around in the water until it cooks how you prefer, then dip it into one of two sauces, I believe one was a sesame sauce and the other like a ginger (correct me if I'm wrong). Small location but great food! Too bad they don't have big tables for groups. It's about $22-24 per person for the Shabu. Comes with salad (tiny), the meat, and ice cream (red bean ice cream and green tea is amazing)
Ate here twice in the same week. Good stuff.

I've always thought macaroons were overrated until I tried these. The macaroons here really set the standard. Perfect texture & perfect flavors. I recommend the classics: Vanilla, salted caramel, coffee, pistachio
great food, nice place to be on acool evening...go with an empty stomach

Bonnie's is the little oasis of non-fussy, good ol' comfort food on an avenue that seems to be predominately Asian or Mexican restaurants. Don't get me wrong, I love my sushi and burrito- but - damn it, I'm American. I love warm greasy, deep fried everything. I am not a lawyer, but I am pretty sure there is a "right to bear a deep fryer" amendment written in the constitution. Bonnie's burgers, which come in the variety of beef, turkey, portobello mushroom, or veggie, are OK and sometimes not as juicy and hot as I want them. However, their wings hit the spot. There is also an option for a mountain of chili nachos, which is a great appetizer for a table of 3-4 people. The fries are a must get side dish, since they preemptively provide you with the undeniably delicious chipotle mayo on the table. The menu also offers other home-cooking delights that range from healthy (soups, salads, and other vegetarian options) to the not-so-healthy (hot Italian sausage). Â Plus, they have the most delicious canned beer I have tasted called Genesee Cream Ale. So good. My favorite part about Bonnie's is that everything about it is chill. The decor has a fifties diner in the middle of nowhere Nevada vibe to it. One time when I ate there, they played non-stop Kinks songs- all the greats. Â The last time I went there, I saw a guy with a newborn baby in his arms cover the baby with an unfolded napkin in order to hold his child with one arm, and eat a huge, drippy burger over the baby with his other. Â How Park Slope is that?

Bianaca was small and cute and charming. The perfect little date spot for me and my husband. When we arrived on a Friday night, there was a 40 minute wait. No big deal since you can wait next door at their wine bar and enjoy some drinks before your table is ready! Once at the restaurant we ordered what felt like a feast. First we started with the Calamari and Fried Shrimp - very good. Next we had the Lasagna - exceptional - and the gnnochi - pretty delicious. Both had decently sized portions (probably more lasagna than one person could eat for sure, but somehow I finished it off anyways). We were wayyy too stuffed for dessert, so I can't comment on that. Although they were jam packed and busy, the staff was very attentive and easy to get what we needed. I would definitely recommend this for a cozy night with your significant other or friends.

Delicious food in this tiny (very cramped) West Village restaurant. The majority of the people there were on dates, which made sense since Little Owl is a great spot for that (a reservation is necessary though). I'll follow up on a couple of the celeb sightings in this thread with Carmella Soprano (Edie Falco) who sat at the table right next to us.

Strange. Â A friend and I went in for drinks. Â We asked for a cocktail menu, based on a read of their website that advertised a great cocktail selection. Â They couldn't find one and when they finally did, the bartender didn't have any of the ingredients. Â The waiter didn't really know what was going on. Â It was such an odd experience - a trip of sorts :)

Becco is amazing! This is one of the best Italian restaurants in the city and I can't wait to go back. The cons: it's crowded, noisy and you're sitting shoulder to shoulder with other diners at many of the tables, but this is the case in most NYC restaurants.

I'm all about any place that serves good, cheap falafel and is open late. While these aren't my favorite falafel in the city they get the job done when you're looking for a late night snack. But be sure to grab a lot of napkins--these sandwiches are constructed with thin pita that may or may not break and make a falafel-y mess all over you. But that's the best kind of mess, right? Another plus: I could have sworn that the last time I went to Oasis it was cash only, but now they take cards for anything over $6. Hooray!

Excellent food with a fresh flair. Â I've enjoyed several dinners and the brunch is fabulous. The bar is well stocked and the service is excellent. Â  I'm looking forward to trying there new Price Fixed menu. Keep cooking CG.

This place was already poppin' by 1:30pm so I am grateful that my party and I arrived early enough to avoid the ridiculous line outside. This pizza was exactly what I pictured New York pizza to be, thin crust and so delicious! We had the white pizza, and then a veggie pizza with roasted red peppers which were sweet and tasty and complimented the sauce really well. I also enjoyed the fact that while dining on my delectable pizza I was able to feast my eyes on photos of various celebrities that also enjoy this fine eatery. I must say, Grimaldi's was the perfect way to wrap up my NY vacay.

Meh. Your average pricey New York restaurant -- acceptable, but not exceptional. A safe choice if you are in the neighborhood, but not worth traveling for. Points of distinction: kid-friendly; personable hostess (particularly in a city where hostesses are often outright rude).

open 24/7, but breakfast only til 5pm? whyyyy?! Anyhoo. So I settled for the much raved about mac attack, which was a pretty good substitute! I'd definitely go for either the truffle or the bacon and gouda--we actually left the plain one unfinished because there wasn't anything really special about it. Truffle lovers won't be disappointed by the strong but not overpowering truffle flavors, and gouda lovers (aka me) will get easily addicted to the yummy gouda savoriness paired with bacon. We also tried the pumpkin seed encrusted salmon served over some sort of squash. I couldn't quite taste the pumpkin seed, but the salmon was cooked well. Be prepared for a wait--or you can just eat at the bar! Will be back for dessert.

Balthazar....a great dining pleasure....I've been here a couple times. Â  I did, however, have the house Merlot which was HORRIBE (very bitter). I've had inexpensive wines which were really great in the past, but this was really bad...had to send it back and this time choose a Cabernet Sauvignon which was mediocre at best...... :( I gather unless you're a wine Â Connoisseur you'll have better luck then I......next time I'll ask either the waiter/waitress or bar tender for suggestions.

I celebrated two birthdays in a row over brunch in Calle Ocho! This is my favorite brunch place in a the city just based solely on the bread basket itself. Last year I came with my girlfriends from college and were amazed by the service and atmosphere. I've been raving this place for weeks to my grad school friends. They couldn't believe there exists such a great brunch deal in the city. 8 types of unlimited sangria? complimentary bread? 10+ types of unique brunch entrees? no time limit as long as you're eating? I'm there! 8 of us arrived for our 12 PM reservation. 2 of us actually arrived Â a little late and they were waiting for our whole party to be there before seating us. We happily waited in the hotel lobby seats right by the door. By 12:15, we were all seated at our table studying intensely at their brunch menu. All of us spent a little time reading the house rules on the side of the menu - no craziness, got it. The waiter was really prompt in coming over to take our orders. Basically our whole table ordered steak and eggs - for 2 extra dollars, u get steak! why not? 2 people did however ordered the vegetarino and salmon crepe. The waiter was quick in warning the portion size of the salmon crepe. Wanting to try something different, I offered to give some of my steak and eggs to my friend in case the salmon crepe wasn't enough food. She accepted the offer and stuck to her initial choice. 2 giant bread baskets were dropped off at our table shortly after. I really wanted to jump out of my seat and ask for third NOW. I know the bread baskets won't last for more than 2 mins and boy was I right. There were so many choices and we all wanted to try every type in the basket. There were donuts with caramel sauce, assorted muffins, chocolate chip rolls, and my fav cheese bread! We just couldn't put the cheese bread down. Drinks came shortly after. However none of the drink orders came out correctly. No matter what we ordered from the white sangrias, we all got havana banana. Both red ones we ordered ended up tasting the same? Â I believe they just gave both of us fresas. We didn't bother correcting the drink orders since it's unlimited and we could swap out flavors later. Onward with more bread! And before we knew it, our main entrees were out. The steak and eggs came out sooooo quickly to a point that I suspect they were premade. Even though my 2 friends ordered vegetarino and salmon crepe, they were ready to serve them steak and eggs too. When we stopped the server and explained to them what they ordered instead, they really pushed them to get the steak and eggs instead. My friend who ordered the vegetarino ended up agreeing to just take the ready made steak and egg. My other friend however really wanted to try the salmon crepe. So we asked the server to take back the 8th order of steak and eggs and please serve us what we actually ordered. It didn't take too long for the correct dish to come out. And we were back onto munching away. I wasn't particularly impressed by the steak and eggs - definitely has been sitting there for a bit. I did however loved my friend's salmon crepe. Smoked salmon scrambled eggs wrapped in yummy crepe - with a creamy white sauce + gravy. Wished we didn't all ordered the same thing and was able to sample a few more dishes. It took the servers a long time to fulfill our second drink order. To make things less complicated, we just all ordered the same thing. The servers were all over the place. We had to remind them 2-3 times to replenish the bread baskets and to refill our water. They accidentally gave us condiments that the table next to us has ordered. The service was nothing like I remembered a year ago. I understand that it can get a little overwhelming with the all the drink requests and number of tables... but the staff really need to talk to each other. My friends and I stayed for almost 3 hours. We just kept nursing the drinks and taking small bites. I kinda wished I didn't ask for the last order of bread basket because my friends had ordered 2 surprised desserts for me - creme brulee and chocolate cake. I didn't know .. so I was still stuffing my face with muffins 3 hrs into brunch. Creme brulee wasn't particularly sweet and the portion was HUGE. The chocolate cake came with a scoop of vanilla ice cream. Yummy but nothing to write home about. Overall, a little disappointed by Calle Ocho. Bread basket still a 5 stars in my heart. Salmon crepe gets 4 stars. But everything else prob 3 at its best. Hope the service improves at my next visit. But as long as u refill my bread basket with those cheesey goodness, I will continue to return.

Sushi is not the only thing in Japanese cuisine! A friend recommended this place last Fall. Today I finally found it! It was not very visible at the busy intersection of West 4th St and 7th Ave. Â  The interior was warm and friendly, but not loud (many Japanese BBQ/Beer places are loud -- it's a cultural requirement). The waitresses were so Japanese: low-voiced, humble, smiley, and with your best interest in mind. They would actually knock on the door of the restroom for you and let you know if the restroom was available. Â They spoke fluently English and Japanese. Anyway, the food. The food was very very very good. The best "black pork" I have ever had. I ordered the BBQ pork belly, the hot pot with pork intestines, and the grilled pork legs. They all had their own distinctive flavors and spices. The aroma of each dish made me feel like being in one of best places on earth. I did not make a reservation. But I recommend that you do if you are going on the weekend night with a group of 4 or more people. P.S. One of the waitresses are having a solo art performance (dance and singing, etc) on April 21 and 22 in the Teatro LA TEA. I found out that many of the waitresses in this restaurant are in the performing art business.

A very small place with a warm and cozy atmosphere. We ordered 2 small pizzas and a plate of calamari for 3 people, which was more than enough. Everything was very fresh. The pizza was thin and crispy and the sauce was sweet, tangy, (which I found delicious) and really stood out . The toppings were just right; they weren't too overwhelming or over the top (as in not too cheesy or the meats too salty). It's can be a nice change from the other neighborhood pizzas. The waitress was very friendly. I also saw an espresso machine but didn't have a chance to try any of the coffee yet (went at night). Though I did see two ladies next to me order some cappuccino and finished it without complaining, so maybe next time I'll give it a try.

I didn't know Japanese crepes were a thing.. just happened to go with some coworkers one morning. They were offering a cup of coffee on the house that morning. Yay! Not surprised by the good reviews! Super delicious crepes, different varieties.. I've had a sweet crepe with strawberries, bananas and cream, and the Thai chicken crepe. Ughhhh, so so good!! Service is super fast and very friendly. I wish I were in town for longer and could devour the whole menu.
Vegetarians rightfully go nuts for this place. If you are one, and you like savory, saucy dishes you have to try. Really, really yummy.
Totally worth the wait. Â Gyro sandwich with hot sauce and white sauce.

My wife and I recently found this little neighborhood gem. Â It is a wonderfully simple restaurant that executes the bistro concept very well. Â We have been back several times and enjoyed it immensely. Â A simple but well executed menu, flavorful food and a nice selection of wines accompanied by genuine service. Â What more can you ask for in a neighborhood bistro?

Came here after a friend of mine recommended the place...he told me the pastas were fantastic and that they were...we had a few apps(wagu beef tartare and shishito peppers) The pastas are great, we tried the mushroom and lamb/gnocchi pastas then shared the octopus entree....as mentioned before on Yelp, the Olive Oil desert is super tasty....our server Luke was super friendly and very attentive...I can't wait to come back!!

What is there to say that hasn't already been said about 53rd & 6th Halal? Â I'll save you the redundancy. Let me just say, that of all the Halal I've ever eaten in New York City... 53rd & 6th is the only one that has NEVER.. NEVER sent me to the bathroom a few hours later. Â And I've eaten it on more than a few occasions. Â The reason is unknown, and that's fine with me. In summary, go here. Â 6 bucks for happiness.

Was planning to have brunch at Cafe Colette but line was spewing onto Street. Walked up Berry & saw Juniper, even though we wanted brunch items & theres none there, we wanted to give the underdogs a try. We sat down and had 3 burgers. They were EXCELLENT and super delicious. Will definitely return... We think the burgers + fries are better than Dumont :o) Must try their sweet potato fries- very addictive..

Natureworks just opened and I've already been there twice. First trip in was for lunch. Needless to say, it was excellent. Natureworks is in the same location of the old 31st street Pump Energy Food, and the menu was pretty much the same as well. Prices were pretty high, but the food was great. I got the Open Sesame which had brown rice, spinach, lemon chicken, cucumbers and tomatoes covered in a tahini sauce. This was one of my favorites when Pump used to be here and I am happy to say this was as good if not better and I am still full the next day. Second trip in I got a protein shake. The shake itself was good, not great, but also priced on the high side (over $6). Good for the neighborhood since there aren't too many places to get a good shake, but not sure if its worth the price tag.

Ippudo was one of my "have to eat" stop when we visited NY last November. Came here during lunch and the line was out the door. The wait time for a party of 6 was about an 1.5 hrs. Good thing I was with other ramen lovers who was willing to wait. To our surprise we only waited 30 minutes. Score! Decor of the place was done well, it has an open feel to it and most of all clean. I also noticed while waiting at the bar that the bar table itself was made up of unbroken top ramen noodles. Cute. We ordered the Shirmp Mayo Sauce, Pork Hirata Buns, Shiromaru Hakata Classic (the best ramen soup ever), Wasabi Shoyu Ramen (it got saltier the more I ate it), and Akamaru Modern.. Everything was delicious. Ippudo has won its way into our heart and stomach. Now only if I can find something similar at home..

Pommes Frites is drunchie food. You get there, and you're stoked. You can smell the fried goodness, and you taste-test a few sauces before deciding on the perfect one. Your mouth is watering at the sight of fellow New Yorkers nibbling their delicious fries. That first bite is oh-so-heavenly and before you know it, you and your best friend are stuffing the last few mayonnaise and curry dipped pieces in your mouth while trying to keep your 5 shots from the Continental down. Then you're done. You feel like shit. "What have I just eaten?" you ask yourself. Witness the Pommes Frites remorse. This place is good, but in a deep-fried Twinkie or bacon-wrapped steak kind of way: it's just not necessary.

The food was great. Absolutely no complaints at all on that part but the host and bartender seem to have an attitude problem. Walked over to be seated and was ignored by the host because he was attending to another party, that's fine and dandy until I called out for his attention and he gives me a fake can't-you-see-I'm-busy-right-now smile. All he had to do was give me some eye contact and tell me he'd be with me in one second while the other party was discussing amongst themselves what to do. I would've been more than fine with waiting. Now the bartender. Why is it that I was ignored while waiting at the bar when he clearly knew I was there? Also, I ordered their version of a mojito and he tells me they're out of mint but 2 minutes later I see him pull out a container of mint leaves while making a drink for another customer. What is the point of this? After waiting an hour we were finally seated upstairs. It's much quieter however the atmosphere gives off the vibe of an unfinished kitchen. There is only bar type seating available in front of an open kitchen but no one worked in the kitchen so it was just dark and filled with bowls. It was a bit too warm especially while eating ramen. Our waitress however, made up for the bad attitude of the previous two so I'm happy to say that not all the employees there are snobs. Hirata buns (pork) - Everything has been said about these and more. I don't think my 2 cents is needed. Akamaru Modern (plus Nitamago for $2 extra) - Everything's been said about this bowl of ramen too but I can't seem to stop myself from raving about it. The noodles were perfectly al dente, the broth was so delicious and not heavy at all, and the egg was perfectly cooked. It was so good I got an extra helping of noodles (kae-dama for $2 extra). Left feeling satisfied and had forgotten about the aforementioned bad service. Only remembered it now that I'm writing this review. I would still return for that delicious bowl of noodles despite the minor cons.

Beautiful dining room and very nice service that is unobtrusive and polished without being stuffy. The menu has some interesting items, which skew heavily on seafood and the dishes are nicely presented and what I had was quite flavorful. Excellent wine list and good choices for wines by the glass. No real complaints here. Would go back.
Hot, delicious, yummy...

If you have the right expectations about what the Knife is (and isn't) then I think it deserves a 4. It's basically a small sandwich shop with a narrow bar along the wall and front window. The food is delicious and the menu is unique and dynamic for a simple lunch joint. However, the food is cooked to order, so if you get a grilled chicken sandwich, they will grill the chicken on the spot. Worth the wait if you aren't in a rush, but just beware it might be a few minutes to get your food even if they aren't busy. Overall, the Knife is great for grabbing a sandwich on the go or bringing something home to eat if you live in the neighborhood. If you're looking for a place to hang out and have a cup of coffee or casual lunch, this isn't the place unless it's nice out and you can snag the table on the sidewalk.

OK I admit it, I'm weak and broke my diet. Â I was famished and I needed something substantial for lunch. Â I made a deal with myself: Â A Cuban sandwich for an hour of cardio. Â Yeah, yeah...I know, one hour of cardio can't possibly burn off all the calories from a ham, pork and Swiss cheese sandwich dressed with pickles on toasted french bread. Â At least the mustard didn't add too many calories. Â To make matters worse I got a side of fried sweet bananas and washed it down with a Goya Malta. Â No regrets because it was damn good.

I always pass by this place going to work. Â I've always wanted to try it, and FINALLY got the chance. Â Maybe my expectations were too high, but I was extremely disappointed. =T MAC AND CHEESE: Okay. Â I had this on 2 occasions. Â Both wasn't the greatest. Â The first one I had wasn't even warm. And I didn't really see what the big deal was about this dish. Â Unless that is how it was suppose to be, then my response will be "are you kidding me??" GREAT HILL BLUE: Â Great concept. Not so great execution. Â I believe the fruit and the jam is suppose to BALANCE the strong flavor of the bleu cheese. The fruit and jam didn't do that at ALL. Â It was all flavor less. Â The Bleu cheese was very strong. Â Luckily, I like bleu cheese, so I didn't mind. Â But when my friends took a bite, you can see their faces. Â Note- Next time, if the fruit isn't in season, try replacing the fruit with one that is. Â Or just put a lot more jam. Â Not everyone likes blue cheese. GRILLED CHEESE WITH TOMATO SOUP: Â Out of all the dishes I've had here, I would have to say that this one is the one I liked best. Â It was a simple dish. Â I Â think I liked the tomato soup better than the sandwich. It would've been better if the soup was warmer than what was given to me. All in all, I didn't have a great time here. Â As did my friends and family. Â Its a very cute establishment. If you go, go for the environment, not for the food. Â But if you're not a hipster, be forewarned, this is a hipster filled place. Â Bring a laptop and you won't be the odd one out like I was. =X Sorry Kickshaw, maybe next time!

This place is great. Â I've been craving it every day since I went last weekend! If it was closer to me, I would be there all the time. Definitely order the guacamole. Â It comes with plantain chips that are absolutely delicious and one of my personal favorites. Â The guacamole itself is great as well, it's very flavorful and bright in taste. I'm a vegetarian with pretty simple taste so I only tried the cheese and spinach and cheese empanadas. Â The cheese was great, crunchy with just the right amount of mozzarella. I also enjoyed the spinach and cheese but I didn't taste the cheese too much. Only thing is, be prepared for a crammed environment because the store is small...but totally worth it!

I really need to get better at predicting when I'll be in need of a glorious, hangover-curing brunch (not hard, every Saturday and Sunday) so that I can leverage this whole "reservations" thing I always hear people talking about. Â Otherwise, my bleary-eyed cravings for Cluny are generally left unsatisfied, a result of the unbelievable amount of time you usually have to wait for a table. Â They take reservations, Eddie! Â IT TAKES TWO SECONDS ON OPENTABLE. Once/If you do get to a table, though, prepare for brunch salvation. Â Everything - everything - here is out of this world. Â From burgers to eggs and salads to hash, you simply cannot go wrong. Â I once had a sandwich that consisted of only bread, heirloom tomatoes and basil aioli. Â IT WAS LIKE EATING SPRING SUNSHINE. And, to top it all off, they include hunks of chocolate, cleft from some chocolaty mountain, with the bill. Â THESE GUYS.

Good good good - Rare to find a cool and cozy place on the UES that has a good mixed crowd. I did not find it to be overly hipster - t's local, cool enough and a little boisterous. The wine list is varied as it should be. I had a Prosecco and it may have been the healthiest pour I have seen in ages. We ordered a pizza as a snack and for a place that has a very limited menu - the pizza was very good. This is exactly the kind of place I would come with a few friends or a date and just chill. I have to mention the service - every one of the staff made a point of coming over to say hello and check on us throughout the night in addition to our actual server. It's an easy place to be....
mmmmm i love this place. everything is good. the guac, the pollito, the steak. the only bad thing is that its always crowded.

After a night out in the city, I went to this place to get some Wonton Mein because it was one of the few places in New York's Chinatown open after 11 PM and I have not eaten Wonton Mein for really long time (the last time I actually ate Wonton Mein was in July 2009 at Hong Kong). Wonton Mein is a soup filled with noodles and Wontons, which are these small dumplings with pork inside. The broth was nice and hot. The noodles were soft and tasty. Wontons were sufficiently good, just wished that they were a little bigger and meatier and that they gave a little more. I had five pieces in my bowl. Service was pretty sufficient. I got my bowl fairly quickly after I ordered. Seeing the waiters wearing Hawaiian shirts makes me actually want to think about about traveling to an island in the Pacific Ocean with nice weather, beautiful scenery and palm trees. The kitchen is actually inside the main area of the restaurant so you can see the cooks prepare your food. Of course, the Wonton Mein is definitely not as good compared to Mak's Noodle at Wellington Street in Chong Wan (Central), Hong Kong, but I enjoyed my Wonton Mein and did not have to pay much for it. If I lived in New York City, this could be one of my options to get some decent noodle soups during a really cold day.
This place is awesome... Been here many times and always consistent on taste. The only thing is it's cash only and in today's society not many people carry cash around anymore.
Really cool atmosphere however the sangrias cld be much much better, especially when it $40 a pitcher. Can you say WTF? Otherwise try the bacon wrapped dates and wild mushroom ain't bad.
Great spicy noodles, friendly staff, fast kitchen, cheap prices. Minus one star for tiny seating area.

Tried this place out for brunch. Â They have a cute atmosphere that kind of fits the name of the restaurant. Â It's not a stuffy place at all. Started off with a cup of stumptown coffee. Â My first time having it. Â Not bad. Â For our brunch 'entree' I had the fried zucchini sandwich that had hot sauce and cole slaw on a potato bun. Â I've never had a fried zucchini sandwich, nor have I seen one on any menu! Â Pretty tasty and a nice twist on a veggie sandwich, and the potato bun is a plus. My friend had the chicken and eggos - the chicken was battered and flavored with what tasted like black pepper and tabasco - very tasty - and they drizzled maple syrup over it and had maple butter on top. Â Def not for anyone on a diet! Â I had a bite, it was pretty good, but not sure I'd order it myself. Last but not least - cinnamon sugar cake donut - homemade. Â It was good for a cake donut, but I prefer the light and fluffy version. I peeked at other people getting disco tots and the portion size is huge! Â It's a big soup bowl full of them topped with cheese....too many to eat alone! I'd def go back to try their other unique creations - their menu is constantly changing, which makes it that much more fun to try new things! Heads up - they don't accept credit cards! Â and it's a BYOB

Gramercy Tavern is definitely my go-to restaurant whenever someone asks me to recommend a top-rated NYC restaurant. What I love most is that the restaurant has a conservative and homey ambiance- not like other top restaurants that have a snooty, "i'm dining like a princess" air to it. The food is top-notch, as can be expected from any highly rated NYC restaurant. Flavours are unique, but not over-done. From my experience, every dish from the mouche-bouche to the complimentary baked goods at the end made me feel warm and delightful. If anything at all, I think they could improve on the bread basket- I love it when restaurants serve "melt-in-your mouth" bread. The bread at Gramercy Tavern is quite ordinary. But other than that, everything else is wonderful. I hardly ever award 5 stars to a restaurant, but this is well-deserved.
Nice Restaurant! Great food!

Excellent Italian food that is reasonably priced. Potato gnocchi was delicious. The service was absolutely great--the food came out in under 10 minutes. My sister and I were looking for somewhere to eat outside and this was a perfect place. I would definitely come back and try eating inside!

I think that the two most important assets to any food business are both a tasty menu and great service. El Diablito has both. Whether ordering delivery from Seamless or dining in, I'm always satisfied by the balanced flavors and friendly staff. I highly recommend the fish taco. It always features a meaty white fish with a crispy, light batter and a creamy sauce. Their chicken quesadillas are always a favorite, too, topped with either one of their homemade side sauces. They regularly feature coupons on Paypal, too! This is definitely an East Village favorite.

The best juicy bun place in town!!! They have quite a few authentic Shanghai style dishes you can order. That said, you have to know what to order! Juicy buns, Wuxi spare ribs, shanghai style fish, pan fried Chinese pancake etc. I can't give 5 stars because the environment is only so so. And it is always crazy packed at busy hour. You have to be prepared for a long line unless you go there at 11:30am or 3pm in the weekdays.

So far I've been here 3 times with in the past two weeks. My boyfriend and I love it here. It's rare to fine a hot spot that feeds the health conscience deliciously amazing food!! My boyfriend won't pass up the steak sandwich and I LOOVVEEEE the sweet potato with herbs. Everything we've tasted has been soooooo good. And the service is on point. We love siggies and we have a new go to place!!

Met a friend here for drinks/bar food last night and had a great time! The bartender was great at recommending drinks and the staff was very friendly and accommodating. I really enjoyed their burger. I'll definitely be back if I'm in the area!

Awesome spot for lunch! Stopped in with some friends- we were intrigued by the idea of Italian tapas. The panini were too enticing so we went that route instead. A friend and I split the Avocado panino- roast mushrooms, tomato, cracked pepper aioli and mozzarella. The panino was pretty big and the bread was perfectly crispy. We each had a beet salad which was also quite ample and included goat cheese and arugula- very yummy. I had the Alagash beer- a nice surprise to top off a great meal.

For the fries alone The Farm on Adderley gets a solid four stars. Those perfectly crisp morsels that are slightly soft on the inside are also perfectly sized, and come with a side of mayo (yes mayo) if you so desire. Mind you, all fries aside, the food was pretty damn good. A socially conscious and community driven restaurant, the focus at The Farm on Adderley is on local farmers and entrepreneurs and creating food made with local, (often) organic and seasonal ingredients. If you have food allergies, I found the staff were helpful in terms of leading me around the menu to dishes that would either be free of allergens or that could be adapted. I went with a helping of fries and a grass-fed piece of beef, while my friend attacked the homemade focaccia bread with zeal and settled on a rack of lamb as her main. The verdict? The helpings were generous and the food: great. My steak was a perfect shade of medium rare, the beef was wonderfully juicy and it tasted as if it had lived a good life. I already told you about the fries, so there's no point banging on about those. I also gave the focaccia bread a go and I have to say, it's some of the best focaccia I've had...in a long, long time. For more: fortheintolerants.com/?pâ€¦.

The ramen here is quite well-crafted. They also offer a choice between a pork based broth or a chicken based broth, which is uncommon but a welcome option. I had the shoyu ramen with the pork base, and the soup is silky and flavorful without being overpowering. The noodles are decent but nothing to write home about. What really shined in this dish was the charsiu pork slices in the soup. I don't think I've ever had a more delicious slice in any ramen before. The balance of fat and meat is excellent and the flavor hits all the right spots of sweet and salty and is a good marriage with the soup. My only gripe is that the ramen as a whole is a little too basic. They didn't add too many toppings to the soup which is nice but there wasn't a lot of each topping. You can certainly add more toppings but I wish I didn't have to spend that few extra bucks for it as the prices are slightly above average. The all-Japanese staff was very kind and the service was good. The interior is cute, a lot of light wood finish and the window in the front give it sort of a muted brightness that helps you feel like you really found a great place that people don't know about. That satisfaction is delicious, admit it. Heading back there for lunch to try the shio black ramen today, you should too.

I can only repeat some of the previous reviews about the over hyperbolized food at Momofuku Ssam Bar. Â David Chang's restaurant had been talked up so much that I started believing the hyper before my first bite. Â He was Santa Claus, the Tooth Fairy, and Easter Bunny, rolled into one. Â I wanted to believe. Â Now having been, I'm upset, hungry and left without hope. I am Korean and I understand Korean food. Â For many, it's smelly, garlicky, spicy and typically BBQ meats. Â I can appreciate the interpretation and influences that David Chang envisioned when creating his menu. Â For me, that vision was lost in poor execution and translation. The first dish was the cured Hamachi. Â That was really, really good. Â Very supple and smooth on the palette. Â The horseradish emulsion was mild and a nice compliment to the buttery flavor of the fish. Â The dried seaweed and puffed rice was a nice touch. Â The second dish was a coddled egg on frisee. Â I forget the exact details, but that's how forgettable it was. Â The legendary pork bun was the biggest let down. Â I thought I was going to see Jesus upon my first bite. Â Instead, I found that the Berkshire pork's flavor was lost in the fatty fat. Â Crisped fat would have been great. Â I understand the concept, but I've had Peking Duck and Crispy Roasted Pig that was a whole lot better and much cheaper. Â The pork sausage and rice cake was the last dish. Â This abomination was too salty to finish. Â I could dig the spicy, it was hot. Â I totally dig the cubing and searing of the rice cakes (very clever), but it was too damn salty. Â I guess I could have sent that dish back. Go to try it. Â Brag to your friends to say you've been. Â But leave your lofty expectations at the door. Â P.s. I hear that Momofuku will be expanding to Chicago and LA.

It's hit-and-miss with this place. First time we went, I had some great gnocchi and spaghetti. Â The store is small and cozy and has good atmosphere. Next, we ordered salmon for delivery. Â It was okay, but had way too much cheese sauce on it, which drowned out the actual flavor of the salmon. Today, I had a vegetarian lasagna? Â I actually don't know what was in it, but it certainly surprised me. Â I think it was pureed squash, but definitely not what I was expecting, and not that great. Â It had some hard bits of vegetable in it that had a bone-like texture... Can recommend the spaghetti and the gnocchi though. Â Also, the bread is good.

Loooooove this place!!! It's fun to take someone visiting NY because they always love checking off the boxes for their order. I've never had bad experience here, food is amazing, service is amazing, drinks are amazing!!!!!

The fried fish was the highlight of my lunch here. You think you're ordering some grossly overpriced tofu stew, but alas there is some method to the madness. You're given a piece of fried fish. It is delicious. It also has a lot of bones, so if you suck at eating fish, womp womp. There's a lot of side dishes that range from "bleh" to "meh" - none really stand out except the fish. You get your tofu stew and rice in stone pots. Do not touch the stone pots, do not open the stone pot. The waitress will do everything for you so don't mess it up. Their seafood pancake is really good and I generally do not compliment anyone on their seafood pancakes. It's a bit oily though--you've been warned. I had the dwaenjang tofu stew, which was alright. The food portions are pretty big and so I took most of it home. I can't really say the tofu stew was that great, which is unfortunate since that is their specialty. Come here to eat the fried fish and seafood pancake I guess? Really spacious restaurant; no wait during lunchtime on a Sunday. And yes, like every other annoying restaurant the receipt gives you percentages on how much to tip.

I went to Paprika for my birthday dinner back in November and have been meaning to review this place ever since. My party of 9 had to wait awhile for a table, about 45 minutes, even though I had made a reservation. Luckily we are extremely forgiving people and for that we were each rewarded with a glass of complimentary champagne. A very nice gesture, I thought, and a great way to kick off my 30th birthday dinner. Â  Had I written this review months ago I would be able to recall exactly what dishes were ordered, but their names escape me. What I do remember are the pillowy clouds of gnocchi I ate. Â They were covered in a rich lamb ragu and literally melted in my mouth. It was a dish made in pasta heaven. My great grandma is full blooded Italian, so I've had my share of amazing gnocchi, but Paprika has hers beat. Sorry Gram. I still love you! Everything else that was ordered was excellent, as well. I know this because we all passed our plates around to see who's was the best. Â I think we were all in agreement that our own dish was the winner. After the meal I began to realize why we had waited so long for a table. Â Once you've finished a truly epic Italian pasta and you've consumed a truly epic amount of Italian wine you simply don't want the fuzzy, buzzy feeling you have inside to end. Â  All things must, however, so I'll sum this review up by saying that the only reason I did not give Paprika 5 stars is that you might have to wait awhile for a table even if you have a reservation. 4 stars for great food, warm atmosphere and good service.

Very small, so be prepared to use your 12-inch voices and not discuss anything that's supposed to be kept under wraps. Â The couscous is A-MAZING - just make sure you get the works (sausage, etc.). Â The servers are friendly and unpretentious, making you feel comfortable, even though you're practically sitting on the person next to you.

Such a fun place and very good pizza. We had the anchovy one and one with ham and mushrooms and both were very good (thin dough and fluffy crust). The cheesecake is very nice and my dad, who is very picky when it comes to coffee, enjoyed their macchiato. The place itself is very nice and worm and kid friendly.
Got the shrimp po boy. All breading and no shrimp. Wack!!! Â Very disappointing considering what brought me here was the Yelp reviews...

Really, I haven't had anything I don't like from this rustic restaurant that serves traditional Greek cuisine. Â Their complimentary pita is warm and fluffy, served with a truly delicious bean and olive oil dip. Â You can get even fancier by ordering their poikilia, a trio of fancy dipping sauces--a fish roe dip for those that like things salty, a yogurt dip for those that like something tangy, and a grilled eggplant and olive oil dip for those that like a little bit of texture. Â Some other appetizers that I consider scene-stealers would be their classic grilled octopus which has the perfect bounce and char, plus their three Greek cheeses melted together in a hot clay pot--REALLY cheesy and smelly (in the good cheese way). Their entrees are a very decent size, especially for the price. Â The braised pork shank was pretty good, but the lamb shank was even better and more tender. Â I have also tasted the lamb chops and short rib--both great. Â My favorite, however, was the whole branzino--so fresh and less heavy. Â It comes with a simple olive oil and lemon juice dipping sauce that I love--don't know why I don't do this myself at home more often. Â I also really enjoyed the shrimp and sea scallops in a creamy tomato sauce. Â Again, pretty big portion size for this! Â The menu has this over egg noodles but both times I've ordered this, they easily let me substitute the noodles with spinach-rice pilaf. Â Service is great.

It's easy to bypass this place. The name outside has faded, but just keep an eye out for the bicycle above the door. Because the place is so small and cozy, it can be too crowded, but tables free up while you wait at the bar. Â The whole place is charming... right down to the bathroom! Five stars for the live music, ambiance, and great service!
Delicious pizza! Crust is perfect and the sauce is sweet. I got a large pizza, half with plain cheese and the other half with sausage, pepper, extra sauce and mushrooms. It was amazing!

I lived in this neighborhood and have seen this place hyped beyond relief and do not understand why. The older Italian gentleman is nice but he can barely keep up with the demand. People line-up for this pizza but I wonder if they're just Zagat zombies. I think of a great pizza as the New York style Famous Ray's pizza. Perfect amount cheese and sauce on a thin yet crispy crust. Many pizzerias can acheive this in Brooklyn and NY in general. DiFara's turns out hot but lumpy and un-crispy slices. The cheese felt like it was runny and the sauce was too strong. That maybe his interpretation of a "rustic" style pizza but it's not great pizza to me. I've eaten there a bunch of times, trying to believe the hype but my impression is that they are over-rated.

It was a quiet, emplty little place, probably deserves a 3.5 for its ambience, and I really want to give a 4 for the food too, but sorry I wasn't that impressed at all. Â  Despite being warned by one my venezuelan friends that this place is not as good as my other venezuelan favorite in the city, I decided to give it a try for my own judgement. It was the perfect spot for late night quick causual bite after the movies. And the sangria was pretty good too, but I feel that their guacamole can do a lot better. Also, I love fish and I love arrepas, but i did not like their fish arrepas. If I go back again, it will be to try things that i haven't tried in their menu and to give it another chance.

Blue Ribbon is one of my favorite restaurants of all time. I remember when I first moved to NYC understanding why people get addicted to the lifestyle here when on a Tuesday I was sipping a gimlet and eating oysters at 2am at Blue Ribbon, I recall thinking " this is New York". anyways- Â  Â The service is a huge reason why I adore coming here, the staff mantains a perfect balance between serious and goofy. The attention to detail is amazing here and everyone is very knowlegable but there isn't an ounce of " stuffiness" or attitude. Â  Â  I also like the fact that I've gone in and spent tons of money, ordering cocktails, bottles of wine, oysters, entrees and dessert- and yet recently I went in and grabbed Â just a beer and burger whose fries were notably tasty, for maybe $25 bucks. Â  Â Whether you are celebrating something or just want a casual late night bite, Blue Ribbon is the spot.

Being a Bonita fan, I wanted this place to do well. Â And it has. Â  I don't love the decor or the atmosphere as much as Bonita, but I like the pork tacos a lot. Â Even juicer than what I remembered at Bonita. Â The tacquitos are fantastic, drizzled with homemade crema and salty mexican white cheese. Â  Excellent tamarind margaritas, nice fresh salsa and really great, smokey porky black beans as a side. Â We also had delivery recently, which was also great. Â Shrimp tacos and a salad were Eh. I still miss the fish tacos from Bonita, but this is very good, authentic Mexican. Â I'd rate it higher than Yola's but maybe a notch below La Superior Â Maybe.

Damn, this place is good. Â I don't know where else you get a shot of bacon broth to start-off your meal. My girlfriend brought me here for my birthday dinner and I was really impressed by the quality and creativity of the food. Â I would compare this to some of the higher echelon restaurants in Montreal. Â Don't expect a light meal. Â Good, heavy food. Â Everything we had was great, maybe with the exception of the strawberry and cinnamon ribs. Â It was good, but maybe a little overdone or the sauce just didn't hit the mark. Â Regardless, I would absolutely go here again and certainly recommend it to people who appreciate good food.

This place is cute and I'm a little bit of a snob when it comes to surroundings other than food. At first I was skeptical but my husband & I went here and the food was amazing. We wanted to grab a panini for our trip back to DC but they are closed on Sundays. Other than that, this will be a first stop when we return to the east vil.

I love ramen. I have a favorite place I go to back in Los Angeles that is my barometer to every other ramen restaurant I come across. No more. Ippudo sets the standard. You walk in, and the decor is modern beautifully mixed with old world Japanese elements. Monday through Thursday they have 2 for 1 sapporo's, which is great. ANYWAY - so you walk in, and all the sudden the hostess says something in Japanese, and everyone greets you, including the kitchen, it's awesome. Service - the moment you take a sip out of your water, someone is there to refill it. I've never waited longer than 5 seconds for a server to come and get the bill from me. Food - ACAMURAMODERN and the PORKBUNS. You have to do it. Get fresh garlic and ask for the noodles to be cooked hard. From the moment that broth hits your mouth I swear you'll be in heaven. You might even shed a single tear when you finish your bowl of soup. The pork buns...I can't describe. Just do it. Trust me. This place is great. Like many other places in New York, you need to get there early. They do not take reservations. The restaurant opens up at 5pm and honestly at 5:30, it's usually packed by then with more than an hour wait, so really try to get there early. It's worth it. Ok seriously stop reading this review and go now wtf.

I came here for dinner with my friend because somehow, he had stumbled upon this little gem and his stomach had told him that we should check it out. Looking at the pictures and the website, my stomach began to get curious too. What was this mysterious place with delicious sandwiches? After a little bit of walking, my friend and I found this restaurant. It's definitely a hole in the wall place in the middle of the block off of a more populated street, so my sense is if you're not looking for it, you can easily walk past it. Since it was a small place, my friend and I were left a awkwardly standing by the door for a few minutes. Luckily, there was Â menu attached to the entrance so we got to take a gander at what was available that night. When we were seated (in a weird corner of the room), the waiter explained that everything served at black tree was organic and locally sourced, including their drinks, meaning that their menu changed fairly often. How exciting. While everything was local and organic, nothing really stood out to me as a "try me!!!" dish. I ended up getting the bahn mi and my friend ended up deciding on the short rib. Our sandwiches came out on some wooden boards, which I felt was kind of unhygienic - wooden boards can keep bacteria for large periods of time, and I don't think using them to serve food is very good for anyone's health. To be honest, I was disappointed with the size of my sandwich. It was really small for what it cost. I mean, it tasted good and I liked it, but that doesn't mean that it's worth it. My bahn mi contained duck and a bunch of other stuff that really blended the flavors together well. My sandwich also contained this pickle (or pickle like vegetable) that was EXTREMELY sour (tart?? I'm not sure "sour" is the exact word but it had me grimacing for a few minutes after one bite) and I'm not sure what that was about. My friend's sandwich contained a radish that was equally as unsavory and he didn't really appreciate it. While I liked my sandwich, I am reluctant to give black tree higher than three stars for a myriad of reasons. First of all, the waiter that served my friend and I, while he was civil, it was evident that he had no interest in serving two Asian young adults. He sprung to life around tables with white patrons, striking up a lively conversation with a group of white folks that came in after us while basically blowing us off. My friend and I aren't here for your hipster racism, bro. Secondly, the price of the food is not worth it, especially because the portions will leave you hungry afterwards. If you're looking for all organic, locally sourced sandwiches, this is your place, but don't expect to be full afterwards. Lastly, the ambiance is hipster - I've never felt so angry eating at a restaurant before. I hate when I'm eating at a restaurant and I'm surrounded by ignorant white folks who ooze privilege but act oppressed. Nobody appreciates your faux ally ship. I don't need to be around folks who think that it's "edgy" to say they live in Harlem when they really live on w102 and broadway. I probably will not come back on my own accord.

Olea is, simply put, amazing. I typically come during happy hour. Quite honestly, you can't beat their deal--half-priced tapas, wines, pints, and sangria. Oysters, bacon-wrapped dates, fried olives, and lamb meatballs galore! They've an Ommegang on tap as well as a great selection of wines. The bartender, Thomas, is friendly, attentive, and knowledgeable. If there is a drawback, it's that happy hour only lasts a measly two hours. Wompity womp womp. Dinner is also great. I recommend the pork chop--juicy and flavorful, and served with mashed potatoes and an interesting cabbage medley. It's my favorite entree on the menu. The entire staff is great. They not only provide excellent service, but they're all also super friendly. And really, there's not much more to say. Olea is a neighborhood gem. Drinking and dining here is always a pleasure. I love this spot!
Yum yum yum! Â  great food .. friendly staff .. Yum yum yum! mahusay na pagkain ... friendly na mga tauhan ...

Great pizza! Although my slice missed the basil. So I would order extra basil. EVEN BETTER PASTA! Pappardelle Speck e Porcini, sooo yummy. Home-made pasta with mushroom and truffle oil. I thought this pasta was better than Babbo. THANKS for the friendly service and Italian music video's playing in the background!

We tried this place bc my sister made a reservation. I was hesistant to do brunch in this neighborhood bc it's almost always a scene and not worth it. Sure enough, it lived up to the expectations. The hostess acted like she was doing us a favor, having waited 30 minutes for a table we had a reservation for, and of course we couldnt be seated until our entire party was there (which is always annoying) but clearly was a way for the restaurant to stall bc our table wasn't even ready. Bartender was not a bartender...barely 10 ppl at the bar and he didnt even look up to give us a menu- not too mention super slow considering half the drinks being ordered were pre-made mimosas etc... Food was very good but didnt make up for the service so I won't be returning. If youre looking for good brunch with a nice experience, you should probably look elsewhere. I might sound harsh but ive been to a lot of great restaurants and bad service is just no excuse-this is the service industry after all. Places like this put greed over the value of a return customer.

Service and atmosphere are amazing. The food is prepared by world class chefs but I was never impressed taste-wise with any of the dishes. I've been to Gramercy at least 3 times and yeah, I rate it A-OK.
Good grandma Slice. Owner was very Nice. when in the area defiantly will grab another slice

This is a fabulous place to book an event. Very reasonable and you get your own private bar and the whole downstairs floor. The beer selection is great and the various Â food is perfect for any guest. I booked a corporate event and everyone loved it. Plus I stayed under budget! This is also a good happy hour place to go after work. I haven't had dinner here but the apps are great. Plus on the weekend it is quieter since it is in the financial district so it is a nice bar where you can talk and actually hear people. One of my fav spots!

Maybe it was an off day, but I didn't think my brunch experience was anything special. Â I ordered the pumpkin pancakes and thought the cinnamon yogurt was a bit too sweet for breakfast, however liked the fresh squeezed oj. Â My friend ordered the breakfast sandwich with home fries which was tasty. Â Sadly though, I was disappointed when the waitress informed us that there were no free coffee refills. Â Who doesn't provide free refills on coffee for breakfast? Â Maybe I'll try coming back for lunch or dinner, but wasn't blown away by brunch here.

I am about to become a serious regular at this place. It's hard to find a restaurant in New York -- particularly in the West Village -- that has food of this quality with entrees priced under $20. It's even harder to find one that has a warm and wonderful atmosphere and a very friendly staff. I particularly recommend the guacamole, the ceviche, the lomo saltado (perfect short ribs+french fries soaked in short rib juice+delicious sauteed tomatoes and onions) and especially the torrejas de oliva for dessert. The torrejas is a olive oil-soaked cake with a bruleed topping and amazing blackberry sauce -- you can definitely tell that there is a serious pastry chef (Pichet Ong) involved here. I cannot wait for Coppelia to get its liquor license, since everything on the menu will go very well with a nice cold beer.

Grimaldi's Pizza is a fantastic pie with fresh motz and pepperoni. Â I crave this pizza every time i'm in NYC. Â This pizza place usually has a line outside depending on when you get there (I waited 30 minutes to get a table) but it was worth it. Â  BEWARE **DOES NOT ACCEPT CREDIT CARDS** ATM is in the building but there is a service fee

Use caution eating these precious dumplings when they hit the table. If you pop on in your mouth you will have a blister as big as the dumpling from the scalding, but delicious pork, crab and soupy filling. The whole roof of your mouth will peel like a sunburn; and if you try to swallow it to get it out of your mouth, you will feel it slowly burn as it goes down your esophagus. Mental note...Bite a small hole and suck out the soup, then bite half of the dumpling to avoid oral injury. The other food is pretty good but the shao lum bao are definitely the stars of this place. Oh yeah be prepared to share a big table with strangers that will stare the 5 stacks of dumplings you ordered for the two of you.

Grabbed lunch from here one workday. Â I got the spicy falafel sandwich with the date smoothie. Â Smoothie was good, but I didn't get any lime from it and I could probably make one just as good. Â It was also expensive, so skip the smoothie next time. Â Falafel was good, not great. Â It has good flavors but they don't layer the different elements properly so they don't mix in the pita which is a shame. Â This falafel is nowhere near as good as L'As du Falafel in Paris. Â If you're looking for a quick bite in Soho stop in, but I don't think it's worth a special trip.
2 Words. SOUP DUMPLINGS. I have never had anything of this sort and now I'm on the hunt to find a place that makes these magical balls of flavor if it even exist!! Must have in NYC!!
Those were the best pancakes I've ever had in my life.

The pizza is delicious-- especially the square slices. Â They have a nice outdoor seating area for both small and large groups to grab some pizza and then sit and enjoy. They also have a restaurant where you can order pizza but they have really good Italian dishes as well. Â The service is usually kind of slow if they are crowded though. Â I got the penne with broccoli, garlic, and oil and they put way, way too much oil in it. Â The next time I went, I ordered the same thing but asked for them to go light on the oil.... nope, still the pasta was drowning in oil. Â They have great zucchini sticks and huge salads too. The spumoni is yummy too, of course! Beware, the parking lot is usually packed!! I've also ordered for delivery from them once and I won't do that again. Â It took about 2 hours for them to deliver a pizza!!
This is a vet busy place, reservations is a MUST. Service: Very good, our waitress was very friendly & informative. Food: AMAZING, huge portions, great tasting food. This place is a must visit.

Kind of expensive for a hole in the wall place, but it is Manhattan after all (and prettttty big portion sizes!). Â I ordered BBQ chicken soft tacos with pico de gallo and they were REALLY good. Â The quality of meat was far better than a lot of places I've tried. Â  The salsa verde was fresh, and really good. Â The chips with salsa were great. Â Overall, a great place if you're craving Mexican food in the area. Â  If I lived closer, I'd go far more often!

I went with a group of five. We had a wonderful dinner! The service was excellent, the entrees offered a great variety and everyone at our table said their meal was delicious. There is a small outdoor area in front of the restaurant but we ate in the back room which has a nice old world decor. Â I would highly recommend Uva and I look forward to going back again.

Gladys, you are great. Drinks: Sit at the bar if you want to learn about classic Caribbean cocktails done right or delve deep into some fine rum. I'm not a rum drinker, more of a bourbon man, but when I told the bartender that, she quickly convinced me to try one of their rum flights. Turns out there's rum that's not syrupy n' sweet but more spicy like rye or smokey like scotch. Awesome experience. Then I tried a Golden Daiquiri since all I knew from daiquiris was strawberry. Turns out, this is closer to a citrusy old fashioned then a sickly sweet frozen drink. Love it. Food: Jerk chicken was moist, spicy, generously portioned and just plain delicious. Peppered shrimp were served head-on which is always fun and just thinking of the slow burn of the sauce is making my mouth water. Yams were a little too starchy and dense for my liking but I think they were true to traditional preparation. Bok choy was a great side too! Service: Bartender was amazing Ambiance: Fun vibes, good music, decor is pretty great. Airy space that would be fun with a group of 6 or so. Great find in our general neighborhood! Look forward to returning.

Came to watch the Argentina / Germany World Cup game (Latin food and drink is definitely better than German! Â Which is a positive given the outcome of that game..) and could not have been happier about the food and drink. The restaurant was packed (due to the game) and as a result, service was pretty spotty.
