Â It took a while for our server to take our order and they were not great about checking back for refills on drinks. Â They even put food and drinks on our bill that we did NOT order. Â They were happy to sort it out, but just a minor annoyance. Â The food and drinks though, were phenomenal. Â Everything was fresh and flavorful and portions were generous. Â The grilled pineapple chipotle margarita?? Â SOOO GOOD! Â The Coconut Kiss was better than any dessert and my goal is to replicate that at home this summer... Service hiccup aside - I would not hesitate to return here when I come back to Brooklyn.
I've been here a few times, and the quality is consistent! It's great Mexican food to go. I loved the burritos and quesadillas. I haven't tried the tacos.

Really awesome Caribbean food. To get to The Islands, I have to walk a half-mile, past Glenda's, Gloria's, Silver Krust AND a Golden Krust, but when I'm willing to spend a little more to get the best, freshest and most delicious Shrimp Curry, The Islands is the only pace to go. They serve traditional Caribbean specialties, a smidge fancier and significantly more delicious than the places closer to me. Fancier how? For example, a large Jerk Chicken dinner includes a piece of breast, and no place up by me makes white meat chicken. Bur I like white meat chicken, so I'm happy. Curry Shrimp is made to order and includes large, pink, impeccably fresh shrimp . Jerk Chicken is crispy and spicy on the outside and moist and tender inside. While I was waiting, Shepard's Pie emerged from an oven, steaming and golden. I'll have to try that next time. Sides are better than average: the rice and peas has an extra dash of something that makes it yummier than the standard, and the Veg side contains cabbage cooked to the point of exhaustion and a light hand with the frozen peas and carrots. The teeny tiny upstairs is reminiscent of an Amsterdam coffee shop, without the billows of smoke.

Great Mexican spot, with that authentic vibe. Great guacamole, amazing molÃ© sauce and real good brisket tacos. Small but good margaritas... Can't wait to go back in the nice weather to sit in the outdoor patio area and try more dishes.

The beer selection was great. It would have been nice to see at least a token vegan or vegetarian dish on the menu, which would seem to make sense considering the neighborhood and the fact that it is 2014, but I guess they are aiming for something else. So be it. My core issue was with the service. We were there on Sunday night; it was not exactly dead but definitely not heaving. After seating ourselves at the bar it took over 10 minutes to get served and getting a refill took even longer. I witnessed other bar seated customers dealing with similar issues. I understand that they may be working out the kinks, fine, just give customers a heads up, I think folks would generally be sympathetic. Most people aren't looking to be waited on hand and foot, just descent service. The vibe I got from the staff was more like they were doing me a favor. My experience makes it very tough to justify returning or recommending it

Is there anything left to be said about this place? I've been wanting to try it and went for it today. Once you realize that its a local noodle joint you stop asking Â questions and start eating. And what a delight. Had the Pork Noodle soup which was pork belly with herbs and spices with hand drawn noodles. I really felt I had died and gone to heaven. Â I could not Â finish it. The best $ 5.50 I've ever spent in my life.

Oh Grimaldi's... for a chain nationwide, you tend to never disappoint me. Surprisingly. Pizza is always crisp, just the right amount of cheese to sauce, and your salads are always my favorite. Not to mention the antipasto board. Super good. Well done, well done.

Ok, first this is a 3 star review, this means some things went well. And actually quite important things: the chef is doing a really good job at cooking. Foodwise, all things were globally very good, subtle, delicate. We had the prix fix. We had burata, raw scallops, tuna, sea bass and a rice desert. The wine was also really interesting. Kudos for that. Now the things why only 3 stars: 1st of, there is something about italian food that is very important when you want to do it right: it has to be fulfilling your stomach. I can say that as a good half of my family was raised there. And I don't mean it has to be to the extreme of loving grand mothers who are literally killing you with food OD. But it is clear that italian food, to be right, needs to at the very least give you this feeling that you don't need anything else in your stomach... and truth to be said, we went for a last byte somewhere else after Fitzcaraldo. Please add more side pasta or rizotto, or just go a bit crazy with Focacia, or may be bring some Cantuci... 2nd thing is, and this is very personal, about the soundtrack. In case you are allergic to post 70s reggae inspired music, you might want to be careful. We had 2 hours of a soundtrack that was really not our taste... and it did not help to make us happy (though it did make us laugh at some points... and god knows that we love many things, but focusing on this 90s reggae was not to please us...). If you don't want to piss some customers, either introduce more diversity or chose for things which are more likely to please a broad spectrum of customers. 3rd thing and this is not at all to blame any one during the service. The outdoor which is actually looking and feeling great at first is also apparently the basecamp of a very tenacious mosquito tribe. My unkles and caff muscles will remember this for a few weeks... no idea if it is because of the proximity of the Newton creek water but this was tough. Honestly not helping to be totally happy about the experience. I surely will go back, may be in the inside, and not taking the prix fixe...

The space is super small but the quality of food was really what surprised me. Their menu comprises of tonkotsu and chicken broth based ramen. I ordered a Shio spicy ramen ($13) and loved everything from the flavorful broth, to the braised pork, to the perfectly chewy noodles. For an additional $4, you can also add a curry rice for a set. The spicy bamboo appetizer was also a wonderful complement to the ramen. Although the food was delicious, they did charge for hot tea which I thought was kind of weird. Also, since the space is small, you'd probably only be able to stay for 30 min during peak hours. Will come back if I'm in the area and craving some ramen!

Came here for what turned out to be an extremely delicious Saturday brunch. The space is bright and airy with plenty of outdoor seating. My bartender was very sweet and helpful, and while I was waiting for my friend who was running late he gave me an article on the Wu Tang Clan to read so I wouldn't get too restless. Get the blood orange mimosas, so good. I ordered the Spicy Omelet, made with andouille, mushrooms, and pico de gallo (I got it without the pepper jack cheese). This was made really well, and the pico de gallo adds a nice touch. The home fries that came with it were also great. And their bacon. And their pancakes :) No wrong choices here. They were also playing great music. REM, Pink Floyd, Journey, Sublime, and Guns n Roses. My only gripe is that they don't seem to include any drinks with brunch. C'mon, gimme ONE free drink with my meal ;)

I actually didn't think Amy Ruth's would be as good as everyone said it was. Â I think when you've grown up with home cooked soul food your entire life...your expectations are high and nobody can cook as good as your Mama or Grandmama, right!?? /:-) Well tell mama 'n em they still make the best greens, chicken, yams, mac 'n cheese, etc....but I bet Grandma Ruth's food is going to give them a run for their money. Â  I've lived in NYC for a month, and have been to Amy Ruth's twice-yup, it's that good. Â I've ordered the Al Sharpton (fried chicken and waffles) both times and I have split a few sides with friends. Â The mac & cheese is sinfully good. Â It actually may be the best mac & cheese I've had in life...and while that's a good thing, it's also sad because now I have to really step my mac & cheese game up to keep my "homemade mac 'n cheese" throne. Â  Amy Ruths you ARE soul food. Â I'm now off to dream about your chicken and waffles and mac 'n cheese. Â Maybe I'll see you this weekend for the 3rd weekend in a row--#skinnyfat! Oh! Â And I love that they keep the Franks and the syrup on the table. Â A girl can never get enough of those, and I'm glad they're at my disposal

If you aren't vegetarian, Joya has excellent Thai food, served quickly, for a reasonable price. If you are, well... Joya's menu is incredibly misleading. The "vegetable" section is NOT vegetarian. Everything on the menu contains fish sauce- something I only discovered after eating there for years. I sat down to eat with an out of town friend, tried to order my usual Tofu Vegetable Red Curry (which, I'll mention, is excellent if you're ok with eating fish) when the waiter informed me that it was not vegetarian. I was disappointed, but flexible. I asked the waiter what was vegetarian on the menu- any other curry? Pad Thai? Salad?...Anything? To my embarrassment, we ended up walking out. Please Joya, could you modify your menu and develop one or two vegetarian entrees? My heart pines for that red curry. Just not enough to make me eat anchovies.

i got a half salad and brisket sandwich and it was scrumptious! I got choc and vanilla ice cream and it was better than average. Â My friends had the cheesecake but I didn't ask how it was. Â  it was great meeting with a group of people here because the menu is so expansive and has a range of naughty and nice options. Â :) I'd go back...

i'm not going to be able to add much that previous reviewers haven't already said... but man, this place is DEE-licious. bacon everywhere. good thinking. it's a little on the pricey side, but as my bf points out, it's actually worth the price, unlike standard brunch fare that isn't anything special. Â at least this is different, more unusual food, and it's also quite filling. on our most recent visit i had the biscuits benedict with bacon gravy, and i couldn't come even close to finishing it. (on my first visit i had the gravlax, which was also delicious but less heavy, and i had to resist the urge to lick my plate.) if you get there no later than noon, then you shouldn't have too difficult of a time getting in.

I just feel happy thinking about this place. Cozy, cute, a great spot for a date, a slightly awkward spot for a just-friends with the opposite sex meal, but whatever. Well, that's what happened. Went there with a guy friend and wow, thought, this place would be great for a date! The food is unpretentious, homey and darn good. I had the pork belly special, the fuji apple soda (delicious), some collard greens, duck fat fries, and the flat bread. Yes, that is far too much food, but well worth it. Went back the next week for Sunday Supper. Now THAT is a great deal. Well worth the wait, but if you go before 7pm, no need to wait! A ton of open tables and a quiet meal before the rush!

What a great breakfast we had. We ordered the chicken and waffles-fried, the chicken was super moist, flavorful and crispy. The waffle was cooked well and tasted good with the syrup of course. We also got their corned beef hash with freshly made corned beef chunks with onions and green peppers. You can taste the freshness and soul feeling. I got it with sunny side up eggs which were cooked perfectly and with their homefries. Â  The meals all together was very tasteful, filling and yummy! The service was quick and friendly. Great place to have some soul food.

Basically just landing in NY off of a 5 hour flight, my friends and I are searching for a place to eat at 9pm while it's raining cats and dogs. Â Welcome to NY??? With a quick Yelp search, I came across Carmine's and we were in the mood for some good Italian food. Â They had great reviews, and it was walking distance of our hotel. Â The location of the restaurant couldn't be better really... it's in the middle of Times Square. Before I get into the food, I will say I was shocked that it was about 10pm by the time we got to the restaurant, and it was completely packed! NY does it right and city really doesn't sleep! My friends and I ordered 2 pastas, and that alone was already a mistake - the portions are MASSIVE!!!! If anyone has been Bucca Di Beppo, you know exactly what I mean. Â We even asked the waitress what the portion sizes are and that 2 pastas would be good for 3 people. Â I honestly do eat a lot, and can confidently say 2 pastas can fill 5-6 people. I forget the items I ordered but will post pictures, but they were delicioius! Â We were to be sure to order 2 different types of pasta, one with a marinara based sauce and another with an alfredo based one. Â  In terms of pricing, it certainly is more on the expensive side where our total with food and drinks was about $100 range. Â In terms of the service, it was pretty good considering how busy they were. Â At the end though, it was quite a challenge to get our check, but with some patience we finally got it. Overall, a great experience! I definitely recommend it if you're in the Times Square area (and I'm betting you will).

We went here on a reccomendation from local friends. We walked in on a late Sunday night Â with no reservation and were seated right away. Our server was warm and welcoming. Frankie's feels like you have stumbled upon a great neighborhood secret. Dining on the patio on a warm summer night by candle light really set the mood for an amazing meal. I also left with a huge bottle of their Â organic olive oil from Sicily. Great place for special occasions. I will be back for another slice of that heavenly ricotta cheesecake.

This is my third time here! Every time I had a good time and had good food. Milk shake is a Must Try!! French onion soup is hot and amazing. Love the potato skin & bacon. Egg Benedict is definitely worth trying. Spicy shrimp & grits are also good!

Although I would never go there if I were in a hurry (because of the wait and the hit-or-miss service), the food never disappoints. Very few dishes in the city can top the grilled corn followed by the Tlacoyo Tres Marias, a corn masa boat filled with goat cheese, black beans, and sundried tomatoes, covered with red and green chile sauces, and drizzled with crema. Rice and beans on the side that actually add to the dish, rather than simply fill space on the plate, make this one of those dishes that you ain't shaking from your memory anytime soon.

Came here for Happy hour after work and they have beers on tap for about $4. Pretty good deal. Owner and waitstaff are nice. Had their po boy sandwich which was good and big. I had a taste of their fried chicken sandwich which was the same thing but the fish tastes better. Also had their almond croissant, which was not house made. Do not recommend.
A Buffalo oasis/outpost that knows what they do....beef on weck, Labatts, and wings (with franks...). Any questions?

The service here is amazing, the food is superb, and i would absolutely recommend it to anyone visiting, or who hasnt been here before. Â like some other reviewers, I would suggest going with a group so you could try a little bit of everything. Â The chicken is amazing. Â Great for some fine italian and also some fresh, real food.

Food is good. Thumbs up for the avocado toast and couscous. Rarely do I like salmon, but their pot pie is pretty good. The atmosphere the servers set here though is "move and eat quick customers so we can get more people and more tips"
This is one of my favorite store in the NYC. Especially the green tea creep cake!!! LOVE IT!! The beef BBQ is really nice there too.. cant wait to go back eat it..

Just had a lovely meal here for perhaps the fifth time. Me: Grilled porkchop special, which comes with the obvious, along with smothered cabbage (see: +butter, onions, bacon) and baked (I think?) apples. Goodbye, vegetarianism; hello, ecstasy. He: Mussels provencal. Total perfection. I'm not a huge fan of seafood but I gave this ago and released a foul, but honest Fran Drescher-esque cry of pleasure. Our waitress was lovely and service was great. I'm currently pregnant with their flourless chocolate cake. It's wonderful.

This place has really nice ambiance and the backyard is so amazing. I thought that overall it was pretty decent, a few minor improvements could make the experience a lot better: The menu was on a chalkboard on the floor. You tip before you get service.. Which is a huge slam for employees who work hard and deserve more. The food was decent and the prices were right, I'll have to come back and try something else. The employees were also extremely helpful and sweet. If there was a 3.5 button I would've clicked that.

went there on fri eve for happy hour - nice ambiance, cool little patio out back, waiters & bartenders all very helpful & attentive, etc. one thing that stood out was that the place was buzzing, but not overcrowded or excessively noisy like so many other establishments would be on a fri in bk. - good spot to unwind in and have a conversation another thing that stood out were the rather measly happy hour oysters, which was a shame as everything else was pretty cool about catfish. $1 oysters, sure, but it was the reason i ventured out there in the first place. i felt a bit underwhelmed having just spent $35 on anorexic oysters & 1 bland beer cool spot, but somewhat expendable

Great 24hrs restaurant for your hungry beast. Try the empanadas. My favorite is Viagra Empanada. Â Do you like meat? Try the skirt steak dish. Sift and juice steak. I promise you that it will be the best steak you ever tasted.

WOW. My favorite food experience in NYC thus far. This kind of menu is basically everything that I've ever wanted to eat. It really, really appeals to me on a very deep level. And it certainly doesn't hurt that it's open 24/7!!!! We arrived at 9 PM on a Sunday night and were given the choice of waiting 15 minutes for an outside table or being seated immediately indoors. Since this is one of those cool places where they can basically open the entire outside walls of the restaurant on nice days/nights so it's all "outdoors", we went for the latter. All the waiters are have super hip funky style, and the vibes inside are super New York-y, if that makes sense. Our waitress was a doll. I drew happy faces and hearts for her on our receipt, and I never do that. OBVIOUSLY we had the Mac Attack appetizer - truffle oil mac and cheese, blue cheese mac and cheese, and bacon mac and cheese. Every bite was just as delectable as I'd imagined from reading previous Yelp reviews. They give you cornbread as your bread, which I love, but their butter is frozen and hard when they give it to you :( We solved this problem by melting the butter over the small candle that was on our table :) My date had the steak with yuca and red peppers, and I had the truffle shrimp risotto (um, BUZZ WORDS!!!!!). We were both delighted with our meals. I forced myself to get dessert even though I was stuffed, and heroically ate pretty much the entire order of deep fried oreos with espresso ice cream by myself because my date was stuffed. Yeah, they were that good. No, I couldn't walk afterwards. Everything about this meal was pure perfection. Thank you, Cafeteria!

I know, yet another ramen review by an Asian person. . . Well I'll keep it short and to the point as I know my review probably won't deter many of you from visiting this tiny mecca of ramen. I would say that this place is probably more of novelty place to many rather than a go-to spot to satiate some good old ramen cravings for few reasons. One: it's always too crowded. I rate dining experience- which includes convenience as part of the equation, and Ippudo is always way too crowded on obviously the most convenient times for meals. And eating in Ippudo is never convenient- it's always more of an investment- a more of just a "to-do" rather than "want-to-do." Two: the soup is always too salty. I don't know how much salt/MSG they put in their soup, but it's way too salty for me. Their noodles, on the other hand, is always very well cooked al dente and remains nice and chewy until the end of the meal. Three: price is way too expensive for a noodle soup of that caliber. Well hopefully they invest in many more locations to thin out the crowd, but for now, they are not good enough to wait long in any line. Totto ramen in UWS - obviously with as much waiting or more- I'd say is a better investment of your time.

Brought 3 of my Japanese friends/clients here. An updated take on Izakaya restaurants. Food was inventive, delicious and served promptly. Vibe was energetic but tables were spread far enough apart that it wasn't over bearing. Delicious bottle of sake from a decent list. From sashimi to yakitori to okonomayaki to daikon salad and many other dishes, each bite was delicious. Why not a 5? Â Kitchen ventilation left something to be desired (not unusual in yakitori places) and being in a basement location I felt a little breath-challenged.

I understand this is authentic thai food but the Â green curry in coconut sauce Â with thai eggplants was Â in inedible. Â It was mouth blistering spicy. I enjoy spicy food Â but to play it safe when ordering i requested it be just medium spicy. It was all heat, but no true flavor and the the eggplant was still crunchy and it was quite oily. This is supposed to be authentic thai? Maybe Â I ordered the wrong thing, but Â this place did not live up to all the hype, i was very disappointed. And why is rice extra? Ive never had thai food where they charged extra for regular rice???? I wont be back anytime soon. I can get better thai food around the corner.

Great pizza over there. Have been there with my family for a birthdayparty. The salami pizza is fabulous! The atmosphere there is very cool. The ingredients seemed to be fresh at all. It was the best pizza I have ever had in my life!!!!

If your AC isn't working it's common curtesy to tell people when they walk in. Unacceptable to still lead them upstairs , sit them down and serve food and only when asked say, "oh yeah, ummm it just stopped working ". I can't speak for their food as we didn't eat anything other than cheese and cold cuts but customer service was a big fail. Â Oh to add insult to injury they also told us it was hotter downstairs than upstairs (where we were sitting) when we asked about getting reseated. Â When we left the restaurant and walked downstairs we learned that was completely false. Â I wish yelp allowed to give negative stars.
Best Peruvian restaurant, i go there very often! Highly recommended.

This place is so good! I've had jerk chicken, oxtail and fried chicken. I love the oxtail the most. The only things that I don't totally love is that the place doesn't have too many tables so you have to do take out most of the time. The tables are mostly used by people waiting for takeout. I also think that they could be more clear about their hours. Several times I have tried to go but it was closed. But, the people who work here are incredibly friendly and care about the food they make and serve, the food itself is delicious and authentic and not too greasy or salty. Get collard greens and oxtail, those are my favorites.

Last week my husband and I had one of the best meals we've enjoyed in some time. The food was sublime, the service impeccable and gracious, the atmosphere tranquil and romantic. So, where is this lost paradise, this culinary katmandu, you ask? Answer: in the basement of an apartment building in the lonely canyons beyond Grand Central Station. Seriously? Seriously. Sakagura is indeed tucked away in an unlikely venue, but when you make the final turn around the staircase, you enter another world. It's like finding a secret doorway to a magical land. Sakagua is basically a Japanese tapas & sake house. Don't go here expecting sushi, because they don't serve it. Instead, you will find an extensive, authentic menu of Japanese small plates, all of which can be happily enjoyed with a selection from their incredible sake menu, or with a lovely cold beer. We tried a good handful of dishes, though I wish we'd had time to try even more (we had to rush off to the ballet). Favorites included: Hirame Ponzu, or Thinly Sliced Fluke Sashimi Topped with Grated Dikon Radish Dressed with a Citrus Vinaigrette. The sashimi was so, so, so good. I could have eaten plate after plate of this fresh, delightful dish. For hot dishes, we loved the house special Buta Kakune, or Tender Pork Belly simmered in a sweet, salty, savory addictive sauce. This is one of the best pork belly dishes I've ever had. The entire portion of meat was incredibly tender and the sauce coated and clung to the whole fatty, glistening mess in a way that begged you to just pick up the delicate little bowl and pour it straight into your mouth. The Gyu Miso Nikomi, or Shredded Beef Back Ribs Stewed in Miso Topped with Grated Dikon Radish were also a big hit at our table. The meat, again, was really tender and the sauce, while savory, had some indefinable element of sweetness that was completely seductive. Other delightful bites included: Ijura Oroshi, or Grated Daikon Radish Topped with Fresh Salmon Roe. The radish was like a pillow, or a cloud perhaps, on top of which glistening orange roe were perched. A little soy sauce added just the right amount of flavor to this subtle, silky dish. The steak grilled on a hot stone was more fun than it was outstanding, but the beef was of extremely high quality and the novelty of cooking it on the hot stone gave the meal a playful element. Desserts at Sakagura are also excellent - we shared the Black Sesame Creme Brulee, which was creamy and not too sweet. Very, very good. Best of all, the service at Sakagura is top-notch. I was extremely impressed with their attentiveness, timing, and generally friendly attitude. It made me realize how often service at many NYC restaurants is lacking, or lackluster. In sum, we honestly can't wait for an opportunity to go back.

The curry beef stew here isn't that great, i do not recommend the curry here. New Malaysia Restaurant in chinatown has way better curry than Nyonya, as always zagat rated so people's perception of a restaurant becomes different.

SERVICE: Order at the front, pay at the front. The guys actually delivered our order to our table, which we didn't expect. PRICE: $5-$10/person VALUE: Good spot for snacks. Southern, Creole vibe. Their crawfish ettouffee was the highlight of my night. Huge portion so I suggest ordering that and something else to (ahem crawfish mac and cheese and a chicken po boy).

This was our second visit to Pinto. The food is great but the drinks were less impressive. Appetizers: Stuffed tofu and mushroom crunch. The crunch was pretty oily but very tasteful at the same time. Tofu was good as well. Entrees: Pad Thai (Great!) and Lamb Massaman (So-so). There was something subtly wrong with the lamb dish and I couldn't figure out what. Probably too much salt. Also, lamb was a little overcooked. Potatoes were perfect. They were out of 2 out of the 4 red wines. I ended up getting the french red wine they had and it was awful. We also ordered white chicks cocktail which was okay. The service was pretty bad but it's probably because they are highly understaffed. And this was a Monday evening, mind you! I'll still give a 4-star since overall I like their food.

Dropped in this little place sometime last year by accident as we were walking around thinking about ramen. Never heard of the place, we walked in and were told a reservation is necessary but luckily a cancellation allowed us to sit down for a wonderful hearty meal! We ordered the sashimi platter which was very refreshing on a hot summer day... And as it's been a long while since I had a traditional pig feet noodle soup (Taiwanese/Chinese dish), we went for the hakata tonton hot pot. Â I would say it was a bit salty, but the flavor was definitely good... Loved everything that was in it but the addition of extra noodles at the end of the stew got us a bit too full. Black sesame was a nice finish for a hot meal during summer time... Good, rich and creamy. Would go back to try other dishes.
I love this place!!!! The Mexican style grilled corn on the cob with a Michelada to drink Â is pretty much the best thing ever. Â The servers are sassy and funny and take good care of you.

I still remember the first time I came here. It was probably 11PM at night on a weekday and I remember telling my fiance (who was my bf at the time), "Do you think they'll be open?". Oh naive me. Of course they're open - we live in Manhattan! So yes, they were open. So open in fact that literally every table was almost filled. We had a great time. The food is yummy (although the rice is so sparse..) and the drink menu was so fun to look at (and to drink!). A nice break from all the hole-in-the-wall Thai places on 9th street, I love the trendy atmosphere here. The prices are not so bad either :)

My family and I ate here last night and we nearly swooned over the food. The lamb shank I had was falling off the bone and perfectly season. My dessert was a warm date cake with coconut sorbet and and carob and was amazing. We will be going back.

Hello, Pies! Meet my thighs! This is not where you go to eat if you're worried about fitting into your skinny jeans. I ordered a chicken biscuit because I wanted a tasty little bite to eat and a key lime pie because Wing L's review was so complimentary. I did not regret my choices at all. The chicken cutlet was so succulent and moist. Crispy, but not at all greasy, breading made a gratifying crunch when I bit in. I adored the scrumptious honey butter that coated the chicken. I had honey butter dripping out and before each bite, I dipped my chicken biscuit in the fallen honey butter like a French dip sandwich because I did not want to waste one drop of that ambrosia. The biscuit was light and flaky. Everything a biscuit should be. I took the pie with me to enjoy the next day. The key lime pie was light with a touch of tang. I had meant to save a taste for a friend, but honestly once I started eating it all good intentions were lost. The restaurant is a small, but fun, kitschy environment. The tables and chairs are old school tables and chairs. It's either fun or brings you back horrible memories of being picked on at school when you were little. Definitely worth making a trip and braving the hipsters for a bite of simple, down home Southern chicken and pies.

Definitely one of the top places in Chinatown. Searching around different sites to look for top places to eat, I come across Super Taste. "Weird name!", I say to myself. So I decide to go check out if this place really is "Super taste"! After reading about the dumplings and the noodles, I opt for the dumplings with noodles. And what a surprise. It was tasty! The handmade noodles were perfectly cooked. The soup had a nice beefy flavour to it. In another reivew, someone mentioned the soup has crack in it? I agree! There's something in there that makes me want to go back for more. (probably msg). And the dumplings were full of flavour, lots of meat and the skin was nice and slimy. 2 stars for value for money 3 stars for the flavours and quality of the food! but really... no stars for the service. Sharing of tables, getting bumped constantly. But what do you expect from an asian place? :) Def a place to try, but it does get pretty crowded, so it's better off coming in smaller groups or even by yourself.

Really enjoyed my early light dinner at ABC Kitchen. Went on a Sunday night on Thanksgiving weekend, and sat at the back bar. Â The Ginger Marg was a great way to start the evening, and the scallops as well as the crab toast were tasty, unique and excellent. Â Followed this with the Brussels sprout pizza, which was fantastic. Recommend getting an egg on the pizza, and save room for the seasonal donuts. Very good experience and enjoyed the location, the service and the food. Worth the cost as well.

You won't go wrong with any of the house special noodle soup, the spicy beef soup or the Mount Qi noodle soup, all of which I've had (though I suspect that some of the chopped vegetables might originally be frozen). Â I particularly like the spicier soups. Â Good hefty servings and lots of condiments on the tables - especially perfect for cold days.
The Suckling Pig Feast was fantastic and a great value for the price. Â Highly recommended as a large format/group dining experience.

f you are a "regular" at this place. Like, they actually know you, I congratulate you on your extreme dedication. My boyfriend and I recently calculated that we have spent thousands of dollars at the meatball shop, and yet every time we go, a waiter will inevitably ask if we've been there before. I highly suggest this place to vegetarians. Isn't that weird? They have veggie balls and you can get them over a bed of fresh market vegetable salad side dishes. Sometimes, this contains hummus, but I've also had beets, kale, broccoli, cauliflower, arugula salad, squash salads, mashed root vegetables, etc. It always comes with four different cold salads. They are fresh, crunchy, savory, sweet, and delicious. These are really gourmet vegetable side dishes. We're talking quality, here. It's also $8. That is not a typo. Get this, and get an ice cream sandwich. And get the walnut cookie. Because, it is really a meringue cookie with chocolate chips and walnuts. It melts in your mouth. So worth trying a new thing. Yumm-o

I was very happy to have found this place so close by since there aren't any other good alternatives for sushi restaurants in my neighborhood. Took my mom here for her birthday and she loved it. The service was pretty decent as was the sushi, for the price you pay during Happy Hour, which was $3.50 for some of the rolls. The Fire Island roll (warm) was delicious but I would advise against the Passion roll - it tasted as if a bit of wasabi was mixed it in. The ambiance is also great with the slightly dimmed lights and antique walls, very nice for dates or gatherings with friends. Not the best for huge groups because it's small and has more of an intimate atmosphere. Happy hour is from 4-7pm, so if you can beat the crowd on weekdays and come a bit before 6, you'll get seats and a quieter environment to dine in. Zest is a wonderful place, glad to have found it.

Please, do yourself a huge favor and order the farro rissotto. You must. The aroma from the parmesan regginao hits you in the face, (in a good way, of course) and the creaminess frum the risotto with the playful halved grapes on top makes this one spectacular dish. Heck, they even make artichokes taste good. Â At 10 bucks, this is a def. a worthier splurge than those spicy duck meatballs, which were spectacularly eh...small. Sure, they were great, and even became known as a specialty for the chef, but the risotto was def. more of a hit among the group. We each got a different entree to share. The "Three Little Pigs" with the berkshire tenderloin, boar belly and crispy suckling pig ear salad not only looked superb, they also tasted wonderful. The gently crusted skin was simply great. The hanger steal was also great. Done medium rare, and very tender. I had the duck breast, and I must say, when you cut it thinly, it is simply divine. The food was a little on the pricier side, but the portions were huge (all xcept the spicy duck meatball), and it was a def. enjoyable meal. Note: pass the dessert. They were forgettable. With so many resturants that serve great desserst, this is not one of them.

the brunch at buttermilk is so yummy , no wonder its almost impossible to get at table here , yes we are big fans of it Â :) management and ownership are awesome , kind , friendly ,warm super nice people , they do really care and have appreciation for their customers Â  we loved it :)))

I went there today and was pleasantly surprised. Â I had a 50% off coupon, which is why I chose this side street sports bar. Â However, the food was so good that I will gladly pay full price for it anytime. My friend and I came in for a late lunch around 4:30 in the afternoon. Â There were a lot of large TV's playing multiple football games and the Ryder's Cup. Â We were told to sit wherever we liked and chose a nice comfy table against the back wall. Â The waitress, who was very pretty and nice, came by dropped off menues and gave us a minute to look things over. Â No big spiel, no "suggestions" of over priced drinks. Â  She came back promptly and took our orders. Â We both had burgers, two different kinds, and beers. Â The selection of beer was decent, nothing spectacular. Â I originally tried to order their signature drink, The Proper Manhattan, which is their version of a perfect manhattan, but they were out of bitters. Â I then tried a seasonal brew and they were out of that too. Â Seems like they need to get their ordering down a bit better. Â  The food took a little longer than I expected, but it was well worth the wait. Â As per my preference, I ordered my burger medium. Â It came cooked medium. Â I cannot tell you how many up scale restaurants can't seem to get this right. Â Every time I bite into a patty expecting a burst of juicy delicious beef, I get well done, dry, hockey puck patty. Â Not here though. Â The seasoning ws ample and the flavors were bold. Â The Proper Burger has white cheddar, grilled onions and bacon on top, just the way I like it. Â They seemed to skimp a little on the bacon because there were only two halves of a slice gracing the top. Â The bun was also a little on the small side. Â Seemed like it could have been chosen to make the patty look big. Â No matter, I devoured the whole thing. Â The fries were an after thought for me, but not for my palate. Â They were crispy, hot and held up to the burger drippings, staying firm and not getting soggy under the juice. We were still a little hungry so we ordered the Honey BBQ wings and the Andouille Sausage Sliders. Â The sliders were good and flavorful, but compared to the wings I didn't even care that they were there. Â The Wings were crispy with a nice bite, sweet in the right way without being puckeringly sweet and they had just the right amount of sauce on them, not drenched, not dry. Â We finished our beers and got the check. Â They were quick and easy with the discount and didn't question it at all. Â Glad we came and we will be back. Good: Food, TV's, atmosphere, service Not so good: Struck out twice on drinks and the burger needed a little more bacon. Â Hell, everything needs a little more bacon.

Maybe it's because I saw Julie and Julia beforehand, but I didn't think it was anything special. Â The steak au poivre was just ok. Â I ordered it medium rare and it came in a dull gray...so cooked way ahead of time and just reheated. Â We were there at 6...so why wasn't it cooked to order? Beet salad was decent. Â Fries were warm. Service was ok. Eh.

This would be among my first banh mi, but compared to other sandwiches I've had, this place is great. The ingredients are fresh and the bread is toasted to perfection. The resto itself is tucked away: a literal small hole in the wall in the East Village. There is next to no seating, but the decor is cool: dark walls with a chalk board menu and some bar seating on the side. I had the side car (meat with pineapple chutney, pickled veggies, not spicey), my boyfriend had a spicey super cub classic; we shared a Vietnamese coffee. The coffee was nothing special (tasted like a regular coffee to me). I didn't try the sig other's sandwich, but he is a self proclaimed banh mi expert (he grew up in the San Gabriel Valley in LA and apparently that gives you expertise in all foods Asian) and said it was great: fresh ingredients, nicely toasted bread, very flavorful. As for mine, I liked it a lot for a lot of the same reasons (I thought the little bit of sweet with the tender meat and then the tang of the pickled veggies at the end was awesome). My only complaint was the laying of the sandwich: all the meat was cramped into the fold of my bread and all the veeggies were on the other side of the bread. Instead of the flavors marrying with each bite, I had one bite veggies, the next bite meat... Not sure if this was done on purpose, but I liked how everything tasted together and the fact that I had to take 2 bites (my mouth is tiny) every time was a little tedious. Pricewise, it's something like $7? Well worth it... Overall, I would come here again (I took half to go and it STILL tasted great 4 hours later).

Like Chipotle, but a million times better than Chipotle. Get your potatoes any way you want 'em--baked potato,potato wedges, potato fries, mashed potato, the possibility feel endless. Potatopia gives the option to go cancer-promoting, artery-clogging, butter-oozing goodness and the option to go lite and healthy Either way, your concoction will be packed full of flavor. I got the veggie heavy potato, which was a baked potato stuff full of broccoli, garlic, jalapeÃ±o, red onion, sweet pepper, green onion with sour cream, roasted pepper. I subbed out jalapeno for corn and I got it without butter, or olive oil, or sour cream, and even so it was delicious!!! My friend got the smashed hit with added steak (extra $3.00) cheddar cheese, asiago cheese, green onions, red onion, garlic, cilantro with roasted pepper. It was definitely a man's potato dish and I would definitely recommend it to anyone who loves comfort food. Both dishes were baked before served so the cheese was semi-melted and warm. There are so many topping and sauce options here, much more than Chipotle, and the staff is super friendly. Stuffed to the brim, we only paid $17, which includes his addition of steak. For $7 a person, you get so much bang for your buck. This place is a must-go!

MY NEW FAVORITE BREAKFAST/LUNCH SPOT(even tho I live out in queens)! Went in at about 11 on a regular monday so it wasnt more than a 5 min wait, thats probably different at peak times as the other reviews say. Small place, Great food, Good Service, reasonably priced menu, weird hipster-esc photos and painting, and did i mention GREAT FOOD! Finally tired out Chicken and Waffles and I could not have been more delighted to have ordered and consumed this fluffy waffle from heaven that was topped with a fresh fried chicken that was smothered with some amazing gravey, the gf had "The Big Boy" which was 2 eggs, bacon,2 pancakes, home fries and corn bread which was equally amazing. They do offer spiked milkshakes that we didnt get a chance to try maybe next time. I'll be back for the steak and eggs!

The hubs and I enjoyed a great lunch at Shanghai Asian Manor. We were quickly seated and served beverages right away. The menu was extensive and we went with soup dumplings, shrimp lo mien and some pork dumplings. The food came out hot and was delicious. Also - the bathrooms were clean!
Awesome spot for something so close to penn station. Tasty pizza, decent wine, delicious salads, and a super nice bar tender. Profiteroles for dessert :) We will definitely be back!

This place is the holy grail of all things Italian. From reading all the Yelp reviews before I went, I braced myself to be shoved around in a massive crowd, especially since I was going on a weekend. To my delighted surprise, it wasn't anywhere near as bad as I expected! Perhaps the rain kept folks away? Now that I didn't have to worry about the insane crowds, I felt free to browse around and look at all the interesting things stocked on the shelves. I was mesmerized by not only the fancy Italian products, but also the astonishing prices that went along with them. But hey, I knew that before stepping foot inside. Keeping a budget in mind, I decided to selectively purchase a few products that in my opinion would be "worth it" - mostly very typical Italian products that I thought would be of much higher quality at Eataly such as fresh mozzarella and gourmet olive oil. Some things to note: 1. They do have a handful of items on sale! Look for those when you walk in. For example, I picked up my fresh mozzarella on sale for only $2.80! 2. There are always 2-3 things discounted at 50% right by the cash registers. I bought a box of Melighe di Mondovi Italian cookies half off for $4.80 that were SO SO good. I wish I bought 5 of those tubs... 3. There's a guy who will conduct a mini olive oil sampling in order to help you decide which oil to get - pretty cool! 4. For a tasty snack to go along with your coffee drink at Lavazza, I highly recommend getting their pack of 4 mini cookies, which you can get for only $1! Minus one star for: a) The utter lack of help on the floor - there were no employees in sight to direct you to something specific that you may be looking for. b) The atrocious seating at Lavazza. I had a delicious Bicerin drink but couldn't properly enjoy it with the tables so crammed together. TIP: Definitely get your coffee drink first BEFORE you shop if you want to sit down to enjoy it as there is NO place to keep your cart. Overall: Everything I bought was great but the cost probably would limit me to only purchasing when I want to impress someone by cooking them a gourmet Italian meal.
I wouldn't recommend this place at all. Really bad service and dirty inside. Â Towards the end of the evening plates were left on tables and the kitchen was a mess!

Mostly this place is getting 4 stars because I love the history behind it. The dining room was full for a private party I believe so we were seated in the bar area. It was freezing outside so I was just glad to be indoors, I didn't care where we sat. When we first arrived it was pretty mellow but as it got later the place became super crowded. We were there during happy hour and this place is right near the financial district so I'm sure this is a popular place to go to after the work day. Service was pretty slow because of this but it wasn't terrible. Food was tasty and the drink selection is amazing. I had a hot cider drink and then a cold cider. Both were seasonal and very good. We also ordered a few different things to eat like a cheese plate, truffle fries and onion rings. Pretty decent bar fare. I also ordered a bowl of their soup of the day which was lobster bisque. It was good but by the time I had gotten it, it wasn't as hot as I would have liked. Also I wanted bigger pieces of lobster in it! Guess I got a little spoiled after eating dinner in Boston... Flavor was nice though and it definitely didn't go to waste. Should have tried their famous pot pie, but hopefully I will get a chance in the future. One thing that I found a little strange was the music selection. The bar was playing mostly modern stuff that didn't really go with the rest of the feel of the place, plus it was a bit too loud. I would still return though. I love old buildings like this one with so much great American history. I hope George Washington's ghost still haunts this old bar, imbibing in a fine glass of Â some old booze and scoffing at all these young folk listening to their Imagine Dragons.

WOW! When I picture Brooklyn BBQ in my head, i see a no frills joint, and that's exactly what Fette Sau is. Converted from an old garage into an amazing BBQ joint, this place is not to be missed. I had a sampling of everything from the pork belly, to the sausage to the pulled pork and some ribs. ALL AMAZING! What really surprised me were the baked beans. I hate baked beans, and let me stress, hate. However the baked beans at Fette Sau looked a bit more like Chili so I decided to give them a whirl. Outcome? I went back for more! The only con is that it tends to be crowded alll the time. So go prepared to wait a bit for a seat. Did I mention the seating is a picnic tables? Does it get much more Brooklyn? Love it!

Pizza. Â Everybody loves pizza. Â Chicago deep dish, New Â York, Sicilian, thin crust, thick crust, the list goes on but at the top of this list is Luzzo's Napoli style pizza. Â The pizza here is other worldly. Â  Diavola - yes it is devilishly delicious. Â Just the right amount of spice in the sauce and the peperoni is perfect. Procuitto with arugula - listen who said you can eat your greens with your pizza. Â Fantastic. Â  This is the place we always bring friends who visit NYC for pizza. Â Great every single time

Terrible terrible terrible service!!! The entire staff including the manager are rude and disrespectful. When we got to the place, we were told that there would be a 30 minute wait. 30 minutes later we were told that were only two more parties ahead of us on the list. After waiting another 30 minutes (one hour total), three more parties magically got on the list before us. All the manager had to say was that "they are a very trendy place and if you want to eat there, you have to wait". I don't mind waiting to be seated, but I don't think it's acceptable for a place not to be able to manage its own seating list.

Very interesting location. It's like a place for those who are in the know. If you're not looking for traditional japanese food, you wouldn't be able to find this place. With that said, if you like izakaya style food, this would be the place for you. You can have some cold dishes, hot dishes, some rice and noodles and an extensive choice of sake. Also since it is underground, phone service sucks. Oh no. Now you'll have to talk to your dinner companions. If you can't survive an hour or so of no texting, don't come here. As for the food~ Must get: Gyusuji. My friend said that this dish was beef tendon. So of course I was disappointed to find that there wasn't any chewy tendon. However, it was really good. There was a lot of flavor and the sauce mixed with the grated radish was delicious. The beef was nice and tender and tasted like good quality beef. There was also some fatty parts that added sweetness to the dish. So I still liked it even though I was misled. Kakuni. This was also a very tasty dish. The pork belly was fatty as expected and the fatty part was melt-in-your-mouth delicious. The sauce was sweet and I liked the hint of sake in it. However, I wish the meat under the fat was more melty as well. I feel like it wasn't simmered long enough. Because it was kind of difficult to cut apart. Not the easiest dish to share. Up to you: Tofu salad. Yummy dressing! The miso dressing is quite good but that was the only good thing about it. I kinda wish the tofu was homemade but it's not. And their choice of tofu was lacking in flavor. And yes, good tofu has flavor! for those of you who think that tofu is supposed to be bland. I also liked that the greens were shredded. It made it easy to eat. Amadai saikyo yaki. I like to try new things so even though every cell in my body told me to get the cod fish, I opted for the tile fish. It was not bad. It could have used some more flavor though, I don't think it was marinated enough. But it was grilled well and I like that it's not a fishy fish. But I don't think it can compare to the Gindara, which is more softer, creamier, and oilier (in a good way). Unless you prefer a drier, less fatty fish that is. Surume Ika yaki. This one was the least of this group. It's just grilled squid in sweet soy sauce. Nothing special. Tastes the same at any other izakaya really. The squid had nice texture though and it was also grilled well. But it was a little low in temperature. Maybe it wasn't ran quick enough. Oh and I think you get only have a squid because the body pieces were flat instead of a full circle. Skip it: Jaga Dango. Potato mochi donut. Sounds interesting right? But interesting doesn't always mean good taste. This one really baffled us. My friend and I really could not understand why the dish was on the menu. It was one of the hot dishes but it tasted like dessert. Just somewhat sweet and smelled like funnel cake. It came with salt on the side which was pointless and did not match well with the dough at all. The potato in the center was tasteless and the mochi texture of it wasn't really good. Bad idea, bad execution. I'd much prefer mashed potatoes or a croquette. Onigiri. 3 words: waste of money. It was literally two small triangular rolled rice with some topping on it and nori sheet on the side. It was impossible to wrap without smooshing the topping. Why didn't they mix the topping into the rice then roll it? I know it's just onigiri but you could put in some effort. Especially if you're charging 6 bucks for it. Although the Mentaiko and takana leaves had good flavor, I could easily buy them and put it on top of rice myself. Save the space in your stomach and the money and get the Karaage or chicken meatball like I should have done. Â  Other than the food, service was okay if not a little lacking in warmth and smiles. Actually, this place is more of 3.5 stars but I gave extra for the food presentation and simply because there aren't many higher end izakayas out there and although the portion is pretty small, it's not extremely pricey either. I'd say it's pretty reasonable. I'll be back.
Yummy pizza! not to much of anything, everything was perfect. Not greasy. although the line there on saturday was about an hour and a half long wait. Well worth trying.

I have two ratings here: one for the salad and main course, and a second rating for everything else. The "everything else" was fantastic. Â The bread basket that graced the table was delicious, and it was all I could to to keep from eating all the breadsticks in it and spoiling my dinner. The Cesar salad is ok, but not wonderful. Â It certainly could be better, but it could be so much worse. Â I would rather have a salad than not, so I guess it's ok. As an afterthought when ordering, I had the pasta added on. Â They serve you three kinds of pasta that change daily. Â You can even order pasta as your main course, and just have as many helpings as you want. Â I was sorely tempted by that option, but I didn't want to stake my dinner on two of the three options. Â Fettucine bolognese sounded plain (unfair of me, since it was fresh pasta and high-quality beef, so it was fantastic!) and eggplant ravioli sounds good, but most restaurants can't get eggplant right (spot on here, so I unfairly pre-judged the kitchen!). After the pasta, I was really looking forward to the osso bucco as my main course. Â It was ok, but not great. Â I've had better (most memorably, at a place in Portland). Â I would call it an average osso bucco, and sadly quite large. The panna cotta for dessert had a powerful fresh vanilla flavor, complete with a dusting of vanilla seeds across the top. As I finish writing this, I realize that I gave a NY pizza place in suburban Vegas five stars, yet I'm only giving Becco four. Â Yeah, ok, that's not really fair. Â I suppose I was hoping for much more out of a NYC Italian restaurant, and anything in Vegas benefits from my relatively low expectations. In any case, my lesson: next time, just have the pasta.

I was thoroughly impressed by Mark. The people that work here are super friendly. It seems like a night time joint, but my friend and I came here for lunch and it was still cool. The food was AWESOME. I got one regular slider and one bacon slider. The bacon slider was worth the extra few cents. The bacon is mixed into the patty and has a really good bacon-y flavor. The regular slider was really great too. I ordered a side of pickles and topped each one with a pickle + tons of chipotle and jalapeÃ±o ketchup. I cannot wait to dine here again.

So, the rolls are great. You may not find your fav at first try so give the other varieties a shot. The lamb rocks. The chana rocks. You get a good indian flavor in a simple to eat roll. Well done. But.... The place if filthy. I mean gross. The floor is gross, the chairs are gross, the table tops are gross at times. What the hell?
Just amazing.

2.5 actually. Â I've never experienced a more disappointing brunch then what we had yesterday. Â  We had been to the Kickshaw several times before the "menu change", but this was our first visit since the switch. Â We both had high expectations because we were so fond of it previously. Â  The service here has always been spotty and yesterday was no exception. Â The portions are very small and unremarkable. Â I will grant you that a four-cheese omelet is a fairly safe item, but it was so small and boring, I regretted my decision to order it, especially when I saw how little it was. Â The waiter said he'd be back with some toast, but when he arrived with my single, dry piece of toast, I'd had enough of this place. Â My girlfriend's meal was equally disappointing. Â "Layered potato cake" was how it was described, but the fact is it was two fried eggs with scalloped potatoes and no cheese. Â And tiny. Â  The pour over coffees are very good, but the brunch left me hungry and disappointed. Â This place needs to advertise what it really is: Â a small plates restaurant. Â Time to step up your game QK.

Disappointing brunch, My eggs came about 45 minutes after our starter. The food is great but the service made for an uncomfortable experience. Instead of anyone telling us the kitchen was backed up or they forgot our order or whatever the staff just hovered around us staring. Our Bloody Marys had no garnishes at all. I saw a lot of staff members standing around leaning up against the wall and the hostesses were not very welcoming. My dinner experience has never been this bad.

Great place to get a quick lunch in midtown. Their pastrami sandwich with pickled jalapeÃ±os is fantastic. Their coffee is really good as well. Everything is always fresh, I love their creative panini selection.

Came here for the second time in a long time today, the hostess didn't seem so friendly. However, once seated my waitress had a good attitude and was very helpful. I ordered a platano relleno as an appetizer, a mango margarita, and the churrasco.The frozen mango margarita was a bit crappy , it was too thick. The platano relleno was amazing though! and the churrasco was even better! juicy and very flavorful. Food was a bit pricey but it was all worth it. Left the place with a full belly and smile on my face. i definitely recommend it. :)

Was here on Sunday night with a few friends. The line was consistently out the door but moved quickly. I was somehow able to score a table, great because it was chilly outside. The burrito ingredients were simple: a steamed tortilla with melted cheese, rice, pinto beans, carnitas (marinated pulled pork) sour cream and hot sauce (2 kinds). The reason we all should be going is the carnitas. The pulled pork melts in your mouth like butter, is seasoned perfectly and feels like it belongs in a much more sophisticated meal than a burrito. All carnitas is not created equal. For comparison, the carnitas at Chipotle is raw sewage compared to this. The pinto beans were good, the rice was cooked perfectly, the pico de gallo was fresh and vibrant and the sour cream and two hot sauces (if you like spicy you will have to ask for the really hot red one, they give you the green one by default) compliment the carnitas perfectly. There is also a complimentary guacamole in which I did not partake. Oh, the ingredients are all sustainable and locally raised; another huge plus. I had a taste of a friend's chicken burrito as well. The chicken is wonderfully seasoned and has a nice smoky, grilled flavor to it that also goes well with the burrito ingredients. All in all this is a great place for a quick lunch or dinner. Even when to the door, the line moves very quickly. the staff is very friendly and the prices are right. Cheap, quick, healthy and delicious...you can't go wrong. It would be five stars if they had Modelo for me to slug down with the burrito, otherwise this place is perfect for what it tries to be.

I really wanted to give this place 5 stars. Â We went for dinner, the food, drinks, and ambiance (mood, lighting, decor, and music- hootie and the blow fish- MORE PLEASE) were really impressive. Â However, they appeared understaffed and after our food arrived our server disappeared for a some time when we were looking to get a second round of drinks (which didn't happen because it was too late by the time he came back around). Â In his defense, it appeared that 3 new tables arrive at the same time. Â  Signature cocktails with gin was refreshing and nice for summer. Â  Food: Fresh spun mozzarella- so fresh tasting and creamy texture- great balance English Pea and ricotta Raviolli- Â my expectations were not great on this dish but it was truly something I will be back for. Â It was delicate, covered in a white wine type sauce. Â perfectly savory without being salty. Â  All and all I will be back here.
Great little neighborhood haunt.

believe the hype! the food here is worth every penny, especially the black label burger. Â my husband is a bit frugal but even he will always say yes! when minetta tavern is suggested for dinner/lunch. the general manager here is awesome and so is the rest of the staff. Â i love this place even more because we didnt get any attitude for recently bringing a toddler during brunch Â (yay!).

This place is super hyped, but I cannot deny that they do serve a good and hearty bowl of ramen. It's good but not good enough for the price. Ippudo's noodle was on a skinnier side, but still chewy. The broth is very rich and milky in color. It's meaty and flavorful, but quite salty. The pork was tender and not fatty at all. Basically, it's everything a bowl of ramen should be. I really like their pork bun though. It's super rich, fatty and filled with tons and tons of flavor, and who can deny that it tastes better with the mayo they put in it. I also like that they put lettuce for the extra crunch. And like the ramen, the pork bun is also on a pricer side, but I think the bun is actually well worth the dough. I would definitely come back and definitely order a few buns for myself.

TrÃ¨s bien It'a new venue though it's already full of nice stories... every piece of furniture has something to tell (just ask for Armel or Mickael) The food is really delicious and the wine list is superb Will comme back (and often)

I loooooove the decor here. If you ever get the whole story, the owners emptied a castle back in the home country, and transplanted virtually every which way knick knack over to this bar. Â Cocktails are pretty good, although depends on who makes them. Â I also quite like the obligatory Guiness pours , if beer is more your thing. Come early or late, since the after work crowd fills this looooong bar to the gills.

Amazzzzinggggg I live in the area and there are few places around here I eat on a regular basis but this is one of them. Healthy food in a semi-food wasteland area, much needed. The food itself is so, so good. I'd say more New American than French, rich and light options, and the drinks are also PHENOMENAL. The yogurt and granola, the huevos rancheros type dish, the toast with cinna butter....all perfect. Ive never been here for anything other than brunch so I cant speak to that but when i come here I tend to linger and the staff is always sweet and relaxed. A little pricey for the portions (...they are pretty small) but still worth the trip. Really nice ambiance inside too.

Came here during restaurant week, price fixed 3 course lunch special, woo! Outdoor seating was lovely, tomato salad yummy, waitress was helpful and friendly - bus service was lacking. Never received bread, had to ask several times for water refill. Overall a nice place to bring out-of-towners but I wouldn't have liked it as much without the price fix.

This place was on our list to go to during our theatre trip, so we took the subway, walked 8 blocks in 90 degree weather but felt triumphant when we reached our destination! Counter guy was outside smoking a cigarette but it gave us enough time to look over the menu. 4 fried and 10 steamed pork and chive dumplings, 1sesame pancake and a huge serving of roasted duck noodle soup and two bottled waters - $11.50. Sat at the counter and ate and perspired - but overall enjoyed the experience! Food was great and everything was exactly as described on Yelp! Counter guy (which is literally right next to the cook top) was coughing away with no attempt to cover his mouth as we left!

Nothing special, but cute location. Â Food was okay, not outstanding or anything. Â They charge extra for sauces which out of principle doesn't make sense when I happened to order quite a bit of food for two people not just your average amount. Â You can't give tahini? Â Lol. Â Wake up, Taim! Â You know nothing about this food culture acting like that, tahini goes hand in hand, this employee was treating it like a separate menu item. Â On top of that this very condescending employee was so rude about it and then felt bad when he realized our order and tried to give it to us but I was disgusted by his nasty attitude. Â He realizes we are entitled to our sauces after the fact? Â I was so close to asking for full refund and leaving the food at the counter, but couldn't stand to be there another minute. Â If I could I would give them zero stars. Never go here. Â There are many other places to try. Â I expected so much more especially because of the prestigious owner. Â SO disappointed.

Contrary to it's name, my favorite dish is actually the Beef tendon Hong Kong style Lo-mein-- they serve the egg noodle and the beef tendon in one bowl with oyster sauce. the meal also comes with a side bowl of soup, where you can turn your lo mein into a noodle soup. Delicious spot for a quick meal; salty but satisfying. Everything you would want from a 'hole in the wall' kind of spot. Don't expect high class service, because this is afterall...Chinatown.

After our original plans feel through, my friends and I ended up here for dinner on a Friday evening. We were seated outside in their garden patio before 7 pm and discovered they have a "drunch" menu. It seems the reviews on here are dominated by the brunch, but the "drunch" three-course menu for $19.95 was a steal! For the first course, the chick pea salad, mesculun salad, and mussels were all winners. The chick peas were tender, and the salad was scrumptious. The mesculun salad was fresh and tasty. The mussels with fennel were divine! For the main course, we all got the hanger steak (what can I say, my gal pals and I love our steak) which was tender and flavorful. The gelato (we tried hazelnut and chocolate) and apple tartine were perfect ways to end the meal. Oh, and we washed it all down with a carafe of sangria! I may very well consider checking out Cafe Luluc for brunch, but my suggestion would be to check out their "drunch" menu M-F between 4-7 pm. You won't be disappointed!

so, so, so good and so, so, so cheap! delightfully decorated with the charm of a confused grandmother. i got the kielbasa plate for $5. it came with three, humongous, crisp (deep fried perhaps?), juicy sausages, a side of assorted vegetables, and mashed potatoes. for five. freaking. dollars. i also had some of my friend's pierogis and borscht and a bit of a blueberry blintz afterwards and ate myself to contentment. it's too bad it's winter and i can't bike like ten miles because i def gained about five pounds after the experience. BUT IT WAS SO WORTH IT! i'd gain 500 pounds for lomzynianka.

now i know why many single people go there just to eat the shao long bao and nothing else. Â the dumplings are excellent, on par with the ones i tried in toronto (had metal tongs, lots of soup inside, tasty); you should eat them and go and try other restaurants nearby cuz the others just stink. Â maybe the scallion pancake is worth it, but that's about it: 2 things very well done.

Gotta love Habana Outpost. Frosty mojitos and coladas. Fattening ears of roasted corn smothered in tasty, fatty things (grated cheese, butter, red pepper). Sunny skies, beautiful music and beautiful people. Every visit to this spot feels like a "daycation" to Cuba whether you sit in or outside. I bought my homeboy from work here and he didn't wanna leave. He lamented about the fact that they don't have anything like Habana Outpost in The BX and all I could say was, "Sorry buddy. The BX will never be as cool as Brooklyn."

I went for the first time this weekend for brunch and loved it. In a town of many disappointing midmorning meals, I left happy. The pancakes were great with berries and syrup. Wifey had a very tasty quiche that I would have been happy to order. Fresh squeezed oj plus nice weather on the back patio. Highly recommended.

The service we received while dining at this French Bistro is comparably better than most places we've eaten in the city. The food was meticulously prepared and very tasty. Looking forward to coming back soon.

I love this spot! We went on a dark and quiet night and practically had the place to ourselves. Aside from my boyfriend's pronunciation of the Shaking Beef (Shah-king beef) the meal was pretty much perfect, and the service impeccable. Amazing beef, and wondrous papaya salad. Can't wait to return.

I have yet to step foot into this restaurant, but I am writing this review because my husband always brings home a pie from this place when he' s on a job site. Â The pies he brings home are one of the best pies I have ever tasted. Â It's not soggy in the middle nor is it oily....does this tell you anything @ how delicious and fresh their pies are. Â I love the crispiness of the dough and it's never burnt at the bottom. I'm eventually going to make it here before the end of the year. Â This place is hands on tie with Lucali's for me.
What a treat to find such great gluten-free, organic food. It was hard to decide what to have because there were so many wonderful options. Food was delicious.
The best rice and peas in Brooklyn! Â They don't need to be friendly or quick. Â They do it their way because they can.

This place is fantastic! I like this location better than Union Square because it's bigger and a bit less hectic & crazy. Everything here is made fresh. Portions are big too. It's casual and the fact that you order at the counter makes it even more casual. Â Both locations have a cool wooden, country-like homey feel. I've been here for lunch and dinner and have ordered a variety of items. The salads are great, the sandwiches are massive and the soups are hearty. It's a bit more pricey than a cosi, panera or hale and hearty but it's worth it. Also, you can get a salad & soup combo like at one of those chain spots. The lunch rush is way more crowded than dinner, but the one time I did come for dinner, everyone was a bit more relaxed and let's just say "not on New York City time". Even with that being said, I'd wait for these meals. The classic country style salad is great. My top 2 sandwiches are the turkey, brie, tomato with raspberry mustard & the Cuban. I bet the breakfast is great too, but can't say I've had it. It's hard to not stare at the fresh baked cookies and pies when you're ordering too. Strange added bonus: they serve beer and wine too! Important to note: the line can be long, out the door especially during peak lunch hours!

What a great burger! I wasn't hugely optimistic about this place for some reason (why am I so skeptical all the time?) but I had a hankerin' for a beer and a burger one weekend afternoon and moseyed on in. I do like the wooden bar -- it's just an inviting place to belly on up and enjoy your burger and suds. There's table seating in the back for the families and groups. So, I ordered a strong IPA (good, medium sized beer list), a Two 8 Two burger, and a side of fries. The bartender was very friendly, took my order right away, and even though she was bs-ing with the waitstaff a lot, it wasn't annoying at all for whatever reason. I managed to get in a decent jab myself. No hard feelings? OK, so the food. When the burger arrived, I probably raised my eyebrows. It looked really good. The Two 8 Two burger has a hash of charred chiles, onions, and a savory sauce of some kind on the patty, with a bit of well melted cheddar acting as a kind of adhesive in between. It's not one of those freakishly large hamburgers, which is a big plus for me. You won't walk out wanting to kill yourself or cut the thing out of your belly with a knife. The beef patty, cooked to the requested medium, is actually fairly interesting. They obviously are very gentle when forming it, as it is pleasingly delicate -- almost crumbly, but not quite. I hope they don't neglect this technique, because it really makes the burger. They say they get daily deliveries of the ground beef from local butcher shop Los Paisanos, a personal favorite of mine. The roasted chiles and onions on the Two 8 Two burger work really well with the cheddar cheese, and don't make things soggy or anything like that. The mild heat is very pleasing and it's a great alternative to your standard lettuce-tomato-onion combo, which I actually plan to order next time, just because I reckon they do that right, too. The bun is a standard hamburger bun. NOT brioche. Why in the hell do people use brioche for hamburgers? Use a hamburger bun. Two 8 Two understands this, and they've selected a mighty fine hamburger bun to use. I guess some people aren't hot on the fancy fry toppings offered. I feel little sympathy, and it's a pity they're even on the menu. The only acceptable topping for fries is salt. (Unless you live in San Diego or Montreal.) I got the regular fries and they were really good. They are clearly made from fresh potatoes, fried in clean oil (I'm actually kind of sensitive to the oil stuff is fried in -- I can tell if it's old and nasty), and amply salted. They give you more than you should finish, but I let it slide, because I'm not the biggest dude and the cook may not have had the chance to eyeball me before cooking my portion. All in all, this is my burger joint in the neighborhood, and I've tried them all. It's really casual, the seating choices (bar, seating area, garden) are comprehensive, their burger is just terrific, the beer list is typically good for this neighborhood, and the service (at least the two times I've been there now) has been quite fast.

I have to try Five Points because I'm a fan of Hundred Acres and a fan of Cookshop, and by the law of association, I am sure I will be a fan of Five Points. But I digress... With an hour's notice we made an 8:00 dinner reservation and headed over to Cookshop. We checked ye olde Yelp for some recs on what to order. Clams? Check. Scallops? Check. Roasted duck too please. My friend doesn't even like clams. Although, I have to ask him if he likes afro clams (suggestive analogy courtesy of G.M.). He likes them now. Ended the meal with the banana sundae. At this time, we tried to figure out if we were sitting next to the cast of Glee. Not sure, but they did look happy.
Super nice coffee girl!! Food was well... edible. Burger wasn't so flavorful, although it was large and pretty! Fries were good, and my scone tasted like cornbread with a few blueberries in the mix.

We went in Sept 2013. It was awesome. Worth every penny. It really does live up to the hype. We did the 4-glass wine pairing and it was perfect. All the wines were so good. All the food was so good. It was just so good. I want to go back.

The white pizza was the best white pizza I've ever had. However the simplicity of the menu left us with very little options to choose from. The cheese calzone was not bad but it was a fun experience none the less.
Dinner was excellent. Â We split three courses for a leisurely dinner. The waiter clued in on exactly what we wanted. Â Service was supurb.

What can I say... I feel like the Bistro has lost its touch. Let me preface by saying that I used to come here on a regular basis, having lived in the neighborhood, whether for a quick lunch or a late-night snack. The burgers were always great, so much so that they didn't even need to be dressed up. The prices ($2 McSorley's? Yes please) can't be beat and I think we can all agree that CB is something of a NYC institution. Now, I feel like with all the volume (especially tourists) they just don't have to try as hard. Case in point, the burgers on Saturday night were atrocious. They arrived cold and unseasoned. Service was deplorable as well. We had to wait 7 minutes for a forgotten side of mayonnaise and our waiter barely even acknowledged us. Very sad, I hope they get their mojo back. I'm not coming back here for awhile.
great happy hour deals! the soft shell crab and rabbit rillette are amazing.

This place is good for latin fast food. The atmosphere is fun, the drinks are pretty good and they have a good happy hour menu that on certain nights is extended all night! They automatically provide plaintain chips with a house-made dipping sauce which is good enough to fill you up before you eat a deliciously fried empanada. I tried the portabella quesadilla and it was good. The guava empanada is also good, but it all felt really heavy. Go here and eat a lot when you have a long walk home so you can burn off all of the grease you've just eaten! I'll be back for a lighter meal and definitely the dim, cool atmosphere.
Worth wait for 2 hours. The ramen is amazing specially the soup. Also the pork burn is delicious.

Marc Forgione has great brunch! Nice decor, nice looking crowd, and awesome food. They had a good wine by the glass selection so we chose to do our own wine tasting by ordering six or eight glasses. That was fun. The waitress was very nice and the manager came by to talk about the wine. The food was very interesting and excellent. I really enjoyed the bone marrow. That was the first time I had had a szechuan button (it's hard to describe but it tingles in your mouth). One of my all time favorite places.

Today I saw a man lock his children in his car with the windows rolled up and wait 30 mins to get food from this halal cart. But having tried it myself I can't honestly say that I wouldn't have done the same thing.
Excellent food, small, relaxed and cosy atmosphere. Asparagus poached eggs are amazing!

I like this CafÃ© Gitane at Jane Hotel so much better than the other location in Nolita! It is a bit out of the way, but it has everything I like about a brunch place -- bright, spacious, vibrant, and a unique menu! This place was 90% full when we arrived around 12:50 pm last Sunday. I was still a bit surprised because it was such a cold and windy day, and people were still willing to venture here. I could imagine how packed it would be when the weather warmed up. It was supposed to be a Moroccan restaurant, but there were a painting and a sculpture of Buddha. It was not odd, but just interesting. I started with the cute Mocha, and ordered two small plates: avocado toast and Dukkha. The avocado toast was as good as what other people had raved about in the reviews. I saw the people at the neighboring tables adding some chili sauce to the avocado toast, so I also asked for it. The waitress told me that it was harissa. It had a nice kick and made the avocado toast taste better! The Dukkha was some bread served with a small bowl of crushed spiced nuts and a small bowl of olive oil. The nut mixture was aromatic! However, it was not easy to dip the nut mixture with the sliced baguette served. No matter how much olive oil I'd soaked the baguette with, the crush nuts still didn't stick.
