I ended up taking the remaining nut mixture home, and it tasted better with honey! My husband started with a banana smoothie and he liked it very much. He ordered a meat ball entree, and it was served in a tagine dish with the lid. It was very cool! I also tried the meatball and its spiced tomato sauce. Both were delicious. The service was attentive without being too pushy. The dining room was filled with a joyous, diverse crowd. This Jane Hotel must be very old, and the dÃ©cor of CafÃ© Gitane was a bit simple and outdated (maybe they did it on purpose). When the sunlight sprinkled in through the large windows, I was warm and content.

I order takeout from this place via Seamless all the time, and I had to leave a review this time because you truly learn how good a restaurant is when things don't quite work out! Â Seamless gave Potatopia the wrong address, so my order took over half an hour to arrive. Â When I called the restaurant, they first offered me a free replacement meal, and later helped me get in touch with the deliver-er (who was at the wrong location, because of the miscommunication through Seamless). Â The food was cold, but still delicious, and Potatopia was incredibly helpful with getting the problem quickly resolved! Â Love them!
Barely a three . The food wasnt consistant Â nor was the service on the next 2 visits.
Awesome Beer selection and the staff is super cool! Music isn't bad either :)

Bogota is great! Had an awesome afternoon pitstop while walking through the slope. The Domino empanada is outstanding! The michelada came highly recommended from the bartender Erin, and did not disappoint! Excellent service from the bar for drinks and food. Can't wait to go back.

I really enjoyed my veggie plate here. For $15, I got a large plate of mashed potatoes, asparagus, brussel sprouts (my favorite), broccoli rabe, and collard greens. I'd take this over pasta any day! We ordered goat cheese galettes to start- they were like turnovers with red pepper and goat cheese, served with greens (with a bit too much dressing). Also tasty! I saw a small roach on the wall, which put a damper on my meal, but I guess they're everywhere? This place is really tiny so make reservations before you come.

We dined at Tony's prior to seeing a Broadway show and had a wonderful experience. The waitstaff was very attentive and helpful, and the food was delicious. Our group of four decided to order three entrees plus a salad given that it's family style, and it was the perfect amount of food (including a little leftover to take home). We decided on the veal piccata, chicken parmesan, and a special order of tortellini alla vodka (it's on the menu with alfredo but they did it alla vodka for a small extra charge). Everything was very tasty! Â The veal was a little tough, but the sauce was very tasty. Â The tortellini was served al dente, which is a classic style but not my preference. Next time I'll ask for it to be cooked longer. Â Vodka sauce was pretty good, but not the best I've had. Â However, the chicken parm was delicious and HUGE. We'll be back!
A very chilled out place with a good selection of beer and good bar food. Nice deco, excellent service and spacious. Â Recommended if you are going with a group of people.

Let me tell you a little story. Â A few years ago, I moved to Connecticut from Los Angeles for graduate school. Â Two of my friends from home came to visit me, and we made a trip to NYC. Â On a rainy Wednesday afternoon we stumbled across a ramen place and decided to give it a try. Â This was one of the best decisions I have ever made in my life. Â The meat was so tender and juicy. Â It literally melted in my mouth. Â The broth was the perfect flavor and consistency, and the noodles were juuuuust right. Â I left floating on a cloud of ramen love. Â The only problem was, I didn't bother to remember the name of the place or where it was. Â Being from out of town, none of my friends did either. Â For months, I could not remember anything about the place besides how delicious the ramen was. Â I felt like the prince from Cinderella with nothing but a glass slipper to guide me. Â Then one night it came to me in a dream. Â "Take the 6 train to Astor Place." Â I jumped out of bed and googled "Astor Place, ramen" and Ippudo showed up on my screen. Â The search was over. Â I had found her. Â  Every time I am back in NY I make it a point to eat at Ippudo. Â I haven't found a ramen place like this anywhere else. Â This is certainly one of my favorite places in NYC. Â The only thing that prevents me from a 5 star rating is that the wait can be rather long. Â But, hey, nobody is perfect, right?
Excellent bourbon selection and the food was amazing. Â In particular, try the crispy duck and crispy brussel sprout with pig ear.

Crowded. A good place to catch up, have a conversation over wine and cheese as the service is slow. Overall they use fresh ingredients, everything was flavorful and well seasoned. The roasted brook trout and crispy polenta were amazing.

Boqueria is a great Spanish tapas place with two locations - in Flatiron and SoHo. Â It's the perfect date spot to share a couple different dishes and try something new over a glass or three of wine. Â Boqueria has a fun, young crowd and super helpful/knowledgeable servers if you're at a loss as to what wine or meat/cheese options to pick. Â We didn't have too much as we only stopped in for a quick bite but the meat and cheese plate, croquettas cremosas (creamy croquettes; three each of mushroom and Serrano ham), and cojonudo (fried quail eggs and chorizo on toast) were all delicious and definitely hit the spot. Can't wait to make a trip back to try more! @datenitenyc

My husband and I battle whenever we order burgers as to whether we should go. He is a huge fan of bareburger because he feels their beef burgers are incredibly well cooked. Their turkey burger is okay, but not as tender as I would like it to be. The elk my husband had he said was over done and chewy. The niche that bare burger has made for itself really lies within the variety that is available, you can choose from elk, vension, buffalo, beef, turkey, ostrich chicken, with innumerable topping choices and the fries come with five different dipping sauces. Each sauce is unique and offsets the different burgers in its own making every visit a unique one. However variety does not always equate to amazing. Overall a really good choice for a burger place.

It's been said this is the best undiscovered restaurant in New York City. I couldn't agree more. The menu is amazing. This is healthy & delicious food. Proof that not everything has to be fried or coated in sugar to be appetizing. The specials are always unique and affordable as well. This place actually introduced me to Freekeh, a middle eastern green wheat grain, which I now crave. It is small and easy to walk right past. I promise you - go there and this will become your "secret spot" too. But...psstt...let's try to keep it that way, okay? At least until they get a bigger place! Oh and, Fidel - I love you.

This great restaurant has Tibetan, Nepali and Himalayan menus. Â The atmosphere was really lively when I was there, lots of people out having a good meal and there is a full bar. Â The steamed Yak Momo were delicious - super juicy with a herbed meaty flavor. Â See the full Momo review at dumplinghunter.wordpressâ€¦.

Don't come here if you are looking for high quality authentic Italian cuisine. This restaurant is geared more towards tourists and the like. I would say the food is a couple steps up from an Olive Garden. Don't get me wrong, the food isn't bad but there are plenty of authentic Italian restaurants to visit before going to this one. What this place is good for is large groups because they have large tables and they also take reservations. The portions sizes of the dishes are huge and are meant to be shared. If you do come, I would recommend the penne ala vodka. As another reviewer mentioned, they put an abundance of garlic in their dishes. Luckily, I love garlic and my girlfriend doesn't mind my garlic infused breathe, however if you aren't a fan, then look elsewhere.

This place is heaven! Â I feel like I'm in Italy when I go here. There are different kinds of restaurants in this place. Ranging from pasta, fish, pannini, cappuccino, gelato, cheese & wine just to name a few. They also sell thousands of different kinds of olive oil, pasta sauces, pasta, meats, fish, and cute kitchen stuff that is very different and eclectic. You can easily spend hours here but it's definitely worth it!

5 stars for what it is--consistently good food at great prices! Found this place through yelp a few weeks back and it has become one of my go-to spots. Definitely a no frills type of place. and there's almost always a line no matter what time of day you come. BUT, its well worth the wait (which usually isn't that long anyway despite how it may look when its crowded inside) since the servers work fast...wait is definitely shorter than it looks like it would be. Anyway, onto the food--the most important part. Â I always get vegetable dumplings ($3 on a plate) and/or the sesame pancake sandwich ($1.50) with veggies. Â Delicious! I'm not vegetarian but prefer to eat veggie 80% of the time and this is definitely one the best veggie meals with great flavor, amazing prices, and good, filling portions. Â Sometimes, me and my bf will share a delishh huge steamed red bean bun (only $1) for dessert if we're feeling particularly gluttonous.

You can't beat the macarons from here, although be prepared to wait in line and be overwhelmed by choices. The rose flavor is delicious, but you can't go wrong with any. Be prepared to spend more money on macaroons than you will ever want to remember.

Been here at least 5 times, always satisfied; refined cooking, great selection of sakes ( literally the "sake cellar", Ichinokura Himezen and Kakurei, yay! ) Food (5/5) daily special soba set for a quick lunch and tasting menu for a slow lunch ~ dinner time star dishes (izakaya-like small dishes): a. kamo roast - tenderly roasted duck b. jidori shioyaki - tenderly (again) grilled chicken, dip it in the aromatic yuzu sauce c. gyutan - tender (yes, tender) beef tongue stew d. chawanmushi - tender (...) egg custard steamed in a cute cup filled with bite-sized goodies including a ginkgo nut e. others: grilled squid, firefly squid, inaniwa udon ( silky smooth for a change ), ochazuke, assorted sashimi, black sesame crÃ¨me brÃ»lÃ©e and sake manju or soba bun with matcha ice cream to finish, and certainly sake sake Ambience (4.5/5) intimate, carefully decorated with a relaxed courtyard feeling, very cute bathrooms Service (4.5/5) nice staff, always make reservations though sometimes you may obtain only 1hr window at the bar during peak hrs

This little (and I mean little) Gramercy Park/Union square restaurant is a must if you live in or are visiting NYC. I just went for my one year wedding anniversary and it was a fantastic experience and very romantic. The service was exceptional and they have a Sommelier on staff who helped us pick the perfect wine in our price range. They also opened a few bottles of Cava to ensure that the one we picked we would enjoy. This restaurant is exciting because everyone knows Mario Batali but it is not traditional Spanish style tapas, expect for those things that you usually don't find on a tapas menu. For example, razor clams, oxtails, tripe, chopitos (baby cuttle fish) duck egg, sweetbreads, bone marrow and it goes on and on. The ambience is beautiful with wine bottles lining each wall, soft glow lightening, candles and a view of the kitchen. Everyone should consider this place but bring the credit card, pricey but worth it!

Absolutely some of the best food I have ever had. The combinations of tastes on each plate will make any mouth happy. If you like different foods with excellent combinations of flavors and textures, you must try MOMOFUKU. YUM
This place SUCKS. How come are the reviews so good? The coffee is bad, the crepes are bad, the tea is bad. Freaking disgusting. Try CafÃ© Gitane if you want real food.

Don't be afraid of the long wait, it is absolutely worth it! I came here for dinner and there was about a 20 minute wait but that was fine since I was really anticipating the pancakes. We ordered the blueberry pancakes, buffalo wings and some fried fish dish that i can't seem to recall the name of. The pancakes are so warm and fluffy and when soaked in the warm maple butter it is absolutely divine! The fried fish was really good but the fried kale that it was served with was sorta gross... maybe I'm just not used to my veggies being fried and served all greasy. The buffalo wings were delicious with the blue cheese. On another occasion I came for the waffles and those were delicious as well. I've tried both flavors of the pancakes and I prefer the banana walnut more since the blueberries were much too sour for me but still good! I really enjoy this place and am dying to try the other dishes on the menu. Ingredients are very fresh and the service here is decent albeit a bit slow. Come here and your expectations of what good pancakes should taste like will completely change!

the food is great as is the service...... But the manly lady manager, is awful!!! She has a horrid attitude and the way she spoke to us was above and beyond rude,,, so much so that we are not coming back. We gave her the benefit of doubt once and came back, but this time no way. No one should be spoken to this way. What a jerk.!!
Had a half a pound of pulled pork, and half a pound of the brisket. Â Also 3 sides. Â And then I wanted to shoot myself for eating so much. These guys can bet I'll be back again.

I have such a love/hate relationship for this place. On one hand, their food is pretty amazing. Their grilled corn is something I always dream about and go back to, feeling very satisfied and happy. The desserts are always worth a try - Grape kool aid ice cream being my favorite. I also love their homemade donuts! Their fried zucchini sandwich is good but with a bit of hot sauce, it's even better. The hush puppies with ranch dip is amazing. My friends raved about their chicken baskets. Here's my issue with them: their hours are so wonky. Sometimes they are closed for events (which we find out by calling them first because we are a bit cautious). They are closed on Mondays. They close right after lunch on Sundays. I went by the day after Labor Day, a Tuesday, at around 6:30 (they close and reopen at 6pm supposedly to serve dinner) in the pouring rain and they were closed! I love you guys, but you're not a food truck and I wish you would stick to normal scheduling. It's also a bit hard to trust a place of business that uses a blogspot as their main website, but I still go back for the delicious grilled corn and treats. Hopefully they will last because they have great food to back them up.

Whilst scheduling a fun happy hour get together for friends, I used my handy dandy Yelp app to see if I could get some listings for well rated spots in the West Village for the event. Â "The Malt House" showed up as a top contender, and I dug the look of their menu and the old, wooden bar look of the interior (based on pictures from their web site). Â Thinking this would just be a fun loving, care free gathering, I quickly discovered I had made a mistake. You see, The Malt House is insanely popular. Â I walked in around 4:30pm (my friends were arriving around 5ish) and the first thing I noticed is that despite me being only one of ten people in the entire bar, every single table had already been reserved. Every. Single. One. This meant most of the folks were at the bar, so I quickly snagged three seats (the only ones available) and held them (making sure to order eats and enough drinks for a few people to justify holding the seats). Â The staff was very nice and easy going and they were totally cool with me holding the chairs. Â When I told them I was ordering a few drinks to justify it they laughed and told me not to worry about it. Â Definitely a cool vibe. Fast forward to about 35 minutes later and the place was almost completely full. Â Literally wave after wave of people just kept pouring in, with more people seated and waiting outside. Â I repeated a few times in the evening that I really wish I had made a reservation and would do so next time. It is worth mentioning that despite having music pumping through speakers on the walls, the volume did not overwhelm attempts at conversation. Â I did not find myself screaming at friends to be heard, a big plus in my book. The Happy Hour menu at The Malt House is pretty darn spectacular. Â Beers are generally about $4, mixed drinks laid out on the Happy Hour menu are about $5 and their gastropub oriented small bites are $5. Â For my drinks, I tried the Bluepoint Toasted Lager and Malthouse Amber, both on tap. Â I much preferred the Lager which had a more forward flavor than the Amber. Â The Amber was light and more of a refreshment along the lines of a soda pop. Â I also had the "Whiskey Business" (see what they did there?) which was reminscent of a very sweet incarnation of the classic "Godfather" drink. Â The servings of the "well" drinks were respectable, not too big, not too small - just right for $5. The food was pretty darn tasty too. Â My friends had the burgers (really kind of slightly oversized sliders) and both friends reported that they enjoyed them a lot. Â I ordered the french fries which came in a fun paper bag serving (as if to emphasize the grease) and man, the curried ketchup that came with them was awesome! Â I also got to eat an order of their wings, which were tasty but not too hot, more on the sweet/smokey side. I'm glad I checked out The Malt House this time. Â I'm definitely planning to go back, but next time I'm making a reservation!

Dinned here on a Thursday night, the wait for a party of 2 was about an hour long. The complementary italian bread with butter was great to start off with. Since everything is served family style, we shared the chicken parmasen and baked ziti bolognese. The chicken parmasen was delicious, it had a nice crust that wasn't too breaded and a sweet marinara sauce. The baked ziti bolognese was also delicious, it was baked to perfection with a nice blend of cheeses and meats. We ended up taking more than half of the meal to go, it still tasted just as great when we reheated it up.

best deal in the city! 5 course for $55 with great portions and quality. their menu changes quite often but i am sure that the texture, balance of flavor and originality will exist in every creation. my fave was the dessert. their popular bread pudding. i'm in love! can't wait to go back!
If you're gonna eat street meat it has to be here. Â This guys has the best truck in town! Â If you don't believe me, go check out the trophy for yourself. Â Best $6 you can spend.

Great Times Square lunch options are far and few between. Margon is a great spot that's filled the void. It's by no means a fancy restaurant, just your typical good old fashioned Cuban food spot. From the outside, it looks like a small place, but once you get inside you can see that the seating goes deep into the back of the establishment, where the kitchen is nestled. The portions here are very generous, to some it's HUGE. You order at the end of the long counter. It can get pretty jammed up, because sometimes there are two or three people that are taking orders simultaneously. If you're that guy that's looking at the board to decide your order while you have 20 people behind you, you'll get some dirty looks. Be sure to have done your research or stand aside until you know exactly what you will be eating. Once you get your order and beverage (there's various sodas and beer available), you take your tray and seat yourself. When at the table, don't forget to generously apply the homemade hot sauce that's on the table in the yellow squirt bottle. I love the fact that there are daily specials. For example, Friday there's Oxtail which I got with red beans over yellow rice and a side of plantains. The oxtail is served on its own platter. The meat is very tender and literally slides off the bone. The rice, beans, and plaintains are on a separate dish. You'll love the sauce so much that all of it is gonna end up over the rice anyways. You can also get white rice or the dirty one, which is basically black beans mixed with white rice. Another great special is Margon's octupus salad that's sliced cooked octupus mixed with peppers, onions and vinegar. It's served in a small bowl, but it packs alot of flavor. This one goes best with white rice and black beans. Another plus is that they also offer delivery. I wish they opened after work, then I'd be going here twice as much. This is the best Cuban food in the area. I recommend checking out Margon at least once. If you think Sophie's is the and all and be all, think again.

Pricey for Falafel, but completely worth it. Â Honestly, all the food here is excellent, including the drinks! Â The falafel is authentic and the best I've ever had, and the french fries are some of the best I've ever had (they come with saffron aioli which is very tasty, though unnecessary). Â The sides are healthy and delicious -- all of them! Â I usually get the cucumber salad, the cabbage, the beets, or the tabouleh. Â  If it's your first time, try the sampler plate with fries and ginger-mint lemonade. Â The place is very popular, gets very busy, and is tiny. Â It has a small bar against the window that fits 4 or 5 crammed-in stools, with a few benches outside for warm weather, so plan on taking out (or ordering if you live in the West/Greenwich Village area).

Gosh this was extremely impressive. I was floored when I entered Eataly. Walking around the ginormous space made me so excited and happy. There's something for everyone's palette. My husband and I put our name down for pasta eatery which was an hour wait at the time, then we headed to the cheese bar section. I ordered the charcuterie and cheese board with some beer to past the time. Everything on the board was fantastic! Some of the best charcuterie I've ever had. When they finally called us for the pasta eatery, I was almost full from the appetizer so we shared the short rib pasta. Boy, oh boy...it was quite the treat! Perfectly cooked pasta with well-seasoned short rib. Top 5 best pasta dishes I've tasted.
food is quite good and it's a nice setting, but the mediocre, inattentive service was surprising. Â and not my kind of scene - lots of bankers in their early 30s with their blond girlfriends.

I had a group of 8 people here for my birthday brunch. The whole experience was perfect. The atmosphere is unbelievable, as Claire says (below), it reminded both of us of our trips to Guatemala. There is also exposed brick everywhere, and there are French doors at the back that open to a gorgeous garden and fountain. There was a lovely elevated nook thing that sat 8 of us perfectly. Our server was so friendly and immediately brought us mimosas as we browsed the menu. Most of us opted for the poached egg, which came with grilled bread (!!), black beans, avocado, and chipotle hollandaise sauce. The mimosas were also amazing- made with fresh-squeezed OJ. Yes. I absolutely cannot wait to come back. I want to bring everyone I know. It's a perfect spot to bring parents, perfect for a date, perfect for a party, perfect in every way. They also only use ingredients that were either grown on their roof garden, purchased at the Grand Army Plaza farmers market, or raised locally (meat). And you can taste it.

Their regular and beef soondubu is really good! However, their seafood tofu soup was a bit off. Tasted like it wasn't seasoned right. Also, I wouldn't order their tofu/kimchi dish as the tofu comes out burnt. I would definitely return for their regular tofu soup or for their two person meat thing (bossam) but I am not so sure about the other dishes. Also note- like any other place with decent food, this place can be quite a wait during dinner. Either go early like at 5PM or make reservations.

What I've Had: Rubirosa Supreme Pizza Would I go Back?: Most definitely Story: Came here during the San Genarro festival in Little Italy. Service was good but the Pizza was the star here. Probably some of the best pizza i've ever had. Thin crust and all the ingredients on the pie were perfectly flavorful and melded great together.

The menu is very simple and they describe what is on each different burgers, fries, etc. I ordered the Cali Burger and my friend ordered the Manly Burger. For appetizers we got the truffle fries and tempura onion rings. For drinks we got the Tropical Green Tea. For dessert we got a cinnamon chocolate chip ice cream donuts! (I think the dessert change every now and then) We got four different sauces to go with our appetizers, two are spicy and two aren't (one being ketchup). The sauces are so good, especially the orange one! The tempura onion rings aren't like regular onion rings, their skin aren't a thick layer but thin. The truffle fries were good too, especially with sauce if you don't want to taste too much cheese. Eating my burger got really messy because the juice soaked the bottom buns. If you don't want to eat something messy, you should get the manly burger. Both burgers were really good nonetheless. The patty wasn't hard like regular burgers, it was soft and easy to eat which I love! The cinnamon chocolate chip ice cream donut was good, however the donut might be a little hard since it's cold.

Num Pang is actually a small chain of 4 locations at this point, it's a Cambodian (near identical to Vietnamese "Banh Mi") sandwich place but they also have a few soup/salad/side options. They have about a dozen sandwich choices, prices range from $8-9.50 and they're cash only. One great feature is that nothing on their menu is fried. The procedure at this location is you order from a window outside, wait for your number to be called, then head up the spiral staircase to the very small seating area (or head over to Union Square if it's nice out). The oddest moves is that there is no customization of sandwiches whatsoever. I was a little concerned as every sandwich is topped with cucumber, chili mayo, carrots, and cilantro and I'm not a fan of cucumber and mayo. They know best though, I couldn't really taste either. The cucumber just added a little fresh crunch to the texture while the small amount of mayo just added a little extra moisture. They load up on carrots which I love, it adds a sweet crunch that you normally don't find in sandwiches. All sandwiches are made on the same 8" slightly toasted roll. The bread is amazing. It's just crusty enough on the outside and soft on the inside. Â  Me and my roommate split two sandwiches, the peppercorn catfish with sweet soy sauce and the mahi mahi with leeks and Thai basil olive oil. The piece of catfish was pretty thin and between the bread and all the carrots and whatnot the fish got lost in the mix. It was a delicious sandwich but the fillet just couldn't stand up to the challenge of being the star of the show. The mahi mahi on the other side was one of the best sandwiches I've ever had. They give you a real generous piece of fish, cooked and seasoned to perfection. It was so amazing that I might go back tomorrow for a second. If fish isn't your thing other options include: Hoisin meatballs w/ jasmine rice, stewed tomatoes, and basil Coconut shrimp Pulled pork w/ spiced honey Pork belly w/ spices and pickled Asian pear Bbq brisket w/ ginger and pickled red cabbage Khmer sausage w/ Asian slaw Roasted Chicken Chimi w/ pickled apples Grilled steak w/ peppercorns and coriander and for the vegetarians: Roasted cauliflower w/ eggplant spread Grilled portabello w/ leeks and a beet vinaigrette Spicy tofu w/ leeks and a ginger soy honey glaze
Best Banh Mi in Brooklyn!! I ordered #1 and avocado shake. Delicious! Can't wait to come back FOR MORE!

Very nice lounge type of atmosphere. Â Food was pretty good. Â Unfortunately place gets pretty busy over the weekends and they weren't able to accommodate our birthday part properly even though we had a reservation. Â At the end, we all enjoyed our food but had a slight bitter taste due to the hassle of getting seated.
Not sure what all the hoopla is about. Had the sisig (signature dish) and a few others. Very greasy. Waiters looked like lost kids who accidentally wandered into a restaurant. Cute decor though.

To be honest, I was quite disappointed. Maybe because of all the good reviews, I anticipated a lot, only to be disappointed. I made reservations for 2 on a Sunday night, and they were really nice calling me twice to confirm and everything and even emailed me their current menu. Actually that night was full, but it was not packed. So we had the strawberry glazed ribs, nothing to awe about, the meat inside had no taste at all and it was a bit dry. Then we had the pork belly, which was nothing spectacular either, it only taste good because it was pork belly but without the fat, it tasted like dry meat once again. The lobster risotto was the only thing I believed that was on point, but I believe the cheese did its job. Then the shrimp... honestly it taste a bit like sweet and sour shrimp from a Chinese restaurant to me. I brought my friend there thinking to show her my good taste, I only did the opposite, I really do not understand the hype over this restaurant. For the price I pay is ok, but to go all the way to Williamsburg just for this, never again.

This is the sort of place you wouldn't look twice at. But oh, how wrong you'd be. The service is quick, and the food is what American fast food should be - hot, savory deliciousness but with real ingredients, not pink slime. The sauce is something you could literally put on anything; the rice has the same consistency as sushi rice, but without the vinegary taste; the protein I had on top of the rice was deep-fried to perfection. This really is a place you need to eat at.

The brunch is definelty Â a good one. The attitude of Cheryl and another woman who works there is unreal. Patronizing, rude, uninviting, nasty...ive experienced this and also witnessed the treatment to others. I started thinking she thought customers were bothersome and that she was doing us a favor. Whatever goodness there is in the food is diminished by the owner's attitude, almost entirely.
French fries are tasty, lamb sausage is great. Turkish coffee smells good, I will come back and try it.

Delicious dinner - the mushroom cigar and filet were out of this world, wine reduction on the steak was perfectly done. Great service. Will def go back. Super cozy, nice atmosphere. Food was well thought out and yummy.

There is 2 parts to this place, there is a restaurant, and there is a small bakery section with seating to grab a piece of cheesecake and sit down. Â There is also another bakery spot around the corner by the theaters. We just wanted a piece of cheesecake for breakfast, and it was the best cheesecake Ive ever had. We ordered a piece of plain and a piece of fudgy chocolate cake cheesecake. They were both amazing.
Great Burger! Just open a month a go! Nice employee so far!! ;) They serve breakfast too! A lot of choices! Cold and hot sandwiches plus vegetarian sandwiches! Nice place!

Loved this place! I cannot believe how reasonably priced you can get amazing ramen for. Â Loved the spicy ramen and pork buns. Â Service was quick. Â We came at just the right time and had our pick of seats. Â The space is totally adorable. Staff was nice. Â Can't wait to go back!

The question needs to be asked: why would you go to a place that you qualify as 'quiet' and bring 10 of your friends? It's people like this who ruin atmospheres at places that used to be wonderful, where you could hear yourself think and your interlocutor speak, where you weren't drowned out by riotous laughing and incessant toasts from the big table. If the place is small, intimate and quiet, please please bring your parties elsewhere (if you think you are quiet when there are 11 of you celebrating something, you are sorely mistaken.)

I came here for restaurant week and for once I ordered off the RW menu. Everything here was delicious. The RW menu was a great value, especially in combo with the Foursquare discount. Watermelon salad - light and refreshing. This was my first time eating yellow watermelon. Grilled brook trout with green bean casserole - Very moist and flaky fish with nicely done green beans and crispy onions. Raspberry ice cream sandwich - delicioso.
Roast Duck w/ Chinese broccoli... MMMMMMMMMMMMMMMMMMMMMMMMMMMMMMMMMMMMMMMMMMMMMM oily, salty, and delish *heart*

Quaint outdoor dining spot. Had the grilled calamari for an appetizer, which has potential to have the consistency of a rubberband they wrap around broccoli, yet this was absolutely delicious. For our mains, my boyfriend had the ravioli and I had the evenings special. Both dishes were filled with flavor and I had to stop my bf from licking the remaining sauce off his plate. Waiters are really cool, all fluent in italian. Something little, yet appreciated. Definitely would go back.
Good prix fixe meal, good service, good prosecco. My only complaint is that Pink Floyd's album The Wall was playing in a loop. That was annoying.

I don't know what to say here. On one hand, its not as good as the places back in LA, on the other hand, I havent had it in so long that it tasted really really good. Nice decor, good service, the tofu was good. I wish they also served the rice in a hot stone pot but I guess thats pretty troublesome good. The banchan was alright, not too bad but nothing blew me away. All in all if I'm craving soondobu I'd probably come here until I find somewhere better. Highly recommend :)

Hooray that this exists and hooray that it exists in Greenpoint! Â  I got a lobster roll and salad, but I should have gotten fries. Â They looked great. Â I ordered the Connecticut Lobster Roll which is the butter (not mayo) kind. Â Loved it. Â Had lobster rolls at some of the world-renowned places in Maine just weeks before having my roll here at Lobster Joint and was quite satisfied. Â  My friend got the Mahi-Mahi sandwich, which didn't really make sense to me, but she loved it. Â So, good. Â  The service was pretty awful. Â She did the thing where you stand there politely in front of her for seemingly endless minutes while she completely ignores you. Â It became clear that, since I was just a lady without a hot beard, I was going to have to make an effort to get any acknowledgement. Â However, the beauty of counter-service is that I just moved on, got cozy with my friend, and ate good grub. Prices are high, but also what you'd expect. Â I recommend.
Fantastic food, a great location, knowledgeable staff, a speakeasy decor, reasonably priced for the CITY = you have to check out Parker & Quinn

With a cocktail list good enough to make one pause, and bar tenders cool enough to make one feel in the know- this bar has moved quickly up a very formidable list of LES bars to frequent. I advise you to go- and don't be afraid to be hungry, the bar food is great as well!

Perhaps it was the high expectations. But I would most definitely rank the Burger Joint higher than the Corner Bistro. Â There was a great charred-ness to the rather large Corner Bistro burger, but there were one too many raw onions. Ultimately, I prefer the succulence and the not-so-subtle greasiness of the Burger Joint burger. Quality wins out against quantity yet again.

My sister lives in the neighborhood, and we had only intended to stop into Alta for a quick bite and a glass of wine, but ended up staying much longer than originally planned. Â Great ambiance, a lively, young crowd, and a flamboyant, entertaining bartender that kept us laughing as we washed down our first tapas with Rioja at the bar. Our one mistake was leaving our roomy spot at the bar, thinking a table would offer us a more desirable location. Â The hostess transferred us to a table sandwiched into this back corner of a small upstairs room, adjacent to a rowdy crowd of 12+ guys enjoying what I considered to be a "guys night." Â My sister and I pretty much had to shout over their obnoxious laughter to be heard by each other. Â However, we figured we'd make the best of it, and order some tapas since we were already warm, seated, and very hungry. Â The bacon wrapped olives and dates were a small portion, but sooo good, as were the fried goat cheese balls. Â The chicken was a little hard to share, I'd recommend to eat that solo. Â But great wine selection, and overall the experience was favorable - the credit I attribute to the hilarious bartender and the tapas, not the seating.

Honestly, I have nothing but positive things to say about this restaurant! Yes, there is always a line and the likelihood is you'll have to wait--but the wait is well worth it. The atmosphere is bustling with an extremely cheery and attentive staff. From the hosts to the waiters to the chefs cooking our meals right in front of us (free entertainment)--the place just exuded a celebratory vibe. And the food is unbelievably good. We started our meal off with the Hirata Buns--basically an ever so soft, texturally fascinating bun with pork belly (can't go wrong), lettuce, and a little spicy mayo sandwiched in between. Tremendous. Afterwards, both my fiancÃ©e and I (who are spice fiends), predictably chose the Karaka Men--ramen in a broth enhanced with spicy miso, simmered pork belly, and a poached egg. Truly the best ramen I've had to date with everything cooked perfectly and an incredible depth of flavor. Easily recommend this place for a date night or for small parties. Definitely not the place for larger groups as the wait will be quite long.

i stopped in here for lunch because of all the great reviews and it was a tasty treat indeed! Â  i was at a meeting over on 4th ave and hustled to get here on my hour lunch break. Â the lady was super friendly and the place was cute. Â and it was fast enough to make it back, eat outside and write this reveiw! i got the #1 which was delicious. Â and an iced coffee which is strong just the way i like it. Â i will definitely consider hustling there again the next time work brings me to this neck of the woods. and i recommend it to you! Â  plus sandwich and coffee were 6.75. Â i say thats a pretty good deal.

This review is STRICTLY for their foie gras donut and nothing more! That donut is so out of control it needed a review all its own. While at the Great Googamooga festival in Brooklyns prospect park, we were in the mood for dessert. We came across do or dines foie gras donut. My bfs bright idea. How bad can it be he said, it sounds like a crazy combo that sounds delicious he said. Okay whatever, I'm game for trying any food once or twice. Now, the donuts looked amazing, and the jelly/jam in the middle looked delicious. It was basically a sugar donut with a foie gras jam, it couldn't be bad!, no way, the jam looked too good! I bit into it. I tasted the Sugar donut part first. Â "MMMM"! I yelled, it's good! Oh, wait. Here it comes, here comes the foie gras jelly taste. I held it in my mouth to be polite and smiled at the guy serving the donuts. I turned around and gave my bf and the couple we were with a horrified look. I passed the donut to my bf and let him have a bite. As we walked away I had to dispose of what was in my mouth because it had to be the worst combination I have ever tasted. It literally tasted like vomit. You know when you have spit - up in your mouth, that taste you get in the back of your throat? Â Yea, exactly what it tasted like. I felt bad for the couple we were with, we made them get one too lol. All i wanted was a frozen chocolate dipped banana, but I'm glad I tried it. I like trying new things but this was just too much. I will most definitely be trying the actual restaurant because the food looks awesome! Update coming soon. Kudos for making this donut, but just not for me!.

Very nice atmosphere, interior, Euro-shabby chic dressed waitstaff, etc. Party of three arrived at 9 pm on a Saturday night for dessert and drinks. Were told by Borat the maitre'd we would have to wait 15 minutes for a table. Stood by bar for 45 minutes, watching several parties of better dressed people be seated. Were pitied by bus boy and one waiter, who gave us some nuts to nibble while we waited. Everyone was gracious and nice. Finally seated with our drinks, ready to order. When he discovered we only want to order dessert, Borat informs us that only dinner is being served but we do have the option of "the sofa," saying with a slick smile "You can stay there all night." Not being the bitchy type, we blithely followed him over to a small sofa tucked behind the Fooz-ball table, in front of a window so drafty we put our jackets back on. There was no table in front of said sofa so we awkwardly held our drinks or had to turn around to put them on the chilly windowsill. (Did I mention it was cold?) Luckily, Borat came to our rescue and brought us a CHAIR to use as a table. A CHAIR. As in the thing one's derriere touchs, not generally used for food consumption. Laughing at the absurdity of the suddenly terrible service we were receiving, we quickly ordered 2 desserts (which tasted fine), paid our bill, and walked past Borat, who cowardly averted his gaze as we walked past him. The food looked delicious and I'm sure if you were ordering a full meal you will enjoy yourself. And if you're looking to sit on a frigid sofa balancing your plate in your lap like family Thanksgiving at Grandma's, ask for the VIP sofa seating.

So believe it or not, this place will cater. Â We had Uncle Gussy's for office lunch and it was one of the best office lunches we've had. Â I've been on my own to the truck and thought it was good, but when we had a buffet of everything that Uncle Gussy's makes, it was really tasty. Â Feta - good, salad - good, french fries - good, dolmadas - good, lamb - good! The only thing was that they forgot the pita so he had to go back and it took another 20 minutes for him to come back with some warm pita before we could dig in.

This place is okay. The pizza is okay. The drinks are okay. The atmosphere is okay. I've been here a few times, and every time I feel like they think they're doing me a favor by allowing me to eat here. Honestly. You want to do me a favor? Don't charge so much for mediocre pizza. THAT would be a favor. THAT would be MORE than okay. But, for now: This place is okay.

Like many other BBQ lovers who have traveled throughout the country, I was sure I knew what great brisket was. But my first visit to Delaney BBQ gave me a new perspective on the experience. Descriptions like " succulent" or" melt in your mouth" sort of fit here, but cannot really convey just how delicious and rewarding my meal was. I choose equal portions of fatty and lean cuts, a half pound in total. As I watched the carving of one beautiful steaming brisket, with perfect smoke ring and pepper crusting, I was thinking that my trek to Brooklyn was about to pay off. I chose coleslaw as a side and added few slices of white bread, and found a seat. I lifted my plate to breath in the glorious aroma and began to sense that this was going to be special. My first mouthful gave a rush of flavor that I knew would set a new hallmark for all of my future BBQ life. I love this brisket and Delaney BBQ is a great place to enjoy it. The restaurant is casual, comfortable and charming, and the staff genuinely conveys your that you are very welcome here. Put Delaney BBQ on your gotta-do list, right at the top.

ABSOLUTELY MY FAVORITE STEAMED DUMPLINGS EVER. My trusty foodie friend introduced me to this place a few years ago via his frozen dumplings that I would cook and eat ravenously during his frequent house parties. I instantly fell in love with their savory with just enough juicy sweetness flavors. They were ridiculously porky and chivey and chewy and pungent - my perfect dumpling. Of course, the vinegar and Sriracha added a different and equally as delicious angle to the experience. I came to the physical plant many months later, and now, every time I'm in Chinatown, I will make it a point to stop by this place. My boyfriend is as obsessed with the quality of the dumplings here, and whenever he's in town, we always go for a quick lunch or snack. The large order of dumplings for $3 is unbeatable, and I often pair it with the noodles with peanut sauce - It's an explosion of flavor and texture in your mouth. The bag of 50 dumplings for $9 is almost even more mind-blowing. They're the best frozen dumplings I've ever had and always come in handy when I'm too lazy or busy to cook. I haven't tried any other items on the menu, but my boyfriend's had the fish balls, which were pretty yummy. As far as the decor and setting, it's not aesthetically pleasing. Really bare with glaring artificial light, but I appreciate the utilitarian aspect and reasoning behind it. Besides, most of their customers are locals looking for a comforting, satisfying, and fast meal. Part of me hopes this place will gain the recognition it deserves, but part of me is just fine with people continuing to pour into Vanessa's Dumplings. Either way, they're missing out.

just came from peaches, my stomach is still aching from the so called turkey meatloaf. it was made mostly of bread tasted no turkey. Â it was more like 2 pieces of bread with a wee bit of gravy. then there was the roasted beets salad. yes there were beets but roasted. wrong ! this was compounded by the mistake i made of eating out doors where the faint ordor of doggy doo could be detected. the only thing that was any good was the red stripe beer. nice n smooth & the waiter was very pleasant. i would rather eat at mcdonalds.

Oh My God, I would eat here everyday if I could. Good variety of choices, and a good value. The buffet is a typical Brazilian "por kilo", pay by the pound set up. It's less if you don't get the meat, there is still plenty of meat on the buffet. This is my preferred dining style, you saddle up, and pick what looks good depending on your level of hunger and budget. No menus, no waiting, it's perfect for kids. Super friendly Brazilian staff. The food is very authentic home cooking, which seems to represent several different geographical areas of Brazil. We come here ever time we are in the NYC area, and I have never been disappointed with anything I've tried. Pretty much my favorite restaurant in the world at this point!

Do they spike their free cheese balls with something? Cuz damn they are delicious! Not sure what it was, but those cheese balls are on point. Oh yeh, drinks are cool too. They only had one pool table and the lines for the bathrooms were long. Friendly bartenders, cool drinks and I love how they display their drink menu...where everyone can see! Caution: did get a wiff of some BO every now and then, but the cheeseballs made up for it.
The namesake artichoke slice is like a greasy orgasm in your mouth. Amazing. One star off though for there being nowhere to eat though; the place is tiny!

$7 lunch special is a good deal for the area: Â 2 appetizers (more like sides) and an entree. Â There is a decent selection and the entree portions are pretty big. Â Definitely a good value. Â My boyfriend and I were both really, really thirsty during/after the meal because I think the food was on the salty side. Â But overall, it was good. And the restaurant is really nice and comfortable and the bathroom is pretty cool. Â Can't really go wrong.

Not bad... not bad at all I told myself, I said ''Nadia, you are at a burger place, have a burger and a beer''. Â Well, despite my reluctance to have a complete burger (yes, because of the calories), I tried one!! Â It was a cheeseburger with bacon... and it was good! Â Of course, I am not sure how a burger with cheese and bacon could ever NOT be good, but anyway. Â Considering how little I eat burgers, I cannot fairly compare it to other places.. but it tasted good so I say thumbs up. Â As for the drinks.. I could not bring myself to have beer - I have yet to acquire that taste... but I did have bloody Marys - which were sub-par. Â All-in-all it wasnt a bad place, the service was OK (could be better), the burgers were good, and the drinks were OK. Â Perhaps if I had drank the appropriate beer, it would have been better.

I don't think I will ever get bored of going to Freeman's... it's pretty perfect in every way. Great food, great cocktails (best Hot Toddy in the city), great decor, great vibe and great service - and you get it all at a reasonable price. Oh... and best brunch I've had. Artichoke dip, skillet eggs and the pancakes are a must. And the Hot Toddy! =)

There is normally a long wait on weekends for brunch, but the food is worth the wait! Â  You have to come prepared ready to do some pretty heavy eating, but the food is delicious. Â We ordered the chocolate peanut butter milkshake which was creamy, fresh, and delicious. Â Then we ordered the fried deviled eggs because we've never heard of that before. Â Those were awesome, as well. Â To eat we ordered the tater tot bowl which was everything tasty put in a bowl together. Â Great for a hangover. Â My boyfriend got the pulled pork bowl with eggs on top, which was pretty great as well, but we both preferred the tater tot bowl.

If you are claustrophobic you might not like this place. As NY spaces go this place is tiny. If you can get passed that, then first order the corn. YUM!!! You might want to share because it turns out you get two corn on the cob for the price of 1. After that everything on the menu is pretty delicious. Cafe Habana was one of my favorite spots for brunch. The best time to go is a week day but if you have to choose a weekend it would be Saturday. On Sunday that place is a zoo. You get all the party goers for the night before craving the corn and their Cuban dishes. Also on a weekend expect to wait a bit, as your party gets bigger you'll be waiting longer. So be warned.

We had a perfect meal. Between two people we ordered a kale salad, 2 apps , 2 entrees and shared a dessert and everything was wonderful. The food combinations were inventive but worked and the menu seemed well curated. The service was just ok but saved by a person who I think was the manager who did the little thoughtful things and noticed when people were looking around for help. The tables are close together which is annoying or gives it a hip european cafe vibe depending on who you are. Portions are not huge and prices are not low but the food is fantastic and we left in a great mood. I would highly recommend Northern Spy for a low key romantic dinner with a loved one or a kick ass 3rd date spot.

If you're in Astoria, you have no excuse to not come to Sanford's. Â It is open 24 hours. Â Their menu is huge and varies from all sorts of appetizers, pasta, salads, burgers, paninis. Â I have tried the turkey burger with fries, a grilled shrimp Caesar salad, and pasta. Â I enjoyed the food each time I went. Â The venue is really nice and has big roomy booths. Â What I appreciated was how quickly the food came. Â There's also a bar in the back. Â Also you can't beat how cheap the food is here. Â The omelette is a standard price and you can add any topping you want. Â The pasta comes in a huge plate and could probably be shared by two people. Â I highly recommend this place! Â Call ahead of time because sometimes it gets really packed.

I love this little place! It seats about 15 - 20 people MAX and it gets packed pretty quickly. We strolled here on a Sunday morning ready to fuel ourselves before a long day of shopping, and the wait was about 20 minutes for a group of 5. The waiter went the extra step in making sure that he updates us whenever the previous tables finished eating or when they were done paying their bill etc. It always makes a different when someone goes that extra mile to make sure that the guests feel important. The food was amazingly done. I loved their home style potatoes and the salad that came with our scrambled eggs. Everything was cooked to perfection. We also ordered the creamed cauliflower soup and the strawberry, banana, nutella baguette to start, and oh my, it was a party in my mouth. All in all, a fabulous brunch experience. Friendly service and good hearty brunch food, I really couldn't have asked for more.

Amazing restaurant, great service, beautiful food. Will definitely be returning. This time I will bring family. My guest and I were surprised that the restaurant did not gain a Michelin Star! Tip: have fingerling potatoes, they are amazing.

Im used to going to the original location on Northern blvd in Queens but decided on this location for lunch with a group of friends. The decor inside is really interesting. Definitely has a more upscale vibe than Northern blvd. And the service seems to be better as well. The bartender and our waiter were the best! Now the food was amazing. ..normally I get the Matador combo..but this time I ordered the Jalea. I ordered the small and Im glad I did. I shared this with a friend and we each had two full servings, and their were still leftovers.The seafood was fried perfectly and wasnt greasy. We also ordered the plantains and rice and beans and they great as well. Our group shared pitchers of sangria and that was very good too..a bit sweet for me but enjoyable. Will definitely return..
This place is great! Â The green sauce is good with any empanada. I tried the Sweet Plantain and Cheese empanada and it was awesome. I'd probably try the guava and cheese empanada next..

Maybe it was too soon after it opened or just a rough night but my buddy and I were overwhelmingly disappointed. Â Sat in the front so we could watch the basketball playoffs. The space is interesting but they've done nothing to make it warm and inviting. It just has no ambiance. There's also a ton of wasted space...at the bar...and in other areas of the restaurant. Now the food. Had the quail and the country ham. Quail was mediocre and the ham was underwhelming. Cant recall what else we had but it wasnt very memorable. Again, it may have been early on in the life of the restaurant and maybe things have improved since then.

Onya was closed on Sunday so I Yelped Udon in the same are and found this place. The zaru undo and zaru soba were authentic and delicious. Very very good, highly recommended. Also tried some tempura and several donburi and they were all great. I would highly recommend the place. Will definitely go back!
They know what's up. And that's all I need to say.

Utterly bang up job every time. Quality and meticulous arrangement is stirring and truly compelling. Miso soup and crab crunch roll is a constant reminder of how nice it is to live in Brooklyn and have a Sushi Specialist next door.

Everything tastes like it's been cooked in something big and metal, which reminded me of my days on the USS Missouri. I had the "beef stew hand drawn noodle soup", which you have to order fast as if it was one word, and was so authentic it was like eating dirt water. The dumplings are arranged on chicken wire shelves and left in hot oil for about 10 minutes before they rip them out of there and try to get them down your throat while they're still sizzling. The dining experience in that fluorescent little room seemed especially authentic with my can of pepsi. The chef is constantly smacking these thick stretches of noodle dough against the counter behind the plexiglas. You'd think he was trying to stretch cable for a bridge. Almost stopped my pacemaker every time, it made the whole joint shake. The young people, they come in with their puffy jackets and don't even want to sit down. The two that did sat directly next to the space heater, which was located by the window next to a gigantic can of Raid (that's how you know the place is good). One young man didn't even take his headphones off to order. And their hairstyles, on the boys even... what kind of country are we running? Good authentic chinese, cheap. Depending on the size of the dumpling, I think you can get about 250 penny-sized ones for about a nickel.

Given the choice of pancakes, fried chicken and bacon or fried chicken and biscuits smothered in sausage gravy with grits, I had to go w/ the former because I wanted some sweet w/ the savory. But the latter is next on the list the next time I come here. Food was good, service was friendly and competent, atmosphere is relaxed and casual and there's a bunch of eye catching choices on the menu. There's also shorter line-ups for brunch than some of the nearby competition, at least on the day I went.
If only our food wasn't cold.

Everything was top-notch here: ambience, service, food - maybe except for the appetizers but I'll get to that. They served a bread basket of warm pita bread - it was so soft and fluffy I couldn't stop eating it. It's probably the best pita bread I've ever eaten. I tried two appetizers: the PYLOS ground meat sausage and stuffed grape leaves. They were both good, but the ground meat sausage tasted like meatballs. I just expected something better/cooler. But the braised short ribs were amazing. It was so tender that I could tear it with a fork alone, and the mashed potatoes with mushrooms were incredibly tasty. I loved the reduced wine sauce that was on it; it imparted complex notes of sweetness, spiciness and savoriness to the short rib. Our waters were refilled speedily, and our server was very friendly too. I love the ceiling of clay pots; very cute touch.

The black label burger is delicious and lives up to the hype. I didn't like the french dip sammy that much. Â Definitely get the burger. Â Carrots were delicious and so was the spinach. Â Bone marrow was soo rich and there's a lot in it.

Okay the line for this place was longer than that of a club. Grimaldi's had a relocation to a bigger venue, but just next door to its old space. The line is always VERY long so don't go here starving. My friends did and almost passed out by the time the pizza came (not exaggerating!). Around 4, the line was significantly shorter. Was it just that day? Or does this happen everyday? No idea. But worth a try! Anyways, so after you exit the long line outside, you are escorted to a waiting room where you can sit and order drinks. We fooled ourselves into thinking that we were actually getting seated but nahhhhh. So by this point, none of us were talking because all of my friends were SO stricken by hunger that they didn't even have the energy to lift their heads. 30 minutes went by and we FINALLY got seated. We dragged ourselves to the seating area and ordered ASAP. Pizza came within 10 minutes. We took pictures. We devoured it in 10 minutes. We were talking again. ALL IS WELL! Something about the brooklyn water makes this pizza different. They're opening one in LA next to my work and they're bringing in a chemist to replicate that water. We'll see if that compares!

Yum! This place is soooooo good. As I rarely give any establishment 5 stars this means a lot. I've been here several times for lunch and have enjoyed it very much. Inside the restaurant feels like you've escaped NYC and ended up in some beautiful summer cottage. The mood is very relaxing. I'm not a fan of eating crepes as meals...only as dessert. However, this place changed my mind and I can go for a crepe anytime of the day now :) I ordered the La Paysanne crepe both times I've been there and it's unbelievable. Others in my party have ordered the spinach crepe, the sausage crepe, and several of the dessert crepes and I've heard nothing but amazing reviews. Crepes are between $9-$10 but they will fill you up. It takes a lot for me to not ask for seconds...I always leave here super full after one crepe. Everyday there's a lunch special - $9 for any crepe + drink (I always get coffee as my drink and the coffee here is suburb. I just wish they were open in the mornings so I can get my coffee from here). A note - they don't open up until 12:30PM on weekdays. On weekends they open up at 11AM for brunch.

This place had good xiao long bao and shanghainese style fried noodles. The xiao long bao tastes a bit like they were frozen and then thawed, but overall, tasty. Would reccomend you check this place out if you have some free time.

Being able to make a reservation on Open Table was a big relief. Â We didn't try their BBQ but the noodle and rice entrees we ordered were delicious. Â More importantly, the service was awesome. Â We were given a quick and clear walkthrough of the menu and the server showed attentiveness to our table. Â Being someone who has high standards for service, I give this place a five for the waitress we got.

This place was highly recommended by a guy who knows NYC. He said it was one of the top three pizza places in the city. Lombardi's did not disappoint. The pizza was very good. We chose the Margarita and the ricotta/meatball. Both were very good. I also liked the quirky set up of the restaurant. We ate in the extension - a few doors down. It was perfect Little Italy!

Eh. Â I'm not exactly sad I went, but I won't be back. Â I came here on the recommendation of Serious Eats, which said this place has the best Wonton soup in the city. Â I'm going with "I really hope not", but I don't think I'll have a chance to find out this trip. Food: I had the steamed bun (not bad, nothing exciting) and the shrimp wonton soup. Â The soup was pretty good until I got to the bottom, where it started tasting metallic and.. bad. Â I didn't finish it. Service: ok, not great. Â A little absent, but I didn't wait too long for refills or anything. Paying: $25 minimum for a credit card, really? Â What the hell. Â Also, they have a printed bill, but somehow could only manage a hand-written receipt once I paid. Â Work will love that...

We had the most wonderful meal here. Â We were in NY for only one night and wanted it to be memorable and it WAS. Â The menu was extensive, the service was impeccable and the food was delicious. Â I highly recommend it to anyone visiting the theater/restaurant row area.

I came with BF and another couple for Restaurant Week and was really happy with the meal we had. The drinks we got at the bar before were deeeelicious (I had the strawberry something... it had citron vodka, some strawberry juice, something gingery and a slice of strawberry on top, it was great) and the place has a nice atmosphere. The RW menu had a really good selection and MAJOR bonus points for the wine specials! The Reisling we had was great, and only $35. 3 of us started with the cooked peach & feta salad which was great - however the mussels & clams were not as well executed. I had the soft-shell crab, which was pretty good. The tiny pasta with vegetables it was served over was good, but not that good. I would have preferred just straight vegetables since ... ya know ... I'm eating a fried crab. The steak with pesto was really good and the assorted heirloom tomatoes that came alongside it were super tasty. Desserts were great. I had the chocolate mousse cake with a chocolate-covered pretzel on top and nutella ice cream. The cake itself was a bit too rich, but the ice cream was perfect and who doesn't love a chocolate covered pretzel? The Watermelon Granita served on a meringue base was awesome. Refreshing, light, sweet but not overly sweet. On top of that, since we were ordering off of the limited menu the service was ridiculously fast. Also, the bathroom is beautiful. It's a nice touch...

An oasis in a hectic city. Five star service. Clean cool & welcoming, the $20 menu great value. Exquisite miso soup, sushi. Kept refilling the lovely green tea and cold water. Many green tea choices. Lovely refreshing green tea ice cream. Would go back tomorrow if in NY.

Looking for something trendy; something that spells romance? This is your kind of spot, but it doesn't stop there... I came here with a somewhat of a large crowd, a group of 16. The dim lighting, the little candles on the table, red wine like bottles as your water pitcher, and antique photos and empty wine bottles on the shelves with vintage books, and having the bar right there beside us, and sitting tightly right beside each other, it felt like I was on a date, on a date with 16 lovely classmates. Uruguayan dish? Yes indeed it is, the chivito completo was a delicious, juicy burger with all the combination of all my favorite, steak, bacon, eggs, onions, and tomatoes. That itself doesn't justify how Â amazing the burger was; it felt like I met a new lover tonight with the perfect pairing with their fries, and occasionally reaching my hands toward my classmate's Crispy-fried sweet potato chips that came with the Milanesa De Pollo. What's better than that? I tell you what, they have servers with the friendliest smiles; dressed in casual attire jeans and shirts...but with that kind of atmosphere I didn't mind it all; it was perfect. Seriously being here makes me feel so caught in the moment and I just want the clock to stop ticking, just like the broken antique clocks on the wall. 4 star and not 5 star? It's more personal than liking a type of a food or not; but not as personal as being allergic to it; but the spacing was a bit too cramp up for my enjoyment. But I don't blame them because it is feeling 30 degree out there, and we are bundled in layers; can't help when my coat keeps dropping to the floor when I'm trying to just finish up with my desserts. AHHHHHH, Desserts? Who can skip desserts, it's my favorites course of all meal times. Â The chocolate cake was a tag too cold for the weather and harder to bite. Â The dessert was a bit disappointing, but not when the Flan landed on the table. It had a creamy and silky texture, but I was almost sure that it had cream cheese inside because it sure did reminded me of Â cheesecake, something Junior's Cheesecakes.

Let's start with the fact that it was my 21st birthday and a pipe burst in my apartment. Boy what a blast. We were late to our reservation (naturally), but they were really accommodating and sweet! Food was fantastic--especially the meatball sliders and the corn soup. When I found out about the cake coming out, they also sent out beignets as a surprise! Which lemme tell you....my mouth exploded. Had a great birthday dinner and almost forgot that I had no ceiling back at home.

I loved this place, but when I came here with Singaporeans who lived in Japan, they pointed all the things they were lacking. So I guess they helped out a bunch in this review. They don't serve tea at all when you eat, and every good Asian food place should offer tea at the start of your meal. It wouldn't have bothered me, but when your spending a lot for dinner, you would expect at LEAST tea! The food I though was great! The Singaporeans, yea it's good, but not GREAT. Then again, I think the first time I came here, the food we ordered was better. This last time we had seafood sukiyaki. The first time was the beef shabu shabu. Also, the green tea ice cream was much better the first time I came last year, but now it was not great. I can get much better ones from the carton at Mitsuwa. Is this trend?!?! I hope it's not, because the first time I came it was awesome! The second time I came, less than a year later, not so amazing. But I'm hopeful!

It was 4 of us for Brunch. While we did enjoy the place and liked the waiters (except for being handed a trampled upon and dirt caked drinks menu...), the food was nice to look at but unanimously considered bland. Given the cost vs taste discrepancy I doubt we'll meet again...
Good food, good white sauce and hot red sauce.

I have been to their different locations multiple times and I have always left feeling full and satisfied. All their appetizers are delicious. I love their steak with chimchurri sauce and their miso-glazed salmon with brown rice. Their low prices are also a huge plus!

I have come about 8 times now, only after 7pm, including once or twice after the kitchen closed; I would come more often if I didn't live in New Jersey. I used to think Dinosaur BBQ in Harlem was the best BBQ in the NYC area, but I was way off. Â Fette Sau blows them absolutely out of the water. Â Every meat we have ever gotten at Fette has been just incredible; like where you just roll your eyes and ask "Seriously? How is this possible?" Â So much flavor, so juicy, not too fatty. Â It's not food that leaves you feeling ready to go for a walk or a run afterwards, but what are you expecting? The downside: the wait. Â I usually have to wait 45-60 minutes in line, and it can sometimes be hard to find table space. Â I have waited up to 1.5 hours just to eat, and felt stupid as I waited, but I always ALWAYS feel like it was worth it when I'm eating. Â I've heard of people going at lunch time and having no problem at all, but be ready to wait if going for dinner.

Once again, just need to drop in a 1 bomb to adjust for hype. Came in today for lunch and forgot that there weren't lunch specials. Solid pad see ew, but 8.50 for lunch in Woodside? Methink not, especially if I'm not getting an app along with. I ended up coming here today because my go-to Thai spot (Thai Central Point, right down the street) was closed. Please check the Central Point if you're in the area and looking for Thai food. You won't regret it.

If you love bread then run to this place now! Really amazing breads, pastries and croissants. I would say it was the best I've Â had in NYC. The coffee was rather average but then again, they are not a coffee shop so it's forgivable. The only disappointment was the attitude of our server. It was a snowy morning and there weren't many customers, no one behind us, but she behaved as though it was Friday night rush hour. She seemed very impatient, barely cracked a smile, and acted like we were really in her way. Aside from that, I will definitely come back again!

I really wanted to be blown away by ABC Kitchen however after our experiences, I was not. Overrated? I think so. I did enjoy the ambiance. It's casual, inviting, has large opened space, upbeat and has a bit of "shabby chic"-ness to it. The patrons range from a young couple in their early 20s on a date, a group of girls dolled up for the evening to a couple in their 50s enjoying a casual dinner out. Unfortunately, I was less than enthused about the food. It was just not memorable enough which was surprising for me since I've heard so much praise. I'm not saying food was bad; just not something I'd expect from a Jean Georges establishment. Service was great. Upon arrival we were immediately shown to our table and the entire time the staff was courteous, polished with our water glasses constantly refilled. I even forgive them for messing up on my order. Perhaps I'll return. I hope for a better food experience on the next visit.

3.5 ____ Wine bars should be: -spacious, yet cozy. -heavenly awesome atmosphere / ambiance yet with minimalist decor -incredible food -bonus if its reasonably priced Heidi's has two of the above. Â Its just too cramped to be a date spot, too cramped to enjoy a meal, and usually too cramped to walk to the bathroom. Â And this is, primarily, why the 3.5 stars. Now that we've covered the space issue- and let's face it- its hard to yawn on Tuesday's at midnight, I dont want to know what its like on Wednesday & beyond - lets move onto the decor. Its meh. Â It's decorated like a tree house. Â Smorgasbord. Â In a cute way. Â but for wine? Â  "Oh, its cute!" Â - its what your friends say when they're really thinking, "Crap, this is small, and Â who decorated? Its as random as Charlie biting a finger." Now.... The Mac & Cheese is awe-inspiring with bacon or lobster as possible additions - mmmm, cheesy lobster.... enough to make a starving Mainer excited... . Â The guac comes in hot, medium, or mild. _______ :::Flashback::: Somewhere.... I've had the souffle before... and this friendly Heidi seems vaguely familiar. ah ha! Â  and just last week I was thinking, "Boy, that Rendez-vous seems to have lost its touch" Â ... Â apparently now I know why. ________ The food is outstanding, but this isnt the type of place you come here for the food. Â Most unfortunate. Â Wine bar trapped inside the body of Pomme Frites.

We made our reservation a week ahead and can only get the table but not at the bar. It's our first time there, so omakase is a must. We choose to have a combination of sashimi and sushi. I also mentioned to the server that I love uni to make sure that it's included. EVERYTHING was sooooo good! And I must say that after trying their uni sushi, I cannot stop thinking about it! Toro melted in my mouth and I just wish that I can live in the restaurant forever. Â  Each of us had 5-6 different sashimi and 10 sushi and it was the perfect amount of food for us. (I stuffed my face when I went to Neta the last time....) The bill was about $125 each and I would love to go back again when I save up enough money. =P

What can I say about this place that hasn't been said a million times. A real legendary place, I hope it never closes. When the health dept. closed them down recently I was present during the inspection that did them in. In my opinion its a prejudice thing. They shut down this establishment for not keeping their roast meats at a ridiculously high temperature yet ignore fast food chains that keep their gross shit room temp all day. Long Live NY Noodletown

complimentary breads: delicioso! Â the best was the one with meat and cheese :) creamy polenta fricassee of truffled mushrooms: rich, creamy, delicious in every way braised short ribs of beef vegetable & farro risotto: fork tender, only wish there was more! spaghetti tomato & basil: simple, good, solid dish. Â while it is a little pricey for what it is, i would come back for this tagliatelle fresh shaved summer truffles: simple, the flavor of the truffles really shine in this dish, but there's only so much truffle flavor i can handle. the only reason scarpetta is getting 4 stars instead of 5 is that they didn't chill our bottle of white wine, they just plopped it down on our tiny table next to the burning candle...

I hate to be the voice of dissent (actually, I don't hate to be the voice of dissent, but let's say I do) but I was pretty underwhelmed with Sanford's, especially after waiting for 30 minutes. Â To be sure, it's a fancy looking place (although with a rich history), done up to be sleek and modern, with thumping beats (is it a breakfast joint or a club?). Â But the food is mostly slightly above average diner fare, and some of it just average, Greek Diner schlock (I'm looking at you, pancakes). Â Though the eggs do lack the mysterious watery texture of some of the worse examples of Greek dinery. Â  The coffee? Â The less said about it the better. Â  Indeed, I've recently discovered that a reliable way of gauging whether I like breakfast coffee is exactly how much of the jug of milk I pour into my cup. Â None? Â We must be at a coffee house. Â Most? Â Well, I suppose we're dining at Sanford's. Ultimately, this is a fine astoria choice, and the prices are reasonable. Â But not enough better than Neptune Diner, or the various other diners to justify waiting. * The prix fixe breakfast is a ridiculous gip except with respect to a few specific dishes. Â Most mains are less than $8. Â Coffee is $1.50. Â Why is the prix fixe $14? Â For the lame looking mimosa? Â Eh.

Love this spot. Â Food is really good...definitely recommend it for brunch. Â I have ordered a bunch of different stuff here and have always liked it. Â The decor is really cool and the staff is friendly. There is usually a long line so you have to wait to order before finding your seat, but the line moves quickly. I definitely recommend coming here!

Great ambiance and service. Beautiful setting with delicious food, wine and cocktails. Very gluten free friendly, with yummy gluten free pasta on the menu (helpful as someone with Celiac). Loved the salmon dish with beans/green veggies, kale salad with oranges and nuts, and my favorite - pasta with homemade marinara and mozzarella cheese. Has become my go to restaurant to take friends and family; everyone has enjoyed it a lot! Solid restaurant, always a great experience.
ambiance isn't nearly on par with the food but the food is great.

Ok, I'm bumping this up after experiencing two must haves at Pommes Frites: Truffle Mayo Poutine The truffle mayo will now be the only dip I ever get, if I'm not already chowing down in the poutine. The poutine is made with layers of tasty gravy, gooey cheese curds, and crispy fries. A little small for the price, but worth it.

After reading all these wonderful reviews on Yelp, I decided to trust my fellow Yelpers. It was a bit disappointing... was it because we order the wrong dishes? Everyone around around table ordered like family style dish with big portions to share. First of all, the Thai ice-tea was super disappointing. That's a bad first impression already for me even before the food came out. It was too milky and didn't taste a bit of Thai tea. Ordered: Appetizer- Fried soft shell crab w/ shredded green mango sauce $16 This was horrible and it was one of the most expensive appetizers. It wasn't mango sauce at all! It was thinly fine slices of mango which I couldn't even taste with other shredded veggies and a strong taste of vinegar. The crab was okay and it didn't taste fresh. Please skip this. Entree 1 - SautÃ© chicken w/ cashew nuts, pineapple & roasted chili Chicken was dry and chinese take outs taste much better. Entree 2- Massaman Curry This curry had a funny taste to it. Wasn't the best I've had. Very thick and had peanuts inside which I thought it was weird. FYI - Cash Only.

This is for the market shopping only. Â They have everything you could need to make any kind of italian meal. Â Yes it is a tourist trap and yes it is expensive. Â But amazing selection of anything italian. Â The meat and cheese counter is great - they will give you samples and advise you what goes with what. Â Even though it is expensive the meat and cheeses go a long way on crackers or appetizers - so not bad for excellent food. Â  You will find something you like here!
Beyond amazing. I can't wait to go back! The portions are huge! I got the Tacos, Red Snapper Ceviche, and Plantains. Too much food for me and my friend. but soooooo worth it.

No place in New York offers more value than these guys. Â Sure you have to wait a bit. Â Maybe they are in awkward parts of NYC. Â But lamb and chicken on orange rice with white sauce and wake-the-fuck-up spicy red sauce for six bucks, WHAT?! Â And, you can make at least two meals out of one. Â I ate mine all at once. Â Don't judge me. Â It was delicious.

Great place with a lot of character. It's small and dark, and even though it's crowded, it's a very nice crowd. The staff is great too and very helpful with suggestions. Tapas are tasty and nicely priced. Will def visit again!
Really big slices of tasty pizza. I save some of them in the fridge for when I don't have time for a more proper meal.

I came across this place while searching the internet. Did not know it existed in my own backyard. So my wife and I went there for dinner 11/30/12. We love the decor and theme of the place. The music playing was great! It was crowed and everyone seemed to be enjoying themselves. Our waitress was charming, friendly and polite. Her service was great and she was attentive to our needs.
