We ordered the Southern Shrimps for starters, they were fantastic! You only get 3, would have love more, but not a deal breaker. We both had the Catfish blacken, it came with rice, red & green peppers and cooked onions. The portions were a healthy size. We loved the food and dessert. This place will be a regular spot for us to dine at. Â If your looking for a nice, warm and lovely place to have good-times, check this place out. I think you will like it! Â We do!

The former Royal Video store has morphed into a lovely local bar with thoughtful local ingredients and killer drafts. Â If I still lived across the street, this would be my local hangout for sure. BF and I stopped in for a late lunch. Â Weird system of ordering food in a little hole by the kitchen in back and drinks ordered at bar. Â Nonetheless, on a warm day with air wafting in on this corner near the bar, ya gotta love this place. $11 bought me a slow roasted Heritage pork sandy with pickled onions and a side of lettuc(hate calling dressed lettuce a salad). Â We shared the fries that came with bf's burger. Â The spicy, sweet pork pieces were pretty delish as was the crispy fries. Â A draft of Troegs dreamweaver wheat was a divine combo. Â Happy hour made the draft $4 which is a great deal.

I'm giving Fish 4 stars for the main reason of the waitress spilling oyster water on the bf. Lol. Jk. Came in for dinner one weekend night after bf raved about their Oysters Rockefeller. I've been searching for a restaurant that serves this and he absolutely swears by it. Oh-Kay! Well...I was not sold by it. SautÃ©ed spinach instead of creamed? Not my thing. It was good tho. We ordered a dozen oysters as usual and was served with 11. I also think I got one bad not-so fresh oyster. New England clam chowder was watery. Catfish sandwich was good and is my saving grace. Would I try this place again? Nahhh.
Consistently excellent.

i've been vegan for a little over a year now and i'm constantly searching for new places that are as good as champs, but they're just not there to be found. i came in today with my mother, a meat-eater, who didn't really understand that vegan cuisine is more than just rabbit food. the greasy spoon diner decor confused her for a minute and i'm sure she was baffled by the menu including"chicken" and "tuna" (although every meat is seitan based i believe). well, she was pleasantly surprised with her food and now considers champs to be one of the best places she's eaten at in a long time. the food is always incredible, this place is cheap, and the friendly staff are seemingly all gorgeous heavily tattooed women. highly recommend for vegans and non-vegans alike.

I've dined in and gotten delivery from this place numerous times since it's opened and I've never once had anything bad to say. The flavors, ingredients, and service are top notch. I've had a variety of the dishes and desserts there and can't pick one favorite. The tomato soup is quite nice during the winter! Don't think twice, definitely go to Samudra. You won't regret it!!

I decided to try a new place for Sunday brunch. This place always seemed to be all the rave and boy is it true! These 5 stars are well deserved. We had reservations and arrived about 15 minutes early. The place was filled to capacity but we were still seated about 5 minutes prior to our reservation. I was shocked but pleased. Once our orders were in liter no more than 10 minutes our food was in front of us. And OMG the vanilla bean french toast was amazing!! The brioche bread melts in your mouth. It almost tastes like a pastry. You get 3 hearty pieces. I couldn't finish it all. The maple chicken sausage was just ok. I've had better at the smith lincoln center. The egg white omelette was very underwhelming. The sauteed spinach inside of it was horrible. But the VANILLA BEAN FRENCH TOAST!!!!! Get it!! You will not be disappointed. The service was awesome from entry to exit. I'll be back!!!

This is a place that should be judged on it's food alone and for that it gets four stars. Seriously delicious! Service was unexceptional but passable and the backyard and interior was typical Park Slope decent but nothing to write home about. I will eat here many more times.

I came back last night 10/14/2013. I had the Bufala & the prosciutto & funghi pizzas. Both were tasty but unfortunately I got very sick. I didn't get sick the first time but then I didn't stuff a truck load of pizza down my throat. So, i'm going to try again (it's pretty obvious that I like this place) & pray I don't get sick.

This place is just alright. Â I was quite disappointed by the On-Choy, which tasted like it was stir-fried in reused oil. Â However, the other dishes were adequate - Beef Rendang, Roti Canai, Hainanese Chicken.
Bison burger is the best meat option here! Chevapi? Not even close to the real thing :/

My girlfriend and I went here for dinner, although I keep reading it's more known for its brunches. Â I made reservations at 3PM on a Saturday for 8PM later that day via opentable.com. Â We got stuck in traffic and I called at 8PM to say we were going to be a little late, they said it's not a problem. We get there at 820PM and hostess greets us with a smile and shows us to our seats. The over-all ambiance of the restaurant is very elegant but simple. The staff was very friendly and observant, coming over to refill water/ask for refills on drinks and clearing away plates to make room for the next part of the meal in a timely fashion. Complimentary bread/butter was served and they gave us 2 fried risotto balls as well which were very good. We had the Argentinian Crios 2012 Malbec, to start, which was delicious We had the grilled octopus for appetizers, which was interesting and pretty good; one large tentacled arm is grilled and served with potatoes and various garnishes. She had the Chilean Sea Bass, which she enjoyed a lot.. I thought it was pretty good too. The grilled mushrooms were a nice touch. I had the Carmelized Beef Tenderloin medium rare, which I didn't enjoy so much. Â The meat was cooked perfectly but the texture of the beef tasted old, like meat that's been sitting in the freezer for weeks. Â I don't know, maybe it's just me, my girlfriend thought it tasted fine. The staff gave us 2 little cold, chocolatey, dessert things when dropping off the check; that was delicious as well. All in all, I had a very positive experience here. The service and ambiance were great, the wine was very good, and most of the food was tasty and just the right portion size.

Yay for good, healthy good! Â I got the salmon burger with a gluten-free bun and baby greens. Â The burger was delicious but because of the avocados kept slipping around and was slightly messy. Â The side for the burger was extra, so keep that in mind. Â I really liked the atmosphere, it was very laid back and welcoming. Â I will definitely be coming back.

I had real high hopes for this place. Â The last time I was in NYC I wasn't patient enough to wait in line so made it a point to come back hoping that time had cooled the masses. Â It was still a 45 minute wait which is totally Â exceptable for a busy restaurant. Â Those pork buns really got the taste buds going and I was very eager to try my noodle order. Â I got the Classic and the first few sips of the broth were heavenly....then it started getting heavier and heavier as it cooled to the point of cloyingly rich and then a little nauseating. They need to get rid of some of the oil that rises to the top of the broth as it cools. Â Noodle were alright but I like mine a little chewier and squigglier. I've always liked places with a raucous kinetic rock n roll energy but I'm getting old and cranky and I just wanna eat my noodles in peace. Â Forget about having a zen eating experience here 'cause it is LOUD but very fun for the bubbly youth of today who can handle the extra fat and noise.
OK, never been here for anything but breakfast and brunch. Â Eggs are tasty but pancakes are the winner here. Â A little pricy but well worth it.

Have been there twice with two different experiences. First visit was on a weekday, not too late (~730 if I remember correctly) and had an appetizer of spinach salad with an entree of filet mignon. Â The Â spinach salad was very good, with a preferable vinaigrette and fresh crumbled bacon. Â While I normally don't order filet mignon, considering its general lack of true taste and meaty hearth, I was in the mood for red meat and decided to give it a shot. Â As far as filets go, it was more than satisfactory, prepared well (if a bit on the well-done side of medium-rare) and had a nice bit of natural juice. Â Service was satisfactory, with a few order mistakes, but corrections were prompt and drinks were promptly ordered and delivered. My second experience came on a Friday after a few steins of beer and a later call time, so to say (~1030). Â Ordered the artichoke appetizer, and it was fantastic. Â Great combination of freshly-chopped hearts, pungent and tasty cheeses and nicely toasted bread. Â The entree of spare ribs, however, was wholly disappointing. Â The grits were soup-like in consistency and the ribs were neither smoky nor succulent. Â While the (shared) dessert of brownie and ice cream was amazing this did little to counterbalance the wholly subpar service. Â Our waiter was either acting alarmingly aloof or simply high; forgotten drink orders, plates constantly mistaken with the adjacent tables', and general incompetence. Â I actually felt kinda bad for the guy, cause he did not act in a mean, bitter or contemptible manner, he was just not very good as a waiter at that time. Â  Will definitely go back if to try the other menu items and take in the almost too-scene-y scenery, but will have to keep myself ready for inconsistent service.

They are known for their wings I guess... but I think the wings are just pretty good. Burger is above average. I don't like that it is always crowded, but I do take it as a good sign that it is a popular place that pleases the picky Park Slope eaters.

I love Barbuto - BUT I will give it a 1 star as they are really awful on the phone and it's just not cool anymore. Also, the service it's truly awful. The worst hosts in nyc. I write this from the table where I have been waiting for a hour and no food came yet. Sasha the waitress needs to work at a post office- she is horribly and terribly rude, it's too much. When she was a door girl she was also always so nasty. Now as a waiter, she either has fake smile or walks off extremely angrily. Someone needs to fire her. To complete the experience, they poured water all over us: needless to say, not even an apology!

my place for burgers in the 'city'. Â each time we have guest come visit we take them here. Â casual, yet trendy and in the heart of soho. Â sampled a few burgers on the menu and all have come out nice; and i always get the tator tots instead of the fries.
Went there for brunch. Â Really good food and drink selection, slow service.

Lam Zhou is amazing. The dumplings are delicious. You can bring your own beer, and some of the tables are communal. The whacking of the noodles during the hand-making process can be a bit LOUD, but - it's all worth it.
This is was some serious market style BBQ. Deliciously fatty in all the right ways. Get there early because the place gets packed!

Mu, Bailey and I did New York in 12 hours...starting from Chinatown and worked our way up to Midtown and this Halal Cart was our last stop. Boy, we sure did save the best for last. To be honest, I had no expectations for this cart. I mean, I thought that it would be a great place to grab food after a long night of partying and everyone knows that food tastes soo much better when you're a bit intoxicated. However, this was not the case. We were all 100% sober, waiting in line for half an hour, and we enjoyed every bite of our food. Who knew that chicken and rice could be so good? It was very flavorful and the sauces that were provided were amazing. One lesson we learned that night was that there's different "red sauces." I put one of their red sauce all over my rice and it was fantastic! Mu had a taste and decided to put some on his...except he grabbed the hot sauce. I don't even want to begin to describe how spicy it was...Mu kept on eating because it was so good. Bailey and I were immensely entertained. Anywho, Bailey and I decided to go back to the cart and eat MORE! Yes, we did! We got the lamb plate this time and it was equally delicious. And for those who are wondering, the lamb was not gamey at all. Score!!!

Was able to go back for dinner on a Sunday night. Shared the meatballs, fried zucchini, kale and short rib tacos with my dining companion. Everything was excellent, including my glass of Provencal Rose. This wine bar is top on my list of places when craving tapas and a great selection of wine!

This place is ridiculously overrated. The skin on the soup buns was too thick and tough. They tasted like they were sitting awhile between being made and being steamed. The jellyfish was blah. The noodles with peanut sauce were passable, but I could do better then that at 3AM after a night of partying in my own kitchen. Combine that with absurdly rude service - unforgivable! Never again. Noodle House in Flushing - here I come!
Did take out pizza (prosciutto). The ham was Â either old or not good quality . They send wrong beverages . Don't recommend. Go to rosa on 69th and grand

These two stars are SOLELY for the mac n' cheese So Armin L. decided that he had to take me here because this was one of his favorite places. It was cold outside and at 3 am had people huddled in the cold hoping to get a table and inside just as many crowding the bar. Eventually we get a seat downstairs which is really the drink/lounge type place. (Read low circular tables primarily meant for holding your martini and NOT your mac n' cheese) Grateful not to be outside anymore I ordered a turkey sandwich of some kind and he had the mac n' cheese and the crab cakes. I ate half of my sandwich and then gave him the other. As I'm waiting for him to finish I notice the flame of the candle in this darkly lit area very close to the other half of the sandwich. Upon further scrutiny I see ... ::pause for dramatic effect:: a fluorescent green worm dancing upon the bread of the other half of my sandwich. (and just so you can get a proper idea see daymented.com/2004/0509_â€¦) HORRIFIED..absolutely horrified we called the waitress over and eventually the manager apologized and comped our meal. Uhm thanks I knew it was going to end up being free but can you stick your finger down my throat so I can throw the other half of the sandwich up? Needless to say I just can't go there again. This was the first (but no last) favorite place of Armin L.'s that I ruined for him.
ahhh sooo goood! deff going back

ok ok, how good could french fries really be? pretty friggin great at this place. the sauces are hit and miss but the fries are amazing, tired dirty digs but who cares, the portions are huge, tons of sauces to choose from, they let you sample any you want, cool place to stop at for a quick bite if youre in the neighborhood.

Pig & Khao (nice pun) finds hitherto hidden connections between Filipino and Thai cuisine, turning them into an exquisite combination that in earlier times might be considered Pan-Asian fusion. Not that there's anything so crass going on here. The khao soi, a soup noodle dish native to Southern Thailand, is a fire-hot take on the dish, with the coconut milk not hiding a hint of the chili heat in the broth. Meanwhile pork adobo, a spin on the Philippines national dish rests in a bowl with a full poached egg and Sichuan peppercorns lightly numbing the fatty meat on the tongue. The cod is a bit too salty, something that probably resulted in the recent switch in fish from salmon, which absorbs the flavor better. It was rainy on the night I came here, so we couldn't take in the impressively large outdoor space. But I wonder if such lovingly prepared fare should have to compete with flies and the hissing of summer lawns. This is food to be savored, arriving at does in irregular but still prompt intervals from the tiny kitchen/bar. The menu divisions here seem designed to confuse, or at least contribute to over ordering. There's nothing "small" about the khao soi or curry fried chicken - these are just main dishes that would be served with rice. Figure on ordering just one of these a person, perhaps with an extra one for the table to share. This should keep the cost at around $50 a head with a couple drinks, as opposed to our feast at $70 each. The drink selection is impressively varied, with an all bottle selection that moves from the hipster trash (Pork Slap and Genny) to regional crafts (Itacha Flower) and pricy Asian imports (Hitachiano). Slurping beers out of a bowl "Hong Kong style" may be inaccurate and stupid, but at least you sip nice beers while doing it.

I have a thing for exposed brick interiors and candlelight. And unintrusive live music. And delicious food. All of which I got at Grape and Grain on Thursday night for a dinner with the ladies. The pita chip and white bean dip is a delicious starter. Everyone ordered the shitake mushroom tart and loved it. All the appetizers run $6-$15. While my tuna carpaccio with jalapeno citrus sauce was quite good, I think I will go for a sandwich or a pizza next time around bc it will likely be a little more filling. Mains run $9-$15. Would love to go back again for a romantic rendezvous.
Fresh foods quickly served. Nice open space with ample seating. free wifi. street parking minimal. I WILL return.

The food is messy and hard to eat. There is a lot of juice in the filling but that makes the arepa soggy. I think there are better places. The chips and guac is great. Yam chips are sooo good, you really can't just have one.

I've gotta say, not as impressed as I wanted to be. I had the honey-dipped fried chicken and didn't realize that the honey-dipping would eliminate crispiness (the whole reason for getting fried chicken, in my opinion). Next time I would go for the plain old fried chicken. The cornbread and mac and cheese were both excellent. I also liked the fried okra. The chicken was just a disappointment.

My friends and I needed to find a last minute spot for dinner and luckily Bea had a reservation available on open table. All the dishes we got were pretty delicious. My favorite was the green pasta. Their drinks were nicely presented however I didn't particularly enjoy the one I ordered bc I like a sweeter/fruitier cocktail, but they were strong! I would def come back again.

Straight up hole-in-the-wall bahn-mi joint. Â  I chose the vegetarian pork (don't ask why), which I will never do again. Â The bread, though, was good as were everything else. Â My date's classic was also delicious. Â Not my favorite Vietnamese sandwich shop (Saigon Shack on MacDougal), but a worth a drop-by if I am in the area.

Been here a couple times - I had a much better experience my first time (very good squid ink risotto, great service) than the second time (so-so seafood linguine, very mediocre service). I expected the lobster in the linguine to be the highlight...unfortunately, it was very obviously overcooked. I made a 7pm reservation and had to wait 20 minutes for my table, with no apologies from the staff. Why did I bother making a reservation?

Super cute!!!! Juliet C. and I stopped by after a disappointing few hours apartment hunting and I must say this place definitely lifted my spirits and filled my tummy quite well. We shared a Cubano plate which consisted of moist, delicious pulled pork, beans and rice. I'm normally not a fan of Mexican food or anything related, but I couldn't put my fork down. Oh wait, I did put my fork down occasionally, but that was only to slurp some frozen Morita (Mojito + Margarita). Yum! We also went back and ordered some fried plantains for our dessert. They were unevenly cut but that worked out in the end since I preferred the thinner sliced, crispier pieces and Juliet, the thicker, chewier ones. Atmosphere wise, this place is so perfect for the summertime lazies. Large outdoor space with decent amount of seating, bright colors everywhere, environment friendly solar panels ... it's a little slice of Cuban hipster flower-power. Definitely give this place a shot if you're around the area and it's summertime!

Love the atmosphere of this place and foods were great! I stayed at 60 Thompson right across the street and this was a perfect little cafe for a brunch. Â Fish and chips were great. Not too fried or too hard. Fish taste fresh. Â French toast was amazing as well. Perfect portion with decent price. As well as mimosa :) Compared to other restaurants in Ny this place is hip romantic and artsy!
Fantastic pizza! This place never lets me down !!
I went there for brunch. The server barely spoke English. He forgot to bring the salt and pepper. The food took a long time to come out. Cute place though. Good coffee, nice music. Kind of cramped.
Reliable pork/chicken broth ramen. Not as good as Totto, but better than Ippudo, and much shorter waits than either. Very solid ramen so it's a good standby.

I began coming here back in 2002 or 03 when I lived in the neighborhood. Â It is the perfect place to come alone and enjoy a HUGE steaming cup of pleasure (whatever yours may be) and a gooey desert crepe. OR for DINNER introduce your friends to this quaint little restaurant that you have loved for years just to find out that they've all known about the place and have been coming for years too!!! Â LOVE IT! The last time I went there with a friend it was fantastic. Usually I go for their crepes but we decided to go for the escargo and two different musssel plates. Â All were amazing and paired with a bottle of their Sancerre. It gets pretty crowded and loud but in a cozy manner where I could still enjoy conversation with a friend. Â The staff is friendly but sometimes rushed.

Please stop going here!!!! The only thing bad about this place is that everyone else loves it too, and it is always packed. Drinks are fantastic, so is the food. The bartenders and servers are friendly....really the only problem is that too many people like this place (not a bad problem to have).
I'm writing this on behalf of my boyfriend who works in the area and eats lunch here all the time: bring back coffee on your lunch special menu! :)

Went here for a special night with my beau! Food was incredible! I ordered the Paccheri Napolitana pasta, and the beau ordered the Quattro Stagioni pizza. Both were extremely tasty! The only complaint about the pizza that the beau had was that each topping was split on each slice, (all of the ham was on one slice and all of the eggplant was on another etc.) Even though that may have been the cook's intentions for us to eat it that way, we both much preferred it when the toppings were all mixed together. For desert we had the Pizzetta Dolce, which was surprisingly delicious! (They use the crust of the pizza dough and spread the insides with house-made nutella) My only complaint, isn't really a complaint at all. I get uncomfortable when service is too nice/talkative. And they were very nice, and tended to our every need...which is great.

Everything was flawless. Spicy Bloody Mary's, popcorn okra, hush puppies, boudin balls, jambalaya, fried chicken, and po' boys...all STELLAR. Efficient service, very cool (very clean) bathrooms, and sweet decor. I'm just glad I don't live in this neighborhood because I would go here EVERY week. Exceptional. And well priced.

I hate to say it, as the staff is very nice for this hood, but this is not what is used to be. My kids loved it so we went alot. The are often very accomodating but the portions are much smaller now, often not hot, and I once had a puddle of beer under my table that took quite a bit for them to clean up, even though it was still dripping from the underside of the table all over me. I hate to be critical but if it is Pies and Thighs, those 2 items should be outstanding. They are not. I think the prices are reasonable if the food was as good as a year ago..

Gluten free Italian and SO good! The place is very small l but very elegant and cozy. Â It's a perfect date spot. My date and I shared a Caesar Salad and the ingredients were so fresh. Â We also shared the braised short rib and that was...eh (hence my four star rating...that, and the service was just OK). He and I shared an entree (a pasta dish with fresh mozzarella and sausage) and it was awesome! Â The portions are great for sharing (normal, "Fit" human portions). I will definitely come back here again.

Omgg to die forrr! Definitely always get extra white + red sauces on the side. The white sauce is amazzing. The chicken and rice together is so good. This place is a definite must if in nyc. Make your way over here! Craving some right now, can't they bring a cart over to LA?

Came here about half month ago. My first Hawaii cuisine experience in New York. At the time when we came, there weren't many people there. The interior is quite interesting, looked modern decorated with Hawaiian nature photography. The food was good, it tasted similar to Japanese food. Seemed like they are customized to suite for westerner's taste. Still I enjoyed all their dishes. and also it was great to be able to taste Hawaiian beer for the first time.
3 star environment. 4 star food.

PIGGY EVERYTHING here is amazing. I didn't do the ordering but from my pictures I'm recommending the intestines, pig foot broth soup thing, and Â etc. Normally not a big fan of pig foot but everything here was very good. We got overly excited and were trying to eat it too fast. I recommend getting the soup a bit spicy and getting it with the rice after. The service was pretty good andddd they had a great muscat cider and YUZU sauce. :)

Food: 5/5. Service: 3/5 (nothing wrong just pretty standard) Location: 3/5 (a bit difficult to get to but I really like the east village) -1 star for being cash only. I hadn't read the reviews prior to going so this was a very pleasant surprise for us. Â The food was excellent and well priced. Â The fact that it was cash only is always a disappointment but I'd still go back. We shared everything and I think the favorites were the Spaghetti Al Limone and the octopus (it may have been a special?)

Stopped in Saturday morning for a late lunch and this place was abolsutely packed! My boyfriend and I resorted to sharing a four person table with an elderly gentleman eating noodles by himself. He was absolutely adorable- bu that's aside from the point. This is definitely a no frills- great food type of place. If you're looking for ambiance, great service and fine dining- this just isn't the place. But what you will get here is a slight wait to get seated, fabulous food for an absurdly cheap price! Quick too. Boyfriend had their $20 promotion for 2 Ginger & Scallion lobsters, which he enjoyed thoroughly. I'm not a big fan of lobsters so can't really comment on how great it was, however it looked fresh and for the price, you can't beat it! I got their famous roast duck + pork over rice and it was literally placed in front of me less than 3 mins after i ordered. ABSOLUTELY amazing. I've had plenty of roast duck and pork over my life both in china and various chinatowns across the united states and I have to say this is one of the best if not the best ! Great flavor and tenderness to both. Will definitely be back again!

This place is very good and so cheap! Ambience is cute and cozy. Finally a place that doesn't sell overspiced, hard, cardboard-y falafel. Instead, it's the perfect amount of crispness on the outside and fluffy on the inside. The baba ghanoush is roasted, smoky deliciousness, and the yummy bread is hot and fresh. The food is actually quite simple and that's probably what makes it good. I almost died when they brought the bill with small piece of cake made with semolina that I hadn't had since I was a wee little girl. Oh the memories!

Joe's Shanghai is the only competitor to Din Tai Fung in Arcadia. As a California native, Joe's is another spot that I must visit when I am in New York. Finding Joe's Shanghai was difficult for me at first because there was a lot of construction making it difficult to make our way into the alley. But it was all worth it when my soup dumplings came. The soup is delicious but you cant let it sit too long because it might soak the dumpling and cause it to rip easily.

For a location so well located to all attractions and sights in NYC I am blown away by the price. Â This location is very cozy, i would say unless you are a snob, which most people that come here are not you sit so close to the neighboring tables that it is almost impossible not to have a conversation or be engaged with them. Â The bathroom is so close to the back that you almost feel as you walk there that you are working with the staff. Â The staff is extremely friendly and energetic, there are some older staff but there is still a very good young blood hipster feel here. Â This location is very French themed, very intimate small Paris dining, with the tables painted with the number and a need to pull out the table for people to sit. Â I would say if you are looking for really fine dining this is not the location for you. Â With that said if you would like amazingly good food and energetic atmosphere this may infact be the location for you. Â Easily one of my favorite dishes of my life was the Duck Confet that i had here, it had a combination of flavors unlike anything i had ever eaten. Â We did the French Onion soup for desert of course, it was really really sweet but still easily the best soup i have ever had. Â My fiance had the steak, the fries were smaller sweet potato fries, the steak wasn't overwhelmingly delicious but still very good. Â At the prices you can't beat this location, it is almost worth more considerations for most dining location in NYC as being a once in a blue moon for a special occasion and could be considered a place to go 2-3 times a month. Reservations a must as they are small and always busy. Â Wine best deal by the bottle.

First visit to The Spotted Pig tonight. Â So disappointing. Â Service was extremely slow. Â The food was just so so. Â The scallops were overcooked. Â The vegetable plate - which was very important to me, as both my daughters are vegetarian, was a pile of overcooked beets, onions, garlic & greens. Pork rillette was just so so! We decided not to order the pork belly as I make this a lot at home! Â Maybe we should have! Â I don't think we will go back.

If you ever get the irresistible urge for falafel I would go no further than Taim. Â I personally always go with the red falafel on white pita and be sure to ask for pickles (in the pita). Â If you're feeling a little more ravenous than normal I would also recommend the fries. Â They come with a unique dipping sauce that is very tasty. Â  It's size belies the popularity of this place, especially recently. Â It must have been written up in NYT or something because the last few times I've been there I was greeted with a line 10 deep. Â So don't be discouraged...just know that you'll have worthwhile deep-fried chickpea balls when make your way to the front.
AMAZING DUMPLINGS, definitely original, even better than some restaurants back in China. I love pork and cabbage dumpling, also their spicy and sour soup is fantastic!
awesome food

GET THE DONUTS!!! Seriously I know you want to watch your weight but the donuts are crazy good and sell out. Â The chicken and waffles is also the tits! Â Me and my wife have been here a couple of times to grab lunch with friends who live in Berg. Â Its a straight shot down the BQE from my apartment in astoria and I often get a spot right in front just before they open at noon. Â Oh... Get there before they open this place gets packed!

The cocktails alone are 4 star worthy. Service maybe a 3 star rate just because they try and take everything away rather too quickly. Came in on Saturday for a dinner party of 6 and noticed that everything, literally everything just had TONS of mayo on it. Even in the freaking paella, all the seafood was drenched underneath a blanket of mayo. Guess that's their signature YB sauce? Not such a huge fan of the food minus the cod. The cod is well prepared (no mayo!) and delish. Tuna tartar is worth skipping and so is the YB salad (has no greens). Def go for the brussel sprout salad and the churros at the end. They try not to seat the entire party until everyone arrives so make sure to have everyone there. Space is a bit cramped upstairs but below there is a huge room for larger parties. The bar got extra packed towards 8/9 PM on Saturday so make reservations just in case!

The food was excellent, service--could be better. Though it's BYOB, we were only permitted to open one bottle of wine (to share between 6 people) because they didn't want us to stay long (their words). I respect that, since it is a small place and six is a HUGE group in a tiny spot, but it was like they couldn't wait to get rid of us. I think they were actually a little disappointed when we ordered dessert. Try going with a small group on a weekday and try the mufungo.
This is a great place. Hope to come back soon

I have to say... Hagi is one of my all time favorite izakaya spots. My first time was with a friend who posted a review a while ago. Between three people, our meal was dirt cheap (note: this IS in the city and it is definitely a bargain). This secluded establishment is tough as nails to find in the middle of the city. Just look for an inconspicuous doorway leading down to a magical room of wonders that is only about the size of my condo. Decor however, made me feel like I walked through a portal somewhere along the the steps which has sent me to an izakaya... in Tokyo. Now considering this place does not take reservations, they were very willing to accommodate to a large crowd... provided u get there a few minutes before 5:30 (which is their supposed opening time... showed up at 5:28 and there were people eating already). We had a party of 14 (with two more coming later). They put us on a row of tables against the wall because the little room on the side already had several parties. Â  Our waiter was very VERY patient with us (thanks buddy) because half of these jackasses had no idea what they wanted. So I took the liberty of ordering for everyone just to make things easier for the poor guy. Considering every three minutes we had to get another pitcher of beer. By the time we realized that we should order 3-5 pitchers at a time, the poor guy already made about 7 beer runs. We also had to order our food in waves because apparently we are all fatties and like to gorge ourselves silly. My personal favorite there is the Yakisoba... has a nice hint of kimchee, Yakiudon, and their seafood okonomiyaki. I would personally stay away from the Curry Yakiudon. It smells like curry, looks like curry, but definitely did not taste like curry. As far as their takoyaki, you can find better on St. Marks. Closing statement: After indulging ourselves on great food and an absurd amount of beer, I just have one more thing to say: I'm going back next week.

We stopped in Mulberry & Vine to take a peek at the new healthy food stop in the neighborhood. Â It's bright, open, spacious, clean (at least for starters), and cozy. We only wanted a quick look, but the male server by the coffee & cookie area was so friendly we ended up staying. Â He offered us a try of the snickerdoodle cookies - very tasty. Â Then he told us we could try anything we'd like. Â  We went to the other end of the counter by the salads and noticed the asian garlic pepper beef with pickled onions in the hot area. Â The girl by the salads said we could not sample the hot items. Â It's too bad, because we ordered this item. Â I would have to say it did not leave the best impression. Â The sauce was good, but the beef was not tender and it wasn't what I would consider a hot item - I wish it had been warmer to enjoy. Â  We, also, tried a sample and ordered the african curried tomato soup with bits of peanut. Â It was delicious, warming, and satisfying. Â I would recommend this item. I would say this place is nice, but I wish they would extend their sampling as they are a new business - to build loyal visitors, Â people need to find their favorites. Â Their choices of sustainable packaging and local ingredients are an added bonus - these are the types of responsible businesses we should support. It's already, unfortunately, seems to have turned into, yet another TriBeCa mommy hub for the women with nothing to do, but lunch and leave their children's messes everywhere - SNORE! Â For the kind parents that are responsible, give their children appropriate boundaries, and are wise enough to impart manners - we salute you and thank you for bringing up proper citizens of the world! Â  I sincerely hope this restaurant adopts firm policies about the expected cleanliness of their guests - as in, please leave your tables clean upon departure. Â It would be great if guest's children were not running wild through the place and strollers we're not blocking all entrances as well - adults need places to relax, too. We'll be back!

I've been to Sud several times and highly recommend it. I have to follow a gluten free diet, but with 24 hours notice, the owner Guiseppe, prepared gluten free pasta for me. Tonight, I took in my own gluten free bread and they prepared crostini. I have never been able to eat crostini in a restaurant before, so it was a treat. The wait staff are friendly and extremely attentive. The food is great! I would love to see this place packed so that the owner gets the recognition he deserves.

I haven't been to The Smith for a year, and sadly, my return to the restaurant was a huge disappointment. I came for a quick business lunch with my manager. I was craving rice and was really excited to see Vegetable Bibimbap ($19) on the menu. We both ordered the Bibimbap, and it was served on a sizzling stone pot about 15 minutes later along with a piece of baguette and butter on the side (definitely didn't go well with the Asian food...) As a Korean who's been spoiled with authentic Korean food, I have really high standard for this cuisine. Needless to say, I was very disappointed with the Smith's version of the bibimbap. The sizzling pot wasn't hot enough to make the rice crackled, while the pickled carrots were way too overpowering and shielded the flavors of other vegetables like shiitake mushroom, bean sprouts, and spinach. The edamame in the rice was a bit weird because you don't normally put edamame beans in the bibimbap. Also, the bibimbap is traditionally seasoned with sesame oil and gochujang (red pepper paste), but this bibimbap had very little gochujang and canola oil. It tasted way too bland that I basically poured salt all over to make it taste better. I probably just ordered the wrong entree, but if you go to The Smith, just stick with the American food and not Asian.

Gigantic portion. My friend and I shared one order of Local Blueberry Pancakes (which was delicious) and (2) Brunch Sides ( Home fries and bacons). It was perfect. A couple sitting next us were complaining about how much food they wasted - they thought friend and I did a smart thing :) There's nothing wrong with sharing when there are like 4 large pancakes on one order. Only thing I would complain is - its cash only . Â It gets crowded around 1pm so try to get there before 12:30pm. Â Love the vibe, decor and its in Tribeca - PERFECT!

I've only been here for drinks. Sat outside during the summer. I enjoyed the outdoor experience of seventh ave. I must say that tThe sangria was not great, so I wouldn't be compelled to come back. On top of not being tasty - a pitcher was quite expensive. Perhaps they deserve a second chance....

My G/F wanted to check ilili for some time now so it being NYC Restaurant Week she made reservations for Saturday. Â Seated promptly we were taken to our table through a noisy main room. Â After being informed that RW doesn't apply to the weekend (would have been nice to know "Open Table") we ordered. Â Service in my view was slow and while the food was delicate and tasty it had cooled noticiably before arrival and lacked in portion size to the point I would have grabbed some White Castles had they been readiliy available. Â As the ladies would say, and generally when it comes to men and meals....size matters. Â Couldn't agree more. Â Lounge however looked like a place one might enjoy.

Bedouin Tent is different from every other Mediterranean joint I've gone to in that they have freshly made pita! So hot and fresh and pairs perfectly with some hummus or gaba ghanoush. You can take your food to go or sit in the back--there's an outdoor patio area for the nicer days out. Â Great fast-causal joint with delicious, filling food!

THIS. PLACE. IS. INCREDIBLE. GO GO GO GO GO you will NOT be disappointed. The staff is quick, efficient, knowledgable, and really friendly, the cooks are amazing at their jobs and everybody looks like they're having a great time. The FOOD IS PHENOMENAL and for the prices? Totally worth it! The drinks are strong, the bread is delicious. The oysters (you can choose from RI, MA, or CA) are on point, and the food is just...incredible. I had the pork chops...the consistency was they fell right off the bone like a perfect rib. And I also had the squash ravioli...amazing. You can't find food like this anywhere else. I haven't been this impressed with a restaurant in the longest time. It's not huge, so you dont feel lost, but it's not overly crowded. It's the perfect atmosphere. Top 5 places in BK thus far. Absolutely.

I've avoided going to Filipino restaurants since moving to NYC years ago, since the few experiences I had left me disappointed - the food is never as good as Lola's back home! But thanks to Grill 21, I don't have to worry anymore whenever a craving for homestyle food hits. Everything I've eaten there so far is delicious: lumpia shanghai pork adobo (huge portion-enough for sharing) chicken inisal pancit bihon sinigang halo halo special (I got this one with Ube ice cream. Halo-halo was great but the ice cream was a little too subtle on the Ube flavor. Will try this w/ Macopuno ice cream next time) Service is attentive and prompt, place is clean, and the owner Henry obviously puts a lot of care into running the restaurant. Also, they just opened a cute little bakery called "Pan De Sal" on the corner of 2nd Ave and 21st Street where they sell yummy pan de sal and other baked treats. Can't wait to go back and sample more dishes!
Everything was great from the cocktails to the delicate fearful hearty fare...pork was great, the steak for a hanger was very tender

eating at Pies 'N' Thighs is like hitting up the snack stand at a hipster theme park. Except the characters aren't in costumes and the food is amazing. our waiter was your typical disaffected unwashed hipster. he seemed genuinely angered to answer my questions, which only made me ask even more - What's in the chicken box? SIGH What's a Morir Sonado? GRUMBLE What's in the water? Who's buried in Grant's Tomb? Thankfully, he was relieved by another comically dressed young fellow and a friendly little blonde girl. The food was amazing and we'll definitely be back with friends to dilute the hipster experience.

So my wife and our son went to Champs yesterday. It's a fave of theirs because all of the food is vegan/vegan friendly. But what occurred to them yesterday almost changed that sentiment. The restaurant is a hipster place where they play heavy metal, industrial goth type of rock music at certain times, along with hip-hop and other genres. Anyway, the wife who's eaten at Champs many times before said she didn't pay attention to the music until yesterday. One of the songs made references to satan, and she was shocked, as the music was blaring. She called over one of the servers and made some comments about the type of music, saying "I didn't know this was a heavy metal music playing place..." The server commented that it was. My wife was basically making a complaint, saying that she didn't think it was appropriate for our son to hear that type of music. The server said she will speak to the manager, and went to speaking to some of her coworkers, and nothing was done. My wife said as she paid the bill and left with our son, there was no acknowledgement of "goodbye" or a "thank you." I went there this morning to speak to a manager, and I was introduced to the house manager or one of the manager's by the name of Jane. I re-told the situation to her and she asked around what time did it occur, and I gave her the times. She was very apologetic and added, "it could've been as simple as skipping a song or two to avoid this..." She offered for me and my family to come by Champs on Sunday and said she would hook us up with a "Champs breakfast or brunch." My family eats there all the time and if I did not get the acknowledgement I felt my family deserved, I definitely was planning on making this issue bigger than it needed to be. Kudos to Jane. Champs says its a "Family Bakery/Diner." When kids are in the place, adults should defer them, and staff should be mindful of that too.

I have never posted anything about my experience at a restaurant. I must say, I have been coming here for some time and have never been disappointed. It has Â been one great meal after another. It is truly amazing!
This place was packed but there was no hassle at the door. Good place to have drinks as long as you can get a table and squeeze visits to the bar.

Oh my. Oh me, oh my. Where do I begin? Arepas Cafe, I think you've stolen my heart. I am so enamored with you, I can't think straight. I can't stop thinking about the cachaphas or the Mami arepa. The Pabellon is hearty and filling. Passion fruit sangrias? Yes. Please. Keep them coming. I love this little gem in Astoria. The staff is friendly and accommodating, and the food is awesome. They have a great happy hour too! $3 sangrias? Oh yeah. It's all so good. Whenever I am in the mood for arepas, I know that this place can do me no wrong. I can't give you any comparisons between Arepas Cafe and Caracas though. I haven't been there yet (soon!), but I think Arepas Cafe can hold its own as the place to go for arepas in Queens. It's a short walk from the subway (N, Q) and it's easy to get to whether you're coming from Queens or Manhattan. So, no excuses. Get yourself over there!

JH unquestionably has the finest bkfst for the price anywhere. Â Cook staff make wonderful food to order. Perfectly made poached eggs and wonderful deep fried potatoes. Unusual oatmeal pancakes dense and tasty. Service always outstanding and their fresh squeezed orange juice is the bomb!

Delicious bacon cheeseburger- arguably one of the best I've ever had with pint of Lagunitas Czech Pilzner (their only West Coast beer) is yummy for $15 special on Sundays. My friend also loves their mac and cheese. It's a cool space, kind of modern bistro. Prices aren't cheap but this is NYC.

Was very excited to finally try Ssam Bar after reading so much about it in LA.. Food is good, but nothing special. Â The rice cakes seemed to have an identity crisis tho... Pork buns were very good... Trying the Bossam next week, hopefully this one meets expectations.
great place to get street meat. it's the sauce that makes it.

Oh Cheryl... I heard about this restaurant from many of my friends so today I decided to do order delivery. I live literally 3 blocks from the restaurant. Â I ordered (from the menu on their website)- Grilled Pork Chop au jus with Mango Chutney, French Beans and Roasted Potatoes, Grilled Burger with Grilled Onions, Tomatoes and Hand-cut French Fries and Fried Calamari with Chili Plum Sauce. You can't go wrong with that, right? I was told to wait 25 minutes... Delivery guy came after 1 hour!!! Â You can imagine temperature of the food - it was cold! Food.. Oh Cheryl...Don't even get me started... Pork chop was overcooked and almost uneatable, overcooked burger came with very thick slice of raw onion, 1 thin slice of tomato and some crapy, generic french fries ... and that "chilli plum sauce" that came with calamari - I think I have the same bottle of sauce in my fridge. Please do yourself a favor and order from somewhere else.

I've worked around Penn Station for the past 6 years and am thrilled that there is finally a decent option for lunch & dinner. The food is delicious, service is great, and I've never had an issue with getting a table, either at lunch or dinner. I've had the fish tacos, lamb burger, veggie bowl, and brussel sprouts side, all of which are great. I had the pasta last night which was just ok (seemed like a spruced up fettucini alfredo), but everything else was good.

Fresh and clean food. What I love about Emporio is the emphasis on organic cooking and lighter portion sizes. Many Italian restaurant overwhelm you, but I have always had a positive experience at Emporio. Even when ordering takeout (my cousin lives close enough and loves their food) the meals are continually delicious and not too heavy.

I friggin' love this place! I love it enough that even though it's shabu shabu and ostensibly winter food, I'll still be coming here in the summer when it's 90 degrees and grossly humid outside. So I'll apologize in advance for anyone who has to sit in what may be a sweat stained seat after me. The side dishes here are mostly excellent, but the star of the show is definitely the Special Tonsoku hot pots. We generally go with the Hakata Tonton Hot Pot which includes tofu, dumplings, an assortment of vegetables, pork belly, and of course tonsoku (pigs feet). If you're the kind of person who gets freaked out by "weird" food items, this kind of place can get you over that mental hurdle. You may not even notice what you're eating when you taste it mixed in with everything else. The best part of the hot pot here though is the ridiculously tasty broth. Close the show with ramen noodles added to the remaining broth for $4 more at the end of the meal. Also, make sure you save room for the black sesame ice cream!

I've been here twice once for brunch and once for a late night diner. Both times the food was consistently great, made with farm fresh ingredients. The service was also outstanding even though the time we went for dinner was perhaps 10 minutes before the kitchen closed - I've been to plenty of places that made you feel very unwelcome towards closing time, but not here. You get the feeling this is a place that truly cares about what they are doing, they have created a very special restaurant. It isn't cheep but it is well worth it.

I love the restaurant Spice Market over in meatpacking, so when I found out that the chef had opened her own restaurant. I had to try it. Basically, it's amazing. I didn't try the sodas, but the pumpkin fries and the papaya pad thai were unique and amazing.
everything is good here! Â love the wooden decor
My go-to Brunch spot. A great place for dinner. A great place to eat. To live! TO LOVE!! And to think, it's only a few blocks from me in the ghetto.

I've been a fan of Stone Park for some time now- we've had wonderful brunches, lunches and dinners in their cozy dining room. However, over the past 6 months or so both the service and food seem to be in decline. During our last few visits we found tiny stones (yes, actual stones) in our potatoes/hash, many, many bones in the fish cakes, poorly cleaned spinach in the eggs florentine, Â undercooked cod and this morning we had eggs that were not only NOT cooked in the desired manner but were quite undercooked. This has been coupled with waiters that were both inattentive and borderline rude. Not checking on us, not ever coming by for refills of any drinks and then merely plopping down a check without even asked if we were ready to go. I really hope that perhaps its a phase where they're training new line cooks or new staff but i'm worried that it's not. I live right around the corner from the restaurant but this morning's visit has put me off returning for some time. Hopefully they can get their act together and find waiters that know how to actually wait tables and cooks who tend to basic steps like cooking things thoroughly and making sure basic prep steps (de-boning, rinsing completely).

One thing that drawn me here is the handmade soba they have in Â specialized. Had their lunch box and dinner with my friends in 2 weeks, like their lunch box big portion @ $17. I enjoy eating it a lot, especially how everything is presented nicely. As for the dinner I went, probably we went @ the peak hour, so the food took longer than usual but the quality was great. We had chawan mushi, duck soba, seasonal mushroom tempura, uni-tororo soba, buta kakuni, maguro yamakake, and ika meshi. Except the ika meshi and uni-tororo soba are not as I imagined, others are pretty good for a normal New Yorker (since I've tried better in LA).

I had wanted to come here ever since I read about the salted caramel sundae. That was my basis for *needing* to come. First of all, I loved the interior. Clean, modern yet classic, well lit. I miss places like ABC. I started off with a blood red orange bellini. It was great - not too pulpy, not too acidic and not too sweet. A little pricey for what it is, but what do you expect. To start the meal, I had a kabocha toast, which was good. The kabocha was just sweet enough, and it was on crispy bread. I tasted my boyfriends raw scallops which didn't do a whole lot for me. For lunch, I had the pizza with mushrooms and cracked egg. Wonderful! The crust was perfectly crispy and the pizza was loaded up with mushrooms and egg. It was split into quarters and I could not finish it. I'm glad I went with this option at the recommendation of our server. To finish, of course, the salted caramel sundae. The salted caramel ice cream was great - not too rich, with the perfect amount of salt. I could have eaten that alone and been content. The sundae came with chocolate sauce and Cracker Jack-like popcorn. It was almost too rich all together - the ice cream, chocolate and popcorn - but that didn't stop me from finishing it. If you are getting the sundae, split it with someone - it is rich enough to easily satisfy two sweet cravings at the end of the meal.

My hubby's favorite place, out of all the restaurants and markets we've been to! Full of flavor, spicy, warm, comfort food. He even got the delicious green sauce to go. We are coming to the city this weekend, and we are definitely coming again.

This place is always packed and there's a reason why. It's delicious, wonderful, and really tasty. Â Plus, it's gluten free. Â I came here a few years ago with a friend who was celiac and she had not had pizza in years. Â This place made her dreams come true and then the carrot cake at the end made it absolutely perfect. The pizza was great - a thin type of crust with Â a great balance of ingredients. Risottos are really complex flavors and leave you feeling full and light. Their cake can be hit or miss sometimes, but is usually amazing. Â It's a little steep in price, but if you want to splurge stop by and just order a slice to go~
SOUP DUMPLINGS ARE THE BEST! Get this. Plan on waiting and plan on reservations and such.. Just make sure you get these.

Decent spot. Â Pretty dark, so a good vibe for a date. Â I got the most amazing service, and totally loved my waitress last night. Â I'm really picky when it comes to food/drinks, and I loved my drink. Â Can't remember the name, Â but it was a spicy mango margarita and tasted amazing, while being slightly different from a typical margarita. Â Shared three tapas - fried plantains with shrimp on top, plaintains with shrimp stuffed instead, and a vegetable tamale. Â All were decent but not fantastic.
Really tasty risotto, friendly staff. Loses a star because of how cramped the place is. You're practically sitting in the next tables lap.

Le Parisien is a comfy little Euro style bistro in Manhattan. Â When I came here for brunch with friends, this place was packed. Â I could soon see why. Â The food was fantastic. Â I really enjoyed the eggs benedict as it came out both fast and fresh. Â Service was solid. Â Pricing is all relative, but the quantity of food makes the pricing fair, but certainly not a steal. Â Would nonetheless recommend this place to others. Â Just have some patience when it comes to being seated for brunch.
Great atmosphere, the menu is limited, but great to go for tapas and wine. Fantastic wine menu and they always play great music. Â Perfect for a date at the bar or even a group.

i was walking by lombardi's en route to a different pizzeria nearby, when i realized that although i've lived in NYC all of my life, i'd never been. mostly because i hate lines. but miraculously, my friend and I were seated with a wait of 0 minutes!! as in there was no wait! the service was quick enough, and nice enough - nothing spectacular. the pizza was great: crunchy thin crust, very fresh tasting ingredients, good cheese to sauce ratio. i would have preferred a sweeter sauce. also tried the white pie, which was decent, but lacked some flavor in my opinion. the pizza almost met my expectations - it's hard to meet expectations when a place is so talked about. the atmosphere was nice, i appreciated the music, mostly frank sinatra and dean martin (admittedly kitschy, but i still liked it) i really liked the atmosphere (albeit touristy, but friendly) and the pizza, but i wouldn't wait more than 10 minutes for a table to be honest. the pizza is on the same level as a lot of places in this area. i prefer grimaldi's in brooklyn.
A very cozy and romantic wine bar, just a step off broadway, with an interesting and tasty menu. The host is very welcoming, Â and will good care of you
Decent spot for noodles soup.

Definitely a great place to sit down and have some of the best BBQ New York has to offer. The ribs are moist and fall off the bone, the brisket is done just right with their awesome dry rub and for NY it's reasonably priced. Just don't take the food to go because it tends to dry out pretty fast in the paper that they wrap it in.

Sometimes on Yelp, Word of Mouth unveils gastronomical Elyism! Â And sometimes it merely allows a whole in the wall to be tested by the purest of Democracies. Â Either way, I love YELP...and find it's use indispensable. But let's be honest about Banh Mi Saigon. Â It's good Banh Mi, but: -ALL BANH MI IS CHEAP -ALL BANH MI IS FAST -ALL BANH MI IS TASTY -ALL BANH MI SHOULD BE IN THE BACK OF A JEWLRY STORE (and if it's not, it should be in the cellar of a chicken farm, or in the loft of a chop shop, or the meat locker of slaughter house)...this is why we love Banh Mi...it's as if Vietnamese People, perpetually full of glee after the French introduced the Baguette, started cranking out savory sandwiches at the drop of a hat for lunch no matter what circumstances or environments they found themselves in. I love this sandwich...as many of you do. Â I need to be fair to it! Â And in all fairness NEW YORK has plenty of it to go around...Even more than Los Angeles where Little Saigon's exist in pluralistic wonderment. In Los Angeles, if you want Banh Mi (Best or just OK) you got to the San Gabriel Valley (Alhambra/San Gabriel/Monterey Park) area...or you travel to Orange County's Little Saigon (Westminster/Garden Grove)...and even then you're looking at primarily PHO. In New York, what I see is primarily Banh Mi...and I see a lot of it. Â Especially in the Chinatown Area, Brooklyn and Queens. You'd think that Southern Californians...caged forever inside our fanshionable Prius' and 300 Series BMW's would be the ones grabbing any cultural offering of a sandwich and jamming it down our throats on the GO. WRONG! It's New Yorkers that love breed of Fast Ethnic Food because it's cheap and usually hand held. Â HAND HELD AND CHEAP are mutually exclusive fast food characteristics in New York. Since everything in Los Angeles outside of eating a Carl's Jr. Big Ass Taco (Fuck you, I'm eating) is predicated on the need to park a car, get out, enter a restaurant and order....WHY NOT SIT DOWN AND EAT SOUP...OR MAKE A SHAWARMA SO MESSY, IT TOO IS RELEGATED TO A PLATE...or a Burrito for that matter (Chipotle Bowl). Â  It seems that Subway, a New York creation, lends further proof...being the most popular SAVE MONEY and SIT DOWN for Lunch on the 3rd street promenade food...no one's driving through a subway..."not never, not no how!" -The Wizard of OZ No construction workers are grabbing a Spicy Italian on the go and eating it while they drive their truck back to the Condominium Development from the Fast Food Intersection 5 miles away. THE FAST SANDWICH! Â ALL NEW YORK! Â THE CHEAPER THE BETTER! Â THE MORE IT"S PACKED WITH OUT OF THE NORM INGREDIENTS THE BETTER!...Banh Mi, Gyro, Hot Dog, Samosa, Rotti, Calzone, Pizza, etc. --------------------------------- Banh Mi is Vietnamese Sandwich on a French Baguette. Â Usually Pork or Chicken Meat with Pickled Veggies and Fresh Cilantro. Banh Mi Saigon uses a spicy sauce rather than fresh Jalepenos. Â I prefer the later. There's just got to be better Banh Mi out there...especially from what others are saying. The Pork was not even tender meat on this one...just the caramelized sugary substance that should normally encapsulate the tender meat. Â That was a disappointment. Â I've also had better bread. GOOD $. Â  COOL EXPERIENCE - BACK OF A JEWELRY Â STORE. There's better...keep searching. Body Massage...........................................Â­..........

If not for an issue of Time Out New York featuring the best eats in Chinatown, I never would have discovered Spicy Village, one of my fave new cheap eateries. Having lived in Flushing for 25 years, home to some of NYC's best Asian food, I naturally scoffed, since I was sure there was nothing new the TONY editors could tell me. But alas, I was proven wrong, as they led me to this little gem on Forsyth Street. It isn't a very big restaurant, and there's limited seating so there's almost always a wait on weekend nights. The experience can be brutal in the summer as there is no air conditioning, but I say it's worth sweating it out for a bowl of delicious hand-pulled noodles ("hui mei," as it's called here) that'll make you sweat some more from a different kind of heat. The highlight of my first visit was a shared dish aptly named "Spicy Big Tray Chicken." Basically it consists of chopped up dark meat chicken pieces (yes, there are bones), cilantro, star anise, and red chili flakes swimming in a vat of hot chili oil. For a couple bucks more, you can have them add hui mei, which I highly recommend. This will easily fill two people even if you aren't ordering anything else. I also had the spicy beef brisket hui mei on a separate occasion, but it was less memorable. Still tasty though. In all likelihood you'll be back for round two, but if you come to Spicy Village just once, the Spicy Big Tray Chicken is a must.

yummmm Balthazar. It is rare that I have such a vivid memory of the crowd, ambiance and entire night, but when I dined at Balthazar that is exactly what happened. We arrived a little late for our 8:45pm reservation, you deff should make reservations, but the host happily seated us immediately. No sooner had we been seated and started to chat our server came over and asked us about beverages, wine please, thanks. Picked up a great bottle of Burgundy with a little direction and then noticed that everyone was having a great time in the restaurant. The ladies next to us were snapping pictures of their friends, people were mingling and it was a comfortable loud. I had THE BEST grilled vegetable salad of my life here. OMG!! Seriously, I love grilled veggie salads, but this had no lettuce just loads of grilled vegetables like zucchini, squash, eggplant, shallots, green peppers, and more. But, wait the best part was the salad was served with a huge chunk of fresh and extra extra creamy goat cheese. Coffee and bread are just additions that make each meal better. I have been craving a fab grilled-veggie salad since I left New York and I am scared to try it anywhere else.

It's difficult to complain with Ivy's friendly crew and wide selection of drinks and late night eats. Â  Stop in for happy hour or a late night bite and you won't be disappointed with the service, decor or quality. Â A friendly atmosphere with phenomenal wait staff too - Marie is one of the best !

Super cute place! My husband and I stopped in to grab some $1 oysters - yumyumyum! We sat in the garden in the back and got to hang out with the resident doggy, who was a cutie! Staff is super friendly and the atmosphere inside (sort of like the interior of an old train) is really different and warm! I'll definitely be coming back!

Really cool spot. I've recently moved to the area and thought I'd check the spot out (as per the rave reviews on yelp). Definitely a hipster vibe, but that's not necessarily a bad thing, the playlist was pretty solid. The pizza was good, but in my opinion a little overpriced. But with $3 beers I can't complain too much.

I've never been to Thailand, but friends who have been have told me this comes pretty close. No, it isn't one of those Sea, Spice, etc type of "Thai" restaurants..there's no loud music blasting, they have authentic dishes, some sound great, some sound iffy, but it's all in here, and the menu is completely different from the cliche Thai/fusion places in the city (it's in English AND Thai). It's a large space and it looks modern and clean with nice lighting. This isn't a scene, there are couples on dates, families having dinner, and friends just throwing back some drinks and munchies but it is a pretty nice place. The tom yum isn't very spicy, so if you like it with your eyes watering, tell your waitress to make it spicy. Everything from the coconut rice to the pad thai to the saute spicy beef was amazing. The dishes were all very flavorful but wasn't overpowering either. A group of 4-6 would be ideal because you can try a bunch of dishes, their menu is huge! Service is nice and prompt, and the portions and prices are just right. I'm normally underwhelmed by restaurants with such high and numerous ratings (I wasn't too impressed with Kuma Inn nor Del Posto for example) but Sripraphai deserves the high praises. Yes, I went all the way to Woodside (from Bensonhurst) on a random Tuesday night to have dinner here, and I'd do it again.
Definitely one NY's best cocktail bars, hidden as a speakeasy, Hard to get in, but if you do: get the Billionaire's cocktail.
This won the best meal of the trip! Everything we ate was delish and fresh! Â We sat at the bar and just really enjoyed the whole ambiance. Â Totally worth it!

Walking to 14th street for a light snack brought us to Dos Toros Taqueria. We have been a big fan of tacos since our Mexico trips and have been looking for a decent authentic tasting tacos. We got Carne Asada and Carnitas which were both very well seasoned and very good. For $4/tacos, it's a bit expensive but they load up the taco with tons of meat :) Â ... yum! The downside is : this is a very tiny place with few little tables & chairs to dine in, they have a line at times but they work the line fast enough so you get your tacos fast but wait for table longer. We'll come back here and try their burritos and prob find some other place to eat.

I love this place! I went here with my best friend for dinner and we had a great time. We had the mac & cheese as an appetizer which was very good and I had chicken as my entree ( i don't remember the name of it, but it was delicious). The ambiance is very chill and laid back. At night, the restaurant is very dimly lit with candles all over. I will definitely go back again. This place is open 24/7 which is a plus! Gotta go back for brunch.

I am really addicted to turkish food. here falafel is so good i tried many things ( chicken gyro , falefel , hummus , spicy something ) all was good ~ i recommend chicken gyro. staffs are kind ~ usually i bring this to my home

I am not sure if I will come back. Went for brunch again and ordered the Onion soup and a salad. I do not know what has happened but the soup was awful this time. The onions in the soup were white and raw, as in not cooked. The broth was just water, no stock, no sherry, brandy, madiera, red wine or cognac. Just water and raw onions with a crustiness and cheese on top. Â  It is quite possibly the worst onion soup I have ever ordered in my life. I can't imagine how or why a French restaurant would hire someone who can not cook french staples. The salad. While it was a typical salad one gets form a bistro, the dressing was a little too acidic for my tastes. I suppose that is a matter of taste rather than culinary skill though. I am not sure if the chef or the owners are regularly tasting the food but they need to start. Mominette gets a second star because the waiter removed the items from my bill and offered me a complementary dessert. So thank you to the servers.
This lamb, rice and white sauce is so good. Ordinarily, I'm not a fan of street meat. However, I make an exception for the Halal Guys. The plates are soooo good and well-priced!

What a delicious find, thanks to Yelp! On our final night in New York, we decided to spice it up and dropped in Kati Roll Company about 30 minutes before it closed at 9pm. I'm so thankful that we made it in time because what we ate was amazing. What's a Kati roll, you ask? Think of the rich, spicy, vibrant flavors that you find in traditional Indian fare unconventionally rolled up in Â paratha or roti flatbread. Honestly, I've never been a huge fan of Indian food, but the twist that Kati Roll Company does with the cuisine made me feel like I was eating a delicious Indian burrito. Love. There are a variety of roll flavors you can select. If you purchase two of the same kind, there is about a $.75 discount. My recommendation: Â Order at *least* two for yourself. Eating only one would not have filled me up. Two took the hunger pangs away, but didn't overly stuff me. We decided to order two different kinds of rolls to share (we ordered two of each): * CHICKEN TIKKA ROLL x 2 ($9.25): I really enjoyed this. The chicken was cut in small cubes and marinated in yogurt and a variety of spices that had a nice heat balance. The paratha flatbread was lightly cooked, chewy, and was the perfect vehicle for delivering the rich goodness to my fat face. * UNDA BEEF ROLL x 2 ($12.25): Phenomenal. Again, bold, diverse flavors seasoned the beef, and when combined with the egg, all rolled up in the roti (a wheat flatbread), it was sheer heaven in my hands. We also were given the opportunity to try their small Organic Salad. Loaded with a large number of fresh ingredients, including garbonzo beans, it was a nice compliment to our rolls. Eating the salad made us feel like we were getting our vegetables in our diet. Kati Roll Company is embraced by the locals. I spotted no tourists in this location; all of the patrons seemed to be residents who had a genuine fondness of this gem. It's unfortunate there isn't a location in California.
If you are not used to IPA, just dont try it. However nachos and other kinds of food is nice for a bar.

Absolutely, without a doubt my favorite neighborhood spot. Cozy, romantic, candlelit dinners in a classic trattoria atmosphere with local art, a breezy bay window, exposed brick walls and a lovely back garden. Great Italian wines (try the Montepulciano) paired with deliciously simple and fresh authentic southern Italian pastas, crostini, salads, meat and fish dishes. The squid ink calamari pasta and rich eggplant rigatoni a la Norma are to die for. They are also amazingly good for events--we had my bridal shower here on a sunny June Sunday in their back garden. It was absolutely perfect--Tonino and Pepe worked with us on a great menu, and our guests raved about the fresh antipasti, lovely pastas and tiramisu. Plus with unlimited wine, no one's glass was ever empty! Highly recommend!
What can I say!? This place is always closed and never have what I want. Disappointing-

For brunch, we had the lemon ricotta pancakes (the lemon curd is awesome) and breakfast stromboli (so creative to have a poached egg in the center); both were delicious. Â In fact, Locanda Verde has inspired me to make my own lemon ricotta pancakes! Â The cinnamon bun is buttery and flavorful, with just the right amount of icing. Â It just melts in the mouth with each bite. 1 star off: A lot of folks like their olive oil coffee cake; I thought it was just okay. Â This is probably the only thing I would take a star off for. Â  I mean, it's just a coffee cake...

I've been curious about this place for a while. Every time I'm at Fairway, I remember that I keep forgetting to try this place out. It was Friday night when I visited and the restaurant was bustling. Since it was just me dining on my own, I thought I could probably get service for one at one bar or the other - I saw two. I walked up to the hostess station to see if that was an option. While I stood there, the hostess addressed the two people before me, then the four other people who walked up after I'd arrived. "Never mind me," I said in frustration. "Fine," the hostess quipped. And so I left, knowing all I need to know about Brooklyn Crab.

I expected more from cafe Orlin. I went for a nice little brunch on a beautiful day on some Saturday morning with a couple great friends. I found the food a bit overpriced and because of our table location, didn't enjoy the ambiance. We were seated outside (great!) right next to the maitre d stand, people were bumping into and talking over us the whole time. It wasnt comfortable. The rest of the placed looked nice. The food we got was a mixed bag. The pumpkin pancakes were fantastic, except for the texture - it was like fried formed baby food. My med plate was good, but not great. They made what was on the plate, it was good, but I wasn't 100% pleased. Anne B got one of the specials, eggs Benedict. If I could have had any of the specials, it would have been well worth it - $14 for coffee (which was surprisingly delicious), juice, and food!
I ordered the wheat sesame noodles. While the noodles were a good, springy consistency, it lacked any peanut flavor whatsoever. It tasted more like soy sauce noodles instead.

I enjoyed the meal here although I wasn't blown away. This is a modern spin on Tuscan cuisine. Did the 7 course tasting menu. A few hits and misses along the way. Â The fish course was the standout. Â Would come back and try some things a la carte next time. Â A bit on the pricey side. Â Good wine list and decent service.

For a group of 4 seeking recuperation after a late night turned early morning debauchery, Isabella's was a come to Jesus moment for us. We were truly saved by every meaning of the word. We had a couple of friends in town visiting, and since it was a beautiful, warm NYC winter day, we decided to venture to the Upper West Side for a little bit of the brunch by the park we'd heard so much about. We absolutely could not have been more pleased. We arrived to an extremely crowded, homey restaurant next door to the Museum of Natural History. Though busy, our wait was almost exactly what the hostess told us, and when she realized it might take a bit longer, she walked outside and bussed and cleaned a table for us immediately, herself. Since we sat outside I don't have a lot to say about the atmosphere, but the service was extremely friendly and helpful, and that's not due to the complimentary Bloody Marys and Screwdrivers. Not only did our waitress have insightful advise on every dish, but she also insured our hangover remedies never dipped below half empty. You really can't find a friend that cool much less a waitress. Because everything sounded so good, we all tried a different entree, and like the Apostles our life was changed. Everything was delicious, fresh and delicious. From the Eggs Benedict to the steak to the egg sandwich everything was beyond good. I DEFINITELY RECOMMEND ISABELLA'S, and if you see a bizarre Southern couple not speaking while stuffing their faces...IT'S ME.

My experience at Room Service was absolutely amazing. The atmosphere was phenomenal, dim lighting and gorgeous chandeliers -very sensual and chic. The food is to die for -their pad thai is the best I've had in NYC. My friend and I also tried the Green Curry, Coconut Calamari Tempura, Room Service Tuna Tartar, and Pan Steamed Mussels With Thai Herbs, all of which were so delicious. Presentation for all dishes were gorgeous. The service was also amazing. Servers were quick and the food was fast. 5 stars for sure!!

Went here for the lunch special deal with a friend. I'm a bit torn between rating it 4 or 5 stars for the value, or 3 for the quality of the food. I feel like overall it was a solid 3. Look, it was great, I got some tasty fish cakes, peanut dumplings, and then green curry with chicken all for $8 bucks! Its a great bargain and more than enough food. Also nice to have the variety of 3 separate dishes. That being said, as I was eating I thought I would really rather prefer one really great dish for $8, instead of 3 mediocre ones. Fish Cakes: Were tasty. I could taste the galangal mixed in. It was nice to see them on the menu, because most places I've been to don't have them. They were really tiny though, and I mean a bit larger than the size of a quarter. They also did not seem especially freshly fried. Peanut Dumplings: Ok. They were nice and tender, tasty peanut sauce, but the filling was pretty bland. Nothing that special, but I don't really have much experience with this dish. Green Curry: It was nice thick sauce, with bamboo shoots, carrots, one (only one!) piece of eggplant, some carrot etc, with chicken. Not the best I've had, but passable. The curry did have this weird undertone flavor though which I found slightly off. The flavor was definitely not as well balanced as some curry that I've had. All in all, if I need a quick lunch that is filling and a good deal I'll come back, but probably not regularly.

My experience here started out with the best chips, salsa, and guacamole ever. I wiped away all previous experiences with corn chips & salsa/guacamole. I have a new benchmark for great corn chips. I was ready to call for another order and make that my meal. However, their menu items were too enticing to turn down. I ordered up a chicken taco, a steak taco, and a goat taco. The tacos were good. Of the three tacos, my favorite was the steak taco. I love Mexican food, so I will definitely be back to try the rest of their menu. Of all the places that I have been in the past year, this is the one place that I want to revisit as soon as possible. Thank you Robert L. & Julie K. for posting pics of those great dishes.

Their soup dumplings were awesome! Â Their soup dumplings were awesome! Â We had a bunch of other stuff, but all I remember about that meal were their soup dumplings...which were awesome. Â Oh yeah, and their pan fried red bean cakes were a perfect way to finish a great meal.

Pros: 3 different flavors to choose your falafel from, you can also choose white pita or whole wheat Cons: limited space to eat in I've been wanting to check this place out for so long, Â since I love its sister restaurant, Balaboosta, so much! :) and?
