I love this place as well. This was the first falafel place that offered 3 different flavors! :) I picked harissa falafels for my white pita sandwich. The falafels were divine - smaller than your ordinary falafels but packed with flavor and super moist! :) the sandwich is stuffed with pickles, diced cucumbers, tomato, etc. The best part was the falafels and the pickled and shredded white cabbage slaw. The place is very small and doesn't really offer dining experience; however, there's a park right across the street with tables. The price is very reasonable for the portion you get. Can you guys open one in Fi Di? Then I'd go for every lunch!!!!! :)

I Went here for a friends birthday, I was happy to celebrate my friends birthday but I was not happy eating there! I am Hispanic, I know what good Hispanic food taste like, I actually know what any kind of good food taste like and to tell you the honest truth this food was disgusting!!!!!!!!!! it tasted like microwaved food! I love tostones and instead of getting tostones I got something rubbery!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!! Â  not great!!!!!!!!! if your drunk maybe that'll help you!! but if youre looking for good food don't go there!!!!!!!! ( I went here about three months agao, never got the time to write a review, but i actually like telling ppl the truth, ignore the good comments, they must not know what good food taste like!!!!!!!!!!!) DISSAPOINTED

Wow! Â What an absolutely amazing meal. Â The wait staff was extremely friendly. Â The meats and cheeses are fantastic. Â All of our meals were out of this world, but the gnocchi in the truffle sauce is one of the best meals EVER. Â It's a little loud, but I'll take the noise cause the food is 5 stars for sure

Amazing service! I walked in and could not find anyone at the podium to check in with. Once a gentleman spotted me looking around, he came right over and offered me a glass of prosecco and apologized for the wait. We were seated upstairs and let them know we had a birthday in the group. Our waiter was handsome and charming! The Antipasto menu had hardly any meat items on it, so we got veggies and cheese (not necessarily how I would compose an antipasto menu). Entrees were fantastic and the staff even brought out a dessert and a sparkler for my friend's birthday. Overall, great experience, would definitely dine here again!

Came here for brunch. The hangar steak and eggs were cooked perfectly - medium rare and over medium respectively. The potatoes were crispy with a touch of salt, no condiment necessary. A homemade chimichurri accompanied the steak - yum! Excellent iced coffee. Great fruit salad. Be sure to get patio seating in the back.
The food was good (not excellent) but our waiter was extraordinary rude. He told us to "hurry up and decide what we want because he had shit to do". Yes. Seriously.

It seems like there is a common trend at Ngam by reading other reviews. Â I don't usually post but was very disappointed by this place. Â I agree with others that the food is good but their service has just gotten awful from what I remember when they first started in the East Village. Â No one can tell me the specials. Â No one can tell me the price of the lobster dumplings. Â Just for pick-up you have to wait 40 minutes. Â People are rude. Â This is not the way that a restaurant should be. Â They've definitely gotten busier and I understand the need to scale up but to have continued poor service is no longer acceptable. Â I hope they change otherwise there are a ton of thai restaurants in the area with much better service.

Piccolo has become my go-to lunch spot. Â The high quality of the ingredients makes this a bit of an oasis in mid-town wasteland. Â They use good olive oil, real balsamic, great cheese. Â The staff is very sweet and friendly. Â All of the salads are really nice - I especially like the tuna salad with raisins and the chicken salad. Â The frittatas are also always delicious and hearty. Â Good espresso. Â I haven't splurged on a pasta lunch, but when I'm feeling the need for a hot, comforting lunch, that is exactly what I'm going for. Â Only downside is the consistency of the portion size - sometimes I get a nice sized salad and other days it is a little skimpy, but it always hits the spot.

Best pickles ever! for dinner had the honey pickle chicken biscuit. flavors of sweet savory sour and spicy were harmonious. biscuit was flaky and buttery. turkey leg fell off the bone. amazing beer selection puts this place over the top.

This place is small and quaint. We went on an early Saturday evening and it was packed. We had a 30 minute wait which was totally worth it. Everything we had was delicious which isn't always the case in most places. As appetizers we had cod fritters and Spanish sausage. As entrees we had the ropa vieja and vaca frita with arroz moro, sweet plantains and yuca frita. Everything was so good, the portions were good, had food to take home. Our waitress was really friendly and attentive. We left around 8 and there was a line of people waiting to get in. I would absolutely go back to this place. I was so happy with everything and the price for all that food was cheap.

Every time when I get out of the comedy cellar I always get the munchies... Hey getting drunk you always have these weird cravings... The place is located right next to the comedy cellar... Ohh and let me tell you there are massive lines just to get a falafel sandwich... So this place must be good... I finally checked it out and it was yummy... I got two falafel sandwich for six bucks...sadly they don't aspect card...cash only...you can get it with Â hot sauce or white sauce...just ask! Â After I got my sandwich I was pretty excited.. It smelled great even through tin foil... There was only one table and two chairs...no seatings.... That was pretty annoying... So after you get ur sandwich u basically have to stand there and eat... One thing I dislike it standing in a public area eating lol... But everything was good and fresh... Tastes like a yummy salad sandwich..too many tomatoes... Other then that... One of the best falafel I ever had! Perfect to go food!

The best Greek food I have enjoyed in a long time. Â We came here during a midday afternoon the restaurant was busy but we managed to get a seat indoors. Â Ordered the calamari and fish with potatoes and salad. Portions were large and the food was well prepared and fresh--the calamari melted in my mouth. Â We travelled from Brooklyn to this location it was well worth the trip. Â I would return but only mid week when they aren't as busy.

I went to this place with my girlfriend. Â The place is small but intimate for a couple to go and eat. Â The food however is great. They have Sicilian and regular slices of pizza some with pepperoni and some plain. Â The tomatoes that are used are all imported and all other ingredients are homemade. Â You can definitely taste this in their food.

If I can judge this place on it's burgers I could justify 2 stars. Â However, food is not the only reason to dine out. Â Our server was not even just rude, he was downright disrespectful to the point he would not even make eye contact with our table of 8. Â He approached us a total of 3 times in 2 hours to seat us, take our order and deliver the check. We actually had to go to the bar to get water and order drinks!!! Â At 12.95 for a burger no matter how good it is, it was not worth the emabarassment we had since we brought chefs from high end restaurants in NYC! Â  There are too many wonderful spots in Brooklyn to waste your time and money here!
It's the Halal Guys, what else do I need to say?

+Pork gyoza: a pretty wafer-thin pancake of six tightly wrapped dumplings, served with a small side of pickled seaweed. Â That pickled seaweed is the most amazing, sweet/savory/spicy concoction and amps the gyoza to an 11. (You know Spinal Tap references are still so cool.) +Nikujil Kake Udon (a.k.a. pork betty udon): broth was borderline fishy? I don't know what that's about, but the more I ate it, the more I liked it. Â The thin pork betty slices added the right sweetness to balance the broth and the spicy red powder in which I doused my dish. Â (I like my udon like I like my men: Spicy. Hot...and fatty. Â Why not? Â More to love.) Cool addition to the Williamsburg noodle scene. Â The dark wooden space is beautiful. Â The main dining table is communal but large enough to remain intimate.

My fabulous friend took me and my husband out to a celebratory dinner since she could not attend our wedding. We were not expecting what was in store for us at Scarpetta. This place is absolutely wonderful! The bread basket alone is impressive. Definitely a perfect way to start off a delicious meal. We shared two appetizers: the heirloom tomatoes (fantastic) and raw yellow tail (light and fresh) Entrees: We ordered the duck ravioli (amazing - the group's favorite) spaghetti (sounds simple but each bite was a little party in my mouth) and ribeye of beef (moist and flavorful) Of course we made room for dessert. We shared the chocolate cake and loved each bite. This was one of the best dining experiences I have had in a long time and I will definitely be back. If you are looking for a fabulous dining experience, Scarpetta will not disappoint.

This is probably the place to go for brunch in the neighborhood. The food is pretty good and tastes pretty fresh. I'm a bit of a coffee snob so I would say they need help in that department but overall good stuff. Fast and friendly service is a plus.
I go to Tina's for lunch sometimes. Bring your appetite! The pork, yellow rice and sweet plantains are yummy. The coffee (cafe con leche) is awesome too. Â really good stuff.

Maybe 4.5 stars. The service was good, ambiance is comfortable(nothing fancy, but clean, nice somewhat rustic interior), and food was also good. Not unique or surprising menu, but all the food tasted good. If I were to pick one, I'd recommend fluke sashimi and karaage(fried chicken) which were again, not astonishing but simply tasted good. Unfortunately I'm not big fan of sake, but I enjoyed their beautiful way to serve the carafe sake. Tasteful bamboo bowl filled with ice and flowers for sake carafe made the drinking time happier. Yea, I'll come back!

Stopped in here on my way to a show for a couple of drinks. The host and server was really nice, but that was all. We only had the french fries and those were overcooked, dry, just gross. I ordered a Bloody Mary and asked if they make it from scratch she replied "yes, but it was made on Sunday." It was now Tuesday and I've had aged 'Mary's, so I ordered it extra spicy. Damn, that was the nastiest I've ever had. Kind of sweet, not spicy at all and I just don't believe that was made in house. No way. I can't speak for any of the food or other drinks and I don't see myself going back again.

I don't typically review restaurants, but I was really taken aback by the utterly fantastic experience my wife and I had there last night! Perhaps it was the unassuming air, the fantastic wine that we were able to bring with us, or just the warmth that comes from feeling like you are guest in someone's home...or the fabulous food!! We started off with the goat cheese tart and the foie gras torchon. The tart was phenomenal. I highly recommend the filet covered both with just the right amount of foie gras and a sauce that is too die for. Also my wife's duck breast was probably one of the best that I've had in the city. And we finished off with the chocolate lava cake which was truly indulgent by this point but for which I have absolutely no guilt... Â  My only real criticism is that the foie gras torchon had an ever slight liver-y taste, but maintained a solid 3.5 stars out of 5. Overall, I would actually give La Sirene a rating between 4-4.5 stars and would not hesitate to rave about it to friend/family member/etc!!

An incredible lovely dining experience; easily one of the most sublime meals I've ever had in the city. The ambiance is romantic, but devoid of any pretentiousness that sadly commonplace in many upscale NYC dining establishment. The service was refreshingly impeccable and warm. The food was romantically impressive. The porcini flan was definitely the highlight of the trio of appetizer we ordered. My brother simply adored the foie gras. The duck main course was faultless. The chocolate souffle was an indulgent finale to our meal. The complimentary desserts of apple tart was elegantly delicious. The only less satisfying part of our meal was the ricotta gelato with melon soup. Somehow, the dish lacked the symphony and delicate balance of the other dishes. Definitely a memorable food porn evening.

This is a simple, elegantly decorated american steakhouse. I had the rib eye, which was marinated in a soy ginger sauce- it was delicious! As is the loaded baked potato. Service was excellent. Decor was very tasteful and modern. Â It is a bit difficult to find - the entrance is right next to the entrance to barnes and noble.

Came here around midnight with a friend on a Monday and it was packed. Very hipster/Williamsburg-esque but very cute and cozy. We got the little nook in the corner up front. I had the sweet tea and apple cocktails while my friend had the pumpkin beer. We also ordered the mac and cheese, burger and fried pickles. It was my first time having fried pickles and I have to say they were very interesting but delicious. We cleared all our plates. Everyone was very attentive and the bartender was very friendly - my friend even struck up an entire convo about beer with him. Definitely will be coming back.

I am absolutely in love with this place. The chicken meatballs with pesto and arugula are AMAZING, the chicken noodle soup is delicious, the brunches are great, and the chicken pot pie is one of the best in the city. I'm normally not a huge sweets person, but I have to write a separate part just based on that. I LOVE the chocolate chip cookies. They're soft and gooey. I recommend them with a nice pot of earl grey tea and milk. The red velvet cake is AMAZING! I'm not a cake person at all, but this one is awesome. The cake is moist and flavorful. The only complaints are as following: On a good night, the autumn sangria is so delicious and unusual. On other days, the sangria is sour and weird. It really depends on the bar tender. The other complaint is the ever so famous wait. Eating at Penelope (especially during Brunch) peak hours is REALLY annoying! The wait is an average close to an hour and a half! My suggestion is to go to the area early, put your name in, and enjoy some of the shopping on 3rd ave and 35th-ish while you wait for your table. Maybe just put your name in and go to the gym first..that way, by the time you're out, you can enjoy a nice, well deserved calorie filled meal :-) For those of you giving Penelope one star because you had to wait in the cold forever, stop being haters! The food is amazing and most of the staff is super nice and eager to please. Stop being brats and give credit where it's due!

I've been here twice now. Both time have been for eggs and bacon. The eggs come with home fries and salad. Servers are nice, atmosphere is pretty and even though the dining area isn't tremendous, they do a nice job of making it feel open and spacious. I wish the home fries were a bit more crisp and less seasoned with rosemary. My pop ordered french toast that he liked but he wished they gave him butter in addition to syrup. We were too lazy to ask for any. And we didn't get why they served homefries with french toast maybe it should be replaced with extra fruit salad or a small green salad. The chocolate froid is DELICIOUS. Highly recommend it.

When faced with a 9 hour layover in NYC, I thought.... Why not go get Xiao long bao?!?! We headed here on a looooong subway ride, but it was fairly close to the canal stop on the j train. We had a short wait and ended up sharing a table with a couple of strangers, which was weird, but no big deal. We had a feast of food- Xiao long bao, fried pork dumplings, and scallion pancakes. It was all delicious and the portion sizes were large. The two of us were stuffed for 15$. The one issue was we were informed upon getting the bill that they have a 20$ min for credit cards.... That's ridiculous. I told him that the card was all I had, and they accepted it, but what a strange rule. Regardless, I would recommend this restaurant.
Get the chicken and go. The chicken is awesome

This tiny little gem in the West Village does not disappoint. We came here for brunch one Sunday and it was a joy. The staff was very friendly and the food did not disappoint. Â Just so you know, there is not a lot of signage at this place. There is a little owl outside (hence the name). It is a very tiny space, but they hold their own (as do all of the small spaces in the West Village). They had some really great french fries and they also had some super tacos on their brunch menu. While the chicken seemed healthy, I would stick with the taco's if you are trying to do something on a healthy plan. Â The chicken just did not have any "wow factor" although was in no way not good. The pancakes and french toast, while not particularly on the healthy side, were very tasty and it seemed quite popular among those eating here for brunch. Thanks for reading and enjoy.
This sandwich will change your life. Â Don't be a noob like me and just stand there waiting until they finish your sandwich - there's a seating area upstairs you can to go while you wait.

I love walking around LES, it is such a cute area and has such great restaurants! Â Contra is definitely one of them. Â I love the space, the decor and really loved the food. Â We had a 7pm Tuesday reservation and the restaurant was pretty empty when we got there but filled up when we were close to being done. Â This made me happy because it leads me to believe you can always get an early reservation and I prefer to eat early anyway! Â  The food: We started with the bread which was warm and delicious, I don't usually take butter on my bread but this butter was yummy! Next came a beautiful, delicious and hearty beet salad. Â Pretty plating (actually pretty plating all around) 2nd course was a very lovely fish! Â This was my favorite savory dish. Â Whatever that green sauce was amazing! 3rd course was the steak? Â Very good. We also added the cheese which was goat cheese with honey and dark crispy things. Â It looked small but ended up being pretty filling There were two dessert courses - one popcorn ice cream and the other ice cream with crushed ice on top. Â I can't decide which was better but they were both awesome. I would highly recommend this place - my portion of the bill including one glass of bubbles was $100, pretty reasonable! Â  Only reason I did not give them five stars was because our waiter was so rude! Â I love a good watier who gives you useful information and you can converse about the food. Â I could not wait till he left the table. Â Rest of the staff was great!

This place chooses to play it quite safe. Their menu isn't anything new. The decor is the same as 90% of the bar restaurants in this part of the city. The prices are actually pretty good considering its Manhattan. If you are looking for a nice place with music for after work and some nicely made bar food but limited menu then Ugly Kitchen does the trick. Its aight, but I wouldn't come back here again unless a special event was going on.

My Jewish boyfriend and I believed in Jesus Christ the day we ate Lombardi's pizza as recommended by the Mensch on our tourbus... Can I even explain to you how it feels to have cheese, that is already melted, coat and caress and slide down the back of your tongue and the crisp yet chewy crust and not-too-overdone sauce cover the roof of your mouth? A part of me died knowing I was leaving NYC to come back to my Papa John's in California the next day.

Came here once for dinner and found the food rich and very flavorful. Came back again for their Kamayan Night (Weds and Thurs only; family-style feast on banana leaves with no utensils), which was a ton of fun. If you're into Filipino food, ethnic food in general, or interesting food experiences, definitely work out the logistics and try this option out. Really recommend the bicol express and the prawns on garlic rice. No need to fill up on beer; you'll get plenty of food.

For late night cheap eats, this place is excellent. I do sometimes wish their falafel sandwiches had a bit more moisture to them, but you can't beat the falafel. And the price is crazy cheap, and they're open until 5 am, and they are lightning fast. I mean, come on, they deserve their 4.5 stars with over 1000 reviews. Don't come here if you're looking for something gourmet--this is about fast, cheap, good late-night eats. And it's PERFECT for that.

The first time I came here was right after Sandy and there was no line... So when my friend in town asked if I could pick up some macarons for his gf, I didn't think much about it. I went over around 4:50p on a Saturday. The line was outside the store down the block toward 70th (not yet around the corner). I think I finally got into the store around 5:30p and then ordered 6 macarons for her and 2 (vanilla and pistachio) for me and my plus one. The weather wasn't bad so the wait was bearable. I probably wouldn't have braved the line for myself. I never really got into macarons because my first experience trying them the macarons were stale (I waited too long to open to box). This time, they were weren't stale! So light--I really like the vanilla one. Colored macarons kind of freak me out, I'm not sure why. Total came out to $26 for the 8 macarons.

Been going there for 5 years and it s still the best falafel. Fast, fresh, and friendly!! the price is going up a little but you still can not compete with mamoun's!! I sometimres go for the shish kebab sandwich and it is delish with real meat chunks in it, YUM!

yes, it's that good. Â the one's who said it was the best square they've ever had... they were not lying. Â they were dead on. Â take a car out there or be prepared for the long subway commute. Â it's worth it. Â get some spumoni if you aren't already stuffed with tons of awesome pizza.

Pretty good Mediterranean-ish small plates for sharing. Good space to accommodate groups even though the restaurant itself isn't very big. The action at the bar picks up a bit as the night wears on, but it's mostly a dine-in spot. Convenient location right outside the F stop and close to all the LES bars.

I love bourbon and if you like bourbon this is an awesome place. The food matches the quality of the bar and for me that's a great combination. The only thing I find a little weird ist he space which seems neither a bar or a restaurant but thats a minor issue. some of the stand out food was the fried grits and the duck, as well as the sear carpaccio. It was a wonderful meal and I would come here again.

One of the best meals I've had since moving to NY. Â Started with eggplant bruschetta, and our party shared linguini and gnocchi, which was the best I've had. Â The chicken and skirt steak were both outstanding, and the sommelier was easy going and knowledgeable, and made an excellent wine recommendation.

The ginger brisket is AMAZING. But at $9, it's on the expensive side for lunch and considerably pricey for a banh-mi type of sandwich. I do find it filling but considering the amount of cheap delicious food in Â the area, I find Num Pang to come up rarely on my lunch rotation. Go here once and eat the delicious delicious sammiches, but it's a bit too expensive to be a regular place.
If you dont want to make a trip to chinatown great option for viet sand. I just wish the chicken was like the city. Other than that its great and still enjoy the chicken sand.
This restaurant is crowded Â all the time. I don't like their food that much, but their sea food soup wasn't bad at all. I like their tea

The weekday early mornings here are usually quiet and not crowded at all so you can have a slower start to a busy day in the city. On many occasions, my friend and I ditched the 8:00am lectures to enjoy a leisurely breakfast here and we always began with latte art and oj. For a decent price, you'll get a hearty meal out of CafÃ© Orlin and they get the flavors just right and their roast potatoes never disappoints (I'm addicted). Their burgers are also pretty on par with the burger joints in the city so it's a great alternative to brunch. Lastly, I've been here for breakfast/brunch/lunch/dinner and I concluded that no matter how crowded or noisy this place gets, the atmosphere remains unchanged and that is - naturally cozy and comfortable, which is not offered in most places in the city. Too bad I don't have early lectures anymore.

Cute little place in the West Village. For the relatively low prices, the food was surprisingly good. Had the brie drizzled with honey and pine nuts to start, then the tortellini with crab meat and sun dried tomatoes. The ambiance in the restaurant is nothing special, but if you're facing out, you get a nice view of 7th Avenue South.
The Empanadas here are great better than a lot of other so call latin restaurants. Â Recommend the Spicy Chicken Empanada and not the Viagra which could not figure out the tastes

Had a great meal here. Â The owner and staff were very hospitable. Â The food was delicious; from the home-made wine & bread to the rack of veal straight from the butcher. Â Prices are above average for the neighborhood but still definitely worth trying. Â I'll be back!
real deal. real food. no BS. good prices. big portions. fresh and delicious. it's one of the reasons to live in NYC.

Absolute must try! Sports the "Best Bartender in the World" & "The Fastest Bartender in the World" in the upstairs lounge - both will wow you with the specialty drinks that they can craft if you just mention a few things that you like in your cocktail. To eat - get the scotch egg! Everyone always looks over and ask what it is, then orders it themselves. It's darn good, that's what! (hardboiled egg surrounded with sausage and fried w/ sauce on the side)

four stars because they will not let me make a reservation. Â Definitely have to get here early because the crowd gets ridiculous. Â The later you come, the longer the wait. The must try - pork bun appetizer. Â wowzers. the ramen - pick the description for the broth that you like because honestly, they are all good. dessert - green tea creme brulee - delicious. A little on the pricey side but you cant make this stuff at home. Â The most I do at home is add in some spam and an egg...call it a day. Happy eating, suckers.

Cheap, delicious & healthy!! Ofcourse, I want it! Â The best part about this place is that they are super fast, extremely busy so surely the food is fresh! This place is so alive. Even @ 2 am people are standing outside in a line. That experience of eating tasty food @ 2 am in the midst of fifty other strangers is rewarding in itself.

My P.I.C discovered this place and I haven't thanked her enough. The flavor in our crawfish/shrimp bag was so good that I actually scooped up my Mac n cheese (also delish) and dipped it in the sauce. It was amazing. The catfish was damn near perfect. Lightly crisp on the outside, soft flavorful fish in the inside, Complimented w/ Cajun fries. Loved it all. Gumbo, was the only disappointment. Literally ignored it after 2 tries. That was fine. I had enough with the rest of the food. Bartenders were cool & lit up when we asked about whiskey. Elbow to elbow at the bar. Need more space! And people need to stop crying about the "cash only"; there's ATMs & banks all over manhattan. Put a H on your chest and handle it. Credit card babies. I'm coming back!!!!

I've been coming here for a while now -- since the place opened. "Kid tested, Mother approved" in terms of the food quality and the friendly service, but I have one better for you tonight: My Mom -- toughest food critic I know -- gave this place a "two raised eyebrows" stamp of approval. (From a hard-as-nails Greek Mama? That's about two stars more than Yelp allows.) We're getting our Arnis from BB now.

This is definitely one of the more fun speakeasies/cocktail lounges in the city. Frankly there are just too many of these in the city...usually they're nothing but overpriced cocktails with nothing else to offer. Employees Only, however, is different. This spot usually seems to have a rowdier crowd and they even offer a late-night menu with some pretty damn delicious food items. One of our friends secured a table for us early on and we were able to enjoy the music and the food while tucked away in the back. They've got great oysters, truffle fries...and their drinks are on par with that of other cocktail lounges. It's a bit pricey...but this is definitely something that you should already know going in. Definitely makes for a fun spot if you're ever in the area late at night.

Best bowl of pasta in town. Â  Its a small spot, very few tables, but worth a visit for lunch, trust me. Â Real Italian joint with real Italian people, a great house red wine by the glass and extremely reasonable prices. Â I don't know about you, but I hate paying $15-$30 for a bowl of pasta. Get the Penne Arrabbiata and you're welcome.

Also: THIS IS A JAPANESE SHABU SHABU PLACE. That means the broth you cook the meat in is flavored only with dashi and the only real flavor you get is from the ponzu and goma-dare. If you can't deal with simple flavors you should look elsewhere. I'm kind of pissed that someone reviewed this place badly after expecting a Korean shabu shabu; that's super different, and should be treated as such.

If you know me (at all), Â I LOVE pork belly, especially kakuni. What is kakuni? Kakuni is chunks of pork belly simmered in soy sauce, mirin, sake, ginger, and other ingredients for hours. I never thought of putting kakuni into a sandwich so I give 5 stars just for this dreamy sandwich. Joju expanded the boundaries of all bahn mis by putting traditional dishes from other Asian countries besides from Vietnam. My friend was raving about the bahn mi fries so I decided to make a pit stop for a quick lunch. The fries are just okay but the "works" made up for it. Think of nachos but with fries and special sauce (brown sweet sauce?), green sauce, spicy mayo, daikon and carrot pickles, and diced jalapenos. Pretty spicy yet so addicting. Now, the bahn mis. I got the kakuni and my boyfriend got the lemongrass chicken with a runny egg (free with Yelp check in). WOW. The meat is flavorful, bread is toasty, and the pickles are tangy. Major(MAJOR) party on my taste buds. My sandwich wasn't spicy because I didn't know I had to ask for the jalapenos. Still tasted great, plus I already got my jalapeno fix from the fries. The only thing that was a let down was the frozen Vietnamese coffee mocha with whipped cream. Nothing special about it. Definitely will be back to try the grilled porkchops bahn mi, beef bulgogi bahn mi, and the kimchi fries. And if the classic and bbq pork bahn mis are good, this will be my go to spot for bahn mis from now on. Don't forget to check in for the free egg! Might as well spend a couple of more seconds if you're already on Yelp. Thank you Joju for the wonderful bahn mis!
Eh. The strawberry cheesecake is good. I've had better from a few other places. The food isn't memorable. At all. Just a tourist spot, including the Brooklyn location.

Ippudo is like that decent looking girl that has a pretty great personality. Â You're like kinda interested but she's making you wait because she's not sure... so you're like, girl, you're just not worth the damn wait. The primary reason you go to Ippudo is the ramen. Â But honestly, the ramen is whatevers man. Â The broth isn't smooth, the pork isn't juicy, the noodles are ok. Â It's one of those things, that's solid on a cold day. Â It's that, ehhhh sure feeling. Â Let's do it. Here's the problem with that. Â It's trendy and cute, great place to take a date. Â You know what that means? Â Like all things trendy in New York City, you're gonna get a beast like wait. Â An hour minimum folks. Â Is mediocre ramen really worth it? But remember how I said this girl has a great personality? Â Well she does. Â It might not be the main reason you go to Ippudo, but their appetizer, the FREAKIN PORK BUNS, holy crap. Â They're ridiculously good. Â If I could just buy a million of those, I would just bath in it like Scrooge McDuck does with his money. Â That's how good these pork buns are man. Â It's just a perfect blend of fat and lean meat. Â Oh geez. Â I'm drooling as I type this up. Â It's as if an angel sliced that perfect piece of pork, sauteed it in a zesty and mildly spicy sauce, put a playful leaf of lettuce on top of it, and wrapped it in a cloud. Â Wonderful..... So if this girl is wishy washy, making you wait, move on. Â It's not worth it man. Â Plenty of other fish in the city. Â Like the Hot Girl on 52nd.... Totto.....

I came here on a weekend night during their soft opening, and they were serving small plates only. I split the nuts, chicken wings, jerky and ribs. I enjoyed the nuts the most; they were glazed with bacon and figs. The ribs were especially small, and kind of dull with a glaze no more special than teriyaki or something of the like. The jerky was tough and seasoned well, as all good jerky should. The wings were okay, if not memorable. I'd be interested in their entrees, so I'll take the soft opening with a grain of salt. Still, I left a bit disappointed.

Love it here, as long as I don't have to wait too long because as soon as I get here I'm starving! The pork buns are terrific (although i enjoy Momofuku's more) and the ramen (especially the Modern) is crazy good. I love the giant spoons that you get and I'm a sucker for the crazy yelled Japanese greeting. They also have some sort of tasty tofu dessert thing that's very good.

I like Amy Ruth's food as I've been frequenting this restaurant for many years. I find that the food over all is good but has changed over the past few years and continues to change not necessarily bad but original styles or recipes tastes better. I love their salmon croquettes and cheesy grits! It's one of my favorite go to meals and I order it ALl time. I realize that the recipe has changed and it doesn't taste as good as it did about six months ago. I don't know either they have a new cook or a new recipe but they should go back to the old recipe, it tastes better! And the biscuits are too thick sometimes. Doesn't taste flaky like a biscuit, not completely bad but can be better! The mac n cheese is always amazing and the chicken and waffles are to die for. The sweet tea will give you diabetes but it's worth it. It always packed in the afternoon and for dinner so breakfast is your best bet for seating without waiting on the long line. Overall, good food but can always be better.

This place is amazing. Friendly staff. Great food and drink at an even better price. Great for groups and or date night. I just hope it stays under the radar so I can continue to keep getting reservations!

The food is a bit on the pricey side, but hey, it's New York. Â The eggs benedict weren't anything special, but it was as delicious as other eggs benedict from any good place to eat it. Â The full English breakfast was a big portion of food. Â The food was just a bit above average. Â The decor is nice. Â Service is great.
I want to eat here daily. oh man the pork buns, the hanger steak was so amazing and tender. the chicken oh man. the sake lemonade. there's only so many words for how happy i was.
This place is awesome. The man who runs it and takes your orders is so nice, and I've tried a ton of stuff on the menu. All delicious. And cheap! We get it once/week, at least.

One of Mario Batali's newest creations, this food market is stocked with the finest products from Italy and locally sourced produce. In addition, it is also host to 12 different restaurants and food halls (including an open-air beer garden on the 14th floor). The restaurants are spread around the market and correspond to each section they are placed in (Le Cucine El Pesce is in the seafood section). Only Manzo takes reservations and the Birreria will start taking groups of reservations next month. The food is great, the wait can be a while, but just remember you can buy yourself a glass of wine and walk around the whole store in the meantime.
price:reasonable service: 4 of 5 atmosphere:4 food: authentic Â and delicious

I was Born and raised in this City ( I'm on the wrong side of 40 ) , and this slop which looks like something that you would scoop up with nachos is not pizza or good . Most of these positive reviews have to be coming from starving students and displaced Hipsters pretending to be natives and who wouldn't know a good slice either way .
Best. Â Burger. In. Â Manhattan. Â Also, I like their brussel sprouts. Â Any place that can make me like brussel sprouts deserves 5 stars. Â Nice vibe to the place.

I was on an Urban Oyster Food Cart tour that ended with this stop. Â  The mini wafel with the spekaloos spread was one of the best things that I have ever eaten. Â The spread was sweet, but not sickenly sweet - perfect. Â The wafel had the best texture with a slight crunch. Â I could have eaten SOOO many more. Â Everyone should experience a true Belgian wafel and definitely the spekuloos. Â YUMMMMMMMMMMM

Had dinner with a girlfriend here last night and the meal was deeeeeeelish! Â I can't wait to try it one of these weekends for brunch! Â Although I hear its pretty crowded for brunch. Â We arrived for dinner a little after 6 and were seated right away. Â For the next hour or so we sat w/ only a few other small groups in the restaurant. Â By 8-ish when we left the place was packed. After reading through their pretty nice menu we deiced on a pitcher of sangria and a mac and cheese app to start. Â Both were fabulous. Â The mac and cheese was the perfect start- it was so creamy and perfectly cooked. Â  Next we opted to split two meals.. the Arugula and Warm Chicken Meatball Salad and the Warm Brie & Green Apple sandwich with ham. Â The meatballs were seasoned just right and when paired with the arugula and pesto vinaigrette it was perrrrrfect. Â I could have easily enjoyed another plate of these.. but I had half a sandwich to enjoy! Â The brie, apple adn ham combo was very good. Â Not as fabulous as the meatballs but still pretty tasty. After eating and drinking all of that you'd think we'd be stuffed but there is something about the lightness of the food that fills you up but doesn't make you feel like the fat kid at the table. Â We decided we both needed dessert and tried the cupcakes. Â While the vanilla vanilla was a little dry (according to my friend) the vanilla with mocha frosting was moist and very good! Â While I wouldn't go there just for the cupcakes I'd definitely cap off my meal with one. Overall a great experience at Penelope. Â I'm looking forward to my next visit!

Despite the heat, I've been craving ramen of late, so early last evening I headed over to Chuko to try out their fare and I'm so glad I did! Â I initially headed to a spot at the bar right in the middle, but one of the staff was kind enough to point out that the position would put me right in the draft of the AC unit, so I scooted down a few stools closer to the door and was much more comfortable for it. Â (Even with the warm temperatures outside I'm too often chilly inside...I dislike AC.) Â So, right off I felt well taken care of, which was appreciated! I started with the Crispy Brussels. Â They're insanely delicious. Â Definitely a must try! Â Carmely and sweet, yet spicy - and the combination of the peppers, peanuts and fish sauce is delightful. Â For the main attraction I got the Miso Ramen with Pork. Â The broth is flavorful, but could be deeper, other than that - I had not one complaint. Â The taste of the noodles, with the scallion and corn and pork is spot on. Â And...ohhhh the pork - Â just the right amount of rich fat to offset the meat - yum! Â The portion was typically more than I can finish - but I housed the Brussels, so perhaps next time I'll do a couple small plates, and then the following time solely a bowl of ramen and no small plates... Â And trust me, there will be many more visits to Chuko so I can better master the ordering!
Great pizza !!, even the kids can tell the difference , mine have become experts.
Went back yet again and still way too much MSG. Left with a soaring headache. Will have to pass on this place despite their pleasant tasting sandwiches.

so i know this place is chieu chao but they speak vietnamese here. they are known for their noodle soups and a few rice dishes. i would stay away from the appetizers and veggie dishes as they are not always fresh. food can be quite salty but i think most asians prefer it that way.

Pancakes without the 'tude and the lines". Â Empty at 10AM Sunday with super accomdating staff. Â Good selection of brunchy and lunchy items at pretty reasonable prices. Pancakes tdf and cooked dark to order. Â The "pancakes" come with bananas and strawberries and are unusually delicious. Â I ordered bacon with and it was thick and also cooked to order. Â Nice roomy, faux French bistro style interior with tables not to close to one another. Â Great Brooklyn Brunch!

What are the odds that I would find this place on a random stroll in NY. When I saw it, I immediately thought to myself...CHEEEESSECAAAKKKEEEE!!!! I was certainly not disappointed. I live in Miami and the closest cheesecake to me is at The Cheesecake Factory. It's really all I know as far as cheesecake goes. So okay, I stopped in for a slice of pie with fresh strawberries. It was really cold that night and I had planned on getting my slice, walking back to my hotel to enjoy it there, in the warmth of my room...NOT! I just couldn't wait so I popped the container open just for a taste. One taste turned into me devouring the entire slice as I walked, attempting to maneuver thru the crowd of people. I wasn't wearing gloves so my hands were ice cold...But I couldn't put the fork down! It was SO GOOD...So freaking good!! The cheesecake was a nice creamy white unlike the one at The Cheesecake Factory which is more of a light yellow. I loved it!!!!! I want more....unfortunately, I'm back home now and I will not settle for Cheesecake Factory!

One of my new favorite lunch spots! This place is tiny, less than 10 tables i believe. Feels a bit crowded, but good service, reasonable prices and portions, and tasty food make up for it. I had the prosciutto sandwich and it was delicious! Excellent fresh mozzarella, decent prosciutto, and no sogginess in bread, I was content. Plus, those olives on the side was a great addition to my meal, and all that for $8.50. I'm definitely coming back. Do note that this place is CASH ONLY, so make sure you bring enough. Enjoy!

Trading Post has a restaurant and bar upstairs and what they bill as a 'whiskey den' downstairs... Honestly though, it's all the same, a 2-story bar-restaurant with exposed brick walls and candle lighting making it a sexy enclave for a date spot, or a flirtatious happy hour with co-workers. Â The food menu is small and consists mostly of artisan flatbreads, which were delicious, and small shareable plates. Â Located in the still Sandy recovering South Street Seaport I'm definitely a big fan of Trading Post and bringing business back to this neighborhood. Â Due to it's size this is a great spot for a big group happy hour or dinner. Â Staff is very accommodating and the cocktails are great. Â Now go check it out for yourself...

Initially, my bf suggested coming here since he loves shellfish, especially clams. I was a little wary when he first mentioned that this place serves raw shellfish. I thought, Yikes! I hope they serve other things too... So, we ordered the shellfish tower, with cocktail shrimp, crab legs, clams, and oysters. (It was supposed to come with sea urchins as well, but they're out of season right now.) We also got the fish soup and wasabi tuna spring rolls. The crab legs, clams, and oysters were delicious -- so fresh and juicy. Oh Fish, you definitely have intrigued my taste buds. The fish soup was sensational, especially with the cold shellfish. One shellfish, one sip of the soup. The wasabi tuna spring roll was soooo good. The tuna was cooked perfectly and the wasabi sauce was great. It tasted like a warm sushi roll, without the rice of course. I loved it. We also ordered two glasses of white wine, which went well with the salty seafood. And they served us some cornbread and biscuits before we got our appetizers and main courses. I liked the warm, sweet, and crumbly cornbread. (The customers before us probably did too, because the crumbs littered the seats.) The biscuits were square-shaped and a little dry for my liking. I have to say though, that this is the most quiet and unladylike meal for me. I usually don't like to eat messy foods outside of my home (heh). But since the food was so good and fresh, I gave up my manners. So for all you ladies that don't like messy foods, you better give up your manners if you decide to come here. (They have a bathroom downstairs for you to clean up after your meal.) Overall, I enjoyed every aspect of Fish: the fresh seafood and wine, the courteous service, the warm little fireplace in the back, and the homey pictures on the wall. I felt as if I was on a ship the entire time. Yes, I love fish, but I've never really loved SHELLfish. But Fish has given me a change of heart. Thank you, Fish, for letting me discover all that shellfish has to offer. And thank you, honey, for taking me here. Next time, we have to try the Red, White, and Blue special. =D

I love Amy Ruth's. It's simple, and consistently good. The servers have always been very nice and welcoming to us and are super friendly. Depending on time of day, their cornbread or biscuits that come to your table FREE are sooo good. I love their fried honey chicken, and the smothered Barack Obama. Also, their sweet-tea and lemonade are awesome.
Good food, good vibes. Awesome service! If youre into craft beers this is the only place in the neighborhood has it on the menu.

This has become our go to restaurant in Brooklyn whenever the kiddies decide to ditch us. Â The food is consistently good with a nice ambiance. Â On Sun - Thur, they have a 3 course prix fixe which is a great deal. Â  I am a huge fan of marrow and always order it when I see it on a menu. Â I use Blue Ribbon's variation as the standard to judge all others. No restaurant has really come close to that level, including SP's regular roasted variation. Â But the last time we went, they had a marrow scallop taco. Â Seared scallops, roasted marrow, cilantro, avocado, jalapeno and a quick squeeze of lime juice wrapped in a grilled tortilla. Â Let's just say I have a new standard now.

Decline and Fall: When the south side of Williamsburg was still terra incognito this place was an outpost of quality. Hipster creep has since caught up with South Williamsburg (despite the efforts of the orthodox Hassidic community to keep the 'artists' on the other side of Broadway). It is now way overblown and the last two times we've been there they can't seem to even do the simple things right any longer. Last week I ordered one of their mainstays, the egg and cheese on a biscuit. After a twenty five minute wait it finally arrived. Unfortunately it was not worth the wait. Â The egg/cheese portion of the formula was salty to the point of wondering if the cap on the salt shaker had fallen off during preparation. The poached egg breakfast entre was OK, although sometimes the combinations of what you find under the eggs are quite inedible. For our money the best breakfast in Williamsburg is actually in Greenpoint at Le Gamin.

best shishito peppers in the city. We had a great dinner with delicious cocktails, wagu beef, vegeterian noodle soup(I dont like pork broth), shrimp tempura and breaded chicken. Also you can get drinks at the bar while waiting for your table. Don't be discouraged by the small bar area. The bartender is very nice/cute, prepares great drinks and it is always pleasant to see him!
Taste great, why give a one star? They have an employee there that slacks off near my building for a smoke break and always makes a disturbing crow animal sound and it's really loud.

Though it was a tad difficult to find (the Financial District is my Bermuda Triangle), once I got to this downtown outpost of Luke's Lobster, I was in heaven. I love how consistent the lobster rolls are at each location...and how laid back and friendly the staff is! I went on a Friday night and it was not crowded at all, even though Stone Street, just a stone's throw away, was hopping. There is only one high table, and a few bar stool seats along an L-shaped wall, so I think "to go" is encouraged during the lunchtime rush. But I was able to grab a seat and enjoy my lobster roll, pickle, Cape Cod kettle chips, and Maine root beer in peace after a long week at work. I will be back...often!

Look no further, this is THE best cuban food you will find, better than Miami. Fresh, clean, delicious food. Especially the churrasco! The manager and servers are attentive and amazing. Love this place.

this place is a lot of fun. nice brunch menu and great dinner. i suspect the staff is imported from a happier neighborhood. i've never met servers as nice in astoria. Brunch Burger $8 but you have to ask for cheese. Done
yum yum yum. the tacos. yum. yum. also, the marshmallow ice cream w/ rice krispie treats. love the american-nouveau/korean twist fusion thing. can't wait to go back...

I remember thumbing through a fashion editorial piece in a magazine one day where they used Wonton Garden as the backdrop to the shoot and I thought "how awesome." That's when I realize Wonton Garden is a pretty iconic Chinatown haunt, you don't really think twice to these things when you've been visiting since you're a little kid. They definitely have a pretty memorable design, especially the old school one before the renovations. A pretty open style kitchen, at least where they cook your noodles. I have to admit, for a place that uses Wonton in their name, the wontons are really not that good here by Chinese standards. A good wonton has a thin skin, a certain pork to shrimp to skin ratio, and able to pop in your mouth in one bite. On the contrary, theirs is like the size of an italian meatball and the skin is thick and too much meat. So I don't really like to go there for the meatballs. The secret here is the beef tripe. It's soo tasty. I get it over ho fun (the thicker noodles) and then hit it with some of their hot chili sauce mixed with soy sauce and it's perfectly spicy and salty. THey also make a pretty good pig's feet. I'm not into it all that much, but my friends enjoy it. I can't comment on the staff too much because it's typical Chinese restaurant experience. They don't hassle you. Just know that you have to be patient with them when there's a football game on the tv.
Outstanding dinner spot. WORTH NOTING: lunch might as well be a different restaurant, different menu, service, crowd, etc. bummer.

I was so pleasantly surprised eating brunch here. Â The interior space is beautiful and spacious, the waitstaff uncommonly gracious and welcoming (especially to little kids requesting Mickey Mouse pancakes), and the food well executed and comforting. Â Is the food incredibly unique or gourmet? Â No. Â But the quiche I had was tasty, as was a biscuit I ordered on the side. Â And the prices really are not bad for Park Slope.

Taste just like my grandmama used to make from cuba.My fiance took me for a suprise birthday.I was soo happy to find out this little placed existed .The food so devine Vaca frita with black beans and white rice is just the food we grew up with.The flan was tasty. I don't drink but my fiance said the mojitos were perfect. All of my friends have been here at some time so we couldn't stop feeling nostalgic about the place. We will be back.Too bad you can't really dance but the live music was great .I tried to convince the management to give me the beautiful painting but they said they can't so I understood...

Great new place. Similar type food to Blue Ribbon Bakery but much better. Try the crabcake sandwich. I got the burger which was excellent but I'll admit that I had a bit of food envy. Also, they have a "specialty drink" that has PBR in it. How can you go wrong...

The Counting Room is, quite frankly, just about as great in ambiance as any wine bar could be. It's spacious, rustically elegant with just a tinge of swanky; it's not too stuffy, which is appropriate for the neighborhood. Some friends and I stumbled upon this place after checking out the Brooklyn Night Bazaar nearby on a weekend evening. The main bar area was not very crowded at all when we arrived, although there seemed to be a big private party down in their basement level. There were also some bizarrely dressed girl (bouncers?) guarding the stairs leading down to the basement - and when I saw bizarrely dressed, I mean furry bunny costumes. Yeah, what the heck. All that aside, we had a good time with good drinks. They have a simple but pretty comprehensive menu of cocktails and wines, all pretty reasonably priced. The service is quite laid-back, perhaps bordering on inattentive at times - which wasn't such a big deal since we were all just hanging out.

A high end surprise experience when we expected a 'grille'-like casual restaurant. Service extremely professional and knowledgeable on menu and wine list. Oysters and a truly al dente pasta app made for tasty starters. I had the whole branzino- grilled and flavored to perfection and the wife had the lobster which she thought was excellent. Milk choc malted cake seemingly deconstructed along with a brioche bread pudding closed out our meal. Comfortably full and extremely satisfied albeit for some big$$$- but felt it was completely worth it. Right next to the Conrad main entrance on North End Ave with very limited signage- we were actually standing right in front of it but looking at the maps app had us circle the block completely on a subzero night- but upon arrival it was all good!
Excellent food, and a nice social atmosphere. In a great location in Park Slope as well.

I was hesitant to come to this place because it's so close to Times Square, so I expected it to be a tourist trap. However, after winning Book of Mormon tickets (yay!) my friend and I wanted to have brunch but were too lazy to go too far. They have a $14 brunch menu that includes coffee and a mimosa. The food was pretty average, the service was friendly, and the place was pretty cozy. They are literally next door to BoM and let you pre-order drinks for intermission

yes, i'm the usual californian mexican snob. not exactly like mexican food spots in california, but dos toros might be the most legit mexican food in nyc. Â carne asada is by far the best meat on the menu. Â big portions, good flavor, good price. Â  and their tip jar always says something witty. Â "tip lincecum" Â "hans toro" Â  go check it out, start with carne asada tacos or a quesadilla. Â you won't be disappointed.

High quality authentic Mexican place. The food here reminds me of the Mexican food I am used to eating in Queens. I recommend getting the 3 taco or 3 enchilada special, because one or two of each is not filling enough. You can choose any three kinds of tacos or enchiladas, and it comes with a side of rice and beans. They offer chorizo, carnitas, roasted potato, shrimp, fish and more! The pollo guisado flavor was especially juicy. I thought the enchiladas were better than the tacos, especially with the juicy mole sauce on top of them. Make sure to wash it all down with a bottle of Jarritos too.

I have always thought that having steak for breakfast was for those who were extra carnivorous but having the Bife a Cavalo at Beco during brunch has completely changed my mind. So so good. The prixe fixe is a great deal and both of the drinks (caipirinha and latte) were delicious. Cash only and fills up quickly- arrive early if you hate to wait.

Open 24 hrs, the food is great, the service is quick, BUT after a certain time, the line to get in is literally around the corner. Â If you have 20 minutes to wait, then I highly recommend you go for the mac and cheese.
Warning: the taquitos are not taquitos. It is a small taco with strawberries and cojita cheese. They are delicious though. Get the michelada with negra modelo, it won't disappoint.

The food is great, the ambiance is fun and it's just one of those places where the coffee sucks but the food is fantastic.. but besides that: yes I am a fan! Just step up the coffee game and I will gladly add the 5th star on there for you!

Great Pizza. Â Bucket List item checked off. Â I probably won't go again due to location, crappy parking situation and extremely high priced pizza. Overall once in a life time experience that is not regreted.

Excellent all around!! Food and service were top notch. Â I enjoyed the beer salad and fettuccine with portobello mushrooms. Â This meal ranks as one of the top meals in my life. Â Atmosphere was great and the servers and staff all spoke Italian. I was visiting from AZ and found this place on Yelp, the next time I am in NYC this place will be a requirement! I would highly recommend this restaurant and can't wait to try something new, everything I saw go by looked sensational! Â Thank you to the staff and chef for all your passion and dedication!!
Corn and Pork. Two of my favorite things and put together... you can't go wrong.

Ordered the spicey basic broth. But the broth was so goddamn thick it made the whole eating experience un-pleasurable. I didn't see an option to ask for a thinner broth so it may be my fault for that part but ugh... The other bowl ordered that night was nice and thin. Perhaps it warrants a second chance. I believe in you!

my boyfriend took me to dinner the other night and half way through the our meal i broke out in a cold sweat thinking he was about to pop the question....turns out it was all in my head. Â its all for the best though since we've ONLY been dating for a year now and i think it would have been a shame to spoil such a great meal! ... oh at some point i should probably talk about the food, try the pork chops they were delicious! had two bottles of wine so the rest of the night was a complete blur....would definitely go back.
got food from them .. not what i like but for the price .. can't complaint.

One of my really good friends lives right above this place and has been talking about it almost nonstop for months now. Yesterday, he finally got me to check it out after a few mid-afternoon cocktails. The walk to this place, which really is in the middle of nowhere, isn't that bad when you're feeling a slight afternoon buzz. First off, the place is really charming. It is very unpretentious, has limited, but solid decor, fitting the overall theme. Minus the fact that our table wasn't really intact, it was comfortable and not too loud. I'm not a fan of Williamsburg, or the people, but I felt comfortable enough sitting down to a nice meal here. As for the food, I'm totally out of my element here. I think there is one other comfort food place I've been to in the city that can compare. That place was Mama's Food Shop down in Alphabet City. I really enjoyed my experience there (and should write about it some time), so I was open to this place providing a similarly enjoyable meal. I ordered the Chicken Sammy, which consisted of fried chicken with avocado, tomato, ranch dressing (gross), onion (gross), lettuce and cheese on a bun. The chicken was alright and the sandwich as a whole was decent when you took a bite and got all of the flavors together at one time. I'd like to hope they would put it on a bun that didn't look/taste like it was from the local supermarket, but maybe that's supposed to be part of the charm. We also tried the macaroni and cheese and the blackened baked beans. I'm a bit tough on macaroni and cheese, and I'd have to say I wasn't a fan. Too creamy, not enough sharp cheddar flavor. The beans didn't taste blackened at all and were a little too sweet and creamy, as well. As a whole, the meal just didn't have anything distinct about it. The waitress was even less remarkable. Maybe that goes back to my slight annoyance with the people in Williamsburg. She just didn't have all of her ducks in a row and didn't seem to care about it. All in all, it's cute. Check it out if you're a big southern comfort food fan, but it won't make you feel like your back at home down south.

Came here for post dinner drinks with a couple friends around 11pm on a Friday night. It's a very dark, neighborhood beer/wine bar with a good mix of people. Bartenders were super nice and not pretentious at all. Good mix of 80s and 90s music playing. We managed to get a couple seats at the bar but the place got really crowded over the next hour. Only downside was a slight B.O. smell no matter where in the bar you were - might not be the bar's fault and after a couple drinks we didn't notice anyway. Would definitely come back.

Luzzo's is amazing Italian restaurant and a not-so-hidden gem in the East Village. Best part near the end of the meal, I heard patrons in here speaking Italian to the staff saying that the food is "perfecto", and I take that meant perfect, so more kudos to the restaurant and the food served. Rewind, so we started out with the meatballs which were large and juicy. You get a trio of succulent meatballs. The sauce it was sitting in was sweet and too addictive that I sopped it up to the last drop with the bread served. Got the Bufala 16-inch pie to share with my wife. It's cut into 8 slices. This is the signature pie with buffalo mozzarella scattered all over the pie. There's also a 12-inch personal sized one, but we opted for the larger just to go all out. Pizza is so awesome. When you take a bite and land on the toppings, you're gonna do a happy dance in your seat. Love the coal fired pizza with the crispy thin crust. The end of the crust is spectacular. This is not your typical foldable NY slice but who's to say you can't eat it that way. Gets it in your belly faster. If you have a craving for pizza this is your spot but pies only. For a Wednesday night, place was full for dinner around 8pm but the wait was only 15 minutes. It doesn't hurt to call ahead to see what the wait time is before you trot over to 1st Avenue.

I'm writing this review as my stomach churns from the disastrous pernil i was served at this place. Not only did the pernil taste like it was drenched in orange juice, my plate plus cup of coffee cost me about 21 bucks. As a Hispanic person who frequently cooks this meal and buys this meal, it's not that fucking expensive. The crowd is horrendous, they're lucky i didn't dine and ditch.

First time I saw this place I was amazed to see a restaurant in this neighborhood. I was also amazed at the building they put up. I have always been there for breakfast - it was delicious. I'm in love with the place because of the extra room the kids can run - it's a kids friendly restaurant and you do not have many around. The breakfast is really good. But my review is on the dinner. Friday night - we needed to go out to eat but did not know of any kids friendly restaurants. I remembered this place and called up and they are serving dinner. So let's go. I got the lamb shank - really good. Kids had the soup and the omelette - all very delicious. Aside from the odd location it's a must go

I loooove this place!!!!!!! the best Cuban food outside of Cuba. family like warm environment that is always welcoming. my friend introduced me to this place and I've been hooked ever since. Honestly every dish is excellent and fresh. I think ill go there tonight again!!!!

I was in NY on business again and I had a business dinner at Lupa. We got the beets and pistachios and the olives as appetizers. Then we had the sweet potato agnolotti which was to die for and the cacio e pepe for pasta. For our main courses I had the fluke with brussel sprouts and potatoes and my boss had the saltimbocca. My fish was cooked perfectly. For dessert we had the tartufo and it's one of the best desserts I've ever had. Lupa was still as good as I remember it. DELICIOUS. I will probably try to dine here every time I come to NY.

This is such a intimate and enjoyable spot. Went here To celebrate a friends accomplishments and they served white sangria with JALAPEÃ‘O!!!! Yeah you heard me right jalapeÃ±o! And they had quesadilla to die for, it was so delicious. The ceviche was excellent. The atmosphere was enjoyable the small backyard patio was so cute, very cute for couple very romantic. The ceviche was good. I totally would recommend this spot.

I came here last week for dinner with the boyfriend before seeing Avenue Q which is just down the block. I think we got here right around when the dinner rush was starting at 6:30 cause it was pretty full. They do not seat people without their full party present so there were a few people waiting on the bench near the front. The place is pretty small with six small 2 seater tables, a table running alongside the wall with a few elevated seats and one large table in the very back. The daily special chalkboard hangs above the large table. There definitely isn't much elbow space and there are coat hangers on the wall. Definitely enjoyed listening to the Thai pop music playing while waiting for the food. Following Yelp recommendations, we ordered the Chicken Curry Puffs, Roasted Ribs and 2 Thai Ice Teas. Everything was delicious and I think the Thai Ice Tea is one of the best ones I've had in the city. Just a note, it no longer comes in a ceramic cup like it is shown in some of the Yelp pictures. Also, the tap water bottle is super cute too! I got the Ratchaburi noodles and the boyfriend ordered the Wok Chili Tumeric Beef. I happily munched away at my noodles and while my boyfriend enjoyed everything else until this point, he couldn't handle the heat of this dish. The waitress had asked earlier about his tolerance and I did too from my eating adventures in Thailand but he felt capable. We had to order another Iced Tea so the milk could calm the burning fire in his mouth. He was not able to go on like Celine Dion. This place can get pretty noisy and feel cramped but I enjoyed it and think it's great place for a date. Service is prompt and food comes pretty quick. I would love to come back soon to try their desserts.

Really 3.5. The house made gyoza and kimchee is outstanding. Spicy pork broth had great flavor. Very creamy and silky, almost too rich. Little higher priced then I would have expected and the place had no heat. I was a bit cold until I got my ramen. All in all a good experience.
got 8 macarons, although they were tiny they tasted like heaven. will come back some day!
Joey. Great job last night. Thanks for taking care of us. Sorry we stayed so late. Cult

The Islands serve the best Caribbean food I have experienced. The food is not too salty and very filling without eating large quantities. Â I like to think that filling food is prepared with love and care. Â The staff are friendly and tend the provide excellent service. Â  The place is small and the decor is simple, but it is a gem and I hope they remain open for decades to come. Â Restaurants are business with a product and Â people have options of where to spend their money. The Islands' combination of great food with great service place them in a special category. If you prefer expensive places with big names, fancy accoutrement, lack luster food, and subpar service then this is not the place for you. If you prefer substance over form then enjoy.

I've been three times now since I teach nearby on Mondays. Had one bad experience with a disinterested counter clerk who didn't volunteer any information about toppings, so I ended up with a piece of meat on a bun. The most recent trip however was pretty much the opposite. I was asked what I wanted on the burger, and it is a generous amount. I sat near the door on a cold day, and a very helpful young lady named Miranda Â ensured that I wasn't blasted with Arctic air, and just generally made sure that my Shake Shack experience was everything it could be. That is the kind of visit that makes somebody a regular customer!

The bad news: I was sharing and my reluctant spouse-person drew a line at the sweetbreads. So I will have to return for those. Pretty much everything was awesome and clever. The salt and pepper shrimp are a play on Chinese American fast food, the mushrooms and barley with the duck are better than Prime Meats' mushroom spaetzle, which is saying a lot. Drinks are especially good, and clearly designed to work well with the food. A smoky tequila cocktail was among the best I've ever had.

Oooh my first Michelin star restaurant! The service is on point here. Definitely a very classy restaurant and the wait staff makes you feel so welcome! The hostess at the front was also very warm and courteous. Monkey bread is a must have! The bread is oh so soft, and though the spreads were jarring at first, I couldn't help but keep going back to the seaweed spread! And when the food arrived, oh it was so visually appealing! For our starters, we chose the Pork Belly and the Egg. The pork belly was delicious, although nothing visionary. For the Egg, I was a bit put off by the runny egg yolk, and the whipped (?) egg white, but hey, I like trying new things. We had the pasta special of the night, which was some sort of duck tortellini (the name escapes me). Heritage Pork and Rohan Duck were both very good, but nothing phenomenal. Mainly, I loved the service and the atmosphere. It was such a pleasant dining experience! According to the Michelin Guide, the criteria for one star is "A very good restaurant in its category," whereas two stars is "Excellent cooking, worth a detour". I suppose the one Michelin star rating is appropriate for Piora, since I'm not sure that the food would necessarily be worth a detour or a 3-star "special journey,". However, the food is yummy enough that you would definitely regret not swinging by if you're in the area.

I'm sorry - bars are about vibe and this one is just too cool for me. They have an impressive list of beers, but the prices aren't on the menu or posted! As in: if you have to ask how much, go away. The food is actually decent - to be fair. If your mission is to convince your friends that you're too cool to care about price when you get a beer, this is the place. You might even run into me - I'll be the guy going down the list of 80 or so beers, asking the annoyed bar tender, one-by-one, how much each beer costs. Feel free to join me.

Came here for a late lunch around 2pm. Place was empty, with only 2-3 people dining inside the restaurant. I sat by the window and my server came to greet me and take my order. Server girl was friendly and nice and my water was refilled many times throughout the meal. Downside might be that the price of the lunch items. $16 for a small entree and $4 for a "home-made" Seltzer when places nearby have pre-fixe lunch specials including an appetizer and a drink for less than $9 is kind of odd and weird considering we're in East Village and not Midtown. One funny thing was I think I saw either someone that looked like or it was really Chef Hooni himself, owner/chef of restaurants Danji and Hanjan having lunch here today in the table right behind me so that was quite an experience. Anyways, back to reviewing Maharlika: I got the following: Pampangan-Style Sizzling Sisig with Egg: $16 -On their website, it says "To Share". Apparently this is NOT shareable as it's not a big portion and sized for 1 person only. But for people with HUGE appetites like myself, it's not worth $16 and better off eating 2 burritos at a nearby Mexican bodega or something. Regarding the taste and presentation of the food, well, this dish consists of hand chopped pork belly, cheek, and ears, & snout cooked 3 ways and set in sizzling skillet with bird chillies, kalamansi, & egg served with Garlic Rice. Don't get me wrong, food itself was actually pretty tasty. It was savory and meaty and definitely something new for me as I've never had Filipino food before. The Garlic rice was different and the Sisig had an addictive taste to it. Lumpiang Barquillos (you get 3 pieces) $5 -Reminded me of a cross between Taquitos (7 Eleven) and the American Chinese takeout egg/spring rolls but thinner and longer. It had a crispy texture and was filled with beef, pork, water chesnuts and served with sweet carrot salad/puree. Home-made Seltzer $4/glass -They have both seltzer and juice versions and are priced the same. The flavors they have are: Ginger, Kalamansi (like a Sour Orange or Naranja Agria), Strawberry, and Cardamom-Lime. SKIP the Seltzer, get the juice instead. Your $0.99 Choice brand Seltzers you can find at a supermarket are far superior and for a $1 more, you can get a draft of beer instead I feel bad giving this place 3 stars but definitely the portion and the prices were the main reason. The staff are really nice and hospitable. Maybe they should consider going 'pre-fixe' like many other restaurants in the area and change/lower the price a bit..I mean lunch is always supposed to be a bit cheaper than dinner and I was surprised the Sisig's price was the same for both lunch and dinner. Yikes~

I wish this place was near my office. Great place to have a sit-down lunch with nice, healthy options. I got the quinoa/veggie bowl with salmon-very filling portion and very tasty. The dish was $19 so a little steep for lunch but honestly a much better option then the stuff around Bryant Park which is more than that for less quality food. Apparently I'm not the only one to like this spot though-my Mom and I showed up at 12 sharp on a Wednesday and still had to wait about 7 min for a table!

I was really excited to go to PT since it had so many great reviews! My boyfriend was getting back from a work trip late on Saturday which happened to be our anniversary so we wanted a nice place but a place that was also low key and close to home. After reading the menu I was pretty much sold once I saw the asparagus gratin. There was no problem getting a reservation and the place was pretty crowded for late on a Saturday night so I'm glad we made one, but they didn't even ask when we came in - just sat us. It's like whats the point? What if they sat another couple who didn't have a reservation? But really it kind of went with the whole vibe of the place - "hello we have a table waiting for you, welcome friends!" I got the mixed green salad and we split the asparagus gratin. Salad was delicious, I mean you really can't mess up a basic salad. The asparagus was really really good but when I think of gratin I think of something more casserole like - this dish was literally 5 pieces of asparagus on a plate with cheesy sauce over it. Like I said, it was really good - but also $14 for a handful of asparagus stalks. The boyfriend got the carpaccio, and said it was awesome once he seasoned it a little more. A lack of seasoning is really what brought our meal down. I got the spinach ravioli and he got the pork osso buco and we were both really satisfied but we both thought the meals were bland. I always thought salt and pepper should be to taste, not to season in general. With our meals I definitely felt like there was no thought put into the seasoning which is sad because everything was actually really good. Just bland. The wine list was really extensive and had a wide price range. Went with a carafe (cause I didn't really need to drink a whole bottle myself) of a wine I've never heard of before. I like carafes, I think it's better to take a risk on that rather than a full bottle. Overall, the service was great, the food was good (but totally had potential to be better) and the price was totally reasonable (minus that stupid asparagus gratin). Plus the space is really cute and cozy - I would go back for wine and appetizers at the bar anytime! I would much rather give this a 3.5 and the service is definitely worth a 5 - but I think the lack of seasoning brings it down to a solid 3 stars overall.
Best coffee I have ever had in NYC.

Noodles are the best. I am totally impressed by this place and their authenticity. I like to show up randomly and get the things I need and my refill and just move on with my day. This is my go to place for lunch break.

Tapas feeds the little beastie in me who wants to sample everything on the menu. Salinas portions are perfect for two, and nothing disappointed. I found the price to be reasonable, especially because of the quality of the food. The professionalism, service, atmosphere and food all lend itself to Salinas being a 5 star resto.

Walking distance from theater district. Â Great ambiance, decent pricing for HUGE portions. Â Great, friendly staff. Â Get there before 6pm to avoid the long line. Â I went along and sat at the table near the kitchen. Â That was a totally good thing since I'd walked there in a downpour and was SOAKED to the skin. Â 45 degrees in late April. Â "Springtime in NY" indeed. I ordered a warm sake, Sapporo Light, Steamed Chicken buns (delish) and a bowl of Karaka-men ramen. Â Extra spicy with bean sprouts added. I can't wait to come back on my next business trip, I'll come back for sure.
Loved the food, great drinks! hard to get a table on the weekend.

How could this be anything but 5 stars? OK, if you cut out the wait, maybe? The goat cheese ricotta with truffle oil was just divine. Can you take something so simple and somehow make it special, memorable, without ruining its simplicity? It's also rare that you see full on tripe on a brunch menu (outside of Chinatown). 8 hour roast ok, but 8 hour tripe? Yes, and I'd encourage you to give it a try. This is one of those restaurants that feels grand but airy. The food is rich but in the perfect proportion. This restaurant is all about everything in just the right amount, and that's why it gets a rare five star rating.

Nice food, average service. It was o.k. experience till I receive my credit card statement! I ate there but also ordered take out, and it was in 1 bill, anyway I put 17% for tips, I have my copy and I know. Today I looked at my statement, apparently they added few extra bucks and made it 22%. Some may think its not much, but to me doing such thing is so wrong. Its no mistake, somebody did it. Its so sad that food is good, but service is spoiling it.

Came here without a reservation on a weekend night. It was quite packed. I was meeting a friend so while I waited, i went to the bar for a drink. It gets crowded and the bar space is TINY. I stood awkwardly next to a pillar, sort of in the way of the waiters and kind of on top of a couple of women who probably didn't appreciate it. We ended up getting a cute table - would have been romantic for a couple - and had a nice meal of duck and wine. Food was good. Service was nice. Nothing extraordinary but it was a nice place to catch up with a friend.
A-mazing!! Delicious and good vibes... Just an fyi, the kani creme korokke (crab creme croquette) has that processed fake crab in it.. A lil disappointment but everything else is delicious!

5 stars for food - seriously love. 4 stars for constant wait-time. 1 star for REALLY rude hostess.
