Â  This place is always packed and doesn't need any help filling seats but customer service goes a long way - ESPECIALLY when there is always a wait. Not sure how much I want to frequent my neighborhood location after last night's supremely rude hostess.... Â Apologies on being unaware the bar was also your jurisdiction for seating and merely asked if I could sit. Â  Seriously, be nice to your customers.

I went here for a birthday dinner in early February. Â I tend to avoid celebrity chef restaurants, but Scott is my favorite judge on Chopped and my best friend has been raving about the polenta dish here for so long that I couldn't resist. The ambiance was a little more casual than I had expected (in a good way). Â You could get away with a suit here or just a good shirt a nice pair of dark jeans. Â The service was helpful without being obtrusive. We started with the polenta with truffled mushrooms ($19), and it was as advertised. Â Rich and creamy. Â It was the kind of dish you really had to force yourself to slow down and savor or else it would be gone in a flash. Â I liked the presentation too. Â The polenta comes out alone. Â Then the mushrooms and sauce, which come in a tiny cast iron pot, are poured over the top at the table. I wasn't particularly in the mood for a protein, so I went with the tomato and basil spaghetti ($24). Â Now I know this sounds like a pretty lame order. Â But it was FANTASTIC. Â One of my favorite things I've had in a while. Â I really can't believe how someone could make such a simple dish like this explode with flavor. Â I tried a few bites of the black farfalle with lobster ($28). Â It was fine, but I wasn't the biggest fan. And we finished with some sort of chocolate dessert that I liked, but didn't love. And that's all I got...

WOW, I tried to get reservations for 4 but it was quite a wait. Â We decided to sit at the bar and what a treat it was. I have never seen a group of bartenders (Ryan, Freddie and most importantly Dominic) so knowledgeable in their craft. We tried several of the Carmines special drinks and were suprised how quick Dominic and Freddie could make them (and with great enthusiasm). We were asked if we had any food preferences and when we said no, we were treated to the best dishes by Dominic. The bartenders seem to have a flair for entertaining. The Carmine's salad, stuffed mushrooms, OYSTERS (yes, oysters !), and veal parm were GREAT ! The cannoli's were out of this world along with expresso's and cappuccino's. The food was enormous and excellent. I highly recommend Carmines and will be coming back very soon with even more guests !

The Bronte burger here is seriously one of the best things I have ever tasted. Seriously. Dead Serious. I go there one day, and im back about 2 days later, even when im just visiting NY and there are plenty of places to eat. Inside is pretty small, but it's not horrendously bad where its just uncomfortable. And if it gets busy, you have to wait a little long since theres only one chef. But im just nit-picking. Food is great, service has no problems, price is good. I love it.

The guys behind the counter spent quite a while making our sandwiches, because they were very large and filled with all kinds of stuff. I ordered the Mr. Bloomburga and my friend ordered something with roast beef and swiss cheese and red peppers in it. Both were okay. The flavors were weird combinations. They both seemed like very particular tastes. If you found one on the menu that you liked, I bet you would really, really like it. Quality ingredients abounded. They seemed to have a very large beer and other beverage selection. And they were selling a 64 oz jug of maple syrup for like $30! There's no seating.

Fonda is delicious. 4 1/2 stars. Some of the best sit down Mexican I've had in NYC. Great guac, good happy hour deals, flavored margs are strong and tasty, the decor is right...this place has everything you want in a Mexican restaurant.

We got lucky as walk-ins to get a table. The place was recommended by a friend and they definitely knew what they were talking about. Quaint and charming. Well conceived italian fare. Plus, they definitely don't skimp on the portions. Respectable wine list. Prices were very reasonable by any city's standards, not simply New York standards. Service was attentive and engaging. We'd definitely go back.

My daughter and I visited this restaurant last night and had a fantastic meal. The food was delicious, and nicely prepared. Our dishes were the perfect temperature and Â were made with quality ingredients. The price was reasonable, and we came home full with leftovers to spare. The service was also great. The staff was very attentive, answered all of our questions, and was friendly. Mariella is a great addition to the neighborhood. It's well worth venturing off the main restaurant thoroughfares of 5th and 7th Aves to find this gem of a restaurant.

DIning in Brooklyn is always a interesting experience and can lead you into a whole other world....of cuisine that it. Kiwiana is a cute little spot on a quiet block in Park Slope,Brooklyn but there is nothing quiet about the food. They use herbs and spices native to New Zealand and you definitely taste the difference. The place was packed to the gills on a Monday no less. but my girlfriends and I had the scallops and grapes-cashew salad as appetizers as well as the buttermilk fried chicken as an entree. They even gave us a complimentary fourth course-butternut squash soup- to compensate for the delay in service. for dessert the flan and bread-pudding were great choices. Overall a cute, clean spot with good food and Â pleasant service. I will definitely be back!!!

I hardly ever give bad reviews but the terrible service I received here needs to be mentioned. While I love the food at Kyclades I have to say that the servers are generally rude and do not know how to respect their customers. I understand Â that the restaurant gets very busy and it is a hectic environment but general manners are still expected. On more than one occasion my group and I received nasty attitudes from the main waitress and were basically rushed through the whole meal. Kyclades offers amazing and fresh seafood that deserves at least 4 stars but the service here is just unacceptable.

Great brunch spot in Chelsea! The backyard patio is the perfect place for a casual, Saturday brunch. My friend and I ordered the burger and chicken & waffles to share. The Burger w/ cheese and spinach was bursting with flavor and amazingly delicious. The fries were perfectly cooked and the aioli that accompanied it was tasty. We also really enjoyed the chicken and waffles. The waffle is more of a french toast, but just as delicious.To drink, we had the grapefruit mimosa which was just as yummy as the food- not too sweet or sour. I thought the food and service were great overall. Definitely go with the burger. If you're not too hungry, share it with someone along with something lighter. The food is delicious but can be a bit heavy, so come with an appetite!

When EO first opened it was THE spot and impossible to get into. Now it's settled into the neighborhood and is a great little spot for drinks / casual dates. Long dark bar with mixologists stirring up fun cocktails. New american cuisine which is well executed. We shared a perfectly crusted steak on one occasion which was tasty. Â Menu is approachable and easy. The bar area can get annoyingly crowded at times but the atmosphere is lively and casual. Great spot for casual dates or drinks.

The food and service is excellent. I had the penne a la vodka as someone here recommended and it was the best pasta I have had! The waitress was really friendly and when we were finnish we were offered dessert on the house, amazing ice-cream! I'm really glad that we followed the yelp reviews and found the great restaurant!

The best Sicilian pizza anywhere ever. Other food is good too, flavorful, delicious marinara sauce. Dishes aren't just huge mounds of cheese and sauce like some Italian-American restaurants. I had the chicken sorrento tonight, it was delicious. Â And the spumoni...(chocolate/vanilla/pistachio ice cream) is perfect.

We had one of the best dinners ever, and we have been to many fine dining establishments all over the world. Â Decor is very simple, country classic mixed with modern Manhattan tones. Â Food is absolutely amazing from start to finish. Â We had barley risotto (too die for), potato gnocchi (equally amazing), and soft shell crab for an appetizer. Â Our main course consisted of branzino, carrot wellington, and pork leg. Â We also ordered carrot fries and snow peas as sides. Â Deserts and wine pairing is awesome. Â Definitely coming back. Â It is just a matter of time before they get a Michelin star.

Intimate, calming tea house with an emphasis on traditionally presentated, rare Asian teas -- a welcome respite from the East Village bustle below. As mentioned, you can request ($15 per person) a formal Japanese tea ceremony, with bowls of matcha and mochi pastries, in the Lilliputian wooden teahouse that fills half the dining room. We also had a Taiwanese oolong served on an elaborate tray, to be brewed in a three-step process that some might find fussy. (You can also have it served in a conventional pot, though.) Cash only.

I've been here so many times and finally get to leave some reviews. Â This is hands-down the BEST Itaian restaurant in NYC. My favorites are burrata cheese, zucchini flowers(seasonal), grilled octopus, tuna salads, pasta special, rack of lamb, and wines recommended by Vincent. Â Whenever I ran into Rocco, the owner/chef, he always greeted me with big smiles and warm welcome. Cannot wait to go again!

The food is amazing! They have amazing tapas! We had Cojonudo (Fried quail egg and chorizo on toast), Patatas Bravas (Fried potatos with tomato sause), Pintxos Morunos (lamb skewers) and all green salad. Seriously, all of them are super tasty. Â I can't even tell one con of them. Well, maybe one, they are a little small size to me. I can eat a lot of them! Â We also ordered the Paella de Mariscos, again, delicious!!! You only need some extra patient while waiting for this dish. Â After we finished all of the tapas, we still waited more than 20 minutes for the paella. Â But definitely worth it! Â If you are a seafood lover, you will like it (It has clams, shrimps, mussels, cod and squid on it. ) Desserts!! The Churros is the best! Like a hundred times better than the subway churros vendors. Â I don't even have to mention their chocolate dipping sauce! And the Torta De Chocolate (warm chocolate torte, marcona almond ice-cream). Delightful!! I can't wait to go back again. My mouth is drooling while writing this review... Just FYI, this place is a little pricey. Â We didn't order any drink, Â after tax we spent almost $40 per person.

for a long time i posed (unprompted) and answered the question, 'if i could only have one taste on my tongue for the rest of my life, what would it be?' and i answered it with 'Johnny Walker Blue' scotch. the black currant macarons of Lauduree give it a run for it's money. too very different flavors, obviously, and i don't expect anyone to necessarily share my tastes, not that i care, 'cause i know i have great taste. But my point is, this place is worth a try, the quality and luxury and extravagance and superiority will be self-explanatory. If you can get past the atmosphere, which i will admit might be offputting. Funnily enough, the first time i tried this place, on the recommendation of a friend, there was NO wait, there were like 4 other people in the store, so i didn't have to overcome a lot of negativity about long lines and rude service and clientele. It was awesome. The vanilla was my fave from that first trip. It was only when i went back with that recommending friend, with the lines and everything, that i tried the black currant, and sampled what was one of the two most delightful combination of flavors i have yet to experience. 5 stars, 5 very big, very tasty stars!

R Jackson I was looking at the website for Auto Exoticar and saw a car that i was intresting in so i call and spoke to Tom Cavallino and was very helpfull to me. he gave me the direction how to get to the dealership and had someone pick me up and take me to the dealership. i saw a2003 Honda Pilot for $7,995 but i made him an offer $6,500 and he accept the offer i am very please in the manner in how i was treated and would recomend this dealership to my family,and friends

4.5 stars! This place is SO good and a welcome addition to the neighborhood. Â The burgers are delicious, the drinks & beer are great, and the staff is incredibly friendly - what more could you ask for in a burger place? If you're not in the mood for fries, I suggest sharing a plate of the nachos with whoever you're dining, they are fantastic. Â Also, if you deny yourself the 282 sauce you are a crazy person. I know a lot of the reviews talk about the size of the burgers here, and I swear the sizes of the burgers are getting bigger each time I go. This is an awesome place to sit at the bar, grab a beer, and have a burger. Â The staff and owner are really nice, and it doesn't hurt that the burgers are perfectly cooked.

I used to have a lot of love for this place but I think the quality of the food has been deteriorating over the past few months. I used to think it was a hidden gem, but now it's busy when I go and the food is disappointing. I loved their pitza which is now way too greasy, and their grape leaves but the last few orders have been hard and dry, they're old and I won't eat them. I wish they would put back some of the old energy in to this place!

Best place for craft beers. I have never seen so many different beer offered in one place. I counted the beer menu and there were 50 beers on draft, and 125 different beers including bottles and cans. So as a craft beer lover, this was awesome!! I got seated right away (granted it was a Tuesday night) and food was good. The burger, brussel sprouts and liver mousse was great. The Mac n cheese and lamb meatballs were kinda plain. Our server was quick and nice. There was no duck tacos as ppl mention so I guess the menu changes.
Decent square slices. I had the grandma, 4.50 for two square pieces. Thin, not much cheese, not the tastiest sauce or anything but definitely not bad.

Literally my favorite restaurant in the city. Every time I'm back in NY I make a dinner at The Smith a priority. The salmon was one of the best I've had, the ahi tuna salad was to die for, and my mom still raves about their mussels a year after I brought her there.

I'd say that it was a 4 1/2 stars, but I am going to round up to 5 stars, given that there were some exceptional dishes. Â It's a very intimate space and the service was attentive, so I admit that this was an enjoyable dining experience. We decided against ordering the tasting menu, so that we can try a bunch of different items. Â The meal started out with a very good sashimi special, with excellent pieces of tuna and shrimp. Â From there, the entrees were very impressive. Â Our sliders were moist and delicious, probably one of the best burgers I've had in quite some time. Â The washu steak was excellent, not as great as ones I've had in Argentina, but probably one of the better pieces of meat I've had in North America. Â It came with these great baked potatoes, that were crunchy on the outside and had just the right amount of salt. Â Then there was the branzini, which was a large piece of fish, cooked pretty well with a lot of great vegetables. Â The portions were very generous, but we made sure there was room for dessert. The green tea panna cotta was superb...I am a picky panna cotta eater, so I was a bit hesitant about a green tea panna cotta, but I am so glad that we got this...then there was the coffee flan and I am a sucker for flan, the caramel gelatin that was on top of the flan made it that much more delicious. Â I can't wait to go back at some point.

Really, Yelp?! Â WHY?! Â Perhaps if you have never had Mediterranean food EVER in your life, this might just be acceptable. Â The Greek salad was fresh and tasty, and I was willing to overlook the overdressing. Â The bread was also quite fluffy and warm, but be aware that they do not actually serve pita (which is kind of odd - it's difficult to eat the mezze platter with the bread). Â Mezze platter (which I ordered as a main dish) was incredibly underwhelming. Â The yogurt tasted like lumpy sour cream, and the phyllo dough and feta was not layered as advertised - instead tasted like frozen, microwavable taquitos. Â Overall, the food was too salty. Â It's too bad, because the restaurant itself has a cute and inviting ambiance. Â Take my advice on this one...if you are looking for Mediterranean food in the immediate area, go across the street to Shalezeh...the restaurant is not as cute, but the food is much better in terms of taste, variety, and quality.
Fantastic pizza. Good enough to sneak into my suitcase :)

we came for brunch with a big group of 12 on a sunday. it was much easier to find room here than any of the nearby places. well we found a diamond in the rough. the decor is tasteful to match the delicious food. their arepas are to die for and they make all sorts of combinations with them. the sauces, the salad dressings and every side just completed the experience. you have to get the yuca fries! trust me. also the service is fantastic and the ladies who run it treated us like family visiting. what more can i say. viva venezuela!
Just three things to say: GREAT service, GREAT food, and GREAT atmosphere. Â LOVE this place (ok, so that was four things).

Ice House has been my go-to spot since moving to Red Hook a few years ago. When all I want is some cold beer and delicious pulled pork sandwiches (2 for $5), this is where you'll find me. Their sweet potato fries come with a delicious spicy chipotle sauce, and are good enough to make me realize my hatred of sweet potato fries was totally unfounded. My boyfriend gets the veggie burger, which he says is decent, and I've recently become addicted to the Frito pie; Frito chips covered in cheese, chili and jalapenos. I was Â surprised to see it on the menu at first, because it's more of a Southern/Southwestern dish, but it really took me back to visiting family in New Mexico. The beer selection is fairly big, random and decently priced. This summer I think I'm going to dive into the shot combo menu. The staff is usually pretty nice, but there is one guy who loves making smartass comments. One time I asked for a water (OMG) and he said "We're all out, how about some water with hops." Please. Better was the woman who let my friends and I smoke inside cause it was 3 AM on a Tuesday and we were pretty drunk. In the spring and summer they open their enormous backyard and let you drink, eat and smoke (only on one side) as long as you like. This is definitely NOT like a lot of Brooklyn bars you probably read about, where kids roam around like wild dogs. I'm lucky enough to have my own outdoor space but if I didn't I'd set up camp here and never leave.

We trekked out to Jackson Heights from the UWS specifically because Samudra had great Yelp reviews. Was worth the trip -- modest interior but very attentive and friendly service, delicious food, and excellent value. There were a ton of items on the menu that I'd now happily go back and try. Recommended!

A very special restaurant in every respect. The food is gourmet quality. The service and staff so well trained and welcoming. The ambiance is world class. Not an easy hike from midtown but well worth the effort. A must for food lovers.

Atmosphere 4 stars Service 4 stars Food 3 stars Overall I would give it a 3.5 It was fine, what was really disappointing was the cocktails and food. There are too many places in NYC to go for brunch that are better. I had the blueberry pancakes with the lemon ricotta on top. I found it a little too sweet for me and a little dry.I had looked up this place on time-out NYC as one of the places to go for brunch in Brooklyn. The menu looked good and maybe it would have been better if I had gotten something a little more savory. I was with 4 friends and 2 visiting from Chicago. Everyone agreed that the meal was "fine" but nothing amazing. Overall I would come back if I lived closer, but as I live in Jersey and 2 friends live in Brooklyn it's unlikely I'll be back, even if I'm in the neighborhood.

Love love love this place. All organic, perfectly seasoned BBQ and side dishes. You can also buy meats and sausages to take home to cook. BYOB as well, so you save super lots of money though the prices are already much much more affordable than other all organic restaurants. Pork belly, burnt ends and brisket are my favorites :)

Meltshop is awesome. If you want grilled cheese, this is the place to go. They serve a wise variety of grilled cheese - go with the one you like. They're all good. Tater tots is a must. Pretty pricy for lunch, but definitely worth it. Especially if you work nearby. Only downside is - if you're coming here for lunch during work, don't expect to get any work done after.

Post-"Daily Show" taping, I suggested to my parents, one of my roommates, and the beau to go to American Retro. Based on Yelp, it seemed like a no-frills restaurant / bar. Well...it was a bar with food that reeked of stale beer. NOT what I was looking for. Ha! So, my trusty Yelp app steered me towards Il Baretto, and it did so wisely. (Good, Yelp app! Good girl!) The place is pretty teeny tiny but very romantic. Five of us managed to squeeze in. The menu boasted many salads, hot and cold tapas, paninis, and desserts. My mother got the bacon-wrapped fliet mignon, served on skewers with greens and fried potatoes. My father got the scallops served with risotto. They both split a pear, blue cheese, and arugula salad. The beau got the grilled chicken wrap. The roomie got the lamb sliders. I got the caprese panini. I had bites of everything, save for the sliders, and everything was delectable! My only complaint is that I wish my panini was a bit warmer; seemed as though it was sitting on the counter for a bit post-cooking. Also, it came with no sides. I'm glad I was able to steal some of that pear salad from mis padres! The risotto served with my dad's scallops was fantastic! My Italian great-grandmother made the best risotto in the world, and this was pretty high up on the list; the saffron really shined through, which is important to me. The chocolate soufflÃ© and tiramisu are desserts not to miss as well. Both held their own very well. They were split amongst all five of us and we were all extremely satiated. The service was friendly, but very slow...it should not take 15 minutes to get a check post-meal when there are only two tables worth of people: us and a small family of three. This area of the city is a bit devoid of places to eat. Your luck for good dining is better found on 9th Avenue. But, if you're in the area, especially after going to a taping of "The Daily Show" or perhaps playing around in De Witt Clinton Park, this is a lovely little option!

the restroom is super high tec lol The food is not exceptionally impressive but definitely a good place to hang out with buddies drinking and ordering small dishes. My favorite is the Yellowtail appetizer and the beef steak appetizer.

I've never been to France but I think if I were a hipster living in Brooklyn that had backpacked through Europe at some point wearing nothing but cut-off shorts and John Lennon glasses, I'd say the French authenticity of this place was on point. The decor is bright, busy and borderline kitschy but it lends itself to the coziness of the space. There was one server running the whole shabang but he was cool, calm, collected and very attentive to our water glasses. I had a crepe with goat cheese, figs, rosemary, swiss and onions with a side salad. It was spectacular and filled to the crepe brim with all the ingredients listed. The entirety became a bit rich towards the end but you definitely got what you paid for (only $8 by the way). My friend had a salad with bleu cheese and walnuts (among other things). It was huge and she was satisfied. Hey-o. It took a little while for us to get our check - we were there for almost 2 hours all and all - but I think the waiter was just giving us time to talk. It was very European of him.

Although my friends weren't impressed with the corn, I thought my first bite was DELICIOUS. I will say though that it's difficult to get all the flavors in one bite (there's mayo, cheese, some sort of spice, lime etc.) so not ever bite will be as good. . .but I thought it was really good! The other brunch food however was just A-OK. I don't think this place is really worth the wait :(

A limerick of love, relevant to those who have been here: Cha-An I adore thee You introduced me to black sesame You usually have a long wait but your tea is great and I end up leaving with such a clean tushy
Great food, elegant and attentive staff. Service is seamless, decor is relaxing yet chic, easy for groups of 2 or four to sit.

I came here on dinner on a Friday night at around 7 expecting a long wait but was pleasantly surprised when my party of 4 was seated immediately. Â  We got the burger, the ricotta gnudi, chicken liver toast, deviled eggs, devils on horseback, and the pesto roasted onions. Â  Overall it was a pretty good meal. Â  - Chicken liver toast - this was amazing. Â I have had a lot of pate before, but this was the best thing i had during the meal. Â We initially ordered 1 order, but we got another one before we left. Â  - Burger- I ordered the burger medium rare and it came out great. Â The burger that has been said to have single handedly earned Spotted Pig a Michelin Star. The meat was just amazing and juicy and you could tell it wasn't your avg burger patty. Â The cheese added a great touch, though don't get it if you don't like Rocquefort because the cheese can be overwhelming (it wasn't in my opinion though). Â It's just a shame that this burger doesn't come with the option of other cheeses. - The gnudi was good but I don't think it deserves all the hype its been getting, the deviled eggs were good, but nothing special. Overall a great meal, I would definitely come back here again and get the liver toast and probably the burger.

Extra Virgin is a great little west village spot. Â This is a perfect spot to come for brunch, the menu is classic brunch foods - eggs benedict, waffles, pancakes, and the like, all of which tastes great. Â Make sure to try and pancakes and if you like banana get the waffles. Â EV also has a full bar if you need a little something to recover from the night before. Â While I'm not a bloody mary fan, my regular brunch buddies are and they rave about EV's bloody. The restaurant feels very clichÃ© west village, small, charming, intimate, full but not overly loud and a good crowd. Â In the warmer months you can also sit outside which is great. Â Rolling in at noon on a Sunday you'll have to wait for 30-45 minutes to get a table but let's be honest, anywhere good in this city you'll wait that long. Prices are reasonable, for a main dish + coffee + one alcoholic drink will run approx $25. Â On my past visits service has been fine thought I went over this past weekend and our server was AWFUL. Â She disappeared for long periods of time, forgot to bring us our coffee and when it came time to pay we had to hunt her down to get the bill. Bottom line: very good classic brunch spot in the west village to go with your friends to eat and discuss everyone's antics from Friday and Saturday night.

Ordered: Â Original Fried Burger, medium rare This is different and worth doing. Â Homemade purple beet ketchup and hot sauce. Â I usually have my snob on when trying burgers cause I am from Texas but this isn't a regular thing - everything is stuffed then fried then cut in half. The result? Â Crispy hoagie-ish outside, moist melty inside. Â Bit too much meat for me personally but probably won't bother most of y'all.
best restaurant in greenpoint despite the fact that I can't go here any more bc it's too popular.

Fish is still a great restaurant. We had: Chilean Sea Bass - Amazing Swordfish - delish Lobster Mac n Cheese - yum Plain Mac n Cheese - very good Mashed potatoes with lobster - great The oysters are still the best and freshest in NYC. Great neighborhood haunt!

This restaurant is as authentic as it gets with some nice additions to their menu. The service is friendly enough and the food comes quickly. The sound of meat being pounded flat is commonly heard from the kitchen. Â The kielbasa is pretty close to perfect.

Food: The green of the day was really garlicky and delicious, but a bit pricey at $8. A fried rice side was large enough for two to share alongside entrees. There aren't a lot of vegetarian options, especially since the vegetarian pho was disappointingly taken off the menu, but our vegetarian party of four ordered two each of the two veg dishes: bahn mi, which was tasty but nothing special compared to what I've tried elsewhere, and a Japanese eggplant special, which was large and had a surprisingly strong and delicious flavor -- even to the non-eggplant lover of the group. The strangest taste of the menu: artichoke keffir iced tea, the multifaceted, slightly sweet flavor of which I can't really describe further except to say that is worth a try for the adventurous. Other: I came here during a torrential downpour and still just got the only table that was available to accommodate my party of four -- so I'm sure there's typically a significant wait, and there's nowhere in the area to entertain yourself beforehand and no waiting room inside the restaurant. The staff was extremely friendly and immediately brought my paper towels to dry off while I waited. As a vegetarian, though, I wouldn't go more than once. It's a little expensive for the area and the limited range of options.

Next on the list was Ippudo NY, GOT RAMEN??????? It doesn't get any better than this: upscale, spacious, admirable, and distinctive food. Reservations are suggested as this restaurant gets packed! Party of seven please..... What's to order? Ippudo salad ($8) Mixed greens served with sesame shoyu dressing-Killed it!! Hirata buns ($9) Steamed buns filled with your choice of pork or chicken, served with Ipuddos original spicy bun sauce. You know we got the pork belly right? The buns have excellent texture. Fluffy and spongy. The pork was seasoned well, but I still like momofuku's better. ;) Yamitsuki Goma Kyuri ($8) Japanese cucumber seasoned with Ippudo's original sesame oil dressing. My girlfriends didn't care much for it, but I did!! Shiromaru Hakata Classic ($15) The original silky "Tonkotsu" (pork) soup noodles topped with pork loin chashu, sesame kikurage mushrooms, memma, red pickled ginger, & scallions. We added a poached egg and extra noodles. The light-brown broth was a revelation. It was nutty, complex, and deeply satisfying, its flavor enhanced by the slices of tender pork. The noodles were firm but not quite chewy, perfectly al dente. Karaka Men ($16) The original silky "Tonkotsu" (pork) noodle soup with Ippudo's special blend of hot spices, topped with pork chashu, sesame kikurage mushrooms, cabbage, onion, minced pork, and scallions. The broth was spicy and lively; fire and pork. It was the miso that made our tongues tingle and cheeks flush. I highly recommend if your craving some good Ramen, Ippudo NY is the best place to go!!
Affordable and delicious vegetarian/vegan wraps and options for when you need a break from fatty, indulgent nyc food.

Firstly, they want you here. Friendly welcome! Seated where we asked at the window with comfy club chairs! Had our first "pickle backs" as we are from queens not Williamsburg. Shot of bourbon with a Chaser shot of pickle juice. What a great idea. Must bring this idea home. Â  Cool vibe, cool server. Good grilled cheese with bacon and pulled pork. Unpretentious local hang out. Will be back!

Food---I ordered the tea set and really enjoyed the Chai Dao DIY even more than the tea itself. Lol. The green tea ice-cream is fantastic. Service---Quite good, me and my friend is well served. Deco---small but cozy, nice for a catch-up between girlfriends or mind wandering by oneself. Price---Above the average but affordable. Recommend the lunch set. Worth a try.

I came here a couple months back, fairly late, with a group of friends, one of whom was meeting up with 2 guy friends who were in town visiting...I'd heard the name and meant to try the place out before, but was fairly disappointed when I finally did..I also was in the area about a month back to give it another shot but essentially walked right in and out.. The setup is a bit awkward, very narrow when you first enter, along the bar, so makes it difficult to get through...the crowd is somewhere between frumpy and hipster to me (i.e. last time i was in a cocktail dress an heels, when the majority here were in flipflops and shorts...also i was more sober this second visit but had no desire to stay either time)... I guess if you want a lowkey spot, this might fit the bill, but the ambiance is very blah to me, and i've never been impressed with the music--if there even is any playing as i didnt notice. Â Strikes me as somewhere that might have been fun a few years back, but now the kind of place you'd maybe drop by for a quick drink early in the night--if you're dressed severely casually.
I am just in LOVE With the Halal guys! Â I work late a lot and will often send an intern running uptown to get my dinner for me (not fair, I know!).
Their unlimited tomato & bread plates are amazing before and in between courses. The spaghetti bolognese and lentil soup were super delicious.

Something about this place has changed..from the food to the atmosphere. Pizzas are now hit or miss. We now order our takeout from their sister restaurant Harry's Italian as it is better and much more consistant. Lets see if anything changes when they open their outdoor seating. Really disappointed as used to really like Adrianne's!!
Don't even bother to read these reviews and come here and eat their food. You will not regret it.

Order the Schnitzel, because what else would you order at an Austrian restaurant? The Schnitz is not quite full euro style, hanging-over-the-plate completely obscuring the potato salad from view, but good and plenty enough it is. Â  Surprisingly, the inside of the restaurant looks less Viennese, more like a place where Neil Young may have gigged in his early years. Credit cards accepted.
Absolutely love this place, noodles are fresh but a bit on the salty side though. Appetizers are delicious and creative. I dine here once a week, never get sick of it ..
Homemade Taqueria I LOVE YOU!!!! Handmade corn tortillas, friendly service, consistent dishes, and great delivery. Â The makings of a solid restaurant..

Black Angus Burger. Probably the best burger I ever had. Pure lean ground beef topped with caramelized onions. And the fries are fresh and amazing. Finished with the Grand Marnier soufflÃ©. My partner enjoyed the very stiff Copperhead cocktail. Just a whiff of it made me dizzy. We were lucky to get a place at the bar after only ten minutes of waiting. This small place fills up very quickly, reserve well in advance. A very classy traditional establishment.

What can I say - unhealthy Katsu is irresistible! The pork Katsu cooked just right - crispy but tender. The curry sauce is spicy but not greasy. The price cannot be more reasonable. Order with a bottle of green tea, then you will have the perfect Friday lunch, food coma comes after lol
Worth the wait, worth every penny, absolutely delicious food. Â I always get the pork buns and the akamaru modern. Â I literally have dreams of eating ramen here. Â It's that good.

Love that it is 5 minutes from my apartment! Â Bareburger is my go-to place for a high quality and delicious burger. Â I appreciate that they have meat options that you could not find anywhere else (bison, elk, ostrich, etc.) and that they provide detailed information about all of the ingredients. Â I have tried the beef, bison, and turkey burgers here and have loved all of them. Â The fries are also delicious and, while they are a bit salty, are a necessity when having a burger.

I had food from the truck, not the restaurant, but it was some of the best food I've had that took fewer than 5 minutes to prepare. I had the short rib bowl and the arancini. The amount of food for the price was fantastic. Lots of good quality beef, a huge chunk of kimchi, a huge pile of pickled daikon, and lots of rice with jalapeÃ±o, tomato and onion. The arancini were perfectly fried and not greasy, with two sauces layered in one cup, freshly grated cheese and a little bit of lettuce. All in all, it was absolutely wonderful.

Mamagyro serves delicious Greek food in a fast takeout model. It is different from a traditional gyro format I have to say. It is not as greasy and fattening and a lot of toppings are available at extra cost. I got the lamb gyro and it is smaller than other gyros out there. You pay $4.50 or 2 for $8. I like how it tastes very clean and a big mess of sauces on top. So, I like it for that particular reason but I think you are looking for a huge gyro that has like 3 sauces on top to dress your grilled meat, you set yourself up for disappointment.

this place is a great family restaurant it never disappoints, the food, service and ambiance is the best in the neighborhood, whenever I crave southern/creole food, this is the only place to go. ps. brunch is 5 star amazing!
As a southerner and an avid chicken biscuit fan, this is one of the best I've ever had. Perfect hangover cure and incredibly delicious!

As I continue my weekly brunch search, this week landed me and my friend at Cornerstone Cafe. Â Since there were just two of us, we were quickly seated. Â Parties of more than 2 had to wait a few mins, since the place is somewhat intimate, parties of 5 or more had to wait well over 30 mins- felt bad for them as I watched them stand in the cold! Â Comfortable environment but loud. Â Wait staff was very attentive and friendly. Â  The eye catching Texas French toast was ordered all around us, however we both opted for the baked eggs. Â I ordered the Italian sausage version and she ordered the spinach. Â Both came with home fries and toast (minus jam). Â The bakes eggs are pulled right out and delivered steaming hot (not in a good way). Â Once cooled down, they were delicious, but I knew that I should have ordered the spinach as the marinara sauce wasn't exactly what my palette desired. Â All in all, food was good, service was nice and the price was right (less than $30 buck total, with coffee). Â Nothing about this place completely wowed me, maybe I should have got the french toast?

Perfection. Â 5 Stars! Food, atmosphere, service... all wonderful. We started with brazed calamari and meatball sliders.. which they split for two.. for the main we both had the pork chop. Â Both pork chops were cooked perfectly... juicy and flavorful... the beans and dandelion were a perfect accompaniment. we shared a bottle of white... We will be back, this is my favorite new bistro!!!

3 stars for the ramen. 1 star for the service. This place doesn't even hold a candle to MU Ramen, where the ramen is 10x better and service is great and not so rushed. Service at Chuko is totally RUSHED to the point of being uncomfortable. Five of us dropped $200 bucks on ramen (believe it or not) they took our ramen away before we finished, our drinks before we finished them, and even the tip we were leaving right out of my hand. The Asian waitress even smashed my finger with a chair while noticeably upset that we sat for a few minutes while digesting our food. As for them ramen, it's good, but definitely not worth a 1-2 hour wait. The ramen was very contrived and did not blow any of us away. (Maybe that's because we eat at the extraordinary MU ramen all the time) Wake up Brooklyn, the ramen is not worth such an insane wait! For now we will stick to the classics like ippudo or Ivan or MU if we don't want to the treated like cattle. Or physically abused.

Came here with my co-workers on a Thursday, it was moderately busy (Not packed but from the outside, it definitely looked like it a was popular restaurant). Â  A couple members of our party were a little late so I headed to the bar with who already arrived and grabbed a couple drinks. Â The service was great and the hostess would occasionally check on us to see if the rest of our party arrived. (Not in a nagging sort of fashion, was very nice and told us that she would hold the table till they arrived). Â  Once the rest of our party arrived we were escorted quickly and the waitress was very attentive, and informative when it came to drink and food selection. Â I highly recommend the cobia, chili lobster and pork porterhouse. Â There were 4 of us and sharing the chili lobster was a great choice as a sharing platter. The veal was alright, needed more truffle (said it had black truffle oil but could barely taste the truffle). Â  For dessert, go with the cheesecake or chocolate chip cookies. Â The cookies come with a mason jar with milk. Â Very "homey" touch to it. If you are picking any dessert wines I would go with the Takaji, Oremus 2008. Â Very sweet and goes well with the cheesecake. Â  Overall a good vibe to the restaurant and would definitely go again.

First off the decor was Amazing!! Food was very tasty! I had the crawfish bourbon balls very tasty! I also had the blackened catfish with Mac and Cheese Delicious! They were serving $4 dollar Hurricanes because Hurricane Irene is coming to town! lol Those were very good! The server was very nice but was slow. Definitely will be back!!
Tina's is a great Cuban cheap eats in NYC. A Cuban Sandwich and 2 beef empanadas were only $10.29. As a Cuban, I feel that their Cuban Sandwich is as close as authentic Cuban in Manhattan.

The atmosphere inside is nice. It has a very quaint feeling. The food was decent. I wasn't blown away by the Huevos Rancheros. The home style potatoes were really good. I wish I had gotten more of those. Also, the latte was smooth and tasty. I felt it was a bit expensive for what it was.

This place is sacred. I don't even know where to start. My girlfriends friend who lives in NY brought us here, I love my girlfriend even more now. I love BBQ and beer, then I came here, seriously I CAME after this meal. Spare ribs, brisket, beans(with burnt ends!!), and this stuff that tasted like pumpkin pie. In fact I can't wait to look at the pics people posted and be brought back to that glorious day when we ate here. Apparently there was a lot of ruckus going on, but I was way to focused on the fact that there was meat in the beans! I we come back to NY, this place is going down! Thank you guys for the amazing food and badass staff!

Amazing off the beaten path restaurant--not ostentatious from the outside but the interior is charming and was surprisingly empty on a Saturday night. I imagine not for long when the word starts to spread. Service is very friendly--the host and our server were both very personable and helpful. Got the Parma pizza. The pizza crust is at the same time light and chewy, reminds me of a hole in the wall pizza place I used to go to in Italy. The pecorino was amazingly flavorful and went well with the slightly cooked prosciutto and baby arugula. I'm not a prosciutto or arugula fan in general but this was very well done. The pasta in both dishes we ordered was satisfyingly al dente, second only to Eataly where it is made in house. And the gratuitous cheese grater made us happy. I got the spaghetti and meatballs: the sauce was the right amount of tomatoey, but the meatballs were a bit ordinary. The sausage in my friends fennel dish was amazingly flavorful, and the fennel was just the right amount of garnish. The only thing I would say is the use of lemon could be brought down a bit for that dish, but my friend found it perfect. Overall a very happy experience. There is also a fancy bar despite this being a small joint--manned by dapper men in white jackets, and with many jars of accoutrement lined up for what I imagine is a wide variety of cocktails. Did not partake this time but definitely interested in seeing what they concoct on my next visit here--which will be soon.

We went last night for my husband's birthday. Â The restaurant is beautiful. Â The staff were just the right amount of friendly. Â We got the tasting menu and had a glass of white and a glass of red to go with the meal. Â The courses were just the right size, and all of them ranged from very good to delicious. Â My only problem was after dinner - Â I went to use the restroom, and it was probably the most beautiful bathroom I'd ever seen, and the stall I used smelled like a urinal. Â It was pretty off-putting and shocking for a restaurant of that caliber. Â I'm taking one star off for it or I would have given them 5 stars.

Friendly and professional from the time we entered through good bye. Interesting setting, drafty in the corner next to the garage door. Menu unusual and foodie worthy, meals a touch small for a hearty eater like myself, by well executed and very tasty. We will return.

As far as macarons go, these are the best I've ever tasted. Â My sister raved about these in Paris but I didn't get all the hoop-la as I always thought of macarons as having that more crunchy meringue type of cookie but I suppose I'd never had an authentic macaron before. Â The cookie at Maison Laduree was top notch, really delicious with a lightness and great texture and flavor. Â Some of the flavors are better than others as the amount and texture of the fillings vary. Â The filling on the vanilla was too thick and rich, I felt like I could not have more than one at a time. Â However, other flavors had superior balance. Rose petal was my absolute favorite; it was delicate and aromatic. Â Salted caramel and pistachio were also delicious. Â I'm a little wary of long waits for anything dessert related so that's the only drawback.

I heard great things about the place and couldnt wait to try their food. First off, this place gets packed pretty quick, so reserve ahead of time for large groups. Second, the service was decent, no complaints really. Third, the food is delicious! Â The most interesting item i tried on the menu was the desert, green tea aficionado... You pour hot green tea over ice cream, red beans and some other ingredients and its surprisingly delicious... It ends being this "soup" like meal... I'd like to come back again and try something off of their entree menu.
The rice and lamb are incredible, the chicken is just so-so. Â Loved the spicy sauce and white sauce, deeeelicious.

My favorite place for Pad Thai. I've brought many of my friends here and not surprisingly, they fell in love with the Pad Thai too. There is a perfect balance between the sweetness, sourness, and saltiness. Palate party! The Panang curry is my second go to entree. The Tom Yum soup is very good on cold days. The prices are very affordable but Song only accepts cash. The place has a hip modern feel. I don't like the pictures on the wall very much but everything else is very nice. Both bathrooms are modern and usually clean. The back outdoor seating is comfortable and cute but the tiny pebbles are awkward to walk on. I love the transparency of the kitchen. You can see the cooks at work from the inside as well as the outside.

We were standing in line for the Grimaldi Pizzaria but the line was so long. Somebody that passed by said this place was better since theyr right next to each other and true enough, the real Grimaldi was said to own this place. They sold the name Grimaldi to former customer and Juliana their new restorant was named after his mom :) the story worked up my appetite. Their thin crust small Pizza taste good :) good ambiance and service.

eo has all the glamour that retaking the LSAT has prettyboy bartender shooed me into the corner to accommodate a few starfucker model types and i had my alimony paperwork spread all over the bar and had to relocate place hasn't been cool in years

Looking like an authentic comfortable unpretentious ramen joint, it sits lonely in the middle of the street waiting for those who crave a good bowl of ramen. Â  We had the Spicy Miso Ramen, and 2 of us had the Charshu Ramen. Â The Spicy Miso Ramen had slices of fattier round cut charshu. Â It was a lighter spicier version of the pork broth as this is blended with the chicken broth. Â The Charshu Ramen had 3 huge chunks, not slices, but chunks of the Charshu! Â It didn't have too much fat and was flavorful. Â Also the broth had the strong pork taste that I love! Â This may be a bit overwhelming for some ramen nub sauces.

Found out about this place via YELP. Â I love Greek food. Â Was turned on to it about the same time this year last year. Â The quest for the best grape leafin the city continues! Â Came here for my birthday dinner. Kefi was outstanding. Â To start we ordered the meatballs and the fried calamari. Â Both were excellent. I really enjoyed the meatballs and the leftover sauce for dipping. Â Calamari was pretty standard, but tasted great. I had the roasted chicken as my entree. Â It was AMAZING. Â Cooked perfectly. Â Succulent, crispy, moist, bomb. Â Served with small potatoes that were equally as good. Â Others around me had ravioli. Â I didn't know ravioli could be made into a Greek dish, but was very happy I tried it. Â  A birthday walnut cake with some walnut ice cream was brought out which were compliments of the house. Â A nice gesture. The food at Kefi was as you probably gathered, delicious. Â I will definitely come here again but I'd like to try another place first. Â  Kefi is a giant restaurant with millions and millions of tables. It has a downstairs floor that is nearly as big as the top floor. Â We were jammed in a corner near a loud air conditioning unit with nearly no light. Â I'm pretty sure we got that table because we were 10 minutes late for our reservation? Not sure. Â We called ahead though. Â Atmosphere is a big thing for me and I was so so on it for Kefi due to its size. Â  Kefi was a great choice for my birthday. Â  I would have given five stars if they served grape leaves and if the restaurant didn't look like Ellis Island Â registration/booking hall circa 1880's. Â (not a joke on immigration, but a slight on Kefi's PACKED vibe)
Great restaurant event, Penne meat Ragu,nice glasses of red and white, service was excellent! Dennis und Ingrid
Perfect! Â Portions, People, Value, Flavor. Â This was a place I looked up on Yelp and it was spot on Perfect! Â I will return.

Fantastic! I have been 3 times and every time I go I am surprised by how much I love it. The food is delicious, the service is amazing, and the environment is unbeatable. You know its good when everyone in there Â speaks Japanese! get the blackened cod with miso sauce!!!!
Best. Ramen. In. Brooklyn. Period. Also, the salt and pepper chick is a must. It is a revelation. I can't stop going to Chuko.

Finally visited yesterday after hearing alot of buzz. The place was packed, barely any space to move (which I didnt mind). We were seated fairly quickly to my surprise since I've heard that the wait times were very long. The pricing was great. Some people say that it was over priced but considering it is in Manhattan it was a great deal. Drink selections were great and fairly priced (average NYC prices) the burger we order had a good amount of bacon, it wasn't huge but IT WILL FILL YOU UP unlike burgers at other restaurants. Very casual setting, wearing a suit will over do it. When we got the bill we were suprised at how low it was. Overall this is a must visit place. Will definitely come back soon.

I'm not a new yorker so... But... I found this place... AMAZING for a quick, fast, cheap, on to go place to eat. I was in NYC for 5 hours and wanted a quick place to grab something to eat. Boom... you come here in the Ktown area. IF you want a la carte you can stand in that line. If you want premade food that is on the fridge section you can do that. They are fast about payment and polite about it. So... I recommend this place to anybody who wants a quick to go eat korean food.

A remarkably large beer & ale selection. Â And delectable food. Â  I enjoyed the spinach & artichoke Â soufle along with the thai curry lobster. Accompanied with Timmermans Pumpking Lambicious. Ohh, what a delight to the palate.

Okay, so I've eaten in both the regular dining room and the tavern. Â The dining room dinner I had there during the winter was so good and I remember the food and service were at least 4 stars. I came back again the other night, this time in the tavern, and I ordered a la carte because the prix fixe options didn't look too appealing. Â The food was rather disappointing. Â I had the mussels, red beans, and chorizo in cilantro broth to start with, and then the arctic char, quinoa, asparagus, and candied tomatoes. Â Both were just okay - neither memorable nor outstanding. The ambiance was laidback and comfortable which was appreciated, but at times a few people were getting rowdy and I almost felt like fresh meat at a frat party. Â While trying to enjoy my meal alone, this douchebag sidles up next to me and starts hitting on me so shamelessly you'd think I had ordered "Drunk married lawyer" as my main course. Â Instead of coming to my rescue and telling the guy to back off, two of the staff just stood and chuckled to themselves, only apologizing to me when he had already left. Â Thanks. So overall, the restaurant gets a 3 because the dining room is 4/5 but the tavern experience was only a 2.

I am a huge fan of Top Chef and loved Harold on season 1. He consistently delivered what seemed to be delicious food and cut the drama out of the show. Â In my opinion, the true Top Chef. With that said, I knew that I had to try Perilla when I was in town. I was not disappointed either. Â The restaurant is cute and quaint, not loud, trying to be ultra chic or modern. Â Something that is very cozy and very inviting. Loved it. My friends and I tried a little bit of everything and it was all delicious. Starters we had: Skillet Braised Cuttlefish- it was light and delicious. I am not a fan of cuttlefish however it was pretty good. Spicy Duck Meatballs- very good. I would have liked them to be a bit more spicy and less salty. you kind of forget its duck. Wild Bison Loin Tataki- absolutely delicious and highly recommended. Â The bison was paper thin and was a perfect compliment to the salad. The dressing on the salad was absolutely delicious as well. Roasted Guinea Hen- large portions and cooked perfectly. Loved the chestnuts. Grilled Hanger Steak- cooked perfectly as well and was a hearty portion. I would recommend this for sure. Pan Roasted Striped Bass- a little bit dry but the sauce made up for it. Also a large portion. Edamame Falaffels- very unique and the epitome of "fusion". Mixed reviews around the table. Most enjoyed it, some said it was gross. You decide for yourself. Overall, reservations are highly recommended, portions are large enough for you not to bitch and moan saying it was too expensive and in general just kick back, relax and let the food talk for itself. Outstanding.

I have to say this restaurant truly lives up to its reviews. I came here for lunch today with my grandma and we were attended by the nicest waiter who really made our experience all the better. We had the brussels sprouts, falafel, tabbouleh, bass and warm date cake for dessert. Everything was delicious and believe me, I know my Mediterranean food... My absolute favorite were the brussels sprouts. Do yourself a favor and get them. You won't regret it. Highly recommended.

I have tried out alot of pizza joints throughout the nyc area and very few make it to my best list. Â This place falls in 2nd place behind Grimaldi's but it was close. Yes I would travel back to this location for pizza even though it's no where near my home. About 15 miles away from where we live. We ordered a sausage and peppers sandwich and 2 slices of sicilian pizza. It was damn good IMO! And we finished it off with some Vanilla and Pistachio Spumoni. Great simple meal.

Let me start by saying the pizza is GOOD: the dough, the sauce, the mozzarella, the fresh basil...all very good. Â  My friends and I wait in line for an hour and 15 minutes before finally making it into the restaurant and up to the counter, where we're told our pie will take an hour or more. We say what the heck we made it this far and we're at famous Di Fara's, so we wait and wait. 2 HOURS LATER we finally each bite into our first slice of Di Fara pizza. The consensus: it's good, but not 3 hours of idle waiting good. Especially, with a full itinerary on a day trip to NYC. That said it's an endearing establishment full of tradition. The owner is a sweet old man who makes every pie from scratch, by himself. In the future I would place my order, work up an appetite while running errands, then pick up a fresh, hot pizza waiting for moi!

Excellent pizza. I'm not usually a white pizza eater and this white pizza was good enough to make me consider it more often. Good beer selection too. Wesley was the best server we had in NYC, great job!
It was a little embarrassing to order the Viagara but holy moly it was worth it! Â Amazing times infinity! Â This place just became one of my top 5 places to eat in all of NYC!

I've been to a similarly-named place in Chicago called the Publican, so I was expecting a similar communal-dining-old-fashioned-pub-like restaurant. This place was slightly different though. I came during dinner and the place was decorated with rustic brick walls, hard wood floors, candles along the walls, and my favorite was the vintage medicine cabinet used to store menus. All of those put together gave a very speakeasy bar theme to the restaurant. We ordered for Appetizers: * Fried Hama Hama oysters with shiso, sansho pepper, and wasabi-yuzu dipping sauce * Grilled Wagyu beef tongue with brown butter yogurt, onion rings and ginger-scallion relish * Pan-seared foie gras on spiced French toast with mango chutney, maple glaze and crispy bacon We ordered for our Mains: * Roasted Chatham cod with manila clams, crispy potato, sesame wakame salad and smoked uni cream * Szechuan crusted tenderloin and roasted belly of Berkshire pork with braised daikon, pickled baby carrots, and slow poached egg in a truffle dashi broth * Pan-roasted duck breast with sesame soy dressing, cassava chips, wokked bok choy and pickled For Dessert: * PUBLIC dessert sampler (3 small desserts) - which included Chocolate Mousse, Sticky toffee pudding with Armagnac ice cream and hot caramel sauce Everything was delicate and delicious, and quite reasonably priced for a one star restaurant. However, the most memorable dishes of the night were the following: 1. Foie gras - the foie gras was grilled to have a smoky outer lining but buttery inside. the french toast was soaked in the mango chutney and the sweetness really set off my appetite for everything else for the rest of the night. (My mouth is watering as I'm writing this!!!!!) 2. Szechuan Pork Belly - I wanted to try this mainly because it was pork belly, and I had tried a pork belly dish at the Publican as well. Pork belly at the Publican was sweet and smoky, but this one was crispy and peppery. I definitely enjoyed this one much more. 3. Chocolate Mousse - The sticky toffee was really good as well, but I wanted to highlight this extremely common and ordinary dessert. Most of the chocolate mousse I've had are one dimensional with over powering chocolate flavoring and sweetness to it. But this chocolate Mousse was light flavorful and fluffy in texture. I couldn't stop eating it!

Very good atmosphere and friendly service. The food is certainly above average. We were there with two kids and the staff was very accommodating. There is no kids menu but we were able to shop around and compose a couple of kids dishes that were just fine. I recommend this place both for couples and families (as long as your children are accustomed to dining out - this is not a family restaurant per se).

Crowded, pompous, not amazing food, and overpriced. If you want to drop some bills on a chic asian dinner, there are way better places to do it. Places where the wait staff might be a little more attentive, for starters. Of course, it's got a reputation for being good, so if you're with someone who has no taste they might be impressed.

Love love love this place! Customer service is incredible! Their staff is very attentive. The food is delicious and very reasonably priced! I would suggest their baked eggs... AMAZING... served with toast and home fries for like $12. Their eggs benedict is also amazing and $10 :) You can't get better than that! Great for the neighborhood folk and everyone else!

Went with a friend for the all you can eat Maryland-style blue crabs. Â Crabs were delicious, albeit very messy. Â Around 2:45pm they ran out of crabs and our server comped us an order of lobster mac and cheese. Â Overall food quality was very good, the service was friendly and it was a laid back atmosphere. Â Good for Sunday brunch.

Went to Ancora for a special birthday lunch for a friend. Â I was extremely impressed with Ancora. Â Very good service and authentic Italian food. Â I am vegeterian and they made me a special Eggplant lasanga which was wonderful! The fried zucchini hot peppers and bread were complimentary and very good. They had wonderful appetizers to chose frpm and also homemad Grappa in different flavors. It is a bit pricey, but it is Wall Street!

My wife and I came here on a Friday around 630 pm and were lucky enough to be seated immediately. The place got crowded 15 minutes after we were seated. We got: Octopus Salad: We started our meal with the octopus salad and it was pretty good, even though I'm not a big fan of cold food. Â Important thing is the octopus was soft but still had some texture. 3.5/5 Boudin Noir Tartinette: Â This was one of the specials. The blood sausage was surprisingly on the lighter side. It was well balanced with balsamic vinaigrette and caramelized apples. 4/5 Croque Monsieur: Tasted no different than a slice of Sicilian Pizza due to the combination of the cheese, sauce and thick bread. While it tasted good, the ham was barely noticeable. 3.5/5 Coq au Vin: Legit. This is a classic dish that many places get wrong. Theirs was exactly what I wanted. Â It consisted of a thigh and leg drenched in a delicious gravy. The meat was as tender as they come. Â 4.5/5 Prices are pretty reasonable and while the portions are small (as it is with most French restaurants), you don't need a ton of food here to get full. Â The interior is cute but narrow and cramped. They have a huge map showing the different wine regions in France on the wall opposite the bar. They take their food and wine seriously and the wine cellar downstairs maybe small but still pretty impressive. Our waiter was helpful throughout. I can easily see Buvette becoming my go to French restaurant.

This place is always freaking packed -- the only time we could get a reservation was 10:30pm on a Wednesday night. I came here with a group of 4 for a (very) late night dinner. We ordered the bone marrow appetizer, which was super delicious on top of some crusty bread. I got the famous black label burger for my entree; I have to say, while it doesn't disappoint, $26 is a LOT to spend on a burger. My favorite NYC burger is still the one I had at Corner Bistro, and that one cost less than $10. However, people probably also come here for the old school ambiance. The service was also great -- no complaints there. -L.

Best square pizza ever!!!!!! Now note that I say square pizza. Â This is because I haven't tried their round. Â Just a little notation there for ya. You can't just have 1 square. Â I normally come here and get 2 but there are those times where I just want another. Â They put their sauce on top of the mozzarella cheese and add some parmesean cheese on the top. Â The dough is GLORIOUS. Â Honestly words do not do this place justice. Top off your night with a small cup of their creamy spumoni and you'll understand the meaning of bliss.

I am in a weird limbo between 3 or 4 stars. I will tell you why. HAPPY HOUR: $5 drafts, well drinks and wine - all the basic stuff nothing too lavish and fancy, which is fine. Have a few and you'll end up drunk anyway. However, there were no happy hour food bargains, this was sad. I was hoping there would be a combo of some sort, but strictly drinks. It's all good though. I usually avoid getting fries elsewhere because Pomme Frites has my heart and I am loyal and will forever remain faithful. However, One Mile House's wide selection of fries from truffle oil to Parmesan and herb were not too shabby!!! I also ordered the Apple Grilled Cheese suggested by our waitress (blue hair and black framed glasses, hiiii) - AMAZE-BALLS. Somehow the thin sliced apples with the cheese works - I never heard of the combo until this place and it so complementary! Also comes with an order of fries, and I am not talking about a small portion either. It's HUGE. Basically a regular order of fries, which is a sharing plate. Let me finish talking about the fries though: it was not soggy. You know when it is all greasy and stuff, damped in the oil. nope. Perfectly fried fries. and not too crispy. Slightly thinner than your Pomme Frites thick fries, but still works. Okay, I am done talkin' about the fries. My friends and I went overboard and somehow ended with three orders of fries that night and two-three rounds of drinks. Whatever it may be, we had such a grand time. I will admit, it was super dimmed and our party was kind of bigger than we anticipated but we made the seating arrangement work.

halal guys ruined halal for me when i tried it. overly hyped, food was bland and had a weird aroma. whenever my boyfriend and i walk by nowadays and see the line, we're always like, we don't understand what the hype is all about because their food isn't that great but i mean, to each their own.

Fun decor, great music, friendly and helpful staff and D.I.Y. GRILLED CHEESE WITH TWO CHEESES ($9) + BANANAS FOSTER MILKSHAKE ($5)! We also had the tator tots with parmesan ($4) and the brussel sprouts ($5)

Arrived just before 8pm without a reservation to a pretty busy restaurant on a Wednesday night. The hostess said it would be about 30 minutes for a table. We went to the bar. The bartenders were attentive, and the drinks were delicious. A little pricey, but they felt special. We were not seated for 50 minutes, at which point we were finished with cocktails at the bar and had started Googling other restaurants in the neighborhood. Just then, we got seated, and they sent over an appetizer on the house. So at least they had the sense to try and make up for their hostess' poor estimation. The food is well prepared, and seasonal, which was appreciated. But the portions are quite small, especially for the price. The menu is brief and not good for vegetarians, or even pescetarians for that matter. Most of the dishes feature meat, or have a meat component. We each had seafood, and were generally disappointed by the overall entree composition and presentation. The fish is served as-is on white dishes, with a more complex side of either vegetable or meat and veg pairings with sauce. Ham seemed to be a component of many dishes. The wait staff seemed junior, confused about whether drinks had been ordered, and reliant on servers and hosts to truly serve and describe the dishes. There is a main room where the atmosphere is enjoyable, but the back room where we sat felt loud and unpleasant. There are also some tables quite near the entrance to the toilets, which I am happy we were not seated at. All in, we spent over $100 per person for drinks, appetizers and entrees. There are restaurants within walking distance of this place where you can get a better meal for that price. I would only go back for drinks at the bar.

Classic Chinese in the heart of Chinatown. Â I make a point of getting Big Wong at least every 6 months as I can't go too long without the roasted meats. Â The prices are good and it is right next to a great Chinese candy store
pouttttiiiiinnnnnne! seriously, try the poutine, it's absolutely amazing.

ilili (Philippe Massoud) [from the 2008 Wine and Food Festival]- ilili's stuffed grape leaves, lamb ribs w/ seared strawberries and roasted scallions, essmalieh dessert w/ shredded phyllo, achta, rose petal jam - grape leaves were blah, lamb was OK, achta is a clotted cream, dessert was amazing

Joe took me to Aurora for our second date. I was so excited I stumbled when I saw him waiting for me at the bar. I was wearing my favorite Catherine Malandrino dress and we sat in the back corner table. He slid his hand up my leg and I almost lost it! The food was delicious, it really was, but what I remember most was Joe and I making our own little world, lost in the food and the wine and each other. We closed the restaurant down, just he and I and the soft din of Aurora closing for the night.

Oh Danny Meyer and Floyd Cardoz how I love you so. I can't justify giving this anything but a 5. Went here for brunch and has the most memorable shrimp and grits I've ever had. I literally wanted to order another one-- it was so good, flavorful, light, and perfectly cooked. The service was insanely good. You know those places that anticipate what you want before you get it? This is one of those places and it was definitely fine dining service in a more accessible simple atmosphere.

I'm a little wary of going to any restaurant in Times Square, and this one is no exception. Â I went here for my birthday last year with a party of 18, and while they accommodated, it was still a little cramped. Â The food? Â It's traditional Italian fare served family style. Â That's pretty much all I've got to say about that. Â I do wish there was a little more room in this place, and the location leaves a lot to be desired, otherwise I would have given this place another star. Â Fortunately, they do have another location.

Everything was awesome. Gnocchi were to die for. Meatballs were homemade. Service was awesome. Just an awesome experience from start to finish. Decent wine selection too. Was a tad dark inside but it made it feel even cozier.

Love this place, but it is best to go off peak when it isn't so crowded. Â The back deck is amazing and the wine and food never disappoint. Helpful, friendly, and knowledgeable wait staff. And, come on, how cute is the wine list?

Creamy goodness. Came here as one stop on an East Village food crawl with my BFF and husband, and while it was deliciousness on first bite, after awhile the creamy richness of the cheesy, rich artichoke concoction was too much for my mouth to handle. I think it would taste even better if I was slightly, or maybe a lot, more inebriated. I don't live in NY, but if I did, I could see myself coming back after a pub crawl.
Ah, Tabare! I miss you, mi amor!

I'm not even a meatball fan, but I really loved this place. Â We did not have to wait at all, which I am sure helped my positive feelings. Â Everything was fresh, delicious and flavorful. Â I can't wait to go back.

I absolutely love Empanadas Cafe. I have been here countless of times for about 4 years. I frequent this place often with friends, who they themselves become fans of the little establishment. I take people who visit me from out of state/country to this place and they are grateful as well. I used to appreciate this place while I was a vegetarian because they have a lot of great meatless options. They are not the authentic Colombian empanadas, but that is the beauty of this place. They expanded on the original empanada, which is still available, and used their imagination to create other delicious recipes. Besides the original shredded beef empanada, my favorites are: broccoli and cheese; jalapeno and cheese; & plantain and mozzarella. Their ice pops are also quite delicious. I recommend pineapple, blackberry, and coconut! If it's around lunch or dinner time, call ahead for pick-up. If you have time, sit in the tiny place, enjoy the empanadas with their fresh hot sauce, and a bottle of Crush. That's what I do. ;-)

I thought was ok, nothing spectacular. Nice flavors, but the salad was way over dressed, and the brussel sprouts overcooked. Â The ravioli were amazing though! Â The bussers and wait staff kept coming over to clear our plates before we were done. Might try it again.
Amazing food, drinks, ambiance and staff!! Loved every single thing about this place! You MUST try the White Cosmo! AMAZING!!
MY FAVORITE RESTAURANT IN THE CITY! The food is absolutely incredible, great selection of wines, the service is on point, and the atmosphere is exceptional. No complaints here.

I've tried 3 times of Cambodian sandwich in Num Pang, it's about time to have some Vietnamese sandwiches. Here I am in "Xe May"! "The Mean Green" is something I've been thinking about, a spiced tofu sandwich within lots green!! Two options of the bread, whole wheat and white. Unlike Num Pang, the bread is toasted and warm. Have a bite!

Love this place, found out about this in "the gothamist" as one of the top 7 grilled cheese sandwich place. I had the Gouda grilled cheese sandwich which also contains black bean hummus, guava jam, and pickled jalapeÃ±os.. WHAT???!...YES, this unholy combination was so delicious! I will definitely get more. I also had the French toast with hard cider pear compote and chili cheese, also tasty. The place is cozy and hip. We went for lunch and had to wait 30 min , but worth the wait , took a little stroll in Astoria to pass the time. The museum of the moving image is not to far away, so you can walk off all the food.

I came with Maha here on a Friday night. Â We walked in and were seated right away, although the place was packed. Â The feel is very festive and really, well, Cuban. Â The service was stellar and the servers were really hustling. We told our server we were there for the Blackboard Eats menu, and she had the bartender whip up an awesome white sangria for us. We ordered the black bean and corn fritters and the empanadas to start. Â Maha opted for the chargrilled chicken, and I went for the bone in pork shank. Â The starters came out piping hot and decadently delicious. Â The place is simple, with the sauces served in little plastic cups. Â The flavors are spot on and the empanada was perfectly fried and stuffed with spicy goodness, and dipped in the green sauce, it made the perfect hot and cool bite. Â The fritters were amazing, although I don't usually like them because they tend to be oily and flavorless. Â These were crisp with soft beans and corn kernels that were still fresh. Â Lovely. The pork shank was fall off the bone tender, and ample in portion size. Â The rice and beans served on the side were also delicious. The chicken was perfectly thin, marinated and charred and an awesome dish. We couldnt finish the mains, as they really are ample, even for the BBE code-this place doesn't skimp. Â  The desserts included flan and a cuban bread pudding. Â The flan was not too sweet and very well prepared and the cuban pudding was sooo good. Â I had to make myself stop eating! For drinks we had the sangria, followed by pineapple daquiri for maha and a capirinha for me. Â The drinks are strong and very good quality. Â  Try the BBE menu before its gone, with an extra drink, tax and tip we came out to $38 dollars a person-awesome!

An LES brunch favorite, the pancakes and crab cakes are some of the best we've ever had, but the line outside on a weekend make it something only worth it on the weekday. Their famous biscuits are very good, but a bit too bit for one person. Â The first time I was there I ordered the buttermilk biscuit sandwich, but found the tomato jam a bit strange and the whole thing a bit dry. Â The second time, however, all was forgotten when I ordered the delicious crab cake sandwich. Â It comes with lots of crab and very little filling, for a satisfying treat. Â My husband always gets the blueberry pancakes, which are also very very good. The third time I went, i got the catfish sandwich on "crusty" bread. The bread sucked and was way too "bready" for the sandwich, the catfish itself was dry and encased in a breadcrumb like crust. I kept thinking how great it would have been if they used more of a beer batter and actual crusty bread, but instead it was a big disappointment. Also, service was bad as well. I think there was only one waiter there, she messed up the order and forgot about us. She was pretty busy though so I don't want to blame her too much, I've decided now that this place is totally overrated and only good for the pancakes, crab cakes and take-out buttermilk biscuits. I would never wait in line for a table.

Ippudo was pretty tasty! Â I ordered the akamaru modern which was topped with their secret miso paste, pork chashu, cabbage, sesame kikurage mushrooms, scallions, and fragrant garlic oil. Â The broth was hot and flavorful, the noodles were cooked to a medium texture (not too firm, not too soft) and the toppings worked as a perfect combination. Â Although, I didn't taste the garlic oil. Â  We got there shortly after they opened for lunch, which was good because we didn't have to wait, and by the time the place started to fill up with the lunch crowd our tums were full and we were out the door. The staff is nice, the decor is cool and traditional, and the service was fast. Â I would come back to Ippudo. - Brownie Out!

Visiting NYC from Los Angeles. The location in the Chelsea Market was fabulous. The ambiance was very nice. Excellent service!I Our first course, the squash appetizer, was refreshing and unique. I definitely recommend it. The rest of the meal was average. Mac N Cheese was slightly over cooked and nothing special. Chicken liver mousse was ok. the highlight of the meal was the sausage and lentils ordered by my brother in law. The flavor of the beef blood sausage was excellent with plenty of fennel, but the texture was a little too dry. Homade ice cream for desert was very nice. Overall, it was a good meal at a very nice location, but nothing to write home about. I was really looking for NY dining to exceed what I can find in Los Angeles and I definitely prefer many of the restaurants in my "backyard" to this one.

These burgers are something else! The bun is soft and fluffy. The patty is cooked just right and really packs big flavor. When you come, go for the truffle burger. It's tastes really original compared to other such as the manly burger which taste more like generic burgers. This is the reason why I am taking one star away simply because it seems that only only one item was unique in character. The fries and onion rings did not taste unique either. The waitress was extremely friendly and flashed big genuine smiles!

The Singapore Kari Laksa soup was featured in the December 2009 issue of New York Magazine in its 50 Best soups piece. Â I am currently attempting to try all of these soups, and whenever I am in a neighborhood where the soup is made, I'm there. This was by far one of the most delicious soups I've ever had.
