Â You absolutely cannot go wrong with this choice, if you like a rich broth and tons of flavor (if you don't like tons of flavor, you should leave this website). Â It was under $6, and kept me full for a long time. Â A bargain I would say. Â Make sure you add a moderate amount of their hot sauce and stir it in real good. Â The seafood in the soup is very fresh, and a great assortment at that. Â They load it with shrimp, squid, fish balls, and chicken, all in extremely generous amounts. The staff is really nice as well (although I did get it take-out). Â It's conveniently located 1 block from the Elmhurst Ave. R-V station, so it's quite easy to get to. Â Make sure your eyes are open though, it's a tiny place among many other restaurants and things on the block. Â If you're out there, or live in Elmhurst and haven't been to Taste Good, GO.

I ate here at this pleasant Chinese restaurant during my first visit to NYC. The pizza and cheese steaks are out of this world! Â I especially like to franks red hot they put on their wings served with a cold one. The football games on big screens are a plus as well. Lastly, the take out garlic and chicken is great. The mozzarella sticks are the BOMB. Â If you like Chinese food, I recommend you pass. Chinese food,wings,and beer will make you explode.
Love this place! Have been coming here for the past year and the food is always good, I've tried and liked: empanadas platano relleno Â  Taquitos coconut shrimp carnitas (so much food!!) skirt steak
yummy yummy. Â great for the drunk crowd.

went back again last Friday for their happy hour, we got: -mussels and fries: Â excellent fries, crispy and not overly salty or greasy. Â mussels had a flavorful broth, but not very fresh. -raw oysters: Â tasted a bit odd, bland (?) better with cocktail sauce, skip the migonette. Â  -fried calamari: Â the day's special, crispy, Â flavorful, and wonderful with the marinara and garlic aioli -red sangria: Â strong and delicious with our meal -strawberry lemonade: Â yummy! Â  finally, they bring you complimentary salted caramel donut holes at the end of your meal, i love them when they serve the donuts at brunch, these are the same, just smaller. Â :-)

Good food, great atmosphere, decor is off-the-wall. Â Our meal was a prix-fix which was delicious, but a little too much for us. Â They have a good wine selection. Â We were sat next to strangers on a long table, but it wasnt too intrusive and we enjoyed the company also. Â  It was a little pricey, but thats NYC for you. Â Good for a special occasion.

Randomly stumbled into this place last weekend and was oh so pleased. It's beautiful. Huge ceiling, gorgeous furniture and all sorts of Victorian paintings, mirrors, frames. A lovely stained glass window in the back. The decor is amazing esp. if you are into that style! I think it's worth going just for the atmosphere alone. Good whiskey selection and good service. I felt the food was a bit lacking. Got spinach & artichoke dip as well as the calamari and thought it was kind of bland. Nonetheless, I'd still come back here for the awesome vibe and whiskey. Hidden gem in an obnoxious touristy area.

Incredible! This place came highly recommended, and I was far from dissapointed. Â It looks like a corner grocery store from the outside, but don't let it fool you, this is a fantastic deli. I had the pho real sandwich, and my wife had the bbq chicken kimchee hero. Â Luckily, i found a park bench a few blocks away because the pho real sandwich would have dropped me to my knees. Â Wow. Â For 6 bucks, what a value because I could only eay half. Â I gave the rest to a homeless guy...I think I made his day. The bbq chicken kimchee was quite incredible also...never thought to use kimchee on a sandwich but I'm sold. Â I wish I remembered whatever else was on that sandwich. Â If someone could get a picture or just send me the ingredients of the bbq chicken kimchee hero...I would be forever in your debt. You must go visit this place, it is truly a hidden gem in a city of great food. Â  Thanks Chris H for the great pictures...I'm going to try making the pho real at home. Â I'll definitely go back to this place every time I visit NY.
Great Steak Tacos : D Â  Â  Â  Â  Â  Â  Â  Â  Â  Â  Â  Â  Â  Â  Â  Â  Really affordable you really get your money's worth at this spot .

I was a bit torn on this one.... The service was great, the crowd was young and hip, the atmosphere is good and the food was good (but not great). I would normally give 4 stars for good but not great food with all those other pluses but when I drop $150 (for 2 people) on a few small plates and a few beers, AND I need a sandwich after, it needs to be damn good food. Especially in the heart of the Gowanus. Long story short, it's a great place to go with friends if you don't mind spending a little more than you should.

Diner is a perennial favorite. Â The front dining room makes you feel like you're in a railcar: Â intimate without being suffocating. Â From the handcut tiles to the custom light fixtures, this places has an exceptional design. Â I have had many great dinners at diner, but the most memorable are about the fish.

- Sunday night reggae/soca/Caribbean party is ON FIYAH!!!! - People start showing up around 12 - If you get there early enough, you can commandeer yourself a seat - Although not very many gyal, the music is good enough to vibe too - Drinks range from $9-12 - Reception sucks - Hard to imagine this is a classy Italian place by day

So, so, so, so, so, so, SOOOOOO good. Really that's all I should have to say. The price is totally worth it. Cauliflower soup=awesome Zucchini tapas=Amazing Whatever tilapia entree my boyfriend got = out of this world. We will definitely return again, and again, and again.

Fourth of July. Such an important day, so I wanted to eat something safe for lunch; Ebi Tempura Udon. Strange taste of soup and hardly cooked noodle, which gave me a runny bowl straight away (Don't give me 12-hr pitch, 'cause I know what I ate.) Not coming back. Period.
Greta food and great people. Â The rabbit was terrific and their hamburgers are second to none.

absolutely love this place. one of my favorite place in manhattan. the best mojito ever. especially in summer night, get a kiwi mojito at the bar. great ambiance, fabulous drinks. i tried salmon or something fish dish, it was above average, but i can't remember details. it was just good. if not drinking, i'd rather go for brunch during weekend. FANTASTIC french toast, yummy and hearty(?) bloody mary :-) grilled potato on side was great too. i've never made reservation to get a table here, but always able to get chairs at the bar. i don't mind eating at the bar here, because bartenders can make real good drinks and don't try to make annoying conversation. a little expensive, but worth it.

Oh dear I'm afraid yellow privilege really got the best of me this time. I've been going to Tasty Hand-Pulled Noodles for years and only JUST realized --after reading a review lamenting the dumpling sauce-- that y'all wide-eyes don't have the recipe for a basic dumpling sauce stored in your DNA, inherited from one dynasty to the next. So! I'm gonna tell you what to do, for those times when you don't know what to dip your dumplings into. First off, the dumplings here are truly amazing. No hard little meat anchors here! These dumplings use plenty of napa cabbage to create a juicy, tender, not-too-greasy, filing. The ones I had today were particularly beautifully-made, like freakin' origami. Architectural, brah. Anyway, ok, so the bare bones dumpling sauce only has two ingredients, and they are: Black Vinegar + Soy Sauce. Dats it. The vinegar is sharp and sweet and balances out the earthy and savory soy sauce. And they work perfectly together like a pair of antagonistic muscles in Michael Phelps' swimmery shimmery bodice. If you wanna fancy it up, you can add hot sauce, or sesame oil (not too much eh) and that's basically it. I think one of the hot sauces on the table has crushed garlic in it? That's niiiice. About this place: well, it's super cheap and it's super good. The broth doesn't come to the table particularly salted, it's got this pure animal bone taste that is just heavenly. And then you dress it up to your liking. But man, what a base to work with! It's like building a mountain when you are already on another mountain. The pan-fried noodles are shockingly delicious. Again, seasoned with a light hand. But even before you add any sauces to it, the frickin' thing tastes like pleasure incarnate. Something about the oil they use and how it adheres to the chewy, perfectly-cooked noodles... makes my stomach get all emo in a good way. What else --the cold cucumber is great, with a well-balanced sauce. And service is quick and happy. Tip them well, you cheap bastards!

DEFINITELY WORTH IT. First time at Laduree, and even though the line was almost out the door, the employees treated us very well! Answered all our questions and they were quite patient with my indecisiveness. We got the box of 8, which came out to be ~$23. Sea salt caramel / vanilla / rose / coffee / dark chocolate / chocolate / lavender / pistachio. It was also my mother's first time having macarons, and she was pleased! Would come back every single next time that I'm in New York City :)

I've been here 2 times, however the last time is what is causing me to write this review. Â My first experience was for brunch, which I remember as being good food, however it was a while ago. Â My last time back to Stone Park Cafe really makes me question going back. Â My wife and I both ordered appetizers, a bottle of wine, dinner, and a desert to share. Â The appetizers were great. Â My wife enjoyed her Corn soup and I my Frisee Salad. Â For dinner I ordered the Pan seared cod, and my wife a vegitable lasagne. Â My cod was very salty and as a cod goes, had little flavor, even with the light sauce they used. Â Under the cod was a Bok Choy which was overly spiced and also tasted salty. Â The lasagna my wife had was not at all what she expected and also was too salty for her. Â There was too much cheese and not enough vegetable (a common problem with any "vegetable" dish). Â  For wine I ordered a 2009 Beaujolais, however what I got was a 2007 bottle that cost me $12 extra. Â Unfortunately I didn't notice the mistake until I got the bill. Â Looking at the wine list off their website I'm not sure how the mistake occured given the two wines are not even next to eachother. Â  For desert we ordered a chocolate pudding which I felt was decent, a little dry if I was too be picky, but decent. Overall, I'd say the atmosphere was ok. Â This is not a restaurant where I would go in with high expectations as some of the reviews suggest. Â As destinguished by my two stars, there's definitely better in the neighborhood.

Sigh... Oh Cafe Luluc where do I begin on the subtle, but very blatant disrespect- other people might tolerate just to eat here, but I won't. I have been to this establishment a few times and with no problems, but yesterday somehow was a very different scenario. I came with my significant other and as usual there was a wait which is fine. We were standing behind a couple who was ahead of us and they were seated within a couple minutes, since they wanted to be seated outside and there was no wait. Another caucasian couple comes in and the seater goes straight to them and asked how many...? The couple stated " I think they were here before us" and pointing towards us. They also didn't mind outside seating, so they were seated. Two Caucasian fellows came in and once again, they were asked if they wanted to sit outside and they say no, inside. Guess what? They were seated and finally when this seater saw our looks of disbelief, we were seated. Not only was I outraged, I was quite embarrassed and made to feel very unwelcome as an African American in 2014. I told my significant other that I no longer wanted to eat there today or ever, so we got up and left. Now, the staff is asking is everything okay like they dont know what happened, and one of the staff says the guys have been waiting for awhile. Really? Where were they? There is never a list of names they take, because it is a first come, first serve basis. I have been here before, I know the drill. If you knew what you did, why ask? Just apologize. Cafe Luluc, if I could give you zero stars I would. I really started to like this place, but no matter how good the food is, it is not worth being uncomfortable and made to feel unwelcome.

I've been here three times with my bro and thought I should finally write a review. This place has some of the best service and food in Williamsburg. The staff is very knowledgeable and friendly (which is hard in Williamsburg, I always feel like the pple (who are normally hipsters) who work at these establishments have an air of superiority and no personality, but not here. The food quality is superb. Each time I have went the food has tasted so fresh and cooked to perfection. There was a minor mishap, where they brought out the wrong plates of food, and it was handled very nicely. The menu changes, but whatever they have will not disappoint you. I love this place and hope it continues to deliver the goods!

Fantastic banh mi! I've enjoyed their classic pork, steak, and pork belly sandwiches. Last time I was there they were playing classic Rakim joints through their in-house stereo so that's an extra 100 points right there. (Other restaurants looking for Yelp love take note! :) Very few seats and the stools upstairs aren't comfortable for more than 15 mins. But you only need 5 mins to suck down their amazing banh mi so it all works out fine. Â :)
this place NEVER disappoints !! Â the best paninis u will ever have are here .. the service is wonderful .. everything about this place isnwonderful

Oh my God this place is incredible. Get there early. Â I got there at 6pm on a Thursday and it was OK. Â When we left at 8pm there was about a 30 min line. The best bacon wrapped over asparagus I've ever had. Â Even their chicken gizzard sauteed with daikon and onion was delicious. I think the food quality here is better than Taisho. Perhaps this place is a little more expensive, but it's worth it. To get in, look for the words above the door that say "sake bar". Â 2 doors to the left of the entrance to Sapporo restaurant.

First time at Minetta Tavern? Get the Black Label burger. It really is a perfect burger. So good it doesn't even need cheese? Crazy messy and absolutely enormous but worth it. Get the basket of pastries! The donut is absolutely delicious. While everyone raves about the Black Label burger, I just want to talk about the donut. Extremely dense and fairly small but each bite is worth the calorie binge. Cozy, in a perfect location, and full of unreasonably attractive people.

I've been to Roberta's a handfull of times, not only because I live around the corner, but because i've always had a great experience there. Â The bib salad is awesome, followed by a huge flat crust, fresh ingredients-made pizza. Â They have a moderately good selection of beers (not sure about the wine selection), and during the winter they have a fire outside. The staff is always lovely and the food comes super quickly (even when it's crowded!). Â The last time I was there, my date and I shared a round table with another couple because it was so busy. Â It wasn't awkward as the tables are pretty large, and we felt so European! Careful when you're trying to find it, it's really easy to walk right passed.

Food 6/5 Service 5/5 Ambiance?Ambience? 5/5 One of he best meals I've ever had. I had the orzo. Sister had the tortellini. Amazing. Go try it folks. . I'm not as elaborate because I'm still dreaming of the food. Carrot cake - best I've ever had.
delicious-super cheap
Fan. As a vegan they had PLENTY of choices for me, and they were legitimately good too. I love this spot.

Thank you Swift for feeding me at ridiculously late hours of night. Thank you also for having a great beer selection - wouldn't be surprised if it was one of the best in NYC. Staff were super-friendly too and clearly saw my plight of hunger & thirst and decided only they could help me - which they did. Woodsy, dim-lit, cozy ambiance.

There is plenty of eye candy here. If the meal ended there, the restaurant would rate a full-fledged 5 stars. Other positives were a genuinely welcoming staff with a strong, though high-priced wine list. Unfortunately for all, this is a restaurant, one striving for creativity and great taste. This is where all goes awry. There were 2 stand-outs-sea urchin rice & Jeju island fish. All the rest was off-point. Unusual yes. Distinctive NO. Tasty TERRIBLE miss. Now it wasn't bad but where is the flavor thread, the harmony, the flavor balance. For that, it's not here. I might have given this a higher mark, if we had less experience with truly good. Food, I wish them well and maybe this was an off night. The lobster was drowned in a thick sauce with no clear flavors, no pungency, no clarity, no robustness or delicacy. This place is an Off the charts miss. Save your $$$$$. Go to any of the other NY 5stars just stay away from PerSe unless you've got an expense account to raid their incredible wine collection. Again, the people here are nice. Maybe go for a chat or better yet find out where they go after work. Meet them there and have a drink with them at the bar. Â Phenomenal MISS the mark!!!. Spectacularly disappointing!!! This was my Valentine's day dinner since I'm supposed to be away that day. Ooops!!! I'll have to take my wife elsewhere when I return.

Meh. SO FATTY. I have traveled all over the South eating BBQ. It's my favorite thing to eat. Why nowhere good to go in Brooklyn, the hotbed of culinary activity? When in Austin I frequent the Salt Lick. In Memphis, more places than I can count and went all around Los Angeles eating BBQ. Even so far as Robin's Woodfire Grill in Hastings Ranch, CA (like 2 hours in LA traffic). I mean, I will go the distance for good BBQ. My boyfriend and I left this place with serious stomach pains. And not the good kind. Greasy, greasy, greasy. The sides, everything. My brisket had HUNKS of fat that I had to cut around. Come on. The whiskey list was great. But the seating style left me elbowing my neighbor while trying to wrestle some fatty meat off the bone of my rack of ribs. Save my life and bring good BBQ to Brooklyn!

I came across this place looking for a near by Italian place n boy was I surprised! Great wine list... I had pasta with meat sauce not a fan but I fell in love with this polenta dish they have... So amazing melts in your mouth...I would recommend for light appetizers n wine

A meat lover's paradise, try the flank steak, lambshank, veal etc. all veritable bargains for the price. Come early or you'll have a frustrating endless wait unless you have the patience of a Golden Retriever.

A little respite from the busy streets and life of NY. I can only vouch for the items on the $15 prix-fixe menu served from 5-7pm -- absolutely loved it. It was a blustery Wednesday night and we had passed Paprika a few times in the past vowing to come back to try the prix-fixe since it seemed to be such a deal! 2 course dinner for $15?? How could you go wrong? Except if... the portions were small or the food just tasted horrible. But that was just not the case!! When we entered the restaurant @ 6:15pm there was only one other group there, enjoying their dinner at the corner table nearest the window. The restaurant was dimly lit with candles and votives on every table -- romantic, cozy, a great place to bring a date. Service was great! We were seated within minutes, the hostess, the waitress, everyone who attended to us was friendly and attentive. Our water was never empty for more than a few minutes. The waitress and hostess checked in with us without being intrusive. The only thing that I would suggest is that they should provide bread plates... we used the olive plate and the bread basket as substitutes... As for the food! Let's talk about the food! As mentioned before we ordered off the $15 menu and because of the price I figured that the quality may be good but the quantity would be small, or vice versa. BUT the portions were impressive! The salad was huge considering and the entree was pretty norm, but for its quantity and its flavor you would expect to pay something upwards of $30+ for something equivalent elsewhere. We started with the arugula + shaved parmesan + apple salad & the goat's cheese + pear + arugula salad. I would recommend getting the goat's cheese salad. It's more flavorful and all the components meld together better, you've got the sweetness of the walnuts and pears, you've got the strong flavor of the goat's cheese, and the bitterness of the arugula. The shaved parmesan salad was a little too bitter for me and lacked something I can't identify. As for entrees we ordered the gnocchi in tomato sauce & the salmon over spinach. The salmon was fantastic! It had the perfect crunch on the outside but was still moist, super tender, melt in your mouth deliciousness on the inside. The spinach was a perfect accompaniment, just salty enough and added a great texture to the fish -- I highly recommend it! The gnocchi was unbelievably soft but the plate left something to desire. Besides the tomato sauce & the melted mozzarella there was really no other flavors, no other textures, and I think it was just too much of the same thing. Again this place is fantastic and I would definitely come back -- next time to try the rest of the prix fixe items! Highly recommended! 5-7!

Great place!! Â Always fun to come with friends, the food & drinks are sooooo yummy :) Â Yuca Bar has such a cool ambiance, everyone there just wants to chill out & have a good time. Â Sometimes there's a short wait for tables, but it's worth it & the service is really good once your seated. Â The guacamole & homemade tortilla chips are awesome, as is the mahi mahi with mango sauce, and the fish taquitos!

Fantastic birthday dinner. Love that all the dishes come in half or full portions for tasting. Had the best octopus ever as a starter, as well as fresh sea urchin on seaweed and fried quinoa on top. For the main, I had lobster in butter with raspberry coulis, and as a person who never orders lobster, it was worth it! My wife had veal cheek, and I wish I could've tried it but she loved it. It lives up to the reviews. The service is attentive nice and knowledgeable. A great meal.

Wife, daughter and I went to Totto to give it a try, and had to wait 1 hour in line before getting in. Â If I was rating ONLY the food, I might bump my rating up to "4". But in rating the whole experience, I'm sticking with "3". The Food - in general, the food was good. I liked my soup more than my wife and daughter liked theirs. They got the basic, and I got the spicey version. That might have accounted for why mine tasted better. Â We started with the pork belly buns - good, and I'd eat more. The ramen was tasty. I prefer a milky pork broth, but Totto only serves chicken broth. And they do a nice job. The Experience - Totto is so small, there is not much seating. Only 2 tables that seat 4, a couple tables seating 2, and the rest must sit at the bar. My wife, daughter and I had to sit at the bar. You sign up your name on a clip board and wait. Standing on the sidewalk. Waiting. No indication when your turn might come up. Parties of 1 or 2, got in more quickly, in fact, some arrived after us, and got in first. That bothered us. Once inside, the staff was friendly and attentive (good), but it's so tight and crowded, it's not really a place to sit and relax and enjoy your meal. You feel like you need to get in, eat fast and get out, so they can get the next folks in. Bottom line: I won't go back. It's not worth waiting in line for the food or experience. There is better food, and better experiences to be had elsewhere. Â  On the other hand, there are long waiting lines for a reason. So maybe you should decide for yourself.
Best of the Best.. Love the food and atmosphere, exclusive only for the best of the best. Never forget ya..

I was recently on holiday in New York City and upon a friend's recommendation I headed for The Dead Rabbit at the end of a long day of sight-seeing. Although the Taproom seemed to be where the craic was at, my tourist feet were having none of it and weren't going to give over until I was in the Parlor with a rejuvenating cocktail. So I sat outside on the cutest little swing chair with my partner-in-crime while the bouncer kept his eye out for some seating upstairs. Once seated, by a truly attentive yet unobtrusive waiter, I was dazzled by the cocktail list. I was going to need a drink in order to actually peruse the cultural and historical work of art that was providing the selection. And I think the waitress intuitively spotted my little dilemma since she asked me about which cocktails I'd normally go for and catered to me accordingly. Twice. And both me and my feet were in cocktail heaven. Similarly, we described our food mood, and lazily agreed to have the major decisions made for us. And once again, we were not disappointed. The Dead Rabbit not only serves ridiculously good cocktails, but it is also the home of what can only be described as the ultimate in cocktail sausages! Might seem a little daunting to tourists since it is downtown and therefore no longer on the regular grid system so helpful for visitors to Manhattan. But don't let that turn you off, the surrounding streets are short and interesting anyway, and the place itself is easy to find, even when you're a slightly worn-out tourist in need of food and beverages ;)

How to sum this place up - cool atmosphere, OK service and sub par food. Yes I think that does it quite nicely. The place is really overhyped and the food is nowhere near as good as at the other 5 thai restaurants within a 2 block radius. I ordered the sea food pad thai and it was one of the worst I have had. Oddly watery with no flavor. I was with a group of 4 and none of the others thought their food was any good. at best it was mediocre. In summary go here if you want to admire the shiny decor but go somewhere else for the food.

Where to start with this restaurant. Well, I guess the most appropriate place would be to address how to eat here. I first found out about the existence of Bohemian after I visited the Japanese meat market that is associated with it. After doing hours (literally) of research on this place, I decided to take the route of emailing them and introducing myself. In this email I was honest about who I am and asked for the opportunity to dine there. I guess it left a good impression as only a couple of hours later, we received an email back with the phone number we could contact to make a reservation (I think we made the reservation that same day as well). The email that was returned to us was personally written and acknowledge things that I had written to them. I'm mentioning this because I want to point out that this isn't some automated response or generic boilerplate email they return. This was some hand crafted, personally addressed ish I'm talking about here. Which, maybe I'm old fashion, I think is pretty awesome. Now onto the good stuff. This place is freaking awesome. From the moment you step in, you kind of forget that you are in NYC. The restaurant is small and the tables/seats are actually spread out so each table has more than enough personal space. The seats are not normal restaurant seats, but instead are something you would buy if you owed a super modern and cool apartment. The owner of the restaurant (who was also our waiter) introduced himself and thanked us for coming in. His service was very good, not intimidating or rushing whatsoever. At one point he even talked to us about what we had written in our email to them. In a city that isn't necessarily known for having the best customer service at restaurants, this was a pleasant surprise. It was like they actually cared about the people eating at their restaurant, which I think speaks volumes about the Bohemian's purpose. This is a place that cares about the quality of food they are serving and the people that are eating it. The food itself was incredible. If you read any other of my reviews, you'll see that I only give 5 stars to places that I believe are the best in their respective categories. The category I place the Bohemian in is for "steak". He steak here was unbelievable. The daily menu for the different types comes on a cow shaped chalk board that highlights which part of the cow the steak comes from. We asked what he recommended and suggested what he thought was the best cut of the day. This stuff was literally dream-able. It came out pre-cut and was cooked perfectly. If you ever get the pleasure of dining in this establishment, please do yourself a favor and order the steak here. We also had the wagyu sashimi which was also incredible. The drinks were perfectly made as well. With the quality of the food that was given to us and the smallness of the restaurant you would think that this would be one of the most expensive meals in NYC. Think again. That's what is so cool about this place. They don't necessarily care about making millions of dollars. They are about providing a quality product to customers who enjoy great food and dining experiences. This is a top, if not the top, restaurant for me in NYC.

Stopped in about 5:00 on a Wednesday for a drink, great selection of bourbons, (I'm a bourbon fan) and the staff was great, two bartenders were very attentive. I will definitely be back for drinks again!

Addictive drugs come in many forms - sniffing, injecting, etc. Â At this cart, it comes in the form of a crack like white sauce. I have been to NY before already, but this trip I went twice to this cart. Â I was given a look of disapproval for going a 3rd and 4th time - I may have to end that friendship. Â I came for a wedding, but instead I took the time to renew my vows of love for the lovely lamb and rice - for better or worse, hot or cold, forever and ever. It may not always seem like it, but these guys are efficient. I recommend the lamb over the rice because of the visible fat content. Â I put on a layer of white sauce where nothing else can be seen. Â Be careful of the red sauce - a good kick. I under estimated it's power and had to get a drink of water. Â It was too much for my brother so instead of splitting 50/50 I ate all but 3 bites of this food from heaven. Hangover or not, this is a great late night food. Â Be prepared to wait about 30 minutes to get your food, but you are entertained by the aroma of the food, the diversity of the crowd (I've seen a fight break out there), and eloquent conversation of nom nom noms. I have been to James Beard Award winning restaurants, but if I could only have time for one meal in New York, this would be it.
So delicious! Friendly staff, incredible atmosphere.

This place is cash only. Got there and there was a mini line- moved fast. Was concerned about the C rating on the front of the store. What's up with that?! I came here cuz my bro made a big hype about this place- said it was the best pizza ever. I had the artichoke pizza- pretty huge for $4.75. It had Alfredo sauce and mini veggie bits. Cheese was over the top. Pizza was 3 stars. Took a star off for price and burned bottom. And another for C rating.

Pretty good -- and certainly a great option for non-NY style pizza in the South Slope. Nothing to travel for, though. I found the plain pizza to be undersalted and the beer selection isn't so hot. Eh.
the best gluten free pizza that I have ever had. you cannot even tell it is gluten free. great salads, great wine and great selection of gf beers. this place is outstanding.
Great place to grab delicious Korean/some Japanese food. Â Everything is pretty much $6 and the flavors are fresh and bold. Â Also, beers are less than $3, which is a steal in NY.

What a cute unexpected modern-ish space hidden under the 7 train! I heard about Himalayan Yak from a co-worker and pictured a hole in the wall but behind those big doors is a nice place serving a variety of extremely affordable dishes. I've never had Tibetan or Nepalese food before and (IMO) it's a bit of a cross of Indian and Chinese food. Started off traditional veggie momos. Even though we ordered them pan fried (other option is steamed) they were NOT greasy. In fact, they seemed mostly steamed with just a bit of frying to make the outside a bit crispy. 8 pieces to a serving and they were very plump and generously filled with green veggies and potatoes. The trio of sauces they give you were pretty good (sesame & tomato, avocado and chili) I also had a noodle soup with vermicelli noodles (note: the menu said Bean thread noodles but this was fine too) cooked with mixed vegetables, pieces of dried fungus, black mushroom and potato served with tingmo (Tibetan steamed bun) The broth was really good and veggies fresh, also had a lot of potatos in it which made it quite filling. I didn't care for the tingmo - even though it reminded me of other kinds of Chinese steamed plain buns - it was much blander. My husband ordered a beef dish that was very similar to what we order at a Chinese restaurant in Flushing. Slices of sizzling beef with red pepper, onion, garlic, ginger etc. He really liked it though he didn't' care for the bhaley - another Tibetan bread - also dry and flavorless. Service was efficient, upstairs had live music and decor is nice and more modern than I expected.

We got a Cuban sandwich, a stuffed corn item (can't remember the name), sweet plantains, spicy spinach, and lemonades. We sat at the counter overlooking Elizabeth street and it was a great quick option. I liked all the food very much but my husband thought the pork on the sandwich was too dry. If I lived near this place I would go by frequently.

Yes this is worth the hype and the wait. Â I waited until I had a random day off from work to attempt to get a brunch in here. Â Went with the blueberry pancakes and a couple pounds of bacon to make the most of the experience. Â No complaints, totally delicious and forced myself to eat every single bite and savor. Â Good coffee and our waitress at the bar was great. Â I would definitely go back if I had a day off.

This is an incredible place for brunch when you are in the mood for something different. Â It is located on St. Marks so is as unpretentious as they come and not really fancy or beautiful as far as the patio seating, but the brunch food makes up for it. I had the pumpkin pancakes (how can you not?) and sausage with pistachios in them. Â So incredibly yummy. This place does not take reservations. Â I think the three of us ended up showing up around noon on a Sunday and had to wait 15-20 minutes and we sat indoors. Â You basically put your name down and they call you. Â If you really don't want to wait, you should try to come earlier. Â Brunch ended up lasting almost an hour and a half and they didn't rush us in the least though we did keep ordering more coffee and tea.

the line that forms here is no joke. we got here 30 minutes before opening and there already was a line. nestled right next to the brooklyn bridge and a famous homemade ice cream place... this place is definitely a tourist trap. but who cares!... the pizza here is freakin' good. they don't serve by the slice but by the pie. we ordered one with pepperoni, sausage, and onions... and the other just plain. i thoroughly enjoyed the pepperoni, sausage and onions pie. the mozzarella was fresh... crust was perfect... and toppings were delicious. as for the plain... it was good but not great. i am totally craving pizza right now.

Note : 6/10 Food : Good Wine: Ok Ambiance : Interesting! Service : Good Went there this afternoon and didn't have a reservation we've been lucky to get a table though. Ordered scallops, mussels with chorizo and croquetas with goat cheese it was good but I don't recommend the mussels which were good but not worth the price. The lamb was good but a little overcooked. We tried three different wines but didn't find any decent wine to please the food. The dessert were good except that the creme brulee which arrived cold at the table, that's a big mistake considering the ambition of the restaurant. Oh also concerning the ambiance I was really surprised that they only played music from the very early 90s, I still wonder why. The service was better than most of the restaurant I have been to In town, but just good, not great. An other time after I go in a restaurant in NYC I feel like the bill concerns more the walls than the dinner itself. For only 200$ and less in Paris you would have an outstanding and memorable dinner (two people), I don't think you can find the equivalence in NYC and everything I tried at this price remains very average.

We sat at the bar for dinner and I had a cobb salad while my friend ordered the market plate (4 sides for $15) option. He had the brussels sprouts w/ honey dijonaise, artichoke hearts with parmesan, tomato, basil, and mozzarella salad, and sweet potato fries. All of the sides were great (definitely would order them again) - except the artichoke hearts, which we barely touched. They were mushy and just kind of unappetizing. I think we were expecting marinated artichokes, but these seemed to be baked. The cobb salad was good - the bacon was a little overcooked (very hard and chewy), but the greens were fresh and the avocado was perfectly ripe. I felt like a fat ass asking for more dressing, but they kindly obliged.

Great service, great food, impeccably clean space. 1) Omurice-- good 2) Osaka style omelet with cucumbers sandwich-- good 3) Hotcakes with orange marmalade butter-- good 4) Cold brew mizudashi iced coffee-- good 5) Siphon coffee-- very good

I LOVED getting brunch here the other day! The House of Small Wonder is so cute and the food is delicious. Everything you want out of a Brunch in Brooklyn. Started of with a mocha and when the waitress swapped it with my friends hot chocolate, she made me a new one free of charge! The croissants were really fresh and although I didn't try it, they make their own gluten free bread in house! Everything on the menu looked great and I will definitely come back here the next time I'm in NY!

I went in and ordered to-go. Got the Underworld and sweet potato fries. It was delicious! The cashews with the apple and the goat cheese, everything went together so well. I can't wait to try another kind of wrap! Sweet potato fries were not the best, but they were okay!

Gyro is disgusting and gave me a stomach ache the hummus sill sucks second time around. I hear the laffa is great but i wouldnt give this place a third chance. The pita is just bland and made with pretty low grade flour and other ingredients.

This place may just be good for drinks. My friends and I came based on recommendation of someone else. So we came for dinner..luckily I had a late lunch so I was not starved. My other friends were. I think our drinks were adequate. The meal however was subpar. It was a monday night and maybe it was Microwave Monday but the food was not delish at all. OMG..I have to pull up the menu to recall what we had. -Coconut curry chicken - STAY away from this. If you never had coconut/curry chicken do not let this be your guide. It was as if the chicken was cooked separately then dumped into the sauce. It was not infused it at all. BLAND! They had this fried chicken ball dish which tasted very sour/tart and I don't think it was intended to. ARGH..everything was just subpar and we ordered about 6 dishes. How can everything be subpar? I mean 1-2 items is okay but the whole shibang to be disappointing was a no no. Will not return.

OK, yes it's pricey. But you are paying for the experience, the fresh warm mozzarella and the great wine. If you have never been, this is one of those experiences you must have. I love their "slogan": they 'cook what they sell and sell what they cook'. I just bought what they cook. We (seven of us) checked out La Piazza, where you grab a spot as it become available and stand at the bar height tables to be served (the wine helped the experience). A couple of points of caution: It can get pricey; it can get very crowded on the weekends (very!); and the restrooms are at the end of the beer section.

I never thought I would get a chance to visit Laduree since it is located in Paris but decided to take a vacation in New York for a week and got really excited to go buy macarons. Â This was on my must visit list :) My friends and I decided to come here around 530pm and lucky there was not much of a line so we really didn't wait. yay! The decor of the shop was super cute and love the layout. There were other things on sale but I didn't get a chance to take a peek. Yet again too excited. hahaha I purchased a box of 12 and it was so hard to decide which one I really wanted to try so I got them all! It is pricy for a dessert but I won't always be in NYC so it made up for my spending there. It was cool that I met the cashier who is also from my hometown of San Jose, CA.

I'm dreaming about their old fashion pizza right now. It's that good. Go there and get it - you won't be disappointed. Also of note, it's not your typical New York thin crust like Lombardi's or Grimaldi's - it's its own special thing. Also, Stone Street can be good fun in the summer months when they close the street and all of the restaurants do outdoor seating.
I love coming here for the atmosphere. The food is okay. I've had most of the items on menu.
Best pizza ever!!!
Sat at the bar next to a crazy old man. We laughed, we cried, we discussed how crazy we were. I felt so happy to be in NY again. The pizza was awesome...great...lovely...yummy. Will go back for sure!

My well-behaved 4 year old and I joined the Ladies Who Lunch crowd on a Tuesday afternoon. Â Our waiter was super attentive, although both my wine and salad took a bit longer to arrive than expected. Â That said, the seafood cobb salad just might have been worth the wait, especially with the white balsamic vinaigrette. Â Considered 3 stars but a waitress fell (and hurt herself) with an entire tray of drinks. Â It was handled well, and quickly, and I'm currently in a good mood, so 4 stars.

For the first time ever, I feel my fellow Yelpers have let me down. Perhaps my expectations were too high. Well, certainly, anyone would expect a good meal (even for greasy street meat) when 2,650+ reviews yields an overall 4.5 star rating! I wasn't expecting the world, nor glitter-specked unicorn meat covered in a golden magical sauce. but I was expecting something that would blow my mind just slightly. All I got was undercooked yellow rice, limp iceberg lettuce, unappetizingly greasy gyro, lukewarm and questionable white sauce, and a nauseating stomachache that has not gone away for close to two hours. I'm wicked pissed. Honestly. Booo. My dear halal cart owners on 69th and York could teach these folks a lesson or two...

OK. Last night I went to dinner here and overate. This morning I woke up thinking I really shouldn't order so much and wondered if it's possible to never eat again. But then I read someone's review about hazelnut french toast. Uhoh. Between two of us we had: -Blue Crab with jalapeno and tomato - DELISH -Hamachi with caponata bianco and meyer lemon - DELISH -Calamari-ROCKED -Trofie with basil pesto, taggiasca olives and parmigiano-reggiano- DELISH -Gigantone with Sunday night ragu and provolone picante -Grilled Branzino with roasted sunchokes, dandelion and salsa rossa-DELISH -Apple Rhubarb Crisp - DELISH -Lemon Tart buttermilk gelato, limoncello granita - FRESH AND DELISH I don't eat meat so that's why everything is fish. I loved the ambiance and decor. The service was great. We checked out the garden area and next time would like to eat in this area. Did I mention I'm thinking about not eating for awhile?

So glad we got a recommendation from a friend living in the area to check out Minca's ramen. It was a pretty cold, rainy Sunday and this is exactly what we needed to warm up (and curb a hangover). You can choose your broth and your noodles. We opted for the spicy miso and the waitress recommended the wavy noodles. They also have thick, thin, and whole wheat noodle choices as well but trusting the waitress with the wavy seemed like the way to go. The broth was delicious and the toppings complimented everything so well. Tender pork slices, corn, and hard boiled egg. We also ordered a side of kimchi and cold tofu to share, and they were also great compliments to the meal. The cold tofu is one of my favorite things to order at Japanese restuarants and it was just as satifying here as any other place I've had it. Simple, cold tofu with soy sauce and bonito fish flakes. Makes me drool every time. CASH ONLY!

OK, here are my thoughts. Â Terrible entrance, humid basementy squalor. Â If you can power through, yer in for a treat. Â Fluke sashimi, awesome. Â Edamame, great, though the produce looks a little aged. Â The sake den with red guard is cool. Â Sesame creme brulee??? Â Amazing!

Good times can be found at Empanada Mama. It's a cute little place that serves up some interesting cocktails with a huge variety of empanadas. Being from Chile and growing up on these little pockets of heaven, I wouldn't say the Mama serves up authentic empanadas BUT they are pretty good and the price it right. The fried ones weren't greasy nor where they heavy which is usually the case. Open 24 hours, this is a great place to grab a snack, light meal, or soak up all the alcohol you drank after hours. I love these little hole in the walls. Every city should have an Empanada Mama. Life would be a better place.

I'm going back..ASAP...Had the brisket and the pork ribs..amazing!! I wasn't too into the potato salad, but my girlfriend was. The sauces on the table are pretty good. One has a pretty nice kick to it. Can't wait to go back and try more. (The rolls are pretty good too)

Fresh, delicious, home cooked and unpretentious food served in a homey setting in the Chelsea market. Â I really enjoyed this place and would love to re-visit. What we ordered: Mac and Cheese: sinful and comforting :)) Brussel Sprouts: perfect contrast of sweet and salty. Harvest Salad: just a salad but fresh and crispy. Mushroom Pot Pie: I ordered this because they are known for their pot pies. While I am not a huge pot pie fan, this was a very original and yummy recipe. The crust was definitely homemade. The filling was a bit too seasoned with rosemary for my taste, but its a good option if you like pot pies and don't feel like eating meat. My friends ordered the crab cakes and scallops and risotto. Both were flavorful and delicious as well. Normally, I hear that there is an hour + wait here, but we got lucky on a rainy Friday night and were seated immediately. Very reasonable prices and super nice service.

Came here for a birthday dinner. Portions for everything are very small. I got the macaroni and cheese which was basically smothered with raw onions. The steamed artichoke appetizer was bland, bland, bland. My friend got the special for the night which seriously looked and tasted like something you would eat at a badly catered wedding in the 90s. THEN both me and another person at our table told our server it was her birthday at different points in the night. After dinner we waited, and waited and waited to the point where the birthday girl Â ASKED us if someone had told them it was her birthday. We had TOLD the server we wanted the date cake beforehand. He still came over with menus at the end so we could order dessert. Are you kidding? The birthday girl looked so sad, totally thinking we hadn't told them it was her birthday. THEN to top off the whole thing, we took TWO photos of the birthday girl, and he came over and said " we kind of have a no flash rule at night" Understandable if you are being obnoxious but we took two photos and there was one other group in the restaurant and they clearly did not care. Afterwards, I got terrible sick and that never happens to me. The point - do not eat here. Also expensive if you want to be full when you leave. Do not go.
There is nothing bad about this place. Have and would eat here every day if I could.
Great fast burritos! The salsas and guacamole are delicious, a great alternative to Chipotle! Only wish they hadn't removed the fountain sodas!

Well we wanted to order take out but we just called and said we wanted take out and not knowing we righy in front she said we close but as I wait in the car literally in front of it then my friend went inside and order take out but her face was priceless. ...I mean what the hell just because yall don't want to stay up late and take this last money cause every customer thats come brings money on the table so after my long ride all I wanted was some spanish food! But Hopefully the food will taste good if not yall will know about it:)

Chef Mark Simmons of Top Chef fame and formerly of Melt Restaurant has recently opened a new place in Park Slope. Kiwiana. Â  Great buzz and judging from the last meal I had with Mark you won't want to miss this one! Chef Mark will personally cook and speak with this very exclusive offering.
