Priced to include tax and tip for $89.95 with great wine pairings...and with pairings like Smoked and pickled green lip mussels with Huia Gewurztraminer, how can you go wrong! Here's the catch.....To get this DEAL you have to pre-pay @ meetup.com/Eat-Me-New-Yoâ€¦

not that ippudo NEEDS any more positive reviews, but here i am, since i just like it so much. i am a ramen addict. i could eat it everyday, in spite of my desire to ban carbs (not gonna happen) this place has great pork buns, i think they are better than momofukus, but the star is the ramen. i like the crinkly kinds the best, not sure if the shape changes anything but htey seem springier and chewier to me. i like me noodles al al denteee. the broth is a little salty, but thats ok with me, and all the toppings are fresh. the only thing that annoys me is they charge you for spicy sauce. why!! plus, i would buy more beer if you gave me free spicy sauce. i love you anyway.

Food was absolutely wonderful. Very fresh and great flavors. Service by our waitress, APRIL was unbelievable!! Â She was great with our choices of wine and food. Â Best Toffee cake for dessert I have ever had.....ummmmm!

More like a 2.5 because of the prices. This is a cute bright place that's perfect for a casual meal. The service is friendly, the decorations quaint/historic. However, the food is only so-so, the prices are more than desirable, and the cleanliness could use some work. All said, this is like any diner (food spattered on menus, no frills, etc), however at non-diner prices. The burgers which came with 1 side were $15-16. Every plate was more than $14. Not a good value considering the quality of the meal. The burger was wayyy less than impressive... tasted like burger patty versus ground beef. Biggest disappointment - the hush puppies. They tried too hard make them interesting whereas hush puppies are by nature delicious. This had random spices in it that was just not doing the job. But thats just me. Not sure I'll be back. I've definitely had better. On a good note, the red velvet cupcake was yums! minus the very heavy cream cheese frosting. It literally outweighed the cupcake itself. Once you scoop that off, you are in chocolaty -red velvet heaven.

I was looking for a place to just grab some casual but tasty food before a show at Bowery Ballroom. Â Yelped it up which usually gives me awesome new finds, however, not this time (a Yelp fluke, I'm sure). The place was semi-cute looking inside. Â Some cool art on the walls. Â The staff was friendly and the cocktails were yummy, hence my 2 stars. Â  But the food. Â Oh the food. We got 3 appetizers. Â It's not that they were bad, they were just, nothing. Â Like I could take them out of a box in my freezer and microwave them myself. Â This really didn't make me want to go for the entrees. Â So I left rather hungry. I might stop back in here if I was walking by and it was during happy hour since the drink specials were good, but I definitely wouldn't order any food.
Two words. Eggs Benedict.
Exquisite setting, perfect service, astonishing food

I'm a fan of meatballs. I like my pastas with meatballs.. i just like to eat meatballs... So i really liked this place. At first, i kind of laughed at the idea of a MEATBALL SHOP... i didnt know they could do so much with just meatballs.. The food is quite delicious. You really can't go wrong with what you get... just go with what you prefer or what your heart desires. no mistakes. promise! I THOUGHT THEIR MENU WAS BRILLIANT! they give you a menu + marker... and you get to mark the items you want for your meal~ mmmm hehehehe! so fun! Their ice cream is amazing! (cinnamon ice cream for the win!) Their cookies... i did not like. So... their ice cream sandwich... it was just okay. But you try and you be the judge. next time i go, i'll just get a scoop of cold goodness.

This weekend I got a tour of Windsor Terrace from a native which, of course, included checking out a couple of the neighborhood bars. Â The Double Windsor was my kind of place. Â It's the perfect place for a relaxed drink--lots of couples on date nights and groups of friends gathering. Â Definitely a diverse group of people. Â I loved the dimly lit ambience and muted wooden tones used throughout the room. Â  I'm not a big beer person but I did see that there was an impressive offering of brews on the menu. Â I'd really like to come back here and try the food. Â The menu is enticing-sounding gastropub fare and looked pretty great but we came after a sumptuous dinner and stuck to drinks only. Â  Overall, I had a terrific time and would highly recommend The Double Windsor. Â I hope to return soon.
Gg

Lived in Brooklyn my whole life but have never been here before, as such I put this place on my bucket list. Finally got a chance to come down here and try their famous pizza. Came here with Â my family around 11 p.m., the line was looongg. I considered leaving because I just hate waiting in lines, but was persuaded to wait it out and glad I did. After you take one bite it is clear why there's a wait. I don't think I have ever had better pizza, anywhere! Surprisingly, the service was exceptional at the place. Usually when you are at a high volume place like this and the place is known for the quality of the food, the service is not of top priority. But I must say I was pleasantly surprised by the service. We ordered 2 cheese, 2 sausage, ans 2 pepperoni and I expected to wait an hour because there wasn't an empty seat in the house. Our food was served hot and delicious in about 20 minutes. I absolutely loved this place, and glad I finally tried it out. Will definitely be back here again, and again, and again.....you get the point.

I came here with a co-worker for lunch because I was having a bad day and it was clear I needed to get out of the building. Â My awesome co-worker saw the look on my face and immediately suggested lunch. Â I asked, hopefully, "Sophie's?" and he said definitely and so we were off. Â We both ordered the cuban sandwich and shared a side of fried plantains. Â The lunch wasn't as remarkable as I thought it would be. Â I had never been to Sophie's before but it was on my short list of places to try in the neighborhood. Â I found it to not live up to my expectations but maybe I just ordered the wrong thing. Â The cuban sandwich was bland and I had to soak it in the green sauce to give it some moisture and some flavor. Â I do loooove empanadas so I will have to give that a try if/when I go back.

My classmate and I came in around 1pm during the weekday for lunch and was seated right away. It is a great place to eat good food and chat near the Columbia campus. (+) I recommend their BURGER. It is super juicy and delicious. The only downside is that near the end however the bottom of my bun was soggy... but who cares the burger was on point! (-) We ordered potato wedges to share as an appetizer but it is small enough for you to eat by yourself. The sauce is great. Overall though it was a great eating experience but will need to come back when I have more money!
Excellent. Why - authentic, fast (once you get a table), and very inexpensive. Two warnings: the place is small, so be prepared to wait, and three stars spicy is extremely spicy!

I've been here a few times now and the food is consistently fantastic. Try the lamb curry - It's fatty but will blow your mind. The sissig is also incredible. Â My only complaint is that the wait is pretty long, even with a reservation. However the staff are really nice and the food more than makes up for the inconvenience.
A great place to walk around and get a plethora of foods. Love the cheeses and watching the pasta be made. Grab a beer at the rooftop beer garden!

Lots of great strengths off the bat: Â quality of food, ambiance, and wine list. Great date spot, very romantic, but also would recommend for groups looking to celebrate something and for old friends just wanting to catch-up over a great meal. Had the squash risotto ravioli to start and then the chicken for 2. If it is your first visit, it's pretty much mandatory to try this chicken. It is true the most delicious bird i've ever had. Served in skillet pan with drippings. Mouthwateringly-good just to think about. Pricetag is high (just warning you), but not uncommonly so for a celebrated chef or for the neighoborhood. Went for my beautiful girlfreind's birthday and will definitely go back.

The amount of options in this place is insane, the price was great! I came here on my lunch break wanting to try something new. I was really impressed overall. The person behind the counter was so friendly and helpful because I had no idea how to order at first and had 5000 questions about what each item was since it is not labeled. For ten bucks I got a HUUUUUGE platter of different vegetables, hummus and a big piece of pita bread. I had enough to last me two days. It was a crazy amount of food and very tasty. I will definitely be coming back here.

We came here specifically for the xiao long bao (soup dumplings) because we heard Joe's had the best ones. Each order gives 8 dumplings; one choice is a mix of crab meat and pork and the other choice was just pork. I thought the pork dumplings had a better flavor to their soup but both were good. There was a decent line when we got there, it was around 8:40 pm on a Saturday night and we waited 30 minutes to get in.

I heard about this bar when it was opening up, read about it, and then saw it in my office elevator in manhattan via the video screen elevator ads... which is completely bizarre... are they stalking me?? Anyway, this place is fantastic. Great bar, awesome prices, cool bartenders... ALL in bushwick! Near the Morgan stop, which is fantastic... I had one of the cocktails (Caulfield's Dream?), and it was great, check this place out. Spacious patio too. 4 stars!

We had never tried hot pot before and this was a great experience! We tried out the tasting menu and I'm glad we did. We were able to taste a little bit of everything and the hot pot was definitely the star. The service was excellent. Our server was the sweetest and cutest lady - as we walked out the door she ran after us to make sure we liked our food and to give each of us a Pez candy from her Pez dispenser. :-) We will definitely be back.
the best lobster roll. ever. hands down.

Took my mother and her best friends here for Mothers day and they loved it. Â No wonder the line is out the door. Â Im allergic to seafood and I was jealous to see them tearing it down...SMH. They are quick with servicing. I would definitely recommend this place!
This place is great. Great food, great drinks, and great service. On a Saturday night they also had great live music. This is up there as one of my favorites in the city now.

I visited NY last week and met someone at Cafe Gitane for drinks, and liked it so much I had to go back on Sunday morning to try their breakfast. Â Loved it: Â Reasonably priced, excellent location, inviting decour, and excellent food.
The lines to this place are unnecessarily long. The vendor down the block has the same food but there are never more than a couple of people on line there. The food is too good, definitely come here.

Went tonight and it is a really cute space. Â Tiny, though. Â I counted about 8 tables. Â Has a really warm feeling (and at first the temperature was a little too warm too.) Â Didn't have a rezzie, so we sat at the bar (which I like to do anyways.) As far as being original with the ordering - we weren't. Â We ordered the sliders, the gnocchi, the pork chop and the crispy chicken. I guess on the way we were ordering-- (come on, food is always more fun if you share!) the bartendress / waitress asked us if everything we were eating was to be shared, to which we said 'yep.' Well, what a pleasant surprise when everything was served pre-divvied up! Â  Now onto the food. Â  The gnocchi was light and the braised lamb was that Â falling apart tender you get from braised meat and Â very flavorful - my friend who isn't a huge fan of gnocchi really enjoyed this. Â  The meatball sliders were juicy (a little messy, so be careful if you're wearing white!) -- and I have to say the appetizer portion comes with 3 sliders which is a pretty generous serving (which is a GOOOOOOD thing.) Â I would say you could easily have that for your meal. Â The tomato sauce was lighty tangy and yummy, the bread what I would consider a brioche type roll went well with the meatball type burger - I think I would go back just for these...but the gnocchi was pretty yummy too. The pork chop was a little disappointing - a little on the dry side for me - but I don't want to give the impression it wasn't good, it just wasn't sublime...the accompanying greens and beans were really flavorful and a very good accompaniment to the pork. The crispy chicken was really great. Â The skin was crispy and flavorful, the meat was tender and juicy - and the sauce went well with the brussel sprouts and the chicken. Â  A bite of all the different items together on the plate was delicious. We didn't try any desserts - because we walked by Grom and I had mentioned I wanted to go there - but from what others had said, I wasn't really all that motivated to try the desserts. The service was friendly, efficient -- oh, they had Olivia Newton John playing (which made me happy) and when I saw the guys in the kitchen dancing, that made me giggle...If I could've joined them, I would've! The alcohol is primarily wine - but they do have a few cocktails and a small selection of beers. The food with 3 glasses of wine came to $65/person.
Better than regular sushi, if you're a vegan, vegetarian, or just a food lover this is definitely a place to check out!

So I came here because I had heard pretty good things. I am giving it three stars because the service was great, as where I may have only given the food two and a half stars. The drinks were good, I had Nina's Knight which I would suggest. The pretzel and beer cheese dip didn't really impress me. A personal preference maybe but I did not like that the cheese dip was cold and I couldn't just dip my pretzel into it. The cheese sauce also didn't wow me flavor wise. They offered bread and butter before the entree arrived, and it was a cold roll, couldn't really eat it. I ordered the shrimp and grits as an entree. Hmm. My family is from Alabama, and I have had a lot of shrimp and grits in my lifetime and I just couldn't get on board. It was Â decent, but I've definitely had much better. I also ordered the $18 entree size, and it was sufficient. Can't speak for their desserts, but they did drop off a ginger cookie with the bill. Cute touch. Service was great though, the waitress was attentive and very friendly.

I have to say, after not being willing to wait 2 hours at Clinton St, me and my friends came here, and were pleasantly delighted for brunch. We all ordered something a little different, from steak and eggs, to baked eggs, oatmeal, etc. Â We each enjoyed what we ordered Â I got the creamed spinach, onion, fresh tomato baked eggs with potatoes and toast. Â One egg was overdone, but it didn't ruin the meal, everything was fresh and well put together. Â I wanted more, even though I was full. Â The potatoes are more baked then home fries (if you care). Tried the oatmeal, and it was pretty good, needed a little more cinnamon and/or syrup. Â  Overall, I will come back here though.

Do I have to tell you how good this place is???!!?!? Â The 5 stars should say it all!!! Â  I'm salivating just thinking about it!!!! Â Chicken & lamb platter extra hot sauce& white sauce ..... GET IN MY BELLAY!!!!!!!!

Dear Cafeteria, Thanks for always being open late at night after the bars close. Â Thanks for being moderately priced, yet deliciously trendy, however prefabricated. Â Thanks for being the old standby when friends visit from out of town and I want to shock them a bit with Chelsea pinash. Â Thanks for introducing me to quinoa... No thanks for the high drink prices however.. you can keep those. Â But definitely thanks for all that good other stuff.

It was a rainy day in Astoria and I couldn't pick a spot with my friend. Then she suggested we go to Broadway for this place.. I was like fine. The decor inside is dim just how I like it! We ordered a crab sandwich and quesadillas. They were delicious even though it took a while, probably because it was cooked to perfection! Will definitely come back to try more items. BTW the busboy was amazingly consistent with his service.

We went in to experience the burger and we were not at all disappointed. One of our new favorite NYC burgers and restaurants. The service was excellent. Food was interesting and delicious. The ingredients were fresh and top-notch. The space is absolutely adorable. I can't wait to go back!

I work in the neighborhood and was with my girlfriend who likes crepes so we decided to check the place out. I ordered a crepe and specified that i didn't want one ingredient that was listed in the menu. When it was brought to me it was packed with this ingredient. When I mentioned to the server that I did asked for no X on my crepe, her response was, "you didnt say that!" I chalked it up to language barrier as she had a heavy accent (russian?), and insisted that I was very specific. She replaced it and the food was ok. She also constantly argued loudly with the kitchen staff in the middle of the dining room, about drink glasses and other assorted subjects. Overall it didnt seem like she wanted to be there, sat outside on the steps the whole time, and we had to be seated by the cook because she didn't come inside when she saw us walk past her to enter the restaurant. Maybe it's just because it was a sunday that they werent on their A game, but the experience left a lot to be desired.

One thing I miss from when i lived in NYC is the diner breakfast. Â A simple thing that you would think could be found everywhere---well it's not folks, so consider yourselves lucky if you are able to eat a yummy breakfast on the quick for around 5 bucks! Â We were staying at the ACE Hotel and if you want to eat at the hotel, you are looking at 20 bucks at least Â Even a coffee in the pretentious Stumptown Coffee will set you back 5 bucks. Â Walk a few blocks. Â You won't be disappointed! Â  I had the 2 egg breakfast with turkey bacon, potatoes, ww toast, coffee. Â Perfection. Â  Glad I found this place--thanks Yelpers!
Great ramen (add a couple of toppings!); loved their sashimi too. Friendly staff. Not crowded. I definitely recommend it.

Fantastic. We had the opportunity to sit up at the bar over the kitchen and the chefs were quick and definitely had it together. The food was amazing! We went there for brunch on a Sunday. Only had a short wait (it is a small spot) but of course worth it! This place is cash only and good prices. I look forward to coming back!

Went to Salt and Fat for my birthday with my wife. The menu is made for sharing. We decided to share five dishes and each was better than the last. The scallops were a perfect opening dish. They were excellently cooked. The pork trotter was excellent, with the egg it was rich and unctuous. The favorites of the night were the bacon popcorn amuse that was sent to the table and the oxtail terrine we ordered. The popcorn was a nice surprise and got our appetites ready for such a wonderful meal. The oxtail was not at all what I expected. It was presented so creatively and it was truly the most well thought out part of the meal. This was one of the best meals I've ever had, and a perfect meal for a chef. My wife chose an excellent spot for my birthday dinner. I recommend it very highly.

My friends and I stumbled upon this restaurant while looking for good oyster deals -- and this place has a great one! It's the one that everyone is raving about: Red, White, and Blue -- 6 oysters and a glass of red wine or white wine or a PBR all for $8! Super cheap, and what a great deal. The first time I came here I ordered the Down East Lobster Feast (usually Market Price, but I got mine for $28). The feast includes a 1 1/4 lbs Maine Lobster, steamers, corn on the cob, and fries. It's a really filling meal, but it's nothing too special. The second time I came here I ordered Scallops Dave's Way ($23), and it was also nothing special. The scallops were so small and there was so much spinach on my plate -- maybe to make up for the lack of scallops love? I loved Fish the first time I came here, but after eating at other seafood restaurants in Queens, I can never go back to paying more so I can look cute but eat less in Manhattan. I ordered the New England Clam Chowder the second time I came here, and it was so soupy. Am I crazy, or is the chowder supposed to be creamy? Maybe it's because I was raised in NYC and have no idea what real chowder is supposed to taste like? Anyways, it was soupy and filled with so many onions -- which on a regular basis I love, but the amount of these onions was overwhelming. The restaurant is so -- tight. It really is. The first time I came with my friends, the table we had was very spacious. But the second time -- we were at a table that was connected to another table -- because there was no room to separate the tables. And we were right next to the kitchen, so we almost knocked over every waiter and waitress coming in and out! So yeah, it's really cramped. I've said a lot of negative things about this restaurant which isn't what I intended for it to sound like, but again, after eating seafood in Queens, where I don't have to fight off as many people (except for Taverna), it's hard to go back to city seafood eating. ...but then again, I'm always up for a food challenge. Cailin's Suggestion: - Lobster Cobb Salad ($24) - my friend ordered this, and I couldn't help but eat almost half of her plate!! Super, super good. The lobster and the shrimp were so fresh!

OMG. They definitely lived up to the hype! I'm literally about to fall asleep standing right now, because I'm SO full! I tried the pork buns bcuz (my fellow yelpers) told me to.. n they were deelishhhhhh! I think it was pork belly inside. Which made them sooo scrumptious! Â  (i honestly dont know about $10 for two measly buns... but hot dam.. they were good!) I ordered the spicy miso ramen.Being the fatass that I am, I added the braised pork (because the menu told me to...lol). Bad idea. The pork buns were enough pork fat; I definitely had a pork fat overload.. -_- (and on top of that.. the braised pork belly added to the ramen wasn't alll super tender.. so it kinda sucked..) *do note: the amount of meat that is alrdy included with ur ramen is really scarce.. I think it was like 1 1/2 pcs ... Either way. Buns and brothhh were super savory... and the service was Â  also great! loved it! :)

People don't come here just for the fries, if that's what you're thinking (though the fries are pretty damn good). Â It's all about the sauces! Â I've had a ton of sauces from here, and I'd say my favorite is the wasabi one! Prepare yourself for a long line!
Best bar on the Upper West Side!! Has amazing ciders and beers and great good! Really fun pickle arrangements. I would highly recommend it!! Had a great time!
Fried Chicken!!!

AHHHHHHHHHHHHH! PITA!!!!!!!!! AHHHHHHHH!!!!!! Here is what you should do. Order like 10 pitas from bedouin tent and eat them, with nothing else or nothing on them. Jesus christ, this is the best pita ever. it comes straight out of the oven like a pizza. GODDAMN IT!!!!! All the food is good so put something on/in that pita. But goddamn it if it doesn't remain the main event. Fuck. I want one so bad right now.....

If you're looking for simple, comfort food, definitely check out Le Jardin Bistro for a two thumbs up cozy experience. I stopped by with a friend, after seeing once while walking around the area, and was glad that we decided to try it. Â The upstairs is a small enclosed candle-lit sun room type area, with vines growing up, that give the restaurant it's name. Â We arrived just in time for happy hour (I'd guess it goes until 7PM) for $5 cocktails! Â Probably the best prices I've ever seen in NYC. Â The cocktails aren't very strong, but my St. Germain based drink was the perfect aperitif. I ordered the bouillabaisse ($22) which had a thick tomato based, with white fish and a generous helping of clams, other bi-valves, and shrimp. Â The bouillabaisse was delicious and the portions are so filling that I ended up taking almost half home. Â The bread for the bread basket was delightfully chewy on the inside with a slight crunch to the crust, sliced in thick slices--perfect for scooping up stew. Â My friend ordered the cassoulet ($20) Â which she said was also quite good. One star knocked off for quite clumsy service. Â Although the service was normal, there were multiple glass shatterings while we were there, and it seemed like the place was still ironing out the kinks. Le Jardin Bistro is perfect for a relaxed date, or a casual dinner with friends. Â I'll definitely be back again!

I thought the food was good but not amazing. I had the Minetta burger, it was a little it salty but the taste was good. Fries were delicious. I went for a late lunch, place was not that busy, which I liked. Service was great. I wanna go back and try other dishes.

Love this new place from the owner of Taim in the west village. Â Best dishes - shrimp, soup and lamb. Â My favourite lamb dish ever! Â The chocolate-chili sangria was very good. Â I also like the design of the this new restaurant -- very fun (and don't forget to check out the restroom).

The food comes out quick, but wont break the bank. what surprised me was that the tonkatsu was ACTUALLY crispy (not grease-heavy, or soggy). The eggs were overcooked but I was so busy scarfing this combo of chicken, pork, and rice(closer to the Korean, sticky kind, not the chinese kind) down that I didn't really care I would certainly like to bring people here and I dare say I'd come here once in a while to quell the cravings

I must admit I have a soft spot for delicious, juicy burgers, and the burger at this place def. hit the spot. It was cooked to perfection and was extremely juicy and tender. Another way to tell the burger was amazing is that almost every person at the restaurant ordered one. Besides having a great burger this is a cool place to grab drinks and catch up with friends. They have good beer and the appetizers are also delicious and worth having - especially the Sheep's Milk Ricotta Gnudi with Basil Pesto (YUM!!!).

There are a couple of different halal carts on 53rd and 6th, but make sure you go to the right one!! Â The famed 53rd and 6th Halal Cart is on the corner diagonal from the Hilton, with the yellow plastic bags. Â  One time, I mistakenly went to one on a different corner, and was left with chicken that wasn't flavored as well, and not as finely chopped/minced/hacked at, and was sadly left a bit disappointed. Â I initially thought that I had over-hyped the chicken and rice plate in my head, but realized later it just wasn't as good because I went to the wrong cart. I always order the chicken and rice, and mix in a bunch of white sauce with the rice, chicken, and lettuce together. Â The red sauce is SUPER spicy, so I just dip the tip of my fork in for each bite. For 6 bucks, you really can't beat the chicken and rice. Love! Â I just wish it wasn't so far...I would be there every other day if it was further downtown.

Of course I came here for the cheesecake. I grabbed a seat at the bar and order up a slice. Someone sitting next to me had ordered a cup of the French onion soup, which looked delicious, so I ordered one of those as well. I had pretty high expectations, but was let down. The cheesecake was really dry and the soup didn't have much flavor. Just as other reviewers mentioned... It's a tourist trap.

After seeing the reviews, I was expecting to not be disappointed. But maybe my expectations were too high? For this to be in Macy's, everything was excellent. If it were in its own little place out on the streets, I'm not so sure. I had the rotisserie chicken with escarole and crispy asparagus. The escarole was amazing... The chicken was average... The asparagus was burnt. My mom had the sea bass which she said was average. I tasted it and I would say it was dry. For what you pay here, the food should be better. Service was good, but nothing to write home about. We definitely won't be going back. The only reason I'm giving them 2 stars is for the brussel sprout/ cauliflower app... A. Maz. Ing.

Let me preface this by saying that this review is really more like a 4.5 My friend and I came here to catch after our original plans for eating at Ippudo were squashed by the almost 2 hour wait. I'm glad we ended up coming here though. Overall the food was really good and the atmosphere lively, but not too loud (for me at least). Over the course of our dinner we had the fried oysters (a special for the evening), market veggies (bok choy in oyster sauce), khao soi (a tiny bit too salty for my liking, but overall really good), and a side of rice. Everything was tasty. As there was a long wait time between the oysters and khao soi, they even bought out a place plate of curried cod, which also tasted great. I can't wait to come back and try the chickpeas, pickled cabbage, and fried fish (whole fish in a stew like broth). Positive note: They are very willing to adapt menu items per dietary restrictions. Although we ended up ordering the special instead, I indicated that I really wanted to try the mussels, but that I don't eat any red meat (the mussels are cooked with a pork sausage). They said that they had no problems cooking the dish without the sausage, should I want to have it the next time I come in. My only real 2 critiques would be the description of the size of the dishes and the minimal dessert options (I really love dessert). There is a huge disparity between what qualified as a snack, small dish, or large dish. Some small dishes seemed like snacks, while others were more like large dishes rather than small. Not a huge issue, but confusing when going there for the first time. As for the dessert options, there are only 2. One of which is halo-halo (awesome). Can't remember the other. While not bad, I think one more option would be perfect. Overall though, I came. I ate. I left happy. (and plan to return soon)

I sincerely hope Master Yasuda forgives my wifey. She has shamed me and my family name. If this were feudal Japan, I'd probably have to commit seppuku with my sharpest chef's knife... Â You'll read about how each species of fish is specifically cut to maximize it's enjoyment and about how the Master will fabricate sushi to appropriately fit the size of each diner's mouth.... fanatical stuff. Read the website, and you'll begin to understand how Sushi Yasuda is a place that worships all that is pure and glorious about fish. In this context, my night of horror blossomed... Wifey and I decided to go out for a fun dinner. Â We step into the austere and peaceful space that is Sushi Yasuda. Â Staff are gracious and very accomodating. Â Everything is set for a lovely night. Atrocity #1: Server: Â "We can have the omakase dinner include half sashimi and half sushi. Â Is there anything someone here cannot eat?" Wifey: Â "Well, I can't eat lamb..." Me: Â (turning bright red and trying to hide under the table) Atrocity #2 (midway into our meal): Server: Â "Is there anything else you would like?" Wifey: Â "Do you have a spider roll?" Me: Â (dying of shame) Atrocity #3 (at the end of our meal) Server: Â "How was your meal?" Wifey: Â "That wasn't enough sushi. Â I'm not full yet... I think I'll have some abalone and sea scallop." Me: Â "You're gonna stuff yourself with abalone!?!?!? Ounce for ounce, one of the most expensive items in the ocean!! Â For the love of god, please shoot me now! The meal was phenomenal. Â But my palate is just not sensitive enough to discern "amazingly fresh" sushi from "pretty fresh" sushi. Â Besides, we're probably on Master Yasuda's shit-list for the crap that wifey pulled in his restaurant. Â I wouldn't be surprised if he doesn't let us in the door again.

Now, I'm not Jewish - but rumor has it that "Traif" is the word for everything NOT kosher in hebrew. Â Boy is that name SPOT FREAKING ON! I had the group menu as I was there for a birthday (the birthdayee also reviewed her dinner on yelp and gave it 4 stars). Â Some of the highlights? BACON DONUTS! Bacon cocktails, and everything to do with pork. Â I might not have known everything that went into my mouth by name, but holy cow, it was all amazingly delicious. Â They were friendly to our large group, the service was great, and the food was amazing. Truly a trifecta of awesomeness - only not given 5 stars as I feel I need to eat off the regular menu before giving it that ranking...
I love asian food. The chicken sandwich which are proposed in this reestaurant is exactly that I like and that I want. Very good

Went here on date night with my boyfriend and we both loved it. Â The atmosphere is very quaint and warm. Â I had the falafel plate and the bf had the lamb plate. Â We'll definitely be coming back....
great thai food at an affordable price. service is very quick.

I went to Calle Ocho for a weekend brunch. Â They have an unlimited sangria bar that I did not take advantage of, but my friends sure liked it. Â I remember my food to be okay, and not anything amazing.

The people who work here are really mean. Â Even the busboys. I once overheard a conversation between the bartender and a patron that went like this: Patron (scanning the drinks menu on the wall behind the bar): Do you have any drinks specials? Bartender: If these prices aren't cheap enough for you, maybe you should go someplace else. I think they try to play up the rudeness. Â Either that, or these people are just mean. Â Once, the waiter brought a plate of fries to our table. Â Rather than inquire as to who had ordered it, when I asked aloud who had asked for fries, the waiter just threw the plate on the table and walked away with a disgusted sneer. I once came here with somebody, and we argued the entire time. Â We enjoyed our burgers, but the argumentativeness of the experience made me depressed. Come for the burgers. Â Don't come for good service, friendly people, a nice atmosphere or bathrooms that don't look like locations from the movie Seven. I've never understood why people in New York put up with things like this. Â We pride ourselves on being sophisticated and much more savvy than our suburban and urban counterparts, but we wait on endless lines, put up with meanness and accept questionably clean bathrooms. Still, I'm going to Corner Bistro next week.

I came here with my bf and had the omakase. Â We spent about $200 here. Â The service was great. Â The fish were very fresh and had an array of choices. Â I must say that it was hard to taste the white fish especially when its cut paper thin. Â The eel is definately the best I had ever had and I have tried a number of sushi places. Â The waiter told me the chef actually grills his own eel!

The food was great, service great, staff was great (and cute). Unfortunately the chairs at the bar - not so comfortable! The whole experience (especially the house cava) was definitely reminiscent of sitting in a cafe in Barcelona. Great concept, great menu, worthy of expansion... :)

Imagine being in a busy street in Korea. People buzz all around and the autumn chill persuades you to enter one of the local food shops in the alley way. If homecooked comfort food is what you crave, this always-busy self-serve deli answers the call. I've never been to Korea, though this is what I'd imagine the place would be full of, no-frills store fronts, Grandma Kim's in the back stirring large pots of rice and soups. Woorijip is Korean food, tasty and simple. You basically grab a tray, grab the food you want, pay up and slide yourself into an open table to enjoy. The buffet food is priced at $5.50/lb and the prepared boxes are about $6 each. There's a microwave if you want to reheat something. Lunch or dinner, Woorijip is a great low-key option. Food without all the fanfare. Satisfying and wallet-friendly. Just do Grandma Kim a favor and clean up your table before leaving, m'kay?

Very disappointed. I spent over $100 for breakfast this morning. Besides the waiter being too preoccupied with hugging the other staff and flirting with the customers at the bar, 2 dishes of eggs were sour, the granola was salty, poached eggs were so full of vinegar they could have passed for pickled And the ketchup tasted like chemicals. Â  The French toast was soggy and undercooked and the bacon was burnt,black. I am a repeat customer, bringing in 3 New potentials and they were all unsatisfied. I couldn't find enough words to apologize to my friends. Not coming back.

I'm currently sitting in Ba Xuyen writing this long overdue update, after inhaling yet another phenomenal banh mi. I LOVE THIS PLACE. I've been back at least once or twice a week since I first discovered it two months ago. Each banh mi has been consistently incredible. Â PERFECTLY toasty bread and each overfilling with protein, whichever you decide. I've tried the classic pork, grilled pork, grilled chicken and meatball -- incredible, x4. Oh, the iced coffee is great too. Excellent and quick service. The ladies are super pleasant. Did I mention that I love this place? I love this place (I love this place(I love this place.)) No place compares. Â Also, I love this place. And now, the sweaty uphill trek back to work!

Review is for lunch. Fresh Salt is off the charts good. Sandwiches and salads are phenomenal. Very quaint atmosphere with a southern twist. Easy to get in and out for a quick lunch. Cost was very reasonable. Would definitely visit again when in NY.

Fried Chicken & Waffles, please!!! I'm an LA girl, so of course I can't help but to compare this place with Roscoe's. I'm going to admit, I liked this place. A LOT. I couldn't stop smiling when I got my plate of Al Sharpton. The chicken was extra crispy on the outside but very juicy and tender on the inside. The waffle was thick & fluffy, just the way I like it. The cornbread was to die for, I asked for seconds. I just couldn't stop smiling. I just couldn't.

I came here with my friend for a belated birthday celebration (for me). Â This is another hole in the wall spot but adorable nonetheless. Â Not too fancy, not too dark, but it's just right. Â The staff was extremely courteous and helpful; Â We were assisted with wine selection, meal of the day, as well as dessert. Â Our waiter saw that she gave me a birthday card and served my dessert with a candle! I thought that was super cool and thoughtful. Best for couples, dates, or besties to relax, chill, and eat pretty authentic french food. Would I go back, most definitely.

The meal was great. We went for out second time on valentines day and it was the perfect decision. The staff is absolutely great and very knowledgable. Everything was cooked to perfection and the staff was able to recommend the perfect wine to complement the meal. Remember you must get desert! ...the banana creme brÃ»lÃ©e is amazing. Prices were a little high but you do get large portions of great food ... Not to mention you are in the village. Bon appetite!

This is definitely a Bistro Petit, very tiny so not good for big groups, and if you are coming for a date definitely try to make a reservation so you aren't waiting around too long for a table. Also its CASH only, so be prepared! We waited about twenty minutes, but the staff was really nice and eventually set out some tables outside so we could sit, which isn't bad but then again in the winter its definitely not ideal. Now down to the good stuff: Appetizer: Truffle Mac & Cheese PROS: We had heard so much about it, we had to try it. It was quite delicious, it was creamy and had that truffle savor in every single bite. If you're a big eater, you should get two since it really isnt that big of a portion. CONS: the only con was that it is such a small portion ENTRE: I ordered the Lobster roll PROS: The green apple in the Lobster roll was quite a nice touch, the bread was nice and warm and tasted buttery as well. The julienne fries were nice and crispy as well. CONS: There really wasnt much lobster in the roll, or much of anything to be honest. Although it was good, I couldnt taste the lobster as the apple over-powered any other flavor. Also I had like 80% bread and only 15% apple and 5% lobster. HE got: the Kimchee Bouillabaisse PROS: Definitely a better portion size, and he said it was a nice kimchee flavor. Had a variety of seafood and was very tasty. CONS: He didn't really have any, said it was delicious, however, for $21 he said the portion could have been a bit more generous. But maybe you're paying for the signature dish,not so much the amount of food. Perhaps if I had eaten something different my experience could have been different. Although the food was good, I don't know necessarily if I would go back. I went there, I tried it, and that's good enough for me.

After two peopl reccomended this new-ish spot I finally found the time to go. YUM! Delicious Greek food that you don't find other places. It's not all spanikopita and pitas. The octopus was wonderful as was the orzo entree...and the shrimp. The Soudzokakia (think meatballs) appetizer was decent as well, but I'm partial to my own recipe for this dish. They also have a full bar with many Greek wines, a few (non-greek) beers on tap too. There should be nothing holding you back from trying this place! Go! I mean, now, call them and book a table because they fill up fast.

We came here after reading a recommendation from timeout new York. It was kind of a shock that our meal starts with fried chicken skin! It was nicely done, but I'm honestly not a chicken skin fan. We like the smelt appetizer, but the sisig (what we went there for) was somewhat disappointing. It was a nice pork dish, but the best part of it was the garlic rice, which was amazing.

The best halal food in the city hands down. The meat is good. The pita is good. The sauce is good. Everything that comes in that tin platter is amazing. The line may be long at times. But they just opened shop by my job which makes things a lot easier for me. Especially when I'm craving their delicious food!

Had the catfish with collard greens and okra. Â Catfish was lightly breaded but I thought it would've tasted better with a thicker, crunchier coat. Â It was moist and remained flaky-- great with a squeeze of lime and hot sauce. Â Disappointed that they served run of the mill Frank's red hot.... Â  I'm a vegetable fan so I was okay with the blandness of the okra because I was craving the sliminess of it-- yum!! Â Collard greens were amazing; tender with the right amount of salt. Â  Also tried the chicken and waffles-- chicken was too dry and the batter was just okay. Â Didn't get to try the waffle though but am disappointed looking at all these yelp pictures. Their chicken wings were great though-- crispy and succulent. Â Perfect to gnaw on and get all the bits of batter and chicken clean off the bone. Sweet tea tasted kind of syrupy-- had to wait for the ice to melt to tone it down. Â  The service was great-- our waitress was friendly and brought the extras we asked for. Â Service is kind of slow but not excruciating. Â AND, the wait wasn't that bad for a Saturday morning! Â We were about 5th in line and it took only about 15 minutes. Â My lucky day!
Loved the brunch here. Â Went with a party of four and everyone was incredibly happy with their food. Â Highly recommended.

This place is legitimately a hole in the wall. Â I brought my Chinese mother here the last time she came to visit and I could tell that even she was a little wary. Â But as soon as they brought out a plate of their dumplings we knew we were at the right place. Â The dumplings had perfectly thin skins and juicy fillings. Â They were far better than the ones we had earlier that day at Vanessa's Dumplings (which has totally gone downhill as far as I am concerned). Â Their hand-pulled noodles are quite tasty as well, although I'm not sure that they were the best I have ever tasted (or even the best in NYC). Â And like most of the hand-pulled noodle places down in Chinatown, you can eat pretty well for almost nothing.

I love this place!! Â My bf and I discovered it when trying to go to Takashi, nearby. Â The first time that we went, we were only able to score seats at the bar, but it was one of the best dining experiences I've had. Â The bartender was super attentive and gave us great recommendations for food and drinks. Â We had the pork chop, orecchiette and risotto. Â The pork chop was extremely juicy and tender. Â I crave it often and sad that I don't live in NYC to get it more often. Â  The second time we were there, I made reservations for 6 for my bf's birthday. Â We ordered a cheese plate, roasted chicken, pork chop, brussel sprouts and roasted mushrooms. Â I loved the roasted mushrooms and brussel sprouts. Â There hasn't been anything here that I haven't loved thus far. Â I can't wait to go back to NYC next time to try more items on the menu.

Perfect place to take my wife for her birthday. If you like meat - take the cote de boeuf. If you don't like meat - take the cote de boeuf. You'll like meat afterwards. Sat in the front room and Leslie was a star. Glasses never got close to empty and answers came before the questions.

Been to this place a bunch of times...Living in Ditmas Park, it's real real nice not to have to go into the slope for some real good beer and a chill atmosphere. However, this place does have some flaws that could prove to be fatal if not addressed....First, the service is godawful. Each time I've gone and ordered a drink from the bartender, something inside me always goes, "man, what a d*%k." They always act like they're doing you the favor of a lifetime by pouring you a 6 dollar beer. Second, Although the food is pretty good, semi-gourmet Â and salty, at any given night, there are only like two or three things off the menu that they actually have in stock. Its like going to six flags when both Nitro and Kingda Ka are broken down. That being said...the burger is dank. On the whole, I will keep going for the draft selection and matchstick fries, especially when I don't want to go far from home. Beware...peak hours it gets pretty packed and you'll have to stand around awkwardly for an hour or so.

Disappointment: they were out of brisket AND the first two beers I tried to order last night (a Saturday evening). Huge bummer that we traveled an hour to Gowanus for brisket, only to discover that there wasn't any! I normally really like Dino BBQ, but the shrimp I had (in lieu of brisket) last night was also pretty bad. Cold and mealy and tasted unfresh. Additionally, my combo plate was missing cornbread, which I had to ask for separately. On the positive side, our waitress was great - really friendly and accommodating.

I'll start by saying I've been to Â Enoteca Maria on two previous occasions and both times were enjoyable. Below is what my wife and I encountered on a recent visit for or 8:15 reservation before we uncomfortably left and ate at Beso around the corner. Waitperson: Joe, an 8:15 reservation is here and we don't have a table available. Joe: well, THEN YOU FIND THEM A TABLE. Classy!

Been here quite a few times for brunch, lunch and dinner. Â What a cool place! Â Can be VERY hard to get a table sometimes (I don't think they take reservations, or if they do, they don't keep them) so get ready to wait. Â Cool bar to grab a drink at while you're waiting, though. The brunch is DELICIOUS. Â Something about the way they prepare eggs makes them tasty as anything! Â Reasonably priced, too. Fried Chicken. Â Fried Chicken. Â Oh my GOD do I love their fried chicken and waffles. Â It comes with a "Maple Jus" (get over yourselves) that's surprisingly tasty (I'm not a sweet fan). Â My friends RAVE about the mac and cheese, too. Â Again, prices are pretty good and portion size is good as well. Overall a great place to check out if you're in the area, for sure! Note: Â I think these guys are open 24 hours so might be a good late-night spot to check out!

For Yale's inaugural Fall Break, I took advantage of the heavily subsidized NYC trip. I take my meals out very seriously, so before I venture into a new food locale, I research area restaurants. Since I had been craving some good Chinese food, I decided on the promising Golden Fried Dumplings in Brooklyn. Two blocks from the Metrotech subway station, this literal hole-in-the-wall was easy to access. I went with two friends, and our jaws dropped when we saw the ever-growing line forming inside the tiny restaurant. However, one glance at the menu and the prices (as well as the mostly Asian clientele) convinced us to get in line. We ordered four items each, and after staking out one of the scarce tables, our numbers were quickly called out and we dove into our food. Bear in mind that we entered this knowing we wouldn't finish everything, and we would have a food coma. I ordered boiled chive and pork dumplings (10 for $3!), roast pork pan fried buns (3 for $1), sesame pancake with vegetables ($1.50) and noodles with meat and bean sauce ($3). All foods from my tasty childhood. Everything boasted a heavenly addition of oil, except for the boiled dumplings--however; even they don't get the healthy food label because of the fatty pork filling. But I wasn't looking for something healthy, I was looking for something that would soothe my tummy, which had been craving Chinese food, no matter how greasy. My friends ordered a variation of what I ordered, but with fried chive and pork dumplings, sesame pancake with egg, noodles with spicy sauce and shredded chicken chow mein instead. What can I say, they're American. Next time you're in NYC, this place is worth the trek out to Brooklyn. Skip the sesame pancake sandwiches, which were too thick for the filling of cilantro, carrot and cucumber. The noodles, while good, also weren't up to par with the handmade dumplings and buns. A definite "Don't Miss", stick to what Golden Fried Dumplings are good at, and neither your wallet nor your taste buds will be disappointed. You can always exercise tomorrow.

A great BBQ Joint. It was loud. Service (at the counter) was slow. But the meats were wonderful. We hung around for about two and a half hours drinking beer and eating some great BBQ. Definitely stake out a table while someone gets food. Our group of 6 waited about 30 minutes to get seats. We ordered about three and a half pounds of meat with 3 large sides for six people and it wasn't a ton of food. So plan on getting a little more meat depending on how hungry you are. Also skip the rolls they are store brought. Ribs were fall off the bone tender but could have more meat on them. Links were good and so were the boneless beef ribs. The best meat was the brisket, so thick and tender! Oh pork belly was awesome; the fat was so rich and delicious. It's artery clogging good.

Love this place. Â Order from Sanfords with my gf off seamless all the time. Â The burgers and sweet potato fries are amazing. Â Pretty much anything we've ordered we've loved. Â I have not even been in the restaurant and probably never will be but I walk past it everyday and it looks very nice. The one negative about the place is it takes a while for them to deliver but it's always worth the wait!
Best vegan bakery ever!!!

Probably the most authentic Japanese restaurant option... around that area. Â They have choices beyond chicken teriyaki and california rolls. Â The appetizers and small plates stood out the most. Â We got a tripe dish that was simple and clean. Â And even though chicken teriyaki might sound typical, the set menu comes with traditional Japanese root vegetables and pickled vegetables. Â Husband thought his sushi set was fine, but has had better elsewhere. Â Service could be better. Â We went at an earlier hour for dinner... felt like the whole wait staff was just staring at us while we ate!

Well, now I'm really glad I moved to the UWS because that just means I get to be close to Jacob's Pickles. My boyfriend came upon this place and since he's a big big big fan of southern food, we had to try it. Skimming the menu I happened upon their Bloody BLT. BACON. BACON. BACON. BACON IN BLOODY MARY. Whoever thought of this idea is GENIUS. Not only was the drink beautiful to look at but so extraordinarily refreshing. Next, to no one's surprise I ordered the Southern BLT. BACON BACON BACON AGAIN. The portions were HUGE and I mean HUGE, like you could eat it also for dinner... maybe even again for breakfast the next day. But most importantly, it was also delicious and I enjoyed the fried green tomato in it-- really brought the dish together.

I'm writing a review of this place because it's might be my favorite place in the five boroughs that I've gotten to go to when you consider the whole package: It's cheap ($5-$10). It's fast (~5-10 minutes). It's reasonably healthy. It is, absolutely, other-worldly delicious. I really can't say more than this. This place fucking rules. I'd give it six stars if I could. The most I can do is denigrate the other falafel places. I'm insulted that Mamoun's shares a 4.5 rating with Taim. That's just fucking farcical, really.

Great food , presentation and menu. Chicken was outstanding and flavors spoke to the same flavors you find on the chicken in the markets of Israel. The pita and hummus outstanding . Eggplant kicked ass. I expect to become a regular here... Great dinning , A real treat if you like middle eastern food or a vegan.

This review is for brunch only. The ambiance of this bistro is lovely and with the door closed, you can almost imagine being in Paris. It's a good sign when the French are a big part of the clientele. Sadly the food didn't live up to it's surroundings. My omelette and my bf's frittata were on the bland side, but the frites and salad were delish. Perhaps dinner here is the way to go.

I had my husbands surprise 65th birthday party there last night in the party room downstairs. From the moment we started planning the party and even during when I misplaced my purse and the manger Viviana helped me locate where I left it by watching the video,she was exceptional. (I left it in the back of the room lol) We were 30 people and what should have lasted only 2/12 hours went on closer to four with all the fun we were having eating drinking and dancing. The waiter service was exceptional and so was our bartender. The food was delicious and they even put a happy birthday at the top of the menu. Â  I can't say enough great things about the restaurant Â ambiance food music staff and attention to detail. Thank you all for making my husbands birthday so special and really easy to plan!

Any establishment with indie music playing and a presence of 20 something's is going to get hate on Yelp. Apparently hipster attire and tattoos automatically means one is "trying to hard." Personally, I think Skytown tries just enough. Walking in, the first thing I noticed is a humble- looking wood paneled LaMarzocco espresso machine. I forget the roaster name, but my snooty-tooty barista/roaster/espresso freak friend nodded in approval. Good coffee, check. Scanning the bar I eye some pretty appealing drink specials and home- made ginger ale (or was it ginger beer? What's the difference?). I had a sip of my friend's cocktail, and though I don't remember what it was, I wasn't disappointed. Another check. The menu is modest, but well put together. Selections rotate on what I assume to be a seasonal basis. I've tried the skyburger (veggie or turkey), mushroom sand which, bacon sandwhich, spare ribs, some dumpling soup, egg sandwhich, an omelette, zucchini bread french toast, and a couple salads. Everything I've had was perfectly portioned, presented nicely, and delicious. Tasty grub, check. The seating area is spacious and casual; an awesome spot for a meal or just to hunker down and get some reading/writing/drawing/watching cat videos on YouTube-ing in. The music varies on who's working, sometimes it's not the vibe I'm in the mood for (c'est la vie) but usually on point. I haven't seen any of these "annoying, trying too hard" clientele some of the haters mention. Atmosphere, check. The staff is friendly and down to earth- not over-the-top fake nice. People are people and if you engage in conversation your kindness and humor will be reciprocated. But don't be shocked when your "EW OMIGOD HIPSTERS" scowl is greeted with a flat affect. You get what you give- bartenders aren't robots. I've had some great laughs here. Good service, check. Now, there are two slight pitfalls I gotta point out: 1. You will walk out smelling like a kitchen. Embrace it. It's a reminder of the awesome meal you just had. 2. My experiences with pick- up orders are a little ehhh; every time something was off, whether it be they forgot the topping on my burger or sandwhich (I was never charged for it though) or my bag was missing cutlery. The overall taste wasn't affected, but this is an area that could use improvement. All in all, Skytown is a winner in my book. I would encourage anyone to check it out day and night because there are different vibes depending on the time of day. And leave your judgey 'tude out on broadway.
Great place, wonderful ramen, lovely ambience, short wait. GO!

I came here to meet up with some friends for dinner. We caught the last 30 minutes of happy hour on a Wednesday so the place was buzzing, but not overly crowded. After I sat down I noticed right away how dark it was because I had to use the backlight on my phone just to read the menu (a huge pet peeve of mine). Once I was actually able to see, however, I was very happy with the selection of food and drinks that was available. I ordered the District Burger which was very juicy and delicious. It didn't come with anything on the side so I also got the Duck Fat Fries to go with it. They were totally worth the garlic breath that ensued. My girlfriend ordered the Goat Cheese Croquettes. They were very good but there were only three of them and they were each about the size of a golf ball. This portion wouldn't satisfy an infant. After finishing our first meals we both realized that we were still very hungry, so we decided to order again. This time I got the croquettes and she got the Chicken Tacos. The tacos were excellent, but again the portion was very small as there were only two tacos serves on miniature tortillas. All in all I'd say that the food was very good, but also very small. If I wanted to spend $70 on dinner I would have gone to a nicer place where that could've meant one human adult size entree and dessert. Come here for happy hour if you can, but not a full meal!

Their food is really really really good .... loved the place, the waitress treats you like family. It is $$$$ quality but for only $$, what else can I say .... I go there every other week with my wife.

GET THE PORK SHOULDER. you have to. I get it every time and everyone always looks at it and starts drooling. If I am feeling nice, i will offer to those drooling bystanders. It's a big shoulder (bone in) with a thick brown sauce on a bed of spinach for those that want some green stuff. Braised tofu is good too.. kind of like a todo version of the pork shoulder. authentic? i don't know but it's real good!

really good xiao long bao--smaller than I've had before but very good! rice cake was also deliciously squishy. scallion pancake with beef also good. very modern trendy decor; kind of makes you think it would be bad or inauthentic but not the case!
this BYOB small restaurant has a rock solid menu even though there are not a lot on the menu. Definitely try the mushroom cigars and the lamb . Love them ! Come early and bring CASH.

Having heard such great things from fellow Yelper Christophe J. , I was ready to finally eat here! Today was the day, so my husband and I went with my in-laws. (See my pictures for more info.) It was hard to spot as we drove past, but the GPS helped on that score. The wait when we got inside was 15-20mins according to the hostess. I gave my name and we waited around. Not easy given the tight space and lack of seating for those waiting on table space. (My father-in-law had enough time to go wander a few blocks and back.) While waiting for seats, I couldn't help notice the music playing overhead (rather loudly) was all the music I'd listened to in high school! (I'm 29 now...) Finally shown to a table, we see that it's cafeteria style. Long tables and long rows of stools. (My horrible back was not pleased with the stools at all.) A waiter was at our table soon after to take our drink orders. Those took about 5 mins. (2 iced coffees and a hot tea with a decaf requested for after we ate.) We did have to make a point of asking for the sugar though. FYI: it was a dispenser of sugar in the raw. You'll need to ask for any kind of substitute like Sweet n' Low. Our food took quite a while however. I was not watching a clock, but I'd guess a 20min wait for it. During the wait we noticed the silverware had a stamp on it indicating it came from Delta airlines and that they were wrapped in bar towels instead of napkins. My mother-in-law had the potato cake. She said it needed salt; which wasn't on the table, much like the missing pepper. She also said her eggs were under cooked for her tastes. My father-in-law had the four cheese omelette which he had no major complaints about. He also wondered where the salt & pepper were. My husband had the Fingerling Potatoes Poutine and enjoyed it a great deal. I tried it and I have to agree with him that it was fabulous. The plate it was served on was rocket hot though, so be careful. MINE: I got the classic dish. Mozzarella and cheddar grilled cheese on brioche served with tomato soup. For the prices charged, I gotta say "meh" at best. The brioche was delicious and the cheese blend was wonderful. My major issue is the ratios. If you serve me 3 inches worth of bread, you'd better match it with the cheese(s). There wasn't even a 1/4 inch of cheese on this! The soup was another "meh" for me. It was blended in a way that made it a bisque more than a soup. It wasn't smooth. It also had a distinct lack of flavor. Tomato, yes, but with no seasonings like salt to enhance the natural yummy-ness of what quality tomatoes should taste like. With a total cost of $55.80 for the four of us; I gotta say it doesn't seem worth it. There are obviously great things on the menu as the Fingerling Potatoes Poutine demonstrates, but it was the yummy exception today; not the rule. I've told my husband we can come back since there is a dessert menu and an extensive drinks menu to try out.

Think Japanese tapas. A lot of fried dishes, but tastefully created. Dishes don't come with rice, so make sure to order that separately. Dishes are relatively inexpensive, but it's small portions so the price can add up quick. Having travelled to Japan, I can tell you that Fukurou is culturally authentic. Pretty much feels like you're in another country. The restaurants dark wood tables and low lighting make the restaurant very peaceful. It's a small place, but the ambiance is killer. It was nice objectively, but tapas aren't my thing.

So. freaking. good. Came here to celebrate a birthday dinner a couple weekends back. It was my first time at the restaurant...aaand I will def be back. Highlights of the meal include the brussel sprouts (holy crap), the hummus, and the batata harra (potato dish). In fact, those three flavors combined yields the perfect bite. I kid you not. The baba ghanouj was good, too. As was the cauliflower dish, and the fattoush. Yum scrum. Didn't try the meat dishes but heard they were very good. Ilili got a stamp of approval from our Lebanese friend, who said it's one of the best Lebanese restaurant he has tried in the U.S. yet (the guy knows his food). Also loved the ambiance -- dim lighting, high ceilings, and a large space, so great for big and small groups alike.

This is a place that we like to visit when we are in the area. Very casual setting but the food is very good. We ordered the rib sandwich and it was cooked perfectly with a good amount of BBQ sauce on it. We also had the linguini and shrimp which was very garlicy which I like but definitely need to share with your dinner partner so both of your breath smells like garlic! Always a good place to recommend in the area.

Wow! Who knew ramen could taste so good!? Went mid-afternoon on a Friday. After first telling us it would be a 45-60 minute wait, we got lucky and were seated after about 25 minutes. We were seated around this big table so were sitting among other people. Very casual, relaxed environment. Nice wait staff. For lunch, we each got the Akamaru Modern since so many had recommended it, and EACH got a side of braised pork. It was a lot of food! Looking back, we probably could've split a braised pork side dish. The broth was amazing, almost a thicker consistency than other Asian noodle soups. I feel like the little things restaurants do really enhance the experience. I remember ending with a nice cup of tea they brought out. Yum.

meh completely describes this place. Mac & cheese rather boring - doesn't compare to delicious ones I've had at other "New American" comfort food places. California Cobb Salad forgettable and therefore over-priced. Â  Service lackluster and confused. Apparently the sliders were dry, as was my chicken. Â  So very unimpressed.

I tend to let a few days past prior to commenting on a restaurant, as I am doing here. We sat outside, which was extremely uncomfortable due to the benches and tables crammed together. Our table was comically wobbly, which was funny but eventually annoying. Kind of like the drunk guy at a wedding reception. The shrimp and grits were serviceable by NYC standards, but nothing that would make you smack yo' mamma. I honestly do not remember the other entree we ordered, which speaks volumes of the impression it left. Overall, a simple unremarkable dining experience where you are getting what you pay for. Above a diner, but not earning a recommendation. May be worth exploring again in six months to see how the menu has evolved.
Charming atmosphere, fantastic selection of cheeses

Didn't try their potsticker. Only making reviews on their beef noodle and vegetable dumplings. Noodle was just average, and the vegetable dumplings were okay too. Nothing too fancy as unread from the reviews. Another thing, the service is a little sloppy. The cashier girl was looking at my bill for 30 second to check if it's a fake.. A bit offensive. And place is a bit dirty. Good things: Â price is very cheap.

This quaint, and what seemed to me as a family owned, restaurant had everything I look for especially when it comes to Mexican cuisine. The food was delicious and service was fair. My one turn off about the service came from when we ordered our nacho app, which we had asked for without jalapeÃ±os, and it came out WITH jalapeÃ±os, without us having to say anything the waiter took it back because he noticed it was on the nachos and apologized and took them back. Having an extensive background in food service.. I was turned off about the act that it came back less than 2 mins later by someone else, which led me to believe that someone in the kitchen picked them out by hand. Even after while eating them, they still tasted like jalapeÃ±os and had some bits of it still on it. Besides that, the food was delightful.
Everytime I take a trip out to BK to visit friends, I beg them to take me here. Those sicilian slices are FANTABULOUS!!!! I usually eat about 6 at a time lol

Don Pepe's is what Italian food dreams are made of. The downside is the cash only part of the business, but the homemade wine, delightful bread and scrumptious baked clams.... these folks are NOT afraid of garlic and I love them for that. :) :) :) Seriously, we consider it a big night out when we can get to Don Pepe's... who cares about Canal street and little italy's over-rated italian joints? We'll skip those anyday and head to Don's. The staff is always attentive, witty and sarcastic - thank you Don Pepe's for keeping it real.
I recently tried the Krabi Seafood Noodles Soup. It was not good. I guess I should have taken heed that it says "not recommended for novices - please no returns" right on the menu.

I went for a late bite with my chef friend who's a friend with Nick (the exec chef). We had roast rabbit, pasta and salad. Everything was delicious, but on a bit salty side. Very casual and friendly atmosphere with a good selection of wine as is the case with most of USHG's restaurants. You'd feel very comfortable and at ease. No wonder all their restaurants are so popular... I'd definitely go back and try more dishes (the signature pork dish!). As a side note, Chef Nick is half-Japanese. Yay!

This was my second time here and I would say both times were great. The cheeseburger is my favorite in the city. The havarti cheese and maple bacon are perfect with each other. The fried egg on top just brings it all together. Before some people complain about the price, like they do on other sites, consider that TGIF charges $15 for a cheeseburger that is unremarkable at best. The Bloody Mary bar is unique but I don't know if I would order it again.

So last week I decided to forget about my diet when my boyf suggested we have dinner at pies and thighs in Williamsburg. I don't regret the decision, but am definitely feeling like a chunky monkey today. Pies and thighs was featured on diners drive ins and dives on Monday and since then we have been thinking about it nonstop. Did it live up to the hype? Meh...... The bourbon pecan pie did but the pulled pork was a little dry. The chicken biscuit was covered in hot sauce and butter, but I didn't mind that! All the tables around us had the fried chicken plate. If we make it back over I think that's what we will have to try. For the next month I will be eating nothing but salads to undo the damage done at that meal! :)
Pretty good place. There is no room to sit in there, but what you get is awesome food for really low price. I got pork on small rice and it was delicious.
