We went here for brunch on a Saturday. Â We were a small group of four, but it still took us about an hour to get seated. Â They need to do a better job of winging it and just pushing tables together as needed because there were open tables. Once we were seated, service was fast. Â I had the smoked chicken hash (starter portion) and cornbread for $9.25 (tax included). Â It was fine, but not stellar. Â Other items are more expensive, but this was the perfect amount of food, if you had already eaten breakfast. A really good band called the Afterwork Collective was playing. Â The vibe here is so ridiculously chill. Â The ceiling tiles appear to be painted tin and lanterns hang from the ceiling. This is a very nice spot. There is a small-ish full bar. The food is not "true" southern, but it will certainly do and the atmosphere more than makes up for any shortcomings.

I loved my first meal at this restaurant so decided to revisit here during RW lunch. The food, except for the Skate wing which was way too heavily salt, was still as great as before especially the pasta - perfectly cooked and balanced dish. My issue is with the service. 1. We ordered a bottle of wine to be served with our meal and we were served our apps 5 minutes before the wine had arrived, by the time we tasted wine we were almost done with our first course. 2. We were never offered another serving of bread after we finished our first serving even though the tables to our left and right was offered the choice. 3. Perhaps my biggest dissapointment was when I was on my second glass of wine, a fruit fly dropped into my full glass of wine. I notified the waiter and he took it away without a word. Minutes later he returned with a clean glass, but no wine was offered. It was a full glass of wine and at restaurant of this calibre, I'm not sure exactly why all he did was giving me a new glass without offering to refill at least that single glass of wine which was ruined by flies. And not a word of apology was spoken. Although the food was good, it wasn't good enough for us to overlook their service mishaps. Very disappointing experience.

Stopped by there for lunch, There selection is limited, but what a culinary master piece. Every dish coming out of the kitchen is created with utmost care and personalized. If you are looking for a quick sandwich to go, you may have an issue with timing. Food is worth the weigh when it will arrive.

For my Birthday I choose St. Anselms Hipster Steakhouse. Â Wasn't disappointed and as always I was stuffed and happy when I left. Â This time we went with one entree and like 5 sides and two apps. Â Good move(as I pat myself on the back) Â Great service...I'm 85% addicted to this place!!!
I came here for Restaurant Week and loved it. I ordered the following: o Baba Ghannouj o Phoenician Fries o Black Cod

Rating: 4.5, Date Dined: 7/9/2011 We were five ladies gathering for a surprise birthday dinner. The birthday girl was indeed surprised and the food was fitting for the occasion. Food Given that this is a Michael White restaurant, we had very high expectations for the seafood. I did check Yelp beforehand for some recommendations, wanting to eat the best of the best while I was here. The amuse bouche was a shot of almond "soup" dotted with olive oil and chili oil. It was unique and definitely whet our appetite for the meal. For my appetizer I chose the Trofie Nero and I am so glad that I did. It is one of the most exciting dishes I've eaten this year. The black squid ink pasta had the perfect texture and shape to pick up the pieces of succulent and spiced shellfish as well as to attract the buttery toasted breadcrumbs. The sauce is light but deep in flavor. I am still thinking about this dish. For my main course I tried the Ippoglosso (Atlantic halibut). It was a beautifully presented dish. The fish was well cooked but sadly under-seasoned. Everything else on the plate, the foie gras mousse stuffed morels, the asparagus, the hollandaise on top of pea puree, was delicious. Most of the other ladies chose the cod as their main course and all of our plates were clean by the end of dinner. We shared two desserts. The olive oil cake was my favorite. It was moist and very flavorful with an invisible crust of crunchy sugar on top. The Chocolate "Budino" was a gorgeous masterpiece that they presented with "happy birthday" written on the plate. The chocolate mousse encased in gelee was technically stunning. The meal ended with delightful petit fours. Service & Atmosphere To get to Ai Fiori, you need to walk up a massive winding staircase from the lobby of the Setai. Upon entrance there is a very large bar where I saw some people dining. I was the first to arrive and was greeted by 5-6 people standing at the front desk. This is certainly a fancy restaurant in where there is ample staff on hand. For a Saturday night, the main dining room was perhaps 2/3 full. It seemed to be a mix of visitors and special occasion diners. The service was professional and trying to be warm, but not quite making it there. Our main waiter did everything right but the rapport seemed a bit forced. Nonetheless the service is on par with the restaurant's stature. We only had one bottle of Sancerre between the four drinkers at the table and the meal was around $100 per person. Next Â time I'd like to try the $84 4-course prix fixe menu. The lasting impression I have of this place (other than the great company enjoyed throughout our three-hour birthday dinner) is the Trofie Nero. I can't stop dreaming about it. I want to bring friends back to dine at the bar and to try this dish.
The best pizza in the world Period. I Wish they were walking distance from my house in queens.

I've been searching for good lamb in NYC and I finally found it! 53rd and 6th (The Halal Guys) is so overrated. These guys do Chicken & Lamb so much better than all the places in Manhattan. Perhaps it's because these guys are from Astoria. Anyhow the chicken is always fresh and the lamb is amazing but filling and I do feel like taking a nap afterwards. Get here early because they leave before 5PM most days. Line gets a little long during lunchtime but it goes quickly. 5 Stars!
great for delivery, though the food tends to get a little cool in the process.

Bubby's, WHAT DID YOU DO?!?! Your blueberry pancakes were the best in the city, a) because they're awesome and b) because of the blueberry compote! I don't care how good the blueberries are right now, this stuff is liquid ambrosia. At least give customers the choice!!!
Great Sandwiches, Great atmoshpere, Great price

Delicious! I have no cause to complain, really tasty food and really large portions of it. High quality ingredients with a really good sense of how flavors blend. (Oh god, goat cheese salad with pistachios, beets, and braised pears? Please please please do it again.) It gets busy around brunch time but everyone is personable, friendly, and efficient.They get extra points for not rushing us out and turning the table even though they had quite a crowd. Word to the wise: brunch is CASH ONLY.

This place has really slipped. Â It's turned into a silly factory for "Sex In the CIty" wannabes from elsewhere. The food used to be rather creative, but on my last visit it was actually lame. Â A glorified Applebee's.
Small, cute restaurant. Amazing food.

Finding a place open after all our sight seeing at 11pm would usually be quite impossible. Â At least, back home it would be. Â Seems like there's a lot of places around here that are open to serve night owls such as myself into the wee hours of the night. Â Sanders Restaurant being one of them. Â Not only are they open late, they're open 24 hours. The atmosphere is really pretty. Â Intimate. Â Dimmed lighting, available booth seating. Â Definitely not what I expected from a place open 24/7. Â Therefore, walking in, I was definitely surprised, but with that, also, expectations went up. A look at the menu, and it seemed like they had pretty tasty things to offer. Â I decided on their Hanger Steak with sweet potato mash and asparagus. Â My friend chose the Ahi Tuna Wrap. Â And then the wait began ... ... and continued ... Yes. Â We waited a long while for our order. Â I know mine was a steak, so while waiting, I tried to convince myself that the reason it was taking so long was that my steak had to cook. Â The server came by to refill our water glasses at least 5-6 times before we got our order. Â We had been walking all day, so I admit we were quite parched, but also helps to give an idea of how long we actually waited for our food. And our wait was in vain. Â We got our food, and the excitement and anticipation ended. Â My steak was burnt, and although I asked for medium rare, the different cuts were cooked to varying levels ranging from medium rare to well done (yuck, I hate well done). Â The outside sear was not a light sear. Â I could have dealt with that. Â It was black. Â Burned. Â Also, although the sweet potato mash sounded good in concept, laid out on my plate like a big heaping mountain, I ended up barely touching it. Â It may have had some value served as a small side. Â But as a huge heaping mountain of mashed sweet potato, it made it unappetizing, and definitely not worth the calories. My friend complained about her dish too. Â And although I try to stray from opinions that are not mind about food, I could see that her ahi tuna was not lightly seared, but instead almost fully cooked. Â The paper around the wrap had gotten moist and stuck to the wrap, probably meaning the wrap had been sitting for a bit before we even received it. Â Which made us think if the reason our order took so long to come out was that it just sat there, done, waiting for our server to come pick it up and bring it to our table. Â And the wrapping left one wondering if they could even wrap properly as bite after bite, the wrap continued to just fall apart. Lastly, it would probably be good to mention that their butter for the bread tastes like absolutely nothing. Â Wish they at least had better bread for their butter, since their rolls and crackers they served were apparently the only things I enjoyed about this meal. An underwhelming experience.

I didn't now what to expect given the mixed reviews. I picked this restaurant based of its location to a night club. I checked the menu online and thought it was worth a try. This restaurant is tucked away in a brownstone on Union Street in Park Slope Brooklyn. It has a warm welcoming cozy feel. The staff is friendly and very helpful. Â  We were a party of 4 ladies having dinner before a night club in the area. We all arrived at different times passed our reservation, but that was no problem as I had called ahead and was told it was okay if we were running late. Our waiter Gonzalo was a godsend. He waited on us hand and foot. Answering every question we had about the menu, food and wine parings, and the origins of the owner. Everything Gonzalo recommended was amazing. The food was fresh and tasty. I could have dessert because I was too full from my appetizer and main course. Between us four, I think we tried everything on the menu. I recommend it all as we sampled each other's plates. Just ask for Gonzalo and say Jackie, Kim, Deborah and Gabby sent you.

A fun dinner out, if you are in to low-key and kicking it old school. This is a friendly, laid-back, family style spot, with a wood burning pizza oven and fresh pasta dishes. Â The hostess (possibly the owner) smiled and welcomed us in, and this wall of Zagats signs at the entry way indicates this place has received lots of Zagats love over the years, so definitely some food cred here. I had the Black Taglierini, which is a fresh black pasta with squid ink that adds color not flavor, and in a sauce punctuated with house sundried tomatoes, prawns, peas and a tomato cream sauce. Â The pasta was traditional, but clearly super fresh. The sundered tomatoes were tasty (house made) and the prawns cooked well, but I'm pretty sure the peas were frozen. The atmosphere here is dated with formica tables, soda in cans, and lots of italian knick knacks providing a down-home vibe. Â The bread for the table was adequate (but not homemade and not particularly tasty) and came with a fix yourself dipping plate and bottles of vinegar and olive oil to put together your own mix. There were families, tourists and all packed in to a very small dining room. Â We enjoyed our meal, and I could see this being a locals spot & fun neighborhood joint. Â The pizza and pasta were solid. Â Not a destination, but a good local spot.
One of the best italian restaurants in the city. Food was delightful, tasty and reasonably priced. Ambiance was very relaxed, cozy and romantic. Will definitely come back here again.
I ordered one slice of spinach&artichoke, all I can say is that the pizza is within the expectation, nothing special to be honest

I booked this place for my friends birthday since he loves Italian food. I had heard a lot about this place and it was recommended by my colleague Â  The ambiance is great and few of the dishes are worth trying. The reason for 3 stars is our disappointment with the waiter, Martin and few specials that our waiter initially told us and took the order were not available. We ordered the Escolar and beef carpaccio and it was just fabulous and we order 2nd helping for both the dishes. While ordering the drinks our waiter took upon himself to correct us on our pronunciation (with a lot of attitude) of the dishes and drinks. Unfortunately, Italian is not my 1st language and so like most people are pronunciation is not going to be exact!!! Additionally, when we were ordering our drinks and dishes, we were disappointed to find out that a lot of the specials were not available since they were running short on key ingredients. I completely understand that the specials might get over but I think, the waiter should have inquired with the chef before telling us what the specials were. Out of 5 drinks Â - 1 beers wasn't available. out of 5 dishes Â - 2 of the days specials was not available We had to continuously look for our waiter in order to ask for more drinks, sides or even our check. I think the restaurant can do a better job with training their waiters to provide more customer service.

This is coming from someone who didn't eat spaghetti. I simply wasn't in the mood. I had another mainstay on the menu, the spiced duck breast cooked medium (rare) with touches of sweet and tangy berry (the garnishes and dressing change seasonally, I believe). The meat was perfectly pink and tender, and as duck tends to go well with fruity emulsions, this was no exception. Expect the fat trimmings to add aromaticity to the flavor. I had a dry and robust red wine to pair. My senses were tickled. I sat in the more quiet area of the restaurant, and therefore it was a fitting venue for an intimate dinner for two. Service was courteous and attentive.
Was it worth the redonkulous waiting time? Â Yeah, I'd say so. Â Make sure you bring a drinking buddy with you.

Oh, how I have missed having a bar of this caliber around! Being fairly new to NYC what I have noticed there being a complete void of decent, cosy, warm and inviting old style English/Irish pubs that strike a balance between catering for casual drinks for any occasion and somewhere with a great atmosphere and even better food where you can enjoy an intimate and enjoyable dinner. Trading Post ticks those boxes and more! It is absolutely beautiful and inviting. The staff are friendly and knowledgeable and the food is fantastic! Add to that an amazing drinks list and a range of different areas - inc a Whiskey room!!! Â ...and it's not just a great place to try out. It's the local you have always wanted.

Great service, amazing food, beautiful location! I went there with Persian and Lebanese friends, very demanding with their home food, it became their favorite restaurant in NY right away. I came with meat eater monsters and vegetarian yogi weirdoes, they both loved it too! The service was always amazing, friendly, and on my 3rd time there I felt like a regular. The first time I came, we had to wait because the restaurant was packed, and that's probably why we were there too. No other place made the wait so pleasant. The hostess seated us in the back, brought us a drink menu and 2 rounds of cocktails ended up on the house. And finally, even though it's not cheap, for the amount of food covering the whole table, it's very decent compared to NY standards. I really don't understand the few bad reviews... I guess haters gonna hate! Recommended Dishes: Flatbread; labneh; chicken and rabbit. PS: Regarding the hipster comments... what the F do you haters expect from an old factory in the middle of nowhere in the north end of Greenpoint??? PS2: What's wrong with people saying they Â pay to get full? That's gross... go to a fast-food and get stuffed for cheap you pigs!
Sushi is good quality. Liked the tempura rolls. The veggie and pork dumplings also very good. Great rap music playing during dinner. Pretty funny for a sushi restaurant.

My new fave soho post shopping / pre going out dinner / girlfriending go to spot. Love the high ceilings, spacious seating area. The cocktails are absolutely fabulous and service is super friendly. The atmosphere is rustic, warm and, rather comfortable. Absolutely love love love the location - there tends to be a wait on the weekend nights so be aware that they might make you wait a bit at the bar even if you have a reservation. That night I had the spicy calamari and the Branzino filet, definitely one of the best dishes that night. Excited to try their brunch!

This is a great restaurant to come and relax with your friends and family. Â I've been coming to Sobaya for more than six years, and it is one of my favorite restaurants in East Village. Â My wife and I like to come here on a cold and rainy day for the Nabeyaki Udon, which is the best in the city. Â I also like their sake oyakodon and tuna steak don as well.
Great quality ingredients combined perfectly. Got a simple honey turkey and cheddar sandwich and it was amazing.

I've only been to Cafe Katja once, but I was absolutely blown away. Â Our meals were absolutely perfect, and that's saying a lot. Â  I don't know anything about Austrian food, and basically stopped in here on a whim. Â I'm not a big sausage fan (interpret that as you wish), but the knowledgeable and genuinely warm bartender talked me into ordering the emmentaler sausage, which was absolutely incredible. Â (She told me that the sausage was "relatively light" because it was made from pork. Â I still don't understand how that makes any sense at all, but she was absolutely right.) My buddy ordered the cheese spatzle, which kicks the crap out of even the very best American mac & cheese. Â Even the sides were inexplicably amazing--how the hell did they make roasted carrots taste so good? Â The cucumber potato salad was also a winner. All that, and a bunch of great Austrian and German beers on tap. Â And a cute bartender, who got even cuter after a few Stiegls. Â And a friendly owner who clearly loves his restaurant. I'm shocked that this place isn't packed from the first minute that it opens every evening. Â It deserves all of the customers that it can possibly pack in. Now stay away, so that I can still get a seat at the bar.

Amazing! One of the best Latin restaurants I have ever been to. The Aji sauce is delicious. Staff is warm and very knowledgeable. Music, decor, and overall feel Â create as close to an authentic Colombian dining experience one can find stateside.

Good, but not great, and I hate having to say that because I was realllllllllly stoked about trying this place. Â I'll definitely give it another shot, but no time soon. Â Part of my beef with this kitschy little Louisiana loving gem were their prices. Â Just a little (not a lot) too high for the size and quality of the portions. Â  We tried the trio side sampler and the Jambalaya. Â They were all foods I've had many times before and am fairly experienced with, so I am confident of my opinion when I say that it's "good food" but not "great". For all of you gluten free eaters out there, there are very limited options for you here. Â I initially called to inquire about this a week before eating there, and received a response that implied that about half their menu is gluten free. When the day came to actually try this place out, we were disappointed to hear from our server that we were misinformed by the employee on the phone. Â There are some gluten free options, just not a lot. They had a nicely stocked bar, and the service was friendly and efficient. Â No complaints there, what so ever. Â They weren't very busy when we went, which was nice, too. Â  The one thing I have to make a note of is their bathroom with the pull chain toilet. Â Apparently it's got some notoriety about it. Â Also, the decor in general was brought in from LA (a lot of it at least.) Â If you ask about it all, I'm sure they'd be happy to tell you the stories about the different items!

I had dinner at Scarpetta last night and the food was amazing. The creamy polenta was to die for and the burrata was great too. I had the duck and my boyfriend had the short ribs. Both were very tasty. The service was very good and the overall experience was great. Scarpetta is a perfect place to get great food and good service.

At the bar, the menu is on the wall. No cherry coke. Instead, the bartender substituted cherry with grenadine. Â I ordered the burger medium and it was thick and juicy. The meat was a tad too dense though. I would have preferred a more relaxed burger. Went at 1:30pm and had to sit at the bar. Started getting packed at 2pm and a line started to form. Definitely going back. I was dared finish 3 bistro burgers next time. Not a problem! =) $5.75 for a hamburger, $6 for a cheeseburger, $6.75 for a bistro burger..aka a BLT cheeseburger. $3.75 for a grilled cheese sandwich, $5.50 for a grilled cheese sandwich w/ TONS of bacon in it). $2.50 for shoestring fries

Definitely recommend this place! Quick meal for lunch and dinner or on the go! Some boxed lunches comes with free soup or salad, they also have a hot self service buffet line, I never tried it. I don't like buying something that goes by weight. So I avoid. Seating can be limited esp during afternoons on weekdays and some weekends, bathroom is small and literally open. Toilet behind close doors and the sinks are outside. Either way, I come here for the food. Tofu stew is great, the rolls are good, kimchi fried rice with egg is okay. Can cost you around $5-$12 or more depending on what you spend and how you spend it.

5 stars for the amazing, well-balanced dishes in terms of color, texture, and flavor 3-4 stars for the ambience and rushed nature of eating in a very busy, crowded space 3 stars for the absurdly long menu that needs to be edited down to their 20 best dishes 2 stars for the single bathroom and line that took 10 minutes (with only a weak hand dryer and no paper towels) My friend and I ordered a chicken soup, the fried taro appetizer, and the green curry with chicken made mild at our request. The soup and curry were AMAZING. I have not had such great well-balanced flavor in years. Not too salty, not too sweet. Just perfect. I am dying to go back and try other dishes. The only thing that confused me is that I saw at least 6 tables that ordered the pad thai which appeared very monotone in color and un-memorable. On the other hand, I was raving about our soup and entree the entire night and next day!

Update 10/26/2014: Â Man, I still love the hell out of this food, but they've got some serious issues with their servers, and also with their ability to fully and properly pack up food to go...I mean...the food is ridiculously good, but they could do with replacing one or two of their less than stellar servers. Â Deleting a star :( _______ i want to live here and eat everything. seriously.

Honestly, this place is all hype. Â People think that the long line means it's amazing and exclusive, but it's so not worth waiting more than an hour for a bowl of noodles that is decent but not in any way remarkable. I actually thought the noodles were underdone (and yes, I'm familiar with the Japanese style of noodle which tends to be cooked firmer, but there's a difference between that al dente ramen style and being undercooked). Â  The chashu was 90% FAT, which is far from the ideal meat-fat ratio. Â The miso broth was good but lacked that signature dimension of saltiness-- I could taste more of the sweet alcoholic fermentation of the miso and not the prominent salty note that's typical of miso ramen. I understand that the kitchen was probably trying for a more refined version of miso than the typical salt bomb, but I think they missed the mark a bit here. Â Minus points also for their menma, which had a weird (indescribable) aftertaste and their rough diagonal cuts of scallions, which just looks sloppy. Â Bean sprouts seem to be in every bowl, and for me, that is the mark of cheap filler. Sorry Totto, you need refinement.

We stopped in for lunch yesterday on a snowy day and were the only customers. We were disappointed in not finding a specific Lunch menu because I had checked out the website ahead of time and saw that there was, indeed, a prix fixe lunch menu. We asked about a lunch menu and were told they didn't have one. So we wound up spending WAY more than we had expected to. So I am rating them 3 stars instead of 4, just for this reason. However, we thoroughly enjoyed our food! We split the butternut squash soup -delicious, with both a sweet and tangy taste. My husband felt adventurous and ordered the Brazilian Pacu Fish Ribs - I tasted them and they were excellent, even to me, who is still learning to like most fish dishes. The BBQ sauce flavor was both sweet and tangy - nice. My short ribs dish was also excellent - boneless and soft. The chimichurri sauce made it a bit different than most short ribs dishes. The serving staff was very attentive, which wasn't surprising since it was empty, but not overbearing.We were too full to even think about dessert, so I can't comment on that. We also didn't try any of their specialty drinks, but stuck to coffee and tea.

I ate here again last week after coming here for my birthday party a few months back. Â I cannot say enough good things about the restaurant from the food to the service to the price. Â Hong is an amazing chef and personality and always makes you feel welcome in her restaurant. Â The food is incredible; we tried completely different things this time. Â The chicken wings and the calamari are amazing, the pomelo salad is fresh and flavorful, and the green curry and lobster dumplings are to die for. Â If I could give more than 5 stars to Ngam, I absolutely would. Â Unfortunately, I don't live in NY anymore so I can only come here when I visit but it is an absolutely necessary stop each and every time.

This is one of the most delicious restaurants EVER! I've been here many times and don't have a single complaint. Make reservations (they are very busy). The service is wonderful; everyone is sweet & knowledgable. The food is unique and will make your taste buds jump for joy! Some of my favs here are: BBQ braised pulled pork sliders w/ sweet potato fries Salt & pepper shrimp Spicy bigeye tuna tartare w/ tempura eggplant Lamb & chorizo meatballs Melted muenster cheese Bacon donuts!!! (I was skeptical about these at first. But after one bite, it was love) Their menu changes sometimes. My brother told me he tried some really yummy bone marrow dish here, but it was never on the menu when I went. I hope I get to try it! I also had my birthday dinner here once. It was about 14 people and we had a pre-fixed dinner (chefs selection). Food is delish & prices are really reasonable so this spot is great for any occasion!
My favorite crepe place in all of NY. This rivals Frjtz Fries in SF in terms of affordable crepe comfort food.

As far as wait times... I think I'm used to a wait for a table after living my entire life in New York, so I'm not basing my review on that. Â  As far as the meatballs... I am a meatball lover and I just can't say that these meatballs blow me away. Â After seeing all the raving reviews on this place, I gave this place two chances (just in case I went on an off night). Â It wasn't memorable to me. Â As much as I want to be on board with everyone else raving about the meatballs here... I would go to Frankie's for their meatballs any day over this place.

Perhaps good as a lunch place, but horrible as an izakaya. All the dishes are too small for the price and the service is not very good. Takowasa looked like it came in a large dish but it was all filler at the bottom with only a couple pieces of octopus on the top. The cooked dishes took a long time to come out of the kitchen. It's good for groups, a large army of Japanese people were getting plastered next to us. They were into it for the drinks though and could give a crap about the food IMHO. I'm not done with this place, I am looking forward to try it again after they have a couple months' more experience. I hope they can get it together by then.
This place is awesome!! I whent saturday brunch: it was pack!! But the mg make it easy to get a table!! Great sangrÃ­a. And the fish tacos r amizing!! Â Love the mÃºsic! Good job guys!! C u soon!

I have only been here a few times but the pizza is delicious, made to order with really nice ingredients. I was out with friends late last night, a Tuesday, and we wanted to get some pizza, but in little italy and China town not much is open after 10pm aside from a few late night Chinese restaurants. I saw on Yelp that Piacere was open til 2am and we walked over and lo and behold as we walked by they beckoned us in. The food was totally delicious and the staff gave us no attitude about how late it was. Granted it's more expensive than a few slices but it's much higher quality (organic!) than most pizzerias in the city.
I regularly go to UVA, really nice atmosphere an excellent wine and pasta. I recently went there for brunch too and really enjoyed the meal. really recommend it! Their gnocchi are out of this world!

I used to be a regular here. But the lesbian bartender on Tuesdays makes her own rules and management supports it. Not good for business. Y'all lost a good steady customer that tips 20% everytime... Â FYI. Bell, Book & Candle has a better oyster special. That's where I'll take my business. Ok byeeeeeee...

An intimate mexican food restaurant with great ambience. But considering the size of the place thats to be expected. I was surprised that the food despite its smaller portions the food was filling and the courses were shared. The Pork Adobo wasgreat if not slightly tough. The desert was wonderful though. Budin de banana was very good. The service was very attentive. They were on top of refilling our drinks and the waiter we had was very informative friendly. Will be frequenting this place most definitely.

Oh. My. Goodness. I don't even know where to start. Fresh, light, healthful, beautiful, and so so so so so tasty. Absolutely delicious. The best lentil soup I've ever had. Marinated eggplant app is absurd. White beat salad is so refreshing. And of course what can be said about the mixed platter other than juicy, soft, tender meat. Lamb the way it should be. Ugh. Almond pudding is INSANE. Texture is otherworldly. The man who cooks the food was willing to speak with us as we were the only ones there (why, I have no idea) and was a humble, sweet darling of a man. This spot is perfect. Aces all around. Deck of nothing but aces.
pros: supercheap, great value, good taste, fast and great for take out. cons: tiny, too crowded for eat-in and the communication can be a challenge.

Hospitality was at it best. While waiting they offered us red and white wine for FREE. We ordered the grilled octopus, peasant salad, scallops and the taverna's house special seafood. HUGE portion, delicious food. Â We were so stuffed and waiter surprised us with free mug.
The food is consistently good, whether brunch or dinner - rustic with bold flavors. Â The service is sometimes a little spotty.
Great food. Slow service. Â Why did it take 50 minutes to get a Salad? The waitress didn't even notice we didn't have our food???

Love Love Love the fries, it's just so good. But to be honestly, the fries ain't cooked crispy when they get busy. This is the one thing i get disappointed sometimes. =( By the way, sweet mango chutney and sweet chili are my top two favorites.

Gave Sugar Freak another chance over the weekend. Â I think that's probably the last time we will go there for dinner. Â I wouldn't mind just going for drinks or maybe brunch. Â I had the shrimp etoufee this time and my husband had the blackened catfish platter. Â Again, the food was just mediocre. Â I've been to Louisiana many times and always look forward to the distinct cuisine...I just don't experience that when I go to Sugar Freak.

I don't see the craze about the fries, as they seem to have the same taste as any other type of premium fries out there. On the other hand, the sauces are differently something to write about. I grabbed an order of the pomegranate teriyaki mayo and the black truffle mayo. Â Surprisingly, I liked the former than the latter, since my palette didn't really care about any dull tastes. Â  That said, I actually didn't mind eating the fries outside the place where a bunch of other people were loitering and eating as well. Â It seems a bit uncomfortable but it definitely is worth the experience.

First review of 2013 with a shiny new Yelp badge on my profile? Â The honor clearly has to go to one of my best dining experiences in 2012! :) My good friend and I wanted to surprise our lovely boyfriends for a joint dinner date, and I was given the responsbility of picking the place. With the Bohemian reservation number in hand, and seeing as I am a complete and utter sucker for all things "secret" and "mysterious," I knew we had to give it a try. Reservations were quite easy to make (no name dropping needed), but they were booked a few weeks out, so if you are lucky to snag the number (no asking me, please! It's a true networking number), make sure you call in advance. After giving the number to my manager (brownie pts, anyone?), he recommended that we forgo the tasting menu and order al a carte. It was a fantastic suggestion. As a party of 4, we paid nearly $80pp, which included much more food than came in the tasting menu PLUS drinks. Definitely order off the menu if you are coming in a large group! The restaurant itself is quite unassuming; walk past a long corrider and you'll come across a small door with a wooden sign that simply reads, "Bohemian." You'll need to get buzzed in and check with the staff for your reservation. The restaurant itself is very small, cozy, and decorated with murals of Japan, a little zen garden, and drums everywhere...that I may or may not have hit while foodgasming... just sayin' We ordered: - Uni Croquettes: Delish! Small bites of uber goodness. - Ikura Caviar + Uni Rice Bowl: SOOO good, one of my faves. Note the portion is small. - Wagyu Sliders: YUMMYYYYY. MUST GET. - Beef Short Ribs Sashimi: Twas a-ok. Not a must get in my book. - Foie Gras Soba: Meh, not so impressed. Pass! - Mac N Cheese: Very unique spin on mac n cheese. Not bad if you're a cheese fan! - Branzini: Portioned very generiously and utterly delish! Def get it! - Lamb Chops: I was bursting at the seams by this point. We really wanted to get a meat dish as Bohemian is located in the back of a meat shop, but this was the only choice left. Verdict: not bad :) And don't you dare forget the booze! Their cocktails are works of art that rival ones found in the top speakeasies in NYC. Their Japanese beer is also off the chain, hella smooth, and ohso perfect with your meal. My friends' guy was so impressed with Bohemian, that he promptly made another reservation for a few days later to take his mom - who is uber picky about food! Can I get a "BEST GIRLFRIENDS EVERRRRR?" Methinks so!
This place gets packed with a lot of guys. I had fun time here and some great memories. ;)
Perfect relaxed, beyond delicious, cool restaurant great from midday to midnight. Incredible drink list, locally sourced food, and super friendly service. Playlist from Ciara to Lil Wayne to Lo fang.

Spicy pork with classic Tomato sauce Smash, with the side salad....Damn!!! This sandwich was done perfectly. Â I can't think of a way to improve it. Â And the salad on the side was lovely. I'm going to keep trying items on this menu, and maybe I'll end up changing to 5 stars; I hope!!!

ZOMG finger lickin' good! The secret (to me)? Toasted pita as opposed to a cold ass pita that's hard to bite. Ordered the green falafel sandwich and ginger mint lemonade (so spicy, so refreshing). I was in heaven, probably because I floated up after eating all that. You know how falafel has a way of maximizing after you scarfed down the entire sandwich before noticing so I was comatose at work after this "light" lunch. You will most likely have to wait a while for you order and eat it sitting on the curb, but who cares? It is delicious. Can't wait to go back and order a platter.

We were looking for a bite to eat at around noon on a recent Sunday. No reservations?!?!?!? GASP!! Apparently, on Sunday in the west village, three people with no brunch reservations are no better than lepers. Ugh. Insufferable city, you! Not sure what element of pop culture is to blame, but Brunch in NYC takes itself WAYYYYYY too seriously. Not so at Palma. I am so happy we stumbled into this place and I will be very glad to return. After receiving a very offRensive reception from the the maitre'd at --half-empty, I might add-- Ofrenda (your yelp review is coming, Ofrenda!) we carried on our search for a place to eat. It was not looking good for us, lines stretched out into the gutter at many places. But somehow we lucked out at Palma. Since we didn't want to sit in the garden, they were able to seat us asap and we Â were welcomed with open arms to one of the best brunches I've had in a long time. The service and the ambiance was wonderful. The veal burger was delightful, the cocktails were spot on, pasta dish I ordered was sublime, the garden was lovely--though we didn't eat out there. I didn't want to go home! By the time we left, the place was packed so they clearly have a following. Looking forward to returning, Palma!

Best pizza place ever in NYC, hands-down. The buffalo mozzarella pizza is to die for!! I haven't read any of the reviews here, but if anyone says anything about taking off a star for the decor or whatever -- YOU ARE AN IDIOT. By the time you take a huge bite out of the perfectly thin, melt-in-your-mouth gooey goodness, you should've forgotten about complaining about the lack of decor and "atmosphere", which really has no place in a pizza restaurant anyway.

An Italian gem in Astoria. Pros: * Comfortable and intimate ambiance. * Friendly and speedy service * Recommend the famous Potato pizza (better than Kale pizza) and brussel sprouts. * Affordable prices for delicious food in ample portions. Cons: * Didn't think anything about the Baby Jesus Cake, it was so hyped up so I expected something out of the ordinary but instead was underwhelmed. Tips: * Make sure to make a reservation, because it gets very packed during busy hours. Would love to check Vesta out for brunch.

We went with a large group and were seated at a back table. The food was ok. I ordered buddhist mixed vegetables. The tofu was soft tofu - I didn't like it - usually that stuff is for desserts, not main dishes. Fry me up some firm tofu with those vegetables! Also the sauce was this pinkish-white cream - kinda off-putting. My son had this chicken dish - it was basically steamed chicken. It sucked. I could have done that at home. No one liked it. Good thing he ordered something else as well or he would have not been happy. My daughter had garlic chicken - that was really very tasty and done well. The popular drink at the table was the coconut water in the coconut - after you're done drinking it they'll cut it open for you so you can scoop out the meat. I'd go back again if I'm in NY, but I'd also rather try something else too, since this wasn't like, my most favorite place ever, and since there are sooooooooooooo many restaurants in the city.
I mean there's nothing left to say
Came here for a date. It's nice cause it's an around the way spot, but romantic cause it's so small and intimate. Fits about 12 people. Great food and my date loved it too! Will come back.

This is my favorite restaurant in the city. Never have I left this place feeling that the food was subpar, the service to slow, or the atmosphere annoying. This no frills establishment focuses on three basics: tasty and well seasoned food, affordable prices, and snappy service. I'm a huge fan of the Chicken Ouzi, which never disappoints and is always filling. Aside from the ouzi, which is a pita stuffed with seasoned pilaf chicken rice, the lamb pitza, merguez plate and vegetable platter are all in my starting line up. I also love the decor. It has an awesome rustic and nostalgic far east feel, even down to the crow bar door that separates the kitchen from the inside dining room. If you Â want supper fancy, keep walking down Atlantic. However, if you want a full belly, some change left in your wallet, and an appetite at ease, Bedouin Tent is the place to come.

If you're looking at this review while standing outside the restaurant, please, don't let the looks deter you. (The line, however, if longer than 10 people, may still deter you and that's okay!) Wah Fung is a greasy hole in the wall - but it has some very tasty barbecue and prices that are considered dirt cheap, even for Chinatown. They specialize in roasted meats over rice with a side of cabbage for $3.50. The roast pork is the best, with a very sweet sauce. The roast duck is also tasty, but I buy that as a whole rather than over rice. They always pack the boxes to the top, to the point where tasty roast pork is oozing out of the edges. Service here can be astoundingly slow. Its a very small business that survives on the takeout demand. There are no tables or waitservice. You just get in line. That said, the meat is always chopped fresh on the spot, so it retains its tenderness and moist texture. So every single person has to watch their meat get chopped up, the rice dished out, the veggies crammed in the side, sealed, bagged, exchange cash, etc. I'd like to see the line move a little faster, but beggars can't really be choosers, now can they? If I remember right, it's cash only or cash preferred.

Cooked with Lovvveeeeeee. I never really understood what that phrase meant, let alone experienced it as often as I do as when I moved to New York. It's what embodies Freeman's. After doing laps around the block like an idiot, I finally located "Freeman's Alley" where the restaurant is covertly tucked away. Once inside, the place is a bit cliche-rustic, adorned with taxidermy deer heads and oil paintings of Presidents. Nevertheless it was a very warm and romantic spot where the whole place has that candlelit feel. CHOW: Artichoke Dip ($10): creamy, salty nom nom nom Devils on Horseback ($6): Saddle UP kids and ORDER these. Blue cheese stuffed prunes wrapped in bacon. Main: Braised short ribs which was a bold choice on a 1st date, even bolder to polish it clean. I live with no regrets. *They've since removed it-- probably a seasonal winter dish. Freeman's is just one of those great places where the atmosphere (in my opinion) perfectly matches the food. Hit.This.Haunt.UP! ............Oh right.. then there was the waiter. I think I'll make a trip back just to drool over him.
What can I say? The burgers are excellent, as was the Greek fries....burger was so juicy....ummm if only I had room to eat another one....

There are two reasons why last Saturday was special - 1) It was the first summer-like day of spring! Â The overcoats changed into short dresses, the suits into shorts. Â Sullen dispositions turned into broad smiles, and barren roads into street fairs. Â Dark stouts changed into chilled ales, and brandy into mojitos. Â  2) I finally gathered the patience to wait for a table at Ippudo! Yes, the wait is very long, but I'll say it was more than worth it 'cause I was well and truly blown away. Â For appetizers we got chicken wings and the shrimp buns. Â I am not a regular meat-eater but I was chowing down those wings like a mofo. Â There was some kind of glaze on it that was just out of control. Â I would have given Ippudo 5 stars just based on the wings, but I was forced to consider a 6th star when I took my first bite of ramen noodle soup. Â  I got the "Akamaru Shin - Aji new recipe, ramen noodles, thicker pork broth, berkshire pork chashu, cabbage, scallions." Â I got the tofu instead of the pork and added a boiled brown egg. Â The flavors were just bursting in my mouth. I am no food critic, so I cannot go into details of such intricate flavors. All I can humbly say is, please try it! It changed the way I look at Ramen. Â Earlier when I saw a packet of ramen, I saw a quick, disgusting meal with no nutrition. Â Now I see a large bowl of steaming noodle soup that inspired the following comments from my friends: Friend 1: "Oh my god, this is so awesome, I am rethinking brushing my teeth tonight" Friend 2 to the waitress: "Do you have Ippudo t-shirts for sale?" Enough said.

As a former New Orleans resident I came to this place a skeptic. I have tried countless "New Orleans Style" restaurants over the years here and not one has been up to snuff. I mean, seriously, how hard is it to get a decent po boy? Anyhow, problem solved. Sugar Freak in Astoria is the real deal. My fried oyster po boy was perfect with juicy succulent oysters brimming with sea flavor and that just right texture. The fries that accompanied it were excellent and they had crystal's hot sauce on the table and every Abita on tap. Winner winner chicken dinner. Their decor is adorable, but I found their bathrooms to be a little over the top. The waitress was extremely friendly and attentive. I will be sure to be back to try their catfish, their crawfish, and their Sazerac.
4.5 stars Lunch special - one of the best values in nyc (especially on thursday). All the dishes are yummy. Buta kakuni, fluke carpaccio, cod, karaage, etc.

I LOVE LOVE meatballs. The meatballs here are just balls of juicy goodness that I could eat over and over again. They were so flavorful and it comes with enough sauce but too much that it overwhelms the balls. The prices are reasonable and portions are good. Come for late night munchies.

This was our first stop on our trip to NYC. It is very convenient that it is open 24 hours. It is trendy spot in Chelsea within walking distance of the Meatpacking district for a pregame or post game meal. I had the Buffalo chicken sandwich, which was good, but fairly high priced as expected. A positive is the complimentary biscuits. A negative is the bathrooms as there are only two total toilets for men/women.

Friendly staff, great food, close to the L stop. What more can you ask for? Seems family-owned. They have my favorite combination of mediterranean food: rice, chicken shawarma and babaghanoush. AND they serve shawarma on TOP of the babaghanoush. Â Mind blown. Falafel is decent - super hot out of the kitchen and very crispy. We also got the special fries - pretty good, kinda expensive to me for what you get. Portions are huge if you get the platter. I'll probably get that next time and get babaghanoush on the side. Lots of seating space. Clean bathroom.

For the price and amount of food you get, this place is so worth it in NYC! Line is ok if you get to their cart early. The rice remines me of stressed carrots. Haha but with the chicken and lamb and the flat bread so good! Remember to ask for extra white sauce. It makes the dish even tastier. (:

Not sure if the restaurant was having an off night, but all I can say was a waste of money. Bread basket was delicious as others have noted. The polenta truffle appetizer was a mess. Luckily our waited removed it from the bill after promising that it was one of the signature dishes. My friend had the beet casonsei which was delicious and quite unique. I had the signature spaghetti and all I can say is that it was majorly lacking in flavor. The sauce was tasteless and you could probably whip up something tastier in your own kitchen. We finished dinner off with the chocolate cake which was delicious. All in all, would not recommend given the abundance of other more delicious, less pricey restaurants in the city.

Last week I finally got my toes did for spring, and ventured off to this joint to try the noodles after a billion of my friends recommended it to me. When I walked in the door, It smelled odd, like the chef was boiling his socks in a big cauldron, the stench lingering in the air with a hint of cabbage and soy sauce, but it wasn't that sort of overwhelming stench that sticks to you. Rather, it's the type that you get immune to, so after five minutes of sitting around you forget about the stench, until someone new comes in and has a not-so-fresh grimace on their face. Anyhoo, Service was pretty slow, and I decided to get the knife peeled noodles since that's what the waitress recommended, and I was pretty happy that they had a bunch of cilantro on the tabletop so you can garnish your entree just the way you want to. Fast forward 15 minutes - Beef Brisket with knife peeled noodles comes, and its pretty bland, the noodles are a bit gooey on the play doh side and I had to put Â about 2 tbsp of soy sauce , a tsp of chili sauce and a handful of cilantro leaves to give it any flavor, Hell, I could have put all those things on an old shoe and get the same taste! I mean, the price is good, but the hand pulled noodles on East Broadway are far superior ( Â though the hole in the floor at that joint scares the shit out of me)
Great food!!! Good for brunch.
All of our dishes were amazing. The best ess the chorizo over playfully pepper and toast topped with fried quail egg and manchego. Highly recommend!!

I am terrified of head cheese, as is my mother. Â So, being a massive douche, I ordered us the Lam'bretta and a Super Cub Classic, sans head cheese. Â The guy working the register replied, "Are you sure? Â The head cheese makes the sandwich. Â Do you want to taste it first?" Â So, we figured, what the heck? Â We took him up on the offer. Â The delicately thin slices of meat he gave us looked nothing like the floating bits of meat in gelatin that I so despise. Â It was light and spotted with various shades of pink. Â The taste reminded me of a less dense version of kielbasa. Â Excellent. Â We ordered a Super Cub WITH head cheese. Super Cub Classic: Â Considering there is four types of pork in this sandwich, it was not as meaty-tasting as I was expecting because the slices were paper thin. Â It was surprisingly light with many layers of flavor, best appreciated by chewing slowly and savoring the bite. Â However, it would've been better with a little more meat on it. Lam'bretta: Â Holy moly, words cannot describe the explosion of flavor and spice that filled my mouth upon the first bite. Â The spicy mayo on the carrots blends perfectly with the curried grease dripping out of the tender lamb shavings into the warmed, crusty bread. Basil Limeade Fizz: Â Refreshingly citrusy with a delicate fragrance of basil. Â I would love one of these on a hot summer day. Iced Lychee Green Tea: Â Tastes exactly like lychee in liquid form. Â It had a full-bodied flavor and was very interesting. Â I'm not a huge lychee fan, so I obviously preferred the limeade. Â But, I can see a lychee lover relishing this drink. Overall, really really excellent and unique sandwiches and drinks. Â The staff is also incredibly nice and clearly care about their food. Â I have every intention of returning to try their whole menu.
Great for brunch, lunch or dinner. Didn't know what French-Mexican fusion would be, but it ended up awesome. Definitely give this place a try. Also $1 oysters during the week so that's always a plus.

I do not have one complaint about this place. Â Every time I'm here, the food is spot on and delicious! Â When I have friends in town, we have brunch here. Â Date night with the boyfriend, we have dinner here. Â I personally love the french toast for brunch and the duck meatloaf for dinner.

One of my friends told me De Mole was rated one of the top mexican restaurants in the city recently. It is great. They use fresh ingredients, the salsa looks like it was made 5 minutes ago. They have interesting vegetarian option you typically dont find like Seitan (wheat meat), Spinach Burritos and Nopales (grilled cactus). Its a good spot with good service, wait staff is always inquisitive about your needs and ready to answer any questions about the menu,. Theres a line around the corner on the weekends but I would try and go during the weekday to avoid the crowd. Ive been going here since it opened its always been clean and fresh tasting. My only drawback is the location. It must be the only restaurant on the street and there some bodegas around that about it. They did a good job with what they had with the interior decor but if they secured a location on Queens blvd they would probably have too much business, Beer and wine only. Theyre sangria is tasty and so are their desserts. Highly recommended
3.5 stars good ambiance, good beer, good service. burger was ok, too much mayo and nothing worth remembering. waitress got our beers wrong once or twice, but we drank them anyway. will return maybe.
Amazing! I could eat this every day

Loved this place! A real gem in the strange pre-gentrified industrial urban stretch of Red Hook. Tasty simple food but very good lobster. Really makes you feel you're somewhere small-town by the seaside - and of course you are right by the water, but in industrial Brooklyn. Worth the walk.

Went there for Sunday brunch. The wife and I got Sunday roast. It was great, although the steak was a bit tough for us. Friend got tomatoes on toast ( which does come w eggs). I had a bite of that and it was great too. Drinks were nice. Selection looks good. The place is nicely decorated and good atmosphere. I recommend.
A very good, solid place for brunch, though nothing particularly special. Order the mimosas!

So sorry, yelp friends, I realize I've been neglecting my yelp duties a lot lately. Â Going Â through a tough transition from SF to NY, which aint all that Â bad, from one great foodie place to another... At any rate, what better way to kick off NY than with one of the most popular pizza spots in the land of pizza spots, Grimaldi's - the pizza institution under the Brooklyn Bridge. Â  I must say, however, my expectations got the better of me this time around. Â My pizza fell a little short, though I have a feeling that my expectations were way too high, given the hype. Â The good news is that the pizza came out blazin hot, with steam flying off, but the cheese was a bit bland and the crust on the tough side. Â  I realize I'm the minority on this one and perhaps I have to give it another shot...and I plan to (they're opening several spots). Â So call this a temporary three stars, until my next visit proves me wrong. Â  After all, if first impression is everything, I probably wont be married and would have no friends. Â =) Â Fortunately for me, NY has no shortage of awesome places that the outlook is bright.

This is the closest I've had to hand-pulled Chinese noodles in the US (but not North America: that goes to the random noodle stand on the second floor of Pacific Mall in Toronto). The soups are flavorful and delicious. Â The dumplings are equally yummy with lots of veggies and come with a sweet sauce oozing with ginger. Â My one gripe is that the noodles aren't quite chewy enough: they were actually a tad limp and the non-uniform thicknesses kind of threw me off. The place cracks me up, though. Â It's tiny, you share tables, and the tiny hostess/waitress is hilarious with her screaming mannerisms. Â And did I mention the bowls of deliciousness are 4$? Â Swoon. I'll definitely be back. Â But not before I try Sheng Wang across the street! -edit- Sheng Wang is better. Â And Fu Zhou Re Ban Xiao Shi (144 E Broadway, incorrectly listed as Lan Zhou Handmade Noodle on Yelp) is MUCH better. -edit-

Best tacos I've had in Manhattan (I say Manhattan b/c better may exists in Brooklyn but i haven't found it yet). The tacos come packed with a bunch of flavor already but they have fresh toppings available on the counter should you need more. The tortillas are made fresh right in front of you, definitely recommend the corn over flour as it's more authentic. Even with Num Pang right around the corner this is best meal in Chelsea market.

I dined in for lunch during their opening weeks and had a wonderful time sitting at the chefs counter. Â I really enjoy how everything is so open so you can view your entire meal being prepared, see the raw bar and the cooler where they prep the fish as well as all of pastry. Â I felt the layout was very well thought out, creating a nice gap between the main dining area and the bar/kitchen/chefs counter which i imagine does a great job of keeping the more formal dining room much quieter during a full, prime time dinner service. As for the food, everything was beautifully prepared and presented. The grilled items are not to be missed, the sardines were complimented by the crunchy frisee, the salty lardons and a perfect balance of acidity in the vinaigrette (and the grill itself is a gorgeous piece, being a focal point of the kitchen.) Â I shared the whole black seabass with a friend but was a little surprised to have found so many tiny bones lingering behind. Â I guess that should be expected when it's advertised as "whole fish," but I figured they would be sufficiently cleaned since the fish was clear of all fins, it's tail and head. Â Not a big deal, but not so cute to pull bones out of our mouth while trying to be cute for your date. Â The flavor, however, was great with a nice bit of citrus and the fish itself was perfectly cooked. Â  Desserts also do not disappoint, the butterscotch pot de creme was amazingly decadent, the apple tart was perfect and beautiful (although I barely got a taste as my date didn't seem to want to share...) but the single most amazing thing I had was the honey-thyme sorbet. Â Seriously, I couldn't eaten a bucket of it. I also highly recommend trying a couple of their cocktails. Â The Tamarind Margarita (from my understanding making a comeback from Tabla's menu) is definitely recommended as is the "Scotch Bonnet," it's light, and the little stem of lavender makes it as adorable as it is tasty.. I can't wait to go back and try dinner, or just cocktails as they are staying open pretty late at the bar!!
they used to sooo good i went to 3 days ago in a long time it was awful! no energy or great wait stuff or even food.. so sad

Kefi is an awesome neighborhood restaurant in the UWS. Â Went here with a few friends on a Monday night without reservations. Â The place is huge, which is a rarity in NYC. Â We started with the selection of spreads and meatballs for appetizers. Â I honestly wasn't a big fan of the spreads, but the meatballs were delicious. Â I got the sheep's milk dumplings, which everyone raves about, and it certainly lived up to the hype. Â The dumplings (basically gnocchi) are so soft and pillowy. Â Prices are not bad given the portions and quality. Â Definitely a reliable go-to place on the UWS. Â Wish they had a location on the east side!

Had to order another #4. It was so yummy so get 2 from the get-go. Awesome manager Scott!! Full of life and so inspiring! #4 and #7 my favorite!! Smaller wraps so get 2, cheaper..try their chai tea.. Full of flavor and it's only $2! You will see me soon Kati roll! I will be back for sure!

We are having a good time going through all of the "Old School" Italian offerings that Queens and Brooklyn has to offer. Don Peppe's seems to be in the upper tier of these types of restaurants. We had a terrific meal there last night.. The room and the building is really nothing to look at .The dark, drab building reminds me of a strip club that might be along the side of Route 1, or Tonnelle Ave, or in some industrial park along a highway.. It's really nothing to look at. The room is just slightly better.. The high ceilings are it's only saving grace.. A really dated shiny wall paper, a bunch of tables holding large parties, a few 4 tops, all in a shmaltzy type room.. But, we are not here to eat the wall paper so, these things can all be looked passed.. The real exciting thing here is the food.. And there is tons of it .The place is set up for family style eating... No one is going to get their plate and sit down and quietly eat. .The room is boisterous.. Tables of 12, 18, 10 are sitting around sharing large plates of delicious food.. We started with their famous baked clams.. A very simple offering done perfectly.. Fresh bread crumbs, a little garlic, and some wine.. Broiled clams. .The clams come 13 to an order, out on an oval plate sitting in the wine and garlic sauce..Making a clammy wine bread soup.. Plates of lemon slices, about three worth, are placed on the table.. The clams were really nice. Male waiters serve you using the double spoon technique.. T Great way to start.. We moved on to the house salad.. Roasted red peppers, chunks of fresh tomatoes, lots of dried oregano, your basic vinegar and oil dressing.. Served in the large wood looking plastic bowls.. A standard in every Italian American home.. We then moved on to a plate of linguini with clam sauce.. This was stellar, exemplary version.. Huge whole perfectly golden brown cloves of garlic, tons of clams, dressed an al dente plate of linguini.. This was a thing of beauty. .Cheese and red pepper flakes served along side. Our waiter came over and skillfully served us from a huge plate.. A nice little touch... We moved on to a simple plate of Shrimp Luciano.. A dozen or so shrimp sitting in a pinkish sauce. Sauce was salty and finished with butter.. The type of dish where you would run the shrimp across the plate and it would take a minute for sauce to come back together covering the white line of the plate.. I was kind of disappointed when the dish arrived as it looked so simple. A plate of broccoli rabe might have been two whole bunches worth from a super market.. Cooked perfectly.. Lots more garlick.. At this point we were stuffed.. we finished with dessert and coffee.. We ordered a carafe of the house red which came freezing cold in a labeless bottle.. The wine was delicious.. Again, turning my preconceptions on it's ear... Chicken Chinese ,Chicken Scarp, Veal Parm, Veal Don Peppe, were flying out of the kitchen.. If we had brought a few more people, we could have tried these things.. Unfortunately, we were too stuffed.. I can't wait to go back..

Ate dinner there tonight with 4 adults and 7 (yes 7) kids and it was great! Had the pasta with eggplant and ricotta salata, spaghetti with clams, pappardelle with veal and mushrooms which was awesome, and some pizzas, and meatballs. Everyone loved the food, our serve was great, and they managed to accommodate us without a reservation! The best part was the Nutella pizza! Great lil place!
Great BBQ! Pleasantly surprised by the quality, would definitely go again~

Went with a party of 7. We ordered a variety of tapas and main entrees. All were delicious. Some of our choices were lobster guacamole, fried calamari, churrasco and arepas. The red sangria was delicious too. Service was good. Would definitely return.

tried this last night, got roast pork over rice, the large and man portions are way too big. there's something to be said for serving the right amount of food, not the most possible. long wait, and after eating a little i had to shit my brains out. something not right with it...

Wonderful food, nicely prepared with fresh ingredients. Restaurant is very clean, and a fun environment. Tuna tartar was amazing, white bean dip is very delicious, and the bison sliders were the perfect snack!

My husband and I came here around 3 on Friday and the restaurant was surprisingly pretty full even though we came at a strange time. I love sondooboo so I was excited to come here because the tofu soup house we have in Chicago is not that amazing. This places makes all their own tofu so I knew I was in for a treat. I ordered the beef and kimchi tofu soup and my husband ordered the seafood tofu soup and then we also ordered the small dukbokki casserole. It was the best tofu soup I have ever had. The tofu was so soft and creamy. I finished my entire bowl. The dukbokki casserole was great too. It was loaded with seafood and veggies and the rice cakes were nice and chewy. The casserole was so huge we had a ton of dukbokki to bring home with us too. Wish we had a tofu soup house like this in Chicago. Oh one thing though, my husband said last time he came here with our friend, they were brought a block of fresh tofu when they were seated. My husband said I looked to white and that's why they didn't bring us the block of fresh tofu with our banchan. Sad because I really wanted to try their fresh tofu. Oh well...

Fine! So food was okay but on a correlation of ambiance and service, the quality and flavor of the food are simply not THAT good to make up for the crowded space, loud and hot quarters, Â and virtually nonexistent service. We came on a Saturday morning. It was crowded but not insane. We were sat at a table for two elbow distance to four other tables. Since this is the East Village one can overlook this little detail. Immediately we start sweating. It must have been a 70-80 degree day but inside it must have been around 90 degrees in this room. I ordered the Poached egg on Potato Cake with Salmon and my husband the Eggs Blackstone which was supposed to come with orange juice. Two small regular coffees arrive (teeny cups, no refills). Followed by the food and the begging starts. My husband asks for Tabasco sauce. Three times. Ends up eating the eggs without because he didn't want the eggs to get cold. My dish included toast but on the menu it was not defined that it was rye toast. I had to get up and ask for wheat toast. The response? You should have said so earlier. Nobody asked!!! The "included" orange juice that was supposed to come with the Blackstone never arrived, although we asked three different people for it. We only saw our waitress twice: when she took the order and when my husband got up to ask her for the check. Horrible service for just okay food. There are a lot of better options in a five block radius. We will not go back!

$4.50 for a regular serving of fries. Poutine starts at $5. Basic condiments are free (Get the Especial {tomato, mayo, raw onions}), a billion other sauces for you to choose from. What is there not to love about potatoes that are fried twice? Mmmmm.

Nice restaurant with huge portions of well, ok thai food. I like the decor but it is very popular and the atmosphere is noisy :) I think that restaurant would be better if less populated since it is such a small place and always crowded the waiters let you wait...

We loved Gramercy Tavern. it is casually elegant, and everything was delicious. what a lovely cheese list, and i was surprised and delighted to get to try a Claudia Fleming dessert (she was consulting)....which i adored.

Yes, I know 2 stars is not the norm for most reviews I have read for Sushi Yasuda, but I have had WAY BETTER sushi experiences. Â Maybe it's because we are Californians and have great sushi in the Bay Area. Â We came here because of the great reviews, but did not find the sushi to be extra special. Â The service was impeccable, however, yet the atmosphere was sterile and pretentious. Â Small pieces, very expensive for what you get, and the sake selections were pretty awful. Â Also, they were selective about who they were turning away -- pretty arrogant. Â If you are looking for decent pieces of sushi and a good value, this is not the place to venture. Â The sushi itself, I must say, was tasty but not enough for us to ever return.

There once was a girl from New York With a great love of barbecued pork. Despite Jews' prohibitions She took trafe positions And did place the pork on her fork. Um, yes. Â I really like barbecue. Â So naturally I was psyched when Fette Sau opened. Â Now, as a rule, I have issues with NYC barbecue. Â Not because it's mediocre, although it is, but because of the incredible cult of preciousness surrounding it: the obsession with 'recreating' 'authenticity' and the innumerable self-conscious Southern trappings that ring as phony as the drawls in 'A Love Song for Bobby Long.' (Hey, I had HBO.) Â Go to the Bryant Park bbq fest if you want to know what I mean: hundreds of foodies, lined up for hours clutching copies of Saveur and relishing the authenticity of the experience. Down south, barbecue's just what people eat, the way we eat pizza. Â Some of it's good, some bad, but it's always unfussy. Â And you know what? Â I kind of like having something that we can't get in New York, that you have to travel for. Â You know how peeps are always prosing on about eating seasonally to actually appreciate the rhythms of what we eat? Â We're so spoiled in New York that we don't realize the same applies to the regional. Rant over. Fette Sau is okay. Â The atmo is very good - sepia-toned (my fave adj) and decorated with antique phonograph horns and other arcana. Â Bar seats are made from tractor seats (cool but v uncomfortable), tables are wood, there's a great bourbon selection and the food's cafeteria-style, served onto butcher paper. So far so good, but the pulled pork was meh - fatty, not very flavorful and utterly lacking in the unctuous melting quality of great bbq - the potato salad a bore, the beans forgettable. RUB, Dinosaur and Daisy Mae's are all better, even though this spot has em all beat for atmo. Â If your main objective was drinkin', with food an afterthought, I'd call this a superior choice. Â But even by NYC standards, you can do better for bbq.

The best -- and most inventive -- pizza I have found in Brooklyn yet. I've been there several times now, and it seems to keep getting better. They now have their liquor license, and are doing it up right with a good wine list and a solid variety of beers. I highly recommend it.

This place is CRAZY delicious. I first went there a few weeks ago and had the chicken platter (the rice and beans are off the hook!) and today I went and got the Cuban sandwich. This restaurant is the truth. Good food, nice people, great prices. Not the best looking place, but who cares? The food is bananas!

I love this place. Why can't all cities & towns all over the world have someplace like this? Food was even better than I remembered it. Iced Mint Tea is superMEGAwonderful (if a wee tiny bit overpriced IMO, I'd be happier if it were a slight bit larger [that's what she said]).

I really liked this place. The atmosphere and food were great. The waitress was very attentive although she seemed slightly overwhelmed. The boar ragu was to die for. The restaurant would have received 5 stars but for the fact they committed a cardinal sin: charging for a tea refill! An iced tea is $3 for a regular size. I was asked if I wanted a refill and said yes and was charged another $3! $6 for what amounted to 20 ounces of tea?! Sorry kids but this is Crown Heights - if you're charging 14-20 dollars for an entree a tea refill should be free. Next time I'll stick to the water.

This is the best restaurant in my neighborhood. It is tiny with a small bar in the front and a few cozy tables in the back. They don't take reservations so try to go early or a little later to secure your table. We have been here twice and got different menu each time in a matter of 3 months span. That means they keep their menu fresh and interesting. I really like their Burger. It is one of the best we have had. It is juicy, fatty and flavorful and a good size. I also really loved their pasta dish. It is small but very very rich. Their Octopus appetizer is small but also really flavorful. So is their Shrimp. We will surely be back for more surprises!

This is based on the new summer menu. I've had some good meals here, but my husband and I just paid $60 of our hard earned money on a tiny, poorly prepared meal. Skip the Mackerel- tiny, thin and tasteless in a soupy broth. The meatballs are pathetic. We had to fill up on beer and bread. The chef might be getting arrogant since there is not much competition in Flatbush/Ditmas Park area, and what can you do when you order an $18 dish that you could prepare better at home? The Chicharron was also a joke- Pork Rinds for $7! Go to any Spanish restaurant (owned and run by latinos of course) in Brooklyn and get better and cheaper. Will not be going back any time soon.

I came here one morning because of a recommendation by one of my friends. Â We had both heard VQ mentioned on an episode of Gossip Girl. Â I had a cappuccino and a butter croissant. Â I had heard that the workers had attitude, but my server was quite pleasant. Â Not long after that, my friend said that she was there and sitting next to Alec Baldwin. Â I will definitely return.

I was introduced to this place by my cousin who happened to be struggling to find a gluten-friendly restaurant for myself, as I am a Celiac. I was scared and was close to not accepting the invitation. I am so THANKFUL that he dragged me here! They had happy hour until 8pm, and every drink we tried was up to par. The calamari special was absolutely delicious! We had a few appetizers on the menu and I cannot complain about anything. We shared an entree, I believe it was the first one on the menu with the chicken and vegetables--also delicious! The service here is 5 star!! The staff was so pleasant always making sure we were okay and didn't need anything... the chef walked over to make sure we were content. She even surprised us with her specialty dessert! I am just so excited thinking about it that I am having trouble getting my thoughts out! All I can say -- a MUST TRY, even for Celiacs and the like!!!!! I am happy to say that I did not get sick and for the first time in a long time I was able to enjoy a meal with so many gluten free options! JUST LOVE THIS PLACE!

Love the vibe here. Great eggs, sandwhiches, beers, tartare and home felt feel. Friendly staff. Huge beer menu, quaint outdoor seating. Weekly pig roast. Go here and sit in the backyard, it's magical. Â They also do a pig head, some of the tastiest pork you will ever get your hands on.

The food alone potentially deserves 4 stars, but add the price/value point... I'm not sure Las Ramblas is really worth the hype. I came here on a weekday night with the bf as we were in the mood for something different, thus tapas sounded pretty ideal. As it was a weekday, we fortunately only waited less than 10 minutes at the bar for a table to open up. I say this because this place is teeny. I am actually shocked how much utility they are able to get out of the narrow space. I started with a glass of their red pear sangria, priced at $9/glass. It was too bad the bf doesn't enjoy sangria so much, because the small pitcher at $17 is a much better value. As for food, we ordered a few tapas to share: - Gambas san martin: this classic shrimp in garlic and wine sauce was very flavorful and perfectly cooked. The only downside though, was that the tiny thing only came with 4 shrimps, which made the $10 price tag difficult to justify. We ended up sopping up the delicious sauce with bread since it was basically a $5 wine and butter sauce. - Patatas bravas: these fried potatoes covered in a garlic aoili were as satisfying as one could expect from hot fried starch. I was surprised by how filling this dish was, definitely something meant to be shared. - Croquetas de jamon: these fried little balls filled with cheese and serrano ham were very good, it's no wonder just about every table around us had also ordered them. I'm usually a big fan of Italian arancini, and these kinda reminded me of that, but creamier. - Serrano and Idiazabel: this little ham and cheese board rounded out our other hot tapas nicely, and tasted especially good with my sangria. I personally found the serrano to be a little stringy, not as good as proscuitto which I generally prefer. The cheese was pretty good, not too sharp with some nuttiness from the sheep's milk. So as you can see, the food here is good as far as tapas go. However, almost $60 for tiny portions and a drink certainly isn't the best deal in this city. I think tapas places are good for groups looking to have wine with just some small bites, but I highly doubt any group larger than four could fit in here comfortably. As for me, Las Ramblas seems a little inappropriate for a date night.

This place is ultra good, cheap and they deliver. Downside of delivery is that you don't get to have the Banh mi after it has just been freshly made. The crunch of the bread and the warmth of the roll as well as the different temperatures of the fillings from jambon, pate, to pickled daikon/carrots enhances the Banh Mi eating experience. When everything has become the same temperature due to it being a sandwich, and the bike ride it takes to get to your house then you miss that experience. Not that the meal isn't good it's just not AS good. If you live on this end of Williamsburg, I'm sure you appreciate the fact that you have this option. In my opinion, Nam Nam's Banh Mi is better than Grand Banh Mi (now under a different name). The spicy is fire. The peppers put in the burn - if you like heat then do it. All the banh mi on the menu is good, the bubble tea is awesome (coconut or taro - both recommended), vietnamese coffee also solid. Really happy this place opened up. A bit regretful that I hadn't yelp-ed about it earlier but better late than never. Way to be delicious Nam Nam!

We went here for an early dinner without reservations. I noticed that they sat people with reservations in the nicer section of the restaurant. For those who didn't make reservations got sat near the bar. We sat near the bar. We made it with 3 minutes to spare and ordered the prix fixe. My daughter ordered meatballs for apps and pasta with Greek sausage for entrees and rice pudding for dessert. She liked the meatballs and pasta. I ordered the white bean soup but got the Kefi salad instead. Rather than returning it, I just ate it. It was pretty good! For entree, I got the grilled branzino. It was ok, tasted a little bit too charred for me. For dessert i also ordered the rice pudding. We were both so full that we had our desserts packed to go. My husband ordered pasta with pulled rabbit and he liked it. Service was barely there. We were served and waited by different people during the whole time we were there. Our waiter only took our orders. After that, he disappeared from the face of the earth, never to be seen again. That's ok. i didn't feel guilty leaving a small tip totalling 13%. I am giving 4 stars for the food. Waiter service is another story.....

This place topped it. Best Italian food I've had in NYC! I was really excited to find this place literally in my backyard and visited with a friend.
