We arrived around 6:30 and the place was pretty empty, so they seated us in the front. I liked the decor in the front area, they had some of those giant wooden tables that look like a horizontal tree as a table and a lot of people could sit there. I wish I had checked out the back dining room now that I've read more reviews but I will DEFINITELY be going back! Ambiance was cool too. It seemed laid back and casual but also could be dressy/fun, and the waiters were dressed casually but put together. Definitely liked the vibe. The service was great and the waiters very attentive (i.e. dropped my fork, waiter happened to be walking by, before I could say a word a new one placed in front of me) and they knew a LOT about the food. The dishes looked very complicated on the menu and had a lot of complicated looking Italian words and ingredients but I have to say the waiters were on par. Instead of just bringing out bread they also brought this seasoned white bean thing to top the bread with. This should have been a legit appetizer but they gave it for free. Yum! It was amazing, everyone would love it. My friend ordered the Papardelle with Wild Mushrooms. It was amazing! The pasta practically melted in your mouth, you could tell it was homemade. It was so full of flavor too and absolutely delicious. I was wary of what to order (warning, their bolognese has beef and veal so if you're not a veal eater steer clear) but decided to be daring and went with one of the pasta specials: Tajarin D'ortice which is fettuccine style pasta with mint, butter and sea salt. Wow was that amazing. It'll be hard to go back and not order it again and again. The portions were generous and midway through I was stuffed but couldn't stop eating! Everything was very heavy (keep this in mind) but so yummy. Can't wait to go back here.

Their black bean burger made California Style with smoked paprika mayo instead of salsa is the bomb.com The waitstaff is friendly and the service fast. I always get the fry-onion ring combo with my veggie burger when I go :) Â One of these days I will try other things like a salad , milkshake or dessert but I am often full cause their portion sizes are great!

I finally made it to this amazing little treasure of a place and now i see what every one is raving about. Â Some of the tastiest home made Italian food in the city. Â Besides great food - place is casual and very relaxed - overall very enjoyable. Â Can't wait to go back for more.

Great service, cramped but airy atmosphere, awesome brunch menu (seriously, everything sounds incredible), classy but not stuffy, reasonably priced (especially for that area). My veggie egg white omelet lacked flavor, however. Â But it was a very generous portion and I thoroughly enjoyed my hashbrowns and turkey bacon. Does not take reservations for brunch.

Went Saturday 7:30pm, no reservations. They told us 45 mins wait. We signed-up on the waiting list and went for a walk, not sure whether we'd come back. Nice walk to the pier and they called us taht they had a table ready within 15 mins of signing-up. The place is smallish, cute, resembling an old Argentinean almacÃ©n. The ambient is loud, warm. We started off with some empanadas (meat and corn and spinach), which were very good. Then we had entraÃ±a (skirt steak), asado de tira (short rib) and milanesa de pollo (chicken milanese). Finished with dulce de leche and banana caramelized pancake and chocolate fondant. All was VERY good and prices are affordable (I guess this is a relative term). Still no wines, but they do allow BYOB contrary to what I had read prior to going, or I would have taken some wine. There is a liquor store 1- 2 blocks, on 6th I believe. Bottom line: highly recommended, won't be disappointed, take your wine and enjoy the food!

Cafeteria has delicious food but takes itself unnecessarily seriously. The mac and cheese egg rolls are to die for, the burgers are mediocre, and the Cobb salad is top notch. I also saw Susan Sarandon here once! She looked great.

Finally gave Cafe Ghia a visit since being here in Bushwick now for almost 2 years. Cute and cozy and menu a pleasure. Everything though was super small (our table was too) and kept rocking back and forth. I guess it would help if I learn to eat in small portions such as what they serve but I'm from the south so brunch means to me getting full not eyeing the desert menu or looking to order another drink. The mocha i ordered was a bit tiny as was the OJ, everything was served in small glasses or cups. The Rachero egg dish I ordered was really great but looked so small on the plate even w/the bacon i added extra to it felt more like an appetizer. Will I visit again, probably if I'm in the mood for happy hour or something w/someone but it's unlikely I'll do brunch.
Curry was ok, but lacking veggies like whoa. If you get the classic, order meat on top, or to-go!

Pizza was a lot bigger than expected and wasn't greasy at all but I found it to be not as tasty as some of the other slices I've Â tried in the city. I really think it was the sauce, it just tasted a bit bland to me. It also took at least 30 mins, probably 45, for our small pizza to come. The place was packed but I still didn't understand why it would take so long given how fast those pizzas cook. Overall it wasn't worth the effort to me given how quickly you can get great slices in NYC.
Great place, and love it on Sundays when they have unlimited sangria's! it's a great deal and the food is delish.. and the little breads that they bring before your meal are the best thing ever.

I ordered the Cajun style Chicken Sandwich with Buffalo Tots meal yesterday. Â The best part of the meal were the tots. Â The sandwich was mediocre. Â When I order a sandwich at any restaurant my expectations is to see all the ingredients placed within the bread and not sitting on the side unless requested. Â Since this place is actually bar food I really can't give it a lower rating, it's okay for what it is.

Cobble Hill classic. A reliable choice for bahn mi, vermicelli noodle salad, and pho. Consistently delicious, reasonable wait/delivery time, relaxed atmosphere. A definite in-and-out environment, this is neither a gourmet stop or a particularly authentic experience, but is always delicious and satisfying. I usually go for the classic bahn mi or vermicelli with tofu and have yet to regret my decision.
Food was amazing as always and topped off by incredible service. Â Have always had an amazing time when going to Gramercy Tavern.

The BEST MIDDLE EASTERN food in the city. A street cart. Who would've believed... You've seen those around the city, you've tried a couple, but none of them even get close to this. WOW! Discovered completely randomly, The nicest guys, very cheap, and super delicious. Everything i've had here was done exceptionally well. I always go with yellow rice and everything on top. Can be a bit spicy so if you have Â a sensitive stomach don't do the hot sauce, but the salad is fresh, the rice moist and flavorful, and the meat, any meat, TASTY TASTY! This is also great for an "experience", as in taking the train out to queens and walking around.

I ate there last night, and the entire meal was executed beautifully. The meal pleased my palate and engaged every sense. We did the 10-course with the wine tasting and I wish I would have written down some of the wines. We had the pleasure of meeting the chef and the passion he pours into his latest restaurant is evident in the dishes he serves. There was not one course that did not stand out on it's own merit. I enjoyed the meal immensely and will definitely be returning. It is worth a visit.

this was a super disappointing experience. i had waited so long to try this place and literally wasted away before my food came because i was so hungry. there was a wedding party going on outside and it seemed like ALL of the kitchen staff were focused on making their food. we had the heirloom tomato salad to start, then sweet potato ravioli and cavatelli with sausage. heirloom tomato salad was pretty good but fairly pricey at around $16 the cavatelli was of good quality and i could tell it was freshly made but it somewhat repulsed both of us by being in similar form to maggots. not appetizing. especially when you have waited 45 minutes for your entree to be served and you are the hungriest person alive. sweet potato ravioli....there were like, 5 pieces of ravioli on the plate. not impressed. my boyfriend ordered the 'bugatti' drink. it was one of those drinks that sounds great on the menu, then it gets to your table, you take one sip and you're like "ok, that was enough....i wish i never ordered this" and then regretfully sip it until it's all gone because you know it was like $13 or more. Â  i must say, service was decent and our waiter could probably tell that everyone around us was also agitated by the slowness of the food. i don't think i would return considering how much the meal cost given the fact that i was still hungry after i left, didn't really enjoy my over salted sausage and spent much of the time aggravated at the slowness of the kitchen. sorry frankies, i wanted to like you but you made it pretty hard!

I've been here twice for lunch. Â Interior is very interesting, really cool decor. Â Food is delicious, portions are not shy at all. Â Staff is friendly and attentive. Â  Mozzarella and tomato antipasto was awesome - definitely get it.
Great falafel! It was only three dollars for a sandwich and it was honestly the most flavorful falafel that I have sampled in the city. It was only 3 dollars too!!

The food was amaazing! It was fast and freshly made. The storefront is nice and quaint. I love to see small businesses with wonderful dishes and friendly staff sprout out of nowhere. The red velvet waffles were just splendid. I think I'll be visiting this place every time I get the chance. They menu is as broad and vast as the grand canyon, corny right? It's the only analogy I could muster after eating such a fantastic meal. Now I need a nap. Napoleon is a little more expensive than I rated it but it's definitely worth it. Keep it up guys!

Always a great dining experience. The food is great, inexpensive, and more than just regular diner fare. They have mango-walnut waffles, chipotle chicken omelettes, and a wide variety of other great foods. The wait might be a little trying for those who are impatient, but it's never too long a wait. On the super generous upside, you can often expect a bevy of snacks and drinks while you wait. There's been coffee, water, sausage, bacon, melon, strawberries & cream, cinnamon toast, and plenty of other great treats. Â And to make it even better, it's all free! After the not-so-long and none-too-arduous wait you're usually greeted at the front of the queue by Gus, (presumably the owner) who makes sure that you're doing ok thus far and will lead you to your table. He often pops up later on in the meal just to make sure that everything is just right. Which it is. It's decorated sort of like a T.G.I.Friday's might be, with "a lot of crazy crap on the wall" but each item that's placed there has been done so with purpose and care. I'd give it five stars but they're not open on Sundays. I've heard that the Suzanne Vega song is about this place, but I've also heard that it's about the Tom's on 112th. (Wiki says it's the 112th, but whatever) oh. Also don't forget the egg creams, they're worth it.

The Greek is really, really good. However, they recently changed the setup so that the bread and spreads you got before your meal are now a $12 appetizer. Not the biggest deal in the world, and still worth ordering (the spicy feta spread is particularly good). Definitely recommend the Brizola for a main course. Sometimes, they're a little slow, so don't go if you're on an intense deadline. Honestly, just go there and enjoy, it feels very European and is a nice break from fast-paced New York sometimes. I've told multiple friends to go and try it. Really good food and wine, and nice people who work there.
A tourist rite of passage.

Went here for brunch over the weekend. Â It is a cozy French restaurant that is perfect for a lazy weekend - do not come here if you are in a rush the service here isn't "quick" as American standards dictate. Our server was friendly but seemed a little overwhelmed or he was new, not really sure which. Â Either way he did know the menu and we got our respective orders. Â  Onto the food!! My friend opted for Eggs Benedict while I got the Southern Fried Chicken. Â I know you're thinking why the heck would you get fried chicken at a French restaurant - but trust me DO IT! The eggs benedict were good but the chicken was tender and had the right level of crunch. Â It was over a bed of sautÃ©ed kale. Â The crunch of the garlic only amplified the flavor of kale. Â Oh and the best part it came with a side of Mac&Cheese!!! The Mac&Cheese was just cheesie goodness, I'd go back just for that. The only reason I gave this place a 4 vs 5 is that the breakfast drinks weren't so great. Â They have fresh squeezed juices that are mixed with alcohol. Â I got the Hawaiian Sunrise - mix of freshly squeezed orange, carrot and vodka (I think I'm missing an ingredient). It sounded like a great breakfast drink and I was so excited to try it but the whole time it felt like the vodka was separating from the drink. Overall this place is great for a lazy Sunday and I will definitely be coming here again. Â Next time I'll stick to a mimosa though.
only been here for brunch (twice). Â The best brunch I have ever had in my entire life. Good service.

Ward III is one of my favorite watering holes. I've been coming here pretty much since they opened and the only thing that has really changed is that it's gotten a whole lot busier. It's unassuming from the outside and inside it's a lot of candle lighting, exposed brick and not-too-loud music. Pretty perfect. The bar gets crowded quickly around happy hour and beyond - it's popular with work parties - but there's a couple of small sofas up front and a good number of tables in the back. The staff and management are always polite. There's been a number of times where, after waiting a while for a table, one of the managers has brought us tequila on the house. Â Additionally, the bartenders are always nice, friendly, and know what they are doing. The food is a whole lot better than regular bar food here. The winners? Smoked gouda + caramelized onion quesadilla, sliders, mini pulled duck sandwiches, and sometimes they do these amazing lamb tacos. Drinks? Pretty much everything they make is delicious and inventive. Their drinks do not play around (taste or price-wise) - this is not watered down cheap stuff; specialty cocktails are strong with a definite masculine edge to them - usually what's needed after a long week. Personal Faves? For when you're in a darker mood: Tortuga, Hell Bent for Leather + the Kentucky Devil. On brighter days: the Angel Zakir. They've also got a nice wine list by the glass, medium to kind of expensive pricing, with some being upwards of $12. This is a place I hope stays around for a while...

I joined Yelp specifically to give this place 5 stars. The food is totally delicious (the bruschetta is totally extra terrestrially delicioustown!) The service was amazing- the waitress and the busboy were attentive and polite. Â The place is also just really homey and comfy on a early winter night. Â While waiting for the bathroom, I admired all the children's drawing on the wall. Â You know when a kid draws a picture of pizza and he or she writes "I LOVE YOU" they ain't lying. Â  Go get some!

Some amazing cocktails - check Great food - check A Backyard for summer drinks - check Wonderful people - check Bushwick vibe - check One thing that keeps it from being 5 stars - check** **The Narrows has by far the worst bar stools in all of Brooklyn. Yup I said it. Now they are pretty, they look wonderful with the backdrop of the space, but they are so so wrong. Well unless you are over 6'4 in which case you might be ok with them. They have no backs, are super high and have no footrests. Even my tall man friend had his legs dangling like a 3-years old. They have a slight dip in them as well. You can't adjust how you sit what so ever.... like I said worst bar stools in Brooklyn. So for that they lose a star, that's seriously how terrible they are.

Just amazingly not worth it. Â My friends and I got here at 7pm on a Thursday and were told the wait would be 45-60 minutes (so no, you don't magically avoid a wait by coming for a weekday dinner; we were told they were packed as soon as they opened at 6pm). Â Ok, we thought, we expected a wait and 45-60 is annoying but not psychotic. Â And it's totally going to be worth it, right? Â For the "best pancakes in NYC"? Well, an hour and 40 minutes later, we finally sat down. Â I'm a big proponent of 'under promise and over deliver', so if you tell me 60 minutes max, you damn well better not go 40 freaking minutes over that. Â I will say that the hostess apologized, as the people at our table-to-be just. wouldn't. leave. after they paid. Â But still - if you're not going to take reservations, your wait times better be very close to dead-on-balls accurate (it's an industry term). Â  Anyway, at least we were finally seated. Â The biscuits were warm and good I guess? Â I don't really know, we devoured them so quickly. Â Well-versed in the menu due to our wait, we ordered right away. Â I had the eggs benedict, and my friends had the turkey chili with cheese grits, and the fried chicken special, and we shared a plate of the chocolate chunk pancakes. Â At least that's what our waitress told the kitchen. Â We were instead brought the special pancakes (with crunchy bananas and a chocolate-chili sauce). Â After the wait, we were clearly not about to accept an incorrect order, so we alerted her to the mistake and she let us keep those pancakes and quickly brought out the correct ones. Â Great! And now to the food. Â The scallions on my eggs benedict were a nice touch, but the eggs themselves were soft-boiled, not poached. Â Really, you can't poach an egg? Â You guys were on Food Network. Â My friends' dishes were fine, but nothing to be excited about. Â  And the pancakes? Â Just....nothing remotely special. Â Actually pretty bland and flavorless, even with the chocolate chunks. Â Remember too that we tried two different sets of pancakes due to their mistake, so it's not like we just got a bad batch. Â They were just so disappointing. Â We all looked at each other like, that's it? Â That's what we waited all night for? Â What in the hell are people talking about? The great thing about NYC is that there are a million places where you can A) get seated right away, or make a reservation, and B) have amazing, memorable food. Â Sad to say this place offers neither. Â You want great pancakes? Â Go to a diner, or even IHOP. Â Yeah that's right -- IHOP has better pancakes than this place. Â  Save your precious time. Â Cronuts are NOT WORTH a bajillion-hour wait, and neither is Clinton St Baking Company.

This yakitori establishment is as close you'll get to the real thing in japan. Â  Â Their chicken is cage free / organic and you can really taste the difference. Â Do not miss out on the chicken knee bone (their staple) and make sure you get there early because it is very limited and is usually all sold out by 6:30-7 pm. Â Everything on the menu is pretty much amazing and I couldn't have asked for a better yakitori in nyc myself. Â The fresh grapefruit shochu is a must try as well. Irasshai!

First, tiny and noisy place with open kitchen banging and crashing away during dinner. Takes a minute to learn to ignore all that noise. Second, this place so laid back. The service was casual and friendly and they act like they need the money to pay the rent or have to go back to work at something far worse. They made us feel like they wanted us there! Food is good. Fresh. Four star gourmet? That's not why you came to this place, i hope. Totally relaxing fun dinner with your pals with good food - ah, yes, no probs. I liked their funky pate. I liked the tomatoes on the ciabatta - big chunky fresh- tasting nicely marinated jobs. I liked my pasta. Left smiling and if there weren't a zillion other eateries I'd go right back.

Ippudo was excellent , especially Â Ramen Noodles were very good.I would Highly reccomend Ippudo for Ramen noodles and some side dishes. The broth had really good pork Â flavor to it ,but after you have the Ramen you fell extremely thirsty.

After casing Vekslers for the past few of months, I dropped in on a recent snowy night thinking, this will be the perfect spot to cozy up to the bar, try the much coveted Pork Belly or a Burger and a pint. I walked in to a pretty empty restaurant, took off my three layers of jackets and sat at the bar. Â The bartender looked at me, turned her back, and fiddled with something on the back wall for a solid five minutes. She finally turned and dully said, "Drinks or food?" Â  "Both," I replied, and she dropped a menu. Â What I wanted was a beer, but she was someplace else. I sat there, to no music and what seemed like all the lights on, and realized after a total of ten minutes, Do I really want to be here? Â No, so I got up and left. Â  Way to introduce yourselves to the neighborhood! Â What I wanted to be my favorite new neighborhood joint will probably be closed in the next 12 months.

This place is terrible. Â The service is painfully slow. Â Our order came out wrong, and the waitress did not handle it well. Â The ambiance, decor, and menu are all lackluster. Â If you're in the neighborhood, do yourself a favor and walk one more block to Mile End or across the street to Fast & Fresh Burrito. Â  The food and service at both are excellent, and even though Mile End often has a wait you will still get served faster than at Bijan's.

Had a small get-together here with firends. Was drawn immediately by the unpretentious/rustic atmostphere--quite unexpected, especially for the neighborhood. Between the four of us, we shared 2 appitizers--fluke sashimi and their special of the day, Hiramasa Tartare--and both fell just slightly short of flavor. The Chicken Under the Brick (for 2) came highly recommended, so another friend and I shared it for our Main Course. This was indeed great, crispy on the outside, well-flavored and moist on the inside. Incredibly satisfying on a chilly night. To sum it all up, I would come back, as the overall experience was great.

Sorry New Yorkers, I come here for the grilled pork over rice because their pho is just ok, okkkkuurrrr? Nothing to shout about unless you've never eaten pho anywhere else. That being said I love the efficiency of this place. They are usually taking your order as you're walking inside the restaurant. I actually call ahead of time because as a starving NYU student, ain't nobody got time for that nonsense when they are packed to the rafters. Food is fresh and portions are ample for $9. Works well on a student budget and location is perfect for those times you're stuck at the Bobst Library. Seating is kinda limited and there is no place to hang your coat in the winter. Just bring your takeout to Kimmel.

I came here in for lunch I think on a Friday, can't remember. Â Had a nice time, the food was simple, filling and good and the beer was delicious. Â I agree, good music and decor! Â I'd be there more often save the long trek from Greenpoint.

It's was my first time eating Pinoy food and I wasn't disappointed. Â The pork belly is amazing and the fries were good too. Â It is pretty heavy and fried though and sparse on the veggies, which my Filipina coworker says is normal.

Had a great experience here. Â Food was outstanding. Love the open kitchen. Wine list was fantastic. Â Bar tender was great (let me try the mead before ordering a glass - they have a mead selection). Nice vibe to the place. Â Service was just how I like it: Polite and unobtrusive, not detracting from the evening at all. Â I will be coming back.

We came here for Korean Restaurant Week on a Saturday night. I thought the staff was amazing. They were really attentive, helpful and nice. They gave us free $13 fried chicken wings for the table. When we spun the Â wheel we got something we did not want, so the host was nice enough to change it for us. However, I was a bit disappointed in the food. I don't know if it is because we chose the $25 restaurant week menu or what, but it is definitely more Asian fusion than Korean. The Korean flavors were too mild and you couldn't really tell that you were eating Korean food. The Makgoli that we got was amazing though. Fresh Apple Makgoli. I definitely recommend this drink to anyone.

I used them to cater my "first day at the new office party" for my staff of 120 and they did an unbelievable job! They were on time, their packaging was great and the all in containers made it easy to give out. Most importantly everyone loved the food. We will definitely use them again.
I just have to tell you I am in love with place. It really makes me want to move to Brooklyn. It is the best handmade pasta in park slope. Also very reasonable and the chef and owner is do friendly

I finally hit up this place a couple of weeks ago, and being someone whose mother can fry chicken better than most any place you will buy it, I was prepared for disappointment. Â But, to my surprise, the chicken was kickin'! Â The crust was flavorful and seasoned just enough. Â The off-the-bone piece of breast meat, which resembled Meat Wad but in chicken form, was amazing. Â Chicken breast is tough to fry to perfection, where the meat is actually still juicy and not dry, but they got it right over there. Â there was also a delectable wing and a thigh (naturally) in the chicken box order. They ain't scurred of shortening and/or butter in the biscuits either. Â These dense masterpieces are a cross between flaky style biscuits and buttermilk style biscuits. Â Honestly, I could have had that and the chicken breast plus my side and been a happy camper. My mac and cheese was scrumptious. Â Next time I will opt to go without the squirt of Buffalo wing sauce on it. Â Personally, that doesn't do it for me on mac and cheese. Â But it was well-made and reeked of comfort food. For dessert, I had a banana pudding pie deal that I had a conniption over. Â My Southern roots make me an automatic expert of banana pudding (well, really, all of this stuff), and they nail it. Â I can't wait for another cheat meal day so I can go back. The price seems high for fried chicken, but I am growing used to this in NYC. Â Still, it won't keep me away. Â Like Arnold said: "I'll be back!"
Food sat very heavy in stomach. Very greasy. Flavor ok but nothing to write home about. You would do better to cross 6 th ave and get food from the Korean cart.

The food at Lupa is amazing! Ambience is wonderful as is the highly knowledgeable staff. I took the hubby here for his birthday and it was perfect, low key, yet homey and romantic. The octopus with farro and salsa verde was amazing and it continues to call my name. I ordered one of the evening special's, a papperdelle with duck ragu (if i recall correctly..amazing homemade pasta and the flavors were perfectly balanced. The hubby had the Braciola Alla Cacciatora, one of his favorites of which he said was one of the best he had ever had..a definite return visit..like i said, that octopus is still calling my name!

I came here for an event and had the opportunity to eat a delicious prix fixe dinner with some amazing people.. Great wine, great food... fabulous beignets... I would really like to come back again and try their full menu :]

Coco Chanel said "You can never be too rich or too thin." Â While I'm pretty sure she'd look down on me for applying this to a pizza review, POSTO pizza is both deliciously rich and thin. Â The rich part comes from the olive oil and cheese - ample amounts of both, yet not overwhelmingly so. Â The thin applies to the crust: think of a cheesy flat bread that's both crispy and crunchy with each bite. Â I am consistently amazed at how many toppings the thin crust can sustain without crumbling. Â The cheese to sauce ratio favors cheese, so if you don't want marinara sauce you can sub it out for pesto sauce. Â Heaven! Â  The salads are also really refreshing as is the House dressing. Â And the cheesy garlic bread makes you feel guilty about ever making the decision to order it. Â However, the pizza does not. Â You can order an individual pie and not feel like you've ever over stuffed yourself and compliment it with a salad. Â  So in the end, Coco would be proud. Â It doesn't put too much weight on me and doesn't break my bank account.
Been there once, it was ok.

I love a good omelet, but I hate that gross-greasy feeling you get after eating one too many eggs. Funnily enough, I didn't get that at Tom's despite eating my entire spinach and cheese omelet and plate of home fries. Basically, Tom's is good diner food done right, and with a charm and warmth (Really, what's more welcoming than someone bringing over a plate of whipped cream and cookies and forcing them on you?) that you'd be hard pressed to find anywhere else.
wow . love it went 5 days in a row , got 5 different dishes , impressed by all!!! Staff kept suggesting different combinations and all worked out Definitely a great experience , food and service!!!

The drinks here are so cheap they dont even need a happy hour. I came here with a huge group after work and the place was pretty empty. There were two bar tenders who were quick to keep the drinks coming. $3 for beers and $4 for well drinks, even when my well drinks were "gin, easy on the tonic" Fancier drinks, were just a mere $5. This is obviously an untapped resource in FiDi where anyone could be hard pressed to find cheap drinks. They also have food and there was a little old lady passing around Cheetos, which my group definitely appreciated as we kept downing drinks. I will definitely be back when I just need some solid drinks and dont want to spend a lot!

I've been going to Theo Gussy's Food Truck regularly now for well over a year and have never received a mediocre meal. Excellent street food and consistent everytime. In the pantheon of food stands, they are a five-star establishment.

Stone Park Cafe has a great brunch menu, once you put your name on the list they'll call you when your table is ready so you can run to the playground with the kids for 45m or head over to the farmers market for a few. Â Their outdoor tables are perfect in the spring, you don't feel like you're eating ON the street. Â Staff is great, coffee is good, and they have high chairs and (some) space for kids.

We stopped in GPH for their happy hour and taco special after having a great brunch experience recently. Â I ended up getting 2 tacos and 6 wings which hit the spot! Â The drink selection is simple and satisfying. They also have a spacious backyard which is great for groups.

After having dinner at the Greek, I now understand the perfect star rating on Yelp. Â They've really perfected the customer's experience and addressed ambiance, food quality, decor, cost and customer service. Â And they even make it look effortless. Â  This is seriously the PERFECT date night spot, with a live violinist and all. Â The dim, soothing light was easy on the eyes and there was no Manhattan hustle and bustle, just lovely folks enjoying a pleasant dinner. Â  We were starving and heavily considering ordering a cold starter with 4 different dips, but our server was quick to point out it isn't worth it since he was going to give us starter bread along with one of the dips anyway (which is organic and wickedly good) so he steered us in the direction of some hot appetizers (the Grandma meatballs and some Pite). Â We then decided to share the Kota Chicken as our entree. Â Every dish was A++ and I'd definitely reorder all 3 the next time. Â This isn't fast food so you might have to wait 20-30 minutes for some dishes, it's so worth it though. Â Portions are not large, but decent and regular-sized portions. Â  The above 3 items fed 2 ladies and we were pleasantly full (not stuffed) without any additional room for dessert. Â I'd recommend ordering additional item(s) if there are any males in the dining party. Â We were quite happy with the bill - not too expensive at all!

Is Sushi Yasuda a religious experience? No; for a religious experience, try sashimi in tsujiki market. Sushi Yasuda nevertheless serves the best sushi in the city. The restaurant itself is a practice of minimalism; in this bamboo box, your senses can concentrate on the nigiri and sashimi. Unlike Sushi of Gari and Sushi Seki, enough space between tables allows you to enjoy a brief respite from the bustle of midtown. And the food: the first bite will unleash your innter gastronome; indeed, savor the hedonistic time, as it ends all too quickly when the bill arrives.

A minor legend among locals and not to be missed if you're hungry and love a value (and copious amounts of curry and rice). Go Go Curry serves plentiful portions of thick, tasteful curry and perfectly fried meats for very reasonable prices, and there is very little chance that you will leave the place hungry if you get anything larger than the small size (which they dub a "walk"). For the ambitious there's the Grand Slam curry (~$12), which you should not eat if you plan on eating anything else that day. It's a massive platter of rice and curry, topped with a fried pork cutlet, a fried chicken cutlet, two sausages, two shrimp tempura, and a hard-boiled egg. Easily one of the best values in midtown dining! Great for lunch or dinner, but you may have problems finding a place to sit for lunch; the place fits more people than you'd think, but it's a popular mid-day destination. Luckily, you can take it to go.

GREAT TASTING PIZZA. FAIRLY PRICED. WOULD EAT AGAIN. This pizza does live up to its reputation. I was really surprised that it was only $14 for a large pie considering this is hailed to be the best. Extra toppings are 3 bucks extra. The tomato sauce was fantastic and the cheese was put on in a very old fashioned way. It wasn't covering the whole pizza so you'd have spots where it was just tomato sauce but it honestly was a perfect cheese/sauce ratio. My only complaint is the crust. Although it was tasty it was a bit tough. I had to put in a good amount of elbow grease to cleanly cut pieces to eat, and their knives are serrated. I asked for a coke to be brought out with the pizza, our server, who looked like a very tall stoner did not remember to bring it. Not great service but who cares it's pizza. Tip is included on the bill! This should avoid head scratching for those of you who like to check charges.
The food was absolutely delicious from the spinach pie to the lamb chops to the grilled octopus yum yum yum

Thanks Yelpers for finding this little gem. Visiting from California and got a seat at the bar otherwise the small place was packed. This place serves up fresh local ingredients, started with the beet salad with goat cheese which was a nice simple dish. Topped it off with the special, pork medallion stuffed with cranberries and walnuts then wrapped in bacon. Very tasty just a tad overlooked and a little dry. It came with parsnips, who new parsnips were so yummy! I want to go back and try the lamb shank. I'll be back...

Soups are really good. Only part that sucks about this place is the wait. The wait can be hours. They need to think about expanding Bc the demand is so high. I would come back if there wasn't always a wait. I had to share a table with strangers. The service is quick Bc they want you out so the next customers can eat. Not to say I was rushed but when we asked for the bills it came quickly. Our table was being cleaned and set up for the next guest before we left. It's worth coming back if you sign in your name first

This place is truly a gem. If the goal of the owners was a fun, festive restaurant they succeeded in grand fashion. From the decor, bright colored murals on the walls, to the music the space feels vibrant and alive. This where you go for after work hang outs and birthday parties. A key ingredient to a party is alcohol and Bogota has all night happy hour Mon-Thurs. I enjoyed my mojito. Enjoyed it even more because it was $5. Did it have a little too much mint? Possibly but it was still pretty good. Sharing food is another key to a festive atmosphere. Upon receiving my appetizer I soon realized this was designed to be shared. My chorizo appetizer was a mini meal. It could have easily been split between 2 or 3 people. The dish had 2 types of chorizo, sauteed onions and plantain chips and was excellent. I didn't know there were different types of chorizo but one seemed noticeably spicier than the other. While it's not a tapas restaurant I could see a group order a bunch of appetizers and sharing them tapas style. I did order a main dish, the shredded skirt steak (Ropa Vieja). It was fabulous. It was moderately spicy and the cut of meat was perfectly tender, not at all stringy or tough. I had it with the yellow rice and red beans which where good. This is a really cool place. The whole time I was dining I kept thinking, that this reminds of Boca Chica except larger. What I didn't like was no bread or chips on tables. There is nothing to snack on while you await your food. Not great if Â your drinking. They have chips with pico de gallo or Â guacamole as menu items. To me that seems petty which is why it get 4 instead of 5 stars.

The bar here is great. There is a tremendous collection of bourbons to try and great cocktails featuring bourbon. It can get kind of crowded at times and the place seems to be filled with (1) people on a first date and (2) huge groups of dude just getting off work. The bourbons are arranged on the wall in alphabetical order and you can ask for a menu with all of them with prices. They offer 1 oz pours of every bourbon for half of the price of the regular 2 oz pour, so do try as many as you can. Oh right, one last thing - they have good food as well.

Gosh, major disappointment. Â Thirty-five minute wait ended up being sixty minutes. Â The Eggs Benedict had a sparing bit of hollandaise; yokes were hard and the Canadian bacon, lacking. Â The potatoes were dry, tasteless - inedible. Even the bread had no substance. Â The Bloody Mary mysteriously became a GGBM with a mumbled confirmation by the server. The music - great if you're into clubbing at brunch. Not quite redeeming, but the French Toast was definitely memorable.
Food: 4/5. A must-go for noodle lovers :) Decor: 1/5. Not for tourists :( Service: 3/5. So-so... Price: 5/5. $6.50 for a big bowl of delicious beef noodle soup? Now that's a bang for your buck! :)

A friend and I waited more than 45 minutes to have brunch at Tartine. Asked if I could have a cup of coffee while I waited -- the answer was no. Once we finally sat down the waitress blessed us with her appearance. My friend asked for "dry" eggs. The waitress informed us rudely that they were too busy to take special orders. While the food was tasty, the overall experience let me knowing I would never go back. There are many wonderful gems in the west village where they actually appreciate your business.
Quick and inexpensive lunch menu. Lets not even mention how filling and flavorful everything is. I sat with a large party next to the massive chandelier... OMG! So beautiful

Delicious yakitori place. Might be my favorite, but all these places are beginning to taste the same to me. That being said, this place is DELICIOUS. The biggest winners here (just about everything is a winner): tofu, rice dumplings, beef tongue, chicken hearts, rice balls, etc etc etc. You just can't go wrong. Expect to wait if you've got a larger group and expect to spend a good chunk of change (greater than $25 per person) but expect to leave full and satisfied.

Finally! Â A place that actually gets it right with the decorations. Â It's all in the editing, people. In regards to the food and cocktails, I'm also a big fan. Â We started out by trying the crawfish boudain balls, and the watermelon punch. Â The boudain balls were amazing and not too spicy, so I could actually enjoy them. Â And much to my surprise, the watermelon punch was super tasty, instead of just super sweet, like I was expecting. Â It tasted like lemonade mixed with fresh watermelon juice. Â Sooo good. As for dinner, the boyfriend had the blackened catfish w/ mac & cheese, and I had broiled shrimp w/ lima beans. Â While I am a bit biased, being from the south and all, I still think this place was pretty spot on with everything. Â The blackened fish was cooked perfectly, and the mac and cheese was almost as good as mine ;) Â the broiled shrimp did have a lot of garlic on them, but they were still really good, and the lima beans were my favorite of all. Â I can't help it, beans cooked with ham just remind me of home. Oh, and the service was great as well! Â I even got my cocktail for free! Â Love this place, will definitely be back.

This is the best sushi I've had in NYC - the decor is sublime, the service is impeccable, and food is always delicious. Went here for a birthday dinner, and decided to order the omakase menu from the bar. We weren't served by Mr. Yasuda himself, but our chef was just as capable. We each had an appetizer + 10-15 pieces of sushi, and some sake. Favorites were the unagi and the toro, but everything was very good. Favorite aspect of the meal was how observant our chef was. He would serve us different pieces of fish, and then subtly observe our reactions to them before preparing the next ones. Eventually, he was serving each of us different pieces of fish based on his interpretation of what we would or wouldn't like, and he was totally right. I tried the pieces that he served to others, and didn't like them nearly as much as the ones he gave to me (and vice versa). Very well done! This is on the pricey side for sushi, but you can definitely go elsewhere in Manhattan and pay much more for lesser quality.

Very ecclectic vibe to this place, makes for very cool ambiance. They play all the jams. I called ahead to check on the wait time as they don't take reservations. We came in at 10:30pm on a Thursday night without any wait at all. We started with the Hirata Pork buns -what a teaser! We also shared the Asparagus wrapped with thinly sliced pork and rice cracker (special on the menu that day) -very good .. and again... a teaser! He had: Shiromaru Hakata Classic with soft boiled egg, bambu shoots, and pork belly. Expensive bowl of ramen with all the add ons.. So glad my ramen was better! I enjoyed (thoroughly) the Karaka Men with a poached egg. VERY SILKY. VERY DELICIOUS! Fantastically mouth watering. Not greasy, not overly salty like most ramen I've had. Definately the best Ramen I've had thus far. Drinks: Sapporo on tap (Yumski) and the Green Tea High (gross) For an extra $2 you can order more noodles -what a fantastic idea.. dont mind if I do. We were lucky we didnt have to wait, but I would definately wait to eat here and can understand why people do. Total including graduity came out to a shocking $86. Very expensive ramen. ... but very expensive very good ramen at that.

For $6, you can't beat the quality of flavors, portion, & convenience. A word of caution with the the hot sauce - a little goes a long way. I usually have a high tolerance for spicy stuff..but boy, did I underestimate their hot sauce! the BBQ sauce is also good, and of course, the white sauce (tastes kinda like ranch). Stopped here after watching Wicked & I'm glad we did. I didn't even finish half of my gyro & chicken bowl. :(

This is a great place. Their appetizers are out of this world. So far I have concentrated on the Baby Grilled Calamari ($8.50) and the Steamed mussels in tomato sauce ($9). The baby calamari is absolutely delicious. It is one of the best dishes I have ever had. I have had it several times and it is consistent. If you like Squid Sushi or Thai Squid Salad, you will love this dish. And for the price, it is one of the best values in New York. It is a very nice size, fresh and succulent. There are several other appetizers I can't wait to try, Carpaccio ($9.50) and Warm Octopus Salad ($9.50). I just can't get past the squid... The only reason I know about the mussels is that it is my wife's favorite. We have the house wine by the carafe, and it is very nice and very reasonably priced. The only reason I don't give Da Andrea five stars is that I have not found the right pasta dish. The pasta is homemade and very good, but I haven't found anything that knocks your socks off, like the squid. But I am going to keep trying!

I came here last night with my girlfriends. I made a reservation a week ahead asking for a nice table since one of them was visiting NY. When we came in the manager, who's the classic "handsome arrogant" guy had an attitude because we were 10 minutes late. He sat us down in a corner table close to the kitchen. All I read about this place was the "family" environment and fresh flowers everywhere, but to me the area we were seated in was an OK village restaurant, nothing special. The waitress was very sweet though and made us feel better after the cold reception. The coliflower was better than the calamari that lack of a sauce. The fettuccine with fungi and truffles were good but a bit dry to me since were Â a bit sticky. If they want to create a cozy environment should take a look at Il Bucco, where you really feel like you are attended by people who care.

My husband and I checked out Juventino last night for an impromptu dinner and were very impressed. Â We had been here for brunch before and that was good too, but dinner took it to a whole new level. Â Everything we had was delicious - perfectly seasoned, inspired plates using fresh ingredients. Â They even started us off with a beautiful cheese plate in place of the typical bread basket, and gave us an amuse bouche as well. Â The servings were generous and well worth the price. Â I Â highly recommend this place.

I went here for the first time this past weekend and loved it. Â I'll try to avoid using the word "perfect" too often in my review, but if it crops up numerous times, you're just going to have to live with it. Â In any case, this is what fine dining should be in New York: elegant and fashionable yet calming. Â You feel like you're in a secret hideaway that's an oasis of peace. Â The servers are friendly. Â They obviously care about the food and drink and making sure you enjoy the experience. Â Dinner took about 2.5 hours and every second was delightful. Â There are no velvet ropes. Â No annoying finance guys trying to act important. Â Just people enjoying a wonderful meal. We arrived and went down a long corridor that'd be easy to miss if we hadn't been looking for it. Â At the end of the hall was a doorbell. Â We rang it. Â A very polite woman opened the door and asked if she could help us. Â When we mentioned that we had a reservation, she knew who we were and smiled. Â We were shown to our seats at the bar. I can't recall if there was music playing. Â The noise level was very low. Â People talked in quiet voices even as they laughed. Â The space is small. Â There are only six seats at the bar. Â There are maybe 10 tables. Â The interior is modern and clean. We had drinks that were named Mint Gold. Â It was bourbon, ginger and a few other ingredients in a tall glass with crushed ice. Â It was refreshing and everything tasted fresh. For dinner, we ordered two small plates, a medium and a large. Â The first two were tuna poke, which was absolutely perfect. Â Little cubes of the freshest tuna I've ever eaten mixed with a light sesame dressed on a bed of baby greens. Â They gave us a side of the seaweed wrappers that sushi comes in so we can make your own. Â Or just eat out of the bowl with a spoon. Â The second small plate was uni croquettes. Â They were good, but with a menu with so many wonderful choices made with fresh ingredients, a fried croquette seemed to break up the rhythm of the meal. The third dish, black miso cod, was lovely. Â A real work of art. Â It came with pickled baby plums, shishito peppers and shitake mushrooms. Â It comes on a little carving board and is a wonderful arrangement of simple yet vibrant flavors. Â I had a bite of the cod. Â After that, the pickled plum. Â More cod. Â The shishito pepper. Â And so on. Our final course consisted of the washu beef. Â The waiter brought over a small bowl of French sea salt and told us that it was for dipping the beef in. Â But he advised us to try the beef without it first, because he didn't think it'd need it. Â He was right. Â The meat was tender, flavorful and perfectly prepared. Â It was served on a bed of crisped potatoes and garlic. I love this place and definitely want to go back. Â It's a gem and really sets a standard for what dining out in New York should be like. Â I can't wait to go back.

We had reservations and went at an earlier time for dinner. Â We knew it would be a long wait, it's a very popular place. Â The ramen was very good, it tasted fresh made and the broth had a good balance. Â Just solid ramen fare. Â It has a nice ambiance and a nice place to meet with friends from out of town to catch up and have dinner.

I've come here several times and have usually liked it, even waiting an hour and a half for brunch. Last night, a friend from out of town wanted to try it having never been. Dinner was good and can't say the service was terrible (although it's never that great or friendly). After paying our bill, we sat for a moment digesting and drinking the rest of our water. Apparently that pissed off our host. We were in the middle of a conversation when he abruptly came over, leaned in and explained to us that if we were all settled, we need to leave as he has people waiting for our table. um. I've heard of restaurants rushing you out of there, especially if they are bursting at the seams with people (which they weren't) but never has it been so rudely forced on me. I didn't realize the service ends as soon as I sign the bill. The food is good but so not worth this shitty attitude. That was pretty much my last visit there.
I eat this every time when I don't know what to eat. Yayyyyy!
Mmm mmm cauliflower gratin! Staff were great too

One of my absolute FAVORITE places to eat in NYC. A perfect place for a romantic date or just catching up with friends. There's always a great crowd, small and cozy place, awesome music, friendly staff.. and it doesn't hurt that the food comes in pretty generous portions! Unless you get a booth to yourselves, be ready to get extra comfortable with the strangers around you. It's nice that the place is small but that means really tiny tables and being squished with the other guests sitting about 10 centimeters away from you. Good for eavesdropping, bad for arm room. Please don't leave this place without ordering the CORN. A little pricey for nearly five bucks for two corns on the cob, but they aren't JUST corns on the cob. They're rolled (laced?) with cojita cheese and sprinkled with cayenne pepper... with a squeeze of fresh lime juice at your disposal. Warm and smoky right off the grill. An explosion of creamy, buttery, spicy and zesty goodness in your mouth. I'm getting giddy just thinking about it. ORDER IT.
Great value! It's been so long since I've seen great entrees priced this low. The salads are huge too. Not much for seating so don't come with big groups.

This great has a great wine list and an excellent place to go after a doc at the Film Forum. Came back here with a big group the last time and it was a good time had by all. Just make sure you make reservations.

Kooky diner with uniquely indulgent comfort foods. Â Feels like it belongs in Austin, TX. Â I came for lunch on a late Saturday afternoon, and the wait staff let me just sit and drink beers until we killed our case. Definitely bringing more friends next time.
It's always be busy so come with two or three ppl only. And be ok to wait. For a little. But its worth it!

I love their coffee, food, beer! Grilled cheese, apple cobbler and a latte hmmmmmm! Service could definitely be better, where do they find the ones who don't like to smile? Sunday brunch is crazy hour so expect some wait time in the middle of the restaurant...

.. Damned freakin' good! Visited on a Friday night around 7 pm as a last resort after we had issues with parking... Oh boy, I wish it had been a first resort! We were seated immediately in a kind of funky interior. Walls make it look like it was a pretty divey place, but the addition of crooked pictures, Christmas lights and such make it look like a pretty typical Astoria spot, but I'm not complaining about ... Astoria chic. I like it. Pretty nice casual joint. Our waiter was very pleasant. It was relatively quiet when we got there, but by the time we left, there were plenty of drunk people (BYOB but people brought a bottle of J.D.?) to pump up the volume. My mother got the "Voodoo Queen," a fried green tomato and shrimp po' boy. It was pretty good, but I wouldn't say it completely blew my mind. My mom really liked it, though. 4/5 I got the Sugarhill burger. WOW! This was awesome! Definitely recommend it. You'll get diabetes. And have a heart attack. But still. The praline bacon was awesome and the sweetness from the honey went really well with the honey. 5/5 My sister got the peanut butter and jelly burger. She's a pretty conservative eater and she asked us a dozen times if she should really get it, but in the end, she didn't regret it. Neither did I after that one bite! 5/5 The smore bread pudding was kind of boring. I wouldn't bother. 2.75/5

I came here with a group of 6 based on the review and it's one of my to-try places. The meal was good but nothing very impressive, I wonder if it's because we're all focusing on the conversation and didn't really pay attention on the food or not.

First place I ate at on a recent trip to NYC. Perfect way to kick things off! I had the cucumber sandwich and coffee; both were great. Chatted with the owner herself: really nice lady who gave us great advice above and beyond what we could hope for. Highly recommended.

Fantastic restaurant, the staff is very friendly and knowledgable about the menu and cocktails. The drink list is amazing and very extensive. Had the pork belly sandwich which was really tasty and had a little spice to it. Great little private dining room in the basement.
i love you guys!!!!!!!!!
One of my favorite restaurants in the world. Â Just had another great meal with some friends from Canada. Â A true dining experience

I miss working around this area so much just because of this place. The consistency of this place is remarkable. It's always the same. I usually start with my personal favorite, their meatballs followed with a panini, I can't finish this much but I just love to eat and taste their menu. Sometimes I'd get their sandwiches off the appetizer menu along with some bruschetta. You really can't go wrong with this amazing place. If you love Italian food, this is a place for you.

We just had our wedding reception there last week, and I couldn't be happier about it. Â Everyone loved the food, and the atmosphere in the carriage house was lovely. Â Also, the staff was very accommodating of the special requests we made. Â They adjusted the menu so we could bring in our own desserts, allowed us to use the garden area while nobody was eating there, and when we asked them to make mulled wine as a special offering, they made some of the best I've ever had. Â Also, the meatballs deserve to be famous.

After all the reviews, I was so excited. Sigh. So you can understand my disappointment once I actually came in and tasted our order. Per the reviews, we went with the bbq pork and pork belly. I am not sure which was which, but what i'm assuming was the pork belly was extremely fatty..like no meat and just fat that was literally breaking apart and becoming more of an oily mess than anything else once we attempted to eat it. Attempted being key here because my husband and I ended up having to spit most of it out. Â We also opted for a Vietnamese coffee and a bubble tea. Â The bubble tea was so sweet, again, we couldn't ingest, and the Vietnamese coffee was average. Not great, but not terrible. Â The radish and carrots were nicely pickled, but I was missing cucumber slices in mine and...just overall-between the inedible sandwich and the bubble tea I am not sure whether it was the food or the disappointment over the food that ultimately gave in a really bad case of ingestion on the way home....My search for some decent bahn mi on the east coast continues....

i LOVE the pastrami/corned beef reuben!!! SO delicious. oh yeah, the cheesecake is great too. :) If you're in NY and catching a show, you should definitely come by and try this place. Â is this something i want to eat on a regular basis? probably not (and probably not a good idea for your artery). Â but if you're like me, who's just visiting and staying in the area, and maybe not from an area that do a great pastrami or corned beef reuben sandwich, you should come try it!! plus, honestly the cheesecake is really truly the best ever. Â i can never eat a lot of cheesecake because i usually find it too heavy. but the cheesecake here is just right. Â not too heavy, fresh, and not too sweet either.
Amazing! Unique menu, fast service (once we were seated, at least) , friendly waiters and waitresses, not too expensive. I will definitely be going back! Â :)

After a less than awesome Korean dining experience at another restaurant the night before, plus another day of cold temperatures, we had to address a growing craving. The photos on Yelp sealed the deal - we had to check this place out. Cho Dang Gol exceeded our lofty expectations. We started with the rice wine, seafood pancake, and spicy pollock. They really hit the spot. I loved the fresh flavor of the vegetables - a different blend from many restaurants - in our seafood pancake and the cool crisp flavor of the rice wine. By the way, some reviewers complain they don't know what to do with things on their table. We found the staff most capable of answering our questions and making recommendations - and they were happy to do so. Next up we enjoyed a seafood stew and dolsot bibimbap. The flavors were robust, the textures fresh and varied. The tofu was amazing and one of the highlights of the meal. Yes, you don't often hear that but fresh soft tofu is a treat. Prices were quite reasonable for the quantity of food and location. The atmosphere is traditional yet bustling.the whole experience package is great.

After 3 months of late nights smelling other people eat Artichoke slices at the 1st ave L stop, i was finally hungry on my way home. Look, the pizza (artichoke and regular) were both freakin delicious and gigantic, but the guy taking orders was way too busy flirting with my boyfriend's sister to provide a non-obnoxious experience. But yeah i'll be draggin my ass back there for more flavorfulness. And I like their sign.

I organized a birthday party here for 15 people this past weekend, and it was an unparalleled success. The selection of small plates that continued to arrive made dining very easy. All the guests had to do was decide their next cocktail or bottle of wine. The service was top notch, and for a large group there was almost no drop in quality. The food is a notch above. Artfully prepared and presented, it brings the concepts of both "BBQ" Â and small plates to another level. Very, very well done.
Stopped by for a snack. Spotted the empanadas. Best decision I made that day. They were outrageously good. With a green sauce to boot. Only regret is not ordering more. Loved these empanadas!

I'm a fan. Â But lets get a few things straight: it is a dive burger joint. No frills, burger on a small paper plate, fries you order separately come on a small paper plate thrown in front of you. Squeezed into a booth. Â With that being said, the burger was good, small but really delicious. Â West village. Â Inexpensive. I'm a fan. Not sure I'd come back though as I live on the east side when I was jonesing for a burger. But nonetheless, I wouldn't not go if someone mentioned it though. Comme ci comma ca.

I've been coming here for years, and one thing never fails... xiao long bao (XLB!), piping hot soup filled dumplings (they come in crab and pork). I think Joe's has gotten a lot of hype of the years, but the pork XLB are consistently good. I prefer those to the crab ones, but I know a lot of people who love the crab ones as well. I usually pop in here and order a few orders of the XLB and that's it. The XLB here are slightly different than the ones served in Los Angeles and the West Coast. The soup in the dumplings is darker, richer, and has more of a salty soy flavor. Most of the XLBs in California have a clear broth in the dumpling. Both are good, but I would have to say they're different from each other. Anyway, I often get asked how to eat them. Here's how I eat them without managing to burn my entire oral cavity. I pick up the XLB in a spoon in my left hand and with my right hand i slightly lift the dumpling off of the spoon by the top (pursed part). I make a small nick of a bite in the upper portion of the skin of the dumpling. I turn the dumpling over and pour the soup out onto my spoon to let it cool. Then I eat proceed to eat the dumpling and soup together in one spoonful/mouthful. And there you go. My XLB eating technique. Try it out.
This place has an amazing vibe, i will definitely be back!! Drinks were delicious and music was great. I will try the food next time.

I appear to be on some sort of poached egg streak. Â Three times in two weeks have I indulged in the runny cholesterol indulgence. Â It was delicious - really a great mix of textures and tastes. Service was a bit casual, but felt appropriately French. Â Small tables and chairs completed the French cafe feel. Not necessarily a destination recommendation, but put it on your list if you're in the neighborhood.

The cafe con leche was wonderful - an unexpected surprise. It was one of the best that I've had in the US. There was no place to sit, but I found a park further down broadway to stop and sip it slowly. When I finished, I almost went back for another. I'm not often in this part of the city, but if I do come back I'll try to revisit this place... and maybe try one of their pastries.

Heard about this place referred from a friend. Â I'm from the area and decided to stop by for lunch and I had the shrimp house salad, clay pot curry fish and an iced vietnamese coffee. Â The house salad was something different I had never tried and it was good. Â The fish rice plate was spicy which was great for me because I love anything extra HOT! Â I did not see anything there to complain about. (Basically I'll come back again)

My life got a little bit cooler the first time I went to Lamazou. Â The fact that I can boast about an incredible sandwich and cheese shop 2 blocks from my house gives me endless amounts of joy. Â Now when people tell me " I just bought a beautiful loft in SoHo", I tell them "But are you within a 2-block radius from Lamazou?" Sucka! I win! Everything at Lamazou is FRESH. The bread (all 14 different kinds), the cheeses (100+ kinds), the meats (36 types/cuts) and the soups. Â I usually get the Bohemian, which has roasted vegetables, pesto, havarti cheese, vinaigrette and the usual lettuce/tomato, on Ciabatta bread. Â  If you're there, and confused about which sandwich to get (because you will be), and are feeling vegetarian for lunch, get the Bohemian! Â I've had other sandwiches from there and love them, but I have a special soft corner for the Bohemian. * Other cool things Lamazou has taught/shown me: + Port Salut cheese + artichoke and red pepper tapenade + whole wheat w/herbs Ciabatta bread + Beaufort cheese + PG Tips english tea You may not have seen me disappear, but I just stepped out to get some Lamazou action and finished this review 20 minutes later. * It's a life-style I've always wondered about, Bohemianism. Â Do real Bohemians still exist? Â I came across this interesting theory called the "Bohemian Manifesto." It divides Bohemians into 5 categories: 1) Nouveau:- bohemians with money who attempt to join traditional bohemianism with contemporary culture 2) Gypsy:- drifters, neo-hippies, and others with nostalgia for previous, romanticized eras 3) Beat:- also drifters, but non-materialist and art-focused 4) Zen:- "post-beat," focus on spirituality rather than art 5) Dandy:- no money, but try to appear as if they have it by expensive or rare items - such as brands of alcohol. I think New York is the land of Nouveaus and Dandies, despite the number of restaurants with "Zen" in the title that are always crowded. Â  I am officially insane and very, very bored.

Vegetarians, I am sorry, but this place isn't for you...Pork Pork Pork Â :) I am a second timer and now have my favorite dishes: Brussel Sprouts (this is seasonal), Steamed Pork Buns, & Pork and Foie gras terrine. -- Also the beer selection is diverse without being overwhelming. I like this place..A Lot

According to urbandictionary.com, smith is defined as "All around known as the slang term for normal, every-day, nothing special. " Â Whoever coined this term must have eaten at The Smith before because this place is remarkably unremarkable.
