Â Apparently Whitney Port, the forgettable cast member from the Hills/ star of The City eats here a lot. Â I would venture to say Whitney is very "smith". Â She's totally not interesting or unique at all, which why it is fitting that she apparently like to dine here. The crowd for brunch on a Saturday morning was huge and people were waiting inordinate amounts of time to get a coveted table at this place. Â Throngs of Murray Hill douchebags thinking they've truly ventured "downtown" filled the place - NEVER a good sign. Â Hopeful and hungry, I was quickly seated with my friend as we had a reservation made a few days prior. Â We were squeezed in inches away from our neighboring tables allowing for many potential elbowing snafus to happen. Â Who doesn't love being crammed in so tight that a sneeze would land in the next tables' food? The Smith provides your table with flat and sparkling water free of charge - unusual and nice! Â Once seated I was dying for a cup of coffee and our server went AWOL. Â My disposition started to turn south after that (cue up bitchy conversation) as I need my weekend coffee. Â We were finally greeted, orders taken and coffee served. Â Phew. Â Our food came and it was a whole lot of OK - I ordered the grilled chicken sandwich on ciabatta. Â It came with cheddar, tomato and a chipotle sauce. Â I think the chipotle sauce was mayonnaise-based and something I could likely whip on my own with ease. Â The sandwich was sized nicely and came with a plate of lukewarm shoestring fries. Â Pretty uninteresting for 13 bucks. I think my annoyance with this place is 1. the crowd and 2. the buzz it gets. Â Please convince me this place is special and I will reconsider my bitchy feelings toward it.

From the moment you walk up to this place, it's appealing. The restaurant is cute and cozy, with a beautiful back garden area. And the food is excellent. For appetizers, we had the homemade meatballs and the arancini. The rice balls were good, but the meatballs -- those were outstanding! The herbs they used in the meatballs were perfect, and the sauce is delicious. For the main course, I had the Fettuccine with mushrooms and my mom had the ravioli stuffed with spinach. Both dishes were great. I loved my homemade fettuccine. The mushrooms were so indulgent. My favorite may have been the ravioli, though. It was so unexpectedly light and bright. I don't think you can go wrong here.

Best damn empanadas... I went for a late breakfast and oh my god. I ordered: -DESAYUNO AMERICANO -MAMBO ITALIANO -SPICY CHICKEN Â  -Pineapple smoothie The desayuno americano was essentially a cheesesteak with scrambled eggs in an empanada and it rocked my world, the mambo italiano was a savory italian treat wrapped in fried dough, and the spicy chicken was just perfect. Everything had the right amount of spice and each bite was bursting with flavor. Â I went here last week, and I'm still thinking about it. Go. there. now!

The food here is great, but really the prices are a little on the expensive side. Also they have one of those guys who you have to pay to squirt soap on your hands in the bathroom. Minus two stars for that antiquated custom!
great mexican food in Queens! great food- well priced! recommend to all who are in Queens and hungry

I'm no expert in Korean food, but I've had my share of meh bebimbap. Went to this place on the recommendation of a guy I met at a bar in Williamsburg (thanks Mr. Han!). Who knew I'd get the best Korean recommendation from a guy at an Irish pub? Just got back from one of the most satisfying (I'm talking umami all over the place, people) meals I've had in New York. Their traditional pancakes are outstanding, and the kimchi soup with fresh tofu so flavorful and rich, you'd think someone poured liquid love into it. Â The best by far, however, is the black tofu, house specialty. It is pricey ($15 or so for four medium squares), but I can't imagine anything more worth it. I mean, really, why wouldn't you try something you've never even heard of? I think the reason this place has spotty reviews is that, as with most restaurants, they do several things very very well, and some only so-so. I thought the bebimbap could have been a bit more flavorful or spicy, but I think that's cause it was the veggie version; I'm sure they're relying on the beef to deepen the flavor profile. Anyway, ASK FOR RECOMMENDATIONS, and then TAKE THEM! You won't be sorry.

This place is good value and cozy in a Greek way! The fishes were very tasty - I had the red snapper, which was nice although a bit greasy. I would probably go back for their interesting appetizers or brunch. Note: The bathrooms were quite disgusting - any self-respecting institution should keep those clean. I know some of my dining companions will not go back because of this!

It isn't bad, but it isn't good. I've accidentally been twice. The first time I thought, "hmm, meh." Not a satisfying experience. The second time was based on yelp reviews and forgetting that this was the restaurant in the area I hoped to avoid. Upon arriving I thought, "blast you yelpers for leading me on." I will not be back. There is nothing to go for. The food is an uneven experience. The wine list frequently changes . . . like as you order. Nothing inspirational. It is neither a good restaurant with a few hiccups nor a terrible restaurant with outstanding elements. It is just mediocre through and through.

I absolutely fell in love with Eataly. Â If I didn't work in Midtown I'd be working around there only for the sole purpose of going in everyday for an espresso and some snacks. Â I've tried their meats, breads, desserts and home made pasta. Â It is absolutely a life changing experience. Â Try to get their and hour early to shop around and enjoy the smells, sounds and taste of Italy. Â  Last time I was there I purhcased a bottle of wine and ordered the sampler of meats and cheeses before our reservations with pasta section of the restaurant. Â I also def recommend trying the upstairs bar area.

Went there last night with a few friends from California who wanted to try some famous Brooklyn pizza. Originally they wanted to go to Di Fara's, but it is closed on Monday so we went to Grimaldi's as a consolation prize. Pizza was served in a timely manner. We ordered a pepperoni, onion and mushroom pizza with extra crushed tomatoes. It was decent, but nothing notable from the local pizzerias near Cobble Hill. Thankfully, there was no line last night which make it much better!

My husband and I were feeling quite ravenous due to the gloom of a dreary Saturday, Ofrenda was the cure. Three youthful, fresh-faced workers greeted us at the door with beaming slightly imperfect smiles, which only added to the charm. As we had walked three blocks in the muggy inclement weather, I was thirsty for a beer. The selection was wide and varied, they even had Presidente. The only man in my life enjoyed the Huevos Pochados, and trust me they were almost tastier than his huevos. Ay perdon. The skinny girl in me opted for the Chilaquiles Verdes. I was delighted because they tasted like the chilaquiles of my abuelita. Must try dinner soon.

Ha! Oh Yuca Bar, how yummy your mojitos are! I've been here several times just for happy hour drinks and left very very drunk. Beware - these mojitos are delicious but deadly. The kind that leave you wanting more and the next thing you know, you don't remember half of what happened that night. Oh I've had a many good experiences here. The food here is quite good as well. Tapas of good portions and great to share with friends. Drinks and good food - you can't go wrong with that!!!

The good: Â  Great Food for dinner and/or desert. Also, the location can't be beat. The bad: Â  Much too loud, and too cramped. Just a note: I hadn't realized that this place was only crepes, they are delicious, but just be aware when you go. My only complaint would be that it's a little cramped and MUCH too loud (we were farthest from the speakers and still screaming at each other) but the waitress was great, and the crepes were amazing. I got there a little early and sat by the bar, as well, where I was surprised to find two very friendly regulars who very much wanted to chat, and recommended the Coney Island brew; so that was nice while I was waiting. I highly recommend the ham, swiss cheese, tomato and spinach combo on the whole wheat crepe, though all the choices looked great. I would be weary of the King Crepe, just Peanut butter and banana, which is usually an old favorite, but for some reason was just WAY too much at the time. Enjoy!
greatest place I ever visited. service is great prices is right.happy that i found this places

As the number 1 Hot on Yelp for a few weeks now, this restaurant easily moved its way to the #1 spot on my list of "to-try-before-i-leave-nyc" in two weeks. Finally decided to go on a Saturday afternoon with my bf, probably around 2 ish for lunch. We waited around 20 minutes, which is pretty average, especially for a place that is so hyped up at the moment. Everything was as delicious as I expected. Balls: beef, spicy pork, chicken, veggie...special was: lamb. Sauces: tomato, spicy meat, mushroom gravy, parm cream..special was: pesto Get it either in a bowl, on sliders, mashed on a roll, or in a hero. We both got the hero, as we figured this was the best deal for your money. Easily the largest option for our hungry selves, and you get a little side salad with it. Â My hero was beef meatball in the mushroom gravy with mozzerla cheese. AMAZING. The wheat bread was perfectly toasted, fresh, and the meatballs laid perfectly on it. Bf had spicy pork with spicy meat sauce, which was tasty as well..and not really that spicy, just had a little kick...and I liked mine better :) Salad was just a bed of arugla with some apples and dressing. A nice, light side to the heavier hero. We also split a side of rigatoni, which was al-dente and marinated in a tasty tomato sauce. Pretty standard. Of course we had to try these ice cream sandwiches. I got chocolate chip cookies with vanilla, and he got peanut butter cookies with chocolate ice cream. Cookies were warm and just the right softness. Meatball Shop definitely lived up to the hype, and I've been thinking about going back since! :)

ambiance was great.. dim lighting, spacious open layout, and lively chatter all around. service was quick and efficient but fairly indifferent. our waiter wasn't helpful with recommendations because he "would be happy eating ANY of the dishes offered." couldn't he have pointed out *something* that stood out? ...at least he wasn't pushing the expensive items, but still, not very informative. he did pick a great white wine for us, reasonably priced at $45, but was a bit pushy about ordering a second bottle, which we didn't need. food was REALLY good. but the small portions were ill-suited to eating family-style. most primi had enough of a tasty oil base to be perfect for mopping up with their... - Foccacia: amazing! had to stop myself from eating more than 2 pieces.. it was lemony and fluffy, infused with rosemary and lightly dosed with olive oil. Â  - Steak Tartara: saturated with truffle oil, this was heavenly. you only get a small strip of the guanciale tho. - Shrimp crostini: only 3 of them and about thumb-size - Grilled sardines: four nice fillets topping a tangy peperonata & balanced with a salty blend of chorizo and chickpeas. - Marinated beets: i didn't get any gorgonzola in my few shared bites, but i'm sure that added the oomph i was missing. ** Fire-roasted garlic chicken: the BEST roast chicken i've had in recent memory. all you could hear was 'mmmm, wow' and 'oh my god!' don't know how they got that garlic flavor into every single juicy bite... utterly delicious!! also probably the best value because you could easily take home half the chicken. - Spaghetti w/prosciutto, ramps and english peas: also spectacular! creamy and covered with parmesan, these noodles were thick and totally satisfying. - Rigatoni w/lamb bolognese: my friends were saying how rich and heavy this dish was, and remarked on how much the lamb flavor came through.. i didn't find it too gamey, but then, i love lamb! desserts were pretty good overall (banana brown butter cake, honey cake w/blackberries), but by that point, i was too stuffed to pay much attention.... except i didn't find the 'La Fantasia di Cioccolata' that fantastic. it was alot of creamy gelato, but i wasn't bombarded with intense chocolatey-ness like i was expecting. i'd like to come back for brunch and lunch sometime... but for another dinner, i'll save it for a special occasion.

I am in love and officially hooked to Zen Vegetarian House. Their best dishes is the General Tso's Chicken and the Chicken Sandwich. This place is heaven for everyone , especially vegetarians (such as myself). I recommend this place for everyone!

Just returned from a delicious dinner at Gatsby's on the Bay. My husband started with Mac n Cheese - outstanding! Â My friend and I shared the Gatsby salad. Â A Winner. Â Our friend had clam chowder. Â mmmm! I had the duck for dinner. Â Usually skeptical about duck - it can be fatty and the skin rubbery. Â Not this meal! Â My husband had the short ribs - fall off the bone and tasty. Â Our friends had the branzino and seafood risotto. Â Both Â truly were impressed. Â I was full for dessert, but our friend had the Gatsby dessert, which he enjoyed. Â Small disappointment, our cappuccino Â was small. Â The only tiny tiny negative. The wait staff was attentive. Â The maitre d welcoming. Â All in all, a wonderful experience. Â We'll be back.

Living far up in Manhattan, I rarely venture into Brooklyn, as it's a long and hot trek on the muggy subway to get here. That being said, I plan on returning to Roberta's, and OFTEN, after my first meal here. Everything -- and I do mean EVERYTHING -- was absolutely scrumptious! The atmosphere here is great. Everyone is friendly and laid back. It's just a pleasant place to enjoy a meal. The patio decor is absolutely worth a peek, even if you decide to eat indoors. They grow some of their own produce in an herb garden outside, which completely floored me. I mean, hellooo, we're in New York City... no one does that! I LOVE IT. Now for the food. Most of their brunch menu items (weekends only, I believe) are unique to Roberta's, as their chefs seem to be creative and eccentric with their ingredients. Ricotta pancakes. I've never really been a fan of pancakes (although I do delight in the occasional banana pancake), but these pancakes were out of this world!! Excuse my lack of better descriptions, but they were somehow extra doughey on the inside, and delightfully crispy on the out. LOVED IT. Soft scrambled eggs. You'd think, "Now, there's only so much you can do with scrambled eggs", right? WRONG. These were the most amazing scrambled eggs I've ever had! The texture alone was a fantastic sensory experience. Light, fluffy, and extraordinarily tasty. Que delicioso!! ** Update: So I drafted the above review a year ago and never finished it! Blame my school schedule. I'm posting it as is, and though I haven't made it back to Roberta's yet, I plan to, especially now that I'm moving to Brooklyn! From memory, I stand by my 5-star review. Though I didn't write about the pizzas, I remember them being pretty dang awesome, as well. Stay tuned for an update! P.S. When I had gone to Roberta's last year, my friend's friend was actually the pastry chef there, so she brought us samples of her own ice cream recipes. They were so unconventional, and surprisingly good! I believe (though don't kill me if I'm mistaken) the flavors were corn, celery, and butter (not all together of course). If Roberta's still makes these, they're definitely worth a try! :)

I've come here many times and loved the food and have never had a problem. Today I felt I've been doing good on my diet, I'm going to have a pancake for breakfast. Be WARNED this is NOT a pancake, it's straight up CAKE! The description on the menu does not describe what you are actually served. The only thing missing was candles! Â I ate the fruit and had 2 bites and was full. It's so dense. It wasn't even good so spare yourself the heartache and do NOT order the pan CAKE!
Amazing pizza! Â I've been coming here for many many years and it always meets my expectations. Â Food is always great, fast service, friendly staff. Â Never let's me down.

The food is absolutely wonderful, but get ready for inconsistent service and high prices. It was pretty crowded when I got there, so that might have something to do with it. The perogies are top-notch and my favorite overall menu item.
Great place with a bustling atmosphere. Healthy choices and reasonable prices. Service excellent and an all around good place to stop in and have a bite

I was excited to try the famous Grimaldi's in Brooklyn, however, I was kind of disappointed. It was just ok in my opinion. Ingredients were fresh and mozzarella was great. I think they burn their crust a bit too much. Gives it a bitter taste. Also, needs more sauce. I think this place is hyped up a bit.
Good fresh, cheap. Â Spicy/flavorful, but not overpowering. Â I prefer the outside area because inside is just too damn loud!!

A diamond in the rough Roosevelt strip of gay bars. My United Nations crew (dubbed because the five of us represent every major ethnic mix on planet earth) blended right in on a Friday night. We saw tables of Indians, white firemen types, Asians, hispanics- just your typical slice of Queens- all enjoying the Himalayan Yak experience. We waited for some indeterminate amount of time for a table at 9:45pm. Upstairs and downstairs, people looked like they were settled in for the long haul. There wasn't a hostess or maitre d taking a list so we kind of hovered in a spot at the base of the stairs, hungry and hopeful. A live cover band rocking a crazy range of music from Hotel California to Bollywood hits kept everyone entertained (and shouting to be heard). Finally a prime table by the window opened up and a waiter motioned us over. Settling in our thin mats on the wooden bench, under an America Ferrera autograph, we found ourselves waiting some more. First for the menus. Then water. Then a waiter. Then the food. Then the waiter with the check. It seemed our food was brought out in whatever order the chef felt like. One appetizer arrived after we were mostly done with our entrees. Strangely, when the check came there was a note to bring the food out at the same time- which we never asked for, and didn't happen anyway. But you can't get cranky because a magical zen aura envelops you as soon as you walk in the door, and when you finally eat the food it caps the incredible experience. The vegetarian momos were the most delicious steamed veggie dumplings I have ever had. I will be dreaming about those little flavorful pillows of amazingness. Yummy tingmo. Scrumptious shrimp salad. Passable veggie thali. The vegetable curry was weak and the mula achar was reminiscent of a green kimchi, but the yogurt was an excellent dip for the tingmo. Himalyan Yak is a unique adventure right off the 74th Street- Roosevelt Ave train station. Try to go when the band is playing- they may let you sing on stage with them.

Really cool place with awesome staff, great food and a real soul. Great and diverse music to top it off. Fat Buddha has a pretty open layout and is pretty spacious by NYC standards. There is a huge oval bar in the center so it's easy to get the attention of the bartenders. And did I mention the food :-) ... the salt and pepper squid and pork buns are amazing as are many other items on the menu.

I'm a foodie from San Francisco. Â Everything was good. Â They did not accommodate special requests but did give a half order of meat balls. Â The noodles were fresh and delicious. The artichoke appetizer fried well and the thin slices of lemon were perfect. Â Us west coast people desire clean bathrooms as NYC has old buildings and? W/C, Â Lavatories superb. Â Wines were good. Â Need more by the glass wines. Â A must try. Â Meat balls were like home made. Â And not over cooked. Â BELLA it's my word for Antonio's
best pizza besides Difaras in Brooklyn . Great outdoor seating quick fast service . and their Italian ices are by far the best if i lived in Brooklyn i would eat here everyday
Great brunch spot. The chicken and waffles are excellent. I kept adding maple syrup to my food because I like it sweet and savory. Go in there and give it a try for yourself.

Not much of a pizza lover, but Flambee's on the other hand....delish! My favorite is the Forestierre. Oh and not to mention the flambeed calva dessert. Super friendly staff and owner Mathias makes this a treat each time

food sucks - dont come here....ummm i hope that helped shrink the extremely long lines for just a sandwich. its out of the world for under $5. i didnt know i can get so much bliss from a sandwich. i come here just about every week because i crave their sandwich every day. i need to get my weekly fix of #1. you can get it spicy too if you like spicy, i eat both, but unforunately my stomache doesnt like it to much. their food is very cheap and good and they will make it to your liking. i havent tried the one across the streeet, but i heard good things, unforunately i am to loyal to this place. this is truly one of the best in chinatown.

So, I went in search of a sushi place after my beloved go-to, Friend House, moved earlier this summer...sometimes when one door closes another door opens! Also I have yelp to thank for introducing me to this place!! I got take out - the place is tiny, but my order was ready to go when I got there. For $25 I got a salad (generous portion, delicious), and 2 rolls. I LOVE that they are all veg and all come with different sauces. Really fun. The ingredients are SO fresh and the rolls are 8 pieces each so I have enough left over that I can eat it tomorrow for lunch! As a vegan, I love a place with creative veggie rolls. This is DEFINITELY going to be my new go-to!!
Best falafel place in NYC, with the best price and the best hours.

My girlfriend had talked about this restaurant for months so I finally decided to give it a go. The decor is excellent and vintage inspired and fun. Pretty small space to have crammed so many tables in but it works. I came at around 9 on a Friday and the place was about mid capacity For the starter I had the atomic fireballs, and, wow! Super hot(temp) and fresh and so delicious! First bite burnt my tongue, had to take a sip, but man were they excellent and the hot sauce was a nice touch. As my main dish I had the Cap'n Crunch chicken tenders with the maple-bacon dipping sauce and was blown away. Again, super piping hot and fresh and just all-around delicious. The Cap'n Crunch dusting was a nice touch and the dipping sauce had me wanting a spoon to finish it off with. Seemed like not so much food but it was very filling. Â Great meal overall. The 4 star review is based on two things(Both very a-typical, obnoxious NYC bull crap): the honey iced tea was like $3-4 and didn't have free refills and of course the place didn't take my debit card; I had to walk across the street to the Chase ATM and pay their fee and my bank's fee(another $8). The meal, bank fees and tip included, came to a total of about $38.
I really love Toby's... I just moved to the neighborhood and was thrilled to find such a great restaurant. Â I love it... Bam behind the bar is great. Â I will continue to show up.

Being a non-New Yorker, I was told the cool thing to do was Brunch on Sundays. So I met some friends here for brunch. Apparently everyone else in the area had the same idea. The place was packed! It took forever to get a table that would seat us.. don't go at busy times with lots of peeps. The food was pretty good. The coffee was a godsend - it had been a late night/morning. The design of the place is cool too - I'm guessing the garage door windows would be lovely Â in the Spring when the weather is nice. And it was super close to the Barney's warehouse sale..which was a plus!

The only thing better than paying $10 for an eight-dollar drink is paying $10 for an $8 drink multiple times and having a bartender named Adam being a straight-up dick about every aspect of my time there (despite the fact that I did not know at the time that he was overcharging me, and I was tipping 25%+ on each round)... Thanks to Adam, I will never again go to Rye. There's about 250 great places to eat in Williamsburg Adam, and I'll be going anywhere but Rye in the future because you are such a dick...

What does one do when it's lunch time, they're starving, and don't want to eat McDonald's? You turn to Yelp & I must say thank you Yelp for introducing me to Margon. Before I went out I to the establishment, I read as many reviews ad possible. It seemed the Cuban sandwich is to die for. However it was upon looking at the photos of the food that made me go. Specifically, the picture of rice, beans, & oxtail. As my fellow reviewers have stated, it does have the hole-in-the-wall feel, but I like that. It's like your own personal spot away from the crazy tourists streaming back and forth. Upon entering you will see the sandwich station in the front. I was tempted for a minute to change my mind and get the Cuban sandwich, but I held strong. I had a purpose. I knew what I wanted. Oxtails. The entree type food is a little bit further on. All the food looked fresh and the steam was rising up from every container. The staff is very friendly. All you have to do is say excuse me and let them know you are ready to order. I must say I got an excellent portion of food. If I wasn't as hungry as I am right now, I would leave some over for later. But I'm not. Upon my first bite, my taste buds exploded with joy over the amazing flavors present. The rice was amazing. I think I could have eaten it separately without the sauce from the oxtails. The plantains were good. Usually when I make mine, they are very sweet. The ones served were not as sweet but still tasted great. The oxtails did not disappoint. The oxtails truly deserve 5 stars. I'm from Barbados and it's hard for me to find really good oxtails. Margon has provided me a wonderful taste of home whenever I'm craving it. Now that I have stuffed myself, I'm going to try & not think of the amount of delicious calories I just consumed. Enjoy!

Very disappointing :( I have been wanting to go to Bubby's for a while. Â The menu online looked good and I liked how the food is supposed to be fresh and that the meat is natural. Â I was also excited to go there because they have a photobooth downstairs near the bathrooms. Â So I thought this would be a fun place to go to with good food. Well... Â you have to pay in cash, which is crazy because who wants to carry around that kind of money in the city. The food was extremely OVERPRICED! Â I ordered salmon which cost $23. Â The piece of salmon I got was the size of my fist (4x3 inches). Â The $6 side of fries was a larger quantity of food compared to my entree! Â And I wouldn't have minded the small quantity of food if it was good quality food. Â The food was mediocre at best. Â You are better off going to Applebees or Chipolte or any other chain restaurant for that matter if you want better food. Also, there were children running around and screaming, even playing in the bathrooms! To sum up: Â NOT WORTH IT!!!!!!!!!!!!

I have been to this place several times. I couldn't get enough of it the first few times. Let me start out by saying the arepas are great--or at least they were. The green sauce is the best part. Sadly, it has suffered the more popular it has gotten as often happens. I think the last three times we went there, I always said "I am never coming here again". The service leaves a lot to be desired. They almost made me feel like they didn't want my business. The (for real) last time I went there, I got pick-up. There couldn't have been less care put into my arepa. I mean, we are talking three ingredients here. How hard is that? Its like a two year old made it. And to make matters even worse, half way through I discovered a 1/2 inch piece of plastic shard right buried down in the cheese. Good thing I found it because it would not have been pretty going down. Â  That did it for me. If you go, eat in small bites and chew carefully.
SO GOOD!
Way better than Grimaldis since it's the real Grimaldis. Â  Has the original oven, recipe, and owner. Â  Hope the tourists don't realize this.

Exceptional food, service, ambiance and location. Easy to get to. 4.4 stars. The lunch menu is reasonably priced. The portions are the right size; i.e. not too big. I have also had lunch in their private dining room; it was a great experience. The place does need a little cap ex, floors etc are showing a slight sign of wear. But overall, still v good. Hence the 4.4 v.s a 5.

FOOD POISONED. Â My father and I ate here in the bar area sharing a salad, cacio e pepe and the signature suckling pig. Â Within hours of leaving we both became seriously ill. Â I called the restaurant to notify them and they sounded genuinely sorry but there was no offer to refund the meal that ruined our weekend. Â  Hey Danny Meyer, how about your kitchen staff washing the vegetables before putting them into a salad? Â I'm disgusted.

This is where I come for ramen when I don't feel like waiting at Ippudo. The ramen here is ALMOST as good, taste-wise, but it is cheaper here by a couple bucks. I also like that they include a lot of the stuff that they would charge extra for at other places, like an egg, or seaweed, or pork slices. They don't indicate on the menu what they put in the bowl, though, so its kind of like a fun surprise each time. I remember loving my first bowl I had here, on a chilly winter's night. I really wish I could recall what it was, because when I came back a few days ago, I couldn't remember and decided to go with what the waitress deemed the "most popular" (the spicy miso). It definitely wasn't what I had the first visit, though it was pretty good. Just not GREAT, and not what I'd been craving. I love spicy things, so it wasn't the spice that bothered me, it was just missing something. I ordered for my friend (who had never even had ramen before) and got him one of the more basic ramens-can't remember which one this was either, one from the first two categories I know. I secretly hoped that at least one of the ramens we ordered would be that magical ramen I had the first time, but they weren't. His was still good, and definitely better than mine, but nothing quite so mouth watering as that first time (guess the first time for everything is always the best...). We also ordered the pork gyoza which were NOT tasty, sadly. They were a bit greasy, and the skin was incredibly thin, and they just didn't hit the spot as much as I wanted them to. I still ate a few of them, and my friend loved them, but I was hoping for more. I know I'm selling this place short with my lackluster review, BUT it really is a great ramen option if you don't have the time to wait around at Ippudo! It's a bit of a hike from anywhere, though, on 5th between A and B, but the good news is, you'll be right around the corner from Lula's Sweet Apothecary and you can finish the night off right! *cash only*

5 stars for their guiness shake. for those who dont know, there is no actual alcohol in this shake. i believe its an evaporated concentrate of guiness with a vanilla icecream shake. It was AMAZING. i love it how it isn't overly sweet with a hint of the guiness malty flavor. their regular shakes are good too. they have this candied bacon shake too but i haven't been brave enough to try it. haha

This is by far my favorite restaurant in Brooklyn. The cocktails are great and the food is delicious. It has a very intimate neighborhood feel to it that makes you just want to eat and drink there all night. Â I have yet to have a bad meal here and a couple of times the chef has taken the time to come out and say hello, which is a nice touch. Â My fiancÃ© and I had our first date here and now we bring anyone who visits NYC or hasn't been here. Â One thing all of us agree on is that the mac and cheese is the best in the city, hands down.

sat down to dinner w/two friends after only a modest wait at one of their front tables with the bench seat. was immediately greeted by a host that put me at ease about the perceived dress code - this restaurant draws a well dressed crowd for sure, name notwithstanding. our waiter, a friendly good-looking guy, got right down to business discussing the specials and answering our questions about one combo of appetizers versus another pairing. we settled on the duck confit samosas and pizza with pickled peppers and red onion. great choice with great tastes. still, it was readily apparent that the vermont suckling pig with dried fruit mostarda was the only dish that could satisfy the taste of three decidely hungry men, two of whom were visiting from los angeles. and this follows on my wholy delicious thanksgiving dinner at campanelli's on la brea. similarly priced, these two dining experiences easily stand out either because i'm a fool from whom who's money he's easily parted or because i know good food. that said, have you tried the hudson valley rabbit duo?

This place rocks my socks. Be sure to make a reservation, it gets booked even on weekdays. Service was friendly, attentive, and knowledgeable. Â If I had the money to spend, I would certainly get the WHOLE menu for $420, as it is offered. Favorites were the lamb meat balls, pulled pork empanadas, and MY GOODNESS, the SKIRT STEAK Â with chimichurri, parmesan potato puree, haricot vert & tomato salad. Perfectly cooked and the potato puree went great with it. I did not fall in love with the fried goat cheese with lavender infused honey. Goat cheese is already strong by itself, frying it makes it over the top. Their lavender honey was not the best I've had either. I've had a better cheese+lavender honey combo somewhere else. Bring cash or your amex card.

Come for the experience, and never when you're hungry, as the $$ quickly pile up!! Excellent quality and nice wine list but after paying $130+ for two (with 2 glasses of wine) I'd expect to be a bit fuller but no, they take their 'tasting plate' sizes quite seriously so yes the portions are tiny. Good for a one-off like maybe on a first date to impress a girl, or maybe you hit the jackpot and you have money to burn, but there are so many other fine dining experiences in this city that will give you more buck for your money. Â Side note: the croquettes and lamb are excellent.

I was excited for STIX - who wouldn't love food on a stick? Â I enjoyed my meal, but I've had better Mediterranean food elsewhere. Â It's convenient, affordable, and pretty good. Â A couple of things need some work, so here's what we (party of 4) ordered: - octopus - this was probably my favorite in the group, although it was odd to see it on a stick. Â The grilled octopus was tender, a bit under seasoned, but the surrounding onion caper olive oil relish concoction saved the day. - mac'n cheese balls - not sure how this is considered Mediterranean, but don't bother with this one. Â Tastes like a bunch of elbow pasta with a cheesy paste holding it together after being deep fried - also on a stick. Â The cheesy sauce holding it together was more starchy than cheesy - leave the mac'n cheese to the experts please. - zucchini balls - don't get this. Â It was like shredded zucchini held together by pasty yogurt and hummus - texture was terrible, flavor was bland at best. - shrimp - we ordered two shrimp stix - these were good, well seasoned, perfectly grilled and simple. Â I hate over cooked shrimp and this was perfect for me. Â  - pork - this was also good, similar comments as the shrimp. - steak/beef - cooked to a good temperature, so not charred and over cooked. Â This was definitely under seasoned though, I had to sprinkle a little salt on it. - Parmesan and truffle fries - these were ok standard fries - it was also served with stix (not for each fry but just a couple stix stabbed into the pile) - sack of potatoes - we ordered this just for the name, sounded so fun. Â These are just cubes roasted potatoes with rosemary and a side sauce (which I don't recommend, the ketchup was better) - jalapeÃ±o hummus - least bang for your buck and flavor was bleh - don't bother. Â This was a tiny portion, more like a dipping cup sizes portion that you would expect of ketchup. Â On top of that the pita provided was tiny, it was thicker than normal pita but super small, think of a oversized cookie size cut into quarters. Â It was fluffy inside crispy outside which I liked but I much prefer the hummus and pita at Taim - you get a lot more and it tastes WAY better. Â Other reviewers wrote about the spread symposium which is a mix of the spreads - we asked for this and unfortunately this is no longer on the menu. Â Takes the fun out of ordering dips, doesn't it? Â Everyone loves a variety of dips, odd that they took it off the menu. Â  The prices look friendly, but the portions are more like appetizers than entrees, so if you need a quick snack it works, if you're super hungry, you might want to opt for a heartier kebab like the ones from Ali Baba, there is a definite price difference, but when you think about how many of the STIX kebabs you need to fill up vs the kebab entree at a place like Ali Baba, it's probably not much different. Â STIX had a good size portion for my taste - I prefer variety so I tend to like smaller portions, but my cousin said he'd probably need 3-4 portions to fill him up. Something else that's odd, interesting, but not that practical is that they served the kebabs and fries in mini shovels - the kind you would maybe scoop ice out of a freezer with. Â While it was a cool novelty at first, it started to quickly take up too much space on the table. Â All in all not a bad meal, it did the trick and came out to be about $25 per person (we all shared everything). Â They also have happy hour from 4-7pm - $4 beers and $5 wines - what's not to like about that? Â The STIX individually are about $5 for one, so have a quick drink and a little snack before a big night ~ $10. Â Not bad for a place to hold you over until the night begins.

Came here pre-theatre based on the rave reviews on Yelp. Â  A great little BYOB (Yay!), cash only spot with delicious food. Â The mushroom cigars were so delicious we ordered them twice. Â We had the citrus shrimp with couscous, country salad, and the chicken kabob with fries. Â Food was fresh and light, but portions were on the small side (we were splitting it among 3 people). Â Service was fast and friendly! Â  Definitely a nice spot to grab a quick bite before the theatre. Â (Go see Death of a Salesman---PSH is amazing!).

I used to watch Top Chef (back in the day when the show had better contestants and less amateurish stunts), but while I appreciated the show, I don't give a flying crap if a restaurant was opened by a former contestant or, as is the case here, a winner; all I care about is good food, which is why a place like Social Eatz (opened by another Top Chef contestant) didn't do it for me with its mediocre, overpriced food. But Perilla is an entirely different story because, well, the food is actually quite good. I came here for the winter 2012 Restaurant Week (don't judge me, please!), and while most participating restaurants give half-assed menus with meager serving sizes, I really appreciated the varied menu selection and generous portion sizes. In fact, this may have been one of the first times that I left a Restaurant Week dinner feeling full. For the first course, both my friend and I ordered the mussels, which were VERY generously portioned. You'll never hear me complain about getting too much food, as there is a direct correlation between amount of food and happiness (true story), but my friend actually made exactly such a blasphemous statement about the first course. If ever there was a moment for the #firstworldproblems hashtag, that would have been the time for it. But the quality of the dish was fantastic, as the chunks of pork mingled nicely with the mussels and paired well with the broth. For the second course, I went with the Braised Goat with quinoa, eggplant puree, and Greek-style yogurt. I absolutely loved the dish, as the braised meat was incredibly tender and not gamey in the slightest, and it was complemented nicely by the smoky, rich eggplant. My friend's chicken dish was quite good as well, as the skin was nicely crisped, and the meat was incredibly moist. Like the mussels, the chicken was "too big" of a portion size for her, and she mentioned that she thought that the dish was oversalted, which I didn't think was the case. Honestly, I think she's just picky. The dessert course consisted of a bread pudding, while my friend ordered the walnut cake, which she actually enjoyed a lot. My bread pudding was solid, but it would have been a whole lot better had it been warmed before serving. Overall, I felt that the meal was pretty good -- the food varied from good (bread pudding) to very good (mussels) to GIMME MOAR (goat). Service-wise, I have no complaints, and I thought that my friend and I were treated well in spite of being obvious Restaurant Week-ers. I wouldn't mind coming back here again in the future, though I probably won't be bringing back the same friend next time.

I was excited when this place opened (not another Latino chicken place!). I've been to their Astoria restaurant also and enjoyed it. And the other Italian places in Sunnyside have not wowed me. I give this place a 3.5 but I always round up. If they would add daily specials, that would go a long way. Menu changes seasonal, but it is tiny. If you are at all picky, don't bother. Food is generally fresh and well prepared. Pasta tastes fresh, which is huge for me. However, due to tiny menu I only come here once every few months. Chef, consider daily specials! A daily pizza (so simple!), daily salad, and daily entree would get me in the door more often.

Went there on Friday night and it was very fun & the food was awesome (try the octopus app as well as tomato buratta salad). We all had pizza which was great. They had some very nice bottles of wine for under $30-we had the Primitivo for $25-not bad! The only negative was that it is very loud when the restaurant is full. But other than that I'd give it 4 stars! I'll definitely go back. Oh and the attentive service was a plus also!

This is hard to admit...especially when writing a review, but I'VE GOT NO WORDS FOR HOW GREAT THIS PIZZA IS. I'm literally afraid I may be ruined for all other pizza enjoyment. New York City takes it's pizza very seriously; it's practically a religion. So, my boyfriend and I went in with an open mind; "Try all, choose best." And, for only the second time in all our years of travel did we forego sampling a bunch of different places (despite our best intentions) in favor of returning to Lombardi's over and over. The crust is the perfect balance of cruchy and chewy. The ingredients are fresh, bright and incredibly simple (often harder to master than most complex recipies). And the cobbled together restaurant feels like the most wonderful maze with only fresh, coal-oven baked pie at the end. As Nike says "Just Do It!" You won't be sorry!

Came here with some friends while waiting for our table at Traif. Getting in: - Walked in and sat at a table Atmosphere: - Cozy, quirky spot. Enjoyable. Service: - Service was great and recommended some amazing pickle backs Drinks: - We had several rounds of pickle backs - They make their pickle brine/juice in house and it's great - They have an extensive selection of whisky/ey Other: -We loved the pickle backs so much we went back after dinner for one more round

My friend who goes to Sterne (women's college at Yeshiva U) recommended we go to Bareburger when I was visiting for a weekend in November. Best garlic cheese bread and red sauce/meat balls in the country! I've eaten here dozens of times and every time is perfect! Great for large groups, but plan and reserve way in advance. Only con is that you can encounter large crowds... Will return often.

This is THE best place in Astoria to go. Beers are great, good is great, atmosphere is chill but cool. Â Perfect for a date, friends or a simple drink. Highlights - Cheese plate is well above what a pub would offer. Â Mushroom burger is stellar. Â You can't o wrong with a McClures pickle martini!!

If you walk fast along W 46th, you'll miss this very narrow store front. It extends a long way into the back but leaves little room for maneuvering inside. 2pm still finds Margon with a long line of mixed white- and blue-collar workers, and seating can be a problem. My first order was the the oft-raved about roasted chicken entree ($9), which comes with 2 side orders. The sides available when I visited were cassava, sweet plantains, rice & beans, or a salad- I chose the yellow rice and black beans and Â sweet plantains. The portions were very generous, and could easily have been split into 2-3 servings (for an Asian appetite, at least). The chicken, yes, fell off the bone, but was overcooked - it was disappointingly dry. Taste-wise, it was also a letdown. It looked better than it tasted. The rice and beans were nothing special, but the plantains were too mushy. Quantity made up for quality. I wouldn't order this again unless I needed a quick and cheap stomach filler. But I hope I just caught Margon on a bad chicken day. The second order I placed was the cubano ($7), a sandwich I always order when available. It was assembled right in front of me, as opposed to pre-made sandwiches just waiting to be pressed/reheated on demand. Simple ingredients- and I assumed store-made; their fresh ham and roast pork were both on their menu- mustard, Swiss cheese, and dill pickles in a 10-inch sandwich roll. Pretty straightforward. Margon's deviation from the "authentic" cubano was the addition of salami, a variation usually seen in Florida. The technique was also spot on- and fascinating to watch!- ending with the pressing of the sandwich, hard and long, in a plancha. And the final product did not disappoint. My only complaint would be that the taste of the salami predominated, instead of all the components working together. But the roast pork and ham were succulent, and the salami, being rather crispy, added a nice textural contrast. The bread was chewy with a crispy exterior; and even with the butter slathered on it, it wasn't overly greasy. Overall a good sandwich, one I would order again. Service was great! The servers were very accommodating and cheerful, and treated you as though you were the only customer in the joint despite the mass of people there. Kudos to the staff. In sum, Margon was okay. Not legendary or great, but a place well worth its price, and one I would revisit again.

I would lean towards 3.5 stars but I am not afforded such an option. Whilst I enjoyed the cornmeal catfish and requisite sides, I was wholly disappointed by the jalapeno cornbread which was served cold and dry. I needed to sip my drink just to get the cornbread down. L&B Spumoni Gardens is not just a restaurant. It is a landmark. It is a "must visit" place in Brooklyn. The pizza as well as all other dishes are the best!!!
Great food, fast service(usually) and has a nice view. There is outside seating, perfect for the summer.

good food and like what they are doing. seating arrangement a bit crazy but whatever

The only thing worse than the 80s tattoos are the stale coffee beans and lousy espresso drinks. No maybe the attitude is worse

Affordable. Generous portions. Flavorful soups. No frills type joint. I'm a fan. Some seating is available but it does get packed in here quick. There is a TV playing Chinese movies at the restaurant. They have a restroom in the back. On each table you will find chopped cilantro in a container, a water jug, chopsticks, spoons and napkins. Their chili sauce is excellent, ask for it if you want to add some spice to your meal. Our server was nice and quick in taking our order. All our dishes came out in a timely manner but the Baby Bok Choy took much longer. Tried their Fried Dumplings, which my mom fell deeply in love with. We had to order another plate just for her, lol. They were juicy, seasoned well, light and had a perfectly cooked wonton skin. Highly recommended. If you want something cool and crisp to accompany your hot soups, try their Cucumber Salad. The sauce they mix the cucumbers with is incredibly addicting. It's sweet, spicy and savory. I want more. You can't go wrong with their soups. For around $6-7 you can get a huge bowl of soup with fresh noodles, meats and veg. Incredibly filling. The broth is light yet flavorful. With each soup you can choose the type of noodles you want (ie. Knife Peeled, Fat Hand Pulled, Skinny Rice, Big Wide Hand Pulled, Regular Hand Pulled, Regular Rice and Small Wide Hand Pulled). The noodles are freshly made and have a lovely chew. Comfort food all the way.

Oh my god, the brussells sprouts appetizer. I cannot stop thinking about how good it was. If you like peanuts and fish sauce, these are the absolute jam. Also mind blowing was the tempura kale app. SO. GOOD.

Perfect neighborhood place, of which there are far too few in Brooklyn Heights. Ideal date place and for married couples who want to enjoy a night together. Too quiet and subdued for boisterous kiddies, but there a couple of larger tables for families. The grades... 1. Value. Grade: B+. Not cheap by any measure, nor are the portions huge, but the food is of high quality, well prepared and I've never left unsatisfied. The bar menu and wine list are very reasonable. 2. Food. Grade: A-. I've yet to have a bad meal. The bar turns out great cocktails, including a handful of signature drinks. For starters, the fried oysters are great but the portion is small. The smoked trout salad is fantastic and large enough for a main course. For entrees, the short ribs and potato puree is perfect for a cold winter night. The hangar steak is delicious, but it arrives sliced, giving the impression of a smallish portion. For fish, go with the catch of the day -- it's never disappointed. The pancakes, french toast and HOMEMADE sausage on the Sunday brunch menu are all out of this world. 3. Service. Grade: B. Unremarkable either way, which means the service is good. Everyone is friendly and generally efficient. The occasional small misstep happens -- a forgotten drink, etc -- but no biggie. 4. Ambiance: Grade: B+ Exactly the type of casual, reasonably high-end place you want to find in a neighborhood like Brooklyn Heights... A worn, comfortable feel... dark, exposed brick, old wooden floors, motiv candles on every table provide the primary lighting. Sunday brunch sees a nice mix of families and champagne guzzlers, giving the place a very happy vibe. Bottom line: One of the best places in the neighborhood. Bring your best girl, your mom and dad when they're in town, friends for alcohol-fueled Sunday brunch or enjoy a quiet meal with some wine and a good book. Grade: A-.

Beyond Sushi was absolutely amazing! Â We ordered a miso soup, a green roll, a sweet potato roll and the roll of the month, which was topped with beet root. Â It was all delicious and extremely filling for being vegan! Â I am a vegetarian, and am usually stuck with sushi rolls consisting of one vegetable tempura or a piece of asparagus, but Beyond Sushi exceeded all of my expectations. Â Go now!

We have been coming here for several years now, so I will offer a cumulative experience with Yak. We've often referred to Yak as "our favorite restaurant." It has never been superior in any one category but with repeated visits there has come a familiarity, a comfort, an "our place" kind of feel, despite being "foreigners" to this culture and cuisine. We had our experimental phase, even feeling obligated to try the Yak stew (we cannot disagree with the chewing on a leather purse comparison). We came to settle on four items: Shabalay (used to be spelled differently on the menu), pan fried chicken momo, and the very British chicken Tikka Masala, always with a couple of plain nan. Over the span of time Yak has had problems with consistency on all levels. Once, we ordered the chicken lollipop and it was raw on the inside. Our usual safe and boring order has varied in quality, but is usually what we hope for. Service is usually pretty good, but at times we've had to wait, too hungry for too long. The servers are usually pleasant, but some of our favorite people are long gone. What keeps us coming back? For me, beyond the comfort of the familiar, it is the green sauce. They provide all tables with three small bowls of sauce. One of them is just plain nasty, the other is GF's (she can have it), Mine and all mine is the green sauce. it is made with vinegar and avocado and maybe green tomatoes and assorted spices. The result of this deceptively simple concoction is an irresistible, addictive tangy effect. Â I slather everything with it and often beg for some to take home. If there was no green sauce which I have not been able to find anywhere else nor come close to creating myself, Yak would lose a star from my review and maybe a regular customer.
Really great food, consistently. Â And great staff. I always make a point to go to Ippudo when I am in town - great experience.

In the heart of UWS where you find the largest population of single women in the city, this place surprisingly has more men than women eating. The reason is - the portion is huge. Brunch pancake ends up looking like the Naan at middle eastern kebab place... no kidding. Fried pickle is fantastic, beets taste great. However, the western omelette tastes just so so. The one I had was very cheesy, oily, and too ordinary. It was lack of the flavor that made me want to order it again.

Great ramen, definitely tasty, rich broth and perfectly cooked noodles. Yummy pork buns that are very filling. While very tasty, we had to wait 3 hours for a table on a Friday night. I'm glad the food was great but not in a rush for such a long wait again anytime soon! So for me its a once in a while meal. Worth trying for sure.
look at the stars, what more can i say......

4.5 stars. Great music, excellent food and good food. three things that are clear winners at Do or Dine! I ordered A Chicken And Woffals and fell in love -- the cornish game hen was moist and with perfectly crispy skin. The waffle was just as spectacular. They have tito's (yes!) and my husband loved the 175 5th Avenue Steak. He ate the kimchee, and I've never ever seen him eat kimchee (hooray!). The key is to get there on the early side to avoid a wait. We walked right in and were seated at 7pm on a Monday night. Note: Their ice-cream supplier has been shut due to hurricane sandy, so all they had was the sliced ice-cream snickers for dessert that night. Must return to try more menu items.

For all those complaining about the service, Don't go to Italy. Italian people are genuine, passionate, hard working and honest to the face. Dont expect the fake smile routine that American employees have. For 5 dollars you travel to the heavens and back, if you are still complaining then take a dunk in the Hudson for your own sake. You can taste the passion in this womens cooking. Its phenomenal.

Bought the Sweet & Sara toasted coconut marshmallows at Jimbos Natural Foods and will make sure to ask for a refund. I couldn't even finish one without spitting it out. I bought these based on the glowing reviews and found they are quite possibly one of the most sickly sweet and terrible rubber-like textures in faux-Marshmallows (?) on the market. Marshmallows are supposed to have a slightly powdery texture, none of that here. Not to mention they are loaded with corn syrup and you can taste it in the mix. Why do so many vegan treats go overkill with the sweetness factor? Â  Worst I have ever tasted. I don't understand what all the fuss is about other than it's trendy. These are horrid and I would not bother with any of their other FAKE 'marshmallow' items after these wretched and over-priced lumps of corn syrup and cane sugar.
The best Salmon Eggs Benedict ever!!!!! Only the French can do it for me..so far! ;p
Lombardi's ricks ad the philadelphia location does too, brick oven and fresh basil. This crust, I love it and I wish the west coast could make pizza like this!

I honestly wanted to like this place. When taqueria diana moved into the neighborhood I was excited. Especially since I live less than 2 mins walk away. And I tried hard by eating here at least Â 9-10 times. But I've had enough mediocrity, and here's why: 1) Cost. $8 for a burrito. Cool, that's standard. But then charging an extra $3-$4 for sour cream, cheese and guac? Surely sour cream and cheese are standard and shouldn't cost extra. But they do. Not cool. 2) The service. Come by here and you'll find that the cashiers and the guys behind the counter are rude. No thanks. 3) The burritos are not that great. Ever read the blog post "dear guy who made my burrito"? That's exactly what their burrito making skills remind me of. The guac, rice and meat are not layered very well. So you end up chomping into a mouthful of guac. I'll give them credit for their nachos and full chicken. But really, if you want good, reasonably priced Mexican food and service then just walk 1 block up the road to Otto's Tacos. If you want great Mexican food that's also very reasonably priced, walk 5 minutes down to El Diablito. Hope this helps all you fellow Mexican food lovers.

I have been a regular supporter of Public for about three years. Today was like eating at a school training cafeteria. We had pork belly on quinoa hash browns, with poached eggs, spinach and tomato. The pork was cold, yet overcooked. The eggs had cooled down as well, which suggested that it was standing in the kitchen for a while before it was brought to our table. I politely asked that they take it back, and bring me a new plate of food. I was relaxed, and enjoying my wine. The waiter proceeded to return with new plates of food, on which they took the overcooked meat, and practically flamed it, drying it out to the point that the cutlery they supplied to the table could not cut through the pork. To add insult to injury they placed the pork belly on a dried burnt quinoa hash. So clearly an act of $*%# you from the Kitchen/Chef. At this point I asked that they take our food back and bring me the bill. After another 10 minute wait, the waiter finally informed me that there was no charge. What a waste of time. While I agree with all the compliments on decor, crowd and location, restaurants fail when they cannot match good food with friendly service. It is not rocket science. A good restaurant would have sent over the manager and prioritized finding a solution, not be spiteful about it. This city is filled with wonderful places for brunch, and Public has become a shallow husk of its former self.
Tacos here can be pretty hit or miss. Service also very inconsistent. Mainly order here out of convenience. Not as good as Chavelas

I will support any restaurant that sticks to a mantra like the one at The Green Table. Â Their menu changes and you can always find something seasonal on there. Â Best of all most of the ingredients are from local organic and sustainable farms, something we should ALL support. Try the grilled cheese, you can be sure that it's different cheeses on different occasions and it's always paired with caramelized onions or some sort of fruit compote which really compliments the tanginess of the cheese or the crispness of the bread! Â I would suggest a half of the sandwich though because the thing is monstrous and if you get half you can get a cup of soup or a really excellent salad. Â Also if they are on the menu try whatever sort of baked eggs are being offered. Â The eggs are cooked perfectly and you can still dip your toast into a bit of runny egg...my favorite. I would highly recommend the Green Table, if you want a bit of quite eat inside the tiny little dining room but if you like to people watch and you're not looking to have any sort of intimate conversations sit at the communal table in the Chelsea Market walkway and watch the crowds...it's well worth it!

cozy, kind of dark restaurant. went around 6:30pm when happy hour was still going on. there was a good number of people at the bar and seated for dinner. it definitely is a bit high end compared to the restaurants on stone street from a visual perspective but the prices are pretty much the same. i got the chandlery (cocktail) which was actually pretty good and the iceberg salad. overall the service and food were good but i felt like the drinks were a bit overpriced but then again, most of fidi has overpriced restaurants/bars

The reason for a 3 star review instead of a 4 star is because their serving sizes are insanely small. In terms of flavor, Adela's has truly got a special thing going on but what's the point if you can expect to leave still feeling hungry! I've eaten here twice (once was dine-in and the other time as takeout) and personally love their Bacalau Guisado (cod fish stew) but its insulting how small their servings are, especially for a latin restaurant where big portions for hearty appetites are generally the expectation. Not so here. To give you a clearer idea, they fill an average sized coffee mug to measure out a cup of rice, a cup of beans and a cup of stew before plating! They take single serving to an absurd new low for restaurant dining. I generally always offer to share my dish with friends or at the very least look forward to taking home some leftovers anytime I go out. With servings being as small as they are you can't offer to share or expect any leftovers since there isn't enough on the plate to fill your own belly. If you order the meal as take-out their portions are exactly the same and as you can imagine the food doesn't fill the containers. I wish I had a picture of how ridiculous it looked. The containers looked half empty, not half full if you get what I'm saying. So yes, the food tastes good but for what you pay you can go to many other local latin restaurants (see my other reviews) where the portions and the price are much better aligned and the food tastes just as delicious. PASS!

You love PORK? Â This is the right place. I mean seriously... SERIOUSLY... I FEEL TERRIBLE FOR: 1. Â Jewish folks - being kosher really blows if you knew how good this place was 2. Â Vegetarian folks - i mean really? you don't know what you are missing out here 3. Â Pescatarian folks - ::sigh:: think of this as the freshest and tastiest fish, but like MILLION times better 4. Â Pork hating folks - you are a retard ok... sorry, i had to get that out. yes the wait here is excruciatingly long sometimes, but just go karaoke for an hour and voila! Â waiting is not so bad! I believe the best ramen to get there are either 1) Shiromaru Hakata Classic 2) Akamaru Modern You can always add additional toppings. For me best toppings to add are: 1) Kakuni(braised pork belly) 2) Menma(bambooshoots) Also, make sure to try their pork buns..... It makes me sad writing this review cause I am not eating all this goodness right now. T_T As always, go give it a shot. Â It's popluar/famous for a reason and I really believe it's worth the hype/wait. Oh and one last thing... i don't know if this is worth anything, but my friend who's been to japan said this was the best ramen he had outside of japan.

The sangria is like magic! I went to Pio Pio with my good friend and her parents, who I was meeting for the first time and was wondering if the four of us would enjoy ourselves. Â Add a couple pitchers of sangria and watch the magic happen. Â  However, Pio Pio is more than their sangria...the food was fantastic and totally reasonable and the atmosphere was fabulous. Â I wish I could remember the name (see above about amount of sangria consumed) but there is a dish that has a WHOLE chicken and bunch of sides and it was only $35 bucks! Â This dish plus a couple appetizers was plenty for the four of us. Perfect place for groups and fun!

Cheap, filling, salty and a bit greasy. Go for the pork katsu. Yes, it's a big piece of meat. I'd avoid the shrimp just because everything here seems so processed.. I dunno. Doesn't scream "fresh" to me, and seafood's gotta be fresh.

I lived in the South for almost two years of my life. Â Some how, some way, these people brought authentic Southern style fare to Williamsburg. Â Absolutely delectable. Â Get the fried catfish box and fried chicken drumsticks a la carte.

My husband and I had an exceptional meal here. We got the tuna tartare (amazing!) to nibble on then moved on to the halibut and pan-roasted chicken for our entrees. Our meal was mouthwatering -good from beginning to end. They also had a great selection of wines to choose from - several options but not so many that it becomes overwhelming. In addition, we liked the layout of the space. Intimate but with great windows to allow plenty of natural light in. The service was great as well. Come for a date or to catch up with a few of your close girlfriends!

My 100th review! Landmarc sure has a fine piece of steak. One of those somewhat limited restaurants where rare equals rare and medium rare equals medium rare. They sure know how to cook em. I actually wanted pasta when I saw that this was a part-italian restaurant. But they only have one pasta dish for every day of the week. No other pastas on the menu. I wasn't a big fan of the pasta special that day so I decided to go with steak (fine choice *pats myself on the back*). Got myself some juicy skirt steak that was flavorfully marinated. But I'm getting ahead of myself. Let's get back to the beginning. I had a party of 7 on my table and we decided to get a lil fancy and order some wine and appetizers. They have a wide selection of both. We got a white wine that was pretty good (no idea what the name was, sorry), and ordered 4 appetizers. We went with the bone marrow, wine and shallots mussels, fried mozzarella and ricotta fritters, and steak tartar. Everything was highly recommended by fellow Yelpers. Sadly, I wasn't blown away. Mussels were kind of sandy and didn't taste that fresh to me. I was not a fan of that. The cheese fritters were disappointing because they were pretty bland. The texture was good, just that the taste was lacking. I love fried cheese, but this was no bueno. Bone marrow was okay. Half of my friends loved it and half my friends were soso, so I think its a preference thing. It does taste very fatty and the salt is necessary or you'd be eating plain tasting fat ("good fat though!"). Lastly steak tartar was probably my favorite and I didn't even like it that much. The steak was finely diced and seemed fresh, but bland. The bread that accompanied it was a little hard and somewhat burnt. Â Overall, appetizer fail. Next time I'd go straight for the steak. Back to the steak. These entrees really helped make my experience better. The skirt steak I had was perfectly medium rare and delicately marinated. Skirt steak is usually a little thin, but Landmarc does it right. It was one really long slab of meat folded together. When I unfolded it, the length was longer than my plate. Portions done right. The fries it came with were crispy and flavorful--also delicious. My friends ordered the 22 oz ribeye (on point!), filet mignon, lamb chops, pasta, and mussels. The bucatina allmatriciana pasta (wednesdays) was really spicy. They should probably warn us on the menu. THAT RIBEYE THO. If you're feeling hungry and carnivorous, one of the best choices was the ribeye. That thing literally covers your whole plate and makes ALL your fries soggy if you don't save them from the suffocating piece of steak. I had a piece of it and it was really juicy and delicious. My friends weren't able to finish it and took it home instead. The dishes come out really hot and everything came at once. That's the way to do it. Our waitress, Lauren, was GREAT. Very friendly, pleasant, and didn't kick us out when we were loud and obnoxious. We had a cake, so she was perfect with her timing and lit the candles for us, even though the ac kept blowing them out hahhah. She did try lighting them multiple times and I appreciate that. I was deciding between a 3 and a 4, but good service makes a difference. Landmarc isn't cheap if you decide to indulge in these fancy appetizers and drinks. The bill came out to be like $530 after tip for a party of 7. Next time though, I think I would go straight for the steak and skip everything else.

So I'm in love. My roomie and I took an adventure here and I ordered the eight pork and chive dumplings in soup... it was only $3.00. Score! It took a while to get my order as the women behind the counter rushed around preparing, cooking and serving everything from dumplings to sesame pancake sandwiches. Watching this scene behind the counter made me exclaim to my roomie, "It's like a dumpling McDonald's!!!". I think she was embarrassed. After my ticket number was yelled by a small woman (Vanessa?), I picked up my soup which was in a massive to go container. It looked like it would be enough for lunch and dinner. I'm embarrassed to say that once I tried the dumplings, I polished off the whole thing in two sittings... the first being squished at a table in the restaurant... the second being on an Uptown avenue bus when I decided I wanted to eat the rest of it. My one regret is that I didn't get any of the fried dumplings... they looked absolutely fantastic being cooked behind the counter in their large skillets of hot oil. My roomie and I have resolved to return so that we can try more of these delicious choices.

crowded during peak times. Â its a grab & go type of place. but, its open late and a perfect late night munchie. Â truthfully, i just like it by itself without all their fancy sauces. Â  *google offers has a 2 for 1 deal going on right now. Â grab it while you can

i've been coming to this location for over 15 years, and can confidently say that it's excellent. the food, the service, the bar, the restroom - it's one classy shop that is often packed for a good reason. had dinner here tonight at the bar: one elderflower cocktail ($15) and two different sushi rolls ($16 & $18); everything very good, including the live jazz. one of the reviewers before me complained about the cost - my response to him is: it's not cheap to run a really high-quality restaurant in midtown, with consistently phenomenal service. this location just does not disappoint, but if it were to, management would remedy the issue immediately. great date spot, too.
best place on the planet, great date night, ambiance is incredible---go here
Great establishment! Very cool British vibe and tons of drinks to choose from. Definitely a fun place to get beers after work. Very nice staff as well. Would highly recommend!

As someone said the thighs are wow. Â Juicy and tender inside. Â The outside is not as salty as some fast food chains but this is fine with me. Â The chicken breast which is also included with the chicken box tastes fine, albeit not as amazing as the thighs. We also had the pull pork sandwich. Â A little messy and soggy but I thought the meat was good. We had mac n cheese and black eye peas as sides. Â The peas were cold and tasteless. Finally we shared an apple pie. Â The pie was served cold. Â A little disappointing given our high expectations. Still, I'll revisit this place again for the chicken box.

This place has incredible attention to detail. While they started off a bit hazy on their vision, at first selling chopped ingredients ready for you to cook at home, then slowly adding on prepared foods, they have transformed into a great restaurant. BYOB, and with plenty of meat-lover and veggie options, it is the food itself and the service that are truly unforgettable. The tamales are great, and the chef's vegetarian special allowed me to be truly adventurous - I could eat it all without knowing what it was! When I was there with co-workers, the server noticed it was turning into a meeting and brought over blank paper and pens for all of us. With my family when we couldn't decide whether or not to have a sweet treat, they brought one over to share on the house. They really take care of you.

I have ordered out from Pio Pio many times. But this was my first time dining in. The food is good, but it is pretty pricy for rotisserie chicken. We were seated across from the bar on the upper level next to the entrance to the kitchen - not the best ambiance. Despite our location, The service was pretty slow and it took our waiter a long time to take our order. After we got our food our water was never refilled, and we were never offered a second round of drinks. With all the great restaurants in HK -- I most likely will not return.

If you're a high maintenance diner, stay away. You'll be "on line" Â for hours with dozens of other hungry grumps and the "service" will leave a sour taste in your mouth that even the crab won't cure. So give your inner curmudgeon the night off. Choose instead to be a patient lover of frozen alcoholic beverages and putt putt. Come through and make a night of it. Gather your friends, put your name in around 6pm, and chill out on a Saturday evening. The dungeness crab in the cajun boil is the perfect summer night fishdish. You'll leave full, messy, and smiling with a belly full of hot sauce --they have at least twenty to choose from.

Breakfast martinis. Don't ask me what makes them breakfast. My friend who recommended them muttered something about marmalade. All I know is that is one delicious beverage. I still dream about the artichoke dip. If you go here and do not order it you are an absolute fool. Fool I say! I also had the club sandwich which was good but nothing too special. My companion had the mac n cheese which I did not try but which he said was similarly good but not amazing. The location on Freeman's Alley makes me feel cool and underground. As does the dead-animal decor. The wacky flailing white duck was our favorite taxidermical wall hanging. It is pretty crowded. The space is small, and we had to wait for a lunch table even on a random Tuesday. But just get a breakfast martini or two or seven at the bar and the wait will fly by.

I love this bar. LOVE it. It makes living in this sleepy little nook on the border of Park Slope & Windsor Terrace even more awesome! I've lived in this neighborhood since 1999, and have seen so many changes just west of us in Park Slope proper, the rampant over-gentrification and skyrocketing rents, the $1200 strollers, and aloof Manhattanites settling in to brood. When I heard there was a gastropub about to fill that corner on 16th & 9th Ave, I rolled my eyes and groaned. But here's the thing - the only other options for a brew or cocktail in my community were Farrell's (douchey cops, firemen & construction workers, surly bartenders who would frequently refuse service or ignore you if you weren't born within 5 blocks of the joint or had more than 2 years of education after high school) and Rythm & Booze (fine enough for a sports bar, but... meh - just try getting a cocktail with a little more thought to it than two ingredients). Enter the Double Windsor. The bar came first, and the kitchen window came second. The owners were in there putting the place together with their own hands - their pride is evident but not precious. It feels comfortable and cool - like the college hang-out you loved grew up just enough to not be annoying but still rocks it. The staff are whip-smart, super efficient and care. I always wish I could afford to tip them more. The music selection is based on whoever's ipod is on the dock... it varies from goth rock to tender love ballads, experimental electronica to deep jazz, hip hop to mmm bop. They have board games there, and you're welcome to bring your own. There always seems to be a Scrabble fest going on! The selection of beer and booze is fantastic and dead on. There are 16 craft beers on tap and they are always in a fresh rotation - once a keg is out, that's it. Love it and move on to your next discovery! Â They featured Six Point brewery a year ago, before all the hype, and made me fall in love with the Sweet Action, until I tasted Bear Republic's Apex IPA. Who knows what's next? Oh, and if you are in the wise, stop off at the gelato place a half block away for a double scoop of their vanilla. Then cozy up to the bar at the Double W, order a My Two Dads (Old Granddad Bourbon, Dad's Root Beer and bitters). Combine. Drink. Genius! (They say they don't have space for a freezer in there, but I'm working on 'em!) The food - oh, my.... I grew up in the South and never had hush puppies this good. I've tried nearly everything on the menu, and it all rocks! They are diligent about the ingredients, and their offerings are seasonal. Once they ran out of their thick sliced, center cut bacon, and so rather than running next door to the deli for a cheap substitute, they just 86ed the BLTs and mac with bacon. (It broke my heart to eat my mac without it, but I survived.) Their soups are made in-house and sustained me through last winter - sometimes I'll just order food to go if I feel like a quiet night in. The burger is otherworldly on the brioche bun! Order it with a slice of their real cheddar cheese and bacon - well... you'll roll your eyes and groan. Prost!

Mmmmmmmmm. Â I can only rate on take-away services and Cafe Habana es muy delicioso! Â We ordered the cafe leche, shredded pork w. rice and beans, and shredded pork sandwich. Â Everything was done to perfection. Â From the perfectly spiced black beans and rice to the flavorful pork (though a little greasy), I could eat this all the time. Â And I don't even like eating carbs!!!

My favorite food cart in NYC. Â Great food at an amazing price. Â However, be prepared to wait in line. Â Order the combo lamb/chicken platter with extra white sauce. Â You will not regret it, guaranteed!

The menu words make it sound so appetizing, but the Mediterranean Salad tastes like cardboard and looks like a leftover. Â Too bad, because it's close enough to my job that I could be there every day at lunchtime. Â I e-mailed the owner, which is a policy I think I will be following from now on. Â They need to know.

Loved our meal here! I could eat their corn dog for days..... We, of course, ordered the goat's neck for our main entree. Â You have to split it, but it is by for the most delicious thing i've had in weeks. Â Especially last week when I did a crazy dairy-free,gluten-free, soy-free, vegan, sugar-free cleanse! Â My taste buds yearned for something delicious, and not even bagels and lox could shake the blues off of them. Our waitress on Sunday night was great, not pushy, knowledgeable and told us that we couldn't go wrong with our choices. Â She also recommended a great beer that excellently paired with our meal. We made a reservation, but ended up not needing one. Â They have outdoor seating and beignets for dessert. Â Notice there is only one dessert option, and that's because it's the only dessert worth eating. Will be back again and again!

Came here with a group of friends to celebrate a friend's wedding. The service here is top-notch.
