Â The guys who served us were awesome; super down to earth, reliable, friendly, and at our every request. Â Among the best service I have ever gotten anywhere. The restaurant is a family oriented restaurant in the sense that when you order plates, they are meant to be shared. Â We had about 13 people, so we ordered from a preset menu they had where they charge per person and also has options for beverages (alcoholic and non-alcoholic). Â We had TONS of food...and all of it was beyond delicious. Â Chicken parm, ziti, chicken franchese, veal, shrimp, and other stuff I am totally forgetting. It was so much and SO GOOD!!! Ooo...by the way, what we paid, included appetizers and dessert. Â I am a huge dessert fan...best strawberry shortcake I have ever had. I can go on and on, but I think you can catch my drift here. I totally recommend Tony's and am totally trying to find an excuse to go here again sometime soon!
First time i went to this place, the staff was nice and friendly. Food was good and it was what you expect from a tacos place. Will go back if I walk close to it again.

Cute cafe/sandwich shop offering food made from decent fresh ingredients. The people in the kitchen clearly know what they're doing, making this a good choice for someone looking for a fast and tasty meal, but not fast food. Of course this comes at a price: sandwiches are $8-$12, which isn't outrageous, but it ain't any kind of deal. The sandwiches we had were the kale with fava bean paste and the porchetta. The kale was delicious, but it was on the salty/greasy side. This is most definitely not health food, even though veggies are represented. The porchetta did not have the rosemary flavor I associate with the classic Italian sandwich; it was more like a mild take on pernil, but it wore its caramelized onions and baby arugula well. Both were very tasty, well thought out and decent portions. Decor is upscale coffee/gourmet shop, and they sell prepared food by the pound, including fried chicken, mac & cheese and several vegetable dishes. The crowd had both the laptop and stroller battalions well represented, and the background music had acoustic guitar well enough represented so as not to scare them off. Â The vibe was maybe just a little too precious for me. That said, if I found myself in the neighborhood looking for something quick, indulgent and a little upscale without being overly posh I'd go back.

The New Yorker weekend begins in hipster enclave Williamsburg NYC with a quintessential hipster brunch. Or if you are the free spirited artist, that's how you begin every morning. Five Leaves is where i'd be headed to for a great start to the day. This small neighborhood spot draws the crowd from Manhattan and the wait could go up to 1.5h easily. Some interesting history with this one- it was opened with the backing of the late Heath Ledger in 2009 (he died before the cafe bar was opened). We waited for a bit despite it being a weekday but was rewarded with the smell of strong brews and delicious breakfast food when we stepped into the cosy cafe bar. Expect refined Australian comfort food (very similar to NYC comfort food) made from fresh, organic, sustainable, locally sourced products. Of course it has to be, it's hipster. The brews are made with Wandering Goat Coffee Co. beans from Eugene, Oregon, a small specialty coffee roaster. The huge and strong cuppa, which was served promptly, made my eyes light up at once. Wanting the best of all worlds, I ordered the Big Breakkie ($13) which came with 2 eggs of my choice (organic, free range), hash browns, whole wheat toast and choice of 2 sides. I choice my favorite avocado and gave the thick cut bacon a go. This was perfection on a plate. Beautifully folded scrambled egg that looked like a yellow rose in full bloom, addictive home made hash browns that were the best i've tasted and bacon steak (not crisps)! As much as i wanted to finish it all, i could hardly get through half the American sized portion! S had the Ricotta Pancakes ($13) with honeycomb butter, banana, blueberries, strawberries served with 100% maple syrup. This dish is so absolutely decadent! Plump fluffy disks of batter complemented by that ZOMFG honeycomb butter. Nothing in Singers is comparable to this stack of heaven. We only managed 1.5 pancakes between the 2 of us! There's quite a fair selection of healthier eats like fruit salad, house made granola toasted perfectly, muesli and oats. Breakfast is served till past noon. Those looking for something more substantial, word is that the Five Leaves Burger ($15) is so insanely wicked. Packed with grass-fed beef, house pickled beets, harissa mayo and sunny up egg, it is impossibly hard to tackle even with bear paws but that hasn't stop anyone from trying. Come nightfall, hit the bar with oysters served w/ rice wine mignonette ($15 for half doz) and all sorts of alcoholic concoction. Five Leaves open till 1am daily so your cravings will be satisfied anytime.
This place is outstanding. Mexican, pizza, burgers, sandwiches, cupcakes, etc. Come here with colleagues and everyone can be happy. Excellent food, fair prices. I recommend for a great lunch.

If there was half stars this place would get 3 and a half, Â good service and good food, very small place where you end up waiting outside. The only real gripe with the place is for how small it is it seems so disorganized and takes a while to get drinks and place orders. I only ate off brunch menu but had good options and will prob return to check out dinner.

My favorite restaurant in NY, hands down. Â The food is fantastic - for sure - but the service and the restaurant itself is why I truly love it. Â Brad, Miriam, and everyone else have consistently made every visit fantastic. Â It strikes the perfect balance between intimate date night and local neighborhood tavern. Â Tables are close but not too close, and the wait staff is attentive but not overbearing. Â It's just wonderful. Recommend: Kampachi Tartare with the little szechuan buttons to start Fois Gras mason jar, whenever it's on the menu Chili Lobster appetizers...so rich, so yummy One of the fish dishes, which change with what is fresh Any of the bread puddings if Chef Ashton has put them on that night Any of the seasonal "sundaes", particularly if there is a berry/rhubarb one!

Really happy that this place opened up as there's really no place to get authentic Hawaiian food in NYC. Â The menu is a bit limited at the moment but it still had two of my favorites: Â ahi poke and kalua pig. Â Both dishes were delicious, and between the food, the island music and photos throughout the restaurant, I felt like I was almost back in Hawaii. Â  I will definitely be back to satisfy my Hawaiian food cravings and to try the rest of their menu!

I have bookmarked Ippudo for years not knowing when I would ever go to NY to try it. I finally got to try it this past weekend and I cried a little when I got my hands on their famous pork buns! The pork buns are seriously godly. It's so simple with pork belly, lettuce, mayo & a spicy sauce and when put together it seriously brought me so much joy for the 2 bites that it lasted. I am hooked and without a doubt, I will be back for more when I'm in the city. (Planning to go toTaiwan & Japan this summer and I'm determined to go to Ippudo there and try the pork buns & ramen) I also ordered the Akamaru Modern ramen and the broth was not that great. I think we have better broth here in LA. BUT they used tonkatsu noodles that were thin, not too soft, not too hard. Perfectly firm and chewy! I love how they cooked their noodles. Also, they serve you hot green tea after your meal. Loved that!

I didn't know they had a Cocoron over here! I was walking aimlessly after leaving a lame party at a nearby bar. Â It was purely serendipitous that my friends and I should choose to walk down Kenmare. Â Passed by Cocoron but couldn't PASS it up! Â Took a step inside and ordered some warm soba! Â Friend ordered the soba tea which I did not. Â It looked so pretty and nice. Â The tea was being steeped via a nice little basket that was sitting ever so nicely in a clay cup. I had the kashiwa soba which was really good but I ninja ate some of my friends stamina soba which I thought was better. Â It tasted a bit smokier? if that's your thing. Â Noodles were perfect, broth was rich, toppings wer ... what can I say, I'm just a sucker for noodles and Japanese food. Â There's really not much else I can say. Â I'm a fan.

The Spotted Pig does everything they can do to hide the stuffy, white linen restaurant they really are. Potted plants abound outside with benches and a place to relax while waiting. The interior is a take on a country pub style, with plenty of kitsch and old-world charm. The waiters come in sneakers and t-shirts, and a sheet of brown construction paper covers each white table cloth. But the hostess and the waitstaff all know where they work, and treat a customer how you would expect. Not directly rude, but definitely aloof and uninterested. I overheard our waiter making fun of the patron at the next table for thinking a menu item was a sandwich. Speaking of sandwiches, a stop here is supposedly incomplete without a chargrilled burger with roquefort cheese ($17). It comes best medium-rare says the chef, and is served with a heaping mound of shoestring fries. I found the whole experience from start to finish extremely salty. The roquefort was definitely the most memorable part of the meal, the sheep's milk cheese definitely a good companion to a burger. Both the interesting bun and saltiness of everything got me deconstructing the burger to check out the interior. I tasted the meat on its own and it proved to be the source of the salt. The grilled on both sides bun was very well-prepared. I would have thought it were an accident had the shoestring fries and the other dish on the table not been so salty as well. The prosciutto & ricotta tart with marjoram ($18) was the more tasty of the two meals, with its ingredients standing out more from the salt than on the burger. The ricotta was especially delicious, but I feel like marjoram was used instead of oregano only to sound fancier. The tart flaked off well, and was probably the reason we waited about 25 minutes for our food to come in a fairly empty restaurant.

I went back recently and I'm still in love. One rule of advice...listen to the other Yelpers - arrive when they open. I got here this time 10 mins before they opened and a line (at least 20 people) was already formed. Luckily, I was seated instantly! This place is definitely worth every one of the stars it was rated. I'm an official fan now that I've found the cure to my 2-hour wait.

Not just for brunch. We had an out-of-town guest and were a little nervous about Cafe Gitane as the reviews emphasize brunch. However, it proved to be a perfect dinner spot. Service good, the ambiance is lovely and the chef delivers. The wine list offers a Â reasonably priced Sancerre which also makes it a winner in my book. Every member of our party was happy with the meal.

great happy hour! Â  even on sunday!! Â from 4-6pm top quality wines are only $6 a glass.. Â i was able to enjoy a german riesling from the mosel area... what a treat. Â plus they were giving away free glasses of sherry. Â two drinks for $6, what a steal. Â the staff was also very superb, letting me try various bottles and they were very knowledgeable about what was what. Â kudos!

Best Vietnamese sandwich I've had in New York, and I've tried a few very good ones. Â I highly recommend the avocado shake too! Â  The atmosphere is very unassuming, but you'll forget all about that when your teeth get around the perfectly textured baguette, and the rest of the yummy ingredients. Â I recommend the sardine sandwich too, though that might be a bit brave if it's your first time~

Come here for a meal or for to-go cappuccino, but don't come here just to sit and drink a cup of coffee. Â The seating in both the back and the front is reserved for those having lunch/dinner, as I was told when I stopped in on a snowy afternoon to drink cappuccino and do a little writing. Â I was given a seat directly next to the coat check, a sort of odd place in between all the action. Â I didn't mind all that much, however, as the hostess was polite in explaining the policy to me and setting me up in my in-between place. Â What I did mind was the "I don't give a damn" attitude I encountered from the counter girl, who obviously lacked personality, manners, and customer service knowledge. Â The rest of the staff was quite friendly. Â  I love the atmosphere here- cozy, casual, and authentic European. Â The creamy cappuccino is some of the best I've had in Manhattan and the food is fantastic. Â On a previous visit I enjoyed a fresh panini. Â Everything that comes out of the kitchen looks delectable. Â A must visit.

Dinosaur Bar-B-Que has a legion of loyal fans up and down the state, and for good reason. I first became aware of this saucy phenomenon at a college reunion in central New York a couple of years ago: the bbq was served at a picnic, drawing a massive line. Then, my brother hosted his birthday here over the summer, so I went in for a deeper look. The familiar Gowanus location is a smart choice: plenty of square footage for the outdoor beer garden/picnic table setup that greets you in front of the building (I'm noticing this trend in other former warehouse neighborhoods, including Williamsburg). Once inside, the rustic lodge decor helps you settle in quickly, even quicker with one of the great beers on tap (can'g go wrong with a Victory DirtWolf or Other Half IPA). Once we were at the table, our server (I wish I could remember his name to compliment him) took great care with our ESL family, navigating the parents through the uncharted waters of a BBQ menu while keeping my brother's kids happy. Then the parade of all things fried began. The appetizers are well worth trying--just as long as you understand that your gut is only so big--leave some room for meat, is what I'm saying. But you'll definitely want some fried green tomatoes and deviled eggs (make sure to try the spicy options and the dipping sauce). The main event was as good as the under-cards: chicken, ribs, and brisket were all delicious. I didn't have stomach enough to fully enjoy it (and, truth be told, my palate for BBQ is not the rarest), but I would definitely do it again. If only to try all the different sauces on the table. Oh, and dessert was also solid, btw.
Great tapas and sangria. Small and intimate great date place..just keep yer eye out for it or you will walk right by!

Kelly Kapowski sighting! Â  Yes, I saw Tiffani Amber Thiessen dining here with her family. I didn't get all weird about, nor was it the highlight of my life, but hey...I won't lie, it does add a little something special to the brunch experience at Buttermilk Channel. I mean really, how many Cheerio childhood breakfasts did I enjoy while watching Kelly conquer Bayside High? Many! So, it was nice to have her around for this one, too. Regardless, I finally made it to Buttermilk Channel after several foiled attempts. We rolled up about 12:45 on a Saturday, were faced with a 30 minute wait, crowded around the bar (not a lot of inside waiting room, fwiw) and took in former-TV-cheerleader speckled crowd. At precisely 30 minutes our group of 4 was ushered back, squarely situated with ample coffee, mimosas (one complimentary with brunch!), bloody marys. Orders were placed for short rib hash, porkchop waffles, pepper and sausage scramble, and other delicacies. OH! And a jelly douhgnut amuse bouche that sent our blood sugar and attitudes soaring. The food was on point. I won't rave on and on about it, but certainly it was not disappointing. My short rib hash was a bit average, but the pork chop and waffles were killer. Service = excellent. Crowd = large. Weekends = crazy. A great stop in Carroll Gardens...next time, I'll shoot for weekday brunch/lunch, maybe then I'll see Screech or Lisa Turtle!

Sublime - went Labor Day, so able to get a table. Hostess held table as we were late due to traffic, with a smile and no attitude. Had a great table and knowledgeable server who really went out of her way to see that we enjoyed our experience. Â Was with two friends, who were equally impressed. Â Excellent menu, excellent wines, all around 5 star experience. Â Only problem - trying to get a table not on a holiday :/ but will keep trying as this is the kind of place you would never get tired of visiting..

I went to Borough last weekend for the first time for dinner and drinks. The bar tender was very friendly and had great drink recommendations. I had the butterscotch martini and the Manhattan.They have a great menu of specialty drinks but also have good well drinks for $4 and $5. The dinner menu had good variety. We had the jerk chicken which was super tender and seasoned well. We also had the catfish bites and the salmon cakes, both delicious. I definitely want to go back to try the other options. It's a new restaurant, still coming into its own. It definitely has long term potential to be a great neighborhood staple.

Cozy, authentic, kitschy, and fun with speedy service and a diverse menu, Sake Bar Hagi is bound to have something for everyone. The service was good, especially the one guy who kept coming back to refill my tea. He get's 5 stars. My group of four also arrived a bit in waves. They were nice enough to seat two of us first since we waited the 20 minutes for the table and immediately placed orders to get things rolling while the 3 other slowpokes made their way in. Takowasa octopus marinated in wasabi - so delish Kushi mori set A (chicken, pork belly, duck, pepper) tasty! Tofu steak with mozzarella - odd, but not bad Edamame - par Hamaguri (clams) very salty, would skip Okonomiyaki - can't beat it if its hot! Salmon and plain rice ball (onigiri)- this thing is the size of a softball Kimchi fried rice - good. I really would like to come back and try more things!

When I want to treat myself to some seriously good food without the hassle of finding a new place, this is my go to spot. The ambiance is great, food is delicious and the service staff is friendly. This place is definitely on the pricier side but you get what you pay for. They have a huge variety of appetizers. So I'd recommend that you order those and share instead of ordering entrees. The service staff will also recommend that to you. 5-6 appetizers between two people should be more than enough. Definitely try their Brussels sprouts and lamb sausage. Took off a point for their cocktails 'cause they're just ok. But the food and dessert are best of the best. You'll certainly want to come back again.

got here right when it opened, and had absolutely no wait on a weekday during christmas week. the akamaru modern ramen is to die for. i will dream of the hot steaming broth, the chewy noodles and the slices of pork belly -- 95% fat, 5& meat -- for weeks and months to come. the pork buns were delicious and pleasantly spicy; my only wish is that they come 4 to a plate instead of just two for $7. me wantee pork buns!

Great breakfast! Â We got there at 10:00 and waited an hour and forty-five minutes for a table. Â But not to worry, there's several coffee and tea spots just up the block. By the time we were seated at 11:45, the wait was 2 1/2 hours. Â The hostess tried to seat us at tiny counter in front of the door...couldn't even move my arms. Â They told us it would be another 10 minutes if we waited for a table...having already invested half the morning...we waited. Â 30 seconds later a table magically became available. Â We ordered the blueberry pancakes about the Southern breakfast and shared. Â The pancakes...pretty dam good. Â Just don't pour then syrup on top since it will just soak right in. Â The Southern breakfast was good and we ordered a biscuit on then side. Â The biscuit was great, but would have been better if it was served at least warm. Â Oh but the cheese....YUM! Great wait staff!

One minute there's a living octopus slowly dying in my mouth and the next minute I hear my friends singing Happy Birthday to me. A waiter out of nowhere dons an afro wig onto me, passes a fairy wand and a beer with a candle taped to it, and all you can hear from the entire restaurant (I shit you not) is "chug chug chug". What in the world?

my friend corey (an "Upstate groupie" as dubbed by the owner himself, lol) turned me on to this place, probably right before the tipping point when it became uber popular (translation: manageable wait times). the oysters are totally on point, shucked perfectly with just the right amount of brine left on the half shell. the beer selection is stellar, and the bartender makes sure you drink what you like by offering a few sips, or recommending something that's similar to your favorite beer. friendly, unpretentious staff. casual ambiance, good crowd. amazing happy hour deal. Â i will be back for sure!

Possibly one of the best late night places I've found in New York. Usually at the end of a night of hitting up expensive beer bars in the city, the funds are depleted and my palate is blown. Enter Hagi. A secret little place, down a flight of steps with barely a sign outside. The waiting list is a great idea, they give you a call when your table is ready, so you don't have to cram into the little waiting area outside the door. Dont' go here with more than four or five people. You won't be able to fit. In short, cheap plates of food, cheap pitchers of beer, and a sake list that is pretty darn good. Ask the server for help with the sake, they actually know their stuff. You can impress your out-of-town friends with your knowledge of this little secret underground bar.

Very cheap sandwiches and drinks. Compare to what I was paying in Fidi for the Banh Mi from the trucks I was amazed on how much food you can get with $4-4.50. The place is actually quite large and clean although just a few benches for seating. But honestly with Banh Mi you don't really have to eat it sitting down anyway so I can see how they designed their store to be more like get the food and leave. The jewelry counter was bit surprising I suppose its something to look at while you're waiting :) But the wait wasn't long at all my sandwich was ready in under 5 minutes very quick. Place is cash only as I would expect and they aren't particularly friendly pretty much typical of any Chinatown places you will find. The Cha Siu Banh Mi I thought was pretty good although maybe too much veggies and not enough meat, but the Cha Siu I got was quite moist and juicy and bread was decent as well. For the price you pay I would definitely come here more given the chance. With all the glowing reviews it's nice to see this place still maintain the good quality that yelp's been giving it.
Loved it! Sat at the bar corner. Jory was our waiter, great service! The cheese plate, some good vino and pasta dinner...all yums! Recommend to all

Food-4 Decor-5 Service-5 This is a good place for a date or power lunch. Both times I came, saw somebody famous. I came here twice in one week. The idea is that everything is farm grown and fresh. I got the Local to drink, it was a vegetable juice- very delicious- veggieish with a kick. I tried different stuff there-the barley soup, the bowtie pasta, beet salad, fish. it was all very good and incredibly fresh. I will say this- I went with four people and 2 weren't impressed 2 loved it. Its healthy, fresh and original. A nice and pleasant comforting meal.

Really loved sharing small plates with a group of friends. No reservation on a beautiful night to dine with the windows/doors open and we got right in. The waitress was great and our food came quickly despite how busy they were. I ate far too much fresh warm pita bread and enjoyed the various things to dig them in. Â Everything was great but the feta stuffed filo dough was to die for.
i got food poisoning, and everything was super greasy. Â pass.
My Favorite Pizza place on the east coast well worth the hour wait

Atmosphere is nice for a date. Food was delicious and the dessert was even better! The service was mediocre. I would say maybe a little under staffed? The pasta here isn't over cooked so if you like completely cooked pasta, you won't like the pasta here. The pasta tastes a bit uncooked and has a slight crunch.

I've had brunch here twice and both times I had a great time. We were seated quickly, the waitstaff was friendly, the ricotta pancakes were amazing, and my party was satisfied. I tasted a bite of my friend's waffles with nutela and mascarpone, and they were delectable as well. No complaints at all, though I haven't been here for any other meal. Would recommend!

Really good food!! I always get the corn, steak with white rice and black beans, fried sweet plantains, and nice alcoholic beverage! It's extremely small so you're sitting a foot away from the next person (if you're lucky, its probably less) . If it's your first date then it can be a bit awkward because it feels like people are listening in or looking at you. Service is a bit on the slow side so go if you have some time because every time i have gone it has been busy. There might be a half hour wait but it's worth it. Don't go with a large bag, or a ton of shopping bags! There is no room for it. NOW GO! treat your taste buds to a nice meal!
always a fest.
One of the fav place which I do not miss whenever I visit NY. Great food, nice environment and live band make the night so wonderful.

To be fair, I don't eat meat. Â I came here with a friend that was in the mood for a hamburger. Â I ordered what might be the one item on the menu that didn't have meat, a grilled cheese sandwich. Â And to be fair, I'm a bit of a snob when it comes to my Â grilled cheese. Â It doesn't have to be fancy, but it has to be good. Â Unfortunately what was presented to me the first time was cold and congealed. Â I was going to just suck it up and eat it, but the bartender heard me say to my friend that it was cold. Â He said he'd take care of it. Â I'm always weary about returning food, especially in a place I'm not familiar with. Â But eventually a warmed sandwich came out. Â It was ok. Â The bread was not crisp, and it really had no taste. Â  I'd suggest sticking to beer here as the mixed drinks seems a bit watered down. Â  Overall, an ok place but I won't be schleping back to Brooklyn just to go there.
I adore this place!! Â Delicious salads, burgers, entrees. Great ambiance. Â Very nice, friendly staff. Â This is the best restaurant in Brooklyn Heights! Â I highly recommend it!

Food 3/5 Experience 4/5 3 story building in hell's kitchen. We were up on the 3rd floor. Really cute, little hourglass details hidden everywhere. Service was great. Menu was okay. I wasn't blown away by the choices. Our party ordered the lamb special, lobster ravioli, pork chop, pecan crusted tilapia and spicy shrimp. The lamb was not cooked properly, so wasn't as tender as it should have been. But still had great flavor. Lobster ravioli was tasty, sauce was slightly bland. Pork chop was cooked well but the dipping sauce was unimpressive. Pecan crusted tilapia was well balanced and cooked perfectly. Spicy shrimp was also done well, sriracha dipping sauce was unique! For dessert we ordered the molten chocolate cake and the flourless chocolate cake. Both were average! Its a unique intimate place, great for friends catching up or having a casual night.

If you go early enough to beat the weekend brunch rush (around 10:30 on a Saturday and we didn't have to wait) and with a small enough party, this place is yum-ee. Â The corn is so good, I would consider going just to stuff my face with that. Â I wish it was a little bigger. I guess I just said what everyone else just did...

I went there for the second time and brought my friends hoping it would be as good as the first time. Service and food were good. We each got a set of food and dessert even though we had to wait an hour and half before seated. But at the very end when we asked for the check, our waiter came back a couple times telling us: "the suggested tip is printed on the bill and that is the Minimum Required amount you pay". Okay, I know some Asians are cheap on tips but I always pay at least 20% for dinner unless I'm pretty dissatisfied with the service. It was rude that he came by multiple times assuming we were cheap. I was upset but still paid 20% for that dinner based on the earlier service he provided. But I am pretty sure that I won't go back.

The food was very good, but they are extremely bold in their *surprise!* pricing, which means I will never be going back there again. I went there with a party of 5, and we ordered appetizers and Sangria. Â After the apps, we ordered an entrÃ© each. Â The food was great, some of the best quality I have had anywhere, after being a Brooklyn Natve for 28 years and travelling all over the world. They would have gotten a 1 star review, if their appetizers and entrÃ©s weren't unbelievably good. So, whats the problem? I never experienced such sticker shock on a check before. Â The entrÃ©s were reasonably priced but the Sangria we ordered was a relatively small portion, and they had the balls to charge $45 for it. Â  On top of that, they automagically add 20% gratuity to a check for a party of 5, which is absurd. Â 20% is a high end tip, 15-18% is the normal automatic amount for large parties. Â And large parties are normally 7 or 8+ people, not 5+, which is the average size of a family. In the end, the jug of borderline-decent sangria cost me $54, and management was unwilling to budge. If my sister didn't LOVE the place and I knew she would be going back, I would have dropped cash on the table for the food, $20 for sangria, and no tip. All in all, a modest dinner for 5 people cost me $220 ($44/person). Yes, maybe I should have checked the menu more clearly, but there is a range of prices you expect with something like Sangria (which should be in the $15 to $35 range). Â Charging $54 for Sangria is absurd. If you do go to this place, you will enjoy the food, but watch for the menu and hidden charges. Â  If you do have a problem with the bill, don't expect management to be accommodating. Â They will just placate you and cite "policy", which anyone with a brain knows that is a load of BS.
No idea why it is so popular. Altered to cater American's needs. But not very Japanese style.

We returned for a full dinner at Aita tonight, and it was fantastic. Every course was done to perfection, service was attentive and we will definitely be back! My husband had pork terrine--served as delicious croquettes with a yummy beet salad--and the braised lamb. Both were cooked well and beautifully presented. I had the octopus appetizer and squid ink pasta with broccoli rabe and clams. The octopus was done to perfection -- tender and juicy, but not overlooked, served with fingerling potatoes and beans. My pasta was exceptional -- blanched broccoli rabe and al dente pasta with a generous portion of clams. We shared the pumpkin tart dessert with vanilla ice cream and cinnamon crumble, which was the perfect Fall treat. Overall, great meal and definitely recommend!
Good chicken, but overpriced. I didn't like the mac & cheese or the grits.

It's nothing to look at, and there were water spots on the glassware, but the food is top notch and cheap. The spftshell crab was nice, and the BBQ pork over rice was great. The place is also BYOB! It got super crowded around 7 on a Friday, but you can luck out if you opt to share a table.
Love the lobster ravioli. This place always has amazing quick service and the freshest food. Can't get any better than that!

It took about half an hour to be seated - this was fine considering that it was a Friday night and because this is really the only sit down restaurant on Newkirk for many blocks. My friend and I hung out by the bar as we waited. Â The ambience is cool and it's vibrant. I had the cornmeal crusted catfish, which was good.
This place never gets old! Best time to go? Late night munchies after clubbing. Mac n cheese will make you go to bed fat and happy! Hehe!

This place is so good, I have recently been going here almost every day. Everything on the menu is great and you can't go wrong. The only downside is its cash only and sometimes the waiters are hard to get ahold of.

Little Collins is a true gem in an area (Midtown East step it up!) lacking in great coffee places. Â Not only do the brew delicious coffee (my latte was great), they also make scrumptious food. Â As an avocado addict, I am in love with The Smash - avocado smashed with feta cheese on a thick slice of toast, sprinkled with pepita seeds and chili flakes. Â Heaven is real. Â Aside from their food menu, they also offer an extensive array of pastries. Although tiny and sometimes cramped during a rush, Little Collins a lovely environment for enjoying coffee, food, conversation, and if need be, work.

This store is complete beauty. The macarons adorn the store and it's as colorful as a candy store. walked here after roaming through central park and tasted each flavor on the steps of the Met which is about 5 minutes away walking. My favorite flavors were Pistachio, Strawberry and Coffee. Simple flavors that bursts in your mouth. I love how they choose to fill the macarons with different fillings. It was an unexpected surprise and very welcoming. In terms of comparison, I have had better macarons from other stores but I do believe these made me extremely happy. Well worth the walk, well worth the indulgence =]
Wonderful pizza! Must eat here.

I love this place so much. I have never gone wrong with the salad. it is huge. a bun without the fun? haha. I am in love with their chicken pho broth but i get it with shrimp or veggies because they char the chicken. I don't prefer the bitterness of the chard chicken. I like their summer rolls. I don't suggest going there in the morning hours.. it is a little quiet around 6 pm

My Rating: Shuttle yourself here right now!! Mr. Quinn, mighty indeed. I had a blast eating here. Everything was on point. The baked beans had tons of brisket ends in it, the ribs were succulent and had a nice dry rub and the brisket was arousing. EVERYTHING was awesome. I told my P.I.C. that trying to decide what I liked the best was like choosing between great and excellent dishes. A conundrum I will take any day. This is usually the part where I balance my analysis with some negatives, but I have none. The sides were all awesome. I had all the pickles and slaw. They were excellente. Had the fries. Fresh out of the fryer, thick and crunchy. Forget Fette Sau. Meet Mr. Quinn.

Did you know "panini" is Italian for "overpriced sandwich"? I think the process involves burning Tolstoy first editions and Monet masterpieces to stoke the panini press. I dunno. But I do know where you can find a good overpriced sandwich. This place. The roasted chicken with spicy mayo is worth the destruction of a few priceless objets d'art, though when they say spicy mayo, they are not misrepresenting the condiment, sirs and madams. By the end of the meal my nose was running, my eyes watering and I may or may not have been gnawing through my hand, arm and/or plate. Difficult to judge when your face is paralyzed. And though I'm certain I looked like a leaking and deranged lunatic, I truly enjoyed my meal. Oh yes- do try the desserts. I mashed a red velvet cupcake into a hole I can only assume was my benumbed mouth. I will also be forced to assume it was delicious judging by the way it looked, though my tastebuds were unable to confirm due to the holy hellfire in which they were engulfed.

The only reason I don't give five stars is because I have nothing really to compare. Â Been here a few times. Had the meatball sub, breakfast wrap, buffalo sandwich. I have never been vegan, but could make the move with places like this. Favorite was the meatball sub, then buffalo, then the breakfast wrap. Â The breakfast wrap was the least desirable, but still good. Thankful I found this place.

Raitng for service and cost. Â As a loyal customer since 2006, I am sad to say Cafe Henri has forgotten its root customer base and has now gone commercial. Â No longer is this an institution for great food and ambiance it has now become a cash cow for the owners of the restaurant. Rising costs are an inevitable part of life but a double whammy has occurred when portion size have also been cut. Â The same burger ordered five years ago has seemingly become much smaller yet prices are have not and in fact risen. Â  Shame on you!

Just came here to try out the corn and it was worth the visit, if you want a quick snack to tie you over between lunch and dinner you have to come by to this place where it seems to be packed any time of day.
Great, quirky atmosphere, great food. Such a different place to go for brunch. Will definitely go again.

Incredible! Some of the best Thai food I have ever eaten! We found a seat without trouble, service was excellent, and the food was a knockout! Plus, our bill was ridiculously low. Â I was scared to eat out in NYC, but this was less than we might have spent back in San Jose. Highly recommended!

I was looking forward to this place, but was sorely disappointed. I never take the time to write reviews, but this was so awful I had to. Food was decent, but service was atrocious. I'd only recommend for people that want expensive fast food as you have slightly less than an hour to complete your meal. As a daughter of a restaurant owner and chef, as well as having managed restaurants, I don't think they are worthy of repeat business or anything but poor word of mouth marketing. Very offended to have dropped so much money to not have time to eat everything we ordered. Restaurants in Chinatown have more tact. I recommend many restaurants and lounges and this will not be one of them.

Walked in here tonight on a whim without knowing what to expect, and we were blown away. The food was fantastic, the atmosphere great and the staff warm and friendly. The highlights of the meal were the lamb, ribs, broccoli salad and spaghetti squash, each better than the last. They are familiar dishes, but prepared exquisitely. It was one of the best meals I've had in a long time, we will definitely be back!

I think this is probably my favourite bar in Williamsburg. I came here pretty early in the day and stayed for most of it. Make sure you get the "Texas Two Step" (Red Star & Tequila). Also has one of the best bartenders around in Tyler, very nice guy. The bar was quiet as it was early but I have been told that the atmosphere is excellent at peak time. Would definitely recommend.

This is by far my favorite Thai place since I've moved here. It's the only place I've seen the food get as close to authentic as I want it to be. I had the roast pork soup and it was delicious. We also had curried chicken puffs..which seems to be quite the popular dish in NY and those were ok...a little sweet for my taste and no dipping sauce. I'd go for something else next time. The other weird thing...no Siracha... But the food is super awesome. It's normal people portions and the prices aren't too bad. It's a little small, but it's a buzzing busy atmosphere.

The first time I went to Grimaldi's, it was early on a Monday night in January. There was no wait at 6:30 p.m. and the restaurant was virtually empty. The pizza was delicious and we were so happy that we'd made the trek over the Brooklyn Bridge for this pizza that we'd heard such great things about! The second time was a warm Saturday evening in May. The line snaked down the block. I thought to myself, "Was this pizza really so good that I'm willing to wait in this line to eat it again?" But my parents were with me and we'd already walked across the bridge, so we just decided to wait in the line, which, surprisingly, moved quickly. We waited less than an hour to be seated. And the answer to my question was "Yes." This pizza is ridiculously delicious. By far, the best I've ever had. I live in D.C. now and miss it so much.

One of the best places in the Village. I love the classic banh mi, which is $5. The pork chop vermicelli ($8) is another staple of mine. But really, you can't go wrong. Note: it gets very crowded at peak hours
Great mojitos, interior design with no personality.

***This review is for BRUNCH only*** Nothing terrible, but nothing memorable either. I had wanted to dine at Jane for the longest time because I had heard so many great reviews about their brunch in particular. Overall, decent, casual brunch spot but I don't think it's worth the wait. There will usually be a long line of people (usually girls) crowding outside waiting for a table. If you are seated by the door (which i was), you will likely have people hanging around behind you waiting for you to turn the table over. Service was surprisingly fast, given how crowded it was. I liked their freshly squeezed orange juice (very fresh!) and you will be served a cold bread basket with two types of bread and strawberry butter. I tried the eggs benedict johnny, which came as two poached eggs on top of a chicken sausage pattie, served on two corn pancakes. It was OK. I also tried my friend's regular eggs benedict. That was OK as well. Portions are a good size to feel full with just the main course. Would I return? Unless I could slide right in without waiting, probably not - I do think Jane is a tad-bit overhyped.
A good restaurant. The bread is tasty. but the lobster inside is a little cold. Making it not a good enough combination.
Sadly, not that great. Just mediocre..but for a city that in my opinion has the best Italian in the world, it's sorta blah. Cool place for a drink though.

Loses one star because of the inefficient seating process. Did anyone go to business school and take operations 101 before designing this?! They text you when your table is ready and will leave the empty table waiting 10 minutes until you arrive. So what happens if you decide not to come after you receive the text? After 10 minutes, the hostess will text party #2 and give them 10 minutes to arrive. And in that 20 minute time frame, party #3 could have been served breakfast. Hence the infamous two-hour wait that is well-known for this establishment. Once seated, service was quick Â and the pancakes and french toast were amazing (they look exactly as they do in all of the pictures posted). Actually worth every calorie. Remember to 1) Bring cash since place is cash-only and 2) Bring sneakers because you will have enough time to fit in a full two-hour workout during the wait time. Well worth it though!

This place is delicious. So delicious. There's great deals, especially for lunch. Â If you're looking for some good traditional lunch food that even the Japanese frequent often this is the place to go.

A very fun place for drinks with friend and a bite to eat. Â I highly recommend the cherry cosmo- it's not too sweet and the cherry provides a nice change from every other cosmo. Â The cucumber fizz is also very nice and light (good for a cool-down on a hot summer night). Â Food-wise my experience is more limited- the fries are good but the truffle fries are a bit disappointing. Â They use a different fry (thinner, crispier) and it's a bit unevenly seasoned. Â The sweet-chili wings are delicious but make sure you specify spicy (if you want any heat). Definitely going back.

Service is impeccable! The location is a good location. Its right off Lexington so accessible by the 4,5,6 on 59th or 42nd (Grand Central). The black linguine is so good! One of the best dishes I've eaten. Compliments to their head chef(s). Will be back! Thanks
Everything is delicious!

This place was wonderful, but super crowded on a Sunday. Â I would totally love to return on like a Monday afternoon. Â  I had a panini which was awesome. Â The bread was baked pizza dough split like a sandwich roll. Â It had prosciutto, mozzarella and arugula on it. Â It was really simple, but tasty because of the quality ingredients. Â  We ate at one of the stand up tables, walked around for a minute and left. Â It was so busy and crazy, I wanted to explore more, but I couldn't handle the crowds.

Awesome place to eat. Food was very good and the portions were generous. The staff were professional. The best part was, for a sit down, white table cloth restaurant, the price was really quite reasonable. Â I've spent the same amount for crappy food and lousy service in NYC. Â Worth the trip.

First the cheesecake - was fantastic. Got the regular 'ol strawberry cheesecake and couldn't finish the whole piece. Yes it's everything they say it is. Now, let's talk lunch. While I totally appreciate the bowl of pickles you get (and yes I ate them all), I wasn't a gigantic fan of the food (or the prices). So I got a pastrami sandwich, and yeah the thing was gigantic, but it was WAY too much, and not really all that good. I only ate about 4 bites of it before I couldn't handle it anymore. Maybe I'm just a sissy. Besides the food being pretty "meh", it was pretty expensive for lunch. Really should have just gone to a mom and pop shop around the corner or something. The three stars are mostly for the cheesecake, though I wish I could separate them.

Not a huge coffee-drinker but LOVEEEE the Flat White here! Â So creamy and delicious, and the barista certainly seemed to know what he was doing. Â It's a tiny place with not much seating, but maybe that adds to its charm a little bit. Â Also got a pastry here which was delicious.
One of the most incredible meals I have ever had.

Just came back from Thirsty Koala and was compelled to write a review. Amazing experience, amazing staff and amazing food. From the lamb lollies to the crostinis to the prawn tacos, everything was top notch. Even though they are not currently serving alcohol, we actually enjoyed bringing our own wine, free of charge! Our crowd consisted of vegetarians, meat eaters and vegans and all were satisfied. Can't wait to go back and try some new things!!!!!

Great but totally average. Came in Sunday for brunch and signed in for the waiting list - the host was very welcoming and kept us updated on wait time. We ordered French toast and eggs Benedict that came quite quickly but disappointed and pancakes that were fresh and fluffy - very recommend. The place is good for a quick brunch but don't expect anything more.

A friendly yet not overly-attentive staff and a fine menu! Lots of space to dine, and the delicious menu options are totally affordable, especially considering the location. Having been to Siggy's twice in two days, I've had the pleasure of trying the absolutely outrageous roasted artichoke salad, which was sprinkled with a tangy, fresh parmesan cheese; the freshest beet carrot apple juice I've had in a while, to which I added some ginger (and when I didn't really like the taste of the first round of the juice, the barista remade it without complaint or extra charge until it was perfect); and a delectable bone-dry cappuccino. I work in the area, and am stoked to go back for lunch on Monday!

Introduced this spot to a few friends that came up from DC. Again it was an hour and a half wait (this time we went to doughnut plant for a snack while waiting). HOWEVER, to make customers waiting happily, they brought out samples for us to try! Buttermilk pancakes with maple syrup. It was deeeeelicious and led me to order that for my meal when we finally got in. Definitely the fluffiest pancakes I've ever had and the syrup is amazing! Even my friends were raving about it hours after the meal!

Thanks Yelp, we drove from Forest Hills to the City for something different. Â Someone mentioned Williamsburg and found Rye because of the volume of reviews. Â  The food was terrific, but almost overshowed by the cocktails Â The Old Fashions are dead on, with 1 1/2 inch cube of ice (one cube). Â Crab cake with the jalepeno/ avacado salsa was perfect. Â My shrimp/ scallop kabab had a nice kick, but probably not for the guy looking to fill up. Â The St. Louis Ribs, wet, were finger licking good. Â My party of 4 will be back!! The only downer was the service. Â The staff was knowledgable and friendly, but seemed to be forget about us.

Pork Katsu is served on top of a mound of rice covered with japanese style curry. Thank god for the fresh cabbage that accompanies the dish...otherwise it'd be a pretty heavy dish. Good food. fantastic price. No reason to give this place less than 4 stars.

We went here this past weekend for brunch after weeks of deliberation - it is, after all, a ten block hike from the 30th Avenue N/Q train station. But fair weather and good spirits carried us there, and we were seated promptly by our friendly waitress. A little pushy, she started her sales pitch on the cocktails as soon as we sat down, and we listened politely before ordering coffees. The brunch menu is great, simple concepts with innovative execution, such as omelets, pizzas, burgers and sides. We ordered the hangover pizza and the L'italiano, Italian toast smothered in ricotta cheese, topped with hot soppressata and then finished off with two poached eggs. The coffee is strong and delicious, and the service was super speedy. After waiting about ten minutes, maybe twelve, we had ourselves a huge thin-crust pizza large enough for us to have split between us, and some delectable poached eggs, Italian-style. Everything was delicious, fresh-made with quality ingredients and cooked perfectly. The pizza can get a little messy, as the numerous toppings, sausage, tomatoes, fried eggs, potatoes, weighs down the pizza dough and makes it a little difficult to pull slices apart and then try to maneuver an effective eating style. But, still quite fun to attempt! We took a look at the dessert menu but nothing caught our fancy so we passed. The waitress acted a little disappointed, and tried to convince us to at least split something, even a lighter dessert like the panna cotta, but we passed and just asked for the check. Aside from the somewhat pushy service, a really great brunch-time experience. If we are in the neighborhood again, maybe on our way to the park or just feel like a brisk afternoon walk sometime, we will definitely stop by again. This place definitely exceeded our expectations. Plus it played great music and had a cool, easygoing vibe.

A lot of beautiful people in a very beautiful space. Very clean table dressing: butcher paper place mats, cardboard drink coasters. The setting was an intimate shabby chic of handmade porcelain tableware and your grandmother's floral butter plates...loved it! I joined friends at ABC Kitchen for brunch last Sunday afternoon. The flavors were a bit overwhelming. I ordered the french toast which was completely covered in cinnamon...great, if you like cinnamon (which I don't). My friend ordered the smoked salmon with a potato pancake and creme fraiche...she thought the flavors overpowered her ability to enjoy and stopped short of completing the meal. I'd like to return for dinner and try a few other items on the menu before I make my final decision about ABC Kitchen.

Came for brunch with friends. Â One of us was lucky enough to get our names in before a massive rush so the wait wasn't too ridiculous. The only negative aspect was having to wait in a crowd and getting bumped into all the time before we could get our table. Â Also, we had to be really aggressive with the hostess to make sure we got seated. Once we sat down though, the meal and service was good. Â I had the lemon pancakes, scrambled eggs, potatoes, and coffee. A little pricey (about 30$ a person) but I would come back again, just not as a regular.

Had the Minced Pork with Onions for lunch. 11 bucks. The Katsu had a crispy and flaky crust, the meat was tender and juicy, The katsu is further enhanced with a awesome soy dipping sauce and mustard with a nice kick. The cabbage dressing was nice a refreshing nicely offsetting the oiliness of the katsu. Overall its a well thought out and successful product. With my bowl of white sushi rice i was happily satisfied.

We went to Cafeteria and waited at the bar area for our table (even though we were told we didn't need reservations when we called). The bar area smelled like filthy dishrag. The sloppy mess of some mystery sauce on the floor at our table was cleaned up only after we asked. Our waiter took our order and did not make another appearance until he rudely threw the check on our table (after we had to ask the busboy for it). We sat with empty drinks and dirty dishes in front of us. If there was a manager, he certainly wasn't supervising. Totally disappointing experience and we vow to NEVER return to Cafeteria. THUMBS DOWN!!

Attractive artwork, pretty place and the food is quite good. Â I've been to parties in their private rooms downstairs, and they were very well executed. Â However, before a concert across the street at Carnegie Hall, the restaurant is extremely crowded and the tables very close together. I wouldn't say the waiters were rude, just extremely rushed. Â  Sometimes eating there felt like I was on a conveyor belt: get me in, seated, fed, pay, out, next.

COCKROACH ON THE TABLE. Saw a huge cockroach walk onto the table and the manager was very unapologetic. His exact words were: "There's been a construction going on right next door and all the roaches are out to find a new home. BUT OUR RESTAURANT IS NOT DIRTY. I'M TELLING YOU, OUR RESTAURANT IS NOT DIRTY." The decent thing he could've done was apologize and make compensations but he did not do either and kept arguing there was no way they can refund our payment. In conclusion, ask at the reception if there's still a construction going on and if they say yes, try another time when it might be a little more hygenic like they blindly argue that they are.

Best. Cocktails. Ever. Ask for Tim. Don't go here to drink beer. Â Don't go here to drink mixed drinks. Â Go here to fall in love with the cocktail again. Â These guys seriously care about the art that is the cocktail. Â Start with something off the menu, and then just let them choose after that. These days I usually just pick a type of alcohol and let them take it from there. Also, they pull no punches here - these are solid cocktails, so plan on a cab or to stumble home! Addendum: Their steaks are PHENOMENAL! Â I have had both the rib-eye and the strip, and they were both the best steaks I have had in quite a long time. Â They server them with rock salt! Â Pure class!

Some of the BEST ramen I've ever had (well, maybe second to Na Ni Wa in Dusseldorf, Germany). This is such a tiny place, so like everyone else is saying - be prepared to wait! I must have gotten really lucky because I didn't have to wait at all. (Come right after they open for lunch, maybe?) I got the Totto Spicy Ramen. Again, I reiterate: SO GOOD. I can tolerate really spicy stuff, and I was sweatin', but I don't regret my choice since it was just so good. Reasonable prices, great ramen, great service - what more can you ask for?!
i went with my relatives, i thought the food was not bad, but my dad said his meatball tasted funky (like it's going bad)....very good service though.

Tinaaaaaaaaaa i ruv you. I've only gotten the spicy chicken platter with rice and beans and/or fries and it is just so effing flavorful and good and i lurve the green sauce and you get such a huge mofo mound of food and i am such a fricking fan of tina's but i really wish they gave you more sauce. TINA! STOP BEING STINGY WITH YOUR SAUCE. Â UNLESS THE GREEN COLORING COMES FROM THE JUICE OF BENJAMINS (i hope not) HOOK US UP WITH MORE GREEN SAUCE. Thanks.
Great location. Â The customers are awesome. Â Food was very satisfying. The neighborhood ladies were in for their Sunday night dinner.

I'll be so bold as to say that these aren't the best fries I've ever had. They're good, yea, but I wouldn't consider them the BEST. But the sauces...now that's a different story! Mango chutney? Parmesan Peppercorn? Holy Jesus their sauces are amazing. I mix BBQ with Parmesan Peppercorn. Free samples are always fun, and when you do give your order, make sure you ask for the sauce on the fries--not in a separate container. (If you're cute and smile, they'll give you an extra pump if you ask.)

I don't know why I don't go here more often! I went for the first time a few years ago and then again a few weeks ago and it was fantastic. I LOVE the ambiance-- such a cool space and fantastic service. When I first arrived and was waiting for my friend to arrive, the hostess said there wouldn't be a wait if he arrived soon. I rushed him and by the time he came, there was no table but she said we could sit at the bar. It was a spacious bar, a really awesome bartender and we were more than happy sitting there. Amazing people watching especially from the bar where there is a mirror high up on the wall that allows you to look up at people. We shared a few dishes: Coconut pancakes with fresh ricotta, mango salad and ginger-lime syrup (very good!) Ginger spiced lychee French toast with lemongrass dark palm caramel and pomegranate mascarpone (OUTSTANDING) and a side of Quinoa hashbrowns (which were good, not fantastic). We had really delicious drinks including a spiked hot apple cider. I really love this place and would love to go back for dinner but there aren't enough veggie options for me!!

Starving and it's almost closing cut off time. Finally got in, I don't know if it was because I was starving... but it was really good! Add some spice to that with the like the elite flavor or something like that. I think all the broths are a hit. So yes. Ramen in the cramp spot is legit. Japan legit? Just might.

This place gets 5 stars alone on the fact that they were so accommodating! Â I made super last minute reservations (that's my style) for a fairly large group, on a Friday night. The women warned me it would be a long wait, but agreed to put our name down. They got us in, adjusted some tables and had us sitting within 10 minutes of our arrival. Awesome. The food was great (I had chicken) but fish was very popular in our group. It is a bit pricey, for the smallish portion. The service was good and the crowd was fun. When we left (around 9:30pm) the place was packed. It was difficult to even navigate to the front door since the overflow from the people standing around the bar. Fun, trendy West Village spot. I would go again.

Dear Purbird !!!! Â  Â  Â  Â I LOVE purbird you made me love chicken again like omg!! I always order out and the guys on the phone are really nice. Since the day I began ordering from Purbird, my orders have been on point and just as I requested. The delivery guy takes no more than 25-35 min, and always on time The delivery guy is really nice(The delivery guy is way to CUTE!!
