This place is awesome. The only reason I'm not giving it 5 stars is because I feel I need to explore more of the menu before committing to an "As Good As It Gets!" rating. We went there late night (after midnight) on a Saturday, so we didn't have to wait more than a few minutes for a table. Â Our waitress was nice and really helpful, especially since they were out of a lot of the menu. We pieced together two dishes - Spicy pork meatballs with spicy meat sauce on polenta.. this was ridiculously good and the polenta added some unique texture - Beef meatballs with spicy sauce on rigatoni.. which was also ridiculously good. They should be given an award for attention to detail. The pasta was cooked to a perfect al dente even at 2am. The menu is easy to navigate and you can create many unique combinations of meatballs with pastas or on sliders etc. The interior has a nice warm feel to it, and the music they were playing was lively and added to the ambiance. I am definitely returning to try out the sliders and more of the menu.. and especially the build-your-own-ice-cream-sandwich desert. !!! Great date spot, but I've heard if you show up at peak times there can be a significant wait. Â Probably not good for very large groups unless you can secure a reservation. Â Also, the prices are very reasonable for the quality of food and ambiance.

Love this restaurant! Â Eaten here a couple of times. Â Staff is friendly - food is delicious! 1st time I was there, my friend and I ordered Pulled Pork sandwich and the Burger to try both - and we were not disappointed - we couldn't get enough of either... Went back for brunch - the bread pudding french toast is out of this world. Â Can't wait to go back and try some other things off the menu. Â  Also bought their homemade cashew butter - mmm good...
Really, really bland kangaroo meat. Pretty good lamb lollies. Decent beer. Nice waitress but really slow.

I went on a date here last night and him being a vegetarian and a picky eater he wasn't expecting the best fettuccine hes ever had... But it was just that! It had bits of smokey salmon in it and the portion was a good size, but he said it was so good he would have eaten another! I had the Nicoise Salad and its was yummy and a large portion but I was hoping for seared tuna and it tasted a bit more like canned than I was anticipating. THEY HAVE KOSHER WINE! We had the Prosecco and it was light and delicious and 20% off on Wednesdays! The crepes were insanely fresh and well balanced and everything there tastes like its made with love!

I must be missing something. My friend told me this was the best chicken and rice cart that he had been to in NYC so I tried hard to like it but it just wasn't right. The line down the sidewalk shows this place is popular. Service: They let certain regulars cut to the front of the line. Not sure how they make that distinction. In order to save packing time, they made us go around the side of the cart to add our own sauce and place our own lid on the container. Food: It's chicken and rice served with pita bread. The pita bread is not all that great. The chicken and rice was good and flavorful but not something that I'm crazy about. Next time, I'll give it another try but just wasn't for me this trip.
I love this place!! Every time I go there the food , service, drinks, and the courtesies of the Mg. and employes has consistency !!! Very attentive!!! Â Awesome place!!! Try!!

I've only been for brunch, but that's enough to make me a fan. The food is delicious and the service has always been friendly and prompt. My boyfriend and I generally share both our plates, and so far everything we've gotten has been really tasty. The restaurant itself is cute and looks clean and upscale. This isn't diet food by any means - I am STUFFED - when I leave the place, but it is really good. I've been three or four times so far, and I've always left in a good mood.

Such a good deal! Â I've never had the hot lunch/dinner buffet, because it seems like everything in the back is more worth it for your dollar! Â  In the back, they have prepackaged Korean foods. Â My favorite: a deal they sometimes have where you pick certain types of dishes for $10 (it's labeled). Â These dishes have included shrimp fried rice, kimchi fried rice, seafood pancake, imitation crab cakes, veggie tempura, fried squid, meat and egg pancake, etc. Â I've been very happy with all of the above. Â If they don't have that deal going on when you come by, they've got a bunch of other dishes that are still cheap and delicious: Japchae, Bimbimbap, Bulgogi, Spicy Pork, etc. Â I've gotten the Bulgogi japchae for $5 and it's pretty good. Â (If you get the Japchae, eat it right away, because the noodles harden. Â Definitely, don't stick it in the fridge...). Long story short, they've pretty much got standard Korean food for a good price. Â They also have a stamp card which you can redeem for items behind the cashier. Â For example, a stone bowl (that the soondubu [tofu soup] comes in at Korean restaurants), seaweed snacks, Korean dessert snacks, water bottles, etc.

Doesn't hold a candle to the Manhattan location. Negatives: Â The Mexican corn, which is the staple at Cafe Habana on Prince St, is a sad facimile. Â Way too much cheese, not enough Mayo, weak corn cobs. Disappointing. Â The Cuban Sandwich can only be described mediocre at best. Also disappointing. Â The fried plantains, which are so good at the Manhattan location, here--feh. Positives: The frozen mojito rocked. Great outdoor nabe atmosphere. Less hipsters than when I first went two years ago. Too bad, I really wanted to support the Bklyn location. I'll be back for drinks perhaps.

We stopped in here after an afternoon of tromping around the Natural History Museum across the street. We needed food, and kind of in a sort of round about hurry as we needed to get back to the hotel and on our way back to festive and culturally devoid Phoenix. Popped our heads in as Yelp told me this was just up the street. Kind of dated, 1980's, faux Miami Vice on the inside. I liked it instantly! All that was missing was my Linda Ronstadt t-shirt and some neon leggings on my girlfriend! Lunner was good. I went simple, had a burger and fries. It was good, bloody, and cooked to medium rare, just like I asked. It might seem like a simple thing, but cooking a hunk of ground beef to mid-rare is a tough thing. Fries were good, crispy, and weren't soggy. Can't beat that! Girlfriend had a fish salad of some sort. I didn't partake as it would lead to dead me, and that would be a shame according to some people. Drinks were refilled to the point of absurdity. To the point that I was happy we got back to the hotel quick, fast and in a hurry as my teeth were floating by the time we got to the front door. All in we were under $40 for lunch, which seems to be the low ball number for lunch in NYC. Had a great lunch, very happy. If I am ever back in NYC, I will hit Isabella's after another trip to get me some culture and some learnin!

Wonderful brunch place in our new neighborhood. Â We go early for a leisurely Sunday brunch and love the coffee, orange juice (must be fresh-squeezed), crispy French toast, and Eggs Benedict. Â They have lovely red new potatoes that have been cooked with rosemary that are just divine. Â Great music and a quiet, relaxing Sunday morning atmosphere make it our go-to place!

Tucked away on a busy but quintessential street in Nolita, Balaboosta provided for a pleasant late-morning brunch on an unseasonably warm winter day. I was impressed with not only the menu but also the fresh and healthy ingredients, the service and the beautiful interior decor. I highly recommend the green eggs and quinoa hash.

FANTASTIC burger. Â Really so damn good. Â My friends did not steer me wrong writing good reviews of this place. Â Excellent fries, great beer (Mother's Milk!) on tap, and a short walk to/from the Bandshell. Â I'm an instant fan. Â If I lived in Windsor Terrace, I'd be psyched to have this as my neighborhood spot.

Quintessential family style Italian. Worth a stop if you are willing to make a reservation months in advance, otherwise you will be waiting for 2-3 hours for a table. Appetizers and entrees are family style, perfect for sharing with a group of 3 or more (or take home the leftovers, which you will definitely have). It's affordable for families, but a little pricey if you're just getting pasta and sauce. Get the veal or a meat dish to get your money's worth. We tried the garlic and olive oil pasta, which was full of huge pieces of roasted garlic and had delicious flavor in the almost-buttery sauce. Caesar salad was also worthwhile with its authentic anchovy paste and creamy dressing. All in all we had a good meal, but I'd only consider it a small step above a place like Bucca Di Beppo (which can be found right around the corner).

Very small portions, unless you want a quick bite, one kathi roll is not filling. Also it is no where close the original middle eastern/Indian kathi rolls. I like their unda shaami a little, but spending 12$ for a decent filling meal is a big No for me. I think this place is more of a hype than quality.
rude, condescending waitress. worst service ever. tiny portions and no tap water. is that even legal?

Great food when you don't want to spend a lot of money or you already spent a bunch of money in the surrounding area and want to feel full. Also great when your drunk! this is the best halal spot so eat away!!

I feel that the $$ rating is a little deceptive. It would be very easy to spend a lot of money on a meal here though it would be well worth it. I had the artichoke mushroom risotto for lunch. It was spectacular. The risotto was perfectly al dente and the artichokes were well prepared. Sometimes when I order artichokes, what I really want are artichoke hearts. If the artichoke is not properly sliced it can make for a regrettable eating experience akin to chewing bark. None of that here. Stop by for a light lunch. But avoid if you are the kind of person who requires Cheesecake Factory portions. Did I mention that the check came with lollipops?

I used to live a few Blocks from DI fara's Pizza and tell you the truth befoer all the publicity it was great ,the lines werent half as long Dom had time to get to know you ,i had a running tab with him , anyways good for him tho although the last timei was there i almost got into a fist fight waiting on line , my freind has never been there and i took him waited 1hoiur and a half for a pie i have moved a way a couple of months now and do miss his pies ,but just as the reviews there really isnt an in betwwen either you loved or hated his pies

Hey all- Go here. Â Now. Â  This is my after work go-to with my boyfriend. Â We both wait tables. Â And after a long night dealing with the crazies, this is exactly what the doctor ordered. Â  Cheap, varied wine list. Â All esoteric wines, for cheap (under $45 for all), and narrowed down to save you the time and effort of searching through the list. As for food, get a pizza. Â With anything else, you're pretty much wasting your time. Â I reccommend the proscuitto pizza. Â It will fill you up and be delicious. The staff is totally chill. Â Any one of them will tell you exactly which wine to get, depending on what you are looking for. Â They know their shit. Â  I think my boyfriend and I are as close to regulars as they have, and they treat us like royalty. Â Go there once a week and you'll be golden, with buybacks every time. Also the music is sweet. Â Think indie with a twist.

One of my favorite place Â to go for delicious Italian food. It's an upscale Italian fiesta kind of place. Bread soaked in a delicious white wine sauce with mussels -genius. Let's understand each other best part of the mussels in sauce is dipping the bread in the sauce. Pasta with shrimp and truffle oil and cherry tomatoes is not on a menu , but you can order it anyways and it's beyond delicious. One of my favorite things is pizza with Robiola and truffle oil, it's not on a menu but you must try it. Dover sole is my favorite fish, it's delicate fish and costs $$$ even if you buy it yourself, but even in Citarella it goes for like $30 per lb if not even more. Service is great, you do get little overwhelmed with all the specials, but at this point I kind of tell the waiter what I feel like and he makes suggestions. And did I mention that place is kids friendly!!! I forgot to mention deep fried zucchini blossoms stuffed with fontina. Yum! Now I am hungry!

This pizza place, which happens to be owned by the real Grimaldi, is next door to Grimaldi's, another pizza place with gaggles of tourists in line outside. Thank goodness I had a real New Yorker guide me to the pizza in NYC: Juliana's. At 4:30 PM on a holiday, we had to wait about 20 minutes in a short line in the sun (the not-so-fun part). The man himself was out front, pointing people to tables and chatting customers up. We got a great table right near the pizza-making action. Our waitress was nice and efficient. We order the prosciutto/arugula pizza and the margherita pizza. Our party of 4 cleaned the pizza pans. They were delicious. Cheesy, fresh, flavorful, a little char on the crust... my favorite was the margherita, for sure. Prices were reasonable - in fact, they were cheaper than a lot of other places (less than $30 a pie). The beverage selection was solid, too. I'd tell you to try this place over other pizza options, but then there might be too much of a line when I try to go back ;)

I love this place. Every single time I've gone, I've not had a bad experience, and I've ordered take out as well, and it was great. This weekend I finally got to try the brunch menu. Started of with a bloody mary, which was near perfectly mixed. The potato salad was among the best, if not THE best I've ever had in my life, and the biscuit was by far the best I've ever had. I have never tried chicken fried chicken, because the name has always grossed me out, but I decided to be adventurous and give it a shot. It was juicy chicken covered with a good amount of chicken fried (though what do I know, never had it before), and wasn't too heavy. Scrambled eggs were delicious, and the fried apples tasted like the best apple dessert I've ever had. I'm so glad this place is within walking distance from me. As long as I live in the neighborhood, I will continue to frequent.

Good brunch food, but the place is very small. It was a bit difficult to move around once the place got full around 11:30 on a Sunday. And I was disappointed that two items on the brunch menu were not available. But overall it was charming and a good brunch option.

I came here for brunch with my boyfriend and a couple of friends who were visiting from out of town. The place as expected was crowded and cramped but since we had a reservation we were seated within minutes of getting here. I am vegan and gluten free and I had called ahead to ask what options were there for the brunch menu for me. The person on the phone said she would go speak with the chef and told me they could do a kale, quinoa salad and also this mushroom soup without the cheese. Unfortunately, when we got there and I inquired about the salad, the server told me that it was part of dinner menu and they could in fact not make it. However, eventually the manager came out and told me that they would make an exception for me and actually make it. I really appreciated that! My boyfriend and friend got the vanilla bean french toast and the portobello scramble, which they shared. My friend's sister got the mac and cheese croquette and the shoestring fries. Also, all the brunch entrees come with a free cocktail or freshly squeezed juice. My boyfriend liked the french toast and the scramble but didn't think they were out-of-the-world. Overall, the service was good, the food was ok - and if I make a reservation in advance I would possible come back here again. But I would wait for 30-40 minutes to be seated. The food by no means exceptional, but was good nonetheless. I do wish they had more options for me.

Delicious! My friend and I ate dinner here. Its a smaller place so definitely wouldn't recommend for groups. The music was a little loud and just didn't really fit the scene. BUT, the food more than made up for it! We got the butterfish carpaccio, grapefruit, avocado, mint and stage; the Â local mozzarella, red beets, pomegranate, yogurt, mint; baked muenster cheese, smoked chorizo, golden appels, crostini; and bbq sliders! ALL the dishes we got are so good. Every ingredient in it was important as it created the best combination of tastes. Would definitely recommend if you are trying a new restaurant. Also, we ended the meal with bacon doughnut with coffee ice cream. I'm not a fan of bacon, so I requested for the bacon to not be on mine. They give you 4 in one dish! 2 was enough per person. Its one of the best desserts I've ever had. To top it all, the bill came out to $65 for 2 people! Thats SO good for what we got!

I down graded this from 4-stars due to the fact that the chicken on my tacos got quickly cold and tough. However, the guacamole and everything else was excellent. I stopped by Habana Outpost because we/ I had been walking past this location all winter and was curious. I stopped in to chat with someone about a business/ website issue, and I grabbed some chicken tacos ($2.50/ each), a large guacamole ($4), and a small beer ($2.75). All in all, I paid a little over $10 for a good portion of food. We ended up sitting outside, enjoying the slightly warmer weather. For those who have been to Black Rock City, Habana Outpost evokes a similar feel - it is somewhat sustainable and it is relatively clean (no MOOP, please!) and I liked the feel overall. Next time, I will avoid the chicken and try the fish tacos.

I was going to give this place 4 stars but then figured its so original and deserves 5. Corn crab chowder slightly too sweet but damn good. The muscles lobster and clam scallop mix forgot the name was pretty good.

Last night I went to SUD with a couple of friends, what a treat! Â The Lasagna with pork ragu was delightful and the Lasagna with vegetables & bechamel was to die for. Â Also the homemade gnocchi with walnut and pesto was the best we had ever had. Â The best tiramisu ever! Â BYOB.

The place was very nice and clean.. The husband - wife - brother waitstaff was very friendly and attentive. Â However, the food was very bland. Â There were 4 of us, and all our dishes were bland. Â Being Indian, we realized most of the patrons were non-Indian.. And we theorized that the spice level was turned down to accommodate their non-Indian customers.

I had the trout; flavorful and very well prepared. My friend had the roasted chicken; tender and flavorful. The service was on point; attentive but not overly so. The restaurant was pretty crowed but we were not rushed. Definitely going back.

Royale. Â I would give the burger 3 stars, at best. Â  You can't give this place more than 3 stars if you've ever eaten a good burger in your life. Â While the lettuce is crispy, the bun looks good, and the tomato slick is thick and juice, the meat is completely flavorless. Â It is also worse than chuck. Â I do like me a greasy burger, but greasy and bland is just a crap sandwich. Â  Aside from the lack-luster burger, the gods must have been frowning on me. Â Because even though i was only with 1 other person, and we ordered the simplest of orders (2 burgers medium with fries), it took a little over an hour to get our food. Â  One hour. Â The place was semi-crowded, and it's not that big. Â I don't care if you have a blind, one armed chef, and the meat is frozen and he had to wait for it to thaw out. Â He still could have made 3 burgers for everyone in that place in an hour. Â And I watched these chefs. Â They were neither blind, nor one eyed. Â On the contrary, they were huffing and puffing back there, moving super fast to fill out the orders. I never, ever complain about service. Â But I neither ever, ever wait an hour for a burger. And if I were to wait an hour, I would expect some kind of apology or something for free. Â And even if I didnt get that, I would expect to have a burger with some kind of flavor. Â  Total, total lemon. Â Not worth 7.50.

Kaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaang!! (star trek fans knowattamean) Anyway...the food is fo'reals Thai....no Manhattan/Park-slope Gringo style watered down flavours. Â This is what you'd get walking around in Thailand..really good selection that changes day to day...no menus...just point and eat up! They have desserts too (ok..smaller than other Thai spots) Â I just wish theyd make some strictly Vegetarian dishes for my vegan "bunny" friends. PLEASE--Krup!!!
Thanks, Fat Buddha, for showing me a fun time in NY! Wish there was a spot in CA like this. I drank till the early morning and hurt much the next day. Haha. BYE!
Went back - same experience of great service and great food!! Thank you, Trattoria Dell'Arte for running a class act establishment! Â I highly recommend!

Okay, this place is across the street and over a year later, this is on my go to list. Â The salads are SO GOOD, so now I love this place. Â I simply was ordering wrong! Â Love that when I call in an order it's ready in 10, but delivery is SLOW 1/2 times, so beware. Â Their spicy green sauce is KILLER. Â Why don't you bottle and sell it?! Â Still think pricing is odd/over-priced a bit ($+2.50 on a $9.50 salad to add an avocado???), but very delicious, so I've come around :) Â  Also, have eaten here but it is CRAMPED - like really uncomfortable, and chaotic. Â Would not recommend eat-in.

This is one good breakfast/brunch place. The space is beautiful, spacious and clean and waitstaff is nice and accommodating. But the most important thing is, of course, the food. I've had the eggs coppelia, the huevos rancheros, and the simple two eggs, and they are consistently delicious. OK OK, what can go wrong when making eggs, you ask? That's very true but they accompany their eggs with delicious potatoes in chimichurri sauce (and these CAN go wrong sometimes...) and give you a delicious cuban toast. Plus the coffee is really excellent, far better than other diners. You leave satisfied without breaking the bank... what else can you ask for?

East 14th is a comfort zone for me. Â My subway stop, my gym, my bars, my smiley bouncer at Crocodile Lounge, my bouncy smiler (waiter) at Curly's Lunch, and lo and behold a new pizza place - Artichoke. Â  "Hey, weren't you here the other night?" the owner asks me. "Oh, it's possible...but I don't remember what your pizza tasted like. Â It was late..." Â (read: I was drunk) So on comes the food for sober Nicole. Â I am offered a sample of pasta fagioli on a nice big piece of bread. Â "Just a lil somethin' we're cooking up tonight," the owner says. Â I am a sucker for Italian hospitality and enjoy the *really* awesome homemade soup handed to me. Â After this sample, I am offered a cauliflower fritter which is equally delicious and, I fear, addictive. Next we talk pizza. Â I am promised that the spinach and artichoke will blow my mind. Â At this point, I feel a challenge coming on. Â I put down my enormous gym bag and realize that my sense of self discipline has little power over pizza. Â No working out for this girl tonight...it's throw down pizza time with the new kid on the block. The verdict? Â If you like spinach, artichoke, and cheese dip with rustic slightly crispy crust...you will like this slice. Â If you love a LOT of said ingredients, you will LOVE this slice. Â It's enormous. Â I've never tasted anything quite like it. Â It is very heavy so watch out, you might need some backup. Â I could not finish it alone. Â  I also tried a taste of their regular (Neopolitan) pizza. Â What stuck out to me most of all was the refreshing tomato sauce. Â Normally I am a "light on the sauce, please" kind of girl but I wouldn't change a thing here. Â  This is my new place to grab a fresh slice. Â I don't know what it is, but they do it right. In my time chatting with the owners, so many people came in and out getting slices. Welcome to your home on 14th street, Artichoke. Â You make us proud.

Cozy little place well suited for small groups. I stopped by with a friend at 8 PM on a Wednesday, and there was only one table remaining, so reservations are probably recommended. We didn't eat particularly much, just splitting a few cheeses and meats, but it was all very tasty. The selection isn't too varied, but it has mostly enough to cater to most tastes. Perhaps due to the cold weather, the temperature was a bit volatile, but they seemed to cater to the customers' preferences when it fluctuated too much. We were also provided complimentary warm wine later during the meal, which was very much appreciated. It's a great place for quiet conversation that also has good food and nice service.

I am going to ignore the crazy long waiting line and impatient waiters in the rating because the pancakes here were SO good, and those are what I had come here for. I had ricotta pancakes with fresh fruit, honeycomb butter and maple syrup on top -- oh my word. This is definitely on my list of favorite brunch spots.

My boyfriend and I come here every weekend for our breakfast and we wouldnt have it any other way!!!! The chef caters to our liking. Â The menu is unique yet traditional. Â Everything is prepared fresh with great service and the staff makes us feel like family! love it!!!

Totto used to be among the better ramen places in NYC (ippudo has always held the top spot imo), but recently the quality seems to be declining. In addition, now that ippudo has a second location in midtown west, I have almost no reason to come here, though it is worth a try. I judge ramen places by their tonkotsu broth primarily, and Totto's broth is heavy and one-dimensional compared to Ippudo's and Jin's, though their spicy garlic topping is quite good (get it on the side and 1) it's enough for 2-3 people to share and 2) you can try the broth with and without the sauce, and modify it to your taste). The pork and noodIes are solid. I REALLY do not recommend the vegetarian ramen. It tastes like undercooked vegetables, and overall is just very bland.

Wholesome, healthy, tasty. Once you've had it once, it's easier than you think to walk right past the Wendy's and McDonald's right next door (if you love fast food like me!). Try the basque shrimp or Balkan "burger" (which is closer to a whole wheat chicken wrap), and start with the pozole roja soup.

Lots of cool places popping up in bed-stuy and this is one of them. Â I was a little disappointed that it seemed to be just full of hipsters. Bed Stuy is changing...maybe a bit too much? But this review is about the food. delicious. I didnt think the service was particularly friendly - she semed a bit too cool for school. I dont know if that was purposeful or not. But I am not into that kind of thing at all. Â I would definitely return to try more of the dishes. The decor inside kind of reminds me of the dining room at Dean Street. I like that its BYO - it kept costs down, but I am interested to see what kind of cocktails will be on the menu once they get their liquor license!

Sigh......after reading all the wonderful reviews I really wanted to love Mezetto!!! Sadly I was sorely disappointed with the food. The restaurant is small but very cute and cozy and service was absolutely wonderful. My friend and I came here for brunch and we ordered the baked eggs Shakshuka and the omelet espanola. Both dishes were quite bland for our taste and the harissa we asked for on the side added little flavor to the dishes. Overall we felt the food needed more spice and for a Mediterranean place the food should be bursting with flavor! I really hope they were just having an off day but with so many other great restaurants in the city I don't think I"ll be coming back anytime soon.
so much better than before ! i had the octopus aioli and the beef cheek stew it was crazy good
Diner had been on my burger list for quite a long time. Unfortunately the burger was as standard as the name of the restaurant.

Went here yesterday for dinner. We were seated right away in this tiny restaurant. Staff were friendly but a little slow moving. Â We'd never has Himalayan before so we weren't sure what to try and opted for some random choices. I ordered a lamb dish with potatoes, curry, and basmati rice; my boyfriend got a chicken curry dish also with rice. We found the food to be overall pretty bland. My lamb had only two chunks of potato and the portion wasn't huge. We both left fairly hungry after finishing our meals. Not positive if the food was consistent with what's typical of Tibetan food but it was an overall "ok" experience.

Heaven does exist, and it's a magical place called Eataly! Want a nice sit down meal that is meat focused? This is your place. Want a delicious sandwich to go on your lunch break? They have it. Want to shop and pick up pasta for dinner that was made from scratch? Come to the market at Eataly. But it doesn't end there. Coffee. Gelato. Chocolates. Meats and Cheeses. Pasta sauces. All within these heavenly doors. Anything Italian, anything in any major food group, they've got it! The prices vary but definitely settle on the higher end of the scale, so it's more for special occasions or if you are visiting. Also, it gets quite crowded, so that can deter me from eating here. If you want to dine in, get your name on a list, then grab a glass of wine and shop around. It's really neat to look at the menus, cookbooks, and pasta being made right in front of you and the staff are nothing but friendly and helpful with any questions you have. Everyone at Eataly loves food and isn't afraid to show it! I can hear the heavenly chorus now...

This place was the culinary highlight of my weekend excursion to NYC. Â I've eaten out in NYC a lot, so I wanted to try something new. Â Found this place here on Yelp. Â The octopus salad was a great starter and the filet mignon was excellent. Â Cute and cozy. Â Loved the thick wooden tables. Â Will be going back soon!

If, in your quest for the best slice of pizza in Brooklyn, you've found yourself beneath the Brooklyn Bridge waiting in line with heaps of starved tourists, you've done it wrong. Sure, that place is a fine pizza joint and they make a decent enough pie, but hop the F train a few stops into Brooklyn and head to Guiseppina's to find the best slice of "traditional" NY style pie. Giuseppina's serves up traditional oven fired pies and offers an array of standard toppings along with a few less common topping items like marinated artichoke hearts. The pizza is absolutely top notch and every bit as good as any other pie I've had in the city. To top it off, you don't have to wait outside in a lengthy line freezing or sweating to death depending on the season and the service is incredibly friendly and helpful. My experience eating at some of the more famous, landmark-type pizza joints has felt like being rapidly herded through the process of ordering, eating, and getting the f*** out, left only with searing heartburn from consuming slices of pizza at a pace that's comparable to that seen in the Coney Island Hot Dog Eating Competition. Giuseppina's, on the other hand, is friendly, intimate, and not rushed at all. They want you to not only enjoy the pizza but also the experience of dining. It's tough for me to really explain how much I prefer this place to any of the other well-regarded pizza places. The experience at Giuseppina's makes me wonder why anyone patronizes those other spots. Sure, they offer solid pies, but you never have time to actually enjoy what you're eating. Give Giuseppina's a shot and I think you'll be left wondering the same thing.

Recently, I was invited to dinner at Minetta Tavern by a certain gentleman, who I've bumped into a few times around the city. We'll call him Mr. Niceguy. You know the type; he's ambiguously "older", absurdly short, has chronic halitosis (and is a bit of close-talker to boot, which makes him nearly impossible to bear), but he is also the absolute nicest foodie on the planet. Generous to a fault, always ready with a compliment or a clever quip about the latest cocktail craze, Mr. Niceguy is just that, a nice guy...not my next love affair. But, a week ago, when Mr. Niceguy asked me out to dinner at Minetta Tavern, I couldn't say no. I like to think of myself as a nice girl, and hey, Bruni just gave 3 starts to Keith McNally's most recent foray into trendy comfort food. Mr. Niceguy doesn't drink red wine, and so our meal began when we were forced to order our vino by the glass, something akin to heresy for the sommelier on the floor that night. Â The minute I informed said sommelier we'd be ordering individually, "We have very different tastes...you understand," it was clear that he didn't. Â I literally watched the enthusiasm drip out of his smile like a slow leak in a flat tire, and this was only the beginning of the evening. We decided to skip the much-lauded Black Label Burger and instead each had a Tavern Steak (a New York strip, served bloody, as requested), potatoes Anna (buttery and delicious) and two glasses of wine (me, a California Zin; he, an Austrian Riesling...with steak!). That's when I knew that, even if he weren't so goddamn nice, it could never work. White wine with steak is a deal-breaker for me, and Rieslings, well let's just say I didn't like grape juice as a kid, and I still don't. All in all, Minetta Tavern reminded me of a poor man's Waverly Inn; the food was solid, the crowd was Ã¼ber trendy, the dÃ©cor was Old New York revived, the atmosphere was brilliantly alive, but the bill was a hell of a lot cheaper. I told Mr. Niceguy, and he agreed. He suggested I blog about it, (which I did, at kimberlybelle.com/2009/0â€¦) I thanked him for dinner and told him I'd best head straight home to start writing. He responded, "Nice." -Kimberly Belle kimberlybelle.com dinnerbelleny.com
Delicious artichoke salad, delicious Bolognese sauce, an okay bottle of wine. This darling cash-only itty-bitty restaurant was a pleasure for a Sunday night cozy dinner.
Great atmosphere, exceptional service, fantastic fare (homemade?). Reasonable prices and delicious desserts. Come eat here!!!
The first 'chicken and rice' most people are ever exposed to. Â Delicious and the red sauce is insanely spicy.

i went here to try the burger and the wings. Â i have read many reviews on this place which talk about how good the burger is. Â I was hugely disappointed. Â The burger was not even average, it was greasy and the garnishment was old and wilted and not fresh at all. Â  The bun was a bit stale possibly a day old. Â All in all i would say the food ingredients are very low qulaity and the preparation is just a notch below a bad diner. Â I have no words for the space itself. Â I think i would start at disgusting and dirty but that would be an understatement. Â Normally i would just walk out of a place that looked like this but i read many good reviews so i tried it. Â i will not go back, i should have listened to my instincts. Â Bonnies is really nothing special at all and obviously has a loyal following but i cant seem to find why.

Such a fabulous Italian restaurant! Definitely reminded of the authentic spots I was fortunate enough to visit when I lived in Italy. Sidenote: I have to say, the name "Uva" totally makes me envision ovulation and ovaries, but once I got over that unfortunate association, I was blown away by the food! If you're a fan of the truffle, Uva offers a number of dishes that will suit your fancy. Their gnocchi is one of their signature dishes and you won't be disappointed. A friend and I also split the truffle polenta. HEAVENLY. My friend is gluten-free (BUMMER!) so her options were somewhat limited. But she absolutely loved her veal entree, as well as the prosciutto & mozzarella appetizer they offered. As many Yelpers have noted, they also have an impressive wine list (and not all the bottles will break the bank). The ambiance is also so warm and inviting. If the weather permits, try to sit out in the back atrium if you can!

Halal Cart... Amazing.. Visited New York and felt like i had to try it. Â I wanted to know what all the hype was about. Â I stood in a long line of about 30 people but got my food in less then 10 minutes. Â I loaded my aluminum dish with white sauce (copying others). The food was amazing and dirty cheap. Â I was able to share my dish with 1 other person and still be stuffed. Â You must get the white sauce because it really makes the dish. Â The rice is also very buttery and delicious. Â Beware of the red sauce it has quite a kick to it. I visited new york for 3 days and ended up eating here 3 times! This place was so amazing that I went here for a late night snack everyday I was here! Â I can't wait to go back and eat more.

So I have this huge obsession over eating large intestines any way possible. You can fry them boil, poach sauteed whatever...my all time favorite dish is MOTSUNABE..SO FREAKING GOOD. It was a toss up between giving it 2 stars and 3, somehow I'll make one bad experience not effect other times that I will most likely go back. I love their food, reasonably priced, they have shochu, and raw calf's liver. But I had this one awful Japanese waitress, who needed desperately to get laid. I know you're probably frustrated at the fact you have tons of rude foreign customers, and that you slightly give less f*cks since gratuity is already included, but please do not treat everyone that way. Â Are you dumb? I guess so. Â And for the rest of the night it just went downhill. So if you want delicious food, come here. But if you want some nasty service to go with it, come here. Down to 2 stars after thinking about her.

We stumbled upon this restaurant in Chelsea Market. To be honest, we knew nothing of the reviews, but only had a little bit of time and way too many choices. We wandered in trying to find something quick and delicious, bumped into this simple menu on the door, and gave it a try. First off, the service was fantastic. They accommodated us since we were in a hurry. The food choices were light and fresh, and tasted oh so good. My wife had the cheese plate, which you can get in many places in NYC, but this was among the best she has ever had. I went simple with grilled veggies and soup. You would think this would be a mundane, basic order, but the food was absolutely delicious, far better than I expected. I can honestly say I've never been this impressed by grilled veggies and wish I could have adventured further into their menu. Next time, perhaps.

Shanghai dumplings is what this place is all about. We had an order each per person. The first three was very good and then it went downhill. The dumplings were either broke when I picked it up (was very careful) or there was barely any juice inside. If all were made nicely, I would've given 4 stars.

Venue - Very cute vintage cafe/bar. The space is small and narrow, with only bar seating and about 10 stools. They serve different things throughout the day: 11 - 4 breakfast/lunch 4 - 6 afternoon coffee/tea and desserts 7 - 12 sake bar Food and Drinks: - Coffee is slowly brewed in unique bunsen-burner-like-equipment. - Vietnamese iced coffee is on the bitter side. I would try their other coffee selections. - The seasonable apple crumble cake was just cold apple pie. It wasn't bad, but it wasn't what I expected. I would skip it and order something else. - Chocolate parfait was nice and light. You can taste the coffee in the jelly. - Sake - wide selection, about $15 a glass on average - Salted fish bar snack (not sure what its called) but omg it was so salty it was inedible - Overall, overpriced mediocre food Service. - SLOW. - Inattentive and forgetful. So I go in with a friend. They take my friend's order but not mine. There are two servers for a small bar of only 10 people. Even with that ratio, trying to get one of their attention is surprisingly difficult. And once I got to order, they forgot my order. And after reminding them of my order, I had to remind them again and finally received my drink and food after much confusion on their part and after my friend was more than halfway done with hers (and she was trying to be slow to wait for me). 3 stars for the food and pricing, 1 star for service.

Not sure what the high ratings are all about. It's a cute, charming place, that's for sure. But that's about where the positive aspect stops. The food took an hour, no exaggeration, to come out. The menu is generally uninspired which is fine, we ordered a turkey burger and a grilled chicken sandwich. Very very basic items that shouldn't have taken more than 15 mins to make. Â  We also ordered drinks and those were also highly disappointing. Completely watered down with no hint of alcohol. They both basically tasted like lemon juice. I went in very excited and came out highly disappointed. Good thing I was using a scoutmob deal at least.

Table 87 is a great addition to the neighborhood. Crunchy, thin crusts, fresh mozzarella they make themselves, careful garnishing and great staff make this place a win for me. Â They have extra condiments on the side you can spoon on yourself such as peppers and roasted garlic. I had a personal 12" Margherita and was there recently for just a slice, and it was heaven both times. I have never been to a place with coal fired ovens. Â The pizzas cook quickly and evenly and give the crust just the right crunchiness. The people who work there are friendly and attentive. I will be back many, many times!

Beyond LOVE Beyond Sushi. Â As a vegan, I am always frustrated at the poor no fish selections most restaurants offer that have sushi on the menu. Â YES!! Â I get it! Â Sushi is primarily a fish menu item. Â However, the fact is that in NYC there are plenty of vegetarians and vegans that deserve to have more than just a piece of avocado wrapped in seaweed and some rice. The salads and rolls are delicious!! Â The single pieces are always perfect especially when trying out something new. I highly recommend this restaurant to everyone that enjoys and appreciates flavorful, thoughtfully prepared delicious food! Â It is a small venue, so be prepared to share the table. Â Weather permitting, perfect place to pick up a lovely picnic and head out to Union Square Park to enjoy the bounty!

Cecina taco! Carnitas taco! Chorizo burrito! Speedo burrito!!!!* Â  (ok, a speedo burrito is not on the menu, and neither is a chorizo burrito, but they rhyme so well and it's what I got after nom-nom-nomming at this place) Bonus: Â the salsa is super runny and super spicy - my Mexican dream come true. Â I hate chunky salsa! Â The tacos are a good size and range anywhere from $2.50-$3. Â Without liquor, I walked away with lunch for under $10. Â STEAL! Friendly waitress, great service, cool decor - go out of your way for a bite at this place!

Have been here couple of times already since discovering this place few months ago. Loves their pancakes, poached egg w/salmon and latte! -1 star for dirty glass at one occasion (still lipstick mark on)!

I'm human, so I've been known to be an idiot from time to time, so as I write this review, I can admit that I didn't visit Mayfield with the most positive thoughts. I was convinced that I'd find a pretentious menu, stuffy environment and overpriced meal options. You're probably asking, so why'd you come. Well, it's conveniently located (I'm lazy), Â I pride myself in being knowledgable about the neighborhood dining options (I'm greedy) and well...I didn't hit the 400 review mark from sitting at home snacking on TV dinners. The decor is cozy and comforting, much more open than the previous restaurant that lived at this location. Plus we learned that they are working on making over the backyard to allow for outdoor dining. Cool. One note of caution- check the menu out in advance. The entree menu is very limited with only 4 or 5 options, so this may not work with the picky eater. We started out with fried oysters that were placed over a bed of salmon. Quite tasty my friends. Most of the plates on the menu are actually small plates, but if you are hungry like me, you likely want to skip to the bottom of the page to the entree section. My friend had the trout (whole trout with head on) and I had the pork chop. Everything was really tasty and the portions were perfect for us, but you should not expect to have any leftovers. We spent around $160 dining for 2, but let's be honest 1/2 of that check was in support of our thirst for alcohol.

My family is Polish so I know my way around sausages, pierogies, potatoes and halupkies. Â  We stopped here for Lunch one afternoon as I was craving some homemade Polish food. I ordered the Mushroom/Cabbage pierogies and my husband ordered the Potato/Cheese pierogies. Â When putting the dishes down on the table, the waitress confused the orders and gave me the Potato/Cheese ones which was a good thing because I liked them better and could steal more of them. Â The Mushroom/Cabbage ones were ok but I felt like they were a little dry. I was hoping this would be a cheap lunch, but with tip it was $20... a bit pricey for just 2 plates of pierogies in my opinion. Â Even though it was pricey, the waitress was nice and the decor reminds me of being at my grandmother's. Â I mean there's deer heads on the wall covered in glitter and holiday lights... if that doesn't scream out being at your grandmothers I don't know what does. Â Next time I'm going to get the Polish platter, can't wait to try it.
Excellent food! Had the moussaka n the couscous - I recommend both. Â Not into desserts but the creeps were top notch. Nice server n great atmosphere...I will be back!!!

Three years and 5 meals after on evolving menus served in a loud restaurant with the most ridiculous reservation system ever ... ... I can tell Traif is a solid 10 stars. --------------------------------------------------Â­--------------------------------------------------Â­------------ P.S. this is a phone-written review and yelp app says: "This review is shorter than most reviews" ... so good !

Yelp is my Bible, because I would have never found this place otherwise. This place makes me want to fly to Brazil and eat all of the food there. As for me, I usually skip over the trivial french fries, mash potatoes and all that junk. I go straight for "rice and steak". That does it for me. Steak and rice! The steak is so juicy it makes juicy fruit dry. But honestly the steak here is so savory and flavorful, every time I think about it, my mouth waters a little. Make sure to get it medium-rare though! TIP: Please don't go for a Snapple or a Coke. Grab a Guarana! It's a Brazilian drink and it tastes amazing.

I really don't understand all the hype about this place. I got the sheeps milk ricotta that everyone is raving about, and the pasta with the lamb ragu. Both were boring and unmemorable. Couldn't even taste the honey or the truffle in the cheese. Prices were ok, ambiance was ok. Server seemed young and inexperienced and spilled both my wine and my water. I wouldn't go back.
Super Clean, casual and fun. They have great coffee and sandwiches. A must if you are in Greenpoint.

I can't. I had high expectations from this place since my friend from Cali had once came here and gave it an amazing review. My friend and I brought our Persian friend here and to sum up, we left disappointed and with upsetting stomachs. The General Tso's Chicken was $14.50; even though it came in the same portion as the $5.50 one you can get at Chinese takeout places. The Roast Duck over Rice was literally drowned in salt- some of the salt didn't even dissolve yet. ($5.25) The Pork Fried Rice was good and costed $8.00 for a decent amount. The only up-side about this visit was the free fortune cookies. (Does that sum up how bad the meal was?Â¿)

This is a really decent taco joint and my go-to for ordering when I want something fast and easy. Â I suggest ordering because they are always so packed. Â My food usually arrives in less than 30 min, but to go order and pick up it takes around an hour. Â The people running this place seem that they would benefit from a better POS system or a tutorial from someone who can teach them how to use it more efficiently--It would probably help them out and make them a little less frantic looking. I will absolutely come back here and keep ordering from here. Â The food is really great!

Have gone for brunch several times...and its just plain yummy! Â I always get an omlette -- and its how eggs should be made: light, fluffy, flavorful. Went for dinner last night for the first time. Â The grilled octupus was excellent...so flavorful w/ the chorizon. Â Other folks at my table had the potato soup w/ bacon...did you hear me say bacon...nuff said! For main - the pasta was incredibly fresh. Â I love al di la which is close by -- but if you Â can't get into al di la - this is where you go for great pasta. Â  I as suspect when I saw it on the menu given that its not an Italian restaurant -- but boy was aI wrong. Â  All you really need is the half portion of the pasta - unless you want to take some home for lunch the next day. Â  Service was super attentive. Â Prices were decent. As a sidenote - the first time I eyed Stone Park for dinner a few years ago - we couldn't get in b/c it was full and we saw Bloomberg having a quiet dinner w/ friends there.

After 25++ visits over the p[ast 3-4 years I have never writen to say how "specia" this resataurant is. The chicken with pharma, mozzerella and brocolli rabe is terific and one entre means lunch or even dinner the next day. The owner/Chef, Renato, is charming and is part of the prersonlity of the maybe 60 seat restaurant.His daughter though can be moody and unpleasant to co.workers and it somertimes spills over to customers. Try to have Peter or Jason as yuour waiter if possible. Tables are too close together unless the people next to you are interesting. Reservations 3-4 days in advance needed for weekends..
Giving it a 3 star due to its service on the night we went. Â The waitstaff were no where to be found. Â How's the food? Its OK.. maybe I might drop by to taste other dishes but we weren't impressed.

Cheap Shanghai Dumplings that aren't that great... I came here since people rave about their Shanghai Dumplings, but I thought it was a little too salty and I did not like the skin of the dumplings. It was too big and that it droops over. Texture was not great. I'm sure there's better else where.

Maialino 2 Lexington Avenue New York, NY 10010-5405 (212) 777-2410 Subway: 23 St maialinonyc.com ************************************** Overall Impression: Located just south of the Gramercy Park, Maialino is a Roman-style trattoria, a warm and comfortable place for any of it's guests - whether they wear a t-shirt or an impeccable suit. The restaurant is extremely well run and managed, as one might expect from any of the establishments owned by Danny Meyer. Maialino particularly excels at pastas, although the Primi and the wine program are remarkable in their own right. Maialino desserts can use some improvement, but other than that this restaurant is absolutely worth a visit, and for more than one reason. Please look at the Maialino picture set here: flickr.com/photos/nicknaâ€¦

I really like this restaurant. Cosy atmosphere, very friendly waiters, large portions to share, good Italian food. Once you get inside, the feel of the place and the smell of Italian cooking gives you just the right feeling. No pizzas here, but very good pasta. We had the Ravioli Bolognese which was very good. I haven't tried the meat or the fish, but from the looks of the guests at the table next to us, it must have been good. For dessert we had Tiramisu and Sundae. Very good and large portions! Not much more to say, really. The restaurat is very close to Times Square, but has its own distinct personality. I recommend this restaurant!

Quelle merveille! In the Financial District, an area typically devoid of non-corporate, Seamless Web affiliated culinary undertakings, Crepes du Nord is a heaven-sent. Â The crepes are better than sub-par, they are delicious! Â It is so much fun to watch the guy preparing crepes in the window, as you wait for a table to free up. If you're looking to stay and enjoy your crepe, be prepared to sit in close quarters with your fellow diners and to be tortured by the smell of their brie and pear crepe wafting over to your table while you eagerly await for yours to arrive. The raspberry and nutella crepe with a dollop of vanilla ice cream was divine! Â It was filled with the perfect proportions of all of the ingredients. Calories, what are those?

Beautiful restaurant with apples all over the waiting area. Very dreamy, even down to the basement. Food, however, fail to leave a significant enough memory for me to go back again -- maybe just happen not to be my favorite dishes.
Can't get enough of this place. Pork bun and karak-men (spicy) never fails..oh and extra side of noodles ($2) which is good portion to share between two people.

We needed a restuarant at the last minute so I did a quick search on Yelp and found Pepe Giallo. It did not dissappoint. When I called to make the reservation, they asked if I wanted to sit in the font dining room or in "the garden". Since yesterday was a beautiful day, I asked for the garden. When we arrived to the restaurant we were ushered back to an open area that was nestled inside the block of buildings. It was the perfect setting for a quite Saturday night dinner. You will be surprised when you see how reasonable the prices are on the menu. Nothing is more than $14.95 and there is a pretty good selection. At the recommendation of the waitress, I ordered the chicken special, which was a chicken in a creamy white wine sauce with eggplant and broccoli. It was very tasty, and a little different than anything I have had before. We also got several desserts. Both the chocolate cake and tiramasu were very good as well. When we got the check, it was less than $100 total for a group of five. Good food. Good atmosphere. Good prices. I think I will be going back.

I'm from North Carolina and I know fried chicken, biscuits and sausage gravy. Â Jacob's Pickles nails them all. Â Flawlessly. Â The fact that they also offers a decadent Bloody Mary with a jalapeÃ±o-infused hard-boiled egg and thick slab of bacon is just bonus. Â  We ordered the fried pickles as an appetizer and, now that i've done it, I won't go be ordering them again. Â They're just mounds of friend dough with a pickle in the middle and, while they are delicious, I'd prefer to save my heart the burden of all that added cholesterol. I ordered the chicken biscuit with sausage gravy and was surprised by only one unmistakable characteristic of the meal: it's SPICY. Â No where in the menu was this indicated so you can imagine my surprise. Â Here's the thing, though: I love spicy food. Â So this was yet another reason to love this place. Also, one final insight: the wait when we arrived on a Sunday afternoon around 1:30pm was reported to be an hour. Â We entered our name in the queue and about 20 min. later we were called. Â This part of my review is intended to be inspiring and hopeful. Â If you see a crowd outside waiting, hang in there. Â It's a big restaurant and well worth the wait.
This place is great across the board. Â We travel from Manhattan regularly just to eat here. Â Never had anything that wasn't great.

Dropped by around 9 in the evening and took bar seats without any waiting time. Got the zaru cold soba--delicious!! The soba itself was a smooth texture and the dipping sauce was savory without being too salty. After I finished the soba, the waitress gave me a pot of boiling water to make the sauce into a broth--also quite tasty. Made the mistake of ordering a small portion. Unless you're already half-full, definitely order AT LEAST the regular portion! Also, the soba entrees with more toppings tend to get pricier. Overall, friendly service and good soba. Looking forward to coming back to try more!

i've come here twice for lunch, and i really enjoy their dumplings and Thang soup... they have a wide selection of vegetarian dishes... i wanna try their smoothie, will update on that review... so far so good :)
WONDERFUL food for tapas style. I highly recommend it. Service isn't perfect but is worth it for what you get to enjoy!
Worse pizza ever, ordered online at 2 am and delivered after 2 hours.. taste so bad and so oily

Had a fantastic meal here and honestly, one of the best waiters I've had in New York. If the managers read this, he worked the upstairs section and wore a silver bracelet. The pasta was fresh, the butter lettuce was one of those "this is gonna be fineeeee" and turned out to be one of the highlights. Olive oil cake is a must have if you like salty sweet. Guys! It is expensive to eat here but worth it.

If you like Belgian Beer, Steak Frites, Mussels (Moules Frite), this is the place for you. They have an amazing collection of Belgian beers on tap and an insane number in bottles. The mussels and fries are amazing (probably the best in the city). Â It is a hang out for francophone visitors to the city and the wait staff are all French or Belgian, so expect to hear . They have two locations in NYC but the east side one has much better service. Can't say anything negative about this place, in my top 5 in NYC.

Everything we ordered was delicious: -Sweet potato noodles (pretty authentic-tasting japchae tbh) -Pot Udon (great broth! tender yet crispy shrimp tempura!) -Scallion pancake (I prefer crispier jeon, but this was good) -Roasted mushrooms (Tasted of fragrant rosemary, meaty in texture and overall best roasted shrooms I've had in some months. We got this dish comped after checking in on Yelp/4sq) One thing I really want to call out is the apple makgeolli. Our only disappointment is that we only ordered one carafe, when we each could have downed a full one. Oh my god, this stuff is dangerously delicious. Tastes like freshly squeezed granny smith apples. We also ordered the lychee makgeolli (not on the menu), which was alright. Not as sweet as the apple (tbh I thought it was very reminiscent of cleaning solution but my friends quite liked it). The atmosphere is nice, the waitstaff very friendly. Quality of the food makes the odd decor seem quirky, and drinking helps too. Would definitely come back here again, solo, dolo, with coworkers, with friends, on a date.

We returned for the legendary brunch on a sunny fall day. I am happy to report that the pumpkin pancakes with the cinnamon yogurt meet their hype. In fact, they were a better possible pairing than I could have imagined. I would describe them as fluffy yet substantial - equal parts pan and cake. For a side, we tried the Mergues (lamb sausage) which was surprising in its soft texture and a very apt savory contrast to the sweet in the pancakes. Segafreddo coffee makes for a good eyeopener here. This meal will be repeated in the best possible sense. A very tasty, very reasonable and very appropriate start to a crisp Sunday in October (or any other kind of day in any other kind of month) The gentleman on the phone was kind enough to let us know when they usually got a rush so we could beat it and he was spot on. Â It takes an effort to get to brunch on St. Marks Place when you consider the commute from Inwood. Â Cafe Orlin makes it worth the effort.

wow, just reading the menu is exciting.I have a feeling this place is going to make me want to take a star off my other reviews. Â but... not really. the appetizers are amazing. Â entrees are good. Â And the desert, not so great.

The French Toast with Brioche was the fluffiest, tastiest French toast I've ever had. Â I would've paid significantly more than $11 for it. Â The back porch is too cute and our waitress was very attentive and personable. Â I couldn't get over the ambiance of the place, let alone the food. The drinks were a little pricey so I left them alone, but overall. A very worthwhile experience.

Excited to try a place for biscuits and gravy, I made reservations here for eight (they allow reservations for parties of six or more). Â  Jacob's Pickles is a meal of extremes: Extreme use of salt--on the fried pickles especially, which made it not so good (you'd think fried pickles would be their specialty!). Â Also the collard greens were super salty as well. Â We wanted something to balance the rest of the meal, but it just added on to the flavor overload. Â We ended up not finishing either of them. Â There was one water jug for entire table that we had to repeatedly ask to get refilled. Â  Extreme portions-- eating here makes you feel like you gained four pounds just from appetizers alone. Â (Actually my aunt said she literally gained three pounds after the fact, so I was not far off) Extremely heavy--if you are looking for a southern food fix, you can come here, and not want to eat Southern food for a while afterwards. Extremely dark--did anyone else have like an issue trying to read the menu in there? Â The small candles just weren't cutting it for us. Â We had to pull out the flashlights on our smartphones. Â Thank god for technology. I love all of the above (salt, portions, feeling fat), but in moderation. Â So I will probably wander back to Jacobs, but maybe after I feel like I have burned all of the calories from that meal that are probably still in my body.

Don't know whether I really need to add to the plethora of good reviews of this place, but here goes: was there for dinner on a Sunday evening and we were prepared for an hour's wait for a table. The actual waiting time was much about 35-45min, but our party was not complete thanks to a lost dude wandering around in Times Square. They were very kind in holding the table for us though, and the great service was continued throughout the dinner. Sadly they were out of the chicken oyster and soft knee bone skewers when we were there, but we didn't really miss it, as we enjoyed other standouts like the chicken skin, gizzard, hearts, pork neck, and the negi tori don (chicken cubes served with a mild or spicy sauce with raw egg.. Mix it all together and enjoy!). Also had the cold tofu, agedashi tofu, tamago and Totto salad which were not bad as well. Have been to Yakitori Tori Shin a few times and I think as compared to that, Yakitori Totto has a slight edge for the variety of dishes offered besides the skewers. Excellent experience. Will be back!
Best burger i've had in Ny - Umami And the Dig Inn seasonal market is outstanding as well

I may or may not be nursing a mild addiction to Ippudo. I can't even remember how many times I've come here now, it's more or less become my number one ramen option in NYC. And embarrassingly enough, I've fallen so hard for the few dishes that I have gotten here the first couple times around that I hardly ever try anything new. Sorry. I'm a bad foodie. Anyways. Wasabi shoyu ramen. I firmly believe this is the very best vegetarian ramen I've ever tasted. The wasabi oil drizzled on top gives the ramen this addictive kick. But make sure you mix it up before you dig in! Or else you'll be that person choking at the table (and no one wants to be that person). I love the toppings (inari tofu, bamboo shoots, nori, etc.), and I will never, ever tire of this ramen. Also great for non-vegetarians who want something with a lighter broth. And get kaedama. Always get kaedama. Even when you're full and both your stomach and your brain are screaming that it's a bad idea. Shishito peppers. The most perfect appetizer to begin your Ippudo adventure with. The one time I forwent ordering this, I ended up staring at the ones the guy across me ordered with a disturbing lust for about 15 minutes (sorry, guy!). Squeeze lemon all over the peppers, dip them in the yuzu salt, and munch away. Try to furtively sneak more into your mouth while your dinner companion isn't looking. Some tips about the wait... Either come with the expectation of waiting about half an hour (the line usually isn't worse than that--a lot of people get tired and move onto Menkui-Tei or some other ramen place in the area) or go at super weird times. Once my roommate and I zoomed in here for a late lunch at about 3 pm, half an hour before lunch closes. No wait. Another time we came on Super Bowl Sunday. No wait. Another option is to come by yourself (who needs company anyways?? Not true Ippudo fans!), since some seating is communal and there's usually awkward one-seaters left. But my favorite has to be leaving my name and going shopping at Tokio 7 before dinner. Nothing works up the appetite like a hearty browse through the East Village consignment stores!

Noodles are far above the standard Chinatown place (I highly recommend the thicker ones). Â I had the mixed fish ball noodle soup and the fishballs were amazing. Â My friend had ox tail, which was enough to make her call this "her new favorite place." On the downside, the soup broth was bland, but after some soy/white pepper/chili paste it worked out fine.
This is a very nice and cozy cafe. They have delicious coffee and great food. Â This is a place where you fill up your tummy and relax your soul.

Really small and a bit hard to find- great for a one on one catchup meal or drinks. The octopus dish is DELICIOUS. Kale and squash risotto was very good as well. Some dishes (kale, pork belly) are too salty. Overall, great vibe and excellent food. Because it is so small, I would not recommend more than two people at a time.

Love this place! Â The food was RIGHT! Â Even though the tv was not working during the World Cup semifinals, their Manager Matthew was great. Â He kept us engaged with good food and drink selections and even suggested a place we Cld go to catch the end of the game when we were leaving. Can't wait to come back for their lamb chops and potatoes au gratin

Came here on a Friday evening around 8ish with a party of 3 and we got a nice corner table facing the rest of the restaurant (love that French-ish style of sitting). Â  We had 1 large #1 pizza special and 1 small Margherita pizza-more than enough for 3 people. Both pizzas were delicious and we couldnt help but shovel it all down. Probably could have stopped after 3 slices but NOPE-had 4 and a half.. The pancetta on the #1 Pizza special tasted so good and the scallions were an interesting and unexpected touch to the slice. If I make it back to brooklyn heights I probably want to try the pizza with salmon on it-quite a unique take on pizza toppings there. The only issue was having them split the check and also not allowing for any modifications on the pizza (my friend is a vegetarian so we wanted to take off the pancetta from half the pizza). Other than that, pretty pleasant experience, friendly staff!

One if the best breakfast places I have been to in New York. Everything about this joint is so hip and authentic from the menu to their style of service. We ordered the veggie flat and the hummus/feta sandwich and quesadilla omelette along with sweet potato fries. Everything was just mouth watering. SPF was the best I have had even when comparing to the ones in Belgium and Amsterdam. I love that they have unlimited refilled on coffee. Overall I thought the price is comparable and reasonable with their service taste and quantity. I would definitely come back again. Â 5stars all the way.

One word comes to mind about Boqueria. Â Flair. Â Yes... Boqueria's got lots of flair. Â it's quaint without being pretentious. Â In fact, it has no intent to become pretentious, ever. Â it's a nicely sized space... sleek & decorative... no gaudiness. Â gotta love it. Â bar seats, table seats for any occasion. Â wherever you want to sit at your own leisure. Â we have been kind enough to merit great food and customer service. Â the hosts and waiters are all super nice. my personal faves on the menu: Â  potato bravos (classic), pimientos (shisito peppers), squid tossed with some greens, bacon wrapped in dates stuffed with blue cheese, lamb meatballs and the seafood paella!!!!! Â  go easy on the potato bravos. Â it's too easy to stuff yourself here when everything is deliciosos. Â sangrias here are not half bad. Â I've definitely had better, but pairs well with their tapas. Â lots to choose from whether you're in a full bodied or light & spritz mood. Â  this place is fun for dates and especially large groups, but it can be quite loud. Â so keep that factor in mind. Â for parties of 6, the restaurant requires a $40 pri-fixe for the whole table. Â It's a bargain, considering I have always left content. Â  walk ins only!

My first review ever... Because it's necessary... I've visited this restaurant about 4 times already, and a matter of fact just got done murdering a steak and whiz about 30 mins ago... Lol If you're looking for a greasy cheese steak joint this isn't the place for you. Go to the mall. From a purists perspective, this is the filet Mignon of cheese steaks. This dude is taking some form of unprocessed lean strip steak and slicing trimming and grilling. I'd bet the sandwich content is probably equal to a 6-8oz sirloin that you would order in a restaurant and would pay more than $11... The bread they picked to use is legit too. The price is a bargain if you know what you're eating. Keep doing what you're doing. The people that understand and appreciate will happily pay for this quality of food. See ya soon.

3000+ reviews don't lie. This place is absolutely worth the wait (and with sake it's not so bad). The sizzling tofu pot was my highlight. It was spicy, sweet, hot, umami-ish.. Really bold and interesting flavors!

One word: charming. Â Too adorable for words, and the food is great too. Â I'm over the $5 corkage. Â But the fried oysters more than made up for it. Â Too bad it's literally on the highway, but you don't notice once you're inside.

i've been to this place twice and had desserts and teas each time. they were all lovely. the servings, however, are ridiculously small. the $17 chef set (3 desserts, 1 pot of tea) really should just be for one person. the desserts are worth 2 bites each, and the tea, 4 cups. since i'm on a limited budget, the serving sizes especially peeve me. if you're loaded, you should keep coming back, but i'm not going to.

Americanized Japanese food? Small plates. Interesting. You can get healthy stuff or fried stuff. In the end, perhaps I prefer something more traditional. Or at least Americanized traditional. Made a reservation for 6:30 on a Saturday with my wife. It wasn't difficult to secure, but by the time we arrived, our server warned us that another reservation was slated for 8:00pm. That was sort of off-putting. I didn't plan on eating for more than an hour and a half, and don't servers have talents for getting customers in and out rather quickly if they need to? Other than that, the service was fine... Started with edamame and fried brie. The edamame was weird. It was like grilled or something after it was boiled. The shells looked gross, but the beans inside were fine. The fried brie was AWESOME. first of all, fried cheese is always good, but this cheese was fried in some sort of edible wrapping. Even the ties of the wrapping were edible. Cool stuff. I was sort of underwhelmed by the menu. I wanted sushi, but sushi without all those gross toppings and sauces all over them. I ended up going boring: fries and a slab or miso pork or something. The meat was good and the fries were fries. My wife got some pork belly ramen and that Japanese egg omelette dish. She seemed to like it and would probably rate the place higher. Also, there is only one bathroom in this place, but the toilet is like a robot that can give you a front wash or rear wash if you'd like.
Awesome, amazing super pricey pizza. We love it.....
One of the better places for Thai food. Food is flavorful and tender. And they have Thai Iced tea. Extra star for that. Decor is chic. A good date place.

I'm not sure if I went to the same restaurant as the rest of you... The service was inattentive, at best (I was sitting at the bar and had to wait quite a while for a glass of water, it took us a while to order and they didn't think to bring us silverware until after they'd brought us our food); the dish I ordered was bland and didn't deliver on its promise (I ordered the "tempura" fish and chips, but there was nothing crispy or tempura-y about it); and it was delivered on a plastic plate. Â If I'm to be honest, the plastic plate was the straw for me (especially because my dining companion got an actual plate...and the place wasn't full so they couldn't have run out of plates...AND I saw stacks of various types and shapes of real plates at the kitchen window)...just truly bizarre.

Great spot! I ordered a chicken bowl with Mediterranean salad, their signature sauce (forget the same... Sorry :/), carrots, lettuce, tomatoes, and corn with their amazing hot sauce. Long live their HOT SAUCE!!! Their hot sauce was the reason I rated them 4 stars. In my opinion their food is lacking flavor. It's appears that there isn't any seasoning. It's my first time experiencing Mediterranean food so I didn't know what to expect. I didn't hate the place and will stop by another time I'm in the neighborhood to try a different dish. I just wish it had more flavor or spice. The hot sauce served as some some flavor for my chicken bowl. If your in the neighborhood give it a try. Just be sure to add some type of flavoring to your dish of choice.

When somebody is doing something right, you should just say it! And Emily delivers a great dinner experience! The ambiance is cozy and elegant with some tables in the front and a great "chef's" table in the back right next to the pizza action! The food is just awesome: you can't go wrong with fried Brussels sprouts, duck trumpets are a great pasta option, and the Emily pizza is a must to try! Finally a great pizzeria in the area!
Very casual interior, excellent price/quality ratio. Will be coming back, whenever back in NYC.

Ranks among my favorite places in the city. Â The atmosphere (teeny tiny, narrow, quaint and smelling of butter), service (casual, warm with a touch of friendly, snarky banter) and food (OMG the food!) really do transport me back to Paris, and some of the better neighborhood bistros, at that. Â  I've probably had each dish on their menu 4x over, and my favorite remains the duck. Â No, the pork. Â No, wait -- the duck. Â No, maybe the mussels. Â Ooooh! Â The pureed carrots! Â Errr, try them all -- you won't be displeased. Â And if you don't have much of a sweet tooth, opt for a second appetizer instead of dessert, which is quite standard here. Â  And BYO? Â What's better than that? Â If you intend to order a 3 course meal, I'd suggest about a bottle per diner. Â (But then, I'm a bit of a lush.) Â  And yes, MAKE RESERVATIONS! (Edited to add: If it's your first time here, do order the duck, pork, mussels or steak -- it represents the best that they make. Â I've noticed that Yelpers who gave La Sirene low marks ordered otherwise.)

I walked into an empty restaurant and the host -_- looked at me and my girlfriend and said we can't seat you without a reservation. Â There was a line of customers because he refused to sit people and this is not the first time I refuse to go there ever again. Â  Definitely not worth the hype.

Excellent service! Friendly staff! Came here for a Sunday Brunch and this place was packed. I was greeted by a friendly hostess who put my name down on the waiting list. The waiting time was about Â 20 minutes. There was barely any room to wait inside so I chose to wait outside instead. I was seated next to the bar ( came here alone). Â I ordered 2 dishes with my a cup of coffee and a Bloody Mary. What I ordered: Steak & eggs - medium rare with scrambled eggs served with roasted potatoes, it was delicious! Belgian waffles - served with apple crepes & whipped cream, tasted great too! Bloody Mary- Personally not my favorite. Â It was too zesty; got too much spice going on. Kind of taste like those herbal medicine drinks. Then again, everyone's taste bud is different. My total bill came out to $29 without tips.

This is not a pizza..it's an artichoke casserole baked on pizza dough. The taste was good, but don't go here because you like pizza. It's a pretty no frills eatery. Service was friendly and efficient.

The area and the place is definitely sketchy looking; not appealing whatsoever. However, once inside it's pretty chill and that pizza is fantastic! The pie I ordered had brussel sprouts, onions and a whole bunch of other goodness on it that I can't recall at the moment, was so delish. Wasn't crazy about the service, but I would go back still for the pizza.
i think it's a lil over-rated. i like the other local joints and their xiao long bao. not big about sharing tables.

Oh how I miss NY pizza. I was recommended this place by a friend of mine to try their artichoke & crab pizza, and after taking my first bite, I know it was something I can never forget! Be prepare to either spend $5 a slice or just get a whole pie for $40, it's definitely worth your money. I waited over 30 minutes for my pie with my friend, but the taste and experience of trying NY pizza is priceless.

Great little burger joint. Try the chicken wings and pulled-pork sandwich or if your strictly veggie, the portobello sandwich with salad is great! Each month or so they feature artists' works, and play great music. Great place for a comfy date or solo eating at the counter. Usually a 10-15 minute wait but well worth it.
Decent. Â Quick. Â Good enough. Â I'd go back, and I'd recommend it for a quick, reasonably priced meal. Â  Food was tasty. Â Service was efficient and quick. Â Mostly tourists.
Easily the BEST chicken fingers I've EVER had

OVERRATED!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!! i think it's all mental, you hear that this place is the shit from erryone else so when you try it, you're conditioned to agree, or else no one is your friend anymore the white secret sauce.. kinda suspicious if ya ask me! ok, ok... i mean, it's not bad, but it's not as good as everyone else makes it sound.. taste better if you're DRUNK AS FACKKKK one time i had the white sauce all over my mouth, and i didn't know... not cool

Tiny place. Bar seating only and only room for about 15 people I think. Got take out and the food is pretty decent. Had a fish taco, pork taco, and the breakroom fries. The fish taco was alright. The pork taco was better. A bit more flavor in it and the breakroom fries is pretty tasty. A lot going on in it but still pretty decent. People were great inside. Friendly and nice. Overall a decent place for some variety by the edge of Chinatown.

On a Sunday evening, the wait was quick. Â Gnocchi was delish - we split it as an app. Â The fish of the day was superb, and the chocolate dessert hit the spot, even if it was $8. The wait can be really long on popular nights. Â The wine is served in non-wine glasses, so it's hard to tell if the servings are the right size, though they did feel a little small. I definitely recommend coming unless the wait is longer than 30 minutes (and it often is).

This is one of those hidden treasure places, found in the back of a jewelry store that always seems to be empty. Their banh mi is clean-tasting, relatively grease-free, very filling (I usually can't finish a sandwich), and CHEAP (3.75 for the #1).
