I would like to stay at Grape and Grain. Will they adopt me? Inside and out the decor is absolutely adorable. I love the chandeliers and the ceiling with the exposed brick. The pink ballons on New Years Eve added to the cute-ness. We had a reservation at the bar, but when we arrived, we were greeted with a smile and told that we could take a table because someone (thankfully for us!) didnt show up. The waiters were very friendly and answered all of our questions, and didnt mind our sillyness at all. Drink menu was awesome! Lots of choices, and lots of really reasonable big drinks for great prices. We didnt eat here, but the food looked and smelled absolutely phenomenal. I'm dying to go back and try it. It was a great NYE spot, but would be a great date spot, or girls night out place too!

Cute little place to pick up an excellent crepe. I love Japanese style crepes and this is the spot to get one! They are open early so its perfect to pick up a breakfast crepe and have it to go with a cup of coffee. I love the traditional style with tons of nutella ... yum. Its my perfect go to place for breakfast to go.

Sofia's is the best wine bar in NYC. Â The wine list is extensive and the authentic Italian dishes from the pizza and sliders all the way to dessert...simply awesome! Great place for a first (or last) date. The only regret you may have is that you will wish you were able to get a table sooner.

The food here taste so good late at night when your tired and drunk from a long night of partying. Â However, when your not drunk and come here during the day time, you realize that the food is pretty average. Â There are definitely better places around to get good roast pork or duck. Â Come here only if its past 2am because its the only place youll find open at that time.

Solid ramen spot in NYC. Â Would I go here over Ippudo? Prob not given that the wait is about the same. Â Totto's broth is VERY hearty so you gotta prepare your stomach it. Pork buns? Too much mayo. I know Japanese people love mayo but come on, mix it up a little with some spice!

Wow! Stopped in today for brunch and was so impressed! My boyfriend and I ordered a selection of small plates and salads -- each one flavorful, interesting and delicious. The four plates, including falafel, "crazy baba", smoky beet and lentil salad, were more than enough food. And yes, the grilled pita (white and whole wheat) is perfect. Will definitely be back.

This is the place to go after the track! It's a "who's who" of celebrities and big shots. The salad is just like the one your Nonna used to make! Order the baked clams and linguine and clam sauce. Cash only ! and don't forget the camera. Bella ciao!!

This is a great restaurant. I went for lunch, had beautiful zucchini soup with curry, scallops with beets, and a very unusual dessert, a Chocolate Bacon Tart. If you put Chocolate and Bacon in the same sentence my taste buds go into hyperdrive,but in the same dish?? Â It was fabulous, even a little cream and bacon crumble on top, and a caramel drizzle on the plate. Everything was superb and price wasn't bad. It was dramatically better than my dinner the night before at Gotham Bar and Grill where the food was a bit boring and over-priced. Â UPDATE: I have been here 2-3 times since and the food and service remain fantastic. The great thing about Gramercy is the staff is not at all snobbish when they could be and make you feel very welcome. Last month, had the tasting menu for lunch, beautifully done, sat across from Philip Seymour Hoffman, my favorite actor!!

So, for Chloe F.'s birthday her mom Mary S (of NYC Yelp Fame) wanted to take us to Perry St. by Jean Georges. I was totally excited and when I found out about their $24 'Taste of Winter' prix fixe menu, I figured the day couldn't get much better. I was wrong. To start, the decor is great, a little too minimalistic for my taste, but great none-the-less. White on white on white, trimmed in white. Right up front on against the windows were these big round booth that comfortably would seat 8, the perfect size of table in my opinion. Not too large so as one can't talk across the table; but large enough to include seven great friends. But on to the menu: The Cocktails: while I didn't take the opportunity to try one (it was lunch people!) They looked intriguing and delicious. In addition to the great looking cocktails there was house-made sodas, including organic grape soda made from different kinds of grapes. The Wine: In my opinion very reasonably priced. While somewhat small and limited, they did have lots of familiar wines and also had a wine special of $22/bottle, of which we partook, it was delicious (a cote du rhone)! The Food: Oh, how delicious!!! The menu consisted of 14 dishes of which you get to choose two. How ever you order it is how it arrives on the table, so if you order the steak first and your salad second, just be prepared. All of the dishes were slightly larger than an average appetizer and after two, plus choice of desert, I was full. There were definitely some highlights to the menu; the Peekytoe Crab Salad, the Grilled Hanger Steak (the most tender hanger steak I've ever had the pleasure to chew on), and the Beet Salad were all fantastic. I think that my favorite of all may have been the beet salad. Quartered beets with what I'm guessing was either house made or imported ricotta cheese, sprinkled with dried cherries, and candied pecans. At this point you may be thinking, what's special about this beet salad? Well let me tell you... sprinkled on top was crystallized/granulated wasabi, it gave the dish just enough heat to cut through the fattiness of the ricotta and just enough zip to balance the sweetness of the beets and cherries. Delicious!! Sadly one dish we sampled was a miss; the Artic Char Sashimi- it was flavorless and boring, only tasting of the lemon zest and olive oil. The best part of it was the crispy bits of fried Artic Char skin that garnished the plate. The Service: Its interesting that two of the worst service experiences I've ever had were in NYC, supposedly the pinnacle of dining...and both took place at restaurants by some of the biggest chefs in NYC. The first was a couple of years ago at BLT Fish, couldn't get a drink to save my life...and the second was Perry St. What gives chefs? It seemed as if they were a bit understaffed, the bartender took our order, only one server, and one busser. We regularly had to wave somebody down to get any attention... the staff wasn't even visually checking back with us from across the room, I don't think the manager even glanced toward our table once! He was actually rude to one of our guests who asked about the coat check - just pointing and saying "back there", not offering to take her coat or anything... Overall: Fantastic and I'd definitely go back and it would have been a 5-star experience except for the service. BC- Loved the bathrooms! Perfect size, great lighting and the level of music was perfect. Very simple and minimalistic like the rest of the Perry St.
You need not order anything except the crab and pork noodles. You will float high into a heavenly abyss of delicate sweet and savory flavors and your tastebuds will love you forever and ever.

I heart this place so much. I would love to give it 5 stars, but because they are quite disorganized during the week, they get a minus star. Let me break it down: It's my at least once a week lunch place and from the sounds of it, other people feel the same way. The bad: Â It's typically quite busy and its just clusters of people waiting. I don't know who has ordered, who is waiting to order or who is just standing there for fun. When they yell, "NEXT," it's usually several people looking at each other saying, "Have you ordered? have you ordered?" Â When you do order they take your order and then walk away. I think it would be beneficial to take my name and also my money at the time of ordering. HOWEVER I deal with the bad because I LOVE their food. The good: Middle Eastern Turkey (Spicy). Perfect sandwich of turkey, hummus, greens and tomatoes. I get it on the pita because it seems less bready then the others and I have converted most co-workers to order it with the pita now. Also tell them to toast the pita. The French Bite: I dont know if it's seasonal but it's there right now and if they take it away it will be a very sad sad day for me. Ham or Turkey, brie cheese, greens and sweet mustard. This you get on multigrain bread TOASTED. Trust me on this. It's a fine science to that perfect sandwich. Goat Cheese Salad: Delicious, the title says it all. My only slight problem is that they stuff the container so much its hard to put the dressing on it and coat the entire salad perfectly. This is hard for people on the go. In a nutshell (after a very long review): GREAT food, cheap prices. Not efficient and can be frustrating from that aspect.

Overrated. Overpriced too. [1] Ramen: not that great. I've been to Tokyo. and LA. Ramen noodles here were just not up to par. [2] Seared Ahi Tuna: I've had better Ahi Tuna at American restaurants. [3] SUPER long line. Like somehow you feel "Jeez - look at that line!! It MUST be good." Only two good aspects: ambiance and drinks. It's more like a pre-club hangout.

Bespoke cocktails are amazing... this really needs to be more of a thing in the Bay Area. Anyways, the bespoke cocktails here are great. The bartenders know what they are doing for sure. The menu has some really good choices too. This place was a great respite from the rain on a Sunday night.

Food: ~Cuban sandwich (3 stars): made to order. Â It was a little bit underwhelming, but perhaps I was expecting too much. Â The ham tasted as if it'd just come from a supermarket, but it was nice toasty when we ate it. Â The melted cheese and sauce made it better than it would have been. Â $5.50 ~Octopus salad (4 stars): even though it was cold outside, I didn't want to stop eating it. Â After eating half, however, I did think that the acidity became a bit much. Â It was essentially an octopus salsa. $10 Wait: no wait for a table for 2 at 1:30pm on a Friday, but it took about 10 minutes after we ordered/paid for the Cuban sandwich, as they are each made to order. I don't think we'll come out of our way to eat here again, but it does serve up simple, decent Cuban food.

We were lucky enough to find a table here at 6:30pm last minute. We got the polenta, duck and foie gras ravioli, spaghetti with basil and tomato sauce and the chocolate cake with salted caramel ice cream. The stand out dish for me was the spaghetti, which was so simple but blew me away. You may not think this dish is worth $24 at first, but by the time your plate is clean, you will! It feels so authentic that you would think your non-existent Italian grandma Â made it for you. The ravioli was also great and very rich so don't be greedy and share. To contrast the two pastas, I would say that I would never tire of eating the spaghetti while I would for the ravioli. The polenta was my sister's favorite and it was truly wonderful with the truffle mushrooms. I love anything chocolate and salted caramel, so the dessert was the perfect combo for me. It wasn't the best chocolate cake I've ever had but it was still superb. For drinks, we had the dimmi pera and mare limpido. Both drinks were recommended by our fantastic waiter John and they were both terrific. The dimmi pera was flavorful and unique. Our meal for two cost about $130. For an overall A+ meal, we will definitely be coming back!

Pretty perfect pizza and a must try for NY pizza fans at some point. Esp watching him make the pizzas. It might be impossible to live up to the hype but it definitely beats the other hyped places like grimaldi's. Not much seating though, and one downside is the crust is blah - it doesn't have the perfect crispy-chewy texture of Motorino's crust but I rarely eat my crust. That's ok cause the two cheeses and olive oil goodness of the pizza is so delicious. Plain or with toppings, you can't go wrong. Funny story - they didn't collect payment because our pizzas came at different times. We ended completely forgetting to pay until we asked our friend how much we owed - had to come back to the restaurant to pay because they forgot too!

Love this breakfast spot. I've stood in 15 minute lines outdoors in the freezing cold for it, and I rarely leave the house if it's below 35 degrees. And no, there is no seating, in-doors or out. But this food is pretty heavy so I recommend walking and eating if you can manage. I always get the grits. GRITS! So creamy and well-seasoned. Then I top it with a soft-boiled egg (this is their standard egg style) and some kind of super tasty sauce like their baba ganush, Sicilian salsa verde, or some jalapeno something yummy. Big fat slabs of bacon or spicy chicken meatballs... I haven't even tried their baked goods, but provided their name and the other amazing dishes I've had I'd say it's probably the bomb. Highly recommended. A god-send for the Bed Stuy brunch folk.

I came here today for lunch with 2of my friends. It was nice that they had a lunch special,which we could get a combination for a good price. The food was of course delicious and all of the waitresses were nice and friendly. Very satisfied every time I come here! :)

Shares an order of the tostones with cheese and I'm glad that filled me up b/c the De Pabellon arepa was eh. The meat was kind of oily, kind of bland and the arepa tasted stale. I wanted to love this place after hearing so many great things about it.

I would rate this place 4.5 if I could. Wish there were more beers to choose from, but the meatballs are amazing. I loved the sliders and you can't go wrong with the standard beef and tomato hero. ALWAYS TRY THE SPECIAL MEATBALL! They had a buffalo chicken meatball that is to die for. Also, if you have the room, have that ice cream sandwich!
Absolute great service. Love the spaghetti with meatballs and great pizza as well. Impeccable service.

it's just ok I would say - little expensive and you can't fold the slice..for a true NY guy no fold is no dice. Roberta's, Paulie gee's etc are much better just sayin' - the locals gotta make it at least as good as those newer hipster spots??
The brisket was dried.

I only shared the hummus dish with grilled chicken and a few drinks with a friend when I went - but it was SO good it warranted a write-up. Â Some of the very best hummus I have EVER had, and I've been to the Middle East a number of times. Â The waiter, who was very charming and attentive, told us the chef imports the tahini from the middle east. Â And the bread was diet-breaking worthy. I am only disappointed that I only ate a small nosh there. I plan to go back very soon.

Came here for brunch last weekend by accident. Â  I love decor of this this place, set up like park benches, very cozy environment. Â The service was also very attentive. Â We ordered the bread pudding for dessert and it was probably the best of all the dishes. Will definitely be back to try their dinner!
This place is absolutely delicious, in every way. Amazing decor and helpful staff. Probably one of the nicest places i've ever eaten

This is my go-to for soup dumplings! I always have the same waiter, I recognize him, but he doesn't recognize me, he probably hates me but I love him! I take all my American friends here to experience my heritage. They are confused on soup in a dumpling, but then we eat them together and then they understand.

Having never tried Cuban food before I was intrigued and subsequently delighted to experience this new culinary world. Â I'm glad I did. Â Fantastic sandwiches, so fresh and flavoursome. Â The Pork was literally the best I've tasted ever..washed down with a very well selected range of beers. Â  Despite the huge space it feels warm in both temperature and ambience. Â Stylish and yet homely with sharply dressed and attentive staff bringing together a true 1930's feel to Brooklyn. Go there, go back and keep on enjoying this wonderful tasty find!
wonderful quality food...the vibe is pretty good but can you guys give the dylan a break? jeeeez...too much of a good thing
Completely worth the wait, Â I actually liked it better than the ramen in japan. Probably because you can't really get things spicy there. Â Their Spicy ramen is the best!
Nothing special for beef pho, too crowded on a Thursday they squished 3 groups on one table and you had to share . Surprised at 4 stars. cheap though !

place is good...food is amazing!!! place is very small so its probaly always gonna be very crowded so dont expect to sit and be in peace...but the food is awsome and very cheap priced...like $20 a person and thats with appitizers and entree...defintly in the mood for it right now..see ya later im there...peace

Not that Lucali's really needs another review, but our experience was as great as we hoped for. Our waitress was great and helpful since we were indecisive. The pizza was great, almost as good as it was in Naples but not quite there. The calzone was amazing. 4 of us split a pizza and a large calzone and we thought we would be hungry after but the calzone filled us up. I wish they had some special dessert, I would have liked to spend more time there. Maybe next time I'll get espresso. (I think they have it?)

i can never remember that street this place is on - e 4th, 5th, 6th - so invariably end up wandering a few blocks either side, when i'll usually end up finding a nice bar, or, on a recent sunday, spending a while in the community garden on avenue b, just around the corner. i am somewhat of a creature of habit when i visit this place, and i just love their shoyu ramen, lots of silky goodness in the broth, and amazing tender pork pieces. Â  Â  not a fan of the nori sheet, but that's just me, not gonna hold it against them. Â  i rarely get anything else. Â  i'm also a fan of the crunchy radish salad with a really nice salty sesame dressing. Â the gyoza are really good too.

After hearing so much about Roberta's on social media, blogs, etc I was incredibly excited to try this place during my weekend nyc trip, and I'm elated to say it lived up to the hype! The Beastmaster (tomato, mozz, gorgonzola, pork sausage, red onion, capers, jalapeno) and Bee Sting (tomato, mozz, sopressata, honey, chili) were divine. Must. Order. These. Pizzas. They were exceptional: Â soft and chewy crust; thoughtful topping combinations; high-quality ingredients; perfect execution. Some of the best pizzas I've ever eaten. If you ask your server, they'll bring you a menu of several additional pizzas that are always available to be ordered. The atmosphere inside is very rustic and most of the seating consists of picnic communal style tables. The employees and clientele were very hipster. I could care less about the decor or fashion sense of the crowd though when the pizzas are so exceptional. We thought we'd be the first to arrive around their 10am weekend opening time, but there were several parties already seated when we arrived at 10:15am. Guess I'm not the only person who enjoys stuffing my face with pizza at this early hour. #pizzaanytime. If Chicago had a Roberta's, I'd be a regular. During my next trip to nyc, Roberta's will surely be one of the first places penciled into my itinerary. Highly recommend!

Obao is a beautiful, relaxing, high end pan-asian experience at a reasonable price. space is beautiful, staff very fast and professional. food was EXCELLENT. I had Dill Fish which was fried pieces on top of vermicelli, vietnamese style. so good even my fish averse bf was grabbing it.

Everything we ordered was bland. Â The decor and service were very good, but the bland food just overwhelmed the rest of the experience. We ordered the cold seafood appitizer which had less than perfectly fresh seafood which is a sin considering this place is near the seaport (yeah I know the fishmarket moved to the Bronx, but still). Â Additionally we had a seafood chowder which was also boring and it was really for two (which didn't help), 1 crab cake (again bland) and an iceberg lettuce salad. Â Between that and a few drinks, the bill was an outrageous $140 without tip. This was a complete ripoff, I will not be back.
this is my fave dumpling place. five for a dollar and i think it's really pork.

The boyfriend and I were looking for a low key last minute dinner spot on a friday night and based on the abundance of open reservations I was surprised by how busy the place was when we got there. We were seated promptly and started with a few appetizers. The portabella and kobe buns were both delicious and even though I'm not a huge fan of shishito peppers, those were great too! We were tempted to try the ramen, but on this visit we stuck to sushi. We ordered an assortment of rolls and pieces and were very satisfied with the quality, freshness and cuts of fish. On our next visit we stopped in without a reservation and ate at the sushi bar instead of waiting for a table. This time we opted to try the short rib buns and the ramen and both did not disappoint! While this is no Totto ramen, it hit the spot without having to trek uptown and wait for 2 hours. I can definitely see this being a regular spot for us this winter when we're in the mood for a steaming bowl of ramen and some delicious, creative buns!

The food was pretty good but the good service earned it the 3rd star. My water glass was always full which is a big perk of mine. It means that they're attentive. The thai iced tea was delicious and came in a much bigger cup than I've seen other places serve. It lasted our entire meal which really helped with the spicy stuff we ordered. Hot pot dumplings were interesting but not too impressive. It was a bit dry and a bit sweet and had too much crushed nuts. A bit sweeter and it would have made a decent desert. We also ordered the Beef Pad Kee Mow and Wasabi Tuna. The Pad had a perfect spiciness for me and I really enjoyed it. The Tuna was perfectly done and a really big piece. Totally looking forward to coming back to try out the other stuff on the menu in the future.

The staff here I found quite helpful in terms of helping navigate the restless sea of Italian cuisine. Keep in mind, this is America, and nothing here is a true representation of the actual fare one might find among the lifetime denizens of a quaint Sardinian estate. Notwithstanding, the uninitiated gourmand should find shopping here a joyous and easy task with the well-meaning staff leading you through the spicy and satisfying variety's of italian wine, cheese, and coffee. Beware, you will spend more than you intend, so this place is not for the faint of wallet. But a fulfilling experience nonetheless.

Great place for Brunch. Friends and I were planning on heading to an over populated/over hyped brunch destination when we ran across Balaboosta in Nolita- which was was quiet and lovely looking- we were all pleasantly surprised when we looked at the menu unique brunch options and delicious morning cocktails. Can't wait to go back!

Pylos is by far my favorite place in town!!! Both the food and the service are terrific! I don't know how many times I've been there, but they already know me pretty well.. :) I love their Greek salad, and a version where they add calamari... Just delicious! I am from Barcelona and it reminds me to my beloved Mediterranean culture. As I said at the beginning, the service is as good as the food. They are friendly and fun! Some of them became friends!
Pretty good neighborhood Italian, with prices a little on the high side for this sort of place. Â Can be very noisy in the main dining room. Â Try the enclosed garden out back.

The music starts off on the loud side, but it is still background music, until...out of nowhere, it's blasting!!! At which point I had a flashback to the only other time we were there with Atif back in '07 and we requested the music be lowered. The owner's solution...drink more wine. ARG. it was so damn loud we were shouting with our dinner companions and after a while we just gave up trying to have a conversation at all. My little guys even started to cover their ears it was just too loud, and the owner really doesn't give a fuck if it's too loud. Not only that, it is weirdly eclectic not going well together music, jumping from Led Zep to Sade, then opera and The Police. Just awful.
came here for my birthday and loved it the environment was great food was amazing had to wait 10min after my reservation for a table because the place was packed but well worth it

Don't order the Frog Porridge. Â However, not that it and all sorts of exotic, "I hear that tastes like chicken type stuff is on the menu. I always get the Chicken Noodle Soup... Of course I get a soda on the Side! youtube.com/watch?v=bXMKâ€¦

Plus we hung out the whole time outside by the car. I will always come back when in Brooklyn and will tell everyone about this place. Hands down the best.

ippudo was our first destination straight from jfk (luggage still in hand). there was only about a ten minute wait or so on a tuesday night, which was perfect, because we weren't fed on the plane and it was just starting to sprinkle; perfect ramen weather. we started with a pork bun each and a fried chicken appetizer to share. i did my yelp research beforehand and knew what to expect regarding the wonderfulness of the pork buns. but my goodness! a giant, fatty piece of pork belly, with a little bit of spice and a smooth, creamy sauce. delicious. the fried chicken, on the other hand, was nothing too special. it was good, but it had nothing on the fried chicken at hurry curry in west la. our bodies were still thawing from the cold nyc air when our ramen arrived. i went with the akamaru modern ramen just cause it sounded intriguing. the broth was pretty good, it was rich and delicious, but nothing unlike i've had at several places around la. the pork belly in the soup was thick and tender, but there was only one piece. i was a little disappointed in the portion size of the noodles given the price. i don't know how much food goes for in nyc, but in downtown la, you can get a lot more ramen that tastes just as good. all in all, the ramen wasn't, by any measure, the best i've ever had, but it was delicious and it definitely did the trick in warming us up and satisfying our craving for something comforting. but those pork buns! damn! seeing as how we weren't sure when we would be back, we ordered another round for dessert. thus, the fourth star. if i lived in nyc, i could see myself visiting ippudo pretty often.

In writing this review, I thought about how best to describe the great dinner we recently had at Locanda Verde. Should I focus on the rustic, homey, woody interior in which the wintry smells of woodfire and anise greeted us? Should I talk about the service that, while a little pushy, was informative and attentive? Or should I talk about seeing Uncle Jesse (of Jesse and the Rippers) as we left? Nah, I decided to go down the cheesy route and describe LV's food, using part-owner Robert DeNiro's movies that I've seen as the rating system. Now onto the food: Lemon foccacia (complimentary): Meet the Parents--Funny and DeNiro was surprisingly comical; the bread was warm, crispy on the outside, and the slight taste of lemon really was a surprising feature. Lamb meatball sliders ($12): Untouchables--DeNiro stole every scene as Al Capone and you wanted more; the meatballs were flavorful and the addition of cucumber created crunch and great taste to the whole package. But for $12, I thought we'd be getting a little more than just 2 small sliders. Fonduta ravioli with wild mushrooms ($19): Heat--Huge expectations considering DeNiro and Pacino on the same screen but kind of a letdown; Similarly, 8 big ravioli with wild mushrooms looked amazing but the filling was overpoweringly cheesy, which took away from the earthiness of the mushrooms Olive oil poached cod ($26): Godfather II--Just a great movie and DeNiro's Vito Corleone was subtly brilliant; The dish looked and seemed so simple but the cod was moist and flaky with the slight taste of olive oil and lemon. Wild chickpeas were a great accompaniment Fire-roasted garlic chicken ($21): Goodfellas--Loud and brash but a thoroughly good movie about family; Served for 2 and they give you a whole chicken carved into 8 pieces. Â Crispy skin, very garlicky (even for a Korean) chicken similar to Asian-style rotisserie chicken with perfectly roasted veggies. Maple budino ($9): Raging Bull--DeNiro's best performance as an actor; One of the best restaurant desserts I've ever had--it's just a pudding but the maple flavor and the rich creaminess are enhanced in texture and flavor by the candied pecans on top. Â This completely overshadowed the other dessert we got, the ricotta cheesecake. What I take away from LV is that DeNiro's movie list is incredible. But also, LV provides a rustic, comforting environment with really solid, simply prepared food. While the food isn't as adventurous or at the level of a Babbo, LV is also a little less expensive and friendlier for groups wanting to have a good time and talk about DeNiro movies.

There are plenty of bakeries and cafes in Manhattan that sell macarons, but Laduree is my uncontested winner. And the ones at Laduree ($2.70 each) aren't that much more expensive than macarons elsewhere. I am blown away at how I can tell the difference between a Parisian macaron and a Manhattan-made one. Swing around Madison Avenue and treat yourself to one of these deluxe cookies!

I bought the groupon for this place and it was well worth it. I had the well-known surf and turf dish. Where there are 2 pieces of lamb chop and a skewer of shrimp. The lamb chop was overcooked and was very chewy. The shrimp was cooked a lot better. For dessert, I had the rice pudding. It was really delicious and I thought the portion was kind of small. The waitress that was assigned to our table is so eager to take our order- she bombarded us with the "Specials" that we cannot understand what she's talking about, Â I asked her to show me in the Menu if it's listed? with that she won't entertain to comply and gave Â me a lingo that is not appropriate for anyone to experience in a place of dining- I was offended and lost my interest to dine with that we left the place disappointed. Loved this place as soon as I stepped in. My boyfriend and I started out with the chips and guacamole which was AMAZING! The avocados were definitely fresh & ripe. still...one of the best in BK!!

This is a very special place. Â I thought the service was exceptional by fine dining standards, although it is a more welcoming, casual spot. Â Not stuffy at all for the level of service presented. Â My server was very well-versed on the wines by the glass and knew exactly what I was looking for when I said I wanted a "funky" white, and poured me a Roussane that really opened up nicely as it warmed up in my glass. Â Interesting and unique selections by the glass. Â  The food menu was fun, too. Â It's a set menu, so if you are particular with your likes and dislikes, you may not enjoy as much the lovely and divine feeling I had, which was just to show up and have my decisions already made for me. Â And it was soooo good, as was the monkfish, and everything, really. Â Also, the bread was lovely, so please order it. Â And even though we didn't get the additional cheese course, which I regret not doing, it looked pretty heavenly at the table next to us. And the desserts were ethereal and really challenged traditional dessert notions, like a wonderful beet puree with goat's milk yogurt parfait. Â At least I think that's what it was, I just know I really enjoyed it. You can trust this place to deliver and to excite your senses. Â I marvelled at what a beauty this menu was and also what an exceptional value this place is at $55 per person. Â I just moved away from NYC, and this place will have to be a part of my travel plans upon my return, just to see what magical, new menu pops up. Â I am so excited I just happened to hear about this place while I was in town. On a side note, I now reside in Los Angeles and have seen a lot of fussy, dieting, allergy ridden and vegetarian diners. Â If you are one of these diners, do be nice to this place if you go, I'd just hate to see the lot of you not like it because it's a place that already has a pre-set menu. Â Restaurants aren't built to "build" a menu just for you and it is embarrassing when I am in the company of these people. Â You know who you are ;)
Yummy homemade udon... what else could anyone want!
Great mussels and frites! I've tried almost every style. Â Apps are good. Nice selection of beers. Â Consistently a good meal and value. Â Attentive waitstaff.

A basket full of fries, what can be better? The moment I entered the tiny store, I was already salivating for what to come. We ordered a large cone of pomme frites with three sauces: curry ketchup, spicy mayo and mango chutney. The fries were so good it really did not need the sauces. The sauces only enhanced the tastiness of the fries. I wish I can go back everyday just to eat those wonderful twice-fried fries. Pomme frites, I will return for more.

OUT OF CONTROL GOOD!!! They don't even need your business, because the lines are out the door. But once you've tired their roast pork you'll never be the same. I've been supporting this family since they were a street cart on Bowery Street. Everything is good, ask for extra sauce, be picky, and all your request will be granted. Get one of these $3 roasted pork on rice dishes and it will fill any big eater. Maybe it's the mound of roasted pork you get, the splash of lard and drippings at the end, dirty floors, lack of AC, no decor, the TLC from chopping every piece of roasted pork, or it's simply the fact that they never take any breaks nor any days off to make a great product. Now that is respect.

Found this restaurant on flavor town USA and thought I would give it a try and it was so worth it !!! Party of two walked in and was seated right away. Â I got the redhead fizz drink which was delicious and lemony. My date and I ordered the chips and dip along with the lamb meatballs which were very tasty. Main courses.. Fried chicken just like the other reviews was AMAZING, I had the smoked trout which was also great! Â Lastly, the two sides fried tomatoes were so awesome and crispy and the broccoli was cheesy and tasted great. Great find here!!!!

Ippudo finally got my business. I know they've been eagerly awaiting my $13 + $3 for braised pork belly for a long time. I apologize that it took so long, but the wait and the timing just hasn't been right for a while. So my time finally came. I made my journey over to Ippudo on a Saturday. It was the first real day of autumn - you know the real autumn where a light jacket makes you just a tiny bit cold, but it's a nice, comfortable cold. Basically, it was the perfect day for a bowl of delicious ramen. We showed up just before 5pm, in time for the daily ceremonial 5pm opening where the nice ramen man hangs the "OPEN" sign right over the window. Thanks to kristine r.'s (note the lowercase k) recommendation, I got the Akamura ramen with pork. Unlike her, though, I had no qualms lifting the bowl to my mouth, so I devoured every last drop of that soup. The noodles were a perfect texture and the medley of various meats swirled into the heavenly broth absolutely melts in your mouth. Perhaps this next bit will show just how gluttonous I am. My biggest complaint is that I was nowhere near full after I finished my bowl of ramen. Neither were my dinner companions, so we ordered one order of pork buns, one order of chicken buns (4 buns in total). They were delicious!! A little too much sauce, but, to me, that's better than the opposite problem. I liked the pork one better, but I definitely have a bias towards pork. Either way, both were delicious. I really can't give the 5 star rating yet. Perhaps when I start craving it more, I'll give Ippudo the final star. For now, I don't appreciate the strategic timing that has to go into dining there. And, the price of the bowl really should have left me full, not searching for more food. Either way, this is possibly the best bowl of ramen you'll find in NY, so the time and money is what you'll have to give into the experience.

Obviously there's a lot of talk about this place, and I finally made my way over there the other day. I was pleasantly surprised that there was hardly a wait, since I've heard and read about long lines. There's nothing more I hate than a long wait for a slice of pizza (I'm looking at you, Di Fara's). I might not hate drunkenly waiting for a slice late at night though, as the namesake slice was absolutely yummy. While the sauce was unmemorable (might not be on the Sicilian, that's next on my list), the artichoke and cheese were great. They more than made up for it. What I love even more is that the slice was huge and filling. You would think that a "specialty" pizza or what have you would be slightly smaller, but these guys aren't messing around. This is some solid pizza, and I can't wait to go back for more.

Last night was my first experience dining at Trattoria L,incontro. So glad we had reservations for a Saturday night as it was very crowded- no empty tables. Fairly large restaurant and I didnt expect the service to be outstanding but it was. The food is so flavourful . Â We ordered the oysters which my husband said was the best he ever had, the baked clams, tasty and served in a lemon butter sauce,the mixed green salad with figs, incredible taste, the kale with pear and a strong parm? cheese enhanced the flavor, the cold calamari salad served with cannelini beans in a delicious dressing were the appetizers. Before the entree we had to order the cavatelli dish cooked with cabbage and sausage in a delectible sauce -to die for!!!!! Â For entree we ordered the branzino fish so perfectly prepared, the organic chicken with panko topped with arugula and papaya was incredible, the veal palliard was a pounded veal chop topped with mixed greens and cherry tomatoes, the pork osso buco was served over a bed of gnocchi. Â All of the sauces were very tasty and flavorful. The extensive wine list helped select the perfect wines to accompany the dishes. It was an hour ride to this restaurant but well worth it. I will revisit again and again and recommend this restaurant to all who are interested in eating perfectly prepared dishes. Bravo! Five stars!

Above average pizza. Fast delivery. It had fresh mozzarella, and thin crust. By the time, we remembered that we had ordered pizza, the handsome gentleman was ringing the doorbell. I really want to try dining there and see how the service is. Delivery and pizza are great though.
Had a great brunch here the other day. Great block. people watching and the men are great to look at. Thank God I moved downtown
Great restaurant. Polite staff. On top of things. Food came out quick. Went on a date with someone my age. Noticed that we were most definitely (by far) the youngest people there.
We had a wonderful meal at Riverpark. Fantastic food & service. Appreciated that the whole menu was available for Restaurant week.

I went to Champs about a week ago with my boyfriend, heard a lot about it and wanted to try it out. Very cute place, friendly an helpful staff. We ordered the cheese nachos as an appetizer and we chose from the build your own burgers part of the menu. For the patty me and my boyfriend both chose the bomber which was house made tempeh and seitan and for the additional fixins my boyfriend chose to make it a patty melt with grilled onions and cheese on sourdough and I chose tempeh bacon and cheddar mozzarella mix of cheese. My burger was very good, bread was soft and tasty pickles were amazing, my boyfriend who isn't vegan really enjoyed his burger as well. The only reason I'm not giving 5 stars was that the melted cheese on the nachos was very cold. Still want to try a lot of things here so I will definitely be going back!

If you're looking for tapas with a Mediterranean flare in the lower east side, then you should consider checking out this little jewel. Â Kudos to the folks who took the pictures of this restaurant. Â It's a cozy setup with one small bar in the back. Â Tables are lined up practically at the door so there's not much room to stand around and wait to be seated. If you're gonna go i would strongly recommend making a reservation and being on time for it. Â On a packed night the food didn't take too long to come out, once your order was finally taken that is. The presentation was IMHO artistic and the taste was evenly matched. Â The pricing for the type and portion size was justifiable.

The food here is almost always delicious. Â Their mussels are great! Â As is there lamb. Â The food might be a bit slow to come out, but I take that to mean it's being freshly prepared. Â Also, the place is usually really busy. Â The service is usually pretty good. Â Maybe a little understaffed at times. Â The chef is lovely and comes out to the dining room to check on people, which I love. Â They have an "early bird special" if you want to eat dinner at some really early hour. Â They are probably the only place in the neighborhood that serves brunch before 11 am, which is great.

Really solid addition to the neighborhood, the food is quite unique and very well executed. Made a reservation for a Thursday night dinner which was very easy through OpenTable. We were sat pretty quickly once we arrived. Server was very friendly and suggested a really nice Finger Lakes red wine that we loved. Decided to order the deviled eggs), Pig Out for 2 and the brussel sprouts as a side. I really enjoyed the eggs and the brussel sprouts. Both unique flavors, textures, etc. and really tasty. Loved how the egg whites of the deviled eggs were crusted in panko and fried. The pig out was good as well - pork was incredibly well cooked and super crispy on top and rich and tender on the bottom. The peanut noodles were just OK for me, I thought they were slathered in a bit too much sauce, but the first few bites were definitely tasty. Overall, definitely worth a try and looking forward to seeing how the menu evolves as well.

Service: We were seated at least 30 minutes after the estimated time. Even when they said our table was ready we waited 20 more minutes. Having had to wait so long I got thirsty and got a bubble tea. Instead of a welcome, the server instantly gave me attitude about having an outside drink and said they would charge me, then offered to keep it in their fridge. We then proceeded to watch the couple across from us and next to us get their food before us even though they ordered well after we did. We asked about the long delay and the server made up some BS excuse about the ramen cooking, even though everyone ordered ramen. Food: Once the food finally came it did not live up to the hype. The pork buns were smothered in mayonnaise, but would have been good otherwise. The ramen was very good, but did not have much pork in it. This was a complete disappointment - Xian Famous foods on Saint Mark's is a good alternative, cheaper, better and friendly service.

I'm afraid to write too effusive a review as it might not make it past the bullshit filter.In the ten years it's been open, Cafe Steinhof has become a neighborhood institution, I've been a loyal customer since shortly after it opened. The food is excellent, a mix of Austrian standards augmented by some very good seafood and pasta dishes. The ambiance is laid back, homey and arty. The music eclectic and appropriate to the hour. The things I like most about Cafe Steinhof is the staff and the bar crowd. All of the staff and the majority of patrons are interesting, intelligent and creative people involved in music, film, theater, visual arts, nary a bond trader or lawyer in the bunch.

Thank God for this place! When you want something tasty, quick, healthy and affordable in Greenwich/West Village, this is the place to go. Â My friends and I would order the falafel and take it to Washington Square Park (not really a good idea now) and devour it in a matter of minutes while people watching. Though I love anything spicy, the green falafel was most satisfying partly because of the mint taste. Â Complete with the special zing in the Israeli salad, you are in for a delicious, memorable treat. Â Larger than Mamoun's size and full of fresh ingredients, the $6 is worth every dime. Â  If you happen to be thirsty for something refreshing, try their ginger lemonade-- it's not too sweet, not too sour but just right.
Best pizza in city. Â The oldest pizzeria in the country. Â There is a reason they have lasted 110 years.

Favorite brunch place in the city. the ambiance there is great, food is delicious, sangrias are out of this world and last but not least the prices are great. What is more to say? Check it out for yourself!

Whoah, 5 star review. And honest to Allah, I don't even like lobster. I don't. Crab cakes, so good. Crispy oysters (ok you can't really mess them up, but yeaaah..) they were great. I took my famously picky, food-frustrating mother here, which is the truest test that most restaurants are not even ready for. And yes, she complained about the bun-bread. "Are you sure you can't dig up some ciabatta? I would LOVE that on a pita." No mom, sorry. All burger bun, all the time, everything. So she gets some fish sandwich, I don't remember and she likes it, she really does. And the fries are perfectly crispy and the cole slaw is of complementary seasoning, with not-too-much mayo. So I've dined-in here pretty often. Drank-in even more often (Shipyard Pumpkin all day). But I was only truly amazed when Lobster Joint really DELIVERED on a delivery order. It was the blackened Mahi sandwich, I remember it well. I remember ordering it later into the evening, second-guessing my choice of a fish fillet for delivery. Everything that can go wrong often does during a food delivery. But no. My sandwich arrived and it was the best fish sandwich I've ever had. The little cup of tartar was just enough. The fries, still crisp despite the commute. The Mahi melted into the burger bun when I bore down and it was everything. I'm still confused. It left me disoriented, as if a mere whisper of a dream, and I had to believe that the round tin and plastic (all that was left) was proof enough that it happened.
this is the montana of bars. Â the beers are reasonably priced. Â the food seemed a little on the expensive side but I did have pants with shallow pockets on.

Great lunch today at The Little Owl. Â The burger lived up to its reputation. Â The beignettes and molten chocolate cake are 100% worth the calories. Â Equally as good was our waiter....helpful, friendly and even brought out both desserts with candles to celebrate my nieces birthdays. Food was fantastic....I will definitely return!

I found these guys on accident when walking back to the Manhattan Club. I am usually leery of street meat as I have had 1 too many bad apples but it just smelled so good and I was so drunk and hankering for some grease and man this was love at first bite. They truly live up to their hype. These guys get you in and out (sometimes have to wait because there are that many people) and in and out again because you want to go back and try something else. I cant even begin with the sauces... They know they are masters with the sauce so they give you plenty knowing you will ask for more. The chicken is cooked so perfectly and the rice and ALL OF THE WHITE SAUCE is out of this world. I wish I was close enough to hit their carts up more but I try to make it a priority of hitting them up after a night of drinking.

This bar is Great!!! It has a great selection of wine and some very different beers. Â Heidi & Ed are great, they make you feel right at home and they are very funny & welcoming! Â I have tried almost everything on the menu and can't decide on what's my favorite because they're all great. Â I plan on going at least once a week and I don't think I can move out of the UES now because this local bar is such a perfect addition!

Though I don't know if this is the best brunch spot in Astoria, it was definitely tasty! I got the french toast panini, which had bananas in between two pieces of french toast, and it was DELICIOUS. Service was a little slow, but that was understandable as they were very busy, and our waitress was really nice! Food was fresh, and my other two friends enjoyed their options as well! I would definitely recommend this to someone looking for a solid brunch option.
Excellent food. Excellent service. Â Excellent atmosphere

Service was kind of lacking, in that our waitress had to ask what we ordered twice after we told her the first time (just the gumbo and chicken pot pie) and also forgot to bring the wine we ordered.She apologized and was saying how tired she was. We all have those days, but really, it's not an excuse. It's not that I don't care, but it's an excuse that is not really relevant. And if you want to provide good customer service, you figure out how to make up for it. Anyway, the food was good, not amazing. And don't come here for ambience.

What an amazing place. I had the omakase tasting at the bar and it was pretty amazing. I had a standard sashimi salad, delicious grilled vegetables consisting of eggplant, shisito peppers and mushrooms, snapper, a array of meats, snow crab dumplings , king prawn and the mochi dessert. I really enjoyed the grilled veggies and chicken meatball. Everything is flavored just right so that you can actually taste the veggies and the fish/meat instead of all the over seasoned food elsewhere. Â I think this place really proves that quality meats and veggies should taste amazing with just a pinch of sea salt. As for the atmosphere, it's really fun watching the chefs in front of you crawling around the bar area for fresh fish and veggies and masterfully cooking and slicing things up. It's an very interesting dinner atmosphere. Overall, I'm glad I found another amazing place to add to my favorites

My husband and I went to Carmine's after seeing a Broadway show. Â The wait was 1 to 1 1/2 hours so we went to the bar to grab a drink. Â While sitting there, our bartender suggested we order at the bar and eliminate the wait. Sure, we've done that before and I was hungry. The bartender knew we'd never been there before but still allowed us to order 2 entrees (serving 3-4 people each) for just the 2 of us!! Â It would have been appreciated if he had told us that everything was served family style! Â He topped off my wine glass a few times because he knew we were pissed! My hubby even put him on the spot and said, "thanks buddy" to which the bartender seemed to get satisfaction. When he brought over a huge dessert (that was actually for another group) as a joke we decided right then..no tip for you! Not one cent and I didn't feel the least bit guilty. Â This guy was a jerk! Don't go to Carmine's unless you want to be made to feel stupid. Â Needless to say, we will not go back. Â The penne vodka pasta was horrible too. Run away from this over-hyped, busy, loud place to somewhere that appreciates their customers. The guy at the door was rude when we walked in. Â That should have been our first clue to leave.

Really really tasty. The staff are ALL very friendly and helpful... Just nice normal folks who give me faith that not all customer service in this city has to be terrible. Â The Israeli breakfast sandwich was amazing and the kale salad too. My husband had the kabob pita... Also SOOO good. I'll be back.

Momofuk-me... this place was gooood. The raw bar is a raw-esome place to start: from the refreshing oysters to the light, tender cobia, to the other-worldly diced scallops. Incredibly flavorful and served in a light, chilled broth (think ceviche-style, but without the acidity), it was probably the best scallop dish I've ever had. This diver scallop walloped Morimoto's similar dish. Â And, although I don't eat much pork (minus the weekly Bloody Mary accompaniment), nor do I have nor eat buns, I went for their most popular dish. And it was bun-believeable. Little did I know the best was yet to come: the chawanmushi with truffle, apple, and quail egg, the chef's special of the night. I get all mushi inside just thinking of this bowl of wonder. Worth the $20+ surcharge, sir. Yep, I'm putting this dish in my top 5. Of all time. Our knowledgeable, super laid-back server recommend the quail entree, which was assembled so artfully, it resembled a forest of sorts, with trees of radish, fig stones, and trails of squid ink. Not even remotely a filling entree as the quail consisted of just four small wing-like pieces, but beautiful and unique. Tasty, but I wanted mo', Momofuku! The only forgettable dish would be the jar of spicy kimchi. Good, but nothing special. Although I basically eat the salt rings of margarita glasses and drink pickle juice like water, I actually found this side to be a bit too salty. Then again, I couldn't see straight after the chawanmushi, so I didn't care. No wait at 10 p.m. on a Tuesday night, so check it out at off-hours, and sit at the bar to watch the extremely chill staff do their thang. I want ssam more of this place.
awesome owners, amazing food, great vibe, just come

Upon arrival, the chef greeted me through the curtain while he was cooking. Â I stood in the dining area waiting for the host to seat me. Â When I asked the chef if I could just grab a table he gave me a hasty 'yeah sure' response. Â In a 'I should've known better than to ask him' sorta way. Â The owner/host Fidel came to me after about 5 minutes to hand me the menu. Â I did enjoy my salad and the key lime pie is delicious (although a bit on the small side). Â Kinda weird that customers have to walk through the kitchen to get to the bathroom though. Â I did get a warm goodbye by both Fidel and the chef. Â  Will probably give this place another shot in the near future.

Large portions, cheap pricing, legitly delicious italian food. CASH only! Get the bolognese pasta and also the Tagliolini ai Frutti di Mare. My BF thought this was the best pasta he'd ever had. Come early - preferably before 6:30pm latest. I came once around 8:30, and there was at least an hour wait. I didn't have to wait at all coming in at 6pm. P.S.Your business will be the ppl next to you's business because this place is tiny and tables are just about 3 inches apart from each other.

Food was great. I had the Proper Burger. Meat was terrific. well prepared. Apps were on par for a typical sports bar. Truffle Parm fries were the best. HOWEVER the service was terrible. Atrocious. Â Granted we were there during the ranger game with 7 people but the place was half empty by the time we ordered. Very long wait for every drink order and the food came out on plate at a time so we weren't able to all eat together without peoples food getting cold. We had to continually ask if the rest of our order was coming. One top of it the manger- or at least the gentleman who looked/ acted like the manger- Â sat down with a couple females friends after we were seated and ate dinner with them. They got served immediately while we waited. Probably will not return other than drinks and a burger at the bar.
Another great find, gotta love when Yelp is right. Â Walked in, super nice and handed us the Happy Hour menu!! Â Prefect!!

Settled in a blustery weekday night to meet a very nice Yelper for dinner. Surprisingly, a bit empty inside - but it was a bit early in the night. The decor was quite cozy and inviting like a nicely remodeled basement feel with soft candles dotting the tables. No Pinot Grigio! That worked out just fine though, because I got a great recommendation from the server on Gruner Veitlinger from Australia. Delicious, light, and mild which turned out to be a nice complement. I may have just discovered my Pinot's successor. We had the sashito peppers for an appetizer which were served with a light lemon aioli that had a light custardy texture. We both selected the classic ramen for an appetizer that had a light broth with pork, scallion, and ginger. All in all, a fine selection for this chilly evening. Menu was quite large and had a vast array of sushi, ramen, and steamed buns which sounded oh-so-delicious. Use your Yelp app for a free Asahi draft beer!

KenScale: 8.0/10 Totto Ramen is a ramen shop in Hell's Kitchen that has been beloved by New Yorkers for a long time. It is constantly bombarded by a long line of crowds looking to get a taste of ramen here. I had tried numerous times before to get a table here (the restaurant doesn't take reservations, but more on that below) only to go somewhere else due to the insane wait time. I finally made the time (and determination) for an hour long wait on a weekend lunch time. The menu is simple, with about five ramen selections and a couple of side dishes available. I went with the "extra spicy" ramen with pork. The bowl comes with a side of chili paste that you can add to give that extra spicy kick to the broth. Oftentimes, Totto has been compared to Ippudo, another longstanding ramen institution in the city. I think the texture of the noodle is definitely better at Totto (not too firm or soft), but the flavor of the broth is more or less a tie between the two. Boiled egg that I added as a topping gave an extra dimension to the flavor. Anyways, the ramen was definitely a winner, more so on a cold winter afternoon. As I already mentioned, the restaurant doesn't take reservations. The way to grab a table is to show up early before the shop opens to be seated right away (either before noon during lunch time or 5 p.m. during dinner time), show up at odd hours like 3-4 p.m. or write your name down and pray that the wait is not too long (it can run as long as a couple of hours). The space is tiny and has that vibe of a shop hidden on the backstreet in Japan. The restaurant takes cash only so be prepared to bring some. While I wouldn't call Totto's ramen the best (I still think the Benkei ramen shop at the Ushiwakamaru space has slightly better flavor), I do think the hype is justified and it's a worthwhile place to visit.

A half rotisserie chicken, a cup of black beans, large plate of rice and a plate of sweet OR crispy plantains ALL for only $8. Mama Adela cooks your feast herself while her grown son sits with some other locals in the 6 table restaurant and yells, "mama" in his Spanish accent to her every few minutes for whatever reason. There is a small TV tucked in the upper back corner of the restaurant with foreign soaps on all day. The wait staff is delightful and the atmosphere is funky, friendly and homey. My god, it is brilliant.

Meh-riam. Â Sorry, I had to do it. The reviews prove my theory that there is serious Yelp star inflation in Park Slope. Â If you take off one star, you get what the place would actually earn in a comparable neighborhood. Shakshouka eggs--the sauce was thin and runny and basically tasted like tomato and onion--nothing interesting. Â The hummus was very chunky--there is way better hummus in Brooklyn. Â The pita was the biggest disappointment--did not taste fresh. It wasn't bad, middle of the road, but seriously overpriced for food that was basically marginally better than a good diner. Â The fries were the most memorable part of the meal. Â Service was good. Â  I'll stick with Atlantic Av for good quick Middle Eastern and Tanoreen for the best Middle Eastern food in Brooklyn.

Carroll Gardens is known for many restaurants but Frankie's is one of the best. Great place for all group sizes and they have a private party space. The beet and avocado appetizer is delicious and every item on their menu is too. Recommendations: gnocchi and cavatelli with hot sausage

Sripraphai is where to go when you want a nice, sit-down authentically Thai meal. The flavors are pretty darn spot on. Similar to my review on I Am Thai, this place trumps all the pathetic Manhattan Thai restaurants by leaps and bounds. This is a reason to get yourself or your friends into Queens. Seriously, it's a straight shot on the 7 train, Woodside is not another planet. Advice: Get there early (before 7pm) or be prepared to wait upwards of an hour or more. It's popular with families. It's popular with everyone who knows anything about good Thai food. Plan accordingly. There is outdoor seating in the back, if you enjoy flowers and fresh air. Note to those hip to Thai: They don't dumb down the fish sauce amounts to American palates, so the food is heavenly!!
Did this place shutter? I tried to come last thursday for lunch, and the menu was gone and replaced with the japanese place next door. If not, they need to update their hours.

I've only ever come here for pies and their ice cream--my birthday tradition--and have yet to stray; I've found no reason to yet. Current line up: Local Apple, Michigan Sour Cherry, Florida Key Lime, Organic Peanut Butter Chocolate, Banoffe, and their special is a Chocolate Pudding Meringue Pie.

A clean, well lit place. A spot for sipping Stumptown and enjoying soft-boiled eggs and writing letters to friends. The staff here are some of the best I've ever had serve me. Its hard to express just how pleasant things are at Iris. From the food (Sandwiches, Salads, Soups, Baguettes & Butter all made with attention and aplomb) to the coffee drinks that always seem to be the perfect temperature. It gets crowded on the weekend brunch times. But thats alright. Awesome things are often popular.

I threw my sister-in-law's baby shower in the outdoor area of this restaurant. It had little rocks on the floor (so ladies opt for the flats/sandals). Some of the tables had umbrellas over the table, which came in handy as it was a sunny day. The food was good and the prices were very reasonable. We had chicken satay, pork spare ribs, spicy pork salad and calamari to start. I don't eat calamari, but I heard from guests and mother-to-be that it was delicious. For the entrees, we ordered chicken pad thai, garlic chicken, fried rice, a shrimp dish and a beef dish. My favorites were the garlic chicken because I liked the sauce and the chicken pad thai. The portions are a nice size too. You will not be disappointed if you eat here; obviously I wasn't ;)

Five stars for food. Four stars for service. Decor and ambiance were somewhere between three and four stars. I can't speak for the landlubbing-variety proteins, but the fish dishes were fantastic. I had perfectly cooked halibut and my wife had the tilefish, which she claimed tasted like "a giant, delicious fish stick." Nice flavor combinations in the accompaniments to the fish too: things like artichokes, black trumpet mushrooms, pistachios, farro & english peas. Do yourself a favor and try the dark chocolate souffle, which you need to order at the start of your meal. It comes with a little pitcher of coffee sauce to pour into the center and is a fitting finish to a great meal.

This place is great for Brunch!! Its pretty spacious inside. You can either sit in the front at the bar area or you can have a seat in the back at a private table. The food is extremely fresh. The service we had was great the waitress was very friendly. I had the smoked ham, cheese and egg sandwich on a bun with potatoes. The food was excellent. Im not sure what type of bun it was but it was really delicious. I would highly suggest this dish and this place Â if your going for brunch!
Great viet sandwiches! except sometimes the bread can be a bit too hard.

This place was on my list of places to eat for a while now, based on stellar reviews, it making nearly every "where to eat NYC brunch" list and the recommendations of friends. Sadly, the first time I went was New Year's day and I don't think my stomach was prepared for the reality-check it got. I had the Benedict Johnny, which was a seriously delicious Benedict. The corn pancake was fantastic and when it's drenched in that egg, you've got yum. The chicken sausage was good too but I needed a knife to cut it, so it kinda messed with the flow of forking on through the egg to the pancake, but it was worth it. A few notes. Like I said, it was New Year's day, and I managed to get there by 3pm. It was still an hour wait which felt crazy, but from what I understand it's par for the course there, and I'm gonna assume that the normal brunch rush was delayed a few hours on account of heavy celebrating the night before. The atmoshpere was... confusing. It was more loung-y than quaint and cozy. I'd say the music was the only really cool part about it but it didn't seem to match the decor. Of all the amazingly styled placed in NY, the Jane was not noteworthy. The food was great for the price and I'd really like to go back. I'd probably make a reservation though first. PS everyone raves about the french toast, but it was sold out when I was there, so just be prepared for that possibility.

A jack of all trades, a master of none. Which is why I am glad Pomme Frites found their calling. One fry, 50 different sauces. Tried the truffle mayo...so good. Took the fries for a walk around St. Marks for a more enjoyable experience.

A great place for a romantic dinner. Ask to be seated on the patio, even if it's winter as they keep it warm. The specials are always great, the fish and veggies fresh and the pasta is home made. I always pick the food then have the Sommelier pick the wine.

Went for lunch during Restaurant Week promotion. Not pretentious or snobby. Very cozy room and unlike some posts, we had prompt and great service. The food was delicious. Yes, maybe a bit on the salty side, Â but still delicious. The artichokes, tripe, cavatelli, and malafatti, were wonderful. Very good panna cotta and olive oil cake. Desserts didn't blow me away as much as the meal did. It's nice that they have $6.00 wines for lunch. Bread by Sullivan Bakery was wonderful.
Authentic, amazingly delicious nterior Mexican food. Chic simple decor, lovely laid back folk... Such a treat!

For me this is worth the schlep to the UES. I fell in love with Laduree on a trip to Paris 2 years ago so I'm thrilled to have one in the states. Even though the macaroon trend is big here now, Laduree is still the best. They have perfect shape, texture, and flavors. They are so worth the $3 price tag. The only disappointment is walking out of the store and not being in France.

I have never had empanada's before and this place has definitely given me a great first impression! First of all, you MUST get the guacamole and plantain chips. So goood!!! I tried the ground beef empanada and viagra empanada. Both were delicious. The ground beef tasted almost like a fried tamale (crispy corn skin, yum!). The viagra (seafood combo) was very unique but still very good! Didn't have a chance to try the dessert empanadas but if I ever get the chance to go again I would definitely give it a try! :) One downside..It took a while for our empanadas to arrive. We got served our guacamole and plantain chips right away. But we still had to wait probably around 15 minutes after we had finished devouring the chips. Might be due to the fact that it was pretty busy when we were there. But I'd still go again!
I don't care for street food too much, but the line is worth it! Defintiely make it there if you're in NYC!

The Pizza Funghi I had for dinner last night (and am eating now as I type) was the best white pizza I've ever had. I'm in love. Â My gumbo was also delicious, however the fried green tomatoes are better at Dinosaur BBQ ( I'm no expert on southern cuisine, but these were not worth the extra bit of effort I feel like I have to put in at the gym when I order something with fried in the name). Last night was my first time at the Green Table but it won't be my last.

Came by for dinner last night around 7:30. First thing I noticed was the decor. The main door is a cool wooden door that makes you feel like you are entering a home rather than a restaurant. After you walk in, you see Â a giant chandelier in a glass case in the middle of the place. The decor makes me feel like i'm going for afternoon tea rather than thai dinner. So yea, the decor is excellent. Food- had the tom yum soup- extremely salty. Also, I had the pad kee mao (drunken noodles). it was described as a spicy dish but I didn't taste any spice?? It was tasty nonetheless. However, it was also very salty. Â I got home and chugged two bottles of water. Prices are reasonable though. two people came out to $30 including tax.

I wanted to go to this restaurant last year for my birthday but couldn't wait the hour during the brunch to dinner switch so I decided to try again for brunch over the weekend. I'm happy I didn't end up there on my birthday because my group was way too big and the space, which is pretty small. The brunch menu was good, offering a variety of dishes. The waitress seemed pretty knowledgeable with her recommendations as that was my first time there. I can't say I would return for brunch, not because my food was bad, but I wasn't impressed. I may return for dinner, but it wouldn't be my first choice.

Been wanting to try this place for a while. I've heard a lot of good things of this place. It was my bday and my friend had suggested we go here. We had ordered about 2 appetizers and each an appetizer. We also got 2 glasses of wine that we asked for recommendations on. Mine was spot on, but my friend found hers to be too sour. Surprisingly enough they actually changed it for her, which was super nice. You get an endless bag of bread to eat with your meal. I had gotten the duck and my friend got the porkchop. Both really good. Overall, really good meal. Downside is that we ended up spending a lot.

I absolutely LOVE Calle Ocho. Â I've never been disappointed. Â I haven't had their brunch but their dinners are all right with me. Â Granted, I tend to get same things - bacon wrapped dates (I Â love anything that starts and ends with some kind of pork product) and the Ropa Veja; but on occasional Monday night, I get a chance to try some of the other apps they have on the menu, and everything is delicious. Â  I might get blasted for this, but their sangria, to me, is just okay...I've definitely have had better. Â If I'm Â there on a Sunday night, I'll drink it 'cause it's free but I much prefer their mojitos.

Trendy spot for brunch. We skipped the wait and got seated immediately at the bar. Tried the Andrey's Egg Sandwich since i heard the croissant was made in house, and bf got the eggs any style. Food was mediocre. Noise level was ridiculous. Probably won't return.

Seriously NYC, what's up with the ridiculous lines at Shake Shack? Â I'm as big of a burger fan as any, and while I find Shake Shack to be pretty tasty, it is, by far, not the best I've had, and certainly not worth a 45 minute wait in line. Truth be told, I wish i could give Shake Shack 3.5 stars. Â The burgers are generally tasty, the fries decent, and the shakes very good. Â But, the lines don't justify the taste. I would gladly eat Shake Shack, so don't discourage anyone to go and try it. Â I'll assure you there is better in the city though.

This is one of the best brunch spots I have discovered in NYC. Outdoor seating is great in the warmer months. The food is delicious, I have never had a bad meal. And what's better than a walk up Stumptown coffee window when you just need a little pick-me-up.

Fiiiiinnally found my way over to Brooklyn Crab, and I've gotta say, judging by the reviews, I wasn't expecting anything great. Â However, I was pleasantly surprised. Â The food was really good! My party ordered a seafood platter, crab roll, clam chowder, crab legs, pulled chicken sandwich, mac & cheese, and everything I sampled was pretty tasty. Â When we were done eating, we went downstairs to play air hockey and corn hole, then hung out and sat by a few heaters (which were plentiful in numbers). My party of 6 took a cab there since it's not very accessible by mass transit, but didn't there used to be a bus that did a pick up from Atlantic Avenue? Â Is that not the case anymore?
ok i visited this \plc and of course the service was great and cool attitude im going back for sure!!!!!!

I found a new spot in Long Island City to hang out with some friends after work. Great friendly staff and decor. I found Open Door to be very social and just a great place to enjoy a meal and drinks. Highly recommended!

I recently ate here over the weekend when walking through the essex street market -- these tacos were simply amazing. Â Everything was SO fresh and full of flavor. Â My favorite was the chipoltle chicken taco, but my boyfriend's favorite was the brisket taco -- either way you CAN'T go wrong. Â And if you're a vegetarian, the guaco taco is delicious. Â We literally ordered one of everything -- you can't beat the taste or the prices. Â Can't wait to go back!! Â Also super cool, friendly staff!
I had the pork belly sandwich. Tasty, Â but very messy. Take a big stack of napkins or wipes.

I just moved to bay ridge and was elated to find this bar is a walk away. A bar for the beer and hot dog connoisseur, this place goes through single kegs of delicious micro brews from all over the state and country in days, and you get to go on that journey with them. Helping you along the way are delicious customizable hot dogs! My favorite is the Bridgeview: Bacon wrapped deep fried hot dog with red onion sauce - sound good? Want to add chill, caramelized onions, peppers and siracha aioli? MmmmmmmmmmmMMMMMM WHY ARENT YOU HERE YET!?

Walls covered with a bunch of different ramen bowls? Well... helloooo heaven! If I had to choose something to eat before I died, Ippudo's Modern Ramen would be a contender. This place has been raved to be the "best ramen in NYC" and I think it may be true! Love: *the huge ladle *fatty yet light broth - it's not heavy, so I drank every drop! *fresh hand-made ramen noodles made on site! *pork buns *great wait staff The wait was so long - we probably waited about 45 minutes even though we got there around 9pm! However, the wait is well worth it. We ordered the pork buns to start as an appetizer and according to one of my friends' cousin was "the best thing I ever ate in my life". That says something right there. After quickly devouring our pork buns, our ramen found their way to our table! Like I said above, I ordered the Akamaru Modern Ramen which had a nice strong garlic flavor. $14 for the Akamaru, but totally worth it. This is a "must eat" whenever I have the chance to go to NY again!

Amazing sandwiches. The pulled pork and coconut shrimp were by far my favorite. Ask for extra mayo because its so yummy. Giving it 4 stars instead of 5 because the blood orange lemonade was WAY too tart, as in hard to drink and had to add water tart. They need to add a little sugar to it and it would be a lot better. Cash only and it's great to either dine in (not a ton of room upstairs) or carry out. Staff is very friendly too.
Wonderful experience at Bogota this past Saturday. Delicious food and great margaritas. Will def be back soon!

When you were like, 8 years old, did you ever say to yourself "Ew grooooss sushi? I don't wanna eat sushi!" Well, if the answer is yes, you should buy a used time machine off craigslist, hop in, dial it back to when you were a kid and PUNCH YOUR 8 YEAR OLD SELF IN THE FACE! JUST PUNCH YOURSELF RIGHT IN THE FREAKING FACE! Because your stupid 8 year old self was too dumb to predict eating at Sushi Yasuda. It is perfect ok!? Sushi Yasuda is perfect. I had no idea fish could literally melt in your mouth. Not figuratively...li-ter-all-yyyyy melt. in. your. mouth. Now spit on your 8 year old self for good measure, just cause you were an absolute IDIOT. Then fly back here in that beat up time machine, sell it to someone else on Craigslist who needs to teach there 8 year old self a valuable lesson, and go immediately to Yasuda. You'll thank me.

I would have never gone into this place without my co-worker's glowing recommendation. It has a small shabby looking storefront sandwiched between a larger restaurant and a supermarket. I entered at 3PM, well past lunch time and noticed that the place was still crowded. I ordered the Roti Canai and the Beef Rendang over rice. The sauces were more flavorful compared to the other Malaysian restaurants I've frequented. Also, the food was relatively inexpensive and the portions were more than suitable for a lunch-time meal. I left a little bit too full but glad that I had taken a chance on the place. I would've given this place five-stars if it looked a little bit cleaner.

I am on the search for NY's best Benedict. Jane ranks among the elite in a city flooded by these delicious brunch delecacies.... I ordered the Benedict Johnny which includes hollandaise, eggs, sausage, all ontop of a buttermilk biscuit. Living in the south most of my life, you really come to appreciate bruncheries offering the so
This is a great new place to have in the L.E.S. The food is original and very reasonably priced. I'm starting to become a regular there.

I really liked the Odeon. I went for Sunday brunch and it was relatively empty, we opted to have a drink at the bar so we could wait for a table outside, but otherwise would have been seated right away. They do make a really great Bloody Mary, my brunch drink of choice. We didn't have long to wait long before we were taken to our table. The hostesses were super friendly, as was the waitress. I had the french toast, and I was so content. It wasn't too heavy, nor was it too soft and light, it was literally perfect. The whole meal was perfect in, in fact. The only reason I am one star short of a full house is because the bar bill was obscenely expensive. I don't know if it was a mistake that I didn't realize until later or what, but it was highway robbery. We had 4 drinks in total and it was in the neighborhood of $67. This is your fair warning. The meal itself was totally reasonably priced, which is why I was so surprised about our bar bill. Just double check it before you leave!
Worth the trip. Plates are smaller, but priced accordingly. Beers on tap are awesome. Service was exceptional. I'll definitely be coming back to this place whenever I'm in LIC.

Started to coming to Los Tacos last summer, not long after it opened. It is so delicious. I come here at least once a week now. Everything is so fresh, ingredients aren't too complicated so you can really taste everything. The corn tortillas are freshly made and delicious. I like to stick with the chicken quesadilla on corn. Many topping choices to choose from, but don't go overboard, let the meat and tortillas shine! Tip: be sure to assert yourself when you hand the taco maker your receipt. if you just stand there, you won't get your tacos.
I went here on a busy Tuesday afternoon and enjoyed their buffet style set up. They had a thorough selection of korean food to enjoy but it is actually expensive when they weigh it.

We found this place on a whim after seeing the rockettes. So yummy! Two slices is certainly filling. The crust is so thin and crispy and the sauce is yummy. Great toppings, we tried the lasgna, chicken, margarhite, vege, broccoli and riccotta bw the three of us. Â Its not a sit down place, just a little counter.

I've only had brunch here, but the food I've tried is excellent. The Benedict has real Hollandaise-- not that packaged glop lots of places love to use. Their potatoes are crispy with the taste of fresh Rosemary, and the apple omelet is a great mix of apples and thick bacon.
