I can understand how people can say the service is a bit inattentive, but if you've been to any good brunch place in the area on a nice day, good luck getting waited on hand and foot. The servers here are at least nice to you, unlike some places in the East Village I've been. Â Just chill out, have a couple of drinks and you'll be even more stoked when you get your food.

I mean, it's not like I can say anything different. I think over 2000 reviews speaks for itself right? Basically, I'm a ramen newbie. YEAH I KNOW. So, out of the very few places I've had ramen, this was probably one of the best. So, yeah, good job Ippudo!

The Pizza here is something that helps put NY pizza on the map. The perfect thin crust, the not too dark flavored cheese, and the awesome brooklyn soda. The best thing I ordered was the Canoli. It was handmade and tasted like one of the best things in the world. I have not had Canoli this good. I'll come back one day!
Came here for a birthday dinner tonight. Great service (Sarah), great food. I had the salmon but tasted the pork chop and the Mac and cheese - all very tasty! Will DEFINITELY be back.

Very small portions, cooked extremely well, but on the pricey side. Had the Mahi Mahi & the ox tail; both were delicious. Except it was pretty expensive & portions were a bit small. Also something that bothered me: Menus outside (Takeout menu) prices are not the same prices they charge in the restaurant.

Listen man. Why is this bahn mi joint different from others? YOU CAN ADD AN EGG. Â I LOVE EGGS. You gotta pay extra for it though... w/e eggs are delicious! It's pricier than other bahn mi''s around the neighborhood (even when you don't get the egg) but it's really good. lol. I get the egg runny so I get some more moisture on the bread, not that it's too dry or anything but it's bahn mi.. the bread is supposed to be like that. The classic one is delicious. I've been here three times. I've Â gotten classic twice and I would recommended. I forgot what I got the other time.. so probably wasn't worth mentioning. Yay. Not 5-stars because I thought this was the best... until I had a REALLLLY delicious one in brooklyn.

More like 3.5 stars but I'm bumping up due to the quality of service. Totally unplanned trip here, after Palm Tribeca on West Street had an hour wait AND feeble air conditioning on a warm August night. Â In desperation we tried to think of area restaurants where we could sit and eat like adults (ie cloth on the table, no bars) - Capital Grille was too far a walk, Spouse eats at BLT for lunch too regularly for that to be a treat. Â Hey, how about the Danny Meyer place we've never tried? We were able to walk in and be seated immediately at 7pm, and although the restaurant got busier as the evening progressed, they were never full. Â Spouse enjoyed one of the four beers on tap and I had an excellent tamarind margarita, maybe the first margarita I've ever had that held its tang and sweetness as the ice melted. For appetizers I had a really interesting "salad" (roast vegetable dish) of smoky grilled eggplant, walnuts and some kind of microgreen with a nectarine broth. Â Our server mentioned the wood-grilled items on the menu in his handing-out-the-menus spiel but I wasn't expecting the depth of smokiness in the food - really nice. Â Spouse had the lobster egg custard, almost mousse-like but with a strong fish-y component and the addition of highly-flavored bonito flakes atop. Â He loved it. Entree was a letdown - we split the whole roasted turbot for two, and although the server said we might have a scale or two on the skin, I had a lot more than that. Â The skin was supposed to be edible, but it was dark gray and flabby, not crisped at all on the grill, and I left it in a heap on my plate. Â The three-spiced fries were very flavorful but were lukewarm, and the cooked mixed greens from the restaurant's rooftop garden were undercooked and bitter. So why four stars? Â Our waiter was friendly and knowledgeable; the sommelier was spot-on with wine recommendations; and the room is cool and civilized and an oasis on a summer evening; apps were excellent; and that tamarind margarita.... Â Let me add about the sommelier, I was very impressed that (1) she didn't push us to order a bottle of wine even though we were sharing an entree, (2) she talked eagerly about wines by the glass, and (3) she spoke to me, female at the table, first and at length about my options before turning her attention to Spouse. Â I'm so used to the sommelier making eye contact and addressing his talk to Spouse, it was refreshing to have someone deal fully with me instead of having my opinions/tastes be secondary. We'll be back, soon.

I really wanted to like this place. Went here on the recommendation of a friend who lives in the area. The place looked nice enough, but the tables had a weird shape--very long and skinny--so if you turned them one way, there's about four feet of space between you and the person sitting across, but the other way and they're only a foot and a half away from you. The Â music was a little too loud and hard to have a conversation. The server who came to take our order was friendly and seemed to be knowledgeable about their beer selections. We ordered the short rib kimchi empanadas and the grilled sausage platter for appetizers, a steak sandwich and the Big Pig sandwich for entrees. Our drinks came out pretty quickly but we were waiting for our food. And waiting. And waiting. Our food comes out, but all at the same time. Sorry, but appetizers are called that for a reason. I make the decision to eat the empanadas while they're still warm and hope my sandwich won't get too cold. Husband decides to just start on his steak sandwich right away and we would take the sausage platter to go. I guess we didn't look too happy because another person (I assume he was the manager or the owner) came over and asked how everything was going. Husband explained that we had wanted the appetizers to come out first, but maybe he didn't communicate that well enough. He clarified to the manager that he wasn't trying to get anyone in trouble, just giving feedback. The manager said he would comp the sausage platter, which we told him wasn't necessary. The empanadas are very bland. I thought it would have some spice because of the kimchi, but there's nothing. There's a little bit of kick from the siracha mayo that was drizzled on top, but one empanada was lying on top of the other, so that one got most of the dressing. The Big Pig had a weird sour taste to it. I realized it was the cole slaw in the sandwich...the shredded cabbage had some kind of vinegar in it. Husband said his steak sandwich tasted sour too. Once he took the lettuce leaf out, it wasn't as bad, but the sour taste was already absorbed by the meat. I tried a piece from the sausage platter and it had a strange sweet/salty taste to it. I ended up spitting it out. When we got the bill, the manager had comped the sausage plate after all. Five stars for service, zero stars for food.

Came here with friends during the labor day weekend so we lucked out by having plenty of space and no wait time. The food was perfect. I've never had filipino cuisine before, and this was an incredible introduction. Everything was delicious. Everything on the menu sounded amazing. I forget the name, but we had the traditional pork hash (recommended by the bartender) for the appetizer which was perfect. I had the crispy fish and rice dish which had the most incredible flavors. Friendly staff more than willing to answer my questions and quick service. Can't wait to go back!

twas quite all right... the eel bowl was very good. the ramen was good. got the thick noodles. was happy about that. it wasn't as creamy/oily/salty as the other japanese places i've been. although, i kinda felt weird about paying so much for ramen when i could just be satisfied with an ichiban at home.... (-2 stars for the prices) seemed a little too nice and clean.. and "posh" in there... i like my food dirty and made at places with holes in the wall.... enjoyed it.. but i wouldn't go home raving about this place like mad...
Super Cheap. Super Tasty. Super Messy - get some extra napkins. awesome.

First time not the last time! We had the fava bean soup,chicken honey and prunes and the lamb couscous all excellent fresh and flavorful . It's like eating home cooking. the chef is the owner and tends to it as you are guests in his home. Sue is helpful and friendly. The place is SMALL so reservations are a must to be safe.

I'm not a sweet brunch type of person, but their banana french toast has to be the best I've had. The crust was nice and crunchy and the bread almost melts in your mouth. The banana syrup was not too sweet and the cream they had was the perfect amount of sweetness and complementary to the whole dish. The basque scramble was also very good. The egg was light and fluffy, the sauces were tasty and the chorizo went nicely with everything. The salmon eggs benedict was just okay. Could barely taste the hollandaise sauce and overall the dish was just average. There wasn't enough salmon for the bread either. It was an almost bland dish.

Dear lord, I'm back in the homeland. I grew up in china, and this place brought me back!! I ordered in Chinese, and the nice people there were forgiving and pretended to understand my broken chingrish. Got the fried pork and chive dumplings (#17), pork and chive boiled dumpling soup (#19), and scallion pancakes. First, this food was practically free, so I tipped the jar like 80%. The food was amazing. Fried dumplings are the way to go; fat and juicy. Eat it with black vinegar to show your Asian prowlness. Boiled soup was perfect to wash down the 5 dumplings I had stuck in the gullet. And the scallion pancake was the size of a NY slice of pizza. Dear lord, I would live in that hot closet of a restaurant space for eternal dumplings and pancake. Why do I live in MI..????? Go. Don't be put off by the authentic vibe; they take orders in english, and I saw lots of Americans come by!

I had high hopes for The Otherroom....and while it was a cool, intimate place to grab a few drinks I was not highly impressed. I came around 11pm with a friend, and was lucky to grab a seat by the bar (chairs in the lounge were packed as expected). Â The bartender was polite, but definitely under-filled our wine glasses-and at $10 a pop I was a little perturbed. Â The music was also a little too loud for a bar/lounge that is conducive to primarily drinking and talking. Â  While the wine and company was good, I'm sure nyc has better options with a similar ambiance and cheaper drinks. Â  I may try "The Room" to see if that's any better. Â Wouldn't necessarily rush back to this place.
Dug the turkey meatloaf with butternut squash and green veggies. Sauce had some nice heat to it. Chefs were great! #paleo #nyc

is it the nicest place in the area? No. Do you mind eating in a small plate with cafeteria like fork and knive? Go somewhere else if you're looking for fancy. Now, the service is way above average, nice and friendly. And you go there for the food: The pulled pork is to die for, looking at the other tables around made me think that i was not the only one really enjoying. You feel the love it took to prepare this food, you figure out the time it marinated and the ingredients that have been added to make it some unique. And then, you get the bill and think: what a treat! I m going back there, ASAP. Next time, i will bring my bicycle in order to drive over the Williamsburg bridge which is right behind, a simple double whammy. Tip: The back room is more quiet, if you get lucky.

Lucky me, it was spring and I was out in the west village with 4 girls. I love New York! There were so may to choose from, risottos that is. I chose from the creamy section and I had a craving for Shrimp and there was Spinach. This place was worth the wait and the walk. Our waiter was the best small restaurant waiter that I have had in such a long time. In fact ever. Rock on Man. He recommended some great food, beer to go with to encourage the girls to be happier with the food. I was at a table of designers and we were all confused by the strange wall prints but we were delighted with spicy olives, a great big salad we all shared. I can't say I loved my main dish but that was because I do not like parsley much. I didn't think it went well in my creamy risotto. Its a place I'd walk to, wait at and eat in again. Thanks for the take away desserts. I asked for a business card so i can go back but they don't have cards, instead I was give a pen with the following imprint Stolen from : RISOTTERIA - NYC 212.924.6664. I wanted to use it to write this review.
I wend back for the Artichoke slice...I was craving it. It is distinct and actually really delicious. This time I ordered it just warm....much better.

was in the mood for some Italian, so my cousin and I went to Carmine's. Â We sat at the bar. Â We didn't know it was family style but the bartender explained before we ordered. Â Well we couldn't get no pasta, the dishes are huge (feed at least 5-6 ppl) so we ordered 2-different sandwiches, a Sausage w/onions & peppers and a grilled chicken w/fried eggplant, when the sandwiches came they were both Humongous with humongous cesar salads. Â Everything was excellent, but we both ate 1/2 of each sandwich...its excellent for a group of at least 4.

My partner and I just finished eating here with a friend. We were greeted by a very nice gentleman. After being seated our server was really nice. She was younger and Â not attentive... The pizza made up for her lack of experience. It's on the expensive side, so be prepared! Overall experience was great!

A traditional Mediterranean restaurant. Â They had a salad assortment platter which was very good, it came with a fluffy pita bread. Â We then shared a Doner platter, like a gyro but open faced....good portion and very tasty. Â  Definitely worth a visit. Â Very reasonable prices as well.
Fantastic pizza (probably one of the best I've ever had), above-and-beyond very friendly wait staff, 10 minute wait, sample of beer instead of description when we asked, and relatively well-priced.

This place is epic, just be sure to place your delivery order an hour or two before you want to eat. They're so popular delivery can take a really long time. I usually order the curry goat with rice and peas, and it's been good every time. Portions are large, so you'll probably have leftovers. Take a trip to The Islands for your Caribbean fix, just remember you're on 'island time'.

UW Husky bar in the middle of the big apple. Â How in the world could you go wrong? Â  I was with a friend, a UW graduate, who had heard of Rattle 'N' Hum, but had yet to visit. Â I met up with him for dinner and naturally with a game being on at 9pm (Pacific) the game was on much later Eastern time so after dinner we headed over to hang out with some fellow Huskies, UW transplants and Seattle natives. Â It literally was like being back in the Northwest - the only time I was reminded that I was in NY was when I stepped outside to smoke. The place is an average size bar with friendly goers and so many beers on tap! Â On a Saturday my friend and I were able to get a great drink special, $12 for a pitcher of Pumpkin Ale and $5 Martinis. Â Could it really get any better than that, especially in NYC? The best part? Â The bar was in the shadow of the Empire State Building....Gotta love the big apple.
Best Iskender plate I have ever had. If you're looking for atmosphere this might not be the place. But if you come for the food, you won't be sorry. Fast and fresh. Really outstanding!

BEST chicken parmigiana I've ever had! Â Seriously. Â And I have had many. My gf loves their bread and caesar salad. Â The pasta/other options are solid, not great. Â But honestly, I could live on their chicken parm. Â Worth the 5 stars for their chicken parm alone.
delish

We were starving and needing a drink after playing with our daughter at Madison Square Park playground on a recent evening. Just up from the park on 5th Avenue, Lulu & Me was so warm and inviting, and brand new. I love the design of the place--it feels speak-easy-esque with white subway tile and dark wood and candles, and a long bar. Forties music was playing and it was ... just what the doctor ordered. The service was friendly, and the wine and beer list was very impressive--we'll be telling our friends. We ordered roasted pork, appetizer almonds, a cheese crostini and a tuna panini (excellent tuna, no mayo, fresh arugula) that our 5-year-old devoured! We were shocked. It was, in all, a sort of romantic evening, very satisfying. I highly recommend. Great place perhaps to take work associates for wine and small plates at the end of the day, or meet friends out at night for good conversation and wine. We'll be back.

This restaurant is amazing. Â I visit New York a few times a year, and this is one of my absolute favorite places to eat. Â I salivate on the plane just thinking about it. Â You can't get Greek food like this where I live in Dallas. Â  One of my friends used to live right around the corner from here, and the last time I was there the two of us ate dinner and had leftovers for around $20. Â We LOVE the lemon potatoes, Greek Salad, and grilled chicken. Â If you are one of the lucky ones you get a special dessert too, but you can't ask for it! Â Sit outside if possible for some great people watching if the weather is nice! Â  My friend has since moved so I have less of a reason to visit Astoria, but I'll still be back every time I visit the city!

Finally made it here after making a reservation a month in advance, which seemed a little absurd to me. The Hakata Tonton hotpot really hit the spot, especially on this rainy day. It's really delicious, as well as the Tonsoku in ponzu sauce. We couldn't stop raving about how good everything tasted. The flavors were on point. However, the service is just RIDICULOUS. They're so SLOW. I don't understand what could possibly take them so long to get things done. If you have anger management issues, I would avoid this place. You could potentially boil internally and just explode for holding in your patience. If I were just rating on service alone, this place doesn't even deserve a star. They're lucky their food is good.

Tried this place out when I was in NY with some friends. Â We decided to try this place out because everyone kept telling us how good it is and how they would compare it to In-N-Out here in California. Â I was super excited walking in. Â I order the Shack Stack with cheese fries. Â  Pretty disappointed. Â I don't see what all the fuss is about. Â The burger was smaller than I was expecting for the price I was paying. Â The cheese fries weren't anything special. Â And they didn't even have any spicy condiments! Â I understand that some burgers are so amazing you don't need any condiments, but I don't think my Shack Stack fit into that category...

I LOVE THE HALAL GUYS. I got a combo, chicken and beef. Drenched that entire plate with WHITE SAUCE. OMG IT WAS ALL SO AMAZING. Beware of the red sauce! Spicy as shit! I only poured a little bit on my plate thinking it was equivalent to Taco Bell Fire Sauce but it burned so much. I would use extra caution! IT'S STRONG!
Great burger, nice staff, cheap beer, no wait, took card. Me happy. Slight let down on the banana and toffee for afters. Maybe it's done differently here, so will still give 4/5. I would come back :)
Beautiful restaurant, great staff and tasty food. Great spot for a celebration dinner or girls night out, tapas are great and the entrees are just the right size.

The food is absolutely amazing. Good to the last bite good. Â Hands down. Excellent cook chef preparer, whatever you call the genius who put the ingredients together for my dinner. Â The service is ........ A 1 spectacular. Â Tim the bartender was such a great guy. Â Super humble super courteous and earned a great tip and our future business. Â  Thank you Tim for single Handley making our experience a great one. Â  I must strongly recommend this place to everyone who dines in this area. Â  Only drawback is they don't have free standing liquor, Â so it's take what we got, which is great none the less (they have an amazing selection of pre made liquors). Doesn't matter though I'm looking forward to trying them all in the near future!

This place is so amazing. They have just about everything I could ever want to purchase for cooking up spanish foods. Chorizo, JamÃ³n, Pulpo, olive oil, etc...They also have a great selection of small lunch plates to eat which are also amazing. definitely worth going to!

I really wanted to like this place, but it fell short. This place isn't on par with Roberta's. I don't know how they managed this, but the pork shoulder and duck breast had an identical consistency. The pork shoulder was good but not fantastic. The duck breast was pretty good. The best part of our meal was the amuse-bouche and the bread (which is incredible). Overall I was disappointed and feel that we overpaid for the quality of food. The wine selection is pretty good. Supposedly the cocktails are great, but I didn't have any...probably should have.

Best Chinese restaurant in Chinatown, NY!!! Known for its wontons(made of pork and shrimp) and soup, you can dream up of many different types of variations to suit your appetite. Beef stew wonton noodle soup, bbq pork wonton noodles soup, tendon and stripe wonton noodle soup, I could go on and on. There are also different types of stir fry, congees, and popular Chinese dishes. Great for take out since they store food in heavy duty containers that you could re-use. Great prices and quick service as well. DELICIOUS!!!

I've heard so much about Ippudo and I thought I go check it out with a friend. The friend is not new to Ippudo. She actually likes the place. I, on the other hand, thought the place was OK. The ramen is overpriced. I had Akamaru Modern. It was different, somewhat tasty. The broth was decent. Garlic oil made it unique. Charsu was ok. We had some other chicken dishes but weren't memorable. I just remember the dishes costing a little too much for the small portion. I can't remember what my friend had. I would go back again. This time I'll take a friend who loves ramen and see what she thinks of the place. Good thing we didn't have to wait long for a table. I love the decor. No wonder the ramen is pricey.

this is a great french fry place. the sauces make the fries! u get so many to choose from. at 1.50 u can't go wrong. they give u a lot in a dixie cup with a lid. i had the garlic mayo. that was pretty good. not too garlicky which was great. nice and creamy. i also had the sweet chili and that was my favorite. not too spicy and it was sweet with some garlic flavor. i love this one. wendys had a similar sauce and i'm glad i found it. i took my fries home cuz it is a tiny place and there was no place to sit. my fries were cold obviously, so i popped them in the oven and they were delicious. hot and crispy on the outside and fluffy on the inside. i'm not crazy about the fact that they very brown cuz it makes me think they r burned but they didnt taste burned. over all the place is great. i def. am coming back for more real soon :)

So I was actually extremely Impressed with this restaurant! Â In New York's theatre district, has an EXTREMELY reasonable menu with tons of selections, even most wines by the glass were under $10 and plenty varietals to choose from. Â So the dining room stretches all the way back and tables are not on top of eachother like most places in the area. Â Decor was so so but the food was fantastic. Â Had the antipasta and a goat cheese salad for the table both were excellent. Â As a main course I had to try the Rigatoni Trecolori just becuase I assumed this was the signature dish being named after the restaurant. Â It was not tri color pasta but rigatoni with broc rab some good oil a nice basil pure and sausage, it had great flavor and was not too filling. Â Service was on point, water always to the top, tables crumbed between courses and multiple servers serving food to the table. Â Desserts: your classic Italian restaurant desserts... Canolli, Tartufo, Gelato... all great. Â  Never liked dining in that part of the city but I am for sure returning to this restaurant. Â GREAT JOB!

1oz whiskies, what an awesome idea. Amazing curation and the small sizes let's you choose several and not get too wasted. Comfort food to die for: innovative yet hits the spot. Crowded and hip but not pretentious (and not too pricey). Knowledgeable and friendly staff. Awesome interior design by Berman Horn studio.

i really liked this place and how sweet and intimate it felt. Â the shared tables are distinctly european and the people there are pretty friendly. Â i didn't like the fact that i had to go next door to their bar and wait for my person to arrive, but it's a pretty small place, so i guess i understand. we had a smoked trout appetizer that came with some pickled vegetables and they were delicious. Â the veal was thin and perfectly cooked and my mushroom pappardelle was great. Â i think it needed a bit more of something... garlic? Â olive oil/butter? Â cheese? Â i don't know. Â maybe some hot pepper flakes. Â but i love mushrooms and i love pappardelle so it's all good. Â  the portions were not cheesecake factory style ginormous and they were just perfect for an normal individual. Â i'll definitely be back, i saw a chocolate cake of some sort on the dessert menu i'd love to try, yay. oh, if you get here after 8.30, be prepared to wait. Â i sat down a little after 7.30 and the place was already filling up.

Holy crap. This place is really good. So good that I may start making pilgrimages to Bed-Stuy just to eat here. So good that I cursed my misfortune that I wouldn't have time to eat here the following day. Yummy, simple drinks on the cheap. Eccentric and sweet service. Awesome music. Number one, though, is that freaking hot chicken. I don't especially love fried chicken. Nor do I especially love extremely spicy things. Yet, I especially love that dish. That with the watermelon salad on the side to take off the heat? A-right.

A friend of mine wanted to venture downtown to check out these dumplings. I must say, totally worth the trip! Not only are the prices excellent (we ordered 10 steamed and 10 fried dumplings with two duck Pancakes for 8.00) but the food itself was extremely tasty. The sigature pork and chive dumplings just melted in my mouth and sandwiches had the perfect amount of Cilantro and carrots to spuce up the chopped duck stuffed between two crispy, golden pieces of bread. If you're on the budget in NYC it's a must visit! FYI, it's extremely tight in the shop, so either take it to go or don't go during peak dining hours :)
Ohhh Minetta Tavern I love you. The cheeseburger with caramelized onions has got to be the best burger ever. The fries are always crispy and come with A LOT. The decor is simply great.

I was very excited to check this place out because, despite my frequent visits to the city and all the great things I heard about this place, I never got to try it. So finally, at 12 AM one night, my friend and I headed over to halal cart to get the oh-so-famous chicken over rice. It definitely lives up to the hype! (and I think it will be 1029 times better as drunchies) FOOD: Great! And oh god, that white sauce...I drenched my food with that. So much food just for $6! The line was long, but it went by very quickly and was definitely worth the ~5 min wait. The hot sauce is actually really spicy but complements it very well. I don't really have another way of describing the food here except by saying it's amazing and everyone must try it! SERVICE: Despite the crowd and the drunk people, the workers were very friendly! Overall, totally worth it!

Nice staff, good service, nice ambiance, good food, and a nice wine selection make this an overall and very solid 4 stars for me. I had a Brunello and then a Malbec that was pretty tasty and very light. Â I also had the steak appetizer medium rare which was perfect with my wines. The staff seems knowledgeable and they're all super friendly. Very good job here and a very warm place to pass the time and sip on some vino in. enjoy!

So freaking crowded...anytime, any day...geez. It did make me feel like I was in Italy with the enormous selection of food, veggies, cheeses, gelato and sweets. The center of the place has a stand up eating area. Good luck finding a spot to settle in. It's hectic! They also have a room where they have cooking/wine classes. If there weren't many people and we hadn't just had a bite to eat, we would have elbowed our way to some grub. Their selection of goodies was ridiculous. I will return.
Let's just say its scary that we live so close to this place. Everything on the menus is what you would want!!!! The bus quits are amazing!! The chicken is mouth watering!!!

After a day of exploring New York City, a friend and I came here for dinner, pretty much ravenous. I was not let down by Rubirosa -- not only was the service very attentive and hospitable, the food was also very generous and flavorful at a reasonable price. The interior is a bit dark, but your eyes adjust quickly. There are also nice flowers that adorn each table. The front of the restaurant seats mostly two-person parties, while the tables in the back can accommodate more people. There is also a bar for seating. We ordered the Rubirosa salad and the Classic pizza with mushroom toppings, which were delivered quickly. The great thing about the pizzas is that you can customize to your taste by just adding toppings. The salad was so large (definitely could feed more than 2 people) -- the leaves were fresh and crispy and the tomatoes were so juicy! The thin slices of mozarella also added a nice change of taste and texture. The pizza itself -- aside from the fact that it was humongous -- was warm, cheesy, and full of zest. I would definitely recommend Rubirosa, especially if you are super hungry and looking to feast!

YUM! All-you-can-eat pasta trio is amazing for only $23! I love that it's unlimited (not that I could eat allll that much), but also that you get to try three different types of pastas! Â Almost everyone in the restaurant was taking advantage of this deal. Â  Additionally, all the waiters are amazing!! They really treat everyone with such friendliness and respect that it made the experience even better. Â The diners next to us were freaking out that they only had an hour to eat before their Broadway play at 8, but the waiters were able to get them their entire 3-course dinner in that hour, and they walked away so happy and pleased that they were accommodated so well. I'd definitely go back! It's a fantastic way to fill up before a show.

I really enjoyed degustation. I saw it had gotten a lot of positive reviews. I also wanted to take my girlfriend somewhere intimate for her birthday. We are both sort of foodies so I thought it would be fun. The exposed kitchen is really cool. We spent half the time bothering the chefs about all the plates they were making. We had the 5-course tasting menu and it was outstanding. It takes a while to get all 5 courses. We were there for about 2 and half hours but that is okay. The plates were small but after all the courses I felt full. I think next time we go we are going to get the 10-course chef tasting menu. It has some things that are not on the menu. I highly recommend this place.

Worth a trip but needs some work The space is great, the food is really good and the bourbon and beer selection phenomenal, but we had some issues. First, the line was extremely long. We expected that but once we reached the front, we realized what the problem was. They only have one scale to weigh out customer orders. If they just added one more station, wait time could be cut in half. I guess that may create a seating issue though. Still, it seemed very inefficient. Second, the bartender, although really knowledgable and outwardly customer-service oriented enough, was so negatively passive aggressive towards the patrons, I was amazed. He stated outright to one that next time, they should leave a tip which would be good for everyone, told someone else he didn't have time to recommend a cocktail, refused to pour beer from a very large jug into a glass for another because "if he did it for one customer, he'd have to do it for everyone." He also refused to continue serving another customer, who was foreign, because he hadn't left a tip. I understand that tipping is the right thing to do and that it must be frustrating for bartenders when people don't tip, but honestly, maybe if he had been a little nicer, it wouldn'thave been an issue.

This has become our go-to restaurant in the city! Â It is a tiny, rustic Italian restaurant big on character and flavor. Â I always look forward to coming here and trying something new each time. Â Although I always have a great meal, I usually find myself taking forkfuls of my friend's gnocchi that is out of this world. Â I should just get a whole bowl for myself sometime. Â The wine selection is great and the wait staff is more than helpful in selecting a wine pairing for your meal. Â The specials are always special and the fish and pasta dishes are truly superb. Â You will not be let down by this place. Â I know that I never am!

Came here for brunch.. I was deciding between 3 or 4 stars.. My mood right now tells me that it deserves 3 stars.. for BRUNCH.. No idea about dinner.. 1st of.. brunch portion was small.. well.. guess the price was not that expensive for brunch anyway.. the french toast I ordered was a little too soft to enjoy.. My friend ordered the kale salad.. It was just ok and I don't find it anything too good about it.. Their omelet was really good.. the omelet of the day was with cheese, onion and something else which I kinda forgot.. :p It was small but the cheese that melt together with it.. was just perfect.. They have complementary pastries.. which I kinda down it in a second.. Too many brunch place at NYC.. sorry Perilla..

The menu is smaller than the original location but it's still super delicious and the wait wasn't bad at all for lunch (although perhaps ramen is not as desirable in August to some)! Â A great midtown lunch option and a great alternative to the crazy waits in the other location.
love this place. cheap and tasty. i got the meatball hand pulled noodles. pan fried dumplings were alright....much better elsewhere.

This place is small and cozy. I'm a big fan of mexican food so I decided to try this place out. First time I went there, I had a great experience. Not sure if I was really hungry or the food was really good. I got two tacos (steak and fish). The steak taco didn't have enough flavoring, but I did enjoy the fish tacos. I also got the baked oysters, which I thought tasted amazing for the first time, but the second time I got it, it was alright. I also got the guacamole and chips, which lacked flavor so I probably wouldn't get that, again. But overall, I was satisfied because the people there were really nice and the food was decent. They also had a live band playing that day. Nice environment to just go and hangout with friends.

This is easily the best pizza place in all of New York City. Lucali is compared to Di Fara but it is not even close. Di Fara's has been around so long it should be an institution of NYC. The setting for this landmark is not sexy, but when it comes down to the pizza- it's nothing more than the best. For a slice the charge is $4, but I would pay $10. That's how good it is. You may have to wait a little while but that's because old man Dom takes his time and still uses scissors to cut his basil, that's old school. You can tell he really cares about every single slice and that's all you can really ask for as a customer. As for the pizza, as you may already know the ingredients HAVE TO be imported from Italy because you cannot get that kind of stuff in Brooklyn, let alone Midwood. The crust is perfectly rolled, thrown, or whatever he does. It's not too doughy but not thin where it falls apart when you go to eat it. The sauce is old fashioned but compliments the cheese so well. Dom cuts the cheese with an old school pencil sharpener, or at least that's what it looks like. On top of the Bufalo Mozzarella, when the pizza just comes out of the oven, Dom grates some cheese on top along with olive oil. You usually see those two steps take place before the pizza goes into the oven but once again, this is the old school way in Di Fara's. Basically, the best pizza around right now. This is a glaring example that the old way of doing things still works perfectly fine in 2008.

I finally got to check out this place after living in NY for almost three years! We went for brunch one weekend since we were dying to try the ube waffles. Â The place is extremely tight, especially if you have a baby stroller! But everyone was really accommodating and super nice and helped us find a place where we can put the stroller comfortably. We had the lumpia appetizer to start. Nothing to report, standard lumpia to me. Â My bf got the tocilog. It was really really good. Super tender tocino (cured pork) and it wasn't too sweet. I had the Dasilog which was the fish version of the breakfast. The fish was a bit Â small but crunchy and savory. Dipped it in vinegar with hot chiles, oh my god so good!! They were nice enough to let us order just the waffles without the fried chicken so we can try them. A really nice and refreshing take on waffles! The ube flavor come through nicely, it was soft and fluffy and I love the purple color. It was served with this amazing guava syrup. We decided to get dessert. We tried the bibingka topped with salted egg and the leche flan. The flan was meh. My mother makes a nice creamy version that you could die for. Theirs is kind of hard and not really creamy. It was disappointing. The bibingka was great. Just like how I remember it. The bread part was soft, fluffy and steaming hot. The salted eggs on top gives it a nice balance. Overall a great experience and I would love to try their dinner menu to taste the more local Filipino dishes they have. They are a bit pricey but I guess it's an americanized, fancy version of Filipino food. The service is A plus plus. The best host and server. He was really attentive and personable and really helpful. Their staff is awesome I must say.
Rib sandwich with sweet potato fries were awesome. Shared chicken tenders which were also yummy. Â  Friendly and attentive staff.

Pricey but worth it. Â $9.25 for lunch is steep BUT in the few months that I've been working in Times Square, it's probably my most frequented spot. Â  The rice and beans is superb - almost as if they put MSG in it! Â (Do they??? Â It IS a bit salty...) I've tried a whole bunch of their meats including oxtail, chicken, pork chop and today the shredded pork. Â My favorite is definitely the shredded pork. Â The meat is just so juicy and fat! Â The lady even picked out a few pieces of skin that are out of this world. Â I'm just a pork-lover, though. Â  The oxtail is also great. Â The chicken and pork chop less so. Â My brother says I should get the chicken sandwich, which is cheaper but I can't resist the rice and beans.

one of my default bars to go to...moderately priced drinks, friendly servers, great menu of bar food, and a separate bar area/eating area with a dance floor. on weekends, they play great music here to!

Went today for brunch with a girlfriend. Â They were fairly fast; staff was helpful and prompt with requests. Â They were also very accommodating with changes. Cantaloupe mimosa was delish and so was the food.

This is a great place to go out on a date and have great food. The Chicken Bastille is absolutely delicious, cant go wrong with chicken cooked into a fluffy pastry. The couscous dishes are also delicious, my boyfriend had the lamb and he said it was cooked perfectly. The food is always pretty consistent, we've been here about five times and haven't been disappointed yet.
Awesome! Â Good service, great food, reasonable priced and fun atmosphere.

I can't wait to come back for dinner! Dinner for 2 seated promptly at 7:15pm (reservations via OpenTable). Small restaurant (40-50 persons), completely packed. We had a cozy booth next to the bar/cashier. Shared a bottle of Prosecco very reasonably priced at $39 ($12/glass). Overall the wine list is not so pricy. My friend ordered the STEAK FRITES ($24) - well sized portion, including a side of mixed salad as well. Cooked perfectly. I had the SKATE ($20) which was so yummy with the butter lemon sauce. Used a piece of fresh French bread to really taste it. Served over a good portion of perfectly cooked French beans. Entrees are pretty generous and well priced for the quality. If I lived in the neighborhood, I would be a regular. I look forward to returning and trying the entire menu and their specials - Challenge Accepted! (Def want to get the Steak Tartare and Duck Confit) Service was prompt in refilling water, refilling prosecco glasses and food seemed to have been served in under 15 minutes! AMEX accepted.

let me start by saying i am a huge burger fan, and this place does NOT dissapoint.. we came two days in a row .. both days the burgers were great, service was phenomenal (thanks Kelsey!!!!) and the place was extremely cozy!! there was no waiting time to be seated, you have the option to sit at the bar or at a table .. ordering ofcourse is pretty simple : there are only 2 types of sliders, and their bigger brothers: the doubles .. the sliders arrive promptly and are scorching hot (the way i like'em) .. experiment with the sauces they have: jalapeno, chipotle ketchup, BBQ or katechup .. (btw, i asked and all are made in-house except the ketchup) .. they also have this nice touch: buy 10 sliders and get the 11th free.. you are given a card which is punched everytime you order a slider .. hand it in after 10 and you are good for the 11th, on them! good job "Marks".. keep it up!! next time i am in NY i know where i will be eating, EVERYDAY!

I'm adding to my previous review. Â  4 stars The other day I had a super duper rib craving and went back to Fette Sau. Â I think $8 got me 1/4lb of ribs, which perfectly hit the spot. Â The meat fell right off the bone, just how I like it. Â If you really watch what you order, you won't run up a bill, and the meat's yummy. Â Watch out for the super fatty things though, too fatty for my tastes. 3.5 stars I was leaving Willbeg for a little while and wanted to go out with a bang, so I thought RIBS. Â Decided to try this place, after seeing good ratings. Â The first night we went there was a line out the door, so went elsewhere. Â However, determined to try the place, we went back the next day. My dining partner and I (2 people) tried a little of everything, the 1/4 and 1/2 pound fare didn't seem too pricey. Â We actually did run up a bill. Â I figured it was "organic" "quality" cuts, so it'd be worth it, and I do cite the meat as tasty, however, I couldn't figure out if it was worth it or not. Â It wasn't exactly the greatest dinner afterthought.

Dined at Da Andrea this past Friday night and there was no wait at 9:30pm. Â What a great atmosphere - homey decor with loud and lively diners makes one feel like they are at home. Â The staff are all very friendly and attentive. Â Only thing is, I saw other tables get offered fresh pepper and parmesan, but we never got any :( Free bread + olive oil to start. After debating with the date, we finally settled on the prosciutto and flatbread appetizer, since its the most popular and widely ordered dish on the menu. Â I would have preferred something a lot less heavy, as the appetizer was a bit much for two people to share. Â You get 6 pieces of super fresh, super hot small-ish flatbread which you are supposed to cut in half and put the prosciutto and a dash of parmesan cheese in the middle. Â It's basically like 3 mini prosciutto sandwiches each... and it got boring. Â Not to say it wasn't appetizing, just boring. Â I was really bored of carbs by that point and we still hadn't even eaten our main entrees! Â  I had the clam/squid ink pasta and he had the sausage pappardelle. Â The fresh pasta, in my opinion, was a little too firm for my taste. Â If it was cooked maybe a couple minutes longer, it would have been perfect. Â The clam pasta was not salty enough and I would have liked a bit more flavor in the white wine sauce - perhaps more garlic. Â The clams were overcooked and tasted like the ocean. Â The pappardelle sausage red sauce, on the other hand, was delicious. Worth a try if you are in the area, but it was not spectacular Italian in my opinion.

I have to agree with most of the posts - been here twice, including "the line" at 5pm when it opens on Saturday and one time for a 45 minute wait. Â Had Akamaru Modern both times - real wonderfulness in a bowl and unlike other ramen I have had in NYC. Also had the fried chicken pieces as a starter (squeeze the lemon over the pieces). Left very, very, very satisfied....

Great place to go for great ambiance and horrible service. Couldn't tell you much about the food, since we didn't have any of it, and probably never will, because the service is so bad and almost non-existent. We saw a couple walk out because they weren't getting served at all. BYOB

Very cute vibe. Great soundtrack. Tiny portions for the price but that's nice if you're counting calories. I ordered the sandwich/soup combo and specifically said "with the ham and cheese croissant" since it was a choice between that or a tomato croissant. Got the tomato, mentioned it to the server, she was like "no, it was the ham OR the tomato". Um, that's why I ordered the ham. I ate it anyway because it took about 30 minutes to get and I was starving and didn't feel like arguing about it (I don't think English was her first language). No coffee or water refills. Probably wouldn't go back, but 3 stars for the decorating and music.

Definitely one of the better Sicilians slices I've had and it's definitely served by some world class jerks. A nitpick would be that it could use a little bit more cheese, but other than that it's the perfect storm of delicious sauce, soft donut-esque dough, and a crispy bottom crust. Â It's not greasy at all and is very easy to eat, one of the lightest slices of pizza especially for a Sicilian style. Â  The regular slice looks god awful, if you come here and order that you might as well make the Brooklyn Bridge your next stop and do a head first off of there. There's about 20 Fat Joe/Bartolo Colon ex con looking slobs working here, only about 1 actually working, and none of them are pleasant and act like they are doing you the favor to end all favors by serving you a slice, it's sad that this great pizza comes from such scum. Â It seems like a formula they stick to so my guess is that anyone with a weeks training can learn the recipe. I wouldn't be mad at anyone who said this is the best Sicilian they've had, it's a must try for a square slice fan and at least for that one try it's worth the garbage service

LOVE this place!!! AWESOME hotpot and BBQ! Nothing imperfect, the meat, the soup and the seafood are just way too good for a hotpot buffet. Unlimited hotpot for 21.99 in Manhattan location and 18.99 in Brooklyn location. need to try!!!

Let me start out saying that this place doesn't need any more good press...but since I've been coming here for 10 years now and it has been the host of some of my most memorable meals her in new york, I wanted to make this my first review on yelp. Â If it makes my opinion anymore valuable to you, I work in the industry cooking at a 3 star NYT. I can't speak for the brooklyn location, it might be better to get a seat but at the Sullivan St. location there is a great atmosphere and the same servers/bartenders since the 90s. If you go often enough, they'll remember you and the staff does a great job of making you feel at home. Certain menu items have changed due to availability over the years but the menu has remained the same glorious mix of everything you'd need for an amazing meal. My favorites: Raw Bar 9/10 - Excellent service and great quality seafood, particularly the oysters...East coast oysters just make sense, always fresh, ask for the blue ribbon hot sauce. Steak Tartare 9/10 - The texture of the beef is the star, it's finely ground instead of sliced, seasoned right to the edge and served with gaufrettes. Classic. Foie Gras Terrine 7/10 - If it's your thing, you'll love it, if not your thing than there's a 68% chance it will be after eating this. Beef Marrow & Oxtail Marmalade 10/10 - Â Airy fresh brioche, marmalade is perfect balance of sweet/savory and served with a side of coarse sea salt? Stop looking at the menu and order this. Sweetbreads 8/10 - Always done well and the arugula is key. Fried Chicken 9/10 - Breaded with Matzoh meal, never greasy and served with honey.. Changed my life. Strip Steak 8/10 - Skip the hanger, this is better.

I'm shocked that I haven't reviewed this place AKA one of my favorite restaurants in NYC. If beyoglu was within walking distance of either my office or home, I would probably eat this at least 3x a week. The combo platter is a meal for two. The dips are way flavorful and the servings are super generous. The bread..... is...... INCREDIBLE. It's always served warm and soft. Outdoor seating, fabulous combo platter, amazing khadayif (SP), and turkish beers. beyoglu for lifeeeeee (yo)

I know I'm going against the grain here, but I'm just not all that impressed with Salt and Fat. Microscopic portions of overpriced food just never thrilled me. For a tappas-style restaurant, the menu is rather limited, and there are hardly any options for vegetarians. The quality of the food is good, but in humble my opinion, it's simply not worth the price of admission.

Wonderful little Italian spot in the West Village. Â Fantastic food, especially the gnocchi, bruschetta, salads, and bolognese pasta dish. Â Delicious breads too! Â Service is decent, could be better. Â Definitely a place to come back to again and again!!

My fiancÃ© and I celebrated our anniversary dinner at The Heath. As soon as we arrived we were in love. Amazing atmosphere, friendly staff, prompt service and excellent food. I also loved the Jazz music...added to the supper club feel but wasn't overly distracting. I don't love loud music when eating and this was perfect. We started with mini pork pies which were a bit spicy but good. Cocktails were also pretty strong and different. I had the house punch and my fiancÃ© had the aberdonian sour which he loved. We both ate the beef & ale pie. It was incredible. The meat inside was so tender and the puff pastry amazing. Also had a bacon marmalade which added a nice smokey flavor. Oh and I forgot to mention the bread and amazing sweet butter before dinner. For dessert we shared the Nutella icebox pie which was great. I cannot say enough amazing things about this whole experience. I definitely want to go back for Sleep No More so I can check out more of the building. After dinner we went up o Gallow Green to check it out. It was a great space with a nice ambiance up there too. I would definitely go back with a group.

I really am addicted to tacos. Â Some may call it a problem; I consider it a success. Â In my quest to eat every taco in Manhattan, this hole in the wall spot near Union Square was next on my list. I came with a friend and had the carnitas and carne asada tacos, both with guacamole and salsa verde. Â They were tasty, well-stuffed, and appropriately spicy. Â The meat portion in particular was impressive. Â They also give you a generous serving of guac, so I think it's worth the extra $1 or so. Â The food was prepared in front of me, and everything was hot and fresh. Â I can't say much about the service, because it's more of a grab and go place, but I had no complaints. There are a couple of a tables in here, but not many, and it can get crowded. Â This isn't the best Mexican spot I've been to, but, if you're in the area and craving tacos, it's a good standby.

I have been here more than a few dozen times over the last decade, and the quality has definitely gone downhill. Â Here's what you can expect: 1. LONG lines/wait at almost any time of day/week. Â I have gotten lucky during the day on a weekday, but even then can be a long wait. 2. You often will be seated at a shared table. Â I have never had a problem with this, but it should be noted, since I have been seated next to people who are angry the whole time they are sitting with strangers. 3. The service will be spotty. Â You don't really have just one server. Â At least a few different people will approach your table, depending on who it is, you will either be helped greatly, or you will be forgotten and you just need to tell someone else what you want. 4. You will usually be offered to start your meal with the dumplings. Â DO THIS. Â This is usually the only reason why people show up. Â Place the soup dumpling on your spoon, poke it with your chopstick so that the soup drips into your spoon, drink the soup, then eat the dumpling. Â Extra points for next spilling any on your plate. Â This takes practice. 5. The food is generally served in large portions, which is fine with me! Â I usually take home leftovers, and order to share with my group. 6. BRING CASH. Â You cannot pay with a credit card. Â Tip is actually included in the total, so watch out for that too, because you have to look at the receipt to notice this (no one tells you). If you are looking for other good soup dumplings, I prefer Shanghai Cafe, where the service is better, it is less crowded, and an overall more enjoyable experience.

I finally had the chance to try out Umami and I was so disappointed =( Â I really really really wanted to LOVE this place. Â I mean who doesn't love burgers + truffles? Â  We came on a Friday night and we didn't have to wait! Â The place wasn't too packed and service was slow =( Â I'm used to bad service/slow service from frequenting Chinese restaurants so I don't care if the service is slow, but I digress. Â  We ordered: Truffle burger - the burger was all right =( Â It didn't wow me and I actually found the burger to be a little greasy =( Â It wasn't juicy, tiny and didn't give me that wow factor that I was looking for =( Â  The Royale - this burger was the same as the truffle burger. Â There was absolutely no wow factor and not juicy at all. Â It was also greasy and tiny. =( Â  We were both so underwhelmed by the burgers. Â The burgers here are definitely way too hyped. Â For the price we were paying, we were expecting wow and we did say wow, at the tiny size =( Â  Don't get me wrong, the burgers were good, but it tasted the same as something you can get at Five Guys, which is a fraction of the price. Â  Cheesy Tots - these were good, but definitely not what I expected. Â It's something everyone should try, but don't go out of your way to come here just to order this. Â This was my favorite dish of our meal. Truffle fries - I was so disappointed and underwhelmed by these fries. Â They were actually pretty horrible to be honest. Â I know the description says "thin fries", but boy were they thin! Â I love truffles and I love truffle over fries, but since the fries were so thin, the truffles over powered the fries and I got a nauseous feeling from eating these. Â There was no potato meat to compliment the truffles. Â I hope umami changes their fries and get meatier ones. Â These fries suck! So yes, you should come and try this place, but don't bother waiting in line. Â It's not worth it. Â Come back when there is no line.

Khao Kang translates to rice and curry / stew/ soup. Â A nice new addition to the Thai food scene. Â  They have a stream table with a variety of choices, choose two items for $7 or three for $7.50. Â We've seen this before with the Chinese lunch boxes in Flushing and Elmhurst - this is similar, straightforward and simple, and this is Thai. There is no waitress here to seat you or take your order. Â Walk inside the restaurant - and if you are dining in, scope out your seats. Â There were 2 tables of 4 and one table that fits up to 10 - be ready to share your table and make some new friends. Â Go up to the steam table and order your meal, pay at the register (cash only) and then settle down some home-style Thai cuisine. They don't make your food to order, if you don't like a particular dish then choose something else. Â We had fish in yellow curry with sour bamboo shoots, pork basil, tom kha gai - chicken galangal soup, sweet pork, quail with bamboo, chili pork with thai eggplant and string beans. Â You won't find many of these dishes in your typical Thai restaurant. Â Everything we tried were tasty, comforting, and authentic- they used traditional ingredients such as coconut milk, galangal, coriander, lemongrass, kaffir lime leaves (beware some of the choices were spicy). Â If you need to further enhance your food, there is fish sauce with chili peppers on the table to kick it up a notch- but we found the food perfectly seasoned and didn't need to add anything. There were plenty of desserts to cool down the heat, as well as drinks (Thai iced tea/coffee, grass jelly, logan). You will only find this food in Thailand or in the kitchen of your favorite Thai host. Â Come with a hungry stomach and open mind, you will leave satisfied and full.

What a neighborhood favorite. Â Too bad I found out about it a little late. Great for brunch, lunch, and dinner. Â Charming middle eastern restaurant with many Â dishes familiar to Israelis and others. Â Warm pita and hummus platter is recommended, homemade polpettine meatballs, and salads. Â Very reasonable prices, too.

Going here is always delightful. The staffs are very friendly and helpful. I wish more people can understand how important it is to have a good customers service skill. Many restaurants I have been to have great food but the service kills everything. This is definitely not one of them. Â Love their food and I definitely recommend this place.

Went with a group of 4 on Valentines day with no reservation and got an awesome booth. The decor looks upscale, but we were fine going in jeans. The service was great. We kept being offered different kinds of bread (the dip that goes with it is soo good). We shared a pasta dish as an appetizer and got two different pizzas, which ended up being very similar so make sure you fully understand what comes on each pizza. All the food was really delicious!! The pizza was great and really tasty and well done. If I'm down in the area again, I'm sure I'll go back.

The best squares brooklyn has to offer. Â What really makes this place is the perfect blend of spices in the sauce. Â The spumoni is excellent although my favorite are the water ices. Â Vanilla chip baby

I had some genius amazing cheese bibimbap in Tokyo so I was thinking, I have to give the cheese katsu a chance in case it is similarly as good. Naw. Â The cheese was like kraft cheese or something. Â Inserted inside the katsu. Â Kinda weird and a waste of my cheese budget. Â Ugh, think of all the amazing cheeses I could have eaten instead. Â I felt gross afterward. Other than that, it was good katsu. Â I've been here twice though and wasn't impressed either time really...Previous time I had katsu curry. Â It's probably good if you get normal katsu though

I ended up here by accident because the people I was with were not from the city and didn't want to go to the LES for beer. The rooftop isn't really impressive as you can't really see anything while standing bunched up against people since it's so massively crowded. HOWEVER, there is major eye candy here so as I pointed out several to my friend. Â  The rest of the group were hungry so here was an opportunity to try some food and ordered the pork shoulder with mashed potatoes. The pork shoulder didn't live up to my expectations as it was a bit bland. Â However, Â I like carbs and the olive oil mash potatoes were very good. Overall, the experience was ok since it didn't leave much of an impression to me

Yum, that is all I can say. I went her for my Birthday and had the signature BoSam dish a full Pork Butt, served with Oysters, Kimchi and Lettuce to make little wraps. The BoSam has to ordered ahead of time but does get you a reservation. All I can say is this place is amazing and can not wait to go back and try something else.

I believe that this place has changed owners since, but to not leave a review would be an insult to this hidden gem. Not only is this place cheap but the food really does Taste Good! (Okay, obviously not one of my better jokes, but just bear with me here.) As others have already suggested, the roti canai is a good starter. I like to follow it up with an order of Hiananese chicken and roast pork (half/half, of course) but each to their own. Just as long as you make sure to get chicken rice. You won't regret it.

The chef here is one of the best in NYC. Â Of cook shop fame he has turned his eye to a spot where he can actually keep his eyes on the food instead of simply managing it. Â Go there for happy hour and get all the bites for 3 dollars instead of 5. Best deal in the city with 4 dollar drafts. Â d

I ate here with my husband and a friend a few weeks ago. Space is larger than I expected, nice, and clean. Waitstaff are brief, but helpful and friendly, and the food came out really quickly. We decided to order a bunch to share, so we had: Coconut soup Larb Crispy pork belly Green curry Drunken noodles Milk tea with pearls Coconut ice cream Coconut rice Beer (something from Laos) Everything was delicious. My least favorite was probably the drunken noodles (just not very special) and my favorite was the pork belly. Mmm. The menu is huge, but they have good descriptions and pictures of everything. It was totally filling for all three of us and came out to about $70, which wasn't bad, considering how much food we got to try. I'd love to go back soon.

When I was offered sausage, fries, orange slices, cookie bites, and ice water while waiting in line, I knew I already liked the place. Â This diner has that random out of date holiday decor going on for itself. Â Cherry Lime Rickeys seem to be a tradition here, it was tasty but just a cherry seltzer drink. Â I had the meatloaf and eggs over easy. Â DELICIOUS. Â My friend had the crabcake florentine. Â DELICIOUS. Â The french fries we had while waiting were awesome and had a kick, but I mistakenly ordered the homefries thinking I was going to get those same fries. Â Our table shared the lemon ricotta pancakes and the sweet potato pancakes. Â They were fluffy, but the flavors were more subtle than I was expecting - couldn't identify any presence of ricotta, but they were tasty still. Â They had Â (what I think is homemade) cinnamon butter, strawberry butter, and peach butter in addition to the normal butter packets. Â If you're in New York and need a reason to go to Brooklyn, you've just found one.

Not so spectacular ending to a spectacular time at radio city music hall. Found this place here on yelp. Was looking for affordable Spanish cuisine not too far from radio city. Mediocre food, served barely warm, felt rushed by our waiter, and had no flan! Stay clear of this place if you're looking for a nice dinner. Maybe a quick lunch spot-- emphasis on maybe.
Everything was delicious, specially the octopus. Great wine also. The wait was quite long, but the bar had plenty of space and it was definitely worth it.
I've only visited the truck, but the tacos are spot on. Â You can eat like a king for under $10. Â Most authentic tacos around. Â Highly recommend!

Fantastic cocktails in Astoria. Great place to meet friends and have a few. Bartenders are always super attentive. I even hosted a surprise birthday party here from my best friend and the staff were super accommodating. No frills!
We eat here before every show we see in NYC becuase of it's size, food quanity/price, and the fast service. The ravioli is amazing as well as anything pasta there. Â Very good salads too.

Fell in love with this place a few months ago! So Authentically Japanese! Fried Mackarel was delicious. The Spicy Tuna and Salmon Rolls were GREAT!! Served with Soy Jelly instead of Soy Sauce (I learned an important lesson in this rest - how to NOT drench my sushi in soy sauce and really enjoy the fresh fish and vinegar enhanced rice flavors) Sake was great too and the Asahi Draft super fresh and Frothy. Love love love.

Dropped by after a trip to the MoMA. I heard so much about it so naturally I had to take a crack at it. For $6 portion size is a great deal. If you're not that hungry you can easily split a plate with a friend. You get a circular aluminum foil filled with so much goodies. The chicken meat is pulled, subtlety yet flavorfully spiced, served up with some very tasty and perfectly cooked pilaf style rice, grilled pita strips and some lettuce. The whole wait took about 20-30 minutes on a Friday at 5 PM. White sauce is a must, red sauce is an option. Holy Halal guys that @#!& is spicy! I painfully regret that decision. A couple drops would of been just fine for me. In other news, the steps of the Charles Schwab building is the official dining room for the Halal Guys as you'll always spot at least 1 person sitting down here scarfing down the goods. Quick tip: They do have more than one cart owned by these guys so if the line is getting out of hand head over to the other carts. There's really no difference.

Its a shame when the food is amazing, but there service is horrendous. Â When the hostess passed us up twice for having a party of. 3, and four people walk (one with reservation and another was a walk in) and we are standing in front of a table for four that wasn't reserved, that is insulting. Â Even better is when our waiter is outside typing away on his phone (apparently our order is not important). If you can stomach rude behavior from the staff, the food is amazing.

Five stars for the steamed pork belly buns alone. Gets very busy and crowded...only came as a party of two and sat at the bar so we didn't wait, but I can imagine the wait for a larger party could get pretty lengthy. Definitely get the steamed pork buns. We also had the seared duck, which was really good, as well as the apple/bacon/arugula kimchi thing. That was just ok. Not a big fan of arugula with Korean food. Bacon was on point though. Finished it off with the spicy sausage and rice cakes dish. Love that they sear the rice cakes a bit so that the outside is crispy but the inside is still very gelatinous. I hear they have big dishes for bigger parties like whole duck or the pork shoulder (bo ssam) and I'd love to come back and try that. Check their website for availability for those things, though, cus I believe it's pretty limited.

I was staying in tribeca down the street from here a few weeks back. I had the fried chicken and waffles 3 days in a row. The homemade soda is really tasty. The hot chocloate was tasty but pretty expensive. I also got banoffee to go and that was my favorite of all. It's a nice first date place, all by your lonesome place, or group of friends place. I will go back next time I'm in town!

Pure is a great place to stop by for a flavorful taste of Thai food... this is significant in an area saturated with Thai food! Their service is good and their decor fits the authentic bill for those whose feel that the ambiance is important... My favorites appetizers are the curry puffs (standard yum) and the Steamed Fresh Roll (YUM!!, delicate and had real crab!). I always order one of their noodle dishes and a iced tea/coffee. Their food is prepared well and is not covered in the generic salty "brown sauce" that makes in an appearance in other "Asian restaurants." Portions are manageable for 1 person and prices are reasonable for Hell's Kitchen. Things to watch out for: ~ Beware of the spicy factor as others have stated... dishes definitely satisfies the heat seekers out there in terms of "bring out the sweat" level. ~ The # of people peak times is a deterrent for those not dedicated enough... just be prepared to deal with it... the food is worth the wait!

The food is good, but the service is soo slow. The server took our appetizer order and disappeared for 15 mins until we finally called him to place our full order. We were served by 2 different servers, which was very confusing, as we had to repeat our orders/requests to each of them. The main dish arrived very late, even though there were only 5-6 people in the restaurant. They should really work on speed and efficiency. I'm still giving 4 stars because they're new and the khachapuri is very good.

Please note that the one star is not to rate the quality of the food, which was excellent, but for the service. We came here because it was near our hotel and nothing else was open due to hurricane Irene. This place was a big disappointment! I would had a better time getting food from the bodega down the street. The minute we walked in, we were getting dirty looks from what it seems to be the manager of the restaurant. We were a bit windblown and wet from the storm outside, which was apparently the cue not the pay any attention to us. He literally went by every table for a greeting except ours. Since i didn't have a big appetite, i decided to order two appetizers knowing they were small portions. My husband and mother-in-law ordered full entrees. I ordered the shrimp risotto, which was pretty good, and the seared scallops, and here's the story. The two entrees came out, the shrimp risotto...and 30 mins later still no scallops. My mother-in-law ordered a tuna tartare later, and it still came out before the scallops. One hour later, i told the waiter to just cancel the order because i was PISSED already. He said it was on its way (just like it was an hour ago?) and would just give it to us for free. It finally came out and it was ONE TINY scallop for $14. Even though the taste wasn't bad, i really couldn't justify it with the price and the time it took to get it. The waiter and who i think is the manager weren't attentive, and we would definitely not come back even if it was less than a block away from our hotel during a hurricane.

I went for a late lunch yesterday. Â Reservation for two at 2pm. Â We both opted for the Tasting Menu, which is comprised of five courses of heaven for $48 per person. Â Some of the dishes I had: sashimi-quality tuna, tender Maine skate, a chicken and ravioli dish, the amazing chocolate souffle. Â The chef's canape, a tomato sorbet, was completely unexpected but flavorful and refreshing. Â Also, the breads! Â I had a slice of fig bread and tasted at least six others, including the garlic and the raisin. Â My least favorite parts of the meal included the meringue and the asparagus sorbet. Â Lunch was long, almost two hours. Â The service was very good, attentive (almost too attentive?). Â The portions were a good size because I had room to eat at least some of everything presented. Â The decor is a little stuffy (floral chintz fabrics and antiques everywhere). Â Still, highly recommended for a leisurely lunch.

Ambiance: A+ The first floor is deceptively small; I was pleasantly surprise when we were lead down the stairs to such a huge area. It's dimly lit, modern and trendy with cool music and lot's of people. The interior design is a feast for the eyes with some sort of petrified-looking limbs of wood lining the walls. Very chic and very fun place to be in. Service: B+ Nice, but we only saw our server once or twice and it took forever to get our check. Not very attentive but not rude or surly. We made reservations and we were seated immediately. Food: A Huge portions. You most definitely need to share. The Matador combo was enough for 3 of us. The chicken was flavorful, well-seasoned, tender, and succulent. It was really great, well-executed chicken. Very juicy. The fires it came with were REALLY good and addicting. I don't know what Peruvians put n their french fries but whatever it is I want it in a Costco side container for a my fries. Â  The avocado salad was fresh and tasty. The salchihas weren't anything special. They just seemed like peruvian hot dogs. The tostones were OK, but the dipping sauce it came with was incredible. It could make rubber soles taste good. It's a fun place to go to with a group of people. The food is good and the portions are huge.

Could this be New Yorks #1 Drunk Food Spot? The lines are long but move quickly. For $6, you get Â a very generous plate of either chicken, lamb or beef, rice, lettuce and vegetable, and warm pita. They offer other options as well, like Falafel or sandwiches. From there, you can either get White or Red sauce. What exactly is the white sauce? Rumors include mayo, Ranch, vinegar, yogurt, sour cream. I just think it's made from heaven. I always stick to the chicken and rice with white sauce. It's simple, filling, and delicious.
As far as street meat goes, there is no better place - period
Great Salumeria, top notch. Â Moz was very fresh. Â  Limited seating but great service and good menu.

I went here for a friends bday, and they seemed really excited to eat here. Â All I heard about was the NYT article and how good the place was and how Bobby was spending a lot of time in the kitchen. Â  What I had to eat: THE BAR MENU: Lamb Tenderloin - 4/5* APPS: Crab Risotto - 3.5/5* Pizza with lamb sausage - 5/5* Tortiglioni(Pasta) - 3/5* ENTREES:(Shared) Taragon Chicken - 4/5* Kale and Mushroom Paella - 4/5* Charred Beef - Â 5/5 * DESSERT: Cheese Cake 3.5/5 If you have high blood pressure or sensitivities to salt/sodium DO NOT EAT here. Â Everything, I mean EVERYTHING, is on the saltier side. Â Apparently B Flay and NYT have noted this, but if you didn't know, you should know now after reading this. Â I find it difficult to enjoy the meals because of how salty it was. Â The only other restaurant where I felt they served this much salt, is Lavo. Â So if you like the food at Lavo, you will like the food here. Â  I love lamb, so I am biased to some extent, but everyone at the table agreed that the Tenderloin and the Pizza were quite amazing. Â I just find it sad that a Pizza its the best app I had there, but in all fairness maybe they had other apps that were better that we didn't try. Â The Tortiglioni Pasta, was a little shy of al dente, which I heard was the way it was supposed to be. Â It was mediocre at best, you could better pasta at Olive Garden, that's right B Flay, I said Olive Garden. Â  I ordered the Paella at the recommendation of the server. Â He said it was their best dish based on his preferences and was becoming a huge favorite. Â It was savory, SALTY, perfectly balanced, a bit oilier than expected, rice was perfectly cooked and crusted at the bottom like a good Paella should be. Â This is one of the redeeming dishes of the restaurant. Â  Tried the Taragon Chicken, and the chicken was moist and flavorful. Â Not my type of dish, but it was very good. Â The crispy potatoes were a bit too over powering for my taste, but it might have been necessary to balance the flavor of the chicken. Â I heard that was the dish reviewed by NYT, but honestly from what I heard and tried the Paella and charred beef were probably better choices. Â  I had the cheese cake, underwhelming. Â  The ambience and service really makes this place and people are very helpful. Â It was my friends bday, and they were nice to bring out some complimentary sherry with biscotti like thin strips. Â Our server showed us our bottle of wine, and then walked away with it and opened it. Â Then he returned and poured out our wine Â That was a very weird experience where I am used to having someone uncork the bottle at our table and pouring the wine directly in to our glasses. Â  Honestly, I expected more from the restaurant. People seem to effected by the NYT review that they almost want to love everything about the food there and are not objective in my opinion. Â But everyone's taste is different, so its very had to put your finger on if its more of the good reviews or varied taste. Â  Â I think part of being a great chef is making tasty food that people will enjoy. Â But I find the amount of salt in the food to be absolutely ridiculous. Â I get nutritional facts at Mcdonalds, Id like some nutritional facts at this restaurant to objectively look at just how much salt is in these dishes. Â  I was very pleased by my visit and pleasantly surprised by certain parts of my dining experience. Â My suggestions is to try the place. Â  If you are a vegetarian, you should have quite a few choices on the menu. Â  ENJOY p.s. did I say the food was salty? Â :)
You're an idiot if you think this is anything above 2 star pizza Anyone who rates this 4 or 5 stars is from Kansas

this is officially one of my favorite brunch places! with $4 mimosas and $5 huge bloody marys that come in mason jars, this place wont disappoint. I came in a group of 4 after Halloween night so we were ready to get re-charged with some good food. I ordered the buttermilk pancakes which were perfect and my husband got a juicy burger with fries. The fries were ok but the burger did not disappoint! Further, the seating was amazing for a day like this - the seats were the most comfiest ever and the wait even sat with us to discuss our day and Halloween in general. Overall a cute spot and perfect for a group of friends on a Saturday afternoon
Phenomenal. Our waitress was a sweet heart. Steak and Salmon dishes are my fave. No complaints.

I am a huge fan of macarons! It is not only delicious, it is crafted in such a delicate and elegant way. Laduree is definitely a special gem. I waited outside in the cold for almost 90 minutes just to get my hands on these babies. I got them in 2 sets of 6. (which means 2 boxes, each had 6 macarons) I chose to get them in the fancy boxes so I can give them as gifts when I head back to my sunny California. The texture and the cream was perfect. They also had limited edition holiday flavors, which is always exciting for those who enjoy the exquisite spices. Whether you buy Â a dozen or just one everyone gets a fancy bag. I really don't understand those who stand in the long line just to get 1 or 2. The trade-off isn't that great. Might as buy a bunch to share! I recommend going in the morning where there isn't a wait! Otherwise bring a scarf or a boo to cuddle with. It will be cold!

Peaches totally ruled. We went for brunch and I was really happy with everything. We sat in the cute patio area and enjoyed some tasty drinks (I got the Brownstone punch and it definitely got me brunch-drunk). The shrimp & grits were super creamy and rich, maybe a bit too creamy, but the mushrooms & shrimp were absolutely delicious. We also had the short rib hash which was even more amazing. The flavors were perfectly balanced and the eggs were poached just right. The indoors seems like it's a large echoey space that might get a bit loud, but if you can sit outside and bask in the brownstones, it's a pretty great spot. I spotted the french toast on the way out, and think I'm going to have to make it back for that. I'm not crazy about Smoke Joint in Ft Greene so I wasn't sure I'd love Peaches, but it was totally worth the trek.
