Love the decor in this spot. It has a ncie rustic feel to it. And their presenation of their food is pretty nice. Â Though their food is pretty good for what it is. They could stand to change their prosciutto croque madame. adding a cheese just made it too salty. Â They definitely needed to counterbalance the saltiness of the prosciutto. Â But i did enjoy their small apps that came before the main course. Â It was a nice brunch experience.

OMG, came here this past weekend holiday and I have to say that I am now craving their banh mi's. Â I think they put crack in it or something cause it's so addicting!!! The beef bulgogi is hands down the best banh mi everrrr! And I can't go without their Frozen Vietnamese Coffee Mocha. Â Too damn gooood! My tummy is happy now that there is a banh mi shop in queens. Yay for JoJu!

My "Cuban" test is the appetizers. If you can't get these right, you don't deserve to have your main dishes tried. Delivery was super quick and the guy was very nice. Prices are cheap, so no complaints there. Here's what I had: Ham croqueta: Tasty, no complaints. Papa rellena: Didn't really care for it. Something about the taste that wasn't right, and I personally don't believe olives belong in these, as much as I love them! And raisins, no, definitely not! I'm not one of those Cubans who like raisins in their picadillo. Beef empanada: No, Uh-uh, no way. This sucks. Yuca croqueta: Greasy, oil oozing, yuckiness. They sent a bunch of green sauce on the side, which at first is garlic-y and quite tasty, but then gets spicy REAL quick. It reminds me of the spicy mojo at Peruvian joints. The sauce was too spicy (and I love spicy), it took away from the food because it lingered on your tongue. A little variety would have been nice for this "sampler". This place falls flat and not worth another visit by me. Another failed attempt at finding good and affordable Cuban food in Manhattan!

Best brisket and honey cornbread in Brooklyn--- so far--*wink* wink* Â  True to the roots of BBQ, this is a self serve spot where you line up and order by the pound. Â Butcher paper, a scale and a spot for the sides. Â Some side sauces, plastic untensils. Â But its no frills when it comes to the meats. Â Really juicy brisket, dry rubbed ribs, spicy pulled pork and maybe on occasion cheese filled pork sausages.

GREAT seafood. I personally am not a fan of oysters, so while my friends took advantage of the red white and blue special ($8 for 6 oysters and a drink), I opted for the clam chowder and the twin tar tar. The chowder was good, but the tar tars (tuna and salmon) were amazing. The portion was very large, and served with kettle cooked chips to eat it with. I will definitely be back to sample some other seafood dishes.

Incredible food and a festive atmosphere. Without a doubt one of the best meals I have had in a long time. Every dish was delicious and the menu caters to all tastes. Special mention to the cavatelli which was the standout. The standard of service was also impeccable which just added to the great experience! Looking forward to becoming a regular.
tiramisu ice cream regular slice is thin & awesome as hell. get a pie!

This place is pretty solid and fairly priced. We ordered the foie gras sushi to start with. Each piece is $5 - pretty steep but the foie was well seared and of really good quality. There was too much sauce on top though, it was really sweet and overpowering, especially with the tofu inari skin which is also sweet. 4 of us shared 2 hot pots - one with spicy broth and one with the clear white broth. The red spicy broth was delicious, but didn't have that much meat in it. The chives were really good and fresh and it was overall a hearty meal. The one with the clear white broth had intestines in it, which i LOVE but the ones here were too chewy and tough. The broth was also extremely salty. I'd probably return if I were in a hot pot mood - the ingredients are mostly really fresh. i'd love to try some of the other menu items as well. Service was very nice but slow at times

I have no nits to pick with Bianca - it lived up to the hype. We got drinks at Von next door while we waited for everyone to arrive and for our table to be ready - and the host came and got us at the bar when it was. I might not expect he'd do this kind of above-and-beyond on a friday / saturday, but it was still a moderately busy thursday, so...kudos. For apps we got a portabella special, the gnocco frito and the lasagnette. All excellent, highlight was the portabellas, lowlight (?) was the lasagnette. I got the Gramigna, which was also excellent. I sampled the Balsamic Chicken (good but forgetable) and the Calamari, which was the best dish of the night. Throw in a couple of bottles of nicely priced wine, and it was quite a night. We hung out and talked well after the bill was paid (no one was waiting, it was late), and closed the place down - no one asked us to leave or anything. Attentive service, expensive, but worth it. Cash only.

What a great find! My husband and I just moved into the area and went here for our anniversary. The atmosphere is lovely and the service is out of this world! Wait staff is very attentive, even re-folded my napkin at my seat when I got up to go to the bathroom. Food is excellent all around, only complaint is that the list of specials is outrageously long, so long that you forget what they started with! But amazing all around, we will definitely be back!

This used to be my favorite brunch place in the city but I've been away for a year and the prices seem to have shot up (or is that my budget has gone way down?). Â MInus -1 star for the expensiveness in the middle of a recession. Otherwise one of the best places for brunch in the city--if you don't mind waiting a little bit (no reservations). Â I took a friend here when she was visiting and she said it was hands-down the best pancakes she'd ever had. Â I'm a fan of the eggs benny and whatever they have on special is always awesome, another one of my fellow bitches who brunch ordered this duck hash thing that was drool-inducing from the other tables. Â  And the pie...oh the pie. Â Wear stretchy pants. Â Trust.
Hands down, best pancakes I've ever had. Probably has something to do with using cake flour and lots of butter....but who cares! Great coffee too.

Meh... wasn't impressed at all. Soup tasted a bit like chlorine (wash your dishes more thoroughly please), portions were measly, and the noodles REALLY did not live up to their hype--too soft, not elastic enough.
Cauliflower with yellow rice Kabob That green sauce YUMZ

I loved that they heavily favored whiskey, and I'm a sucker for lovely stationary. Their fantastic menu is printed in the vintage style - though aside from that, there wasn't much else in theme. They have some really unusual cocktails, and though I was wary of the Green Monster, definitely give it a try despite the herby chartreuse and green tea mixed in. Other than the $1 oysters and wings during happy hour, I wouldn't come here for food. We just got the Ploughman's platter, which is a decent amount for two people, if you want to save room for all the yummy alcohol. It is a bit smaller, and I can't imagine a group of more than five sitting comfortably here.

I came here for dinner and it was great. Very intimate and cozy. The staff was attentive and the food was awesome. I recommend the roasted giannone chicken and the hazelnut panna cotta for desert. Great date spot!

Just got a quick take out lunch from Margon. Cuban Sandwich with everything on it was delicious. Rice and Beans with Plantains as well. 9 bucks. Really can't beat that around this area. Can't wait to try other sandwiches and plates. Definitely better than Sophies and seems to be a lot fresher. Will update after trying the other goods soon!

I love french food but the brunch we had is basically american. My friend had to go to work afterwards so we didn't drink but probably the wines are more french than the food. The four stars is for the decoration and the company of my friend :)
I heard its good so i went with my friend. although the price is cheap, food tasted bad.

I came here for brunch with two others and we were informed about the long wait but agreed to wait and sat on a little bench in front. It was probably one of the 1st really hot days of the season and I asked for a glass of water and recieved an ice cold glass. That was the only positive interaction had for the day. Finally we were sat and our server announced that one of the dishes was unavailable. NP because no one in my party wanted it anyway. So we place our orders and she comes back 5 minutes later to tell me they are out of the salmon hash that I wanted to try. I get salmon scrambled eggs instead. Drinks come out slowly. Table beside us gets sat. We get coffee and cocktails and we wait. The table beside us gets their food. Hmm... OK maybe what we ordered takes a bit longer. They proceed to finish their meal. I start fishing the olives out of my bloody mary to get something in my stomach, because at this point, we are all starving. Our server stays way across the room from us and goes so far as to come over to the table beside us and keep her back to us. We try to get her attention and she averts her eyes and stares off into space. We flag down someone else "she looks at us like we are bothering her" and ask can they send her over. After more waiting, someone brings us water. Then by the time the drinks are completely watered down and half finished out comes the scrambled eggs. No explanation or "sorry for the delay" All it would have taken was a "hey there's a delay in the kitchen, we're working as fast we can" To wait over 30 minutes for eggs and pancakes and to be completely ignored is unacceptable. The food was good as well as the coffee. However with so MANY options for brunch in Brooklyn or NYC in general. I wouldn't return or suggest this place to anyone.

A new restaurant in Greenpoint that is actually new! Despite chef's resume including such local establishments as Diner and Reynards, you won't find a burger or fries anywhere on this menu. Not your typical Williamsburg fare. Refreshing and delicious. In addition, there is PLENTY of space, which is a bonus for those with infants or children.

This place is legitimately addicting! I've grown up eating Banh Mi sandwiches my entire life from NY and Cali, but this place is no joke when it says "modern" Viet sandwiches under their name. --Joju Monster: Definitely my favorite. A banh mi with BBQ pork and fried egg = protein heaven. --Kakuni Pork Belly: Pretty good, only gripe was that my piece was a bit too fatty. --Loaded Banh Mi Fries: You're either not hungry or a fool if you don't get the fries with banh mi toppings or a fried egg on top. --Giant menu of cheap drinks! They even offer a frozen Viet iced coffee! BUT, if you love coffee flavored foods/drinks...Joju offers COFFEE JELLY as a drink topping! Definitely an appreciated change up from tapioca for your bubble tea. Tip: The Yelp check in for a free Thai iced tea also requires you to get the Joju Monster and Loaded Banh Mi fries! Not complaining though!

I'd like to start by saying I will definitely be back here. Â  We came for brunch on Saturday morning. Â I ordered the Latin Breakfast with fried eggs. Â It was great. Â  Drink wise, I had the michaleda and he had a chipotle marg which was clearly made with canned pineapple so not great. Savior ! Big shout out to Marcos, the Chihuahua born and bred chef at my work- a true taqueria miner, and partner in my long commiseration of the availability of good New York Mexican food, who put me onto Taqueria Lower East Side in the first place (though he had NO idea what the address was, only a rough description of what was nearby). This place is about as close to the Californian boarder as it gets- excellent tacos (barbacoa in particular), great tortilla soup, awesome rice & beans, and its all quite cheap as well! They also bring FREE CHIPS to your table- you're likely thinking 'huh, so what? who cares about free chips?' Most Mexican restaurants in the city charge upwards of $6 for chips and salsa, something almost unheard of in every other state of the union. Let's review- recommended by a Mexican chef longing for the rich flavors and nostalgia of his past (this means more to me than you, likely), food great (likely the best I've had in NYC, definitely the best on the basis of consistency), and they do the free chip thing (a standard throughout the US that is somehow lost on NYC). Add the fact that drinks are very reasonably priced, especially considering the area-- I prefer an ice cold Bohemia. *If you're tired of reading, skip to this point* This review is very long and boring, in summary: If you are a true fan of Mexican food- and more specifically tacos, and have enjoyed its flavors in Mexico, East L.A., San Diego, etc, and feel like NYC is a desert for these flavors-- you will likely find solace here.
Delciious food - knowledgeable waitress- very friendly atmosphere.
great wraps,very tasty! took the Veggie one and was really great! nice place to grab a quick lunch!

Full setu (set menu) served to you in minutes. Not a place for that two hour date. But I love it. Problem is I want to eat here every night.

Went there for dinner after years of blissfully ignoring this spot. Â Don't know what took so long; had a great meal. Â If you want to have a nice dinner in the slope, Stone Park should be at the top of your list. Â Fantastic.

I loved this place! Â I did come after the usual lunchtime rush has had its fill, so I really can't say how they hold up under pressure, though... The pizza itself was fantastic, although they could have been a little more generous with the toppings, considering the price and their reputation. My girlfriends and I hardly get together, but when we do, we love exploring and trying good food. Traif has been on my radar for awhile and as my good friend May L. suggested - we need to get more people to go so we can try more dishes. That's exactly what we did. All 7 of us. There was a little snafu in the beginning with the water, but after that cleared up, our glasses were constantly being filled. The staff was also extremely helpful and friendly. Can't wait to go back and order a la carte.

This is a I-eat-here-once-a-week-because-I-live-down-the-Â­street-and-it's-super-cheap kind of place and not a holy-crap-this-tastes-amazing kind of place... - The fried dumplings aren't great; ours didn't have fried enough skin and the meat wasn't flavorful. - The boiled dumplings are doable once you douse them in a lot of soy sauce. - The hot and sour soup was ok; there were some weird chunks of stuff I had to spit out. - The sesame pancake was pretty good, though the outside wasn't as flaky as I wished it was. I came here solely for their breakfast Â selection as I came here before and had lunch. Ordered Middle Eastern Eggs and Buttermilk Pancake with berries. They were both delicious dishes. I hate to have to write this review but after my experience last night I'm left with no choice. Note: this is not a review of the food. i like how you've re-decorated the Old Devil Moon space, but if you're going to take over a spot so sacred, make sure you do it 150% PROS: fresh, seasonal ingredients fantastic wine sensational, juicy and delicious chicken way to incorporate fried chicken with poached egg on a sandwich CONS: i am still hungry (even after appetizers and entrees) you served $13 chicken with a slice of lemon and no sides whatsoever; i would have appreciated at least a bit of parsley the waitstaff was disorganized. i stood for 5 minutes until someone asked if i wanted to sit, i had four different waiters, and the "main waitress" was very inattentive and obviously disinterested. the brunch menu piques my interest; however, with such reliable, delicious options right around corner (Westville, Redhead), this Shark just might need another bite to be sure...

I never experienced Do or Dine prior to the critical acclaim from major daily publications or the attention derived from the whole "ZOMG, THE CHEF IS SO CUTE AND ON FOOD NETWORK!!!11!". Perhaps it used to be more low key or more personable, or perhaps it used to just be "better" in some difficult to quantify way. I respect those opinions, but my take is that this place is still a load of fun to visit and offers really great food for a totally reasonable price. I suspect, given the increased attention this place has received over the past year or so, that most people considering a meal here already kind of know what to expect. But, if not, Do or Dine is adventurous dining. It's the type of food that is created when talented people begin to disregard all the staid and long-standing rules and traditions of owning and operating a restaurant. The entrance to Do or Dine is the massive and intensely yellow awning that adorned the Indian restaurant that preceded Do or Dine. The only signage indicating that you've arrived at Do or Dine is spray painted lettering just above the door that is all but invisible until you are right at the door. The interior is not large and once you've stepped in the front door, you can see basically the entire restaurant. But, there is space for groups up to 8 or so I would guess. During the warmer months, Do or Dine has a sizable outdoor area behind the restaurant that is also good for groups. Service has been consistently good for me at Do or Dine. I know this is one area that's been criticized of late, so perhaps it is worse in comparison to the early days of this establishment. But, the waitstaff has been knowledgeable, friendly, and helpful on my trips and I don't ask much more than that really. In terms of food, there's not much that isn't worth trying. The Dr. Pepper frog's legs were a little too sweet and Dr Pepper-y for me, but that's the only menu item that hasn't really appealed to me in my visits. The foie gras donuts are better than you expect them to be and the Chicken and Woffals is also excellent. I'm not a big fan of tartare, but the steak tartare at Do or Dine is a MUST. Perfectly chopped raw beef, exceptionally seasoned and served with toast points and an espresso sauce. In terms of food, your best bet is to go with a group, get a bunch of different things and just share. The dishes at Do or Dine are perfect for sharing around the table and you'll want to sample as much as possible because it's all good. It isn't the best food you'll ever have, but the combination of exceptional preparation, playful concept, and great ingredients makes it well worth giving Do or Dine a shot. All of what I've mentioned would be sufficient to recommend Do or Dine, but the fact that all of this is priced so well makes it all the more attractive. Our last trip was a group of 5 people. We all drank beer, had a few shots, and a few cocktails among us, ordered a boatload of food, and ended up with a bill of about $230 if I remember correctly. Had we been in a comparable restaurant, I'm confident that we would have spent at least $350 on our meal. A dinner for two could be had here and easily come in under $100 depending on drinks. So, to wrap up this massive wall of text, open your mind to some new culinary experiences and give Do or Dine a shot. Maybe it was better in the beginning but that doesn't mean it's not still great.

despite no seating i am giving this place 5 stars amazing tortillas all the fillings are fresh and wonderfully flavored i crave tacos from this place and in my half dozen experiences here i have never been let down i only wish they had an restaurant in LES closer to home

Â Maybe it's the extremely high Yelp reviews that draw people here (this is definitely one of the reasons I visited). outdoor movies in the summer!

We had a fabulous cpl of hrs casually eating drinking and chatting on our last nt in NYC. The atmosphere was a perfect respite from the noise and rain, service was superb and the food was great and well priced. Wld def recommend this to anyone looking for a nice casual meal in great surrounds.

These frites remind me of my favorite Belgian hamburger stand in Paris, Les Frites Bruxelles. It forces you to have the fries as a meal, not that I'm complaining. I stop by here whenever I'm getting my hair cut a few blocks away and snack on the fries while waiting for my appointment. Going back for my second time to Walters in almost two years I was horrified. Â My first time was great. Â This time a different story. Â First off the oysters were warm. Â Bad sign. Â The name, the menu, the big TV that will still play sports (even though this venue is far far away from a sports bar) and the knowledgeable servers all embody what I would want from a place to hangout. I wish I could give this place 2.5 stars. They don't really deserve 3. We ate there last night. Sort of bland but okay food. I'd rather go to mom and pop's, but next time, I'll hit Chipotle.
The squash soup is souperb!

If you crave Mexican, there is only one place to go. The tacos here are my favorite, they just have the best flavor. My husband loves the steak burrito. The Sangria is great as well. I have never had a bad meal here. Very comfortable atmosphere, good service too!

There's a reason why there is always such a long line at this Grimaldi's location in Brooklyn. Â There are only a few pizza joints that I would give a 5 rating too and this is one of them. Â It's definitely worth the try if you don't mind the wait. This was very very good. The place is crowded but the food is spectacular. The French onion soup was the only part of the meal I thought was a bit lacking -- too much cheese so it was impossible to eat without a long string of cheese stretching inelegantly from your spoon/mouth to the bowl. Not a dish you want to eat on a date. And it was just bland, somehow--rubbery cheese without enough beef broth/onion taste. However, it was warm and comforting on such a blustery winter day. The butternut squash and ricotta agnolotti (available as either an appetizer or an entree for lunch) were AMAZING. They were swimming in butter and sprinkled with some herbs and pumpkin seeds, which added a crunch that contrasted with the soft, almost sweet filling. SO good. My friend had the roasted lamb sandwich, and the bite I had of it was also extremely good. There was a spicy mayonnaise or something within, along with pieces of lamb and some grilled zucchini (I think). The bread was very good, soft and not stale or crunchy. I only wish I'd had room for dessert...but alas, next time.
I love the vibe, so nostalgic with collectibles all over the restaurant. Friendly staff, good food, BYOB!

Creative menu but flavor falls short. The disco ball distracts you from the sticky tabletops and poorly trimmed lamb. Shared 7 dishes. Tartare and deviled eggs were the best of the night. Lamb was really gamey and too fatty. Took it home, trimmed it and made a damn good fried rice the next day. The veggie dumpling nachos were clever but I expected more. Wish they would focus on amping up their food game and work on the basic customer comforts like AC and cleanliness. I am not a clean freak. I proudly eat at Grade B and Grade Pending places as long as the food is worth it. But they are charging enough to keep the servers from sweating into the food and to buy some cleaning products. Highlight of the meal? Discovering a truth about myself - I like graffiti in bars but not restaurants. Would go back for drinks in the garden. Not much else.

I am a huge Pho guy so I have been to a number of different places across the city and New Jersey. Â Saigon Shack was just okay, nothing special. Â First, its pretty small but the food comes out very quickly. Â I think it took about 10 minutes for our food to come out. Â However, I am used to a more authentic bowl of pho. Â I'm sure the other food is great but I wouldnt come back here just to get a bowl of pho.
The renovation was worth the wait; more space, nice decor and price remains very reasonable. The garden is just a wonderful addition. But... can't make too much noise coz the neighbors will complain.
Must try: Lobster soup from the appetizer. Â Love it. Scallops (6) from the entree. My friend said the lobster roll is good.

Comfort food to the max!! Â  If you want to escape NYC for a moment and enjoy some good comfort food, come here! My friend ordered the Jambalaya and I had the pulled pork sandwich. Â The jalapeno cornbread was a little too dry for my liking and I couldn't taste the jalapeno at all. Â But my friend enjoyed it and said it was "oddly addictive." Â  Then I got to my meal. Â Not only was the sandwich itself gargantuan but they were more than generous with their sweet potato fries. Â The whole meal was outrageously delicious. Â The pulled pork was juicy and well seasoned. Â The sandwich was so big I didn't think I could eat it by picking it up so I took off the top bun and started off with the meat inside. Â Warning: Â once you start it will take all your self-control to stop eating! Â I thought I would try to use some self-control and so I placed the top bun back on top of half the pulled pork and half the fries and asked for it to go. Â Who was I kidding? Â 30 minutes later, as I was sitting down to write a paper, I was already digging into the leftovers and finished it off. Â Although the fries could have been a little bit crispier, this meal really hit the spot on a chilly October night.
so gooood
I'm pretty much all about any place that has a breakfast sandwich with garlic aioli on it, and deep friend macaroni and cheese balls with ranch. In my mouth. Please. Now.

Â  The portions are really big, which means bigger plates, which should also mean bigger tables...but it's not the case. tables are pretty small. I had this place bookmarked for what felt like years. I had heard so much about it from friends, family, etc and so when I finally made it back out to NYC I had to check it out. Vodka pizza, butternut squash ravioli, beet salad, lamb pasta, meatballs, all delicious! We could hardly move after eating but the chocolate chip bread pudding called our name at the end and also didn't disappoint. Not to mention the total bill was beyond reasonable.

I read that the wait could be lengthy, so I made my reservation the day before. I loved it! I don't really like Chinese food... normally. We waited for about 20 mins for a table for three for lunch on a Monday We got the crab and pork soup dumplings and scallion pancakes. Ridiculously delicious and the family style serving is so Italian and perfect. Loved the service, and is a great spot to go to before a show! It can't be a regular thing, but that is what makes it all the more special.

Delicious! Last week, an enticing offer of $1 oysters and $6 glasses of champagne drew me in. Hands down the best empanadas spot. Call in your order because they are made fresh and the wait is annoying. Make sure you try the "platano maduro" ( sweet plantain)..

I could eat falafel and hummus on a daily basis, easily. This small shop is tucked away on a little side street and you would almost never know it's there unless someone told you or it popped up on Yelp. I ordered a whole wheat pita with falafel, hummus, green sauce and tahini. It disappeared very quickly. There's a counter by the window but not much else. When it gets cold out, I'm not sure where I would eat. Other than the size (which actually makes it more charming), I would definitely recommend eating here.

I love Red Cat! I had very high expectations after reading the NY Times review and through word of mouth. Red Cat lived up to its hype! The room had a real Brooklyn pub feel which may not be great for a romantic evening but worked for a birthday celebration. Our waiter was casual but attentive. The food was amazing. The Zucchini appetizer was the hit of the evening. A must try!

Had the tasting menu and it was fantsastic! The porcini flan was served with crab and had a nice truffle flavor, my husband had the chilled oysters with caviar, which was better than mine! We both ordered the wild salmon that had a nice amaranth seed crust, I cant even begin to describe how delicisou this was! Great food experience! To taste on the menu: - starters: (1) soup dumplings & (2) lobster. - main course: the famous chicken!! Food was delicious and service with a smile. Drinks: they have descend red wine but... Taste their homemade Jameson-Banana. Delicious!!!!! Strongly recommended!

First off I just want to say that my wife and I were really enjoying ourselves here and this would have been a five star review if it wasn't for the very unprofessional manager. Â We went on Saturday and after reading some reviews about how busy this place gets on the weekends we figured we had better get there early. Â We were there around 5 pm and we pretty much had the place to ourselves. Â The restaurant is very cute and cozy and the menu looked great. Â We ordered the calamari to start and then I had the stuffed pepper and my wife got empanadas for our main course. Â The calamari was good. Â They use a cornmeal crust which we really enjoyed but the dish was a little dry. Â After finishing our appetizer and waiting a while for our main course we asked our waitress to check on our food and she apologized for the wait and went to tell the manager that we had been waiting. Eating Cuban food my whole life and growing up in Miami, I can say this place is hands down the most authentic Cuban place in NYC. While there are some pricey places in Manhattan, and taste wise they don't disappoint, they don't have the feel from Rincon Criollo. Big plates, big family, lots of love, just like a Cuban restaurant should be! And best of all, they're run by Cubans!! It might not seem important to non-Latinos to have a Domican person (just as an example, I'm not picking on Dominicans!) run a Cuban restaurant, but it's pretty much the same as a Chinese person running a Japanese Sushi place. The taste is not authentic, it's a fusion, and while that's not all that bad, for someone looking for a taste of Cuba or Miami, a place like this is gold! Â  The wait staff is always super sweet and helpful, the food is delicious, and I always make sure I go there when I need a taste of my old home. My recommendations is the Vaca Frita and Mamey milkshake!

The food here is phenomenal- the most authentic Mexican food that I've had, eating myself thru every restaurant in NYC. We've never been disappointed with the food; however, the service was horrible recently. Service time was an an hour to receive our appetizer and over 20 minutes to obtain our check. The growing restaurant needs to hire proactive staff ASAP.

I have not yet been to this newer BCD, only to the older one, but because going there was like a ritual I felt like I needed to post a review. Coming from Florida, I loved this place because I never had access to quality Korean food, so to me this placed tasted like gold. I pretty much ordered the Kalbi and Korean BBQ every time (#1 and #3). We'd come here every weekend after a long night of going out since it's open 24 hours, and I'd bring ALL my guests here. Â But of course if you're not Korean, you get crappier service and more stoic facial expressions, but oh well. I'm willing to forgive them a little for their tender juicy meats. Luckily I also had a Korean roommate who'd usually be with me and could communicate to them in Korean.

This place was packed at 6pm on a Thursday evening! we lucked out and walked in at the right time and got two seats at the middle bar like area right away, which was great since we had to do a quick dinner before heading to our broadway show. Â  We ordered the pork hirata buns as a appetizer, which was standard, was not a big fan of the mayo, probably should have asked for less or no mayo if I had known it would have been a lot. I ordered the spicer ramen of Karak-men with an egg added and my husband got the Akamaru Modern with an egg as well. Â  Ramen was good, definite must try. Would I come back again? Most likely but I would probably want to try other places like Momofuku noodle bar to compare

Missing that west coast food truck gathering? This collection of temporary pop-up food stands will satisfy your longing (assuming it's not the gasoline smell you desire). beautiful

We went again on Friday night. Had the FG&J (Foie Gras and Jelly Sandwich). It was unbelievable!! For dinner I had the Burger and it was perfect. The bread was just the right size, not too big as to overpower the burger. I had the sweet potato fries as well and they were delicious. Its going to be a long week working off those dishes!

I always get the chicken/lamb over rice. I still can't comprehend how freaking good this is. Â This is probably one of my favorite places to eat. Â I always have to eat here anytime i am in town. Halal Cart is the best!!!!!!!!!!!!!

So delish! Even though you have to wait about an hr to get seated for brunch it was well worth it. My bf was getting cranky but then after trying the food he did say one word after:) Tomatoe soup is amazing!

This is where my office decided to go for a holiday lunch. I am not Greek but it's like I was in past life, as I love me some Greek food. Is this the quintessential NY slice? Â Does this put to shame all who have slathered sauce and cheese onto dough inside a hot oven? NOPE! Â but its not bad either We got the pepperoni square and a Grandma slice. Â Both were good, but not as awesome as some might think. Â I did not immediately return home and compose a symphony or recite sonnets to praise the culinary gods of pizza. If I ever recite sonnets, I either need coffee badly, or I've had too much coffee.
