The pricing has actually went up drastically, and their portions are medium sized. Their food is very delicious (but has a LOT of MSG if you're going for noodle soup) Definitely recommend to try their marinated duck, their seafood guo tiu and their curry mei fun!

I just had to stop by this place while hunting for food place in NYC as I've heard so much about it (not to mention those chase commercials that play nonstop) but I was pretty disappointed. I was recommended the classic beef meatballs with the tomato sauce and for $7 for 4 meatballs that could not be mixed or matched.. it was over-priced and not worth it. Â The meatballs were hardly extraordinary. Â I probably would have found the same satisfaction eating the meatballs from a chef boyardi can. Â I love meatballs, but I think I'm just going to have to stick with some good ol swedish meatballs at ikea.

A truly phenomenal and fortuitous find. While in town with my family of displaced New Yorkers, we were stumbling through lower manhattan in the cold searching for a warm drink with a spot of whiskey. What we found was a warm and inviting establishment with a delicious Irish coffee and a spicy cider-like concoction. Would certainly return.

I loved it. I love Ootoya to death. Waited in line for about 45 minutes but was so worth it. Wanted to sit inside but couldn't wait any longer and took the bar. Bar seating was still nice. tofu salad was HUGE!!! Every ingredient in it was amazing. Loved the bonito flakes in it. Tofu was so soft. The sauce it came with was so flavorful. Definitely recommend this appetizer that was prepared quickly. Ordered the Salmon Saikyo has my entree and loved it. Got it in the set, which came with steamed egg custard, my absolute favorite. The custard was perfect. The saikyo was tender and prepared just right. Food here is so light, authentic, and natural--essence of Japanese cuisine. Next time I'll try the rice dishes. So many people around me ordered them. The servings are huge and they look and smell so good. Such good food display. The best part was dessert. OH MY GOD. THE DESSERT WAS SO AUTHENTIC AND DELICIOUS. Tried two different ones. The mochi was the SOFTEST mochi I've ever had. The jelly sugar was concentrated yet not overpowering. The green tea ice cream was even better than ciao bella's. The sweet rice cake took me to another world. Ugh oh my god everything about the dessert was just heavenly and the best part was that they were so cheap! $6-$8 each and so good I'd wait in line another hour for a bite of another one. Will be here ALL THE TIME since I live two blocks away. ONE OF THE BEST PLACES IN NYC!

Love this place! Had a really, really great experience here with some of the best casual service I've had in ages. It was a Sunday night so not too busy. Nice atmosphere. Very New England seaside style interior. White, clean, lots of natural wood. Both the bartender and server were very friendly. We took a look at the placard menu and placed our order. I had the Crab Cake sandwich and my friend ordered the Lobster salad. YUM! Both of them were exceptionally good. Most everything on the menu looked delicious. We had a really great time chumming it up with the server and bartender. They offered us a "Pickle Back" on the house. Which neither of us were aware of. It's a shot of Whiskey backed with pickle juice. A Brooklyn staple, we were told. This is now added to my short list of neighborhood haunts.

Mediterranean/Middle Eastern flair. The decor is really nice. There is an outdoor patio in the back that has good shade coverage during the day. The food is absolutely delicious. They bring a warm, fluffy, oiled and seasoned loaf of bread with a small side of olives for the table. I got the green shakshuka, which was the perfect size. My friend loved her eggs benedict. If they have the wild berry champagne cocktail, get that with your brunch. It's delicious. For the quality, amount of food, and the fact that it's the UWS, it's well-priced. I will be back.

Really cozy, cute place with great food and service. Went to Ichabod's on a cold, rainy night and it was perfect - so cute and comfortable. Â The small plates were delicious - squash dumplings, chicken liver pate, shishito peppers and a special mac and cheese with truffle oil and mushrooms were all excellent. We weren't that hunger so we didn't have large plates or dessert but I can't wait to go back and try that sundae! Wines by the glass were reasonable and good. Overall a great neighborhood place - I just wish it was in my neighborhood!

I've tried the food several times now - it's rather good. The Five Leaves Burger is a feast. The optional truffle fries have a taste that's too intense for me, and quite frankly have a weird smell. Wait time for food is, on average, very high. I never got away with less than 30 minutes. The big update is, however, Five Leaves now takes Visa and MasterCard... Shocking, I know.
Now this is what I'm talking about.... Yummy yummy yummy,... juicy . fresh and fantastic...... worth waiting in line for. and the Â hot sauce is actually hot!!!!!!

Discovered this place last summer. Â Their fried chicken and biscuits are very good. Â I was sold. Â Not too pricey and lovely outdoor area in warm weather. Â (Yes it overlooks the FDR but just over that is the East river and a lovely view of Brooklyn). I recently went back for brunch and it was very affordable and delish. Â The portions are a good size, not too much but enough to satisfy. Â The staff are always attentive and welcoming. Â I have been a few times by myself and they always make an effort to be engaging and friendly. Perfect for a meal in an area that is lacking decent restaurants.

My friend told me about this restaurant a few weeks ago and told me it was delicious, cheap and generous on the portions. Â She was right. I was nervous about the size of the restaurant after reading some of the other reviews, but five of us met there at 8:30 pm on a Monday night and were able to get seated right away. Â And it didn't feel cramped at all, even with a full restaurant. Â Instead, we had a very homey, cozy experience in the dimly lit room. The Food (enjoyed family-style) (1 Appetizer) The Gnocco Fritto w/Stracchino Cheese was a great way to get the tummy wanting more. Â The puffy fried dough didn't feel or taste too greasy, and the cheese was a delicious gooey delight. (2 Pastas) Â The Gramigna con Salciccia e Peperoni was basically a hearty macaroni pasta with meat sauce. Their Lasagna is definitely one of a kind. I suppose it was the Bechamel that made it a thick, creamy goodness. If I ate any more than the little portion I took, I would've had a heart attack, but I would've died happy. (1 Seafood) The Fritto Misto was a bit of a giant fried mess. It came with a pile of fried zucchini on top, and you had to dig thru the pieces to find the fish and shrimp. The fried zucchini was like eating pure grease. That said, the rest of it didn't taste bad, but I think we could've done without this dish. I also think it should just be an appetizer, sans fried zucchini strips. (1 Meat) Â The Straccetti di Manzo was awesome. Thin slices of filet mignon cooked to perfection with rosemary. Just melted in your mouth. (3 Desserts) Â The Torta di Mela (chunky apple tart) reminded me of a really yummy Jewish Apple Cake. Â The Tortino di Cioccolata (Choc Mousse Cake with choc ganache) is just too much chocolate for my taste, but I'm sure chocolate fans would enjoy it. Â The Tiramisu was tasty as well. The Price Only $23 per person (including tip/tax) for having extremely satisfied, full bellies. I can't wait to go back again!!

I had high expectations for this pizza joint since everyone raves it as one of the best places for New York Style Pizza. I guess I'm not used the sogginess of a pizza, but I didn't like it that much. We ordered a large pizza with pepperoni, sausage, and mushroom. The pepperoni had a lot of flavor though. The seating arrangement was extremely tight. The person managing the seating squeezed as many people as possible in one long table. So, we're basically sitting next to a stranger and hearing their conversations. Yeah, not my cup of tea. Overall, we spent $24 (including tip) for pizza. If I'm going back to NYC, I'll try another pizza joint that doesn't require standing in line. We only waited 10 minutes, but it is ridiculous to read how people stand in line for 2+ hours.
The best pizza I've ever tasted. The ingredients are imported and you feel like you are there!
Nothing fantastic. But at least you could sit outside.

Not my kind of place to be honest. Loud music, shady people, too dark. Meh. The reason it gets 2 stars and not 1 is because of the $4 "Sportsman" special of a beer and a shot of whiskey. Outside closes at 11. When we were asked to move inside the staff member was an absolute asshole about it. Not really needed, we weren't being rude or obnoxious. I think these people take their hipster lifestyle to a whole new level here. Please get over yourselves.

Great food. Got the fried chicken. It was delish. My roomie got the steak and it was good. Nothing special. The food comes out when it is ready but there was a long wait between my roomie getting her steak and me getting my fried chicken ... Like 15 minutes.

I had the chance to share Catfish and French toast with my wife. The dishes served on the table beside ours were equally or more appetizing. A kitchen, services and place to repeat. Ifeoma was terrific, wonderful smile thanks again.
Ive been here so often I never check in. Good homemade food at a cheap price. The place is tiny. Just a lunch counter with stools. Like Thursday the best for their corned beef and cabbage.

Posto is some of the best pizza in the city. Â  Crust is paper thin and crispy. The sauce, cheese and toppings are always fresh and tasty. Â I've been frequenting their partner restaurant, Gruppo for some time now and was excited to check out Posto since I moved to the neighborhood. Â I was not disappointed. Â  Their lunchtime menu features a lot of great deals, I like the 2 plain slices and a soda for $5. Â  Not a bad deal (although Gruppo was the same for $4). Â  Their salads are also great. Â  I would rate it a couple notches below Gruppo because I felt the service was a little subpar. Â  But I will gladly deal with subpar service for some excellent pizza.

Such a unique place to have a great mix grill or grilled fish, the food is so tasty and the staff are so friendly, they have a great collection of appetizers as well and the bread is very great as well. Of course do not forget to check in and you get a glass of wine with any fish or grill ;)

Alta has a wonderful atmosphere and vibe. We went here on a semi whim since it was near the path station, and I was pleasantly surprised by the crowd.. We hovered the bar for seats (there was an hour wait otherwise!) and lucked out! The bartender already had red and white sangria lined up and down the bar, completely prepared for the masses to order it! We got one of each, and both were delicious (I personally like it with more fruit, but the flavor in the sangria was great on it's own! We ordered 4 tapas. All were a bit overpriced for tapas sized portions, but delicious nonetheless: - Scallops with acorn froth (it tasted like thanksgiving for scallops, mmm) - Shrimp and Chorizo (very well done with an avocado puree) - Steak tar tar (i think this was my favorite!) - Avocado stuffed with shrimp and something spicy (a close second to the tar tar) They were fast and delicious. I would recommend it if you have the $$ for it! They only take Amex or cash though, so come prepared!
I got delivery from this place. Â It was fast and the price was reasonable. Eel avacado Spicy Salmon Spicy Tuna All were pretty good. Â Will definitely order again.
Best Nutella crepes in the financial district. Great little spot to eat on a date. The service is great - very friendly wait staff.
Wonderful little bar with good people and atmosphere

I can't argue with the reviews about the food---it is spectacular!!! But I think success has gone to their head and now, at times, you can expect attitude--particularly when it's busy. From what was once noted for an atmosphere of warmth and charm, unique for an Â UES eatery, Heidi's has turned into a "Well this is how it is at Heidi's" tone. In the past you could expect to see owner's Chis and Heidi welcoming you and saying hello. But nowadays, all too often they are nowhere to be seen; and the staff doesn't express the same desire to please that was such a genuine part of Heidi's House's roots. As Heidi's grapples with success, I hope they can recapture the feeling and atmosphere they once had; Unfortunately, success on the UES does not depend on such things and being "Trendy" may be all that matters. Best of luck in the future

In a word: Overrated. The ambiance feels like a subdued, conservative 80's hotel. The service was rough around the edges; although our server was nice, he was nervous, seemed overworked and made a number of errors. He also talked to us like we were his school buddies. For this price point and type of dining, the service should be much more professional and precise. Â  The food is generally flavorful, the plating is enticing, but my prix fixe menu felt repetitious, and at times forced. The root vegetable appetizer was tasteless, but the foie gras truffle was perhaps the best and most innovative item on the menu. Juni is not on par with the finest restaurants in NYC for food, service, or ambiance. Â We did not enjoy our dinner enough to plan return visit.

Upon walking in, there was only one other couple in the place. You'd think the food would come quick, but NO!. After my gf and I ordered tacos and fajitas, there were 2 more groups of people that came in and they got their food before us. We figured they wanted to bring out everything at the same time so we patiently waited. But when we got our food, we realized that the extra time we waited wasn't for our benefit but it was the time they took to overcook our chicken and make it dry and barely edible. Plus, the gravy that came with the black beans was too thick. Pros - Well there are some but not enough to make me go back here. The presentation was good. Everything on the plate looked very nice but like I mentioned above not everything tasted that great. The avocado was great! but lets thank mother nature for that. The place was clean and the service was decent. Their bathroom was also clean. Service - The waitress we had seemed to have disappeared when we were close to done eating. But we didn't miss her one bit! The other girl was more than happy to take care of the rest of our requests.

Yup, still churning out the delicious small plates and strong sangria. I add to the list of recommendations the fried cheese-filled squash flowers, the bacon-wrapped dates, and the deviled eggs. The lighting is appropriately dim, and the double height ceiling with wraparound interior balcony make for a more spacious and airy feel.

Thought the pizza here was pretty good, though it didn't quite live up the hype. My favorite was the RPS, though the Beastmaster was good too! The crust is soft, almost like pita bread, which was not what I was expecting. Definitely worth trying this place out, though I don't think it's the final word in NYC pizza.

Omg. Chaka masala, tikka masala and the coconut naan and mango lassi are the best! We came here New Year's Day. It was very crowded and we had to wait 30 minutes very small location, maybe 10 tables. I saw that they had take out. We might try that next time. Service was wonderful, we always had our glasses full of water. The staff was very friendly and helpful. A must go if you are in NYC

It's so hard to determine a rating for this place. Â I absolutely loved it when it first opened but had lost interest after a while. Â The place is perfect for just getting together with friends for chit-chat. Â  The twelve-leaf oolong tea is good. Â It comes with the complete tea set. Â Would not recommend eating dinner or desserts here. Â I am surprise they still aren't good with desserts. Love their bathroom. Â I always enjoy clean and greatly designed bathrooms at restaurant. Â Who wants to go to a disgusting bathroom after eating?

It is hard to find this alley... But when you do, it will be woth the trouble. Because it is a really nice place- young crowd, nice music, a lot of bloody Mary's s Circling around ;) Good food also! But most imporatante: cool place! :) Don't miss this!

Jack may have some respect for his own wife Frida, but the way Jack treated my wife was absolutely shameful. Â  My wife (who is a whopping 8 months pregnant!!) and I stood for 20 minutes in front on the sidewalk and watched two pairs of people arrive after us, kiss and hug the owner, and be seated. Â Keep in mind, they do not take reservations and this is a first come, first serve joint. Â To seat friends in front of a pregnant woman on a summer evening in August is about as classy as a man who doesn't give up a seat on the subway. Â  Not very nice Jack! Eventually, Jack's friends will stop coming to his restaurant and he will need a customer base. Â Eventually, Jack's mediocre food (based on Yelp reviews - we never sat down after being treated so disrespectfully, but I hear the fries are the highlight of the menu, so...) will not be enough to sustain his business. Â Eventually, Jack will wish he treated his potential customers a little better. Â Good luck with that, Jack!
I love the quick lunch boxes. The buffet on the other hand has sometimes dishes that are lukewarm. I really don't like their kimchi. Once you found what you like it's a 4 or 5 star place though.

This is a fun spot, if you have an evening to kill and good solid shoes. Â The shoes are a must have, as you will likely be standing around waiting for quite awhile or walking over to a less crowded bar to beat out the 1 - 2 hour wait. Â  Having said that the interior decor and tucked away location are the real draws here. Â The decor is shabby chic hunting lodge NYC style. Â Pretty cool and a good atmosphere. Â  The food was pretty disappointing actually. Â The menu is typical farm to table type food and the prices are pretty reasonable, but the execution of the dishes is just disappointing. Â Food came out lukewarm and unsalted. I would expect better for the price. Â I had the pork shoulder, which was tough, unseasoned, and a bit dry. Â  The play on baked beans was nice, but not enough to salvage the dish. Â  I want to like this place more because it is cool and likely deserves another try.

I ate a homemade onigiri (see Marianna's review for a perfect definition). Freshly-prepared. Remarkable. My lunch was a small salad with smoked salmon and a spicy salmon and mayo onigiri ("You must really like salmon!"). The price was about $8. My salad was served in a charming wooden bowl and I believe the dressing was homemade and possibly mixed right in the bowl. Ashbox gets the fifth star when the regular coffee is better, or when I've tried the daily special. It was a chicken curry, Japanese-style, when I was there. It was popular. I'll go back. I am learning to love what I believe is everyday Japanese food (see Niko Niko on Wall Street).

So for a girls' night out my girl friends and I decided to come here for some Southern food and pickles. Honestly, I'm not much of a pickle person but I LOVE biscuits and I was really craving fried chicken so I decided, why not? The first thing we did was...order drinks of course! I got the Pink Picket Fence which had gin, freshly squeezed lemon juice, and something called Chambord? *shrugs shoulders. Anyways it was good but I was disappointed by the small glass it was provided in. Â I was expecting a littlee bit more for $11. Anyways we ordered 2 appetizers to share. Â The first dish was the fried pickles and they were amazing! Normally I find pickles to be too sour but frying them in batter really helps to balance out the flavors nicely. Honestly, I wish we just got 2 orders of the fried pickles instead of the 2nd appetizer we ordered which was the 4 types of pickles for $11 (carrots, string beans, jalapenos, and dill pickles). This was just way too tangy for me. Â My taste buds couldn't take eating more than a few. Â But like I said earlier, I'm not much of a pickles person anyways. Â  For an entrÃ©e I ordered the mushroom gravy smothered chicken. Â This was really good however, after awhile the creaminess was overwhelming. Â But don't get me wrong, I still enjoyed this dish. The buttermilk fried chicken was crispy on the outside and juicy & tender on the inside. It was perfect! And I'm a sucker for biscuits and this biscuit did not disappoint! This entrÃ©e also came with cheesy grits which were alright. Â But I think the creaminess of the mushroom gravy plus the cheesiness of the grits was just too rich for me. Oh one thing I'd like to add is that when I first picked up my napkin from my plate I found a dead fly under it! Ugh! I was just going to grab a plate from the empty seat next to me but the waiter (who seemed equally disgusted by the bug) quickly retrieved a clean plate straight from the dishwasher ( it was still nice & hot from having been through the hot wash!) So A+ for service! All in all, I'd give this place a 3.5 if I could. I'm not sure whether I'd come back because although the food was good, it did not suit my personal taste. Â However, if I were to come back I'd definitely order the fried pickles again!

This was an interesting experience. We came here for brunch, and they were "running late" and asked us to wait about 30 minutes until they were ready to serve us. Not having much else on our agenda, we decided to order some coffee and wait it out. They specialize in a super thin, crepe like consistancy flatbread. Sounds weird, but it was really good. Super rich, but good. The server was really friendly and super helpful in selecting our food. It was also great that he suggested we just get one at at time, because after one, we were stuffed. The place is SMALL and super crowded for dinner. It's almost impossible to get in and out of the tables, unless you're a child - there's literally about 4 inches between each table. This is not a place you go for privacy - this is a casual place to grab a quick, tasty bite.

As mentioned on their website, Terroir Tribeca is an elitist wine bar. But it is a wine person's wine bar, and certainly not for everyone. Nevertheless, Paul Greico's wine selections are exceptional, and have few peers among other wine bars in NYC. Working through a Terroir wine menu is like listening to a Girl Talk album: a heady experience that leaves one as excited as confused. The menu does represents varieties you'd see at typical wine bars (i.e. Gruner Veltliner, Malbec, Sangiovese), but there are certainly some out-of-left-field selections, like a Chasselas from Switzerland, a Dornfelder from the Finger Lakes in New York, and a vin jaune from the Jura. TT has one of the few wine-by-the-glass menus where I feel the beverage director is sincerely trying to expose me to new and interesting wines. Â You can literally drink yourself around the world: the wine menu features 10-12 featured wines by the glass, and has 60 other reds and whites offered by the glass (6 oz.) or half-glass (3 oz.). The mark ups are there, but reasonable given the depth and quality of the wines. Despite Terroir Tribeca being my favorite wine bar in NYC, it is one of my least favorite wine menus in NYC. Although I agree that Riesling is one of the greatest white grapes and that Michael White is a douchebag for abandoning long-time front-of-house partner Chris Cannon in the grand pursuit of Restaurant Empire, do I need to see such geeky, editorial commentary on a wine menu? It is difficult enough to work through a cumbersome, 40-page wine list.

They have a range of empanadas but frankly i have had better ones in the food trucks around the city. The outer covering is pretty hard and the filling is not as flavorful.The plantain chips are amazing but i would go here only if I had a crazy empanada craving
I love these the tacos! Â Don't forget to get the meat and chicken combo. They taste delicious! Â I've been searching for a good place to get tacos for a long time. Soooo yummy!

I went here for brunch on a saturday and honesty, enough can't be said about this restaurant. The food was beyond superb, I especially recommend the parfait, any croissant and the eggs benedict with goat cheese. No hyperbole, this is the best brunch I've had since I've been in NYC. More than the excellent food, the management and waitresses were very pleasant and helpful in navigating the fairfully elaborate menu. Very pleased with my experience, I will be going back again and again. I think this restaurant, although it is new in the area, will become extremely popular very soon.
wowsers! Â its a super sweet little spot. I'll be back.

Cheap eats. Peking duck on sesame bread was really good. The large soup is enough for 3-4 people. Not sure if this location delivers but the Williamsburg one does. Come here if you're looking to get stuffed for under $5/person.

Nice, romantic setting: gramercy tavern is a restaurant in a beautiful setting. The food is very good and the service is good. We went on a New Year's Eve and I think they had an abbreviated menu. The food was excellent, though. Even though I prefer restaurants with more interesting menus, this restaurant has high-quality cuisine. Definitely nice for special evenings out.

Perfect spot for a cheap, quick and hearty meal, which is exactly what I needed before my seven-hour bus ride out of the city. I sat down at a back table so I could put my suitcase out of the way. There was only one waitress, but she was quick and attentive. I ordered the 1/4 chicken combo with beans and rice for just $6.50. It came out of the kitchen within minutes. I finished nearly all of the food except for some of the rice, and it was all very satisfying. Go here even if you're not in a hurry. The food quality and price is a winning combo.
Really loved my first dining experience here. The gentlemen behind the counter was great. Texan and baogolgi are wonderful! Hope this places does well. I will be back really soon!!!

Fun vibe, great food & cheap! Have been a few times & have tried the fish tacos, enchiladas, rice & beans...all consistent & super good! Compared to other, more upscale mexican restaurants in the neighborhood, the food is just as good (if not better) but it's totally affordable!

Sweet and comfortable sunny spot in a not-so-crazed corner of Williamsburg, my bud and I tucked in here and were so happy with ourselves one late afternoon this week. We shared a fried chicken box (I didn't each much but: best fried chicken I've ever had? Pretty possibly, I'll have to come back starving and see) with a shredded brussels sprout salad side, which, topped with toasted pistachios and a bacon vinaigrette, was mouth-puckeringly good. We had some nice light local beers, we loved the Neil Young playing in the background, and the mosey mid-week stride with a smile from all the staff. But absolute best of all in my book: a chocolate cake donut the size of a babies head, so moist it nearly dripped, with a satisfying crunch to the top. So good I wanted to curl up inside it, and to be honest at that size I nearly could have.

One bad experience sure can ruin a place for a lifetime. I have eaten here only once and will never be back. Yes I would like to give them a second chance but there are too many places in NYC that I know for a fact are great. Â  The best way I can sum up the food is uninspired, and in such a competitive market uninspired equals not worth a second trip. I was at Cafeteria with a group of four and not a single dish we ordered was anything special. But the food alone is not what gets this place the embarrassing one star. What does then? Well when you mix average food with an incredibly rude waiter you end up with a remarkably bad experience. Our waiter was extremely rude, slow, and made multiple mistakes with the orders. The icing on the cake was when the waiter had the nerve to include the tip on the check which is not Cafeterias policy for parties of our size. When I saw this I was infuriated mostly because the waiter was so rude and inept. For the first time in my life I went to the manager and complained about the waiter. I told him what had happened and asked that his tip be removed from my bill. The manager wasn't that helpful and while he did remove the tip he never asked what he could do to improve my experience. All in all it was one of the worst experiences I have had at any restaurant

Second time visiting here, first time for brunch. Â I have to admit I have a fetish for the belt driven fans on the ceiling and industrial decor. Â Makes me want to build something similar in my apartment. One thing not different between dinner and brunch was the noise level. This place is definitely at the upper end of what I consider tolerable and hearing a person two seats down is a challenge. Â There was not a great deal of cheering for the multiple football games on save for one young lady whose voice was amazingly well projected each time after Green Bay had a good play. Â Disclaimer, I am not over 40 and did not have a career playing bass guitar with a touring rock band. Beer selection is good. Â Had a lager from Brooklyn of all places which made the noise level tolerable. Â We tried a number of the pickled jars and brussel sprouts were my fave. I had the huevos rancheros special which was quite good. Â Portion size was a little on the small size but that could be my perception because I desired more of this deliciousness after it was all gone. A sampling of the mac and cheese was quite good as well and though I cannot positively identify what variety of pasta was in there, it was most certainly not macaroni. One liner: Â Good food, cool retro industrial vibe, a little too loud to visit regularly.

Mixed review. Great food and quick service BUT A CONCERN, I walked in alone and asked for a table in the garden. I was told none were available. From my vantage point, I could see at least two free tables. When I asked when a table would be available, the person checked, came back, and led me to a table inside. In the garden, there were four open tables. I am chagrinned and despite the good food and lovely setting, I felt unwelcome throughout my meal. And my singlehood had a lot to do with that feeling. HMMMM.... Also, it's too damn expensive for the neighborhood. Seriously, folks!

Special hidden brunch place, will have to wait a bit to get your table. But that's how it is for brunch usually. The bacon spinach skillet is great, portion it's ok for me. But wouldn't fill up a guy for sure. Would probably come back here again to try their other things on the menu.

My boyfriend suggested going to Luke's Lobster. We went on a weekend, a bit past lunch period and it wasn't exactly crowded, but there are not a lot of seating options. If you have a large group, I suggest not eating here. I would say they can seat 14 people, 8 stools along the wall and one separate table for 6. The choices were also just okay. I liked that we had a "Maine soda" Â options. But being able to really only have a shrimp roll, a crab roll, and a lobster roll was pretty disappointing since they were half-rolls and fairly small. Oh, and cold seafood. I mean I liked them, and as only the 2nd time I've ever had a lobster roll (the first one I tried was at Wild Edibles and I liked theirs better), it's possible that they are well above average. The seafood was indeed cooked well. The roll was decent. But because of the portion and lack of variety, it was just boring.
i eat here once a week. the bib salad is amazing... i never had a bad meal from roberta's. this place also has a knack of attracting 'the attractive' ;)
We were late for 30 mins but they got us a table very quickly even thought there was a long wait line. Delicious before-meal-bread.

Rosemary Chicken Wings. Calamari with the San Marzano sauce. Ooooh baby! And that was just the beginning of a fun, cozy night at Carroll Place. This place was packed, not surprising for a Saturday night, so it was a good thing we had reservations. The location is right in the heart of the Village which worked out perfectly for us since we were headed to a comedy show at the Cellar around the corner. The vibe? Casual and warm. The staff? Friendly and helpful. The food? WOW! We started with a few appetizers and since I'd read on Yelp about the wings, it was a must try. So glad we did. Crispy and flavorful and sooooo delish!! The calamari was very good but the marinara sauce was the hero of this dish. The menu consists of "small plates" and main dishes, so you can busy your tastebuds with cheese boards and marinated olives or sliders and various meats. The main dishes of the night for us consisted of the Margherita pizza, the Homemade Pappardelle with braised Pork ragu, the Linguini Vongole and the Homemade Lasagna. Everything was delicious for the most part, but I did feel the pizza was pretty uneventful. Maybe it was because we had the basic pizza as opposed to exploring some of the more interesting ones. But the show stoppers of our meal were the desserts. The warm chocolate cake was gone in an instant. Holy crap it was good. And the Nutella chocolate Calzone was unreal. For the love of all that is holy, GET DESSERT!! I love places like this. Gastro pub atmosphere with amazing food. Carroll Place is a cozy fun restaurant/bar in the heart of the Village with all the right moves. Great food, great ambiance and excellent service.

LOVE this place!! Threw a birthday party here for 30 people. Â The service and food was AMAZING! Â We couldn't believe how reasonable the bill was. Â It is definitely our new favorite neighborhood spot!!

Hello, Jane. Why haven't I dined here before? On a beautiful Saturday some girl friends and I decided to enjoy the day with an indulging brunch. One of the girls was running late for our reservation but luckily by 2pm the crowd had died down so we were seated right away once the final girl in our party arrived. Seafood breakfast is usually done sloppy or just served as overcooked crap. The Benedict Jane was spot on! They don't skimp out on the crab/crawfish meat in their crab cakes either. Not stuffed full of fillers to drown out the delicate shellfish taste. This may be a bold statement but it was one of the tastiest crab cakes I've ever had in NYC. The tarragon sauce atop the perfectly cooked eggs complimented the dish well. I cleaned my plate of the potatoes & spinach and was just full enough. One of my friends ordered the roast chicken salad which for me would be on the bottom of my list of choices, but the dish was surprisingly flavorful and filling. Â Silky chicken went well with the salty bacon and blue cheese yet the dish remained light and well balanced. My other friend ordered the Farmhouse scramble that came out with a plate covered with eggs that were fluffy and tasty with the Gruyere, caramelized onions, and smoked ham. The space itself was tastefully decorated. The tables were tight but the tall ceilings and windows along the front opened up the space. We enjoyed our casual meal leisurely with laughs and light cocktails. Jane, I shall return again to sample more of your fare.

I ate at Carmine's on the UWS several years ago with a big group and thought it was good. We went to see a Broadway show as a family and the 44th St location was close so we stopped in. The place was jam packed on a Friday night during the holidays. That being said, the food was well prepared, and the service was amazing. Not at all what i would have expected. Both in terms of food and drink service, as well as, the above and beyond type of service. I would highly, highly, highly recommend Carmine's to anyone visiting Broadway or living in NY and out for a night on the town with a family.

For me, Totto beats Ippudo and Momofuku both on taste and cost. Small venue with a long counter and a handful of small tables. Love sitting at the counter and watching the cooks masterfully cook the noodles and other food. Wait can be long at peak times, but service and food make the wait worth it. Their pork belly buns are a great start to the meal and the ramen brings me back here to eat every time I visit now.

I've wanted to check out Uglyduckling ever since it opened, and finally had a chance to. It's hard to stand out on Smith Street due to all the other restaurants, but Uglyduckling has done a good job. The space is part of the old MTA building that's now next to Lululemon, so it has super high ceilings, and painted brick walls. Looks great. They also have 30 beers on tap (nothing too crazy, but some good local crafts). Their menu is also pretty extensive. Whether you want to eat by land or by sea, they have several options. Don't be fooled by the name though; they actually have several vegetarian options that sounded great. But of course, that's not why we came here. The Ugly poutine (provolone, duck confit and sweet BBQ) was solid. Not your typical poutine, to say the least. The BBQ sauce goes well with the duck, but don't expect something reminiscent of Canada. The fries were bit soggy, likely due to the deep bowl they were served in, but still good. My friend and I both got Uglyduckling burgers. Sadly, they've changed their menu a bit (either permanently or for the week I was there). Their website still lists their namesake burger has having a fried quail egg and pork belly. The one that was available when I went (first week of September) instead included fried cheese (I forgot what kind) and grilled onions on top. Not quite as adventurous, but it was still a damn fine burger. The breading on the fried cheese (I forget what kind it was) added some nice texture (kind of like when you get the Shake Shack burger with a fried mushroom on top). I got mine medium rare, and it was cooked perfectly. They offer three condiments (ketchup, mustard and mayo) and the burger tasted great with any of the three. Since we ordered the poutine, we didn't want to overdo it with the fries, and they allowed us to make a substitution for any of the other sides, without additional charge. My buddy did the grilled veggies (squash, cucumbers, and possibly other gourds). I did the sweet potato hash, served with kale. Delicious, but totally defeated the purpose of not getting fries. Definitely worth it. Only complaint was that the sides were a bit oily, so it made the veggies seem a lot less healthy. Service was great. Our waitress made some great beer recommendations (and gave us samples in fancy glasses). Also, I left a bag on the ledge behind our table, and when I came back looking for it two hours later, our waitress popped out of nowhere and handed it to me. Can't beat that! All in all, Uglyduckling is a welcome addition to the neighborhood, and I'll definitely be back. Hope to try the duck confit sandwich for lunch.

Chances are, if you've never been to Australia you have not had the opportunity to try authentic Australian cuisine. You are missing out if this is the case. And Thirsty Koala is delicious enough for me to want to book my flight straight over to Sidney. The service is fast and friendly. Prices are very reasonable. Dietary options are actually surprisingly diverse. My boyfriend is obsessed with the Crab Sliders. I loooove their salads because they aren't boring run-of-the-mill types. You will even find the owner running around making sure things are running smoothly and she will greet you with the warmest smile in Astoria. Oh, and don't forget to greet the chef; she is rooted in the community and is passionate about each plate she sends out from the kitchen. Meat lovers and vegetarians alike, unite. At Thirsty Koala.

Lovely little place with great awesome coffee and lunch sandwich selections. Just one thing.. Only 3 tables or a bar by the window.. It will be fully packed around lunch time.. But you should try this place!!!

Yes! I finally got to eat at one of the most coveted ramen establishments known to man. You can be jealous now. A culinary sampling of New York just wouldn't be complete without a visit to Ippudo. Unfortunately I got on the wrong train and was delayed 45 minutes, further building my anticipation. Nothing beats a bowl a bowl of slurp-tastic ramen on a cold winters day so I was overjoyed that I only had to endure a 30 minute wait. I had to order Ippudo's signature bowl, the Akamaru Modern to which I added a poached egg. The lunch set also included a side salad and choice of side rice dish. I thought it was a good value for $16. I'm also a sucker for pork buns so I threw in an order of that as well. I really liked the pork buns. I can't believe how delicious these animals are. Crispy skin, savory fat and tender meat all contained in a pillowy soft steamed bun. Perfection. The tonkotsu broth was the star of the show, dark and beaded with oil and melted fat, it was both luscious and smooth. A mellow yet assertive flavor only made more naughty with the introduction of the gooey yolk of the poached egg. The chasu was tender and delicious but not the most tender I've had and there was only two modest slices. The noodles were also a bit soft for my liking, I prefer a nice firm snap to my noodles but still quite good nevertheless. Overall a great experience, albeit a rather expensive one for a bowl of ramen, salad, rice and pork buns but when shared makes a rather good lunch-sized portion for two. A must try!

I hate to do this, but Woorjip drops some serious stars in my book. Â I popped in for lunch recently and the food was really average at best and some of the offerings were just bad. I left feeling grossed out. I opted for the pay by the pound and had small tastings of Â various dishes. Â The bulgogi was dried out and was more fat than meat. Â I had some tasteless "spicy" tofu. I tried some shitake mushrooms and kale which was disgusting. Â The egg slices were flavorless. Â The baked mackeral was a huge disappointment. Â (Dried out and it was displaced skin side up, so I only discovered this after it was already on my plate.) Â There was also a strange dried thing crusted on it. Â Like crusty roasted solidified fish guts or something?! Blarf. Â  There was a long line of people waiting for the buffet. Â The more I think about this place the more grossed out I feel. I see them exchanging out dishes here and there, but never the serving utensils. Â Grubby hands all over the place. Â  This meal was a huge disappointment. Â It's not cheap either. Â My lunch was $10.18 (also got a bottle of water and a bean sprout soup). Â The bean sprout soup and the bottle of water were the only things that I liked. At one point in my life I liked Woorjip. Maybe I just caught it on a bad day? Â I'm not sure, but it was enough to turn me off so much that I'm not going to ever go back. Â In my opinon, you're better of doing a lunch special at one of the other million restaurants on that street. Â If you do decide to go to Woorjip, then I would opt for the prepackaged selection of foods. I like the idea of a quick place to grab a quick bite, but the quality of the food is entirely lacking. Also, the thought of sharing a buffet with all of NYC is also kind of disgusting.
Dumplings are some of the best in the city. This place is definitely a new York city staple.

I did not like the fact that we had to wait an hour for our table and the food was okay but not for that price, the place is definitely too pricey. I like the interior design of the place and I like the different sangria's they have during Brunch - they are very tasty. So all and all an okay experience but not a place I want to come back to knowing how many awesome places there are in New York.

We saw Bono here. I feel like that alone is enough reason to go to this place. But I'll continue on just in case you're not a U2 (or humanitarian) fan. Ambiance: Hello Rat Pack. It has an old school feel: checkerboard floors, black and white photos lining the walls, a wooden bar with gold accents and burgundy booths. I felt a little deceived to find out it was renovated in 2009 so I have no idea how much of the ambiance is authentic vs. strategic. Food: After 2 days of uninhibited indulgence in all that NY has to offer, I opted for the fish b/c I needed a decadence break (*hangs head in shame*). It was light and buttery and very good but after seeing my date's Black Label Burger I felt like a pretty big idiot. I did have some fries. Best fries I've ever had at a restaurant (I'm a shoe string fan btw.) Service: Waiting for a table can be a little tricky as they have a small strip of space between the bar and other tables for you to stand around in and attempt to order a beverage. It took the bartender a few beats to eventually give us the head nod but we got our first round w/in a reasonable amount of time. Our waitress was very patient and friendly while we perused the menu and ordered drinks. About 15 minutes after being seated the host actually moved us one table over to accommodate a larger party to sit next to us. He was extremely polite and apologetic about it and at the end of the night he thanked us again for our understanding which I thought was a nice touch.

I give the 5/5 for the vegetarian lasagna Since the first day I got there, it's the one thing that I get Even if I tell myself to try something else....I end up w the veg lasagna It.s a a white sauce On the heavy side....but I absolutely love it
Went to Ippudo in July, was so impressed with the food and atmosphere of this place. Â The Hirata Buns were a hit with my daughter. Â Can't wait to go back to New York to visit again. Â Awesome!!!!

I never knew that crepes could get all crazy weird and tasty! I am kinda obsessed with trying to taste every single crepe on the menu! Customer service is nice and you can watch them elegantly make your crepe in front of you. The place is kinda small with a bar seating at the window for 2 or 3. They also have a really cool window display. Which you really don't see very often when it comes to the food industry.

Nope, nope, nope. They get one star for the food (and that's because I'm feeling generous) and one star for removing our glasses of wine from the final bill. We got here about an hour and a half before they closed on a Sunday night. No reservations, but we were seated at a table by the window right away. Water and bread were provided, and the waitress took our drink orders. She asked immediately if we had any food allergies, which I found odd, but given they offer so many gluten-free options, it made a bit of sense. I decided on the Cavatelli, and my husband got the Gnocchi. After we placed our order, we settled in to munch on the bread (tasty, and served with a garlic oil dipping sauce that was even tastier) and wait for our food. And we waited. And we waited. And we waited. And then? We waited some more. I kid you not, it took 45 freaking minutes for us to get our meals, and I'm fairly certain the only reason it came out when it did is because I had to ask the hostess (the only employee around at the time) to see if she could find out where our food was. She smiled, said she'd check with our waitress (who had come to our table about 15 minutes earlier to say our food was on its way). A couple minutes later, I saw the hostess walk back to the door to resume her post, without even a glance in our direction. Then a different waitress came out and once again said our food was on the way, and offered a half-hearted apology. I know you could feel the frustration rolling off of me at that point. The food finally came out (delivered by the apology-giver, not our original waitress, who never came back to our table the rest of the night), and it was only marginal. I'm convinced that she made the kitchen pull my pasta from the water and plate it just to get something in front of us. My Cavatelli was crunchy. Not like al dente, but like it wasn't given enough time in the boiling water. One of the first pieces I tried to pick up was a clump of pasta, which stuck together. The sauce was very runny, and I'm not even sure it was supposed to be there. It was also surprisingly vinegary, almost over-poweringly so. The best I can say is that it had a good spicy kick to it, which I hadn't expected. My husband liked his gnocchi, but wasn't blown away by it. He said the pesto was tasty, but that he had expected more from the gnocchi. When he says that we can make it better at home, that says a lot to me (though I do have a pretty kick-ass gnocchi recipe). When all is said and done, I left feeling hungry, frustrated and disappointed. For that kind of wait, the food should have knocked me out of my chair. Didn't happen. The least they could have done while we waited was given us another piece of bread. Didn't happen. At least the wine was tasty.

Great dinner tonight. Â 2nd time here and again was not disappointed. Â My wife ordered the linguini with clams which although was not on the menu, was encouraged by waiter who said any favorite could be accommodated. Â I had the linguini with mushrooms, sun dried tomatoes, arugata with a light tomato sauce. Â The fried calamari was delicious especially with the spicy marinara sauce. Â It's pricey and steered way from some of the other dishes that looked yummy but maybe next time.

The best Thai food in NYC. Â I've been to both locations and they are the same. Â I usually order a duck dish (roasted duck, duck salad, or noodles) from here and they have all been delish. Â I've also tried the papaya salad, chicken and ginger, soft shell crab app, and fish cakes. Â I have no complaints with the food.

After taking a 5 year hiatus from yelping, here goes... "I'm Hankering for some Hanco's!" That has been my motto since last week when I "discovered" this wonderful oasis of cheap, yummy asian food in the desert of Brooklyn Heights crammed with more costly Japanese and Thai cuisine. I just moved into Brooklyn Heights for the summer and was craving some bubble tea. Thanks to Yelp I found this place and just when I was going to step out the door to explore, serendipitously my bf brings home a honeydew melon one from Hanco's. Since last week, I have been back there 5 TIMES. For the meals, I've only gotten the chicken sandwich which is chock full of goodness. When I bite into the toasty bun and savory chicken with pickled carrots, it transports me to Nirvana. At $6 a 'wich, the passage to Nirvana is quite economical and so-worth-it. I think the ladies recognize my face because of my frequency and one of them gave me a sandwich card the other day. I'm actually embarrassed but I keep returning. I've been meaning to try other dishes but I just can't get enough of the bun's toasty goodness. Tips: 1) I got the whole wheat today to be healthier but I regret my decision. It's not as toasty/crunchy as the white bread. So do yourself a favor and just get the white! 2) If you call in advance, they will usually have your order ready by the time you swing by. I know! I have them on speed-dial (hangs head). Considering I live less than 5 minutes away, it's pretty sweet to just walk in and pick up my meal in a seamless transaction. Pay-stamp-carry-and-go 3) The drinks are meh. Although I know better iced thai tea and bubble tea exists elsewhere, I find myself ordering here only because of its convenient location 4) You can customize your dish per degree of spiciness: mild, medium, and spicy

Best bar in Greenpoint/Williamsburg! Great atmosphere and a big selection of beers. Spristzenhaus is the most sociable bar I've ever been to. There is a great sense of community even though the majority of us moved here from other parts of the world. Love the dining hall style seating areas, no booths and small tables mean the place is one big social house. And you can play jenga! Huge islands of beer on tap featuring many German beers and other great brews! Beers are on the more expensive side average $7-8 per glass, although they are damn good beers served in their original glasses. Food options are limited to pretty much fries and bratwurst. Not a place for food, but definitely a place to drink! I used to come here every weekend with friends, and now all my friends are bringing their friends here!

What is it about a food cart that gets people oooohing and aahhhhhing?! Â  Me no get it. It's tough steak that has been undercooked an hour ago, and then re-heated/de-ecoli-ized/charred after you order it.. but still undercooked on the inside. Â And it also happens to be tough, even at rare. :- / And let's not even mention the massive amounts of fat on each tough piece of "steak". Â  And and and.. Â the fact that the same guy you pay and who touches money, is also making your food. Â And I didn't see Purell anywhere in sight. Some of the guys are nice.., some aren't. Â But I don't go to a cart expecting anything good or bad of the service.
over hyped

Amazing!! I have been going here since it opened and it keeps getting better and better!!! Food is tasty along with the Red Sangria to wash it all down! My Favorite empanada is the Brazil along with the Polla La Plancha! Veal Rice Balls are amazing as well!!
I didn't really care for it, the chicken was dry, didn't have a lot of flavor. Â It could have been I just got a bad batch, or my taste buds weren't working so good that day.

This place was absolutely OVER HYPED!!! The food was not bad, but it was definitely NOT worth the 2 hours wait (Yup, you heard it right 2 hours wait for brunch). We think it could have been better if it wasn't for such bad services. First, the hostess magically lost our name after an hour even though we were sitting outside and came in to check every 20 mins (because the "waiting area" was actually too small, only 2 chairs, and almost no space to wait inside, so we opted to wait outside in the cold). After realized her mistake, instead of honor us the next table on the list she pushed our party all the way down to the bottom of the list again AFTER ONE HOUR WAIT. If it wasn't because of our out of town guests that were dying to try this place we would have left. Second, after 2 hours we finally got our table the waitress took our orders and then disappeared. We had to ask another waiter for extra fries. Then of course they forgot the fries, by the time everyone else was done we asked ANOTHER waiter to cancel that extra fries order and he said it's coming....yup, it finally came after everyone was done eating. Third, this place is horrendously LOUD. You can't hear anyone next to you unless you join the rest of the restaurant and start shouting on the top of your lung. In the city that spoiled with delicious brunches around every corner, needless to say we will never come back here again, out of town guests or not!

I've been to many pizzerias in my day, but I must say the one place where the taste of the food remains constant; no matter how many times you go is L&B's. It's a place where its cool to just come and chill out with your friends; over some amazing pizza. Of course, they only have a restaurant right next door to the pizzeria; but personally, I'd have to say they're known for that pies, and square pies at that. There's just something that sets it apart from other pizzerias; maybe its the sauce, maybe its something else, but whatever it is; I was extremely satisfied the first time I went and every-time thereafter.

Had the lobster special - tasted fresh, loved it. Wish they had pre-cracked the lobster more as I must not have enough strength to crack it myself, needed assistance from friends. For our appetizer we got the tune spring rolls - which were literately a piece of tuna in spring roll wrap -wish it had a bit more in the veggie department. Otherwise great food! Would go again!

i am an old lady and i like to have brunch before noon. this place opens at noon. when my friends chose it, i was wary (i also live in prospect heights so the burg's a bitch to get to). so cute! so inviting! and so close to the train! with huge mugs for coffee! my dear friends, already loyal patrons, said don't even LOOK at the menu. get the baked eggs. baked eggs? i asked. that's not even on the menu! TRUST ME, they said. it's a special and you need to get it. TRUST ME!!! we each ordered the same dish and i'm glad, because that means we each got a huge thing of chorizo and eggs and red peppers and cheese all bubbling away in a cast iron skillet, a huge side of garlicky potatoes and 2 thingies of bread. i couldn't finish it, and i had been starving. all that for like $9 or something. i am sold and totes coming back. they need to put that damn thing on the menu! there is also an ATM in the back. fee is $1.75. in case you wanna know.
I love this place. I go often! I recommend to everyone in the NY area.

Ootoya has taken a significant step backwards, at least at 18th street loc. Â It seems nearly all of the prior service staff has left, and it is a significant step down nowadays. Â Basically, while everyone was very friendly, they don't really know what they are doing. Â Food delivered to wrong table, delivered at different times, not knowing the menu. Â The place is too pricey for this kind of thing to happen. The food is still delicious, but a big part of coming here is the serenity and overall experience with presentation, etc. Â I get worried when a place of this price range drops off this much in terms of a consistency.

Walked across the Brooklyn Bridge from Manhattan to burn off some calories with Grimaldi's as our end goal. Â We read that the wait can get up to an hour but we were still shocked when we saw how long the line was. Â We walked up to the restaurant, saw that the line started a few feet away and started walking....walking.....walking.....towards the end of the line which was almost towards the end of the block! Â We waited in line for about 20 minutes but then came up with the ingenius idea to phone in our order. Â AWESOME IDEA! Â We picked up our small pepperoni pizza about 15 minutes later and headed down to the river where we ate with a great view of Manhattan's sky line. The pizza was pretty good. Â Not the best I've ever tasted - I thought the crust could have been a little crispier and less doughy but the ingredients on top - the mozarella, the pepperoni, the basil - were all super fresh and super tasty. Â And the small pizza was huge for only $14 ($12 plus $2 topping)! Was it worth the hour long wait? Â Probably not. Â But worth the 15 minute to go order wait :) By the way, the cannolis here are super good here! Â Kind of expensive at $3.50 a pop but they are huge and a great way to end the meal!

I had never been to an izakaya before and it was a really interesting experience! I wasn't quite sure what to expect, but as soon as my friend told me he discovered this restaurant on Anthony Bourdain's show I was embarrassingly excited to check it out. We split a bunch of dishes and I let him order me a beer (it was average). The dishes ranged from really good to inedible.* I really enjoyed the steak, meat skewers and seafood pancake while my friend really liked the udon. This place is worth checking out, especially if you are an adventurous eater who wants to avoid the mecca of touristy restaurants in times square. *the inedible dish was our attempt at being brave. We clearly failed.
My favorite Thai restaurant!

LIC Market should consider expanding by buying out the lot next door cause i'm tired of the long waits on the weekend! I'm such a fan of this place that I try to make it here at least once a month! Â  Such good food for the price. Â  yum yum yum!

best gnocchi, ever. that's over a few gnocchi dishes i had in italy - so the shit was good. restaurant had a cool vibe - inside reminded me of a dim (yet cool) lit dive bar. by that i mean exposed brick/cozy/friendly - not pee/poo/vom. ate there with 3 other friends - everyone's food was great, and we got some different appetizers which were all good as well. after you put your name in i recommend crossing the street for 2A to have a few drinks while you wait. the place was way less crowded than the bar right beside supper, and they had buy-backs until 8 or 9 which was nice.

Today I checked off this nice little spot in Queens, Salt & Fat. The place scores points for decor and atmosphere, but I have to admit, I was not blown away by the food here. The menu had a good range of options (at least 20 if I remember correctly)and the prices were decent. I purchased 3 of the restaurant's offerings during my visit. I had the Korean BBQ wraps, Oxtail Terrine and the Fried Chicken. I'm not going to hang this place out to dry and I'm sure some of the other offerings I did not have are good, but I did not leave the place saying to myself "Can't wait to go back". As the old saying goes, first impressions are lasting ones. The food Korean BBQ Wraps: The wraps were ok. It came with a piece of steak,a little spicy and sweet sauce, crispy shavings wrapped in Boston lettuce. Truly nothing to die for but not bad either. Oxtail Terrine: The first time I ate Oxtail in the shape of a cube! This dish actually was the best amongst what I had. Most flavor, unique presentation and a decent portion of tender Oxtail with two nice sauces to compliment it. At first I thought I was given a piece of chocolate cake by accident. Fried Chicken: Some fellow Yelpers touted this spot as having the best Fried Chicken. I gladly wanted to see if it was Indeed the case. Frankly, I left wanting more. The overall flavor just wasn't mind-blowing. However, the breast portion of the chicken was extremely tender. It was impressive being that the dish was fried. Overall: Inexpensive, nice ambience, but more hype than great to die for food. Well, I'm glad I got this one in the stat book. I look forward to my next adventure on the town!

Great thin crust Napoli pizza. Â Good beer. Â Good music. Â Funky vibe. Â If you're intimidated by funky, Â don't come but if you want a great evening, Â great food, Â great music, Â put his on your list. We tried tried the Greenpointer with Procuto. Â  Awesome! Â The other pizza with saprosota which is what pepperoni wants to be when it growa up.

We came here on a Saturday night (had reservations) and PIGGED OUT. Â  All of the food was so good, we just couldn't help it! Â I had never heard of this place before my visit, but it's definitely one of the many cute, trendy places in SoHo with delicious food that is worth a try. The appetizers are where it's at with this place. Â Fried olives to dip in cold lebne, crispy cauliflower, to-die-for hummus with pita . . . but the king of our smorgasbord of appetizers was the pita pizza. Â Instead of tomato sauce, they spread a carrot puree on top of crispy pita bread as a sauce base, then dab it with a couple of huge slices of warm goat cheese and some caramelized onions. Â Mmmm MMMM mmm, we liked this pizza so much we decided to try to make it at home one night. I was very happy with the vegetarian entree, a delicious pasta that had asparagus and lots of other green vegetables and was buttery, salty, and delicately flavored. Â It was such hearty, simple, fresh and satisfying food -- with a unique twist -- and I really wish I could have tried everything on the menu! Â The place was hopping with customers but I found our service to be spot on. Â Drinks came quickly and appetizers and entrees came when they were supposed to. Â We took our time with our food and got our check when we needed it. Â The atmosphere is a bit busy and loud, so I wouldn't call it romantic, but it's still a pleasant dining room. Â Good to go to with a steady boyfriend or girlfriend, family or friends. If you haven't tried this place I'd highly recommend making a reservation and arriving hungry. Â I hope to go back soon!
Favorite "diner" in the neighborhood. Â Friendly and fast service, delicious food, reasonable prices, and DUH! 24HOURS!!!

Based on my observation, Petite Abeille is divided into three different sections/settings for various groups of people. 1st section (near the entrance of the cafe) - more like a place to hang out for small group of people (two, especially friend's outing). Relax and nice location for a laid back weekend with intimate friends. 2nd section (mid section) - more like a place for family brunch. Kids are welcome! One of the cartoon characters is showcased in this restaurant (cannot remember which character it is). Very comfortable and homey. Lastly, it's the third and last section of the restaurant - outdoor dining experience at the little garden-feel outdoor space. This is suitable for couples and business partners. My friend ordered a bacon, mushroom omelette and she likes it. However, I'm a little disappointed with my special waffle of the week ( with strawberry sauce around the waffle and top with banana, kiwi, and blueberries + whipped cream). Should have more fruit on top; this dish is definitely overpriced ($12). Tastiness wise - not so good, can be improved. Most likely I will be back for omelet next time! Hope they make nice omelet =)

Not much to add here, but I'll give it a shot... Il Bambino is probably my favorite place to eat in Astoria, and definitely one of my favorite spots in the city overall. Â Whenever a friend comes to Astoria looking for a place to eat, Il Bambino is ALWAYS my first suggestion. Â I must have tried 30 different paninis from this place (no joke) and none of them have ever disappointed. Â  You might think that a panini sounds unsatisfying (I know I did at first), but you could not be more wrong about the sanwiches at Il Bambino. Â The Porchetta panini is hands down my favorite. Â The Italian Meatloaf is also incredible, as is the Prosciutto with fig spread, Speck with apricot butter, Artichoke with goat cheese, every single one of the brunch paninis, etc. Â You truly cannot go wrong with anything on the menu, and their specials are always top notch as well. Â  The staff is also very friendly and laid-back. Â My only complaint (and man is this splitting hairs), is that for as much as I've been here, they still don't seem to know who I am. Â Random and arbitrary, but it would be nice to get more than just a "Hello" on my 812348th visit to the place. Â Definitely won't stop me from coming back time and time again, though...

Much like the Penang of the area, it's a Malaysian restaurant that's located within the Chinatown radius. The menu is almost exactly like that of Penang, interestingly enough. The Hainanese chicken is good, chilled and tasty, few bones and a good amount of hot sauce and soy. The garlic chicken was deep fried and dry, though. Sizzling tofu was great, and the sizzling beef okay, but not enough of the dishes in my opinion. Deep fried sweet & sour whole fish wasn't bad, but it was a bit too crisp at the tail. And the roti canai was good, although the curry lacked a piece of chicken in it to gnaw on like most places. Spicy kong xing cai (Chinese water spinach) was good, too. Hainanese chicken rice was okay, others had the coconut rice, but the rice is a broken short grain, interesting and different for those not used to it. Overall, not bad, they were flexible serving a large group of 9, and added chairs at our request. They seat reservations, and they have a good set of swift staff cleaning off the table as you finish off dishes (they don't hold anything in the kitchen, they just bring it out when ready). Busy, too, they have a lot of people there packed in eating. Also, the guy's bathroom - long thin entry corridor, makes one cringe when going through it past the entry door because who knows how a fat person could make it through? Rather disgusting on that side.

I love dumplings. They are a staple in my freezer and I eat them all the time, all meat and veggies combinations, boiled or fried, as a meal or as a snack. These dumplings were fine but weren't great. I had the fried dumplings and while the dumpling skin was absolute perfection, the meat was far too salty and also tasted like it had too much binding product and not enough real meat. There are better options within walking distance.

The juicy beef patty makes this burger. Â Compared to places like Five Guys and In N Out, all those extraneous toppings just seem a bit, well, nonessential. Â If I could take the Shake Shack patty and stick it in an In n Out burger, life would be golden. I can imagine that for some people, the price of a SS burger may be the biggest turn off when comparing it to another comparable fast food joint. Â I mean, let's be honest. For the price of a SS burger, you could buy at least 5 McDonalds cheeseburgers. Â However, if you want a high quality, thick, juicy meat patty, you're going to want to go to Shake Shack. If I was a NY residents, SS would be my fast food splurge hands down. PS If you've got the room, give one of their shakes a go! Delicious!!!

Now thats what i'm talkin 'bout, this place is my jam!!! I've been here like a million times and they never fail. The quality of food used to be soo much better, but like with other restaurants; once they become more commercialized the food progressively changes. Still the BEST Malaysian restaurant in NYC hands down. But the downside is they don't take credit, CASH ONLY, so don't forget the benjamins. Malaysian food in itself is considered fusion because their cuisine is influenced from neighboring countries India, Thai, Cambodia etc. Â I know, enough with the history lesson. Here's the rundown Roti Canai; The ever so popular appetizer; A light crispy and flaky pancake served with a curry dipping sauce that has pieces of chicken and potato in it. I ALWAYS get this when I come here. Hainanese Chicken; Steamed chicken (served room temp) on a bed of cucumbers with a sesame soy sauce and an awesome kick ass hot sauce on the side garnished with cilantro. Classic Beef Rendang; Tender pieces of beef braised in a mild (sometimes greasy) curry sauce, served on a banana leaf. Pretty decent Sarang Buroung; A nest of deep fried mashed taro potato filled with a sauteed medley of shrimp, pork, chicken, peppers, red onions, black chinese mushroom and cashew nuts. MUST TRY!!! Sizzling Tofu; Fried soft tofu with ground pork, peas, carrots, broccoli in a brown gravy served on a sizzling plate. This might sound funky but if you try it you won't be dissapointed Kang Kung Belechan; Chinese water spinach sauteed with garlic and chili with shrimp paste. Authentic Their different types of Whole fish is always a crowd-pleaser. I never got the chance to have dessert because by the time I'm done I'm already two waist sizes fatter. But it's always, ALWAYS worth it In conclusion, GET YOUR ASS DOWN TO NYONYA STAT...... and when your done licking that curry sauce off your lip don't forget to thank me

My husband says he had the best lasagna of his life and he's pretty picky! I had the spaghetti pomodoro and loved it, because it was so simple, but just so well done. The spaghetti looked like they were homemade and al dente. Very pretty little restaurant with a lot of flair.

Biscuits: fair. Pickles: very good. Beer: terrific. I would return for the high-quality, value-priced growlers ($13 bought, I think, 32 ounces of very lovely IPA) and bar snacks, but not for dinner. Cheese grits were basically a bowl of butter; I was happy enough to spread them on my biscuit, which was dense and crumbly (bordering on dry). Okay, but not a biscuit I would stake my reputation on. Fried chicken: sweet, thick, moist batter, not the crisp, peppery variety more common in soul food restaurants up here--again, not my favorite, but nicely paired with hot pickles. Spinach salad with mushrooms was fine, too, but special mention goes to the crisp, delicious, and generously-portioned bacon. The space is cozy, with plenty of unvarnished wood and attractive lighting.

I love the back yard. The chick pea salad is delicious. The beers are carefully curated and the mixed drinks are good. We like the pretzel bites a lot. The vibe is great and the people who work there are so nice. Some of the food is over-seasoned. The flavor profiles are aggressive. Sometimes the first bite is great but the more I eat, the more I find it to be too much (the specialty burger, the pickled fried chicken). Way too much fried food on the menu. I get it - farm to bar... but, though I like fried food as much as the next person, that's not where they excel in my book. So, I prefer grabbing a drink and an appetizer to eating my whole meal here but I'm hoping that some of this is still just opening kinks that they'll work through over the next several months.
What can I say, very ok. Â Great location and decor though! Â OK, I ran out of nice things to say...Bye!

Okay peoples...judging from the folks who previously reviewed, i don't think they are all accustomed to AMAZING Caribbean food. Â And this is defintely Carib food, I grew up on this stuff, and no the ox-tail does not make me want to slap any one's mama! Â I think it's great that there is authentic Carib cooking available in a neighborhood where the food options are rather LACKING, but 5 stars, that's a bit extreme. The rice and peas tasted a bit burt, the callaloo was okay and the ox-tail, was average. Â For some serious ox-tail, head to the hole-in-the wall spot on Nostrand...now that is something else. Â  She is a super sweet lady, but I think previous tastebuds have been a bit off. Â Maybe I'll try something else from her another day...I dunno.

Quite the find in the Flatiron District. Great happy hour menu, $6 for wine, just a stone's throw from Union Square, it's hard to beat. The atmosphere is great and some of the best Mac N Cheese that you'll ever eat - which is phenomenal coming from me since I am not a fan of Mac-N-Cheese.

As I first step foot through the doors, unsure of what to expect, the scent of apples and wood heightened my excitement for what was to come through the next set of doors. I'm from the oc/la and came to visit ny for my anniversary. I really wanted to go to Chief's Table in brooklyn, but from all the raving reviews and the limited 18-seats, we were unable to get a reservation. Anyway, the food was delightful. Lunch ends at 3 but they still sat us down being we were late. My bf and I decided on the tasting menu, both with some variety of foods. Collectively, nothing screamed out at me, but the asparagus and cheese and the kobe braised beef were notable. I'm not sure if they gave everyone a pre-appetizer and extra desserts, but I loved it! Creme brulee on the house? my favourite. Also the coffee was fantastic, really compliments the entree and prepares you for dessert, plus i've never seen raw sugar cubes. By the end of our meal, we were so stuffed that we couldn't put a dent in all the sweets; cookies, creme brulee, chocolate souffle, peach thing, chocolate treats, and more! I almost forgot to mention the service, impeccable, very gentle if i could describe it. Our lunch was very intimate and romantic, (even though we were trying to take pictures while they weren't looking, total tourist/instagr.am junkies). I highly recommend this place for reasons being lunch is only $55 (thats a steal!!), it is so intimate, and perfect for a girls get together, business meeting, or even an anniversary. p.s. jackets are required, my bf didn't have a jacket, so they let him borrow one. :D

Woah! This pizza is amazing. This is coming from the adult who would frown at Pizza parties as a child. I have since realized that it's not that I don't like pizza, I only like great pizza. Went for lunch and it was fantastic. At tentative staff, we received or order in a decent time especially considering how busy they were. If you like Arugula their Arugula salad is a must. I'm enjoying all of the finds that my new employment location has to offer.

Cannot put into words how much I love Gaia Cafe The. pasta and the pizza are amazing and the ingredients taste so fresh. In terms of value for money, Gaia is unbeatable, nowhere in Manhattan comes close.
Descent pizza. Bit over priced. Not the best pizza by any means as they claim, but it's historic. Worth going one time and no more.
The lamb is so good but chicken and waffles is such a disappointment. The jerk chicken was bland and has no flavor. The waffles was decent.

Â too inexpensive for the fresh handmade dishes. I. Love this place if could eat there food all day everyday I would. Â  If I could marry there chicken box I would and the bourbon pecan pie would be my best man and I would Â have an affair with the. Biscuits there that good !!!

This off-the-beaten-path bar reminds me of a speakeasy from the early 1900's. Decorated with old black and white photos, sawdust covered floors and a vibe reminiscent of an old-time tavern, the downstairs taproom is perfect for unwinding with a pint of Guinness. Upstairs, however, is where the real magic happens in my opinion. Though you might wait until space allows, the cocktail lounge, or parlor, that resides on the 2nd floor is where you might have imagine the "upper classes" to have wined and dined. The cocktail menu and selection is impeccable and the staff certainly knows how to create a palette pleasing drink that can suit a variety of consumers. I didn't have the chance to try their food menu but from the looks of it, it seemed to be on par with the cocktails. A lovely place to take friends or visitors for a special occasion, I highly recommend hitting this spot up if you happen to be in the area.
I've been coming here since I was a child in the 80s and just never stopped coming here. The most authentic Cuban cuisine in all of Queens. Outstanding from staff to food.

So I've been here a few times since I live down the street, and it's been usually a very delicious experience, but the last time my boyfriend and I were there we saw a rat behind the bar. Told one of the workers, who spent all of 2 seconds looking for it, and then kind of brushed us off. So that's pretty disgusting and we probably won't be coming back.

I had high expectations for this spot, and they were completely fulfilled. I was such a fan, in fact, that I had to come back again a week later. Had heard great things about this beautiful restaurant from lots of people, so was excited when two friends agreed to go for dinner a few weeks ago. We had a reservation, but one of our party was running quite late, but this was not a problem at all. We were treated very well by everyone and enjoyed some wine at the table while waiting. The complimentary dip and pita was delicious, but I thought I would regret ordering the trio of dips as well, but was proved wrong. Definitely the right choice. Came back last Friday night for a late dinner with more friends and was skeptical as to how we would be treated as we had already had quite a bit to drink and were just ordering appetizers to share. However, I was pleasantly surprised when there wasn't so much as a sideways glance from the waiter at our order. Again, everything was delicious (awesome meatball appetizers, just as a recommendation) and we all left very satisfied. Big ups, Pylos.

What a great bang for your buck in the SoHo area full of pricey shi-shi restaurants!! Their $9.95 lunch special is one of the best deals in town!! Known for being the biggest foodie in the department, today I was pressured to find a cheap group lunch by my co-workers so I chose this place after doing a quick Yelp search. When we got there around 12:45pm, it was already packed and Â we were told that there's a 10 minutes wait.
