However, just as my desperately hungry co-workers were about to cross the street to find out the table availability of the other restaurant nearby, the manager came out again to inform us the table will be ready in a second....which ended up being 5 min.. My Italian co-worker was like, "that's how we do business!" Â LOL! Overall the service was fast and food was pretty good! Nothing fancy, just casual comfort food, but the portion size is extremely generous, especially the pizza! The pizza was also my favorite choice for the lunch special, it's thin and cripsy, just the way I like it! Everyone was pleased with their food, and gave me 2 thumbs up for the excellent price! Grazie Yelp & Il Corallo!!!

Came for brunch here this past sunday with a party of 8. I didn't make a reservation because I knew some people were going to be late. That's just how my crew roles. Turns out more than half of my party was late and Extra Virgin was quite busy. Nevertheless, when asked what the wait time would be for us, the hostess(es) happened to have a big table available, but with only 4 members, we couldn't accomodate that table until my full party arrived. Therefore, they couldn't guarantee us the spot. 30 minutes later, most of my party had and the big table was still available! And, the place was still packed! Were they reserving the table for us without telling us? Whatever, that in itself deserve 4 stars. I got the Salmon Egg Benedict as usual when I go to brunches. Which was good. As usual. Which means my review of their food here is probably inadequate. So, I'm also rating from the impressions of the other 7 people in my party. Four Stars.
delicious food. fun decor. great drinks. delicious food. upstairs space is great for parties. what i don't understand is why they won't deliver. absolutely baffling for the UES.

I'm a ramen fan feel this place is over hyped. Â The ramen tastes gritty and after visiting two Toto Ramen locations I noticed their noodles in both places were a tiny bit undercooked. It wasn't bad just over hyped.

Fries with Old bay seasoning -- nuff said! Greasy tasty 'siesta-inducing' sandwiches. Doesn't make for a great lunch option but excellent tasting food. Need to make this a regular after-work drinks spot! 3.5 stars

This is one of my regular restaurants for good, filling Italian food served by friendly staff in NYC's busiest area. Busy and crowded can sometimes be an understatement here, because the place gets packed with tourists and business people, so plan your evening accordingly. I prefer to go at a later hour, after the Broadway rush subsides. As for the food, the stuffed mushrooms and the chicken parm is a good/safe choice, and so is the shrimp scampi. My friend and I ordered a mango martini, which was delicious. My only complaint is that the noise level can get very loud, so this is definitely not a "getting to know you" type of restaurant.

This bar is a favorite of mine and many of my friends. Definitely drop by for a pickleback and a some great eats. The only caveat I have about this place is that it's pretty packed around happy hour (but that describes most bars in that area). Late night, I've never had a bad experience here.

I am a huge lover of italian food and this place wasn't all what I hoped for. Â it's true that this place is much better for groups as the portions are for sharing but the quality of food is not what it use to be. Â Everything is overly salted or overly bland. Â Carmines use to be my favorite spot for my fix on italian but that was 4 years ago and has gone downhill ever since. Â I decided to give this place another shot but it's still not what it used to be. Â It's definitely a tourist spot now.

Soooo I spent a week in Thailand last year, tried different dishes on my first day, and either they were too spicy or way too different for my tastes. Â I spent the rest of the week eating pad thai at every meal. Â And no, I'm not some close-minded American who has to eat a hamburger abroad. Anyway, my point is that it's very difficult for me to find something I like on a Thai menu (besides pad thai, bien sur). But at Song, nothing is a gamble, as everything is delicious. The portions are generous too, and everything is affordable. Two things I don't like about this place is the wait (I've had to wait over an hour at times) and the music. It's WAY TOO LOUD in here...almost club-like, which I'm not a fan of for dinner. Otherwise, overall great food.

this place was recommended by a friend and was pretty good. Â we came on tues night, and it was hopping. Â i couldn't get a reservation for 4 people until 9:15. Â  the calamari app and and beet salad were delicious. Â for entrees, 3 of us shared the roast chicken and monkfish, and they were tasty. Â the roast chicken was a great deal, considering you get half a chicken. Â we also got the potatoes and greens on the side. Â for dessert, we shared the chocolate budino and the salted caramel and pistachio gelatos. Â the budino was amazing. i like the feel of the place, since it's a remodeled garage and totally industrial.

Lombardi's gets 5 stars upon the request of my boyfriend, who eats everything AND my cousin, who is THE pickiest of eaters and is from the west coast (ie NOT accustomed to anything remotely close to good pizza.) I WAAAAS going to give it 4 stars, because I think that you should just be able to walk in and grab a slice in a true pizzeria and you can't do that at Lombardi's. But the boys convinced me that the fact that Lombardi's is made to order makes it 5 stars. Â "Pizza is an art," Tyler says and it's an art that Lombardi's does well. And with a sigh, and a smile, I concede and agree... Lombardi's pizza IS art and it deserves the 5 stars. FYI: We got there JUST in time! Around 11:45 AM on a Saturday. Any later than that, and you'll have to wait for a seat. BUT, everything comes out very quickly. We weren't really rushed out of the place, but I could see where people might feel that way on a busy day. The pizza is phenomenal, with crispy, freshly made crust, fresh mozzarella (not the shredded packaged crap), and a tasty sauce (better than grandma's, sadly for her). The bruschetta is a little mushy, but the tomatoes are fresh as can be and it's still very tasty. This is a must-try in NYC!

I thought the location was great, food was good, but service was pretty bad. We saw our waiter a handful of times, and he told us the pizza takes "90 seconds" to come out which definitely (although he probably was being sarcastic, or not) we were excited about-- but, with the wait and crowed, we waited 45 minutes for the pizza. He also may have just forgot to put it in until we inquired about it 25 minutes later. Â  I thought the manager was friendly when I inquired about why it was taking long, and ten minutes later it arrived. I would skip the calamari, it was okay. The standard salad was also okay, probably could do with some more salt. Their brick oven pizzas were all really good- not the BEST I've had but pretty darn tasty. Ask for a side of marinara-- it was also pretty good to dip crusts in. The olive oil was wonderful quality- add some crushed pepper, salt, lemon and you are good to go if there is a long wait for you too. I think it is worth the visit- just beware that the time around lunch is SUPER busy and you may not get the best service.

At first glance at my pho bowl, i was sincerely disappointed. It looked so teeny, but with further inspection, and boy did I inspect this bowl, it was quite loaded. All of the flavors were there and the noodles were the same kind my mom used, so stars for that! It's probably the tastiest pho I've had in BK, and I can easily say NYC. That's because most places here are subpar. If this was in my neighborhood, I'd totally frequent it everyday.

My favorite place to grab a glass of beer for dinner or in the middle of night! This place is just one block away from my apartment, so I stop by with friends or alone very often. Contrary to other pubs in the theatre district, this place is rarely packed during the dinner time, so I can always be seated as I walked in. It offers a good selection of Western beers, and I especially like their Belgium draft beers. Fish&chips is also good to have with these beers! Â  Plus, this place has very luxuious, victorian, or antique, interior design! The tens of unique victorian photo frames with unusually high floor makes it so special and different from other pubs in Theatre district. You can enjoy both drink and good atmosphere here with your friends as long as you want in the middle of night.

Ok so, Maybe it,s better than the one in the east village because it.s a new location?! The flavors arena ve more depth than the one in the e.ville It.s like there.s an extra step of love and cooking The service is friendly And for a busy Sunday the wait-turn around was quick for a 1pm brunch Group of 6 and a 20 min wait....not bad, or we just got lucky Mediterranean brunch was great Atmosphere pretty Lots of sunlight and bright whites

Wandered in here freezing, hungry, in need of a cocktail! cool vibe inside - totally chelsea. Â grabbed a couple stools at the bar, friendly service. 6 dollar lichee mimosas always get's my vote. Â had the green dumplings, very tasty and generous app size serving. imitation duck tamarind chili sauteed over veggies was sooo good, spilt it with a friend, could have topped it off myself! we both had a key lime pie martini for dessert came with cookie crumbs on top! between the two of us we have 5 cocktails 2 apps and 1 entree and the bill was like 60 bucks plus tip- totally do-able and worth it! go with friends or even on a cheap date night.

I've eaten here and gotten burritos both times and I don't understand why people love this place. Maybe the rest of the menu is superb, I don't know, the food was okay both times, but nothing special at all. There was nothing I'd describe as "authentic", just regular burritos you'd get at any standard Mexican place. Â If I didn't live a couple of blocks away I would probably never eat there again, Â there's just nothing special that would make me go out of my way to return.

This was my first time trying Austrian food and the waiter was very accommodating, checked up on us at the right times when I needed him place was very refined and the food was great! Can't wait to go there again

Awesome ramen joint; NYC has many fine noodle selection compared to any other city. This is one of the contenders as this place perfected all three critical food ingredients: the noodle, the broth and the pork. I ordered Shio Black Tonkotsu and my wife ordered Miso ramen. We both agreed that the Shio Black ramen had a much better broth flavor than the Miso. In terms of the overall taste, the broth complimented the noodle and the pork was exceptionally flavorsome. The noodle was different like skinnier than ramen noodle usually is- great texture and firmness. Pork was marinated well and torched just a bit. The gyoza was just ok though. Nonetheless I am judging only the overall ramen taste as this was solely based on the merit of noodle.

good bye chipotle & qdoba! This place is soo good. I came here after a training with a co-worker. She's a vegetarian and only had a bean burrito, which she loved. While I had the grilled steak burrito. It was soo good! It's actually as big as the burritos from chipotle but more tastier! Highly recommend to everyone!! I can't wait to go back!!
Good Â sangria really poor customer service! and my partner got food posion at this place.

For NYC standards, the viet food here is good, which isn't saying much. Â If this were Houston, TX or Westminster, CA, I would rate the food subpar. Â  The Banh Mi I got was their special, and I did enjoy it, but I wish there were a bit more of the pickled daikon, and parsley in it. Â It also had a nice spicy kick to it. Â  The fried egg option puzzled me. I don't think I've ever heard of someone putting an egg on it. I also ordered the vermicelli with beef, but I also wondered why there wasn't grilled pork as an option.

I think this pizza is way over-rated, and I don't know how this 80 something year old man caters to all of his patrons. My friends and I ordered two pies and although the ingredients were fresh, the pizza itself was very soggy. We waited for an hour to receive our order and each one of us were thoroughly disappointed. Â I don't really recommend Di Fara - there are much better places that you can get an excellent pizza pie in Brooklyn. It was NOT terrible, but I don't ever wake up craving this pizza -I've definitely had better. Â Maybe the pizza was better tasting when the owner was in his prime?... or maybe we went there on a bad day? The best thing about this place was watching the owner make each pie, constructing each order with ingredients from his home-grown garden. Â Unfortunately, the end result did not taste that memorable. Â I really wanted to fall in love with this place, but just couldn't. I want to return back here Â in the near future because everyone deserves a second chance...

I don't see why this place gets amazing reviews. I didn't find anything special. I was hoping to find a classy bar with good wine and instead it was super-crowded, super-loud (college kids feel), dirty and stinky. They had only 2 red wines available by the glass (both mediocre). i'm sure a lot of people like it, but I wasn't impressed.

I love this place. I used to go here all the time, and I have stopped in here and there and they have a great brunch special. I used to go for dinner and the pasta has always been amazing. For brunch I had the duck confit with hash and that was amazing. You can have that and a cocktail for 15.00 I believe. Cute place, and great staff.

Great selection of beers!! We stumbled on this gem not so long ago! The staff is amazing. If you are looking for a beer in a dark/wood bar you have found it! Try the Bronx brewery beers! Really good!!

Chinatown has so many places to try you never know where to go. Wife and I were looking to have lunch and we usually go to our favorite. We pass by Big Wong's and she convinces me to go inside. Its her family's favorite in the neighborhood and the duck is suppose to be good. Coming in this place it looks bad and you dont expect much. Wife convinced me to have duck over rice ( she knows I love it). Â She went for the beef chow fun. Within literally less than five minutes of our order the food arrives and the check! Â I got to say the duck was delicious! The noodles were great too. Very tasty and couldnt believe food came so quick. Place was packed for a wednesday at lunch time. Looking around people were all enjoying the food and all the dishes looked great. Makes you actually want to order more. Service was pretty good waiter always came by. Like most places in Chinatown its cash only. Bill came out to be like $15. Pretty good for two people. Overall, give this place a try it might not look clean and welcoming but it will satisfy ur tastebuds. Got to give to the wife on this one. She warned me doesnt loook the best but its worth it. Tip: Just stay away from the bathroom its gross!

Visited with my hubby and his fam for his grandmother's bday. I had the honey fried chicken with the cabbage and candied yams. IT WAS AWESOME! For my drink I had the half lemonade and half sweet tea. My mother-in-law ordered hers with unsweetend tea. I should have followed her lead. Between the drink and the canided yams,which were more like sugar yams, I had the worse sugar rush and headache after the meal. :( However, I would return and do what my MIL did and instead of the candied yams I would opt for the baked mac and cheese. My husband had the mac and cheese and it was cheesy and delish!

What's there to say? $4.50 for a gigantic Artichoke slice? Amazing. It's creamy, salty (not in the bad way), and delicious. As a bread lover, the huge crust with some residual artichoke sauce is a plus. Whenever I'm nearby, I make sure I grab a slice regardless of the line. I'm definitely going to try the crab slice next time!

I went here Â a while back with a friend, since I'm yelping now I'll write a review for this lovely place! We both were impressed with the food, price range, & service! The food was really delicious, it was something new for both of us, we tried the spinach with cheese crepe & Â the ham & cheese crepe. Well balanced flavor, not too over-powering. We wanted more so we ordered the banana crepe with chocolate sauce. They have an outside patio which is really nice as well. Despite having little difficulty in trying to find the place & navigating around the neighborhood, we know how to get back here so definitely will come back!

this is my new favorite restaurant. my boyfriend's, too. the sake panna cotta is divine. the foie gras soba is phenomenal, and so are the uni croquettes. everything this place serves is absolutely delicious. and the plates, sake cups, sake servers - they were all so beautifully made. the atmosphere is wonderful.

This place is BOMB. Â My girlfriend brought me here for the first time early in the summer, and at first I was totally Not Stoked on the whole window-service-lack-of-seating deal. Â But let me tell you: Â I would happily sit my bare ass on the sidewalk for this food. Â The pizza--THE PIZZA--is crazy good, and my girlfriend digs the veg flat + grits with the almond romesco sauce. Â The salt cod potato smear on the Nonna's breakfast sandwich was a little overwhelming for my taste, but everything else about the sandwich is A+. Â I'll be back over and over and over again.

I definitely agree with all the other reviews so far - this is a quality joint. Â Well made cocktails, good selection of beers and reasonably priced specials. Â I haven't checked out the patio yet, but the indoor space was a great environment and not too loud to have a conversation.

$6 for yummy cheap food. Â I wish they had these in LA. Â I ate this twice in NY. $6 rewards you yummy moist rice, some slices of nan-bread, and slices of chicken or whichever protein you like. Â Serving size is massive. Â 1 serving enough for 2-3 people to share The white "ranch sauce" is extra delicious to drown w/ your rice. Â They also have red sauce but it's extremely spicy; I'm talking burn your mouth and you'll feel it the next day. Â You've been warned :P TIPS -They don't have water so bring some or pay the $3 for a drink -Sauce is bomb. Â Get as much as you can

I work across the street from here on Thursdays and decided to try it out for dinner one day. Â I ordered the Harissa flavored Falafel sandwich with wheat pita (I skipped the Tahini). Â It was really good! Â The portion size is fairly generous. Â The place is pretty small, so it's not necessarily a good "eating out" experience if you're going out with friends, but it's a good place to stop by if you're on the go. I would give this place 3.5 stars. Â The food was pretty decent, I'm just not really a falafel person.

Mmmmmm meatball sliders. That's what everyone comes here for, right? Well, they are worth the trip. The space is teeny tiny but doesn't feel cramped. Our waitress was friendly and attentive and did not rush us at all. The pacing of the service was perfect, which means a lot when you've waited a month for your Friday night reservation. Back to the sliders - they are as good as everyone says! Just delicious, meaty little morsels that are the perfect way to start your meal. Beyond that, I can't be that helpful with the standard menu. We both had the special of sea bass over lobster risotto, which was incredible. A side of truffled mushrooms was a tasty treat as well. I give the Little Owl a lot of credit for a) living up to the hype, b) making their diners feel comfortable and welcome in a space that could easily feel overcrowded and c) keeping their prices reasonable. There were some good values on the wine list and I don't think any of the entrees were well over $30. I feel like this is the kind of restaurant that could easily rest on it's laurels and try to turn tables as quickly as possible, and it' speaks highly of them that they don't.

Everything we got, from the drinks to the main dishes was phenomenal. Kimchi pancakes were perfect and the Bibimbap was one of the best I've had. We ordered and everyone had a try of everything. The braised short rib fell apart in your mouth as did the pork belly. 3 of us got the Bibimbap and both the chicken and the pork were delicious. The service was great, drinks were strong. I'll be returning here shortly

Heard lots of great reviews from people about this place. There was a person at the door to greet you and maintain the line, kinda like a bouncer. He was super friendly and got us to our seat right away. Although the oven was being reheated, the pizza came out promptly. Many selections on toppings, gotta have that ricotta cheese. The pie was a little sweet for me, and the price was a little higher than most, but you are paying for experience so it was well worth it. It gets crowded pretty quick during dinner hours but the place is huge.

My favorite neighborhood spot for great food and friendly service. Â I enjoy brunch here almost weekly, and their lunch and dinners are excellent as well. Â The specials are always interesting and tasty, and the servers and bartenders are welcoming and friendly. Â It's also a great option for a late night drink and snack. Â For quality food, excellent value, and a true neighborhood experience, the Tavern on Jane is a must.

Cute little French cafe bistro in West Village. It's warm, romantic and inviting. Food & wine is excellent, as expected. - Risotto with horseradish: interesting, and the horseradish was not overwhelming (as I expected it may be). - Lamb chops: super tender and delicious, can't go wrong with this choice - Salade aux lardons: delicious! it may be a bit rich for some people not used to blue cheese, but this "salad" was surprisingly amazing. The only thing wrong with this place was our particular server. He seemed a bit stand-offish, didn't smile too much, perhaps just a bit awkward. He also didn't ask if I wanted more wine, which was a shame.

I really wanted to give Hudson Clearwater a better score but alas, there were two things that really just bothered me. Let's start with the decor. Very typical cute West Village restaurant - cozy and warm. The food - delicious. No complaints about ANY of the things that we got (both of the clam appetizers, brussel sprouts, steak, chocolate bread pudding). Everything was fresh and seasoned perfectly. The drinks - some of the best drinks I've ever had. I got the Hudson Mule - very delicious. The waiters - ahh....you would think that for a restaurant of this calibre that the waiters would be a little more organized...but alas, no. We had 3 different waiters throughout the night...although, the one that we ended getting most of our food from was great. But the first two waiters had NO idea what they were doing. It took them almost 10 minutes to even come over and give us water. On top of that, it took them another 10 minutes to come back and see if we had any questions about the menu. The host was nowhere near the front of the restaurant so it took them nearly 10 minutes to seat us for a reservation we were on time for. The host then told us to wait at the bar saying that: "the table will be ready whenever the tables clear up..." - very vague and unclear. I didn't know if I was supposed to get a drink or not. So I didn't. After waiting 10 minutes, during which I could easily have had a drink, the host finally comes back over and tells me not to get a drink as the table is almost ready... All in all, the food and the drinks make it a worthwhile experience, but I don't think I'll be back again. There are many other restaurants nearby with equally as good food with much better organization and service.

Enjoyed this place quite a bit. Great for happy hour - cannot do much better than $5-6 for a beer or mixed drink. The variety they offer as part of the happy hour is terrific. Also, the food that is included under happy hour is a great deal too - can't go wrong for a $5 burger that actually is full of flavor; my friend also said that her calamari was quite good too. Only downside is that the place is quite loud (even during the late afternoon) with music blasting. Overall though, does have a cozy vibe and isn't pretentious.

Got a reservation for a family at this restaurant. And I have to say, I was surprised by the bulk of food that one order brought along. Although it is VERY pricey (around $40 a casserole and $25 for bulgogi), the food was excellent. If you are to go to this restaurant, I definitely recommend making a reservation first. There will be at least an hour wait if you do not make a reservation and go during peak hours. We ordered 3 casseroles - Classic Kimchi Jun Gol, Budae Jun Gol, and Seafood and Tofu Jun Gol, and of the three, Budae Jun Gol was definitely the most satisfying. It was so satisfying that we took the broth home! The bulgogi was delicious, though I don't think they gave us as much as the price entails. If you are willing to spend a lot of money on good korean food, I'd definitely recommend this place.

I found this restaurant using yelp while I was walking in the area. I had no idea it was owned by a famous chef. Great atmosphere and wonderful service! I had the special of salad and three pasta choices followed by dessert. The food was good but nothing to write home about. I usually love Italian food so it was a bit of a let down. It was a bit of a let down upon finding out it was owned by a famous chef, you would think with all her experience she would have had better food.

Decor- modern with plenty of space at the tables Staff- Friendly but not overly so Food- Pretty good...I felt it was a bit overpriced for the quantity and taste. The brunch menu is standard, nothing blew me away in particualr there. I had the scrambled eggs with fried oysters and a side of greens. Interesting combination and seemed to work well together. The green bean side dish is awesome though, get it if you go.

My brunchmates and I made it to Freemans right after 10am this Sunday. Â We were swept into a wooden, taxidermied, "Maggie May" playing overhead, LES mecca. Â I'm struggling to not use "ironic" as an adjective when describing this place. Â Service was nice and very attentive. Â I had as many cups of Stumptown coffee as I could consume (epic win for the sugar cubes) prior to the arrival of my meal: Â a Â roast pork sandwich with pickled zucchini and garlic mayo with a side of field greens. Â Who cares that it was 10am and perhaps better suited for the lunch half of brunch - this was delicious! Â We all split a side of the cheddar cheese grits -- amazing. Â I think these were the best grits of my life. Â All in all, I loved every moment here at Freemans -- great service, endless coffee, awesome tunes, a few ironic moustaches and a dead goose on the wall. Â I want more.

My coworker and I were craving wine and cheese. Â After a long day's work - we just wanted to relax in a laid back ambiance with a bottle of wine.. or three. Since we worked on the east side of Midtown.. we decided to do some yelping and research for a wine bar near by. Â  My coworker mentioned something about a wine bar on 50th street that her boyfriend and she wanted to go to but had a long wait the weekend before. Â  I realized the wine bar was actually right across the street from my apartment... it was fate. We got to Sofia right around their opening time ~5ish. Â We were the first customers so we could pick any table that we wanted to. Â Of course we took the half outside/ half inside seating. We ordered the Meat & Cheese platter with a bottle of their Pinot. Â  The platter was absolutely delicious -with their proscuitto ham, many different cheeses, and baguettes. Â  By the time we knew it .. the bottle was empty and decided on getting one more glass of the same wine. Â Unfortunately, that one glass turned into 2... in which was equal to a bottle (pricing wise). Â Should have just ordered a 2nd bottle instead of another glass........ =( Â Oh - and the place got packed around 5:30-6ish on a Thursday night. Â I live right across the street and believe me.. it is packed every night. However, wine + cheese + rain + Sofia = happy happy me

I had a really poor experience at Le Barricou. I'm not one to complain, it takes a lot for a bad review from me, but the lack of customer service here really ruined our brunch. I'm sorry to say I won't be back and I wouldn't recommend. Firstly, we were told we had to wait for 30 mins for a table. It was a busy Sunday so that's not totally unexpected. We ended up waiting for 40 minutes before finally getting a table for a party of three. The table was actually a table for two with a third set of cutlery squashed on. This was frustrating because we had seen two couples who came after us get seated before... if we were just going to be crammed in a table for two, why couldn't we have had their tables? The decor is really lovely but it didn't help when things got worse. We had to use two of napkins to balance out the wobbly table when we first sat down and I asked for more napkins but didn't receive any until half-way through our meals when I asked again. We ordered straight away because we knew they were busy, including a couple of iced coffees. 20 minutes later still no drinks, we inquired to where they were, but they still didn't come out until after our food.The food itself wasn't too bad but the service was just so poor. Our waitress barely tended to us and we couldn't get her attention when asking to check on the coffee and napkins. It was indeed the bus boy who helped us out here on both occasions. We received much better service from the bus boy, so thank you, you should be serving!

I had my birthday dinner at Landmarc. I love this restaurant because they can accommodate large groups. The staff is very friendly and made great wine paring suggestions for the different entrees we chose. Usually, you would expect the meat portions to be small but NOT here. The pork chop was HUGE and I mean HUGE. I think two of my friends had to share it because the portions were so generous. I love their grilled octopus and bone marrow. At the end they surprised me with a cute one-bite tiramisu and cotton candy. Everyone left full and happy with caramels in their hand. I will be back!

Honestly the best macarons I've ever had. I got the Chocolate Coconut, Strawberry with sprinkled sugar (these two have marshmallow filings!) and also rose petal. These macarons melt in your mouth and aren't super hard/crispy on the crest. So good :D p.s. I'm from LA and I heard the macarons @ Bottega Louie went up to $3/macaron. So $2.8 would worth your moneda. Love, Jwan

I've been here twice within a week's time with my family and we all love this place. Â  The first time was because we wanted to try a new place and saw their menu by our door. Â Perhaps we got there during peak (8:30 on Friday night) but the wait was pretty long (1 hour) as the place is pretty small. Â The owner (completely down to earth and unassuming. Â We even traded gaming ideas as my younger daughter was getting bored) and the waiters were very nice and tried to make us comfortable during the wait. Â They also explained that they have a policy of not rushing their customers, which is completely understandable. Â Therefore, I strongly recommend a reservation during the weekends. The second visit was because we liked the food and raved about it so some other family members wanted to try it out. The food is very good and fresh and was always served with a smile. Â The Fiery roll is their popular roll. Â Our favorite is the 249 roll. Â We also liked their Thai spring rolls and of course, their fried banana with green tea ice cream. Â The decor was perfect for the neighborhood. Â The overall ambiance is very comfortable and nice. Â Our favorite seating is by the lighted, color changing, bubbling tank.

Pizza at Luzzo's is great. Â But when I called to put in my order today, they quoted me a new - different (higher) price than at their website. Â Normally I do not quibble about two dollars, but this time I happened Â to have the exact change for my pizza, tax + delivery tip (the place is cash only and so is delivery). Â  When I pointed out that the price on their own website is different, they said that the online menu is for a different location! Â Well, it its not, it has a little map next to the menu and the phone # of the 1st ave place. Â  Not a nice way to treat someone that orders from your shop once a week, Luzzo's. Having something else tonight.

The dumplings and chinese pizza are amazing. Â Great place to go for cheap eats and good Chinese food. Seating is very tight (only ~6 bar stools and counter) so expect to go someplace else to eat...not a big deal.

Came here twice and I still adore this place. Definitely a culinary experience. They switch the menu every few months so it's like trying a new restaurant every time i come here. Great for date night and great for a friendly reunion. The walls had interesting paintings and the garden seating is so pretty. 1) First time was for my 1 year anniversary and everything tasted wonderful. They started us out with complimentary sweet potato soup served in little cups, fish kampachi (very fresh), pork belly with apples and cinnamon (delightful), spare ribs with strawberries and pomegranate (sweet), foie gras (Personally not a big fan of it but my now ex-boyfriend loved it), scallops (super top choice), fatty tuna on fried eggplants ( not greasy at all), chicken with hosin sauce (a bit of a rip off because I can do it at home, but it was still good), and sweetbread (very rubbery...and I finally found out what sweetbread was actually made of). 2) Second time was with friends. We ordered almost the same as above but they Traif twisted some of the flavors. Quite interesting because we ordered the same dish as I did last time but the flavor were completely different (in a very good way). I tried their bacon donut with their home made coffee ice cream. I wished they sold their ice cream for takeout because it was delicious. Will be back soon!

Do you love bourbon and whiskey? YES - Go to Post Office right now. Order yourself a cocktail and the most amazing pulled pork sandwich you will ever experience. NO - Doesn't matter. Go to Post Office right now. Order yourself a glass of water and the most amazing pulled pork sandwich you will ever experience. And if you're not in the mood for pulled pork, go for the chicken liver sandwich. It's equally delicious and definitely worth trying. Â You also must try the steak tartare. It's packed with flavor and very generously portioned. For food this good and at prices from $5-14, it might be one of the best places in williamsburg to grab a drink and some grub.

As a long-time customer of Perry St, I'm quite disappointed with their placement of new tables in an area directly in front of the entry that use to be the lounge / waiting area. Really, one of the primary reasons one comes here is because of how relaxing of a restaurant Perry St is. The design is first class, the space is quiet, and the staff consistently delivers on creating a smooth (even "transportive") dining experience. It's no accident that it has been listed on Zagat's list of restaurants best for quiet conversation. However, I've always had to request a "table away from the back" of the restaurant in order to ensure I was not blessed with a view of the restrooms. When I made this most recent request, I arrived to find that I was to be seated less than 2 feet from the front door, on a bench (not even a proper chair!). We left immediately. I sincerely hope that management re-evaluates table placement because I'm truly at a loss as to how I can book a reservation here and ensure a good table. Seems like a crap shoot at this point now that seating both in the back and the front are sub par. I guess I shall request a table "in the middle" of the room? Management, please read this and don't ruin the true value that Perry St has consistently offered over the years: Gorgeous, quiet surroundings and respect for the customer. I'd rather you raise your prices than continue with these new, horribly-placed tables.

Very decent Cantonese-style food. The place, however, is nothing to look at. The tables and floors looked like they had a layer of grease on them. But...pretty typical of Chinese places, I say. The food is great, so just overlook these minor details. The service was a bit spotty. It took a long time to flag down a server. That is pretty weird. The rundown: Wonton with mein (wontons were good, but I was not a big fan of the accompanying noodles) braised tofu (nothing special, but you got your daily serving of veggies) Amoy chow mai fun with pickled veggies (this dish was excellent, I am still salivating over it!) Next time I want to come try their congee and also try their dishes that are listed on the wall (only in Chinese).

Consistently decent since its opening. This has become one of our go-to brunch spots when in the neighborhood, and it's all about the pizza. On a warm day, the glass garage-style doors create an inviting atmosphere both inside and out. Sidewalk tables are quick to fill up with tourists wanting to see a "Top Chef Master." Sadly, you will find that crowd here waiting for a glance at JW, as well as legit New Yorkers noshing on decent food from a small and fairly basic menu of pizzas and other Italian and New American fare. Â  We generally stick to pastas and pizzas, and often choose from specials. The cheese menu is tiny and basic. Don't expect any standouts here. It's kid-friendly which is great when my niece and nephew are in-tow. Staff is nice if not a tad slow. Overall an ok spot for a quick lunch or brunch. Skip dinner, and keep your expectations in check.

The fresh noodles are really excellent, 5 stars. The Mt Qi Sour Broth is really great, 4 stars. The Mt Qi Beef and Peas fixins? Barely passable, 2 stars :( Similarly, the dumpling soup did not have that much flavor in the broth, but the dumplings were good. The place is not consistent and does not have one dish that is flawless in every way. The only way to achieve this may be to get the dry noodles. I also saw them kicking around an empty vat labeled MSG. Fun. Time to try Lam Zhou to see if they have a better package deal: soup, noodles and fixins.

This burrito is sad. You are eating a sad burrito. All y'all thinking that this place is closer to a real taqueria than to Chipotle need your head examined or a plane ticket, straight up. Â Imagine a straight line, with "real taqueria" on the left, "Chipotle" on the right, and you find Dos Toros on the gringo side of the equation. Â Truth. That said, you can do worse, and my advice is to stick to the tacos, skip the bland/watery guacamole, and don't overlook the cheap beers.
Love this food!! Non greasy, flavorful, good prices= yum a thon! Good place for gluten free vegetarians!
Food and service were both great. Kinda expensive though. $50 for a piece of fish.

Another Restaurant Week try out. Headed here for lunch and even though we made 2 separate reservations for our group, they were nice enough to put both tables together. The place was crowded on a weekday at 2PM. Once our party of 12 was seated, we received bread and olive oil. We all ordered from the menu and here's what I tasted: -oxtail terrine and bitter greens: consistency similar to pate and flavorful -pureed white bean soup: salty with a few whole white beans and pasta at bottom. Seemed to be lacking something... -house made pasta with Heritage pork ragu: perfectly cooked and tasting pasta with tender and chewy slivers of pork -veal meatball with swiss chard and chickpeas: meatball was dry, tough and very dense -house cured cod in winter vegetable soup: tasty broth -tartufino: like a chocolate truffle, get this if you like chocolate -ricotta with honey: delightfully light and refreshing I felt the food was mediocre. Perhaps the dishes from the non-Restaurant week is a true testament to the quality of this place. Service was attentive and accommodating. Bathroom cramped but clean.

Last year I was delivering an ebay package around the corner at about 5:30 in the evening it was cold and it started to rain. Â I ducked into Clinton Street, No waiting and had the Best Blueberry Pancakes ever! Â For dinner. Â Loved it. My advice don't follow crowds in NYC to brunch & Sat night movies. Movie mattinee and brunch for dinner. Â Perfect. Â No waiting. No worries:)

Completely pedestrian.... Hadn't been in over a year so decided to pay them a visit last Saturday. Â definitely remember Landmarc being much better in the past than what we experienced Saturday night. Â It's just such a basic and boring menu, and the real disappointment came from the fact that these basic weren't even executed well. Â Goat cheese profiteroles and salad to start...simply nothing special at all. Â Entrees were salmon and hangar steak...the hangar steak was tougher than most I've had at much better places like Little Giant and Perilla to name a few. Â The salmon just was completely straightforward, not accompanied by anything exciting or creative. Â  The restaurant prophet says....pass up Landmarc for Duane Park, Locanda Verde or Bouley upstairs. Â We won't be needing to go back to Landmarc a third time. Â I'm out!

Great, laidback place to grab a beer and some grub. Don't let the fact that it's a bar fool you--the food here is a must! I've had the burger, pork sandwich and grilled cheese and everything's been super fresh and totally beyond what I expected (even the pickles on the burger are crazy good). And they come with a mountain of fries which are totally TO DIE FOR! On top of that, there's a great selection of brews (which changes a lot so don't get too tied to a fav.) to wash it all down.
Amazing brunch! The food tastes as good as it looks. For drinks, try the fraise made with fresh strawberries and celery--really refreshing and delicious.
I love their food and desserts. However the last brownie I had tasted like fridge..yuk!

Brunch it up! This LES spot is perfect for brunch with a little Mediterranean thrown in. Â I spotted this place on Yelp right away based on its ratings and sheer number of reviews. Easily points at a consistently good meal and I was not disappointed. Stopped here on a Tuesday morning and we were seated right away. Â Cute spot with three rooms of tables. Â Staff was smiley and prompt with service with clear expectations for all staff members to take care of their "room." For my brunch, I selected the poached egg with potato pancake. Â It also came with smoked salmon and a cucumber dill yogurt sauce. Â The dish overall was a home run and a good reason to come to this Cafe. Â The eggs were perfectly poached with the delicious ewey gewey egg yolk and the potato pancake was a crisp potato perfection. Â The two complemented each other very well. Â To me the salmon with dill sauce was nice add on to the side salad but I saw many people eating it with the egg and potato as well. Â It also came with two pieces of toast. Â I had the americano coffee and am definitely interested in their other coffee options as the lattes and espressos looked yummy!

One of my favorite brunch spots in the city. If you want sweet, look no further than the Vanilla Bean French Toast. Sublime. If you're feeling savory, one of the eggs Benedict variations - the Johnny (corn pancakes!) or the Lobster (lobster!) Their salads are also on point.

I went after lunchtime on a weekday. Â Their menu is interesting and you can tell management puts thought into what and how they serve. Â The churrasco was amazing. Â The server was very nice and patient with my questions. Â The food came very quickly too. Â The rice and beans were to be expected. Â I recommend trying this restaurant.

Despite waiting for ages for a table and enduring my tipsy friends during my self imposed dry month Highlands managed to surprise me. The bar scene was very 'Manhattan' and single girls could be interested by the high ratio of men drawn in by the scotch selection which was vast and reasonably priced. I would come here specifically for the scotch eggs which were fantastic but everything I tasted was very good. Perhaps I wasn't expecting that or perhaps it was memories of celebrating Burns night as a kid but everything gave me a warm fuzzy feeling and I left sober and very happy which is a rare combination for in English boy.

*Most delicious food ever tasted* The chef does an amazing job at creating experimental dishes with savoring taste that will just leave you flabbergasted. The ice cubed tequilas are a must try as well. Everything there was just super awesome. Can't wait to go there again.

After searching for places to satisfy my BBQ craving, decided to give this spot a try, based on the number of reviews and how highly it's rated. Walked into a cozy space with semi dim lighting. The line was about 20+ people deep but didn't wait more than 20min. Went with the bbq brisket sandwich (with bread), a small side of burnt end baked beans, and a small side of sweet potato casserole. The workers were friendly and very helpful with recommendations. I split this order with a friend and it was filling for both of us. The brisket is cooked perfectly! Literally melts when you bite it. The baked beans with burnt ends is amazing. I'm not normally a fan of beans but if they always tasted like this, I'm sure I would be. The casserole was great as Â well. With pieces of pecan, the texture was nice. All three complemented each other really well. A filling meal for two in New York for only Â $16? Not bad at all. I'm originally from Cali and I'd definitely prefer this over Phils'. Yep, I said it! Would love to come back!

Went to Cafeteria a few days ago, and although the atmosphere and ambience of the restaurant was nice, the food was not up to par as all the reviews say. The service was not as bad as most state. I was expecting to be served by pretentious waiters, but I was caught by surprise when they served no different than a regular restaurant. The staff was polite, but a bit slow and that may have been due to the fully packed hotspot. As for the food, I ordered the macaroni and cheese with bacon because of the great reviews for it. I was fully disappointed by my order. It was an exceptionally creamy macaroni and cheese, but definitely nothing to write home about. The macaroni itself was overcooked and mushy. Definitely not mind blowing. Â I also ordered a side of green beans and garlic. At least this was up to par, but I'd like to think its difficult to screw up green beans. A friend of mine ordered the special for the day which was the fried catfish. The main protein was delicious. Perfectly breaded and seasoned. As for the the corn bread, collard greens, and whipped sweet potatoes that came with the catfish, I must speak highly against it. The corn bread tasted like some awful health food that was dry and without flavor. The collard greens were extremely salty. (Felt like I was going to have a spurt of high blood pressure when I tried them) And the sweet potatoes were ordinary and bland. I was expecting maybe a hint of butter or a hint of brown sugar, but it was definitely a disappointment as well. I'd say the restaurant is worth going to once just to experience it. But, I know I have no plans of returning again. I can find a much better restaurant with much better food for a better value.

It would have been tasty but they put spicy sauce all over my gyro when I said ONLY tzaziki! I'm one of the few weird people in the world who just doesn't like spicy food so I didn't enjoy my lunch AT ALL. Plus the side of grape leaves I ordered were tough, not easy to bite through. Extremely fast service but they need to focus more on getting the order right, sorry Uncle Gussy

The person who recommended this place said it right - it's a place that you should go if you're in the neighborhood but it isn't so good that you have to come down to East Village to eat it. The fries were really well cooked - crispy on the outside but still some softness inside. We got the mango chutney and then the house sauce along with onions/jalapenos with one order. It was enough to fill my cousin and me up - it was a solid midafternoon snack/appetizer amount. We were lucky enough to grab a seat but there is severely limited seating, so people should plan on taking it to go.

It's very understated Japanese and despite the method of getting in, bohemian is a pretty awesome place. Things we loved: oysters, mini burgers, short rib waygu sashimi Not really that big fans of the froie grois soup as it was cold. Â That's just my preference. Would highly recommend the Nigori Sake! Will be trying Bohemian again

Cute, cultured looking place in the heart of Manhattan's culture-free zone, otherwise known as Midtown. Salads and paini are equally good, although they aren't as healthy as I'd like to pretend. My biggest complaint is that the line gets pretty long during lunch-rush, but I suppose that's a sign of a good spot.

I've come here for happy hour a few times. Great happy hour and it goes on till 10. $3 yeungling bottles and $6 lychee martinis and other drinks (used to be $5 but they upped the price). Service was really good and friendly. Sometimes this place can get pretty crowded. Haven't tried their Asian themed food yet but I always come for the drinks anyway.

So delicious! Was meeting a friend here for brunch and arrived about 15 minutes early. The staff was so friendly and accommodating, let me hang out and read for awhile and even brought complimentary watermelon slices to the table. On top of exceptionally friendly service, the food is AMAZING! It is the most flavorful simple food. Their special was a chicken wrap with eggplant, hummus and a romaine salad. It was moist and flavored perfectly. The prices are also ridiculously reasonable. A huge wrap and a side salad was $6.75. I think the most expensive thing on the menu was like $12. At the end of the meal they bring you complimentary cookies as well. Just a really nice place to grab lunch or dinner. Warning. Keep your eyes peeled for it though. My friend and I both walked by it! If you miss it, walk turn around and go back. So worth it!!!!

I love the chicken meatballs here! Its so yummy. If you can, I recomend doing take out. They don't take reservations, and its a pretty small place. Like most places, you can put your name down and they will call you when your table is ready. I prefer take out because the service isn't that great. Espeically during peak hours. I had a bad experience were the waitress took our order and then just never came back. We had to flag people down and basically the bus boys became our waiters. They were helpful, but the actually waitress was not. The food is still really good though.

Adobada Tacos!!!!!!!!!!! I tried all four of their tacos but this is their best one and the only one that matters. Â They were all good but adobada made the biggest impact. Â I'd rather get three adobadas than getting a variety. Â  The adobada is a marinated rotisserie pork with pineapple (similar to al pastor) on a handmade corn tortilla. Â It's so thinly sliced, juicy, a little fatty, sexy, buttery and tasty. You can get the either the taco for $3 or the quesadilla (a bigger taco with cheese) for $4, both are amazing. Â  Wash it down with some horchata or Mexican coca cola and your day just got better. The line moves quick and the staff is super chill and friendly. Â  No seats or tables. Â Minimal communal counter space. Â Eat standing or you can walk around the chelsea market and find a bench to sit and eat.

amazing food. Â Loud & lively atmosphere. interesting cocktails served in cute little mason jars. Â the 2 hour wait for 2 people was a bit ridiculous... BUT we enjoyed everything we ordered. i would have given maybe 5 stars if not for the ridic. wait. Â  which includes: -radishes with sea salt & butter Â .... if you haven't jumped on the radish bandwagon, now is the time to do so. -charcuterie ... came with prosciutto, spicy chorizo & sopressata served with a side of delicious warm and crusty bread. Â Damn, why am i eating bread when i just ordered pizza & pasta? Â no such thing as carb overload. -orecchiette pasta with braised goat... pasta perfectly chewy, spicy & the goat was awesome. Â I would order this again for sure. Â  -margherita pizza ... the crust was soft and chewy.... while the pizza was salty, gooey with mozzarella and chili oil was just over the goddamn top. (SO GOOD). Â the pizzas are their specialty here...not to be missed. Â  MMM, mmm & mmmmm. Â Once you get seats here, the vibe is pretty casual and rambunctious. Â Live it and enjoy it.

I wish this place was a little closer to my place or else I'd be a regular here on weekends! I brought my parents here for a brunch once, and I was pretty impressed. It strangely reminded me of Brooklyn w/ its decor and ambiance.

dont look any further for the best Napoli style pizza! worth the wait. A bit of wait, but it was worth it!! lots of fresh toppings (get the classic small pie with extra cheese and mushrooms, amazing!)

it was a Saturday and yes i wanted to try something different and whats more different than Nepalis food. the Place is small and can accommodate about 20 people. If you are going there definitely get the Momo. i got the fried ones and they were really good. As for the main course i had the chasha shamdey and found it not to be spicy but do order the Chille chicken, it was awesome. all in all i would try this place if you are looking to get a taste of Nepal.

Oh my gosh. Those dumplings were fantastic. I came here because my mom's coworker recommended it. I must say though that the non-dumpling dishes that we ordered were rather bland. Their string beans were undercooked and very tasteless; my family only ate half the dish and didn't even bother to consider taking it home with us. So when you come here, JUST EAT THE DUMPLINGS.

We arrived 10 minutes early for our 7:15 reservation last Wednesday and were told they were running on time. But they weren't. We stood at the end of the bar and watched tables remain empty. As we had been staring at 2 empty four tops for a while we asked why we couldn't be seated. We were then offered "our" table in the bar. (I had specifically requested ahead of time not to sit in the bar area and had been told we wouldn't) Â They were 3 deep at the bar, it was very noisy and the people Â encroached on the diners in the area. We were told we would have to wait longer if we wanted the main room. Tables were kept empty because they were ramping up. they were open 6 weeks, so we didn't understand that. They need to fix the reservation system as it was frustrating and a bad start to the evening. perhaps spread out the reservations more if you are slow and want to keep tables empty. Â We were eventually seated at a table that had been empty for a half hour. We had: crab risotto, large size Â - a bit mushy, but tasty, portion small for the large size sausage pizza - just okay, have had much better octopus - very tender and tasty, just a meager portion orata - person really liked it Kale paella - the hit of the evening and the reason they got 3 stars and why we would return Pork chop - seasoning is a bit overwhelming steak - also enjoyed by the person potatoes - very salty but tasty, we liked them we did not have dessert.

Love the brunch there, they have great Salmon Benedict with an excellent sauce. They even offer a single side pancake if you want some sweet with your salty meal. Dinner is also very good. their fish dishes are light and well rounded. Overall a great little spot

They got hit hard by Hurricane Sandy, but they are open!! Â (Currently cash only). While seated, you can look at the wall and see the water marks from the flooding. Their kitchen was devastated, but they cleaned up and repaired and everything is brand spanking new. (Yay!!) They have a limited menu, but it's still a wide selection of food and drink. My favorites include the "skinny" margarita (100 cal.) and deep fried okra (see, it all balances out. Well, that's what I tell myself). They offer a decent variety of vegetarian and a couple vegan menu items too (veg chili, black bean tacos, salads, etc. etc.). The "Evacuation Zone Burrito Bowl" was too much for me to finish, but I dug it. Â Check out the Post Sandy menu online. Oh, and don't forget Taco Tuesdays either ($2 tacos)! I've enjoyed many black bean tacos and margaritas or mojitos here. *Burp* Just go now and support a local business. These folks are super nice and worth it.

Good food and wine. Â The pita dip sampler thing was good, but the hummus had a weird texture. Â Service was good, atmosphere was great, menu was varied enough to keep things interesting. Â Would definitely go again.

My wife and I corrected a long oversight in having a lovely dinner at Drunken Munkey last night! Â The place was buzzing and full (always a good sign!). Â Arun told us it would be a few minutes for a table, and offered us a stool at the bar where we had drinks while we waited. Â The drinks were fantastic! Â I had the Indian spiced old fashioned, a classic old fashioned with indian spice infused simple syrup. Â A subtle, but really nice touch that perfectly fit the theme of this British Colonial Indian spot! Â My wife had the punch, which was not too sweet, an had a really clean fruit finish. Â  While we waited, one of my favorite underrated aspects of dining is the music choices. Â An amazing mix of Talking Heads, Billy Joel, Jamiroquai, the Beatles, and a few Bollywood favorites played throughout the night. Â Other reviews have said the music was too loud, but either the owners turned it down, or the reviews are unfounded, because the volume was perfect if not a little soft. We hadn't finished our drinks yet, when Arun showed us to our table. Â We started with the fried okra and panipuri. Â Both were terrific, with the latter as a particularly nice starter. Â The panipuri shell was crisp and the puri water was floral and refreshing. Â For our entrees we split the lamb chops and the shrimp curry. Â The chops were perfectly cooked, with a really nice char. Â The meat was not gamey nor fatty, and the potatoes and green beans on the side were also very flavorful. Â The shrimp curry was my favorite. Â The rice is clearly something that is not a throwaway here--it is cooked with care and the finished product is a rich jasmine rice where every grain is perfect. Â That said, the highlight was the curry. Â It is a rich deep curry flavor, not too spicy (although Â we love spice!), and after finishing the shrimp, we sopped up every remaining drop with the soft, charred naan. Â Each entree came with a very spicy chili pepper, which we chopped up and put in the curry which gave it some serious bite! For dessert we had the rum ball, a gooey rich rum and chocolate cake ball. Â All in all, we loved it here and will no doubt be returning soon!

Best breakfast in the city: civilized, quiet, and perfectly Continental. I usually go for the bowl of cafe au lait, a perfectly buttery croissant, and maybe the soft boiled egg avec soldiers. Â It's the best way to start a day of shopping, with a relaxing coffee and browsing the paper.

Woohoo! Â As good as it gets! is the perfect way to describe Cafe Katja. Â I can not speak highly enough about this cozy Austrian restaurant in the LES. Â After hearing rave reviews about this spot for months i reluctantly agreed to give it a shot. Â My previous experience with German/Austrian food was mostly from beer gardens so I was expecting mediocre bratwurst and sauerkraut and I wasn't very excited. Â  Cafe Katja is nothing like any other restaurant I have been to in New York. Â Every single item you eat here will be the "best" of that item you have ever had whether it be the unique and delicious spatzle, quark dumplings, or pork belly or the more ordinary meatballs and roasted carrots. Â I've never been so happy to pay for roasted carrots in my life! It is definitely worth starting with a large beer or glass of wine and a few pretzels for the table. Â I would also recommend taking a look at the "Specials" board as it led to me eating one of the best heirloom tomato salads I have ever had. Ultimately what cuts Cafe Katja above the rest is not just the amazing food but the intimate and festive environment. Â On any given night you will find this place full of people engaging in gluttonous eating and drinking and laughing and smiling the whole way through. Â Adding to the festivities are the waitresses who are a blast to be around- they love their environment and they make you love it too. Cafe Katja should be on every ones list of "must try" restaurants and once you do I'm sure it'll quickly become an old favorite.

Another Tapas spot that my friend recommended to go for dinner. Ambience is nice and the restaurant is cozy. We had a fairly large group so we just ordered a lot of different dishes. The restaurant was packed but I could've sworn I only saw two waiters. One wasn't dressed as one so I assumed he was the owner or manager helping out on the night. The food was ok but the service was very slow. They even forgot to bring out some of the dishes we ordered. However, biggest disappointment was that they don't serve Sangria by the pitcher. You serious bro? Never seen that before. Probably not gonna come here again. Food: B Â  Portions: C Service: C Ambience: B- Price: B

NO SIGN ON THE OUTSIDE! We walked right by it. This came recommended by a coworker. We checked out Bo Concept Art First Thursdays in DUMBO so we figured we'd swing by for dinner. It's right near Henry's End, a restaurant that serves an assortment of Wild Game meats daily. Waiters are dressed in white button downs with red ties tucked into their shirts, adorned in red aprons. No wait on a Thursday Night at 7pm. Cash only. This is Italian fare done right with affordable prices. Kudos. I'll be back. Bread - half a ciabatta loaf sliced, spicy EVOO dip w/ crushed tomatoes, parsley, CRACK! DAILY SPECIALS -Shrimp, Mussels, Clams in broth (~$15) - soup tasted like Chinese broth, not oily at all, seafood was yum, good starter -Stuffed Seppialini (~$12) - came in the form of one big piece, ample tomato sauce, stuffed w/ breading, one piece of grilled french bread, seppia is cuttlefish -Pappardelle (~$12) - heavily infused w/ mushroom sauce, i'm a huge sucker for this pasta, esp when homemade, so good ENTREE -Pork Chop ($13) [served with pickled hot cherry peppers] - a tad over done aka dry, nice char on outside, not crazy about hot cherry peppers w/ it, also served w/ a parmesan mash WINE -Fume Blanc ($10 x 2) - perfect accompaniment to this meal Total came out to $46/pp after everything

Good food that offers flexibility on the menu. Although they come in small portion it's not good for peeps who wanna pig out since its kinda pricey, taste of food is mediocre but if you wanna guzzle or booze up, welcome! Staff are good and courteous. If you wanna experience the real taste of Filipino dishes this is not the place. It's Pinoy dishes made fancy...

Coming from Houston where there's a plethora of authentic banh mi shops where the bread is baked fresh from the oven, thus I'm a bit biased when it comes to banh mi. For me, Banh Mi Saigon was so so.. not that impressive. The baguette itself fell apart with each bite.
The diver scallops were a delicious way to start and by far the biggest pork chop I've ever had. The food couldn't have been better, the service was spot on and the ambiance was perfect.

This is one of my favorite Greek restaurants and I drive all the way from Long Island to eat here. The food is consistently delicious and everything is fresh. I love the fried calamari, grilled octopus and the stuffed shrimp. The peasant Greek salad is great as well. There usually is a long wait but it is well worth it! I also love that they give you free dessert at the end of your meal. Come here and you will not be disappointed!

Ate here for lunch. The tacos flavor wise were spot on delicious. The staff was friendly and quick. However the reason I am giving this 4 stars is that my order was not right ordered 2 beef tacos and received two chicken instead. On a good note I will be coming back again.
It's ok. I dont see the big hoopla about this place. The price per slice is more expensive than Manhattan. I wish them good luck but it's not for me.

This place was amazing! Â I had a Girl's Brunch outing here. The service was good and the drinks were amazing! Â They offer unlimited drinks for $14 for 1.5 hours. Well worth it. My girlfriends said it was the best Latin food ever. I love the chicken empanadas. You can tell they were made with love, very flaky and yummy. They tasted more like a pastry. This place highly recommended, a definite repeat!

Hands down one of the best meals I have ever had. To start, the ambiance of the place is great, its nice but not intimidating and you feel cozy. For how packed it was, my table was private and in a great spot in the restaurant. The staff is also beyond helpful and the service was great from the bartender to all the waiters that assisted. The time it took for each course was perfectly laid out and I never felt rushed. Each thing we ordered was better than the dish before. We started with the small bar plates, 3 for like 17 bucks. The eggplant, burrata, and beef crudo. The sizes were perfect for two people to share without getting too stuffed. Then for appetizer I ordered the octopus and my sister got the shrimp. This was hands down the best octopus I have ever tasted, and the flavor was really unique; if you like octopus you absolutely need to order this dish. I tasted the shrimp and loved it also! Heavy on the garlic but I love garlic so to me it was perfect. For the main course we shared the paella and the charred beef. Both were soo good and i was genuinely upset when there was nothing left. The beef was cooked to perfection and it was so flavorful. The paella was just hands down delicious and had a cool spin to the dish. The rice was crusted on the bottom which added a great texture. Both were great choices and i highly recommend either. For dessert my sister ordered blackberry crostata which was AMAZING. The first bite had everything you could ever want in a dessert, warm, cold, salty and sweet (I am gluten intolerant and knew it advance I was going to cheat throughout this entire meal and it was well worth it). You cannot leave this restaurant without trying this dessert. They also gave complimentary dessert snacks and a small glass of wine. Amazing meal, dying to go back and worth the month wait between calling for the reservation and actually going to dine!

It's definitely a little pricier than just a regular lunch, but it is so, so good. I've tried the brisket, pork and one of the specials they had (bison - delicious!). The pulled pork was among the best I've ever had, anywhere. And it is plenty of food, whether you get the tacos or burrito you will be FULL. Mmmmmmm.

This pizza is amazing, probably the BEST I've ever had. HOWEVER, it doesn't excuse the staff. My friend and I were surprised that during rush hour, there was no wait for a table for 2. The hostess walked a mile ahead of us. She had started walking back from the table before we even got there. The waitress was not that great. Who brings soda before the waters? And another waiter spilled water on the floor, on my foot and my flipflops. And he just left it there. We said thank you to our waitress as we left, and she didn't even have the courtesy to nod her head or smile or anything. She ignored us and went to the next guest. Normally, I wouldn't mind that in such a popular place, but it really wasn't even that busy. Definitely need to up their game in customer service.
For the cheap price this food actually tastes very good. The lamb is superb, the guys are very friendly. Definitely worth the long lines!!!!
Yuck!! Was not impressed at all. Overpriced chicken bits that did not inspire my palette at all. McDonalds taste better and I hate McDonald's.

Not much new to add. Most of the dishes we ordered were fairly standard, and the staff certainly wants to move you in and out. Now to thier claim to fame, the soup dumplings. The pork dumplings were delish and the crab dumplings were superb. Â A must try if you're out in New York.

I cannot say enough good things about Stella 34! The restaurant is beautiful, immaculate and comfortable, which is out of place for it's location - the heart of midtown! Upon entering the space, you forget that you are at "the largest store in the world" and in the heart of one of the busiest cities in the world. The staff is very friendly and the service, first class! My family and I decided to go all out for this dinner! We got the meatballs, rice balls, calamari and the polenta for starters. All were divine! A few friends raved about the meatballs, so naturally we had to try them! And now I too will be raving! I got the Spaghettini and I do not have enough words in my vocabulary to describe what was going on in my head when I took my first bites! The sauce is simply perfect. Who knew you could have the perfect amount of spice, lemon, red sauce and crunch all in a seemingly simple pasta dish! I would eat this every day if I could! For dessert, gelati. Wow. I don't think there was a flavor that was undesired by my table! Apparently, it's flown in from Florence - delicious! I also ordered the tiramisu (because why not!) At first, I wondered what it was, because it certainly did not look like tiramisu! They should rename this dish "Deconstructed Tiramisu" By far one of the best I've had, and I consider myself a tiramisu conoseur. During our meal, we were greeted by the general manager, Matthew. This wasn't your typical "manager walks around to make sure the servers are doing their job" talk. He already knew everyone was already doing exactly what they were supposed to be doing! He simply wanted to have a chat! He was warm, inviting and genuine, much like the character of this restaurant. Please, if you visit one restaurant in NYC, make it this one!

Pinnacle of Perfection -- Not sure you can even call this pizza, lest you create confusion by lumping it together with "everything else" ... you've got your neighborhood slice joints ("2 slices and a coke for $5!"), your cut-above slice joints (i.e., "Joe's Pizza"), and then you have this amazingly beautiful ... something ... from Grimaldi's. Â Would eat here every day if I didn't have to spend my whole life in line.

SCRATCHbread make delicious focaccia featuring a crispy greasy bottom, and delicious pizza, which is the focaccia with stuff on top. The next day it is still yum but not delicious because the crispy underside becomes soggy and oily. They make a yum but not delicious brownie with texture like a dense flourless cake and something a bit like icing in the middle. I prefer gooey brownies so you might love it nonetheless. They make a plantain and mole muffin-thing (the Bed-Stuy version of banana and chocolate?) but that wasn't out of the oven yet. The chai cinnamon bun was a bit frightening - it has large crumbs of coffee bean in with the sticky yumness and I got tired of those quickly. Worse was the black pepper (which they also use on the foccacia) - I really disliked the strong flavor of the pepper and wish they'd used jalapeno or something else. I couldn't finish the bun's sticky yumness due to the coffee and pepper which is unprecedented in my history of consuming sweet things.

Was on The Best Thing I Ever Ate (in a bowl), and I love noodles, so I went to check it out with my girls. Â It's a hole in the wall, so if you're looking for ambiance, this isn't the place. Â But the noodle soup was delicious! Â The guy in the kitchen can be seen through the door slapping the noodles, which is cool. Â They come out piping hot and soft and delicious. Â would be a great meal for a cold, rainy night like when i went, or when you have a cold. Â the dumpling appetizers were so good we got a 2nd order, and wanted a 3rd. Â oh, and it's super cheap. Â we paid like $20 for 2 appetizers and 3 bowls of soup. Â the restaurant is tiny, so not good for groups
In the words of a drunk friend at 4 in the morning, "It's sooooooo goooooood!"

If you're looking for a low-key, quiet, romantic spot to spend the evening, this is it. Â It's a little out-of-the-way, being in Alphabet City, but that's part of the charm and the appeal. Â  My date and I went on a Sunday night at 7:30 and were one of only three couples there. Â The bartender/waiter was helpful with wine suggestions and was attentive to our needs, while still giving us space to talk and enjoy a long, relaxed meal. Â  I got the margherita pizza, and he got the baked meatballs. Â Both were total perfection. Â They have a couple of sparkling wines, if that's your persuasion. Â I had two glasses of the Malbec and loved it. Hope to visit again soon!

As an Italian citizen, I will readily admit that I am an Italian snob having grown up with fresh cooked excellent Italian food. As a result, my wife and I actually tabulated and in the six years we have known each other we have been out to eat Italian less than a dozen times. This place was without a doubt the best place for Italian that we had. The ceviche was great and the olive oil cake is something that my wife has replicated at home.

If you're planning to dine in here, be aware that the quarters are VERY tight. I would recommend coming here with a very good friend or someone you've been with for at least five dates. This isn't the spot for romance or catching up with someone you haven't seen in years. It feels that Wild Edibles' aim is to educate consumers about where fish come from. Both the menu and the fish counter signs have ratings that allow consumers to choose - providing information about how "sustainable" the fish's sourcing might be. Keep in mind that you can't come here assuming that all the fish is sustainably sourced - they leave that up to you. I ate here for dinner at the bar, and had great service. The food was delish - I had the trout, which was covered with salad (that had bacon and apple slices in it). I asked the waiter to recommend a red wine to pair with it, and he delivered. As one of the other reviewers mentioned, it doesn't smell fishy in here. However, if you eat at the bar, just keep in mind that the dead fish will be staring at you while you eat their comrade. ;) A little spendy, but worth the bucks.

When I first walked in I thought it was going to be the same old over-seasoned Puerto Rican food that you would get at the local Cuchifrito. To my surprise, the food was excellent. I went there with a few guys from work and all had good things to say about the food. The wait is a little longer than your average PR or Dominican restaurant but well worth it. Everything is fresh and seasoned perfectly. The staff is friendly and the LES history covers its walls. The seating is limited and the place kind of tight. They only accept cash, but who cares? The food is great.

Super crowded!! We came to see what the buzz was all about. The fries came in neat paper cones, and the tables even have holes so you can stick your cones into them. These fries were indeed good, and nice and crispy while really nicely cooked on the inside. But in the end, they were just fries. We ordered Rosemary Garlic Mayo with our fries. The sauce was very good, but it ended up being tastier when mixed with ketchup. You've gotta give them props on all the creative sauces they have on their menu. It was good, but it still blows my mind how a place that just sells fries is so popular. I guess I'm just not a potato person? : ( Go if you enjoy fries. Go if you're near the area. However, if you're just 'meh' about fries and getting here requires quite a trip...it's not worth going out of the way for.
Good place

I am a big fan of Pio Pio, but I decided to try El Pollo Inka Peru with friends. The interior of the restaurant was very appealing and relaxing. We ordered one of the combo specials and extra chicken, beans, and yucca fries. Everything came out in a few minutes and when we were finished, we were glad we decided to eat here. Everything was terrific and the staff was very nice. This was as good as any Peruvian food I have ever had, including Pio Pio. We will definitely be back,
Fantastic food, great room, and solid service make this place a standout. Â For a moment I forgot that I was in Soho, and felt transported to Spain. Just a great overall vibe.
Very good food. Â Well prepared with a good menu. Â Service was excellent, as well.

Man, I'll never forget my first encounter with Prince St. Pizza. I was at my job working hard, probably skipped lunch that day or consumed something really small and unsatisfying...fully knowing that I had a lot of things left on my work to-do list I turned to my coworker and said, "Hey! If you're staying late, wanna have a work dinner party?" - this just basically meant, "Hey, while we're both stressed out and planning on working our butts off till about 9pm or so, can we order dinner so we don't die?" Pizza seemed logical and we ordered from Prince St. Pizza because other department co-workers suggested it. We ordered a square pie because they're my coworkers favorite (and who doesn't like a good square pie?) and we got half pepperoni because I'm usually not a pepperoni person...they're usually hit or miss for me and I can generally do without them...BUT HOLY MOLY PIZZA PEPPERONI!!! This isn't your average pizza pepperoni...THIS IS LIFE. They use these small, thick cut, little pepperoni rounds that are so insanely flavorful and provide a little bit of a spicy kick - but it's not too bad, I mean trust me - I can barely handle spicy things...although I've made great strides in the past 2 years - just last week I ate deep-fried mac n' cheese "atomic fireballs" because they were deep fried in a batter of sriracha and break crumbs, they were deliciously spicy as hell but nothing that drowning them in ranch sauce couldn't help...anywhoo, I digress :). Prince St. Pizza is now one of my favorite (if not THE favorite) Manhattan pizza spots. Their "Pepperoni Square" is by far one of the best pepperoni pizza square pizza things I've ever put into my mouth. DOOOOO IT.

This joint is so warm and so genuine. It delivers a casual intimate hole in the wall atmosphere that makes you feel really really good. They don't serve alcohol but are cool enough to let you go out and pick up a few red stripes down the block and bring them back. Affordable. DELICIOUS. Islands Jerk Chicken will melt you and bring you back to life. By the time your done eating you will be high on perfect Caribbean delight and a little drunk on proportion- there is plenty to take home after! Absolutely perfect experience. Took a first date there and got a second one at the end of the night! And believe me- i'm not that fly- it was The Islands. thhheeeee islanddsssssssss. mmmmmmmmm. go there.
OMG G-O-O-D!!! I have to give credit where credit is due....this place is a real gem in Queens! The Korean BBQ wraps and the Truffled Beet Salad are examples of true oral pleasures!

Great brunch, we were seated right away. Â The vanilla bean toast is all that, and the biscuits and gravy were spot on as well. Â We each had two cocktails, they were that good. Â Excellent service. Â Would definintely come back.
