El Cocotero takes seemingly simple elements - rice, beans, corn, beef, yucca, Â fresh fruit juices - and turns out unbelievably rich dishes. The atmosphere is simple and to the point; a few leafy frond palms, a large Venezuelan flag, an open kitchen and a small yet perfectly divided dining area make for a welcoming restaurant. You may as well have stopped off in a small roadside family restaurant in South America - the waitresses and cooks shout back and forth in Spanish, always with smile and lots of laughing. We had a reservation for 7:30 on Friday night and our table wasn't ready so we enjoyed an appetizer of fried yuca with sour cream and guacamole. The yuca was light and crisp; and when topped with a creamy mix of the two sauces, was the perfect light medley to start the meal. We were quickly seated by the affable and gregarious waitress/hostess/superwoman, Rain, in a small corner both, which was intimate and secluded enough to have a quiet conversation, but also close to the table next to us, leading to an impromptu discussion about food and culture with our dining neighbors. For entrees we chose the Calamari Salad and Pabellon Criollo. Calamari was lightly crisp, lemony and snappy, served over a healthy portion of fresh greens. The Pabellon Criollo, a shredded stewed flank steak with white rice, lightly fried thick slices of plantains and spiced black beans was divine. The meat simply melted, and combined with the rice and beans was satisfyingly filling and rich. The beef was tender and burst with complex flavors, it tasted as though it had been stewing for ages to achieve such a soft texture. We split this dish between two and it was more than enough. A great off-the-beaten-path find in this part of town - homey, appealing and friendly. The owner came to our table at the end of the night to chat, which was a nice welcoming touch. Highly recommended for a small group dinner or a date.

Totto is one of my go to ramen noodle shops. The chicken based stock they use for their ramen is the best I've ever had and brings about a sense of warmth and comfort that other foods just can't match. For those who are not huge fans of tonkatsu ramen b/c it is a bit too rich, this bowl of noodles will have your inner Goldilocks purring with delight. For me, I actually marginally prefer tonkatsu ramen from the likes of Ippudo since I feel it has a greater depth/complexity of flavor, but a nice bowl of chicken based ramen cannot be underestimated. Â  Ambiance is not why you would come here. The line is long (expect 1+ hour) and the space is cramped, but if you are around, I would recommend you leaving your name and checking back later.

You know how researchers starve rats for a long time so the food that they use to condition them becomes the best thing that ever happened to them? Many moons ago, my friend came upon my yelp reviews-- "ARGHHHHH HOW CAN YOU GIVE IPPUDO ONLY FOUR STARS??!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!"Â­. That said, I returned to this place last weekend ready to have my mind re-blown by their ramen. The wait was long (they said 45 minutes, it took more than an hour). Although I can't expect much when I come in on a Saturday night. I'm not good with waiting. My mood becomes exponentially worse when my hunger begins to rear its ugly head. We politely asked the woman at the desk how much longer it was. Her response was a cold, bloody stare. The other woman at the desk shuttled back and forth between the bar and the kitchen delivering drinks. A bit of name confusion w/ another friend we bumped into (Hi Eddie!), shuffling, and bad words later we were seated. We were seated across from a huge mirror wall. I suppose it's nice watching myself eat. We ordered the pork buns, the akamaru modern topped additionally w/ Kakuni Â (MEATTTTT), and the special ramen. The pork buns were delicious. Although it's 8$ for two fist-sized buns. My akamaru modern was sooooo rich. The only thing stopping me from picking up the bowl and spilling its contents into my mouth was how hot the soup was. Special was good as well. Our waiter was polite and quirky. At the end, I was happy and bloated with sodium. But I wouldn't have had it any other way. 5 stars for food, 1 star off for the wait.

I still don't really get the hype of this place. Yes it's good, but not good enough in my opinion to ever wait in a long line for. My first gripe-I really wish they'd invest in some cheddar cheese. I got the bacon burger this time around, it was good (a little heavy on the peppers) but definitely tasty. The fries are OK. Their signature draft beer was good. Â I'm never in a rush to go to shake shack but it's good every once in awhile. I do like that they have some variety on the menu- burgers, veggie options, fries, shakes, ice cream, beer, wine, etc. can't hate it, but don't have it either. This locations employees were great! Also, outdoor seating was a plus but watch out for birds. They were a little too bold for me!
Get the bistro burger Best burger ive had in a LOOOONG TIME sooo juicy and the bacon was so crispy ! Service was great the waiters are nice .. Def a spot to go to if your wanna hit a chill bar

Get the pork buns! My favorite thing to eat was the braised pork belly. It literally melted in my mouth. The ramen was okay, but it was the pork belly that really sold me. As for the restaurant, it has an odd layout but the tables for big groups are really nice.

This was so gross. It took forever for delivery. And when I opened up my food after waiting for 40 minutes for it to finally arrive, there was a very long hair wrapped around the meat. Never again will I eat gyros abd gyros were my favorite food of all time to eat but not anymore because of this place. So I wasted my money and I did not even eat any food because it was gross to look at.

The best dinner I have ever had! Wife and I both loved every dish that we had. We both did the price fixe dinners and was a lot more food than I was expecting. Had foie gras for the first time and it was wonderful. If you are a lobster bisque fan like my wife I definitely suggest that. Best she or I ever had. Recommend Ai Fiori very highly.

The best. Each time I've been there, the owner comes around and makes sure we liked our food. Last time, he even had a special pie made specifically for us because he found out one of us is vegan and he wanted to know what they thought.

No love for butcher bar. Â Burnt ends and pork belly were so fatty neither my husband or i could eat them. Â Other things tried were OK, but in Astoria there are so many amazing places to eat, there's no room for second chances. Â Too fatty, too pricey, moving on!

Why hello cheap and delicious food in NY! You will find this little hole-in-the-wall shop by the line out the door. The steamed pork and chive dumplings were amazing and 8 is enough for one person. The filling was flavorful and the dumpling dough was just the right consistency, not too thick. The sesame pancake was also ok, more doughy than I expected, I'm no sesame pancake expert though. There are a few seats inside, if you can get one, it's fun while you eat to hang out there.

I would say more three and a half stars. Solid drinks (the price helps) but the food isnt that great. Its good... not great though. Don't be deceived by "tapas." Portions are bigger than tapas. Chicken wings have 6-8, Dumplings were 6, the thai lo mien was rather large. We had a big group but shared between 3. Five dishes were ordered for 3 of us and it was too much food. I would do 4 dishes for 3 people. One thing is for sure though, the price is right and the service is good! Good for groups!

Tom's has the best atmosphere of any diner in Brooklyn- but the food is really sub-par, as much as I hate to say it. Get the pancakes.Don't drink the coffee. It's a great early am destination for families on Saturdays- but by 9am it's packed. Closed on Sundays.

One of the best dining experiences I've ever had. I took my wife here for her birthday and despite the fact it was our first time there, we were treated as if we were royalty. Upon arrival, the hostess noted that I asked for a more private table and brought my wife back to the dining room to allow her to choose which table she wanted to be seated. The service was phenomenal throughout the meal. We ordered the 3 course meal. For me, the smoked trout was the best thing that either of us had that night. I ordered halibut entree, which was tender and delicate. My wife ordered the lamb papardelle and a duck confit special, both of which were very rich, but not overpowering. We couldn't decide on our dessert courses and asked our server, Gabe, about the blueberry corn sundae, chocolate bread pudding and peanut butter semifreddo. We ultimately picked the bread pudding and corn sundae, and we were delighted when Gabe brought out the semifreddo as well. Just another little thing that made us feel special. By the way, next time I go back, I'm choosing the semifreddo, although each dessert was incredible. The personalized note from Chef Michael Anthony which I received shortly after dining there again made me feel very special, even if it is standard for this restaurant. Although this experience came with a price, about $100/person before tax and gratuity, it was worth every penny.

What can I say about Blue Ribbon that hasn't been said? Reviews always represent a little insight into who we are, where we have been, and what we are like. Blue Ribbon is a good place, but there are way better sushi places in the world, and at these price points there probably shouldn't be. Overall, it is a place for people that love a scene to be seen at, like sushi a LOT, and don't mind the price of things, in general. The service is pretty consistent, although they really shouldn't allow babies and small children in after 9 or 10pm.. Babies and children whose decibel levels hurt the ears.. Decent sushi, decent sake selections, decent service and a decent ambiance. A decent meal, especially if you are splitting the bill.

I am a huge fan of this place. Â The atmosphere is romantic and cozy, great for a date. Â My favorite on the menu is the shitake mushroom tart. Â Sooo good. Â I've also had the meatball pizza with carmelized onions and the peel & eat shrimp. Â Can I just say that these shrimp must've been the bullies of the shrimp community - they were HUGE and definitely screaming, "Eat me eat me!!"

So my food adventure in New York continues. This was actually suggested by someone when I was looking for new places to eat before my trip. Eight Turn Crepe is in the same block as Rice to Riches and Lombardi's Pizza. So even if I didn't hear about it, I would've easily spotted it since it's right by the 6 train and on the way to Rice Riches. So the dilemma was, how do we fit all that food that these three places are all in the same block? That's what your second stomach is for... for desserts. WHAT WE ORDERED: *Azuki Berries Crepe: The main reason why we picked this: it came with matcha gelato! If there's anything green tea on the menu, that's most likely what I would be ordering 99% of the time. The crepe came with strawberries, azuki beans, whipped yogurt, matcha custard creme, slivered almonds, and pocky sticks. The presentation is obviously super kawaii. It's a little bit more compact compared to the crepes that I get at Harajuku crepes in LA. The texture of the crepe also kinda threw me off a little though since it wasn't the usual smooth crepe texture since it's a rice crepe. Nonetheless, it was delicious! I liked the matcha custard creme with the azuki beans. They also neatly roll the crepe and put it in a paper pouch, so eating it on the go is not such a hot mess. I think ice cream cones are overrated and ice cream or gelato should really be eaten in a crepe cone :D. The restaurant is super tiny. Like two bar seats, tiny. The place was empty when we went, so we were able to enjoy our crepes inside the store and people watch since you're facing Spring St. It's cute how they have "crepes" inside a cloche displayed in their store-front window. It kinda reminded me of Beauty and the Beast... you know when Beast had his precious rose? Another go-to dessert spot for me in New York!

Over hyped. I didn't think the pizza was that great for the long wait prior to entering the store and then for the long wait as they baked the pies fresh. It almost felt like waiting in a movie premiere line, then leaving it to wait in the food stands. Kind of pointless. But that being said, if you are a tourist and interested in going to a NY staple, this is your place. I am guilty as charged since I did come once when I was visiting many years ago! It's like going to time square... you just have to do it!
The filet is the absolute best! This place is consistently delicious and it's cozy and comfortable inside. Definitely worth it for dinner.

This is an excellent place to grab lunch, but only for takeout. Â It gets way too packed in there for any kind of relaxing lunch break. Â But if you want solid korean food, Woorijip has it! Â Yes it is not gourmet, but there is a large selection from pre-packaged items to a buffet bar. Â This is my go to lunch spot when I want asian food. p.s. for first timers, make sure to look around...yes it's packed and stressful, but there's good stuff all over the place!

One of my favorite brunch places in the city. I was drawn here because of how much I like Jane's sister restaurant, The Smith. Make sure to make reservations, because you're going to wait anyways. Prices for brunch items vary from $15-20, with a complimentary drink (bloody mary, OJ, screwdriver, bellini, cocktails). The Benedict Johnny is a bit disappointing, but still good. The Jane is certainly good. I haven't tried the Lobster Benny yet, but it's next on my list. All in all, the food is good but really similar to what you might get at The Smith. The atmosphere is a lot better though, with a funner crowd and a little more lighting.
Best.Pizza.Ever. A simple pie of deliciousness. I can still taste the truffle oil in my dream. 3 girls shared a pie plus a calamari and we were full and happy. Love the quirky decor too!

Authentic Thai cafeteria style with a modern looking decor. Â Just a short walk from the Elmhurst train station. When I walked in, I thought my vision had gone bad and I couldn't read the menu. Â But upon further inspection..they had the menu in both languages, English and Thai! Choose either 2 or 3 mains with rice (only a 50cent difference, I would go with 3 to try other items). I went with the 3 mains $7.50 on top of a mountain of rice. Ordered green curry, string beans, and sweet pork. - Green curry is super spicy, but it has a nice slow burn. I need to stress, they give you a MOUNTAIN OF RICE! I'm glad they did because my green curry needed some starchy grains to wash and soak in the heat! - String beans make me feel like my meal is somewhat healthy without feeling too heavy. - Sweet pork was seasoned well and bursting with flavor. Thai ice tea $2 was bit on the sweet side, but after the ice melted it was okay. Â  Thai ice coffee was strong and sweetened with condensed milk. Â $2.50 Desserts I had Black Sticky Rice with Coconut Milk and Green Tapioca with Coconut Milk, both weren't too sweet, and it had the perfect texture to end my meal. Ample seating if you decide to stay, tables are clean and bathrooms are maintained.

Ok...well, how should I do this one. Â I went to Corner Bistro tonight after a good frind of mine informed me that some survey on Yahoo voted this burger joint as the "best" burger in NYC. Â The reason this came up is the fact that a favorite place of mine, Dumont came in 2nd on this list. Â I was intrigued immediately. I had a day off and some other business to attend toin the area so I figured today was the day to see what all the hype was about. Â I went with my wife and a close friend who happened to live right around the block. Â We stepped into the Greenwich Villiage eatery and it looked like what I had expected, a cramped space filled with bodies. Â That doesn't bother me, in fact, it is encouraging and excites my taste budsknowing that crowds mean good food(except in midtown). Â We waited around 10 minutes for a table. Â I grabbed a round of drinks while we waited and was disaapointed by the tiny draft mugs, maybe 10 oz. at the most but the price matched the pour, two draft Stella's and a pinot grigio for 14 bucks. Â We sat at a great table and was visited by a waiter. It was a very New York customer experience, a la "This place is awesome, I know it, I don't need to sell you on it, if you leave there are two more warm bodies to take your place." Â I ordered the Bistro Burger and a plate of french fries. Â The burger came within 5 minutes. Â The bun was a package bun, s the same you would get at a neighbor's cookout. Â The bottom bun was completely covered by a slice of white raw onion and the patty was placed on top. Â The burger was thick, juicy and cooked well(medium, as I had ordered). Â It was covered with American cheese. Â It was served with bacon,lettuce, tomato and pickles. Â It was a good solid burger and for the low price of aapprox. $7 in Manhattan, it is a bargain. Â However, it does not deserve the high praise of "best burger" in NYC. Â They put no effort into the fries, which are shoestring and in my case luke warm. Â The tiny paper plate the burger arrives on is not a large enough area to manipulate your burger as you see fit. This is a great option for a cheap, good burger if you happen to be in the area but not worth a trek, take my word for it. Â Don't believe the hype
I absolutely love this place ... I used to eat here almost every week ,Just $6 for a dish . Must try Lamb over rice is owsome.

Came here with 5 people on a Saturday at 7 pm and they said we couldn't sit until 10. So we decided to try another week. Came back 3 people on Saturday at 6 pm. Still 1.5 hour wait but they do text when you're table ready (thank goodness for places like that!) and we got a drink elsewhere. They called us back a little before the time was up and we sat upstairs. Funky, crowded space. Burger and fries were great (though difficult to pick up and dip those skinny fries!) and we also had burrata and gnudi, the latter of which was awesome. service was a little slow but overall great place - worth it on a night when you're prepared to wait. And not bad for $$$.

We were very excited to try this breakfast place because of all the good reviews. But it was a bit of a disappointment. It is one of those places u tried it once and never go back again. We waited an hour or so to get in the restaurant. We ordered salmon egg benedict, spanish scramble and blueberry pancake and coffee. The food was meh...it was edible and it was just not deserving all that good reviews. The place is full of tourists and when we went in the hostess asked us if we had U.S. phone numbers. When the check came out they added the tip to the total..I mean apparently this is a place for visitors. If u live in new york u know there are better places out there and this one was just not one of them.

Ordered lunch delivery on seamless. Ramen was just okay; maybe because it was delivery I really couldn't taste anything outstanding. The Gang Nam Style Buns was quite good but was a bit too fatty for me. The food was a bit pricey too for the quality of it. Probably will try something else next time and update.
Got the bronte burger like the yelp reviews said, and it was like no other burger I've had. Portions were a little small but the flavor and experience was awesome.
This place is mindblowing! the ramen is so soft and tender. my favorite is spicy miso and tsukemen (pork broth). THEY WERE DELICIOUS!!!!!!!
excellent service. excellent wine recommendation. my fish was a bit dry. I will be back

I went here with a group of five other people for my birthday dinner this past Friday. Â Do call ahead if you have a large group. Â The restaurant was very accomodating, but I think the heads up helped. Â It is quite tiny. The service was great, and the place is super, super cute. Â I love that it's BYOB and casual and fun. Â The food was rather hit or miss. Â The people in the party who had fish - salmon, porgy, etc. - got delicious meals. Â The seafooders got meh meals. Â Not bad. Â Not great. Â Fairly priced. Â But I'm really starting to think you can't get good seafood in New York. Â  You should go. Â Definitely go. Â Get a whole fish (watch out for the bones). Â Bring a bottle of wine (or seven), and some good friends, and have an awesome time. Â But maybe don't get the seafood.
Just really, really good. Â Most of the time, in NYC, Boston, San Francisco, you pay big bucks for mediocrity. Â Junior's is neither overly priced nor mediocre. Â It is excellent.

Personally, I really don't get what's SOOOO great about Ippudo. I'm a huge ramen fan but I think their noodles are too thin - almost like angel hair. Their broth is very greasy and oily, and although it's delicious on the first few slurps, I'm regretting it by the end of the meal. My favorite thing on the menu are the pork buns. I actually wouldn't mind going there, having an order and a beer as a quick happy hour, if I were in the neighborhood. I'm not going to complain about the wait because it is what it is. Although, they now encourage you to leave the area and call them back to check on your status. That was a great improvement. I will however complain about the greeting staff. Understand that people are waiting for upwards of 2 hours to eat a bowl of noodles. I heard a customer say, "I hope my name comes up soon, I've been waiting a long time." She gave a smile, and rolled her eyes as she turned around to face me. Basically, she rolled her eyes at him in MY face. Then she gave me the same "smile" and asked me to confirm my name. I blankly stared at her and realized how futile it would be to even say anything. You're the short, doughy greeter at a noodle shop, not the door person at a club. Get over yourself and learn how to be courteous to your customers - especially at a Japanese restaurant to a Japanese customer.

This is one of many ramen places in the city and as pricey as it is for ramen - I'm never disappointed! Â I've tried the Classic, the Modern and their specials at times and my favorite is still being the Modern. Â The flavors of the broth is what makes any ramen dish for me. Â  I do love the dÃ©cor of the place and the servers are sooo attentive which is nice. Â And I will say, the bathroom is pretty clean which says a lot about a place to me. Â This place does get packed so make a reservation if you plan on going between the hours of 7pm - 10pm. Â  One thing I will tell everyone to try is their samurai short ribs - to die for! Â The marinate and sauce is delicious! Â So tender that the meat falls right off the bone....Mmmm. Â  On a good, cold day...nothing better than a bowl of warm ramen noodles! Â Enjoy!!

Casa Mono is easily my favorite restaurant. We've come here multiple times for birthdays, promotions, and anniversaries and Casa Mono raises the bar every time. Thank goodness it is a tapas restaurant because you get there and want to try everything. Here you have to opportunity to try several different plates without getting too full. I definitely recommend making reservations for the bar in front of the chefs so you can observe all the care the kitchen puts in to each dish. Sitting here can also help you decide what you want to order while you enjoy some wine. Venture out of your comfort zone here, you will not regret it. We tried Babbo, one of Mario B's other restaurants, and by the end of the meal we wished we had gone to Casa Mono. There's no need to go into the details of each dish, because its more rewarding to try them without a pre-existing opinion. The setting of the restaurant is lively but romantic. The staff will help remove any uncertainties you have about the menu items with detailed suggestions. Don't expect to eat on the cheap here. If you have wine, 5-7 small plates, dessert, and coffee, with tip you can expect to spend $200-$300 for two. I would be lying if I said it wasn't worth every penny.

Okay, I really can't say this isn't amazing pizza, because it is. Â However, I would not wait on line for this pie. Â It is great to go when it isn't too busy, but if not, no way would I go here. Â One thing that is pretty irritating, is that the wait for take out is just as long as the wait for dine in. Â As a resident of Brooklyn Heights, Grimaldi's really drives away any possible neighborhood fans.
Great choice. Chicken waffles and portobello scramble very unique. Highly recommended for breakfast.

The soup dumplings are freaking awesome. They are busy so expect to sit with other people at the same table at peak hours. Just make sure you bite a hole and let it lose it's steam before burning the rood of your mouth.

Anyone who gives this place any less than a 4 seriously probably doesn't like pizza. All you need is a slice of their creamy artichoke pizza and you'll end your night on a high, happy note. Â It was the best artichoke pizza I've had in my entire life. Â Well, it's the only artichoke pizza I've ever had... but still, it was ridiculously GOOD. Â Enough said. Go here. Â NOW!

Had the yummy tuna,beet and avocado crudo, the special of the day was asparagus with yogurt, egg and cheese YUM and whole wheat pasta w/ potatoes,cheese and veggies was SO good. The rustic Italian setting is adorable. It can be hard to get Â a reservation but you should be willing to sit at the bar for the food. Also, try the pasta with mussels.

Have quickly become a regular at this place. Great place for a full meal, just drinks or anything in between. Love the ever-changing menu, the staff and the small space is wonderful. Also, to anyone who was put off by the small plates, the portions have definitely grown since they first opened.

Ok so I've been to the Melt Shop once before and it was pretty good but I've just now had a very disappointing experience there. I ordered "The Award Winner" which is blue cheese, white cheddar, bacon and cranberry jam. The only award this sandwich won with me is the award for most disappointing sandwich ever. I love the idea behind it but this sandwich was very poorly executed--maybe because the guys were in a hurry to get it ready? I got back to my office and the sandwich was not melted. An un-melted sandwich from the MELT shop? Not good. So I'm deciding whether I should a. suffer through a lukewarm grilled cheese or b. microwave it and risk the bread getting chewy. I went with option b, I'm still unsure if this was the right call. The proportion of the ingredients was also off. The blue cheese was essentially non-existent and there was way too much of the cranberry jam. The jam even overpowered the bacon which was a huge bummer because it was really excellent bacon. I also ordered the creamy red cabbage slaw. Make sure you don't do this. It's not necessarily bad, just worthless. I was really bummed out by this sub-par sandwich. :( Not sure if I'll go back here.

Came in here a few months ago for brunch. Really super food and service. i was kinda drunk but I remember the service and food being good (promise). Â Next time I'm getting the fried green beans tho, I missed those last time.

$6 for Chicken over rice. $4 for a Gyro. $6 for a Falafel. The food was crazy good and it didn't break the bank either. The guy at the cart was really nice and service was great. All the food was good, but the chicken over rice is to die for. The chicken is so tender, not overcooked, rice was flavorful, the cut up bread was a nice touch. The white sauce (Tsatsiki sauce) gave the dish a nice pump of creamy flavor. The red sauce Â (hot sauce) is super spicy so don't use too much if you don't like spice. LOVE IT! LOVE IT! This cart stands out above the other zillion Halal carts in Times square.

I was a bit skeptical about restaurants at south street seaport...i figured they were all horribly overpriced places aimed strictly at tourists, but this place totally rocks. Â  the menu is completely affordable, and the meatloaf sandwich really is as good as people say. Â The decor is trendy, hip, and rustic (think urban loft) and the bathroom is lined with subway tile. i love me a good subway tile!

I have only been here for drinks, but it is one of my favorite places to grab a great drink before heading out for dinner in the West Village. They make several great whiskey cocktails! Â The bar tenders are all wonderful, and very good at what they do. Â The atmosphere is swanky and comfortable. Everything I have had on their cocktail list is top-notch. Â I will continue to go there for drinks. Â One of my favorite places in the village.

One of the best brunches in the city - and their other meals aren't bad too! Their vanilla bean french toast is amAZING - and i'm not normally a french toast type of person - I'll choose eggs any day normally. The vanilla bean french toast is so yummy, custardly, and fragrant that you really don't need to put any syrup on it at all! It's on their limited brunch menu on Saturday and their full brunch menu on Sunday. Their flatbread with goat cheese and carmalized onions is also phenomenal - it's covered with toppings yet is somehow still light and toasty. Egg dishes and salads are not bad either - but they definitely don't beat the french toast and flatbroad. the only real overrated item on the menu i think is the very pretty looking but not very flavorful scrambled eggs with salmon and marscapone cheese. pass on that. the rest is great! A favorite brunch location of mine.

Nice and yummy! Just got back from dinner here, g/f and I had 3 starters and a salad and the swordfish kebab, and everything was delicious! The swordfish was really well cooked, and they seated us within 10 minutes outside. Would love to go here more! Def. recommend!

When I was growing up in my momz belly, almost ready for departure in this cruel, cold world, my mom requested a cup of Dahl from Govinda's, the restaraunt that primarily serves and feeds the Hare Krishna community. Now, I am an adult, able to think and make decisions on my own volition.I am always down for Govinda's Kitchen in downtown Brooklyn, off of Schermerhorn and Nevins. it's Buffet/Steamtable style, all vegetarian, all fresh vegetables, soups, curry's and breads. I enjoy the breaded tofu in a cashew sauce, paneer and peas curry with a beet salad. I might finish that off with homemade mango cheesecake(YOU KNOW!) If you appreciate a bountiful, nutritous meal, with no bullshit check this spot out.
great quality food - brunch (eggs benedict) might be the best in the city. Â dinner is really delicious as well. Â fries, galosh, and salmon are good.

Pretty damned good comfort food. If you're on a diet you probably want to go somewhere else. Good craft beer, cool people and good value. Definitely stepping into a different place for the neighborhood which is a nice change of scenery (not that the scenery here is bad, it's great - this place is just nicely different).

Went here for Happy Hour one day after work to meet friends for a drink. I still had to hit the gym that evening so skipped on the alcohol, but did have a taste off their happy hour menu. I got the shrimp ceviche which was very tasty. My friends had the fish tacos, short rib sliders which they claimed were delish as well. I'll be back to try this place out. Friendly service, good food so far.

Once again the spot was loaded. Wine was pouring out generously. People were having fun. Servers were fun as usual. Bartender was extremely generous on wine. Bread popped up in a small satchel. Wine dine lose urself kinda stuff lights were dimmed. Ladies were just taking pics. Some extreme poses. Some too funny and some too drunk but all pics made sense since it was halloween. Now 5 stars !!!!

As a chef and transplanted New Yorker living in Boston places like the north end grill reminds me of why New York is one of the great food cities in the world. The dinner was unreal from apps to dessert and our table of 4 had 4 courses each so we cover a lot of the menu. Â All the desserts were top die for, I had carrot cake sundae Â and even this most simple sounding dessert just blew me away with flavor, texture and originality. Kudos to the team there and I will be back

Juniors you are slipping!. Changing the way you make your strawberry cheesecake just to save some money!. My slice had a bite of strawberry but tablespoons of gel filling. Stop being cheap. You have many loyal fans. Go back to the old way of making cheesecake!!!!.

I went here last night as my date has been insisting we go for the longest time. Â I was pleasantly surprised to find this charming restaurant inside this alley. Â I walked in and saw things like antalope heads hanging on the wood adorned walls. Â very rustic. Reminded me of a cozy ski lodge in Aspen. Â I am already so in love with this place! We had a drink at the front bar, I ordered the Freemans martini (I think it had whiskey in it) It was THE BEST! Even my date tried some of mine and loved it:) Â  Had dinner in the corner of the back room. We had the squash salad to start. Â He had the chicken for dinner, and I the Lamb stew. Â I was actually a bit hesitant at the idea of eating "stew", but it did not soup-like at all, which I liked. very flavorful and yummy! Overall, I cannot wait to tuck back in there on a chilly night and dream I am somewhere else :)

I had high hopes. The food was okay. I had the french toast which had three little slices of bananas. So much for "banana french toast". The sauce tasted like sweet banana foster. My BF got the basque eggs. The eggs were okay. Nothing amazing. I much rather go to Tartine down the street. Probably won't return.

Not sure what all the fuss about this place is. Rolled in today (Saturday) with the bf to have some brunch and if the tables next to us weren't packed so tight, I would have walked out. The service here was horrible. The restaurant had perhaps 8 tables of people when we first walked in and there were 3 waitresses and a busboy. That is less than 3 tables per person... not busy! First it took about 5 minutes for someone to even acknowledge us when we walked in despite the group of waitresses chatting amongst themselves at the bar. Once we sat down, it took another 10 minutes for someone to take our order, and that was only after I chicken-necked myself. After that, 20 minutes of nothing. Our coffee didn't come, our orange juice didn't come, nothing. Our "waitress" stood by the door daydreaming for pretty much the entire time we were there. She seriously had a glazed look in her eyes. Maybe she's pregnant, maybe she is waiting for mr right... who knows and who cares! I want my effin coffee! So after 20 minutes, the food arrives and still no coffee until we ask for it. So then our OJ and coffee come AFTER our plates are down. I hate that cause I ended up only having 2 sips of coffee before I left in a huffpuff. The food was mediocre. Both of our salads were super salty, the potatoes bland, and the eggs overcooked. My boyfriend was flipping his over-easy egg like a flapjack and it stayed in one piece. My omelet was a dish sponge. WAH WAH. Totally ruined my Saturday morning.

Been to a few ramen places in the city and i have to say this is the best. Despite the long one hour wait, it was worth it. The chicken broth for the ramen was so good. The pork was so tender!!! I ordered the miso ramen which was delicious. I will be back again to try others!!!

I was visiting my brother in NYC this weekend, and we stopped for lunch here. Â You order downstairs, which is tiny, and can eat upstairs in the small loft. Â There are a few stools and some stand up spaces to eat, plus a spot where you can sit on the ground. Â We were luckily able to snag a couple bar stools (again the loft is quite small and there were several others in the loft). Â I got the mackerel sandwich and it was delicious. Â I love mackerel; the fish was so moist and delicious, and the sauce and crunchy bread brought it all together. Â My only complaint was that it was a little bit small for my taste (plus it was just that good). Â  My brother mentioned that this place can get quite crowded though. Â That aside, they make a hell of a good sandwich.
This place is good but it is very tight so it's better to go during off hours. The knife noodles are also pretty good. Very authentic place.

So fresh and so delicious! I got the veggie soup (they have a very small menu) and I was impress by all the vegetation they put in it! Seriously so damn good. The only reason it would get 4 stars instead of 5 is because the place is too fast pace. When I eat out I want to sit and enjoy it, not get rushed in and out. With that out the way I can also add that the wait time was next to nothing even though there were 4 people ahead of me. The soup is so worth it! (Not date night friendly)

I try to make it here for lunch a few times a month since its right near my office. Â The Regina, Black Forest Â and Milano sandwiches are all personal favorites. Â I recommend getting a half sandwich and some soup, or some of their tabouleh. Â Gets very busy during the weekday lunch hour..

If you're looking for a great restaurant with superb service and ambiance, then look no further! My boyfriend and I came here on our anniversary date and upon checking in, we were greeted graciously and were seated in the dining area. The tavern area is great for those who want a more casual environment. It was a little noisier than the dining area but nonetheless the restaurant interior was beautiful from the tavern to the dining room. Our server, Anna, was really funny and she even offered us complimentary bubbly as a toast to our anniversary! The menu is very simple and does not contain a lot of entrees as everything is prefixed. This is personally a good thing to me because you know everything on the menu tastes great and it doesn't need a lot of options to mask the other plates. As an appetizer I chose the chilled corn soup. I really wanted the smoked trout but since my entree was going to be the artic char, I didn't want to overdo it with the seafood. My boyfriend however, chose the smoked trout as well as the lamb as his entree. When our meals came we drooled over how complex the flavors were. My chilled corn soup had this bubble that had traces of corn juice of some sort that explodes in your mouth when you bite into it!! Very delightful. My boyfriend was told that he got the second to last smoked trout of the night and the reason being is because the smoked trout was just absolutely mind blowing! It practically melted in your mouth!! The entrees were equally good. My artic char was cooked to perfection. I am a stickler when it comes to overcooked fish. The artic char was so tender and moist. I would definitely recommend this dish to anyone who loves fish! I took a bite out of my boyfriend's lamb entree and it was cooked perfectly to medium, just as he has asked for. For dessert we opted for the cherry lime sorbet and the chocolate semifreddo. My boyfriend who's not usually a dessert person had to agree it was worth indulging for. As we were eating our desserts, a second plate of complimentary raspberry rhubarb came with writings that said, "Happy Anniversary!" It was the most adorable thing and I am so glad we came to Gramery Tavern because our server really made sure we had a memorable night. Towards the end, just as you think it couldn't get any better, we were offered a tray of mini delectable cookies and a morning breakfast muffin to take home! Everything was done right here! You just can't compete with the service!!!

This place is a true hidden gem! It's easy to miss, since it's tucked away at the end of a small elevator lobby of one of buildings. Look out for the sign hanging outside the building with a big arrow pointing you towards this little quaint hole in the wall. Seating is limited, but I came here early for lunch. The food has a lovingly homemade touch and feels down to earth and healthy relative to other greasy New York fare. I ordered the bibimbap. The flavors were delicious, especially the vegetables, which they claim to organically grow themselves! The smell of the fragrant sesame oil was also reassuring and tasty; most of the time, you end up not tasting any in run-of-the-mill bibimbaps. All this, plus two side dishes and a small cup of soup for under $10. The lady behind the counter was extremely kind and friendly. And this is so conveniently located near the train station. No longer will I have to trek all the way to K-town for great Korean food when I'm passing through the city in a hurry. Plus, this place opens early, unlike most decent eateries which only open at 11am. I'll definitely be coming back for more.

Grey Dog is a delicious breakfast spot. Â The building is also cute. Â I had the Grey Dog's Breakfast with bacon and she has the Village Pancakes. Â Perhaps we came at a slow time (9:15 on a weekday), but there we several open tables and no rush from staff. The coffee is good, several steps up from Starbucks (my normal brew) and is plentifully refilled.

Since my last glowing review of Chavela's, I'm afraid it's gotten too big for its britches. We attempted to go here for dinner on a Friday but promptly left when we couldn't even get to a hostess through the packed entryway. We decided to try a few weeks later for brunch with a party of four. Again, the place was crowded, but we were able to get a table after about 10 minutes. The problem was that the table was clearly meant for two, not four, and a nasty draft kept coming in through the door. I wanted to ask if we could wait for another table, but we ultimately decided against it because the server kept disappearing, and we were starving. I'm afraid I don't remember much of what I ate because I was so uncomfortable in the situation. But I still had my glorious delivery, at least, until yesterday. I tried not to abuse the kindness of the delivery staff, who kept coming to my apartment despite it being located a few blocks out of their delivery zone, by calling well before the dinner rush. But I guess when I ordered a few weeks ago it was a little too late. The manager was obliging, but politely asked that I check ahead of time in the future and explained that they were getting a lot of orders and that they wouldn't be able to come if the restaurant was busy. Perfectly understandable. So when I called yesterday, I explained the situation to the woman on the phone and expected things to be fine. She pulled up my address by my phone number and to my shock, she said that the manager had put a note on my account saying they will not be delivering to us anymore. I tried questioning her about it, since it was contrary to what the manager had told me, but she rudely told me that they were just too busy and hung up. Perhaps they are "just too busy" now that Prospect Heights is getting overrun by the yuppie crowd spilling over from Park Slope. Perhaps Chavela's doesn't need me anymore, and perhaps I should just accept it and move on. But for now, there is an emptiness inside of me that can only be filled with rice and beans.

This village-y Thai place is comfy and intimate, but don't come here hungry because the service will have you waiting. Â Desperate for a beverage, I walked up to the bar but still had to wait 5 minutes for some one to appear. Â It's probably less of an issue if you don't go during dinner time, since there were only 3 servers that didn't really have clearly delineated roles which may have contributed to their inefficiency. Â I ordered a dragon beer on draft which was strong and unexpected. Â We wanted to get the Chilean sea bass hot pot, but they were out of the fish so we had to get a seafood assortment instead. Â The description said it would be very spicy, but I would have described it as mild. Â The flavors were standard Thai fare. Â The green papaya salad was fresh and the street style pork was like galbi-flavored shish kabob (could have mistaken it for beef).

Really? Â I'm looking at these other reviews and thinking "was I really in the same restaurant?" Â Maybe if you're looking for a bar but NOT a place to eat. Â Trust me! Â We told the waitress we had theater at 8:00 PM. Â We waited for someone to take our order, we waited for water, we sat for 35 minutes before they even brought our salads. We had a quick seven minutes to eat so-so food. Â Avoid this place if you want a good meal and certainly if you want to be on-time for the theater. Â  Oh, and it's LOUD.

Sunday Supper offers an appetizer, entree, and dessert for $27. Hard to beat in the city, and always well worth it. The restaurant has a great atmosphere, and moves at an appropriate speed (at least for Sunday nights). There is never any rush, but everything still has an appropriate flow. My favorite way to relax before beginning another work week.

Good food and this place gets packed so it's best to have a reservation. Â While I loved the food, i thought it was a bit overpriced. Appetizers: beet salad with goat's cheese, horseradish crÃ¨me, soft herbs, hazlenuts. Â I'm not big on beets so not a fan but everyone else liked it. fried east coast oysters with savoy cabbage slaw, cayenne-tomato butter. Â I really liked the oysters. crispy and flavorful. warm octopus salad with fingerlings, chorizo, frisÃ©e, olive purÃ©e. Â Super good. Â the fingerlings were yum and so was octopus. Entrees: pan roasted chicken sweet potato salad, bok choy, hazlenuts. Â  Chicken was juicy like everyone said. Â But not amazing. Â I like the sweet potato salad though. For sides: Didn't like the broccoli rabe too much. But I really liked the brussel sprouts!!
Delicious, carefully invented fresh food. really lovely meal enjoyed by all! Gnudi to die for!!!!!!!

I must confess, my friend is a part-time member of the waitstaff here. So, yes, a bit biased, but feel compelled to write a review. The atmosphere is great - new age Italian feel - clean, cute, quaint. Great place to do work. I had a dinner and a breakfast here - fresh ingredients and vegetarian options :) The menu consists of a unique collection of dishes. Baked eggs are delicious!!

Came on a Monday night and parked right in front, on the street. Seemed like plenty of parking available which is obviously a bonus when eating out in Brooklyn. We ordered two pies, one large cheese and one large pep & sausage. Â The prep the pie right in front of you using fresh looking ingredients. Â  Although circumstances didn't let us enjoy the pie right out of the oven, I can still say the pie was way above average. Â Not too greasy with the right balance of cheese and sauce. Â I would recommend this joint for anyone looking for high quality, New York style pie.

Really, really love this place. All the food is great, and service is so quick for a bar that's already packed by 6pm. Bartenders are super courteous and treat you really well. I am especially appreciative of the fact that they have two floors with lots of room to sit and loads of tvs to watch. I am definitely behind all of the beers they have on tap. While it does get crowded, it's not as if you won't be able to find somewhere to hang out. Great bar with some great ambiance and lots of pretty people.

sweet afton is a solid bar you can count on in Astoria. my favorite time to come in is during the week, it gets really packed on the weekend nights. drinks are well made. try their hot cider during the fall/winter. you can pair it with bourbon,rum, etc. their food is delicious enough to stand alone as a restaurant. their regular burger and portobello are outstanding!! sweet afton is a staple in the Astoria bar scene and I would recommend it to anyone looking for good drinks and food in a cozy atmosphere.

Just went back for dinner and all my criticism about the food has been addressed. I ordered a special - spaghetti with pesto - that I could easily make at home. But this was a really impressive dish. The best homemade noodles I have ever eaten. Ever. Dense and chewy and perfect. Great amount of veggies and sauce. And thanks for the vegetarian special. I also had the curried cauliflower. Which was also incredible. Roasted cauliflower is always good but this was so delicious and flavorful. Just watch out for the salt. My date had steamed clams and cooed over the broth the whole time. I drank really good wine. She had a really good cocktails. Think these guys really hit their stride. The crowd at dinner at 5pm attests to that. A really solid competitor to Bar Corvo now.

Ate here a couple of says ago and I got food poisoning from this place. My friend and I believe it was their soup we had because she felt queasy after eating it as well. I think they left the soup out for too long that it was not set to the right temperature. Spent the days puking. And also they have a lot of fruit flies that when two of them went inside my drink. You better think twice before coming to this place, you might end up getting sick!

This place is great for low key hangouts especially for happy hour and brunch. Â During Tuesday happy hour, the tapas are half off! My favorite tapas are the espresso bbq costillitas (fall off the bone baby back ribs in a mole style sauce) and mejillones al tequila (mussels swimming in a tomato based sauce). Â I usually ask them for extra bread just to sop up the sauce from both dishes. Â  My favorite brunch item is the yuca benedictos. Â Guacamole, cilantro hollandaise and oozy egg yolk have a menage trois on top a bed of potatoes with shrimp. Â It's one of the few prix fixe items that don't come with a side of home fries or rice and beans. Â Trust me you won't miss the side dish. Â  This place used to be in the one $ price range and has creeped up into the 2 $'s price range in the past couple years. Â It's worth it though.

Their ramen is very delicious and big portioned. Also liked the pork katsu my friend ordered. And it was so cheap, the three of us only spent like $35 in total. It was even cheaper than two people having dimsum in Chinatown! Definitely recommended this one.

I went to Room Service in April when I was in NYC. I went to dinner at Room Service before going to see a musical at the New World Stages which is nearby. This must have been around 6pm. I expected to wait a while to get seated but we got a table right away. "Room Service" theme carries along to the decor and the drink menu. The drinks are packed with fruity flavor. Room service plays a lot of good music. I actually heard some StÃ©phane Pompougnac. The service was pretty good. I expected the service to be mediocre because I've heard that in NYC service is not that great but I came to NYC and I got lucky every single time I went to eat I guess. That or I'm easy to please. The food wasn't the best Thai food I've ever had but it wasn't bad either. I think all around I had a pleasant experience and I look forward to going to Room Service again when I go back to NYC.

Heard really good reviews about this place, but I think it's mediocre. Probably would have given it 3 stars normally, but due to price (it's quite expensive for what it is), downgrading to 2 stars. It wasn't a terrible meal, but nothing special. I didn't absolutely love anything. The spicy tuna hand roll kind tasted like canned tuna, perhaps it was the seasoning, not sure, but it was just OK. The sushi bombs are ok, $19 for 12 pieces of sushi. Too expensive, considering Â the rice to fish ratio. Way too much rice, in comparison to a tiny/thin piece of fish. They still have good flavor, but just too much rice and $$ I did like the yuzu as the palate cleanser. It's sweet and refreshing. The service was also ok. I'd come back here if my reservation to Roberta's didn't work out, otherwise probably won't come back here.

Arepas Cafe did not disappoint. Â The Reina (arepa stuffed with chicken and avocado) was great, especially when you top it off with the sauces they have. Â FYI, the hot sauce they have is crazy spicy. Â Not for the faint of heart. Â The tejadas con queso (sweet plantains topped with cheese) are what fat kids' dreams are made of. Â Next time I go back I plan on trying some of the beverages they serve.

Communal seeting was off-putting upon entry BUT Food is DELICIOUS and the waitstaff is attentive and nice- no snooty hipsters here. The owner was present and charming, giving us some gratis sake and talking about his love of food ....just like an old world restaurant. loved the sense of family in the place- you would think you were at grandmas house.

Hello Jackson Heights Residents: I went to Pollo Inka for the first time on 1/31/14. Â This restaurant was recommended by a co-worker of mine. Â I must say that this chicken, rice, maduro and avocado salad was amazing! Â To me is just as good as Pio Pio but a bit cheaper. Â The only thing that I have a compliant about is the beans, they were to watery. Â  But everythng else was delicious!!! Because of the beans I will give it 4 stars. Â Thank You.

Four words: Crab Xiao Lum Bao. Â People rave about the pork only version, but I come here for the crab version. It's the pork version with added crab meat and crab roe. Â It's rich and decadent. Â If you have a cholesterol problem, I would stray away from these. They come out oozing hot, but the child in me cannot wait to devour these dumplings, and I end up burning my tongue every time. Â It is so worth it! Joe Shanghai is a must!

I could live off Hancos sandwiches. If you are body and calorie conscious like me, get the shredded chicken sandwich on whole wheat with no dairy (sans mayo and butter). One time my husband got me a sandwich on white bread and I refused to eat it. I took the insides out and put it on whole wheat toast and it wasn't the same. Their bread is incredible. All of the ingredients balance compliment each other in just the right way. If you get it "hot" it will come with jalapenos. I suggest getting it medium and keep the bottle of Sriracha sauce on hand...I pour it on every bite. The vinegar from the veges balances out the spice. It's a sad story when I drop ONE pickled carrot on the floor... Cherry on the sundae: Punch card which gets Â your 10th sandwich for free.

I would give Ba Xuyen closer to a 3.5 star rating than 4, but bumped it up for the super nice employees. The interior is very simple and no frills. At the back, the employees take your order and make the sandwiches. At the front, there are four tables that are littered with crumbs. On the sides, you can pick up a cold drink or some Vietnamese snacks. My brother got a #1 cold cut banh mi and I got the #8 grilled pork banh mi. We also got taro milk and honeydew milk. It totaled to $14, which is ridiculously cheap for how much food we got. The milks were really good and we kept swapping to try each others'. My banh mi was good, but not amazingly so. It has a nice, toasted baguette filled with pickled veggies, a lot of meat, and hot sauce. I'm not quite sure what was missing, but it was significant enough that I wasn't gobbling down the sandwich like I usually do. As far as banh mis go, I wouldn't turn it down if I were in the area and craving some Vietnamese food.

Tavola is an authentic Neopolitan pizzeria and pasta restaurant in New York City's Hell's Kitchen neighborhood. Â Originally an Italian grocery store the original sign and some of the grocer's shelves can be seen along the left wall when you first enter this long, rectangular restaurant, but my eye was immediately drawn to the massive wood burning oven at the far end that cooks the pizzas. I ended up chatting with the owner, Nick Accardi, who took over this restaurant in the spring of 2012 and he proudly told me about the restaurants long history and why they are so passionate about the food they make. I also had the chance to chat with the handsome Italian bartender who spends his days in Brooklyn as a struggling artist. Â This neighborhood restaurant is definitely worth crossing town to check out. Â Antipasti range from $8-13; pasta and entrees are $16-28; and the individual pizzas range from $10-19 -- while the pastas all looked good, I knew I was going to order a pizza. Â After chatting with Nick I ordered a glass of Sangiovese and the Calebresa Bona which comes topped with Esposito's hot sopressata, fresh ricotta, plum tomato and basil. The thin crust is substantial enough to cradle the hot cheeses, meats and herbs that melted in my mouth. Â The salty toppings had just a bit of heat but nothing that would set your mouth on fire and I used a bowl of olive oil that Nick gave me to dip the crust of the pizza so when I was done there was hardly any evidence that a pizza was once there. Â  Do you like pizza? Are you in New York? Head over to Hell's Kitchen, say hello to Nick or the friendly Italian bartender, Francesco and try their pizza.

I went to Buenos Aires in 2010, and since then I've been tirelessly trying to find the perfect Argentinian restaurant. PorteÃ±o isn't perfect, but it's very good, and puts Industria Argentina (TriBeCa) et al to shame. I went to PorteÃ±o (the word PorteÃ±o means resident of Buenos Aires) this past Wednesday night with my boyfriend and parents. My parents live in New Jersey, so this was a great location for us, about a 5 minute walk from Penn Station. However, it is in a little bit of a neighborhood dead zone, at 10th Ave. and W. 27th St. I'm guessing they don't get much foot traffic. The decor was dimly lit inside, but not dark. It was small, but not cramped. The tables were spaced well so we were not on top of our fellow diners, and there was a bar as well. I had called to make a reservation (no opentable), and the owner took the reservation himself. He introduced himself as the owner, and provided very warm service over the phone. The waitress was very kind as well, and the service was above average. They came over right away when the wine glasses were empty, and did not hesitate in wordlessly refilling the complimentary bread and olive oil. They also re-fold napkins while you're in the restroom, which is a nice touch. The wine list was great, with reasonably priced Argentinian Malbecs AND Chardonnays. It's really refreshing to see Argentinian wine that isn't just Malbec and Torrontes. The empanadas here were FANTASTIC. We decided to try the beef, spinach, and vegetable since we wanted a sample of everything. The spinach was lackluster texturally, just spinach inside, although it was cooked well and had good flavor. However, the beef was exactly like I had in Argentina. It had great flavors, and the meat was extremely juicy. The pastry, which so often becomes dry, was flaky and buttery, exactly how it should be. The vegetable empanada was mostly corn and cheese, and that had a nice buttery sauce inside. These were some great empanadas. For the meal, everyone had the matambrito beef, which was flank steak rolled with egg and vegetables. I tasted a bite, and it was delicious. I had the rigatoni with chorizo and ricotta salata, which was a nice twist on a typical rigatoni/red sauce dish. I loved the large chunks of ricotta, and they were not shy with the parmesan cheese! Woo hoo cheese! They also had lomito sandwiches on the menu, which are basically Argentinian cheese steaks, but with ham (they put ham on everything!). The value was fantastic as well. None of the main meat dishes were over $25, empanadas were 3 for $10, and the pasta dishes and lomito sandwiches were only around $13. I definitely hope to return soon.

What you should get here: THE LOADED FRIES. The banh mi fries are super crispy, hurtled into heaven with pickled carrot and daikon (do chua), cilantro, jalapeno, garlicky soy glaze, cilantro sauce, and spicy mayo. The kimchi fries are similar, but with one pickled veggie replaced by another. I prefer the kimchi fries for extra spice and acidity, but both are some madman's answer to nachos or poutine - stuff loaded onto other stuff, culminating in irresistible hybrids of textures, flavors, and cultures. I'm only being a little facetious. The droolworthiness of the fries make JoJu worth a trip, even if the sandwiches may not. As you can guess, JoJu makes no claim of being authentic - even their "original" banh mi is not very traditional, and the menu includes other Vietnamese-inspired sandwiches that scream Asian fusion: lemongrass chicken, bulgogi, kakuni. Generally speaking, they make great sandwiches. I like the heavy slathering of pate on the original. But their banh mi bread is inconsistent. Twice now I've sampled JoJu's sandwiches at Yelp events, and the freshly toasted bread is always warm and wonderful. But when we visited as part of Qian W's posse, the bread was much denser and firmer, not warm at all. The meat in the "original" was also cut way too thickly. They've since begun slicing the meats thinner, but my bread most recently was again completely cooled. Such a shame! Toast the bread freshly, JoJu! Do it for us! As for value, the $5-7 pricetag is pretty great. I usually polish off other banh mi but can tackle barely more than half of JoJu's. Outward appearances suggest comparable sizes, but nope! Joju's are stuffed densely and generously. Along the same [x on top of y = sheer awesome indulgence] principle as the fries, add a runny fried egg to your banh mi for $1.25 (or check in on Yelp and get it for free). Free wifi (check your receipt for a password) and a large, varied drink menu (bubble teas, milk teas, yakult drinks, Vietnamese coffee, fruit slushes, etc.) make this a good place to breathe for a few moments in the bustle of Elmhurst. Not during peak times, though - the space is clean and narrow and only sits about 20. Even on a Sunday at 3pm, there was a line halfway through the restaurant, and every table was filled by people already eating! Good thing banh mi are ultra-portable.

Mixed feelings. I don't like to give bad reviews but my friends and I are angry. Â We have been waiting 4 hours for our pizza. Â Not cool, Artichoke Pizza, not cool. Â We've called every hour and they keep saying it will be here in 15 minutes. We live SUPER close. Â Yes, we could have just picked it up, but no one wanted to leave the party. Â HUNGRY. Okay so they reimbursed us and hooked us up with a free bottle of wine and free pizza. Â They are a-ok in my book now. Â But still we had wait 4 hours.

Beer for brunch, I like it a bunch! I can imagine my Teddy Ruxpin saying something like that, if he had eaten brunch here and if he had an audio cassette inserted in his back that had those words on it. Came here with bffc* for brunch on a beautiful Saturday. Â It was crowded but we got seated quickly. Â  Started with a mimosa for her and a La Chouffe for me...what a way to get started! I had the croque madame and she had the croque tomate. Â Both were great, served with salad and super tasty frites. Â The toast on which it's served is very toasted and seems hard to cut, but it's just a very crusty bread. Service could have been a bit more attentive and it would have been nice to have been offered dessert rather than just handed the check, but if you've got good Belgian beer and good food, then you have my heart. Â  To paraphrase Teddy Ruxpin, I like you Petite Abeille, will you be my friend? ____________________ *best friend from college

I normally LOVE Fish and I enjoyed my meal here (Red, White & Blue special plus Swordfish and Lobster Bisque cannot be beat) BUT we waited a really long time in between our oysters and our appetizers. And then they overloaded our table with appetizers AND our entrees. Well, which am I supposed to eat first? Eat my appetizer and then stomach a cold entree or eat both at the same time like a savage? Not only that, but by the time we ALL (an entire table of 6 sans the boyfriend) finished our meals, the Boyfriend still did not receive his entree. When we asked our waiter about it, he told us 2 minutes. 10 minutes later, his entree came STEAMING hot, which obviously means they forgot about it until we reminded them. So he had to eat his entree in less than 10 minutes to try to keep up with the rest of us. I think I might try somewhere else next time.

We had dinner at Bustan on a Tuesday night with a party of 4. We were seated at a table with the view of the kitchen and the Chef standing by checking the plating of every dish as they went out. Everything that came out to our table tasted fresh, both familiar and innovative. We talked to Chef Effi who graciously sent over some of his proposed dishes like lamb pizza, a citrus broiled shrimp, a plump and juicy eggplant dish, a long platter of israeli appetizers and fresh pizza oven bread, salmon, sea bass...Everything was sublime! The staff and the chef made us feel as if we were dining at a friends home. Contemporary, organic interiors , warm and inviting service and simply great food you can eat regularly means we will be back on our next visit to NYC.

So finally we met the owner of this place. WOW! He is so attentive and polite. Seen him walking around helping the staff and chatting with the customers that were coming in. This review is for the owner.

So I finally got to taste this pizza and it was well worth the wait (which I confess was a bit long). Â But I would do it again. Â Pizza done to perfect with succulent pepperoni. Â I will be back for sure. Â Again and Again and Again... Loved it.

I love Paprika's Pappardelle with Braised Oxtail Ragu! So good! This $14 rich and robust braised oxtail ragu is a perfect hearty meal for cold winter! To top it off, Paprika also offers 2 course prix-fixe dinner for $15 everyday from 5-7pm, which is such a fantastic dea!!! Â There are many good Italian restaurants in NY, but Paprika is one of my favorite spots because not only they serve tasty and reasonably priced food, but also the ambiance is cute, romantic, and cozy. And the service is great too, friendly but not invasive, fast, and attentive. Restaurants like Paprika make East Village my favorite dining destination where I can find many charming, cheap, and delicious restaurants that I'm more likely to become a regular. On weekend nights it's becoming increasingly more difficult to find a table unless you have a reservation. It's a great place for group dining especially if you are with friends on a tight budget. They'll be pleased and thank you for letting them enjoy good meal without breaking the bank!
Fantastic Banh Mi. Their lemongrass chicken sandwich is equally great. Love this place!

I feel like I'm just beating a dead horse writing this review so I'm going to KISS it. We were there for NYE and it was a truly excellent experience. I had the cassoulet, and it was amazing, as mentioned, but what was the stand out? The goat cheese tart. That thing was a little piece of heaven. I really can't remember the last time I was so blown away. It was light in texture, smooth, gooey... it was... just.. I am going to spend the better part of 2014 trying to recreate that. The service was outstanding. I will definitely be back for that fois gras and filet... it looked awesome.

The food here is very good. Authentic with fresh, crisp flavours. We had the parpi chat, murgh tikka marsala, the neer dosa, the lamb cutlets, bihari dal, roti and paratha and rice, then ordered Chicken Tandoori (we were already full but kept on eating). The mango Lassi was the best I have ever tried. The atmosphere is lovely. Simple, clean and modern with the perfect lighting. Highly recommended.

I went here for brunch and sat outside. Â It was very relaxing and enjoyable to be there, but the food was somewhat lacking. Â Well, what I ordered was anyway. Â I am beginning to think that I always order the worst thing on the menu :/ I ordered the sausage grinder. Â It sounded so good because it had ricotta and broccoli rabe (which I LOVE!) Â The sausage wasn't crispy, which is how I like sausage to be, especially in a sandwich. Â Also, the ricotta was overpowered by oregano. Â I can taste that spice from a mile away and honestly, I think it should be banned....I hate it. My gf had the pasta with broccoli rabe and cici beans....that was delish and it was that dish that warranted this place the third star. Â  we paid $20 each.....so it's not cheap, but I wouldn't expect a restaurant owned by robert deniro to be so :) I probably would give the place one more try...order something else or maybe try it for dinner.
Excellent food, great wine selection, excellent music. Â The service could be improved. Crowded and noisy for dinner, especially in the front toward the bar.

I went to mamouns last night it was great as it always is. The food was perfect and the atmosphere was also the same always packed. I had a chicken kebab this time and it was good too. But the best is the falafel sandwich.

What a hidden find! Â As soon as you exit the J/M Hewes Station, you come across this quaint cafe right by the train underpass, but as soon as you step foot into Moto, you are surprisingly welcomed with such a romantic ambiance and cool vibe. We came here for a light dinner and the food was excellent. We arrived on the early side, so it was even more romantic. Â  - The braised portuguese octopus was so delicious and cooked to perfection - absolutely tender and the flavors were amazing. It was accompanied by fingerling potatoes, harrisa, parsley, picholine olives, and lemon - a great complement to the octopus. Â  - The carnaroli rice risotto with fava beans, market mushrooms, & parmigiano reggiano was so delicate yet rich in flavor. Â A hearty dish, perfect for cold winter nights, definitely makes you feel so warm and happy. Moto also offers a variety of wine by the glass and beer menu. Â We just missed the happy hour, but we were still happy with our beverages. Â Also, this place does accept credit cards, so perhaps this was a recent addition. Â No need to worry!

Momo-fuku-ing GREAT! I'm so happy we made our way over here on Sunday evening for our last dinner in NYC. There was no wait at all (they don't take reservations unless you're having the pork butt bo ssÃ¤m with a large party), and we got a nice spot at the bar. The space is contemporary and minimalistic with dark wood walls that bear only three photos of Johnny McEnroe (apparently owner David Chang is a huge fan?). We started out with some modern cocktails. I had the Sawyer (Beefeater gin, angostura, peychaud's, orange bitters, lime juice, & simple syrup) - I LOVE anything with gin and orange bitters, so this was the perfect way to start off the evening. It was cool to see that the modern menu was a compilation of different cocktails created by artisan bartenders from NY, LA & NOLA. But it's ALL about the steamed buns here! Man-tou buns stuffed with a thick slice of pork belly that melts in your mouth, cucumbers, scallions and hoisin sauce topped with Sriracha sauce - so amazing that you can't just have one. Yes, it was so good that we ordered two plates of it, so we could both have two of the deliciousness. For our main dish, we had the whole boneless porgy with ramps and maitake mushrooms for two. The medium sized fish was grilled and extremely tasty, though we wished the chive pancakes that accompanied it were not pan fried. There was enough smokey flavor from the fish skin that eating it with a pan fried pancake was too salty. I could have been happy with stuffing them into some more man-tous. We paired the fish with some refreshing sake. Apparently there is a fried chicken dish off the menu? Or it could only be at the Noodle Bar. Nonetheless, I would go back to have two orders of those steamed buns all to myself.

Came here on a sunday for brunch with a bunch of people because we couldn't go to Penelope. This place also doesn't take reservations but they told us the wait would be a hour compare to Penelope which was like a 3 hour wait. anyway that one hour wait turned into a hour and a half almost and most of us were freezing just waiting outside than we finally were able to get in and we were all starving by than. The food was great and I loved their breakfast sandwich! everything was perfect in that dish and wasn't greasy for me. Their spicy tomato soup taste great, just like spaghetti but without the noodles haha and their chai latte is delicious too! Even though they don't take reservations, they deserve 5 stars for the service, as long as we waited out there, they were nice enough to have one of the waiter come out with cups of hot apple cider to warm those who were waiting outside. That effort and service they give to the customers was amazing and thats why they derserve 5 stars. I say it's worth the wait if you want to eat here, great food and great service!
Cuba is a beautiful restaurant with GREAT food. Definitely get a reservation if you're going for dinner Friday-Sunday.

Loved everything about this restaurant. The space is beautifully designed, comfortable and cool, spacious yet inviting. The floor to ceiling windows give it a wonderful indoor yet outdoor feel. Excellent service. Now, to the food. Five of us all together which is perfect when you want to taste as many dishes as possible which is what we did. Cod cakes. Mwah! Mushroom flatbread (a meal unto itself). Mwah! The salmon and pork chops entrees. Â Mwah! Mwah! And did i mention the racquetball sized meatballs stuffed with herbs? The desserts are handcrafted and delicious. Loved the coconut cake! We'll be back for sure!

Been going here since 2006, the portions have gotten a little smaller & they raised the prices by a dollar. However, the food is even better then I remember each time, always have more then enough leftovers to take home. I always get the lamb since I don't eat chicken, at $6 a plate. Best spot in the city for late hours, especially for the weekend. Deserves 5 stars because they're consistent, makes great food at a decent price & I'm willing to make the trip from queens!

Absolutely delicious food, excellent service, wonderful atmosphere, and appropriately priced. Just got home, and the first thing I wanted to do was reward them with a great review. A warm mix of romantic and friendly, with fresh and desirable dishes that make you feel good eating them (the sauces were especially impressive), it was the perfect night out.

This is a quaint, adorable little neighborhood spot serving up tarte flambÃ©e, a deliciously rich, salty, crispy Alsatian flatbread that has crÃ¨me fraÃ®che, onions, and bacon as a base onto which you can add a variety of toppings (e.g. wild mushrooms, gruyÃ¨re cheese, goat cheese, tomatoes, etc.). I believe it may even be the only place in the city serving authentic tarte flambÃ©e. We had the Traditionelle (crÃ¨me fraÃ®che+caramelized onions+bacon), Forestiere (mushrooms), and one with gruyÃ¨re cheese...Everything was yummy and cheap (~$10/tarte). We had three, but ordering 2 would be a perfectly filling meal. The beer selection wasn't huge, but it was well thought-out and well matched to the food. If you just dropped me out of thin air into the restaurant, I would have guessed that we were in a smaller town in France. Almost everyone in the restaurant was speaking French and the decor and even the style of the menu felt just like what you see in casual restaurants in Northern France. They even had Picon BiÃ¨re-- a strange beer and orange liqueur cocktail that I've never, ever seen in the US. The owner and waitress were both from Alsace and seemed really passionate about the food and excited to introduce newcomers to it. This is a great addition to the neighborhood and I recommend checking it out! P.S. (Hint to the owners-- It would be a dream come true if you guys could do authentic crÃªpes too. I've been looking for 5 years and haven't found a single place stateside that even approximates what you get in France.)

Been here twice now for brunch and both times have been impressed with both the food and the service. Servers come around quickly and frequently and the food comes out quickly, especially for the volume of people. They give you bread and bottles of still and sparkling water for the table as well. To top it all off, on nice days the wall to the outside opens out and gives diners a breath of fresh air... at least as fresh as the air can be here in the middle of Manhattan. As for food, I've had the Ranchero Scramble and the Avocado Sandwich. Both came with hearty portions of avocado, which I love, and both were very good. Great place for an American brunch.

Everything about this restaurant is amazing, from the food to the hand soap they use in the restroom. Ordered from the tasting menu and it was just superb, although I must confess it is quite plentiful so if you are not very hungry choose a la carte.

We ate at Blue Ribbon last night. Â Loved the place and we will be back next time we are in New York. Â Everyone loved what they ordered. Â The staff could not have been better. Â Best fried chicken I have ever had. Â One person at our table did not finish his meal and did not want to take it with him. Â The staff that cleared the plates told the manager who came over to ask them if everything was ok. Â He wanted to make sure that it was cooked well and that he enjoyed it. Â Great service and incredible food. Â Great place to go after theater because they are open late.
Great Service! Great drinks....awesome food! Best "michelada" and fried chicken in NYC.

After a impromptu trip into the city to see a show, our group of 4 found ourselves over-hungry and without a idea about where to eat. Considering how hungry we were, a McDonalds would have made the cut. I naturally found my location on Yelp and lead my group to this restaurants based on the fact it was the closest to us with the highest Yelp rating. Normally, I avoid this part of town like the plague. The last thing I want is to blow my money on a tourist trap restaurant. But .. I can't begin to tell you how pleasantly surprised I was by this place! The decor is nice. The service was OUTSTANDING. The menu had something for everyone. You will find the typical Italian-American dishes as well as house specialties for the curious palette. I really enjoyed: Pasta Fagoli soup Caprese app Ravioli del Giorno (3 cheese) with the house ragu as well as a few bites of the dishes from my group, of course! I can't say that I will be running back to this place only because I feel like this city has more to offer me. This part of town is not a typical dinning location for me anyway. I would, however, eat here again if I was in the area for a show and not interested in leaving midtown to eat. I would also HIGLY recommend TT to anyone looking for a nice Italian meal before/after a trip to Broadway.

Their soup is GREAT !!! I am a ramen fan but never ever had any soup this good. (more delicious than Ippudo) We went there at 3 PM and waited for 15- 20 minutes. (it was their slowest time. and do not try to come in a big group. They can accommodate only 4 people top.)

I came here last night and my experience was great! I got here around 6:30 PM and was seated immediately. The decor is very nice--spacey and comfortable. Seating is good for either parties of 2, 4, 6, and probably more. They had a lot of tables. Dim lighting also helped set a relaxing mood; it was romantic, but not too romantic. There was also a nice bar area if you were interested. Service was pretty good in my opinion. Right as we were seated, we got our menus and a bread basket. They asked if we needed any drink menus and was friendly when we said we needed a few more minutes. We ended up ordering the Classico appetizer, which had clams, shrimp, and mushrooms.
