This was delicious. I usually don't enjoy shrimp that much, but this was cooked just right. I ordered the Gnocchi alla Baba entrÃ©e and my boyfriend had the Farfalle Primavera. The gnocchi was cooked just right, soft and chewy, and the farfalle had a nice healthy taste to it with a lot of vegetables. The waiters were attentive and stopped by to ask if we needed anything or whether our food was good. They came around each time we got our food to ask if we wanted some pepper or cheese on it. At my stay there, I believe at least 5 waiters came to serve us, whether it was with cheese, pepper, utensils, menus, or dishes. At some other restaurants I have visited, waiters don't serve you if they're not assigned to. Not at this restaurant! I was actually surprised when a different waiter took our bill. I think tip was included in our bill also. Oh and one last thing, as we were leaving, the host (I think) eagerly followed us a few steps and asked if we enjoyed our meals. Thumbs up here. I noticed that the listed attire for this place is "casual." Maybe it was because it was a Monday at 6:30, but most of the people that dined were dressed up--no jeans and mostly collared shirts. My boyfriend and I were in jeans, hoodies, and sneakers, so we felt a little out of place. As a matter of fact, we were painting ceramics in the day and happened to get paint splashes on our clothes. (It was entirely my fault.) I just couldn't help but laugh the whole time. So I hope they didn't mind that we were dressed like bums. Overall, I had a good experience here. I think I saw two floors here, so seating should not be a problem most of the time. Stopping here before a show is probably a good idea. I would come back for a nice quiet dinner.

Alrite people, this a dinner review for J&N, a forest hills gem located at the end of austin street and intersecting Ascan. Went here on a tuesday night on a double date with wifey, Michael K, and Natalie. Never been here before but I always drive by this place when I'm headed towards the Jackie Robinson Parkway and going to BK to work. Has definitely been on my bucket list for awhile now. We were seated close to the entrance. The establishment is not big, per se, but it is long and narrow and operating out of a small kitchen. A full sized bar commands the place and is very prominent upon entering. We decided to order a bevy of plates , so we can munch on a few things rather than individual portions. At first, we ordered a wine bottle for the table : Cabernet Sauvignon, because we classy like that. The appetizers consisted of an amazing hummus plate with chickpeas in the middle and partially oven toasted pita bread and we also opted for the lamb meatballs with pureed cauliflower ( my choice of course because i love broccoli's less know cousin). The appetizers were great and very well made, i was surprised. I didn't know what to expect on Austin St. sometimes because a lot of the relatively new restaurants flop within six months of opening. On to the entrees, we had the : Kale Chicken Salad with herb croutons and Steak Salad. Both were very good and we didn't order to much due to it being so late. I enjoyed the dim lit, intimate atmosphere, especially in a local spot. Heard from my sitter that Brunch here is pretty amazing as well. Will be returning to try a few more items on the dinner menu such as the cheese boards, seared salmon with cauliflower and spinach, and also the J&N burger. ( Yes, i like to keep my dinner options open. Don't you?). check this place out , yelpers..

We found our way here in search of ceviche and left very satisfied. Definitely try the ceviche (obv), lobster taquitos and sangria braised short ribs! To top it off, the service was excellent. Â We'll definitely be back!

Charming Thai restaurant in park slope! Food: Overall a 4 /5. spicy noodles with shrimp - generous portions of shrimp. The vegetables and herbs that were used complemented the dish. Rich in flavor, but it was a tad saltier than what I'm used to. These were the flat rice noodles Mussels - huge portions and the sauce was delicious Pad see-ew - it was full of flavor but i thought it was ok. Half way through, I wanted to try a new flavor. It didn't stand out compared to other pad see-ews. These were the flat rice noodles. Pad Thai - I have to admit, it's among one of the best pad thai dishes I've tasted. Excellent flavor and portion size. The only thing is...there's too much bean sprouts, but you can always push it aside. Service: It was ok. My family came on a Saturday night at 7pm. We waited for about 45 minutes. They were extremely busy, so they did the best they can. I was glad that they refilled our waters without us flagging them down. They came by once to see how our meals were and if we needed anything else. Ambiance: Pretty modern. They have a small section for bar seating. There is indoor and outdoor seating. I recommend trying the outdoor seating on a cool night. Â Their menus are on construction paper and the specials are handwritten, which is rather unique. Tips: They do not take reservations and it's CASH ONLY!
Delish and fun. Â I LOVE noodle soups and miss having veggie options - the vegetarian ramen here is amazing. Â If you're lucky, there will be shrimp buns on the special list, those are unreal.

Great drinks and atmosphere! Also, the staff is so friendly, not pretentious. Â Great place to host a party because they arent the NYC ridiculousness of paying over $1000 to buy bottles just to get al your friends in. Also, the place has wonderful character.
The wait is long. The food is good. The bloody, just okay. Will I be back? Probably not. Too many other options without the hour foreplay.

Big fun. Â This place I really love, though it's got the special appeal of being a go-to spot for people coming into Grand Central Terminal. Â But good prices, great food and drink, Â (not suggesting their special, expensive evenings unless someone is taking you there...), and excellent sake. Â One of my favorite places in the City.

So pleasantly surprised at how beautiful this place was. The decor and lighting is just so inviting. Staff is professional and attentive. Food is inventive and new. Nice way to start a night in the city. Check the dips out they're not to be missed.

So one thing you should know about me it's very hard for me not to order chicken and waffles when it's on a menu. Every since going to LA and having Roscoe's I've been hooked. The Buckwheat waffles and chicken at Pies - n -thinghs were good but no Roscoe's but really I would not even try to compare them they are totally different things. So Peis - n - things chicken was flavored very well, the waffle was soggy. I can't rate them for anything else but if you looking for C & W keep looking.

Went here for my engagement dinner after my fiancÃ© proposed to me in Central Park. The staff made the night incredibly special for us. We were treated to complimentary champagne, and we received a free dessert with "Congratulations" written in chocolate on the plate. We also received complimentary courses and a tea cake to take home for breakfast the next day (it looked as though everyone who dined at the restaurant received these goodies as well!). All of the food was amazing. We split a seafood salad to start. I forget what the entrees were (I was too distracted by the fact I had just got engaged), but it all tasted amazing (I do remember that). And the bread cart was super unique! Great place for a slow-paced, romantic dinner!
Meh... the variety in sauces is wonderful, but the fries you dip them in are not THAT good. They're okay. Plus, it's a small cramped space...you can't be in there too long, it gets uncomfortable.

This is one of my top 5 favorite NYC restaurants! It's best to go first thing in the morning to avoid a wait, but I've never had a bad meal or cocktail here! The food is fresh and the specials are always good, but I'm head over heels in love with their linguine and clams! The service is professional and I always feel like Im having a NYC moment, eating and window shopping in soho! A must visit. Bon appetite.

Whenever I walk past, this place is always bustling but luckily we were able to get a table for two around 11:30am on a Sunday with no wait! The brunch gods were smiling upon us. I got a beautiful iced cappuccino and the entree of a poached egg on top of goat cheese potato cake with ratatouille. It was tasty and a good size for your buck. We also tried the lavender creme brulee which was heavenly. The lavender flavor really shone through the dessert. Service was speedy and attentive. It really does feel like you're dining in a French cafe!

I'm posting the same review for both Totto and Ippudo. This is not because I'm lazy, but because I've done some serious statistical analysis to determine who has better food. Here we go! DISCLAIMER - I did not calculate the percentages in order to skew my decision. I have scientific proof that these are the weights that should be given to each of these ingredients. RAMEN (60%): Broth (33%) Totto - 7.9 Ippudo - 9.9 Totto's broth was good but was lacking a little salt. I must say that when paired with the beef, the broth was perfectly seasoned, but on its own, Ippudo's broth is what I will get to drink in Heaven. Noodles (25%) Totto - 8.6 Ippudo - 6.8 Ippudo's noodles were more like soba noodles than ramen noodles. Totto's were better but I've had better noodles at many other places. I must say, I was slightly disappointed. Pork (24%) Totto - 10 Ippudo - 9.7 Both places were AMAZING. Neither place really skimps out on the pork (although Totto's is overflowing) and the melt-in-your-mouth succulence is indescribable. Other (12%) Totto - 9.1 Ippudo - 9.2 All the other fix-ins for the ramen were delicious at both locales. The eggs are perfectly cooked and they give you tons of veggies, bamboo shoots, and narutomaki. Also, if you order the spicy ramen at either place, they'll be sure that you can feel the heat. Price (3%) Totto - 7 Ippudo - 4 Ippudo is mad expensive. They charge you for the pork in your ramen and even if you don't get it, it'll run you a pretty penny. Quantity (3%) Totto - 9 Ippudo - 8.2 Totto gives you a lot more but Ippudo isn't far behind. Combine the Ramen with some Pork Buns and you'll be fine. PORK BUNS (40%): Pork (39%) Totto - 10 Ippudo - 9.1 Totto wins the pork battle once again and with a little more separation than in the ramen. However, neither one really lacks taste or texture, although the Ippudo pork could be SLIGHTLY softer. Bun (38%) Totto - 8.5 Ippudo - 10 Ippudo's bun is what angels sleep on. It's soft, melts in your mouth, and has a tiny bit of sweetness that goes well with the salty, savory, and spiciness of the other ingredients. Sauce (17%) Totto - 8 Ippudo - 9.4 Ippudo's spicy mayo beats whatever sauce was on Totto's pork bun. As mentioned before, the slight hint of spiciness is part of the perfect formula for pork buns. Price (3%) Totto - 4 Ippudo - 4 Price really wasn't a factor, although, both were overpriced. Lettuce (3%) Totto - 8.1 Ippudo - 8.2 Although Totto uses mixed greens while Ippudo uses iceberg lettuce, I really thought the iceberg lettuce let the pork bun's real nature shine through better than Totto's greens. But as you can see from the rating, the difference is negligible. Final Score: Totto - 8.78 Ippudo - 8.98 Ippudo wins by a hair! But to be honest, I'd go to either again in a heartbeat.

Last week we went there, as a party of 5, to celebrate a friend's birthday. Of course we brought along a birthday cake that we bought, and I politely asked the waiter to store it and bring it after the dinner was over. We ate a lot of really delicious food, to be precise, $280 worth of food. Boqueria charged us $3.50 per person with the most ridiculous explanation I've ever heard in my life: "cake cutting fee." I politely told the manager how disappointed I was about this. It's not like we used their restaurant to eat the cake. It was a birthday and after 4 pitchers of sangria, lots off appetizers and food - we wanted to celebrate our friend's birthday, with a cake. But we had to pay $17.5 + tax, for this privilege. I think this is very greedy on Boqueria's part, and no matter how good their food is, I am not planning to ever go back there.

a great spot for a late night snack. the classic black bean taquitos are delicious and not too salty. the sauce with fresh lettuce was a good complement. the staff is super friendly too! this was my first time having taquitos and I would likely come back for more

Gah, I hate to be one of those vegetarians who recommend mock meat meals only to have carnivores roll their eyes. But I swear, eat at Champs and you totally won't miss the meat. I'm a huge fan of their breakfast burrito. It's a big portion filled with yummy tofu scramble & spicy "sausage" topped with a chipotle sauce. So good! I really like the savory crepe, but my all time favorite is the fake BLT. It's a monster triple decker of flavor. For dessert, the vegan cheesecake is what you need. The kitschy diner decor is a fun contrast to the edgy-yet-adorable tatt'd severs. Never had a bad experience here, so it's ranking among my favorite breakfast joints in the 'burg.
Macaron!!! I've had their macarons in France and this location is just the same! Love their pretty boxes and packaging. Personal favorites are pistachio and coffee.

I don't know why everyone is still so crazy about this spot and late at night you'll see the usual long line stretching down right by the Hilton. Over the years i think the guys have been getting too big for their britches as the quality of food has gone down. Few years back the lamb and chicken were of great quality and the rice was perfectly cooked. Now as of today 2013 chicken is of poor quality with cartiledge, lamb is overly cooked and dried out and the yellow rice is not even cooked all the way through as you'll chew on not full cooked crunchy yellow rice. So sad to see what use to be a great cart go down in quality as their success is too big now. The only item that's quality is the same is the famous white sauce. Yes it's all about the white sauce. Not sure what the secret ingredients are in the white sauce but it makes anything taste good including the poorly prepared chicken/lamb over rice. Good to see that at least the sauce is still good. Also the 5 alarm small container of hot sauce. Wow, that is super hot as i can only use a bit over my plate. Hopefully they can get their act back together.

We were looking for a relatively light dinner so only ordered an appetizer to share and salads, but both left a solid impression. Â Oh my what glorious flavor! Â We were also pleasantly surprised with the complementary pea dip and warm flat bread. Â The salads (h o r i a t i k i ), although relatively simple, were fresh and perfectly seasoned. Great Pizza !
Good burgers.. Slow service.. But nice atmosphere and their Malbec is worth a try..
Great bahn mi and loved the bahn mi fries. A bit disappointed with the bulgogi sandwich though. Too much mayo and the kimchi didn't taste like much.

My fave shwarma place in the city. When friends come from out of town-- I usually take them around to concoct 'Grace's MacDougal Street Sampler', which consists of 1 Chicken Unda Roll from 'Kati Roll', 1 Israeli House Toast from 'Press Toast', and 1 Lamb Shwarma from 'Mamoun's'.

Yum! Authentic fresh Japanese noodles. I came here on a full stomach because i knew i wouldn't be able to eat it any other day so i dragged my boyfriend here with me and i ordered the lunch combo that includes a rice bowl and bowl of noodles. As full as i was already, i still stuffed my mouth and enjoyed every bite of the noodles! The udon noodles was so fresh and the soup broth was tasty. i wish i would've had an empty stomach when i came, nevertheless, i still enjoyed the food. The ambiance felt as if i was in Japan. I loved the decor and the service was very friendly.

i enjoy eating in this Restaurant food is amazing always a good experience. The gluten free pasta is super~ they are very friendly, it is a pleasure eating in Bistango I recommend it to everyone like good Italian food and all the people need to eat gluten free, it is the paradise a big plus are the prices !!! congratulations

I went in for a beer and fish and chips on the recommendations of Â co -workers and I rediscovered Mollys. But Â just when I thought they won me over --the bartender tried to get over blatantly overcharging me for my fish and chips. All for naught --They won't see me again !!!

I go here at least once a month for brunch because it is so incredible!! The breakfast Â brioche Â sandwich is a must for brunch with a bloody Merry or fresh squeezed orange juice! The servers are all very happy and welcoming as well. If you come here for lunch or dinner the Vegan burger is to die for! Their regular burger is also incredible, but as an avid meat eater, I still go for the vegan burger ( it's one of the only delicious veggie burgers I have found). All of that being said almost the whole menu is worth trying. The cozy low key environment tops off the experience and makes it a must if you are in Bushwick!!

Great food. Â I as disappointed to only eat here once while on my business trip to NYC. Â Its a Japanese diner, its not fancy but the food is very good. Â A large group would be difficult becuase of the size and popularity of this plce. I will go back.

These Japanese style crepes are really delicious!! The outside of the store reminds me of a Harajuku store front in Japan. Inside is a very small space but neat and clean looking. The crepes I've tried are the BLT, Avocado Shrimp, Azuki berries & Yuzu Soda. After eating them, I felt like it was a gourmet meal instead of a normal crepe. From the beautiful presentation, you can see mostly all of the ingredients from the top view. very well designed cone holder/togo bag. For the price, you get fresh & high quality ingredients. Like the bacon in the BLT is thick/juicy, the shrimps are plump and have nice texture to them. Tofu sauce & yogurt whip is light & tasty (feels healthy:)) and the homemade chocolate truffles is to die for in the real matcha green tea icecream! They even use rice flour to make their crepes wheat free. I'm craving to go back and try out the rest of these guilt free crepes on their menu!

Yes! to French press coffee. On to the food: The Grain salad with farro, lentils, barley quinoa with tomato vinegar and green apple dressing was way too salty. So salty that I didn't finish the blend. Â  Grass fed steak & cage free eggs. Friend said it was "alright," but wasn't impressed. In terms of decor, this place definitely is going for the wood washed, airy cleanliness of a modern country kitchen. Which is a peaceful thing that's for sure. The food, however, wasn't that impressive in the end. But the coffee? You can't go wrong!

I was looking forward to trying any of the Momofuku restaurants during a recent trip to NYC. We decided on this one. Upon reading the reviews I couldn't wait to try the interesting menu! But after my meal I found it to be very "just okay". I hate to say this, but I feel that this place was wayyy over hyped. Small portions for pretty prices. It was packed, so of course everything took a long time to arrive. Pork Buns. Since my visit its become clear that everyone loves them. They were good. 2 pork buns with delicious pork, a small amount of hoisin sauce and green onion. The meat was good, but it was basic. Small Portion. We were 3 people and there were 2 buns. Sweet Breads- I forget the exact preparation but they weren't the best Ive had. I'd say they were unfortunately some of the "not better" ones I've had. Rice Cakes with Spicy Sausage and Chinese Broccoli- I found this to be overwhelmingly spicy. It had a kick. I love spicy and heat, but it was borderline overpowering. I'm not looking for overpowering when I'm going to a fancy Asian fusion place. Not much sausage. The broccoli was good and added a nice texture compared to the glutinous rice cakes and mushy-like sausage in sauce. This dish left me feeling full. The chewy glutinous rice cakes made my stomach hurt. Unfortunately I found it forgettable. It took me a few months to write this review because, well, I kinda forgot about it. I liked it, but I was expecting so much more from the way reviewers were tooting Ssam Bar's horn. It's glorified Asian Fusion Cuisine. I guess I should stick to authentic Asian cuisine. I will say service was nice enough and the restaurant was beautiful.

Came here on a Tuesday night for my suite mates birthday. There was really no wait. as we walked in, we saw the grill where the cooks prepare the meal right in front of you; it looked cool, but we were seated in the back. Anyways, once we were seated we looked over the menu-- and as a non seafood eating (typically) gal, the options were very, very limited. I settled for the hot Udon noodle dish (only one of two noodle dishes they offer). Once we had all ordered our food, the waitress told us that there was $20 order minimum per person. I wish we had been told this before, as it could really be a deal breaker for some. Anyways, we then ordered more stuff from the menu to fulfill our $20 requirement. I ordered a side of chicken dumplings. When the food arrived, everything tasted very... hmmm i guess "authentic" would be the word to use. yeah, everything tasted very authentic. After the first few bites, I got used to the seaweed taste in my udon, and it was pretty good! also, the chicken dumplings were pretty amazing! overall, I thought the food was pretty good (considering I have a pretty westernized palette), and the presentation was great!! I would probably not return, but that's mainly because I am not a big seafood person, and that's mainly their specialty. also, if it's someone's birthday, let them know, they'll be sure to celebrate with you! ;)

Ok. Â So this is not a "classic" burger, but man oh man is it tasty, juicy, and cooked just right. Â I have to agree that the fries weren't anything special, but who needs them? Â I was saving my calories (not that I needed to take in more) for the cheesecake spring roll. Â It was as good as advertised. Â I would recommend you try both.

Okay, fine. I might have gone here at 4 am after a night out, but look. When a food cart has a line at 4 am you know it must be good. What I do remember about the food here is that the rice and the chicken were seasoned so well that they were both very flavorful. Honestly though, I think most of these reviews are a result of the high from a night out in New York, but nevertheless, it is completely worth it to come here, especially given the alternatives that are a worse use of your dollar (artichoke, cafeteria). WARNING: do not put on too much red sauce. My friend put it on for me, and I mistakently let him do whatever he thought was best. Biggest regret--ruined my food and my night. Okay maybe that is an exaggeration, but certainly made it harder to eat.

Um, if I were rich- and lived in NYC- I would eat here every day. Our meal Friday night at Yakitori Totto was a Japanese food lover's dream. Since travelling extensively in Japan this past year, my SO and I are always on the look-out for food Japanese food (and unfortunately there is none in DC that is (a) not sushi (b) affordable). This place really impressed us! We ordered a lot of different dishes, but the standouts were the tuna and avocado salad with flying fish roe, yakitori- pork belly, eggplant with miso, bacon-wrapped mushroom, and the chicken skin (crunchy goodness that you know better than to eat, but after a lot of saki, you abandon all hopes of healthy eating), and the rice dish with raw egg, chicken and scallions (this was unreal- I am trying to find a recipe to make this at home). Service was decent, given that the place was packed. There is a good saki list, as well.
Ambiance and food combined make this a classic west village spot to impress a visiting friend or date.

The food was great, the service was pretty good, but what won me over was their energy to right a wrong. A cup of red sauce got knocked over next to me and splashed up on my dress. They got me seltzer and a rag, and bought my table another round of drinks immediately. I have had similar experiences in other restaurants and at Fish they took care of me far better then any other place. Yes, the world is clumsy with me. :) I will be back there again soon. They gave me a great 1st impression, and the food was really good.

My husband took me here for my birthday and we loved it!! They wished me a happy birthday when we arrived which was so sweet and just took really good care of us the entire time we were there. The food was amazing! Everything else that we saw come out of the kitchen looked incredible too but I'm not sure we'd ever be able to bring ourselves to order anything other than the pork shop and the Evans chicken. :O) Both were amazing!! We also got a little cheese and shared a bottle of prosecco and we were surprised that the bill wasn't near as high as we expected for such a wonderful meal at a great restaurant. You can't beat the location either! We really can't wait to go back.
Brunch here was DAMN good. I don't remember what I ate, but it was delicious. Huge wait on the weekend...Grab an open spot a the bar if you don't want to wait.

WOW. Â We looked at restaurants on our GPS under Italian and this came up. Â Walked in the smell would bring you to your knees. Â PLUS they were playing Italian Opera. My boss said if it is half as good as it smells we are in for a treat. Â Well it was better than that. Â My boss is a pro with Philly steaks and Philly Hoagies and he had one that he said was a HOMERUN! Â One of the best he has had. Italian food is my most favorite and I had Penne Alla Boscaiola. Â  OUT OF THIS WORLD. Â I have eaten in the "little Italy's" in Boston, New York, Scotland, San Francisco, Minneapolis MN to name a few. Â The food quality was 5 Diamonds that all I can say. Â I will make plans whenever I am NEAR this place to go in and try other items. Â Our tiny waitress with her cool black glasses (Tanya???) I do not remember was personable and just so funny about her restaurant. Try it you cannot lose!

5 stars for service however the food was not what I expected, except for the Paella and Date Pudding, I will definitely go back for those two! I ordered a bunch of stuff but what was a disappointment was the Burrata they had as a special. It was stacked with sliced tomatoes, arugula and red onions; thick enough to outshine the burrata, not worth the $18 for an appetizer. The place is cozy, welcoming but definitely don't go with more than one person, it's tiny! One of Heidi's best asset is service, they are all extremely nice and accommodating! There can be a wait list sometimes so tried calling in advance to put your name down.

Loved this wine bar! It didn't have as large of a selection as I imagined in wine, but good none the less. The service was fun and helpful; they kept our waters full and bread basket from going empty. The food was absolutely delicious and the final bill seemed like a deal for the quality you recieve.
This place is great! Food is awesome! Long Live the Potato!!!

Came here with friends (3 people including myself) and had a wonderful time. I must admit that this place was small but when i went it wasn't packed at all. The food here is cheap and that's what makes it great too. The food is cooked once you order so you don't have to be afraid of cold food. All the food here is spicy so for people who don't enjoy spicy foods, its OKAY! Just tell the guy that you don't want it spicy. The table counter is filled with all sorts of spicy sauces so if you LOVE the spice, you HAVE TO come!

Went here for the first time last night and sat in a very pleasant corner booth. Â The decor was simple and classy -- no craaazy items on the walls etc. Â It was quite romantic. The service was almost perfect. Â Our waiter was professional yet funny, and not scared to banter with us. Â There was definitely a feel-good vibe running through this place. We ordered the fried oysters (A-), butcher steak (B+) and fried chicken (A). Â The surprising thing was the reasonable prices. Â 15 dollars for an entree in a nice place is definitely good to see. Â All in all a great evening, and I will be back.

Great tapas, great atmosphere, and good place for groups! The service here is pretty good, but the food is what really makes this place stand out, o yeah and their sangria helps too! My favorites here are: - Potatoes with garlic alioli yum! -octopus salad -bread rubbed with tomatoes and garlic and some prosciutto on top is amazing -fried quail egg and chorizo on toast is a must try -croquettes are delicious ( mushroom are my fave) -shishito peppers are the best thing ever - lamb meatballs - good hanger steak - paella is a great dish and perfect to share They also offer great daily specials so pick a few dishes and share away! Try the churros with the chocolate sauce for dessert.

The first time I ate at Bouley was in 1996. My mother in-law took my husband (fiancÃ©e at that time) and me for dinner to celebrate our graduating Graduate School from Columbia. The experience Â for me was beyond divine. Even though it was almost 12 years ago, I still remember being delighted by every course we were served! Little did I know at that time that Bouley would close down that very year. I've never forgotten that meal. I really think it was one of the best meals I have ever had....in my entire life! So, after 12 long years of Bouley having closed, reopened, moved locations and so on, I finally went back to try it one more time. This time I went for lunch. They have a great pre-fix deal for lunch for $48. Read more about Bouley at: therestaurantfairy.com/?â€¦

The food and bourbon selection here is excellent -- you definitely get what you pay for, and the menu is incredibly solid, well-seasoned, filling and effing delicious. That being said, I don't think they're shelling out for the additional servers they need to keep up with the restaurant's increasing popularity. I'm thrilled that more people are spending money at this restaurant, but when I went two weeks ago for dinner, there were two waiters working for a packed house and bar. No one asked us if we wanted a second cocktail (we did), a food item we ordered was forgotten when our entrees came out, and when we reminded our very polite yet clearly frazzled waiter about it, he ran off to get it and never came back. Nobody checked on us during our meal, and it took an hour to get our check. Nobody asked if we'd like to see a dessert menu (we would have). Still, food was great, but as I write this, it's just a bad experience that makes me think the owner is cheap. Staff your restaurant properly if you want people to want to come back.

Never go out for dinner in NYC on a Saturday night without a reservation. After being quoted for 1 hr or more waits at every restaurant we asked, my friend and I were hungry and grumpy. People shouldn't be allowed to talk to me when I'm hungry. I might accidentally bite off your head. We saw Tartine and there was no line outside. I walked in the door and almost ran into a couple seated right by the door having dinner. There was no Maitre D' to greet us because there was no space to stand. I'm astonished as to how they managed to fit tables into every little corner in the room and were still be able to move around. Only in NYC. The food was solid. Brussels sprouts made with dried cranberries and agave nectar, mussels with white wine and a side of fries, poached pear with prosciutto, and the (French) onion soup were all simple yet good. There must of been at least 4 other tables celebrating birthdays. With BYOB it's a great deal. Note to self: Next time bring some wine and cash.
I can't say enough good things about this place. Go at 10:30, 11. Easy, delicious, beautiful space. Good music, great service. Brunch search stops here.

I really had big expectations. I live nearby and knew they were going to open a risotteria, so I kept walking by to check they would finally open. I finally went there after the summer... A big let down. The risotto was eeeewww, and they got the cooking completely wrong, the wine was expensive but tasted cheap. We were a big table and that clearly was a major challenge for them. Sorry, not sure I'll personally be back, I can definitely cook better risotto at home. Still, if you like risotto but are not sure how to cook it this could be a nice enjoyable restaurant.

The pizza is divine, but the service is horrendous, the waiters are outright rude with vengeance. I've always had bad service at the place, but last night tops it all: I was sitting with my friend, I asked the waiter for a cup of water he didn't look at me nor did he confirm in any visible/audible way, I asked again, same thing happened, no confirmation. I asked the third time, and the waiter SNAPs and yells at me loudly in the middle of the restaurant, using slurs and insults. I made him understand that his lack of confirmation is why I asked many times, but he just went on to service other tables. I asked another waiter who witnessed the scene whether this is acceptable behavior for a waiter in this restaurant, and he basically said its my fault since I asked three times for the same thing. I said thats ridiculous, and that I'm leaving, the waiter extended his hand showing me the door. This is New York, and I don't usually expect the best manners and politeness from waiters around here, but this went over the top. Grimaldi will not have my business again.

An East Village staple, this all-Belgian-Fries establishment is a must for anyone who hasn't checked it out yet. Â Their menu consists of small, medium and large-sized fry cones. Â They have over a dozen different sauces that you then smother you fries in. Â Be careful not to combine this tasty treat with a trip to Paul's Burger Joint later in the day or you might not get out alive. Â But please do yourself a favor and go there...now!

Terrific little space where seating is exclusively at a bar that wraps around the preparation area in a long U-shape, creating an appropriately intimate interaction with the bartenders. The original cocktail list is about a page long and looks like it's constantly changing. I find it hard to resist any drink that has egg whites, so naturally I gravitated to the Partridge in a Pear Tree, a gin n pear number. My friend got the James and the Giant Peach which was also excellent, even for someone who's not a huge whiskey fan. We were in a hurry so couldn't order food but the food menu looked and smelled scrumptious and at one point we caught a strong waft of bacon. It was dark but not too crowded or loud on a Thursday night. Will definitely be coming back, maybe with a date.

LOVE this place! Hate the fact that I live two blocks outside their delivery area! Things not to be missed: Truffle potato salad Mushroom, caramelized onion, goat cheese panini On Mondays they have a half priced wine and they always have a nice cheese plate from Murray's that I have to remind myself to share with the rest of the table. Also the back has charming patio. Â Lots of wooden booths and hanging vines. Â Great for a summer night date or get together with the girls.

Ay dios mio. I sigh and close my eyes when thinking of that delicious ramen. Â At the first sip of broth, it was as if a show choir of flavors was dancing complex, gorgeous choreography in my mouth while singing "yes! yes! yes!" Â  I ate at Ippudo for the first time last night. Â It wasn't my first time going; I must've stopped in at least 10 x before but couldn't put up with the wait. Â This time I must've found the right time pocket because I was seated within 15 minutes of arrival. Â I think it helped that I was alone. Â  This food was so good that I couldn't bring myself to brush my teeth for hours after the meal - I just wanted to hold on to it, especially since they don't do leftovers. Â (The flavors won't be as good, which I can see, actually, since as the broth cooled it was less tasty.) It is worth the wait, and I miss the taste so much that I'm going back tonight.

Not sure what all the hype is about here. My boyfriend ordered the Nutella French toast and I'm not sure how he ate that shit. In my opinion it was the worst French toast ever. I don't think brioche bread is supposed to taste stale and I thought French toast was supposed to be soaked in egg and then fried. Penelope's version of nutella French toast was none of this; in fact, it was nutella spread between two pieces of thick, stale bread. $15 and simply put...Awful. I ordered the Penny's egg sandwich on a croissant and it was good, exactly what I needed at the time but I have made better egg sandwiches in my own kitchen for a hell of a lot less then $9. The pesto sauce on it was good but not $9 good. It's unfortunate when the best part of your meal is the $5.50 fresh squeezed juice.

I love their food. Â However, the last 4 times I've ordered from here, it has taken over 1 hour and 45 minutes to receive my food. Â When it says 30-40 minute delivery time on seamless, I expect it to take 30-40 minutes. Â When I call after an hour, I expect the staff to be apologetic, not upset that I'm inquiring about my food. Â And most of all when I ask why it still hasn't left the store after an hour and half, I expect a different response than "we're super busy". You're a gyro shop, it takes 10 minutes to prepare at most. Â c'mon man. Â Hate to say it, but will have to stop ordering from here, even though I love the food.

I expected more. Lombardi's has been named again and again as one of THE NY pizza spots, so I finally gave it a shot. Now, I'm not going to pretend to be a great pizza expert, as I am one of those dreaded Caifornians who keep being mentioned in these reviews. But I know what Di Fara's in Brooklyn tastes like (review coming soon), and this place is not even in the same ballpark. There is practically no cheese (at least on the original pie), and the thin curst verges on flimsy. On the plus side, service is very friendly, and we didn't wait long for a 2-top table on a Thursday night around 9 - maybe 15 minutes. But it's not worth crossing town by bus and subway for.

This is a very nice little restaurant settled in a quiet neighborhood. They have several outdoor seating that should be taken advantage of during the warmer seasons. The pasta here is quite good and on an average of $15 that is portioned reasonably. We had the spaghetti with baby clams in a white wine sauce and gnocchi of the day with shrimp in tomato sauce.

Two stars is defined as Meh. I've experienced better. And truth is....I have experienced way better. At first glance, you're overwhelmed by the extraordinary number of ingredients in each dish. "Wow, butternut squash foam, toasted sesame seeds and lebne! (meatball)" "Oooh, skirt steak with chimichurri sauce, oven roasted jersey tomato and shoe string potatoes! I hear chimi is great with meat!" OK. So that was shock. Now for the awe. Waiter comes over and gently places the large dish in front of you. Hurray! I was so hungry, the fast dish coming out is a pleasant surprise. But wait....where's the beef? Where's anything? Waiter, where's the rest of the dish? ridiculously small servings. Now i know what you're thinking. This is tapas we're talking about. On the contrary, just because tapas are meant to be smaller portioned dishes, is no excuse to insult diners with small Smurf sized portions. A good tapas bar serves a sizeable amount of food that is meant to be shared. You want small enough dishes to be able to sample a multitude of dishes but not small enough that you need a microscope!. Example: The skirt steak with chimi sauce (15 dollars) came literally with 4 slices of steak each the size of a packet of sugar. (not to mention the chimichurri was nuclear green) I left disappointed and more importantly I left hungry and with a whole in my pocket. If you're prepared to drop 400 dollars to feel something in your stomach. This is the place for you. It's a pretty restaurant, but overpriced for what you're getting and taking advantage of diners who don't actually know what tapas are supposed to look like. ("my dish is kinda small Sarah. "no no jane, they're supposed to be really small, its SPANISH TAPAS" ** stars - stupidly overpriced for what you're getting, and the food wasn't even all that great. Bring your magnifying glass to view the food and the menu. As for decor, really beautiful decor, almost like a 2 story barn with iron chandeliers. Just do yourself a favor, if you and your friends really want to go out for good food and enjoy spanish tapas, there are many tapas bars around to choose from. This one is more for the looks and trendiness than anything else. Good luck. For those of you in college and on a budget. This place is off the charts on my break-the-bank-o-meter.

Scarpetta located lower west side is good for dining at a table or just eating at it's ten seat bar as you enter. The staff is professional and the food has been consistent during my eight dinners. The decor is very masculine with dark woods and rich deep colors. I always have a pasta course and meat or fish entree. All have been very good and some excellent. Desserts are worthwhile for sure. Come here for the food and good atmosphere for nice conversation with friends, date or a business meeting. The wine list is extensive and well rounded. Be sure to make a reservation. The location is also great for other places to have a night out with a group of friends as the bar scene in the Meat Packing District is very good.
Fantastic. A perfect dinner experience. The food, the drinks, the staff . . . flawless.

I had brunch here today for the first time an I have to say it was AMAZING! My friends and I were looking to try a new restaurant and we will all definitely be returning. I had the Texas French toast with a side of home fries. I'm am literally obsessed with their French toast it's the best I've ever had. I would recommend it to anyone who was a first timer. It is enough to make you want to come back every weekend for brunch. Kudos to the chef!
super cool spot, with super cool dishes and cocktails. Â sadly i didnt like the bong smoked oysters...
Excellent and original food! Nice service.

What a great little find! The best roasted chicken-even the rotisserie is from France. Â Everything is very fresh and high quality. Â We were going to get it to go but ended up sharing the table and met the owner. Â She was a delight and told us about her quality chickens. Amazing apple tart. Â Everything tastes very homemade. Â Great vibe, location and food.

Last week my friend and I were tackling her bucket list of must try eateries in Manhattan. Â That coupled with my New Years resolution to expand my list of go to restaurants in my neighborhood brought us upon this amazing little nook. Â The restaurant we intended to go to was packed, which led us to Five Tacos. My girlfriend and I sat at the bar of this spotless little joint and decided to have a drink and try the tacos. The food was incredible and the different sauces complemented the tacos perfectly. Â I am very big on service, and the staff was very attentive and accommodating. Definitely a must go!

I went on a business trip to NY and had been craving some good old southern cooking and I had heard about Amy Ruth's and decided to try it. My first impression when I arrived there was that it was an extreme difference in the atmosphere than I saw on the website. The outside looked like hell and the inside made the restaurant look unappetizing becaue it looked like a fast food joint. I was expecting it to look a little more like a cozy family restaurant with history like it had been advertised on the website, and less like a fast food joint on the inside but oh well, I still decided to stay and give it a try and...glad I did! I ordered the Barack Obama (smothered fried chicken) Â and 3 sides (mac and cheese, potato salad, and collard greens) because I felt like being extra greedy! Even though the food came to the table barely warm, the chicken was moist and the mac and cheese was cheesy enough for me (which is saying alot cuz I like cheese) and it still satisfied my craving for good soul food...I ended up getting a doggy bag and a piece of red velvet cake to go which was very rich and moist and tasted home made :-) I will be back again but next time I'm gettin the chicken and waffles!! I just hope next time I go there, the inside and the outside look a little more cozy.

this place is more about drinks and noise than food. ordered tacos and it came with pieces of uncooked differnt type meat mixed in with the actual meat type I ordered. the hostess stood at the front texting on her phone and ignoring people while snapping her gum. this place is just trashy and the food is not good. won't be back.

I've been here twice already and I think the concept definitely has a lot of potential. Â The chicken is of the highest quality, and you can tell by its tenderness (chicken tenders, duh!). On my first visit, I had the lime chicken, which was grilled. Â Unfortunately, I don't quite remember what sauces I got on the side, but I felt that this was a very nice and classic rendition of lime chicken. Second time, I brought a friend and we tried the buffalo chicken (and I was told to get the spicy version). Â We paired it with the Carlos sauce, which was some sort of mayo. Â I loved the buffalo sauce. Â And then, the General Tso, which was an interesting take on the Chinese-American classic. Â And, the soy ginger sauce was great too. Â Both orders were perfectly breaded -- and not too fried. I think for me, the only downside is that the price can be a bit steep, especially if you go for lunch. Â 3 fingers isn't quite enough to satisfy me, which means that I'd need 5, although admittedly, I am yet to try any of the sides, which also look good. Â But even then, you're talking about 12 bucks for lunch. Â For dinner, I don't mind paying that. Â Not at all. Â But a place like this could definitely stand to have some sort of lunch combo, maybe coming in at 8 or 9 bucks. Â With that said, I do look forward to returning for a quick and tasty bite. Â And, I might add that I've talked to the owner on both my visits and he's quite attentive. Â Good job so far.

Been getting my sicilian pizza with rainbow spumoni from this place since I was six. I didn't know how good the sicilian pizza here was until I tried others... and... realized I was spoiled. I have an unhealthy love affair with the spumoni... I buy a quart size thinking I'll have it in my freezer for the entire week... but it only lasts one night. Seriously people, sicilian pizza + spumoni are a match made in heaven.

sliders, i dont eat often prefer a burger. taste was alright, not bad but not one of the best i tried. small place. dont know if their meat is organic. not much variation. good place to stop by to grab something quick. i should have told them no onions since i dont like fried or steamed. also didnt ask how i want it cooked.

Stopped here for a late dinner with my gf & roommate after grabbing flights @ Good Beer. Was in the mood for some Latin food, & Yuca Bar really hit the spot. The 3 of us walked in around 10, & the hostess told us we'd have to wait about 20 minutes for a table. Hungry, we opted for open seats @ the counter near the door. To our delight, the hostess came back a couple minutes later to lead us to an outside table. We were quite satisfied with our food selection. We shared 3 tapas items & 1 entree: red snapper ceviche, platano relleno, arepa con carne, & puerquito Cubano. Everything was tasty, but all 3 of us loved the entree. Fatty pork shoulder with a mojo sauce & mashed platanos make me salivate merely recollecting. The drinks were solid, as well. My roommate had a mojito, while my gf & I opted for caipirinhas. I vowed to find a bottle of cachaca to make my own in the near future. Overall, very satisfied. Our bill was a tad pricey, but drinks accounted for nearly half. We all left stuffed after cleaning the plates. Several blocks away after our meal, I realized I forgot a bag with 2 bottles of Lightning beer on the ground next to the table. We were much relieved to recover them from the hostess upon our return a few minutes later.

We've ordered the whole grilled chicken several times at Purbird, along with one or two of their salads, and each time we've had it, the chicken was EXCELLENT, just the best damned grilled chicken I can recall eating. Â In fact, we cannot get past that grilled chicken. Sooner or later we'll have to try one of the other things on the menu, but each time I think of passing up that grilled chicken, I think, "...the hell with it, I'm gonna get that chicken..." Yes, the menu is limited. Â Wise choice. Â They decided to concentrate on one thing, chicken, and, boy, do they get it right. Â There are a lot of places that could take a lesson from Purbird. Â  I doubt that my words can convince you how good this chicken is. Â Do yourself a favor and either drop in or call them for a delivery if you're lucky enough to be in their delivery area. Â Order the full grilled chicken. Â If you can't finish it, you can take it home for a second extraordinary meal later. Â Nope, not cheap. Â But if you like chicken, you won't begrudge one cent of the price. Lucky me to have Purbird in my neighborhood...

one of the best sandwiches that i've put in my mouth in a long time. got the super cub classic and it was delicious. Bread was crunchy yet doughy - a perfect baguette for a bahn mi. would 100% return and recommend to anybody around the neighborhood.

this review is long overdue, and i went with my girlfriend months ago. I still look forward to going back again. the first thing i noticed was that the location and decor was all well balanced and put together. the day we went, it was nice and sunny so it made for a nice country home dining ambiance. our waitress was great! very informative, patient, and had honest recommendations such as the grilled flatbread, kale and endive salad. my girlfriend had the linguini with brussel sprouts and mushrooms, and i had the fried chicken. both dishes were excellent! very tasty and done well. first off, i want to say the pasta was done well because its done the right way, a nice sauce with ingredients that were well paired to create a nice harmony of flavors with the pasta. not like some restaurants, where i know pasta isnt their forte and they just end up giving you tons of sauce with overcooked pasta. this is a sign of a restaurant who simply has a good chef, and cooks, which usually leads to the rest of the menu being delicious whatever you might want to order. the fried chicken i had was also done well, the batter was a more crunchy and chunky and country type of style which was great. as many of has tried many different kinds of fried chicken, i don't care if people say they don't like it. fried chicken is one of the many things that can be very subjective and screw all you who try to make it sound like your opinion on it is the only one people should listen to. and on that note, if you've been here recently and had to wait in line for a long time and have complaints, shut up, and just go eat something. otherwise understand the fact that restaurants get busy, they get popular and yes, other people will gladly wait as well. try making a reservation or go out and eat some more and realize on weekends and days that people obviously go out to dine, it WILL be busy. anyways, back to the food. the waffle that came with my fried chicken was cooked nicely, and i was thankful that we chose to eat there at a time it was not overwhelming for the kitchen to serve dinner. its tough when its super busy and people are being attentive to consistency. overall, dinner was exceptional and buttermilk channel definitely satisfied our tastebuds and appetites. OH, props to the bartender, and for them having great fresh juices. we didnt get a chance to order any specialty cocktails or anything but, our campari with grapefruit juice drinks were so great and you could taste that they actually used real fresh juice, verses some places that say they do and just use fruit nectar or bottled. I know i'll be going back again soon to try other things on their menu. maybe even something from their vegetarian menu!? (everything sounded delicious on that menu as well) i didnt notice anything that i didnt like, but the food game is tough, so we will see how they hang in there next visit =)

MMM...I'm preparing of a trip to Seoul this Dec and I'm told this place is pretty authentic. They make their own tofu (organic, mind you...) My gf Grace C. brought me here for the Soon Doo Bu and the hot stone bowls. We had the kimchi soon doo bu & the octopus hot stone bowl bi bim bap and it was soo good!!! :D Of course, this was after some insane sample sale shopping so we were VERY hungry too. Nevertheless I love the atmosphere and ambience of this place. Its got the small, neighbourhood bar kind of feel and there were tons of korean people there = good place for korean food. Looking forward to Seoul next month!! :D

Reservations were made for the restaurant but upon arrival, we made a last minute decision to dine in the Tavern section of the restaurant. The warm space was inviting and we had heard a rumor about a certain hamburger. We were seated promptly at a table facing the window. Service was attentive and friendly from the get-go. We were informed that the limited time burger was on the menu today. So, $26 burger it was! We dined on the cauliflower soup (divine), beet salad (humdrum), house made sausage with spaetzel Â (transcendental), pork chop (best rendiiton to date) and that burger. Oh, that burger. Well worth the price tag, those wagyu beef deaths were not in vain. Dessert was something I can't recall but the server thought one dessert was not enough and brought us out a cookie plate which we devoured like a bunch of little piggies. Which was expected because the table we had was above the vent where the bakery resides and we smelled the sweet aroma of passion fruit caramel the whole time we dined. Worth a return visit and next time, I may even make it to the dining room.
Short and simple, Chipotle style setup with food that blows Chipotle away for a comparable price.

Best Pizza in NY, I understand that statement sounds ludicrous but as far as ingredients and taste Grimaldi's stands above the competition. Fresh cut mozzarella, no single slice sales, a line always outside, this pizzeria is without a doubt something to recognize. Take out and indoor seating is available, a scenic backdrop of the Brooklyn Bridge is very close as well as the Brooklyn Ice Cream Factory. A MUST TRY. Even if the service can be a bit sour, I overheard one of the host ordering a young couple to wake their slumbering child from the carriage since there wasn't any room inside for it.

After an awful experience at Solomon's Porch, my friends and I left there and wandered around Bed-Stuy Looking for a place to fill our empty bellies. Â Lo and behold we stumble across Peaches Market. Â Now I had not been there since back in the day when it was The Akwaaba Cafe. Â However I was delighted to see that someone took over the location and put a good Souther restaurant there. We were seated promptly. Â Our server...a bright young woman with an extensive vocabulary began telling us about the Menu. Â She was great, had a lot of spunk, pizazz, was very much herself, but still so helpful and polite! We started out with the Fried Green Tomatoes....they were delicious!!! Hmm. Â Two of us chose the BBQ Shrimp with Pineapple coconut rice (My personal choice)...it was divine! Â This is a small serving which is good if you want to have an appetizer and dessert. Â One of us had Â the Ribs, though I did not try them I heard they were great. Â Also one of us had the Tilapia I think it was...or some sort of fish....which they cleared off their plates. Â  Then it was time for dessert. I had the Peach Cobbler, which our server described perfectly as "More Peach than Cobbler". Â I loved it this way, you really get to taste the flavors and the peach along with the crust...so good. Peaches Market was delicious and I cannot wait to return. Â It will be great when they have their liquor license as well. Â After a long week grown folks need some grown folk beverages. Â  But I will be back soon see you all there! Happy Eating! Marshana

It's my first time here, and I already love it! Everyone is extremely nice. I ordered an iced latte and a coconut muffin. I'm very impressed that they steam the milk for iced lattes because the texture is so much better than just milk. The prices are great! I'll be coming back for sure!

I am so glad that this was delicious pizza...I was truly thinking it was just going to be another tourist attraction. I was wrong. At least on this day the food was great and service was attentive. The overall ambiance would make me come back. We ordered a large pizza with fresh garlic, onion, mushrooms and black olives. It came out in a timely fashion and was piping hot. The sauce was yum...not too sweet or tangy. The crust was golden brown and mostly crispy. Also, the pizza was not overly cheesy and heavy with oil. They use fresh mozzarella which is not oily at all so the pizza seems less heavy. We were seated upstairs by the window that overlooks the making of the pizzas. We were able to watch them prepare everything. It was a fun experience. The staff were nice, competent and quick. Everyone was smiling and helpful. We will be going back and also trying and comparing other locations :)

Great fresh authentic Korean buffet. Perfect place to grab a quick lunch or to try numerous dishes at the buffet. They weigh your food and charge about $8 per pound so its totally reasonable and everything was delish!

Probably over-hyped. So if you're reading this, I'm probably doing you a favor - when you go, you'll have more normal expectations and not leave disappointed. I was told this was the best italian restaurant that a number of my friends had been to. I would definitely not go that far. The blue crab crostini was fairly bland, the corn ravioli was decent but also not super flavorful. The steak was cooked really well (sometimes it seems medium rare done right is hard to achieve), so... they've got that going for them. Can't remember dessert, but nothing was so great that I would put this back on my "have-to-return-to" list. Seems as though I did miss out on the ricotta though - bummer.

I have never been a fan of Italian food. Perhaps I was always exposed to Jersey Shore type Italian food (I am not judging, only merely making an observation). Too much tomato sauce and never enough of anything else. I was accustomed to "bleeding" Italian food, if you know what I mean. My friend suggested this place for his birthday. Aft first, I was reluctant, but being it was for a celebration, I acquiesced to his requests. The host at the door was extremely friendly. He remembered my name all through the evening. I was impressed with that. That little gimmick will definitely get a customer back. But this place didn't need any gimmicks. After waiting sheepishly for an hour (the host with his charming good looks promised a table in 15 minutes), we were finally seated in probably the best seats in the house. A nice cozy dimly lit table along a wall full of books with a good view of the kitchen. We started off with gnocco fritto ($9.50) with imported cuts, they were small morsels of heaven and they looked like little pillows. My friend ordered the seafood pasta ($12) which was adorned with beautiful lush seafood. I ordered the fritto misto ($15) with red mullet. Both excellent dishes and very well priced. Our cute waitress even suggested a nice bottle of white wine for $23. Unfortunately, she clearly needed some ESOL classes. But cuteness will get you everywhere! In the end, we were satisfied with our meal and Mr. Piggy Bank was safe for another night.

I have heard many good things about ABC and had the opportunity to join my nephew and his wife to celebrate their 8th wedding anniversary. All I can say is "go here NOW". The food is wonderful, inspired and is absolute top quality. Not a whole lot for my wife (Gluten free) but the menu is great. My nephew and I shared the chicken liver on toast and it was incredible. We also ordered the calamari, which was very good. I'm trying to figure out how to manage to make this (the chicken liver pate') an entree'. We then ordered the burger with cheese, arugula and pickled jalapeno peppers. Accompanied by really good, crisp fries, these burgers were awesome and cooked perfectly. My wife had the Carrot and Avocado salad, minus the croutons, which she enjoyed. The other entree's were the Ravioli (which absolutely melted in your mouth) and a pizza which was also quite good. They have a fair selection of bottled beers and we thought the IPAs were a little lacking. Dessert was the Salted Caramel Sundae - ice cream, salted caramel popcorn and chocolate sauce - outstanding! We wanted to order the donuts but they are only available during brunch and dinner. Not a cheap meal by any stretch, but worth every cent and also requires a return trip - just make sure to make reservations.
One of my favorite meals this year! Awesome flavors in every dish.

I love Fette Sau. We came here in the middle of the Great Brisket Rampage of 2014 (the week I ate almost nothing but BBQ) on a whim, but it turned out to be one of our favourite restaurants of the trip. I'm terrible at estimating how much food we need to order, so I asked the guy with the meat to use his best judgement and it was pretty much spot on. We only managed to get seats at the bar and at first I was a bit apprehensive about the whole tray on the bar thing, but it was nice being able to keep the beer flowing as we gorged on tender, delicious, smoky meat. Needless to say, the drinks selection is also excellent and we stayed on both to keep drinking and out of fear my jeans would burst when I stood up.
This place has TERRIBLE service, ordered two mains only got one! When corrected them, they didn't care, just gave us the cheque.Not a good experience on a honeymoon from New Zealand :(

Had a dinner for 7 people for my mom's 60th birthday here last week and it was absolutely perfect. The atmosphere was very nice - happening but not so noisy you couldn't here each other. The service was fantastic - very helpful and responsive but not rushed at all. And most importantly, the food was excellent. We had a special burrata and smoked prosciutto appetizer that was creamy and divine, and a mussels starter that was also great. Some of the entrees included the pasta with wild boar ragu, the Bronzino, the fettuccini with shrimp and scallops, seafood risotto, and the bolognese - all were outstanding. The server recommended a great red wine to go with the meal that everyone really enjoyed. And the desserts were equally delicious. Â I highly recommend the crepes with chocolate sauce and the gelato. Couldn't have been happier with my experience here. Will definitely be back soon!

Stumbled upon this place and was highly disappointed. Our service was awful. The wine was overpriced to begin with, but the really tragic part was that they only give you half a glass! The wine barely reached 1/4 of the way up. Not only that, we had to remind our waitress what we ordered after waiting 20 minutes for drinks when we were one of 3 tables present. She had completely forgotten that we ordered anything at all! From that point on we were ignored by the wait staff and treated like lepers. Very disappointing.

Made reservations a few weeks in advance to take the wifey and in-laws who were on their first trip to NY. Â We also reserved the duck in advance. Our reservations were for 10 PM, so we were starving. Â We ended up ordering a few appetizers because our eyes were bigger than our tummy. Â Our order consisted of the pork buns, kim chi, and the massive duck. Â Our duck came with a few sides; Â potatoes with duck fat drenched and bak choy. Pork Buns - Â good, but Chairman Bao (in San Francisco) and Ippudo are better. Â  Kim Chi - Â unique, but again nothing to write home about. Duck - WOW!! Â This is a huge dish, enough to fill the 5 starving tourists. Â It came with rice, buns, and sauces. Â Personally, I liked the ginger and hoisin sauce the best. Â It's kinda like peking duck where you make a sandwich but if you want less carbs you can use lettuce. Â  We were each impressed with this dish; how flavorful and tender the duck was. Â  The staff was pretty good in re-filling our drinks and accommodating our requests for more sauce and veggies. Â Would be happy to recommend and come back!
Kind of out of the way but the burger truly was amazing. Loved the drinks too.

Came for brunch last Saturday armed with a 12:45 reservation. I actually walked right past the restaurant because it is tucked in a hotel to the right of the entrance. Reservation: the only blip in our experience. We arrived at 12:50 for our 12:45 reservation and were told that our table had been given away. in 5 MINUTES. The reservations person actually seemed surprised we showed up. I mean--we were just surprised that she was surprised. She had to have someone obviously more experienced at seating people find us a table, and then forgot to apologize about screwing up. Ordering: not a big deal but table next to us was seated a few minutes after we sat down but somehow got bread and full glasses of water right away and even ordered before we were able to flag down someone to find us a waiter. I was hangry. Important looking employee in a suit ended up coming to smooth things over and take our order Food: got the skirt steak which was above average; meat was ok. Of course I was famished so inhaled the entire plate. Bread basket was so so good. didn't care much for the spread but the choco chip mini muffins and the little round breads were amazing Drinks: tried the blanco, tropical, and one of the reds. Sangria was strong and tasty, was refilled very often. Wished there was more actual fruit in the drinks but still was amazing. The servers even asked if we would like our drinks filled one last time AFTER clearing our plates. I liked Calle Ocho a lot overall, and will be coming back with the intention of doing a toasty tour of the museum of natural history afterwards next time!
Where else in Midtown Manhattan you can buy actual food for $2? It's a mob in there, try not to push around, wait your turn, please??
Anything taste good after midnight. There food can get real salty at times. It depends what chef you get that day.

Not bad for lunch. Â Small take-out place wedged in between fabric shops. Â Place was basically empty when we walked in at 12:30 on a Wednesday. Â  They offer dishes with four choices of meat (pork aka "go go", chicken, sausage and pork katsu). Â They come in various sizes (walk = small, single = medium, etc.). Â  I got the chicken. Â The curry itself reminds me of tamarind curry that my mom uses in some dishes. Â Kind of sweet and sour, dark in color. Â The chicken comes in breaded strips across the top of a layer of curry with the japanese sticky rice underneath. Â There is some shredded cabbage on the side. Very filling and moderately priced ($7 for a small).

Absolutely outrageous. I don't know how it's taken me so long to review Lam Zhou, but this place is incredible. Nothing on the menu exceeds $5.25 and everything is amazing and fresh. While you eat, you can hear the "whack! whack! whack!" of the guy hitting noodle dough against the steel table. Watching him make the noodles is truly something else. The dry noodles with pork are insane. I prefer the lack of broth just because I want to taste all the noodle goodness. As other reviewers have said--their dumplings best Prosperity, although I still love them and will continue to go. Somehow, some way, it's never crowded. Ever! I guess East Broadway is kind of out of the way, but if you're an F man (as I am), this is one easy, totally worthwhile trip.

I read all the reviews on Yelp. Â I figured this is a good place despite some so so reviews. Â I then spoke to a friend who had been and again a so so review. Â It was GREAT! Â We got there and there was a line. Â They told us a 30-40 minute wait. Â We got inside in under 20 minutes. Â The service was great. Â They were quick and polite. Â It is a small restaurant but you don't notice once you start talking and eating. Â The appetizer sizes were very generous, at least two people can share and appetizer. Â Everything was fresh and good. Â I would go again in a heartbeat.
Very limited choice on food. Plus, the service,,, (Im already speechless). However, the back yard garden was amazing.

I went to Petite Abeille this morning for breakfast and it was nice and quiet and virtually empty at 9:30 on a Saturday morning. The restaurant's atmosphere is great--cheerful, mellow, cozy. I love the tintin books that line the walls. But--the waffle was bad. I ordered it because folks here extolled it and I found it pretty unimpressive. So, I'd recommend this little bee but get the omelet. It looked better.
Best burger I've had in a very long time Â fries are crispy on the outside and softly cooked on the inside.

I've only been here once, yet I call it one of my favorites. The first and only time was around 10pm on a weekday, and their happy hour did not disappoint! What does disappoint is that I've found it kind of difficult to go back - because there are never any day-of reservations available (I'm not much of a planner...) and/or the wait times are too long. I'll keep trying though. The moules frites and the generous pours of malbec were enough to bring this restaurant to the top of my list.

I've been to Woorijip dozens of times for lunch and will continue to go a dozen more times. You have two options when you enter: 1. get lbs and lbs of food at the buffet, from about 20 different choices. 2. go to the back and get something prepackaged. They're constantly bringing out fresh food for the buffet, which is divided between a hot and cold section. Some of my favorites are the vegetable pancakes, kimchi pancakes, kale salad, bulgogi, and kimchi. I avoid the fish here. If you want a relaxing meal, don't go. But if you want to bring food to the park or office, it's a solid choice. Also, the music they play while you wait in line is sometimes hilarious. Listen for it.

Really cool little place with great coffee, atmosphere and tasty decently priced food. So why only 3 stars? Â It's no longer freelancer friendly! No wi-fi, all table service. It makes me miss the old location. Â I wish they could have kept both of them open.

My girlfriend brought me to this place and had been raving about it for several months. Â I had very high expectations heading in, but boy did they deliver. Â The food was incredible and the service was second to none. Â I will definitely be going quite often now and have already recommended it to several of my friends.

Great service and even better food. Menu is simple, but has variety. Sandwiches run $8-11. They have meat and cheese platters with an amazing selection. Â I've eaten there on numerous occasions and have had take-out as well. The atmosphere of the restaurant is appropriate for a date or even a large group. Outdoor seating area is nice on a summer night. It's out in the back of the restaurant. Â My only complaint is that the lighting outside is a bit dark. I had to use my cell phone to see the menu.

I was afraid that we had picked the wrong time to eat here. Friday afternoon lunch was packed. But we had just flown in from Miami with no reservation and hoped for the best. Well, as expected, it was a bit of a wait, but it was well worth our time. The food was absolutely perfect and the energy and vibe were intoxicating...or maybe that was the 4 scotches I had... either way, this plays rocks!

This place has been on my list of things to try for the longest time. Today was the day I get to try it. I had gotten the vampire killer - which is pretty much consists of all things garlic. My friend got the wasabi one. Both were really good. I would just say that the breading of the vampire killer was a bit much but it definitely added good texture to it - nice and crunchy. The good thing about the chicken fingers is that they actually have meat inside unlike most places where they consist mostly of the breading. The only downside is that it's on the pricer side for only 3 pieces. I originally thought that it would be enough, but I was satisfied after. Then surprisingly became extremely full 1 hr later... But overall, good :)

Only giving it 3 stars because I have never been inside the actual location. I ordered take out one night via seamless.com , it took about 45 minutes to arrive which is standard, okay from top to bottom I had the buttermilk fried chicken with mashed potatoes and gravy. It was pure yummines my chicken was fried perfectly crispy on the outside and juicy on the inside, the mashed potatoes were smooth like butter and the gravy delicious, how can I forget the sautÃ©ed broccoli which was your basic veggie sautÃ© nothing special but good none the less. I also had the Mac and cheese which wasn't the best Mac I've ever had but it was good enough for me to def go back for more. Lastly I had the bread pudding YUMMERS !! It came with a warm white chocolate sauce intended to be drizzled over the top, perfect combo, can't wait to way here again I may have to make this a regular thing.
stomach ache after a one hour wait for a table is not my kind of place! food was good but I'm not that experienced in traditional korean cuisine and pricey, too

One of the top three resteraunts in Forte Green. The food is consistantly good, the service is always extremely friendly, and the place is aways packed with local folks. What I love about Olea is it combines the best of Brooklyn with an authentic European ambience but never borders on kitchy. Â The Lentil Salad is a stand out item. I tend to think the appetizers are stronger than the entrees but the food has always been great. The drinks are really delicious and it doesn't hurt that the regular night-time bartender is a stone cold fox. It's a great place for a date or to round up the local brood for a laid back night of good wine, tastey food, great live music, and a comfortable never rushed experience.
The skirt steak, mussels, and shrimp tamales are INSANE.

This is one of those restaurants that prove you don't need a super fancy or big to have an impact on a neighborhood. Yes the corn is good, but its the atmosphere, the music, and hell, the rest of the menu, that make this place what it is. I will say the server we had was kindddaaa a bitch. But she got better towards the end of our meal. I think it's just overwhelming to work in a small space that is constantly packed with people.

We stopped in for a light bite. I SO wanted to get the couscous because I saw plates and plates of it being served, and it looked utterly divine, but I exhibited a modicum of restraint and stuck to the game plan. What's even worse is that we sat at the bar and got to see plates and plates and plates of avocado toast coming out...grrrr, we were planning to get that at Beauty & Essex so that too was off the list. So we ordered the organic roast chicken sandwich to share and I was perfectly happy. The chicken was seasoned and the roasted tomatoes and chipotle mayonnaise were perfect accompaniments. I got anchovies for my half...yum...The baguette comes from Parisi Bakery up the street, FYI. Even the greens were dressed very well! Will definitely have to come back on a future visit. For some friggin' avocado toast and couscous, n'est-ce pas??

If I lived closer to the LES, you bet your ass this would be my favorite spot to grab a bite to eat and enjoy a few drinks. I love the decor, ambience, everything about this place. I love that you walk into a bar/restaurant and beyond the corner is a whole other bar thats even cozier! Not a huge fan of the dead animals hanging all over the place, but the lighting, furniture and music easily make you feel relaxed. If you're going for just drinks make sure to try the French 75, it's a glorified liquored up lemonade, and if you're in the mood for food, they have great cheese plates, and the devils on horseback are a must have! PS- Â I think the bartender in the back looks like Johnny Depp!

First NY pizza I tried. It was great. Coming from LA, I don't think I can ever eat pizza there again. Although it was really good, I would still rather wait longer for Grimaldi's Pizza in Brooklyn. Despite that, this place is still a must go!

Order the fritanga and some maduros. Bogota does a fabulous job labeling the menu's gluten-free and vegan items, and they fry their empanadas in canola oil. Early week visits mean Happy Hour all day. Their coconut margaritas on the rocks are my personal jam, but I've yet to go wrong alcohol-wise. The coded menu will help you out Â once you're past your prime. Order another fritanga, it'll sober you up. The ribs are cooked in red wine, so order those too. The decor is on the kitschy side, but with my mouth so full of delicious meat, I barely noticed.

During a stay in New York in December, I was looking forward to a meal at CafÃ© Sabarsky after several New York friends had recommended it. But unfortunately, the Â breakfast I had there turned out to be a big disappointment and put a damper on the start of our first day of holiday vacation. Food was not prepared properly (for example, the eggs were not cooked as described on the menu) and some things did not come out at all (we were told they were out of some things that were listed on the menu--but told this after our food arrived and we inquired about it). It took about 30 minutes for us to get coffee after we ordered, despite the fact that the cafÃ© was not that crowded; when it did arrive, it was underwhelming, a big surprise for a Viennese cafe. Â  As others mentioned, the service was also problematic. We had a hard time getting help when we needed it and some of the servers didn't communicate very well. That's forgivable, but what's not is the sarcastic attitude of one female server when we inquired about a food item that did not come out of the kitchen. The cafÃ© itself is gorgeous and the Neue Galerie itself is worth a visit. For the menu prices, however, CafÃ© Sabarsky can do better and my experience there does make me inclined to visit Gutenbrunner's other restaurants.

They have some good items, particularly the Mexican falafel sandwich and the Baja Fresh salad. I'm removing one star because I think they are a bit pricey for their falafel sandwiches/salads. Unlike what some reviewers posted, I would not say the salad is big enough for two lunches...and I don't consider myself to have a particularly large appetite. I'm removing two stars because i have specifically gone here to try out their T-Rolls on 5 different occasions only to be told they are not available that day. The first time I was told they were not available yet (even though they spammed my email with advertisements about them). All of the following times I've gotten there and waited in the long line just to be informed that they're not available that day and that I should try the following day.
