I don't think the T-Rolls really exist...so why are they on the menu? I won't be making the effort to come here anymore...
So much food, so cheap, so yummy! It made my entire New York trip. The only not yummy dish was the beef noodle soup. Everything else was amazing!

Had a random craving for a Crepe last Saturday night and googled some places in Astoria. Cafe Triskell popped up with the best reviews. Walked all the way and it was so worth it. Who knew a little hole in the wall would have the best crepe ever?!Thin, airy and flaky all at the same time. I had the butter & sugar with Nutella. I will definitely return for more.

It is a bit pricey for drinks but worth it. Â  The place is clean and well run. Â The appetizers are not your typical bar food, I enjoyed everything I sampled. Â Who knew tater tots could be fancy, lol. Â  The drinks are excellent, they don't skimp on the alcohol or taste. Â  The clientele is a mix of the after work business crowd and nearby law students. I keep going back!

UPDATE: Orlin is featured prominently in the new NBC show, Smash! Love the show and the cafe! Orlin is one of the best little cafes NY has to offer! It's open 24/7 which makes it both a great breakfast spot for pancakes, eggs, etc and a perfect late night place where you can fill up on whatever greasy pleasure will help you soak up all that alcohol! The service is nice..very laid back and they'll oftentimes invite you to select your own table (as long as it isn't busy). The food is great...I haven't found a dish there that I'm not fond of. Location is fun, safe and trendy..awesome neighborhood to walk around and explore..(maybe burn off a few of those calories you just consumed). A great spot all in all!

I recently moved to Woodside. After arriving here and walking by Peking BBQ, two things came to mind. A. This place looks like a piece of shit. B. There are always people waiting inside. Normally that can only mean one thing.... it's awesome. I've now been in Woodside for about 6 months and I've eaten at PBBQ about 8 times. It's a prefect meal and super cheap. The chicken is succulent and they serve up some of the best fried rice out there. Can't beat this place.... go ahead and order a #1... you're welcome.
Cafe Cluny is reliably good and has the feeling of a restaurant that's been around for a long time. It's cozy, the drinks are good (try the vodka and ginger one) and I've never had a bad entree here.

My wife ordered poached eggs and when the plate came it had 1 hard boiled egg. The waitress said the menu had a typo and it's only 1 poached egg. We asked for them to make it softer and more runny - they obliged. When the 2nd attempt arrived it was exactly the same and the meal was swimming in dressing. The couple next to us was complaining that they had been there for an hour and only one of them had their food. More flys than a poop factory too. Overall not a very good experience.

Da Marcella is an unpretentious, cozy Italian restaurant on Houston. The service was warm and friendly, like walking into a family-owned restaurant (which I suspect is what it is.) Â This is one of those places where even if you are entering for the first time, you get greeted like you are their most loyal customer. The meals were good and hearty, and for less than $12, it really was quite the deal. I liked the Spaghetto Cacio e Pepe, but I think I will try something different the next time--it didn't quite have the zesty taste of other Cacio e Pepe dishes I have had. It wasn't bad, however, and it was very fresh. My wife's Tagliatelle alla Bolognese was better--she was very happy with her meal. While I think I'll order differently the next time, I certainly was not disappointed. The place is warm, friendly and unassuming, with good food at a great price.
Great place and lovely staff highly recommended

Very BAD restaurant - not even worth to review it. I'm doing this so that other people will know not to try this restaurant. Inside the restaurant very hot, food no good. What a waste of my money. Will not come back and please don't even get curious on this restaurant .

Yum! Was just a few streets over when we got hungry while visiting from out of town... opened up yelp and saw these reviews... THANK YOU fellow reviewers. We fed two of us (with sodas) for $7.75. I can't do that out in the suburbs, so remain wildly impressed that we were able to do that for a dinner in NYC!! Oh, and we both really enjoyed our dumplings and sesame pancakes, so we werent sacrificing flavor for the sake of our budget!

Oh God! Best drinks I have had in my lifeeeee!! Bartenders arethe best I've seen in a long time, and the food is pretty good too, so what else to say? The steak is amazing and the potatos as well. Didn't really like the oysters, but everything else i have tried it pretty down to the point. Again I got to say, hats down to the bartenders! it is not too big, which I like, but it gets pretty crowded so be sure to save yourself a seat on time!!

I loved everything about this place. Outdoor sitting with heaters! The best to enjoy a chilly Sunday outside. The food was amazing, the grilled polenta with poached egg, fennel, cheese and prosciutto is outstanding and the Bloody Mary is as good as it gets. Last but not least, the staff was awesome, very nice and efficient I really recommend this place and can't wait to be back.

Delicious! These rolls are such a good idea and they taste great! If I were to give a small critique my husband thought they were a little dry so maybe a delicious sauce in the rolls would top it off!!

Wow! Amazing place. The meal was ridiculously good and our waiter made excellent recommendations for both food and wine. We had the tasting menu which was perfect for both my husband and I. Every single thing we had was wonderful and unique. I'm still dreaming about the dessert - popcorn ice cream with blueberries and carmel popcorn- it may have been the best dessert I have ever had. So good. I can't imagine leaving this place even mildly unsatisfied. The only disappointing thing was the muffin they gave me for the next day. It was a nice thought, but the muffin was a bit dry. ;(

Three of us came here on a Friday night around 8pm. Â Expecting the dreaded usual wait at this time, we were delighted when a table was available for us. Â Thank God for snow storms! Customer service was great from the start. Â Highly attentive and thoughtful, our server patiently answered our questions and recommended the portion we were ordering. Â We shared the tofu salad and three set dishes for strategic eating which allows each of us to get a bowl of rice (option of brown, white or mixed), miso soup and the egg custard. Â  -Tofu salad is like a cold souffle next to yummy bonita flakes on a bed of lettuce. Â Highly recommend this delicious dish. Â  -Our sets (if I still remember) was the washu beef, silky pork belly and a kimchee hot pot dish. Â The presentation was beautiful and the food tasty. Â Having the hot pot made really balanced our meal. Â I believe we liked the hot pot the most but I would come back to try the other dishes. Â We didn't expect the egg custard to be savory, but nonetheless, it was silky and warm, ending our meal nicely. Â The sake helped us to stay warm, too. Â  If you desire a more private, quiet, roomy space and the ability to carry conversations without raising your voice, dine on the second floor.

We went for NYE, so of course it was crazy busy. However, our server was so great and the food was prettyyyyy tasty. The whole roasted branzino was cooked just right and the brussel sprouts, nice and crispy! Got a huge dessert platter with amazing goodies, like a key lime meringue and hazelnut brÃ»lÃ©e. And, of course champagne at midnight! Would definitely consider going back for a non-NYE meal.

Caracas Arepa Bar is a nice place to go for a quick meal. The interior is dimly lit. The patio in the back is a nice touch, with little decorations. Some of the seats are made of plastic crates. They were almost comfortable. The guasacaca and chips was good, though it looked like the guacamole had been sitting for some time before since a bit of it was oxidation. The chips are not as good as the ones from Empanada Mama. I had the Surena arepa. It comes with chicken, chorizo, avocado and some sauce. The corn cake was delicious, crispy on the outside. One arepa in almost enough for me, but I'm a big guy so most people should be satisfied. The bathroom was decorated with old newspapers, which I found amusing... unfortunately, there was some graffiti on there.

Yes pizza was okay and yes its the oldest pizza place but this doesn't mean you should make people wait in front of a bathroom for 15 minutes. There was a line in front of the bathroom. They also don't give high chairs to families with a baby and when you ask them why they say that "this place is so busy usually and because of this we dont have high chairs". You dont have to be arrogant just because you are the oldest pizza place in town. What makes a place worth going is their service and respect and attitude to its guests. Also, I ate better pizzas.

3.5 stars for fluffy meatballs. The price kinda makes me wince though - it's about two dollars for 1 meatball. Which is sorta painful when you realize that eating one order of four meatballs is not going to fill you up. It's pretty good with the sauce though.

We stayed here and was a pretty decent hotel, perfect location and comfortable beds . However the restaurant is very over priced for the quality of food ! You are better off going else where and they seem to take pretty long to bring out the food . We tried a dinner app , the calamari , it was good but not 16$ worth I know we are in NY but still! For lunch I ordered the Cobb, it was def not worth it the avocado was brown the chicken was dry and the cilantro vin was the wrong dressing for a Cobb! The staff was very nice but forgetful. I do have to say a great cocktail list go for a drink not the food!

Just delicious! tried it 3 times. Review is based on brunch/lunch time (so not the crazy dinner time rush) and always with pasta as the entree. Â  Appetizer: the Polpettine were good but not awesome; the Ricotta de Pecora was just so creamy and delicious, Â I could probably eat only that for 3 meals a day Entree: The pastas just taste so good. So far I've loved the Tortellini, the Cappelletti and the Stracci. I'll be back to try the rest. If you have a sweet tooth you must leave space for dessert. Â It's creative and yummy and I love that they've spent the time thinking about it (unlike many other places) Dessert: Â Strawberry something or other was amazing, love the panna cotta and their take on tiramisu Give it a shot - you can't not like it!

For cheap dumplings, a good place to stop. As a broke ass student, it's nice and filling. And the quality isn't bad either though you could find better elsewhere, but for the fact of $1/4 dumplings doesn't give much room to complain about. I'm a fan of their dumplings, fried or boiled. Other stuff on the menu doesn't really appeal to me, but to each their own.

Did I NOT really review this wonderful place after using my Yelp! coupon to eat here? I must (may) be suffering from early-onset Alzheimer's. In a way, you need to see this in context. I'm a Seattle boy, and seafood to me means slingin' salmon at the Pike Place Market and 'Hangtown Fry' breakfasts at the Athena Cafe. Wild Edibles, with its fishmonger locale and limited seating (without, alas, a view of Elliot Bay) and its laidback (but attentive and knowledgeable) staff harks back to yesteryear. Oh, and they have those good NW oysters like Hama Hamas, Hood Canals, Skookums and the wonderfully fleshy & rich Japanese import Kumamoto. And, of course, they also have the Eastern oysters that maybe are better known and loved by Yelpers! Whatever they offer is FRESH! Briny & delicious. And just to comment on a previous post: I've never seen any reason to tip more than 10% despite the persistent move to higher numbers (where will it end?) and in view of both the inflation of restaurant Â prices and the upward movement of the minimum wage. I earn minimum wage, and no one tips ME for doing my job! In any case, I don't feel I "made a mistake" by tipping 10% nor did I get any grief from staff for doing so. We paid in cash and were cordially waved goodbye and invited to return.
Went here for a friends Birthday the cocktails are amazing and all $11 or less! Â Love the selection of draft beer. Â Great time here with friends. Â :)

For the lady and I, this is our usual default spot when we just want a quick, light, usually healthy meal. For non pork eaters we find that there is a lot to choose from and be very happy about. Sit out back when it gets warm. Service is always friendly and prompt. Here is what we recommend - Soups are always on soul warming: Rustic creamy tomato soup Cream of onion soup Potato and roasted mushroom soup Salads are perfect to start out with: Panzanella Chickpea & Feta salad Baby String Beans Potato salad Crustini before the Panini: Tomato fresca, rosemary ricotta, black olive oil Goat cheese, honey, rosemary oil Spicy avocado and goat cheese - Israeli favorite Paninis after the saladini: Roast Chicken mozzarella, arugula and spicy mayo Fried Eggplantroast mushrooms, goat cheese, spicy mayo Drinks: Sixpoint Sweet Action, Cream Ale Iced coffee Awesome wine specials -get the Riesling when they have it 4 stars because they need to get a proper espresso machine for after dinner doubles. If you have room: Red velvet cupcakes

this was a pretty sweet dinner spot. Â i snuck in with a friend a little after 630, before the place was packed. Â we both ordered from the recommended lists on the chalkboard overhead. Â i had the chili dofu, he some kind of beef dumpling (i forget the name). Â i thought mine was out of this world. Â the tofu had this really rich, thick texture and the chili sauce was spicy, but nothing you couldn't handle. Â very well balanced. Â  and for $7, who's to complain? Â the portion was big enough that i couldn't finish it. Â it's hard to find deals like that in the city. Â  my only beef with this place was that it was understaffed. Â so it took quite a while for our plates to be cleared, check to be brought etc.
Come here during the restaurant week. Speical menu. Really cozy place.
If you do nothing else, stop in this wonderful little place on 37th and have their hand cut sweet potatoes. They are amazing! Â Above the call of duty service. Staff takes pride in their restaurant.

Red Cat offers one of those dining experiences that keeps you pining for more. Â My date (who had the "most amazing salmon of his life, ever" there) and I cannot stop talking about this restaurant. Â We both had an entree and spilt a bottle of red wine, and walked out of there paying alot less then we thought we were going to. Â The staff is the most welcoming I have experienced in NY. Â Highly recommended, and if you decide to go and want to invite me, I would be down.

I guess if you order the drinks on their menu, they are great. Â But if you go in there and ask for a cocktail that is different- even a classic one like a French 75- they are incapable. Â It was watered down champagne. Nothing artisan about that.

The hype is real! It is a bit pricey. I bought a box of 8 for 22 dollars. But, it is worth every penny. The macaroons are light, fluffy, and sweet! It definitely won me over. There are a lot of options to choose from, my favorite macaroons are lemon, strawberry, vanilla, and coffee. There is long wait. It is a trendy spot, the employees are a little grouchy. I did love their uniforms. I did enjoy the macaroons and I recommend them to anyone. Food/Photo Blog: lovethephotographer.tumbâ€¦

The most amazing drinks...margaritas really. The tamarindo was my all time favorite and we had a lot of drinks that night. Â If I had to choose the last drink I could consume before I died it would be Barrio Chino's tamarindo margarita!! Get ready for the spice!!! The food was decent. Â Totally worth the wait and tight space. Â Beautiful experience.

I've now come to Ai Fiori for dinner and lunch, and it's official: Â I have a favorite NYC restaurant. Â Service and atmosphere are fantastic, the prix fixe menus are quite a value for the money (and I say that when lunch for 4 with 2 basic bottles of wine ended up over $500), and the food.. well, they do things with truffles and lobster that continually amaze me. Ai Fiori is the real deal, from bread through dessert. Â I need more special occasions in my life.

Small, cozy, quaint place to which the food and people make up HEAVILY for it. The ascending and descending to the top dinning floor is quite a feat to trek up being that they are narrow. It gives more kudos for the staff on how they roam up and down them fluidly and with dishes. You can choose to sit at the street level which is counter top/ring side seats to the amazing cooking action. The portions look deceiving. For a guy it's fine, but I was so full mid way, i thought I was going to roll down the stairs. Ox tail is the type of comfy dish you get that goes well w/rice. Most dishes come w/rice, salad and plantains. The jerk chicken had a little kick in it, but i really craved to add sauce to it. Thank goodness i got mostly dark meat. Can't imagine how to eat that white meat dry. Flavors are good all in all.

Had a really nice brunch here this morning. Decor is modern, but not stuffy. Staff was pleasant. We had a reservation, but certainly didn't need it as the place had only a smattering of people there for brunch. We stuck to the breakfast-type brunch items as we were not in high-roller moods. (The menu includes a wide variety of appetizers, and more substantial lunch items in addition, but the prices for these items are quite a bit higher.) We were started off with an amuse bouche of roasted peppers which were tasty but not amazing. I ordered the gravlax with poached eggs and toasted brioche. I've never had gravlax before, but it didn't disappoint. I was pleased with the portion size- about 5 nice long slices- especially for the reasonable price, and it went really well with the poached eggs and brioche. My friend ordered the spinach and goat cheese omelette, which she got with egg whites only, and said it was very tasty. Her side of pork and jalepeno sausage was just so-so. With fresh-squeezed juice for me and coffee for my friend, the bill came to a little under $50 (not including tip). Reasonable for such a nice dining experience. I would certainly recommend Perry St to those seeking a quiet, tasty, weekend brunch in an elegant setting at a reasonable price.

Apart from the awesome and friendly staff the fries are the best. Their dipping sauces are all amazing and they have more than a handful to pick from. But if you don't know what to pick don't FEAR you can try as many as you want ;) but I do have my favorites... Vietnamese Pineapple Mayo and Peppercorn Parmesan are must haves :)

Gave it a shot, & it definitely lives up to its mark! It's about $2 more expensive in Seattle, (but hey, according to the NFT book, & their numerous awards hanging on the wall, it seems like a good shot to try). The downside is they take cash-only, but their sandwiches won me over. The bbq pork was my favorite, and pair it up with a bubble tea (Quickly on Grand St.) you have a perfect lunch/snack combo. Can't decide if it was the best I've ever had, but it definitely ranks at the top. It would be nice if the sandwich was a little worm/toasted a bit to give it that extra crunchy taste. That would have been perfect. I also like how they have a few places for you to sit as the wall tables. Although crumbs are EVERYWHERE. They should think about sweeping the floor more frequently. Another interesting observation....they have a mini jewelry department IN the store...that showcases jades, gold, etc. I found that a bit weird, but oh well. I'm here for the sandwiches, & got what I was craving for!

JACKET REQUIRED. This place is NOT cheap! Bill for two people came out to be near $300. BUT, I still give it 5 stars, not cuz I'm bougie like all my friends proclaim, but because they really hook you up. I made reservations (you should DEF make reservations). We went on a Thursday night and the place was packed. Â  We started with a complimentary pumpkin soup. It was so good... I ordered the Organic Colorado Rack of Lamb soubise of cippolini, zucchini mini puree black truffle sauce. Portions might be small for a guy, but it was more than enough for me. My friend got the Organic Long Island Duck Roasted with white truffle honey puree of organic dates and white turnip and the Organic Connect Cut Farm Egg organic date puree, red onion confit, pinot noir. He enjoyed both :) We ordered a peach dessert and a chocolate souffle (I wish they had a menu online so I can write the proper names :/). OMG. And the free stuff just kept rolling in: - red wine ice cream, - complimentary something creme brulee - complimentary 3-tiers of cookies. I wish they told us of all the free food they were going to stuff us with. But then again, we probably wouldn't have gotten anything if we didn't order dessert. After our fatty meals, a man gave me a goodie bag. Inside was a complimentary loaf of bread (it was sweet and light). It was definitely romantic, prim and proper, and abundant. I'd love to come here again :)
This is the most authentic Neopolitan pizza available in New York. You will consistently find Italians eating here, speaking Italian, watching Italian soccer, and drinking Italian beer. Â Legit.
Really good food. Nice enviroment. Price is good!

It was okay, the food was a bit fussy rather then tasty. Â Overall there were too many competing flavors. Â  They were out of quite a few menu choices that we were interested in trying, and we were there by 7 PM. Â The waiter helped us with the wine selection, which was excellent and reasonably priced. Â The noise level went from loud to moderate.

Incredible. Greek food is underrated and Kefi is a gem in the Upper West Side. This place simply blows Taverna straight out of the Mediterranean waters. The friendly, attentive staff made sure we were always taken care of and there seems to be plenty of space (multiple floors). Never order chicken at a Greek restaurant...that said, I personally don't eat lamb but can attest to the excellent seafood quality. The grilled octopus was tender and fresh...almost tasted like some type of forbidden land protein. The pita appetizer is a home run too. Multiple difference sauces, all incredibly flavorful. Free refill on the basket just in case too. Highly recommended.

Love it! I think next time I'll just keep ordering repeat orders of the "Red, White, and Blue" and just get drunk off of chardonnay and oysters. The Chardonnay involved with this deal is pretty much box wine, so don't get your hopes up too high, but six oysters and a glass of wine for 8 dollars is about as good a deal as you can get in this neighborhood. The Oysters were blue points, and were big and fresh. Better then I expected considering the price. As a lover of the beach, and a Massachusetts native I also have to give this place a lot of credit for the laid back "salty" vibe. For example, you can choose PBR to go with your oysters as well, and jeans and a tee shirt are pretty much acceptable attire. I also ordered Mussels for my main meal and they tasted quite fresh and came in an awesome sauce. Not as amazing for me as the oysters, but still very good. I got a glass of Pinot Grigo with my meal that cost me $8 in and of itself, but it was SO much better then the Chardonnay that I didn't mind too much. Fish is a bit loud and crowded for a first date, but is definitely a nice place to go with the significant other. I plan to make mine come back here with me many many times.

The vermicelli dish was on point. That grill pork with shrimp and spring roll over spaghetti was really good can't complain. My boyfriend had the soup he didn't enjoy as much as he enjoyed my dish but nice Â overall definitely go back.

Looking to satisfy your Burger/Taco needs? This is the place to go. The place is a hidden gem in the Les area. Must try the fish taco, the Fries and the Mint lemonade. The staff is friendly and the prices are defiantly affordable. You can actually customize how you want your burgers. OMG i forgot to mention the Bacon wrapped dog... Droolll. They also have a large selection of Hot Sauces from all over the world which is a plus in my book since i love my food with a kick. Hands down this is one of the best burger taco joints i've been to.

Don't come here for authentic Argentinean cuisine. If you're okay with that, then go with some friends - not with a date - and enjoy. Otherwise, another restaurant with pretenses that falls short due to turning blue collar food into white collar, and lack of customer service. Having been to Argentina before, I notice that all restaurants I've tried in NYC miss the mark by a lot. It ain't hard, people!

The good: Â Margaritas were excellent. The bad: Â Linty napkins -- don't wear black pants or a shirt. Â Slow service -- delay between dishes was 15-20 minutes. Â Food was underwhelming. Cuban corn - really acidic compared to other cuban corn I've had. Also not enough cheese. Mac and Cheese -- they added bacon and pork rinds to mac and cheese and IT DIDN'T MAKE IT TASTE ANY BETTER. That is a travesty to pork products. The best mac and cheese is made from just macaroni and cheese at Beecher's -- when will people learn the secret is just USE HIGH QUALITY CHEESE and SEASONING. Frita Cubana - this burger was raved about in Time Out NY and I have to say it's a solid "Meh." Â I ordered the chef's recommendation of medium for the burger and I should have stuck to my normal rare/medium-rare. Â The burger meat was not seasoned and there is no excuse for that. Â No amount of cheese or whatever can make up for that. Chicken arepas - the chicken (spicy, well seasoned) and guacamole were excellent. The arepa shell was tasty and crunchy WHEN HOT. Â Unfortunately, the bottom halves of each arepa was ice cold. Overall a solid "Meh"... after I had to dust off the lint from my pants. Â Honestly, we're not in Cuba and there is no excuse for cheap, linty napkins.

Oh my dear Pies N Thighs. What can I say here to express my deep and abiding love for you? Seriously, about a month or two ago my boyfriend and I came here for Sunday brunch for five weeks straight. Perfect, excellent hangover brunch. One of the happiest joys of living in Greenpoint is biking it over to Pies N Thighs brunch after waking up at 2pm on a beautiful sunny Sunday. Brunch is my favorite time here. Strawberry-blueberry pancakes with cinnamon maple butter and a breast and a thigh. Simply does not get much better than that. CHICKEN BISCUIT is the shit. You need to order it. For all you reviewers out there who give this place negative reviews and didn't order the CHICKEN, you just made the wrong choice. Ordering anything other than chicken at one of the best fried chicken places in the city is like ordering fish at a steakhouse. You have to know what you're getting yourself into. Must-haves: -Fried chicken -Chicken biscuit -Lemon Poppyseed Donut

This place is tiny! Â I came on a weeknight with a small group, and we all really enjoyed ourselves. Â The menu isn't too big, and depending on your table size you may end up ordering the entire menu. Â All the bottles of wine were $25, which was great, and we ordered a Malbec. Â We really enjoyed all of the food - it was definitely unique and all very tasty. Â There portions weren't very big, but we all got to try lots of different things which was nice. Â Each dish came out with a full description on which ingredients were used and for what purpose. Â I would only recommend coming here with people you're pretty close with, as the place is very small and you can end up crammed in a corner on a wobbly stool. Â I'm still a bit confused on why the call themselves and Indian/Asian restaurant, but it was a great experience regardless!

went around noon, there was hardly any wait. Â they've lunch sets that comes with choice of ramen, side of salad, choice of side+rice. I love the broth! extremely flavorful and delicious. Â the pork slices weren't as tender as i hoped it to be. OH, and the pork buns are yummilicious!!! service was so friendly and prompt. Â I need ippudo in florida! :)

The service was friendly. Â My appetizer was the guacamole and it was fresh with a big portion. Â I had the Parpardella which was awesome. Â  You could tell the pasta was freshly made and the short rib was braised properly. Â I would have liked a little more short rib in it but the flavor was spot on. Â Thank you for a very enjoyable diner. Â I definitely will return.

Got there at exactly noon. Waited about 5 minutes for a table for two. Â We shared the pork buns which were killer. Â I had the classic Ramen and my husband had the spicy. Â Both delicious but I'd get the spicy next time. Â The broth was so flavorful and clean, not greasy at all. Â Noodles were perfect. For $2 extra, my husband got an extra serving of noodles halfway through his soup which he absolutely loved. Â There's no egg in the ramen, which I've never known to happen before, but it wasn't listed in the ingredients so that was my mistake. Next time I'll pay the extra for the egg. To me, it makes a huge difference. Only reason I didn't give this a five star review is that you can't take out leftovers! I only ate about a quarter of my soup and the rest had to be thrown away. Â What a waste!

My family comes here regularly because we cannot last that long without coming back. Don Peppe has become a staple in our diets now. It's an old school Italian American family style restaurant. Do not come here if you're on a romantic date or on the Atkins diet. Also, I think it's safe to say that this place is not too vegetarian friendly, and if you're scared of excess fat, then hate to break it to you, but everything here is dripping with olive oil (and sometimes butter). The wait staff is extremely helpful on menu recommendations and to help decide the portions (everything is made to share). -side note, the menu is a giant board on the back wall that lists everything they have. They're a super friendly bunch that recognizes their customers and treats them well. Things you have to order: - Baked clams- what they're famous for, they're small clams topped with a buttery crumble that you need at least a half dozen of for yourself. - Linguini in white clam sauce- best linguini in white clam sauce I've ever had in America. It's so simple that it's unfair. Ingredients: linguini, clam, white wine, full cloves of garlic, and parsley overflowing in olive oil. Prepare to ask for seconds. Â  - Veal Don Pepe- breaded veal cutlets topped with fresh seasoned raw tomatoes and red onion. It's a great combination of ingredients that gives this dish a great bite. - House red wine- I say house because I have no idea where it's from. If you order for two, they serve it in a 12oz glass bottle. If you order a bottle for the table, they serve it in a fifth glass bottle. Wherever it's from, it's fruity, cheap, and pairs well with the food. Things that are also worth ordering: - Fish in lemon sauce - Grilled Portobello - Roasted red peppers - Cannolis If you're preparing for a marathon, this is the place to go the night before. It's hands down my favorite place to carbo load. GET THE LINGUINI IN WHITE CLAM SAUCE.

What is going on with their seating arrangement?! I was placed in the back room against the left wall between a table of 5 and a table of 8. In the middle and far right were two parties of 10. I understand it's Manhattan and every store owner is greedy to maximize profits but did they really think that placing a couple in a "party room" was the best seating arrangement for their 'valued' customers? They are very lucky this was not a first date but I felt bad for others who might pick this restaurant looking for that 'intimate factor' and instead receive a rowdy neglected table.

A few notes: - waiter hot, attentive and super-cute accent - Caribbean/mexican style food - playing classic Bob Marley tunes - if summer, much cooler to sit up front than in back room - anything with the mole verde sauce is better than sin itself

This place is fabulous. Just got back from Thailand a few weeks ago, and Pure is as close to the original as I can get. The restaurant is pretty small and no frills - you'll probably have a bit of a wait and the wait staff wants you in and out. A friend and I headed over around 7PM on a Tuesday, put our names down for a 20 minute wait. There are a bunch of bars in the area, so I recommend getting a drink at The Snug, Vintage, etc. We got a call with about a 5-10 min heads up. The food was delicious. If you're expecting typical American Thai food, this place may not be for you. They are not afraid of making food authentically spicy. We had the green papaya salad and crispy tofu to start. The green papaya salad is great - the perfect balance of sweet, salty, sour, and crunchy. For dinner, we split the wok-charred with calamari dish and the Krabi seafood noodles soup. The calamari dish is tasty and very good. I would get it again, but I wasn't blown away. The texture of the calamari was perfect though - perfectly cooked and tender. The Krabi seafood noodles were out of this world. There's a note on it that says it is not recommended for novices, but it was hands down my favorite dish with incredible flavors. It comes with flat rice noodles, but I think I would opt for different noodles next time - maybe handmade egg or thin rice noodles. The tomato pork broth is delicious, and I couldn't get enough of it.
Family meal is set on gooood. Great portions too!

Stumbled upon this place one day with a group of friends and we had a great time. The ambiance is great both outside and downstairs. A wonderful date night with a fireplace in the back. The food is great, I particularly like the wine selection and the bruschetta.

The Good - The food, the atmosphere, and definitely the sangria. The Bad - My sloppy memory of the experience, so will have to go back for a second visit! Determined as I was to try some authentic south american cuisine, and having resourced Pio Pio as a suitable venue, my friend and I slightly blurred the experience by having a few drinks before we arrived which resulted in my memory of the evening being a little wishy washy! I do however have a happy and hazy memory of us gushing on about how firm the calamari was, how tender and succulent the roast chicken was, and definitely how much we were enjoying the very authentic and rather large pitcher of sangria. Being new to the U.S., and from England originally, it reminded me of Spanish cuisine but with a wicked twist! What else can I remember? The dining area itself was dark, boisterous and a little hectic, with various large dinner parties going on, which for this type of restaurant was perfect, and all added to the atmosphere of what I imagined a Peruvian street restaurant to be like! They say that alcohol magnifies your emotions, and if there is any truth in that, then Pio Pio was indeed fantastic, and well worth a visit! In the name of being fair to other restaurants I am writing reviews about however, will definitely being going back for a second visit minus the tipsy topsy drinks so I can double check that the food and overall experience was indeed as good as I remember!

I've been here for brunch a couple of times and it's definitely one of my favourite spots. The pastry board the first time I went was one of the best things I've ever had for breakfast so that always sets things up nicely. I was very happy with my duck hash with poachies, but was looking longingly at my girlfriend's salmon... with which she kindly did a quick swap. I went again on Friday which prompted the review. It wasn't quite as good but this could be because it was on a weekday. My all day breakfast with grits was cleaned up pretty swiftly with a good americano, and the only problem was with all the courses we ordered there wasn't enough room on the table! The service was also very good and much appreciated. Pretty sure that this will be my staple brunch recommendation for anyone visiting the city, so if you get an influx of Brits, apologies.

We must have gone on an off night because I'm being generous giving three stars. We were really excited to get a table on a Friday night without a wait. Pretty large rush of people later in the evening. Ordered the avocado tofu, which tasted more like avocado than tofu. Had to douse it in soy sauce to keep myself from wishing for a taco or chips to eat it with. Not the best start... Deep fried tofu was like a miniature sukiyaki, and the skin of the tofu slips off into a weird gooey fried texture. Fried chicken and eggplant -- eggplant was bitter and not fried as the menu implies. Mackerel was strangely gamey, and the pork belly everyone raves about was tough and served lukewarm. The best dish we had was the yakisoba, which is served inside a delicate omelet with Japanese mayo and ketchup. Also not a fan that we have to order drinks. On the plus side, service was pretty fast.

Minetta Tavern is really good, but not great. We started our meal with the bone marrow and mussels. The bone marrow was fantastic, and perfectly done. The mussels were OKAY, but nothing special. For entrees, we had the lamb saddle and black label burger. The burger was really very good, but it's a little unjustified at $28 given that I've had burgers of equal quality for much less money. The lamb saddle was also just OKAY. It was a rather fatty and difficult to eat cut, given it did had decent flavor. For desert we had the caramel chocolate tart and pots de creme. Both were very good, but not extraordinary or at all surprising - basically they tasted as I would expect. All together it was a good meal, but the restaurant doesn't live up to expectations and honestly makes me question the validity of Michelin star ratings. I've had better meals in my life at restaurants not nearly as lauded as this one. I will give the restaurant credit for having a great classic atmosphere and solid service.

I love ramen - but as a vegetarian, I so rarely get to eat it. Fortunately, a friend knew of the off menu vegetarian option. Delicious. And the option to simply get more ramen to fill up your bowl? That's the best.
that s great!!! a pork chop... no... an amazing pork "shop" a fish... a whole grilled fish! so what! just try it but you know the neighborhood... It could hurt your wallet

The grandma style meatballs were really great, and lamb sausage was not bad either..Grilled Â Octopus could be little better... it would be more better if it was grilled Â more and more tender. Great full bar :-)
best ramen ever I couldnt eat enough of it the service is just ok it took forever for us to grab 2 seats we waited like everyone else the buns were amazing you must try this place if in NYC
Pretty good! Lamb and chicken combo! It was good, but a little too much for me. I enjoyed the other halal carts better and went with a plain gyro.

This place is an amusement park for foodies!!! Everything from the food to the kitchen products sold here, is of the best quality.This is the go-to place when in NYC. Mario Batali and his team did an exceptional job putting this genius idea together.

This place was so good, I got the meat sweats after gorging myself for the full 2 hours - fish balls, beef, pork, chicken, fish, squid - you name it, the place will serve it to you plate after plate. After tax and tip it cost about $28 per person for a party of 6. The only complaint was that it was a bit warm since so many hot pots were being heated at once.

My favorite patisserie in the world. Not joking. I was fourth in line when it opened today, so I'm going to unofficially say that I'm the first to review it, as Caeser wrote his review prior to going in. There, 'nuff said. Beautiful shop. Lovely packaging of course, for their world famous macarons. Today's flavors in my box included: Strawberry Mint, Vanille, Caramel avec Beurre de Sel (that's Salted Caramel for you beasts out there LOL), Cassis et Violette, Coconut, Green Apple, Orange Blossom, and I forgot what the last one was. They didn't have the old-time favorites like Anise and Red Fruits. Of course they tasted scrumpdiddlyumptious. The only thing that I see different from the Parisian ones was that these seemed a little bit more dough-y, not like the ones on Rue Royale that have a flakier meringue to them. It varies from their salons and acts more like their Charles de Gaulle outposts that this one has no salon nor baked goods. Just macarons, ice cream, candles, chocolates, tea, and other souvenirs. Rumor has it is that a tea room is to open in Soho in the near future, but don't quote me on that. One last tip, a special New York flavor and coffrette are being introduced for Fashion Night Out.

The brunch Vanilla Bean French Toast was hands down the best French toast I've ever had -- tender and moist and thick with just the right amount of sweetness. And it's so filling! I could only finish half. And it comes with a complimentary cocktail! I recommend the strawberry Champagne. Very fruity.

One of the things I love about the city is places like this. Great food and cocktails, good vibest, busy places bustling with people and great conversation. I always have a great time when I come here :) The ONLY thing is, the place is very narrow, and when it gets super crowded you may have a sloppy drunk spill someting on you... so just beware.
Best pancakes ever. Just outstanding. Nice outdoor seating in the sun, waiters were nice and food came out with little wait time. This was at 2pm and the place was pretty full. Signs of a good eatery
Excellent food! Just had a delightful dinner at Cafe Linda. Service was perfect. Walking distance from hotel.

Excellent Italian food, great atmosphere. Â  The spinach gnocchi and spaghetti were both very good, as was the house chianti. Â The tiramisu was also nice, but I could barely stomach it after the other dishes. Â This is a bit of a hidden gem in the West Village. Â Would definitely recommend it. Don't forget to bring cash, though.
Heard a bunch of hype for this place. but tried it and this place is bomb. its pricey. a bowl of ramen for 15 bucks. def worth every penny..

Highly recommended by a friend of David S.'s, I walked into CookShop with high expectations. Â And, like many impulse choices, there were both hits and misses during my dining experience earlier this evening at CookShop. Â First, the preliminary information: service was VERY good (but that's only because the waitress handled all of my questions really well and didn't look like she wanted to grab the steak knife and stab me). Â The place itself is huge compared to many other NY restaurants and I would totally come back here again (maybe tomorrow for a simple Christmas eve dinner!). Â Think Bravo's TopChef if it was a restaurant. Â Clean, simple, and elegant. Â Just like the food. Second, the food. Â For starters, I had the special: Long Island Razor Clams with a lemon-butter and herb sauce. Â Really good. Â Fresh. Â Simple. Â And I love the smell of lemons. Â My partner-in-crime Sonny D. sampled the Grilled Montauk squid with black olive and fava beans. Â Not a complaint from him either. Â This meal was starting to look good. Entrees: Suckling pig "a la porchetta" with a fennel salad and quince mostarda (mine!), and a grass-fed New York hanger steak with all the fixin's (Sonny's!). Â Who can say no to a slice of different portions of a suckling pig rolled up in pig fat and deep fried? Â And then served on a bed of shredded fennel and topped with a quince dressing? Â Yeah, I didn't think you could either. And who can forget dessert. Â I sampled the warm caramel bread pudding with spiced ice cream (I didn't care for the ice cream. Â I did care for the bread pudding though) and Sonny got the sorbet sampler (3 scoops: black fig, tangerine, and pear cider). Â  Overall, this was a pretty darn good dinner. Â And the best part, it was all locally-grown produce which supports New York State and the metropolitan area, as well as being environmentally conscience. Â And, there were unique dishes (aka. not boring!) Â Cookshop has officially been inserted into of my favorites.

FINALLY! after months of long lines. My roommate was able to pick up an artichoke slice for me and i am forever grateful. I must say, the artichoke slice was phenomenal. You know that great creamed spinach you get at really good nyc steakhouses? Its basically that slathered over a thick crust (minus half point since i'm a thin crust dude) with really tasty cheese and artichokes on it. Big plus on how enormous this slice is. Had to deduct another half point on the wait (fortunately i didn't have to) which is how I was able to get to 4 stars. Also i believe there were only two choices yesterday - plain and artichoke. Get the artichoke!
My least favorite of the Momofuku's. Â Food is OK, but nothing amazing.

This place is a fav in the neighborhood. Â Their chicken liver spread is a most beloved starter. Â  And, now I hate to advertize this, but when I was in there for happy hour today they had dollar oysters. Â I don't know if that's a regular thing, but if so I will certainly be more regular at their happy hour. I've been several times and every time they hit the mark with food and friendliness of staff.
Solid BBQ. Â Not my favorite, but you cannot go wrong.

IF YOU ARE A SELF RESPECTING WOMAN WHO IS LOOKING TO EAT SOME DELICIOUS FOOD OR RESERVE A TABLE FOR A BIRTHDAY PARTY LOOK ELSEWHERE PLEASE!!!!!! I made a reservation for a birthday dinner several days before the actual day. They only offered me two different times that were way apart. And by this I mean the interval was ridiculous. Something like 6:45 or 11:30. I opted for the earlier one, even though my friends worked until 7 and could not get there on time. Upon arriving, I took a seat at the bar and was kindly offered a cocktail by the AMAZINGLY helpful and welcoming bartenders. They had taken my card and put it on file to reserve the table, and told me my table would be mine for two hours. While I waited for my friends to arrive at the bar, the MANAGER came up to me and told me I was gorgeous, but he would need to personally take in my dress (since it was a flowing, shirt dress with no belt) because my "dress did not do justice". When I exclaimed, "EXCUSE ME?!" he proceeded to add that I needed to show more leg and my figure because the dress was unflattering. HE CLEARLY HAD A RING ON HIS FINGER AND IS A MARRIED MAN. When my friend interjected and made him know we saw his ring, he simply shrugged and told her she was mad because he didn't flirt with her. :0 Once my friends arrived at about 7:30, I went up to the maitre d and informed him. He looked at me and told me he sat down others in MY TABLE, WHICH WAS RESERVED FOR 2 HOURS. He then continued to add that walk-ins take precedence, which completely baffles me because, JEEZ what is then the point of making a reservation?! IT IS MEANT TO RESERVE A SPOT FOR AN ALLOTTED PERIOD OF TIME. Unfortunately these two massively uncomfortable instances were enough to ruin my perception of the restaurant. The drinks were delicious. The food was as well. But POOR POOR POOR POOR POOR and PUTRID SERVICE. I AM DISGUSTED. The owner would do well in firing their entire management staff. Like I said the food was good, but the quantity was a joke, as well as the pricing for such menial meals. The most surprising thing out of all of this was after I expressed my annoyance I was not even offered an apology. Simple. I will never return again. If you appreciate honesty at its best, you'd believe this review for all its worth, because I give credit where it's due.

The pizza was great. Tried a traditional cheese pizza and I liked it. It wasn't greasy... it was perfectly cooked. There is a nice history (seeing how it is the first pizza place in America... even though they moved from their original location) and that is a cool place to eat at with friends from out of town. Â I will go back and bring friends!!!

I chose Samudra for a spot of Indian food during a business trip based on its good Yelp reviews. Unfortunately, this was one of the times where I decidedly disagree with the majority of the other reviews. Samudra was pleasant enough and the service was good, but the food was quite underwhelming. The Mumbai-style pav bhaji tasted like it was mostly tomato paste and had the wrong consistency. The pav they used was also wrong: it should be lightly toasted, buttered sandwich buns; instead they used microwaved, heavily buttered dinner rolls. The onion dosa was just a plain dosa with mostly uncooked red onion sprinkled inside. The accompanying chutney and sambar was lukewarm and not very flavorful. There's certainly plenty of competition in Jackson Heights, so next time I'll be trying someplace else.
The breakfast-based food is excellent. Â Also, I hate beets, but love their beets salad! Â Whatever you do, do not order the fried chicken.

YUM! Â If you like Malaysian food this is your spot! Â And you need a reservation so plan ahead! Â Approaching the restaurant on a Friday around 6PM and seeing people waiting both inside and out, I was happy to spot a few of my dining companions already in. Â We had a reservation so once enough of us were there they sat us while we waited for the rest of our party. Â We were a group of 14 and I think that is about the max size they can support at one table. Â There were a lot of groups around us and as I've frequented here a few times in the past, I always seem to remember tables always have quite a few patrons, so this is a great spot for groups, something Malaysian food lends itself well to. Most the food is very good, but there are some misses, especially anything with chicken in it - too dry. Â The staff tries hard and service is good. Â All in all, a real winner for Malaysian food in NYC!

This is a really cute place. My brother and I came here after searching for a good lunch place in BK. He and I both got the pulled pork which was so good. I pretty much always get pulled pork if it's on the menu. He got the sandwich and I got the sliders. The sauce on the sandwiches is different from sauce I've had before. It was a little spicy and tangy but it was great. We came here right after they opened on a Saturday. It was pretty dead even though the waiter seemed a little preoccupied. It was kind of annoying since we knew what we wanted to eat and drink just a few minutes after sitting down. If I were walking near here in the future, I'd probably stop in.

The latest edition to this block of new restaurants on 9th between 53th and 54th Sts, it offers a middle ground between the divey bars across the street and the somewhat fancier joints next door. Alfie's is mostly craft beer bar, partly restaurant, and a schmidgen sports bar. Despite only two tvs there was no shortage of guys walking in wanting to watch "the game" while we were eating. I enjoy reviewing new joints, so let's get to it. Service: A+ Friendly and just attentive enough. Our water glasses were kept as full as if we were in a white glove restaurant. Â  Food: A 1/ Â kale tuscan caesar salad with dressing on the side. Topped with five perfectly grilled pieces of shrimp with the tails on, homemade croutons (stale burger buns likely but much better than your typical prepackaged crouton) and Parmigiano-Reggiano shavings provided a fresh, healthy option. 2/ burger. choice of salad, fries, or sweet potato fries. Sweet potato fries all the way! Comes with ketchup. I asked for honey mustard. must do. the honey mustard has a slightly spicy kick to it. yum yum yum. I was told the burger was good. the patty was sizable. see photos Decor: A Wood here, wood there, wood everyone! Modern rustic. minimal with every object clearly well considered. seating is spaced so you're not on top of each other. I don't know about you, but I don't care to stick my ass in people's faces as I get in and out of a table. Bathrooms: B-. Â Single for ladies. Wood everywhere, industrial rolls of rough toilet paper. Clean enough. Crowd: B- A solid mix of older folks, tourists, afterwork crowd, douchy frat boy types. A guy next to us (wearing a backwards cap no less, so 5 years ago) was shouting something about the majority of his one night stands. Lovely. There's sidewalk seating and they do take reservations. The two tvs are on opposite ends of the bar so you'll either cluster by the bathroom, or right by the front door. If you're sitting outside, you can see the one all the way at the end by the bathrooms- if you're wearing your glasses. Chill spot, definitely worth checking out if you're in the nabe. Welcome to the hood Alfie's!

Sometimes, when I want to cheat on Dizzy's, I go to Applewood for brunch. It's like stepping into a friendly family restaurant in Ohio. The coffee is delicious, the food is fresh, and the menu is always changing. I really love that they always offer biscuits, which are my favorite form of bread. Perhaps it's a bit cramped and overpriced, but for the occasional visit, Applewood is a worthwhile adventure.

After 10 days of pure, sublime eating binge in Singapore, I came back to New York wondering why I didn't eat more Malaysian food. Â My mouth would just start salivating at the thought of Roti Prata, laksa, chicken rice and Bah Kut Teh. Â Sure, I can make my own laksa and my own Bah Kut Teh but mastering the art of spreading that roti dough and having the patience for alternating poaching the chicken from hot to cold water were beyond me. Â And at these kind of prices, there's just no reason to. Everything was delicious and I wonder how far they'll deliver :)
Always satisfies late night or early morning...Food is pretty good! Â Open 24 hours, yippee!!!

Went in the evening and took advantage of their 2 for $15 which is excellent value. Only a few tables so is very cosy. Arribiata is fairly spicy and grandmas meatballs were very good. Girl behind the counter was a little frosty but the food made up for that.

Went here on a sunday eve/night...was pretty quiet and emptyish. the decor is nice. waitress was attendtive. didnt come here for dinner, just something light and some drinks. we had wings, which were pretty good and corn on the cob-which was blah! needed a kick. i had the soco sangria, which was decent. i'd def return to try something different.

Breakfast anytime is best part. Also good lunch and dinner menu. The Mac & cheese and chicken & waffles are a must try. Prime Chelsea location. Try to go off peak to avoid long wait. Eatery in Midtown West is a "wannabe" of this spot.

Everyday I go to Just Salad on 51st and Park Â and pass Uncle Gussy's on the way. Â The line is always at least 10 people deep. Â Today while en route to Just Salad I decided to change course and try Uncle Gussys. Â This was my first ever food truck experience. Â I got the chicken over rice. Â The chicken was all dark meat, very fatty and hard to chew. Â I got grossed out after 1 bite. Â I removed the chicken and just ate the rice with lettuce and tomato. Â I will never go back to this food truck again. Â The whole time while eating, I was thinking of what kind of food poisoning this meal is going to give me. Â Not a good thought.

MMM MMM .. . And once again MMMM! Yakitori Totto, please open up a west coast operation. Â So delicious, So tasty, So mmm. Â  Items I recommend from my magical night at Yakitori Totto: Tuskune: Â Basically long Chicken Meatballs, I recommend getting them with the tare (sauce) vs shio (salted) but either way you can't go wrong Aspara Bacon: Â Bacon wrapped Asparagus . . . need I say more, your getting protein and veggies Negima: Chicken thigh with scallions threaded between classic and probably what you think of when you think of yakitori, but you've never had it this tender before Harami: Skirt Steak, for those who don't want chicken Bonchiri: Â the tail of the chicken very tender very delicious Only drawback of Yakitori Totto is they get busy quick, and reservations are a no no after 7pm. Â Luckily there is a FANTASTIC Karaoke bar next door and they have cheap drinks, yakitori totto will call your phone when your ready. Â So get a Lil' tipsy, Sing a Lil' and then bam delicious dinner, THEN return for some awesome possum Karaoke and that is an excellent evening. Last parting item, when I was there they were offering Yebisu Beer in the bottle, you can't get yebisu everywhere, so take advantage. Â My favorite Japanese beer except for Orion.

We ate in the outside patio area of the restaurant. It was pretty awesome and was the first time in a long time that eating outside in NYC didn't feel like being in NYC. The food was great as well as the service. I would definitely recommend hitting it up.

These guys are still pretty good and I can say that I have been going here for about 10 years now. They are basically the McDonalds of Halal Cart food in the city. They have however traded up a bit of taste for speed and cashflow. Still $5 for a mixed platter, $6 with Pita or soda The major down side recently has been...in order to speed up the process the food is no longer made to order...they precook the food (there is a lot of turn over so no worries on the freshness) and then dump it into plastic containers. C'mon guys...someone is going to get the bottom of the barrel one day and it is not going to be pretty. Also the use of plastic containers Â to store the precooked food turned me off a bit. The chicken used to come in chunks now has been reduced to hash or pulled chicken at best. and the lamb is almost ground up before they have chopped it too fine. I think this is what give Sammy's in Queens the leg up on the halal guys.

Was gonna dock a star for the lurking feeling the server kept trying to upsell us on the more expensive wine and a couple more appetizers and entrees (which we of course did not finish) , but perhaps she just wanted to make sure we didn't go hungry. Still, each entree serves 2.5 normal grown men. Calamari was great but no tentacles. I think it s their great tomato dipping sauce that makes it so tasty. Zucchini fries are like good ruffles with ridges potato chips without the guilt (seemingly). Veal parm was the standout favorite. Server was right - with 8 guys we really could've ordered another one of these. Linguine clam in white sauce was gross - no flavor or sauce to it. All the red pastas were good - spaghetti with meatballs, baked ziti, and rigatoni w mozzarella and eggplant. The flavored of all three started to blend together, but the best was I thought the rigatoni w mozzarella and eggplant. Somehow that combo worked well. Oh their mixed drinks was so watered down It sucked. Stick to the liquor on rocks. Or wine beer. Liquor on rocks gave vicious pours too.

Friday night and we were seated right away on their quaint little patio (sweet!). Â 10 minutes later we were approached by a hostess, "who sat you here!?" (suggesting we sat our selves). Â " well this table is reserved for some VIPs!" (suggesting we were chopped liver!?) Situation handled very poorly and unprofessionally. Â Not wanting to ruin the night and make a scene, accepted a table in their very loud and cramped dinning room (not sweet). Â  The food really wasn't bad. Â It is one of those places that you would want to return to to try other things, and I totally would if not for the extremely low level of service. Â Other reviews have it pegged when they say you will never see your waitress more than 2x's. Â Which is fine with me since their attitude made me feel as if I should stand up and serve them drinks! Â Who you will see allot of is the overly eager bus boys. Â We ordered the corn and every time I took a bite and placed it back on the plate I would hear "finished sir?". Â I wouldn't mind it so much if it didn't happen 10x's in 15 minutes, no exaggeration. Â However, this is still better than the waitresses who will decide for you when your done! Â I suppose the bread was just there for me to admire for a second and not to eat!? Â  I am someone who thought that by deep-frying, anything can be made better. Â Avocados, are not one of those things. Â The mild flavor of an avocado really has no chance against the thick salty crust. Â Imagine the disappointment of biting into an onion ring with no onion inside. Â The empanadas were stellar. Â Maybe not authentic but very tasty. Â Nice texture to the skin without being thick. Â The famous $5 corn is ok if you really like spicy mayo. Of all the Coffee braised ox-tail I tried this one had the best flavor. Â Nutty and chocolatey goodness over egg noodles, but where's the beef?? The blood sausage was also up there, Â great herbal undertones in a loosely packed link. Â Imagine pate in a tube, buttery and delicious spread on bread (wait, where did my bread go!?!). Short rib + msg + grill = good? Â Short ribs were cooked very precisely to order. Â Medium actually came out medium!! Â Could it be they actually have a chef that grills by feel and not by timer?? The food would have deserved another star or two but dinning is about the overall experience and the service just leaves a bad taste in your mouth that overshadows the slightly above average food here.
Love this place! Great date night joint! Foods amazing!! Service was great, bouncer has such a welcoming smile(tall black guy) & love dark ambiance and crowd is always chill

One of the best meals I've had in the city. This place is small and unassuming but it packs a punch of great food. Definitely get the meatball sliders for an appetizer, it change any bad feeling you have about veal. For a dinner, get the crispy chicken. Every ingredient was so good, I was close to licking the plate. If you're in the mood for fish, get the halibut, which was also perfectly cooked.

I am looking forward to my next trip to Fette Sau. When I popped in it was 30 mins before they closed so a lot of the good stuff was gone for the day. The staff was really accommodating and didn't give us a hard time for being those jerks that come in at the last minute. We ordered a few different things they had: pulled pork, ribs and brisket. The meat was meh actually... a bit too dry. I am going to assume that it usually isn't like that here because I am really looking forward to trying it again. We also tried the beans and potato salad. The potatoes were great but the beans were definitely not for me... my friend totally gobbled them down though. The staff was nice, the layout is cool and it is definitely a popular place.. usually the line is nuts here!! Be prepared for that if you are heading there for dinner hours... like any day of the week. Well I am hoping next time the food is better but I would recommend it regardless!
Greatest late night food spot ever. Â Order the poutine. Â You won't regret it.

The friend chicken and waffles were good I finished my entire plate. My friend Brett was pretty hung over so he didn't eat too much of his. The wait to be seated is about 40 minutes but the wait list guy is entertaining.

They rename this place to Vanessa's Dumpling and I am not sure if this is the place where my friends used to go or if there is another no name dumpling house... but I don't care for their Sesame Pancake with Beef. THANK GOD I didn't go crazy and ordered a whole bunch of them! L and I decided not to go crazy and just ordered one to share and I told her that Prosperity Dumpling is so much better. The Sesame Pancake is a lot more fluffier and softer in texture. Â Not to mention it was already made spicy and since L trusts my judgments we decided to leave Vanessa's after being disappointed. We got to Prosperity and L loved them more and said I was right! Yes, Prosperity is smaller but it's so much better!
Service was good, food was not. Â Did not enjoy the onion soup or the duck special in any way.

Best Sicilian slice ever!! Spumoni Gardens is a must-try for any pizza fan. The bread is perfectly chewy and the crust is bar none. The cheese melts into the bread to form an unbelievable and unique texture. The sauce is on top of the cheese it is deeply layered with flavor and a little sweet. There is nothing I dislike about this pizza. I have only ever gone to the pizza parlor, and not the attached restaurant, but the restaurant has a line out the door at night so I assumed it also fantastic. The Spumoni dessert is also a favorite of mine. It is best enjoyed outside on a warm summer day. Spumoni Gardens has an old school Brooklyn feel that is hard to find. If this place was closer by, I would stop in all the time.

Absolutely horrible service. The pretentious snotty hipster Williamsburg douche of a host/server continually lied to us about wait times and kept letting other parties in front of us. He also needs to learn how to count, because 6 minutes and 45 minutes are not the same. I wouldn't go here again if I was paid to.

I generally don't eat halal from food carts and this was my first time trying The Halal Guys. I ordered the chicken platter and immediately noticed the color of the pile of chicken....grey/pinkish? I thought it would be grilled and have that freshly grilled flavor... Nonetheless, everything was seasoned well and it tasted pretty good, but I felt like I swallowed a brick half hour after eating it. I'm don't really have a sensitive stomach either...but either way I will try this again at some point and perhaps get something different.

I had the Pulled Pork Sandwich. Â The meat was very good and tender. Â There were some bits of really fatty pieces in there though. Â Also, I didn't feel like it tasted like a Viet Sandwich, but more like an American Pulled Pork Sandwich that was a little sweet and spicy. Â There are Viet Sandwiches that I've had for half the price...that were larger and have more that "Viet Sandwich taste" I crave. Â It may be due to the add of the mayo, which was good, but changed the taste to American food. That is my main complaint. Either way, sandwich was still good!

i LOVE the chicken shawarma platter here...i get it with babaganoush and the green salad with lemon dressing..Delish :) I have also had the hummus, the cheese pie, the meat pie and the other chicken plate (Can't remember the name offhand) Fresh Pita comes with meal, as well as hot sauce and tahini. Great Service! Great prices! Stop in you wont be disappointed!

You go Batali!! Thank you for the great Spanish food. While I was a little hesitant about how a good Batali's take on Spanish food would be, seeing how he is primarily known for his Italian cuisine, my wife and I were happily and deliciously surprised. Did we like the food? Let's put it this way, the moment we set one foot out the door, we were already thinking and talking about when we were going to return. Everything was incredible. We ordered pork croquettes, scallops with blood oranges and rainbow carrots, sepia a la plancha with salsa verde, pulpo with fennel and grapefruit, and skirt steak with onion mermelada. I won't go into detail about each one because I'll get too hungry just thinking about it. Rest assured that everything was delicious. The service was good considering how busy the establishment was. We sat at the bar and had fun chatting with the cooks as we drank some great Spanish wine. I've lived in Spain for over 8 years and I fancy myself relatively knowledgeable about this cuisine. Batali's food, while not entirely traditional, is a delightful take on Spanish Tapas. If you like tapas and love sea food, you must stop by Casa Mono.

After enjoying the juicy goodness of this burger out on the westcoast.... iv been patiently waiting for the day it would make its journey to the eastcoast. Alas... it finally landed out here in the big apple. Im all about the MANLY BURGER....how can u go wrong. beer cheddar cheese.... good lord it has beer and cheese already. then you add crispy onion rings?? every burger should have onion rings. and finally the coup de grÃ¢ce...... BACON LARDON.... as cliche as it sounds... everything is good with bacon. TRUFFLE FRIES.... loved the fries, crispy and thinly cut. just the way i like my fries and just the perfect essence of truffle. FRIED PICKLES.... wasnt really a fan. im used to having them as chip size, like at hooters. Â these were thick sticks of pickle spears. possibly if it was cut a little bit thinner i wouldve enjoyed them more

We went there 2 weeks ago with our family. It was great ! You close your eyes and you're in Paris. Busy, tables every where, nice tablecloth on the tables (that's really how we apreciate restaurants). The food was delicious, the service was fast and very politely handled. We will go back for the oysters, the duck confit was excellent and...the profiterolles were.....well, close your eyes, you are in a bistro in Paris.

I got a reservation for brunch on Sunday. And it was not very crowded, so I think without reservation you can still get a table shortly. The brunch menu is concise, so it's easy to decide what you want. We got egg Benedict, which was cooked perfectly. The lamb slider is fine, not as good as I expected. Salad is fresh. Decor and ambiance are great. Just wish the service could be faster. Overall , I still recommend this place for hang-out with friends.

It's a small and simple place. I ordered stew beef noodle. It says the noodle is hand-made because it is "La Mian", but actually it is fast noodle. A little dissappoint... Beef is delicious and noodle soup is good. Next time I may try "bao zai chang fen"~haha~

5/5 stars for me. What a place! A definite must go to on a Thursday night or Saturday night. Bring a date, bring a friend, bring a grandparent, bring a stranger! 8:30 and 10:30 on both nights they have Flamenco dancing with Reynoldo Rincon and his family (wife, son, daughter). They do two shows while everyone is eating and talking at their table and it is electric. The traditional dancing, the atmosphere, the energy. Now, to the food! The waiter, Julio, was a huge help. As a group of 4 men he suggested we get 8 tapas. We selected 2 each. I won't go through them all but they ranged from octopus to sardines to serrano ham croquettes to goat cheese stuffed olives. Julio was upset we didn't two of the best sellers (shrimp in garlic sauce and a churrasco with quail egg), so he brought them out anyway. Â UNREAL. We had a few pitchers of red sangria and some after dinner traditional sherry. What an experience. Don't think this is a seafood place only, there are plenty of non-seafood tapas to try. Sit at the bar, get a table, just make a reservation! Until next time.

utterly fantasic restaurant. Â Great, informal atmosphere, attentive and smart staff, and phenomenal food. Â can't say enough about theplace. Â Pricey, but unlike so many other restaurants, totally worth the splurge.

My boyfriend and I only ever order the Carnitas for 2, usually paired with a pitcher of sangria. I dare someone to find a meal that is better priced. Yuca Bar's Carnitas for 2 is the best deal in town! And we always get the chicken wrapped to go, and use it as stuffing for a chicken sofrito omelet the next morning, using the onions and shredded chicken. Can you really get four meals out of a meat dish that includes short beef ribs, a half grilled chicken, four lamb sausages, and four chorizo slices? And the "Meat Plate for 2," as I refer to it, is served w/pickled jalapeÃ±os and carrots, rice and black beans, and mouthwatering crispu yuca fries.

This review is for their brunch menu. I came here after a late late late night out. I'm pretty sure I looked presentable/normal but probably due to paranoia, when the waiter offered me coffee, it seemed as though based on their tone, they really thought I needed it. Despite that, the staff was extremely friendly to the point of uncomfortableness-not in a bad way but due to unfamiliarity. What was really neat about this place is that the sous chef came out and served us complimentary orange julius which was tangy sweet and refreshing. I saw him come out several more times throughout our meal as he helped serve customers. This is such a nice notion. I'm not sure if this is common but I do know that they just started serving brunch very recently so it might have been a way to establish their customer base. I tried their two poached eggs laid on a bed of collard greens which was pretty good. As a dessert, I tried their apple cided donut holes which were great. They were filling so I'd recommend sharing.

Are you kidding me?! They didn't let us in with two strollers and the hostess was a complete bitch. I'm sorry but I don't understand when a child becomes a burden. Disgusting. Had to walk out without even trying their food. Parents don't attempt to go with your kids since this place is def. not kid friendly AT ALL!

I'd much rather give Lombardi's a 3.5, but since I'm unable to do that I think they fall under a 4 more than they do a 3. Â Yay for their fresh ingredients - eating a pizza with fresh mozzarella cheese is rare! Â The garden salad was very tasty; I loved their dressing! Â I was also in love with the pizza sauce and fresh basil on the pizza. Â The crust could have been better, crunchier; instead, it was on the soggy side. Â The last bite of the crust was crunchy, but flavorless. Service is friendly and mighty quick; I presume they're used to the constant flow of customers. Â It's too bad they can't accommodate more people. Â Boo on the cash only policy. Â I tried a local brew, Brooklyn lager(?), and enjoyed that, too!

Very authentic Japanese food. If 75% of the patrons are Japanese, you know it's authentic. They have awesome lunch specials just under $10 and it comes with so much food. I had the chirashi lunch special and it comes with shrimp tempura over rice, soba noodles, an egg custard (salty and not the sweet kind) with miso soup. That's alot of food for $10. Very delicious!! The soda was overpriced at $3 for a glass from the fountain. Do call before you head over for lunch or dinner. They were closed for a whole week during July 4th.

Was super excited to try this place based upon the reviews here, and maybe I got an off day but the bartender was very eh. We first posted up by the window and waited for a while and received no service, we moved to the bar and waited some more, even though the middle aged Mitch Hedberg look-a-like saw us and then didn't come take our order. Finally a middle aged blonde came over and took my order first. My boyfriend ordered a beer and she informed them they were out of that and something else she couldn't remember and then immediately started to walk away. It wasn't busy, no one else was waiting to order, she was just bailing. Also, cash only. Their ATM has a $2 service fee so plan accordingly. Didn't have a chance to try the food, but can't see any reasons for returning to do so.

Came here on a Â Tues night and took advantage of their young musicians showcase of live jazz in the bar next door area where they serve a full menu as well. There's no cover for the young musicians showcase, only requirement is to have one drink. I spotted a Malbec for $7.25 so no complaints about the one drink rule! The music was pretty loud since it's a small space so it made it difficult to hold a conversation with my friend. However, the musicians were really talented so if you want to do this, just go with someone who you'll be comfortable not talking to and just enjoying the music. I got the pesto lasagna which wasn't as big as I anticipated from the yelp reviews but still substantial. It didn't blow me away but was satisfying. My friend's pizza margherita looked like a better choice and was cheaper and bigger. I ended up paying $25 with tip for my entree and glass of wine. I peeked in the garden area which is good for winter or summer since it's actually indoors but makes you feel like you're dining outdoors. This could definitely be a cute date place and I'm curious about their pumpkin cheesecake, so I might be coming back. Service was polite but somewhat inattentive.

I wasn't planning on writing a review for this place because I already wrote one for song and they are the exact same place. However, tonight I ate two new dishes that I enjoyed so i felt the desire to express myself. I ate two new appetizers that were both really good. First I had the Thai spare ribs which were tasty. They were the dry and crispy kind which I really enjoy and they came with a nice tangy side dipping sauce which have it a nice zing. Second I ate the chicken and noodle soup which was absolutely freaking amazing. It was so tasty that I didn't want to stop eating it. I devoured it in like 2 minutes. The broth was addictive!! As for my main meal it was delicious of course. This place never lets you down.

First of all, coming from a critical eater, 4 start is a big compliment. Â The place is intimate and charming. Â The owners are attentive and easy going. Â There were many good dishes, and the presentations are stella, with feminine touch. Â The memorable dishes were the sunchoke, onion soup, duck breast and the goat cheese with apples. Â The chef's palette seem to lean in the delicate & refined spectrum, and succeeds in extracting clean flavors. Â Almost like applying kaiseki techniques to global ingredients. Â The results are delightful. Â The drawbacks to me were the first and the last course. Â Unfortunately, 1st impression and last impression, although minute, sets the tone in major ways. Â The potato starter was heavy on the vinegar, left caviar undetected. Â The texture was unclear. Â The coffee coconut mousse was too cold in temperature which disrupted the flavor and the texture and came off too traditional since my expectation was built high by all the courses before then. Â More diversity in wine would be nice too. All in all, you won't regret visiting this well ran establishment and taste some great food without dealing with much formality. Â I'm just expecting and hoping for more and would like to try again when the menu changes.

Ill start with the drinks. Sangria was fruit cocktail dumped into some white wine, but it tasted good. Â The app's were good. The arepas were good but a little bland. Lots of fried food and fried cheese's. I wanted to go eat a head of lettuce after word but otherwise I cant complain. Very friendly staff.

Absolutely the best. Great atmosphere, great food, and reasonably priced. When you go, either be real hungry or go with friends because everything is served family style. The food and the quality is about as close as you will get to the real thing in Italy. Enjoy!

I feel like the BYOB policy has inflated the reviews here. The food was okay, but not amazing. I remember that we shared the goat cheese tart, some sort of a red meat (veal?) stew, and the lamb dish. The stew was incredibly oversalted to the point where I didn't even want to eat it past the 3rd or 4th bite. The goat cheese/truffle tart was good, but totally overpriced (about $17). I also didn't find the service that friendly. I'm not sure if it was just me. While the place is cute and quaint and the BYOB policy is very attractive, I probably would prefer to spend my money elsewhere.

I'm surprised I actually haven't reviewed this yet, despite having been here many, many times during pancake month. I've had many a pancake here, and they are great, and the maple butter that comes with it is fantastic.
