The fried chicken is great, and the short ribs were also good, although sometimes it's been a bit off. The half-price wines on Mondays and Tuesdays are a great deal, especially in larger groups, but the wait on weekdays for groups of 6 can stretch over 1.5 hours, so either get there early or go in smaller groups. I've also had less-than-warm service from the staff holding the reservations, which has been kind of a downer, but the food is always really great, and it's definitely worth a special visit, so long as you can stomach the wait.

I was searching for good nepali restaurants as I was craving for the food so badly after coming back from a trip there.I saw Himalayan Yak having good reviews and decided to give a try. And I am so glad I did that. It was amazing, both food and the dinning environment. They serve Tibetan and Nepali food. Their decor is very classic and unique. Oh well, at least they are very unique to me since I am not Nepalese or Tibetan. We ordered beef Thali (traditional Nepali combination platter), Shpata (beef chilly), and some other spicy beef dish that I forgot about the name. Honestly, I am not sure how authentic the food is as I am not native. But they definitely taste good. I will say they taste almost as good as those I had in Nepal and Tibet. Beef Thali is very tasty and I like how they give you the great combo of meat, veggie and carbs in one order. The other two dishes are relatively spicy but also very delicious. We went on a weeknight. But I heard there will be band performing on Friday nights. So people who like their traditional music should go check it out at Friday night. I will definitely go back for more yummy tasty food :)

came here for brunch a few weeks ago didn't know what to expect. I was very pleasantly surprised. The place itself is is nice, it looked cramped from the front but they have a fairly large backroom where most diners are sat. There aren't a lot of options on the "brunch" menu (they have a lot of things on the menu but only some were included in the prix fixe brunch) but they all looked good though Ill have to come back to try them. I had the strepizzate(sp?) which is basically a fancy way of saying you get a platter of tasty things to eat. First there are "creamy" scrambled eggs of which I was at first leery of as I like my scrambled eggs on the dry but fluffy side, and these were not that. they were kinda mushy and had a weird look to them. Don't let that deter you though as they taste delicious especially since they drizzle a little olive oil over them. Then there's the home fries which while nothing special are perfect examples of home fries for which I was grateful. I don't need any one messing with my home fries thank you. There's a nice little salad, just some mixed greens with some oil and lemon juice on them which is actually kind of refreshing. and last but not least was a crostini of bread ( I think they bake it on premises) with goat cheese and smoked salmon. De-lish. I am a huge fan of smoked salmon and goat cheese so when put together I was very happy. All in all an unexpected find with a bunch of things that I do want to come back and try including the house made pizzas which we saw a few of floating past us as we ate.

How do you know when you really love a place? When you wake up the next day dreaming about "La Chiquita"; the sandwich of your wildest dreams. Oh yes, she is just the right size, has so many layers to discover, absolutely delicious and I'll be darned if she isn't downright sexy. I had to come here for dinner again the next night because it was all I could think about. That and getting a mojito. Seriously. I could not believe how good a vegetarian sandwich could be! But that didn't stop me from ordering and devouring as much as I could off of the menu (Please note that this is what we ordered in the course of 2 separate dinners. We are not Shamu.) Â Their classic cuban sandwich is as close as you're going to get to "legit" north of Miami. The Ropa Vieja dish was something you'd expect to get served at your Cuban friend's grandma's place. The mojitos are deeelish and their other cocktails are even better. If I remembered their names I'd recommend but, hey, that just means I had a great time, right? However, Guantanamera on 8th Ave still holds the title for best mojitos in NY in my book. The restaurant itself is chÃ­c (love the decor- pristine white walls with ceiling fans immediately evoke thoughts of cuba). The live jazz on weekends is actually pretty good (the trumpet player rocked my socks right off), and their staff is laid back-- yet attentive, which is nice. Cafe Havana, you just got b*tch slapped. And her name is "La Chiquita."

Spouse ordered pastrami on rye. She thought it had a peculiar taste and left half on the plate. I had the onion soup and grilled cheese. Soup was excellent; not much you can do to foul up grilled cheese. The outstanding service saved this from being a 2-star revu.

Came here on a rainy Sunday, and when I say rainy I mean monsoon like weather which caused us to sprint here from the previous bar. For our group it was a nice spot to grab a beer and a bite to eat. As others have mentioned, the meatloaf sandwich was really good - It was less like the meatloaf I grew up with and more like a burger, but that's not a bad thing. I liked how you paid for the food upfront as when we were finished we could simply get up and leave rather than sit around for a check. They have a couple outdoor tables that would be a great spot to chill when it's not raining like a page out of Jumanji.

i'm going to have to give 5 stars just for the fact that it's 24 hours! that is huge bonus points in my book. the food is delish! have seen parker posey outside the restaurant, and i'm sure other celebs dine here. always crowded on the weekends. food is pretty good. their drinks are original and have a good variety of non alcoholic drinks as well. love the truffle mac and cheese here. only downside is it can be a little pricey for what u get. we need more places like this in NYC! they call this the city that never sleeps, and yet, i don't see many more restaurants like this around that are open ALL NIGHT. just regular diner fare. i would say the true city that never sleeps would be Las Vegas. CC

I guess I'm not impressed by this place. Â From the name, I was expecting more than just a place to get food - like a REAL commune where artists, Â authors, etc. get together and share their talent with everyone in an accessible way -- something truly different for our 'hood but it's not very different at all. Â Same old type of food and it's overpriced. Â  They hit it right by giving it this name because it peaks your interest and it draws you in. Â But as someone posted previously, the execution is lacking. I've gone into this place about 4 times and each time I've left without ordering anything so I can't comment on how the food tastes. Â I've left because I can't get over the prices and from looking at the showcase of prepared foods, I never get the WOW! factor to fork over the cash for this food. Â So, I've given up on the place. The staff have always been very friendly though. I hope they stay in business however since our little hood needs to have options. Â I just feel like this place is too "schtick" for me...but then again, there are plenty of people who like "schtick".

The BEST pizza I have ever had. I yelped this place before trying it out, and I fell in love with it. During my 5 day trip to Manhattan, I visited this place three times! For my party of two, I ordered the Broccoli/Mozzarella and Grandma's Pizza. Both were oozing with cheese, pounded with flavor, and absolutely divine! I also tried the garlic knots, which were delicious, but best eaten while hot. The pizzas were big enough to share, and were quite filling. For 12 bucks, and for such great pizza, I was in heaven. The only downside is the size of the place. With only four seats, and a countertop, you're guaranteed to get cozy with other folks eating there. This is a definite stop for every time I visit Manhattan. I definitely recommend this place to all pizza lovers out there :)

Ward III is my go to spot for three reasons: 1) The food is flavorful and portions size are priced right and great for sharing. Definitely order the Truffle Mac and Cheese and the Lamb Tacos. Â  2) Bartenders are friendly and not bad to look at:-) 3) Fresh innovative cocktails that are reasonably priced

Went to this place for Mother's Day with a group of 7. It was a beautiful place tucked away in a unique alley. The decor fits with the location. It's cozy, but large, with many rooms. It's decorated in a hunter's lodge style that's very reminiscent of the concept - old-American. There are stuffed birds and deer/moose heads all over the wall. This place is NOT for vegans. The staff took us in on time and sat us in a small room. They were fantastic throughout our brunch experience. Not faultless, but very attentive and fair. They noticed the room was hot and opened the windows. The waitress forgot to submit our appetizer orders on time, but came to us to let us know and apologize, without us asking and even took ALL the appetizers off the bill. FANTASTIC! Â The place was spotless and quiet, though lively. Everyone was well dressed in edgy wear and it was a pleasant experience until... The Bloody Marys got there. They offer 3 Marys on the menu, but all 3 came in small glasses with mostly just tomato juice in them. Almost no garnish at all (there is a caper berry (not flower) floating in there somewhere) and just a little bit of horseradish on the bottom. It wasn't seasoned well nor did it have a good amount of alcohol in it. It was REALLY plain. Also, the ice cubes were almost the size of the glass and made getting at the garnish impossible and watered down the drink even more. Other drinks were nice. Notable: St Germain cocktail and the Pisco cocktail that used to be called Andie Walsh. Also of note is the strawberry soda which was fresh and delightful. The Yuzu drink was just a hard limeade by flavor and if you don't like Gin, you won't like most drinks on the menu (did you guys lose the concept of Whiskey in early America?) Anyway, we all sipped our drinks until... The food arrived. That's where the bubble burst. The food is about as inventive and tasty as IHOP. No, really, it is. I had the Smoked Trout which is a basic ingredient to begin with. It's quite salty and slightly smoky. It was served with cornichons, caper berries, toast, two hard-boiled eggs cut in half and horseradish mayo. None of those things were inventively presented. They were literally placed on the wooden plate as is. No garnish, no fresh herbs (it was May), no nothing. I ordered a side of bacon, which came as... you guessed it, simply 3 slices of thick cut bacon (it actually was delicious, but all 3 orders of it for the table came cooked to a different grade and it wasn't ordered that way.) The flavor profile of the dish: Salty and bland. VERY salty, actually. That's it. There was nothing else to it. The bread wasn't buttered and it wasn't toasted. It was stale to the point that it was hard to chew. The eggs weren't seasoned. They were just boiled and cut in half. The gherkins and caper berries are delicious things, but they just added more salt to the plate, which as I said earlier, was the tone of the dish. Not very filling and definitely not memorable. It's a dish that could have been, if someone had put in some effort, but no one did. Others in my party had the hamburger (mostly lettuce), Spring Veg and Field Mushroom ragu (soupy MESS x2) and poached eggs with roasted (grilled) tomato slices and cheese grits (yup, that's all that was on the plate.) I didn't hear anyone comment about how good the food was. My mother told me later she hated her dish (the ragu) and she loves eggs, and mushrooms and peas. She just thought it was completely boring and something my father can make (not a compliment, believe me.) Anyway, the meal ended with bananas foster (decent) and brownie with ice cream. Garnish? None. Fruit? Aside from the banana, none. These guys don't do garnish. They don't do fresh. Maybe they think restaurants 200 years ago didn't know about lettuces or bitter greens or herbs? If that's their idea of old-American cuisine then I wish they'd just disappear. Anyway, I really think a pinch of parsley or a chiffonade of sage really aren't too much to ask for in May, especially on a bland dish. A raspberry or mint sprig would have made any of the desserts. Too bad because the space has potential and the staff is excellent. They just need someone who knows how to cook.

The food here is decent. Definitely not what I'm used to seeing when going to a Korean restaurant, but I feel like this place presents in a way that's more palatable to people not used to eating traditional Korean food. It's also a lot more expensive than traditional Korean food. Put in the extra effort to look for an actual Korean restaurant, and you'll probably have a better meal.
4 stars but not a fan :-P But not 3 stars though. 3.5 maybe. 2 hours of waiting outside... 10 minutes to slurp my soup... Delicious ramen but didn't impress me... Not worth my time haha

Sushi Yasuda is a sushi purists' dream: incredibly fresh fish with minimal adornments--only those highlighting the inherent beauty of the sea's bounty ever take a place atop/inside each carefully crafted gem. Â The dining room itself is bamboo ceiling-to-table-to-floor, a quiet study of understated elegance in substance--symbolic of the culinary delights and Chef Yasuda, himself. My dining companion and I have been blown away by the impeccably pristine quality (a double emphasis that is well-deserved) and minimalist approach. Â Add to it, Chef Yasuda offers a wide selection of choices from which to have your taste buds tantalized. As with quality produce, the best sushi selections will depend on the seasonality and availability of fish/non-fish items. Â It goes without saying to get the maximum experience, it is best to focus on Chef Yasuda's suggestions (marked on the menu in red ink) or ask him directly if you have the pleasure of dining in front of him at the sushi bar. His NON-FISH items that have profoundly left an impression on us: - Uni: The most sweet, nutty, and intricately-flavored urchin roe we have ever had--a pinch of salt crystals on top added the final touch for a tongue-gasm. - Peace Passage Oyster: The intense taste-fragrance and first notes transported us to the ocean. Â We normally order small and lacy oysters at raw bars, so we were surprised how such large and plump ones appealed so perfectly to our tastes. Â Also revelatory was the final note of flavor: both of us felt a gentle taste of palate-cleansing wasabi. - Mirugai Himo (meat from inside the giant clam's shell): Similar to the oyster but a bit milder and crisper in texture, I preferred this one to the oyster--the opposite for my oyster connoisseur dining companion who is more seasoned in appreciating the intense aromas of raw bivalves. - Three Eels (Dark Anago, White Anago, Dark Unagi): All three had distinct textures and tastes, each freshly made to order--blanched then grilled on eel grills. Â If you never had sea eel, you must try the anago--its texture and natural sweetness are unbelievable. Â The extra care and variations in preparation made it a joy to eat truly fresh eel, since unagi in most sushi places has a chemical taste found in freshwater fish like catfish and tilapia. - Ika: The truly masterful preparation was alone worth it. Chef Yasuda deftly scored the squid at an angle, then cross slitted in two more directions. Â Not only for show, this made the texture incredibly smooth and without the need for unpleasant fiber-gnawing. Â Perfection came with bits of salt on top that added a crunch to the truly tender squid. The FISH that have totally impressed us: - Sardine from Chef Yasuda's hometown of Chiba: This is the most flavor-intense fish we have ever enjoyed. Â The texture is incredibly smooth and naturally high oil-content a dream. - Gensaba: Like the sardine, this mackerel has intense flavor but a firmer texture. - Tail Toro: Truly sublime and flavorful! Â If available, an absolute must for the toro-lover. - Ivory King Salmon: Thanks to another friend wanting to order salmon sushi in our first visit, we were able to explore a fish we usually doid not order. Â Boy, were we ever glad that we did--the most luxurious icing on the proverbial sushi cake! One overall tip: While I do enjoy some sashimi, I recommend going nigiri whenever possible at Sushi Yasuda. Sushi Yasuda and Sushi Sono are the two sushi restaurants I recommend passionately and unequivocally. Â Even if both were equidistant from home, I would go to both equally because they are very complementary and have very little overlap among what we enjoy at each respective location. Â I favor Sushi Yasuda for its incredible non-fish nigiri and specialty fish nigiri; I favor Sushi Sono for fish specials, sashimi and nigiri of whole fish, special soups, and cooked array of seafood items.

I enjoy going to this place because they got good home style food. Â  I really hated it when Bourdain came to this place. Â He tends to ruin places that he puts on TV. Â  Even on a Monday night I still had to wait for a table. Â Pre-Bourdain, Monday was a short/no wait night. Â  Dessert is a steal at this place and food is always fun to eat. Â Good to get together with friends or a late night drink.

Definitely my go-to for brunching in NYC. Great prix-fixe menu for brunch - try the nutella french toast, pumpkin waffles, or omelet. Staff is super sweet. Two reasons I didn't go 5 stars: 1. Food is not always consistent in awesomeness: omelet was a little cold this morning 2. The wait is ridiculous - 2 hrs but they "called" us back early....only to have us stand there for another hour. So you should've just let us be for a while until you were SURE you had a table. That's the whole point of BuzzTable....

Came here again around Christmas time. Decorations were great. Service was horrible. Food came out lukewarm and on chipped plates. Â Order was not correct. Not sure what's going on here. Love the space. Please get it together Lillie's. Thanks !

The Five Leaves Burger may be the best burger in the city, and the Kale and Anchovy Dressing salad is without a doubt my favorite salad around. Â Brunch is good, but a weekday breakfast is an even more reasonable and nice experience.

I have been here a number of times just for a drink or two then on to another place. Their cocktails are fantastic. One of the best old fashions I've ever had. The decor is very Moto-esque (since I hear they were designed by the same guy). So, we finally decided to eat here. I ordered the squabcock. Presentation was fantastic, but it was tough vainy and generally not good. Maybe this is the nature of the squab seeing as it is a domesticated pigeon, but I did not enjoy it and will not order it again. Â I ate as much of it as I could and grabbed a slice afterwards to fill up. The only other problem is that it is cash only. I will be returning, but just for an appetizer (the table next to us got the mussels, and I thought about changing my order they looked so good) and a cocktail then on to the main course elsewhere.

I went on a ramen kick this past summer (you know, going two, three times a week to various spots) and I was not able to find a better ramen joint than here. Â I got hooked on their miso w/chicken but have yet to try the veggie one which i heard is amazing (word of mouth and apparently here). Â Their apps are really good and I housed a bowl of chicken wings the last time I went. Â Salty with some lime juice on top and you're golden. Â There are only four wings, but have you ever seen a chicken with six? Â  Of the two buns they serve, I would definitely take the pork belly over the shrimp any day. Â This isn't because everyone and their mother is getting off on pork belly these days, but simply because the shrimp is fried and seemed to have too much batter (oh, but the pork belly here is something to get off on...wow that just sounds waaay dirtier than I expected, but I digress.) Â Not to mention, the the cilantro, carrots, cucumbers, and whatever sauce they put on there compliment the pork belly so well. I didn't read many of these reviews, but i'm sure people pointed out how long it can take to get a seat. Â Again, the last time i was there, I witnessed at least three groups of two or more people get turned around at the door simply because they were too busy. Â They don't take reservations so sometimes you just need to luck out with timing. Â If you go by yourself, you have a better chance of getting a seat sooner than later, though that can vary (i've been seated in under 10 minute or up to 45.) Â I'll usually give this place a max of an hour wait without scoffing at it. Â There are good bars in the area that you can booze at while you wait. They also have "panda" sake that comes in a glass cup that you can bring home afterwards and it also come with a lid. Â I highly recommend this just for the practical aspect. Â The sake is tasty, though =) I went to ippudo, but chuko takes top billing in my book. If I lived any closer (about a 30 minute walk) i would come pretty close to broke because I would eat here all the freaking time.

Because the wait at Taverna Kyclades was 1.5 hours, this was our alternative for dinner on a Friday night. It wasn't very crowded when we arrived but the place did start to fill up. The service was really friendly and accommodating. We got to taste two different wines before settling on a bottle of red. Â We shared a lot of appetizers amongst the six of us. Â The spreads are okay, but the other appetizers are quite good. Make sure you get the octopus and calamari. We also shared main dishes - swordfish is yummy and the salads are generously portioned. The pizza is great deal for the price - huge steak pizza for $12.50! Â When time came for dessert, we were very skeptical about the baklva ice cream. But being a curious bunch we tried it and it was very good. An inventive dessert! Also don't miss the creme brulee; we had to re-order after the first one. This is a nice place for a casual get-together with friends, especially those on a budget. Â It's one of those few places where you can see your dining companions and actually hear what they are saying. Â I do think they could add in a few more tables in the middle of the dining room to make it feel less barren.

For hooking me up with a view of flowers while I wait, I guess that's cool. For hooking me up with free food while I wait, that's definitely cool. Strawberries? Don't mind if I do, sir.. Coffee? Yes, please. This is about the only place I'll order an egg cream or a cherry lime rickey from, but I couldn't tell you why. It just feels right somehow. This place just feels right. It's like it got warped here after an episode of "Leave it to Beaver" or something. Sure, as other reviews have pointed out, at the end of the day it is JUST diner food. However, it's diner food done better than almost anyone else. As far as the service is concerned, while you won't get free food for waiting in the south (most times), you will get the same kind of attentive service, though it will probably be from a meth-addled old white lady at Waffle House at 3am as opposed to these guys, who will cut up with you and laugh at your ridiculous jokes. However, this is NYC, and I have yet to see anywhere else here that gives this level of service without having the decimal point shifted one place to the right by the end of the meal.

The vintage look of this coffee shop and convenience of this location may lead you to think this is a great breakfast option. However, if coffee is what you need, be aware that you will not get it until 30 minutes into your stay--and by the way, they had to run next door as they ran out of coffee cups. And 45 mins in we've only just gotten our food--which was decent enough but not worth the insane prices and the battle with their terrible service. Go elsewhere, please. God forbid you're hungover as the delay for coffee and carbs would be near unbearable.

I went to Marc Forgione on the back of a review in the New York Times on the place (1 Michelin star helped bring me here too). We got here 30 mins before our reservation and were seated immediately on a Friday night which was a pleasant surprise. The food was terrific, the standout dishes were by far the chili lobster (it was really hot!) but so unique and delicious in its flavor and presentation. The entree was what I was looking forward to though before I got to the restaurant, their specialty, the chicken on a brick for two. I don't typically ever order chicken at good restaurants b/c it tends to be the "boring" meat and generally chefs don't like cooking it (source: Kitchen Confidential)....but this chicken was simply outstanding and perhaps the best I've ever had. Tender and juice swimming in a light sauce and potatoes. It was the definition of comfort food. I went back in October so I forget some of the other dishes but was very happy with the meal overall. Service was good and I liked the rustic ambiance. The only negative is that there's a bad draft that comes through the entrance (they don't have a screen door) so try to avoid sitting by the entrance or you'll be feeling a draft through dinner.
Great service. Delicious fried yuca and ceviche. Beautiful interiors, definitely recommend.

I'm a little ashamed to admit that I've lived in Park Slope for 7 years and have never been to this place. Â I'm going to go ahead and blame the fact that all of my friends live in Manahattan, so I tend to go out more there than in my own neighborhood. Â That, and I tend to feel a little awkward going to places to eat by myself. Thankfully, one of my UWS friends came to hang with me in Park Slope yesterday and we stopped here for a quick lunch. Â She had one of the design it yourself salads (tomatoes, goat cheese, grilled chicken & sunflower seeds) and I had the grilled portabello sandwich and fries. Â YUM! Â The salad -and particularly the goat cheese - was really good and the portabello was heavenly. Â It was marinated in a balsamic vinegar (I think - I'm going to go back and confirm) and came with a garlic mayo and was absolutely delicious in a very mouth-watering way. Â The fries were pretty good too. Â The lady next to use ordered a burger and it looked soooo good - I'll have to go back and give the burger a try, for sure! And although I'm not a beer drinker, my friend is and she confirmed that the small beer selection is impressive. I noticed a lot of people popping in to order food for take-out, and the guys behind the counter seemed to be really quick to prepare and package up the food, so I'll keep that in mind next time I want something quick to take home. The service was fast and friendly and we really enjoyed ourselves. Â I'll definitely be back, since I can comfortably sit alone at the bar area and not feel awkward. :-)

Came here on Friday night for a pre-Living Room concert dinner, so didn't have a chance to really appreciate everything, but what I DID experience was pretty damn good. Â Great atmosphere, really cute, with a nice sort of chill ambience that made me feel immediately comfortable. Â  Food was overall delicious..I ordered the Tagliatelle with Prosciutto, and my friend ordered the Priest Stranglers. Â Mine was a bit salty, but the waiter had warned me about that, and it still had a really rich yummy flavor. Â The pasta itself was great, just the right tenderness and it tasted incredibly fresh. Service was pretty decent, and our waiter was knowledgeable and generally available. Â  We did have to wait a bit for the food (20 min), but I chalk it up to the fact that they were making everything fresh, which makes it alright. Â  I will definitely come back and try the rest of the delicious sounding things on the menu.

We tried the Organic Black Truffle Mayo, Mango Chutney, the Special Sauce, and the Parmesan Eggplant dips. Â My faves were the Special Sauce and the Mango Chutney. Â Great late night snack. Â Near closing time, they'll serve you fries, but unfortunately, you won't be able to sit inside.

To all you haters, who dis Jimmy's taters: You just don't understand. Yes, they are unconventional, but it's cause they've taken taters to a whole new level. Jimmy's = Tater Heaven. Oh, and the owner is really cute, too.

Since the last time I came here, which was 4 years ago, Grimaldi's has gotten a lot bigger and popular. Â Four years ago, it was a little shop in the middle of the block. Â Now, Grimaldi's moved to this white castle at the corner of Front Street. Â The place expanded to two floors. With two friends of mine, we waited in line for hours just for a couple of slices of pizza. Â When you finally get a table, you might as well order three whole pies, one for each person, because the slices are so thin and you are starving from waiting so long. Â Once you place your order, be prepare to wait another hour or so for your pizza, because they make each pie from scratch. Â You are so hungry that you might start eating the peppers from the table. Â Finally the pizza come and you take the first bite, and it is not that amazing. Â It's just regular pizza with fresh mozzarella and fresh basil. Â Grimaldi's famous tomato sauce does not taste that different from a regular sauce. Â Although, the slices were very crunchy due to the fact that the pie has a thin crust and bottom. Â The whole pie cost $16 for the large pie (18 in.). Â It is $2 extra for extra mozzarella or sauce, or basil. Â  Service was decent. Â The waiters were really busy trying to serve all the tables that we were forgotten at times. Â The check took a while to get to us as well. Personally, the pizza was not that special for me to wait in line and pay more than double of what I would pay at Two Bros.

Absolutely wonderful! Great laid back place - Started with a lemon zest doughnut, moved on Chicken and Waffles and finished with a Sour Cherry and Pear Crumble pie. Great find in BK - amazing food, very reasonably priced - oh, a few local beers to choose from too. My new brunch fave!

I came here on a Friday night for date night and it was pretty easy to get a table at a reasonable time the day before. Â What I initially liked about this place is they don't cram tables too close to each other. Â The service overall was fine, although they request that you put in all orders (appetizers and entrees) in at the same time, which makes me feel a bit rushed--I like to figure out each course one at a time. Â  We started with the squash dumplings and the tuna tartar. Â I really liked both! Â The squash dumplings were really flavorful, I couldn't stop mopping up the sauce. Â The tuna tartar was tasty, but it's more creamy that the normal citrus/lighter kinds. Â It comes with are big, homemade potato chips. For my main course I had the halibut--wow! Â It was very light, perfectly flaky and soft and the fregola and veggies were the perfect accompaniment. Â It's that kind of entree you order time after time. Â My boyfriend had the cavatelli which was good, but didn't blow my socks off. Â It was also on the heavy side with the sausage and ricotta. Would definitely come here again--every dish was a hit!

I was deciding between 3 and a 4 stars, and decided to round up and give Thelma 4 stars, and then switched it back to 3 stars after writing out the full review. After realizing our first choice brunch place had way too long of a wait, we were intrigued by the appearance of Thelma on Clinton to the casual passerby. Though the restaurant only had a few patrons inside at 12:30pm on a Saturday and looked more like a bar scene than a brunch spot, we decided to give it a try. We were looking for a place where four friends could catch up and hear one another without yelling over the rest of a crowded restaurant, so this looked like our spot. The ambiance was great, the staff was friendly, the prices were affordable, the only slight disappointment was the menu/food. There were about six brunch options on the menu (mostly involving some variation of eggs: a quiche, a frittata, eggs Benedict, etc.), and no substitutions were allowed. I ordered the frittata. It was alright, though clearly a slice cut from a full frittata and warmed up separately. The side salad was delicious, but I didn't care much for the potatoes. Overall, the ambiance and restaurant itself are adorable, but the food (I believe my fellow diners felt similarly) was not fantastic.

Indeed - the falafel is probably the best in Manhattan (and best high-end in the city; there are other contenders, all in lower price ranges, but whatever). Never dry. Never bland. But! I joined yelp to spread the word about the Sabich. Once upon a time, I was one of those freaks who hated eggplant, creamy sauces, and hard-cooked egg. Now that I have had a Sabich, I don't even know that person anymore. Sabich. Sabich! Of course I would appreciate it if they took cards, and had shorter wait times. But a line out the door, while annoying, is usually indicative of greatness. As it is here. Oh, and not that this information should be relegated to afterthought status, but their pitas are SO fresh, floury, and delicious.

Not at all what I was expecting. Small, simple menu with options, and pretty great prices (especially considering how much food was served). Service was excellent; they answered any questions and even replaced my chopsticks within a minute of seeing mine fall from the table. When I looked at the menu, I thought I wasn't going to enjoy my food but I actually got full before finishing, and was annoyed that I wasn't hungry enough to eat more. Food tips: Pork buns are a must. Samurai Ribs are awesome. For dessert you should try the mascarpone/green tea ice cream cheesecake thing. So good. Other useful information: It can be kind of loud, so not the best place to go in situations where you need to talk (first dates, for business, etc). Also, every time I go I end up spending a lot of money- but the prices aren't crazy, I just always end up ordering a lot of food and sake.

A great place to eat after walking the Highline in NYC. Just a few steps from the 26th street exit, you can walk up from the Village and wind up here for a great meal. Three things: very good food prepared individually (no assembly line); owner very knowledgeable about Argentinian wines, which were fabulous, and the inside is not too loud, cosy and not heavily refrigerated. How many places in NY can say that? I enjoyed trying some wines I would not usually come across. Everyone raved about the Grilled octopus appetizer. Spices and seasoning were interesting and not overdone, and if you don't like your food overly salted but properly seasoned this is a great plus. Pork chop was extremely large (if you are hungry); the Bronzino was very elegant. Mushroom pasta very good with real mushroom flavor, and the Vegan butternut squash soup was superb, although served too hot. Good selection of single malts and other drinks. You feel you are in a place where the staff have the passion for food. Finally, one of the best crÃ¨me brÃ»lÃ©es I have ever had. Would go again.

The cheeseburger is very common, nothing especial. Foods are down-market product but the steak is thick. For the same price you can have better burger in NYC. However maybe it's a good place to have a drink because of the local atmosphere.

If you are looking to eat traditional, and GOOD Vietnamese food, Do not go here.. It was pretty unsatisfactory and extremely overpriced for the food that they serve.. The sauces were tasteless and/or non-existent. We paid $19 for dry rice noodles with a teensy bit of crab meat and nothing else!!! I wouldn't even serve someone that for free in my own home. What a rip off.. I really cant understand any of the positive reviews.. We ordered 5 things all together and not one of them stood out. I have eaten a lot of Vietnamese food, and this was possibly the worst.. If you gonna charge me that much dough, you better be serving your A-Game , Falansai.. Sorry, but.. You just dont cut it. Will never go back there
Well worth the wait.

Still one of my favorite restaurants in New York City. Service is always top notch here, welcoming and never overly stuffy nor pretentious. Waitstaff is both accommodating and attentive. The pizza makes excellent use of the wood burning oven and the TC burger still rivals some of the best in the city. The space and decor itself is beautiful.

This place is awesome. It's super quaint and right down the street from duckduck, so naturally it's great after you've filled up on happy hour drinks. It's very small, so keep that in mind if you're in large groups. Also, it's definitely on the quiet side. Other than that, the staff is incredibly friendly and willing to help out with any questions. I was in a state of starvation when I went, so I didn't peruse the menu very long. My friend recommended the spicy pork sandwich. It was delicious. Just what I needed. The bread is super thick and yummy. Also, the spice had a solid amount of heat and flavor. I really liked their use of cilantro. I will definitely be back here to check out more of their options!

I have been coming here for many years - before the cookbook was like an number one best seller, and a hit on Amazon, before wearing table cloth shirts and ironic facial hair was the norm for men age 20 - 40 in Brooklyn everywhere *cool*, basically before you could open a "Brooklyn-Aesthetic-Theme Restaurant" (which of course you can now...even in Manhattan, need proof, go to Fedora, or the Gingerman in MIDTOWN) and once upon a time this was the original...all those things I mentioned exists because places like Frankie's were soooo good everyone wanted to copy it. Unfortunately their perennial popularity has lead to a bit of a slide in quality. But it's still damn fine. So go, just don't mind if they got a little pompous, it's part of the look.

I think Public is one of those solid 4-star restaurants. Quality, but nothing mind blowing. So my friend and I ordered: Appetizer: Fried Hama Hama oysters with the wasabi-yuzu dipping sauce - Amazing! Probably my favorite dish of the night, highly recommended. The fried oysters are wrapped with some kind of leaf and then dipped in to the sauce which all just works so well together. Mains: Venison over dumplings and salsa, and duck breast with a sesame soy dressing - Venison and duck breast were both super tender, but the overall dish was okay. The complements to the dishes (like the dumplings with the venison and the chips with the duck breast) were good. Dessert: Chocolate hazelnut panna cotta - Really standard, wouldn't really recommend it, kind of regretted not going for the Hokey Pokey ice cream My main takeaway for the restaurant: appetizer and cocktails were my favorite part, mains could have been done better, loved the ambiance, and would try here again for brunch. Cheers :)

Wait for Han Dynasty was 35 minutes this past Saturday night - having been turned away with estimated wait times of 2 hours before, we decided to suck it up and wait. They'll text when your table is ready, and the manager told me over the phone that they were opening up reservations sometime in October, so watch out for those. We ordered: Spicy cucumbers, Dan dan noodles, Wontons in chili oil, Dry pepper style chicken, and Double cooked style fish. Spicy cucumbers: mother of god, these are a feat of wizardry. Diced cucumbers in soy sauce, rice vinegar, sesame oil, red pepper flakes and sesame seeds... So simple and so friggin addictive! Must order. Dan dan noodles: Really generous portion of doughy, chewy noodles with a ground pork and scallions. These were actually pretty spicy and very very good. Dry pepper style chicken: Fried morsels of chicken that were crispy on the outside without being too greasy. They're marked as a 8/10 on level of spiciness but I found them to be manageable, mostly because I was careful to eat around the slivers of dry chili peppers that they saute with the dish. Wontons and double-cooked style fish were ordinary and not on the agenda for next time. In terms of authenticity, I will grant that the appetizers are authentically Szechuan. Less convinced about the entrees: Han Dynasty's mains are laid out in a variety of cooking styles and then you pick the protein that you want in that style. It's a little too "one-size-fits-all" for me, and reminded me a bit of the Chinese-American takeout mantra: do you want that with beef, chicken, shrimp, or tofu? I would also suggest that you get one non-spicy dish (like the Three Cup Chicken). After a few bites, the "numbing" quality of the Szechuan will start to take hold, and everything will taste like a one-note shade of FIERY.

I want to start off by saying my Fiance loved this food and I'm sure he would rate it differently. But as a Venezuelan I was disappointed with the arepas. The rice and beans were average. I have heard many good things about this place but I have to say it was just average to me.
goddamn, those fuckin' pancakes. Also, if you aren't prepared to wait at least an hour, don't go.

I'll preface this review by saying that the rating is high because the food is so cheap. The food itself is home made and pretty standard. The restaurant itself is essentially a hole in the wall with a few barstools fro customers who choose to eat in. There's one guy taking orders and you'll catch a glimpse of the woman who makes the dumplings. The dumplings are usually precooked and just waiting there for customers (they'll heat them up, of course, on the stove). You can get your dumplings steamed or fried. DEFINITELY GO WITH THE FRIED BECAUSE IT'LL TASTE MUCH BETTER AND YOU WON'T END UP BEING JEALOUS OF YOUR FRIENDS. Add a little bit of soy sauce and these dumplings might become your everyday meal especially because 4 dumplings can fill you up quickly.

Excellent restaurant. I'm originally from Caracas but have live in DC for over 24 years. I was thrilled to find this spot. The food, ambiance and price were great. I had tequenos for appetizer, a Reina Pepia arepa for main dish and shared a cachapa. The drink of choice, Polar beer. This place reminds me of the many low-key restaurants in Venezuela. I will definitely come back when I'm in NYC.

One of the greatest date nights we've ever had. Real, substantial Italian food in a beautiful atmosphere and friendly service. They donated a certificate to the non-profit I work for, so they have a good sense of community! I would recommend it for ANY occasion, and for people looking for real, high-quality food that takes you on a trip to Italy!

Get the full pound. You really, really, really won't regret it. However, if having a single serving, always get the sandwich. Pickled cucumbers are good. Sweet potato Casserole is a must-try, rich and flavorful. Skip the burnt ends as an entree and get the baked beans instead, and the broccoli salad is solid. Do not have the sweet corn and edamame salad, probably the only disappointing thing on the menu.

I've tried, but I cannot think of a better way to spend a lazy Saturday morning in the company of old and new friends than brunch at Freeman's. We were in the city for Bike New York weekend and friends of friends recommended this place. We were a party of eight, plus a baby, so the restaurant reserved the Wine Room for us. Â ASK FOR THE WINE ROOM. Beautiful, romantic, intimate setting: a rustic wooden table, gorgeous fresh flower arrangements in homey mason jars, surrounded on all sides with cellared bottles but with plenty of room to get in and out. Their brunch cocktails are lovely: I enjoyed the French 75 and Death in the Afternoon, both champagne-based, and several friends raved about the grown-up Popsicle drink (a Popsicle made with tequila and raspberry purÃ©e, served in a glass of champagne.) The food was incredible: We started with a couple of artichoke dips, which were crusty on top, creamy within, just the right blend of decadent cheeses and wholesome artichoke hearts. The toasts were pleasantly crispy but chewy enough not to shatter into pieces with each bite. Also sampled the Riders on Horseback, a goat-cheese-stuffed date that's wrapped in bacon and broiled until crispy and salty-sweet. Wow. Â  Main courses: everyone's were superb, but I especially enjoyed the roasted asparagus topped with eggs and spicy hollandaise (perfect over-easy eggs, whites barely set and yolks liquid and golden) and the toasted cheese-arugula sandwich (gorgeous char-kissed toast giving way to an avalanche of cheese, held together with a spicy arugula web.) This Baltimore girl gives extra points for Old Bay chips, too, especially when they're fried in-house. The side of bacon I ordered was not crispy as requested, but I think that's just because it was cut too thick! It was not limp, however -- chewy and meaty. Â I ate one piece and my husband gobbled up the others. Service was attentive, but not smothering: several staff helped us, and all were helpful and apologetic about the lighting (it was a little flickery and dim, but honestly, that just added to the ambience!) Tip was included for a large party, which was fine by me, and I especially appreciated that they told us this rather than letting us double up unknowingly. I hesitated about giving five stars (I'm picky) but honestly, I can't think of a thing they could have done better. Â It was a a wonderful meal, reasonably priced by New York standards, and I'll be back as soon as I can!

Wouldn't say everything here is Cuban, what I would say is that everything is here is pretty darn good. Had the lomo saltado short ribs. That's some good tender meat right there. Also tried the lechon sandwich. Also some good stuff. Was going to pass on dessert, but our waitress, who was really nice, convinced me to try the torrejas de oliva. Its like a bread pudding with a brulee top. Excellent. What is also great about this place is that its pretty affordable and 24hr. I would totally come here instead of a diner or mott street.

Picked up a few rotisserie chickens, ribs, and shrimp fried rice for the football games this Saturday. Â Great food, great value. Â The chicken really stood out, juicy and delicious. Â The ribs were good. Â Shrimp fried rice was recommended by a friend, and did not disappoint. Â It was light, not greasy, and loaded with good quality/fresh shrimp. Â Get the extra green sauce (30 cents per small container, or $3 for half a quart container). Â It's got a little heat and goes great with everything. Â I'll be back!

Good food, good service, good price. I haven't been able to make it here for the prix fixe dinner, but it sounds like a great deal. 15 bucks for an appetizer and entree. One day, I will have my way with the prix fixe dinner, but for now I'm content with paying 13-16 bucks for a delicious pasta dish. I called early in the day to make an appointment for 7pm, and even though our entire group did not show up until about 8 o clock that night, they were fine with seating our incomplete group. We ordered just about every pasta dish, and they were all very good. However, the breaded chicken is very dry, and tastes like a huge chicken nugget. The portion was decent for me, but most of the guys agreed they could have gone for more. This place would be a great for a romantic candle lit dinner.

Oroshi tonkatsu is awesome here at Ootoya. It has just the right amount of crispiness as well as flavor. The pork belly wrapped in tomato is very flavorful. Tofu salad is a great choice for appetizer. Earl grey ice cream and anmitsu makes for an exquisite dessert selection. Overall, wonderful experience.

This place was fine; the decor is decent. It's obvious that they tried hard but it somehow misses the mark. I found the restaurant somewhat soulless. Â The space was too tight - they set the tables very close to one another (about 6" -8" inches on either side) and we couldn't really concentrate on our food/conversation because we were overwhelmed by other people's convos on either side of us. Â The sun shone through the windows and was a bit blinding for those seated facing the window. The prices are a bit inflated. We started off with a crumpet with bacon marmalade. Â For $5 it was a disappointment - it wasn't spongy. Instead it tasted somewhat bland and dense. Â The marmalade was also kind of tasteless. Â The portion are small. Â The salt cod hash was solid. Â The baked eggs were pretty good. Â  The coffee, though only $1.75, came in a small mug, and was not bottomless. Â This is unusual for brunch (and unacceptable, actually). Â We're happy to see new restaurants open up in the area, but I think we will head back to Tom's for brunch in the future.

I have a general rule when I go to restaurants--the patron, if possible, should be accommodated. I'm not talking about ridiculous requests. Or demanding something that cannot be even considered possible in a rational universe. But as a person who works hard for her money and feels like it is a special experience to eat in a restaurant, I expect the place I spend my hard earned money to try, on even a slight level, to try to accommodate simple menu requests and diversions. Where shall I begin with this horrible experience? Well, we walked into the cafe for the first time. We took a menu and saw that it was limited, but we decided to go with a panini and the gnocchi. So then this is when we entered the Twilight Zone. We asked the man behind the counter, we saw the female chef/owner walking around behind him, if the panini sandwiches were "pre made" and he said, "No, they are made on the spot" which made us happy. We wanted to make a custom panini--not something radical and something you can get at any restaurant. The man looked shocked. He shook his head. "No, you cannot choose what you want on it." We stood there confused. "Why can't you just put chicken and cheese on it??" He just stared at us. He was very odd. He seemed scared of the request. But he goes and ask the chef/owner and comes back and says, "We can make this sandwich and names one...." and we say, "But we don't want THOSE ingredients....we just want this and this...." VERY simple request. And he just said, "No. Cannot do that." Ummmm.....why?? Why if your sandwiches are made from scratch can't you make a sandwich with what we want in it?? Then we ask for a side of fresh mozzarella. And again he says, "No. Cannot do that." You cannot slice some cheese for us??? Just a side of cheese?? "Nope. We cannot....." And so on and so on........... And then I saw the sign. The sign that says don't ask for anything different. No changes to the menu. This type of diva/controlling chef/owner behavior is a REAL turn-off and something as a paying customer that I will NOT tolerate. I was not being demanding. Really, really ridiculous. Will not deal with chefs who are such control freaks.

I keep thinking restaurants in Brooklyn will be cheaper than restaurants in NY, but that's totally not the case. Regardless, had a great experience here. We got the tomatoes and basil tostini and the white beans tostini - both were excellent. Had the penne a la vodka as my main - delicious and a good portion. Only slightly annoying because I don't eat meat and asked if I could swap out prosciutto for vegetables, but they said I had to pay extra to swap (from meat to veggies....). We also had cocktails - don't remember what I drank but they were good. Would I schlep all the way to Brooklyn to eat here and pay Manhattan prices? Honestly, probably not. But if I'm ever in the area again (unlikely), then it's worth a visit.
One of my favorites in the city. Â Seriously, why leave Greenpoint when you've got a place like this?

Cheryl's is my usual go-to spot when I'm in the BK because I can always count on them to soothe my palette. My server was great, as were the others. But something that Saturday was different. Maybe it was a bad day, or the cooks were in a funk because there was something off about the food that day. My rum punch is usually the bomb and my starting point. But that day it was weak. The curried mussels were weak and not as flavorful as they usually are. My broiled pork chop was superb! Even the mango salsa was good, merging well with the flavor of the pork. I wasn't feeling the roasted potatoes. They were rubbery and dry. All in all the atmosphere was warm and inviting as always, which made up for the imperfections of my food. I'll go back though, their overall track record with me is good, so I'll forgive a one time offense, which I hope will never happen again.
Good drinks liked the cucumber Ginger soda. Accommodates large groups, but the room sounds like a kids' cafeteria. Â  Flounder was great!

The food is decent and the decor is very pleasant. Unfortunately one waiter's rudeness made me never want to return. I was having some wine and an appetizer with a friend on a Saturday night. For some reason the waiter decided that we aren't going to any more and told us that he needed the table before even offering us the opportunity to order more food or drinks. We had only been there for approximately 20 minutes and still had wine in our glasses. This is unacceptable. Oh, and not once were our waters refilled. Restaurant service 101...

Yes, I am Asian. Yes, I eat a TON of Spanish food. So having lived in a predominantly Spanish neighborhood my whole life and being a foodie, you learn to explore your surroundings. I never really cared where the origin of my food came from, at the end of the day, good food is good food. I can say that I have eaten Colombian food, Mexican food, Ecuadorian Food, Dominican Food, Puerto Rican food, Peruvian food , Argentina food, Uruguayan food , and Cuban food. Rincon Criollo is a Queens institution for Cuban cuisine and it's been open for the better half of 60 years. The decor seems like something straight out of Cuba and the service is always welcoming and friendly. Btw, their Bday celebrations at the restaurant is very "festive." I have yet to order the super popular dishes here, the Arroz con Pollo or the Ropa Vieja, think I will try these when I get a group of people to go. Oh, and this place was featured on Diners, Drive- Ins and Dives. The food: Croquetas de Jamon- This dish is so near and dear to my heart. A block away there used to be the Broadway Sandwich shop and the croquettes here tastes exactly like the ones in the other restaurant. These are essentially ham croquettes, but don't think of the regular ham you normally think of, it's more like ground up pieces of pork with mashed potatoes with a slightly crunchy exterior. I love it. yelp.com/user_local_photâ€¦ Ropa Vieja- shredded beef in tomato sauce. This dish is one of Cuba's most popular dishes and it didn't appeal to me in the beginning because I am not a fan of any kind of shredded meats. The dish here is really good. The broth is slightly sweet and the beef is really tender, this is a must order. Rabo Encendido- It's essentially an oxtail stew in a tomato based broth. The dish is really nice, the oxtail is nice and tender and the tomato adds a touch of acidity. The oxtail itself is a good size and the meat is pretty easy to get to. The order comes with two sides, I chose the tostones which is good but could be a little crispier and the Moros y Cristianos. yelp.com/user_local_photâ€¦ yelp.com/user_local_photâ€¦ Lechon Asado- I ordered this roast pork dish on Sunday and boy is it a lot of food. The sides I picked were Moros y Cristianos and Yuca con Mojo. Moros y Cristianos is kinda like purple rice with beans already cooked inside with small chunks of pork, this is probably one of my fav rice dishes. The Yuca con Mojo is cassava with garlic sauce, the garlic is intense, don't exhale too hard lol The cassava is really soft and the garlic is nice but it's a little plain. The pork is nicely cooked, too bad there is no crunchy skin =( It seems like a nicely cooked roast pork dish, it is on the salty side though. yelp.com/user_local_photâ€¦ Sandwiche Cubano- The Cubano sandwich here is solid. It's a big ass pressed sandwich with ham, roast pork, swiss cheese, mustard and pickles. It's a nice sandwich but I remember thinking the bread could be a little better. Bistec De Puerco Empanizado- breaded pork steak. It's a pork cutlet that is really pounded out. The flavors are nice and the pork is really tender but the dish was on the greasy side. Bunuelos Rincon Criollo- they are essentially doughnuts in a simple syrup. The doughnuts are made of yuca, sweet potato and anise. The doughnuts are nice and crisp, the inside is nice but it's a little redundant. And the simple syrup is a tad sweet. yelp.com/user_local_photâ€¦

I came here with my parents after having walked by the newest incarnation of restaurant for months. I thought it looked fairly tacky and probably not worth trying, but after the reviews we decided to give it a shot. We ordered a spread of appetizers and two entrees: Octopodi- grilled octopus which I thought was not over cooked and nicely grilled, but not spiced to a point which complimented the meat 3.5/5 Calamari- one of the best I've had! Perfectly cooked and lightly breaded, oiled, and spiced, but the tomato sauce was lacking distinction and punch 4/5 Spanakopita- amazing! The best I've ever had. Very crunchy filo on top, equally cheesy and bright, lemony, not overpoweringly spinachy, garlic, and firm filo on the bottom. 5/5 Saganaki graviera- lightly fried cheese, which I thought was nicely cooked and not greasy, but also underwhelming. 3/5 Pikilia- overall I believe that the spreads were alright, nothing bad but nothing impressive. Usually, we order something similar at Niko's in Westchester (see my review) and they are no more. They were all nice, but none had any punch. There wasn't enough garlic in the tzatziki and I haven't had such underwhelming taramosalata before. 3/5 Traditional Greek salad- I don't know where people have been, but traditional Greek salads don't include lettuce. However, it seems to be a theme these days, so maybe it's an Americanized bastarding trend. Anyway, my dad wanted to order a large and the very nice, tall, ponytailed, heavily accented (swoon) waiter asked if we were sure (very quickly, just as he said everything else). I had forgotten to tell them everyone said the portions here are huge and they weren't kidding! We got a small and it was delicious with not too much olive oil, particularly the feta. They even added pepperocini! Mmm... 5/5 Baby shark- I was really excited to try this, as I have never had shark before, let alone baby shark. Unfortunately, I was underwhelmed. The meat was grilled perfectly, it was very fresh, and came with a nice side dish (which I regretted, but again was my own fault) of horta/dandelion greens (I hasn't had this before either) and some of the garlic potato dip. I think they gave me an entire baby shark and almost 98% of it is now in my refrigerator...3.5/5 Special Halibut- this was also very fresh, but not necessarily the best piece of fish from the market. For the most expensive item we ordered, it certainly wasn't special, except for the size. Complimentary galaktoboureko!!!- everyone gets their own and trust me you don't want to share. It's heavenly, delicious, extremely gustatorily titillating. Just go and try it, there is nothing more for me to say. 6/5 The service was excellent, our waiter very polite and properly (not overly) attentive, as were the bus boys. When we arrived everyone in the entrance greeted us, a very nice change from many places. The decor is clean, but lacking any kind of pizazz. The storefront needs to be modernized and they need to do something so the place isn't so noisy when there aren't too many people there. However, most of these things don't affect my rating. Overall, I think this is a solid restaurant and would return to try a few more of their dishes. The prices seem steep, but I swear, the portions are worthwhile.
Delicious food. Fantastic drinks. Bartender was on point. Cozy decor. I'm a BIG fan. You'll find me here, a lot in the future.

Started with the pink picket fence (gin, lemonade, and chambord...yum) and the dilly green beans. Not a match made in heaven because the drink was sweet and the beans were spicy, but each were fantastic. We both ordered the smothered chicken biscuit sandwich on a recommendation from a friend, and were both glad we did. Great, fattening, delicious southern comfort food in New York City. We're just disappointed we forgot to get some pickles to go.

Just went last night. Â Knew nothing of the place but was enticed by the Yelp reviews - and yup, lived up to it. Â The duck was heavenly! Was clueless as to "Scotch egg" so tried that too. Â Hmm, quite nice (tho' heavy, complete with bacon, so definitely share.) And, following reviews, we also go the meatloaf (something I would never otherwise order) which was indeed quite nice - or, should I say, "is" since had to take 3/4 of it home given the Scotch egg & the large portion of duck. Â Note: their wine by the glass is a bit pricey. Â But nice overall, including ambience & great service. Â Enjoy!

This is really as good as it gets in Brooklyn. Actually, the best. Â I live not far from Glasserie so I've been there a few times for dinner and a few for brunch and have never been disappointed with the food or the service. Â I've brought friends and colleagues and everyone has loved the food and the ambiance. Â The flavors in all the dishes are so surprising and as far as I'm concerned, the portions are perfect. Â I'm not American so I'm actually relieved when a restaurant brings me dishes that aren't piled with too much food that I can't hope to finish. I love this place and have no trouble recommending it to those who can truly appreciate excellent food and who esteem creativity found in all the details of well executed menu.
Truly, as good as it gets. Â  As with all AMAZING dining experience, you must plan ahead!! Â Ippudo is truly truly truly worth the wait.

This place was pretty good! I'm not even big on toppings on my pancakes but these blueberry pancakes were really delish! I also got the fried chicken sandwich. It came with fries and coleslaw. No complaints on that either. Oh you may want to add more of their special mayo to the sandwich. I'll be back to this place!

I went to Lucali because of the reviews I read here on Yelp. Â  When it comes to ordering your pizza you choose from a list of fresh ingredients, don't pass up on the basil. Yes Yelp, the pizza is very good, perhaps not my favorite in the city, but definitely worth the trip. However, I think the real stand out here is the *CALZONE*. Â We ordered the medium. Â Which was BIG. Â I can't imagine what a large would look like. Â But it was perfectly cooked and pre-sliced for the three of us. Â  I can't remember what we chose for the ingredients but the ricotta was sublime. Â It's been about two weeks since I went and it still haunts me. Â I mean, damn man, thats a good calzone. The restaurant was crowded but not too loud, we showed up at the tail end of dinner service and had to wait about 10-15 minutes for a table. Â  A great atmosphere, very friendly service. It's obvious the chef has his heart in this business and I'll be back soon with more friends.

If awesome were a bar, it would be this place. Incredibly sophisticated little bar that only serves beer & wine and eliminates the need for any "I just turned 21 and can't hold my alcohol crowds". Considering the place is cash only you do leave saying "did I spend that much?" but since the place is dim and the mood is set its much easier to leave saying "I'm so in looove". GREAT crowds. The staff is extremely polite and easy to strike up a conversation with if you have difficulty picking a beer or wine, although if you have never had Delirium Beer or Chimay I highly suggest! Definitely a fan and would make the trip from Jersey anyday and any season. Small and Cozy - the perfect fit for one of those "need to get out of my apt nights but don't feel like hitting up a club" Â you'll leave satisfied everytime : ) Girls, best part - flat shoes and casual attire are almost a must!

Enjoyed dinner at Basso 56 Monday evening and everything was Â  wonderful. We were seated promptly and the the service and the food were excellent in all respects. My wife's sea food risotto and my gnocchi with ox tail ragu were both outstanding as were the owners wine pairing with each. The complementary olives and bread with olive oil was a nice touch. Â We were treated as family on our anniversary night and nothing could have been better. Thank you Basso 56 - we will be back on our next trip to NYC!

This place was so fun that we came to try the burger and wound up staying all night. The burger was delish, the perfect size, and very tasty, but I can't recall any other details about the burger at this time. We also had a million pork slaps. They were great tasting and fun, and did the job. Even though it was pretty chilly outside, we stayed on the back deck for many hours, and the heating lamps did the job of keeping us warm. The atmosphere back there was very communal and rambunctious. We had a great time, and I have no complaints.

Great place....I'm so glad it is my neighborhood but for others it is worth the trip....However, why-oh-why have they stopped offering their amazing prix fixe until 7PM....I haven't moved to Miami yet, so I don't want to eat at 6PM....Please restore the prix fixe through 7PM......merci!
I took my girl friend for birthday we had good time at Sanford's they have Greek American menu we love this restaurant in our neighboord food and servis is good plus 7/24.

My wife and I stopped in 2 hours before closing and the place was hopping. They host/waiter pointed at us and two other waiting couples to come with him. He was going to seat us all at the same time...we followed him and he led us to a big circular table. We had to eat at a table with a bunch of strangers. Fine, no big deal, we can handle this. But, just for the record, they do not do this in China in sit down restaurants. Only in a few NYC Chinese restaurants. When one of the couples complained about being seated together with strangers the waiter was very exasperated and loudly exclaimed there is now where else to sit. They begrudgingly sat down. When ordering, we went through several unavailable items until we got to an item they actually had, which ended up being the duck over rice. They wouldn't sell us half a duck, but only duck over rice. They claimed they ran out of the half duck...which makes no sense since they still had duck over rice available. So, since nothing else looked appetizing, we shared that one dish. They brought out tea, but my wife's tea had floating thingies, perhaps old rice, in it, so she didn't feel comfortable drinking it. The duck was Very Very Very fatty. There was minimal meat. I've never seen so many pieces of duck where the amount of fat was greater than meat. The rice was flavored with a touch of soy sauce. The dish was not worth any money. In fact, they ought. To pay me for the wasted time and Â stomach space. Â It was gross. We quickly got up, paid, and left. Bottom line: Do not go here to eat. Unless you want to feel like a farm animal being herded around and eating slop.
WOOOOWWWWWWWWW yeah that is all I have to say. I LOVE the burgers, the bowls, and especially the sushi. Oh I think I forgot to mention the sweet potato tempura fries. YUM!

I'm giving four stars just for the spicy tofu banh mi I had today. Mooncake may just be the go to lunch place for me when I'm in our NYC office. It's caddy corner from it for Pete's sake. Why not, right?! The banh mi was all the goodness of spicy sweet tofu, the crunch of pickled daikon and carrots and the freshness of cucumbers and cilantro. The bread had the right crunch that didn't rain crumbs all over you or tear the roof of your mouth, and yet soft and chewy inside without being doughy or soggy. I also had the Thai iced tea which was also good. I would have preferred Thai iced coffee, but that wasn't on the menu or I missed it completely. Next time I'll have to try the shrimp vermicelli salad and ginger iced tea. I placed my order online for pick up and paid by credit card. Although, I understand if you dine in it's cash only. I placed my order at 1:12 and got an ETA of 1:17. Left at 1:20 to walk across the street and sure enough, it was all packed and ready for me. It couldn't have been any easier.

I used to frequent this place when I was around the area. Â They give you a pretty good serving and it's not too spicy. Â They just serve the typical curry rice platter with either fried pork, shrimp, or chicken, all of which are quite tasty. Â Occasionally they'll hand out coupons to get a free topping. Â That is always a welcomed addition.

Given its Bourdain pedigree (which I didn't know about before coming) and the friendly guy at the bar yapping away in Japanese with a Japanese couple, I wanted to like it, but it was just meh. Â Had the wasabi shumai - certainly delivered the wasabi kick, but was otherwise just ok. Â Then had the tofu steak and it was covered with mozzarella cheese, and surrounded by watery "sauce" which is water from the tofu diluting the teriyaki sauce. Â Really meh. Â I've had some GREAT tofu steaks in LA so hard to be ok about this. Â Scraped off the cheese to just get at the tofu, which was ok. Â Finally, had the mentaiko fried rice, which was the best of the bunch. Â This was decent, but not something to come back for. At least the wait wasn't long - I got there at 11:30pm.

One of the best for 20 years. Whether for a special occasion, a romantic dinner or an important business lunch, Gramercy Tavern is the spot. Â Food is excellent, service is totally professional and the atmosphere is amazing.
Akumaru ramen and pork buns. Â I actually wake up craving this stuff, its like crack. Love this place, I reco going late for lunch 3pm -- and you wont have to wait an hour for soup.

This is one of the mom-and-pop ethnic eats treasures of NYC. Â The menu is quite limited -- if you aren't wild about banh mi, there's not much point in schlepping to Sunset Park -- but it's as close to Vietnam as you're likely to get around these parts. Â And they do have some non-banh mi dishes. Â A little known joy is their durian shake. Â If you haven't tried durian, Google it before purchasing.

Unmistakably, unequivocally, and undoubtedly the BEST pizza I've had so far. This is my second venture to this pizza heaven, and it was just as remarkable as my first experience. The old-fashioned pizza is a MUST and this time around, my friend and I decided that the other half would be covered with mushrooms. As a reminder, the only way to enjoy your pie, is to pair it with nice, cool Peroni, and you should have one while you wait as well. Double your pleasure, double your fun!!! The crust is baked to perfection, not overdone but just charred just enough to have a detectable crisp. The pie isn't too doughy so it's a slightly, thin, crisp, flavorful pizza. The sauce is composed of ripe, robust tomatoes and is very, very fresh. The cheese is not too oily and salty like some pizza parlors. A combination so delicious that I'm salivating juts at the thought of it again. Cheese and tomato sauce in perfect harmony coupled with a thin crust that's unlike anything you've ever tasted before. Then add a Peroni (or three) to facilitate the digestion of the cheese, there my friend is a complete and absolute recipe for success. The pizza was NOT covered in mushrooms, it was drowned with toppings, mushrooms on top of mushrooms on top of mushrooms. You are forewarned, Adrienne's is a MUST and not for the faint of heart. Your taste buds are about to go into hyper drive, so strap in, grab your fork and spoon, don't be shy and DIG IN. As a reminder: - Adrienne's does not serve slices, onlyfull pies, so come hungry. - Don't forget that plain pizza can also be good pizza, in this case it's SOOOO DELICIOUS. - This place gets pretty packed because it's just so awesome, so plan accordingly and everything should go fine. - Warning: One pie MAY be enough to satiate the appetite of two ravenous human beings but another pie should be keep handy in case of a dire need for more sustenance.

2 of my girlfriends and I went to Perry St for lunch during restaurant week. i had been wanting to try a Jean-Georges resto for some time (preferably for a discounted price). basically, the service was top notch and food was superb. 3 courses......app/entree/dessert: app: burrata cheese app - Â it was good, but i was really craving the rice cracker crusted tuna, which was unavail. entree: cod - DELICIOUS. one of the best fish dishes i've had in a while. dessert: fruit dish - this was my least fave. choco lava cake was a better choice, even for a non-chocoholic. restaurant was beautiful in terms of decor+ location (right on water, overlooking the Hudson). simplistic+white interior was reminiscent of Miami. recommended! service was excellent.

Great pizza. Only waited 30 mins. We had the pepperoni and a white pizza. They were both fantastic. The pizza came out very quickly after we ordered it. It was about a ten minute walk from the subway.

Go on off hours if you want to avoid the insanely long waits, at Monday 1040 AM we were seated right away. Â Having been our first time to this well acclaimed establishment, the lady and I ordered 2 of the more talked about dishes; the blueberry pancakes and the southern breakfast. Â Yes this month (February) is pancake month, but the flavor of the day did not sound appealing, crispy banana something or other. Â The place is located on the LES in which takes me forever to get to being that i live in the UWS. Â But i would say this place is well worth the commute if and only if there is not a long wait. Â  The pancakes are amazing, yes its true fluffy goodness that has a buttery aftertaste. Â The toppings of fresh blueberry and warm maple syrup is also great, and thats coming from someone that doesnt even enjoy blueberries all that much. Â The Southern breakfast was a perfect balance of savory and sweet with our sweet pancake dish. Â It came with cheese grits, fried green tomatoes, eggs, and bacon. Â Sounds pretty standard I know, but man we were amazed at how good everything was. Â The bacon was outstanding, sugar cured and tasted like it was cooked in maple syrup. Â Fried green tomatoes are just OK, and at 7 additional dollars to order as a side, i would skip it. Â Cheese grits and the eggs were both good. Â I also ordered the biscuit with jam, and it is huge, easily able to share with 2 people, I wish it was more put together, instead of crumbling as soon as you touched it. Â The flavor was there, and the jam was very good though. Â The hashbrown side was also ordered and i wish it was more crispy, instead it was almost like a borderline mashed potatoes with a charred skin on top. Yes there were dishes that we loved, dishes we thought could use some improvement, but this place is worthy of taking your out of town guests.

Burger #242: Front 242? I really hate that band. While at dinner #1 (previous review), I was discussing the burger at Minetta Tavern that I had to eat right after. But there happened to be local New Yorker at our table who swore that Minetta was over-hyped and Coner Bistro was THE place to go for burgers in NYC. So being the trusting fellow I am, that's where myself and a coworker walked to right after our Italian dinner. Corner Bistro is basically a bar with a few dirty tables in the back. We ordered the burger, medium-rare, with fries and some scotch. A few minutes later, our burger was presented before us. yelp.com/biz_photos/8XLhâ€¦ It looked simple enough; very light charring, fully melted cheese, and ample bacon. The smell was very homemade, as if someone bought a 5lb tube of 80/20 meat and cooked it on a flat top grill. It ended up tasting just like that as well. The burger was thick, under-seasoned, and uninspired. It was a tad overcooked and not cooked that evenly. The bacon was nice, but didn't fill in the much needed salt gap. yelp.com/biz_photos/8XLhâ€¦ Past that, the fries were pretty bad. Bad enough to be left uneaten by a pair of men who needed something to snack on with their scotch. Overall, it was a lackluster meal that not only failed to deliver on the promise of a great burger, but also left me overcome with desire for a good burger that we left and started walking to Minetta Tavern. To be continued...

I was so excited that there was a new Korean restaurant in town and that it was HUGE with lots of seating, however, I think I got emotional ED, which is to say I got too excited too quickly and was left disappointed. My first time I stopped by for happy hour and sat alone at the bar, downing their $1 oysters. That was great, the oysters were fine, and the bartender was nice. My second time I brought a couple friends for dinner. I was surprised how expensive everything was - I don't mind paying big bucks for food that's worth it, but that really deterred me. I was also surprised how limited the menu was. I got bibimbap per usual, and it was pretty bland. My friends were not impressed with their food either. Â Not many options for non-meat eaters. Wah, wah. Oh well.

Cute little pizzeria with table service. The seating is a bit tight. Â Waitstaff are pleasant. Â Short wine list, reasonably priced. Â Salads were good- we shared a house salad and a Mediterranean salad. They were well dressed. Â Pizzas were very good. Â They are thin crusted, so a large is enough for 2 people. Â There are also small pizzas that serve one. The shroomtown was very good. The 4 cheese white pizza was really good. Â Microwaved chocolate chip cookie and ice cream were unremarkable. Â  Overall a nice, above average place for thin crusted pizza.

Based on one visit, superb experience, hence, review might be impartial. I had poached eggs in chive-pork-gravy sauce. Ohhh, heav(y)enly. Yes, absolutely amazing variation of classic eggs Benedict. This dish is so delicious, I would not mind it being my only brunch option for the rest of my life (I'm crossing my fingers that won't actually happen. I like having options). But, I digress. So, yes, delicious poached eggs on delish biscuit, and topped with somewhat spicy gravy containing pork pieces Â with consistency that resembles sausage.

Love this place, it never dissapoints! Came here yesterday for a date (a party of 2). We did not have reservations and were well aware that we would have to wait because there is always a wait! We were told that it would be a 25-30 minute wait and were pleasently surprised when our table was ready in only 10 minutes. Our waiter Danny was fantastic. He was really helpful, upbeat and fun! We had the Mac Attack to share (A MUST when coming to Cafeteria). I had the fish tacos from the appetizer menu (there were 3 mini tacos) definitely enough as a main course. The garlic green beans were delish! My boyfriend had the lamb burger - medium and it was perfect!! Instead of the regular fries he swapped them for the parmesan fries. For dessert we had the fried oreos based on Danny's reccommendations and he was right! The oreos completely melt in your mouth! AMAZING!

Bar none, the best place I have been to in New York City. Â Been here twice. First, you need to secure a reservation well in advance, especially during the peak hours.
