The decor is exceptional, very modern and a great view anywhere you are seated. The service is equally as wonderful. Both times, our waitress was charming, likeable, kind and cheerful. The first time I went, had a bottle and we had the sommelier help us with choosing a bottle of wine. We pointed to a bottle that caught our eye, and he recommended an even better bottle, within our price range. It was amazing. It was a Venetian wine, Villa Spinosa, Jago Valpolicella Ripasso. The second time, had a glass of the pinot grigio, this was inexpensive (for the place), and very good as well. Both times, we chose the polenta with mushrooms and truffle as an appetizer. This was the greatest thing I have ever tasted in my life. There are really no words. The polenta is separated from the truffle infused mushrooms, and the waitress merges all the ingredients into a round dish. The taste is exceptional, you'll never eat anything as soft and great tasting. This was definitely the highlight and a must-order. I had to taste the infamous spaghetti. I ordered it both times and it is fabulous. Definitely lived up to the hype. While it is not as wonderful as the polenta, it is extremely fresh and very simply tasty. I thought it wouldn't fill me up, but it did. The second time, ordered the baby goat with broccoli rabe and pancetta. This was excellent. The goat melts in your mouth and the broccoli compliments it wonderfully. Overall, an excellent dining experience and I would definitely recommend.

It's all about questionably sanitary cart food at 1 in the morning after 10 shots of soju. Â All you need is the rice (flavorful), chicken (so good), lamb (awesome), white sauce (gotta have it), red sauce (pretty spicy). Â All for less than $7. Â Nuff said.

While exploring around NYC with my friend, I was attracted by the cute little sign "Eataly Gelato". At first we thought it was just a tiny coffee shop with Italian gelato, however we were amazed to see how big Eataly NYC was. It included grocery, restaurants, coffee shop, chocolate store and gelato store. My rating is only based on the gelato section. But I must say that the gelato here was probably the best gelato I've ever had! Especially the hazelnut flavor! The gelato here is simply AMAZING and I will def come here when I visit NYC again!

Either I'm cheap or a savvy traveler, but none the less scanning through tasty looking Groupon Deals in an essential part of my vacation prep. And.... Â oh snap I am glad to have found this place and their delicious dinner that overly filled my belly. Â Scanning the menu I had no clue what a Croque Madam was. It was described as smoked white meat turkey breast, gruyere cheese, with homemade bÃ©chamel sauce & topped with a sunny side organic egg. The intriguing ingredients lured me into ordering it & BAM!!!!! This was one of the best Sandwiches I have ever eaten & upon swallowing my last bite I actually missed the sandwich and longed for another one. Â  The attentive staff, delicious food, strong drinks & money-saving Groupon all have me wanting to return for round 2 at this spot.

We went to Edi & the Wolf on a rainy weekday. We were a party of 14 or so. My experience of the food is that it was OK. The flatbread me and a friend shared was really great. It came out warm and delicious although small it packed together great flavors and made it the highlight of the evening. A few of ordered the same beer the Weihenstephan Hefeweizen. Instead they served us Radeberger Pilsners. We told the waitress and she apologized and brought the correct beer. I ordered the Wiener Schnitzel. The potato salad side and lingonberry jam was quite good. The actual Scnitzel wasn't fried as much as I wouldve liked instead of a nice golden fry it was pretty pale and not very crispy. When it came time to pay the bill comes out and gratuity is not included. So now everyone is trying to figure out what they owe (something I hate when going out in large groups). I wish they would've included the gratuity to make everyones job a bit easier. Instead after a few minutes we are told to get up and figure it out over by the bar. The bar is also very small and we're about 14 aside from that it Â was rude. We spent a good amount of money and shouldn't be hustled out. The food was OK. The flatbread is really great. The service is where they really fell flat. People go out for the experience. Food can be forgettable but a good time is what you want to walk away with.

had a wonderful time at bouley with a group of clients. loved the crisp smell of apples at the entrance and the food was delicious. really enjoyed the ambience of vaulted ceilings and candlelit dinner with fantastic service
Used to work here as a server! This place is one of NY's finest, everytime we go we have the lamb risotto

We have been wanting to eat at Battersby ever since reading about it last year. We made it the number one pick for a weekend trip to Brooklyn, and we are so glad we did. It was the best "tasting menu" we have ever had, with great value for incredible food. Part of the fun with the tasting menu is the element of surprise, and it's clear that the kitchen wants guests to be delighted. The food was inventive, fresh (incredible crudo), summery (tomato and watermelon gazpacho; fresh anise leaves straight from the forest); and well balanced; without being precious. The atmosphere is perfect - simple and cozy, with the emphasis on the food, not the place. Wish we could come here for every date night.

It's like nothing you've ever had before and SO SO good! Throw your ideas of sushi out the window and go try this place. So fresh and unique! The best part - you can stuff yourself to the gills knowing that you're eating healthy, tasty food. JUST GO!

A great East Village hot spot. Â A friend and I stopped by here two Sundays ago. Â I told here "let's go to this cute little place I know - there won't be a wait". Â Wrong. Â  The wait was an hour at noon on Sunday. Regardless, the food is great and the menu is slightly unique. Â If you're a health nut you'll have plenty of options. Â  Service isn't exceptional but nothing to complain about either.

Pretty good! Went around 5:10pm on a weekday, and there was already a line! Wait was about 30 minutes or so for a party of 3, not too bad. Server forgot one of our ramen orders, so points off for that... I ordered the Spicy Totto Ramen. Very good, but the pork was a bit rough. The noodles were a very good consistency. I think I will order the Paitan next time Also, I recommend the spicy tuna don!!! Right amount of spiciness, very refreshing with the slices of cucumber that come with it.

Made an early - 6:30 is early by NY standards - reservation here for myself and my parents. It was the perfect atmosphere for us to catch up and eat well. The hostess/waitress/owner? Seated us immediately and was lovely despite Â the demands of running the entire front of house. My parents go to France often, the atmosphere and in my father's words this place 'truly transports you to France and the only difference is there is a working air con'. Â To start we had Â escargot, country pÃ¢tÃ©, and tomato soup/goat cheese special. For mains the chicken, mussels, and calves liver. I would say the chicken was the star, crispy skin and full flavored. Escargot was delicious and calves liver was cooked perfect, deliciously slightly pink on the inside. The mussels fell a little short, this did not stop me from devouring any my mother didn't find in the creamy white wine broth. Profiteroles and Island capped the night with a ruby port. I love a place that serves ruby though this one was really mild. Will dream of the profiteroles and pass on the Island next time.
So good, Pork Meatballs! love it and it comes with bead!

After wanting to hit this place up for the last couple of years, today was the day. We waited an hour & a half for a square pie & I was prepared to be wowed. Unfortunately the crust was seriously burnt & Mr. D. had to really work the pizza cutter to get through it. No napkins, no fan, and seriously, God Bless Mr. D. because the back story & amount of time he put in is commendable, but he should hire someone & take a break. I saw nary a smile. I wanted to love the pizza but burnt & crunchy is not how I like my pizza. I enjoyed watching him grate the cheese & cut the basil but an hour & a half wait for a pie & $32.00 to boot? Glad I tried it but I won't be going back (I saw him poke at a burnt spot in my pie..maybe he knew...)

One of my favorite place in the city. Been there quite a few times and have been there on various occasions (brunch, dinner, drinks). The food are always made with fresh ingredients. Love their brunch, they use really fresh eggs and have their own versions of mimosas (i believe I've had apple and also blueberry before). I can still remember once ordering a brunch with eggs and lobster and it was so delicious... lobster was sweet and juicy and blended perfectly with the eggs. YUM. For dinner, they generally serve some small bites of amuse bouche, which a lot of times i wish i can get on my dinner plates. The appetizer that stands out is the "egg in a jar", it's a concoction of eggs, cheese, and big pieces of black truffles, all mixed up in gooey goodness, and THEN you dip it in bread. However, you may consider going light on entrees as it is pretty filling, not to mention that it costs close to $40. The entrees are hearty American style, with decent portions and quite a bit of flavor. That is not to say it's boring, but just homey. I'm not a big fan of their evening cocktails, as much as i enjoy their brunch ones. Most of them are fruity infused and pretty light, which is not my cup of tea. The desserts are great, i think i heard some where they have a pretty on par dessert chef. I've had pretty much every dessert on the menu (last i checked) and i can't say i've been disappointed. My favorite is the BANANA BREAD PUDDING. Even though it could be interpreted as a bit on the sweet side, it just tastes so good with the pecan nuttiness and banana sweetness. I can tell you that i've bought many friends there just to have this, and it never disappoint. Â  The environment is chill, laid back, with wooden panels, exposed bricks, and antique items all over. With the candle light, it does come off to be quite a decent atmosphere to go on a date. However, it is still casual/relaxed enough to hang out with a few friends or coworkers . personally, i think i can hang out there from brunch through dinner and then straight into evening cocktails/desserts and still feel at home there. With all that,. i haven't even mentioned the service yet, which is always very friendly (i think we have introduced ourselves to them on a few occasions), laid back, attentive, and never feel rushed. Generally, even with the nicest restaurants, i always find something to complain about. But Marc just hits the spot in almost every area. My suggestion would be to hang out at brunch, sip on a few mimosas, have some great eggs, and stay and relax a while. Oh yeah, did I mention they have a bottomless mimosas? Update: Went to brunch today and had the chilli lobster and eggs benedicts. I always think they have a super under rated brunch, for i never really seen them on any top brunch lists but everything i've had there are always top notch. My only complaint is that they only have brunch on Sundays and it ends with last seating at 2:15 pm, which is quite early. I'm sure i will have many more updates in the future as this is a place i find myself coming back to often.

Good American bistro/seafood place; upscale with laid back vibe and actual space to eat in (ie your neighbor will not elbow sparing with you). Â What more can you ask for in a Manhattan restaurant? Definitely rec.

I came here for a snack after lunch and before dinner. It hit the spot although it wasn't fantastic NYC pizza. I ordered the artichoke pizza. It was over the top and really rich. Think of a pizza with alfredo sauce. I also ordered the sicilian pizza and it was decent, but again nothing too exciting. Service could have been better. The guy behind the counter wasn't friendly. They also reserve all the tables so if you just grab a slice your seating is limited.

Went there for countless times. The food there is soso and I thought the price was ridiculous for the quality I was getting (compare to the other restaurants in Chinatown, you definitely can get the same stuff for cheaper!). The reason why I've went there for countless times is because all my non Asian friends wanted to have Malaysian instead of Chinese. But despite all that, the food aren't bad, but can't say its tasty to have to keep on coming back out of my own will lol...

Thoroughly pleasant wine bar/bistro with French culinary chops and Bay Area spirit to spare. Too many times I had walked by this place assuming it was some overrated or mediocre French place for undiscerning tourists. Lo and behold, they've been open less than two years (and moved into the neighborhood not long before yours truly). The generous happy hour (a flight of any 3 pours from their quality wine menu is only $10--or $6 glasses from a smaller selection) drew me in and I finally checked it out on a date with the SO. We chose to sat at the bar even though it was early bird dinner time and the more intimate tables, as well as the reclaimed funky movie theater seats were all up for grabs. Our waiter (I want to say Alex) looks like one of those guys you're sure you've met before. He was friendly and brisk, with a touch of 'tude, but not of that cliche French waiter stuff. The food ranged from very good (my duck confit) to delicious (the SO's ravioli made of wheat flour stuffed with comtÃ¨ and cottage cheese--a specialty from Valence, no less) to superlative (the escargot gratin appetizer, smothered in garlic parsley bread butter). We didn't even have room for dessert. The prices were medium to medium-high for comparable French bistros, but the quality is there.

Just when sandwiches were getting lame - I Found Num Pang and sandwiches became good again. Start with a toasted long roll and add peppercorn catfish along with sweet soy sauce to make a great sandwich...but wait, there's more - for toppings enjoy some carrots and cucumbers and feel like you can pretend it's healthful and in addition to being the best tarting sandwich you've ever had. Â The service is quick and friendly and the seating upstairs serves its purpose in a hipster sort of way. Â There's beer for sale - so be sure to enjoy one with this delectable dinner or lunch.

This place is just fascinating! For starters, it is HUGE. You walk in and you are immediately absorbed by the large amounts of Italian content all over. There are restaurants, fish markets, butcher shops, cheeses and meats displays, herbs and Olive Oil, wines, places to buy cookbooks, areas to sit down and eat, a rooftop bar, and more! Yes more! You can almost call it an Italian Oasis! Definitely worth checking out. At least for a nice glass of wine on the rooftop (The Birreria). Or if you're a random walking tourist, a noted place to use the restrooms right next to the Flatiron building...

The great restaurant and delivers the most tasty Thai food I have ever eaten. ABSOLUTELY worth the trip into queens. The food is spicy. Waiters are good and cooperative. It tastes real thai food. They have very long menu which you cannot go through in one trip.
Service is quick. Â Quality of meal is very average. Â Ordered chicken shawarma, chicken schnitzel, and vegetable couscous. Â Of the three the shawarma was the better and the vegetables the weakest.

Healthy food, an abundance of vegetarian options, lots of leafy greens, great blended juices and smoothies. I had a hard time deciding what to order, but fortunately my lunch companions let me sample their choices too, so I got to experience a range of Siggy's offerings. Cozy restaurant and good service, with decent prices. Siggy's would be a standout in California, where high quality fresh vegetables are ubiquitous. In Manhattan, it is truly a gem, and worth the trek across town for lunch.

This review is only for the dinner menu. Â Breakfast/brunch may be better. Hubby found this place and so we went there for an early dinner, hoping that they had their breakfast menu all day. They didn't. Â So that made me sad. Â I didn't find anything on the dinner menu that looked all that exceptional. If I had more time in the city I'd have suggested going back for breakfast instead, since those choices did look good I had the curry chicken salad. It was ok. Slightly too salty. Â My 6 year old really enjoyed his mac and cheese, which made me happy ... but since his favorite is Kraft, I'm not sure if that's really saying all that much about the quality. Â (I actually tried it and found it extremely bland. Â I wouldn't order it.) The place was really super loud. Â I could barely hear myself think.

Lucali in Italian means " Delicious Pizza" ... Patsy Grimaldi's and Lucali's are the Heavyweight champions of the world of Pizza. A fight we will never see and a fight we never want to see..... Lets just enjoy the fact Â that NY owns the two best pizza places in the world, and proud New Yorkers can make the claim that the closest contenders are still in NY... but they are distant contenders. Mark keep up the great work!!

Loved the cheddar waffle and the warm, sour cream donut. Wish there was a vegetarian brunch dish calling my savory name (goat cheese and spinach sounded like it would be mediocre), but made my own with the waffle and a side of grapefruit. Have heard about this place since it opened and now will head back in the hopes that the menu changes again and calls me.

Sad to say that recent meals here have fallen short of the once epic meat mayhem that I experienced in years past at Fette Sau. In fact, I dare say I've had better BBQ at Hill Country than what I gnawed on yesterday evening. But before I whine about the pitfalls, I'll wax poetic about the things I love here. The location is prime, right off Metropolitan it's an easy ride from the city and the front picnic tabled alley is perfect for kicking back on a warm summer's day. The staff is always friendly and unpretentious, the selection of bourbons and beers are a nice afterthought. But should you desire to dine here, be sure to get there around 7pm... right before the rush starts and a line out the door forms. Good luck finding a seat to enjoy your carnage as well, since for all the hype it does not inhabit a very large space. As far as your meat options, I found the 1/4 lb of pork rib was juicy but the 1/4 lb of was brisket dry to the point of dehydration and I hardly touched it. My side of Pickle Guys half sours was delicious, though I already knew that those were a winner. I found the potato salad overly oily and the baked beans were both undercooked and ketchupy. The accompanying dinner rolls were straight from the grocery store, but still soft and pillowy. Honey butter as a condiment would have been a nice touch. All this ran my a little over $20 but for anyone with a significant appetite I've seen folks spend upwards of $40/pp. And to be honest, it didn't scratch my carnivorous itch. Perhaps they've been off due to their constant lines and endless hype, but I'm still in search of excellence... and it looks like Dinosaur still has my heart.

Very attractive, dimly lit upscale pub feel. Tables are packed together so you will be rubbing elbows. Our server had the personalty of a cardboard box and should not be working at this type of establishment. Overall the food is good and reasonably priced but the drinks are outrageous. The El Diablo shown on the menu without a price turned out to be $19! Every drink we had was more than the entrees we ordered! The famed burger ($16) itself was 4 Star but with hype I expected better.

I used to enjoy coming here when I moved to the neighborhood seven years ago. Â The food was never mind-blowing, but it was satisfying and I would usually have a pleasant experience (enhanced by libations). Â Now, I find the service pretty spotty; our entrees were forgotten last night and we were offered the dessert menu after appetizers. Â This place just doesn't feel worth going to anymore, no matter the convenience if you live close by.

I celebrated my birthday here two nights ago (and did last year too). Â Yerba Buena is consistently an amazing restaurant. Â Beyond the fantastic food and drinks, Yerba Buena provides a great ambience. Â Every employee makes me feel so special and welcome every time I come. Â  When my boyfriend and I walked in, Angel greeted us with a handshake and sat us at a very cozy booth toward the back of the restaurant. Â Our waiter was very helpful and kind. Â Our waiter and other members of the staff checked on us multiple times throughout the meal to make sure we were comfortable and satisfied. Â At the end of the meal, because it was a special occasion, I was brought a sparking pineapple wedge. Â We asked him to take a picture of us and, since the sparkler had just burned out, they gave us a new pineapple and sparkler (and sang Happy Birthday again!) just for the photo. Â  My boyfriend and I (and the friends we have taken there) highly recommend Yerba Buena. Â You will leave happy and well-fed!

I have been coming to the odeon for a long time now. Â It would be a wrong if I did not leave them a review since I eat here almost every month. Â They have become a staple in my dining life. Â Every visit exceeds my expectations and the consistency is what keeps me coming back. Â I hate going to places where the food taste different each time or the service is hit or miss. The last time I ate here was in early September for dinner on a Thursday night with my boyfriend. Â We always start with oysters (it's our thing now). Â They are fresh and never have any shell pieces. Â I've been to a few top restaurants which I will not name where they are full of shells from poor shucking. Â For my entree I got the pork chop and he got the burger. Â Their pork chop is delicious and worth trying if you like pork. Â It has a good flavor and is very juicy. Only downside but it does not keep me from coming back is the wait for brunch. Â If you come at the wrong time you could be waiting 30-40 minutes. Â If you get dessert try the donuts!! They are AMAZING and worth all the calories.

3.5 stars. America's first pizzeria... so was definitely a "must try" for a foodie who loves pizza. great space with fun atmosphere :) short 15min wait for a sunday lunch luckily. we went with a half n half Large 18" $23 ((White Pizza / Pepperoni,Mushroom,Sausage)) pizza was delicious, but i cant say THE BEST ive ever had to any extent. ricotta on white pizza was fresh and fluffy, but these slices definitely needed marinara sauce to make it yummy! the dough was fresh and fluffy, crust was a lil bland, but pizza overall left me happy :) great service and menu selection.

Excellent restaurant. Â I sampled the alligator bites and was pleasantly surprised by the taste. I also recommend the Seafood Gone Wild and the Fried Cheesecake. Â Don't leave without trying the Fried Cheesecake. Â This place is easy to miss on the outside and I felt the tables were a little close together, but that's normal in the city too. Â I'd definitely go back. Â Bayou is great for a first date or celebratory dinner. Â New Orleans all the way, baby.
Best Conn-style lobster roll EVER. Â I go to their Lobster Truck in the City as often as possible. Â Crazy expensive, but really awsome. Â Just perfect.

Man,....so after a night of Le Bernardin and Wechsler's Currywurst & Bratwurst, my friend and I continued our ridiculous night of eating by finishing it off with Pommes Frites. Â Yes, that's right my fellow Yelpers. Â I went from an epic 3-star michelin 7-course tasting menu, walked over to East Village for German food, and I completed the night with Belgium fare. Â Boo-yah! Â Double Boo-yah! Â I did this only because I was going back to Shreveport in 36 hours. Food (8.5/10) = Got the regular size of fries and not the larger ones because I was watching my weight. Â Got the sweet mango chutney, and the black truffle mayo. Â These sauces are winners. Â I'm a winner. Â I was "bi-winning" Ambiance (7.5/10) = A fun atmosphere to chill out. Â Like how the tables and counter tops have holes for you to put your cones of fries. Service (7.5/10) = Nice and quick. Â Got my fries in no time. Overall Opinion = These fries are hella good. Â What really makes them epic are those sauces I mentioned. Â Go get some pommes frites! Â You don't need to go to Le Bernardin and Wechslers first to appreciate the goodness of these fries.

SURPRISE! Happy birthday, babe. : ] So this year, I decided to treat the boyfriend to Gramercy for dinner. I was a bit apprehensive about it because of our experience at Per Se last year but there was nothing to worry about! The atmosphere is completely different; much more relaxed, warm, welcoming and lively. Glancing at the menu, we leaned toward the tasting menu but I was thinking "eh? warm CABBAGE salad? idk..." I asked the server how the salad was, his reply? "It's AMAZING" Â And so, we went for it, with the boyfriend substituting the veal for the very aged rare steak. I'm very picky with wines because I still don't like how they taste. The server's wine recommendation was great though. I loved the Leitz Riesling! Food was de-li-cious. The scallops and veal were very good. Boyfriend loved his aged steak. The smoked trout was by far the best thing I've ever tasted in my life. Perfect presentation, all the flavors worked very well together. The lobster soup was just okay though. That cabbage salad I was worried about? Love, love, loved it. Chocolate dessert, very sweet, and came with "Happy Birthday, William" written on it. I didn't want the cheesecake really, because they tend to be so sweet. Their cheesecake is perfect; light, creamy, not too sweet and just the right portion. Service was excellent; water glasses never less than half full, attentive but not overly so, and very helpful. Everyone was wonderful and they flowed as if they were performing a dance. Best part of all, I never felt as if I was out of place. It was a perfect experience and well worth the money. We'll definitely be back. See you soon, smoked trout! I miss you.
Cuban was especially delicious

This place is incredible! Â Layover at JFK last night...searching for some authentic Italian cuisine. Â Google search led us to Don Peppe's (South Ozone Park - Queens). Â We were seated immediately -tight quarters but lots of friendly conversations going on. Â Lots of Italian people dining here which is a good sign! Â Menu is on the wall on a black board...many choices...all look delicious. Â Our waiter came by, described the specials...and offered us beverages...house red wine is relish! Â  Party of three...we started with the house salad...family style. Â I could have been content with just that...fresh beyond belief...from the crisp, green lettuce to the obviously imported tomatoes that taste like they came from your grandmother's garden. Â  And the dressing...mwah! Â It was the lightest, freshest, homemade Italian imaginable! Â Olives green and black...incredible. As one member of our party had a seafood allergy...we had to shy away from the clams...and although the veal gets total raves, we opted for spaghetti with garlic and olive oil first...delicious! Â Plenty of garlic and sauce. Â The pasta was not homemade...only downside of this entire meal...and not a big deal. 2nd course chicken with lemon and butter...can't say enough about this dish...wish I could make it that good at home...pounded thin...tender and moist beyond belief...vibrant lemon butter sauce - bright with a hint of fresh parsley! Dessert we split two...tortufo and a cannoli....seriously THE BEST cannoli ever. Â Filling so light and creamy...again AMAZING! If you are in or about the JFK area...this is a MUST!

5 steps to thoroughly enjoy your meal at Â  Ippudo: 1. Enjoy the loud applause of the employees welcoming you in Japanese. 2. Then order just two things. -HIRATA BUN -SHIROMARU HAKATA CLASSIC (with nitamago). 3. Of course finish every last morsel of food on your plate, for you aren't allowed to take the leftovers home . 4. Enjoy the complementary roasted green tea that helps you digest your meal. 5. And before you leave go to the counter where they prepare the ramen, it's so cool!

Excelent place. The service is very attentive, the chef came personally to the table to see if everything is fine. The food is just great, you have to try the octopus.We payed 80$ per person with wine included.

Truly delicious, authentic southern Italian!! Â Our granny chef for the evening was from a small town outside Naples. Â Many happy people were already enjoying dinner when our group of 5 arrived. Â I would highly recommend going with several people, as you can order and enjoy many dishes. Â The server was happy to accommodate family-style dining, and refreshed our plates as necessary, without any fuss or disturbing the flow of conversation and eating to do so. Â I recommend all of the following as incredibly tasty: fennel salad, meatballs in red sauce, stuffed figs, burrata mozzarella, manicotti, pork tenderloin, rabbit, and tiramisu with Nutella (sorry, I don't recall the names of the dishes, but you'll be able to identify them). Â We are all rhapsodizing the quality of the food and moderate prices, long after.

My wife and I were in the mood for something casual and decided to try this rincon on a Saturday night after reading the reviews on Yelp*. What a treat! The place is small but full of activity. We waited some 20 minutes for a table but were entertained by the jukebox and their rendition of singing "Happy Birthday" to two unsuspecting diners. Â Once we were seated, our waiter Marcelino never rushed us and was cordial enough to explain the various dishes on the menu. Unlike the details on Yelp*, there is no full bar here and they don't carry Cuban beers either. We didn't bother to ask Marcelino why but settled for two Estrellas from Barcelona which were pretty good. They also have a variety of wines but we decided to stay with the beer. My wife had the Ropa Vieja with white rice and black beans and I had the Lechon Asado with Arroz Moros y Cristianos and Yucca Con Mojo. The Ropa Vieja had a little too much tomato sauce and my Lechon was a little on the salty side but both were well seasoned and delicious. I have to say that the Yucca was absolutely perfect! We are planning to come back and next time I think we'll try the Chicharron de Pollo and Rabo Encendido which everyone seems to talk about. If you're ever in the area, this place is definitely worth a stop. But remember: if you decide to come here on your birthday, don't say you haven't been warned.

With all the development that's going on in the area, I hope this cafe stays afloat because it's great for the daily specials which are under $10. Â I love that I can be in and out of here well fed in 15 mins or less.

Yea dude it's unbelievably awesome. The truffle burger is so worth a second visit. I kinda wasn't expected a wow moment. It's been my experience that when people hype something up, it becomes a victim of its own success. I wasn't expecting to come in here and Be thunderstruck. I was however. And I will be coming back for another round. Real soon!
Unreal sandwiches , nice atmosphere

I think we ordered almost one of everything on the menu. Â Came in on a weekend and the place was lively but not too packed. Â We didn't have to wait long for a table. Â I just want to preface this by saying that the drinks were not that great, we had bloody marys and some mimosas. Â The bloody marys left a lot to be desired in terms of flavor and there was about a 1.5 inch thick chunk of peppery mess at the bottom of the glass. Â That being said, we weren't here for the drinks so it doesn't really matter. We got a small jambalaya because we had so much other food coming. Â This was probably my favorite dish of the meal. Â It was flavorful and hearty with a little kick. Â We ordered the fried seafood platter - the star of which was the catfish. Â The meat was light and fluffy, the batter was crispy, and the whole thing was melt in your mouth delicious. Â I was really disappointed with the hush puppies. Â I feel like that's something I can't find very often and was expecting some crunchy oniony doughy goodness. Â Instead, what I bit into was a greasy, crumbly, corn bread-ish thing. Â The other people at my table liked it, maybe I was just sad because it didn't taste like onion at all and that's what I love about hush puppies! Â The cajun mac and cheese was good but nothing to write home about. Â The deviled eggs were pretty delicious, the only one I didn't enjoy was the shrimp one as it was very fishy, too fishy for my taste. Â The collard greens and the sweet potato fries were good. The decor in this place is extremely cute. Â Almost looks like they went to a bunch of different garage sales and picked up kitschy little items from all over the US. Â Service was friendly. Â I'd come back for the jambalaya and catfish. Â YUM!

Hillstone is a restaurant that has followed me my whole life. Â I used to live in Atlanta and I would go almost every week after church to eat with my parents and their friends while growing up. Â I went to college in Boston and there was a Hillstone near government center, and I would go when I was homesick. Hillstone is always consistent in taste and the staff has always been attentive and are able to anticipate what you need before you ask for it. Â If you are looking for good solid American fare then this is definitely the place. I shall be a Hillstone loyalist til the end.

It's a very good italian restaurant with a lot of home made pasta options, pretty good portion sizes and good service. Their fennel salad is really good. The pasta I had was good, it was the mushroom one, but it was very overly salted, and I love salt, but it was just too much.

i was so excited to finally try upstate! i came here on a monday at 530 to make their happy hour special. The oysters here were delicious. The two that i tried were both east coast oysters but i can't remember the name. I just asked the waiter to suggest the tinier ones that didn't taste too seafoody. For the entree i ordered the clam linguini which was the perfect amount of everything. My boyfriend ordered the fish which came with roasted corn and tomatoes which was good. I wish the portion for that was a little bigger.

Amy Ruth's became my favorite soul food spot in Harlem, hands down. Â Don't come here expecting anything to be made to order but expect this to be cafeteria style food that's delivered to you. Â So if you're looking for somewhere to eat in a hurry, Amy Ruth has you covered. Â Despite the fact that everything is pre-made, that fried chicken was damn good. Â Great batter, excellent fry, and more importantly juicy, delicious, well seasoned chicken. Â Their cornbread was better than average, it was the sweet kind and moist rather than the usual bland cornbread I'm used to getting. Â The mac n cheese was pretty standard (why can't anyone ever give me al dente noodles!) but all in all a very good value.

Oh man. Spicy Spring, you win. This is the most simple yet most AMAZING pizza I've ever had. Granted, I am from LA, but I have tried other pizza places around NY quite a couple times and this one square slice stole the trophy for the best pizza yet. I don't know what the other reviews are talking about - it's not very spicy at all (although I'm Korean so spicy is my forte). However, everything else about it was absolutely perfect. The crust and dough was so deliciously made - the crust had the perfect crunch yet chewiness to it and the dough in general was soft, dense, and almost buttery in flavor. The cheese was not salty in the least and was perfectly stringy and in perfect proportion to the rest of the pizza. The pepperoni on the pizza also perfectly crisp and oily and the tomato sauce itself was sweet and stood out in flavor all by itself. The square slice was also a perfect amount - not overly filling yet extremely satisfying. This place truly hit the spot. The tiny restaurant does get crowded so try to come in the weirder hours to avoid the line and to be able to sit down and eat. Thanks Prince St. Pizza for the most amazing slice of pizza ever, but at the same time, curse you Prince St. Pizza for the future pizzas I will always be disappointed with everywhere I go.

After hearing all the hype about Locanda, I decided to come here for a bday celebration and brave the wait time for a dinner spot at the bar. Â They weren't kidding about the long wait (around 1.5 hours on a Tues night) but the bar was so fun and lively. Â The cocktails are yummy (I especially like the Sgroppino primavera!). Â For dinner we had the lamb sliders, sheep's milk ricotta, blue crab crostini, papardelle with lamb bolognese, Â and the orecchiette with duck sausage . Â All was very good, the ricotta was light and heavenly and the lamb sliders were savory (although only 2 per serving). Â However, the winner of the Â night was the tripe alla parmigiana....OMG. Â Tripe in a tomato-based stew filled with carrots and basil topped off with organic farm egg; the tripe texture went great with the stew. Â I could eat like a dozen bowls of this dish. Â The bar service was great overall and ended the night with complimentary glasses of champagne; after all this how can one not have a good time at Locanda Verde?

Fried starches, evolution makes us all love you so. Â We can all agree. Â Put down your swords. Â For Mr Fries. Â Ms Donut. Â Chief Frybread. Â Uncle Funnelcake. Â Sir Youtiao. I'm a soggy fry man, and these were a treat for me and my friend the crisplover.

so delicious! Â for this reason - it is worth potentially living in murray hill ;) spinach and artichoke dip is made with FRESH artichokes. Â with more artichokes than spinach. Â and i loved how the pita triangles were grilled crispy. grilled cheese with pesto, tomato, artichoke - again, so so delicious. THE BEST empanadas in NY! Even though the location is a bit random, i drive out here just for the food. Its really good quality and unbelievably affordable. They also have a variety of options. Love this place!

This place is delicious! The french toasts are amazing and the Andrey breakfast sandwich was very good. Pretty much everything I tried was delicious.! would highly recommend and it it was reasonably priced for NYC.

I saw Pies -n-Thighs on the food channel and decided when I went to NYC to check it out. I went there with a friend recently and I ordered fried chicken and apple pie with a minty julip type drink...everything was good. Its an eclectic place with a cool crowd. I would go back again.

I believe that all anyone really wants in this life is to sit in peace and eat a sandwich. -Liz Lemon A wiser woman, there might not be. Olea allows a person to do just that. During lunchtime especially, the vibe is so relaxing. I ended up waiting for my friend for about 15 minutes, but the waitress wasn't pushy at all; she just made sure I had something to drink and left me alone. Sure, the pint glasses they use for water have white marks on them (ostensibly from stacking), but I ain't never scurred. The menu is full of all sorts of tempting options, but I narrowed it down to their Chicken Club: chicken breast, bacon, herbed yogurt, endive, roasted tomato-green olive spread. Served on brioche with salad and patatas bravas on the side. And believe me, it's just as tasty as it sounds. It was juicy, full of flavor, and the papas bravas were excellent as well. I can't even tell you how many times I've walked by Olea on the way to and from other engagements, but from now on I'll be walking in, rather than by. Because this adorable little restaurant is warm, welcoming, and they make some damn good food.

My go-to burger place for over 6 years. The burger isn't fancy, but its quick, tasty, and cheap and always perfectly cooked. Â The fries and beer are equally delicious. There is often a line out the door, but I usually just find a seat at the bar and happily drink a McSorley while I wait for my greasebomb meal on a paper plate.

The Pizza Fiorentina was pretty disappointing. Â The crust was horrible. Â It had zero flavor and tasted as though it had been frozen :( Â The toppings though were OK. Â However, nothing special. This place seems to do better with their pastas, but I won't be back.

I definitely found my go-to Latin food/margarita spot to visit when friends are visiting. Great small place. I go here all the time and the food is great, with the service being really good also
Excellent food great service nice ambiance we really enjoyed there tapas I would love to go there again thank you

It won't bring you back to your grandmas shack in Italy but theyre not trying to be...come hungry & youll sure as sh*t leave full, thats the name of the game here...the portions & quality for the price is pretty fair..tourist trap alert on highest level but it's a safe bet if you need a super sized italian meal..not the most authentic or cozy place but its good for what it is Chicken parm was the size of Foghorn leghorn, breading was good not great but it wasn't greasy & it was cooked really well..$26 but it's basically 3 very good pieces, perfect for 2 hungry people..it's the only reason I'd go back..quantity over quality wasnt the case for the chicken, though it probably is for the pasta heavy dishes $13.50 for garlic bread is top 10 most absurd menu item ever, should be making year round shipments to ur house for that price..the free rocks i mean bread was horrible Meatballs were good but passable I'd go back but then again I'm a fan of Olive Garden too..as long as you know what to expect you shouldn't be dissapointed

Great lunch special! You get a salad or soup, small appetizer, and large entree for $9-12. Very attentive wait staff that never let my water get empty (which is quite the tall order). The thrill of bringing someone down a dark alley to a cool destination really starts off the experience nicely when you can sense from the others mind " WTF' Where the hell are you taking me". Really delicious Brunch spot. The wait is about an hour and place is pretty small so the squeeze is a little bit tight, but the food is very well worth all of these minor discomforts. The poached Eggs over the Salmon Hash-browns was very delicious! I will definitely be back here!
Even if they have tiny tables the sandwiches are great, perfect crisp bread, amazing flavors. Good coffee too

I normally wouldn't pick tuna for entree and was surprised that I enjoyed it. I think the dill pickles they put on was very good. I really liked the dish. Tasted some of friends salmon dish and it was interesting. Did not like my friend's chicken dish, nothing seemed special about it. prices are the biggest downside, I would not want to pay as much as I did for what I got in food and drink. service was great, bartender was friendly and fun to talk too

Really delish sandwiches! Great lunch option in Union Square if u don't mind taking it to go as seating is limited. Â Wish there were a few more options but the ones they have definitely don't disappoint.

Soooooo yummy! Â I can't wait to go back. Â We went for brunch this morning ... we had a big group (9). Â They were totally accommodating and sat us in the back. Â The server was really nice and helpful, as well as all of the other people working there. Â The food was awesome. Â I definitely think the chicken biscuit looked the best. i come here when i crave a nice sit down clean affordable dumpling meal in chinatown. the sesame pancakes are sooo good with meat fillings, the dumplings are delish and the soups are yummy too. perfect for a cold winter day. they do get really crowded and seating gets hard to find but turn around is pretty decent since its not a slow eating pace here. everyone is sort of on the go and just wanted to grab a quick bite. they also have a bathroom that isnt as dirty as the other chinese places in chinatown
Food was exceptional, but of note was the staff who are the most professional I have seen in a while. If you want Â good food and Â quality service this is the place to go.

This place is only worth three stars when they make the sandwich right. Â Two stars when most of the sandwich has cartilage and connective tissue. Â They are ok for Elmhurst but there's definitely better bahn-mi out there. Â Even when it's put together the right way, it doesn't taste that good. Â Their bubble teas and summer rolls are just ok too.

45% Pretty decent, but far from the best street food. *** I've come by The Halal guys twice so far. Â My first visit was in Oct '13, and my most recent on Nov '14. Â I visited while sober, so that might explain why I didn't give it '5 Stars!!!!' Â However, I did take the food to go, and had it with a beer at my place. Halal guys is a chain of food carts that serves a few dishes like shredded up chicken, Â or finely chopped up lamb (or lamb and beef, I forget) gyros meat, or a combination of both. Â Usually its served up under a generous plate of rice, along with some yogurt sauce and hot sauce on the the side. Â  Pits of pita bread are also thrown in on top before the plate is sealed up. Â There might be falafel, and the option to eat a pita wrap, but I don't recall ever seeing anyone order that. Â  Part of the appeal of Halal Guys is that the carts open until late hours of the morning, its fairly affordable being around $6 including tax, and its tasty, greasy, hearty food. Â It makes for a solid option after a night of drinking. Â I don't really enjoy going out drinking and seldom do that, so for me the experience was to try out the food for what it was. Overall I think the food is somewhere between pretty good and average. Â I don't think its notably better than your run of the mill halal cart. Â Nonetheless its pretty decent and tasty if take it face value. Â It does work much better with the yogurt sauce and a beer. Â I've only tried the lamb and chicken combo with rice so far. Â I'll get more into the specifics in terms of what enjoyed or not so much. Lamb and chicken with rice. Â $6 including tax. Â Id rate this dish 45%, which is somewhere between pretty good and average. Notes: - Serving temperature is good right out from the cart, remaining somewhere nicely warm. Â I think it makes a good amount of difference between eating it there instead of taking the food home, even if it doesn't take you much time. Â Then again you have to omit drinking beer, or risk getting caught drinking in public. Â I've been lucky so far with a bottle out of a bag. - The chicken and lamb gyros meats truly are nothing special, being neither good Â yet thankfully not poor. Â Its more or less what it is, although the meat, particularly the chicken seems over-cooked and dry. Â Chopping it up into fine bits seem to be a way to cover up this, giving the meat a more passable texture. Â Flavor wise, this is a more tasty dish, its hard to deny that. Â The meats seem predominantly salty in flavor, with a decent amount of fat that adds to the richness. Â The saltiness is bit too much for me, without the yogurt. Â Thankfully the oils from the fat are not unpleasant. Â  - Adding the yogurt sauce tends to add a creaminess and tart essence that works well against the saltier meats, it also seems to alleviate the meats being so dry. Â I choose to omit the hot sauce, as I find the heat levels too aggressive and overpowering. Â However I rarely use hot sauce for anything. - The rice used isn't a bad starch. Â Its neither too dry or mushy, and its coated with a bit of oil or fat. Â There seems to be a good balance between meat and starch. Â It certainly fills you up, but without feeling you've just had a starch bomb. Â Surprisingly I feel little discomfort after eating a whole portion of this. - Having a good beverage is a must. Â A good simple beer chilled at the right temperature with some carbonation seems to compliment the heaviness well enough. Â There's nothing fancy here and I see no fault with that. Value is okay. Â Sure its relatively cheap, but low prices doesn't mean you're getting a deal. Â Its high volume street food that's executed just enough to be satisfying, and its not like the ingredients are remarkable in any way. Â Most of the stuff is precooked, so its just a matter of quicky reheating meats and scooping it into a container. Â It beats most fast food easily, but thats not saying much. Service is alright. Â The staff seem cordial. Â Waiting times tend to vary. Â I've had to wait 15 mins without a line, and 5 mins with a line. Â It depends if the guy working the cart is cooking up a new batch or not. Â Its good enough for what it is. Ambiance is non existent. Â Its street food, and Im not holding them against that. Â  Recommended half-heartedly as something you may want to try out, especially if you're not entirely sober and after other places have closed down. Â I wouldn't call it an essential dining experience. Â Its great as cheap food when you're not sober. Â Its decent if you're sober and taken at face value.

Not worth it. The wait was so long as there was no reservation available. No place to sit while you wait. I stood and kept getting hit by the customers and waiters coming through. The head waiter kept telling us that our table was almost ready when it actually wasn't. Finally we are seated. To even get a waiter's attention was SO difficult that I contemplated leaving. But since I had already waited an hour for this place, what is another 10+ minutes? We ordered. Water does not come until our food comes. AND my ravenous self was staring at the tables near us, THEY ALL GOT BREAD. WHERE WAS OUR BREAD?!?!? Anyways, so my friend and I got the tagliatelle bolognese as well as the pork belly. Pork belly was just all fat. NO meat. What kind of dish is this?! I understand that pork belly has a lot of fat.. I've eaten it at a lot of places. But if I order the entree version, I expect some meat on it! The tagliatelle was less disappointing. It was a homecooked pasta, something you can make yourself. Not exciting. Not innovative. But this place isn't that. I recommend it if you want a down to earth meal. But you can get this pasta anywhere else in the city, don't suffer through this long wait and horrible service for it.

one shouldn't go broke eating ramen every night unless you eat at ippudo. it has a nice decor inside. and thats probably what you're paying for. the benches/banquets where a little uncomfortable to sit on. we had a few appetizers that were tasty, but they were $8-$10 per app. there was only one of them that i didn't like. it was the asparagus wrapped in pork belly. but it wasn't like the pork belly that i was used to getting from chinatown. it was more like just the tougher part of the fat from the pork belly, wrapped around the asparagus, breaded and deep fried...was very rubbery and not so good. i figured if fat was deep fried it should at least be good & crispy like the skin when you're eating fried chicken. also, the miso ramen was ok. the noodles weren't like ramen noodles. they were more like shanghai dan dan noodles. not what i was expecting. the slices of pork were very good, but you were only given 2 slices of pork. the miso broth was sort of mild which is what i prefer as a lot of ramen i have is too salty. i like a little spice with my hot broth. i asked the server for hot sauce and he brought out a teaspoon of chili paste out to the table. i added it and it wasnt enough to even change the taste of the broth. after we saw the bill, i was charged $3 for that hot sauce. WTF? you're charging $16 for ramen noodles, and then you're going to nickel and dime me for a teaspoon of chili paste? is it right to charge customers for condiments? at least let them know ahead of time. it would be like McDonalds charging for ketchup. don't know if i would try this place again. bill for 4 people was over $100 and no alcohol.

I dont know why I'm not really a fan of ramen, or why is it like that coz I should like it coz I'm asian kind of things....but I'd eat it, and so i did. Came here with the bf and two good friends, and the kid, we were seated at the very far back in front of the wall, on a narrow table that could only fit the bowl of soup we had to order. As I was browsing through the yelp reviews on what to order, I finally decided to try the chicken-pork broth and the pork gyoza as appetizers. They only had one fan that circulates the place sadly it was placed at the back,so as the bf sat in front of it, all we can breathe is the air with his perfumey aroma that comes with it. The gyoza's came and oh boy they were quite hot,small but tasty. One cold bottle of beer came too with that. The bowls of ramen came, looking not bad with all the stuff inside. AFter a few sips of the soup, I already had to try out the condiments in the small table just to make up for the flavor I am looking for, pepper, chili oil and some chili powder which by the way was not chili at all. In short, the soup was too bland for me, although I might say the two pieces of smoked pork meat was very flavorful, that was the only thing that I really liked with my meal.The noodles was good as promised but of course theyre only noodles. Sad to say I ddnt really finish the whole thing. And so we left the place shortly after the meal, for sure the fresh air was a sure sign of relief that I was really out of there.
