Came here on a Friday night in which it was busy but the wait wasn't too bad, prob 5-10 minutes. Wanted to try out their 'special' burger so a friend and I shared a truffle burger, duck burger, sweet potato fries and truffle fries. Honestly the texture of the duck burger seems similar to beef, so I wouldn't have known it was duck unless they told me. It had an interesting sweet taste so it wasn't too bad. The truffle burger was good but I didn't find it spectacular. Truffle fries were alright and the highlight of the day goes to the sweet potato fries due to it's distinct taste. I found the portion of the fries to be larger than expected which was good. Overall, would stop by again if in the area.

My boss was shocked to find an opening on OpenTable and booked it right away for later that night. It was a business dinner for 3, but I would go back again! We ordered the Chef's tasting menu. I don't know how else to describe the food, the experience, and the ambience except unbelievably amazing...My favorite dishes of the night were: - Halibut - fish was cooked just perfectly, tender and flaky with great sauce - Duck Breast - tender and perfect medium rare. There was also so much flavor packed in the mushrooms; I could have eaten a bowl of them - Pear Panna Cotta - It came in this clear cup and when you pick up a spoonful with all the layers - just gorgeous This is food at its best, showcasing the beauty of American cuisine. I would come back again...but probably only for a special occasion. It's not a place I can frequently visit (even though I would gladly do so) with that price hah.

I was fortunate enough to be taken to Gramercy Tavern for my birthday recently, and really had a great experience. Â Overall, the restaurant is beautiful -especially the main dining room, and the service was very friendly throughout. Â  We started off with Mistral Martini cocktails - a lavender flavored gin based drink. Â Overall, it was very good, although the lavender does become a bit strong toward the end. Â After that, we tried the Orange Blossom - a champagne based drink with orange essence. Â The Orange Blossom was a very good, simple cocktail with great flavor. For the first course, my girlfriend had the chilled asparagus soup. Â I thought this was a very unique soup with great flavor. Â The lobster and hazelnuts gave the soup some additional texture. Â if you're looking for an appetizer that won't be too filling, this is a great choice. Â I tried the smoked trout - which was a nice choice as well. Â The trout had a pronounced smokiness, but not too overbearing so as to cover up the natural taste. Â Very simple dish, but very enjoyable. For the second course, my girlfriend had the duck breast and confit. Â The duck was very tender and flavorful, although I think a lot of the other entrees seem more interesting. Â I tried the pork loin and belly, which was also very good. Â The meat was well cooked and the sides were also fantastic. Â I think if I returned I would try a fish dish though, as that seems to be a specialty. For dessert, I had a cheese plate and found each cheese to be fantastic. Â My girlfriend had the lemon pound cake - which was fantastically sweet. Â  Overall, a fantastic dinner. Â Overall I find the menu to be pretty simple (hence the "Tavern" perhaps), but it is well executed and memorable.

Came here for dinner with couple of friends. Â The place was once well known with their cheap price, good food not too good of a service. Â This time we went there price was average, food was below average, service was none. We order their famous roast duck. The dish came out cold, skin was not crispy and was really fatty and salty. The yeung chow fried rice also came out not hot and was bland. Â It seems like they throw the rice and the ingredient together in the wok and mix it up without the stir fried. The beef chow fun was bland too. The only good food that we order was the stir fried lobster. Service was the worst. The first waiter we ask to refill our water, he walked away mumbling something and never came back with it. Second waiter same thing. Â We were about to ask the third waiter, the second waiter saw us waiving our hand and he finally remember and finally we got our water. Â The place was not pack with ppl. Â They don't seems to be that busy to not hear our request and forgetting about it. Since we are paying for avg price food, at least give us an avg service. Â We still have to tip them base on the price of the bill.

Shroomtown pizza. If you like truffle, this is the best. Â When I first saw the pizza when I brought it back to the apartment, I was definitely disappointed. Â It just looked so sad. Â One bite and I was absolutely hooked. Â Perfect CRUST. Â Perfect cheese. Â Perfect sauce. Â I'm drooling just thinking about it. Best pizza in NYC. Â I know it's a strong statement, but it's the truth. Â Give it a try.
Small place, very crowded with good reason. Â Didn't like the loud music so much but I can't complain too much. Â I love the menu and the food was great. Â Really good service def give them a try.
Chips

This was my first visit coming from California, but my family always speaks highly of this place. After circling the neighborhood for parking, we entered the tiny building that filled the air with an aroma of delicious food. We had a slightly larger party but were accommodated nicely with two tables, which we didn't mind because it was a small hole-in-the-wall Chinese joint. Aside from the typical Asian service (which is also experienced on the west coast), the food is on-par with authenticity and flavors. I had the Singaporean rice noodles (cooked with onions, peppers, BBQ pork, and curry spices) and sampled other dishes like the soy sauce chicken and roasted duck, both of which were amazing. The food also came out extremely fast, but fresh and piping hot. I loved the kitchen bell that kept going off, letting the servers know the food was ready. It just added to the experience for me. This place satisfies the craving for authentic Chinese food and I would definitely be back when I visit again.
Four stars because its too crowded but the unlimited sangrias and great food, kind of makes up for it.

This place is a well oiled machine. Â Line out the door but moves fast. Â Falafel plate consists of six falafel balls on a Mediterranean salad for six bucks. Â The hot sauce is hot but a nice addition. Â Washington park is a block away and a nice place to eat as this is take out only.

I sat at the bar on a weeknight around 7 pm . I was lucky enough to get a seat. I ordered the tuna appetizer and the grilled octopus salad . The portions were ample. The octopus was cooked perfectly. The atmosphere is incredibly charming, quite and relaxing. The food came in a timely manor and the service was very good. I enjoyed my time there I decided to stay for desert. I ordered the crÃ¨me brÃ»lÃ©e . Perfect to split between 2 people. It was a surprisingly enjoyable evening.

An interesting concept. I unfortunately didn't have time to really sample the food more than a burger. The wasabi mayo was actually pretty good, better than I thought. Though I'd like to see a wasabi mustard as well. Burger was nicely made, good quality, but a little small...maybe a 1/3 pound patty would work better. The portion of fries was huge. A little too big I think, by volume you get more fries than burger. I think a home made malt vinegar would go better with the fries. Or perhaps a salt and powdered wasabi sprinkle? I'd like to go back and try more from these guys next time I'm in New York.

Probably the most unique part of my experience here was the setting. Perry St. is right off the Westside Highway and situated at the bottom of one of Richard Meier's towers. So the highway is roaring with New York City craziness, but when you walk into the restaurant it's so calm and peaceful. The food was good, but not great (I had the peeky toe crab salad, tuna burger, and chocolate cake). I still highly vouch for Jean-Georges primary joint on Columbus Circle. The drinks, however, brought the rating up from a 3 to a 4 for me. Probably one of the best Mojito's i've ever had. Especially in the scorching summer heat...it was FABULOUS. I'd go back just to chill at the bar.
Very long wait. Pizza was delicious and very reasonably priced. Worth the wait as long as you can sit outside and enjoy a few drinks.
Simply amazing. Worth the trip and the wait. Get a square slice while you wait for your whole pie to cook.

Great Italian restaurant with good food. Â We always come here for the following and have always left satisfied: - Mussels - Tagliolini Frutti di Mare (seafood pasta) - Panna Cotta - Straccetti di Manzo (thin slice beef filet with rosemary & potatoes) One star off for the crampy and often noisy space. Â Most people just eat and go. Â It's really not a place to sit for 2 hours and have a long dinner.

Luzzo's represents real pizza napoletana from what I experienced this past weekend..their ingredients are fresh, lovely ambiance and excellent service. Â The pizza is amazing I had the Arugola pie and their brutta ma buona and we were delighted with food. Â I will definitely bring my family back and they earned a faithful customer. Keep it up guys :-) Omar Matos
So glad that Forno is just a few, short blocks away. Â Have never been disappointed whether it's for takeout or dining in. Service with a smile is the norm here and food is consistently good.
Tasting menu was delicious. Â Service impeccable. Â I loved all of the little touches, including the muffin for my breakfast the following morning.

I have been wanting to come to this restaurant since I moved to the West Village, and last night I finally did! It was everything I hoped it would be and more. The ambiance is romantic, but I also saw a lot of groups there, so it is really good for a data night or a girls night out. The food was awesome. We started off with bruschetta, which was pretty standard but the olive oil they have is some of the best I've ever tasted and when you drizzle that on top, YUM! I got the spinach gnocchi with Gorgonzola sauce which was amazing! I really wasn't expecting it to taste how it did, the sauce was not overpowering at all. My boyfriend got the seafood risotto which was delicious too. I would definitely go back. It is not super pricey, but it is cash only so watch out for that.

Great pulled pork and great service at a great price.l I just went for the second time to Juniper with 2 friends. They were out of the rib sandwich so two of us had the pulled pork sandwich. It was fantastic! Meat was tender and moist, BBQ sauce was tasty (though not particularly creative), and the fries cooked perfectly. The other friend had the burger; she said it was good but not great. The total bill for us was under $40!

Restaurants can evoke feelings, much the way food can. This one feels like home...it's cozy, laid back, and warm. A place I could spend time with friends or family for hours, just sitting and talking (though I'm not sure the restaurant would be so happy about that). I've been here twice, both times for dinner (though the descriptions of brunch are pretty mouth-watering). One time, my whole family dined at a large table in the front. The service was impeccible and the food superb. The second time, my husband and I dined cozied up to the bar. The drinks and interesting selection of good beers was great, and the food was delicious. My favorite taste for the evening was the sunchoke side dish. It was AMAZING - a garlicky, lick-your-fingers-clean kind of taste. Mmmm. I would go back anytime. But, I think next time will have to be for brunch.

Despite the trendiness and touristy aspect of Shake Shack, I've always loved the food. The burger is well-balanced and not overly beefy like so many restaurants. The Shroom burger (deep fried mushroom stuffed with cheese) is the real highlight and even though I'm not a vegetarian I usually order it. The shakes are great as well and everything is affordable by Manhattan standards ($10-$20). Â  The new Battery Park City branch (sorry, there is no such thing as the "Lower West Side") is a welcome addition to the neighborhood. It's always busy as expected, but the best time to go is on a Saturday or Sunday night. You can order and have your food in 10-20 minutes (I usually go around 8-9PM). Try doing that a Madison Square Park! I guess it's because most the tourists are gone as well as the WFC workers and the location has low visibility. Also, the indoor/outdoor seating is usually full (even in this 100 degree heatwave -- there is NO AC).

Noodle dish is very tasty and better than a lot of Japanese owned Ramen noodle restaurants in Manhattan. Only thing for me is the price of appetizers. $8 for Gyoza is waaaaay too much. I am a big fan on Chuko and I'm so happy that they are in Brooklyn, but overall Tabata and Nippori win!

I've tried to get into Ippudo for dinner a couple of times before but was discouraged by the long lines. This time, I decided to go for a late lunch and was seated in about 20 minutes. As the hostess leads you inside, you are bombarded with people screaming Japanese greetings and a lot of noise from the hustle and bustle. I've never been to a proper ramen joint in Japan, but I suspect the atmosphere must be very similar. I ordered the Akamaru Modern and my friend ordered the "original". We also ordered a yellowtail sashimi appetizer called "Hamachi Goma-Shoyu", which was a yellowtail sashimi dish with egg yolk sauce and sliced jalapenos. I was thoroughly impressed by the ramen and it lives up to its billing. The broth was flavorful and the best part was the noodles, which were cooked perfectly al dente. The Modern was more savory and spicy compared to the original and suited my heavier palate better. The roasted pork in both ramen were equally delicious. One of the biggest disappointments about eating ramen is finishing the noodles and having no more soup left. Not a worry at Ippudo though since for $2, you can order the "kae-dama" which is another serving of noodles provided you have sufficient broth left. The way I see it, you end up getting two bowls of delicious, authentic ramen for $17. Now, the appetizer. I was told that Ippudo served up some delicious appetizers but I was a little disappointed in the yellowtail. The fish had good texture but lacked taste. The egg yolk didn't do anything for the dish and the sliced jalapenos had no kick--nullifying its appeal. For $14, it was basically the price of a bowl of ramen and I would have rather ordered another bowl. That said, their other appetizers seemed delicious and I recognize that we probably should have ordered something else. But the star of the show here is obviously the ramen, and in that respect, this place deserves all the praise it gets.

I came here on a Saturday evening, and I was surprised at how laid back it was. Given the history of this place, I thought it would be swarming with tourists. Instead, we just walked up to the bar, order Magners cider (on tap!) and had a chill conversation for about an hour and a half. The bathrooms were clean, and the bartenders were nice. I'd definitely come back and check out the museum upstairs!

Only came here for dessert - they had amazing homemade mochi (my favorite was the earl grey chocolate), which comes in a sampler set of 3; also tried the iced matcha latte and hojicha anmitsu (green tea jelly, rice glutinous balls, sweet syrup, grass jelly, green tea ice cream) which started off not that sweet until I realized the sweet syrup was all at the bottom, so try to keep that in mind as you start digging into the ice cream and jelly at the top. Both were great options on their dessert menu and I'd love to go back - the atmosphere is great (perfect for a date); only caveats are that the place is small, on the second floor, and is cash only!

Go to 7A (no i dont work there!!!) Â The drinks are better across the street at 7a and they are much nicer. Let's just say I expected attitude in new York and aside from this place, everyone during this trip was perfectly enjoyable. Go to 7A across the street, they are way cooler. My boyfriend took me to new York and we stay two doors down from this yuca bar, he was so excited to take me there because he said the food is really great last august when he visited, so we stopped in to check their hours. Saturday morning we made it a point to come grab some seats. We walked in and asked for a four top outside and said we were waiting for our friends. So the little lady tried seating us outside with two tables and the manager says we can't do that because of fire codes. Ok, we as a restaurant owner I'm very well aware of how strict city codes can be so we just returned the tables and sat at both to hold. There were PLENTY other open outside tables at this point, so my boyfriend sat at one table and I sat at another. We ordered a few mimosas and appetizers, and then the manager comes out and says he needs our tables when there were obviously other tables outside available near us. We said we were seated here and they knew we were waiting for people. He says no we don't seat partial parties. We said a few things and i was super polite about it, again, being in the business and knowing my boyfriend really wanted to eat here, i didnt want to make a scene. I then said Well we were seated by them and we didn't know. Â just then our party walked up and the jack ahole manager takes the extra chairs and takes it from us and says no, we can have one chair per table Â because we were separate parties and would not allow them to sit with us and they they had to go wait up front. There was not one party up front waiting for a table. Quite upset, we just got up and walked across the street to 7a and they accommodated us and our puppy in every hospitable way possible. We watched the tables from across the street and only didnt seat for another 15 minutes or more. So the stupid manager lost good business. After we ordered our drinks next door we realized that yuca bars mimosas very only orange juice compared to 7a 's very well made drinks, you can see this from the street if you peer in. Mimosas were more champagne colored than the deep orange juice color you get at yucas! So more for your money at 7a.The menus are very slightly different. Yuca was probably so quiet on that busy brunch and 7a was completely packed because of their not so great management style that makes people steer clear from them. I'm not just promoting 7a because I had to use them as a backup plan, I actually went there the very first day in new York and the waitress I had was super sweet and the guy with the super cool monkey pin helped me figure out what to do with my stuff, so I enjoyed them twice in one trip.

Came here for a 2nd time this past Saturday. The 1st time I went here was with a sizeable group. Â We ordered a ton of sushi, plus a few sides and pork buns, etc. Â Everyone loved the food, and I liked that their special rolls were unique and not full of gross things like cream cheese or excessive mayo. This past time was just a table for 2. Â Place was not even close to being 1/2 full, but it was still fun; I really liked the atmosphere & communal seating. Â We ordered a few different things - spicy miso ramen, pork buns, wedge salad, brussel sprouts - all of which were delish. Â Major props on the ramen! Â It was very flavorful and not too oily. Staff was also excellent and very accommodating. Â Offered to make lychee sochu drink less sweet, brought out water/drinks promptly, helped with menu selections, etc.

Went here on a friday morning 11:00 - there was a half hour queue for a table for 2. Ordered the pancakes, which were _spectacular_ - amazing flavour and texture, with blueberry dripping over every bite. Really tasty. The wait for my pancakes was way too long though (I think they lost the order)--so they gave a complimentary banana choc chip muffin, which was also excellent. I can forgive the accident of service, that happens; Food was good. will go back.

So glad I finally ate here! I had been to Tavern several times for drinks but had never had a meal. Â After hearing from several neighborhood lifers that this was THE neighborhood spot, I decided to have dinner. I had the veggie spring rolls to start and was so happy they weren't the standard sysco frozen spring rolls. Â They are made fresh and you can tell. For my entree, I had the special, which was a roast chicken with curry. Â Again, you can tell everything was fresh and made in house. The food was great but my favorite thing about Tavern is the vibe. Â When you walk in, you are instantly welcomed and made to feel like part of the wonderful, if not slightly eccentric, west village family.

We went here on a whim due to a hankering for some oysters on the half shell. We proceeded to order the blue point oysters and steamers as they were on the menu that day. The oysters were flavorful and plump and the steamers were a thing of beauty. I would have liked a few more steamers for the price(14 bucks) but Â given their deliciousness I cant be too upset. For the main entree the wifey went with the lobster club, which was lobster roll goodness with the added benefit of bacon. The roll came out overflowing with very large chunks of lobster meat. I choose to get the lobster shepherds pie. I went with this choice because I haven't seen that type of offering before and was intrigued. I wasn't sure how mashed potatoes would meld with sweet lobster meat, but it was a match made in heaven. I dont think it hurt that it was a cold, windy november day and this dish was just what the doctor ordered. The shepherds pie was stuffed with large chunks of lobster meat to my delight. One always has to wonder how much actual lobster will actually be in a dish when you try a restaurant for the first time. All the food came out in a timely manner and tasted extremely fresh. Â Overall the place is small, but it has a very cool vibe and great food. Got to love the paper towel rolls on the table as well, makes it feel authentic and laid back.

Cheap, maybe good... But we will never know. We came here about 10:45a in the morning on a weekday, and the slow service was slow. Probably our fault for being stubborn customers for choosing to sit on the other side of the restaurant because it was easy to move our luggage over here. But the waiter was swamped and did not attend to us when we were standing there for a whole minute. She didn't seem to want to serve us even when we told her we were here. Giving two stars for what could have been. Went to Joe's shanghai instead, well, that's another "interesting" review...

Good thing I no longer live walking distance to the King anymore because otherwise I'd be 20 pounds heavier than I am. When I first heard of this place, I was hesitant. How could such incredible quality food come from a street vendor?? I've been eating from here for over 2 years and NEVER had a bad dish. No matter what time of day you come, the food is always FRESH and ready to serve. They use the best ingredients and have perfected the falafel and chicken. That chicken? If I could learn how to make it as good then I'd be a happy girl. Even the veggies are a nice touch especially when you get the hot sauce. It helps you cool down. Do yourself a favor and try something from here. Always friendly and working hard. Five stars!
love it here. food, price, environment are all fantastic!!!

It's really a 3.5 for me. If you're not going to be any where near a Din Tai Fung or Crystal Jade and you're in the mood for xiao long bao or pork dumplings filled with soup, Bao is an easy substitute. I was with a large group and they ordered a lot of the other stuff which I didn't really need. As for the dumplings, I prefer mine a bit smaller so it's easy to fit a whole dumpling in your mouth. Flavor is good, portions of the pan fried noodle and vegetable dishes were small. Clean modern setting was nice.

I stopped by for brunch as a party of four on a Saturday, and the place wasn't particularly busy at the time. I split an order of the bone marrow and brisket burger and the swine benedict; the former I found to be not terribly juicy or flavorful, although it came with very nicely-done fries that were crispy on the outside but still soft and potato-y on the inside. The swine benedict was decent and had meat with nice flavor, but it was just a touch on the smaller end for brunch entrees. I also had the Wake 'n Bacon drink, which was decent but wasn't quite the right mix of sweet and alcohol-y for me. Not a bad option for brunch, but just think there are better value meals out there, and I just wasn't as enthralled with the burger.

I just moved back to Brooklyn last week and am so excited to have Martha a few blocks away. The restaurant is lovely -- I like the simple wood and metal look, and the garden space out back is nice. Our server was friendly, and the service was fast. My brother and I shared the brussels sprouts (glorious) and the swordfish poke (also delicious), and I had a bite of his pork belly bao (the flavor profile was not as interesting as the other dishes, but it was very well prepared). All of the ingredients were fresh, and the flavors were well balanced. I will definitely be back!

more like 3.5 for me? came here for brunch after seeing all the positive reviews in yelp..the service was very good..friendly staff...we got the burger and the duck hash...the burger was good, pretty delicious but i do not know what the big hype was about..me and my friend both did not like the duck..will probably give it another chance...

I don't see the point in reviewing a place with 900+ reviews, except that, I'm going to comment on something aside from the corn, which although orgasmic, is over-exposed. The food is divine. Shuffle through the hundreds of other reviews if you want details on the explosive menu. I opt for the fish tacos with rice and beans. It's just damn good. What rocks about this place is the vibe and the loyal Cuban flavor. The mango margaritas, the guava cocktails, and, my favorite, the rad red lit bathroom and plate of plantains. It's bloody hot in the Summer at the bar, so unless you want to peel your ass off a red vinyl stool, squeeze in the back, and I mean squeeze; or go with a group of four so you can score a booth.

There are many reasons to love Olea, but the thing that makes me happiest about the fact that it's in my hood is that it's good for so many different occasions: happy hour dates, girls' brunch, dinner with the folks, lunchtime laptopping...it somehow feels comfortable for all of these things, which is rare. And the food! It's consistent and delicious! I think it's best to share some of the Mediterranean tapas and perhaps a salad or main. If you're there for dinner, don't miss the brussels sprouts. I know, brussels are the new black. But these are crispy and flavorful and magically delicious. I could eat them by the pickle-barrel-full. The haloumi cheese over romescu sauce is a hit, too. Brunch is also great. I'm partial to the fresh, elegant, and tasty Savory Parmesan French Toast with peas. I'm not a bloody mary person but I understand theirs are fantastic. Downsides: occasionally snooty service/hosts, and what everybody else says: how hard is it to get pita that is not reminiscent of communion wafers?

Came here for dinner and was a big fan. The place is small and cosy with sidewalk seating. It was quality Brazilian food that was well prepared. I have yet to try the brunch but I can see how this place can get packed. The food is well prepared and I had zero issues with the service. Then again I also ate late @ 10pm when busienss was slower. Both plates we had (filet minon and moqueca) were simple yet very good.

Finding a good brunch place wherever I travel to is extremely important for me because I am an early bird and I do enjoy a good sweet/ savory spot that has coffee to fulfill my needs in the morning. My godsister and one of our friends got to Friedman's around 12, which was considered lunch already, but were able to grab the brunch dishes. We ordered 2 of the specials of the day which was this SWEET POTATO HASH type thing with an amazing pouched egg on top, the APPLE/ PEAR PANCAKES as well as their FRIED CHICKEN with Â CHEDDAR WAFFLE. All of the dishes were great, except I wasn't really feeling the cheddar waffle. I'm not sure if it was because of the syrup with the cheese or what, but it wasn't as good as I read it. I'd definitely come check this place out again. ENJOY! PS: Prepare to wait like we did if you do not get there early.
All I can say is: now I want to find the truck!

Not what it used to be!! The portions are much smaller and the prices are much higher. There are much better places for the same price and the portions are bigger. Would not be going back. The hot sauce is amazing though.

My husband and I went here on 6/21/13 for dinner. We had reservations for 7:15, but arrived a little early. They sat us immediately, which is a huge plus in my book. Not only that, but my request to sit next to a window was honored. (A suggestion to them however would be to turn the tables sideways so all members of the party could see out. I ended up with my back to the view). We told the waiter we were not in a rush, and we never felt like the the entire night. We both enjoyed a pasta dish, strong drinks, and friendly service. I would definitely recommend this place to anyone looking for something middle of the road price-wise, and yet feeling like it should cost more.

Wonderful staff. CUTE getaway from the city. Pricey, but it is brunch afterall. Only grumpy and stingy people (who don't understand that restaurants make killings through brunch) would be unhappy. But this place is so cute, that it should make your day!? It was not busy at all when I was there on a weekend afternoon..? ATMOSPHERE/AMBIANCE/DECOR lalala: Â 5/5 Lovely wood furniture, and the backside-outdoor seating! They had outdoor-sidewalk seating too, but the seating in the back...!? Sooooo cute! It was really peaceful and chill. I felt like I was away from the hustle & bustle of New York. It's homey, modern, and tavernlike without being bro-ful, lol! SERVICE: 5/5 The waitress was cool, the guy who seated us was cool. They were very pleasant. FOOD: Refills on coffee. Tasty alcoholic brunchy drinks. Their eggs benedict (forget which :(...think it had prosciutto or something.) and their french toast was tasty. I always never finish one brunch entree alone. Their menu brunch selection was great, for a picky brunch-hater like me. Their side-of-bacon was tasty too.

Think a good izakaya in Midtown doesn't exist? An introduction needs to be made to Sake Bar Hagi, a hidden venue on 49th Street. It is not, first of all, the restaurant at street level. Take the stairs to the basement level, open a narrow wooden door, and put your name and number on the waiting list. Once a seat is available, the host will give you a call and five minutes to make your way over to claim your spot. The room isn't that large, but the arrangement of tables and seating makes the most of what they have. The delivery of warm towels before the meal was a nice touch, and started the meal on a positive note. Throughout the night, service was efficient and understandably terse; nonetheless, we had all of our major needs taken care of and everything came and was taken away on time. The staff is very much experienced in handling the crowds, which range from professionals just out of work to large groups of college students. While I can't speak to the Sake Bar Hagi's namesake, I can say that the food here will surpass expectations. I hesitate to call them "Japanese small plates", but these dishes are best when shared. The takoyaki is probably what I was least sure about ordering, especially as I'd never had octopus before. Chewy, lightly seasoned, and served with tenkasu and pickled ginger, it was quite a contrast of flavors and textures. I would have preferred something a bit more aggressive in terms of taste, as I found it rather bland and in need of more seasoning? Overall, not a bad dish, but not something I would order again based on my own tastes. The yakitori was our next dish, and I was pleasantly surprised with the generous serving of noodles we were given. Deciding to avoid the dab of mayonnaise that came with it (thankfully they didn't mix it in for us), we dug in. The noodles were cooked to a nice al dente, and the sauce that it was topped with was savory, slightly sweet, and not overly salted. The fact that there were some napa slices strewn in as well made us feel a little better about eating a giant pile of noodles, and added a nice crunch to each bite. A good dish to share, and one I'd order again... except perhaps next time, I'd opt for the miso version. And finally, the okanomiyaki, my favorite of the night. Often described as a " Japanese pancake", ours was served in a hot iron plate. The dough was crisped perfectly, and the addition of pork and vegetables made it even more hearty. Sake Bar Hagi delivers on almost all dimensions, and is a good choice for various occasions and groups. Keep the wait in mind, but know that in the end, it's absolutely worth it.

I love Dig Inn, but this location is the most disorganized I've ever been to. The staff is largely confused, can't hear orders over the loud music, and have twice now put someone else's order into my bag. Would someone from an experienced store please help these staff members out?!

Came in on a Sunday afternoon. Wasn't too busy. There was a great, throwback vibe to the place. Checkered tablecloths, bottles of soda, a bright red neon sign in the back. It just felt like old America. As I sit down, I am promptly greeted by my waitress, who runs me through the menu like a pro and recommends the vodka pie. She was very friendly and eager to please. She brought me delicious free bread and joked with me throughout my meal. I received my pizza prompt and hot. It was fantastic. The ingredients played off each other in perfect harmony. Prosciutto, mushrooms, cheese, basil. With each bite I wanted more. It was the best NYC pizza experience I've ever had.

La Pulperia is a hidden gem and I am so glad we went there! On a Tuesday night there weren't a lot of people at all, so we were quickly seated. The sangria was delicious and the waiter was very kind in accommodating us to only a half pitcher, which was more than plenty. I am still thinking about how good the scallop ceviche was and how I want more! We decided to share the whole fish, and got it fried. It was really good, but I wasn't a huge fan of the sauce, but loved the apples that were on top, it added a great touch! I definitely plan to come back. cute place for date night!

yum great brick oven pizza! Â the crust is nice and crispy and just the right amount of burn on the bottom of the pizza. Â YUM! we ordered 2 pizzas one with tomato and mozzerella and one with sausage and roasted red pepper. Â both pizzas were really great! Â definitely get the tomato and mozzerella, it's simple and very flavorful. definitely a must if you're visiting nyc. Â this place gets super crowded because a lot of tourists go to this place too. Â make sure you get there early or be willing to wait a while to be seated.

I came here for dinner a while ago and had a delicious meal! Â And this time it was brunch. Service was nice. Â Both times I have been here, I sat in the bar area as I didn't make reservations and there was quick availability up front. I had the huevos rancheros. Â 3 eggs and salsa and black beans all baked to perfection - what can go wrong? Â Nothing except me being uncomfortably full at the end - the best feeling in the world. Â  yum yum yum
Interesting ice cream flavors and a great place for tea where you learn the correct/traditional process to drink. The wait took awhile, but otherwise it was a nice ending to a long night of food!

Fan-bloody-tastic is all i can say. The muscles are delicious, the beer is pure goodness and the palce itself makes me in a better mood just by walking into it. Came here with a group of 4 on a Saturday night and surprisingly there were lots of open tables. The staff is really attentive and courteous.

Business dinner here. Expected quite a lot from the place to be fair and it wasn't Locanda Verdi or Peasant. This is a notch below both those Italian eateries. But still good. Does that make sense? This is not the most innovative Italian place in terms of interior or food, but if unlike me you aren't expecting that and you want higher end Italian food that tastes good and is fresh, this is a good choice.

Fresh farm vegetables come right to the table. The make the most dimpliest dishes come to life with so much creativity and food is so super delicious. Great wine as well. A place I truly enjoy visiting but I wish making a reservation became easier, maybe the should expand.

Delicious in every way. The free wings are spicy and saucy Szechuan. The burger with their aioli is delicious. The fried chicken and cornbread waffle is a must- goes perfectly. The PB&J panna cotta was delicious and I hate PB&J- service was great and price is right.
huevos rancheros. amazing. egg, sausage sandwich. amazing.

This place is amazing. Everything from their sour cream to their hot sauces to their guacamole is home made from scratch and you can tell. The tacos are huge for the price! And they are open late! Best taco in ny.
I always love this spot. Great cafe con leech to start. Clearly the corn is great if you like cream and cheese. The steak and corn salad is a must!

I came here for the first time my birthday, based on the recommendation of a couple of my friends. Honestly? Â I thought this place was great. Â The cornbread came wrapped in waxed paper, piping hot with soft sticks of butter. Â Ordered just about every appetizer on the menu and I had the jambalaya for an entree. Â By the end, I was totally stuffed! Â I had a great time here, the food was good and the drinks were superb. Â The waitstaff and bartender were really pleasant and I would call the service exceptional. This place just isn't for meat lovers, my BFF, who is a devout vegetarian, came along and there were enough selections on the menu for her to choose from and not feel left out.

Searched for "brunch" on Google Maps. Thanks Google! The wait for Saturday brunch on 12/1 was about 40min for a table for two around 12:30pm, but we sipped mimosas on the sidewalk while we waited. And after less than 10 minutes, we were offered seats at the bar. This was great because the bartender had already given us great service when we ordered our drinks, and went out of his way to run outside and give me a book of matches after I told him I didn't have a light. The decor is classy, relaxing and comfortable. I tend to not pay attention to this sort of thing; usually when I "notice" something about the environment of a restaurant it's because something is off. So when I say I didn't notice anything, it's a compliment. It was warm and cozy, music was a quiet background murmur, and even though we were seated at the bar I didn't feel like I was crowded by the people on either side of us. I didn't even look at the regular menu, I was focused on the insert of brunch specials for the day. My friend and I decided everything looked so good that we would split (almost) everything. I had the hot apple cider with whiskey and cinnamon, and we took the spicy marinated olives, homemade ricotta w/ caramelized apples, and creamy spanish almond soup as they were ready. The soup was extremely rich and filling, I was surprised how good it was. The flavors of all three plates really complemented each other; and my friend and I both looked at each other in surprise after clearing our plates: we just got brunch without eggs and potatoes, didn't we? Minus the alcohol, we spent $20 on food. We left full and happy. Will be back.

Nice little pub close to Times Square. We got there around 5:30 and were able to get a seat by the window. Staff was very friendly with good service. We ordered drinks - fantastic beer selection including flights. The Brickyard salad was simple and light, the pork and veggie sliders were good - not best ever but solid. Overall very pleasant experience and we will return.
Nice atmosphere and brick wall!

Loved Ponty Bistro! The food was unique with a mixture of African and French spices and options and the service was outstanding. It is a small restaurant so it's more suited for a party of 2 or 4, but it wasn't especially loud. It's definitely not a cheap place, but for what you get it's more than reasonable. My wife and I shared the truffle mac and cheese and the french onion soup, which were great while I had the sirloin steak and my wife had a shrimp special and then we shared the french crepe for dessert. All excellent. We really enjoyed our meal and despite being seated for over 2 hours, we didn't once feel any pressure from the staff. They really couldn't be nicer. Highly recommended!

After Casa Mono, one of my favorite places, we followed up with Public. Public has been around for ages, back to the days when I lived in New York, but I had never gotten around to coming here. Â It's a great space. Â The food overall was extremely good, use of fresh, farm ingredients, in interesting combinations. Produce was first rate - the oysters and the venison were amazingly fresh, the combinations, such as the salsa verde and cabrales dumplings with venison were original and worked very well. We had initially planned on sharing the appetizers, but open the arrival of the foie gras (remember we had foie gras last night) and oysters, we decided I'd have the oysters and my friend would have the foie. Fried hama hama oysters with shiso, sansho peppers, and wasabi-yuzu dipping sauce - fresh oysters, perfectly deep fried which combined well with the peppers and the sweet, bitey sauce. I then had New Zealand venison loin perfectly prepared medium rare, tender and a nice gamey flavor, with salsa verde, on top of oyster mushrooms and cabrales dumplings, cabrales being a Spanish cheese, cows milk from the north of Spain, akin to a blue cheese. Sticky toffee pudding which reminded me of all those great sticky date puddings I had in Australia, so moist, sweet and rich, with Armagac ice cream, creamy with a bit of zing and hot toffee sauce.

Camaron del Pio as an appetizer, huge shrimp, wonderful guacamole and chips. We were happy from the start. Sangria kept us going, and the Matador Combo, recommmended by many, was more than sufficient for 3 of us, and would easily have served one or two more, as it comes with so many sides and offerings. Daniel J, below, posted a picture of Matador and all the parts,whichought to help I was too busy Â enjoying it all to remember to take a shot..

I took a long hiatus from yelp bc it was getting wayyy too repetitive writing review after review of the same thing. Â My creativity to explain delicious food & good service can only go so far, which is why I went from yelp enthusiast to ughhh no more! Â  However, brunch at Feast revived my desire to share all the goodness that comes with NYC brunch!! Â Feast was uhh-mazing. Â It's cozy, rustic free was legit especially on a cold NYC weekend. Â Our table was a repurposed antique sewing machine! Â The pedals were right by our feet, so adorbs. Some people in our party were late, but no one at Feast made a fuss or seemed to care even though they were busy. Â The brunch comes with a drink, entree, & an array of apps. Â We were given a bread basket, yogurt parfait, carrot juice shots, potato tart. Â Besides being beautifully presented, it was super fun for all of us to have little tastes of everything. Â It's a really great way to start off your brunch! All of the entrees are just the right size without making you fall over with the itis. Â The whole brunch experience was filling but at the same time, light enough for you to walk away to enjoy the rest of your careful Sunday afternoon. Â My smoked salmon was so delicately prepared with pieces of trout & poached quail eggs. Â I thought it was delicious but I don't think i would order it again but quite frankly, I can get smoked salmon at a lot of places. Â What I did love was my friend's souffle pancakes and I wholeheartedly dislike sweet entree dishes. Â It was so incredibly fluffy - a true blend of pancakes and a airy/light souffle. Â All of us had to stop ourselves from stealing bites of hers. Â Feast is a charming place to dine with friends! Â You'll leave filling full, having tried a variety of eats, chatting in a homely, rustic decor, and not suffering from itis!

This is a review of the place as a market: I've yet to sample any of the major food-stall like restaurants or rooftop beer garden. Â Yes, it's expensive, some prices are ridiculous. Â But it is possible to walk out with some amazing food without spending an arm and a leg. Â  I gotta say I am addicted to the 3-year old prosciutto and the house-made bocconcini...just exactly the right combination of smooth and saltiness. Â The fresh pasta is great too (I'm partial to the squid ink) only I wish the people in line in front of me would make up their minds! Â ("Can I have a few of the pea ravioli. Â Yes that's good. Â Oh, maybe a few more. Â Wait take a couple off and give me some tortellini instead...Oh maybe not...do you think it would be a good idea to serve both...?") Â Finally, the fruits and vegetables are really high quality (with the exception of patty pan squash which I love, but always look really sad here,) and while some is exorbitantly priced, most staples like onions and peppers and broccoli rabe costs no more than in the supermarket and is definitely fresher. Â The rotisserie chicken is good, tho. I think they must not serve much of it since they seemed to have scaled the rotis part of the store back. Â Wellfleet oysters are only 50-cents more a piece than I pay in Wellfleet. Â I've gotten some good bread here too. Â  I do not understand why the quality of the gelato is not as good here as other Battali outposts, but it's definitely a cut below here, and really the only real disappointment for me. Â Why?

The original pizza was awesome. A perfect balance between the salty crust, the sweetness of the tomato sauce, and the occasional high notes of the basil. The only thing we might change next time is to add extra cheese...and some beer.

First of all, I would like to apologize for entering this place looking like a hot mess. I was not expecting it to be as fancy as it was. Second, because it was so fancy, I was not expecting the food to be as amazing as it was. Getting that out of the way, I feel like my conscious is clear to continue. Brunch in Brooklyn has always been such a nightmare because there is always a ridiculous wait. But once we entered we were seated right away. However, once we were seated, our waitress disappeared for 10 minutes and I thought she was fetching water from a well. There were a lot of people and we realized how large this place was so I'm not docking any stars for that. Time may have also been going slower because I was starving. When she came back with our water we let her know we were ready to order drinks and food. The boyfriend and cousin were all with me and were craving the sweet taste of the south so we all ordered lemonades and sweet teas. Also, don't forget to redeem your free cornbread! It was basically perfect. Not too moist, not too dry, warm with a crunch outside and served with, what I think was, a compound honey butter. I saw on the menu that they make croutons with cornbread so I can imagine how delicious that would be. For the food, had the following: Clinton Hill Omelette- Meh. It was alright. I actually felt bad for the Boyfriend because my cousins and my food were amazing. I let him eat mine. Fried Chicken with Red Velvet Waffles- My food. We've been having really awful, thick waffles with Chicken and Waffles lately so this was a refreshing change. The waffle was warm, chewy, and had the red velvet goodness. The chicken was also delicious. It was a little greasy, but what the hell... I was eating chicken and waffles. Franks Red Sauce made it all the better so I was happy to have that on my table. Sausage and Grits with Lobster Sauce- My cousins was probably my favorite. I was hesitant to order grits because some places don't do it right. SoCo does it right! They were creamy and buttery and the lobster gravy that was on top of it made it all the better. We were there for a pretty long time but the wait was well worth it. I will definitely be returning looking like a million bucks!

The service was not good and the food was not great. Â I'll stick with the Smoke Joint. Â I had to wait a little too long to be seated. Â I had to remind the server to bring my drink. Â I had the Turkey Meatloaf sandwich for lunch with a side of macaroni and chesse, was not good. Â This place gets a thumbs down.

Maybe I'm just not a big halal person, but I thought this food was good and nothing more. Â Certainly enjoyed it, but didn't blow my mind. Â For $5, though, the chicken and rice is a fine deal, especially in the hustle and bustle of the Avenue of the Americas. Â The red sauce is super spicy, which I love. Â Beware if you have a sensitive tongue. As street fare goes, you could do a lot worse. Â I imagine this place is EXCELLENT drunk food, but I haven't had a chance to test that theory.

We've eaten at this place before and really liked their empanadas. So much that we decided to do catering as appetizers for our wedding. I placed the order online and worked with Patricia through the entire process via email. She was great! It was easy, quick and painless. We're so happy that the empanadas were a major hit among the guests and was all gone by the end of the night. The delivery arrived on time and was delicious! It was beautifully set up and served as a special part of my wedding. We ordered the breakfast; ham, cheese and pineapple; ground chicken and ground beef empanadas. Pretty layout on the trays. The green sauce is amazing! I wish I kept some for myself at the end of the night! When I purchase it separately, I love getting the sweet plantain and cheese and the breakfast the most.

Very good food but not worth waiting more than 10 minutes for as the nearby guys provide a very good substitute. The hot sauce / white sauce is what makes the whole thing special, remember to ask for extras if you are a spicy food guy like me.

Great brunch menu...awesome decor. Went on a Sunday around noon and it wasn't even packed, so I was able to quickly be seated at the chef's table. Had the brioche french toast and it was delicious. Definitely going to be back.

Its amazing... Its worth the wait once in a while if you can find a line that isn't around the block, but chances are you wont. However, go anyway... if its your first time you'll be blown away. Its just delicious. I consider myself a pizza expert/snob/connoisseur and I will not comment on whether or not its better than Lombardi's. They are both amazing. Both worth going to. I only leave out one start for the hassle it is to get to Brooklyn (although I've heard they opened a NYC location?) and the excessive line that almost unavoidable. Whatever it still rules.

Fried chicken is good. Just in life, it's a good good thing. At peaches? It's AWESOME. The batter is perfect - just the right crunch, with a bit of sugar, and salt and pepper. Ordered the Hot and was hoping it would be hotter than it was. This would probably qualify as a medium, especially in a place that's known for its hotness! But nevertheless, well played peaches. Side of kale was good. Side of Mac and cheese was good. Appetizer of fried catfish balls, so so. Appetizer of shrimps and crispy grits, pretty good but not amazing. Overall- just order the chicken and make sure it's hot!!

I wish I could give this place 3.5 stars, overall I had a good experience here. Â The restaurant seemed spacious but there was nothing memorable about the place. Â Nothing stood out. Â  What really stood out was the banchan and service. Â This was the first time I was served a fried fish as a banchan, and I have been to quite a few korean restaurants. Â They were also on top of refilling them, I love fishcake! Â  The food was a little on the overpriced side in my book. Â I decided to go with Dolsot Bi Bim Bap like always and it was not the best one I have ever had. Â It was decent, there wasnt that much food in there but it was pretty expensive. This restaurant is a solid choice but there are better values in ktown.
Good food, awesome ambience...an ideal date spot. However, we rushed out after discovering an army of ants planning their attack on the wall by our seats. Gross!

I'm so glad this place moved into the neighborhood. Â It's basically fast (good) food with beer. Â It has a nice, modern interior and plenty of seating. Â When you place your order, you get one of those little buzzers that goes off when it's ready. Everyone who works there has been very nice. I have had sushi rolls, chicken teriyaki, sweet potato fries, seaweed salad... all were great. Â But the most addictive item on the menu is the pork bun. Â It's the size of a hamburger or pulled pork sandwich. Â Braised pork topped with banh-mi-like veggies (think cucumbers, radish, carrots), a bit of bbq sauce and I think a hint of spicy mayo. Â It's a crack sandwich.

We went there with my wife for a date night. It was a great experience: the place is nice and cozy (we got the window table!). Service and food were great. We keep this place for our special occasions!

Ate at Thelma on Clinton this past weekend. Even though they are still ironing out some service glitches (no spoons with the soup etc.), this is an excellent addition to the neighborhood. Before stepping in, I was a little worried for a few reasons. First, I wasn't a huge fan of Salt Bar, Thelma's predecessor (same location and chef). Second, the small plates thing is a bit overdone with a new Tapas place opening practically every weekend. This is a completely different experience than Salt Bar. The atmosphere is completely updated and improved. The food is also far superior and much more interesting. The small plates aspect is actually fine. The plates aren't too small and the only tapas-esque dish in site is the bacon wrapped dates (I can forgive them for that one). The cauliflower soup, onion risotto and aforementioned dates were excellent. The only slight disappointment were the baby back ribs, which were slightly tough. Overall great experience. We will be back!
I would only go here drunk at two in the morning.

Best pasta I've ever had. Â The all you can eat deal lets you get 3 of Becco's homemade pastas for a really reasonable price. Â And it was delicious! Our table shared the meatball platter, the breaded shrimp, and the prosciutto plate, all of which was fantastic. Â I don't know much about wine, but my dining companion, who knows more, said the selection was extensive and appreciated the bartender's helpfulness and showmanship. The service was great, the atmosphere was inviting, and the evening was perfect. Â 5 stars!

Real Brazilian food and damn is it delicious. I had the Feijoada, billed as the national dish of Brazil and it was super filling and damn good. Washed it down with a Brazilian beer that tasted like Peroni. A little outdoor seating is nice if you can find a spot. I'd definitely go back.

I generally really like Balthazar and often refer to it as my favorite restaurant. They have a great fluke, and needless to say, their steaks are super delicious. Their oysters are just okay though, and I think that might be worth noting. I'm not sure how popular a dish it is, but for the price, I'd much rather get oysters elsewhere
Delightful dishes. Super fresh and great service! A must visit and if closer there is De Mole II.

I am impressed! I've walked past this bar many, many times and it doesn't look attractive at all from the outside (sorry). A group of us finally visited due to good reviews and I was REALLY happy with my experience. It's very casual with a bar in front but tables for sit-down food. The waiter was SUPER attentive and friendly, and we were a large group of 10-12. He helped us with our orders. I got the pork belly and I was not disappointed. Just enough fat and meat proportion. The wings & appetizers were also tasty. They also offered complimentary shots and took one with us, which seems like customary here from other reviews, but I like it! I'll come back just for the atmosphere. They had a good happy hour when we first arrived to, to stock up on a few tasty cocktails.

We were 5 people, seeing a show across the street, and needed a place nearby. I admit expectations were limited, but I have to say, we had a very good dinner here. Ambiance is bustling and hectic, and we had a large round table that was plenty roomy. Server was friendly, attentive and efficient. Knowing about the large portions, we were careful not to over order. We started with the fried calamari -- while the rings could've been fried a little darker, it was perfectly good, crispy and hot, and neither greasy nor rubbery. Next up was a caesar salad, also a pleasant surprise -- the romaine leaves were very fresh and crisp, and the dressing lightly applied tableside with a fresh lemony zing and not too salty. We only ordered two mains -- chicken scarpariello (whole bird version) and linguine with shrimp (subbing garlic & oil for marinara sauce). We opted for the chicken with roasted potatoes, peppers and Italian sausage, and it arrived on an enormous oval platter -- we couldn't finish it, but it was delicious: hot, flavorful and garlicky with juicy meat, good sausage, charred peppers, crisp potato chunks and a nice, winey sauce. The shrimp tasted fresh enough and formed a nice, lighter counterpart to the hearty chicken. We had a Rutherford cab to wash it all down and were out with time to spare for the show. A very good alternative to Trattoria Trecolori (which I also like for pre-theater), especially with a larger group (say 5+).

For my first visit, I asked the staff to recommend a sandwich. The cashier suggested the "Hemingway" cuban sandwich with ham and pulled pork. After a short wait, the sandwich was hot and ready. It was delicious, not too spicy, and huge!!! I could not finish it. (They also sell Mexican Coca-Cola in cute glass bottles, very 50's)

The pizza was great, I shared the margharita pizza with my sister but I wish I had gotten my own to eat all by myself. The overall atmosphere was pleasant, and Saraghina is definitely a place both where the family can get together and have a fun meal and two people can have an intimate date by themselves. My only complaint is that while the staff was friendly, they definitely did not cater to their customers' needs during my visit. It took forever for our waiter to even notice we had finished our meal, and only then did he tell us that the place only took cash payments. We did not see any signs or indications that this was the case, and my sister had to leave and get cash from a nearby store. The waiters and waitresses seemed to rush between tables and overall Saraghina seemed very understaffed.

Staying away from the Smith, for sure. This was my second time there in two weeks -- I was there for a private party last week and the food and service were both underwhelming but I figured it was the catering aspect that didn't work. Â  Then I went today for brunch and the waitstaff was even more fake than they were last week. Â I don't understand Â the point of hiring "attractive" service people -- I want my waitstaff to be genuine and efficient, end of story. Â These wannabe actors were neither. We went for brunch today and while it always hurts to pay $10 for a glass of Cristalino, it's business as usual in NYC. Â What is unforgivable is when I ordered the "eggs anyway" brunch plate, they refused to add mushrooms to my scrambled eggs. Â I offered to pay extra. Â I asked if I could have the mushroom omelet, only to have the eggs scrambled instead of made into an omelet. Â The very young waiter again snidely refused, with an "I'm sorry" that was so disingenuous as to be offensive. Â My $3 cup of coffee went unrefilled throughout brunch. Â No one asked us if wanted another glass of overpriced champagne. In this economy, a $30 brunch is going to mean something and I will not be returning to the Smith, unless they start hiring grownups and learn about customer service. I'm stunned this is owned by the same people as Jane.
Awesome food.... Great staff... My Fav in NYC.... I now live and Tokyo and always find my way back for the Lobster Cannelloni... Best in the world.
Where can you get a PB&J, a delicious beer on tap, AND play Connect Four and/or Buck Hunter Safari or a "Dark Knight" pinball machine?... ...The Levee! Gotta love it.
I couldn't decide between 4 and 5 stars. These are some good soup noodles!

Petite Abeille has gained notoriety from being featured on some TV shows and news articles, etc. I came here with some family looking for a good place for brunch in the area. It's very cute, has a nice vibe, and seems versatile in it's appeal, from families to young couples to tourists. We were seated promptly at a cozy table near the bar area, our server was nice and patient with one of my family members who is hard of hearing. I ordered eggs benedict, my other family members ordered an array of different sandwiches and some drinks even (full bar). Service was impeccable, my water glass was always full, and we were consistently checked on even though the place was pretty packed. The menu was revised recently apparently, it's a bit small, with your average breakfast and brunch choices, nothing that really stood out in my eyes. My eggs benedict (sans ham of course) was delicious, the hollandaise sauce is house made and it showed. While they are known for their waffles (which are large in portion and looked delightful), I am glad I went with the eggs benedict. All of my family members were happy with their choices from the burger to a salmon and dill sandwich, all portions were large, moderately priced, and full of good flavors. I would not hesitate one bit to come back here with people visiting, unless they are vegetarian for the options are lacking.

Shockingly disappointing performance. Â I brought a large group of people in from out of town that have been eagerly anticipating the Ngam I have been touting for months. Â To my shock we experienced inattentive/dismissive staff, long delayed/poorly timed/incomplete food delivery, and overcooked duck. Â My party received the food delivery at several different times. Â Such a difference in time that the people that received their food first had finished and were clearing dishes before the last people received their meals. Â When my "Cutie Duck" arrived it was anything but cute. Â It appeared to have been cooked beyond the edible point on the majority of the plate. Â I then pointed this out to the waitress and she just smiled and had no explanation nor provided any form of options to rectify the situation. Â They were just more than eager to push out the "check" and turn the table. Â Chef Hong please bring back the Ngam I know and love....
Service and raspberry martini was great... Pasta with scallops was over cooked. Good but nothing special about the food, disappointed but will be back to try the brunch!

I had a great meal at Burger & Barrel on Friday night. Â The waitress was really friendly, the food was delicious (just got the classic burger with sweet potato fries- I really liked the secret sauce, might have been the first time I didn't need to put ketchup on a burger), and the atmosphere was warm and classy, so it still felt like a nice date spot even though you are chowing down on burgers. Â It's also conveniently located across the street from the Angelika, making it the perfect spot to grab dinner either before, or after catching a movie. Lastly- maybe I have just gotten used to the 60 calorie chocolate pudding packs.... but I thought Burger & Barrel's homemade pudding and cookie dessert was out of this world!

I've been to Brindle before, great-homey dishes. Â I booked a large birthday party dinner that is coming up soon and they offer a great prix-fixe. Â I'll round back with the full details of that party -- Brindle Room hope it's just as great for my party!!!!
Went here to eat with a friend. I ordered the blueberry pancakes, and I loved it., the Mimosa's were great and the ambiance was really cozy. Great place for brunch!!!
Definitely tops my tapas favorites list. Tiny space, so get ready to squeeze in when you can. Bold flavors, good wine, festive setting. Everyone's there to eat good food and have a good time.

Got to "The Pines" at 6:30 on a Friday and was delighted to hear they had an open table, even though reservations are highly recommended (wish it said that on their site). just had dinner here with my wife and thought the food was OK but a little greasy

This place was awesome. I came into town one weekend and met up with some old friends and it was suggested we go here. And a great decision it was. They are known for a long wait, so we put our name down and they told us 4 hours! I have never been given a 4 hour wait time in my life for any restaurant, so now we have to try it. Well, while at a friends apt nearby, sure enough they called after about an hour and a half and we got right in. The atmosphere is really cool. We sat in one of the big square booths as we were a lot of us. There were so many people waiting when we got there and it was so cold out. We ordered a few things to start: Tako Wasabi (raw baby octopus), I didn't like this at all, it was sour and spicy, two things that don't go together and I love octopus. The Hirata Buns which were delicious, the Ippudo Teba Gyoza, and the Samurai Rib. Those were excellent. For dinner we ordered the Kogashi Miso Ramen and the Akamaru Modern. They were amazing. I wish I had access to this place, I would go all the time. They don't take reservations but I find this place worth the wait.

With about a 4 block walk from the G train, I arrived at Nam Nam, which is located closer to corner of Â Manhattan Avenue and Leonard Street. Â The decor is not bad. Yellow painted walls with classy paintings on it. Â There are about 8 to 10 cushioned seats total, some wooden tables. Â The owner is very friendly. I asked him which banh mi to get. He suggested the pork, so that is exactly what I got. I like all of these options, but I couldn't decide. Â They have cold cut, pork, chicken and vegetarian sandwiches. I did ask about the facilities, being that I needed to use them, and he explained to me that their bathroom is out of order, so we could use the deli's water closet next door. Â So keep this in mind! Â I am compelled to mention this because I ordered the iced Vietnamese espresso with condensed milk before I knew this. (Why, oh why?) Â I wanted to let you know that their banh mi is amazing and worth traveling over to Montrose Ave. Â Closest train is G at Broadway and B46 from Kings Plaza. Â I did see a L train stop somewhere close by, but I think it's like a 15 minute walk over here. Â On the way from the train, I saw an auto repair shop, a wholesale meat seller, and an amazing savings. Â I really did enjoy my sandwich. Â The bread was really crunchy(toasted), the carrots were pickled just right, and the mayo has a hint of garlic(just in case you despise the lingering tasty smell of it), and the meat was delicious. Â The cilantro and cucumber was fresh and made the smells of banh mi mouthwatering. Â I need to state that a few pieces of the pork had cartilage so you have to chew thoroughly or just rid of it. Â I believe that my espresso was so strong that my eyes started blinking less. Â This is a great place for studying, since it is quiet. Most people take their orders to go and no one really sits here for long. Â They have great big window doors to let the natural sunlight in. That makes me happy! Â (that and the good food, that is!)

I'm not really sure how to write this review or rate Scarpetta... As soon as we walked in, our party of four was immediately happy with the inviting, yet cool atmosphere. Inviting bar and pay special attention to belts on the mirrors in the dining room...I like. The bread basket was wonderful and the cheese and pancetta bread was a nice touch. We had the short ribs with farro and seared sea scallops with sunchokes as our appetizers. Both were delicious and I would happily order again. As we were not too hungry (late lunch) we decided to order three pastas and share. 1. A friend ordered the rabbit cavatelli. Alright, so I wasn't brave enough to try the rabbit, but the pasta tasted like it was made in my friend's grandma's kitchen in Firenze. Just perfect. 2. Black tagliolini, a squid ink homemade pasta with lobster. Perfectly light, flavorful and overall delectable. Order this dish if you like simple wonderful textures and flavors. 3. Beet and ricotta ravioli with pistachios. This dish makes me want to giggle with happiness as it consists of three of my favorite flavors. The ravioli was paper thin, perfect and filled with the most gorgeous rich concoction. Not only did it taste wonderful, but splitting it in half and seeing the beautiful red pop out of the pasta with the green pistachio touch was a visual treat. The food was sensationally delicious. Every bite was an explosion of freshness and subtle yet lasting flavor. However, with all of this said, we had one of the worst waiters...ever. He was abrupt, rude and didn't pay any attention to us at all. As soon as he realized we weren't going to order the whole menu, we were ignored. Annoying waiters never bug me...I live in LA, it's filled with stuck up people who WORK at posh places...however, this waiter rubbed us all the wrong way. Up to the point where this was my birthday dinner and we decided to forgo the birthday candle and head to our next location. We all have a deep respect for the service industry and always tip 20%. For the first time ever, we tipped less than 15%. I do not think this one waiter reflects the whole restaurant as the ladies in the front of house were lovely as were the people I made reservations with. So, I'm rating it at 4 stars based on the wonderful food and dÃ©cor and taking of a star for the waiter....but really, the food deserves a 5.

Excellent selection of Thai food that sometimes borders on unusual. Nice to see a Thai establishment that doesn't play by the usual standard fare. Also, prices are surprisingly excellent not only for NYC, but by any standard.
The drink tasted like cranberry juice. Â The steak was good but extremely small. The mash was decent. Their macaroni and cheese is what keeps people coming back.

So I was excited to take my fiancÃ© out to dinner to a fancy french wine bar and after a 20 min walk we were pumped to have our socks knocked off. We went around 8 and the place was PACKED. Luckily I had made an appointment the day before, but seemed like people were coming and going easily. First thing we noticed is that it's pretty stuffy and the tables (and people) are very close together and loud. I personally don't like that atmosphere, and I understand it's a wine BAR but I expected a little more.. Class maybe? The host was a gentleman, our waiter.. Not so much. He seemed a little snooty and rolled his eyes at our simple dinner order (and seemed offended we didn't stay for dessert!) The dinner menu is honestly pretty pricy (but, then again it's NYC..) I can't spare any stars because of personal preference because the food was honestly amazing. We ordered the salmon crostini's which were so so good! My fiancÃ© ordered the FrisÃ©e Salad (delicious! I nicknamed it the "manly" salad.. It had bits of bacon and a poached egg on top.. It was a really yummy hot salad) and I had the Classic Amelie salad.. Which was also delicious. Everything was super fresh, but we didn't even want to stay for dessert. It was way too crowded for my taste and it felt like we were on the couples date that sat next to us (I could hear everything this girl was saying and found it hard to even carry a conversation with my own date!!) But, it is a typical bar scene and if you're looking to just hang out and order some wine- this place is perfect. I suppose it's a good place to bring a date you don't really wanna talk too? The food is very delicious, but for the price and the atmosphere, you could probably find something better (at least for my personal preference)

I ate here last night and was thoroughly impressed. I started off with a papardelle dish with pork (in sausage form), spinach, and parmesan and it was outstanding. I followed this with a braised pork dish that was good, but could have been hotter. However, it came with a side of something that resembled either couscous or mashed potatoes and was cheesy; it was downright delicious and improved the entire plate. My cousins got the pollo ala daviola which had great seasoning and has been good every time we've come. Also, two other pasta dishes, a carbonara and a fettucine style dish, were both delightful to the tongue. We had a meat platter as an appetizer and the prosciutto was high-quality and flavorful, and another meat, I believe called Cotta or something similar, was reminiscent of roast pork. I liked it, but the rest of my family wasn't so big on it (more for me). We had a great wine from Austria's Sudtirol region---a red--- that was a great choice. A piquant start and fruity aftertaste. I will seek it out again. I will definitely return here and recommend this to friends.
Always great, love this place! The tagine is my favorite!

So...Debbie is a TERRIBLE waitress. Â She was inattentive and complained about how tired she was. Â Quite a few times we tried to get her attention but she looked so frazzled and ignored us. Great falafel sandwich and I tried the gyro So good, the meat has a crispy charcoal taste that I love.

So my brother and I had reservations in the city to celebrate his birthday, but he decided he would rather stay local. I heard of Il Falco from a co-worker who had never been there, but heard amazing things about it. I am so glad we chose to dine here tonight; so much so that I am writing my first ever yelp review. Just like someone had mentioned, it was our first time there but we felt like regulars. The waiters greeted us by name (which they got from the reservation), had the chef personally come to our table to say hello, and provided excellent service, including crumb service (my personal favorite). The ambiance was wonderful; dim lighting, cozy, old-school feel. The complimentary zucchini and bruschetta that was served at the beginning was delicious, and a perfect precursor to the rest of the meal. We had an outstanding lobster appetizer (it was $50, but well worth it). My brother had the veal chop and I had the Branzino (served whole and deboned table side). We ordered the pineapple dessert where they heat fresh pineapple on a skillet and marinate it with caramel sauce and grand marnier (nice spectacle to watch, with flames and all). We had a pretty inexpensive bottle of red wine ($40), which was great. The staff served us shots of grappa on the house, and we finished our meal with two single espressos. It was a FANTASTIC meal, and I wholeheartedly rate them with 5 stars. it's a must go-to Italian restaurant in LIC.

Still wonderfully delicious. The best fries you can ever have. Ordered a regular and was enough to share for 2. Tried the Vietnamese pineapple mayo and sweet mango chutney ($1 each) and neither disappointed. Even saved the rest of the sauces to bring back home with us. A satisfying pre-dinner snack.
This place is so awesome. I can't recommend the pork buns enough. And everything on the menu is good (so far)--even the raw octopus with wasabi! Wish they took reservations.

I loved this place- no, I LOVED this place! I have nothing but good things to say about Barbuto's food. It's classic and simple and I want to keep eating every bite that I had over and over and over. From the menu, it doesn't look like you can go wrong, but I can highly recommend the pork belly and figs (I suppose the only complaint would be it was kind of too big a portion, but also I would have eaten seven, so never mind), the roast chicken (also an enormous portion, and I also never wanted it to end), and the chocolate pudding and chocolate tart. And if that wasn't enough, it's a nice, friendly place with excellent service. Is that enough good things? Can I go again now?

I rarely give 5 star ratings to restaurants but this place deserves 5 stars. Both the waiters were from France, and enjoyed chatting with the customers. Its a small restaurant but we had no problem getting a table late on a Sunday night. My friend and I started off with a small carafe of wine (I love the way they have different sizes so you can choose accordingly to your needs). For our main dish, we shared a Tourto Marianne Beef and a Tourte Marianne Veggie. It was like a quiche almost but with puff pastry on top and below. The beef one was pretty much the most amazing meatloaf ever. The veggie version was delicious. The waiter told me he disliked vegetables but he liked this dish, and it was amazing! It didn't feel like I was eating Â vegetables. I really wanted the Tourte Marianne Salmon but they ran out... The most popular desert dish that everyone ordered was the Calba Tartes Sucrees, which is a thin crispy "pizza" with apples, cinnamon and Calvados brandy. The waiter came out with the brandy lit on fire and literally poured the fire onto your desert. It was delicious as well. My friend commented that a scoop of vanilla ice cream would be perfect on top of our desert. You can choose to add Nutella for $1. I can't wait to come back for yet another delicious meal!

Such a quaint place! perfect for a cute date night or dinner with old friends. The corn crab chowder was AMAZING. & we loved their signature dish, the Cioppino, as the broth was the perfect compliment to the seafood. I definitely will go back!

This place is absolutely amazing hands down. Â The food was cooked perfectly. Â The service was outstanding. Â  We had the chicken coconut soup and chicken pad thai. Â There is a Thai restaurant in Queens that I love, and TukTuk will give them a run for their money. Â  I'm so happy that we found this little GEM in LIC. Â My husband and I will be coming back again soon!!

Had the grossest dinner I've had in a while at this place. The first time I dined here wasn't a good experience.. My 2nd visit last night was extremely different.
