With this being said, I will only dine at Peaches for dinner....you've won me over. ;) TIP: Try the warm brownie/ice cream dessert with the "Bundle Up" drink! (heaven) lol

My favorite Thai restaurant in UES! Â I don't think they're BYOB anymore, but we managed to make it work by feigning ignorance :) I went with a group of girl friends and we split several things and all were delicious. Â There wasn't a stand out dish because everything was amazing and I could never pick just one thing. Â I think this place is undiscovered because we were able to walk-in sans reservation and there were no issues. Â  Ambiance/ vibe is really cool, too. Â Totally coming back here.

I came here the other night for a drink with a friend. The ambiance is quite nice and the staff amicable and friendly. The cocktails, though tasty and well made, will definitely put a dent in your wallet! However, if you're feeling fancy this is a good go-to spot.

I never made it to SHO, so when I read that Shaun Hergatt was opening a new place, I was excited. Â My partner and I went last Thursday, 8/22. Yes, it's a splurge: Â 4 courses for $90, 6 for $120, and the tasting menu for $180, but well worth it. The space is quiet, elegant and restrained. Â The decor is not perfect, but it is very nice. Â I very much like the menu format: with the 4 and 6 course meals, you can create your own meal: there are 5 categories: cold apps, hot apps, fish, meat and dessert - with 3 choices each, and you can chose any of the 15 for each course - great flexibility. (I use a 3 star rating system for each course, based on the Michelin restaurant rating system) Â  They served 3 amuses: a carrot tulle with goat cheese - **, a corn chowder custard - ***, and a wild mushroom ragout (or something) - **/***, all excellent - and they gave us 2 of each, so fortunately, ghw912's experience was not repeated here. summer squash - langoustine - naval orange reduction - marigold: Â ** (out of ***) Three well-sized Langoustine in a squash puree. The meat and sauce were very delicate and lively. Â I think the citrus notes were a little strong, and some of the meat was just slightly soft - overcooked I think. Still, quite wonderful. satur farms toy box tomatoes - bush basil - tomato gelÃ©e - blue basil flowers - * My partner's dish - I only had a taste. Â We are both familiar with Satur Farms' produce, and we both felt that this was tasty, but not at the level it should be - the tomatoes ARE the dish, and they were good, but not overwhelming with flavor like great heirlooms or Satur at their best. potato fondant - black bass - flourless gnocchi - curls - truffle sabayon: *** Just fabulous. This was laid out like a village with the Bass at the center. Each element was great, and the combination of flavors when I took bites together was sublime. Â The bass was done perfectly - light but rich in flavor with succulent skin. The gnocchi were airy with explosive chive flavor, and the sabayon was transcendent. My only issue was that there were fennel buds on top of some components, and I hate fennel, but I easily took them off and put them to the side. I think their flavor was too strong for the dish anyway. purple artichokes - ravioli - sylvetta arugula - pinenuts: ** My partner's dish. I have a food aversion to artichokes, but I can eat them occasionally if they are done exceptionally well, as they were here. Â Substantial artichoke ravioli. My Partner was thrilled with these and rightly so - great texture and flavor - light with a nice chewiness in the filling and a great juxtaposition between the dough and the inside. Â  anise hyssop - grimaud duck - chef's garden candy beets - hibiscus jus: *** When I took a bite of the duck, it was so rich and flavorful (and I eat A LOT of duck) that I actually said 'WOW' out loud. Â Juicy and rich, but firm. Â I was worried about the anise hyssop, but it was delicious and spicy, Â adding some rough texture to the creamy duck and an earthiness/vegetal/spiciness. Â The Beets were ok, and the jus was like a sweet, super-concentrated gravy - divine. Â Overall, one of the best duck dishes I have ever had. peaches and cream - cucumber - basil: ** This was my dessert. It was a dollop of peach ice cream on a layer of basil ice, I think - with cucumber yogurt mixed with peaches underneath. Â To be honest, this wasn't my exact style of dessert, with the yogurt and vegetal aspects, but it was so complex and tasty that it won me over. Â So many different textures and flavors combining. Frozen meringue - lemon - blueberry - sage: *** My partner's dessert. Â Wow, just wow. Â Now THIS is my type of dessert. After a few bites, I told K that she better take it back or I would finish it. Â The richness and sweetness of the light meringue were offset by the crisp and tart of the fruit, and the herbal essence of the sage. Â K referred to it as a 'deconstructed pavlova' and I think that is right on. Â  The petite fours were black mission fig beignets - ***, beet tulle - */**, anise leaves in chocolate - *, and nougat with celery salt - ***. Â The beignets were some of the best things we have eaten in the last year, and the nougat with celery salt was a crazy but brilliant combination that worked perfectly. Overall, the food was delicate, complex, focused, somewhat innovative, and delicious. Â As you can see from my ratings, there were a number of high notes, and the mean was consistent enough to categorize it as great. The service was very good, still finding its groove in places, but our primary server (Jason, I believe) was so good, spectacular actually, that I give the service the highest marks. Â The wine list is small, seasonal, and focused on solid boutique producers. Â I had a glass each of Riesling, Morgon VV, and Moscato D'Asti - all very good and reasonably priced. Â Overall, I would say that Juni is a welcome addition to the top tier restaurants in NYC, and I look to going back.
Perfect place to get a light dinner before seeing Stomp, a half block away. The place is very cozy. The menu is simple and the food is good. Bacon sliders were very tasty.

We went to Cuba for my boyfriend's birthday and all 8 of us loved the experience. The food was great, the drinks were strong, Â and the waiters were very nice. We sat in a small cozy room w/ drapery on the ceiling and at times the room got very loud with live music from the front room, but the music didn't last all night. We started with ceviche, which was as delicious it can get. I had a paella dish and my boyfriend had skirt streak. Another friend had chicken stuffed with shrimp. That was everyone's favorite.

After being a Yelp voyeur for almost a year, I've decided to break my silence after my experience last night at Ilili. Â While their food is four stars, I'm hoping Ilili will realize that although they are located next door to 230 Fifth, they don't need to covet thy neighbor's attitude. Â  First off the space is really cool, although the many mirrors can be a bit confusing (both me and my friend, who arrived separately, almost walked into the mirror by the entrance). Â We decided to start off with drinks and apps in the lounge, but asked the hostess if there would be a wait for table if we wanted to have a full dinner. She kindly assured us that there would be none. Â  Once seated, our lounge waitress seemed a bit overwhelmed when we told her we simply wanted appetizers, unsure whether to give us the prix fixe restaurant week menu or the regular one. Â She was visibly calmed when we asked for both. Â  I ordered the Lebanese wine, which was the first I had tasted from the region and it was amazing. Â For apps, we had hummus and babaghanoush, which were both great and accompanied by incredibly fresh, delish, honey-flavored pitas. Â  An hour-later, we decided to get a table for dinner, but were told by our bouncer-esque hostesses that there was now a twenty-minute wait. This would not have not been an issue at all, if the two-floor restaurant was not half-empty. Â Both the first dining room, which caters mostly to large groups had about four empty tables, and the second floor, where we sat, was lined with at least five empty tables for two. Â  I don't mind waiting for a table at a great restaurant, but no need to create an illusion. Maybe the mirrors confused her? Once seated, our new waitress was so friendly that we didn't mind her overly apologetic attitude as our food was continually slow to arrive. Â We ordered more apps, graped leaves and chankleech, a deliciously-seasoned feta, onion and tomato salad. Â We then moved on to kebabs, lamb for my friend, tuna for me. Both yummy....for dessert we ordered the Essmalieh, a napoleon of shredded philo and Achta (like clotted cream) sprinkled with shredded pistachios. It took almost 15 minutes to come, but was soo yummy, that after four hours at Ilili, it almost made me forget about the service issues, which were further acquiesced by complimentary baklava. Dinner was about $50 each, not to bad, considering what we ordered. Â If I'm craving great Mediterranean food I make a reso and go back, but I'd probably be happier at Mamouns.

The food is excellent, but ever since this very popular restaurant has expanded a few years ago, you don't feel treated as special as the smaller Thai establishments in Queens, and that makes a difference. It has sort of become an atmosphere close to a soup kitchen, they serve your food and bring your check as soon as possible. That being said, it's still delicious and a good bet when things are not too crowded. They do not dumb-down the spicy dishes for non-Thais or sweeten everything like most in Manhattan. I also like to peruse their dessert case and grab something sweet for the ride home.

BEWARE: Bad Management has Taken Over I have been to Sushi Yasuda a number of times, all for lunch, and enjoyed the fresh quality sushi. Â  I am disturbed, however, by the treatment we received the last time we went for lunch. Â Like so many other times we have been there, we ordered the sushi lunch special. Â We told our waitress, and the sushi chef. Â  However, when the bill came, they charged us for a la carte, which was more than twice the price of the special. Â  I have never seen this "manager" before, but I think he needs to be taught some manners on how to treat customers. Â He was so rude I may never go back. Â I heard that the ownership was changing hands - I hope this isn't a sign of the future.

Love the Meatball Shop. It's calling my name as I type. Granted, my first and only trip AS OF YET, the veggie of the day was the glorious red beet, which I have a bit of thing for, so right there I was sold. Â As far as crowded noisy complaints go, I've been in NY for less than a year and I don't mind. Yeah, people are close, but it's an experience, and who goes on a date to the meatball shop? (nevermind, awesome people go on a date to the meatball shop.) No one is getting engaged there, you don't need initimacy. A friend and I went on a weeknight around 9 and waited for about 15 minutes, and then ended up eating at the bar because well, we were hungry and didn't mind. There's a place to sit, a place to put your food, what's unacceptable about this? Â Newcastles are 4 bucks, which is great, and the wines were moderately priced. I'm a sucker for risotto and beets, so my plan was to incorporate those into my meal, no matter what. Â I skipped the sandwiches and went for spicy pork balls with red sauce over risotto. Â I wasn't sure that it would work in a way other than "I like all this stuff so no matter what I will eat it", but it totally did. Â DELICIOUS. The risotto was with corn and chaterelle mushrooms, and was perfectly done. I got a side of the daily vegetable, BEETS, with some fresh ricotta, and just went to town on those. Perfectly roasted. My friend got spicy pork balls with polenta (which was some decent polenta!) and creamy parmesan sauce, and the house salad. Way good, but I was too happy with my food to get too distracted.. We skipped dessert (I know, a travesty.) because we were so damn full. Â But it's worth saying that I had leftovers and when I heated them up in the morning, my roommate who lives on the other end of the apartment and never emerges, came out to ask what I was eating. I shared the joy that is the meatball shop!
If you could grow a pizza plant and eat it right off the vine this is what you would get. Phenomenal.
Vegetarian Chinese, safe bet!

Yes, Eataly is 50,000 square feet of all things dedicated to Italy. Â And 50,000 square feet in Manhattan is a LOT of space. Â And yet, somehow it felt as though I was walking in Time Square with all the people around. Â Yes, there's a lot of food for take out (fresh bread, full fish, meat and fresh pasta stations, desserts, etc). Â There are also 6 restaurants (pizza, pasta, vegetable, fish, rotisserie and the one high end one), many with hour long waits. And yes, this is opening night. Â And yet, as flustered as the waiters/maitre d'/chefs were, they managed to stay gracious and friendly while dealing with all of us. Â  There's a LOT of Italian spoken here from the waitstaff to the chefs (pastry chef who was delivering a tray of his goodies at least). Â In fact, if you're Italian, I believe this may become the new embassy. Â And if you like Italian (food/people/culture), this is definitely where you should be. We tried the desserts (the rice fruit mini cake and the tiramisu) and both were delicious. Â The dark chocolate of the tiramisu offsets the creaminess of the sponge cake perfectly. Â The rice fruit cake is light and yet balanced. Â It's not too sweet and yet no one could accuse it of being bland. Â All in all, these are some of the best desserts I've had anywhere, much less "to go counters". Â  We also had dinner at the fish restaurant. Â Wait for 2 was about 30 mins and Mario Battali just happened to be in the kitchen when we sat down. Â We ordered the smoked fish of the day (salmon) and the grilled fish of the day (ordara). Â Served head and tail on, the fish was perfectly cooked, juicy enough despite the skin not being soggy at all. Â The smoked salmon, well, I'm biased b/c I've not yet seen smoked salmon I didn't like. Â  I should also mention that we broke a wine glass as we sat down. Â The staff was so fast and efficient in how they handled the situation that instead of feeling ashamed and leaving soon after, we then lingered over dinner for over an hour. I used to work across the park from here and if I still did, I probably would eat lunch here every day for the next few weeks. Â As it is, I'll have to just stop by and pick up food to go. Â Having said all this, be patient and be prepared to wait in line.
great food love this place. the burgers were good.

Anyone eating at any other BBQ place in NYC, IS WASTING THEIR TIME!!!! Â This has to be, by far, the BEST BBQ I HAVE EVER HAD!!!!!! I can't go into detail about any one thing, because everything was great. From the brisket, to the short ribs, to the brisket baked beans, OMG! Â The only reason why I can't give this place five stars is because it needs to be BIGGER!!!!! Â But the quality is unmatched, and well worth the wait. You will see a lot more check ins from me here!!!!!
Really cozy place for friday or for another day.

It was good, loved the cucumbers and tomatoes, but they are so shiesty with the hot sauce. Seriously TWO tiny little drops and it was only topped on the veggies. Once you got down to the falafel - nothing else was there. I prefer Maoz.

Went here for a friend's bday. The food, service and atmosphere were great. If you are looking for something casual, good food and not expensive this is the best place to go. I don't usually eat pork but Espresso BBQ "Costillitas" was amazing.

Holy Seafood Tower Batman!!! Â My wife ate here a couple years ago and always raved about Le Balthazar, which is an enormous raw seafood tower featuring fresh lobster, crab legs, clams, oysters, snails, shrimp and a shrimp and calamari salad. Â I was visiting the city from Houston and we made reservations well in advance of our trip. Â I was not disappointed at all in the Seafood Tower. Â I even got one of my good friends to try (and ENJOY) oysters from the tower. Â The tower also comes with a great cream sauce which I highly recommend (also comes with the classic cocktail sauce). Â My meal could have ended here but no Yelper would stop with an appetizer. Â As a true eater, my entre was the Steak Frites which I would describe as above average, especially after having the amazing seafood tower. Â The BÃ©arnaise sauce on the steak was creamy and provided the steak with the extra flavor kick that it needed. I would definitely like to come back and try the Onion Soup as I had to pass on the hot summer night that I went.

Yum. Had eggs benedict and a bloody mary on a beautiful sunny Friday afternoon. Okay, when I walked in it was morning. Server was great...and she was from Chicago. Go figure. Food and drinks are very good and the service is great. The benedict comes on biscuits, which is way better than english muffins. The bloody comes with a pickled egg and strip of bacon. Who wouldn't like that? Front doors/windows were wide open and gave it a nice open airy feel on an 80 degree day. Walked up Columbus and down Amsterdam til I found this place. Was exactly what I was looking for.
Great food, small place. Â Only takes cash so watch out for that! Service is very speedy and the pizza is as good as advertised. Â  The perfect pizza would be a pepperoni with extra mozzarella!

This is a very nice looking restaurant. Â The inside screams swank and chic. I came here with my boo as one of our first restaurants when dining out here. They had no problem sitting our group of 4 down with a bunch of random strangers. Â This happened twice. Â Once as we sat down at the long table behind the chandelier - a group was already seated there. Â The second time happened as the other group got up and a new group sat down right next to us. Â It wasn't that bad, I'd prefer that over having to wait. The food I thought was alright. Â I wasn't wowed by it, and then again I wasn't repulsed either. Â With so many thai options on this street, I wouldn't come back until I've tried them all.

Dekalb is amazing! Â I feel like my words can not even do it justice, but I shall try... Â The restaurant its-self is inspiring, made of all reclaimed wood, and the old hospital windows lining the ceilings and walls cause the vibes from the awesome band to flow throughout without being loud. Â The Staff is friendly, and is eager to welcome you to the neighborhood. Â  The Mussels are served in a creamy salsify and leek broth, and the portion is generous. Â I found myself looking for more items than just the grilled bread into the broth, at one point I think I may have just been eating it with a spoon. The Polenta fries, infused with banana, smothered in a leek ragout, and topped with crispy Serrano ham.....someone sure knows the way to a womans heart! Â The perfect combination of crispy, creamy, salty, savory, and je ne sais quoi! The Lamb exceeded my already high expectations for it...fork tender, melt in your mouth, braised goodness! Â served with perfectly cooked root vegetables and crispy kale which added the perfect texture to the soft lamb...ugh still dreaming about it 5 days later the panna cotta sort of blew my mind...now I graduated from culinary school, and I have experienced panna cotta quite a bit in top restaurants, even made it myself...but NEVER have I experienced a panna cotta this creamy, this rich, this.....addictive! Â I have never been a huge fan of panna cotta, I could take it or leave it usually but the panna cotta with caramel 'glass' Â had the texture of an insanely creamy cheesecake!! I can't even fathom how they managed to achieve this velvety, decadent mouth-feel but needless to say I will be back...to try every last item on the menu, hang out with the friendly staff and take in the good vibes! Â The only downside of Dekalb is that I don't live in Brooklyn!

Order the truffle fries. They are yummy. The decor is also pretty cool, it says 'hipsters with money'. Behind me was a stack of vinyl records and bartender with some nice tattoos. You know the drill. Jars instead of water glasses, a lot of visible raw materials, wood, metal, etc...Though as far as trendy restaraunts/bars go, I didn't see any taxidermy... I also was sitting next to a rather famous celebrity. It was a fun time. I would go back!

Their hand pulled noodle clumped together in the broth and they were softer than what i have wanted. Â Overall the broth and the noodles were tasty. Â I ordered the boiled dumplings on the side and mixed them into my noodle soup. Â Nice combination! Â The dumplings were real tasty especially for $2 . Â Great place to go to in the winter. Â Place was a dive of a place but had its own chinatown character. Â The place is off the beaten track on the outskirts of chinatown and you can watch your noodle being abused in the corner.

I went here for brunch last weekend. I haven't done the NYC Sunday Brunch thing in a few years, so it's good to see that it's still a healthy tradition. It was a gorgeous day, and at 11, we had to wait for a few minutes, but there wasn't any trouble getting a small, semi-private table in a corner. I think we just lucked out. The menu has some creative items, but it's more or less typical brunch fare. Portion sizes are on the larger size, so for a small person, it was more than enough food. I ate as much as I could and still felt bad when I was full, and so was the plate. The whole space is bright and airy, and while the bathrooms are a bit out of the way, but there is a photo booth in the long hallway to keep you busy if you have to wait.
Inexpensively Awesome.

Smashed potatoes are great! MP salad and octopus meze are good. Beer selection is varied and pretty large for a Greek restaurant. Large selection of single malt as well. Lemon chicken sauce is great! Â Souvlaki sandwiches are good. Not great. Risotto with spinach and artichoke was too cheesy for me, but flavorful. I am very full after not eating that much. Similarly full as if I ate Chinese food. Hmmm? Not digging that at all. Wonder what the secret ingredient is? Â I've been drinking more water than usual with dinner too. Could be something, could be nothing. Service is good. But something is off. They seem helpful but are not around when you need them. Hostess Â was nice. Ambiance on street level and upstairs is equally pleasant. Dessert was apple baklava and yogurt with honey. Asked for Greek coffee no sugar, came with sugar. Dessert was the winner. Hands down. Ice cream with baklava was wonderful. Would have given it 4 stars but this "I just ate Chinese food and I feel like a balloon" feeling is just wrong.

Brunch is my favorite meal. Â Especially if it has froyo! Of course went for the parafait: homemade frozen yogurt , granola and fruit. Â  I need to update later on after I've tried more and to go for dinner.
there are so many reviews that I dont even think I should waste my time.... I will be lost in the shuffle.....So here it is- short and sweet- NOT WORTH THE WAIT the end

I came here on a Friday with a friend for lunch. We ordered the smoked salmon crepe, some sort of pesto pasta dish I can't quite remember the name of and a pitcher of the bellini. The bellini was mostly peachy and could barely taste the fizziness of the champagne. The smoked salmon crepe was too salty...it's smoked salmon, gobs of cream cheese and pesto wrapped in a crepe. There was way too much cream cheese that I ended up spooning 80/% of it out. The flavors didn't meld well together. The crepe was too thin for it to balance anything out. The pesto pasta dish was far too dry and bland. It tasted like plain boxed pasta you get from the supermarket. I must say I was really disappointed with the food. This place did make up for it by half price bottles of wine. We salvaged the subpar meal by splitting a bottle of Pinot Noir. Bottom line: Not memorable enough for me to go back.

I have to add to the chorus of raves. I love this place. If this place was simply competent, I'd be a regular, simply for the fact that there's no other Itaian food for blocks. (I'm sorry, Singha Pizza is just not the same). I'd go often Â more often but I like to save it up for special occassion - birthdays, anniversary's, promotions at work. The place has a family feel (in fact, Husband and Wife team at the helm but the waitstaff has clearly been "adopted" and the customers are treated like honored family relatives journeying to a festive table. In additionm to the great meals, I always learn a little something about food, Italian culture and/or Corona on every visit. The specials are always truly special (a rare or seasonal ingredient from the market, a chef's inspiration they want to share) and the menu is not just written, it's composed (as is is the food). I waited a few visits to finish my review in part because it's one of those restaurants where you really have to turn off your phone, hide it and bask in the meal (no note taking). Hand made pasta - classic and authentic. Â Family recipes are the foundation but they always return from annual trips to Italy with new dishes. Â Full range of meat and fish selections. Great wine selection, for reasonable markup. Personally, it doesn't feel right to eat here without wine.

if you're looking for a Hawaiian food spot besides L & L in the Financial District, this is THE spot to go. A native Hawaiian friend of ours recently recommended this place in Williamsburg so we trekked our way over to try it out, and it was surely worth the travelling. For my husband, the loco moco really hits the spot. Although priced for $14 which is more than the island's price, the dish is flavorful and very similar to the native one. It is very saucy with tender meat and a fried egg on top. I personally like it with white rice because the sauce itself is heavy, but if you're a SPAM fan, then you must try the spam fried rice for an additional $2. It's unique and worth the workout afterwards! I had the shoyu chicken which had a perfectly marinated taste and served with mac, salad, and rice. My only problem with the chicken is that it was a bit hard and pink, which makes me think that it was defrosted immediately from the freezer. Because of the flavor though, that didn't bother me and I finished the entire dish! Service was great and the atmosphere was cozy with pictures of the island's uniqueness surrounding you. The Hawaiian music playing in the ground was also a plus to make you feel relaxed. Â I would surely come back again and next time order the poke, the famous tuna appetizer.
I had no expectation going in. Now I love the place.

I forgot what good pancakes tasted like until I came here. The banana walnut pancakes were to-die-for, but I just can't finish 3 pancakes on my own. The accompanying sauce was also yummmmy. Grapefruit juice was beautifully tasty. Service was generally good, but I got ignored a bit sitting in the corner. :( Â Had to stand up to get my check.
I absolutely love love! Great brunches to dinners, and don't skip lunch either! From friends getting together or 1st dates, it just hits the spot. A must go!

Fantastic! My friends have raved about this place as the best ramen in NYC so I had pretty high expectations. I went for late lunch today and the wait time was about 30min. I ordered the Akamaru Modern with a poached egg. I really liked the sesame flavoring that came with the broth. The ramen noodles were the perfect chewy-ness and the broth had the perfect consistency. Overall, very pleased with the service and one of the top ramen shops I've been to.

My friend and I came here on a Saturday after failing to find the ever famous Smorgasborg. Since it was extremely humid, we definitely felt our energy draining as we gave up on our Smorgasborg food adventure. Luckily, Grimaldi's was right around the corner from where we were walking, so we decided to grab lunch and replenish our energy here. Apparently, Grimaldi's boasts as New York City's first pizza restaurant that cooks their pizza in a brick oven as opposed to the stainless steel ovens we all know and love. While I don't know how true that is, I was honestly just glad to put something in my stomach. Since my friend and I arrived there before the lunch rush, we missed the line and were seated fairly quickly on the second floor. It's evident that Grimaldi's tries to maintain an atmosphere that encourages patrons to talk to each other - our server told my friend and I, as well as the table next to us, that "We're all one big family!". I thought that was cute - how often do you see restaurants encouraging people to talk to each other?? My friend and I decided to order a small pizza with half pepperoni and half Italian sausage. When our pizza came, it was extremely hot - fresh out of the brick oven. I couldn't help but be internally disappointed at the size of the Italian sausage. While half of our pizza was covered in this delicious meat, the size of the sausage itself was pretty mediocre. However, I am comparing the sausage chunks to commercialized pizza chains, so maybe this might be the actual size of legitimate sausage, and not some hormone injected mystery sausage. After struggling to cut off a slice for each of us, my friend and I finally dug in. The pizza was steaming hot, with gooey melty cheese and a crunchy crust - just how pizza should be! Grimaldi's gives you a fork and a knife to use for your pizza, and I was almost tempted to do so because the slice was that hot. But then I thought, "I'm a New Yorker, what am I doing?" and ate it with my hands. Everything tasted pretty fresh, when compared to all the free pizza I get during the school year, so I was definitely a fan. What prevents me from giving Grimaldi's five stars is the fact that while the pizza comes out piping hot, it quickly gets cold in the center. By the time I had finished my first slice, my second slice was kind of hot bordering on warm. So when I ate my second slice, my third slice was just a little over room temperature. I mean, the amazing thing about pizza is that it tastes good no matter what, but its just a little disappointing not to have experienced the stretchy cheese with every slice. Another reason I won't give Grimaldi's five stars is the fact that its cash only. As someone who hates cash only places, having a cash only establishment automatically makes it harder for me to give you a five star rating. But overall, I had a good experience, I'd probably come back if the line isn't normally to Queens.
Delicious! Â Really great interior.

This place is so good. I don't know where they get their cheese, but it's incredible. The pizza is delicious, but it would be a crime to come here and not order a calzone. But be forewarned, Giuseppina's will ruin you for all other calzones in NYC.

Really good food, I've been here for brunch and for dinner, both amazing. I like the personal attention from the staff, and the changing menu, I never get bored with the same meal. On the downside the meals are really expensive, even brunch, long the bargain meal of the week is pricey. It's worth going to, but be prepared to spend some cash.

BEST pizza in NYC. What more can i say! Fresh and super delicious ingredients. Their plain margherita pizza is the best. Simple sauce with fresh basil and cheese. Yumm! The crust is super crispy and light. Loved the plain calzones too. We dined in with a 3 year old and the chef provided her with a ball of dough to roll and pizza sauce. She created her own mini pizza. He then baked the pizza specially for her. I thought that was a super warm gesture. Full marks to their customer service! It's a BYOB but they do have some beer and soda in case you forget to bring your own. We love the place and keep going back for more!

I'm writing my first Yelp review because I love it here. I work in Jersey City and take the PATH into Greenwich Village just to eat here about twice a week. The food is consistently fresh and delicious and the waitresses are friendly and attentive as well. Great atmosphere + great food + great service = 5 stars.

Too good. I'm just re-hashing but Â the pork xiao long bao are just so, so good. Just order that, maybe some rice and you're set. I wasn't a fan of the crab tomalley (I just searched up the term, it seems to be correct) xiao long bao but the fast service, great food is fantastic. If anyone expects a Michelin-like environment, don't. This is still a Chinatown restaurant. This includes cash only, lots of Chinese, crowded, in a dense apartment building, dirty outside, etc. It was still fantastic though.

Loved this place! So wonderful to find such an attentive staff in the Restaurant Row area near Times Square. My cousin was in from out of town and staying in a hotel nearby so we tried to choose a place that was convenient and delicious - SUCCESS! Our waiter suggested a wine we both loved and the braised short rib entree was fantastic. After dinner, the manager(?) came by and gave us a shot of their special fall drink on the house. I am looking forward to going to La Pulperia again!

pluses: very, VERY delicious pizza, very nice service minuses: no menu, so you don't know real prices. you are ordering pizza or calzone (nothing else) and add different ingredients (not knowing the price!!), in the end you get the 70$ check for 2 and you're like WHAT??? byob too, they don't have alcohol

This place is tiny and gets loud and crowded, it took almost 10 min for me to make my way to the bar and to order a drink. This was a Wednesday night and it was this business, i wonder what this place would look like on a Weekend. The drinks run about $15 each. I ordered one drink before my group wanted to leave and try another place, but this was the smoothest Manhattan i've had anywhere.

What more can you ask for? Tasty hand pulled noodles for $6 or less. This place is a bargain and you get a large amount of food. As the name of the store implies, they are famous for their hand pulled noodles, and they live up to their name. Their hand pulled noodles are very chewy and well-prepared. Out of many hand pulled noodle shops I have tried, this is among the top. The broth for the noodles is also very good. It is not too salty and the flavor is light and not over the top. Much of this place is self-serve, so don't expect much in terms of service. But what more do you expect when you get great noodles for a bargain price? There are styrofoam cups on the table, which you have to get yourself to pour water from a pitcher, which is served to you. Utensils and napkins are also located on the table. The place is small, and only good for small groups.

I had the combo of 1/2 chicken and drunken peel and eat shrimp. The chicken was very good and juicy, shrimp were not that good, seemed old not freshly cooked. The mac and cheese was pretty good and the kale and beans also not bad. I would go back when near by but I would not go out of my way to come here. I could see this being better with a larger group so you could try different things.

Amazing. When I am within a 1 block radius of Pommes Frites, my stomach sings its name. Good even on a full stomach. The honey mustard wasn't the best, but the Mango chutney was falalalala! I was also having a blast sampling their flavors until I began feeling guilty.

Yay!: West Village!! Kusshi oysters Roquefort burger Brussel Sprouts Boo!: Going on 5 days -- still waiting for a return phone call from the restaurant to get a copy of my receipt. Seriously, who doesn't return a call?

Hard to beat the 5-for$1 price. Â The dumplings are actually quite good, with a solid chivey flavor and usually well-browned on one side. Â There is soy sauce and (watered down) Sirarcha hot sauce to help. Â Only a couple of stools and shelves to sit and eat but you're probably just grabbing a quick bite in any event. Â They also sell bags of frozen dumplings for I think $8-9 for 50, which has to be one of the steals of the century.
Outstanding Food, Great Ambiance - terrible service from young hipsters who make you think you are the one serving.
Beyond delicious. Amongst my favorite if not my favorite place in town. Must have: Crab xiao long bao Shanghai rice Shanghai noodles Also pretty good the fried duck although extremely greasy.
Cozy place to grab a bite. Â Had the chocolate chip pancakes, Â a great treat to start the day with.

Wow, this is a real gem in the area. We didn't beat the lunch crowd, and the place was already packed from the counter to the door around 12:30PM. Luckily we did managed to grab two seats. It started to thin out around 1:15PM. When the owner had a second to breathe after the lunch wave, he came over to our table and offered us a free roll for taking too long on our order earlier. This type of service and hospitality is unheard of in a fast casual setting. If you have read this far, the best time to enjoy this place is to have a late lunch starting at 1:30PM.

this place is really cool. the space and interior has a nice vibe, love the ambience, mellow and relaxing. the food is so fresh and beautifully prepared. we did the tasting and everything was delicious. the food itself isn't really japanese but the preparation def looks japanese. we had crudite with cheese fondue, mushroom croquette with uni on top, a cast iron skillet of whole branzino with veggies, smoked duck, mini burger, ikura rice, and sake panacotta and flan. good solid meal and not too expensive, unpretentious setting even though all the secretness of getting a reservation makes it seem like it might be. kiyo-san, the owner, is super friendly and makes a point to greet every guest and invited us back to the kitchen. it feels like a place where maybe you can just order something not on the menu. like how great would it be to just finish a meal with a nice bowl of ramen (if you're not stuffed already) that the chef whips up with whatever is in the kitchen.
Outstanding on every level. This level of food in such a no-bullshit laid-back environment is too rare. Don't miss the cocktails.

Came here for brunch. Awesome! there is usually a wait, but you can also eat at the bar. The french toast is good- its like a banana fosters with delicious bread! I have the monte cristo, I highly recommend it. The atmosphere is nice and I always seem to run into someone I know. The 2-top outdoor tables are cute!

Pho Real pho life! The Pho Real sandwich tastes like Pho! I have taken all of my so cal friends to eat this and they alway get a trip on how much this taste like pho. So far I'm 8/8! Â Two of those 8 being Vietnamese who love their pho! I don't really understand why someone would think to add avocado to this sandwich, but i don't really care because it sure does work! I've tried the turkey with kimchi sandwhich, the korean bulgogi sandwich, and the blt. The blt comes close second but if i'm ever in the neighborhood i'm ordering the Pho Real!

This place is popular! Thankfully, the bar across the street can sit you while you wait and they have a lot of the same stuff. But don't order there, just get a drink, and wait. The restaurant calls the bar when your table's ready. We had... The fish sauce wings (6 wings) The pork neck These two above were our favorites. But also delicious... Papaya salad with black crab Duck salad Curry noodle soup Warning - the papaya salad is out of this world spicy. Some people call it 'challenging'. We had beers and some drinking vinegar and a cocktail - all wonderful. Oh, and sticky rice, of course. Lovely meal, lovely service, lovely environment. Fairly pricey.
Best lemon poppy muffin ever...flavorful, full of zest, & moist! Looking forward to actually sitting down in this little gem for a meal real soon.

Although my gf and I went on a Friday night, we were able to get seated asap. I would definitely recommend making reservations though since seating is limited. First of all, it was nice to sit and watch all of our dishes being prepared in front of us. Â It allowed us to see what looked appetizing (everything). The poached egg appetizer was on point. The flavor combinations were unique and left me wanting more with each bite. The grilled octopus and pork belly were flavorful and cooked perfectly. Â For dessert we shared the torija. Brioche soaked in butter and cream topped with caramelized sugar. Mmmmm. For value go with the 5 course meal. Â We had 3 dishes each and split dessert and were content, but another dish wouldn't have hurt. Service was also very good. Â All said, I recommend this place for a date or with a few close friends to enjoy some rather tasty food combos.
I could eat their dumplings everyday and not get sick of them. They are pure deliciousness. The noodles and pancakes are also worth ordering.
This place has only a few real vegetarian options but they are really good. The veg tempura was delicious. Â The seating is uncomfortable and the place is tiny.
I love the pork buns here! Everything I tried so far is pretty yummy. The only thing that sucks here is the WAIT.
Intimate and cozy. Great breakfast and lunch selection. Love how they use organic eggs and milk. Oh and did I mention fresh whipped cream? Yeah, that just tops it all off for me...pun intended. :)

My FH and I went here. Â I got a beef wellington (I've always been intrigued by this dish after watching Chef Gordon Ramsey serve it a hundred times on Hells Kitchen) and he ordered a chicken dish. Â Chicken was terrible. Terrible because we both have Indian taste buds that have been singed over time with a multitude of spices. It takes more than simple vegetables with salt and pepper in a broth to satisfy our taste buds. Â Did not like the chicken at all. Â Very very bland. Â However, I absolutely loved the beef wellington. Satisfied my curiosity and it was delicious. Â Very juicy and flavorful. Â The sauce that is served along side the potatoes were perfect. We actually ended up sharing the Beef Wellington and cleaning out the plate on that. The chicken was only half eaten by the poor fiance who was just bearing it for a while until he saw I had eaten half of the wellington and was filled up. It's pretty big and thick so very satisfying! I would go back again for the ambiance, service, and beef wellington. Service was excellent, very polite and attentive. Â Bar looks great so I'll probably stop by there sometime as well. It was packed on a Saturday so make a reservation ahead of time.

Ramen was sooo good. We also tried the pork buns, brussel sprouts, spare ribs they were all excellent. We went for a late dinner 10pm on a Saturday and only waited for 15 mins for a table. Can't wait to go back.

I only went for their pork soup dumplings, which were very good. The crab soup dumplings were delicious, too. The place is packed with noisy young crowd, and the service is what you would expect in a restaurant in Chinatown: rushed and impersonal.

DECENT! And that's huge. Let me explain why. First time here. Came off the strength of...Yelp actually. Didn't know much about the menu other than they seem to have a decent happy hour. Empanadas were solid. Not life-changing. But about one of the best deals you're going to get for $1. I'm serious folks. Don't read over that. We had their most popular dish, as per our extremely helpful server, guide in this case, the bisteca encebollada, and it did not disappoint. ONLY downside is they don't take card. I'm from CA where every place does. That's more my fault than anything. Lessons learned: carry cash, support neighborhood biz, and find more happy hours like this one.
I had a great time here. Uber friendly staff and not as pretentious as other places in the area. Loved the Lychee Martinis and the DJ was awesome. Everyone was dancing. LOVE Fat Buddha!

I needed a birthday spot for my husband and 15 of our friends plus our baby in a stroller. I didn't even realize Da Mikele was kid friendly, I just remembered eating here once and loving the delicious food. I coordinated the dinner via email during an extremely busy time at work so when I asked for pre-fixe plus all you can drink, they sent me a menu I skimmed over and approved. When we got there, the servers (who were attentive and placed bottles of wine at the table so we could self serve- amazing!) started placing multiple plates of apps to our group. At which point I realized the lengthy menu was everything that was being served for a mere $35 per person!! We got salad, bruschetta, risotto balls, polenta, pizza, pasta, Â and risotto. So much delicious food we even got to pack some to go (which never happens at a group dinner!). I also noticed a few couples in the restaurant mix having a nice romantic dinner. All in all, great food, decor, ambience, service and if you're planning a party, it's a nice spot to tailor an event to your own taste.

Good ambiance, great cocktails and great music each and every time I've been there. Â I've had sandwiches, appetizers and mains and have been seated at the bar and at tables and food and service have always been great. Â Good place for a first date as it's not too loud and it's not stuffy. Â It's a bit pricier than some of the other places I go to in the area (2 glasses of wine, one appetizer and a very simple, albeit delicious, pasta entree - cacio e pepe - came to $72, including tip the other day), so I don't go often, but if you're willing to spend the extra buck I'd definitely recommend.

Been dying to go here for a while, and finally stopped by with a group of friends after work for one the "loca tuesdays" happy hour--- Half off appetizers, and drinks!! Started off with a passion fruit mojito, coconut mojito, and mango mojito-- passion fruit was my favorite. Beware these mojitos are strong, it's probably like 95% rum and 5% syrup-- but I guess you get more bang for your buck. We sampled a bunch of tapas: these were our favorites: 1) Favorite: Croquetas de cangrejo- these cakes were so nice and fresh, and they crumbled apart in your mouth- and it went really well with the mango-jalapeno salsa. These were gone in seconds. 2) Platano relleno- really big fan of savory and sweet dishes, and this dish did not disappoint. One huge slab of sweet plantain stuffed with pulled pork- 3) expresso bbq costillitas-- didn't really taste the coffee flavor, but these ribs were sweet and the meat was falling right off the bone. 4) Calamari---- the calamari was crunchy and standard, but the sauce makes this dish shine-- caper Aioli-- we practically drank the sauce, it was so good. 5) arepa con carne--- presentation was beautiful and the dish was great as well-- corn cakes with shredded beef on top 6) Mussels- huge appetizer- accompanied Â with some delicious crusty bread these were not so great: 7) Shrimp skewers- the dish sounded pretty fancy, but overall it wasn't that flavorful 8) Fish croquettes- honestly it tasted like fish sticks - but the dipping sauce was good- it was passion fruit and chipotle dip. 8) The beef tacos- tacos were burnt, the beef had absolutely no flavor, just slabs of meat Overall, it was an enjoyable experience, and I want to come back here next time and sample more dishes Â such as the empanadas, the fish tacos, Â ceviche, and Â try the sangria

Delicious! Best pizza ever IMO. Did not even mind the 1.5 hour wait, it was totally worth it! The ONLY thing that kept me away from giving the full five stars was the interior... not that it's too old or anything, but the Air Condition was on so high at 10pm at night mid-September, (and we sat right under the vent), that our pizza got cold before we could enjoy the second slice. It was kind of a bummer because the first slice was like HEAVEN. Hopefully there can be some kind of improvements? Will definitely go back. MUST HAVE IN NY.

Assuming that burgers are religion, brand me a heretic now because I didn't find the burger here better than Breslin. For brunch, we ordered the Black Label burger and the shirred eggs with mushrooms. The burger, which is really what we came for, was light, airy and juicy but didn't knock me out of the park. Don't get me wrong, things don't have to be heavy to be satisfying but it just didn't have the meaty flavor that makes or breaks burgers for me. The eggs were forgettable. Service was impeccable. But to come here again when given the choice? I'd go to Breslin.

GROUSE. What the hell??? Did I miss something??? I was expecting AMAZING since reviews were fantastic.... Ordered the pulled noodles and had an order of dumplings (dumplings were pretty good). But the noodles?? You must be kidding. And the restaurant is pretty disgusting. They need to clean up the tables and the condiments..... Water has no lid and it seems its been out for a long time... Esp since summer is coming around I am sure that will be a great spot for little flying buggerssss. No thanks.

My friends and I came here last Friday night, and I was really disappointed with the quality of food and the price. First things first, though, I will admit that we didn't order "smartly:" I got a fish dish, one of my friends got duck, and the other got the tagliatelle bolognese. Here are my tips based on this experience: 1) DON'T waste time and money on the appetizers. The bread and oil is quite good (not the best quality olive oil, but it's free so whatever), and the apps just weren't worth the money. 2) DON'T order anything other than pasta, and have a backup plan in case they're sold out. I ordered gnocchi, but 15 minutes after I ordered the waiter came back to tell me that they had run out. I ended up ordering salmon trout which was so mediocre I got a burger from shake shack after we ate here. (Don't judge me, I have needs). 3) DO bring cash, and lots of it. My friend's duck was very fatty, but the tagliatelle bolognese my other friend ordered was delicious. I want to go back and try the gnocchi eventually, but I definitely will not order anything else on the menu.

DO NOT EAT PHO HERE DON'T DO IT. I understand if you're eating vietnamese for the first time - its not bad. Sadly it was not my first time - and it really was, without exaggeration, the worst pho I've had in my life. I've had pho here and there in Flushing, Queens - Chinatown, Manahttan - and I can pretty much say with confidence that anywhere is better than this place. 8 dollars?! FOR PHO?! I have never had a more expensive pho - and I've had much better for less money and more food. The noodles are clumped - because they clearly cook it and leave it in the bowl til someone orders it. *facepalm* five pieces of beef? really?! THAT'S IT?! (ok granted the beef itself is OKAY). But where is the eye of round, the tendon, the omosa - there are just barely slivers of anything. The worst part - is the broth. Compared to all and any of the broths out there - its so bland. If you think its good - you are missing out on so much. Something is just fundamentally NOT PHO about it - I couldn't even finish the bowl it was that bland and disappointing. It's also not hot. kinda a little hotter than lukewarm. I talked to my friend from California about this place - she lives in a highly populated Vietnamese area. And she also agreed that it was the worst pho she's had in her life - for all the above reasons. I did have their pork banh mi - pretty good but there are also other banh mi places around and I wouldn't go out of my way to go here for it.
Holy mother effer is this good when you're wasted from a night out.

Foods amazing portions okay prices moderate the view & vibe does it for me the managers are great waiter I had could've been friendlier but everyone has a bad night other than that couldn't praise this place enough we'll be back !
If you like thin crust pizza, this is the place to go. I came here several times for pizza and enjoyed every time. I also like to eat the rice pudding afterwards!

I just had the maple buffalo finger and they were in-edible. They were overcooked and tasted like rubber. You'd think if all you do is make chicken fingers you'd at least know how to cook them. This place has been consistently disappointing since it opened.

Came here at 6PM during the week with my girlfriend just to pass the time and have a few drinks. The place was empty, aside from a few people sitting outside. We sat at the bar. The bartender (later learned her name was Liz) was super friendly, told us all about the drink menu and the food menu and really went above and beyond to make us feel at home. She gave us a history of the place, the chef, etc. told us about the Brisket night, the Crawfish night, etc. I would have sworn she was an owner...but low and behold, she was 'just' a bartender. Damn place better be paying her well, or I'll scoop her up and open a place of my own with her at the front.... The rest of the staff was friendly, young and energetic. Very attentive. Engaged in conversation, yet knew when to leave us alone to talk to eachother. Needless to say, we took her recommendations, had the Watermelon Gimlets which were really great. Came in a mason jar and we learned they use the owners own cold pressed watermelon Juice in the mix (which he sells in containers under the name juisi). The drink was really good, could have been a touch stronger (as I was hoping to get an early buzz on)...;) but great nevertheless. We had some snacks at the bar, as we had dinner plans with friends at Ippudo later in the evening. So we had the nut mix which was really good (had dried cherries, bacon bits, cashews and some spicy stuff mixed in). it was perfect bar snack. We also had the shrimp chips, which made me chuckle because the pastel flavored things were something I always had at an old chinatown favorite of mine. They're addicting, sort of like eating a lighter version of a rice cake in chip form with a hint of shrimp-ness...it came with a sauce that when dipped the things popped like pop rocks..real cool and another perfect bar-snack. I was hungry, now that people were coming in and eating, and all sorts of interesting things were popping out of the kitchen...so as per Liz's recommendation I ordered the Chicken Wings...they were perfect. big meaty fried super crunchy with a asian spicy sauce drizzled on top. Reminded me a little of Pok Pok, but I actually enjoyed these better (I know, how dare I say it, sorry Ike...lol)... All in all a very enjoyable late afternoon. I will definitely be back, promised the bartender I'd try the Goat Neck (whatever the heck that is) and come for the brisket (no clue how this chef would prepare it, but Im interested in finding out.) :)

Ordered two orders of chicken spring rolls , which were absolutely delish. Pad Thai was very good. Red curry was just ok in my opinion but had eggplant in it. Inside is very nice and chic, especially considering each entree is 7.95! Grade a rating

Thin crust pizza. Â Always crispy with flavor. Â We always order a large pie with pepperoni and sausage. Â They use ground sausage so you taste sausage in every bite. Their tomato sauce has a lot of flavor with the right amount of seasoning . Â My mouth is watering writing this review!

This is probably my favorite NYC restaurant. The atmosphere is so intimate and romantic. I think it's a great place to impress a girl. I've been here twice and both times food was impeccable. The interesting item on the menu is Negros y crujientes, which is pasta in squid ink broth and the interesting thing about is that it's literally a blue/black colored broth. Needless to say that after eating this dish your smile is not something you want to show off.

We ate here on Aug. 28th. We had been here several years ago and the food was good enough to be memorable, so we came back during our US Open tennis viewing trip. The crab meat dumpling was excellent as we had remembered. We also ordered a veggie dish, a chicken dish, and a fish, and all were very tasty. Our waiter was attentive and brought our food very fast, filled our waters constantly, and even changed our plates. Definitely the best meal we had in NY Chinatown by far. A tip: the restaurant is small and wait will be long, so get there early.

first time there, the first thing i notice is this place is run by Indians and yet they were speaking japanese to me, and there are japanese ads all over the place, and of course, japanese menu. Aside from the interesting combo, the food itself is great, i had the minced meat katsu and it tasted great. will def go back and check out other dish

So far, have only been here once to try the grass-fed burger. Â I would say possibly the best hamburger I've ever eaten - done classically (no extravagant toppings, etc) and very tasty. Â The staff was very nice and attentive. Â I can't wait to go back and try one of the salads (which looked piled high) since we overheard the table next to us raving about it amongst themselves. Â  Â I very much like the local sourcing of ingredients - I think it is worth it to spend a little more for good quality ingredients.

Not as good as the last time I went, but still pretty good. Â A friend of mine from Naples introduced me to Luzzo's several years ago and it was great. Â I recently learned though that the owner has opened a few others pizza spots and takes no part in the kitchen work anymore. Â  The pizza's are good and because they are thin, you can try a lot without getting filled up. Â Although I didn't try it, the truffle oil piza comes highly recommended by my friend. The pizza's are all between $18-25 for a 12 inch and you can easily have three of them between four average eatinng adults. Â  They'll get you on the wine though. Â We had the house red and it was $30 per bottle. Â It was probably more like $8 wine from the grocery store. Maybe call ahead and see if you can bring your own.

I love the Neue Gallerie -- but a lot of that love is due in part to Cafe Sabarsky. It's just like being in Europe - the furniture, the art, the atmosphere. It's all dark wood and blue walls and makes me feel like I'm in a Degas for some reason. And the line up of desserts! Sigh. I love the apple strudel and the opera cake. And I've never met a dessert at Cafe Sabarsky that I didn't like.
The Pines is killer! Gowanus is on fire (not the canal, although you could probably set fire to the canal) Completely worth the walk across the lovely canal.
Cute venue with tasty food, but nothing justifies the obnoxious attitude of the staff and the ridiculously long wait times.

The most pleasant Â culinary surprise in my 5 months in Manhattan. Â The food is absolutely scrumptious and relatively inexpensive!! Â The lamb ikender kabob was transcendental and the eggplant/tomato appetizer and warm bread that they brought out unforgettable. Â I'm not a vegetarian but my date was trying out the combo veggie plate which was also very tasty. Â  An appetizer, bread and 2 dishes for less than 45 dollars!! The ambiance is upscale without pretention, and sidewalk seating is available if the weather allows. I left this place, enthusiastically asking for the business card and ecstatic that I had found this upper east side gem. Only 2 minor complaints: Â My waiter was socially awkward and seemed to lack peripheral vision and the facial muscles required for smiling. Â Furthermore, the bathroom lock didn't work. Â I ended up walkin in on a guy who was pissing (wondering why the idiot didn't lock the door) and a few minutes later, another man walked in on me while urinating. Â In reality, though I would show my penis to an entire crowd for food this good. This is arguably the tastiest food that I've had in New York. Â I'll be back EDIT! Â I must let all of you know that I returned to Beyoglu and the fresh puffy bread that comes with the meal was not half as good as my previous visit. Â It was flaky, overcooked and salty. Â After further investigation, I learned that their bread chef had left for another gig. Â Still good though but I bring it down to Â 4 stars from 5.

Oh my god their Pancakes are so Good! Walked in for a late brunch on Sunday, ordered the Pancakes with fruit to share with a friend as a Starter... Amazing, the Pancakes were airy and fluffy, Thick but not dense and buttery, they were so light that they had a crisp to them, by far the best pancakes Ive ever had yet. The best part which i love is that they give you good Quality (real Maple) Syrup on the side. We also ordered the Pulled Pork Sandwich with melted cheese Garlic Aioile , too good to describe. Everything was delicious. The staff was Friendly and attentive. I will make sure to come back again just for the pancakes, to die for! Trust me.
Exceptional meal, outstanding service and star treatment after a little twitter mention. Small plates were delicious, main course was prompt well planned and executed incredibly. We will be back.

Amazing. Awesome. Superb. Graffiti was recommended to me by 2 of my closest friends, so when I knew that I would be in the neighborhood, I decided to make a reservation and give it a try--see what the fuss was all about. This place is cozy and charming, which is another way to say that it's super small, but make no mistake about it, Graffiti is all about the food. The service is great and also knowledgeable. My party and I ordered the mango paneer, the green chili shrimp, the zucchini hummus pizza, and the braised pork buns with apricot chutney. All of our dishes were delicious and truly special. The paneer was full of flavor and wonderfully consistent. The green chili shrimp was a true highlight, wonderfully cooked, both buttery and crunchy at the same time -- I could eat this all day. The zucchini hummus pizza was topped with crushed wasabi peas that gave it a wonderful combination of flavors that was an entirely new flavor experience. The braised pork buns were also equally delicious, the saltiness of the braised was complimented superbly by the sweet apricot chutney. For desert, we shared the coconut macaroons, which were delicious. However, the strawberries, almonds, and truffle oil, served with home-made pepper ice cream was something truly remarkable. It was both familiar and different at the same time -- sweet and salty, salt and peppery. I had high expectations and I was still amazed.

This place is adorable! Its the perfect summer hang out spot. I go here to people watch and enjoy the beer and corn. The seating outside is cafeteria style, so you have to be on the prowl for an empty seat and will probably end up sitting next to random people. Although the corn is not ideal for trying to be cute because it gets everywhere, it's AMAZING. I've tried the tacos and they were lacking something and on top of that I really wished they'd add cheese! I only wish the margaritas were a bit larger for their price, but its a great vibe on a beautiful day!!

Beautiful space. We were seated in the front, by the bar. Emporio has a rustic theme: pink blossoms adorning five feet long branches in a large glass jar, chalk board menu, wood oven stove, wooden benches with black iron legs. At night Emporio becomes a wonderful date night place: they bring out tall eggshell white candle sticks and iron candlestick holders, and then the place is aglow with diffuse lighting. The food was ok. I will not penalize them for their lunch prix fixe menu. My friends and I shared a Margherita pizza, Tonnarelli Cacio de Pepe, Wild mushroom risotto croquettes, and a beet salad. The Margherita pizza was acceptable, crisp, not too much sauce but it was not spectacular. The pasta was cheesy and hand made, the beet salad was mildly sweet and I enjoyed the golden raisins. I wanted more food and better quality food for 25 dollars but I will be back. I need information (ie more food sampling) before judging their cooking capabilities. Next time I will try the grilled octopus (that my friend raved about) and try more of their pizzas.

Went here to try the Mexican Style Corn on the Cob after spotting this place on TVFoodMaps (.com). Â Great corn! Â The cactus tacos were good, but not the best. Â The portions were generous. Â  If you go for lunch, go slightly before noon to catch a table.

I thought the other yelpers were over exaggerating, but as soon as I put that panini (deliciozo) in my mouth......I could not even describe how good it was..You have to try it for yourself! :D I know it's strange to say, but i could literally taste the love and care that went into the one sandwich. I never knew what people meant by that until I tried this panini

5 stars. I give 5 star reviews if the place I'm reviewing is (in my opinion) the arbiter to which all other venues of this style should aspire. That being said... here we go: My wife and I split 3 empanadas at 2 AM: Desayuno Columbiano, Spicy Chicken, Pernil. They were all phenomenal. My favorite was the spicy chicken. It was SO good. Also - each empanada costs like $2 and change.

We didn't have a reservation but arrived at 8:30 on a Saturday night hoping for the best. The female owner was extremely nice and accommodating and was able to squeeze us in. Aside from the room being small, crowded and bereft of decor, we were most disappointed by the food. The Brussels sprouts were lackluster at best. The squid salad was ok, but at $19 we expected something better. The lamb entree was decent but served lukewarm. The halibut was jaw-droopingly small - it must have been 2 ounces. We split it and had literally one bite each. The fig chocolate cake was average at best, the coconut ice cream was the best part. Other complaints included dirty dishes stacked in a corner visible to all and the chef ringing a bell loudly from the kitchen every few minutes. Server was nice, nothing special. Â  Overall we would not return or recommend it to others.

This is a very good place to eat. Â The food is good for Mediterranean style food. Â But being able to watch Bobby Flay cook and run the kitchen makes up for lack of seats. Â The bar and small lounge have the full menu. Â  They are first come first serve. Â  If you want a real seat make a reservation.

We were lucky enough to get seated in the back room that was super pretty and usually for private parties. The service was okay, a little slow and at times inattentive. The food was amazingly good, everyone had a pasta, we tried a few apps as well and all were executed perfectly. CASH ONLY only Wine, but tons of wine... The prices of the food are super cheap, but expect to spend a ton of cash wine while drinking with drunks and winos like I do. The downside, the room was blasted by freezing cold air-conditioning. I get that it is a super old space and it is humid in NYC right now, so keeping the space cold is logical, but I was freezing. Also, the music is bad. We discussed how great restaurants can be totally ruined by playing stupid music. Playlists people, don't sign up for those stupid radio services...they suck. You can not pick a genre of music like, POP or ALTERNATIVE and expect it to provide good ambiance. I would certainly go here again, next time I am craving a delicious bowl of classic, fresh pasta!!!

Though this place clearly is in no need of another rave review, I just wouldn't feel right about not letting the world know how awesome I think this place is. I've read the horror stories about massive wait times for brunch (and even witnessed it once one Saturday morning when hubby and I thought we would take a chance - after being quoted at an hour and a half wait, we decided to go someplace else) but figured that MLK Day, even being a national holiday, was still a Monday and wouldn't be as bad as a weekend. Luckily, that gamble paid off, and we were seated within 15 minutes. It was actually so quick that while we were waiting, we realized that we didn't have any money (it's cash only), so my husband went up the block to the ATM, and I was called right after he left. I was told I could be seated, but that the server wouldn't come to the table until the whole party was there. Fine with me, more time to look over the menu. So yes, it's a small place, seating is tight, Â blah blah blah. I ordered a Mexican coffee, and while I definitely prefer my drinks on the strong side, this one was mouth-puckeringly so. The tequila actually gave the coffee a sour taste. And being that warm beverages and alcohol are separately two of my favorite things, it was kind of disappointing that they came together in such a lackluster way. I tasted the regular coffee though, and it was perfectly competent. Now, on to the food! I went in knowing that I had to try the blueberry pancakes that amaze everyone, and settled on the huevos rancheros as well. Was a little skeptical about that one, because while it doesn't seem to be a particularly difficult dish to make, I have had yet to have a good experience with huevos the past couple of times I've had them anywhere (tasteless, stale tortilla, etc.). I can happily say that this renewed my faith in the Mexican breakfast staple. It was a big round tortilla covered in eggs and sauce and little dollops of avocado and crema on each quarter of the plate, and just... Â MMM. And the pancakes - now I'm always skeptical of hype, but these bad boys delivered. I don't usually order pancakes out, because we make them every weekend at home, and on the rare occasions that I do, it's usually of the healthy (i.e. whole grain) variety. But these were by far the best I've had in years. Like, melt in your mouth goodness. Now I do have to put out there the the hubby did not enjoy the meal nearly as much as I did. He thought everything was pretty mediocre. But, this isn't a joint Yelp page, and I'm reviewing based on my own experience here, so Arianna says - GO. NOW. YUM.

Our order: Crab-cake banh mi, and rice with shrimp and spring rolls (w/pork meat - be careful vegetarians!) Stella: The table we sat at was all sticky. It wasn't busy - the restaurant had only two clients at that time - so the table should have been spotless. The crab-cake was spicy, after Blaec specifically asked them NOT TO make it spicy. The waitress forgot to bring me my cucumber lemonade, and on top of everything - we got PORK spring rolls on our rice & shrimp plate (we do not eat meat). (Blaec even checked to make sure they did not come with meat.) What's more, the sauce overpowered the flavor of the crab, leaving much to be desired. Needless to say, we won't be back.

Worth the wait. Though, would advise driving here as there is no waiting area in the winter. Your choices to wait in is Western Beef or a strip club. LAWL the western beef is pretty large so if you take each aisle slowly, it's a good gem. Fruit section is varied. Worse comes to worst, the liquor store is on premise. Nothing like sutter wine in brown bags... Classy. My only regret is that I couldn't eat more / didn't invite more ppl. Order everything you can. You won't go wrong.

I've had 3 different ramens and they're all brilliant. I had the salt'n'pepper chicken wings and they were brilliant. Their funky little tap for sapporo produces beer that is brilliant. ALSO I only finished my soup 2/3 times, as in: it's a big serving. ALSO- they're gonna ask if you want the garlic chili oil. Say yes, put all of that stuff in your bowl, and shut up.

Have walked by here several times and finally tried it for the first time last night. Â I enjoyed it... thought it was a solid Italian food restaurant, with reasonable prices. Â Maybe my friends and I ordered the right thing because everything we had was dependably good - pasta bolognese, shrimp & pesto risotto, lamb shank. Â This place is certainly a good choice for a small group dinner. Â Even the wine was reasonably priced, with most bottles south of $30.

OVERPRICED TO THE MAX FOR ALRIGHT FOOD. First of all, BE WARNED. THERE'S A ONE DRINK MINIMUM PER PERSON. Which means you know you'll be paying $8 right as you walk through the door. I mean, what restaurant MAKES you buy a drink? What's wrong with these weirdos? Secondly, the food here is alright, but it is SO EXPENSIVE FOR WHAT IT IS. Glancing over the menu, you might be like, okay these dishes are decently priced. UNTIL YOU REALIZE YOU GET SERVED LESS THAN AN APPETIZER-SERVING OF FOOD PER ITEM! We ordered the Taro Croquette, Zuru Teba, Salmon & Salmon Roe dish, and Spicy Tuna & Avocado roll (which comes with jelly soy sauce instead of regular liquid soy sauce... interesting). The food was alright, but the servings are all extremely TINY for the prices! For $15, the Salmon & Salmon Roe dish was TINY! As were all of the other dishes! All of these dishes for two people, and neither of us were even that full. Be prepared to spend a lot of money for a $$ restaurant if you want a filling meal. The service here is pretty good, aside from the fact that they forgot one of our orders. It was probably unintentional. Hm. The feel here is pretty authentic. It reminds me of a nicer, smaller version of Kenka on St. Marks, but overpriced. If you go to the bathroom, it's very clean and has one of those fancy Japanese toilets. They also all of a sudden started playing this deep bass music that you hear in movies when something really bad is going to happen... and then played happy music the next second. I thought it was really weird... and it gave me anxiety paired with the alcohol they FORCED me to buy. Not a good restaurant feel. I don't recommend Fukurou, due to how pricy it is for the food. I would come back if the prices were knocked down a bit, but they probably don't need or want to since their restaurant is so small already. For similar but cheaper food, try Kenka (con: not as clean, long waits, lower quality food) or Ennju (con: less adventurous menu, jankier environment).

Good food at a good price. Neighborhood imbibers take note: Monday night is happy hour all night. Have been to this place like 20 times, never disappoints. Reliable south american-fusion style food with lots of comfort foods. One time they had a steak covered in coffee? That was actually pretty tasty. Don't overlook the empanada sampler. You can have 4 different kinds. We vote for the Domino and the guava! The delivery service is excellent. Food arrives well packed and warm. This place is great for groups. Very crowded on Friday and Saturday nights. If only they would put cushions on the chairs! Â They care about service and put care into the food prep. And they have fun live music. The fish tacos are a favorite, as well as the bargain bbq chicken.

I just wanted to start my review off with a fuck yeah. and a clip of Meg Ryan faking an orgasm. So this place has really good BBQ. If you haven't seen it before it looks like your about to walk into someones garage or something. This is the only place where I've waited in line and didn't care. I will say that the last time I was here i felt like it wasn't as good. But I also came a day after eating at Babbo. So yeah. My bad. K. Focus. The food here is really awesome. The best BBQ in my opinion in the city. ANNND I'm giving this place 5 stars because like after 11PM they will sell the rest of their meat inventory on potato buns for a few bucks....thats where the fuck yeah comes into factor. Everyone is really nice and patient. Sometimes the fattey's behind you (ohhhhh see what I did!?!?!) get a little overly eager. Just shoot em down with your I don't giiiiiivvvvveeee aaaaaa ffffuuuuuuuccckkkk face. Go here - your taste buds will thank your cheeks and teeth for left overs later.

What a let down. Â Went for dinner with some girlfriends. Â It started off great by being seated promptly by the very nice hostess, but all went down hill from there. Â Our waitress was nice, but lacked the abilty to go that extra mile. Â She seemed like she didn't want to be bothered even to explain some of the menu items. Ummmm...stop being a waitress if you don't want to make suggestions to newcomers to your restaurant. Â She actually said, "we've been open 9 years, so everything is pretty much really good". Â Really? Â How pompous of you and your restaurant. Â  The food: Â eh. Â Mushroom ceviche was ruined by too much sauce and ginger. Â Friend wanted Kangaroo, but they were out, so she went with foie gras. Â She's had better. Â Other friend had scallops which were fine. Â Entrees: Â we decided on the cod dish, tenderloin and pork and the venison (which was very undercooked). Â I tried them all and was not blown away by any of them. Â The worst part about these entrees is that it took about 45 min to 1 hour after they removed our first courses for them to come out. Â Mid way through this extremely long wait time, they brought over some awful cold soup amuse-boushe of sorts. Â  I guess someone figured out that they completely forgot about our meals. Â No "sorry", just..."your dinners will be out shortly". Â Finally the dishes came out and they weren't even hot. Â Luke warm at best. Â After dinner, they tossed 3 glasses of wine and 3 desserts at us, again, to clearly make up for the exhorbitant wait for our dinners. Still Â ... no "sorry". Â Just here you go. Â 'Oh, thanks'. Â The dessert sorbets were ok. Â 2 were great, others just fine. Â And there was an odd taste in the toffee pudding. Â FInally I asked the waitress why we were brought all of these extra items (because frankly, even though I knew why, I just wanted someone to fess up and apologize), and she said it took too long for the kitchen to fire up our dinners. Â Again, no apology. Â Hmm....I'll bet, given her awful waitressing ability, that she was the one who did the forgetting. Â If you see your table sitting for a long long time with no food, maybe you should double check that you put in the food order. Â  My friends and I really enjoyed the ambiance of this place, oh, and the watermelon gimlet drink. Â YUM! Â The wines that were recommended to us by the fun gent in the great tie weren't that good at all. Â Even after we said what we each enjoyed, he got it wrong. Or, maybe, their wine list by the glass just isn't that good. Â  Overall, 2 stars for a sad, looooooooong night.

Overall pretty good. Sometimes the quality is not as consistent as the wilshire, LA BCD (the best one in my opinion and i've been to quite a few of them in LA). The little fish is great if you know how to handle it. They have fast service and the line goes pretty quickly. The broth sometimes tastes watered down. We occasionally get the seafood pancake but the tofu is really more than enough for one person. The seafood pancake is on the oily side. The panchan changes every time, but i like the potato salad one the best. The cucumber one is also pretty good.

I came here twice for Saturday brunch with friends and each time we were very happy with the food and services, although I agree that it's a little overpriced. To begin with, we had Bloody Mary and it is really tasty. Then we ordered Griddle Special, Smoked Trout Scramble and Tenderloin Benedict, they all taste very good. I do think the portion is a little small though. Both times our waiters were very friendly and nice, but it's true that sometimes the food didn't come out as how we asked and had to ask them to bring it back again. However, all over the dining experience is quite pleasant.
NE, NW - they're pretty indistinguishable. Try the BBQ sauce instead of the hot sauce.

Had dinner here with my son tonight and it was good. I had eaten there alone a few times before. My only complaint is that the onions in the guac are too big and overpowering. They should either use sweet onion or leave them out all together. Great neighborhood spot and we will def go back.

This place is an awesome addition to the bar scene in bay ridge. Great American beers on tap that are always changing.
