I've been there 10 times and haven't had the same beer yet but there's always something in the style that I enjoy. This place knows how to make awesome simple bar food. Nothing too crazy but the flavors are all top notch. The backyard is excellent and I can't wait for the weather to get nice! Do not miss out on this spot with diverse beer, solid food, and great people running the place this bar will be a hit for a long time to come.

Excellent, Excellent, Excellent food. Â I mean, the PBLT (pork belly lettuce and tomato) was the right choice to make. My girlfriend had Bobs Burger and I was equally impressed. Â I would definitely recommend this spot to EVERYONE!!!! Plus - all of their meats are organic too!

I would say the Ramen is a OK. Went in a windy Tuesday noon for lunch special with my friend. The line was ok and the staff were really nice. Like the deco of the restaurant. When we entered the hallway of the restaurant, all the staff greeted us in Japanese with a joyous voice, cool. Ramen was less than decent in portion, yet quite tasty with rich and oily soup. My friended said the rice was really good. Crowded and obviously the staff wanted us just finish the food and leave. It took them around 8 mins to get the change for us. All in all, this place is worth trying but somewhat pricey. Very commercial and westernized rather than an original Japanese-style ramen stand where you feel cozy and down-to-earth in the streets of Tokyo or Osaka.

If I had to sum up this place in three words it would be yum yum yum!. Cured meats are great...as are the crostini and the panini I have tried. As mentioned by others...don't forget the dessert and coffee.
An amazing meal, service & atmosphere! Will definitely be back & would recommend to anyone. While not a cheap night out- thoroughly worth every cent.

Awesome, thanks to yelp. We headed there following numerous advice and it was has expected. Waiters are quick and sympathic, blue berry paincake are delicious, full breakfast is well prepared and the price is in accordance, less than 20$ for two. Next visit we will come back!!!!

One of the best meals I had while we were in NYC. The corn was amazing, in addition we ordered the Cuban sandwich and the grilled skirt steak. Both were as amazing as the corn. Also ordered the ice blended Mojito but that was a little too sweet for my taste. Service was mediocre, but it was busy so can't complain. The place is pretty cramped too, but for the food, it was all worth it.

This place is yummy-whether you get the regular cheeseburger or the Shakeburger, its scrumptious, soft, tender and delish! Burgers are $4.50 so it's not that bad of a deal for a quality burder. They tend to run a bit small in size, but hey, at least you can enjoy one without feeling like a fat lard after :-). Also a fan of the fresh squeezed lemondae, not so much on the shake-they are TOO sweet and heavy for me - the fries are just ok, but if you're here, you know you're ordering them anyway to go with the burger. Enjoy! If you work in FiDi, definitely make it out here, even if it's a long walk over, definitely do so before the weather gets mucho frio. Best times to come: 1130-1145 and after 130!
Great staff, great beer selection, a bit pricey but well worth it

I'll level with you: Overall, this place is hit-or-miss... And the kitchen is slooooooooow. But two things it understands are French fries and poached eggs. Bank on those. The "Russian Spy," a Moscow-mule variation. Demand a copper cup from the lazy Francophone bartender.

I know pizza in and out ,and this is the best hands down. Â I don't care that it was the first pizza joint in the U.S. Â This is extremely good pizza, probably the best. Â We had a half pep, half mball onion, and one of their white pizzas. Â I love specialty pies, but don't waste your time on the white pie. Â The vibrant red sauce pie with fresh motz, little cupped pepperonis (I forget what those kind are called,) Â and perfection for crust. Â The white pie was a thicker pie whether it be from the crust or the extra cheese on it. Â Suprisingly, I was not that interested in the white pie, with such a perfect red sauced pie next to it. Â Great pizza. I'm going back there often. Â Love the taste of a coal oven pie, can't beat it. Â Number one in my vast book of pizza places tried! Â DELISH

It took them only 3 months to reign supreme in Mexican Food category. Their home made Guacamole is delicious and I am in love with their tacos. The Chorizo Taco is fantastic....My favorite dish, however, is the Cochinito Chiapaneco, pork back ribs, absolutely fantastic ! Their Tres Leches cake is one of the best I ever had. BYOB by now which is a big plus !

As the more and more new customers come in this happens: Price goes up Quality of meat fillings goes down More shortcuts are made Wait times are longer now Lines are longer Person behind me on line is pushing up against my @$$ because the the people in the back Â are trying to get into the store and wait online...why can't you just wait online, but extend the line outside the place...? Â OR is it cause you just want to grind up my ass...barf/ No longer my go to spot for dumplings. Â  Much more other dumpling spots around the corner and down the street.
Really good Italian place. Menu very Italian. Food good. Service friendly. Nice wine by the glass. Prices good. Will definitely come back.

Meh. Came for a late lunch the other day with a friend. Because of the holiday, they were serving brunch all day. Started with a cappuccino, which was solid. Ordered the porchetta panino which was very underwhelming with small bits of pork, random globs of mustard, and forgettable caramelized onions. The side of arugula salad was atrocious--it tasted as if the entire salad was washed in a saline solution. Otherwise, the place has a nice ambiance and pleasant waitstaff. TL;DR - worth your time if you're just getting coffee; food is sub-par at best.
Been here for brunch, lunch, and dinner. Â Brunch is overrated - really not worth the wait; lunch and dinner was terrible; horrible service and food so salty.

Really enjoyed a dinner here this week. It was my first time, and I thought the burgers were delicious. I was early for our reservation and took a seat at the bar. When my friend arrived, despite a table being offered to us, we decided to eat at the bar. I took the mushroom and gruyere burger (loved the dijon added) while my friend had the Bash burger. It was hard not to inhale the burgers. We ordered medium and we got medium. It was perfect. Our tap beers (IPA and the Milk Stout) perfectly complemented the meal. I will definitely be back.

Came here at 3:59pm on a Saturday and made it for brunch with no wait! Hooray for hangover/lazy Saturdays! Ermerrgerrrdddd the Benedict Jane! The crab/crawfish cake actually tastes like it has a lot of crab in it. The dish also comes with delish fried potatoes. Vanilla Bean French Toast was too sweet in my opinion--but I guess that's what you should expect when you read that it is made of creme brulee batter. Ordering one dish of this for yourself is just too much to handle. I would recommend sharing it. Also, get the +$3 strawberries and bananas. It actually makes the toast taste much better; I guess it adds some variation to the taste. (Also it makes you feel better that you're being at least *slightly* healthy...) The major shocker was the $6 glass of orange juice. I guess the OJ was fresh and all, but I really should've asked about the price before I ordered it! Also, +1 for the super friendly and attentive waitress!

Absolutely delicious. Definitely worth the wait. We went around 5pm to put our name in so that we could eat dinner at a normal time. After we were seated, the food came out very fast. They also have build your own ice cream sandwiches. Soft cookies with rich ice cream after flavor filled meatballs. What more could you ask for? Mmm.. so delicious.

Tasting menu. Changes Daily Amazing! Bacon donuts were fantastic - just the right amount of saltiness and sweetness. Loved the Pork belly smoked risotto, short-rib sliders, watermelon gazpacho, spicy bigeye tuna tartare and strawberry glazed ribs. I will be going back, as a matter of fact, I cannot wait to get back here to try everything else on the menu. Liked the beer selection and cannot wait to go back and get my fix of Inus and Gunn beer. Friendly service, deserves every bit of 5 stars. Get the Bacon Donuts!

I'm truly disappointed. I had so much expectation for this place. Came here for lunch. We ordered the Cookshop Mezze (the only thing that I would order again), the Chilled Carolina Shrimp Salad, the Grilled Long Island Squid Salad, and the BLT. Other than the Cookshop Mezze, the rest was just average. Portion is small. The kids had the BLT which I don't understand how you can get it wrong. For $15, I'd expect it to taste at least as good as the ones I pay back in L.A. for half of the price. I understand that the cost of living is higher in NY, but it can't be 100% higher and be of an inferior quality. I am just very underwhelmed. My kids are 12 and 11 and can usually find things on most restaurants' menus. However, I would say that their menu is not kids friendly.

Great place for peaceful brekky in a beautiful neighbourhood. We walked across the Brooklyn bridge to here the other day, and it is a pleasant walk. Avocado toast w soft boiled eggs did not disappoint! They have almond milk for lactose intolerant me to put in my coffee. Yum! We went back another time for coffee, enjoyed it very much.

This is my new favorite after work spot to go with a friend or two. It does get crowded but I usually get lucky and find seats at the bar or sandwiched between groups which suits me fine for a couple of drinks and an app. If you do want to sit down right away, call up first. Really great happy hour deals and good drinks. Their menu is not your typical bar fare and has items like chicken-liver mousse (amazing), bacon wrapped dates and salmon tartare but also includes the go-to's such as truffle fries, tacos and mac&cheese but done up a little more refined.

If i could give them 10 stars, I would. Â Emorn and Eric (husband and wife duo) are so friendly and its clear that they cook with love. Â  I go at least once a week and it is always always delicious. Â I've had their specials several times when they have them on Fridays, and I'm convinced they are only capable of producing amazing meals.

My friend T told me that I'd wake up thinking about soup dumplings the following day. Â I thought this was impossible because the only food I wake up thinking about is Five Guys Burgers. I hate when T is right, but he was right. Â I almost don't mind that I burned the crap out of my mouth on the first try though my lower lip is bright red and I no longer have taste buds. Â I still want to go back now. Â Like, right now. Â Soup dumplings are great (I only had the pork) though there is definitely an art to eating it correctly which I obviously have not mastered. We also had the crispy beef which was good too, but was not soup dumplings. Â  Place is pretty big, wait was 45 minutes on a Friday around 6:30 (we got foot massages across the street while we waited) and they seat patrons in wherever they can fit you.

Best Halal food I've ever had. Â Went on a Monday around 12:30. Â The line was pretty long but got longer after we had gotten our food. Â They had a limited menu with just a few things if I remember correctly but I'm sure that's to the customer's advantage. The three of us ordered the "Combo" plate which consisted of a small side salad, a couple small pieces of pita bread, a generous sharing of tasty yellow rice(saffron?), and the most moist and tender helping of chopped chicken and lamb. Â I think that's what did it for me...how delicious the meat was. Â I have had dry chicken and lamb before but this place cooks it perfectly. The location is nice...you can sit on the sidewalk seating nearby. Â The meals will really fill you up but not so greasy or thick that you will feel bloated, in my opinion. Â I snarfed it all down and felt just find afterward. Â I love the word snarf...

Equally as great as their flagship location in Paris. The location is quaint but is staffed with nice workers willing to engage you in possible gift ideas or discuss their most popular flavors. The only downside is that these delicate macarons are hard to transport in the summer heat of NYC!!! __ June '12 Health Score - A!

Came here after work around 7pm wanting to try something new. If you come, try to make a reservation and don't come starving because the dishes are small. It was hot and my bf and I were not extremely hungry so Casa Mono was just what we needed. We got a seat at the kitchen bar in two seconds without reservation. It was fun watching the men cook up the little dishes. Everything looked cooked to perfection. Pumpkin Goat Cheese Croquettes were being made constantly so we ordered and did not regret. It's fried crunchy goodness on the outside and hot soft creaminess on the inside. The Duck Egg and Mojama (salt cured tuna) came out a bit salty but the hidden potatoes underneath were yum. Bf got the Skirt Steak, which was so much more worth it! Same pricey price, but had more flavor that I definitely wouldn't have thought of. No wine this time, but I think it would have complimented all our dishes. For the grand slam, we got burnt vanilla custard. If you crave sweet and burnt together, get it here!

Incredible and I mean incredible vegan burger. Incredibly fresh made on the spot. They offered vegan and straight carnivore bacon options, fascinating. Great selection of local beers. They were absolutely accommodating in swapping around tables so we could fit our whole party in their tiny space. Their portions however tend to be on the smaller side, relatively speaking.

I love Bianca's! This was my second time here. Bianca's is great, because it is delicious Italian food AND the prices are so reasonably perfect. (Cash only) You cannot make a reservation here, but you can get a drink at the bar right next door while you wait. (We have never waited over 30 minutes) No worries if you haven't finished your drink once your wait is up, just bring the glass over to Bianca's. Not to mention the charming host, hostess, waiters, and waitresses I have come by during my dinners here, but the restaurant is so charming as well. My boyfriend and I got 2 appetizers, 2 entrees, dessert, and a bottle of wine (Chianti!) for $86!!!!!! You simply cannot beat prices like that in NYC. We brought his parents back this weekend, and we will be sure to come back again and again! You can't go wrong at Bianca's!

I brought my sister here for her birthday dinner and we had an incredible evening. The space is intimate with candlelit wooden tables. They have these adorable tables for two in the front that are perfect for a romantic date. Â The larger tables with the bar stool chairs are not the most comfortable in the world, but the experience more than makes up for it. The overall atmosphere is classy, without the pretentiousness. The food here is authentic Italian cuisine. Everything is extremely fresh and the pasta is made in house. I highly recommend the organic pasta bolognese for an entree and the outrageously good caprese salad for an appetizer. I've had caprese salad a million times before, but PT's is exceptional. The chocolate moose with vanilla bean ice cream for dessert was a party in my mouth. The prices are on the higher side, but nothing out of hand. A perfect Williamsburg restaurant for a nice evening out.

I have been here a few times already, this place quickly became my go to spot for drinks and food after work, the food is amazing, the steak tid bits with blue cheese is awesome, and their service is great, the Ber keeps are attentive and just really awesome people. I love this place

Yum! Came here for brunch on a beautiful January morning. You must get the Chicken Biscuit: fried chicken cutlet on a biscuit w/ honey butter & hot sauce. Such goodness. They have a huge selection of pies, and I opted for the S'mores pie that day. It was a winner. I also tried their orange juice & beer drink. Nice & refreshing. This place is cash only and quite affordable. Go!

this place is a small whole in the wall in new York's china town. it was a couple blocks for the subway but worth the walk. if you're with a small group, expect to be seated with strangers. this is my first experience and I'm quite positive that others were a tad uncomfortable eating face to face with strangers too. i love the soup dumpling here, especially the seafood one. It is so juicy and each bite (for me) was tastier than the other. I like to eat it with chili oil and dip it in the vinegar soy sauce they offer. the lo mien is yummy too. i was so stuffed from the hot and sour soup and dumplings that i couldn't finish the lo mien. in terms of cleanliness, it reminded me of any type of Chinese restaurant in china town. the service was prompt but the waiters have heavy accent. Â this was my second trip there, and it wont be my last.

I was reluctant to visit Gyu-Kaku. From the outside looking through the window the place seemed small and mostly a bar. I was surprised when I brought Â family to dine there. The place is very large with many comfortable booths in the back. The hostess sat us at a very large booth with a Korean BBQ grill. I ordered the a mug of Kirin beer. It was Gigantic, Frosty and thirst quenching. We proceeded to order various items including the Kalbi Short Rib, Harami Skirt Steak and assorted veggies. But you must order the Garlic Chicken Noodles and the Fried Shishito Peppers ( warning the peppers are diabolically hot and not for the faint of heart.) For dessert we had the heavenly Fried Banana Cheesecake Fritter which was simply amazing. The Fritter was warm and tasted as if Junior's cheesecake was melty in your mouth goodness! It was a great yin n yang to the ice cream. The ambiance is fun, clean friendly. The restaurant was reminiscent of an authentic beer hall in Tokyo, that I was fortunate to visit in 2000. I will be back. Tell them Mr. B sent you and get 10% off your attitude about Â having to cook your own dinner!

I can't believe we spent 30 dollars here, for 6 slices. definitely worth it. neighborhood's a lil sketchy. i felt like ive gone to mezzogiorno! asked for more BASIL, really fresh, handed it to me straight outta the box. HAND GRATED CHEESE asked for PEPPERONI, super fresh, cute things Attraversiamo!

It's a cool place. Very pretty, and the food was good. It's got a certain feel about it, a unique restaurant. I enjoyed it a lot. I got a Shirley temple too, very yummy :) It's a great place. I'd go if I were you.

I lived in Belgium for a year and these fries do not do the food of the country any justice. The special sauce which should be the equivalent of homemade mayo is straight from a Heinz bottle. This place is a joke, might as well go to BK or McDonald's and pick up some Hellmann's Mayo on the way home.

this review is for the sandwiches / wraps, not the packaged goods / groceries portion. Â  the wrap i got (tuscan wrap) was pretty bad. first the guys making the dish didnt know the ingredients so they had to check the board - a bad sign. the grilled vegetables were cut into massive chunks more fit for barn yard animals then humans. the wrap ended up more like a C class burrito with soggy oversized vegetables in it smothered in what appeared to be mozerrella cheese. Â Everything was really bland and flavorless which may explain why it was so over salted? i ate half of it and couldnt finish the rest and wont be surprised if i get some stomach troubles from the little i did eat. Â  with so many better options literally down the street, the cooked food at f&s offering is sub-par and will not last long if it doesnt improve. Â plus half off sushi after 3pm is super scary considering how warm the coolers are at this place - sketchy but maybe good if you want to get sick and stay home from work

Pretty cool scene here -- kind of dark, the music is at a level where you can actually have a conversation and has a pretty laid back atmosphere. Â Definitely a good 'chill' bar to go to after work or on the weekend. Â We also ordered a meat plate of some kind and the hummus. Â Both were very good.

I got the Plato NavideÃ±o, which is the Venezuelan traditional Xmas platter. A Â must try if you come here. The Hallaca is delish, as well as the pernil and the hen salad. The ham bread is a bit salty but still tasty and moist as it should be. Yummy! The music is nice though I would've loved to hear some Gaita to make it perfect, lol.

With over 1500 reviews and 4.5 stars for a food truck.. what more can I say? Get the combo with the lamb and chicken and rice, but you have to ask for the white yogurt sauce separately (either that or they forgot to hand that to me). Yes the line is long, but it goes pretty quickly. I particularly like the location, mostly since the bf and I were able walk over after putting our name down at a nearby busy Japanese restaurant (refer to my review on Hagi), and devour the lamb and chicken as a starter (no kidding) before going back into the restaurant. Totally worth it when you're trying to binge as much as possible in a short span of time in NYC!

Yep had it yesterday. Â It's everything they say it is. Â Delicious! Â Had the Falafel in the pita with white and hot sauce....yummy! Â My husband had the falafel platter which comes over delicious rice.

This was one of the first restaurants we ate at when we first moved to Manhattan because I heard good things about it. Turns out, the food really is just average, and the services is sub-par. We had just moved from LA at that time and LA has such a great variety of authentic Chinese restaurants that we really were not impressed by Joe's Shanghai at all.

Place to be when its freezing cold and windy outside. The Decor is modern w/ appetizing pictures of delicious foods that they serve. Wait time is to a minimum Staff is prompt and courteous (tea pot is never empty) Most importantly the food. Soup Dumplings (hit the spot, warm tasty soup in delicate but not too thin skin) Good mix of Cold/Hot foods I usually stick to the appetizer menu (that's all you really need)

I recently returned to Kilo and felt the need for an update. I'm hoping the owner reads this. Last time I came the female hostess was so sweet and welcoming so my overall experience was very good. Now they hired some strange guy in a too tight tee shirt who the minute I walked in to see if my date had arrived pretty much blocked my way into the place. He got in my face and told me I can't come in. I told him to back off and I have a reservation. Strike 1! When we sat, my date ordered a glass of Malbec and he proceeded to endlessly drone on about different wines so needless to say we both had no idea what she got. It's a $12 glass not a $300 bottle just bring the freekin Malbec! I ordered a beer and he left the empty bottle. I asked him why he left an empty bottle on our small table and he said "so everyone can see what you're drinking" I don't really think anyone gives a shit about what $6 beer I'm drinking. Strike 2! Not halfway through our first drink he came to the table 3 times asking if we're ready to order. I told him I'll let you know when we are ready and to please stop interrupting us. His response was "this is a small place and we need to turn tables so you need to order right now. We ordered and he practically stood over us trying to clear our plates before we were done. Strike 3! Don't get me wrong. The food is good and the place is cozy but this guy turned me off to ever coming back to Kilo. If the owner follows YELP my advice is you shouldn't have someone who behaves more like a bouncer than a host greeting your guests or you'll have more people like me never coming back!

Probably the best bar we visited during our recent weekend in NYC (we also tried Death & Co, Experimental Cocktail Club, Mother's Ruin...all of which were excellent as well). Just a cool, crazy scene inside...fabulous ambiance and music. And at one point a burlesque stripper came out to lap-dance this dude who was being celebrated by the bar staff, which was pretty awesome, but don't expect that during your visit there. We got lucky! The bar area was SUPER jammed and seemed pretty social too (I chatted/flirted with a couple of strangers over the loud music on my way out)...but here's a tip: if you want a more civilized experience at E.O., come hungry and ask for a table at the back. They serve food till 3am and ushered us right in (Sun at 11:45pm, place was jumpin) when we said we'd be ordering food. So why 4 stars? The food..total meh. We ordered a grilled cheese and quesedillas, both bleh. Should've gone with bone marrow poppers and reuben fritters. Next time!

Had an amazing experience here with my friends. We recommend The White & Green, The Axel Rosenberg, Six Points "Get Safe" Saison, Get there early, or be prepared to wait! read our whole review here: thewalkinkitchen.com/201â€¦

On to the entrees, we asked the waiter for his recommendations, and he responded with the Vaca Frita and the Quesadilla de El Salvador. I had been eyeing the Vaca Frita anyway so I decided to go for it with his blessing. It was Cuban skirt steak, latin fried rice, tomato escabeche, avocado and fried eggs. And oh man was it good! The steak was tender and teeming with latin flavor, the rice was a little dry but the escabeche (tomatoes, red onions, lemon juice, and parsley) gave it a nice little kick. The fried eggs were perfectly cooked with the yellow of the egg spilling out upon first cut which I also mixed in with the rice. Â The girls got a Cuban sandwich, Tortilla Espanola, and Quesadillas de El Salvador. Now the trick to the unlimited sangria is to eat slowly, so everyone (except me because I was so excited by the delicious food on my plate) enjoyed their meals at a dignified pace. Everyone was happy with their food, and we all vowed to come again soon! (Especially since our bill came out to only $21 each including tip- what a deal!!) To read the rest of my review, check out my blog - City Lights and Tasty Bites citylightsandtastybites.â€¦
I know this place made me throw up and miss part of my first week of work, but keep those lychee martinis coming!

We came in on a Saturday night party of 4. Â They don't take reservations but there wasn't a wait. Â We ordered the following: Â Fettuccine with clams Â $15.00, This week's scallop special $18.00, along with the shrimp special. Â Everything was pretty flavorful and delicious. Â The fettuccine with clams had a lot of garlic in it and the texture of the pasta was perfect. Â The shrimp special was also very flavorful. Â It came with 4 shrimps over a bed of "paella". Â We also ordered oysters and calms. Â I think I still prefer Fish in the West Village but this spot hits the spot with no wait! Â :)

After waiting over an hour and shelling out over $70 for two people for a couple appetizers, two iced teas, and two sub-par ramen bowls (tip not included), I can confidently say that this place is completely overrated by Yelp users and it should not deserve a 4 to 5 star rating. Pros: Friendly and good service, modern and fun environment, and delicious appetizers. We got the pork/chicken buns and a deep-fried lotus and shrimp special appetizer, which was definitely the best part about our meal and I highly recommend. Cons: Oolong iced teas were good, but not great and the amount served was only about 6 to 8 ounces (after the ice), and refills are not free, which was something that our server failed to mention. I got the Tori Ramen and was disappointed not only in the very salty broth and little amount of food, but the lack of ingredients that came with the noodles and soup. My girlfriend got the Wasabi Shoyu Ramen, which was not only very salty, but very sweet, and eating the tofu that was completely soaked in the broth was like eating candy. Both of us love authentic noodle soups and it's rare that we leave even a single drop of broth, but in this case, half of our bowls were still full of the broth because we did not find it eatable/drinkable. In conclusion, we left disappointed, unsatisfied, and feeling a bit ripped off. The ramens that we ordered were not only small in size and limited in ingredients, but they lacked a full and flavorful broth, which in my opinion is the best part about any noodle soup. I don't mind paying a lot for good food, but $17 for a bowl of crappy ramen is not what I expected on a Saturday night out with the girlfriend, especially at a place tauted as one of the best ramens in New York City.

Num Pang probably deserves a good rating because the sandwiches really are good. That's the most important thing about any eatery; good food. Num Pang adhere to an almost consistently high standard with their fresh ingredients and great sandwiches. I'm rarely ever disappointed on that front (stay away from the Chicken Liver though). I've eaten there a lot since I my wife first took me there roughly one year ago. I guess the true test of a how good a place is relies on how willing you are to return and clearly Num Pang passes that one, because the amount of times I've enjoyed their food is in the double digits. My favourite sandwich so far has probably been the Pork Belly on the Special menu. The switch it up occasionally, but it has come equipped with an Asian Pear, or Pickled Rhubarb, either of which adds a welcome sweeter element to the sandwich. You get some veggies in there (I think some carrot and maybe a lettuce leaf), good crusty bread and some very tender, melt-in-the-mouth pork. This is one of my favourite sandwiches in the city and I take a lot of people out there to try it. However, I'm giving this eatery three stars for two reasons. First of all, the place never seems too clean or tidy upstairs in the seating area. They're obviously going for a dimly-lit punk aesthetic akin to somewhere like Crif Dogs, which is fine if you like that sort of thing, but a place always scores a point with me if I can see the table-tops are clean, and it looks like effort has been expended to keep the place looking hygienic and nice for customers. Still, they do HAVE a seating area, which is something - and if you intend to take your food away, this isn't a problem. As a takeaway joint this place gets a fourth star in my book. Secondly, the staff there bother me. I think a lot of it comes down to policy and Num Pang actually has signs up essentially saying that they're not there to accommodate your special requests. The removal, or addition of any items within your Num Pang sandwich is strictly prohibited. Â I think that as far as they're concerned, their job is to get you in and out without any hassle, and they don't need to be appreciative of your business whilst doing it. I get the feeling they go through a high turnover there, because I've seen a lot of people working at the store. Some people have served me with a polite attitude, and then gone on to serve others without enthusiasm, and sometimes I myself have been met with a complete lack of enthusiasm at the counter, whilst my friends have had a more positive interaction. You know what? I get this. I really do. They're probably not getting paid much, and I wouldn't want their job personally either. It doesn't even piss me off, but the place still loses a star for it, because the over all experience could be improved if the store were run differently. I'm not saying it needs to change, because I'll still eat there a lot going forward. But if it did change, I think it would be welcome. Â  -MVB

Nothing spectacular about the food or service. It's what you come to expect of these restaurants in Chinatown. My girlfriend loves their Wonton Noodle Soup. I always order a rice dish when hitting up one of these Chinese restaurants and I can say for sure it is nothing special. It is better than some of those dingy dirtier places, but overall not all amazing. As others have said, prices have increased and portions have decreased, but that is true for most places nowadays so no biggy.

Happy Hour until 10PM!! Need i say more? Enjoy a nice cocktail and some good food as a pre-game to your night out in the city. The ambiance is very trendy and romantic with candlelit tables and good music playing. It can get a little crowded so get there early to get a table. Prices? Vodka w/tonic $5 during HH, can you top that?? I would def recommend!

This is the best pizza in the WORLD! by the slice, all you're gonna get is cheese, but it is the perfect piece of cheese pizza! Call in a whole pizza to take home and you won't be disappointed. Small seating area, so you may have to walk and eat. Very friendly staff. Prices are great, too. I would eat it EVERYDAY...!!

Just when I thought all the mediocre banh mi shops in NYC couldn't get any better I finally made it this this shop in heart of Sunset Park and was I surprised how good it was. I have tried both the number 1 (pate with head cheese) and number 8 (grilled pork) banh mi sandwiches. Both were very delicious. They use good bread and don't skimp on the fillings. A few things I would change though would be to use real french baguettes (the thin long kind) instead of the large sized breads. Also use french butter instead of mayo. I have yet to see a banh mi shop in NYC make it this way (mostly due to cost). Otherwise this banh mi shop highly recommended and is worth the trek.
1. Â Food is excellent. Â 2. Â Call in advance if it's busy. 3. Â Bring cash for food and parking. Â 4. Â The place is small; see number 2.

A wonderful spot with an East Village feel in an otherwise lackluster neighborhood. We showed up around 9:30 on a Friday night and had no wait, but I can see how easily this place gets crowded. (4/5 stars for the lack of space...) The food selection is broad and pretty fairly priced. We got the Grand Plate- Chef's Selection which, at $55, was more than enough for two of us to share and a great way to sample the menu items. The beer list is huge and the servers are not at all snooty about helping you make a selection. The real icing on the cake was one of their homemade grain mustards that we fell in love with. We asked our server about it and he struck up a deal to conveniently package a few oz. of it up for us to ring up at the counter and take home. Some serious customer service there, folks.

After eating at Traif a few weeks ago, we wanted to try this sister restaurant, and this past weekend, we did just that. Overall, we enjoyed the experience at Xixa more than Traif, though both were great. The service was just excellent, the food was amazing and the decor is really interesting. We ordered 10 dishes to share among 3 people, and they were all pretty much excellent. My favorites were the fish tacos, the corn flan with crab, and the fried Brussels sprouts. I also love that the menu is divided into categories based on actresses personalities. My only criticism is that a few of the dishes were just too tiny for the price. $17 dollars for one bite of food per person? A bit steep, but overall an excellent experience!

The place is hit or miss in terms of happeningness. I like the setup. A nice date spot - they have many tables for two. Also not a bad spot to grab drinks with friends - they have a pretty big table booth like spot that can sit larger parties. Good service. Good drinks. No complaints. Okay place all around.

Great Ramen, though line can be long. Â Apparently this place is a major chain in Japan, and no considered top quality there, while in NY, its a Hot Spot. Â Try the Modern Ramen, or their specials. Â Good wings too.

Dark and rustic atmosphere great for a date, or perhaps snogging the cute waiter in the bathroom with the see-through door. Tasty stuff all over the menu. Great for cold night. Seating more like manhattan than in this borough restaurant.

The Smith is crowded, full of NYU kids, and a bit expensive. Who cares! It is still fantastic. Â Why you ask? 1 ) They make an elixir called The Traveling Brit. It is, by a big margin, the best drink I've ever tasted. I know, it is a very bold statement considering I've tasted the Caipirinha at Sunita Bar but I really mean it. * 2) I love scantily clad college girls. Scratch that. I love all scantily clad girls and there are lots of them here. 3) The chicken pot pie and onion rings are delicious. 4) The dinner booths are very cozy and there is always a comfortable buzz around which makes you order that superfluous bottle of wine. Okay, who am I kidding? There is no such thing as a superfluous bottle of wine. * and how ironic considering that I am moving to London soon?

Can someone explain to me why one can experience Brooklyn's Restaurant Week for $25 a pop, but in Philadelphia it costs $10 more? Unfair. I was very lucky to experience "Dine In Brooklyn" last weekend at Kiwiana, at the recommendation of my BFF, Maddie O (Yes, she's Elite). Amber C and Kyle L even schlepped all the way down from Greenpoint to join us! This gorgeous Park Slope restaurant is tiny and bright, with small glasses of fresh flowers covering all surfaces. So cute. The fresh and homey decor made me want to Pin it for all the world to see! Our server was super likable, with a casual yet professional attitude (wanna be friends?) Now, the food. I started with the seared sea scallop on top of cauliflower and bacon mash, which was served on a giant scallop shell (I didn't even know the shells were that big!) It was gorgeous. For my main I chose the fried chicken, which Maddie O had gushed about. I never order fried chicken. Ever. I don't usually eat dark meat (upon cutting into the thigh, I had to ask my dining mates "is this done?") but I should more often. Juicy and delectable, this chicken was drizzled with TRUFFLE HONEY and served alongside a crisp kale salad and mashed potaters (which were unfortunately room temp, dammit). I simply could not decide on a dessert so I was more than happy when our four-top agreed on getting four different menu items and sharing. We tried the molten chocolate cake, the bread pudding, a lemon mousse and the "pavlova," which is a meringue filled with whipped cream and topped with fresh fruit. Totally stole the show, in my opinion. Can't wait to go back.

the third time i try to eat at this joint, i finally make it in. luckily it was a ten-fifteen minute wait. my friend and i sat at the bar, quickly ordered limeade with rum and their praised corn. it took us awhile to order our entrees, but i ended up ordering the shrimp tacos, which came with rice and beans. first let's cover the drink. limeade with rum on a hot summer day just hits the spot, nice and refreshing! second, the corn. it wasn't the most ah-mazing corn i've ever had. don't get me wrong, it was pretty good, but definitely not something praiseworthy, at least not in my book. the cheese, chili powder, and lime definitely add some good flavor to the grilled corn. but it was completely drenched, that you forget you have corn underneath. and i dunno if it's supposed to come out lukewarm, but i prefer my grilled corn hot. last but not least, i've had mexican corn, and this does not compare to the real deal. it's a nice rendition, but not what i am used to. being born in la and spending the last nine years in sd, you can't help but become a conossiuer for mexican eats. good mexican food is one of the meals i miss dearly since moving out to the big apple and i've come to terms with the fact that i just won't find it out here. this isn't to say that mexican food I've come across is horrible, just not the same. last but not least, the shrimp tacos. the tacos were delish! shrimp was a little overcooked, but the pico de gallo, guacamole, cabbage, white sauce, chipotle sauce on the side, and a squeeze of lime all over the business did make my taste buds have a little dance. overall, this place has decent food, but i just don't know that it's worth the long wait. if i have to wait more than 15-20 minutes, i will gladly move onto the next restaurant.

Dom DeMarco is the Jerry Garcia of pizza. People who see pizza as nothing more than a cheap and quick indulgence will leave scratching their heads. People who appreciate food made with love and patience will find an experience bordering on the spiritual. In fact I think it's best for your first visit to go with someone who's been there before - a guide, if you will.

Calle Ocho, you used to be my favorite spot till you moved and changed the menu... I am giving you 3 stars only because your Brunch is still okay, your sangria is amazing, I love the complimentary pan de bono and your calamari is exceptional. Other than that.. the menu is blah.. and under NO circumstance should you ever order the Lechon.. A restaurant should never classify itself as 'Cuban' and serve bad Lechon. We Cubans do NOT fail at roasting pig.

Expect a crowd at brunch. We were placed in the backyard with iced coffee on a tray as we waited for an open table. They didn't forget about us (which was a huge concern of mine) and we were seated well before our 30 minute estimation. The food comes out as it's prepared, so you might get your food waaay before the rest of your table does! But who cares when it's so delicious. We were there for brunch and got the duck fat biscuit, cast-iron pancake & the breakfast burger with a side of greens. Did I say it was delicious? Definitely going back.

To walk by Chuko and smell it's awesome food and not stop by is a test of true strength. So delicious and homemade. Can't have wheat? No problem. They'll serve up gluten-free (noodle free) ramen. Kind of an oxymoron, granted, but it's a great way to enjoy a treat that would otherwise be out of bounds. EDIT: I went recently and was told that the broth has miso and soy, so the gluten-status is unclear to me. I pretty much left in tears (of sadness) since I couldn't be sure enough to have dinner, but I'll go back in a better emotional state and ask (and update here).

I'm a little mixed on this place with food but overall atmosphere is great. Loved the poached eggs on salmon but today the insides were a little cold! Â And my eggs today were supposed to be on avocado but it was runny guacamole instead. Just a little bit of a letdown for $20! Â Also the coffee was good last week but today was sour. The place deserves another shot though. Great for morning meetings!
I started coming to this place in 1970 when I moved into Sullivan St. Really good food but I feel it's time had passed. Same great service it always had but the magic is gone

We love this place, and it definitely still does not dissapoint. Â This time we also got the pork buns which were delicious, The pork is so tender, but i must say i think we prefer the pork buns at Momofuku though.

This place is rather cozy (read: cramped and crowded), and the menu didn't excite me with the usual fare of poached eggs, French toast, omelet, etc., but everything is well done, and the prices are fair if the portions are not generous. French toast reminded me a little of the Trader Joe's frozen French toast, but fresher obviously. Just nothing terribly special about it. Andouille sausage and pepper hash with poached eggs was a more savory and more successful dish, but unlikely that I'll be craving it again any time soon.

Had the whole menu there practically. Â Family outing with parents, sisters and their family, and myself. Â We made sure to order everything on the menu. I would say that the fried chicken was the biggest disappointment of the evening. Â I wanted some real down juicy well seasoned fried chicken, but I had a leg and thought, "maybe the good ole Colonel does mass produce decent fried chicken." Â But with some of the syrup it definitely helped. The waffles were nice and fluffy and I would say definitely the highlight of that plate. Â If I deboned the chicken and put syrup on the chicken and made a waffle sandwich, probably would have been a bigger fan. Mac and cheese was cheesy (a little under salted and overcooked for my taste), yams were good, collard greens were good. Â Basically all the sides were well made. Â Found myself dipping into everyone's sides here and there over and over again. Pork chop was a little disappointing as over sauced and cooked. Â  But OMFG, I got the turkey leg with sauce and that was over the top. Â As soon as I bit into the first big tender wing, I was in heaven. Â It was the best part of thanksgiving (and in my opinion the best section of the bird too) on one plate with a healthy serving of sauce.
Delicious "neighborhood" pizza in Brooklyn that would be the best artisan pizza in town in any other city in the U.S.

Great place - beautiful dining room, really friendly service. Â Our waiter was really helpful and amusing - clearly an actor with a lot of personality. Â His descriptions were thorough and much-needed, since I can never remember what a chacroute is... Great frisee salad and hiramasa tartare to start, he suggested a ridiculous, unusual trebbiano blend white wine that I loved. Â We had a veal chop special entrÃ©e and the pork chacroute, which is pork three ways over a bed of shaved brussel sprouts in carraway and mustard. Â Really spectacular. Also try the walnut liquer, Nocino, with the cheese plate, and the pecan pie bread pudding. Â We went all out, best meal I've had in a while... I bet weekends are packed, but on a Monday night, it was low-key and perfect... Highly recommend.

Look. I'm Vietnamese and I'm from Southern California. I'm about as close to a Banh Mi Connoisseur as you're going to find around here. The first time I walked by, I thought this was the busiest jewelry shop in all of Chinatown. I got in line just to see what the fuss was about. I got to the front, still had no idea what was going on, said "yes", gave the guy my $4 and next thing I know I'm eating the best Vietnamese sandwich in New York City. Don't fall victim to the "fancy" Vietnamese restaurants that would somehow convince you poor white folk that these sandwiches could possibly be worth more than $8. This is the place to get it and this is the price you should be paying. (Though, to be fair, if you're in LA it's close to $3.) Sometimes, when I have to pause from shoving the banh mi down my face in order to breathe, I sing the Vietnamese national anthem in my head. These things are so good they make me proud to be Vietnamese. I don't even know the Vietnamese national anthem.

As every other review about the Ssam Bar states - the pork buns are seriously AMAZING. If you come here and don't get them you seriously need to re-evaluate your life choices. They melted right into your mouth and... and... and... what was I saying? Anyways, they were absolutely delicious. Now I'm craving some big time. The place was super busy, so my friend and I sat at the bar. The service was fast and accommodating.

We went on Sunday night and had a great time. Our bartender, Steve, was a very charming host. The beer selection is quite good, particularly the draft offerings. The Left Hand Brewing Milk Stout was absolutely delicious.
Oh, man. This is the best restaurant in the area for sure. Everything I've had on the menu is delicious and the prices are super reasonable. Get the fried oysters... you will not regret it.

Nice, distinctive restaurant. Not your typical Japanese noodle bar. It's fancier and a good place to go if you're looking for ramen + atmosphere + you don't mind sharing a table. You can also get your own booth if you're a big party. For me, the ramen is okay but there's too much noodle+soup and not enough toppings. I'm a bigger fan of momofuku.

Wow this is such a little hidden gem. Why haven't we met before. Deciced to eat at the bar and perhaps my best decision of the evening. The bartender chip was amazing, informative and friendly . We ate the fluke crudo over apple to start alongside the pate and pickled vegetables. For entree we had the pork tenderloin. This is without doubt one of the best dishes I have had in ages..I truly didn't want it to end Finished with the brioche, pear and ice cream. Perfect finish to a great meal. Drinks are top notch. This place actuallly knows how to make real cocktails.I recommend the new fashioned and fake Russian. This could be a one of my top 5 in the Â west village. Cosy and non pretentious its a must visit.

Everything so yummy. Had the chicken and waffle and sausage and gravy over biscuit. Started with mac and cheese balls. Everything delicious and as tasty as brunch gets.visitn from houston..il b back next time in nyc.
I live right near this gem -- yes it is cheap yes it is fast yes it is AWESOME dangerous combo if you ask me.... just avoid "typical" dining hours, as it gets ÃœBER crowded.
Super tasty dishes; pleasant, efficient service; acoustically challenged when at full capacity.

I bring everyone I know here, It's that good. I'm a vegetarian, none of the people I know have gone veg so there's something for everyone here! Service: waiters ALWAYS know what they're talking about. They're always nice not always big talkers but I'm fine with that. Food: I think its the seitan fajitas I love... or the burrito... I think its the fajitas. AHMAZINGGGGG. My dad who is so against anything that isn't meat also loved them (bonus points to de mole!) Their desserts aren't usually something you'd write home about but I do like their tres leches cake. They have Jarritos!

Great place to catch some games/ drink craft brew, wish they had a few more tv's.. probably 2nd favorite bar in the city after Stags Head..40 different beers on tap and they rotate what they have. Frequently have brewery nights where they tap their stuff, the wings here are a little small but fresh and cooked well, they won't grill them if u ask, hot sauce is really good.

Living in nyc, my stomach would get pangs of missing in n out. Â And the ubiquitous white castle and wendy's burgers just don't do. Â Unless you need to flush out your system, of course. Â Actually i think that'd only apply to the former. Anyways, it was during those episodes of missing the best burger ever i'd venture down like 7 blocks westward to corner bistro. Â It's no in n out, but for the time being in ny, it'd do.

Cute little place for lunch!! I love watching the guy making the soba noodles. He's so smooth and quick. The waiters are also attentive and quick. I ordered the tempura eel hot soba noodle. I was a little sad they put the tempura in the soup, so it was all soggy and it was hard to pick up with my chopsticks. I did improve my chopstick skills and was able to pick up the soggy eel without breaking it towards the end of lunch. The soba noodles were al dente enough and each noodle was the perfect length to slurp. The broth was a little sour for me though. My boyfriend ordered the duck hot soba noodle and that was also delicious. I would like to come back and order the udon noodles next time.

I've stopped at Mamak twice now and was very happy both times. I had the beef short rib stew. It is awesome. I would definitely recommend going out of your way to stop and get some food here. The iced tea with honey is stellar as well. People talking about it being expensive must be new to New York. Dinner that fills you up for $11 is pretty good in my book.
Ended up randomly having dinner here and couldn't have been happier with it. Â The atmosphere is amazing as is the food.

I am always up for trying something new and when Jim brought to my attention that there was this cute little Cambodian sandwich shop near his office we could have lunch at, I jumped at the chance. Â It looks like sort of a stand and that there isn't seating, but if you peak inside the cramped area where you pick up your order, you'll see these scary spiral stairs that lead to a place upstairs where you can eat. The interior of this place is very no frills, however, their sandwiches are quite delicious. I opted for their peppercorn catfish sandwich. Â Everything is made to order while you watch and wait. Â Very delicious flavor, plentiful and different. Â I really enjoyed this. Â The fish was prepared just right and was quite fresh, the greens, the carrots it was topped with were also fresh and tasty. I would come back to try some of their other sandwiches. Â If you are in the Union Square area and are looking for something different, cheap and tasty, I'd swing by here. Â Your taste buds will thank you!

Ate here for the first time last night and wow is the food good! I got the bahn mi burger which was amazing, as were the fries. The couple that work there are super lovely and friendly and you can tell they really care about the food they are putting out. Such a great little place and can't wait to go back and try more!

I'm not supposed to review this place, because we want to keep it a secret. So all I'm going to say is that the wait is worth it, but the ferry stops working and there is no way to get home. Go for the crabs, but make sure you have a ride.

Yeah I said it......Totto is better than Ippudo, and if you get there before 6pm you won't have to wait. Â The food comes out fast and they expect you to eat and leave in the same manner. Â I got the miso ramen (white girl ramen), my friend got the spicy. Â The noodles are al dente, and i probably killed 4 trees from all the napkins I used. Â Ramen is a horrible date food. Â  Lesson learned.

This new cafe is most welcome to the neighborhood, which lacks a decent lunch spot. Â  Although the vibe is really nice, everyone is friendly, and the menu is decent, these guys could use a couple of tips with the food. Â I have two main problems: 1) bacon fat. 2) portions. 1) I know there is a trend toward loving fat these days, but everything has a limit. Â Bacon fat in your burger? Come on guys. Â Bacon fat in your apple confit on the turkey sandwich? Â Why? Â The reason we needed a new lunch spot was to have a LIGHTER lunch... if I want lard, I'll go to one of the many mexican joints. Please lighten up! 2) The portions for many of their sandwiches are pretty tiny. Â If you get a salad side instead of potatoes you can count on being hungry in the next couple of hours. Â An exception is the tuna melt, which is really nice. Â The worst portion is the daily scramble... I'm sad to say that this dish was really disappointing. Portion was tiny, the potatoes were overcooked and had been sitting around. Â And I could have made much better eggs at home. Â (Sorry!) I'll probably keep going here because I'm in the neighborhood and I want to support them, but I hope they read these reviews and take them to heart. Â They are great people, they have the right idea, and they are just starting out. Â I would definitely give them time to figure these things out and will continue to return, hoping for these improvements to take place.

Food was good and menu inventive. Â Service was solid and friendly. Â Lines were long - but I guess people want to check it out. Â I almost docked them a star because: a) the wait was a little long - but admittendly not their fault just popularity...and (b) they brought me the wrong food - but I think that was because it was loud and crazy (popular place:), and the fixed their mistake pretty fast. Â Atmosphere was fine I don't give a crap about the whole hipster or no hipster thing, the place is decorated well, and so is the tattooed staff.
Delicious food, and excellent service, deliveries are also very fast, I love quesadillas de huitlacoche.

I ordered this lemon shrimp dish with capers over risotto. The presentation was terrible but I'm not judging it based on that. The food was about a 2 on a scale of 1-10. I'll describe it this way: soggy, bland rice topped with 5 unseasoned shrimp from the freezer. The waitress came over and I told her I didn't like the food and she proceeded to the next table to take their orders and never came back to the table. Eventually the runner came to the table. I told him what the situation was and he was very professional. He asked me if I wanted something else, which I declined, and he went and told my waitress that there was an issue at our table. Of course she already knew there was an issue because I told her. She had a really bad attitude. This was probably my 2nd worst (nicks lobster near kings plaza has the distinction of being the worst) dining experience in my life. This was my fourth and final time coming here. The best the food has ever been in my opinion, is mediocre.

This place has promise. Â I'm still liking Fette Sau more, but am intrigued. My husband and I came here for Our Date of Meats in our indulgent spree of going out all the time because we don't know when this baby is showing up (and thus when our dining as a couple days will be swiftly curtailed). Â Double sliders with cheese? Â Tasty, drippy (that's good!), and thoroughly acceptable, but not the best sliders we've ever had. Â Lithuanian sausage? Â Likewise good but not mindblowing. Â Root beer float? Â A root beer float--and is it just me, or are all Wburg eateries of this rough aesthetic serving root beer floats these days? We went to Fette Sau afterwards for pork belly (dessert!), which cemented that St. Anselm may be the offering within the Metropolitan & Havemeyer dark meats & beer triumverate with the most room left to grow. Â That's fine. Â It's new. Â Grow, St. Anselm! Â Make something good of yourself! Â I'll be back to visit (with a quiet baby in a sling) sometime this summer to see how you've developed.
I agree with Julie K and some other yelpers. Really don't understand why this place generates so much traffic. Greasy, not autenthic at all Thai food.
Best potatoes & eggs.Everything is fresh.Fidays Fish day.Very old school and worth every penny.

This place is so insanely cheap. I always have a riend wait in line while I go next door to Kung fu tea for some bubble tea. Be prepared to wait in line for at least fifteen minutes. The smell is amazing, get the pork on noodle instead of rice and get veggies. All for only $3.75
Food was good, service was good, BYOB was great. Â  Little expensive for what you get.

Delicious! A friend introduced me to this place and now i take every out state guest there. Every New Yorker knows about this place. The place is tiny and always super busy but the food is worth the wait. It's my favorite place to go to in the summer. They have a sit down restaurant and a take out Â place next door. The wait for the restaurant is usually long but worth the wait, They will not seat you if your whole party is not there. The take out place next door has same Â and a few tables inside and benches outside. Even thought it is crazy busy you the staff never makes you feel that you have to rush. Back to the food: Always have the corn when you go! it's amazing! The Avocado and Cheese sandwich is to die for also. All of my friends seem to love the Cuban Sandwich.

Located in an alley way of China Town, you can't miss it, there's hoards of people just standing outside waiting patiently for their number to be called. We waited for an hour, only because everyone in your party must be present for them to even consider you, and yes, they do check. It's a small restaurant that's of course filled with as many tables and seats as it can possibly hold and as you walk by the front door you see the big "C" for inspection and you wonder to yourself "why am I eating here again?", but trust me, after they bring out that first tray of steamed xiao long baos, you'll know why. We luckily got seated with two other parties around a large round table. It felt like speed dating, sitting down and dining with people you don't know. The xiao long baos here are definitely different than any I've had in CA, the pork filling was richer and the broth thicker, cloudier and full of flavor. Beware: you may be full after eating 4! so watch what you order. Along with our 3 trays of XLBs, we also ordered wine soaked chicken, spiced beef, noodles with fried pork, Shanghai thick noodles with beef, steamed buns with condensed milk and salt&pepper shrimp (Yes, that's a lot of food. Yes, there were only 4 of us. Yes, we had to take home some left overs, some, not a lot.) What stood out to me the most to me was the Shanghai noodles, super flavorful (trust me, it's good because we've ordered it at 3 different restaurants in CA and none of them tasted like anything) but it was different here. The salt&pepper shrimp was really really good, this is my favorite dish and it was made with so much flavor and spices here, I kept eating them even though my stomach was ready to explode. And if you've got a sweet tooth, get the steamed buns and dip it in the condense milk, perfect way to end your meal, or eat it in between waiting for the next dish.

So this is my second review for this place. Â I believe in second chances, and this place really impressed me. Went with my sister for dinner. Â Got the shrimp and grits which were phenomenal! Â I mean I am still having dreams about it. Â My sister got the burger (my boyfriend got it the first time I went) and she loved it! Â I have to make sure to get it the next time I fo As I said before I really like their wine list (didn't buy any because I work in the wine industry and would never buy wine at a restaurant considering the markup) but they put a lot of thought into the list and have a great selection. Â That is always a good sign. And who doesn't like a free cookie to finish off their meal? Readhead you are OK in my book!

Super cheap food spot. It looks bit intimidating from the outside but it's definitely worth a try. I got the beef stew noodles last time and it was amazing. So hearty. They also have amazing chili oil. Really need to go back and try the wonton noodles that everyone is raging about.

came here for happy hour at a bar on a sunday Come early so you can grab a seat! the bar gets crowded and it's quiet small! Good margaritas and good guacamole. Friendly bartender Only complaint I have is the space. Wished they can extend the happy hour deal to the tables that they have and not just at the small bar

I just moved to the area so I keep finding little things that really warms me up to my new home. Dekalb is certainly of those places a hidden gem. My friend and I were looking for places that would accommodate her special diet. Saw a sign for warm soup. From the outside look like all the other apartments near it just with a garage door not to far from the door making a slight difference. Well I'm glad they had that little sign up. We went in to find a warm place with warm colors of wood and the smell of fresh coffee just brewed greeting us with friendly people at the bar drinking from their coffee cups. A beautiful deity amazon woman with big hair greeted us and gracefully took us to a deeper area. A room completely made of windows ambient lightning and soulful music playing. I sat down on a church pew really feeling the sacredness of this place. We looked at the menu to find things that my friend could eat. I got the endive and she got the braised salsify to start. Then I got a almond stuffed trout and my friend got a vegetable burger. Followed by the parsnip yogurt dessert. The endive was savory and refreshing. I tasted the braised salsify assuming it would be salty but was happy to find a subtle sweetness. The almond trout was big enough for two people to eat but bc of this snow my appetite was large enough. The veggie burger she enjoyed saying she would come back for it again. The dessert was a masterpiece with the pyramid shape topped with a glass like caramel, a rare taste that wasn't overly sweet but just right. Got the check totaling $66 before the tip this had me and my friend nodding at each other yes we found our church of food. Usually food like this is easily $120-$160.

I like the location and restaurant but think the food is decent. We had one of the family style pasta dishes with marinara sauce. The sauce was good and pasta too but nothing to get excited about. A good spot for after the theater and enjoy the decor of the restaurant. Doubt I'd go again unless I was with out of town guests.

Pros: vegans and non vegans can eat pizza here. Pizza was pretty yummy. Cons: the place smells like old water and my pizza was supposed to have hot chili oil but there was not a molecule of spice. Either they forgot it or their chili oil isn't spicy. Overall -2 stars bc of the smell and the pizza wasn't mind blowing. Willing to try again however

This was the best spanakopita (spinach pie) I have had in recent memory. Â Tasted like only fresh spinach, moist but not too moist, and flaky phyllo. Â It was so good I don't even remember what else I had. Â My wife is Greek and admitted that her mom doesn't make it nearly as well. Â It is a bit overpriced for a spanakopita, but worth it for the quality ingredients.

Thoroughly enjoyed my experience this past weekend at Bar San Miguel. I was itching to try it out since I heard it opened recently. I am a big Mexican food lover, and I was very happy with the food and service. Our server molly was very patient and friendly. Lord knows I always have a million questions about a new menu and she answered them all with a smile. Â My one and only idea of something to fix would be the cocktail menu. I found it very limited. I would've enjoyed a fruity tequila based drink, but all I could find were overly tart margarita fusions. Other than that, I left very happy :)

I really love this place. Not only have I never had to wait for a table, but every time I go the food and service is amazing. While I have yet to drink here, I'd like to soon! The booze selection looks awesome. Thankfully, the food is great and reason enough to come to Cobble Hill. The brunch French toast is awesome, it's filled with peanut butter and bananas. Mmm. Service is cheery, and vibe is nice.

With over 1000 reviews I wasn't too impressed with this place. It's quiet authentic, I ordered a very standard pad Thai but it was on sweeter side. Maybe my expectation was too high. It's ok to me, I feel there are better Thai food in Hell's Kitchen.

Really reasonable restaurant for those glutenfree peeps. Â Lots of tasty options. Â The pizza is great, though the options for toppings are pretty interesting. Â The risotto is surprisingly fantastic (I mean it looks like oatmeal). Â The tiramisu was delicious. Â Though the setting is more cafe than restaurant, I was pleased and so excited about eating here. Â I made little mmmm noises the entire time I was eating. Â I even horded the breadsticks away from my eating companion. Â AND you can buy it to go and to stock up. Â Tiny victories everywhere!

What a great discovery! Â My friends and I wanted to eat at a Thai restaurant and used yelp to figure where in East Village we should eat, and I'm glad we chose Ngam. I always complained about the lack of great Thai restaurants in NYC, but now I actually have a Thai restaurant that I would recommend to others. Â All the food I tried at dinner were excellent, and even the drink was great. Â For appetizer, we shared papaya salad (which was spicy and refreshing), Chiang Mai fries (not what I was expecting but still good), and Tom Kha soup (loved the coconut and spicy flavor). Â For dinner, we tried the papaya Pad Thai (great sauce), green curry fried rice (on the mild spicy side) and the green curry with chicken (spicier than the fried rice). Â My wife got a fruity Thai iced tea, which is made without the condensed milk, and it tasted great. The atmosphere is very vibrant, and it's cool to see the chefs cooking at the front of the restaurant behind a counter. Â I would definitely come back to try more dishes!
This place is cool and the food is good...makes me feel like I am in Mexico. It is well worth the visit.

Definitely make a reservation. Even though the place is relatively large and we went on a Monday night, it was packed. We got there a few minutes before our reservation and had to wait for a few minutes before we got a table. The hostess was friendly and offered to let us order drinks while we waited. We were sat quickly though and soon started on our voyage of delicious food. We had the patacon with guacamole and fried calamari to start. Both are large servings and both are delicious. The guacamole was amazingly fresh and the chipotle sauce for the calamari was the bomb. Although the menu explicitly says no alterations and only a paella with meat is listed, they happily made a seafood paella for my wife (and kept cheese on the side of the patacon dish for my sake). I had the skirt steak with cilantro mashed potatoes and gallo pinto rice and beans. Everything was so tasty and the portions were a very hearty size. Their aji sauce is so good and they sell bottles of their sauces. I could barely eat any of my main dish because I had to save room for dessert. My wife and I were only able to split a flan, but we were glad we tried it. They have all day happy hour on certain days - I had a few pine coladas - my only regret is that I could not drink them faster because they were so cold! Our server was great. He was really friendly and even found out the name of a song that was playing. I look forward to coming back soon.

Five stars. For the original, fairly priced menu, alongside reasonnably priced wine and attentive service. More honestly a 4.5 star but the low-key, no pretention atmosphere won me over. Favorites: Pork for two. Kale and rice in duck fat. Scallops. Devil eggs. Decor. Average: beets and quinoa salad, the unique dessert on the menu.

Loves this "hole in the wall." Â Exceptional take-out (although tiny booths are sometimes available). Â Falafels, chicken souvlaki pitas, baklava, spinach roll, the TEA! Â Excellente! Â Excellent service as well. Â They're quick! Â They handle "out-the-door" lines very well. Â Been going here since a small child with my parents.

Very disappointed with the food and the service. Stopped in alone for a quick Caesar salad after a trip to the Museum of Natural History before a meeting downtown, and it took almost an hour to get a lemonade and a salad (both of which were a big disappointment). My waitress seemed to forget about me, even though they weren't busy, and a table that was sat 10 minutes after me had drinks from the bar and an appetizer before my lemonade even came out (not even close to worth the $4, btw). I was really expecting a lot more.
Stopped here with the family after an event at Poet's House. It seemed even more crowded than other Shake Shack locations Â but everything was of the same quality as elsewhere.

Pommes Frites has become an East Village ritual for me. Despite being free, the special sauce is one of my favorites. If only these things were more nutritious... For the ultimate one-two punch, pair a cone from Pommes Frites with a wiener from Crif Dogs (God help you).
First visit to New York, and one of the food place on our list.......Grimaldi's. The wait is worth it.

Was invited to meet family for brunch at a local restaurant that just opened near their house. Â Talk about a treat - the atmosphere was very welcoming and cool. Â The staff was extremely attentive, too. Everyone at our table ordered something different - I was very happy with my eggs (mmm, delish) but I am definitely returning to try the pancakes - they looked incredible!!! Â Looking forward to returning and sitting in their outdoor garden - another unusual perk in the middle of Brooklyn!!!
Fun place to grab a quick sandwich or get some of the real deal Italian food. YUP, real deal.

Farm to table wannabe. Trying to bring locally-sourced, healthy ingredients and recipes and give it that New York, Hell's Kitchen swag...but not so much. Food seems to have decent ingredients, high quality and interesting ideas. But execution is a bit off. They seem to serve everything in a cast-iron skillet, which in theory sounds awesome! I love things in skillets because they keep it hot the whole time, and add some flavor. But in order to do so, they keep a lot of it sitting in a 300 degree oven and then crank it to 800/900 for finishing. And some things come out dry and/or burnt to hell. Even the food runner who brought it out looked at it like uhh...here you go... Don't get the squash lasagna, not a good vegetarian lasagna. Side dishes weren't bad, recommend the kale gratin (yum cheese), meatballs are small, purple carrots with pesto sound better than they are. We actually sat at the counter high top railing facing the other tables with our back to the bar. Servers I saw interacting with tables seemed to be really nice, bartender was a little snooty and too cool. Seating was super super tight, the hostess actually pulls out the large wooden tables to let you in. And once you're in, you're in: no bathroom breaks. Harder to get out than being a window seat in a plane. Not sure under what circumstances I'd try this place again, but would try the lamb and chicken next time around - saw lots of folks ordering it.

This is a great small and intimate low key spot Â for innovative, delicously crafted, very reasonably priced food, with highly attentive personable and friendly service. I had a delightfully unique and tasty comfortable lunch for about $20 (large bowl of Lentil Soup with bread, perfectly grilled free range chicken sandwich on pretzel bread with a Chipotle sauce, side salad with vinaigrette, fresh French pressed coffee at the table, and a complementary desert pastry!)

Ate at Amy Ruth's on the first day of my 7 day trip and was still dreaming about the juicy chicken and crispy waffle until days after I got home. Â  I highly suggest eating the chicken with both the syrup and the hot sauce together.

This is hands-down the best restaurant I've been to in Sunnyside. My friends and I checked it out for Sunnyside Restaurant week, which made it easy to try a number of dishes for a reasonable price. Salt & Fat has a casual, but chic interior , and our waitress was sweet, but efficient. Our meal began with a bag of (addictive) bacon fat cooked popcorn. Then came the appetizers: bahnmi buns and Korean BBQ wraps, both scrumptious. The buns had thick slabs of pork with a tangy mayo-based sauce, and the wraps blended the crunchy lettuce with the melt-in-your-mouth BBQ meat perfectly. As for the entrees, the rumors are true - that oxtail really does fall off the bone. My pork trotter was crispy and flavorful, and paired nicely with pickled greens and yet another mayo-based sauce. The meal closed on a simple note with the chef's dessert, a pear tart with granola and ice cream. The whole time, I was thinking how lucky Sunnyside is to have some great fine dining right in the neighborhood. Take your date, friends, family - do whatever you can to go!

The view was amazing, the food was delicious and creative, and the staff was very friendly. We were assisted by Alexis who managed to make my first visit to Blend an enjoyable experience. I definitely will be coming again...

Love their prices. I always have the same thing. The half chicken, sticky rice and mango salad plate listed under the salad category. Large portions for only $8.99 any time of the day. Delicious, but since I have been having it for many years, I realize that it recently is not as flavorful as it used to be. Also,the music is really too loud so it makes it uncomfortable at times. But I still go back!

2nd time was a charm. Gyro was good, the continents were fresh. I expressed my concern regarding my previous order and the manager saw that my order was filled properly and delivered fairly quickly. The humus was very yummy. I do not typically like humus. I will definitely give this place a try again.

Time Arrived: 11:45am Sunday Time Wait: No Reservations, No wait Party: 2 People Atmosphere: Cozy, classy (Love the floor to ceiling windows), Natural light Food/Drink: Ordered the Poached Salmon Salad for brunch, which was good. Nothing too spectacular. Definitely tasted fresh, but not sure if it was worth $21. As a side, me and my friend shared a side of "fruit" to add some healthiness to our meal. This was a little disappointing because it was more like sweet caramelized apples, not really what we were expecting. Service: Good Overall: Loved the atmosphere. Came here because we couldn't get into the Little Owl. The food was just average, a bit overpriced for its quality...but cute spot in a great area!

Eataly is right down the block from my husband's office, and he grabs lunch there frequently. We stopped in for a quick dinner on a Friday evening, and ate at Le Verdure, the vegetarian cafe (mostly because it was the first cafe we saw and were in a hurry). We were seated promptly, and the service was great -- our waitress was friendly and really took note that we were rushed. The food was good, but nothing was amazing. The real bummer here were the prices -- two apps, one shared entree and one beer came to more than a full meal with drinks would at many NYC restaurants. I was kind of shocked at the cost, TBH. I can't speak to the quality of the groceries, but I wouldn't come here for a sit-down dinner again. Way too expensive.
Good pizza- not worth the wait.

Came in for an after work happy hour last week, and despite the crowd of thirsty attorneys, clerks, and law interns, the servers/bussers were completely on point, attentive, and otherwise excellent. I would definitely come back! DRINKS: they have a decent selection of craft beers on tap as well as bottles, and of course a full bar. Since this was a work function, I stuck with beer, and ended up having the Shock Top wheat ale since just about everything else on tap was fairly generic and/or an IPA. Would definitely like to see a more seasonal approach to what they stock (right now = summer, which = summer ales, wheat ales, shandies, etc). SERVICE: all of them were great, but one in particular remembered everyone's name almost immediately. They were all very attentive when drinks ran low, and cleared empty pint glasses/bottles out very quickly from the area. I didn't arrive until after the party had started, but I could see reservations signs on the tables we were at, so it looks like they were willing to accommodate us during a busy Thursday evening happy hour. FOOD: can't comment on this because I came for a few drinks and then left. PRICES: about what you'd expect from this part of town. Nothing to write home about with regard to specials, but not overly expensive either.

I'm a BBQ snob so I know to steer clear of hyped-up NY smokehouses. Â Sorry Fette Sau, I held out for years knowing you didn't have a chance, but finally relented to the hype recently and am sorry to say I was right. Sauces are either far too sweet or bland, which is not a huge deal cause the meat can do without them and the rolls are totally bogus. Invest in some white bread, y'all. One star for the very good sausage and another for the above-average sirloin. Â Brisket was also OK, but the beans were inedible.

As far as the regular slice.... it sucks. tastes like camp ingredients. I love the setup, the feel of it, and the specialty slices look decent -- But the regular slice was a total disappointment. I really wanted to like it and put it in my pizza app, because it's in a good food oasis, but I couldn't live with myself if I recommended tourists to go here. They are so busy though. I shake my head when tourists come here and are like "Oh my god! NY pizza is sooo gooood!"... nahhh, not here. ... and it's expensive. If you come here, go baller and get something big - probably the only way you'll be satisfied.
