I LOVE the crabmeat dumpling! But sadly that's the only high light. Other dishes are just ok. Or if you go to Joe in 5th ave, try the duck smt in the special menu. It's pretty delicious. Grab a bubble tea nearby if you have to wait in line. But share it or do not finish it cause you'll be too full for the food. Oh and Im also really impressed by an old waiter's table-setup skill in Joe Chinatown. A must see!

The atmosphere evoked a very impressive fine dining experience. Located on the second floor of the Setai hotel, upon entering the restaurant you get this sensation that you will be in for a welcoming treat. Although the selection in the restaurant week menu was not up to par, the accommodating staff and delectable entrees maintained the restaurant's fine reputation

Worst pizza of my life! Came here for my first night in NYC. My bf and I shared a mushroom, spinach, and red pepper pizza. I noticed they sell red peppers by the jar here so I figured it must be good! Its pretty expensive for every additional topping, like $3 or $4. There was no wait but it was also 9pm on a Wednesday. The pizza was super soggy and didn't taste like anything special. We ate the leftovers for breakfast the next day before going to the Met and it was the soggiest leftover pizza I've ever had. It was like it was already digested or soaked in water or something. So gross. Pizza is one of my favorite foods and this was the only place I had NY style pizza at so I'm pretty disappointed!

EVERYTHING in this place is good. Sandwiches, appetizers, drinks, everything. Big portions for great prices. You'll definitely get a full meal for under $10. Some of my favorites are the banh mi fries, the BBQ pork, the pork belly, and the bulgogi. Their coffee is surprisingly good too. You might think this is a small, hidden spot, but the word has gotten out. Good luck avoiding a long line, especially on the weekends.
Really cute, solid French food, byob

Almost 4 stars for me. Â The wine was a bit pricey and my wife's skate wasn't the best I've ever tasted, but the food was good and the service and atmosphere were excellent. Â For the money I think there may be better finds out there, but I think they offer a solid product.

Been here a few times with a friend and for some reason or another my friend always gets more food than I do, even if we order the same plate. The food is decent but overpriced and I Â have patronized this business for the last time. The service is bare as it is more of a fast food type atmosphere. There is a young loooking guy that has always wears his hat backwards and been there in the kitchen everytime I have been there, for some reason he has douche bag written all over him, I mean who can be happy working at a place like this for long. There's countless better options in the area for the price and service.

One of the great things about New York is that the simplest of places can burrow deeply into your memories, especially the fond ones. Five leaves, for me, looks like this: Sunny summer brunch day outdoor dining. Park sounds. Waitress friend. Â The kicker: an artful bowl of house made ricotta adorned with honey comb, fresh thyme, sea salt and mouthwatering figs. Oh so perfect beginning to an oh so perfect day. or: Long-awaited reunion with visiting mother. Â Toasts for new beginnings, the warmth of friendship, and enduring love over some bubbly lovely. Crisp, cold, ocean perfection oysters. Â Oh so perfect ending to an oh so perfect day. thank you 5 leaves. xo.
The service is super nice, but the food is just okay. I would love to rate it better as I like the idea and the design, but the taste is simply not very impressive and the portions are small.
We were in and out pretty quickly. It looks like there could be a wait depending on the time you chose to eat. The pizza was amazing as expected given the reputation.

This place is beyond one of the BEST sushi places I have EVER been to. San Fran, Texas, and even other places in the city don't compare to this little treasure trove. The service was seriously one of the best and the servers were so wonderful. Great experience, I'm going to bring everyone I know here.

Delicious!! So this review may be skewed because it was during the madness of restaurant week. I went with a large group-there were twenty of us divided into two tables. One table was served promptly and mine...well was about ten minutes behind the other. The food presentation was unoriginal, except for the falafel which came out in cubes. We had a variety of appetizers. I would definitely recommend the red pepper, kibbeh nayeh, cauliflower, eggplant, falafel and wouldn't do the watercress salad again. The lamb shank was delicious but came out as a piece of shredded (because it was so amazingly tender) lamb on one plate and two little pieces of cabbage + yogurt + citrus to wrap the lamb in. DO IT. It was so flavorful despite looking rather dull. The vegetarian entree option, the fate, was bland (make sure you mix it). We also tried the candy bar and the cheesecake both of which I would highly recommend, especially the candy bar which was not too sweet or chocolatey, but had a lot of layers of flavor. The atmosphere was interesting for a middle eastern restaurant because it seemed more Asian with sliding doors and the bathrooms more ying and yang. The music was really loud so it wars hard to talk but made it feel more fun. I wouldn't rush to eat here again but if in the area definitely stop there for a good meal.

i like to eat ... ALOT. when i get married, i fear that my hubby will quickly divorce me and/or have an affair with our hottie neighbor next door* once he finds out how many cookies** i can pack in ... or when he finds out how much i like to put garlic and red peppers on EVERYTHING. as much as i like to wine and dine, i am (surprisingly) one of those few NYers that doesn't like brunch. it's not that i don't like the food - bring on the waffles! - it's just that i really can't eat that much early in the day. if only brunch food could be served dinnertime - i'd be golden. however, this past sunday after church - i only go when my uber-catholic mama is in town (SHHH!) - the fam was hungry and we needed a place to eat nearby. stat. seeing as how i've throughly enjoyed my long dinners at stone park cafe in the past, we quickly decided to head over for brunch. not to sound like rachel ray - is it possible to hate someone that much you've never met? - but everything was utterly delish. from my mimosa (bubbly!) to my salmon platter (oh, how i miss eating toasted bagels!) to the bro's omelette (so savory!) to my ma's pancakes (they MELTED in my mouth!). and everyone was soooo nice - from megan at the bar to our waitress from TX. YEEHAW! i'm not gonna lie - i'm still not a brunch convert, but SPC fucking hit the spot. too bad my stomach was bulging when we went to urban outfitters later. now, there's a way to stop compulsive shopping. * - obviously, he/she will NOT have my effervescent personality. ** - or brownies or fish or falafel or peanut butter or sour patch kids, etc. the list really DOES go on and on.

Went here once and had a pleasant experience. Decent food at a decent price and interesting setup in a killer location. Since then, I've tried to go twice and both times I've encountered terrible hostesses with attitude. Prime example: On a Wed. night, the host told me I had to wait until whole party Â arrived before he would even tell me what the wait time is. Fair enough. After three friends arrive about 10 mins later, he tells me it's TWO HOURS. Um, was it really necessary to make me wait 10 mins before you gave me that information? And he was totally unapologetic. Oh, and one of the friends I was with told me the last time she went there, she saw a roach. When she complained they paid her no attention. For the love, go somewhere clean with decent service that deserves your custom.

Awesome little burger place. You walk in and it looks like an old school diner of some sort. It's not sparkling clean, but that's what gives it a fitting ambiance. The burgers are nice 'n juicy for $7-9, they give you plenty of fries, and the beers are in the 10-12oz range for $3-5. Don't forget this is the W4th area, where prices are generally inflated more than the Michelin Man. Definitely a place to check out when you're in the mood for a juicy burger that won't break the bank.
Comfortable. If not close atmosphere. Prompt food service. True, authentic Italian that no one could possibly be dissapointed with.

LOVE this place! They have one of the best burritos I've had in the city and definitely better than Chipotle / Qdoba. Pros: Love how they melt the slice of cheese onto the wrap instead sprinkling it on-- definitely makes a huge difference! The burritos are super flavorful without being incredibly heavy! Cons: Definitely not a sit down place but rather a grab and go kind of place. It gets PACKED during dinner time so the line might be out of the door! I would not recommend the spicy sauce unless you can really handle the heat-- it's HOT! Definitely a neighborhood favorite!
overrated but pretty decent

Balaboosta is a nice cozy place with an open kitchen and pretty good food. We ordered the cauliflower and hummus to start - cauliflower was amazing and the hummus was the same as most regular ones. Â For dinner my friend and I split the market salad, a calamari appetizer special, and the chicken. Â The market salad was great and had cashews, cheese, and apples in it. Â The calamari was kind of strange - it was more like a stew with merguez sausage, beans, cherry tomatoes, parsley, and grilled calamari on top. Â I think the sauce from the sausage just kind of threw me off. Â The chicken was good too although I think you definitely need the sauce that comes with it - without it was a little bland. Â I do agree with other people on the portions because after we ordered we thought we were going to be STUFFED and we actually ended up with just the right amount of food even through we split 4 appetizers and an entree between two of us. Â Overall I think it's a good atmosphere with food that's beyond just "A-OK". Â Definitely try the cauliflower appetizer!

This is a hidden gem. It's hard to get to, maybe even scary depending on the time of night and route of travel but when you pass all the lions, tigers, and late night bears you'll be in for a real treat. Their dips are great, especially their guac. and no matter what you order under their entrees, I don't Â think you'll be disappointed. Some of their entrees can be portioned largely like the burrito and some can be just right like their quesadillas or rice entrees, however, all of these have made me and my stomach happy for the past 2 years that I've been coming here with friends and family.

Went for lunch. Started with a cucumber gin drink which was very refreshing and you would never even know it was alcoholic. Appetizer of calamari which was not worth it - same thing you get anywhere. It said "pretzel dusted" but I didnt expect fried. I ordered the waldorff salad which was amazing! So refreshing! My cousin for the burger which was also equally tasty. A great place for a nice lunch with awesome drinks and nice ambiance. Strongly recommended.

Just went here today with my friends. Had a great time. We arrived around 6:15pm (it's good to make reservations in advance) and the place was still relatively empty. Â It gets really crowded by 8-8:30pm. The restaurant itself looks decent; clean, comfy, though you may jostle for space with neighbors who are right behind you. Although we had to wait a while for our food (almost 30 minutes...but that's because they were making the lasagna from scratch), the food was pretty good. I like the fact that their menu is small but contains a decent f variety of food. We had the cold tomato soup, Margharita thin crust pizza (8 slices), scallops, and lasagna. Everything was delicious if somewhat slightly expensive. We did have the Jesus cake. It's alright...I'm not sure what the hype is. It tastes like chocolate flavored corn bread basically. It's better to have it with the ice cream rather than on its own. Overall, it's definitely a decent place to check out. Would recommend!

I've always heard great things about Cafeteria. It was a hot summer Sunday and I had been strolling around, having already missed arranged plans I was on the search for some grub. Low and behold there it stood: Cafeteria, and I was excited once I realized this was THEE cafeteria I had been hearing about for awhile. I headed to the door. This particular day they had outdoor seating which looked adorable but tight. Inside it was just as tight but when we requested a table for two inside was what was available so we took it an ran. I imagined this place to be way bigger. For some reason anything that has a lot of hype around it I always assume it's just some large really nice spot. Although this place is pretty cute with all the white, it definitely ain't huge (unless I missed a section). It's close quarters. There is a long booth with each table set in front of it so don't be alarmed when you're getting elbowed by strangers enjoying their meal beside you. It wasn't the worst thing though. The wait staff here is decent. Our waiter came by and gave us our menus. I guess because the spot is so busy they don't hang around and chat for too long. He seemed pretty preoccupied We ordered mac and cheese spring rolls, which tasted delicious. Think of a spring roll. Empty out the insides and pack Mac and cheese in there. Excited yet? Now dip it in smoked gouda sauce?! AMAZING. It was really good. A little skimpy on the serving size but delicious none the less. I ordered the veggie burger with fries. I was pleased that they had so many vegetarian options. They had quite a bit and that's always exciting. The veggie burger was okay. I've had yummier but this one was just decent. I can finish everything always but this time I had to actually take my food to go (Once at home I drowned it in buffalo sauce and it was way better). For dessert, they had another nice list to choose from. Â We settled on deep fried oreos. They came with a scoop of espresso ice cream and a milkshake shot. Talk about delicious. It was a dream, that dessert. I really enjoyed it. Overall the place was cool. If in the area I'd stop by especially since they are open 24 hours. I'm not in a major rush to head back though.
The sicilian is amazing, never had a slice this good, and that's comming from a guy that has lived in Brooklyn all his life. You have to try it to believe it. Well worth waiting on line for!!!!!!!!

The ramen here was a bowl full of delight! Â Not a huge ramen lover, but I must admit, this place definitely got me. We waited overall an hour. The hostess told us to come back in 30.min to make sure we don't miss our name, but we may wait another 30 min. At least she was honest. Luckily there was a bar a few hundred feet away. We killed 30min in there then came back. Didn't get called til another 20 min. Mind you, this was around 9:45pm on a Thur night. Not much to look on the menu. Just pick the broth and then your toppings. Food came out quick and we were out in 20min. Well worth the wait! So don't come super hungry, because you're gonna wait.

I came here for date night, and I loved every minute of it! Our server was wonderful and attentive, without being a nuisance. I had the chicken entree, and it was the best I'd had all year. I've bought their roast chickens at their bakery (before it closed) on many occasions, but this dish was on another level. Our meal came to approx. $300, incl wine, tax & tip. Worth every penny!
Mussels are really good at an inexpensive price for a lot. Awesome food at a much cheaper price than it seems like it should cost.

A must go to restaurant in NYC. My mom and I ordered pancakes,fruit, and orange juice. The food was delicious and very big portions are served. You must get a piece of cheesecake. It is the famous Junior's cheesecake! I prefer their breakfast over their dinner menu, but all of the food is great. It's also a great location, in the heart of times square.
I like the double tortilla type tacos they serve here.

Based on the very solid reviews, a friend and I went to Bahche on Saturday night. Â I am completely boggled by all of the four-star ratings. Â I had a chicken pesto panini that tasted off -- there's no other way to put it. I took home a spinach phyllo pastry to go, and it, too, tasted off. Â Both featured a weird bitter taste and an odor I'm going to refrain from characterizing. Â But I don't believe the food had gone bad -- I think this is how their food tastes. Â Mediocre and unremarkable are two words that come to mind. I've never actually written a negative review on Yelp -- I don't feel good about doing it, and figure there are others out there who will. Â But after having a really disappointing dinner for two last night and knowing that $50 (including a 20% tip) could've been much better spent, say, at Cubana Cafe on 6th Ave, I really felt like I needed to. Â The menu is very brief, and some reviewers had noted that. Â They don't really serve "dinner," per se, although they said they are testing one or two entres every night. Â Maybe this is a better brunch place? Â Maybe they're better at catering? As others mentioned, the space is huge. Â And looks it when empty -- there was only one other table occupied in the entire space on a Saturday night when lots of people were out. Â You'd think the service would've been attentive, but I can't even say that was the case! Â I will give the waitress the benefit of the doubt and presume she was new. Â When a table of two orders one dessert, isn't it customary to serve it with two utensils so it can be shared? Last, the street is not inviting at night. Â I've lived in Bklyn for 20 years and I get it -- this area is turning around, millennials are moving in, etc. Â It's Gowanus, not Park Slope. But the street the restaurant is on is not one you'd be inclined to walk down, and indeed no one was anywhere in sight when we left around 8pm. Â There's at least one body shop on the block and many of the buildings are either still warehouses or they're not currently being used; however, it was too dark to know for sure. Â  So all that said, I just don't get it!

My roommates (and fellow Yelpers, apparently) rave about Roberta's, but I give it two shrugged shoulders and one raised eyebrow. The toppings are fresh and fairly tasty, but the pies themselves are bland and mediocre -- about a half-step up from what you can expect to get for free at a bar like Alligator. I will pass. And make a trip to Grimaldi's or John's.

a bit pricey but amazing place to visit! Â originally planned on eating dinner here, but after hearing how long the wait was going to be, we just browsed and left to eat elsewhere. Â came back the next day to purchase little goodies to take home.

i went there with two friends, excited because I live in Bushwick and it was nice to think there were different kinds of food in the area besides Mexican and fast food (which I have no problems with...). So we went to Moto, we were all hungry, the food is all $15++ and the food is all tiny. My friend ordered the lamb, and when it came out I felt sorry for him because of how tiny it was. My other friend had the mac and cheese, who was also still hungry after eating, and even though it advertised some gourmet and interesting ingredients (it's called the 'Aepler Macronnen' Swiss Alps Mac & Cheese with bundnerkase cheese, onion & homemade apple sauce) Â it wasn't very good. And I can't remember what I ate. Just remember being annoyed when the people who showed up in 1930s swing outfits walked in. I think people are confusing "cool and good" with "different" because it is an unlikely place for a restaurant of this kind to exist in Bushwick. If it was in NYC it would be gone in a month.
Fantastic bartenders. Â Great bourbon selection. Â Huge outdoor patio. Â Haven't tried the food yet, but the menu looks promising. Â Prices are generally reasonable.

I haven't been to France in almost 8 years (a little piece of me just died just having said that), but Le Parisien came pretty close to bringing me back without the use of teleporting. Don't know why but I was expecting more of a romantic high end atmosphere... and I'm glad that it wasn't. The mood was casual yet intimate and had a certain je ne sais quoi with its vintage posters, cafÃ© furniture and candles. It reminded me of all those little bistros I would pop into for a meal while running around gay Paris (pronounced "PAH-ree" of course). The owners are French so when it comes to generating that French bistro feel, they know what they're doing. One look at the menu and I was hooked. Steak? Duck? Mussels? Tartare? Check, check and double check. Heck, they even have escargot. I don't eat snails though; I had too many of them as pets as a child. Still, they got 'em. Appetizers -Duck Prosciutto with Melon and Fennel Salad: To start, I had this special. Although the duck was tasty and the melon ripe and juicy, I just wish there had been more of le quack. Oh well. -French Onion Soup: My friend ordered this for his appetizer. I was able to steal a hearty spoonful of the broth/cheese/bread combo and thought it was superb. Just how I remembered it. Entrees -Duck Confit with Crispy Potatoes, Mushrooms and FrisÃ©e Salad: The potatoes weren't particularly crispy but the duck skin sure was! Crispy on the outside and juice dark meat on the inside on top of a fresh bed of frisÃ©e and thinly sliced mushrooms. My only qualm was that portion was on the small side as well. I guess they guard their duck very closely here. -Steak Tartare with Salad and French Fries: Definitely my favorite of the night and the LARGEST of all the entrees. They present you with a giant slab of perfectly seasoned raw beef with a raw egg yolk on top in it's shell alongside a bed of fresh greens. Oh and they give you a hearty serving of delicious, crispy fries. If you love steak tartare this entree is your best bet! It satisfies all of your cravings. Ok my cravings. After all of this food, I had to forgo the dessert menu even though the items looked delicious. Other diners around me kept ordering the crÃ¨me brÃ»lÃ©e which I kept hearing was fantastic. Service throughout by our lovely French waiters was attentive but not overly so. I also loved the selection of wines by the glass which were posted on the giant chalk board near the front. Love that they have wines from Cote du Rhone. La Parisien has definitely become my go to French restaurant that won't cost me my first born. They have a $13.95 brunch special that I really want to check out but let's be honest, unless they decide to serve steak tartar at that time, I'm coming back for dinner first.
Maybe I am being too harsh on this place, however for the price you pay, it's overpriced. Even though the food was very good, the decor is outdated. Sorry.

I like to think I am a banh mi master by now, having stuffed myself with about 6 different ones in one day in Vietnam. That being said, how does this Chinese Take-out-looking place stack up? Wait, why am I asking you? This is my review. It stacks up fairly well. I ordered a pork banh mi for $4.50 (a pretty good price for NYC I'd say), and received a very sizable sandwich. The bread itself was toasted/grilled, but in my opinion a bit too much, as there were visible burn marks on the bottom, and the baguette in general was too crispy; it wasn't a good, flaky crispy either, but a hard, scared-for-your-gums crispy. It wasn't inedible though, so I plowed through it. The fillings were great, and had everything you expect in a banh mi - cilantro, daikon, pork, pate, cucumber, spicy mayo-y sauce. Additionally, there were PEANUTS in here, which I never had in a banh mi. It gave the sandwich a unique flavor and texture, which I enjoyed. The pork itself was a bit dry for my tastes, and le girlfriend said it reminded her of beef jerky (which, coming from her, is actually a compliment), but to each their own. To close my little meal, I had some of the jackfruit shake. If you don't know what jackfruit is, it looks exactly like a durian - big and spiky - but lacking the unpleasant rotten onions taste and odor. I wouldn't call myself a fan of the jackfruit fruit itself, but the shake was pretty good. Then again, that was because it was very milky rather than jackfruit-y, so if you like your shakes as natural and raw as you can get 'em, this might not be for you. Overall, my sandwich was very enjoyable (and cheap), and the shake served as a decent finale to my meal. It's not the best banh mi I've had, but is it one of the best in NYC? Certainly a possibility.

Wow ... Really terrible experience! Â  Steak was underdone and just about everything arrived cold to the table. Â  The manager (tall thin curly hair) was nasty and very unhelpful. Â  Our party of 12 will NEVER return! Â  Spend your hard earned money elsewhere.

A friend visiting from Ohio had Balthazar's on her to-do list for the weekend, so we went for a late lunch. We couldn't get a reservation, so we put our names in and managed to have a meager 90 minute wait. Â Just our luck! The weather was beautiful, and we expected the delay, so we had already picked up a stock of cupcakes from Everything Frosted. Â We walked up and down Spring St. for a while, doing some shopping, and then... Balthazar's dining room has a very classic look, with peeling silver mirrors and tarnished brass, lots of woodwork and yes... defunt dumbwaiters converted into lighting. Â The room is big, and the acoustics make it sound like the floor of the stock exchange, but it reminds you that there are living people around, and they're excited to be there. Our server was just attentive enough. Â He showed up when we needed him, stayed away when we didn't. Â He was a little assertive with the wine and food suggestions, but that's just doing his job. Â We had a light lunch and some appetizers and a good bottle of white wine to wash it all down. Â I had the bar steak and frites, which were perfectly done and very tasty. Â Everyone else enjoyed their meals, though the ham and gruyere sandwich was a little soggy. Â It took a little while for our food to come out, and I have a feeling it sat under the lamp for a few minutes before we got it. Â Despite that, everything was tasty and presented simply. Considering the reputation and the popularity of the place, I was surprised that the food prices were really reasonable. Â The average plate was around $23. Â For three of us to have lunch and a bottle of wine, the bill came in around $110. Something that I liked about the very close, small tables, however, was that we got to talk to one of our neighbors, found that we had some common interests, and became fast friends. Â I know that others would find that annoying or weird, but everyone had a good time. Â Additional lunch plans were made. To sum up: Balthazar's food is good, prices are reasonable, but the place is a little loud, and because they are busy there is a danger of food coming more slowly than you'd like.

OK, went to Laduree today and was extremely disappointed. Â First off a waited in an unorganized line that snaked out the door (which let flies into the store-Gross!) Â Then after my 45 minute wait (which is short next to other reviews), I chose 2 of each of the following flavors: Rose, Cafe, Vanille, Lemon and Salted Caramel. Â  The Rose, Limon and Salted Caramel where okay, nothing to write home about. The Cafe was flat tasting and the Vanille was disgusting. Â Maybe it was a bad batch of Vanille for they were soggy and sloppy. Â The macarons simply had no body to them. Â The taste and flavors are too safe. Â The consistencies of the cookies themselves off-putting. I've had macarons in Paris and these didn't measure up. Â Maybe it's the flight over from Paris that dogs out the macarons quality. Â I'll stick to Bisous Ciao in the Lower East Side. Â The flavor of their macarons are amazing, Laduree USA was all hype!

A bit of spiced up version of Chipotle. I prefer a shredded cheese instead of the slices they melt onto the burrito. I would avoid the hot sauce, it made the burrito so Â spicy that it was basically inedible. However, the rest of their ingredients are quality and they serve some great Mexican.

Ridiculously slow service. Â We sat down at 7:15 on a Thursday night. Â The place was 1/2 full. Â The bottle of wine we ordered almost immediately after sitting down wasn't brought to us until about 8. Â The whole affair took over 2 hours. Â My entree was missing a crucial element. Â Yes, they gave us a couple of free drinks in the process, but I would have much rather had a meal served in a timely fashion. Â I won't ever be back.

Let's start with the obvious: The Xiao Long Bao is tasty and worth the wait if you love dumplings. They are soup dumplings, do not burn your body with them. Luckily I had a good 30+ minutes to look at the proper way to eat them in some of the reviews on the outside wall before going in. A few more obvious things if you've read anything about Joe's: You need to go inside to get a ticket and then wait for the host to call your number. She was pretty correct about the wait time. We got lucky and got our own little table, but most everyone is seated with strangers. I'm not sure I would have felt as good about it if I hadn't gotten lucky. If you are sort of a stick in the mud , I don't think you'll be happy with this place. You have to be a little flexible to get to the delicious food. I would come back in a heartbeat though!

Hands down, still my favorite 24 hours/brunch place in Astoria. I am usually always here for the brunch menu. For less than 20 dollars you can get one entree, one hot beverage, and two alcoholic beverages. If I am catering to my sweet tooth, I will get the waffles with fresh fruits. The waffle is just right, nice and a little bit crunchy on the outside and soft on the inside. If I need something savory, I always go with any of the Benedicts or corn beef and hash. And if something healthy... the create your own omelette. The staff is pretty good and always almost the same faces. Just if I had to make one minor critique, it may be that the hostess sometimes are not so friendly. But still a great place to dine at and the atmosphere is always inviting.

Food is good - slightly on the salty side. Â The Xiao Lung Bao is very good. Â I go there just because of that. Â Otherwise, I would NOT eat over there: Because ...... First, they add 15% service charge despite their less then professional service. Â (Yes, there is a sign saying about adding the service charge - but it is printed on a regular white piece of paper with small letter font - may be a 10 pt. font? from 5ft away???) Â  Â Cash only and automatically add 15% service charge. Â And make sure you ask for the change when you pay the bill or your might not get your change back. (That happened to me twice - accidental?) Customer service and clearness is way way way below par. Â I had to exchange my utensils and my vinegar for Xiao Lung Bao because they were not up to par. Â And the fun part was that: Â I particularly had to beg them to give me a new vinegar because they insisted that they were clean. Â (And you call that a Customer service with automatically 15% tips?)

I don't get a lot of the criticisms towards this place. Â It's a bar and there will be TVs with sports on, get over it. Â Other than that, the $13.95 lobster special is a remarkable steal. Â The seafood is always fresh. Â I do enjoy their beer selection (had myself a Brooklyn Lager Pumpkin Ale which was seasonal). Â I've tried the shrimp pasta and the salmon as well and both were cooked to perfection. Â I am also not the type to enjoy big touristy crowds especially in my neighborhood. Â Fishmarket, as a local spot, definitely does without it.

used to live 5 minutes from this joint--this and tom's are my two biggest regrets about moving (okay, and maybe Sit and Wonder as well). Â  The Islands is a chill and relaxing kinda place, though it can get pretty busy on a friday night. Â The food is so great and the people working are genuine (running joke abt how they were going to fatten me up wiht oxtail before i left the neib) and you know there's some die hard local fans cuz people seem to know each other in there. Â  And might i suggest: rice & peas, and oxtail oxtail oxtail

The food was pretty good. Especially the cheese plate and the serrano ham. On a nice day, they had a couple of tables outside and they had their large window's open, so it felt like you were outside even if not.

Fantastic new restaurant in the West Village! Â My fiance and I had dinner there a couple of weeks ago and everything was wonderful. Â Great ambience, staff, and of course, food! Â Can't wait to go back!

Decent food. But I had to view the food under a microscope before I ate it; The shawarma plate was around $15 was a quarter of the portion you would get at Oasis for $10. True sadness. Never ordering here again :/

I'm still on my Â italian kick, and still nothing beats Biancas.....not even close. Now straight to the food! Appetizers: Mussels with marinara (fresh and lovely, but i thought it was suppose to be in a white wine sauce?), and the calamari (I absolutely love when they leave the body as wholes and not pre-slice.) Entree: Delicious spinach gnocci with gorgonzola sauce Â with a nice light cream sauce. The tasty chicken cutlet was thin and crispy but surprisingly Â tender. Â And the pasta from Penne All Arrabbiata seemed straight out of the box and boring. Its a pretty fresh & homey itlalian restaurant, but i rather get drunk while waiting 45 mins to be seated sardine style at Bianca because its $8 for their mussels and their way more generous with their servings and their pasta leaves me full and content. Tips: -Don't sit inside during the summer...i couldnt stop sweating and there is NO ac, but there was no other choice since it was about to rain and they closed off the outside seating. -Trust your waiter for their choice of wine, I really enjoyed the bottle of white which hit the spot for my description to him for Â "a wine just right for a summer's night." -Pasta dishes are portioned for girls and not manly men....so make sure you order a secondi!

Finally. We tried going here in the summer and the line was down the block. We definitely weren't waiting on that. Last night we happened to be in the city and were planning on going to 99 Miles to Philly but when we got there it was packed. Heading back to Queens, hubby suggest we try Grimaldis. It was late about 9:30pm so I figured it would be worth a shot . We got there at 10:15pm and yahhhh no line. Maybe because it's Halloween weekend or it was cold who knows. Trying to find a parking is stupid but we got lucky because someone from my hubby's fam was out there and happened to know the people that own the place. Hookup! We waited outside for 5 mins. The seating is definitely packed and not my preferred way to eat but I didn't even care. I was so hungry and excited to try this pizza. It came fairly quickly, maybe 15 mins. On arrival it was a beautiful looking pizza. Thin crust, done well not burnt, fresh tomatoes and mozz and a few pieces of basil. My first taste- It wasn't an explosion of flavor like I expected. But it was good. I liked the fresh flavors of the mozz, sauce and hint of basil. The crust was the right texture and just crisp enough. I must say I enjoyed it thoroughly. And yes hubby and I ate the whole pie. And he's not the type to eat more than 1 slice in a sitting. I would definitely come back on an off night when there's a chance of a small line. I don't think I would wait 2 hrs on a line for this though. Solid pizza.

Service: Each time I've gone to Brickyard the service has been great. Â Very attentive and they actually treat you like they're happy you're eating at their restaurant. Food: Â It's a pub, but for pub food it is one of the best i've had Price: Typical for NYC bar. Â e.g. $7 pints

You will most likely see a line out the door every time you come here but don't panic! The people who work here are QUICK. So you're probably thinking, it's just Belgian fries, who gives a crap? It's the multitude of delectable sauces, man. I'm in love with the Parmesan peppercorn, cheddar cheese, and almost all of the mayo options. Be careful when picking a fries size because they are all quite big! A regular size should do you just fine. Enjoy!

What happened with this place? From its past glory the only thing that remains is the high prices. Â We had a reservation for 5:30 but were not seated until about 15 minutes because the main dining room was still being set up. The evening went downhill from here. The entrees and desserts were mediocre at best -- neither the flavors nor the presentation warrant the exorbitant prices. The only redeeming quality was the bread which was great. The worst part about the dining experience was the service. Â I have been to a number of French restaurants in both France and NYC and had never encountered such poor service. Â Not only did our main waiter not know that he needs to take away the decorative plates when bread is served, but consistently kept making snarky remarks. Â Note to manager: upscale service does not equal rudeness, and one cannot claim to be upscale if your servers do not know basic tenents of service and food presentation. The same waiter was bullying other tables into ordering additional pre-dinner drinks and expressed great displeasure if none was ordered. To top it all, two additional items that we had not ordered miraculously found their way into our bill -- had I noticed them, we would have been charged $50 more for things we never ordered. A half-apology is all we got for this mistake. If you care more about your actual dining experience than about prestige or Zagat's ratings, do yourself a favor and go elsewhere. The Landmarc and the Greek in the vicinity both offer a superior experience both in terms of cuisine and service.
Love the food here!!! Came here for my birthday dinner. The seafood pasta is AMAZING!!!!! My partner loves the pistachio Â creme brule! Yummmm

I love this place! The black sesame creme brÃ»lÃ©e and the cookie it comes with are so delicious (ask them to add an extra cookie, you won't regret it). Even though I am partially lactose, I still get it! Haven't tried anything else on the menu so can't say if they are any good but from what I see when I look around the tables, they all look pretty darn tasty. Oh yeah the wait gets pretty long so come early and put your contact info down.

Food: Delicious Portions: Generous Price: Reasonable Room: It's LES...so yea, its small ...er...charming but too loud most nights to make it a good couples hideaway. Leftovers: almost assured and you'll enjoy! Oh, and they're NICE people too! Enjoy

Damn good empanadas and damn cheap shots/drinks in a hole in the wall place with a huge customer line. Perfect amount of cheesy dough-y deliciousness that come in a small package. Love it!, but maybe except the lines and waiting. But well worth it.

They give you a lot of food for the money, and the ingredients are pretty good and well put together. This isn't the best Mexican food I've ever had, and the menu is really limited (which explains why the food is cheap), but if you're in a hurry and want a good burrito to go, this is your place.
Worst meals. The soup tasted like a bowl full of ranch dressing. Three times. All bad.

This is a wonderful Austrian restaurant. I had the Viennese meatballs, roasted vegetables, with spaetzle on the side. (they seem to let you substitute potatoes and Spaetzle at will). A wonderful comfort food dish. A glass of Gruner was indicated, and it was good. Â  They had a very good apple strudel the first time I went (in cold weather) - a fat slice of buttery flaky pastry with a very fine crumb, and a nice dollop of real whipped cream on the side. In the summer, strudel was not on offer...sniff-sniff, but pastry does not hold up well in summer humidity...members of the Society for the Prevention of Cruelty to Strudel? Â  Price was mostly bumped up by wine - around $11 a glass, if I remember correctly, and if you have 2, that's a little more than most entrees. But live a little! Austrian/German is one of my favorite comfort food styles. This place offers a fine rendition of it. Mid-priced, pleasant atmosphere.

Holy DUMPLINGS, BATMAN!!! This place is awesome! The ONE thing I needed to do on my trip to NYC was to eat an authentic Chinese meal in Chinatown, and boy did this place deliver. Tucked away on a small little street, Joe's is hands down the best Chinese food I've ever eaten. Here's a look at what we ordered for 5 people: Soup dumplings: 2 orders, pork. Make sure you order these first as they can take a while sometimes. The soup inside the dumpling just explodes in your mouth when you take a bite and there's really little else in the world much better. Kung Pao Chicken: perfect. Not too fried and the right ratio of chicken to vegetables and peanuts. Beef w/Broccoli: amazing. The flavor of the beef and sauce is picked up by the broccoli and it was cooked to just the right consistency. String Beans: SOOO GOOD! Fried perfectly and still al dente. Pork Lo Mein: yummy Chicken Fried Rice: two thumbs up Spring Rolls: we ordered 5, but the waiter suggested only 3. We thought this meant they would be massive, but they were just slightly over-sized. We could have done 5, but still glad we went with only 3. I would recommend this place to anyone and everyone visiting NYC. I will just keep dreaming about Joe's until I can one day return.

If there is more stars I can give, I want to give them all to Num Pang. This was the best sandwich... ever. The baguette had just right amount of crispiness on the outside and moist on the inside. The flavors are strong but blend so well together. I had the tiger shrimp roll and asked for extra sauce ( spicy mayo). Â something I seldom do cause I'm always on a diet. But it was sooo worth it. Plus, don't forget to try the roll with some Vietnamese hot sauce on it. Yum. Dreamy. Foodgasm!!

For the past year that I've been living in Brooklyn I haven't left the borough much and I knew this would be so upon moving here, but prior to my move I used to work and live in the Soho/Tribeca area for close to 15 years. Mooncake on Watts will be missed as it was my everyday source of nutrition and every time it hit the spot on the damn nose. I remember getting their famous grilled Salmon plate over brown rice and side salad for $8.50. Add a Boylan's Seltzer water and call it a wrap for dinner. I took meetings there, dates there and my ex-girlfriend and I used to dine there often and then hit up Circa Tabac for a drink. Or my lunch would be the Crawfish and Shiitake mushroom wonton soup with noodles and a scoop of hot red pepper, THAT my friends will clear up any case of winter sniffles. I think I've eaten EVERYTHING on this menu and it was great, it was cheap and it was made with love. Shout to my guys in the kitchen and Amy (Owner) she is such a doll...the nicest woman on earth, because I practically lived in the building adjacent to the restaurant and they only accepted cash, sometimes I would forget and she would let me eat and pay later...(you got to build that kind of trust man!!) I even replicate their Avocado side dish with sesame seeds and organic soy sauce...super good. You know what...I'm going to hit Soho for a dish of Salmon now!

Honestly, I have never gone out of my way to review an establishment until I came into Confessional. Have been here for both dinner and brunch and i must say this place is worth every penny. Erika, is awesome! Great customer service, great food, great ambience, and theme. This place is definitely versatile enough whereas you could go here for any occasion, whether it's a date, meal with a group of friends or networking event. Highly recommended. For those that know what latin american food is supposed to take like, come here, guarantee that you won't be disappointed. The same goes for folks that aren't accustomed to latin american food. Theres an option here for everyone.
Cocktails are a must here, as they are certainly experts in the classic drink realm. Absolutely LOVE this place.

Um, wow. The banana flambe crepe here is the best dessert crepe I have ever eaten in my life. Totally blew my mind. The Moroccan mint tea was spot-on and took me back to Morocco. The service was friendly, polite, and heavily-accented. In a really cute way. The dinner food was quite tasty too, and fairly-priced for food of this caliber. The veggie pasta and the savoyarde crepe were highly enjoyable. This place gets the full 5 stars for the great prices in addition to very good food, plus the best dessert crepes ever.

More like 3.5 stars to be honest. Solid atmosphere and staff works exceptionally hard. Prices? High. Very high. Higher than one would expect high. Crowd? Not bad but don't plan on sitting. Sweet Afton is a hip place. Williamsburg hip, but in Astoria. Positive or negative? You decide.
Great montaditos!! My daughter loved the chocolate bread and the pepper who works there! I love " ElÃ­as TINTO DE VERANO
Wish I was drunk when I had it, maybe it would have tasted outstanding and my mind would have justified the $5/slice price tag...C'mon, folks, it is just an okay!
Wonderful thin crust pizza! Best in town!
You cant get more food for the amount of money you spend here. Prepare for a line of 10 min or so tops. No seatings. Try the sesame pancakes

I wanted to love love love based on reviews on here and it being a Coliccio restaurant. The setting is odd, in an office park in an office building. However the setting once inside is stunning as is the outside seating. The views of NYC are amazing, I just wish that the food lived up to the surroundings. The service was amazing and the plates were beautifully built, but the flavor was just lacking. We had the scallops, octopus and hamachi dishes. After one bite of each, I really didn't want anymore. I found the cheese dish we had for dessert to be the best thing I ate. For the price, there are better more centrally located places to try.
Great little noodle place with maybe 12-17 seats. Happy hour 17-00, 3$ a draft. Fantastic Udon, dont miss this place.

The first time we went was pretty good. Service was great and the novelty of it all made up for the average food. Â Then the next handful of times we went back, it started going downhill. Â We were so pissed the last time that we have made this restaurant officially dead to us. Â (Not that they'd care, of course.) We arrived starving and were told by a male server/host there would be a 5-10 minute wait. Â Great, that's fine. So we stand around the front area, waiting. Â About 15 minutes later, a couple leaves, and our spirits were buoyed. Â FOOD! Â A few minutes later, another couple arrives. Â It is important to note at this point of the story that they are Korean, and we are not. Â They are ushered in to sit. Classic!! Â The best you can ask for. Go go go !!

SO INCREDIBLE. AND AT THAT PRICE, INSANE! Takes a little focus to find the place, they're below ground, but when you find it.. man this place is a treasure. The lasagna was amazing! . Spinach gnocchi too! (though not as filling as I would like) I don't think there was any item there that I tried and did not like, everything was just on point! Go with as many friends as possible and share so you get to try everything!! Thinking of their food makes me drool every time!

It was a nice place to go to eat, the dÃ©cor of place had a very cozy feeling to it and the atmosphere was reasonably friendly and the service at the restaurant was very friendly and attentive. The woman waiting on us was very friendly and it was nice to see that she had a great personality and it definitely made staying there for dinner a pleasure. The duck confit was excellent as was pretty much everything I had, this was the first time I had duck to eat but it was actually a lot better than I was expecting. Going to this restaurant was definitely one of the best places to go in New York. It was really nice to go to and I would definitely go there again if not for the food definitely for the service. I was very impressed by the service and it's always nice to go to a restaurant where the servers are great people because that's who they are as well as just doing a good job for a good tip.

Atmosphere: great! One of my favorite places I've eaten in New York in this respect. Very haunted mansion chic, and all tastefully done. The food: The steak, mac & cheese, and chicken were very good! Everyone in our group agreed that the mashed potatoes were obviously from a box. The "mixed vegetables" was actually six rock-hard brussels sprouts on a leaf of lettuce... But when we sent it back they took it off our bill so I can't complain. The service: very friendly, but not the most attentive that we've had in NYC. About 10 minutes after our table was cleared we had to go find the waiter to ask for the check. Overall: I would definitely eat here again, but stay away from the mashed potatoes or so-called "mixed vegetables "

It's nice to see a new restaurant in a location that has been empty for years. I have eaten here twice and like it a lot. Â First, you can get a seat without a reservation. Â The service is good though a little rushed. The special asparagus and tomato salad is memorable but my favorite has to be the fried fluke fingers and whole belly clams. Â As a former New Englander nothing says "comfort" Â to me like fried clams. Â  My friend ordered the meat loaf and liked it. Â The burgers with homemade Aoili and fried onions look huge and I will try one next time. Â Nice beer list and wines too! Â Think it is going to around for a while!! Â The waiters all tell you about their reverse osmosis water system because it is free now but surely they will be charging for that little extra in the future.

I like Woorijip. They have a good variety of hot and fresh Korean food selections here all the time. And a good variety of different beers, soju, etc. Lots of seating. But the place gets crowded during dinner hours. A good place to come for a quick bite or pre-game the cheap way..no tipping necessary :)
Not too big, but delicious. Connecticut style very good. Totally a snack not a meal.

Our experience here was pretty uneven. We started off strong: I had the bone marrow & oxtail marmalade, and my boyfriend got a half dozen oysters. The oysters were perfect. They had a wonderful mouthfeel and tasted like the sea. The bone marrow was deliciously fatty and well-seasoned. The serving was a bit large, but that's not really a problem. Unfortunately, it was downhill from there. I had ordered the shrimp provencal, which is served with cheese ravioli and spinach. The cheese ravioli was pretty straightforward, and I don't mean that as a compliment: it was just a handful of floppy ravioli filled with ricotta. There were also a few small shrimp, one of which still had a bit of its shell. The dish came coated in a sauce that I would describe as thick and brown. It tasted strongly of butter and flour, which are good things, but shouldn't be standout flavors in a sauce. Sauce is supposed to be subtle but beautiful, to improve everything it touches, to ensnare the mind and bewitch the senses. This was not that. My boyfriend had the duck confit, which he liked despite the fact that the skin wasn't very crisp. His potatoes were nice, toothsome and tasting brightly of lemon. But the salad that accompanied the dish was bizarre: large pieces of lettuce with thin strips of tomato rind, completely undressed. For dessert, we decided to share the "Chocolate Bruno," which the waiter described as a cross between chocolate mousse and flourless chocolate cake. It tasted awful, and the texture was worse, like taffy or stale jello or old gum, clinging to the back of my teeth and the roof of my mouth. It came on a very hard white chocolate base, which was reminiscent of plastic. The scoops of vanilla ice cream on the side tasted like off-brand low-fat grocery store garbage. It was not just underwhelming but actively bad. The service also left something to be desired, on a number of a levels: - As we entered the restaurant, a guy in cargo pants and a checkered shirt leapt from his bar stool and asked, "How many?" I know it's not a fine dining establishment, but I was still kind of thrown by how underdressed the host was. - At the beginning of the meal, they brought out a crusty loaf of bread on a undersized wooden board with a dull small knife. We hacked at the bread for a while and got crumbs all over the table. The crumb situation was not rectified until after we had ordered dessert. - When we ordered, our waiter praised the choices we made a little too enthusiastically ("Wonderful!" "Magnificent!"), as if we were slow children who had made him a finger painting. - Several of the waiters had made rather unorthodox decisions about their grooming. A number of them looked unwashed. One looked like he had gotten tired of introducing himself to his neighbors as a registered sex offender, so he chose a mustache that could say it for him. - The check was accompanied by a solicitation spiel, something about a bike ride for multiple sclerosis. Charity is good and MS is bad, but I found it hugely inappropriate and kind of unpleasant. I'm tempted to demote them to one star on the basis of that, but the oysters were really very good.

this place is meant to be a 'chef's hangout' which i take as a good thing. they dont take reservations (unless your 6+) and i have waited here for absurd lengths of time, but the host is a great guy and there is always a great vibe at the (cramped) bar. this has to be one of the most diverse menus in town - whether you want fried chicken, paella, oysters or foie gras, its all there. this is usually a bad thing, but not here, all dishes are fab. with the dim lighting, permanent buzz and service til 3am, it is hard to top this NY favorite.

Beware of imitations, this one is the epitome of all halal carts, the mother of all street meat. The line around the block doesn't take too long, and confirms you're at the right place. Don't pass this up as some other street cart, and even though they essentially only serve one dish (in chicken/beef and spicy combinations) - it's one of the best dishes you can buy in New York City for the price.

great price for house wine, i think we got a glass pitcher for 21 dollars and split it among 4 people. gnocchi was excellent, however we ordered ziti with spicy tomato sauce and eggplant, and there was nothing special about it. i felt like i could have cooked that for myself at home. also, my friend ordered the special soup of the night (shrimp bisque) and did not like it at all. prices were really affordable. atmosphere was alright, nothing special. staff was very attentive. If i were to go again it Â would be for the house wine and gnocchi only.

$2.50 for Falafel, you really can't go wrong at that price. Â I've been to both this location and the EVil location. Â This is one of the places I've frequented more intoxicated but have also had sober. Â The hot sauce is my favorite but if your not used to it go easy with it. Â Sometimes if I'm really fat I will get a falafel here and an aloo unda at Kati Roll or a fries at Pommes Frites and eat both. Â That's the way us fat kids roll.

Here's what we had: 1. Â Crispy oysters with seaweed salad. Â Delicious. Â I'm a sucker for oysters in all forms, though. Â They were perhaps a tiny bit overcooked, but still really, really nice. Â The itsy-bitsy seaweed salad was good, too. This was the most memorable and unique dish of the evening. 2. Â Seared sea scallops. Â Again, I'm a sucker for scallops and these were very sweet and had a nice texture. Â Two beefs with the dish - it was $23 for 4 scallops. Â And two out of the four were quite small. Â I would expect for that price that they would all Â be sizable sea scallops. Â The size difference also contributed to the done-ness being inconsistent. Â The two that were (too) small were sear and cooked perfectly. Â The two that were big a plump were undercooked. Also, the rest of this dish was equally tiny. Â Tiny plate, miniature vegetables scattered around. Â In fact, the more I write about the dish, the more annoyed I'm getting. It should be an appetizer and sell of about $15. 3. Â Burger. Â No complaints. Â Great fries, too. 4. Lemon Blueberry Cheesecake. Â I wanted to lick my plate. Â Second favorite dish of the night. The service was good, too. Â I don't think I'll go out of my way to eat here again, since there's a bridge between it and me, Â but it was a pleasant experience, none the less. Â I can see why it's a hood favorite.

I ordered their burger and was offered the choice of fried bun or a regular bun. "A friend bun is our thing." I ordered the fried bun and didnt expect anhting more than a slightly toasted bun. What I got instead caused my heart to stop. The burger was stuffed inside a zeppoli. I dream about this burger. Bring a couple of friends and share it. Make sure one of your friends is a cardiologist.

I've come here with my girlfriend a few times over the last month or two, and had a blast each time. Â The bartenders are cool and the food (fresh oysters) is great. Â The front opens up when the weather's nice, making it a great day drinking spot. Â Dinner next.

I was introduced to Piccolo Angolo a few weeks ago by some of the regulars and because I like meatballs, I was urged b my friends to order some. Not only were they delicious, they were the size of bowling balls! Â  Just a impressive was the garlic bread that actually has fresh garlic in it and the wait staff whose personality and efficiency were very impressive. Also I learned that during the week you can have your leftover meatballs made into a sandwich to go. Â One of our party had that made for him but my meatballs were long gone by the end of the meal! Â  This is a restaurant I can not wait to visit again and after tasting a few more dishes will probably revise my rating to 5 stars!

Amazing food here!!!! I was here for my friend's birthday last night! Lol The bacon popcorn was delicious !!! That hint of bacon taste ... Emmm omg I want that again ! Then we had crack and cheese which was AMAZING!!! Get this!!! Lol Then the taco!!! Oh wow awsome combination!! My steak was great too!!!! O want that yummy meat again right now! Lol

I've gone to this place about 4 times now and the service keeps me going back. Excellent recommendations from the bartender with an extensive knowledge of all of the whines. Food is excellent. Steak tartar is a must! Most deff a great place to go for a relaxing glass of wine.
Great ambiance and Ginger martini's. Food is very good, but not memorable. Over $100 for two people with drinks. Â Good for the french bistro NYC decor, but not a special occasion restaurant.
Japanese food and curry. What isn't there to like here? Was the review too short?
Meh. Eggs Benedict were just OK and the grits sucked. I think they were instant. The gratuity pastries were really good. Â Overpriced.

If you want a fun and authentic experience of japanese yakitori and sake bar, this is the place to be. Â With light, small plates of japanese dishes like skewered yakitori meats, sushi and sashimi, or fresh uni means you'll never be bored as you sip and sample different foods and sake. Â If you're looking for something heartier, try their pork belly and kimchi or spicy cod roe on spaghetti and an ice cold glass of beer. Â  I've been here several times but during my latest visit, a friend and I ended up sitting at the bar and ordered one dish after another -- the bartender/waiter was more than attentive considering the amount of patrons and activity going on and even offered his recommendations for sake. Â We ordered the wasabi octopus, tuna sashimi, fresh uni, yellow tail collar, beef skewers, fried oysters, pork belly and kimchi, spicy cod roe with spaghetti, two glasses of sake, two Kirins, finished off with two bowls of sesame ice cream. Yes, that was for the 2 of us... Don't come hungry or during the dinner rush; you'll find yourself waiting at least an hour or more. Â If possible, come by earlier to avoid the crowds. This place offers more than the usual Japenese cuisine so if you're not accustomed to Japanese foods other than sushi, be prepared to be a little adventurous. Â Casual dining setting and a great place to grab dinner and drinks with friends, prices are reasonable for the location when compared to similar yakitori joints you'd find in St. Marks.

First time trying this place didn't feel welcomed and the guy messed up my order. As I was patiently waiting, I've noticed names were being asked after the customers order. (like how starbucks asks for your name) For me, nothing was asked, just a quick and go order, didnt even get a reciept. even though my order messed up. I was hoping the prosciutto pressed sandwich was worth the wait...definitely not! Thinly cut...not true, it was thick and tasted like ham to me. Wasn't happy at all. I'm not going back here and next time the people who work there should be more welcoming. Service is everything if you want customers even new ones.

This is when quantity beats quality. I've passed this place a million times. It always has a HUGE line. Currently, it has a "grade pending" post on the window. Â A year ago, I swear I saw a C grade up in that beetch. Â Today, I was in a "why the Fuck not mood". Â Tomorrow, I may pay for it in the bathroom. Â Just kidding. Â I hope. The line usually goes out the door and probably 12 plus feet into the sidewalk at peak lunch hours. Â Today, when I was about to walk past it again, there were only four people on the sidewalk. Â I hadn't eaten yet. Â Obviously, Jesus was trying to tell me something. Btw, it's take out only, but lucky for us, there's the ghetto ass park across the street. Â Score. Â  The key to getting through the process of ordering is NOT to look at the conditions inside. Â Leave the judging up to Jesus. Â Just put yourself in that roast pork happy place and know that for less than 4$, you're about to get more meat then you can handle (that's what she said). Â  Is it the best? No. Â But they give you more meat then rice and some bok choy underneath said meat mound. Â There's some good flavor. Â Not great, but good...enough. Â Did I mention it was under 4$? Â If you aren't a fat kid eater like me, you can actually share this portion. Â I don't share. All in all, sometimes, slumming it is ok. Â Just never tell your friends you went here. Â Yelp is a different story. Â Speaking of, if this place keeps getting written up by douche bags like me, it's not that far away from having white boys with beards wearing jeggings in line between the Chinese people who frequent this joint (see Prosperity Dumplings). Â Oh, well. Â Enjoy it while it lasts.

Really nice place. One of our faves in the neighborhood. The long waits at the weekend are a testament to how good it is. The cappuccinos are delicious and so are the croque monsieurs. Service is always quick and efficient.

It really is as good as it gets at Mamoun's! Â Nostalgia brings me to Mamoun's as I used to live on Mamoun's offerings in New Haven. Â The smell of perfectly charred lamb in the air --- brings you to meat heaven! You can get a pretty decent meal at Mamoun's for less than $5 if you are vegetarian and a little more if you are not. Their pita sandwiches are stuffed with lettuce, tomatoes, parsley and onions, with sesame sauce. All of their vegetarian sandwiches are priced at $2.50 -you get a choice of falafel (fried seasoned chick pea mixture), hummus (chick pea dip), Â or baba ghannouj (heavy creamy dip of eggplant and sesame sauce - one of my faves). Â They also have stuffed grape leaves, makdoos (eggplant), and tabbouleh (salad of cracked wheat, parsley, lettuce, tomatoes, onions & lemon juice). Â For the meat sandwiches ($5) - hmmmm meat - you get the same basic stuffing as the vegetarian with your choice of shish kebab (lightly seasoned cubes of grilled lamb), kefta kebab (grilled ground spiced lamb) or donor kebab. Â You can get the chicken version for all the above as well. Â But I like the intense sweet type of charred lamb - so I always go for the lamb. They do all of the above in "platter" form - ie. it is a deconstructed sandwich and they charge you about double the price for a little more meat. Â  They have a crazy hot sauce - IT IS HOT - that you can have with your sandwiches / platters. Â Just remember to be respectful. Â You have been warned. And dont forget the freshly fried falafel balls! Â Gosh - it is a bargain at $1 for 3. Â I could easily eat a dozen. Â  They do some soup and dessert stuff but I have never been able to get pass the pita sandwiches and the falafels! This location is really a hole in the wall. Â There are 2 booth tables for like 4 people (you could probably try to squeeze in 2 persons on each bench but you will have to be really skinny!) so it is more a take-out place. Â They do have another 2 benches outside the store - not much help if you are a big group. Well worth a try if you havent already discovered Mamoun's. Â They throw in the middle eastern music for free! Â They are opened from 11am to 5 am everyday so you can always pop in for a late night snack - just watch out for the NYU students coming out from their all night parties - er study groups.......

The yakitori bar is one of my all time favorite things to do and Yakitori Totto did not disappoint. Â  The food was fantastic. Â The chicken hearts and beef tongue were out of this world. Â The traditional chicken was great especially when combined with the shishitou peppers. Â My daughters favorite was the bacon wrapped asparagus and my wife enjoyed being able to order Calpico-Hi (something you cant always find outside of Japan unless you make it yourself). Â  We gorged ourselves for over an hour and left very satisfied. They only take reservations for a certain portion of the restaurant leaving part of it for walk ins. Â So when we called at 4:30 on a Wed they were already booked up for reservations in the time we wanted to be there (6:00 because we were catching an 8:00 show). Â We made a point to be there right at 5:30 and were seated almost immediately. Â  It's a little smallish and there is no real waiting area if theres a crowd to get in so the top of the stairs can be kinda tight. Â By the time we left the place was packed and had to navigate the stairs through a crowd.

The people making tacos are so friendly. You know these tacos are good whenever there are Asian people choosing tacos with salsa over the Asian place in front of the restaurant, which I thought was pretty funny. BUT, they do have a killer salsa. Yum

Such tasty paninis! Â Perfectly pressed bread and amazing fillings, like smoked ham, BBQ chips and truffle aioli, or porchetta, blue cheese, and arugula. Â We will definitely come here again. Â Oh and if you order white wine, they'll keep the bottle in the fridge to keep it cool. Â And we never had to ask for them to refill our glasses. Â Great service.

Great place. Good food. Love their coffee. Nice outdoor seating along Columbus with retractable awning. Prices are not too bad. Service is good. There is usually a long line - get there early for brunch.

Fast, cheap ($6 or 7), delicious. Could you really want more? I got the chicken and rice classic with white sauce. They drown it in sauce, so watch how much you want. Ask for the hot sauce on the side since it is really very hot. One order is enough to share between two people. Line may look intimidating but they're super efficient.

Photos don't do this place justice. Chicken, lamb gyro, and rice? That sounds like something you could get at any Mediterranean restaurant. What really brings this place together are the sauces. I've yet to come across a white sauce as delicious and creamy as 53rd & 6th's. It's creamy, yogurt-like, but without any of the tartness (and the gross cucumbers bits) that many other places have. I swear that it must be spiked with mayo. Add in a dash of spicy sauce (careful: it's super hot) and you've got something that reminds me of a good spicy tuna roll sauce. There's really nothing like this on the West Coast.

Love this place. Cozy & friendly atmosphere. Great place for happy hour. Drinks are worth every penny and food is delicious. Nachos de chorizo & cochinita tacos are a must here! Mango margaritas are my fav here. Orlando (bartender) is always very attentive & makes awesome micheladas. I'm here at least once a week & never get bored!

My wife did a restaurant search on her computer and found a few she asked if I knew, then asked where this one was, I said sure close lets go there. Â This was one of the best choices I have ever made. Â I have been in over 130 countries, over 1000 towns and cities, and eaten at many Michelin 5 Star restaurants, Trattoria L'incontro holds its own and then some against them all. Â We arrived with no reservation, but were immediately seated near the Pizza Oven. Â Now I have read some of the reviews, noisy and loud, well guess what I did not see people on cell phones, they were talking to each other, laughing and having a good time, that works for me. Â I liked the look of the room, very open and large, decor worked for me also, I liked it immensely. Â I could not ask for more attentive and knowledgeable waiters and staff, you never had your glass empty for more than a minute. Â I read one review where the first thing is too expensive, guess they have never really been to an expensive restaurant, over $400 for either a lunch or dinner for two. Well enough about that, lets get to the reason you go to restaurants, the food. Â I don't know how the waiter remembered all the specials, but when he started my mouth watered. Â I immediately took the soup special, for the life of me I can not remember the name, but it was absolutely wonderful with little meatballs. Â My wife is not a soup eater so she only tasted it but liked the taste. Â Another great thing about this restaurant is that you can share. Â We shared the Tuna Carppacio salad, and the Lobster salad. Â Our next course was pasta, we decided on the Fettuccini with Arugula and Prosciutto. Â How do you describe perfection, the taste was amazing, salty but not overly so, just a gorgeous dish that has my mouth watering just writing about it. Â Now we had the Cod, the sauce for this dish and the Cod itself melted in your mouth, now I am not a potato eater but I was using the potato to lap up the sauce. Â What an amazing meal. Now to the desert, I had the Fig Gelato and also Zambaglione. Â I like the Gelato, it was delicious, but the Zambaglione was amazing and I recommend this to everyone. Â I also had a Cappuccino and my wife an Expresso, I don't know how you make Cappuccino better, but they did. This will not be the only time I go to this restaurant, they will see me often since it is less than half an hours drive from my home. Â Now I had expected to pay well over $200 hundred for our dinner including the wine. Â Well I was pleasantly surprised that we did not even come close to that figure, so expensive not in my estimation. Oh and the dress code, to me is casual, I was dressed in overalls. My thanks to everyone for a truly wonderful gastronomic experience.

Fresh food, good food...Very pleasant staff, just do patrons a favor and put specials on a menu, it's a huge recital, by the time waiter is done you have forgotten what he mentioned first, if you even understood what he recited at machine gun speed, in an accent...Worth the try if you happen to be in Astoria, with that being said not sure how the location and ambiance can reflect or excuse their prices.

I've been to ABC several times, it's a great space and good location, but the overall experience definitely does not deserve a 4 or 5 star rating. The $15 personal pan pizza id very mediocre and highly over priced. The "dusted" calamari is fried , this needs to be clearly stated in the menu, i don't know when this became a euphemism for fried but its not explained properly on the menu. Also the selection of dishes is quite limited and not that interesting. Service is just OK, as was mentioned earlier nothing close to "fine dining" standards. Not one of the top spots in the neighborhood. Good place for a drink and snacks, sure.

Delicious! I grew up in Queens and Pio Pio is famous for their rotisserie chicken with secret green sauce. Their empire grows! This branch is enormous. The deco is cool. The music is fun. Service great. We ordered, and I skipped to the lou...when I got back our meal was there already! Incredibly fast! We were in and out in under an hour. The bill came to $56 with a shared combo plate and two drinks. The fries are incredible...what do they fry those in? Thick steak fries with a nice flavor. The avocado salad goes wonderfully with the juicy, flavorful chicken...the perfect match. The sangria was tasty (not too sweet, which I hate). I highly recommend.

my favorite neighborhood restaurant for 10 years running. Â just make sure you arrive at a slightly off time, otherwise the wait can be insanely long. Â  i've never had a bad time here or a bad meal. Â my kids are addicted to the gnocchi. Â their cookbook is great, too. i cook from it all the time.
The corn is a MUST!!! The entrees are ok- I recommend getting the corn- to die for.

This is the most conveniently located restaurant in New York. The food was above average for an Italian restaurant at its price range. The atmosphere had a nice neighborhood feel to it, and the waiters were very attentive. Perhaps a little too attentive.

The Chop Shop beef and broccoli dish was incredible -- tender and well spiced. It's the only Thai place walking distance that I have found that I actually enjoy. The garden in the back is certainly a nice touch (at least when it isn't raining!).

This place has great decor and the food is solid for a thai place that has plenty of competition in the area. The vibe is slightly more upscale and decent spot for a low maintenance date. The service is good but can be a bit slow bc its gets so busy and the narrow layout hinders people moving around, but I will hit this place again on occasion.

I would have liked to have liked BrisketTown a lot more than I did, so this is a difficult review to write. On one hand, the small touches such as the wedge salad (with roasted almonds, and pickled red onion) and the home made pickles that came with the meat were excellent, but on the other hand, BBQ should have starred. The pulled pork was ordinary at best, and both the ribs and the brisket seemed hurried. Perhaps the Texas-inspired rub was lacking in complexity and depth (as if the smoking times were somewhat shorter than ideal or perhaps the rub wasn't applied with enough vim and vigor or not given time to develop any sort of crust). Or perhaps it was just smoking times... the brisket was definitely a whole lot fattier than I am used to. Maybe I just wandered in on an off day. It was definitely good, great even, but it did not hit the high notes that I had wanted. The beer menu was a little limited to the microbrew set. As nice as it might be to feature a good variety of beers, it's pretty clear that not every beer pairs well with BBQ. The wait staff was excellent, attentive and welcoming. Some of the nicest service in Williamsburg. Finally, I agree with at least one of the other reviews. The collard recipe has to change. It doesn't work.

When my bf & I walked in it was like the coldest welcome ever. Â The guy that "welcomed" us happened to be our waiter & he really made my birthday dinner pretty dismal. Â He was slow as hell, kept texting on his phone, & never smiled once until we were walking out the door. Â I had to keep flagging him down & asking him for water, even though the place wasn't crowded. Â There was another waiter Â there that seemed to be really good. Â I think he noticed my facial expression & brought us over a free glass of wine. Â I already saw the Yelp check-in offer, but I had a Groupon & never requested wine. Â Besides, I was still pretty hungover from the night before. Â The wine was pretty horrible. Anyway, the octopus salad was pretty good. The calamari was decent. We also ordered a cold mixed platter but we sent it back. Â We didn't like it or understand it. Â The grilled whole Branzino was delicious and came with a side salad which was nice. Overall, the food was good. Â I can't say that it was good enough for me to overlook the service we received to go back. My bf really enjoyed the fish so if anything we may go back for that. Â Otherwise, I see no real reason. Â There are plenty of restaurants that can make a piece of fish, without making you feel like an invisible customer.

The food was great! Their pizza is definitely a must try for staten islanders. I gave it 4 stars because they seemed not to be too organized when it comes to table seating. However once my friends and I sat, the waiter service and food was perfect!

The sawdust is a cute touch...till it makes you fall on your bum bum in front of everyone at the bar! Â AND I WAS SOBER! Good times, good times! This place has got character. Thats what makes or breaks a place for me, ya know. Since i dont drink and I go to bars I tend to take in the atmosphere more than your average person. Everyone was jolly, the place was clean, the food was good. Its a pub so they have standard pub grub. They do it well. It can get a bit crowded....waited a while for a table for 6...for a 2 or 3 party it shouldnt be too bad.

Put some kimchi in a container. Realized while standing in line that they had prepackaged kimchi that was better value. Clinton Street Baking Company and Restaurant has been voted "Best Pancakes" by New York Magazine two times! But lets not get it twisted, this place is much more than just a pancake joint. In 2001, husband and wife team Neil Kleinberg and DeDe Lahman, began a journey to be known as having the best baked goods in the city that were hand-mixed in small batches. Today they have most definitely achieved their goal and the success tastes so, so sweet. So sweet in fact, their customer are willing to wait for the goods. The normal wait time for brunch on a Saturday morning is a few hours...and people do it with no hesitation. When you walk into the tiny restaurant, you see the kitchen and everyone that works in it, all the patrons enjoying their food, the freshly bakes goods in the small case and the employees who look really thrilled to be at work. The case in the front contains all kinds of yummy goodness such as: muffins, cakes, pies, scones, cornbread, etc. The Brunch, lunch and dinner menu consists of many mouthwatering options like Pancakes with Warm Maple Butter, Clinton Street Omelette and the Fried Chicken Sandwich. For a first-timer like myself deciding what to order was a really tough decision. Luckily, my friend Angela was along for the journey and we shared the Fried Chicken Sandwich and Brioche French Toast. So let me guess...this all sounds fantastic but you don't have time for a 2 hour wait for brunch? No problem Clinton Street Bakery delivers. They also have takeout and a fabulous way to pre-order cakes and pies for your next event.

Three stars for Dom DiMarco, the extraordinarily fresh ingredients, and the history of the place.
