Darn yelp! I think you over-sold it! I came here expecting pure awesomeness and it really was just... sorta cool. So don't come in here with huge expectations. Every-so-often, a restaurant comes onto the scene where it is universally adored by the creme-a-la-creme of Yelp -- aka, my friends. Â Enter Traif. Â This is a restaurant named after the derivative of the Hebrew word "teref" which means torn and is now commonly used to refer to anything non-kosher. Â How could I NOT love this food? Â  I arrived shortly after opening because my primary goal was to snag the two seats right in front of the chef. Â In most cases, if I could, I love to watch the chef prepare food. The detail, the meticulous work, and, let's be honest, the smells from an open kitchen is one of the guiltiest pleasures when it comes to eating. I started the meal with one of their specialty cocktails, if I remember correctly, "Rude Little Pig" (Lapsong-infused tequila, cointreau, pomegranate bacon rim) which was strong but the idea of a bacon rim always win. For entrees (that was shared), we started with a refreshing fig, goat cheese, walnut spring salad (to open the palate) followed promptly with the "Thai Spicy-Sweet Chili-Glazed Calamari". Amazing! Get it! Â The calamari was tender and wonderfully glazed. Next came the "SautÃ©ed Sweetbreads, artichokes, asparagus, roast mushrooms". This dish was almost solely for me because I love offal and I rarely (and there is proof!) turn down sweetbreads. Â It was delicious and balanced well with the vegetables. Fourth dish was the "Seared Scallops, Creamed Corn, Sage-Pistachio Brown Butter" which, once again, I need to say GET IT! Â This dish was perfect. Â The warm scallops lovingly seared and then laid gently upon a soft, cozy bed of creamed corn then drizzled with the sage-pistachio brown butter. HOW! HOW! HOW can I not have dreams about this for days to come?!? And then...the "Strawberry-Cinnamon Glazed Baby Back Ribs" Yes. Â I'm talking about fall-off-the-bone succulent baby-back ribs that was so flavorful, I had to hold down my friend and shove a strawberry-cinnamon explosion into his mouth. Â Was it worth it? You bet! Of course, there is always room for dessert and the hot "Strawberry cobbler with passion fruit cream" was the great end to the meal where spoons fought in a white ramekin showdown shoving hot fresh strawberries cradled in passion fruit foam into hungry mouths. Â Thankfully, the staff at Traif noticed the burn marks because with the check came pieces of "golden pineapple drizzled with pomegranate molasses and mint". By the way, did I mention how great the staff is? The chef conversed intermittent with us as did everyone behind the bar. Â  Friendly, attentive, fantastic! Next time, I want to try: ~ Bacon-wrapped blue cheese-stuffed dates, spinach a la catalane ~ Duck confit lettuce wraps, banana-tamarind prik ~ Stuffed corn cake, marinated rock shrimp, champagne mango ~ Braised Berkshire pork cheeks a l'ancienne, polenta, prune jus ~ Bacon doughnuts, dulche de leche, coffee ice cream Do I recommend Traif? You make the call. Â Seriously, give me a call. Â I'll be there.

YOU want to go to Williamsburg for dinner? YOU? I can't believe it! "Look, making fun of hipsters is so 2007. Been there, done that. I'm at peace now" This conversation gave me pause for thought while debating my rating. On the one hand, I was advocating moving beyond appearances, yet on the other I couldn't escape the suspicion that I was getting carried away by the ambiance at Tabare. My first visit had been spurred by the glowing reviews of Laura A, sarah w, and peter d. Now I may discount peter d's reviews (*) as his profile headline screams escape from responsibility ("when you're young, there are no mistakes. only research"), but I take 5 star reviews from Laura and sarah seriously. So, I will echo Laura's description of Tabare: "Rustic style but sophisticated and yes, trendy too. It's charming. The lighting is beautiful. You will feel comfortable, it's cozy; it's sexy. You can fall in love." Ok, that's where I draw the line. No amount of mood lighting, or sexy atmosphere can send me running to read Shakespeare, or Keats. It's what's on the inside that counts, so let's talk about the food. Now, that's where the relationship gets complicated. The extent to which Uruguayan cuisine is influenced by Italian, Spanish, and Portugese cuisines is surprising to one not too familiar with it. I debated for a while on what to order, looking for something different - but ultimately going with the empanadas (caramelized onions, gruyere & fontina cheese; and chicken, onions and peppers) and the handmade Ravioli of the day (goat cheese, ricotta, sun dried tomato, butter sage sauce). I got a taste of the things to come with the warm bread basket that was accompanied with homemade Tapenade and orange zest. Simple, but well executed: that was the theme of the entire meal. The empanadas were so different (thicker, but not heavier) in texture from any I've had in New York, that the next morning I engaged my Puerto Rican colleague in a long debate on this. The olive oil based dipping sauces served as the perfect accompaniment, till the taste buds were wowed by the Ravioli - which must also rank as one of the best I've had, and Italian is one of my favorite cuisines. I was also surprised by the Alfajor, as the ones I've had in the restaurants and bakeries in Jackson Heights are fairly consistent in their interpretation with each of the dulce de leche filled cookies being ~ 1/6th of an inch thick. The version at Tabare had cracker thin crisp cookies, with dulce de leche & chocolate ganache, and sea salt caramelized walnuts. It was different, and I liked it - but I appreciated the dule de leche flan more as it had a mousse like texture. I was fascinated with the way the flan wraps around the fork as you slice it down, alternating the grace of a ballerina with the sensuality of a stripper working the pole. This reverie was interrupted by ecstatic sounds from the table next to me upon being offered complimentary flan (the owner's grandmother's recipe). That HAS to be my pet peeve with Tabare: three visits - and not a single complimentary appetizer or dessert, when almost every table (with female patrons) has been rewarded. I would protest at the discrimination (*), if it weren't for the work ethic, dedication, attentiveness of the owners as they bring you water, serve you food, make recommendations, clean the table - one can only wish them well, and hope that they succeed in their "hamlet away from the village" (Tabare). Ultimately, when all elements: food, service, atmosphere, and value (~$35 per head) come together, how can one hold back one's affection? Sometimes, attraction is as much a result of how similar something is to what one knows, as it is about how different it is - especially if thoughtfulness ensures perfect execution on the details. ======== (*) I kid

It's because of The Levee that I know what broken cheeseballs in my ass feel like. Â They're sharp, like shards of fiberglass, and will damn near cut you. Â You kind of have to duck walk home. Â That said, this is best dive bar in Williamsburg. The Texas-Two Step special is legendary -- A Lone Star and a shot of surprisingly good tequila for $5 bucks. Â If tequila isn't your thing you can sub bourbon on the special, just ask for A Two-Step with Evan. There's a nice array of real-deal bar food -- hot dogs, sloppy joes, nachos. Â Even better, you can stuff your face with free poofy cheeseballs and Twizzlers. Â There's a rad jukebox that always seems to find the right mood, a lively pool table, Buck Hunter, darts, and some mostly complete board games. Â If you're inventive, cheeseballs can subsitute for lost board game pieces -- Connect 4 gets pretty messy -- and bring new life to old games -- like Jenga baseball. The bathrooms are really the only ding. Â They're in the front right by the bar, and when it's busy, the snaking lines of people waiting really cramp the main bar area. Â And it will be busy -- the weekends fill this place up. There's not much else to fault. Â The staff is cool, the cheeseballs are free, the drinks are cheap, and the (God bless) Texas Two-Step is one of the best deals in the city.

We had some friends come to town for a conference that they were attending near Union Square, and the Edible Institute had suggested Almond as a restaurant that conference attendees should check out. We made the mistake of taking the Edible Institute's recommendation, instead of doing our own research. This place is mediocre and overpriced (appetizers are ~$10-$20; entrees are ~$25-$40). As a foursome, we ordered: - The wedge salad - The thick-cut bacon appetizer - The marinated octopus - The duck entree - The pork milanese - A side of brussel sprouts - The chocolate pot de creme for dessert Taking them one at a time: the wedge salad was just some iceberg lettuce with a too-thick cream sauce. I still can't believe that thick-cut bacon could be so tasteless and bland. The marinated octopus was by far the best dish that we ordered. The duck entree was totally mediocre--neither well-cooked nor particularly well-flavored. The brussel sprouts were roasted with bacon and (I think) honey, so it would have been hard to mess them up too badly. The chocolate in the dessert was pretty good, but the cream on top was disgusting. Do yourself a favor and DON'T go here. I live in Park Slope and, at the risk of sounding like a self-righteous Brooklynite, this is the kind of pretentiously-fancy, ridiculously-overpriced crap that makes it hard to venture to Manhattan for a sit-down dinner. I can't believe that places like this stay in business, when there are so many hundreds of places all over the city--at any price point!--that are so clearly better.

I really wanted to like this place. It's world famous and is the only location (well of two in NY) in the US. Service is top notch here. They were really on top of things and were really nice. That was definitely a plus. They even folded my boyfriends napkin back onto his plate after he went to the bathroom, which i thought was a bit strange, but kinda nice. Food: After asking for suggestions from my waiter, we got the famous pork buns, I got the akamaru modern ramen and my boyfriend the vegetarian (gluten free) ramen. (he doesn't like pork) The pork buns were pretty spot on. It was the best thing I ate that night. I would highly recommend them. The ramen on the other hand, was good, but I was expecting this amazing broth. The broth didn't especially stand out to me. It was good, but not the hype people were giving it. My boyfriend's dish was terrible and it cost us 18$. For a vegetarian dish that had special sauce in it and very little food. Skip the vegetarian dish! I think if I ever give this place another try, I may have to try another type of ramen, maybe the spicy one. Overall, good and decently enjoyable, but not worth the hype nor the wait. Pork buns amazing, ramen good but skip the vegetarian ramen.

Total score! This place is sweet from start to finish. Great, clean decor, smart menu, tasty beers, fresh oysters and lobster roll (that's what we had), and very friendly service. Maybe you'll get lucky and Matt will be your server! Enjoy. It's a nice break from the hustle and bustle of NYC streets.

Pretty much kenka's in mid town. Great happy hour drink specials if you can beat the crowd before 7 PM! 3$ hot sake bottles, 4$ wine, 3$ beers. I've had the omu soba - a little too sweet for my taste, but interesting Mackerel - pretty good Tako wasa - I just love the chewy octopus and wasabe combo. I could eat this every day marinated hamachi - forgot the name of it officially, but always a winner. Hamachi + ponzu + mild red onions Kara age - yum per usual Oden - recommended if it's cold out, delicious! Great pairing with raw fish dishes Grilled squid - very nice and chewy, not super flavorful but fun texture There are so many other things I want to try - it is a bit pricy (4$ for kimchi??) but it's a great alternative to going all the way down to kenkas. It does get quite loud so be prepared to shout, which is fine as long as I have enough hot sake to keep me going. Yum.

Crowded, loud, and overpriced. i am a big fan of italian food, be it pizza, pasta, osso bucco, or anything else. This was a poor rendition, especially considering the huge number of more palatable and enjoyable places nearby. The service: Very good. The waitress was attentive and our food came out quickly. This was by far the best part of the experience. The place was crowded and loud, and clearly played host to people who were unimaginative and unadventurous and couldn't think of anywhere better to eat. They lose points because they couldn't split the check onto separate cards. Â I understand that it is a luxury, but it's a pretty common thing to do for young professionals. They gave us attitude about it too. The food: Oversalted, underflavored. I got the pizza which was standard and not worth the money. There are a dozen better artisanal pizza joints in NYC, including otto's nearby. My friend got one permutation of the risotto, and he said it was over-salted and soupy. I generally trust his taste since he studied cooking at cordon bleu in paris. all in all, there are so many better options that offer a more comfortable and satisfying experience. I would give three stars because the service was great, and that counts a lot, but the food matters more to me and that brings it down to two. B-

La SirÃ¨ne and its family are a rare find in this city. A place where you will be taken care of, treated as family and have a wonderful dining experience. What I really enjoy about La SirÃ¨ne is the responsiveness of the Chef/Owner, Didier Pawlicki, to his customers. As a preliminary matter, the food is delicious. The ingredients are incredibly fresh, and Didier's recipes are clearly crafted with intuition, care and great taste. But what makes the experience is Didier's passion and his care for his guests. And his staff adopt the same approach to taking care of their customers. Upon entering, you feel like you're in a friend's dining room, over for a dinner party. Didier and the staff takes your mood and your tastes into account when he makes his recommendations from the evening's menu, and your trust of their judgment is rewarded by a meal which will leave you speechless.
Awesome food!! The food was fresh and the place was very clean!

Ok. Let's be honest. The best thing about this place is the drinks. They are pretty cheap comparatively. Of course, I get the same thing every time - a Grey Goose Martini and then a Half-and-Half because that's what I like. The martini is only $10! And it's always made well. The bartenders are all cool guys - very friendly. I am fond of them. And the music is always good. It creates a nice soothing atmosphere - especially when I am feeling lonely in my ugly neighborhood. The food is hit or miss from what I've heard from others. I really really like the Eggplant Rollatini (but it's not always available), the Pizze Margherita, Braised Short Rib entree with polenta, and the Top Sirloin entree - although I didn't like the cooked radicchio, but the rosemary sauce was quite tasty; and in my opinion, it could have used some polenta on the side. But what couldn't use polenta on the side? I LOVE polenta :] Also, my friend really liked the Bucatini alla Carbonara. And one time she had a fish special she really enjoyed. I never ever eat pasta when I go out so I wouldn't know what it was like and I thought her breaded fish was overpriced and it had so many bones she almost choked on, but hey, I am a good cook so it takes a lot to impress me. Overall, I love this place because it's really pretty inside coming from the really ugly-ness that is outside on 3rd Ave - I mean, have you seen the hookers? Cause I have! They love to stroll around my street. One time I was leaving for work at 8:30am and a prostitute was passed out on the sidewalk outside of my house! haha. OMG. I gotta get out of here! But Bar Tano is lovely. It reminds me of Europe with it's beautiful lighting and tin ornate ceiling, and it makes me feel all warm and fuzzy inside. And apparently there is jazz on Thursday nights which I will have to check out and report back on...

I've always been impressed with how versatile Alta is for dates and big groups...its unassuming entrance among the expensive brownstones in the west village and its dimly lit interior makes you think romance. Â Then you see all of the big tables, hear the incredible sound of conversation of the main dining room, and read about the Whole Shebang on the menu, and it makes you think about huge birthday parties for groups of 12. If I had my choice, I'd prefer Alta for a big-group dinner over a date especially if you can get a table in the more private upstairs room (you have to go through the kitchen to get there...think the scene from goodfellas)...Alta's menu is so expansive that you want to eat with more people so that you can try all delectable-sounding tapas listed. I say "delectable-sounding" b/c not all of the tapas taste as good as advertised. Â On my most recent visit, I was kinda disappointed at how many misses there were compared to the hits. The good dishes were the simplest: -Crispy brussels sprouts were fried and roasted to perfection...addictive like potato chips -bacon wrapped dates and olives--honestly, the only way this dish was not going to taste superb was if the bacon was soft and mealy...thankfully, the bacon was crispy yet tender and the rest is history. -Lamb meatballs were more flavorful than your usual albondigas and had a middle eastern kick to them Meanwhile, others fell really flat. The awesome-sounding uni risotto may have been the worst dish...small dollops of uni could not save the bland risotto (maybe it was our mistake for ordering this at a tapas restaurant). Also, while the grilled octopus was solid, I was really surprised by how small the portion was--I know this is tapas but 4 tiny pieces of octopus leg for $10 was unjust. Â Finally, our churros looked fried and delicious but were dry and the dipping sauces could not save them. What is amazing though is I've named just one-tenth of the dishes on Alta's menu...it is very well possible that the other nine-tenths consists of some of the most ethereal foods you will ever eat. The solution: come with a big group and try the whole shebang.

Lovely soups that aren't your typical tomato/basil ones, and their Moroccan mint tea is wonderful. It's very "sweet" inside, feels like perhaps it was decorated by an Anthropologie person who had a lot of old farm old style items around. Small tea tables mostly.

Love this place! Food is good but you have to wait for a long time if its crowded and it's hard to heard your name called. Drinks were weak the last time I went, but had been strong previous time. This is an excellent place to go if you're catching a show or movie at BAM and is conveniently located near multiple subway stops and near the Atlantic Terminal. Try to go during the day if you can get away from work.

My one and only James decided to try Olea last Saturday night. I mean, every time we drive by the restaurant, especially on Sundays around brunch, you can always count on people lingering around the corner on Lafayette waiting for their name to be called for the next available table. Our waitress was super nice and not overly or under attentive; just the riiiiight balance. Perfect. She did, however, misguide us in the very best way possible by saying their carafe of sangria is actually a full-on grown up pitcher (think 8 glasses) for either one person who's just angling for a horrible hangover the next day or two people who just want to get really tipsy and if they drink enough water that night won't wake up with a headache. We chose a bunch of tapas: whole-wheat pita with a beet skordalia (more like a beet puree) and feta dip; shrimp with lemon and garlic; marinated anchovies over arugula; salmon empanadas (special); and organic chicken meatballs. Plus an arugula salad with pears. Everything was solid overall and the food came out quickly. James did think some of the dishes were a little salty (namely the feta dip and the shrimp) and I did agree with him too, but I was on my fourth glass of sangria, so i would've agreed to anything at that point. James totally dug the salmon empanadas and I wolfed down the chicken meatballs; both were delicious. The anchovies just delivered; be sure to order it if you love to eat whole sardines. We both adored the skordalia and although the chunky feta dip was a tad oversalted (or maybe it would've benefitted from not being salted at all), i did keep munching on it. We'd both return, hopefully for brunch next time.

This restaurant is so good! I recommend you this restaurant! The only problem is that we can't pay by card, only cash! nice servers, great location, perfect atmosphere and vibe. Servers we extremely warm. Very good pasta in a spacious restaurant. I love love love this place. Delicious. Cash only.
Great spot. I love that you can order exactly how much you feel like! The food was great and the atmosphere fun. WIll definitely head back.

I went here again and I have to qualify what I said earlier. Â The restaurant has a new chef and I don't think polenta is his or her forte--it was burnt and the flavors didn't hold together. Â On the flip side, the spring soup was delicious as usual and so was the chicken. Â The market salad was also weaker than usual. Â The proportions of the various greens were off so that the flavors weren't blending together. Â  It's still really good food and a wonderful ambiance but it may take a few weeks to iron out the kinks.
4 stars?!?! Nooo, this place does not warrant 4 stars at all. The pizza was edible, nothing spectacular. With all the amazing pizza places in NY, this place does not even rank.

Very good. Not cheap but the quality is a step up..and you pay for that. Gluten free options, and a simple menu. Being that i am a chef the simple menu means your food is thought out and way fresher! The coffee is sublime.

I love this place and try to go whenever I'm in NYC. Everything is great, especially the rice paper wraps. The mighty mushroom, crunch n munch, and green machine are my favorite rolls. Good pricing. The drinks and desserts are niceeeee too. Friendly staff, except for one itamae, who is very curt and looks pissed off, he's the man, very badass.

Came here for my 1/2 birthday and farewell dinner to my BFF Neth--it was one of the best 3 hour dinner of our lives. Kiyo (the chef) even came out and talked to us a couple times. Love the space-- huge skylights in the middle of the cieling, and recessed garden on the side wall. Couches as seats makes the whole room feel like youre at someones house-- Kiyo's house. Food...everything was excellent and thats why this place gets 5 stars ($15-25 an order). It's tapas style, very easy to share, sizeable portions. Here's what we ordered-- 1. The cavier-- this lasted us through all our courses. Get it, have it on the side and dip into it when youre waiting for your next plate. Comes with beet, cucumbers, radishes, etc. 2. The mushroom uni croquette-- melt in your mouth uni. Its a small fried ball filled with savory mushrooms, and topped with a generous amount of the most seductive uni Ive ever had. 3. Oysters! You can buy a dozen for $30 or 6 for $16. I say GO FOR THE DOZEN! Caught from Massachusetts, so fresh and silky. Best part though was instead of cocktail sauce, Kiyo makes this amazing apple vinegar sauce instead. Seriously. Go for the dozen. 4. Market Price Sashimi-- you choose 3 of the 5 they have, and they give at least 5 pieces each. They dont skimp on this. 5. Today's Special Wagyu -- TONGUE. How could I say no? How can anyone say no? Yum. Comes with fried potato and garlic. Make sure to take each bite with the rosemary. 6. Black Miso Cod-- Yeah you'd think all cods should be the same since all Japanese establishments serve this-- but youre wrong. Dont be stupid. Order it. We ordered it twice. Something about the seared skin, and buttered meat...very irresistable. 7. AND last but not least, the sake panna cotta. Not too sweet, just the right amount of alcohol. Helped keep our buzz going from our own bottle of sake. But just FYI-- its BYOB. Dont worry though, Rick from Sakaya can hook you up with a bottle.

I think it's safe to say, we all love BCD. Who doesn't love soon dobu? (It's okay if you don't; I forgive you ;) ) This place is crowded most of the time. It's good for gatherings - large and small. With a large group, it's best to make a reservation and make sure everyone gets there at the appointed time! Or else, you might just lose your spot. If you've never had soon dobu before, you're in for a treat! I usually order the seafood one, mild. Everyone has their preference, so try one or two kinds until you find your favorite. The dish comes with fried fish (yum!).

Had a hankering for potatoes in fried form so made my way to Pommes Frites for the first time. I asked for the roasted garlic mayo and I'm not sure I actually got it - the mayo didn't have the subtle sweetness from roasted garlic. I can't even really identify what it was but it had a unique tang to it. The fries themselves were also ok. Can't say I've ever had real Belgian fries as I've never been to Belgium, but they were much larger/thicker cuts than I had imagined. Not the best fries I've ever had but they hit the spot. Really large portions if purchasing for just 1 person. I'd still go back to try other sauces and the poutine!

I'm almost positive that I've hit sushi snob status. Â I can't order "sushi deluxes" any more - not that I go to restaurants that even have that on their menu. Â  Thus, I was only mildly excited about Sushi Yasuda despite the rave reviews. Â Fresh off my meal there, I am happy to report that I now have my "happy place" in Manhattan. Â  Set in midtown amongst the high-rises of our financial crisis, I'm rather surprised to find such an amazing sushi experience since all of my great ones have been in hole in the wall spaces that smelled of sushi rice. Â Sushi Yasuda is set in a posh modern space that reminds you more of the W than of Tsukiji. Â  Still, the moment you sit down at the sushi bar, I found myself whooshed back to Japan. Â The warm towel always does it for me. Â They also bring out a little wet towel that is scrunched up for use on your fingers. Â The chef encouraged us to use our hands to eat - the proper way to eat sushi. Â It was actually the first time that I did this during an entire meal and I must say that I LOVED it. Â  We ordered the omakase, which isn't listed on the menu but our chef happily obliged us on our journey. Â Fifteen to twenty pieces later, I finally figured out where heaven really is. Â I can't remember all that we ate but amongst the highlights were: - East coast Tuna - It's lightly seared and not fat at all and yet amazingly smooth and tasty. Â They would get 5 stars on just this piece alone. Â  - Florida eel - One of two pieces of eel that we ate and this one was soft, fresh and probably the best piece of eel I have ever eaten. Â I know that I can no longer compare fresh eel to the stuff you get frozen at most sushi restaurants. Â You owe it to yourself to try eel at a real sushi restaurant. Â  - California Uni - Call me crazy but it just seemed to taste better here than even what I've had in California. Â Softer and more buttery with less of the "fishy" taste. Â  - Japanese Mackerel - Perfection - Sardine-family fish - This was an interesting one - sort of a short digression from the norm but which kept the tastes varied so you weren't eating the same thing every time. Â  - Scallion sprouts - After we asked the chef to end our meal, he asked if we would like to have this piece at the very end and we said sure. Â He pulled out the scallion sprouts out of a very small wooden box and proceeded to make pieces of sushi - adding I believe some salt and soy sauce. Â I'm not sure if it makes the perfect ending or if it would have been better in the middle but I loved it. Â I love trying new things and this was a prefect example. Â It completely changes your palate and in this case really helped us to wrap up our meal. Â  We also had the usual toro, salmon, tuna and some other whitefishes (not as great). Â Our meal ended with a glass of hot black tea and we left feeling utterly satisfied. Â It really was an amazing sushi experience - completely deserved of a 5 star rating.

Couldn't keep me away for long from bustan, went for a brunch again only two weeks after I've been there for the first time. cannot speak highly enough of this place, as a native middle eastern and big foodie it's by far the finest modern mid eastern restaurant in NYC. litteraly amazing food.

I went to Olivier tonight with my husband for dinner and I really enjoyed this place. I had the lamb shank with some amazing french beans and potatoes. The food was great, the atmosphere was very nice and the service amazing. I'm excited to have this restaurant in the neighborhood and I think it's a great addition to the area. I have just couple of suggestions for the owners: the place is TOO dark, please put some more candles on the table or do something, as I could barely see the menu and my husband during dinner. Also the menu needs in my opinion couple of more appetizers and entrees (perhaps a nice beef for one person or a pork chop). Overall a great restaurant!

Not that this place needs yet another review but the ramen is delish, the head chef is sexy and the line up is worth it!! Â Lunch special is great to share with two people and they always finish the meal with a hot black tea. It is worth the hype but if you come at 10:45am you can get in right when they open at 11 am for an early lunch. Try everything on the menu and ask for their specials. Don't be rude to the hostess or she will make sure you don't get any ramen!!

Before my trip, all of my friends recommended trying this infamous halal cart. Honestly, I didn't think some chicken/lamb over rice dish could be THAT amazing, but boy was I wrong. The meat was cooked to perfection, I liked the lamb a lot more than the chicken, though both were really good. As our friends suggested, we drowned our food with their white sauce. We forgot to use the red spicy sauce unfortunately, next time I will keep that in mind. And best of all, $6 for a huge platter and very generous amounts of meat, what more can you ask for?! This is a MUST TRY if you come to new York!!

As of now, you have seen that Joe's Shanghai has had 602 reviews before mine. Â Let me add mine to the cacophony. Â I've been eating at Joe's since the start, back in the 90's and the one thing that they have always done well is their consistency with their soup dumplings. Â Nothing has changed with their excellent overall quality: it has been consistent since day one. Â The thing I remember about Joe's is that it replaced a restaurant called Chef Ho's in the same location, and Chef Ho's also had awesome soup dumplings, which makes me wonder if Joe Shanghai is owned by the same people. Also, regarding the detractors of Joe's, remember that you will probably be seated with others as it's a small restaurant; you will probably be surprised by having a 15% gratuity added to the bill (a small price to pay for the best soup dumplings in New York and quick service). Â As for those who say it's a tourist trap, it isn't, because the food you're getting is similar in taste to what you get in other neighborning Chinatown restaurants. It is only perceived to be a tourist trap because Joe's is in many travel guides. Â Also, prices are low, compared to it's competitors. You'll get 8 XLB with each order, not 6 at a higher price at other restaurants. What you will be getting are what I call the "big three" in soup dumpling quality. Â That is, a cloth-like, thin chewy skin, a semi-dense broth, and well-flavored pork/crab. Â I have yet to find another place that serves dumplings like these anywhere else in New York, save Joe's Ginger, which I will get to later. Â Remember when you visit this place, the reason to come here are the soup dumplings. Â The fact that they make all their other dishes well (all Shanghainese-style) is a big bonus. Â My favorites are the Shanghai fried flat noodles and also the rice cakes. Finally, for those of you who like to have their own table, Joe's Ginger, also owned by Joe's Shanghai is one block up Pell Street and on the same side. Â You can get the same dumplings more intimately Â with less noise. Â There you have it. Â Enjoy my friends...

Went here for a special occaison (dad meeting the bf) and had an excellent meal. The buffala mozzerlla app was by far the BEST mozzerella/tomato dish I've ever had- which is saying a lot considering I order/make it quite often. The spinach gnocci was superb, and so was the fish entree. I gave up sweets for lent, but was told that the pannicotta was amazing. Wine was great, price was right, service was great- we got there before 7 on a Saturday and were seated promptly for a party of five and did not even feel rushed when the crowds came pouring in. I will definitely be back, often.

The name Umami now comes with a heaping serving of hype. I came with high expectations, and left satisfied but not blown away. We arrived at around 7PM and the restaurant was filled but not crowded...by the time we left at 8:30PM it was packed. I ordered the Manly Burger and my partner ordered the off-the-menu Five Spice Duck. We also got sides of tempura onion rings and truffle fries, which were both great. The onion rings were some of the best I've had...they were less greasy than your norm allowing you to eat a few without feeling sick. After splitting the burgers perfectly, we were upset that we hadn't ordered the famed Truffle Burger. The Manly definitely delivered, their way of cooking the patty is unique and very rare even by the standards of someone who enjoys a medium rare burger. Extremely high quality beef and beer cheddar made for an enjoyable experience--other condiments i.e. tomato, lettuce are not present and the crispy onions tend to lose their crisp in the molten hot cheese. The Five Spice Duck Burger made me feel like I don't have a refined palette because it was definitely too fragrant of a flavor profile for me. It sort of tasted like the smell of the food bar at Whole Foods, that combination of every pasta and salad dish from cuisines of every realm of the world melding under a single hot lamp. My apologies for the ridiculous and graphic description, but when you bite into this thing, you'll know. We finished our meal with the sea-salted caramel ice cream which was great. I found the prices to be fair and the service to be helpful. Our server did warn us about the cooking preparation and the medium rare treatment, unlike some reviews have mentioned. Having expected a much different experience, I'm not sure I'd travel out of my way for Umami again but I could see it becoming a semi-regular jaunt if I lived in the area. Although it's not my absolute favorite, it's definitely worth stopping in at least once.

Solid spot. Traditional Greek food coming from a well known top area chef. The atmosphere is also traditional, but trendy at the same time. Their burgers were great and I loved the calamari. Awesome spin on salads as well.
Food and drinks are exceptional. Love the decor. They are not and open table and reservation staff is not very friendly, they expect you to call and confirm the day of the reservation. Really!!?

I was really surprised to see anything less than 4 stars for this place. Â This is a great, fast breakfast spot. Â When you are late, in a hurry and want eggs or pancakes this place is awesome. Â  I come here a lot on my way into work in the morning. Â I recommend this place all the way.

One of the best, if not THE best, places to get falafel in Manhattan. Â AND, they're practically open 24hrs! Â The food is great, the price is right, and the service is FAST. Â Good luck finding a table! Â This is definitely a place to get it "to go"

People expect me to know everything. "You live in New York? We're coming to visit and see you and itwillbesomuchfun! Damn ... you should tell us where to get dinner!" And then my career as a journalist finally comes in handy. I have to run down the checklist of where, when, who('s going), how much are you spending and why in God's green earth haven't you gotten that thing looked at? Inevitably they will answer all those questions incorrectly. When? 7pm on Saturday* Where? Times Square** Why? We just want to seeeee yoooouuuu**** How much? We're willing to pay for a decent meal -- $10 or so. You see, when you have friends visiting from out of town, they're just not used to how much everything is, nor how much effort will be involved in getting there/getting a table. They can't handle the trip straight to the Lower East Side (which is why people eat at Appelbee's in New York -- sometimes familiarity is comforting). But sometimes I come to Yelp, and I ask it, oh great and wise green wizard***** for a suggestion, since, y'know, that's ostensibly what it's for, and it spits back the absolute perfect place for what I'm looking. Trattoria wasn't something you'd confuse for a straight-out-of-Arthur-Ave-Italian joint, but it certainly was all the things I needed it to be with picky eaters from out of town. The food was good, filling and not overly priced. The wine list was varied enough to give them the feeling that they were actually choosing something other than 'red' or 'white' (which is something they do in the big city). And it was close enough to their hotel in Times Square that I didn't make them walk too far, but far enough away that we weren't violated by the neon and gaudiness (which we got later, when I took them on a walking tour of Times Square). I'm definitely adding this to my list****** of Italian places near Times Square where I can take tourists. * - Â As if there aren't 20 million other people going to dinner at that time ** - Despite it being the center of your favorite TV show, there's lots of places I've never been, or know well. I can't take you on the Sex and the City Tour, either.*** *** - I once had four female roommates at one time, so it's entirely possible I probably could take you on this tour. **** - If you really wanted to see me, you'd come with me to Hooters, 'cause that's where I like to go. ***** - Has shot the food. ****** - I really do keep a list. It's in MY MIND.

They should franchise and have 1 location in every borough. Â The Chicken Shawarma is absolutely amazingly delicious. Very scrumptious!!! And the Falafal too. Large and fried to perfection for a nice crispy outside and soft fluffy inside. Love that they put Hummus and Tahiti in pita. The red cabbage adds extra flavor and crunchiness. Â I substituted Taboulli for the LTO in Shawarma. Â Their spicy red sauce is bursting with flavor and intensity. Â Just hot enough that it does not last forever nor make you sweat bullets. Â Tunisian style med pitas, entrees and desserts with a little hint of French culinary flair. Â Food is fresh and hot. Â They have a self serve water urn on the shelf. Â The ambience is lovely bright and relaxing. Â The tables are beautiful solid wood raw cut wood with a light stain and varnish. Â Cool Mediterranean decor and artwork is priceless. Â Great prices $16 for 3 pitas.

Don't be thrown by the "Mediterranean" label for their brunch menu--you still get the classics. I am still looking for my go-to brunch place on the Upper West side, but I may have found it. Â  They give you a free drink with your entree (bloody mary, mimosa, bellini, coffee etc). Â Yea so it's probably Â built into the price, but at least it seems like you are getting it for free, right? Â Brunch also comes with a small basket of banana and corn bread. The eggs benedict was really good. Â Perfectly poached, and comes with a salad or a side of fries.

Gorgeous gorgeous gorgeous bar. Â Great date spot - circular wood bar, lovely locals, fantastic art deco theme (they must have spent a fortune renovating this place). Â  Had a delicious hangover burger here and some vino to set me straight - plus they have a well thought out wine list and the help staff were helpful and attentive. Â  Very cozy, sexy place, can't wait to park myself here for several hours in wintry weather. Â They've got booths here too. Â Do go, but don't tell too many people about it, please.

I don't usually venture out to Chinatown that much. It's a little far from me and the crowds there make me really anxious. However, my friend took me to Joe's Shanghai for awesome water dumplings a few weekends ago. I've never had water dumpling and I figured it was just a name for boiled dumplings. I WAS SO WRONG. These are a billion times better than boiled dumplings. These karate chop regular dumplings' asses off. Joe's Shanghai has communal tables, so you sit at a round table of six to eight people. There seems to always be a line, but I haven't waited longer than 10 minutes. They are crazy fast inside. There's a particular way of eating WD's. The key is to be careful (hot)! You place a dumpling onto your soup spoon and take a tiny bite of the doughy wrapping. Inside, the little nugget of is swimming in a delicious little pool of broth. You can slurp out the broth or spill it out on to your spoon. You're provided with a vinegar-soy sauce that nicely balances out the richness. It can be a bit of a mess. Chinese scallion pancakes are different from Korean ones (duh), and I think I prefer the Korean ones. I need more scallion and seafood. Chinese ones are chewier and thicker, but Jim liked these a lot.
Today is my girlfriends birthday and she is a vegetarian. As an avid meat eater, this places is great. The food is wonderful an the atmosphere is outstanding!!!

This review is based on the food I had here. I wasn't drinking any alcohol at the time I visited so I can't comment on the drinks. I did have a tasty virgin pina colada..delish. They have a cozy back area if you decide to come in a group..it's more private. The restaurant wasn't too big overall but I believe there is a lower level as well. We were served promptly by the waiter. I didn't get a chance to view the entire place as I was late to meet my party so I just rushed to the back. Later on in the night, I thought I heard live music but not sure. For appetizers I had the cerviche and it was good. Nothing earth shattering. For my main meal- I ordered the Snapper (fried with tomato sauce). It was quite bland actually. The fish was unseasoned..the floured coating was still unseasoned. the tomato based sauce was even more unseasoned. It was truly a disappointment. It came with white rice and black beans. I wish I had gotten something else. My friends ordered oxtail and I think they enjoyed it. I would like to go back for drinks and maybe try something else on the menu. I did taste my friend's dessert (tres con leche), have def had better but anyho.
Great place to sit next to a fireplace and play some jenga!

Last month, my friend planned a surprise birthday brunch for her boyfriend at Jane. She made advance reservations, so we didn't have to wait long for seats. Â The decor at Jane is unlike any other brunch spot I've been to. Chic decor and great, cozy ambiance There's two floors of seating and both floors are spacious and cozy. For my complimentary cocktail I ordered the White Peach Bellini which was light, refreshing, a little bubbly from the sparkling wine. I enjoyed it very much. My boyfriend ordered the Benedict Jane. The Benedict Jane is poached egg covered with a rich tarragon Hollandaise sauce, sitting on top of a moist and delicious crab and crawfish cakes and home fries on the side, This was really a beautiful dish! I tried one of the Benedict Jane and it was great. I really enjoyed the meatiness of the crab and crawfish cake. It's very different from most eggs Benedict I have had. I ordered the Benedict Johnny which is similar to a regular eggs Benedict. Poached eggs topped with a rich, creamy, roasted tomato Hollandaise sauce sitting on top of a maple chicken sausage, and corn pancakes with home fries on the side, I really liked the home fries because they were crispy and crunchy and possibly the BEST home fries I've had! Â Another thing I loved the most about my eggs Benedict is the yolk was oozing out and it was a runny yolk. Apparently, we all had room for dessert and had the Pumpkin Chai Profiteroles which was seriously pumpkin heaven! There was pumpkin ice cream, candied pumpkin seeds, pumpkin paper, and chai sauce. I really liked this dessert because you can taste pumpkin in different textures, shapes, and sizes. My favorite was the pumpkin ice cream - seriously delicious! The next dessert was the Seven Layer Chocolate Cake. Absolutely Chocolate heaven! The seven layer chocolate cake consists of chantilly cream, whipped gananche, and a chocolate sauce. This was amazing. It was moist, chocolatey, creamy, and just... it'll take your breath away! I really enjoyed our brunch at Jane. The staff were very friendly and nice. The food was beyond perfection. I would love to come back here in the near future. I most definitely want to try their sister restaurant: The Smith as well. Tip: If you order your entree from the brunch section, it comes with a complimentary cocktail of your choice.

Get here early for happy hour and order a Margarita! Tapas Tuesdays!! Hands down, the best happy hour I've ever been to. Half off on DELICIOUS Â tapas that includes cubanos, empanadas, calamari and some of the best ribs you will ever have. I highly recommend getting there as early as possible though, it can get pretty crowded. Although, their drink specials are excellent and staff is extremely friendly despite how hectic happy hour could be. I'll be back to Yuca Bar many many many times and definitely back for Tapas Tuesdays.

Love this place, so happy its so close to me. My friends in the city commute out to come here, it's that great. The scallops are amazing, BLT buns are one of my faves, and the fried chicken is delicious! It's all tapas style, which I love! Won't break the bank either!

this is a fun place. if you have a group of your best friends you'll have so much fun. the food is great. the wine is cheap and the atmosphere is loud and energetic. you wont break the bank having a good time here.

I took my husband and his family here for his 30th birthday dinner. I've been here before, and it had always been good. They brought a huge bread basket. For appetizer, we ordered fried calamari. Super fresh and awesome. For entrees, we ordered chicken parmagiana and their special of the day seafood linguine. Both were amazing. Everyone was happy and stuffed. I did bring a birthday cake and was told when I made reservations that they charged $2.50 per person for bringing an outside cake. If it was any other ordinary birthday, I would just order dessert there which happens to be very good. But it's a special birthday, and I got him a custom cake. It was the first time, any restaurant I've been to has ever charged for bringing in a cake. I thought it was ridiculous, considering two of the people in our party were 2 and 4 year old kids. They didn't even eat off their plate. So extra $15 for 6 people just for bringing in a cake. That's the only complaint I have because other than that, it's a damn great restaurant.

I grew up eating Cuban food cooked by mu Abuela and my mother so I have really high standards when it comes to Cuban restaurants. This place met, and exceeded those expectations! My mom said when she was growing up they used to go eat there all the time. Listen, mi Abuela does not eat at any restaurants. Ever. So the fact that she used to go here on the regular was enough to sell me. We went for my moms birthday and they really go nuts when singing to whoevers birthday it is! Would be embarrassing for somebody who doesn't like the be the center of attention but it was a lot of fun. My fiancÃ© and I had the picadillo and the bistec empanizado and shared. Both were delicious and the closest to my grandmothers I have ever had. I also sampled my dad's ropa vieja and my mother got the bistec rincon criollo. Both, especially the ropa vieja where amazing. Highly recommended restaurant!

This is my all time favorite Italian restaurant. Â It's casual and welcoming...most importantly is that their pasta's are incredibly tasty... its like you're in pasta heaven! Must order: tagliatelle, cappelletti and garganelli

This was an amazing restaurant. Â I was in the mood for a good Italian dinner, chicken Parmesan to be precise, and I got a great meal. Â The atmosphere was really nice, and the food was great. Â The service was fantastic too! Â To me that's just as important as good food. Â I'll come back here again.

Well, after an incredibly thoughtful and informative note from the GM here I have to update my review to reflect the incredible customer service they offer here. One of my complaints was the difficulty finding this restaurant in the massive mall complex located at the listed address. He responded that he realizes it's hard and they're going to clarify the directions on site and online. Awesome! A second concern was that they don't take reservations. He noted that while they still don't do so for lunch, they began offering dinner res' a few months back ... also awesome. I really appreciate businesses that take customer concerns & feedback into consideration like this - and for such a large restaurant group I can't help but be a big fan!

I truly hate writing a poor review for a restaurant that clearly wants to provide the neighborhood with delicious unusual food. I was so very excited for its opening but I don't know if I'll come back. A couple of weeks ago before the holidays, I wanted to celebrate with a dinner in and ordered takeout. We ordered the beef curry and fish curry with a side of roti. The order was supposed to be ready in 20 minutes and I maybe got there 5 minutes late, at most. When I walked the food back to my apartment -- 3 blocks -- the food was cold. Not ice cold but nowhere even near lukewarm. The restaurant was empty and something tells me the food was ready faster than 20 minutes. The roti were hard as rice paper before it's placed in warm water. In addition, the portions were shockingly disproportionately small compared to the price. I had thought we would share the 2 entrees between 2 people but there was maybe 1 entree's worth of food if you combined the dishes. I don't really know if the flavors were any good but they definitely weren't spectacular enough to shine through the temperature and size. I'm sorry Selamat Pagi but it was an utterly disappointing dinner for 40+ bucks with the extra side of rice. We went to the bodega next door and bought cookies and chips to make ourselves feel better.

Out of this world food... I mean, seriously... EVERYTHING I eat here is good, every time. Not many restaurants do things that right. I first went for the steamed pork buns (like everyone else, I imagine) but I go back for the rice cakes with spicy sausage.

Tilly Y. said it well: Â "upscale but not pretentious" - an experience that I'm always seeking out. Â  Pros: Â  - Creative, well-thought out dishes, many that will blow you away. Â The filet I had was probably the best I've ever eaten. Â The bombolino with smoked maple syrup dessert, I'm still dreaming about. - Really really excellent staff. You can see the training, from the knowledgeable wait staff - never a "let me check" answer, to the light touch of the runners (gosh does it drive me crazy when the runners act like bulls in a china shop), to the coffee server's Escoffier-like final twist of the saucer to align the spoon just so, everyone truly seems happy to see you, right down to the coat check person, even tho we didn't check our coats. - Ambiance and design. Â Classy, roomy (especially for Manhattan!), high ceilings, not too noisy, the right level of light, a great balance of dining room versus bar vs open kitchen - none of which intrude on each other and muddy the atmosphere - a common problem in space-constrained Manhattan eateries. Cons: - Only one, really, that prevents me from giving this a full 5 stars (which I reserve for places that hit everything perfectly) -- the occasional dish that just seems to fall flat enough that you wonder if anyone ever tasted it. Â Because the rest of the place just works SO well, these mistakes, while more minor in a lesser establishment, stand out really strongly. Â Case in point the pea tendril salad, which, on paper, sounded amazing and creative. Â In execution, the overpowering lime juice really destroyed the dish - obliterating all the other flavors (seemingly chosen really carefully), and the pea tendrils were less tendrils but more awkwardly-sized fibrous mini-stalks - difficult to eat, without much flavor. Â But we did discuss this at length with the waiter, who handled it with aplomb, with smiles all around. It's very easy to smile a lot at North End Grill. Â One of my new favorites!

Dangerous Martini's, wonderful veal cutlet parmigana hero. Â Wow.. the tartufo was almost as good as the stuff I had in Piazza Navona in Rome. Wonderful experience as soon as I went upstairs. Â  Tip - downstairs is crowded, avoid it, head upstairs where there is plenty of space.

Oh Eataly, you're such a tease. You were the guy I drooled over from afar. Reading about your grand opening and succulent offerings made me so excited to finally meet you in person. So who can blame me that I waltzed into your open arms (or doors) with high hopes, fresh back in NYC from the shores of Asia? But alas, my dreams of being swept off my feet by some Italian stallion were crushed. Sure, you were so handsome and suave in appearances, with aisles filled with delightful authentic Italian goodies, chock full of refined olive oils, well-crafted fresh mozzarella and smooth almond nougat (looooovee). But looks ain't everything, folks. The hefty price tags displayed that you think way too highly of yourself. The long lines meant that you were well-sought after (and probably had a big head) - I prefer the road less-travelled, thank you very much. And the confusing layout meant you liked to play hard to get. Sorry, I don't play games. My dining experience confirmed the truth. It was a first date gone bad. Appetizers already got off on a shaky start - with sweet shrimp that would have been delicious if not completely overwhelmed by the heavy hand of lemon and salt and capitone that was ridiculous to eat with the entire vertebrae still encased in the breaded and seared chunk of eel meat. The main course of a whole seared fish was only mediocre - nothing special. We enjoyed eating the caper berries and olives more than the fish itself to be honest. It felt like going out with a guy but wanting all of his friends instead. The wine was probably the most worthwhile, but yet again, any guy looks better with wine. The overpriced gelato was like a half-ditched effort for the kiss goodbye. Sorry, Eataly, don't think there will be a second date.

Quiet, casual, but most of all delicious. This is what I envision when thinking of NY pizza. Got the bufala, and everything about it was perfect. Crust was chewy yet crisp. And the mozzarella? A+. Luzzo's is a must!

Pretty place, not so good food. Â  Not really sure why it has a Michelin star? The food: -Fried oysters - mediocre, have had better exterior not as crispy as I'd like, too soft. Â I was told to eat it with the leaf, but it didn't make it taste much better. -Grilled kobe beef tongue - meh.. mediocre -Foie gra on french toast w/mango & bacon - Good, not mind blowing -Polenta and aleppo crusted cod with a smoked corn and barley risotto, and truffle-huitlacoche vinaigrette - Dry, not much flavor -Roasted duck breast with sesame soy dressing, cassava chips, bok choy and pickled chilies - I would have enjoyed duck from Big Wong more than this dish and for $27 for few slices of duck, you can get 2 whole ducks at BW's :) Don't expect to be WoWed here by the food, but by all means, go for a sexy drink with your date.

Blew my mind. Definitely worth the hour wait. Just get some beers at the bar and before you know it you'll be chompin' on some hot, bubbly pizza. We ordered The Mootz with vegan fennel sausage, Arugula Shmoogula, and Hellboy. Hellboy was simply amazing. Don't be scared to try the hot honey, it's just the right amount of spicy and sweet. I think they might sell bottles of it too! We casually mentioned to our waitress of a birthday in our group and by the end of our meal Paulie himself came by with a dessert pizza, candles and all! He was super sweet. Even with the place jammed packed he visited each table. Really goes to show you that there are still some restaurant owners that care! Can't wait for my next visit.

Treated my favorite cousin to dinner here last night and it was great! I read the other reviews and was excited to check this place out. As soon as I walked in, the host (possibly owner) was in front and immediately greeted me very warmly. I told him I was treating my cousin to a birthday dinner and he said he'd plan to have a slice of chocolate cake brought out after we ate. I was seated right away as the tables were pretty empty but the bar was poppin' with after workers enjoying happy hour. The look and feel inside is warm and what you expect from a nice gastropub: tiled wall (behind bar), dark wood, dim lighting, tiled floors. We split the white bean crostini, hake wrapped in kale and the mushroom fettuccini, everything was DELICIOUS, extremely fresh and so tasty. Then after our meal, just as promised they brought out some chocolate cake with a candle for the birthday girl. We had a great time and really enjoyed our food...will be back!

The good was very tasty and well prepared. We went around 5 PM on a Friday and had no trouble getting a table. It started getting busy as we were leaving around 6:15 PM. The service was good. Everyone was polite and courteous. The prices seemed a bit high, but it is Midtown. This was out first visit. We'll be back.

I came here for New Years eve dinner and everything was absolutely perfect. The restaurant is small and cozy, but you don't feel cramped at all. Service was impeccable, food was phenomenal and the drinks were top notch and creative. Â Highly recommend this place.

I came here on valentines day and was late for our reservation so they gave our table away. The people were really nice so they gave someone else's table to us after waiting like 2 mins. One of the staff saw me holding so many flowers and offered to put it in the refrigerator for us which was really convenient for me cause the tables were really close together. The reason i would give it 4 stars and not 5 is because it took a long time to get our food. The couples next to us got their food before us even though they came after us. They even ordered the same food as us too! They were also offered wine but we weren't ): So i felt a bit mistreated but its okay it was a nice day. Overrall the meal was pretty expensive for just three dishes adding up to almost 80 dollars.

Great food for when u need that meal to full u up. My girlfriend took me here when we go into the city. I'm never disappoint here the food is awesome and hit the spot . A must do if u even a little short on cash .
The truffle burger is the best burger i've ever had. This experience has honestly changed the way I eat burgers. Nothing I have tried since then has come close.

I don't have any idea what it means to be gluten-free, but apparently part of the lure of Risotteria revoles around this trait. Everyone makes mistakes in their lives and in my opinion, if you go to a restaurant called Risotteria and don't get risotto you have made a mistake. To get pizza here is tantamount to going to Doughnut Plant and asking if they have muffins. Yes, they are in the same family, but look at the sign out front and the name on the menu and act accordingly. The menu is full of risotto options and I went with a shitake, green beans and sweet corn mix. It was excellent. Texture is of course very important in making risotto or why else would Gordon Ramsay always be screaming about the f'in risotto on Hell's Kitchen and that part was perfectly done and the flavors of the dish complemented its consistency. The gluten-free bread served with the meal was kind of good and kind of awkward at the same time. I kept eating it, but it was not your typical bread, lacking gluten and all (?). The tables are absolutely jammed together, side by side, and they have to be pulled out for a party to get in. This is ridiculous, you are literally at a two-top and your table touches the two-tops on either side of you. When the people next to you have not gotten their meal, you can feel them looking at your food and breathing on your shoulder and listening to your conversation. Risotteria makes good risotto, as they should given their name, and there are so many different options this is definitely a place to come back to when you have the craving...and of course when you want to live on the edge, gluten-free. Special thanks to Rachel A. for suggesting risottoland.

If you go in understanding that Di Fara is as much about the experience (mostly waiting) as about the end result, you can't really be disappointed. There are two or three pizzas I like better in the city, but being able to watch this guy touch the pans in the oven with his bare hands is quite the treat.

Located in a great neighborhood, is this great restaurant. Â The nice thing, is that the bar area is done just as professionally as the rest of the restaurant. Â A menu that is well above average, served by a professional staff with smiles on their faces. Â Though, you are highly likely to find this place crowded, it is worth checking out at least once.

I came to Bubby's after the yelp elite event to wait off my buzz, and it was the worst choice. There are some tasty beers on tap, and I was powerless against them. The bartender, Steve, was nice eye candy and made a recommendation for the turkeyburger. It was really good, juicy, with bits of veggies. I also had a chocolate chip cookie and a peanut/chocolate/graham cracker pie slice to go. Food is good, atmosphere is very family friendly. I've never seen so many kids in one place, outside of NYC parks.

I had the half chicken meal with two sides. Â The chicken was good and juicy and flavorful. Â I had roasted potatoes and cauliflower on the side and a French lemonade soda. Â It's good, healthy, quick and the price is reasonable. What else do you want? Â I might try the chicken wrap sandwich now that I see a picture of it on yelp because what I ate is more like a dinner. Â I'm stuffed.

One of the best Chinese joints in NYC. I love this place. Especially the pork buns and dumplings. Great lo mein and seafood dishes. However sometimes the food is much better than other times. But always well above the average. Unfortunately they do not accept credit cards of any kind, so bring cash.

Okay. Wow. The rave reviews to this place is not new, but this is what I will say: it's only worth coming here for the pancakes. Â Anything else will make you just feel jealous. I ordered the Southern Breakfast , and ended up eating most of my friends' pancakes. Â I can only speak to the Blueberry Pancakes. Why are these pancakes so orgasmic? Yes, orgasmic. I literally had to stop for a moment after the first bit and just say "Whoa." Â They're fluffy; so fluffy that they just melt in your mouth. Â So buttery, with the perfect combination of sweet and salty taste. I just can't explain it- except that I've never had pancakes like this. And the blueberries-- so fresh, so juicy- I don't know how they maintain their circular shape being so juicy. Â And the maple butter syrup- so unique in flavor, and the perfect enhancement to the sweet/salty switch off. Â  I can't even describe anymore, you'll just have to experience it yourself. Â Surely worth the 1.5 hour wait (tip: go with no more than 2 people- heck go by yourself and wait around the corner a Stuffed Artisan Cannolis) On the other stuff: nothing else here compares to the pancakes, in fact for a true Souther breakfast (with grits, and home fries, etc- go down the street to Alias). Â  The sugar-cured bacon is good, but you sick of eating it after two bites. Â In fact, I had all 6 pieces in the Southern Breakfast and got pretty ill. That's a lot of fat! And sugar. Â I made the mistake of attempting to my health conscious (ha what a joke at this joint) and ordered poaches eggs- which they did NOT do well at all. It was laced with vinegar! Served me right I suppose. Â  The cheese grits were disappointing- it was okay; but it kind of looked....unappetizing. Like vomit-y. Â No bueno. Â  Lastly the fried green tomates- THOSE were good. I think it was also the fact that it's hard to screw up anything deep fried but I like to panko-esque crusted batter and the juiciness of the tomatoes. Â Ironically, there weren't enough of these items- except for the bacon. It's worth the wait every now and then but if you get discourage, you can grab a good brunch at Alias down the street (which has true Southern style breakfast- fried chicken in the am- yum!) But bottom line: pancakes=heaven.

I was introduced to Mamoun's by a friend whose son went to NYU a few years ago and was a fan of Mamoun's ever since. However, it seems that the subtle changes are leading this place to a decline - may be not visible yet due to long lines but in taste. Yesterday, Â we got falafel sandwich and it was filled with small dried up falafels and a sour tasting tahini. The pita was chewy as if heated too long in the oven. Â The quantity of salad was also smaller and I was actually able to eat the whole falafel without dropping anything on the table - they don't bother with plates, which is a feat that I never accomplished before. Disappointed, I tried the Baba Ganoush sandwich and the sour taste of tahini was more pronounced there. Most importantly, the hot sauce in the bottle that always was colored red is now a light brown. It does not taste the same either. I heard someone order his falafel with the hot sauce and I did the same and guess I got what tasted like a bottled hot sauce, which usually has too much vinegar. The guy taking orders (now he is translating orders in Spanish, dos falafel con picante? )was the same so wonder why the change! Mamoun, Please, you need to come back to the original standards.
Friend introduced me to this spot. Great food. I really liked the mini empanadas. The dipping sauces compliment the food very well.

I was going to talk about their silly policy of having people wait out in the cold (even if it is an enclosed area) until the entire party is seated. I was going to talk about the hostess/greeter talking shop to a trainee while I was in earshot (did you know a party of 2 is allotted 1.5 hours at a table?). However... All of that is water under the bridge because the moment we were seated, everything moved so smoothly, from drink service to food service, I forgot about that whole silliness. The food was so damn delicious! I started out with bacon soup (on the house). It was so savory, I couldn't wait to get my hot little hands on my food order. We had glazed chicken sriracha wings (tasty, but not special; bonus points for no breading); strawberry- cinnamon glazed ribs(delicious! Fell off the bone into my mouth); salt & pepper shrimp (juicy, buttery and crispy at the same time); pork BBQ Â rib sliders (Amazing! It literally melts in your mouth); and, muenster cheese with chorizo sausage (I don't eat cheese or bread, but this was too delicious to not at least taste. Which I did. A few times.) You would think with all that food they'd have to roll people out the door, but no! The portions are sized just right so you're satisfied without feeling like a pig. If you're the type who believes that a bigger portion is a better meal, I still say give this place a try! The prices are reasonable enough that for less than 100, you and a friend can have a feast. We had already made our minds up after the disappointing drink selection (it was all tailored to complement the meats) that we would eschew dessert and head to another place for drinks. But, she offered us the menu and, curious, we found ourselves ordering the bacon donuts (don't be grossed out - you can barely taste the bacon it's so mild. And actually, unexpectedly delicious!) and the custard dish (the name escapes me right now, but the combination of whipped cream, custard, chocolate, caramel and sorbet was pretty awesome). I must say, I didn't pay much attention to the ambience because I was there to eat, but Â the place is cozy with dim but readable lighting and I did notice when they brought out a high-chair for a party with a baby. (Personally, I don't think this place is ideal to bring a baby, but for the most part the kid was quiet, so what do I know? I only mention it in case you absolutely have to get out of the house and can't get a sitter). I will warn you - make reservations. Especially on weekends They are gracious with you being a little late, but anything unexpected and they may turn you away. It's to help the chef - the hostess was talking about it. Will I go back again? That would be a hell to the yeah. As a side note , we were there 1.25 hours.

This place is so cute and fun for lunch! They have a menu that changes with the season that always features fun, interesting sandwiches! They're all so different and varied that you'll definitely want to try them all! They also serve some yummy baked goods and random knick-knacks as well! The only issue being that the sandwiches are a bit pricey and nearly $10 each. Definitely give them a try though. You won't be disappointed by the quality of the food!
Go on Friday and get the lunch special!! It's always the same shredded beef special and it runs out every Friday, so get there early.

This is probably one of my favorite places in the city to grab a drink. The drinks/wine list are great and the ambiance is perfect. It's classy, but not over the top and you can actually sit, enjoy your company and have a pleasant conversation. The minus one star is b/c if you come during busy time, the wait could be a little long and there really isn't a good "waiting" area.

If you're in the mood for some delicious Cuban food, then Margon is the place to be! Â Always come here for lunch when they're serving Ox-tail. Â Braised to perfection, fall of the bone goodness. Â Add some dirty rice, soft cooked plantains and you got yourself a full lunch for 10 bucks. Â Depending on the server, their generosity varies. Â If you get this sweet cuban lady, expect more food. Â Avoid any of the guys at all cost. Â Never had their cuban sandwiches, but from what my co-workers said, theyre pretty amazing, and very cheap. Â This is a must try for Midtown Lunchers!

Unimpressed with the overcooked pork belly on my "OG" that took a really long time to come out. Â The flavors were bland, and now I see why they offer free spicy mayo and jalapeÃ±o. I was there pretty early, and it was slow. Â I would give them another try at night when the buns are hopefully ready, and the kitchen in in the groove.

We had brunch here recently and I say it was an all around great spot. Â We had a seat right by the window, which I think is probably nicer than actually sitting outside. Â The outdoor patio is kind of in a parking lot, but the view is nice from inside. We ordered the mushroom and truffle omelet and the poached egg and hash. Â Both were delicious. Â  I tend to order anything that says truffle, sometimes it's heaven on a plate and other times it disappoints. Â But this truffle omelet was one of the good times. Â It will probably be my go-to meal whenever I come here.

I echo all that have given the food served in this restaurant positive reviews. Â The fish they serve is super fresh and tasty. Â You can definitely tell that not a lot of seasoning goes into the fish which is great because too much seasoning takes away its natural flavor. Â The octopus is amazing and desserts yummy. Â I did take away 1 star because I felt the prices were a bit high. Â Expect to pay about $80 for 2 for dinner. Â Would I go back and recommend to others, heck yeah! Â As a matter of fact, we've already ordered take out from this place cuz the food was so good :)

Went here for a birthday dinner with my husband and loved the food. Particular stand out favorites for me were: Fluke Ceviche - very fresh and melts in your mouth Citrus Salad - somehow made fennel edible (i'm normally not a fan) Garganelli mushroom ragu - great pasta dish to share but be careful as it can be quite filling and you must leave room for your main course Arctic Char - perfectly cooked and also a great portion of fish I also have to say the service was admirable. Our water glasses were never empty and the waitress showed up at all the right times. The one minus for me was the seating. It felt a bit cramped with all the tables jammed next to each other. You can hear the conversations of the diners on either side of you and they can hear you. I know restaurants want to cram as many tables in as they can to maximize on their revenue but for a $200+ meal they should spread it out a bit as it really affects the ambiance.

Awesome brunch! The food was amazing and the spicy bloody marys are truly addictive. I know I will have cravings for the drink. Â  The bacon honey glazed biscuits served before the food came was delicious. Â We particularly loved the Eggs, Bacon and Cheese popover. However I didn't really care for the French Toast.

My love of my life and I went here tonight and we had the best time. Â IT is a cozy place with excellent food. Â We split the portions and it was amazing. Â Get the pork chops for sure! Â Thank you! Â -Jimmy

Definitely a place to eat. I came here on a date, we were waiting on a line for about 15 minutes before we stepped in. I didn't mind. Once we were inside the place was a bit small and hectic, that being said the environment still had an easy going vibe to it, based on looking at other people eating/talking and just overall hanging out. Everyone is given complementary corn bread, and glass of water. One good thing about this place is the wait time between when you order and when the food hits the table. It's a very small wait. I ordered the Porkchop and Waffle with Macaroni and Cheese. I wasn't too satisfied with the mac n cheese, it tasted kind of watery and tasteless, at least to me. My date was scarfing it down talking about it was the best. The porkchop and Waffle was on point though, the porchop was cooked to perfection and the huge waffle was nice and warm, tasted good. Doused everything in syrup. Overall I liked my time at the resaurant, I give it a 3 because I feel there are things that could be improved on, mainly quality of food and the portions. I feel the menu is a tad overpriced for the amount of food you get on your plate. I would go again. I would recommend it to a friend as well, with mention of price/portions.
Great shop for fries. The poutine is not as special as they claim. I wish I could try all the variety they had to offer. Big draw, and nice place for a quick snack of frites.

My friend Kiki had taken us here because she said that the uni soba was to die for. I love uni, and I love soba, so the 2 combined was really just a brilliant concept I had never heard of. I'm thinking that this dish is even better during summer because it's such a cool dish, however I wasn't disappointed. I prefer my uni on rice because I feel that it really magnifies the flavor of the uni.
Kian was great with beer choices.. nice food and a warm feel to the decor.. on this cold cold nyc nite, alfies Â was a home from home.. a great find.. thanks yelp..

This is the most completely fulfilling food experience you will ever have. Everything is unexpected and brilliant. The staff runs like clockwork. The pricing is on par with value but is definitely special occasion only for us, but absolutely worth it! Highly recommended!

The night we went, the chef wasn't in himself. 10 course tasting menu is very experimental. Great service and waitress who walked us through the meal. The food itself started out with a bang, but as we progressed through the courses, it didn't really get much better and slightly went down in quality. Oh well. I heard the 5 course tasting menu last year was heaven. Unfortunately, the 10 course tasting menu this year was so-so.

I'm not a big drinker but after reading all the positive reviews about the food, how could I not try it. Ordered the Smoked brisket hash which comes with eggs and toast. Very good flavor and good size portion that filled me up. Needless to say, I cleaned off my plate. Looking forward to my next visit and getting the ribs!
Huge omelettes and bottomless coffee. No kids menu for breakfast but the kids can split a stack of pancakes. Elizabeth was our server and she was sweet. Very good service and great food.
It feels weird to be grateful when a hostess is actually nice. But since this place is really popular, their hostess doesn't HAVE to be --but it made my night that she was actually nice!

- one of the best pies ive ever had. the price was justified.. my chinatown resident friend ordered her regular meat Â and veggie laden pie.. we visitors ordered a white pie with tomato and spinach.. - while im never one to order meat products on my pizza...this pie was fkcn delicous.. the meatballs and pepperoni were of excellent quality by themselves.. Despite the ridiculous 2 hour wait for lunch on a Saturday afternoon, i was glad I stuck it out. Â Roquefort burger was phenomenal. Â May be up there as the best burger I've had. Â Came with the fries with roasted garlic in them.. Â great touch.
