Houston's is one of the few chains that does it right - and does it right at all of their locations. Although this isn't under the same name, Hillstone is part of the Houston's chain, just under a different name in NYC (because we're all too snoody and don't go to chains!). The bar is a great place to have a couple drinks - cool jazz band, nice atmosphere. No problem to wait for a table in this place. For the food, it's all good. I crushed the ribs and spinich dip - and they were awesome. It's a really cool joint and exactly what I remember Houston's being like out West - love it.

Went with a small group of friends and we shared about five or six different menu items including the steaks, avocado fries, and more but i have a memory lapse right now, but all were so good! it's not cheap but it's a good meal overall. Â the sangria was deli-sh but watch out, it's super strong!

Came here when it first opened...they didn't even have a food menu yet cause that's how new they were to the neighborhood...ordered and Espresso...and BOY was it STRONG...sure woke me up since I worked a flew blocks away...will do edit this review once I go back and taste the food...

wow, date cake was truly amazing. Â ask for it. loved the decor, felt so rustic. other than that.... no bread...always kind of ticks me off. lamb was too gamey, i almost threw up. quail is UBER small, don't think about sharing. we ordered 3 entrees and brussel sprouts hoping to share between 3 people, portions were too small. Â definitely get at least one appetizer and one entree for yourself without sharing. on a weird side note...is it normal that when you walk downstairs to the bathroom there is a random guy sitting by the staircase playing the harmonica??

OMG. Â This place makes me want to give up my comfortable life in suburban DFW and move to an apt across the street from them. We were in NYC for only a few days but I made sure this place secured a spot on our "must go" list. Â That meant we had to take a subway from Midtown, but we don't mind that generally. Â It was cold and windy and the long 5-6 blocks from the station to the restaurant almost got us to ditch the plan and stop at Peter Lugar's. Â So glad we didn't. We were told it would be a half hour wait and she showed us to a little corner at the end of the bar where we could stay out of the way and not be outside in the cold. Â Eventually, seats at the bar opened so we grabbed those and ordered wine. Â They offered to feed us at the bar but since we had already waited 15 of our 30 minutes and the bar stools aren't very comfy, we opted to wait for a table. Â In the end we waited an hour because there was this one table of three who WOULD NOT LEAVE. Â I mean, really people. Â Lingering over coffee and dessert is fine after a nice meal. Â But they sat there another 30-40 minutes after paying the bill. One of them actually leaned back and put their feet up. Â  The hostess apologized and I told her I just feel bad for the waiter who isn't able to flip that table... Anyway, we finally got our seats after she went and asked them to vacate. Â  The waiter jotted down the menu and we were so hungry by this point we were afraid we'd order too much. Â He helped us decide what a reasonable amount of food was, and what we ended up with was the perfect amount. Â There were three of us and for starters we shared a bowl of nettle soup (WOW) and Â linguine with I think a wild boar ragu (AMAZING. ) Â For mains we had Â two orders of pork belly and an order of short ribs. Â I can't recall what all the veggies were on the pork belly... potatoes and I don't know, something yummy. Â Mine, the short ribs, came with parsnip puree and fiddle head ferns. Â So that was two new foods for me in one meal (nettles and fiddle heads.) Â  We had one of each dessert... A greek yogurt thing with candied kumquats, a flourless chocolate cake and I honestly can't remember the third one. Â Whatever it was, I know we ate it all and giggled like children. Â  I'll have to ask hubby and update later. Anyway, five stars for such an inspired meal, even though we waited over an hour when we were told a half hour and we missed the last M train to our hotel. Â  No accounting for some people's children.

OH YEAAAAAAHHHH. Â An awesome beat-up diner yields a plethora of culinary delights. Â Definitely pricey, but worth every penny. Â The aesthetic here is awesome too, and it's fun to people watch. Â The bar is cool, and relatively speaking drink prices won't kill you. This place is fucking awesome. Â Babe waitresses gently pen the menu on your table in a beautiful calligraphy (jkz they scribble it !) for you to read. Â The only thing on the set menu is a crazy ass burger waiting to mess you up with pleasure. Roast chicken in restaurants oftentimes resembles a dried out basketball, but here it is incredibly succulent and tender. Â Lots of butter is my guess. Â The heirloom tomatoes were not a lie but in fact wonderful. The swordfish filet was light and flavorful with an amazing tomato and caper side. Â Kale rounded it out nicely, the perfect secret ingredient to add to the magikul cauldron from whence the feast came. Â They spice to enhance, not to mask. Â Subtle flavors and stealth meats. Wine pours were not as big as I would have hoped at $9 for the cheapest glass, but the gruner was from my favorite producer and was fresh, dry, and made a great wingman to my fishsss. Didn't try dessert, but that will come next time. Â And every time after that. Â Forever. Â Amen.
Warning: The crispy pork will change your life.
We used to love this place bit it's gotten spotty. Old croissants and stale white bread toast for breakfast..really?!? A great classic beginning to falter.

Great pizza cooked in a 1000F wood fired oven for less than a minute. Very authentic and delicious. The Caesar salad was tasty and served with whole romaine and anchovies. Small candlelit dining room makes an excellent date spot.

Updating my review... My friend lives so close to this place so I had to stop by and eat here again. Â Plus, I wanted my boyfriend and friends to try Empanada Mama because I liked it so much the first time. I tried the spicy tuna empanada and it was so bomb. Â Flavorful and it had that extra kick to it. Â My new fave at Empanada Mama!! I hated the wait though... we came around 10PM and we still waited 30MIN+

The meatballs are A-OK. Had the classic w/ parmesan cream sauce, braised kale and polenta. Everything was good, but if I had to pick a meatball to rave about, it'd be the ones at Sora Lella. What I will rave about are the ice cream sandwiches. Yeah, it was 25F outside, but it was crowded and warm inside. We split a caramel ice cream w/ chocolate chip and brownie cookie sandwich, and an eggnog w/ peanut butter and gingersnap cookie sandwich. This is what'll get me back here, especially when it gets warm enough to get take out and eat outside.
Awesome place for the potato lovers... Other foods are also good..

Being a regular at a Little Collins in Amsterdam, I thought I should probably try out this Little Collins as well, even though they are not related... I had a coffee and the Big Dill breakfast sandwich here. The Big Dill was not really huge and not big on dill, it was alright, but did not have a whole lot of flavor. Â The other item on the menu I wanted to try was The Smash. Â It looked pretty tasty, but, alas, I discovered it too late in the trip to try again. The coffee was really good and the staff is friendly and takes care of the clients. Â Definitely a small place, I think seating for 14 people, maybe... The experience was good, but I'll need to stop in again when I am in New York and try a different breakfast option.

Oh Wafels and Dinges, you remind me how much I love Brussels! This simple snack is great for one person, or to share. I'm a simple girl, so my favorite thing to get here is the Liege Wafel, a soft and chewy waffle, with nutella and bananas. This delicious treat can get sticky, so be sure to pick up a few extra napkins! If you don't have much of a sweet tooth, don't fret. They also carry a few savory options for you to enjoy. This travelling gem on wheels can be found all over the city. If you haven't had any luck stumbling upon them, go to their website. You'll find the days, times and cross streets of where they'll be.

Very cool place, beautiful inside, 2 levels and outside tables. We had a brunch for 5 there. I had huevos rancheros - very decent portion size - and a couple of spicy bloody maries, 1 included with the main course. The waiter was pretty awesome too. Point off for the unisex restrooms: if the place is full (and it was due to cinco de mayo) - you ll be standing in line.

I've been wanting to try this place for a while now. A couple friends and I were in the neighborhood and decided to do a late brunch. The wait wasn't long and we were able to get good table. The menu looked really tasty and I wasn't sure what to order. I was starving and a burger sounded really good. I opted on getting the Original with a fried egg on it. For $10 you get a juicy burger with a generous portion of fries. Not too shabby. The only flaw I had was that the egg was way over cooked. Before our waitress(really sweet) left I just made sure that it's going to be "runny yolk". She said that it was. Once I got it and started eating it. I noticed that the yolk wasn't runny at all and about cooked through. I didn't want to send back a 1/2 eaten burger so I just went with it. I just wished I broke the yolk before hand to check it out. Other than that it was a very good meal. The $6 Micheladas were refreshing as well. All in all it's a cool place to grab brunch without breaking the bank.

Transported to a grand brasserie on a Parisian Boulevard; that is how I have felt every time I have come to Balthazar. Â And that has not been nearly is enough over twenty or so years. As a vegetarian, there really isn't that much of a selection of food (omelet, croque monsieur) but the overall experience is fantastic. Â Excellent, old school professional service, upbeat ambiance, and plenty of time to eat a fanatic meal. Go on an off time to get a good table and stay a while.

I really enjoyed Smorgasburg Mighty Quinn but I just couldn't love their store. The employees are super friendly! It might be that at Smorgasburg it's more fresh and delicious straight out of the oven whereas in the restaurant they seem to have heated up.

I was on date with my bf, First time we sat downstairs, waitress was very sweet and helpful we had really good time, second time we sat upstairs with live music, worst thing ever!! First they took forever to get our order ready, second food sucked!! Too salty and service sucked as well. Going to try one more time because I love Nepali food and my bf is from Nepal. Hope it was only one time thing.

Ideal for a group dinner...cozy yet vibrant ambience with a manageable noise level. Â Good cocktails - especially the Spanish Manhattan. Â  The fried goat cheese, bacon wrapped dates and the paella were highlights. Â Knowledgeable staff and attentive service. The torija is a must-try - it was such a hit, our table ordered two.
Almost exactly like Bar Toto, but the food and service are both even better. I guess that kind of makes up for the fact that the area of the neighborhood isn't as cute.

Nice and friendly counter guy, but what's the big deal? Got my egg sandwich. Â  Hmm...didn't get any free coffee as advertised on Yelp! That's odd. And you know...I'm too shy to ask. How very un-NY'er like of me. Cool counter space. Â Great place for pancakes on a snowy morning, if you can go into work late. It's ok, but lots of options for this type of food elsewhere.

I'm no connoisseur for Greek food but this place is pretty good. Great atmosphere and excellent service. Waiter recommend a decent bottle of wine. The octopus and grilled scallops were very good. The sea bass w/ pistachios is a great mix. Dessert is reasonably priced. The greek yogurt is mixed well.
We had the shami kebab, chicken tikka roll and unda Aldo roll, as well as mango lassi. It was delicious! Only $5-6 per portion. Portions are not big. Delicious! Definitely coming back

I don't have much to say since everyone has spoken for me! Awesome. Good. Cheap. There was more food then I can finish! They have 2 carts. One on each side of the street. My bf was making fun of the people who were in the long line that stretched the entire street while we went to the shorter line on the other side, it's the same company people!
Good brunch, good breakfast. Great bloody maries.

I am a bit conflicted about writing this review. My experiences at Beyoglu have been overwhelmingly positive for the most part. The food, while not the best in town, is good enough and cheap enough to make me keep going back. My last experience, however, will make me think twice about returning. Upon walking into the restaurant this past weekend (following the snow storm), the slope to get into the restaurant was covered in an icy water. Without any visible signs or warnings, I stepped onto the slope and fell pretty hard coming into the restaurant. The manager, instead of expressing any concern, immediately said, "we have a caution sign over there!" The caution sign was placed about 10 feet from the entrance, and this remark showed me the manager's concern was only about the potential of me taking legal action against the restaurant, rather than whether or not I hurt myself. We were immediately ushered to a table and then ignored for the rest of the meal by the management. Nobody came over to check on us, ask if I was ok, or offer anything to repay the situation (free drink, appetizer, dessert, etc.). The treatment by the Beyoglu staff left me with a sour taste in my mouth, and the food itself does not make up for it so much that this will be my go-to. I'm very disappointed in this situation, as I have most likely dined at Beyoglu 30+ times and have recently moved even closer to the restaurant. Unfortunately, I will most likely be finding another Mediterranean go-to. So long, Beyoglu.
After eating at the typical expensive NY eateries, it's good to grab a $5 bowl of noodles. The noodles were super fresh and the soup was perfect. It's a bowl of love.

Oy, i ate so much when i went here last weekend. Â The dishes are tiny, but deceptively filling. Â Or maybe we just ordered a lot. Â It's japanese small plates essentially, and accordingly I recommend going with a group to get to taste a bunch of the dishes. Â  LOVES: the agedashi tofu melts in your mouth. Â the cold soba is perfectly cooked. Â Hirame Carpaccio - the fluke, roe and shiso combo is magical. Â Kimchee sashimi rice bowl - one of the more filling options and i can't say no to kimchee, ever. Â Spinach - delicious but teeny tiny. Â Black Sesame Cream Brulee - great sesame crunch. Â  SO-SOS: the eggplant 3 styles - I tried two of them: LOVED one and the other was just ok. Â  Mashed Potato in Donut Batter - conceptually super exciting but didn't taste much like potato and I wished the dip was sugar, not salt. Â  MEHS: the chocolate dessert special - it was not that good and had some fruit cocktail thrown on top. Â  Overall, a fantastic meal with a lot to excite the palate. Â Service was also outstanding. Â We had a water spill and a server showed up with a dishcloth in literally seconds. Â They have ESP. Â What a great find!
I loved their soup dumplings. so good.

J'taime! We came into this place after Bouley's stopped serving lunch. That was quite alright with me as there was way too much eye candy in there and i needed my man to stay focused on his salad. So, thank you Odeon for being slow with unattractive patrons - except for us, of course! I had quite a nice Malbec paired with the ever so amazing, delicious, and heavenly croque monsieur with a side salad. I believe this is the first time ever that my side salad was paired perfectly with my main. What i mean is that the salad dressing had the same hint, taste, as in the Â taste of my sandwich. They were both different 'sauces' but were prepared oh so nicely. This was hands down the best croque monsieur that i have ever devoured. The molten chocolate cake was a nice addition as well..dont forget the hazelnut ice cream!

What an amazing delicious Italian treat nestled on a quiet tree lined street. Â We came in on a Friday night, and were able to grab seats at the bar with no problem. Â Our bartender/server, Giovanni, was amazing. Â He started us off with some lovely bubbles, and helped make recommendations for some great starters. Â  There wasn't calamari on the menu, but he checked with the chef and had some made especially for us. Â The handmade fettuccine bolognese was the highlight of the evening for me. Â I can't wait to eat here again, and will definitely request Gio!!!

Saw this a couple years ago written up as the best burger in NYC. Â  At about 6 bucks, the price was right but the cheeseburger tasted like any regular burger I could make from regular old supermarket meat. Â  Nothing tasty at all. Â Not bad, but I've definitely had much better burgers. Fries at Â 3 bucks served as a tiny paper plate of skinny fries that look just like McD's but don't even come close to that excellent taste. Â Skip. On the plus side: Â service was fast, atmosphere with the Christmas lights was super cozy and great.

This review is based on a limited, drinks-only visit, so take it for what it's worth. I will also say that I have no experience with the well-known establishment that formerly occupied this space, so luckily I have no pre-existing prejudices in that regard. My main gripe with this establishment is the vibe, which just seems...off, somehow. Â While the space is tastefully appointed, it lacks character and instead feels sterile, like the show-floor in a upscale furniture store. Â To me, it seems the owners tried a bit too hard to create an environment that, even were it successfully executed, would frankly feel out of place in this neighborhood. Â And though I have never visited their other nearby joint Parlor Steakhouse, I feel reasonable sure I would get a similar impression. Â  The crowd was likewise disjointed: Â a mix of casually dressed patrons elbow-to-elbow with the decidedly more fashion-forward. Â Nothing wrong with that per se, but there was a distinct lack of 'buzz' in the room, the kind you would get if all the elements were jiving. Â One particularly jarring element: Â a restaurant designed to invoke some kinship with the written word has two large, glaring flatscreen TVs behind the bar. As for the drinks, they were of the type and quality you would expect at a place that is more interested in style over substance. Â The Manhattan I ordered wasn't particularly enticing and was expensive to boot. Â As I mentioned, I didn't try any of the food, but I will say that the menu smacks of your typical modern American cuisine. Â Oh, and if I was in the mood for a $50+ piece of meat, this would not be the place I would go. I will say that our server was cheerful and attentive. Â But overall, I can't see myself becoming a repeat customer.

blah blah blah ANTLERS ON THE WALL blah blah surly waitress blah blah ADORABLE COBBLESTONE ALLEYWAY blah blah predictable appetizer blah blah RUSTIC HUNTING CHIC blah blah salty entree blah blah DRIZZLED SUNDRIED THINGS blah blah inattentive hostess blah blah THIS MUST BE WHAT LIBRARIES ARE LIKE blah blah irritable staff mediocre food coasting on a bygone reputation BUT LOOK AT THE STUFFED PHEASANT IN THE CORNER. Save yourself a hundred bucks and buy your own damn antlers.

This pizza is intense - but in a pretty good way. It's more like artichoke dip on top of bread than pizza in my mind. Definitely a good idea to share the signature artichoke Â and the Sicilian to counter some of the extreme creaminess of the artichoke pizza. I like that this location has more seating in addition to offering slices. Good for late night as well as lunch or dinner.

We always love this place for great Italian food. We took my friends parents from Rome here when they visited and gave it a thumbs up. So you know its pretty good. I actually liked it better when it was a cozy restaurant in the west village but it has made a good transition still welcoming and consistently producing great Italian fare. My only one gripe is that the food can sometimes be over salted.

I really really like it here. Â  From the times I've been here, the place is wildly popular, and understandably so. Â There seem to be a lot of complaints going on, but having been to Morini several times, I have basically nothing to complain about. Â Save for the one time this weird bouncer-looking guy was weird to me at the front, and I guess he worked there, but I'm not sure, and it was overall an awkward 35 seconds. Then we were seated. Â No biggie. Â  Addressing some concerns...I guess it's fairly expensive (though not relative to the neighborhood, or anywhere in this city), I guess it's tough to get a table, I know it can be loud, but seriously, how do you not like the food? Â And for people complaining about portion sizes, jesus god, how much do you eat? Â We ordered a plate with selection of salumi, and swear to god there was 50,000 calories on the plate, not including bread. Â A delicious 50,000 calories, but still an obscene amount of food that was difficult to split between three of us. Â I see one complaint about there being a few slices of cheese on a cheese plate. Â Have you ever ordered cheese at a nice restaurant? Â It's served per piece. Always. Â Shutup. Onto the things I've ordered. Â I mentioned the salumi plate. Â This was incredible. Â The bread they serve is excellent, rustic and crunchy. Â The meats we ordered were the Speck, the Lardo (I think), and the Fegatini (duck liver). Â I think it was Sam Sifton who said, you can spackle a room with the amount of duck liver. Â It's true, container full of pure fat. But it's good. Â So good, my friend who turned up his nose when I suggested ordering it, feigning disgust, was practically digging it out with his fingers after I made him try it. Â  If you're looking at the apps, I've had the Polpettine every time I come here. Â It comes with more bread, I think, and is an awesome saucey plate of meatballs. Â The sauce, speckled with cheese, is delightful, especially for scooping with extra bread. Â Should be the first go-to. Â Last time I was here, I ordered the calamari. Â This was a small dish (fine, but it's an app), but it was seared really well and had a lot of flavor. Â For the record, I like calamari almost any way, whether deep fried along side canned marinara, or actually made in an interesting way. Â This was the interesting kind. Â Not an appetizer, but I've also ordered the brussels sprouts. Â Not the best brussels sprouts ever, but still a yummy side bowl that masquerades as healthy (certainly the "healthiest" thing I've ordered here). The pastas. Â Oh, the pastas. Â When here, this should be your focus. Â Like any of Michael White's pastas, these are heavy and heavenly. Â I ordered the tagliatelle with the ragu my first time here. Â I've ordered it every time since. Â It's awesome. Â Super filling, the ragu is delicious, and it gets wrapped up in perfect forkfuls with the tagliatelle. Â Love it. Â So much, it's #2 on my best pastas ever list, the first being the Marrow and Octopus pasta at another White establishment (Marea). Â Other pastas to consider -- the garganelli (pasta quills with cream) and gnocchi Â are delightful, but not to be ordered over the ragu. Â The last trip, my bf ordered some special pasta. Â I think it was rabbit something or other ragu, can't remember. Â I remember it tasting good and looking better than the usual ragu. Â It wasn't though. In addition to the mains, every time we come here, we've ordered a bottle of red. Â There are some decent options, which are pretty reasonable. Â The waiters tend to be moderately helpful here, though I think there's room for improvement. Â I don't think we've ever gotten dessert, and come to think of it, have never bothered with a main. Â So I guess this is a top review based on meatballs, ragu, pasta, and plates of salumi. Â Whatever, it's good stuff.

After 15 years, still never disappoints. Â Fresh ingredients; efficient service; warm friendly propietors; phenomenal pasta selection; delicious pizzas; tasty entree specials; fesh salad; great appetizers; yummy desserts; sensible/reasonable wine prices .... Get the picture? It's a home run for good food, good vino, good service at a super reasonable price. Â  Now I have a hankering for some Farfalle de Spiaggia, Fettucine Buttera, Black Taglierini, Taglierini Sorrento, Cappelini Limone, Papperdelle Funghi, Tortellini Boscaiola, Minestrone, Pureed Carrot Soup, Pizza Esotica, Tartufo, Tiramisu ... that's the biggest "problem" there, making a choice!

Very, very good! After finally trying this place (seems like every time I wanted to go there was a line or totally packed, which to me doesn't necessarily mean the place is good) we came in for early dinner around 6 pm, no crowd.. Sangria was excellent, lots of fruit, little ice, tasty! Â Hummus app was good, pita bread and regular table bread was excellent, and I'm not a bread fan.. I had the chicken cutlet with spaghetti on side in marinara sauce. the cheese was melted perfectly, 3 big ass chicken titties cooked to perfection (often overcooked in chick parm) and lots of sauce (which usually places never give enough IMO).. I gave it my 3S meal (stuffed, satisfied and sleepy)! My girl had eggplant sando, but didn't like it. I'm not a big fan of moulinyan unless it's cooked perfect, which it was.. she didn't care for it much, but she's real picky, adds so much salt to everything.. However, I must say I had to add salt to everything. I'm not sure if they don't add salt purposely, but all the dishes needed a little. I'd rather have to add it myself than have it over salted like many places do so you order more drinks, but they need to add more salt, a little more.. Great service, good atmosphere, I will certainly be back and recommended!

Stopped here after i realized they don't serve slices at Grimaldis. Well, they don't serve slices here at Julianna's either. What they do serve is an awesome margarita pizza and very nice hospitality. A gentleman convinced us to split a small pizza between the two of us. It was a little too much for me as I was trying to save room to for a few bites at an Elite event down the street. The pizza came out piping hot and perfectly crusty. I ate my crust. I don't know if it was the best pizza I ever had but it was definitely up there and the staff was so nice I had to write a review. The decor was super cute. Great place for a casual date.

I've been here three times now. The first two times were outstanding; this past visit was so, so disappointing. What made this restaurant unique was that it wasn't just another high-priced tapas restaurant. It had some truly delicious food with a gorgeously romantic ambiance. Now, all the dishes that stood out (razor clams, fideos rossejat rapida) have been "transitioned off the menu". During our most recent visit we tried some new dishes to us which included the foie gras, and their pulpo dish. "Meh" all around. The foi gras was more or less bland and the pulpo was just not a fave of mine. We of course ordered the paella, which truthfully is just not their jam. I prefer mine a bit more crispy, plus I bit into too much chicken gristle as well as a bone (yuck). Of course this place is spectacular on a summer's night. They open the roof and you're surrounded by freshly cut flowers. But, My hubby and I resolved that our fave restaurant is no longer our fave, and we will alas never return :(

My two experiences at Basso were pretty different from each other, but I will still give it 5 stars based on the spectacular, completely memorable dinner we had the first time dining at Basso. I think if you order what you know is good (I did my research on yelp the first time -- lobster crepes and duck!) you will have a fantastic meal that you will remember and savor for weeks (or months) to follow. Last time, we wanted to be slightly more adventurous and tried uncharted territory (at least on yelp). At the last minute, I veered away from the duck (MUST GET) and chose a striped bass filet instead. Big mistake. It was a very mediocre dish. My boyfriend had the grilled lamb chops, which was pretty good, but nothing fantastic. I was more disappointed with the fish as I expected a clean and refreshing dish, but ended up with overall blandness. I think it lacked some acidity -- I remember squeezing the lemon over the fish and still thinking it was just... meh. Scallops were okay... but again, the carpaccio was probably a better choice for appetizer. The chocolate crepes were soooo good though! Maybe I just have a weakness for Basso's crepes, savory or sweet. I kept eating it, even though it was completely smothered in dark chocolate and I was dying of a sugar overdose. Basso can be truly one of the best meals (at this price point) in the city if you know what the right dishes are, but I can also see why yelpers were underwhelmed with their dishes and expecting better Italian fare given the wonderful reviews. Oh also, one last note (very important at that). Try the sangria. That is all.

All I can say is great food & great service. Â One of the co-owners waiting on us and he made the evening fun and personable. Â The food was adventurous and delicious. Â I ordered the snapper with yucca fries. Â Crazy good! Â Deep fried whole fish with a onion/lemon salsa and fish row on the head. Â Fries were hardy and perfectly cooked. Â The steak was buttery and melt in your mouth. Â Atmosphere was happy, even if I personally like the music a little bit lower. Â My water glass was never empty... service was excellent. Â Overall, for an ecclectic neighborhood place, it doesn't get much better.

We went out of our way to come here, it was a weekday and a beautiful, warm October day, 10 minute wait at most. Once we got seated, we scanned the menu and were excited to order and finally try this place out. Since my two friends and I were all ordering the same ramen, with one variation- one bowl without pork belly, it would be easier to just have one person order, simple enough right? Wrong. As I was ordering, in the middle of my sentence, the server cut me off, held her hand up at me, looked at my friends and said- "Wait, let me ask them what they want." Whoa. Speechless. Not sure how to react to that one except it killed my entire once-excited-feeling. She gets the title for being the rudest person to ever take my order. She made me feel extremely incompetent. I was speaking in plain English, lady, not sure what her problem was. I couldn't help but think- Did I stutter, was I talking too slow, too fast? In tongue? She rarely came to our table to check up on us. And in our small interactions with her, like - 'Hi, can we please have some more water?' She didn't say a word, just really cold. Really bizarre. We observed her at other tables, she was smiling and jolly with the other male patrons, even kneeled down to explain the menu offerings. The ramen came and it was unmemorable, in all honesty, I've had better. Sure the bowls are big but it doesn't mean the raman was filled to the brim, the taste wasn't there and its really too expensive for such a mediocre meal. So the experience was terrible and off putting. I decided not to tip on my share... there's a first for everything. My friends were free to do what they wished since the rudeness wasn't directed toward them. We head down to use the bathroom before heading out. As I was using the lady's room, I hear the server interrogate my friends outside the door, saying its customary to tip 20% in nyc. My gfs explained the situation and how she was being rude. I come out, asked if there is a problem but she just walked away. #1 - I understand how tipping works. #2 - I understand what customary means. #3 Customary is not mandatory. Trust me lady, I worked in a Japanese restaurant in college, when someone doesn't tip 20%, heck I've had people tip my colleagues 0%, you just move on. Get over it. People have reasons for tipping, its a personal preference. Â  To chase people down and question why we didn't tip 20%, ON top of the ridiculously poor service, is really something else. We spoke with the manager and he said he'll have a meeting with her. I wish I knew her name, it was a Japanese name. The hype was overrated. To say she was unprofessional is an understatement. Never coming back. Try Totto Ramen instead, they are 10x better on every level imaginable. Â  And that's all I have to say about that Â -Forest Gump.

An extremely fashionable place to eat your weekend brunch at.. It's hip, and tons of celebrities and fashionistas are aware of that. Â I've eaten here many, many times and have found everything very tasty, and plates come out fast. The coffee and teas are amazing - but with one barista you sometimes don't get them till you're finished your meal. (I've actually toted some bottled water once or twice in preparation for it..) There are 4 tables outside that seat 3 each, and they're very friendly to puppies - they even allow you to sneak them indoors if you assure them they'll stay firmly in the bag (how french!). The wait time can be tedious though at prime times. Also to note - cash only.

Bustan was all booked up on a Friday night. We nearly left but the hostess encouraged us to hang in for two at the bar, which is really just a another dining area anyway. That worked out. The package rates the four stars. Here's the details: Mazettim, single (hummus), 5: served with freshly baked flat bread; excellent and distinctive - you just think you've had hummus until you've had this hummus! I suspect there's some high-quality olive oil in there Lamb shwarma, 9.5: packed into two nifty chinese-style buns, tasty (someone posted a photo) Mushroom flatbread (pizza), 13.95: more of the flat bread, smothered in cheese, mushrooms, duck pastrami, tasty, but I wouldn't order it and a mazettim at the same meal top shelf whiskey, 15: Won't happen again with me. chardonnay, 14 TOTAL: 69.45 HERE is the promised second-visit update. We returned to the hummus mazettim (though we received the bowl by mistake). The rating holds firm. We'll be back. Some deets: Burrata, 13.5: really delightful and different than what I've had at other restaurants. Squid a la plancha, 10.5: nicely charred, a little chewy, a tasty tomato-based sauce, served over something I can only describe as Texas Toast - the bread is everywhere! even if it was a good sop for the sauce Whole baked branzino, 28.5: very well spiced and cooked with crispy skin and flavorful meat sauvignon blanc, 12 TOTAL: 86.6 New visit ... New deets! (19 Jul 14) We had smaller appetites - here's what we did: Mazetim, single, smoked eggplant $6 Hummus bowl with tandoori chicken $16 Greek salad $15 With booze ... TOTAL: 61 - and not too much bread! Shout outs to Scott and Elena for making us feel welcome BONUS: Good decor! BONUS: The staff wants you to return! BONUS: Promising outdoor space in back BONUS: The hummus from the Mazzetim selections at $5 is a good value SHOUT OUT: Some of the best hummus anywhere, anytime. It might be a lot of tahini. TIP: Booze seemed pricey, especially the "craft beer" list with some selections at $10. Beer at $9 was hard to swallow. I'm on a boycott! TIP: Make a booking! Probably inadvisable to go without one and there's really no where to wait TIP: Order carefully to avoid getting a lot of bread SHOUT OUT to Scott for keeping a couple of bar seats for us when we ran over on a Saturday around 730 PM for our second visit
I love ropa vieja and the barman.

Went to Sunday brunch with my boyfriend. Such a great experience! Excellent food and amazing service. Special thanks to Carlos who was very patient and accommodating (we came with our cocker spaniel Charlie). Don't be put off by the line outside, it's totally worth it. Five stars!! Highly recommended! We'll be back.

I stopped by for a cappuccino because the cafe where I barista uses the same Counter Culture beans, and it's good stuff. Unfortunately the espresso in my drink tasted over-extracted, and the whole thing was very meh. Cool looking space though.

Love this place! Came here three times already this month and perfect all those times! Dan dan noodles, dry pepper chicken, and cumin style beef are really good. Not sure how they do this, but dan dan noodles & dry pepper chicken are so addicting....! Service is good, too. Quick, fast and reasonably nie service.

Tucked away underground, Sakagura is a hidden gem of a Japanese restaurant. Upon finally reaching the end of the stairs, you'll be greeted with an amazing ambiance that only a Japanese restaurant can really prepare for it's customers. Walls lined with fine sake and plum wine and Japanese businessmen hurrying in from work to cheer a beer. From the clientele and servers, you know this place is a legitimate Japanese restaurant. Â  I just had Salmon Roe and Ume Onigiri and one of the specials of the day (Soba with Sea Urchin). It was one of the few times I've had sea urchin, and to those who haven't had it before, it's a bit hard to explain. Imagine a melt-in-your-mouth piece of salmon sashimi, ground into a fine buttery paste and that only touches the surface of flavor your taste buds will enjoy. Staff and waiter were friendly enough. For such a place, Japanese is obviously their first language so you may have to repeat your order once or twice, but they are helpful no matter what. I saw two Caucasian businessmen who seemed very new to sake and the waiter seemed quite helpful to them in explaining the different varieties and what they may enjoy. Overall, the decor enough leaves for an unforgettable dining experience. The food will set you back about $20-50+, but for a place like this it is definitely worth your money. They certainly don't have Japanese restaurants like this back in Southern California, so if you're ever out in New York and what authentic Japanese food, definitely try out Sakagura!

This place is ok. It's cheap, but everything is so small you have to buy like 2-3 things per person. The place is dirty and the kitchen is gross. The food is decent and I wouldn't say don't go, but it's not the greatest place.

My favorite piece of chicken is the butt. Â So delicious, a must try. Makes the next juiciest chicken you've ever had anywhere else look dry. I've never dropped 50 dollars on CHICKEN and I didn't even regret it.

I had to take my review down a star. Service is still great and the roll of the month for March was amazing. What wasn't good? The bland coconut curry soup base! Oh man, I was so disappointed. I am going to give it another try with the miso base next time. It's called beyond sushi, because the sushi is good. I will say the sweet potato black bean brownie is AWESOME!

Pretty good place. I had the challah french toast with a side of bacon. The french toast was delicious. All featured dishes come with an orange juice and coffee or tea (they have decaf). I wasn't a big fan of the mint tea. Also, doesn't take reservations for brunch on the weekend, but expect to wait at least 20 minutes for a table. The place is bigger inside than it looks, but tables are close together so it's cozy.

right across Citigroup's building, so it's really convenient spot to dine with clients here. Italian flavor, the inside is just totally European feel (laid-back but somewhat serious). Mostly elder people, nicely dressed. Food is proper but nothing would wow you. Even disregarding the price tag, I actually didn't enjoy the meal there that much. Service is fast and efficient, somehow surprises me.

Love the mulled cider, love sitting by the windows, love the atmosphere, and Ross is a super nice bartender! I need to go durring the day for coffee/brunch time. Another great bar by the Jefferson stop!

This place is quite a find. Went here with a friend who works in the same neighborhood. the ambiance is very interesting. You walk in through a curtain. The bar is kind of dark which adds to the whole effect. We had a group of about 7 and sat at a long table in the back. The beer menu is quite extensive and delicious. The waitress was very helpfull and they had 2 dollar mini burgers and dollar hot dogs. Both were delicious. The mustard was home made and the burgers were really awesome. I would bring people here. very cool spot.

First the food. Â After finding this place with is tucked down the stairs from the street, I had the truffle melt with tater tots and dipping sauce. Â The melt was great and tater tots were way better than the lunch room variety. Â The service however was flat. Â On the menu they had a special which I ordered and they charged me full price for all. Â When I pointed this out they just said their menu was out of date and the new menu would be fixed. Â Ummmm, I could have cared less what a new menu is going to say, and sadly they didn't bother to refund the overage. Â For being crappy with customer service Melt Shop, the 2 star is yours.

I absoluteley love Employees Only, it is probably one of my favorite bars in the world; rivaling strong contenders from Stockholm, Berlin, and Cannes. EO brings that great New York vibe into my that list, and it's awesome drinks paired with friendly, funny, but most of all professional bartenders bring it to the top of said list. It was a long time since I tried the food, and to be honest, I was probably pretty drunk when I did, so let's leave that for now. My favorite drink here is the BIllionaires; a serious cocktail with bourbon and absinthe bitters. Late night chicken soup and PJ-Sundays add a divey portion of fun to an otherwise elegant and sophisticated bar that somehow feels just right. The only negative thing I could think of is that the drinks can be somewhat inconsistent depending on which bartender you go to. Perhaps its because of all that Fernet we're having though...

Amazing restaurant. Middle Eastern is one of my favorite cuisines and this place really nails it. The Lamb Shawarma is out of this world. Incredibly tasty with a lot of spices and flavors to awaken the taste buds. The Falafels also have incredibly delicious spices in them. The Hummus is is very creamy and smooth. The Kefta Kebab has a nice kick to it. The Baklava is one of the best I have ever had. The portion sizes on the platters are enormous, especially for the sides. The staff is incredibly friendly and helpful.

Although service was terrific and the vibe pretty great...being your typical BK hipster hangout (which I love by the way), unfortunately the food fell a bit shorter than my expectations given all of the great yelp reviews. Had the pulled pork appetizer (forget the name - something jam) and it was pretty good when smeared across the sesame seed cracker and topped with the pickeled onions it came with. Booker T. burgers for my sister and I (reg burger topped with a piece of fried chicke), and for my mom another burger that they had on their list of daily specials (was just a reg burger with an onion ring on top). All three burgers, although juicy, were extremely bland. Collard greens on the side was honestly the best part of the meal...my mom and sister second that emotion.

Typical of what you'd expect from the usual lower east side restaurant: small place, long lines, and delicious food. I would have to say this place met my expectations. I've been waiting and waiting to check this place out and usually long waits equates impatience and high expectations, but i left enjoying my breakfast. Get the pancakes and lather with butter. Order the southern breakfast (FRIED GREEN TOMATOES..CHEESE GRITS, yum) and enjoy.
Good wine, good food, but a little overpriced given the small portions of the dishes. Did enjoy my visit there, though - will probably go back for some more drinks, not food, though.
Just got a chance to dine here last night. It was almost a full house. Had a great dinner experience. Great food, and great service. Two thumbs up.

I've been coming here for almost ten years, and I just love it. Â The convenience, the variety, the yummy food. Â I love that I can pop in at any time and just grab something to go, and it will be delicious. Â It's part nostalgia, certainly, but I love it.

I love spicy food so I ordered the Karaka Men. Â We were starving so we also ordered the Hirata Buns (Pork Buns everyone on yelp raved about). Â Overall, I really enjoyed the ramen. Â It was very flavorful and I loved the texture of the noodles (kind of chewy!). Â The $20/person out the door. Â I guess it's New York but it's RAMEN!!!

Yes! Finally was able to get myself into this place! Called the beginning of the week and was able to land a reservation for the time I wanted on a Friday night! How perfect. Upon arrival the person outside tells us it's fully booked unless we had dinner reservations. Well.. Lucky for us! Walking in you'll see gypsies of fortune tellers around the bar. The back is the dining area, very small too. We had a great corner seat and ordered the bone marrow poppers. This was very good!! Definitely recommend this as an appetizer. I also ordered the duck confit salad and it was probably rated as one of the best salads ever. Comes with a lot of duck meat! And of course don't forget the drinks, they're all great!! This is a great spot for a date night and staff were all so friendly. Love love love employees only.

Uva not only exceeded my wildest expectations, they did so and more! Everything about Uva was top notch and amazing. The waitstaff was very friendly and knowledgeable about the menu. The recommendations were perfect, and our glasses of water were being refilled without having to ask. I started off with the polpettine for my starter (little meatballs). They came immersed in a wonderful marinara sauce with some lightly charred ciabatta bread. I devoured it. Delicious! For the main course, I ordered the pappardelle with veal ragu. It was beyond scrumptious and left me wanting more! My friend enjoyed his veal that was topped with eggplant and pecorino. He kept on saying he wished there was more! Finally, for dessert, the highly recommended hazelnut sponge cake! Fantastic! I enjoyed everything that I placed into my mouth at Uva. I haven't given a 5 star review in a while, but Uva sure deserves it! I promise to be back, sooner than later!

Besides the 'fried' smoke, everything else is just wonderful. Delicious tapas served with a smile. Go for the tuna, and fall in love w/ the lamb! And always, always try the jamon... Yes, I will be back; art gallery first and some tapas later...

Based on all of the great Yelp reviews we decided to try this place out for an early dinner on a Saturday afternoon..and we're so happy we did! The food and service here is phenomenal. Let me first preface that we dropped in around 430ish and were seated right away. There was already a line but for a part of 2 we were seated within a few minutes. This place gets busy, so we got lucky as the wait jumped to an hour plus as we were enjoying our meal..so get there early or be prepared to wait. Yet i digress..ahhh, the food..the menu reflects a fresh Mediterranean menu. We enjoyed the fresh catch of the day perfectly roasted, with fresh herbs and drizzled in olive oil..superb. We also ordered the calamari, cooked to perfection and the Greek salad which was wonderful, a true Greek salad indeed. Each meal is accompanied with toasted bread served with olive oil and even a free dessert..yes, I said free. Most importantly, it's delicious! Sadly I forgot to inquire as to the actual name of the dessert but I do hope that they serve it on my return visit. It was a lovely phyllo dough served with a soft, buttery sweet custard sprinkled with cinnamon, brilliantly simple and delicious. Run don't walk to Taverna Kyclades, just go early so you miss the wait.

Hipsters Would Save $ And Get More Service At Blue Smoke! Fatte Sau was a flat scene. I hope this kind of crap experience never reaches my favorite neighborhoods. My wife and I were shocked at the prices here and embarrassed that we went out of our way to try this place with her Brazilian cousin and his wife who were visiting NYC. We had canceled reservations at Blue Smoke in Manhattan (bad mistake), as we wanted to show our guests what Williamsburg Brooklyn was like. After jumping on the L train, we arrived thirsty for some beer. Each pint of craft beer was $7 a piece, but we really wanted to save one dollar so we opted for 1 gallon (4 pints) of craft beer for $27 + tax (I bought the first gallon so we didn't have to fight over who got to keep the dollar we saved). After a few sips of beer, it was time to order what we came there for. We ordered one half chicken, 3/4 lb of beef brisket, 8 St Louis style ribs (8 ribs, not racks), one pork sausage, 2 corn on the cobs, 1 cup of baked beans, and 1 cup of potato salad. Now guess how much that came to? Total for all of this was $108. Add the $30 for the beer (tax incl) and that comes to $138 + bar/counter tips, or about $35 per person. For a little less, we could have stuck to our Blue Smoke plan and enjoyed a far better dining experience. Below I have broken down the differences between the two restaurants... FATTE SAU Â  Food = Very Good Â  Prices = Expensive Â  Dining Experience = Rustic, primitive Â  Cleanliness = Poor At Fatte Sau, it's cafeteria style, which means they slopped all our food onto one large metal trey, then our party had to self-serve to paper plates. They don't carry / offer communal serving spoons / utensils here. We resorted to pouring the baked beans from the cup onto your plate (?), and we had to double-dip with our forks for more potato salad. We shared a picnic table with strangers who piled up soiled-paper napkins that eventually spilled over into our party's 'zone'. Bussers did not come by to clean or remove garbage until we got up to leave. Waters were self-serve and the cups were a generous 3 ounces, so I/we had to get up from the awkward picnic table seating every time we wanted more water (I'm 6'-4" tall, so it's a challenge to get in/out) . There was nobody refilling our waters (seems like a simple job, right?). One of two bathrooms was "out of order", causing there to be long waits. The people at the food counter had a very take-it-or-leave-it, what-you-see-is-what-you-get attitude when I asked about serving utensils and if there was more chicken and corn coming out (of course there did when we returned to our seats). BLUE SMOKE Â  Food = Very Good Â  Prices = Reasonable ($18-20 main meats, $9 sides, x4 peeps = $96) Â  Dining Experience = Above average (linen napkins, water & bus service, etc) Â  Cleanliness = Very Clean Because of Fatte Sau's poor level of service and overprice items, I WILL NEVER RETURN TO THIS PLACE. I went to Mighty Quinn's BBQ in East Village not long ago, and the prices were way more reasonable (we spent $75 for 3 people), the dining room and bathrooms were clean, and there were people cleaning our table as we ate, refilling our waters, and adding things like more napkins and wet naps. It was just a far better experience. It's your money, treat yourself well.

I believe most of us will be biased toward things we loved when we were young. Â I know McDonald's isn't the healthiest food choice in the world but I will defend their Happy Meals to the death. Â Same goes for Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles, those ridiculous Jansport strings, even more ridiculous Jnco jeans, and Saved by the Bell (even the dreaded new class!). Â This is why I am biased towards this Peking BBQ place. I remember frequenting this chicken place since I was eleven or twelve. Â It looks like another Chinese place except the Chinese guys are from South America and speak fluent Spanish, catering to their best clientele. Â The price used to be like $2.50 for a quarter chicken with fried rice (this is number 3 on their menu). Â The place used to have all the 'hot sauce' that you wanted for free at all the tables. Â The interior was not in the best shape but it had its own flavor. Â  Then, for the business sake, the place underwent a minor transformation to make it look more presentable and use technology to take orders and payments. Â But the food has still remained the same. Â Number 3 now costs $4.70 (inflation time!) and the chicken/rice combo is as good as I remember. Â  The chicken is as popular as it ever was. Â There is usually a line during lunch and dinner time and on Sundays after the Catholic church across the street lets out, a vast crowd forms outside Peking BBQ. Â Most of the clientele are of Latino heritage and if anyone knows rice with chicken, it's the Latinos. Â The food is all that counts in this place and if you are bold enough, try the 'hot sauce' (spoiler alert: not really hot) and the Colombiana drink. Â For me, going back to Peking BBQ brings me back to a time where I wondered why my friends preferred Kelly Kapowski over Jessie Spano (I had a thing for Jessie at the time).

This place is amazing. I love it. It's so versatile. I've been there on a little romantic date and I've been there with a group of friends for a BDay. The decor and space is great ... and cozy. You really can't go wrong with any of the food, but I'll name some of my favorites: Bacon Wrapped Dates & Olives stuffed with almonds (can I order 50 more, please?) Fingerling Potato Saltimbocca Carpaccio Of Beef Tuna Tartare Crispy Brussels Sprouts Â (these are simply divine) Pulled Pork Empanadas Braised Short Rib of Beef The desserts are awesome too - they change a lot though so I didn't bother putting up the ones I had because they aren't there anymore. P.S You can order everything on the menu (The Whole Shebang) for $420.

I was disappointed. Line was outta control so I was expecting something GREAT! Once we were inside the pizza came quickly but it was nothing exciting. Cheese was nasty, crust slightly burnt and the sauce had no redeeming qualities. There has to be better New York pizza out there.

Well, decided to finally give this place a try after seeing crowds for months in front of it. Â When I got there, there was already again a crowd waiting, I put my name down, waited patiently in the line and close to 70min later got a table. So the Ramen are ok, wasn't thrilled, couldn't see any good reason for the crowd except that we're close enough to Times Square and a lot of tourists/hotels which might help to keep the hype up. Â For all the rest of us, spare yourself the wait - there are better and easier options here in town ;-)
The service and food were fantastic. Definitely worth the visit and price.

Dined here this past weekend and really enjoyed the experience. Â Although the place is small and the tables are right on top of each other, the ambiance is laid back and the staff is very friendly. Â  Although complimentary bread is typical at Itallian restaurants, Piccolo Angolo took it one step further and provided both regular Italian bread AND garlic bread on the house. Â The garlic bread was AMAZING, although I would not recommend partaking if you are on a date - especially a first, second or even third date. Â That stuff is STRONG! Â  Between my five friends, we shared the Tricolor salad, the Capresse Salad and the artichoke heart appetizers. Â All were delicious. Â  For my main course, I chose the rigatoni alla vokda. Â It was prepared al dente without being too hard and the "cream" portion of the sauce was very subtle so I didn't feel too guilty about it. Â My friends had the lobster cannoli, chicken parmesan and eggplant paramesan and everyone was pleased. The only reason I did not give this restaurant 4 stars is that I had a very bad stomach ache when I got home as did at least one of my friends. Â As a result, I am slightly hesitant to rush back.

I am not going to go on and on here. In fact, I will apologize as this isn't so much of a review as it is an strong suggestion. GO HERE! If you are in the neighborhood, live near by, or looking for a fabulous spot at the Marcy Avenue J stop. This place has an amazing vibe, and screams chill. I know that "screams chill" may be an oxymoron, or maybe I'm the moron. Doesn't matter. This place is just very cool, and I think anyone who is looking for a warm, relaxing environment to enjoy some good cocktails need not look any further. Small, but solid selection of beers. Reasonably Ryes, and other creative drink concoctions. Cool music, and a great crowd. I didn't eat here, but they do offer a small menu.

The trick to avoiding the massive lines (at least for brunch) is to arrive a few minutes before they open (11:00 a.m.). Â We arrived a few minutes before 11:00 and even though the rest of our party didn't arrive until 11:15 (everyone has to be present to be seated), we had no trouble getting a table. It's definitely pricey for brunch (16-18 an entrÃ©e) and the food is hit or miss. Â Some dishes were absolutely delicious, while others were just okay. Â Let's start with the good: the lemon ricotta pancakes were heavenly and literally melted in my mouth. Â They came just as advertised, complete with toasted almonds that added a perfect crunch. Â The salmon plate (it was a special) was tasty, but very simple (literally lox, onions, capers, parsley and lemon - where were the carbs??). Â Definitely could have made this at home and saved a lot of money. Â We also ordered a whole wheat biscuit that came with honey butter. Â The outside was crispy and delicious, but the inside was undercooked and soggy. Â I had a bite of my friend's grilled cheese, which was heavy, but very yummy. Â The shoestring fries were also a hit with our table. Â I have a soft spot for skinny fries, and these were skinny perfection. Â  The atmosphere is very cute and similar to what I imagine would be the setting for the Mad Hatter's tea party. Â I loved that there were coat hooks next to each table and there was both a high and low hook (it's all in the details!). Â My only gripe decoration wise was the abundance of cute piggy banks/pig pictures - there were cute pigs everywhere and 90% of the menu items featured some sort of pork - does that creep anyone else out? Â It just seems wrong. In sum, get the lemon ricotta pancakes - amazing!! (If half stars were available, I would have given 3 1/2 stars).

The pulled chicken sandwich was flavorful, moist and the BBQ sauce was good. Â The corn muffins were good but overpriced at $4 for a few. Â The mac and cheese was creamy and good, but I don't think it can compare to baked mac and cheese. Â It was also a bit over priced at $4 for a small container. Overall, the quality of food is definitely good, but the value isn't the highest out there. Â Nevertheless, I will be a repeat customer and I'm sure my rating will go up once I try the real BBQ stuff. Astoria is quickly becoming the foodie capital of NYC. Â I might need to move out before I become a total fatso. Ok I tried the burnt ends sandwich - this alone brings it up a star. Â Melts in your mouth and the contrast with the sweetness of the burnt tips with the bbq sauce is outrageous.
A beautiful setting. I had a perfect erbsensuppe mit minze, and then a milchkaffee with a sinful topfentorte. Vienna in New York.
Fantastic food! Try the duck. And the Margarita was awesome: not too sweet, just the right strength.
Great Vegan food! The service is great. They have an awesome menu. I love the Mozzarella Sticks! I also love the fries with all the different toppings, YUMMY IN MY TUMMY!

Post-theatre this is an excellent spot, as it's one of the few things open at after 10 and right in the theatre district. I had been craving a reuben and it hit the spot big time! Cheesecake is great as well. Portions are large, so you could split between 2 people. Although we had a short wait for a table (it was packed!), once we ordered our food cameout in minutes...fastest service I've ever exeperienced. A must-do for a NY visit!

BrisketTown might be misnamed. They should go by the name of RibTown because frankly the pork ribs here are better than the brisket. That's not to say that the brisket is bad. On the contrary its excellent. The slices are huge with nearly 1/3 of each slice of brisket brimming with fat. But brisket has always had a high floor and low ceiling. Ribs on the other hand have the potential to be the best dish on a menu but are often times screwed up. The ribs here at BrisketTown are expensive for starters. At $16 per 1/2 lb you are looking at basically 4 ribs, or $4 a rib. But what you get is fantastic top notch smoked meat. Tender ribs with a nice charred outside that isn't too dry but still has good smoked texture. For around $30 a person you will get enough good meat in this tiny South Williamsburg eatery to satisfy your hunger. Also the can koozies are free and you can take them home! Sweet souvenirs! Note : come early. By 8:30 pm the pork ribs were out... we got the last order. And let me tell you, that is what you definitely want. I want to say BrisketTown is somewhere between 4 and 5 stars. There wasn't much of a wait when I came at prime dinner time on a Friday which is a plus. The food is great but the price is a bit on the high side. Still you can't have it all in NYC - quality, service and price. Pick two.

We all feel so committed to the accuracy and detail of our reviews; I know I would like to think I have a "standard". If I asked any one of the Yelpers of how they write their reviews, more often than not the answer would be the same as mine; "I include the important facts supporting my rating". But, on this occasion I am reviewing an excellent property and awarding only 4 stars because my thoughts on a 5 star place make me hesitate thinking, "could this place be that good?" Boqueria on Spring street is bright and lively. The space is comfortable with a modern feel. The kitchen is open with bar type seating around it and for the curious looking to watch a great kitchen in action, this is a fun place to sit. We needed some time to look over menu and wine list not because of it's size but because of the quality selection (as my friend had said, "we could be here all day just trying one thing after another"); and, it was that good. So, from the top we ordered the squid, croquettes and jamon: simple, fresh, balanced, and traditional style tapas. I actually lived in San Sebastian, Spain and was happily surprised at how good this place was. To add to the food, we ordered a great white wine from the daily special list and it was a great wine, balanced and food friendly. A good value for your dollar, Boqueria in Soho was excellent. I am some what at odds with myself since this really was a five star experience but my sensibilities on the ultimate rating has me asking, "this couldn't have been that good?" And regardless of it being 5 or 4 star, after reading this review, one could only ask yourself, "why am I not sitting down and eating some of this wonderful food?" Try this place and like myself, you will be back for more.

Food here was fantastic. My friend and I shared the black eyed peas appetizer. It comes with yummy shrimp on top. So good! Then my friend got the duck. It was cooked medium but I though it was a little more medium well, still it was so good. The rice with veggies mixed in that came with the duck looked great. I loved my picanha. It was delicious, great flavor. And they did the side rice so well. The portions were nice and big so perfect for sharing. And it was all reasonably priced considering what we got. 50$ for two with tip! Very nice indeed. It's a pretty little restaurant. Nice ambiance and the staff was welcoming. Nice touch of culture and color. I was sad the place wasn't full. Maybe my friend and i were there on an off day since Brazil had been kicked out of the world club. I hope it's around for a long while.

I really wanted to love this place...but...the service was slow and the food not as good as I was hoping. Had two attempts before finally eating at this place as it is always so crowed. Love the pigs everywhere...

Got the matador combo togo. Comes with rotisserie chicken, rice, beans, fries, fried plantain slices, and slices of hot dogs. Also comes with an avocado salad. Comes with this yummy green spicy sauce. The chicken is soft and moist with enough flavor. It was not dry at all. Dip it with green sauce & your good to go. The beans I could've done without. Nothing really special about it. Rice could've also had more flavor. They didn't give any ketchup at all and the green sauce didn't really go with the plantain and hot dogs. It was also dry. The avocado salad was good though especially with the light green dressing it came with. This meal could feed about a party of 4-5 people!

This restaurant reminds me of Italy. Â When you are in Rome or Milan the restaurants char the bread and it is delicious. Â That is how they do it at Locanda. Â We ordered the bread with the fresh ricotta, it was amazing. Â The ricotta had a pool of yummy olive oil in the center and thyme, salt a and pepper. Â We also ordered the special ravioli which was stuffed with beef, veal and pork and topped with a fantastic tomato sauce with basil. Â Everything was first rate at Locanda Verde.

Simply amazing. Was lucky enough to have a private cocktail party before hand. The wine was great, but I felt they had too many non-vegetarians dishes while they were serving before our meal. First course: insalata, which had tasty greens, a delicious manchego cheese, with radish and sherry. The three courses were terrific. Wish there were more vegetarian options but I thoroughly enjoyed my meal.

Fresh. Fun. Smelly We were looking for shrimp dishes in the neighborhood. We ended up at FISH without knowing it was The place to be for Seafood in the Village, some say in the whole city ! We ended up not getting any shrimps but an order of Lobster Mac&Cheese and a Lobster Feast ! The Mac dish was full of Lobster, very cheesy but missing a bit of seasoning I must say. The excitement that this place created in me really enhanced the experience. I loved this very dusty seafood smell, as well as the kinda negligÃ© style of the servers and way to close alignment of the tables... It's so NYC ! My favorite part was wearing a bib to devour my lobster feast and if course using my fingers for most of the meal !! So yum ! The experience was fun and the food pretty good. It's a must see, must eat in NYC but I do believe they tend to rely on their reputation a bit with so-so seasoning abilities and a quite poor service (check out the back of their shirts tho...) I do will be back and enjoy it for sure. Bon Appetit ! bonjourclem.com @Bonjourclem Xoxo Clem

GREAT italian food! The owner is the sweet older man, hes great! His son who has been taking over, well sadly he's kind of not nice, not friendly, rude and insulting. Â it's such a shame....the food is amazing!

One of the few places that really matters in the Meatpacking District.I loved the pasta. Nice decor. Great place.

I'm not usually a fan of tapas/small plate restaurants, but this one was pretty good. Went on a Thursday evening, around 7:30pm or so. Â Place was pretty full, but we snagged the last available table. When you sit, you're greeted with some delicious popcorn that is cooked with bacon fat. Â :P Pork belly was a little disappointing, but the trotter (pig's feet, grounded up and mushed into a crispy patty) was very good. This place is pretty good, though I wouldn't necessarily come here that often. Â But for a nice treat in the Sunnyside area, it's great.
Great place they have here. Not sure I'd take 3 trains to go there again, but nice place.

For Years (30) The CORNER BISTRO was Perennial # 1 Best Burger in NY .. Love this place, great prices, and great ambiance and energy. Sad to say, the Burgers have gone Down in recent years. originally we wanted to go to Totto Ramen, but because of timing we were not able to go there and found this place on yelp! =) my friend and I are glad we gave this place a try! the wait was not long. the place is busy and loud with music and the shouting from employees about dishes? it got a bit annoying, but eventually you can learn to ignore it. anyway, there were many choices on the menu and everything sounds so delicious! my friend and I ordered a lot of food for two people, unknowingly that you CAN NOT doggie bag any food! so please make sure you can eat all the food you ordered and not waste food! ;) the appetizers of fried shrimp was ok normal cocktail kinda dish, the pepper could have been better, but the BUNS! my friend had the veggie and i had the pork, man they were delicious!!! we even craved the buns everyday for 3 days! it was that good. We loved the food, the atmosphere the only bummer was our server. She made us uncomfortable. Made us feel like a bother to her. Spending $350 for a meal and made to feel unwelcome is unacceptable
Caracas is awesome! Â  From the delicious food, service and ambiance. Â This is my new favorite lunch spot!!

Great happy hour sake & bbq meat, go here a lot with a friend after work and am always satisfied when I leave.

I ate here once quite a while back, cute little neighborhood spot, cozy, BYOB. Cash only. Â Not good for large groups. Food pretty decent, though the one thing I recall is not having enough carnivorous options.
OMG.. French fry heaven... Cooked to perfection with so many yummy dipping sauces... How to choose, Â how to choose

This place rocks. Â Feels like you are on vacation! Â I had the king crab roll which was awesome. Â Gorgeous view, friendly bartender, reggae music, good beer. Â Seafood is always expensive but this place makes you feel like you are in a small town on the Chesapeake. Â Great relaxed vibe and welcome change from the normal New York hustle and bustle.

I love this place! Â You can eat your meal al fresco. Â In the back, there is an open patio/backyard where you can take in the beautiful garden and adorable water fountains. Aaaahhh....Nyonya, how do I love thee, let me count the ways... Stumbled on this gem on what was my maiden voyage to New York. I say stumbled, as my Great Aunt, cousins and I were staying a few steps round the corner while on a girls weekend to the Big Apple - so this house of Malaysian Gastronomy was right there waiting for our discovery. We phoned ahead and got an 8 o clock reservation earlier in the day as we were a party of five and coming from England, thought a Saturday night might be pushing it to arrive on spec. Glad we did as it was jumping when we walked through the front door, every table full and hungry dinner guests waiting in the wings. Â Decor was calm, unobtrusive and quietly tiki chic, despite the happy buzz emanating from the dining room. Menu was extensive and narrowing the decision to just a few appetizers and five entrees was tough. Appetizers: We opted for the Roti Canai - light, crispy-chewy and delicious - a wonderful edible utensil when wrapped around tender morsels of spice infused chicken and for sopping up the rich curry gravy left in the bowl. Seaweed Salad - delightful melange of shredded sweet jicama juxtaposed with the strong briny notes of the seaweed that tastes like only the seaside smells. Spring Rolls - ten very easy to eat crispy spring rolls served with Thai Sweet Chili Sauce...nom nom nom... Entrees: Mango Chicken - fresh tropical citrus marriage of mango strips and moist chicken in a spicy sweet and sour sauce with onions and peppers, Beef Rendang - reminded me of a Malaysian version of Osso Bucco - sans the veal and the bone of course, but beefy chunks of perfectly braised meat in a deep cinnamon based spicy sauce...Malaysian Spareribs - a workout for your pearly whites Â compared to the Rendang, but lightly spiced and not too chewy, Malaysian Buddhist - a kaleidoscopic cacophony of vegetables and fungi in an oyster sauce type gravy - though i have to say, palate had Â a moment of panic when it thought a piece of the intestine dish had landed itself in this vegetarian dish - both palate and myself quite relieved to find it was a piece of fermented tofu skin (phew - had a nervous laugh to myself) and lastly, Chicken in Clay pot - chicken infused with basil and chili - quite delicious. All these epicurean delights served with coconut and brown rice and two bottle of wine between five of us and very reasonably priced. Can't wait to go back to NY just to have a rematch. Viva Nyonya!

Solid go-to spot in LES, open late (2am). Purchases under $10 are CASH ONLY. Some of the best wraps I've had. And when I say wraps, I mean like the actual wrap part - made from scratch after you order, it don't get no fresher than dat. Also has unique combinations of food. My favorites are the Brothers Grimm (Chicken, pickled shitake, raisins, plaintain chips, etc.), Mowgli (Grilled Cauliflower, spicy pineapple, shallot, bbq chips, etc.), and Teen Wolf (Falafel and yeah you get the point - they are creative and tasty). All in all, ingredients are made fresh, wraps are warm and gooey, and... + 1 for Tator Tots. Also love the sweet potato fries. (the only think I don't like about this place is every time I ordered a beer here (which I don't do anymore) it has been lukewarm) Good sauce too - my guess is a mixture of ketchup, mayonnaise, and some some of chipotle.

If you live nearby, be warned that delivery takes FOREVER and the pizza's not nearly as good!!!
Great chicken and lamb dishes, and the mujadarah was awesome. Â I've eaten at a lot of Middle Eastern places, and lived in Middle Eastern countries, and this food stacks up with the best of them!

Good cuban food on avenue c. The appetizers were yummy. The chicken with rice was a testy and big plate. And the maduros were delicious. The the glass of malbec was not that good. I will come soon

It was the best experience I've ever had. - Really hot Bengali/Nepalese girl I honestly thought it was okay. Pio Pio was very hip and modern, loved the atmosphere. Â We sat off at one of the tables to back of the bar. Â The bartender waited on us and we had great service. Â Definitely a must try if you are looking for Peruvian food.

This place is one of my favourite places in the entire village area. Not only is the food cheap (probably $7-10, on average), the portions are generous and it's delicious. This is another place that just didn't wow me. Â I'm beginning to worry that I'll have to go into the city for food that wows. Â  They serve firewood pizza with fresh mozzarella, basil, onions, mushrooms, pepperoni, and a few other ingredients. Â The pizza was incredibly fresh, but I was honestly hoping for more options to add to the pizza to give it a bit more flavor. Â More meat options like prosciutto or salmon maybe? Â I dunno. Â Maybe more greens like arugula? Â  I went with a small group of people around 6pm, and as luck would have it, we were seated right away. Â  Everyone seemed satisfied enough, but no one was falling out of their chair. Â Maybe I just need to come back to this place with my boyfriend? Â Have a firewood pizza, wine, and enjoy the romantic atmosphere? Â It is a beautiful restaurant. I'll give it another shot when I have my boyfriend with me, but I'm still giving it three stars for now.
Love the brunch food, love the atmosphere. Can't wait to come back for sandwiches. And the Michigan vibe is fun -- they have Bell's on tap!

I never expected to find a true Australian place is Queens, NY but this place was a great surprise! The waiter was so personable with me while I waited for my party to arrive and helped me order something that I would truly enjoy. Their kangaroo burger with feta cheese was delicious!! I would recommend this to everyone for anytime of the day but their Sunday brunch specials are unbeatable in price and flavor! I will definitely have to revisit this place in the future:)

This is hands down one of my favorite restaurants in NYC. The food is amazing, the service is great, and the atmosphere is fun. It can get a little crowded on certain nights and on weekends, and it can get a little pricey if you're drinking there, but it's worth it because once you eat here once, you'll be immediately trying to figure out when you can go back.

So cute. One of those places you go awwwww on a summer night. Good food. Good sweets. You have to go smell the bathroom you even go awww. This place makes me feel Elegant in Brooklyn and who knew Brooklyn made me feel that way and not clutch onto my bag so tight.

Going to Gaia is like going to your mom's Italian kitchen. Â All of Gaia's food is amazing- and I'm really picky. Â Gaia herself is lovely, and always takes the time to ask how you are, etc. Â Everything is fresh, wholesome, and delicious. Â i have tried two salads ($7)--both of the dressings were lip-smacking- and the greens were fresh. Â She makes her own bread for the sandwiches. Â All of the sandwiches are tasty. Â My favorite is the Milanese ($5). Â The white lasagna with pesto was out of control ($5). Â It tasted like fresh, homemade ricotta. Â Now let's discuss the baked goods. Â Biting into one of them transports you back in time, away from any stress you may temporarily be experiencing- and puts you right in Italy. Â Her desserts are not too sweet- which, sometimes can be the case. Â Finally, the prices. Â This place is a steal. Â You absolutely can't go wrong here. Â You will be running back for more. Â The only downside that I can think of is that can be slow at times. Â But, that is kind of the charm of it...
The Avocado BrÃ»lÃ©e Salad and the Grilled Asparagus were both so delicious!! I think they are perfect dishes! And the staff is very friendly. I highly recommend it and I'll definitely return!

I'm sorry, but how this place gets the rep it does for good pizza, I will never ever know. Â I AM FROM JERSEY. Â JERSEY GIRLS KNOW GOOD PIZZA. Â This wasn't it! Â The thin crust should be a recipe for success...however, I always find their pizza to be on the soggy side. Â Also, I hate looking like I have six heads when I just want plain pizza. Someone wanting plain pizza, that's hard to comprehend? Â Sorry, I'm a purist. Â  My office orders from here all the time and I always turn it down. Â I mean, there are plenty of better options around (and cheaper pizza options..i mean seriously, a pie with two drinks is $25? Â Get real!), why not get more of an easier crowd pleaser? Â I guess they equate quality with price (trust me - that is a LIE!). Â  All I want to know is who Adrienne's PR people are, because let me tell you...they have everyone brainwashed into thinking this is good pizza. Â It's not. Â I'm from jersey. Â We know!

We ate here last night and it was quite yummy. Â I had a marrow bones and the lamb shank and the hubby had the steak tartar and the boudin noir. Â Everything was cooked great and seasoned well and there was an ample supply of crusty chewy bread. Â It was great for cure for the insanely cold weather. Â Note that the portions are quite big. Â Another great thing about this place wine prices, not a huge mark up, so ordering a bottle won't break the bank.
Great for Breakfast. The Chilaquelas were amazing. Not a horrible price when it comes to brunch.

LOVE this place. Â Tacos are so full, juicy, and taste amazing. Â Had al pastor and pollo - both great. Â Lots of quality ingredients that give it a great overall flavor. Â The tacos came out quickly after ordering. Â It's a small place with seating for maybe 8 - I went late on a weekday night, so not many were there.
