It's pretty cheap and the tacos are BIG - it's a great value. Â I can't wait to come back to try the burritos and chips. Â So happy with this place. Â Highly reccomended.

There has been a lot of hype surrounding Grimaldi's for as long as I can remember. I never ended up coming though, mainly because of the long lines comprised of tourists and the fact that the other awesome joints that have popped up in Brooklyn are keeping my pizza tooth happy. But we finally ventured out on a recent Saturday night with a few friends and sampled some of the famous NY-style pizza. I have to say, I guess I am biased and really tend to prefer Italian-style pizza because while our pizza was tasty, I wasn't in love the way I have been with other spots. It is good, don't get me wrong, but it wasn't mouth-watering-kick-ass awesome. I couldn't even really eat the crust (not a good sign). On top of that, it was incredibly hot in the restaurant (on a night that wasn't) and the service wasn't great. The waiters seemed very rushed and didn't have time to even bring us water refills for a while. I'm glad I went for the Grimaldi's experience, but probably won't be rushing back anytime soon.
Fun place, great food! They have a TASTY kale dip that is to die for, and overall they have some good selections. The service was good, and the bartender friendly. Good spot for a nice bite to eat.

That's soba!? Whoa. Â It's so fresh! My bf and I stumbled upon this restaurant after staring at a blank screen in the theater on 14th for 30 minutes before management declared it's projector broken and unable to play the 3 hour batman movie for which we had alloted our time. Fortunately, east village was right around the corner with random, amazing options such as Soba-ya! How I have not yet discovered this until now is shocking to me. It hit me I've probably been cooking soba all wrong (overcooked)! My bf got the cold soba and I got a hot soba (yasai). Both were delicious. Toppings were light but flavorful. The broth was tasty. The meat was tender. The noodles were amazing. I officially love soba thanks to soba-ya and will now begin to try all other popular soba places! I will be back to review soba-ya after my soba quest.

wow. stumbled in here last night after getting drinks down the street - we were in the mood for something different ie not a burger. there was absolutely no one inside which was a little offputting but i'm so glad we took a chance. we had two of their "build your own cocktails" - a choice of two different kinds of rum and a ton of fruit juices. i had a white rum with strawberry guava juice - DELICIOUS. it was definitely more about the juice than the rum. it tasted barely alcoholic but again, delicious, and they were pretty cheap. i had the loco moco with egg fried rice... holy shit i want this for dinner every night for the rest of my life. super cute homey, simplistic decor - perfect spot for a dinner date. i will be back!

Thought the food was ok. Place was pretty run-down. Yes it was pretty authentic puerto rican food, but honestly I have had better in many other places in this city. Ok if you are looking for that type of experience.
Terrific food, all day brunch, great coffee, great prices - and they play Piaf. I love this place.

Walk in for the warm atmosphere. Stay for the great service and drinks. Beautifully decorated bar situated along a row of bars that seem less classy from the outside, so it stands out. Bottles elegantly line the shelving on all the walls, and soft orange backlights give everything a romantic glow. Plenty of places to sit or stand, but be warned that it is usually packed on weekends! Just the right kind of bustling but not so much that you can't have an intimate conversation. Our bartender, Diego, always takes care of us with a handsome and easygoing smile. The spiced sangria is pretty amazing, and all of the small plates sound really appetizing. There's something for everyone on the food and drinks menu. Great place for a casual date or nighttime drink, be it wine, cocktails, or beer.
Falafel doesnt get better than this dude. They might not have the fluffy fresh whole wheat pitas that Hummus Place has, but there's something about their falafels that just rocks. Awesome prices.

Due to my job which entails alot of traveling and eating at restaurants, it has become harder to be impressed by any restaurant. Â Red Cat definitely impressed me with it's simple interpretation of modern American cuisine. Â I had the quail which is the best rendition I had outside of Saigon House's Vietnamese version. Â I also had their roasted pumpkin salad which was very refreshing. Â Deserts are a little disappointing since the dinner was excellent and unexpected, I thought I would be surprised by the deserts. Â It is a small quintessential NY restaurant so reservations is recommended. Â Surprisingly, the wine list is very affordable. Â Red Cat is a gem in NY that I would highly recommend trying.
Amazing bar. Have a large choice of wine, wiskie and have a nice workers. can meet with friends and have some meeting there too.

Love everything about this place. The sleek, yet cozy atmosphere. The small menu bursting with freshness, color and flavor. Thai and Chinese staples, with some unusual twists (lettuce cups with fish!). Go with a group open to sharing as you'll want to try as many dishes as possible. And book a table in the garden if you can get one. Still thinking about that Panang Curry.

Bouley is great. It's so underrated it's unbelievable. The food here is excellent and like some other reviewers have said up there with the greats in city, making it one of the best in the world. No, that's not hyperbole. Before I forget to mention it they bake their bread on site. Not a lot of restaurants do that, even the greats! This just goes to show the top quality of the input from the chefs. I am not going to recommend anything on the menu because as often as my girlfriend and I go we have never had a sub-par dish. The ambiance is cossetting, warm and embracing. Sorry I cannot find better words than that to describe it. The waitstaff are also some of the best you can find!

My SO and I always have a tough time come dinner time figuring out what's our craving and where to eat. Â Welp, my SO stumbled upon this VERY cute place while surfing the Net and suggested we go try it since it was 1) in my hood, 2) inexpensive & 3) cuisine neither of us ever had before. I must've walked by this place a gagillion time and just never paid attention to it. Â Once you step inside, you're transpired to a different place because the interior is dark with palm tree plants and foreign (Brazilian?) music playing. Â The hostess is a sexy mamacita w/an authentic accent. We ordered the following: Arepas Chips w/Guacamole, Yuca Frita's, Chicken Salad and White Corn Pancakes with pulled Chicken. Â OMG!!! It was ALL very flavorful and delish! Â Now I'm NOT a big Guacamole fan but I REALLY loved their Guacamole! Â The Corn pancakes were SO tasty and I finished it ALL! I must say, my SO and I are so excited about finding this place that we're talking about bringing our friends back soon! Â Yes, it's THAT GOOD! Â They have FRESH fruit juices along with very tropical alcoholic beverages. Â It's also VERY reasonably priced for being in Chelsea.
Currently my favorite Soba place in NYC. Â The noodles are awesome, with the buckwheat flown in from Japan and worth the wait. Â Soba-koh is getting close but I still pick Soba-ya.

All I could say is if your lookin for pizza in Brooklyn I recommend this place. It's a tourist spot for people craving for NY pizza! Expect long lines and long wait time they also take long cooking your pizza because it's cooked old style brick and coal. But it's worth it for the experience. When you walk inside it's smells like coal mixed with pizza smell it's not that typical smell you would get from other pizza places. The servers are all happy dancing to the beat of whatever music there playing 80's type of music. The desert was so good especially the cannoli. Stop by and try it for first timers, you will not regret the wait!

I had the privilege of dining at Perry Street the other night, actually by accident. My friends and I had plans to go to the Spotted Pig nearby, and of course, because they refuse to take reservations there was a 2 hour wait. So, a quick search on Yelp led me to a restaurant that I had on my to-do list for ages. Well, I remembered why once we got inside the stark modern pretentious hotel-like interior: Perry Street is part of the Jean Georges Empire. And it did not fall short of my elevated expectations. To start we shared a few appetizers, the highlight of which was the crispy poached eggs with caviar and vodka cream. I want to spread that vodka cream on every piece of bread I eat from now on. The entrees we sampled at our table were equally tasty: butter poached lobster with lemongrass and lime broth and potato ravioli, grilled Colorado lamb chops with caramelized brussels sprouts and pistachio pesto, and for me- don't judge- the organic fried chicken with Meyer lemon marmalade, crispy black trumpet stuffing and mashed potato. Each dish had something surprising, yet maintained a refined balanced approach to what would otherwise be considered some pretty heavy dishes. Bottom line: save up some money that will be well-spent and go here.

While in Time Square I checked Yelp for a place to eat, and this place had a high review rating so why not. The food was average, not worth of a 4.5 star rating. Every dish came out at a different time leaving other people at the table waiting, and to top it off I was charged for fries that were supposed to replace vegetables that came with my dish. Would've been nice to know they charged for substitutions before hand. The waitress was very nice. No kids menu. Wouldn't recommend it.

I waited in a line here for about 45 minutes. Â Everyone said it's worth the wait. Â They were right... it's definitely the type of pizza you'll only have here. Â Very thin, lots of cheese... it tasted great. Â  But if you are like me-- and enjoy crispy crust-- so crispy you can hold it up by the larger end and it sits straight horizontal- then go elsewhere up the block on Henry.

1 star for the quac, minus 4 stars for service and entree. We ordered guac within a minute of sitting down, they wanted our drink orders, but we werent sure if we were going to drink. when the waitress came back less than a minute later, we both hadn't even glanced at the drink menu, but just ordered the jalepeno margarita on special. she asked us for our food order but were werent ready. she asked us again under a minute later. sensing her rush, we both ordered the same thing, enchaladas de mole, which i thought contained just a little chocolate sauce. So the guac come out and so do our drinks. Guac is good, as it should be for $8. LESS THAN A MINUTE AFTER GETTING OUR APPETIZER, THE ENTREES SHOW UP. We really had no interest in our entrees, as we had barely had 1 chip each. The entree itself was covered in chocolate. It really wasn't good, it was kind of gross. Maybe I ordered the wrong thing for me, but i mean, even the enchalada itself wasn't that good, reminded me of something i might put frozen in the microwave. Nobody asked us if we were happy with the food or anything like that. So we are still working on our entrees when the waitress asks about desert.... and she asked 3 other times before I got the check. For some context, this was a Tuesday night and the place was less than half full. I did not understand the rush. Will not return.

I got the Nutty Buddy wrap and Spicy Mang Roll Combo and it was totally delicious! Especially, when I threw on the sauces to kick up my veggies a notch. Beyond Sushi offers a nice assortment of rolls, wraps, natural drinks and healthy snacks. With a quaint Japanese sushi/noodle shop decor, Beyond Sushi may not be huge, it's still a nice place to grab an equisite bite on the go. I'd recommend all you Sushi deprived Vegans, look into scratching that old itch at Beyond Sushi.

I've passed this truck many times and it's the aroma of the fries that gets me... I finally decided to try it out and boy, was I not disappointed! Â  The chicken pita deluxe on whole wheat was delicious and is definitely a must-order for next time. Â There wasn't quite enough tzatziki sauce, so I might have to order some extra on the side next time. Will definitely go again, but expect a 10-15 min wait :)

Yup, Joe Shanghai lives up to its hype. Â There's not much left unsaid in the 480+ reviews here, so I'll keep this short. Go for the pork and crab meat soup dumplings. Â They're right-out-of-the-steamer fresh, every bit as juicy as you'd imagine, and perfectly delicious. Â The other things on the menu are fine, but nothing worth writing about. Service is rushed but they are also efficient. Â And this is Chinatown so "hectic and harried" sort of goes with the territory. Â I find it to be quite energetic and festive. Â Definitely worth a return visit.

The menu is very large and most of the items we have tested were delicious. Ginger mojito was excellent. Our favorite dishes were Dates, Paella, bass tartare if you like ceviche, brussel sprouts and hanger steak. When we asked for jamon and other typical tapas dishes, our waiter told us that this is not a tapas restaurant but a small plate Mediterranean restaurant. The deserts were excellent too. Highly recommend pot de creme and chocolate lave cake. We were seated on the first floor where there is a great wood fire place. The second floor had windows overlooking backyard and looked very nice too. Since you end up ordering so many dishes, it can get expensive.

Now I see what the other Yelpers were saying... the service is so slow. I can't tell who's back in the kitchen, because with three people going in and out from the back where the kitchen is, it took over 20 minutes to get water. This experience will probably not dissuade me from coming again, but I'll be sure to budget about an hour to get just one arepa next time.

You know what? For how pricey it is, I thought it would be more expensive. We had a wonderful meal, ate way too much, very attentive (but not intrusive) service, and got out of there without losing an arm or a leg. The beef wellington was incredible (the spinach flan is a little dorky but tasty); the salad with seared ahi tuna and avocado was good (if over-dressed); the crab cakes and truffle mac and cheese were very good, the mushroom soup was sturdy and delicious, if lacking in a dramatic flourish. I'd definitely go back and try other dishes. I recommend the Bogle Petit Syrah; at $23 a bottle, it's a good value. But, sure, go ahead, get one of the expensive ones if you want.
Go for the full/half pie - square pizza only. Slices are never as good.

I've been using Yelp religiously for a few years to plan my dining, so I thought it's time I contribute with a review. After all the research I'd done and lists I'd made for the various cities we visited, the first place that popped in my head was Gramercy Tavern. Â My wife and I ate from their tavern menu almost three years ago, and we still talk about it to this day. Â For me, the sign of a great meal is one that's memorable and this definitely hit the mark. Â I remember eating the meal and thinking to myself, I wouldn't even know where to start to try and create flavors like this. Â Amazing. My only regret was skipping the dining room menu the next time we were in New York. Â That mistake won't be repeated...we'll be back eventually!

To start off, and I really hate to have to do this, but I feel the management needs to address this issue: each time I have been, I have seen with my own eyes, little children putting their mouths and hands on the BBQ sauce bottles that are on the tables!!!!! Yes. Their hands and mouths. (I love kids & have kids myself). Parents didn't care or even see, some parents were on the line leaving kids at tables waiting. Whatever, I always get everything to go anyway. However, I recommend that you use the sauces up front near the counters where you pay, if you don't want to have the sauces the kids sucked on. Other than that, I have eaten here many many times and it is very good. The lamb and pork belly are especially good. The sides are meh. The other meat is always great, fab ribs. Highly recommended! Be aware that its kind of pricey. Not cheap. But you are paying for high quality. Be aware that there is waitress service for the drinks but you have to line up all around the place to get your food. People try to snag tables using their kids or bags or whatever, so I don't stay, I always get it to go because its all just annoying frankly, especially when its busy. So go early. Also, the servers at the counter really take their time, and there doesn't seem to be enough of them really - I feel their stress of people waiting in line. One guy doing all the meat? Seriously? And if you want the ribs they take extra time. Someone has to go all the way and get them from the back kitchen. Takes like an extra 15 mins sometimes. But very yummy!!! Be patient.

Oh Cafe Orlin, what would I do without you in the neighborhood. Sundays would not be the same for sure, or Tuesdays or any day really. This place is probably one of the most consistent restaurants in the East Village. There's no better place than Cafe Orlin for brunch. Period. Tunisian eggs, side of labnah cheese, bloody mary. Sold.

Solid. Great food, friendly service, good lighting and the right music. Down home Southern classics w/ a twist - kale or chicory salads both winners, pigtails w/ tater tots YUM! Meatloaf and mashed sandwich on pullman loaf and great bloody mary's. The bone marrow on toast points is as decadent as it is good.

The Good: This little spot looked like a scene straight out of the Single Ladies television show. It was cool, trendy, modern, and attracted a lot of beautiful well-dressed customers of color. The music was a combo of soul/neo-soul/r&b, some instrumentals/originals that have been sampled, and a few unexpected genres. I ordered the Buttermilk Fried Chicken and Red Velvet Waffles which seems to be a pretty popular dish. It was gooood. Also at our table was mac n' cheese, okra and tomatoes, and the Blackened Salmon dish. I tasted everything and . . . while it wasn't "authentic momma's kitchen" it was delicious and beautifully presented. The server was friendly, quick, and even had some post-dinner entertainment suggestions for us. The Bad: $14 for a Mixed Drink. Lord hammercy. The Ugly: One could (and did) easily spend $80 on a conservative-sized dinner for two. Choose wisely.

NYC's best food cart two years in a row for a reason! I've traveled to Palestine and the Middle East several times and enjoyed the Chicken Shawarma more than any time I've had it overseas. It was juicy with a great sauce served on fluffy flat bread. Great food, good price!

I looked online to see where to get the best cheesecake in New York and and Junior's popped up several times. Did not disappoint at all. It's family owned so everything seems like it still matters. The food was great and the staff was very friendly. We ended up sitting at the bar so we could be seated right away and the bartender was very attentive and personable. Never tried any other cheesecake while in New York but I can say that it's probably the best I've had. Definitely gotta use their online delivery in the future.

I am always a bit reticent to try "fancier" pizza places. Â But no one should fear trying the pizza at Rubirosa. Â Outstanding! Â They are very accommodating - you can get half of one pie, half of another, on the same pie. Â I think at no additional cost. Â The sauce tasted like it was made that morning with tomatoes fresh off the vine. Â The toppings were also fresh from the garden. But also truly outstanding here is the pasta. Â I rarely order pasta at restaurants because it seems so easy, so unremarkable. Â I have been mistaken in this belief for some time, I believe. Â If a place makes their own pasta, I think I need to be more openminded. If you can scope whether their pasta is excellent in advance, all the better. Here, the pasta is outstanding! Â The flavor is really different from the ordinary pasta you are likely used to. Â Fresher. Â And the ingredients in it, like the pizza, are really fresh. Only thing I ordered and could care less for - the duck bruschetta. Â I just was not into the duck at all. Â However, the shrimp bruschetta was really tasty. Â The shrimp was perfectly cooked. Â Kind of hard to eat though. Service was nice. Â Our server was laidback, accommodating, chill. Â I felt like I'd want to be friends with her. As one from DC where prices are a bit lower than NY, generally, I was really pleased with how affordable Rubirosa was, too.

This hole in a wall is a place that every local and tourist should experience. I usually try to come in during the day, since it's not bombarded by patrons like most other overrated tourist traps located around the Seaport. The daily specials on food and drinks are more than a good reason for me to keep on returning. Especially, the Mondays and Tuesdays Lobster deal for just under 13 bucks! You just can't beat that. The food usually arrives quick and with great care, and the staff is very down to earth.
Excellent!!! In the land of mediocre Mexican food, Los Tacos blows them out of the water.

I've dined at Perilla about half a dozen times now so I guess it's time for a short review. As 4 stars on Yelp states- Yay! I'm a fan....yes I am. Last Â visit we did the beer/food pairing with the folks from the Blind Tiger. I can't remember every course we had but suffice to say it was well done and it is something we would do again. Great service...innovative food. The signature duck meatballs are a must try and the calamari salad is one of my faves. Give Perilla a shot.... it's worth it.
Great place! I love our (almost) weekly date nights at Tuk Tuk. I thoroughly enjoy unwinding here with a glass of wine and good food.

Hands down one of the best rib eye's I've ever had in my life. Its a special menu item, so I don't know how often they offer it. They only take reservations before 5pm, so call as soon as you can in the AM -- otherwise you can do what we did, show up and hope to score open bar seats. Be warned: GET A RESERVATION if you want a table or a booth -- the wait for a table without a reservation was 2+ hours. The bartender was friendly, informative, and took her time to recommend menu items and special drinks. They have a great bar selection of craft and microbrewery beers, small distillery spirits, and small vineyard wines. If you're looking for the typical Robert Mondavi crap wine, forget it. The artesian bread warmed up our appetites, so that by the time our duck meatballs arrived, we savored every spicy morsel. Â  But the real standout was the Rib Eye. Perfectly done medium rare. Juicy, succulent...my mouth is watering just thinking about it. They served it with the best mashed potatoes I've ever had -- four balls deep fried on the outside and creamy and whipped on the inside. The other side I'd recommend was the carmelized apples, onions, and bacon mix -- it is out of this world. For desert we had the doughnuts -- but to be honest, we were so full from the dinner we barely made a dent (though the few bites we had were very sweet and tasty). A perfect place for a special date or a night out with fellow couples.

Charming, dim-lite restaurant with a European vibe perfect for a romantic date. I went with a group of friends and we enjoyed an intimate conversation at the corner round table. I got the Oxtail Ragu, which was delicious! The oxtail was tender and cooked perfectly, and you can tell they roll their own pasta! Props for originality. Only thing I was slightly disappointed with was the portions, as I was left slightly hungry still, after my ragu. But still, an amazing restaurant to try out!

Wandering around, looking for a slice of Naples-style pizza, and BAM. Price is OK (~$3/slice, depending). Taste: not bad! They warm up the slice for you in a brick oven, and they used smoked mozzarella which I haven't tried before on a pizza, and liked a lot. The sauce was on the sweeter side, made onsite I think with some roasted red pepper. What stood out was the owner. He clearly had a lot of pride and love for his shop. Posted on the wall are various people who've come by for a slice from the 50's onwards. As soon as I ordered, he was bursting to tell me what was special about his pizza, and when I told him I was dining in, he insisted I relax and enjoy the food before paying. I felt more welcomed and taken care of in this little place with counter seating than I have at most fancy restaurants. Will be back soon to eat through the rest of the menu!

I've had this place on my list & I am so glad I finally made the trek to Chelsea to eat here. Decided to eat dinner w/ one of my girl friends here since she was craving steak. I, on the other hand, was craving Cuban. So I thought, eh, why not?! From beginning to end, service was amazing. The waiter was really tentative & made sure we enjoyed our food. I ordered the spinach salad w/ grilled chicken. The chicken was grilled just right - not too charred. It was seasoned lightly yet was still flavorful & the strips were decent in size (not too large or chunky, phew! saves me the hassle of cutting, ya know?!). The chunks of dried figs added a nice touch of sweetness. The candied walnuts added that oomph to the salad, oh my! Perfectly sweet & crunchy. And the goat cheese? I haven't had such creamy goat cheese in a salad. Pretty amazed at the quality of a simple spinach salad. Delish! And dessert?! WHERE DO I BEGIN?! That flan was THE perfect custard. And there must be crack in the sorbet scoops because I have never had such creamy, delicious coconut & mango sorbet in my life. That. was. fricken. amazing. And 3 desserts for $20?! HELL YEAH, GO FOR IT!

Crab pizza was unbelievable, and this is coming from someone who doesn't like pizza that much. Think crab cake on a piece of pizza. Friend got Artichoke and Sicilian, both of which were pretty good but not extraordinary. Artichoke pizza is essentially artichoke and spinach dip spread over pizza. Not our cup of tea exactly. Cash only, no seating inside, and two small benches outside. There's a dining room next door, but I think you order the same pizza and get a sit-down experience there. They wouldn't let us bring our slices from next door in. Confusing system.
Yep, a busy Saturday night so ended up sat at the bar. Great atmosphere and the steak frites were good

This has to be the best dining experience I've had in my NYC trip so far. After walking by this place one day, I was excited to see some vegetarian meatball options. I headed down on a balmy Wednesday evening. It was hopping, but was able to snag a bar stool in about 5 minutes. I gotta say the menu was one of my favorite parts of the Meatball Shop. Its well designed and the options are great. It makes up for limited dishes by offering them up in multiple combinations of your pleasing. Sides can be part of your main. What a fucking smart idea. Want porcini risotto on the side or underneath your pork meatballs? Your choice. Beer options were simple but smart. Wine options also looked good. Bartender was great and seemed quite excited about the food. Even convinced me to get an ice cream sandwich. Impressive. Add a few more taps and add back the salmon meatball option and you'll get that 5th star...

This place is the best new wave pizza spot in the city. I can rant about John's and Totonno's, but Lucali makes a fine pie and has a pleasant setting. It is minimalist and it is not cheap, but the pizza is terrific and it's BYO to boot. They typically have wait, but you can give them a cell number and head to a bar to sit it out.

After a day of shopping for bridesmaids dresses with my friend who is getting married next year, she treated us to dinner at this place on a Saturday in June 2011. Â I was going to try something new but of course I had to try their chicken pad thai which is my favorite.(My first taste of chicken pad thai was at Tara Thai in Washington, DC about 15 years ago. Â It was delicious. Â Ever since then, I have been on the hunt for excellent pad thai so at every Thai restaurant, I always order that.) Â The chicken pad thai at Room Service was one of the best chicken pad thai I've ever had. Â It was well seasoned, had all of the ingredients for pad thai and was just perfect. Â We also tried the curry puffs which melted in your mouth and the chicken satay. Â All were very delicious. Â My mouth is watering thinking of it. Â The decor is really nice inside. Â The restrooms were well-decorated too. Â Our waiter was attentive and courteous. Â I'm planning my next visit there soon.

Had a fantastic meal. The green curry tofu was so good that I ended up spooning out all of the curry sauce till there was no more. Somehow that didn't feel unhealthy, but I guess that's the point. The sweet potato app was fantastic. Nice ambiance. Full, but not too crowded.

Being from Austin, I am a HUGE fan of tacos of all sorts. Gueros is a great little place with some extremely delicious tacos and some others that need work. I've gone through almost the whole menu and I can say hands down that the Al Pastor and Brisket tacos are incredible. Both the friend chicken and shrimp tacos were dry and rubbery. The shrimp wasn't fresh and was pretty flavorless. The catfish taco almost ruined my meal. It was slimy and again pretty flavorless. I really like this place- there many other places you can get queso! But, I will just stick to the couple of tacos that are stellar. It would be ideal if Gueros would have a tomatillo salsa along with their homemade habanero.

The fries weren't spectacular. Truth be told, I was a little disappointed. I expected to be WOW-ed and my reaction was a "Meh." I would go back because I LOVe potatoes but I've had better. Plus, there is a HUGE variety of sauces. It made my head spin. I think I'm purist. Fries that don't require any condiments and still manage to wow you, are the best.
Best Mexican food I've had in New York. Amazing burritos, delicious guacamole. Great service, fair prices and its never crowded. Better than Calexico. I will be coming back again and again.

I found this to be a standard, high end, unspectacular restaurant you find in a large US city. Beautiful, albeit staid and soulless, setting. Â Professional and attentive service. Â Food was a bit mixed. The squid ink trofie pasta was superb, though the portions were teeny tiny - maybe 7 to 8 strands at most. Â Really? Â The cod was average - a bit salty for my taste - and the size of large scallop. Â The rye cocktail tasted like a flat whiskey and ginger ale. Â I was hesitant since I knew this was in a hotel, but it was located between my meeting and hotel. Â Oh well.

Good carne asada, a little disappointed in the adobada. A little more seasoning would have made it way better. The homemade flour tortillas were okay but got soggy really quickly and fell apart. Salsa was yummy and the guys behind the counter were really nice about putting a little more on when asked. I recently moved back from the west coast and have been looking for a good taco shop, so this place is solid for New York but can't really compare to west coast tacos.

i have been going to l&b since i was a child . it use to be great over the years it has gone down hill . dont get me wrong the squares are still ok . but if you dont get them fresh out the oven they tend to suck. i ve tasted much better Â the service in the pizzeria is also terrible . the workers dont seem to care and are rude . make sure when you order you get a fresh pie . they tend to make a bunch of pies and leave them on the oven , sometimes for over an hour .

This place is muy delicioso. Â Seriously good! Fun and relaxed atmosphere! Â Corn was beyond good. Â Guacamole was fresh and tasty and went great with the fresh plantains. Â Price is right! I'll be back for sure!

3.5.... Liked the BRASIL - $2.80 traditional Brazilian style empanada with ground beef, olives, sauteed onions, and potatoes...get 2 .They are small. Â The green and red hot sauces were delicious with this empanada. Â You should eat them at the restaourant and not take them to go to eat several hours later, as I did. Did not like the spicy shredded chicken empanada. Â It tasted too much like Taco Bell seasonings.

One of the very best Italian restaurants in New York. It's not classic though - the atmosphere is a little "clean," not super warm and friendly, and the portions are not what you'd typically find in a standard Italian place in the US. Not that they're too small, just that we're usually used to getting so much food you either have to take half home, or be rolled out. The pasta though is fantastic, the desserts are delicious, and the entrees well prepared. Not the place to go for your moms spaghetti and meatballs, but you can have an excellent meal here, and have your eyes opened as to how Italian food can be when prepared in the right hands.

For our next stop - let's just say we left Motorino just on time, and barely. Â With traffic thinned out substantially we actually made excellent time trekking to Carroll Gardens but unfortunately there were no parking to be found for a good twenty minutes - twenty long minutes that would lead us past no less than four pizza parlors including our eventual destination - Lucali - yet another location dubbed by various national publications as the best Pizza in America. With Steve-1 showing off his parallel parking skills a mere block away it was a quick walk to the doors of the small space and despite arriving at 5:45 we were thwarted - the first table available would be 7:15 according to the young lady at the door. Â Standing and waiting to inform our dining partners of the news and feeling a tad discouraged what happened next still leaves me puzzled, but regardless of the reason (I'm pretty sure the Pizza Gods simply loved our ambition) after approximately five minutes of waiting one of the folks ahead of us in line opted out of her seat and suddenly we owned a 6:00pm table for four. Â  With Steve telling us stories of Mark Iacono's ground up (literally - he built the oven, the tables, and the chairs) operation and the months spent watching Dom make pies in order to perfect the art door to Lucali would open at six on the dot and we were quickly ushered in a table near the front - close enough to the window for some natural light to blend with the candles, but also with a great view of Mark as he worked the dough and chopped ingredients in a nearly Zen-like fashion - head always up and watching the room as a stark contrast to Dom's nearly non-stop eye contact with the pie. With only two options on the blackboard - Pizza or Calzone - and perhaps ten total ingredients to top the pie we opted for a single pie to split amongst the four of us - half with artichoke, half with portabella. Â Watching Mark work the dough, top it carefully, and place it in the wood burning brick oven while my friends chatted I had no doubt it was going to be good - it was like watching a ballet - but I had no idea it was going to be the best pizza I've ever tasted. With a thin crust - crispy, light, and irregularly bubbled yet able to hold up to the ingredients with ease, sweet tomato sauce with a hint of smoke and basil, and handmade mozzarella at its base the pie was exemplary. Â Pliable yet toothsome, sweet yet savory, slightly soggy at the center but not oversaturated with oil - really, no, I can't top exemplary as a descriptor. Â Add on simple yet flawless mushrooms and sautÃ©ed artichoke hearts - my heart melted with each bite because I knew that at the end of the day I'd have to go back to eating Pizza that wasn't this good. With the bill ($26 for a single pie) paid and our flirty server heckling us when we suggested we were heading elsewhere for more pizza (note, Mark's brother recently opened a Pizzeria and we probably should have gone there too!) we made our way outside to find the line longer than when we entered - clearly others already knew what I'd just learned - that something this good is something worth waiting for.

You can not help but love a place that constantly evolves and whose owner(s) truly care about both their atmosphere and the product they are serving. I've lived in the neighborhood since this place first opened up, and have loved watching it's transformation into a full fledged day and night spot. I remember when they were eager to get an alcohol license and recently achieved that, I can't wait to see what's going to come next. Hearing the live music when I walk by, the aroma that wafts into the streets and the quality of coffee, food and wine make this spot one of my favorites in all of Brooklyn. Right next door is another coffee shop called Champion, one that's always been a more 'on the go' kind of place. I don't think their coffee is worth the price, and they aren't all that friendly. Milk and Roses has a friendly staff that are anything but stuck up, a personality type that seems to infiltrate some of the newer spots that have opened up in the neighborhood. I love seeing them, speaking with them and just enjoying the vibe inside. Â It's decorated with so much care, pride and real skill. My only gripe would be they don't accept cards, which makes it a bit inconvenient sometimes as there are no banks nearby to get cash and it's a bit annoying to have to pay those ATM fees just to get a coffee. If you are looking for a unique atmosphere, great food and drink and a friendly vibe...check out Milk + Roses! Their sandwiches are to die for, made with so much care (not in a toaster oven like next door). The newly renovated back yard is BEAUTIFUL!

Delicious! Went here recently for a quick lunch. Â The service is amazing. Â The waiters and staff are extremely social, helpful, and friendly. Â The ambiance is very warm and welcoming. Â  The food itself was really good. Â The sandwiches all looked and sounded great, we ended up only ordering two, which were splendid. Â The fries were a bit new for me. Â I've never actually seen or had such thinly cut fries. Â However, to my surprise, they were really good! I would definitely recommend Hillstone.

Had the Grand Slam curry. It was honestly fantastic. Really nice, small place for a quick bite to eat. The shrimp tempura was pretty crunchy and the pork katsu was done well. I recommend adding an egg to balance out how salty the dishes are.

YUM! If you like authentic Japanese food and noodles, you will have a great dining experience at Sobaya. We stumbled upon this place on a weekday afternoon, and I am glad we decided to eat here. Getting the lunch special is probably the best way to go. For about $16, you can choose a rice dish paired with a noodle dish (soba or udon, hot or cold). I got the Magurodon (tuna over rice), which was absolutely delicious. If you enjoy big pieces of raw fish, this dish is for you. I think this was the first time I had a maguro-don in over 5 years. Maybe even 8 or 10! The cold soba that I ordered with my magurodon was tasty as well. The two dishes combined are very filling and definitely worth the money. I cannot remember the last time I had such a filling lunch. Note: check-in on Yelp and receive a free bottle of Kirin beer or sake!

Don't understand what the fuss was about. My date and I ordered completely different meals and neither were good. This place seriously lacks salt. I have the 'legendary' blueberry pancakes, with a side of smoked bacon and the jalepeno corn bread. She had the fish tacos. We split the apple pie and each had a scoop of ice cream. The fish tacos fell apart at the first bite. They were goopy and lacked flavor. The blueberry pancakes were ok. The compote on top was good. But after a few bites of the overly-sweet pancakes were dying for some salt. I thought the bacon would provide that balance, but it's didn't. Even the apple pie lacked balance. All in all, really cute place, and they gave us scones on our way out, but I probably won't be back. BTW-The scones needed salt as well...

if i came here with a lot of people this place would have been fun. Â There is an abundance of space to stand and chat and sit around. Â I like the simplicity of the bar, but no drink specials???? No boiler?? QUE?? why not? Meh I think that I have better cheaper spots to go to however if I ever end up in the situation where I have a large group I will probably go there again. Â Otherwise my alcohol consumption will take place at a cheaper location that offers bartenders with better conversation like......International Bar.

-Lobster Claw Bloody Mary (amazeballs) -Conneticut Lobster Roll -Club Lobster Roll (the celery isn't too powerful but the chives make it decadent) -Lobster Mac & Cheese (I'd go here just to eat this. Portion is big, can share amongst 2 people although you won't want to). Cute, little, shady sitting area in the back, perfect for the May breeze. Lobster explosion in your mouth. Who doesn't love that?

Very disappointed with our meal here. The Burger was $19 which would be ok if it knocked our socks off. It came out very dry, definitely overcooked. One noticeable thing was the lack of fat in the meat, we really should have sent it back. Don't waste your money on the burger here. Â I ordered the "crispy" duck over kale and farro. The farro was excellent and was the star of the dish, not the duck. The duck was the furthest thing from "crispy" and the layer of fat under the skin had not been rendered off properly, it was also very poorly seasoned. It was however a good quality duck breast, just very poorly executed. Duck breast should be well seasoned with salt and pepper, skin side down in a cold pan, bring up the heat to medium and let the fat render off the skin, pour off excess fat and allow the duck to cook through 75% of the way on the skin, then flip over and finish meat side down for a minute or so. This gives a properly cooked duck breast with a nice crisp skin, not a soggy skin advertised as "crisp." The breast was bland, our waiter had told us it was one of their most popular dishes. The Chocolate Bread pudding was unimpressive, a warm oval chocolate muffin that was cooked well and was moist, the flavor was decent. The roasted peanut ice cream that accompanied the bread pudding was excellent, but the thin slice of crispy bread acting as a garnish was comical. The capper to the evening was getting charged $24 for 4 glasses of club soda with a splash of cran. At $6 each it became a matter of principle, now it was time to complain! The waiter indicated he thought it was crazy too, saying they gave us bottled soda water (we did not ask for bottled), he removed $12 from the bill. We are in the food industry and have moderate expectations. We thought we were in good hands as they mention their Executive Chef had consulted for the infamous ChefsThomas Keller and Alice Waters. Are we missing something???? Not sure I understand the reviews here

WHAAAAAT!!! I went to New York in January and I haven't reviewed this yet? WHAT WAS I THINKING!!!!!!! THIS WAS THE BEST PIZZA I HAVE EVER HAD.... and I have had a lot!!!! I went to John's on Bleecker a couple days before, because I heard that was the best... and it was GOOD... but this is better!! Their basic cheese pizza is basically a Margarita Pizza, fresh basil and mozzarella! Awesome! The crust was awesome too! It did suck though that their ATM was busted, and they don't accept credit cards. This is a reason alone to fly from California to Brooklyn! Oh... and expect to wait..... and to sit right next to random people. lol. i love new york!

Good food, long wait, and not everything was available. But im no complainer. Food was really dahm good. But I dont think many places are worth waiting an hour for and i love love love brunch! If i go to the city and wanna have good brunch I wont go back and wait and hour but I will go in and eat there food anytime without the wait. Wait blows food is great

Still can't get over the fact that they got rid of the ssam burrito...but I ordered 4 plates of the pork buns to make up for it, and they didn't dissappoint. Â Thought that the uni with tapioca was a little texturally strange, and wouldn't order it again. Â The flank steak was tastey, but possibly a bit too raw, which for me means almost purple. Â Overall a good meal, and definitely recommend for anyone, but especially for meat eaters as there are few dishes if any without it...also a little annoyed that they got rid of the mochi from the dessert menu. Â Bring back the burrito and mochi!

This is the best pizza in NY. End of discussion. If anyone tells you that is not true, you should no longer be friends with them. The square pie is better then the round pie but get both just to be safe.

UPDATED 4/8/14 This place is a chain. There is one that opened first in Brooklyn. I've been here 3x but will definately coming again and update my experience as they will soon be offering lunch menu. FAVORITES - Hibino Teriyaki Chicken $15 (generous with the meat, vegs change) - spicy scallop with roots $5 (tapa option but haven't seen it offered again) - grape veggie juice $3 (21 ingredients) - ice cream sandwich (green tea ice cream, strawberry, red bean) - argula with tofu skin (tapa option) PRO - new $5 tapa options daily - authentic japanese food - high chairs available - fresh fish - nice interior design - got to interact with the one of the chefs CON - inexperienced waitresses Â  Â  * waitress took forever to give the bill. Â  Â  * while we were enjoying our food, waitress would disturb us to walk through the Â  Â  Â  tight aisle when she could have walked through the other aisle. keep in mind we Â  Â  Â  have a stroller Â  Â  * water refill needed to be asked. Â  Â  * I needed to follow up with the waitress to give me my food that I asked to go - not childproof (a young child was sitting on a heavy stool and fell) - not all tapa options were available - many sushi rolls have shiso leaf which i'm allergic to (only spot had it though) - no kids menu - no written dessert menu - no staff says Arigatou gozaimasu/thank you for coming here - only 2 credit cards for 1 group NOTE The crowd seemed like - singles night on Thursday - family night on Friday - couples night on Monday Offers delivery Mon-Fri now. Fried pork entree was a little dry and using flaky bread would have been better.

I've had Yuca Bar in my bookmarks for a while now, and when me and my co-worker/buddy/foodie partner Shilpa decided to look for something to eat after leaving the office...we probably hit about 15 places in 2 city blocks before we decided to check my bookmarks and come here. SO glad we did. At first we were just outside and realized that it was Tapas. Â Neither one of us really wanted Tapas because we actually wanted to eat like normal people and not birds. Â But it was cold as hell, and there were a lot of people inside so we figured it must be good unless everybody was just trying to avoid the cold like us. So in we went. Â We were immediately met by a friendly hostess and sat at a table. Â The ambiance was cool and people's food looked GOOD! Â I was totally in at this point. The lady next to us had a hamburger that looked amazing, and there was incredible looking tapas all over the place. Â Good portions, prices not bad at all (most tapas average around 13 bucks but the portion sizes are cool...and i found out that on tuesdays its half off). Â Of course, it was monday. Â ah well. Turns out the lady's hamburger next to us was a vegetarian hamburger. Â She loses major cool points for that, but i had the real version and it was incredible. Â Shilpa had a pumpkin crusted salmon with potatoes that was SO good that i'll be going back soon to get what SHE got. Not more i can say about this place other than its a definite win. Â Go here w/friends, on a date, etc and you'll be happy you did...and the location in LES is right near everything anyways. Â  I'l definitely be back!

Junior's Restaurant is a delectable eatery, conveniently located less than three minutes from the center of Times Square. I spent my birthday at this restaurant on December 30 with a group of friends. We came for an early lunch around 11:30am. There is an option available where you can call ahead about half an hour for your arrival in order to have a table set for you when you arrive. This was very helpful because even though the restaurant was crowded when we arrived, we were seated immediately. The servers were incredibly friendly, and the atmosphere was warm and cozy with colorful decorations for the season. Everyone raved about the rich food and delicious sandwiches. To finish, I had a slice of creamy cheesecake with a cute candle. It was a perfect stop to relax, refuel, and warm up before heading out into cold, windy New York City.

Today was the first time I had a taste at Brooklyn Belly. The music was pumping and everyone seemed cool and relaxed very patiently waiting for their food. Everyone who stopped by had a smile and even a few dance steps. I had read the reviews and all were favorable. I had choices of fried shrimp, jerk chicken, conch fritters , I was on cloud nine. When it was my turn to get my food I did a two step out to the back seating area to enjoy my fried shrimp and jerk chicken. The batter on the shrimp was amazing and the jerk chicken was seasoned very nicely. This place is a must do.And when you do, I can guarantee that you will be back over and over, Amen !. You don't find this kind of vibe too often, so please don't sleep on it. And when you do check it out , let me know what you think !

The best Thai food! So cheap, and you get a great atmosphere to boot! Be prepared for a long wait that usually isn't quite as long as the time given to you (it's worth it). You can walk around the block while you wait- it's really cute and there's an AMAZING chocolate place by the theater where you can grab hot chocolate or a sweet snack. They sometimes pressure you to get up and go as soon as you are done eating (understandably since there's usually a line out the door), but if you just make it clear that you're going to take your time they'll back off. Oh, and did I mention HUGE portions, especially for NY?

Nice restaurant. Â I'm definitely coming back, had great energy and good food. Â I had the Garlic burger, it wasn't the best but lots of flavor. Â Fries were above average as well. Good service Good food Good crowd Like it.

Oh Meryl. Now I know why you decided to play a Polish woman in Sophie's Choice. It was definitely not to win an Oscar, that's for sure. Walking up Manhattan Ave, I recognized a restaurant that I didn't recognize. You know the food must be amazing if the owners had this conversation. Owner #1: Let's name it Polish for Polish. Owner #2: No, let's name it Smaczny, for tasty. Owner #1: These names, too easy. Does not seem like we fought for this restaurant. Owner #1: Okay, Lomzynianka, it is. Ordering Kielbasa, Hungarian pancakes, and pierogis, my man friend and I felt as though we had to scarf food down to prepare for the harsh winters ahead. Then we realized, we were not Polish Grizzly Bears and that we were not about to hibernate. The Hungarian pancakes were the highlight of the evening. If I could, I would dress him up in a tranny outfit and get him a spotlight (I use "him" because it was pretty meaty) Sorry Kielbasa and Pierogi, you are the back-up dancers. See, Poland? See what you do to me? You make me hallucinate about transexual pancakes! But it's so worth it.

Amazing experience! Imagine going home to mom's or grandma's only to discover she's taken up organic farming, charcuterie and gourmet cooking since you moved away from home. And she's laid out an impressive spread fresh from her garden and farm right onto your plate - and into your cocktail glass. The Green Table's food and drink are not only fresh and tasty, but the flavor profiles also are a sophisticated surprise turn after turn. And the entire staff makes you feel like a long-lost relative finally home to relax and take in a great meal. It's all a veritable treat! Oh, and remember to save room for dessert!

To rhyme Kefi is not so easy, Should it match with eye, or free? Anyway, I was late, my friend early, I found him below, not too surly. The lack of windows though could've been cause enough, despite the shelves of pottery and dishware. Â Oh, Kefi! Did I pronounce it correctly? I ordered the striped bass, fried to crisp, juicy, with mass. Not overmuch, with scallions chopped, olives & taters which the fish topped. Overall a good dish, just not delish. The service was friendly, my friend thought nosy - questions at the end about his meal, his stomach turned. T'was goat cheese, too late he'd learned. I'd come back to Kefi: sides, the dessert I'd try. The uptown locale is not so easy, though it'd count as an odyssey.

Bouley is a top notch expensive restaurant. The food is very good, makes you want more. We did a prefix menu tasting, and the service was outstanding. My boyfriend even said that his complimentary walnut bread was the best bread he ever tasted. My experience was good. Overall this place has a more romantic/intimate field to it.

I've been going to Halal Guys since 2006. Â Price went from $5 a platter to $6. Â They currently add onions on top of the chicken they serve. Â Make sure you tell them that you don't want onions if you don't like onions.

Nice pick. I ordered the champagne with passionfruit and strawberries, shrimp in plum sauce appetizer and the spicy basil fried rice. Everything tasted good. The drink just tasted like rose or something, nothing spectacular. The food was relatively cheap, particularly for nyc. The location is a trendy street in Hells Kitchen. Right near broadway. Â Yuppie crowd. The place is really tiny, but the service was very fast.
All i need to say is that the place is great ! ... starting with the service to the food to the atmosphere ! great spot to visit and enjoy a great meal ! keep it up guys !!

This place lives up to the hype. We went mid-week around 3pm, an off-time, and it was about a 15 minute wait in line. I am sure most times, the line stretches down to the water, but we were lucky. Tables are nice, not overly big, but all parties sit comfortably. Staff is great. We ordered a small pepperoni pie and it was cooked to perfection. Loved the crust, it wasn't too thick or undercooked. They use San Marzano tomatoes and sauce which is always the best. It was delicious. The bill for lunch for two: Â pepperoni pizza and one Ice Tea: $22.00 with tip. Not bad, and worth it! Â I reccomend trying to eat here at least once.

The food is great and addicting, and you get a crap load of it for only $6. I like the mixed chicken and lamb. You are guaranteed that the food is fresh because of the sheer amount of people ordering it-- they are constantly cooking new batches of meat and rice. However, the serving size is so huge that it's easy for me to want to vomit as I scrape the last few bites out of the foil bowl. I overdid it and ate this two weeks in a row, so now I can only stomach this once every few months.

I don't get what all the fuss is about! For price point and just what other restaurants there are in the neighborhood, the product should just be better. I'd take a walk to Washington ave and hit up sunshine co. Almost the same thing just way better executed!

Very high quality sandwich shop, specializing in Italian-style subs, except Godzilla-sized and pretty delicious. Â DeFonte's is very hard to find, as in smack-in-the-middle-of-nowhere-hard, but it seems to always be busy, especially around lunch time which speaks volumes about the value for the money. Speaking of which, a full-sized sandwich is equal to nearly two sandwiches almost anywhere else and costs almost as much as two sandwiches as well. Â Seriously, a full sandwich here will make a Subway's footlong look like a kid's meal and in comparison, taste like a McDonald's burger tastes in relation to a real hamburger. I was too chicken to try out the eggs and potato sandwich that everyone raves about but my next trip will definitely see me holding one of those bad boys. This place is strictly take-out, so don't go expecting table service. Â Order at the counter, pay for it and go. Â Since you'd probably be driving, I'd suggest hitting the wharf at the near-by Fairway on the other end of Red Hook. Â They have some nice tables by the water that you can sit at as long as you're shopping there as well; I'd suggest a nice peach for dessert. If you're really into sandwiches or just want to discover what a truly excellent sandwich is please do yourself a favor and go find DeFonte's. Â You won't be disappointed.

Ridiculously good. Like, explosion in your mouth kind of good. Things to note: 1) Absolutely make reservations - this place is so tiny (barely seats 10) so it will, inevitably, be quite packed 2) In fact, it's so small that they have no bathroom so make sure to handle your business before you come here (or else you'll have to visit the bodega across the street) 3) Cash only 4) Bring a bottle of wine with you - they don't sell alcohol 5) Come hungry & don't leave without trying the homemade doughnuts! 6) I wouldn't compare this to a Michelin rated restaurant but for the location, quality & price, it definitely deserves 5 stars We had: Appetizers: Wild Mushrooms (yummy but could be skipped), Mac & Cheese with Truffle Oil (if you like smokey flavors, you'll love this version), Pommes Frites (soo fresh & the accompanying homemade ketchup is on another level) Entrees: Kimchi Buillabaisse (this dish epitomizes the cuisine here - never thought korean/french fusion would taste soo good), Lamb Shank (so rich in flavor) and a Kobe Beef Burger (my fiance loved it). The attention to detail is superb. Dessert: Citrus doughnuts (homemade, light & so fresh) We had an amazing dinner and will definitely be back soon.

Let me just say "AMAZING". If you ever want a quick bite to eat Â and friendly smile. Go to Dig Inn. Â And if your ever in need of a sandwich. Go to Kay Kay. She is the best. When she gave me my sandwich she said " I made it with love so love every bite" and Iloved every bite of that steak and avacado sandwich. I'm getting another one tomorrow.

Cute ambiance and extensive wine menu- tho mostly by the bottle. This is more of an upscale restaurant (no happy hours or specials). The Beet Salad was OK, but the fish tacos were awesome!! The reason for 2 stars: The staff. Not outright rude, just completely unfriendly. The bar was full when we got there or my friend and I would have sat there to talk and share some bites. There are probably 7 dining tables in the place, and only 1 was taken when we arrived at 6:30 on a Thursday. At about 7:30, we were asked if we wanted dessert now because the table was reserved. Um... we had 4 plates, two glasses of wine, its been an hour, the place was empty and we have to leave? They also never asked how the food was, or the typical restaurant stuff. Overall it was fine, but it wouldn't be my first choice to go back to with all the other great restaurants in the area.

Brunch was delicious. Â Awesome ambiance for lady's day out. Â Unlimited mimosa for $14.00, Â Saturdays only. Â  I ordered sausage (chicken anjouile), grits, scrambled eggs, and a side of home style potatoes.
Happy hour on drinks and food is 4-7 everyday inc weekends :-)
Probably the best Brooklyn spot for a viet sandwich. Â The service is great also. Â I always ask for extra spicy and they gave me a small bag of green peppers to DIY if they didn't add enough.
This place is far from where I live, but totally worth the trip. Cheese under sauce? Deliciously different.

Crab meat & pork dumpling - UNBELIEVABLE! So good. My family has lived in Yokohama, Japan and has tried dim sum everywhere and never tasted such delicious dumpling before! And for such reasonable price too! We have yet to try all of their 22 dim sums but the ones we've tried so far (wonton Szechuan dumplings and shrimp dumplings) were wonderful. There are usually lines but the wait is not too long and definitely worth the wait!

really great food. Â i especially appreciate that they have only a few options on their menu (plenty of them--i just don't like being overwhelmed with choices at a restaurant) but all the ones i've tried are excellent. Â loss of one star because it's pretty pricey.

Great location if you are looking for an upscale Latin food. My second time at Calle Ocho, as usual, friendly staff members, great appetizers, awesome drinks, and that YUCA bread, oh boy I could not get enough of it. (I wish they would market that). However, I was bit disappointed with main courses, Mar y tierra (Too salty), Salmon (My friend liked it), Vaca Frita al caballo ( the meat was so tough that you had to chew about 100 times) and lastly Gaucho (Gnocchi was too greasy, and another tough meat). Moreover, the staffs were friendly but they were rushing us, coming by every second asking if we were done with our dishes, I was annoyed by it. Another weird thing is that, they knew we were celebrating my friend's b-day and they asked who the b-day girl was but they didn't really make it special for her. I mean I'm not asking for OUTBACK B-day cheers with b-day song but bringing a little candle with the dessert we ordered would have been a nice touch. oh well, I give Calle ocho three stars

WOWza!! Â This place has THE best bluebery pancakes in the city! Â It's busy all the time, especially for weekend brunch, so expect a wait. Â Good time to go is during the week. Â Really well done comfort food. Â Totally fresh and delicious. Â If you dont' want pancakes (whats wrong with you?) Â I totally recommend the crab cake sandwich or po'boy. Â Make sure to try a few of their pastries too. Â The biscuits are sent from some Southern heaven! Â Basically, you just can't go wrong here**

They have a penchant for saying "no" to customers for off-menu requests. ("can i have a little extra broth?" "no.") Â Their welcome shouting scared my girlfriend a bit. Â But their product is very very tasty and a welcome haven on a cold day. Â  Wait wasn't that bad. Â Cute table made of the insta-ramen. Â RIP the guy who invented that fuzz. For me, the oft-cited Akamaru was SOoooOOOooo UuuuMamiiiii. Â  Best ramen base since my days at Halu in San Jose. For the lady, a novel taste in the not-on-the-menu vegetarian ramen. Â Not sure what that base was made of, but it was good. Â (It disappeared into a belly before it could be accurately IDed). We also caught the waitress NOT speaking japanese.

Wow. Just... I don't even know how to begin. Minca might possibly be one of the best ramen places in New York City. Granted, I have not tried all the ramen places in the city, but if there is another place that has the delicious, rich, flavorful, porky broth, the amazingly tender chashu, the generous portions and great service that Minca has, PLEASE TELL ME NOW and I will high tail it over there like it is my job (I wish it was my job to try all the ramen places in NYC. If only. A girl can dream, can't she?) But seriously, this place has got it going ON. Sure, it may be small, somewhat stuffy (no air conditioning) and very different from the hip, modern Ippudo, but it's a nice change of pace. It's not at all pretentious; they just get down to the good stuff. It's very homey and personal. When you first walk in (happy to see the small "Minca" sign after walking quite a distance from the train station), it welcomes you with a whiff of the intoxicating aroma of ramen and gyoza. You sit down and enjoy the glass of cold gen mai cha while looking over the menu. You order the pork gyoza because all your fellow yelpers raved about their gyoza. And when that gyoza comes, you will be pleasantly surprised at how thin and tender the gyoza skin is and how juicy and flavorful the insides are. It is delicious and you will want to eat the whole plate, but you must be nice and share (unless you came alone... then I say, GO FOR IT!) And then you await the ramen. When that ramen is placed in front of you, you will drool a little. It's okay, no one will judge you (I certainly won't). Your stomach will rumble in anticipation. Please, just start eating already. Do not delay the gratification that will follow. I ordered the shoyu ramen and my friend ordered the basic (salt and garlic flavored) and both were delicious. Her broth was so garlicky and flavorful, I kind of wish I had ordered the basic. But the shoyu was also really good. The whole meal was just really enjoyable. The noodles were a little firmer than I was used to, but it wasn't necessarily a bad thing. The chashu was wonderfully tender and it melted in my mouth. And I love the bamboo shoots too. It all went together so well. And being Asian, I was happy about the prices for a bowl of ramen here compared to Ippudo or Momofuku Noodle Bar. I intend on making more trips back to this place. So please, do yourself a favor right now and try the ramen at Minca. You're welcome, World.

I could eat sesame pancakes with veg. ALLLLLLLL day if i lived in lower manhattan. Get two and that's pretty much a meal right there. I got one with just vegetables, and one with beef. Not a fan of the beef, so i just removed it and had two with just veggies. Cucumbers, carrots, cilantro, and a chewy, almost naan-ish sesame bread taco pita fusion thingy. Â Oh my god. And they're only about .75 cents. I have yet to try their actual dumplings, and you know what? i don't even care. i'm sure they're good.

Looks like I'm just preaching to the choir... This a nice spot and worth a repeat visit. We arrived at 6:30pm on a Saturday and the place was about 1/3rd full. Cool interior with a warm Spanish vibe. Quiet and easy to carry on a conversation. Great food - particularly the avocado and the calamari tapas. Attentive service albeit almost too quick on the delivery (the dishes came rapid fire so we ended up eating much faster than normal). Our server recommended a great bottle of red but the name escapes me. My brother in-law picked up the tab so no info on cost
One if the most pleasant restaurants in the city. Best spot for a romantic dinner. If the whether is nice they will uncover the rooftop, it's simply gorgeous. Paella was to die for.

You will not expect this place to be that GREAT from the outside. I have been living in this neighborhood for few months now and I have been going to restaurants surrounding this one but never dared to go in. But I should have! The garden is great on a nice day. I went in for late lunch with few friends and everything we ordered exceeded our expectations. Amazing Lentil soup, fresh made pita, and amazing Beet salad. Try Pitza! I am lactose intolerant so I can never really enjoy eating normal Pizza but PitZa is great!!!

I heart Jacob's Pickles. Â  Their food is splendid. Â I've had dinner, drinks, and brunch at Jacob's and they were all fantastic. Â  Things to enjoy while at Jacob's: - honey chicken with spicy pickles on a biscuit sandwich - the greatest cheese grits of your life (will ruin all other cheese grits for you) - the chocolate bread pudding - the fried pickles (or really any of their pickles) - the spicy margarita - the bacon, eggs, and cheese biscuits - their root beer selection :) Things I can't wait to try: - the turkey leg dinner - the mac 'n cheese Jacob's Pickles (along with Cotta) have become my newest "go to" places on the UWS. Â Thank you for being so awesome!

Had a really sweet first date here in August. As usual, I'm the one that gets to pick the restaurant. In other words, it has become my duty to choose the right place or I will be blamed. I haven't had Belgian food since I was in Belgium three years ago. I'm not sure if it'd be just to make the comparison. He's a frequent gym-goer so he was trying to lay off the carbs tonight, plus he said he already ate! LOL what the heck dude. Anyway ... I ordered a full pot of mussels, which seems to be their most popular thing. They were so good, I did manage to force him to eat some, plus the fries. I also got the skirt steak entree because I'm fat and always hungry. It was perfectly seared (grilled) and I almost ate the whole thing. After they cleared the table, we stayed and enjoyed a few more beers. One after another, until I decided I was going to puke. Awesome night!

If you're over 25 or are dining with more than 4 people, stay away. Staff is unnecessarily rude and ridiculously arrogant. Bar and wine selection is very limited. I've had better tapas in Costco from the free sample counters. The upstairs "private room", which requires a walk through the kitchen, is at best a fire trap and turned out not to be so private. However, if you're a 20 something that is into trendy scenes and paying top dollar for the privilege of being abused by a team of self absorbed morons, then you are going to love this place!

I came to this amazing restaurant because of the reviews my fellow yelpers have given this place and they were not wrong. Â This was one of the best meals I have had in a long time. First, its a small restaurant with fantastic music. Â The people who work there are very nice, efficient, answer questions, and the chef's wife (owner I assume) and the chef come around to talk and check on everything. My husband and I started with the steak tartare app and the pickled mussels. Â I have to say, the mussels were a surprise. Â They were served in a jar with homemade butter and little pieces of bread...amazing!! Â I have never had mussels this way but I will be back to have them this way again. Â The steak tartare was perfect, presented with a cracked egg with the yolk in it to mix in, tremendous. Next, my husband had the ribs and I had the scallops. Â The scallops were cooked perfectly and the ribs were some of the best ribs we have ever had. Â We ordered a side of hand cut fries which were again amazing but served with three homemade sauces. Â My too favorite were the plum ketchup and the bacon something...let's call it bacon delicisioness (however you would spell that). We finished this off with a bread pudding that had a small scoop of vanilla ice cream and a slight orange marmalade in it. Â  The total bill was around $160 with tip and drinks, a little pricey but I would pay it again! Overall this is such a nice addition to the slope and desperately needed. Â You have to try this place, believe me you won't regret it.

to say i really like this charming place would be an understatement. the decor was eclectic, simpatico and amusing. we were fortunate to be sitting next to the windows and discussed at some length the way the light hit the windows of the building across the street, which in turn reflected golden beams of sunlight onto the mirrors on the wall of the restaurant, which in turn bathed the lovely senorita l. in a rosy glow. we also had a silly discussion about a strange but amusing statue in the room, of a nude woman. her head was disproportionately small; her facial features were rudimentary in contrast to the rendering of her torso. what amused us most though, was the elaborate and peculiarly stylized depiction of her pubic hair. it is a petite place, perhaps a bit too petite if one has claustrophobic inclinations. i wonder if the name of the restaurant is ironically redundant as it is in english. the server was a wonderful character. she had a kindness and joie de vivre about her, that contributed to the rosy glow and bon ami ambiance. briana m. was kind enough to go out and buy a fine malbec that was perfect with our meal. imagine my surprise when i ordered the thai curry cod, and it was as fabulous as mr. unlucky's secret soup surprise! i guess great minds think alike. the cod had a perfect texture and each bite of gingery, coconut rich, brothy morsel was savored.

Awesome, awesome, awesome! Went here on a whim one night and everything was fantastic. Â Truly everything. The shrimp with guacamole appetizer is my favorite. Â Get here early because there was a line out the door by 7 pm on a Thursday.

*Brunch Review* Our original plan last Saturday was to try Penelope's for brunch but the two hour wait for a seat was too damn long and we were too damn hungry. Â We were surprised to learn that ilili had a brunch menu so we took the 10 minute walk over. Â There was no wait at all. Our group that day included vegetarians and one person with a dairy allergy. Â Our waiter was very thorough in pointing out what items were safe to eat for all of us. Â We all decided to go with their $28 pre-fixed brunch. Â You get a choice of coffee or juice, one cocktail, one main dish and a side. Â I went with the braised lamb shank and cubed fries. Â The fries were very salty but the braised lamb shank is what really turned this from a 4 star review to a 5 star. Â I tried a piece of a friend's grilled beets and that was delicious as well. Â As I mentioned, this place was not even on our radar for brunch but it turned out to be a wonderful plan B. For those with little ones: Â There is room for strollers in the coat closet. Â They have plenty of high chairs and you can use the ottomans in the restrooms as a changing table.

We went to that restaurant yesterday and we had an amazing time! The service and food were both wonderful and we appreciated the corner table for the two of us as it was very romantic and cozy. The artichoke appetizer was outstanding as was the Porcette. Our waiter informed us it takes time to prepare and the dish was totally worth the wait. Also enjoyed the special cocktail for desert which was like drinking a chocolate covered cherry. We will definitely go back.

This place was good, but I think it is overhyped. Â There are many different types of sauces, but they weren't that amazing. If you peek into the kitchen, you will see jars and jars of mayonnaise. Â The French fries are thick and made from real potatoes (you can see bags and bags of potatoes in the back as well). Â They use the same oil to fry loads of potatoes, and I'm not sure how often they change the oil... We tried the roasted eggplant, which was OK. Â (You can ask to try different sauces and they will give you the end bits of French fries to eat with them). Â We ended up getting the Parmesan Peppercorn and the Mango Chutney on regular fries (which is the smallest option they have) ($4). It was more than enough for us. Â If you get sauces on the fries, rather than in a separate container, it's only $1.50 more and they layer the sauces for you if you want more than one sauce (so they put in a layer of fries, and then a sauce, another layer of fries and then a sauce). Â If you get sauces in a separate container, it's more expensive. Â You can also opt to just get the fries with mayo and ketchup, which are free. Â  Seating is extremely limited so plan accordingly, especially if it's snowing outside.

OMG what a disappointment! We went specifically on the 4.5 yelp rating. Haricot vert salad to open was just fine. My wild salmon was overcooked and tasted farmed. The cioppino as a DISASTER! Each piece of seafood had that unmistakeable taste of notfresh. Overcooked AND notfresh! WTF?! We're just flabbergasted that a restaurant so highly recommended could disappoint so thoroughly. I hate to hate on a cute nice establishment like this, and maybe they had an off night, but...whatever. If you're a restaurant that specializes in seafood, make sure you serve it fresh.

Great addition to the neighborhood, have been wanting to stop in since they opened a few months ago and finally made it. Worth the wait! Split the Crab Leg/Shrimp combo, Crab sliders and Crab Roll with the bf and enjoyed everything. Super tasty and delicious! The Crab legs and shrimp had a nice, spicy, cajun seasoning. The Crab Roll was stuffed with crab meat and the sliders were fried to perfection. The spot itself is super welcoming, it has the feel of a small seaside crab shack with friendly staff on Franklin Ave. The lovely owner was there and made sure everyone was enjoying their food. Will be back SOON!

So strange .. The food was bad ... Quality was bad .. Prepared ..bad ... It was just disgusting really. I feel horrible really bc the service was amazing . They were so sweet.. To the point where I couldn't tell them the food made me nauseous... The wine was cheap..so much so that I didn't finish it !! (Which is wild). I had the pappardelle and oxtail- tasted like cheapp noodles with canned beef soup... My friend had the veal meat balls with penne.. - tasted like tomato paste and turkey meatballs... And there was this powdery grit to it .... I ordered chianti... Tasted like warm pomegranate juice ... Before we even sat.. And before we were given the menu.. He offered bread and oilives.... Â  Of course we obliged....somehow I find it strange that it was on the bill.... Yelp you've failed me here...

If you're headed to a show, Junior's is a decent spot to grab a bite to eat. Â I was flying solo so it was easy for me to grab a seat at the bar while others were waiting for a while. Â Be warned that there will be a lot of food served to you so you better be ready. I got a tossed green salad to start and that could have been more than half of my meal. Â I also got the steakburger which was enormous and just ok. Â I had to get the cheesecake since they're famous for it and it didn't disappoint. Â It was definitely rich and I wish I hadn't eaten so much beforehand so I could have really enjoyed it.

I live a couple of blocks away and am desperately seeking an alternative to Grimaldi's (who's lines out the door are a lesson in the value of strong branding - not quality; Grimaldi's pizza truly stinks these days.) I really wanted to love Juliana's when it opened. Ordered takeout a couple of weeks ago and - while it was immediately apparent that the pizza is better than Grimaldi's - it's not good enough to bring tears to my eyes OR make me a regular. But the real problem is the disorganization: took 30 (!) minutes to get my takeaway. Guys at Juliana's - a piece of advice: get a professional to manage the floor. You're missing out on an opportunity to stick it to your neighbors (which I know you're dying to do.) Their product has jumped the shark but you're not making any friends with the mess and long waits. Meanwhile, I'm going to revisit Igancio's down the block...
This is my favorite greek restaurant in NYC because of the subtle medely of authentic Greek flavors. Favorite Meal: Greek Salad or Octopus Salad to start followed by Lamb Shank and then Kefi Coffee.
vodka pizza, classic pepperoni pizza, the chicago beef sando special, and calamari....ALL AMAZEBALLS!!

My hubby and I recently went for our eating through nyc date night to this charming and cozy restaurant based on a recommendation. Â Read up a bit and also noticed the "Critics' Pick" Â designation from New York Mag which I find always a reliable pick. Â We heard about the Italian with Korean influence concept and thought it'd be an interesting pick for our latest food adventure (esp for my Italian hubby and Korean me!) ~ and what a beautiful and delicious adventure it was. Â You would never know from the front of the restaurant which looks like a quaint bar that past the bar it opens into a dining area set with a zen decor with a view of a pretty garden.
