Â Starting with our refreshing cocktails (get the "Yes Ma'am" ~ a watermelon concoction which hit the spot for our night out!), then the light and fresh sashimi tuna with beets and sesame starter, the pasta was cooked perfectly and my husband relished his charred fig duck rigatoni and the pea and truffle agnolotti made me a happy vegetarian. Â A Â MUST is the cheese plate which included the most glorious cheese which we had to ask the waiter about and was told it was a cheese with truffles which had the most decadent flavor. Â We are cheese lovers and we had never had such a cheese! Â The food was so artistically presented and the service was great. Â Finished with a light strawberry delight of a cake. Â The owner Simon stopped by to check in on us and was really warm and made us feel at home. Â It was really a creative and easy fusion of flavors ~ we will definitely be back for a dinner with friends and for sure for more delectable cocktails on a much needed night!

The food here was good, the dessert was even better! They had an amazing 2 layer chocolate and hazelnut cake that was plated beautifully. The servers were really nice. The ambience of this restaurant was great and they are kid friendly. They even have a kids menu options.

I went with two other people on a Friday night. We got there at 7:30 and put our name on the list. I thought we would have to wait maybe 2 hours but we were seated within 45 minutes. We each got a pork bun which was delicious (Japanese mayo makes anything good) and then I got the extra spicy ramen. The extra spice comes on the side so don't be too scared by the multiple chili peppers on the menu. I added most of the offered spice and it was pretty spicy, but delicious. The main disappointing thing for me was the small amount of meat, I got pork and it was just two small pieces. For the price I expected more meat.

Quaint, casual little restaurant in Nolita. Unfortunately, our party of 6 had to wait about 45 minutes to be seated at 8 on a weeknight, but we sat outside at their smaller tables and enjoyed a bottle of wine while we waited. The avocado toast appetizer was unique, as it had chili pepper on it as well, but the main standout was my couscous entree, which had chicken and sausage, blended with pine nuts, raisins and peppers. I would definitely return for great meal at an affordable price. *Cash only
Great crepes! Tried the nutella with strawberries crepe, yum! Teeny Tiny little place...
Some dishes were okay but not great. Cheap atmosphere inside, Mexican waiters(bath boys?) were annoying.

You enter Dos Toros, and it's like you've stepped through a door into San Francisco. The burritos remind me so much of what you can find in the Castro in San Fran. Friendly service, compostable silverware/cups AND delicious, fresh, wholesome food. A simpler, more straight-forward concept than Chipotle (there is one salsa). You can't go wrong.

An entire restaurant devoted to meatballs? Heck yeahhhh! I met my friend for dinner here and since it was just the two of us we didn't have a problem finding a table. The menus are cool because they are laminated and you get to check off what you want using an erasable pen. Our waiter was really nice, brought us water right away, and pointed out some of the highlights of the menu. I ordered the the kitchen sink salad with the spicy pork balls and the classic tomato sauce. The salad sounded great because they put the meatballs on top of some greens, which helps you avoid carbo-loading (too much pasta...) Service was pretty fast and the food was delicious! The salad came with chickpeas, beets, slaw, and some sort of pickled cucumber. The salad was fresh and peppery and I don't usually like beets but these were really great because they didn't taste as earthy as they usually do. I ate every single bite of veg on my plate. The meatballs were pretty good, they could have used a few more spices, but the tomato sauce was really yummy. I would definitely come back and try some of their other balls! I loved how their menu let you create whatever combination you wanted: sandwich, meatballs on their own, salad, on top of pasta... you name it you can do it!

Cash only place... only flaw once again but the customer service was great. We got here at 930 on a Sunday and it was still relatively packed. The pizza was also really good. 2 small pies were good for 4 people... well 2 of them were girls who didn't eat much.. lol! We had one margarita pie and 1 half white half margarita. We put sauteed spinach and panchetta on the full margarita pie and pepperoni with mush rooms on the other and yes it was as expected! GREATNESS! I also wanted to try their clam pie but we were pretty low on cash so that didn't work out too well. Overall, I'd come back here for pizza but I wouldn't want to wait on that long line during rush hours

I was nervous because we decided on this place based on a recommendation, friends were coming in from out of town and I couldn't bare the thought of (a) displeasing them or (2) making them wait 2 hours for food. Thankfully, neither of my fears was recognized. We got there just in time (7:30) before the place got out-of-control crowded. We had antipasti Gaeta and Pomodorro to start. The Pomodorro was like a delicious, enormous bruchetta with pignoli (YUM) and the Gaeta was a salad with smoked mozzarella cheese and pears. Our entrees were the Salmon ravioli, goat cheese ravioli and the fettuccine roma. I had the Roma and it was a fantastic, garlic-y pasta with sun-dried tomatoes, mushrooms and artichoke. Everyone's ravioli was scrumptious and plates were cleaned all-around! We had the house red and it was also tasty (and affordable at $22/bottle). I wanna give this place 4.5 stars. IT WAS FANTASTIC. Seriously exceeded my expectations. Our friends were glad they went with my recommendation and I LOVE when that happens ;)

Bumping my review up a star--Cho Dang Gol is excellent. Â Not sure what happened the first time I came, but that was for lunch and this follow-up was for dinner, and dinner was the bomb. Before we continue, a glossary: - dubu: tofu - cham: soft - haemul: seafood - soondubu or sundubu: spicy tofu stew, which is one of the things Cho Dang Gol is recommended for. Â Their menu doesn't call the stews "soondubu" specifically, but if it's called "something something dubu" and it's in the stew section, it's soondubu. Â Or, in any case, it's what you want if you wanted soondubu. - pajeon: scallion pancake. (Per Jason S., pa = scallion and jeon = pancake. Et voila.) - kimchi: if you don't know this, who are you? Where are you from? Are you a Martian? If so, can I see your ship? If you take me to Mars with you, will I be able to leap great distances like John Carter? On Mars, will there be a beautiful scientist-princess waiting for me, and will she inexplicably speak English with a deep, soulful British accent? Â Will she maybe know what kimchi is? And if she does, how come you don't?[1] Back to the review: My tablemate and I split: - The kimchi & beef cham dubu and - The vegetable cham dubu. Â  They were terrific! Â Small stone pots of bubbling, spicy red stew. Â The kimchi & beef was the more powerfully flavorful of our two bowls, but the veg option was good on its own. Â  Note: I'm told the haemul cham dubu is the best, so if you're a fan of fruits de mer, consider that. Also note: Cho Dang Gol is known for its tofu. Â They make it on the premises, apparently. Â I've never liked soft tofu but, here, I relished it. Â I'm told they make it softer and crumblier than usual, and while I haven't had tofu enough to compare, I'd certainly believe theirs is excellent. For an appetizer: a small haemul pajeon. Â I've found these pancakes are usually greasy and flat, but here the dish was a thick, chewy cake colorfully striated with long stalks of scallion and full of seafood. Â It's filling: the small is more than enough for two people, and that combined with the banchan and the two dubus stuffed us. Cho Dang Gol tops off your meal with a serving of spicy, if slightly too sweet, ginger tea. Â  If I had any complaint it's that the ginger tea was spicier than the dubu, which they warned us would be spicy. Â (It might be spicy for you if you grew up on a 19th century potato farm in the Ukraine but if your tongue has ever so much as tasted a dollop of Cholula and not recoiled in agony, I'm thinking you'll find this stew more flavorful than spicy.) It's not a beautifully designed sort of place but it is cozy and casual, with friends, dates, and families throughout. Â It's a great place for a cold evening. ---- [1] John Carter reference thought process: Kimchi is red. Mars is red. John Carter was set on Mars. I watched John Carter the other day. QED.

Malatesta, oh where have you been all my life?! This place is wonderful! My friend told us about how her coworker (from Italy) raved about this place, stating that it's the only decent Italian restaurant in the city. Boy was he right! I came here with 2 of my girlfriends. First of all, they're very true to the Italian feel. No air conditioning, strict window ventilation. You have the option of indoor or outdoor seating, and it's pretty crowded. Go with the outdoor, it will definitely make your day. We started with the bruschetta. The bread was crispy and soft, all at once. The tomatoes and basil were definitely fresh. Talk about a great choice! We then ordered their special for the day- Lobster Fettuccine and a Ravioli Al Formaggio. My friend loved the ravioli, she said it was absolutely great. My other friend and I had the lobster, talk about "worth your money". They gave us huge chunks of lobster, the pasta and sauce combinations worked wonders in my mouth. Add a little black pepper and olive oil, you're basically set for life! The service was very decent, had them refilling our water and bread. They were very prompt and quick, given how crowded the restaurant was. It also seemed like a great place to have a night time dinner date, a very romantic feel to the ambiance. My only issue with this place was the odd location. It's next to the Hudson River on the west side. Not so accessible by train. Had quite the hectic walk just trying to find it, but definitely worth it. I highly recommended!

This place is unbelievable! I cannot speak for all of their meals, but the Gorgonzola Burger is mouth-watering. I just booked another trip out to NYC this fall and will definitely be visiting the Spotted Pig. It is great to go to a spot on vacation and not be rubbing elbows with all of the other tourists. This place is packed with actual New Yorkers in a fun part of town. The drinks are great and so are the appetizers, but be warned, it gets packed. I guess if it isn't packed it isn't good. Don't forget to run across the street to Magnolia Bakery afterwards!

Good service, good food and no lines! Â I have always been more partial to soba, so to be fair, I might be a bit...biased. Â I rather like their hot soba noodle soup dishes, especially the one served with duck and scallions. Â While not terribly complicated, it is a good warming dish for a winter day. Â Their offerings are varied enough and well priced during lunch and they have some interestingly varied beer selections (try the buckwheat beer at least once). Â Overall, this restaurant can be relied on to please with decent service and consistently good food, just so long as you like soba.

My absolute favorite pizza in Brooklyn..the square slices are to die for...they are best fresh out of the oven. Â This pizza is sooooo good it's no wonder the place is always packed. Â If you are in Brooklyn you MUST go here

The samizen lunch special is the best deal. For $11 you get a nice assortment of sashimi, tempura, soba, and some other dishes. Consistently excellent. Wish there was a greater range of appetizers. But they know what they are good at, so I can't fault them for sticking to their strengths.

I came to Tia Pol on a recent trip to NYC with my boyfriend, his uncle and a few of his uncle's friends. Â It's very small but has a great feel and the food was delish. Â This is where I had squid ink for the very first time, and, although I had a slight allergic reaction to it, it was heavenly. Â Be sure to get the roast piglet and the croquettes. Â Other stellar things on the menu are the razor clams and the blood sausage. Â I could definitely see myself here for a happy hour and not leaving for 4 hours because of good food, drink and ambiance. Great first date place.

OK... I'm doing it... I'm giving a 5-star review with reckless abandon. Recently came here for brunch and this place is wonderful. Everything from the ambiance, decor, drinks, food, and service. They manage to perfectly strike the balance between laid back and sophisticated, with attention given to every detail. Bonus: the blood mary was one of the better ones I have had in Williamsburg.

this place has the absolute best tacos among several Mexican/taco joints in the neighborhood. Â Every taco on the menu is excellent, and I have had them all. Â My favorites are the fried chicken, fried shrimp , el pastor, and brisket. Â and lets not forget about the nachos. Â the nachos are smothered in delicious gooey cheese, a whole avocado, creama, and other goodness. Â i would be lying if i said i didn't have the nachos as my dinner once or twice. Â  and you get fresh frozen maragritias, Mexican beers, and Mexican sodas and juices also.

Believe the hype. Â Hit up MQ's at 3:30 on a Saturday afternoon and avoided the crush, grabbed a table for 4 with no wait, and proceeded to excessively over-order...except it was so good we managed to polish it off. Â  Rack of ribs had an awesome dry rub, balanced and perfectly crunchy. Â The pulled pork was moist with lots of bark. Â The wings were good but I didn't think they fit in; they had a spicy Asian style sauce Â with ginger and scallion notes; it looked like the 1/2 chickens were simply smoked, which I would have preferred. Â For me, brisket is always king, and this was a Mighty order that rivals Hill Country's moist brisket for the #1 bite of meat in NYC. Â  The beans had lots of burn ends, the sweet potato casserole was as much dessert as it was a side, and both mayo and vinegar based slaws successfully cut through the richness of the meat. Despite the apparent difficulty getting a table and limited side options, Mighty Quinn's earns a respectable 2-seed in my personal NYC BBQ power rankings.

My favorite delivery place in Hell's Kitchen. Â Try the Brasil and the Hawaiian empanadas and especially the fig, caramel and cheese dessert empanada. . Â It can be difficult to grab a seat in the small space if you eat in, but the pitchers of sangria are enormous and pretty tasty.

the yakitori here is so delicious, specially with some sake and beer to cleanse your palate with. Probably one of the best yakitori places I've been to in nyc. Start off with a cold dish by ordering the salmon siokara and then work your way onto the grilled meats, try as many different ones as you can. I liked all the chicken and beef ones. Their amakara chicken is delicious too.

The brisket is pretty on point. This place in general is a good idea that just needs a little fine tuning. I really think this place could be great. Cut a star for the pulled pork. Call me old fashioned but that ish should be shredded, hence the name, pulled pork. Sides are good too.
Good Pizza but very uncomfortable seating and an unfortunate wait if you show up during prime time.
Fantastic and reasonable Japanese food (not really any standard sushi on the menu) two blocks from Grand Central. Â Expansive sake menu. Â Great atmosphere. Â Authentic Japanese ... bathrooms.

Food was average, wait was way too long. I think they were understaffed when we went. No one sat us down, no one bothered giving us menus. Ordered the quesadilla, a house wrap, cookie, and lemonade. My lemonade and cookie which was already made didn't come until thirty minutes later when everything else arrived. Don't come here if you're in a rush.

Came here with a group of 7 friends for brunch on a Saturday and found the space to be cozy and fun. The restaurant is long and narrow, with limited seating, so reservation is recommended. The food is southern comfort - items on the menu included shrimp and grits, chicken and waffles, biscuits and gravy, etc. Coffee/mimosas are included in a fixe prix option. The coffee gets refilled frequently, and service is prompt but not intrusive. I ordered the biscuits and gravy but did not enjoy it, probably because I didn't know what it was and what came wasn't what I expected - the gravy was extremely creamy and heavy, and I probably only had two bites of it. Should've gone with the salmon... The chicken and waffles, however, was very good. The chicken was pretzel-crusted! The portions are not as massive as what you'd get in a southern restaurant in the south, but they're very generous and more than enough for a normal-appetite person. The mimosas are weak - predominantly orange juice - but that was fine with us! Our party was loud and rowdy, and we stayed for a long time after we finished eating, but nobody bothered us. The checks also come clipped inside Goosebumps books, which you can write it - a very cute touch! Price was very reasonable, about $25/person including tax/tip.

The all-you can eat pasta and antipasto deal is the best value for your money in the Times Square area. Wonderful pasta is cooked al dente and selections change daily. Sometimes they substitute risotto for one of the pastas and the risotto is heavenly as well. Make sure to make reservations way ahead of time for pre-theatre as the restaurant is packed before the theatre.

Well deserving of five stars for the great prices and great taste. Â Best bang for the buck at this establishment! Â Tried the falafel plate and a shawarma. The Falafel: The perfect size, the crispy crunch, the wonderful flavors that tease your taste buds, and above all....not too dry and not too greasy. Â Also complimented with white sauce, makes the falafel even more tastier. Â Best falafel I've tasted in a long time, even in comparison to traditional homemade I've tasted. Â  You have to try it in order to understand what I'm talking about! Shawarma: Can you say "MEAT?" Â Meat and plenty of it. Â Tasty with all the right flavors. Â Juicy and tender! Â Not burnt and dry like other places. Â The meat did not have a strong lamb flavor either. Â It was very subtle! The place is small. Â We happened to visit when it was 90 degrees outside. Â Was lucky to find seating on the bench right up front. Â  Will come back to eat here when I return to NYC! Didn't try the hot sauce. Â Might have to try it next time. Â It's popular enough that I believe they charge you for it. Â Me, not a fan of spicy.
A little gem in the UWS, everything about this place is just right - a well chosen wine list, a delicious menu with a nice Mediterranean Â twist, Â friendly service and the perfect music.

I've long heard that Taverna Kyclades is the go-to place for Greek food in Astoria - a place I couldn't pass up. Taverna Kyclades does not take reservations and on a weekend, you will often be waiting in line for the next available table. I was there on a weekday and at around 7 p.m. there luckily wasn't much of a wait and within a few minutes my party (there were five of us) was seated in a prized corner table in the outdoor seating area on the sidewalk. The food at Taverna Kyclades is served "family style" as sharing is highly encouraged. Looking to try a little bit of everything, we ordered: Â  Â Grilled Octopus (two orders) Â  Â Grilled Quails Â  Â Kyclades Special: stuffed clams, stuffed shrimp, lobster tail, fillet of sole and scallops (two orders) First off, the amount of food we ordered was perfect for five people. We were not overly stuffed but very satisfied. Before our food came out, we were given some incredible tasting bread. It came soaked in olive oil and other spices and was the perfect thing to hold me over until our food. Once the food started arriving I was ready to dig in. The highlights of this meal were definitely the grilled octopus and dessert (I'll get to that in a minute). The other two dishes (quail and Kyclades special) were good, but I was expecting to be blown out of the water by the best Greek food in Astoria. These dishes failed to do that and specifically, the fish was run of the mill seafood that I think I could have gotten at any other restaurant in the surrounding area. Everyone in our group was disappointed by the quail. It lacked any real flavor and was something I would discourage anyone from ordering. Onto the highlights... the grilled octopus was delicious. It came out chopped in small bite-sized pieces and had an incredible grilled charcoal flavor blended with cucumber and other flavors. It was a big hit among everyone I was with and I know we all would have easily eaten a couple more orders. The dessert was also one of the best part of the meals. At Taverna Kyclades dessert is on the house (until they run out each night). They give everyone at the table an order of a Greek pastry. I can't remember what it was called (it wasn't baklava) but it has an incredible sweet, rich flavor to it with a nice fluffiness provided by some sort of custard or cream. It was delicious and the perfect end to the meal.

Came here because I saw that this place was listed on Serious Eats best fancy fried chicken list. This review is mainly about their chicken because I kind of forgot everything else I had but the chicken was so good, it's enough to be the sole reason you try this place. I got the white meat buttermilk fried chicken. It was perfectly crispy on the outside and very moist on the inside without being greasy.

i was introduced to this cart by my sister and my cousin who swear by the food! Â there was a line and i was warned to chill on the red sauce and add the extra white....and boy were they right. and make sure your subway ride isn't too long as you take your food home....the food aroma takes over the entire train.. : )

Impossible to get a reservation, but otherwise totally worth the planning ahead. I have been here twice now. Prix fixe menu was a great way to start as it includes a good variety of food (and it is a lot of food). The restaurant seems to change what is on the prix fixe pretty often too. I also really liked pork gyoza - sizzling and so good! Definitely recommend it, especially for cold winter nights!

Delicious Dumplings! Great cheap eat! Their dumplings are a bit crispier on the outside than some of the other dumpling spots. My lil brother said to me, " Bums can afford this." I said, " Yea, they can; are you going to advertise it to them?" "Hell No." He replied.

This is my favorite place to eat in the city. The wine is affordable and the food is outstanding. The staff is great as well. After gorgetting to make reservations for a special night with my girlfriend they found us a great table to my never ending embarresment.
heaven!
As good as it gets.

Easily one of the best Thai restaurants in NYC. Chefs and waiters from Thailand. Presentation very appetizing. Dishes with peanut sauce a must try - Thai salad, shrimp pumpkin. All appetizers are great.

The line still stands. The macaroni and cheese holds its reign among the best I've ever eaten. The scene continues to meld the late-night Chelsea crazies with the post-club revelers. After hours and way after dark, it's the top choice for a alcohol-absorbing meal that's affordable, frenzied with buzzing client and always, always open.

Who would have thought? After seeing the strange exhibitions, this was a definite YES! The presentation, flavorful dishes, like the beef tartare, cucumber gazpacho, beet salad, roasted pork, and blackberry crumble pie, we could have all returned for more 'art'! This place is a MUST!

fact: the bronte burger will sweep you off your feet! I like that it is a bit untraditonal here & that you don't get a choice of fries. With a burger this size, a salad is really the only option. I fully intended to only eat one half, but when something tastes this heavenly, it is fantastically difficult to enact self-control.. yums.

I finally went to Gaia today after hearing that the coffee is good, since I'm constantly on the search for an authentic Italian espresso that doesn't require sugar to be drinkable! I was happy to see that there was also fresh squeezed OJ on the menu at a very reasonable price. The espresso was a bit corto for my taste, but the flavor was better than most, maybe just a teensy bit of sugar needed, but I didn't add it. And the OJ was an awesome surprise. The only negative experience happened when, mid sip, one of the employees cranked up the radio. Suddenly I was being blasted by Celine Dion and then Pink. I could no longer concentrate on my reading or my beverages. I was thinking to order food but the music was so aggressive and annoying (so un-Gaia mind!) that I high-tailed it out of there. "Oh well. Another one bites the dust," I thought. I'm really hoping some quality control over the music and volume happens because it seemed like an otherwise really cool place and I'd love to try the food that the customers were raving over. I still can't figure out why so many cafes allow employees to play whatever music they want to listen to all day instead of music that creates a nice atmosphere for their customers. Still searching...

Very good, We tried the Noah's Ark which includes lobster, shrimp, and crab sampler. Next time I would have just gotten the lobster it is that good. It is simple and clean. Lots of Lobster on a toasted butter roll with celery salt and a little mayo. It was perfect and highly recommended.

My new favourite place! Â  The staff was very hospitable, careful and so friendly. Food was excellent, fresh and tasty as Peru! I recommend you to have juicy chicken and salad and ceviche was tasty too! I had a spicy margarita, and it was supper ;-))

Laredo, Texas born and bred....so I feel distinctly qualified to comment (and so help me if I hear ONE MORE hipster talk to me about "the most authentic Mexican restaurant" in NY, I will bitch-slap those Warby Parkers right off, and no, that one spring break you spent in Cancun in high school doesn't raise your "cred"), but Tres Carnes is legit. This hungry Tex-Mex girl very highly recommends Tres Carnes, which is the closest thing you'll get to a real Michelada and Mr. Corn in the Atlantic seaboard. It's not what I would say is exactly "authentic" Tex-Mex, but it's better than Chipotle. I like Chipotle, but it gives me the impression of what some white person in Denver or Seattle who has peripheral interactions with Mexicans interprets Mexican food for an Anglo palate. Tres Carnes seems more like what some white person in Austin interprets Tex-Mex; still not the real thing (it never will be), but superior to anything else you'll get around here. Definitely have the Michelada clasica and the street-car corn with lots of Valentina sauce. For any other homesick South Texans out there, It tastes like home.
I had the "Bee Sting." Spicy sweet perfection!

I thought about four stars but I soon came to the conclusion it was well worth five stars. Although the wait is very long I see it as a once every few months type of place. We arrived at 630 and were out by 830. A guy drove from Detroit to try Doms pizza. My only complaint is the wait, it could be run way more efficiently but the guy helping Dom was like a chicken with his head cut off. It worth the wait just to have Dom personally make the pizza. The pizza itself is absolutely amazing. I love Brooklyn style and this is the perfect Brooklyn pizza. Four cheeses grated while make each pizza, handmade sauce made in small sauce pans in the back, fresh basil grown in the window, and olive oil, lots of olive oil! Make the hour trip from midtown, you won't regret it at all!

I've been to Pylos twice, once for brunch and once for dinner: Â It has great, authentic Greek food at very reasonable prices: Dinner: The food is incredible and the service is friendly. Â The wait-staff is attentive but not pushy. Â The wine list is quite interesting as all the wines are Greek, which is different that I'm used to seeing, even at Greek restaurants in the city. Â Try the Pastitsio: you're in for a treat. Brunch: This is basically a standard brunch with a few interesting Greek twists. Â As the decor and service are nice and the prices fair, I think it's one of the better places for brunch in an area full of good brunch spots.

Maybe my expectations were too high coming here, but I'm a little disappointed with the food at Mooncake Foods. Someone really needs to teach the staff here how to julienne their veggies. As many before have commented, veggies come in huge chunks, and it really takes away from the experience. However, I have to love that no matter what I order, it is quickly and efficiently prepared for me. No long waits here! Lobster and Mango Summer Rolls: This was my fave dish here. The summer rolls are excellent, the sauce is good, but dipping the roll in the sauce actually takes away from the lobster yummyness. Better to eat the rolls without the sauce. Thai Steak Salad: Steak was cooked well, sauce was good. The actual salad was just okay. Very generous on the steak portion. Octopus & Spinach Noodles: Octopus was cooked well, and there was much more if it than I expected. Noodles were good. Salad was just okay. Miso-Glazed Salmon: Loved the salmon, didn't really care for the rest of what it came with. If I come back, maybe I can order this with just salmon and rice?

Pizza = 5 stars Why the 4 star rating? 1. No seating. Well there is, but it is a bunch of mismatched tables and chairs clumsily put together. Good luck finding a seat, too... With the volume of customers, you will have to huddle around a corner waiting for a party to leave. 2. OH THE WAIT! You come in and it instantaneously smells awesome, if you come hungry, you might suffer. The waits can be over an hour for your pizza, as Di Fara himself makes each and every pizza himself, crafting it, getting it in the oven, then breaking fresh basil and showering olive oil over the pie right before it meets the customer. So really, if Yelp allowed half stars, this would be 4.5. Note: They close between lunch and dinner. So no Linner, if you ever thought about planning for that.

I don't think I've met a nicer person in Manhattan that N. Y. Dosa man. Â He just makes you feel good. Some people can do that and some can't. Thiru does. His vegan indian style cuisine is fantastic. Â Get the rotti curry or anything Thiru suggests. Get to know Thiru by being a regular and get preferential treatment. Â The food itself is simple and delicious and gives you energy without weighing you down. Â All that and Washington Square park for a dining room? I declare it to be fantastic. Bottom line, the curries at N.Y. Dosa are the most balanced, and internally flawless that I've ever tasted. Try it.

I decided to try this place after so many great reviews. I had to wait 2 hours to get my pizza since they are closed between the hours of Â 5pm - 6:30pm. After all the wating outside in the cold, I found the pie to be salty and nothing real special. I had better pizza in the bronx on Morris Park...ie Patricia's.

Nothing special here. Came here for a Saturday brunch...AKA you get cheated out of the complementary drinks. Worst eggs benedict I have had in a while....drenched in hollandaise sauce. Â Yes, there is such a thing as too much butter.

This morning I had the best brunch here with two friends. Had the Tunisian sandwich (minus the egg) and it was ohh so yummy. Friend had the scrambled eggs with herbs (green) and quinoa cake and loved it too. Service was great.
Great happy hour scene when there on a Friday evening. Bartenders were friendly and efficient. Not too loud. People surround bar on all four sides....Good vibe.

We came here for brunch and had the BELT sandwich and the John's Benedict. Â Both were great. Loved the sausage on John's Benedic and the fries that came with the sandwich. There was a little bit of wait to get in but after the great food it was definitely worth while. The ambiance was also great filled with young people. To make it short this was one of the best brunches I have had in NYC.

Everything about our experience here was fantastic. We came for my mom's birthday before seeing a show and they made sure to get us out on time even though we were running late for our reservation. Eddie took care of us and was so accommodating and sweet. He gave us amazing recommendations and got our order in and our food out at lightening speed per our request. The drinks were also fantastic! When there was a little confusion over what ceviche platter we had ordered, they served us the $29 tasting platter for the $13 price - that does not happen in NYC! At the end of the meal they brought out dessert with a candle for my mom and everyone sang her happy birthday and came over to wish her well. It was truly like we were a part of their little family! My mom cried because she felt so special. This restaurant is not one you want to pass up and I recommend it for any occasion.

This place doesn't need another review, but I am going to give it one because it is my favorite restaurant in New York. It's unpretentious, and the prices are reasonable for what you get, which is gorgeously crafted, explosively flavorful pasta served by a professional, attentive staff. I've yet to eat a single thing here that wasn't ohmygoodgood delicious.
While visiting family in NY, my husband took me here and it was AMAZING. Â  We live in the South so we definitely know great Southern food and this restaurant is great.

Great beer choices. They have a ton of beer selections, coming from countries like Germany, Austria, the UK, Australia, Japan, and even Sri Lanka! I came here on a Sunday afternoon after brunch, and was able to find seats at the bar. It is a small place, with a little kitchen, serving burgers, hot dogs, and some specialty items, like Thai BBQ Wings. I have yet to try the food, but plan to when I return. Also, the bartender is awesome, and plays great music!

If I could give a 0 star I would. I had the most TERRIBLE experience ever at Hagi last night (Thursday Dec. 4th). Previously, Hagi was actually one of my favorite places in the city to go to to have mentai pasta. My friends and I always ordered 2 orders of mentai pasta along with 5-6 other dishes among 2-3 ppl every time we were there. ;-P This is how much we loved the food here. However, the BIG problem here is their service. I have to admit that no one goes here for a great service. But it was not something that would ruin the dining experience. But last night, because of one wait staff's rudeness and completely ignorant attitude, we absolutely hated our whole experience there. As usual, we went to Hagi to have some good food and sake. Everything was just as same as our previous visits. We waited for about 5-10 min then were seated. We decided what to order and called our waiter to order. Our waiter was the tallest one out of all the wait staffs there and he had a slim figure. While taking our order, he couldn't have been anymore careless. Especially, when we said we wanted to order an Okonomiyaki. He asked if we want it with "beef or pork" with his poor diction. When we asked if they have seafood option, he said yes then "yelled at us" saying that he was busy and we needed to decide fast. This was totally unacceptable behavior but we let it pass since we really didn't want to start an argument. While we were dining, he never took away our empty dishes (unless we asked or a new dish came out and there were no space on the table) nor paid attention to our table. He once came by and looked at our "empty" sake bottle and just "slammed" it back on our table and left. When we wanted to order more we had to call another waiter to reorder. After dinner, we asked for our check. We were just finishing our sake in the glasses for about 15-20 min after the Â check was dropped. He continuously came back to our table (I think he came around 5 times within the 15-20min we were finishing our dinner) and kept "tapping the check with his finger" and said "there are lots of people waiting." (But it was after the kitchen closed and NO one was waiting at the time!) So we just gave our credit cards to pay. When the check came back he automatically added 18% tip to our credit cards. Then, he disappeared. So finally we called another waiter to ask why the gratuity was automatically added when we are only 3 people. He was trying to say something but as I told him that I am NOT some kind of tourist and I probably ate at Hagi 20-30 times in the past. Then, finally he apologized and corrected the amount. As I said before, we love the food here. I love anything with mentai here. Their fish are very fresh. (love uni, and sashimi here) It is just purely sad to see that they have such a poor service. Just because of one misbehaved wait staff we had absolutely terrible feeling leaving this place regardless of how wonderful their food was and how good the bottles of sake we ordered. After last night, I would never want to go back there and put up with such a non-sense attitude.
The place for being on the run to and from Manhattan - and they do a mean felafel.

BEST TACO/BURRITO PLACE EVER! I usually am not this into mexican food because I hate the minuscule amount of super dry and overcooked meats that usually go into tacos or burritos. This place, has THE BEST pork I've ever tasted!! I had a soft taco with pork, and another with steak. The pork blew me away! Succulent, juicy, and flavorful meat was so delicious! The salsa was also nice and spicy, and the guacamole was more on the zesty side, which I always prefer. I was also really impressed that the steak meat was perfectly cooked, but just not as flavorful as the pork. They are super generous with the meat, guaranteeing that you will be full! This place is such a gem..cheap and delicious! I just wish there was more room to sit and eat!

The only Panamanian restaurant I've ever been to in NYC. Contrary to the stereotypes, not all Panamanian food is composed of tails and feet, though some people may find some of the cuts of meat in some dishes questionable. Anyway, Kelso is fantastic, and a great deal as well. The vast majority of the entrees, and all of the soups, are under $10, and these are reasonably large portions. The appetizers are cheap too, most of them are $1-$3. The braised pork with plantains and the chicken stew are both excellent. The empanadas are delicious and they serve Sorrel! Recommended.

We went here for a book club meeting after one of our members recommended it. Very cute place, nice atmosphere and not too crowded. We split a bunch of appetizers to start and all were quite good -- the yucca fries were stand outs for me. My cousin and I split two arepas -- the "del jardin" and the "De Caraotas", both minus the cheese. Really delicious and filling. We didn't get drinks so I can't comment on that. The service was adequate -- nothing special and not at all friendly, but nothing to complain about either. I'll definitely be going back.

Just popped in after getting a yelp invite about the place. We ordered 3x Lobster rolls Connecticut style , one shrimp roll and one steamed lobster. We also had the woopie pies but the they don't make them so I'll toss in a note about them in the end. The lobster roll was delish. The buttery roll compliments the lobster. Not to crazy about the scallions but they were pleasant enough that i Â wasn't searching them out to remove them. Size is on the small side but I personally believe in quality over quantity . Mostly claw meat and lobster in every bite. My mom had a bite of the shrimp roll and was not impressed. She couldn't find a shrimp which is odd for a SHRIMP roll but she also didn't like the dusting of paprika and cinnamon. The steamed whole Lobster was perfect. Not over done and well with the free butter and lemon. Actually a better buy then the rolls if you ask me (1.5 lbs for $14 vs. the $16 for Â the sandwich) The cashier did mention the seating next door. Offering it to us while we waited . Though we didn't stay the gentleman that did had his food brought to him. The only down side was that I spent about $67 and they didn't even give me the chips that come with the sandwiches. So about 4 bags they jipped me on :( The woopie pie was a little dry and lacking that buttery butter cream flavor. Not awful but not awesome either

Wifey and I come back here everytime we're in NY. The food is still exceptional, but don't take our words for it. Â Here are two recent endorsements from total strangers during our many visits: 1) Persian family (mom, dad, 2 daughters) waiting in line with us. Â The 2 daughters get sick of waiting and ask daddy if they can go down the block to a less busy Halal cart. Â Dad gives 'em both the evil eye and a stern dressing-down. Â He tells them both, "We stay here!! Â Dis is best food!!" Â I half thought he would bitch-slap his own daughters for the blasphemy they uttered. 2) Caught a cab to Union square yesterday. Â Chatted with the cabbie who was an affable fellow and just happened to be Egyptian. Â I asked him what he thought about the 53rd and 6th Halal cart. Â He looked me straight in the eye (while still racing down Park avenue at 50mph) and said in a serious tone, "their food... better than any restaurant!" 'Nuff said...

Update: this place is still the shiznit, but make sure to check that your order is correct before you leave the restaurant. They called my name, but I got some random person's sandwich with tabbouleh and carrot slices instead of the falafel I had ordered and didn't realize until I had reached the park. It was gross, to put it simply.

The hostesses were EXTREMELY rude. I had a reservation (I was really early and told them so). They claimed they didn't see my reservation, and I had to literally show them my open table email, as WELL as my call log showing them that they called me to confirm a day before. I was so fed up with the hostesses that I ate at the bar. But the bartnender was wonderful as usual, and the food was outstanding! Eggs benedict and creme brulee french toast are like no other.

The ramen is fantastic, it's a simple fact. The price, however, is steeper than most. I suppose this is one of those "get what you pay for" situations but there are certainly other ramen spots in NYC with competitive quality and cheaper prices. Regardless, Ippudo is definitely a place you must try once and most likely you will return many times.

Best vegetable dumplings I have ever tasted! Â  I had the pork-crab dry noodle with egg noodles. Â It was tasty and I enjoyed the dish but didn't quite live up to the high expectations that had been set by the dumplings. Â  We shared 2 apps, a bottle of wine, entrees x 4, 2 beers, + tax/tip = 26 bucks per person. Not bad!! I would come back and try some more of the enticing menu-- or just eat a bunch of dumplings.

As one of the most reasonably priced Jean-Georges, I was really excited to try Perry Street. Â Lovely atmosphere with the very monochromatic scheme and soft lighting. Â I would definitely go back, but sit at the bar and get appetizers. Â Here is why: Â waitress was mediocre, appetizers superb, entrees lacking. Â The pumpkin soup, calamari, cracker crusted tuna, and crab dumplings were all exquisite and scrumptious. Â Burger was A quality entree- fries and Russian dressing esque sauce made it, but the proportions made for challenging eating. Â Overrated fried chicken-I have had more impressive fried chicken from Dishes- which in case you don't know is a popular midtown buffet style haunt.

AMAZING. Need I say more? Luckily, I live super close. As a recent transplant from NJ, I am loving my new home - Â Roberta's is one reason why :))

Great ambiance, beautifully plated food and healthy sized portions are what this place is all about. Â The service was swift and we were able to get in and out in less than 50 minutes. Great little place! So warm and inviting, fantastic cocktails and appetizers. Had the pani puris and chilli cheese toast with cocktails. The ambience is really cute too :-)

Vitae was everything I expected and more! The food was excellent and the service was over the top! The entire experience put a smile on my face! I will definitely be back! Thank you for a great experience Jason!!

Food's good, but nothing memorable. Had the soy chicken n duck. Â Pieces that were given weren't 'good parts' and not very meaty. it's more like 3.5 stars. cute little place, got there bright and early so there was no wait at all. tried: eggs benedict - ehh..i've had better. Talk about a young refreshing place. Its a small place tucked in on chinatown's Baxter st. though they make up for their small restaurant with huge flavor! I have been waiting since I moved to Baxter st. for these guys to open up and I finally got my chance at their food. I had the fish taco and Breakroom Fries, they did not disappoint. The piece of fish was fresh and had great crunch on the fried exterior, but a taco needs other components to complement the fish, needless to say the Breakroom did it right. My two favorite were the house sauce and the pickled onions. Following my taco I had the Breakroom Fries. To start it was a huge portion and they only cost $4.95. Service wise I was impressed on how organized they were for only being open 1 day. Im looking forward to trying more of the menu so I hope these guys keep up the good work!

Shrimp roll is good but not as good as the lobster roll. Soups are also tasty. Loved the selection of bottled craft sofas and beers. Overall it was an expensive lunch but unique and tasty. I think we'll save it for those once in a while casual lunch splurges.

Out. Of. This. World. Â The ingredients the Special Salmon roll are perfect. The spicy tuna bowl is out of this world. The freshest fish and the cheapest rolls in Brooklyn! I am now Silver Rice's humble servant.

A long line up in the cold but worth every second. I've been waiting for about 15 min. Very good noodles in a very rich (maybe too rich) chicken and soy. In a nice portion. The pork is too fat, almost only fat... I recommend the chicken. Nice spice with the extra spicy version.

Have been loving it here these last couple of years. Sitting by the bar is a must, at least once every few months. Sushi pieces are fabulous, perfect rice quantity, superb tasting fish...always. Always happy going here.

They mean too much to me to betray them now.

Supposedly the first American pizzeria (though I am of the New Haven school - visit Pepe's when you get the chance: yelp.com/biz/frank-pepe-â€¦ ). Good pizza, often long lines. Top Chef, Top Notch. I had the opportunity to check out Top Chef's season one winner Harold's new place and from the moment I walked in the door I knew I was in for a treat. Unlike a lot of places in NYC that are located highly trafficked streets with a focus on interior execution that is sometimes overpowers the food itself, Perilla, is located just off Bleeker on Jones and feels like a neighborhood place that I'd be hitting at least once a week if I lived locally. Once seated at the bar the friendly staff hooked me up with a wine list to review, a glass of water and my starter cocktail. Seated to my left and right were friendly customers, all excited to be there and all clearly enjoying their meals. My enjoyment began when I looked at the menu I was pleasantly surprised. While the base ingredients were straightforward and what you would expect to find on any fine eatery, this wasn't a menu of safe standards but a fresh Asian influenced yet but not fusion approach. It was refreshing. I opted for a 4 course tasting menu so I could taste the range. The quality of food and the preparation were perfect. You can tell that Harold looks to surprise you with a hint of mint here and a unique flavor there just to keep you on your toes, but they all work together and the base element of the dish is so perfectly prepared that you can really appreciate the quality of the ingredients. I think it's a bit auspicious that Harold's first night offically open was the night of the James Beard Awards and while he was in the kitchen this year I will expect he'll be at the awards ceremony at some point in the near future. I only hope that I'll be able to get in next time I'm in New York.

Is there such a thing as a perfect meal? Â This designation is of course highly subjective and is therefore likely immeasurable. Â I'm reminded of the scene from 'Dead Poets Society', highlighting a fictional Mr. J Evans Pritchard, PhD and his method of measuring poetry by 'how artfully the objective of the poem has been rendered' and 'how important is the objective?' Â  Like the aforementioned measurement of poetry, one could attempt to measure a meal - it has an objective, a sense of self indulgence, infinite transmutations, and in the case of Degustation's 10 course tasting menu, a calculable rhythm and meter. Degustation is a restaurant meant for (and I hate to use this term) 'foodies'. Â The food is refined, elegant, beautifully plated, and utilizes French techniques that foodies will instantly recognize (e.g. application of foam and mousse's, advanced charcuterie techniques, clever use of hydocolloids) but refrains from the expensive crowd pleasers such as foie gras', lobster, etc. Â The application of simple and cheap ingredients (the one deviation would be the wagyu 'cheesesteak' - sublime!) into something truly special requires a talented Chef, and an appreciative audience. I'll resonate the note of caution that others have documented - when ordering the 10 course tasting menu, come hungry, pace yourself, and succumb to the expertly informed and patient waitstaff. Â Of course you're in good hands with the cooks, who construct each plate in front of their audience of diners. Â Without breaking a sweat, these cooks sling out the food with perfect cadence, with just enough of a break between courses to subjugate the blissed out reaction to the duck egg mousse en brioche with bacon, but not long enough to curb any enthusiasm for the tasty duck confit on croute with a balsamic reduction. Â  I mentioned before that Degustation amply and expertly uses inexpensive ingredients. Â This assertion is substantiated by a succulent goat meatball (goat meat runs about $6-7 a lb) in a squid ink sauce, or a rabbit terrine ($7 per lb) with spring artichokes, which is brilliantly executed despite its low cost. Â Or few simple segments of tangerine, coated with a red wine gelee and completed with their 'secret sauce' of Pop Rocks, which was one of my favorite dishes of the night given its innocent brashness. Â  Similar to Mr. J Evans Pritchard's scale, every diner I know substitutes their own - to wit, the interplay of price and quality of the meal. Â At a very reasonable $80 for ten nearly perfectly executed stanzas and a masterful sense of meter, Degustation scores an easy 5 stars.

I love cafe orlin, and not just for brunch! Hummus is some of the best in the east village. Solid comfort Mediterranean food

Yum! Great NYC pizza :) "America's first pizzeria" apparently. Def a touristy historical pizza place to check out. Came for dinner around 8 pm on a Monday, we waited around 10 min not too bad. Mediocre food. Chicken fried chicken - not crispy and lacked flavor. House cut tortillas and guac, overly peppered Nestled in an out of the way corner in the Two Bridges section of downtown Manhattan you'll find this charming little restaurant. Casa Mono was not what I expected. Though the dress is casual, the place had the feel of being stuck between being the local in place and the local trendy in place. The evening started off with flagging down a waiter to take our order. Then we had 3 other people come by and serve us and take our orders for the second round of tapas. We had no idea who our waiter was until we asked the 4th person who came to our table. Servicewsie: I don't recommend Casa Mono. Mr. Batali would not be proud. The bright side: the food was good. Out of 9 dishes, 7 of them were delicious. I highly recommend the fois gras with cinco cebellos, sweetbreads with fennel, pulpo with fennel & grapefruit, duck with cranberry mostaza, lamb chops, and the pumpkin & goat cheese croquets. The tripe with chickpeas was flavorful; however, it had very little tripe, so not much can be said about the tripe itself. Fideos with chorizo and clams had no flavor whatsoever and the chorizo was dice and sparse, leaving me wishing for chorizo links to enjoy. In truth, I regretted ordering that dish.

The food isn't that bad. Just make sure not to let your eyes be hungrier than your stomach. It's about $6/pound for the buffet. The chicken, Bulgoki, and kimchi fried rice are what I Â usually get. There are a good variety of food to choose from. My friends and I stop by here at night to get a quick drink since they have soju and beer available. There's a Korean milk drink that we mix with our soju. So good. It gets pretty crowded and it is a small place. Finding somewhere to sit can be annoying. The line can go all the way around the buffet line sometimes.

Celebrated my 20th birthday here on January 25th. Â We reserved at 6pm for 6:30pm dinner. It wasn't packed. It has a coat check and the lounge area. Food : We were a group of three people and our waiter suggested us to try sampling 3 appetizers each instead of getting 3 entrees. We ended up ordering 8 dishes because I wasn't feeling hungry and I only ordered 2. To my surprise, we couldn't finish the total of 8 orders. Although the portions weren't huge, they were very delicious and filling. 1.Grilled Spanish Coast Octopus - the octopus was average but I loved the lamb belly that came with it. It was super flavorful and fatty. I don't usually (like rarely) eat fats but this one is a YES. 2.Moussaka- the eggplant dish that I found intricate yet delectable 3.Phoenician Fries - Different from regular fries because it's wider and more flavorful. I loved the dip that came with it 4.Calamari A La Plancha - Calamari and corn! It was the best combo ever! 5. Veal Bacon - Bacons in mini pancakes. I recommend Octopus, Calamari, Veal Bacon, Duck Shawarma and the dip. I really want to try their yoghurt dip. I think it is a nice place for fancy adventurous/fun dinner. I only didn't give 5 stars because I had stomach problems at night. I am not sure why though.

I live in Japan - I have eaten ramen in almost every major city and small towns along the main rail lines. In total I have eaten at 32 Ramen Shops in Japan. I can say with authority that the ramen at Ippudo are very good. The noodles are definitely on par with what you find in a lot of ramen shops in Japan. The broths are fantastic! The tonkotsu broth is very rich and creamy without being greasy or bland. The only criticism I have is that you are paying double the price of ramen in Japan. You will have to wait a long time but that's the price you have to pay for a very rich creamy perfectly done tonkotsu broth. Setagaya... hmm I am not sure how anyone could be happy to announce they like that place, it's marginal at best. The noodles are definitely not fresh and the broth is just not as evolved, complex and flavorful as Ippudo. I will say that ramen like all food is completely subjective, but some thing are recognized as "standard". Ippudo has done well in New York because the founder took a lot of time to study Japanese and American tastes and what you get is something universally tasty. Some people might not like it but that's as authentic as you will get.

Ok, now...wait...I have to lick this DELICIOUS bbq sauce off my fingers...so, I can...type. Ok, I am back. All I can say is DAMN, DAMN, DAMN! I didn't know y'all. I didn't know. So, we wanted Southern food and we had had some mediocre experiences with other joints so we were a bit tentative, that is before we Â realized that we had found the soul food nirvana. Napoleon conquered our taste buds and took no prisoners. Everything we had was AMAZING! We even ordered dessert after seeing the reviews and, I who am not a sweets person, almost had a knock down drag out over the cherry pie and coconut pineapple cake. Napoleon...I don't have the words. I am committed to ordering often. Thank you for putting your foot in it!

Love, love this place! Â Not pretentious at all, as some reviewers wrote. Â Drinks are fantastic, fresh, flavorful and worth every penny. Â Food is ridiculous. Â Brunch is anything but just eggs and potatoes. Â Try the Molettes. Â Hidden secret: try their tequila shots with a sangrita chaser. Â Best I've ever had. Â Service is smooth and relaxed just like the vibe.
Good authentic typical Thai place. If you are a fan of spicy stuff, this is your place.

They serve pizza and a some appetizers and drinks. The pizza is definitely not the best I've eaten in Manhattan. Contrary to what the yelp page suggests, it's not all that kid-friendly because they have zero high chairs or booster seats. They did take our stroller to storage, which was nice. The staff was not that friendly, which was surprising and disappointing. Cash only. ATM on-site. Spent $28 on one, small pizza and a tea.

This place has a nice layout and a much better menu of food and beers than most in the area. It's a little pricey for what it is but I'd go to eat and get a seasonal beer anytime because it's quality. The scene isn't anything special but it's nice to have a place that has some more amenities then most of the lame bars in the hood.
Excellent. Get the rice combo

VERY GOOD but if you think japanese = sushi, it may not be there place for you. They have more casual daily japanese food. In Japan, Ootoya is franchise and really cheap like the half of the price but the food here is decent and delicious. I can't complain. I've been there several time but will be going more in the future for sure.

Ate here for dinner on a Monday evening. Â Cool location, romantic atmosphere, friendly service, and pretty good food. Â The cauliflower soup was a very pleasant surprise. Â The fried Risotto balls were OK (unless you ask my cardiologist!). Â The steak was excellent. Â We split everything for no additional charge. Â I regret not having any pasta but we'll make it happen the next time around. Beer selection was somewhat mediocre, but I expect that at an Italian restaurant. Â I imagine the wine selection was quite a bit better but I'm not a wine guy.
Phenomenal food. Ask the staff for their recommendations and choose what sounds best. You can't go wrong. Highly recommended for brunch; and make reservations.

I used to love this place but it has turned into a tourist trap. The wine menu is still a very good deal but the food is sub par. I d remember when the food used to be excellent and you could wine and dine and take your time. Now it is like a cattle call. You are rushed as soon as you get in the door. The tables are so close together it is very uncomfortable.As I sat in the bar area waiting for my reservation I noticed A female manager drinking alcohol with no shame at all. No professionalism and looked like she had just rolled out of bed. Lidea B. seems that that she has lost control of this once "gem" .

Drinking wine by the cup.... yeah, cup. I'm in love. Came back with my bf and we both agreed that this is a new spot. The food is delish, the drink menu is supremely limited, but reasonably priced and gets the job down. Unendingly chill vibe (this includes the wait person, as in one person, who is usually chilling in jeans at a table and difficult to distinguish from the patrons. However, the place is so tiny there's no way to be waiting long for anything). This place is great!

Taim probably doesn't need anymore 5 star reviews, but here it is. What you read is true. Taim does what they do - as in falafel and smoothies - VERY WELL, especially the falafel part. It's a tiny little space with a big big presence - and you'll love every bit of the sandwich, platter, salad, whatever you decide to have. It's fresh, simple, fast, affordable (although cash only) and delicious. Oh - and you'll never even notice it's vegan - so much flavor. It's a weekly thing for me.
The pancake is lovely, they serve the beakfast menu even in dinner time! Blueberry pencake is great, ans milk shake as well.

My 200th review! I decided to write it on Jean Georges' Perry Street. Â I've been a big fan of Nougatine and The Mark Restaurant, so why not take try out Perry Street? Â I've been wanting to try it out since New Years but haven't had a chance to go. Location: Perry Street by the West Side Highway Be prepared to take a long walk from the train station... or just drive! Â I was pretty lucky to find a parking spot in 2 minutes on a Saturday around 11:30am... but then again, I usually have good luck finding a parking spot. Â I have a parking angel watching out for me. Food: Overall, food was great but not outstanding for a chef of Jean Georges reputation. Â With that noted, it's still a GREAT DEAL for brunch! Â Worth a trip for brunch and then take a nice walk along the West Side Highway to watch the view & water on a beautiful sunny day. The brunch deal includes 2 entrees and 1 dessert for $26. Â I came here with 3 other friends... so what do we do? Â We order 8 different dishes and shared. Highlights of the meal included the Amuse Bouche (Broccoli & Cheese), Artic Char Salmon and Sweet Chili Crab Dumplings (with Cilantro and Celeriac). Â I personally liked the Cod with Miso-Yuzu Glaze (with Baby Bok Choy & Sriracha), but one of the girls at the table mentioned that she didn't think it was buttery enough. Â For those of you that know me, I don't do butter. Â  I also liked their Spinach & Goat Cheese Omelette. Â The goat cheese flavor was muted, so it doesn't slap you across the face when you eat it... although I do crave the strong flavor of goat cheese from time to time. Dessert: With the $26 deal, there are 2 choices of dessert, so our group got both to try. Â  1) Warm Valhora Chocolate Cake & Vanilla Ice Cream 2) Cheesecake, Strawberry and Rhubarb Compote, Candied Almonds, Rhubarb Sorbet I personally prefer the chocolate cake. Â You can't go wrong with chocolate. Â The strawberry dessert was good, but I didn't think the cheesecake was cheesecakey enough. Â Is that even a word? Â If I didn't know any better, I would have thought it was a cake instead of a cheesecake. This place is so cute. Prices are very fair. The food is delicious. That goat cheese...mmm. The wine flights are an amazing deal and a great way to expand your wine repertoire without having to invest too heavily in anything. I discovered an amazing red from Mallorca that I would never have otherwise tried. It was recommended by one of the two absolutely WONDERFUL waiters we had that night. I felt like I made two new friends by the end of the night. This place takes care of you and there is no air of pretentiousness at all. Just a great, great spot for wine & food in a lovely atmosphere.
Absolutely DELICIOUS. The octopus is to die for.

The best brunch I've had in a while! Both things we got were outstanding. The pancakes were made to perfection paired with amazing maple syrup. I would definitely suggest the chicken sandwich as well. The ingredients paired perfectly and the bread was super fresh. Definitely want to go back!
What a find! We've become addicted and now come every two weeks. The food is delicious and doesn't feel heavy. The fact that it's vegan is such a plus!!! Highly recommended!

I've heard great things about this place since moving to Woodside, so I decided to finally try it. I just ordered Drunken Noodles (usually one of my favorite Thai dishes) and was a little bummed. While I asked for "medium spiciness" noodles were completely mild and a little bland. I had to mix in a substantial amount of extra peppers and fish sauce I had on the side to punch up the flavor. Also, perhaps this was my mistake, however I was a bit disappointed that the noodles didn't have any other veggies in it other than tiny cherry tomatoes and basil (after re-reading the menu I realized vegetables weren't listed )--I will have to rethink my order next time I decide to give this place a second try.

The service here is great. Â I overpaid one time and they remembered to pay me back on my next visit. Â Very great people working here. Â  The Banh Mi, not so great. Â It's definitely made for the western taste buds...you know, the same people who order General Tso at eat in Chinese Restaurants.

Decided to stop here for dinner after a long day of work and an hour of shopping. Thanks to reco's from other Yelpers , I ordered the meatballs as an appetizer . Â best choice ever! Â The meatballs were tender and very flavorful with just the right amount of sauce. Â They were also on top of a "to die for" creamy cheese. Â Yum! For my meal I ordered the long square pasta (can't recall the name, sorry!). Â  It was divine! Oh and of course the view was very nice. Â I knew to ask for a window seat, thanks to fellow Yelp reviews :-) the only reason I'm not giving this place 5 stars is simply due to being charged $4/drink for a diet coke. Â  It's one thing to charge for refills, but nowhere on the menu did it tell me that. Â Come on, folks - just tell me and I'd be ok with it (or at least know not to order 3 of them!!).

Oh boy, were we in for a treat or what!? Since our first trip to NOLA last year, we've been dying for the flavors up here. Sugar Freak freakishly reminded us the good food that we had down there. The gumbo was simply full of bursting flavors, and most importantly, it was not mushy. There was a bite to it. The vegetarian muffuletta was simply, "I can't believe it's not meat!" I had a quarter of the muffuletta at Central Grocery in NOLA, while that was sensational, this vegetarian variant was even better: it tasted so lush without the guilt. And yes, there was the drippy olive oil, something that you have to experience eating a muffuletta. Dessert must-have: Popcorn pudding with salted caramel (dump cake). What the heck is that? I want to slather it all over my fat belly right now. All the servers were super friendly and sweet. For once, I ain't bitching!

Absolutely fantastic! Â This place is incredibly popular and loud-try to snag a seat outside if it's warm out. We started out with the tilapia ceviche, which was incredible. Â Light and fresh. Â And the jicama in it! Â I've never had jicama in ceviche before, but it added just a touch of sweetness which, in my opinion, made the dish. Â Yum! For dinner, we shared the Carnitas for 2. Â Everything was delicious and perfectly seasoned and cooked! Â The meat was tender and very flavorful. Â Accompanied by delicious rice and beans, this dish was great. Â I love this place and wish I could find something like it at home!

Lordy, Lordy, Lordy. That is the best pizza I ever had. Total dive, barely a place to eat. Two slices (one white, one white with spinach). Fortunately in NYC on business for a few days, so I intend to return for dinner again. And lunch. And breakfast. And snacks. So close to the tourist trap of times square you'd think it wouldn't be quality. And you'd be dead wrOng.
it's a chain falafel place, but the food is always good and fast, i'd always ask for extra hot sauce, i would go back.

Why must you be so far from me, Joe's Shanghai? Truly my fav Xiao Long Bao in the states. I should also note that I have never gone to Taiwan and have only eaten soup dumplings at Din Tai Fung here in Arcadia, CA. Warranted? **Shrugs shoulders** Super hot when they come out so be careful to not burn yourself and your neighbor. Rice Cakes are good and so are the jelly fish noodles. Communal seating and the waiters are rude. No offense - but all authentic Chinese restaurant waiters are rude. That's how you know you are getting the real stuff! It's a give and take relationship. I will take amazing food with expected sub par service at a Chinese place any day!

First we came here was for dinner and it was amazing. The calamari was fresh and fried just right. The curry was excellent and the coconut rice was perfect. But then we stopped by for their lunch special and it was disappointing. We had the pad thai and green curry and it was kinda cold and felt like it was microwaved.
twitter update

It's 1:10am and I just came from Mark with a bellyful of the best sliders. VERY RARELY will I write a review as soon as I leave a restaurant, but I'm a huge fan of late-night eats and Mark just hit the spot. The Lakers game was on, good music, it wasn't too crowded, and the service was great. Sliders are $2.50 a piece and come with cheese and onion. Beer is $5 and fries start from $4. Very affordable considering it's in the city. Good vibes, good beats, good food. Easy 5 stars.

I was craving some french onion soup so after a little research I found out that cafe triskell's french onion soup was voted the best in NYC in 2013. It's only open Wednesday through Sunday and the hours are pretty weird. I was surprised when I walked in and found the place empty. It's also very small and there's not a lot of tables. However it does have a rustic french feel. The waiter was ok although I was slightly disappointed that he didn't smile the whole time I was there, he just looked tired. Now on to the french onion soup, I was expecting it to give my mouth an orgasm but sadly it didn't. It was just ok really, nothing special. Personally, I don't think there was a lot of cheese on top, i would have probably given an extra star if it had more cheese. I honestly don't believe that this is the best onion soup in NYC, there's probably so many other french places in manhattan that make it better. They give you bread on the side and butter. The bread is good when you dunk it in the soup and it would have been so much better if it was hot. And they sprinkle flour on top of the bread which proves to be very messy. You get flour all over the table, your hands, and clothes. Is it really necessary to add flour, I could do without it. They only take cash which is very annoying, I really wanted to order a dessert crepe but I didn't think I would have enough cash for it. The total for the French onion soup was 9.80 including tax. I left the waiter 3 bucks when I was only supposed to leave him 1.70 just like the menu says 18% gratuity recommended. He looked at the cash on the table and looked pissed. I won't be going back, I suggest you find a french place in manahattan.

Although all the food we ate here was very good and I actually really like the place ".THEY SERVED US A DEEP FRIED MOUSE ON THE BOTTOM OF OUR CHIPS " No joke my boyfriend ate a piece of it thinking it was Â a pepper..And after calling the waiters attention to the fact I quote " I think these chips were a little mousey" We got nothing off our bill .....!!!!!!!!!!!
Great sushi and service and it's a very unique experience.
Every time I order here for delivery food is still hot. Everything on their menu is delicious. Definitely recommend this place.

I followed all of the amazing reviews when I tried out this cute, local spot. We got there and there was a wait (always a good sign), and we had a very helpful bartender pick us out a half bottle of wine. Everything was great- the food- the ambiance, our super cute waiter. Conveniently located in the food desert that is murray hill (even though it's in gramercy). Get the eggplant parm- you won't be dissapointed!

I love their small plates and their drink selection. The lamb meatballs are always a must, as well as the cabbage salad and bacon wrapped dates. This is such a cute restaurant, nice service and an adorable bar. Great lunch time date place. Such a perfect restaurant.

It was late-ish. Not really, but it was Sunday so many were back at home watching Breaking Bad or the Olympics. But we're rebels, hungry rebels. We quickly checked our trusty Yelp app and beelined over to Upstate - after 1st and 2nd choices were closed. Once in and seated, we had 5 mins to get our orders in - like I said, it was late-ish. There were several appetizing options on the menu, but we narrowed it down to the Scallop Ceviche and Shrimp w/Beans and Organic Rice. Both dishes were superb. The scallops were insanely fresh and the ceviche was actually a very grown up, sashimi version of the Latin delicacy. The Shrimp dish was also spot-on fantastic. Giant, delicious shrimp served atop a hearty bed of Southern style rice and beans. Full of flavor. Great ambiance and service w/a smile - no wonder this place has such stellar reviews.
Amazing place! one of kind food and excellent service! I would give it 10 stars.
came before a show. got a burger, a decent burger, but an expensive burger. that is all i have to say.

I picked this place and D has never had Korean BBQ. Everything is weird for D, D will not try a lot of things. This is someone that I definitely can't just pick a restaurant and expect D to be okay with the food. I have to make sure the place is not weird or for the adventurous eater. D approved the Korean BBQ and was willing to give it a whirl. I wish they offered more and better banchans. Their kimchee was good, but we didn't get that many variety of banchans. The Galbi here, I really love - marinated perfectly. However, I didn't care for their seafood pancakes here. They put the imitation crab sticks in their version. I hardly got any real seafood. Sigh. This was definitely a disappointment. The other downside is they don't take reservations and they don't even call you if your table is ready. I would come back here with another friend that is more open minded to food.

As everyone has said, the kale salad was amazing and vegan friendly for my passionate vegan friends out there. I chose a vegetarian entree myself and got the farmers basket which was essentially an awesome warm salad with a poached egg. I was most impressed with the cocktails, mainly the one made with 'Ecuadorian moonshine' - it tasted like a fancy alcoholic version of an orange cremesicle - if I wasn't so responsible I would have spoiled the rest of my brunch and evening drinking those. My party of 3 was sitting at a table at the front and the front windows/doors of the restaurant were opened up onto the streets so the whole experience was great. Great service and food, would definitely come back here again!

We ordered this for an office lunch yesterday and it was all delicious! Delivery was a bit slow and they forgot a side salad, but we did place a very large order, so I'm assuming it just got lost in the shuffle. Everything is very cheap and quite delicious. Fries were mediocre, but tzatziki and hummus are good and pita is warm, even when delivered. We would definitely order again!

Ivy definitely has the key components for success but is not quite there yet. I came here with a large dinner party, on reservation. We were seated in the mostly private cozy back area which was perfect considering we were a big group and awfully loud. The menu is standard with lots of sandwiches, salads, burgers, and a few creative sides and add-ons here and there. The highlights of the meal for me was the truffle mashed potatoes, cheesy brussel sprouts with herbs, and the nicely prepped chicken cutlet they used on their sandwiches. Pat La Frieda blend burger was under-seasoned and overcooked. For whatever reason, this place is obsessed with turning up the heat! Nearly every sandwich at our table was doused in hot sauce, sriraracha aioli, or covered in hot peppers and jalapenos. Some dishes warned about their spicy nature on the menu, while others did not. Reason I'm mentioning is because the sandwiches really didn't need to be masked, they were solid as is! Overall I would not return for dinner but if you're stuck with a big group I can see Ivy doing the trick. Nice cocktails and a good place to pre-game for your night out.

Man, their meatballs are so freaking gewd! The way it works is that you choose one ball (classic beef, spicy pork, chicken, veggie), a sauce (tomato, spicy meat sauce, mushroom gravy, Parmesan cream, pesto), and sides. Side selections include polenta, white beans, risotto, salad, roasted veggies, and a few other sustainable items. We went with the classic beef with classic tomato and "Everything But The Kitchen Sink" salad; why have one or two sides, when you can have it all? We also had the spicy pork with mushroom gravy and "Everything But The Kitchen Sink" salad. The meatballs were so tender, moist, and bursting with flavor. The mushroom gravy was my favorite, but even the classic tomato sauce was delicious. The medley of roasted vegetables were so divine. I loved the cauliflower and carrots; so simply prepared, but so rustic and tasty. The next chance I get to visit New York, this will definitely be a must!
this shawarma is s good im jizzing in my pants

All my pizza and Â fantasies center around L&B. I get back whenever I can, freeze half a Sicilian pie and put it in my suitcase (If you're thinking about doing the same it must be a checked bag for two reasons: 1. It stays cold. 2. The sauce counts as liquid). Unfortunately, I haven't had as much airplane luck with the spumoni or ices. They're better enjoyed outside L&B's on a hot summer day.

A group of us were out here for dinner on a week night. The decor is true Parisien along with the fact that the staff are French. While glancing at the menu, I was excited to see french onion soup + escargots, different types of mussels and steak frites..which I feel are the quintessential french dishes I prefer to get. The onion soup and escargots were in fact delicious! My husband was dead set on ordering the Steak frites but ended up going with the Beef Bourguignon. It wasn't terrible but not a great dish. I just don't feel beef should be partnered with noodles. Other dishes were good at our table. The salmon tasted fresh and fantastic. The service did not help our dining experience. Our french waiter, whom I spoke to in French, felt so rushed that night. Our entrees took a while to arrive a the table and when they did things were disorganized. I did not receive the Â mussels that I ordered. I was supposed to get he ones with seafood broth. Instead I received the tomato sauce which I didn't noticed until I started eating and getting towards the bottom. Overall we both didn't get the ideal dishes we wanted. I'm not opposed to coming on another time for dinner and brunch.

This is my favorite restaurant/bar in Brooklyn. Love the food, love the beer/wine selection, almost always love love love the music. Some things that get me down: its cash only the host can be a pain no liquor is served However, none of these things really get me down (except the rude host thing, that almost ruined my evening last time I was there), I put them out there more as suggestions for how Moto could be even more awesome.

I want to love this place, but the food just isn't that great. Â Good atmosphere - casual, downtown feel - great space. Â Lots of lines on the weekends for brunch, but it's a fun place to take people who haven't been before. Â Completely reasonably priced.

This place is YUM. Stumbled across this place with a friend on a Friday evening. Waited only 10 minutes, but knew it'd be good because it was packed. Service was just alright, they forgot to bring my friend's wine until we asked about 2/3 through. Oh, but the food is yum. We shared 3 dishes--falafel, calamari, and sauteed spinach.
