The quantity was perfect for the two of us, especially with that awesome bread served with it.

I was so anticipating trying Ssam bar since I've never been before. Â Maybe my palate is off. Â Or maybe I'm just not that into the items here... All i know is that i was not impressed. Â Sure, there are people who would swear by the place but their bossam or their port buns are not that extraordinary. Â But i did like their set-up...

Waited half hour / 45 minutes at 3:30 in afternoon. Liked the amount of scallions, bean sprouts and meat they added to the dish (more than other places) but the spicy oil in the broth was a little alarming at times. Took away from enjoying the flavor of the noodles. Maybe just wasn't expecting it and I do love spicy (korean) ramen. I most recently had been to Ramen Yebisu in Williamsburg and couldn't help but compare, thinking this bowl was just as good as the one I had there and did not have to wait.

starting going here one saturday night about 5 months ago and loved it so have been back every saturday night since, in addition to some week nights. went there january 12th with my brother and actually started to think that they had sold the restaurant, the experience was so bad. for starters the waitress was very distracted. the hanger steak was good but where was that delicious tomatillo pepper salsa? there was maybe a teaspoon of it, and those delicious cowboyfries were super duper soggy. we waited forever for the meal, and even longer for the dessert and there were only three other people there. i am hoping that this was an off night for someone, i so loved this place, and now i am torn. i will return soon and i will be keeping my fingers crossed.... come on alice, i was was one of your biggest fans!!!! i told everybody about this place!!!!

I've been wanting to try this place for a while, but it always has a super long wait! Came here during lunch time on a week day and I only had to wait 15 minutes! Pros: Super yummy corn. I can't tell what kind of cheese is on it, but it was delicious, and normally I don't like most cheeses! Also, the Cuban sandwich was really juicy! Cons: The chicken quesadilla was unfortunately not very good. It tasted like cancer in your mouth, over-cooked! Overall, yummy experience. I'd definitely come back for the corn and Cuban!
OK food. Infused vodkas are too sweet. Not really sure why they're always packed. Cute ambiance.

We went to Junior's after hearing that they have THE BEST cheesecake EVER. We tried the Raspberry Swirl Cheesecake and it was "eh." Maybe we weren't in the mood for cheesecake, but it didn't WOW me at all. Overrated? Possibly.
Waiting time is too long ( 1- 1.5 hrs) , not worth it.

The shrimp Bloody Mary is reason enough to give this place a try, but as a bonus, the food, decor, and bartender were all great. The shoestring fries are a great companion to any sandwich, especially the amazing chicken club. My friend got the spinach and blue cheese croissant and ate every bite. Great Brooklyn brunch spot.

Hillstone (formerly Houston's) is one of my favorite go-to places in midtown. It's consistently good, service is very professional, the booths are cozy, the ambiance is nice and dark, and they have unlimited refills with the soft drinks - which always gets high marks in my book. Â  I've tried most things on their menu but 90% of the time I order their fabulous veggie burger. It's the best I've ever tried though I am quite certain it's not low fat or diet by any means. They won't give away the recipe but it's made up of brown rice, beets, prunes, soy sauce (?), honey (?) and I don't know what else, but it tastes even BETTER than their hamburgers - believe me! The bun is buttered and toasted and very bad for you but it's just SOOO good. Â The burger comes w/fries on the side but you can substitute for something else - like a veggie, yummy cole slaw, small caesar salad, or the big, beautiful, loaded baked potato (yes, it's loaded with butter, sour cream, cheese, bacon, scallions). Hillstone wins my prize for best veggie burger but also gets the grand prize for the best ever loaded BP!! Â Sometimes I will split the veggie burger & baked potato w/my companion and we're still full - it's a very large portion. Â  Houston's also offers great entrÃ©e salads, delicious veggie sides, yummy artichokes, sandwiches, steaks, fish of the day, and their ribs are to die for! We never have room for dessert - in the 100x we've been, we might have gotten the warm brownie once and yes, it was delicious but I can't imagine anyone being hungry for dessert after all that food. Hillstone doesn't take reservations and if you get there at 7 during the week there could be an hour wait so plan accordingly - you can always hang out in the Barnes & Noble while you wait.

As Ippudo has set the standard of Ramen in this city, I suppose it's only fair that I compare Totto's ramen with Ippudo's. I have tried both the super spicy and spicy ramen here and the problem with the super spicy ramen is that it completely drowns out all the subtle flavors of the broth. The spicy ramen however does let you taste all the different flavors and even though it's a very good broth, I would still rank Ippudo's broth higher. Where Totto does rank higher in my books is the noodle and the pork. Â The noodle is more chewy and the charsiu pork is blowtorched which gives it the perfect texture and sweetness. So Totto loses out to Ippudo in terms of broth but Â wins in almost every other aspect including wait time and price. It's a tough call since the broth is such an important part of the ramen experience. I am going with 4 stars for both.
South Brooklyn staple. Wonderful, deep-rooted Italianness. The sauce will blow out your ears like the voice of Frankie Valle. And that's a good thing.

We were visiting NYC from out of town and had to hit this place up because we saw it on DDD. It was just as good as it looked on TV. The wait staff was nice and attentive. The restaurant was classic Williamsburg with great outdoor seating (seating is not just what you can see from outside, so don't be afraid to go in if it looks full). I had the catfish fry with cornbread, coleslaw and a garden salad. The catfish and cornbread were gluten free, which was such a nice surprise! The renegade iced tea is awesome, too! My boyfriend had the chicken and waffles and he died over them. Our whole group decided that this was their favorite meal in NYC! Go check it out!

Kids! You should be looking for new & exciting (anything) you know and if you don't like falafel or street meat this might be the place to try both! A falafel pita (deep fried chick pea balls) with white sauce and lettuce in a pita is only $5. That's pretty standard fare if you are a New Yorker, but what you might not know about is their new chicken shawarma! Pita $5 plate $7. Chicken on a rotisserie type deal with all kinds of unique spices makes way for a delicious new style of moist chicken! Try it over yellow rice with a little bit of hot sauce, because this hot sauce makes this Mexican sweat. You'll get plenty to share. Thank me later. See you there.

Great atmosphere. Really cute dim open restaurant/bar. Exposed brick and nice retro modern lighting. A great place to sip drinks and people watch. The drinks are really exceptional. Â They don't have their menu online, and I can't quite remember what was in my drink, but the first was a coconut, lime, basil concoction where the top 2/3 was frothed coconut milk (and creme?). It was delicious. Other great drinks followed, a chipotle one, which had a nice kick but not strong enough to obscure other flavors. Service was a little slow, but I wasn't there to rush.

Love love this place.. although I really need to stop coming here on breaks and actually come here when I have the time to take it easy and enjoy myself. The oxtail is my absolute favorite. Yes, please! Seconds? Sure. Just bring me some extra lemonade ;) Make sure you save room for dessert.. especially if they have freshly made bread pudding. You may need to sober up a bit after a piece of that goodness!
go for happy hr, get the regular margarita and the fish tacos!

3 1/2 STARS. After much anticipation (mostly from watching Marc Forgione's delicacies and genius on Iron Chef) I had dinner here. Let me list the plus first, because there were many: Amazing cocktails Great service Great ambience Great cooking techniques Good and original food I love to take a cerebral approach to food, I like to be challenged and surprised, but I do not take pleasure in eccentricity if there is not great flavor to the food. I mean great, not good. Overall, Forgione's food was perfectly cooked - the scallops were buttery, the fish full of moisture, the eggs cooked at 63C had a perfect texture, and the lump crap ceviche had a great texture. However, except for the ceviche, which probably had the best harmony of flavors, the other dishes lacked some detail or another, and several of them had an overpowering saltiness to it. The cod dish (a fish soup) was too salty to appreciate the sweetness of the scallops and shrimp and the savoriness of the clams. Also it lacked a bit of acidity. The truffle egg 'bruschetta' was superb but again the flavors were a bit flat (the truffle wasn't of the most perfumed I have had). So if this waren't Marc Forgione's restaurant, I would have rated it a solid 4 stars, but this is his restaurant, he is an iron chef, he is creative and has solid dishes but my dining experience was rather muted. I dined several times at Traif in Brooklyn, and I was expecting a similar approach to food. All the dishes I have had at Traif were superb and complex and just so godly that you often have to eat them with your eyes closed. I was expecting this restaurant to give me the same challenge and pleasure but it did not. I think you should try it once but then head to Traif. Traif's chef, Chef Jason Marcus, deserved to be crowned soon, and I am looking forward to see him on TopChef or Iron Chef. PS: The desserts were very decadent and flavorful. Also Yelp should price this at 4 not 3 $. 2 appetizers, 3 drinks, 2 entrees, and 2 desserts were at about $240.

I come here at least once a week and I've never been disappointed. Everything I've had is great- granted I've never been for brunch. Staff in awesome, pasta is always fresh and homemade. Great specials excellent prices, love the atmosphere. Try the chicken giovani or the four cheese pasta with walnuts.

The food here is awesome and ridiculously cheap. Just don't even think about dining in, unless of course you don't care much about talking to the person(s) you're with; it's way too damn loud in there.

I have such mixed feelings about this place. The food is great and it's a very reasonable price. The service is pretty much non existant. It's pre made curry poured over pre cooked rice, yet I've waited 15 minutes or more for an order. The place has also become a hang out for college kids who obviously have nothing better to do. There are a total of 4 tables and yet half the time they are occupied by these kids, who are NOT eating... just sitting there talking. Paying customers with actual food should have these seats, but management never does anything Â about it.... If you have 45 minutes to kill, and can manage not to kill these loafers, you will have a good lunch

The hype is for real! I came here with a few friends on a Wednesday night immediately realizing that it's BYOB we sent someone from our group to go across the street to get some tall boys. We ordered the cap'n crunch chicken fingers, chicken empanadas, and disco tots. Cap'n crunch chicken fingers were excellent but the dip was amazing sweet and spicy.The sugar hill burger is hands down the best and most unique burger I ever had. It is sweet but not overpowering pecan bacon is awesome and the blue cheese adds a nice compliment to it. I could go on and on about this place but you really need to go try it for yourself.

Great egg and cheese on croissant! The place is classy but comfortable. I would love to hang out here for a couple hours with a good book. They've got a full brunch menu plus juices and some alcohol. The owner is very nice, too.

Now that's a spicy guac! Yes their guac has a pretty high heat level, but there are plenty of pricey drinks to wash it down with. My friends and I came here for the tacos and guac. The food here was good and the service needs a little work. It's a hole in the wall without a sign screaming come "get tacos here!", so small that there were lots of moments of hustle bustle and rubbing of the back of my chair. I think by the fourth time the waitress bumped into my chair I got an apology. It was also lacking a little elbow room between tables. the tacos here are small and listed in the appetizer section of the menu. The guac is spicy and is serve with a red pepper sauce, just remember that you can get lots of free refills on chips so if you are coming here just for drinks just order the guac and wash down the heat with your drinks. I wouldn't plan to come here with large groups and or more than four people. it gets really crowded right after work.

Another great west village spot with no pretentious waiters or bartenders who think they are rock stars. low key atmosphere, nice people at the bar, and the second best hamburger Ive had in nyc. a simple menu but thats all you need, the fries are just right too, none of this breaded fries garbage so many places offer. also some very reasonable beers on tap. it get crowded at night, good reasons, so get in early as you can. plus the bar itself is a beautiful antique worth seeing for its own sake. dont hesitate! the sports on tv is not my taste but if you want to follow the "game" you cant find a nicer spot...

I just visited NYC for the first time, I live in Austin TX. I went to quite a few restaurants and this one was the bestttttt. There was a 45min-1hr wait, which is quite a while, however the amazing hostess said she would text me when the table was ready. What? thats awesome! haha. so we went to a bar to get a beer and the wait went by quickly and I received the text and we went back to the restaurant and were seated. The atmosphere here is just so great. Its busy but still intimate. I had a burger and fries which was amazing. We also shared some oysters which were fantastic. Next time I go to NY this place will be #1 on my list to go back to.
Best felafel I've had in NYC, and I still can't believe the price is locked down that low. Hot sauce is very good too. Service is fast.

Been getting the banh-mi here for about a year - great go-to for $7! Â Not very appealing to eat-in at, but I've done it and it's okay. Â The pho with oxtail broth and chicken is also amazing (and really two portions in one.)

To Brooklyn Crab's credit, their ambience is pretty spot-on. I've been to a number of seafood and crab houses throughout the Northeast coast, and this place has all the right trappings, from the giant crab perched outside and the Great White shark's head in the front to the wooden picnic tables and the bottles of artisan hot sauces decorating the booths. Four of us came with high expectations -- not having read any reviews beforehand -- and we were thrilled to be seated almost immediately in the coveted topmost area (this was around 5:00 pm on a Friday). But great trappings a solid seafood spot do not make. On the plus side, the service was efficient and our waitress was accommodating and very friendly. We started with the fried whole belly Ipswich clams which were delicious -- lightly fried to a crispy but not greasy outside, allowing the briny buttery natural goodness of the clams to shine through. Then my friends ordered a dozen of the oysters, half "house" and half du jour. Not being particularly fond of raw oysters myself, I can only say they seemed to enjoy them. But seriously, how can you mess up raw oysters? The mains are where this restaurant falls short of hitting any respectable mark. First of all, the food is insanely overpriced considering the mediocre quality of the seafood itself, not to mention the portion sizes. Three of us had the steam pots -- one Southern and two Northeast. Now, for $36-40 per pot (!!!) I would expect the whole nine yards and then some. But my Southern steam pot only included 4 very small blue crabs -- granted, they were males at least, but only about the size of a woman's closed fist -- about 6 somewhat dirty and unseasoned mud bugs (sorry, crawfish for the uninitiated), one half cob of corn (seriously, you couldn't give me the whole cob at that price?), four dry and tasteless slices of andouille sausage (wtf?!?), and 2 tiny red potatoes. No shrimp. The biggest issue I had was the quality of the seafood. I'm from Maryland, so trust me when I say I know exactly how a freshly steamed blue crab should look and taste. These were not fresh, nor were they hot, suggesting they had been steamed long beforehand and then probably quickly re-steamed to order. The crawfish were unseasoned and cold. The worst indication? I left hungry, even after finishing (somewhat reluctantly) every last morsel in my pot. Sorry Brooklyn Crab, but I shall not be returning. For one thing, my pocketbook can't take being ripped off in this sh*t economy, and besides I'd much rather go to Mary's Fish Camp or Brooklyn Fish Camp, where the prices are more than justified by the high standards of the food itself.

For real, I haven't had such a dining experience in some time. The combination of the disco-ball cool downtown vibe of the dining room posted up next to the BedStuy meets Portland steez of the patio is just classic. Slap that with the customer service reminiscent of a French brasserie w/a dose of hipster chillaxness. Add a heaping dose of fantastic, imaginative dishes and you have straight-up unpretentious premium Brooklyn cuisine. Luckily, we were a group of 4 and our combined selections amounted to nearly half the menu, which by the way couldn't be more appetizing. While the names of the dishes seem to have come from a happy stoner, the dishes themselves can only come from a refined, decadent meets comfort palate. The beef tenderloin was like butter. The E666s w/baby octopus and ume - also buttery. Foie Gras Doughnut. Butterness. Everything seemed to incorporate sophistication w/an indulgent, ironic twist. Whoever did this did it w/heart. I thank you!

Third time back and I'm still at 5 stars. I walked in on a Friday night with a party of 3 and was told that it would be 20-25 min for a table inside but that if I wanted a table outside it could be as fast as 5-10 minutes...if you really don't want to wait long, sit outside to enjoy the beautiful weather. Service was still fast despite being seated outside and you can still hear the great music being played. New foods I've tried this time: Lomo saltado (my god it was heavenly), churrasco (cooked perfectly) For drinks we had the Camilito, the cucumber and passion fruit mojitos, all very strong drinks for the price. Loved them. Again, I've never had an issue here even walking in on a Friday night. Till next time.

I recently had brunch here with a couple of friends. I perused the menu online before I went and was very excited about it. We ordered the huaraches de pollo, the biscuits and gravy (added a poached egg) and the Mexican "eggs Benedict". The pollo was delicious and a nice size portion, the Mexican Benedict was also delicious, but the portion was so small it looked like an appetizer, the biscuits were odd... They were dense and a little sweet, they gravy came in a gravy boat on the side, it was tasty enough but as it cooled it started to break and look a little weird and the poached egg also came on the side I'm a bowl on top of a piece of lettuce. I thought the presentation didn't make any sense. Service here was also off, we had three different people serve our table, and not one asked us how our meal was or if we'd like anything else. I'll go back here to try some other dishes but I'm not sure id recommend it yet.

Somewhat disappointed with this restaurant. After reading reviews online I was looking forward to eating here. Service was good. Very nice atmosphere. The food was just ok and for the price I expected much more. I won't be going back.

man down....body ache and cold sweat. Â at least I was able to see Leslie my friend from grade school and enjoy this wonderful orgasm in the mouth experience....creme brulee like desert with a sugar carmelized crust that blows your mind.....squid stuff with ox tail with squid ink sauce.....were faves....the lamb was super tender....a must in nyc

It is hard to find something decent near the Penn station so we were happy to find this place. Fast service and great lunch option, we enjoyed our meal and made it back to the station to catch the train on time. Definitely a go if you are looking for a good meal in the area. Service was very nice and fast. Place is very quiet inside so you can enjoy the conversation.

I went with my son and husband the first Saturday of July which was my first time. Â My son wanted to go again because the first time he went he wasn't happy with the service. Â He wanted to give them another try and they did not dissapoint. Service was excellent many employees on staff and were attentive. Â I ordered the short ribs which was fabulous. Â The men ordered the chicken and red velvet waffles, which they enjoyed. Â We also had the skillet mac and it was very good. Â Oysters as an app, not bad, but of course not enough. Â Give it a try.

This is my new go-to place for Monday evenings. I haven't been on the weekend at all, but it's just right during the week. The bartenders are awesome and friendly. One of the co-owners has been there everytime I've been in. He's really friendly and sweet. He's always wearing a cap and glasses and rolled up jeans. The Ward III cocktail is damn good! It's a combo of Maker's, fresh strawberries, egg white, peychaud bitters, lime and nutmeg. I've also had a number of bespoke cocktails. I usually ask for bourbon based, spirit forward and something citrusy with a little spice to it. Never been disappointed. They are super creative up in here, so get a bespoke cocktail made to your specifications. They will do a fantastic job making you happy. The food is damn good too. The pulled duck sandwiches are awesome. I generally don't like duck, but these kind of don't taste like duck. The salmon croquettes are quite good as well. The one thing I haven't liked there is the mac 'n cheese. I'm picky about my mac and this stuff just wasn't cheesy enough. The crust was awesome, but that's where the awesome ended. The rest was not cheesy and very greasy wihtout much flavor. The decor in here is a little random, but it works. My ONLY complaint about this place is the DJ. I have only been on a Monday night, which one would think is rather quiet, but this guy is TOO LOUD. There was some Springsteen blaring when I walked in the other night and I couldn't even hear my friend. I had to ask the waitress if the DJ could turn it down so we could have a conversation, which luckily he obliged us. But it's just unnecessary for the crowd and for the space. But that's really my only complaint. Otherwise, it's a fine establishment that I will continue to frequent.
Best pizza I have had! Warm atmosphere! Friendly staff! Only negative thing I can say is the line to get in but worth the wait. The owner even greeted and chatted with us as we waited in line.
Fantastic food and service! Try the sizzling sea sick (spelled wrong, but pronounced that way) a must have! Everything my lady and I tried was delicious and worth coming back for!!!
I love this place! The selection of cheeses are amazing.

love everything about this spot, from the kick-ass bartenders to the portraits of the various walters splattered throughout the establishment. then you've got your food- my personal faves are deviled eggs, spinach artichoke dip (if you're feeling naughty), the french dip sandwich, and fresh market oysters. the kitchen stays dear to my heart by remaining open until 1 and the bartenders never cease to rock my world with the timeless classics they mix up (both in cocktail form behind the bar and in beat form comin' out the speakers). hands down the best local cocktail joint in the area. ask for alejandro or tommy and tell him katie sent you...he'll know what to do.
Delicious pierogies, keilbasa! Two thumbs up!!!

Simply sublime. A wonderful pairing of innovative tapas and interesting varietals in a casual but elegant setting. There's much to be explored here but the tasting menu is where it's at. The space is very intimate, with seating only at the bar facing the chefs' pulpit allowing you to see every step of careful preparation in the organized and efficient stations. Even a moment of observation will whets the appetite for the delights to come; you'll want everything.

In short, making delicious italian affordable in an area where everything is over priced and lacking quality. We went on a Monday, and it was busy. Â Reservations would be wise. Â We got a small table in the back against the wine wall. Â And like many other places, very tight and intimate with the table next to you. Â So don't think you'll be able to have a conversation with your date without the input of your neighbor, because they will hear all that is said and you will have no secrets. Â  The beauty of this place is the prices. Â Yes, the entrees are about $25+ a person. But the VALUE of the food makes it worth it. Â In many places in the Theatre District you can expect those prices, but the value and quality of the food is hit or miss. Â Here, expect greatness. Â The specials for the night were never ending... as a server myself, I couldnt believe how long our server went on and on and on and on about things that were new, and in addition to what we saw. Â We really didn't remember half of them. Â But what did catch our attention was the pasta dinner special. Â For $24 a person, you get a salad or the antipasto as a starter, and then three different pastas that are never ending. Yes... never... ending... as much as you want. Â The selections for our night were penne bolognese, wild mushroom ravioli, and spaghetti marinara with fresh basil. Â I don't eat meat, my boyfriend asked if it was possible to get any combination and avoid the meat pasta, to which the server said yes, absolutely, they could make a no meat dish. Â I wasn't expecting that, I was just thinking, I'll skip that meat pasta. Â  Water was served when we sat down, and bread basket and olives as well. Â Since it was my boyfriends birthday, and we had a connection in getting our reservation, glasses of prosecco were brought over. Â It was a really nice touch. Â  We both got the salad, and with my boyfriend being picky about his salad dressing, he was really impressed. Â He loves his salad dressing...but its gotta be flavorful, and plentiful. This was both. Â When it came time for the dinner, the new plates were warm (nice touch), and the pasta served in great portions. Â I skipped the penne bolognese, and got the wild mushroom ravioli, and the spaghetti with marinara, and then, to my surprise, they brought out a pasta made "special for me'! A penne dish with fresh vegetables and olive oil. Amazing. Â I was so happy. Â The thought for them to do that was great.. it wasnt on the menu that night as part of the pasta special, so I was very grateful. Â With dinner we got a bottle of one their $25 wines. Theres a whole page of wines available for just $25! Categorized in light, medium and full bodied reds, whites, and sparking. Â Makes it easy to pick something new. Â  Dinner was cleared and dessert with a candle was brought out. Â Again, such a nice touch. Â We felt very special and well taken care of. Â  We had to rush out because of a show at 8pm, so getting the check in time was a bit stressful. Â We watched the clock tick and we didn't get the check. Then when we did, the prosecco was included. Â I felt REALLY bad saying something, as it was complimentary and a nice gesture... but I didn't order it... and the comp was not reflected on the bill. Â When the bill came back, the dessert and prosecco were on the bill, but properly reflected as a comp at the bottom. Â  The service was great, the food was delicious and the atmosphere was cozy and warm. Â We left cash for the bill and ran to the theatre. Â  For the wine and two pasta specials, our bill was $77. We left $100 in cash to compensate for the extra effort and complimentary items we received. If you're looking for a nice dinner out before a show, or something you can guarantee is going to be quality, and where you'll be well taken care of, this is the place to go. Â Even if we didn't get the extras, it was worth it. Very much worth it.

Really good, and not in the back of a bodega. Went to the Proletariat beforehand (loved) and needed sustenance that didn't come in the form of wheaty bubbles. Cheap, large (1 and a beer is totally filling) and great choice of beers. Seems to get a drunken late night crowd that will probably eat anything. Â Also really nice sauces (coconut masala) was my favorite.

Tried twice to like this restaurant and it failed miserably both times and its all due to the service. This most recent time we came in, were greeted and the hostess said we would have a table in a few moments. Â If we had known it was going to be 20 minutes we would have tried to get a drink but when we got tired of waiting for them to get us for the table and tried to get that drink, the bartenders were too concerned with their own conversation to give us the time of day (had their backs to the bar- big NO NO) Made it to the table eventually. Â The waitress was very nice. Â My husband works in the business so the kitchen sent out a bunch of extras to our table. Â They could have been coursed out better but whatever, the food was all very very good. Â In the middle of our courses my husband was still eating off one of the salad plates and the waitress came over and took away his share plate from under him- food was still on the fork!!!! BIG NO NO. Â To top off the evening, the waitress came over, knocked the candle onto the floor spilling wax everywhere- on my purse, my husbands jacket, and his shoes. Â Are you serious? Â I would have appreciated someone offering to dry clean our items even if we would never have taken it but all we got was a pathetic "Sorry". Again, the food was awesome but I will never return because the service was so unbelieveably terrible.
Been to Grimaldi's few years back- Â This is a tourist trap in my opinion. Â The qualify of pizza does not justify the wait time. Â  If anything, I'd much prefer Lombardi's pizza in Little Italy.

the macarons are undoubtedly the best i've ever had. my personal favorite is the salted caramel flavor--sooooo good. yeah, the macarons will run you $3 each, but they're worth every penny! why minus 1 star? because my experience, on multiple visits, has been that most of the employees are d-bags--plain and simple. unfriendly, rude, and make it seem like they're going out of their way to, well, do their job...? ex- if i'm spending $40 on one of those gift box dealies, don't roll your eyes at me (or at least wait until you turn around and aren't facing me) when i politely ask if you could actually get me a pink box instead of a purple one, you little punk! whatevs--the tasty macarons make it worth putting up with the crappy employees.
I did not like this pizza, I guess u dont know what real pizza taste like unless you try Difaras, thats a message for everyone who gave this place five stars.

I waited over an hour and a half in a crowded bar/waiting area and for the first hour, I did not have a seat. :( Â  I decided to wait that long because of all the raving reviews Lombardi's has. Â In addition, they've been around for a loooong time. Â So it's just a matter of trying out to see what's the big deal. Â  When the pizza came, it was alright. Â I was not totally impressed because my pizza was slightly burned on the edges. Â But that's ok because I do not Â eat the crust anyways. Â The toppings were mediocre but the pie is really huge. Â This is definitely to share with like 3-4 people if you're going to order more than 1 pizza. Â  I do recognize the excitement this place brings. Â The decor is rustic and the crowds are very vibrant. Â I really like the neighborhood area and the overall atmosphere.

What a great place for a lunch date. Â The thai food my friend and I got was delicious (and a bargain at the special lunch prices - I got the Pad see ew and sesame tofu appetizer for $8.50). Â The drinks were also great - we chose from a selection of handmade fruit mojitos and had a key lime martini with graham cracker crumbs as our dessert. The decor feels like a vintage luxury hotel - black and white tile with chandeliers, and showy light fixtures - which was kind of cool.

We went for Sunday brunch and waited an hour to be seated because we heard the brunch was amazing. Â I don't know why people think this place is so good for brunch. Â The food was ok, but you can definitely get the same quality down the street from another restaurant without having to wait such a long time to get a seat. Â The bloody mary which is supposed to be the best was not good at all, the grits are not even grits it is Farina that they try to pass off so if you think that you are going to be getting grits don't waste your money. Â Everyone seems to think the brunch here is so amazing but if you know anything about good tasting food and have other brunch places that you thoroughly enjoy I would go to those places before trying this place. Â Hope this helps some of you make a decision!

Don't waste your time. The food is OK, but the oh-so-twee, disneyfied "farm to table" cliche is obnoxious, and the crowd is plucked straight from the "I just moved to New York OMG trendy overpriced food" world. Â This is Alphabet City, and these Florida cornballs just don't fit in. Anyway, the fried chicken is great, the side delicious are great (I like the beans). Though I wish there were some healthier options and better salad options.

Cozy, great staff, fantastic food! The olives were amazing. Â Highly recommended. Lots of great small plates to compliment their wine selection. Didn't get around to trying the pizza but i hear its very good.

Loved the restaurants and market all in one. I had no idea how huge this place was from the outside but I walked into foodie paradise. Tried so many things but my favorite was the charcuterie served at one of the standing tables inside. For sure going back to this place because it was a highlight of my NYC trip! Oh and I got chocolate I could only find on special order from Italy!
Good food. A little touristic. A little too pricey. But always solid quality. You get what you pay for. I recommend this place.
very good empanadas .. i had the reggeaton the sangria was good and we also ordered plantian chips with guacamole it was very tasty!

I went here for a nice dinner with the boy. We had made a reservation during a busy time, and we were seated right away. The ground floor of the restaurant is ridiculously tiny (like 10 tables) so we were literally rubbing elbows with our neighbors throughout dinner. And in this tiny, TINY space, there was not only a live band, but also a picturesque man fastidiously making hand-rolled cigars in the corner (which are free to customers - just tip a few dollars). All of which would have been awesome, if the place had been significantly bigger. As it was, we yelled desperately at each other to form a conversation, over what would otherwise have been very pleasant music. The food, by the way, was delicious. DE-lish. Highly recommend the ropa vieja...like whoa. We struck up a conversation with our server, and he mentioned something about booking spaces for parties. What? Booking this entire tiny restaurant, we said? No, sillies. Of course there would be an entire basement floor, ten times bigger than the ground floor, lit beautifully with candles and antique lamps, quiet and lovely and exactly what we were looking for. Given the quality of the food, the authetic music and the cigars, I would definitely come back - drinks on the ground floor, dinner below.

Came for happy hour after I read all those good reviews (and the bad ones too). I am always on the look out for cheap, quality sushi. Zest delivered. Went on a Friday night with a party of 5 and literally ordered everything on the happy hour menu. The sushi was very fresh and they do not hold out on the ingredients. Other than the sushi, the chicken fried rice on the menu was so delicious I had to order a second. The place is still relatively new compared to their competitor across the street. I had such a good experience that 4 stars seems fair since I have not try their regular menu.
food is okay, Its always many people. some food is reaaly good.

We went here this week and really enjoyed it. We sat at the huge back patio to enjoy the evening air and it was comfortable and staff was friendly. I had an adult lemonade that was perfect, slightly sweet but not sugary. We had macaroni and cheese balls with a plum bbq sauce, pretzel bites with a cheesy dip and burgers with spicy peppers and olives. For dessert we could not resist ice cream sandwiches made of carrot cake cookies and filled with cream cheese ice cream. That was so good! Everything as pretty amazing. We'll definitely go back soon. And when we go I'll opt for the pickled fried chicken. The only thing we couldn't figure out was why it was so empty. Go there! It's so good. You won't regret it.

If I were on an episode of the "Best Thing I Ever Ate - Brunch Edition", the Tres Arepas would be my pick. AMAZING. Went for brunch with four friends. We had a 2p reservation, but had to wait at the bar for about 20 minutes. Restaurant is very small and a bit cramped. We all did the $12 unlimited hour of drinks, and I'm pretty sure they did not count the drinks had at the bar against us. Once seated, the waitress was extremely nice and attentive. I ordered the Tres Arepas, which were PHENOMENAL. So good that I didn't even want Â to share (luckily arepas are not exactly a sharing food). Every bite was truly amazing. I will dream of this dish... literally.

This place has great food at good prices. For $8-12 you can walk out Â full and the food is extremely interesting. The nanban and black pork are great and I can't way to try mire. The cute japanese girl who usually works at the counter is very nice and always willing to suggest her favorites. You gotta try this place they really deserve your business.
in and out is better. burger fi is good for the lack of a wait time

Good , fast & cheap. Â If its fast and good, it wont be cheap and if its cheap and fast it wont be good..and if its good and cheap its generally not fast. Â Not so with Joya. Â  Went in on a rainy Tuesday evening and we were sat right away. Â Ordered the summer roll app, the see noodles, a green curry with shrimp and the tom ka soup. Â  The soup was watery and should of had more coconut milk in it but still was good for the price. Â The summer roll presentation was beautiful. Â Looked like a japanese roll. Â However it tasted like it was wrapped in a wet paper towel. Â Not really what i expected. Â Inside was some fishcake and tofu, i dont even know what was in there really, but it was pretty. The curry was very plain served only with potato and no veggie at all in there. Â Tasty though not the best ive had by a long shot. Â The noodle dish was the winner of the night coming out piping hot and very good with the thicker noodles. 2 thai iced coffees , needed more half and half , milk was used like skim. Â Healthy i guess but again not very tasty. Â  After that i had enough and asked for the check. Â Was 32$ Very reasonable but next time i go in it will only be for noodles. Â Service was quick quick quick. Â  Personally there are better Thai places on court street. Many. Â Cafe Chili is awesome and even Ghang next door is better then here though not as bustling. Â  All and all it was good, fast and cheap. Â But not great, sublime or extra ordinary in anyway.
The chimichurri sauce is out of this world. Love the hamachi, avocado fries and short ribs also. Interesting way that they serve octopus. The brussel sprouts are great too.

came here about 8 months ago and loved the place. Â I had had the chicken dish KOTA and thats what i went back for with my date because I remembered that it was literally to die for. Went back last week and the food has changed, the chicken was not what i remembered at all. I don't know why some places can't just stick with something good when they've got it??? Â Service was so so then and worse now. This pompous skrawney looking waiter guy with a bowtie "helped" us, very unprofessional in his approach, and arrogant. My date wanted to throw her water at him lol. Anyway thanks for embarrassing me!

Vanessa's dumpling used to be one of my favorite cheap eats. Back in the days, when they didn't expand the dumpling house nor have chain restaurants,dumplings tasted so much better. Dumplings were $1 for 5 pieces!!! Now they're $1 for 4 pieces. :( Beef pancakes were $1.25, now they're $1.75. =( Dumplings tasted much crispier and better back then. If they still maintained the price, quantity and quality of the dumplings, I would've given it a 5 stars. Still not a bad place to for cheap lunch, snack or dinner. You get every penny worth of food.
Absolutely love the chicken and ribs! NOM NOM!!

This place is a highlight of my working in Forest Hills. They have a great selection of craft beer. Only down side is you can't get attached to any one beer because the taps rotate pretty frequently. I am also in love with the fried liver appetizer.

Last minute decision to go there for dinner for NYE, and it was a GREAT idea. Â We ate off the pre fixe menu which was a great selection. Â (Looking around the room, most people seemed to opt to order from the regular menu though. ) Â Appetizer was scallops in brown butter - cooked perfectly; Â Branzino for main course-- FANTASTIC, prob one of the best I've had, Â it was in a roasted olive, tomato and garlic sauce on the bottom; Â Dessert was a chocolate brownie more like a cake, which was molten in the middle with a very rich vanilla iced cream on the side. Â The party scene was great, good DJ and music and great fellow diners. Â  The bar area is great for hanging out as well. Â  Only complaint is there is no coat check, and it's just too nice of a place not to have one.

Kind of stumbled upon this place in the closing hours of the chelsea market and immediately wanted to try this place for dinner when I saw they focus on locally sourced ingredients. I'd give the service 3 stars but I want to talk about the outstanding chicken pot pie. The pastry was perfect and the portion just right. Not too large but enough to satisfy my very hungry stomach. It wasn't heavy with cream and had just enough delicate flavor to make this possibly one of the best pot pies I've ever had!

The food here is top notch and the service is very quick. Every time I've went my food is always hot and ready to go. My only pet peeve is that the servers aren't the friendliest people around but I must admit they get the job done.

We went out for KEFI, at Kefi, But had anything of a good mood . I had a couple of day old mousaka. heated in a microwave, warm on the outer areas and cold on inside,I could tell by the color of the cream on top it was cooked a few days prior it was also burned on top . Â The staff were great ! PS Â It did'nt even taste like Greek food !!!
Great service and nice atmosphere. Pizza was good and the arugula salad. Crust a little to soft for my taste but my husband loved it.

A perfect place to chill after the Brooklyn Flea on a Saturday... The decor is really cute and homely and the staff are pretty friendly too. We ordered the lamb sandwich, which didn't quite live up to what we had in our heads... in looks anyway... the lamb was actually in the form of meatballs! The tastiest meatballs I have ever eaten that is. I can't wait to go back and try something else on the menu.

This has to be the best Indian food I've had in New York since moving here last year. The samosas were beautifully made - not soggy, perfectly flakey crust, and great dipping sauce variety. We got saag paneer and aloo gobi with garlic naan. Paneer had the best consistency, super fresh, and the gobi veggies were cooked to perfection. Level of spice was amazing. And yes, expect lots of cilantro, but it's SO good. And another plus - BYOB. Price is just right and the service is incredibly respectful. It's not the fanciest of places but I hardly noticed that. I will be back again and again!!
I used to like this place more, recently everything tastes very oily to me. Â Nevertheless, interesting selection at reasonable prices. Â Nice variety of different bottled teas.

We had dinner at Carmine's one night and the wait was ridiculous. I told myself.. this better be good! So fortunately the food was pretty good but what surprised me were the servings -- they were HUGE! Good thing our waitress tipped us in advance so we ordered just enough for four peeps. This place was fun and lively, but do expect to wait a bit to be seated. One thing that bothered me a lot though were the menus. Menus on the wall? Really? I was squinting so hard trying to read the menu 15 feet from where I was seated.
This was the best restaurant I have ever been to. The chef is an artist. Â Every dish was beautiful and amazing. Service matched the food. Expensive but totally worth it.

doesn't this place have a fire code? Â clowns in a clown car likely have more breathing room than this place on a super drunken freezing saturday night just after the 4am bars close. Â kudos to the staff, for putting up with this and making an amazing falafel for $2.50! by some miracle, we scored a table. Â we had the bottle of hot sauce and our dining companion told everyone that the hot sauce was really weak and they should put a lot on. this was hilarious at 4am. Â  oh, and santa claus was there asking for donations?

The original $1 deals are indeed done, but they do reduce the prices of their 5-piece selections on Wednesdays, so if you happen to like one of the five they curated (you cannot mix & match), it's ultimately the same. Went with their Mediterranean collection (it'd be more appropriately titled Fish Sampler) which includes tuna 22, tuna 23, smoked salmon 72, smoked salmon 75, and anchovies 77. The no-nonsense cashier shot a smile and a thank you as I departed, but looked thoroughly annoyed and equally intrigued by the cellar excavation of an industrial mixer going on outside the entrance. Food was solid enough, very affordable especially pound for pound against tapas joints, and even without the bread would make for a substantial enough meal under $6*, but given the new limits and meh service, I won't be back as much as I would have if it remained "dollar mania", though the 'garden' out back might entice me to drop by with some folks on a random Wednesday in the future. (*More of a value for dinner where the prices remain the same and this becomes a very cheap date with some drinks and fries/patatas...Either due to this change or the lack of as many NYUers during the summer, they were very slow when I visited during lunch.) Drop off your business card to enter a raffle of sorts.

I have died and gone to potato heaven. Literally as you walk in the door, the perfume of freshly baked/fried potatoes fill your senses. Potatopia is where potatoes meet Chipotle meets Yogurtland. Yeah sure you they have a few pre-made potato selections but whats the fun in that? Step one, choose your potato style. They have the usual french fries and tots but they also get pretty darn fancy with potato crinkles, potato skins and even smashed potatoes - 9 options in all. Now here is where the fun begins, the toppings! If you're anything like me, when I was given this option I freaked out just a bit. Thankfully we didn't have to commit to anything but the protein at that time (shrimp, lox, steak, chicken, sausage or bacon), it is worth mentioning that proteins come with an additional cost. I was right to be overwhelmed with the toppings and sauces. There were so many different options that allow for you to completely customize your potato experience and to my knowledge there wasn't necessarily a limit of toppings you could get. Each meal does come with one included sauce, more at an additional cost. The wait for our potatoes to be prepared was a bit longer than I would have liked, but the wait for freshly prepared potatoes was so worth it! Between the boyfriend, we decided to try one of their signature meals and to create our own. We had the Lower East Sider with the fries instead of the tots, it was topped with lox, scallions, sour cream and their house blend of salt. We also got tots mixed with steak and chipotle ketchup. Both selections were great, however both were bit too saucy for me. Unless you can scarf down your meal relatively quickly, heavy sauce will equate to soggy potatoes. Next time, Ill just get sauce on the side. Aside from the delicious eatings, Potatopia is fun for the potato aficionado. From their cute potato cartoons that pop up randomly throughout the store and on their containers and napkins to their cute potato musings on the wall. Who knew potatoes could be so much fun? Fun fact: Did you know that the average potato only has about 110 calories? Its all the deep friedness and additional add ons that give then a bad rep. Be mindful of your add ons and you will find that a healthy potato based meal is possible.

Another milestone, another NYC restaurant. The Â funny thing is, the last three milestones were all places I went to in a week (I splurged big time) yet, I waited hundreds of reviews apart to write about them. Actually work keeps getting in the way (dammit!) and the backlog is getting so large that places are closing left and right, before i get to review them. In fact I understand that Bouley's Danube has gone away and I've never got to try it! I also understand that since I've been here, Bouley has moved to a new locale. Better that than closing! For my last meal in NYC I had decided to come here for the fact that it was; within walking distance of where I was staying, Jean Georges had a killer deal but was too far for the time I had left, and of course the raves I'd read from my research. Walking down the street Bouley stood out with it's large wooden door and reddish facade. As you enter, the smell of apples surrounds you, and you realize that there are shelves upon shelves of them. Passing through the corridor you are greeted Â by a very polished man with a very distinct French accent. I think since they've moved, the dress code has been bumped up to jacket required but even before that change, we were well under dressed compared to the business power lunchers and special occasion celebraters around us. Would this affect how we were treated? Did we look like the dreaded tourists? I was a bit nervous at first but there were a few disparate examples of casual throughout. As we perused the menu it struck me that there was a tasting menu for lunch. Argh, only and hour and fifteen to spare. Could we do it? Our server said that she could get it done but advised that it wouldn't be the experience that we were meant to have because it would be rushed. Good advice I say. So we went with the a la carte approach. After perusing the menu, we ended up with: Amuse Bouche -Apple-Mint Sparking Soda Entrees -Maine Day Boat Lobster with fresh porcini mushrooms, black trumpet mushrooms, pencil asparagus, parsley root purÃ©e and burgundy wine sauce -Wild King Salmon with morels, crosnes, morel purÃ©e, fava beans grilled a la plancha, naval orange powder, and clementine glaze Cheese Course - Small taste of Roquefort BrÃ»lÃ©e with bartlett pears and burnt black mission fig jam Pre Dessert -Texas Pink Grapefruit Soup infused with green cardomon, star anise, and tahitian vanilla with campari sugar and fromage blanc sorbet (pre dessert) Dessert -Organic Passionfruit And Blueberry Meringue with passionfruit-caramel sauce, huckleberry coulis and provence lavender ice cream -Truffles, gelatins, maccaroons, caramels, and a few other small sweets. Wow. Let's get something straight here. We ordered the two entrees and the one dessert. Everything else was complimentary. Man do they aim to please. I thought we were getting the express lunch and it still turned out to be this amazing tremendous meal with every single item being fantastic. Remember the questions I asked earlier? Well the answers were resoundingly no. I've been known from time to time, to push the limit of "business/casual/elegant" based on my mood, but we were treated as well here as I've been treated anywhere, despite our comparably casual attire. The service was elegant, affable, and perfectly timed from start to finish. Whoever said the French were snooty never dined here. To top it off, the Maitre D' gave us a parting gift as we said our goodbyes. They've certainly shown what pampering a food lover it like and I shall return in anticipation of seeing the new locale. Michelin, give Bouley another star already!

My husband and I are visiting from Australia and came here for dinner on our first night in New York and it was soooo good!! It's a gorgeous little family run restaurant and the pasta is some of the best we've ever had. You have to try the spinach gnocchi and their daily specials. We loved it so much we came back the next night! It's also very cheap compared to many other restaurants in New York and the staff are friendly.
Food and service very mediocre, probably wont go there again.

Fantastic soba place. Service is quick but expect a wait around dinner time on a Friday night. If you come with only 2 people they tend to seat you sooner. I really enjoyed the Stamina Soba 2, which I really enjoyed but my fiancÃ©e had the Kimchi pork soba which was very delicious. The Stamina has a much lighter broth and went down really easily. Felt really good when I finished. The Kimchi Pork is a lot more richer. Â I'd recommend both. They both stayed warm to hot all the way till the end of the bowl. Looking forward to coming back and trying their dipping style next time. We all had the soup ones.

this is the best place ever. i wish you annoying 30-35 year olds would find a better way to waste your wednesdays. good burger. good gnocchi stuff. if you are like me and not rich then this place is nice for a date or bday with a couple friends, etc. or if you are an annoying want to be cool 30-35 year old then come here and drink on a wednesday.
I live this place!! I come here for the shrimp dumpling soup!!! Just order it. Trust me!

Was here last night, a very casual and intimate Saturday night dinner. And I really enjoyed it and satisfied. I have Quinoa, Octopus tapa, and Brochette Platter for 2 as our entree, which is a combination of Lamb, Stake and Chicken. We also had red wine with our dinner. Everything is amazing including service, I can't wait to come back try something else. In fact, I believe there are many good unique places it's worth to try in downtown area. Such as LES, Nolita, village area. Balzem is definitely one of them.

D: So went to Verlaine for the first time, and have to say, it lives up to its reputation. Â Verlaine is a nice place to grab a drink for a first date, after work or for pretty much any other reason. Â Many of the drinks are drinks with an Asian twist. Â I recommend the lychee martini. Â Was there during the happy hour which goes from 5pm-10pm. Â A longer happy hour for a cheaper price than most places in NY so definitely a good deal. Â Around 9, the DJ came on so it started getting a lot louder and hard to be heard. Â But nothing worth taking away from the 5* rating. Â Definitely a good place to pre-game or just to hang out with friends. C: Came here as my first date with D! Also was my first time at Verlaine after yelping for a place with great happy hrs. Ordered the yummy lychee martini, delicious and pretty strong! We came here on a Wednesday night.. not too crowded, great place for get together to grab a drink or 2. Came back a few weeks later with a couple of girlfriends on a Monday night, ordered the white sangria from the happy hr special. Highly recommended! I think I downed the whole drink in 2 mins. My friend ordered the Vietnamese Bloody Mary (also on the happy hr special) Â thinking oo exotic. That was pretty gross unfortunately. Nevertheless, def the place for the start of the night or just a mini weeknight get together.

This place is always so busy and I feel like a chicken without a head. However, the soup dumplings are to die for. We did order a few other meat dishes which left me feeling quite thirsty. Although the atmosphere makes me want to run out, the soup dumplings bring me to a state of bliss that everything just doesn't matter anymore.

Went to SoCo on a Saturday night with a party of 8 to celebrate my BF's birthday. Our reservation was for 8pm and they seated us right away. Ambiance: Soulful and southern, very inviting. Service: Excellent and very attentive. Food: Delicious! I tasted almost everyones food at my table. The BBQ chicken was divine and perfectly cooked (the sauce is spicy). The red velvet chicken & waffles umm YUMMMM Skirt Steak: very good but the potatoes were a little cold Macaroni and Cheese: Fantastic Lobster and Shrimp grits: never had grits before and i was pleasantly surprised, perfect texture and taste. I definitely recommend this restaurant and i will be returning.

Came for restaurant week but settled for the regular menu - no regrets. The food was spectacular. Decided to try pretty much all the yelp suggested tips. Scallops, Beef tar tar, tempura string beans, duck breast, organic chicken and steak. Dessert was good too.

Despite being familiar with Greenpoint Ave., mostly because of Brouwerij Lane, I was surprised I had a harder time finding this place. Heading west, walk past the big "BAR" sign and to two large barn style doors with "60." A cozy inside, it was not busy before 7:00 on a rainy Monday, but there clearly was a line and people waiting outside by 8:00. The Ricotta Be Kiddin' Me is a white pie with an incredible fresh ricotta along with sausage, "ham," and basil. The Delboy's spicy soppresatta has a good amount of heat behind, but worked perfectly with its fat and the pie's sauce. Service was great and the pizza flew onto our table within minutes. My new favorite Neapolitan (or of any style) pizza in New York.

Went on a Tuesday night so it wasn't too crazy in there. But despite that, the service was kind of slow. Â I had to repeat various orders to 2 different guys several times. Â  The food was okay. Â Got the grilled octopus which was swimming in a medley of tomatoes, onions, and celery. Â Tasty, but slightly salty. Also got the salsiccia pizza (some sort of meat and olives on it). It was alright. Again, salty, but that's probably because of the olives. I've definitely had better pizza. We tried ordering dessert but it was taking FOREVER for the tiramisu and panna cotta to arrive. I asked about the dessert for the 2nd time, and they said it was on the way. It wasn't really on the way, so we cancelled it. Â When we did that, the waiter seemed really peeved. Â Whatevs. It's a cute and cozy restaurant, and they gave my friend's kid some colored pencils and coloring sheets, so that was cool. Â  It's a nice addition to the neighborhood, but I don't feel a particular need to go back.
Delicious, healthy food, incredibly helpful and friendly staff, charming atmosphere, reasonable prices, what more could you want for a quick lunch or dinner?

Does what it says on the tin: pounds and pounds of hot, messy, juicy seafood to order with your choice of seasoning. We came in with a group of 9 at 7:30 PM Saturday night, and were seated shortly before 9 PM. The host will text you when your table is ready, so we wandered to the sports bar upstairs for some beer while we waited. We got it seasoned with everything, and it was delicious. Heavy on the garlic, so be ready to ward off vampires afterward. Crawfish, shrimp, and crab legs all delicious. Our waitress was kind enough to show us how to properly peel a crawfish - the staff were all really nice! The best part? Taking off your gloves and realising your fingers don't smell like food. Score.
Olea has awesome happy hour specials. Â My friend and I drank lots of cava, and ordered their patatas bravas, mushrooms, and meatballs. Â All were delicious and definitely recommendable.

I enjoyed Casa Mono for a cozy (very cozy) dinner with friends. We were walk-ins so we had to vacate by a certain time for the next folks, but managed to squeeze in a great meal. I had the razor clams recommended by our waiter and they were very yummy in texture and flavor. Also tried the patatas bravas which were okay. The choice of fingerlings was great but I wasn't big on the stuff that they were smothered in. My last dish was pork belly, which was a little dry and not fatty enough for full impact. I also tried my friend's tripe, which was yummy if you're into offal, and the baby octopus, which was just okay. For dessert we had bread pudding, which was warm and tasty but I didn't feel tempted to shovel it in my face with giddy delight. The place was very charming and had this trendiness to it, but it was soooo small and loud. We had a middle table and were frequently bumped by waiters as they attempted to squeeze between the tables. We were shouting at each other to be heard. I liked the clever under-table water glass storage to make room for dishes, and the service was very friendly and timely.

Dropped in for a post-workout welcome-in the weekend meal of pad thai last night. Noodies did not disappoint. Quiet enough, super intimate and at the same time, casual. We got in right before they closed. Server was attentive, and the pad thai was on point. The atmosphere is very warm and the plate wall's a good look. We didn't acknowledge that it brought us in at the time. But it did.
A few coworkers and I went for lunch one day. Service was just ok. The food was good. I highly recommend the yuca fries. You don't get a chance to get those everywhere and they are good here.

So disappointed! I love Terrorir, the sister restaurant to Hearth. Terroir has awesome wine and delicious small eats. I assumed the Hearth resturant would be equally awesome. Here is what I ordered and my rating, 5 being the best: Chartcuterie for 2 Â - 3/5 - it was good but nothing very unique about either Whole roasted fish of the day - 1.5/5 - nice presentatio but bland Charred sucrine salad - 4/5 - cooked greens, seasoned well Colorado Lamb - 4/5 - great texture and flavor Veal & Ricotta Meatballs - 3/5 - tasty but I had better meatballs Polenta Â 4/5 - creamy yumminess Mixed Greens - 3/5 - cooked spinach, nothing special Hen of the woods (grilled mushrooms) - 2/5 - I love mushrooms but the grilling/frying technique killed the flavor and texture of the mushroom Service - 2/5 - Service was so slow and the restaurant was not even busy. I waited a long time for my order to be taken and for the dishes to come out. My friends and I asked about the tasting menu. Waiter simply stated that its a 7 course meal chosen by the chef as stated on the menu. Clearly I get that but it would be nice if he tried to sell it to me or tell me what the courses are. At the end of the meal we ordered tea which took 15 minutes to bring out. Its just boiling water, how hard is it? My dinner party was 5 ppl. Intially we ordered the items listed above minus the lamb. But the waiter made a comment that "this is a good amount if you're not that hungry." So we added the lamb entree which was great. But in the end way too much food.

Happy Hour from 1-4AM?!? YES. My friend and I were walking around after stopping by a wine bar. So glad we did! I ordered the beef baked empanada & my friend ordered a breakfast empanada. We shared an order of yucca fries & guac and they were DELICIOUS! I don't know what's in that guac, but it was addicting! The servers are awesome, the music is on point, and even the diners next to us were friendly! We even shared our yucca fries with guys who had ordered plaintain chips for their table.

I've really enjoyed both of my experiences at Kinjo. The food is fresh and tasty and the service is prompt, polite and informed. It's a great combination and one of the better casual dining experiences in Ft. Greene. Great for friends/family or a date. Get there!

Ippudo is a huge chain in Japan, so it's amusing when people here think it's this new ramen shop that just so happened to open up in New York. Part of a larger restaurant group (with a lot of $$), the menu here appeals to the masses and is very well executed. The wait can be unbearable (45min/ 1.5 hrs ?? no thanks), and the service here feels sloppy at times (because it's a chain resto) so it creates a haphazard atmosphere. That said, it's a great introduction to ramen and the various styles / toppings. I'm partial so usually stick to shoyu or hakata ramen as that is my preference, topped with chashu pork and nitamago. You can't come here expecting Michellin star service and life changing ramen, but you will have a very enjoyable, tasty experience if you go during off hours where the wait is more tolerable. I wouldn't recommend it for a date (why waste an hour waiting for ramen?? - which isn't date food anyway), but for an early dinner after shopping or a casual dinner it's perfect.

A piping hot cider liberally spiked with spiced rum was just the thing to warm me up after a cold afternoon's walk. Upon walking in, I was enveloped by the warmth and cheer that Sweet Afton offers to its patrons. A late Sunday afternoon (helped by the fact that a football game was on and SA does not have a screen) meant that it was far more laid-back and less crowded than what you would find on a weekend night. Dim lighting and flickering candles set a cozy romantic mood or a very chill atmosphere for relaxing with friends. No wonder Sweet Afton is a very very very close second in terms of my favorite places to have a drink. The bartender handed me the hot cider in a glass cup that was wearing a little paper neckerchief. How cute! I enjoyed a basket of beer-battered deep fried pickles along with the cider. Thick little medallions of McClure pickles were dipped and fried in a light, airy, and crispy batter. Although deep fried, it was absolutely not at all oily or greasy. It left no residue on my fingers. Be careful when you take the first bite because it's soooo hot. A burst of hot pickle juice will explode in your mouth causing you to salivate even more with its tart taste. A hot juicy pickle surrounded by a crispy yet light beer batter made a delightful snack on such a cold day. Don't hate me because I live so close to Sweet Afton.

Beautiful food, beautiful wines, and excellent service. Â Really quite exceptional in every way, well except maybe for the tiny space, but in nice weather, you can sit outside which more than doubles Battersby's seating area. It's not cheap, so unless you have Benjamins burning a hole in your wallet, I would consider this a Brooklyn event restaurant a la the Grocery or Saul, but not quite Chef's Table or Blanca. Â That said you can choose between 5 ($75) or 7 ($95) courses. Â We had the 5 and that was certainly sufficient - and our waitress even said so which I appreciated. Â I also appreciate that this is not a rent-a-jacket kind of place, so you'll see a lot of people dressed pretty casually. You tell the waitress any food allergies, restrictions, or preferences - then watch each plate emerge from the tiny tiny kitchen (HOW DO THEY MAKE THIS DELICIOUS FOOD IN THAT KITCHEN!?! - it defies logic, there must be magical helper gnomes!). Â Each plate is expertly plated, presented and tasty. Â Match that up with some cocktails and wine, and Battersby ranks right up there with a lot of high-end places in "the city." The wait is unbearable so make sure you try for reservations if you can get them!

This cafe is without a doubt a hidden gem. The moment you walk through the door you are greeted with a friendly, genuine smile. Amazing coffee, tasty healthy food with vegetarian and vegan options. Oh and you cannot go past the home made cakes and slices. All in all a cafe worth checking out!
The best tacos, fries and drinks in ctown!! Â The service is great and the food is amaZing!

I have celiac this restaurant is not gluten free Â I ate there and was so sick the next day.i also ordered a glass of wine they have the nerve to charge 18.50 a glass . I would not recommend this restaurant for anyone that has celiac .

Absolutely fantastic Japanese restaurant, the atmosphere was definitely inviting, and the food is very good each and every time the only complaint might be perhaps if they wen't a little lighter on the salt, it wouldn't be so easy to fatigue of eating there (not saying the food was bad)
Fantastic food for a birthday dinner party of 10 people. Â Great for sharing!

This was the best Middle Eastern restaurant I've ever eaten at. Â The chicken shish kebab was heavenly. I highly recommend coming to this place when you visit Williamsburg. Â It self-serve and the atmosphere leaves Â something to be desired says my dining companion but I love it. Â It is extremely reasonably priced in fact I would say it's cheap.
Every time I come here I am so happy I did. Â Great Â food, good wine, friendly staff, warm, inviting space, and reasonable prices. Â Love it.

Let me preface my review by saying if this place were in Texas it wouldn't last a week. I would give maybe three stars. Now that thats out there, Fette Sau is fun, relaxing and delicious. I went on a Thursday night around 9 and it was packed. Not to worry, it took only a few minutes to grab a seat at the bar and begin sampling their handful of really well picked delicious beers on draft. They have a great whiskey collection too... we tried a Hudson that was stellar-- and apparently from New York's first distillery since prohibition. So, informative bartenders give this place an extra half star. We looked over the menu, which was limited as BBQ places usually are, and ordered brisket, pork shoulder, and ribs. The ribs were outstanding. The brisket was a bit dry. The thing that stuck out to me most about this place (as compared to the Texas joints) are their weird BBQ sauces. Let me tell you, a good BBQ sauce can make you forget that your brisket is dry. My dining amigo loved one (but he was from Seattle... what does he know?) but I found it WAY to vinegary. When mixed with the thicker, spicier one it was closer to the real thang, but still not enough to make me forgive and forget. Its always crowded, so don't go if you're looking for an intimate place to have a quiet conversation. You are probably going to have to share a giant picnic table with 15+ people. But hey, thats fun. I will go back to Fette Sau for two reasons. The previously mentioned bar and the delicious broccoli. Thats right, the broccoli. I've never had broccoli melt in my mouth like this. I've also never had broccoli at a BBQ place but thats neither here nor there. It was really garlic-y and had some sort of chili flakes going on. Its THE must-order item.
Great sandwiches and paninis at Clinton. Â The service is fast and friendly. Â  I keep going back for the very tasty coffee - better than most anywhere around this 'hood.

My roommate and I came here to celebrate his birthday, after a riotous & uproarious performance at BAM, following our combined consumption of about a liter of bourbon. An overflowing glass of Taittinger for each of us was a perfect beginning to our meal. The atmosphere in the bar is incredible, very lively but also discreet and celebratory. The dining-room environment is a little less inviting, in my opinion, because there are a few too many tables, plus a few too many members of waitstaff buzzing around. It's wonderful being somewhere people are enjoying themselves, but this is a little much... My most favorite part of the meal was the Crispy Pig Trotter, easily, possessing approximately one million layers of sumptuousness and amazingness: delectable & piquant & crunchy & creamy. My least favorite part of the meal was the Black Label Burger, which was just okay, because there was absolutely no sear on the meat, and it could have used a bit more salt -- however, the brioche and the fries were fantastic... The cocktails were consistently superb, although expensive, but very much worth it. Our waitress wasn't very welcoming, nor very patient. Although we both knew exactly what we wanted, having read dozens of reviews and seeing hundreds of pictures, we were very prepared, but she couldn't be bothered, seeming entirely disinterested. Really, her presence was bothersome, she acted so unpleasantly not just to us but to the tables around us as well. Nobody was being loud or obnoxious, she was just rude. We ordered the Black Label Burger, Oxtail and Foie Gras Terrine, Crispy Pig Trotter, and Roasted Bone Marrow. This should have been an absolutely foolproof meal, but the main obstruction was our waitress' stubbornness and lack of consideration. We asked that each course be delivered individually, because we wanted to take our time and enjoy ourselves, but she insisted on removing things before we were finished, and she demanded on bringing additional items before we were actually ready for them. Thankfully, however, the doorman was nice, the hostess and manager were friendly, the bartenders were very attentive, and the bus-boys were all very kind and generous.

its location will probably always ensure a nice-sized and -looking crowd, but it definitely won't be because of the food, which is simply not good. Â and then there's the fact that they're stingy with their bread and olive oil. Â i mean, seriously, what gives that you'll only dole out 3 tiny thinly cut slices (for 2 people) in a basket that clearly has room for more. Â it's not like i didn't see a huge bowl of pre-sliced bread at the kitchen doorway. Â better that you use smaller serving plates so as to create at least an image of bounty. Â as for the entrees, why do the owners think they can charge what they're charging for food that sucks? Â cannot think of one nice thing to say about the meal other than that it had both of us in a constant state of disbelief, as we realized that we were eating what others around us were eating but weirdly weren't bothered by.

I never thought I would love a sandwich more than Paseo's grilled pork sandwich. But Â Num Pang has certainly given Paseo some stiff competition, lucky for them it's way on the other side of the country. Lucky for me - I can enjoy both as I travel back and forth between the two coasts. Hubs and I stumbled upon Num Pang actually after a grueling day of filling out a 41 page application for an apartment in our new home city of New York (WTF???). We were tired, frustrated and frankly questioning our sanity for moving ... and then we had our sandwiches and life was good. We ate late/early - some weird time in the later afternoon so there was no line whatsoever and they were plum out of pork belly. I tried the Khmer sausage (highly recommend) Â while hubs had the duroc pork - both delicious. The bread is perfectly chewy, crisp, soft...the refrigerator pickles just enough sour/tart. The only thing really missing are some sliced jalapenos. Definitely an updated take on the Vietnamese banh mi...and smaller than your traditional banh mi at a higher price, but oh so tasty.

It was 6 o'clock and time to get my happy on. It had been two weeks since I'd seen my ladies and we needed to get our talk on without breaking the bank. Maialino did the trick with it's casual rustic atmosphere and awesome happy hour drink and food specials. We basically ordered the whole HH menu. I got a Roman Shandy for $5. It's a refreshing summer girly girl drink. It should probably come with a little umbrella. It's a blonde beer with Orchard Apricot, amaretto, lemon, and nepitella. We ordered 3 pizza rustica square at $2. They're made with potato and thyme, with lemon, grana padano, and pecorino. I probably could've had a ton more. Also got $3 pork cracklings with vinegar. PASS. People rave about these but..meh. Not much taste to these little dudes. Next? $7 risotto croquettes. These were so good. They come piping hot with a deliciously breaded outside and oozing mozzarella inside. Kind of like a high brow mozzarella stick with risotto. Lastly, $7 spicy shrimp crostini. Meh. Pass. Total bill with tip: $63. For me: $21. Can't complain.

really good. i had half plain half spicy sausage. nothing special about the sausage. i had the plain because i just wanted to taste their pizza without the bells n whistles. personally i prefer the tourist trap grimaldis on a tuesday evening or something when there are not many tourists around. i have yet to try di faras. i would go again this time id order extra cheese (lombardis is light on the mozz) the homemade meatballs and maybe some veggies. keep in mind each topping is 3 bucks extra.

Random Saturday night and hadn't planned out what we wanted to do for dinner so I wandered up Hudson and remembered how great my brunch was here. We were basically immediately seated at a communal table. Nice people next to us so it didn't bother me. We shared a mozzarella & tomato salad, gnocchi, hummus and tabouli. YUM. Yum to all. Everything was delicious and it was the perfect amount of food for two people had overeaten that day. The gnocchi was incredible fluffy compared to so many places that make it so dense. Servers were extremely nice and helpful. They actually read our minds when we needed things - always love that. My only complaint is that the table we were sitting at was the closest to the door so the second people walked in and were waiting to be seated or find out how long the wait was, we were dealing with the draft coming in. Not sure what could be done with that but it was freezing.

The mac n cheese really isn't that great. I ordered the buffalo chicken blue cheese and it was actually bland for me. I didn't taste the blue cheese or buffalo flavor. Other than that, the service is not the greatest like most other reviews say. I'd say find a more customer friendly place and avoid the hype. Oh and their $10 minimum per person policy--it says we KINDLY request our overnight guests to RESPECT our $10 minimum. NOT THAT YOU ABSOLUTELY HAVE TO KEEP ORDERING (like our server commanded us to do)..maybe you should change the wording if you absolutely want to enforce this--oh and if service wasn't so incredibly poor and slow, maybe people would not be so hesitant to order more. =)

Come autumn, all I want to do is drink beer in the West Village. It has that glamorous, bohemian, "New York" feeling, that i'm-wasted-in-a-cozy-sweater feeling. That I-could-be-a-great-writer-if-i-really-tried feeling. So after two weeks of eating healthy and avoiding alcohol, I decided to cash in big time at Corner Bistro with my favorite dining partners: me, myself, and I. The crowd at 3pm on a weekday is old and haggard, with a smattering of GQ types and a few foodie tourists. I sat down at one of the ancient wooden tables, carved with various symbols and the names of previous customers, and promptly ordered a Cheeseburger ($6) and French Fries ($2.75).
