I read about a page of my book in peace, wondering whether I should've gone for the gold (McSorley's for $2.75) when my order magically appeared in front of me. The burger was huge eight-ouncer, with a familiar, juicy, homemade taste.The onions snapped off like broken rubber bands after the first bite, but they were raw, so no big loss there. On the other hand, the fries were pretty terrible and McDonald's-esque, with an aftertaste that sent me scrambling for the nearest dessert. But that burger and the calm, dark, autumnal atmosphere gave me such a great feeling that I really couldn't care less about the bummer frites. Next time I'll go for a burger, a beer, and the company of a few Hemingway types. We'll discuss the pros and cons of being married to the sea, trade wooly cardigans, and all will be right with the world.

came here last night with a friend, and it was packed! luckily we had a reservation. the place is very dark and trendy...i think a lot of people there were getting dinner and drinks after work. i got the classic burger, which came with fries and 2 large onion rings. the burger wasn't anything special...it was quite small. but the meat was cooked well. the fries were mediocre, but the onion rings were really good and super crunchy! it was overpriced though, $15 before tax and tip. oh well...typical american bistro.

I've been to Nyonya for as long as I know. They are always very friendly with their wait staff all wear the traditional sarong as aprons. The decor is very family oriented and the setting is appropriate for large groups. Food can be ordered individually or family style. I would highly recommend this restaurant to my friends and even my Malaysian friends would agree that their food are absolutely authentic.
Aside from the 1-2 hour wait time, I have no complaints!

Excellent price for delicious sandwiches, everything is so fresh! Â My first time here was last thursday and i had the french goat cheese sandwich, the sweet of the figs was just perfect. I will be a regular here for sure, thank god is just a block from my work.
Food was yummy (but a bit too salty for my liking). Great little find. Decent prices. The cafe itself is nice and small. Will definitely drop by for lunch again.

This place is decadent and offers a very unique dining experience. It's not someplace I'd be able to go on a regular basis, but definitely worth it for special occasions. Go with a group of friends and try as many dishes as possible because everything is fresh and delicious.

Love this Japanese take on a "chipotle"-like experience. Our group of 6 dropped by on a Sunday for lunch and sat at the raised communal counter (as the rest of the tables only accommodate parties of 2-4.). Hubby and I shared a few items. The best item by far was the tempura sweet potato fries. A generous portion of the crispy, salty, and sweet fries are the reason this is a 4 star review. I also appreciated the different sauces they have here. The teriyaki ketchup, wasabi mayo, and spicy mayo were all really good and fun to try. Â We also ate the spicy tuna burger which I would NOT recommend as it was kind of bland (had to be rescued by the sauces). Lastly, we had the broiled salmon volcano roll (spicy salmon, onion, avocado, tempura flakes, sweet & spicy sauce, scallions, togarashi pepper, sesame seed) which was delicious! Great option for a $10 meal!
I loved this pizza , it was really tasty!i went for dinner a few weeks ago and enjoyed the charming decor of the restaurant Â as well as the food.

We stumbled upon this place while we were walking. Â The menu is fairly simple, but everything was fresh and delicious. Â They have a house made veggie burger, and you have the option of throwing an egg on it. Score! But the best part was the Bloody Mary, possibly the best one I've ever had. It's spicy so you may only be able to have one, but oh so worth it.

Does anything smell better then the scent of cooking butter? I think not, so when you get even 20 feet of this place, you're salivating at the wonderful buttery smell of FAT. It's very exciting. This place is pretty much in the middle of nowhere and we couldn't see the sign. We all arrived here and we were allso confused. Us- Is this it? Where are we? Is that a magic tunnel? What is the meaning of life? Anyhow, its BYOB (AWESOME!) and the food was great! Mussels, escargot, steak, fish, duck! All super heavy and buttery, and all sooo good! Eat here, it's good.

This is a 3.5 star review. I went in late October and had a good time here. You first walk into the restaurant in a room filled with narrow little shelves with apples on them. Then you walk into the main dining room which is like your grandmother's auberge. It's quaint. I did the tasting menu and it was good. There were several dishes I liked such as the lamb medallions which was probably the best lamb I've ever had and the porcini crab dashi was very tasty. Some not so much like the port wine sauce that overpowered the filet, or the skate/langoustine dish that just tasted like pan-fried food. The wine was good, the sommelier was very friendly but I was disappointed that they weren't many robust wine options to be had or at least by the glass. I really liked the bread trolley which was dangerous. Could you imagine if your job was to push a cart full of about a dozen tasty breads? My favorite was the cranberry bread. There were also a few amuse bouches along the way. There were some dishes that were absolutely amazing and then there were some that were just eh. For $175 for the tasting I was hoping for a bit more, but I would be willing to come back. The lamb on it's own was enough of a selling point for me to just order off the regular menu. My service was good and everyone I interacted with there on the staff was very friendly. The bathrooms downstairs are interesting, or at least the ladies' room is it's kinda of a like a red victorian boudoir set up. The restaurant is really close to the train too.

This place was really great, I came here with two Serbian people in the group and they assured me the food was spot on authentic (I truly believed them considering how few tables around us were speaking English!) The smoked meat platter and cheese platter were a fantastic start, that "appetizer" spinach pie ended up being my whole entree, so good and so huge! My friends ordered pork shoulder, chicken kebabs, and "Karadjordjeva" which was a thick pork & cheese schnitzel thing... all of it was fantastic! Will definitely go again!

I went for my surprise bday dinner and we enjoyed it. Food was on point, everyone in the restaurant also seems to be having good time. Our server was nice since she gave my bf an extra shot since I checked in through yelp and had my own free shot.

I love the food here. Â Its elevated comfort food - between the TO DIE FOR bone marrow dish with escargot - which is very hearty to the skate dish I had (I try and order Skate as not many places do offer it on their menu) to the amazing portion of lamb dish I had. I keep going back thinking about the first dining experience. Â Absolute must - great for any occasion: date night, dinner with a friend, or just because!
We just finished dinner here. Fabulous, authentic Italian pizza. Lovely service. Warm, cozy atmosphere. So happy to finally have great pizza in the neighborhood!!!

Wow is a great word to sum this restaurant up. Service amazing, food out of this world, ambiance nice, decor very pretty. We had reservations and were sat right away. The staff was very attentive and made sure we were answered and refilled without having to wait. As for what we ordered here it is: Pa amb oli: typical bread with tomatoes and olive oil on top. Delicious that we ordered it 3 times! It only comes with two good sized pieces and we were a group of 5 so order accordingly. Cana al Horno: This was my least favorite, but only because I didn't like the taste of the cheese. Everyone else in the table loved it and it was cooked perfectly. garbanzos fritos: OMG this was amazing. They were perfectly crispy which I had never experienced with this plate and addicting that we ordered this one 3 times as well. We raved so much about this that the waiter brought out the chef so we could give compliments. He was extremely nice and grateful we were having such a great experience. fideos canarios: I have never had rabbit before and let me tell you I was really surprised, tender good taste. The fideos were perfectly cooked. patatas bravas: the best I've ever had. smothered in their spicy sauce and perfectly crispy it is a must to be ordered. We had a few other typical things, like the manchego cheese and the jamon serrano which you can't go wrong with Dessert was also great having one that was chocolate and vanilla. Highly recommend this and will be back there the next time I'm in NYC. The only drawback is that on a Monday that we went the kitchen closes at 10pm which was kind of early.

The cheese plate, pasta, and wine are good but the restaurant's waiting bar area is very small and crowded spilling over to the guests enjoying their dinner. Â If you're lucky, you'll get a seat at the bar. Â The service was OK it wasn't bad but it wasn't great either. Â The food and restaurant didn't really stand out for me and the price was not as friendly as Otto. Â I would rather go to Otto than Lupa. Â Otto has this AMAZING cheese plates in addition to the black truffles honey, cherry, oranges and a huge selection of pasta and pizzas.

How do I rate simply prepared yet succulent and quality swine served to you on a prison tray in a cafeteria setting with beer available by the gallon at affordable prices? Â  I ripped the loudest belch on the walk back to the subway. Â Positive Review Complete.

This was a lovely restaurant. The views of the Hudson were great, the service was terrific and the food was delicious. We came for Father's Day brunch and were not disappointed. We had: Mushroom Asiago & truffle oil omelet Â - delicious and very light (I got it with egg whites). Braised Beef Short-Rib Hash - Delicious Burger - my daughter loved it Mac n Cheese - the girls were fighting over it Biscuits & Gravy - delicious but a little heavy on the sausage (I was the only one who thought so) Bacon Bloody Mary - Amazing! The waiter was lovely and gave us good recommendations. The bathrooms were clean. We would love to come back for dinner one night. All and all a great experience.

My husband and I ordered three dishes - pork sausage and rice cake/ quail / ham. All three of these were salty- you might want to be caustioned about this. We are Asian, and in general very tolerate on salty food, but these were more than we could appreciate. Momofuku's saying this is what they meant to be, then what should we say..I Â thought this still should be inforomed at least through yelp. One additional note- pork and rice cake tastes of MSG.. It gives attractive flavor at first, but eventually could make you feel " oh I'm done with this oily and greedy ingredient".. That's what we felt. Restaurant reveals very hip ambient, which was very nice, but food was not impressive at all. We read some article about chef's achievement and expected something special, but unfortunately that was not what we encountered last night..too bad.. :(

LOVED this place. And we were actually quite lucky, only a thirty minute wait haha. I probably wouldn't wait more than forty-five minutes, not THAT worth it. But they make the noodles themselves and you can definitely tell. We were stuck at a community table but it didn't really matter. It's just that anyone who has read my passed reviews know I can't stand community tables haha. But they do have plenty of personal tables though. Quite noisy, but fun. It was actually my first time eating real ramen, I always went for the udon bowls. And I was quite pleased :)

I would've given them a higher star but I really wish restaurants would stop serving sodas in bottles. I hate paying $2 for a small bottle of soda. Food-wise, they're superb! I'm usually a fan of benedicts but I've noticed their other breakfast options are much better than the egg benedicts.

NY pizza at its finest, at least in my humble Californian opinion. Â Some tourists look forward to the landmarks and sites... Â I was excited for the east coast food, especially the pizza. Small place in the theater district and very unassuming. Â Barely any room to sit and eat (small counter and a few stools), but the tight quarters and friendliness of the regulars that visited gave it a cozy and family feel. Â  Next time I'm in NYC I would go out of my way to stop by again for a slice... or two... or three.

Fried calamari was really good there is seating outdoors which I would've loved if it was summer time so I may need to visit again in warmer weather Food is really cheap and still tastes good Waiter was ok

I went here again this past Monday and paid $33 for drinks (for 3 people for a couple of hours no less) and a show. A fight between some of the most stereotypical douchebag hipsters broke out over a game of pool and it was pretty much the funniest fucking thing I have ever seen. A flurry of tight fitting flannel shirts and think black rimmed glasses. They might have well have been slapping each other with their Iphones. The staff handled it pretty well and one awesome bartender got the more aggressive hipster (this is not saying much) into a choke hold on the ground. The fucker kept on screaming "I CAN'T BREATH!!!" which was funny because he sure could scream like a pansy for someone with no breath. The best part about all of this was that there were two dudes sitting at a table near the fight that were playing chess. They didn't even flinch and proceeded to play the entire time. I love this place. I love pint sized Beam Creams. Fuck yeah.

Isabella's is just such a pleasant experience. Â It's my favorite (eclipsed, maybe, by Cafe Lux) for brunch, and late casual lunches...especially in the spring and summer when the doors are open and you could sit all afternoon (eye-oogling Shake Shack across the street). Â Love this place...across the board perfect; quintessential UWS.

This place has some serious lobster, I traveled across the country by car, checked out a lot if places across the way, this was the best. It's right near the bull on Wall Street. Their pickles are really good to! If you like lobster eat here, if you like seafood the crab roll was super good also. My girl and I are huge fans!
Take a break from your afternoon shopping and get some cappaccino and dessert. Duh. It is so good here xooxox

The laid back, chilled atmosphere is an oasis in this mad town, and we didn't have to compete with the loud talking that is so common in New York. Food was delicious - ordered the seafood stew and the special sausage dish. And had the coconut tapioca for dessert - again, delicious. Perfect spot in a great part of town for a Sunday evening.

Arranged to have a surprise birthday party here for the lady with 13 people. I booked a week in advance and increased the reservation a few times and they were perfectly accommodating. At the last minute, more people arrived but, again, ilili staff were great and accommodated everyone in the lounge - really appreciate their flexibility. Once there and settled everyone started off with a mix of dips - hummus, baba ganoush, Brussel Sprouts all around. Tasty! I wish the pita had been warmed. Also, drinks were a bit slow to roll out, but I think the server was spread thin so no fault there. For mains, I had the chicken kebabs, others had assorted mezzes. My dish was quite tasty, though I can't say it was outstanding. The star of the table was the gnocchi. It definitely gave me order envy. Overall, the food was solid, though perhaps a bit pricey for what it was. The service, although slow at times, was great and the servers friendly. Very nice experience
unremarkable food in a remarkable setting, i'd say. this space is truly delightful--even the slightly wobbly chairs and tables have a way of being charming.

After only being open one week, this is only going to get hotter. Â The attention to quality is evident in the only brunch menu. Â The fried chicken on the cheese-waffle is delicious and bountiful. Â The waffle french fries with dipping sauce just tasty as all out. Â The BLT with pickled green tomato is one thick piece of well cooked bacon and the grilled peach salad with fried pimento cheese, tossed with frisee and grape tomatoes is a very nice salad. Â Good ice tea. Â Can't wait till the full menu opens up. Â Did not mention this yet, but the whole staff is very nice and the chef Jeff McGinness is a welcome addition to NYC.
Great Japanese Curry Rice. They flavor their curry with roasted pork, and it's significantly better than the standard St. Marks Kare Risu. Lunch for under $10.

Really good Italian and serious value for money. Â Simple, fresh and delicious. Â The type of place that feels relaxed and casual - the perfect neighbourhood joint. I wish I could move it round the corner from my apartment. I had ravioli - Joe had gnocchi. Â I overdid the delicious fresh bread and olive oil, but it didn't stop me from ordering the tiramisu too. I'd definitely come back here - perfect place to end up after a walk/bike along the Hudson River.
extremely busy during dinner hours in weekend especially. decent dishes and prices. restaurant's interior design is great as well worth visiting.

I heard so many things about Ippudo before actually going this evening. It was great, but not sure if it was worth the wait. 1. I had the chicken buns, not the pork buns. Meh, good but not out of this world. Next time I will listen to other reviewers and go for the pork buns. 2. I had the modern ramen, which was recommended by the server as the staple ramen dish that Ippudo is known for. The pork was tender, sweet and savory, but that was about it. I wish it would have had a little more of a kick, and something else other than 2 pieces of meat and noodles. I expected more meat for a $17 bowl. I may go back if there is not a wait, but plan to also check out momofuku.
Delicious chicken and the sides are wonderful too. My go-to is sweet potato mash or creamed spinach. As good as it gets!

My dad and I went here on a Tuesday afternoon. Nice outdoor seating (and big indoor space), decent coffee, and good vegetarian options. I got a cheese/tomato/avocado/chipotle mayo sandwich and my dad got an omelette. I'll go back for dinner sometime!

Absolutely love this place. Seriously like Italy. The market is authentic along with the atmosphere! I've only purchased from the market and ate at the gelato/panini stands in the front. The gelato was good, nothing too memorable. The panini was out of this world. Will definitely return and choose one of the sit-down restaurants.

Food was all around very good, especially the pork soup dumplings. Â The pork fried rice was great and a big portion, too. Â Some of the dishes were a bit on the salty side but could be just me, since others in my group didn't seem to mind. The service was good, if a bit rushed, but prompt and response for the most part. Â  The decor is... nothing to write home about. Â Your typical (?) Chinese restaurant that's been in business for years and years and have not renovated in years and years. Â But all in all, clean "enough". Only true negative is that 15% service charge is automatically added on the bill, so when you are paying, be sure to check and not double-tip. Â And they only take cash.

One of the best deals for a great, tasty meal on the UES that I've found. Â As Turkish restaurants go, it is far and away my favorite in this part of the city. The swordfish kebabs were an amazing deal ! Â The Mezze Platter is a must try. Â Great outdoor seating in the warm months. Â A great place for locals, and worth the trip from another part of Manhattan (even for notoriously lazy Manhattanites!) .
good food and good price. hate that they don't take credit cards or have diet coke. but somehow that keeps getting overlooked.
It's was super fancy, but the taste was a bit bland. I don't think I'll be eagerly waiting to be back.

My friend took me to try this pure thai place couple weeks ago, I was surprise that how special this place is. Â Their papaya salad and coconut rice were amazing. Â The noodle soup was a little difference from other thai place out there. It might not match a lot of people taste. Â The soup was sweet, spicy and sour. Â If you are the 3s' type person, then you shouldn't miss this. Â My friend love their noodle soup, but I'm not a big fan of it.

can we say meatball pizza!?!?!?!!!!! who would have thought meatballs on pizza would be good. def not me. but when i bite into it, wow. sooo good. the lines are long and they won't seat ya til the whole party is present. but it is worth the wait. they also deliver, and its still good. not soggy and the thin crust is still crisp. sitting in the back room with the oven is great! watching the pizza's come out is like being part of the action. service is ok.

This was about the 5th pizza joint I visited during my trip to New York. This was also what I felt to be the most authentic New York pizza I had ever tasted. I ordered a single slice of the margarita pizza as I was saving room for every pizza place I passed. I sat down with my single slice and for the first time in my life I tasted fresh mozzarella. It was warm and gooey, and super stretchy! The sauce tasted fresh and fresh basil leaves top the pizza as well. Â The crust was thin and crisp and added just enough to the flavor without overpowering the freshest toppings I have ever tasted. Well, I gave up and saving room for another pizza place, stood up, walked over to the counter, and ordered a second slice before leaving Prince Street Pizza. It was just as delicious as the first. Environment: This was one of the cleanest pizza places I visited on my trip. The walls are lined with Italian celebrities that have stopped by to enjoy this authentic pizza. Apparently this place is a favorite of the former Soprano's cast. Verdict: A must eat!

loved the atmosphere, was psyched to sit outside but there was construction across the street that was driving me insane so we moved inside. Really great service, we had the duck, lamb and pork - all of it was really great! I think our favorite was the Pork Chop. The german Torte for dessert is a must!!!!!!! great texture and flavor.

Absolutely loved it. Â I'm not a vegan but I'm avoiding animal protein for health reasons. This is the best vegan food in the city. Â The bread is gluten free. Â Even if you ignore the vegan bit, this is really, really good food. Â Unlike a lot of vegan places they don't try to give you a bunch of soy protein based fake meats and other artificial stuff that's loaded with salt and chemicals. Â They cook veggies well enough that you don't care you aren't eating meat. Â Their cashew cheese actually tastes better than many dairy cheeses. Â Their MOB's flatbread/pizza like things are excellent. Â Some of their dinner entrees aren't available for lunch and are very good so go for dinner. Â Very healthy and delicious. There are long communal tables and there usually isn't a wait. Â Service is good. Â The place is pretty chilled out and is great to go with a toddler. Â I would definitely go there even if I was pretty carnivorous.
Pretty cozy spot, menu reflects most Shabu Shabu I've been to. It's a nice quiet place if you just want to sit back and talk over some good hot pot.
I had eggs benedict, which was yummy. I want to come back here to try the pumpkin pancakes. Plus, weathers warmer now so I'd love to sit outside on a Sunday for brunch.
Awesome food. You can also eat there during the day for lunch as well.

Eataly is a fantastic place, no doubt! Â Sure, it can get very crowded... Â However, it's a fun place to get a glass of wine, and sample some excellent cheese and salami. Â In addition, fantastic meals are to be had in one of the various dining spots, and you can even go shopping for some gourmet pantry essentials imported from Italy. Â Premium fresh seafood, meat, and dairy products are also available. Eataly is a destination... A unique experience that is certain to impress!
your service , and your food terrible, you must to development Â before late, thank you

Food coma indeed! Â I thought the eggs benedict was really good, too, with Â its perfect hollandaise sauce. Â Only thing I wasn't loving was the biscuit with the benedict. Â By itself, the biscuits are amazing, but when paired with the eggs benedict, it just felt a little too heavy to me. Â The bacon was perfectly crisp and delicious as well. I am from California we have family run pizza place here that I have eaton my whole life. That is until I had the pizza at Lombardi's Â I went on vacation there and decided to try out Lombardi's. Now I have been spoiled for pizza anywhere else. That was the best pizza I ever had in my life, I am 58 so that is a few pizzas Eileen A Lakewood, CA
I am appleciated this place in nyc that we can eat decent japanese grilled fish in nice atmosphere. 3.5stars

It's a Christmas Miracle! A real taqueria in New York City. I didn't think I'd ever see the day after moving here 3 1/2 years ago from San Francisco but today I finally had a real burrito in the city. If you're looking for a West Coast style burrito this is the spot and it's the real deal. It wouldn't be the best place in SF but for NY I give it 5 stars. Anyone who can't tell the difference between this and Chipotle or thinks Chipotle is better has either never been to California for a burrito or doesn't know what a real burrito is supposed to taste like. Hint: they don't have Jasmine rice in them nor do veggie burritos have carrots, bell peppers, or other veggies. Chipotle is Mexican fast food (owned by Mickey D's) and not very good Mexican fast food at that. This place is a real taqueria with fresh ingredients and no frills style. The only thing missing is horchata! And for those SFers out there, the review below that said the burritos taste like Gordo's is right on. If you want a real burrito, this is the only place to go in NYC.

Cafeteria, you blew my mind! I wasn't expecting much, just a reasonably delicious brunch with a reasonably delicious cocktail. Thanks for exceeding my expectations with the most flavorful, authentic southern food I've had outside of Louisiana in a long time. When I sat down, I had to order the bloody Mary. Small, but it ended up being just the right size with just the right spices and garnishes. For breakfast, I was trying to decide between the Green Eggs and Ham or the Chicken and Waffles. I went with the Chicken and Waffles after the waiter suggested they were the better of the two and I'm glad I did! The chicken was a little dry, but when syrup and and buffalo type sauce was added on top, it ended up complimenting the fluffy and flavorful corn waffle really well. My dining companion got the lemon ricotta pancakes with bacon and grits and enjoyed every bite as well. We were both surprised to see grits on the menu outside of the south, but they ended up being delicious as well. For a small, trendy restaurant, Cafeteria still has a great neighorhoody feel. I can imagine its quite busy on the weekends/after the bars close as its a 24 hour place, but in my opinion, totally worth the wait! I definitely want to go back for cocktails and appetizers, as they had a very extensive drink menu and a very inviting bar area.

I come here often and I always get the same thing. I order the Billie Holiday drink, which Chivon makes perfectly and the Fried CHICKEN. How can you come here and not order at least one piece of fried chicken?! Yes, yes I know they make other things here like grits but the chicken is a must have. It's seasoned to perfection and crispy. I have tried fried chicken from many places but Peaches makes the best.

Another C Town institution (Food gets a 3.75 stars). Â  There are few places in the city where you'll find skater punks, hipsters, yuppies, tourists and ladies in full on fur coats on the same line. Â  The dumplings (4 for a dollar) here are just the start of it. Â There noodles and soups are solid options but the thing that keeps me coming back is the Sesame Pancake Roast Pork sandwich. Â The pancake they use as bread is crisp on the outside and fluffy on the inside, the meat is salty and fatty and all the flavors from the shredded veggies in between are better than any other sandwich you can get for even double the $2.25 price tag. Â  This spot is a straight value play and would get a a higher rating however the service, cleanliness and crowding definitely takes a certain frame of mind to enjoy. Â So expect good food on the cheap, understand what your getting into and you will not be disappointed.

LOVE this place. Excellent food, always piping hot and plentifiul, excellent service, cold beer always, and cheap. If you haven't been, GO. Â Prepare to wait about 20 minutes some evenings, but it's worth it.

I am not a fan of formula restaurants. With that finding a good choice of restaurant in the theater district is difficult. Why is that? Isn't Manhattan meant to the greatest place on earth? If so, why you have so many areas that are difficult to find a great choice? Penn station area? Theater district, hell's kitchen, there are many forgotten corners of the island. Why? In any case, Becco has a strict twin door policy. The vestibule between the two doors is the coat check too. If you mistakenly, or foolishly try to open the second door when the first one is still open, your hand will physically be stopped by a hostess, who rather sounds like a NYPD employee that a restaurant hostess. "DON'T"T OPEN THE DOOR!' - "are you for real? did you actually just speak to me like that?' So once we are in, the place is full, full. We are taken to the second or third floor, endless dining rooms later we get seated. There is no pasta menu, rather a three choice of pasta, all you can eat. I felt like pasta so we ordered. My wife chooses the steak. Pasta: waiters walking around with huge pasta serving dishes, swimming in sauce. All ok, nothing wrong with them. Call them american pasta, or pasta soup, if you are into that kind of thing then you'd call it great to amazing. Steak: large slab of meat like an island on a white plate. Did taste good. Cannoli - very good. Wine. Ample $25 selection. That is fair. We chose a $70 and it did taste great, but got lost in the formula menu which gave the overriding feeling of seating in a canteen, not conducive to fine wines. Probably better than most other italian in the area. But be warned.

I can normally get a pretty good feel for how good a Chinese restaurant is going to be by the percentage of non-Chinese people I see eating there. There's usually an inverse correlation between the number of white people I see and the quality of the food I'm going to get (although the price will generally go up ... see PF Chang's). I'm not blaming them, but it's just the way it works LOL. Shanghai Asian Manor throws a nice curveball into that formula. To be honest, this place is actually packed with people of every ethnicity, it's clean enough that I don't worry I'll be spending the evening on the porcelain goddess, the prices are pretty reasonable, and it serves some really tasty Shanghainese food. If you're a fan of soup dumplings, this is probably my second favorite place for them in Chinatown, right behind the neon wonder that is Shanghai Cafe Deluxe. The reason I come here more frequently though is that most everything else they serve is pretty good as well. I'd definitely also recommend the Shanghai-style rice cakes as well as the sautÃ©ed snow pea tips. The pork fried buns (sheng jian bao) are probably the only semi-disappointing thing I've had here, as they tend to be too dry, especially when ordered for takeout. The other plus of this place is that the service is much better than places like Joe's, where you're basically herded like cattle and forced to speed eat. Also, pretty much everything but the soup dumplings sucks at Joe's, but I digress.

Went there for lunch on a saturday. Fast casual joint with really nice reclaim wood tables. Tasted the brisquet, the half chicken and the wings. The bbq sauce is delicious. The wings were way too spicy. Missed out on the sides somehow...
Recently trekked over for a quick lunch. Â We had the fabulous/affordable veggie dumplings, chicken soup, and a sesame pancake. Â Best lunch for 2 under $10.

Lots of hype around this place. After a few months of wanting to go and reading all the positive yelp reviews, decided to try it. First off the place is packed with tourists. Didn't see one local there. Ambiance was nothing special. The fried chicken was excellent but very small portions. My brother got the chicken wings which had a lot more meat. The Mac and cheese and Cole slaw were the best sides. All told, it was a nice place but I wouldn't wait more than 10 minutes in line for the food. They can't help all of the tourists there, but the ambiance is more New York guide books on every table as opposed to a Harlem staple.

I'm a man who likes portions in abundance. Â Preferably the food will be of a high quality and ideally it will be Italian. Â Becco's prix fixe never ending pasta deal therefore represents a robust and affordable blend for volume eaters like myself. Â Deals like this get me fired up so I went there with my mom and we both agreed that it was an excellent decision. Â The atmosphere is busy, the food rich, and the portions proportionate to your determination and natural eating ability.

Came here for dinner with my friends on a Saturday night, we waited for about 30mins for a table. I had the Chilean Sea Bass which was the special of the night and it was so juicy and tender. Go try it out!

Place is pretty good.. One thing I found was the meat was a little dried out.. Dried out and not at the correct temp. Then, i looked at the process behind the preparation.. It's smoked well and everything but, meat goes from the smoker into the walk in fridge? Â Meat that has been previously smoked and plastic wrapped is Â taken out and heated up at 300 degrees.. So, you spend 18 hours cooking the meat at 120 or 130 degrees but, right before you serve it, you crank it up to 300 degrees? Â  They provided NC Vinegar Sauce for the pulled pork.. They have a K.C Masterpiece style BBQ sauce, they have this super Cumin sauce where all I can taste is cumin.. Felt like it was going for a Arthur Bryant type of sauce.. Not a good version.. Maybe they chose this sauce for brisket. They have a hot sauce that seems to be a mash of peppers.. Â I liked the K.C Masterpiece sauce the best.. I only tried the German Potato Salad.. Which was not German Potato salad but, a pickely version.. Lots of dill and mint.. A potato salad yes but, a German one, no.. Staff was nice and this place must rock in the summer.. Good selection of whiskey.. A young hip Brooklyn BBQ place.. They sell beer by the gallon and food by the pound.. It's all pretty good.

Definitely a fan of this place. Really cool out spot to chill and ppl watch during the warmer months. Drinks are good and the food isn't bad at all. I had the grill chkn--hmmm yea its been a while lol. Can't miss w/ this place. It does get crowded and hard to find seating sometime but hey u can always take ur drink to go and head to the park right up the block. Oh--they sometime show movies as well.

Been hearing about this place for months so finally decided to check it out. Really glad I did. Will def be returning (just not in large groups its a very very small dining room)!

Went last night and the food was actually very good and the atmosphere was very nice. Why I give it only one star: If you have a good allergy/intolerance, be careful before ordering. A Jean George Restaurant in New York. Â We came during restaurant week. Â The decor is miinimalist, contemporary. Â We came on Labor Day dinner after the US Tennis Open. Â Not too many people here. One word: FOOD POISONING. I usually don't leave reviews unless my experience is completely positive or complete disaster. I got to New York this morning, had Poached egg and rosewater waffle, shortly after party in the bathroom all day. UGH. Please make sure your food is alright. I'd heard that Frankie's 457 was great but my experience was anything but. Â Cold and discontented staff welcomed us, reminded me of my trip to Germany. I love love Â love Num Pang. My fav is the pork belly but I also have much love for the steak sandwich as well as the shrimp. This place is the bom diggity if you didn't know now you know !!!!!

Great evening ambience. Try to get into this place early evening for a not to crowded dining experience, especially those brave enough to dine alone. Trust me this place is worth it! I'm giving Bonnie's five stars because I didn't have one complaint. I ordered the burger, my boyfriend ordered the wings and they were both awesome. Everything tasted very clean but still the way a burger and wings should. Service was quick!

the food is great but i have to minus one star for one disappointment Â  which is when you order that great burger out, they don't cook the bottom half of the bun a little so it doesn't fall apart by the time it gets to your door. Â i'm very close by too and yet it gets soggy. Â  its a heavy one so the roll on the bottom should be crispy or toasted well to hold it together. The food is good, the service is very casual and the decor is not great . It Â is very loud sometime and the chairs outside are very cheap and uncomfortable .

Like the Italian saying "Fare la scarpetta" I definitely mopped up my plates...there was not a morsel to be found..duck foie gras ravioli..mopped!...vension entree...mopped!...panna cotta dessert...mopped!
