Scarpetta has a modern feel with mood setting acoustics. I could hear some background music but it wasn't overpowering. The music in the bar area was louder but that noise never made it into the dining room. A nice touch that is sometimes overlooked. The service was helpful but not intrusive.. They kind of melted into the background just like the music. Overall we loved the place and will definitely be back to mop up some more plates.
I love the twin sandwiches they sell after the dinner menu isn't served anymore. They are juicy and delicious and who doesn't love twins!

This is a really nice spot that has an old school feel. The bar is really nice and I've go just for a drink. On to the food though... The bone marrow here is plentiful and amazing. The $26 burger was really good, but I've had a better burger and it was about half the price (Father's Office fyi). The risotto special we had was really good as well. We ate at the bar and the bartenders there were very knowledgeable and helpful with the menu. They actually recommended not getting the burger and going with a steak. Specifically we were recommended to split the Dry Aged Cote (which comes with bone marrow). Next time I'll go that route.

UNBEATABLE tacos. Â Take their recommendations seriously, some items on the menu (fish & steak tacos, guac) is way stronger than others. Didn't love brunch. Â Both La Esquina and Barrio win there Appreciate the fresh-squeezed lime juice in the margs. Staff rocks. Â Owner's great and almost always around.

Just ate here on Friday and was pleasantly surprised. Great Belgian beers, nice mussels, amazing salads and desserts. Super friendly service and kids got to eat free (that night at least). Will go back!

I took my girlfriend here last week. Â I was a little lazy making the reservation (didn't do it until the morning of, on a Friday), so the only times available were 4:30 and 11:00. Â So on the weekends, reservations are a must, preferably a day or two in advance. We had some time to kill, so we grabbed drinks at The Room on Sullivan, just South of Houston (basically 1 block away). Â 11:00 may be a late dinner, but it was worth the wait. Â The restaurant has a dim, romantic atmosphere and the service was unbelievable. Â We ordered a bottle of Lambrusco (sparkling red, highly recommend) and the sommelier came over to highlight the finer points of the particular bottle we chose. Then the culinary adventure began... We started off with two appetizers: speck and broccoli rabe with ricotta. Â Both were delicious - especially together. Â For entrees, I went for the gnocchi and my girlfriend chose one of the specials, a whole fish. Â Although the gnocchi was delicious, the portion was rather small. Â The fish on the other hand was a generous portion, too much for her to finish in fact - lucky me :-) Â They filleted the fish right in front of us, which was a nice novelty. After we finished the entrees we had finally reached the real reason we chose Lupa in the first place, the tartufo! Â This decadent dessert alone justifies the trip. Â The shell is a soft, chocolate-hazelnut and inside you'll find an explosion of fruit and vanilla ice cream that just overwhelms the senses. If you're having trouble getting a reservation at a reasonable time, I'd recommend eating close by and skipping dessert. Â Late night (around 12 or so on the weekend), the restaurant really clears out and you can just walk in to try the tartufo. Â The portion is large and very share-friendly. Â If you're looking for good Italian food in Manhattan, Lupa is definitely worth checking out.

I am probably Salt & Fat's worst enemy: I don't eat red meat or fish, I'm severely lactose intolerant, I hate cheese, and I eat lean/"right" whenever possible (i.e. sober). Â In turn, that should make Salt & Fat my worst enemy, but I went out on a limb for an evening to meet up with some other Yelpers. Given my limited options, I only had: Persimmon Salad (minus cheese and meat): I loved, loved, loved this salad. Â I gotta tell ya, I'm a sucker for candied walnuts. Â The salad was well put together and extremely cold and refreshing. Â The rest of the table enjoyed picking the meat off my plate. Fried Chicken: Big portion (four thick pieces) and extremely, extremely filling. Â It was good -- a tad bit spicy -- but it wasn't out of this world. Â I ate chicken fingers every dining outing of my life for approximately 15 years, so I've had fried chicken anywhere imaginable. Â I am like a chicken finger connoisseur. I did try the desserts, though I didn't want to overdue it since dairy and I don't get along well (despite that fact that I love ice cream to death). Â I tried a selection of sorbets: apple miso, thai iced tea, and white peach jalapeno. Â It's almost disturbing how much they each tasted like their flavors. Â They were all very fresh and appetizing, though I'm not sure how much I could've eaten. Â The sorbet that came with the rice krispie treat was my favorite. Â I can't remember the flavor, but it was sweet. Overall, I did enjoy the food and the service was good/attentive. Â We shared a bottle of red wine, which was tasty. Â For someone as picky as myself, I do look for a large variety of items, specifically veggies (they were out of the Brussels sprouts) as well as the option to tailor menu items, but that was a little tricky here given the specificity of each item. Â I guess I'm just too simple (or am I too complicated?) for Salt & Fat.

My father was one of their first customers (1939). I moved out of Bensonhurst Brooklyn in 1971 to Woodside Queens and still managed to go to L&B at least twice per month. My wife and our kids moved to New jersey in 1983 and went to L&B at least once per month. We now live in Winter Garden Florida and fly up to L&B 6 times per year. It is without a doubt the best in the world!!!

I went in the day time around 2pm and it was not crowded at all! The food was delicious. I order barbecue chicken, macaroni and cheese and candied yams. Definitely one of the best soul food spots around.

came here on a monday night with my boyfriend for some wine/cheese/dessert and was not disappointed! large wine list that was affordable. we ordered beef carpaccio, with lemons and capers and parmesan cheese...so good! also 3 course cheese plate, the foccaccia bread it came with was unbelievable...made in house. my boyfriend gobbled it up and we waited about 10 minutes for another fresh batch (complimentary...we weren't charged!). also got bruschetta which was very fresh, one order was definitely big enough to split. the waiter was very attentive. we sat in the outdoor area, very romantic and intimate, candlelit. for new york I thought the prices were reasonable- 3 glasses of wine, bruschetta, 3 course cheese plate (TONS of cheese), carpaccio, and warm apple pie came out to $70 with tip. the food was more than enough for two, I don't even think we could finish the cheese! will definitely come back for another romantic night!

Been here several times - for girls night out, dates, etc and the meal is always spectacular. I highly recommend the skirt steak with accompanying chimichurri (ask for a double..you'll need it). The white sangria is also yummy!

I took my husband to the Little owl for his birthday dinner. We got to the restaurant about 10 minutes before our reservation so they placed us in the "Perch" which is just their little area built over an old set of stairs where 2 people can drink wine and wait till their table is ready. We unfortunately had to wait over 20 minutes but we happily drank our wine while enjoying the cozy ambiance. For appetizers we tried the lobster ravioli, which was great, so light and savory could have had it as a dish! For main meals I got the pork chop- which was great! it was perfecty cooked and I got brussel sprout fries instead of the normal accompaniement. My husbands fish was ok, a little bland for his taste but he said hands down my pork chop rivaled babbo's. For dessert we had the raspberry beignets which were yummy with the nutella. theyre a great option if you're not a huge chocolate person like me. Overall was a great experience in a great area, now only if you didnt have to wait 30 days for reservations!

What with all the hype and the 45-minute wait (despite arriving before they opened on Sunday morning), I feared I would be disappointed. Fear not - the blueberry pancakes are light, fluffy, packed with blueberries, and even more delicious dipped in that warm maple butter. Not sure what I was expecting with the sugar cured bacon, but it turned out to be like bacon candy - sooooo good! I don't normally get excited about bacon, but this was exceptional (and exceptionally decadent, as my husband pointed out). No complaints about the service - they took our order pretty promptly once we were seated, delivered the food within a reasonable amount of time, and brought the check just when we started looking for someone to flag down. We got a mixed berry scone and a banana chocolate chunk muffin to go for my in-laws, and they loved their baked goods. Highly recommend this place - definitely worth a visit. It's nice that they take your name and give you a fairly accurate wait time so that you're free to go do other things, but there really isn't much to do in the area (and it's not a very nice neighborhood).

this place is pretty chill. i like it b/c it's low key but not so dive-y. bartenders/waiters are nice. i lost my phone there a few weekends ago - one of the bartenders helped me look for it, and checked around even after i was gone. he remembered me the following week and asked if i ever found it - pretty nice guy. they don't serve food past midnight... bummer.

Maybe because I'm used to Ham Ji Bap in Flushing, I was not that impressed.... Â  My friend got Bul Gogi and I got spicy pollock. Â She said that bul gogi wasn't very tender..... Â  It wasn't bad, but I've just had better.

I'm always complaining about how awful Manhattan's K-Town food is. Well, I found a Korean food alternative, just 3 streets away from K-Town!!! The restaurant isn't a fast grab-n-go, although the waitresses do seem to get a little pushy with the check. The restaurant is as traditionally Korean as it can get- from the dÃ©cor, to the ajumma waitresses, to the food, so take your time to enjoy your dining experience! It's very rare to find such an establishment in Manhattan. You'd have to trek out to Queens or Fort Lee to enjoy this type of authenticity. They do not take reservations, but you should be seated in 10-15 minutes even during peak dinner time. If you're going during colder months, I'd highly recommend bundling up because you'll most likely be waiting out in the cold due to their lack of a decently-sized waiting area. As for the food, they're decently priced- comparable to that of Keun Jib and Geum Gang San but not as extravagant/expensive as Kristalbelli or Gaonnuri. But the food is more delicious than at any of the four Korean restaurants aforementioned. They apparently make their tofu on premises, so it's super fresh, super soft, and super delicious. If you're a fan of Soon Dobu, I highly recommend ditching BCD for a night and trying Cho Dang Gol. I'd also highly recommend their Kkong Biji. It's a hearty stew consisting primarily of ground up soybean (the same bean used to make toju) and braised oxtail or bone-in beef. They also have a Kimchi Kkong Biji, for those of you who want the little spice. It's a great Korean dish, that not a lot of restaurants have because it is time-consuming to make. This has to be my favorite Korean dish, apart from Kalbi jjim, which they also have at Cho Dang Gol! For you Korean barbecue lovers, they also have Korean barbecue.

The place was really small only a few tables if i remember correctly. I felt like i was on top of the other guests we were eating next to, it was so tight. The noodles were just ok, a little too hyped up for me. The dumplings I had were pretty big but kinda bland I thought. Maybe they were having a bad night I don't know. I would def give them another try though. I didn't really hear any banging from the noodle pulling going on in the kitchen. The service could have been a little better.

SQUARES from a cheap locals' spot .. that's all my friend orders & he swears this is the best brooklyn pizza of your life (its not bad, but definitely not the best pizza i've had) marinara tasting sauce ON TOP of the cheese & still STEAMING HOT since its fresh out of the oven! the THICK crust isn't very flavorful but it has a nice crusty texture (although i always got a side piece) $2.25 per square BUT you're probably gonna want 2 so if you have 4 ppl.. I SUGGEST getting the half tray since its $19 for 12 pieces! we ordered on the pizza side BUT they also have a restaurant and a TO-GO counter if you must end each meal with a sweet note, YOU'RE IN LUCK. hop in the TO-GO section & order spumoni. although it's not that flavorful because it's NOT REAL ICE CREAM (more like an icee), its cheap! $2.25 for 2 scoops on a cone!

Excellent food. You must get soup dumplings, and its the first thing the waiters will ask you. The service SUCKS, and the tip is already included in the bill so they don't seem to care if they don't treat customers well. That aside, beef brisket noodle soup was excellent as well, spicy szheuan beef was also excellent. Make sure you get there early, because it is packed and lines get long. It is a popular place and many of the people in the area recommend it.

The decor here is fantastic, and the service is great. Â As a whole, I am a huge fan of Perry Street, although it is a little bit out of the way. Â I think I still like JoJo and Jean-Georges better in terms of food, but as a whole this place is still really good! Definitely worth trying!

Stopped here after reading reviews for lunch. Great food! Had the Tuna Burger!!! Freaking awesome! Wife had seafood cioppino with lobster and muscle and shrimp and scallops. All cooked perfectly. Non- over done or Raw. Just PERFECTLY cooked! Fried oysters were great too! This place lets you BYOB so I only wished I knew. Lol~~~ will recommend friends and come again. Owner did tell me on weekend it's a hour wait!!!!! It's not a restaurant that will shock you and aww you. It's a small little place with down to earth good, hearty food which you can enjoy with friends and family over a bottle of your own wine!

Great NY style restaurant. The service was personable and friendly. Â The bar had great choices. Kept with the northern tradition of beer selections. The owner made sure the experience was to perfection. Comfortble, friendly, enjoyable place for family or someone just wanting a pint and delish snack. It has become a tradition to visit woodrow's each year.
crab soup dumplings..... a must place to go in New York...

The food is great, but over priced. Â A regular salad 12 Dollars, really? It seems the local restaurants are starting to take advantage of their customers, because there are not that many places around with good food. Â We need some smaller places a little cheaper to give them some competition. Â 12 Dollars for a salad, crazy. Â I noticed after I had ordered for my wife and I. Â Never again.
will write complete review later!
Cheapest meal in the city. Â Standing room only. Â Great potstickers, great sesame pancakes.

Very yummy food - all the bratwurst/ meats, herring dish, salads, sauerkraut were extremely tasty. Very hearty and yet somehow manages to feel "light", perfectly seasoned, perfectly cooked. Great space that opens onto the sidewalk in the summer! The ambiance is really great, quite casual but something of a bohemian-type feel. Great beer selection.

Three stars because the food is so good but the service is so terrible! Our waitress was sitting the entire time talking to her coworkers instead of being attentive. She forgot to add bacon to my sisters burger and she forgot the onions on my cousins omelet, we had to remind her and then once it was made she stayed sitting for a while before bringing it to us. Talk about lazy! My chicken panini was amazing and the black and white extra thick milkshake was to die for. I would definitely eat here again but hopefully with a different server.
This place was absolutely amazing! GREAT FOOD and SERVICE! The octopus apptz was simply amazing! The short ribs...OMG!

The taste of the pastrami at this place beats out Katz's. It's not too heavy, and has just the right amount of flavor. I got a regular pastrami sandwich on rye with swiss and a side of hot sauce, plus a side of grits. So good. Be sure to call ahead to see if they'll be open when you're coming by. They only deliver at certain times and sometimes close during the day to go to religious services.
This is a great place to go if you are looking for a filling/cheap meal. Also a cool place to eat and the location is prime.

Great service and liked the ambiance. Â Food was very so-so (at best). Â If you cook well, you can make it better--had the pasta primivera (they may call it something else), beet salad and crab cakes.

Used to heading to the Upper West Side or one of the villages for brunch, I was super excited when my roommate discovered that there is brunch near our apartment. Eager to see if we had finally found our go-to brunch spot, we checked it out yesterday. Upon arriving, the first thing we noticed was that there is literally no place to stand while waiting to be seated. We awkwardly stood near the door behind the red curtain since the couple in front of us was already squeezed in the tiny space between the tables and curtains. Luckily for us, we only had a 10 minute wait, during which we also ran to the ATM next door to grab cash (cash only!). I ordered the Eggs Benedict with Smoked Salmon and my roommate and I decided to indulge and share the Apple Pancakes. The Eggs Benedict was fairly standard though the biscuits were a bit too soggy. The mashed potatoes that came with the eggs were delicious! Not quite sure why it was slightly pink colored, but I could definitely eat more of it. The apple pancakes were fresh and pretty. Be careful not to pour too much of the strawberry jam on them though: the jam is tasty, but definitely overpowers the pancake. While Nook didn't blow my mind, the food was solid, the wait was short, and I'd come back.
Large portions....come hungry

So this was my second time coming and how different it was than the first time!! I was extremely satisfied and more!!! The manager personally messaged me and gave our meal on the house next time we came because we were unsatisfied. Even that itself speaks volumes because they really want to keep the customers happy! As a disclaimer-- you can bring your own alcohol but they do not serve it. So please come prepared or just go dry! We got the BBQ+hot pot. We highly recommend the original and kimchee. The other soup flavors have cloves so if you bite into it, it may ruin your taste buds for a little. The meat was marinated great with tastiness! We had the beef and duck. Highly recommended. For hot pot-- we had a lot of seafood and beef with even more veggies. Our service was impeccable this time and I was happy. I didn't even show the free coupon until the end so they were so great. I would hope last time was a fluke. The only reason it wasn't a 5 is because of the alcohol which I know people can live without! We definitely spent a couple hours eating!!
Food, service, ambiance where all top notch. Â My enduring memory will be seeing Ross Gellar eating ice cream here.

Get the potato hash cake for brunch or benedict. The place is big, not too busy during peak brunch hours. I'd recommend this place for groups. They also have a deli in the front as well. not sure if that's part of Alice's Arbor, but looks like they make good sandwiches there.

Ehh, Â I wouldn't recommend running here. I went for brunch with a friend a couple months ago. There are very limited options in the Bed Stuy area, so I was thrilled to try it. I had the fried chicken (of course) , grilled asparagus and potatoes . It was a good dish,.. not hardly the BEST ever. I haven't tried it since and I live 3 blocks away. My friend had the trout or salmon.. (can't remember) & he kept picking at MY plate. Not that it sucks.. just wasn't spectacular to me. However, the drinks are amazing. Very strong.. just how I like it :) The space was a bit awkward. I felt claustrophobic since the tables have no room between. It was pretty packed when I went on a Sunday. Â Cash only - as well. Honestly. There are no options in Bed Stuy, so residents are delighted to have somewhere to go. 5 Stars, in my opinion, is awfully high. Don't go with the same expectations I had. Â But try the chicken.. it supposedly is their best dish.
The ramen is good, not great for the 2 hour wait. Â I prefer Chuko in Brooklyn.

Part of the B.R. Guest Restaurant Group, Isabella's on the Upper West Side is practically a NYC brunch institution. I think of it as the uptown sister to Blue Water Grill. Â Served only on Sundays - brunch at Isabella's on a summer afternoon on the sidewalk is a classic NYC activity. Located near the Museum of Natural History in yummy mummy stroller heaven - expect both a mix of families and ladies who lunch. waffle at Isabella'sBrunch at Isabella's is a great deal - your choice of a cocktail including bellinis, mimosas, champagne or a blood mary + coffee or tea gratis with your brunch entree. Favorites include a variety of eggs benedict - smoked salmon or crab cakes and fritattas and waffles. I usually go with either the crabcake benedict or the pecan waffles with blueberries. While the food is good - I wouldn't say it's extra special. Isabella's is more for the experience and atmosphere. Â A truly pleasant no-fail choice to bring out of town guests and family.
Beautiful restaurant and great prices!
One of my favorite Williamsburg destinations! Â Amazing whisky selection, delicious food, awesome ambiance. Â I love it!

Fast, clean, great service and the empanadas are very good too. Lots to choose from in three basic styles, white flour, corn and organic which was whole wheat I think...If you find yourself near here drop in and you won't be disappointed.

I love Cuba. Â It's my favorite restaurant to visit when I am in the city. Â Everything I've ordered here, I love. Â The live music here is definitely a plus and the restaurant itself has a nice, relaxing, romantic vibe to it. Â The mojitos are nice and strong and authentic. Â I've had several of the seafood dishes, and you can't go wrong with any of them. Â Everyone I take here loves the place and then takes their friends.

After a gym workout I was eager to find something tasty nearby and Yelp recommended Kobeyaki. Â Thus, my gym buddy and I made the short trek over. Â  I was intrigued with the "Asian" fusion of the restaurant and decided to try a spicy tuna burger, despite the semi-uninterested cashier telling us that the bowls were the most popular. Â To be honest, the bowls didn't look that special to me and reminded me of takeout food from the likes of Cafe Zaiya or Woorijip (Japanese and Korean quick eats places). Â The wrapping of the burger is interesting, but a little unnecessary. Â What's inside is what counts! Â The burger was disappointingly smaller than I thought. Â The tuna patty was nicely seasoned and cooked and I liked the sprouts and veggies that came with it. Â I doused it with Sriracha. Â It was an enjoyable burger, but nothing I would crave again after the gym. I loved the tempura sweet potato fries, but they were almost cold. Â Still a little crispy, but definitely not "piping hot" like some of the other reviews say. Â I'd say they'd been sitting around a while before they ended up on our tray. Â I could only imagine how perfect they would have been had they been fresh.... Sauces to choose from include spicy mayo, wasabi mayo, and teriyaki ketchup. At around $13 for a burger and side of sweet potato fries, I think I could probably find a more fulfilling meal elsewhere, but I'd still say Kobeyaki is a decent meal if you can't find anything else.
Amazing wine list. Had the pork chop on a Fall night in New York that tasted oh so good with golden raisens and sliverred almonds. They play really good music here too. Highly recommend.

I'm from Arizona. Â My roommate is Mexican. Â This alone qualifies me to say what I am about to say. Barrio Chino is orgasm inducing. Â I would make love to their mole. Â I might even kill for their mole. Â If I lived anywhere near this place, I'd be obese from gorging on their mole. Â Hell, I'm looking at pictures of their mole right now... and salivating. Â  It's a sad day when someone living in the Sonoran Desert would rather eat Mexican food in New York City.

Way too packed ALL the time and I guess you can call what they do "service". You will wait outside to be seated. The food is mostly traditional...but if you must order one thing, order the dumplings. I recommend going with a group so you can be seated on a revolving table that lets you "pull" whatever entree your'e interested in and share. The dumplings are a must. A tad too touristy though.
Their chicken burrito was wonderful and the sitting out experience good, staff was also very friendly.

Food is amazing. The eggs Benedict are probably one of the better ones I've ever had. Even the sides that came with were well made. The salad has a light flavorful dressing and fries were devoured. Â The Pancakes were crispy on the outside and a fluffy cake like consistency where they dissolved in my mouth.Out of this world. I didn't even realize how much I ate! The only downfall was the service was slow and they kept trying to take my plate when I wasn't finish so I felt rushed.

First of all, i'm deducting one star because the service was lacking considerably. However, the food was awesomeawesomeawesome! We ordered a small plate of wings, two burgers and a coke that totaled in $34 - not too bad for two people in park slope. I went here specifically for the wings and was not disappointed! Â I braved the Hot wings and thought it was perfect. Â This is a hotness that builds up over time! Â The first few bites I was like, "oh this isn't too bad" but by the fourth one my lips were actually on fire. Â In a good way. Â I am curious to try the hotter next time... We both ordered burgers for our main meal and I was sure they wouldn't compare to the super delicious wings. Â Boy was I wrong. Â These are hands down the best burgers in brooklyn! Â They are char grilled which means they're cooked exactly how you asked and have an amazing flavor! Â All the normal toppings are included: tomato, lettuce, onions, jalapeno peppers, cheese, then carmelized onions and bacon are an extra charge. Â The only negative thing I can say about the burgers is they are rather large and leave you feeling very full afterward. Â But hey, it's a good value and seriously, these burgers are amazing. More about the service. Â On a Saturday night around 8p, we were pleased with the barely 15 min wait to be seated. Â But then it took almost that long to have our order taken. Â People who ordered their food after us, got it before us. I had to hunt the waiter down to ask for more water. Â But you know, I would only deduct half a star if I could. Â The food was so tasty I can easily forgive some slight unattentiveness. Â  Go to Bonnie's! Â Eat wings! Eat burgers! Be merry!

The drinks were great, and so was the food, but the service was a little slow. Â I had asked for some brown bread about 3-4 times before the waitress finally brought it out to me. Â I ordered the trout for dinner and although it was tasty, it was FULL of bones. Â I suppose one would say to me that I ordered fish, and it is to be expected, but still.... I'd have hoped for it to have less bones. Â Not in every bite. I'd go back again though, and possibly order the schnitzel the next time.

This is one of the few Filipino restaurants that I'll keep coming back to, only because Filipino home cooking is usually so much better. Filipino food isn't always the most attractive, but Jeepney does a great job at bringing Filipino food on a more appetizing plate. Everything here is pretty good, so I'd suggest just reading over the menu and pick what sounds good to you. If you like garlic, definitely get the garlic rice. When they get their liquor license back, it'll be even better because they had this white drink with hibiscus flower that was delicious! The staff here is great. The past few times, Kristin served me, and she's always super nice and helpful. Definitely make reservations if you plan to come here, just to be on the safe side. I've seen it get pretty crowded with waits around 30-45min around prime time.

My husband and I are staying in the lower east village and wanted to have a nice dinner close to the hotel. Â Thelma 's at clinton did not disappoint. Â In fact, everything about Â the meal was so tasty..from the onion risotto to the bacon wrapped dates to the lamb stew and desserts. Â We had a nice quiet corner table and enjoyed every one of the small dishes brought to us. Â This restaurant is a gem and we definitely plan to come back next time we are in the city.

Fried chicken skin - small but awesome Squid skewers - is it possible to get squid an awesome texture? Braised seaweed - oh yes...so gooood, sassy sauce Monk fish liver - fun to try, but...um, I wouldn't get AGAIN Shrimp balls - moist and delicious! Spring rolls - so lovely and crispy Salmon soup - mmmmmm, smoky Everything is sharable. Fast and authentic. Under $15. My tongue was delighted! The waitress came across a little brusque, but I think it was a language barrier combined with our fatigue. Next time, I'd like to try the larger dishes. Everything we got were small plates.

At the heart of this hole-in-the-wall unassuming restaurant is GREAT food. If that's what you are looking for, I would definitely recommend it!! If you are looking for an overall wonderful dining experience from atmosphere, to selection, to service, you may be a little let down. Â Sometimes to try a unique place like this with a truly authentic cuisine you have to let some of that go. When you arrive you may not be 100% sure you are in the right place or that its open if you haven't seen pictures before hand. Â The kitchen is on the lower floor, and the dine in space is in a loft-like space above it. Â Because of this, the dine in space can get really really hot (the kitchen is right below!!). Â If its a cool day with a breeze this really isn't a problem, but I imagine in the hot summer it could be miserable or even unbearable to eat in. Â In this case it would be nice to just get the food to go and go eat in the nearby park. Â It seems at some points there is only one person there... aka the same guy is cooking, taking orders, sitting people down etc. Â We essentially were given a pitcher of water, had our order taken, and had our food delivered and that was the extent of the service. Â Don't get me wrong they are super nice, but they are obviously busy and its not your typical restaurant where people are checking in on you, etc. Now, let's get to the best part... the food!! The menu is not extremely extensive, but it has some unique caribbean options along with the traditional dishes you would expect such as jerk chicken. Â The group I was with ordered the jerk chicken, curry shrimp, and oxtail entrees, and they were all to die for!!! The large portion is huge, and I would say the small is plenty unless you are absolutely starving. Â The entrees come with a salad, cooked cabbage, and the best red beans and rice I've ever had! The food was literally prepared so fresh and all the spices and flavor really hit the spot. Â All of the dishes were the perfect amount of spicy. Â It was the kinda meal where you really didn't want it to end and you really didn't want to get full until you ate ever single bite. Â Even if you don't have any experience with caribbean cuisine I would definitely recommend you try this restaurant if you are in the neighborhood!! I'll definitely be coming back sometime soon, you can't just get this kind of food anywhere...

Got a salad. It was kinda small or the price. My friends got burger. They said it was alright. Nothing stood out. They do have a pretty wide selection of wine. The service was only okay. We waited for like 15 minutes for the check. I didn't mind... It was Friday night. I really like the ambiance tho. The lighting and smell was perfect. It feels really nice. I would suggest you to dress up a little bit before you go.
Can't ask for someone to make a better pizza. I have nothing else to say on the matter.

I have been here several times and have never been disappointed. From the great food and service, Nai does not disappoint. I recommend their mango sangria, which I have never had before until I tried it there, along with the octopus and ham croquettes. Their desserts are just as good, with the creme brulee ice cream or the almond tart.

Very usable web site; changes daily and includes specials. Have only been here for late lunch on a slow day, but was very impressed and plan to return. Waiter was unobtrusively attentive; burger was very tasty and chicken was high quality; prices were reasonable, and interior was new, comfortable, very clean and left us wanting to come check this place out on a busy night!

Cheap price, lots of food, good quality. Those are all the things that make halal guys amazing. First, let me give you a warning, and I want you to pay attention because this is extremely important. !!!!!!!!!!! BEWARE THE RED SAUCE !!!!!!!!!!! Oh my goodness. On my first trip to halal guys, my foolishly foolish fool of a friend POURED the sauce over my plate. Thinking nothing of it, I let her as the more experienced new yorkers loled. After my first bite I cried. It hurt so much but it was good... but it hurt so much. I've never experienced so much pain while eating. And my leftovers gave me gastric reflux over and over again (but it was so tasty!!!) My friends and I decided that we had to come back and try the food sans hot sauce. I got the chicken and rice combination with the gyro. IT'S AMAZING. I prefer the gyro but it's nice to get a little variety on your plate :) Same price as the chicken and rice but you get two toppings! ($6 per plate aint bad... leftovers generally last me for 2 additional meals for a total of 3 meals for $6). ***Tips: - The line is long but it's not horribly long and it moves fast. - There are TWO locations near MOMA. They taste the same, but usually the line caddy corner from the museum is the shortest. - If you cross to the museum side, there are tables and chairs there. The fountain can get wet so you don't want to sit there. - If you use too much hot sauce, the blackberry mojito from the starbucks across the street is amazing and works wonders (probably because of the mint).

Since I moved to Gramercy I'd been lusting after dinner at the Tavern. Â After months of dropping hints to my boyfriend he surprised me with a birthday reservation in the Dining Room. Â Yipee! You feel like somebody really important from the moment you set foot in the place. Â Low lights, great art, and more diamonds on the patrons than you could find on W. 47th. Â I have to admit, we spent the first 20 minutes pointing out the unbelievable baubles on the fingers of our neighbors ("OMG! Â Don't look now, but you have to see the ring on the woman in black at the corner table! Â I think I've gone blind!"). The service was impeccable. Â Our waiter struck the perfect (and almost unachievable) balance between allowing us a slow-paced, leisurely meal and patient attentiveness. Â He was precious and very knowledgeable. I started with the smoked lobster appetizer which was generously portioned and buttery. Â For my entree, I had the striped bass. Â Nicely done with beans and a light sauce. Â My portion, again, was the perfect size. Â My boyfriend had the veal to start and the hanger steak as his entree. Â While he liked both, he found that portion of his entree to be a bit small. Â I will say though, by the time I got through my entree I felt that I legitimately had enough room for dessert. Â Personally, I prefer it that way, I hate feeling sickeningly full as I leave a restaurant. Â For dessert I had the chocolate bread pudding and he had the nectarine tart. Â Both were amazing (though I was so drunk at this point that I'm not sure I would have known if they'd microwaved a hostess cupcake and put it in front of me... Classy, I know.). Â Also, throughout the evening we were sent delicious nibbles "compliments of the chef." Â These included an heirloom tomato sampling and a baby eggplant plate, such a nice touch. Â Of course, we were also given muffins as we left. I was so impressed by my evening here, it may be awhile before I can save enough pennies to afford to go back, but I'll be counting down the days!

$1 for Four Chive and Pork Fried Dumplings $2.50 for Eight Chive and Pork Boiled Dumplings Handmade, Fresh, Delicious, and Affordable! What more is there to say? Oh yea, go get some NOW! {Note} Their Sriracha Sauce (hot sauce) can be watered down sometimes. There is also MORE seating available here compared to Prosperity Dumpling.

I found this restaurant by accident with my boyfriend, his friend, and my boyfriend's brother and it wad AMAZING. Â  The empanadas are probably the best I've ever had. Â They're so flavorful and they're not greasy. Â The first time we went we couldn't believe how good they were. Â The second time it was just me and my boyfriend and they were good but nothing like the first time. Â My boyfriend was so curious as to why they were so good the previous time that he asked the waitress who was working and who made them the last time. Â We found out his name was Carlos. Â All I have to say is that Carlos is the man and we always ask if he's working so we know if we should order empanadas. The soups are also really tasty as well. Â I get the Chicken Tortilla a lot, which is excellent. Â Last time I got the Ajiaco and that was also really good. I've had the patacon before and it was good but it wasn't like a sandwich like I'm usually used to. Â Here it was flat with the plantains on the bottom. Â I just folded it up and made it like a sandwich anyway. Their Aji sauce really is good on everything. The atmosphere is really fun and the place is good for groups. Â It does get pretty busy on weekend nights though so plan accordingly if you have a big group. Â They also make you wait until all the members of your party are there before they seat the group.

I like Joe's Shanghai.. but what is up with the waiter? I felt like the waiter was trying to rush us out? I know it was around closing time, but there were still 2 LARGE tables sitting there and EATING. Cleaning up a table with 3 people is not gonna make you go home that much earlier. We had one soup dumpling left and the waiter stood next to us with his hand on the chair waiting for us to eat it so he can take the steamer away. Then when we got the oranges, I didn't even get a chance to eat it yet and he comes up to us, grabs the plate, and says, you don't want it anymore, right? I immediately told him, yes, i want it.

Best value in New York for sure. Great service, great ambiance, unbelievable food, and great wine list at all price points. The food here always impresses me (calamari is great, as well as the Arctic Char and Cod), but I hear from friends that everything is amazing. You can get appetizer + entre + wine for about $50 a person, and it's easily worth over $100. If you can make your way out here, you'll be pleasantly surprised.

You know something is the bomb when the line is 30+ people deep. Â Mighty Quinn's, by far, had the longest line at Smorgasburg and it was worth the wait. Â You must get the beef brisket sammie! Â Smoky, tender brisket nestled in a soft broiche bun Â complimented with cucumbers and pickled onions. Â Mmmm. Â I'm salivating just thinking about it. Â Best beef brisket I've ever had! Will I stand in this crazy long line next time I visit Smorgasburg? Â Hell yeah! Â With any luck, they'll have the pulled lamb sammie that I saw featured on Unique Eats. Â That ish looked legit.
very berry mojitos.... YES PLEASE ! mac and cheese sampler. steak sandwhich. pancakes. grilled cheese all of this post debauchery.... even tastier.

Was just introduced to the best chicken sandwich I have ever had. From the perfect bread to the incredible sweet chili and lemon mayo. This place is a must and $11 could have been $15 and still worth it. I will be back as soon as possible. Bluey's Burger cannot be missed
Definition of Pretentious. The hostess was a stupid snob. Put me out. There are so many better places to eat where the staff will at least pretend to be nice.

Insanely crowded when a friend and I went for brunch on Sunday, Â but in a jovial way. Rather expensive ($12 mimosas?) but their strawberry banana pancakes were the fluffiest, puffiest, most delicious pancakes I've ever had. I had poached eggs on english muffins as well, which were cooked just right (not too runny, not too solid). My friend kept looking around the restaurant for Harvey Keitel, who apparently goes there a lot. Sadly, Harvey did not show for us. In every other respect, a successful brunch.

Sorry I am very very sad to give you a 3. But you moved and your ambiance is wack and I swear your food has gotten worse. You are cheap with your bread, your drinks were weak and you changed your menu. I used to come here all the time and I don't plan on coming back to a restaurant in a hotel. ADIOS Calle Ocho

I noticed the great reviews and needed a good spot for a group of 8 people. Well I scored and looked like the best hosts for suggesting Cafe Mogador. Location is great, prices are good for every ones pocket food selection covered vegans and nonvegan good looking place they have a patio you should try to request Drinks were tasty and different. I like to try something new but also for it to taste good. well it had a good combination of both. Wait staff was pleasant. one thing, I had called a few weeks prior asking if reservations were needed, I was told no. When we arrived, the first thing I was asked was "do you have reservations". That made me very nervous. I had 8 friends with me. I also mentioned how I was told no reservations needed. The hosts talked to the waitress and in about 20 minutes we were seated. So my advice call and ask for a reservation. Insist on one.

long waiting! but worth the eait.. for starters we had pan cake balls,the munchkins tasted good i wish it was served with a sweeter sauce instead of lemon sauce i had a very sour tart taste and i guess i like my pancake with a sweeter sauce like maple or chocolate.. i had teh huevos rancheros which was interesting..and my other half ordered scramble eggs which he loved.. our server was super good James! the total of our check was also affordable...good food for good pricing.

Oh my god, I've been dreaming of this place since I ordered dinner on Friday. I've only gotten delivery, so have no idea what the inside of this place is like, but the food is phenomenal. When my friend insisted we order dinner there, I looked at the menu and was admittedly unsure about the combinations of things in the wraps. Fig dough? Date and pumpkin seed dough? Bean sprout slaw and sweet potato chips? Melon?! But just trust them - everything is amazing. The combination of flavors is so bizarre but works so well. I was full after just half my wrap (they are gigantic!) but I kept eating it because it was so good. The tater tots and fries are also delicious and come with what tastes like the special sauce on a hamburger - I think it must be ketchup, mayonnaise, and relish. I would trek down to the lower east side from my usual haunts on the upper east side just for a meal at Wolfnights!
The falafels, hummus and baklava are amazing. The swarma I've definitely had better.

We had a full meal for two, good food too, for less than $14! Nice choices, and a buffet for those who like to pick their own combinations. Food could have been a little warmer, but nonetheless an excellent place!

The best Japanese I have eaten in New York. Dare and go for the conventional - the grilled satsuma-imo is divine! As are of course the more fancy dishes (the duck skewers were incredible), and all sorts of grilled fish. Extremely attentive service, very 'authentic' (I have lived in Japan several years and consider myself fairly well acquainted with it, as my waistline still attests). When you don't drink alcohol, it's actually not expensive at all - we had a bill of 65 bucks incl. taxes for two people who had eaten to their heart's content, which for such delicious food and such a great atmosphere is hard to beat!

This is Herald from Season 1 Top Chef's restaurant! Â He was my favorite on that season, I was so excited to go here for restaurant week. Â I asked my server if Herald came by often, and she said he was working tonight. Â He invited us back to the kitchen and actually specially cooked our food because he knew I was a fan. Â He's a great guy and has a great operation. Â Check it out, I think you will be very pleased. *Enjoy*

I cried the first time I had the lamb over rice here. Like tears flowing flowing, snot dripping, total mess of a person on the corner of 53rd & 6th. Embarrassing... Admittedly, it was because I laid on the hot sauce, but I could see people being reduced to joyous tears about the deliciousness that is the Halal platters made by the Halal Guys. I thought that this Halal cart was like every other Halal cart in the city. Boy was I wrong on so many levels and my taste buds got a double dose of joy and pain. Now, it used to be that there were impostor guys wearing yellow hoodies similar to the trademark ones worn by the Halal guys in order to trick you into order sub-par Halal food. However, it seems like the Real Halal Guys have colonized the whole block, with locations on the SW & SE corner of 53rd/6th and NW corner of 52nd/6th (at least when I went there last week). They all serve the same thing so find the one with the shortest line and have at it! If it's your first time, get the combo (chicken and lamb) platter ($6) to get the full Halal Guys experience. Eventually, you'll develop your preferences for lamb, chicken or both. In my opinion, the chicken is moist though rather bland in terms of seasoning while the lamb is more flavorful without the gaminess and moist unlike other carts in the city. You can find the sauces in bottles along side the carts. The white sauce is delicious and can be a savior when you've put on too much of the red sauce (not to be confused with the BBQ sauce). Lay on the white sauce and mix, eat and repeat. I have found that putting the red sauce to the side and dipping your fork into the sauce before you scoop up the rice and meat to eat lets you control how much red sauce you consume. It's surprising how little red sauce you actually need because this stuff is concentrated Hellfire... super potent stuff. They open in the evening and stay open until wee hours of the morning. The longest lines are usually at 1-2AMish when the drunk munchies start kicking in. For some reason, the Halal platter tastes 1000 better when you are drunk and hungry. Probably because you can ignore how many calories you are consuming and turn into a Halal-eating tornado. And after you consume that whole platter, you won't be hungry again until you are ready to go out again. Whether you share with a friend or have one to yourself, for the same everyday low price of $6, you can get one of the best Halal food in the city. Something you plan your day and/or night around. 5/5 Stars

The atmosphere is cute and cozy . Great for a date night with the girls or your significant other. I ordered a Strawberry-vanilla margarita which sounded interesting, but totally worth the try it. Everything was amazing. We also ordered Plato Mexicano which was more than enough to share for 2...and for dessert we had the flan de coco. The Jamaica tea is also an interesting but great drink, it was made with hibiscus and it was extremely yummy. I absolutely love this place! I've been there a few times now, the bartenders are nice the servers are always busy and can be a little delayed but their personalities are great and they're attentive. Â I hope they stick around for a while
Yes, the wait can be long but stake out your claim at the bar for the 6-8pm happy hour: $6 buys you 2 draft beers. Â  Akamaru Modern ($15) + kakuni addition ($4) -- hits the spot every time.

3.5 Stars -- I have always heard of the famed Balthazar and walked by on multiple occasions, but never with it as my destination in mind or had the time to wait in its incredibly long line! Today, my friend, Phoebe, and I dropped by a bit before noon for brunch to find that not only was the wait only half an hour, there was a few seat open in the bar area. We ended up taking our name off the restaurant wait list and sat in the bar area. We had a small round table (which was not stable, but fixed right away by one of the wait staff) next to the window. The food is a bit pricier, but the quality was quite good. Phoebe ordered the Bella Donna (I think that was what it was called -- poached eggs atop polenta). I ordered the Crepes Du Jour (buckwheat crepes with ham, scrambled eggs & Gruyere cheese); it came with a side of salad, which had a light vinaigrette and sun dried tomatoes. I have to say Phoebe's dish was better. The salad for my dish was amazing, but the crepes were so-so. The buckwheat crepe was a bit tough and in general, the crepes felt dry and there was not one ingredient that brought the dish together. Additionally, the waiter was not the most accommodating. We did not order drinks and he basically did not treat us well after that and was flattering the table next to us with toasted bread (we got none at all) and did not take the time to answer our questions (such as what he would recommend; he answered, but left quickly when a pretty blond was ready to pay 2 tables down). I am always disappointed when a famed restaurant with good food and reputation does not maintain it with a friendly wait staff. I am not sure I would return to Balthazar. The food was decent, but not outstanding. The service was meh. For a French brunch in NYC, I definitely prefer Tartine.

Mamoun's is not the best falafel in NYC and is far from it. Sure its cheap, but you get what you pay for, as they only put two tiny pieces of falafel in their sandwiches and the rest is all lettuce. It's not filling and gave me a stomach ache after. I only give it two stars, because they have good hot sauce - super spicy so be careful. For a falafel sandwich, I recommend Cheeps in the East Village or Pita Joes on 14th St.

Don't let the hostess ruin your day! I came to Calle Ocho this past weekend for a Bachelorette Brunch and overall I'd say it was an excellent experience. Getting a reservation can be tough, but I called the Friday before to see if there had been any cancellations and lucky for us, there were! The person I spoke with was great--very nice and helpful. Now onto our arrival....it started out rough. There is apparently an issue with waiting in the hotel lobby so the Â hostess wanted to seat us early. Not a problem except that our entire party was there and she said that our 2 hours time slot would start as soon as she sat us. We let her know (very nicely) that if that was the case, we'd rather just wait for our whole group--since our reservation wasn't until 12 (and the restaurant doesn't actually even open until then). Her response could not have been ruder or more unprofessional. It was really astounding. Determined not to let that ruin our special day, we ignored her stink eye and asked to be seated at just before 12 when our group was present. Our meal proceeded famously--the food was good (the omelette and vaca frita seemed to be the favorites), the sangria was excellent (the Spanish Harlem reigns supreme). Our glasses were constantly filled and we sat far longer than our allotted seating time with no issue at all. From the bus staff to the waiters to the manger (whom I spoke with before leaving to let him know how wonderful everything but his hostess was), everyone else we interacted with was great. I would definitely come back again!

For me this is as good as it gets and the service is always as good as the food. Â  Was there the other night and there was a minor issue. Â The chef who was out on the floor at the moment making sure everyone was happy, saw what had happened and personally took care of it. Â  Can't wait to go back!

Everything was tasty. Putting deep fried chickpeas and lemon in the crispy calamari was an awesome idea. Flavor of sardine was fresh and great. Should I keep going? Basically, everything was yummy. Dining here gave you no pressure, price was affordable too. The only bad thing is that it's too popular, HAS to make a reservation.
Decent pizza. Make sure to get it fresh. Overpriced and definitely overrated, but still good.

Great atmosphere and decent service, but mediocre food in comparison to the other Thai restaurants in Hell's Kitchen. Â The lunch special appetizers are ridiculously small portions (tiny finger foods), and the flavor is bland and unimpressive. Â With all of the Thai options in the neighborhood, you can get much better value for your money elsewhere.

Bone marrow Ox tail is fooking awesome main reason why we made the trek... Â Everything thing was good but was missing the wow factor... Rack of lamb duck breast and the pigeon was just Ok Chocolate Bruno was good but haf way too much ice cream 3 scoops not that it's a bad thing Oooo and it gets super packed ppl hanging around the bar invaded our table space. If I do revisit it's gonna be for the bone marrow Ox tail

Every option that we selected was delicious (we had the selection of pita spreads, jumbo shrimp, lamb chops), and the couple at the table next to us seemed to order the entire menu. Great pizza love it

A great deal for lunch in the area. It's weirdly inside of a building. You go past the lobby and there is a deli on the right back. I ordered the spicy pork, Jeyuk Bokkeum ($8.95). It comes with a banchan, soft cabbage with a red pepper sauce and kimchi. There also was a miso soup. There are a few tables to sit down and eat. I ordered my plate to stay and it was huge. A salad, rice, and a large portion of spicy pork. Good thing I was hungry as the meal was basically enough for two. Large portions of cheap Korean food. I approve.

I've walked past Saigon Shack a bunch of times during my lunch break, and today decided to try it after popping in and out of a few places on MacDougal trying to make up my mind. Â I ordered the Crabcake Bahn Mi and it did not disappoint! The balance of the crabcake, carrot, daikon, cucumber and spicy mayo sauce was perfect and the bread was a fresh crusty baguette. The ingredients were fresh and delicious. I picked up a menu on my way out, Â they have a nice selection of Pho and Vermicelli dishes as well as salads and an espresso bar. Yep, I will be be back to try their other menu items as well as the espresso bar. And most definitely the lychee shake!

Food = delicious. Bottomless sangria = awesome. Wait staff = d-bags. When the host learned that my friend and I didn't have reservations, he whispered to the other hostess and they both looked us up and down and said that it would take twenty minutes to be seated. Fine, that's ok. We were there on a Saturday during brunch. We get it. After being seated, the waiter flung our menus at us and quickly went through "brunch at Calle Ocho". Since he went so fast and we'd never been there, I said "sorry, what was that last thing you said?" and he rolled his eyes, let out a big sigh and walked away. My bad, I should have kept up. I am a New Yorker after all. Â After ordering and eating for about ten minutes, our waiter asked us if we wanted dessert and we politely declined. I finish eating first and the waiter quickly grabbed my plate, napkin and glass. I thought this to mean that he was efficient and looking to give me as much table top space I needed. How thoughtful! But no, as soon as my friend put down her knife, he swooped down and grabbed that as well. That's ok, she was done cutting her tortilla anyway. We're about fifteen minutes into our meal and he drops the check on the table. We pay and leave a generous tip thinking that would make him back off a little but it only made things worse. There was a point when my friend finished her food and was about to set her fork down and he grabbed it from her hand! But for all I know, she was just holding it up for him. She's considerate like that. We were in the process of finishing our sangrias when he came around and said "you guys want anything else?". We finally got the hint and left. It was 3:30 pm on a Saturday, I guess they were busy and needed the table space... my friend and I do take up a lot of space with our combined mass of 210 lbs. The food is the only redeeming factor. The sangria bar is cool but at the same time, communal punch bowls just reminded me of those old college days filled with jungle juice/trashcan punch.

The ramen was very good, the ambiance, not so much. Very small place, room for 20 or so. I sat at the bar, and the heat from the burners was intense. This was my 2nd experience with Ramen, my first in NYC. My other, in Washington DC, that place had great ramen AND a nice ambiance. Is it really that hard to clean a place up and open a restaurant? I would classify this place as a "Ramen joint" dingy, hot, and cramped. Excellent food, but unfortunately the decor was so poor that for me, it really ruined the experience. It was so bad, that when I first arrived, I almost turned around and left without eating. The ONLY reason I stayed was because so many other reviews on Yelp really praised the food. I must admit, the food reviews were accurate, I'm just surprised very few talked about the ambiance. If this place didn't have a line waiting outside and a series of great reviews, I doubt anyone would walk by and try it on looks alone. To me, that's a shame, and shameful.
Recommend the Pad thai and sweet potato fries. Check in to get a complimentary beer or wine.

After checking-in with the hostess, I was able to admire the interior space as I was led to our table. Â Rustic wooden beams contrasted beautifully with the buttermilk-colored walls and arched passageways. Â Understated chandeliers, wall sconces, hand-painted murals and antique artworks painted the space with casual elegance. Â  What a pleasant surprise to see that Julie had arrived first and was already seated at our table! Â While waiting for Christine, the two of us got a chance to briefly catch up and order our first round of drinks. Â After perusing the cocktail menu, there wasn't a chance in hell that I could say no to the "Jalisco Pear," composed of tequila, pear liqueur, and allspice dram. Christine joined us just moments later. When dining at Gramercy Tavern, you have one of two choices: Â the $88 a-la-carte prix fixe (dinner), or the $116 seasonal tasting (dinner). Â With the latter menu, guests are not able to select specific dishes, unlike the a-la-carte option. Â My girlfriends and I opted for the seasonal tasting menu, because someone forgot to tell us that we're not ballers. Â  Moments after we placed our orders, a gentleman carrying a large basket of bread and a pair of tongs approached our table. Â We had the choice of sliced sourdough or a whole wheat boule - or both, if you're anything like me. Â Butter and sea salt accompanied. ~ First course: Â Fluke Tartare~ Radish bits, orange segments, and bite-sized pieces of raw fluke came together "tartare-style" in this sexy presentation. Â The dish was finished with dollops of black caviar. As stunning as it may have appeared, I found that the fluke tasted unpleasantly "fishy." Â The verdict is out as to whether it was intentional, but the caviar only accentuated that strong flavor. Second course: Â Clam Chowder~ A halved, pan-seared scallop - a single shrimp - and, what tasted like, a tempura-fried clam, appeared at the bottom of a shallow bowl. Â Celery root soup was poured over the ingredients and topped with smoked trout roe. This dish would have been dynamite had it not been for the roe. Â I did my best to push it aside but, ultimately, I was defeated. Third course: Â Halibut~ A perfectly-cooked filet of halibut sat atop a surprisingly flavorful carrot broth and a vegetable melange, including cabbage and mushrooms. It was at this point in our seafood-heavy tasting that I finally enjoyed every aspect of the dish. Â Bravo! Fourth course: Â Duck Dumplings~ Three handmade dumplings were stuffed to the brim with salty, finely-shredded duck meat and surrounded by a rich broth (I'm guessing it was beef) that was studded with cooked turnips and black kale. All three of us loved this course, but found it to be a bit salty. Â The duck meat reminded me of a ball of tightly packed, shredded brisket. Fifth course: Â Roasted Sirloin and Flatiron~ A small medallion-cut of each, sirloin and flatiron, was prepared medium-rare and served alongside chestnuts, beets, and ripe pear. This was the course that I wanted to love most of the five savories. Â It also happens to be one of the reasons that I voted for the pricier tasting menu. Â Sadly, I was disappointed; the beef was incredibly hard to cut, tough, and chewy. Â It also lacked in flavor but, luckily, we still had a dish of sea salt on the table from the bread service. Â  Â  Dessert course's amuse bouche: Â Deconstructed Goat's Milk Cheesecake~ A round, graham-cracker/shortbread disk separated a dollop of whipped, goat's milk-based cheesecake "filling" and a small scoop of Concord grape sorbet. Aside from the duck dumplings, this was my favorite "course," despite it being an amuse. Â The pungency of the "filling" was perfectly cut by the sweetness of the sorbet. Â The graham cracker disk added a delightful crunch and texture. Dessert/sixth course: Â Coconut Mousse with Passion Fruit Ice Cream~ While this plate appears to be "busy," all of its components worked brilliantly together, both in flavor and texture. Â In the center stood an ample scoop of passion fruit ice cream, which was surrounded by toasted coconut nibs. Â A ring of fresh passion fruit puree came next, followed by fluffy coconut mousse. Â The mousse was topped with crunchy meringue "puffs" that, from afar, looked like cotton balls. Â Finally, another ring of passion fruit puree encircled the outer perimeter of the plate. To conclude~ I can easily see why Gramercy Tavern is a favorite among New Yorkers and tourists, alike. Â The space is lovely, the service is smartly on-point, all of the ingredients are sourced from local farmers/producers, they've got a great beverage program, and the food is good. Â However, people said that a meal here would change my life. Â It didn't. I look forward to returning to the restaurant - only next time, I'll enjoy my meal in the more casual Tavern room. Â I'm more of a "cheeseburger and fries" type of girl, anyways.

This is my first review after about 7 visits. They do everything right. Large resto with lovely outdoor patio, you never have to wait long to find a table whether you're a group of 2 or 8. If you must wait, they have a great bar with cheap beer, fancy whiskys, and everything in between. The decor is cool, if a little overplayed (industrial gaslight, reclaimed wood), but as with all great restaurants, the pizza is what will keep you coming back. Fresh ingredients and the best chewy dough/crust. A bit different from the standard NY pie, these are smaller, chewier, with a crispy bottom, and a thick layer of toppings instead of a meager distribution. The staff are pleasant and helpful. Great place for a group- split a bunch of pies!

The extra star is for the "EFFORT" in Decor. 4 girls (like sex in the city show), Met up together for a nice Dinner. ALL this Â reviews mention about the decor and service. Which I must say very impressed with all the dimmed lights and a Huge Chandelier as a centerpiece. Food came within 5 minutes after we all ordered, Pretty quick. FOOD IS AWFUL I must say. Â Will stick with my other Thai places around the neighborhood.
The freshest Thai food ever. So many great entrees.. Nothing beats the Massiman Curry... Great take out, better atmosphere inside... cold beer, great service and food. Always reliable.

I would not be surprised if someone told me the word ngam was Thai for yummmm! Â Have been here twice Â and both times, the food was unbelievable. Â The green papaya salad is amazing, and the spicy drunken noodles are the best in the city. Â There can be a long wait for a table, but they take reservations, so that is the way to go. Â Ngam and Pam Real Thai in Hells Kitchen are my two favorite Thai places in Manhattan. Â  Service is friendly and fast. Â Tables are really cose together, but that's Manhatran for you! P.s. Get the spring rolls!

We have been here a number of times, sometimes small groups and others larger--about 10-13, and each time they are very accommodating. Â The service is superb and the staff is courteous and friendly. Â We have tried almost everything on the menu and it always tastes amazing, as do the drinks! Â I would definitely recommend Yerba Buena to anyone looking for good, quality food that is not overpriced!

Apparently I am missing something. All I hear (and read) about is Di Fara's, Di Fara's, Di Fara's - THE BEST PIZZA IN ALL OF BROOKLYN - I couldn't agree less. If rude staff that moves at a glacial pace, dirty dingy walls and ceiling tiles, broken chairs and tables and greasy, burnt pizza make for a fantastic dining experience, count me OUT! Let me not forget to mention that I could not even bring myself to eat the entire $5 slice that I had waited over half an hour for - the grease consumed my hands, wrists and forearms and the charred crust was equally as vile. I even went so far as to subject myself to a second round of this place, only to be let down even harder. I get the historical value of a business that has been around as long as Di Fara, but in my opinion, all this place has to offer is HISTORY!
Heard nothing but good about Don Peppes have to go some day have family still lives there!!I love family style also will go ASAP!!
The best pizza I ever had... Ever!!!!

This is a must if you are vegan and a great restaurant if you aren't. Well thought out menu, excellently prepared, friendly and attentive staff. We had the pulled "pork" bbq sandwich which was big and delicious and the "chicken fried" seitan which was delicious as well. Ham and cheese croquet was good. Excellent desserts Will be back!!! Finally an excellent vegan option.

Went here last year for a friend's birthday. We were a party of four on a warm summer's eve, so we expected an hour wait. Then it started raining and they had to consolidate the terrace, so ended up waiting almost two hours. Still worth it. Octopus was phenomenal. Seafood was great. Side of greens are very odd tasting/preparation. Overall, would come back!

I don't frequent Middle Eastern or Mediterranean places so I can't really compare, but this place is clearly authentic and offers fresh and delicious food! After walking down Atlantic Ave one day Â I recognized the name (from reading on Yelp!) and stopped in to get a menu. The staff was so friendly and I was impressed to see the fresh pitas being made. I went back later that night and ordered the falafel platter with 1/2 baba ghanoush and 1/2 hummus. The pita was definitely the best part; for one it was HUGE (I barely finished a 1/4!), obviously fresh out of the oven and flavorful! The rest of the platter was also really good, and what a steal - $6 for 4 falafels, Â hummus, a salad (with incredible dressing) and the huge pita! Will definitely be back to try again as well as other dishes!

We ate here after the Live with Regis and Kelly show. We walked there, and it was maybe 7 or 8 blocks south. We got there at 10:45. They said they had a breakfast special, but because we had yet to eat anything that day we moved right into lunch. We had fun trying different empanadas. We each picked three. There were three of us, and it was plenty! We also ordered a chips and guacamole appetizer, and were pleasantly surprised to find that it was plantain chips. They were so good. I wish I could remember every one we tried but...I do remember the spicy chicken was so good. Very spicy and wonderful. Their margarita was good. We had the classic, but it had a just ever so slightly tropical twist. I would definitely recommend this place!
The last few times ramen has been average. Â For my taste, Â Toto ramen is the place go to satisfy my ramen craving!

The Theatre district is always pretty busy, and most restaurants are packed before/after show times. We walked right by Jr's and like the casual/diner vibe and strolled in. Hardly a wait, friendly hostess', and the food looked good! My hubby and I both ordered burgers; his beef, mine turkey, and both were delish! Cooked med-well, and still juicy and flavorful. The fries were great, our server was nice, and the atmosphere was very upbeat. We didn't order dessert, but we saw tons of people getting huge slices of cake, shakes, cheesecake... had we not ordered huge burgers, we would have had room. This is the place for a quick bite while hitting a broadway show, and it's casual and not very pricey.

I came here for bachelorette brunch with a large group of women and this is thee place for a damn good brunch & time! As soon as we arrived, after making reservations, we were seated and a very friendly server came to tackle drink orders. She was attentive and got every single one of the 15 drinks accurate and all were brought to the table in a timely fashion. The coffee was delicious and our server made sure the cup stayed full! I ordered the biscuits and gravy...OH MY GOD. I haven't had biscuits and gravy this good since the time I spent in NOLA. The atmosphere of the restaurant was very nice. The service and food were spectacular. You just cannot go wrong here. I can't wait to head back!

i kinda wanna copy and paste ken k's review of this onto mine because he shares my sentiments exactly. Â i remember my host for the wknd brought me here and swore that it would blow my mind in terms of french fries (he knew how big of a french fry fiend i am) so we got the double order of fries and the roasted garlic mayo, the sweet chili, and the war sauce. Â good, yes. superb? no, not really.

If I could eat here every day I would. The food is my favorite in Astoria and the service, whether it be in the restaurant or for delivery is awesome. Just writing this review makes me want Il Bambino NOW!

good food, bad service. we came here around 1 pm on a weekday and the place was nearly empty, but the service was SOOOO slow. we waited forever to get menus; we waited forever to get our drinks; we waited forever to get our food! speaking of food, i had the sheep's ricotta gnudi in brown butter & sage, which was quite delicious. a smallish portion, but plenty for lunch. i had a nice bottle of hard cider to go along with it, too. (i would have given them 3 stars but i have to deduct one because they have rabbit on the menu and places that serve my pets on a plate are just not cool.)

Spinach and artichoke pizza - SO GOOD! I mean, it's like you eat KFC fried chicken, or Mc Donald's Angus burger for the first time in your life. They are just so devilishly awesome! What makes this place more fun is, you grab a GIGANTIC slice and eat outside the shop while standing, hanging out with friends. Quite an experience reminding me of getting late-night bite at the food truck during good old freshman year days.
Very good pizza...super thin and crispy...nice amount of sauce...$17+tax for the 14 inch...$25 for the 18 inch

My favorite plates for the night: - Strawberry-Cinnamon Glazed Baby Back Pork Ribs: I don't like pork, but this dish made me change my mind. This dish reminded me of a Japanese approach to bruschetta. I'm in love. - Mom's Key Lime Pie, Graham Crust, Pineapple : YUM!!!! My least Fave: - Soupy Paella "De Taller:" Cockles, Shrimp, Saffron Broth, Bomba Rice: I don't know how I feel about Soupy Paella. It was kinda weird. Also, they have to do a better job cleaning the mussels. I almost chipped my tooth. For those who live in Manhattan: This place is definitely worth the trip out to Brooklyn. Trust me!

Ok.. so I may not be completely with the majority here but the experience at Barrio was not what I expected. Â I'm not sure what type of tequila was in the grapefruit magarita but it didn't do me any wonders. Â I'll spare you the details but I woke up itchy and apparently my body was rejecting whatever I ingested. Â Tip: If you're allergic to tequila, don't do it! Booo hoooooo Barrio. Â  Michelada was the best thing we ordered.... highly recommend. The two types of tacos we got were good... one was the calamari and the other a fish. Â The calamari added dimension and texture to the otherwise bland taco. Â So I didn't partake in the 3 cup condiments bestowed upon us... okay my fault. Â Tip: Â try the condiments or you'll be eating unseasoned food! Â  Please learn from my mistakes folks or you'll remember Barrio Chino the same way I can't forget it.
3 words, Black Label Burger... The best burger I ever ate.

everything I have tried is good. it does seem to take a bit too long when ordering a sandwich and there is one other person in there. great on those lazy days when i just don't want to cook but still want healthy food this is a great option. the owner is nice as is the staff.

I love this place! Best Pizza I've had in NYC and the service was amazing! The waiters know about all the wine on there list and will help you find something to your taste. It's a small wine bar and they get very busy but it's worth the wait! LOVE, love, love this place!

First visit to a new neighborhood place. Â This place has no personality, atmosphere is boring.....music good. Â I felt I was throwen back into the "wine bar" day. Â The waitress appeared to careless if we were there or not.....never broke a smile. Â When asked about one of the pizza's she said she had never seen it and then asked her assistant....he explained. Â Our soup arrived shortly after the order, but the pizza's took over 1/2 hour....I even had to ask what happened to our order. The pizza.....it wasn't worth waiting for!!! Â The crust is bought frozen, similar to pre shaped frozen ones from Whole Foods. Â I also ordered there veggie lasagna, much better than the pizza, but still so so. Â We won't be back to this place.....to many better eating places here in TriBeCa.
Food is fantastic. Waited over an hour for a bar side seat. The uni is extremely fresh. Saki is perfect. Wait staff we're pleasant. Portions are small and pricey.

I have now been here for drinks, brunch which was also drinks and dinner. I think this is one of the best places around in terms of food and ambiance. They have great cocktails, and great appetizers. I have not got a main course but they always have something delicious. The brunch cocktails are pretty cheap and on Mondays they have all you can eat mussels.

Oh. My. Goodness. Â I am in LOVE! Came here with my boyfriend for our one year anniversary, and I was just blown away. Â  At first I was a little skeptical, because it was on the 6th floor of Macy's, but boy it was such a good decision to come here. Â  To start, our waiter was SO nice! Â He was very proper, and was quick to make sure we had everything we needed. Â Then there was the food.... DELICIOUS! Â I had the Paccheri with braised beef ragu, and the boyfriend had the eggplant. Â my dish was the perfect proportion. Â It was satisfying, but not overly filling. I loved the staff, the food, the ambiance, and decor...not to mention the view of the empire state was spectacular. Â  Easily 5 stars.
mac and cheese with jalapeno cornbread was amaaaazing! The drink menu is extensive with bottled beer, cider, good wine choices, and mead which I rarely see. There was also live music on Friday night.

Wednesday night at 8:30pm and NO reservations. It was PACKED. - No Problem, you can wait for a few minutes and we will sit you shortly. We sat at the bar and half way into a glass of wine we were moved to the table and given our menus. What a wonderful tuna carpaccio... A bit too loud to enjoy good conversation without yelling but if you need to take a date and are aprehensive you wont have enough in comon, this place will do the trick! It will be impossible to engage in deep conversation. The teas are also amazing so make sure to try them.

As a Southern California native, I know good new-American cuisine. Â This has got to be some of the best. Â The rock shrimp hush puppies and buffalo chicken lollipops are addicting, and the tuna tar tar is very fresh. As for entrees, Â I really enjoyed my bacon cheeseburger, and my friend said the veggie burger was the best she'd had in her life. Â  Aside from food, the service is very attentive and drinks are imaginative and strong (bourbon swizzle is my fav, and I'm always impressed with the assorted bloody mary menu for brunch). Â  And something I can't say for many places in NYC is that the ambience is fantastic! Â Dim lighting, festive atmosphere, and big comfy booths to sit in. Â This spot is definitely becoming a regular for me =)
Wonderful experience! Â Food is delicious & artistically presented. Beautifully decorated Â with warmth & creativity. A fun & relaxing atmosphere.

Get the white borscht. Everything else is excellent, most notably the stuffed cabbage, the roast chicken, the breaded pork chop, and the goulash, which are all accompanied by mashed potatoes lightly sprinkled with lines of fresh dill. But do try the white borscht. You won't be sorry, unless you are a vegetarian, and then you'll be grossed out because the base of white borscht is sausage water.

Great pizza and cozy ambiance. Posto is small and romantic, with low ceilings and low lighting. The pizza is really great as is the spinach salad. Haven't tried the pasta, but the ravioli that went by looked delish. I also like any place that serves Hoegaarden.

Love it! Â the food is right and the atmosphere is real homey. Â  I recommend this place to anyone with the desire for food and fun. You gotta have the corn and Cuban sandwich! Â Writing this is making me want to go there right now.

Love this place! It's my go-to for Thai in Long Island City. Super authentic Thai cuisine and the service is great. The decor is trendy and very welcoming. All of the Curries taste amazing and portions are big enough for left overs the next day. A must-try!

Food and service were pretty good here. We have not tried burgers or steak, but pirogis and duck spatzle were good, although pirogis were not exactly what we expected. The portion sizes are not very big, so order appetizers. Overall I would not rate this place 4 stars if Â it didn't have a great selection of Czech beer and eastern european hard liquor. This is the first place I found in NYC that has Staropramen on tap. Add to that jazz on Tuesdays and you get a really good motivation to try Korzo at least once.
Small but the food was good quick and cheap. Very friendly service

I was torn between 3 and 4 stars but decided only 3 because at the end of the day I don't think value for money is that great.
