I should mention, I had a decent time here, and the food was good enough; but it really is quite pricey for what you get. The highlight in the end was not the food but the amazing decor and vibe of the place, they have done a really nice job.

Such delicious and cheap potstickers and dumplings! They have several different fillings to choose from, but at $1 for 4 you can buy several people's worth and try them all! The potstickers are golden fried to perfection, and the fillings are just the right texture and taste. You can order cold dumplings to take home and cook later, and the fried pancake isn't bad either. But definitely stop by for some potstickers if you can. The store itself is quite small and really not meant for eat-ins. There are some seats to the countertops, so if you are lucky you can snag one. Otherwise, you can fill a small thing of soy sauce and grab and go.

food is realy tasty and worth 5 stars. Â one of the best pancakes and tasty scrambled eggs. the only complain i have: the place Â is very busy and hectic. it is not a place to relax over Â a cup pf cafe and a sunday brunch. way to crowded. would be much more enjoyable if cut some 2-3 tables.

High quality Japanese meal and especially good value during lunch time. Â Please do make reservation so to ensure prompt seating. Â They are always packed around lunch time. Â For about $15 you will be full and satisfied.

I'd passed by this place a hundred times before finally deciding to pop in for brunch one day. I'm so glad I did, and can't believe I waited so long! Excellent standard brunch fare, and pretty good dinner menu as well.
Fantastic little spot to get a bite in St Marks st the burgers are soooo tasty, for a man 2 or 3 will do the trick, fries are great and the service was very nice and friendly. I liked it a lot.

Food was good, service was always around. Attractive crowd on a nice Saturday. So far, a good meal. The a/c wasn't exactly strong and in a packed place, the airflow was lacking. Kinda made a tough dining experience. It was close enough to being a sauna that I almost considered taking my shirt off. I'll give it another shot and hope that maybe the a/c was broke today. So I ended up going back during a weekday for lunch. Less packed, plenty of air and comfortable. Food was just as good as the first time. I had a tuna melt on rye. Maybe I should just avoid the weekend brunches.

I got the Mata Hari cocktail, which was awesome, and some kind of cheesecake/creme brulee dessert, which was also awesome. Drinks are $14 but they're unusually good. Great art deco interior - plus, in the back half, the whole ceiling is a giant skylight.

Styled after a quaint 1920s speakeasy and tucked discreetly behind a tarot card reader's storefront, Employees Only is old-world sophistication from the perfectly mixed cocktails to the perfectly coiffed bartenders. Â  The pictures don't do the ambiance justice. You're in the hands of some of the most talented and creative mixologists in the city, so this isn't the time for a gin and tonic. Â Order a specialty cocktail and let them impress you or your date. Â  I'd love to update my review with tales of Â bone marrow poppers and elk and lamb chops and steak tartare and my elation at never succumbing to vegetarianism.

Bistro style with an open kitchen -- very cute decor. Â The happy hour drink prices were great, especially for that neighborhood. Â Convenient location for us as we were going to the Gramercy Theater after. Â Went with my boyfriend with a groupon and there was so much food, we couldn't believe it and ended up giving 2 stix of lamb and the rest of our fries to our friends who were on line for the show. Â The bartender was super nice; our waiter had only worked there for 2 weeks, but he was sweet to us and attentive. Â The groupon is a ridiculously good deal and we will go back for sure if in the area. We had the lamb with mint. Â Excellent. Â The tzatziki Â is out of this world, Â The fries were fresh and perfect. Â The spinach and kale salad was just ok. Â You're supposed to "massage" the kale, otherwise it's hard as a rock, and it was. Â Boyfriend didn't like it. Â The baby spinach was delicious, though. Â The salad wasn't ice cold (i hate that), and the dressing was good. Â We wanted to try the mac & cheese balls, but none of us like mushrooms and they come with truffle oil..? Â Maybe could have had them skip that, but we opted for the light and cheesy and tasty zucchini balls. I have eaten in swank restaurants in NYC with wine parings, prix fixe $300 a person. Â Obviously, this place isn't comparable to that! Â But I'm giving it 5 stars because the food was just really good; fresh and innovative. Â That's how I base my reviews -- food!

We didn't know to much about Junior's when we visited the city in November. We were walking up and down Times Square looking for a place to eat after a long day of flying from LA when we noticed it. We walked in and the hostess seated us right away. The food was delicious and our server was fantastic!! The only thing I wish I had tried was the cheesecake, but after my amazing sandwich I was stuffed!
Great food and loved the kid's menu. They have a changing table in the bathroom. Having a reservation was key, since the spot seemed popular on a Saturday night. Good, fast service.
great fries, loved the sliders, and the sweet potato soup was excellent.

We had to wait in the line outside when we got here, but the nice French doorman was friendly and understanding about the chilly weather. He tried to get us in as soon as he could. If you don't care for the nice packaging, make sure you tell them you want the free box. It's still a pretty mint color :) I always love their seasonal flavors they have, but pistachio will forever be a favorite :)

Quite dissapointed, I have heard so many good things about this place and decided to give it at try at last. It turned out to be quite dissapointing. I had the set menu for dinner. The portions were way too small, it was almost a joke. For my 6-dish-entree, i literally had a plum as one entree. I dont think i will go back.

Ok, heard about it, tried it, and loved it - at least a few bites of it. It's ooey, gooey, drippy, thick, rich and massive, and honestly I wouldn't know if I could finish a whole slice. I am going to guess that Artichoke Pizza is best in moderation, depending on your tolerance for grease. Fine dining pizza it is not, but it certainly has a cult following. With a small room with a couple of communal tables, and a few benches outside, be prepared to line up, wait, and devour your pizza bent over your knees if you're lucky to get a seat. In any case, make sure to grab napkins! As for the taste, the white artichoke pizza was certainly the best and their signature flavor - you can't find this flavor in most pizza joints in town! I definitely enjoyed every bite I had, but still appreciate that I wouldn't be able to handle it on a regular basis! Would I come back? Definitely!
The first time I came here I couldn't believe how good the food is. For people who like fish and pasta I suggest the Lobster Pasta, and for dessert the chocolate pizza.
Love Love Love the Jerk Chicken and holy cow the garlic shrimp is great! Mac and cheese is tasty as is the cabbage and rice and peas.. I am all about the islands!

Brunch at Yerba Buena FTW! The food was great (though the buzz I had attained may have added an additional star) when my friends and I checked out YB for brunch on Sat. I ordered the Tres Arepas. Â  Though they are smaller than Caracas' arepas and yellow from yellow corn, I liked them better here. Â The three arepas contained short rib, pork, and chicken with egg, respectively. The next time I go, I'm going to try the fish tacos! Why was I buzzed? Â $12 AYCD (all you can drink) mimosas, bellinis, and jalapeno bloody marys (quite a powerful concoction) for the first hour of our brunch meal. Â Our group ended up squeezing in 4-5 drinks each.
First Time in Dover , young dynamic team, and the proud of wanted to do better every minute shows and paid off! From the meal to the service !

Simple, clean and elegant food. . .they really pay attention to the details. Â I have been there several times, often by myself but sometimes with a boatload of friends, and I have yet to been disappointed. Â The roast pork/broccoli rabe sandwich is the bomb! Â My friend loved her arugula, grilled peach salad. . . the proscuitto really was a nice salty contrast to the sweetness of the peaches. All in all, a great addition to the neighborhood and if they get some beer in house, I might have to change my address.

3.5 stars. The waitresses were super nice and very accommodating for our large group (9 of us). I got the spicy basic pork ramen with the thick noodles. It was good, but to be honest, with the thick/oily broth and the super fatty pork belly, the dish was a bit too rich for my taste.

Very small restaurant, and a traditional tapas place. We had the scallops, baked stuffed clams and lamp chops. Everything we ordered was good, nothing out of this world. The baked stuffed clams were the best. The place is quite expense, around 10 to 15 for each Tapas place, and you need at least two to feel full, however it is in Greenwich. The service here was excellent, very friendly hostess and nice waiters.

Initially I wondered how St. Anselm would fare being in such close proximity to the grilled-meat mecca that is Fette-Sau. But here's something all vegetarians should know about St. Anselm: you can actually eat here! BBQ spots are usually wasted on us, but St. Anselm does due justice to the grill by creating various dishes of grilled vegetables, including daily specials. I came with a friend on a quiet sunday evening and we each had a glass of beer (note: all beers at St. Anselm come in 8oz. sizes, so not really a place to go if you're really looking to hit the booze). My friend and I shared the Spinach Gratin (which wasn't overly creamy or disgustingly dressed with a thick white sauce...very good), grilled cauliflower, grilled mixed eggplants with a slice of fried goat cheese, and some mac and cheese. Everything was very, very good. The vegetables weren't overcooked and all had very unique flavors despite being simply prepared. Bonus: If you do feel like you need to indulge in more drinking, the backyard of Spuytin Duyvil is right there.
Overpriced and overrated. There are much better options in the area. The food is decent at best.

Amazing food ! Pretty pricey, but their food is amazing. I ordered the longislog, which was very good. My fiancee` ordered the Chicken and Ube waffles which were also amazing! Love it here, the only thing is they have a very little desert menu. This def. is a more modern Filipino restaurant, can't wait to try their sister restaurant Jeepney!

This pizza is sinfully delicious. Â For awhile I only got the margherita because I don't like artichokes. Â The margherita is very very good! Â A friend forced me to try a bit of his artichoke one day, and from that day on, it all changed. Â It is warm, creamy, cheesy, tangy, crisp... it is SO worth burning the roof of your mouth. Seriously. Â It is a difficult task to finish a whole slice, and the guilt definitely sets in. Lines are long, the place itself is not by any means glamorous, and you eat sitting on a crappy little bench or on the stoop a few doors over. Â But that's part of the experience, and it's all worth it!
delux
Lots of good beers on tap, good food. Â Prices are a bit too high tho or i'd give 5 stars

I don't think I've ever seen a two-seater table that's the size of my nightstand. This place crammed as much seating space as it possibly could and everybody was pretty much trying to make way for someone else all the time. I don't what the deal with the corn is. I expected the corn to have way more mayo and cheese and sweetness and *kick*. It's is certainly not the best food I had on a stick. The food was kind of more diner-esque than I was expecting, so I was sort of let down. The chorizo side looked and tasted like canned meat sauce. My spicy eggs and beans brunch dish was okay, but yes, it didn't resemble anything worth waiting in line for.

Super-thin noodles and tasty broth were excellent. The wontons were in my opinion good but not exceptional. The wonton clearly contains a section of pork and a small chunk of shrimp, and the two were not really mixed into each other. I personally like wonton contents to be more shrimp-y with the pork playing a supporting (but necessary) role. These wontons while flavorful were more balanced between pork and shrimp. Â The noodles were nice and firm (not mushy) and wispy thin. The noodles were all tangled together into a big clump in the soup making it hard to take reasonable bites. Next time, I'll try the noodles in their other tempting dishes (pan-fried noodles or cantonese style lo-mein).
Solid Arepas. Nice quiet ambiance. Beautiful Waitresses. Would I come here over Caracas?...The answer is probably no.
The food was good, salmon tartar was very tasty, This place is not to be confused with the Jane Hotel, which my friend did. The service was pretty swift .

Everything was delicious. My boyfriend and I had the 50/50 burger & burnt ends a la carte. The brioche bun is perfect for the 50/50. Our server was super sweet and attentive. Â We'll definitely be going back!
Fried chicken does not apparently belong on thin pieces of sourdough. Â Not. A. Fan.
believe they hype, order the sicilian. leave the gun, take the cannolis.

I won't wax on about the food, as that's been done before. It's good. I will say that the brussel sprouts are a must-try, as they were delicious and I have always thought of brussel sprouts as one step above dog food. Cash or Amex only = annoying. What's with the attitude? From the person who answered the phone to take my reservation, who seemed to think I was lucky he was talking to me; to the hostess who - again - seemed to think I was lucky to be there; to the servers who toss things on the table and leave...really? Great food and ambiance, but the attitude got pretty old.

This is a phenomenal spot in the West Village. Â It's a quaint, toasty restaurant with a hidden gem of a year-round garden out back. Â The tables in the garden area are rustic with a glass (or glass-like) table top that gives the feel of a cafe. Â  My husband and I have come here a handful of times over the last few years for boozy coffee and dessert. Â The coffees are phenomenal. Â My latest coffee discovery is The Irish Nut...which is by far, the best nut of all! Â I drank that with a slice of Pumpkin Cognac Cheesecake...and I forgot all about the fact that it was butt freezing outside. Â I've never ordered a real meal here, but others tables around me have, and it always smells incredible...especially the pizza. Â One of these days, I will eat lunch or dinner here!

Good food with large portions every time. Lunch is around $9, which is solid for the area. Barely a counter and overall cramped space, but quick service (never waited more than 5-10 minutes for lunch) and really nice people.
Went back to give it another shot. Â Still not impressed. Â Good sangria but that's about it. Â Won't be back

I've waited in shorter lines for Roller Coasters. I've had an easier time fighting for a seat on the rush hour F train. If I want to go through all that time and effort for BBQ, I'll just raise my own cows.

I was here for a pretty laid back engagement party earlier this summer, and was very impressed with the space. It's very spacious, with long picnic tables + benches and large open windows. The space, along with a good number of beers and wines, makes for a great place for summer drinking. One downside is that it can get pretty hot in the summer, since the windows are all open to the outside. They also serve some foods (I remember only the jumbo pretzel) that go down well with all that beer. I can't remember prices as I had an open bar, but I believe it was fairly average.
Good food, nice atmosphere quick service. Mosquitoes out back and need to re-upholster their benches.
the service sucks. the food is mediocre. the decor is drab, the open kitchen is dingy. you're in new york, you can do much better.
One of my favorite breakfast spots in the city! Not only is the food delicious, but Johny and the rest of the crew are absolute characters.

FYI, this place will not seat you until all members are present, even if you have a reservation. So even though it's one of my go to places for big groups, make sure you tell everyone to get there ON TIME, otherwise everyone will be stuck waiting for the last straggler of your group... Rigatoni a la vodka with mushrooms is amazing. I also always get the chicken marsala, which comes with plentyyyy of sauce. Baked ziti is also good. For apps, the calamari is done well. The mozzarella en carrozza is great, but it's basically fried cheese so it's very hard to make that fail. The tiramisu is generally good, but has a little too much of an alcohol-y taste for me, even though I know it's supposed to be like that. Also got the tortelloni with alfredo here once.... a little bland and forgettable. Other than that, I've always had great dining experiences here! Been here 8+ times!

My cousin booked a reservation for his finacee's birthday. We went there last Friday. The whole experience was sublime. Highly recommended for anyone who wants to take a peek at NYC's high-end dinning places.
Everything people say is true. If you want a different, delicious, interesting meal this is it.

Simple dinner menu but they know what they do well. Â Beef wellington pretty much melts in your mouth and the salmon dish was also well thought out and executed. Â And the scotch cocktails... wow. Â I had the spicy orange one and it was deeeee-lish. Â And pretty strong so the $13 or so price tag was well earned. Â  Great spot for an enjoyable, tasty, uncomplicated meal out.

One word..."CORN"...corn with cheese and paprika (i think) sprinkled all over it....what a tasty corn... I came here on a rare but very warm day in October...of course prime lunch time! The place was packed but seated quickly. Smushed next to what looked a business meeting and two casual hippies. It was definitley hot and could not steer away from the fact that I was slowly burning up and wasn't sure if a cuban dish would have made it better for me to cool down...but the corn was worth it. I got the quesadilla which was OK but my friend got the pork dish with rice and beans....let's just say I ended up picking at her food...the bean and rice was satisfying

Excellent restaurant with Israeli/Mediterranean flavors. Possibly better than my favorite Taboon or Barbournia. No reservation and it was full when we got there at 6pm on a Saturday. Â I don't think you could go wrong with any dishes. Â It's a tiny place and it was extremely noisy thanks to a group of screaming women.

OMG! This place is the dumpling TRUTH! Â Delish. Â I had the pork and chive dumplings and the sesame pancake. Â This is a great place for fast cheap eats. Yum! Â The one thing is that I wish we could have found a park or something so that we could eat. But it's a great deal

i went there at 5:30, didn't know they weren't open until 6. made a reservation for 2. asked the hostess if there was a bar nearby and she suggested a coffee shop 2 blocks down. went to the coffee shop, and got back to lucali at 6:05. they gave my table away. 5 minutes. maybe even less since there was a family Â in front of me putting their name down. now, if i came by, made a reservation in person, and asked if there was a place nearby to go for 30 minutes, wouldn't it appear that that means i would be back? i'll stick to grimaldi's or di fara, or actually any other place than this.

Here we go, off to Neverland! Think of a wonderful thought, any merry little thought! So I got here with my very close feline friend around at exactly 2 pm on Saturday for brunch. I called them to make a reservation a few days earlier, but Homey don't play that! I get there and the mist of the fresh baked breads and pastries forced themselves down my untrimmed sniffer. There was a line extending outside the door for brunch and I noticed a lot of groups were waiting. I asked a fellow gentleman with a bopping baby, ( I really wanted to rub the baby's head, sooooo softttt!) if he was waiting to be seated or get a table, he said for me to go ahead to the hostess. I slither by the crowded aisle, walking sideways and shuffling like I do everyday, passed a very large and in charge woman on the bar who I had to crouch to get around her contours. Get to the hostess, YOWZA! So beautiful and curvacious! Â I see her, she sees me, and I ask for a table for two. I was anxious to hear her say " There's a long wait for a table." But instead, she says " would you be willing to sit outside?" I looked at my friend, who nodded with certainty and was famished to the point where she was almost mute, and we got seated within 5 minutes. I was very pleased and amazed. Out of the at least 50 or so restaurants I've been to in NYC, this hostess was EXTREMELY nice and let skip the groups. We walk passed the seated brunchers and to the back patio. Very windy and cool, I might say. Off to the food. She ordered the Cocotte and I, the Hangover Sandwich. I wanted something hefty to Â get me through the day. I asked for a medium rare, but got it slightly more cooked than I asked, NO BIGGIE! It was juicy and with the green and funky salad combined with Belgian fries, I had a good chow-down . She was very pleased with her Cocotte, the Pancetta was just right and the Gruyere cheese really turned her on. I mean, well, with a bit of Itis on the side. I had no complaints except that there should be probably be two waiters outside because when you're outside, you have to go in and get their attention. As we finished our meal, I handed the hostess my card (scratched out with my number and full of gratitude). She looked at it with amazement and incredulity. I realized I should have stayed and talked to you (hostess), holla back! Or else, I'll be eating there again. :)

Empanada mama was fantastic. It is in a fantastic location too, especially if you're out drinking in the Hells kitchen neighborhood. We tried about eight empanadas, Also had the fried planting chips, shake, lemonade-essentially we ate like pigs but it was too good and I'm not in this area too often. I noticed they have a 1 - 4 AM happy hour and also a standard evening happy hour. It was crazy busy on a weekend night and it was a little hectic, cramped, but the service was still very prompt and accurate. The waiter and busboy were very attentive and accommodating. I noticed all the staff working very hard and fast. I also appreciated the busboy ensuring the wall seating/tables were kept clean even though it was so busy. They were on top of the service game. I will definitely return here. Prices are right on point too. A great little spot, check it out. My favorite empanada was the "Cuban".

The people giving this place 5 stars must be getting takeout. I barely had the stomach to even eat the food because I was so disgusted by what I saw. There was 1 guy preparing food behind the counter, and he wore NO GLOVES. While he prepared our food I watched as he wiped his nose with his hand, put raw bacon and sausage on the grill, then cut up a banana and arranged the slices in some pancakes, prepare toast and breakfast sandwiches, all with his visibly filthy bare hands, wiping them only on his dirty apron. Disgusting, I couldn't get out of there fast enough.

What a cute little hidden gem around Union Square! Â I met my friend here for lunch on a weekday and the place was of course packed! Â I opted for the croque monsieur and my friend ordered a salmon sandwich and of course we both opted for a side of yummy fries. Â We didn't try the mussels, but have heard very good things about them! Delicious flavors, large portions (I had leftovers), cozy little ambience, friendly customer service, and a prime lunch spot. Â 2 girlfriends playing catch-up over an extended lunch in a cute little cafe.....it was the perfect setting! You can't go wrong at Petite Abeille!

The food here was really excellent! The atmosphere of the place was really great too, overall I loved it. My only complaint is that it seemed like it took a little too long for the food to come out, but once we got it it was definitely worth it, so i'll probably be returning here!

Barboncino is a really fantastic and much needed pizza spot on Franklin. I've been waiting for it for a year and a half now and it has not disappointed. The decor is beautiful and the food is delicious. Great for a date night or a group spot. Can't recommend it highly enough.
Fantastic place for brunch. The grits are fantastic.

I have been waiting to try Ippudo since my last trip to NYC two years ago, and it definitely didn't disappoint. More importantly, my partner has never understood my insane cravings for ramen, but after our experience here, he totally gets it now. We got the Akamaru Modern, Karaka-men and pork Hirata buns! So delish. Overall, excellent service and food. A bit expensive, but I think it's worth the splurge. This is definitely a must eat for anyone who's visiting NYC for the first time.

Love this littel spot a couple blocks from the Christopher street Path. Beautiful, yet crowded open air dining room in the summer, and one of the smallest bathrooms in the city. Very cheap entres for the quality under $20. REAL Italian waiters. Great place off the beaten path. It does fill up very quickly for dinner on a sunny day.

I consider this place a Filipino staple in New York. They offer a lot of comfort food. We came in as a party of 11 people so the server may have a little overwhelmed with our orders. We pretty much asked for almost everything on the dinner menu. He was entertaining though and explained each and every item, ingredient, and how to eat the dishes. Our order ran from appetizers: 3 Baluts, Arroz Caldo, Lechon Kawali, Spam Fries, Sizzling Sisig and Chicken Skins. For entrees: Kare Kare, Pork Adobo, stuffed Pusit, Ginataang Langka Prawns, Beef Kaldereta and Garlic Rice on the side. We paired it with drinks such as Pacquiao Punch, Teo Tita, Lea Salonga, Sharon Cuneta and of course San Miguel Beer. All the condiments were also enticing as well: Jufran Banana Ketchup, sugar Cane & Coconut Vinegar, Magi Soy Sauce and Calamansi. Lastly, we had to order some desserts: Leche Flan and Maja Blanca (rice pudding with corn & Skyflakes). We thoroughly enjoyed our first time dining experience here. It would have been 5 stars had it not the server forgot the order of coffee in the end and the Ginataang Langka Prawns were on the saltier side.

Always a popular spot in Woodside, which means good fresh food all the time! If you stop by here on a fri/sat nite, expect to wait 30mins. I have been frequenting this place for a couple of years. Back when they only owned one spot, a backyard, and basement level tables. Now they have taken up three spots and designed the place to have a more asian/zen vibe. Originally recommended to me by a thai friend, so you know the food is good when locals recommend it. The backyard garden is a nice touch, and the waiters are friendly. The price is great, have had dinner for 3, drinks, appetizers + entree for less than $50. What it comes down to though is the food that keeps the crowds coming: Appetizers: Softshell crabs with papaya salad is always a hit. The beef satay is good as well. Entree: Barbecue chicken with coconut rice and papaya salad - always yummy. Pad thai is pretty good. The curries here will definitely provide a punch in your mouth feel, my parents always go for this one. Beware, if you ask for spicy, they don't holdback which makes this place a gem. Ginger chicken with ginger rice, delicious, my mom makes this and it's just like her homemade dish. Honestly, I don't think I've had a bad meal here. Conclusion: The food is worth the wait, however if you'd like to avoid the crowds, go there early around 4pm.
Ordered grandmas pizza and basil and tomato pizza. Both were average; grandmas pizza was particularly disappointing.

The decor is modern as the Rchard Meirs builing that houses it, as is the cuisine. Had their fried chicken and it was sublime. My sashimi appetizer was excellent; fresh and tagny. The servie was as attentive to detail as the decor and the food. Most memorable of all was the rhubarb and lychee trifle which was unbelievably good - sadly a Special for only another week or so as apparently the chef insists on the freshest market ingredients. The service was also very good in this lovely modern restaurant with views of the Hudson. Not cheap but absolutely good value for the quality.

Dined here on a Tuesday night after receiving recommendations from multiple friends. Got there a little before 10 and waited less than half an hour for a table. The interior decor was very nice and had a very "trendy" feel to it. I ordered the special ramen (I forget exactly what it was, but it was spicy). To my surprise and delight, our entire table's food arrived in less than five minutes after ordering. Not the BEST ramen I've ever had in my life, but the noodles are good and the broth was excellent! It's a little over-priced as far as ramen goes ($13+ for a relatively smallish bowl), but I would definitely recommend this place to anyone in the neighborhood with a craving for some good ramen.

The Devil May Care, because their Churros are sinfully D-licious!!! Dark, bitter-sweet chocolate tub to dip your crispy fried sugar-coated churros into--perfect snack--Tempura Fish Tacos seriously inventive--Fresh, tender, whitefish in a egg batter has asian influences. Â Decor is newly renovated fun, playful + colorful. This local downtown eatery has late night hours, so healthy, tasty snacking for after work or play, their guacamole & chips are healthy + fresh...good snacking + good for you! Check them out!

The decor is great, the restaurant is very crowded, lots of tourists, food is good, not remarkable. Could use a few lower priced bottles if wine. Waited 1 hour after my reservation. If you live in NYC there are other very good options. Service was excellent though.
Eat Italy in New York City

Stumbled upon this place while walking around on a Saturday night. They had a late night happy hour special of $5.00 beers. It's pretty spacious and has two rooms with more tables in the back. The music was all classic hip hop with a lot of Jay-Z hits on rotation. The beers were different and not the typical sort that you find in most bars. They have the dessert menu on the back of the drink list- not sure if they serve sweets at night, but it's worth asking. The service was good and the people seemed very laid-back. Loved the vibe. The bathroom was pretty dirty, but what do you expect at a NYC bar. I would definitely go back and try an actual drink next time.

Went there for lunch with a friend and we were chatting it up until our portabella and kobe buns came to our table, and then silence! For the both of us: food too good to talk while you're eating. Am craving it right now as I write this. The bun itself is how you would imagine a cloud to taste. The texture was so pillowy soft, and the taste sweetly hit the spot. We both had the wasabi ramen as our entree. Thank heaven for perfectly cooked tasty noodles. And what great service! Can't wait to go back.

Bf and I were in the area and looking for a place to have dinner. Going down the list, we declared what we *didn't* want to eat to narrow things down. No Asian. No Italian. How about Ethiopian? Meh, not in the mood. How about Mexican? Eh sure, I guess I could do Mexican. And so I thought of Barrio Chino, which I been to several times before but never really thought much of it. One of my friends from LA was quite particular about her Mexican food (as most Californians seem to be) and always only wanted to eat here. It was also always packed. I never got it. So here on an early Sunday night at around 6:30pm, this place was already bustling and packed with people. We got there just early enough that there was a free but just vacated two-top for us, and as soon as we had sat down and our table was bussed, the place was at 100% capacity, and there was a small line waiting at the door and outside. For vegetarians, there aren't too many options, but enough that there are some choices. We started with the guac and chips, which came with a dish of salsa as well. The guac was good but the raw onions were quite kicky. Salsa had a nice slow burn. Bf had the enchiladas verdes, and I had the order of three cactus tacos. I didn't care for the tacos but the enchilada was pretty good, though also chock full of raw onions. The food here seems to be more authentic Mexican than the heavy cheese-laden Tex-Mex that we're used to around here. But still, nothing was that amazing. The place must always be bustling for a reason, so maybe their meat options are really good. Eh, I'd be ok if I don't come back again.

Saw it several time from yelp and finally tried it today, and it was great. They use noodle imported from Japan, and for the extreme spicy ramen, you can adjust the level by yourself though it is still not spicy even I poured down all bowl of seasoning. The smoked pork is a little fat but perfect with the ramen soup. Definitely will go back!

I curse this restaurant, I really do. Â Ever since I had the bone marrow here two years ago, I've been futilely searching for something like it in L.A. Â I found it amusing later when I was flipping through my not-for-tourist guide book and it mentioned the Blue Ribbon and its marrow. We also ordered oysters (yummy but I forgot which kind we got). I also ordered the chicken barley soup and the skirt steak. The barley was very crunchy and the chicken seemed freshly grilled and plopped in. I am not used to soups like this. I guess I prefer the old fashioned soups where the flavors have been cooked together and have melded. It was still good, but different. I could barely eat my steak which thankfully was just three slices with lots of onion and mushrooms swimming in a gorgeous flavor. A friend had the duck which was good but we liked the mashed turnip that went with it more. Oh, and my vodka tonic was excellent. Â  Every time someone tells me they're going to NYC, I tell them they have to come here (as well as Babbo) because this was one of the highlights of my trip.

Took a chance on this place and was curious about. Â I went with the three items and everything I chose was great. Â Of course the sauce the sauce the sauce in the items were amazing. Â I got the green chicken curry. Â It was very good and flavorful. Â Then got two other selections. Â  The sauce was so good that I ended up eating everything. Â All that rice. Â I will pay for it on the scale tomorrow but for now I am very content. Â Food is good and I highly recommend. Â  I didn't think it was too spicy but someone not used to heat might think it is . Â Be ware but the counter person will tell you anyway.

THERE IS A HEAVEN, and it is at SOCO with its fried chicken and sizzling mac-n-cheese. Best of all, your arteries won't feel clogged afterward! This place is happening .. DJ lightly spinning on Friday nights, food is ridiculously good, drink menu is creative and fresh .. I'm drooling as I'm writing this review. Service and ambience was on-point. Staff was kind and considerate, and always checked up on us at the right time and made sure the food was good, even on a busy Friday night. TRUST THEIR RECOMMENDATIONS! Unlike every other New Yorker, they're not trying to hustle you. Definitely worth the wait and the return trip!

Finally tried Highlands for Valentines day. It was a set menu so I am commenting on just the set menu that day. We started with a lack luster Barley Soup, a bit on the luke warm side. Main was a nicely prepared Short Rib. We tried two desserts, one Short Bread with Strawberry and the other a Chocolate Molten Cake. They were both average. The service was excellent. The waiter was very knowledgeable and the host was most attentive, however the food was not good enough to bring me back for dinner. A good meeting spot for a drink at the cozy bar area.

The place was crazy crowded. Â We stopped in for an order of empanadas to go which took quite awhile to come out. Â We tried the Brasil and it made a good late night snack. Â A tad on the salty side but a decent portion.

NYC has great food and amazing tapas places. Tia Pol does not even rank in my top 5. The food was average and the the service was spotty. Â  Â  * Patatas Bravas had too much mayo. * Pimientos estilo gernika had no flavor (hard to believe .. right? ) * Lamb Skewers were ok * Gambas al ajillo were swimming in oil. I feel a tapas dish should play with your palate. Tia Pol's dishes are boring and lack distinction... very disappointed

This place is fantastic. I went there last night with my girlfriend for dinner. Had to wait an hour, which was unfortunate, but well worth it. I had the totto spicy ramen with char-siu chicken, and she had the same, but extra spicy. I personally like really spicy food, so I will probably go with the extra spicy broth next time, and maybe try the pork. This was easily the best ramen I've ever had. The noodles were perfectly tender, and the broth was seasoned so well. We also had a pork bun as an appetizer (I completely forgot the name of the dish) and it was sublime. In total, we got 2 ramen bowls, 1 appetizer, 2 sakes and 2 sapporos for a grand total of $51 dollars, a steal in my opinion. If you don't like to wait then I recommend getting there early, because I'm sure the line starts to grow quickly, but once you try the food, you'll see why people wait so long (such as myself). 5 stars. Note: Cash only, no reservations and largest groups they can seat together are 4, so if your party is greater than 4, you will be split up.
Had the shrimp, rice, plantains, beans, chicken and the beef + chicken sandwiches. AMAZING! Will definitely be back. Was fresh and flavorful.

What a great gem in Astoria! Truly, a breath of fresh air and just what I needed after a long day of errands and other typical Friday work things. A friend and I went in for happy hour around 5:30, it wasn't too busy at that time. We sat ourselves, were greeted by TWO (count em TWO) servers within minutes of being seated. Funny, charming, and friendly servers too! The decor is simple, brick walls, wooden chairs, it's a rustic type of comfort place...Though they need a fireplace to complete that ambiance. Drink specials were great so we decided to order the fried pickles and the mac and cheese. The people at the table next to us ordered the Bua sandwiches which looked great, and they seemed to really like... but this girl is a veg so none for me. The mac and cheese is SUPER comforting, super good, and definitely large enough for two people to split. Oh man...I'll have dreams of that stuff. As for the fried pickles, my friend is obsessed with fried pickles like no other person I know, like I don't know if you read my reviews but most of the time I am with her, we are getting fried pickles. She said the batter was one of the best, and I have to agree...However the sauce was just not cutting it. I could definitely eat those pickles alone... But if you are going to put a sauce to dip fried pickles in, it better be damned good. Altogether, for three mixed drinks and two platters our bill was under 15 each. Not too bad for a Friday night dinner. Oh and just FYI this place does get busy around 6:30ish so be prepared to sit at the bar or wait for a table.

This is working into my weekly lunch rotation. I'm still not convinced on the burger entirely, but its satisfying and my coworkers love it. My go to are 2 single shack burgers add pickles and onion, and a large soda or their root beer. No fries cause then it'll be too filling. One day I was super hungry and couldn't concentrate and ended up saying 2 single cheeseburgers. What I got was bread cheese and meat. So word of advice, if you're that hungry, write down what you want so you dont screw it up. Also they're running shacktoberfest this week, can't wait to get some beer and wursts!

Was worried about tiny portions for a huge price but Boqueria more than exceeded my expectations - it was excellent! Â Went with two visiting friends, one a vegetarian and all our food was delicious! Â The pan tomate is great; manchego was just 2 pieces for $5, but then again, only $5. Â We all enjoyed the patatas bravas and the mushrooms. Â I had the mackerel and the salsa and oil drizzle made me want to lick the plate. Â Whenever creme brulee is an option that does it for me, but I wasn't a fan of their version; we also found the churros a lil dry. Â However, I would go back just for the Spanish toast dessert - soooo good, another plate licking temptation. Â The pitcher of sangria seemed a lil overpriced at $34, however it was good and not too sweet. Â  All in all, I'll would definitely recommend Boqueria and look forward to trying the Flatiron location too.

This is one of the underrated gems. Coal oven pizza.. Honestly, this place deserves so much more ratings and recognition as much as Grimaldi & Lombardis ughhh! Food came out extremely quicker than I expected, which was such a surprise. Thought they rushed my food but IT WAS SO GOOD. I got the #5 arugula pizza except I added truffle pÃ¢tÃ©&basil which made it even more of an amazing perfect touch & combination to it; proscuitto, fresh tomato sauce; mozzarella; and all! Perfect balance of salty prosciutto, sweet fresh tomato, light truffle, with a mixture of yummy bitter arugula and cheesy mozzarella ughhh yumz. PLUS THE PAPPARDELLE SPECK e PORCINI!!! from the pasta itself; homemade(taste/texture/freshness) just how I like it.. With the right creaminess, mushroom flavor to it, and a good touch of some truffle oil-- simply delicious I tell ya!! A MUST GET PASTA HERE !!! Sure in weekends it'll get really busy and crowded... It's a nice pretty small Italian restaurant for the city, which will get unbearably hard to manage but regardless the food is great! They've won the pizza contest a few times and been voted best pasta before.

Don't mistake undercooked game-y chicken for "moist". This was a lousy, poorly cooked bird. Yeah I said it. Their fried chicken is BAD. Salad garnish was good, but bad chicken can be life threatening. Cornbread was good, but where are the biscuits the NY Times said belonged in a museum? Who in their right mind takes that off the menu after getting a compliment like Burger = stale homemade chips fried earlier in the day, and a stale bun they didn't toast. Peanut brittle is alright, but honestly should be a freebie. It's not $5 good. Plus c'mon people. The bacon fetish has to stop. Anyway, I wouldn't crave this or buy a jar like they're hoping. It's not a must have, sorry. Oh, but the real warning sign....stale ice cold boring rolls brought the table, Â plus some really creepy service reaching into out table from weird "gotcha!" angles, Sad. The owner chef was there, and I had huge hopes for this place based on the reviews, menu, and back story.
Decent place to go in the area, lively, but I would say it's a tad overpriced - especially the food.

Well I went here today with a few colleagues for a beer. Â It turns out they have quite a selection of beers on tap. Â Most people are here for dinner obviously. Â The place is a great place to eat, a real bourgie dining room feel, which is nice now and then. Â  Anyway, I had a Stone 13th Anniversery Ale which was very tasty. Â I'm sort of just getting into beers really, and when I find the right ales, I'm really impressed. Â This one was great.

The first time I tried Super Taste, I was worried that it wouldn't live up to the hype. My worries were unfounded - the spicy beef noodle soup was one of the best things I've eaten, ever. Now, every time I go, I worry again that their food will have gone downhill - how can a dish be so consistently perfect? But it is. The noodles are sproingy (yes, that's a word, in my book), the broth is deeply flavored, the beef and greens are tender. This is no-nonsense satisfaction, and it comes cheap.
Good food, nice garden, however they need to install some ventilation for the kitchen.

After a couple text Â invite messages from my cousin upon discovering this place while driving in the neighborhood, I finally gave in, what the heck! So, with the whole gang fully attired for this small, very simple, and an empty stomach, we tried it out. We ordered a couple appetizers like : Summer Rolls, Crab CHIPS and the traditional Banxho. I'll just say that the Crab Chips is my fave, we ended up ordering a few more =), then for the main course, I ordered the Lemongrass shortribs, while the rest of us ordered the Cari-ga or Chicken Curry. I am happy with what I ordered. Its basically like BBQ pork, and the portions are not small neither too much. Also, the chicken curry was nice, but doesnt come with Rice which I think would have been better because the curry sauce is too strong and needs something to balance it. Service, cant really complain. The food came one by one, just as we wanted it. The servers are fast and friendly enough. Its a small place, and dont expect much. It could be pack. Food is good though, I just didnt see any Vietnamese person around, I don't know if thats a good sign. Prices are a bit pricey, for the ambiance and food, yeah, pricey. I agree with the other yelpers. Will I come back? Absolutely!!!!!!!!!

The food is always fresh and that's not surprising. The owner of the restaurant can frequently be spotted buying fruit and vegetables at the local farmers' market. The food is delicious and their Tiramisu is heavenly! The atmosphere is hard to describe. The place is large and buzzing with energy. Unfortunately, they don't take reservations. I especially recommend coming in the summer and trying to get a seat near the open windows.

Love this place! I used to come in all the time when I worked nearby as it was only a few blocks away. I usually get a Pork Katsu curry or Chicken Katsu curry with boiled eggs and sausage (there's a special for it but I forget what it's called). Their katsu is super crispy and tender and is drenched in curry sauce (don't worry it always looks like there's too much sauce but there isn't). Bottom line: this place is fast, cheap and yummy. If you're coming with another person, I would definitely recommend the grand slam (comes with chicken and pork katsu, 2 sausage links, and hard boiled egg) to split for under $15.

Went here last night after an awesome knicks game. I've been here before but for the veggie burger and some cocktails. I loved the tomato basil soup and the biscuits are appeasing to the eye but very dry like a pancake without enough milk. Â I loved the peach palmer, it was delicious and the mason jars were ultra retro and comfy. Overall, I loved the decor, its like a mix of futristic and retro mashed. Need to come for brunch! :)

A place that offers, seafood, gloves and bibe....YES PLEASE! We went there on a Friday night around 5:30. We were pleasantly surprised that there was no wait. Although there was a crowd of people that came in right after us. Â We were seated near the bar, so it was a small table with stools. It really was not comfortable but hey, Â the things I go through for good food! Â The service was great, Â very fast with constant check ins. Now for the delicious food! crab cakes($10)- the best I've had in a long time. Too bad there was only one crab cake. fish basket with fries ($12)- decent but I've had better. combo: 1lb of shrimp and 1 lb craw fish. The was the best deal for $25. We had it at medium spice with the boil's special sauce. Medium spice was perfect because we got to enjoy the food without reaching for the beer every minute with our slipper gloves. There were probably 10 of shrimp and 8 crawfish in the combo. The shrimps were huge and fresh, and I love sucking on the head to get the sauce. The sauce was to die for: it was buttery, garlicky and spicy. I wanted to shove my face in the bag and lick every drop. Needless to say, I will be back!!

Did not have a good time here. Â The host was rude and MEAN. Â Yes, we had some late stragglers in our group... but they told us we were to be seated at a smaller table or we would lose our reservation all together. Â So we sat sans a few people. Â When we asked if we could move to a bigger people to accommodate the stragglers, the host said no because they were booked... and having a few more cramped into our smaller table would violate their fire code. (she basically told our straggler friends to get the f out). Drinks were plentiful... but I'm not a drinker so it probably wasn't the best idea for me to go. Â Especially since the food was not great. Â I got a concoction that looked like a giant yellow cabbage patch head aka the burrito sucio. Â  It was bland and didn't look like a burrito. Â It was definitely not what I was expecting. I expected a good meal based on all the great reviews and the high demand for a reservation. Â It just seemed like an over-hyped place that I do not plan on going back to. Â  P.S.... it doesn't help that the girl at the next table spilled her glass of sangria on me. Â What a way to end a horrible experience and meal.

Had the two8two burger and enjoyed it. Â It was juicy and the bun, though wimpy, was good. Â  Everything else needs work. The burger didn't come with lettuce and tomato or pickles. Â Apparently you need to ask. Â And the fries are extra. Â The 4 dollar "Greek Fries" are ill conceived. Â The Feta simply falls off, so you're left with fries and side of crumbled cheese. Â  My waiter was "not a beer person" so he wasn't able to point us in the direction of a tasty beer. Â If you're a waiter at a burger and beer joint and you don't like beer, at least pick the brain of someone who does and get informed. Â  The decor of the bar is great and the staff is pleasant. Â And they have the most important thing, the burger, down. Â There is room for the place to improve. Â But unless they actually do improve, I wouldn't recommend.

best deal for oysters and beer in NYC!!! the lobsters are small but you definitely get a good bang for your buck with up to par sides (french fries, onion rings, corn, etc.) great for group atmosphere and definitely worth the wait the oysters are super fresh and savory ... absolutely delicious!! service is friendly and attentive

This is our new favorite dinner date spot. Â Everything we've tried has been crazy good. Â  I recommend the beet salad, followed by the veal. Â Staff is very friendly. Â I just wish they had a few more tables!

Firstly this place is small and doesn't take reservations so your wait will probably be outside...but you can drink there and that is one of the only issues I had with this amazing find in the West Village. The feel of this place was rustic and felt alittle bit like being transported to a sea shack on a rugged coast back in the UK. It's full of charm and very busy...which is what you want from a fish restaurant. The Red-White-Blue Oysters deal was phenominal...6 oysters and a glass of wine for $8! We then followed it up with some clam chowder and lobster mash...both amazing! Special mention should go to front of house who looked after us even though one of our party was late and it took some time for us to get seated. I intend to bring friends, relatives, dates infact everyone I can back here in the future...they'll never get rid of me!

Awesome food, great service, fantastic ambience -- one of the best dining experiences I've ever had, not just in NY but anywhere. Â I know restaurants can have an off night, and I'm sure cookshop isn't immune to that, but this was one time where the stars must have been aligned: warm summer night with just a hint of a breeze, al fresco dining, nice waiter and bussers, terrific bartender (thanks, Kalani!), courteous hosts, and delicious, creative food. Â In a city like this, it's hard to return to the same restaurant when there are so many new ones to choose from, but I think cookshop will be on my permanent go-back list from now on.

This place makes me feel like I'm in San Jose or Milpitas again. I do believe the Vietnamese food is better on the West Coast (you can challenge me on this if you have substantial evidence). Ba Xuyen does however make one yelplicious banh mi for the price and quality. Plus the ladies behind the counter are usually quite nice and thoroughly entertained by my Chenglish. The bread is toasted and there is a selection of other goodies if you choose not to go the sandwich route. Two friends actually just went on a romantic getaway to Vietnam...the food must be phenomenal.

I initially really liked the interior of this place upon arriving and the menu seemed unique and to have a lot of options. Â Unfortunately, the food was not very good and the waitress seemed irritated and unhappy from the start. Â  We had the kale and calamari salad. Â The calamari was flavorless and not grilled quite enough. Â The kale salad was dry and bland. I ordered the Baja Fish tacos. Â When the dish arrived, I initially thought they sent me the wrong item. Â The fish was battered and fried in a hard fish and chips batter and it was served in one of those hard taco bowls like you see on those infomercials for making your own tortilla bowls. Â When the waitress asked right away how we liked everything I told her that the dish wasn't what I expected. Â And she sort of condescendingly told me that Baja fish tacos are fried. Â It wasn't the fried fish I had a problem with, but the many times I've had baja fish tacos they are NOT covered in a hard, fish and chips batter and they are placed in a nice soft tortilla, not a hard tortilla bowl. Â The description in the menu said nothing about this. Â I have never sent food back but I actually sent it back because I really couldn't eat it. Â The waitress seemed annoyed by the request. On the upside, my friend ordered the whole trout which I thought was very good. Â The grilled asparagus was pretty good. The waitress brought the check as soon as we received our dessert without us asking for it.

I enjoyed my meal here but I would stick to the basics and stay clear of the pricier side of the menu. My oysters must have been shucked with a chainsaw, I had to spit out several bits of broken shell and grit, not worth it. If your server doesn't mention the prices on the specials be sure to ask, I ended up with a $30 entree which had I known better I would have passed on. The squash dumplings were nice, try those.
Excellent! One of the best places to bring a date.. was there for lunch today. excellent!
Great DJ but drinks were not strong. Happy hr prices were $7 a drink. We did pickle back shots all nights and it was definitely watered down. Still had a great time dancing though!
One of the best meals I've had in Manhattan. Â The food is awesome, the decor is lovely, and the service is impeccable.

I have changed my mind. Â Eataly is pretty fucking annoying while also decent for the food. Â Being stood up for date is giving me time to see the flaws as I wander aimlessly. Â Not letting me claim a table without my full party sucked. Â So I'm standing here drinking a beer getting run over by tourists. Â One star deducted.

This place is great! I love the pork dumplings, with chive or onion. The pork sandwich is great too. Everything is better with the duck sauce. figure on about a packet of duck sauce per and item ordered. I haven't had their sushi but i would expect that it is very good for the money. The only knock on this place is that they don't clean their tables off and quite a few people can't seem to keep their mess on the tray or remove their tray when they are finished with their meal. but what do you expect for a 5 dollar meal great value in the notoriously expensive union square area.
It takes them a while to seat you but the food and cocktails are on point. Try the Bowery Fix. It's incredible!

This is my first Yelp review, so here goes: Met up with a friend around Union Square, and she suggested we try Ootoya. Had never heard of it but apparently everyone else has because the hostess told us 45 - 60 minutes for 8:30 Thursday night! We gave them our number anyway, not expecting anything, but sure enough the hostess called after 45 min and even left a courteous voicemail. Happy to have waited because the food was damn good. Never had Japanese food sets, and seriously one of the best katsu and mackerel dishes I've ever tried. And don't forget about the yakitori. Try: -Chawanmushi (who knew egg custard could be so good?) -Tsukune (just do it, trust me on this) -Buta Aspara (can't go wrong with pork belly) -Saba set (mackerel) Server was polite, friendly, and helpful. Mostly Japanese staff, although the white tall guy and short Asian girl (typical NYC odd couple) at the host/ess stand didn't seem to speak any Japanese. They still managed to keep their cool despite all the hungry people rushing their little host table. Overall great service as to be expected, especially at Japanese restaurants. Our hostess even apologized and thanked us for waiting, not like she could control the popularity of this place. Popularity and long wait time well justified

This tiny, dark, 8-table, BYOB eatery delivered pretty good food at great prices. Â And even when the place completely filled up at 8:30, the service from the lone waiter was solid: attentive, friendly, and knowledgable. For appetizers, the mushroom cigars (pureed wild mushrooms rolled in a flaky phyllo crust and sprinkled with truffle oil, served with a truffled vinaigrette arugula salad) were awesome. Â The beet salad was good, the crab cakes decent, but the tuna tartare was too sweet, a little too warm, and didn't taste fresh. Â We ordered the filet, Nook garden pasta, and Tuscan chicken for our main dishes, and the only one I enjoyed was the Tuscan chicken (spinach- and cheese-stuffed chicken breast in a parmesan sauce). Â The sauce and the doneness of the filet were great, but the quality wasn't...and the pasta (penne with eggplant and zucchini in an alfredo sauce) wasn't bad, but it was nothing special. Â The sides were quite good: red wine braised cabbage and the sauteed spinach.

I came here with my mom and a friend for brunch. I love the decor and atmosphere. This would be a nice spot for a low key date. It's a tad bit pricey but it's Tribeca so that's to be expected. My mom and I had both had greek salads and bloody mary's. Food was good and we had a very friendly bartender that humored my mom's requests. And they give out caramels. That's a plus.

My husband and I celebrated both our birthdays on 1/29/11 and ordered the tasting menu. Â I had the lamb as the entree and the steak for him. Â Both were a very big disappointment - served after a long wait, both dishes were lukewarm and salty. Service was uncertain. Â The bill was not surprising for a restaurant such as the Grammercy Tavern but my husband and I felt the quality of food and service was severley lacking. Â  Â Will not go back for sure.

I've been coming since back in the days. It's been that long, lol. The food is always good with a little of Chinese influence. Service is quicker than finding parking. And it's located across from Ferrara's if you want some Italian sweeets.

Very good ramen. Â One of the best I've had in the city. Â The broth was thick and flavorful. Â I had the thin noodles with the pork (char su). Â I definitely recommend it. Â The restaurant is a little small so this might not be good for large groups. Â I don't think more that 4 people can fit at a table.

I came here today for breakfast and I was surprised by how many people were there for a Monday morning. It was 10:30AM and almost every single table was filled. On the food, both my cousin and I had the 2 eggs any style that came with a protein, wheat toast and potato hash browns. My over easy eggs were fine, the bacon was a little bit wilty--wish it had been a little more crispy but the star on the plate was the potato hash. OOOOmygosh it was amazing. You could taste all the buttery goodness in every bite. Overall a solid meal at a decent price and I would probably go back because it's pretty close to my apartment.

WOW!! The font door was impressive , when I opened door good music good vibe cozy place, walked up to carver , very helpful on helping me with ordering .sat down started eating brisket was like none I've ever tasted it just melted in my mouth (fabulous) sides where excellent had salad wedge w/ blue cheese dressing and collard greens ( fabulous ) with a couple of glass old school bottled cokes awesome .. To top it off finished with baked goods (pies where great ) awesome awesome awesome !!!!

Absolute must. Price is the best I've ever had for any food in New York, period. Portion is great, and that white sauce is better than anything out there. Spicy sauce has a great kick, and just a little goes a very long way. Went during lunchtime on a workday, and still got my food insanely quickly. Can't go wrong with this choice.
It's okay. what does halal mean anyway?

Food was quite flavorful. We opted to sit outside since the weather was delightful but inside was the better choice. Started with a smooth drip coffee served with condensed milk. Â My boyfriend and I shared the Khao Soi (thanks to previous Yelp reviews) and ordered a side of garlic fried rice and longonissa sausage. I wouldn't recommend the rice since it was nothing special. But I would recommend sharing the Khao Soi! Would I return? Sure, why not. Enjoy.
Fantastic every time.
We went to Boqueria after walking out of a place a few blocks away (which I won't name). Â It's a very comfortable space with a great menu, and the food really delivered. Â I'd recommend.

Seriously. Awesome. We went here during the Saturday brunch rush - the staff was super nice and helpful. The hostess worked extra hard to be sure everyone was acknowledged and informed about wait times. She did a bang-up job despite the angry stroller moms harassing her. The food was fantastic, as were the drinks. I got a peach bellini & my fiance got the spicy Bloody Mary. All I can remember was how amazing my eggs benedict were. Extremely pleasant experience overall. Just keep in mind, if you're going during a peak time (ie weekend brunch), put your patient pants on and be prepared to wait a bit. The time will pass quickly with a stroll through the adjacent park.

Locanda Verde is a perfect spot for brunch, lunch and dinner. Â It has a great cozy atmosphere with a reasonable noise level. Â You can even pick up coffee and pastries on the go if you don't have time to sit down for a full meal. Â  The menu offers diners varied choices to select from -- whether you're craving fried chicken, seared scallops, pasta or seasonal vegetables all for relatively affordable prices. Â The wine list, whether by the glass or bottle, offers something for everyone. Overall, a great addition to Tribeca!

This place is fun! Â The tables are communal and everyone working there seems so energetic... running around and shouting strange things I can't understand! Â  I brought my mom around lunchtime on a Saturday... I wouldn't say it was the "ideal" mom spot, but she really liked it I think! Â Due to my lack of ramen experience, I boringly asked the waiter what the most popular dish was and ordered that. Â It was the one with the pork and the hardboiled egg and it was super-tasty. Â That egg! Â I was talking about that egg all day. Â I'm not even a big egg person! Â How could half of a hard boiled egg in a bowl of broth be so delicious? Â The hunk of pork was pretty good, but I have to say I would have rather had several more eggs thrown in there. Okay, sorry for the egg ramble. Â Overall, my first ramen met expectations. Â It was a tasty and satisfying meal in a fun atmosphere.
Very good japanese restaurant. Food is not expensive. The environment is good. One point not so good is that the server is not so friendly...

Super delicious! Just ate here with the bf, we both had a guaco taco because of the Yelp raves about them, and they were correct! Super fresh and tasty. Love the way the corn and avocado mix! I also had a cola-braised pork, definitely as delicious as I remembered from the Hester Street Fair this summer, you can actually taste the cola marinade, but it's not overwhelmingly sweet-perfect! My bf had the brisket taco, he thought it was good, pretty standard. We had a great chat with the owner(?) about their tacos, other good taco spots, other good food neighborhoods, etc. He was majorly friendly and down to earth, so I figured I'd come give them a great review! I would do 4.5 stars if I could, but since I can't I'm going to go with 4 because I like my tacos about a dollar cheaper. For fancy tacos though, this is definitely a better bet than Snack Dragon.

I came here on a cold night and was happily comforted by the cozy dining room and delicious food. My buddies and I did the all you can eat+salad/dessert. We ended up trying every single flammie, in addition to the potato and beet salads and the calvados sucree. The gratinee, salmon, and biquette are really special. I'd avoid the provencale because it lacks the flavor that the others have. I've never had Alsatian food before this, but it was a great introduction. Â I really want to come back and try their brunch! The service is a bit slow, but it's alright. I kinda got the feeling the waiters were judging my friends and me for eating so gosh darn much, but hey, it's all you can ate and that's exactly what we did. Totally worth it.

My favorite thing about Zest was the ambience. It's small and cozy but it doesn't feel cramped or overcrowded. I suggest making a reservation though because they seem to give priority to those who have reservations. The sushi is good and the staff is friendly. The Happy Hour menu is definitely worth checking out--everything (appetizers, sushi, drinks) is only $3. Even when it's not Happy Hour, the prices are reasonable. Your wallet won't feel a thing.

I liked this little place! Â The poutine was very good, and I will have to get their fries by themselves sometime, too, they are crispy and perfect. Â A key word, though, is "little" because this place is small, and mobbed at peak times! Â Next time, I'm going to go just when it opens or something, so I won't be overwhelmed by the crowd. Â  A good place, though, and I'll definitely go back.

Food took over an hour to arrive, and when it came it was cold. I called to check on my order after 45 minutes and they said it just went out. it came 25 minutes later. The sodas were warmer than the food, that's not a joke, they clearly weren't refrigerated.The delivery guy called to say he was there, and he wasn't, he was down the block. Â He eventually came down the block and delivered the food. Â Food was nothing special.

For this price, the veggie sushis are excellent. They are tasty, creative, attractive, and well made. Service was fantastic. I would like a few sushis with regular Japanese rice. Also, they should use a few Japanese veggies and pickles. Nevertheless, I'll be coming regularly now.

Best Falafel I've ever had. I always make it a point to stop here when I'm in New York. I usually get the falafel sandwich which is absolute Â perfection. The ratio of tahini sauce to falafel is just right and even the pita bread seems above average. And the price is ridiculous - its $2.50 for a sandwich. The only downside is very limited seating indoors (although if its nice out, you should be eating in Washington Square Park anyway). Also, on my last 2 visits, there were food tours there, so I had to nudge my way through a horde of yapping midwesterners who couldn't pronounce shwarma to save their lives. Â But that's a small price to pay for the heaven that is Mamoun's Falafel.
Cool place, wasn't a fan of the burger, or the butt on the wall that was staring at me while trying to eat said burger.

One of my favorite brunches in the whole city. So many fantastic options to choose from for $12, plus coffee plus baked goods. My personal favorite is the chilaquiles, but if you're really hungry the Plato Don is enough food to feed a small army.

Excellent service and lovely food in a cosy bar and restaurant just a stones throw from Times Square. We all had pasta and enjoyed it so much we came back a second time to sample something else. Bella is a very welcoming host and her staff were friendly and attentive. I noticed also they take orders for intermission drinks for Book of Mormon which is situated next door. This is a must visit for excellently priced food for those staying in Times Square.

Very charming intimate atmosphere. There were a lot of Japanese speaking people here which made me think "if Japanese people like it, then it must be authentic" Black Sesame creme brulee Sesame is usually a very overpowering flavor but the black sesame and creme brulee was a very delightful surprise of deliciousness. Chocolate sou flee with raspberry sauce very very rich and fluffy. Two kinds of freshly baked scones like the chocolate scone but didn't eat the other one, we tried figuring out what the flavor was - we think it was a Taro scone.. hm.. I wouldn't recommend the scone. Assam tea great pair to finish with the desserts above Minus one star because it's Cash Only, No Reservations with a very very awkward waiting area.

Came here after work for a few drinks with friends. We had a decent sized group (started out as 3, turned into 6) and this place fills up quickly. The bar area is really small but they do have an adjacent dining area which is where we ended up. While the staff was nice, they had a ton of rules for a bar. It wasn't as easy as just showing up and getting drinks; it was "do you have a reservation?" (for the bar, really?) and "we can't seat you in the dining area until your entire party is here" and "you can't sit in the dining area and just order drinks". Their house red wine is terrible (and cost $14, seriously?) but their cocktails are alright. The house made ricotta is pretty good, as is the scotch egg. There are way better bars around.

When friends invited me to Yerba Buena, I was immediately excited by the name because of the popular yerba mate in Argentina (like as popular as Starbucks in the US). Â As a pisco sour fan, I wasted no time in ordering a yerba infused pisco cocktail. Â It is incredible. Â Get it and drink it. Â Overall, cocktails are creative, south american influenced and diverse. Â For dinner, we went with four people and sampled most of the appetizers for dinner. Â We had plaintains, potato croquettes, chicken empanadas, hamachi ceviche, tilapia tacos, and choclo (that huge kerneled peruvian corn). Â The ceviche and choclo were favorites, but everything was delicious and happily devoured. Â Only complaint? Â No reservations, so expect a wait (tragically, at the bar with a yerba pisco cocktail in hand). Â It is too small for big groups, but 2-4 is ideal. Â If the wait it too long, try "Supper" kitty corner from the restaurant, which is also great and does not take reservations.

The plus side is the food is delicious and the portions are reasonable. The down side is that the place is cramped and often very busy. The prices were a little high but so was the quality. Service was decent and I'd definitely come back for a nice seafood meal. If you're ordering somthing on a bun that comes with fries it's generally $15-20. If you're ordering something from the grill it's mostly $20-25 but doesn't come with sides. Meals with sides are mostly $25-35 (sides by themselves are $5 each but are generally large enough to share). I like that they always have a good number of fish choices available and that they'll cook it however you'd like (grilled, fried, blackened). I ordered some special of the day, I don't remember why kind of fish it was or the exact price but I do remember how good it was. The grilled fish was cooked and seasoned perfectly. They left part of the dark flesh generall discarded on a filet but was very good anyway. The dish came with mashed potatoes and green beans which were also nothing short of ideal. Overal my Fish experiece (other than the hour wait) was a plesant one and I'd definitely come back.

Would it be so bad to say that this place is a nicer-decorated, more spacious Yakitori Taisho or Oh! Taisho? While those two, on St. Mark's Place, have a more bustling, grungy, Japanese hole-in-the-wall kind of feel, both share the same literally underground atmosphere that is clearly welcoming to both Japanese and non-Japanese alike, with similar price points. I stopped in with a friend for some yakitori and day-drinking before seeing a play a few blocks away. So, here's the setting: Friday night, 6:00pm. No wait! Awesome. I definitely wanted to come early after reading reviews about the seemingly treacherous cue that forms every evening... We sit down at the bar. Japanese bartender gets us our pitcher of Sapporo. We order deep fried squid legs (special of the day) and Set A of the Yakitori: pork belly, chicken, beef, and small, whole, roasted green peppers. The squid legs were nicely fried and served with a tempura dipping sauce, but were extremely tough. So after messily trying to bite off a third, or half of the legs and failing to do so easily, I ended up just putting the whole thing in my mouth, stuffing my face like a barbarian. Yeah, it was real pretty (and chewy). Set A of the yakitori was good, but nothing special. The peppers were interesting! A little oily but nicely salted and roasted to get a nice tenderness. 3 stars for the creativity and uniqueness of flavors of the food we did get and the service. Service was on the slower side, which I usually don't mind, but the restaurant wasn't full yet and it took quite a while just to get a few skewers of meat. We sat on the far side of the bar where the televisions were. It wasn't a particularly loud area, but somehow it turned out to be a sort of odd sound-suck spot? It was really hard to hear my friend who was sitting right next to me. Can't really complain about that though since it's the bar--about half of those at the bar were by themselves looking to quickly eat some food and get out of there, so not being able to hear someone else's conversation would probably not be an issue. Anyway, I'd recommend not sitting there unless you're by yourself. Also, only a single-stall bathroom. Sad times waiting in line. We didn't end up ordering any of the main dishes or sake, so I am almost sure that I missed out on some great things that I'm sure that this formally izakaya and sake bar has to offer. More reason to come back, hopefully with better luck overall: on seating, service, and food.

It was Christmas Eve, and we spent 30 minutes waiting in line for a chicken platter. That is what the holidays are for! It was about 32 degrees outside and there was a line of 30 people waiting in front of us. Because of that, we knew this place had to be legit. We got the chicken platter which consisted of chicken, rice, and pita bread. It comes with veggies, but we aren't veg lovers. It's served immediately and piping. hot. There is not a seating area for it except for benches and random seating around the surrounding buildings. I didn't find anything spectacular about it. I thought their chicken was a bit rubbery and the rice was overcooked. There were some bites every now and then that was great, but it was inconsistent. I do think $6 is a good deal for it, but I'm not sure I would wait 30 minutes in the cold for it.

We checked out this place on the recommendation of a friend... We've gone to four brunches in a row now. Tater heaven is amazing, but the food I had was solid, but not outstanding, which I wasn't expecting. Don't get the huevos rancheros. Just don't. Cash only sucks... but only because I have Chase. And they can burn and die. I love the bloody marys, they come with a pickle, are a tall pour aaand extra spicy, which I love in bloody marys. I've had the malted caramel shake which is aaamaazzingg, and I've heard the key lime is just as tasty. There's one awesome server on Sundays but there's also one stuck up server... sooo whatever. Come here, don't get huevos rancheros, get tater heaven and a caramel shake(and a bloody mary on the side), say your last prayers and eat your way to heaven :P

Fast, cheap, fresh Italian. Â Fantastic for a quick lunch time drop-by. Â The bolognese sauce is good on anything....if you have extra sauce (you probably will) when you're done, you can dip the breadbasket bread in it and continue enjoying. downsides are that its cramped quarters (only seats about 6, 10 if its sunny). Â during good weather, it is one of my favorite lunch spots - no hassles, no pomp, no circumstance. Â just food.
LOVE the lamb over rice with white sauce...delicious. I waited in the snow for a hour for a plate...yum

Its as wonderful as my fellow yelpers say. Â Really 4.5 stars. Â  Its just not quite all the way up to FAVORITE PLACE OF ALL TIME status, but its on the super high very much recommend list. Do yourself a favor and order duck...duck... Â well just duck duck (sigh, if only they had mousse on the dessert menu you could order duck duck mousse). Â But if you've read through a few yelps then you didnt need me to tell you to order the spicy duck meatballs and the duck breast entree. Â  The apps are the real star here. Â Actually i think apps are the real star everywhere, so add to your list the crispy calamari salad for sure, and if you have room for one more, the pork belly was also unique and delicious. Â And do not leave the restaurant without sharing some Risotto with your tablemates. Its really decadent. I was nervous about ordering the hangar steak because the Yelpers either raved or were disappointed, but mark me up in the Yay column, cause it was perfectly cooked, had great texture and had a lightly sauced plate that was good enough to lick clean. Â  If you have room for dessert, you cant beat the experience of a freshly made donut, still warm when it arrives at the table. Â I also adored the complimentary recently baked peanut butter mini cookies that were brought out with our coffees. Â For me, a simple perfectly made cookie trumps any other kind of dessert. Â Although I did kind of regret not ordering the 'must-place-your-order-before-dinner' teacup soufflee that I saw float by. Â It smelled heavenly.
Great at what it does - whiskey and southern food. The food was top notch and the ambiance was great too. Definitely try the grits.
Good, not outstanding food- Maybe not completely authentic- spicy and tasty Though
This restaurant is a little pricey, but the food is excellent and the portions are very big. Atmosphere is very nice also.
Good stuff. No booze. Bit hipster, but a decent one-time visit.
the first time I went there, I got the basil cheese pizza that was fresh out of the oven which was pretty good. Â The second time, however, I got a sausage pizza that wasn't good at all.

Yummy! I love this place! For what it's worth, I like it better than it's sister on Perry. It is very cramped though, but the drinks and food are excellent. I get the same thing everytime: "The Chicken with Rice". Boring, but delicious, especially with that bonus guac on the side! In the words of Rachel Ray, "Yum-O!"

reputed as one of the best, under appreciated, noodle spots in the city and I was not dissapointed.
