You can taste the hand made noodles and dumplings and the quality stands levels above the price you pay for it. It's a hole in the wall place, so seating isn't the most intimate, but definitely worth traveling for.

Great place! I have eaten here before, but just take out and it was fabulous. Went here for a Sunday brunch and two words: Yogurt Parfait. WOWOWOWOW! Delicious!!! I got the breakfast buritto and it was very delcious! I love the atmosphere here and that it's actually not that big. Â Gives off a great cozy, trendy, dinner space. Â Love it. We did have about a 30 min wait which was fine. Â Gave us time to walk around the neighborhood. Â  Astoria, I love you!

I thought I loved fries, then I met Pommes Frites. Â Pommes Frites just stole my virginity... like I had never tried a proper fry before. Â Ok, I kid, but it's a damn good fry. I actually have legitimate hunger pains for this place. Â A zillion sauces to choose from and they'll let you try it first! Filipino run (and probably owned?) so I'm even happier to support. Â The employees have always been super nice and friendly! Â When it's not busy they're willing to spend some time talking to me about the sauces. My only complaint is that there CAN be a long line (usually at butt o lock in the morning when the drunkies come)--its great all the time but especially great after a night out. Â Also, its such a teeny place, literally a hole in the wall, and it's really hard to get seating. PS, saw them mixing a sauce in the back and a huge amount of Patis was poured into whatever flavor he was making. Â Awesome. Hah.

Service here is great! Â Small and specialized menu which makes ordering easier. Â But no matter what you order, you can't go wrong. Â Breakfast is a great time to go if you can make it. Â Fills up quickly, so make it early. Â A trip to their Â boulangerie is a must!

This is my new Go-To spot in the Crown Heights area when I'm there, which is, sad to say, infrequent. But after discovering this place, I'm readjusting my weekend bike route. I know reviews of bloody marys (proper puralization?) are over-done, but... they make a fantastic one. And the Croque Madame is killer. Plus the bartender chatted with us openly and we had a great time.
Poor service. And I found a price tag on my curry puffs :( very dissatisfied, I don't understand what's the hype about :(
This place is a goddamn joy and that's all I'm going to say about it.

We don't have dessert. Only booze said our waitress. Possibly the best reply I'll ever get from a waitress. Fried chicken sandwich was delicious, fried cheese curds were a win and their booze list is pretty sweet. Sweet Afton can do no wrong!

The pizza is very good. The building is attractive. The line is absolutely outrageous. We got there maybe 30 minutes before they opened and the line was two blocks long! When they did open the doors, we almost made it in, but were the 2nd group when they closed the doors once the restaurant had filled. So incredibly tragic!! It was hot (there's no shade when you are that close to the door) and I was so hungry. They eventually offered bar seats instead of a table which we, of course, took. The pizza was delicious (4 stars), but was it worth the line?? 3 stars for the experience, but it's not one I would wish to repeat.
Good samwich. Vietnamese style. Why go there? They have good Vietnamese sammiches. Have one. And the Lychee shakes are good too.

I'm sorry guys...rude staff, burnt crust...just not all that. Â I was not impressed, went there 3 times to give it the benefit of the doubt since everyone is always giving it such rave reviews. Â John's, Grimaldi's, Patsy's and Flushing's Lucia's are all better choices to me.

I've been wanting to try this place forever for brunch and finally got the honor today. Being rainy and windy, we showed up and got a table for two within 5 minutes on a Sunday at around 1 pm. The place is cute, nice decor but the seating is a bit cramped as the tables are very close to one another and you can definitely eavesdrop on conversations or squeeze into your seat (if sitting on the booth side) awkwardly. Service was a bit slow, the place was packed despite the bad weather. They have a few outdoor seats. Food was excellent! I was really impressed with my roasted artichoke provencial dish. Came with a poached egg, cheese, and pancetta and all the flavors mixed in was so good. I wiped my plate clean. My friend had the Monte Cristo sandwich which came with fries. The fries were amazing! I love fries and these are one of the best I've ever had (up there w Ace Hotel fries). They're thin, fresh, and super crisp and not oily at all. Man I so wanted to order my own side of fries! Would definitely go back, I liked the ambience, price points, and the food. They take RSVPs but only for parties of 6 or more.
It's ok. Not that good and not worth the hype.

It's definitely a good place for quick and warm homey food! In the dead cold of winter, I stopped by to get the hot and sour soup two days in a row. Boyfriend got a $1 order of fried dumplings. I wouldn't want to get the dumpling noodle soup again though--too much noodles and only 3-4 pieces of dumplings. But for anything else, you'll probably spend about $4 and be very happy!

Having lived in Southern California for 2 years, I was surprised that some of the best tacos I've ever had were in NYC. The prices are super reasonable, and while the line was long it moved pretty quickly (we waited around 15 minutes). A great snack or lunch pre-game, especially when you're low on $. The tacos were the perfect amount of chewy, and the staff super up-beat and friendly.

Super good. Service was excellent, everything from salad to dessert was superb. Tasteful cocktail menu with none of the "hey, we're mixologists" bartender shtick that makes me want to order a Schlitz in disgust. Â Nice atmosphere, though I'm not at all a fan of the bench seating trend that seems to be catching on in NY, particularly in Brooklyn. If I'm spending more than $50, give me a seat back, please! Notwithstanding this very minor gripe, I'll definitely return.

Tasty thin-crust pizza, solid ingredients, love the coal-oven char, but I have to say there wasn't anything that knocked me out of my seat. Â I definitely enjoyed it and thought it was a good pizza, but shudder to think that it potentially could have been at the expense of hour(s) long waits. My friends and I arrived on a Wed about 15 minutes before it opened, was quickly ushered in with only a few parties ahead of us, and were served promptly and quickly. Â That's the kind of wait I would put up with for this pizza, but if I saw the line up snaking further down the street? Â Probably not. Also tried Lombardi's a few days prior to this trip - I like Grimaldi's better, found that the pizza was overall more flavorful, and texture of crust crispier and more pleasant contrast to the toothsome toppings. Â However, I was a big fan of the pancetta at Lombardi's, of which there was no comparable topping at Grimaldi's. My point of reference, the pizza I hold all pizzas up to? Al Forno in Providence, Rhode Island. Â Their grilled pizza is absolutely exquisite and an experience worth making the trip out for.

This place serves great moderately priced arepas. Â I typically get the one with the sweet plantain and pork. Â The ambiance is so-so, and it may take a bit for the food to come out from the kitchen. Â The empanada appetizer is overpriced for what you get in terms of quantity.
Excellent cheesecake!!

Pros: Good creative food. Great service. It's a nice break from K town. Some things are staple Izakaya items others are stuff I haven't seen before. But most are pretty good. Cons: Short Happy Hour. Can be quite a wait during busy times. Hard to find. Also kind of pricey as it is a higher end place than the St Marks joints. Overall: Recommended for a different flair on the Izakaya standard and a good place for hanging out or just dinner in the area if KTown is not your thing.

My mom and I could write a book about all the time we have spent together eating oysters. Â In fact last weekend we ate oysters for dinner both Saturday and Sunday in NYC. Sunday's location not only blew away Saturday's, but it blew away the majority of the places we have been. On Sunday we went to Upstate and I'm already trying to figure out when I can get back there. We sat at the bar and ordered half a dozen oysters 3 from east coast 3 from the west. Out waiter was very knowledgeable and helpful when it came to recommendations and he introduced us to the tatamagouche (pei) which were so fantastic we had to order another half dozen of those alone. We then had the squid salad. I'm salivating as i write this!!!!! Let me preface by saying that squid is pretty much my go-to dish so I eat it weekly and would say I have a very good idea of what makes a good squid salad and this it. Cooked literally to perfection, it had perfect consistency- I could've eaten 2 more orders but as we later found out we had the last one. Boy, did i feel bad for the guys next to us who tried to order it after. For Dinner we split the fettuccine with clams at the recommendation of our kick ass bartender/ server. Â Not something I typically order but this guy clearly knew his stuff so we went for it. Good decision- my eyes were rolling into the back of my head and we shamelessly licked the plate clean. Â It was again, perfection. I was drinking wine that evening but The craft beer selection (on tap) was pretty substantial and seemed like it would well accompany their food selection. Kudos to the owner, our server and the small but expert staff they have at upstate. I almost don't want to admit how good it is because I don't want to share my stool at the bar!

I'm not really a gyro kinda gal but my husband made me go one night and now, I'm a convert. I have chicken souvlaki with mama sauce - totally delicious and very nice quality of chicken which was tender, lean and with a great char-grilled flavour. The tzatziki sauce is also slurpworthy. I like the fact that they're not too massive and are reasonably priced. My hub had the mama gyro x2 option for just $7 while I, smugly virtuous, ordered the solo $3.95 option the first time I went. Balls to the smug vituousness, Ima ordering TWO babies next time. Saved one for the next day and it was surprisingly delicious having been nuked in the microwave for a minute. There's a choice of white or wholewheat pita and a loyalty card. The gyros & wraps are advertised as having fries inside so the first time I ordered, I didn't order a side as I was planning. However, there were exactly 3 fries in there so I was a little disappointed. Lack of intro-gyro fries and weirdly early closing hours (9pm?!) lost 'em a star for me, but I'm being pedantic. Also, who I can only assume is MamaGyro herself, told me they were extending their hours in the summer. It seemed to be PapaGyro who wanted us out at bang on 9pm (they have about 6 stools and a bar for eat-in). Doesn't Papa know that he's serving the city that never sleeps - or never stops eating gyros? I think mama and papa Gyro live in my building cos I'm always seeing them - maybe I should slope up to them and discuss the paltry intro-gyro fry situation...

I had ramen in Japan so I have a pretty high standard for ramen, but this was quite good! I prefer to have thicker ramen noodles though.. The pork buns were super soft and flavorful. Definitely worth a try, but not a fan of the hour-long wait.
Cute place, liked the ambiance. Good for groups but a bit on the dark side and probably better for a 1:1 date. Lots of couples hanging out or small groups. Nothing spectacular about the wine.

Every detail in the restaurant is finely tuned from the tableware to the lighting & decor to the food service. Â  All of the dishes we ate were very, very well prepared and the delicious cocktails are prepared properly with fresh ingredients. Â The service was standout. That's rare today, even in food cities like New York. Â Bravo Vitae!

I guess I'm a bit partial to this place, as I've been eating here since I was young enough to talk. Thankfully, the prices change just as often as the establishment's name... which isn't a lot. I assume that the latter is because of the imitators and spin-offs, but eh. The menu is unchanged, and that's all right by me. I'd give this place four stars for what you get, and that's: 1) Fast service. You don't stop by for a chat-and-chew, but for an express meal. On the flip side, be prepared to sit next to strangers if you've a small party. 2) Cheap grub. Enough said, really. Chinatown is great for its sub-$5 eats, and this joint is king. 3) Relatively tasty authentic Chinese food. What more can you ask for? Personally, I prefer to go overboard with congee, fried cruellers, and wonton noodle soup each and every time. The congee has the right consistency, their cruellers are popular and tasteful (even if said taste is mostly oil), and the soup base is a good blend of sweet and salty. If I don't feel like getting anything special, this is the go-to spot.

Dear Yelp, I disagree. It was not worth the 8 block walk for lunch. It was plentiful and crispy-fried, with a nice enough japanese-hole-in-the-wall absence of a vibe, but it just doesn't cut it for what Japanese food really is like - very, very tasty. Not coming back.

The best ramen in NYC! If you really enjoy great ramen, and have seen the movie "Tampopo" you know how hard it is to create that great tasting, mouth-watering broth. Well, Ippudo comes close to it. The ramen is the best tasting broth I have had here in New York. Don't listen to those who fringe on paying money for good food, just think of the moment your mouth comes into contact with the ramen, broth, and pork. Delicious to the last drop. While some ramen places are very stingy with the pork portions, I think Ippudo does a great job serving up more than 2 pieces. If you are a foodie, don't think about the prices, just go for finding the perfect bowl of ramen, cause here you just about find it!
The food and the drinks were awesome, exactly what my bf and I were looking for on a weekend morning... Comfortable, relaxed, and intimate. A bit pricy for a brunch, but definitely worth the trip.

Yea why do i call mexican taco spot and i get some Chinese guy answering and taking my order. Hung up and not ordering from that place. I want mexican food i want to hear spanish mexican guy say hello not Chinese guy!!!

MY GOD...hands down, my fave dumpling place in NYC. Not easy to find but worth the journey. Â I would eat a full meal for about $3: 10 dumplings, hot n sour soup, and a sesame pancake. Oh, and be prepared to be aggressive in ordering. Â The neighborhood Â Asian elders have no hesitation in pushing you out of the way to place their order. Â Plus, the staff will ignore you if you just stand there waiting to be acknowledged. Walk in, cash in hand, look at the woman taking orders in the eyes, and order. Â No need to be courteous...they just want you in and out. This place is tiny and a line of people trying to yell their order not uncommon. Love this place.

We were visiting NYC with our cousins and wanted some yummy japanese, didn't know where to go so the 4 of us started to yelp, and finally after a long hour of going back and forth and being indecisive my boyfriend says "we going to Sakagura"! We were so happy that someone decided. YAY, Japanese!!! We came to this restaurant, as we were directed to walk down the basement, it felt sketchy but when we stepped into the restaurant everything changed, the decor reminded us of Japan, the smell just brought happiness to our faces and the sound of people eating and chatting just made us feel safe and that we had made a good choice! Â we didn't make an appointment, so we waited for 20 mins and when we sat down and the food came, then the sake. Wow, every dish we got just blew us away, the duck, the pork, the sashimi but I especially loved the uni soup with the poached egg. AND then there was desert, I love black sesame Â and their blk sesame creme brulee topped with more black sesame ice cream was ridiculously good.!. Well done boyfriend! I can't wait to come back this fall! :)

I went a few years ago for dinner and liked the cocktails but found the food pretty unimpressive. My husband has been wanting to try so we went without a reservation yesterday and were seated pretty quickly at a bar table. Â We really wanted to love the meal- had good wine and good service but were very disappointed especially given the prices are so high. Mediocre $40 steak is pretty displeasing. You can do better for dinner in NYC, but good for drinks, not sure about brunch.

I and the 4 other people in my party agreed that Umami Burger was worth the 2.5 hour wait. Just have someone from your party (or everyone) arrive 2-3 hours earlier than you would like to eat, put your name down and go to a nearby bar. They text you a link to a website where you can check how many parties are ahead of you and the anticipated wait time. EASIEST WAIT EVER. So everyone at our table tried the thin fries, truffle fries, tempura onion rings, smushed potatoes, the Original umami burger and the Truffle burger. Fries were nice and shoestring, although I think I prefer Spotted Pig's. Truffle fries get soggy. Tempura onion rings lack the crunchy, crispy onion ring fried battered shell that I love in onion rings. Smushed potatoes were... just potatoes...smushed. The sauces they put out on the table are great, especially the spicier ones; however, the umami ketchup is forgettable. All in all, ignore the appetizer menu unless you're starving and want something on the table as soon as possible. Now onto the burgers... All the burgers are medium rare- perfect and charred with a little U on top. The burger sort of falls apart in your mouth, crumbles away. As my friends put it, it literally melts in your mouth. The Original burger was good but there was a little bit too much tomato in my opinion. The parmesan crisp was a nice touch. The truffle burger- amazing. Rich. Truffle-y. Nice salty finish. Definitely the group's favorite. However, I only had half of it and was told that having the whole thing is a little too rich. Burgers are a bit on the small side, so if you're starving, you can probably eat 2. Since we waited for so long and had some parties unfairly sat before us, the hostess hooked us up with free desserts- ice cream sandwiches from The Good Batch. This dessert review will not be that great because it was kind of a blur at this point; I was undergoing major food coma as I had just had a late brunch Clinton St. Baking Company 4 hours before and combined with everything else I ate, I wanted to die at this point. We had the Double Chocolate Peanut Butter ice cream sandwich which sat between 2 chocolate stroopwafels. Now, I've long since been a fan of Dutch stroopwafels and their crispy outsides and gooey sweet centers. I don't think the stroopwafels in this sandwich contained the iconic gooey center of a classic stroopwafel- these were more like plain chocolate wafers. The second ice cream sandwich was paired between a chocolate chip cookie and something similar to Momofuku's compost cookie, but in the classic style of Umami, was more salty. That was delicious. All in all- easy wait, meh appetizers, great burgers, good desserts but then again who makes bad ice cream sandwiches?

My boyfriend and bff and I went to upstate b/c of an oyster craving- the staff here first of all are awesome. There were no tables, but the front house lady took our phone numbers and texted us when a table was about to leave. When selecting oysters sometimes the challenge is knowing what to expect- if you are able to describe what you want, the staff will get it for you. The oysters may be a bit pricey- they are totally fantastic. So fresh and delicious and the craft beer selection is amazeballs.

Went here for lunch today. To say the least it was decent. I definately feel that I have had better ramen. There is a lot of hype surrounding this place and I cant say that isnt well deserved considering that it looks just like the ramen shops in japan. The wait wasnt that long which was great. You gotta put your name down on s waiting list and after about 20 min we got seated. I got the first thing on the menu, cant remember what it is called right now. Overall the noodles I would say was the best part of the meal. I guess I just expected more, the chicken broth was kinda thick for my liking and it may be just me but it had somewhat of an afyer taste. Overall good deal of $13 and the guy who seated us was super cool. Other then him, i feel kind of rushed throughout the meal. Also doesnt accept credit cards

I don't think I need to write very much; my rating says it all. Great food, great wine, great service, great atmosphere. Sitting outside on a comfortable night with a glass of wine indulging in some creme brulee and people-watching is definitely my kind of night. AND, I didn't spend a fortune. :)

I absolutely love the atmosphere at ABC Kitchen, kind of a rustic, romantic place. We had 8:30 reservations but ended up waiting about 35-45 minutes because the people at our table were lingering or so they said. Â I was a little disappointed that they ran out of the scallop special our waiter recommended. We ended up with the mozzarella ball and then also a cheese and cured meat place to start, both were excellent. Our group had the pork, ravioli, sea bass, and halibut for dinner and everyone enjoyed their meals. For dessert DO NOT MISS the sundae, salted caramel ice cream with popcorn, peanuts and chocolate. It was amazing. The service was just okay, our waiter was nice but was MIA a lot and it took awhile to get drinks. Â Overall I would recommend, I love that everything is fresh and organic. Â Read the back of the menu and it tells you all about the restaurant and how they source their food.

It's a shame when really good food gets overshadowed by bad service. So 4 for the food minus one for service. I do hope to come back here and hope to gain a different experience. Came here for lunch and had brunch type food. Pumpkin pancakes, blueberry pancakes and huevos rancheros. All the pancakes were light, fluffy and had a homemade feel to it. The huevos rancheros were good, although I prefer my tortilla crunchy. But good overall. That being said, the food was definitely fresh. The food alone would draw me back .Really nice brunch spot. Has a nice outdoor seating area, which is perfect for those beautiful days. However, we had the unfortunate luck of having bad service. Our waitress was a magician. Just disappeared after taking our order. Trying to get refills on water was a major task. Good thing the place serves up some good food. I do hope to come back and experience a different result from the service. I found out it was open 24 hrs. Nice touch.
Oh Damn!!! What a surprise! Â This is seriously good food! Do the slider with the chipotle ketchup; crazy good! Shake Shack has some serious competition here!!!!

You don't have to be a Greek-lover to love this food. Honestly. If you didn't know it was Greek because you're not as familiar with the genre, I bet you'd LOVE it. I sure did and I'll admit to being somewhat of a Greek novice. I went with a large group, so a lot of food was ordered and delivered to our table. Here is how it went down: Appetizers: Kolokythakia kai melitzanakia tyganita: it's fried zucchini and fried eggplant (thinly sliced) with a delicious white sauce for dipping. Salty and super tasty. Saganaki tou merakli: melty cheese. Kind of like fondue, though a harder crust on top. So maybe a cross between creme brulee and fondue? Super cheesy, super delicious to eat plain or on warm pita bread. Poikilia: it's three dipping sauces for your warm pita (seriously, it's like they serve it right from the oven, super soft and warm and delicious) - one is a tangy yogurt dip, one is eggplant (not chunky, more like a puree), and the third is a fish roe dip (I didn't try, a bit out of my comfort zone!) The ones I tried were really flavorful and went very nicely with the pita. Salad: Horiatiki: Similar to the salad I make myself at home regularly. No lettuce, lots of tomatoes, cucumber, red onion, feta cheese with oil and vinegar. Nothing too "Greek" about it, very tasty and light. Main course: I ordered the Krasata Paidakia which was recommended by our waitress. It's braised short ribs with mashed potatoes. Brown sauce was really flavorful, the ribs were really tender and the mashed potatoes ("potato puree") were a nice compliment. Overall, I walked away quite impressed. We were a very large group with a large number of credit cards, and the wait staff didn't give us any trouble. Food was delicious - even the desserts (which I don't normally care for) were sweet and enjoyable.
This is for Delivery. Thought everything was pretty good, lunch portions were on the small side but everything was falvorful and I would order here again.

My group of three came at a good time because our wait time was fairly short at 15 minutes or so. We ordered the Akamaru Ramen, Wasabi Shoyu Ramen, Shiromaru Hakata Classic, Yamitsuki Goma Kyuri, Hirata Buns, and Tako Wasabi. We had Nitamago and Kakuni with all our ramen choices. The Hirata Buns ended up being the favorite part of our meal. The flavors were pretty amazing. Of the ramen choices, the Wasabi Shoyu was the least liked, however after you dump all the spices into it, it was alright. I definitely prefer the noodles that came with the Akamaru. It just had a better texture in my opinion than the kind that was with the Shoyu and Shiromaru. The noodles they came with was a bit fatter and slightly chewy like you would find in those Neoguri Ramyun packets. Not to say they were bad. I enjoyed those too. The Kakuni and Nitamago gave the dish a little bit more variety but I wouldn't say they were worth the additional $6 total. The Yamitsuki Goma Kyuri was interesting. Japanese cucumbers are nothing like what you'd see at your local grocery store. There's nothing about it that resembles the soft melony bits like you'd find at home. It was crisp and crunchy all throughout the cucumber which I liked although not quite as refreshing as our own. Tako wasabi was our least favorite. They chopped the octopus into 1 cm bits and put a lump of wasabi beside it. Really simple. I don't think the dish really does anything for the ingredients. Ippudo is well known in the East Coast and it's become the standard to which I compare all other ramen joints I visit. The service is nice and attentive from my experience and the broth isn't so fatty that it coats your mouth with every spoonful (Toki Underground, I'm talking about you). So 4 stars it is. I'd really like it if they had ramen choices that mirror what I see in the comics with the crab on top of it all holding flags. Maybe if I go to Japan...

I had my birthday party at Verlaine and I could not have had a better experience. I absolutely loved all the employees- the staff were helpful, friendly, and accommodating. The food was delicious and the space is beautiful. Overall, an incredible experience and ambiance.

Celebrated Mexico's Independence Day here both Saturday night and Sunday! They had margarita specials and a mariachi playing both nights! It would be perfect if every weekend was like this! The chicken tacos were very tasty and even the chips with salsa were to die for! Because of the friendly staff, the great bartenders and even the welcoming owner, I must say I recommend this place to anyone! I would have given it 5 stars but 13$ for guac is a little too pricey for my budget! But to anyone willing to spend some good money on delicious food then I'd recommend La Pulperia to any touri$t.

I'm in the industry as restaurant owner I know what's to run a business, let tell you this was absolutely amazing I would rate 6 stars for the service. They were so attentive that it amazed me so much. The food was incredible if you go there order appetizer Tete de veau $13 Goat Cheese tarte $12 entree, i liked the most and you have to order it is the pork belly $19. My favorite restaurant in New York.

Very pleasant experience. Â We went today, Mother's Day, for lunch and while just about every other restaurant was packed on this block, Butcher Bar was not, which is a shame. Â We had a great experience. Â The service was friendly and attentive, which isn't hard when only one other table in the courtyard is occupied, but these waitresses were great to us. We ordered a platter of three meats and two sides, although another side of cole slaw came with it anyway. Â First off, the smoked pork belly was so good we got a second portion later. Â Second, those Double-Smoked Burnt Ends are the best thing I had. Â We would have gotten a second portion of those, but I had to finish half of our little girl's pulled pork sandwich. Â Now the beef brisket was too dry for me to enjoy, but the sides of mac 'n' cheese and yummy green beans were demolished in no time. Â I also liked the baked sweet potatoes I tried too. It's a nice little BBQ place, something I think Astoria needed badly. Â It's small, smells amazing, and has a nice little courtyard in the back which is great. Â There is no doubt in my mind that we will be back at Butcher Bar this summer.

What started as a fire ended in embers. I went to Quaint when it first opened several years ago and was blown away. Ive been back many times since, and it seems to be getting progresively worse. The space is, Â as the name suggests, Quaint, and the outdoor garden is a great place to eat on a cool summer nite. However, the food has gotten very sloppy and the menu slimmer and slimmer. The prices would be fair (if not a tad high) if the menu items delivered on their promise. Since your choices for restaurants without flatscreen TVs in sunnyside are next to none, Quaint is worth a look. Just don't expect much.

A gem of a find! A friend and I stopped here after hanging out in the area. The decor was very welcoming, splashed with ambient lighting, wood counter tops and tables. Staff was also very friendly and the bar had a number of craft beers on tap. Let's get to drinking! I originally came in for a few pints but after ordering food, little by little, this quaint place began to set itself apart. It all started with Â the Gado gado. This Indonesian salad mix of greens, eggs, and prawn chips has a remarkable flavor and has a slight spicy kick that immediately won me over. This alone got us to order more food. We also got the Terong bakado which was spicy eggplant, soft and warm but not mushy. Mussels sauteed in a deliciously mild coconut curry with crispy dough to dip in the sauce afterwards. And coconut meatballs with a red puree on the bottom that was phenomenal. I've never had a coconut flavor infused meatball before and this was a treat. I came to learn afterwards that this place was the same place that makes Van Leeuwen, my favorite handmade ice cream sold out of the cream colored trucks around Manhattan. And they served it here as well! I couldn't think of a better way to end a meal. This is a wonderful place to eat if your taste buds are adventurous and is looking for something new, or even a fresh spin on something already familiar.

When I first came to NYC this past summer, I was introduced to Supper early on. Â Very glad about this fact, because Supper is a great Italian spot which happens to be close to my apartment. Â Really fresh pasta and other dishes as well. Â The meatball appetizer is amazing! Â The wine menu can get a little pricey so beware. Â Also, cash only, so make sure to bring some with. Â I'd recommend one of the pasta specials, whatever sounds good, you really can't go wrong. Â Everything is made fresh to order. Â Check out the sister restaurant lil' Frankies, also in the East Village.

Yummmmmmmmmmmmmmmmmmm, que rico! This hole-in-the-wall of a restaurant has great character, friendly service and delicious food. For a little over $9, I enjoyed a huge portion of rice and beans, along with half of a delicious roasted chicken. This is the kind of place where you not only enjoy the food, but you also feel like your money spent is going to a great and deserving group of people.

Our waiter Nick is the only reason I didn't give this place 1 star or no stars, he was polite and personable. The food The menu lacks any sense of a seasonal quality, braised meats and heavy winter dishes. Â Apples and deep dark chocolates on the dessert menu Deviled Eggs - basic Duck Fat Cashews - Boring (small) Nacho Potato Chips - Good Octopus - Tough and not good Bone Marrow - Cold and not properly heated Grilled cheese - they fell apart and had an unpleasant taste to them Pork Belly - small but delicious Bacon Wrapped Dates - overly glazed and sweet Bone Marrow Burger - my friend said this was very tasty Braised Short Ribs - frist off, on a summer menu? No way! secondly, it was TOUGH and DRY! Dry braised meat! Ridiculous! Salmon - okay Pulled pork - overly sweet Skirt steak - nothing special The Drinks Mediocre and not consistent. Â We had four vodka Gimlets among other drinks and none of the four tasted the same.

I'm a big fan of Banh Mi but I've had better. Â  The banh mi place on St. Mark's is much better in my opinion but this is a great little spot for warm weather picnic style sandwiches. I don't reccomend the jewelry.

Northern Chinese style noodles and dumplings reminiscent of the Taiwanese noodle soups and dishes that I grew up with and often crave~ Sadly, I can never seem to find any good Taiwanese style restaurants in Manhattan, or yummy restaurants such as Lao Bei Fang Dumpling House where I can get great hand pulled noodles and ho fun at a super low price - $3.50! They make their dumplings with a thicker dough which I normally find masks the taste of dumplings, but Lao Bei Fang manages to create tasty dumplings using the thicker skinned dough. Â I am very impressed~ Now if only they could open up a small dumpling/noodle house in Manhattan, I would be in heaven...
Food was terrific! Â Brussel sprouts not to be missed. Â Hummus with shrimp -- OMG

Had a craving for something hot after the snow storm we had today and this place hit the spot. I was a little surprised when I walked in because its not your typical pho place - it looks like a bar (presumably because it originally was and they bought out and converted the space). It definitely fits in with the local flare. There isn't a lot of seating, with a handful of two-person tables, two larger tables and half a dozen bar seats. Menu is pretty straight forward with the standard Pho and Banh Mi selections. Reasonably priced ~$9 for a bowl. This was my first time having Grilled Lemongrass Chicken Pho - I was a little skeptical but it turned out to be pretty good! Didn't expect much from the service (as I usually don't at most authentic Asian establishments) but the ladies here were pretty friendly and attentive. There was a family-owned vibe to it, with all the ladies sitting at the end of the counter gossiping about stuff. Will definitely go back again - for now, a tentative 4-stars until proven otherwise.

100 Montaditos is truly a little neighborhood gem--especially on Wednesday night, when they offer $5 plates of selected sandwiches (meat, veggie, Mediterranean, chocolate, or "black label"). I made the mistake of being greedy and ordering 3 such plates (each one has 5 sandwiches), thinking that they are bite-sized. Well, I definitely had 2 days' worth of lunch from the leftovers. The lesson is: don't be greedy. There's a lovely garden in the back that was blissfully laid-back before 6 pm and quickly filled up after 6:30. There's also plenty of expected Spanish-themed drinks like Sangria, some beers, and Albarino at about $5/glass (not happy hour prices, this comes standard). This place is seriously affordable, even with the regular menu prices (three of those sandwiches will fill you up unless you're famished). There are a few small detractors: (1) The cheap tabs have NYU-dents and other Millennials flocking, but that's the target demo. (2) The business model prizes the churning of hundreds of Montaditos to its hungry audience over all else and allocates staff accordingly. You seat yourself and wait until they bring your plate (there's no tracking system with numbers/receipts; they just find you somehow). This can result in order confusion and made it a little awkward in leaving the tip (there's a jar by the register that the staff shares, I guess). Our table was taken over by someone almost the second we got up, so they have plenty of customers. I see this place sticking around.

If you want some of the best cheap eats in NYC, come to Vanessa's for some incredible dumplings, scallion pancakes, and bubble tea. You won't be disappointed! It will be dumpling heaven in your mouth.
I enjoyed my meal. I want to go back and try something I didn't have.

This place is great. Make a reservation! Â Even on a weekday! Â  I'm not someone that knows authentic food, but I do know good food, and Pylos has it. Â It's on a street with lots of other restaurants, but it's worth walking down a little further just for Pylos. Â I'm not going to review all the amazing things that I ate, but they do have great saganaki and pita, stuffed grape leaves and seafood overall. Â I'm not really a lamb eater, but from what I've heard, the lamb here is tasty as well. Service is friendly and fast. Â Also, if you don't know about greek wines, they are willing to help you out with accurate descriptions of the wines and tastings. The decor here makes it a great place for a romantic date, but the space makes it a good place for group dinner as well. Â The one thing that I do have to complain about is that I think that some of the plates are a little expensive for what they are (serving size wise...), but overall, this place is definitely a favorite of mine and I will continue coming back!

I first discovered Crispin and the magical transformative properties of good cider here. Love the decor and laid back ambience and down to earth service. Last time I had grits for brunch which was so good I wanted to lick the plate clean. But I managed to hold myself back. Definitely a great Astoria standby.

You know if I had the recipe for the Parmesan Peppercorn sauce, I would smother it over everything I ate. I would probably eat my fingers by mistake just basking in the glorious deliciousness that is the sauce. So the lady at the counter was extremely helpful in letting us choose the dipping sauces. "This is your first time here?" she said. I guess the deer caught in headlights look came off pretty loudly when we walked through the door. Seconds later, she had a napkin out and had several dipping sauces strategically placed on the napkin. She then proceeded to fry some fries as we looked at the menu and graciously told us to try each sauce(accompanied with the freshly fried fries) and tell her what we liked. We chose Â Parmesan Peppercorn, Mango Sauce, and Mayo... oh dear Jesus... dipping sauce love! We ordered a regular to share between the two of us and without much hesitation went to work. Oh man, truly a blessing in disguise. Now if it weren't for the two ladies working there who were openly gossiping about their boss and one of their coworkers in Tagalog(oh yes, I understood you guys) I proba bly wouldn't have been laughing as hard as I was while we were there. Aside from that, it was a great experience and thank you for popping my Frites cherry.

So ironically, my least favorite thing at Pio Pio was the chicken. The dark meat was fine but the white meat was so painfully dry that my table didn't finish it. My friend and I actually loved the shrimp soup (chupe de camarones) the best. It's huge! They offered to split it into two bowls for us and when we got our bowls we thought they accidentally gave us 2 separate orders. Second best was the Chilean sea bass. It was a small piece of fish (to be expected) but it came with a ton of sautÃ©ed spinach and mushrooms that rounded out the dish. Would definitely come back again though!

Old-school Brooklyn pizzeria in Dumbo. Get ready to wait though, because this place is super popular. I always bring out of town guests here - you have the Brooklyn Bridge, the Promenade, Jacques Torres down the street....what more could you ask for? The crust is perfect - chewy, thin, never greasy. The ambience is down-home Brooklyn and always authentic!
This is too good to be true. It's like home cooked meal below 72nd st. So need this fix once in a whole! Â Great find!

More than we expected. Â Amazing menu with season ingredients. Â I would advise that you expect to pay more than $$, the least expensive item for entrees was the Burger at $14 with the bacon jam. Â But, it was one of the best burgers I've ever had!

Definitely come on a weekday! For two, wait time 5 minutes!! The location is prime, and their pizza is AWESOME, I honestly can say, I've never had a better pizza. Wow its gooood. Everything is so stinkin good and fresh about their pizza! Cash only

This place is always crowded, but worth the wait. Â The soup dumplings are what most people for there for. Â i like them, but the noodles w/ dried bean curd sauce is my favorite along with the pan fried seafood noodles. Â The service is above average compared to other Chinese restaurants.

Food was ok. Tasted like olives garden. Nothing special at all. However, the food portion is HUGE. there were six of us and we ordered spicy wings, rigatoni w white clam sauce and lagsona. we were stuffed and had leftover, so don't over order. Enjoy

An exceptional dining experience, even for New York. Especially memorable for it's simple execution of fresh ingredients and creative takes on traditional Italian. Go with a group so you can share the small pasta portions, Maialino's best dishes. Very warm and knowledgeable service in one of the least pretentious or stuffy Hotel restaurants I've been to.

I am probably going to be beheaded for the following statement but I stand for the truth and the truth must be told: Posto's pizza is much better than Artichoke's, Good Fellas and all the other super famous but overrated pizza joints in the neighborhood. Okay now that this is out let me tell you why: The pizzas here are thin, fresh and aren't very "heavy". I can have 3 slices and still feel good while one slice of Artichoke's white pizza pie makes me feel like I just ate 3 whales with a side of dolphin. You MUST try the shroomtown pizza it's my absolute favorite. SOO flavorful and packed with mushrooms it sends me STRAIGHT to la la land after the first bite. They also have a decent selection of side salads, I like the beets one. I've also tried the Mexican chipotle pizza that I can't remember the name for and that one is also pretty tasty. Definitely try this place out, you won't be disappointed. I just wish they opened late (but it's probably a good thing they don't for the sake of my body's weight).

Ate here tonight and gotta say, this place is awesome! Â From the ambient light decor to the floor-to-ceiling glass walls, we really enjoyed this place. Â I truly dislike tapas (feel like I'm always missing something) but this place has made me rethink my feeble opinions. On a chilly Sat night we waited about 20 mins (or one cocktail) at the bar and were attended to quite promptly. Â The waitress (named Allison, we guessed her name as Gail or Sarah) was very lively and also honest about the menu. Â We chose 4 dishes: Sweet Sausage, Broccoli Rabe, Mushrooms & Taleggio panini; Sauteed Asparagus with lemon & thyme; rissoto with cheese and Â a small arugula-pesto sandwich- my dear God were they great. Â Add to that a nice Barolo and finish with an apricot smeared cheesecake and grappa - and you have the happiest couple in the 'hood. Â Seriously though, if you're unhappy with this meal you're smoking something fierce and should get your taste buds examined. Â We eat out a lot and for a place we found just strolling the streets, this spot easily gets the coveted 5 Yelp stars!

LOVE LOVE LOVE THEM! Although I don't have much of a sweet tooth I am surprised to say that I do love wafels and dinges. I prefer their liege wafel and go for the unlimited dinges for an extra $2. I love buying their spekulous jar. That spread is so yummy and I can put it on nearly anything bread, crackers, apples, toaster wafels etc . As for calorie count...I don't even bother because these wafels are really THAT GOOD ;]

This is one of the staples in Woodside, as this location has been serving up great Thai food for years now. Â The food is very in the middle-americanized Thai category. Â I would recommend this restaurant for people who have never tried thai cuisine. Â Alot of the food have a mild-hot spice and tend to sit very well with people who have never tried Thai food before.
The best halal in the city. make sure you go to the right one.

It was my first time there couple of weeks ago and I just LOVED El almacen. Â There was a bit of a line but we just went to the wine store down the road to pick out a bottle of wine since the waitress kindly told us they have BYOB for open bottle fee for $5. Â  When we finally sit down, we were sitting at a cozy table next to an old wall lamp and that was secluded despite it's sucha busy restaurant. Â The menu was totally worth the wait. Â EVERYTHING on it looked good! Â I got the chilli relleno and my bf got the Tilipia and they were both excellent. We wish we live closer to it so we can try their lunch menu too! Remember it's cash only though!

Really cute place! Ambiance spoke a lot upon arrival, I immediately felt comfortable and at a close friends home. Service was great. Food menu is a bit limited but I definitely want to try out more of their pasta options. Crazy cheap prices, I would come with a group of hungry girls and just order a bunch of things! Unfortunately, I have been here with non drinkers so I really need to fix that so I can get boozy off of their wine menu!
Amazing food, outstanding service! Their specials are even more extensive then the regular menu. A go to for a special occasion!

ADORABLE brunch place. I absolutely loved my breakfast sandwich with perfectly toasted bread, slightly runny fried egg, hash browns on the side. Cozy decor in the restaurant and we waited maybe 15 minutes for brunch on a Saturday. The wait flew by because we got seats at the bar so my friend and I could catch up out of the cold. If you come here (and you should!) try the breakfast sandwich :)

Life Under the Sea.... Â I put about 3 Sebastian's down at the Lobster Joint. Well worth the trip on the temperamental, because the food, service, value and ambiance was spot on. Finding a better seafood haunt than the Joint would be a tough shell to crack... Don't forget Greenpoint is a destination neighborhood,check out the shops and experience authentic, local Polska flavor. Like a Red Hook North for the kielbasa-lover in us all...

Five stars for authenticity. Â I've lived in Paris before, and this is exactly what Americans croon over when they visit that lovely city, a great meal at an affordable price, with a quality wine paring, all wrapped up in a French little bow. I'm amazed, Le Parisien is just like a restaurant you'd find down a back street in Paris. Â  I'm not sure what Â I had, but I assure you it was good and I will return.
Great food reasonably priced. The meatballs and Octopus apps Great pasta and Â The best tiramisu Arber is the man at the bar

In all seriousness -my dreams have come true! Â No need to waste time and energy thinking about cooking dinner at home because on any ole night, we can go to the market at 8pm and mosey on over to this wonderful taco stand for din din. I ordered some guac. cause I could live on it and two tacos: one chick and one cactus. The chicken one was so delicious I could cry and the cactus was not so I went back for another chick. I think slimy cactus is an acquired taste or maybe it's a tradition in Tijuana that I know nothing about and whatever, I respect that! Back to my point: The extra order of guac was not necessary because the 2 chick tacos we're filling and totally satisfying. My honey ordered some quesadillas and said they were awesome. I had a bite of the chick one and it sure was! Â This place is a blessing from the heavens because the neighborhood was really lacking in the area of fresh tacos.

The ramen was cooked to perfection al dente. Best ramen I've ever had! The broth was also very sweet and you could tell it's been simmering for hours especially by the size of the pot which was really a metal barrel. The service was amazing and because we sat by the bar the chefs were literally right in front of us! They seemed like they were having a ball working there. They even posed for our pictures. The hand charred char sew was pretty good and the most exciting part was that we watched the blow torch right in front of us. The food gets 5 starts but the 1 hour + wait for 3 people gives it 4.
good
The interior is really pretty, and the food was good too, the price is reasonable, and the waiters are really cute lol I would totally recommend this place to anyone and everyone !!

I have been there quite a few times. I love sitting outside when there is nice weather because it's a great place to people watch. There is a big business crowd that hits stone street around happy hour and it's a fun atmosphere. I like ordering the old fashioned pizza and splitting it with a friend or two. There pizza is good, not the best I've ever had but it's good and I also like there bread basket.

This cafe is a touch overrated but a place I'd frequent often if I lived in the neighborhood. In fact, i sort of lived in the neighborhood- for a week- and I did come here twice because it's good, affordable food with an interesting menu and a delicious atmosphere. For me, the superlative cuteness of the joint is its best asset. See the pix I submitted-- From the chalkboard outside under the scalloped awning to the bright cupcake decorating the wall behind the espresso machines, you couldn't ask for a sweeter looking spot to rest your feet and sip a cappuccino. Even better, theirs is an excellent cappuccino, the best I had on this trip to NYC. On my first trip I followed my own proclivities and had mozzarella, tomato, and pesto panino. It was tough, I wanted to try them all, but a good caprese is my soul food and I can't seem to find truly wonderful fresh mozzarella in LA. Also it's hard to order a proscuitto when you're facing a wall with a huge diagram of a pig dissected into cuts of meat. So the panino was good- hot and tasty with mozz much more decent than I get in LA. Not a life-changing sandwich that you may expect from the many 5 star reviews, then again its a bit sad if you need a sandwich to change your life, no? I followed with the brownie, since my server concurred with the reviews on that point. It was extremely rich and dense- a bit too rich and chocolately for my tastes. Brownie-wise, I think I like the boxed mix-and-pour best with no nuts added. I couldn't even finish it, something that literally never happens with me and desserts. On my second visit I ordered what I felt I "ought to"-- the prosciutto/blue cheese/fig panino that everyone loves so much. That was me branching out, since blue cheeses are my least favorite and I am not a big fan of cured meats, even in Italy. So you may not be surprised to hear that I did not care much for the panino. Too much sweet-and-sour going on for me. I had a mini epiphany-- I don't care for blue cheese. Â And that is _okay_. Â I don't have to eat it from now on. So there. That day I had another stellar cappuccino. I followed with the cookies and cream cupcake. It was huge in size and also disappointment. It just tasted like a generic pile of calories without the moist sumptuousness to warrant eating it. But it bears repeating I'd be a regular here if I lived nearby. I'd have 2 cappucinni instead getting dessert.

I searched Yelp by star ratings and proximity to our hotel for a restaurant - wow! Â Yelpers did not fail us!!! Â This was a most excellent meal. Â We ordered a hummus/falafel plate, Greek salad, and eggplant dish. Â All were delicious! Â The atmosphere is more of a take out, casual type of place - no table service - it was very clean and well appointed with middle eastern decor, and very friendly employees. Â The only complaint I have is that they charge $1 for a small, albeit delicious, pita, but it was so good I'm not even going to dock a star! Â Yum!!!!

Grimaldi's claim to fame is being the OG pizza place of NYC. Between Joes and Lombardi's, Grimaldis was actually my least favorite. It was still good, but since I actually compared it to the others, it gets a 3. It was more expensive and less flavorful than the other 2 places - plus the pies were smaller. That being said, it is still good NY pizza, with friendly and efficient service - AND conveniently located across the street from Rice to Riches for dessert :).

There is a price increase to 1.25 for four pork dumplings. Â That 25 cents might not seem like much but it is when it is a 25% increase to me. Â This saddens me greatly. Â I guess all good things have to come to an end. The dumplings are still good and the quality varies from batch to batch like always. Â I think there is an price increase for most of their items on the menu.

For authenticity HK is just what I was looking for. I love the fact that HK is on a side street and looks very basic from both the inside and outside. Fo the food Cantonese is the only way to go. Wonton soup has become broth and not much more. Well, not at HK. The food is top notch and so much different then the fake Chinese restaurants all over manhattan.

I heard this place gets crowded and there would be a wait so I made sure I had a reservation before coming in for brunch on a Saturday. Of course, I was running late so I called in and they said they have a 10 minute grace period, Phew! The service was efficient and the food was amazing. The Mac and Cheese was SOOO GOOOD. I would say it's probably the best Mac and Cheese I've ever had. Just the right amount of crust, cheese, salt, ugh, everything about it was just amazing. This "side" does come in a decent portion that'd be good for 2-3 people. I would dare to just order two mac and cheese and call it my entree. It was my first time having this fried chicken and waffle combo and I'm so glad that I chose to have it at Soco. The fried chicken and red velvet waffles were amazing too! I think I'd prefer mine with no syrup and extra powder sugar instead. Regardless, it was still pretty perfect. The skirt steak was cooked medium rare to my liking and it came over a bed of sautÃ©ed spinach and sweet potato hash then topped with two sunny side up eggs and cress. The dish was topped with a smoky sauce that gave the eggs a unique barbecue-tasting flavor. The hash had too much onions for my liking but my guests enjoyed it. The fish and chips were a disappointment. The fish had the strongest earthy, muddy, dirt taste to it and it did not pair well with the kimchee aioli sauce that it came with. I'll never order this dish again. The fries were just okay. I opted not to have the unlimited mimosa hour because I had a minor in the party and didn't want to cause any complications but I'll definitely be back to get my drink on. I also can't wait to try out their other dishes for lunch and dinner.

Food was decent, but nothing to really rave about. A subpar cheese and meat plate, bronzino with far too many bones remaining, roasted half chicken that was not terrible, but certainly overdone. The problem for our table of four was honestly the atmosphere and an incredibly rude service staff. From the minute our 7:30 reservation began we felt rushed. We seated at a table right in the flow of traffic, and were pressed to order quickly. Throughout the meal utensils were hurled at us, and plates were removed the moment 1 person was finished. (meaning everyone else was still eating). After we had two bottles of wine and plenty of food. We were offered the desert menu. The waitress returned a moment later to tell us there was another seating and asked us to pay the check. She assured us we were told this when we sat down (it was now only 9:15 and we were NOT told this at any time) All and all an unpleasant dining experience, for food that really not worth the annoyance.

If you don't eat meat and probably if you do, this place is the bomb spot. I never new about it when I lived in WB, but I'm glad a friend turned me onto on my last visit to NYC. I was a little skeptical of a vegan diner. Even as a vegetarian it was hard for me to envision breakfast without cheese, especially for dinner. It somehow didn't occur to me that everything I can't usually eat at a diner would be fair game in a vegan diner. I had a burrito with fake chorizo and fake cheese. Christ, I don't miss meat often but now when I do, I'll be craving Champ's vegan meat. Â Both of my friends had some sort of Huevos Rancherosish thing. I had a few bights and was cursing my burrito (until I took another bight of it). I'm already a paragraph in and I've failed to mention the plantains. Killer plantains!!!! If you're a vegan, a vegetarian, a lover of fake meat or just anyone who enjoys delicious diner style food, defiantly hit this place up. For diner food it's on the pricey side, but for a lunch or dinner spot in BK it's on the cheap side.

Went to Tuk Tuk last night, only the second time we've eaten in the restaurant. We usually always order delivery, but with our elevator out we were pretty sure they weren't going to deliver. As always the food was delicious. I had one of their new menu items, Ba-Mee-Moo-Dang, best mushroom soup I have had. The broth was delicious, the egg noodles with the roasted pork in the second bowl was amazing. I finished the entire thing. My husband had his usual Duckahollic, it is a wonderful duck dish he gets every time. I usually get the Pad See Ew, never gone wrong with it, always a perfect sauce. Food there has a great presentation that you don't get when you get delivery, but their delivery is always reliable and just as good as eating in the restaurant. I highly recommend if you are living in the area or just stopping by.

All I can say is "WoW" . I'm a big fan of Japanese culture and I've always wanted to try traditional Ramen after watching Goku and Naruto go through like ten bowls wanting more ... I did my research and a few places Naruto Ramen, Ippudo, and Totto. Totto was my first choice because I heard some much about it and the reviews were promising. I honestly have to say from the three this has to be my favorite spot! My personal opinion when I think traditional I'm not looking for a huge open space with lavish decor (though it does look nice on a date). I prefer the attention to be placed into my meal, especial if I could be waiting from anywhere between 20min to hour and half (worth the wait) to be seated! Totto gets packed but the crowd is great, full of energy and smiles. The Spicy Ramen (pork) is AMAZING!!! I live on the Long Island but I'll take a trip to the city just to have my Totto Ramen! Naruto Ramen was horrible Â and Ippudo is great too but not as great as Totto, which I believe they try to make up for in Decor. Hope this review helps but if you're uncertain about a Ramen spot stick between Ippudo and Totto (Totto being the #1 Choice)
Great spot!! great music!!! Great staff!!!!! Â  sometimes its alittle to crowded for my taste but def one of the better chill spots!!

My friend let me choose a place to eat last weekend so I decided to come here because I read on a article how some chef's enjoy eating here plus I look over there website and it sound very promising. I got there first and lucky we got a reservation because this place was getting pack and they were just open too. I sat down and order myself a beer and a cold sake to drink while looking over the menu. i knew exactly what I wanted already from reading the menu online but i needed to pass some time so I look over it anyway. The hotpot was the highlight so i needed to choose that plus they have collargen inside. How can you pass that up?? My friend finally show up so she look over the menu and we decided on the hotpot plus a few items to start with. We order the yellowtails sashimi, foie gras sushi and something else but i can't really remember it. yellowtail-it look nice but the fish wasn't fresh enough for me plus they put fried shallot or garlic on it so it took the taste away from the fish foie gras-sound delicious but when it came, it was ok....surprisely enough i was quite disappointed hot pot-it was hugh and there were tons of veggie it in so my friend like it alot. I wanted to try their dumpling but i only found like 2 pieces in the whole hot pot. It was ok, nothing special. The broth itself was ok, a little toward the bland side. We also got the ramen noodle for extra $4 and guess what?? it was dried noodle that you get from opening a noodle package and If i knew that in the first place then FORGET it. It wasn't even special In the end, I walked away buzz and quite disappointed. Next time I am not going read a stupid article about some stupid chef's who like it. YES he is white so he think anything EXOTIC will taste good. I should just follow my own path, at least i can't blame anyone afterward lol

Def a hidden gem in the Bedford-adjacent restaurant scene. ALL of the food here is great (think "high end comfort food"); I have had just about everything on the menu. My personal faves include: AMAZING truffle burger! Maybe the best burger in Williamsburg. Jambalaya that is the perfect level of spicy - very very tasty! Mac n Cheese - crusty on top and creamy on the inside. BYOB - another plus. Also, Tom, the owner, always comes out and makes an effort to personally speak to each table. I love it and will continue to go back often!

Sad to say over-hyped. I should have seen this coming. Â In most reviews about this place, words like "bohemian", "no frills" and "value" always come up but what about the burger itself?!?!? I get it. Â The whole nostalgia of coming here during your college years and getting a decent burger for cheap while having the option of getting a McSorley's is cool. However, does that really constitute it as one of NYC's best burgers??? I ordered a medium-rare bistro burger (BLT and cheese) that was cooked right but it lacked flavor. Â The bacon was overcooked to the point where it cracks and falls out of your burger. Â The rest of the toppings and bun was ok but nothing special. Â  In the end, there are much better burgers out there that are made with better quality meat and flavor. Â Its a burger that you can easily duplicate in your own kitchen. Â Its not bad but not great as well.

Came here for lunch for something different than a butter bagel and I loved it. Â I got a small portion but found out you needed a $10 minimum to use Debit (midtown location) so I ended up adding a shrimp and an egg to my pork katsu. Â  I think the dish was just perfect if you are craving Japanese curry. I will probably go again but ill bring cash next time.

Props for being out there in freezing weather. This place is like an institution. Been 3 years since I last came. Now I have a kid. Feels a little soup Nazi-ish but didn't have any probs. the $10 big daddy was Delish. They didn't skimp on the meat. I have been cutting down on rice as I've been getting overly sleepy on it. Whatever you do do NOT park at C town. There are signs and it's not fair to the people shopping there. Anyways got that over yellow rice with red and white sauce. My little one loved it too (without the red of course)! The other people after me were lackadaisical about where to stand in line and order. The big dude taking orders was NOT cool w that. Â Also pay the guy at the end on the right near the passengers window. Was just as good as I remembered it. Plus it is right by the Xmas tree and wreath sellers so it was kinda nice. This place rocks. Simple as that. The food, the wine - everything has been obsessed over and worked on until it's just right. It's high-end, sophisticated food presented in an unfussy, elegant manner - just my speed. Everything's good, but I enjoy trying some of the more outlandish items - like cox combs - which I find to be just as tasty as old standbys like skirt steak. Sit at the counter and watch the guys work - it's impressive. Mario Batali, you've done it again!

Wow - unique and amazing venue! If you love meat in a no-thrills but quirky venue, this is for you! You pay by weight, grab a beer and sit at a bench - great for groups and quick stops! Â The sides were also delicious - it would be very (too!) easy to over-eat here! Highly recommend!
Authentic southern BBQ with simple menu concept, loved it. Great food, easy service, all the essentials.

I've been coming here for years and I'm two stamps away from getting my free notepaper cube. I can't wait to go back and get my prize. I think that's what the card is for. (--) Â too much packaging (+) they speak to you in Korean

You will know it by the long line that awaits the majesty of The Halal Guys. They open late, get the chicken and rice with lots of white sauce and a few dabs of red sauce and you are good to go. Â This is the perfect late-night food because it's really filling and you get a lot of it. Â We went there aftering doing MOMA on the Friday free night and it was the perfect way to eat out. Â There's a lot of food and I had plenty left over for the next day. Â Make sure to get plenty of white sauce, because it is so good. Â This is a food truck...so seating is where you can find it.

Burrito Box offers a huge, quality burrito, but it is just a bit too expensive ($10.15 with guac.) They really need a burrito-bowl option like other take-out mexican restaurants. Â The burrito is just too filling (especially with the chips).

Wonderful ambiance and food! Â Tapas were VERY GENEROUS as compared to the size of standards tapas and delicious! Â Highly recommend the squid cooked in it's own ink and papas alioli. Â Call in beforehand to make reservations during flamenco timeslots (one at 8:30pm and another at 10:30pm on Saturday). Â Not every table has a good view of the dance floor (which is why I rated this a 4 and not a 5), however the sound permeates throughout the restaurant (pretty loud). Â Bon apetite and enjoy the show!!

4.25 stars. Ordered the shawarma sandwich and a side of hummus. Â The shawarma had a generous serving of lamb, and came with some lettuce and onions and sesame sauce. Â The lamb was very tender, but a bit too charred. Â A bit more lettuce, onions, and tomatoes would've been nice, but overall a very tasty sandwich! The hummus was delicious! A small side serving with extra yummy olive oil, it was accompanied with slices of fluffy pita! Â  I'll definitely be back for lunch again!

One of my favorite spots to eat in Astoria. The food is amazing always throwing for a loop. The service is better than most places in Astoria, my server Kathy is sweet smart and quirky. Always a great time when she's around!

Went there at 5pm, the bar was almost full, every table was empty and 'reserved', except the two tables alll the eay in the back. Managed to find seats, and ordered lychee martinis. at 5 bucks each they couldn't be beat. The place filled up (including the reserved tables) and while there were people standing behind me ordering, there was no spilling, no overreaching, and no attitude. Good mix of a crowd with no obnoxiousness by any of the crowds that I outlasted. Music was ok. Would I go back? Definitely, just not yet, I don't want to burn myself out this place just yet.

i've been here often enough but never reviewed it - but it stands out from others on this street, so definitely worth a mention. Â  i enjoy the preview of coming attractions, the array of desserts that greet me upon entering, as though a good meal is a means to a ricotta cheesecake finale, but first things first ... i know it's been said that the service is impeccable but it can't be overstated that there are plenty of people and all attentive, in the right place at the right time yet not overbearing. Â  last time i had a hankering for something more simple, an all-time favorite which unfortunately is not on their regular menu. Â i asked the server if i could order off the menu and he unhesitatingly he invited me to - i ordered pasta alla putanesca. Â i didn't expect it to be perfect, but it was, spicey with the tomatoes and capers, two different types of olives, the hint of anchovies. Â  i've never been disappointed here. Â the space is large - it is sometimes full, sometimes empty, but we always mange to get a table. Â i'm especially impressed at how accommodating the place is and how warmly the staff invites us. Â  on one hand, the prices are high; on the other hand, i just about always manage to make a lunch of it the following day. Â  five stars.

So my sis and I decided that hot wings, cheese fries, and hot dogs from greys was not enough for dinner. Decided to try dos toros. Out of chipotle, qdoba, oaxaca, dos toros the by far the best fast food mexican food. I LOVE mexican food so impressing me is difficult. I got the burrito bowl with steak asada and guac. "this is the best food I've ever had in my life." I kept saying this to my sister while eating it. I think this will be my new go-to place for any meal. I love dos toros. Kind of reminds me of a really good Mexican place in London called Tortilla.

Why is there a line half way around the block? Â Because this is some of the best street food in NYC -- indeed, some of the best food in NYC in any format. Â The choices are simple -- chicken, lamb, or a combo. Â (I always choose the combo.) Â Whichever you select, you will have as much mouthwatering rice and meat as you can possibly eat -- all for just $5 or $6. Â Be sure to try both the white and the red sauces, but you might want to ask for a small container of the red sauce so that you can apply it in small doses (it burns like fire in anything but tiny quantities). THREE POINTERS: Â (1) The same guys have 3 or 4 carts within a block or two but the most popular -- and, I assume, the best -- is on the SW corner of 6th Ave & W 53rd. Â (2) They don't open for business until the evening. Â So whatever other cart may be in this location at lunch time is unrelated. Â (3) Â Just tell them "to go" if you won't be eating it there. This may seem obvious, but it isn't. Â You'll see half a dozen people who didn't make this request struggling to get their own lid on the container. Â (It's harder than it looks.) Â Plus, when you ask for it to-go, they give you a bag and sauces on the side.

Roaming around in the West Village I stumbled on this place. Loved the yelp reviews it had and decided to try. I ordered the Spinach Gnocchi. As other reviewers have said - it was totally amazing!!! I will be back as much as my budget allows to me come here because I have become a big fan.

I have never had a bad experience at Cafeteria. Â I usually try to stop by when I'm in town. Â The food is always on point and the staff is trendy, friendly and cute. Â  (Miguel is the bomb) Â They also stay open late....so if you need some great food to soak up the liquor you just drank....look no further. Â  A few notes for the first-timer: Must haves: Â  Chicken & Waffles, Mac-n-Cheese Spring Rolls and of course....The Rude Margarita, complete with a pepper for that extra kick.

In the last three months, I've been here three times. Twice for dessert, and once for lunch on a weekday holiday. I highly recommend the hojicha anmitsu if you're into traditional Japanese desserts, and the black sesame crÃ¨me brÃ»lÃ©e, no matter what you're into. The portions aren't huge for lunch, but I was very satisfied by the unagi kabayaki, available on Mondays. Their tea is also very good, as you would expect from a place with tea in its name. Cash only, and it seems to get very crowded on the weekends, but it's definitely a great place to go to on weekdays!

Love this place!! The food is awesome and the ladies always smile and ask if we like the food or nay. So sweet! Every time I go to Korean town, I always go to bcd... I had miss Korea once, wasn't as good as bcd hahaha

Being a Paleo fanatic I was so psyched for this place to open as there is nothing in the City -- to the best of my knowledge -- with Paleo as a concept. And to top it off, it is right near where I live. Imagine the possibilities. Â Now, even though I have eaten there several times (again, there are no Paleo options and only in dire situations will I still eat here!) I am not happy with this place and wish it made major improvements. The food is way over-priced and to be honest not that great. I can cook most of the things they make and was hence expecting a lot more creativity. It is almost impossible to get out of there with a simple takeout meal for under $20 as apart from the chicken meal ($20!!!) the way things are proportioned is very confusing and illogical. They have so many options in a cold bar setting that they will not warm up for you, but even if they did, why can't they pick fewer things and have them hot and fresh? Further, they have to measure each cold item one at a time, so if you wanted a meat and two sides, they literally have to weigh each one at a time and then put it on a plate. It takes way too long for food that is a slight step up from the Wholefoods salad bar. Did I mention how expensive they are? Last time I was there $12 bought me two tiny pieces of turkey meatloaf served cold without a side dish. I was starving afterwards! They used to have really good chicken wings that were free range and reasonably priced, but I guess that wasn't good enough for them and they scrapped them from the menu. Â  Finally, and this is annoying, they put these little quotes and words of wisdom on a sign outside from time to time. While I am not a nutrition expert, I do know the difference between grassfed, free range, pasture raised and all the other words of Paleo wisdom. Apparently, their expert doesn't as I have seen numerous signs with mistakes on them.

First time trying Locanda's brunch, and I found it quite tasty. I went savory and had the roasted chicken which hit the spot after a late night. Our server was good spirited in dealing with a few of our brunch-mates who had seen better mornings. They take reservations which is a huge plus, lines can brutal Sunday mornings. Definitely recommend for a Saturday or Sunday late morning.

My bf and I were in the Brooklyn area for a weekend away. It was 4:00 on a Saturday and we were trying to find a place to eat a late lunch. Most restaurants in the area were closed until they re-opened for dinner, except for this place, so we gave it a try. It was fantastic. I got the black bean burger. It was on a fresh roll, and the salad it came with was simple but had an amazing flavor, not sure what they put on it. Would definitely go back to this place if we're ever in the area again.

Was expecting big things after the hype from friends and via yelp. The Halal Cart on 53rd and 6th is super famous and has been recommended to us enthusiastically by many friends and family. We came across the cart at the corner and you can't miss it because it's the one cart which the humungous line. Luckily these guys have it down to an art and keep the line moving. Â For only $6 you get a plate of rice with two wedges of pita bread and your choice or lamb, chicken or combo meat. Â They also have a La Vic's-like signature white sauce.

Totally been lazy about my reviews lately and have a lot of catching up to do...actually this location is the reason I am Yelping again. Â Last Saturday I was hit with an odd desire for Chicken and Waffles...I needed it that day and nothing was stopping me. Â I looked on the phone for NJ spots for it and found the top 10 locations in NY. Â My wife was in the LES during the afternoon with her girl and low and behold when I picked her up we were less than a half a mile away - which was awesome because I wanted to go here more than the other 9 locations anyway. Â We got there around 9-9:30 and it was pretty busy but no wait (score 1)...its pretty much a typical trendy NYC spot that tries to look like a hole in the wall but puts out a candle and nice settings rather than full tilt $h17hole. Â I am a huge geek for milk shakes and as the self proclaimed Grand Puba of the MSC (Milk Shake Crew - a loose knit group of other milkshake heads) was uber stoked to see they offered boozed up milk shakes...I order the White Russian and it was banging - a lil heavy on the booze side but most wouldnt complain about that. Â We also got the lollipop buffalo chicken wings which were banging...just enough bite, not hot for the sake of being hot and very flavorful. Â Jax ordered the Turkey Chili, I didn't try it but she said it was great. Â I, of course got the Chicken and Waffles and after my initial craving in the afternoon, almost 9 hours later my itch was scratched. Â The fried chicken was incredible and ranks up there with Redheads...flatout awesome - they serve it only with butter maple syrup rather than maple syrup, melted butter and a mix like some but they nailed it on the mix as it was delcious and pulled all the flavors together. Â The waffle was not as cripsy as I would have liked (litterally the only thing my picky a$$ can gripe about) but all together I was very, very pleased with the experiance. Â I would like to go back again when I have yet another Chicken and Waffle craving but def gotta try the others on the list first.

This is a traditional Japanese restaurant, they have sushi but I think their best dishes are their entrees. Seems most come wt an egg custard (never had it before, I think it's a special thing, it's not sweet but seems popular, I didn't prefer it myself). I had a sashimi on rice bowl and it was very good. The girl next to me at the bar ordered a Japanese style fried chicken dish that looked amazing, kinda got envious. Only thing that bothered me was that they were supposed to open at 5:30 and there was a big downfall of rain and everyone has to wait outside til they opened the doors at 5:40 just as the rain began to stop. But once inside and seated, the ambience was lovely and the staff were as sweet as pie:)

Overall, this is a pretty good pizza joint in NYC. Â I've had some good ones in NYC but this is up there at the top. Â We went with my family of 15 people and they did a real good job at serving us and suggesting the right amount of food. Â There are a few things that I didn't like: 1) They didn't like when I asked for ranch. Â I don't know when pizza became all snobby but I've noticed lately that when I ask for ranch at pizza places, it's looked down upon. Â I don't care if you like A1 sauce with your steak or ranch with your pizza, you're the customer! Â If I want some ranch, give it to me. Â If you don't have it, just say you don't have it and leave the attitude in the kitchen. Â Hehe - I just like ranch with everything. 2) Bottle of soda is literally a mini bottle...with no free refills...for $15,000...I guess it's a NYC thing but I'm used to having a large diet coke with my meals. 3) They charge $25 for us to bring our own cake and eat it there. Â Now I would understand if it were small party and they were trying to be cheap with not ordering dessert at the restaurant BUT we were a party of 15!
