Â Either 1) we didn't want to pay for 15 desserts because we already paid for a bunch of pizza/salads/drinks/etc or 2) we just like the cake at the dessert shop or 3) they don't have cakes so we ordered one. Â Don't charge us $25 to cut it up - if you have to, try to consider waiving to larger parties as a favor for bringing in a large party. =D

There is no reason to go any place else for high quality Japanese shabu shabu. Get the sirloin beef set, and you'll be all set to conquer the world/ that video game/ your foozeball opponent/ that mosh pit at the concert of that band/ a phonecall with your grandma. Whatever it is, this is all the fuel you need. Don't forget to ask for fresh garlic to add to the dipping sauce. And the spicy plum paste thing that is already on the table adds a nice tangy touch. You also get yummy red bean ice cream with the set.

O-M-to the M-F-G this place is pretty rockin. Â Very seldom do I walk around this part of town, but whenever I do I see the fat line and am tempted to wait. Â The ramen isn't that spectacular in itself, but the broth...the mf'n broth! Â  It's like magic. Â They can seriously put a packet of top ramen in that broth and sell it for $50, people will still wait in line. Â You can tell there's a lot of heart and soul in the broth - and it shows. Â Even though the wait can be a bit atrocious, it's definitely worth the wait if you're fiending for your ramen fix.

Came to Jack & Nellie's on a lazy snowy Saturday post noon after much deliberation over where and what and how to eat. Spent less time on deciding on the menu once I heard salmon lox over eggs benedict was one of the specials. The eggs were not as runny as I would've hoped but the balance between the saltiness of the lox and the neutrality of the eggs was pretty spot on. Did not get a chance to try any drinks. Â  To note: The neighborhood seems friendly enough, parking was a bit difficult.

Came here for Valentine's Day and were seated without a wait. Â The restaurant looks small, but there's a downstairs with different rooms. Â Pretty cool, unique atmosphere. Â Food smell traveled throughout, though. Â Seated downstairs, you really don't benefit from the live music, so that was a bummer. Â When we left and passed through the front room, I felt like I missed out. Downstairs is romantic and nicely decorated. Â Food was very good. Â Had the croquetas de jamon serrano (serrano ham croquettes, tomato salsa) for an appetizer. Â Entree, I had the salmon rio miel (salmon, orange glaze, onions, string beans, hearts of palm). Â The dish overall was very tasty, the salmon, however, was much chewier than I (or anyone, for that matter) would prefer. Â Bf had the pollo guajira (chicken breast, sweet plantain, mozzarella, mushrooms, zucchini, white wine sauce) which he simply described as "Nom nom"--his portion was pretty big. Â For dessert, we shared the bombon cubano (warm chocolate cake, molten core, vanilla ice cream) which was absolutely delicious, though not the best when I recall similar desserts. Â Still, highly recommended. Â Puerto Rican bf well-versed in Spanish cuisine was happy with the meal. The deduction in stars is mostly due to our unenthusiastic, unwelcoming and never present waiter who undoubtedly didn't want to be there. Â Perhaps because it was Valentine's Day, or he just hates his life, not sure. Â We constantly had to ask for him, whether it was for water, to order, to pay, etc. Â He forgot things we asked for and certainly never checked to see if we needed anything. Â Upon being seated, (and after we flagged him down) we inquired about the Valentine's Day Prix-Fixe. Â When we decided against ($150 for two, which he regarded as a really good deal, though, if you did the math, wasn't Â much of a deal at all depending on what you ordered), and ordered off the menu, he seemed annoyed. Â  The service wasn't entirely terrible, we had an excellent busboy who we were tempted to hand the entirety of the tip to. Â  Would go back sans that waiter and if seated upstairs.
I love this place! get the buckwheat pancakes. Yum
I love this seafood restaurant.. yummy food and reasonable price!!

Part 3 of my afforable/ trendy resto visits. A clusterfuck if I do say so myself. You either have to have a PhD or be one of B.F. Skinner's rats to navigate Eataly. The marketplace runs in the middle of the restaurants, which results in a chaos of people trying to pay for their goods, drink a glass of wine, or stand waiting for their tables. There are restaurants at Eataly, only it's impossible to find them because they are so badly sectioned off from the other stations. When Di and I eventually found the pasta pizza resto (this was my "I just ran 6 miles and I'm cheating on gluten" type of nights), we found out there was an hour wait. We put our names in and were redirected to the 'Piazza" to order wine. The wine was actually good but we "weren't allowed to sit at one of the Piazza tables" since we weren't eating anything at the "Piazza". Hello! We were told to kill time at the Piazza by the Pizza resto. It's not like we were just 'getting a drink'! How is our money at the pizza place less good at the piazza?! It's the same fucking corporation! That left a horrible taste in my mouth. Finally, we were seated at the pizza place. I ordered a prosciutto/ arugula pizza that actually tasted delicious. Di got pasta. It was so al dente that it might as well have been raw. Nasty. She wound up helping me with my pizza. 3 stars is probably generous. My pizza was in fact awesome, but the headache of Eataly itself will not warrant future visits. Good pizza places in Manhattan are a dime a dozen. Sure, it's cool that Eataly serves 'authentic Italian products' but it's certainly not worth the hassle.

There's not much that I can say about this place that I haven't already. Â The ramen was delicious and the pork buns were so damn good. Â The pork buns, definitely the best pork buns I've ever had EVERRRRRRRRRR. The service is top notch, although the only real thing that can dock a star is the price. Â Its about 25 per person for the meal. Ouch, for a ramen meal, but once in a lifetime meal so its worth a try!

My girlfriend and I went here for brunch yesterday and unfortunately we will not return. She had been there many times and always had a fantastic experience. Let me start with the good. The food was fantastic. Fresh and very tasty. My Bellini, while 9 dollars, hit the spot and the fruit puree used to make it was top notch. Unfortunately our waiter was the problem here. He was smug from the start and treated us like garbage. After we sat down i noticed that our table was very wobbly so I asked if we could be moved to another table or have it fixed. He said he would fix it and preceded to climb under the table and start jostling it all over the place. Our drinks were spilling all over the table so my GF and i grabbed our drinks and held them up for about 5 min while he continued to try and fix the table. After we had ordered, he proceeded to ignore us for the rest of the meal. My water remained empty for the rest of the time while we observed him filling other patrons glasses. After our food arrived he did not stop by to see how our food was or acknowledge our existence. We finished our meal and sat there for about 10 min waiting for our plates to be cleared but no such luck. I asked for our check and even when he brought us the bill no words from his mouth, a grunt, and the plates remained. When my GF was trying to sign the bill she had no room to do so as her plate was still on the table so I grabbed her plate and made a little noise as I did so and stacked our plates in front of me. Our server was at the table next to us and saw me do this and still would not come by to clear our table! We we left him a very generous 15% and got outta there. It is unfortunate as this place has fantastic food but this poor schmuck has soured my palate and I will not return.

The knife-sliced noodles (dao xiao mian) here are amazing and authentic. They're wide, thick and chewy strips that are basically just shaved off a ball of dough with a knife, and are the perfect al dente pasta. They have seven different varieties of noodles in different shapes and textures. And at $5, you can afford to try 'em all at some point. I had the beef soup with knife-sliced noodles, which came with spinach and a little sprinkling of preserved pickled vegetables (zha cai). I added a little bit of fresh cilantro and a spoon of the homemade chili oil, and I was in beefy, brothy, noodley heaven. The beef was a little bit tough and tendony, but had such great flavor that I didn't really care- I was focusing on the noodles. I also tried the dumplings, and I was blown away. They had the perfect skin- not too thick and not too thin- and just crispy enough. The meat filling was the best part- unlike some dumpling places, where the meat can be soggy, mushy, or sketchy in other ways, the pork was delicious in its own right instead of just being a secondary part of the dumpling. The best part? The dumplings are under $4 for a WHOLE PLATE. Yum. Reminds me of the noodle stands that I frequent when I'm in Taipei- just cleaner and a lot closer :)

I was DYING for tapas, having just spent weeks in Spain. When my friend called and suggested the village, I chose this spot. The wait was minimal, considering our visit on a Friday night at 8pm! Las Ramblas in Barcelona is NOT the place to grab delicious tapas, but the one in the West Village sure is. I would keep your party to a minimum though, this place is the size of a walk-in closet. The best tapas were the croquettas (pockets of deliciousness), lamb chops, spinach and shrimp in garlic sauce. And, the wine list was full of my favorites from Spain! We'll be back soon.

not worth HALF of the price. I have been here before and understood there is usually a wait however last week it was a bit extreme. The hostess asked if my whole party was here - yes 4 ppl, and then said okay 20 minutes max 40. We ended up waiting 1 hour. I kept telling my friends the food was worth it but they just kept looking at Jaques across the street hoping i would stop being so persistent. FInally the wait was over and we were crammed into a tiny space where peoples asses were in our faces while we were trying to eat and have a good time. When the waitress came to place our table settings she gave us each a napkin in front of us Â and then threw the forks and knives onto the middle of the table. For the tiny table that it was this action seemed SO harsh and barbarian. Reminded me of what my mom would do when i was 8 years old and she was busy with other things, except with a spoon, never knives or forks. The food i kept raving about, in the end did not match my expectations, and failed to justify the wait. To add insult to injury the bill was heinous. To wait an hour for food, get terrible service, and feel rushed out with a crowd of ppl in this tiny restaurant all mashing their asses near our food was just a gross experience. In the end we all had to laugh that i am so terrible at picking restaurants and that i was never allowed to choose a place again. Oh and the drinks were weak. I had been here before and remembered the drinks being good but that was a huge contrast from before to now. My friend told something to the waitress about it possibly being made stronger and she said "its a standard recipe" Well the recipe sucks Cafe Habana. - and never will i be foolish enough to return. On top of all this in house disgrace, when i got home i threw up and i believe i got food poisoning from this place.
AMAZING BRUNCH. Some of the best biscuits EVER. slow whisked scrambled eggs were really good -- like cheesy, buttery grits. cool place and staff...my new favorite brunch spot!

Holy Dumplings. This place is much larger and more aesthetically pleasing than Prosperity Dumpling down the street. This is helpful when it's cold and you need.to. stand inside and wait. I'd say it's about equal in deliciousness though. The dumplings are tasty (I prefer the boiled pork & cabbage as well as the pork buns), the staff is super friendly, and there's a huge window so you can watch the guys in the back stuffing & folding the dumplings... very cool. Oh, and you can get to dumpling heaven for two people under $10. No brainer.

Good brunch spot. Lots of rich foods which makes it a great stop to cure your hangover during your walk of shame home after last night's bender. Tight space though, so if you're still stumbly, you might spill the syrup on the next table over.

yummy!!! yummy!!! Just off Montrose too? and the customer service was awesome... bit of gristle on the 4th out of 4th order I didn't like is all. Other than that it's right by duck duck bar and their awesome prices (nam nam & duck duck) are right on!!!

I'm not a vegan or vegetarian. Â I love meat! But my good friend wanted to try this spot and I'm glad she did because I'm hooked! Â I tried the Fiesta roll, Spicy mang roll (my fav), Mushroom roll and all three were amazingly good! Â I tired a piece of their veggie brownie and it was also yummy. The workers are so friendly, the place is clean and food is delicious I'll definitely be back!

I have mixed feeling about ippudo. First of all ramen is supposed to be a low budget, quick eating type of food. My Japanese friends would be shocked to hear that I went out for ramen for dinner and even more so that I waited over an hour to eat it. But I love ramen so I had to eat here. That being said, the ramen was awesome. I had the akamaru modern ramen. The broth was the key. It had this creamy garlicky taste that makes it unique. The noodles itself were on par. The pork chasu was great. Nice portion, tasty, fatty...mmmm! I also had the pork bun and I agree with the other reviews that they are pretty fantastic too. They treat their pork well there! I've been to both totto and ippudo. Totally different places. The atmosphere in ippudo is more upscale and trendy. It was 15 bucks for the ramen which is dang expensive for a bowl of noodles. I would go back again, but it's not somewhere I would be going to every week. So my rating is solely based on the food. If I took account the price and wait it would be 3 stars.

Went here yesterday service was quick and easy. I don't usually eat Crepes but I had a pay pal offer so I went out and gave it a shot. I had the chocolate nut party and it was really good ! I also had a vanilla shake and that was ok. It's really small in here though it's a stop order and eat on the go type of thing because there's only space for 2 ppl to sit in. Staff was very friendly btw

I have been to this place twice and after the third time, I don't think I will go back. i went there with a friend for dessert. We ordered a set of chef's selection and they all came scatteringly without a complete presentation. The guy waiter was rude. We also added 5 bucks for the tea with the set. They ended up charging us 2 dollar more because two people were drinking it. Ridiculous! We gave them cash and the woman was requesting 18% of tip and asking if we wanted changes back. Yes, we do. The place only cares about money. They take no credit cards no matter how much you ordered and you always have to order two sets for two people. Their food is cheap home made food and but they charge way more than how much it costs them to make it. IRS should do an audit at this place to see how much tax they invaded by taking only cash, probably the only place in St. marks that does not take credit cards.
Regular food to me .. I had the chicken tacos which seemed like small burritos... Would I come back again? yes but I wont get the tacos
Fast, Cheap, & Indian....What more can you ask for. the Portions are small yes, BUT that just gives you an excuse to eat more then one.
Visiting from DC. Salmon lunch combo is legit!! Â Freshest salmon I've had at a reasonable price.
Great food, great prices. Â Excellent falafel!

I love it when the critics like Adam Platt from NY Mag write negative reviews and the entire place is packed and booked solid. Â It accurately portrays the value of his profession. Â =) This was a wonderful restaurant with interesting dishes that were wonderful in their (seeming) simplicity. Â Yes, the lobster appetizer is well worth it and delightful. Â The salmon dish was prepared perfectly; if you like your fish cooked until it's jerky this will not be your place - it was barely seared. Â Perfect. Â Bartender made some excellent drinks and the waitstaff was fun and friendly. I will definitely be thrilled to eat there again!

this place is Peter Lugars... but in Manhattan. this is a more of a old-world, antiquated european tavern. dark, yellow lighting, brass-tipped wood.... i think the floor was tiled. basically none of my friends finished their black label burgers. i heard about all the hype but 1) you couldn't really eat the burger, the volume was unmanageable, 2) the meat was too lumpy and firm, 3) it was dry, 4) it was too salty. the marrow was good. but how can you go wrong with marrow? it's kind of like making a bad burger.. it can only be so bad. i probably would've paid $18 max for this burger. it wasn't worth the price. if you're in the area... go to Corner Bistro for like half the price. maybe less.

My 3 previous reviews of this place have been filtered out by Yelp's obviously crude and poorly-tuned filter. I might jokingly say "Help! I'm a prisoner in Yelp's program!" I persist because I enjoy seeing whether honest human communication can survive in an increasingly computerized world. I find this the most comfortable and enjoyable restaurant in the neighborhood, lunching there once a week on chicken in a few forms or liver or portobello (the sandwich is a very nice construction) or papardelle with either Bordeaux, Malbec or Cote de Rhone. Mussels once in a while. In almost two years, believe it or not, only a single dish (cauliflower soup) failed to please me. Perhaps it is best that my reviews be censored because it is getting increasingly crowded at lunchtime. Happy New Year!
Too expensive for what you get. Very tasty, but not worth it.

I first discovered Gyu-Kaku in L.A. and I turned cartwheels when I heard it was coming to NYC. Now that it's in the theatre district, I haz a happy. I love coming here with groups of friends, and it's great for a romantic date as well. I wouldn't bring a toddler but it's fun for kids who are old enough to know not to touch hot things and please don't grab Mommy's beer. You can get an awesome deal here, but you can also get carried away and end up draining your bank account before you know it. If you come with friends, make sure they aren't those kind of friends who always manage to slip away having only handed someone a $20 when they had the filet mignon and three bottles of wine. We all have those friends. Luckily, I don't go out to dinner with those friends, so I've only had great experiences here. The food is great, it's so much fun to embrace the chaos and cook it yourself, and the camaraderie of that experience can't be beat. Go during happy hour and get a course menu and a couple of Asahi beers and go crazy. It'll cost you about $30/per person and you get a lot of options! The service can be a little spotty. Sometimes they bring things out in a weird order, or they forget things. Just be clear and keep asking for what you want.
Food was ok, nothing amazing. Pricey for overall experience.

UPDATE: They have all the sports, and are good about changing a TV if you want to watch a random game. Will fill a growler (from anybody, not just their own branded ones). My go to sports bar in the area if I am intending to eat anything.

So this review really goes out to Dolores and Randolph for turning around a horrible experience into loyal guests that will definitely return. We arrived early for our reservation and then waited 15 minutes to be seated, when asked when our table would be ready we were told another 10 minutes (it was actually less, but wow really?). We ordered some coffee- which we would have expected to be much stronger, it wasn't. Anyway, while eating my sister discovered a small piece of plastic in her lemon ricotta pancakes -- not a big deal, I've been in the industry for 7 years... unfortunately it happens - I just did not expect it to happen here. Overall though the food was delicious, we started out with the steak tartara which was really great. Everyone truly enjoyed their entree's as well - they portions were decently sized, everything was fresh, hot and extremely tasty. The service throughout the entire meal was on point, our server was very attentive and truly did whatever he could to meet our needs and make sure that we had an enjoyable brunch. After he could tell we were a bit disgruntled, he sent Dolores over to check on us. Her hospitality could not have been better, not only was she concerned but her concern was genuine. Brunch ended up being on the house and we were given one of every dessert. Of course you can throw free things at people at make them happy, but what really made us happy was her overall concern and desire to make sure that we walked out of her restaurant having a positive experience and wanting to come back. Well, she surely did just that and left an ever lasting impression of how awesome the management team really is at Locanda Verde. Great food and great hospitality -- we will definitely be back very soon!

We arrived at 2pm for brunch on New Year's Day expecting to wait awhile. Â For two of us, the wait was 3-3.5 hours, but we expected as much, and we put our name down. We ordered the clam chowder (that came with a warm biscuit), which was delicious and the highlight of the meal. Â We also had the blueberry pancakes, fried chicken sandwich, and a side of apple chicken sausage patties. All of these things were good but probably not good enough for me to come back (especially with that wait). Â I really didn't see what all the fuss was with the blueberry pancakes and maple butter - they were good but definitely not 3-hr-wait good... Service was good - I think our server was covering the whole restaurant by herself!

THE "BOUNCER" AT THE PLACE WOULD NOT LET ME IN BECAUSE I WAS IN A TANK TOP, THEN CONTINUED TO CALL ME A FAGGOT AND A GAY ASSHOLE? Disgusting. This is Chelsea in NYC and you are going to discriminate not only someone who has been a patron to your restaurant, but discriminate those who would normally feel safe in the neighborhood? Enjoy serving gross wedge salads and stale fries. Â This place is a DINER, not a restaurant. All these other reviews are fake but i assure you this is real.

So been wanting to come here since my boyfriend and other friends have raved about it and I was excited to see that I was coming here for Valentine's day. Unfortunately, it was a bit disappointing. Here's the breakdown: Service: I heard the place don't usually take reservations on daily basis, but I guess they took reservations for those who wanted to dine here for Valentine's day. When we walked in we were seated right away. It was a prefix menu that night so we only had a choice of drinks that night. The meals were quick...too quick that they were a bit anxious to take my plates away while I was still working on it, so they can bring in the next plate. I didn't like that they didn't ask how I was doing with my meals and only came over to pick up my plates. Food: As a complimentary side before we get started with the meal, they had this amazing bacon flavored popcorn! Seriously, I would just come back for the popcorn. Then we had another complimentary goodie before we started our meal. It was this shot of chilled artichoke soup and it was pretty delicious. So our first course from the prefix was this raw yellowtail with bits of crispy ham and winter citrus. This was by far my favorite dish of the night! Usually you taste the fishiness from the raw fishes when you do it sashimi style but this was melt in your mouth goodness! The winter citrus complimented the yellowtail so nicely. There was an avocado pure on it but I didn't really taste it. But overall the flavors of this dish were so refreshing I wanted a second round! The second course was a berkshire pork belly with little neck clams in a bacon broth. Honestly, this dish had a weird combination. I didn't think the pork balanced well with the little necks. The third course was a hake with mussels in a coconut broth with matsutake mushrooms, and bok choy. The coconut broth was unique and complimented the dish well. I wish the broth was much more stronger though. But the matsutake was cooked perfectly and saved this last to soothe my palette. The fourth course was a NY strip with beets and potatoes. The hightlight of the dish was the smoked yogurt and red beets. Even though the steak was cooked medium rare, it was not a good cut. I didn't really enjoy it as much, but smothering it with the smoked yogurt helped it. The beets were refreshing. The dessert was a black forest cake with dark chocolate,cherries and cream of some sort. The cake wasn't as moist. This wouldn't be my dessert of choice if I had to choose, so I was a bit disappointed. But it helped a bit when they brought out the complimentary two chocolate dipped strawberries to finish off the meal. Nice touch...nice touch... Ambiance: It was a small in there but cozy setting. It wasn't anything that really stood out to me. Overall: I believe everyone deserves a second chance, so I would definitely come back another time to try their tapa style dishes that my boyfriend and friends raved about.
I can cross off going here for dinner. It was a little pricy for being ok. The brunch looks great and I look forward to checking that out.

Best after drinks food ever! Also awesome food before hand too. Apparently, 7:30pm shift until after is the real deal but this place is open before 7:30pm too. Order to $6 Combo! Option of ranch, bbq, and spicy sauce! If you haven't tasted the spicy sauce, then try it first before the drench your whole combo with it. They will drench it with whatever sauce you ask for. Also, apparently the workers here are "supppposedly" staff rotation of other halal chicken rice carts in the area. Â O wells, its like sushi......you don't go to a non-crowded place for fresh food haha And yes it is a tourist hot spot. - no seats - stand up or find seating by fountain - to go food but best eaten fresh there - long lines

A wonderful young lady I know lives in the area and we always walk by here, a bit agog at the hustle and bustle. "We should really try that place!" has been our refrain for, like, 6 months. So we finally did. Food *I got a burger and enjoyed it. Totally exciting and exotic, right? I know! Burger was well prepared, juicy and gooey with cheese. Very tasty. The special sauce didn't have much of a discernable flavor, but didn't detract by any means. *The fries. Oh man, the fries. Crispy and (I assume) gently tossed in truffle oil (or equivalent), bursting with flavor. Hated having to share them, but I'm a gentleman and all. *She got a salad that looked like a generous dinner size. She finished it. I don't know or care much about salad so that's all I got. *Admittedly, we didn't go out on too much of a limb with either of our orders, but the rest of the menu had some really appetizing and enticing options. The chicken sandwich and mac 'n cheese looked especially good. I was pleasantly surprised to have an internal "what to get?" debate. Drink *We didn't get any. So lame. *BUT the cocktail list looked very good and fairly priced. When I return I shall order off it, multiple times. Appointment *Front of house felt a bit congested, but was actually quiet considering how crowded it was and the sliver of space between tables. *They've outfitted the space well for couples and 2 or 4 tops. Very casual. *A sign says more dining space is available downstairs. Service *A tad on the slow side but we went on a Sunday night on a long weekend so maybe the house didn't know that people would be going out that night, and staffed as they usually do on a Sunday night. I'll go with that. Overall, a good meal, especially if you live in the area. I won't rush or even walk briskly back, but I will be back! Of note, it seems like they do a helluva brunch service, but judging solely on how crowded Saturday and Sunday mornings look and the crowds lingering outside.

If you took ice cream, infused it with pork fat, and melted it down into a hot, steaming puddle, it would not be half as deliciously smooth, rich, and creamy as Ippudo's ramen broth. Forget the noodles - although they're good too - you could make a meal just out of that heavenly broth.

What a great place!! The atmosphere was sexy and just breathe taking. Customer service was phenomenal and the I believe he was the manager. But he was so nice and very welcoming to is at eating at Print. I love the fresh half oysters with champagne vinegrette, I swear it's like a butter melting in your mouth. I ordered the rabbit; the rabbit was tender, moist and awesomely delicious. I ordered a jack and coke, my favorite! Overall my experience was awesome, no compliments.

This place was amazing. Unlike Grimaldi's they take cards. The pizza is fresh and flavorful. Easily some of the best in NYC. The vibe is welcoming, despite the unfortunate war going on between them and Grimaldi's. The theatrics of that situation makes for an interesting story and a fun eating experience. The dough is great, the sauce is great. Fresh mozzarella, flavorful pepperoni. Love this place.

Poutine review only, and it's a disappointing one. I tried the poutine (my very first poutine ever), and was pretty disappointed. The fries were crunchy, but way too salty. The brown gravy barely tasted like anything. The cheese curds came from a big bucket of dry-looking pieces of cheese curd (though they did moisten up and melt eventually.) Overall it just looked and tasted that something that's totally greasy and unhealthy without any of the redeeming taste value. Perhaps it's a better idea to just get the normal fries and try their special sauces.

Now this is a New York meal. Â One of those you've been waiting for to reaffirm how beautiful it is to be a foodie in this city. I went on Christmas Eve eve, with snow around the window panes...it's the west village...table for two...you get the picture. Â The duck, the oysters, the cauliflower, the sablefish, i would love to go on. Â  It's a tucked in, small space, so go early and try to grab a seat at the bar while you wait for your table. Â Trust me, beyond worth it.

Surprisingly the bar food was very good. We have been here a few times for drinks and apps. The atmosphere is very nice, but late on weekends the projector screens with music videos change the nice atmosphere.
I love the Thai pai More familiar with the hell kitchen location, even if this restaurant is very noisy, I can t stop enjoying my dinning experience!

Came here for a birthday brunch and hurried back within a week to dine again. The wings are to die for. They have a special crunchy texture on the outside that I've never experienced anywhere else! Shane, the chef, came out to greet us when the waitress told him how obsessed my husband and I were with the wings. Unfortunately, he didn't disclose his secrets to making the wings so yummy. Back to brunch - I had the "mushrooms & garlic" which was very flavorful and the eggs were prepared perfectly, a little runny, and my husband had the burger, which he had again a week later for dinner! The draft beer list is quaint but more than adequate. My husband had the rare Voss, and the witte from cooperstown, NY. I stuck with cocktails. 4 stars because the liver pate amuse bouche wasn't to die for. Can't wait to go back.

Came here for brunch last weekend and the food was fantastic!! Â I shared the Toffee Glazed Brioche Bun (a little on the small side but AMAZING) w/ a friend and then got the eggs w/ brussel sprouts and pumpkin, which sounded a bit odd but tasted great! Â I didn't have the coffee but my friends that did really liked it. Â  The service was good, although it took a little while to get our food. Â It was busy even though it was early (for my anyway) on a Sunday - 11am, so make sure you get a reservation.

Got there on a sunday when it opened at 9am. We still hadto wait for an hour. Â I had the biscuit sandwhich, my brother got the chocolate pancakes and my parents had gotten the french toast and another set of pancakes with sides of cheese grits and a biscuit. Â Honestly when it was all done, it was just like any other breakfast we could've gotten elsewhere with out the wait. Â This place just wasn't as great as I expected. The place is clean but really small. Not worth the wait, I wouldn't come back unless I got seated right away.

Does anyone else think the Pork Buns taste like burger king original chicken sandwich, except spicy and with pork? Â Amazing. My first time here definitely wont be my last. Great to split the ramen with a date, do not order two. Had a cold tofu and avocado app that changed my life, also my underpants.

So both hubby and I requested from our Secret Santas that we get money for a nice night out somewhere in Manhattan. Â Since hubby wanted to go to the American Museum of Natural History on the last night that we were planning to be in Manhattan, I've decided to rely on the wonderful reviews of our fellow New York Yelpers to pick a place! Â First restaurant that came on this list was Calle Ocho! Â "Hmmm? Â 4.5 stars... looks consistently good for the most part... and only a block away from American Museum of Natural History! Â SCOOOORE!!!" Â :-D And I must say, it is an expensive restaurant (but mainly b/c hubby didn't got to head towards the FREE SANGRIA BUFFET. Â NOOOOO!! Â He HAD to have a Cosmo!!! Â With Absolut Citron vodka!!! *rolleyes*) but the service was great and we loved the food!!! Â He had the Bistec and I had the Lomo. (Not sure if that's the proper name. Â  It was the dinner special on Sunday.) Also, the waitress was more than willing to substitute this garlic and olive oil thing for their standard plantain/black bean bread spread (which I liked, but hubby HATES bananas!!!) to go with their VERY FRESH and warm rolls (Definitely a nice touch!!!) And did I mentioned the free SANGRIA BUFFET??? Â  (Okay, I'm a tee-totaler. That said, I took a small sample of it with my meal just to try it out. Â It was quite tasty, but I'm not that much of an alcohol drinker and after a few sips (like not even a 1/4 glass even...) the imminent alcohol headache happens. Â :( Â  But I figured that most of the people here on Yelp can take in MUCH MORE alcohol than I do to get the alcohol headache. Â LOL!!!) I would LOVE to come back again next Christmas for their brunch!!! Â But we'll see if I will ever *get* to a Sunday brunch in Manhattan. Â (Until this year, we have NEVER been to Manhattan on a Sunday... much less on a Sunday morning, for "economics reasons." Â Long story! Â You don't wanna know... *rolleyes*)

I'll admit I was nervous about eating at a falafel place. For one, I did not know what a falafel was and two, because of that I didn't want to shell out money on some mystery food. I still do not know what exactly a falafel is, but what I do know is that Taim serves a VERY tasty meal. For those as clueless as me, order the green falafel on wheat bread and you'll feel like a pro. I first want to thank the nice lady waiting in line with me for the best advice in recent memory. The green falafel on whole wheat was a great choice. The falafel seems to melt in your salivating mouth with a delightful mix of cream, fried chick peas, wheat bread, and fresh tomatoes. I am still surprised to this day because I was really skeptical when I first went. For those who want an authentic New York experience but are tired of eating pizzas or hot dogs, CHECK THIS PLACE OUT! Even if you are intimidated and have no idea what a falafel is, just follow in my footsteps and you'll be glad you did!

I wish I could give Perilla 3.5 stars... First of all, it's in cutest area of the Village, so after brunch or dinner, you will be able to walk around and stroll through the more residential and hip areas of Manhattan. There are plenty of bakeries and ice cream shops where you can indulge in a few sweets, if the dessert menu at Perilla doesn't suffice. The restaurant itself is small, romantic, and relatively modern and simple. It's the perfect spot to go to with a girlfriend/boyfriend or as part of a double date. I wouldn't recommend parties of over 4-5 to go, since there is limited seating. We started off with the spicy duck meatballs because they seemed to be all the rave, according to fellow Yelpers. However, I found that it was just-okay. The meatballs may have been a tad bit overcooked, so it was a bit chewy. The meat definitely did not melt in my mouth, as I had expected, and the "spicy" aspect of the appetizer seemed almost nonexistent. Maybe I had set my expectations too high... We then continued to the calamari, which I find difficult to mess up. We got the Roasted All Natural Chicken and the Hanger Steak. Both were cooked to perfection. What else can I say? The dark meat and white meat portions of the chicken were not dry and the steak was cooked to a beautifully red medium rare. They were good portions too, so we were stuffed. I would give Perilla 3 stars because I didn't find myself wanting to go back. I don't think the dining experience was as memorable as I expected it to be. The food was great, but I feel as though I could find something of the same quality at a much better price elsewhere. And you'll find plenty of 20-30 year olds in the restaurant for dinner. It's definitely a place for date night!

This place is awesome. The owner/ chef is very friendly and will take his time to come around and check up on tables. The price is reallllyyy great and the portions are huge! One downfall for some is that you will most likely be waiting a while for a table, especially during the warmer months, but they do offer free glasses of wine while you wait :) This will always be a go to spot in Astoria.

The Brooklyn Star has a special place in my heart, as does most of Brooklyn, because it reminds me of Boulder, with its hipsters, hippies, health-nuts, and everyone in-between. Unsurprisingly, many of the patrons of The Brooklyn Star veered towards the plaid + black-rimmed glasses. We stopped in for a quick mid-afternoon snack: ox-tails marinated buffalo wing style, bone marrow, and chilled beers. It was a great pick-me-up. There isn't too much to eat, in terms of quantity, of the ox-tails, but what little meat there was was quite good. And the marrow on perfectly toasted bread - fantastic. I love the southern feel and I'd definitely return to try some of their dinner entrees.

Wow.. the fried chicken is amazing. Did not taste like greasy at all. Ordered mac and cheese, fried zucchini sides. Mac and cheese was good, not great. but how can mac and cheese every really be bad?? Fried zucchini A+. I ordered the chicken box, friend ordered the cat fish. which tasted very good too. the chicken and biscuit was very excellent. Cant wait to go back...

Walking in on a cold fall night, it is not hard to understand why this popular Brooklyn Heights' neighborhood restaurant is a big hit. Noodle Pudding simply oozes warmth, good Italian food and friendly service. The prices are more than affordable, and you are dining in a romantic golden colored candle lit room. The menu focuses on classic dishes with an adventurous twist. The pappardelle with venison ragu was simple but yet so flavorful. Although tiramisu was ordered on every other table, and looked very yummy, at the end of our meal I was simply too full to try.

I tend to either concretely like or dislike restaurants. Despite three visits now, each time dragged there by people who were awed by the great business they were having, Taverna Kyclades gets my first firm 3-star of "...meh." Meh, in the classic sense. Not that it's bad, just...a meh of apathy. Â The wait times were okay.The portion sizes, generous. The salads, large and easy to share, with giant slabs of feta. The fish...meh. And for a place that rides on its seafood, "meh" is not good! I've had the whiting, the filet of sole, and crab-stuffed sole (and bites from many other companions' entrees) and I was never once blown away. It's not /bad,/ but it's all a bit bland. At least it's not painfully dry? The sides are also pretty pedestrian and uninteresting, more for the purpose of filling you up than wowing you. I used to be nearby this restaurant often, hence the frequent visits, but ... I don't really think I'd go again. It could be worse, but really, it could be better, for all the hype and the massive waits.

Good food good service. I got the egg white omelette with mix green. Brunch choices are pretty limited tho. Freemans is definitely one of the most artsy restaurant I've visited in the city. I wouldn't say the restaurant is not clean, but when I was planning to leave today, I saw a little mouse running across the room... Didn't really how to act on that. I was shocked and not at the same time. I mean It's an old building and it's nyc.

Very cozy place in one of the best neighborhoods in Brooklyn. Very tasty meals and very nice service. The gnochi are amazing and you can't leave the restaurant without order the checkpea salad, mmmm excellent.

Yawn. Â I think it was good that I visited the place for the experience. Â However, I thought the place was overrated and not worth the money. Â The place was too chaotic for my taste. Â I just think it's a lazy way to experience Italian food. Â Maybe I'm fortunate to be able to experience local neighborhoods such as Astoria, Howard Beach, Morris Park (blahblahblah) that a place like Eataly makes me wonder "Is there really a recession?"

Adorable restaurant with great atmosphere, but the runniest mac and cheese I've ever had. So unfortunate that the food was terrible because I really did enjoy the space as well as the lovely jazz band that plays there on the weekends.

Everyone was very polite, friendly from the moment we walked in the door. We arrived a bit early, Â enjoyed a glass of champagne at the bar and was then escorted to our table. The dining room is sectioned off into 4 different areas, Â separated by softly painted walls adorned with beautiful at work and lighting. The dinner menu is a 3 - course fixed menu with an amazing selection of meats and seafood prepared with the freshest selection of mushrooms, Â vegetables and spices. Â Dessert was just as amazing so save room. Overall it's definitely worth a visit! Â Enjoy.

We were looking for a small plates restaurant in or the theatre district and Briciola popped up. We loved the ambience; a small space, natural wood wine racks lining the walls and communal tables with subway tile. The food was mostly enjoyable. Â We started with an item that is regularly on the menu - bruschetta served with speck, melted blue cheese and arugula. Â It was very good. Â This was followed by one of the specials of the night - a grilled octopus salad. Â This had a variety of textures and flavors - grilled octopus, roasted creamy potatoes, celery, and a reduced balsamic. This was excellent, but would have been superb with some grilled lemon. Â We contemplating ordering a second (while requesting grilled lemon) and regret that we didn't. The last item we ordered was a normal menu item - grilled lamb chops with balsamic and fingerling potatoes. Â Ours arrived, and to my dismay, there was an issue with it: it either it had two coarse human hairs on it or it perhaps the two hairs were from an artichoke heart...coated in balsamic. Â No matter how I tried to convince myself it wasn't human hair, I couldn't. Â One of the "hairs" actually arrived appeared to have a follicle root attached to it, which just creeped me out. Â Our server took that one away and then proceeded to tell me several times that it wasn't hair. Â He alleged it was hair from the potato. Â I do a lot of cooking, and I've never seen a "potato hair". Â The kitchen did fire a new lamb dish, but it took a really long time to come out, it was under-seasoned (I'm sure they were trying to get it out as quickly as possible) and it was actually a bit overdone. Â Also, from the time that we pointed out the issue, we were persona non grata with the wait staff. I felt like I had two dining experiences. Â One 5 star event Â and one 2 star event. Â I'm really torn about how many stars to give...but in the end, I'm going to go with 4. Â That's based that even two weeks later, when I think of grilled octopus I ate that night, my mouth waters.

This tapas inspired menu is always interesting and delicious. Every dish is big enough for two people to enjoy or 4 people to taste. It's fun to try so many different things during the course of a meal. The small space ends up feeling warm and inviting rather than cramped. The list of spanish wine is inspired and when you order by the glass you get a mini-carafe, which really makes it worth the money. I have had somewhat variable service here, but never bad service. I have been with some people who found the food to be on the salty side, but it has never bothered me. The only real downside is that the desert is not worth eating and this isn't really a place to come with more than 4 people. Other than that it's one of my favorite places.

Fantastic restaurant!! We've been here a few times for special occasions and really enjoyed the food. Buffalo mozzarella and prosciutto appetizers are so good. Service is professional and friendly. It gets a little loud out front and seems a bit quieter and brighter if you sit in the back room.
amazing food, and I saw Madonna there!!!! wow!!

The cuban sandwich was delicious. Â The avocado salad was weak - and now that I am thinking about - I don't think there was any avocados in it.... hmmmm..... interesting. The brownie for dessert was pretty weak too. Â But the place is super cute, small, basement spot - great place for a weeknight dinner and drink. The service was bad but, the waitress was sweet. Â Highlight of the night other than my good friends company, Jesse Eisenberg was there on a date- Jesse Eisenberg anyone? Zombieland? Michael Cera's bizzaro... I love seeing celebrities :)

I have eaten at the Toloache in the West 50's and loved it. Â But dinner at the Greenwich Village outpost was mediocre. Â I adore suckling pig but their version was as hard and dry as a hockey puck. Â If the quesadilla contained the promised huitlacoche I would be very surprised. Â Likewise the truffle. Â It was just boring. Â We decided to pass on dessert and got some very good baklava at Mamoun's.

love this place. like a fat kid at a candy store....u wanna try everything! its literally ard the block to where I live and can neva go wrong when ur starving and have nothing to eat. the bbq meat is just divinely good. love the steak and ribs. yum, yums, yums. they switch up the buffet, which is a pleasant surprise to my taste buds. I love the corn, the diff rice, the fishes, flavorful chicken, pastas, veggies, starches...I mean literally all kinds of delish Brazilian food at such a affordable price. u cant beat that.

While we loved the decor, and the pizza was good, we felt that this did not live up to the hype or to our expectations. ATMOSPHERE A strong point. Loved the non-descript front, leading into the warm inside. SERVICE We waited a while to be seated, which was to be expected considering the crowd. During which time, we had a few drinks, which were great. I made the "mistake" of suggesting to the hostess that since we had two kids with us, we could take a table for 4 instead of waiting for a table of 5 (since there were a few open tables). I think this must have put us on a "trouble" list or something, though I was as humble as possible when I mentioned it. We were finally seated in an outside room, next to a drafty slamming door. Not a big deal. The service reminded me of many original Williamsburg restaurants with the "we're so awesome, and way too cool for you" hipster attitude. What solves this? A little humility, Â perspective, and of course, competition. FOOD We ordered two pizzas, a carrot special, and a "truffle" pasta special. I want to be fair to the place - the pizza was very good, and the drinks were as well. The non-pizza items... not so much. The "truffle" pasta had maybe one drop of truffle oil over the entire dish. The carrots Â - which were many - came with all of a teaspoon of "smoked ricotta." Sorry, but the non-gastronomy selections were small, overpriced, and didn't quite cut it. Â  This is a great place for pizza and drinks, but I'd suggest you avoid anything other then the pizza. Try the bar for this. TS p.s. and to the tan-knit-cap-hipster bus-boy... let people swallow the food in their mouth before ripping their now-empty plates off the table. Patience is a virtue, and you can wait.
Pizza yeah! Not as good as artichokes but it has seating, so it's good enough for me!

Pros: SOUP DUMPLINGS!!! Cons: Cash only. LONG LONG LONG LINES... Creator of the BEST SOUP DUMPLINGS... EVER. I kid you not. Pronounced "shao-long-pow" and simply DELICIOUS. Learn how to slurp... I mean, devour them by checkin' out other regulars who munch. Definitely order any and every seafood item. Stuff will sound exotic... but it's oh-so-yummy!!!

Ba Xuyen's classic banh mi (#1) is one of the best I've tried. Â There's a certain futility to going around the city in search of THE best -- after a certain treshold of quality it just becomes about preference. Â Well, my preference may well be Ba Xuyen. Â Perfect bread, juicy cuts, flavorful pate for the price banh mi is supposed to be ($3.75). Â Props also to the basic cafeteria-style seating in a field where most competitiors literally leave you standing. Â Honestly, the only thing the recent explosion of banh mi shops might have on Ba Xuyen is location/convenience. Â Sure, this was a trek out to Borough Park, but it was worth it. Â (4.5 stars)

Hands Down! One of my all-time favorite restaurants. Walter Foods is a sure-fire guarantee on a great meal and dining experience. The food and drinks are always made to perfection. The staff is always fun and attentive. The atmosphere is always pleasant and never over-bearing. Classy interior with a beautiful backyard. I've happily given this restaurant so much of my business and they have never let me down. If you're looking to impress a date or large group of friends, go to Walter Foods.

Amazing. Â "best lamb in NYC" quotes my fiancÃ© who is the snobbiest of food snobs out there! Â He LOVES this place. Â  It is worth the wait. Â it's best to book a couple days in advance as well, the place books up quickly.

Maybe I was expecting too much, having heard so much good things about the food here. Meh, it was okay. 45 mins waits + not-as-savory-as-I-thought food = Over-rated slightly. It's still a good restaurant with authentic and reasonably-priced food though, but I believe many competitors are just as good. I was walking in thinking Pure Thai will be an irreplaceable experience. In reality there are too many other Thai restaurants along 9th Av that makes the long wait not worth it.

They have healthy food here contrary to the name of the place. I ordered the Sesame Tuna w/ side salad. Tuna came out like sushi, raw only instead of rice there were sesame seeds wrapped around them. Side dish was cucumber slices with a dressing, not sure what it was but everything was delicious. The side salad had a mystery dressing also. This place gets BUSY, it's NOISY and it's pretty dark inside, just know before you go. AND beware you have to tell them you want the appetizer or entree for some things - for example my tuna came as an appetizer, thought that's what I ordered for $15, but then price was $20 on my bill, waitress told me I told her I wanted the entree. #OK.

One of my favorite picks for lunch in the area! food is good, simple, extremely in-expensive (lunch special can get as low as $6.90. seriously!) and cool ambiance. Take a look up to the ceiling - and see the exquisite mirror collection!

How do you get into this place? Good luck finding the door at night. It's nice that this little restaurant exists in the middle of all of the nothingness that is going on in the surrounding streets. However, we did not have a good experience. The drinks are terrible but the food is good so only come here for dinner if you're ok with bad service. We were a group of 10 on a Friday night. There was 1 waitress for the entire place & though this place is tiny, she didn't do a good job at making us feel welcome. It was difficult to flag her down. Our group ordered in 3 separate waves & got our food at all different times. The food coming out 2 dishes at a time in 10 minute intervals is not ok. The drinks were so so so bad that some of us even sent them back. The chips and guac and the soft tacos were pretty good though. Interestingly, though this place closes at 2am, the waitress came by and set the bill down in the middle of our table at 12:32am, when half of us were still eating and waiting on drinks. Talk about feeling kicked out. Since we planned on having more drinks and this place doesn't close until 2am, I found this to be extremely rude. Not 1 of the 10 of us will be returning. Kudos to the nearby bar who benefitted from this.
Holy Sh*t!!! This is hands down the best pizza that i have ever had and it's such an experience going there. I am happy I was able to go with my family and cannot wait to go back.

Point blank, best pizza I've EVER had. Only drawback is the wait. The first time I went on a sunday afternoon and had to wait an hour and a half for two pies. Second time I went on a weekday afternoon and only had to wait 20 minutes for two pies.

Finally i came to this place! Been hearing and reading alot about it. Pizza was great! Drinks were really really good. Sangria was very good as well. Atmosphere is date appealing as well as just kicking back to a meal. Highly recommend it.

Holy mother of all waits - quoted at 2 hours on a Friday at 730pm for 2 people - but they called after an hour fifteen. There is something twisted in ur brain that makes u want to eat there more when u hear the absurd wait time. The standout here imo was the chawanmushi (just sublime, way better than the often free egg soufflÃ© you'd get at a korean restaurant, and similar to sakagura's). The pork belly, while absolutely delicious, is nothing different from what u get in ktown when u order samgyupsal aka pork belly). The beef tongue was also excellent - tho I have had better beef tongue - I'm a tongue eating expert. Grilled mackerel was also very good. So all in all, I thoroughly enjoyed this place and they have an extensive menu, but I don't see myself waiting 2 hours to dine here again anytime soon. They've got alcohol here now, in case u were wondering. Good sake of course.

How the hell have I not written a review for 53rd & 6th...this place is my life line I've been eating at this cart for years. I dont care what time of night it is, the weather, how long the line is. I'm innn thereee. Its the best Halal in the city. Halal elsewhere just doesnt compare. I've gladly introduce this cart to a few people and I feel like I've changed their lives forever lmao. Beware of the little containers of hot sauce, a little goes a long way. This is the ultimate 4-5 in the morning post-clubbing meal. Eat it.

Like others, I came here with a friend before "Sleep No More." I felt that the ambiance and service contributed a lot to the overall experience of "Sleep No More." Our waiter Edward was fantastic - very funny, knowledgeable, personable, and attentive. He was so funny - my friend and I wanted him to join us for our meal! There is live music and lots of entertainment throughout the meal before you attend the "play." We both started with the black kale caesar salad, which was delicious. Great dressing, really fresh ad hearty kale, and generous helping of parmesan cheese. I had the cod with chips, which was fantastic - the fries are spicy and crispy, and the fish is perfectly cooked and battered. My friend had the roast chicken. For dessert we both had the apple bread pudding, which comes with a citrusy ice cream. All in all a very fun experience, great food, great service.

As a personal trainer in the city it is always nice to have a great spot to go to between clients that serves some healthy and delicious menu choices. Several of my clients are locals of Bakehouse and the restaurant gives off a very noticeable family vibe. Great staff, great food, great service. Try the Tuna Nicoise Salad, Scallops, Â or grab one of their fresh juices to go on a Saturday or Sunday morning to start the day. Three Thumbs Up and great addition to the West Village and NYC!

I'm giving this place 3 stars. Â That means I was satisfied. Â I think the biscuits and gravy was good. Â Could have been warmer through - coming out of the kitchen. Â The taste was yum though. Friend chicken was also yum. Â I had a pecan donut too and that was really tasty. Â  The wait on the weekend was really short - like 20 minutes. Â They told us like 45 minutes which was a gross over-statement since my party and I left to get drinks while we waited but we were called very quickly. Â Good and bad since we had to quickly finish our drinks. Also, the apple was good, but I think the Blue Stove is better. Â  Service was ok. Â I'd return here.

Liked this restaurant's accoutrements, coziness, atmosphere in general, and can vouch for the chicken dishes and bruschette (w/ funghi) and bottle Chianti we had last night. Plus the tiramisu. Dug being under the elevated F train trestles. Good job.

One of the few Italian places in the city that I tend to come back to fairly often as it's consistently reliable and reasonably priced. Â  Flat buns- hard not to like salty (prosciutto) over warm baked soft mini breads. Â The bread cuts the saltiness well. Â It's the only place I've been to anywhere that serves it this way. Â I feel more Italian places should serve prosciutto this way but I'm guessing most would rather you drink their red wine with it instead and not have the delectable addictive hot bread which would make you fuller quicker and order less. Â  Olive oil- The olive oil here is quite yummy though I think we went through it in like 5 seconds as it was in a tiny bowl. Â  I used to order the squid ink tagliolini dish as that was ol' reliable as well as the papardelle sausage but I think my favorite pasta dish there these days is the Homemade Cavatelli with shrimp and salmon in pesto sauce. Â I'm typically not a huge fan of pesto or non-tomato based sauce but it was subtle and light enough for me to enjoy it. Â The pesto was not overpowering and the chunks of salmon were generous and fresh. Â And as long as you enjoy cavatelli, adoringly described as maggot-shaped (or some might say silkworm) pasta, then you will enjoy this dish.

Is it too early to go again, if I was just there on Saturday? The penne alla vodka with chicken was so yummy...and can you say cheap?!?! $9!! Sold!! My friend had a glass of white sangria for $5...she liked it...I wasn't able to taste it but am absolutely going to next time I'm there. I asked the server how long their $5 mojitos and sangrias lasted and she said, basically, all the time! Really delicious food, phenomenal prices, and outdoor seating? Yup...I'm going back. I don't know how busy they get at brunch but I really enjoyed the energy of my Saturday early evening (6:00) stop.

Mona Lisa calls to me with the one of the best pizza places that NY has to offer. I came here on a weekday for a late lunch and there was a slight wait for a table 10-15 minutes. We didn't have to wait long since it was a little slow. We knew what we wanted so we ordered right away with cold ice teas all around. It was hot outside and the cold drinks were refreshing - the peach flavor was just right. We ended up ordering a 14" (6 pieces) with spinach, mushrooms, and prosciutto. I was ravenous and knew I would enjoy every bite of the pizza. We each got 2 slices and it was the perfect combination of toppings and well spread. They were generous with toppings and cheese and the crust was made perfect (crunchy on the edges but not burnt). I don't normally eat crust but this crust I ate -- a testament to how good this pizza is. The tables were spread out with enough space and the atmosphere was festive.

As some of you know, potatoes fear me. Â I cackle at the thought of them being mutilated through slicing, chopping, or grating. Â I grin when I smell their little, starchy bodies browning, cooking, and sometimes being burned to a crisp. Â Then, I devour them with delight. Â I also like to humiliate them by smothering them in hot sauces, cheeses, and/or mayonnaises. Â The torture of the potato never ends with me. Â If they could, they would run away on their short, stubby legs at the sight of me, screaming all the way. Â Lucky for me, they are born without any means of escape, making them all the more attractive as victims. Pommes frites has become one of my favored potato-torturing venues. Â They know how momma likes her potatoes, and they give her what she wants. Â According to Rachael W., the potatoes were better in the past. Â I, unfortunately, did not experience that time, so I can only judge these potatoes now. Â I love the paper cone they come in, the variety of dips you can choose, and the strength of flavor of those dips. Â I have never finished my potatoes and thought, "Damn, there weren't enough fries" or "I wish I could have tasted the garlic in that mayo." Â To the contrary, the potato sticks are plentiful and the condiments are divine.

Based upon their ambience, my husband & I and company decided to try it out - We were pleasantly surprised & satisfied :-)! Since their burger meats are purchased from Los Paisanos Meat Market, it can't go wrong with it. Â The FAVORITE BURGER of the evening is the "Breakfast Burger". The ambience is not too shabby, but for some, it can be considered a wee bit dark. Â Personally, I don't mind it too much. If anything, the only "negative" is the open kitchen aspect - By the time you leave the restaurant, you & your clothing items smell like burgers...:-|

This is the kind of restaurant you pass a million times and never really think twice about coming. Â It looks cute and energetic,but I never had a real inclination to actually venture here. Â There was something about that didn't fully appeal to me. I went yesterday, Sunday, for an early dinner with some friends and their baby girl. Â We figured it was energetic enough that no one would notice if she was fussy, plus the reservations were easy enough to make online. I arrived first and ordered a drink at the bar. Â The bartender was extremely helpful and even made a drink that wasn't on the menu. Â It was an okay cocktail, but definitely something I wouldn't order again. Â I thought the service outdid the cocktail, so I sipped it with a smile on my face and endured. Â Important to note they had a nice beer selection focusing on independent breweries rather than the big 3 garbage companies. We were seated in the back at an awkward table since it was stuck in the middle of a busy intersection so waitstaff had to squeeze between us to get to the back tables. Â We were constantly worried that hot food or dirty dishes were going to fall on our heads! Â  It was far too loud to hear anything our server was telling us. Â We all had to lean in very close to hear a single thing he said about the specials. Â I'm assuming this is because the restaurant is covered in tile amplifying everything. Â It was so loud in fact that when the baby cried, we didn't hear her AT ALL. Â Crazy, I know. The other issue we had at our table was that the chairs slide back on the tile floor. Â I guess we were stuck on an uneven floor, but it was really annoying to keep pulling myself back to the table. So I ordered the short ribs and the rest of my party ordered the flounder. Â The food came out very quickly and were presented in an aesthetically pleasing way. The portions were actually really small, which was slightly disappointing based on the price. Â  The fish dishes would NOT have filled me up and I'm a small woman. Â My dish was delicious with succulent short rib and fried potatoes smothered in a rich spicy tomato mayo sauce. Â They only gave me one short rib, which was nice in size, but definitely not a portion to be proud of. Â I left slightly hungry, but satisfied enough. Â Didn't feel like eating dessert here since the noise was getting to me. Â  The staff was great and the decor really cute. Â They did not have a changing table for the baby, which is weird since they offered us a highchair. Â Why have a highchair if you don't have a place to change a diaper? Â  Overall, it was an okay experience. Â $25 for short ribs when in fact there is only one rib seems a little steep to me. Â The burger and beer special seemed the way to go on Sunday night, at only $15. Â I'll try that if I do come back.

Salinas is a very solid tapas restaurant. It is expensive. By default when you go to tapas restaurant you anticipate to order many or at least quite a few mini dishes and experience a great variety of foods and flavors, but with prices of $18 and $26 per one tapa - a couple can easily spend around $200+ with a drink or maximum two. Service is great, nice presentation, very good taste, tiny portions (even for tapas). In summary - definitely worth a visit for a romantic date or just a night out, but only if you have am extra $200-$300 to spare.
Bartenders steal your money if you leave it on bar. Burgers are made from rancid meat, partly overcome in the chile. Drinks are all overpriced. Bathroom is filthy. Whole dive is infested with rats.

Ok Ok I told the guy behind the counter that I would write a review on how freakin delicious these sushi were. Spicy Mang was not too sweet & a nice kick but not burning. Mighty Mushroom was earthy, smooth, full. I agree with another review that no more than two!!! I was so full. Washed it down with some of their bangin blueberry lemonade. And it looked so beautiful on the plate! When I was paying the guy (didnt get his name, but it wasnt the chef) geniunely asked me what I thought and if I enjoyed it there. Too cool! Â This place totally caters to us vegans. I love sushi but was very limited on selection and now.... sushi all the time. Fours stars because I'm broke and this is a place I just cant afford to go often. But if you can, I recommend! They have a special earlier in the day. My meal came out to 18 dollars and change. Don't worry, I'll be back!!!!
making fresh food, great pasta. I enjoyed lunch close to overcrowded Broadway in Soho.

Looking to go back as soon as I can. Had a quick lunch at this sophisticated, easy-going, stylish, laid back, on-the-mark modern/primitive/eclectic decor and ambiance a la ABC Home stores. Simple paper placemats with earthy off white uneven-edged plates and china bread dishes, thin water glasses that are oh so pleasurable to sip or gulp out of. Â Clean, stylish, to-the-point fresh food like fluke citrus ceviche, wholesome bread, salt cellars, wheat grass with jalapeno and lime shooter sin a mini 50 ml beaker.

This Upper East Side gem is great on value. The portion sizes vs. price tag was terrific. Who knew that could exist on the UES? The food was solid. I didn't love anything that was put in front of me (minus the bread) and have had better fare at other Turkish/Mediterranean places but, I solidly enjoyed everything and at that price? Fughettaboutit. The mezze platter filled with hummus and the likes was a great way to start the evening along with a filled to the brim glass of decent pinot noir. I was stuffed from the apps so I went with the namesake salad with a side of doner (sliced lamb). The salad with grilled chicken was fine. Nothing crazy, just a chopped romaine salad with a bit of feta, not so ripened tomatoes, onions and room temp grilled chicken. For the price of $8 and change it was a decent salad. The mound of sliced lamb that I ordered on the side was also pretty regular. No complaints. But, to reiterate, I wasn't shouting from the roof tops about my love of this not so seasoned lamb. It was A-ok. The portion sizes were huge and I took most of my food home with me so that's always a good thing. I'd come back definitely if I lived on the UES for an affordable night out!

The 10-course tasting was relentless. Â Each course came as a surprise, innovative and delicious, and I kept waiting for a miss, only to be taken floating to the next cloud. Â The experience was not unlike that of Momofuku Ko, and after Ko, it was my best meal in the city. Â I'll try to document it here, but I suggest you book yourself a spot at the bar to see for yourself. 0. Dinner kicked off with an amuse duo: a croqueta and a Spanish "tortilla." Â The croqueta, with pork, summer corn, and paprika aioli, was the consummate croquette, a crispy sphere sitting in a smear of zesty sauce. Â The tortilla with shallot confit, quail egg, thinly sliced potato, and fresh lightly pickled chiles was a superb bite, a just-charred packet of flavor gleaming with a thin handsome burnish of oil. 1. The first official course was a gazpacho with heirloom tomatoes, fresh chives, smoked mussels, and cucumber. Â It was a bright, masterfully balanced cup of summer. 2. Â Broccoli rabe, pineapple foam, and parmesan cheese broth may not sound particularly appetizing, but believe me, it was. Â The rabe was sauteed and partly tempuraed with the full bitterness of the green left intact. Â This was balanced by the sweet touch of pineapple foam dissolving slowly into the thin but distinctly tangy cheesy broth. 3. Â Sucrine lettuce, sugar snap peas, pickled ramps, lamb bacon, toasted hazelnuts, fried egg mousse, edible flowers, and asparagus - how can I ever look at another salad again? Â This was an artfully composed plate in both taste and presentation. Â Lamb bacon is one of the best inventions ever, and fried egg mousse? Â It should smother everything. 4. Â Cured Tasmanian sea trout with scallion cream cheese, cucumber, black pepper, sorrel, red onion, and crispy trout skin was an exquisite evolution of Lox and cream cheese, mildly familiar but grown up. Â The trout skin took it to the next dimension. 5. Â A sardine trio hit three for three on exciting preparations of a fish that can easily be oily and bland. Â Part one was grilled sardine with roasted red pepper and sorrel. Â Then a crunchy little sandwich with pickled onions and cilantro, topped with a thin slice of Fresno chile. Â The third and my favorite was marinated skin-on sardine with potato salad, parsley, and mustard seed. Â I never thought of potato salad as anything but boring. Â Until now. 6. Â Slow-poached egg with fava beans, peas, cabbage, red pepper, and garlic crouton in a serrano ham broth was the weakest course. Â The yolk tended toward a sunny solidity that broke in unnatural clumps unsuited for marriage with even the meatiest of clear broths. Â Still, it was tasty, with a quiet saltiness, and the peas were casually the best I'd ever had. 7. Â The scrambled duck egg with brown butter, Greek yogurt, crouton, and lamb bacon, served in an eggshell in a bronze egg cup, put Â the previous course to shame. Â This little dish, taken in little bites with a little spoon, made me feel like royalty. Â It was, to mix my metaphors, divine. Â Flavors ran deep and rich, and the textural play of the smooth custardy base with the crunch of crouton and shards of lamb bacon was magnificent. Â One of the best things I've ever eaten. 8. Â Rabbit confit en croute - cooked with a mire poire of celery, onion, and carrot and served with heirloom carrots, morels, chanterelles, and dabs of red pepper reduction - was worth whatever karmic dock comes with eating cute animals. Â Despite the strength of the supporting cast, the rabbit hopped to the spotlight, cooked to tender juicy meaty splendor and sandwiched between barely-there slices of bread. Â The heirloom carrots, no doubt a parting gift for the dearly departed and dearly delectable Bugs Bunny, were phenomenal, a hard thing for carrots to be. 9. Â Oxtail potato cannelloni with crispy shallots, glazed radishes, fresh herbs (chives, dill, cilantro, mint), pickled radish, and pickled Fresno chile was the final savory dish. Â It was hearty but not heavy, a strong finish and another clean plate. 10. Â Dessert, torija with blueberry, cherry, and raspberry compote, was sublime. Â It was a simple recipe of brioche infused with cream and caramelized in plain view, but it managed to dwarf every other bread pudding I've ever tried. A bottle of 2001 Castillo Labastida Rioja Reserva recommended by our server accompanied us throughout the tasting. Â It was just right. Service wasn't doting, but Degustation is a small, busy operation, and I never once felt neglected. Â On the contrary, our friendly server was always accommodating, indulging me by repeating descriptions of dishes and ingredients as I scribbled like a nerd into my notebook. The space and set-up add to the charm of the meal. Â All-bar seating yields intimacy and a close view of the kitchen. Â There isn't a ton of room to stretch your legs, but this was no issue - with course after awe-inspiring course traveling from live kitchen to table setting, I spent most of this glorious dinner on the edge of my seat.
Meh. Been there a few times. Not impressed. There are far better restaurants in the city.

Warning: This place is tiny! If you eat at this restaurant, don't bring a big group. We ordered the calamari appetizer and beef lasagna. It was very delicious. Although, this place was really warm because the heater was on at full blast. Everything is basically self service. They give you bread, but the oil and vinegar and plates are on a shelf for you to retrieve. Water and cups are also self-serve. Even when you finish your meal, you bus your own table. I think this place is quite affordable for Manhattan. If you feel claustrophobic, get your food to go...this place is primarily a to-go place.

This is one of my favorite places in NYC. It's just the sweetest place. A little Italian joint with gorgeous green house seating in the back. I easily got a reservation for a group of 6 on a Saturday. We all completely loved our main courses and desserts. They served bread with an amazing spice-infused olive oil as an app which was also delish. We didn't have any drinks because my younger sis was with, but it was such a great night. Overall I spent $40 for my sister and I, which to me, in NYC, is a great deal. Plus, we definitely ate our fill. Service was mediocre, but the overall experience made up for it.

this burger lived up to its hype. i wish NY was quicker on food than cali, but at least we got it. i got the truffle speciale and it was delicious. it was messy to eat because the yolk exploded and started dropping down my wrists and arms but it didn't stop me from inhaling it. the biffle ordered the truffle shiitake royale and the sauce on that is delicious as well. the truffle fries were good but ours had little cheese on it. i guess this depends on who's eating it; biffle thought it needed more cheese and i thought it was too salty and avoided the cheese. service was whatevers (there were LOTS OF SEATS open but we had to wait for "the servers to catch up") but the burger is so good, i'm willing to overlook those minor flaws.

90-105 minutes to deliver a grilled cheese sandwich? You would think an establishment with limited to zero seating would have their delivery game down pat and be more efficient. Â If their delivery took less time then they would obtain my business. Â I shall now order from elsewhere. Â  I added one star because when your food is finally delivered it is good (when it is not cold from taking so long).
The best sangria and tapas in the city!
Good price, good taste, big quantity and LONG lines!!!!! If there were not many people waiting, should give a try. Not very worthy for waiting in chili windy day in Jan like I did.

Great spot for a drink. Feels like a cool speakeasy but they do food and drinks. They have an excellent cocktail menu and clearly put a lot of passion into what they make. Staff is friendly and attentive. It wasn't too busy at 6-ish on a Thursday but definitely started getting packed by 7-ish.

So I found myself here on a Saturday night after a birthday dinner with friends. We walked by and peeked inside and we thought everyone was having dinner or something. Not much action going on by the bar. Come to think of it, not much action around the whole lounge for a saturday night. But we walk in anyway and realize people are just sitting at tables have their drinks. We made our way to the bar and ordered up these much raved about lychee martinis and a few other of their cutely named cocktails. The lychee martinis were okay. But much better if I have had them at $5 a pop instead of the $9 or $10 I paid. Soon these few people got up and left so we grabbed their chairs by the bar and just chit chatted amongst us girls. It's annoying when people lean up on on the back of your chair, especially when you have your coat hanging on it. The music was starting to put us to sleep so we had to get out of there after an hour. I probably would come back if I had nothing else going on, but definitely want to check out the happy hour if I ever get around to it.

Bad reservation service. BAD. Came here at 9pm as a party of 6, and as expected we were told to wait for about an hour. Surely, we roamed around the neighborhood while we waited, and after an hour we got a voice message (note: not a phone call) that said they can only hold our reservation for a short period of time. We ran back and returned to the restaurant in 3 minutes, only to learn that they cancelled our reservation. The reservation lady said they tried to call us but it didn't go through...well that's a first for me to not get a call when I'm just roaming in Midtown NY. Anyways, we decided to just wait in the restaurant, and after half an hour, a table opened up, but it was for 4 people. I asked the lady can she add two more chairs and somehow having two more chairs at a table doesn't register in her mind. So, we stared blankly at a group of four that came in after we sat in the restaurant to wait (they started waiting after 10pm, we started waiting at 9pm) take our tables. At last, after another hour, by 11:30pm, we got our table. And I lost my appetite. Slightly above average food. Yakatori Tori Shin had better reservation service and better food.

Walked over with the boyfriend to try their famous pho#1. I'm not a big fan of the cilantro and bean sprouts so I decided to order the east side ink. Boyfriend ordered the pho#1. The east side ink was basically a roast beef sandwich with melted cheese and bacon. Who could deny the tastiness of bacon. But sad to say, that was the only tasty part of the sandwich. It was also layered with jalapeÃ±o peppers which i had to take out cause it was just too much. The rest of the sandwich was just ehh. It was a pretty decent size sandwich though. Â As for the pho#1, it was spicy. I mean yeah, it says that there would be some hot sauce in it and I could take a decent amount of spice but it felt like the guy who made it poured the whole freaking bottle of hot sauce initial.
