I also thought they would ask how spicy you would want it but I guess not. All I tasted was the hot sauce and the sweet sauce. I guess I could tell why they named it pho#1. You do get the bean sprouts, cilantro, mint, and the sauce from a pho and it was a pretty big sandwich. Yes the sandwich was different, yes it is a good portion, but will I order the same sandwiches? No I will not. I honestly didn't think they were anything special but will give this place another try.

Sort if nondescript from outside, comfortable but simple inside. I probably should have gone with a sammich. The French toast wasn't expensive, but also wasn't much food, compared to French toast at other restaurants. The coffee cost a couple bucks and didn't include free refills. The orange juice that comes with the meals tasted fresh, although it was a tiny glass. The server seemed overwhelmed, and rarely came by to check on us, and forgot parts of orders. So to sum up: food was decent, value was okay although probably should be better for the area, inside is comfortable although a bit chilly, and it's nice to have a good brunch place there, where there's not that much going on. If I go back, it'll mostly be for get location.

I'm always up for cheap eats and cheap brunch is just icing on the cake! $4 eggs include eggs, salad, potatos AND toast. So much cheaper than other brunch places in the area and now I don't feel bad ordering extra food because the eggs are SO cheap. I tried and loved their French toast. It's Texan apparently, so slices are thicker and oh so puffy and soft. The fruit on it was also really fresh. None of them were sour or rotten and the presentation was wonderful. I would highly recommend coming with a friend and sharing the $4 eggs and then getting something else you'd like to try.
Their chao kwai thao is very good as is their roti canai. I always bring my parents here when they come to visit me.

I'm not a big fan of Mediterranean cuisine, but I liked this a lot. We made reservation but had to wait a little at the bar because the restaurant was packed on Fri night. First of all, the ambience was great, warm lighting, high ceiling and intimate. By intimate, I mean that there is virtually no space between us and the next table (something you must get used to dinning in Manhattan). The menu is consisted of small plates and grilled kabobs. We ordered both. Everything was very tasty and everything was very small. For dessert, the ilili candy bar was very good but the baked baklava looked and tasted strange. Four of us ate for $240 with absolutely no wasted food or left-overs.

Loved the food, decor, the cozyness and the super cheerful staffs. I have been a fan of van leeuwen icea cream for a while now. But never knew my favorite ice cream was produced and supplied out of a little room in the back of this small restaurant. But, this is not the only thing that makes this place special. Despite barely having more than 5 entrees in their menu, every dish I have tried here is remarkable. From the appetizer menu, my favorites were the deviled eggs and the crispy chicken wings. Â For entree, the soto ayam and the fish curry are the winners. However, the 2nd time I went there, I was sad to see that they didn't have the soto ayam in the menu anymore. I want to give this place a 5-star, but for the location they are in, the price doesn't do justice to the portion. They need to be less stingy when it comes to the size of their entrees.

Went here last Saturday night for a 10pm reservation for two. We heard it was a great date spot and were able to make a reservation same day. Upon arrival we were greeted cheerfully by the hostess, who gestured us to our cozy seats facing out the large windows towards the street. Such a cool intimate vibe in here - maybe 10-12 seats total and almost all of the restaurant has a view of the kitchen. We started with the truffle Mac and cheese and baby lettuce salad. For being such a trendy, ubiquitous dish, the truffle Mac and cheese was head and shoulder above others I've had recently. Smaller penne noodles - perfectly creamy cheese, plenty of truffle flavor without being overpowering and a light bread crumb dusting broiled perfectly. Definitely get this. The baby lettuce salad was a great way to get our greens and don't get me wrong it tasted fantastic, but I wouldn't go back solely for that. It's a good option to balance out some of the heavier flavors. This is an incredible French-Korean fusion restaurant where the best entree combines each nation's signature dish - Kimchi Bouillabaisse - amazing! This was served piping hot, full of fresh seafood (shrimp, scallops, mussels, fried tofu, pollack) and housemade kimchi. The beef bourguignon was also incredible - the braised grass fed short rib literally fell off the bone, and the crushed potato doused in the short rib jus was unreal. We also met the friendliest people next to us - they were regulars and enlightened us to the "not-miss" items on the menu. Definitely a cool, chill crowd here. Also - they're BYOB so bring your favorite bottle or two.
Best breakfast in NYC !

There is a long wait... however, it's worth it. Try their lemonade, it's delicious. I've taken friends and boyfriends after that and they agree. The Large is large enough to share. Get the peas and rice (it's rice n' beans). Their entrees come with salad, cooked veggies, and rice. And one time when my boyfriend wanted some soda, the guy / waiter went out to buy him a can. HAHA. The smalls are under $10, and the large is only a few dollars more. It's ususally around $15 or so each... I go with the Jerk Chicken, usually.

O.M.G!!!!!!!!!!!!! I thought we died and gone to french fry heaven!!! My husband loves anything potato. We found this place on the food network t.v show and put it on the map for when we went to NY. We walked for miles to find this place and we figured we would need to walk off all the carbs after anyways. I am not big on fries like my husband but this was the best fries I had ever! Â They only cook french fries they are the best in the world specializing in the art of french fries or what ever they call them. When we walked in the place, there were a couple of Filipino ladies that were very kind and gave us plenty of free dipping sauces to try. Â  Â  It made me think of my Filipino girl friends back home in San Jo, you know who you are. When my husband got his order of fries he had been thinking about for the last year, he looked so shocked in all the photos I took of him Â with the fries. Shocked Â because I was actually going to let him eat all of them by himself? Nope! Â It's that Â the portions are so freakin big! Check out the photo's I posted. When ever we go to Red Robins he gets the bottomless fries and it's never enough. Â He even eats off my basket. You see Â my husband can eat, Â and any one that knows him, knows that about him, however this one time he couldn't even finish what he ordered which was a large.WHATTTTT! Pommes cooks the fries twice and the dipping sauce was so yummy. I had the Mexican cat-sup. No salt needed. It's a darn good thing that this place is not in San Jose, CA, Â or we would have some serious clogged artery's because we would go at least once a week that's how good they are. If you ever visit NY you have to put this on your list of places to eat. Sorry Tyrus, next time.

I went there with two friends and thoroughly enjoyed the evening. The place was packed despite it being a rainy Monday, but we were seated promptly for our 8pm reservation. Each of us ordered one appetizer and one entree, and their sweetbread appetizer & escargot appetizers must have been one of the best I've had in the city. Their seafood ceviche, however, was a disappointment both on the plate and on our palates... It's not their specialty, after all. The entrees were very good, but not as memorable as the appetizers, I wished I had ordered two appetizers instead... We were also excited to read great reviews about their desserts, but the two we shared were a bit too sweet and kind of boring. All 3 of us loved their espresso and coffee, as well as the festive atmosphere and great service. Although I prefer to go somewhere more quiet for a date, it's a great place to dine with a group of friends. With a bottle of very tasty and very reasonable red wine (around $40), we spent about $80 per person after tip. Not cheap, but certainly well worth it for their solid performance on food, wine, and service.

I was here a couple of weeks ago with some friends and highly recommend it! Â It was a fun, laid back place but the food was very good. Â We had a sparkling rose which was oh so tasty to go with our several dozen assorted and yummy oysters. Â They were sadly out of the lobster mac and cheese which we wanted to try, and the tuna tartar which really makes me want to just give 3.5 stars...but the service was so friendly and fun I bumped it up rather than down. Â The cod special was very tasty and so was the skate. Â Not a good place for a quiet dinner...but very fun with a small group!
Small tables, small plates, good food, big bill, pleasant waitstaff, found a hair in one of our lattes, won't ever go again.
Amazing food! Such a warm, welcoming and accommodating service! The flavors took me back to Ukraine, back to my childhood. Authentic dishes and the decor is such a treat! Highly recommend!

LOVE the Cuban sandwich with it's fresh pork that's prepared daily, smothered in melting cheesy goodness and finished with plentiful ham. And there's pickles and mustard and it's $4 cheaper than Porchetta...competition is good for the market right!

Awesome family restaurant. Different 'italian grandmother' chef each night. Good size portions and good wine list. Duck and eggplant boats were our favorites. 5min walk to the ferry. See you again soon!

This place is overrated. We stood in line for 45 minutes before the cart opened for dinner. As we were standing in line and a couple behind us mentioned that they wanted to eat here for their 1 year anniversary, and they drove far away just to eat here. Guess it must be that good to come here on a special occasion. We ordered the chicken-lamb gyro combo with rice. We were in Greece for 13 days before coming to NYC, so we ate a lot of gyros. Eating the gyro was not the same, since it is supposed to be meat sliced from a meat spinner. It seems like the chicken and lamb was sliced up and then grilled. The chicken and lamb was extremely dry with the rice and lettuce. Â In addition, You had to put the white and/or red sauce on it for some flavor and moisture. That is too bad because if food is made well, you do not need extra sauce. The food is cheap for $6, and you get really full. However, this our last meal in NYC, and the most disappointed one. Note: For those eating at this cart, please remember to throw away your containers in the trash can. It was gross to see containers lying on the benches and on the sidewalk. In addition, it helps keep the streets of NYC looking cleaner. Cash only.

This place is important. Â It saw a lack of competition in the nieghborhood for awesome freshly baked bread, and offers delicious things at reasonable prices. Â The folks at the window always have a smile. Â I got the focaccia with kale pesto, red onion and a few other things a few weeks ago and when I came today and they didn't have it, the lovely girl in the window offered to spread some pesto on it anyway. Â I'm currently writing from my carb coma. Â Luckily I passed out with a big smile on my face.
One of our favorite hidden treasures on the upper east side! Try the traditional or the chicken sandwich with veggies! The food is wonderful but the space is tight so try to go on off peak hours.

I came here with a group of friends, and had a good time! The decor is really interesting - there's a chandelier in the middle of the dining area - but it's supposed to be authentically Thai. Food was good and cheap! Chicken satay had an interesting plating. I got the green curry soft shell crab, which was delicious. Unfortunately, I'm not sure soft shell crab goes well with curry, because it ended up getting a little soggy, but the curry itself was fantastic. My boyfriend got the Room Service Pad Thai, and it was also delicious. This place isn't fancy, but it has good portions and solid food. I would probably come here again if I were in the area.

This is the first place I ate at in NYC- and don't regret it! It set up my whole day to success. The only reason it gets 4 stars is because it was an hour wait (place is tiny), but I guess I can't complain if it was that good! The staff was friendly, up beat and fun. The manager made sure to talk to us and make sure everything was good- I appreciated it! Now the food, my bf claimed to have had the best Benedict ( w salmon)- that's says a lot trust me! Cocktails was good but not mind blowing, they had two specialty, I only had the Magdalena. Lastly, shout out to the bartender for the free shot, a shot of rye was given to everyone near the bar and staff- pretty cool and fun!

Me and two roommates came here during the summer and I still remember every part of that meal. It was one of the best meals I've ever had! We had a 9 PM reservation but ran about 15 minutes late and they still seated us immediately. Goat Cheese tart- AMAZING! This is a must have. I was having a really difficult time sharing this with my roommates lol. It is savory and delicious and I love the texture. Escargot- This tasted like escargot I've had in paris and it was delicious! Especially with the bread. Moules Rochelaises- Again this was delicious. The apple and curry mixture was awesome. I got the Tournedos Rossini (the filet mignon) as my entree and the meat was cooked to perfection. It is topped with foie gras so I basically couldn't ask for anything better. Also Entrees come with unlimited vegetable sides and even if you are not a vege person you will love them. They are delicious! I can't wait to go back!

Sunday late afternoon Seamless Decent delivery time Beef and chicken Rendang Nasi Lemak It was very reasonable lunch. Seamless transaction was smooth. I wanted shrimp Rendag but not luck, changed to chicken. My chicken was tasty with unidentified dark spiced sauce and the same sauce in beef was also tasty. For delivery, the container was in a rectangle plastic container so coconut rice took over the most and small main (beef or chicken) pushed to the corner with boiled egg with another unidentified sweet-tasty-dark sauce and some pickles were on the other corner. I wished everything were on one bowl (paper) that I see in the photos. It's like a Japanese Don (over rice) and this way, all the flavors meet the end (bottom) and especially sweet-sour juice from the pickles and that makes very tasty. I would order from them again because it is the best Malaysian that delivers to my area that I know of. There is Cafe Asean (inconstancy in flavors), not for me.

This place is great! The food is so cheap but so good and huge portions. We got the cheese and potato pierogies to share and I got the roast chicken as my entree. The place is small and quaint. It is decorated cute and the service is great. I can't wait to go back.
This place is amazing. I came a food tour and tried their signature sandwich here. They make their own mozzarella cheese and the bread is so fresh. Delicious! I can't wait o go back for lunch!

Japanese hotpot is a lot of fun and the ingredients are very fresh here. Â I've been several times and have always walked out very satisfied. Â An order of the prime beef tends to be filling enough for me, but, if you are concerned that you will leave hungry, it is worth starting off with an order of their bee bim bop. Â It is the best I've ever had. Â My Korean friend is very picky about her bee bim bop and finds that this is the best she's ever had in New York (and I mention this because she certainly has more experience with bee bim bop than I). The wait for a walk in can be rather long and the foyer too tiny to keep warm, so plan on bundling up in the winter or kill time browsing some of the cute shops on 11th street.

Although a bit pricey (fairly standard for NY City prices), the food truly was inspired. Â From the perfectly fire-roasted eggplants in the Babaganoush to the perfectly warmed bread, the food was quite memorable. The food really was tasty, variety was plentiful, and this upscale setting really is unique for middle eastern cuisine in the City. Â I will certainly be going back with my friends to this spacious, trendy restaurant.

Do not get the shredded pork! I have no idea what that was but its basically pickled veggies, something strangely fishy and pork POWDER?! Had to go back for the number one. It was good, though I wouldn't call this place great by any means. I think Hanco in Cobble Hill is better.

They have a great Italian beer selection with a knowledgeable gentleman in that area. I have yet to try the food but it all looked and smelled great when I was walking around. I only wish it wasn't so crowded at any time of day, but that's a good thing to see a place frequently packed.

We wanted to check out this place after all the awesome reviews that we had rad about this place. The ambiance is awesome..clay pots on the ceiling. we got seated with no wait at about 830 PM on a Sat evening.. We started with the grape leaves, meatballs and the large shrimps as appetizers. for the main course we had the short rib and the lamb chops. All the food that we ordered was really fresh and tasty..The food is on the pricier side but you get what youre paying for!

So let's see... The people that work here are really nice and I've got to say, the food is pretty nice too. I started off with their Steak Tartare: yum. I followed that with the Pork: also good - not as good as my appetizer but good. WHY NOT 5 STARS: Place is very small so it felt claustrophobic and loud.

Eataly = fun and delicious. Go to the pasta/pizza restaurant (hopefully you will get Le as your waitress- she is so wonderful) and order the TSG (Traditional Specialty Guaranteed) pizza then proceed to the chocolate counter and order a $1.09 shot of chocolate. If you do this you will never be sad again.

We just wanted a slice of pizza to tie us over till dinner but no such luck as most of these famed NYC pizza joints do not sell by the slice. There was a massive crowd milling about outside waiting for their chance to eat this coal fired pizzas. We opted to do takeout which involves making your way through the hungry line of people waiting for a table where you have to go to the kitchen in the back. We opted for the calzone for $13 and could add any two items along with the ricotta cheese. We ordered the sautÃ©ed garlic spinach and meatballs. The wait is awkward because you don't want to remain in the kitchen where all the staff are frantically working. Nor do you want to stand outside of the kitchen in the narrow hallway as you're pretty much staring at diners and also being in the way of servers. But you don't want to be so far away that you don't hear your order being called! This is take out limbo if there ever was one. Anyways, our calzone was done in about 20 mins and we took the massive thing to the park next door. It was a nice day and obviously other Lombardi customers were there since the trash cans were overflowing with Lombardi pizza boxes. I'm sure the kiddies who play in that playground must love all the tourists who treat this play area as their dining room. Other than the annoying pigeons, it was nice to dine outside on a warm sunny day. The calzone did not disappoint even though I wanted the pizza. The calzone's Â dough, which I imagine to be the same as the pizza dough is the right flavour and consistency without taking away from the other ingredients. The marinara dipping sauce tasted very simple but very delicious as it made the calzone even more yummy. The marinara is made with San Marzano tomatoes, which makes for a very balanced sauce. The meatballs and the spinach were both well seasoned and made for a very substantial late lunch for two. I'd love to go back and try their pizza! CASH ONLY! On a very side note...the washroom near the kitchen is super awkward. The wall in front of the toilet gives you no room to sit properly. Sorry for the odd detail but I had to mention it.
Awesome place! Best burger in the city. Excellent service and quaint atmosphere. Highly recommend it.
Wow. Amazing. Â Just come here and try it yourself!

So at around 10am on this fateful Thursday morning, I received an email in my Inbox informing me that we were going on a team-field trip to Il Corallo Trattoria. I was pleased while also being intrigued as this location had never been sampled by myself while most of its surrounding neighborhood had, this would be an exciting lunch. As we were rolling in 15 deep, 15 of my esteemed colleagues shuffled into this classic Italian joint and were ushered to our long table. As we began saluting one another's accomplishments of 2012, it felt a la Goodfellas, well played Mr. Ilardi. There was Crostini Pomodoro, Mussels, Prosciutto, and Insalata Puglia - these were just the appetizers. My colleagues ordered a plethora of Cucina Italiano - Taglierini Sorrento,Farfalle Di Spiaggia Â Salmone Fettucini, Lobster Pesto Ravioli, Rigatoni Sardi. The food was indeed solid. The conversation was hilarious, and mustache jokes were tossed around. We even had a colleague order Tiramisu because apparently he wasn't thrown from the massive plate of pasta he had just engulfed. Il Corallo Trattoria - you did proper things to all of us. Indeed, we all have stomachs full of fantastic cuisine and are powering through this sunny afternoon at the office.

Mmmmmmmmmmm sooooooo gooooooooood. Three of us showed up at 7p Thursday night and were told there'd be a 2 hour wait. Â So, we walked around the corner and drank for two hours. Â No problem with that. Â  The wait time was accurate but completely worth it. Â I ordered the classic beef naked balls with their spicy tomato sauce over polenta. Â A friend ordered veggie ball sliders. Â The other friend had their special meatballs (mint with raisin) in a salad. Everything was delicious!! And then.... ICE CREAM SAMIMCHES! Mmmmmmmm ice cream. I'm such a sucker for ice cream. Especially in sammich form. So they let you mix n match your cookie to the flavor or ice cream. Â These are pretty large - definitely shareable. Â And absolutely tasty! The size of the place is a little obnoxious; they really cram you in and there's only one bathroom. But it was a fun atmosphere (shared table) and the food really was fantastic.

Mmmm, Market Table. Â Joey Campanaro does not disappoint with Market Table. Â If you are a fan of the Little Owl, then you will love Market Table. Â The Yellow Fin Tuna appetizer is amazing and just the right blend of spice and citrus. Â From the main courses, all of the fish dishes are incredible, especially the arctic char. Â I particularly enjoyed the whole fish (branzino), but I didn't care for the escarole mix that it was served on top of. Â It really didn't compliment the flakiness of the fish. Â I felt like the whole fish could be served simply with olive oil and lemon over greens or something a bit lighter. Â The pan roasted chicken is also quite good and is served over a yummy sweet potato salad with brown butter. Â Overall I really enjoy Market Table. I have been there several times and have not been disappointed yet.

The savior of Hester Street Fair vendors, Cafe Grumpy became the go-to place on Saturdays for lattes. (Coffee is served at the Fair.) The baristas are friendly and the lattes are smooth. The baked goods are a little pricey.

WARNING: This post will be a bit biased, as I am a vegetarian, reviewing a BBQ restaurant. First off, you may be asking, "If she is a vegetarian, why in the world, of all the meat-free spots in Williamsburg, does this gal choose a BBQ joint?" I had a friend coming in from Boston to visit. He eats meat. A lot of it. He competes in BBQ cook-offs and sometimes even wins. Boston doesn't have good BBQ. Fette Sau does. Now that that is cleared up... I ended up ordering every single side. He ordered every single meaty thing possible (give him a break. He's tired of Bostonian French cuisine.) The potato salad was really good (not too mayo-y), as was the broccoli, which was basted in really great herbs. He raved about the pork belly, and even took photos of it to make his dad jealous. (Yet no photos of me. What am I- chopped liver? Granted, he probably WOULD have taken photos of chopped liver.) Anyway. They have some fun soda flavors in bottles- orange cream, sarsaparilla, espresso, etc. Tried a couple of those, but ultimately ended up drinking a lot of whiskey. Good whiskey. In an area that typically only serves PBR, I was very surprised to see what all they had to offer at the bar. I would come here again solely for drinks, actually. All in all, if you like BBQ, come here. I've lived in Texas and I know just how big a deal good BBQ is, and if you're a Southern transplant, I definitely would recommend this to you to get your messy, greasy, fatty fix.

Not really worth the hype or the long wait in line. The only thing decent is the soup dumplings. Nothing really too special about these dumplings except for the size. Also, don't bother ordering anything else. Things I usually get at almost every Chinese restaurant does not look the same here and tastes pretty bad. If you want some soup dumplings, just go to any Chinese restaurant in Chinatown that offers dim sum and they should have it.
Amazing. Â Reminds me of sitting on a dock in Maine.

Everyone raving about their fries and dipping sauces are right! Delish! Â Burgers are pretty decent size considering we r in nyc, and fry/onion rjng combo def big enough for 2. Beer was reasonably priced also-25 oz was around 7 dollars, my 25oz light beer was 5 dollars! Hah! Only thing that wasnt impressive was it def looked like the typical burger shack with wax paper lining the reusable fry basket, but i dont need sterlin silver to cut my burger either. Make sure u ask for sauce on side if u r picky, i got western burger bc of the onions n mushrooms, n it came w a sauce i wasnt crazy about, but my boyfriend loved. House sauce was a little bbq-like. Napkin burger has nicer ambiance n selection of foods in general, but bareburgers fries blow it outta the water, in my opinion.

Came here with my gf for dinner around 8pm on a thursday. It's about 1/2 hour wait they said but I'm sure we waited for at least 45 mins. It is super packed and crowded. Â We had to share a table with a party of four that was finishing their meal. Ordered the scallion pancake, shanghai flat noodle, pork soup dumplings and crab soup dumplings. The food was ok but the soup dumplings were warm at best when it came out. I kept on getting hit by the waiters when they walk by because I sat on the edge and it was so packed. When the party of 4 left, the waiters were cleaning/wiping down the table shaking the whole table while we were eating. I thought that was pretty inconsiderate. Then they seated 2 more parties of 2. Yes, that's 3 different parties of 2 in one table. Awkward. In conclusion, nothing spectacular and there are other shanghai places in CT that ain't as crowded.

Southern California has much better Peruvian food, sorry to say. I was underwhelmed with many of the dishes. Lomo saltado wasn't saucy. Pio pio chicken was meh. Plantains were dry. And lil smokey sausages with french fries was kind of weird. The ambiance is nice. It's very dark and modern (kind of feels like a club).

I've always dined in the Tavern, not the dining room, but it hardly matters. Anything you order at Gramercy will be delicious, and the staff is always helpful and friendly, always offering friendly recommendations. Sitting at the bar to eat offers the same tavern menu, but sometimes is more fun if you're alone or just a party of two. If you want a great meal with great service, go to Gramercy. Also, Micah Danger in the kitchen is an amazing chef =)

This was my neighborhood diner for about 10 years and it made me not like other diners as much, as a result. The food was always fresh, fast and served with a smile. It's a little sad that Gus isn't around to great you and hassle you, but Tom's lived on. The Turkey Melt sandwich is amazing, burgers are solid and I always went for straight ahead eggs or corned beef hash for breakfast. It's worth the wait, especially since you get cookies, oranges and coffee in line. Once you get inside and get to listen to big band tunes and enjoy the decor, you'll settle down. Get an order of Silver Dollars to share with your table - you get to sample the unique butters and damn good pancakes.

I'm going to keep this simple. You will most likely wait at least 2 hours. They don't take reservations. Our party waited for 3 hours. Needless to say we were HANGRY. I thought to myself that even if the food is amazing I'm writing a 1-star review. We order, we eat. The food is outstanding. The service was good. It made up for our wait. I licked my plate clean. I died and went to heaven when I finished it off with a chocolate and salted caramel pot de creme. Really simple menu but prepared excellently.

The sushi here is very good and very affordable. There are a wide variety of different rolls and each one that I have tried has been good. It's a small place, I guess you could call it cozy. My only complaint is the waitstaff "hovers" constantly.
Those pork buns are magic. I've heard the wait can be really intense, but I didn't experience that on a Sunday afternoon. The ramen is huge though, so arrive hungry!

I go here fairly often... I've been here for dinner a few times but i usually go for lunch for the burger or short rib sandwich which are great. Â Chopped salad is pretty rad also. So glad this is close by on Myrtle... hope to see more places like this in our neighborhood. Â They have a nice outdoor area as well.

While it should be expected from such an acclaimed ramen restaurant, my problem about this place was still the damn wait. If it weren't for the special occasion of visiting NYC to see friends, I definitely would have ditched the place from the minute they told me it was a 2.5 hr wait to eat at another wonderful restaurant down the street that easily could have been just as satisfying as Ippudo. Nonetheless, I waited it out, and even endured the extra hour it took for us to get seated. I do admit that as one who has not experienced it before, the walk from the front lobby to the our table was pretty kickass because of their traditional way of welcoming the guests into the dining area. Â Although not a standard layout of a traditional ramen eatery, the restaurant's general way of running the floor is very cool. I ordered the Akamaru Modern, and it was served very hot. To the waiter's instructions, I mixed all of the flavors to make it one consistent bowl. The first taste was absolutely wonderful. The broth tasted hearty and rich, which I took a special liking to, perhaps from the dreary weather outside. Their use of tonkatsu noodles is a great call. The noodles had texture but a nice softness to it, and it also blended and complimented the taste of all the ingredients. The meat melted in my mouth and the rest of the ingredients tasted of high quality. I do wish that they gave a little bit more than a 2-3 slices of meat, as it was a larger bowl of ramen than in most other places, but hey can't complain. Â I also had the pleasure of trying (and finishing) my friend's Shiromaru Traditional, which also didn't fail to impress! I liked my Akamaru Modern slightly more because it had more of that garlic and miso taste which I enjoyed very much. The meal ended with cups of green tea, which really refreshed the whole experience and made a great conclusion to the night. Until we were too tempted to order a round of pork buns. Needless to say, they was amazing. The pork belly simply melted in my mouth, fused with the soft white bun and tangy mayonaise sauce that simply worked together perfectly. Very pricey which made my friends and I reluctant to try it at first, but that experience really made us understand why and regret nothing. The only downside I could think of is that they could have put another slice in the bun, and I'm not saying that to be greedy. The bun just wasn't as full as it should be, given how much meat I get in my taiwanese bao's for half the price. Like my Akamaru Modern, it just lacked a tiny bit that would have made the dish more complete and over the roof. I left that place feeling so very happy for the rest of the night, kind of as if I were slightly inhibited. It was definitely the closest experience I've ever had to real Japanese cuisine, and at the end of the night, I am very glad that I waited out the hours and hours of anticipation for this experience (for the most part).

Despite the high prices, small portions and cramped seating this is one of the best restaurants in Brooklyn. They just serve about half the amount of food I'd get at most restaurants with a similarly priced menu. Everything on the menu that I've had is perfectly prepared with the exception of the salted chocolate caramel pie. It is so intensely salty and sugary that it made me shake and ruined my meal. the thing is that I managed to forget that I'd ordered it before. Why did I order it TWICE!?

I'm starting to come here at least once a week. On my other visits I've tried: - Special pasta w/ mushroom, olive oil, garlic - Delicious - Taglioni ai Frutti Di Mare - Seafood cooked well, sauce was delicious, pasta was cooked perfectly al dente, would order over and over again - Black linguini with Frutti Di Mare (special) - the first time squid ink taste actually made a difference in taste rather than just gimmicky color - Lasagna - Crave satisfying - Pasta special w/ prosciutto, garlic, olive oil - I've concluded you can't go wrong with any pasta dish from Bianca! - Pasta special w/ sausage, broccoli rabe - Great amount of broccoli rabe and sausage - Grilled radicchio and prosciutto - Great grilled flavor on the radicchio - Tagliatelle alla bolognese - Sauce was meaty but did lack flavor, not my favorite

Finally, I tried The Halal Guys. It was very very good. I got the mix over rice and both the chicken and the gyro was good, but I liked the chicken more. The white sauce was awesome and the Egyptian guy who took care of our order was very welcoming and friendly. also, the pita bread was very yummy. The prices are very good $20 for 3 people with drinks! I will go back again in my next trip to NYC.

This place never fails to disappoint. Service is always excellent. Food is always great. It's a bit expensive but always with it. The hirata buns are definitely what keep me coming the most. The ramen is always on point. They average out to $14 dollars for a bowl of ramen. But it is worth it. Cause you will be full. You can add boiled eggs or mor pork for $1 each. You get that and an appetizer, you won't have room for desert. Don't know much about the drinks since I go for the food. This place is busy at all times. They get 4 stars only because the wait is always long. If only you can reserve. But you can't at either locations. This is their first restaurant... they have opened a new one recently. The other one is on the west side on 51st street. You should expect a wait at peak times for dinner between 5-10pm. They close at 11pm mostly. The wait time around that time will always be 45-2hrs wait. So plan ahead and just reserve a spot in person cause you can't do it by phone. But it is always worth the wait.

Delicious, and so cheap. We split the mini empanadas appetizer (so good) and followed it up with an arepa apiece. The bill came to $20 and we were stuffed. Service and atmosphere were both good. Great place for a casual, affordable, and tasty dinner.

If I had a million dollars to spend at an antique fair, this is what my house would look like. Walls of vintage mailboxes are used to deliver wine to their monthly wine club members. Faded issues of Better Homes and Gardens sit on a rustic magazine racks. Long, plain lightbulbs with their filaments glowing inside hang in an industrial straight line. And walking through the frosted glass and metal bathroom doors, you're either expecting to go see the principal or confide in a private eye. Colors are dark an rich. And my favorite, the wine room has a hand decorated wall complete with rows of brass studs and little random brass moldings. Sigh, what I would do with a wall like that in my study. Oh wait, I don't have a study. Oh, the food sucked cuz we were there for a set menu brunch with a group of 16. But I would love to go back, get all decked out in a slinky pewter dress and fishnets and try the michelin star menu at the bar.

Having been inspired by the Food Network's Anne Burrell's review on Blue Ribbon in the city, I decided I had to second her raves on the beef oxtail & marrow marmalade. Â I had a similar dish once before in a different restaurant, but there was that Â je ne sais quoi about this one. Â Spreading the marrow with the wooden sticks, kissing it with oxtail stew sauce onto ttoasted garlic bread, then sprinkling rock sea salt, I must say I had a good time playing with my food. Â Fortunately, the creation is a warm, comforting guilty pleasure---it's almost devious in a way. All of it together is so bad---I mean, high fat content and then the salt....clearly a cardiologist's nightmare, but my edible dream come true! Â  The raw bar serves my Western oysters---a huge plus in my book, and the bar servers are super friendly. FYI, weekends get pretty packed, but the bonus is that they're open late night!

OMG if you are looking for a delicious 5 course lunch or dinner you NEED to go here. All the chefs in the back freshly prepare your gourmet meal. You can watch them making food from the door before their entrance and see whats going on in the kitchen. The service was amazing and for how much food we got and for how delicious it was, the set lunch price of only $35 per person included 6 courses! all delicious and melt in your mouth. YUM! always going back here.

Spicy wontons! YES! But the seating is just awful, and it took quite a while. Â When you finally get the food though, all the grumbles before that seem to melt away, and you're just enjoying rich flavors of pork and seasonings.

it's our staple brunch place near midwood. Â  we have been here a few times. Â we love the walk - it's a sight seeing tour of victorian houses. Â the food is always good. Â i love the fisherman's eggs; the french toast is good. Â my boyfriend has tried several egg and meat dishes and likes them all. Â the service is always a hit even when they are busy. i will be here on nice days. Â the back yard is cute and lovely - a great place for brunch on a sunny afternoon.

Don't be afraid -- eat the pigs feet! Despite what other reviewers say, I've always had a pleasant experience here. Â Yes, it is small and can get crowded, but that's part of the atmosphere. Â  I've found the wait staff to be very friendly and attentive. I've tried most of the menu, and would recommend everything. Â This place is know for it's use of pig parts, and if you're not squeamish, you'll enjoy it. Â The grilled tonsoku, veal liver sashimi, and tonton hop pot are three of my favorites.
Amazing Fish and Lobster Tacos. Highly recommend!

We ordered a slew of appetizers; most notably the headcheese, which was banging, but also the pickled eggs, the kale salad, some blue cheese & compote, & some potatoes fried in duck fat (ranked in order of personal preference). I ordered the heritage pork meatball sandwich, & was well pleased with its heft & its taste.

This is a late night kind of place for me. Â Been a favorite haunt of mine for years now. Â Stumble in for the after party at Cafeteria. Â This is comfort food at its finest. I'm talking about the Mac and Cheese Trio : Truffle Mac n Cheese, Bacon Mac and Cheese & the traditional Cheesy Mac. Â I fiend for their Mac N Cheese, often, btw. Â The dates with blue cheese and almonds are one word: Amazing. Â Big fan of the chicken and waffles as well. Â If you are there early, grab a wildberry mojito. Â I appreciate the drinks but that is not why I come, at all. Â I love this place with a big group, especially since they set up the private back room. Â Makes for a bit more upscale and intimate experience back there now. Â Bathrooms with the window in the back must have been a guys design, its the only thing I dislike about the place. Â But, don't be shocked to see the full gamut from the uber trendy, eclectic, bohemiam to just plain janes of all ages. Â It is amazing for people watching. Â But if you stripped away the ambiance and the people, it would still just be an amazing comfort food experience. Â Just order the right stuff: Mac N Cheese! :)

Party of four. Â We had a 5:30 reservation (the only time they had available), therfore we were running a little late for a 7:00 show. Â  Â We forced ourselves to order very little because we had very little time to enjoy the meal and we could not take anything with us. Â Service was adequate, not great, basically they brought us our menu's quickly, took our order and brought the dishes out within good time. Â Server checked on us once, when the entrÃ©e came out and the rest of the time we had to keep flagging him down for drink order, dessert, coffee/digestif, and bill. Â All the while he was standing by the cashier/register station 8ft. away from us talking with co-workers.... he's lucky my husband tips well. We had the stuffed mushrooms. Â Only eight of them, which I thought was a little skimpy for the price, but tasty, Chicken with lemon sauce 8 pieces descent amount and very delicious. Â They charge you $10 for a side of pasta for the table.......... Great, no problem, but the side was extremely small. Â I make pasta all the time and I can honestly say it was about a 1/4lb of linguine (if that!!), as cheap as pasta is, they could have added 1/2 a pound and still had a huge profit! Â Tiramisu was delicious and HUGE, we had to leave half of it. Â They charged us a corkage fee of $28, which was more than I expected but, it was my favorite wine and I would have paid a lot more if I would have purchased a good bottle there. Â  I will go back with more time, to order different things from the menu and enjoy a slower paced meal. Â Hopefully we will have more attentive service.

First thing I had on the street in new york because every time I passed by it there is always a crowd of patient customers waiting in line for the food. I see people in the hotel eating it for lunch as well. It was really good. I had the combo, a nypd recommended it to me.

OMG, incredible. Â  It's rare that a place so hyped up can meet expectation but I remember standing in line for 20 min, getting my food and next thing I know the food is gone in my stomach. Â  I completely inhaled this and will come back to this place each time I go to NYC.
Good!

Awesome! Â Gluten-free selections. Spectacular service. Friendly wait staff and a warm and cozy environment. My 10yr old LOVED it! Â We try 1 gluten free restaurant a month and this is by far the best we've had. Gluten free bread, pasta meatballs and her favorite -red velvet cake!!! Â I have never given 5 stars to any place but Bistangos deserves it!!

Apart from the soft-boiled instead of poached eggs, we had a good brunch there, at a good price -- eggs dish + juice + tea/coffee for $15,50 --, which would deserve a 3 or 4-star rate, but the service was so poor that I can only give them 2 stars. I really felt like in Paris... but in the wrong way: I could tell our waiter was French only because of his attitude (and I'm French too!), unfriendly and barely polite. Not sure I would come back, I would rather go to any other place with a nice and considerate staff, as I'm used to in NY.

The wait is long, so what? At least they let you grab some Japanese beer at the bar while waiting. It's expensive, so what? It's the best freakin ramen in the States! I won't make this review long because there are so many reviews on this restaurant anyway. Akamaru Modern - MUST. GET. With an egg, of course. Tori Ramen - If you want something else. Very clean taste. Chicken broth tends to make me feel gross afterwards.. Not this one! Pork Buns - W...t....h.... WHY SO GOOD?!?! You must get this. I don't care how full you'll be from the ramen. This is a must. I have yet to try their desserts.. But this place is as close as New York will EVER get to a real Japanese ramen. And I will forever love this place.
This continues to be one of the best restaurants in the city. Â I prefer to sit upstairs but regardless it is always an amazing experience and I wish we could eat there even more often

All I have to say is don't forget your earplugs. It's so loud you can barely talk or hear. I wouldn't recommend taking your mom or granny. Our server was nice but overwhelmed. We ask another waiter for a bottle of wine and he promptly got it and took our order. Amazing food, cozy room. Loved the riceballs and veal parmesan but would have preferred spaghetti instead of the penne rigate it came with.

Awesome, unbelievable food, lives up to the legend and the fame! Got there on a Saturday morning, at around 1130am and were the last people to sit immediately, so plan on arriving there soon after opening to avoid the long waits. The atmosphere is also spot on. We got the pork buns. Get the pork buns, you will not regret. Just get them.. Trust me. I can still taste them ah.. We then got the regular ramen and the spicy ramen (forgot the Japanese names). Really delicious flavor and just the right amount of broth and noodles. Eat them asap cause they are meant to be eaten right as it is served. The spicy ramen is not TOO spicy and has a good flavor to it. We added an egg to our order - they make these perfectly. Finally we got the dessert with green tea ice cream, red bean, green tea jelly, and mochi, with a mint leaf and a Japanese milk you pour over. It's $9, pretty good mix of flavors for dessert, and fairly worth it if you feel like splurging!

As a huge fan of grilled cheese, I was very excited when this stand opened. Â It's a bit difficult to find, down the stairs toward the subway by Lexington and 53rd. Â The staff are super friendly and seem actually happy to deal with the crowded midtown lunch masses. Â Get the tater tots and homemade lemonade with the grilled cheese of your choice (I love the tuna melt). Also, fantastic for a cheap breakfast. Â Just finished their egg white wrap with 3 egg whites, oven roasted tomatoes, swiss cheese and turkey. Delicious and about $6 bucks. Portions aren't huge, even the sandwiches could be bigger, but they're satisfying.

The food is good, thus 3 stars. The Muscles - yum (and I haven't liked them before, but the sauce was great) the bruscetta - quite nice with eggplant and cheese. And MEATBALLS...mmm spaghetti and meatballs were sooo good. BUT as good as the food is, the prices are high - $16 for spaghetti? This place now has a corkage fee ($15) preventively high. The servers don't talk to the management about the corkage fee (with a new liquor license). Â And the wine menu (which is suppose to change sucks too, so PLEASE change it). Lastly, the decor is odd. It is the "unfinished look" or is it unfinished? I can't tell..... and it is HOT, what happened to their AC?

I moved away from Brooklyn recently and I am now having Biblio withdrawals symptoms. I miss this place so much. Everything is amazing here. Awesome and varied beer selection, great staff, laid back but classy atmosphere and *phenomenal* food. The brunch here is life changing. I recommend everything. Like, Everything.

My family went here to celebrate my graduation 5/31. I saw the sign on the door about no tank tops and thought that my sister would not be able to go in. Unfortunately, that was not the case. We didn't know it was family style we thought it was just a regular menu. The waiter was very polite and helpful especially since we were new to the restaurant.Though I didn't like how the main meal dishes were separated into two. After the ziti 15 mins or so later we got the chicken parm. I thought the food could be a little warmer and not separated. The bread was warm, but not hot and fresh like Cara Mia which is our favorite place. Overall the food is good and it is a place to go to if you like family style and their style of serving food.

you know it's legit when it's also a jewelry store. there's nowhere that competes to banh mi's down in houston...but this place comes close. bread is fresh, toasted perfectly. toppings on your sandwich are just right. go for the grilled pork - spicy. it's large, so be prepared to walk around after :) for $4-$5, a great and filling lunch to stop in and try.

Recently dining at Cafe Orlin provided yet another example of why I totally love my girlfriend so much and how we have so much in common and often think alike. It had actually been a few years since I had last eaten at Orlin, and it was our first time eating here together. After coming in from the rain, we planted ourselves at a table in the farthest section over from the entrance. My girlfriend didn't even really look at the menu since she pretty much knew what she wanted. It took me no more than a minute or so to decide what I wanted, and as soon as I put the menu down she asked me what I was going to get. I told her the penne with chicken (prepared in a cream sauce with sun-dried tomatoes, mushrooms, and mozzarella). She gave me a surprised look while simultaneously uttering the words "no way, that's what I'm going to get." It happens a lot with us when our thoughts are synchronized. It's awesome. She then acknowledged that it's her favorite dish on the menu and, as it turned out, it was absolutely delicious and the perfect portion size. The chicken had very nice moist herbal flavor and the cream wasn't overloaded or too thick...a splendid concoction. Love and good food. What can be better than that? I like the chill, laid-back atmosphere. It's not grandiose by any stretch of the imagination, but comfortable and generally quiet (with exception to loud-mouth Charlie talking loudly on his cell phone for what seemed like 20 minutes). I found it incredibly rude and irritating, and if I hadn't been so focused gazing into the beauty of my girlfriend's eyes and enjoying our conversation, I might've gone over to the guy and voiced my displeasure at his blunt-force discourtesy by telling him to finish his call outside in the rain. I didn't let it ruin our mood, however, and shortly thereafter the man left the cafe. Of note, our server was very friendly and provided quality service.

Crispy crusty, gooey cheesey goodness. I stopped in during a Soho shopping break and had two huge slices (margherita, pepperoni). Browsed the many pics on the wall while waiting for my slices. Devoured them, burnt the top of my mouth a little because I couldnt wait for it to cool, and was a little too stuffed afterwards to continue shopping so I went home and took a nap. I would like to recreate that afternoon in the very near future.

I stared at the menu for awhile, trying to figure out if I should order 1 or 2 of the chicken biscuits. I'd heard such great things about it, and at only $5.50 it seemed so low on price that I questioned if it'd be big enough for me. I went conservative and ordered only 1, which ended up being a good move. Was it insanely delicious? YES. Perfectly fried chicken, doused in buffalo sauce, plopped on an over-buttered bun, and dripping with juices on every bite. Should you eat more than one of them in a sitting? Probably not, unless it's your last meal and you have no issues with massive butter consumption. Couple of things to note: Yes, I did have to wait about 20 minutes for a table on a Saturday morning. And I did try another item on the brunch menu--the chocolate cake with coconut doughnut. I say skip the doughnut and keep your eyes on the chicken biscuit prize.

this place is a mainstay in my rotation. **** for brunch! Place is a fave! Really good food and great prices. Steak and Eggs are a great deal though my favorite are the arepas benedictos w jamon. huevos rancheros and french toast also kick ass. Only complaint is the coffee, weak stuff. *** for other. I think the dinner is good. Fun spot and awesome deals on Tuesdays. Reliably good Latino food. The chips are a unique blend of tubers which go well w the guac.

Ok so I really don't want to be the one who ruins the party here, so I won't :) but I must stay true to my opinion on those reviews (otherwise what's the point...). I really have nothing bad to say about this food, but I also struggle to understand the crazy hype around it. To me it was just a pretty much ordinary mediterranean fast food type of meal. Maybe because those crazy good reviews here build up an unrealistic expectations or maybe because I've lived almost two decades in the Middle East but that falafel and shawarma just didn't do that to me. I've had the Teaser platter btw.

its basically a takeout place. Â they have a couple tables - but dont count of them. Â there's always a line - but it moves pretty quick. we had the lamb schwarma - was incredible. Â the hot sauce has quite a kick -- i eat a ton of super spicy food, so if your spice tolerance is not high, would suggest you go very easy on the spice. the hummus was really good -- the kids polished it off and asked for more. Â same with the baba ganoush. would definitely make a trip if we are in the neighbourhood again.

Great cozy little Italian restaurant. A coworker and I went to Caffe Linda for dinner while on a business trip after seeing the high Yelp ratings. I ordered the whole wheat pasta with arugula. While a very simple dish it was very good. I didn't feel miserably full after my meal. (That's not a knock on the portion size either. It was a decent portion. ) My coworker got the black linguini with seafood and she rated it a 5 star dinner. For dessert I had the coconut sorbet and she had the tiramisu, both excellent. Â The prices are definitely on the higher side but luckily for us we got to expense it.

This is the pizza experience I was hoping for on my first visit to Brooklyn! A good friend of mine had read glowing reviews in Time Out, and being in walking distance to her place, we decided to check it out. We were pretty hungry by the time we got there, having had drinks at a nearby pub just before. We were quoted a 40 minute wait time for a table at 7:30 on a Sunday night, so we just decided to get it to go. It would have been nice to linger over dinner in what looked like a pretty intimate, warm space, but we were starving! Within about 7-10 minutes of ordering, we were walking out the door with three hot boxes of pizza. Thank God for wood-fired ovens! We ordered the Arugula, Eggplant and Zucchini, and the Margarita. Hands down the Arugula was the best. The salty shavings of parmigiano reggiano mixed with its peppery salad accompaniment made for a perfectly balanced pizza. The Eggplant and Zucchini pizza was good, but nothing special. The Margarita was pretty fantastic. All the ingredients were pure and fresh, cleanly distinguishable on your taste buds. Perfection. This was also the first time I've tried flor di latte mozzarella, which was on all the pizzas. It made for such creamy goodness in each bite. Â Chicago pizza just can't compete.
Great lunch spot. Â If you don't know what you want to eat, you'll find something to your liking here.

I've always had a decent experience at Hu, and love the food lifestyle philosophy they subscribe to. However this morning the service was brusque and unfriendly. There were 4 other customers at the juice/coffee bar, it was not busy at all. I was ordering the demi vert and the fellow helping me directed me to the fridge for the pre-made juices. The one I wanted wasn't there, and he was very reluctant to make a fresh one for me. When he handed me the juice, he asked if I wanted a straw and threw it at me. The woman ringing me up on the register was rude as well. The manager made a weak apology which did not seem genuine at all. I am never going back there. Their branding it great, but it does not follow through to the people and their attitude.
There is much better if you search in the nooks and crannies of NYC. Grimaldis is good, but highly overrated.

This was my second time eating here - I was not part of the Yelp community back then. A friend who lived in Woodside said this Thai place a pretty good and that I should try it out...when I got there I had a mini deja vu moment - I had been here before but about 2-3 years ago . It was relatively warm that Sunday, so I figured what the heck I'm a glutton for pain - bring on the spicy foods. The front of the place is not fancy, but once I walked up close I noticed they had expanded since I was last there and now they have about three store fronts worth of space! I suppose even in this recession, good Thai food is still a winner. In addition, the melting pot of patrons waiting to be served is a testament that this place is genuine and plain Thai food goodness. It was packed as expected but the wait wasn't too painful, it was a breezy and sunny Sunday, about a 15 minute wait. Once seated, My friend and I ordered a chicken curry puff to start along with a Thai ice tea + tapioca. The puffs were gone in about 2 minutes, we were hungry. I like spicy foods, but I'm definitely not hardcore - my friend who was Korean reminded me that their stuff is particularly spicy. He went on to order this bowl of curry chicken + rice. With that I chickened out and decided to stay safe with a Pad Thai...I know, I wussed out, but there's always next time. After about 30 minutes, we had finally got our food but that is not before we flagged the waiter down twice. The Pad Thai was quite tasty and flavorful, noodles weren't clumping which indicates they weren't overcooked. Judging from the pink faced Korean guy sitting in front of me and beads of sweat on his forehead, either there was a pretty girl smiling at him or the dish was very spicy, or both. I was sort of glad I got the Pad Thai. We sat near the door to the terrace area which was for the outdoor diners, along with the entrance to the restrooms. This will set the premise for quite an entertaining scenario as the line to the ladies room grew and some women just couldn't wait, so many just ran into the men's room. In one instance, a couple came out of the men's room which caused some eyebrows to be raised by the people sitting around the area. I understand it was a particularly busy day, but it would have been nice for the waiter to let us know that the food was a bit delayed. We were both hungry and sat around for about 30 minutes before my friend had to ask where the food was. Food was great, but the service was OK and in my book that is fine once - will definitely return when I can. Happy fooding.

I was very unimpressed with the food. The empanadas were dry. The shrimp skewers were meh. The brussel sprouts were tiny but were probably the best thing I had and that's not saying much. The space is nice but loud. I would not recommend it based on the below average food.

Mmm, corned beef hash w/ poached eggs then with a little dash of ketchup and their hot sauce. YUM! Oh and their biscuits and gravy is to die for too! Their FRESH homemade biscuits are seriously to die for. I LOVE IT! This place is definitely one of the cuter places for brunch. BUT the only downside, it gets packed and it took a while to be able to seat our table of 6, but I guess trying to seat a group of 6 for brunch is always a lot harder... Besides the wait, I do have to say this place is a must try! The food is just DELISH!

Di Fara has been my favorite pizza spot since my first visit in High School, over 11 years ago. If you're looking for a clean, fast pizza spot where servers kiss your behind, this is not the place to go. However, you'll be missing out on the best slice in NYC. Dom makes the best pizza, hands down.

Ordered 12 pieces of fried pork & chive dumplings ($3) and a large wonton soup ($2.50) to split between the two of us. Both items were average and nothing spectacular flavour wise. Very cheap prices which will definitely fill you up but really nothing special at all. The place did not seem very clean and the guy taking all the orders (who also handled food) had a cold (he kept sniffing his nose and clearing his throat), which made me kind of uneasy.

One of our local favs - great guac, delicious salads, enchiladas, steaks, excellent drinks and fantastic staff. Â Big plus is they are open late night for that last call before bed. Â Only downside is it gets quite packed on the weekends but def. worth the wait.

When you find a place that you know you love despite waiting for a table or quick service, you don't just stop going out of frustration, you find a better way to accommodate yourself. The first time I came here it was on the weekend for brunch and the wait was long. Now, if I can help it, I come right when they open to be first seated. It's unreal how quickly the place fills up even on week days. That being said, the food is always so goddamn good. I always get the Down by Law chicken sandwich. I sub the avocado fur onion rings and it is amazing. Bacon jam?! The best thing ever made. I love this sandwich so much that it is hard to try new things, but I think I'm okay with it. The corn fritters are delicious, the decor is one of my favorite things about it, and my boyfriend loves the Mexicoke. It gives you a hip but homey feel and I can't ever see myself getting tired of it. Thank you for existing, Queens Comfort.

Very poor delivery service. They took my order I waited over an hour to get a call back and they said that they weren't going to deliver to me. The food looks great and I wanted to try it, but its not worth the effort. If you want a pleasant delivery experience STAY AWAY!!

Bbq is good for NYC, but if u had BBQ in Memphis, Â K. C. & Texas, don't expect anything close here. Â The lines r just too Long. Â They could easily make 2 or 3 lines, but they want u to wait on 1 line to make the customers think u r waiting for something Â really special. ...

We came here after lunch one day to kill some time, so we did not order any food other than mouchi and zenzai. We also had the jasmine pearl tea. From the images online, I imagined this place to be a very relaxed, cool, and large place where one could read a book, drink some tea, maybe even close one's eyes a bit on the chair. I believe they might have some space like that, maybe the lounge? although it costs like $40 dollars to reserve the lounge I think... When we went in at 2pm it was a bit packed... we sat at the bar because all the tables are taken. Mouchi was good. Green tea ones are def. better than the chocolate ones. Zenzai was a little disappointing. Now the tea... it was good tea, but it is not a drink some tea at your own pace place. The teapot is tiny... which holds maybe 3-4 small cups of tea. The first time they served my boyfriend and I each a cup (small), and took the teapot away.. and we were like thats it??... good thing is that after we were done, they brought it back! so yay, more tea for us. The problem is that maybe it takes a lot of time for the water to boil or for the tea to steam... We would always be waiting and waiting. We had two pots of tea over the course of maybe an hr.. it is a small pot and we had two people. So this was a bit disappointing, as drinking tea should be a relaxed experience, not so much full of anticipation :(.... We were sitting at the bar, we didn't read although we both had books, it was too awkward with the staff standing there and eating their lunch at the same bar, we waited for our tea and left... It was pricy too... I guess it wasn't bad, just didn't fulfill any expectation whatsoever.. Oh no credit card accepted.

I find this place to be extremely overrated. Â  I'm not sure what the big deal is over the fries here. Â They are good, but not exactly mind blowing. Â  And for the price they charge, really nothing spectacular. Â  I think based on the reviews present, one would think they were preparing to taste the finest fries ever created. Â  Â THEY ARE JUST FRIES. Â  Â  Similar to anything you would taste at a decent burger shack. Â  The dipping sauces are nice, but they don't compensate for waiting in line for 10 minutes to get a bag of fries. Â I really believe that Pommes Frites is a case where the herd mentality has set in and everyone seems to be buying into it.

We had a group of 10 (5 couples) and got 6 apps and 6 entrees. It was MORE than enough and the bill came out to about $85 per person with a few bottles of wine and tip included. To start, we got the jonah crab claws, kusshi oysters, short-rib sandwiches (2 orders), and baguette & pretzel bread (2 orders). As for your main courses, be certain to get the mackerel. Scary though it may be with it's face and teeth, it is SOOOOO good with creamy lemon sauce and fried croutons. Even my husband (who is not a fish fan) could look past those little beady hate-you-for-killing-me eyes to get in there for the real thing and snag (more that a few) bites. The veal sweet breads were a favorite on the table. But MY FAVORITE was the spicy pork sausage. And I mean SPICY! It also came with caramelized carrots. I've never tasted deliciousness with a texture quite like it. Warning: If you are going to get the grilled dry aged ribeye (and I do recommend it), make sure you only order it if you have 6 to 10 people in your group. For $125 a plate and the heaping amount of delicious red meat, there's no way we could have eaten any of the other options we ordered AND the ribeye atop. Â  Additionally, our table enjoyed the roasted lamb and loin. Meh. Tastes as good as lamb can. The fish-ball hot pot was by far the most surprising. I could eat that six days out of the week. Deliciousness all around! Â  On a side note, the staff is extremely kind, and helpful. My only advice is that you show up with your entire party to put your name down with the host, but then plan on taking your posse next door for refreshing drinks at Sholbreds AND/OR the 12th Street Ale House (for $3.50 pints!!!) to wait out the 2 hours it will probably take to get your table ready. Regardless of the long wait to experience MomoFuku's, it was well worth it and extremely memorable. I'm only reserving one star because on the extreme wait. Doors open at 5:30, but people start lining-up to get their name on the list around 4:45!!! Also, although trendy as it was, the actual restaurant was VERY small, packed, we could hear the people next to us fighting, and I'm sure our group of 10 was rowdy and annoying to the bar patrons next to our table......I only know that because a prissy girl turned around and gave us the stink-eye when we were playing credit-card roulette for the bill. But hey, Random-Easily-Annoyed Girl, what do you expect for a Saturday night, in a tiny restaurant, where everyone is trying to be heard, and you're sitting next to ten 30-year-olds (without kids) who just found out that they don't have to pay for dinner??? Also, one of our friends was just made a Judge in Washington DC! Ce-La-Bray-EET!!!! Hol-lee-daaa-EEEY!

I've been eyeing on this restaurant for weeks. So I decided to give it a try and since I was working I can only call for take out. First try did not pick up, second try did not pick up. Okay next day, also called and did not pick up. Went over there to get a menu, only to find out that they do not have one either. So the next day I tried calling them and they picked up this time. I guess this place isn't for take out. I ordered Camarones burracho and something else for my manager. The food was so expensive and it did not taste good. There was only a few pieces of shrimp and it was so dry due to the fact that it is over cooked. The rice is also very dried. It did not fill me up either. Skip this place and go somewhere else.
It's okay. Love the bread the most. Fillings were alright, but nothing spectacular.

My boyfriend's really into burgers, as well as How I Met Your Mother (see the episode Best Burger in Manhattan), so we decided to check out the Corner Bistro to see what all the fuss was about. Â We're still wondering. Â We had a cheeseburger and fries. Â The fries were just not good. Â And the burger, though nice & thick, leaves much to be desired. Â It wasn't horrible; it just wasn't great. Â Also, the bun kind of crumbled as I ate it, and I noticed that a few other yelpers mentioned the same problem. Â Overall the burger was definitely over-hyped. Â And I wouldn't order the fries again. Â Cheap beer though!

I was very impressed with the overall quality and creativity of the appetizers (duck shwarma, dandelion greens and brussel sprouts in particular). I will say that the entrees left something to be desired. I had scallops which were sandy and overcooked, and my friends had the "mixed grill" which honestly was the equivalent to something you might get at a mid-level restaurant but priced like a premium steak. Also quite expensive (I know it's Flatiron, but still). Cocktails were just OK, but they have some creative drinks. All and all, great for a few drinks and mezzes, I would be reluctant to go again for a full meal given the price and quality of the main courses. I'd rate it a 3.5 but round up to 4 for excellent and professional service, which is rare.

Things I regret: 1. My perm in 6th and 7th grade 2. Shaving half of my head in 8th grade 3. Being caught on film in Z. Cavaricci's and fingerless lace gloves 4. Not going to Alta sooner What a great find. I went because of all the great yelp reviews. A lovely cozy, long bar with a super friendly bartender. The fireplace in the back is perfect for this week's arctic weather, though if you venture too close, the woody-smokey smell could overwhelm your food. Can I wax poetic about the brussel sprouts? The little green balls that my mother force fed me as a child? The small cabbages that resulted in epic battles of food hiding and dog feeding under the table? The brussel sprouts at Alta may be some of the best things I have ever had. The lamb meatballs too, were unbelievable. So the decor is 5 star and most of the food is five star, but the four is just because (ugh... I'm being super picky) the duck confit was perhaps cooked a bit too fast and the mussels were just not good. But to turn me into a brussel sprouts fan? This place has to be good.

This is my go to place after work (or before work for breakfast). I love this place. They have happy hour after four and it's never too loud or crowded. The staff is always very friendly . It is always nice and clean. It's big enough for a hanging out with a big group of people and casual enough just to sit and have coffee. The food is your typical bar and grill type food,burgers and fries, but they have good specials and the sweet potato fries are delicious. There is also a deli that is part of the bar and grill so you can order to go. Definitely worth trying out if you ever stop by Roosevelt island.

Two 8 Two is exactly what this part of Brooklyn needs and deserves. We don't need another boutique or baby shop or pet shop (no thanks, PetsMart, even though I have a dog) or 'artisinal' whatever shop. We need a burger and beer shop! And we have a stellar one now! The burgers are excellent, all of them that I've tried, and all cooked to perfection (you don't have to specify 'medium', 'medium-rare', etc., and there's a beauty to that). So are the hot dogs. So are the nachos, fries (not so much the Greek fries, mind you) and onion rings. Great beer selection and brilliant cocktails/spirits/mixed drinks. I would suggest sitting and ordering at the bar, though, as the table service can be inconsistent (save the most dedicated and conscientious bus service). Also, no pickles, hello? Plus, if you do the maths, you save a few bucks by ordering the basic burger and adding toppings a la carte instead of splashing out on the 'Pub Burger', which is delicious nevertheless. Finally, yes, decor. It feels a bit too much like a place that's just opened after having ordered all its furniture and decor from a restaurant-supply catalogue. I second the other reviewer's note: where's the character and charm? You get it from the staff behind the bar (and the stellar busperson) and the food itself, but it could use some more local, aesthetic flavor. In all, I'm Two Hundred and 82 time sold on Two 8 Two!
Food a 5...service a 3.5...the food was great! Prices amazing...what a find. Went with Cambodian noodle soup and beef belly noodle soup. Half country duck to go...all for less than $20.

Great food, comfy environment. Â Tiny little place with large portions of delicious, flavorful food. Whether you are a vegetarian (roasted carrots and mushroom and buratta bruschetta!!) or a carnivore (burger or strip steak), you will not be disappointed. We arrived NYC at 11 pm and were thrilled to find a table and a full house at this local eatery.

Couple things: 1.) this place is legitimately overhyped on yelp. 2.) the service is slow 3.) the Benedict Jane which was recommended was not that great. Best part of the dish were the potatoes. 4.) blood Mary was actually pretty good. 5.) this place got two stars because there was an eggshell in my dish, in my first bite, and that just ultimately ruined the remainder of my experience, my friend had a crab shell or crawfish she'll in her first bite so that destroyed hers as well, my cousin like her baked egg dish Â no weird errors there.
