Enjoy.

E for effort... but the end result was not that great. This restaurant seemed to try super hard to elevate itself into something else, but it didn't execute on simple stuff. For example, my vegetable omelet had merely a trace of chives and goat cheese on it. Under a round-shaped scrambled egg product. I struggle to remember the rest, it was so forgettable.

There was a 5 minute wait for a table for two on a Saturday night. Not bad. The staff at this establishment are really nice. We waited for a table at the bar which we didn't mind. In 5 minutes the hostess informed us that a table was ready and thanked us for waiting. It was nice. The decor at this place is extremely cute. I found myself lusting over their vintage table tops. They did a great job at this place. What we ate: We started with their Pork Boudin Balls and Cracklin: They were good. But I missed tasting the pork in them. The fried bits of pork could also use a bit of garlic. The spicy mayo on the other hand were amazing. Jess ordered the shrimp Po'Boy. She spared nothing, the Po'Boy was completely devoured. I still hear of how amazing the bread was. I guess it was good. I unfortunately wasn't offered to taste it. I got the regular buttermilk fried chicken. I wanted chicken with waffles but at sugar freak their chicken and waffles comes with a cutlet. Boring. I was happy with 4 pieces of dark bone in fried chicken resting on my plate. I wouldn't say that its the best fried chicken in NYC but it was pretty good. I'd save the calories for better fried chicken next time though. Okay, it was just okay. Dessert: This is where Sugar Freak shines. And why I'm itching to go back there soon. Very soon. We got the BEIGNETs. It was to die for. They were these night yummy donuts and came with this heavenly sugary dip. It was awesome. We left Sugar Freak with a serious food comma and big smiles on our faces. I'd come back.

In short: over-prized miniature slice of pizza with burnt crust. What a disappointment! I love pizza, so I was very excited to try this place after learning it's what of the best 10 pizzerias in NYC. I was lucky, there was no line when I got there (on a Wednesday evening). Usually 1 slice of pizza is enough for me, but I ordered 2 slices thinking it was going to be the best pizza ever! Good thing I did, the slices are so small I stayed hungry after 2 slices! On one of my slice the crust was burnt to black and it was inedible, on the other one it was completely dry. While the sauce tasted really good, and the fresh basil was a nice touch to it, I found the cheese too salty, and the pizza overall too greasy. For $ 10 (for 2 slices) I was expecting more and better!

Where should I start ? It's definitely one of my favorite restaurant in the city. The food there is beyond any Mediterranean food I have ever tasted, each dish has its own distinguish unique flavor, the portion are pretty big which is a big plus :) The waiters are pleasant Â and polite, the wine selection is remarkable !!! You should definetly try the shrimp kadaif and the fried olives I mean, I would recommend all the dishes cause I've tried them all :) but enough said ! Just go there ! You'll see, your not gonna get disappointed

This place is my Achilles' heel. Every penny spent is worth it. While I have enjoyed their fresh brunch, sunny interior and delightful patio, I much prefer this place for late night dates or special occasions. Get surf and turf. I like to share their amazing filet mignon with a lobster tail, assortment of oysters, followed by chocolate mousse. That said, if you're gonna go for breakfast, go for the steak and eggs. This place buys some of the best proteins and fresh produce you can hope to find! The interior is also very comforting, bright, and clean, a nice change twist on a new england - meets-brooklyn vibe. You can tell the place is staffed by veterans, people who've work manhattan's service industry and bring the same finesse and elegance downtown.

Few would consider ramen to be good hot weather food. Â However, when Totto opened, I felt compelled to schlep (schvitzing all the way) to the outer regions of Midtown to check out. At Totto Ramen, Mr. Muneketa (of Yakitori Totto, Aburiya Kinnosuke, Soba Totto, etc fame) has called upon the services of Chef Hideto Kawahara, who is allegedly a ramen legend in the Fukuoka prefecture of Japan. Here, Kawahara plies his skills in the form of chicken paitain ramen, miso ramen, vegetarian ramen, each with iteratively spicier doppelgangers available for additional cost. If you're lucky enough to score a seat at the bar, you'll be treated to dinner (or lunch) and a show. Before you, a trio of resolute looking cooks churn through service in the open air kitchen. The char siu pork shoulder is slowly braised, rendering the normally tough cut of meat into an unbelievably tender bite. Watch as the bits of pork are blow torched Ã  la minute, giving the exterior of the pork a crispy charred contrast, while the interior remains ethereally moist and delicate. Collagen is a beautiful thing. Rich people pay a lot of money to have it injected into their faces, and at Totto Ramen, chicken collagen is gleaned to form a rich, gelatinous, hearty broth. The velvety texture of the soup was on par with what I consider to be the New York ramen all-stars - Ippudo and Minca. Watch as the cook manning the noodle station plucks noodles from a vat of water with an expert snap of his wrist, flourishing and flicking the noodles to expel excess moisture. The noodles were evocative of an ideal ramen noodle - thoroughly cooked, yet 'ha gotai' or al dente, springy, tender, satisfying. The ramen is completed with the obligatory strip of nori, crunchy scallions, and discretionary toppings such as bean sprouts, mushrooms, boiled eggs. I've always thought that the East Village held the uncontested edge in ramen domination. However, Totto Ramen deserves honorable mention in the hall of ramen fame. Fast service even though it was crowded. My friend and I got seats by the bar almost immediately. I ordered the chicken thigh don and my friend had the pork loin. The lunch set came with standard salad and miso soup, I love the ginger-soya dressing and the miso went well with the meal too. The rice was abit hard but after mixing it up with the yakitori sauce it tasted pretty good. The grilled chicken was tender and juicy I finished all of that but only managed to finish half bowl of the rice. Great value for lunch set@9.50

Bicerin....do it! This was a fantastic type of little coffee. To set the mood: it was a LONG day of walking and loitering and waiting for exploding vagina fireworks. So, I wasn't in the best of moods with the rain and people pushing and generally being New Yorkers in enclosed spaces. So, I wasn't feeling the crowds that engulf Eataly...BUT the place is HUGE! I was well surprised with the amount of space available. It will be crowded, but it's a great concept to eat a bit of nibblies here and wander around with your wine there. Just expensive...you can find a lot of the same items cheaper elsewhere in the city. You're going for the experience. GET THE COFFEE.

I am so happy to have come across this spot for brunch! I had the crab cakes benedict, my boyfriend had the T-bone steak and eggs, and we shared the peach cobbler for dessert. The food was AMAZING and the portions were great. We sat in a communal table indoors, which wasn't bad. However, I wouldn't recommend outdoor seating for couples- though it's a great option for a group.

4 or 5? reason or bias? Bias. *bias switch on* Off the beaten path; you will walk and grumble, yes. BUT, once there I assure you, you'll thank me, cause you never would have imagined such a cozy and cute little place amidst the fugly building surroundings around this part of Woodside. The inside is very small but quaint; brick walls, nice lighting, nice combination/proportions of colors. Me happy. I must thank the incomparable Maria M. for indulging me in this gastrorgasmically experience! My enchiladas de pollo were superb; the mole RIGHT what it should be; spicy yet flavorful enough for me to delight in the chocolate gist.... the guac (Maria's favorite) didn't super impressed me, but it was great nonetheless. Tacos al pastor were delicious, as was *pause of emotion* my ceviche! yum, yum! Mojito and Tecate at hand, check. And last, but certainly not least; the flan. "Oh my friggin lord" -as Maria would say. Coconut flan was sooo delicious that I will forget your pesky distance and bias myself for you. *bias switch off*

I drove past this place literally hundreds of times, and always glanced at it but shrugged it off. Shame on me. Had I known it housed such quality food at such affordable prices, I'd have been a regular here long ago. It looks, feels, and most importantly tastes like a place which should cost way more. $17 steak entree was cooked according to specified doneness, well seasoned. Hand made tagliatelle with a lamb ragu was clearly a fresh pasta, and cooked to perfection with just enough bite and that texture that you just KNOW didn't come from a dried pasta out of a box. And for only 10 bucks? Incredible, considering the sauce was not short on meat at all. It had a very rich taste to it. Also tried one of the $7 flatbread specialty appetizers, with meat (was it prosciutto? Can't remember) and fontina cheese, which was basically a quesadilla with an Italian kick, something I could make in my kitchen and nothing fantastic, but good quality ingredients were obvious and it's kind of the perfect munchie food. The ONLY reason this place gets 4 stars is because the service felt just a tad too slow and unattentive. And an offering of fresh parm for my pasta (never happened) would have taken the dish to amazing level.This is not enough to keep me away. They'll see more of me. Especially for those butternut squash ravioli in the truffle oil for 9 bucks. YES. And check the specials board, they had some solid offerings on it! Dinner for two, without alcohol, and including $10 tip -- $50. Left with some pasta leftovers even, thanks to freely flowing bread and olive oil throughout entire meal. Major win.

Best fries in NYC or really, best fries anywhere. They double fry their homemade, fresh cut fries, so you get the classic crispy exterior and soft, moist interior. What really sets them apart though are the (mostly) mayo based sauces and there are over 20/30 to choose from. Â Good any time of day, especially good after a few drinks. Â In Greenwich, right across from the Stomp theater.

I came here by pure accident, randomly walking in after having a snack across the street at Otafuku. I didn't know what I was getting myself into, but I'm certainly glad I came here for what would be lunch. Since we weren't too hungry, my family shared two bowls: Kamo Nanban Udon and Yasai Soba. Both were very delicious, and both the soba and udon were very fresh and filling. The broth was a little on the salty side, but not totally unbearable. I will however take away a star for that. Service was fast and efficient, and relatively attentive, though we did have to wait a bit before we managed to get the bill. The food adventure in NYC continues. One thing I love about big cities is that the adventure never ends.

Really great find in New York!! I was pleasantly surprised by how good the banh mi is! Â Very different from alot of other Banh mi places i've been too. Â All of the flavors really stand out! Â It's nice and big too and has bars for you to sit at. Â  The only reason why I gave it a 4 was because the guy said they were out of banh mi and that they were getting ready to close at 7. It was only 5 at the time so I got really confused. Â  Stop by and grab yourself one!

It's not a fancy place but you will forget all of that once you taste their food! Their smothered beef ribs are my favorite followed by the catfish. They just started serving beer and wine which is a huge plus! Prices are reasonable and plates are more than enough.

This place does not need another review. But but but...for me I need to document what I liked here lest I ever forget (which is highly unlikely, but hey you never know.) Nelly and I dropped by after the Joshua Radin concert, both slightly high on his insanely wonderful performance. Â  Guacamole: yummy. Grilled corn: Shleukhp. Chicken in mole sauce: sigh how I love you. CUBAN SANDWICH: I want one. Right now. And no I dont want to share, I want to get fat, get your own. Drinks are strong, one and I was good to go:) Definitely coming back. Â ALL THE TIME.
love their dumplings!! Had some shrimp dumpling today with spicy sauce! The price is great and dumpling taste delicious! Definitely going back there and recommending to others!

I LOVE this restaurant. Â It is a great place to meet up with friends for dinner but it is also a great place to just go to the bar and have a glass of wine. Â The staff is fantastic and everything on the menu is tasty.

Food is amazing. From the former management and kitchen staff of Bonita. All of the good things from Bonita carry over, but they've added their own to this place for sure. Their tequila selection is amazing, food is awesome. Service is top notch. Try the Diablito margarita, its so spicy and sweet and like no other margarita I've had in nyc! I'm from southern arizona and I KNOW good mexican food!

Came here on a Friday night after work with 2 people. There was a small line but the line moved fairly quickly. Didn't have to wait more than 30 min tops. Â We ordered the brisket, spare ribs, brontosaurus rib, and the special pork cheeks. For the sides we got the buttermilk broccoli with bacon and sweet potato casserole with maple and pecans. For the free add-ons with the dish, we got all of it (cucumber, celery, red onions, chiles). For the meats: If i had to pick only one favorite, it would have been the brisket. Then the spare ribs, then brontosaurus rib, then the pork cheeks. All the meats were EXTREMELY tender. They all had lots of flavor and some pieces had quite a bit of fat in it. The reason I liked the brisket the most was because i thought it had the most flavor to it. For all the meats, they sprinkle some sea salt which I thought made the meats taste better but at the same time, it was almost overboard on the saltiness. I loved the smokiness they were able to infuse into the spare ribs. Just my own personal preference but I hope they didn't use liquid smoke to get that flavor into it. It was however really flavorful. When I saw the worker bring out my order of the brontosaurus rib. I did not know it would be that huge. Pictures does not do it justice! You could easily share that with one other person and both of you would be full. One issue is the cost for that rib. It almost costs 3x as much as the other meat dishes but you don't really get 3x as much meat, probably 2.5x compared to the others. Hard to say which is a better deal. I feel like the brontosaurus rib lacks flavor when compared to the others. The meat is very tender and they do an excellent job or keeping the juices in. For that size of meat, I was surprised that I could take all the meat off with just my fork. I think the novelty of the size of the rib wears off quickly and you'll some to your senses and order the other things. The pork cheeks were very tender but very strong pork flavor. If you don't like strong pork flavor, I would not recommend this. Another thing about their meats is that there is quite a bit of fat in them. Obviously that makes it more tasty/flavorful but sometimes it was uncomfortable eating Â a chunk of fat in my mouth. For the sides: I thought the buttermilk broccoli was just okay. It really doesn't burst with flavor but it helps cut through the fat, salt, and sauce from the meats. To me the sweet potato casserole tries to mimic southern candid yams. Instead of sugar, they used maple syrup. I'm sure both dishes use quite a bit of butter but the candid yams definitely uses more. For the add-ons: My favorite was the cucumber. My least favorite was the cucumber because it was too pickled. The chiles wasn't bad, it just added spice but for me, it didn't complement the rest of the food. The cucumber was refreshing because of all the salt and sauce from the meats. I am glad that they had something like that. In addition, the cole slaw helped a lot too. I think those two sides helped cut the salt, sauce, and fat from the meats. Service: Service was excellent. They help bring your food to your table. Because the seating is like cafeteria style, you can't reserve your seat in advance unless you were already paying for your food at the cash register. While we were eating, a patron sat down at an empty table and one of the staff members came by and asked where was the rest of his party. He said they were in line ordering but she said that he had to give the seat up because there were other parties ahead of him. It's understandable and fair. As we finished out meal, we wanted to take our bones home for our dog and the brontosaurus rib bone couldn't fit into their standard boxes so I explained the situation to one of the staff members and she went above and beyond. She took the bone, wrapped it in butcher paper, then saran wrapped it!! That's attention to detail and service. Overall we thoroughly enjoyed this place. The ambiance wasn't bad either. Not the most creative way but it works for them. I only wish the prices were lower. It is quite pricey here but we thought it was worth it and will definitely be coming back here again.
Great food and celebrity-watching at this uber-cool spot.
Bash burger should not be missed. Accompanying french fries were soft and yummy. Great service. Amazing wine offerings.

When in New York with my older sister, we always make a pilgrimage to Carmine's. Lines are out the door, and for a good reason. The food is consistently good - the wait staff knowledgable and accommodating, and -- the reason we go -- it feels like a traditional Italian New York experience. We always have Caesar salad, spaghetti and meat balls and chicken parm. It isn't a place for amazing Italian food, but it is great for Italian comfort food.

Came in at off peak hours (around 2pm on day after Thanksgiving) so we were able to get a table with no reservations. As mentioned with the other reviews, it's a bit on the pricier side but it's well worth the quality you're getting.

Came here for brunch after circling around West Village one afternoon in the cold. I can't think of another place that does hole-in-the-wall better. Omelettes (a la Mexicana) were light and fluffy as they should be...improved by a side of chorizo. It was a little drafty sitting by the door when it's 15 degrees outside, but at least my food was piping hot (unfortunately so was my entire plate). Service was friendly albeit not particularly efficient, but my coffee was always refilled and I left more than well-fed.

I don't think I've ever had such a simple pasta (black pepper and pecorino) taste so perfect, complex, and just perfect. Really perfect and delicious. The rest of my table also had pastas, which were all cooked to perfection and had just the right amount to leave you satisfied but not so full you need to take a nap upon leaving. The apps, however, were pretty small and probably shouldn't be split among a group of people. When we called for a last-minute meal, they made it sound like they wouldn't have any tables, but we walked into a half-empty restaurant. I've yet to come for the pizza happy hour from 5-7 during the week, but I bet it would be just as lovely as dinner.

Rotisserie duck review! After having a knockout experience at the noodle bad with their fried chicken dinner, I had to give the rotisserie duck large format meal a go. Sadly, this meal didn't do it for my like the fried chicken. It's a 3.5 star experience, and worth checking out, but nothing life changing. First, to call this a rotisserie duck dinner is kinda a misnomer. They stuff pork sausage under the skin of the duck and roast it whole. The duck is presented whole, table side, and taken back for carving and placed over a bed of rice to absorb all of the juices. So why is it a misnomer? Because when sliced, you have 2/3rds sausage and 1/3 duck under the skin. The flavor of the sausage also permeates the duck throughout, and is the main flavor. The duck is served with thick chewy pancakes, lettuce, rice, and a few sauces and herbs. Flavors are good and you can experiment with different combinations and ratios, which make it fun to play around to get that illusive perfect bite. Sides, we had the potatoes and the broccoli, neither of which were especially good. Not bad, but kinda blah. Overall, with drinks and a few orders of pork buns, which are just as excellent as at the noodle bar, came to $49 a person for 5 people. Pretty reasonable, and good, but not world shifting. It's worth checking out, but I don't think more than once.

I am not sure how useful this review will be since I didn't have a main course the last time I dined here but here is what I do recall: -The places is BYOB, which is great because there is wine shop across the street. -I had the corn clam chowder which was OK, but a bit on the fishy side for my taste -The service was pretty good, and even though the waitress forgot my french fries, she was very apologetic and offered me desert on the house -everyone at my table had a main course and were very satisfied with it (2 whole fishes and a burger) The atmosphere makes you feel like you're in a little French bistro on the edge of the world. Â If you want to get away from the hustle and bustle of Smith street, this is the place to go.

I rarely give 5 stars as I am rigid with my views. But, this place is a total score for me. Both falafel and hummus sandwiches are done perfectly and beyond affordable. I regret that this place is cramped and one can barely move inside when packed, but everything else compensates for it. I went to this Mamoun's location for the first time two days ago. He took my phone without a doubt and did this huge favor for me. Everyone else as his staff were also smiling, despite the crazy line behind me and busy environment. So, customer service is everything to me, and I got to say that I am beyond pleased. Tipped them double the cost of my order. But, very well deserved.
Amazing burger experience here. Â Good steak options and other selections. Â Wine list fantastic. Â Ambiance is upscale but very approachable.

This place Â has a very cute atmosphere and attentive service. The cocktails are good, and the $5 leek tart is a good snack with a drink. But it feels like the owners are pinching pennies ($3 for 2 slices of bread) and if you try to eat dinner here you will leave hungry. After our first meal here when we expressed that we may have ordered too little (5 small plates and a dessert) the owner explained that next time we should order the large dishes since we'd only had small dishes. So we gave it a second chance so we could try some of the three entrees. The pork shoulder is actually a small disk of pulled pork with no flavor. The lentil entree was astonishingly bad: cold brown lentils with three cold green beans and some cold carrot tops laid on top. In this case I was glad the portion was small. Â The roasted cauliflower small plate is also served cold. This Â is around the corner from us, but if I want to spend $70 on dinner for two I'll go somewhere for warm food that doesn't leave us hungry.

I just went here last night for an early dinner for three - it wasn't very busy when we went in so we got a great seat near the back. The restaurant itself is fairly small so I can imagine when it's packed it can be a little tight on space. The decor is really cute and has somewhat of a nautical feel. Everyone on the waitstaff seemed to be wearing nautical striped tops, which also added to the overall ambience We were greeted by a man who seemed to be the owner (maybe Dean?) who was very nice and friendly. Our waitress, although polite and friendly, seemed a bit timid during the whole dinner and had a little difficulty giving us good direction when we were asking for suggestions. They just started serving dinner so maybe that's why she didn't seem so confident in her suggestions. The food overall was good and well cooked. We had the zucchini chips, burger, bloody mary moules frites, and vegetable curry bowl. I enjoyed how thick the hand cut fries were that came with the burger and that they salted liberally. Nothing worse than an under salted french fry. The moules frites were not as amazing as I had hoped but again, well cooked. There was something missing in it I couldn't quite place. A lot of diners around me seemed to be ordering the vegetable curry bowl - it's hearty and filling. I think I would like this place better during the day, their breakfast menu looks great and I can imagine how cute the space looks in the daylight. I'm planning on going back on a weekend to try brunch! See photos of Jack's Wife Freda here: maisondesreveries.com/20â€¦

This is a great place for to grab breakfast or brunch during the weekdays. Short 15 min wait and you can order to go. The smoked salmon scramble was creamy ooey gooey deliciousness, the buttermilk biscuit breakfast sammich is a solid staple as are the blueberry pancakes. You can always call ahead and order if you don't want to wait. Cash only!

3.5. This is a very spacious Colombian restaurant with a patio located in the back of the place. All the tables and chairs in the patio are so close to each other so I was able to hear another customer's conversation clearly. Â I do not like that because that lets me I know for sure that the customers sitting near me were able to hear the conversation that I was having with my friend. I would like some privacy. The waiter was friendly and the service was decent, but not spectacular. I ordered the pork chops (main entree, this one is $16) with yellow rice, black beans, and spinach sauteed with garlic. The pork chops were soft and tasty. It was a little bit burnt on the side but I wasn't able to taste it. The rice and beans were pretty good, but I felt that the yellow rice could have been more authentic. Where is the distinct Latin American taste?! I liked the spinach even though there was not even a hint of garlic. I enjoyed the meal overall, but it's definitely not the best Latin American meal I have had (you would have to go to Hispanic mothers for that). For dessert, I had the tres leches cake. I've had way better tres leches cake elsewhere. Overall, Bogota Latin Bistro is a decent restaurant with decent service and food.
This place has the best service I have ever encountered since Marriott!!! And the food is awesome!!

Enjoyed the food, enjoyed the experience. I enjoyed Mominette with a large group of people to celebrate my friend's birthday. Â We ate in the backyard garden. First of all, the garden is simply beautiful with pergalas illuminated and long wooden tables and benches. Â It really has a very rustic atmosphere in all the right ways. This is definitely a place to take a date. We had to wait just a small while because another party was clearing out. Â We were seated by a waitress that was attentive, but super laid back. Â  As we contemplated the menu, the chef came out and walked us through the pre-fixe that we worked out. Â It wasn't pre-determined like another place we thought about using. He wanted to gage food preferences and allergies at the table. Based on our answers, he was going to cook us a great meal. Â This is great service and that alone would make me want to come back. Â It's not every day the chef comes out to meet your party. I had a ginger margherita as a cocktail which was delicious. We had a red beet salad with goat cheese, asparagus salads, red snapper, beef bourguignon, duck confit, polenta that was to die for. Â I can't remember all the dishes, only that they tasted fanatastic. This is a great place to go for a date, and also a party. I highly recommend it.

What a sad, sad demise this place has seen. When the restaurant section opened in the market a few years ago, it was a delight: fresh food, good service, casual atmosphere. Fast-forward to last week: nearly inedible food, and service that was even worse. Oysters had shell fragments in them; lobster roll tasted like freezer burn; bread was inedible. had to wave down the two indifferent waiters to order more drinks; never received basics like refills on water or bowls for clam shells. a disaster. We'll never, ever go back--which is saying something, since this place is around the corner.
The atmosphere is very cool and laid back. Â The FOOD was AWESOME!!!! The taste, the smell, just so good words can't describe. Its a repeat place for sure :)

I've been coming here since 2007 and over the years it really has deteriorated. The Japchae now is filled with onions instead of REAL ingredients. pretty lazy cooking, pricing for the quality of food you get...it's a major disappointment. The food is tasteless and bland

I love this place and try to celebrate important occasions with my family here. The menu and flavors are always exquisite. The service is impeccable, precise and flawless. I am glad that they have kept their high standards throughout all their years.

I really really wanted to love this place as much as everyone else did but I just didn't. I'm sorry. The blueberry pancakes were....okay. Not worth a two hour wait. Maybe something else is though. Sorry Clinton. We tried.

The bartender was Â very sweet and funny, as Â  was the waitress. Â im helping open a real estate office on atlantic and I have been checking out the area for food spots, I had a great meal for under $15.00 and happy hour -2 for 1- til 7 pm what a treat !! Ill be back for sure!!! The 2 Bijanis Â were great dont tell my boss!!

Japanese Cuisine I've read about this place on midtownlunch.com for a while now and I finally had the chance to try it out over the weekend. My verdict? Â Boy it is good!!! Â I was with my other half, so we ordered the 'Grand Slam' lunch with extra rice. Â What comes with your 'Grand Slam'? Â A little bit of everything. Â You get a chicken cutlet, a pork cutlet, two pork sausages, 1 piece of friend shrimp and an egg over yummy Japanese curry. for just $12.50 (well $14 if you get extra rice). Â It is good enough to share for two people. The meats were cooked to perfection, I might say. Â The meat doesn't taste dry, but very moist and tender. Â The fried shrimp was good too. Â I have to admit, I don't recall ever eating Japanese pork sausage, but after I took one bite of that, I had to save it for the end of my meal. Â It tasted really good!!! Â And of course, the curry! Â Most curry places have carrots and onions, etc. Â But their curry is just plain, which is not a complaint. Â It's nicely flavored and tasted good with all the meats. Â A worthwhile meal! Rice dishes here vary from $5 for a basic small with just curry to about $9.50 for an extra large with one topping (meat, etc.). Â A good value for the city. Â I thought some of the topping choices were interesting, like cheese. Â I haven't had curry topped with cheese before though. Â But if you are daring and have a big stomach, you can go for the Grand Slam with everything. Â But be warned, it is ALOT of food! The restaurant is kinda small, with seating for 8 in tables and about 8 in bar type seating. Â Decorated in Hideki Matsui and Yankees memorabila, the restaurant was created as a tribute to the baseball player. Â Therefore everyone who works there wears a #55 shirt. And remember every 5th, 15th and 25th of the month, you get a free topping coupon!

My heart be still!!! Wings were awwwwwwsome! Although next time we'll order the medium wings cause the hot kicked our a$$e$ but we liked them anyways :-). Their burgers are perfect and juicy and their chipotle mayo adds a kick to those burgers to make them ridiculously SLAAAAAAAAMMMIN!! Def will return and I CAN'T WAIT :-)

I came here for a friend's birthday. Decor was nice and simple. I liked the outdoor patio in the back of the restaurant. Good thing people living in the apartments near the outdoor patio don't hang their clothes outside their windows. I wouldn't want someone's socks or underwear falling on me. I ordered a medium bacon royale with gruyere cheese. But it came out medium well. From first sight, I was disappointed because I thought it was going to be dry. BUT it was still very juicy surprisingly. The brioche burger bun Â had a nice bite. It complemented the patty very well. It's not your normal soft burger bun. I was going to order onion rings but my friends who got there earlier told me they were too greasy when they had it. Service was great from the waiter to the bar tender. One of the female bartenders really knows her whisky. Plus we had a nice conversation with her. She let us sample the difference between two whiskies. That's probably because we were drinking a lot too.

Bistro food is some of the best food. Â The ambiance is one of energy and the satisfaction that comes from good food. Â This is not the kind of French food that anyone could think of as frou-frou; rather, Balthazar's provides hearty, delicious meals that have diners cleaning their plates without regard for the American preoccupation with counting calories. Â  We started with oysters to share among the four of us. Â We selected half a dozen each of the kumamoto and the wellfleet. Â They were fresh, heavenly, and they tasted of the sea! Â A mollusk fantasy at our table! Â For our main courses we selected the steak frites ($34) (medium-rare, with the Bearnaise sauce on the side), moules frites ($26), and the skate wing ($24). Â The French fries were crisp and exactly as they ought to be. Â We finished off the meal with coffee and sorbet. Â A full noon meal, but we left feeling fortified and quite satisfied. The menu is brasserie food done with such quality as to defy expectations. Â Make a reservation ahead, because in the some twenty years that this establishment has been in business, I don't think it's ever been empty. Â The food is delicious and the energy of the crowd is palpable. Â With a delightful fare of food and quick service, Balthazar is just about ideal.

@ Kate S. from Seattle, WA. Wow. I have been going to The Scratcher since the day they opened. You must be a pill. I've never seen a bartender behave in the way you are describing, even when it is merited. Perhaps the problem is your terrible personality and not the wonderful people who work at and own The Scratcher. Please, do us all a favor and never come back.

My favorite pizza in NYC. The staff, chef, and owner are all really cool and friendly. I felt comfortable moving to Mulberry St in part because I knew this was on my block! Awesome salads too. I like sitting at the bar the best to interact with the bartenders. I've had nearly everything on the menu; it is all fantastic but you can't go wrong with the pizza. 6 stars
Great food, great prices and great service Well worth the trip to brooklyn for this place.

Scarpetta is not for those looking for a budget friendly dining experience. However if you are looking for some of the best spaghetti with tomato basil sauce you will ever have in your life, this is the spot. I went to Scarpetta on a whim with a few out of town coworkers a couple months back after showing them around the meatpacking district and taking a stroll down the highline. After working up an appetite and a thirst for some good food and drink, i referred to my yelp app to guide us to some quality eats. Scarpetta looked promising and the reviews seemed to mention a variety of dishes so there looked to be something for everyone. And there was.

This place is an absolute hidden gem! Well...actually not really, because of their HUGE ASS line down the street! Ha! There are tons and tons of halal carts in the city but this one is claimed to be the best. And boy, it was. It is near the theater district, so as we were heading over to a Broadway show, we made a pit stop here. It's cheap, fast, and the food comes right off their grill, still scorching hot when you get it in your hands. Their sauces are also DELISH! I remembered I put way too much spice on mine, but I still scarfed it down. The Halal Guys were also passing out nice eco-friendly tote bags with their logo on it to everyone afterwards. I am so sad they don't have any of this on the west coast!

Austrian cuisine: a mystery wrapped in an enigma. Other than the obvious references to wieners, beer and Josef Fritzl, I am happy to admit that I was blissfully ignorant about Austrian cuisine. And by extension, I had never been to Cafe Katja. But my friend suggested this place after we poked our heads into Schiller's and ran out with our heads in our hands, horrified by the masses of shrieking girls. We were welcomed by an uber-friendly man, who sat us opposite a large mirror and took our drink orders. I started out with a delicious cocktail involving absinthe, gin and some other inspired ingredients I can't recall. By the end of our cocktail we were upgraded to two seats at the bar, and while the place is indeed tiny it was easy to get our food orders going. We ordered the epic sausage sampler, and a side of spaetzle. Red wine to go along with everything. Clearly this is not a "hot July evening" sort of place, unless you enjoy eating ten pounds of meats and sauerkraut in a bikini. It's a rich experience, but not nauseatingly heavy. I am not a sausage aficionado and can't point out the difference between an emmentaler and a bratwurst to save my life. But what I did notice was that the sausages were perfectly cooked. Crispy on the outside, steaming hot and tender on the inside. The sampler was a serious endeavor, and came with little buttery dumplings (delicious) and a bed of sauerkraut. Mustard on the side. The spaetzle helped the meat go down- as did the wine. I think that when reviewing a restaurant the main question should be "did it achieve what it set out to do". That is true of any critique, be it in art or film or music. Sometimes the intention is there but the execution falls short. Other times the intention is unclear, which leaves us with the benefit of the doubt. In the case of Cafe Katja, it succeeds at serving delicious sausages and other assorted Austrian fare in a low-key, friendly environment. I suspect that's exactly what the people involved were aiming for, and they achieved it in spades. The only blemish on an otherwise fantastic experience was that the bar waitress made a boo-boo on our cheque and over-charged the schnitzel out of it. We noticed and she fixed it. Overall a great little find. Dankeschoen, Katja

pretty damn good. Â i don't normally seek out thai food. Â but i would say this place is worth the trip maybe 3-4 times a year. went for lunch, so no wait (whew, i heard the wait was terribad). Â i'll try to remember what we ordered: 1. Â crispy watercress salad. Â yea, this was pretty good. Â sweet & soury. Â i took some home. Â it wasn't so good then - should have known cause it was fried. Â but when it was fresh, it was delicious 2. Â fried softshell crab in green curry with pineapple & pumpkin. Â spicier than we asked for, but it was good. Â although, i wasn't that impressed w/ the softshell crab. Â overall, this was on the bottom of my list of the dishes we ordered. Â  3. Â duck curry with basil (the one w/ bamboo). Â yeah, this was pretty awesome. Â  4. Â chicken soup (not the tom yum one). Â the soup was...i guess the only way i can describe it as dense and flavor-packed. Â a little too much flavor for me, but it was still really good. Â they really packed the soup with chicken and mushrooms. 5. Â the salt & pepper pork thing. Â not really to my taste. Â this was ok, the picture looked a lot tastier. 6. Â coconut rice. Â awesome. Â who doesn't like coconut rice? 7. Â chicken rice. Â mediocre. Â didn't taste like much 8. Â something else...oh yeah. the pad thai. Â yeah, i read somewhere how the little bits of dried shrimp was supposed to make this dish from common to awesome or something. Â i guess if you like dried shrimp it will. Â otherwise, it tasted pretty standard to me. 9. Â some black rice dessert thing with coconut milk. Â this was ok, i don't really like this stuff 10. Â some sticky rice wrapped in some leaves with banana filling. Â not as good as #9. i wish we got soup noodles or even the rice plates. Â those looked really interesting and good. Â but i still really liked my meal. Â and it's really affordable as well (bonus points!), unlike those other crappy thai places around manhattan that overcharge.

Small restaurant. They won't take reservations after 7pm or if you have less than four people. The assorted seafood hot pot was filled with fresh seafood - fresh, live seafood - even the lobster that was cut in half in the center of it was alive and waving its claws. As no one in my party was Korean, it was a little overwhelming but a great experience. My only tip is that you must use the buzzer on your table or you might sit there all night.

Loved this place! I came here during the week and it was kind of busy, but luckily my friend made reservations, so the wait wasn't bad at all. Â We had this amazing view of Manhattan from our table, which just added to the splendor of the whole dining experience. Service there was spot on! We had this great waitress, Stephanie, who recommended us drinks and food. Â I got a coconut mojito and my friend got the lychee, both of which were tasty and strong enough. Â But the food was the diamond of the evening (on top of the view, of course), we ordered the arepas and the chorizo mac and cheese, both of which were bangin' but the chorizo might have been just a bit too heavy. Â The arepas there are a must, though! I recommend them highly to anyone going there. Â For the main course, I got the burger, which was fantastic, it was stuffed with bacon and cheese and dolloped with Guacamole--loved it. Â My friend had the lemon chicken, which was pretty good too, not as heavy as my own plate. We skipped dessert because we were stuffed, but I'm definitely coming back here.
Excellent. Cebiche limeno 4.5 stars. Chicken pio 4.5 stars. Some dish with shrimp, scallops, and a white wine sauce 5 stars.
CASH ONLY. Try the eggs florentine.

2.5/5 stars for me here. What a shame. It really is. To think that Bobby Flay would open a new spot downtown and be on top of his game..you would think...not at all the case though. Seems like he may have fallen into the all to familiar "i'm a celebrity chef and people will come regardless trap" with this one. The only reason this place has 2.5 stars from me is because the food was good. To think he got the hard part right! I will run you through my experience. 8pm reservation. Group of 4 there at 7:45pm. Seated at the table at 8:55pm. No stopping over to ask how we are doing while we wait, if there is anything we can do, etc. Once we sat down, the service was improved. The only hiccup was a missed appetizer, which happens. I am more than willing to look past that. The food was delicious and fairly priced. Our waiter was helpful in his recommendations. We had the pita appetizer to start as well as the octopus. We also had the paella, which was incredible. We had the beef and the pork chop for our entree's. For dessert we had the gelato, the bread pudding, the chocolate hazelnut and the peach cake...all were delicious. I left spending a few hundred bucks and feeling really disappointed. Waiting an hour for a table when you have a reservation is pretty wild. It's even more wild that the manager wouldn't think to make up for the wait. I would have graciously said it is unnecessary but the fact there was no attempt is telling of the type of place this will be. A celebrity chef going commercial in a hip neighborhood. He'll do just fine with the type A crowd that he expects. I would recommend going to Lafayette, down the block or Bar Primi. Â At least Andrew Carmellini we can count on for not selling out and giving us a great neighborhood spot. Leave Bobby Flay to do the midtown and uptown lunch spots. Until next time...

You want weird food? They've got weird food. Crispy Pig's Ears? Check. Goats Neck? Check. Spicy Crawfish? Check. Yeah the place is small. And the portions (except for the crawfish) are smallish This is New York, for God's sake! Even PEOPLE are smaller here. You want big? Go to Texas. The food was good. The service was quick, and beer selection did include a couple IPAs I didn't know. What else do you want? --Drink Club NYC is a roving group of NYC drinkers. A different bar every week!

This is where I had my very first slice of pizza in New York. Â It was good, but not jumping of of my feet good if you know what I mean. Â Don't get me wrong, it's good pie. Â It didn't have the OOOOMPH factor you know what I'm mean?!?! Â Walk a couple of blocks to Carve and now you're talking my language!
Really loved this place, food was great. service good and a nice feel. They are a bit pretentious on reservations but it wasn't too bad.

The food is average and could be considered pricey, but Eataly is worth checking out at around 10:45 for a walk through and then sit immediately at 11 at the Pasta/Pizza restaurant for an early lunch. After a sampling target a second restaurant before the noon rush. Place turns into Times Square around noon and loses most of its appeal. Rundown on the food: -Mozz antipasti - pretty good, but you can do better in Hoboken -Agnolotti -impressive, but not mind blowing - Verduretta Pizza - good, but nothing special - oysters - ordered a dozen...selection was weak and what we were ultimately served seemed average at best. It's more of a unique experience than anything else and if you're local and a Whole Foods junkie, a great alternative.

My son and daughter-in-law recommended this place on a recent visit to NYC. Â We had the lunch special - salad and their three daily pastas. Â On this day they served a wide noodle (forgot the name of this particular pasta) with a fresh tomato and basil sauce, a mushroom ravioli and a rigatoni with veal sauce. Â All were fantastic! Â They have a special wine list with all wines priced at $25, which was perfect for lunch. Â Not sure when I will make it back, but this place is definitely on my go-back list. Â Recommend a reservation, even for lunch on a rainy day.

This place saved the day! I took my boyfriend out for his birthday. We started at 1 or 8 and it was so terrible we left after appetizers. I had read about Bistro Petit and knew it was in the neighborhood so we headed there. The tiny little place had room for us! They do have a bathroom but it was broken (leaking or something) so we used the bodega. It's BYOB with no corking fee. Wonderful. The whole experience was great. The chef was great. The food was great. I can't wait to go back!

My idea of Chinese food is golden fingers and fried rice. So when I came here with friends, I was kind of apprehensive about what I'd eat. Food - Delicious. Ive never liked dumplings of any kind, and didn't think I would like them here. I couldn't get enough! You have to get them if you come here. Our General Tso's and some noodle dish were delicious as well. Everything is served family style. Service - quick, not much else to say. Atmosphere - Much like Chinatown itself: hectic and busy. If you come here with more than 5/6 people, chances are you are not eating together. There are communal tables. If you come with 7 people, and there is a table with 5 seats open, guess what? 5 people from your party are sitting there, and the other two are sitting someone else. Unsure if they take reservations, though. Our party of 4 sat at a table with two other ladies, which worked in our favor. Said ladies taught us how to eat the dumplings, and what was good here. I was very pleased with my experience here, and will definitely be back when I'm in the area. Check it out, if you haven't been.

To be fair, I was completely drunk when I went to Cafeteria one evening around 4am. Surprisingly (or not too surprisingly!), the place was pretty full. Yet my boyfriend and I were seated almost immediately. Just in case you didn't get it the first time: we were trashed. And I spent the entire time slapping my boyfriend in the face to wake him up (on his request, to my defense). Apparently I wasn't doing such a great job, because each time I slapped him he'd complain I wasn't doing it right and ask me to do it again... Being sober as I write, I can't help smiling at how ridiculous the whole situation must have looked to the people sitting next to us... Now the food is diner food... pretty good but not too exceptional. We shared the mussels, which were pretty good, after which I think I had the BLT (or was it the chicken club?). It was also pretty tasty, but then again I think I was too drunk to be able to tell the difference. My boyfriend got a burger, which was huge and a little too rare for his liking. Kudos (and +1 star) for staying open 24/7.

I used to Love Big Wong's food but over the years the food quality has gone down. It used to be locals but now it's almost all tourist there which is good but for locals the service has went down too. The waiters are more rude now and rush you to go. It's just not the same no more =( And they give smaller portions now toO =\ Â price is OK still. Also I don't like the name change. I like the old name Big Wong.

Visited on a Monday night 6 pm and wife and I had place to ourselves. We walked up and down Mulberry Street with no particular Rest. in mind and chose Benito One by size of menu. Huge Huge selections offered-All Italian of course. Place is quaint and music heard was a tape of Judy Garland singing Broadway hits which kind of startled us, but its in diference was okay with us. Huge wine selection offered and very reasonable $7 a glass or $24 bottles offered. Homemade Sangria on menu. Whole Baked little neck clams cooked with very good seasoning and juicy. Fresh Stuffed shells with Ricotta and Spinach saw 8 come out hot and melted fresh mozzarella per order. Veal Parm nice with Al Dente Penna in homemade sauce (chunks of tomato) also very good. Wife raved about 2 meatball side order filled with garlic and fresh ingredients. A must !! The place is nothing to rave about-but good choice to save money and not get stuck at touristy New York places which are plentiful in this area. We saw gluten free on menu but we were unconcerned on that and went with extra gluten homemade fresh. Extremely polite Wait Staff and no wait problems on food, but remember, we were only ones there, until we were leaving, the place got busier. $64 bill +tip for plenty food and soda. Saved Dessert for Ferraro's around corner. Would travel back again-but might be better places to be had. Luck of the draw. 6 page food menu though offers much.

Nyonya was a big disappointment. The decor was nice and the prices were fair. The service was friendly but inattentive. The famous roti canai was a weak effort. A good roti pancake is slightly moist and chewy, this one was dried out and tasteless. The pancake should not crack or shatter when you tear it. Ours did. The accompanying coconut milk curry sauce was okay, though also slightly bland. We also ordered the chicken wings tied with screw pine leaf. They arrived piping hot and crisp fried. So far so good. The problem was that these nicely fried brown wings were hamstrung with plant-based green twine. These babies were strapped down tight--which made it difficult to extract them from their bondage without burning our fingers. That would have been okay if ties added to the taste or texture of the wings but the planty twine didn't serve any obvious purpose. The worst part was that the wings barely had any meat on them, so it was a lot of fiddling for nothing. Â The accompanying sambal dipping sauce was nice, but all in all, it was a lot of work for very little return. The mango shrimp flat-out sucked. It was a warm fruit salad dressed with ketchup and decorated with a few tired shrimp. The shrimp tasted of iodine.

Maybe there's better pizza out there...but then again, maybe there's not. Â If you're a tourist, it's a must-see. Â If you're not...well, you must ignore the tourists. The traditional Margherita pie (and tradition is everything here) is killer and I'm sure people will agree in another 100 years. Â The white pizza, which I just had for the first time, was also incredible and won over the ladies in the group. Â And while I last had it at Lombardi's years Â ago, a roasted pepper pizza and meatball pizza has had me chasing the dragon at brick/coal oven pizza places ever since.
Food was excellent. Had a salad, fish tacos, and maquecas, delicious! Drinks were amazing. This rose/pear drink, yum. Service was wonderful! The manager was a little too suave, but he was great.

My first two kati rolls (potato with egg and chicken) almost made me lost my way home. Maybe that's another reason why you shouldn't eat while walking. They have nice chai for less than $2, too... definitely a more realistic one compare to Starbucks' "so instant" chai. The beef was too tough for me, and I have not tried the spicy cheese and the lamb ones. Just stick with my first love.
Excellent Shwarma and low prices make this a winner. The service could be a little more helpful and friendly, but I'll still be back!

They stuffed 3 of us on a 2 person table on a regular Friday night. The risotto was bland and could have used some more spices. Recommend for a one-time try if you really like risoterria? Yeah. Â Would I visit again? probably not.

What a lovely little place. In a city full of uppity places, this was a great Brooklyn type spot in middle of the village. I felt welcomed. I came here on the recommendation of a chef friend of mine. Rabbit Sausage was absolutely incredible. Portions aren't large so best order a few things and share, tapas style. Pork chop was average, nothing memorable. Bottle of wine was decent, again nothing terrible nothing great. The ambiance and service are sellers for me. Price wasn't too bad either. I'll be back.

Open door is by far my favorite spot in L.I.C. The food is always excellent, I love the meatloaf, and the sliders always seem to hit the spot. All servers and bartenders are kind and friendly, and are all excellent at what they do (Billy and Thomas are great behind the bar, Hayden is a great, knowledgeable waitress. even the chef/owner Nick, is a super nice guy!) I have never had anything less than a delicious meal here, my number one choice, anytime I'm anywhere near by. Keep it up, guys!! You're the best!

I love this place so much! Please don't ever close down due to health inspection reasons Cafe Orlin. I've been here for brunch, lunch, dinner and it's amazing. My boyfriend took me here to celebrate our two year anniversary and it's very intimate inside. The smaller tables have fresh flowers and candles for dinner and the noise level isn't ridiculous at all because it's a relatively small place. (Get the portabella mushroom ravioli). When morning comes it transforms into a perfect little cafe to eat brunch with your friends. There's outdoor seating, but it might be harder to get if you have more than 2 people. PUMPKIN PANCAKES! That is all. It's also open 24hrs on the weekends if you need another round of ravioli or pancakes. ;D

I thought Yelp would bring me somewhere amazing. But sadly NYC food has disappointed me yet again. I'm on a "must pay rent/1 going out meal a week" diet since moving to NYC so there's pressure on my dining out functions! Let's start with the positives. The service was great (my hot/SUPER nice waiter was the highlight --- Tim! The vibe was very homey yet modern and cute! And the free beer from checking into Yelp doesn't hurt either. I got two free beers on accident, so I'm drunk off my light weight ass as this is being typed...but I digress. Okay, lets get to the good stuff: the food. I got a spicy tuna, California, and pork belly buns. This could be all NYC in general, but on the West Coast, spicy tunas (almost always) automatically come with cucumber and avocado. Sadly this is just a literally spicy tuna. My non real crab California was just a piece of literal imitation crab and avocado. I mean ya couldn't even mince it to pretend? Throw me a cucumber for texture? Boo. My bill plus tip was around 30, so I'm just saying....could have done more. Although the sushi was fresh! The pork belly was cooked beautifully, pressure cooker amazingness. But with just a piece of lettuce and more mayo sauce on it...it was too much fat on fat. A nice pickled, citrus intensive slaw would done it wonders. Less is more, me thinks. But thanks to the free beers....I'll let this slide Zutto, don't think I'll be coming back though.
Great selection on menu, clean and very helpful wait staff. Grace is excellent and very knowledgeable. Salmon is Devine but the shredded Brussels sprouts are out of this world. Highly Recommended

This place is amazing!!! Customer service was amazing. Seated in 10 minutes took our order quickly, brought our drinks quick (&this was a packed Saturday night) the food was WAY better than I expected
Yummy traditional Cuban food with consistent flavor, great service and prices! I'm a fan and so is my 4year old

A very popular place for brunch, indeed... We made a reservation for 10am on a Sunday and when we got there, there was a line of people waiting outside of Jane. I don't know how long the average wait time is if you don't make a reservation. I ordered Jane Benedict (the poached eggs were delicious, but I didn't really like the crawfish cakes because they were bland). My husband had the salmon scrambled and a friend ordered the vanilla bean french toast. I recommended all three, especially the french toast. The portions were huge, so they were worth the price. :) Even though the place was crowded the entire time that we were there, I didn't have a hard time having conversations with the people at my table. Our waitress was kind and we were notified politely when they wanted us to leave to let other people dine there. Will go here again... :)

I love this place. If you want good food and good drinks this is the place to go. They have great tapas so you can share with your friends. They are known for their mojitos. If you sit by the bar the bartender is nice enough to ask how strong you want your mojitos. They have great customer service. It might be a little loud if you want a quiet setting. Theres usually a wait time so maybe call earlier to see how long you have to wait before going there.

D-E-licious!! I have either been eating subpar pizza my whole life or this literally is the best pizza I have ever had, and I think its a little of both. This place is amazing!! I came here on a Sunday afternoon with two friends and waited less than 20 minutes to be seated. While in line we quickly became friends with two New Yorkers that were such a hoot! The conversations and their sense of humor made us forget we were waiting in line for the most delicious meal! Gosh I love NY! Once we were seated the owner (I think) came over to greet us and make sure we were comfortable. Our waiter promptly took our orders and made awesome suggestions. We ordered a small size Bufala Mozeralla and the Mozzarella, Prosciutto, Arugla, and garlic pizza (No. 4 special on the menu). Wow! So amazingly good!! I put on 5 pounds just thinking about it. Julianna's is a hallmark restaurant of Brooklyn and if you are in the area and miss out then good luck finding better pizza because it doesn't get better than this folks! Historical aside: its well known that Grimaldi's is the original best pizza in Brooklyn which is right next door to this place but the name was bought out when the original Grimaldi's closed down. So Julianna's, is actually named after the mother of Patsy Grimaldi's the original founder and Julianna's is in the Grimaldi's original location. I only learned this waiting in line behind some Brooklyn residents...but fun facts nonetheless.

Fun date spot. We sat at the bar. Waiter was really nice and calamari was great. Lots of good pastas to choose from. It's a trendy spot, very soho. Other Italian places in the city are better but if you're looking for this area very reasonable and good!

It's a special thing when you get perfectly cooked (and not in fried form) calamari. And that's exactly how my evening started off at Basso56. Their grilled calamari appetizer with eggplant puree and arugula was so light and delicate--the squid barely cooked through so it was awesomely tender. After setting the bar high with the appetizer, I ordered the homemade tagliatelle with shrimp, asparagus tips and sort of a creamy pea sauce. Unfortunately, I found the pasta dish to fall short of the measuring stick the appetizer had set. There was no depth of flavors, it was all very earthy--it just needed something to set it off. Overall, nice restaurant and I'm glad I found it, but not entirely sure I'd come back with all the other Italian restaurants to try in Manhattan!

Love. Maybe I'm just starved for good brunch places over in the 'burbs (NJ), but Petite Abeille embodies everything I love about brunch. 1. Delicious food. Waffle with mango, berries, and REAL strawberry sauce. Smoked salmon sandwich with egg salad and DILL! Lovely extra touch to help my love affair with dill. And fresh fruit. 2. Cozy decor: natural lighting, antique suitcases and bare bulbs. Transports me out of the crazy busy city and into a tranquil space (except it's still super crowded). 3. Friendly service (though a little slow at times). Cons: crowded and a tad pricey, but hey - this is NYC.
love their dark smoky broth! Â different from the usual shoyu or shio broth i've had at other joints but just as tasty. Â nice and cozy with friendly service.
Ordered their Tunisian eggs and corn pancakes... Delicious and fresh. I also had the best cappuccino

Dumplings were ok... Â didn't like the service... they took too long, and was not very attentive. Now back to the food... dishes were well standard, but I was trying to see how their rice cakes were... and i found out... Â Filled with nasty brown sauce, and the rice cakes were too mushy, no bite. Â Yack!!! Result - No GO!

*Really deserves 3.5, not 3 stars :) Pros: Cozy and cute decor, fresh ingredients, innovative twists on traditional breakfast, quick & friendly service. Cons: Limited weekday breakfast menu. I went to Penelope on a Friday (SNOW DAY!) morning with two others. Â We waited for about 25 minutes, and then were seated and served. Â  The juices are fresh and delicious, as a fan of grapefruit, I really regretted only getting a small grapefruit juice, since the large is about 2.5 times bigger. Â  The meals are healthy or decadent, and the menu has a good combination of both. Â  I enjoyed my abuelito's egg sandwich- in which I substituted spinach for the ham. Â It had a great tangy balsamic sauce and perfectly poached eggs. Â The creaminess of the egg blended very well with the toasted bread and balsamic. Â  My dining partner had the pumpkin waffle which was amazing. Â The pumpkin flavor is subtly mixed in and the cranberries add a perfect tang. Â  If you come here on a weekday, realize that you might have less of a wait, but are not going to be able to enjoy the nutella french toast that Yelper's have been raving about! Â However, I would definitely recommend the charm, taste, and variation of Penelope to anyone in Manhattan looking for a great breakfast.

On the short list for favorite NYC resto. It's phenomenal. It's not fancy, but you need to make a reservation well in advance (leave a message on their voicemail with preferred date/time and they'll call you back). Like other reviewers mentioned, it's a REALLY tight, cramped space, but it's soo worth it. Everything was delicious -- get the chili pork dumplings, pickled ginger scallops, braised pork buns, green chili shrimp, and any of the desserts.

Minetta Tavern seeks to envelop you in a time warp from the moment you step through the red curtains just beyond the front door. Â It's dark - there are no windows and the place is furnished with dark wood everywhere - it's loud - the place is incredibly popular and designed to feel crowded but not cramped - and it's decadent - as exhibited by the extensively meaty menu and huge bar at the entrance. Â Minetta is the kind of place you might expect to see Don Draper. Â It's definitely playing off of that sort of vibe. This extends to the food, which is of course the most important part of a visit for me. Â (Minetta seems rather scene-y, so this might be secondary for some patrons.) Â What's more honest and old school than a burger? Â Minetta serves two. Â You've heard about the black label and yes, it is great. Â I'll be the contrarian voice, though and say that I might not order it again. Â As amazing as it was, $26 for a burger is still $26 and the jr. varsity burger is not bad either. Â Next time, I'll try the steak. Other miscellaneous criteria all acquit Minetta well. Â Service was attentive, polite, and appropriately gregarious. Â The drinks were good and there were a nice variety of options. Â The value of a meal at Minetta is overall quite good, with the possible exception of the burger (blasphemous, I know). Definitely come to Minetta, definitely get the black label burger, and definitely enjoy the excitement of the scene. Â I'd also definitely come back, if you can deal with the hassle of going to one of the most popular places around right now. Â However, a little bit of artifice that I can't shake keeps it from becoming a top drawer location for me.

The best deal in FiDi. It will take some navigation to get here given all the construction down town. Â once found, this is a pretty good deal compare to other restaurants in the area. Â  Â expect nothing less than any other shake shack out there. Â  the line moves. Â make sure to get there around noon. Â anytime after that, the line builds up!

biggest mistake I ever made upon stopping by here with a friend: bringing with me an ikea bag. I was waiting for my friend to finish ordering and the smell of snootiness in the air was inevitable. The staring did not stop either. However, if you do want to indulge in $3 mararons and imagine yourself in Paris as you chew into these delectable treats, go for it!

Date Visited: 10/2/09 Time of Day: Dinner I was in NY visiting friends and they suggested we go to this place for dinner. Â What a great choice! Â We sat in the garden which was absolutely beautiful. Â It was such a warm and cozy experience. Â The lighting makes you feel like you are at a fancy European backyard soiree. Â  As for the food, I was equally impressed. Â I had the Lasagna al Pesto. Â If you like pesto (yes please) and cheese (most certainly) then this is the menu selection for you. Â The flavors come together in the most delicious way. Â While at first sight the bowl looked small, once I started to dig in, I realized that I should have shared with a friend. Â Nevertheless I did my best to eat the entire thing. Â My friends had the pizza which looked equally inviting. My stuffed friends and I decided to split two desserts: the tiramisu and the pumpkin cognac cheesecake. Â One word: YUM!!! Maybe it was due to the two bottles of wine we shared over the course of our meal (or the fact that the desserts were delicious) but after we ate dessert, we were left with mouthgasms. Â  I would definitely come back here and recommend it to others. Â This is a great place to catch up with friends and I imagine the ambiance makes it a great date locale.

LoMein here rocks! Â Right texture, made fresh. Â  Dumplings are tasty, not drowning with salt or msg. Excellent value for a hole in the wall. Â Place full of all types of people incl Asiana .. always a good sign.

Food: Combo with rice, lots of white sauce and a moderate amount of hot sauce, same like everywhere else, right? NO! People always slam it cause the line is sooo long and there are shorter lines. True. But the fact that they keep selling means that the meat is ALWAYS being prepared and cooked fresh. Meat does not sit there for 2 hours before a hapless street creature comes knocking. I started doing a new thing by taking it home to eat and mixing some freshly diced cucumbers, onions, and scallions in. This kinda masks the greasiness of the food. Drink: Prepare to drink alot of fluids afterward. Has to have alot of MSG in that white sauce or else it would not be any good. Service: Long lines but fast moving because of the quick turn around time. These guys are pros, take your money and hand you food in a fluid assembly line fashion. Crowd: Big crowd of locals, out of towners, drunks, sober people. Bums too, lol, they stand there asking for money since its cash only. Be prepare to feel like a caged animal as tour buses loop around to have tourists point and take pictures of you with an awe struck face.

one phrase. i can't believe i ate rabbit and actually enjoyed it. this place is awesome for combing fresh ingredients and deceiving your taste buds. too bad it's a bit out of the way. the place is busy everyday it seemed and it was friendly. all the waiters/waitresses wear white t-shirts!
I haven't been here in years until yesterday evening. Two words- Italian mimosa and Mac and cheese !

Buster's is now open for dinner so...why are you reading this...? GO! This evening's sumptuous repast consisted of broiled snapper over quinoa with veggies. It was, as Buster's food always is, out of this world. There was a key lime pie for dessert that even I (who won't touch a dessert that doesn't start with "choco...") was knocked out by--killer graham cracker crust! There are too many Starbucks, Subways, and (Christ!) even a Domino's in this 'hood. Support local, homegrown, and GREAT spots like Buster's.

They make them while you wait so they're always piping hot and fresh. Â This place was a tiny hole in the wall that my mom and I tried when she came to NY to visit me. Â Great super cheap dumplings, but perhaps not the best I've ever had. Â It's a little out of the way for me, and not quite amazing enough to make the trek all the way down there on a regular basis, but I'll always stop in if I'm in the neighborhood.

Went here for a birthday dinner with 5 people tonight and loved it. All of the staff were friendly and happy. The drink at the bar was great - can't remember what it was called but it had St. Germain and Prosecco. Starters of oysters were okay; I like my mignonette to be traditional with red vinegar, not a big deal, just a preference thing. Butter with the bread was AMAZING, like a whipped herby dream. I had the scallops for my entree and they were great. Grits were a yummy side. Dessert was the candybar cake, which was actually on 3 lollipops, which was fun and unusual and tasty. Finished it with a latte and a smile. Would definitely come back. Thanks to Cookshop.

It is both so wonderful and so dangerous that this place is so close to my apartment. It is truly the best Italian food you can get so cheaply probably anywhere in the area. The food is authentic and impossibly fresh. The tagliere di formaggi comprises a board of cheeses (some homemade) hugging a tiny crock of truffle honey. Divine. I could have just eaten this, but I wanted to try more, so we also ordered arancini and frittatini di pasta. The arancini are incredibly light, considering it's a fried ball of risotto. The frittatini di pasta is a dream - lightly crisped pasta studded with pancetta (or maybe it was speck?). In any event, they are both fabulous. We could have stopped after appetizers, but why? My friend ordered the butternut squash pasta special - tender fettucini swathed in a creamy butternut squash puree. Her boyfriend had the meatball dish, which tasted, in my opinion, the way every lasagna should taste: scalded cheese over a piping hot dish of tiny meatballs, hearty tomato sauce, perfectly cooked pasta, all baked together in a perfect dish that, despite scalding your mouth when you can't wait for it to cool down, is heavenly. I had the pasta alla matriciana: pancetta, tomato sauce, onions, and pecorino cheese - and although it's a simple mix of ingredients, the sum of its parts was more flavorful and interesting than I had expected. We also got a drink each. Split three ways (with tip), the total was $44 each. Small, cramped space; service is a little curt; but the food and the price are pretty unbelievable!

I always get the chicken and lamb combo. You just can't go wrong with it. Ask for extra white sauce. Don't be ashamed, you won't regret it. $6 for your great meal, you can't ask more than that. Last time I had to wait around 40 minutes to get my food in December cold, but it was totally worth it
overall: teeeny tiny portions appetizers: best part, though still small pastas: small and unimpressive
I love their crab soup!! It's the best I've ever had!! Â I would definitely eat here again if I happen to be in New York.

grateful for another kid friendly find in the city.... and it's yummy authentic japanese food! Â  The noodles are freshly made and delicious. Â Our table got a combination of both soba and udon and everyone was pleased. Â  Crowded, but we didn't wait long. (arrived at 3pm on saturday) It's loud for kid noises and casual enough for kid messes (we did leave a nice tip, though b/c of our little ones' mess). FYI Â the high chairs they use are the kind that attach to the table top. Â It was our first time using one like that. Â We liked it, as it really buckled our son close to the table and made it easier for him to eat his food and engage with the table.
I love Bianca! We went this weekend for the 4th time and it's always great. My favorite dishes are the Salmon and the Lasagna. Everything is delicious and well priced. The service is always friendly.

I took my husband there a couple of weeks ago for his birthday. I e-mailed the restaurant to make a reservation for the 5 course tasting menu and to find out if they can accommodate all of my food allergies. The chef came through for me big time. The food was incredible!!!!! Roasted carrots with a pistachio pesto, risotto with sea urchin and lobster, roasted cauliflower, red cabbage and hen of the wood mushrooms served with a slightly spicy scallion sauce., were just some of the dishes. Course after course the meal just kept getting better and better! I look forward to going back!!!!!! The only reason I am not giving it 5 stars is because of the wine selection. The wines are organic and bio-dynamic, but these are funky and odd tasting. We were able to taste a few and i chose the least weird. The wines are expensive for what they are, ranging in price from $14-$19 a glass. If they were really good the price would not have been an issue.

I really, really wanted to like this place. The reviews are so great and I love the "in the know" aspect of the hidden door. But at the end of the day the food was under seasoned and underwhelming. We shared several apps, sides, mains and a dessert. Not one of them was good. They were just ok. Sorely lacking in salt and overall flavor. Again, too many good options in NYC to waste calories on this crap. I was a nice day and I heard that they had a lovely garden. Wow - that was an over promise. It's actually tiny with a few uncomfortable looking metal tables & chairs. The cocktails were nice. I might come back to sit at the bar and have one. But the bar scene was kind of d-baggy. So probably not.

this is the premiere thai food to eat in that area.... i also recommend trying to eat in the outdoor area that they have in the back, its already August so try and get out there before its too late. prices are good, food is terrific. if you go with a party of 6 or more, and someone is still waiting long for their food be sure to ask for them to check on it in the kitchen... as with all thai restaurants it gets busy and lots of orders coming/going... eat here.

This is my take on the whole dining experience which you can feel free to take with a grain of salt because although I have had my fair share of ramen, I am by no means an expert. The ramen which this place is known for has great broth, quality ingredients, but only so-so noodles IMO....I've had better. Overall, I have nothing against the ramen and I think it's very tasty, but I differ slightly from some of the more gushing reviews with regard to this category on the menu. As far as atmosphere, I was impressed by the space. Service was also very friendly and I liked the enthusiasm of the cooks. My visit here was when this place first opened and it definitely felt like a "scene" with a pretty lengthy wait. All in all, a pretty good dining experience and if you are a ramen lover I would definitely recommend giving this place a try to at the very least compare it with some of the other reputable ramen places in the city. Over and out.

Nothing special about the place itself, but the best banh mi in my opinion. Far and away better than, for example, Hanco's or Nicky's. For frame of reference, I also like Banh Mi So 1 (ground pork/chilis/no mayo), but not nearly as much as Ba Xuyen. This place has the best bread, which I think is a mix of wheat and rice flour. Very light and crispy.
it has a very pleasant patio. not an extensive by-the-glass offering.

I LOVE Miriam! The workers in here are really nice - although sometimes slow, but it's usually cause they're busy. The brunch food here is SO delicious. I bring visitors here all the time and even though it's not fancy or unique brunch food, we always leave satisfied. I'm addicted to the labneh cheese they make. Pretty much everything on the brunch menu tastes great. I always get the Israeli Breakfast or the Potato Pancakes dish. Definitely try this place out!

OMG! We were not through dinner and Â we're almost pushed out by a mob on a birthday party. Our table was crushed. Spent $700+ on a not so good dinner with bad service. This is a bar NOT A RESTAURANT. No apologies from any manager. Never seen anything like this happening on a reputable restaurant. The manager is a complete moron!

We had friends from Spain visiting NY and my husband and I have heard about Tavola through a dear friend. We thought it could be a true New Yorker experience to take our friends from overseas to this restaurant, especially with the history that it holds. When you walk in, you have the feeling of an old school grosseria converted into a restaurant. You can tell that every single detail has been thought and it takes you back to at least 50 years in time. A true New York, Italian experience. The food is amazing, the brick oven pizza especially is one of my favorites, one of the best I've had in NYC so far...you can eat as much as you want and you won't feel heavy at all. As we walked in, the staff, very friendly and the owner Nick, were there to greet us, we felt like we were at home. I started of with a Presecco...delicious. One of the specials that night was lobster ravioli, all hand made with a light cream sauce....we were definitely lucky. The menu fits all palates and suits even vegetarians. Â They offered us gluten free pasta, since my husband can't eat gluten and that was a great choice. The service overall is great. They let you enjoy and savoir your food yet, they are very attentive if you need anything. The prices are absolutely reasonable and the atmosphere is fun and inviting.
