I LOVED LOVED LOVED the Tavola experience and now I don't have to have the excuse of having friends from overseas....we are definitely going to visit more frequently. Amazing experience!! Thank you everyone at Tavola!

This is a quaint little place in the Murray Hill-ish area. It was a nice surprise, with Parisian decor and little Eiffel Towers decorating the space. The quite strange thing, was that my friend and I were about the youngest people there...strange indeed. Let's move on to the food... escargot - deliciously pesto and buttery, and large! worth it, not over cooked in the least mussels espagnole - (with chorizo and tomato confit) delicious mussel pot served with frites, perfectly sized mussels and just the right amount of frites steak tartare - quite the portion size in the best way, the meat was fresh and the flavors were great...can taste the garlic, but not overwhelming, also served with frites creme brulee - the sugar crack topping could've been a little "crispier". it was good though. i only say this because i didn't hear the "crack" when my spoon broke through the sugar layer, great use of vanilla bean TLDR - great french restaurant with decent prices and good food.

I was at La SirÃ¨ne last night with two french friends for a birthday dinner and it was wonderful! As a lifelong francophile who has lived and visited France, I thoroughly loved this restaurant experience, which truly reminded me of being in France. There are plenty of good french restaurants here in New York but rarely do you find a cozy place like this where you can spend 3 hours at the dinner table just like in France. Didier and the staff were wonderful. Didier even taught my friend how to "sabrer" (open) a bottle of champagne with a spoon. The Moules dijonnaises, Tournedos Rossini and the Fondant au Chocolat are must haves. I will definetly be back soon.
Update on my favorite spot: They still rock! Â I sat in the outdoor area for the first time yesterday, and loved it. Â Awesome burger and great service. Â A+!

We stopped by Vitae last night (a Tuesday) for drinks. Unsure of what to expect at a resto that seems to draw the younger, hipper side of Midtown after-hours, we were pleasantly surprised by the cocktails: an excellently executed pisco sour, followed by Vitae's rift on the Manhattan. Most cocktails are made with house-culled (and often house-rendered) ingredients. A bit pricey (abt $14 each), but nothing out-of-ordinary for this area. The X wooden, stand-up bar tables at front allowed for good people-watching through the windows and of those who enter. Never got to sit in the bar chairs (all full!), but wish we could have - loved the design of the place. It was busy - reservations needed, even on a Tuesday. Service was professional, but friendly. Well-conceived wine list, thanks to GM / somm Emily, with a traditional range of bottles.

I would of given the place 5 stars if it wasn't for the very rude and obnoxious hostess who would not stop staring at our table. She honestly stands there and looks so bitter and jaded it brings the place down. Â  Yesterday was my second time there and aside from her the place is awesome the food is amazing and the Wild Berry Sangria is to die for. Â But dear Hostess, you really need to crack a smile every once in a while ..

I really wanted to enjoy this place as I've been hearding awesome reviews.... Unfortuantely it didn't live up to all the hype. Â Don't get me wrong, the bartenders know what they are doing, but the space is way too crowded. Â Also, the bouncer asked if we had any friends coming (we answered "no") and basically told us that we might be the last people let into the bar, so it's good we wouldn't be meeting anyone else. Â I was a little releived when I walked into the bar because it was already pretty crowded, with just enough bar space to order a drink... After I came back from the restroom, the place was MUCH more crowded and there was barely any room to move. Â I was just mad the bouncer would lie to us like that... we downed our drinks, and moved on. Maybe i'll come back for dinner one day?

I had such a good time at ToJ this past weekend. My friend and I shared a bottle of Riesling, fried calamari, a goat cheese fritter salad, and and a steak dish with potatoes au gratin. We finished it off with 2 glasses of rose, and a bananas foster. We had a little private room/table in the back that was so cozy. Our server was friendly telling us about Ireland. My water was refilled often, but was not intruding. I was so happy with my experience, I will definitely be back. Highly recommended.

Came here on the recommendation of the Concierge of the Waldorf. Fabulous pick! Excellent for pre-show dinner. Small intimate dining room/very cozy. Exceptionally friendly staff overcome the challenges of right quarters. The food is outstanding. All fresh farmed sourced. We had the meatloaf (loved it), Salmon (delicious) with sides of fingerling potatoes and leeks. Leeks were just ok but fine. Be sure to order the fresh hot bread! Thanks for a great, memorable and enjoyable dining experience.

ABC Kitchen is an American restaurant in NYC that sports a modern, fresh, and inventive menu. Â With so many great restaurants in NYC, ABC Kitchen stood out for me as a perfect combination of an outstanding menu coupled with a great atmosphere. Â It also helps that it's one of Jean George's restaurant. My Overall Rating - 5 Stars (Atmosphere, Service, Food, Return) Atmosphere - What I love about NYC is that most places don't have much of a restaurant "front" - unless you're in Times Square. Â ABC Kitchen essentially has a pair of white doors as an entry, and if you didn't know that you'll miss it. Â Once you open the door you enter a beautiful restaurant. Â Up front is a bar and waiting area. Â There is wood everywhere - white tables & chairs. Â It has an elegant, rustic charm. Â You know if this much attention is placed on the interior, the menu will match it. Â 1 Star. Service - Superb. Â We seemed to have multiple servers, and our main server was very friendly and helped with menu recommendations. Â Also, we were not rushed, even though they were getting busy. Â They didn't press us to just get our orders in, instead they wanted to make sure were getting what we wanted. Â They even split their famous carrot/cucumber salad for us, cleared the table after each course, etc. Â Fine dining with even better service. Â 1 Star. Food - The menu is so fresh and unique. Â The carrot & cucumber salad is the BEST salad I'd ever eaten. Â The carrot is marinated and cooked, and has the texture of a protein in a salad - tender and hearty even. Â Also amazing was their crab toast. Â The crab tasted so fresh, but the star was the toast, which had held the crab for the initial crunch bite, and then softened as you enjoyed your bite. Â My main course was a ravioli in a pork ragu. Â The ravioli (single) was amazing because inside it was an egg! Â Breaking into the ravioli was like breaking into a sunny side up egg. Â I've never seen or eating pasta with this technique. Â Desert was the caramel ice cream sundae, which was served over chocolate & caramel popcorn. Â I was so full, but I still devoured the dessert. Â One last note, their fresh cocktails (nonalcoholic) are as good as the food. Â I had a cucumber line soda that was so fresh & delicious I would buy a case if they bottled it. Â From start to finish the meal was flawless. Â 2 Stars. Will I Return? - Yes. Â ABC Kitchen not only has a seasonal menu, but it's a menu where you want to order everything. Â My next trip to NYC will no doubt include a trip back. Â I can't wait to see what's next on the menu. Â 1 Star. My Yelp Rating Scale (Sum of all parts): 1 Star - Atmosphere - Is it a cool dive? Â Perhaps an upscale place? Â No matter the type, atmosphere plays a big part and I'll give a star if I like it or thinks it has great charm. 1 Star - Service - You can have a great meal with bad service. Â But that's also what can make a five star joint drop to four. Â It's important to the dining experience that service is great and on point. 2 Stars - Food - I'll award up to two stars for the food, since this is the main reason we dine out. Â Sometimes the extra star is given for value, but it's really all about the food. 1 Star - Will I come back? - If I know for a fact I'll return, I'll give this a star. A place has to make an impression for me to return. Each Category can be given up to 1 star except food (2 stars) because I consider all these categories important to the overall dining experience. Â I will sum them up to provide my final Yelp score.

Definitely one of the best food trucks that I have had. Â The main thing about food trucks is the price point, and then you are left thinking what kind of quality of food you could be getting for the price. Â  This is not your typical Chicken/Gyro Combo and rice truck/stand. Â For $6 I got the Combo platter. Â The chicken is not butchered like other street meat carts. The pieces of chicken were actually identifiable as chicken and not just scrap meat. You could taste the quality in the marinade as well. Next the judgement on the yogurt/cucumber sauce. Â This is LEGIT sauce. Â You can taste the freshness and quality of ingredients that went into making this sauce. Â It's all about the tartness and the consistency that has me giving this place two thumbs up. Â As with any sauce, it should not overpower or mask the flavor of the food, but provide and complimentary flavor enhancing profile to the main star of the show. Â No complaints on the rice either. Â This place is a must go.

Friendly owners. Awesome fresh unpretentious italian food. The closeness of the tables did not bother me, which it usually does, because everyone was into enjoying their experiences. This place is the real deal as far as wholesome iexperiences. Btw, I didn't see the tiramisu stay on anyone's plate for more than two minutes.

Perhaps the best Italian food and service anywhere?! From the moment we entered we were greeted to a packed house but personal cheerful service from the host stand that made the short line not matter. We had reservations and this place was jammed. Lovely atmosphere with incredible food from beginning to end. Modified menu that kids loved. Lobster carbonara and burrito prosciutto appetizer were delish. Desserts OMG meringue cake better than my wedding cake and a chocolate ice cream that was yyummmmmm. Fantastic all around!

DEAR GOD I LOVE THIS PLACE. After 5 years of living a town over, I finally deemed it a priority to try Salt & Fat, suggesting to my husband that we go here for my birthday. It is centrally located off the 7 train, with a clean but unassuming store front. As we were brought to our table, we were given little baggies of free popcorn (i believe they were flavored with bacon fat. mmmm), which kicked off things right. I was moderately hungry, and my husband and I ordered the following: Fuji Apple Salad (perfect appetizer) Yellowtail Tartare(heaven) Oxtail with purred onions (yum) Korean Pork Wraps (wish they were bigger, but very yummy) Duck with Lychees (a little pricey at $23, but the portion of duck was generous and not covered in fat, so well worth it) Our bill (including drinks, but no dessert - was too stuffed) came out to $80 w/o tip, so it was a little pricey for the tapas-sized portions, but the quality of the food made this worth the expense. Can't wait to come back in the future to try everything I missed, and especially to experience new items they put on their menu! Definitely a gem of Sunnyside!

Was going to give it a 1, but I think the food is decent if you can make it that far into the meal. Â  I've been going to blue ribbon sushi in brooklyn regularly since they opened and was very very sad when they closed up shop. I'd been to the brasserie a few times but not recently, so we decided to try it (you can order sushi items from brasserie's menu now). Â A few other posts have mentioned the service and it was really terrible (hence the 2 stars). Â  Â  After we were seated, we waited and waited and waited. We were served water but nothing else--no bread, etc. The table next to us placed their order and received their appetizers. Â We were in a corner and kept trying to get someone's attention (there were a lot of servers) but we couldn't get anyone to notice us. Â After about 25-30 minutes, we told the host we were leaving. We went down the block to al di la and were seated and munching on their fantastic bread and butter in less than 5 minutes. Â With such great restaurants in the neighborhood, I'm not sure how this place stays in business with such terrible service.

Order the Black Label Burger. It was one of the best burgers that I've had in my entire life. I usually prefer cheeseburgers, but this burger did not need cheese or any other toppings. It was juicy and very very very tasty! I ordered my burger medium well and it was a perfect pink. My boyfriend and I arrived at 5:30, when the restaurant opened. We waited less than 30 minutes and were able to get a table. Reservations are very difficult to get!

Had the Hakata Tonton hot pot. The pot was way toooo shallow. The contents were mostly veggies with 3 small pieces of pork feet, 2 dumplings and 3 another tiny pieces of pork belly. Considering the quality-to-price ratio, I would not go back there anymore.

Sotto 13 is fantastic! Especially so if you're looking to book a large group reservation. I hosted a birthday dinner here for a group of 17 people and they were so gracious and helpful. They sat us when the majority of our group arrived. Â The manager was super attentive and made sure my needs were met and checked up on me a few times. They have a large wait staff so service was pretty prompt when we needed it. Everyone raved about the food and left feeling full. It was surprisingly light on the wallet for such a large group dinner. Btw, the website photos don't do the decor justice. The restaurant is much more modern and romantic in person. The lighting is perfect. Perfect place to dress up if you feel like it. Give it a try! My only complaint was that when the orders came in, the servers didn't remember who ordered what so we had to shout around the table to try and find the owner of the dish. Gets a little annoying if you have to do that 17 times. :( Otherwise, I'd give this place a 5 star rating!

I was very much looking forward to brunch at ABC Kitchen. The service was so poor it diminished our entire experience. Our waitress disappeared after the initial "hello" and we had to engage several other wait staff to assist us. She was not able to tell us the specials without making errors, spoke so softly amidst the noise in the restaurant, she was inaudible. We saw her for our order and then never saw her again--water, coffee, ketchup, bread, dessert menu were all accomplished by us hailing down other gracious wait staff. Â The food was good but sadly, I've had better service at TGI Fridays!!!!! Not happy with the overall experience for a restaurant that has received rave reviews...therefore won't be going back anytime soon.

We had omelets, and home fries and it was very excellent. You cant really do a lot to an omelet, but the ingredients were fresh and the home fries was delicious. I had the greed omelet (feta and tomatoes) and my wife tried the ham and cheese. Portions were generous and prices very reasonable. You cant beat the retro ambiance. The place was pretty packed on a Saturday noon. What stands out is the service, prompt and with a lovely smile. We will have to go back to try the burgers. There is a very reasonable and excellent car wash ~200 yards from this place called Beverly Hills Hand Car Wash and our car was pampered while we enjoyed the meal. Definitely going back for both.

What a gem. Great staff, great food - best steak tartare basically ever. This is a great place to come with one or two other people and just taste test a bunch of delicious french food. The tables are very small and the restaurant does get very crowded. We waited and hour to be seated but just grabbed a glass of wine, sat by the window and enjoyed the ambiance. I can't wait to return!
Ok for the experience, food didn't impress me at all.

I believe that if you Â know what to expect, you probably wont get(/too) disappointed. So im letting you know now, expect a long wait in line and the food to be worth the wait. Three guys one cart. Be ready to tell the first guy what you want, the second guy what kind of sauces you want/dont want, and pay the third guy. Their deliciously seasoned chicken and lamb comes chopped up and makes for easy chewing and enjoying. I asked for extra white and hot sauce which they squeezed a whole lot of over the meat and rice. We couldnt wait to eat it so we enjoyed it at a nearby planter/benches while hungry, fatass, nasty pigeons sat and watched us.

It's all about the sauce, people. Â  I've been here twice. Â I like this place, but here are a few things to possibly maximize your enjoyment: 1. Ask to be seated upstairs. Â During busy times the giant downstairs space gets very noisy (unless you like that sort of thing). 2. All the folks at my table had fish dishes and they were all tasty, but primarily because of the delicious sauces. Â Look closely at the description of the sauces (and ask questions). Â  3. I can't speak about the Chicken Pio but it seems to be a big hit. 4. The sangria was very sweet but very tasty. 5. We had good service both times but I wonder if sitting upstairs helped - it's a much smaller area and might be easier for waitstaff to manage. Â  6. ONLY AMERICAN EXPRESS OR CASH - this is a pain in the ass, but if you know before you go it's just a minor annoyance.

Who would have thought that you can get a good burger in Chinatown? The service is friendly and the beef in the burgers is fresh and tasty. Â Love the creativity behind the menu items. Â  Definitely get the Breakroom Burger with fries.

Great BBQ place!!! I first discovered Mighty Quinn's at Smorgasburg, and am so glad that they've opened up a restaurant in Manhattan, and in the East Village, no less! Their beef brisket is so succulent - not dry at all, and I like that they cut out excess fat before serving it to you in a sandwich. Ribs are tasty too, and my friend had the half chicken, which she liked a lot. The restaurant is fairly big - there is a lot of seating, and would be good for a casual big group dinner.

I don't normally order pizza delivery - when I decide to indulge in pizza, I like to enjoy the full "pizzaria" experience - but the circumstances last night called for it. Â I enjoy Luzzo's (as do Italian friends) and I heard good things about Ovest. Â I ordered the Bufala (square) and was not let down. Â Fresh, tasty and totally satisfying. I happen to live nearby, so I'll be back for more - but next time, in person.
Everytime I go, I'm never disappointed. I love their spicy pork and seafood soup.

What an awful experience. My friend and I went in for a cup of coffee and a snack. We were brought our (burnt, awful) coffees and then our waitress permanently disappeared, until we were asked for the bill - which shocked us. $8 for two coffees! Apparently they were bottomless, but we were never offered a refill or told any such thing. Rip off. Terrible service, bad attitudes, ridiculous prices. Another hipster nightmare destroying Brooklyn.

NOTE:The following is primarily a review of the service, attitude, and overall "vibe" of Westville. If I were rating the quality of the food it would be a four or five star affair. However, as a frequent meal eater(as many as 3 times daily!)I feel it is my duty to inform the public about the indigestible aspects of the Westville experience. The dining experience at Westville can be summed up with the slogan "The discomforts of comfort food." For the record, I am a longtime Westville patron. Each bite holds the flavors and nostalgia of a home-cooked meal where you always earn your dessert by eating every last vegetable. I have been to both Westville in the West Village and Westville East several times over. Both places (especially the West Village location)are a wee bit larger than your average paper bag, and usually you end up with people loitering around you eye balling your table as you choke down your broccoli rabe with a swig of your freshly uncorked bottle of wine. Tonight I decided to give the 18th street location a whirl, the newest addition to the Westville family tree. Size wise it is definitely the papa bear of the family. Unfortunately, while trying to enjoy the delicious meals in front of us, the waitstaff were constantly afoot, clearing plates with vegetables so new they practically were still coming out of the ground. Before even puncturing the first bite with our forks the waitress had returned, asking how the food was as her eyes darted around for anything to clear. I had the displeasure of facing the main sprawl, so I could see all the huffy workers whispering about how long we had been eating there and how much joy we seemed to possess in our souls. There were about 6 people trying to push us along so that they could seat a new crop of anxious diners that had arrived. I am sorry but congratulations for having a delicious AND popular restaurant! With 3 constantly crammed locations! I feel very bad for you in this booming economy. As a passionate eater and appreciator of all things local, I find it more than irritating to be treated like dirt while being a seated, paying customer. We ordered appetizers, a bottle of wine, entrees, dessert, and coffee and were literally scoffed at for wanting to finish our bottle of wine. We overheard one bitchy waiter sneer to another " They've been here a f-ing hour!" I have not felt so rejected during a dining experience since I sneaked a pack of junior mints into the school library in sixth grade. And that was because they feared chocolate smears would ruin the books! Westville, what's your excuse?

I went here for a weekend brunch. You can't make reservations, but my wait was only 5 min. The service was speedy fast. I ordered the blueberry pancakes and they were amazing. Everyones food looked really tasty. I will definitely be back!

What a lovely restaurant in the UES. It's extremely laid back in here and the decor is homey. Our server was kind but not as attentive as we would have liked. Complimentary bread and olive oil is provided. We decided to start with the Wild Mushrooms, Arugula, & Parmigiano Cheese Bruschetta and Calamari Grigliati. The bread is toasty, warm, and slightly soft in the middle. The mushroom topping was smooth, clean, and perfectly seasoned. The Calamari is lightly breaded and grilled. I could taste a bit of curry powder in the seasoning. The warm calamari and cool salad that comes with this dish work so well together. For Entrees, I was able to try the Gnocchi Di Ricotta and the Vitello Gratinato Con Melanzane (Veal Topped w/ Italian Eggplant). The Gnocchi is cooked perfectly. It has a nice chew, yet melts in your mouth. The creamy black truffle and chive sauce is rich and has such depth of flavor. Highly recommended for anyone who enjoys gnocchi and creamy sauces. The Veal is light and savory. The eggplant on top melts in your mouth. This dish is packed with flavor. Another winner. It gets packed in here quick, I strongly recommend making reservations. If you're looking for a restaurant that offers quality and delicious food in a relaxed environment, look no further. Uva is where it's at.
yummy but pricey!

FOOD was great. Branzino- tasted like it was caught fresh that day. And grilled octopus was the most deli-sh octo I have ever had. Meatballs - of course good. Hanger steak my finance had... was ok, nothing special. Definitely go for the seafood, understated atmosphere, service and and great Greek Wine-priced well too. Sad I've lived on the UWS and i just discovered this place. One issue was the our reservation was for 8 pm. and we arrived at 750- and finally got our table 825- but that screw up was not a huge deal. And I will surely be back.

Solid veggie dumplings. Tasty and cooked well. Skin was a bit thick, but Chinese dumplings always seem to have thick skin compared to gyozas or mandu. Sesame pancake is amazing!! Freshly fried fluffy deliciousness stuffed with pickled veggies. Tons of cilantro -- my fav. It's huge for the price! Very chop shop, no nonsense service. Get in, get out, get eating. Awesome.

I am absolutely in love with Gaia Italian CafÃ© - the food, the ambiance, the prices. So, so good. The only sliiight con is the counter lady's attitude, but that's very negligible considering how I barely have to interact with her. My friend and I shared four paninis (I know, I know ... that's way too much :x You really only need 2-3 paninis for two people. One would've been fine for me). We got the Milanese (chicken cutlet + pesto), Goloso (proscuitto + mascarpone + baked pepper), and two other ones that aren't on the online menu. Weird. o_o They both had proscuitto and cheese, though, and they were fabulous. One of them had proscuitto and melted brie, and the other had proscuitto, ricotta, and another kind of cheese. They were all absolutely amazing, and I really don't know what I'd say if you could only get two. I did love the Goloso, though, because the mÃ©lange of flavors and textures was so unique. I love their homemade toasted bread. As a side note, I really didn't think they fit my schema of what a panini was - you know, pressed meat & cheese & veggies between two slices of foccacia? Yeah, the sandwich isn't pressed at all ... so it could get kind of messy. (Well, only the Milanese got messy because the pesto was dripping down). The proscuitto is delicious and generous, and the cheeses are really good-quality. Everything is so exquisitely-made that I'm astounded that it's all so ... inexpensive. o_o They serve water in a small carafe and they give you two very small cups for you to pour your own water into. I was surprised because I basically had to repour my cup every few minutes. (Why not invest in bigger cups??) The ambiance is comfortable and trendy, and relatively spacious for a Manhattan dining establishment. I'm not sure how they can afford to keep it like this, but perhaps it has to do with being located in the basement ... o_o. Either way, I like the open tables and the Italian magazines/books everywhere. The tables are a lot bigger than necessary, and they're good for spreading out work on. At the end of my meal, I asked for a box for my panini. The counter lady asked if I would rather have aluminum foil, and I responded "You don't have any small boxes ...?" and she snarkily replied "If I had smaller boxes, I wouldn't be offering you aluminum foil." I guess it could've been funny, but I was just caught off-guard. Either way, she didn't detract from the 5-star experience; I'd still return to Gaia and bring all my friends here. :)

Like everyone says, this place is very cozy, small and adorable! We got the spinach dip and it was REALLY good! I also ordered a panini, which was pretty OK but nothing spectacular like the dip. I ordered a Lambrusco and it was perfect. Chilled, bubbly, sweet red wine! It was also POURING rain so we waited it out while inside. They were very nice and didn't bother us too much, even though there was a bunch of people that were waiting to come in. They seemed very low key and friendly. They aren't snobby at all, and very accommodating. My friend had a big duffel bag with her so they offered to take it downstairs and brought it up when we were leaving. Â I didn't really have too much of anything else, but I definitely want to come back for more!

Solid choice for dinner in the Theatre District. It can be tough to find a good meal without getting totally gouged on the price in this area, but Trecolori has found the balance. You can easily get dinner and a glass of wine for $40 per person or so, depending on what you order. I've been here a couple of times (the Farfalle Primavera is outstanding) and have been consistently impressed with the service. While this is a touristy spot (like every other restaraunt in the Theatre District) as a local I still use it as a go to. The atmosphere is nice and the service is friendly and efficient. As the other reviewers mentioned, it does tend to get pretty crowded so if you don't want to wait, call ahead.

Completely overrated. Â My family and I arrived at 5:30 pm on Sunday night, gave our names and weren't seated until after 7pm. Â When I went up to the hostess to ask how much longer the wait would be she asked for my name, mumbled something under her breath and walked away. Â It seemed as if other parties were being seated ahead of us. The restaurant is tiny and loud. Â Everyone waiting in line outside was offered free wine but that didn't make a difference for me. Â Once seated we ordered calamari and clams to begin. Â The appetizers were decent. Â  The bread we were given was slightly burnt and tasted more like a crouton than a nice crusty piece of bread. Â They were out of the scallops and sole so we ordered shrimp stuffed with crab meat and red snapper. Â Both entrees were bland, having no flavor at all. Â Even my lemon potatoes weren't anything to write home about. Â  This establishment lacks ambiance, customer service and in my opinion you can find far better food elsewhere. Â I'm not sure what all the hype on Yelp is about.
Delicious and cheap. Enough said.

WOW im so excited I found this place. I taught I was going to miss curry forsure after moving from LA. We went here one day and I ordered the Grandslam and my Fiance ordered the chicken curry. I opened the box of the GRANDSLAM and I was so amazed how much food was in there. I ended up saving some for later and had it for dinner as well! The price is inexpensive but I would not recommend eating there. Take out is what i do always!

Always a shame when really good food is overwhelmed by its obnoxious surroundings, making for a so-so dinner. Â  Marlow's has a great low key decor. Â The food, for the most part, was delicious, but some simple things were surprisingly not very good. I stole one recipe and have made it at home many times (thyme-sprinkled, honey-drizzled, ricotta smeared bread. So simple, so good.) Â Had chicken under a brick and it was the star of the night compared to the fish my friends ate. Â Started with a cheese plate that had one good cheese, and one that the waitress recommended that was completely underwhelming. The oysters were good, but nothing mind blowing. All this was totally killed by the long, long wait and overly pretentious atmosphere. Somehow the simple decor did nothing to combat the ooze of the crowd. Meaning, a roomful of people with an Â I'm-so-happy-to-be-seen-waiting-here-2-hours-for-Â­a-table attitude was quite boring. Â Makes them do nothing to make you comfortable during the long wait, and nothing to try to make the wait less. Â We went to a nearby dive bar to get a drink to survive the wait. Â Won't be going back because there's never a need to wait 2 hours to eat in NYC.

Excellent Spanish tapas in the city...and I've had tapas in Madrid, Sevilla and Barcelona. Â While no tapas will be as good as what you get in Spain (ie, authentic jamon iberico de pata negra), Casa Mono comes as close as you can in the U.S. Â Really loved the razor clams & gambas and wine list is excellent with a knowledgeable Somm there...for white get an Albarino or Txakolina and for red, I prefer a Ribera del Duero (Pesquera, specifically) over Rioja (although I do love Lopez de Heredia). Â Great date place too - if you can get the stools at the food bar.

Came here for an anniversary dinner. Â We showed up on time and had a short wait before being seated at a table. Â Note, to be seated at the sushi bar, you likely have to request it as it seems it can be crowded for dinner. I'm definitely a self-proclaimed sushi fanatic, though not necessarily a connoisseur. Â Meaning I like to have it as often as possible and am not always the pickiest when it comes to sushi. Â Better sushi than not sushi, right? Â We each ordered the sushi matsu combo with a la carte nigiri added later on. Â The food was great. Â The fish was fresh an the tamago was some of the best I have had I a while. Â The pieces, we're admittedly small, but well proportioned allowing for a good balance of fish and rice. Perhaps the best part of the whole experience is that the combo is a great value, as are many of their price fixie items. Â For a restaurant that just recently made it onto top 10 restaurant lists of NYC, the meal came out to less than $100 for two including tip. Â Definitely would recommend this to anyone looking for quality sushi at a reasonable and fair (but not cheap) price. Anniversary dinner - success!!!

I recently encountered Roberta's at Madison Square Eats and realized they serve my type of pizza. Super thing crust, baked in a wood burning oven, with the perfect balance of chew an crunch, and of course a nice selection of seasonal and fresh toppings. Their signature Â Bee Sting pie, a gooey spicy pie with mozzarella, tomato and soppressata that's finished off with a drizzle of honey, is their best seller at the moment. But the latest contender, The Stephen Hawking which melds pecorino, mozzarella, tomato and fresh ramps, is a close second. Having tried both I cant imagine what the options must be like at their Bushwick establishment and cant wait to head over there.

who doesn't love this place????!!!!! good beer selection great sexy bartenders and barbacks great music and once in awhile you will find 40 bucks on the floor and buy your friends a round of beer. cheeseballs!
Wrapping up my Thursday evening here. Better crowd even though the place is dead. Proper wings were "hot off the press".

There's no better snack to be found in East Village than the legendary Pommes Frites, an authentic (as authentic as one can get thousands of miles from Brussels) Belgian friterie. For around $6, grab yourself a regular cone of fresh, thick cut fries, and choose from around 20 fry sauces...ketchup isn't recommended here, unless it's the curry ketchup! My personal favorite? The rosemary garlic. But the sauces make this place; you'd be crazy if you didn't select at least three! Note that seating is limited (three great wooden seats out front, great for people watching, and two communal benches inside). Definitely a to-go atmosphere. Best fries in town, and as I'm reviewer ~2100, obviously others would agree.

Unfortunately my love affair with Riverpark has ended. Even if the space is gorgeous..... the service has killed it for me..... and I will never be back. Came here for dinner with a bunch of girlfriends on a Friday night. No complaints about the food at all that night. We ordered a few appetizers to share and each got an entree and enjoyed the food and company. What was disturbing that night was the fact that we can hear a bunch of waiters congregating nearby each arguing who was going to serve (or not serve) which table. There even seemed to be a manager present that participated (NOT directed as he should of) this absurd and inappriopriate conversation as to who had too many tables and thus should not get another. They didn't even have the courtesy to sort this out behind the scenes. Should a restaurant of this caliber and this many months under its belt still be figuring out staffing issues????!!! Then this week decided to drop by for a lunch since the weather was gorgeous. Hostess was very nice and selected a nice table for us. The busboy came immediately to get us water and bread.. but then that was it... we waited a while before a waiter came (said waiter was the same waiter I had previously mentioned in my review..). He came by and we asked him for the wine list.. and he gruffiingly said he'll go get it. Then we waited and waited.. he finally came back with it but basically handed it over as if he was doing us a great favor... then we waited and waited and waited and waited... and I Â had enough. Obviously our waiter does not enjoy his job.. nor is he very good at it. And to have been seated for almost 30 minutes and no one to come by to take our order is unacceptable. So we did the unthinkable... we got up and left.. and not even a person in sight to complain about this horrible service to...... Service (specifically the wait staff) has always been the thorn in my overall rave about Riverpark... and now it seems like it's the end all for my love affair with this restaurant. The 2 stars is for the gorgeous space. Even the menu seemed uninspired.... I had a hard time picking anything of interest to have.
Huge fan of this place. The ambiance is was rustic and cozy. The food was warm and Â comforting. The french dip melted on my mouth. I cant wait to go back for more.

We ordered the burgers, cheesteak, eggs Benedict and everything was bland. We saw our waitress once. Took the bus boy 15 mins to fill our waters up. Service is very poor, I do not suggest it. Very disappointing, the execution on food is not at all good. Ambience is the only reason I would give it a star.

Reservation for Sunday brunch, 1 PM. They don't seat you until your entire party is there! I got there on time, but three others in my group were slightly late. All the reservations were running ~15mins behind schedule, but we were seated around 1:30 PM. Without a reservation, I overheard a group of 4 that had to wait 1.5-2 hours... Benedict Jane and Johnny were both very popular and delicious. One of their specials was a pulled-pork benedict which also looked amazing. The best part is probably that the proportions are generous and you'll definitely be full. Also complimentary drink (alcoholic or orange/grapefruit juice). Packed place, lots of waiters/busboys moving around. Very popular, a good solid place for brunch :) Definitely make reservations before going!

This Scottish gastropub tucked away in the West village is about to become my favorite cozy after work spot. Decorated like a rustic cottage - taxidermy deer and all -the exposed brick gives it's already warm appeal a toasty hug you need to get out of the cold. Their menu is full of classic dishes (lamb sausage roll, crab ontoast, schnitzel, beef Wellington, shepherd's pie, etc.) and their Scotch list is amazing! The staff is beyond friendly and our waitress was able to recommend an amazing whiskey to soften the blow of them pouring the last of my favorite brand into an Old Fashioned (ugh). This place is the bees!

I can't believe this place has been around my whole life and I just tried it today. We waited about an hour for our pie on a cold Sunday afternoon. It was definitely worth the wait. We ordered a regular pie with garlic and cherry tomatoes and it was absolutely delicious. The prices are steep, but seeing the way the pizzas are crafted really does make a difference. There are no shortcuts taken and you can tell Domenico takes his pizza seriously. While we were eating, we overheard a group saying they come there once a month. It's that kind of good.

My last experience was horrific and after doing some more research, I'm never going back. Â  My younger sister was visiting from Ohio and I thought she had to get some true New York style pizza! Â When I heard thad Grimaldi's was scheduled to move November 28th (a week away at the time), I thought we have to go! My sister, boyfriend, and I ate there the night before Thanksgiving. Â The line was thankfully very short. Â While we waited for our pizza, we looked around. Â Half of the pizzas were burnt, like charred black, inedible burnt. Â We were worried our pizzas would turn out that way. Luckily our pizzas came out well. Â But while we ate, no waiter check in on us. Â Our water glasses were empty for our entire dinner. Â We even asked a waiter for water, and still no water arrived. Â It wasn't until we got our check that they finally refilled our waters. As soon as we paid, they wanted us out. Â We couldn't leave, because my sister was in line for their tiny bathroom. Â We didn't feel comfortable taking her things and waiting outside because she had a lot of bags and we didn't want her to go outside in the cold without her coat. Â  It would have been fine if our waiter had asked us politely to leave, but our waiter slammed a bunch of plates and menus on our table. Â A couple minutes later, while my sister was still in line for the bathroom, the waiter rudely urged us to leave. Â He was clearly irritated with us and loudly grunted, "Can you please go? Â There are people outside and it is very cold. Â Can you go?" Â  We started to grab our things and the waiter already brought in the next family. Â They stood breathing down our necks as we had to grab my sister's coat, purse, bags, etc. Â The waiter almost pushed us out the way to set up the table while we were still getting our belongings. It was the most terrible experience I've ever had. Â They ruined our night. Â We've always brought our family and friends to Grimaldi's, but no more. Â We have never felt so unappreciated. Â After seeing how they make everyone's pizza 1/2 burnt and how they treat us, it is clear that they do NOT care about their customers. Â They generate so much money from the number of people that come in that they don't need to care. Â I don't want to give my money to a place that feels like the restaurant is above the customer. Â Where the restaurant feels like it can get away with anything. AND AND AND...the reason why they're moving is because the owner (Frank Ciolli) owes rent money, despite the fact that he owns 18 pizzerias nationwide. Â Sleezy. Â The original creator of Grimaldi's also regrets selling his business to Ciolli. Â What does that tell you?

Cutie Patroller report This is the closest wine bar from my clothing shop CutieRoom (located next to Gentlemen Farmer ) so I often come by for wine and a small snack after work. Jadis is reasonable and has a wide selection on their wine menu as well as serving French Tapas. The whole kitchen is behind the bar counter and they don't use any gas appliances for cooking - pretty much just an open toaster and panini press! I don't recommend to go here if you are expecting a hearty dinner but sometimes I will crave their Spinach Chicken Salad..it is so good, filling, and guilty free for skinny bitches! Â The place is always crowded but never uncomfortably too packed (after my blog post, there is no guarantee ;). It's simply cozy and homey. The wine I normally order by the bottle is only $25, and by the glass $7. ''Cheers!" by Cutie Patroller
Other than the wait....perfection!

I am not a ramen person. Â I think ramen should come in packages and be spicy and be about a dollar to eat. Â  This place is the only place I would go back to for ramen. Â They just did something to it that made it delicious and so worth going back to. The only thing that makes this place less than my number 1 go to place in the village is the price and the line. Â  Pro Tip: They open an hour before they serve alcohol (or at least that is what they do on Sundays), so if you want a beer with your ramen, you have to get there at noon. Pro Tip: go on Sunday for lunch, right as they open. Â No lines.

The food here was beyond outstanding. Every first bite we tried was filled with big eyed expressions, a leaning back from the table and an "Oh my God!" statement. Seriously... the beef Ren dang (sp?) was to die for! I don't know if ever in my life, I've had beef melt in my mouth ... literally. And the flavor..! But the appetizer of indian pancakes dipped in that sauce... WOW! The other dish we had was mango chicken. Ummm yum! Â Nyonya is definitely one of the best out there and their pricing is really good. I highly recommend the satay and the roti canai. The taste is very authentic, and I am sure to be back soon.
The ramen and sushi are both surprisingly delicious. It lacks the reputation of its ramen competitors like ippudo and totto because it is a Japanese restaurant and not a ramen restaurant I suppose

The Crack Pie is so good, it's a sin. The Cornflake Cookie with chocolate chip and marshmallow is yummy and has a great crunch to it (I bought 1, and then came back the next day to buy 1/2 dozen for my friends). I tasted the Cereal Milk flavored soft serve, and it was surprisingly good. Â It's like the leftover milk after a bowl of Honey Bunches of Oats.

I think the man helping us was the owner... He was incredible. He was running and starring here! He had a tat of his dad on his arm that he was proud of as much as the quality of their Italian food and vino. Our choice of the night was the Prosecco - Castellon di Roncade from Italia. The food was SOMETHING TO CALL HOME ABOUT. Order anything!!! Eat on their patio if it's a nice day. Definitely a conversational atmosphere, good for dates if you want to intellectually connect... Something about the patio atmosphere evoked that in us at least lol. Def coming back!!

You just can't beat cheap and delicious late night eats from a hole in the wall establishment in Chinatown. Â Sesame pancake with duck was filling and flavorful, the various styles of pork and chive dumplings are juicy and seasoned well, and the shrimp dumplings were ok, but a bit bland. Â With all the options, will definitely come back to try other parts of the menu. Be prepared for taking out as the seating is minimal, and the lines are long.

Stopped by this place this weekend-around the corner from my house....I'm indifferent with the square that I got..was expecting a mind blowing experience. Maybe it was just that batch , so will give it another go soon..all honestly, I have had better pizza though...

A good mid-range option in Chinatown with prices that would be more in line with the budget category in any other section of Manhattan. There's a nice selection of Hong Kong-inflected Chinese fare. The emphasis is of course on noodle dishes, but there are also sub-$10 bo zai fan with a variety of mix-ins. The dÃ©cor is bit brighter and more contemporary than either than the average banquet hall or dingy noodle joint, so this remains a good option for the out-of-town guest or reluctant friend venturing into the less tourist friendly areas of Chinatown for the first time. There's a good level of English, both in the menu descriptions and the staff at hand, which makes it easier to wade into the 'stranger' parts of what's on offer for non-Chinese speaking neophytes. The portions are very large - we started with an appetizer (soup dumplings) and wound up abandoning our main courses halfway through the meal. The noodles are appropriately rubbery, the XO sauce sweet and the meat tender. A great workaday option.
I like the atmosphere, and the food. great place to go in town.
Excellent place
The food (the patty melt) was pretty solid and satisfying though the wine (a Chilean red) was terrible and horrendously overpriced. Â Drink beer here.

I wasn't sure whether it was the jazz music singing to me in the background, the old fashioned tin ceilings and the chocolate brown hardwood floors, or observing all of the names and initials etched in our butcher block table; but this restaurant felt very comforting, uplifting and "old New York" to me. Corner Bistro's food menu is simple: Burger, cheeseburger, grilled chicken sandwich, BLT, chili, and French fries. The full bar menu, on the other hand, is much more extensive. Susan and I each started with a cider beer and split a custom order of chili-cheese fries (I say "custom" because chili, cheese, and French fries are all on the menu, but they aren't offered as the combined greasy masterpiece which I ordered) as an appetizer to our Bistro Burgers ("Bistro" is the addition of cheese and bacon). The cider beer was cold and the chili cheese fries were a hot mess (in a good way). Thin, McDonald's size French fries, were piled on a plate and topped with American cheese slices and doused with homemade beef chili. Pasteurized-processed cheese is normally something that grosses me out to the point of avoidance (except when used in grilled cheese sandwiches), but it worked well with this dish because this type of cheese is creamier than other varieties, such as cheddar. Plus, the chili was piping hot, allowing the processed product to melt seamlessly over the fries. (Oh, who knows, maybe I'm just trying to console my inner "white trash!") Our Bistro Burgers arrived on small, 6" diameter paper plates similar to those that cake used to be served on at childhood birthday parties. Fresh iceberg lettuce, a thick tomato slice and white onion graced one half of the bun, while the thick beef burger patty topped with melted American cheese and bacon graced the other. After a sprinkle of salt and a lather of ketchup, I united the sandwich together and took my first bite. Fitting my mouth around the burger wasn't easy, but I was determined to taste every element, from the bottom bun to the top bun. Susan and I must have been silent throughout our entire meal. I was so entranced by my Bistro Burger, that I was speechless. The fresh hamburger buns must have been buttered and grilled prior to the addition of ingredients, because they held their shape beautifully. The beef patty had a crusty, perfectly seasoned and salty exterior giving way to a velvety medium cooked interior. The crunch from the lettuce, onion and bacon was a welcome textural and flavorful contrast to the soft bread, meat and melted American cheese. All in all, a perfect cheeseburger. *Something to note when dining at Corner Bistro* CASH ONLY

I didn't know how to enter the building. Please tell me I am not the first... My boyfriend figured it out. So smart. In case you're like me (which I hope you aren't), the door is on the left side... where there's a handle... We ordered Shrimp Pad Thai to go. Our plan was to have a picnic of asian food at Prospect Park. I really loved the pad thai! When it ain't orange, it's already a good sign. It's annoying when people say they've had the best pad thai in Thailand and compare every pad thai dish to that. Well, I am going to be annoying. I've had pad thai in Thailand, and it was the best. Ever! This one was really close to that. There's this smoky sweet flavor. Try it. Some might not like it because it isn't what they're used to. But I'd definitely come back here for more Thai food. The ambiance is typical (as in Brooklyn red bricks awesome so cool typical).

My husband brought me here for my birthday and overall it was a really great experience. Â I'd been wanting to come here for years, starting when we lived in the neighborhood but just never got around to it. The interior is really warm and inviting. Â The decor is pretty traditional with candles and copper sconces. Since it was after Thanksgiving, there was some holiday touches that made the place feel really homey and comfortable. Â We were seated right away in the dining area (there is a bar/tavern area when you first walk in that's more casual). Â The website says dress code is business casual but most people were dressed down. Â I wore a dressy top with high-waisted black pants and I was probably one of the most dressed up diners there. Â Our server was a friendly guy and did a good job of regularly checking in with us. Â My husband pointed out that they didn't acknowledge my birthday even though he mentioned it when he made the reservation. Â I'm not one for the extra attention except the table next to us was congratulated on their anniversary and got complimentary glasses of wine... We opted for the seasonal tasting menu, which gets you 7 courses including two amuse and desert. Â With the exception of one course that had too many flavors going on on one plate, everything was really delicious and the presentation was nice. Â The waitstaff who actually brought the food to us were awkward though..they tried to explain what the dish was but stumbled a lot and never made eye contact so it was kind of odd. Â They would also speak to each other in their native language which seemed out of place for this type of place. We got a bottle of cava which was amazing and went well with our courses. When we got our deserts, they ended up bringing me an extra dessert with a candle and wished me a happy birthday...so i guess they figured it out later? Just weird that it wasn't acknowledged up front. Â Then after we cleared three desserts between the two of us, they brought out a plate of petite fours. Â After THAT they brought out two muffins for us to take home and eat for breakfast...really nice touch! At that point we were stuffed to the max. Â  It's not a cheap meal, but I was surprised that it was quite "affordable" given that it's 7 courses plus extra sweets..places like Per Se or Daniel will charge more than double. Â Overall we had a great night and a lovely meal. Â We'd come back again and maybe check out the tavern part to see if there is a big difference.

Does not hold a candle to Gordo in Berkeley/SF (even though I've learned that they model themselves to Gordo, my favorite burrito place in the world!)...but in NYC, it'll do. If Dos Toros, were in SF, I'd give it 2.5 stars (the beans were not cooked to tenderness...and the burrito wasn't well wrapped, and the flavor lacked an extra zest, possibly missing pico de gallo). In SF, I'd probably not come back to Dos Toros. But in NYC? Â I'll give it 4 stars. (btw, every other burrito place in NYC would receive 1 star). Also--if you're here on a coldy windy night, be prepared to encounter a very crowded place with no available seats--you'll be eating your burrito standing up if you have it "for here." If you're lucky you won't even have to stand next to and over the garbage can while doing it (one dude was relegated to eating his burrito over the trash receptacle area).

I arrived at 5:00 and they were ready for us. A party of six easily accommodated in this beautiful, hidden gem tucked away in the heart of the village. The food and service was OUTSTANDING. The servers were extremely attentive and food was so fresh, I think I was temporarily transported to Italy. Don't miss an opportunity to go here. I will definitely be back!

I wanted to like this place more than I did. Â The food was pretty good. Â The staff was great, especially Sabrina the bartender. Â The ambience is lacking. Â It was very weird walking in the back and seeing the "zombie" men in the back playing video games. Â They maybe should have a seperate section.

Consistently great soup dumplings My favorites are the crab, pork ones. Try to avoid large groups, it will be a wait. If you do have a large group, make sure everyone is there, or else they will not seat you. Orange beef is very good, though it could be a little thinner like at Chinatown Brasserie. Most people come for the soup dumplings.
Good but not as amazing as it was . Become so popular I feel that it's affected the quality of the food ..staff are great music killer good beer selection.

My friends and I really enjoyed this restaurant last night as this was our first time there. The happy hour special--from 5-7 pm--is unbeatable. Sangria and mojito only--made just right for just $5!!! After a couple drinks at the bar (the interior is charming albeit a bit cramped/small), it was time for dinner. We snagged a Savored deal and our waiter was very helpful with answering questions and giving suggestions. We shared the codfish fritters and empanadas for appetizer. They were delightful and each dish was accompanied by a tasty sauce. Most of us chose the Paella Valenciana for the main which was very tasty although my plate had just one small piece of chicken. Nevertheless, it was still very good. Off to the side of our table, there was a guy rolling cigars lending an authentic ambiance to the restaurant. I am looking forward to returning again---good food, service, festive atmosphere--what more can you ask for?

I came here with two of my friends on a Saturday afternoon for brunch. The place looked packed but we were lucky enough to get a table outside after only waiting ten minutes. I ordered the poached eggs with grilled tomatoes and halloumi and I really enjoyed it! It was a great combination and the eggs were poached perfectly..not too runny, not too hard. The portions were a great size too. My friends each ordered the skirt steak sandwich with fries and that was really tasty also. Oh and for dessert, we shared the waffles with rosewater and yogurt. This was just okay in my opinion. Not sure if the flavors complimented each other. All in all, this is a great brunch spot and the prices are very inexpensive. I want to give this place four stars because I really enjoyed my dish...but the service was so slow, I would have to rethink coming here.

all i have to say is it blows motorino out of the atmosphere, and i live down the street from the so called best "new wave pizza" or whatever....the backyard is great, i dont mind waiting the 20 minutes or whatever it takes to get a seat in the cozy dining room! the crispy glover can be made vegetarian and is still delicious! The margerita is also wonderful-plain and simple and yummy! while the specials of the day are tasty and interesting, they are very very small and very very expensive. id stay away...overall, a wonderful dining experience each and every time!

Don't think twice before going here. Every tapas ordered was out of this world in both visits. Our waitress was extremely helpful and circled all of her recommendations to please our group (1 vegetarian, 3 meat eaters), so definitely ask for some help because there's Â a lot to choose from. Romantic, dim-lit, rustic atmosphere that feels like you're in Spain. Get the sangria. YUM!

I'm not in love with this place. I only came here because of a Scoutmob deal for 50% off on tab and it was nearby the event venue I was coming from. Service is good. Beers are good. The food was just not too memorable. Not much of a fan. Glad I didn't pay full price.

Don't be intimidated by the tight spaces or cash only mandate. These Aussies know food better than most. The burgers are some of the best in the city. The pumpkin salad is fresh and delicious. It's a neighborhood favorite.

Thank you fellow Yelper's! Â I wanted to celebrate Chinese New Year's in Chinatown with some good soup dumplings, and I came to you for suggestions. Â It was between Joe's and another place, but the other sounded like I wouldn't have room to sit. Â  I was not disappointed- as soon as we receive menus, the efficient waiter asked how many soup dumpling orders we wanted. Â They were working on those gorgeous babies while we browsed the menu for more good food. I wasn't crazy about the boiled pork dumplings though- they were heavy and not appetizing enough to have more than one. Â  We also ordered delicious sauteed water spinach and some baked turnip buns, and I obviously didn't eat fast enough, because my brother got most of the soup dumplings! Â I will be back again.
nice recipes

My favorite place for pumpkin pancakes. Â Contrary to Reviewer "Jackie S.", I found them to be highly texturally accurate. Â The potatoes were adequate. Â  Docked one point for the wait time; there's nothing wrong with being busy, that's usually a sign your restaurant is the shit (can I cuss on a yelp review?). Â But they were way off with the estimation of the waiting time. Â Not cool!

Why do I always end up here? 'Hey, I know this awesome place we can go to!' says the NYU college girl I shouldn't be hitting on. Okay, I'll follow you, but only because I'm too drunk to care. Or so I think. By the time I end up at Employees Only, the place is packed to the brim: every bar stool taken, every inch of space filled with sweaty New Yorkers, and even the alcove by the entrance is lined with members of the New Jersey Society of PDA Fetishists. In the rare times that I've gotten to sit at a table, I've had the most awkwardly repeating scenario of mildly attractive cougars hitting on me. At least they paid for my drinks, as I can't afford these prices. All of this said, I have to catch myself from giving too scathing a review: I'm only really critiquing this place in its state between the hours of midnight and 4am. That said, you can do a lot better; but read other people's reviews before you make up your mind on the meta of Employees Only. It's entirely possible that I'm just not cool enough to get this place.

The service was incredible. They were extremely courteous. The environment is extremely lively. We purposely made our way to Queens just to try the live octopus sashimi. It was extremely delicious. We were all antsy at first but it went well. Def recommend.

I don't typically go to sit down restaurants when I eat alone, I'm more of an easy-at-the-bar type of diner, but this place seems to do both well. Â The bartenders were friendly and make a great house cocktail (I decided to try the rye one while I waited for my food). Â I ordered the snapper and it was perfectly cooked and seasoned. Â Someone down the bar ordered some fries with mussels and gravy (Poutine?) that I already feel like I need to go back to try. Â  I had a pale ale beer on tap after my meal that I don't remember the name of, but it hit the spot. Â The hostess thanked me for coming in as I left and really made the whole experience pretty great. Â I would definitely come back with a date, or with a group, since the booths toward the back looked comfortable. Â Well worth the trip from Williamsburg to give this new restaurant a shot.
Dropped by after class and tried their Belgian waffle & a cup of iced chocolate. Delicious!!
This is the best pizza I've ever had, each slice tastes so fresh. If your in the Dumbo area its a must!!!!

I've been to graffiti over 5 times in the last couple years. Chef Mehta has really thought through "fusion" and creates an environment / ambience which really differentiates it from other places int he city. The restaurant is cozy, with smaller parties sitting at a communal table with other diners. Some items to try: Mango Paneer - Excellent Zucchini Hummus Pizza - Exellent Cumin Eggplant Buns - My favorite - great flavor! I had the opportunity to meet Chef Mehta the last time I swung by. He is such a geniune person and personally seated us. He also offered a drink and a free appetizer after chatting with us for a bit. Definite must go, would recommend it to anyone!

A few weeks ago I decided I had to come to Il Bambino to experience the phenominal paninis that everyone raves about. I ordered one with chorizo and something else (don't remember, maybe it was chicken?). It was ok, just a regular panini. I didn't see what all the hype is about. The guy behind the counter was your average hipster, with a bushy beard and too-cool-for-school attitude. Meh, I wouldn't go back.

Every time I visit Chinatown, I make a point to go to this place. Â It is very small and can get hot. Â 4 excellent handmade dumplings for $1?!?!?! Â I always get the pork ones and they are also available to go. Â There are some tiny spots inside to eat, but it is usually too hot and crowded since they are soooo goood.

Mexican Korean fusion that works. Â The bowls and burritos look good, but I always get the tacos. Â 3 tacos for $10 is a good deal, and they don't skimp on the taco filling. Â I love that they tailor the taco toppings to the protein filling instead of putting the same garnish on everything. Â The variety and balance of flavors has been well thought out. Â My favorites in order are: 1. The veggie taco: sometimes veggie tacos are boring, and sometimes I only order the veggie option so I can pretend to be a little healthier. But here it's actually my favorite option, the cheese and Korean flavored veggies are a surprisingly tasty combo. Â The pomegranate on top is genius. 2. Â Short-rib taco: sweet and savory, the kimchi and pear slaw on top is spicy and sweet. Â Every bite is satisfying. 3. Korean fried chicken taco: It's tasty, but sometimes I think the ratio of breading to chicken is a little too heavy on the breading. Â  I've probably tried the fish and pork, but I don't remember. Â I wish there was a grilled fish option. Â I was totally underwhelmed by the edamame falafel, I thought it was dry. Â And falafel with refried beans in the same taco was kind of a fail. Â But my friend loves the edamame falafel bowl, so... to each her own. The space is a little small, so take out might be a better bet. Â Get it to go and then go to one of the nearby dive bars to chow down. I've had it delivered and it was fine, but they are best eaten super fresh. Service is a little slow, especially when I'm super hungry, but that just means they're making it fresh. Â  Keep it up Kimchi Grill :)
Worth the wait and any other reason you may have to not visit. Â  The modern ramen here is my favorite dish in the whole of NYC.
My favorite sake bar in Manhattan hands down...It can get a bit crowded late night but it is worth the wait!!

Definitely not a 5 star restaurant. The place is nice, the food - could be better, not having a set menu has it's pros and cons. supporting local food industry and farmers - is a good cause, but not always the best choice on the plate, same goes for wine. Left Â disappointed ...

Solid chinese restaurant but would not go out of my way to eat here. The roast duck was great, fatty in a right way and good. The egg noodles with roast pork was a little disappointing for me. The broth was good but not deep with flavor and the roast pork again just didn't do it for me, but definitely edible. Cash only, quick service, sometimes share tables. Prices are good. Food is good, but not great.

Went here for dinner Sat night. Â  Pros: Nice looking place Good service. Onion bread was not bad. Cons: Special already sold out by 5:30, it sounded good, maybe prep a few more. Awkward timing of the food (some fast, some slow) Food... The food was totally Meh. Â We were at a 5 top and only one person had anything good to say (They liked the cauliflower... which I tired and it was good). Â The pizza app we got was runny, and soggy. Â They cut it in big pieces and with lots of onions it just feel flat. Â I also got the mixed grill. Â I have a hard time saying no to lamb. Â I wish I had. Â The beef and pork were tasteless in a watery bean sauce. Â The lamb was awesome... all two bites. Â It was nothing but bone. Â Smallest portion I have ever seen. Â I was surprised it was good so well for the piece I had.
Very good lunch special, cheap with lot of servings. However, I had to run to make it in time for the special, so I recommend extending the time.

Wish they had a better drinks menu beyond beer and cider but other than that this place is great! Â Think Traif with Korean/Asian influenced menu and minus the hipsters. The chef worked at some fancy restaurants and opened up an earnest, honest place in Sunnyside of all places. Â It's an odd spot since most restaurants in the vicinity are ethnic and/or no frills eateries but it works. Â Their dishes are small, almost tapas style but thoughtful and services was great!

Oh, man... Delicious. Â We were looking for a great restaurant to spend our last night in the city...and decided on the West Village. Â I popped onto Yelp, and found lots of reviews speaking favorably of Extra Virgin, so I said... "We shall go...there!" Best eeney, meeney, miney, moe outcome, ever! We were floored by the deliciousness of everything we ordered. My wife had the Goat Cheese/Beet Salad to start, which was outstandingly fantastic...I had the prosciutto wrapped scallops. Oh my (insert deity here ), was it just the bee's knees. Crispy prosciutto, perfectly seared scallops...oh, and surprise!!! Pesto mashed potatoes hidden underneath some fresh watercress... I had the hanger steak entree...which was expertly prepared, with caramelized onions in what tasted like a balsamic reduction, with their fries and gorgonzola cream dipping sauce ( COME THE F ON! ). Wifey had the butternut squash ravioli...heavenly. Â  The best part about Extra Virgin, is that the plates are plentiful, but not to the point that you can't at least consider dessert. We rocked the warm chocolate cake with malted milk ice cream. It was really delightful. Â The dining room is cozy ( to coin a phrase so oft used in New York ), and the hostess was ridiculously nice. All-in-all...a wonderful, wonderful meal. See you again soon...

Huevos! I've got quite a few cafes near me but I always make the extra trek to Lunitas. The food cannot be beat - everything is super fresh and I always feel like I'm in someone's comfy home. The owner is muy simpatico and plays great music. EAT -The Fulton egg sandwich on the cheddar chive jalepeÃ±o biscuit - savory goodness -Fruit/Granola/Yogurt - no skimping whatsoever - freshest variety of fruit -Empanadas - all homemade, you can taste the love! I love this spot. Best cafe in the hood. The only way this place could get better is if they had homemade whipped cream for their hot chocolates. I haven't checked on this matter but will look into it come winter and report back. NOM.

4.5 Was at Hotel Chantelle for happy hour and and came here after for a drunken bite. Carnivore wrap - SO GOOD. The angus meatball inside is seriously fantastic, great flavor, moist, some sorta grilled motherlode of yum that you just can't place, but don't care where it's from as long as there's more of it. Fries were decent. Burn yoself pipin hot tho. Beware. Also taste good inside the wrap. They also have swings which is great, since the wait for your food is UBER long. Â Granted time and space are elongated or condensed depending on your level of inebriation, regardless, felt like an eternity that was slightly alleviated by the swinging motion of my chair. Oh, and you will also get yelled at if you stand on the bench outside and dance. Damn broski making wraps, sometimes you gotta get your dance on after you eat a wrap! nah mean? *note, wrap may inadvertently spray sauce on your dress shirt since its wrapped up tighter than the girdle of a baptist minister's wife at an all-you-can-eat pancake breakfast. This will make you sad, so eat with care.
Filipino restaurant. Short staffed. I have been waiting for 40 minutes for bicol "express" (lunch special) Food here is pretty good, but I have to give two stars for their very slow service.

Don't know what all the fuss is about. Just went for brunch-- really looking forward to it after the yelp reviews. The feel of the place is really nice and inviting, but the food was fairly mediocre. Too much salt. Not enough sweet on the brunch menu. (The bacon, however, were grease-dripping sticks of heaven.) I would go back, but only if I couldn't find anything better.

This place is amazing. Â The food is cheap, tasty and filling. Â I've even been to this place twice in one day. Â Its as good as it gets for street food. Â It will not make you sick either. Â The line is insane at all times of the day so grab a friend and be prepared to stand in line. Â Its not as long as it seems. Â  Tip - Their white sauce is great to add. Â Their red sauce is hot hot hot.

Excellent brews. I really enjoyed the Ear Inn Ale. The bartender was really nice and talked to us about the history of the bar - and the ghost. There aren't many places where you can learn and drink at the same time! A nyc gem. Perfect bar for Halloween.

I'm surprised that this restaurant received great reviews. I, honestly, did not like the food besides the baby jesus cake and the pinot noir wine. The homemade mozzarella appetizer was also good. My boyfriend and I ordered the cavatelli and pappardelle - both recommended by our waiter. The cavatelli wasn't that great, but the pappardelle was decent. Both were too salty and the pappardelle was too oily. The best thing about it was that it was appropriately priced. The service was okay. The waitress/hostess who seated us was oblivious to the fact that she did not give us menus, or ask us if we wanted drinks (usually done when they seat you). We had to ask them to give us menus. They weren't really attentive - seemed like they were more interested in talking to their friends at the bar. I was really irritated when the couple who came after us (probably 30 to 45 min after) got their food quickly - they were pretty much done we left. Perhaps the restaurant forgot that we were paying customers?
One of my favorite places to eat when in New York. Â Warm, homey atmosphere, good food and not a scene. Â I always have a good time here.

Outstanding in every way. Each dish was better than the last, from the thinly sliced & battered pan fried eggplant, to the grape leaves (piping hot) stuffed with spicy rice & ground sausage to the succulent rack of lamb. We asked our lovely & funny waiter to pick a nice bottle of white wine & he came back with a bottle from Santorini that was perfect & a great value too. The vibe is dreamy & the food doesn't disappoint. I live in the neighborhood & think this is one of the best restaurants in the East Village... No small feat!
This is a great place for meeting the girls after work! The drinks are strong and inexpensive and the tapas are delish!!!!!! Get there early enough to get a decent table.

They tried, and well, I guess that's worth something. In their defense, it apparently was the first nice day in Brooklyn of the season, and so, it was the first day they opened garden seating. Consequently, they were understaffed, and the hostess had to take our order until the waitress eventually got to us. Â When our food FINALLY arrived, it wasn't worth the wait. The French Toast was burnt, the Nova eggs were just ok, and who doesn't give you syrup when you get French toast? And don't get excited about the free mimosa - I'm not a lush, but Â it's in a kiddie cup. Just sayin' - I wasn't impressed.
ok i'm ready for the haters of this review... i think this place is a tourist trap and there's better pizza out there in brooklyn. Â that's all.

Late night dining at its best! Honestly had a great experience, Oysters Steak and a fantastic salad! I was full for days, but glad I got the chance to check it out! I can't wait for my next trip back!

Meh. I went once in 2008 (or 2009?) and I thought it was great. Worth the hype, even. Then I went twice in the past year and it was just okay. I don't know if my tastes changed or what. I have heard that the original guys behind 53rd and 6th sold it and it's under different management now, but I have no idea how valid that is since a quick google search brings up nothing. In any case I don't think it's worth the long line anymore.

I have been a Macy's customer for over 30 years and love this new addition. The view is wonderful and the food and service are just what a NYC trattoria should be. Order a few appetizers to share along with a pizza and a bottle of wine and you will not be disappointed. I have been here for both lunch and dinner and the menu and service is consistent. Try the fried calamari or meatballs as appetizers. The risotto balls were a little to mushy and not too hot so I would not have them again. The eggplant and salads are also great and very Italian. This is not a department store dining room for ladies looking for a cup of soup and half a sandwich. Macy's is a NYC institution that everyone should enjoy, not just the tourists. Go for dinner or just have a great cup of coffee and a delicious Italian pastry late at night. Delightful!

I have returned to add a well deserved update to my poor review in 2012. They have totally turned it around and I have been going there regularly. They really put love into their food and the waitress we have had on numerous occasions for brunch is wonderful. So glad this place is living up to it's potential.

I didn't know that I would experience a first at Jacob's Pickle! A first in terms of EPICLY AWFUL/NON-EXISTENT SERVICE! Well, I absolutely LOVED the food. The Honey Chicken and Pickle Biscuit was mouthwateringly juicy with a little kick from the spicy pickles. The portions are ample and I was full after about 3 bites, but I finished every single morsel. Sooo good! (It could also be because of waiting almost 2 hours for our food... see below). My friend had the chicken bacon egg and cheese biscuit, which was good, but I would go for the honey chicken over that any day. Also, a big win for the cheddar grits. 5 stars for the food and beer and cocktails! Now back to the service. Serious star and tip deduction here. Our absent-minded server disappeared for a full 90 minutes after taking our order... now you may be thinking how the hell did 90 minutes go by. Well, my friend and I hadn't seen each other for a few months and had a lot to catch up on and we weren't starving, thankfully. So imagine our surprise when we look up and check our phones and see how much time has passed. We look at the three tables around us and realize that they have all eaten and left and had new patrons sitting at them. In fact, one of those new patrons ended up getting their food before we did! No sign of our waitress still so we found a busboy who proceeded to find our waitress who then brought us the wrong order (two cheeseburgers)... she told us that's what we ordered until she actually checked her note pad and realized she had royally effed up. No apology or acknowledgement, but she just disappears again for another 20 minutes obviously putting in our order for the first time. At this point, she brings us our real order. Seconds later she leaves us our bill without an apology or anything! 3 HOURS we spent here... and not on purpose! Now, I will probably be back because that chicken biscuit is the truth and I am praying that things will be better. I just hope this is not the way they treat all of their customers.

Well what can I say that has not already been said? The RHLP is doing really sinfully good things to lobster in many ways. I have had their rolls at the Prospect Park food truck rally so I already new how frigging awesome they were, but I had the pleasure of trying the bisque and the lobster mac and cheese and I was happy. The mac and cheese I assumed would have little bits of shredded lobster throughout but dammit if I didn't pull an entire claw out of this little dish, twice at that! The bisque was equally as lobster filled and delicious. I often make lobster bisque at home but have decided it's waaaay easier to just buy it from them and attempt to pass off on my own....so ummm you will be seeing me again very soon.

Ok let me start by saying I think the food and the atmosphere here is amazing. BUT... and this is a huge but... the experience is NOT. First, even though you make a reservation days in advance do not expect it to stick. They require that YOU (not them) call before 3pm the day of the reservation (which in my opinion is sort of pointless in making) to confirm the reservation or else the CANCEL your reservation, no questions asked. And don't think about being even 10 minutes late in calling... it will be canceled period. Second, they only accept American Express or CASH. Yes cash, the thing nobody seems to carry anymore. So if you are expecting to go there with a group of friends and split the meal on credit cards, don't. It makes the process of "paying for the meal" and complete hassle. Third, the staff is, well eeeehhh. They act as if they had 3 Michelin stars?? SO before you go beware of the headaches that may ensue.

This restaurant is nestled in a beautiful neighborhood, and has outdoor seating in the back. Clean, welcoming, and pleasant, this restaurant has tasteful decor and food that makes the mouth water, as well as friendly staff. Note: This restaurant is known for its Ceviche.
