Use the Ceviche Tasting - it's a good idea if you want to try a variety of items and is presented in an amazingly beautiful manner. Also, the chips that come on the house with two sauces are excellent. The Toro con Palta is very salty and the fish tastes old. The presentation is wonderful, but I wouldn't recommend it. The Atun Blanco is creamy and delicious, with a medley of flavors. It also looks fabulous, although the flavors can be strong. The Ceviche de Pulpo is quite tasty, and the capers add a nice touch, although the dish is a little salty. The Anticuchos are juicy and bathed in a sauce that compliments the meat. It is also quite soft and comes with creamy and crispy yuca. I highly recommend this dish. The Tamalito Verde, while not green, is delicious, with flavorful pork and all kinds of other goodies. Try it - it's good. Also very good for sharing. The Salmon (entree) is fantastic. The fish is very good and the mashed potatoes it is on are creamy and delicious. The gravy however is the highlight. The Peruvian Tilapia is surrounded by a spiced and creamy sauce, and the rice it is on is very good. The best part is the crispy fish topped with salsa criolla. The Lomo Saltado has a very interesting sauce, and the meat is good, although a little bit out of my comfort zone in taste. Overall, the food is very good, although it doesn't feel very Peruvian. Also, I did feel a little disappointed by the food. The quantity is quite large, but the flavors become somewhat monotone after a few bites.

Thoroughly average experience. I had the ravioli which I found to be a bit thick, however the filling of fava beans and ricotta cheese was very tasty. My boyfriend had the duck confit which he found was quite over-seasoned, but he still ate it relatively happily. We enjoyed two cocktails, I had the mango and rum cocktail (very flavourful and delicious) and my boyfriend had a negroni, which was made well. Service was quite good in terms of being attentive to the table, however the food took a while to come out of the kitchen considering we were one of the first tables in for the day for brunch. Overall a good experience, but won't be hurrying back.
Nice Spot for date night

Seriously. This place is hilariously rude. All the talk about how awful service is really sadly true too often. (I mean, if the NYTIMES' Pete Wells HAVE TO say shit about you. I mean, Pete practically be handing out stars like candies to most restaurants dinersjournal.blogs.nytiâ€¦) Pizza is good, but come be ready to deal off the attitudes.

Totto Ramen is great. So great in fact, that there is ALWAYS a crowd of people waiting outside. The place is small and can accomodate about 20 people at a time. You can easily wait 30 mins on a random night for 2 people, or 1hour on a saturday night for a party of 3. Â I suggest coming in during off-peak hours, or dragging a friend to wait with you. BUT It is worth the wait!! Unlike most ramen, I didn't find the broth too salty, and didn't feel bloated or sick after finishing my bowl... it was just right. The char siu pork inside (and the appetizer of pork) is cooked to perfection and delicious. Â I have gotten the miso ramen both times I went here, and I love that they put a scoop of miso on top of your bowl so you can mix in however much you desire. The portions are definitely filling and toppings are abundant too! Did I mention the staff is sooo friendly? Even though there are tons of people outside, they won't rush you and always greet you with a smile. The food comes out extremely quickly! (and made right in front of you!) Minus one star because the extremely extreme spicy ramen was not that spicy!? That's unfortunate.

Eataly is a great idea but not the most put together place I've ever been. It's like a shopping mall of fine Italian foods, pastries, coffees, meats, gelatos, you name it. Its a bit overwhelming though. A great place to see for yourself.

We stopped by Mark's Burgers after dinner at Xian to taste their famous silders. Â The restaurant looks more like a bar/lounge than a burger joint. My buddies and I walked in and ordered one regular slider (cheeseburger with onions) and a bacon slider (cheeseburger with onions and bacon). Within 5 minutes, the burgers came out hot off the grill. Â After one bite, I came in my pants....these sliders are fucking great! The sliders comes out hot and fresh! Â The bun is very, very moist, the beef was so so thick it was sticking out the edges of the bun. Â The mix of the beef, grilled onions, bacon, cheese and moist bread was a perfect symphony of tastes.....so delicious. I could have eaten 10 of these! These are the best sliders ever! Yes, I want more!

Appealing ambiance in the bar area, with a wide selection of drinks -- wines, beers, and liquors. Â They even have beer sampler flights, which is a nice way to try a bunch of new beers. Â Service is professional, if not particularly chummy (then again, why would anyone expect that here?). Â There are about twenty seats at the bar itself, and about fifty at various tables around the room. Â  Drink prices are in line with what you'd expect -- ranging from slightly expensive beers to some very expensive wines and liquors. Â The food menu seemed pricey and no food was had. Convenient to the High Line, if you feel like a tipple before/after trekking it.

Brunch - It's all about the biscuits and gravy. Finger licking good. They even braise the greens that come with it. I will walk the mile that it takes to get from my apt to this restaurant for brunch just for this dish. This is the only memorable item for me on the brunch menu, but this item alone is enough to justify a four star rating.

I'm not a big fan of food carts, but this one is a rare find. Discovered this cart over the summer, been back five times, and have tried half the menu. The service is friendly and fast, and the food does not disappoint. The choices are tasty, plentiful, and priced right. Well worth the trip and the search for parking.

This place is amazing! Â The food was fabulous, the service fantastic, and best of all they treat you like on old friend dropping by for dinner. Â I felt like I was with family enjoying great food and company. Â It made my 3 days of work seem like a vacation.

there's nothing better than a metal tray stacked with pulled pork, a 1/2 rack of slow cooked ribs and a slab of pork belly that instantly melts in your mouth as it hits your tongue. Â oh man, i'm salivating just thinking about it....LOVE THY MEAT!

Great for vegetarians visiting the area. If you go with a group you have to have the same spice tolerance because you want to try everything because it is delicious. However if some want it hot and some want it light and you settle on medium you'll all be unhappy. The food itself gets 5 stars, service knocks it down 1. What could raise it 1 is if it had a price fix for groups coming. Like, everyone pays $10 and you get horrid good food for everyone. Otherwise you just argue about all the good options on the menu.
I Came here today for a Birthday Dinner... The place is Amazing ... I order the Pork chops with Collard greens the food was very Delicious ... I will come back again

Get the lychee martini: it fits quite nicely with Verlaine's loud, pumping music. (Thank me later.) Friends and I stopped in for drinks. A bouncer checked our licenses - all out-of-state, and none from the same state - then let us in. Verlaine is a decent sized lounge, but somewhat bare, making its high ceilings and long bar all-the-more obvious. A light crowd mingled amongst themselves, keeping the hub-bub to respectable levels. Unfortunately, it's crazy dark due to sparse, orange-tinted lighting. Casual light fixtures grace the front area, but nowhere else. I almost set up an event here but I'm glad I didn't; there's a time for romantic ambiance, but when night-vision goggles are needed to read the menu, that's a problem. We sat table-side after being told a server would be with us, but one never came. (When we tried to order from the bar, they sent a server over.) Service aside, the bar turns out some strong martinis - I quaffed the aforementioned Hanoi lychee martini ($8; with a welcome splash of pineapple) and sampled a coffee one. Both were pleasant, and I'm not usually into martinis. Potent drinks, good company, and no cover make a good combination. I'll be back.
The duck burger didn't taste like duck, but it was juicy enough to be enjoyable.
Honestly there's nothing really special about this place other than it's location. For after work drinks right down the street from Grand Central this is your spot.

I am back to Sik Gaek again! Thanks for my dear NYC Yelper friend for organizing!! This time of course I know that it is absolutely important to call ahead and make sure that Sannakji is available and plentiful before we make our dinner plan. Fresh Octopus ($24.99) - Watching the octopus swimming leisurely in the tank does makes me feel guilty as some of them would ended up on our table - I know they are still moving and they kind of stuck to your chopsticks but it is definitely tasted a lot better and not a horrible experience Assorted Seafood Hot Pot ($79.99) - A sight to behold! All these LIVE seafood in this boiling red broth.. I can relate to a scene from hell...lobster still alive trying to pull itself out of the hot soup...his claws still trying to grab anything near it..... - Deliciously good! With fresh veggies, noodles and of course tons of seafood and shellfish Extra Fried Rice ($4.99 each) - After we finished the leftover broth was used as a base for some fresh fried rice done right at our table! Watermelon Soju ($29.99) - A healthy option since it taste definitely more juice than Soju, but fun to share with a group... I drank 2 of those!! I will definitely come back so Sik Gaek for the Seafood Hot Pot with a few friends., so sinful and delicious experience!!

I am a restaurant enthusiast and I happen to own 5. I also won Iron Chef. What I do know if while the food was good and the service was immaculate the way whoever owns this restaurant allows the managers to run it is despicable. I had a problem with my order, rack of lamb to be cooked medium and it came out rare. No big deal someone just didn't feel the meet properly or maybe a slow burner or a cold oven. Either way quick fix, however my waiter informed a manager and he continued to sit at the table with his friends drinking in the open on the floor. Now me personally yes socializing is a part of the job however 20 minutes later and I was watching and counting and 3 drinks the manager proceeded to get up and walk downstairs not to be seen again for another hour. I understand there is a lounge downstairs but when I went down to take a peak at the rest of the decor he was again no where to be seen. I am astonished that the owners of such a well spoken of restaurant would allow this sort of non professional behavior to be conducted in their restaurant. Â Lo an behold the manager re appeared and continued to sit with his friends until me and my associates left. To our great disappointment Cafeteria was not all that we had hoped it would be. I will not be recommending the restaurant nor will my associates Â because you have to wonder if the managers on duty can be getting drunk and not care about the other tables in the restaurant what kind of a example are they setting for the rest of the working environment, and how much detail actually goes into what they do. Management aside thank you to our server for attending to our ever need and being so tentative.

One of the best dinners we had during a quick trip to NYC. My fiancee and I arrived late, at about 10:15, which was great since we were seated right away. We started off with that steakhouse classic, the iceberg wedge. This one came drizzled with a warm bacon dressing, which fused with the blue cheese to help us set a record in making a salad disappear from the table. Fantastic. She had the hanger steak with garlic butter, and I opted for the NY Strip Au Poivre. Both of us could not remember having such expertly grilled, delicious steaks. Truly, off the charts delicious. But then the sides... Pan-seared mashed potatoes: perfection. The barest hint of truffle, piping hot, with a sturdy crust that gives way to wonders within. Every potato should aspire to end up like this. Cauliflower: surprisingly light, full of great flavor. Apparently they grill the cauliflower in a mesh basket, and I'm definitely going to try this at home. It came away smoky, dry (in a good way, as opposed to soaked in brown butter or something), and balanced well with a slight drizzle of good balsamic. Really excellent. I had a red wine from the tap -- don't even know what it was, but it was good stuff. Dessert was a quickly-devoured chocolate and sea salt pot de creme. Our server was a model of professionalism, very helpful and welcoming. Next time we're in town, we'll be back for sure.

Average Italian food. I'm not quite sure why it is rated so high. It took us ten minutes to get food menus but when we were approached with menus our waiter was very nice. The pasta fagoili tasted like Campbell's soup and there was nothing spectacular about the entrees. Sub-standard...

This place is a great new addition to the bar and restaurant scene in new york city. The atmosphere, as my girlfriend said was "electric" as we walked into the bar with a party on the Mezzanine Level that we were attending and another party down stairs. Â Great music by DJ, very nice hospitable staff. We loved Paul with the Â Irish Accent, excellent bartender with a great knowledge of beers. Â I was so happy for my friend Alan, he chose this place for his party and what a party it was! it is also his "afterwork hangout" during the week with friends. It is just a pity I work so far away from the "Three Monkeys" otherwise it would be my hangout spot too. GREAT PLACE!!!!! Â Next time we go back we will check out their food menu, looks Amazing

This place deserves every ounce of praise it gets. Kind and wonderful waitstaff and amazingly delicious food. The challah bread (and consequently, the challah french toast) are legitimately unreal. Cheap prices for outstanding food.

Not the cheapest meal you can have, technically. I've spent half of the past school semester eating frozen food from Costco and that puts me at around 30 cents per meal... but these dumplings are just as good, if not better. My friend and I trekked through the frozen tundra that is currently New York City to this tiny place and it was well worth it -- I had 10 dumplings and my friend had 15+ (ugh...) -- total was under 5 dollars! The place gets ridiculously crowded (meaning...five plus people are inside) and there's not much eating space. But I'd still go out of my way for delicious pork and chive dumplings. And they aren't like the crappy soggy dumplings that most people make. Perfect amount of crispiness.

It was a very cold and windy Sunday and I was meeting 2 friends here. Ended up being the first one to arrive so I took a seat in the corner by the windows (it probably wasn't the best idea because it was the coldest by the windows). We were HUNGRY! All of us ordered the bleecker burger and scarfed it down like we hadn't eaten in days. It was just what you expected -- a very large burger and fries. Not sure if the place next door is affiliated with this place, but you had to leave the restaurant through a side door and go downstairs to get to the bathroom. There was a cool bar vibe downstairs. Both the restaurant and this downstairs area were not very crowded on a Sunday, which was nice. Our server was great, friendly, and checked in on us multiple times throughout our meal.

Now let me preface my review by saying that I am no expert on Japanese Pubs, but the food was extremely tasty and filling. I really liked the decor, and the casual atmosphere. On this night, the restaurant was filled with a diverse crowd, and even a few kids. The soups are HUGE and savory. On a cold night, like the night my group visited, the soups really hit the spot. The service could have been better: we waited 10 minutes just to place our drink order. But overall, I would say it was a good time and I would recommend it to others. I however, probably will not be back.
Fantastic all around. Â Great food, service and ambiance!

Don't even know why I'm writing this review. Â It's obviously unnecessary. As everyone else has pointed out, $1 gets you five delicious A+ dumplings, and quick. As many have also pointed out, you can buy them in bulk, for the same price, frozen. Â I live in DC and bought 100 of these bad boys to take back home. Â I've been eating delicious dumplings for months. Â Life is good.

i've definitely had better tapas but i can't complain. it could be a lot worse. had an early dinner there and it was very very empty! but i have heard that it does get crowded due to the flamenco dancing later in the evenings. i'd have to say the little chorizos are delicious

My girlfriend and I have been going to "shi shi" restaurants about once every two weeks and this was next on the list. Let me tell you that I think the hype is totally true. AWESOME SERVICE? check AWESOME FOOD? check The food was awesome. Based on everyone's recommendations, we got both the spicy duck meatballs and the wild boar belly. I liked both alot, but I have to admit that I think the wild boar belly was MUCH MUCH better. For entree's, my girlfriend got the duck breast and I got the special, the braised lamb neck in massaman thai curry. Both were amazing!!! We also got the risotto as a side, which in my opinion, was the best thing of the night!!! This place is my 2nd favorite restaurant in the city outside Ippudo now!

This place is a standard go to for me. Ive been served several times by the same waitress, and am sad to say I cannot remember her name! She has been so awesome every time, genuine and always enhances our experience at the smith. I like the menu and the selections work for me and my taste. The service is attentive and I like the atmosphere. I am a fan of this place, its a little big and not cozy but I love the look tile look and the interesting photos. Its not anything that i would plan for a special occasion, but somewhere I go regularly when meeting up with a friend or 6. I Â will continue to enjoy my experience at the smith!

So after checking in with the hostess, I was very close to leaving. Â Not only was the wait 45 minutes, the hostess was rather rude!! Â After deciding to just wait it out, we got our table in 30 minutes. Â I was super happy we did after we received our meal for EVERYTHING was cooked to perfection and the quality of the food was high. Â It was so good that I didn't care about the bad impression that I first got! Â Very excited to go back on my next trip to NYC.

The staff was pleasant, and the portions are pretty large but the food is also very pricey. I ordered the oxtail with rice and peas. It was very bland. It lacked flavor and was very oily. I'm from the islands and by no means am I expecting it to taste like my granny's oxtail, but I've been to places throughout Brooklyn where the oxtail would blow your mind with flavor. If you're from the Islands, I think you'll agree. Needless to say, I don't think I'll be going back to this island. ;-)

it was really good pizza, but considering the long wait, the fact that i walked out smelling like a mixture of olive oil and smoke and that it is so hard to get here from the city by metro, i dont know that i would recommend it as a place worth revisiting. dont get me wrong though, dom puts his heart into each pie he makes.

Very good food. Very creative and fresh. I had the veggie burger with lamb (definitely get it with the lamb if you are not vegetarian), and the FiancÃ© had the gnocchi. Gnocchi is definitely hand made and very rustic in taste. Sadly had to knock off 2 stars because of service. Don't get me wrong, everyone is VERY nice, but they all appear to be novices in the service industry. Waitress actually took my order and then ran off, forgetting to take my date's order along with mine. They just need to tone up their service skills a little and run a tighter ship. They should start with the pacing of food. Our food came out in 5 minutes. We barely had time to sip our first drinks, and as a result, did not feel the need to order a 2nd round. Generally a very nervous and confused energy coming from the wait staff. My wish for this place is that they become cool and suave with their service, making me feel like I want to spend $20 on an entree and sit and drink for awhile. It seems they are trying to be a fine dining experience in Bedtsuy, and they have the food and decor to back it up, but not the service skills.
This is basically spinach artichoke dip on a deep dish pizza. Enough said. GO GET SOME!

Love at first sight! Keep in mind, I'm a food snob. If dining by yourself, I highly recommend (my waiter's recommendation) the Argentine Pinot Noir, lamb skewers, and the asparagus with balsamic, Parmesan and a fried egg. I'll be back! Â Don't let the new building fool you - this is great food and a great experience!
Best Vietnamese sandwich in the city. It was flavorful, warm and the bread was just right. Â I had the classic. Â  With tax came out to $7.08. Â They even accept CC.
Really good breakfast spot! Lots of delicious options. Indoor and outdoor seating. I see why all the reviewers like this place.

Went here for dinner last night around 10pm, to avoid a wait. We were sat immediately and our waiter was very attentive. He was great for recommendations and suggestions. I ordered the Mac n Cheese, which was very delicious. It wasn't too salty or cheesy. The biscuit was massive and soft. The Buffalo chicken and cherry waffle was an interesting mix. I was not a big fan of the chicken and it's batter, but the waffle was amazing! Highly recommended!

Stopped in for a light meal. Â Since I am already in love with the prefix menu, we went a la carte. Â We started with the fromage plate of French cows milk cream, butter Brie, and homemade ricotta with honey and toasted almonds. Â We chased that with the tomatoes done 4 ways: Â spicy gazpacho, tomato confit, fried heirloom tomato, and a blt like you've never had. Â  We conserved some room by splitting a light but tasty entree of crispy fried wild stripped bass over spinach stuffed ravioli. Finally, we indulged in their caramel bread pudding. Â This dish is all about the sauce. They should bottle it, make it illegal and sell it on the corner. Â This caramel sauce can put an end to the world's drug problem. Â There would be peace in the streets of Mexico. Â This place is just great.

I walked past this place months ago, and I was intrigued by its hole-in-the-wall-ness and dirt-cheap prices. Â I love Mexican food, but I'm a firm believer that some food is better cheap, and Mexican definitely falls into that category. I brought my gal pals (plus one guy pal) here on a Saturday night. Â I'm always late, so when Robbie and I showed up 30 minutes after the agreed time (sorry ladies), they had just been seated. Â  Place has a great vibe, and they make the most of it's small space. Â It's covered in cool junk, AND the TV was playing Ferris Bueller's Day Off on repeat. Â This was a big A+ for my friend Ali. Â I mean, really, this is an A+ for anyone, but I digress . . . The table split guac (yum) and a few round of margs (nice 'n strong), and I grabbed chicken tostados and a plate of rice and beans. Â Food was tasty, drinks were good, and the price was right. Â There were six of us, and each of us payed $25, which included tip. Â Heck yes. The only downside? Â This is not a place to sit around and chit-chat. Â The second our plates were clean and our drinks empty, the staff started haggling us to leave. Â I get that they have tables to turn (I've been a waitress many a time myself), but I thought they could have been a bit more graceful while they were kicking us out the door. Â That being said, it wasn't enough to turn me away from this place. Â It's a gem, and I'll be back.

if you love beer and bacon, then you need to go here...the food menu is amazing...haven't seen it anywhere else...the staff is attentive and friendly too...i had my birthday get-together there and everyone enjoyed themselves...the Bacon is delish...i recommend getting the Beer & Bacon Flight...worth stopping by at any time...

I love Zen Vegetarian House. Â My favorite appetizer is the chikn nuggets. They are crispy beyond perfection. Â My favorite meals are the basil chikn, sesame chikn and mango chikn. What I like about Zen is the workers are very nice to me. They Â always smile and engage in small talk even though they don't speak good English. They are very polite they know about good customer service. I feel good Â spending my money there. Kudos to you Zen. I'm a satisfied customer.
Delicious food, great service, and a perfect place to dine al fresco. Will definitely return. Â The heirloom tomato salad was so good that I wanted to lick the plate.

I don't understand why this place is rated so high. I came here with my boyfriend for dinner the other night and it was just terrible. At first when we walked in and the waitress didn't know where to sit us, cause its such a tiny place but whatevez. There was this very loud group of people sitting right next to us and at one point the music, the noise level just gave me a headache. Moving on to the service, at first it was decent but later they didn't even acknowledge us. I tried getting their attention but I got ignored twice. It took them 15 minutes to replace my fallen spoon. We went in there with a groupon and when we asked for our check, our waitress gave us an attitude. I don't know about you but I like my server to be polite, not rude. The food was okay, not mind blowing or anything. Definitely had better italian food than theirs. First few bites were pretty good but after awhile it was just really blah and lack of flavor. Not to mention we waited 30 minutes to get that food. However their pecan pie was really good, a bit sweet but good. I guess they're just known for their brunch, but after my experience here I don't think I would come back Â to try it

Came for lunch and although it was really good, I wasn't wowed. Â Don't get me wrong, everything was fresh and beautifully prepared. Â I'll do the the omakase for dinner next time... Love that they don't accept tips though. :)

Translated as the Creole Corner, this Cuban joint is a hidden gem that many would not bother to look twice at. From the outside, this place is as formidable as the neighboring storefronts. It gets a bit cozier inside, with ~20 tables all tightly squeezed together. I ordered the Ropa Vieja ($13.95), Shredded Beef in Tomato Sauce, with choice of two sides. The shredded beef in tomato sauce was outstanding, tender shredded beef in a sweet and savory tomato sauce. Don't let the portions fool you, as they can be quite filling, on top of the two sides. My first side was the maduros, which consisted of 5 fat slices of fried sweet plantains, soft on the inside and caramelized with a slight crispness on the outside. My second side was the yuca con mojo (cassava with garlic). The soft yuca is sort of in-between a soft potato and taro, with what I would consider requires an acquired taste, slightly on the bland side except for the hint of garlic flavor. Other dishes I was able to try was the: - Rabo Encendido (sauteed ox tail in tomato sauce) which is Wednesday's special. Boy oh boy, three very sizable pieces of delicious fatty and tender ox tail that fell off the bone with a flick of the fork. - 1/2 Chicken Rincon Criollo, which I had high hopes but was met with pure disappointment. The chicken was slightly dry, and the crispy skin had little flavor. I would avoid ordering this dish. - Pork Chops w/ minced garlic and onions - The pork was extra crispy, almost reminding me of lechon. It was very tasty though ever so slightly on the salty side. Pork eaters, you won't be disappointed. - Side: French fries which were dry and tasteless. I ask myself how they could mess up such a simple side. Season with a little salt, dry the potato slices a little bit more before throwing in the deep fryer, and you'll have one tasty and crispy fry. - If you're looking for something indigenous to drink, try the JupiÃ±a, pineapple soda. The only downside to this place is that service can be quite poor, erring to almost rude. When we were trying to understand the items on the menu and asked the waiter a few questions, he seemed to be a bit agitated and impatient. Also, he never came by once to check up on us or refill our glasses. Twice we had to get his attention, once for drinks and a second time for the bill. On the bright side, we took our time eating and hanging out here, and they never seemed to have a problem with that, which is most likely because we came on a Wednesday night and only 2-3 tables were occupied.

Q: What can I get for $5? A. Chicken & Rice from the Halal Cart B. 20 piece Chicken Nuggets from McDonalds C. Footlong sub from Subway D. 5 Dollar slices at the Pizza Place E. All of the above. The answer is E, but your half right.... another answer is a LYCHEE MARTINI !!!! Times are tough these days. Some happy hour specials are good, but you are limited to what you can get. The quality isn't that good either at times, but Verlaine solves that problem. The TASTY Lychee Martinis will only cost you $5 a pop before 10pm. This is definitely a place to get some drinks before going out on the Lower East Side. The place can be a bit tight at times, but it's DEFINITELY worth it!!!
Great spot and great food. Â Absolute best meatball ciabatta in the city. Â Salads are also amazing and some really healthy options.

oh sooo good. Got the 50/50 (beef brisket and pulled pork) sandwich with a side of mac n cheese and mashed potatoes. As someone who loves mixing food together this was heaven. Not only was everything individually amazing but the mac n cheese with the mashed potatoes, and the mashed potatoes on the sandwich with pork and brisket...a true food orgy. The Mac n Cheese.. DELICIOUS, the Mashed Potatoes...DELICIOUS, my 50/50 sandwich...DE-LI-CIOUS. Their homemade sodas/root beer with cane sugar is also (in case you haven't guessed by now) VERY ENJOYABLE...haha I bet you thought I was going to say delicious but serious it's really good.

Though I really like the food at Sweet Afton's, I think the patrons and service could be improved. The only time I received decent service here is when I've come with my friends who are regulars at SA, thus chummy with the staff. Otherwise, forget it. I came here once between brunch and dinner and had to wait 10 minutes until the waitress decided to tell us that. On top of that, the crowd here is hipster, and as I am not, prefer not to surround myself with them ;) That being said, the food and drinks are good and the interior of the bar is dead sexy. Both count for a lot in my book, so ultimately I have to recommend SA for both. It's a terrific date spot and you will leave with a delicious meal in your belly. Their signature "pickle back" shot is worth trying - a shot of whiskey, followed by a shot of dill pickle juice. Sounds awful, but man is it tasty! Also, their mac and cheese is gourmet and earth-shatteringly yummy. It sucks for big groups, as there is only one table that can accomodate more than 5. So, my recommendation is go when it is slow so you can get the best service and best seats. Unless you like crowds and hipsters, in which case, go on the weekend.

We walked away ambivalent as it felt like this place was trying a little too hard. Â It's like when you meet people for the first time and he/she is wearing too much perfume/cologne, has on too much make-up (either sex applies), overly manicured eyebrows, too much Botox around the pouty lips, or too much silicone, signaling with overly-branded clothes, etc. Feeling like an old fart bitching about how loud it is in here, but it's impossible to have a conversation as the music is aggressively, almost obnoxiously loud. Â And with everybody yelling to try to impress their dates with useless information about their lives, the volume just ratchets higher. We tried a bunch of dishes - probably too many...most of the food felt overly flavored and the most memorable part was the more subtle herby lentil salad. Â We also had the marinated white anchovies, twice cooked duck, the pappardelle, and Brussels sprouts. Â Once every now and then you get sick of eating as the flavors are too heavy and you hit the wall. Â We hit that after two bites of the entrees and zombie walked thru the rest of it. The desserts were well presented but ultimately not that interesting. We'll give this place points for service and effort but not sure if we're coming back any time soon...sorry.

Really nice place with a very aesthetically pleasing interior as mentioned by several others. The brunch menu is pretty balanced and includes something for everyone. The portions themselves are actually of a very good size, so well worth the price! Brunch cocktails are fairly priced and aren't too overpowering. Overall, a very cozy atmosphere with some delicious brunch options. Plenty of seating too for larger groups - maybe consider a reservation though to be safe.

I wish they had Luke's on the west coast! But sadly lobster is not as easily accessible :( I had the LOBSTER ROLLl and it was delicious! I liked that they wrote on the menu that you can ask for your roll without butter, mayo and/or spices. I'm sure the butter and mayo would've tasted amazing on the roll, but I got mine without the two because I generally like lighter, fresher flavors rather than rich and buttery. There was a generous portion of lobster served on a warm, toasted bun. SO GOOD. I like strong flavors so I could've used more spices on mine though. The Lobster Roll on its own was $15 ($16.33 including tax), which comes out to be a pricey lunch given the size of the roll, but definitely worth the indulgence every now and then. They also have stamp cards! Too bad I don't live in NYC :(

One frigid winter evening my friend Camila and I were on our way to meet my friend Alex for some dancing at "The Rub" at Southpaw. 11pm and freezing the line is around the block and we weren't about to wait two hours in the cold to get in. We opted for drinks and by Alex's suggestion, ended up at Cafe Steinhoff. Dimly lit with a old tavern feel. Not dingy, musty or smelly at all, the space is divided in two by a wooden floor divider with glass panels on top. 3/4 of the space is separated for tables while the other 1/4 is for the extensive bar that spans the entire length of the restaurant. When we were seated we asked our very knowledgeable server what their best fruity drink on the menu was. I cannot remember what the name of the drink he gave me was but I do remember that it was strong. I was very pleased :). He also offered us a menu and though skeptical because I had never had Austrian food before, Alex assured me it was excellent. I chose the Chicken Paprika sandwich which was a chicken cutlet on a very flat roll (I liked that) with a delicious mini salad on the side. I can even remember the flavor now. Cafe Steinhof is usually packed on weekends and they don't take reservations. First come first serve. However, late night is a breeze in terms of getting a table. I'm planning to go here with my sister tomorrow night. Hopefully it wont be crowded.

4.5 stars. Went with my brother and sister after a day of shopping in Williamsburg. Get the shrimp Â with garlic and lemongrass and the linguine. Phenomenonal. We also had the duck noodles and baby calamari, which were good but not not quite as good as the shrimp or the linguine. Service was very good (5 stars). Would recommend. The only reason I'm not giving 5 stars is the lack of seating. Only one table the rest of the sitting is bar seating, albeit classy bar seating. Which is fine for 2 people, but more than 2 is a little awkward. But I would definitely recommend this place to people.

Came for restaurant week lunch and went with the $35 menu option. Started with the Insalata di capresi which was delicious but tiny. Chose the malfatti for my entree. The pork was tender and flavorful but I thought the sauce was too salty. Got the panna cotta dessert. Probably one of the best I've ever had. Creamy but light! Overall very good but portions too small
Nice decor, great quality food. Â Menu and service are very well done. Â The drinks are done right, good date spot
Best pizza I ever had in my life. Everytime im in NYC I make a big effort to go.. light flavorful pizza..

came here w/ some friends as other options nearby were completely full and booked incredibly happy it worked out that way i am a big fan of thin crust / artisanal / coal oven pizzas - Luzzo's is my favorite in the city - they also do a truffle pate pizza called Tartufata so when i saw a Tartufata on this menu, i jumped on it, albeit with cautious expectations it was absolutely phenomenal! the combination of everything, and the meat as well (which Luzzo's does not do) - i would say, this may actually be better best pizza in the slope? maybe, but i need to try all the others as well to confirm :)

Good pork and chives dumplings for the price ... for $1 you get 5 dumplings, steamed or fried your pick. Tiny teeny place with quite a long line at around 4 pm on a weekday. While I was there, there were a couple kids lining up ahead of me. There was one Chinese man who has no manners whatsoever, trying to cut ahead of me and the kids in front of me. He pushed in between two kids in front of me, waving $2 and demanding dumplings. Thankfully the owner served the two kids first, despite the obnoxious guy's attempt to get his attention. The man brazenly cut ahead of me though, which pissed me off, but since I am 2nd generation Asian who doesn't speak Mandarin Chinese, I couldn't tell him to get in line. Anyways, on to the dumpling itself. It was just OK. I like the thin dumpling skin, but I feel like they cook too much dumplings on the stove at one time the skin doesn't get crisp enough. There were too many dumplings stacked up close, sometimes on top of one another, that I am afraid they got steamed and the skin won't get crisp. If you happen to be around the neighborhood and hungry for some cheap snack, then by all means stop by. If you plan to make a trip here, I think it's not worth it.

The food and service were exceptional. The chicken rillette was exquisite along with the presentation. We ordered a variety of entrees from the fish and chips, Beef Wellington and the duck, everything was prepared so perfect. We truly enjoyed this dining experience. Â It's conveniently located by a couple of train stops. Put this on your list of places to go in Brooklyn. You will not be disappointed!

I came here for dinner and let me just say... their yuca bread (contains yuca and cheese) is freaking delicious. Â They come warm and when you bite into it, it's soft and chewy... perfect. I ordered the Vaca Frita Al Caballo (skirt steak, latin pork fried rice, fried egg, and avocado) Â The fried egg covered half my skirt steak and the over half had some type of sauce on it. Â The sauce paired really well with the skirt steak but sadly, on the half that wasn't covered, the steak was a little on the dry side. Â I didn't care too much for the pork fried rice and my fried egg was a little cold. Â Overall, it was an okay dish but I would order something else the next time I come here. Â  The sangria was also good, can't wait to come here for brunch, heh-looo unlimited sangria!

We had their guacamole and chips and the guac was really geat! Â The drinks were very unique and strong. Â The bartender that made the drinks was innovative. Â Great atmosphere and great service. Definently recommend this place for anyone looking for a good place to hang out and want some great Mexican drinks and food

With recommendations from a friend, the BF & I had Saturday night supper.. at Supper. Along with the very generous complimentary portion of country bread & white bean dip, we started with two appetizers to share: Baby veal meatballs - Yummy balls of meat, indeed! Â Don't forget to save some bread for that sauce! Grilled octopus - SKIP! Â Although I refer to myself as a Seafood Whore, these sea creatures were way too rubbery for my liking. For dinner, we each ordered the same pasta dish: The Timely Priest Stranglers. Â This was a perfect bowl of comforting pasta - simplicity done right at its best! Â I'm day dreaming of the beautiful matrimony of "Dad's Sunday Marinara sauce" & soft Ricotta cheese. Â Please note that the pasta portions are large - I could barely finish half! Â  And finally, we ended our carbo-loaded meal with their Tiramisu. Â Supper makes a damn good one too. Also, if you have a chance to walk around, the restaurant venue is huge! Â I discovered at least three separate seating areas on my way to the restroom (good spot for large groups?). Â All in all, I was super smitten with our meal and would definitely come back for a big bowl of comforting pasta & tiramisu.

I love coming here as this is one of a few "non-uniform" Thai restaurants in the city. Thai restaurants are everywhere but nothing outstanding like Pure Thai! I've tried 3 noodle dishes : Tom Yum Sukhothai, duck soup and yellow dried noodle. All of them taste very original. I am Â a picky Thai girl who loves Thai noodle (not just Pad Thai) and noodle are something I can eat everyday in Thailand. All I can say is Pure Thai not only cares about the soup or the taste but they do care the quality of each noodle type for your option. The yellow noodle here has just perfect thickness like "thin spaghetti" and is cooked al dente which remains the stickiness in the texture. I love the fact that they care to make their own noodle like you can get Â from the stands in Thailand, not just be too easy by going to Chinatown and get the "very very thin" yellow noodle like you can find from Mee or Big Wong. The thin white rice noodle here is superb. It has a special quality that we call "sticky and tender". Even in Thailand not every noodle place would care to get sticky and tender noodle because they only think nice flavor soup is more important. For me, noodle also plays a big role! I also love their papaya salad as it's very fresh and crispy plus not too sweet! I would recommend you add raw blue crab for extra $2......yum yum.. Don't forget to get concentrate Thai Iced Tea or Iced Coffee to go along with your food. The decoration here is very retro. They tried to make you feel like Thailand back to 50-60 years ago. Pure Thai has an excellent business strategy and is a good example for a successful Thai restaurant that thinks out of the box.

Today, my friends and I wanted something new for lunch. And since we were so we were so sick of regular burgers, we went on yelp to see what was around. I was surprised to see Ruby's as a highly rated place because I've always walked past there on my way home. So we thought, why not give it a try. Everyone, or at least most, recommended the Bronte Burger and as a meat lover, I LOVED IT. It was a burger that had sweet chili in it which made it so sweet and juicy, just what I was looking for. And the burger didn't come on a regular burger bun. It came in ciabotta and I thought it was a great twist to the burger. The restaurant was really small. Like tiny. And if you some of the other reviews, it's true. But after my first time going there today with 3 other friends, I thought that it was the ideal spot for small, closer gatherings with friends and maybe for a date. The service was good. When I was there, there was one waiter, waiting on all the tables but it wasn't too bad since the place is tiny. The wait for the food was a little long, I felt. It's probably not normally like this because they had a huge take out order. But it was totally worth it. I will definitely go back. Hopefully soon. Lol. Seriously, go and eat at Ruby's! It's To die for and I've never had Australian food like this.

The best ramen I have tried in nyc. When we arrived, they told us it would be a 40 minute wait. However, 5 minutes later they called our name. We were lucky, and we ordered the Chicken Hirata Bun for an appetizer. It was delicious. A soft bun with chicken in a flavorful sauce. For our main course, I ordered Akamaru Modern Ramen, someone else in my party ordered Wasabi Shoyu Ramen, and someone else ordered the Classic Ramen. The Akamaru Ramen was amazing. The broth was hot and flavorful, and the noodles were springy. All the toppings they included were great, and I would even suggest adding an egg on top. The classic also had a great broth and delicous noodles. The Wasabi Shoyu wasn't bad, Â it I didn't love the broth and I wouldn't order it. Finally, for desert, we ordered the Green Tea Creme Brulee. It had green tea under the sugar crust as well as green tea ice cream above it! A nice way to finish a great meal. I will definitely come back here.

Went there earlier with friends and although small, the food was really good. I got the lamb curry sandwhich, spicy, and it was actually spicy! Being Caribbean, it's very disappointing when foods say spicy and they aren't (which happens too frequently) so I was impressed by the lunch in the sandwhich. Very small so wouldn't recommend planning on getting a table, but worth it. Plus lunch special comes with free drink and snack for like a buck more.

I live on the corner from this place. First of all, I have to give kudos to the soup..its all about the oxtail soup OMG its very authentic and delicious...always hot and fresh and yummy. The cheesesteak empanada is pretty delicious also... plantain chips with guacomole I give a thumbs up too! The downside is that they are impatient, rude and always in a rush in that place. Â You are not treated very nicely to be honest and even the owner is nasty sometimes no matter how nicely you ask for things lol. Â I asked her once if she could just put a little more juice in the soup (which i get often) instead of so much plantain which takes up most of the soup and she got nasty and me being me, just said ok no problem! I still get the soup there even though Im now vegetarian I cheat and just take out the oxtail. Â  If this place had nicer people working in it I would give it 4 stars but the service and attitude is in serious need of improvement!

Can I give this place 3.5 stars? Â Went to this place on a Friday mid-afternoon because otherwise, we would not have been able to get in there at all. Â This place is a little too popular for it's own good. Â Not that it's a bad thing but for the hype, thought it could have been better. Â Known for their ramen, we both had their ramen and while the broth was really good, didn't think it was anything special. Â The noodles you can find at basically any setagaya restaurant on the St. Mark's strip, though. Â For a big eater like me, I hoped they would have had bigger portions but twas not to be. Â We also ordered the pork buns which was a bbq'ed thick slab bacon. Â They were pretty decent compared to Momofuku but for the price, it was worth it. Â In the end, if you're not hungry, then yes, go here because by the time you get a table, you will. Â Just don't hope for a huge serving and you won't be disappointed.

Have had most of the food on the menu and have yet to be disappointed, I live around the corner. Beer and cocktails (made on order) seem to be just as well thought out. Wine list is nice too although sometimes I'm in the mood for European wine, which has not been an option. Get there at opening for brunch, if the dinning room is too loud, stay in the bar area, same menu. Fried chicken dinners on Sunday and Monday nights are very much worth it. Staff is friendly and seem to be happy to be there.

Come early and stay late. The cocktails are great and fairly priced, especially for the quality, but the steal is the jalapeno infused tequila and a sol for $6. I expect this place to get better and better going forward, as they're not totally done with the menu or interior but there's no reason to wait on going to the coolest new place in brooklyn.
Great wine pours. Glasses are better value than bottles. Staff have fun with patrons which is good. The tapas are fine, nice even. Not tapas bar amazing but the wine makes up for it totally!!

Recently went early on a Saturday night, first time, with my son, who is moving to Madrid for a fall semester and was ready to taste some different foods. Â We loved it! Â A bottle of Rosada Rioja and 7 small plates of heaven, including duck hearts w pickled peppers, tomato sauce and freshly grated horseradish, crispy pork belly, bone marrow and salad of watermelon, tomato and aged goat cheese. Â Service efficient. Â John Besh came in while we were there! (celebrity NOLA chef)

VERY welcoming. When I made the reservation I mentioned that it was our anniversary, and not only they acknowledged both at the entrance and once seated at our table, but they also offered a glass of sparkling wine each. Very sweet. The place is cool, with wonderfully lit rooms by candles. Beautiful high ceiling. Exposed brick walls everywhere. Food: Gd but not great. Nothing hit me as exceptional. Kangaroo: just ok. Not raving about it. Lamb belly: very good. Pork tenderloin and belly: Delicious, but very small portion. Duck: Not warm enough and completely rare (had trouble cutting it). Tasteless. Dessert sample (3): just ok.

Not a bad place but not very impressive for the price. My boyfriend and I started with sangrias, one rose, one white. Both tasted like fruit punch with apple slices in it. I understand fans of sangria like to mask the alcohol taste with fruit... but there was absolutely no kick to these drinks! Our waiter was veryyyy impersonal. Any questions we posed to him, he would answer quickly and shortly. We asked for recommendations since the menu was very long and overwhelming, he basically read off 3 or 4 dishes without really selling it to us. We ended up ordering 5 tapas and 1 dessert which was the perfect amount. My favorite dish was the patatas bravas, a simple dish of fried potatoes in a spicy sauce. Eat these quick or they'll lose their crispness, the quality that makes this dish shine. The scallop ceviche was also good but wasn't impressive because you can really get this dish, or something with a similar flavor profile, at many other restaurants. The beet and strawberry salad was yummy but overpriced for the small portion size. The beef tartare with fried quail egg was a tad too salty for me as were the lamb skewers with salsa verde. For dessert, we had the churros with hot chocolate. Tasty but the churro batter was a bit too thick for my liking. Oh, how I miss the churros from XOCO in Chicago.... Altogether, the meal cost about $100 but we both thought we could have spent the same amount elsewhere for a more impressive and satisfying meal.

Took my fiance here for his birthday. It was both our first time, decided to get a cheese platter and a few glasses of wine. The menu was a little confusing but the waitresswas very helpful. We then had amazing gelato, and bought some food to take home with us. Very different type of atmosphere, would def. go again.

Worst pizza EVER!! I should have gotten a clue when they told me they don't have garlic bread. What kind of italian pizza place doesn't have garlic bread?? First, the pizza arrived cold. The pizza was soft and flimsy with cheese sporadically placed on top. Yes, the whole slice was not covered in cheese. I actually considered pulling out a slice cheese from my fridge and putting it on top of the slice. We also ordered a house salad..... I am not even going to get into that! I cannot believe this place has four stars.
amazing food. is actually authentic and the flavors are all really well balanced. decorated well but super tiny in size. expect to wait to sit.
Price hike! It's no longer $1 for 4 dumplings. It's now $1.25 for 4 fried or $3.00 for 8 boiled.
This place takes brunch food to a whole new level. We went here with a group of about 15 friends and each and every person loved it. If you are looking for THE brunch spot in NY, look no further!

My friends' and my favorite place to get brunch in Williamsburg. Â We always order the eggs benedict because it always come out perfectly. Â The roasted potatoes and salad that come on the side are to die for. Â The decor is cute, and the waitstaff are friendly and attentive-- and on more than one occasion our table has gotten a free scone. Â Prices definitely reasonable (for Williamsburg). Â Love this place!

Such a tasty experience without pretense. Â Comfort food at an elevated level. Â The JW Chicken was incredibly moist and flavorful. Â The patate dish was decadent. Â Must get the recipe for the shaved cauliflower salad. Â The desserts were elegant and far from the typically cloying fare. Staff was welcoming and helpful. Â A must go restaurant.

Great tapas, very reasonably priced. The garlic shrimp & chorizo w onions was among the best I've ever had. Seafood paella was great too but a bit on the fishy side. The skirt steak could be sliced a bit thinner. Overall very pleased with the food and service. Red sangria tops off a great experience.

This is one of my favorite new places in my neighborhood. Great prices, great food and great proximity if you live in the area. I'm giving it three stars because they do not accept credit cards. If they did, four stars easy. I'll be back, though!

Japanese BBQ. Who knew? Everybody knows that Japanese cuisine offers sushi and ramen but that doesn't mean they would lack in the art of bbq. While I appreciate their half off happy hour specials - it is still quite expensive if ordering just meat. I've been here twice and had all of their bbq meats - the best one by far is definitely the kobe style bistro harami. After a few seconds on the grill you can taste all of the intricate marinade on that beef. A hint of salty, a hint of sweet and just the right amount of tenderness goes a long way. A lot of the other meat dishes, even though they are around $3-5 they don't really give you a lot of meat. You would almost always order more than 1 plate of a favorite dish just to satisfy your hunger. I always order the sukiyaki bibimbap as a rice dish to accompany the meaty dishes as well because frankly just the meat alone is never enough. I think one of the best things are their desserts. I tried their green tea ice cream, green tea crepe, the chocolate lava cake, and the banana caramel cheesecake "xango". Depending on what kind of dessert you like - i think their selection caters to all different types of dessert lovers. If you like green tea the crepe is definitely a home runner. It is better than Megu's green tea crepe but I always feel as though there is something missing - probably an ice cream accompaniment. The crepe is excellently made with the thinnest of the crepe layered between the mousse. The first time I went they actually ran out of the crepe which was super disappointing. Luckily the second time I came they had it. If I were to come back it would definitely be my first choice of dessert. The chocolate lava cake misses one huge component - a fudge center. If it had a warm fudge center it would escalate to a favorite dessert for me. Even with the vanilla ice cream side it doesn't do enough to wow my palate. The banana caramel cheesecake comes to a close second. There is something about fried cheesecake and banana that is so hard to say no to. It may come off as a tad bit too sweet but with the crunchy exterior and a little bit of vanilla ice cream it's all worth it. It is definitely a dessert you should share with your friends/date and not something you can finish by yourself (not for fear of getting type 2 diabetes). Because of the close proximity to Port Authority I see myself visiting this location close during happy hour in the near future. It is definitely not a place I would want to go after happy hour since their prices are a bit too expensive for bbq. ~happy eatings!

Why Come Here? Fantastic, roatating selection of microbrews and oysters, casual setting Upstate is an example of a simple concept executed perfectly. The focus, as the name implies, is on a rotating selection of craft beers and oysters. In fact, they don't even have a freezer which means the oysters selection often changes daily. The beers also change frequently among unusual varieties of brews that will give even the most seasoned connessieurs something new to try each time. Throw in the casual setting and friendly service and I could easily come here once or twice a week. However, it would be a shame to miss out on the full menu which also varies depending what's fresh from the sea. While I found everything to be enjoyable, if the house cured salmon is on the menu it's an absolute must order (review below). Â My non-oyster picks are below and I'll add any new dishes I try to my DishEnvy page. House Cured Salmon: Â This is the best cured salmon I've had outside of Norway - it literally melts in your mouth and doesn't let the smoke and salt overpower the fish. Get it! Calamari Salad: Â This dish has a strong char flavor even though the calamari don't look like they've been grilled. The kale also holds up nicely to the squid.

I think this place is cool mostly because the psychic out front is REAL! I saw her giving a consultation to someone. Now if that someone was just drunk and she was faking it...I don't want to know. Let me live thinking EO has hired a professional just for decorum. I came here with some coworkers after dinner at EN Japanese. The place is TINY and it's rare to find seating. The ambiance is really nothing special once you get past the psychic. The drinks were stiff but not memorable. But for being in W Village and serving up cocktails without an air of superiority in such an atmosphere is actually commendable. Definitely a worthwhile stop on a speakeasy crawl, but probably not somewhere I'd show up to for another reason.

Loved Dos Toros the minute it moved in, Â but since it has gotten busier and it has received more press, the quality seems to be deteriorating substantially. Tonight my husband and I each got a burrito. Both were inedible due to an obscene amount of hot sauce. Last time the guacamole was bad and the chips were stale. And the time before that, the salsa didn't taste as fresh as usual. Not to mention, the staff, which we initially found relaxed and chill seem to have new chips on their shoulders. We understand the stress of serving a seemingly endless line, but please don't act like you are doing us a favor by taking our money. Love their emphasis on sustainability and local ingredients and I hope their business to continues to grow, but if the quality and the service keep slipping, we will be satisfying our taco and burrito cravings elsewhere.
Lots of food for $10; awesome flavor. Â Definitely worth eating here, but if you're not taking the food to go, it would be best to go during off hours as there are only like 3 places to sit inside.

Sangria was good...and strong from what I recall. Â Of course we started with other sangria prior to the pitchers we had here. Â We had the carnitas mixtas and the starter sampler platter. Â I feel like we also had a variety of empanadas, too. Â Food was decent, but salty from what I recall. Â And, there was a TON left over. Â I took it home and ended up disposing of most of it. Â Ate the rice and beans though. Â Ha.
Very nice setting and very good italian food. I ordered a veal dish but I think the move would have been risotto or pasta.

Been back two additional times, and Cuba did not disappoint. What's wrong with you? Go there! Â (But make reservations or be prepared to wait at the very small, very crowded bar) I've since tried the red sangria, and it's nice and strong, without being too sweet or cloying.
This place makes me have flash backs to living in Beijing for 6 months. It is THAT GOOD (or bad?) Spot on dumpling/noodles at a super affordable price. I go once a week.

My first time at the Meatball Shop was quite the experience and it kept me coming back for more! My first visit happened to be when they switched to a new system- so our order never went through. However, the manager came out to apologize and took care of us while we waited for our meal- great service. The food itself- I had the Meatball Sandwich and some sliders that were shared. My favorite were the pork meatballs with Pesto- AMAZING! I tried the others as well, but these were definitely the juiciest and most well seasoned. Vegetarians, don't fret, they take care of you too! I've brought a few veggie friends here and they have raved about how amazing their vegetarian meatballs are- and I've had them as well, so I can safely say you won't be disappointed If you're in a drinking mood- try the Sangria- it is delicious! Oh and their menu's are super simple, however, not conventional. Make sure to use the markers on your table and select what you want- from the protein to the cheese and the type of sauce- it's a fun process! Enjoy!
Very disappointing meal and service. Maybe I expected too much. Check your bill before you pay!

The ricotta and truffle raviolis!!! Â  That's all I need to say. Â Really enjoyed the whole meal, but I'm still thinking about that dish days later....wanting to go back for it. Â First time in a long time I said "wow" after a dish.

OH MY!! This is one of those places that make go UHMMM... So from the outside you could tell it was very crowed, sure enough it really was. So while you wait they take you to a next door bar with a GREAT wine selection and your yummiest cheese and spanish ham, yum yum. When we finally got called for a table, we sat at the bar, cuz it was pretty much what they had. However everything that we try that night was worth remembering. The scallops where just amazing, the quail to dye for and did I mention the wine was awesome!! So way the 4 starts instead of 5? Well it's a very small place and to have waited and still sit a the bar was a little turn off. Overall its a must do!
Got lucky to get a seat at the bar on a Sunday at 12pm. I have to say the Vanilla Bean French Toast was the best french toast I have ever had and the Lobster Benny was quite good as well.

Hands down a great place to get eat a bit of the Mediterranean. Â Food is inexpensive and the fact that is a BYOB is an added bonus since I like to pair my wines with my food. Â Great food, great service...a highlight is the fact that the owner does the rounds to make sure everyone is enjoying their food. Â Will definitely go back for as long as it remains as good as the first time I had ate there. Â Job well done, keep it up....

I want so badly to give Degustation 5 stars but the service simply did them in on the night of my dining experience. As almost every review states, the 10 course tasting menu is extremely experimental and can produce both amazing and slightly off putting dishes. I guess that's the only true way to keep it fresh is to experiment and I appreciate that. The atmosphere is interesting but the narrow walkways behind the tables can be a bit of a pain if the waiters need to grab anything behind you. Add that to the fact that we had two separate 25-30 minute waits with no courses and we were a bit thrown off. Luckily the food was delicious enough and the wine was flowing at just the right frequency to keep me content. Absolute stars of the night were the torija dessert, a brussel sprout dish with seaweed puree, and a sunchoke soup with uni and apple. Can't wait to try this place again so I can bump it to 5 stars. Foodies will be flocking here for years to come!

The place is beautiful. Good food. Dress code is smart casual I would say but if you were dressy you would fit in very well too. Lots of room to sit at the bar as well as cozy booths. Service was good, attentive but not too much. Went here for dinner and drinks menu is simple yet good. Wholesome food. Meatballs were superb, calamari great, nachos huge! Only reason for four stars is the music didn't really fit the scene and the volume crept up and up so we couldn't really chat towards the end of the night. Food was slightly pricey for what it was, however still good and worth it for the setting. In a touristy area but managed to feel tucked away, whilst still remaining busy and lively. We loved it and will be back with visitors. The ceilings alone are worth stopping by for a look.

Our family decided to separate to shop the streets of Chinatown. Of course I decide to instead search for this place. I had to try it after reading all these reviews. I walked in the hot hot sun to arrive at this little hole in the wall. I decided to order the boiled shrimp dumplings ($4 for 8),boiled vegetable dumplings ($3.5 for 8), and the sesame pancake ($1) The dumplings were pretty good. Enjoyed the shrimp more than the vegetable, which was mostly cabbage. Thought those had a little odd aftertaste, but liked that they had a little kick. I liked how they have the boiled and pan fried options, because I definitely prefer to not have greasy dumplings. Thought there was a good amount of filling, but goodness way too much wrapper, so as guilty as I felt, I didn't eat the entire outside But OMG, the sesame pancake.... So good and to think I almost didn't order it. Â Only $1, I could eat this everyday. My belly might not appreciate it, but my tastebuds would. Again, greasy fried dough, but hey, I'm only on vacation for a couple more days. It was crunchy on the outside and oh so chewy on the inside. It was huge and I ate it all! Couldn't stop myself...best sesame pancake So, I would give the dumplings 3 stars, but the sesame pancake is definitely 5

perfect dinner after a long weekend - i imagined a steak would be the perfect complement to a relaxing evening, and i was right. Â decor is fantastic - exposed brick, wood floors, scalloped wood ceiling, buzzsaw blades forming bases for the ceiling lamps, and a good mix of Yes, Santana, Stones, Curtis Mayfield and others on the stereo. started with a glass of Stillwater Farmhouse Ale, a biting beer with a sweet edge. Â loved it. Â my partner had the Blond, which boasted a crisp citrus flavor. Â next, we split the avocado/shrimp salad. Â nicely cooked and chilled baby shrimp in a lime and maybe chive light cream sauce over a halved avocado, with was just warm. Â the mix of the warm avocado flesh with the cold, vinegar/citrus sharp shrimp went well together. Â maybe a little more for $10, but a good way to start. dinner we split the butcher steak and pork chop. Â the butcher steak, medium rare, was served precut into bite-size portions topped with garlic. Â 4 star steak - just soft, delicious and the garlic just made it pop. Â the porkchop was 5 stars, undoubtedly one of the best porkchops ive ever eaten. Â and this rating, regardless that it came medium ( we asked medium rare). Â everything about that porkchop screamed perfection - perfect consistency, umami tingling sauce - i gnawed the bone clean. Â  we also split the pan fried mashed potatoes as a side - a not-too-greasy, crunchy and light snack. Â one side definitely enough for 2 people. finished up with the pear bread pudding with raspberry sauce. Â moist, fruity sweet with a great crunchy topping. a great dining experience - will definitely return. Â 4 stars all around, with a 5 star porkchop.

I would definitely recommend the comatose with extra bacon and SHARE it. With the amounts of extra toppings and sauce poured on top of such an innocent potato, you've got yourself a snack that will hold up for pretty much the rest of the day.

City oasis in Brooklyn? Walking in here you would never think it was a restaurant in Brooklyn. The front outdoor space is very pretty with lots of garden decor. They have music outdoors and it's a perfect place for sipping a coffee while working. Service was great and can't wait to come back to try the food!

WOWIE!!! Â I was extremly impressed with this cute little place. After a long day at the Brooklyn Museum we were hungry and as you may know there are not many restaurant options in this area, I did a search on here and found this one and decided to give it a try. I am so glad I did. This looks like just a little hole in the wall, but of course those types of places are always the best. Â  Â  When you first go in there is just a kitchen and a set of stairs,the stairs are not friendly so watch out or you will fall to your doom,especially going down them. The eating area is way cramped (as in like 7 tables all so close they are touching eachother) so if you don't like feeling crowded go at a less busy time of day or take your food to go. Â  Â The prices are great for the amount you get,and the food is pretty much as perfect as it can get. I tried the jerk chicken with rice and peas.So spicy I drank 2 lemonades-which is just how it should be:) The service was friendly and pretty fast.
Absolutely love this place. It has a great atmosphere,food, Â great drinks and a swanky decor. My friend Nina introduced me to this place :) . The friendly service and food are consistent.

Love this place. Been there a few times for Brunch and, gotta say, it's super tasty, not too pricey (for brunch in the city at least), and has a nice atmosphere. There's a bit of a wait, but it's worth it! And the coffee is phenom. Will get back there for dinner one of these days..

This is a cute, small bar on 1st ave. Some drinks are really good and some are really bad. The menu is small and it goes from little tapas apps to huge meals, so not in between. The food was just okay, nothing special for the prices and almost all fried. The service was good, the staff is friendly, but its very hit or miss. I think with all the other options around in the area, I would def not go back unless I had a groupon or something. There are a lot of better places in that area (like the one right next door, I forget the name but its all black and the inside is really trendy/chic)

Like any true New York hot spot, the wait time for brunch at Clinton St. will take you anywhere from an hour to two and a half hours for weekend brunch. They open at 9am, but I can assure you by 9:05am the restaurant is completely full and you will have to wait an hour at least. How do I know this? Â The BF is serious about his brunch (and not waiting), so he's made me come here at 8:30 on a Saturday morning to try this magical pancake. At around 8:30am, there were already quite a few other hardcore brunchers lined up and signed up on the waiting list. We were lucky enough to be the last table seated - can you imagine? If we came at 8:35, we would have already been TOO LATE. In another experience, I came here at 11AM for a table for 3 and we actually had to wait close to 2.5 hours. Yikes! Luckily, they take down your phone number and will text you when your table's ready. As a self-proclaimed "not a sweets person", this Wild Maine Blueberry pancake turned me into a sweets person. I love the crunchy exterior of each pancake, yet fluffy interior that just melts into your mouth as you bite in. The warmed maple butter is another essential that makes these pancakes to die for! If sweets aren't your thing (ha), you will also have to try the sugar-cured bacon. Essentially these bacon strips are baked with brown sugar sprinkled on top - and believe me, it is addictive. In this Southern Breakfast, there will be fried green tomatoes, fried eggs, grits and of course this sugar cured bacon. Even if you don't order this southern breakfast, I urge you to order the bacon on the side. If you like bacon, you will not be disappointed. Minus 1 star for the long long wait time. If not for the long wait, I would come here much much more often.... mmmmm.... pancakes.

very disappointed. Â Went for lunch and got put in the back room, which I found to be very bleak and uninviting. Â I ordered the veal. Â It looked like a meat pancake. Â No garnishes, nothing. Â Very unappetizing and it wasn't very good. Â My friend had the pasta and that was a bit better. Â The wine was great and I liked our waitress. Â Would not return. Â Hope Mario's other restaurants aren't like this one.

Long wait but fast service and reliable and tasty food. Â No reservations unless you know one of the owners (not that I do). Soup dumplings crab or regular pork are must-orders. Â The scallion pancake is really crispy and savory. Â Shanghai fried noodle is very oily but so delicious. Â Other favorite dishes of mine here are the chili bean sauce carp belly (lots of bones but a really sweet cut of fish braised in a delicious salty and spicy sauce) and the vegetable and meat wonton (a somewhat lighter but still yummy option on the menu). Â Another specialty here is the yuan ti (braised bone-in pork shoulder served on a bed of wilted spinach) - I think it tastes as it should but the pork could be a bit more tender, nonetheless a strong choice as well on the menu. Prices are so cheap, especially if you come with a big group of people. Â You can easily spend far less than $15 per person (incld tax and tips) for a gut-busting meal.

SOUP DUMPLINGS This is the places for amazing and inexpensive soup dumplings. Portions are big so bring some friends and they give you green tea with every meal. Wouldn't go here for any other reason other than the dumplings.

The food is 5-stars. Â Great dishes including a fantastic mushroom chawanmushi and some great lamb. Â The decor on the other hand is WAY too stuffy. Â "Jackets preferred" (on OpenTable's description) I think makes people less inclined to come and a more relaxed atmosphere would make the restaurant experience better.

If we had only had the square it would have been a 5 star rating. The soho square pizza we had last night was great, saucey and chewy flavorful crust. But a pizza place has to be at least partially judged on it regular slice, and that was just average or even below depending on your average. The cheese was a molten glop on top of a floppy mushy wet base. My husband who usually skips the crust (I do not approve) actually used it to scoop up some cheese and left the rest in a pile with the floppy under crust which had come loose and laid limply on the pile. I actually think that maybe they should only offer the Sicilian style pizza as some places in Italy seem to specialize in just one type and that seems to be working out for that country. There was also a picture of James Gandolfini at a pizza place that was clearly not Prince Street Pizza which was confusing, but probably has a good explanation. We will stop in again and get the SQUARE and review it by itself.

Queens Kickshaw will serve you a delicious cup of coffee but, alas, it will not be cheap. Â The aesthetic inside is beautiful - wooden, rustic. Â They also have live music, on occasion, which is always nice in the neighborhood. Â And this neighborhood needs this kind of a place.

Excellent burritos and tacos. Actually, everything I've had has been superb. Super friendly folks to boot! Â Affordable and quick, and continuously exceeds my expectations. Â Don't even think about going across the street to San Loco - I'd rather lick the sidewalk!

Decent spot. Â I did the restaurant week menu with a few girls and everyone agreed it was pretty good. Â Nothing out of the ordinary, but a solid spot to try if you're in the neighborhood. The hummus was great and the shrimp were delicious once I removed them from their shells. Â My chicken entree was relatively unmemorable and my cheesecake was decent.
