I worked near here awhile and kept seeing crazy lines, figured i should give it a try. It's not half bad but it's no L&B. Don't go at exactly dinner time try when its a little slower but sometimes even lunch seems pretty busy. prices food and service are all pretty good but not nearly good enough for some of the lines ive seen.

My friend wanted Moroccan and I was gonna take her either to Cafe Mogador or Nomad but we could not find parking. So I decided to check this place out instead. It's a very cute little cafe, more French than Moroccan, very much SoHo atmosphere. Which is all fine with me, but the food was mediocre. The olives and oranges we started with was yummy (Originality: 4 stars, Presentation: 3.5 stars, Taste: 4 stars) but anyone can put that together. I had the couscous with Merguez sausages (O: 3 stars, P: 4 stars, T: 2.5 stars) which was so disappointing. The couscous itself was so bland! Moroccan food is not supposed to lack in flavor! My friend's Hachi Parmentier (O: 3.5 stars, P: 3 stars, T: 3 stars) was slightly better but not by much. The dessert was more satisfying, thankfully. We had the bread pudding (O: 3.5 stars, P: 3 stars, T: 4.5 stars) which was very light and delicious. Over all I'd say come here for a glass of wine and some beautiful people watching. Or a cappuccino and dessert while you chat the afternoon away.

This place is as well-stocked as Paris Hilton is well-read. Asked for one of the cocktails in their drink menu. "We don't make that one anymore." Asked for brisket. "We're out of that." Friend asked for a beer. "We're out of that." Asked for another beer. "We're out of that one." Asked for another beer. "We don't have most of the bottled beers on the menu." Asked about the tuna. "We're out of that." And to top it off, when we were paying she returned with my credit card. "We don't accept American Express." I'd say "hopeless" but that's probably evident. Food was nothing special. Waitress said the margarita was great - something I'd be willing to Â challenge her to a duel over. Bah.

The pumpkin ravioli with asparagus was really phenomenal. I've never tasted anything like it. I'm giving them three stars because they automatically included 20% gratuity on our check. I thought the minimum was 18% for large groups... that's just not cool. Our waiter didn't even do anything special nor was he particularly friendly.

Decided to chose this place for my first ever brunch in brooklyn. My friend and I got there and were told by a tattooed chic acting as "hostess" that it will be a 45 minute wait. We decide to take a quick stroll through he neighborhood and got back after about 25 minutes, only to be told by the above said "hostess" that she called our name a while back--is 45 minutes different in brooklyn than manhattan? She told us the next table would be ours and then proceeded to seat people who came after us...I guess we were being punished for daring to not be their when she called our name. My friend wanted to stay, even though I just wanted to go somewhere else, and when we finally got seated and got served our food which was okay but certainly not something to write home about. I asked for a coffee refill and got a lukewarm dishwater instead...so to speak. I politely asked the waitress if she wouldn't mind getting me a hot cup of coffee. I was then informed that because they serve coffee all day (their brunch is from 10 to 3...so i guess Â a day is different in Brooklyn), there is no guarantee of getting a hot cup of coffee but she would try! Yes my friends, we were honored indeed by her deigning to "try" and get me a cup of hot coffee. I have friends who waitress and I know what a tough job it is but I also know that many serve staff do their work with warmth and courtesy and leave their bad moods and attitudes at home...but it seems this little non-descript restaurant with mediocre food and arrogant and rude wait staff is above all that. So if you guys happen to be in the neighbor hood, just walk up to 5th avenue and select some of the wonderful cafes and restaurants that I saw are there including one called Dizzy's which I later found out would have been a much better deal then this pretentious little hole we went to.

I had heard great things and it was pretty great. It was about a 20 minute wait when I went, but worth it. I brought friends who Â had never been to NY before and so this is one of those places you go when you want a nicer than a walk up and get a slice on your way somewhere in the city. Nice sit down, place and the staff was pretty nice (by New York standards) Gracious slice sizes, and the beer offerings were pretty great too. I would definitely return, and the wait would be worth it everytime. The toppings were fresh, and you can tell it is a good brick over pizza... not as greasy as other pizza you can get in the city. This place is consistent. Pretty good to order anything on the menu. Every time I go, it's always a hit. I prefer this location over the one in Estvill. I like the ambient and decor of this restaurant. Not too expensive, but always safe pick for good food and service. Busy on weekends.

This place was amazing. The food tasted so fresh. We had the Mezze platter and hummus was to die for. Chicken kebab was very tasty. We also had Turkish red wine, It was okay. Service was good and fast. I'll be definitely coming again!

All you people that are giving this 4 stars are truly blowing my mind!! There Arecibo better middle eastern restaurants in Brooklyn! This place should not even be categorized as a restaurant, as it only has a bread oven to cook everything in. No grill surface whatsoever!! If it was called Bedouin Bakery and only sold pita bread my rating would be much higher as the bread is really good and fresh. All you people that don't know any better and keep ranting and raving about the hummus and babagnus, go 4 blocks down the street to Sahadi's. It's light years better. The falafel is not good mushy and flavorless. Just incase you've never eaten falafel it is supposed to be crunchy outside and soft inside. Try Mamoun's the best! Even crappy Cheaps falafel near St Marks is waaaaay better. Avoid this place at all cost. If you rated this 4 or 5 star please try another place then you will see what you have been missing all these years.

I went to Locanda Verde with three friends, and we had an overall delicious experience. The food was really really good, the portion sizes ok, and the prices reasonable, but maybe a tad high, NYC wise. The service was sweet and attentive, but it was clear that they were busy: they initially forgot a glass of wine for my friend (we had to remind them, then it arrived), and when we were having coffee, they never showed up with my milk. However, it's relatively small things, and all in all we had a great night there.

This place is becoming one of my neighborhood go-tos for quick weeknight meals. Â I'm not usually a falafel fan but I like the way they make 'em here. Â Of the three falafel flavors (Green (herb blend), Yellow (harissa) and Red (red peppers)), I like Green best - nice blend of herbs. Â I love their baba ganoush - thick, creamy and smoky. Â The toasted pita that comes with it is substantial - fresh and doughy, topped with zaatar. Â I wish it came with additional pitas without my having to order more since I always seem to run out of it when there's about half a container of baba ganoush left. The place itself is tiny, with maybe a total of 8 -10 seats so I typically pick up to-go. Â Service is quick and efficient.

Could be four stars, but my waitress was not very friendly or present until it was time for tip and the drinks are slightly over-priced for their size. The food was pretty standard nothing to rave about. Except the dumplings! Definitely check-in and get a free order but then order an additional one. They are surprisingly fried but OH SO DELICIOUS. Like actually. What I did like about this place is the atmosphere. It's a nice place to unwind after work. There is good music and modern decor that puts you at ease. The space is dimly lit and great for conversation over a simple meal. I had the slow roasted pork sandwich. It's not bad but it seemed like all fat. The French fries are delicious. They are moderately thick and crisp. My friend had one of the two pasta dishes that she described as average. The proportion was filling, but the quality could have been better.
Great pizza! good flavor and just the right combo of sauce and cheese. we had the arugula pizza, the pepperoni pizza, and plain pizza. very impressed
Lunch at Bouley is an amazing bargain. Â $110.00 per person with the wine pairings. Â Food and wine were exceptional and the place is beautiful in the way great restaurants used to be.

FIVE BUCKS! Can't beat the value here! Can you believe how much food, and good, unique food, you can get from Veronica's for lunch? You can see just how good it is by its popularity - the line gets long and people wait up to 15 minutes! That's real un-substitute-able popularity. If you work downtown, you should try this place once. But don't get there after 1 o'clock. You run the risk that they run out of chicken. Their mac n' cheese could be a bit better, but still I always get it. I like the jerk chicken because the curry and the stewed chicken get a bit messy. Try Veronica's, and compare it to any BBQ restaurant in the city. Â I think it's just as good. Yes, Veronica's was a finalist for the vendy awards.

The soup dumplings are amazing. The last time I was there, they weren't that soupy but still were delicious. The general tso's chicken was really good as well. The chicken was cooked well, and it was real chicken unlike most chinese places you go to. The sauce was a bit sweet, but that is the way I like it.

I was attending a trade show just up the street on 10th Avenue and needed to find a place to take a colleague. Â This turned out to be the perfect place. Â A hidden GEM on 10th Avenue. Â I made a reservation, which was a smart move since the place filled up shortly after we arrived at 8pm. Â The space was charming, warm and cozy. Â Not what you would expect for the area. I have to start by saying our server Natalia (who single handedly waited on the whole place) was the best!! Â Without totally gushing about her, I will simply say that she was very engaging, and her enticing manner drew you in as she told you the specials, she made all good recommendations for food and wine and she was thoughtful enough to have our food split in advance since my friend and I were sharing. Â  Worth a mention is the cocktail list was quite interesting as well. Â I had the Macenudo which was crisp, citrusy and tart. Â Delish! Now to the food! Â We had the burrata and octopus appetizers. Â Both were absolutey delicious. Â My friend and I also shared the whole fileted bronzini and also the rigatoni with chorizo. Â Again, terrific dishes. Â Perfectly executed. Â Our other friend got the pasta with mushrooms and that looked great as well. We were too full for dessert so we opted for a sparkling dessert wine which the perfect ending to a delicious meal. Â I would definitely go back here again.

Didn't know they open late till 2am, but they definitely can serve you a simple dish with great taste, such as their Wonton Noodle soup. It's pretty plain, but the best restaurant is one that can give you a memorable food with its simple ingredients. Plenty of wontons in one bowl and the noodles, although it's a little too soft, when I took a sip of the soup, it reminded me of wonton noodle soup that I had in Hongkong way back when. The food came out fast and the service was pretty good for a chinese resto. Not recommended to come here with more than 4 ppl for such a small place. I simply dig this place when I visited NY this past weekend. Totally recommended for every noodle whores like me. And you bet, it's CHEAP! Less than $5 per bowl (before tax).

Friendly service, good ambience, and delish food. The tomato salad, octopus, and empanadas were out of this world. Fish was great and also the burger was decadent. I cannot emphasize how great the service was again...

When we got into the area, we were a little confused because the restaurant is in a secluded area with no other shops/stores around. There's really cool graffiti art everywhere and lots of street parking available. (although we were a little nervous about leaving our car cuz the area looked a little shady) The service was great and the food was delicious. We got the roasted potatoes to start and then ordered the burrito pizza. Whoever thought of putting a fried egg with runny yolk on a pizza is a genius. It was awesome. My husband got a cup of the single origin iced coffee and loved it. I'm not much of a coffee person, but i had a sip and it was pretty good. It kinda sucked cuz we sat at a long table across from each other but right in between 2 other parties. They were really loud and so it was kinda annoying.

Mmmmmm good hangover food :D Hahaha. I was craving for some soupy food and udon was the perfect choice! I think we went kind of late, which is perfect because the place was just sort of scattered with people. No wait. My friend and I both got sets, she got the Oyako-don with udon, and I got the beef with rice with udon. Both were great. And then - my headache from the hangover magically disappeared! (....or was it the Advil that my friend gave me...?) Nonetheless, yay for delicious, plain, hot broth with perfectly made udon :)
delicious brunch. I highly recommend the huevos racheros. only drawback is that even if you make a reservation, they seem to make you wait 5-10 mins every time.
A neighborhood gem. Excellent friendly service. Good latte and the "mash of the day" served a with breakfast never disappoints.

Yakitori is Japanese grilled skewered chicken meat and offal. Â It can also be broadened to include other meats and vegetables. Â The entire experience is reminiscent of Spanish tapas, in that you order lots of different things, and can easily share and try everything. Â The rather small second floor eatery is apparently a favorite of Thomas Keller's, Eric Ripert's, and Anthony Bourdain's, among others. Â Here is a run down of our selections, and a few thoughts on each. Skin: A favorite of many when it's still attached to the bird. Â Why should it be any less good skewered and grilled? Â It had a nice bit of char flavor, crispy edges, and softer interior between the folds. Â I liked this, but would have loved it even more if all of the skin was super crispy :) Â I would still order it next time, and PS you feel less guilty if you share! Soft Knee Bone: Okay, I went into this one pretty sure I wasn't going to like it. Â I was told that it would be a strange texture, and that I would have to chew it for a while before I could swallow the whole thing. Â Let's just say, I chewed one piece briefly before I decided spitting it out (into a napkin, of course) would be my best option. Â Not a fan. Gizzard: This was my first encounter with gizzard as well. Â I was okay with it, thought the texture erred a bit on the chewy side along one edge, but enjoyed the spicy and somewhat crisp texture of the par-grilled onion skewered alongside it. Â It was a nice touch, and made me feel a bit less weird about eating grilled gizzard. Â Would I order this again on my own. Â Probably not. Heart: Would you believe that the heart was one of my favorites? Well you should because it's true. Â I was a bit hesitant going into this one as well, but to be honest, I really loved the flavor of the heart, the texture wasn't weird, it was super meaty, the grilled flavor was great, and it was juicy. Tail: To be honest, I nibbled around the edges mostly. Â I enjoyed the slightly salted charred flavor of the edges, but the texture was a tad off-putting. Thigh: Honestly, I'm a white meat person, but I'm gonna say, these thighs were really good! Â They were so juicy and tender! Â Perfectly (simply) seasoned, and even the fat had a good texture. Â I often find chicken fat to be chewy if it isn't super crisp, but this fat was just fine by me :) Japanese Fried Chicken: This was also a popular choice. Â I mean, it's fried chicken. Â What's not to like? Â This one is doused in a slightly sweet and tangy sauce and topped with sesame seeds (so it's not really crunchy anymore, but the flavors are great). Â This is also a safe bet if you're unsure of some of the less obvious options. Chicken Meatball: It looks nothing like a meatball. Â It looks more like a kebab, but I guess if you squished a raw meatball onto a skewer it would be a kebab, right? Â This baby was soooooo juicy and flavorful, I wanted it all for myself. Â It was better than any chicken meatball or chicken kebab I've ever had in my whole life. Â It was juicier than I thought ground chicken had any right to be! Pork Belly with Scallions and Mustard: These were also skewered with onion, a nice contrast of texture and flavor to the pork belly. Â The pork belly itself was not melt-in-your-mouth tender, but it was also grilled, and not braised. Â I accept that the texture would be a mixture of tender and slightly chewy along the fatty edge. Â I liked it overall though, enjoyed the grilled flavor in the meat, and thought the scallions and ponzu were a good accompaniment. Â The pork belly is also offered with lemon and mustard as an alternative. Tori Dango: These dumplings were another hit! Â The chicken meatballs inside were juicy and delicious, and the sticky rice on the exterior was a fun flavor and texture addition. Â I've never had dumplings coated with rice instead of wrapped in dough, but I would definitely order these again! Â If you are afraid of offal, these are a great option! Zucchini Tempura: These are stunning! Â I've never had tempura like this before! Â Each thickly cut piece of zucchini was crusted with rice cracker bits. Â It offered a nice flavor and a completely unique texture to each piece. Â This plate was also served with some smoked salt for you to dip or top your zucchini tempura with. Â It was delicious and a wonderful touch. Avocado and Tuna Salad with Tobiko: I loved this salad! Â I could have single-handedly eaten a vat of it. Â It was a great balance of textures, with the soft, buttery avocado, the fresh, raw tuna chunks, and the tiny little fish eggs popping in your mouth in between bites, offering a glimpse of briny flavor amidst this perfectly dressed salad. Â So fresh! Kyona Salad: This salad was good, very unusual, but good. Â It had a slight fishiness from the teeny tiny fried baby sardines, and a bit of tanginess from the cream cheese. Â The poached egg was part of the dressing, making this a truly unique salad, unlike any I've had before. Â I had seconds.

You cannot come here without eating at least 3 slices of Sicilian pizza I usually cannot eat this much of anything EXCEPt this pizza I can eat it forever and it's always fresh best place in Brooklyn hands down anddddd their regular pizza is really good too but Sicilian is the way to go

Great selection of tapas in the EV for this tiny spot, so I highly recommend reservations on any given night. We did some orders of short rib tacos, fish tacos, tuna ceviche and empandas which stuck out for me - but that is only half of what we ordered. Â Overall everything was great and they also have an excellent selection of fun cocktails to try. Â  Just make sure you are ready to come pay. Buon appetito!

I can't say anything that was bad about this place. My lamb chops were cooked to perfection. And the salad had pomegranate which is my favorite. Â Brought back how my mom prepares the lamb chops. The serves was good. The manager came to check on us. Even asked if our table was ok. It was next to the outside and window which I didn't mind but she was kind enough to insist and sat us down somewhere else. The kangaroo burger slider was so delicious. Â My bf wasn't sure about trying kangaroo so we ordered one slider which we shared. The spread for the bread was olives and I love olives my bf on the other hand hates them but loved the spread which was a plus.

I've passed this place lot's of times and always either come back after close or gotten denied when I suggested it for a place to meet. Â Finally went back the other day and have already been since. The setting is as expected for a cheap Chinatown dumpling house. Â Not a ton of seating and with how busy this place gets, seating can actually get hard to come by. Â By why sit anyways when you can watch the women work their wok-magic - when I took my food to go I watched them like artists fit the dumplings into the huge steamers and toss the mung beans in an enormous wok, so beautiful. The food is very good, very simple (no surprises) and very very cheap. Â For my first trip I got the 8 pork and scallion dumplings in the soup broth (about a quart of broth) and a veggie sesame pancake. Â The pancake was awesome and greasy and pretty substantial for $1.50. Â The soup, which included bok choy and some other veggies along with 8 dumplings, would have been enough by itself, and easily enough to pay $5.00 for (what the two items together cost me). For my second trip I tried to plan more accordingly for the eat-and-walk I was about to make back to my friend's place in Stuy Town. Â Still craving the dumplings but realizing soup would be impossible I decided on the 4 pork dumplings. Â I also got an order of 3 pork buns (a little smaller than some Chinatown bun places but just as good on the inside). Â And, of course, I ordered another sesame pancake. Â Total was again $5 and probably more filling than my first meal. Such a cool place, cheap cheap cheap, and very good simple food. Â I would challenge anyway to be satisfied and spend more than $6.

Such a satisfying meal, great ambiance and it was all during restraunt week! They deserve extra cheers, as it has faithfully been great food and decent service when the place is empty or half full, but the place was packed to the gills on a sat night and it didn't hurt the food or service one bit. Try as many meze as you can, better to go with a small group so as to share with one another. My branzino was flavorful and the mustard greens excellent. My partner's lamb shank also was well executed, not to dry and plenty of flavor. The cocktails have an ounce of effort behind them, and I was happy with the "exile" sort of a honeyed margarita without the salt.

YUM. Food and service were superb. I love cheese and olive oil, and fancy versions of both served to me by friendly waitresses. But, let's get serious . . .I want to go back to this place for one reason only: the dessert. The warm chocolate cake with sea salt gelato blew my mind. Â  Yum.

Wow. Â 250 reviews already. Â What more is there to say? 1. Â The brussels sprouts are... just brussels sprouts. Â The waitress volunteered that they are one of the most popular dishes, but now that I re-visit the menu, I think they forgot the creme fraiche. Â And the pine nuts. Â Oh yah, and flavour. 2. Enormous whole shrimp was another dish touted to be a crowd pleaser. Â Enormous, yes - two of them, in fact. Â Unfortunately, ours came out tough and overcooked. Â Pity. Don't worry, I'm not going to be all hater on the entire menu. Â The cilantro dipping sauce that came with the pulled pork empanadas were nice and punchy. Â Blue crab risotto was also flavorful and, admittedly not overwhelmed with blue crab, still a tasty dish to share. Â The fritto misto de mare was a subdued collection of deep fried sea-friends that provided a few fun crunchy bites, but paled in comparison to the most basic $2.99 plate of fried smelt you can get at dim sum (well really, aren't tapas just Spanish dim sum anyways?). Â I was hoping for more fatty juicy goodness from the braised pork belly bits skewered on the BLT, but the components as one were a nice touch. Â I have to say I was ambivalent about our remaining dishes, although I must express a firm preference for the torija over the fennel panna cotta (more sweet, less hard-to-put-my-finger-on-it funk, please). Overall, I think it's a fun place to eat and hang out. Â It can get pretty loud on the main floor, but still fun to sift through the bountiful menu and see what comes back from the kitchen. Â I can't say I'd go back with the expectation to have consistently "knock my socks off" tapas. Â However, I would go back from the ones I liked, and to satisfy my curiosity and see what else comes up the next time I spin the wheel.
One of the best - a modern New York classic. Any trip to New York for the holidays without at least a visit here for a canele is incomplete. We had several :)
My first time trying viet sandwiches. WOW. MIND BLOWN. So glad my friend told me about this place. Plan on going back!
One of the best Pizza places in NY..the one hour wait was totally worth...should try the ice cream factory at the end of the street after this stop...

I came here last night with my friend and we both sat at their bar area because we simply thought it would be the best spot and it was! The restaurant is very well dressed. It was simple with it's wood infused decor. The soft lighting from the hanging paper lanterns made the restaurant feeling comfortable and relaxing. With jazz playing in the background, we were immediately greeted with warm towels to clean our hands. Personally I thought it was a very nice touch indeed! I ordered their homemade soba with grated yam and raw egg yolk ($16) and it was absolutely delightful -- I wanted more. I enjoyed the sliminess of the yolk over the sliminess of the grated yam and when combined with the soy sauce, it had the perfect amount of salt to bring out the flavor and taste. We also tried some of their yakitori but I thought it was okay. The meat was a bit dry and tough. I thought it was over cooked and wasn't seasoned well enough. Personally, I wouldn't recommend it as it's overpriced and not worth a shot. Although watching the guy making them was pretty entertaining. Their homemade tofu ($6) that comes with three different flavored salts are also worth a try! My friend and I shared it and the taste of the tofu was silky, chilled and just utterly refreshing. Let's just say, If you can't figure out what fresh tofu should taste like, imagine processed mozzarella from the supermarket vs. freshly made mozzarella from the a deli. It's just that good!!!! Best of all I like this place because they are a chain restaurant from Japan. I assume most of their ingredients are local but their menu probably mirrors the same ones from Japan so that is a plus in my book.

Throwing down 5 stars for a 100% vegan spot in Williamsburg with a super friendly and attentive staff. I'd give it 6 stars if they served booze, but hey, this isn't my place of business - so who am I to demand such things?? Loved the Drunken Cowgirl and Elberto's Burrito (or something similar to that). Both were delicious, and the burrito wasn't overly enormous. We were served by a tall redhead on day one and a blond with some awesome tattoos on day two. Both were fantastic. Hopefully they can tell who I'm talking about so they can get some recognition! Great service, guys!

I don't understand the mega-hype and the long lines this place gets--it is, after all, just a ramen shop--but, it is really quite a good ramen shop worth at least some of the wait.The tonkotsu broth here is on another level of delicious, and the presentation is great. The atmosphere is raucous and evocative, and the service is on point. I haven't had much of a chance to explore the menu, but everything I've had in my visits here has been very delicious. I recommend Ippudo, but i don't recommend waiting more than a little while to get in.

It took a while for me to venture into Onyx (now Greenpoint Heights!)... but now, it's my go-to spot for starting or ending an evening. Great place to grab a drink after work... After all, I have to pass it on the way home... Similarly, I've gotten out of cabs after a night out with friends, seen the red lights from down the street and decided to stop in and grab one more. I meet my roommate here for Taco Thursdays (!!!), and bring out-of-town friends for a few drinks. [The guacamole is great... Pork Tacos are my fav] I like Onyx because I can hang out alone, watch whatever they happen to be playing on the TVs, and not feel like I'm going to be followed home by some weirdo. On that same note, not a lot of conversation happening between people perched at the bar... But the bartenders are ALWAYS friendly and welcoming. Did I mention the patio is BEAUTIFUL. In fact, the whole place is super classy. (I hear they're going to heat the patio during the wintertime...) I really enjoy hanging out here. I've been meaning to check out Karaoke night (Mondays?) - I've been brushing up on my repertoire.

Awesome place, I can't wait to go back! We came in at 10:30 on Saturday night and were told that there would be a 30 minute wait. They offered to take our number and call us but we opted to hang out at the bar. The bartender did not seem to notice us at all while we waited (we were standing, as there were no seats left) and I mentioned this to the owner. He apologized profusely and really made us feel like VIPsafter that. The food was amazing, we had the brussel sprouts, olives, and a special (baked parsnips) which were so good. I ordered the butternut squash salad-it wasn't a large serving but it was delicious. Tip: you can call the day of to make reserverations!

This place is a great addition to the neighborhood- a great bar at night and the brunch menu is so original and delicious, loved the kale mushrooms with quinoa hash brown. Also great how tax is included in the price! Only suggestions would be to have espresso coffees (really wanted a cappuccino but there wasn't any) for brunch time and to change up the music, both times I've been in the music has been annoying 60's tunes- a place this cool with this great decor needs to play something a bit more current and hip. Deff will be coming back more though!

Dos Toros could beat both Moes and Chipotle to the pulp even if they teamed up. Â Never again will I ever spend $$ on Chipotle or Moes. Â I tasted what real food tastes like in Dos Toros. Â I got a chicken burrito AND YOU CAN ACTUALLY FULLY TASTE THE TENDER CHICKEN. Â I've always thought that the taste of the chicken wasn't strong in a burrito because the other fillings were overpowering it but no. Â  Plus it's just a tad more expensive than Moes or Chipotle. Â  The place is really really small though. Â They do have a few seats but lines can easily cramp up the space. Â For a small space, it does look very clean and minimal decor is pretty nice. Â Better for getting it on the go. Bonus: the servers were a group of cute, upbeat, young guys who all seemed to be friends with each other (they make food assembly line style) and very friendly to their customers.

Well I was really excited to eat here and the atmosphere is great with lots of energy. But we ate in the restaurant instead of outside and we got an order number and the food was made in a food truck outside not the kitchen. Also when you sit in the restaurant you hear the bathroom dryer so loud cause they keep a door open so GROSS! I was with someone and we ordered the the steak platos and the chicken platos. I was so excited to eat and the steak and chicken had no seasoning and there was a little bit of food that cost $35.00 with 2 guava drinks. The black beans with the reive though were great. Now what saved this ridiculous restaurant from me giving it a 1 was the grilled corn with all these great condiments. I will never go back the money and taste of that dry tasteless meat was enough for me.

My boyfriend and I have wanted to try out Marc Forgione for sometime now because it has a Michelin Star and $14 bottomless mimosas on Sundays. Â  We decided to have brunch here, last Sunday, and ordered the chili lobster and eggs off of the specials menu, fried quail and waffles and a side of sausage. Â All of the dishes were so delicious. Â If you love spicy food, the lobster is definitely the way to go and the bread it was served with was yummy and perfect for sopping up the sauce. Â Also, if you have ever been to Roscoe's in LA and loved it, try Marc's take on chicken and Waffles and order the quail & waffles - This dish definitely beats the chicken and waffles you'd get at Roscoe's. I left the restaurant very happy... this may be our new brunch spot!

Absolutely the most unpleasant dining experience I've had all year. The people who work here are plain rude; seems like they don't care if they get your business. Some of the staff can't pronounce English numbers correctly so I noticed a lot of confusion when they were shouting out order numbers. I had plenty of time to observe as I waited 20 minutes for my order of 8 dumplings. Ick, doesn't seem like the cleanest place either. . . Take your money elsewhere.

I have died, and gone to PIZZA HEAVEN... I must say that I didn't wait all that long..about 15-20 minutes for a pie on a Thursday night. Seriously though, unlike any other NYC pizza experience I've ever had. After ordering my pie, I grabbed some modelo especial's at the supermarket across the street. No one seemed to mind I was enjoying a cocktail while I waited. This place is a dump.. seriously you would never expect something so delicious and amazing to come out of here. The interior hasn't changed a bit since the place opened god knows how long ago. All of that is superficial to the product, I was memorized watching the boiling cheesey goodness come out of the oven (check out the picture's I've included). There is one old Italian man that makes the pizza. They average about 20 pies and hour (I asked!). Keep in mind this place is only open for 3 hours in the evening - 6pm - 9pm! I guess when you charge $25 for a regular pie and $30 for a Sicilian you only need to do 3 hours of business a night...

This is a very small restaurant, but the food is pretty good. I felt like they gave us extra attention. probably because we had a group of over 10 people and the restaurant can fit around 25. Ordered the lumpiang shanghai for the appetizer. They're small spring rolls with a sweet dipping sauce. Super crispy. Super yum. For my main course, I ordered the beef with rice. That was alright. A bit too greasy for me.

Their halo-halo bumps this review up to 5 stars - get the special with ube (purple yam) ice cream, but make sure you bring a friend to share! Or come on a hot day and eat it for lunch. Shaved ice with beans, coconut, nata de coco, leche flan, sugar palm fruit, sweetened condensed milk... and how often do you get to eat something PURPLE? On the owner's recommendation I also got the Crispy Pata (the Chinese love this, she said) and was presented with a giant hunk of deep fried pig knuckle. Crunchy skin, tender meat - I could feel oil oozing out of my Â pores by the end, but it was definitely worth it. The Daing (grilled milkfish) was very soft and delicious too. Just one note: don't expect any vegetables unless you order it on the side. I'd definitely come back to try the adobo, pork belly, etc. Pretty quiet on a Monday night; the owners came out to chat and were very friendly.

My favorite Filipino spot! I've been here three times? I'd come more often if it wasn't such a fat fest that I always feel bad about after. My workout for the impending meal starts before I even order -- stomach clenching as soon as I'm given a menu and glance over all of the artery clogging goodness. My go to at each Filipino spot that I've been to(and probably yours) -- sizzling sisig. Incredible! Pig and Khao makes my absolute favorite. Topped with a raw egg, it's fattier and saltier than anywhere else, and also seasoned better. Along with a side of incredibly fragrant and sweet coconut rice(so good that I can eat standalone) I could finish the whole plate of chewy, cartilage-y pork bits on my own but somehow have the self-control not to. Alas, more is coming! I usually also spit the khao soi -- this dish is equally incredible. The curry is creamy with a mild heat and has a very distinct coconut presence. The egg noodles are wonderfully chewy. The bowl is topped off with a generous amount of crispy noodles. Any leftover coconut rice is soaked in the curry and always finished, mmm. I've also tried the baby back ribs(saucy, meaty and extremely tender) and octopus salad(nothing special and kind of expensive for what it was) but have gone back to my two go-tos. Louis CK puts it best -- The meal is not over when I'm full. The meal is over when I hate myself. So of course, the meal must be topped off with the halo halo. I selfishly devour most of the incredible flan and ube ice cream before spooning as much pinipig as I can onto each bite of shaved ice. And now, I hate myself. Worth it.
Bad service, Bad food and this place ruined my brunch experience and made me bitter betty for the week to follow.

This was my one of my favorite breakfasts in Williamsburg. As we walked into this cute diner and sat at the bar I caught a glimpse of some hot chicken and waffles walk by me. I could not resist.... and man was I happy about my decision. I would suggest to get the gravy on the side. I was savoring every single bite so as I started my second half my waffle was a bit soggy but I still managed to eat the entire thing. I probably shouldn't have because I basically had to be rolled out of the place but it was just TOO DELICIOUS TO STOP EATING! My friends food was also good, eggs, corn bread, bacon, potatoes ect. Went there on a Monday no wait.

Just when I thought I'd have to stroll down to Long Island City to avoid the guidos and bros, I remember I had Sweet Afton bookmarked and man, I feel like this is where all the hip in Astoria are kept. Came here on a Saturday night with a girlfriend and this place was packed with the kind of crowd you would find at any West Village bar: your average, single and successful, young 20s to mid-20s hotties, only difference is they're not in suits and in Louboutin heels and a heavily-powdered face, because why would you? The inside felt like a Christmas bar with an modern American wood meets a dark cave setting. There is definitely a lot of hipsters--if you ever needed to find Astoria hipsters, it's like all of them are crammed in this bar. Took us a little while to get a table; we got a high table and sitting on the stool, with my back against everyone, was probably the most annoying thing of the night. I got shoved in, got my back rubbed violently, got my shirt dragged a few times because it felt like bodies were rubbing everything. I had the worst seat in the house. Do not sit on the stools with your back against everyone because chances of you choking on your food are high. My friend and I got some drinks; I got Naragansett beer and we both got Screwdrivers with fried pickles and fries. The Screwdrivers were bad. Alcohol was strong but nothing worse than being made with Minute Maid. The fried pickles are....overrated. It's just fried pickles fried in deep oil, something we all can do if we buy a fryer. They had a some pepper in it which ruined it for me and they were easily soaked. I really love the lively setting of this place but I will come back for their burgers. Drinks, not so much.

Sure it was raining and cold out but that didnt stop us or all the people in line. Â Best $6 spent on a midnight snack to share with friends. Â The portions are huge and me and my 3 gfs were able to share an order.

Always liked that place and always will. More a lunch place for me, dinner gets too "cool" and then i can't stand the attitude and the smelly waiter anymore. Lunch, i can deal. Food is always good, sometimes they tried too hard but burger or steak always a 5 stars. See you soon

I love bone marrow. Lupa was on the mark last night. Perfectly prepared, just enough of a salty flavor, with a perfect crostini bread. I ordered the duck ragu with fresh pasta. Small portion ( if i was on chopped they might say it was not an entree size portion but and appetizer ). Â The duck was cooked well but was lacking a little bit of salt to extract the flavor. The dish was a little bland but still very good. We also ordered prosciutto and 3 cheese selection. Amazing!!!!
Cash only... try not to add too many toppings to the pizza!! Frowned upon! Grandmas meatballs are delicious!!

Place is definitely over hyped. Â Yes, they have extremely good soup dumplings, but let's also judge this place for other things. Â The place is crowded and packed like a sardine can. Â It's noisy. Â The waiters rush the heck out of you. Â Aren't you here paying for the whole experience? Â So why is it I feel like the one that must bend over backwards to get some service? Â Remember, you are the paying customer, not part of their, "they get rich, you get out asap," plan. Â The decor started out nice, but is really in the need of a make over now. Â  As for the other food here, it's okay, nothing above the other area establishments. Â The price is slightly higher than the area competition.

As my friend said, "this is the place for those who don't want to go all the way down to chinatown for some good soup dumplings and don't mind spending a few extra bucks." WISE WORDS. Here was a quote when we asked how spicy the fried rice was: us: "wait like........ is it inedible?" waiter: "it's....... acceptable." HAHA Food: - dan dan noodles: very delicious. can be a little on the spicier side, but the veggies and the meat work really well with the noodles. loved the noodle texture. simple noodle dish but tasty! - supreme spicy fried rice: my friend and i have a pretty good tolerance of spiciness so we may not be good judges BUT we both thought it really wasn't that spicy. it's more of the aftertaste that has the spicy kick, but it's not too strong to take away from the flavor. One thing I didn't like were the small bits of pork (or something) that i couldn't chew through so i just took them out. - scallion pancakes: good, but nothing special (i recommend putting the sauce from the dan dan noodles on it, for some extra flavor) - SOUP DUMPLINGS: the original beef were really good. they were not the BEST i've had, but they were solid! the broth was tasty, on the cleaner tasting side. We also got the spicy xiao long bao and they were really good too. my first ever spicy soup dumplings and i liked them. i personally liked the original more though. Service: average. Price: a little more expensive than what you would see in chinatown, but still not bad! (soup dumplings were about $8 for 6) BUT, they take credit cards! yay. As you can see, we ate a lot of spicy dishes... but luckily our bowels are still in tact. Overall, really good food here! Recommend to anyone who wants to check out a new soup dumpling spot in this area! I shall return to try some of the other foods. It's been open only 2 weeks and they already had a lot of people. impressive, but deserved.

So I happened upon this hip Turkish spot while waiting to hit a new exibit a couple blocks away at the Met. We rolled in here around 12pm and quickly grabbed cheeky seats at the bar while everyoe was struggling to get outdoor tables. The decore is funky. The staff is mostly former-Soviet satellite citizens speaking in their native tongues. The food is of a high-quality. We only really got the Meze plate that had a couple of the usual eats but also had a couple other articles of Turkish food that I'd never tasted - and they were off the hook. Toss in a couple Belvedere Screwdrivers first thing in the afternoon and this made the Met an even better experience than usual. Nice job Beyoglu - if I ever am in the area again - you'll get hit with my business.
Amazing pizza. So perfectly thin. The shroomtown pizza is on a whole different level.

Overrated, overpriced, and OVEREXPOSED. What is the big deal with this place? If fine dining (some restaurants are &27-$37 a head) in the middle of a cafeteria-esque floor with tourists walking around looking at you hits your soft spot - this place is for you! If roaming around inside the 30,000 sq ft "market" is your thing, be prepared to feel incredibly claustrophobic. The ceiling is about 12 feet high - not high enough with all the people inside. I could feel my breath condensating. On a brighter note, the expensive gelato was pretty good - ask for pistachio or vanilla bean flavors. Almost better than the ones in the motherland. Don't get sucked into this tourist trap like I did - you're better than that! Go to a specialty Italian deli where you won't overpay and wait in line for eternity.

This is my second time at Lupa, and both visits have been nothing short of amazing. Tonight three of us shared an assortment of cured meats, vegetable dishes, a special chicken entree and two deserts. The three of us left debating which dish was the best, and no one could decide. 'Its not as if anything was bad... Everything was great. It's a matter of what was the greatest!' The decor is also noteworthy- comfortable, chic and intimate, but the staff and music make me and my visiting friends feel at home. Finally, the wine list was amazing- and our waitress/bartender Emilia had great recommendations. We tried a range of white and red wines, and I particularly loved the after- meal Amaro. Try lupa. You can't go wrong- unless you fail to make a reservation!

Oh how I long for chicken and rice........drool. Why can't I find this in LA?!!! If anyone knows where I can get something like this, PLEASE msg me!!!! I got to this truck some time during the evening and the line wasn't too bad..about 10 people in front of us? The whole time I was thinking to myself..how great can it be..it's just chicken and rice........ I ordered the regular chicken and rice plate with the white sauce. Thank GOD i didn't get the spicy sauce because my friends said it was really spicy (she asked for just a little too). Without the spiciness, I basically inhaled the plate!! Such simple ingredients..but so DELICIOUS!! What is this white sauce?! I'm so sad I can't get some here in LA.........If I had a jet plane, I'd totally hope on it and fly myself to NY just for this. YES, THAT GOOD!

Postings for the opening of Fort Defiance have been appearing in my Google Reader and Inbox. What caught my attention was the mention of a "New Orleans Style" Muffaletta being served. Being from NOLA and a lover of the great sandwich, I grabbed my boyfriend, we hopped on our bikes and were in route to Red Hook. The spot is ABSOLUTELY fantastic. Every little detail made me smile with it's perfect placement and lack of pretense. What made me frown was finding out sandwiches are only served during lunch (currently 11:30am - 2:30pm). It's okay...still in the mood for a beverage. A lovely list of classic cocktails along with the point of recipe origin was listed on the menu. Between the two of us: Cucumber Collins - perfectly refreshing and very light Mai Tai - Instantly wishing to be on a beach watching sunset Watermelon Gin Punch - one of those drinks that I didn't know I wanted until it was right in front of me! Their own recipe and seriously I could have stayed for a few more. Prescription Juliep - Mint Juliep with Rye and Brandy...THE BEST JULIEP I'VE EVER HAD. seriously. We had hoped to make it back today for lunch but woke up a little too late (and it was raining). Hopefully will be back as soon as possible for my sandwich. Staff was lovely and this place is definitely worth a visit. If you have time on your hands...order a SUMO Collins. You have to go to find out ;)

Cute place. Ordered chef's prix fixe and green tea cheesecake with sake icecream. The green tea cheesecake with sake icecream was pretty damn good. There was a slight bitter flavor to the cheesecake from the green tea which I liked. I was skeptical about the sake icecream at first but changed my mind once I tasted it. It works for some reason. As for the prix fixe, it came with first course, black sesame icecream, which is basically vanilla icecream mixed with black sesame. The black sesame flavoring was not as strong as how I had it last time but still as good. Second course was the mango pudding with whipcream on top and and grapefruit whoopie pie. Â Mango pudding blew my mind. Grapefruit whoopie pie was also delicious. It's awesome how much flavor they can compact into both desserts. Finished off the prix fixe with scrumptious sesame short bread cookies and a macaron. Macaron tasted interesting, not the usual macarons that I usually have. It's delicious nonetheless. I love this place :)

AMAZING! I have been coming here for years and always left happy and fulfilled. The staff is very nice; just about all the waiters remember me. Their square slices, Caesar salad, baked clams, and chicken sorrento are amazingly delicious. I can't get enough of this place. They always make awesome desserts which I can't say no to. I will be a customer for life!

I've heard so much about this place but finally decided to try it on a Thursday night. Â I went with a friend and when we got there I was told that it would be about a 40 minute wait but i figured I might as well try it. Â There were probably 7 parties ahead of us but the line did move fairly quickly. Â We sat down in about 30 minutes and we had already decided what we wanted at that point so we got our food within 5 minutes of being sat. Â This place is the definition of a whole in the wall. Â Place is extremely small and great for parties of two; if you have a party of more than four, they will split you up into smaller groups. Â  The ramen itself was very good. Â I ordered the Spicy ramen with pork and added a steamed egg. I'm not a big fan of buying ramen but I thought this was pretty good. Â The only reason I gave this place four stars is because of the wait but I can see what all the hype is about.
I like this restaurant very much , all the special dishes taste wonderful which I've never tried before. Especially the different kind of cheeses and sausages.

it's so funny how we found this place. we were craving ramen and found an obscure address to a ramen joint. i started to ask this random guy on the street about ramen, then i saw his shirt "I heart Ramen" and i said, HEY! that's what we wanna eat, and so he pointed us in the direction to Ippudo. Like most NYC restaurants, you have to wait. i like the noodle choices. definitely get the soft boiled egg and a side of braised pork. who doesnt love braised meats?? AND, if you still have enough broth left in your bowl, you can re-up on noodles!!! who does that?? they will give you another "ball" of noodles to help you finish off the broth. awesome!! the entire waitstaff likes to yell at incoming guests. i guess this is japanese tradition to yell "welcome!!!!(!@#*^!*@#^!!!!" when customers arrive...or when an order is up...or maybe just whenever they feel like it, so the place is kinda loud. but it's a noodle joint. no need for ambiance.

Love the concept, but a little pricey. Â  I have only eaten here once. Â I really enjoyed it and unexpectedly loved the pineapple. Â My only gripe was the lack of main dish choices and the price. Â I felt like it just costs a couple dollars more than it should. Â It is sort of cafeteria style, so you don't think it should be $15-25 per person. It is not pricey enough for me to have sticker shock, but I sort of did anyway.

Yummy roti bread (like nan) & curry sauce. Â  Good noodle dishes. Â The coconut rice is heavenly and aromatic--I can easily down a couple bowls. Â  Our service was good, but can depend on your server. Â  Great value for a Zagat rated restaurant in the heart of Little Italy.

this is pork at it's best. go with a friend (or two) and order the Maialino al forno. it's a large section of the ribs, shoulder, loin, and belly. slow roasted for several hours, then the heat is blasted at the last second to form a crispy skin (which sort of tastes like pork rinds). it's not on the menu and they only have 16 orders of it per day (so make sure to call ahead and tell them to save one for your table!). it comes at a price of $72...but it's meant to be for 2-3 people. my family is from the philippines, so we have a good idea of what a good roasted pig tastes like...and trust me, it was bangin'. good luck staying awake after finishing it.

I stopped into The Grey Dog's Coffee one weekday morning expecting a quick, cheap, but delicious breakfast. I ultimately managed to get 2 of those. As soon as I stepped in, I was shocked to see so many people lounging around at such an early hour. I guess I was the only person in a rush to get to work Â The place is huge too, especially for a coffee/breakfast joint. The line moved fast, though, and I ultimately decided on a savory breakfast-the breakfast quesadilla with an iced coffee, of course. I was shocked at the price. $18 for breakfast? That is not what I had in mind for my pre-work breakfast trip. Although you order at the front counter, I was able to sit down and someone brought the quesadilla over to my table in a timely manner. Tucked inside the quesadilla was scrambled eggs, cheddar, roasted peppers, onions, mushrooms, and bacon with a side of sour cream and a delicious green salsa. It had the right stuff, baby. The quesadilla, albeit expensive, was definitely a large serving. I took Â 1/2 to go. Despite the cost, I was a happy camper. I would come back here for a real weekend, sit-down, chat over coffee type of breakfast but not for a quick bite before work.

After the wait and excitement finally we enjoyed the roast pork and soy chicken. Â Even if you fly to Hong Kong, I don't think you'll be able to find a place that beat their price. Â  I enjoyed the soy chicken more thank the roast pork. Â If you are traveling far to bring this home, like we did, here are a few tips: - Ask for extra ginger scallion sauce in a separate container. Â They didn't charge extra and didn't give us a hard time either. - Order the meat only, no rice. Â The rice came too soggy after we brought it home. Â  - make sure you share or else you'll be eating leftover for days. Â The portions are ridiculously huge. For my roast pork, big Wong is still number one on my book.

This place was full of attitude. The food was not that great. You get what you pay for. I heard Beet is ten times better then Song. I am done with this place. Â Never understood all the hype. bye bye song.

After getting take out about a month ago...we decided to go have dinner at Giovanni's Â and had a decent meal. Â We were greeted and seated by Giovanni himself, which is always a classy touch, plus he is a good looking man. He told us the specials and recommended a yummy red wine (wish remembered the name of the bottle)...so I ordered the seafood pasta special, and the stuffed squid app and the bf ordered the meatballs and the tagliatelle special...the squid and meatballs came out first...the squid was ok, nothing to write home about, but the meatballs...OMG...the softest meatballs I have ever had in my life, they were so delicate and yummy! Â My pasta dish was good, nice amount of mussels, clams, squid and shrimp in a spicy red sauce, while the bf tagliatelle was ok, needed salt. Â We decided to share a tiramisu and I'm a tiramisu snob, Â I was actually pleased with the tiramisu, it was cream, soft and just how right.

I really love Paprika. Â My good friend brought me here many times when I visited her in the past. Â I went back recently for brunch and it's still the best brunch deal on St. Marks St. Â $13 for an entree, coffee/tea AND a OJ/mimosa/bellini. Â The place is a cute, cozy spot with an airy feel and super nice staff.

We came for a friend's birthday, which we made a reservation for, and they were completely unprepared. We thought we made a horrible mistake showing up 10 minutes late, but our table was not ready for an hour and a half, and then they switched tables on us after taking our drink order. Now for the food, one word, overpriced!!! 2 empanadas for $9 that are totally average, yikes!! I had the chicken stuffed with plantains, cheese, and mushrooms, and it was honestly pretty bad. When you're starving and you think the food sucks, there's an issue. My chicken was dry, the filling just tasted like canned mushrooms, motzerella cheese, and half a plantain. Nothing about this place tasted Cuban. And to top it off, it was all expensive. We had a $500 bill, and they never even brought out a slice of cake or something for the birthday girl. I have no idea where the 4 stars on yelp comes from. Not ever coming back. Good thing the rest of our night was amazing.

I'm giving them 5 stars because the only issue we had was so small, and I am certain it had to do with the newness of the staff, who have , I am sure, become adept at everything. We tried the Writing Room one day for Brunch. We are big fans of the Parlor which is operated by the same people and thought, let's give it a go. Now, I don't know how many YELP readers, if any, ever had a chance to dine at Elaines, which is the former tenant. Obviously the reputation for Elaines preceded it and I really felt that people (at the end of Elaines days in business) went there for the ambiance, not necessarily the cuisine. I am happy to report that the Writing Room has kept an air of that "Elaine's-esque" era and amplified it by leaps and bounds with its sharp dÃ©cor. Sure, you still can find pics of Truman Capote on the wall amongst many other notable scribes and performers, but it is a modern, clean, more updated feel. So on ambiance it gets an "A" We were 6 for Brunch, which has been known more than once to overwhelm the less confident server, which was not our experience at all at The Writing Room. Due to our large number we made a reservation. Immediately upon arrival we were shown to our table. Took a blink or three before anyone came over and asked about our desire for beverages(that'd be the only issue, which I'm sure has been overcome) We had a mixed bag of a crew so there were a couple Bloody Mary's as well as lots of Sparkling water. The Bloody Marys were great. Spicy, great garnish and really hit the spot. As it was our first visit we ordered an assortment of appetizers, who am I kidding? we ordered one of EVERY appetizer! Everything was great. The entree's came out hot and were cooked to perfection We tried everything from the Chicken Salad to the Salmon to the pancakes, and all items were a smashing success. I would highly recommend THE WRITING ROOM, and look forward to our next visit! with love, The UES critic ! xxx

I got there at 12pm for Brunch and the restaurant was super crowded from the people waiting for a table to Â the people waiting for all parties to be presented. I am amazed that they made their waffles fresh right in front of the customers which is pretty entertaining to the kiddies. Finally the hostess seated me and my friend at a table. I ordered the Gaufre Dame Blanche and my friend got the Gaufre Banana Split. The portion size was small...just one waffle on a plate topped with whatever you ordered and it cost 10 bucks. Mainly I enjoy the vanilla bean icecream more than the waffle itself. I felt that we were being rushed because they are people waiting for a table. Shoot Â we were paying customer too...WTF!! The experience wasn't as awesome as I thought it would be. I am a bit disappointed.

Cheryl's is a brand-new place in my neighborhood! Today, I came in for lunch. The service was friendly and the food was excellent! They have a soup, salad, and sandwich menu for the lunchtime crowd (prices ranging from $6-$8). The breads the sandwiches came on were outstanding! It's a quiet neighborhood spot (but I can't promise it'll remain quiet when people start hearing about this place)! The service isn't terribly speedy -- this is a more leisurely place. Their scones and muffins are great. Their brownies come with highest recommendations. They are homemade-tasting, chock full of chocolate chips, moist, and warm! A must-have! The coffee is excellent and so is the hot chocolate! Later, they have much fancier (and more expensive) dinner offerings. And -- I have not come in during dinner hours, but I have walked past Cheryl's during dinnertime, and the SMELL is phenomenal! Also, it looks like it is a great date spot, because the place is lit by candles during dinner-hours. UPDATE: I have been coming here regularly since this place opened. The food is always delicious, innovative, and healthy. Also, the service has sped up a great deal since this place opened. It has also really increased in popularity -- last week when I went, the place was FULL!
Just went there for lunch. Ambiance was amazing. Wine + Food +Dessert = Amazing. Â :) waitresses were amazing and always checking if we needed anything. More like a family restaurant though.

Just visited Ivy for Happy Hour last week while in Manhattan. Cool, urban vibe at the bar with great happy hour specials. Â  I had the burger and it was spectacular. Â Procecco special was $5 or $6 per glass. Â You can't go wrong. Â  The bartender was very friendly and attentive. Â Location is easy to get to from Columbus Circle/Central Park area. Â Only a few blocks away. Â  I will definitely go back for Happy Hour the next time I am in the area.

Antonio, Antonio, where for art thou Antonio??? Â Our waiter Antonio was the best, looking all cute with his mohawk and his fine customer service! Â And thanks Antonio for that extra pitcher of tropical sangria "gratis"!! Girls Night Out with Quana Q. and the gang always makes for a good time. Â I must sadly say that I had to take a star away because the booth we were in was so doggone small that my feet kept falling asleep! Â But of course, I won't let that ruin my taste buds. I opened my 3 course meal with salmon ceviche accompanied with popcorn and naturally the greedy girl in me sampled the calamari and gallitos that were on the table as well. Â Second course was the duck 2 ways. Â Okay, let me just start by saying that hands down this is the best duck I ever tasted! Â Braised, moist, tender duck on a bed of bitter greens with a sweet plantain lentil "pulled duck"stew. Â Dessert (you already know how I heart desserts) was a Latin twist on creme brulee with raspberries and soft baked cookies. Â  I was surprised by how many people were strolling in getting their eat on at 10:30pm. Â Or maybe they were just coming for the fabulous sangria. Â Brunch at Calle is definitely next on my list. *NOTE: Popcorn accompanied with ceviche is so damn good. Â It's actually my new staple.....try it with soup instead of crackers!

Came here with a friend one night after work for a bottle of wine and some pizza, and must say, Sofia's has a great, warm ambience and very friendly, helpful waitstaff (although I was at first admittedly intimidated at first with all the tattoos). Â Would definitely go back next time I want wine after work!

This place is legit. If you read my other reviews, you can clearly see I am not one who just says everything is great. I'm especially critical of Italian food because I cook it myself, and use only the finest ingredients. This place does it better than I do. There's no other place on earth I would order lasagna besides this place. It is fantastic. The cold cuts are as if I shopped for them myself in an old fashioned Italian Pork Store in Brooklyn or Staten Island. Yum. The atmosphere is great. Down to earth, all about the food. You used to hear about places like this, and thought they died out. You'd be wrong. There's one left, so get here ASAP.

I really like this restaurant...its on a small quiet street...there is a beautiful garden on the inside with flowers, trees, the food is delicious especially the crispy cauliflower..a cute lil bunny ran past our table while we were eating
I have been going to this place for 10+ years reservation for tomorrow showed up tonight empty and rude hostess would not seat us thanks. Something about your restaurants everyone has an attitude.

i really don't get it. how does this place get a 28 on zagats (same as jean georges, per se, le bernadin). the pad see ew was OK (about the same as the lemongrass chain), the curry dish had chicken that was super dry... even the thai iced tea was just average. what am i missing? maybe it's me as I think song in park slope is super overrated too... so i guess if you like song, you will probably love this place

Didn't like the wait which was an hour and half long. But the service was great and the food was amazing. I wouldn't say that it was worth the wait but if there was no wait I would give it five stars.

My only complaints are that the ATM is like buried in some weird corner, and they always run out of Ruffles ranch dip. Those flaws considered, this is easily the best Deli in ABC City. You get 2 pickles with one sandwich! Yeah!!

One of those little known gems in the East Village. Feels homely, in a good way. Excellent ramen, and occasional Tokyo Bossa Nova on vocals and guitar if you're at the right day and the right time. Very low key.

Dayyyyyum. My roomie and I went to Fette Sau last night for the first time. The space is sooo cute, but it was packed so we got take out (luckily we live right around the corner). There are three long picnic tables, and it would be a great place to go with a bunch of friends if you could get enough seating, but it seems like its always that packed. We shared half a pound of brisket, a quarter pound of pork belly, a side of burnt end baked beans and a side of dante's german potato salad. Everything was absurdly amazing. The whole thing came out to $26. A ridiculously delicious BBQ dinner for $13 each - need I say more??

I yearned Greek cuisine and ventured out to the EV to accompany a friend for a delightful meal. As expected, on a Fri night - business was booming. Said friend and I were seated at the center table to wait for an open table. Which to me, was perfectly acceptable. We quenched our thirst with a truly unique Macedonian/Greek Sauvignon Blanc. Within several minutes, a table was made available. The service was impeccable. Water kept flowing without questions. Waitstaff was on point, knowledgeable and in no way overbearingly nice. Without fail, I order a simple Greek salad. However, this salad was far from simple. The tomatoes were sublime. I bet they have a secret garden in the kitchen. It was sweet and juicy. The wrapped grape leaves had the expected ingredients: rice, ground meat (in this instance, it was veal) and delicately seasoned with all the right herbs and spices. My main course was the "psari sta karvouna" which translates to the best fish, served whole I've had - in a while. The special of the evening was a Branzino. Perfection. My dinner, thus far was phenomenal. To rate my friend's entree, admittedly was very good. But, I know what I like and, let's just say - I'm glad I do. The item was the "lavraki me tsigarellia" - it was a striped bass with a pistachio crust and a side of chard and spinach sauteed with celery, fennel, onions, tomatoes and crumbled feta. I prefer simplicity. A little salt, pepper, olive oil and fresh lemon juice. My fish was devoured, head and all. And let's not forget the dessert, because... well, why not? Not too keen on overly sweet sweets so I insisted we get the Greek yogurt dish with a sour cherry mousse. It was served with a crispy Phyllo dough smack in the middle. Light, refreshing and just my way of ending an already perfect meal. We were the last patrons for that evening so, we thanked the attentive staff of Pylos and I made a mental note to write this well deserved review. I shall be back as frequently as my wallet can handle and perhaps with a party bus.

Surprisingly good location in Times Square! This place has a lot of seating (but you'll still want a reservation), and all the food is ordered family-style. Each platter is expected to feed around 2-3 people (and thus costs around $20-30 each), although a very hungry Italian-food-enthusiast could probably finish a dish by him/herself. They have a fairly good selection of appetizers, pastas, and other entrees. The calamari was great, as was the three kinds of pasta our table got. For dessert, we tried the Titanic, which was a veritable heap of brownie, ice cream and whipped cream. To top it all off service was great as well!

Their constant line is evidence of high-quality food served fresh. Pile up a plate full of steak, chicken, vegetables, some more steak, maybe some beans, and a little more chicken...and you're going to pay about $7. It's ridiculously cheap and ridiculously good!

When I visited this amazing restaurant as a birthday present, I had no idea what I was in for. I'd never even heard of Bouley, but apparently there's a lot to research. There's Bouley Botanical, the urban farms performance kitchen. How about the Test Kitchen, where for $175 Â "students will watch and ask questions as chefs from the Bouley kitchen craft fresh, seasonal ingredients into a beautifully presented tasting menu with ideal wine pairing." And there's "Brushstroke," taking unique seasonal ingredients and putting them to work in Asian cuisine with that perfect touch of sophistication. Yes, there's quite a bit to Mr. Bouley than the restaurant of his namesake. This review concerns the luncheon tasting menu, which was an eye-popping $35 before they hiked the price. The Black Cod Marinated with pistachio miso, heirloom tomatoes, elderflower, homemade raspberry vinegar, tonka bean and fresh verbena was breathtaking. I was a bit surprised at the use of heirlooms here, as I personally find them to be the Cousin Oliver of the tomato family. And elderflower teamed with verbena is a natural treatment for sinusitis, so their applications here are equally baffling. However, the chef is obviously a mage because it all came together flawlessly. The mushroom soup could very well be the most amazing soup I've ever had. It was masterfully prepared with the right thickness, not overly rich but very mushroomy in the best way. I don't see it on their online menu right now but if the Forager's Treasure of Wild Mushrooms with sweet garlic, special spices, grilled toro and black truffle dressing is anything near as good, I'd say it's worth trying. As a surprising kicker, our dessert seemed to take forever. Before we expressed any discomfort, Bouley came through with style, offering a large platter of various sugary treats that eclipsed our paltry little order tenfold. There was so much on deck we couldn't come anywhere near to finishing it all. And to top it off, they still brought out the original order of Hot Valrhona Chocolate Souffle with coffee ice cream and chocolate mousse. To say that it was impeccable is to quite simply sound repetitive here, as I'm singing their praises like I'm opening at Carnegie Hall. Short story, put this gold mine in your bookmarks because as great as the New York eating scene is, Bouley is as top shelf as it gets.

Remember when you visited Greece and ate so much good food you had to be dragged to the airport on the way out? Remember the fresh tomatoes, feta cheese and perfectly cooked meats & fish? Want 5-star Greek home-style cooking? Come here. I won't spoil anything, but would come here everyday if I could. Highly recommended.

Guinness Shake!!! I have to start it off with this I really liked it. A good friend had me dying to go and try it and it was worth it. The sliders were the best I ever had. The sauces are pretty good to. I would 100 percent go back again. The only problem I had was the place is kind of narrow.

Went here for Easter Sunday Brunch. Service was terrible. They were out of coffee. There was a huge wait for the orders of 2 of the 3 people at the table. We were ready to leave before the food arrived. The waitress, seeing that we were anxious (after waiting roughly 40 minutes for a mozzarella sandwich and an omelette) asked if we were in a hurry. And by the way, the place wasn't even that crowded when we were there. Only after we left did we realize they didn't even bring us some of the things we orders and they charged us for them. Not a good experience.

One of the best brunch places in NYC! Amazing toffee glazed brioche bun! Although their thick cut bacon is nothing close to the one I had at Peter Luger and their porchetta is a little on the dry side(I'd prefer Porchetta's version) , their prosciutto was ok and the Malfatti Al Maialino was just delicious! I can't wait to try their dinner menu.

I can't stop raving about this butcher to all of my friends! Actually, I've told everyone I know about it. This is a whole animal, organic, humanely raised, locally sourced butcher and it is halal. Plus, the place is spotless. Not only that, the prices are so good. I love food and the butchers there share my passion for it. They are so helpful and nice! Go there!

Had this place in my bookmarks...finally made it there last night. Â They actually messed up our reservation, but sat us anyway, which was warranted since the place was not full when we got there. Â  We shared all our plates, which was just enough for 3 females. Â The calamari was awesome! Â Def suggest this as your appetizer. Â We had the lamb chops and a special tortellini w/prosciutto in a white cream sauce. Â The lamb was inconsistent as we each had one pc and each had a different take...one was dry one was good with lots of fat, and one was just ok. Â The tortellini was pretty good, but did not knock my socks off. Â If I was in the neighborhood, I would try it again, but there's a lot of other places on my list I'd go to first.

In General I liked the place, lets start there. Â Service was good attentive and responsive to our needs. Â We got our food in a timely manor. Â The food was good at the very least. Â  Here's the problem I had with the place. Â I've passed this place by a dozen times and if it wasn't for yelp I would have never known it existed. Get some lighting out side dude. Â It's dark inside. Â I'm an older guy but I don't think My eyes are going that bad yet. Â I mean I don't need glasses to read and i had a hard time with the lighting inside. I know paying con ed sucks but one light here and there would help. Â Oh yeah get rid of the christmas lights it's tacky. Â The decor Â was just plain also. The community table in the middle was a nice touch. Â Build off of that and bring the place together a little more. Â  The next thing that all the things that I drooled over on the pictures here were not on the menu. Â Dude you gotta keep the favorites whatever they are. Â I showed the waiter pictures of what I wanted and they weren't making it anymore. Â He said that they change the menu every so often. Â If your comfort food at the very least have a Chicken fried steak. Â maybe it's just me. Â  I went with my 2 daughters and we all had Burgers (For that i would have gone to Bareburger which BTW are amazing). Â That's not to say the burgers weren't good, they were. Â  Another thing is that the Soda choices are one of those specialty sodas which for the most part are not good IMO. Â My daughter ended up drinking water because they didn't have Coke or Pepsi. Â Gotta have something to fall back on right for people like us. Â I mean Bareburger has there own soda but at least it taste good and close to the "real thing". Â  What we had we enjoyed and it was good, no dought. Â I will go back for brunch and see what they have then. Â They no longer make the pork belly sandwich thing either for brunch. Â  3 Burgers 2 sides 3 sodas $60. Â  I don't know maybe a bit pricey, and I'm not hipster enough. Â Maybe it's me. I will go back a few more time because they do cook good and one visit is never indicative. Â I just hate surprises.

A tiny gin joint with sophisticated drinks and a lovely interior. Classy without pretensions. You could roll in wearing mega-heels with your friend in jorts on a bike and both be happy. And your friend could park said bike in a designated spot by the door. They'll give you a solid craft brew or a super-complicated absinthe concoction. Hell, you can order a shot of Chartreuse. And a Bud light. Heavy on the Brooklyn vibe.

Before this month, my last trip to this Tony DiNaps was over 4 years ago. I remembered it fondly with its huge portions, giant dining room and the most deliciouzzzz strawberry shortcake I've ever had. My most recent trip shattered those fond memories. *glass breaks* My boyfriend and I went to Tony DiNaps for one reason - it was only three blocks away from the theater we were going to. Â This was on the polar vortex pt 2 day where it was snowing and below freezing in the single digits. So my plans for a delicious ramen dinner nearby went kaputz and we came to Tonys instead - because again, it was freakin close to the theater. We ordered the baked clams, pasta bolognese and the broccoli rabe. The baked clams were kinda soggy. The best baked clams are super crispy, crunchy on top and then delicious inside. These were not so. The broccoli rabe wasn't bad. It was easily the best thing we ate that night. The most disappointing was the pasta bolognese. They gave us just straight up tomato sauce with bits of meat. There was not even the slightest hint of cream. It was just bland. I ended up dousing my entire plate with parmesan just to add some flavor. The service was okay. My waiter had an extremely thick, and heavy Italian accent. I wondered if he was actually Italian or just an actor practicing his accents on customers. He was nice enough, but sorta slow and and whenever we needed him - he was too busy goofing off to notice we were trying to flag him down. All in all, I should've known better than to come to this tourist trap. At least with Olive Garden I get unlimited buttery bread and a mint after dinner. If you're really in the mood for family style Italian near Times Square, just go to Carmine's instead. And if you specifically want Tony's, go to the UES location.

I've walked past here various times but after almost 9 months of living in South Slope, I have finally discovered this place and I am so glad that I did! We came here for brunch on a Sunday and were promptly seated. The restaurant was pretty full and there were a lot of tables despite the size of the restaurant (it isn't too big) but it does have a small bar. Against my better judgment, I ended up doing the $16 unlimited alcoholic brunch versus the $10 unlimited coffee/juice/tea option. With my mimosa, I ended up ordering the eggs benedict, which came with a side of bacon (4 strips) and potatoes. My date ordered his sake bloody mary with french toast which came with a side of fruit. Both were delicious but its only the egg dishes that come with potatoes and bacon. If you're definitely wanting more food, I would order the eggs benedict. The french toast was very yummy and sweet (even before dipping it in syrup) but it came in small individual pieces of bread. Either way, it was a delicious, boozy brunch which ended up with me passing out for the rest of the afternoon. Good service, yummy food and drinks. Definitely a solid brunch restaurant that you need to hit up!

I like this place! I thought it was a bar, but it's more of a restaurant with a small bar in it. Â Nice ambience, music wasn't too loud and crowd wasn't too skeavy. Â There's an upstairs and a base level, both with a bar and tables to sit at (waiter service for the tables). Â Menu looks awesome but we had eaten somewhere else that night. Â My main reason to come here was because they serve Pimm's Cup Pitchers!! $25 each, they give about 5 drinks altogether, not bad!
