Although I have to say the Pimm's Cup at Highlands is much better...it was still good. So a nice little tidbit of info, there is a third level to this bar, that would go completely un-noticed, unless a member of a bachelor party came over to you and said "Hey, do you want to join my friends for an open bar, private party on the third floor???" Â Needless to say, we had a great time and it was awesome being in this little room, without a huge crowd, that overlooked the street. Â It seems as though they had a dinner party first, where the chefs cooked in an open kitchen right in front of their tables. Â Pretty cool. Â And the Flourless Chocolate Cake that they had extra of was to die for :) Â can't wait to try the rest of the menu. Â Nice spot in the village.

Grimaldi's under the bridge used to be my go-to spot, when I visited NYC. Â Since Grimaldi's franchises can now be found in Phoenix, Vegas, Denver, etc., I've most certainly gotten my fill of them, as a west-coaster. This time, we decided to try Juliana's, since the original oven is where the magic happens. Â It was outstanding. Â The pies were cooked perfectly, the toppings were all top-quality, the service was excellent. Â I liked the charred undercrust and leoparding Â better than Grimaldi's. Best part? Â The line was 1/2 the length of the Grimaldi's line and moved much faster. Â I'd say we stood outside maybe twenty minutes on a very busy Saturday during Labor Day weekend. Â Overall, I liked the pizza, friendly service, and line much better than that of their next door neighbors. Juliana's is my new go-to spot for Brooklyn pizza.

I adore this place! Cozy ambiance, great, simple tasty food and courteous service. I definitely recommend coming early as Jadis can get packed fairly quickly. But anytime I've had to wait; the staff was always polite, offered a seat at the bar if there was room and made sure to seat me and my party as soon as they could.

Sometimes its better to review a place once you go back a few times. And unfortunately for Oxcart, I hadn't reviewed when I first came here last summer. A friend of mine lives in this neighborhood so when I come down to visit, he loves to take me to spots in this up and coming hood. I went for dinner and liked it, went for brunch that same weekend and loved it; the cute blondish brown haired waitress was fast, friendly, funny and the dude bartender was cool. Music was great (smiths def!), the hash was incredible and the coffee ruled over my hangover. I left and couldnt wait to come back to brooklyn for more. I came back a few weekends ago and couldn't believe the change. The staff was on edge and nervous, new possibly but i couldn't tell you since i'm not from the area. We ordered coffee that was completely forgotten until our food came (something forgivable because it was pretty busy). Once our food came, i bit into my hash and realized it was cold in the middle. Â I waited for someone to come and after i wasnt acknowledged or asked how the food was (i was a manager in a place for a while so i tend to be a bit patient), i decided to walk to the bathroom only to feel bad for the staff. The chef or manager was pretty fu*king mean. I heard something along the lines of "...if you cant do it ill find someone who can." Not exactly a motivational tool to positively influence yours employees dude. I just paid the bill and bounced. From here on out, I'm going to stay on the professional side of the neighborhood on Cortelyou road. I hate to be an ass, but this place would've gotten a 5 the first time, but between the cold food, the staff,and the jerk comment, it went to a -1 star very fast. .Also, i asked the waiter how they made the pretzel, and he told me they actually don't make it there. if thats the mutual thing everyone loves and its not even made in the place, what does that say about the rest of the menu? Go back to your old way and maybe, just maybe this spot will make it.
Excellent place with delicious healthy food at a really reasonable price for lunch or dinner. Become one of my staples

I had the pleasure of going to lunch @ Trattoria today and WOW! What a wonderfully pleasant experience I had from the time I stepped in the door till the time lunch was over and I exited the premises. To Start, your greeted with 5 star Customer service and seated thus the same. They have some really jaw dropping art sculptures on the walls located throughout the restaurant. The customer service is at 5 star's plus in that your greeted and cared for straight to the dining table. Ohhhh how I love this and couldn't have been more impressed and certainly very happy:) Our waiter was awesome and extremely attentive with outstanding service. We were a party of 3 and ordered the following appetizers & lunch offerings. We ordered the Burrata Caprese, (Ohhhh How fresh, light and deliciously creamy this was)! We also ordered the Braised Octopus & Calamari and I can Â honestly say this isn't a dish I would've done on my own as I'm a fried food Â seafood lover normally but this was an outstanding dish in that it was light but very flavorful with delicate pieces of very fresh Octopus, Calamari and cherry slightly stewed tomatoes. Another friend ordered the Meatball Pizza and was equally pleased with their selection. While I didn't taste this personally I was assured that the Meatball Pizza was outstanding. In addition I ordered the sausage/peppers & onions fennel which was bursting in flavor and so delicious. We did not have dessert due to time constraints but they certainly did look quite appetizing and delicious as they have servers who come around with a tray of their fine deserts on offer for you to choose from and take right then and there. Dining here was a grand experience and an experience I look forward to doing again. The lunch portion sizes were small but fitting for midday, although the prices were high. The dining experience was exceptional and this includes the customer service. If you have clients and or other business you need to impress with nothing short of fine dining this is definitely the place to go.

My obsession with Bao Haus had me jumping for joy when Bao Shoppe finally opened in my hood. However, expectations versus reality were a bit out of kilter. First, i want to compliment the owner for a great looking spot: plenty of seating, art gallery, and prompt service. However, I think the portions are way too small to justify the price. $23 for 2 people (5 baos) pus a soda, and I was hungry ten minutes later. I got the OG (pork belly) and the Texan (brisket), and though I adore pork belly, the bao I got was 60% unedible fat. With an already small portion, this definitely hindered my enjoyment. I'll def continue making a trek to the city to get the real thing.

My boyfriend and have walked by this place many times and we always say that we are going to eat there sometime. Finally, we went there for dinner and every dish that we had was amazing and blew our minds! First we had the steak tartare, which came with a quail egg on top and a side of arugula, pickled onions, toasted bread and horse radish cream. Portion size was good and it was so delicious. For my main entree I had the buttermilk fried quail with spoonbread and collard greens. It came with two dipping sauces - buttermilk dill and honey. My boyfriend got the Berkshire pork chop which came with glazed ribs, fried cheesy grits and sautÃ©ed greens. Both were mouth wateringly good! His entree was a better deal though. For dessert we had a the sundae which had toasted marshmallow and hazelnut ice cream. We will definitely be coming back here again!

What a meal! Having studied abroad in Barcelona, I was excited to try this Tapas haven on the West side. Rule #1: Sit in the back! They have an accordion roof that opens up on nice days. The decor is beautiful with velvet chairs and dark wood tables. Flowers are everywhere. And I mean, fresh flowers, everywhere! It's divine. Looking over the menu, it was hard to choose what we wanted. Everything sounded great. We tried to Crispy Artichokes (Grade: A) and the Garlic Shrimp (Grade: A+). They even offered to bring us more bread so we could "finish the delicious sauce". Score. For dinner, I had the red snapper pesca del dia (fish of the day). It was broiled on a bed of lemony potatoes and a light salad. It was light, but filling, and I literally licked my plate clean. My friend got the Half Chicken Breast which was grilled perfectly and coated with coarse salt which we found out was from the island of Ibiza. I think that made the meal for Â her. It gave the chicken a great crunch. We finished each bite off with a sip of Tempranillo red wine (a Spanish red). The food + atmosphere + service was all around terrific. At the end of the meal, the owner introduced himself, told us about the special salt that they get flown in, and was so inviting! Not only was the food fabulous, but it was certainly an experience for us. I recommend this for a date. There was a couple next to us who were very lovey-dovey, and while I would usually find this, how should I put this, annoying, I found myself wanting to be there on a date!!! To my next boyfriend, please plan our first date here. I will 100% be returning to Salinas. You should too.

Gyu Kaku has multiple locations throughout the city and I've been to two of them. The interior are similar by nature and have a certain warm and comforting feel to it which is by all means a welcome atmosphere especially when you are getting together to eat some delicious bbq. I went to the one at 44th st and it was not crowded like the one at Astor place. I came in late as my friends had already been seated and started eating without me (Great friends). The place is rather confusing and big at first and I had no idea where they were but the receptionist directed me to various locations and ask if I could find them which was surprise because usually the receptionist ignores me as I look for my friends through this maze of a restaurant. I found my friends shortly after and when I sat down I did not have a chance to look at the menu but I am certain it is the same as the one I went to at Astor. We had pork belly, beef tongue, duck breast, and six other dishes of various different cuts of beef. They offer 3 types of sauces on the side, however, I did not find it necessary as the meats were marinated well which penetrated the meat so when it was cooked, you could clearly see the caramelization. Every bite was mouth watering and I could not help myself as I came back for seconds. The staff was fairly attentive and changed our grill as often as they could so we did not have to wait long to eat between the intervals. In conclusion, it was a good experience as although I am not a fan of BBQ especially in the city due to overpriced dishes of meat, this place happen to win me over with their attentiveness and service. The bbq is well worth it and you would not be disappointed in trying Gyu Kaku, however I would stay away from the sauces as although they are unique and delicious. I felt that it overpowered the taste that you can only get from caramelization of the meat and it made it way too salty.

I'm leaning more towards 2 1/2 stars, but the watermelon ale was extremely refreshing and tasty. Â They have a nice selection of beer and I also enjoyed the 90 min IPA which had a strong flavor but was delicious and not at all bitter. Definitely has the look of a chain restaurant or a college dorm. Â They have more posters, taps, and other items on their ceiling than you've seen in any TGI Fridays or Applebees... combined. Â  Staff wasn't that friendly, service was odd - 3 people would get their drinks and the other 3 would have to wait, then 1 drink would come and then we'd wait and a second waitress would bring the last 2. Â Very strange system they had going on... or lack there of. The burgers, fries, and nachos were tasty, but definitely over priced. Â  If you are coming with a group definitely grab a table in the back, but fair warning it gets warm back there. Bathrooms were gross, yes most are in the city, but still just saying...

This place is great! It's very cramped and looks like a whole in the wall, but it all works so well. The music selection is rap/hip hop ranging from the 90s to present, exactly what I like. The music isn't too much though, so don't let that discourage you. I was seated at the bar with my sister, so we had the bartender as our waiter. For drinks, I asked for the jalapeno lime margarita received a habanero margarita (not even the habanero grapefruit one). And I really don't like habanero. I blame the bartender for mishearing me because I said it pretty clearly. My sister got the red sangria, which was delicious. For food, we got the guacamole, which was awesome, some of the best guac I've had! We also got the enchiladas verdes, which were amazing as well. We got a chorizo dish as well, which was nostalgic of recent trips to Europe. Unfortunately I don't remember details of the order, but it was definitely some of the best Mexican food I've had. I give it a 4/5 because of the waiter's unfortunate errors and because it was slightly too cramped for my liking, especially since there were no more coat hangers for us to put our long coats.

This place is a bit of an enigma for me. The dishes are creative and unique, but the flavor just wasn't there in some of the dishes. I ordered the halibut with truffles, the crab appetizer and my friend ordered something that looked like Spam but was a pate. The crab crostini was delightful, but they couldn't make it any smaller. I realize I am paying for atmosphere but give me something. I left starved. The night life was incredible and the atmosphere was insane fun. I will come back for the drinks but not the food. Oh well.
Great food, cute drinks, good service. Whenever I have friends in from out-of-town, this is the first Brooklyn spot I take them to, and they always walk away wishing they lived here.

Bareburger is a great place to dine-in or get takeout when craving a good, juicy burger. Â We got takeout here the other night, and even though we had to wait an extremely long time to get our order, for some reason it was worth it. Â The next time I ever order from here, it will definitely be from their online portal so that I can decrease the next wait time. I decided to build my own burger (turkey on a brioche bun). Â The bun was very soft and fluffy, the turkey meat was sensational, and the lettuce, tomato, pickles, avocado, and turkey bacon all made this one delicious burger. Â I only wish that it was warmer by the time I got back to my hotel to eat it. Â I must say that the burger was huge and I wasn't able to eat a side with it; however, I did have one fried pickle just to see how it would taste, and it was good. I definitely recommend this place for any good burger lover out there!
Memorable food--the best spaghetti I have ever had--simple and flavorful. Â Polenta was sensational and short rib ravioli exceptional. Â A little on the pricey side but worth it!

My boyfriend kept raving about Marlow and Sons after he went there a couple of times without me, so we decided to go again so I could check it out for myself. It's a bit of a trek from the Bedford L station (I keep forgetting how long Brooklyn blocks are!), but it's not too bad. Marlow and Sons is located next to Diner, and in fact the two restaurants have the same owner and share their chef. The menu at Marlow and Sons is really limited, and mostly consists of appetizers, panini and small plates, as well as a few entrees. Â I also believe they change their menu pretty frequently. We ended up sharing a bunch of stuff: - Oysters: they only had East coast oysters the night we were there. They're usually not my favorites, but the ones they had (from Maine, if I remember well), were actually very tasty. - Mushroom crostini: delicious. - Chicken liver pate: that was a disappointment. I usually really like pate, but this one had a very strong taste, and we just could not eat it. But our server was nice enough to take it back and not charge us for it. - Soup of the day: potato-based soup with romaine and bacon croutons and a raw oyster... pretty tasty, but not out of this world. - Brick chicken (entree): this was just delicious... I normally don't really like to order chicken, as it can be quite bland, but this one was really juicy, with a really crispy and yummy skin: just great (almost as good as the one they serve at Sfoglia!). So overall the food was really good. Their drinks are also great: I strongly recommend the dill gibson, which is delicious (they pickle their own onions): we had four of them each!! Service is also really friendly, and the atmosphere is great: nice sidewalk seating, and beautiful restaurant inside as well. I'd go back for sure. 4-1/2 stars.

Went on the recommendation of a yelp elite and holy smokes, it was everything she described. Trendy ambiance but not pretentious, everyone was very friendly. The cocktails are a must try!! I ordered the My Thai and was amazed that a drink could be so artfully crafted. Appetizers were smaller than usual portions and we came with friends so we were able to share a few plates. We were a table of four and ordered 4 appetizers including the kangaroo carpaccio which was really small but delicious. Foie gras torchon was executed well, wagyu beef tongue was exciting and the oysters with shiso leaf is now the only way I want my fried oysters. We had a few snacks before coming here unfortunately and were too full to try the entrees but rest assured, we are coming back soon to try the rest of the menu. Knock it back with their cocktails and you'll be one happy chap.

Solid food. Gnocchi: with braised rabbit, gnocchi was perfect, sauce was awesome, very hearty Tagliatelle: hubby practically licked the plate. 5 stars Octopus: definitely worth getting - thanks to the guys outside the restaurant who told us to get this. 5 stars Boss Tom: yum! Have a reservation. Try their cocktails. Come hungry for pasta

The Mother of ALL Cheesecake sits right here at this location. Maybe your mother could make it better, but she's not selling it to NY. You cannot possibly go to NYC and not visit Junior's. As a matter of fact this was told to me before I ever even dreamed of going into this city. I thought, how could a cheesecake be any different from the ones I grew up eating in Texas? Well, I got schooled real quick. There are two kinds of cheesecake in NY and there are great debates over which is better. There is Junior's: dense and crumbly and lemony with an almost breakable ledge around it. It just sort of falls apart at the edges, but the inside is heavy and thick. It's also doesn't have a lot of height, it's so dense I don't think it could hold its weight, not sure. But, it's exactly the way your cheesecake should taste. I think. Then there is the cheesecake that is NOT Junior's. It's light and with more of a cream cheese taste, less lemon. It's airy and tall. It smoother and sort of melts into your mouth. It's cheesecake lite, but I don't consider it to be true NY cheesecake. THIS is the true original. And you will crave it long after you've taken the last bite. I seriously cannot keep it around, it just disappears. Add your favorite topping, mine is cherries, but their strawberry one runs a very close second. They also have a million others, but the original should be the first one you taste, then go crazy on the less stellar flavors. When I think of NYC cheesecake I think of Junior's. Period, the end.

This place is now our number one go-to when we can't decide what we want for lunch or dinner. Â It's super affordable and they have outdoor space in the back. Â I like a good deal but I try my best to avoid this place on a Wednesday - it's a packed house and very chaotic. Â The prices are so reasonable that if it's your first time, please go any other night. Â  The first couple of times that I went here, I was a little confused but the person who runs your food was always very helpful. I've tried a bunch of their sandwiches, fries, salads and sangria. Â The sangria is a little weak so we typically go with the bucket of beer. Â This place has a bunch of vegetarian options too which makes it easy for everyone to find something that they like. Â It's a lot easier to go here with a small group of people 2-4 unless you go on an off-hour. Â Expect to wait a while for a table on a Wednesday night but we haven't had a long wait any other time we have gone. Â  They recommend 5 sandwiches but typically I am full off 3 - they also give you free chips!

We loved this place! Â On Saturday night we went to the village for some fun and a comedy show and decided on Las Ramblas for dinner. A true tapas place this great restaurant brought me back to my youth and my time living in Spain. The place was packed and we were able to secure a great high top table along the back wall away from the hustle and bustle of people coming and going. The boys had beer while the girls had both red and white sangria which they said was very, very good. Having felt at home, I ordered all sorts of tapas and only stopped because we were running short on time and were stuffed to the gills. The octopus and the baby calamari were prepared perfectly and our friends not being accustomed to eating as we like were more than willing to sample a little of everything. The tortilla espaniola was really great and I think it was the best I've had this side of the atlantic. I think we would all agree though that the favorite of the evening was the duck sausage and quail egg skewers. Wow were they delicious! All in all, we had at least 7-8 tapas and there wasn't a loser in the bunch. Come here and if you have an adventuresome palette, I promise you'll love it.

Easily the best food I have had in Brooklyn, everything tastes homemade and fresh, the staff is simply charming and the back dining area makes you feel like you're out of the city. Love and would go back anytime.

I came here for Restaurant Week with a couple of friends. Â I have had Mediterranean cuisine before but never Lebenese inspired food. Â  Overall, I had a pretty good experience here. Â The decor was very nice, the food was decent, and the waiters were friendly. Â  I ordered the following from the prix fix menu: 1. For starters, we ordered the Whipped Chankleesh, the Mouhamara and the Phoenician Fries. Â The Whipped Chankleesh was okay - it was really salty but I'm not sure if it was supposed to be like that or if they just made it really salty. Â I would give this a 3/5. Â The Mouhamara was unlike anything I've tried before but was really good. Â It had a sweet nutty taste to it that I enjoyed. Â I would give this a 4/5. Â The Phoenician Fries were nothing too special, but they were good. I would give this a 4/5. 2. For the entree, I got the Braised Lamb Shank. Â This came in the form of a burger, which surprised me as I was expecting something different. Â It was very good though. Â I'm not the biggest fan of lamb because it can sometimes have a "wild" taste that I don't particularly enjoy. Â However, they cooked it very well and the meat was very tender and didn't have a "wild" taste. Â It was also extremely filling and I almost couldn't finish it! Â I would give this a 4/5. 3. For desserts, I got the Labne Cheese Cake. Â It was a lot smaller than I imagined, but that's probably because I'm used to American restaurant's huge dessert portions. Â It was pretty good, but nothing too special stood out to me. I would give this a 4/5. In terms of decor, it was very nicely designed with high ceilings and cool decorations throughout the restaurant. Â I would give this a 4/5. Our waiter was also very friendly. Â One of the staff members had told me the wrong information when I asked him about something on the menu, but it wasn't a big deal. Â Overall, the service was a 4/5. So overall, I give the food, the decor and the service a 4/5. Â I would recommend this place.

The only reason I went is because a.) my friend from cali was in a venture to find the best pizza b.) i have an excuse to go to grimaldi's c.) my other friend from NY wanted to give it a whirl End result? Â Ok, anyone else who been here knows the wait sucks. Â Atleast the view there is beautiful, especially at night. Â Once we got inside, the staff are very helpful, and thoughtful. Â When we got the pizza it was ok. Â I'm not much of a fan of thin slices but I didn't feel that WOW factor eating. Â I just felt like I was eating an overpriced pie. Â I wont make any mistake that the ingredients in it was freshly made, but I got really annoyed that part of the crust is non-existant. Â Lol, no i shit you not, part of our pizza crust is not even there I dont even know what happened. Â Anyways, it was a great experience just to go and try, but I wouldn't come back. Â My friend who came from Cali wasn't really that impressed either.

I am going to have to agree with most of the other reviews on these empanadas! Â They were good! Â We got 6 of them for take out and ate a few hot and even had a few later in the evening cold and they were still good! Â I didn't dislike any of the ones we had but I would say maybe the Cubano one was the least favorite. Â All of the others we had were good. Â  I would come back if I were in the neighborhood next time!
The food here is incredible. The service was outstanding. I was very impressed with the menu options and the drink pairings. Well done.
Real pizza with real ingredients. Highly recommended.

We used to leave work extra early to try to get here early for lunch and make the first wave to be seated. Most of the time, we didn't make it there in time and ended up being in the second wave :( There is one chef there that's super nice when we sit at the bar and if we let him know that we're in a hurry to get back to work (after having waited for almost 45 mins to be seated), he whips up our dishes quickly and we don't have to wait until a waiter comes to take our order! Their spicy ramen is my favorite because of the straight homemade noodles! The pork belly and the broth were delish as well. I always ask to have an egg added in because a bowl of ramen is not ramen without an egg. This is seriously one of the BEST places in NY for ramen, if not THE BEST. The wait is definitely worth it. Wish I could savor the taste of their ramen in my mouth FOREVER.

Goddamn this place makes great tacos! I ordered the cola braised pork taco ($3.85) and the Goat taco ($4.75), and it definitely hit the spot. Jesse, the owner, made it fresh in front of me and topped it with fresh onions, cilantro and whatever complimented each meat. The meat part of the taco was juicy and succulent, and the toppings just make it even better, along with the crema and guac! Jesse and the cashier Jessica were very friendly and down to earth people! So these guys got my five stars!

I very much so want to give this place more stars because I had brunch here and it was delicious. I got the Schnitzel sandwich and it was a hangover dream. perfectly fried, with delicious flavors. Even though there aren't free refills on coffee they make a mean cup o joe. So I thought dinner would be excellent. I was sadly mistaken. I ordered the Pork Belly and they were tough and salty and the accompaniments were bland. Then had the flatbread with the Speck and Horseradish which was quite delicious--lots of flavor and fresh. Then had the Skate, it was again very salty but besides the salt had no other flavors. I had to spit out the chestnuts that are on the plate. They were disgusting. Then had a dried out brownie that was just completely aweful like it was left out for days. And everything we ordered was recommended by the waitress? Go for brunch stay away from the dinner.

Rumour has it that this place is owned by Bono. Don't know if it is true, I'm not to sure and I don't think it would make a difference to me. Just like everything in NYC space is tight, but it only adds to the charm. We actually sat upstairs, food came out rather quick even though I order the Cuban sandwich which does take some time to prepare. My impression of the place is more of a bar with food, versus a full on restaurant. I could see meeting friends here for a snack or a couple of beers before heading out for the night. I really do like the look of the place and the food was not bad.

i really like this place!!! Â It has a cute atmosphere and solid food presentation. Â The food is soooo flavorful - and different - yum! only thing is - it's a latin place - so if you're vegetarian - options are limited - so beware! i eat fish - so i had some options. Â I ordered the blue cornmeal crusted calimari tomato and plantain salad with a tamarind-type vinaigrette. Â This was good - but its a bit too heavy - with regards to the vinaigrette and crusted calimari - and I had initially thought it would be more a salad then just creamy-ish crusted calimari. Â Nevertheless - it was really flavorful and I certainly enjoyed it! Â  I also got the beans and rice - which were yum! My dining mate got the ribs - he said it was really good, but super heavy - to be fair, he asked the waiter for the most fattening/heavy thing on the menu. For dessert we shared peppermint ice cream with chopped strawberry salad on top. Â It was a refreshing way to end the meal - and the ice cream tasted really fresh. yum - i really like this place - i'd definitely come again - glad to find a new latin spot to add to my list of options. Next time - I would prefer to do family style so I could try more stuff, but less portions of everything!
Nice space...very fun and loud. Â The food was ehhh....not that great....very bland. Â Sangria tasted like kool-aid. Â Not sure that I will be back.

I'm a native Southern Californian, and I definitely pride myself on being a Mexican Food connoisseur. During my time in NYC, I was shocked at how awful the Mexican food was throughout the Big Apple. This is supposed to be the greatest city in the whole country! Â  Luckily some Bay Area hipsters shared the same frustrations as me, and took it upon themselves to open up Dos Toros near Union Square. This place is definitely legitimate. I found myself coming here 4-5 times a week. My taste buds were happy, unfortunately my bowels were not (too much information?) Everything on their menu is delicious. I was especially fond of their burritos and quesadillas. New Yorkers, if you wanna get a taste of some California style Mexican food, then hit up Dos Toros asap. Beware, the line does get extremely long during popular lunch hours. BY FAR the best Mexican food I ever had in NYC.

The food was excellent. I especially loved the pesto pasta, the impossibly moist roast chicken--I normally find chicken excruciatingly boring, and the crazy bold chocolate pudding. DELICIOUS. The sweet potatoes are cooked perfectly and spiced very well. The eggs were perfectly cooked and the bun was divine. The atmosphere is lovely and the food was outstanding. The ambiance is warm and inviting and the staff is friendly and helpful.

I thoroughly enjoyed my experience at three monkeys. They've got many levels to chose from including a rooftop lounge. All the staff I encountered was friendly even though it was pretty busy on a Friday night. I ordered a cucumber chill to start off with-cucumber vodka and lime juice. It was pretty string but still refreshing. You could smell the cucumber as soon as she set it down on the table. I chose the sliders for dinner. They allow you to choose three of any combo and that decision was the hardest part. They all sounded so good! I ended up with buffalo chicken and lamb and liked them both, though the buffalo sliders were far superior. I will definitely be back here.

I have been a Spotted Pig fan for some time now but for some reason or another have not given it its due review. Â The Pig was one of the first restaurants I had been recommended to visit by one of me restaurant co-workers when I first moved out to the big apple. Â Two and a half years later, it still holds a special piece of my hungry heart and remains one of my favorite NYC restaurants. Â  The Service: When you first step into the Pig, you will see that the quirky decor, the brick walls, the casually dressed service staff that make it the go to gastropub of the NYC. Â The actual dining area (minus the new second floor) is quite small and tight. Â The service staff has always been friendly and helpful. Â However, I have found that the actual food service to be slow. Â So just as a fair waring, you may or may not have ample time between courses. Â Make sure your w/ good company! The Cuisine: From what I take, a gastropub is a restaurant institution that serves a combination of tasty gastronomical treats (gastro-) and great beer and wine (-pub). Â Taking from the handful of times that I have visited, the Pig is absolutely the pinnacle of what a true gastropub should be. Â For a bit of the breakdown of the menu, there are some staples and seasonal dishes that the Pig offers. Â Here a quick rundown of their staples. Pot o' Pickles: If you like pickles, you'll definitely have to try these house pickled pickles. Â Sour, tart, crunchy and oh so tasty. Â  Chicken Liver and Toast: Now i'm not the biggest Chicken Liver fan. Â But Chef April Bloomfield will make your hungry tummy a happy tummy with this snack. Haddock Chowder: Â Silky but chunky chowder that warms the body, tummy, and heart. Â Oh yeah, its pretty damn tasty too. Â  Sheeps milk ricotta Gnudi: Â This "naked ravioli" brown butter and sage plate might be one of the best dish I have EVER eaten. Â A definite must try when you are here. Â Absolutely mouth watering! Â  Burger with Roquefort Cheese and Shoestring Fries: Two of my favorite things in world - meat and blue cheese. Â What makes this dish even better, is that it is a LOT of meat and blue cheese. Â The garlic and rosemarey shoestring fries are a nice accompaniment to boot. Â  I've had a Handful of their seasonal dishes and I have yet to run into one I have not liked. Â Now, I am pretty bias towards the PIg's Staples, but if you think you will be a multiple visitor like me, definitely don't be afraid to venture and give other things a try. Â  The Drink: I swear that the Spotted pig serves the best EVER ginger ale. Â Perfectly fresh, cold, carbonated and gingery. Â There are also a nice selection of beers and wines available. Â One of my personal favorites Pork Slap Pale ale is served here. Â And at $5 a can...how can you go wrong?!? As far as I'm concerned, the Spotted Pig was love at first bite. Â Definitely a must eat when living and/or visiting NYC.

The food is really good hear but I enjoy going during the less busy times. It can be loud but the servers always seem to be on their game. I don't mind the more boisterous times but when I usually skulk in I am there for a quick snack at the bar and a well made cocktail. The not so bloody martini is a favorite. The main food draw is their absolutely stellar brussels sprouts. Everyone mentions them for a reason! And the phoenician fries are good too. After going at least once a week for the sprouts I decided I'd just have to learn to make the recipe for myself. If found this link online to the ilili brussels recipe and have made it twice. Works great! neurotickitchen.com/2012â€¦ I also enjoy their kebabs for a sit down meal and ordering a mezze sampling with a big group so I get to taste it all. It's an experience not to be missed!

Had a great seafood squid ink linguine. Pasta was cooked expertly and the seafood tasted very, very good. Also enjoyed an affogato made with organic ice cream that was positively amazing. Very will to visit again next time we visit Brooklyn.
Having the 'Monster Burger' two patties, bacon, fried egg and blue cheese. Just what I needed after a long day. Yes!!!

If you are a fan of cheesecake, you must go to Junior's. Seriously, just do it and you will not regret it. I can't comment on the food, as I have only stopped in for cheesecake a few times after attending various Bway shows. I have had the Red Velvet, Chocolate Swirl, and Chocolate Mousse. It's hard to pick a favorite. They really are equally amazing and delicious! Â The slice of cheesecake is huge, and its a good size for two people to share. Junior's gets crowded in the evenings after the Bway shows let out, as it is very convenient to the theater district. The longest wait I have had has only been about 15 minutes (this was on a weekend) which I don't think is that bad considering the location. The seating area is large and can accommodate a decent amount of people. Â  Enjoy!

It was a great experience. The bartender was fun to talk with, she said she was from Zaragoza and very cool. She recommended me great drinks. The waitresses were very cool and you can have tons of fun with. The food was ok. The environment was wonderful!

Was there last night with 6 friends for my birthday. Â Could not have asked for anything better from this place. Â The place is not too small and not too large. Â Service felt personalized even though there were 5 other groups there. Â The BYO feature was a definite plus. Â I'll be honest and say I don't really remember leaving but I do remember the food. Â EVERYTHING I ate was incredible. Â We had Mac N Cheese for the table (2 orders), a number of BBQ Rib sandwiches, a chorizo burger, a regular burger, and an order of muscles. Â Some had sweet potato fries and others had the spicy fries. Â And these weren't just spicy for the sake of having a spicy fries option. Â They were damn good spicy fries. Â And no they weren't burn-a-hole-in-your-sphincter spicy. Â They were actually flavorful, spicy fries. Â I am definitely headed back for more. Â btw: they even have a TV there in the event you absolutely need to watch the game. Â We had them put the Knicks on and all was right with the world that evening, in addition to it being my birthday. Â  To sum up using an entirely tangential point, this place was so enjoyable that we had our host (and owner btw) poor shots for not just our table but the other tables as well... some of whom actually drank them and others who preferred to remember some of their Saturday night. Oh and we had not one but two chef interactions. Â Super nice and friendly guy. Â Do yourselves a favor a go to this place. Â We don't want them going anywhere. Final final final words. Â I've been to Fette Sau and this place is better, period. Â The vibe here is better and the service is better. Â Hell, there is no service at Fette Sau and good luck finding a seat at that place. Â Fette Sau is good but you aren't doing anything there other than eating. Â Juniper is a place to actually enjoy yourself while having great food. Â Though let me also say that this isn't just a BBQ place. So if you are looking for straight up brisket by the pound, go elsewhere. Â But if you crave what Juniper's menu offers, definitely come.

Food is good, service is so so but this place was super busy. Huge line!! We ordered the 4 sides on the market plate and ate that as a appetizer. That was the highlight of the meal I would say. The salads came in a big bowl and the Greek was pretty good- a little dry. I would recommend the Moroccan carrot side!
Very cute spot and really strong drinks! Â Look forward to going back to trying out the food menu. Â We only sampled the roasted almonds with our drinks and they were great.

I came here last night and had large pommes frites with the mexican ketchup and the curry ketchup especial!!! Delicious!!! And the best part... it's gluten free! :) If you would like to know more about gluten free, vegan, lactose-free etc. food options in NYC, check out: lackoftolerance.com

I haven't written a review in a long time due to forgetfulness, busy-ness, laziness, etc... but this place was so awesome that I am doing everything I can to remind myself to come back here! Â The idea of a finger food / chicken finger joint is brilliant, and especially so when the food is actually freshly cooked and made with fresh ingredients. Here's the deets. Â The fried green beans were not super greasy, nor limp, like other fried green beans I've had. Â The truffle fries tasted like, well, truffle oil. Â These guys did not hold back - they were sooo good. Â They gave us a bunch of sauces to eat with the chicken and sides, but honestly, everything was so good that the sauces weren't even needed! Â I often look at sauce as a reason to cover up something questionable or to improve bland food, but here it was like icing on a cake. Â We had the wasabi chicken fingers and the original. Â Both were piping hot and delicious. Â I was a bit skeptical about the wasabi, thinking it would be overkill, but it was the perfect amount. Finally, the fella that owns this place was a pretty awesome dude. Â He was really accommodating to us and wanted to know our feedback. Â He gave my mom a free bottle of water - and he remembered her name. Â He seems like a genuine person, running a genuinely good restaurant. Â i'll be back. Â This place is super.
Great espresso, great service, great atmosphere! I just love this place! The only was if could be better is if they accepted credit cards for purchases less than 5 dollars...

Great neighborhood spot... you will definitely be surrounded by locals (a lot of those are foreigners living in NYC) and those who are also frequent diners of Cafe Orlin. Prices are decent & the menu, though Mediterranean in style, offers a lot of options. Awesome place for people watching, especially if you sit outside. Favorite dish: Middle eastern eggs (even at 3 in the afternoon) Service can be shaky but always very nice & approachable staff.

Still yummy. Not empty at lunch at all. We started with squash on toast---like brusschetta-delicious. I had lentil soup.. Then I had roast brussels sprouts in mustard--great. Desserts I tried the salted caramel ice cream and my friend had concord grape tart. The latte was large and lovely. All in all a lovely birthday celebration I was so pleased to be back having been there but once for dinner.

I loved so many menu items at this place It was hard to decide what to get. Two crabcakes on perfectly toasted bread with a delicious sauce. Im not a fan of cilantro but it just worked. I enjoyed this sandwich so much. The atmosphere here was pretty cool. Theres a separate bar area, too. This place is one of my faves for sure.

Cold barbeque. There is no excuse for serving cold barbeque at a barbeque restaurant. However, I'm sure their brisket and duck would taste great warm. The pork belly tasted like a pork rib you would get at a mediocre chain barbeque place, only with tasteless fat attached (which should have been the good part). Their vintage Holstein sirloin had an unpleasant cinnamon taste. You'd think they were going to grind it up and put it in a meat patty to be sold in one of those street carts. Their beans tasted like burnt sauce. At least they were warm. The sausage link was ok. I just wish they had eased up on the fennel. All the meat looks so good you almost instinctively want to say it tastes great. I really wanted to like this place, but it will be hard to give them a second chance.

The atmosphere is perfect -- exuberant, lots of wood and candles, gorgeous interior, bustling and fun. Everyone's right about the ricotta -- wow. It had the consistency of Greek yogurt -- creamy, smooth, fresh. The deconstructed beet salad was outstanding. Was that a spring pea puree and roasted kumquat -- no idea but it paired perfectly with the roasted beets. The roasted carrots with yogurt were a stand out as well. Didn't love the broccoli raab -- it was mediocre. My eggplant pasta was very good, too.

Another glam dining room in East 40's. It was a nice surprise to find a cool new restaurant in midtown wasteland. The food was ok. The wine was very good, a pinot noir. Â  It seems that they invested in the decor. The ambiance is cool. The music was a disaster, you could only hear at the bar, in the salon was horrible. The presentation of the plates were original. The place has quality. Â 200 dollars for two.

I had a small half white half margherita pizza with veggie topics with my fianceÃ©. The pizza was quite tasty and filling. The char on the bottom was also perfect. The ingredients are fresh and whatever kinda marinara they had on the margherita it was sensational. Wish they had chicken as a topping though. Sadly they don't and hence negative the star from what was really a supremely good pizza.
Best Thai restaurant EVER! Eating here is like eating in Thailand ;) Should try fry cat fish, tom saab, kor moo yang, everything is so good!

This is an excellent restaurant that deserves more attention than it's gotten. The food is arguably the freshest and Â best tasting Thai I've had, but its not your typical local Thai place. Everything is "elevated" in the sense that the ingredients taste fresher and the food is much more refined than other Thai places. Recommended dishes: papaya pad thai, duck with lychees, & Thai burger Note about the burger: if's definitely a winner but the fries (oh the fries) steal the show!

Was visiting NY and needed a place to grab dinner with friends. Â This was OK, we sat at a communal table downstairs and it was really busy, but the service and food were good. Â The appetizers were good. Â I had the bone marrow burger which was also good, had the richness of bone marrow but didn't blow my mind. Â Good beers on tap.

Best Thai place EVER It's in Hell's Kitchen - and there are probably half a dozen Thai places within a 5 min walk. This is not the most glamorus one (this distinction would go to Room Service) but the food is miles ahead of any other place in the area. Try the BEEF SALAD - the dressing is five star cuisine. Everything we ate there so far (only beef and shrimp stuff) had a fresh and different flavor from the ordinary. And it is a rather low price venue.Check it out! The service is extremely fortcoming and you get a fresh bottle of water on your table as soon as you are seated. The restaurant itself is small but nice.

Bonnie's Grill makes an awesome burger. A burger best served medium rare, with cheddar, pickles, raw onion and a Brooklyn Summer Ale on the side. A juicy, messy burger that gets all over your face. A burger big enough to leave you in physical pain after eating the whole thing, but tasty enough to still be sad that it's finished. A burger that you dream about. (They also make some of NYC's best buffalo wings.)

The food is damn good. The views are nice. Â But, the terrible service will ruin it for you- especially if you've worked in service before. No team work at all when a larger party is sat. All the servers just hang out by the bar and shoot the shit. The only people on their A game are the friendly water boys and bussers. If you get Richard, or the pear shaped lady with a frizzy dark pony tail... Just leave. She's a wet blanket and Rich can't balance more than 2 tables at once. We waited 25 minutes before we had to ASK for our check. They forgot my fries, the coke was flat, you never asking how any of my food was- oh, and even the hostess was too busy smacking her gums to thank us for coming. I'd be embarrassed to be the manager of that place.

This place is a bit cheesy and a total tourist spot but good nonetheless! I came here a few weeks ago with my family on a week night and it was packed! (I definitely recommend making reservations.) Huge, family style portions. We got the caesar salad, stuffed chicken with marsala and a pasta with tomato and eggplant sauce - everything was good! The staff is pleasant and the place seems to be running like a well oiled machine.

The food is amazing here. Â My friend and I had the steak, meatballs and some oysters. Â They get quite a bit of people at the bar, so it can get a bit cramped. Â I'm guessing on weeknights it's a bit better.

We ate at Manzo last weekend & decided to have the strip steak - this was the bigest rip-off I've ever had. There were 3 slices of steak about 2" x 3" Â x 1/4" thk for $35 We didn't mind the price but expected to get a whole steak - this wasn't even a quarter of a steak. This wac accompanied by a single fingerling potato cut into 4 pieces - you've got to be kidding

My parents haven't been the same since I expressly forbid them from going back to Harbour Lights: -But, Kira, the oysters... -The oysters are great. The view is amazing. Everything else sucks donkey. -Yes, but... -END OF DISCUSSION. We have tried many substitutes, with disappointing results: Docks Oyster Bar (too corporate and stuffy); Grand Central Oyster Bar (too mismatched); City Island (too Red Lobster)... Aileen L. to the rescue! "Why don't you try Fish? It has great seafood. And it's totally affordable." Done and done. My parental units and I arrived on the scene in the middle of a Sunday afternoon. The space is rectangular and narrow, the dÃ©cor casual verging on divey. The restaurant was full, but not oversaturated. My companions stiffened the minute we stepped across the threshold. (It's an asocial thing.) I could sense that they were about to ask to go somewhere else. Luckily, at that moment, we were escorted to our table. Everything on the menu looked so appetizing: I wanted everything. Unfortunately, the Maine Sea Urchin was out of season, but I consoled myself by lapping up the following selections: Bluepoint Oysters: While these have my stamp of approval, I grimaced at the accompanying horseradish dip. I felt like a tool ordering a side of cocktail sauce, but it had to be done. New Orleans Gumbo: It was fine for what it was. Maybe I'm just not a fan of the dish. (My father shook his head disapprovingly at all of the vegetables I left behind in the bowl.) Scallop Ceviche: This was a Matrix-style "Woah." I was impressed out of my socks. Perfect consonance of lemony tartness and oniony kick. Half Pound of Stone Crab Claws: It seems that I have been completely spoiled by Joe's Stone Crab's offerings in Miami: Those babies blow past these completely. No contest: Fish's versions were disappointingly tasteless. (It might have been an improvement had they been served warm.) Take two with the cocktail sauce! Lobster Mashed Potatoes: The chef was a bit too liberal with the dressing, but this side was still really tasty. Lobster Mac N' Cheese: This was the most expensive item we ordered. Including my father's 1.25 pound lobster. (Huh?!?) Needless to say, it was absolutely not worth it. The pasta lacked flavor, and the cheese tasted fake. Please sidestep this item and save your craving for Poco's delicious, creamy version. Epilogue: Some hits. Some misses: More than I would have liked, but such is life.

yumm. i love roast duck noodle soup. the noodles are thin and good here, and the duck is nice and meaty (which isn't always the case around here). walked out paying 5.25, including tip. i wish they did put some greens in there so i would feel a little healthier, but for the efficiency, affordable price, and quality of the food, go!! :) yumm. i can't wait to try the beef chow fun. update! last time i went and i got the roast duck over rice - the duck portion this time around was not as generous or meaty, so i recommend sticking with the noodle soups (hearts). and i also ordered the "galan cai" (is it called chinese broccoli or something? i'm not sure how to translate it), but it's very tasty here! just crispy and soft enough. my brazilian american friend came with me and was very happy with the chicken with garlic and black bean sauce dish she ordered, so ta da, you should just go and feel happy that you got your money's worth somewhere in new york... until you go to chinatown ice cream factory and then spend as much on delicious ice cream (red bean!!) as you just did on your entree... but sooooo worth it in both cases.
I'm in love with AppleJack Collins, cask ale and fried pickles. Great bar, great food, great people.

Stocked is a great option to have for days when you feel like home cooking, but just don't have the time to do it yourself. Menu is a little limited, yet everything is delicious, well prepared, and made with quality ingredients. Try the capicola style roast pork sandwich and you'll understand. It's also easy to keep it healthy too, there's multiple veggie sides sold by weight, and their rotisserie chicken (either the barbeque or the herb) is seriously incredible (beats my own chicken roasted a la T Keller).

I came here on a date and I loved it. My date and I enjoy a mixed seafood dinner with clam sauce and linguine noodles.The platters are big for two or three so if you go with that amount just make sure you all are on the same page about what to order. Our waiter suggested white wine with our order and it was so good!. He was very knowledgable about the wine as well as the food. I loved this place I cant wait to go back.

The Double Windsor is no doubt, one of the best options (for bars) around the Bartel-Pritchard Square/The Pavilion/F/G-Train (15th Street/Prospect Park) Subway stop area. With having only Farrell's and Rhythm & Booze in the nabe as the only bars, many people like myself have been waiting on a good place to go out to. The Double Windsor has a great selection of draft beers that look like that they will rotate as the seasons change. They have been doing good business and everyone is definitely happy that there is finally a great bar in the neighborhood. I have only sampled their fries, but look forward to having some of their other food offerings soon.
Ramen, sake, beer! + pork bun x 10000 = happy happy! such a good place to eat, go early!

Great space. Cute outdoor patio. Service was welcoming and helpful. The truffle Mac n cheese was great. I had the short ribs which were ok. They really skimp on the side veggies. I think there were 3 small carrot slices and 5 string beans. It was just strange. A friend had the mixed seafood with risotto and loved it. The watermelon sangria was tasty and strong.

If you get to 53rd and get confused on which cart it is since they all look identical (down to the uniform) - it's the one with the monster line! Don't worry about the line it moves really fast, they know people want there food and they move like clockwork and don't short change you on the portions. Now the food - amazing!! I have been to over 30+ carts around the city and very few can compete on size and NO ONE can compare on taste. Simple menu. I usually go with the Lamb over rice - you can easily share it but I am greedy and want one all to myself. The give you a cup of white sauce but there is more on the side. Â If your thirsty there is a Guy who sells bottled water or cans of pop for a $1. Really hits the spot late night.
Favorite restaurant in New York. Food is excellent, service is impeccable and the atmosphere is elegant but comfortable. This place sets the bar for what a dining experience should be.

More stars because the waiter was friendly and chivalrous. Very small place, great for intimate meals. I love brunch. My favorite meal of all time. Even though it was crowded, we didn't have to wait long. Service was excellent. I can't rave enough about it. The food was just typical brunch food, nothing special. The rosemary fries were not what I expected. They were... mashed potatoes. Oh well, ignorant me.

We stopped by here for a late lunch on a Saturday afternoon and found the food to be amazing. The humus was some of the best I have had and the grilled shrimp salad was delicious. Everyone was happy with their entrees. They did not have a kids menu but gladly made a small plate of scrambled eggs for my little niece. The dinner menu looked great and I hope to try it soon.
This place has really god food the decor Â of the Restoran is very cool with a ceiling of clay pots. The service was great as we'll. we will undoubtedly be going beck very soon
I get that you changed your menu and you are re-branding, ok. Just please bring back the veggie burger. It was seriously the best one in the city. And that's saying a lot.
Chicken rice wes perfect i alway here for it. You can select white meat or Â leg or wing Â  Â But Â service not really good just order and eat. The restaurant is not really clean

Out of all the restaurants I went to NY, this was the biggest disappointment in terms of food. The food is 2 stars because it was such an after thought and not even that warm or fresh tasting. 1 star because the service was so spotty. The first guy was so cool in finding us a table outside. The place was packed, but the other waiter forgot to take down a couple of our orders. They tried to make it up with dessert, but we didn't feel like having dessert. I own the cookbook; so I guess I'm just gonna cook from there.

came here with my family and was amazing. the place is cozy and cute. i think good for date nights. and perhaps for formal family nights as well, if you have those~ anyways, our waiter was more than accommodating! and food was gooooooood! my family happened to order every specials and from what i remember, pastas were a-ok but fish, meat, and salads were more than great! and yes, my tiramisu! they were good too! next time i go, i would love to try how their main menu items are like. it was pricey, but i cant wait to go back :)

This place is so awesome.... I walked in from a rainy, hectic day in Soho to a feeling of European cafe getaway. I started with a beautiful cappuccino and the staff patiently waited until I finished and then ordered couscous/eggplant/hummus dish. Ate lunch with a fresh watermelon juice which was totally refreshing! Â Loved the vibe from the staff and space. Good music, great food. Can't wait to come back!

Went here with a group of 5 for Sunday brunch and was not disappointed. It was busy, but we were seated almost immediately. There weren't a TON of brunch options, but considering our group has vegetarian, dairy-free, and gluten-free requirements and everyone was happy, I'd say there were plenty of choices. I had the fancy grilled cheese sandwich with tomato soup. It was very good! Also had a coffee beforehand and beer after. We don't see each other often so we lingered for another hour over drinks and they never rushed us out. Great spot!
Went back with my husband for our anniversary. Â Food not so good, service not so good. Â Not a great experience. Â What a disappointment after such a fabulous first experience.

I stumbled upon this hole in the wall. And it's clean too! They have a nice and clean back area to dine. For the price, you can't beat it. I got an order of their roasted pork on a bed of rice and beans with plantains in the side. The pork is juicy and I savored every bite and touched it up w their green sauce. I haven't had Cuban roasted pork this good. And it was less than 10 bucks. The people that work here are nice and friendly too.

This restaurant well deserves this 5 star rating. Â The service we received as impeccable. Â I can't express how much we appreciated how attentive our waitresses were and how awesome they handled our party. Â We had a party of about 25 people for a bday party and the bday girl secured the lounge area. Â It was very awkward to sit and eat in the lounge area and a little crowded but we asked the waitress if we could have an additional table to spread out at and accommodate all the food we ordered, she quickly agreed. Â Since we adjusted our seats, they also had to adjust who received which dishes. Â There was a little bit of confusion but they were extremely quick on their feet to adjust to the change. Â Being a large party, a couple of us asked to have a separate check and the waitress was more than happy to let us. Â We were asked if we wanted drinks and were never pushed to order anything from the bar. Â We asked for water and our glasses were never empty during the night. Â We asked for a pitcher of water for our table during the night and she was more than happy to give us one and quickly refilled it when it was low. Â  We ordered four appetizers on the menu. Â I was a little surprised to see that the menu had changed from the last time I was there since I had a couple of favorites that were no longer on the menu. Â So I did a quick yelp search and we settled on ordering the Mekanek, Lahmajeen, veal sweetbreads and duck shawarma. Â The duck shawarma was my absolute favorite. Â It only comes with two so if you have any more ppl eating than that, order accordingly. Â The peanuty sauce made the shawarma unbelievable and there was also a sweet flavor mixed in as well. Â We actually ended up getting this last and it was a great way to end the meal. Â We told some other guests in our party to order it after eating it and they loved it as well. Â The veal sweetbreads were my second favorite. Â The lettuce cups were a total surprise (even though it says it in the description) but I loved the flavors of the sauce along with it. Â  The Lahmajeen was a pita topped with lamb and a yogurt sauce to go with it. Â Can't go wrong with this dish. Â It's very safe. Â The Mekanek was my least favorite. Â The sausage was a bit gamy and tasted a lot better if you threw a lot of the oil/sauce ontop of it. Â  Our friends also ordered the brussel sprouts that the waitresses kept raving about and I was curious to try. Â While it was sweet and tasted good, I'm not sure I could eat a whole bowl of it. Â It's still brussel sprouts. Â  They also ordered the bone marrow. Â I'm not a big fan of bone marrow but when you put it together with the vegetable mixture they provided, it was excellent. Â Without it, it's just fatty and greasy. Â It is extremelyyyy greasy so be forewarned. Â  During the middle of the night, I checked in using four square and received a free rose sangria as the special. Â The waitress was more than happy to get me a glass when I showed her the details. Â The rose was a little too light in the sangria and the cocktail had a lot of orange juice but it was free so I was happy. At the end of the night, we did get charged a $2 cake cutting fee per person since we brought in our own cake and 20% tip was automatically charged to our bill b/c of the size of our party. Â We were more than happy to pay 20%+ for the excellent service we received. Â This is truly one place that deserves it and I wasn't offended or unhappy to pay it at all.
the starter of bread w/ white bean dip is enough reason to go! :)

Danny Meyer's Maialino overlooking the Gramercy Park creates the perfect setting for a lazy weekend brunch. With big bay windows and an airy atmosphere, the ambience is comforting and delightful without being overtly pretentious. A homely bar greets at the entrance. The service is attentive and pleasant. I ordered the Cacio E Pepe (soft scrambled eggs, pecorino & black pepper) with several glasses of the refreshing freshly squeezed OJ and coffee. The eggs were cooked to perfection, delicate and airy yet not overdone with creamy additions. The pecorino and black pepper added just the right amount of kick. My brunch partner and I also couldn't resist the Brioche with the blood orange marmalade. The confectionary seems fresh and homemade. Overall, this was a wonderfully relaxing experience and I look forward to many more visits to Meyer's creation.

I really liked this place a lot the first few times I tried it, but as time as gone on, I've realized how overpriced a lot of the dishes area, especially given the costs. The biji jigae and the cham dubus (soon dubus) are all really tasty - the tofu is great and the broths are delicious. I also love all the banchan/little dishes you get at the beginning, plus the small fresh tofu bowls they give you to begin your meal, and the delicious ginger tea at the end, which is very refreshing. But I just can't believe that things like bulgogi or galbi are $27-30 for a single-size portion, or that a bibimbap in a stone bowl could actually be $18-19. The bulgogi wasn't marinated evenly, and the portion being so small given the exorbitant price makes me think I don't want to come back here again. The wait here has also become ridiculous, which makes me want to go to other places to get my soondubu or Korean meat fixes.
You can never go wrong with BCD Tofu House - consistent quality food and service (whether its in the afternoon or 2am). Â Love the seafood tofu soup and the little fish side dish.

Arrived with 5 other friends for a birthday brunch for one of my girlfriends. The wait for a large table was 20-30 minutes. We waited at the bar and since one of us was pressed for time, 30 minutes later we decided to eat at the bar instead of waiting for the table. The brunch menu has a prefixe option for $24 that includes one drink, one entree and either coffee or tea to finish. We neglected to tell the waitress we were doing the pre-fixe option when we ordered but she was very nice about asking for manager approval to change our bill. The difference was a total of $10, not a huge amount, so we would've been okay if they weren't able to change the bill but it was cool that they didn't give us a hassle about it. I ordered the Rhubarb Shrub to drink. It's a non-alcoholic drink that consists of rhubarb vinear, sugar, lemon and perrier. The vinegar overpowered the drink and I can't say that I enjoyed it very much. I finished it with my meal but I wouldn't order it again. For the main dish I ordered the french toast stuffed with banana and housemade Nutella. I added bacon for an extra $3. When the dish came out they had forgotten my bacon so they brought it on the side later. The french toast was satisfying. It was YUM! The bacon was perfect. To share, we ordered the razor clams egg salad, which contains caviar and lemon aioli and the truffled portobello mushroom pot. Both were DELICIOUS. I HIGHLY recommend the razor clam salad. It was an enjoyable brunch! =) Give it a try.

The thing I like about this place is that all the dishes have a little twist to them that separate them from all of the other thousands of brunch dishes in manhattan. Â The ambiance is cool here also; a very "open" arrangement makes you feel like you are always part of the party. Â I got the TeaSmoked Salmon Benedict which was fantastic. Â I also got a side of Chorizo--equally as good. Â Give this place a try, but be ready to wait for a table!

First lunch of 2012-retro W'burg retro chic decor- check. Â Nice wooden booths. Â Housemade sodas, a bar with many options. Â I was enjoying my booth early in the meal. Ordered: Cesar salad $8 Lobster Roll- $24 The food came together as requested. Cesar was garlicky, respectable, too full of nice brioche croutons. Â I would skip the Cesar. Â Head straight fot he Lobster Roll. Seasoned w/ some Old Bay, herby, chunky on brioche it is a mighty fine lobster roll. Â Fries were super salty- love that. Â Quite a bite for $24, but all in all worth it for a taste of summer on 1/2/12.

Boo on cash-only policy. What is that!!???!? That's ridiculous. Especially when your food costs at least $10/person anyway. That said, Lombardi's was great pizza. Loved the sauce. However, the crust was too crusty. As in, there was just too much of it and I had to do some weird maneuvering to get a good sauce-to-crust ratio at the end. If you follow my reviews I am all about ratios.

I'm amazed my husband wrote his review of this place so long before I did! (Sam S. 1/2/2012) It is only when eating with family of his, that live near by, we ever go to Uva. Always around 6:30pm and always on a weeknight, typically Wednesday. It does get crowded around 8pm, but we are done by then and on our way out. The food is always on point for us. We've never had to send an item back or point out a mistake. We always sit in the backyard/garden style area. The roof panels are removable it seems and can make a summer meal out there quite lovely. The staff are generally polite and don't hover. Though a tad more hovering wouldn't be a bad thing here. It does bare mentioning that the seats can be hard on you if you have spine concerns or weight concerns. (Sadly, I have both.) It can feel cramped if, like me, you are a larger sized human. The prices are not out of line for quality NYC meals, but that just means it's an appreciable hit in the wallet.

Is anything better than free, unlimited sangria at brunch? I think not... I have been coming here for a long time and the food is always excellent, the waiters are always friendly, and I have never been rushed out. And believe me, I STAY and drink sangria for hours. Like, five hours. And no one ever gives me dirty looks, I love it! This has become a staple in my tourist routine as well- everyone I bring here loves this place! The atmosphere is surprising- it's much bigger and brighter than it looks from the outside, and the continual salsa music echoing in the restaurant makes you want to get up and dance. I heart salsa. I have never, ever had a bad experience here, and it's probably one of my most favorite places in NYC.
Fantastic for families and groups. Delish dish! Reservations recommended early. Always a good time.
Might sound like hyperbole, but after multiple Â trips to Lebanon, Israel and elsewhere in the Middle East, this is still the best falafel I've ever had. Do it!
It was nice and cozy. Quite romantic for me and my date. Wonderful ambiance. Food was really good and pretty good portions. I would definitely return.

I had heard of Taim at least a year ago but I wasted 365*5 meals( Yes, I am one of those ppl who eat more than thrice a day) not tasting this heavenly delight. What is wrong with me!!! People I have only one thing to say you have to, have to eat here!! Its tucked in a little corner off 7th avenue and completely inconspicuous till you smell the Falafel as you enter the block. Believe it or not it was like one of those cartoons where the aroma tickles the nose and drags you into the store. I am a big fan of falafels and wanted to try all their three flavors and hence ordered the platter. The six beautiful falafels were luxuriating on the hummus. Crisp and juicy, they are like no other falafels I have devoured before. The salad was light and tangy and tabbouleh was a welcome addition to my already amazing platter. Pita was nice and fluffy with some yummy masala sprinkled on it. Believe it or not I licked the plate clean with both the bread and my fingers.

Excellent restaurant with market-driven fresh ingredients. At a lot of restaurants these buzzwords are just a lot of talk, but at ABC Kitchen the produce is as fresh as life itself and the difference is in the taste. Had the pretzel-crusted calamari, suckling pig and salted caramel sundae. All are recommended.

5 stars, 5 stars!! Highlands is a great spot for just about anything: date, cocktail, dinner, night out, whatever. Cocktails are amaze balls Â (especially the French 75) and the food is deelish. Mahi mahi, kale salad or braised ribs are To die.

Portions are Texas sized and despite the fact that you will want to order a sandwich and a side and a drink and maybe a second smaller side, you really should just stick to a sandwich. Â  The pulled pork sandwich is the best I've had in the city. Â I tend to not go too heavy on sauces and as I saw them slather even more sauce on mine, I almost wanted to stop them. Â Luckily for me, they know better than I. Â Miqhty Quinn's buns are high quality brioche-meets-potato-bread buns that not only handle all the juices and sauce without falling apart on you but they actually do taste good. Â  The spoonful of cole slaw (2 types - one mayo based and the other vinegar) really does add something to the whole plate as well. Â  The true stars though are the meats. Â The pulled pork was juicy and so flavorful that I'd probably eat it off the floor if a piece fell. Â Will R. felt the same way about the burnt ends (think pulled brisket). All in all, this is walking distance from us and has just become our favorite BBQ place. Â No more need to trek all the way to Hill Country.

We wanted an old fashioned Italian meal. Â This was great. Grandson of the founder joe served us and he couldn't have been better. Â I had the spaghetti in white clam sauce. They took the clams out of the shell for me. Â All the taste but none of the work!! Â My husband had the veal rollatini. Â Very tasty. Don't add salt. Â Had it with Marsala sauce. Â  Nephew had the meatballs and he raved. I am a Caesar salad snob and this was one of the best. Â Tasted the anchovy but not overpowering. Â  Â Awesome fun time.

I really liked the brunch I got, which was the churrasco and eggs. Â The steak was quite flavorful and really good. Â Came with a pleasant sauce and really added to the flavor. Â Would've taken it as an IV, but I hydrated with a few cups of coffee instead. Â Plus you get 3 eggs and some potatoes. Â Afterthought, I know, but, the steak was the shining factor. The sucky part was the mimosa - that was terribly made. Â $15 for any entree, coffee, and drink.

i went there just because a friend of mine who's visiting from wyoming looked inside and found the bar and the idea of japanese grill interesting... i'm a big fan of cheap eat. but robataya did a decent job of defeating me. we sat at the bar where all the yelling and grilling was going on. the server took the order from you and then yelled it out to the chefs who did the grilling in front of you. the chefs will climb over the grill or use their little oar to get the raw ingredients, which were hanging out in front of you. you know fish, squid, steak, veggies, etc. the whole thing was fun to watch. and it's fun to see the way they prepare the food, which is very cool. we ordered a whole red snapper, scorpion fish, cod fillet, enoki, zucchini, japanese yam, and mochi! they were all good. but the cod was the best thing of the meal. oh and we also got the rice with salmon and salmon roe. the food was excellent. but the service was really slow though. we waited for 30 minutes, which wasn't bad for a friday night dinner. but the whole cooking thing took kinda forever. they grilled things very slowly. that made the food really good especially when you have to grill the whole fish. but the whole meal just took forever because we had to wait for 15 minutes for anything we ordered. we had a lot to catch up so the wait wasn't a problem. but it would suck if you came with someone you bring to entertain but you don't want to hang out with e.g. customers from work. but it should be good for dates though. and the chef was attentive. he knew that i was waiting anxiously for my enoki to come and told me that he would make that next. and he had a nice smile but that's beside the point. interesting dining experience. but i love my hole-in-the-wall food though.
Had a tasty light brunch here.

I liked Traif. The place itself was pretty cool, and it wasn't AT ALL crowded, which was surprising. We had the tuna tartare, followed by the truffle toast/egg/rabe, some whole roasted fish (IDK IT WASN'T MINE) and I had the scallops. The scallops. Were. Beautiful. The tuna tartare was great too--it was served on fried potatoes (think potato chip, thicker though, not crunchy really) and were a little spicy. The amuse was some type of chilled gazpacho-esque soup in a shot glass, and to close they gave us a cube of watermelon with who even knows what on it (I had had two of the Spritzes by this time, which were a fresh take on a mimosa, and therefore I just didn't really care when she told me what it was), but it was cute, and refreshing. Ohhh right and the bacon donuts, just get them. Generally, though, it was all very good and my cook/boyfriend (who is EXTREMELY hard to please) really liked it as well. I'd go back if I weren't so tired of cute Williamsburg-y places.

The more Filipino restaurants in this world, the better-- especially in manhattan... mm correction, ANYwhere within reasonable driving distance to DC (235 miles) that gives me a reason to get out of this bubble... i'll do it~ i'll totally do it. As with many other fancy filipino restaurants i've been to in frisco, LA & chicago, these happiness-inducing dishes are not the most affordable (the filipino knows how much filipino food costs to make! =P)-- and apparently average price for brunch in nyc. nonetheless, this place makes me very excited. this restaurant IS special & is on to something that's destined for greatness (filipino cuisine with the modern twist). the fact they serve filipino-style eggs benedict (w/spam, yes foreal), sisig, & calimansi mimosas... i mean come on~ calimansi mimosas?! ..genius... sheer genius.

Quite possibly my new favorite place for barbecue. Don't be intimidated if the line stretches out the back door. We waited just about 15-20 minutes to be served and seated on a Saturday night. Get the brisket, the pulled pork, and the baked beans. We came here for a later-night second dinner and though not very hungry, I devoured everything. The brisket was so juicy and flavorful, and with just the right amount of fat. The pulled pork was tender, and also a tiny bit fatty. And the small $3 serving of baked beans, served with a hefty portion of burnt ends mixed in, is the perfect size and side. Nice bunch of beers on tap and super friendly servers. The seating situation can be a bit unpleasant. First come first serve - but made somewhat less chaotic by someone who directs the next party in line to the next seats available. I'd advise against coming with a large party, but we did notice a pretty big group seated side-by-side along the windows that night.... Guess it worked for them!

I have to admit that the akamaru modern was the bomb. Like many others, the broth was to die for. But don't sip it all up! (You'll want to get an extra serving of noodles!) The pork buns were also good, but I personally took out the white bun part so that I could make room for my ramen! Â The green tea creme brulee was so-so.
I love waffles, so I had to try this place out. I thought it was good, but nothing over the top. I'm interested in coming back for seasonal specialties though.

First off, let me say what a lovely little place this was. I been for Brunch and dinner and the food was amazing. Reminded Â me of my last trip to Italy. Â And if this review was only on the actual meal itself, I would have given it 5 stars, hands down! Unfortunately I have to report beyond the meal. Last Saturday, the wait staff was great; although I do not know how the kept smiles on their faces. A taller man, with light-ish hair Â color, was yelling at them the whole night. He was disrepectful to the staff; insulting and berating them in front of customers. He had an attitude with anyone who came in contact with. It was so obvious, it ruined my meal... and I was so uncomfortable, at one point I almost said something to him, but I was trying to enjoy a meal with close friends from out of town (I was embarrassed in front of my friends as well). After that, we left our kind waiter a generous tip (we felt that we could at least Â make up for some of the abuse he had sustained!), and vowed never to return! It is unfortunate because the food was great, and the other time that I went to eat at Aurora, that man wasn't there and the atmosphere was a lot lighter and much more pleasant for all. And it was not just me that noticed it, an older couple sitting next to us was also commenting on his blatant disrespect to his staff. They said that he was the manager. So, overall, great food, great service, poor management!
Excellent brunch. Â Might suggest sitting outside if you don't want to feel like you are the only 25-year-olds in the whole place.
