I went there for a business lunch, its a must if you like meatballs. Duck meatballs are a must try, ambience and drinks are good too. Cant comment on economical value because i didnt pick up the check :)

I would suggest to the proprietor of Juventino that he either relocate the establishment to Manhattan or open after 11:30 AM on weekends to make it clear he is not interested in having families with young children at the restaurant. No matter how many times the word 'heirloom' appears on the menu, being rude to parents of young children is not a sustainable business practice.
Just wanted to update since I've been here quite a few times now. Pasta here is PERFECT. Enough said.
Best seafood in Manhattan

Blue Ribbon is the place we always end up when deciding upon a special-dinner locale. Â "Let's go somewhere different this time!" Â Yeah notsomuch. Â It's romantic, manly, delicious, fancy, and comfortable...kind of like Brooklyn itself. Â Whoa. The wait is long, but so what? Â Have a drink and relax. Â It's a special occasion. Â Sometimes anticipation of an event makes it all the more amazing when it finally occurs. Â Roller coasters are a lot less fun when there's no wait, right? Â Mmmm steak.
It is good. Â But not to go out the way. Â We tried 4-5 pizzas for a group of six. Â It is good and fresh, but ehhh nothing memorable. Â I don't get the hype. But everything in Williamsburg is hyped.

Came here for brunch after hearing about it from multiple people, and we left full, happy, and boozed. Â  Love the AYCD sangrias and all of the choices they give! The rules were a funny (but good) way of stating that you gotta be able to handle yourself without getting "cut off." The havana banana smoothie rocked my world and the gallitos were amazing and definitely enough to feed two, as the menu states. The bread box was the icing on the cake, and I'm not even a bread person! Â Chocolate chip bread, and some other warm, soft, chewy goodness. Â Can't wait to make my way over to the west side again for this!

I would give this restaurant 5 stars except I felt ignored by the front staff - she barely greeted me at the door and when she did finally say something it was with disdain that she pointed at the table for one. Â I almost left but glad I didn't - food was excellent - lovely presentation and a great mix of flavours!

Dinner date location suggested by husband's co-worker--a big win! Caveat for review-we only tried the gluten free options. If you are gluten free and you have a lovely partner/friend/family member, or a willingness to eat an entire pizza--you should put rubirosa on the Â short list asap. Shared the mozzarella sticks and rice balls to start, if only because I can so rarely indulge in fried food. Both delicious. Mozzarella sticks were freshly fried and heavy on the cheese, while the rice balls (arancini) had a great mix of cheese to rice to herb ratio. As for the pizza--by FAR the best gluten free crust I've had so far. A little sweet and what I thought was likely a good amount of potato flour or starch as a base, but crispy and less mealy than others. It's not like you're going to mistake this for regular pizza crust, but for a creative approximation that actually tastes good, I'd say this gets a thumbs up. We tried half cheese/basil and half with sweet sausage. Sausage was tasty and not too greasy, although I might go for something with more kick next time. A bit on the expensive side & a little smaller than their non-gluten free options, but a delicious indulgence if pizza is normally off the menu. Only regret? We ate too many appetizers and (I) didn't have room for dessert. Next time!

What Grimaldi's used to be! Started by the same owners who became disillusioned with the commercialized pizza business. We had the no.1 with pancetta and truffles and the quality of the ingredients really came through. Also has the margarita with sliced meatballs. The red marinara sauce was extremely fresh! This place comes highly recommended.

Best place!!! The best R'n'B and Hip Hop on the stereo and the best meatballs and sides ever. Everything is nicely down to earth and everyone is having a great time. Tried almost all different types of servings, except for the desserts and sandwiches. The regular beef with spicy sauce is just amazing! Make sure you go!

I happened to be wandering around K-Town on a Saturday afternoon and was famished. Â I really craved Korean BBQ, but came across the Woorjirip, which had decent pricing and no crowd. I don't know much about "authentic", but I do know the food is incredibly delicious, especially the garlic tofu, the glass noodles and the spicy pork. Â I enjoyed all of my pickings at the buffet, which I had with a can of Korean white grape juice. The price and choices are great, and I'd definitely take my friends here for a nice meal.
Love this place -and for lunch? OMG. I've been going to Ssam Bar for quite awhile now and have never been disappointed. Stop by my foodie blog for more.

The staff was friendly and the place was nice - food was fine but forgettable. We had a few different apps; the meatballs were pretty crummy actually, and the risotto balls were meh. Fish stew for dinner was good enough but nothing especially notable.
Pleasant staff in this tiny cafe, which serves authentic Breton French food. Great for crepes and soups. For weekend brunch, get the brioche French toast. Â A cozy place to go on a cold winter day.

Love this place! Been here only once for dinner (which was so-so) and many times for drinks (which is always amazing). This place is a bit hard to find, as it looks like you're walking into a psychic's shop. My favorite cocktails are the Fraise Sauvage and Amelia. The bartenders here are friendly and I enjoyed chatting with them about their drink making skills. Definitely a gem in the West Village.

This food truck (yes, it's a food truck), is run by the friendliest group of gents. I have only eaten the falafel, which is the best I've ever eaten. A side order is abudnant and modestly priced. I like to mix the hot sauce and tahini. Accepts credit cards.

My friend just got done with the Ny marathon and wanted to replenish his mind body and soul with some carmines!!! Even though I was trying to avoid times square for my whole trip you think i'm going to tell the man no?? Come one he just risked his life for 5 hours running his heart out! We took down 2 big plates of pasta! Don't think we finished them but they were dam good. All washed down with some brewskis! Â Then off to the village underground dun dun dun

Great spot if you like wine, sangria and finger foods (Tapas!). Â It can get pricey so it's best to split it with a few folks but it's a nice treat. Â The sangria is excellent and they don't rush you out off your table which is good. Be prepared though, it is a tight spot. Â They have pub size tables and chairs but everyone is usually very polite.

I was in town for a week on business and was able to stop in both on a Tuesday and Friday night. While Tuesday night was slower, the bartender and owner were both very inviting and friendly, enough so that we came back on Friday night for a much needed wind down from the week. Thanks to Ina, our rockstar bartender, we were able to have a successful and fun trip to the city, even though the blizzard of 2013 was bearing down on us. Thanks to Yelp Ads for helping us find a great place! We'll definately be back.

I was intimidated by this place for a long time because it seems like a noisy monster most of the time I walk by, but turns out it's for good reason. The Â mojitos are good & strong & go down too easy. I was also very happy with the food. I would say only 1 out of 10 times I've been that the food was limp and not glowing with freshness. The Steak tacos are Â exceptional, the guacamole & salsita is very nice and the stuffed sweet plantain is great. Those 3 things & a mojito are what I get every time. Perfect for two and delicious 9 out of 10 times.

My roommate and I definitely got food poisoning at Sunny And Annie's last night. Â  I ate with Roommate A at Cocoron. He's fine. I ate Sunny and Annie's for dinner with Roommate B. Â We both have food poisoning. I got the Bush, I believe: Â lemon chicken, roasted seaweed, mozzarella, cucumbers and jalapenos. I used to love Sunny and Annie's but I won't be going back now. Â Can't risk food poisoning, and this may not be the first time.

The hands down best sandwich and best value In the city that never sleeps.. Â No matter what time you crave it's open.. Â 24/7 365! Â  If you like falafel this is the spot to go 1st always... There's always a line but these guys are very very fast!!! Â It used to be 2$ .... Then jumped to 2.50... Now 3 bucks but still the best value in nyc for taste size and price! Amazing snack or meal anytime!!!

The burger here is excellent but it seemed mine got a bit too much seasoning on it in the middle. Â Comes a la carte, fries extra. Â The bar is quite nice too especially for that area. Â The service was very good and attentive. Â Patio has very nice plants etc, and is worth a visit! Â Long Island iced tea was $10 and well made.

Heidi's house is my favorite restaurant in the UES, and one of my favorites in the whole city. Heidi and her staff are always friendly and helpful, the food is delicious (especially the specials which change daily), the atmosphere is warm and comfortable. No complaints. One note-- Heidi's House is tiny. Great for two people, sometimes okay for 3-4, but nothing over that.

Friends were in from out of town and we thought we'd try the LES location. The food was good and so was the service until the bill came. We paid and still had half of a $40 pitcher to drink. Before anyone could take another sip we were told the table was needed for a new party. I can understand being asked to hurry had we been sitting for a while, but this wasn't even 5 minutes after paying. Â It left a bad taste to what was the middle of a great night. With so many restaurants in the city I'll try somewhere else next time.

I am tremendously picky when it comes to Italian cuisine. Â  My husband My husband and I came here tonight for dinner and we had the chicken franchese and the assorted seafood dish. The food was excellent and authentic. The pasta was cooked to perfection. Â Our server was very attentive and friendly. Â The prices were pretty decent. I highly recommend this place to anyone that wants to enjoy a good meal.
love their pizza.

Sweet little place. Â Great bartender, great cocktails. Â The grilled cheese sandwich was excessive--in a good way (and the tomato soup it came with was awesome but tiny!). Â One star deduction only because they ran out of the entree I wanted!

Recommends: Tagliatelle, Stracci Ordered: Tagliatelle, Cappelletti, Stracci, Torcia, Tortelli di Carciofi Spent: $10/pasta Alright ladies and gents, here goes another one of those huge best-kept-secret revelations that I hope I don't hate myself for: $10 MONDAY PASTA NIGHTS AT MORINI AFTER 9:00 PM Yes you heard me correctly, $10 a pasta. From the chef who brought you the famous Fusilli at Marea, comes a night when you can have that same quality of pasta for only $10 a bowl. W*F NYC?! This makes up for all those countless hours spent waiting for cronuts, nutella bars, and super chef Shack Stacks. I shall say no more because the pasta speaks for itself and the bread will drive you ultimately over the edge to carb heaven. Special shoutout to amazing chief sommelier Nadine who gave great customer service - one of the best I've seen in NYC. But in all good NYC fashion - book at least 3 weeks in advance on Opentable. Spots go fast!
Another great brunch spot for me and my peeps...yummy Turkish eggs!!

I love the high ceilings with skylights and the open airy feel of this restaurant! The decor was trendy industrial. Came here for brunch right when it opened on a Saturday morning, with no wait. We shared the Turkish eggs and the fry on. Turkish eggs were two poached eggs on Greek yogurt submerged in oil infused with Moroccan spices. I have to say this dish took some getting used to, but in the end it was quite good. Interesting combination of creamy Greek yogurt with the salty and flavorful Moroccan spices that we mixed with the runny egg yolk. The dish was a little bit too rich for my taste, but my husband loved it! We also tried the fry on, which consisted of two eggs over bread with Â shishito peppers and mushrooms on the side. This dish was not that great, very run of the mill, and the combo of things on the plate didn't mesh in my opinion. The fresh squeezed juices are good, but very expensive. A cup of grapefruit juice runs at seven dollars, not sure if there are refills. Oh yeah, the lavender honey biscuits given at the beginning of the meal were delectable, and we asked for seconds. Great infusion of lavender flavor in the honey. Overall, solid well cooked brunch in a comfortable atmosphere.
I came here with my boyfriend to get local tapas from a highly reviewed restaurant. The food was good, the sangria was kind of blah though, stick to the wines.
Love this place. Get the sea urchin or the Korean burrito. Would be 5 stars except everyone else seems to love it too - too crowded!

Food is okay - the free bread and Calamari Frito were delicious but the service was bad. Our waiter was a guy with a mohawk and we sensed a bit of an attitude from the get-go. We brought a cake with us and were charged a $12 "cake fee" - $2 for each person at the table. Each person got an unevenly sliced sliver of the 10" cake cut by the "pastry chef." My friend went home with less than 1/2 of the 10" cake and there was no way we ate all of the other 1/2 at the restaurant. I would think twice about going back which is a shame since I have been there twice before and had great experiences both those times.
This place is small but the food is so good. And cash only. Recommended number 5 with thin noodle and homemade shrimp gyoza

Great campirinias. Very loud. Mediocre service from chill brazilians. They are sweet and kind but you might wait a very long time for water. The cheese bread is amazing. It's honestly really good. I am primarily a veggie person so I've had the rice, beans, egg and collard greens twice. I think its amazing. I never knew collard greens could be so delish. My husband loves the meat there. The sandwiches are served on gorgeous looking baguette. Neighborhood staple. Nothing to go out of your way for.

I. Love. Joe's Shanghai. Soup. Dumplings. Â BUT, Joe's does not deliver to my office, so when I got the craving, I had to find an alternative. Â After much review searching, I settled on Shanghai Asian Manor, clicked off a Seamless order, crossed my fingers, and hoped for the best. "The best" is not what I got (soup dumplings were not as good as Joe's), but everything I tried (soup dumplings, watercress shrimp dumplings, and hot and sour soup) was very good. Â I especially liked the sauces that came with the dumplings--one even had whole anchovies in it, making me think they made their sauces in the restaurant instead of buying siracha in bulk. If I were walking down the street and Joe's Shanghai and Shanghai Asian Manor were next door to each other, I'd choose Joe's. Â But next time I want Chinese at work, I'll definitely order from Shanghai Asian Manor again.

Everyone's been raving about Jean-George's ABC Kitchen, so I decided to see what the talk is about. The restaurant is part of ABC Carpet & Home. You can enter it from the furniture store all the way in the back or at it's official entrance on 18th Street. DECOR I went in from the back since my friend insisted and had to walk all the way from the back to the front to be seated in the back again. It was very antique yet modern looking. I can only describe it as... yuppie-hipster. Everything gave you the ambiance of fresh, organic, green, and eco-friendly. It's as if they were completely furnished by ABC Carpet & Home, hmmm..... The plates were definitely from the home store... SERVICE Beside the really grumpy girl that gave my friend an attitude since he was trying to get seated 10 minutes before dinner opening, everyone else was very nice. Courtesy with a smile, very attentive and informative on the menu (I was confused about the difference between market table and appetizers; market table portions are smaller). I felt appreciated. FOOD - Chicken Liver Toast: I never knew how good chicken liver can taste as a spread. - Sugar Snap Pea Salad with Parmesan Dressing and Herbs: Fresh, crispy, healthy, unless you find the cheese too heavy (I don't). - Pretzel Dusted Calamari, Marinara and Mustard Aioli: Tasted like perfected fried calamari at a pub. - Whole Wheat Bigoli, Pork Ragu, Parmesan: I don't get it, but meaty. - Seared Arctic Char with Spicy Corn Broth: Fish is moist and flavorful combined with the corn broth. Skin is crispy. Combination is awesome. Lesie approve! - Salted Caramel Ice Cream Sundae with Candied Peanuts & Popcorn: I never thought I would like salty ice cream, but it works! The caramel flavor is light, so even with the whipped cream and chocolate syrup, it's not as heavy as it sounds! I think I can get used to salty ice cream! - Organic Root Beer: It's green! The root beer flavor is concentrated on the bottom. Floating around is the minty taste. Interesting... - Fizzy Lizzy Raspberry Lemonade: This was the first time I've heard of a Fizzy Lizzy (It's a bottled flavored seltzer/soda). Yummy! DISTRACTION There was a solo house fly flying around during the latter part of dinner. It landed on the plate on the table next to me. And then it tried to fly to my table. And then it landed on my friends plate. *shudders* TL;DR Fish is yummy! Drinks, Chicken Liver, and Salty ice cream is a good surprise!!! o_O Fly? Fly! Eek!!!

I had a fantastic dinner here with my dad recently. He had the pork chop special and I had the fish of the day, striped bass. The pork chop was gigantic and everything was delicious. We finished off the meal with creme brÃ»lÃ©e and a chocolate torte. I would highly recommend checking this place out. One note - they only take cash or Amex.

The best thai I have had yet! I live right next to Joya and have eaten thai food all over the world and have yet to find a more flavorful place than this. I first tried the pad see yue and was not that impressed so I didn't come back for a few years. I gave it another try and had the pad thai this time and have been coming back for years ever since. The difference between their pad thai and all others I have had is the flavorful abundant sauce. All other pad thai seems flavorless and dry now. I also highly recommend the veggie pad thai, veggie spring rolls and a thai iced tea! They also have great curry and a nice selection of beers on draft.

This is my favorite pizza place. I've only ever gotten delivery from here, so I can't say I've ever eaten a super fresh, flaming hot, straight from the oven into my piehole pie, but this pizza is incredibly tasty. Their salads are good too, but I usually end up eating the pizza first until my stomach cries uncle. The delivery is pretty fast, and the guy on the other end of the phone is a pleasant human being. It's always a little surprising when a neighborhood spot ends up beating out NYC pizza legends like Patsy's, Grimaldi's, etc. The only other place I've tried that rivals Il Porto is Lucali. I could pretty much eat pizza from here everyday.
best pizza in history!!!!! sooooooooooo goood! Â def not for those on a diet!
had breakfast arepa on saturday with a deliciously sweet sugar cane drink. Â i was satisfied and buzzing for the rest of my day! glad caracas is in the hood! Â really affordable too.

I have been going to EO for the last 5 years. I have tried countless other bars but EO is special, a place I return to quite often. I live close by so may be it is a habit, but the place is always amazing. The decor and the way the place is laid out, makes for a fun night every time. One of the great things about this place are the bar tenders. These are true professionals and their cocktails are always among the best. I guess the fact that this place is owned by a group of former bar tenders shows. Â  Also the bouncers only let in the people who belong there. They are always courteous unlike other places and keep a vigilant eye on what is going on in the bar. You tend to become friends with them. I Â always try to drop by just to have a chat with KC Smith who happens to be lead bouncer there and a major reason for this bar's continued success.

Secret exclusive "dining club" esque restaurant... may be difficult to get a reservation here but it's worth it! A very small and cozy restaurant that comfortably fits max 24 ppl, complete with a zen rock garden. Relaxing and casual ambiance, feels like you are dining at a friend's house. Â Food is amazing - possibly top 5 meals in NYC. We way over-ordered, but prices were so reasonable- was under $90 per person including wine. FIRST VISIT: We tried the oyster bucket (HUGE and delish), succulent sashimi, uni mushroom croquette (lovely dish and I'm NOT an uni fan), smoked meat platter, pickled cucumber w/bonito jelly, head cheese & tongue (pass), foie gras soba (amazing combo), roasted branzini (all the veggies and the fish were spectacular), miso black cod (very buttery maybe too much for me), fried sweet potatoes with a honey sauce (to die for), washu-gyu sliders (juicy goodness its KOBE + angus beef cross breed), and chocolate creme brulee (heavenly). Couldn't stop eating - it was all so delicious! SECOND VISIT: Bill $120 per person but had loootsss more alcohol. New stuff: I tried the little neck clams which were good, but too fishy for me (granted first time I've ever had raw clams before). Â Cheese platter was soooo good, I can eat straight cheese all day long. Â Two of the three cheeses were very strong, sharp, pungent type cheeses - so if you don't like blue cheese type varieties - skip on this dish. Â Also tried both fried potatoes - definitely get the sweet potato satsuma ones over the regular ones. Â Sake panna cotta is so light and delicious. Â  THIRD VISIT: New item - short rib sashimi friggin amazing FOURTH VISIT: vegetable fondue holy moly that sauce can make even a shoe taste delicious

I've been to Freemans twice now; first time I went was about a year ago, service was not great, but food was pretty good. I decided to give it another try this past weekend. The service was somewhat better this time, but the food was bland. I've had many better brunches in New York and probably won't go back again.

My husband and I went there on a Saturday night pre-theater around 6:30 pm. Â  We ordered the fried baby artichoke for an appetizer. Â The artichoke (5 pieces) was deep fried and served with crispy fried parsley. Â It was a little bland and could have used more seasoning - fortunately the table provided a salt shaker. For dinner, I got the special -- home made tagliatelle with broccoli rabe and clams in a light garlic sauce. Â The pasta was really fresh but there was not enough garlic and the dish also needed more salt. My husband ordered the gnocchi with Gorgonzola. Â It was a very simple dish, but not in a good way. The gnocchi was bland and served with a white cheese sauce, but didn't have a lot of flavor. One could easily imagine serving the dish with more herbs, micro-greens and even some bacon. Overall, it was an acceptable meal but nothing special though the restaurant is very reasonably priced.

This place has such great food. I have been here for brunch, lunch, and dinner and had great food at all meals. The brunch is a great deal and is unlimited, though you really have to get on the waiters to serve you and make your unlimited drinks worth it. On the food alone I would give it 5 stars but the set up is often too tight and the service is really slow sometimes but the yucca fries make up for it. Although the last time I went my waitress was phenomenal and actually recommended the Malbec instead of the Pinot Noir. Definitely make it a point to check this place out!

We happened to venture in here on a Thursday night after we left an event around the area, and I was pleasantly surprised at how good the Chicken Fried Steak was. It was quite succulent and oh-so-yummy! We also shared the biscuit which was soft and delightful to bite into! As per the venue, it wasn't crowded, but decently filled and service was just average.

The business is great here. I never manage to find a seat easily, but the food is really good. Self-served and cheap. Hot, cold, warm, you name it. Great place if you're a fan of Korean food. But yeah, like I said, hard to find a place to sit.

When a gastropub has a laundry list of accolades such as a Michelin Star, a feature in Vanity Fair written by Anthony Bourdain, then you can safely assume the establishment provides high-quality food. It's not just any gastropub though. The Spotted Pig pushes out comfort food, British style. Chicken Liver Toast -- For all you Asians out there, think of the pate that comes in the banh mi. You'll have to get use to the muddy-like texture but once you get past that, it's all smooth sailing. The crunchy toast is a great complement to the mush-like chicken liver. The flavor was ultimately very mellow. It's a great precursor to the main event. Chargrilled Burger -- A crowd favorite. Heck, Google their famous burger and see pages and pages of sites describing their infatuation and even recipes in hopes to replicate the item at home. The patty was remarkably thick, easily one of the thickest burger patties I've ever had. The bun was heavy and firm, somewhat crunchy around the edges. The one ingredient that completely changed the burger was the Roquefort Cheese. It's a sheep milk blue cheese which altered the taste of the burger. I, for one, am not a fan of blue cheese. It makes me think that the cheese is far past the level of expired and, in the end, makes me feel ill. All I could taste was the cheese. It really took away from the flavor of the meat. To each their own. Â  The shoestring fries were great, tasted like chips to me. Make sure you dip it in tons of ketchup! The restaurant seems to draw in a lot of celebrities. Supposedly, Jay Z co-owns the joint. I even sat next to Aziz on my last visit!

This is a hipster bar. But I love a good hipster bar. I'm here on a late Sunday night and this not only the only place in the neighborhood with some life, it's the only place with fun. Good times. 4 instead of 5 stars for a great spot with should be cheap bar but with not so cheap drinks.

Friendly staff, great environment, delicious food. I ate the pork chop, which was amazing, and house made chicken and shitake mushroom sausage, yum. My partner had the duck, which was incredible. The waitress saw we had flowers and offered to (and did) put them in the cooler downstairs while we ate. Definitely will return for another meal and would like to try some of the sister restaurants!

Note: This review is for when I ate at Yasuda's two months ago. Â I just got around to writing it. I sat at the sushi bar, and Chef Yasuda was my chef. Â My friends and I ate omakase style. Â I highly suggest you go omakase, too, if you have Yasuda as your chef! The atmosphere and decor of this restaurant are nice. Â I've eaten here a few times, and I like how it's simple and clean. The service was very good, but I think that's to be expected from a place like Yasuda's. Â The waitresses are attentive, ready to clean the bar, give you more tea or sake, and so on. Regarding the actual nigiri that I ate, I tried many different kinds of fish, including white king salmon, cherry salmon, bluefin tuna, unagi, anago, halibut, and Spanish mackerel. Â The menu is organized into different groups of fish; for instance, the "tuna" section can consist of normal tuna and bluefin tuna. Â I like this, as I can try different variations of a fish that I love; for instance, I like how I'm able to try silver salmon, cherry salmon, white king salmon, and so on! The sushi's generally very fresh, and Yasuda likes to add his own sauce to flavor each piece of nigiri a bit. Â There are a lot of species of fish on the menu, and some are unavailable depending on the season. Â Overall, though, there are a lot of choices of fish for you to try! One of the last things I ate was a salmon roe roll. Â The reason I bring this up is because his seaweed is amazing. Â That's really all I have to say about this, haha; if you can, try the seaweed! My friends and I got green tea and red bean ice cream as our desserts, and the ice cream was, of course, good. Â You can't really get this part wrong, though! I personally think that, of all the sushi restaurants I've had so far, Yasuda has the best sushi rice in the city. Â The fish is fresh, which is great, but his sushi rice really does make you realize how important good sushi rice can be. I don't know if Yasuda's has the best sushi in the city, but it's definitely one of the best, in my opinion. Â The total bill came out to be $150-200 per person. Oh, yeah- Chef Yasuda also gets bonus points in my book because he's buff as hell for a sushi chef!

I must say, it is always a delight to have a good meal and think to yourself that it was Michelin worthy. Â Of course, I'm not on the star committee and quite frankly, what do I know about class and elegance? Â However, I do know what I like and what I am impressed with. Â So it was to my surprise that after a friend's birthday dinner at Public, I found out it was a Michelin star. I love going to restaurants with an unbiased premonition so I can judge with my own tastes and opinions. Â Public's decor was stunning and that alone I was impressed with. Â The course did take a while to prepare, which I have no problems with (as long as it's within a reasonable frame) because greatness takes time. Â Regrettably, I can't comment on my food because it's been 2 months since I went and quite honestly, I don't remember what I got. Â I do remember how I felt, and I can say I felt satisfied with the quality. I would not be opposed to coming again for a celebration of a friend's name day.

I was here on a Friday night with a party of 6. Â We had a reservation and were seated fairly promptly. Â The restaurant is quite large for NYC, and there is a surprising amount of space between tables. Â You don't have to sit with the couple next to you, so that's a plus. I started with the provoleta, a blend of "Argentinian cheeses." Â It came with some type of bread to eat with it. Â The two things combined ended up being a lot like a mozzarella stick. Â I ate two of the four bread thingies because it was just too heavy. I split a soft taco dish with a friend. Â It came with shrimp, chicken, and beef fillings. Â We substituted a 2nd order of chicken for the shrimp b/c of a shellfish allergy, and they were very accommodating. Â The chicken was delish. Â My sangria was good too ($8 per glass on a normal night). Â Everybody's entree was pretty gigantic. Â Those who ate their whole dinner ended up uncomfortably full. Â None of us had room for dessert. Â On a positive note, everyone must have enjoyed their meals to have gorged themselves. Staff was extremely helpful. Â Bathrooms were clean. Â It's a nice restaurant. Â I don't know that I'll go back for dinner though. Â It was pricey after all was said and done, and I'm not sure that the food was THAT good. Â (Except maybe for the rolls you start with. Â Some other reviewers mention them too. Â Scrumptious!) Â  I'm torn between 3 and 4 stars because the place was just all right for me. Â I would love to go to the brunch that everyone says is amazing though.
Sounds degusting

Felt like we were being held hostage. First - the food was amazing. My husband and I went for the 8-course tasting menu for V-day. So we were in a great mood and excited to try this place. We went to Traif last year and LOVED it. BUT 1 hour and a half in we had 4 plates. The first plate was 4 veggie chips. No joke. At one point we waited 45 mins in-between plates. Then they brought out a plate they had already brought out earlier. I made jokes about it with the server - and we were trying to make the most of the situation but COME ON. In the end the meal was 2.5 hours long and we managed to have 6 out of the 8 plates. They gave us a glass of wine and a coffee for free. But despite loving the food I don't think I'll ever go back. Even once I said something - they acted like it was our fault somehow. Pretty annoying. Butchered the evening.

holy crap the wraps here are AMAZING!!!!! i'm craving it again. omgggggggggggggggggggggggggggg. steak pieces, greens, apples, feta cheese...sweet potato fries. nom nom nom nom nom nom nommmmmmmm oh and the seats are swings! ^_^

Definitely overrated. This is one of those places where your friend will say, "Oh my God, you HAVE to try this little place over on Lafayette..." Yawn. As far as a meal goes, it was all just underwhelming. I would say it's probably because it was so hyped up... That being sad, it really is just "meh" at the end of the day. This of course was for brunch, so on dinner I can't really speak. So maybe they have a better side! That would be lovely... though I'll never be back.

I'm not gonna repeat what anyone else said about this restaurant. Food is definitely good - Hainanese Chicken Rice and the Roti Canai are both Â must-gets. (But my favorite Hainanese Chicken Rice is still the one in Savoy in LA :[) Anyway, the only reason why I'm writing this review is because I want to say DON'T GET TAKE OUT FOR THE HAINANESE CHICKEN RICE. Portion is soooo much smaller! It was the first (and only) time that I didn't get full from a take-out in NY. And this is LUNCH (which I mean to imply that I should get full easier...)! Argh. Portion is so much different when you eat inside. That's all :) I hope you still go to eat in the restaurant! :D

Sometimes, good things are happening to you when you list expect them. Last week I had to kill some time, I walked into Bubby's. There was not much good that day, surly nothing that could indicate the amazing journey of flavors I was about to experience. Do yourself a favor and go kill some time at Bubby's, and make sure you ask for the Applewood Smoked Heritage Pulled Pork Butt.

I went for brunch. Beautiful Room. Very pleasant servers, although they need to train their newbies better. (Like encouraging them to find someone who actually knows the answers and not just keep saying "I'm new here" or making things up). Rather pricey for what you get. I have no idea why crab cakes Eggs Benedict is $10 more than every other kind of Benedict at $26. I saw it come to a table. Still didn't get why it was nearly $30. I didn't hear orgasmic sounds coming from that table either, so... The carrot fries are over-rated. It really is a subjective matter of taste. I thought they were bland and that the sauce was mismatched. And they are NOT healthy since they are heavily battered and deep fried. The teenager at the table said she liked them. But she didn't finish them. What is NOT over-rated is the french toast sticks. Yummy! We placed a second order. The lemon curd is delicious with the sticks and mixing it with the syrup can make the dish addictive. My Schnitzel was so hard that it was difficult to cut. I had already sent back my bland farmer's tea that tasted like hot water after a 10 minute steep. So I just sawed my way through the under-seasoned/over-cooked cutlet the best way I could. Eventually I gave up and decided to taste it home and season it properly later. The teen really enjoyed her frittata. Her mom's fruit parfait was whipped to perfection. So it's hit or miss. Don't spend too much $ and keep it simple and should enjoy your visit. Try to go on a sunny day when you get all of that lovely light streaming in from the courtyard.

This place is mostly a noodle place. The food is okay. Spring rolls are actually fried eggrolls, almost like the ones you get in chinatown. The curry fried rice is dry curry fried rice. Its so-so. NOW the SERVICE SUCKS. THE PEOPLE WILL TRY TO RUSH YOU OUT QUICK. Â AS I WAS FINISHING MY PLATE, THE LADY SWOOPS BY AND TAKES MY PLATE (without asking) THEN USES MY NAPKIN TO WIPE THE TABLE. WTF. If you want a nice thai dinner go somewhere else.

I have been wanting to try Extra Virgin forever and was really excited to go Saturday night. It was a monsoon outside, but this place was still packed. The bar is not nearly big enough to hold all the people waiting for tables. We walked in a little before 8pm and had to wait 30 minutes for a table. I thought the wait was pretty reasonable, but I later found out why.... The food was very very good. Its cute that they give you a choice of olive oil to be served with the bread, hence the name Extra Virgin. I had the sea bass which was extremely well prepared and well seasoned. I'm not a big fan of fennel or mashed potatoes, but the bed the sea bass sat on was delicious. My date had the red snapper which was also very good. The roasted Brussels sprouts were awesome. I would love to give this place 4-stars for the food and atmosphere, but the service leaves a lot to be desired. The hostess had a bit of an attitude, but I wouldn't want that job either. The waitress was fine, but was rarely seen after we placed our orders. The two in charge of seating though were a constant presence. I understand that the restaurant is popular, but I didn't come here to be rushed through my meal like I was at Chili's. The guy was constantly looking over my date's shoulder to see how much we had left. He also kept bugging the tables on either side to see if they were done, even though they still had food on their plates. The food is excellent, but the employees needs to learn some manners.

Ate in the bar on a recent stint to the city. Â Nice to eat so well without reservations, in a bar, wearing shorts. Sometimes it is fun to do the sit-up-and-beg tasting menu thing, but actually I think I am done with that after eating here. A recommendation from long time New Yorkers. Almost felt like I could be living in the hood, my wife and I secretly watching the well-heeled families Â in the bar mowing through $200 meals with kids in tow. Isn't it terrific to eat amazing food in a casual atmosphere? After all, its all about my enjoyment as the customer right?

*****REVIEWER NUMBER 99***** Ptsss Ptsss Ey Buey Este Taco Esta de Pinche! (Mexican Accent) I Usually have to go California for some REAL TACOS but NOT anymore! Tiny place, but people don't sit there for long, so you can find a seat within 10 minutes (while you order, perfect time!) Ordered 2 Tacos Carne Asada and 1 Tacos Grilled Chicken. Chicken was a bit dry and had some burn pieces (BLEH!). But Carne Asada (With Everything in it. Soft Taco) Was soo Tastefull, Guacamole and Salsa all over the meat and juicy Steak!. Price is not Bad $ 4.00 Eeah, so for under 12 bucks you get 3 Tacos and a Happy Belly! Will be back for the Burritos, They LOOK THICK AND FILLING. But I will still go back to SAN DIEGO FOR TACO DEL GORDO! for now, i'll stick with this....

I went there today with a friend and a gentleman named Ara waited on us and he was awesome! Great service and suggestions. I eat gluten free and dairy free so sometimes it is difficult to find things that are yummy while out to eat and this place was perfect. I also recommend the lemon "cheesecake", I got it to go and I think I like it better than the real stuff!

Have had Freemans bookmarked forever and finally tried it for brunch last month - and I am happy to report it lived up to its hype!! Â Really cool alley entrance with pretty lights strung up and flowers outside. Â The restaurant itself has an old english feel with the deer heads and pheasants on display. Â The cocktails were amazing and service was really friendly. **Helpful bathroom tip - make sure it's locked, I walked in on a guy!!
Go on Monday after 9pm for industry night when all the pastas are $10. Â Go with 4 or 5 people and order everything. Â Drink lots of wine. Â It is foolish not to.
One of the best italians I've been to. The food encompasses all the traditional elements of italian cuisine and yet is modern and refined. The tiramisu is a killer.
this place is only ok. the food is Â good, but way overpriced, the service is correct, I don't like the hand written menu on the table, obviously without price, surprise!!!!!
Went here on a first date. Great option I think. Not too formal but still a nice environment. Food was good as well

I loved this little gem of a restaurant! Delicious perogis and you can mix the kinds Â (I did potato/cheese and mushroom/sauerkraut!) Service was super quick -- by the time my friend went around the corner to buy beer and got back (Byob) our food was on the table! Great place to go for a homey and stuffing meal.
Met local friends at the Midtown location. What a treat! Ramen here has no resemblance to the dried, salty packs you may have sampled. Try the pork rolls and any of the broth based dishes.

don't believe the hype! Â Our dinner was memorable for all the wrong reasons--ridiculous service--two of us ordered the four course prix-fixe. course 1 arrived 1/ 1/2 hours later the main courses arrived--they had forgotten the pasta course--the apology "I misread the computer" Â They were going to take back all the main courses--at $49 a pop we didn't want them reheated--so they brought the pasta last. Â The stellar dover sole had seen the coasts of dover many years ago--tough, overcooked and those supposedly crist potatoes were four , really, I counted, forlorn mutant french fries stuck in a bed of salty spinch somewhere under the sole. Â The lamp was also not etable--our friend tried sawing away but after 1/2 the first chop gave up--to apologize for the pasta mix up, the captain brought an after dinner sweet wine to the two who had lost out on their third course--we reminded him their were four at the table--he said "Well, I thought you were finished with your wine for the evening". Â The desserts arrived along with the usual free complimentary one and they were nice enough to take the dover sole off the check, we didn't ask and in fact protested. Â After all, we had had a really good time laughing at how bad it was--the other two main courses black cod and boullibase were also average and lukewarm. Â So the kitchen doesn't function properly, they are using mediocre ingredients, the front is confused but apologetic and at $160 a person (without the $49 dover "sole") it makes most of the city's really good and extravagently expensive restaurants look like bargains for quality, service, and experience.

It saddens me greatly that I lived in Chelsea for 2 years and only now discovered this gem! Great food at really reasonable prices. I had the chicken with roasted kale and quinoa, topped with avocado. It was seasoned incredibly well with great flavor; portions were huge, too! Friend and I also had a bottle of very reasonably priced red wine $32 that actually tasted good! Total bill was $80 for a bottle of red, chips & guacamole to start (also a generous portion- we got through about half of it), 2 entrees and a mac&cheese she ordered to go for her boyfriend. Awesome, yummy deal! Food came out fast too and service was exceptional. Go! But not when I go, because I don't want you taking my seat! :)

I loved this place... Some of the best Mexican food I have had in the city... and the prices are brilliant for what you get. I only gave four stars because our waitress was unnecessarily snarky . Also, the place is tiny, which I think gives it a great atmosphere, but also means you could wait anywhere from 20 minutes to an hour and a half to be seated, as they only take reservations for parties of two or eight. But that's not too much of a problem, you can just go grab a drink and come back, they are pretty good at keeping track of who's waiting. Their margaritas are also pretty fantastic.

I was visiting a friend in New York who promised me a delicious noodle soup and rice porridge restaurant. Coming from California, land of the Asian food, I was very wary and not expecting good food, but not fantastic. How wrong was I?? My friend ordered the duck rice porridge/congee and I had the egg noodle soup with duck and wontons. Woooow! Best wontons I've ever had!! Now, I like to look back and reminisce how good it was and how sad I am to be so far on the west coast. The duck is very good, too, although nothing that has stuck with me like the dumplings did. I had a bite of the rice congee and again, very delicious and very much above average, but nothing that truly sticks to me. The restaurant itself is bordering on hole in the wall, but hey, I'm only in New York once and I'm willing to overlook a less kindly and sparkling clean service. But the place is cheap - about $6 per bowl - and you get free tea, so very good deal in my opinion! Now someone please ship some wontons over to me!

I remember having brunch down in this area of the Village a while ago, and there was a place that had unlimited Mimosa's for $15 per person. Couldn't find that place, but was glad I stumbled upon this place with my friend. We arrived at 11am on a Sunday, so No Booze, until after noon. Â (just be aware) Â  Â Regardless, we found more than enough enticing and diverse menu items to keep us occupied. First order of the day, is coffee. Â Straight and strong for me. Â Fu Fu, and special "creme" for my friend. Â Whatever works for you. Â But my coffee was refilled continuously throughout my meal, without ever removing my forearms from the table. Â Even though that sounds "truck driver-ish", it speaks to a certain attentive level of service. My friend had some egg dish in crepes which was good sized portioned and enjoyable. I asked about their specialty, and they said it was their Mediterranean breakfast, which consisted of Eggs, over a spicy flavored tomatoes and peppers, Â all ringed by a fresh pita. (see picture) I ended up not eating the hard yolks, but overall this was very satisfying, relatively light, Â and very tasty. Overall, the service was excellent from beginning to end. Clean bathroom, and reasonable prices. Â (under $30 total with no booze), Â and toward the end of the meal were offered a booze option, since it was past noon, Â but that ship had sailed. This place is a solid four stars, if you're into slightly different breakfast options. Â (they also had steak & eggs, etc.)

Another crepe spot. Good, nothing makes it spectacular but what do you expect? The crepes are very very good. I've never tried a savory crepe but the sweet crepes (strawberry, banana) is usually what I go for. But they have a lot of interesting options on the menu. What's different about the crepes here is that are folded and turned into a cone shape. A new experience if you are used to crepes on a plate! They take credit cards. Small place though! (Like most other crepe shops)

Out of all the ramen places I've been to in NY, I like Totto the best. (Ippudo, Momofuku noodle bar, Ken, and Totto). But, expect to wait in a LONGGGGGGG line. I got the Totto Spicy Ramen w/ boiled egg & it was absolutely AMAZING. I was expecting the ramen to be pretty spicy, but it wasn't that spicy (still good tho). The char siu pork inside the ramen was super juicy! Because I waited for so long before I got seated, when I first got my bowl, I was pretty disappointed at how small the bowl looked....but, don't let it fool you! It will fill you up! :) It's pretty small inside, but it has air condition, so no worries! :) The workers are super friendly which is always a nice little plus! ;p

This place rocked! For an impromptu dinner we couldn't have been more impressed. Â It's been a really long time since I've randomly walked into a restaurant on a Friday night and left excited to return. The semifreddo is an absolute MUST!

As my husband just said when I asked him how many stars, "I'm fine with five!" Yummy start to finish with gracious attention from the waiter who let me try the wine before deciding. Fresh, delicious and I would frequent if I lived nearby. All good!

The food was simple and good. I pass by this place all the time and see people waiting to get in, but I don't think it would be worth it if I had to wait to be seated. It's 24 hours, so I guess they don't really have that much time to clean, which explains--but does not excuse--the dirty, smelly bathroom. It was really grimey and gross. Good thing I went after I was done eating.

Solid and worth a try for sure. Â We started with a new menu item, the radish and cucumber salad which was excellent, very flavorful and perfect on a warm summer evening. Â The blue crab and jalapeno was also tasty, fresh and seasonal as well. Â The oriechette was good and I particularly liked the duck sausage mixed in. Â The brazino and sword fish entrees were both on par but not overwhelmingly memorable. The room is great. Â It's a bit loud but very vibrant and feels very "neighborhoody". Â  There's a nice cross section of people there although I'm not a big fan of all the second year Citi/Solly analysts crowding the bar during week nights while seemingly planning the next banking crisis. Â The service was a bit spotty. Â Our waiter ended up being great but the gal behind the bar completely gave us the "snub" while she "shot the breeze" with one of the other bar keeps. Â I'd go back next time I'm in the neighborhood in any case.

I came here for breakfast based on a recent recommendation. I was told the nutella french toast was fantastic and just the perfect dish for someone in the mood for a sweet (versus savory) breakfast. I literally went to bed the night before giddy about the french toast I was to have the next morning. Fast forward to my morning at Penelope's. I had a pep in my step when I came off the subway. Little did I realize there would be such a wait mid-week?! That is a good sign - the place was BUMPIN'. I can't imagine what it's like on Sunday morning. So I waited, and waited, and waited. Finally table is ready. I walk in and take a look around. This place reminds me of Peels. Cool. Then I look at the menu even though I already know what I'm getting...but wait - there's no nutella french toast. Bummer! Just regular. So I order the regular along with chicken sausage. The french toast made with bread that was WAY too thick. Batter barely got halfway through. Fail. Chicken sausage was fine. Not memorable, though yes, I would probably order it again. So would I come back? Yes - to try one of their savory egg sandwiches. They seem to be wildly popular. I also would like to try the nutella french toast on of these days. But I will only come on a random weekday morning.

I'm not really a lobster kind of person...I usually go for crab...but, we trekked all the way to brooklyn flea to sample what had been touted as the #1 lobster roll in nyc. In all honesty? Â I was pretty excited. Â Luckily we arrived before the lunch rush. Â For $15 you get your lobster roll (maine or connecticut style), a bag of chips and a pickle wedge. Â Lobster roll is packed full of tender, juicy claw meat with a super light coating of mayo it's barely even there. Â All is on a crispy buttery toasted bun (OMG soo yummy) and the chips compliment this roll perfectly. Once you have your food, head over to a nice shaded spot on the steps and dig in...It's a lot more filling than you'd think, so start off with one and then get another if you really have the room for it. Â We tried maine style but maybe we'll go for connecticut style next time.

Like John Travolta in Pulp Fiction I crave the Royale with Cheese (and bacon). Ive been to this joint 3x and its just as good each time! I always order the Royale with Bacon and Cheddar ($8.50) cooked medium with a side of some thin crisp fries. The burger is big and juicy burger with bacon and complimented by a soft and seemingly fresh bug in addition to pickles, lettuce and a juicy tomato slice. If bacon isnt your thing the regular hamburger is $6.50 and the cheeseburger is $7.50.

A return pilgrimage on a New York visit after a couple of years away. Â Remembered this as one of the best burgers ever. Â Finally scratched that itch but found it an overall disappointing experience. Â Dive-like setting is kind of fun, but can't say the food is a highlight...burger meat did not taste like good quality stuff.

Definitely a fan of the brunch. Â Unlimited sangria!! Â Only managed to try the reds (1:30pm reservation is a bit late considering the sangria faucet turns off at 3pm), but I loved the fruit in the Harlem and the not-to-sweet Mulatta. Â That was one of my concerns - that the sangria would be sickeningly sweet. Â  There were some options on the sweeter side - one of the white sangrias had lychee in it and that's always bound to sweeten things up, but it was still delicious. Â  I am also very grateful to be able to remember the names of the sangrias I had, although perhaps that's a sign that I did not get my money's worth of sangria :) Â  Another concern -- the food. Â  Previously I'd been here for dinner and was unimpressed. Â Brunch however is great value - the entrees range from $14-$17 or so and with the unlimited sangria we definitely had $30+ worth of food and drink. Â  I opted for the Pollo Ranchero which was surprisingly good. Â My friend also loved her paella -- the sticky rice was infused with some kind of mushroomy flavor that was a pleasant surprise. Â Another friend got the quesadilla for a safe, fail-proof option. Â Wasn't amazing, but also wasn't a failure as a quesadilla, which is exactly what she was looking for. Â  Verdict: Â Would do again in a heartbeat. Â Maybe plus taco cart. Â You need the food to help with the sangria! Â It's gluttony with a purpose. Â Unfortunately reservations go out almost two months in advance so it may be a while before I make it to the UWS for another sangria induced coma.

Unlike the other restaurants and bars that cater to the young and hipster loud crowd, Sud is a calm oasis in Bed-Stuy. It feels like a hybrid sports bar and restaurant (the TV and the ATM in the lobby feel so out of place against the otherwise rustic atmosphere) but we quickly discovered that it is a very low-key, quiet place to have a comforting meal and conversation. They have a small menu, but there are plenty of options when it comes to the appetizers and crostini. I was very pleased by the caprese salad -- no balsamic, but they had an addictive pesto drizzle over the burrata that was very delicious. My main dish, the truffle tagliatelle, was also ridiculously creamy and flavourful, while the rustic "poor man's pasta" my bf ordered was divine. I even had enough for leftovers, which extended the pasta bliss through the next afternoon! Unfortunately, the downside is that the winter temperature permeates very strongly in the restaurant -- my bf kept commenting on how cold he was during dinner, and he's usually a space heater in lambswool. We're looking forward to the summer when we can return for good eats in a warmer climate.

Foodies paradise!! Â This is a tiny place in Williamsburg. Â It's right next door to Marlow and sons butcher shop. Â We went there for brunch. The place was super crowded but the staff was very helpful in trying to get us seated. We only waited about 5 minutes which was impressive. Â The seating is very right which means I was able to follow the hipsters conversations on either side of us. Nonetheless the experience was great. Our waitress wrote the specials on the white paper table cloth. Â Nice touch. Â And from what I understand the menu changes daily with what is locally fresh. Â  We started with a sardine app which had Beats mandarin slices with a homemade cream. Â  Â Ridic! Â My lovely gf had the lobster omelette. Perfectly done. Lobster was plentiful in a nice sauce wrapped by a moist omelette . Â Sided with cubed potatoes with made from scratch ketchup. Â I had the duck hearts with collard greens over a light egg salad. Â the duck hearts were cooked perfectly and the flavor was brain meltingly good. Â Highly highly recommended for anyone who appreciates the culinary arts.

I think that it is wonderful that Sushi has become something more of a fixture than a fad in America. I also think that there are many interpretations of the experience that are valid and unique. Still I feel there is something valuable about honoring traditions. If you truly love Sushi in the Japanese tradition this is the place to go. If you mix tons of wasabi paste in your soy sauce, if think that fat sliced pieces, or flashy maki are what it's about you won't like this place. I have been going here since 2001 and every time I know I'm going to be in town I try to work a visit in. I take sashimi first and I have never been disappointed with the freshness or quality. I usually order some toro if available and move to nigiri then maki/ hand rolls. The important thing is to respect tradition and let yourself have a relaxing more traditional experience. * Clean understated decor * Shaved wasabi not paste * Tuna lovers delight * make reservations, sit at the counter at least once

I am not a seafood type of guy, but this place made me fall in love with them!!! I never thought I would say this but I actually crave this place every now and then. One of the best seafood restaurant in NYC. Period!

I used to go here all the time when I lived in Boston and would come down to visit. However it was a Pizzaria Unos then and it was only cause we did not know any better. I had been meaning to try The Smith for some time but never really made it happen. Well yesterday I MADE IT HAPPEN. Â We went for Breakfast and it is for sure in my top 10 breakfasts of all time. Â My friend got the Sausage with poached eggs and cornbread and I got the poached egg with potato waffles. Â  If i could of eaten all of mine and all of my friends I would of. And then if i could of ordered something else and tried it. I think I would of. I had to force myself to stop eating. Â I think i want it now actually. ... i gotta go.

Took my mother here for her birthday this morning and yes it was an hour wait for two people on a Monday morning. So we were finally seated, greeted by our waitress and handed menus. Â It was such a hard decision to make because everything looked so good! But, we both decided to get the blueberry pancakes with the sugar cured bacon. Â  The pancakes were nice, fluffy, and warm with warm maple butter on the side. Â However, I wanted the warm maple butter to be sweeter. And the pancakes were nothing SPECIAL to me but, they were ok. Â Also since one of my fav breakfast food is sugar cured bacon, it was like heaven when those pieces of bacon were entering my mouth....aaaahhh, I would love a couple of pieces right now. Â  Cons: expensive for breakfast, the wait, cash only and I did not see a sign anywhere advising me of such before I sat down to eat!

Lunitas is just the platonic ideal of the cute Brooklyn coffee shop. Owned / operated by an adorable couple who always have their adorable baby on the premises. Probably because they just opened and they're looking to gain a toehold they are super doting - like friendliest coffee shop employees in history. Pastries are quality. Coffee is french press - sometimes they let it get a lil bit too gritty, but they keep it strong / fresh. They sell handmade baby clothes. The music is sometimes a lil bit too loud, but it's usually a great place to relax and get some work done in the morning. The neighborhood really needed Â this place.

Food was great in an historical setting. Lamb burger really hit the spot. The salad greens were fresh with a delicious honey balsamic dressing. The porterhouse pork chop with baked apples was thick, cooked perfectly and tasty. The lemonade was tangy. The setting was lovely. Service was mediocre. Arrived too late to visit the museum upstairs.
Great romantic place. Its my first time to experience this kind of service. you must come and see it..

My newly NY transplant friend never had Artichoke Pizza. We ordered the signature artichoke slice, a margarita slice, and a crab slice in one go. Sober (even better). Â What ensued was a gluttonous hot mess. The amount of crab on the crab slice was generous to say the least.

I have been to this place three times and there was always a line outside about half a block long. Â Be prepared for a wait that is about 20 minutes to 30 minutes during rain or shine. Cold or not. If you are allergic to waiting on long lines then this place is not for you. Avoid this place. Run, not walk, away from there. For those thinking that they could get the pizza ahead of everyone else, be forewarned that the line for take out is the same exact line as the one for those waiting to dine in. Â This makes sense since each pizza is made to order for everybody, dining in or not. No ordering by slices and no credit cards accepted. Â Cash only here. Now that the information about the place is given, how is the pizza you ask? Â Damn good. Â I have a preference for thin slice pizza so I was already a little biased toward this type of pizza even before I got here the first time around. Â I have tried the white and regular pizza each time I was there and I was never ever disappointed with the quality of the pies that I've eaten yet. The regular pizza is crispy thin crusted with a little burnt oven taste, giving it a slightly smoky flavor. Home-made mozzarella cheese and sauce are used while Â whole tomatoes slices and basil leaves are baked into the pizza. The white pizza. Â Same wonderful crust but slightly soggier because of the olive oil used in place of the regular pizza sauce. Same home-made mozzarella cheese but more of it on this pizza. Â There is a hint of garlic. Â Wait too long and this pizza might get soggy and limp faster than the regular pizza. Â This shouldn't be a problem if eaten fresh. The seating is a little tight inside. Â The seatings and tables are packed in very close together. I have never experienced the rudeness of the staff that a few other reviewers reported. Â My impression is that they are so overwhelmed with the constant crowd that they were never able to give you undivided attention but were professional enough when you wave them over.
Hit or miss. Have eaten there several times. Always packed. Great service. Food: sometimes fabulous, but other times, not so much. There's better options in the area.
I really do not like what I ordered, Spaguetti Marinara with Shrimps, the shrimps did not taste like it, anyway I want to come back again to taste something else as I saw some interesting plates.

Had a lovely meal here with my 3 yo daughter, who adored the chicken soup. Â The grilled meatball sandwich could have used some dressing, but overall I was happy with our meal and delighted to have a new and decent restaurant in the neighborhood.

The panini of prosciutto di Parma it's amazing, the service is great, you have to try the ginger beer, the price is really fare for the quality of food that they have, also the environment is good to go after work to have dinner.

this 1 michelin star restaurant was a complete disappointment. the taste of my mushroom ceviche with miso aubergines and ginger ponzu dish was way to strong. the mushroom itself tasted very nice but the sauce was overwhelmingly sour+salty+sweet sauce, probably overgenerous with its ponzu sauce. this ceviche+ponzu(citrusy+citrusy) dish drove me nuts. gulped a mouthful of water per bite of mushroom. grilled scallops with sweet chilli sauce, creme fraiche and green plantain crisps- scallop tasted a little raw on first bite, but improves on each subsequent bite. sweet chilli sauce+creme fraiche combo on top of the scallops were really nice though, although the ocassional taste of coarse salt was just too much. again, gulping down several mouthful of water for this dish. the sourness of my 2 appetizer dishes totally killed my taste buds and appetite for dessert. might go back to give it another go if i'm around the area and is too lazy to walk around. 1 star for scallops, one star for decor.

I love The Smith! I diner here with friends about once a month. Its always good, fun atmosphere, not too expensive, and good location. Pros; not too expensive, easy to have a good dinner and a glass of wine for under $35, fairly easy to get a reservation on Open Table, great menu of American foods, good wine selection, near the movies Cons; can get loud at dinner, at little crowded at times but thats to be expected

It's good, but it doesn't really stand head and shoulders above all the rest like everyone says. Also, I think the hot sauce is TOO hot. If you get the chicken with rice (which you always should at any halal cart) be glad they give you that extra pita--save it for once the hot sauce is searing off the roof of your mouth, it will help a bit

I'm really surprised that this place received such positive reviews. Â I went here for brunch, and it was fine, okay. Â We were seated in the garden, which was nice. Â I wanted to give the place a second try. Â I went back for dinner, and we were seated again in the garden. Â We had 5 ppl around one small bistro table, and the waiter would not let us put two tables together. Â He asked that I sit on the wooden bench rather than bother the other table to lend me a chair. Â Then we asked for olive oil for the bread...and were told no. Â Since the table was snug, I asked if we could order a little at a time but keep the menu. Â We were told no, we could not keep any menus (they gave us 2 menus for 5 ppl). Â Overall, the blonde waiter with a goofy look on his face sucked, but the food was good. Â I can think of several places with good food and bad service that deter its patrons from returning...and this is one more to add to that sorry list.

I cannot wait to come back here and order some more dishes. Â I was lucky to eat here with a group of nine people and was able to try more items than I could imagine. Â We must have ordered half of the menu. Â The outside of the restaurant appears small, but there is enough seating inside and the waitresses are patient. The Roti Canai was too small of a serving for my liking and the price, but the Satay was very impressive. Â The meat was very tender and the sauce was to die for. Â The crispy fish cakes were aromatic and the perfect texture, served with a sweet chili sauce. Â I loved their coconut rice. My favorite meat dish was the Fish Filet Golden Aromatic, which was crispy fried pieces of white fish coated in a smokey, light curry sauce. Â The fried pork chops were also delicious, and so was the Fragrant Chicken. Â I am not a huge fan of Sambal dishes, but they are starting to grow on me. Â I adore okra, so I had to order it with Sambal. Â However, with this okra dish, I have had better elsewhere. Â  Normally, I love black rice with coconut milk, but it was very watered down. Â Next time I return, I will definitely order another fish filet dish and try the Sizzling Tofu. Â Too bad they do not serve ABC ice.

The bf took me here for a surprise bday dinner and we had a fabulous time. I loved the apple entryway but it didn't match the somewhat old fashioned dining room. All of the service is friendly and attentive - from the coat check to the waiter. Â For example, the tables all have a lamp or candle to add to the ambiance but I almost tripped over the cord on the way to the restroom. Our waiter crawled around to hide the cord and assisted me when I returned to my seat. Now for the main event. Although tempting, we were not hungry enough for the tasting menu and I'm glad cause with all the extras we were stuffed. Â The bread was good, with an impressive variety. The amuse that came first was interesting but not something I'd ever order - basically beet gelee and creme fraiche. The Return from Chang mai lobster was fresh and unique though some of the textures were a little odd - tasted like pate in the middle. The sashimi tuna did not taste as fresh, and wasn't anything special. We had the duckling and the lamb chops. Both were very good, especially the perfectly tender duck. I thought the lamb was a bit more game-y than I prefer but the bf loved it. They also gave use complimentary potato puree which was good but too buttery for my tastes. We waited a pretty long time for our entres but I was kinda full by then anyway. For dessert we ordered the chocolate frivolous despite being full. They gave us a tiny dessert with curry ice cream and pineapple that was good. The frivolous turned out to be a sampling platter which we couldn't finish. Lastly, a plate of petit fours came out which we bravely sampled but again could not finish. On the way out they gave us a lemon cake. It was a little dry (the next day) and I'm not a big fan of lemon but it was a nice gesture. So all the desserts we tried were all good but lacked a 'wow' factor. Overall the food was great, although some of the 'extra' dishes were not good enough to eat more of. I would give the food 4 stars but the amazing service and great company made the experience a 5.

I shared the porkloin katsu curry and the tenderloin katsu don with my friend. I would recommend both, but if you had to choose one, go for the katsu curry---it was delicious! The bread crumbs and the pickled things in it made the difference. Â The white rice was cooked to perfection (keep in mind I like it on the softer side). Â Each dish was $11. The katsu don came with miso and katsu curry didn't. I'd definitely come back!
Best beef pancakes in town. Long lines, horrible customer service. It's cheap eats, what do you expect.
Loved the food, loved the service, and loved the ambience. Everything was lovely at this restaurant.

I have been looking to go to Grammarcy Tavern for several years. We chose the bar menu and I was so underwhelmed compared to other restaurants we went to. Service was rushed and unattentive....disappointed

This place is down the street from my store and it's hard to resist the wonderful smell of fresh baking pitas each day. I've never done anything wrong to them, so what's up with that? It's called customer service, dudes. Sorry that I give you $ and ask to skip some fillings. After encountering their smirks and rudeness again today, leaving me to feel like I wanted to crawl under a rock, I am not going there again. Doubt they will care though! xo

Don't understand the great reviews. Â I admit i have no experience with authentic hawaiin cuisine, and im basing my review on my own sense of taste. Â We split what was essentially spam maki for an appetizer, and then split an order of locomoco and glazed chicken entrees. Â Flavors were very one-note. Had a wonderful Sunday evening here. This is my 4th time here and it gets better every time .... On Sundays after 6 they have some great traditional Irish music ... The best Irish coffee I have ever had and some great tasting food ... We had the fish and chips and sausage rolls which were both wonderful ... They give you a bacon mayo with the chips and it should be illegal !!! We had a few different mixed drinks which were all great ... The staff were very friendly and checked on us constantly to make sure all out orders were good ... It's pricey but your paying for the quality of the drink and food ... Looking forward to becoming a regular on a Sunday and trying the Sunday lunch the next day ...
COOOOOOOOOORRRRRRRRRNNNNNNNN. Â I could come and just eat 3 of the corns. Â But the fried plaintains are good too.

Prosperity is the archetypal hole-in-the-wall dumpling joint. Â I'm convinced that there is no better bang for your buck in all of New York City when it comes to dumplings. Â That's not to say there might not be some place out there with fantastic dumplings and buns, but with FIVE dumplings for ONE DOLLAR (not to mention the $1.75 sesame pancaked with duck sandwich), Prosperity can't be beat. Â I literally just went there 4.5 hours ago and shared 10 dumplings, 4 pan-fried pork buns, a duck sandwich, and a bottled water for $5.75 and I haven't felt the need to eat since. Â  Prosperity's only real competition is Vanessa's Dumplings. Â Vanessa's has some advantages--namely slightly more variety and more seating (Prosperity has seats for about 6 people total--but the flavor at Prosperity puts Vanessa's to shame. Â There's absolutely no reason put soy sauce on a Prosperity dumpling, all that you need is just a tiny bit of hot sauce to give it a kick. Â These dumplings have a nearly ideal pork-to-dough ratio, the dumpling is not over fried or dripping with oil (which is often the case at Vanessa's), and the pork has a superbly rich flavor. I vehemently declare Prosperity to be the king of cheap dumplings (sorry Vanessa's, you still hold a special place in my heart).
LycÃ©e martini for $6 and it's not happy hour... I'm sold. And their food is really good. Try the crispy spring rolls. I love coming here when I'm in Hell's Kitchen.
This may be the best pizza I've ever eaten - Got there at 430PM on a Monday and there was no wait :) washed it down with 2 Brooklyn Lagers and was sighing with delight after ever bite.

This is the best Italian food I have ever had The food was immaculate. Â The peppery meat lasagna was the high point for me, with dipping the delicious bread in the remaining sauce being a close second. Â My wife spoke with the owner for some time and when she found out it was my birthday, she treated us with 4-5 Italian dessert pastries, which were each better than any that I had at any other point on the trip...and we were regulars at the Plaza Food Hall, which is great in its own right (for a price). Â The owner is the sweetest lady and was literally calling out to us as we left wishing me a happy birthday. Â Ignore reviews that claim she is anything but nice - those people must suck. I will absolutely be back.

we went on late on a weds night after a long plane trip from california. Â i have to tell you... it was majorly crowed for a weds night. Â don't ppl have work to do the next morning? anyhow, we put our name down when the host informed us that there's 30 min wait. Â that's a long wait past 10 pm! Â so we walked to another restaurant, didn't like it as much, returned... 'n voila! Â our table was ready... way before 30 mins! Â pleasant surprise. the atmosphere is definitely bustling and slightly noisy from the small space and number of people occupying. Â we ate upstairs in a booth. Â i ordered the roasted halibut w/ pureed lentil 'n stew tomatoes. Â absolutely delicious! Â it was perfectly seasoned... 'n i just loved the creaminess of the pureed lentil. i ordered the pimm ginger cocktail, which was something that was new to me. Â it was slightly sweet with fresh ginger 'n cucumber taste. Â very refreshing after a long, hot day... even though it was mostly on the plane or hanging out at the airport. Â the flourless chocolate cake was light 'n fluffy with rich chocolate taste without the heaviness that the flour provides for most chocolate cakes. service was pretty good although our waiter didn't smile too much or introduce himself. Â however, there was a waitress who came by with bottles of water whenever we were out. Â it was almost as if there was a webcam looking down @ our table, which signaled to her when we were done w/ our bottle. Â 'n yes, we were a thirsty crowd! the only negative i would have to say would be the lack of space. Â it was quite stuffy inside w/ need for better circulation. Â there's a nice breeze from the water outside! Â and it didn't help that there was a loud party next to us w/ just wouldn't shut up. Â too much wine, i suppose. i gave it 4 stars, because i really loved the food. Â i would highly recommend it to all visitors 'n locals alike.

the go-to coffee shop in Midtown East. Â This place was MUCH needed in the neighborhood. Â Wish they had more seating, but that's not really their fault. Â Tiny - delicious - STRONG coffee (be prepared - It knocks you on your arse - in the best way possible.) ... Staff is exceptionally friendly and nice too. Â Big fan.

Beautiful restaurant, friendly staff, if the food catches up it could easily get 5 stars: The newest addition to Carroll Gardens (for now Frankie's up the street just unveiled a new building & everyone is a buzz what may be coming to the hood next). Â I really like the thought behind EVERYTHING that has gone into this establishment. Â From the name (after the channel of water connecting governors island to BK) to the map on the menu that explains the name, to the bistro style menu - lots of options. Â Supporting the local (and I mean very local merchants the italian shop Caputos & the pork store on court street here in carroll gardens) and great lines. Â  They only take reservations for parties of 5 or more and luckily we were 5 on a Tuesday night however, we had to reschedule or reservation to Friday. Â When we arrived they didn't have the reservation on the books however handled it very very well. Comped us drinks until we were seated. Â As for the Food it is good - not amazing, not compelling but good. Â For a area that has become a foodies dream the food needs to step up a little. Â Sweet potato croquettes too fried not enought goat cheese sauce, schnitzel was amazing, fried chicken texture over fried but flavor very good, nimen ranch steak rubbery, warm lamb salad good. We passed on dessert but had a great digestive - the mistletoe; try it you'll love it!

Great Burger, great little outdoor space for squirts. Â This place is a little light on atmosphere, but is perfect for kids and the burgers are legit. Â Similar to a shake shack burger (I used to call them west coast burgers; Bistro Burgers were NYC/ east coast archetypes), but bigger than shack burgers. Â We went at 6 on a Sunday and every other group there had kids, which was really nice. Â  Delicious spot we will definitely return.

First, let me start by saying that my coworkers and I were really looking forward to this place finally opening. Â There aren't a ton of options in the Financial District beyond the usual Stone Street fare, and post-Sandy, there are even fewer places to go for an after-work drink. Â  Unfortunately, when we finally visited the Dead Rabbit, we were extremely disappointed. When we arrived, the downstairs pub (the Taproom) was extremely crowded. Â We weren't terribly surprised, since the place is relatively new, so we tried to take a look upstairs (the Parlor). Â We were stopped by a middle-aged man named "Ted," who told us that we couldn't go upstairs at the moment, but that he would take our names and let us know when a table upstairs opened up (by his estimation, in the next half hour). We gave him our names and sidled up to the downstairs bar to get a drink. Â In addition to being pretty crowded, the Taproom is extremely narrow, with very little seating. Â Servers and patrons were constantly elbowing past us, forcing us to either cram up against the people waiting to order or hug the drink rail on the wall to avoid getting pushed. Â We ordered a couple cocktails, which were pretty unremarkable, and waited for our table. Â  Over the next 45 minutes, we saw Ted wander past us maybe a dozen times (we were only 15 feet from his position by the stairway leading upstairs). Â He never said a word but made eye contact with us several times. Â Because he wasn't calling out anyone's name, we assumed that he had a pretty good handle on who was on the list to be seated. Â Silly us. We finally walked up to Ted and asked how long our table would be. Â He asked for our names (uh-oh) and said, "Oh, yeah, I couldn't find you. Â I gave your table away."
