Â We informed him that we were standing right in his line of sight for the past 45 minutes and that he had walked right by us numerous times. Â He responded with, "Oh, you must've been in the john when I looked for you." A.) We weren't, (B) Seriously, all of us?, and (C) You still couldn't have at least called out a freakin' name before giving up and giving our table away? Anyway, we were finally seated about 15 minutes later. Â Four of us were crammed at a tiny little table that was clearly only meant to seat two people comfortably. Â We ordered another round of mediocre-yet-overpriced "signature" cocktails and ordered a couple small plates. Â We were informed that if we all tried to order food, they wouldn't have room on the table to serve us (Seriously??). The food (veal meatballs and chips w/ dips) was really underwhelming and not at all worth the wait. Â We didn't stick around after the snacks, but instead left in search of a better bar. Despite the Dead Rabbit being one of the closest bars to our office, my coworkers and I probably won't be returning, and I've told other people thinking about trying the bar to either skip it or, if curiosity gets the better of them, to at least set their expectations VERY low.
Great food and EXCELLENT service!

After reading yelp reviews the entrance still faked us out but did find it! Â Four of us for dinner and we ate inside by the open kitchen. Â Apps tried cheese plate and oysters. Â We had the duck, steak and bass. Â Nice bottle of wine. Â Shared mousse for desert with expresso coffees. Â Everything from beginning to end was very enjoyable. Â Service was attentive and not overbearing. Â Prices reasonable. Â Will return.

Amazing appetizers (pork butt, dumplings!, mint chicken salad). Mains were a disappointment by comparison but are still very tasty on an absolute scale. Excellent service. Elegant Thai iced tea presentation. I will be back!!!

When you first walk in, you wonder to yourself if dining here is a good idea. It looks dingy and the place screams claustrophobia. However, the food is delicious. The platters are $10 but worth it. Rice, beans and maduros go in one to go tray. The other tray is for your meat. YES, YES, YES. Let me drink a Presidente while I'm paying on line. Not sure you can consider this to be a clean place but it has an "A" rating. My belly tells me it has an "A" rating for food. My doctor says it's a "C" rating for your health, so splurge (eat voraciously) sporadically. IFHTP 3+

Mediocre at best. While the service was phenomenal the food really just wasn't that great, especially for the price. Tough calamari, dried out chicken. There is far better Italian food in NYC so I would advise you keep looking to avoid disappointment.

My go-to Latin food spot in East Village. I come here often especially in the summer when there's outdoor seating. The food is really good (my favorites are the veggie arepa and the empanadas) and so are the drinks! They have happy hour quite often so its definitely worth checking out.

Honestly one of the best sandwiches I've had in the city. Quality and flavorful ingredients on toasted foccacia. It's one of those places where I'm not scared to try something new on the menu because it'll most likely taste great. The only negatives are that the foccacia is quite hard to chew. The texture is a hard crust french bread which has a nice flavor but after a few bites - it sure does give your jaw a workout. I tried the filet of roast beef which was delicious. The beef was sliced thin, perfectly seasoned and tender. The sauteed onions had a nice smokey light flavor (not greasy) that complimented well with the tomatoes, swiss, and field greens. Don't forget to ask for a side of their garlic mayo - goes amazingly well with the roast beef. I'm not normally a mayo fan but the garlic mayo - delicious! Prices are really good for the quality of the sandwich. Everything on the menu from sandwiches/salads are around $8.75. They also serve a small selection of breakfast sandwiches/soups/pastries/coffees and teas. The cafe is small so it wouldn't be an ideal place for large groups. There's a counter space for seating on one wall. And a few small tables and chairs. The ventilation could also be better as the air was filled with a smokey aroma probably from their open food prep/kitchen area. Overall a great cafe for artisan sandwiches. I can't wait to try out other options on the menu - apparently the crunchy tuna is one of their most popular.
Great spot to meet, to eat, drink and lounge. Never had a bad meal here nor a bad cup of coffee. I like their merguez sausage sandwich and the their variety of sweet and savory crepes are great too!

Mmm, "wow," and "so good" was all I kept saying as I devoured my beef stew with wonton noodle soup. That dish is absolutely phenomenal and simply just the best. I had always been a fan of Wonton Garden ever since I was a little girl when my parents used to bring me to the original restaurant. I was devastated when they closed down, but when they reopened at this new location I just never found time to go because I am never in Chinatown. I am so glad I picked this place for lunch today. The broth was so beefy and delicious, the beef was very tender, and the wontons... well, no where compares! I did find the egg noodles to be overcooked but nonetheless I was a very happy camper with the dish as a whole. Call it nostalgia. :) I did, at one point, bite into a piece of pure fat, it was so gross I had to spit out. Don't expect to come in and be treated like royalty as this has your typical Chinese restaurant kind of atmosphere, no gimmicks kind of place. Just be warned that gratuity is already included in your bill and the handwriting is really bad so you would not notice if you just look at it very quickly. The prices are a teeny bit higher here as it is a tourist trap but is still cheap nonetheless. The restaurant is well ventilated with air conditioning in case you are weary to go in on a hot summer day like I originally was.

I really liked this place. I have eaten here only once but the food was very tasty and everyone working there was Thai. I sat outside in the patio and I really enjoyed the atmosphere. I would definitely come back here again. Â I also thought it was cool that they sell different Thai foods to go in the fridges they have in the front of the restaurant. Â The menu was cheap which is common for Thai places. Â I can't emphasize enough how nice it is to sit outside, on a nice day of course.
This is a great spot in the SOHO are and offers late night dining, which is a huge plus! Â The duck confit is delicious as are the oysters. Â The bakery and any of the breads are always delightful.

Definitely hit the spot for lunch. The service was great, we walked in around 12:10pm and was immediately seated. I ordered the ropa vieja and it was so delicious. I think I scraped the plate when I was done. For my drink I had a glass of red sangria and we were out of there by 12:50pm.

Mighty Quinn's is always packed with a line out the door, but the line moves relatively quick. The workers will help you find seats and shift people if necessary to get your group to fit. That being said, my favorite options here are their pork cheeks and ribs. I've tried their sausage, brisket and baked beans. The pork cheeks are so tender and flavorful. The ribs are a dry rub but I like my ribs saucy. I added a ton of BBQ on the ribs and they were delicious. The brisket was a little stringy and dry. However, the guy sitting next to me was saying how the brisket was better than even the brisket he's tried in Texas. *Shrugs*

My partner and I dined here during our last night in the city, and it was the perfect way to end our holiday trip. We both indulged in the chef's 8-course tasting menu. Every dish was phenomenal made exponentially better by the uber-attentive service. We opted for the wine pairing, as well, which was an excellent choice. Two drinks at the bar, dinner and wine pairing put us north of $400, but it was worth every penny and every minute of the three-hour service. Hoping to come back during our next visit.

Love love LOVE this place. My boyfriend and I moved to Park Slope a few months ago and were yelping around trying to find good Latin food. THIS is the best. The first time we went for brunch. Started with guacamole, of course, which was out of this world. Â The bf had the Colombian breakfast and I had the Latin breakfast with a side of coconut french toast. The portions were huge and left us completely satisfied. I also pounded down a couple DELICIOUS pomegranate mojitos [only $5 at brunch] with fresh muddled limes, mint and pomegranate seeds. And although the drinks looked petite, they packed a punch that caught up with me quickly. During dinner hours they bring complimentary plantain chips with homemade salsa. Which is kind of sweet and spicy almost reminiscent of a Latin duck sauce. Strange, but quite tasty. We've been back for dinner a few times since. Did i mention $5 drinks ALL NIGHT mon-wed? The only reason I wouldn't give them 5 stars, is they seem to be a bit understaffed at times. A few times we've waited up to 10 minutes to be greeted, have drinks delivered, etc. So, maybe not the best place to grab a quick bite..but certainly the best place to grab everything else.

The hostess kicked me out the door since my party has not arrived yet. I had to wait for my party out in the cold. And the cruel thing about it, I can hear the waitresses laugh so hard for what they did to me. Ok, I understand they're busy and I still want to try the yakitori and compare it with my authentic yakitori experience from Tokyo, Japan. As soon as my party arrived we went upstairs to be seated. Disappointment - really tight, customers are elbow to elbow in a very cramped space. I was still excited to have my first yakitori. Another disappointment - The food taste like gas from the grill. I do not mind it being pricey knowing I will be happy with the food. But yuckkk!!! Aside from the bad treatment, it was really a very disappointing night.

I read tons of hype about this place...yes its good but hands down best Thai EVER?? I don't know. The place is huge but they definitely pack people in...service is so-so. The food was good but I feel like I've had better or comparable Thai at other places in Queens. We got a pork appetizer that I didn't like very much, the meat was chewy and dry. The papaya salad is unique and delicious. I got the chicken with basil and eggplant, it actually was a little bland for my taste. They are definitely heavy on the garlic so maybe not a place to take a date. ;-)

..... i had high expectations of this place after reading everyone's reviews, but i'm sorry to say, it fell short. i tried the following: - black sesame creme brulee - sakura flan - earl gray chocolate mochi - cold (something, i forgot the japanese word).... it's ricecakes w/ redbean paste - lavender mint tea - white peony tea - lemon verbena tea "the you-know-what over at you-know-where is better," i whispered furtively to my friends who were with me. i had to keep my voice low because we were sitting at the bar right in front of three waitresses who were diligently wiping teapots and teacups, casting long empty stares over our heads. the 'you-know-what' i was talking about referred to the black sesame crisp that came with the creme brulee, and 'you-know-where' was kyotofu. i found the black sesame crisp at cha-an too thick, chewy and slightly stale. i like my black sesame crisp to be lace-thin and crunchy. yah, just like at 'you-know-where'. i can comment on each individual item i tried, but i shan't. i will, however, say that the prices here are a bargain (relative to the proportions). maybe i'm getting what i pay for, because i think that none of the desserts really stood out. they tasted too similar and the flavours simply fused with and disappeared into one another. after a while, you don't even care anymore if you'd just scooped into the black sesame creme brulee or the redbean paste or the greenbean-based sakura flan, because they all tasted the same. it was around this time when my tastebuds were screaming "boring!!! boring!!! boring!!!". :( as for the teas, i like the vast selection offered here. the lavender verbena was delicious, with matching fragrance to boot. the white peony, so so.... tasted way too mild to earn a proper description. the lavender mint, sadly, tasted more like regular peppermint tea with undetectable lavender flavour nor smell. i gotta mention that they brew most of the tea for you here, so expect to get a pot of tea water sans leaves. hence, perhaps the white peony and lavender mint teas were underbrewed? who knows. in conclusion, this place isn't so bad that i'd give it less than 3 stars. in fact, i'm willing to return here again to try the cooked food, but i'm more than okay with skipping dessert. (IMO, fans of black sesame should head over to 'you-know-where' and order the black sesame sweet tofu; it is far more superior there.) note: toilet bowl is installed with lots of buttons, including bidet functions. fancy schmancy.

I have been meaning to update my original review of this place for awhile, I thought I gave it a 2 last time so was going to give it a 4 this time....but I would like to actually give it a 4.5 now. Anyway, since the first time I went here I've been back a few times and they have given me everything I ordered. Â The peasant salad is great and the grilled calamari (and i dont even like calamari unless it's fried) is so insanely good. Â The octapus is very good as well. Â And the house wine is cheap and good. Â We came last night again and had the best waiter ever, they had run out of the free dessert so he gave us a carafe of the house wine instead! Â Which is way better than a free dessert anyway! Â The only problems are sometimes the service is slow (and bitchy) and when you leave you are so full you want to throw up.
The extra spicy ramen was to die for with pork and boiled eggs. Â Plus the port buns were delish as well. Â Worth the 1hr wait but not come too hungry.

I have been to Grimaldi's four times and the pizza has been either excellent (twice) or just ok (twice). On excellent days the sauce, cheese and crust are perfect. The crust is very thin but somehow its crunchy on the outside and soft and chewy on the inside. On the ok days the sauce has been bland and the crust has been dry. I would tell my friends to go for the experience, pray for the excellent pie and enjoy the rehabilitated DUMBO pier area and park.

Great broth and flavors. Wished they gave more meat, but it's the norm to get 2 prices of pork I suppose. The Wait was a bit long and it was pretty warm inside but we would come back when we are in town.

They have Polar beer, jugo de parchita and a full bar. That was good enough for me. The staff was nice. I have had better Venezuelan food in NY, but this was definitely not bad. Their empanadas are pretty good, but their arepas could improve a little-the dough just didnt taste very good. Their tequeÃ±os are tiny and they come with fancy sauce for dipping. They really should find a better tasting sauce.

i have to say I'm quiet disappointed with the pizza... This always happens when you have too high of expectations.. I've been wanting to come here forever.. We have party of 8.. on a sunday evening.. it was not hard to get a table at all that's a ++ Â we ordered clam pie .. I personally think it's Â a little bit too dry.. plus it takes forever .. hence service was slow I'm not a pizza expert here but I've tasted better pizza before.. My overall experience here wasn't as good as I expected.

i had some roast duck wonton noodle soup yesterday for lunch and good god i miss you NY Noodle Town. why do you have to be 3000 miles away. people think i'm weird when i talk about the amazing flavorful broth of Â your noodle soups in 3rd person, why, because no other noodle shop has it. i also miss your bbq overrice dishes and your creamy congees with crispy dough. while you may not be the best in all that you serve, you are one of the many reasons why NY is the best when it comes to chinese food in america.

Your clubbing experience in NY is not complete until you eat a bowl of chicken and rice at 3am blackout. This place is so delicious...and they give you so much food! I recommend getting half chicken and half lamb for variety (although if you are drunk I am sure you will hardly notice the difference). Go wild with the white sauce, be conservative with the red sauce. Â Trust me, whatever amount of hot sauce you think you can handle, use only a quarter of that amount. Â If this sauce was a pepper it would be hotter than habanero. Watch out for imitators! Go 53rd and 6th!

The restaurant name had me at hello. It's a tiny place with a decent menu selection w/ appetizers, pizza, and risotto. Â Also they offer the pizza and risotto a la gluten free. Â I honestly couldn't tell the difference but hopefully my belly did. Â Risotto was good - but nothing memorable. Â i think there's a lot of potential - great concept of a restaurant. Â I wish SF had something similar.

I don't understand all the great reviews. A friend even recommended this place to me - she said they had the best pizza and they always stop by here while in NY. My husband and I both thought the pizza was bland and overpriced. The bottom crust was soggy, the rest of the crust was burnt tasting. There was hardly any topping on it - considering they charge about $3 per topping, we expected it to be more substantial. We still felt hungry after finishing 3 slices each. The service was okay - not overly friendly, but not rude, though we did feel rushed. Maybe this is just a NY thing. I have to say the $3 slices we had from Patzeria Perfect Pizza in Times Square were a 1000% better.

Came here for my b-day dinner back in December...we had a very early table because we had a play to catch...and perhaps because we were one of the first tables of the night, they just weren't up to bringing the magic. Everything we had was just fine ... fine for a date night, but not memorable enough for a birthday dinner. Willing to try it again, but for now it stands as a "meh"

I'm pretty sure I could eat a tub of the smoked liver mousse from here. Who the hell says that? Too bad it's only seasonal. The sirloin tartare is also a must. I'm not one for raw meat, but I would high five this dish if I could. Â The spicy pork sausage and rice cakes makes my mouth water thinking about it. Really glad I don't live in NY or else someone would have to roll me around town from pigging out here.

I think at this point adding to the 170 or so glowing reviews may be moot, but this place hit the spot for me. I took my brother, a pizza junkie and aficionado, and we enjoyed the mushroom pie. When I used to live nearby, the lines deterred me , but we hit the timing just perfectly at 3 on a Thursday, and were seated right away. This pizza reminded me of New Haven pizza, which may be a crime since this is NY, but the most famous New Haven pizzeria, Pepe's, has a similar coal-fired oven. The difference here is ingredients. Grimaldi's uses a fresh-tasting, slightly chunky sauce (which, if it is canned, I'm fooled), silky fresh mozzarella, and other fresh veggies and spices. The pizza comes sprinkled with a few basil leaves, and a crispy, sometimes charred crust.
One of my favorite spots!!! Such good food and so much fun! Love it! Love it! Love it!

How much more food could I have eaten last night before actually exploding? Needless to say, the only thing I have eaten today has been a small salad. That definitely was not the case last night as after attending a Yelp event where I had gorged myself silly I then hopped over to this intimate gathering that was basically a private event set up by a fellow Yelper Sally W (Godmother of Chinatown). I am so glad I decided to come and not skip out or I would have passed up on a terrific meal. As about a dozen of us took our seats at a large communal wooden table we were greeted by the friendly staff and the owner, Joshua, and the restaurant manager Nathan. All were very attentive and offered us first class service. The restaurant itself has a classy chic vibe with a hint of the old country thrown in. Warm, inviting, and indicative of the part of town it resides in. Great for a casual date, or a dress to impress meal. There is so much to choose from on the menu. Sally W chose a terrific saki for the table that was chilled and had a nice plum flavor to it. We all decided to order a bunch of small plates to sample as a starting point. I think everyone were all drooling in anticipation. A few of us shared the following - Ebi Mayo- Fried Shrimp with Yuzu Mayo. I really enjoyed this! Just the right amount of seasoning with a light crustiness to it. Shishito Peppers - Charred Fried Japanese Peppers, Yuzu Salt, and Lemon Aioli. Not too spicy with just a touch of saltiness to them. Nice plate to share as there is a good amount here. Hirata Buns (Steamed Buns), 3 per order. Kobe Beef - Â Hijiki, Red Onion, and Togarashi Mayo. Pork Belly - Lettuce, and MisoMayo. Wow - these were both very good. Theirbun is served open style and reminded me of Pac Man! Delicious - can't go wrong with either one. As my main Ramen dish I had the Wasabi Shoyu Ramen - Soy sauce,chicken and vegetable based noodle soup, topped with bean curd, wasabi, menma, kaiware radish, shiso, scallions, and wasabi infused oil. AMAZING!!! Such complexand rich tastingbroth! The noodles were perfectly al-dente as I like. The ingredients were well thought out and accentuated each other perfectly in this bowl of heaven. You can tell they take great pride in their ramen here at Zutto. Can it get better? Hell yes! For dessert we ordered a few things to devour - Brioche Bread Pudding - Caramelized Banana, House Made Vanilla, and Ice Cream. I am not a big bread pudding fan but this just made me change my mind! "Coffee And Donuts" - Coffee Semifreddo, Foamed Cream, and Zeppole Donuts. GOOD GOD!!! That coffee drink thingy is amazing. Almost like a chocolate malted foamy drink. The mini zeppole's were melt in your mouth goodness. I walked away from this meal so happy, fat, and content. Such an inviting and friendly staff to go along with the terrifically prepared food. Along with the fun and warm group we were with made it even better. Also, even being in this part of town the prices are quite affordable. Quite the gem for sure. Thanks to everyone at Zutto for a wonderful evening!

So my brother loves this place, and I am trying to figure out why. Maybe because its a stones through from his apartment? Maybe because he loves chips and can't stop raving about the ones from here? Whatever the reason, we decided to go here for lunch. We both got the chicken platter. It was good but not amazing. I felt like something was lacking in the seasonings. It wasn't he right mix to make it perfection. All that being said, I do get why my brother loves the chips. They are good! Thick and crispy, can't go wrong there. They were so tasty, I ended up just eating them and not the salsa I got to go along with them. Might need to go back and get more chips so I can try that salsa.

You HAVE to go here for brunch and try the House Eggs....accompanying it with this beverage called The Black Velvet. (Guinness and champagne...it sounds funny - but it is delightful. Actually, their taps are so cold and so clean - I think their Guiness is the best pint in NY.) For desert go for the date cake or MY favorite... the grilled doughnuts. :) Dinner time is really special as well....live music... so cute. Â Just don't go right at 8:30 on a Friday or Saturday or you may have to wait a minute. p.s. the staff is great.
First time here. Sausage sampler was fantastic! The for two portion is all the food you need for two people.

Food was great. Tapas style. The place is extremely small so you will share your small tables with others (unless you have 8 people in your party). Â The staff also explains the food very well - it makes you appreciate the food more.

Finally got to this place after being discouraged from going on several weekends by the long wait. On a summer Friday at 1pm, there was still a 30 minute wait. I had the blueberry pancakes, which were amazing and were served with what tasted like a maple syrup and butter mixture. Also had a side of cheese grits, which were nice because they weren't too runny and the cheese was blended well. Would have given it 5 stars for the food, but the prices are a little high and when my friend asked for some more maple syrup, they tried to charge him $2 for it. Oh, and they are cash only - I'm alway skeptical of cash-only businesses.

First time here. The waitress said the restaurant is "tapas" style. Â We felt it was more like glorified appetizers. Â We had the Korean Wrap, BLT Bun and the duck (big enough to be considered entree as per the waitress). Â  Pros: The korean wrap was pretty good, the steak was delicious. Â The Blt bun was good but we have had better baos. Â The duck was DELICIOUS. Cons: The wrap and buns come in 3s and they were $9/plate. Â I would pay for a solid $10 if it came in 4s instead. It is just better for sharing with even numbers. Â The duck could be a little bit cheaper, it was asking $23. Although the decor strives for simplicity by design, there were tons of water marks on the ceiling and the walls were dirty. Â The ceilings/walls really should be fixed b/c it messes up with the ambiance. It was pricey especially if each plate was considered "tapas" style.
I always knew this place was a take-out korean fast food type of place. Â What I did not know was that they serve alcohol here. Â No wonder why it's always crowded.

It's pretty small but the taste of the food is biggg. (if that makes any sense at all) The price is more on the heavy side but the Cafeteria Burger, though simple, was rather fulfilling. The Mac Atac was also definitely delicious. Breakfast food is served from 8AM until 5PM. The service was really good too. Our waiter was either overly metro or simply gay (most likely gay because.. well hello. it's in chelsea) but super friendly. AND i thought he was just so adorable! its not too often where you meet an asian guy who is cute. But anyways.. the food was really good. It's a trendy place for young adults, i'd say. Good place to just sit and chill with your friends over some delicious food. But the place is usually packed. There is usually a long line to get in during the night time. i think day time should be fine on a good day. i went around 3 on a Friday and there was no wait. next time you want to make lunch/dinner plans, check out Cafeteria! * they have matches!
Great Sicilian pizza, great service. I almost didn't go inside. It looks like an abandon garage. Great place to hang on Sunday have lunch and watch the NFL at the bar.

Gotta say I was pretty impressed with the food. A little on small side of small plates but very tasty. Friendly service, and chef on the line all night. A beautiful space design. Will visit again and try more.... Mushroom paella was great!
I ate here my last night. It was the worst experience at a restaurant of my entire life. The service is a disaster and the manager is awful.

Perfect for a pre-theater dinner or just a nice simple meal with a friend or date. Â They have a HUGE selection of wine, where the selections look more like a novel than a menu. Â  Last night, my girlfriend and I had the unlimited tableside servings of 3 different Â pastas which also came with an appetizer. Â We were pleasantly pleased and very satisfied by the end of the night.
Wow

Gonna try and keep this review small, just like Upstate's hole in the wall space. I was lucky enough to catch up with a friend here while in NYC on a week long business trip from SF, and was really excited to see a great selection of West Coast oysters here in addition to the more standard East Coast & Canadian varieties. What really blew me away (not sure if it was a special) was their $25 lobster bake: A) good luck finding lobster in any city for under $40, and B) this was cooked spectacularly! Not rubbery from being overcooked, not swimming in water from being under-boiled; it was lobster perfection! Will definitely be back on my next trip to NYC.

Spring 2011 Tasting Menu What to go there for: the experience The first course is brought to the table. It is a fluke tartare shaped into a perfect circle dotted with fresh chives, juiced with splashes of citrus, and finish with a mint garnish. The fish is creamy, fatty counterbalanced by the bite and acidity of the chives and citrus. They don't overpower the tartare. The fish is still the main event. I can detect, ever so slightly, the freshness of the ocean waters permeating through the gossamer flesh. It's fresh. It's juicy. It's gone too quickly and I'm hungry for more. Next comes a carrot soup swirled with some lime yogurt garnished with some shaved baby carrots. Sweet spring carrots, the sour bite of lime, and the tartness of the yogurt come together in a marvelous harmony of balanced flavor under a smooth texture of puree'd soup. The shaved carrots add an additional texture of crunch. A hint of cumin makes a sudden appearance as the soup travels easily down the throat. The soup is warm and inviting and playful from the contrasting flavors. A long plate housing a trout fillet with a ciopollini onion and raspberry puree and pickled onions comes afterward. How could one imagine that trout and raspberry would pair well together? Apparently they do. Perfectly. If there ever was a zenith for umami it would be this. The warm bite of soft trout fillet; the pillowy softness of the puree; the sweet crunch of the pickled onions; a combination of sweet, salty, and savory literally melts in your mouth. The trout is cooked perfect - soft, buttery, rich, and moist in flavor. I can barely wait for the next bite but take time to savor this moment. Peace is further prolonged by another comforting dish: green garlic broth with rabbit dumplings. Cutting a dumpling in half and gathering some broth on my spoon I put it in my mouth. I am suddenly sitting in a warm sunny field overlooking the ocean on a summer afternoon in France, rabbit dumpling soup in hand. Usually comfort food takes you to places where you've been before; grandma's kitchen, picnic at a park, your favorite uncle's restaurant. This takes me to a totally unfamiliar place. And still it is comforting. The broth is light but rich in garlic and chicken flavor. The dumpling skins are not soggy but cooked at a perfect al dente. The meat is gamey but not pungent. I give my respect to the rabbit that gave its life for this moment. Comfort now has a new meaning. The final savory dish is a sirloin steak. The steak is perfectly cooked served with sweet potatoes, and spring squash. The steak is so soft that a fork will suffice in cutting them into bite sized pieces. The sauce is a light demiglace which isn't too heavy as though not a single drop of butter was used yet still rich in flavor. What could go wrong with meat and potatoes? This was exactly that; just at a heightened level. The meat is juicy, moist, made possible but soaking up the wonderful sauce. The potatoes, saturated by the sauce as well, go down like mashed potatoes. The squash brings a sense of completion by rounding out the flavors with its freshness and bitterness. By now my stomach has had its fill but there are two more desserts on their way. The first dessert is a tarragon meringue with orange sorbet. It is a palate cleanser; a precursor to the main explosion of sweet indulgence that is to come. The meringue is not sweet; it's refreshing. The freshness of the tarragon rids my mouth of any residue of steak, rabbit bits, or trout that would adulterate the flavors of sweetness. The coolness of the sorbet lightens my mouth and the citrus creates even more saliva. I am beginning to wonder if my taste buds have any more juice left after such explosive experiences of flavor. And now, the finale. It is like the final movement of Shostakovich's fourth symphony. Where do I get to the strength to muster through the finale after enduring hours of such intense yet joyous music? I suppose it is called a "finale" for a reason. I am presented with a banana chocolate cake with hazelnut crÃ¨me. It doesn't sound impressive. It doesn't even look stunning. A bark colored wedge of moist cake layered with hardened chocolate sauce accompanied by a small pool of hazelnuts covered lavishly with crÃ¨me. My fork slowly cuts through the tip of the cake. I gather a piece of hazelnut and dip the cake with a touch of crÃ¨me. My taste buds are invigorated suddenly with a new found energy. The rich chocolate and sweet crÃ¨me swirl together into the moist cake and suddenly there is an unexpected crunch as my teeth bite into the fragile banana brittle that is hidden between layers of guilty pleasure. There is final crunch of nutty sweetness thanks to the presence of hazelnut bits that were lingering in the side of my mouth. I close my eyes to try and understand why bananas, chocolate, and nuts go so well together. At this point, who cares? Who would have thought a simple chocolate banana cake could taste this goo

Is this place awesome or is it the greatest? Crepes are amazing as well as the pasta dishes and the salads I've had them all. The pissaladiere (yes I googled the spelling) is pretty good as well but they have anchovies on them which some people may not like. Of course if you're a wine lover you'll have wine with this but the Jenlain Ambre is Â a great beer that's a must try. Cash only but for an amazing not overly heavy meal this is worth it.

Typically i give a restaurant 4 stars because the food or the menu was simple or average. Â This is sort of the case. Â I ordered a salad a 'create your own' not so bad, right? Hum here's where it gets confusing, so i really only prefer a few ingredients in my salad and lets be honest here no ones eating a salad because it sounds better than REAL food. Â So, with that said I'm creating my own, the problem is i have to choose a million ingredients because i wont hit the minimum for delivery. Â So i'm thinking OMG i ordered a large and with all of this 'stuff' in it its going to be enormous and filling. Â NOT SO MUCH, why you ask, because theres a few pieces of each ingredient in a bowl that could be considered a very large small. Â  Â  I will order from here again and try something else, but I'm not one for ordering because its trendy lunch spot, i will order again because I've passed it and its clean. And yes its in walking distance and i still want delivery, thats why this is NY!

Had a lovely outing here. I'd kept passing here and peeking in. Reviews were great so we gave it a try. Glad we did! What a sweet place. About 18 seats total, a few small tables and the rest by the bar. Wines were great and they let me taste a few till I found what l liked. The food was good, and they've got a shelf full of games so we entertained ourselves playing Battleship till the food came. YAY!!! The most expensive thing on the menu was $20. Totally laid-back and unpretentious. Thumbs up!

As good as it gets. The bone marrow burger was a home run. The only thing more superious were the pork belly nacho's, which were probably the best nacho's ever had - ever. Pair with an Allagash White and you got yourself one hell of a meal. I would do weekly if it were in my geographic location.
All I have to say have to say is Wowwww .... Prime Rib!! Enough Said! Let the picture speak for itself

After all the great Yelp reviews thought it would be a good local place to take a friend from NJ. Unfortunately we didn't get much farther than the door as the two hostesses, who looked barely 21, were less than helpful, had to get their attention from their personal conversation to let them know we were interested in sitting at the bar for drinks. One seat available, we asked if one of the (many) free chairs at the table tops could be moved over to the not at all crowded bar area, to which they barely acknowledged me and said no without even looking. Aren't hostesses supposed to be hospitable? Not here. Too many great places in the area to waste giving this place another chance if that's how they treat potential customers.

Stopped in while visiting family in Brooklyn- so glad we did! Loved the comfortable atmosphere, laid-back and very homey. Dishes are served family-style & come to the table as they're ready, great for sharing. We enjoyed radishes with uni & shrimp butter, chili spiced Chinese long beans, delicious whole trout & egg noodles with duck sausage & bok choy. Menu changes daily with providers & produce sources provided. Â Will definitely be back next time we're in town!
Service at this place was superb! Make sure to try the cucumbers and spinach.

Had the chance to try the Michele pizza (prosciutto and mushrooms). Although it did taste like quality pizza, I didn't think there was anything really special about it. It was good but definitely not the best.
Best dumplings I've ever eaten in my life. The prices are unbelievably cheap too, especially for New York City. 4 dumplings for a buck, you can't beat that with a bat! Foamie approves.

Great place just off the main drag. Cool, classy interior with great food and good service. I think we got waited on by several waitresses, which was different, but the fact that they all wanted to see how we were doing was pretty nice. They had Abita on tap, which instantly makes them a winner in my book, and the Mac and Cheese was -- and I'm about to go punch myself in the face for saying this word -- decadent. Mostly cheese and a little mac; the way it should be at a bar. We all split an order of fries, which were alright on their own, but when combined with the spicy mayonnaise, are downright bangin'. Definitely coming back here the next time I'm in Astoria, maybe for late night.

The service in the dining area was VERY slow. Â I was not expecting fine dining - just a quick, casual meal - but this was exceptionally slow. Â Not surprisingly, the fastest part of the service was when it was time for the check...which included an auto-gratuity. The food itself was good with huge portions. Â After reading about the empanadas, we ordered a couple of different empanadas to try. Â They did not come with our meal, so we asked about them and were told, "Yes, they are almost ready." Â The empanadas never came, the waitstaff never even looked our direction for us to flag them down to ask again, and then they tried to charge us for the empanadas. I agree with some of the other reviews - stick to the take out counter if you decide to eat here.
Love this place for a fun post-show, late dinner and drinks with girlfriends. Such a fun vibe and an amazing wine selection. I definitely recommend it to others!

Came back to visit after Apartment 13 was transformed into this French bistro. It is a lovely space and plays French music on the speakers. If you like being in France in a bistro the atmosphere and food will not disappoint. The food and drinks are reasonably priced. Food is good if rich. A little too much effort at being French considering it's on Avenue C. Â Cocktails are ordinary. Don't come here for drinks unless you come for the wine. The outdoor seating on the first and second floors are wonderful settings on this late summer evening. Overall, this is NYC, this place tries too hard to be Parisian, it's not Â a NYC experience.

I thought it was pretty good here but alot of people beg to differ. Especially those who've had ramen in Japan. I still like it here but willing to try some other places. Maybe I wouldn't eat here again however. It was too loud and the wait was absurd.

Ahhh the famous Ippudo. After leaving immediately when the hostess told us it would be a three hour wait, my friends and I decided to try again. This time we walked by before it opened for dinner at 5:30. At 4:30 there were already a couple of people waiting outside the restaurant hoping to get their names down. My friend and I came back around 5:20 and there was already a substantial line...again this is just the line to PUT OUR NAMES DOWN. The line started outside and once inside, looped in front of the bar. This is insane. But tip - if you really want to try Ippudo without the multiple hour wait, come before it even opens! After getting our names down, I got a text from the restaurant telling me to download their app that'll inform me when our table was ready. I thought this was pretty neat! Because they said the wait would be an hour to an hour and a half we walked over to St. Marks Bookshop to kill time. A little more than an hour later I got a call that our table was ready! However, just a note - your whole party needs to physically be there before they seat you. So, actually we had to wait a few more minutes, but still, not too bad. We ordered the famous pork buns and I got the Akamura Modern ramen. The pork buns were great but Momofuku buns were SO MUCH BETTER than Â Ippudo buns. There was mayo in Ippudo's, which some people may like or not mind, but I am not a fan. Also the Momofuku buns were melt-in-your-mouth amazing - just the right amount of fattiness. The Ippudo buns were much drier and harder. Now onto the ramen, I thought the broth was excellent and very flavorful, and not overly salty which I've come across before. However, I do think it was a little overpriced as I've had just as good, if not better ramen back home in SF/the Bay Area (Ramen Dojo in San Mateo for example which is about ~$9 versus Ippudo's ~$15). I don't think I'd come back on my own since the wait for this place is INSANE, but maybe if I was accompanying a friend and showing them around. Still, Ippudo has great customer service and great food, it's just a bit pricey!

Ordered delivery from Ngam on a Sunday night. Â Something leaked a bit in da bag and while nothing was ruined, it was kind of gross. Â The delivery guy volunteered to replace the semi-ruined dish and actually followed through, which was pretty awesome. Â The 20% deal if you order through Seamless is great too.

The food and coffee were great. They make most of their baked goods on the premise. We had a blondie and it was crunchy around the edges and chewy in the middle. The reason why I gave it three stars is because the AC was not turned on high enough. Felt a bit like a greenhouse.

I give this place 5 stars for this reason: I can wholeheartedly say this is the best brunch I've ever eaten. Bold statement, I know, and I don't usually think of Latin cuisine when I think of breakfast - but take my word for it - this place serves up a satisfying brunchito. I ordered the crab cakes benedicto, and I don't think I spoke a word during our entire meal because I was mesmerized. The poached eggs, guacamole, and spicy crab cake all melted together into one creamy, hearty, spicy mess - but the most delicious mess you can imagine. And to top it off, chipotle hollandaise sauce. This sauce made this dish perfection, adding smoky undertones to the traditional breakfast sauce. As if this wasn't enough for the hungry bruncher, it came with a side of homefries - a mix of regular and SWEET POTATO homefries. These were crispy, flavorful, and went along perfectly with every bite of the crab cakes benedicto - try dipping the sweet potatoes into the chipotle hollandaise sauce and you'll be having cravings for weeks, I promise. The prix fixe menu is a sweet deal - 10.95 for your meal and either a bloody mary, mimosa, screwdriver or OJ and a coffee or tea. You really can't go wrong at that price - and the coffee here is delicious. Eclectic atmosphere and music means you'll be dancing out the door afterwards, exclaiming to your friends that your meal was so good. Try the huevos rancheros - one of my fellow diners had that and it looked equally amazing. It's my next victim, for sure.

Campania makes some really great food. Obviously their pizzas are the best, coal fired little pies with amazing and fresh ingredients. I would be happy with everything on the menu including their non-pizza items and they have some great apps, but I usually stick with the pizzas. The bar is really good too. I usually stick to beers which isn't a problem as they have a nice selection of draft and bottled beers. Large wine selection and the glasses are filled to the top, if you know what I mean. Anytime I have friends visiting and we want to go somewhere nice this is where I come. Probably the best pizza in the area.

Pizza for breakfast? Â  Sotto 13 has great brunch deals that comes at a prefix with drinks that you can make bottomless. Unfortunately Sotto 13 caps your morning drinkfest at 90 minutes but seems to be loosely enforced when it's your birthday. Came here for my big sis' bday, who wanted pizza for brunch and we came to the right place. Mushroom pizza with truffle oil and if you're missing breakfast too much then add an egg on top is delicious, especially to wash it down with your mimosa. Â  Don't care for pizza in the morning? The prefixes come with classic breakfast dishes. Â Get the bacon well done if you like it crispy. Â Lamb sausage was a bit too salty for me. Â Skirt steak and eggs over a bed of crispy hash browns was on point. Very family style brunch, works perfect for bday brunch because you'll look forward to the siesta after all those mimosas!

This place has been reviewed enough times for most folks to get a sense of what's going on. Â We are primarily interested in the cooking and presentation, and don't give a flying squirrel about atmosphere, patrons, etc. Â We could care less about the "beautiful people" that hang in the area. Â Having said that, we really enjoyed lunch! We had the Marinated Beets with goat cheese crema, radish, snap peas and sunflower as a first course. Â Pappardelle with bolognese ragu and Almond Crusted Halibut as main courses. Â Pasta is fatta in casa, and is very nice. Â The fish was cooked perfectly. Â For dessert, the pistachio cake with cherry rhubarb conserva, pistachio crema, rhubarb sorbetto. Â Each dish was perfectly executed in this chef's opinion, and we came away from the place extremely satisified with our selection of a lunch place from among the many good places in the area. Â Highly recommended!
A delicious variety of macaroons to choose from, each light outside and fluffy inside. Pistachio, Carmel, Pralines and Vanilla are great choices if your not sure what to try

meh, i have had better. Pizza was good nothing special, I prefered John's Pizzeria in time sq, as well Anthony's Pizza in garden city over this place. Â Maybe it was just over hyped to me and i was expecting THE BEST PIZZA in the universe at this place -__-. Overall it was nothing to write home about. Lastly service was not to good either, maybe the waitress was having a bad night. We ordered 3 diffrent types of pizza, Regular,Sausage, and Pepporoni which were all Avg. Maybe it will be better next time.

Very good overall (3.5 stars). Average Banchans. Broiled mackerel (great), Daegu tang (above average), Haemulpajeun (oily and dense with lacking of seafood but mostly flour...just terrible). Other dishes are authentic as most of Korean restaurants are.

I highly recommend this place! It's so warm and cozy and I love coming here for a nice romantic evening. The best part is you can BYOB! There is no uncorking fee. The food is really great and you can see the guy making your food and smell all the aromas of the kitchen. (good and bad, it gets a bit buttery sometimes and you can smell the steak being cooked for the table next to you). This is a small restaurant so make reservations. They have really amazing dessert. Really good date spot =)
I miss the days when Sanford's was a greasy spoon decked out in Golden Girl's pink. Â Way to pricy now.

Sakagura was my first japanese tapas dining experience. My boyfriend and I were able to get a same day reservation for 7:30pm on a Tuesday - which was a score considering this place can be packed. I had read about the hidden-ish entrance so I wasn't phased by the exterior of the building - but my boyfriend was pretty convinced I was leading him into a darkened basement to kill him. Once we got to Sakagura and saw the awesome atmosphere we were both really excited. I based our food picks off other Yelp reviews since we were both pretty unfamiliar with this type of food. We went with the steaks on hot stone, tuna sashimi, tofu salad, fried mushroom and taro, the fried chicken bits, chicken meatballs, and one of the fish dishes, and of course the creme brulee. Everything was so delicious! Service wasn't rushed, the dishes came out gradually so we sipped our sake and were able to really enjoy our meal. It was a very cozy date spot. May seem a little expensive but we were out of there under $140 for a full meal including sake and a few beers. I've since been back several times for lunch and while the food is still top notch (and they have good lunch specials), its definitely a little more hectic with the lunchtime traffic from all the local businesses.

5 stars for the incredible service, 3.5 stars for the food. Service: We arrived around 10:30 and got seated immediately. Our waitress was extremely friendly and attentive. Gave us water whenever we needed more water -- and fast. At the end when we were paying the bill, she was very accommodating to our need to split the bill. It was quite complicated but she seemed happy to help us no matter what. Gave her a big tip! Food: Just average. I got the frittata. The pesto sauce was pretty good but the eggs themselves seemed a little bland. My friends got the Huervo Rancheros -- it was quite a big plate. I got a taste of it and it was filled with flavor. We all finished our food and licked our plates clean. The appetizer we got was some crab thing. Don't get it -- totally not worth the money we paid. It was such a small amount and I could have eaten it in 2 bites, not to mention splitting it between 3 people. All in all, I would come back just for the amazing service we got :)

The Normandy duck breast were amazing! The whole grilled Porgy were amazing as well! Portions were just right. Six of us came, six of us left extremely full & happy :) Thank you for the complimentary mini-cupcakes.

This place is one of my favorite Italian places in NYC! I LOVE the pasta dishes and the prices absolutely can't be beat. My friend and I had pasta and wine for UNDER $30 total...not common here. Downside is, the place is a little tight once your seated and of the SEVERAL times I've tried to eat here, I've only managed to get a table a few. I've even tried to put my name in a return to a friend's apartment a block away but they wouldn't go for that. As much as I love it, be prepared for a wait.Additionally, it is cash only, which has caused a few people to hop up from the table and have to search out at ATM nearby.
The best ice cream with salted caramel sauce. In.The.World 'nuff said! 6 thumbs up from 3 in our family!!!!

I don't remember how many times I come here. It is in my top list. There was one time that my order might have got lost and I ended up waiting quite long for my food. But if I remove one star, that will be personal because I know that I still want to come here again and again.

I read an article on the New York Times recently that Cafe Cluny is one of the most popular restaurants, located in downtown Manhattan, that many powerful women go to for important corporate and networking intra-business lunches! They are up in line with ABC Kitchen! Unfortunately for me, I work in Midtown so making the trip to W12th doesn't seem logical, but I've frequented the place for weekend brunch dates. Even at 1030-11AM, there is a wait. You can easily leave your cell phone number with the hostess and she will call you once the table is ready. The restaurant tends to squeeze all their patrons in, so be ready to brush elbows with a handful of people. I find that there are lots of young families and couples dining at Cafe Cluny- they all exude the "naturally chic" and I love it! As for the food, I have yet to be disappointed. I would say that the price point is also very reasonable, considering the quality, cleanliness, and presentation of each dish. I am a sucker for their eggs benedict, homemade granola, and their grilled tuna burger- three dishes that are on rotate at the moment. And of course, their hash browns. What is a breakfast/brunch without hash browns!

I've been a patron of La Lanterna since my precocious high school days, back in the 90's before Greenwich Village became overrun by Starbucks and fast food establishments. Â Honestly, the place hasn't changed much since then, from the dark interior to the efficient hustle of the waitstaff. Â Oddly enough, I don't feel like the prices have changed much over the past 15 years, either. The back patio is a nice option on warm days, though in the winter I find myself drawn indoors to the fireplace. Â If you're looking for a cafe that's whisper quiet and secluded, La Lanterna's not your place. Â But if you're looking for a lively cafe that's still cozy and quintessentially European, you'd be hard-pressed to find a better choice than La Lanterna.

This is a dumbed-down Americanized version of the great Vietnamese sandwich. Â I had "Da B:" -- bread was more like an American bun than a crispy rice four Baguette -- ground pork was rather tasteless. (Ground pork on bahn mi? Â Never saw that in a real Vietnamese place) -- carrot slaw was nice and tangy but the huge amount overpowered the sandwich -- I requested spicy but it came completely bland with a container of hot sauce on the side. -- Bottom line: over stuffed sandwich; underwhelming flavor. Vegetarian spring rolls were insipid and tasteless unless dunked in the peanut sauce. Â Side salad was pleasant - huge portion for the price. Delivery service was prompt and friendly as others reported, but this didn't make up for the mediocre sandwich. Â Find a Vietnamese neighborhood or try one of these places: Â newyork.seriouseats.com/â€¦.

the original, the best, the platonic ideal of a falafel place. the falafels are great, the shwarma is great, the kofta kabob is great, the hot sauce in GREAT. why they actually took seats out is beyond me, but Â they did. good cardemom tea, decent desserts., and CHEAP prices. i've been eating here over 30 years, and can't imagine stopping any time soon.

ok, i am a kid, i Know i am not supposed to write reviews on the best restaurant in the world. let me just say i had the best cheeseburger in the world at the little owl. perfectly cooked classic burger bun 2 or 3 slices of firm juicy mouth watering bacon 1 or 2 slices of melted american cheese one blessed cow. 1 more perfect bun i went there for my graduation dinner and it was way more than i expected. my family heard that some critics said that the Little Owl was the best burger in the world but and i TOTALLY agree. i cant comment about the alcohol but the iced tea was great. the service was more than i can ask for my sis wanted tomato juice and the waitress said she might have it in the Â basement and she went in to the basement and got it. the location was perfect. there was not a lot of cars beeping (in fact there was none at all) It was quite busy but not loud. Tip: make a reservation next i will try the pork cops me and my dad are trying to recreate the burger but i don't think we will come close. the desert was great
Everything was fantastic from start to finish. Get the spaghetti. Sounds so basic but was simply amazing. Reservations are a must.
Truly lovely people, atmosphere, and thankfully (!!) comforting, delicious food. Best of luck - looking forward to stopping in for a home cooked meal again soon.
I have one word for this place - disgusting. The meat that I ordered looked like somebody chewed it and threw up. Gross. NEVER going back!

I came here a while ago with my family. The food was decent, but not exceptional. Today, I returned because my first two restaurant choices were unable to accommodate us. Bad choice. The tall, thin guy at the first door should work in a stockroom somewhere so he doesn't have to interact with human beings. He was rude and snotty from the moment my sister and I walked in. He told me that I and my 11 year old sister would have to wait in separate lines. She's tall, so I assumed he mistook her for someone older, so I told him she was a child and I was uncomfortable separating. He said in a very snobby tone, "You're missing the point! One of you has to stay here and the other has to go to the other area to make room for others." Partially from the asinine rule, but mostly because of his incredibly offensive attitude, I decided to leave and find another restaurant. As I left, I heard him (as I'm sure he intended) tell the other host, "She doesn't understand; let her go." Â I am so put off and will never return to a place where I can expect to be insulted before I even step out of the foyer.
Ippudo I love you! But you have to stop with the shouting...

What can I say about Lucali that hasn't already been said? 225+ reviews and 4.5 stars? Well-deserved for sure. Everything about my experience here was great. Here's why: - 1.5 hour wait turned out to be only about 30-40 minutes. - It's tucked away in a nice and quiet little neighborhood in Brooklyn. - Ambiance, ambiance, ambiance. The decor of the restaurant is adorable and it's got this rustic, authentic Italian charm. - You can watch them make the pizza right in front of you (refer to pictures), so you KNOW exactly what's going on in the kitchen. - I haven't ever tasted authentic Italian pizza (I will this summer though!), but I think that Lucali's would come pretty darn close. - All the servers are pretty females (I know, I'm a girl but hey, I'm allowed to admire my own species)! - BOTH the pizza AND calzone were sooo good. I really don't think you can go wrong with either one and I like that their menu is simple (those are the only 2 items on the menu, though you can personalize it by adding toppings). Neither were too heavy or overbearing! (That's saying a lot, especially because we're talking about pizza and carbs here.) Overall, I would DEFINITELY go back and might even consider venturing all the way to Brooklyn just to eat here again. LOVE, LOVE, LOVE! OH, and... In my humble opinion, Lucali TRUMPS Grimaldi's. (Grimaldi's is good, but not THAT good... no ambiance whatsoever and the line is just waaay too long!)

Came here for some late night drinks with friend & co. during a quick trip to the city over the weekend. We sat out in their little sidewalk patio area, talking, laughing, and grooving to their awesome playlist. Can't comment on the food since we didn't order any so the stars are purely for the chill atmosphere, the great music selection, and the friendly service (thanks to Eugene with his Irish accent and impeccable sense of humor). Oh, and an additional star for creating the opportunity to randomly poll the strangers who were taking a smoke break on the sidewalk and who overheard our intense debate regarding the percentages of men and women who watch porn and whether that is a moral or immoral thing to do and who came over to us on their way into the bar and simply said, "You can ask it." For the record, their (paraphrased and simplified) responses were: Man: I watch it and think it is immoral (referred to TED talk). Woman: I watch it and y'all should keep on doing it. Our patio seating also gave us front row seats to an intense drama unfolding on the sidewalk between a woman and her male companion with whom she was clearly unimpressed while her friends looked on with detachment like BeyoncÃ© did in the elevator. I mean, don't you just love people watching especially when it comes to New Yorkers?

4 stars for the pork buns, 3.5 stars for the ramen. We came here on a rainy Saturday about 10 minutes after opening and only had to wait about 5 minutes to be seated. Â I'm not a huge ramen fan, but have had my fair-share of good ramen in California/the Bay Area/Socal. Â I agree that this place may be over hyped, but their pork buns are delicious. Â The soft bun, combined with the flavor packed (and not too fatty) pork and spicy mayo was amazing! Â Definitely order the pork buns!!! I had the Akamaru Ramen. Â The tonkotsu broth combined with the garlic oil was very tasty; however, I prefer my ramen noodles to be thicker. Â These noodles did not have much of a bite to them and were not chewy at all. Â Overall, I enjoyed my meal, but would not go out of my way to return.

Two times in a row I've ordered from here and it's been a disaster. The first time I was sent the wrong salad, and no sauce for my sides. The second time it took over and hour and I got no dressing for my salad..not to mention they weren't very kind when I called asking for them to deliver dressing, and it took another 30 mins. Terrible service.
Not quite French. Â Offers consistent, delicious food. Â Attentive and friendly staff. Â Good wines. Â Cozy atmosphere.

I love this place. Â Cash only, no reservations, whole pies only. Â You might wait an hour but it will make it all the better. Â Plus- you knew what you were getting into. Â Make sure at least one pie you order is plain with fresh garlic (free!). Â Don't let your friends bully you into getting all toppings. Â Although they are delicious, everyone ends up stealing my plain in the end. Â Simplicity and perfection. Â Best ingredients, thin crust. Â I always come here for special guests. Â  No desserts on the menu, so go across the street to Rice to Riches or Pinkberry.

I really felt like the evening was a complete waste of money. I went to Degustation for my 33rd birthday celebration with my husband and 3 foodie friends. Â We planned on doing the $80 tasting menu; which is advertised as 7 courses. Â I chose Degustation for their innovative looking menu and the chance to sit around an intimate open kitchen. Â The restaurant itself is lovely and the wait staff was incredibly attentive. Â The food was interesting and tasty; however when our 7 courses were over we all went out for pizza because we were still quite hungry. Â I have done many tasting menus before and have always felt I had eaten a meal when it was over. Â Last night was incredibly disappointing as I felt each course was literally a bite or two and we left feeling as we had just eaten an appetizer. Â There was no energy in the open kitchen that made it worth having an open kitchen, some of the chefs looked angry and unhappy to be cooking which made watching them uncomfortable and not interesting.

Quick tasty pizza slices near Times Square. I only had time for a quick bite before my show on one of my last trips to NY, so asked the folks at the ticket booth where to go, and they recommended this place. It was just a couple blocks off Times Square, quick, and very tasty pizza - crispy thin crust, tasty sauce, fresh toppings (I did the tomato, basil garlic one) - $4/slice. Definitely recommend.

I am 100 % Italian, and trust me..no one knows TRUE Italian cooking like I do. Raised by an Italian Nana, Lidia served me proud in hiring a great executive chef to offer a menu that can really make your taste buds sing! The decor is close and cozy, not intimidating at all. Ordering was easy as everything on the menu was enticing! I opted for the Sinfonia de Pasta..an excellent choice for pasta lovers that desire a few variations in one sitting. Â The pasta is served "all you can eat." When I went 2 weekends ago, I was served 1.) Linguine with Pesto and green beans, on which the Pesto was not overpowering or overly seasoned..it was perfect and light. 2.) Penne with a creamy red/orange sauce and basil..my favorite...it melted in my mouth. 3.) Mushroom stuffed ravioli...not too heavy and a great little bite. Other dishes that were ordered that evening: Wine Short Ribs marinated for 24 hours in wine and served with kale and gnocci and the lemon chicken..great portions and flavors! For dessert, the four of us each ordered something different 1.) Poached peaches with ricotta - peaches were poached in an Appiana dessert wine and were absolutely divine with the sweet ricotta. 2.) Apple strudel with almonds - amazing 3.) Vanilla, no egg Panna Cotta - AMAZINGLY smooth and light, a really different and delicicous choice 4.) Chocolate Zabaglione Mousse Cake - ( my choice) great chocolate, light, a nice hint with dark cherry sauce. Definitely choose Becco for dinner when in NY!!!

this is a great place! everyone should eat here! the wait was long the first time we came here and we were really hungry so we left and went to some other pizza place. then we went again like a day later and this time we stuck around. we waited about 1 hour. the inside is big and really nice. the waiters were ok. the pizza was great. the best i have ever had. a lot of people and a lot of waiting but its a definite place to go to!
Tried the lobster cannelloni and it was good. Only issue was that space was a little right. Looking to try the meatballs next time.

I was excited to try this place out after reading all the great reviews. Solid food but nothing impressive. I do not find the empanadas that everyone is raving about to be so amazing. I ordered the Chicken Mofongo and got pork instead... Same thing happenned with the empanadas. So make sure your order is taken correctly. I also had the Bacalao Fritters as an appetizer and I do not recommend getting it. It's two tiny, VERY dry fritters. Not very appetizing. My boyfriend is Dominican, so he knows his cuisine. Neither one of us is looking forward to coming back. Again, the food isn't bad but isn't great either.

Just got a late dinner. Excellent cocktails! pork dumplings were fantastic. Got a pizza and some Mac and cheese to split with my wife. Very tasty. Finished off with Ice cream and flour less chocolate cake. Very chill with the projected screens showing old tv shows. Quiet at around 10pm on a Sunday. Very relaxing.

Abundance of free alcohol! No, not buy one, then bottomless... Just free booze with meal! Choose from a list of about 12-15 large drinks!! One of my favorite places in the city! Perfect, lively, FUN atmosphere filled with big tables of friends. But without the music so loud you can barely hear your friend sitting next to you. Also-- the food is reasonably priced ($12-$14) and is actually delicious Latin dishes!

this place is pretty cool and unique in the City. Â the place is huge and contains everything you can imagine to make a fine italian cuisine: Â amazing pasta, cheeses, meats, etc. there's also several seating stations that function as mini-restaurants. Â i did not try the famed fresh gelato but did grab a sandwich. Â service was rude but eh what do you expect. Â the sandwhich was overpriced at nearly $12 for a small baguette but it was tasty. Â probably would not return but definitely worth checking out once

Loved this place. Â 1) BYOB 2) Great food. Â We got the mushroom cigars and each of us got our own dish - steak and fries, tuscan chicken, some lamb dish, and ahi tuna. Â Absoultely delicious, especially the lam dish. Â 3) they take reservations even though the place a hole-in-the wall, 4) the waiter/hostess (place is small enough to have just one) is really friendly and very good with recommendations. Â I am definitely going back there.

If i lived in NYC, I'd be able to try out their entire menu but alas, I live 3,000 miles away on the opposite side of the country (for now, I may be heading east in a couple of months!). I've only been here a few times but they make one of the best tofu scrambles I've ever had. The pancake slam is my favorite so far. Their sautÃ©ed kale could use some work but the salad makes an excellent substitution for that. I've only been to Champs back when they were on Ainslie St so I can't comment on the decor of the new location but I'm sure it's cute as hell.

Came here with two friends and it was fantastic. We started with gaucamole and it was outstanding. Also, it was a HUGE portion - they don't stint on guac here! I got the fish taco and the mushroom cornmeal quesadilla. The taco was delicious but the quesadilla blew my mind. It was almost like a taco in shape - they stuffed a crispy cornmeal tortilla with cheesy mushrooms and folded it up like a taco. The margaritas were perfect, the staff were exceptionally friendly, and decor was fantastic. The only thing I didn't like was the volume of the music - turn it down so I can talk to the person who's sitting 6 inches from me without screaming! But I guess that's just trendy NYC for you. The food makes it worth it.
The best veggie burger in town hands down. The service is great and the food is always good. The wait can be long, especially in the winter.

A friend and I ate at Pure Thai last night. It was my 2nd time there and it's one of the better Thai food restaurants I've eaten at, and I eat alot of thai. It's decor is uniquely Thai/ eastern asia, resembling a side of the road, dive, cookhouse but with charm and character. We waited for about an hour on a busy Saturday night but sat at a bar next door waiting for our table (the restaurant only seats about 20). Upon being seated, we Promptly ordered our meal. Starters came out 10 minutes later. We started with the veggie spring roles and curry puffs. Very basic dishes at most Thai spots, these were spot on and the home made sweet and sour dipping sauce for the curry puffs was a great touch. Our entrees came 10 minutes later and were piping hot. I ordered the pork and crab dry noodle ($12). Very much like a ramen dish without the broth it was very tasty with large pieces of pork and perfectly cooked noodles. Only complaint is the lack of crab meat, it was very small pieces of crab. My friend ordered the pepper beef ($12) dish medium spicey. This dish was very good too, although couldve consisted of more large pieces of beef and less large cuts of green peppers to fill the plate. Aside from the long wait, the food is well worth the price and the atmosphere and ambience/ authenticity is a welcomed change from all the typical Thai spots in manhattan.

A little torn. If it was brunch I'd do 4 stars, dinner 1 or 2. Brunch is great, partially because its the only solid eggs Benedict / Norwegian around, partly because they nail it. Good cocktails, nice backyard. Dinner- barely stewed items in the beef bourguignon (have had it twice). Tried the lobster special which was described as lobster meat over asparagus and pearl onions. The serving was super small- now, I get it, it's lobster- but it was over one sprig of asparagus cut up and one pearl onion. If they'd at least made it a solid stew packed w veggies it would have felt worth it. And for what 90 cents more of veggies? Â Just an indicator of how all of dinner is just kinda off point. Again, go for brunch but pass on dinner. Esp w other good options so close (try all the sides at Dear Bushwick!)

Let me just say the food was very good, the bar for this type of fair is drastically lower in this region of the us, but let's just say they're one if the best of what you can get from hipsters cooking "traditional southern comfort cuisine" but the service rivals none in the I'm too cool to give a shit about my tables, once the guy took my order he never came back, it took ten minutes to get a glass of milk, upon finishing my meal I wanted a piece of pie (PIES and thighs) after another substantial wait I finally make contact with the waiter, he gives me a menu and poof he's gone again, mind you this is not a weekend brunch, Â this is a weekday. After another long wait period I said fucking it, I'll just order from the counter, the girls says to me "just a minute let me just finish this up." She was rearranging doughnuts, Â the phone rang and she answered I walked away, Â as soon as I get back to my table the server appears, Â "would you like a piece of pie to go?" No! I still tipped well above 20 percent because I could see the bus ser working hard and to punish him because the server is worthless would not be fair.
Old reliable - certainly not your first choice, but when it's this late at night, you take what you can get.

Meh, the deserts were not the greatest the pistachio canoli was ok, but not quite as good as a restaurant here in florida makes them. Just ok.. the bread with vegetables and herbs was quite good though. 3*
Consistently delicious, Â not to mention cheap and fast. Huge fan!
Great food, decent prices, and very gregarious staff! If you like French food this is the place to go!

We celebrated our anniversary here and will not soon forget the special night that we had at Bouley. From the beginning while we waited for our table until dessert, they were attentive and knew that this was a special night for us. THe food was spectacular and the wines picked by our sommelier were a perfect match. we will return soon and hope that our friends will too, this is a very special place, top of the top!

I decided to stop by Xe May today after walking around the neighborhood. Although the space is small, the sandwich shop definitely has a very homey and warm feel to it. The owners are also super nice! Since I get classic viet sandwiches all the time from other places, I decided to go with something different. I asked the owners what they recommend and they told me the lam'bretta had been getting great reviews. So without hesitation, I got the lam'bretta. The sandwich itself smells AH-MAY-ZINGG!! It was soooo good. The flavors were strong, but definitely not overpowering. You can still taste the daikon, cucumbers, and cilantro (i mean.. what is a bahn mi without that?!) I also decided to get a drink too, and instead of getting a usual viet iced coffee, the Fresh Basil Soda Limeade caught my eye and I ordered that instead. It was extremely refreshing, and had the right touch of sweetness and 'tangyness" (and also.. having a drink with a fresh slice of lemon and basil leaf makes it feel like you're drinking something healthy haha). I would definitely recommend this drink as opposed to getting a can soda. I cannot wait to come back here and try other sandwiches!

If you don't already know about Joe's Shanghai soup dumplings, crawl out of your cave and go get some. And please bring me a dozen. The only thing i have to add is that, lately for me, an order of soup dumplings is not complete without the PEA SHOOTS. Sometimes they're not on the menu and I think they cost as much as an order of soup dumplings, but totally worth it. Â YUM.

Today was my first time at SoCo and i must say I had a 5 star experience.The place had a nice decor. Our waiter was the sweetest young lady. The chicken and waffles were DELICIOUS ! The chicken was extra juicy and waffle was soft a fluffy. My boyfriend and I went in for just a quick brunch but felt so comfortable that we ended out trying almost every alcoholic beverage on the menu LOL. Oh and the macaroni was to die for !!!!! We will be back soon. When you check-in on yelp you get 10% off your meal and re waiter didn't hesitate to give us our discount. Overall it was great.

I have to admit I'm really not a fan of the idea of Japanese barbecue. You pay a pretty extravagant price to cook your own food (which you have to focus on or risk burning it), which is more easily made at home. I am pleased to report Gyu-Kaku has proved me utterly wrong. Super Bowl Sunday resulted in a full day of happy hour prices with frankly unbelievable value. The meat itself is also unparalleled: Gyu-Kaku provides you with sauces in which you can dip cooked meat, but it's frankly unnecessary. I have no idea how they've done it, but their meats are prepared in ridiculously delicious ways. I could gobble all of them up without anything added. I think the menu is a bit daunting to a first-time visitor, but the staff are knowledgeable and informative. I'm sure more visits will also improve my selection of meats, and I look forward to my return. Completely unrelated to the review of the restaurant, I have to admit I am not at all a fan of the survey they give out at the end of the meal. If I were being honest, I would've marked no for the overwhelming majority of responses, but none of those reflect on my server negatively (while I imagine management thinks do).

Hey! don't read reviews bellow 4 starts - not worth your time ;) I have lived in Billyburg for about 5 years - i come to this place religiously - diner, brunch, you name it - food is always awesome. they have great steaks, sangria chicken, deserts, coffee is good too - sauces are awesome... just go! their newer, sister restaurant Rosarito Fish Shack is also good and has an great atmosphere. ;)

This place is amazing! I visit AGO in LA often DeNiro also owns it. You can not go wrong with anything here. I had the special spaghetti noodles, browned butter and shaved truffles! It was fabulous! We started out with the warm ricotta and ended with nectarine and buttermilk gelato Highly recommend this place

Thankful to live & work by Little Owl. Â While after many years of burger lunches, skate & pork chop dinners I am no longer ever 'wowed' I am also never disappointed, which means a lot. Â Service always feels like my buddy is just pouring me a glass of vino so I can relax on a quiet afternoon with sun drenching & warming a little neighborhood spot. Â  While the sliders & burger is go-to lunch order for 90% of patrons, be a rebel - have clam strips + lamb sandwich, leave smiling.

I went there on a week day rather early to avoid the wait. Everything I had to eat was on point. I love that it's a place that specializes in vegan and meat items. Seems like a great place to take a group where one person has a food allergy and the other person is an avid meat eater. You will leave stuffed and very happy. Service was pretty good too. If you're in park slope and craving a little Latin flavor, go here.

I love the food here. Â I like that it doesn't follow all the rules of barbecue. Â I get sick of overhearing people in line bitch about how they don't have mac n cheese (I think they do now) or how the potato salad isn't drowned in mayonaise. Â  It's a German name, folks, maybe that should tip you off that it's a little different than your standard barbecue. Â I don't care if you're from South Carolina, or Memphis, or Texas, or wherever the "best" barbecue is from. Â This is its own thing, and it's great. The pulled pork is the best value. Â It costs less per pound, and there are no bones adding to the weight. Â It's amazing. Â I once yearned for different sauces, but now I love the ones they have, combined or on their own. Â You get nice potato rolls and can make mini sandwiches with different combinations. Â The ribs, while a little pricier, are also delicious. Â I'm kind of like a kid in a candy store at FS. Â I'm so tempted by all the options. Â I often go for some pulled pork, a few pieces of brisket, a sausage, some potato salad, and pickles. Â If I'm extra hungry, or it's more than just me and my girlfriend eating, I'll go for the baked beans, which are delicious and have bonus meat in them. Â Sometimes I'll get a few pieces of pork belly. Â So rich! Â They've also got that new fangled home-fermented saurkraut. Â Tasty. Â And healthy, I hear. No problems with the food, really. Â I think they need a different system for ordering. Â They have huge communal tables made of wood so thick that some of the table legs take up seating. Â You'll see what I mean.
