Â Also, it's really tricky to negotiate waiting in line, ordering food, and then finding somewhere to sit. Â What if, after waiting in line for 30 minutes (which is common) you can't get a seat? Â Well, I usually let my girlfriend sit and hold the seats while I wait in line, but people can get pissed off at this, especially if they just got their food. Â The system is store-like in that you order by the pound at Â a counter. Â Sort of like going to a butcher. Â I think that's the concept they're going for. Â Fine. Â But there's only one guy cutting and weighing the meat. Â If you're into american whisky, they have a huge selection, including some very obscure ones. Â They also have a great selection of micro brews, but honestly, I'd like a lighter beer to go with my heavy meats. Â A PBR, Highlife, or Bud would go great with this food. Â Sixpoint's Righteous Rye, while stellar, is just too thick in this context.

They have awesome empanadas. The spinach corn ones were amazing. The guacamole was smooth and flavorful. Try the fish tacos. They were tasty and the cabbage added a nice crunch when you bite into it. They made a mate iced tea for me as a pick me up. It was delicious with a hint of mint and ginger. If you're wondering about this place, don't. Just go! At the end of our meal we go Argentinian cookies which were to die for!

The biggest problem is their seating process. They arbitrarily make you wait up to 45 minutes or more. The food is ok but certainly not worth waiting 45 minutes for. Even with a reservation they will make you wait up to 15 minutes. What's more there is no waiting or reception area so people bunch up at the entrance and the stairs. It becomes elbow room chaos. The overall dining experience does not produce enough value for prices charged yet they keep raising their prices every year. All in all not reflective of Â the type of restaurant they are trying to be -- high end New American. Service can be good or bad depending on your luck. Same goes for the dishes, sometimes care is taken. Other times they're somewhat sloppily assembled, going by their own standards. Most of the servers are professional but some are a little bit dizzy and inexperienced and the rest fake it till they make it. The ambience is slick with live jazz some nights. The sushi is pretty good. The steak is mickey mouse, go to a proper steakhouse instead. The burger is decent but also overpriced. You can most definitely get the same or better quality burger at more than several similar places in the city at a lower price than what Hillstone charging.

From a bike ride along the Belt parkway/Staten Island bridge on a nice Saturday, the girl and I weren't ready to pack up and go home. We were HUNGRY!! There were a few dudes fishing by the bay, and we weren't about to eat Sushi around here, thanks. We are in BROOKLYN! We have to have some Pizza! Am I right!?!?! Yes, I am. We have gone to Franny's, Difara, but.. We wanted a place closer to where we were and asked a few Brooklyn rezzies... One guy said Lenny's, then another heavy set guy interrupts, "Ey, ho.Wddya born yesterday, hah? L&Bs on 86th, now THAT's a Pizza! Lenny's... D'afugouttaheya~!" . The first guy reluctantly concurred and I asked the heavy set authority of Pizza for the directions. "It's far from here, but worth it. It's on 86th after all them Chinese markets and where the train ends.. They gotta sign that says Spumonis. 86street.".. Sir, we aren't from around here, but thanks for the super-local directions. We thanked the semi-scary man and got on Yelp for more juicy details and, more importantly- directions. From where we were, yes. It was quite a bike ride, and realized... They HAVE a parking lot( When do you EVER have a parking lot around NYC!?!?!) My GF, clearly a bit tired from the long/dangerous bike trip AND Hungry as all hell cursed out, "Oh goddamn it! We coulda drived here!!!" Knowing she gets a bit... lethal when she is starving, I diverted her attention to the happy groups of people; families, couples, buddies,... entire group of Automechanics... They were all enjoying this... Square pizza... ?.. Not a NY thin slice? Both of us have never tried a square pizza before. No. wait I have. In highschool, when that disgruntled lunch lady used to flop that half cooked, pale squares with dehydrated red sauce and goverment cheese on it.. Yeah. Now that sucked!. My heart sunk a bit, from my childhood trauma. I sure hope that Big guy is right... But then again, the outside seating area is PACKED and they all seem extremely happy. This place can't be that bad.. Can it? We got in line, trying to see the process of ordering. The two guys by the kitchen window basically nods to you, when they are ready to take your order. You state a single slice, or a box. A regular, or the pie. We decided to get one of each. Â Sitting down among Local Â Brooklynians, we stare at these two rather plain pieces of Pizza. GF went for the square first, while I got the semi-thin crust. "..OMG..Oh..My GoD!!!".. !!!!! Are you choking dear? Are you alright!? .. "This is rediculous!". Before I could even try a bite, my thoughtful one ate most of it. Her eyes are telling me to go get more. Hey, I haven't even tried my semi-thin slice yet, damn it. .. But since I am P-whipped, I get back on line. I got two single squares this time- fresh out of the oven. Nice! I notice that my slice of pizza is no longer a 'triangle', but more or less a trapezoid with bite marks. " The slice is ok, nothing special".. Gee, thanks for the spoiler alert, dear! Now onto the Squares. I already have seen Â everyone around me devour this thing... My significant other also swoons about it.. I am the only one that hasn't converted to this idea of a great tasting, thick square pizza. I bite into it, thinking I will get that same sad disappointment hit my palate- just like long ago when I had those horrible Highschool cafeteria squares. I could just imagine in my mind that big guy that told us about this place bragging to his friends at a 'social club'- "Oh get this. I sent these outtatownahs for pizza today to L&Bs..Hahahaha". Then something happens. Holy mother of god, what is this!? This is seriously good. The dough is crunchy on the bottom, almost like a mochi-foccaccia center. The sauce is sweet, and yet tangy- a perfect marriage to the loads of Mozz that have melted into the dough. My GF looks at me, "Ya see!?!? Ya see now!?!?!" . Yes. I have convereted too. This IS friggn' good. Pizza does not have to be a particular shape or form to be excellent. .. Hey, that would be pizza profiling, or something. But yeah. This is fantastic. How does it compare to other NY institutions? Hard to say. It's like comparing Le Bernardin to Sik Gaek. Ippudo to Zuzu. A Cassoulet that a French Momma made to Meatballs in Sunday Gravy that a Italian grandma made... All great, but just can't compare them the same way. Before we left, we decided to try out the hero sandwiches as well to go. Got the chicken with tons of mozz, balsamic vinegar, sundried tomatoes and olive oil. Absolutely sick! We also got the sausage and pepper one too. That was also a homerun. Seriously, do these guys know how to dish out great food or what!?!? The bikeride back to where we left our car was slow and painful. We were so stuffed! Now if only they had a Hammock somewhere..... hey lets ask that big scary guy again...
Never disappointed. Â Paulie is so friendly - he looks like the offspring of Directors Scorcese and Allen. Â Mostly the pizzas are fantastic - Greenpointer, Hell Boy highly recommended.

This little hole in the wall was pretty good when I went a couple of weeks ago. Â The food was really good...I recommend the softshell crab, bonito sashimi and the okonomiyaki. Â I would've given this place a 4 except the extremely long wait really irritated me. Â What was more frustrating was that when we got there the host told us that it would be a 1 hr wait. Â We ended up waitng more than 2 hrs. Â When we finally sat down and ate, I must admit that the food was very good...not worth the wait but still very tasty. Â This place is also very cheap so if you like good cheap eats and don't mind waiting an eternity then this is the place for you.

Seriously impressed. It's very rare that you experience a totally new culinary experience. Definitely one of my top 3 restaurants in NYC! I love the fractured dining room - it makes for a very intriguing layout, a surprise on every corner and a great combination of elegant and hunting lodge. I really like the cocktail menu (The Bramble is yummy), and neither the artichoke dip nor the devils on horseback can be ignored. Food was really good. Barkeeps with quiet, stylish flair. Guys who know their shit but don't flaunt it. Great for lunch/brunch/dinner and for large groups. Â They take reservations for brunch for parties greater than 6.

I had two friends in from out of town. Â One lives on the west coast and one on the east coast. Â They absolutely loved the dining experience at Pylos. Â I would recommend all of the items that we ordered. Â  Appetizers: salmon cakes with fresh herbs and olive oil, served with greek-yogurt skordalia and kolokythakia kai melitzanakia tyganita!!!! Main Dishes: brizola and the lavraki me tsigarellia were to die for!!! Of course they had a bottle of wine. Â The prices are so reasonable, the decor was awesome and the staff catered to us well!!!
Nice food and dishwares. Very good service.

Went back any everything was perfect again. Â My reference to the location was simply because I live in Nolita next to bowery, so I can't take the subway and it's about a 20 min. walk. Â However, I would walk much further than that for this restaurant. Â Favorite in NY :).

My daughter and her boyfriend are big fans of Lidia since they have been to her pricey restaurants. Becco has made me a big fan of Lidia and I am going to this restaurant whenever I am in town. The bread, bread sticks, olives, & white bean dip for starters where just to difficult to stay away from. For entree, I had the sliced steak sprinkled with shredded horseradish and served on roasted root vegetables and buckwheat polenta. The chef would not even hear it if your order is other than rare or medium rare.... Chef's right the steak melts in your mouth. That dish would always linger in my buds. Dessert was zabaglione with fresh berries but since I am a big fan of panna cottas, I wished I ordered that instead. I still finished the zabaglione though by myself! Oh... don't forget about the great staff! Only one of few places I've been where the moment you turn your head one of the staff will be there for you. And they are very knowledgeable of what they serve, & warm & friendly! I'm very glad I agreed with my daughter to go for Becco. Too bad though, we were so stuffed that we dropped going to see the movie "Julie & Julia" and headed back to our hotel.

Four star rating is quite high in my book but they completely deserve it. This small and low key looking place is a trip out of New York and straight to Caracas. I love everything about the place - the nice and easy going staff, down to earth and simple cafe decor, the $3 sangria, the wonderful hot sauce and obviously the amazing arepas. There are varieties of arepas with the same main ingredient - i.e. multiple types of chicken, beef, pork and cheese arepas. Â  So far, we tried some chicken, tuna, shrimp, cheese and vegetarian ones and they are all just really satisfying. Great food with no pretension. Much better than most of their counterparts from Manhattan - at least the ones I know. Drinks are good too. I really liked the sangria that had some orange slices in it. They also have good milkshakes. I want to try all the other arepas. I have not tried the beef, pork and baby shark arepas yet. I am not sure about baby shark since I am concerned about their population in the wild but I'll definitely try everything else. I never had a complaint about my visits there, was always satisfied and I look forward to going back for years to come.
Yakitori...Tori...Tori...

Went to Becco last night, this is my second time there, went back because the first time the food was exceptional. Â The waiter seemed perturbed to serve you, one of our appetizers was the fried mozzarella carrozza. Â This was definitely not home made. Looked and tasted like something packaged and heated up. Â Presentation was horrible and the pasta dishes had no flavor...

I'm in love with this place. Â  Great spot to grab app and drinks with friends. Â Or have dinner and catch up. The decor is amazing and fun. Â The food is probably some of the best Thai I have had in the area. I am super picky about my papaya salad because my mom makes it from scratch. Â But this is some seriously good papaya salad with a spicy twist... trust me I have had some bad salad at some other "thai" palaces ones) and spicy basil noodles with imitation duck is fabulous!!! Tip: I tried their take out not as amazing.. go there

WHAT HAPPENED CALLE OCHO??? Broke my heart! I've loved this place from way back when too. Last Sunday I came for a dinner in the new location for the first time(now hidden inisde the Excelsior Hotel). I went with 3 of my friends because we all had a pleasant experience earlier in April at the old location (even with a snippy waiter). So we sat and had our drink orders taken, and was given a good sized tray of pan de bono (i love) while we perused the menu. We had decided rather quickly and had looked around to signal to our waiter but he had some serious blinders on. Even other waiters didn't manage to notice us waving our arm in the air, or our "excuse me"'s. Finally, after about 20 minutes we managed to flag him down as he was heading in another direction, and he explained to us really slowly (I'm sorry was this snack time at nursery school???) that he was going to put something down and then come back to take our order. So he came back, and took our order as promised. We ordered a lobster ceviche, calamari appetizer, an arepa appetizer, and 3 entrees for 4 ppl to split. WE WAITED AN HOUR BEFORE ANYTHING SHOWED UP. We were ready to complain but we were afraid of the possibility of the staff messing with our food, (NO 'TUDE BEFORE THE FOOD!!!) because waiting a whole hour for SOMETHING to show up is UNACCEPTABLE. Especially when we order something like lobster ceviche. Did they select a baby lobster for us and had to nurse it in the kitchen into a full grown lobster?? And that was actually the last appetizer to show up out of the 3 ordered. (it was actually my favorite too. the flavors were great) but the other apps were just ok. They were not as great as I had remembered. The calamari was tender but it just tasted not as good as the last time. The entrees came, a seafood paella, skirt steak, and salmon w lobster mash. They were all ok, the paella shined the most. but the steak was a little chewy, not the great skirt steak i remembered. Also, it took more just to flag SOMEbody down for more water. The funny thing is, as we were nearing the end of our meal, 5 different people came to ask us if we were done, our own waiter being the last. We waited this long for food, can we just sit back and try to enjoy this?? We were so annoyed that we just gave up and finally said, yes please just take it away and just end this meal. There was no offer to look at a dessert menu or anything. I was just so DISAPPOINTED, I doubt I will ever go back. It's really sad when you see one of your favorite establishments seriously go downhill.

After hearing quite a few good things, and being new to the area, we decided to give this place a try. We were very disappointed. We waited entirely too long for our table..and we had a reservation! The place is very small and crowded, normally not an issue for us but it was extremely loud and just zoo like. The food was nothing special which by chance matched the nasty server we had. She obviously hates her job and takes it out on the customers. Wouldn't recommend this place to a dog!
If you like meat, this is the right place for you.

Back again for an AMAZING FAMILY DINNER this time. Â We shared antipasto, cheese, pasta, steak and fish - and lots of great wine and prosecco. Â Everything was wonderful, and the service was great, considering it was a Sat. Night. Â So glad my recommendation worked out - what a great place for a celebration.

I'm in NYC every few weeks and always make a point to eat mussels at Petite Abeille. The space is small but inviting. The staff is warm and friendly, and the mussels and frites simply rock! Wednesdays are all-you-can eat mussels night, but I never get through more than one order. Add a Stella or choose from a multitude of Belgian brews. Gastro bliss
Iced Americano was great, barista was really nice, nice interior to sit reading the paper or catch up with friends. It's a neighborhood gem!

Came here on a Saturday at 2,3pm ish. No line at the time, but more people came in afterwards. The servants are friendly and helpful. Ordered deep fried fish (from the chalkboard menu), Kaeng Hang leh (pork shoulder and belly), Papaya pok pok, and dessert (ice cream+coffee+chinese fried doughnuts). The fried fish was very flavorful, except there's not much meat to it. so we had to be very patient to take out the little meat in between the fishbones =) you have to be patient and careful to eat this one. Also ask the price before ordering, the price of this dish depends on the market price. Kaeng Hang leh, my favorite one, it tastes like some traditional asian dish my grandmother used to make for me. So that's authentic. Papaya pok pok salad is very refreshing, a little bit on the spicy side. The dessert is ah-mazing. The servant came with two bowls and one plate, one bowl filled with coffee (I think it was Vietnames coffee), the other ice cream (I think it's vanilla flavored). He then dumped the coffee in the ice cream bowl. and then we dipped the chinese fried doughnut in this little puddle of deliciousness. I even made that at home myself for a few times afterwards. Tastes just as good! Overall, it's a unique and authentic place. They provide spoon and forks but no knife. I googled it, seems that's the way Thai ate. They cut with spoon, and use forks to gather food into the spoon and eat the food off the spoon. =) really appreciate this place, would definitely come back to try other dishes.

Great food, nice vibe. My wife and I went to Upstate on a Tues night around 7:30. There was a 60-90 minute wait. They have a small bar area but not much room for waiting so we walked around the neighborhood. It ended up being right at 90 minutes. It's a very small restaurant, maybe holds 35 people. It's a very cosy and comfortable restaurant, noisy in a good way. They have a small but interesting craft beer and wine selection. I had a very good Saison and my wife had a glass of wine. We had a variety of oysters for appetizer, which were fresh and excellent. My wife ordered the fettuccine with clams, which was very good with a large number of clams in the half shell. I had the scallop special, which was 4 large pan-seared scallops on a bed of squash and mushrooms. It was excellent. The service was friendly and efficient. The total bill as about $75, which was reasonable for the good quality. We'll definitely go back to Upstate next time we're in NYC.

The place is always crowded, and there is always a long line -- but definitely worth the wait. Charming little spot with cute country - french decor, and a wonderful location for brunch. I had the french toast, and enjoyed every bite. Â Our waitress was so attentive, and accommodating. Â She even took the time and effort to search for all of our t-shirt sizes, but they did not have the design or size we needed :( Â She offered to give us a call once they came in, so that was a nice follow-up effort. Â  Do come here with a hearty appetite. The meals are filling!

What a gem this place is! Stumbled upon it after catching a show, and could not have been happier than I was walking into the bright lime green interior. Â Angel was able to find us a seat right away, despite it being packed. Â We started with guac and plaintain chips, and I could not stop smiling. Â The green salsa they brought out was even more delicious than the guac (if that is possible). Â The guy at the table next to us was chowing down on the entrana la plancha dinner. Â He was a regular and said it was his favorite. Â Game on. Â We split that, and had a heap of empanads to share- all were delicious. Â Angel was one of the finest service staff I have encountered in my professional life (I work in hospitality), or my many fine dining experiences. Â He was quick, attentive, very pleasant to chat with and so warm. Â I wish I had one of these in my city- I would go there once a week!

OMG!! Â The pumpkin ravioli! Â Heaven! Â Deliciousness! Â Amazingness!!!! (Nice place with delicious (!!!) pumpkin ravs, but one point is deducted because the bread was chewy and too cold. Â Stick in in the oven for a few minutes, Paprika people!)

I'm surprised this place isn't packed with people, given the price and the quality/uniqueness of the food. The chef literally pulls the noodles for you right after you order it, so its fresh and elastic! I only ordered vegetable noodle because it was my first time there and I didn't know what to expect (its only 4 bucks with A LOT of noodles almost enough for two people) --- it turns out both the soup and noodles was really tasty. Definitely give it a try if you like noodles and want something different from Cantonese food or DimSum.

this place is the BEST! Â however, it's a very different dining experience, and you've got to be prepared in order to maximize your pleasure. Â I've read bad reviews of this place, and it's usually because the writer didn't take the time to get the lay of the land, to properly understand how the place works. Â A map would help, and I have yet to find it if it exists. Â I'd advise you to check out a few different counters, the seafood, the pasta, etc, and be willing to experiment. Â Order what you're familiar with. Â The place can overwhelm with variety and size! Â But the food is excellent, the atmosphere very fun and lively, the workers very friendly!

Hands down my fav restaurant. Â I cannot come to NYC again without coming here. Â I've been twice now and I dream of the food. Â It was so good. Â And, I can go more since I am moving to NYC! Make a reservation! Â  Service- perfect, flawless Food- perfect, amazing, flavors perfectly paired. Â Cannot say enough. Â Had the trout with lentils, friend had risotto. Â Risotto is hard to make right and my friend is picky and she loved it. Â Even the bread was good. Â Another time we went everyone but me had the steak frites- apparently very tasty as well. Cocktails great. I am a bathroom girl and went twice. Â Nice bathrooms. Cannot wait to come back! Â Love U Balthazar!
best pistachio cannoli i ever put in my mouth!!!! nuf said

I'd give a three for the food - had the meatballs which were missing something essential in the spices, and a four for service but the ventilation ruins it all. It's so bad that all my clothes - including my t-shirt I wore under my shirt had to be washed because they smelled so much of food. I'd recommend somewhere else I you can't get a seat outside.

Food is good--extra star for the reasonable prices and convivial atmosphere, including friendly service. My friends enjoyed the steamed mussels as a first, and I was delighted by my ravioli: veal and spinach, in a sauce of cream, mushrooms, and prosciutto. Would definitely go back. (Note: convivial could also read as loud and crazy-busy. I didn't even recognize the place from the photos of the empty restaurant.)

Great food, but much more casual than many of his other restaurants so don't set your expectations for Marea or Ai Fiori. Â This is more like traditional Italian rural/country cooking than the fancy NYC-ified dishes he usually does. That said, the food was all great, and they always have some sort of unique/special wine available by the glass... stuff you would never see available by the glass in other places. Â Bar Boulud does this too and I hope this idea catches on all over.
Really nice atmosphere, good beer selection, and nice music. Â Nice place to relax and people watch...

I've been here twice, once for dinner and once for a private party in the backroom and both times the food was EXCELLENT. Maialino reminds me of wine country with their decor and old country style interior. On the exterior, the restaurant looks very classy, but once you step in you realize this is not that type of restaurant. I wouldn't call it trendy, but it has a casual feel to it without being TOO casual. When you get in, you notice alot of wood furnishing from the bar table, seats, wine cellar to the tables, decorative accessories and flooring. I especially love the plaid dining table clothes. As for food, during the time I was here for dinner I ordered the Funghi mushrooms, white wine & anchovy; Coda Alla Vaccinara oxtails, carrot & celery; and Pollo Alla Diavola peppered half chicken & pickled chili. None of these dishes will overwhelm your appetite as they are not huge, but each had very distinct flavors. The Funghi had a very fresh taste to it as the white wine really gave it a nice alcohol kick. The oxtails were marinated in tomato sauce with the stew of the carrot & celery and I really liked the tanginess of the flavor on the stew. The half chicken was very simple, but extremely juicy and moist. I could tell it was intensely seasoned because it was full of flavor from the first bite! Maialino is a simple restaurant that has a very cozy feel to it. It's located in the quiet area of Gramercy Park and easy to get to. There's usually parking around the area so it's never a problem to drive to either. Nothing on the menu will be shockingly out of the ordinary, but the food is real solid and extremely flavorful here. Also, it's great that anyone can have a casual one on one dinner here or if they want they can have a private celebration as there is a backroom for a large party.

I give this place two starts because the customer service is really bad. They don't know how to serve customer . All of thing they do is just walking around. The food is not that great . I don't know why other people give this place 4 and 5 starts. Horrible customer service !

Was here last Saturday after a while I had been missing. Chargrilled burger: still in the list of top-3 best burgers in the city, hands down; huge delicious patty good enough to wake up Lazaro. And the fries are just amazing: super-thin, super-crunchy and super-tasty. Too bad you have to wait hours before getting a seat. :(

Lovely place, great atmosphere...wonderful selection of wine. Â Waitstaff is classy, knowledgeable and non-invasive. Â  Have only tried a couple of small bites, very good. Â Sat in the window with a friend on a Sunday at 4P and it was lovely to have a great glass of wine and watch the world go by. Â Although wines are not inexpensive, you are sure to try something you haven't heard of before and love it.

Fantastic restaurant, fastantic food. Â It's quite impossible to get a reservation at a decent time via Opentable, though walk-ins are welcomed. Â I suspect people call in their reservations, but I haven't tried. One of my favorite dishes here is the cheeseburger. Â How different can the lowly cheeseburger be, right? Â Well, it was surprisingly good without being greasy. Â This is one of those places that I always recommend to friends asking for recommendations, and it hasn't disappointed yet. Â And don't let the reservation situation deter you. I just wish it's easier to get reservations on Opentable!

Never had ramen other than from Wal Mart but it was strongly recommended while visiting NYC. Â  Love it, amazing flavor. Â  Yes it's a big bowl of broth with skinny noodles but who knew you could make it taste so friggin good. Â  I can't compare this place to any others since it's my first time but I can say it's very clean with great service. Â I'd say the decor has a lunch feel to it. Â It doesn't scream "get comfy and hang out". Â  I'd go back. Â  Anxious to explore others locations.
My wife and I always love eating here. The staff are fantastic and the sushi superb. Try curry udon on a cold night & anything on a warm summer evening.

Burger and fries with an asian twist. Other than the serious hype, this place has okay food for the price. Its 12 bucks per a burger which is a little bigger size then a double cheeseburger in mcdonalds. The line was crazy long as my party had to wait for 40mins. Tho I arrive 30mins late it was surprising that everyone was still waiting. We had to go to another place after for more food, the place is nothing special and for the price and line I would rather go somewhere else.
This place is a true 5 star Pizzeria, the flavor from the mozzarella, tomato sauce and the crust are perfecto! only wish they had a Di Fara here in the windy city.

The pizza here is crazy good; not even sure if it has toppled my current favourite at Di Fara's, but this creation borne from a roaring 900F+ oven has certainly has bested the pies I've had at Fornino's, Grimaldi's, or even favourites from New England like Frank Pepe's in New Haven and Al Forno in Providence. We had the Crispy Glover and the (off-menu) Bee Sting. Â Although the touch of honey on the latter was a delicious mix of sweet and salty, we still thought that the Crispy Glover was a more flavourful and mouth-watering experience. Â We loved the savouriness of the guanciale and red onion, highlighted with just enough heat from the chilli to round things out. The surprise of the night came from the deceptively simple but overwhelmingly delicious grilled eggplant. Â Beautifully matched with summer squash and an assortment of fragrant herbs, the grilled vegetables were served amidst an intoxicating tomato clam broth. Â First thought? Â I hope this recipe is in their cook book! Â SO GOOD.

me and my friend had the brunch in the Saturday afternoon. about 15 mins wait, which was ok. the space was small and packed as the typical west village restaurants. FOOD: satisfied before we sat down, there were orange juice waited for us as part of the brunch pre-fix ($14.95): juice+entree+coffee/tea we had Croque Monsieur and Grilled Salmon Sandwich. ---Croque Monsieur was really yum. crispy bread covered with melting cheese and ham. ---Grilled Salmon Sandwich was a bit too dry. not very impressive but fulfilled. SERVICE & ENVIRONMENT: cheesy it took about 10 mins for our waitress to take the order. the food were served in 10 mins after that. after 30 mins when we were almost done with our main dish, the bill was thrown on our table without asking if we wanted anything else (of course, we wanted desserts!). after i reminded one of waiters that we wanted our complimentary coffee, he asked us to switch to another table instead because there were a group of 6 waiting outside. Â so we switched to the widow/sofa seats. isles and seats were very narrow and tiny. the waiter didnt help us, we gotta figure how to get in ourselves and asked people in the neighbor tables to remove their table first. Â the seats were very DIRTY. lots of bread crumbles on them... 5 mins after the coffee was served, we were asked to switch to ANOTHER table AGAIN. plus, i asked for napkins (to swipe our dirty table) for THREE times and no one gave it to me... not to mention we didn't have any chance to order dessert coz waiters/waitress werent available most of the time... very disappointed to its service.
Good every time we go. Â Great value and delicious food. Â We typically get shabu shabu for two with prime beef.

Me likey : ) Â We walked up and the name was nowhere in sight... just an key-shaped insignia. Â Turns out that if you flip it around, it's the initials E. O. Â Snazzy. Â The space is all art deco-ed out with interesting lighting fixtures, metal parqueted ceilings, and even the staff is dressed in 20's attire! Â Nice and swank at night, but probably really enjoyable on a sunny day b/c they have huge sky-lights and a garden-esque kind of deal all the way back with mini fountain and more sky-lights. Â The bar was busy with tons of beautiful people mingling. Â I mean, we had diplomats, some Brits, a troupe of slick Italians... you name it! Â Extensive drink menu... they serve martinis in classy round glasses instead of the traditional fashion, which I though was uber cool and set the mood. Â The menu was really diverse... the bf had the Parmesan pork chop, which was AMAZING, and I had an interesting Brown Paper tilapia, which was wild rice, pumpkin puree and the fish, all wrapped in a paper bag and baked so that the fish absorbs the pumpkin flavor. Â Genius, pure genius. Â Everyone else in our party looked pretty pleased with their choices and it was an overall warm & pleasant place.

Carmine's is a nice place to grab a Family Style Meal. Â  Walked during the Midweek and was granted a table immediately. Â Food was good and a decent value for a restaurant in the Theatre District. Â I would recommend a Pasta Dish and a Meat Dish to share amongst 4 people. Â  Anytime I walk by this place it seems to be busting at the seems. Have Fun. Decor wise nice to look at a welcome distraction from trying to read the Menu on the wall.

I tend to bias upward when writing reviews, yet this time there is no bias at all, it is truly worth a five star. We came here for its shabu but later determined to try the sukiyaki. Â As always, prime rib eye set is our choice. It was a little bit salty but other than that food quality was of high standard. Compared with momokawa, Â I'd say this place is a bit more free style...but yeah, Â both are worth trying. Last but not least, go for their ice cream, Â it has been included in the set already. Nice way to call an end to the dinner!
Not bad- but just crammed with tourists 7 days a week- staff seem a little jaded and rushed - food good but there are better options on roads less travelled

Went here on a weekday evening with two friends and the wait was over an hour, which wasn't really that surprising. That gave us enough time to go down to Chinatown for some ice cream. The place is rather large and super trendy but I don't get what the hype is all about. The ramen was good, not great. I left feeling 'eh'. I probably won't be coming back.

Where did my other 1/2 of the deviled egg appetizer go (we received 3 halves)?! Â Lol, it was really good though. No complaints about customer service, staff was excellent and cool. Â The place itself is made for the hipster crowd. Â Really interesting decor, I liked the environment a lot. My best friend and I both had a burger with fries. Â Burger was huge, fries were excellent. Â The food was excellent. Â Where they lost a star was dessert. Â I had the special of the night which our waiter recommended to me and it was just not for me. Â He looked so excited about it, I just told him it was great, but lied I did! Â It was some sort of custard-pudding type vanilla thingy topped with graham crackers and raspberries, I think? Â I don't remember the dessert well but it really wasn't for me. I'd go back though and order something else for dessert. Â Easy to gain weight coming here...lol, so worth the weight gain!

Really, the food here is average. Chicken was dry. I've actually had better at other carts. The convenient seats near it is a plus. Other than that, i'd say go elsewhere. Came at 10:30-11pm, wait was less than 5 minutes! (mid week)

From the front of the house to the back of the house staff they are excellent. My wife and I try a new place every friday since moving back to NYC. This place was found by one of our daughters so we had to try it. Well, needless to say it did not disappoint. We had to wait but it was worth it. The drinks & appetizers at the bar were great. The bartender was friendly. He makes a great of a Caipirinha. When we sat down the waitstaff was prompt and attentive. Though my wife and I cannot eat spicy there was enough on the menu to make the night wonderful. Even the manager sat down with us at the end of the night to talk. Â In all this place is a keeper and a place that My wife and I will return with our family and friends!

The worst night of my life. My BFF is visiting from DC and after we went shopping for our two dog rescues we bought leather leashes with matching collar from Will's leather's getting it monogrammed and I made the unfortunate decision to actually dine at this horrid place because I apparently like so many customers left my purchases behind. With 30 minutes after leaving I realized I left my bag at my table but as I returned to a unhappy staff and a rude owner with his guests, I asked for help to look for my $300 purchased item and the co- owner himself had the nerve to say "no, you didn't have a bag" I'm in shock and will save the world from ever coming to this hell!

THE PRICE IS RIGHT! 53rd Street and 6th Avenue at night is the perfect place to be for halal chicken or lamb meat! Â I am usually not a huge fan of lamb meat because I can taste a certain after taste that I really can't stand. However, when my friend got a plate of half chicken and half lamb on a bed of safferon rice, with a side of greek yogurt and hot sauce, it was to die for! Â I highly recommend this hang out spot with plenty of seating on the steps to the side, beautiful night life, plenty of people watching and GREAT food. Â I love New York and good eats like this make me want to come back. Â My friends and I got lucky because supposedly the line can get pretty long at night and apparently this cart only comes out after 6pm, therefore don't be fooled by other carts that might occupy the same spot at early hours! Â There were plenty other Halal carts too but you should definitely try the one at this corner. Â A plate of food and drink for only 8 dollars. I left very happy!

The 2 stars is for the service, but I'll comment on the food first. The pizza was certainly fresh, with real mozzarella and a crushed tomato sauce. Â A small pepperoni (6 slices) was MORE than enough to feed my friend, Lindsey. and me. Â We each were only able to eat 2 slices. Â Not my favorite pizza, just because I'm not a huge fan of straight up slices of mozz on my pizza. Â But definitely worthy of a try. Â And prices are decent too. Â $12 for a small pizza sans toppings. Ok, so the service was absolutely horrendous. Â There was a line of about 10 people at noon on a Monday when we went, but we prob didn't wait more than 25 minutes to get in. Â Definite plus. Â The guy/host that runs the show (who may be the owner or manager or who knows) was really nice. Â He greeted us when we got in and made sure to ask how things were and ask that we come back when we left. Â Another plus. Â But the waiter was horrible. Â They have so many people wanting to eat there that they just want to get you in and out. Â I asked for a root beer and I got a 'tude from the waiter saying they didn't have any today. Â He was probably annoyed just because that's prob the 192384th time he's had to say that today, but honestly, how was I supposed to know? Â Then the table next to us tried to get his attn and he completely ignored them. Â I was sorely disappointed. Â And his tip showed it. Â I worked in the restaurant biz in college and even if you're in a crap mood, you best move on and do what you're supposed to do - serve and please the customer. I wanted to take my family there in April, when they come to visit, and I probably still will. Â But only for the satisfaction of saying they've been to the famed Grimaldi's.

I've only had empanadas a couple times in my life. But I've never really been wowed by them before. Not until I came here. The boyfriend and I just wanted to grab a light lunch and empanadas seemed appropriate since they're pretty small. I looked around and literally everyone had an order of plantain chips and guac, so naturally, I ordered one too. For some reason I was expecting the chips to be sweet, but they were very chip-like. Very crispy and slightly salty. The guacamole tasted Â fresh and delicious. They give a very generous serving of it so we had enough to eat with our empanadas as well. As for the empanadas, there are so many different kinds! I was quite overwhelmed since I was planning on just ordering one. I went with spicy chicken while the boyfriend went with the chorizo and ground beef with the masa dough (corn). I made the right choice. Each bite was sooo flavorful. It's crazy how much it has for such a small little pastry. I really enjoyed the masa dough as well. I think the spicy chicken empanadas would be even better with the masa rather than flour. It's a really small restaurant but don't be too intimidated. They are super efficient with their seating. We were pretty impressed how many tables they can accommodate for such little space. More restaurants should learn from places like this.

Koreans like myself are natural born trendsetters and hipsters (if you've been to Korea, especially Seoul's Hongdae and Apgujeong Neighborhood, you know what I mean). Not that I'm saying this place is Korean or Korean owned/operated, but it really reminds me of the many cafes or coffeeshops in Seoul due to its detail, bohemian, vintage looking interior. Books on the walls, a Piano, multiple tables, a bar, an outside seating area in the backyard (when the weather permits!!), this place is probably a gem in the neighborhood of Greenpoint, a neighborhood neglected by many and probably hated by hipsters since it's right next to Williamsburg. The atmosphere is quaint and cozy. The noise level is average so don't come here to talk or laugh out loud. Most patrons are working on their laptops during the day while sipping some Espresso based drink. There is a restroom for your convenience as well. You are also a subway ride away from Long Island City if you need to get to Queens or even Manhattan. Coffee is decent here and prices are reasonable. Prices range from $2-$2.75 for Americano or Macchiato and a bit more for specialty drinks. Overall, what a great find, love the vibe and LOVE that it's not that crowded and definitely a place where I can escape the city on the weekends for some much needed relaxation and down time. **CASH-ONLY**

Overhyped. Quality of food and service has gone down hill since "The Halal Guys" became a go to spot for New Yorkers and then eventually tourists. Better than some halal carts but nothing better than decent. Good if you're in the area and are starving on a budget. The line is not worth it anymore.

Wajima is an authentic place for basic Japanese food. If you know what you're getting into, you won't be disappointed at Wajima. Let me elaborate. The place is run by Japanese staff, which makes for great Japanese food but not so great on the service because their English leaves much to be desired. My waitress did not say a word to me, not sure because she was busy or she just didn't have anything to say to me in English. She just nods, with a frown on her face, but I got what I wanted, so I guess that was not too bad. Don't expect any service or kindness beyond the basics here - they are not very accommodating. Not good for kids, because kids needs a lot of accommodation. Anyway, you gotta give it to them when it comes to the quality of the food and the efficiency. I went during the lunch rush, without a reservation, and was seated in about 15-20 minutes (party of one), because they are extremely efficient, which you can be if you only have 3 items on the menu, which were the 3 different lunch sets they have. My food took 5 minutes to make. Most people sit down, eat their lunch, then leave, no fuss, does not take long to go through each customer. The ingredients were extremely fresh, perfectly prepared, delicious. Well-executed Japanese comfort food. I got the Sanmizen set. Chirashi was fresh, sushi rice was a bit heavy on the vinegar but not a dealbreaker. Tempura shrimp was nice a crispy, with sauce already in the bowl. Miso soup was good, but nothing to write home about - I can make the same at home with fresh miso from a Japanese grocery store. The cold soba was delicious - the noodles had a nice texture, fresh, with delicious cold bonito broth. The highlight was the chawanmushi - the steamed egg. It was interesting - tiny bits of lemon peels gave it a refreshing kick. The soft-tofu-like fluffy texture means the eggs were cooked to perfection, with an amazing umami savoriness that makes me wonder how they make eggs so perfectly. Quite impressive. So, if you want a quick, delicious, brutally efficient basic Japanese food for lunch, Wajima is your place on the UES. $12.50 for the amount of food on the lunch set and its quality is really quite a steal and well worth it. Can't say the same for dinner - if it's the same food for double the price I probably won't be there, because that will be too expensive.

I totally agree with all the other yelpers, indeed this one is a great find!! Every year around this time, my wife and I have this craving for typical french bistro food from our honeymoon. We have been looking for a whole in the wall, straight to the point, no frill french bistro food. Food was excellent!! It was as good as the one that we had during our honeymoon. So here's what we order: Escargot-on point, and excellent. I just wish for more french bread to soak up all the buttery, garlicky deliciousness...hahahahh (sorry...i'm a fatty who appreciates food!) Beef tartare- was amazing!! Seasoned on point! Steak frites-was so awesome, sauce was good. I asked for rare and guess what..i recieve my rare steak... Duck confit-was super crispy, a bit salty but thats okay you have the salad that counters it. After all the food that We ordered plus a bottle of 2011 bordeaux, the damage was less than $150 (tax&tip included).. Overall, when you're in NYC...give this place a try...my recommendation go during weekday and make reservation, like a said they're small... Bon appÃ©tit!

This is one of my favorite burgers in the city. Â Their blend of meat, coupled with the cheese and onions is absolutely delicious. Â I am also a big fan of the bacon option, and love that they mix it right in with the meat. Â Their sauce options are also stellar, especially the jalapeno sauce. Â The fries are a little dry but the burgers more than make up for it.

Pros: Great, broth, springy noodles, recession price meal and fast service. Cons: Plastic utensils (including bowls!), cheap decor and small menus. That still doesn't trump the fact that this is a great tasty meal for $5 with change! I will definitely come back.

I loved it! So much space that if it's just a couple of you and you don't fit at the many tables, you can likely find a seat at the bar. It's huge and yet it was packed for lunch on a weekday. My friend and I sat at the bar by the front door. I had the prix fixe lunch for $25, which is definitely worth it. The beet and yogurt salad is awesome; I didn't even know there were non-purple beets and I actually like them better! The hake was cooked very nicely and the mustard sauce was delicious, but my one complaint is that there was too much black pepper in the dish. My friend had the gazpacho, which was good and definitely tasted like strawberries, but not overwhelmingly so. We shared the strawberry dessert which was scrumptious! And lighter than others, I'm sure. I love the ambience, such wonderful decor. Great place!! I will definitely be going back again and again.

I've never really gone at a time where it was so packed, I usually get there just before the rush (11:45am) this place is great for drinks and food. You must get their chips & guac. even the salsa is really something else. The chips have got to be fried back there it is always so crispy and doesn't taste too oily. I love their beer selection and their margarita selection. The very last time I enjoyed their strawberry mojito. Great place to go when you're craving mexican.

The prices are so reasonable which is awesome. Â The food is great - I've never had a bad meal here. Â The wine is delicious too. Â I really enjoyed the pasta, which was cooked perfectly and had a flavorful sauce, but the stuffed chicken breast was just OK.

I wanted to be blown away, I wanted to leave feeling like my belly was thanking me. Â However, I was somewhat disappointed and mildly satisfied. Â I left feeling like I got a glimpse into where David Chang is trying to go, but was distracted by my desperate need for water (yup, the food was salty). Â  We ate here for lunch. Â We started with the tripe dish, I loved it. Â I love tripe, and probably love any preparation of it. Â That being said, this dish was very tasty, and one of my favorite tripe dishes I've had. Â We then had the spicy rice cakes and a pork shoulder dish. Â They were both quite salty, and would have been great if we could have had some rice. Â  We ended with a cold grapefruit pie which was pretty good. Â It helped cut through all the salt and rich flavors. Â (But actually, this was salty too, the crust was made with Ritz crackers. David Chang's dishes (in my opinion) are Korean at heart, however, I think he over does it with his flavors. Â Korean food is simple (for the most part), but delicious in its simplicity. Â The food at Momofuku was salty and the flavors muddled. Â There was just too much going on. Â However, I appreciated what David Chang was doing, he was trying to bring a new level, a new page to the food he probably grew up with. Â So in the end, I bought his cookbook to get ideas and inspiration for my own cooking.
this guy knows the oyster business inside in out. Â he buys them fresh in the morn, and serves till they are gone. Â I like your style man.

HUGE place, service is just okay, but large restaurants tend to have this issue. Get the poutine, it's amazing (not traditional canadian poutine but the idea is the same). The wings are pretty standard but good. The food came really quickly, and they have a pretty large beer selection. Next time I'll go a little earlier to avoid a wait (though we only waited around ten minutes during the height of the dinner rush).

Probably the best dining experience ever. 1st you must go to the bar and try at least 3 or 4 of Karens speciality drinks.. They are really the "best" I ever had.. If you are feeling brave, ask for a shot of some of the finest Japanese whiskeys to ever hit NYC. Karen is also a lively spirit who is awesome to talk too and makes the experience that much more pleasurable. A must is also the mac and cheese. I am a huge mac and cheese guy and this is hands down my favorite. Can't wait to go back to NYC and visit this awesome establishment again.

I am so glad I stumbled upon this place while staying at the Hudson hotel. The empanadas were amazing!! You can choose either a wheat or corn-based shell and they have tons of options for the filling. I tried a wheat shell with spicy chicken and a corn-based shell with beef filling. Â Everything was fresh and flavorful. It was also filling. If you're in the area you have to visit. Start with a few empanadas and order more if you have room. This food is so good that it leaves a lasting impression. Â I can't wait for my next visit to NYC!!
This place is spectacular! We had a few tacos and burritos at our table and just passed them around. Everything was above our expectations.

This place is seriously overrated. The "Bao" is simply an exposed Chinese bun with literally 2 pierces of meat and vegetables on top. For $3.50 per "Bao" and the ability to finish it in 2 bites... Honey no. I mean I admit it is quite delicious, but I feel like they are robbing people with these prices. Make the "Bao" bigger or lower the prices! The bubble tea is mediocre, nothing spectacular. Decor is mediocre. Oh might I add that this place is CASH ONLY... It was one thing if the reason to do so is to keep prices down, but that's obviously not the case. I'll pass.

Solid ramen. I am no ramen expert but I enjoyed my veggie ramen. It had an interesting flavor, almost fishy but very delicate. The noodles were a great texture. My only complaint was that it didn't have too much actual veggies in it. The Brussels sprouts were awesome! They tasted fried and had peanuts and jalapeÃ±o peppers on top. I definitely want to go back and try the pork bone ramen, which my friend tells me was so delicious he couldn't stop eating.

It was my birthday, and my boyfriend and I, being the newly-arrived-in-Park Slope Omnivore's Dilemma-reading yuppie couple that we are, wanted to try this place's prix fixe menu for dinner. Â We expected to be served delicately decorated little plates of delicious seasonal foods and then walk down the hill to Uncle Louie G's for dessert. We had the "delicious" part right. Â And everything was definitely pretty. Â But we were dead wrong about the "little" part. Â Worst of all, it was all so amazing that I couldn't stop eating. Â Seriously, the food was giving me some kind of disorder where I couldn't leave a crumb on the plate - troubling when the portions are as huge as they are here. Â An enormous bowl of the best corn chowder I've ever had was followed by an enormous bowl of risotto and an enormous chocolate dessert. Â Everything augmented, of course, by an enormous bread basket with local olive oil for dipping. Â  When there was finally nothing left to eat, we got up and sloshed on home to mid-Slope. I was more than a little ill for the rest of the night. Â  Â Happy birthday to me. Â We'll be back, of course - just not often enough to make gluttons out of us.

3.5, really, but definitely does not deserve a 3. Practically a 4 for the music alone -- Beck, Radiohead, Talking Heads, et al. Nearly every track they played is a regular on my shuffle. Servers are clad in white shirts and bowties. The French bistro vibe is nice, clean, classic & simple. Pretty legit cocktail menu. Standard beers normally served in BK. My French Dip was good, but the menu could be a wee bit more extensive. I would come back if I'm ever in the hood -- nice vibe; reliable food; awesome music.

I love Italian food, and I love happy hour. Cent'Anni has both. Happy hour is half off wines by the glass, draft beers, house cocktails, and some call liquors. This is an amazing deal. No buts about it. The pastas come out piping hot and are really tasty. You can build your own bowl, or try a savory classic like rigatoni with meatballs and sausage. My husband and I go in here a couple times a week and enjoy chatting with the bartenders and grabbing a bite. Give it a try!

Okay, the white sauce is good, it's worth the wait. I get it. But there are two other carts owned by the same people serving the SAME food with NO LINE within easy walking distance. Just look for the signature 53rd and 6th Yellow t-shirts on the other street corners if you're skeptical, but the stuff is trucked in from the same place to all three locations. But hey, if waiting in line is half the fun for you, or you're so drunk the words on the Yellow t-shirts are swimming before your eyes, then don't let me stand in your way. In fact, please stay in line and sober up while I go get me a plate of delicious food from around the corner. ;)
in the words of my young nephew, "it's just too complicated." indeed... the macchiato though, helped stave off a temper tantrum.

One of the best pizzas I've ever eaten! So so good! Need to go back asap. Lines are long, so I would suggest making a reservation. It's also BYOB.. bring a bottle of wine so that you can enjoy it with the delicious pizza :)
i love this place

Having been convinced by yelp and a coworker to give it a try, i decided to finally try their Xiao Long Bao. I have tried Â a TON of different places Xiao Long Bao in new york from Shanghai cafe to Shanghai Cuisine to Shanghai gabaghoul. The Good: we did not have to wait long(like 2 mins) to get in. The waiters were responsive to us fast. The calamari in black bean sauce is quite good. Very spicy but good. The bad: the Xiao Long Bao are only adequate. Not the best, not the worst. In addition the crab XLB tastes entirely too fishy. Also the service is not that great. I ordered a cup of water and he brings me a scalding hot glass of water. Umm wtf am i supposed to do with that?? Take a bath??Plus we got stuck next to some loud annoying idiots :|. Summary: I felt like it was like going on a date with a REALLY popular person at school only to find out they have no personality. I kind of went expecting the XLB to give me some life altering experience and to redefine the Xiao Long Bao experience. Only to find out it wasn't even as good as some of the ones Â I already had :|. Not gonna bother with this place again, the atmosphere is subpar with the xlb being average. There's better nearby :| and certainly not the second coming of Xiao Long Bao by any means necessary. If you're expecting angels to sing while you eat it, not gonna happen :|

Been back here three or four times since the last review and the food seems to have gotten better. Easily the best Tom Yum Goong I have had stateside. It has that sour peppery taste that is difficult to get right, but these guys seem to have the perfect balance. Best cure for a Sunday afternoon hangover. Their fish ball curry is also pretty amazing and well prepared. The service is prompt even when they are busy. For some reason the consistency of the food seems better on the weekends for whatever reason. Definitely coming back again. The prices are right and the menu is so expanse that I will never get bored of this place. Do yourself a favor though. Do not come here and order pad thai like I see so many average people doing. Explore the menu and you will really enjoy this place.

My gripes: -I'm not a fan of pizza at restaurants. It's just who I am. The four cheese (quattro formaggi) pizza was meh. Uneven cheese distribution and okay crust. The pesto and the wild mushroom ones were the best. -They sat us downstairs in the dark basement. It was hard to see anything and they even dimmed the lights further. -They were not ready for our group even though we had reservations days in advance. They just haphazardly put some tables together. -Service wasn't very good. Took forever to get our orders in. -Bathroom line also got ridiculous as our meal was winding down. What I liked: -The manager, or whoever was in charge of keeping us happy, was great and very personable -Food is super affordable -Beer selection isn't huge, but what they do have is alright, considering the area -A slice of birthday cake! I believe it was on the house -Easy to get reservations -It was quiet enough to talk to even with half the basement full

After reading all these GREAT reviews about the mac & cheese, I finally went to Soco. I ordered 2 orders of chicken and waffles (one for me, one for the Boo) and an order of mac & cheese. We brought the food home, I placed the food into the oven for a few minutes and my kitchen all of a sudden had a strong garlic smell. The mac & cheese was OVERLOADED with garlic, beyond belief! We rarely ever throw food in the garbage and guess where that mac & cheese went? The photos I've seen of the mac & cheese are deceiving. There was not one ounce of cheddar, it was all white cheese. The chicken and waffles were nothing to write home about. Chicken lacked seasoning, had NO flavor at all and the syrup was heavily diluted, we just grabbed some good old Aunt Jemima from the kitchen. I should have saved my $54 and made my own damn mac & cheese for 1/6 the price. Will not be going back. So disappointed.

The food here is delicious. My husband and I recently moved to Park Slope and Krupa Grocery has fast become one of our favorite neighborhood restaurants. We've been there several times for dinner and it hasn't disappointed us yet!

The first thing people want to know is: is this better than Ippudo? Yes. My wait was around 30 minutes (if you hate waiting, you should eat with more exciting people!). I ordered the spicy ramen with pork, it was $11, from what I remember and I have to say, the noodles have a stronger texture, which I loved, and the broth was rich and almost creamy? Thicker? It wasn't watery, but it was denser? I'm horrible at describing these things, but it was surprisingly delicious. The meat was savory (though I think Ippudo gives a bit more). I also liked it felt like you walked into a home instead of a restaurant. It wasn't trying to be too modern or too cool or too clubby. It's a nice little restaurant that serves amazing ramen. No gimmicks.

Ippudo doesn't really need another review, you just need to go! Best ramen ever on either coast for serious! At lunchtime, get the set with a small salad, and sticky rice with your choice of topping: eel, cod, pork, or yam. Amazing decor and service. When I move to the village (in my dreams) I will be an Ippudo regular.

Wow. We were just looking for some after drinks munchies food on Saturday night and thought burgers sounded good. We stepped in and it was like we walked into another club with their blasting music. It wasn't the cheap eats we expected but rolled w it anyways ,... Appetizers of truffle fries, tater tots, corn salad and guacamole were amazing. We could have done without the gauc but everything else I kept grabbing over and over. For my entree I got the Mac n cheese which is really a starter but it filled me up. Rigatoni pasta (yum) with a cheesy base and tasty bacon. My friends raved about their dishes too which were the lamb burgers, the fish and the pork ribeye. The pork ribeye was a bit raw (it was weird to us too?) but had good flavor. All in all, I'm really impressed and will come back !

If you're in town, this place is a must. I didn't think the pizza was mind blowing but it's a classic so you have to go just to say that you went. I bought a Sicilian 1/2 tray and it was more than enough for two people. I had leftovers which was great because the pizza still tastes delicious when reheated in the oven. Location: I found that the place was in the middle of nowhere. I had to go out of my way just to go here but I decided to go for it because everyone said it was great and I wanted to judge for myself. Ices: I think I enjoyed the ices more than the pizza itself. It was a hot summer day so that might be the reason. I had the coconut and it was amaze-beans. Overall I think this was a one time thing for me but it was good food. The prices could be better though. I paid $20 for the 1/2 tray.

this place is not worth the wait plus you smell after you come out eating from this place. the pizza is alright and adding toppings at this place can be pricey their service sucks and i dont like sitting in their high chairs i like their pastas from there tough
Fish tacos are verrrryyyy Â tastie

First things first: The Smith does things to string beans that will make you weak in the knees. My guess is that they dip them in something delicious, drop them in something more delicious and then throw them into a vat of fat, which cannot help but lead to a mind-blowing finale (and it does). In all seriousness, they are crispy without losing any flavor. We had them as a side for our burgers, but for me, they were the stars of the evening. We arrived for our 7:30 reservation on Saturday evening to a bustling restaurant. Be sure to arrive with your entire party and make a reservation or else you'll be waiting at the bar, awkwardly Â nursing a drink as you ogle the plates of food passing before you. The only downside to this establishment was the pre-dinner wait time (despite the reservation) and the substantial wait for our food (30 minutes). We all got the burgers because we're pigs. We also ordered a plate of swedish meatballs because we're impatient pigs. The swedish meatballs were good, but on the mini side. The sauce was oh so decadent. So good we asked for more bread to sop it up (remember, we're pigs). The hamburgers come with either fries or a side of choice (for $2 extra). We all shared the fries, mashed potatoes and did I mention the string beans? The burger buns were made from quality bread and the meat was perfectly seasoned, juicy and had a nice spice to it. And the special sauce is YUM. The mashed potatoes and fries aren't really noteworthy. Overall, I very much enjoyed my experience at The Smith. I can't wait to try their pastas. I'll be back! With a reservation.

This ramen place is absolutely divine. Â The food is from heaven it is so good. Â The broth is totally amazing. Â It has a oniony fantastic taste that is totally not gamey or fishy - just wholesome goodness. Â The lines are insane so my husband I went when it opened and it was just awesome.
Great sandwiches here and friendly staff. The avocado shake is a must have. Also, the sandwiches are still amazing after being refrigerated if you decide to take some extras home.

We recently moved to the neighborhood and were looking for restaurant options. Â We found The Farm on Adderly on Father's Day and loved it--great food, good service, and kid friendly. Â We've been back a few times and have enjoyed it each time. Â It's busy on weekends, but we take that as a good sign, and make sure we have plenty of reading material for the wait.
The pizza is not so different from most other pizza joints in Brooklyn. I have definitely had better squares elsewhere. Their hot food is average. Overall, it is a friendly place.

My mom was in town from California and I had heard great things about Bogota so we went for dinner last night. I have never been welcomed more kindly and enthusiastically. Everyone from the host to the server to the bus boy. Just incredible. Their menu is very extensive and the waitress was able to make solid, firm recommendations. The ropa vieja is a must try. And their fried plantain chips with Bogota's very own aji sauce hit the spot. I don't traditionally like spicy foods and the jalapeno kick was light enough that I could enjoy it. And happy hour all day Mon-Wed? Will definitely come back to this place. LOVED IT.

Food at Perry St was amazing and nice waiters, but serving all courses in an hour to sell the table again is ridiculous. Especially if you pay more than 100bucks each (desert not included). We ended up ordering more wine and ignored the multiple tries to give us the bill, just to get the feel of a proper night out
This place is amazing for brunch. They're extremely accommodating for small parties of 2 or 4. Food is great, sangria is outstanding. Price is right!

This place was very good. Ht my Vietnamese craving nicely. Had the traditional pork sandwich as the shrimp rolls.Oh yeah, and I added the fried egg to the sandwich. No complaints. The food was actually massive. I was shocked at the potion sizes. Good prices. I'm a fan.

Wonderful!! We were going to another place and there was an hour and a half wait... So we decided to give this place a try. What a wonderful meal! No wait!! Everyone had their favorite thing... Eggs Benedict, French toast with caramelized bananas. Â Great coffee! Â Oh, and did I mention, no wait! And a beautiful decor... We will be there again on our NYC trip!

great pork buns...like the best. small place and loud. good short rib sandwich, but the bread was too toasted. need to try the pork shoulder here, but you have to wait like 3 months. the milk bar sucks now because they moved it across the street into a small closet/shithole/dump.

I have been living in the area all my life and it is finally great to see a different type of restaurant. Zona Sur is great and the food is amazing. Their Egg pizza is delicious and the Steak sammy is just as great! I look forward to their brunch, mimosas and live band on Sundays, such a wonderful little gem!
Made to order dumplings. Had the fried pork and chive dumplings, sesame pancake and basil and chicken dumplings. Was good and got lucky cause wasnt very busy.

I had high expectations of Ai Fiori considering that this establishment had one of the highest reviews among NYC Italian restaurants. Â Oh boy......was I disappointed. Coming from DC where there isn't a single good Italian restaurant (or none that I have found so far), I have done my due diligence on yelp and found that this was one of the top restaurants open during lunch on Saturday. Â Based on the reviews, I learned that Ai Fiori is the sister restaurant of Marea and is supposed to be tad lower in standards compared to Marea so I figured that this was going to be my best bet. Â At $38 for appetizer+main course for lunch I didn't think there was much to lose. For my appetizer, I had the Torchon, a great foie gras dish accompanied by a bose pair filled with zabaglione (custard) filling and toasted broiche (super buttery bread). Â The foie gras was topped with a thin layer of glazed sugar (which I could hardly taste). I have mixed feelings about the appetizer. Â I like it in the sense that it is novel. Â The Â foie gras blends well with the buttery broiche and the mixture glides through the mouth as if the food were moving around a frictionless surface. Â On the flip side, the buttery broiche masks the taste of the foie gras, and made me wonder if a butter substitution for the foie gras would have been sufficient to trick me on an off-day for my palate. Â Needless to say, I would say that pairing of this dish with a strong wine would completely mask the taste of the foie gras.... For my main dish I had the dish that everyone raves about...the Trofie Nero aka squid ink pasta, ligurian crustacean ragout, seppia, scallops, spiced mollica. Â  The one thing I found fascinating about this pasta is the extra "chewiness" factor. Â I'm unsure what this pasta is, but it appears to be a denser version of a fettuccine-like pasta that was curled in the form of a helix. Â This may remind you of rotini but it is not. Imagine a dense fettuccine wrapped around a chopstick. Â This form makes you bite through parallel layers of pasta unlike a rotini and this seems to pack the extra punch of "chewiness". Â  The big negative about this dish is that it was overly salty. It already packs a punch of salt from the seafood that goes into it...and it seems as though they added more salt on top of that. Â I found that too be a big turnoff. Overall, my impressions of the food were subpar and strictly based on it, I would rate it somewhere around 3.5-3.75* range for a restaurant of this caliber. Â The experience, service, and atmosphere were great (a bit of pretentiousness, but if you read the reviews, you were warned) which pushed me to give an overall rating of 4* instead of a 3*. I suggest venturing out to other restaurants in the area. Â Apparently, Lupa, Marea, Babbo, Scarpetta are better, if not, equivalent restaurants and I strongly suggest you take a closer look at other options as I have a hard time believing at Ai Fiori provides the best for what you pay in NYC.
Good food, good service! Â Everything was prompt and delicious.

This has to be one of the best mexican food I've had. i would like to credit Yelp and my iPhone for helping me find this place. We were in the West village and needed a place for dinner and those two came to the rescue. We were seated immediately although it appears that reservations are highly recommended. We got there early enough and were able to get amazing margaritas for $5 as we had 15 minutes left until the end of happy hour. Margaritas were on point and rather strong.. Don't let the small size fool you. I ordered the veggie enchiladas with corn relish. I wish it had a little more corn but that is my only critique. My companions got the veggie quesadilla and the mussels. All four of us shared a plate of their soft fried plantains and cheese plate. All plates were clean at the end of dinner. We also shared a plate of guac and chips. Definitely the best guac I have ever had. Sorry Chipotle :) We finished off dinner with dessert. We shared the egg custard cake and the oreo cheesecake. Again plates were completely clean at the end of dessert. Ofrenda is HIGHLY recommended. The prices were not too horrible for NYC. We split the bill four ways and it ended up being about $45 per person including drinks. And three of us had two drinks each. I think getting the drinks during happy hour definitely helped with the price but overall I thought it was money well spent. I would DEFINITELY go back to Ofrenda the next time I am in the city.

The good food was only made more enjoyable knowing that we were spending so little. Â Very crowded little hole in the wall. Â There were less than 7 stools available to sit on...so not a good idea for large groups. Â I'd suggest that if you are with more than 2 ppl, that you figure out what you're going to order outside the restaurant, and send only one person in. Â The menu seemed to have changed; larger now. Â It took about 15 mins for the dumplings to cook, which seemed slower than before. Â Sesame pancake still one of the best I've had when fresh. Â It's like fried bread with banh mi filling. Â If you speak some form of Chinese, you should ask for it fresh and hot. Â Otherwise, this can be a crap shot. Â I had the duck and another time, the egg. Â I think I'd prefer the egg if it had not been cold. Â Both were very filling. Â Pork and chive dumplings were delish. Â Veggie dumplings, though good, do not compare. Â Shrimp dumplings were ok. Â I would recommend.

This may be my new favorite restaurant. I cannot believe this place has been open for two years and I didn't know about it. First of all, they have so many choices. And, as someone who is always on a diet, they actually have some great options that are basically low or no calories, even though they specialize in, get this....pigs feet! They have tons of authentic Japanese items, hot pots (which cook beautifully before your eyes from raw ingredients into an incredible stew), sashimi, really well priced sushi rolls, yummy salads, and the most delicious Japanese ice creams (even though I am on a diet, I love ice cream). It's a great place and a great value.

there is no reason to wait on line for mac&cheese at 12:30 am on a weeknight. Â  we watched other couples being let in ahead of us for 15 minutes, walked away and found a diner that was interested in taking our $. jerks.

Brunch from 10am - 4pm on WEEKDAYS? Winning! I came on a Thursday early afternoon in search of brunch after recovering from a grueling red eye from SF. And WOW, what an adorable little spot! I felt like I was walking into a little garden cottage. According to my friend, this place is packed on weekends, but on a Thursday around 1pm, it was fairly empty. At the recommendation of my friend, I ordered the Corned Beef Hash which was Beef Brisket with Potatoes and two Poached Eggs ($15). GET THIS. It didn't look large, but I was immensely full all day after devouring it all. I can't recommend this dish enough. Seriously, GET THIS. It was superb. The beef was extremely tender and flavorful, made all the better by the egg yolk from the poached egg. Heaven. Minus 1 Star because the prices were a bit high, in my opinion. Worth it though.

Definitely a divey, local diner type of place. They even have this super old-school register. Love it. They only have countertop seating and bring cash! I stopped by around 8:15am on my way back from the gym. They make omelettes to order, which are surprisingly healthy for a place that definitely looks like a greasy spoon. There wasn't too much butter used, thank goodness. I hate when my mouth feels like an oil slick from all the oil and butter most restaurants use. My vegetarian omelette was chock full of spinach, onions, tomatoes, and mushrooms. Almost a frittata in that there was a ton of vegetables, and the egg was just enough to bind it all together. Some people may not like that, but I was a fan. The guys who work there are really nice, and it's super cheap. They also have pierogis, french toast, pancakes, etc. Remember - cash only!

One of my favorite restaurants in the city so far. Â Went for Meatball Mondays and had the spaghetti and meatballs, which were absolutely divine, down to each hand made thick noodle. Â The meatballs were perfectly moist and well seasoned, the bread was delicious, and the warm buzz in the room didn't prevent us from hearing each other easily. Â There is a downstairs area that looks like it can be booked for larger parties too - which I may do in the future. Â Love this place.

Let me preface this review by saying that I'm a big fan of halal guys on 53rd & 6th. Â Now I've found new spot that is better! Â This place is the best chicken and rice, HANDS DOWN. Â I discovered this place last Thursday night and I went back the next night. Â If I was closer, I think I'd go every night. Â  Let's get to the food. Â The chicken has so much flavor to it. Â It's not dry at all. Â Usually, most halal carts add some lettuce and a piece of tomato. Â This place actually adds a 'real' salad including pickled veggies. Â And ask for the hot sauce. Â It's not overbearing hot but a good flavor to it.
Best food I have had in LIC! Small plates. Great lamb chops, tostadas, veal meatballs! Brunch is awesome! Kids eat free! Bottomless Mamosas and Bloodies. Â Clean, great staff, and fun vibe!

Visited again in the last evening at "Pommes Frites", Its was kind of spot check to evaluate my findings. I realized that this time potatoes sticks were really good according to the standard and sauces make is more delicious for me and it tasted hot till the end and i say at Pommes Frites you will he having combination of two: (Fries + Sauces) = Tasty and hot fries I agree previously i didn't get sauces and may be my first experience was bad due to it.

We were a party of three and visited just 90 min before the 3:30 pm closing time; the place was packed with 45 min waiting time. It was worth the wait though: the Akamaru Modern was delicious, my friends were all satisfied with their orders, the crepe cake was creamy (creamier than the one we've had at Hagi Sake Bar the other night), and the service was par excellent. Bear with the waiting time!

I made reservations for new years day ( thank god) and it was a good thing I did as it was packed. The burger was excellent and the fries equally as good. Very friendly service too and the servers were always there to top off our water or bring us coffee. To date, I have only done brunch here thus far. This is the second time I have been here and I will be back!
Had a fantastic bowl of Ramen here last night. My only complaint was that the portion was slightly too small; I wish I had ordered more chashu.

A great experience every time. Worth a trip for the Awwamis alone! The Middle Eastern staples (shawarma, hummus) weren't overly impressive, but the real dishes (Kibbeh tartare, fried Kibbeh, brussels sprouts, lamb meatballs, and the SEA BASS!) were absolutely delicious. I did a tasting menu here once and it was all over the place - seems best to decide for yourself what you want to sample. Awwamis for dessert are a non-negotiable must. Not great for anyone on a budget, but great for any adventurous eaters willing to pay a premium for something really great.
Four words. Duck. With. Flowering. Chive. Nuff' said.

Good and popular brunch spot, it's a little overhyped and the waits can be long even with a reservation but it's a solid brunch choice. The food was good but you could visit a few other places in the area of similar quality with less hassle

I found this place by chance walking around with a friend, and the moment we saw they made Japanese style crÃªpes we were hooked!
