What a fabulous find! Â This intimate wine bar is a little off the beaten path on 52nd Street between 10th and 11th, but well worth seeking out. Â The small plates are delicious, the atmosphere is warm and welcoming, and the service is perfect, smooth, accommodating, and unintrusive. After reading so many positive reviews, I had to check this place out myself. As you can see I gave The Thirsty Koala five well deserved stars. The service was on point. The drinks were delicious and the food was extremely fresh and pretty nice sized portions. My tummy was very full when I went home. This place by far beats many local places. I will definitely return for their Thanksgiving special. Why cook when you can enjoy fine dining at a very fair price. Thank you ")

I am not a person who eats only organic or who goes out of my way to recycle but the atmosphere at Bareburger certainly makes you see how relevant the latter is. Â From the materials in the bathroom to the signs that point out how much water the sink is saving you see how far out of the way they went to make their shops sustainable. Â The food was pretty good though I was a little annoyed my burger didn't come with lettuce and tomato. Â I got a run of the mill burger with minced pickles on top and some fries. Â The fries were pretty good but I wish they had a sweet potato option. Â I didn't notice a real difference in the organic fed burger but there was something nice knowing you weren't getting any chemicals. Â The restaurant was not crowded at all around 7:30p on a weekday night. Â The service was fine but nothing to celebrate. Â It was a quick stop on the way home and I left feeling like I wanted something with a little more taste. Â Maybe it all goes back to the lack of tomatoes.
The service was so bad that I did not stay to finnish my food. Â The manager was rude and obnoxious, so my party and I just got up and walked out.

Had the brisket, it was outstanding. A bit on the fatty side, but delicious. It's not as good as dinosaur bbq, but it's damn good. Warning, there can be a wait. Food is served cafeteria style. Great portions. The pomme frites are good too.

Thanks for the review. Â I ordered exactly what everyone posted. Â  Hainanese chicken Mee Saw Roti Canai It was really good. Â I'll definitely come back. The only negative thing about this restaurant is CASH ONLY.

When I first got to the there I had to wait a few minutes for a table. So I waited in the bar area which was a very tight area i remember it being hard for ppl to get by. I ordered a Martini which was extremely strong I wasn't able to drink it myself. For dinner I had the meat loaf which was the BEST meat loaf I ever had from a restaurant!! I also had the trio of Mac and cheese which was delicious. For desert I had my favorite fried Oreos which was also delicious. Service was fine I don't remember having any issues. For a my 1st time I enjoyed myself and the food was great, I definitely will be back a few more times.
Had a nice late lunch there today. Â Had the Tom Yum Soup with a salad and mushroom dumplings. Â All was exceptional and the service very good. Â Will definitely be back for more.

Mehhh... I don't know. My friends suggested Westville for dinner this past Friday, and after checking out the menu, it seemed pretty cool. However, I found it to be really underwhelming. High prices and small portions... but this is Manhattan. We were also extremely rushed... we didn't feel encouraged to order dessert or drinks or anything. Not sure why the waitresses didn't seem that keen on us being there. And there was hardly a wait this past Friday night. The grilled chicken entree was dry and barely flavored, but I admit I enjoyed the plantains and the pesto mashed potatoes. In fact I think if I ever come here again, I'll just get the sides. Other than that, there is nothing that unique about this restaurant. Brotip: definitely not worth the hour long subway ride.

LOVE this place. Really cool atmosphere, good food, friendly waitress, and the Jazz band on Saturdays is amazing! So far I've tried the mussels, artichoke, kale salad, cauliflower, mashed potatoes & pork - all delicious.

I have been to Walter Foods twice the first time I left thinking its was the best meal I have ever had in Williamsburg apart from Peter Luger's. Last night the food was so mediocre the chewiest, rubbery steak and the service was so lacking in personality or interest it was just BAD! I guess this place is inconsistent which mean I won't be rushing back anytime soon!

Came here on a Sunday night with my boyfriend on one of our very first dates. The place was fairly packed and they sat us in the little 2 person bamboo-type bench so we had a view of pretty much the entire teahouse -- made me feel as if we were sitting in a big stationary swing in someone's Japanese garden. The service was SUPER friendly and attentive. The decor was so cute. I ordered a pot of the Yinzhen Silver needle (white tea) and my boyfriend ordered one of the blooming teas (can't remember which one). We also split an order of the green tea and chocolate mochi (2 were green tea, one was chocolate). This was my first time having mochi and it was so yummy with the tea! We stayed and enjoyed our tea and talked for maybe 2 hours... I think we had the best seat in the house! Everything was great about Cha-An and I would highly recommend it for anyone who loves tea.
great atmosphere and friendly workers!!! excellent choices on condiments!! Great burger and great hotdogs!! must try!!! BREAKROOM BURGER!!! GREAT CHEAP BURGER SUPER SATSIFYING!
I came in with low expectations for this place. I left craving for more! Delicious food and great ambiance. Will come back again. Had the "fish" wrap and potatoes with the spicy mayo ( mind blowing)

My favorite restaurant hands down! My friends and I have been coming here for over 5 years. Im kinda obsessed with the avgolemono and will get 2 bowls. Love those crunchy breads. The mint lemonade is perfect in the summer.
Pricy! but food was good!

I was in love last night as Gaia Italian CafÃ©. Perhaps it might be no problem to drop Â several Â hundred dollars here. I could not but buying a book. This is a nice thing that I am one of the fun of the Gaia Italian CafÃ© bookstore. The bookstore also is an outstanding assortment of books , art , zines and DVD as you will be attracted . Each time while I pass by Gaia Italian CafÃ© I can not but enjoy their arrangement.

Minus the odd hipster walking in for a go bag between wakes and bakes, this place serves a very, very Chinese clientele. Which is usually a good thing. There were only a couple other people here on a very late Saturday afternoon. We got two large orders of dumplings ($3 each gets you a baker's dozen or so), which, while seemingly redoubtable at the start, we ably scarfed up. The dumplings were quite good, but I'm not quite ready to crown them the NYC champs. This place is good for dumpling enthusiasts and ideal for takeout. I rarely comment on these things, but it was not exactly top shelf in terms of decor and there were large flies buzzing around.

All of his Tamil food is so good that you don't have to know that most of it is vegan (lassis aren't a traditional Tamil drink, and they are what hold up the menu from being entirely vegan). Â (Pro-tip: Most Tamil food naturally falls in the vegan category.) Â Thiru makes everything on the spot. Â And he remembers all of his customers (and he has a lot of regulars). Â He has offered a viably edible vegan option to the NYU / E. Village area, and his faithful vegetarian & vegan clientele have gotten him to become vegan too.

Bar Bruno, what to say. Â The positive: decor and ambiance are great. Cozy little restaurant, sort of an American bistro with art on the walls, small little tables, and a coat rack to boot. The music is splendid, and the crowd is a nice, diverse set of people from around the neighborhood. The service is spot on; there was only about two waitresses and one bartender and they worked very hard to keep customers fed and happy. The most vital part of any restaurant besides running their operation smoothly is their food. Bar Bruno's food was absolutely terrible from start to finish. My wife ordered the burger which wasn't cooked to temperature as it was completely over done, dry, and tasted like cardboard. I ordered the skirt steak, which although was cooked right, it was way over salted and killed my palate. The french fries were standard, formerly frozen, they're the same thing you'd get at any local diner. Having said this, the prices are outrageously high for the quality of food received. Â If you're a business that's trying to keep up with the other restaurants nearby, i.e., Prime Meats, Dubuque, Buttermilk Chanel, Fragole, you have to USE quality ingredients. You can't charge top dollar for abominable, tasteless food - period. Simply put, I will not be returning to this restaurant unless serious changes are made to their menu and their quality of ingredients. I do however, hope they succeed, as I hope all small businesses in the neighborhood succeed. Â Having said that, Bruno needs to stop fooling their customers with a nice decor and warm atmosphere, and concentrate their energy on producing quality food.

We had reservations but they were backed up so we had to wait 30 min for a table. Â The service wasn't great and after raving about the mussels, the waiter comes back to tell us it is not avail nor were the scallops i wanted. Â The food was subpar, cheese fries were cold. Â 2 of our dishes were much too salty. Â Although edible not worth the price. Â We were 3 girls who had no wine, and a 30% discount off bill and we still paid $50 a person.

What a little Thai gem! Â Certainly one of the hippest neighborhood Thai food joints around, with it's mod interior and weekend DJ. Â There's almost always a wait if you get there after 7pm, even on a Tuesday (45 minutes on a Saturday)! Â But the food and the prices make it worth the wait! Â Cheap drinks at the bar help pass the time too! Â My Thai dad would question the authenticity since they automatically set the table with chopsticks, but my true test of a good Thai restaurant: Â the Pad See Ew. Â And I'll tell ya, Joya did not disappoint! Â Even my dad might forgive them for the chopstick thing! Â The massaman curry was tasty too. Â One would think that a non-hole-in-the-wall Thai place would mean more expensive food. Â Not true at Joya! Â 4 people who ordered 2 apps, 2 drinks & 4 entrees - with a generous tip - paid a total of $60!! Â It's almost like eating in Thailand!!

EAT HERE. very good italian food for amazing prices ($10 for a great serving size of pasta post tax). i tried the artichoke appetizer, gramigna, and the tagliatelle, and all were very good and so reasonably priced that the bottle of prosecco ($33) ended up being the greater half of the bill. seek this restaurant out even if you don't live in this area - it's probably the best italian food for the least amount of money. TIPS - CASH ONLY - make reservations for larger parties - however you can usually can walk in for smaller groups after 930 for only a few minutes wait - wine list seemed pretty good (prosecco was fine, not amazing but not bad), but they only serve certain wines by the glass and don't do half bottles - definitely recommend everything i had above (also the lasagna, which looked amazing) - pastas are very generous with the meat, and also rather generous with the sauce, which thankfully is lighter in flavor and good to dip bread in as well - atmosphere is a bit cramped and stuffy
very nice..

When possible and within budget I always try to go organic. And when you have a boyfriend that has a gluten sensitivity - places like this are a godsend! Surrounded by colorful storefronts and restaurants, Bareburger is easy to look over but to do so is such a waste. The interior of Bareburger is very cozy and inviting with a mixture of wooden panels and exposed brick walls. Although it appears small, the restaurant has a few private booths, some raised benches that allow for larger parties, a few tables for smaller parties and individual seating. Their menu is awesome, everything here is organic and natural with a ton of gluten free options (with everything clearly marked). Don't let the name fool you their menu consists of much more than burgers they also have a variety of sides, salads sandwiches. Clearly though - their burgers win! They have a laundry list of pre-made burgers with all the fixings, if you go with this option you can customize your protein and your bun (gluten free, brioche, a wrap, on a salad - you choose). They have recommendations for the best protein pairings but don't let that stop you from exploring the menu! The usual beef and turkey patties are available but for the adventurous they have exotic meats such as elk, bison, goat and even wild boar! There is also the option of building your own burger where you can basically build your burger from scratch with cool gourmet items like duck bacon and cauliflower humus! Unfortunately the burgers don't come with french fries but they do have the option of regular and sweet. I unfortunately am not adventurous and went with the original burger with a wild boar patty with a brioche bun. The patty was juicy and flavorful, not gamey like I had imagined. It had the usual cheese, lettuce, tomato, onion and special sauce - absolutely delicious. For you gluten free peeps, everything on the menu that is gluten free is clearly marked. All of their meats are gluten free and the seasoned/flavored proteins are marked if they are gluten free. While the burgers seem a little pricey but lets just think a bit about what you are paying for - organic options and grass fed meats its worth it. Another fun fact, Bareburger has quite a few accolades - since 2011 they have received Michelin recommendations AND have been rated the Best Burger in NYC by Zagat each year. Just go try it!

What a cool concept - a supermarket and several restaurants all at the same place! All fresh and top of the line products, hand made pastas, fresh breads, and freshly sliced and butchered meats. I love grabbing a glass of wine, some cheese, and salamis from the appetizer bar, then walking around the supermarket with my glass of wine while waiting for a dinner table at one of the other restaurants. The only reason I didn't give this place 5 stars is because it is very very pricey. This is a "once-every-few-months" type of place for me, but I fully enjoy myself each time. This is also a great place to take visitors or out of town guests for a fancy night out.
Much ado about nothing. Â I did enjoy their regular red slice but not the wait. Â Get your logistics together. Â Creating an artificial line by delaying the production is not worthy of people's time.

Amazing Pizza! I have heard many great things about the pizza here and its definitely delicious! I would recommend and have recommended this place. I have also heard this is the best Pizza in NYC? I wouldn't argue with that! Definitely try out. The food was great, service was GREAT and there were MANY people waiting outside. If my review doesn't convince you, let the swarm of people waiting to eat the pizza convince you!

This small tapas bar in the E. village serves up some pretty tasty food. Â You walk in, and it looks exactly like a bar with a full bar to your left and various tables surrounding. Â The workers were all nice and friendly, Â The pitcher of sangria was only $20 and you have 4 or 5 different flavors to choose from, and best of all it was a full pitcher. Â We tried around 6 or 7 things, all were good. Â Definitely a solid place if you are in the mood for some tapas and cheap drinks.

This place is tiny, tiny but the food is yummy, yummy! I order lunch from there like 3 times a week. They have great pasta dishes, panini & salad. The pappardelle with the sausage is my favorite, but i also love the prosciutto & mozzarella panini is my close second. I have also had the Calamari & black ink pasta and the chicken milanese...so good! I guess I'm working my way down the menu. ..thank god for cardio!

Okay I grew up in Saudi Arabia and I used to eat Shawarma's Every single day, and when I moved back to America I could never find a shawarma that compared. When I tried Oasis I was pleasantly surprised. It was the closest thing I had ever tasted and although its not EXACTLY the same it is damn close!! .. their shawarma's are sooo flavorful and their hot sauce isn't just hot its packed with so much flavor and they are just 5 bucks.. I mean come on!! who can beat that. I ALWAYS stop by and grab one every time I pass this place. A must visit and a must eat for anyone!
Quality pizza, but there was a long wait for it.

I have to admit that I had been dying to go this place. Â I like ramen and I especially like genuine ramen. Â Ippudo has been getting all the latest raves and reviews, from foodies to chefs alike, and they have been consistently good. So, I came here and waited the signature 2 hours to get into a New York restaurant that is currently all the rage. Â Be aware that they do not take resevations. Â However, if you go in person and give them your name, they will give you a wait time and you can come back. Â For restaurants with extremely long wait times like Ippudo, it is good to do this early and then go and take a stroll. Once I get in with my girlfriend, we are so starved that we actually proceed to order half the menu and sample a bottle of sake too. Â Everything is consistently good, just as previous reviewers have said. Â Good, but not fantastic. Â I would skip the appetizers (they are standard asian fusion fare) and go straight for the ramen. Â The service is attentive, but at times, rushed because literally, there are about 100 people waiting for your small seat. Â The dining room is a mixture of Japanese steakhouse-like communal seating and private tables. Â It is a good place to go with a fellow foodie or a friend, but not so much for a first date if you are looking to impress. Â  I did not come out of Ippudo feeling so completely wowed that I was dying to go back right away. Â However, I also did not come out feeling jipped for the long wait. Â The food is good, the wait is long, the service is thorough but rushed, the hostesses are a sea of calm in the chaos and it is a good place to hang out with friends before hitting a bar but not for a lingering date. Â So there.

We walked in without a reservation for an early dinner and decided to sit outside. The beautiful hostess greeted us warmly and made us feel welcome. We all ordered cocktails that took a while to get to the table, but were well worth it once they did. Try the watermelon mint drink, very refreshing . The service was attentive and polite, very professional. I wish I remembered the waiters name. The food was good, not great, I felt the portions were a little too small. When we were almost done with our meal it started to rain and we moved inside by the bar. Some of our food got wet and we lost our drinks in the storm. The manager noticed we lost our drinks and insisted that he send us a round at the bar. This wasnt necessary , we told him that he didn't make it rain and we chose to sit outside. He brought us to the bar,made room for us and told the bartender to take care of us. We appreciated all the pampering and will be back.
The Brussel Sprout Caesar was to die for. Overall great meal and definitely worth many repeat visits.

DON'T GO HERE! SERVICE IS TERRIBLE AND THE WAIT STAFF IS RUDE. First time here tonight - I went to go pick up pizza that I had ordered. As soon as I walk in, I am hit IN THE HEAD by one of the servers (description: tall, pony tail blonde, oafish mid-30s male) Â who is carrying a tray with food on it. After the waiter drops off the food and comes back my way, I expect him to apologize for almost knocking me unconscious. Instead, he tells me not to stand where I was standing. ARE YOU KIDDING ME? I'm standing by the door in your cramped pizza restaurant. Where else do you want me to be? Outside in the rain? He didn't even have the decency to apologize or show any remorse. The manager/owner who witnessed the whole situation didn't seem to care either. Sorry, but the dining/take-out experience was ABYSMAL. Not to mention, the pizza was MEDIOCRE AT BEST. Never going back here again! You're lucky I'm not pressing charges for assault. OVERRATED!

Great local spot with lots of craft beers. The beers on tap constantly change which is nice for people looking to try new things. There isn't much like this bar up here, so I'm very happy they moved in. I think they have a small outdoor area, but since it has been cold I doubt it has gotten much use. The layout is a little funky and there isn't a large open space for people to congregate. Very cool place, good beer, good prices, happy they moved in.

Place was recommended, very happy we decided to eat here for lunch. Since it was a weekend the wait was very long, but it was work it! We ordered the 'Le Grand' which is a two tiered shell fish platter. Shrimp, muscles, clams, oysters, periwinkle snails, half lobster and fries. It was amazing!! You can easily can be shared between 4 people. For dessert we got Creme BrÃ»lÃ©e and also Apple tart tatin. Both were very flavorful and not too rich. Again, easily can be shared. My favorite was the Creme BrÃ»lÃ©e. Great for groups, special occasions, staff is very helpful and great ambience. I would definitely come again next time I'm in NYC.

Chicken and gyro mix. Extra EXTRA white sauce, Extra Extra Extra hot sauce. They give you a lot so technically it's enough to share, but who would want to anyway? This is just one little review among the thousand 5 stars. Â Remember, there are 3-4 locations just across the street from each other, and they're ALL the halal guys. Â Don't make the noobie mistake of going to the longest line because they're all the same place, just different corners. Â But don't mistaken, there's only ONE (or 3) Halal Guys and you can only get it at this corner. Don't get the imposters. It's NOT the same, AND they don't give you as much either.

I love and appreciate the variety of carefully crafted dishes on their menu. Each item is a collection of interesting pieces that seem to honor the season as well as nutritional value and flavor. I enjoyed my cheddar bacon sandwich, which they added an egg onto, LOVED the french fries and appreciated the salad. I was very curious about so many other items on the menu that I would love to go back to try more. This is the kind of place where I would be more than comfortable trying something I've never had before or even something I may have decided that I have not liked in the past.
yeah... what the other yelpers said. AMAZING. WOW. however you want to put it. best $6 I've ever spent... times two. because i went back the next night. then i hit the gym.

My little bee - you buzz in my ear and tell me things - tell me of spring and of tiny treats to enjoy. Waffles and such. Mul Frit in the evening. Omelets for lunch. I don't know about the other locations, but I do like this one - especially the Tintin posters on the inside. The food it is tasty, the coffee even better. Â A good place to have a bite. To sit and talk awhile. It is not cheap but it had a character to it I admired.

AMAZING DESSERTS. A little expensive, but so worth it. We picked up four and sat outside, away from the crowd of the restaurant, which I would recommend. After enjoying the perfection of their innovative little treats, I am pretty intent on coming back to try the food. There seems to be a real (and rare) artistry here.

Tonight was the time for a Villagio premiere and they passed with flying colors. I ordered a Mozzarella Burrata as an appetizer: it was excellent with a decent tasty piece of mozzarella and good Prosciutto on the side. I was really happy with it. The main course consisted of a Fettuccini Alfredo with grilled chicken: again a great dish, well cooked pasta and a tasty delicious sauce. The chicken was excellently grilled and very tender with a very fine taste. My friend ordered a Linguine Nettuno, which was a great dish as well: tasty salmon, shrimps and fine tomato sauce. The dessert was an Italian cheesecake, again very tasty and good. The price was very decent, especially considering the location and quality of the food. There are a couple of over priced venues in the area and it is easy to think that Villagio suffers from the same syndrome but no, they offer a great value for the money. In fact so great that I don't see a lot of viable options close by besides Petrossian or Porter House (TWC) for different cuisine, though and also a different price category. Â  The only detail to notice is that the internal noise level can be a bit on the high side, mostly due to the acoustics of the room. Because of this, candlelight dinners aren't the strength of Villagio - for those, other establishments such as Petrossian are better. I would say that the pasta dishes is where Villagio shines: they are the best value. Some appetizers are almost the same price as a pasta dish, which can be worth to note: in comparison with the main courses and desserts, they can be a bit on the high side of the price scale. I recommend this restaurant warmly.

Only opened 5 weeks ago, according to our hostess. There are a few kinks to work out. My guest's chair headpiece came off when he moved to bring it out from under the table, but they had apparently just received a replacement batch of a different construction. The waitress didn't seem to know the menu very well, but I assume that will be fixed soon. The food was good for brunch and it's a very curious concept to bring asian flavors to brunch. Their chicken wings and waffles were pretty decent; however, the waffle itself was a bit heavy and not as crisp as it should have been. I would have liked to see a more boneless piece of chicken used instead of the wings with the tips still attached. The porridge was quite amazing. I was very impressed with the flavors of the mixins. Everything was well seasoned and the water spinach was very well cooked. The unique flavors of every condiment made this a great dish, but they should probably take away the giant wood tree chunk it's served on. Our waitress was barely able to lift it. It's just gimmicky... Overall, I will definitely return. It's a good location, just a block or two from union square. I hope this place survives.

I think this place deserves a lot of credit: they cook on induction, small footprint, lots of glass and views of them cooking, the risotto is very good and everyone I could see was keeping their "cool." Can't think of a better place to grab a beer and some rice, "Italian" style.

Get ready to wait (and wait and wait) but its fully worth it. Everything is perfectly prepared. The steak is delicious and the sides are amazing. I recommend the truffle fried mashed potatoes as a must but everything was wonderful. The grilled tomato and burrata was an unexpected but delicious surprise. The wait is often 2 hours but can sometimes be 3 hours so go early, out your name in, and grab some drinks next door.

This is one of the best Italian places that I've ever tried. Â Period. We came here in a group of 4 at 11PM on a Sunday evening, and surprisingly, it was still busy with tables. Â We started off with prosciutto di parm (carne) and Escarole, walnuts, red onion & pecorino (insalate) as appetizers. Â The insalate was huge enough for all 4 of us to share. Â I ordered the ricotta gnocchi with sausage and fennel, which was great, but I took a bite of my boyfriend's spaghetti aglio e olio and it was amazing -- it was spicy and flavorful. Â For dessert, we ordered biscotti and vino dolce (pretty much biscottis with a small glass of riesling) and I had a bite of my friend's grapefruit sorbet, which were both good desserts. Everything was fairly priced and I would love to try Lupa again the next time I go to the city.

Came here on my most recent trip to NYC because of all the raves i've heard about this place. We waited for 1.5 hrs in the cold and rain. I am not complaining about the wait since it is NYC and a lot of popular joints have at least up to 2 hrs wait time. I can't really say it was worth the wait for me. I mean it was good, no complaints there, but it wasn't GREAT! The portion, price, and broth were just average... nothing spectacular... Well, at least I can cross off this place on my list of must try places~

I stopped by recently when I was in the neighborhood. I moved to Queens and never go here much, but I was pleasantly surprised with the new menu. Who knew you could raise real live water buffalo in NY? I ordered it and ate it. Delicious. Who knew that sardines could actually taste GOOD and not like those fetid things in a can? Wow, the grilled sardines were so fresh and savory. But the crown jewel was a dish of deliciously seared razor clams, pork belly, and caviar on top of butter. It's like the surf and turf dreams are made of!
Beware of the super hot spicy sauce! Try the rice with a combination of chicken, lamp and falafel. Definitely different from any Halal I have had on the street.
YUMM Sangria rocked. Service was so= so... granted it was packed. Great menu and food... highly recommend it We dont remember what we ate.. but we know we loved it!!! :)

I wouldn't recommend to go for a good fish to the Fish. One hour waiting. Excellent Kumomotos Overcooked (almost fried(( red snapper. Sent it back. Tough scallops. At least I could eat them. Crab cake was delicious but with too much mayonnaise. Too much salt and butter. Next time i will have just kumomotos and a reservation.

i come here for two reasons and two reasons only. 1) everything is simple, delicious and impeccably prepared. 2) i shamelessly wait for eric ripert* to breeze through the door for his yakitori fix. as a poor grad student, the only hitch was that when i came here with one of my college buddies, we racked up an insane yakitori tab in the blink of an eye. Â it was definitely worth it, but it would have just been even more worth it if we had encountered that breezy mister ripert. Â yeap, still shameless. ordered: thigh and scallion. chicken skin. gizzard! chicken oyster! skirt steak. some vegetable ones. but yea no really, if ripert frequents this joint, how can it not be a winner? *eric ripert = le bernardin

Do all good things get ruined in this city? On my second visit, after they expanded to meet the demand, I got the hearth broth again which was a lot more watery and less flavorful. Â Totally not worth $7. Maybe it was an off day, but either way, I'll stick to making my own broth from now on.
What this place lacks in poetic culinary techniques, it more than compensates with o'bay and garlic.

A pricy choice in this Brooklyn area. But the ramen and appetizers worth the price. The signature Miso ramen is not bad at all comparing to any other famous Ramen in Manhattan. But their special ramen might be too "creative" sometimes. I tried one cold ramen with bacon and cheese and couldn't really appreciate it.

Great place! Ordered the Swiss burger and it was delicious, big, and filled up my stomach since I was STARVING! However the location is in an odd spot next to a cemetery so be sure not to get lost on your way back! The service was great! The waitress who served us looked happy with what she was doing and asked us if we needed anything. The drinks were soooo good and refreshing. One star off because I wasn't quite satisfied with the desert I had which was the waffle with the ice cream on top. The place itself is quite cute, it looks like one of those 1950s diners you see in movies where there are little stools. Will definitely come back but maybe in another location!
OUT-standingly cheap, tasty, and pretty but awesome all around. (also, strikingly friendly for a real china-town experience)

Came here with a friend when he had a travel budget from work, because as much as I try to deny it I am still on the broke-ass college student struggle bus in my post-grad life. Made last minute reservations on Open Table the day of and could only get a 10pm. I called and tried to sweet-talk the hostess into bumping it up to 9pm, we dualed and called it a truce at 9:30. Why then, Ms. Hostess, did you almost end up giving my table to the reservation-less couple ahead of me in line? There were also 5 empty tables by the time 9:45 rolled around. Â  Here's a review of our dinner menu- Beef Carpaccio - the very definition of classy and trashy, there was a Jenga-style presentation of french fries covered in fancy-mayo on top of a bed of shaved raw beef. The contrasting textures of the meat and the fries was wonderful and the flavors delicious (def: fries weren't dripping in oil but weren't soggy and limp). but I fail to see how it could have satisfied a whole table of 2+ as an appitizer. Pan Roasted Chicken - Reasonable serving (at least a quarter of the chicken), that achieved the difficult task of even-distribution of flavor throughout the meat without being dry. I wished I had ordered a full side of corn because the sprinkle that came with the chicken was DELICIOUS. Spiced Long Island Duck - The winner of the evening, the duck tasted vaguely smoked and the serving size was generous (~3 large hunks of meat w/ bone). I didn't expect the poached fruits that came alongside the meat but the contrast between savory and sweet was great. Serving size is definiately a big positive to this restaurant; while portions aren't oversized, each of the entrees was enough to leave one feeling full, which has not been the case at other similiar farm to table restaurants I've visited. Service was also solid with a waiter who clearly understood and enjoyed the food. The Californian in me is always skeptical of farm-to-table restaurants on the East Coast, but this place does it right.

when i first moved to the city, i read about pommes frites somewhere and made it my mission to find it. Â i worked in chelsea at the time, so after work i took the c, e train to 14th, took the l over to 3rd, and wandered around in circles in the lower east side (and at one point ended up in alphabet city) for about 45 minutes trying to figure out which direction i was walking. Â it was cold, dark and 8pm but i finally found pommes frites (and realized i had walked past it about 3 times). *cue heavenly music* it was SO worth the wandering! Â fries with mayo are one thing, but PF fries with all those different kinds of mayo is another. Â vietnamese pineapple & sweet mango chutney are my favorites and i heard they have new sauces now. i went back once a week for about a month after that. Â oh sweet bliss.

I was looking for a nice dinner for a birthday. Â The atmosphere seemed very intimate and the food looked good so I figured I'd check it out. Â We started with a platter of the La Tor cheese and crackers and a bottle of wine suggested by the waiter - a 2012 dry, crisp white wine. Â For the life of me, I can't remember what kind, but it was $65 for the bottle - which was pretty good value since you get about 6 glasses per bottle. Â  We got the hamachi tartare to start. Â The hamachi fish was delicious and saturated in a lemon juice and paired with thinly sliced red grape. Â The red grape really helped ease the bite of the sour lemon juice. Â I wasn't too thrilled on how much lemon they used, but it was not a bad crudo dish to start with. Â I've previously been here and had the beef carpaccio, which I believe is a much better alternative, although a bit on the salty side. We opted for the Pici pork ragu pasta, which I thought was the best dish of the night. Â The chewy al dente noodles were cooked perfectly. Â The pork ragu was very flavorful without being overwhelming. We ended our meal by choosing to share the Hanger Steak cooked at a medium rare. Â In my opinion, this was a better steak than what I've gotten at Peter Luger. Â It's also a different cut of steak, but overall, I think the flavors and texture was much better. Â The potatoes served on the side were crispy on the outside and had excellent flavor. Overall, I really loved this place. Â I really wanna come back to try more of their pastas, which seem to be more of their forte than their meat and fish selection.

The pork-and-cabbage dumplings here are my favorite combination of substantially chewy wrapper and perfectly seasoned/mixed stuffing. Â I have no words, only an appetite for the sesame pancake. Totally unrelated to the rating or "the dining experience": the bathroom has an AMAZING amount of graffiti on it.

Did I really just pay $7 for a bottle of Brooklyn beer at MSB? Yes. Yes I did. And I'm ashamed. I'm ashamed I paid nearly $125 (including tax and tip) for our dinner for two for food that was good, not great, and but a single beer per person. Clearly value is not one of the MSB's strong points. The food is all well-prepared, but the experience falls short. Beer served in bottles? Napkins stacked high on the table with the chopsticks? Sure, in a dive it works, but in a restaurant where a $23 entree is on the low end, the charmlessness falls flat. Dont' get me wrong - we liked our food. The chawanmushi with snails was unexceptional, but at least the custard wasn't overcooked. The roasted mushroom salad was exceptionally tasty, and we both adored it and wished for seconds. The calamari salad was fun to eat and had an entertaining variety of onions, pickled. We enjoyed the crab claws but found them difficult to eat without shellfish forks. Our branzino was tasty, slightly overcooked, and the oil-based sauce was interesting but not exceptional. Perhaps we didn't enjoy it as much as carnivores because we avoided pork, offal, and other meats. But service is service, value is value, and the MSB just fell short on the latter.

If you love Mexican and French food as much as I do, you will love this restaurant. Â This is definitely not the place for someone who is lukewarm for either cuisine. Â This is for serious Frexican lovers. Â We had the guac, the mini raviolis, the roast chicken and the hanger steak, all of which were delicious. Â Yes, the service is a bit slow, but we came in at 10 pm and weren't looking to rush our meal anyway. Â Everyone was super nice and attentive. Â We will absolutely be back because there is so much to try!
The long wait is totally worth it, best ramen I had in NYC. But the pork buns are to die for. If you go you must order the pork buns

Came in on a whim after walking in the area and seeing their sign outside for happy hour sushi entailing $3 rolls. The sushi and avocado roll was simple, well crafted, and delicious. My Vegetable fried Gyoza could have been better but they brought my very picky friend extra ginger dressing, spicy mayo and tempura crunch with a smile. The service was very nice and attentive and they let you BYOB. Will definitely come back!

I always think of Thai food as being healthy, with nice fresh flavors of cilantro, lime, and ginger, and usually in a nice, relaxing setting. Â Well, you won't find those flavors or any peace here. The pad thai is so greasy, not in a sesame greases way, but saturated in a cheap, bland oil without any basic flavors. Â Really foul! Â The veggies in red coconut sauce weren't bad, but not worth going back for. Â I'd rather spend more money for a better meal.
Excellent service, very clean interior and Amazingly fresh and delicious sushi- one of the BEST sushi restaurants in NYC

Was pleasantly surprised by this little gem. Great Matzo Ball Soup and a perfect Tuna Salad (something about avocado, red onions, sweet balsamic vinaigrette, and arugula...) I'll be sure to visit again when I'm in the city! :)

Came here with the boyfriend for the burger. We were here early, maybe 5:00 ish, and there was Â a wait though plenty of tables were open. This reminds me a little bit of Umami where they strategically make customers wait to generate lines and hype. Not a fan of this practice. I think the best way to describe this burger is "grown up". The blue cheese is very powerful to say the least, and seeing as I'm not a fan of blue cheese, I was not a fan of this burger. The brioche bun was perfect as was the marbling of the patty itself. I understand that the blue cheese is the focus of the burger's flavor, but I think the patty could have used more seasoning or at least some salt for the love of god. In contrast, the shoestring fries were awesome. Crispy, well seasoned, oily perfection. I loved them. Won't be back :(

With superb pasta and a truly outstanding selection of salume, Lupa is one of the better Italian restaurants near Washington Square Park. While the food is certainly excellent, the customers here are packed in to an almost uncomfortable proximity and dessert is decidedly an afterthought. However, if having elbow room and good dessert is not on your 'must' list for restaurants, definitely head here for a great dinner. I have probably eaten at Lupa about six times and each time was very good. As for pasta, the Ricotto Gnocchi is probably the best, closely followed by the Carbonara. For secondi I have to recommend the Pollo Alla Diavola. It is peppery, comes with a great jus, and has this piece of bread with chicken liver spread on it that alone makes the dish worth ordering. As for the salumi (or "carne" as it appears on the menu) there is only one way to go: the house-made Coppa Cotta!! Oh man. So, so, so awesome. Unless you are lucky enough to be seated in the back room, get ready for one loud, cramped, and fairly dark dinner. I am aware this is an Osteria-style restaurant, so I guess that is part of the Romanesque atmosphere. Anyway, don't bother with dessert. They are all pretty mediocre. Kee's Chocolates and Dominique Ansel are both walking distance, however, so the dessert issue is not really a problem. If you go to Kee's for dessert try the creme brulee truffles and if you go to Dominique try the wwayyyyy underrated Frozen Smores. Anyway Lupa is awesome. While Babbo and Scarpetta might be more solid five-star locations, for the price it is difficult to do much better.

This cute and cozy wine bar is the perfect place to spend a romantic evening out. They have an extensive beer and wine selection with very knowledgeable staff. It is a little pricey, but then again it's Midtown... You can still find a nice wine and beer there within $10-$15.

So after reading so many good reviews here on Yelp about this place (and after dreaming of some good dumplings for so many months) I finally came here with my bf. We came on a Tuesday night and it was pretty empty,aside from another couple who came in seconds after us. I thought "Great! No lines!". But it just so happens that they don't make small batches of the FRIED dumplings..which were the ones I wanted. They only make them if your buying a lot Â or I guess if there is a lot of people there,so we ended up having to get the boiled/steamed ones. Anyway, we proceeded to order. My bf and I each got 10 pork and chive dumplings and a beef sesame beef pancake. The sesame beef pancake is no longer $1 as I had read before...they are actually $1.75. Still not a bad price. Before leaving the place, we doused our dumplings in some soy sauce and enjoyed them while walking. Since its cold in NY right now and it just snowed,the benches in the park across the street were cold and wet so we didn't opt to sit in the park. But we will when we go back some time in the Spring or Summer (because we certainly will make another trip back). In conclusion, the meal was delicious, satisfying, and cheap..just as I expected :) 20 dumplings + 2 sesames beef pancakes = $7.50 How can u beat that?!

I love this place! Been coming here for a little over a year. It def can pack a crowd so get there early to enjoy the place before its packed and i mean PACKED. Food is great, Lychee martinis are just freaking awesome. Im here atleast twice a month. I love it that much

I miss this place... Â I used to live across the street in Stuytown and being Filipino, it was the closest place I ever came to having home cooked meals like my mom used to make. Â While living there, I used to stop by once a month, so I've just about have had everything on the menu and not once have been upset about what I ordered. Add on the fact the staff is very friendly (been quite a few times where the owner and myself would sit talking like we were old friends and even on occasion shared food.) Â Out of all the Filipino places I tried in the area, hands down the best.

I wonder if this place has become a New York staple for burgers. Â Is the Shake Shack to New York like the Inn & Out Burger to California?! Â It was unfortunate for my boyfriend who was too sick to eat anything watch me eat my burger. Â I got the ShackBurger which comes with a special shack sauce. All the burgers have the option of being ordered as a single or a double aside from the shroom burger (veggie) and the shack stack which are the mini burgers. Â I had to have a shake because of the namesake, so I got the caramel shake which was delicious! Â I am not sure if it's because I hadn't had one in so long that it was so good, but I think it was that dang good! Â The prices were okay, and the service was quick and efficient. Â They also have hotdogs, frozen custard, booze, and food for dogs too! Â I liked the outdoor seating area here at Battery Park, it's not as scenic since it is on the outskirts of the financial district - but it was just nice to be outside.

Long wait, slow turnover of tables, nearly absent server... but the burgers are just impossible to describe. My group ordered the unlisted/off-menu cheesy tots, which are pretty dense. Maybe if your mother always used to pack you a brown-bagged lunch and the only moment you felt jealous towards our school lunches were the tater tots we guarded, maybe then you'll think the Umami version is somehow special. Otherwise, they weren't very good. As for the burgers, I really don't think you can go wrong with the traditional red meat patty. I've been three times and ordered the Original (parmesan crisp, shiitake mushroom, roasted tomato, caramelized onions, house ketchup), not because I get comfortable with one thing and do not like to branch out (the second time I went to Umami, I actually split a California burger with two friends after finishing my first, and it was equally amazing), but because the Original is just pure and delicious. To be honest I really dislike mushrooms, but I keep them on this burger because the proprietors know what they are doing here. I highly recommend trying this place out. The taste is so perfect that I can overlook almost anything else.

Say it with me now: brunch, devils on horseback (bacon wrapped dates, toasted), artichoke dip. As in: go to Freemans for Brunch, get the devils on horseback & artichoke dip, and pick one of their generously portioned main courses and you'll be able to enjoy the taxidermy-inspired setting and the company you came in with to your heart's content. Don't get me wrong, Freemans' dinner is good (the dip and dates are on the dinner menu after all), but of the 3 times I went for dinner, I've always wished I went for Brunch instead. Note: first come, first served unless your party is six people or larger. Â Brunch goes till 4pm on weekends.

was not a fan of the over-salted asparagus-calamari noodle dish. Â generally the flavors were really heavy and overwhelming, not subtle enough for my taste, including the kabocha fries. Â perhaps we ordered the wrong things... I did like the coconut drink with chunks of fresh coconut flesh, so thus the redeeming second star.

Came here with my sister and brother in law, awhile back, after see the Rockettes. I don't think this place is anything amazing, or out of the ordinary. You get decently good food and portions- I ordered the tuna melt- and it fills your belly and you enjoy it enough. Would i flock here though, every time I head into the city? No, I think it's almost on par with a fancy quality diner. The cheesecakes are good, Â in terms of the filling, but I always love crust on my cheesecake to balance out the variety of flavors, so for me it wasn't that good, but it's a personal preference, not a reflection on their food.

I love this place! I called them about an hour before on a Saturday night trying to get in for dinner with a group of 6 people. They said it was busy, but they would try their best to accommodate us. I mentioned that one of the people in the party was elderly (my grams!) and they said that they definitely didn't want her to wait, so if we could be there in a 30 minutes, they would hold a table for us. We ended up being there in more like an hour because my grandmother isn't as quick as she used to be, and they immediately sat us at a big table in the back. I was so sure they would have given our table away as the place was packed, but they honored our reservation ..even though we were late! So impressive. Everyone was so warm and friendly, and the food was delicious! I had the pasta with walnut pesto (I don't even like pesto, and I loved this!) The best was their tomato salad with potatoes and greens. The overall vibe of this place was just so warm and cozy, lit up by candles- we all felt so at home. I would highly recommend this place to anybody looking for a cozy, quaint, no frills rustic italian spot!

Nai tapas is my local favorite, I have gone back at least 5 times in the past three months. Try to make it there for happy hour and get a pitcher or half pitcher of their sangria. It may not be strong but it's tasty and goes well with the 3-4 orders of tapas you shoul get there (or more depending on the group size). Tropical and mango are definitely my favorite nai tapas sangria flavors and highly recommend trying both especially if you like fruity flavors. Some menu favorites I always go back for: -Patatas Bravas -Croquetas de pollo -Mejillones Rias Baixas Also stop in for the amazing service :) the staff really makes an attempt to check on you and get to know you. I always love introducing new friends to this place for that and the amazing flamenco shows they have on Thursdays (I think they also have one over the weekend) but I've only seen the one on Thursday and it is truly a magnificent experience. You can't take pictures (it's distracting) which is a good thing because it's something worth experiencing through the naked eye.

Trust the reviews and get the dumplings everyone else is making a big deal about. Â You will not regret it. Â My souvlaki could have been warmer, but other than that it is good food for a great value and attentive/friendly service in a lovely place. Â The establishment is bigger than one might expect, and it was very crowded on a Tuesday night.

I was excited to go to this place. I love the concept of new seasonal american and it means I can usually find something healthy to eat. I went with my mom and her friend and we ordered two salads and 3 entrees. One of the salads called "market greens" was just so simple. Literally shredded greens with some salt and pepper and maybe some vinegar. Boooring, but fresh. I was expecting sauteed greens like kale and mustard greens but I guess thats my fault for not asking. The bibb salad was pretty good but also on the simpler side. Entrees- I had the special scallops and although they were delicious, again the dish lacked complexity and the portion was meager. All it came with was a tiny bit of puree that didn't even last to the last scallop. At 17$. So I was a little disappointed at that, my mom and her friend seemed to enjoy their mackerel but I also thought it was a very small portion for the price. I'd have to say the highlight of the meal was the dessert which I did not have very high hopes for. Buttermilk pannacota on top of a peanut butter crunch with quince. Very unique but after a couple of bites I was hooked. Delish. Service was good and friendly, and there wasn't a wait early on a saturday night. All in all, I'd be willing to give it another chance. Maybe order the burger instead or ask more questions about the starters.

This is easily one of the best meals I've had in New York. A friend who tends to be a very adventurous eater suggested we try it (he'd heard good things). I was hesitant at first because of the nontraditional menu, but don't let that scare you off. Three standouts for me: The hot dogs were out of this world. I didn't even know hot dogs could taste like that. We ordered more after trying them. The lamb belly was so tender and tasty. It actually began a conversation at our table as to whether it is possible to orgasm from food. The melon and naan on the side was perfect. I could have eaten that lamb all day. It took three of us to polish off, though we'd ordered a ton of food. Cheese plate was great for dessert, but my boyfriend also ordered this lemon curd thing that blew it out of the water. I'm crazy about anything lemon or citrus, and his came with the most amazing biscuit. Service was very friendly. We sat outside which was nice. And their beer selection was great. The bartender was nice enough to walk me through all the fruity/girly options, which I'll give him some bonus points for.

I was here for the first time today and overall have to say that I was disappointed. Â You need MORE BACON. Â If bacon is in the name of you bar, then you gotta go all the way, not halfway. Â The bacon sampler was flimsy at best. Â Not enough bacon and the bacon wasn't thick. Â Me and my friend ordered the cobb salad and there was barely any bacon in it. Â We had to ask for more bacon. Â Seriously guys, if your name is "BARBACON", you need to go further. Â I love bacon. I love meat. Â This is a great concept and I was excited to come check it out. Â But I wouldn't come running back. Â I left disappointed. Â And outside of the host and hostess, the service was awful. Â I sat at the bar with friends while waiting for a table and the bartender was completely detached. Â It got worse when we sat down. Â Had to constantly try to get the waiter's attention. Â Had to ask for plates for the appetizers. Â Had to ask for knives. Â Had to ask for water.
FINALLY- somewhere good in Astoria! Romantic and fantastic food. THANK YOU VESTA!!!! If only you were closer to my apartment.
Really enjoyed this place. Â Tacos were great, had the grilled chicken entree. Â Both awesome.

They have cardamom cake! Â It is well-spiced, dense, and crispy around the edges. I bet it would go well with coffee, although I didn't order any. Â  I tried their chicken shawarma in a laffa wrap for lunch today. Â Delicious! Â The filling was generous on juicy chicken, hummus, pickles, and veggies. Â It's large enough for two modest lunches or one large one. Â Since my friend and I sat at the counter, I liberally applied their cilantro spread every few bites, hehe. Â  All the ingredients were fresh. Â The restaurant is clean. Â Service is attractive and friendly. Â Decor is modern with rustic accents. Â It's probably my new favorite lunch spot.

After reading all the reviews on Yelp my husband and I were very excited to try this place since it very hard to find good vegetarian sushi. Â The overall experience here was OK. Â I don't think we would drive out to the city to go back to this place. Â Would definitely try other rolls if we are in the area. Â  We tried 4 different rolls. Â The mighty mushroom was the best one, would definitely recommend that roll. Â Then the curried cauliflower was decent, it had more flavor out of the three we didn't care for. Â  The roll of the month tasted like raw veggies with rice and the sauce that came with it was pretty tasteless. Â The Tofu piece (forgot what its exactly called - it has two pieces of tofu on it) was pretty tasteless as well. Â  The presentation of the rolls is excellent and the chef is very friendly but I like to rate place on two things how the food tastes and service. Â This place gets four stars for service but two stars on taste. Â  Since this place is vegan I think they should amp up their use of spices to add some flavor to the rolls so that it doesn't taste so much like raw veggies and rice.

Yo, I'm like the super average dude, and this place, THIS PLACE, was phenomenal. Seriously, went here for a friend's birthday (my gf and some of her friends) and we had an awesome time. The bartender reco'd a tasty wine. It was well priced, but didn't taste cheap. Which I appreciate, cuz they could've screwed us over with something that tastes like Yellowtail, but they didn't. It was a semi-dry full body red, hints of a ton of different shit...blah, blah, blah...all of that, Bottom line=delicious. I drink a lot of wine, and I know good ones. This was one of them. Just ask, they're good at suggesting the right ones. Next, the food. Small plates. Not always my favorite, but these delivered portions that we shared between four people. The big plates, um, equally as delicious, and well worth our time and palettes. We had a bunch. Definitely try the POLENTA. It's not to be missed. Which I'm sure tons of other people will reco, so I'll add the MEATBALLS to the list. Why? Because I'm a dude, I like to get full, and they were delightfully soft, full of flavor, and swimming in a tomato sauce that would make an Italian grandmother proud. The chef came out to check on us, which is always a nice touch. My GF grilled him about his techniques, and he was super hospitable about answering questions. This place is a no-brainer. If you like robust food and honest service, you'll quickly find out why this wine and tapas-esque bar has "Austere" in the name.

Great salads, fantastic coffee and, for anyone kicking around the city during the day, nice breakfast options including a continental breakfast of crusty French bread and jam. Â My favorite dish: The couscous. Â Another favorite detail: no cell phones allowed.
This place deserves 5 stars . My friends took me there . I wouldn't go there if i had to pay , but this time dinner was paid so i just had to enjoy ! Service was outstanding .
Their cherry blossom and lemon macaroons are DIVINE.

can people stop raving about this place? its just at all that special! the only story worth telling about this place is the fact that by some weird chance drew barrymoore and her boyfriend the apple guy aka justin long got sat at the same table as my boyfriend and me. i just remembered looking up and seeing a guy that looked strangely familiar looking at me while taking his sunglasses off. then a girl coming from the bathroom with an EXTREMELY familar voice sat down next to me. then i realized it was them. nudge nudge to the boyfriend and out came the cell phones. yes we spent all of lunch texting our friends about how ugly and skinny drew is in real life. stupid justin long even made fun of us "the couple that texts together, stays together"

Really loved this place on all levels. Â Was in town for a wedding and a friend made reservations here b/c it was one of her favorite new spots in the City. Â First of all, no recession at this restaurant! Â NYC may be suffering, but L'Artusi was bursting with activity, and for good reason. The space: see the pics. Â It's more impressive in person, managing to avoid the cliche "mid-Century modern" and "contemporary Victorian" genres that are all the rage right now, while feeling both modern and charming. Â For the record, it's LOUD, but I figure this is just part of the NYC dining experience. The food: for the most part, outstanding. Â I docked one star b/c the flank/skirt steak dish was way too rare and lukewarm, but otherwise, I loved the octopus, the orrechiete(sp?), the hamachi, the bruschetta and the quail (the latter was absolutely terrific - full of flavor and citrus taste). The service: Â very good. Â Our waitress was patient and friendly considering the crazy bustle going on around her. Â We waited a bit for our table, but service otherwise was well-timed. The prices: Â this is kind of interesting. Â It's not tapas size portions, but it's not entrees either. Â As a guy, I needed at least 2 dishes to fill me, but our table of four just shared 6-7 dishes. Â But the prices per dish were reasonable - about $15-$17 each. Â Yes, you need to order more than one, but then again, maybe you're just having a lite meal, in which case the perceived price is very acceptable. I loved it and will definitely go back next time I'm in NYC.

Great drinks and ambiance. Getting a little too crowded for my taste these days (they need to cap capacity much sooner at night...) but if you can manage to get in early and snag a table, you're golden. Bartenders are all great. Slushies are always way too strong-whether that's good or bad-your call. After trying just about everything on the menu...I tend to stick with the fried chickpeas or the burger. Mother's ruin is no longer a "hidden gem" but it's still a great go-to.
A perfect place for pick -up orders. I had chicken pad thai and it was delicious. I would definitely visit there next time.

I have to say that this was one of the most refreshing dining experiences I've had in Park Slope since moving here almost 2 years ago. I'd walked by GFT&M a bunch of times and last week in the spirit of the new year, we decided to call up and find out what their "vegetarian board" was all about. Usually a restaurant like GFT&M isn't accessible because the menu is mostly meat and the veg options are always something like sauteed vegetables and couscous. Really!? Vegetarians are more than couscous! I digress. When I spoke to a waitress she was so excited to tell me about the vegetarian board, so we decided to try it. It's a cute space, on one side lined with shelves of ingredients, from the outside, almost looks like a coffeeshop. Very warm and friendly. Our waitress (who I'd called earlier) was so excited that we actually came in. We gave her some feedback (e.g. I like mushrooms!) and then waited until a meal was served. While we waited, they brought some olives and bread to nosh - yum. Then the entrees came, two glorious boards full of grains, vegetables and more! Â Both entirely unique and beautifully presented: Board 1: marinated oyster mushrooms, sauteed bok choy, this mouth watering squash gratin (god i want to eat that again!), a veggie tamale, mole sauce and salsa verde, roasted potatoes Board 2: delicious faro and bean salad, grilled brussel sprouts, jasmine rice with horseradish greens, lentil soup, a take on mashed potatoes It was like an eating expedition, traveling from each end of the board discovering new tastes, textures and aromas! And - the best part is that the next time we go, it'll be a totally different experience. We enjoyed ourselves so much, that we decided to get the chocolate mousse - and that was a grand idea, it was delicious. It's hard to get a meal where vegetables and grains get first billing and you can get excited about a meal, in a city full of restaurants claiming to really understand a vegetarian palette, but GFT&M seriously gets it.

I came here with a group of Jews for the first night of Passover. Someone said that gluten-free is Kosher for Pesach, so it seemed like a good option. I read about Anthony the owner in previous Yelp reviews, and was delighted to have him greet us with pride and seat us before the rest of our party arrived. The service was amazing from start to finish. We ordered some apps to share, so here are the things I got to try: --Artichoke appetizer - really good, in a flavorful sauce and the artichokes were cooked perfectly --Istriana (crabmeat appetizer) -- the crabmeat was sweet and juicy, and served like a salad. Reminded me of ceviche a little, because there some citrus flavor --Bistango salad -- nothing crazy here, but the greens were fresh and apples provided a nice contrast --Salmon entree: salmon was fresh and cooked really well, and a generous portion with visually appealing crosshatch grill marks. It was served on top of veggies (kinda undercooked) and with a bit of creamy potatoes We also ordered 2 bottles of wine at $34 a pop. The bill came to about $50 per person, which doesn't seem crazy for the cuisine and the location. Definitely recommend it. It's a very cute place with great food and ambience -- you won't regret the experience.

I love L&Bs. It's a family owned establishment and the owner is so friendly with all his patrons. Here's the lowdown of the things I get regularly: Sicilian square: if you're a saucy person like me, you'll LOVE this (go for a middle or a side so you get a "handle"). it's perfect and light and airy and delicious. I've never encountered a bad square. Philly Cheesesteak: This thing is huge and delicious. Great for sharing. Homemade hazelnut ice cream: it tastes like Nutella ice cream. So much hazelnut flavor!

Went with a group of friends to catch up. Â Fantastic food fusion Thai, Vietnamese, Philipino. Â So we ordered a little of everything on the menu and there was nothing I wouldn't recommend. Â The food is fabulous from the appetizers to the desserts (and I don't typically enjoy cooked banana). Â The staff were very friendly and helpful the kitchen is small so they like you to order everything together. Â The reason I gave it Â 4 rather than 5 stars was because from the moment I sat down I felt a pressure to hurry, eat and leave. Â I mean they were giving us our cheque before we had finished dessert. Â It just didn't make for a relaxing evening. Â The outdoor area by the way is lovely however you can't book so make sure you get there early. Â Would definitely go back and give it a second go but I don't like to be rushed I like to relax and take my time.
Amazing. Dined here many times and never disappointed.

Stay CLEAR AWAY from this pathetic excuse for a Thai restaraunt. the service is HORRIBLE! A group of 3 of my friends and myself went for dinner, after 15 minites of sitting at our table and not getting served i was thoroughly pissed off. I called a waitress to come and take our orders we orderd everything at once entrees, drinks and our appetizers. We then waited another 40-50 minutes for our meal. During Â the process of waiting, the table in front of me, which was a table of 8 that came in 10 minutes AFTER us, got thier food 15 minutes before us...mind you that we were just a party of 4 so how can a party of 8 Â that came in 10 minutes after us get all their meals before US???? Â I was BOILING with disgust and anger after being ignored we canceled our order and we walked out. I Â NEVER had such bad service in my life. I came to Sripraphai with high hopes of getting some good thai food instead i got horrible service and a bad appetite. I wish I could give this place no stars!

Love this place ! I am a regular customer there lol Â I fell in love with Kobe burger. Thsi is a definite winner ! and sweet potato fries- out of this world. and plate with rice/salad and beef/shrimp - amazing ! I guess the secret is in the sauce !!

Great lunch at ReViVer today. Â Good addition to the nabe. Â We had the Carolina BBQ chicken and the Balkan Burger (which is in a pita). Â Both were great and flavorful. Â Portions are not large but well portioned. Â Would go back and try some of the other items.

I came here in January for my friends birthday. We were a party of 5, it was a Thursday evening. The place was, surprisingly, not busy, and it seemed as if only a few parties were waiting to be seated ahead of us. There were several empty tables and the restaurant didn't have that "we're crazy busy" vibe to it. When I checked with the hostess, she said, in her best baby voiced valley girl, "Um, yeah, it's going to be two hours and 45 minutes before we can get to you, it's REAL busy." First of all, that's not a thing. It's impossible to expect a wait that long ahead of time. Secondly, I work at Blue Smoke, and within the group of friends, we had people who work at El Centro, Vynl and Industry. So it's not as if we are restaurant virgins or people who've never worked in one before. We expected a wait, but really, little girl, 2:45? You're bullish*t. We decided not to stay. A couple of months later I had a mediocre experience at the bar. Being that I work at a bar pretty well versed in Bourbon, I figured the bar staff would be knowledgeable. However, I was wrong. I'm the first to admit when i don't know something, and overhearing the bar staff, incorrectly, educate patrons at the bar who now assume they are getting gospel, I had to laugh, and when the bartender asked me why I was laughing, I told him. He got really defensive and basically told me I should drink somewhere else. A third time i came back, because a friend of mine REALLY wanted to go there. I drug me feet in, but had a great experience. Our server was ridiculously attentive and fun. I know that's a personality thing, and has nothing to do with your actual place, so kudos to him for being an awesome human. However, the place isn't anything special and most of the people I've encountered there have a giant chip on their shoulder. You're working with food, not saving lives people. And learn to smell out your colleagues in the industry. We know your job and are willing to let a lot of things go, but incompetence and ignorance are not those things.

Wow, everything we had was fantastic. The flavors are both deep and punchy. We shared some charcuterie (pickled tongue -- amazing) and addictive chard stems, then scallop special (perfectly cooked, great flavors), a side of shishito peppers, and the best steak I've had in ages. My husband had a nice glass of Lambrusco and I asked the waiter to surprise me with something in the scotch/whiskey/bourbon arena. I told him a little of what I tend to like and he nailed it with a great rye I had never tried before. You can also have a less pricey meal, but before we knew it, it felt like we were celebrating. Welcome to the neighborhood, Krupa Grocery!!

Brunch only: Truffled eggs benedict, fabulous. Â Beignets with Lebanese clotted cream, soaked with orange blossom syrup; fabulous. Â Hummus side order, pretty darn good. Â Honestly, this brunch was a combination of some of my favorite things, and I couldn't have been happier with the food. But! $4 6oz. coffee with no free refills... super lame. Â The brunch pre-fixe is a pretty good deal, but again- $4 refill? Really. Â Especially after a fly landed in my first cup and I had to have it replaced (the coffee, not the fly). Â As much as I liked the food, I really would have liked better, more attentive service. Â Oh, also, my server didn't know the menu very well and I had to question her explanation of the dish I wanted... which was slightly embarrassing for both of us! Â Maybe she didn't usually work the brunch shift? Regardless, I intend to return because the food was so good. Â Next time though, I'll skip the coffee.

Best burger in the city. Thick and juicy. Cheap ale. Don't wait in line for a table, just order at the bar, it's so good you'll swallow it in less than 3 mins anyway. Bistro burger comes with cheese & bacon. It does not, however, come with ambiance, spacious accommodations or a smiley bartender. I think people confuse no attitude with bad attitude. That gray haired bartender dude simply has no attitude, neither good nor bad. Does that make him a douche bag? He does not say "what can I get you" He simply points at you. You order, he delivers and that's it. He won't ask if you enjoyed your burger or whatever. He knows this shit is good.

Definitely my favorite Malaysian restaurant, and one of my top faves of any cuisine in NYC. Why? Because it is so tasty! This is an authentic place (not a fancy/formal one) with somewhat abrupt (but not unfriendly) waitstaff. I always try a few dishes, including a new one or 2. Prices are inexpensive so it's easy to be adventurous. Â Among my faves are any of their fried noodle dishes (they're all good!), the oyster omelet, the Malaysian spare ribs, pork with yam, and sizzling beef or sizzling yee mee. DO NOT forget to try one of the shaved ice desserts--chendol or ABC. They are so good, sometimes I can't decide and get one of each! Â Luckily, they're not too filling (after a big meal) but very tasty (and may induce a brain freeze).

One of my fave casual brunch spots in West Village! I have a tendency to get bored with breakfast/brunch entrees, but Joseph Leonard succeeds with classic brunch food adding some tweaks to elevate the flavors. Â I usually go with the egg sandwich (which you can add bacon to for $2...why wouldn't you?) that comes with a side of brussel sprouts with sriracha. Â The croissant is flakey and the Brussel Sprouts with Sriracha (also avail as side dish) may sound weird at first, but tastes great; you'll wonder why you've never thought of this yourself before. Â I've also tried the French Toast (with nutella and bananas) and it had a nice crisp sear on the brioche while still remaining pillowy soft on the inside. Â For sides, we tried the garlic sausage (one of the better breakfast sausages I've had) and, drumroll please, the Country Fried Bacon (fried bacon with tabasco sauce and honey). Â Fried bacon...I know right?! Dead. This is a place where you can dress casual for brunch, lunch or dinner. Â Great variety on the menu; you can't go wrong with any of the sandwiches (try the pork sandwich on the weekdays!). Â I Â prefer their brunch/lunch menu to the dinner menu. Â Service is friendly, but not outstanding. Waiters are outside socializing with friends a lot of the time...at least make it discrete! Â Love the West Village vibe, but the restaurant is tiny and doesn't take reservation, so avoid the brunch rush and come at off hours! They serve brunch till 4 on the weekends and lunch till 3:30 on the weekdays--great hours for late risers like myself!

UNSANITARY - Counter guy has BLACK DIRT under his finger nails. Â He touches your money, then touches your slice. Â GROSS!!!! Really loved the pizza, but I can't stomach FILTHY fingers touching my food.

Twice I've been here and twice I've left floating away with a good buzz and a full tummy. I willingly make the trek and drop the cash to visit Calle Ocho. As every one raves, the bread balls and the black bean dip are incredible! And the sangria satisfies my thirsty liver. Most recently, my friends and I had the berry drenched one. Sabrosa. Check this place out. Make the reservation! And be prepared for a lively, flavor packed meal.

Place gets packed. Was here on a thursday night around 7 and had to wait 30 minutes or so. The bar was packed so I went next door to E's bar to kill time and have a couple of drinks. Atmosphere here is really good. Most of the tables are communal so chances are you may have to sit there. Had the sausage gravy fried chicken biscuit w/ cheese grits ($15) and also tried the turkey leg ($18). Turkey leg was big and wasn't spectacular, but was good. The sausage gravy was really damn good as was the biscuit. Soft and full of flavor. The fried chicken was good, but far from the best i've had. Wish I had the option of ordering dark thigh meat but had white meat instead. The cheese grits were good but a little too heavy for my date. Got a 32 oz growler for myself. Think it was $15 which isn't bad at all. Would definitely go back and try the other dishes and drinks.

Absolutely amazing!! everything is so delicious, you won't regret going here and having an excellent meal. Must try: Seared Foie Gras Don't forget to make a reservation. It will make the whole experience much pleasant

This time however, I was little disappointed because I ordered ribs with brown rice and it came pretty fast but I saw a strain of hair plus the rice was not properly cooked. I like Mooncake foods but I was not very happy last Tuesday. Anyway, hopefully they will be careful next time.

After seeing this written up in the NY Times this week, a group of 10 of us decided to give it a go. Â While I generally feel that you can never go wrong with ramen, this place was pretty exceptional. Â Very straight forward menu, with lots of ramen add-in options. Â Even though everyone raved about the pork (I don't eat meat), I went for the Spicy Vegetable Ramen with the extreme rayu (spicy pepper oil) add in. Â This was superb! Â On a bitter cold winter night, this flavorful bowl of awesome was just what I needed. Â I started with the Avo Tuna which was also great. Â The wasabi-esque paste (not sure how else to describe it) that came with it was unbelievable. Â With a small jar of hot sake, a can of hot tea and great company, I loved this place.

The pizza was REDONKULOUS. Â Perfectly cripsy, a substancial amount of crust, good amount of mushrooms, proscutto was still moist and not burnt. Â  Good amount of cheese to sauce ratio too. Â The boy said that he preferred our neighborhood-fancy-pants pizza place, Amorinas, better, because the sauce there is sweeter. Â I have to say that I liked the garlic-y tangy sauce at Fornino's better...plus I think the crust quality here is better too because it tends to be a bit doughier. Â (Amorinas tends to burn the crust, which I think is a cardinal pizza sin). The salad was unremarkable and the dressing was more sweet than vinegar-y. Â  I would give the pizza alone 5 stars, but in NY there is a plethora of equally fabulous pizza places, so I'd feel weird about proclaming Fornino "the best of the best." But for the record, it was really f*cking awesome.

I do like this place, and have very little that is not positive to say about it. Â The food for the most part is excellent, & the wine is a great deal. Â I usually get the Calamari Fritti; which is the best fried calamari I have ever had, & the incredible Osso Buco. Â The olives & breads are fantastic, the deserts... awesome! Â My only complaint is their pasta. Â I don't think they do pasta in a truly memorable fashion. Â It's ok, but it leaves me short of... Wow! Â It's the reason I don't hang a fifth star here. Â The wines are great. Â You can always find a $25 bottle to pair very nicely with your meal. Â What a deal for Manhattan. As in my other NYC reviews, parking is ok as far as NYC is concerned. Â Street parking is brutal, but plenty of garages close to your meal. Â Public transportation is a short walk from the A,C, or E lines (Off of 50th ST or 42nd ST stops). Â Taxis are always cruising by as you are right in Hell's Kitchen just outside the heart of the Theater District. The restaurant has many feels to it. Â Not crazy about the front entry dining room, as it is really too busy, too bright, and the traffic is non-stop; as this is a very popular place! Â The upstairs has a great Manhattan feel & it is great for even a bit larger crowd. Â I have had several business dinners here and I like being upstairs. Â The bar area is congested, but manageable. Â Eating in there is also crowded, but you understand you are really in a pub. Â If you are going for a dining room, hold out for it. Â But, if you don't mind that more casual atmosphere, it has a cool rustic feel to it. This is tremendous NYC value in my book. Â The food is on the whole very good, and not overpriced. Â They offer specials that are convenient, and I can say with certainty you leave full, & not feeling ripped off. Â Again, the wine prices per bottle are the way to go. I like the service here. Â A hard working group always. Â I enjoy that most everyone has a wonderful Italian accent; it adds a great charm. Â I have found the Becco staff to go out of the way to be creative in order to let you have a very pleasurable dining experience. I Give Becco a B
