I hate pretentious places, like the hotel across the street. I love tasteful, laidback places with affordable drinks like Verlaine. My friends and I end up here ever so often... that says a lot! $5 Lychee martinis! They have an extensive drinks menu, but please be wise in ordering. My friend got something that tasted meaty once. Yuck!

FYI this is an _Austrian_ place. Not German. Similar, but different! I came with a friend at 8:30 on a Sunday night and got a table almost immediately. This had me pretty thrilled as it is usually not the case at Katja. We started by sharing the beet salad with caraway, goat cheese, and pumpkinseed oil--all in all it was pretty fantastic though I wished the taste of the pumpkinseed oil came through a little more, and that the caraway seeds were integrated a little better. They were just sprinkled raw on a hunk of goat cheese. We both had a liptauer sandwich (my favorite, and ridiculously inexpensive at $6), which is a fresh cream-like cheese with paprika over a slice of toasted bread, sprinkled with fresh diced radish and served with a pickled veggie garnish. We lingered with a glass of wine for a while and eventually settled on the warm chocolate cake with cherry compote. This was not really the highlight of the meal. The cake was too densely chocolate for my taste, not very hot, the accompanying whipped cream was kind of sour (?) and the cherry compote was also a little sour and didn't seem very fresh. I wish we would've tried the fig and almond tart. If I come back soon, I'll definitely give that a whirl. We payed a little over $30 a piece and stayed for over 3 hours. The waitress was a teeny bit obsequious but didn't seem hostile after we stayed for so long. All in all a great meal, and I'll be back a bunch more.
Delicious and very affordable! Â Great pasta, good wines and the atmosphere can't be beat. Â Good date place.

Unimpressed. First, the place is loud so If you are looking for something more intimate, stay away, but Â that aside as it didn't sway my rating at all. First course, I had the meatballs. They were pretty good and portion was plenty enough to share for 2-3 ppl. Then I had the 3 pasta special of which I had 2, spaghetti with tomato-basil and rigatoni with a veal bolognese. Both were Cooked very aldente which I hate. Didn't enjoy either at all. Luckily the meatballs and bread filled me up. Aside from that, the service was not great. No one checks in to see how you are doing or if you need anything. It took forever for me to track someone down to get a water refill and no one ever came around to ask if I wanted more pasta (or for that matter, if I didn't enjoy my first helping as my plate was half-full. Finally, the table was very wobbly that I had to hold it still with my feet throughout dinner and the one point I didn't pay attention to it, my wife's martini spilled. She did have the swordfish which she enjoyed very much. All in all, I wouldnt go back unless my wife really wanted as she and her family really enjoy it there, why, I don't understand. There are PLENTY of better italian restaurants throughout the city.

Dark Horse is great - served as a haven from the crowded, hot, food-lacking elite event at Manhattan Proper. Not to downplay the event - Ruggy is awesome and knows how to throw a party... but one can only withstand a packed, stuffy, HUNGRY crowd for so long! Dark Horse is not much different than any pub aside from a few aspects: -Each booth has a private flat screen TV. And the bartender is more than willing to accommodate your requests. -The menu is pretty extensive, more than your average pub food, but still affordable. The french onion soup is lovely. -They have daily drink special that last the whole day, not just happy hour. And with a yelp check-in your second drink is free.

The service was great. Â Our waiter made suggestions so that we ordered plenty of food to cover our group of five but not so much that we would have felt that were taking advantage. We had the calamari, chicken parmesan and spaghetti and meatballs. Â The calamari was one of the best I have ever had, it was crispy and juicy. Â I felt that the chicken was dry and covered with cheese and sauce to try to moisten it up but my fellow diners thought it was delicious. Â The spaghetti was perfectly cooked and the meatballs were yummy. The ambience is definitely better than Carmines. Â We could actually hear each other at the table without screaming. Â There are great pictures of actors with a reference to their Broadway show. I would have given them 2.5 stars if I could for overall. Â The service and calamari was 5.0.

I tried this place last Thursday for a business lunch. Inside space was bigger than I thought (their entrance is pretty small and narrow). I had two appetizers as lunch. The portion was big. I had baked flat bread with mozzarella & tomato and grilled chicken salad. Flat bread was a good call. I will go back to this place!

This is a great Coffee Shop. For so many reasons. Ready, Set, Go: 1. Top notch bagels and pastries 2. Hilarious Staff 3. A super awesome "This is a Window" sign so you don't smack your face into a glass wall 4. Rewards Program 5. It's not a big box place, you see where your money goes 6. It's called Blue Spoon 7. Quick 8. Close to a ton of offices and subway stations 9. Need to get to 10 10. The prices aren't out of this world If you need a place to go for a quick bite for breakfast, a snack, or even lunch - Blue Spoon should be your go to. It has that hipster "I'm buying coffee but I'm revolting from society by avoiding starbucks" vibe which I dig.
Great find for authentic Japanese in midtown Manhattan. Would definitely come back. Great atmosphere and service too.

Had lunch here and was pleased with mostly everything. The host was very gracious and welcoming, whereas our waiter (a tall Asian man wearing traditional garb) was quite cold. Pork Belly Buns: Two per order. The presentation is simple (none), they could have been hotter (temperature, not spice). Tom Yum Soup: Really flavorful, and they did not skimp on shrimp, mussels or mushrooms, which was great. The vegetable summer roll was tasty but for $7 I think 1 roll cut into 3 pieces is overpriced. There should be two per order. The chicken curry was lackluster. The vegetables were overcooked. The chicken was bone-in and tender, the rice was well prepared, but the whole thing together was just mediocre. I wouldn't order it again. The thai eggplant dish was a good version of fried baby eggplants. Mine could have used a little more salt and spice (the sauce was quite sweet), but I think that is a personal preference.

Bistro Petit. Your organic grass-fed local beef burger is.... the best burger.... when it' seasoned up with a lot of salt, and has kimchi under the burger, and some tomato, and I'm a little drunk, sitting at the counter, watching the kitchen, not thinking, just tasting, chewing, living. Cauliflour soup. Love. Beet Salad with fried goat cheese balls. Love. Beef Bourgingon (sp). Jealous I didn't order. Homemade Cookie w Vanilla Icecream. Love. Thanks, Salty Chef Park.

I want to give them 5 stars because of the amazing food, super cute decor, and great prices but I was pretty unhappy with the server. I work in the service industry so I know how to be a really easy, kind, good costumer. I always tip over 20%. I know it's a crappy job but I also know millions of people are constantly trying to get hired into the industry, so I never understand how restaurants end up with such bitter, unhappy, unwelcoming servers. Our server, a blonde girl, was completely rude, acting annoyed that we even walked in, just overall impolite even though I was obviously trying to be kind. I ended up leaving a couple dollars less than I usually would have for tip (granted, it was still probably 18%) and as I was leaving all of the other employees of the restaurant were sweet with their goodbyes and I immediately regretted doing that since their tips are probably pooled. So I want to say sorry to all of the other employees there for me taking my annoyance out on their coworker and thus also affecting them. Either way, I would recommend Pies n Thighs, it's delicious.

the peking duck pancake is SOOO GOOD! buy one to eat then and there, and then another to eat on the way home. i don't understand how they charge so little because they give quite a bit of duck for that price. the spicy wontons are really good also, but only if you like or don't mind cilantro. the place is tiny, so i would recommend getting everything to go and eating elsewhere. this place is much better than its competition, properity dumpling. i ordered the peking duck pancake there and it is a JOKE compared to the one they sell at vanessa's. i don't even know how they can call that peking duck- the meat is pretty much minced and they give you a teaspoon of it. and the sesame pancake there is thinner and just not made as well. so just go to vanessa's- the quality is much better!

I love this place. It's dark, often loud & crowded to the point of inducing claustrophobia...Which is why the house covered up the garden in the back with a permanent clear fiberglass shell. Christmas lights & candles are strung for lighting; both the more manageable volume & the more intimate setting make it better for smaller crowds & couples that want to escape the "party dinner" thing. I used to drink a lot of beer. I discovered Negra Modelo, Xingu & Brahma here. Beers are $3 at happy hour, which takes over the majority of the Week in Bogota. Otherwise they're $5, which is still about the average you'll pay citywide for a friggin 12oz draft of Americana. Hell, $3 will only get you a draft of bargain asswater in outerboroughs dumps Coctails are strong & cheap. Caipiroscas are actually really good, but that's the only coctail I've ever ordered here. I can't drink CachaÃ§a ever again. Long story involving a Liter bottle of Pitu... I do not drink cocktails anymore, I'm sorry. Somerset Maugham once called them a "vile thing" - Â I just learned the hard way. I don't really drink at all anymore though. But I Digress. Entrees are large & come with any number of excellent sides. My younger (older) sister actually gets the vegetarian plate - just a choice of side dishes served with rice & beans - every time she comes here. The arroz con pollo is hearty, cheap & delicious, but comes with black beans. The roasted chicken is always a conservative but solid choice, & I'd get it with their porky delicious red beans, yellow rice & Maduros :) If you like beef, try the ropa vieja - shredded Cuban style skirt steak stewed for hours with wine, capers, onions, peppers & spices. Or if you're prepared to hotbox the sh*t out of the whip on the way (whilst someone else is driving of course!) - the Bandeja Paisa is the Bomb. Get ready. Also known as Bandeja MontaÃ±era, this is the national dish of Colombia, & means Mountain or Country Platter. Â on one end of the platter is the base heap of rice. A grilled skirt steak, chicharrones (deep fried pork fatback), a fried egg, Maduros & an Arepa line the plate the rest of the way down, & a big 'ol bowl of beans comes on the side. While you might need to hibernate for a day or two (the chicharrones alone will cause rapid-onset Itis) - this platter will be worth it. Just do yourself a favor & don't drink more than a beer with that much fat. A few shots or maybe a stiff neat scotch beforehand will do wonders, however. For appetizers I personally typically stick to a plate of empenadas served with green crack (aji sauce) but I have a friend who still talks about the taco soup a full two years after he had it All in all, whether you're coming for food or for drinks, It's one of the few places restos around where one can bring groups bordering on obnoxious (in both size & demeanor, whether or not that's to blame on the price of the booze is up for debate) - enjoy a great meal at reasonable prices and get hammered all night for less than you'd pay in any Hipster bar in the city. I've been coming here for almost a decade on and off & never had any problems.

Lovely date night location. Â Cozy ambiance, great menu and fantastic food. Always a fan of places you can go to casual or dressy and this place works for either. Glad to have stumbled over this restaurant. There are so many great options in the area but this restaurant is a must!

I have been avoiding Shake Shack like the plague... Seriously.... I'm the kind of person that once I taste something amazing... that's anywhere in near proximity to me... I'll crave and eat that thing all the time... without reserve... or restraint..... So when the Shake Shack "buzz" happened years back.. I watched.. I admired.. I read blog pages... I salivated at the pics.... and told myself... "STAY FAR".. otherwise you will gain the 30lbs you've lost over the years....and you know... you don't need to gain it back. WELL! ...Working at the World Financial Center.... its pretty hard to avoid... and even through my pregnancy in 2011 - I avoided... returned from maternity leave.. I avoided..... - but finally gave in - December 2012...... Let the obsession commence. --- Shack Cheeseburger...with bacon... Perfect size.. just right...juicy patty.... not overbearing or too gluttonous.. even tempting to eat 2 possibly...and they are always made with care. ---Cheese Fries A friggin MUST..... I adore these fries... and the American/Cheddar Sauce... is really light.. not gunky.. or having a pasty consistency like other places.. - however! must be eaten immediately.. or it will get very soggy... Considering getting sauce on the side going forward... been noticing a lot of patrons doing so. ---Root Beer MY MUST have... can't say no to Draught Root Beer.... ---Frozen Custard Shake! I always find room... - Vanilla.... I add Malt.. and I'm happy....no need for all those extra toppings... I think I've consumed enough calories in the meal already..... Although ! Yesterday!!!! I tried a CONCRETE instead! ...with Peanut Butter Sauce and Malt....and that was DIVINE... perfectly thick.. dense... and smooth.... no more shakes... Concretes for me going forward... --- Customer Service I've only been here probably 3x... and the darn cashier said - "Hey Alysha!... shack burger.. bacon .. right?... cheese fries too!"..... I was impressed..... the amount of people that crowd this location - Mon-Friday.... and she remembered me?.. I guess I'm so sweet... how could you forget? :) TIP - Come after 1:30pm *if during a work week... even after 2pm is better.. Anytime before that... is a mad house... too crowded...and no seats.... But with spring/summer approaching.. sitting outside will be a pleasure... Next up for me... Their Griddle Dogs!! ... nothing like a crispy grilled hot dog... hmmm I'M SOLD!

OK so definitely a winter spot especially if you enjoy really well crafted comfort food in a jovial. lively, warm atmosphere. Â Coming from too may years in the pacific northwest i especially enjoy the urban (guests) meets rural (taxadermy) wild game decor. Â  All the dishes I had in the 1/2 dozen dinners here were totally delicious (yeah some a bit overly creamy and salty) but the one dish that stands out was the, and I don't think my memory is fading here, bulgar rissotto. Â ok it might not have been bulgar but it WAS a very common grain that was cooked to such perfection that i may never appreciate arborio risotto in the same way. Â I don't even remember what was in the risotto texture was so perfect... oh yeah, if you're a brussel sprout fan they're also really really good (yeah yeah I know they're easy to make but come on...) especially with a small batch bourbon... Â  footnote 1: only criticism is the wait and the cramped quarters... again, yeah yeah yeah i know dense city, popular place but it's still annoying... footnote 2: the front of the house service was really professional, especially the host who might be one of the incarnations of buddah...

Carnitas taco... amazing. Rajas taco... mouthwatering deliciousness. Queso nachos... heck yes. It's got limited stool-only seating. BYOB. Probably my favorite new place in East Village and worth the walk from Union Square.

My boyfriend took me here for dinner and absolutely love everything about it. If you like a nice casual place this is it. Service was great, very attentive. Food was delicious, I had their special for the night which was short ribs mac and cheese and I can only say WOW...best mac and cheese I've ever had. My boyfriend had the chicken and waffles which was also good. I will definitely come back to this place. We first tried to go for a sunday brunch but too crowded. Thank God we decided to come back and give it another try because we were not disappointed.

0h STAGE restaurant you lovely little devil you.. HOW I MISS THE DAYS OF CALLING THEM UP AND ORDERING N A HUGE BREAKFAST FOR THREE OR FOUR DOLLARS... hands down best perogies around especially the ricotta ones! I've had everything from their chicken soup to the perogies to the breakfast to their borcsht... everything was amazing if you don't mind the aesthetics of this place a small, a small tight narrow little restaurant with a diner counter, ultimately you would have a satisfying dining experience. I suggest taking out the food though just because of the size of the restaurant and the fact that it gets very packed in the morning for breakfast... actually it's really packed throughout most of the day into the evening.. so yeah take out...

The decor and vibe is great at Walters. I have been for lunch, and recently took my parents for dinner which exceeded our expectations! The service was spot on as well as our cocktails and dinner. Well done, will be back later this week!

Brunch/Breakfast on a random Friday when I was back in the city. Fabulous place. It wasn't crowded and we walked right in without a wait...so rare in the city, even on a Friday. Ordered the Middle Eastern Eggs and was going to order a side of yogurt and granola because I wanted something sweet but the waitress was soo friendly and helpful that she reminded me that there would be a sizable serving of labne with my eggs and it might be too much yogurt then. (She was right.) I had them scrambled and they were fabulous. The labne was soo rich and tangy and had the perfect about of bite. Although I like savory more than sweet, I am not a fan of super salty food (i.e. I get the unsalted pretzels at baseball games and auntie anne's in malls). The israeli salad was super fresh and crisp and provided a great balance against the heavier labne. A bite of the eggs with the salad and then a piece of pita with the labne...made me soooo happy. My friend got the breakfast sandwich and seemed very happy with his meal as well. We were so concentrated on eating our own food, I don't think we bothered asking if the other wanted to try. I also got a chai, which was ok. I forgot to order it with skim milk, so that part is on me, but I expected it to have more spice and flavor. I ended up ordering a cappuccino to go when we were leaving. all in all, I definitely plan on going again. Hopefully the pumpkin pancakes aren't seasonal and I can try them...just need to go with someone who wants to go halfsies on something savory too.

Oh man, I wanted to like this place so much. I would give it one star but since I've been ill I haven't had much of an appetite so I'm just going be nice. On to the meal: Fresh Squeezed OJ- It's fresh OJ. Not much to talk about Renegade (Honey, Lemon, Ginger drink)- Surprisingly refreshing! I love ginger so I enjoyed this drink a lot. Rob Evans- Comprised of a biscuit, egg, cheese, and sausage gravy. Unfortunately, I had a short black hair in my food. I was starving and just cut out a major part of the area the hair was on so I didn't complain. I wasn't too hungry anyways. It was very rich and definitely comfort food. I ate about half and was full. I would order this again. Chicken and Waffles- Le Boyfriend ordered this but he let me try some. I've had much better elsewhere. I prefer Popeye's and Eggos compared to this. The chicken skin was bland, although the actual meat was juicy, tender, and flavorful. The waffle- I didn't have it because it didn't look appetizing, but according to Le Boyfriend, it was doughy and thick. Normally we like light and fluffy waffles... OH and he also found a hair in his food. Pecan Butter Crunch Donut- The thickest raised donut I've ever had. It was more like a cake donut or a loaf of bread. The flavor was there but it was too heavy to be considered a raised donut for me.

I've had many many xlb throughout my life, the best is still Din Tai Fong dumpling house from Taiwan. Â Joe's weren't bad, but the skin on the dumplings were still too thick. Â It was deliciously juicy nonetheless, and the crab dumplings were even tastier. Â I recommend getting both the crab and the regular to compare! Â  We arrived before 7 on a Saturday, only waited 10 min. Â It may look like alot of ppl but it moves very quickly.

I am sooo in love with this place! Best BYOB place ever (no cork fee)!! The food is amazing (had mushrooms cigars, stuffed rosemary chicken with chive mashed potatoes and ended with warm apple pie and ice cream) and the staff is super friendly. I would give this place 5 stars but the place is super tiny and they only take cash. Besides that i will def be making this place one of my regular spots.
meatloaf was the best i had in awhile. Â would go there again. my girlfriend got the burger which was damn good too. priced very reasonably for manhattan.

yummmm! Â i got delivery from here and it was great. Â The pizza is so thin that you don't feel disgustingly full after 2 (or 3!) slices. Â We got one large pizza with onions, bell peppers, and !asparagus! Â which I thought was a cool different topping. Â We also got a small meat pizza which is small enough that one person could eat it and feel full but not over-full. Â Everything about this pizza is done properly. Â There isn't an over-abundance of cheese or sauce or toppings..its good portions which is hard to find in this calorie-happy super-sized world.The garlic bread we got was ok - but I probably wouldn't order that again. Â The delivery time was 20 minutes and on a busy saturday night I thought that was very decent timing. I will definitely get pizza from here again - next time I might go and eat inside b/c i've passed by this place and it looks cute. edit: i went inside to pick-up a pie recently and realized that i HAD been here before. Â When I was apartment hunting for my very 1st apt in nyc - my brother and i got hungry and happened to fall upon this place...who would've known that over a year later its my neighborhood favorite pizza shop! aw.. :)

I really don't get the average review rating. Â  If I had seen 2 stars before going here the first time, I wouldn't have gone. Â  Tonight was my second time there. Â  First of all, had about the best service I've had in months and months. Â She was unreal. Â We sat in the bar area and had awesome views of the harbor. Â  I felt like I was on vacation here - like on Cape Cod or something. Â  The crab was great, crab cakes very good, beer was ice cold. Â  Prices aren't bad. Â  Tons of space to sit outside (the wait can be very long but they'll text you). Â The place was packed today. Â It was one of the nicest days of the year and sitting there was such a treat. Â  There is also a free ferry to and from Pier 11 off Wall Street during the weekends in the summer - it drops you off right behind the Fairway Market. Â  A great experience and really enjoyed for the second time.

I'll start with the bad (which isn't that much) and then the good. Bad: most just the service. Â it seems that all the waiters and the person passing out the tickets for people to wait have attitude. Â Also, not a big fan of the shared seating. Good: the FOOD! Â love the crab pork soup dumplings. Â my other favorite dish is the lion head meatball. Â  Everytime family or friends have visited, I have brought them to this place. Â And everytime they say when they come back to NY, they want to go here.
Okay. I don't like to throw 5s around. I didn't experience the whole menu. Have zero opinion on the sushi but did have some tuna that was tasty. Japanese pancake made the meal. Straight awesome.

Why am I not living in LIC again? I should be. Great view of the city with great cozy restaurants. Cafe Henri. Passed by here a couple of times and bookmarked it in my head. Cute French restaurant. French onion soup and dark chocolate crepe. How French can I get? A quiet chilly Monday afternoon sitting at the booth looking out and watching their patrons. Ahhhhhh not working tonight. Thank God! Their soup was perfect, did not give me that overpowering onion taste, it was sweet and light. They have a pretty good amount of crepe flavors, but as always I went for the chocolate. Yea, not a berry fan. I'll eat it if I have to but will never ask for it. Anyhoooo, the crepe was thin enough and not doughy, good amount of chocolate in it. Love it. But then again I already loved this place even before setting foot in it
I get delivery from here pretty often and have never been disappointed; the food is tasty, well-prepared and flavorful. Â I've never been inside the actual restaurant, however.

I found this place near Lenox Hill hospital. I've never had a Gyro which french fries in it and it was fantastic. Â The price was very reasonable, and I had two of mamas gyros. The spicy mayo was excellent and so was the barbecue. Â I would deathly recommend this if you looking for a reasonable takeout lunch.

Had dinner here last night and this may be my new favorite Thai spot in the east village! - Food - delicious, twist on traditional Thai (ex: papaya and zucchini pad Thai) - Cute decor - Amazing service - asked us to move tables to accommodate a larger group and gave our party of 6 complimentary desserts and cocktails.

What a nice little find! Â It is a bit out of the way (another 5+ minutes after getting off the 1 train at Christopher St.), but it's so cozy and comfortable that it's worth a trek there. Â  It's dark with wooden tables and chairs, and empty wine bottles adorning some of the shelves. Â The waiters were straight-up authentic I-talianos. Â I loved the menus - a long sheet of paper attached to a wooden panel of sorts - it almost looked hand-written with a consistent but limited number of selections that all looked appetizing. Â The 1/2 carafe of wine options are great for tables that want both red and white but don't want to commit to a bottle of either. The mussels were tasty and fresh with a white wine broth. Â The spinach gnocchi with gorgonzola had delicious flavors, but definitely a filling dish. Â I was impressed by how good the spaghetti was - kudos to them for being able to execute such a simple dish so well. Â I was too jazzed about the special I got - fusilli with shrimp, zucchini and tomatoes - I'm somewhat indifferent when it comes to pasta unless the sauce is stellar, and this was a little bland. Prices were VERY reasonable and we never felt rushed. Â I'd love to come back here for another mellow evening meal; I really think the out-of-the-way location helps contribute to the relaxing atmosphere, and the food and wine seem to be consistently good based on my experience and everything I've heard about this place. Â Love it!
The Southern Fried Chicken wings were excellent! Â  The mac - n - cheese bites were really good! Â Skip the meatballs! Â Atmosphere was great!
Beer List is Better than Average bar. So are the burgers. Patio out back.

The poutine surpasses any served north of the border - as if to pay the Montrealais back for outdoing NY's bagels and pastrami. A must-do when nearby, although it probably has around a day's worth of calories. (And yes, they give you a spoon. What could be better than eating fries with a spoon?)

For the wait time and the $200 bill, not really sure I was loving Ippudo. Last Thursday 5 coworkers and myself came here for my boss' send off dinner. We arrived at about 6:15, and we were knew were going to have to wait which was fine. It was rather busy, and we saw the line outside and I never thought we'd get a spot. But it was a 30 minute wait, and we killed time at the bar where they do 2 for 1 happy hour but only with their two draft beers. Which is kind of stupid but people buy into it. Once our name was finally called we were looped around to the back to a table in the corner. The table was extremely low and almost uncomfortable. After being there for not even 15 seconds, the hostess came back over and told us that a bigger table that was reservation opened up and if we wanted it, it was our. We were all over that! After being seated once again, we started to check out the menu. We figured it would be best to just order appetizers and have a few bites of everything. We had scanned the menu and narrowed the list down but of course wanted to pick the waitress' brain to see if we missed anything. We were basically right on point we everything we had planned to order. She suggested that if the 6 of us were going to share to order anywhere between 6 to 8 plates. We ordered, edamame, 2 orders of pork buns, one order of shrimp buns, Hamachi Carpaccio, crab and avocado dip, the shrimp special of the day, Tofu Yasai Tar Tar and the Maguro Tataki. The edamame of course was your standard. It was served with this powder that we were all trying to guess what it was, we were saying everything from ginger to mustard seeds but it turned out to be a citrus based powder. Added an interesting taste to it, but I certainly wasn't getting any real hints of citrus. The buns! The girls who had the pork buns, died and went to heaven. They were so good, they ordered another round of them. The shrimp buns were also just as good. It was one piece of shrimp, tempura style, in a light airy bun accompanied by a piece of iceberg lettuce and a spicy mayo sauce. The Hamachi Carpaccio, which was thinly sliced yellowtail sashimi with Japanese carpaccio sauce. This was just okay. The presentation was outstanding, but when fish is going to be served liked this, for me personally I want it to be really cold and this was room temperature. The crab and avocado dip was an absolute stand out and I think everyone at the tables favorite by far. It was rather simple too, it was basically just a guac base with crab meat in it. Served with what might have been the smallest box of chips and for more chips it was $2. We hadn't quite finished our dip and the buser had cleared it from our table. The restaurant manager was kind enough to notice this and brought us out a little bit of a smaller version, which we finished before it even hit the table! The shrimp special of the day, was grilled shrimp in a clear garlic sauce. This was another dish that I thought was really good, out of the numerous dishes that we had. The shrimp was grilled nicely and the sauce had hint of flavor but also of chili flakes. It was topped with potato sticks which I haven't had in ages but the two paired nicely together. The Tofu Yasai Tar Tar. What a disappointed. And I feel bad because I was the one who wanted this because of my veghead diet. Talk about boring. They could have made this dish much better by marinading the tofu in the sesame dressing rather than the suggestion of just pouring it over the dish. Again the presentation was great but the flavors didn't come close to its pretty looks. Finally, the Maguro Tataki. This was raw tuna, served with avocado and grapefruits and in the grapefruit juice. The tuna acted a bit like a sponge and soaked up the grapefruit juice, giving this dish a citrusy bite to it. For the busy eatery, the service was very attentive and took good care of us. The decor of this place was really a stand out as well. While it was dark, with the tonal colors of the wall and the giant stick tree brighten the joint up! I'm not sure I'd be running back here anytime soon, although I would like to try the ramen. But with that being said, I'm sure I can get ramen in Ctown for a better price and maybe a little more authentic!

Good place for brunch without much of a wait. I actually prefer the egg dishes over the waffles here. The waffles are on the crispier, lighter side, and I tend to prefer the dense chewy ones from Wafels and Dinges. I highly recommend the cocotte dish. Baked eggs with bacon, goat cheese, and mashed potatoes. Not healthy, but very satisfying. We also ordered the sausages and mashed potatoes, which I didn't like as much. Nice patio in the back when the weather is nice, and you can order baked goods and coffee to go at the front counter.

while they have been open just a few short days, I am really impressed with their spirit, their vision, their sense of adventure.. A bunch of young, first time restaurant owners putting together an eclectic and creative menu.. They will be getting their liquor license soon.. The food was pretty good and unique.. Pot stickers with cheese and salsa would be an example of interesting and creative.. Deep fried deviled eggs with shiso and Srirachi would be another example.. Everyone is super friendly, I think this will be a fun local hang out spot.. Again, brand spaking new, if you are in the neighborhood, stop in and say hello.. Apps are like 6 bucks... Can't beat that..

I think this place is SO OVERRATED.. it's ridiculous. Granted, it's good.. But not amazing.. Came here with two other friends being told that the wait was 40 mins-1 hour to wait nearly 2 hours..I'm willing to wait but only if the stuff is worth it.. The broth was overly salty, oily.. and I just felt unhealthiness flowing through my veins.. Not my thing.. Not worth the wait, or the money or the excess calories. But the meal was somewhat redeemed with a complementary dessert courtesy of my sassy friend who spoke to the manager about the wait..

I have been going here pretty regularly for the past few months. With so many restaurants in Williamsburg fitting the "I want to be different like everyone else mold" this place really stands out. I feel they have one of the best bartenders in the city who makes incredible drinks and the food is nothing short of great. A very simple menu done extremely well. Rye also has a kick ass brunch with this pork belly benedict that is to die for. It's one of the best single brunch items I have ever had. Considering they could be charging much more for what they are putting out I find it to be very good neighborhood pricing.

I love this place but the maitre d can get a little snippy if its crowded--which it often is. Killer wine list, reasonably priced. When I was there, we had squash blossoms, fried and stuffed with crab meat. Beautiful. So tasty. Also, house made dumplings were the shit. I had short ribs, some people I were with had roast chicken (awesome, French train station style). We didn't have dessert so technically the meal hasn't yet ended--I have to go back!

The food here is awesome. Â It's been said. This is more of a public service announcement. Â People - This place is tiny. Enjoy your food. Â Savor it. Â Don't rush. Â But then GET THE HELL OUT. Â THERE ARE PEOPLE WAITING FOR TABLES. Â THEY'VE BEEN WAITING A REALLY LONG TIME. Really, people. Â This isn't the place to sit for an hour after you've finished your meal conversing and slllloooooowwwwlllly sipping your wine. Â There are places for that; they're called wine bars. Â Or even bigger restaurants. Â But not this place. But yeah, definitely come here.

This is a hidden treasure, and as much as I'd like to keep it that way, I just have to let you all know what an amazing place this is. Â Never been before, first time, also in the hospitality industry and was really blown away. Â The carding at the host stand is a bit odd, but the nice host Â kindly offered to check my coat and bag. Â I went after work on a saturday around 6:30 with three other co-workers, no wait and was promptly seated at a very nice spacious table. Â The decor is homey and comfy, with great lighting and sound. Â Made us feel real comfortable real quick. Â Our server Phillip did an outstanding job at guiding us thru the menu and offering wonderful suggestions that we real were blown away with. Â This guy is good, he answered all of our questions(believe me there were many, we in the biz too, lol) with not even a pause. Â I like that service was not overbearing, but still at a very high quality. Â  Great support staff as well, all charming and friendly. Â Almost three hours later we left with quenched thirst and full bellies, even though Â we really only intended to stop in for a quick glass of wine and maybe an appetizer. Â The cheese and wine is priced at a competitive level with restaurants of this caliber, but happy hour(from 5-7pm everyday I think) Â is a steal!!!!! Â We will be going back soon.

I'm going to be generous w/ 2 stars here. Maybe I'm an idiot for ordering non-noodle dishes at a place with the word Noodle in it, but still that's no excuse for lackluster food. The noodle dish I tried was very passable and the congee looked good at the other table but I was very displeased. I'd give this another shot since it's all Chinese clientele and the congee looked good. Ordered: -Shanghai crab meat steamed buns ($6.95/6) - good -Oxtail w/ curry ($6.95) - horrible, tasted like rubber, came w/ potato chunks and diced scallions, my chopstick bounced back when I poked into the meat and I'm not exaggerating, I left half this dish uneaten, there was also 1/4" of oil floating on top, served in casserole clay pot -HK lo mein w/ minced pork ($5.75) - noodles were good, 2pcs of choy sum, i tried this -Iced Tea w/ milk ($2.50) - looked like coffee, tasted like awful lipton, tons of ice Total came out to $15 after everything Pics: meetup.com/teamfoodie/phâ€¦

My girlfriend and I had a pretty good time at Cafe Ghia. We got the tempeh reuben, the pulled pork sandwich, and split a cup of soup. The soup had great depth of flavor, and we both enjoyed our mains. The pulled pork was tender but nothing special, and the sauce was a bit heavy on sugar and light on vinegar, but that's the way most barbecue sauces go I suppose. Their coleslaw was exceptionally flavorful, and the bread in my girlfriend's reuben was terrific, but the soup and these other parts of the meal were not enough to really put the meal on the whole onto a higher plane of quality. The service was friendly and the ambience was nice (quiet and dim giving a sense of intimacy and relaxation while also playing a relatively eclectic selection of music that didn't interfere with conversation), and as I mentioned, some aspects of the food were even better than good, but at $12 for a sandwich or burger and upwards for a proper dinner entree, I just couldn't justify the cost. I did enjoy it enough that if I made more money I could easily imagine wanting to come back. As it is I'm in no rush.

If you want to eat good food with good friends and be in good company among the friendly waitstaff who provide good service in a restaurant with good atmosphere, you have to check this place out. They also play good music in the background. The free popcorn is really good. Wings with bleu cheese also super good. Good stuff.

I was walking around, Â trying to kill time. Â The pictures of menus in the windows cough my attention! Â I looked inside the window thinking yeah right, Â with this prices, Â how good could it be. Â Noticed an A on the door, Â just so happens that I was there 5 minutes before they open. Â Ppl started to wait outside! Â So I figure Hey! Â Give it a shot. Â GOOD CALL!! Â food was very good! Â Service was great!!! Â Price, Â food, Â service were really good, Â check the pictures! Â Must try place!!! Â :-) Happy Happy Happy!
Great brunch on the UWS - will definitely be back. Very friendly service, one drink included, and food was delicious with generous servings.

So totally because of Yelp, I decided to try and get a table here around 7:30 on a Saturday. The host told me that she could seat the 3 of us in 45 minutes at the table outside, which was fine by us. When we checked back in 20 minutes later, she told us we could have a table inside if we could finish in about an hour's time because of a existing reservation. We took the opening and I'm glad I did. There was plenty of time to enjoy our meal. I had the sunchoke salad and the Maine oysters. My entree was the bouillabaisse with a glass of chardonnay. Everything was very good and the host even served us on a few items and she was very friendly and warm. I really liked the whole experience and would definitely return to try the rest of the menu.

Boys: Listen up. Â Take your lady here and woo her in the garden. I went here for brunch with my girlfriends and can't wait to go back for the ideal dinner date. Â We got a great seat outside (which is beyond cute and romantic) soaking up the perfect Sunday afternoon weather. Â They have delicious single cup coffee and a salmon benedict that I'm still thinking about: equal parts bread, egg, and just the right amount of hollandaise sauce. Â We didn't want to leave, so you better believe, us belles ordered up some dessert. Now fellas, if you're still reading, and you want to score extra brownie points with the good lookin' girl you've taken to this sweet spot, if they have it, you best order their semifreddo. Â Don't even ask her if she wants it. Â She does. Â And if they are all out of this special, the tiramisu won't sent you back either. Â  As you can tell, just one day here with my girls has revved me up for round two with one lucky dude.

I'll give Quaint 4 stars for the outdoor seating which was gorgeous on a lovely summer night and the comfortable indoor setting - for that Quaint lives up to its name. Nice, clean and casual bistro. The menu is small! Thought it was kind of funny that pasta of the day had "m/p" next to it...it's not lobster. Would be cool to just have a special and add pasta dinner choices to the menu. Anyway, I went with the Mac n' cheese appetizer and the roasted chicken breast for dinner. For the price a little extra would be nice. Mac n' cheese was tasty and was enough for two people to split. The roasted chicken breast was succulent and tender, really good I recommend you try it. Waiter was cool and often came to the table bringing water. Overall if I'm in the neighborhood again I'd come back.

I have to say that I am a big big fan of Gyu-Kaku. I have tried Gyu-Kaku at various locations, and I love them all!!! This is awesome Japanese BBQ, and you can get a great price if you go during their happy hour. Beef tongue is always my favorite, and I always get Green Tea Mille Crepe for dessert. The service is always very good. They are very friendly, and they explain everything very clearly. For this one in particular, I like the environment the best because it is spacious.
I really liked their Katsu.. I forgot which one I got but I thought it was great. Big portions too.

It is hard not to go overboard with the food here, because everything is great. I try hard to order the "weirdest" stuff on a menu like this--things you don't get to order just anywhere. Traif listed both "Roasted Bone Marrow" and "Pork Cheeks" and those definitely qualified as unique. Both were wonderful, though the pork cheeks more so. The roasted bone marrow was more ceremonial than anything--there is hardly anything to eat--though the beef tartare (raw ground beef + eggs + spices) was delightful if you're into that sort of thing. The dessert that they are perhaps most attractive for, the bacon doughnuts, is precious. The fried dough itself is light, fluffy and a picture of perfection. Served with a dollop coffee ice cream and with crumbled bacon on top, it is a seriously American breakfast. The bacon, however, is disappointing--a small notch above bacos bacon bits. This happens a lot with desserts with bacon incorporated, so whatever. Don't miss this place!

A good stopping place if you need a quick bite to eat -the tea was nice and hot; the sandwich was just the right size. Â For the upper east side the price was fine with very prompt service. Â I noticed people lined up for the coffee. Â It is tiny and very crowded-not a place for large parties; families of 4 were jammed in at the small tables.

Everything was amazing! Â I ordered the Fresh Fruit Short Stack, which was perfectly crisp and fluffy with just the right amount of chocolate and banana. Â I didn't even need syrup! Â My BF ordered chicken and waffles, which was again, nothing short from perfect. Â He then ordered the chicken biscuit, which without even taking a bite, you knew would blow your mind. Â The mimosa brought me the perfect buzz to heighten my taste buds for perfection. Â Everyone needs to try this place!

The only reason I can't give this place 5 stars is because I've had Boiling Crab in LA and although this place comes close in comparison, it just doesn't hit the mark like Boiling Crab does. If you're from LA or have had Boiling Crab you'll know what I'm talking about. They don't take reservations but you CAN call ahead and put your name down. My fiancee and I had drinks from the bar while we were waiting for our table. I had the peach lemonade and she had the mojito. Both were really good but took a bit longer than expected, considering that the bar was empty and no one else was waiting for drinks. The apps here are pretty good. We had the mac and cheese, crab cake, and calamari. The calamari is ok and the crab cake is decent .. but the mac and cheese is ridic. get it. The shrimp here is consistently good. Very big and succulent. I only wish they'd let it sit in the sauce for longer to let it soak through the shell into the meat. Once you peel the shrimp you will have to dip it back into the sauce. But that's a minor thing since the sauce is awesome and I would probably dip it back in anyway. The one time I had crawfish here it was just ok. The meat was pretty brittle and I had a hard time pulling it out of the shell without it breaking. It might have been because it wasn't crawfish season. Haven't tried the crab or lobster yet but plan to. Also once you finish all your shrimp/crab/lobster or whatnot, make sure to grab a couple orders of steamed rice and mix it in with your leftover sauce.

Our wait was an hour and a half! Good food at a good price, but is it worth the wait... dunno. Noise level doesn't really allow conversation. Our table of four got a wide variety of balls and sauces but we voted that the veggie balls were the best! Service was attentive despite the wall-to-wall people.
Stuck to their more popular dishes and I would give flavor and quality a D+. Would not recommend.

OOOMMMGGGG! Where do I start...I dont understand why this restaurant has so many good reviews. Well I was totally fooled by their reviews. I called in and ordered at about 3:30 in the afternoon, I was told 20-30 minutes to receive the order. All I ordered was Â the most basic food to make on this planet. (wht rice and roasted chicken) It took them nearly a bit over an hour to get my food delivered. The manager is the worse he did not want to accept the delay and mess up on my order. He in no way wanted to accommodate me as the paying customer. Will not recommend anyone to eat here.

Well yes, you're going to be waiting. A long time. The hosts were a little unwelcoming, but hey I get it, long morning to be dealing with people. As we became increasingly hungry, we started yelping and I didn't know what to think. Will this be worth it?! It was. We both got omelettes but split the little pastry plate first bc we were both about to pass out. Got the deal w the meal and mimosa for $15, drinks were good. Muffins were yum too! Our server was welcoming and nice which was great. She also noticed we were ready to order immediately and was cool about it. Liked that. I saved the receipt so I could give her a shout out, but of course the receipt paper faded and now I don't know. But she was amazing... thank you! The place is a little loud, but the food came out quicker than expected. Made us wonder why the wait is so long- are these people hanging out after eating? It wasn't really that type of atmosphere, but oh well who knows.... anyways we got fed within minutes, and our omelettes were amazing. Everything tasted fresh and was definitely not a disappointment. Would return, perhaps on a weekday when maybe it wasn't as crazy busy!

The food here is great but the wait is always ridiculous and the cashier is always on her period. I highly recommend the fried avocado/jalapeno taco, al pastor and skirt steak tacos. However, make sure to eat them quickly since the one tortilla is not really enough (this is usually not a problem).

what a little gem in the midtown east neighborhood. Â i've walked past sofia's over a dozen times, staring in awe at the colorful lights that are hung year round, but never had a chance to go in until yesterday. as i expected, the place is very small. Â you can call it quaint or cozy, but it is very small and they don't take reservations. Â there is also no waiting area so as you're hovering over other diners, it can get uncomfortable waiting for a table . Â in other words, you'll want to race there from your midtown office in order to get a table. Â i also overheard that they do not accommodate parties larger than 4. so, i got to sofia's around 6pm and snagged a table for 2. Â the sweet riesling that i found on their menu brought back memories of when i first discovered this light white wine. Â my friend and i also got their special pancetta pizza of the day. Â the thin crust was right up my alley and after a few slices, i was disappointed that i didn't have any room left to try any of their other delectable small plates. i'm looking forward to returning again for another after work drink/light meal with a friend.
this place is always busy and crowded. It takes awhile to even be acknowledged by the staff. The food is good and I love the sangria! You will get buzzed from it.
Always a treat to come here when I visit NYC. Good food at a great price. Be prepared to wait during lunch and dinner rush.

My favorite restaurant of all time. There's always a wait to get into the place, but it's totally worth it! The soup dumplings? THE BEST. They're famous for good reason. And the dumplings aren't the only worthwhile thing on the menu! Try the Shanghai noodles. When I die, heaven had better be FULL of them, because they are the tastiest noodles I've ever eaten! I'd recommend Joe's to anyone. Yes, it's crowded and noisy, and since it's family style you may be sharing a table with a stranger, but it's all part of the experience. Everyone should go here at least once for amazing, authentic food!
It's my favorite restaurant. Â It's a seasonal menu with delicious food. Restaurant can be a little dark and difficult for parents to see the menu. Get the baby Jesus cake!!

Just ate here for restaurant week. Dinner was very good (grilled peach and arugula salad, skate entree). The dessert, however, was a work of GENIUS. Billed as a "spring roll" of cheesecake with graham cracker crust....the outside tasted like a crispy, paper think churro and was filled with warm, light, luscious flavorful cheesecake. One bite in I said "This is the best thing I've eaten this year." Bravo. True brilliance on the part of the Chef.

Yerba Buena was a great dining experience. The food is fresh and delicious, the cocktails are unique and complementary to the food, service is friendly and responsive. The East Side establishment was a little small, but it gives it a nice private ambiance that is conducive to creating an atmosphere that actually allows you to conversate with those that you are dining with. I would definitely go back again... and I'm actually wondering why I have not yet done so.

I love good hangover food and this is on the top of the list. It is not good for you but it tastes sooo good that you do not really care as soon as you have your first bite. I am not sure if I just do not do spicy or that kind of spice or if the food has been off a couple of times but the last two times my visit to the bathroom has not been pleasant every time after. That is up to you to find out I guess... Because it tastes so damn good I had to try a second time to see if it was just me or if it was the food, that says something about how tasty it is. When you go just make sure you find the right cart, that was a challenge to find out though. I went to the South east corner of 53rd street cart, just to specify because I have noticed that the reviews for this is for both businesses on each side of the street and they are in actuality competitors.

Some of my best dining experiences have been at fusty restaurants (Le Manoir Au Quat Saisons, Le Maloises, Almeida), and consequently I am always whatever the opposite of nonplussed is when a restaurant looks a little homely and lived-in; after all, I'm here to eat the food, not the cutlery. Luckily, GT delivers excellent cooking which nullifies the stodginess of the surroundings (Biggie Best drapes, overstuffed furniture, cheap-looking ceramic pots stuffed with daisies). We had the seasonal tasting menu. Each dish delivered bolder flavours than the last, starting with the smoked arctic char and pickled ramps (is there a more now ingredient?), followed by a buttery crust/wobbly interior spinach and goat cheese tartlet, thence on to a porgy (not a pig as I learnt) fillet with beautiful summer squash and assorted blanched greenery and a slick of lemon-yellow beurre blanc, then a punchy goat curry with one spinach lasagne handkerchief, an ethereally light curry sauce and wonderfully fresh summer veg (question: why swiss chard and not callaloo, in keeping with the Jamaican theme?), and dessert. Mine, the berry sorbet with verbena granite, was the meal's only misstep - too much granite, looking like a puddle of piss-yellow snow, and taste wearysome after the first couple of exploratory bites. My wife had a cheese plate, which was delicious, although a little chutney/herbage/fruit wouldn't have gone amiss. Good service, lengthy wine/spirit list an additional plus.

It's a wonderful place with a lot of choices and the food was good but not splendid. It's more a tourity place that you really could feel a restaurant atomosphere. I feld a bit rushed by the waiter to eat and to pay..... PG

I am in love with Traif. It is great to have a restaurant of this caliber in Brooklyn. A cute and casual ambiance set the tone for a relaxing dining experience. The service is and food are on par with high end American New restaurants but with a Brooklyn price tag - how could you not love it?! The highlights of my meal were the tuna tartare and the bacon donuts with dulce de leche ice cream. They had my heart at bacon donuts! Other great items include bacon wrapped figs and the chopped chicken livers with balsamic bacon toasts, rosemary and shallots. I will definitely make another trip to Traif for the tasting menu.

This place is fantastic. Â The specials are always wonderful, as is the regular menu. Â The food is great quality and cooked to perfection. Â The wine list is nice as well. Â This place gets crowded so its a good idea to make a reservation.. Â I have heard the outdoor garden in the back is nice to sit..but have not gotten to sit there yet. Â  I love this place....and will continue to return.

So we're here from out of town. Â We are staying within .2 miles at the Mondrian Soho. Â We call and the hectic annoyed female answering the phone demands to know the exact address AND cross streets of our hotel for delivery. WTF? Â If we are in a strange hotel in a strange city within .2 miles do we know? Â Nasty woman. Â No pizza stars for bad NYC attitude.

My number one brunch place, and a favorite dinner option in brooklyn. Â Food always fresh, honest, tasty, and reasonably priced. lots of local produce, and usually a few different fish and other great protein options. Â straight forward cooking, good ingredients, fair portions. Â the space gets a bit loud, but the service is always pretty good. I go back whenever I can

The wait can be 30 min to an hour for dinner, but it's well worth it. Â Haven't had a bad item on Â the menu. Â Loved the yellowtail collar and kimchi fried rice! If you're adventurous, try the chicken gizzards.

Sooooo here goes..... I wanted to try one of the best brunch locations in Brooklyn, and The Farm on Adderley came up. The reviews were interesting as well. Upon arrival, I noticed the resturant was a little busy, the hostess looked a little "overwelmed". After waiting 40 minutes to be seated, the seating area was a little tight. The atmoshere was cool though. I had the Sausage and Eggs dish and a side of Bacon. The scrambled eggs were really good, however the sausage was UNDERCOOKED and most of the bacon was burned. There goes my dish!! My girlfriend had the French toast and strawberries, which was AMAZINGGGGGGGGGG!!! I was soooo Jealous! The service was standard. I'll go back to give it another shot, especially with the great reviews. Â Maybe next time it'll be better.

Came here last night with a few friends. Â I had the mussels that were ok, and the shrimp & lobster grits that would have been better if the seafood was not overcooked. Â Staff and ambiance was great...My food? Â Not so much.
Isn't she lovely! Lovely Irish lady serving. Fish n Chips also good. Chicken Soup very generous. Lots of locals.

I have not been to the joint a mere few yards from my place of employ but my beloved co-worker just termed it as: "A joyless hipster sh/thole...with a decent cappuccino and an OK blueberry muffin. It's everything I hate about Brooklyn...I can stay home [in BK] to be insulted." So the five stars are to offset her otherwise hilarious observation. I will skulk in there shortly. Comments to come...

This place is the epitome of what brunch should be in a city that is the love child of NYC and Paris. Â It is by now a NYC institution and its reputation for great ambience and very good food and drink is well deserved. Â  The place itself is beautiful, especially at the holidays. Â It always draws a diverse, well-heeled and interesting crowd of people speaking a variety of languages. Â The service is surprisingly warm and very competent. I have been a few times for brunch and it has never disappointed. Â If you are a Bloody Mary fan, by all means order one (or more!) here. Â Ask for it spicy and you will not be disappointed. Â Theirs are so good that you will be craving one for days afterward. Â  On our last visit, we shared a plate of Wellfleet oysters that were so fresh and delicious you would think they dug them out of the sand a minute before. Â My friend had the grilled ham and cheese which she pronounced amazing and I had a delicious herb omelet with gruyere cheese and smoked salmon (the $9 surcharge for the latter was a bit irksome, admittedly, but the buzz from the Bloody's made me not care too much). Â We also had a cone of their delicious, salty frites. Â Also be sure to try the whole grain bread. Â Yum. We shared profiteroles for dessert (and from the looks of it, so did a lot of the tables near us). Â They pour the chocolate sauce at the table and leave the remains thereof on in a pitcher. Â So good I poured it onto a spoon and almost mainlined it. Â  A brunch like this is not cheap by any means (with tip about a C note per person) but you don't (or shouldn't) do this every day and you walk out feeling great about life, so what is the harm once in a while?

Went with a group of friends last week and had a great time. Â The selection of beers is truly impressive. Â Dozens of hard to find beers on tap, including a delicious cask ale. The food was also a pleasant surprise. Â We sampled a large portion of the menu. Â Really enjoyed the tacos, meatballs, deep dish pizza, buttermilk chicken sandwich and short rib empanadas. Â They have a smoker on premise that they use throughout the menu (smoked meats in the tacos, brisket, smoked turkey, etc.) Â They're still working through typical opening issues-they just opened last week- but the service was friendly and efficient. Â Great addition to the neighborhood!

OMFG this place is awesome. Â Went here last night for a really late dinner, got in at 9:40 pm, but seated at around 10:30 pm. Â The ambience and service were awesome. Â Here's what we got. 1. Â Round of sapporo beers ($6) 2. Â Salmon sashimi ($16) - This was a great starter, included slightly seared salmon around of bed of veggies. Â There was also small pieces of grapefruit which happily bursted with tartness. Â Also, great mayo sauce drizzed on the plate helped accentuate salmon. 3. Â Traditional ramen ($13) - GREAT, AWESOME, FLAVORFUL broth. Â Only came with 2 slices of meat and it wasn't even that great. Â However, I slurped the entire thing up. 4. Â Modern ramen ($13) - A whole new taste that seems like it's driven by satay sauce. Â I initially thought that this was my favorite, but it could be a bit bold to eat an entire bowl. 5. Â Miso ramen ($12) - Without noodles, the broth was sweet, especially for a dinner entree. Â But this has to be eaten with the thicker ramen and it's perfectly complimented. Â  We shared everything, so as I finished 1/3 of my bowl, we literally switched three times. Â I thought that was a great way to eat it, just because all the broths are so different. Â Go there now!!! Â GREAT place and I wish they had it in Chicago :(

Hands down my favorite bar in Queens. Best times to go are happy hour and on the weekend for brunch or just drinks (pre-7pm). They have super delicious and creative cocktails and a small but solid food menu. The bartenders are all wonderfully personable and possibly the least pretentious set in the city.

A nifty, casual bar that's worth traveling across Brooklyn for. I live in Crown Heights and happily take 2 trains to get here. They have great daily beer/shot specials, a big booze list and beer selection, board games to play, juke box with true classics, and yeah, free unlimited cheese balls! I haven't tried their food yet, but I've heard good things (except an updated review down the line). This is the best hipster-esque dive bar I've been to.

Our reservations were on a Friday evening at 6:30 pm but they were accommodating and allowed us to push it back to 8 since we had Grimaldi's around 5pm. We had a fairly large party of 10 and sat in the back of the restaurant. Since they are currently under construction, it was a bit hard to find since you have to enter the lobby and then head downstairs to find the entrance. We probably ordered over 20 plates of food but since the party was large, I only had the dishes at our side of the table. We had the assorted sashimi, the crab clay pot rice (this takes a while to make so be sure to order this first), tuna tartare, tamago squares with meat inside, pork belly, and wagyu beef that they cook in front of you with butter. My favorite dishes would have to be the tuna tartare and the wagyu beef. The wagyu literally melted in your mouth and smelled sooo good since it was cooked on the table. Since we had about 20 dishes and sake, it was $70 per person after taxes and tip. I will definitely be returning here the next time I visit!

this place is REAL good but not perfect. -first dinner there was amazing. absolutely no complaints. SO GOOD. -second dinner was just okay. we ordered the same things as the first visit, but they were not prepared nor did they taste the same. one of my biggest pet peeves is when a restaurant is not consistent. -first brunch there was good. VERY reasonably priced...well, aside from the orange juice. the juice was listed on the board but no price was given, so when we got the bill and almost HALF of it was attributed to two glasses of OJ at $6 (!!!) a piece, we were feeling very keanu reeves ("woah."). -second brunch was good and we steered clear of the juice this time. however, the table next to us had some people who were clearly friends with the waitress and they received their food a good 10 minutes before us, even though they sat down AFTER we did. tsk tsk! oh and they also have what my boyfriend has declared the Best Dessert Ever: a braised pear on ice cream with chocolate sauce. so good.

Don't turn around, uh oh. Â Der Kommissar's in town, whoa uh oh... I encourage you to listen to this while you read the review. Â Go ahead, live a little. youtube.com/watch?v=hIZSâ€¦ Â  So I now have a favorite beer and sausage place in the neighborhood! Â Very small and unassuming space. Â Nice beer selection, about 5 or 6 taps and about the same amount of bottles. Â Very chill vibe. Â Cool bartender not afraid to shoot the breeze with you. Â Oh yes, and the sausages. Â Tried the kÃ¤sekrainer (cheese-filled), the kielbasa and one other that was a little spicy and garlicky. Â All were delicious. Â Also had sides of kraut, spicy pickled veggies and pretzel bread, all of which were also good. Â Odd drawing on the wall that we couldn't really figure out, but I'm ok with that. Alles klar, Herr Kommissar?

I love you Vesta. Â Delicious food, cozy atmosphere and friendly service. Â I have gotten their hangover pizza. Â Twice. Â It's that good. Â It's a thin crust pizza that is layered with a slightly spicy, tangy tomato sauce, cheese, chunks of sausage, bacon crumbles, seasoned potatoes, and topped with a sunny side up egg. Â You can't finish this in one sitting so it's great for sharing or taking home the leftovers. Â The warm bankie is quite yummy too. Â I was a bit skeptical about the baby jesus cake because, ew dates? Â Do not miss out on this!!! Â It doesn't have any overpowering flavors, which I think is a plus in this case. Â The cake is warm and moist, drizzled in some kind of syrup, and served with a cannelle of fresh whipped cream. Â Definitely one of my favorite places in Astoria.

With exotic combinations of too many flavors sometimes the dish gets lost in the ingredients. Innovative or simply gastronomic acrobatics, I'll leave that to someone else to decide. Our table tried a great range of dishes, small medium, large plates as well as desserts. The common denominator was- the flavors become confused and the basic ingredients lost in over sauced, and drowned food. The staff is nice, attentive, courteous, and a bit pretentious. There is talent in this restaurant, but don't hide it under the layers of cream, butter, and salt.

My boyfriend and I stumbled upon this place after hitting the gym. What a diamond in the rough. The bar is very roomy. It's long and wide. There's tables everywhere. We ended up going all the way to the back and sat at a table with very cushiony seats. Our server, Monique was very pleasant and helpful. She handled my very picky boyfriend quite well lol We ordered the pulled pork sliders, French fries and chicken quesadilla. Everything was very yummy. The fries were so good and whatever mayo they serve with it is to die for. I would eat it with a spoon if it was socially accepted lol I got the mango margarita. It was so good that my boyfriend ended up getting one as well after the espresso margarita he ordered, which was very strong and, as he said it, difficult to drink. I tried it and it was just too much. Too much alcohol and too much coffee. We spent about three hours there. It wasn't crowded and probably would have been quieter had it not been for the group of four guys that were sitting in our vicinity and insisted on screaming and yelling because why? I don't know. The only thing is tv overload! Wow, there are so many tv's and they are SO bright. My boyfriend is sensitive to bright light, so the tv overload made him slightly uncomfortable. We will definitely come back to this place. I am eager to try other items on their menus.

Fantastic accidental experience as an alternative to the 40minute wait for Rosewater down the street. Â Quaint and clean interior with excellent service. Â The only downside I can think of is that there is only one bathroom, so plan your break wisely during a crowded day. Â Now for the food. My friends ordered the vegetable pie with pear chutney which they gave an excellent review. Â The Eggs Florentine I experienced literally gave me a food orgasm. Â The most divine flavor I've tasted in a breakfast dish, and the portion was just right. Â If you want an experience like that, go now. BTW they offer you booze in the morning, so if you need a little hair of the dog during Sunday brunch, look no further.

I don't get this place. It's very tiny and you are basically bumping into the other table whenever you move your chair. I'm a thin guy and felt huge sitting in this obnoxious place. The food is mediocre. Nothing great. I ordered the eggs Florentine with a side salad. I found a dead ladybug in my salad. When I informed our server, she goes, "ohh. sometimes they are in the arugula." Umm. That is definitely not something you should say to a customer... Â They never sent over a manager or comp'd my meal. I just received another salad which I was inspecting the entire time for more bugs. If you want tiny portion sizes, terrible customer service, and mediocre food then this place is for you!

This place blew my little mind, and my mind is not easily blown when it comes to ramen. We went at a super weird time on a weekday, so there was no wait whatsoever. Score. A couple days later I walked by and there was a two hour wait. Fools! I hadn't eaten all day because I was hungover in one of the worst, hottest NYC days of the summer so I was cranky and needed this to cure me. I ordered the Tori Ramen, which the waiter described as light and delicate, and indeed it was. The broth was a combination of pork and chicken, the noodles were silky and perfect, the chashu was thin and not fatty, the soy egg and bamboo shoots, nori and shiso all complemented the lightness of the broth and noodles excellently. My friends both for the Akamaru Modern ramen. I tried the broth, which was a pork broth seasone with scallions, garlic oil and red miso paste that you mix in, was to die for. Absolutely incredible. Our waiter was really knowledgeable and answered every single question we had, describing each type of ramen perfectly! I wanted to try all of the ramens. I'm actually kind of sad that I live in SF, a ramen desert, and won't be able to come back here in the near future. I'm still daydreaming about it!!!

4.5 stars... I friggin LOVE this place... not only bc they serve a mean side of grits, but bc every bite i take of everything i order is absolutely delicious. omg the grits. i love the grits... almost makes up for the fact that the mac n cheese isnt available for brunch. Grilled chicken club.. moist, salty, perfectly mayo'd. crayfish omelette - sublime. poached eggs with ham and fried green tomatoes with gravy over biscuits... - like dinner for breakfast in the most fabulous way, and heaven on earth? the jalapeno bloody mary. service - great. atmosphere - casual and cute. i'll admit the prices are a bit high for brunch, and there are no brunch cocktails included in your meal price, but everything is fresh, and have i mentioned the grits?? after you're done eating, go sit outside on the rocking chairs to digest. bubby's, i love you.

This review is for the cellar downstairs. The waitress was very friendly & she knew the menu very well. Â She gave my friend and I a sample of white wine which I ordered a glass of. Â It wasn't sweet & it was nice & dry. My friend & I had the olives, the Beecher's three cheese plate & prosciutto. Â Everything was delicious. Â  I would definitely go back here. Â The only thing preventing me from giving it one more star is the noise level. Â It seemed to be a "chick spot" at the time & it was pretty loud.

Lam Zhou is my favorite Chinese Noodle place in the city. It is cheap, delicious, and authentic. As you walk in, you immediately get the feel of a chinese place, with old women making dumplings in front of you, locals shouting out orders, and the trademark linoleum floors you find in chinatowns across the world. I had the Beef noodle soup and I was definitely impressed. From the chew of the noodles, to the amount of beef they gave, for five bucks, I'm not sure you could get a better steal in Chinatown. Again, do not expect service...or great "ambiance", just enjoy good cheap food. It also helps if you can speak chinese, but again, that is not necessary. Lam Zhou really is as good as advertised.

Absolutely amazing! The pork belly buns, squid, and ramen were out of this world. All the servers work as a team so you don't have to wait around for your own waitress/waiter to receive service. If the menu is confusing, they will explain everything to you in a clear manner because the servers are very well trained and know everything on the menu. This restaurant is immaculate all around, including the restrooms and decor is great. Only negative thing I'd add is that there's a bit of a wait (and you cannot make reservations) but the food is very much worth it. Stop reading and just make your way there NOW!!!

The food was lovely but there were very few options without dairy and unfortunately very little effort was made to make a person with allergies feel welcome. The waitress did ask the kitchen but came back with only two options and never checked if the bread served had dairy. Overall the pasta was delicious (a bit too much sauce for my taste) but if you have any gluten or dairy allergies there are very FEW options and the kitchen seemed fairly unwilling to be accommodating.

Loved it! Want it in California! They need to expand this awesome concept. I loved everything about it. The casual openness of the dining area merging into the kitchen. A big community table with surrounding tables. Great wait staff. And most of all the menu and food. Tried the special pork, manchego, and chile meatball as well as the veggie. Both fabulous. Had a perfect salad with butter lettuce, asparagus, fava beans, bread crumbs. I wanted everything on the menu. The Tarragon lemonade was also wonderful. Prices on everything were great.
so good love this plave!!! best brunch eva even though we had to wait

NUM PANG might make the best sandwiches in all of new york city. i would pit this sandwich menu against that of any high end restaurant, shack, food truck, cart, you name it. truly AMAZING amongst the all star roster, the stand outs are as follows: runner up - BRISKET SANDWICH - absolutely tender and sweet. beautiful beef flavor, not overpowering, substantial, blends perfectly with the crunchy Asian style slaw #1 menu item - PORK BELLY SANDWICH - this pork belly is cooked to perfection. slowly braised for tenderness and depth of flavor, quick sear for caramelized exterior, perfect amount of Asian style sweetness, complemented well by the thin layer of pear slices. the crunchy slaw is again fresh and an adequate textural contrast. the key to these sandwiches is two fold. all sandwiches have a spicy aioli that coats the interior of the wonderfully toasted rolls. these sandwiches are perfect and no one should recommend any changes. i have been back several times and will continue to do so. the other location near grand central puts out quality product as well. just when i thought nothing could be better about this establishment, i hear notorious big rhyming in the back ground as I experience gustatory pleasure ...

Attended a dinner with a seriously large group tonight at this restaurant and was completely wowed by the experience. The food was fantastic. Started with the arugula salad, which was "perfect" and followed with roast chicken over polenta. I don't even like polenta but it was wonderful in this dish. The service was both efficient and gracious. Overall, an extraordinary experience. I will hurry back.

I wish I could say the pizza was fantastic, but... it's okay. It's more of an experience rather than a great meal out. We got there an hour or two before closing on a Sunday, and the seating area already had the gate rolled down. However, we put our name down for two pizzas, the margherita and the meatier one. We waited at a nearby Dunkin' Donuts for an hour before knocking on Di Fara's back door and sitting at one of the few tables inside. You may have to stand for 20 minutes until someone gets up from a table. After one-and-a-half to two hours, our approx. $35-each pizzas were ready. The first thing I noticed was that they were drenched in olive oil. The toppings slid right off the pizzas. They were thin, slightly chewy, and soggy, except for the parts of the crust that were burned black. The pizza tasted fresh and flavorful, but it might have just been all of the oil. I gobbled up two slices before calling it quits. Our party of four departed with about one full pizza's worth of leftovers. It's cool to see old man Dom making the pizzas, and the guy taking the orders is very friendly. That being said, I don't think this place is worth a pilgrimage if you're coming from far away, although it might be fun for a one-time thing. It's simply too expensive and too long a wait, and the pizza quality isn't worth it.

My boyfriend and I went here for restaurant week a few nights ago--the food was excellent but the service was not up to par. We had to wait almost an hour beyond our 10pm reservation time to be seated. After the meal, they brought us the wrong check three times (while we waited yet another 30 minutes), as they kept trying to charge us for alcohol that we had not ordered. Somewhat understandable given the chaos of restaurant week, yet still a bit disappointing. The food, on the other hand, was delicious. They brought out a complimentary calamari dish to start out with--it was perfectly fried (crispy but not greasy). I ordered the peekytoe crab salad with market vegetables as my appetizer (it was delicate and tasty) and my boyfriend ordered the house-made burrata with strawberries (also delicious). We both ordered the beef tenderloin entree--mine was perfectly cooked and I loved the swiss chard that it came with. We then split the molten chocolate cake for dessert--warm and gooey on the inside with a crisp crust on the outside. I would definitely recommend the restaurant week menu--just be prepared for an overwhelmed/annoyed waitstaff and a long wait. I would give Perry St 4 stars for the food, and 2 for the terrible service = 3 stars from me.

I'm giving it three stars, because although it was quite delicious, I thought that the itty bitty sandwich was overpriced. I went obviously to try it out since there was so much hype surrounding its opening. I had the veal meatball sandwich. It tasted great and you could tell the ingredients were fresh. However, the sandwich, at $8 is not a bargain. I also tried the blood orange lemonade (I think that was what it was) and I agree with another reviewer that it was way too tarte. It's definitely a good place to go to once, but it will be tough on my wallet to go there everyday for a meal that won't leave me feeling full.

i want to give this place 5 stars but the wait is ridiculous! it's worth it, but i've taken so many people here when we were hungry and they got so exhausted from waiting, they didn't fully enjoy the experience. therefore, go 30min-hr EARLIER of when you actually plan to eat. free cornbread. always got the chicken and waffle (white meat). portion size is pretty diesel, even for guys so don't get greedy! tried the yams and mac and cheese as sides. i didn't particularly enjoy them. their sweet tea is REALLY SWEET. beware. haha. also. they won't seat you until your whole party is there, so make sure you all arrive together.
