Love that everything is organic, and that they have gluten free and vegan options. _ 3 BEAN & SQUASH SOUP +QUINOA Â  Â  Â  Â  Â  Â  Â  Â  Â ($4 cup/$6 bowl, +$1.50 to add quinoa/brown rice) _ BROCCOLI SAUTEED w/garlic ($6) Â  Â  Â  Â  Â  Â  Â  Â  Â  Â  Â  Â  Needs more garlic. _ BLACK BEAN & SWEET POTATO CAKE ($8) Â  Â  Â  Â  Â  Â  Â  Â  Â Topped with salsa which is fresh and delicious Â  Â  Â  Â  Â  Â  Â  Â  Â but overpowered the cake flavor. Â  Â  Â  Â  Â  Â  Â  Â  Â Next time, I'd ask them to put the salsa on the side. _ WALNUT BROWNIE a la mode: Â  Â  Â  Â  Â  Â  Â  Â  Â  Â  Â Vegan & Gluten free. Â  Â  Â  Â  Â  Â  Â  Â  Â  Â  Â Topped with a scoop of vegan vanilla coconut milk ice cream Â  Â  Â  Â  Â  Â  Â  Â  Â  Â  Â (choice of vanilla or chocolate ice cream) and chocolate sauce on top. Interior: Cool paintings, gr8 mix of music (funk, r&b, salsa), gr8 service, friendly staff. We were greeted, served and seen off warmly. Affordable organic food w/gf + vegan options! Will gladly return!

This restaurant is the perfect UWS Brunch spot. The outdoor seating is great. I ordered the capellini which is angel hair pasta with lobster, jumbo shrimp and sea scallops. The jumbo shrimp, lobster and sea scallops were bursting with flavor! So delicious I'm salivating as I'm typing but the pasta was weak. It's tossed in a lobster broth but I felt it needed Parmesan to add a little kick...a little something. For dessert I ordered the caramel cake, it was just too sweet for my liking. Everything here was good, and I probably will be coming back when the outdoors seating opens. Â Great spot Isabella's!

Came here for a birthday dinner on a freezing evening. Was underwhelmed to learn we would be dining in the backyard, but the space heaters (and our big raucous group's collective body heat) warmed the space nicely. We had tapas served family-style and everything was excellent. I mean really, really good. The waitress was great about keeping our glasses full of sangria, and was a good sport about the fact that together, the twenty of us can be a real pain in the you-know-what. I wish I could remember what we ate, but all I can remember is that it was delicious. It's not far from our home, so we'll certainly be going back.

Amazingly delicious risotto, creative combinations, and such a cute little place. Â Every time I go the staff are super friendly and accomodating. Â The food is reasonably priced and you leave full and satisfied. Â I love the flavors they offer and the range of salads and appetizers. Â I keep going back and never get tired of it.

I loved Alta. My sister was visiting from DC and we wanted to go to a tapas bar to get drinks and some food to snack on. This place was perfect! It is adorable inside! We sat upstairs on the cool little balcony that overlooks the downstairs dining area. We ended up ordering entirely too many tapas for two people lol but it was fun to try everything! Everything was delicious! My sister has a gluten allergy (womp womp) but we were still able to order a ton of yummy tapas (sans gluten) and I didn't even have to complain because everything was still delicious! I will definitely be back to Alta. Maybe with my boyfriend next time. Definitely a good date spot.

BXL Zoute is a great place to have lunch or dinner and I surely enjoyed a good belgian beer here. They have a wide selection of draft beer and good knowledge of each one which they happily share. They even stored my luggage during the day and gave me a good and fast lunch before heading to the airport. Service was excellent. When I'm back in NYC, I'll go back for sure, love it there!

Pork belly with poached egg was delicious, although a little bit of a small serve. The Shan Noodles were very plentiful and much better value, with an amazing broth. Definitely sit out back, and the $15 all you can drink self serve Yeunling is a steal too. Definitely would go back...
Wow. Best pizza I had in NYC. I didnt know how I would feel about trying NYC pizza because I'm from Chicago, but it was great! YUM!
Great service, very friendly staff. Â Food was above average but the wait was a tad long. Â Overall pleasant experience and would go again.

There is this orange sauce to dip the fries in, or you can squirt it on your burger. Just find it and use it because it's great. I order it RARE!!! So that it weighs more. I feel like rare meet is lower in fat. In fact, I know it is. For a fact. I wouldn't say: the best burgers ever!!! because I love In-n-Out Burger but I do thank my lucky stars that this place is right down the block from me. Sometimes I fantasize about emptying my bank account and just shuttling back and forth between Blue Ribbon Sushi and Bonnie's Grill until I feel sick or run out of cash. I LOVE: burgers I WISH: bigger rootbeer

the place has great food, at super cheap prices.... so expect to wait a while for a table on the weekends..... it seems its a good date place, for cheap guys to take their dates...hahaha... Drinks are a good Â and service is great. If your date takes you there..then u know hes cheap but has a good palate...lol

after long day of shopping, I love the convenience of this place by Union Sq. went there for a quick dinner on Fri around 7:30pm and there was no line. Â I got the PULLED PORK sandwich...was juicy, bread was light and crispy & topped off with special creamy sauce. dive place & tiny but they have a spiral staircase for seating upstairs. would try the pork belly & catfish sandwich...and ginger beer next time.

Went here last night for the first time and was overly impressed by everything from the quality of the meal, service, ambiance, and more. My girlfriend and I ate in the back garden section, definitely worth the extra 15 minute. The downstairs looked intriguing as well and housed a chill instrumental jazz band at a tolerable volume. We each had our own pie for our meals and that alone was more than satiating. Ideal place for a romantic evening with your significant other, amongst other occasions.

Overall food was good, especially the sardines, pork chops, trout and octopus. Not really into the pumpkin goat cheese, skirt steak, and the cod fish croquettes. Didn't get to try the more exotic stuff as my friends were a little squeamish. Service was sub-par, we arrived 30 min late for our reservation and were promptly dismissed in an 1 hr 30 min - the next seating. Meanwhile if our waitress was a little more attentive we'd be able to have a coffee. The other peeve was the poor ventilation, you needn't go out after coz everyone will know you had dinner at Casa Mono. Bar Jamon i suspect would be a mad house as i was there at 5:30 and by 6 it was already packed. Not recommended to hang out, mabe in the summer when they open the windows.
Wonderful little place. Great drinks, food and the staff are all very charming and genuinely want you to have a great experience. Superb little spot.

Tiny... Tight, but they know how to run a kitchen. Â The staff is young and proud and eager for you to try their food. Â We enjoyed an excellent pinot noir, and amusee of mushroom soup. Â My parents are very critical and loved the trout as well as the monkfish. Â Human sized portions, on little plates and you appreciate it because the table would be overwhelmed with a platter. Â The carrot salad was fresh and zingy and my dad stopped talking, focusing on his warm spinach salad. Â Dessert was ridiculously good. Â Gingerbread cake with coconut ice cream and a molten choco-awesome (filled with angel's tears... It was divine). Â Reservations are highly recommended... Like I said, it is teeney and there's no place to wait for a table, 'cept outside in the frackin' cold, which it is, unseasonably, in the middle of May (what's up NY?!)

Mezetto offers innovative and modern twists on classic Mediterranean and Middle Eastern fare that can only be described as absolutely delicious. It has an ambiance that is suitable for different occasions and party sizes, whether it's an intimate date or group gathering. Not to be missed are the falafel steamed buns (you'll never want to eat falafel any other way again), truffle mushroom gnocchi, mezze trio (eggplant, hummus, and labne), scallops with cauliflower and raisins, and skirt steak. Â They also have very interesting cocktails and desserts: must try is the Limonana which uses Arak, lemonade, and mint - quite tasty! All in all, the food is excellent, service attentive, and overall experience refreshing.

I went here for brunch with my friend and my cousin, who I was in town visiting. Â We missed the brunch crowd - hooray! Â They woke up too late, lucky us! I had a mimosa with my brunch, and of course it was delicious, as are all mimosas! Â Then I ordered the Huevos Viejos (?). Â It was similar to huevos rancheros, of course. Â But was sandwiched between two delicious CRISPY tortillas. Â They stayed crispy up until I finished my meal, and man did I savor that thing. Â The flavors melded so well and there was avocado and and....man it was good. Â I can only vouch for that delicious creation. Â Both my friend and I had it and she loved hers too. Â My cousin had something else, which she loved. Â But, I'm sorry, I was too involved with my delicious food to remember what it was. Â Maybe pancakes. Â Maybe. Also, their coffee was really good. Â I keep exeriencing gross coffee at places I order it. Â This was not gross coffee. Â It was delicious coffee that woke me up and prepared me for my day trekking manhattan with my backpack before our bus home to DC! Yum. Â Awesome last meal with my cousin, for that trip!

Sakagura offers a traditional japanese food along with the sashimi and other known japanese food. Â I truly enjoy all the different variÃ©tÃ©s of sakes they offer. Â I used to go to sakagura during the lunch time for their lunch specials. Â It may be hard to find in the beginning If you had never been there but it's worth the trip to the basement of the office building.

I went to this restaurant with my cousin who frequents this establishment. It is a great place to eat and relax. I enjoyed the delicious food and wine. The restaurant is dimly lit and it has big windows. It has beautiful dark wood throughout the restaurant. I like the small candles at the bar and tables. The flowers on the table and bar area added a nice touch as well. The spacing between the seats is a little tight however it is cool. My cousin and I were discussing a book and the table next to us read the same book. All four of us had a nice conversation.There is seating by the windows and it is cool to see the neighborhood. You can sit by the window and feel the nightly breeze on your skin. There is also seating at the bar which is great as well. This restaurant could have been in an episode of Sex and The City. I could see Carrie Bradshaw having brunch here to work on her column or the ladies getting together to gossip. Â  We were attended by Devon and Carter. Devon is awesome and friendly. He made me feel really welcomed. Carter was nice and he selected a great wine for me. I do not recall the name however it smelled like a sweet fragrance. We had an appetizer that consisted of bread, cheeses and various meats which was excellent. My cousin had the meat and mozzarrella pizza that was delicious. I had the chicken breast salad and it was good. The food was fresh and amazing. For dessert, my cousin had the apple tart with cinnamon ice cream. I never had a dessert like this and I was pleasantly surprised. Overrall, I was very pleased with my dining experience at Grape and Grain. This place can handle all your needs whether you are having a dining experience with a group of friends or one friend. This place looks great for couples especially first dates. The vibe is cool and the prices are reasonable. I look forward coming here again. Also, the bathroom is very clean. I was surprised that I didn't have to look out for "droplets" on the toilet seat. Not only is Grape and Grain a cool place to chill but it is very clean as well. Please check this place out because you will have a good time!!

I went for brunch one weekend and started off with the "i Suppli" which was a risotto croquette filled with buffalo mozzarella, fave beans, squash with mint. Â This dish had a great texture however the risotto was a little lost in the cheese and the strong mint flavor. I then proceeded to 2 pasta dishes; the "le Penne" and "le Pappardelle." Â The penne was excellent bursting with flavor. Â The pappardelle was very good but not what I expected at an Italian restaurant. Â It was more like a Beef Stroganoff. Â  I finished the meal with "la Torta" which was a flourless chocolate torte served with a hazelnut gelato. Â The torte was nothing special however the gelato was fabulous. Great food combined with great service makes this place a true winner. Â I highly recommend it if you're in the mood for some "innovative" Italian food.

Sunday brunch in Manhattan. Enough said. If you expect anything less than a line out front and a hurried, hectic wait-staff, wait three hours for lunch. However, if you are the brunching sort... Isabella's is a great spot. They may say 20-30 minute wait, but that is to run off those of you without the determination (tourists) ;) The front of house staff is always kind and efficient. Which is amazing considering the attitudes they must get from us custies. The food is usually spot-on and your first drink is included! Where else can you go for a meal for two with a drink for 35-40 dollars? Great breads and strawberry butter when they remember to bring it. The Benedict is a good standby and their omelets are not heavy... I am a fan!

It's hard to know where to start as I love everything about this place! The risotto, regardless of which one you order is amaaaazing. In keeping, the panini's regardless of which one you order are equally amaaaazing. Â The food is right on par with that of little cafe's out of Italy itself and if you're a crazed addict of the San Benedetto line like I am--you will LOVE that this is one of the few places in the city to find the Italian iced tea (in both peach AND my all-time favorite lemon) to go alonside your meal. Â It's a great place to go and be nostalgic about Tuscan culture. Â It's small but it's cozy and the stafff is super-cute. Â Bring friends, squeeze up into a table and enjoy, enjoy, enjoy!

Score! Â Four large fried dumplings for only one dollar! This is a tiny hole-in-the-wall joint in Chinatown. Â My friend and I stopped by here for a quick breakfast to go and got 8 pork dumplings for an even $2. Â Four was enough to fill up my belly to start the day. The dumplings were huge and filled with pork and chives and the dough was a bit thick to my liking. Don't expect much service here. Â I had to repeatedly ask for soy sauce while the man completely ignored me to take the next persons order. Â  There were only two stools so there's not much room to dine in. Â  Cash only as are most places in Chinatown.

i've ordered delivery at least 3 times from BXL East and recently dined in the restaurant on a sunday afternoon. Â not only are the moules frites a great treat, but dessert was perfect without being over the top, and the waitresses are SO friendly! Â this is rare in nyc. Â they were attentive without being pushy and they seemed genuinely friendly. in addition to the moules frites, i've also tried the truffle mushroom and cheese croquettes, the croque monsieur sandwich, and the profiteroles. Â everything was very good. Â some highlights from each dish are as follows: truffle mushroom and cheese croquettes - for $12, we got 2 medium sized square patties that were lightly fried. Â the filling tasted more like cheese than mushroom, but that was fine by me because it's rare that a dish with "truffle" in its name actually tastes like truffle and in this case, i could taste the truffle! Â there was also a little side salad to make you feel a little less guilty about clogging your arteries with grease and cheese. croque monsieur sandwich - this was exactly as i had expected, but very greasy. profiteroles - amazing. Â so amazing that i have no regrets or shame for having ordered these first while we waited for the unlimited moules frites special to begin (4pm on a sunday btw.) Â they came served as 3 puff pastries with vanilla ice cream sandwiched in between each, chocolate sauce drizzled all over the plate and on top of the puff pastries, and slivers of almond amply covering the plate. Â did i say amazing? Â AMAZING. i can't wait to go back again and see how close i can get to the record of 7 pots of mussels. Â for those who like to sample many different flavors, you can even choose a different broth for each pot of mussels that you attempt to devour. so glad to have this neighborhood gem. Â i just hope they don't increase their prices because the area is already scarce in affordable, weeknight, and lazy weekend dining options.

This place has the best tapas I've had in NYC. We had a reservation for Friday night at 9 and were seated after a short 5 minute wait. The place was packed, which is always a good sign. We ordered a variety of tapas and non disappointed. The specials were very good and well explained. The fried artichoke salad was very good as well as the pan con tomate (tomato bread). The huevos rellenos (deviled eggs) were surprisingly good. I wasn't expecting the flavors to really stand out considering I grew up eating them. The only dish that I did not care for was the chicken liver mousse, but others at the table liked it. I just didn't have a taste for it. The variety of wine was very good and the wine lady (separate from the server) did a really good job explaining the wine and describing it's weight. I'm definitely a fan and will return!

Great atmosphere and food! I highly suggest the mussels. We shucked out the mussels and let it sit in the sauce, and it was amazing. Everything was beautiful and cooked perfectly. It's a perfect casual dining experience. We were also engaged here! See you next year for that awesome anniversary Landmarc!

This is a cool pizza spot! Remember I said Pizza spot... Â Do not come in here.... thinking that the menu is large with Pasta dishes.... NO! This chilled out spot are for those who loves wine, cocktails with great pizza. The appetizers are pretty good too.... Again no calamari nor mozzarella sticks on the menu... Lol! I'm just saying.... you gotta know what you are getting into.... As an appetizer, we tried a tomato and cheese special that was good... but I should have tried the watermelon salad... that looked delish We shared a pie as we had other places/events to attend.... it was the meatball pie... it was thin crusted pizza.... my only complaint us that they could add more meat as it is the main topping.... a little stingy on the toppings. Other than that..... service was excellent. The vibe, Â atmosphere, Â people were nice and relaxed. Great place for drinks and good pizza.... if you are in the mood!
Calling this place good is like calling sex, reproduction.

Holy crap this place is delicious. Â I dropped in after having my brows done at Joey Healy's brow studio on East 70th. Â There was a bit of a line - it was midafternoon on a Wednesday. Â But the wait and cost were rewarded. Â  I got a box of 8. Â They were truly deliriously good. Â  The hype is for real. My favorite was the vanilla, the carmel, and lemon. Â Such amazing flavor and texture. Â And they were not overly sweet. Â The Rose Water was very odd, though - I do not recommend this unless you love Rose Water. Â It tasted a little like the molded soaps my grandmother kept on her sink.

Very cozy place to have a small get to get together with a few friends. There were mini couches and soft sofas. The food was phenomenal, I enjoyed it very much. I will definitely recommend the Uni Croquette Â and the Washu-Beef Tartar. Those two were my favorite of the night. Salivating just writing about it now. The uni was fresh with a lovely croquette crunch. It was definitely a nice pairing. The Washu Beef Tartar reminded me of an nice italian slice of pizza. The beef was spread out like tomato sauce on top of a nicely baked flat bread. Â Super delicious. My 3rd runner up dish for recommendation is the Assorted Mushroom Risotto. I love mushroom but I was never a fan of risotto because of the thick creamy texture. This dish was a perfect balance of mushroom and it was slightly creamy, which wasn't too overwhelming. Â  I shared a couple more dishes with my friends but wasn't a fan of the watercress salad and the washu burger (sweet potato fries Â that came with the burger were good). The foie gras soba was pretty decent. The soba had a nice texture and foie gras was ok. This restaurant deserves a 5 stars because of a delicious first dining experience, Â and it got me wanting to return to try the rest of the menu! Tip: Search through the sanitation website for the phone number but you will also need a reference from a previous diner in order to obtain a reservation for this restaurant.

Before coming to this place, I've only ever eaten soba served cold. In my mind, soba is supposed to be cold, and ramen is supposed to be warm. That is, until I went to soba-ya The duck soba served in warm soup is unlike anything I've ever eaten! The oil from the duck slices mixes very well with the clear and yet deeply flavorful soup base, while the soba, unlike ramen, does not absorb the soup, and so provides an interesting contrast to the taste of the duck. The atmosphere is pretty nice as well, with the theme very much feeling like a actual Japanese room. It's slightly more expensive than other noodle shops in the area, but not by much. There is usually a wait line outside too, but not too long. One of the few place I go back to again and again and again.
These people are very nice, seem like they love the neighborhood, their sandwiches are top notch, they cost abit more then other places, but it's worth it, tastes amazing, fresh always!
Exquisite! Â Everything we had here was amazing. Â I would highly recommend the scallops as well as the pork tacos. Â They also had a really nice cognac that we savored with dessert.

I hesitated to do this review only because writing about it leaves me drooling and craving for more. Â  If there's one great culinary lesson I have learned from NYC, it is that there is so much more to Japanese food than sushi, udon, and tempura. Â  I first learned this lesson at awesome O-Taisho which I'm devoted to but a friend convinced me tonight to check out Y. Toto. Â It's on the second floor up a long flight of stairs but well worth the walk. Â Juicy kobee beef tongue, a skewer of cow hearts, skin ... that's right skin on a skewer (I don't know if it was chicken skin or the skin of their competition), awesome skirt steak ...mmm... Â Everything was deserving of the term "delicacy." Damn I want more! Even their soup and rice porridge with chicken and egg left me ecstatic. Â Off the hook, high quality, authentic Japanese food (and very cute waittresses) makes this Y. toto worth the price. Â My only complaint was that the portions are pretty small but I have the appetite of a race horse on steroids.
My favorite place for brunch. I love EVERYTHING.

I'm a huge fan of this place. I've been here at least 5 times. The lunch specials usually leave me so full that I'm ready to bust a gut. Everything is just so good here that I just can't stop eating everything. I've always ordered the hot noodles here since I'm not a fan of cold noodles. The agadashi tofu is heavenly, a nice slight crunch on the outside and soft in the inside. I've also ordered the rice bowls with tuna or salmon. They give you a good healthy portion of fish here. The one minor criticism I have is the seasoning of the rice. There's a bit too much rice vinegar in it. The service is good and I hear Japanese being spoken amongst the customers. I can only guess that's a good sign....

As we were walking out of Banh mi Zon with full stomachs and smiles, the friendly guy behind the counter said that we should write a review. This one's for you, buddy. As a banh mi lover, I have eaten a fair amount of these super tasty sandwiches in my day, and I gotta say that Banh mi Zon is right up there. Â Fresh, sweet, salty, tangy, and delicious. Â I can't necessarily say that it's better than Banh mi Saigon, which is also very good, but it is right up there. Â The Banh mi Zon version is also a little bit different, with shredded chicken on the basic sandwich instead of just pork, but it doesn't lose any of the flavour. Â One of our party, a banh mi rookie, had the version made with pork patties, and loved it so much that he finished the whole thing before he even realized it. It is kind of a hole in the wall, but very nice with a friendly vibe. Â If you're craving banh mi on the LES, Banh mi Zon should be your first choice.

Now I see what all the fuss is about! Â I've been hearing for years how great Kefi is, but finally just got a chance to try it out this weekend. Â We had reservations for 2 at 8pm on Friday night, and were seated immediately when we arrived. Â There were tons of people waiting outside and by the bar area, so I'm not sure if they were there for drinks or waiting for a table, but I didn't have to wait at all. Â  The menu had tons of options, no matter what kind of food you're in the mood to eat. Â Everything on the appetizer menu sounded delicious, and next time I go I might just order a bunch of appetizers and skip the entree because what we ordered was fabulous! Â We had the meatballs and the calamari, and I'd definitely recommend both of them! Â The calamari comes with some kind of lemony yogurt sauce that was very unique compared to the marinara sauce that I'm used to seeing.

This mamouns blows the Hoboken location out of the water as far as flavor. The lamb shawerma sandwich was so flavorful, and of course, the hot sauce was BOMB. It's a small location, so I took mine to go and went straight for Washington square park! My only qualm is, that they didn't have the delicious mango juice that the Hoboken location has.
Are you kidding me!!! Wow...great food!!! And the price is great. Shawarma...yes please. Grab some baklava and and a Mabrumeh for dessert!

I was here on a busy Sunday craving some good sweet breakfast food. I looked online at the menu so I already had my heart set on the brioche French toast. There was some sort of special going on so I was able to get this plus a coffee and juice for $12.50!

Checked it out on a weeknight based on the stellar yelp ratings and it was underwhelming at best. Â Had the broccoli rabe & egg, calamari & pork cassoulet; shared a dessert as well. Â It's the kind of place that lists all the dishes' ingredients, which makes them sound great on the menu, Â until you taste the actual dish, and realize that they were relying on the interesting ingredients at the expense of execution. Â You know? Service was fine. Â Ambiance is nothing special and even cramped. Â Dishes are tapas-style, so not expensive, but they are quite small. Â All in all a mediocre dining experience given its potential. Won't be back.
Best Soul Food I've ever had! Recommend to anyone wondering where you can still get tasty soul food in Harlem.

Was here with my family upon their urging me to give the place a try. Well my family was right the food was very good. It's like eating in a friend's mother's kitchen. The owner kept coming out of the kitchen to make sure we liked her cooking, we did. She was very hospitable as were her two sons who help her run the place. When we were finished eating the owner brought out dessert for our table, gratis, she said she did not want to throw it out as she was closing after we left. Did not want it to go to waste. We need to go back again to try more of their offerings. Went back and tried their Falafel, OUTSTANDING is all I can say. Her pickle medley inside the sandwich is what brought it over the top for me. Can't wait to go back. We have been back many times and Wafa's food never fails to disappoint. Her hummus, Babaganoush, are amazing. The meat, cheese and spinach pies should not be missed and are a great way to start your meal. If you live in the area you must give Wafa's a try. My Daughters review below is even more detailed...

Is the burger here delicious? Absolutely Would I say it's the best burger in NY? No way. Sorry, but my heart still belongs to Shake Shack ... or even Greasy Nicks up in Westchester. As a testimony, I'll say that I've lived by Corner Bistro for almost three years and have only stepped foot inside three times. The main reasons are: 1) Like I said the burger is definitely juicy and flavorful, but ultimately disappointing after all the hype that's been built up about it 2) Unlike Shake Shack, where I'd gladly spend an hour basking in the sun in Madison Square Park, I'm not as inclined to be compressed between crowds of men and women vying for a table in a dingy restaurant 3) The reason for said compression is that there is almost always a wait 4) In my experience the staff has never been very friendly. I mean c'mon. Why do they have to be? It's not like people will stop flocking to Corner Bistro because a waiter was curt. But for me personally, grouped will all my aforementioned qualms, I would prefer a more full dining experience then the one I've had at Corner Bistro. Of course, when it's 4 am on a weekend and I'm hungry, everything I've said goes totally out the window ... oh well
Simply amazing! Went in after reading about it in yelp. It's true, really really great fast food.

We came here on a Sunday afternoon for brunch and it was crowded. We waited about 30 minutes for a table. We had the mimosas and the blue fin avocado rolls to start. The tuna and avocado were good but they serve it to you on a piece of bread. That was a little disappointing. For my meal I had the macaroni trio. It was absolutely amazing!!!

Imma be real honest. My obsession with Umami Burger has become a problem in my life. Anytime the topic of burgers comes up, the U that lies above the perfectly melted in-house cheeses comes to mind. The medium rare beef can, on occasion, still be mooing, but I don't care - I love it. My most recent endeavor involved a couple of menu items that I hadn't tried. This is a rarity for me. I know what I like and I stick with what I like. Side note, before I begin gushing about the food - our waiter was absolutely delightful. I don't think I've ever had a server here that was rude or seem disinterested, which I think is a pretty good track record. OKAY. Onward to the menu items! My food partner in crime and I went with the Allagash White, because Maine beer is always a good choice, we shared "Manly" fries, and we each ordered "The Royale." Here's what I learned from this experience: 1) Ordering fries with bacon on them is always a good idea. ALWAYS. 2) I didn't think the Truffle Burger could get better... BUT THEN THEY PUT SHORT RIB ON IT AND IT MAKES ME WANT TO CRY THINKING ABOUT IT. 3) If my royale suddenly became a human, I would marry it instantly. No questions asked. I always worry that I oversell Umami... but then again, I have yet to be disappointed.

Amazing. Absolutely delicious. Fantastic location and great staff members. We met the manager, Lance, who was the nicest man and he made several fantastic recommendations. We had two appetizers and two entrees and each dish was mouth watering, and they are not shy with their alcohol. My bf had two drinks and is currently content and fast asleep. We live right across the street and will definitely be coming back to enjoy their happy hour. I can't wait to bring my friends here! Great addition to the neighborhood!

If you're in the area, great neighborhood place to meet up with friends for a casual dinner without breaking the bank. Really that sums it up: decent food and wine with friendly service. However it's not a place to go out of your way for.

I"m big on customers service, and this has to be 1 place where I always feel welcome. As soon as I walk through the door I'm greeted with a smile. The food here...amazing! Drinks...spectacular! Dessert....off the charts! I recommend going for brunch and trying the Tofu Scramble (and make sure you take advantage of their happy hour lunch specials offered from 11 a.m. to 5 p.m. on the weekend). Best thing about Bogota is they accommodate small reservations (I typically only reserve a table for myself, and a friend). Please be sure to try Bogota very soon. Trust me, you will not be disappointed!

Its been like 15 years since I've been to NYC, and Pommes Frites. Â The city is still awesome and so are this fry joint !!! Â The fries are amazing, you really don't need any of the sauces but they work too, I had that blue cheese sauce on the side and it went well with them.

My second French breakfast in Brooklyn. I have passed Traditions every single time going to Bedford Avenue and only this past Saturday did I make my first trip inside. Once we entered, we were greeted with a little skinny French man yelling, "BONJOOOOOUUUUUURRRRRR!" Literally, every single person walking in will get a longer bonjour than the last. My first impression was how small it was with how many tables they cram into the dining room. Taking a look at the menu, I knew instantly what I wanted this time, the next time, and the time after. The list of crepes is huge and it should be, since they are so easy to make. Since I was familiar with the croque madame, I ordered it again while my girlfriend ordered a crepe with figs, goat cheese, rosemary, and caramelized onions. Both dishes were absolutely delicious, but I have to admit, I wish I got more than one bite of that crepe across the table. Before eating, I also ordered the Hot Apple Cider, which at $2.75 was a pleasant surprise I wasn't expecting walking inside. The final bill came to a little less than $25, which isn't too terrible for breakfast, but also isn't a steal. I definitely will be coming back to Pates et Traditions with my accent and beret sooner than that guy can say Bonjour again. PS! I also want to come here for dinner. It looks like a beautiful place to enjoy a dinner with someone special. From driving by, they dimmed the lights beautifully and the menu can only be just as delicious.

Great home style Cuban cuisine! Half cuban myself, this place was dangeroulsy authentic and had the "Cuban feel". The place even got me sentimental, with all the pictures hung up on the walls. It reminded me of my grandmother who died nearly five years ago, and her familiar Cubaness. The best part was when the well-respected now elderly owner walked in and shook everyone's hand eating. His cuban accent, oh my god, you don't find that in New York City. It felt good to hear it, reminding me of my family in the Miami Suburbs. Â Now, for those who are completely unfamiliar with Cuban cuisine and culture, go and try this place! If you've never tried Cuban food, or even if you have and wasn't feelin' it, I highly reccommend this place. Let me say its not that far out there, so for picky eaters, you won't be having escargot or frog legs in Thai chili sauce. The flavors are all familiar, and dishes consist of rice, meat, and beans. Atmosphere is chill, and service is great. Only thing though, the bread isn't really Cuban bread, haha, its Italian lol, but since its pretty impossible to find pan cubano over in the city, its totally acceptable. And hey, bread is bread! Equally delicious and crispy. And conyo! Excuse the language, but their Vaca Frita is amazing, a shredded beef dish in an onion based sauce, similar to the classic ropa vieja but its not in a tomato based sauce. For pork lovers, they have numerous amount of tender juicy pork options. A non-pork eater, I can not say how it says, but everytime my dad orders it, it looks fantastically fresh and juicy. And the flan, my Tita orders it every time she comes up from Miami, and I think its what she looks forward to every time. Certainly a 5 star restaurant, won't find anything else like it in New York City.

So impressed! From the food, to the crowd, to the entire atmosphere. Ah-ma-zing! If you're bored with food and ready to taste new flavors, you have to come here. Reservations have to be made 31 days in advance from the date you want to go. Wish we had arrived a bit earlier to browse through ABC Carpet & Home but it closed at 7pm. Note for the Ladies....wear your biggest best heels! I went on a Saturday night and the ladies are dressed to impress.

I love this place! Â First off, the guy who works there gave me two free samples before I could decide out of their like 14 flavors(ok, maybe I'm exaggerating). Â They cook their fries, what do I mean cook, I mean deep fry their fries in a wok at high temperatures. Â You can smell the greasiness from outside their shop. Â I love the creative condiments that they have listed. Â I mean Rosemary Garlic mayo!!! Â Oh yes! Â This is to-die-for! Â I have to say French Fries are a vice of mine, but I must have them! Â They have two different sizes, I believe: small and large. Â I haven't been in a while almost three years, but hey that doesn't stop me from yelping them. Â I also got a poutine for the road, and if you're on a diet--do not (I repeat! Â Do Not) get them. Â They are rich, creamy, heart-attack clogging deliciously unregrettable until your doctor tells you your diagnosis good. Â I would say that this place is pretty popular among the college crowd, but that should not deter you. Â It's yummy and that's why you should try it! Â =) Â There is limited seating.
Fun and delicious place to drink margaritas and have fine Mexican food. Good service and relaxed, casual atmosphere. I'd recommend the guacamole and cod.

This place is by far my favorite restaurant! I have nothing bad to say about it except sometimes the wait can be a little long which is to be expected for such a fantastic place! I never tried Thai food before, but Room Service was a great first time. The calamari is a MUST! The people there are very friendly and the decor is beautiful! It's kind of tight seating and not great for really big parties but it's perfect for a date night or a catch up session with friends! The drinks are great as well!

Totto Ramen is a dinner AND show! I absolutely love this place, it's the best ramen place I have tried thus far. The wait: I got there at 5:30 for their dinner service and the wait was already 45 min- 1 hr! Totto ramen faithfuls are ON it. So be early! The inside sits maybe 20 people at a time or less. The food: the most popular dishes are the spicy ramen (11.25) and the mega ramen (15.5) with a choice of either pork or chicken. Go with the PORK. it is so good. it's soft and moist and ... I'll just stop there. If you like eating spicy things but not TOO spicy, don't be afraid to go with the spicy ramen. Add ons- things like the seasoned boiled egg, avocado, bamboo shoot (comes in a bag unfortunately) etc etc... Â All very good. The broth- my favorite part of the whole dish. The broth is thicker than most ramen making it feel like a more heartier dish and Â It's flavored with garlic paste, among other things. giving it that come-hither smell and umami taste. Also, a shoutout to the very courteous staff. How they keep calm in the mob of people is amazing! Will definitely be returning. **CASH ONLY!

Was ONCE a great, amazing brunch spot, but now it's only mediocre. Â Bloody Mary's are just OK but are quite expensive @ $10. Â Food is good but not what it used to be. Â Hope they get back to the quality and goodness they had once.

I don't have falafel very often, but this place definitely tops everywhere else I've eaten. I've heard that Taim has the best falafel in NYC, and just from my one visit, I am inclined to believe it. I had the basic sandwich with green falafel, and it was within my hands in just a few minutes. The sandwich was delicious and surprisingly filling. I can't wait to come back and try the other menu options!

I've come here two weekends in a row and I am about to go back this weekend -- that's how much I love this place! Â It's now my favorite brunch place and I can't stop talking about it. Â In fact, before discovering this gem, I hated brunch. Â I found it puzzling that people would wait hours to get seated, just for a meal of eggs, which I could easily make in my own home. However! Â The eggs benedicts here are amazing! Â They have a delightful variety -- the benedict jane and johnny. Â Johnny is my favorite, though jane is not bad. Â The chicken sausage in the johnny is so good! Â The jane is ok though I am not a big fan of sea-food flavors in my breakfast. Â The french toast is also amazing, as everyone else has raved.. plus the servings here are quite generous. Â Finally, the best part is that I don't even have to wait hours! Â For once, a brunch place that takes reservations -- amazing!

Top quality across the board. Â Amazing service and mouth watering dishes, especially the appetizers. The feel is very classic and there isn't any theme or special feel, just really good food combined with really good service.

Came here with a group of 10 or so friends on a Friday night. Â The food was great - I got the Blackened Brick Amish Free Range Chicken and shared the Kale and Artichoke Fondue. Â Both were delicious. Â We ordered several bottles of wine and the bill was still very reasonable. Â I will be going back.

My friend told me about this place and I came to Chinatown looking for it. It's very small! Can only fit 4 people in the small hole in the wall. The guy can speak a little English, but they work hard for their business. Everybody goes here (not only Chinese people) $1 for 5 dumplings! I got 10, then I wanted more and got another 5 and ate it all there. ahaha, it was pretty filling, I could probably eat more, but I saw other people were getting like 5 dumpling for one person, and here I was eating like a fattie... so I resisted on getting another 15...

I can't believe this place is so popular. I had the Mega Ramen, which started off pretty good and there was a healthy amount of pork. Unfortunately, as I started eating the pork I realized it was heavily salted. It was tolerable for a few bites, but as I consumed more of the bowl, I realized I was not going to be able to finish it. I got about 40% of the way through it and thought I'd take the rest home, add some low-sodium chicken broth (and a potato to absorb the salt). However, when I asked to take it to go, I was informed that they did not have any containers, which is ridiculous in a ramen joint. So at least half of a $17 ($15 bowl + $2 poached egg topping) serving went to waste. Now I'm home and feeling ill from all the sodium. And the inside of my mouth and lips are numb, which leads me to believe there was some MSG involved. Finally, the noodles are prepackaged and had zero flavor of their own. The only good thing was a healthy pour of sake for $6. I will not be returning.

true new yorkers only... place is small, they have like 8 tables all together or something like that...service can be slow at times, Cash Only (sucks). Food is BEYOND amazing, Croque Monsieur, Apple Pancakes and even the regular Eggs Benedict are amazing! BYOB But this place is great, you can see a lot of celebrities and fashion people there regularly.

I absolutely love this place... So do my soros and my son!!! From the plantain crusted chicken to the rellenos to the passion fruit mimosa to the empanadas and xangos (which are to die for) also the churros! I have been here over 25 times in last 3 years n planning a graduation dinner here with ther affordable pre-fixe menus

Osteria Morini is a fun and vibrant restaurant, a bit more concerned with providing their guests an enjoyable evening rather than putting out flawless pasta. The food here is fairly good. The parmesan soup was really warm and satisfying on a particularly cold night and my girlfriend and I both agreed the tortellini inside were exceptional. The pasta is heavy, and not really in a good way. If you, gentle reader, have been to Marea you know Michael White will often cut the richness and creaminess of his dishes with the use of seafood or a punchy red sauce. That counterbalance was pretty absent on the two dishes we had, the Garganelli with truffle butter and the Cappelletti with prosciutto. Â While both of these dishes were very, very tasty, they were rich on an almost unappealing level and sitting in big pools of oil. Suffice it to say both my date and I did not feel totally awesome after downing these. The dessert actually suffered from a similar overuse of oil/cream, and this was on a pretty objective level. I had a chocolate hazelnut budino that was roughly 95% cream/egg yolk and 5% chocolate and hazelnut. The color of the actual budino was a whitish beige, not so dissimilar from the whipped cream on top. The little bites of pear in this was very inventive and refreshing, but the dish was a disappointment in that there really was not much of a chocolate or hazelnut taste. The room is really big and the seats are packed in but it is Soho and seems like a pretty fun atmosphere. The waiters are extremely attentive and very nice. I really want to give this place 3.5 stars but I just can not round down due to the fact that every single truffle dish had absolutely no truffle oil and actually only had real black truffle. So word.

After watching this location change hands several times over the years,along came Peaches. Will this be another failed restaurant? Will it come to the demise of its former next door neighbor Breadstuy? NOT EVEN CLOSE! No your not going to cram a group of 5 I there easily; but who cares. Wait time is nominal depending on the day. Food is carefully crafted. Nothing synods out more in my mind than the menu. " a classic American restaurant with a nod to the south"

Food is excellent on the fundamentals - the menu is classic with just a few twists. Oyster mushroom hash, as many have noted, is basically superior to any other potato vector currently available. Burgers, brussels sprouts, octopus in pasta, we all know what these things taste like when they're really good, so I'll spare you the extended description. The only problem I have with this place is they're charging green-food prices without the actual green food. "Humanely Raised" and "Natural" are basically marketing weasel-words, which is a shame, because I would definitely travel to LIC from Prospect Heights to eat here if it were the real deal.

The Greek sits in a part of Tribeca that you forget exists. It doesn't feel like a Manhattan restaurant. The thing that stands out at the Greek is the sheer inability to compromise. This is a restaurant that invites you for dinner and bathes you in attention. But if you don't like it, you can go fuck yourself. Are you an Interior designer who thinks native farm equipment isn't art? The Greek don't care. Want a bottle of wine from any country besides Greece? The Greek don't care. Want to sample some "Mediterranean fare"? You know the stuff loved by people who think Greece and Israel are the same country? The Greek don't care. Want a cocktail that doesn't include Greek liquor? Well... the Greek sort of cares about that actually--it has a full bar. But their cocktail menu is pretty much all stuff you've never heard of combined in ways you never thought of, each drink more delicious than the last. I didn't sample all the cocktails but only because the first five's effect wouldn't allow me to. It's an ouzo/Mataxa-phile's heaven. But you can still get your martini. The food tastes like food made by a Greek person. And the restaurant has a really social, neighborhood-y vibe. It's the kind of place where you accidentally make friends. Best enjoyed in large, lazy doses. Like a Greek island.
Best Monday Spot in the city, bartenders are awesome and so is the food. Boom baby Boom.

One of, if not the best restaurant experience I've had in the city. Worked on the same block and would pass by Pellegrino's many times a day. Waiters and manager(s) greeted me with a smile and small conversation outside every single day, and would very regularly offer me coffee to go. I'd tried their food to-go at my office multiple times, happy to always find two loaves of bread, extra parmesan and a huge portion of whatever I'd ordered (pasta) all fresh and warm inside. I then decided to go in and sit, and was pleased to be seated at a big table, with great decoration and pearly white napkin and table cloths. I was served fast, had my water refilled by the ever-smiling waiters throughout the meal, and had a few glasses of wine that were just right. Pasta was incredibly fresh, had various ones from the menu, while the rigatoni alla vodka stays my all time favorite meal of an Italian restaurant in NYC. Beautiful sauce, asparagus and mushrooms, and they made it all vegetarian for me! Also asked if I'd like anything else to replace the meat. Oh and did I mention full bar? Cocktails, alcohol, whiskey, soda, etc. Huge portions, delicious food, incredible service. Deserves all its praise. I would give this restaurant six stars if I could.

Fried chicken cutlet on a house made buttermilk biscuit with honey buffalo sauce and buttermilk herb ranch. Those are the words that lured me to The Anchored Inn brunch today after having inspected the online menu. Last week while walking around the area I even spotted a sign that read "Chicken Biscuit" advertising brunch and an outdoor patio. We arrived today, primed and ready to order the chicken biscuit. Sure, I'd glance at other menu items from sheer intellectual curiosity alone and I took the dive environment in stride: I'd soon be having a chicken biscuit. Alas, we were too early as the biscuits were still being made. The responsible part of my mind appreciated the fact that these were homemade biscuits. The impulse driven hunger pang fighting glutton was severely disappointed and blurted out "french toast!". Not to curse the French and their toast, au contraire, but to order what to me seemed like a sloppy seconds, what with all the promise of buttermilk dreams and fried lust. I regrouped but fear my wife never did. So ignoring the disappointment of being too early for housemade biscuits, my french toast arrived in a paper serving apparatus that fries usually come in. Napkins? Try paper towels. Cutlery? Try plastic. Water? Self pour in the front. Add self pour coffee or tea and this would start to resemble a Holiday Inn Express. I tease, of course, but just be aware of these things before embarking on a brunch. It's a very egalitarian picnic feel that some may find too casual and others just right. As for me, I was too busy downing the french toast for the simple reason that it was drenched in a delicious dulce de leche sauce. I ordered a side of bacon that proved crispy, fatty foil to the soaking sweet bread. The presentation and plastic utensils reminded me of ordering from the Wafels and Dinges truck. The bathroom was like stepping into a pit of graffiti, which had me wonder about next time bringing a spray can of paint so I can leave my mark on the walls. I did appreciate seeing the name "Edward Snowden" scribbled on the wall. Hanging from the walls are fascinating paintings that range from Chairman Mao to fantasy wizards to Vladimir Putin. I could definitely see this as a place to drink and drink again. The absence of the the chicken biscuit was disappointing but I'd see this more as a place to have a main course of beer and side of brunch as opposed to brunch and a drink on the side. That's not meant as a criticism but rather where I see the Anchored Inn's strengths. The music was blasting out doo wop hits from the '50s, adding to the feel like I was in a roadhouse stop on a cross country trip somewhere in Kansas. Having been raised in the ethnic enclaves of northern NJ where this kind of music is a must at weddings, the early morning appearance of Dion DiMucci's "Teenager in Love" did test my aural patience. Still,a vastly better atmosphere and quality of eats than anything in my central Queens home turf. With warmer weather I'd consider coming back at a later time when the biscuits have been baked and the outdoor seating is far away from the crooning sounds of doo wop.

cabbage w/ miso was okay...udon dishes were ehh....the salmon rice cakes baked were pretty good. I've had a whole variety of food here and none of it stands out to me. Pork belly is about average here..All the food was pretty standard and their soups were nothing to write home about. Not as good as st marks area food. Its more the fact this place is a lot better than sapporo and super close to me. They have their kitchen open until 2am and so if you want food thats not pizza that late..this would be the place to go.
yum yum yum....and thats just the owner Â lol. food was great as well

i love gottino. seriously, their website says it: ilovegottino.com. after my first visit to the little gem, i kept finding myself coming back to sit at the cozy bar. the place is small and intimate, completely inviting, and serves utterly amazing food. if you go to the wine cellar downstairs, there are stacks of wine, barrels of apples, onions, nuts, dried fruit, and vegetables. perhaps i'm a sucker for anything rustic, but gottino is one of the best finds in the city. M and i always sit at the bar. that way, you can chat with the staff, ogle at the piles of meats, cheeses, desserts, and breads, and share food easily. the menu is small plates - a little bit like french tapas. everything is perfectly and lovingly prepared. wine: in the winter, my go-to wine is a red montepulciano d'abruzzo. in the warmer months, i love a good rose. i was delighted to find that the same region creates a most magnificant rose as well. affordable and delicious. starter tapas: we always begin with their prosciutto. it's buttery and sliced so thinly that it virtually melts in your mouth. we usually get the shaved brussel sprout salad, as well - paired with walnuts and pecorino. it's light and simple, and pairs wonderfully with the fresh bread drizzled with olive oil that continuously appears next to your food. main tapas: last night, the first thing we laid eyes on was a large platter of cold lamb with butter beans, covered with fragrant rosemary. we ordered a plate of that immediately. the beans were a little bit charred, which i love, and somewhat sweet. the lamb itself was awesome, and really fatty. i didn't mind. as M said "i usually don't say this, but this fat is GOOD FAT." it was true - that little lamb had put on quality weight. we also ordered a plate of smoked salmon {for me - i had two bites of lamb} - which came with creme fraiche, capers, and sliced onions. it was among the better pieces of smoked salmon i've ever tasted. it's like everything at gottino is made of butter and melts fantastically in your mouth. dessert: our friendly french barman recommended we have the tartufo. i've heard about this dessert but never actually tried it. theirs is made with part hazelnut, part chocolate gelato, and rolled in a massive amount of cocoa. i limited myself to three bites, but geez louise, it was one of the most decadent things i've ever tasted. bottom line: there's nothing wrong with gottino. everything about it right, fantastic, and amazing. i can't wait to go back as soon as possible.

Very very good Mexican food for a decent price! We order via seamless and were very pleased with the food. The shrimp was amazing, the tortas were killer, and the blue corn tortillas were delicious. It's a great addition to the neighborhood and I will be going there often.

Attended a private party rehersal dinner at Olea for about 50 people. Â The appetisers were delicious to start us off. That was just where our adventure began. Â Every selection, every course, was presented and prepared to perfection; for all members of the party, and in a timely fashion. Â I can not say enough about the multitude of flavors with just the right seasonings. The wait staff is second to none. Â They really make you feel like you're part of the family. Â I would certainly go out of my way to eat in such a cozy and friendly atmosphere as Olea offers again! Â I highly recommend it!

I would imagine this place to be a great date spot, being that I walked in with a friend and I noticed almost all the other patrons were on a date (haha)! Dim to dark lighting with candles on each table, wine glasses in hand, all with that dewy "look into your significant others eyes" thing going on. DID I PICK THE WRONG PLACE TO EAT?! Surely I was not on a date, BUT I was craving skirt steak after a long Wednesday and this place had great reviews. Located on a corner, it wasn't overly packed and the waiter was quite attentive. Started off with one of their specialty drinks (forgot the name, but it looked like a white wine sangria). Too sweet for my taste, but having some beer to even it out did make it better. As for the meal itself, I ordered the skirt steak (medium rare), with mashed potatoes on the side (there is a fries option as well). My friend had the pappardelle in bolognese meat sauce. My steak was cooked PERFECTLY medium rare and it came with a side of two different sauces-loved and finished both (ask for extra, it may come in handy)! I also loved the pappardelle - fresh pasta and wasn't overly sauced. If you're coming in super hungry, I'd recommend ordering an appetizer first, being that the dishes aren't huge. Overall, a great experience in what seems to be a quiet neighborhood.

Wow. Â I was about to write "meh", and then I saw it as one of Yelp!'s preloaded ratings. Â I guess that pretty much sums it up. Â  If you're really that into meatballs (my girl is for some reason), go for one of the meatball specials at an Italian steakhouse: Prime 112, Delmonico's, etc.

Lunch review 4.5 stars. Jean Georges is my 5 star threshold and this comes oh so very very close. Second best lunch I have had in the city. $35 two course. First course. Blue crab with avocado and grapefruit foam. This was recommended to me as a signature dish. It was FANTASTIC. The crab meat was so fresh and juicy. There was a good amount of fresh avocado but not overwhelming. The grapefruit foam was a nice unique touch. This dish was fresh, felt refreshing. It was small but quality over quantity. Second course. Thanks to Yelp reviews that highly recommended the squid ink pasta, that is what I got. Wow, what a great choice. This was unlike any pasta I have had. Really flavorful, great seafood, great presentation. Portion size was solid too. Dessert. They brought a dessert tray to show me the desserts. They all looked incredible and creative. I wish I had a bigger appetite since I didn't have the room to properly enjoy a dessert. But I was impressed with the selection for sure. Service. Very attentive, not pushy at all, and overall, as good as you could ask for. Setting. Beautiful new hotel, 2nd floor. Really nice space. Not as stuffy as I thought it might be. The quality of the space is a big plus. So very close to the 5 star rating. I am guessing, given how fantastic lunch was, that the prix fixe dinner could easily be a 5 star and I plan on trying that as well.

We had reservations for Thanksgiving. We walked in and found the place packed. We had reservations and were immediately seated at a table. We ordered the fixed price 4-course thanksgiving meal for $49 per person. We also had a Cote du Rhone to complement the meal. The carrot ginger soup was a great beginning. The mixed green salad looked simple, but the dressing and candied walnuts and cranberries really escalated the dish. The main was served on a large plate. Â A large turkey breast rolled and stuffed with a mushroom stuffing was accompanied with purÃ©ed sweet potatoes, mashed potatoes, and butternut squash as well as haricot verts. All were thanksgiving classics and were fantastic. Fresh homemade cranberry sauce was served in a large bowl on the table. The dessert was choice of pumpkin pie or cheesecake with coffee or tea. The slices were huge! Service was very attentive. Everyone including the Owner Debbie was extremely friendly. By the time we left, we felt like regulars. A wonderful meal. Highly recommended!!
expensive and loud, but good drinks! great meet up spot for after theatre, as well.

I must say this place has fallen off a bit in terms of the food. I love me the bbq ribs that were once served at the same location under the Houston's name. Â They definitely changed something in the recipe. Still keeps me coming back though.

A recent addition to the notable eateries and bars on Hudon is MÃ©mÃ©. Crafting tapas and dishes with a North African point of view; sambusaks, merguez and tagines can be enjoyed in an ambient eatery that's clearly Middle Eastern, sans the kitsch of Ali Baba and the Forty Thieves. Unexpectedly, the Gnocci with Ricotta and Truffle Oil is phenomenal. Jane on West Houston, you better watch out! There's a new gnocci in the city and it's pretty darn good.

Because they are about to open a Din Tai Fung in Seattle, I just had to give myself a preface of Xiao Long Bao before that main event. Joe's Shanghai has apparently been a staple in the New York Chinese food scene since the beginning of time. Because of this, its fame made actually getting the food an arduous task. We waited an hour in the cold Â for a table to be ready at the Chinatown location. It was so annoying... But when we actually got inside, it felt pretty authentic. We just got 3 orders of beef xiao long bao for about $6 ea. It was enough to fill up 3 people. Quality was good and things came out really fast. The only thing that might be a turn off to people who aren't accustomed is the service. Just don't expect happy faces when you come to dine here. Just get in, sit down, order your food, pay, then leave. The servers will appreciate that the most. BTW: CASH ONLY

pretty good diner food. Â simple, straightforward. Â in and out quick. Â the line keeps moving. Â however, completely overrated. Â people take cabs from manhattan to eat here. Â it's ridiculous. Â wait for an overcast day when everyone's assuming it's going to rain and enjoy the food for what it is. Â love that they'll bring you coffee and bacon as you're waiting in line.

I echo previous rave reviews. Came here on a Wednesday night with my hubby and 20 year old twins. The food was OUTSTANDING. Hubby and I had the Â fig salad and the poached lobster. Kids had risotto (I am not a risotto person but it was delicious.) Dessert was Â a sea salt Â caramel panna cotta. Hubby had a raspberry tart. Service attentive. Great signature drink list. Owners are adorable. The restaurant has a gallery section that features LIC artists. We will be back. A great addition to the neighborhood .

This lovely little spot on a quiet sidestreet in Windsor Terrace is like dining in with friends. Giuseppe and his kind, attentive wife/partner offer morning coffee and pastries (nice), but we went last night for dinner and had a meal that was both delicious and--well, serene. No waiter bloviating about a long list of specials, no pretentious menu citing the source of every sprig of thyme; a small but satisfying roster of homemade Italian choices, a red or white or bubbly available by the glass, and a peaceful country-ish little room in which to enjoy it. (And there's a bit of parking available on street nearby.) The star attraction here is the house-made ravioli (I had the squash variety, silky and sage-infused), but my daughter's tagliatelle with meatballs and husband's salmon were also lovely. It's a quirky spot--I would've liked to have been offered some pepper or extra Parmesan, for example--but the warm welcome more than made up for it. On a weeknight they were underpopulated, too--so the lack of a Soup-Nazi-ish wait adds to the relaxing vibe. Prices not cheap, but fair. They do brunch on weekends!

If you want fresh sushi this is your place in New York.There are millions of sushi restaurants but the word fresh is the key when eating decent sushi .Yasuda has a nice location and they have special rolls as well.
Good brunch place mostly Mediterranean food. In pretty neighborhood.

Pork Betty was so amazing! We got a bowl of rice just so we wouldn't waste that tasty juice left in the plate. Scallop handroll was so delicious. Recommended to us by the owner. Â Next time I will order 4 of them and call it a meal. The "bombs" were fun, I really liked the one with eel. Loved the presentation as well. Karage chicken was fried to perfection. Tender juicy pieces of chicken with a crisp coating. I came here in the winter, so my piece of advice is - avoid that door!!!
Great convenient store to stock up on korean food! All types in convenient packaging to take on the go. There's also seating to eat indoors. Pricing isn't bad either!

Num Pang...you're tiny, kinda dingy-lookin' and your sandwiches are a bit drippy....all the reasons why I heart you! Delicious sandwiches with lots of flavor and generous portions. Â I've tried a most of their sandwiches already. Â My favorites are the fatty-fat Pork Belly (Emeril would be proud) the Coconut Shrimp (it's got some heat but in a good way) and the Grilled Mackerel. Â The Mackerel was the most surprising...you would think that it's a tiny slice, but NO! Â It's was like a 1-lb slab fishy goodness!!! Â I thought maybe they made a mistake, but stopped caring as I dove in to my sandwich. Oh and get the corn while you're there.

Had a rocky start here. First, the place was packed. Â They brought us through the main area, DOWN the stairs, then UP the stairs, then told us to wait. Â I was so confused where I was until a smarter friend pointed out we were next door and still at street level. Â We waited next to a group of very loud Europeans and I was really giving up hope until our waitress brought us to a table downstairs. Â We essentially had the entire "floor" to ourselves with very light music. Our waitress then went ahead and recommended 2 very good bottles of wine. Â We ordered various appetizers and entrees. Â The veal meatballs and the pork shoulders (sorry, never took italian class) are definitely worth trying. Â The rest of the dishes were decent but not amazing. Â I was looking forward to the Tiramisu but they ran out, so I skimped out on dessert. Â My friends seemed satisfied however. Overall, good place. Â We had a great meal but I think that was Â partially due to our table location. Â I cant imagine being nearly as pleased had they sat us upstairs. Â Still worth checking out. Oh yes, cash only. Â We had 8 people and ended up sending 3 people out to the ATMs to get enough cash.

I've been back a few times after my first not-so-great visit, and have to increase my rating. Most recently, I had an absolutely delicious mid-week dinner, and left very, very happy. The food was again delicious, especially the tuna sashimi and the scallops, and the service was much, much better. My only problem was one assistant server who rushed us with our appetizers. We still had almost half of the appetizers remaining, and she bussed our plates. When I told her we were still working on them, she said she was just making room for the entrees, which was kind of annoying, since she took our appetizer plates away and made it awkward to continue eating them. Despite this, our main server was excellent and we had a great meal. Will be back again.
This was my first trip to Astoria and I have to say, if the other restaurants here are anything like Sweet Afton I will have to visit more! Tip: Try the fried pickes!

I've been here quite a few times. And yes I'm Thai, so I have a pretty big bias on Americanized Thai food. The resturant was recommended to me by my mother, who when mentioning a thai resturant to go to she will always answer, "Lets go to Sripraphai." And comming from a very traditional mother who does not like to eat out much is a compliment. My family and I use to come here fairly often, when the owner and her family opened this place up and it was only a room and a kitchen. Now it's huge. The food is great and "authentic" if you really like spicy food ask for it. The resturant closes early around 9:30 so get there early. At night the resturant gets crowded. I would suggest going mid afternoon around 3-4pm. No reservation, first come first served. Also a big plus is ask for the menu with the pictures, it helps you decided what you want to eat. Come hungry.
I'm from DC - the pho there is really fantastic since there is a huge Vietnamese community - the pho here is the only pho I've ever had that rivals it - defintely a great place!

A real gem. I didn't know what to expect as I enter what appeared to be an office building and went down some steps. I walked in and was struck by the inviting and cozy restaurant. The list of sake was outstanding, as was the waiter who recommended different ones to try. For food we had the following which was excellent Hirame Ponzu (this was so refreshing, I could of had 3 dishes of it) Ebi Sticks Maguro Natto (my husband liked, it wasn't my type of dish, I realize fermented soy beans aren't my thing) Gyu Miso Nikomi (completely melts in your mouth) If you like authentic Japanese dishes and an impressive sake list, you won't be disappointed!

Could never get a resy for dinner so I we ended up going for lunch. Â A bit on the pricey side but the food was excellent. Â Pulpo, fried oysters, pumpkin/goat cheese croquetas, skirt steak with romesco and pbelly with plaintains were all worthy Â of round 2. Â Service was great and a glass of wine is really 1 1/2 glasses which was a nice addition. Â I'll be back for the Jamon!

I looooovvvvvvvvvvveeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeee this place to pieces. The service is friendly. The food is delicious. The oxtails fall right off the bone and the sauce is delightful. The cow foot stew is omg. Everyone I referred to this place agrees that the food is off the chain. I love it, love it, love.

Ahh Little Owl! How we love you! We recently moved to the West Village and were looking for a "neighborhood spot" to frequent when we found this place. It is fantastic! The staff is friendly and the food is phenomenal. I highly recommend the halibut and the barolo. You may have to wait a while for a table but it's totally worth it.

we had just come from a bbq and i just wanted a salad, when we stumbled upon this place. had no idea they were known for their seafood! had the peasant salad which was so fresh and delicious! the block of feta they give you tastes perfectly mild, just how i like feta. and the tomatoes, cucumbers, and onions are tossed ever so lightly in olive oil. we also got the grilled octopus which was the most tender octopus i've had. we actually didn't have any seafood here but from what i saw of the table over, the shrimped looked huge and butterflied beautifully, and the fish was whole, fillet'd, and deboned. my bf got the quail, and that was even finger licking good. i wasn't too crazy about the lemon potatoes as everyone else seems to be. maybe bc the sweetness remind me of sweet potatoes or yams...which i am not a fan of. i was also expecting more of a roasted potato while this was almost a Â mashed consistency. seems like usually there is a wait, but on july 4th evening, we got a table right away. will definitely come back if in astoria again for their seafood! a quick tip- they take credit, but tip is cash only, so make sure u have SOMETHING on you!

Great spot to catch up with girl friends (or perhaps for a date). Â Typically doesn't have a long wait for a table, attentive service, and really conveniently located (nearby subways/generally central). Â  Not a ton of selection on the menu (food) but enough choice to find something for everyone (vegetarian-friendly) and great options for sharing. Nice, chill wine bar vibe and the crostinis are delish.

A new cozy Thai restaurant that just opened up on Ninth Avenue. Of course, I'm gonna need to give it a try since I always stop by Alvin Ailey for dance classes. The name of this place is a play on word, noodles & nudies. The decor is pretty simple, but it makes such an impact by mounting bunch of plates/bowls on one wall and left the other exposed brick. It does really attract the passersby to stop and look! There are 8 tables on one side and the bar on the other. Really well design for such a small space. We sat down and asked the waiter what's good. He recommended Cold Tofu for appetizer and Yentafo Noodles for the entrÃ©e. I said why not? Surprise me. BTW, I went there with two other friends. They ordered Fried Mushroom Dumplings and Kee Mao Noodles. Cold Tofu is a signature dish that you have to try! It's really savory. Kee Mao Noodles topped with fried basil is tasty. Nice touch! What surprised me the most is Yentafo Noodles which they try a different approach by using tomato broth instead of a stinky tofu one. It tastes really good. They don't have a long list of dishes on their menu, but I'm sure they're all good!

Found a convenient place to jump into on a fifteen degree afternoon. Service and food were equally great. Would absolutely come back to try their diverse dinner menu. An Indian restaurant that serves scallops, crab and duck dishes?!? Count me in.
Always great even when you are in a hurry. Lombardi's is a couple of blocks from my office and is great for a sit down pie or delivery. It's a soho landmark for good reason!

Absolutely love this place. Â Been here twice, each time given wait times of 1hr+ but being seated within 45min (that's a win in my book)! Â This place is terrible for groups unless you are good at predicting in how many hours you will be hungry (1?2?). Â The prices are reasonable and the sides are delicious. Â The weird thing is, I've been here on two occasions, months apart, yet the meatball special has been "buffalo chicken" both times?? Â Recommend getting the hero, which I feel is the best bang for the buck and your stomach. Â Also, the mint chocolate chip ice cream sandwich they have is very minty. Â Like toothpaste minty. Â If you're into that.

Ventured over to Hell's Kitchen on a Sunday morning after hearing rave reviews of this place and I'm glad we did. Â The menu is filled with empanadas with all different combinations. Â My friend and I each ordered 3 empanadas each including: Huevos Pericos (breakfast all day!), shredded chicken, greek spinach pie (similar to a spanakopita), brasil, cuban and the reggaeton. Â They were ready relatively quickly and absolutely delicious. Â The Huevos Pericos is my personal favorite - but thoroughly enjoyed them all. Â Will definitely be back. As the others reviews say - this place is tiny, but well worth it.

The strangest thing about Astoria is that all the Greek restaurants there suck. All million of them. When my wife started working in the area and we started discovering supposedly superb restaurant scene of Â this "new SoHo", we were sure to be mesmerized with all those tavernas with unpronounceable names. Every one of them tuned out to be worse than another. Then my Greek friend, restaurant owner himself, told me about this place. Â  Tonight was our second trip. What can I tell you? The food is great, just nicely prepared and perfectly seasoned fish, salads and vegetables. Is it worth waiting in a tiny corridor for an hour? Definitely not. This place makes sense off hours, off season, on a rainy weekday. Waiting for 20 minutes to pay your check and discover that you can't tip on the card adds insult to injury. P.S. There is a large Greek restaurant almost across the street from Taverna Kyclades, always empty, one full table at most. How bad is the food there, if everyone waits for hours to get a tiny table in Taverna and doesn't walk across the street? P.P.S. There are no good Russian restaurants in Brighton Beach either.

I made many orders from this place, they have tasty food and the prices are ok. The delivery is very slow. The food came after more than an hour in both of the times. They charged for coke and french fries but I didn't get it in the delivery. This happened more than once. I wish they hired someone else that can take orders.

The food was awesome, the crowd was chill, it is small but it didn't feel cramped. it was a tuesday night as well, the music is nice too --up to date not too loud. the beer selection is small but well worth it especially for the price. bangin' burger sliders, they're larger than the typical slider as well. cheese fries bangin' too! got the guiness milkshake and that was delicious too. Another one of me and my girlfriend's awesome finds :)

I really like Terroir's East Village location, so I pretty much knew that I'd likely be in for the same here in Tribeca. But, surprise! The Tribeca location is way more spacious than its East Village counterpart. And that's always a plus in my book! What I like about Terroir is that it has a casual ambiance, which is especially great when you're getting together for a chill night out with your girlfriends. But, on the other hand, if you wanted to come here on a date, it can also exude an air of intimacy, which I find a bit more true in the front room, which is made of mostly two top tables. I've seen groups here in the back, which is something you'd likely not be able to do at Terroir EV. I like that the staff is knowledgeable on the wines and most importantly that they pour you a taste before they fill your glass. I'm by no means a wine connoisseur, so although your description may sound delightful, my taste buds have the last say. And nothing's worse than paying $14 for a glass of wine you hate. Which is why I appreciate their willingness to let you "try before you buy." These guys have also recommended some really great wines that I think I otherwise would not have tried before. As for the food, I've tried a variety, but I'd say that they make some excellent bruschette. My favorite is the tomato, basil & egg bruschetta. It's fabulous - just order it! Seriously, I'd eat one right now if I could! Solid charcuterie plates and delicious red wine & oxtail risotto balls. We've ordered the saucy mozzarella balls and the fett'unta bruschetta (aka garlic bread) and used the bruschetta as a vehicle to sop up the last drops of the sauce from the mozzarella balls. So good! Happy hour prices have gone up from $6 to $7 for select wines and the free glass of sherry is now $2.50, but I believe Tribeca's HH is a full hour longer than EV, so I'll take it! And, I'll definitely be back. You'll recognize me with a glass of wine, shoveling that tomato, basil & egg bruschetta in my face...

Tiny little gem of delight! No, they do not take reservations and I have waited 3 hours for a table but it is so worth it! When the wait gets long, we just give them our number and then head to a bar or come back after a nice stroll around the block. Really, there's a ton of bars around there so don't just stand there waiting. Start your drinks early! One thing I do admire about their no reservation policy is that they abide by it no matter who the guest is. Shrimp & grits - Amazing. Very tasty and you feel comforted and loved after a plate! Makes you want more but you have to hold yourself and resist. Jumbo lump crabmeat - Don't get this... This comes with a side a hardcore mustard which unfortunately becomes the best part of the dish. The crab doesn't have the fresh taste to it and whomever pulled the meat out of the shell didn't go a great job so you literally had to eat it with care since 99% you'd bite into little pieces of shell.
