Crispy braised pork hock - This is what I call badass! I've been here around 10 times and I always get this as an entree. Yes, I do want to try other plates but I can never get myself to cheat on the hock. I feel like they've changed the hock in recent months. It's become much smaller but yet tastier. Still, to me it's a tad on the bland side so I love spreading some of the hardcore mustard which I save from the crab over the meat. Try it, it's awesome! Escarole side dish is tasty but I can't wait till the brussel sprouts are in season again. I haven't had better than here! Hashbrown side dish is crunchy on the outside and soft and gueey on the inside. Spring stuffing - just get it... It's great! I'm a huge fan of Gabe's especially since he humbly works at the bar and takes care of everyone sitting around. I actually had no idea he was the owner until the end of the meal. I remember asking him about the pate and after he introduced it, I thought to myself "wow, this bartender is well trained!" Ooops!

Actually had some time off yesterday and had a late weekday lunch with a friend. Not really knowing much about the place, I was pleasantly surprised with the menu and wasn't sure what to try. I settled on the Yuca brunch dish with a poached egg served over shrimp & potatoes that were really tasty. The sweet plantains were good, but I prefer a different version than what they serve here. The white sangria was also delicious and was a good serving for $6 a glass. How can you beat happy hour from 1 - 8?? My friend had the coconut fish & chips with yuca fries which looked really good as well. Overall, enjoyed the lazy, late afternoon lunch we had.

For a while, Japanese "fast food" style restaurants were everywhere in Manhattan, then they started fading away a bit (giving way to tons of cheap sushi joints). Â Pretty much at random, my girlfriend and I ran by Kobeyaki while looking for some eats. Â The storefront was welcoming, with a *big* wood door with a handle substantial enough that it actually says to "Pull Hard" on it (I know, I know). Â When you enter you're greeted with big pictures of food on one side and booth seating on the other side. Â The counter/cashier where you order is towards the back with a nice, cleanly laid out menu. The menu isn't huge, but that's the point. Â There are some sushi rolls, rice or salad bowls with a protein, desserts and burgers (including a spicy tuna burger). Â It's nice and simple so you don't get lost in a ton of choices and the food gets out faster. I ordered a Teriyaki chicken salad bowl while my girlfriend got the Beef salad bowl. Â We also ordered an Eel "Special" Roll to share. Â The salad bowls are quite substantial, with a wonderful mix of crisp vegetables topped with chicken in a *wonderfully* sweet sauce. Â It's not overwhelming, but just right to satisfy the taste buds. Â The beef bowl was definitely a bit heartier, but that's hardly a shock. Â Either way, it was delicious! The eel roll was gigantic and it's served in a really cute serving platter shaped like a boat. Â The eel had a nice, roasted flavor to it with some sweetness. Â Add on some of their wasabi mayo (available at a fixings table) and maaaan you have some delicious eats! You know a place is good when you're already thinking about going back before you've even left the first time, and Kobeyaki definitely fits the bill!
As long as you're willing to hike this far out into the east village, you're in for a solid burger for now a bad price.

It's pretty good. Chewy noodles, deep broth, Okay-char siu... I prefer Totto Ramen though. Compared to the hours long wait in front of Ipuudo? Not worth it - I would wait half that long even for Totto.

After hearing about this place, finally made it here. I expected a long wait but it was still pretty ridiculous - an hour. The classic beef meatballs in a spicy sauce were good and flavorful, though the tomato sauce tasted like it was from a jar. I'm sure it's not, but still tasted like it. The spicy pork with mushroom sauce was good too. The meatballs were very tender and weren't dry at all - very well made. The mashed potatoes were actually pretty delicious. But what's not when it's covered in butter?? I had the chocolate banana cookies with mint ice cream, which was good, although I couldn't taste the banana at all. This place was good, but not one hour wait good. Very friendly and efficient staff, though.
Really enjoyed there food. The price was ok also. I went there wit my wife and kids. They attended us very well. Friday night they had live music there. I would definitely reccomend
This place is a total hidden gem. It's never crowded but the food and wine are really stellar! It also has a cozy little back garden, perfect for summer nights.

Today was the second time I have come to Clinton St. Baking Company and just like the first time, the wait is obnoxiously long. We actually had over 1.5 hour wait. Eventually we were able to get seated and between the three of us, we got the spanish scramble, eggs benedict with smoked salmon, huevos rancheros, pancakes with warm maple butter, and a side of sugar cured bacon. The first time I came here I had the smoked salmon scramble which I remember to be pretty good. Like most reviews say, the pancakes are amazing. They're very fluffy and flavorful - it's just awesome! The eggs benedict I was a bit disappointed with. It was served over a biscuit and while it is different, I think I would've preferred it to be over an english muffin. The biscuit made it very heavy and really takes away the flavors of everything else. I tried the heuvos rancheros with the chorizo. It was alright - it was a mess to eat because everything was saucy with the salsa and the guac. I didn't try the spanish scramble but the person who had the dish said it was pretty good. The sugar cured bacon reminded me of pork jerky - very different taste coming from bacon which is usually very salty. I think I would only come back here if I really have a strong craving for pancakes because the wait is just ridiculous. It might be better during dinner hours, but brunch/lunch hours will almost guarantee you a 1+ hour wait.

Fraudulent charges. 2 pounds of brisket at 25 dollars a pound. Nice try. Your BS prices are now put up for public to view. Credit card disputing charges. Watch what they charge you and don't be intimidated. They are liars and cheats, that is guaranteed.
This place was awesome! -- Great location -- Amazing Food -- Awesome Drinks -- Professional Service -- 5 STAR everything!
This is what I said to my friend after taking my first bite of a spinach arthicoke slice: "I think an angel just came in my mouth." I don't how else to describe it.

the first several times i ordered from or ate at song, they were pretty damn good -- especially for the dirt cheap prices. but i find with each subsequent visit i'm more & more underwhelmed. maybe my memories are just distorted by my continuing expectations, but calamari that was once crunchy & tasty is now rubbery & bland, & noodle dishes that were once loaded with fresh, delicious ingredients are now greasy & mushy. you can do much worse for thai, i guess, but i'm losing faith in you, song.

Seriously I drive across Brooklyn just to come to this place. Â This place is small, but its all worth it. Their fresh baked pita is to DIE for. Lentil soup, tasty, falafels delish. Chicken platter yum-o. Pita pizzas-great! Â Minus a star because they dont take credit cards.

There is nothing better than catching up with a close friend over delicious food and cocktails! Before we headed to a comedy show at The Stand, we had dinner at County. The seating is family style. We went at 6pm so THANK GOD we did not need to sit by other people. We each started with a cocktail. I chose the Lavender Diamond, made with Gin, CrÃ¨me de Violette, Dry Vermouth, Hibiscus Flower, Orange Bitters and Rose Water. I'd compare it to a floral martini. The cocktail was well balanced but a bit strong. I did like it but it was definitely a sipping drink...not a chugging a drink! Ingrid went with the Hudson Swizzle, made with Vodka, Fresh Blueberry & Lemon, Ginger, Pomegranate, and Orange Blossom Water. We decided to split an appetizer based on Yelp! reviews. The Salmon Tartare was made with Crispy Sushi Rice, Herb CrÃ¨me Fraiche, Fresh Grated Horseradish and Lemon Zest and Sesame Garlic Topping. This was SO GOOD! The sauces really complemented the salmon - so tasty! Ingrid ordered the Pan Roasted Chicken. The dish featured organic chicken, garlic mashed potatoes, braised collard greens and pan drippings. The chicken was very tender! I was a bit jealous of what she ordered when I saw it! She is a good friend though, so she let me try some. She also ordered a side of Garlic Herb Parmesan Fries. She said we could "share" it - I clearly ate more than my part, but we cannot let fries go to waste! I read rave reviews about the House Cavatelli, made with Pork Ragu, Fresh Ricotta, Braised Kale, Lemon Breadcrumbs, and Pecorino Pepato. The pasta and the pork were great however the lemon breadcrumbs were a bit excessive. It would have been ok if there was only a dusting of breadcrumbs and not a blizzard. After I finished my first drink, I ordered the Candied Ginger Old Fashioned, made with Bourbon, Ramazzotti, Candied Ginger, Angostura and Orange Bitters. I loved this drink! For me, it was much more smooth than the first cocktail. I never really upload photos of me enjoying my cocktails, so here is one for your viewing pleasure! :) Ingrid and I are both big fans of dessert (because we are humans), so we decided to split one. We went with the bread pudding, topped with a bourbon glaze. This was delicious! Overall, a solid restaurant with a strong cocktail list, delicious entrees and great service. I would recommend getting the Salmon Tartare appetizer and the Bread Pudding for sure!

Deceivingly large... surprisingly exotic... the brunch at Miriam was one of the best I have experienced. Â  While the place is cash only for brunch, it is bustling , yet spacious, ensuring that you will quickly get a table (I know... weird, right?). Â They have a great selection of unique drinks and the menu servicing everyone from the traditional brunch fare to the adventurous eater. Â The waitress was a great help in considering what we were all to order, from drinks to food and always checked in (a sign of great service!) Sandwiches, eggs, israeli salad.... they were all super yummy. Â And I know when I say super yummy you don't believe it because of my word choice... but it is!

A real gem. Carpaccio was some of the best I've ever had. Coffee was superb. Very busy and they don't take your name so you have to be somewhat diligent about getting seated if there's a wait, but totally worth it. My new favorite cafe in NYC.
After all the great reviews we were overall disappointed. The food was good but nothing spectacular.

The Empire Diner is like falling in love. Unassuming, unexpected and it completely catches you by surprise. My boyfriend and I stopped in for an early dinner before heading to what we knew would be a horrendous prix-fixe birthday dinner for a friend at a drag bar uptown and I was completely and utterly blown away. I know who Amanda Freitag is from her appearances on Chopped but I've never experience her food before today. She made a believer out of me. The Mac and Cheese was an exercise in flavor profiling, restraint and nostalgia. In a word: perfection. The charred octopus Greek salad fired on all cylinders and even the modest grilled cheese was elevated to deity status. My new mission in life is to run through every expertly crafted dish on the menu and rant and rave about each one as I go.
Great BBQ! not the best i have ever had, but really really good. Plus it's in a hot part of town, if your in the area you will not be disappointed. really busy, but all around great food!!
Best falafel I've ever had and you cant go wrong for 2.50. Ask for spicy but be ready for a little sweat!

Is it possible to rate a restaurant 100 stars?!!! I dream of Ippudo ever since my visit in NY. In fact, it hurts just reviewing it 2 months after my visit because reliving this in memory kills me! Someone purchase me a ticket to NY so I can fulfill my craving!!!! My traveling buddy and I came around 5 as we heard that the wait can be VERY long. Ours took like 30-45 minutes. They have a bar at the front so you can drink while waiting, which is smart and something we took an advantage of. We were then seated at the counter where you can watch the cooks make every individual dish. It was such a cool and mesmerizing experience! Of course, we shared one order of the pork buns. OMG. OMG. Every bite....OMG. So simple yet so bomb. The combo of bun + pork bun + mayo + lettuce was so divine and heavenly in the sense that you reached some kind of nirvana. I felt happy and at ease. The only problem is that I only had one!!!!! But then it was time to move to the Akamura Modern ramen which might possibly be my favorite because of their light broth. I realized that I am more of a light soup type of ramen girl. And Ippudo has it down. You don't feel like there's hella MSG or salt. It was really on point. Noodles good. Flavors good. All on all, solid bowl! Ippudo come to SF!!!!!!

A more-than-enjoyable time for lovers of food and drink, alike. The food is fantastic and the bar selection can't be beat. Keep an eye out for celebrities and off-duty chefs headed to the invite-only third floor.

After reading all of the excellent reviews for this place I made a reservation for dinner for my boyfriend and I on Friday night. Our reservations were for 9:00 and when we arrived on time we were told he would have a table for us shortly, within 15 minutes. Instead of hovering over the diners enjoying their meal we left our phone number and decided to circle the block until our table was ready. After 20 minutes without a call we returned to the restaurant to find two parties of 4 waiting outside to also be seated. Now there were 10 people waiting to enter this small restaurant and after another 20 minutes of waiting outside we discovered that the two parties had 8:30 reservations and that inevitably we would be waiting quite a while until they were sat before us. The two parties were seated around 9:45 (1 hour and 15 minutes after their reservations) At 10:05 we saw a table leave the restaurant and we entered thinking that it would finally be our turn to be seated. NOPE! The owner gave our table away to a gentlemen waiting no where near as long as us. He said he would have another table for us shortly to which we replied that was what we were told over an hour ago and exited the restaurant to take our business elsewhere. Oh and let me also mention that another couple entered the restaurant without reservations and were charged at by the manger with he finger wagging 'No way, not tonight". They knowingly overbook this restaurant and pay no mind to leaving you waiting in the cold for hours. RUDE, ABYSMAL SERVICE!

Wonderful! Â An intimate, romantic restaurant with delicious food and drinks! Â If you like raspberry, I highly recommend the raspberry mojito. Â **Tip they don't take reservations for parties under 6. Â We heard that this place was more known for their sides and appetizers so we went a little crazy: Table bread and olive oil (spicy or extra virgin) is served. We ordered a lot so here are the rankings -- Top 5 were the best. 1. Chardonnay Steamed Mussels - THE BEST EFFIN mussels I've ever tried in my life! 5 stars! Perfectly cooked and wonderfully flavored with fennel, garlic, shallots, lemon confit, and tarragon. Â That broth was so delicious and perfect for sopping up with the table bread. Â I'm already dreaming about these. 2. Truffle Mac and Cheese Tart - Really amazing deconstructed macaroni and cheese tart. Â If you like truffle oil, you'll go crazy for this as you really taste the truffle-ness. Â Really addicting after the first bite. Â  3. Lemon Crusted Chilean Seabass (entre) was SO delicious with the interesting potato puree and salsa verde/avocado on the bottom of the plate. Â The fish was wonderfully steamy and fresh. Â Did not notice the crispy artichokes, however. 4. Fries with Gorgonzola fondue -- thin crispy fries with a really amazing cheese sauce for dipping. Â  5. Pan Roasted Sea Scallops - scallops were served perfectly seared with a potato pancake,warm bacon vinaigrette and roasted apple. Â The sour cream was an interesting touch. - 6. Hanger Steak Au Poivre (entre) this was your basic steak frites dish. Â The bÃ©arnaise went well with the thin, crispy fries (but I went more for the gorgonzola fondue dipping sauce). 7. Pistachio Crusted Goat Cheese Salad - This was a tasty salad, of julienned roasted beets, endive, watercress, slivered granny smith apple encasing the soft goat cheese at the bottom. Â  8. Roasted Butternut Squash Soup was pretty good.. not very memorable but it was comforting and flavorful for sure. 9. Braised Short Rib Tacos - two soft corn tortilla tacos, they were good. Â I'm not sure if I care for short rib tacos in general. - (There were 3 other dishes I didn't try much: Lobster Tortellini, Brussel Sprouts with carmelized apples and pancetta, Roasted Artichoke Parmesan salad). Dessert: Creme Brulee -- great custard and thick carmelized sugar top Because I tried so many, I'm giving this a 5. Â I hope this review helps those deciding on dishes. Â Service was alright, the wait was worth it and as for the crowdedness --its NY people. Â Nothing new about that! ;)

Knowing this is the "original" New York pizza place adds to the experience -- great pizza, worth the price and the trip. Â I've been back several times since. Â I'm giving them a "5 star" just for nostalgia alone. Â It's true what "they" say -- you can't get this kind of pizza on the west coast.

Planned to visit here after reading great reviews. Was lucky enough to come across the mobile van in Brooklyn and had the harissa falafel... Words cant describe how tasty it all was!! The falafels, quinoa and hummus were just outstanding! Cant rave about this enough!

Hudson Clearwater is the speakeasy of restaurants. Â Well knowing that it was hard to find, I was completely baffled by the other 2 doors in which I thought were the entrance. Â It wasn't until a passerby in the neighborhood who guided us to the actual entrance. Tip of the day: Â The entrance is on Morton St, not Hudson. What a cute restaurant! Greeted by a small gardened yard and attractive wait staff, how can you not like this place? Â What is it about hidden places that pique the new yorker's interest? Â Trying to avoid my all time go to meat - duck, I ordered the hanger steak. Â As Dan T notes, it was quite a generous cut and executed very well. Â However, I would have preferred it if my boyfriend's duck breast was on my plate instead -- I can't help it, I love duck. Â  The olive oil cake was a bit odd for dessert, and personally thought they should have made an olive oil ice cream to pair with it. Great date spot, I would recommend going again!

Good coffee is hard to find but good Cuban coffee is impossible to find, until now. The Cafe Con Leche is the only way to start your day & the sweet treats they have are to die for! If your downtown and need a coffee or sugar fix, you've got to stop by here. Great walk up window, that makes it an easy and quick stop.

After going to Pearl Oyster Bar the night before and not satisfying my craving for seafood and oysters, I decided to hit Fish with the g/f. While the physical space isn't as nice as Pearl, Fish definitely hits the spot with a decent selection of oysters (vs. no selection at Pearl) and fresh seafood. The abundance of specials (PBR and oysters for $8, lobster feast for $20, and crab feast for $21) make this a good go to spot for seafood. Fried oysters with seaweed salad is good as well.

I am a native new yorker and have been living in Manhattan for the last 10 yrs, this is the best restaurant in NYC. Â Amazing food, amazing staff and amazing ambiance. Go for lunch sit at the bar order the soup and sandwich its always amazing, ask for the soup first then the sandwich will come with a side salad ... satisfaction guaranteed. If you are unaware of the aforementioned you are welcome.
It kicked bobby flays ass and its atop of premier asian food a must go
Ordered take out for lunch the other day. Its cheap. Its pretty good. Its prepared well. Its clean. It didn't blow me away, but I'll probably get it again. Solid food for the money.

After returning from Singapore I was starting to worry I wouldn't get my Indian fix nearby. Â No worries, Benares is great: food is authentic and they're not shy with the spices. Â It's as good as Indian back in Singapore, though admittedly more expensive. Â Servers have been attentive as well.
One of the best pizzas in the city and the world... great place for a date; would highly recommend.

My favorit bar restaurant in BROOKLYN,try anything on the menu, It is truelly mouth watering delicious!!!! A no joke kind of a place!!! Â  They even have a rare Whiskey from Sweden, make sure to ask the bar tender!!!

This restaurant gets 5 starts for the ambiance and people, however, the Manhattan that they made me was horrible, who puts Grand Marnier in a Manhattan. Â That dropped them a start. Â  What drops it three more starts was them changing the tip that was on my credit card bill, adding an additional $6. Â  I would recommend that anyone using a credit card to pay at this bar check their records thoroughly and hold onto their signed copies in case you need to dispute a charge.

I thought the food was pretty decent. Â What was really cool was the ambiance. Â I love the craft beers on tap as well as the shared picnic benches. Â We love venturing out to Brooklyn and all their good eats. Maybe dinner is better than lunch, so we'll probably come back again. Â For ambiance sake, it's better than Hill Country. Â For food, Hill Country wins.

have you had the grilled corn? do yourself a favor and order it. as for the rest of the food there, it's so-so. but that might be because the grilled corn is SO banging that nothing can tantalize the taste buds after that. and seriously, as a veg, i know there's gonna be a very limited selection at a cuban place. service is meh, getting a spot inside (and if you do it's pretty packed) proves to be difficult but there is always the quick eats extension around the corner.

I love this place! The food was great (especially loved the beet salad and cold curried carrot and coconut soup!), the atmosphere was wonderful and the service was good! I brought my two year old with and they were very accommodating. They have butcher paper on the tables and thick crayons so that was a big hit with the toddler as well! If I lived around the corner from this place I would be coming back all the time. New favorite spot in the west Village and perhaps in all of Manhattan! ;)

tiny place, friendly staff, soup of the day-vegetable with couscous , wasnt great jsu average. however, main dish special-chicken papay was Delicious hands down. crepe with chicken and spinach was good. bill came out to 90 including bottle of wine and tips. one negative is no credit cards accepted and spacing

Best spot. Â Great price, and great system; if it's crowded, you can get a pint or some wine next door, and the affable Maitre'd will come and get you! And you can bring your drink with you! Â  Great food and prices, it's amazing how many people I've recommended it to and it worked out perfectly for them! Â LOVE IT!

Walked by here late last weekend and went in after being easily tempted by the thought of taquitos which were outstanding. Crunchy, tasty, very reasonable, and the hot sauces really hit the spot. Awesome place for late night cravings if you're in the area.

Very reminiscent of people watching brasseries in the cobble stoned streets of o'l Paris, but this place is in a small street in Queens where not many people are walking around... to be watched. Â  Nevertheless! Â They serve heaping bowls of coffees (or cafe au lait), deliciously crisp lamb sausage baguette sandwiches, fluffy french toast with a side of fruit salad. Â This place is really cute and the food does not disappoint. Â The service may be a little inconsistent during high-tide but when is anything French wham-bam-thank-you ma'am? Â It's a socialist background, so I've been told. Â  Take it slow and enjoy life (well, the food!). This is definitely my go-to Saturday brunch spot in the LIC neighborhood... would even go as far as an outer-borough brunch recommendation being how easy it is to get to via subway.
The rest of this overpriced behemoth I could do without, but they do something to their iced cappuccinos that is so out of this world it is indescribably delicious, I dream about them....frequently.

My 400th review. To me, a tavern brings about images of olden times where travelers come and go, wanting food, alcohol, or, simply a place to gather and rest, similar to an inn. Dim lighting, the presence of a bar, intimate seating, plus a volume amplified by inebriated guests would best describe the atmosphere inside one. Minetta Tavern is a perfect example, but with a touch of class. A humongous plate of BONE MARROW ($21) kicked-off our night of debauchery here. Oozing with all that fatty goodness, its luscious flavor pairs hand in hand with the shallot confit that's slightly sweet in taste. We placed it atop a buttery toast that altogether we couldn't seem to get enough of. Again, this order is huge so it's best shared with someone. I enjoyed the subtle way the flavors of their OXTAIL and FOIE GRAS TERRINE ($17) creeps up on you. One bite, two bites, and you get that punch-in-the-face flavor profile. It's earthy and tangy, I really enjoyed this dish albeit its small portion. Â  Famed for the $28 BLACK LABEL BURGER, we simply cannot resist ordering one. The meat itself is a combination of four different types of cuts: brisket, short rib, skirt, and dry-aged rib eye. High-grade quality as you can imagine. Cooked medium, it came out glowing pink in the middle, juicy, and oh so succulent. The brioche-like bun promotes the burger's cause so very-well with its hint of sweetness that highlights the beef all the more. Only topped with caramelized onions that's obviously cooked in the beef fat, this entire burger seems so simple yet very sophisticated in taste. It comes with a side of their house fries that's rather addicting in all sense of the word (ask for mayo and ketchup for dipping). For what it's worth, the price tag somehow seems reasonable. Their PASTA ZA ZA ($19) did not fail the pasta lover in me. Freshly made and perfectly al dente, the texture is so worthy of praise. It's prepared with pancetta, (yes, Italian bacon!) sage, and parmesan, then topped with fried egg that you'll have the honor to mix up altogether. Watching the egg yolk ooze out as incorporates itself with all the elements of this dish is a pleasure in itself. What a lovely plate of comfort this was. Order it and thank me later. Sealing this night on a sweet note, CHOCOLATE SOUFFLE ($19), sil vous plait! Can I say, best ever? Hah! I know it gets thrown out there a lot, but I sincerely mean it. It's one of the sexiest and most decadent desserts I've had. Superb! Sharing is highly recommended. Â  As part of Keith McNally's empire, the same genius behind Balthazar, it's no surprise to me that Minetta Tavern would live up to its hype. Fantastic food and stellar service, they earned their one Michelin star, fair and square.

It's always hard to take parent's to dinner. You want them to be pleased, but you want to enjoy the experience as well. Â You don't want them to bitch about the price, but you don't want to take them to a dump. My mom tends to feel "old" if she is in the presence of people her own age and thus likes to go to young and "fun" places. Â And while she pretends to be easy to please, she is really nothing of the sort. I decided to take her to Scarpetta. Having eaten at the one in Miami, I knew one thing for sure: the food would be great. Â Also, considering it's close proximity to the Meatpacking district, I figured the atmosphere would be lively as well. Upon arriving we were treated graciously by the hosts and asked to wait at the bar while our table was prepared. Â This is something it seems that all the Scarpetta's do. Â Once seated we were presented with their incredible spreads and bread basket. Â This is no ordinary bread presentation. Â The basket has choices from homemade focaccia to stromboli with smoked mozzarella and salami. Â The dips go even further. Whipped mascarpone butter is the perfect accompaniment to these delicious breads as is the tomato confit and olive oil. It only gets better from here. To start we were able to try many amazing things. Â My favorites were the creamy polenta with truffled mushrooms. Â I had this in Miami and although incredibly rich and a meal in itself, it is so delicious. The scallops are another must. They were perfectly tender and paired wonderfully with the mushrooms and truffle butter. Another great starter are the beef shortribs. They are braised and served with a vegetable farro risotto. They were tender and rich. A few starters that were much lighter but in my mind not nearly as rich or satisfying as the few above are the raw fluke and the crispy frito misto. The fluke was lovely, light and simple, just didn't really stand up to the other dishes at the table. The frito misto was also surprisingly light and one of my mothers favorites. For our entrees we decided on the spaghetti, which really does deserve every bit of the hype it gets as well as the black cod. Â The black cod was the only real "miss" of the night. Served with caramelized fennel and concentrated tomatoes, it was served with a chicken stock sauce that rather overwhelmed the fish and was too meaty. Â The spaghetti was heavenly. Described on the menu as having tomato and basil, it is miles beyond your average spaghetti. We were soo full, but they had all these incredible sounding desserts and we couldn't resist. Bread pudding was surprisingly good and the pumpkin panna cotta was a bit of a miss for me. Scarpetta is the unique type of restaurant that anyone would fall in love with. Our service was great, the food delicious and an atmosphere that was sophisticated yet relaxed.

foi grass? LMGTFY Â  Anyway, ate at Roberta's on a Wednesday night around 8:15 and found a seat at the bar (inside) right away. I was worried from reading other reviews here about the vibe from the staff, but Â quickly found it warm and helpful. Had a salumi plate (excellent), a sweetbread entree (also excellent) and the Falco pie (a take on traditional Napels style salciccia I believe) which was technically done well. To be fair, the only thing wrong with it was that I've had the exact same pie in other restaurants and have been happier. Nothing the pizziaolo can do about that, the pie was spot on crust-wise (crispy, with a bit of char) and a good ratio of sauce to toppings. Â  With dinner I had planned on wine, but the bar had two of my favorite beers, so... Hitachino Â White, Â and Modelo Especial. Who doesn't like wine with dinner, but if you're really going to do pizza, in Brooklyn, beer's the only way to go. Â  The space is nice, just cozy enough without feeling too cramped, and I have to admit falling in love with the front. Cash only here and an ATM right out front? Pure NYC. That would never fly in SF, unless... plus the outside seating area is huge, about the square footage of the restaurant+, and covered from the sun/rain. Â  Overall, a great effort by a young-ish staff, and a wonderful addition to Bushwick, and the rest of the borough. Â  My only beef with this place, was that I had a great meal, and didn't bring anyone along to share it with. Â  On my way out, I started thinking how my night would have been, had I walked in committed to the ideal that the whole scene was "too cool". Â Gad I let that go at the ATM out front.

Is it possible that not one single person out of 59 people is going to mention the GALLONS of oil used to produce these lovely curries they speak so highly of? I'm truly shocked. I've NEVER had such "greasy" curry. Ugh. The jerk gets lotsa press. Signature dish, maybe? I also tried the mac n' cheese. Boooo. Meh.

A must have when visiting New York. Â I was told that wood fire ovens are banned in New york, with the exception of this place and some other place that I can't recall. Traditional NY thin crust style pizza cooked in a million degree wood fired oven, there's no substitute. If you do go, the default order is a pizza margherita (basil, mozzarella and tomato sauce). Just awesome. We tried about seven other places in NY including momofuku, this is the best one. Cool place, well worth the wait!

I hesitate to give this place a good rating because my friend got very sick and had to go home after eating the scallops. Â I decided to have my birthday dinner here and I was so excited after reading all the reviews. However, I was highly disappointed with the outcome. Â The trout was good but nothing to brag about. Love this place I've been going here for years the lamb is good chicken is good the pita bread is good . There white sauce isn't the real tasiIkyi sauce but pretty close
I loved the atmosphere. Â The staff was great, very knowledgeable about the food and the drinks.

God those balls were tasty! You know food is good if I will wait an hour to eat it. I heard about this place from a friend and it intrigued me. A whole restaurant? of meatballs? But really it is nothing like what I pictured (I am embarrassed to say resembled something like that of an Ikea plate with Swedish meatballs and some ektorppoÃ¤ngkivikberry sauce). If you go doing an off-hour it is 4 stars. Â Pricey, yes, but even if you're just "window shopping" it's Â a fun experience.

I don't like the rub they put on the their barbeque at all and the bbq sauces are not good. The side dishes are also weak. The place gets very crowded and you usually have to wait on a long line. The food is also pretty expensive.Then once you get your food it will probably be impossible to find a seat. I haven't been to sau in a while and I have no desire to go back. Next!

I went there with my wife tonight for our anniversary.. Â ordered the median steamed shellfish, which turned out to be bad. Â  The seafood wasn't fresh at all, 4 clams, 2 snail, 2 crabs, they were all gone bad, Â that account for 30% of the food on the plate.. I am used to the high prices and mediocre coffee at Starbucks. Cafe Boca Ciega has great Cuban influenced coffees and treats. This is a can't miss spot in not only TrBeCa but New York City as a whole. The staff is excellent and well versed in their art. Their coffee packs quite a punch...and absolutely love it.

Jeff, who I assume is the owner, was very responsive to my emails and took my reservation for 8 people just one day before NYE, which I greatly appreciated. Â Everyone in my party thoroughly enjoyed their meal, each ordering something different on the menu. The highlights of my meal were the burrata caprese, eggplant manicotti, pasta special of the evening, which was a homemade papardelle with short rib (?) ragu, and the brussel sprouts. I love the ambiance of BL and think this restaurant is great for any occasion, whether it be an intimate date or a group dinner. Â And the noise level is great, such that you don't have to be yelling to speak to the person next/ across from you. Â Thanks Jeff & team for an awesome NYE dinner.
This place is decent and the prices are not great but are what is to be expected in that neighborhood. Â The banana muffin was pretty good. Â Coffee there is too strong but not entirely lousy.

Wish I could give zero stars. Ordered and waited 25 minutes before they told me they had to make what I ordered. Why bother...great Mexican food across the street at San Loco. This place is miserable.
Can you get crazy for dumplings? If you try these believe me, you can.

After living in NYC for 13 years, I finally tried Pommes Frites for the first time last weekend. Why only 3 stars? Because I've had the real stuff in Belgium and this did not meet my expectations. However, kudos for the variety of dipping sauces and ingenious location in catering to drunk NYU kids and hipsters at 3 AM.
near work, good atmosphere. decent menu!

I really like the space and feel of this restaurant. Â The pastas are also very delicious. I wouldnt mind throwing a dinner party in the dining room in the back. Â There's a very homey feel about the place.

I went there recently and I have to say this is a great place if you're looking for Penang style hawker/street food. It is very authentic and the food come very close to what you would get in Malaysia especially in Penang Island. Even the waitress is from there. I can't speak for other "types" of dishes since my goal was to get those exact food I mentioned above and for that I was very satisfy with it.

I have heard a lot about this spot. Â Free cheesy poofs? Probally one of the best drunk snacks. I came in here with someone I randomly met at a concert. Â We were able to get seats at the bar and were promptly served beers. Soon, I realized why these seats were vacant...the people playing pool constantly kept putting the pool sticks into our back. Â We obliged, not that is was really there fault. Â What was annoying was this guy constantly sicking his arm between us as we were trying to talk to eachother. Â He kept taking our cheesy poofs too.
