EDIT: DO NOT get the food at the cart with the "express lane" sign. This is their bad, D-grade quality and portions. Don't go to this cart if you want the good stuff. Go to the cart a few feet away at the SW corner of 6th and 53rd. In front of the Hilton (with the big lit-up "Hilton" sign). The chicken (and lamb) over rice is PHENOMENAL. ----- Tastes blander and different from what I had in January. Smaller portions of rice and meat. Less seasoned. Even the sauce is thicker and more like mayonnaise. Did they get lazy or something tonight? 04/25/14 11:20 pm

4.5 stars... The King of Falafel won a Vendy award in 2010 for best street food in NYC, they proudly display their trophy on a pedestal by their cart on Broadway and 30th street (a block from the Broadway N/Q in Astoria). I guess the lines for this cart can get pretty long but I only had to wait for 4 people and it moved quick on a weeknight. Typically they have one guy taking the orders/payment and another guy dishing out the food. The guy taking my order was very nice and personable, one of the things I'm sure contributed to his success. I got their chicken platter (seasoned chopped chicken on rice with salad and choice of white and/or hot sauces) which they also give you a piece of falafel (which is actually pretty large and oblong verses the typical ball you get most places). The chicken was higher quality than I've ever gotten from a food cart and was seasoned and cooked perfectly, the falafel was also awesome and flavorful without being oily at all. The prices here aren't the cheapest I've seen from street carts but they're still a great value, especially considering the quality and quantity of food. Â I got the white sauce which was ok but when (not if) I go back I think I'd go without the sauce because the chicken is so flavorful and juicy it doesn't need anything. I wish I could just skip the salad and rice fillers and get a platter full of the chicken and falafel, they were awesome. The only problem is that there isn't a park or benches in the area so finding a spot to eat if you don't live in the area or want to stand is a little problematic.

So four years later, I'm singing a different tune about Habana Outpost. I met up with a group of friends after work, and since it was a bit chilly outside it wasn't packed. The spacing/seating was plentiful, and it didn't feel like we were sitting on top of another group. I bet this might change when it's more crowded. The drinks also have improved--I started with the frozen margarita and then switched to the spiked lemonade. The girl behind the counter asked how spiked I wanted it! So of course I said very spiked. The tacos were decent--I had the fish and the pork, and the pork was the clear winner. It was juicy and flavorful, while the fish taco was cold and sad, but I ate it anyway. The atmosphere was much better as well--there was background music and no smoking, and much better eye candy. Service was great--the ladies behind the bar were funny and kept the line moving quickly. Glad I gave this place another chance, especially since summer is just around the corner. Cash only!

I just had the avocado/hummus wrap and it was quite tasty! Â I'm also not a vegan so I was a little hesitant to go in, but I'm glad I did. Â I will probably start getting lunch here more often since it's near my job and everything I saw coming out of the kitchen looked delish! Â  The staff also seemed friendly so that's a bonus.
This's a small bar with excellent bar food. The $1 oysters happy-hour are oh great value and open your appetite for more! The ceviches are amazing!!!! I do recommend it for a pre-dinner!

Ate here a few days after they opened. Great space, very clean and nicely decorated. As the name suggests, the soup dumplings are the star of the show. Super thin wrapper skin, and very flavorful soup. The meat is not dense at all. I prefer the classic pork filling, but my more adventurous friends liked the super spicy and wasabi flavored ones. Saw some other people ordering the entrees, and they looked good too. Also, the wait staff was very friendly and attentive. Will definitely be back!

All I have to say is Truffel-Fries! I would give this place five stars, but they didn't have too many vegetarian options. I was a bit disappointed by that, but the food they did have that I could eat was pretty amazing! I read a few bad reviews indicating that the service was bad. I did not have that type of an experience. My host and server were both really really nice. They kept the water flowing like, well, water. And checked in a few times to make sure everything was ok. My experience was a Wednesday night, that might have been why the service was so good. I walked by on a Sunday afternoon and there were a TON of people ahnging out waiting to be seated for brunch. I could imagine that when it's that crazy the service might suffer, but be realistic in what you expect.

I went to Minetta Tavern for the first time on a Tuesday night. Â We called over a week in advance and the earliest reservation we could get was for 10:30. Â We showed up at 7:30 hoping for a cancellation or to sit at the bar. There was a wait of 3 groups of 2 ahead of my group of 2 to get bar seats but I enjoyed the fact that the bartender managed the wait for bar seats and it wasn't a free for all to grab seats as they opened up. We were seated around 8:00PM and the wait for seats at the bar had grown to 8 groups behind us. Â The bartender, from France, was extremely friendly and we enjoyed sitting there and chatting with her. Â  We split they're daily special appetizer an asparagus salad, which I would give 3/5 stars. Â It was very good but definitely not amazing. Â Both my colleague and I had the black label burger with fries for our entree. Â The burger was delicious. Â Probably among the best I have had in NYC and I can't name a specific one that was better. Â The fries were top notch as well. All if all the food is very good but the restaurant is very crowded and on the pricey side. Â I would definitely recommend going to try the burger at least once but Â it is not a place I will be going often.

This is a craft beer/cocktail establishment in Midtown East/UES. What's that? There are bars that are not Irish Pubs in this area? Yes. At least one. The vibe here is like a hipster cheers. I'm not sure if the people who come here are actually regulars or if it just seemed like it...all I know is that, by 10:30 or so, the whole room was singing happy birthday to someone who was given a shot lit on fire for the occasion. But I digress. We came in last Saturday evening around 9. The first little bar area wasn't quite full at that time, so we sat down there and never made it any further. So, I'm sure the rest of the place is amazing, too, but I can only speak to the front bar. I was excited to try the beers AND the cocktails, as it all looked so amazing. Started off with beers. It ended up being a saison night for me. On the bartender's recommendation I tried the Stillwater "Existent", which was a dark saison (what?!). I then moved on to the Other Half "Laatse Ronde", which was a smoked saison (huh?). Both were pretty good. I then moved on to a cocktail. I was intrigued by the cucumber and basil gimlet, but also a bit wary, since I typically dislike gin with the intensity of 1,000 suns. The bartender eventually convinced me, and the drink was incredible. No terrible bitterness here-- just a delightful, refreshing, vegetable-y cocktail. We also downed some delicious bites. Both varieties of oysters (Kusshi and East Beach Blonde) were excellent, and the truffle popcorn was SAVORY TRUFFLEY HEAVEN. HEA-VEN. Okay? Seriously, I would like to make this a regular part of my diet. The only slight negativo was that by the time we left (maybe around 11:30), this placed was totally packed. The bar area was far too small to accommodate everyone who was crammed together in that little room, which made it crazy difficult to frequent the bathroom. Regardless, The Jeffrey is one heck of a tasty good time.

Came here for a friend's birthday on a Tuesday night, and there was still like an hour and a half wait. I didn't mind too much, since it was beautiful outside, but if it had been cold out...that would've sucked. Anyway, I had never had good ramen before, so this was all new to me. We got some appetizers - the baby octopus special (which was ok), some chicken and pork buns (delicious!) and the fried shrimp in mayo sauce special...which was absolutely to die for! i could've just eaten the pork buns and the fried shrimp all night, and been totally happy. I got the ramen with shrimp dumplings, which was pretty damn good. Overall it's a fun place, with good food, but I'm not a fan of places where you know you will always have to wait an hour+. Also, just reading other reviews and learning about the MSG doesn't help.
i am so behind with my "eats" through nyc, i'll post the pics and say nothing lol Room service- 5 stars Service -attentive Atmosphere-chic Food-execellent-everything was superb Get some!!!

I saw a review further down that said the Buta Nabe wasn't all that great, and I have to agree. Essentially it looked like 4 or 5 pieces of bacon cooked softly in a broth with a lot of cabbage and a little broccoli rabe. Tasty enough, but not exactly what I was expecting for "Steamed Pork Rib and Vegetables Served with Original Soup Base in Hot Pot" It wasn't terrible, but it wasn't outstanding either. Fortunately, I somehow managed to skip the wait. Apparently 1:15 PM on a Sunday is a nice sweet spot or I'm just that lucky.

I'm not crazy about crispy skin pig which seems to be all that everyone talks about when reviewing Pig and Khao. I didn't come very hungry and just ordered garlic rice and a side of longanisa sausage for brunch which are both staples when it comes to Filipino food. Both were great except I literally poured a small dish full of oil from my rice, which was really unappetizing! Other dishes I've tried include the sizzling corn beef hash and Khao Soi (red curry). Not bad but nothing worth remembering. I still rank Maharlika over this place! Though it might be a tiebreaker between their playlists. Alternative rock/oldies vs. Old school hip hop- hard to choose!

Very nice experience!!! Excellent food(timballo warm octopus salad,gnocchi and pizza served with their homemade spicy oil...A MUST) service attentive and a very pleasant atmosphere. Nice outdoor seating as well.,Missing the Italian classic apperitifs and digestifs(Campari grappa limoncello amaro etc)Maybe in the future.
Great food, great service by Erin. Very attentive and friendly. Food was hot, tasty and well presented.

Great restaurant, its always nice to see the cuisine of nz and au elevated to a classier state. The foie was incredible but then when is it not and the parsnip soup had a nice touch of curry. For mains the pork belly and pickled daikon dish was superb! The miso is so subtle yet transforming. And for dessert look no further than the hokey pokey ice cream, a true kiwi classic that is hard to find in the states.

Really nice brunch venue in the Village. Busy as hell though, so be prepared to wait. The food was a mix of good old traditional brunch fare but also some nice innovations. If you can be bothered to line up - it's worth it.

Not sure why this place has such good reviews. I live right across the street so I really wanted Yuca to live up to the hype, but it totally disappointed. Really overpriced and spoiled tasting food. I got the yuca burger and my friend got the mushroom quesadillas. I'm the kind of person who finishes my plate pretty much every time I go out to eat and I literally couldn't keep going it was so bad. My friend ate 1/4 quesadillas. Really a disappointment.

Khao Kang is a recently opened Thai restaurant. Â Esarn!! Â Authentic. Â Home-cooked. Â All dishes are kept hot on a steam table. Â Everything I got was delicious. Â No complaints here. Choice of 3 items will only set you back $7.50! Â Seriously. Â  Special thanks to Rich W (Yelp Dad) for recommending this place. Â Loved it!

Food here does not disappoint. Squash soup was well presented with toasted pumpkin seeds and a yummy drizzle-flourish. For main course I had the appetizer size seared diver scallops with a light curry sauce and chopped vegetables--delicious. Appetizer size with the soup was an ample lunch. My lunch mates had the smoked trout (a hit) and the chicken salad (excellent and hearty). Elegant decor, clean, and excellent service (except for a minor snafu with our reservation--otherwise perfect.) Bring your foodie friends and enjoy!

I had their Calamari - which in my opinion (I absolutely love calamari) was just OK, nothing special and it didn't really stand out. It actually was quite bland... my friend also mentions that it tastes like it was cooked from being frozen, not fresh. It was not crispy or chewy like it should be - I was disappointed. The sauce it came with wasn't that great either. I'd give this a 2/5 stars calamari, definitely could've been much better! I had two shared entrees: their seafood paella and another rice dish in which I cannot remember what it is called and can't find it on their online menu, either unfortunately. The paella was GREAT - loved it. Came with shrimp, octopus and mussels, very good- definitely a winner. The other rice dish was also really good. It came with a yellow sauce and the texture of the dish was creamy and soft. I also had a pitcher of their Sangria and boy, do they serve some strong Sangria. I had some trouble finishing it, but of course, good alcohol should never go to waste! Pretty cool atmosphere too with the wooden sticks lining the walls of the downstairs dining area and the awesome attic lights hanging low from the ceiling. Noise level was quite high, but I didn't mind! An extra star for big portions!

Went here for a friends birthday and this place was amazing! the atmosphere is great, a little clustrophobic at times while moving about the place but you dont feel it while seated and dining. The live band and the cigar roller is a plus. The food is too die for! The Cevichi, Pinchos, Tostones, and the Paella are a must here! We had dinner hear a week ago and I am still thinking about the amazing food!

Weeknight dinner. Researched and found Â this place in my quest to continue my Filipino restaurant obsession. This place doesn't seem to have a quick table turnover so my group of 6 settled for outside seating. Apps: Chicharon bulaklak and Lumpiang Shanghai were just straight up NO's for me. Had to tell my friend who wanted to try lumpia for the 1st time that this wasn't how it normally tastes. Bad start...really bad start if the lumpia isn't right. Main Meal: YOU RAN OUT OF BBQ PORK? EXCUSE ME? Blasphemy. Kare Kare, Bistek, Pancit and Lechon kawali were just mehhh. Just not that memorable. Dessert: Leche Flan. No. Service was sub-par. Disappointing overall. Go to Woodside, Queens for CHEAPER and BETTER authentic Filipino food!

Having tried Pies n Thighs in Billysburg, I believe Peaches' Hot House has THE best fried chicken in Brooklyn! If you like HEAT and you're daring, go for the EXTRA hot chicken. Â For the mild at heart, stick to the regular and mild and you still wont be disappointed. This bird is cooked to a tender crisp and NEVER dry. Next best spot is Yard Bird in South Beach Miami minus the heat. So stay local and go to Peaches! You'll thank me later Sidebar: it's ALWAYS crowded because its THAT good. If service dips, its b/c wait staff is stretched (so be EASY) but food remains consistent for past two years. Happy Hours are M-F from 12-7pm. Three down and you should be quite nice. Anymore, be sure to CALL a cab!

This place has a location in LGA which is TERRIBLE....or maybe it was just terrible because I got the artichoke pizza which was just white sauce on bread? Super nasty. So I don't know if it was terrible because of the location or not, so I won't base my rating on that occasion. But at this location, I got margherita pizza and it was fantastic!!!!! It was late at night, and the place was packed, but things moved along quickly enough. Delish!

Just discovered this restaurant recently and I'm really glad I did. It's a small place and the service is pretty good. Staff is welcoming and attentive. The food is delicious! The smoked salmon with goat cheese, avocado, and red onions is to die for! I also had the delicious creamy tomato soup. The only downside is that they only accept cash but they have an ATM so that makes up for it.

place is waaaay too crowded and the wait is too long. the food is good, but not for a 2 hour wait. - chicken liver toast: good, not spectacular - special of the day: fried balls of some kind of veggie: good - gnudi: not as good as i had hoped. i don't know what exactly the filling was, some kind of strong cheese. it was good, very rich, but a bit too heavy. all my friends loved it though. - roasted quail: so-so, discovered that i don't like to eat quail unless they debone it. it was so dark i couldn't tell if i was eating bone or not, and too much bone, not enough meat. the flavor itself was fine. - pig cheek: fantastic, so tender, like pulled pork, but more tender and juicy, definitely the best dish -banofee pie: take that back, this was definitely the best dish. banana, toffee-caramel like filling, with marshmellow flavored cool whip. fantastic for $8

Great place! Â Excellent food, service and prices and a cool, friendly, funky atmosphere. Â The grilled tilapia, steak and mashed potatoes were delicious and the chicken alfredo looked really yummy. Â Love that you can get a nice glass of wine for under $10! Â I would recommend and will be going back.
The value here is crazy. How crazy, you ask? Crazier than dressing up in a clown suit and hitting someone with a dildo. That crazy.

Usually if I walk into a restaurant and see skinny jeans, Â artfully disheveled hair and distressed furniture I immediately leave. Everything was that tiresome combination of weird ingredients and quirky / minimal plate presentation. But the staff was friendly and down to earth and food here is so good, I've Â been thinking about it for weeks. The hamburger was perfectly cooked. The bun fluffy and fresh. I don't usually like lamb, but the lamb stew was delicious. The banana cream pie was just ok, but the CheesecakeÂ and Warm Apple CakeÂ were very good.

Despite getting lost twice en route, I'm glad we stuck with our original plan to visit Buttermilk Channel. Â  Everything I could ask for in a restaurant: Â delicious food; fantastic and charismatic service; great dÃ©cor and ambience. Â Finding it was like a Godsend. Our waitstaff was kind and very helpful. Â He brought us nuts and bacon when they found out about our plight to find the restaurant, and he helped us find our way back to the subway to get home. Talk about service! You must have the buttermilk fried chicken with cheddar waffles. Â It may go against everything I believe in terms of healthy eating, but it was so worth it. Â The chicken feels more like it is baked; it does not have the same greasy and heavy feeling that fried chicken usually has. And while some of you are thinking "cheddar waffles?", let me assure you the cheddar gives the waffle a nice, sharp bite. Benton's Ham Wrapped Trout was almost as good. Â  I don't think I've ever had grits before; they were a nice touch to the meaty, flavourful fish. Dessert was my favorite part of the meal. Â While my wife won the main course pickin', my dessert choice buried her's. Â I don't care how stuffed you are, order Doug's Pecan Pie Sundae. Â It is exactly as it sounds: pecan pie and ice cream served in a parfait glass like a real sundae. Â The pecan pie is nice and sweet, and when mixed with the ice cream, it is such a nice finish to the meal. Â  The chocolate chunk bread pudding was a very nice dessert, just no pecan pie sundae. Â Salted chocolate butterscotch is a nice contrast to the sweet chocolate. The decor is quite nice and the atmosphere has a class vibe to it. Â There's just something about it that makes you feel very cool. Â  If you're looking for a nice place to take a date, take that person here.

This place is 2 of 5 stars for the following reasons: - Food was good, not amazing = -1 star - Supposed to open at 11:30am as the website, signs, and even security guard at the building said. Â They didn't open til 12pm. Â Kept people waiting. Â In NY, Â you should know better than waste someone's busy, precious time = Â -1 star - For a Japanese place that considers themselves premium, instead of nice chopsticks, they use cheap throwaway wooden ones that gave me a splinter and cut my lip. Â Hard to enjoy my meal when my lip was killing me = - 1 star
Fantastic attentive service. Authentic gravy Â fresh fish. Excellent dining experience. Highly recommend!

Really loved this place. It's a smaller, dark, candle lit place with a really nice staff. Moderately priced. Calamari was amazing, I was actually pleasantly surprised by how spicy the sauce was. I ordered the Sicilian shells with sausage which was great, but couldn't keep my fork out of my friends special of the day, a whole lobster with linguini, so good! The only thing that could have been better was dessert, Bread pudding was alright, nothing to write home about. Overall I'd return

I think this place may have been way too overhyped. I took a trip up to NYC once and decided to see what the hype was all about. I don't know if it's because I think all fries taste the same, but the fries at Pomme Frites were just, OK. They did taste a little different, but for the price I'd say the overall experience was okay.

Came here with a friend for brunch and ended up getting a very meaty brunch indeed, although that is partly my fault for picking two meat dishes to split. Gotta say, there were some highlights and ... lowlights. Service -- okay. Nice enough? They took a little longer than I like. Kitchen mixed up our order. They came out to apologize. I ordered a diet pepsi and although I asked for clarification, I still suspect that it was a regular pepsi... Food -- Also okay. Hanger steak + Eggs -- Great flavor, but we ordered the steak medium or medium rare (can't remember) but it came out well done. No pink in the meat. Kind of a bummer, because if it had been cooked to our preferences this would have been the highlight. Biscuits -- flaky, and fine. I tend to like mine with a little more flavor... Sausage + Gravy -- also fine. cheese grits -- MMMM. Eggs in general -- just eggs. and so on. I don't know. Nothing stood out, sadly, but I also didn't hate my meal. I guess in my mind this place is the definition of "A-OK."
My wife is gluten-free and I am not, but I am not a big fan of Italian food. Nevertheless, Bistango has become one of our favorite restaurants.

Such a quaint spot. Nice large windows and quiet enough for good conversations. The kale salad and small bites are great! Â Beef tartar was really good. Great quality. Mixed drinks are refreshing. Will go back. It's a quintessential west village spot!
I love their pizza...especially with pepperoni! Â  I just wish I didn't have to wait on line...but it is worth it!

OMG!!! okay so i'm obsessed with their flat noodle with beef!! omg!! love it!!! it's a bit tangy and if you add the hot oil, it makes it oh the better!! love it love it!! Usually when you go to other chinese noodle places, the noodle and beef comes in a plain beef broth, but this place has it all figured out!!! trust me...go try it...

Came here around 9pm on a Friday night with Â a few friends and was seated immediately outside . Service is great , extremely friendly and attentive with a great ambiance . We had 2lb mussels in white cream sauce , not the best sauce by a long shot but still 2 lb of mussels and fries for 20 bucks aint bad . The roasted chicken was a little bland but I have to say the high light for me was Carbonnades Flammandes - Sirloin tips and Leffe Brown stew for 19 usd . On a cold night this would be a winner . I will be back .

Hands down one of the best burgers I have EVER had! Was in town for work and in search for a burger. A quick search on yelp I found them and saw they were closing in 30mins and my hotel was a 10 min walk away! I got there with 20 mins left and luckily they were fulfilling some to-go orders and what I like to think as the "eye" I shot to the host they sat me. I grabbed the menu and didnt know what in the world to get, this and that organic this, bison this and I didnt want them to be mad I came in so late so I just ordered the first thing that popped out... The "Supreme"! Whoa was that things good, nice sized organic (everything is organic here) 83/17 beef patty blanketed by a slice of colby jack cheese, country bacon, 3 huge Bare Burger onion rings smothered in the special amazeballs sauce all on a soft brioche bun. So good. Since my meal was to be reimbursed I order a side of fries, deliciously crispy and a 16oz of Ommegang beer. Not much else to say except I cant wait to go back to NY just to eat here again.

Hoofed my way over to Minca yesterday right after work. There was no wait, which I loved, sat right at the bar area watching all the magic happening in the kitchen area. It smells good in there. I got the Miso Ramen and my friend got Wahoo ramen...both topped with chicken as opposed to the pork. I really enjoyed slurping up my big unladylike bowl of ramen, among all the guys sitting there I somehow got the biggest portion. This is a good spot to hit pre-bar and I'll be back when the weather turns colder again. P.S. : Don't worry, those wild vegetables they warn you about on the menu are quite tame and delicious.
Fonda is a perfect spot to brunch/dinner. Great place to take that special someone knowing that you cant go wrong with place. Staff is great, food is absolutely amazing and in whole, Â a great vibe.

One of the various beer gardens in Williamsburg, I gave it serious points for the diverse clientele it attracts. From frat boys just graduated from Georgetown to hipster fab, to families (with actual babies)....great to see such a great mix of people. The Jenga and board games are a delight. The fireplace is a classy touch perfect for the winter. The expansive outdoor seating is a boon for spring/summer/fall. The drinks are quite affordable at $6 for a pretty nice place in prime Williamsburg real estate. They also allow you to reserve tables for large gatherings which is super cool if you want to have a birthday or celebration planned here. Bartender service is fast, no hassles, and on point. Theres a lot of other places to go in the hood but you can't go wrong with having a Kolsch here. Also their kale salad is ON POINT. I will be back.

I love Uva! Boyfriend and I came here for wine and appetizers twice in the past couple of weeks. The wine selection is AMAZING - I feel weird saying I want to try them all ;). Â I'm addicted to the bruschetta, but don't overlook the olives, they're hiding in the appetizer section. Finish off the meal with the meat antipasto for a great post work night. The service at Uva is so welcoming, a great mix of attentive and knowing when to back off, and the decor is very romantic. Definitely a great date place - leave kids at home (for all of us). I'd definitely recommend Uva.

Worst service I've ever experienced in NYC. Went there for a birthday dinner. Server was very rude from beginning to end. However the server was not just rude to us I did see him being just as rude to another table nearby. The food was decent. Everyone ordered a little bit of everything. Nothing really stood out except their squid ink pasta and avocado truffle oil salad. There are tons of other average cozy Italian restaurants in that neighborhood so will not be returning.
Since I love french fries, and I love cheese curds, I love Pommes frites. Â They serve poutine, and this is what I ate. It was delicious!

All day this past Saturday, I had a craving for galbi (Korean short rib), so, after debating the merits of going into the city and coming down on the side of laziness, my husband and I Â walked from Clinton Hill to Prospect Park to try out Kimchi Grill's new storefront. I'm a fan of their truck (it parks near my workplace once a week), but I've got to say, the brick and mortar experience was disappointing. I ordered the kimchi bowl with short rib, expecting the meat to be tasty and tender and just a little bit fatty. Instead, my bowl came with meat so overcooked it appeared black. (I actually took a photo, thinking I could include it here to show I'm not exaggerating.) The short rib was tough, dry, and totally unsatisfying. Their other menu options may be better, but I was so bummed with my dish that I won't be coming back to try them.

Cheeky Sandwiches is the best reason to ride Yo! Bus from Boston! We were starving on New Years morning, waiting in line to ride back north. Cheeky Sandwiches is about two blocks away from Yo! Bus's (nearly unmarked) pick-up and drop-off location. I ran over for two sandwiches, some beignets, coffee, and jasmine ginger ale. I nearly missed the bus, but it would have been worth it! We got a braised beef sandwich, and a fried chicken biscuit and hot damn! These are classy-ass sandwiches. Expertly prepared (if a little slow), and the perfect size. When I'm in PDX, sure I like to pig out at Pine State Biscuits and then spend the rest of the day in bed, but these sandwiches were sized appropriately enough that despite their richness, we didn't feel gross afterward. The gentleman behind the counter was very sweet and patient with me, despite my hungover hurry. Also, great price considering it's NYC.

Went here for my birthday dinner. Walking in you can just smell the goodness. We had a mix of breakfast and dinner. You must try to chicken and waffles. I definitely want to back for brunch. Must visit!

On the recommendation of the concierge at the Surrey (she said it was a favorite of the staff--how can you go wrong?) I marched my 21 yr old son through the rain for a casual dinner. Â The place was busy, but had a table for two (reservations only for tables of six or more). Â The staff there are friendly, helpful. Â Service is spot on, despite busy night on a rainy Sunday. Food was excellent, chosen from a menu that tries to be authentic and yet accommodate the American palate. Â My only criticism is that tables for two are smacked against a wall and the place is LOUD. Â Aside from that, I will come back each visit because there is still much to try on that wonderful menu! Â Loved it!

Love this place. My family is Cantonese, and in looking for good, inexpensive places to eat in NYC, we ended up eating here twice during our visit. The roast meats are excellent, especially the duck. Also good are the wonton noodle options (or any of the noodles). A meal of 2 rice & roast meat dishes, 2 wonton noodle and roast meat dishes, and 1 plate of steamed greens came to about $22. Incredible. To top it off, the wait staff is cheerful and friendly. We noticed that a lot of the Asians who come here don't tip after their meals... despite this expectation, the wait staff was still really accommodating to the Asian customers (including us, and we left them a grateful tip). (Note: On their menu and in many guide books this place is called Big Wong King, but the sign out front just says Big Wong.)

The pizza was so delicious at Patzeria Perfect Pizza. I am so glad my good friend Bobbi Billard introduced me to it. When we walked in to the shop- it was a very small New York style room, than coming from Montana I was not used to. It was so busy and packed but i loved every minute of it! It felt like I was in the episode of Seinfeld- like the soup nazi, The guy who took our order wasn't too nice until we tipped him ;) lol and it was like a line up- Â but the pizza was sooooooooooo good and it was a great New York experience! xoxo Jenna

Went here for "date night" with the wife. We arrived early, about 6:30 and the place was already packed. We had to wait for about 20 minutes - but the food was worth it. While waiting, my wife and I discussed the decor - which we found to be completely bewildering - it didn't really match the style of the menu at all. The wife thought it looked like a diner that was trying to look fancy. It was vaguely colonial with a few modern hanging lamps near the window. There was a strange mix of music playing - Ramones? Really? I won't soon forget the experience of being in the bathroom, which looks like one you'd find at a seaside condo, and listening to "My Bloody Valentine." It was so busy that the waiter seemed to be more than a bit harried. He was really nice, though. Â The beer selection is good. I had the Southhampton Double White - which is fantastic. The wife had some o.k. wine. The drinks were delivered with popcorn popped in bacon fat. I'm not big on this bacon trend - but this stuff was like crack. I liked my wife's dishes the best, she had the shrimp with watermelon. This was easily the best dish of the night. The scallops with carrot puree was also excellent - the puree was amazing. I had the steak wrapped in lettuce leaves - also good. Â I found the tacos with pork belly to be too fatty - but what did I expect? (the place is called Salt & Fat, right?) We had the ice creams and sorbet for dessert. Incredible. The thai iced tea ice cream was delicious and the cucumber sorbet was a perfect contrast to the dishes I'd had earlier. If you're looking for ambiance and perfect service go elsewhere. if you're looking for great food that rivals that of the best restaurants in Manhattan, check this place out.

Overall: 3.5 stars and trending upwards. Any establishment is better than the $%^& Uno's Pizzeria that sat at this location prior. The Smith, Â is a fun place. It reminds me of a Schiller's Liquor Bar or Pastis with its subway tiles and old-school bistro feel. The photo booth downstairs is great to cram into with three others after several rounds, and the barber chair by the bathrooms is good for several minutes of inebriated amusement. (Great, spacious bathrooms too...for once). The beer selection is great as is the food and the pricing. Beer-battered string beans let you inch towards those suggested daily vegetable and beer targets at the same time. Brilliant! I've been twice, and eaten only once. This place is fun, and I think it has potential that it'll realize after a few months spent on working out its menu/service kinks.

The food at Hunters is very good. The staff is variable- some are friendly and helpful, others blasÃ© and too cool for school. What bothers me is that Hunters does not clear the snow in front of their restaurant on an extremely busy stretch of Smith Street. Snow turns to ice, and today several people in front of me fell on the slippery surface this morning. I tried my best not to follow their suit but failed and fell. I called Hunters and left a voicemail alerting them of the issue, and let them know that I fell. I never received a return call or an apology. Tonight the ice is gone, but I am still annoyed about their carelessness and lack of apology.

Holy smokes - 1,500 reviews? Seemed just like yesterday I penned this turd of a review for my first ever skate with Yelp (yelp.com/biz/jyoti-bihanâ€¦). Now I sit at this virtual vista overlooking 1,499 reviews in the rear view mirror and living 2,798 miles away from that first diatribe. Time flies. Anyhoo, I'm not here to talk about years of previous musings... I want to rap about one of my favorite haunts in Nolita, Mother's Ruin. I'm a sucker for these types of establishments; dark interior, good vibes from regulars, indie music that'll get you snapping, and killer handmade cocktails. I'll succumb to the hush-hush, Draconian rules of indulgence every now and then, hammered down by the likes of Milk & Honey and PDT (forbidden from talking to strangers of the opposite sex, voices contained to the pitch of their choosing, et al.), but at the heart of my enjoyment are places like Mother's Ruin. They don't take themselves too seriously, but deliver a product that's right up there with Manhattan's best. Feel free to be yourself without getting the stink eye from bartenders because you don't make your own bitters and care little about who Dave Arnold is. Just pop in, have a great time, and enjoy spending your hard earned money however you'd like. At the end of the day, that's what a bar is supposed to be, right? Good on ya, Mother's Ruin!
Excellent Italian food. Â Great service. Friendly and clean. Â The food is grea.
I love Korean food. Now I don't have to travel far. It's three houses away from where I live. Great service, atmosphere and food.
OMG this place is amazing.

They now have hot sauce, but you have to ask for it. Â It is great. Â Not sure why they don't have several bottles of it out at the sauce counter like the other sauces though, a bit weird. Â Also, they should have a more classic KC BBQ sauce IMO.

Came here last night for my bf birthday dinner. Our reservations were at 6:30 and based on the reviews I was expecting it to be somewhat crowded. It was not at all. We were seated right away. The food was GREAT! We had the special which was bay sea scallops...they were okay. Nothing special. We also got the spicy duck meatballs which were amazing!!! For our entree we got the special Rib eye to share that came with two sides-- potato gnocchi and bitter greens. Everything was delicious! For dessert was the sticky toffee pudding which was also fantastic. The only reason I didn't give 5 stars was for the atmosphere. There was no music playing and anything above a whisper would have been like yelling and your neighbors could hear everything. Way too quiet and stuffy for me. A little background music would have made a huge difference!!!
this place is really good

I'm not sure if I can write an honest review of Sunny and Annie's because I've never been here when I wasn't completely hammered - but I'm going to try anyway... The pho #1 is the sandwich to get. I'm sure the others are good too, but none are this unique. It tastes just like a bowl of ph! OK, maybe not exactly, but it's damn close. It comes with a healthy amount of sriracha so if you're sensitive to heat make sure to ask them to take it easy with it. I love my spicy food and the standard amount is enough to melt my lips off, which I rather enjoy, but you might not.

I must send an update you guys way because the food here is AWESOME. Â  It's been over a year since I talked about my beloved $5 stoop brunch, but since then, I have been back several times and had the breakfast. Â The grits.....holy mother of grits, are soooo good. Â Full of texture and not to mention, your choice of several toppings to add, thus building your own specialty order of grits. Â I got mine with salsa verde and a smidge of freshly cracked black pepper. Â I didn't even make it to work, that joint was down the hatch!! I've also purchased their freshly baked breads. Â For the second year in a row, I've purchased bread here to make fresh stuffing for Thanksgiving (get that Stove Top shit outta here). Â Can't remember what I got last year, but this year, I took the girl's recommendation of pork maple mesquite sourdough. Â I sliced into it when I got home....with little pieces of pork hidden inside. Â Damn, I can't wait to taste that stuffing. Â My car still smells like bread today. Â  Â  They now have pizza, available after 1:30pm, so I once again have to stop by and try that. Â Everybody is real friendly and down to earth. Â Please stop by if you have a chance, please.

There have been so many reviews on this restaurant, but I really wanted to put my two cents in! Â I love this place. Â The food is great, the space is cozy and the service is impeccable! The hot potato chips with blue cheese fondue is to die for. So scrumptious! Â Warning: Â Do not order unless you are prepared to eat the entire bowl and then some...
overall a very good neighborhood restaurant but while some dishes were very good others were nothing to be excited about

Viva xiaolongbao!!!! Raaaaaaaaah!!!! A truly mind-blowing experience. The best of NY!! Â Don't leave NY without trying crab meat soup dumpling or else you will be missed out on eye-opening culinary experience....I'm dead serious! Food:A++ Service:B-/C+ Atmosphere:C You are not an official New Yorker until you've tried Joe's Shanghai!

I loved the food here. Â It was the perfect blend of Korean food and high class dinning. Â We came for anniversary and they treated us like rock stars. Â Champagne glasses, personalized menus and a special dessert plate. Â What a wonderful experience.
One of it's kind pizza... The wait in line was worth and only after we left I realized I had over 5 slices of pizza. Try the plain , simple margarita pizza to enjoy the real taste

Great place to stop after an afternoon of museum hopping. Â Two coffees and two cakes came to $30 and I didn't mind at all. Â The cakes were luscious - the chocolate deep with a tinge of apricot, the fruit tart light and sweet and with a little crumble on top. Â Everything came with home made whipped cream (including my coffee!) and it was nice to sit and relax for a few minutes before tackling the Neue Gallerie. Â We'll be back.

Excellent selection of bourbons with a menu that compliments the whiskey specialty. Â The craft cocktails are also excellent. Â Service is attentive and well informed. Â We made the trip out from Manhattan to try this restaurant and we were not disappointed.

Living around the corner from this place, and considering the limited food options in this neighborhood so far, I desperately wanted to love this place. Â I went in on a weekday nite, my suitor friend and i were the only ones at the takeout counter, and yet somehow everyone who entered after us ordered, paid, and got served before us. The dirty look we got from behind the counter was on par with looks we typically get due to our interracial pairing. Not only did it take practically 40 min (and normally i would've never waited, but was so hungry couldn't bring myself to leave the promise of food), but we were clearly charged a different price than others. Â Despite the bad impression, I still couldn't wait to try the food. The fried chicken was overly breaded and soft, and the mac and cheese lukewarm and bland. Â I had to add salt, pepper, and my own seasonings to it when i got home. Â So disappointed, and will never ever go back to this place of inequality.

The food and cocktails here are incredible. I'm a big fan of the oysters at happy hour, there is a touch of jalepeno added to their mignonette sauce which is lovely. The goat neck curry is one of my favorite dishes in the neighborhood. There is really nothing here that i've had that isn't impressive.

First, shout out to the bartender who let me and my friend charge our phones at the bar while we ate dinner. Being a tourist in this city puts a drain on your battery, amiright? Delicious food, as everyone has mentioned. The bread basket was a great starter. I order the spaghetti with basil - so simple, but yet...SO GOOD. My friend had the duck ravioli which was great as well! We didn't get any appetizers/dessert - just a quick bite to eat and off to Broadway!

Very friendly lady behind the counter, she explained the specials to me (it was my first experience with Korean food), and the meal was great! Â Perfect place for a quick lunch. If Â I lived in the area I would certainly come back. Â I'm amazed I found the place but noticed a small sign outside the building.

Best pizza in south park slope. Â I don't know if it's because clearly all the Italians go here or that it is also Italian run, but ya it is pretty damn good. Â I get the baby size (ie personal pizza) margherita.

This place delivers when they feel like it. They deliver to our building everyday and I called on a Friday night to place an order and the lady told me too far for delivery. When I told her that they deliver here all the time she hung up on me. When I called back she didn't answer the phone. Never again will I order. Well not like they'd delivery anyway. The food isn't that good.
Yumo. Â Best place to get lunch in this hood.

If you're in NY, don't order those pizza by the slices that you see walking down the street because those are not fresh and will not do any justice to NY pizza. Do try Lombari's, wow awesome taste. We tried the clam pizza or clam pie they call it for $26, it can feed 2-4 people depending how much you eat. It is sauceless. Their salad was ok and I so wanted to try their regular pizza with tomato sauce that I saw on the table next to us. They ordered a simple pie with basil leaves and I loved the chucky mozerella slightly burnt by the oven. I will definitely go back there to try that!

So happy to have good Korean food in the neighborhood. Most of my friends either love or hate Korean food, so it can be hard to get a group together for bbq in K-Town, but this place, which is fusion and has a more extensive menu, is perfect for a big group of friends. The service is AWESOME, the drinks and the food are great, and the ambiance is perfect. My girlfriend and I had a snowy Christmas lunch there yesterday and didn't want to leave because it was so cozy and romantic inside. The place was full (but not loud), yet the staff were incredibly friendly and in no rush to get us out of there. We will definitely be back.

Really... How long do I have to wait? First came here at 6 20 pm and they said the waiting time was 45 minutes... Fine, let's wait. After 45 min they said it was 20 min more. After 30 min they said it was 20 min more. Are you kidding me????? I had enough, you guys better not trust those people, for a B rated place!
What a find! Excellent food, staff was great, service was fast and no-nonsense. Love this place! Will come back often.

best heroes, but.... they got the BEST SICILIAN SLICE IN AMERICA. even though brooklyn is a separate country (because its so far and always has traffic) i will wait in 2 hours of traffic both ways in order to have this pizza. i would kill a man for this pizza. the regular slice isn't even worth trying. i go with a friend or gf, get a half tray of 12 slices, get a hero, doesnt matter which one because theyre all bangin, 2 pepsis and im set. no im not fat, im a small white male. there is nothing in america that compares to L&B. if anyone tells you theres better pizza they're liars or crack heads. no offense to crack heads reading this worldwide, i acknowledge and appreciate that you took the time to read this.

I went back today and bought 3 orders of pork and chives fried dumplings ($3) to share with my bf. I went around 3pm and there was no line and hence no wait. The dumplings were yummy and I didn't have a hair in my food this time so I gave this experience 5 stars.

Last Saturday was absolutely gorgeous, so my roomie and I made plans to walk down to the seaport for lunch. A lot of the restaurants down there are pretty bad (for example, Red...I don't want to talk about it...) We recently discovered some of the side streets though--like Front Street--and we were shocked by what we found: a surprising number of small shops/bars/restaurants...like little hidden gems in a dump of tourist traps and overpriced frozen margaritas. Anyway, I had actually heard about Cowgirl Seahorse a few months ago, so I suggested we try it. It's literally underneath the Brooklyn Bridge, and the only way you know it's there is because of a big pink seahorse hanging outside. The place was about half full with some families and a couple groups of girls at the bar having brunch. I immediately fell in love with the decor--very cute and kitschy . We're both vegans, so there wasn't a whole lot we could eat--but not a problem. Roomie ordered black bean vegetable tacos and I got the veggie burger with sweet potato fries. We loved both. The tacos were hot and fresh--but I think my burger won. It wasn't frozen crap--it looked like it was made in-house. It was also huge and came with lots of lettuce, tomatoes, onions and pickles. The rest of the menu looked great--I saw lots of eggs and mac and cheese come out of the kitchen. The ribs are supposed to be good too. The drink menu was also verrry tempting, but we both had a long day of day-drinking ahead of us so we opted out. When all was said and done, we each had more than enough food for less than $11 each. Above-average comfort food in a great atmosphere. Definitely worth a visit if you're in the area.
Best date spot in the hood. Â Love the skirt steak, I get it every time. Â Good wine selection -- also to note: wine half off before seven. Â Deserts pretty kickin too.
Good Sicilian pizza, but not sure what all the fuss is about.

My husband and I went for lunch and shared a "flemmy" combo, which comes with a salad and a drink. This is more than enough food to share (especially for lunch). Our bill was under $12. The food was excellent and service was great. We'll definitely be back.
The food may be good but delivery takes FOREVER. If you're hungry do not bother.
This place is legit. Â Worth the wait. Â I prefer the gyro platter. Â Make sure you drown it in the white sauce. Â The hot sauce will set your world on fire so be careful.

I came here for breakfast for the first time today. They always have humorous signs outside on the chalk board! I love the idea they want to portray but the food is not so great for the price. I had a cup of coffee with coconut milk and a vegetarian breakfast wrap with sweet potato. I do not eat beef and had asked if the chili is made with meat (staff was unsure). I thought this was extremely disappointing. The wrap was a crepe (why didn't they say that?) CRACK COFFEE later that day with a friend was nice and worth a try ($3.50 for 12 oz.) For the $14 bill, no thank you. I would rather go visit JUICE PRESS any day.

Amazing! Gluten free was simple for them to do and they really knew what they were doing giving my celiac nervousness a break. The service was amazing and the food was to die for. The garden patio is worth the wait - absolutely adorable.

So, there's not much of a view. Putting that out there now. But, the roof is so cute and well decorated. Picnic tables and tented areas. Also, plenty of space in the bar area. We came for July 4th so not sure what the orig food menu would taste like. We had a lot of meat and sausages. And one of the best BBQ chicken I've had.

Have been here twice in the past couple of weeks and both times were very enjoyable. The staff is very friendly and is a great place to catch a game, as I was there a few weeks ago with a couple of friends to catch the Jets on MNF. They have an extensive beer selection that is quite good and the items on the menu are tasty and come in nice portion sizes. I found myself there again this past week to meet up with my sister and brother-in-law before they headed to the Beacon to catch a show. We split the calamari in a sweet chili sauce with toasted almonds, which was very tasty. We also had the mac n cheese bites with roasted red pepper ketchup (very good) and had one of their Oktoberfest specials (bratwurst sliders) which were also very good. The bartenders are attentive and friendly, while the atmosphere is great, whether meeting friends for a few cocktails or to watch a game. It is a nice respite in Midtown Manhattan, where establishments can either be bland or tourist traps. I will definitely be back.

I'm really not going to say anything new in this review. Â It's all been covered - this place is FABULOUS. Â Your best bet is likely late on a weekday because it's teeeeny tiny. Â On the flip side, the advantage of this is that Chef Mehta is incredibly hands on with every diner. Â Both himself & his wife (I think?) bring out each dish and describe exactly what's in it, which flavors are at work, etc. Â He's not only a great chef but it's clear he has an incredible passion for food and his work and wants to share that with everyone who visits. Â Another plus - we had a group of 5, and Chef Mehta served us an extra portion or two with each dish so that it would be easier to share. I honestly don't think I can pick a favorite. Â The only dish we did not absolutely love was the chicken flatbread (it's not listed on the menu online so maybe it's new?). Â My dining companions were stuffed (and drunk - $25 bottles, EVERY bottle) but I beggggged them to let me get the warm truffle almond strawberries...and every single one of them thanked me afterwards. Â Ok, so that one may have been crowned the unanimous favorite! Go to Graffiti today. Â Thank me tomorrow.

Wonderful restaurant! The bar area is reminiscent of an old NYC tavern-great menu options and a phenomenal wine list. When friends and I go, we always sit by the bar because we love talking to the bartenders about what to drink. They're knowledgeable and will suggest the best concoction to go with your mood and your food. The other part of the restaurant is an unforgettable experience-impeccable service, fresh ingredients, and overall a creative menu that uses the best food of the season. I have never been disappointed. Gramercy Tavern should be reserved for special occasions because you need to take it all in to truly enjoy it. If it were up to me, I'd have a special occasion at least twice a month just so I have an excuse to visit this timeless and classy New York Institution.

If you're reading about Chef's Table at Brooklyn Fare on Yelp you're either wishing you get the opportunity to eat here, reminiscing about your amazing meal, or just heard about the place and want to know what the all the fuss is about. For me personally, this was the best meal of my life. Â It was also the best experience I've ever had at a restaurant. Â Yes I'm not a rich man and it cost me $700+ for 2 people but with that combination plus the fact it was for a special occasion made it worth it. I can sit here and give you the whole megillah but as others have also mentioned I can't do it any justice. Â I will list the highlights. - Such an intimate setting. Â Just 18 guests who are all as eager as you sitting around a semicircle table watching the kitchen prepare all the meals. Â It's always amazing seeing professionals do their thing whether its artists or athletes. Â This time it was chefs. - The chef Cesar is such a humble, cool guy. Â The whole staff for that matter. Â I chatted with most of them throughout the night. Â They really made the night feel special. - 20+ tasting course of just amazing fresh seafood. Â I am not a foodie and I don't pretend to be so I can't tell you what they did to make everything so excellent but they served dishes I've never seen before. Â For me that was the best, tasting things I never have before and might never taste again. - Desert and wine were just as amazing. I anxiously awaited eating here for the entire 6 weeks since I was able to make a reservation. Â The night exceeded expectations and then some. Â If you can do it make the call and hopefully you can get a reservation.
Perhaps the best French fires in NYC. I will definitely be going back - huge plus that they are open until 4am!!!!! The fries are literally addictive. Cute staff too!!!!
Awesome beef soup noodle. It's really hand made. I saw the dumplings being made there and they were awesome too. But if you are looking for a fancy place to have Chinese, don't go there!!!!

Mouth on Fire! Had the falafel for the first time, under estimated the hot sauce. Mouth on fire! Â Finished it with my stomach full. Â Worth the price ($2.50) Â Be careful if you never tried the hot sauce, it's super hot! Â A little goes a long way. Â Mouth is still on fire, but will return again when my mouth is healed. Â When I went there was no line, went on a monday at 3pm.

If you're coming with a group, get the seafood tower. The smoked mussels are delicious. The house infused gin and tonic is beautifully balanced and they even leave a big slice of grapefruit for you. Not to mention, Brooklyn Gin is my favorite.

Overall, the dishes we got were very good. On that alone, I would go back. I'm not sure about the vibe of the place though. We stopped by on a Friday night, expecting a wait. We were told there were two seats at the bar, which we said were OK. But the hostess said we had another option - to check out their other restaurant down the street. She talked it up to the point that it kind of made us feel unwelcomed when we said we wanted to stay. I know she was doing her job, but to go to that part of the neighborhood, you probably aren't just winging it on a Friday night. You are there for a reason. When we ordered, we got three dishes, but we were told most couples get four. It felt pushy, since as a grown up, I know I can order more food if I'm hungry. I did end up getting another and was not disappointed. The food is very good, but it also didn't wow me as many people write on yelp. Â  What I wasn't crazy about was that the place really wasn't all that special. The interior isn't much to look at, and the music was the same Pandora channel you hear everywhere else in Williamsburg. The clipboard holding hostesses at the door reminded me what I don't miss about NYC, and that there are many places I love more in Williamsburg.

I came here last week for a Kamayan Night and it was awesome! They were running a little late with our table, which was a tad lame (especially because they don't have a liquor license at the moment), but our server was super nice and apologetic. Lovely, lovely, lovely. 5 of us went here last week and had a great time. the atmosphere is very zen and calming, even though the space is not huge. We ordered a ton of things from the menu, these were the highlights: - maguro natto - fermented beans, if you can get past the smell and add lot of wasabi, this was good - hirami ponzu - best fluke sashimi ive ever had and the presentation was great - grilled japanese eggplants - yumazing and very different tasting - pork belly - i dont eat pork, but this was DELICIOUS and my friends were kind enought to let me try and then share:) - dessert - the special was amazing and now am desperately seeking japanese crackers, the server told us that you can only get them in japan - sake - amazing selection fo sake, we did splurge and get a 200 dollar bottle, totally worth it. overall, a great meal, service was spotty but when we had his attention, he was great. cannot wait to go again.

I came to Cafe Ghia for brunch at about 12:30 on a rainy Sunday. Although we were quoted a wait of 20 minutes, we were only standing for five minutes or less when the host seated us at the bar. After much deliberation, I ended up ordering the Ranchero Benedict for $13 and added Braised Bacon on it for an extra $2 at the waitress's suggestion. As the menu describes, this meal consisted of poached eggs on corn griddle cakes with avocado and huancaina sauce, served with a side of greens. The bacon was added under the egg, above the bread, and I HIGHLY recommend adding the bacon. This was no thin, store-bought bacon. This was centimeter-thick, hearty bacon. The sauce was really flavorful, the presentation was nice, I was nicely full afterwards, overall a great brunch item. My friend ordered the Biscuits and Mushroom Gravy with a side of green beans for $10, which he then topped with two fried eggs. He was sick and congested so he couldn't taste much, but from the bite I had, I thought it was good. Overall a nice meal. The waitress was really helpful and nice, the atmosphere was pleasant, and the $3 bottomless coffee was good.

Dinner at Osteria Morini was overall enjoyable with some surprising combinations and well-prepared pasta dishes. The veal tongue crostini starter was excellent and the most memorable part of the meal. Â The veal tongue was creamy and savory and paired well with the sweet red onion marmalata. Â The crostini had a crisp, grilled texture but still had a soft, warm bite. Â There was a perfect amount of spread for the crostini provided. We sampled four different pasta dishes: the Spallina (double ravioli with squacquerone cheese, rabbit, and porcini), the risotto with caramelized onions, taleggio, pear, and red wine sugo, the Torcia (squid ink pasta with shrimp and seppia ragu), and the pappardelle. Â Of the three, I especially enjoyed the Spallina; the ravioli had a perfect amount of bite, the filling was delicious, and the fried sage leaves that garnished the dish were excellent. Â The risotto had an interesting combination of savory and sweet from the pear. Â The texture of the ravioli was good but not the best I've had. Â The Torcia came with breadcrumbs which added good texture, and the pasta was nicely cooked al-dente, but overall, the dish was not particularly memorable. Â The pappardelle was also cooked well but the sauce was a bit too creamy for me. For dessert, we tried the panna cotta, which was served with walnuts, pomegranate seeds, apple, and mint. Â The panna cotta had a great, smooth consistency, and the pomegranate tasted very fresh. Â We also sampled 3 sorbets: the fig-saba, pear, and blood-orange mimosa. Â The texture of sorbets were inconsistent; the fig-saba was nice and smooth, but the rest were a bit icy. Â The pear sorbet had the best flavor. With our meals, we had the lavender-eldeberry soda and ginger soda. Â The lavender-elderberry soda was very good and well balanced-it didn't taste too floral, but it was a bit hard to detect the lavender. Â The ginger soda was unmemorable with a strong, upfront taste and diluted finish. Service was friendly and efficient, and sitting at the bar was comfortable.

Momofuku Ssam Bar offers a great take on Korean-American fusion. Typically when I think of Korean-fusion items like bulgogi burritos come to mind so it was nice to have a different style for a change. Momofuku Ssam Bar is Â a small restaurant so I highly encourage calling ahead of time for reservations as this place does get packed. I came here with a group of 7 for lunch to try the bo ssam as well as to indulge on their other items which included: Hurricane Island Oysters (3/5) - The oysters taste like any plain oysters you could get at the store. Having been to Seattle the oysters here weren't all that impressive. Spicy Pork Sausage and Rice Cakes (5/5) - This was a nice take on one of my favorite Korean dishes (dduk bok ki). The soft chewiness along with the delicious flavor of the pork sausages all complimented each other nicely. The small spice of the dish only further enhanced the taste. I definitely recommend this dish. Pork Buns (4/5) - The pork buns were tasty but I think it's only because of the sauce. The pork itself lacked big flavor but the tenderness of the meat really made the dish. Bo Ssam (3.5/5) - This thing is not for the faint of heart, it's HUGE! After our first couple of dishes most of us were feeling pretty content in the stomach, then they slapped this monster on the table. The bo ssam is eaten in the same fashion as Korean bbq. You get a wrapper (lettuce) and stuff it with the super tender bo ssam meat (pig) and accompany that with many different types of sauces... try them all! If I could make one adjustment to this dish I would also add rice which I think would help the overall texture/flavor. Overall: Momofuku Ssam Bar wasn't anything exceptional, but it Â was good and I definitely recommend everyone try the bo ssam at least once.

Daaaaaamnn. This place is oozing with love and family and togetherness and good ass food. Friend and I came here on a Sunday, and we knew we were in for trouble. First of all, there are numerous houses of worship in the area (and I mean at least 3 within a 2 block radius), so I knew everyone would be scrambling to find food after their respective religious services. We left around 11am (really early for the two of us) and set out on our quest for comfort food and a really unhealthy breakfast. When we finally reached the Amy Ruth's, we had to wait 5-10 minutes to be seated. It could've been worse, and it has one of those waiting booths outside. Anyway. We were greeted with amazingly amazing service. You really feel good there. The woman who served us called us "honey" and "baby", and the atmosphere upstairs was just plain cozy. Drinks and food came so quickly, AND the kool-aid of the day was cherry - SCORE. Onto the food: first thing we tried was the cornbread. Delicious. And I don't even like corn bread usually. I got the chicken and waffles (reverend Al Sharpton) and oh. my. goodness, I instantly began comparing it to KFC, Popeye's, Pies&Thighs in Williamsburg - none compare to Amy Ruth's delicious fried chicken. The meat was juicy and the skin was amazingly crispy. The waffles were fat and fluffy, yet crispy in all the right places. I ate some of my waffle with the maple syrup that was provided, which was very unique syrup. It's much more liquidy than the typical IHOP or Aunt Jemima syrup. It tastes just as rich as other syrups, but it's somehow more..buttery and a bit momentarily bitter? It's hard to explain, but it's different. It was good syrup, but their waffle held on its own enough for me to eat it sans-syrup. My friend loved her strawberry waffle drenched in the syrup, though. Overall, delicious meal. And the Kool-Aid was delicious too. Trust me, Kool-Aid can be ruined. Looking at the menu at first, I was like "is this going to be worth the money?" However, I was starving because I hadn't eaten since the afternoon of the day before, and I could not finish my waffles. When I left, I was so full I thought I would die for 15 minutes. My friend must have been annoyed when I kept asking her, "is my life ending?" I go through similar feelings with IHOP, except after recovering from IHOP I vow that I'll never eat there again. With Amy Ruth's I *know* I'm eating there again. Bottom line: service and atmosphere as good as its amazing quality food. A great bang for your buck because you will NOT leave hungry. Worth the wait.

After seeing The Spotted Pig in Food & Wine, GQ and Conde Nast Traveler I decided to go there last night. The Spotted Pig does not take reservations. I called around 6:30 pm to see how long the wait was and a gentleman advised it was an hour to an hour and a half. I called again around 7:15 pm and the wait was down to around 45 minutes. When I got to The Spotted Pig and gave the host my name I was told to expect to wait for 45 minutes. My girlfriend and I were seated within 20 minutes. I think we got lucky. The service was very friendly. I am not sure if I like the decor of ceramic and other pig items or not, but I do love how casual and unpretentious The Spotted Pig is. I agree with other yelpers that the tables are packed pretty tight and the low stools do not help out my bad back much. The Spotted Pig Bitter Ale was real ale pulled and served at cellar temperature. The Deviled Eggs had a great taste and texture. The flavors were perfectly balanced in the Seared Squid with Cilantro Butter & Fennel. This is one of the best squid dishes I've had in a while. When asked for a personal recommendation our waitress boasted that the Chargrilled Burger with Roquefort Cheese & Shoestrings was one of the best burgers in The City. The meat in the burger was packed very lightly, which allowed for maximum moisture in it. Tossing the shoestring fries with fresh rosemary put The Spotted Pig's fries on my 'best fries' radar. Â  I am not sure if the burger is one of the best in the city but it was pretty damn good. Crispy Pork Belly with Bean PurÃ©e also came with swiss (maybe rainbow?) chard. The pork belly was perfectly seasoned and I barely needed a knife to cut in it to it. Summer Pudding with Creme Fraiche was the first time I've seen a cold pudding served in the United States and did not disappoint. I think the pudding was even made in a proper pudding basin. I would advise against ordering this dish unless you really love tart summer berries. I enjoyed it very much. Probably the best part of the meal was my coffee that was served in a French press. Like the squid it was one of the best coffees I've had recently. The coffee was on par with European coffee.

KenScale: 8.5/10 The Spotted Pig is probably the most well-known gastropub in NYC, period. Getting a reservation at this restaurant helmed by chef April Bloomfield is notoriously difficult at this restaurant that doesn't take reservations (last time I checked in, I was given a wait time of two hours, so I didn't get nearby since then knowing that, although I would be more than happy to wait, my friend(s) who join me would probably lose patience). Lately, I had a opportunity to go on a pretty early dinner, so I decided to use that opportunity to finally check this restaurant out. The dinner time starts at 5:30 p.m., and I walked in for some beer and wrote my name down at 5 p.m. I was not impressed with the other restaurant led by chef Bloomfield in the city (The Breslin) other than their famed lamb burger, so I tried to manage my expectations, Fortunately, there were truly outstanding winners coming out from the kitchen, and the best dish wasn't the famed burger. I started out with a bunch of bar snacks. Deviled egg was tasty and so were the greasy devils on horseback wrapped in bacon. My winner, though, was the chicken liver toast that was absolutely delicious with great balance of flavor. While everyone is talking about the burger here and all the tables I've seen ordered at least one (more on the burger later), my favorite dish of the night was the simple-looking yet truly outstanding sheep's milk ricotta gnudi with brown butter and crispy sage. The ricotta inside was just pure decadence and I can't stop thinking about that dish with soft texture with bold flavor. Yes, the burger was also great, but I think it could've tasted even better without the roquefort cheese whose strong flavor somewhat undermined the juicy texture of the meat. While I understand where the hype is coming from, I wouldn't call this burger the best thing that happened to NYC. I was beyond stuffed by the time I finished the burger, but wanted to try at least one dessert. I'm so glad I did because the seasonal tart that came with bananas was one of the best tarts I've had in a while, with awesome flavor working very well with the silky smooth bananas without being overly sweet. Your best bet to get seated at The Spotted Pig is to show up 1-2 minutes before 5 p.m., write your name down and hope for the best when the dinner service starts at 5:30 p.m. There is just no other way! I liked the charming, divey gastropub feel of the restaurant with tons of pig figures on the wall. The restaurant has a full bar with nicely prepared classic cocktails (my favorite was Manhattan), so either go with some cocktails or brews to wash down the food. The Spotted Pig certainly lived up to its expectations, and I'll certainly come back next time I want to have a casual pub food night with bold flavor and skillful execution. When you go there, though, be prepared to walk on your way home.

Dined on a Monday evening with reservations through OpenTable. I was the last minute addition to an original party of 3, and they allowed me to join. The ambiance was very pleasant--very cozy and homey. Everything about the place gave you a very traditional Italian home feel from the decor to the dishes on the table. The staff was very friendly and our waiter was very knowledgeable. A couple guys in our party asked for wine recommendations and he let us taste a couple nice whites before we settled (unfortunately, I wasn't paying enough attention to remember the name... sorry!) The pasta dishes are small but shareable. All of them were cooked at a perfect Al Dente... very important in distinguishing an okay pasta from an excellent pasta. We ended up ordering a good 6 dishes/entrees to split amongst 4 people. Here were the dishes we ordered: Pastas... Tagliatelle - the only thing that stuck out to me on this one was the pasta noodle. It was a wide noodle and seemed like it was freshly cut. Besides that the sauce was okay. It tasted like a decent meat/marinara sauce. Garganelli - this was another delicious one. The perfect creaminess and blend of flavors from the prosciutto and truffle butter. We enjoyed this one! The daily dinner special: A burnt Cappalletti with wild boar (not sure if this is what it was, but it looked like it). This was absolutely delicious! Very light yet had a good mix of complex flavors from the gaminess boar and the subtle smokey burnt note from the pasta. We were impressed by the Al Dente-ness of the Cappalletti. We tried both Polentas: Funghi and Salsiccia. Unanimously FUNGHI blew us all away... wow! It was packed with flavor from the wild mushrooms and cheese . Naturally most kinds of shrooms, and especially wild ones, greatly influence the flavor with its umami components. Ricotta is another very flavorful cheese, so those two merry well. The polenta itself was a perfect creaminess consistency. It was very fine and disintegrated quickly once in the mouth. The Salsiccia was just okay... it tasted like a lasagna polenta. Again, great consistency and texture on that one as well. Entrees... Braciola - pork chops are usually tough to make well... for that exact reason... it comes out too tough and dry. This one was not! However, despite the nice moist pork chop, I felt the flavor was not all there. The cut was pretty thick so the meat was not a well infused with flavor to the center. It was decent, but not the best pork chop I've ever had. The dinner finished off with a bang! The waiter must've really loved us because he surprised us with a delicious complimentary dessert, the Budino di Noci. MY gosh it was really good! The creamy walnut custard was very indulgent but yet not too sweet with nice and crunchy burnt sugar top. After that we all got cute little teacups of hot chocolate. This is not like any other hot chocolate you can imagine. It was like drinking out of a chocolate fondue pot. I was overwhelmed by the richness of the small 2 oz teacup of a nice blend of dark and milk chocolate with some cream mixed in, topped with a fresh whipped cream. It was really good, especially if you love chocolate. If not a big fan of super sweet things (like myself), I'd recommend even sharing with someone you're comfortable sharing with. One of two sips does it! Lastly, the check... everything above for 4 people came out to $58 a pop with tax and tip. Somewhat pricey, but with wine and dessert it was pretty good. Overall, good job to Chef White! The fantastic pasta tasted very home-made and not overly creamy. In my opinion, this is what real pasta should be. The dining experience and food was impeccable and we enjoyed our time at Osteria Morini. 4 stars... I recommend it!

Neat atmosphere. A hidden gem of the city. If you're in the mood for British food, this is a great pick. The fish and chips are amazing. Service was decent, but a little slow. However, the ambiance is very unique. I'd recommend coming here with a group as opposed to a date.

I came here with 5 other friends during the soft opening period. Â I have to say it wasn't very good for a few different reasons. Â Maybe they will work out the kinks but until they do.... 1.) We waited at the bar for a table for over 1.5 hours and they have no real snacks to order other then the regular menu items which aren't really appetizers. 2.)
