I like Roti Canai with the curry chicken dipping sauce. It got me hook on it. As for the food, the Pad Thai & Pineapple Fried Rice was a bit spicy for my taste.

Been here three times and it's great every time. And no, it's not the Martini's talking- which by the way are uh-mazing. Cute spot to go for a date or with a bunch of friends. The peruvian corn, chicken empanadas, each and every paella, quinoa and ceviche (which changes all the time) are definitely worth trying. Someone every time I visit there is a birthday being celebrated. However, the desserts didn't impress me much. Only reason to be stingy on the last star. But I would go back. And back again.

Extremely nice service, very friendly. We wanted to get the best on the menu and we were provided with very honest answers, food was awesome and the price was quite reasonable. Loved it and will be back again

Best sushi I had in usa period . Their quality is incomparable to even some great sushi restaurants in NYC. Hands down. The best!!! ( I'm Japanese and I'm impressed) all sushi chief were Japanese . anything they make is up to japanese standard and this is not your typical sushi restaurant in NYC at all. If you like Americanized sushi (California roll, spicy tuna, boston rolls etc) they don't serve that kind of sushi ....

Always love coming here. Great beer, amazing food, fantastic atmosphere. I really like their beer selection with their porterhouse brewing company selection and other different beers than the rest. Would love to write more but I should go back to work because i spent so much here on their fantastic beer and food. :)

It's places like Prosperity Dumpling that make me proud to be a New Yorker. Â They serve some of the best fried pork dumplings I've had anywhere, and definitely at the lowest price. Â I live in Dumbo, but I walk over the Manhattan Bridge several times a week just to grab dinner here. Â I get an order of 5 perfectly seasoned fried pork dumplings and a sesame pancake for a grand total of $1.75. Â Best deal in town!
Loved, loved, loved the breakfast pizza. The ambience is also really nice. But the highlight was the server, Arlene--she will make your dining experience fun and memorable.

When it is late night and you are in the West Village this is pretty much your best option for a late night meal. Yes, I skipped the Halal Guys at 53rd & 6th avenue. Yes, I skipped Papaya Dog. Yes, I skipped my bagged lunch in my fridge. But what I probably should have skipped was this place. The customer service is friendly. The tables were dirty even on a Monday at around 2am. I guess that is to be expected. Â  What was even dirtier was the hot sauce dispenser bottle. I ordered 2 Falafels at $3 each. The presentation was good but the taste left much to be desired. The salad stuffing was fresh. The pita bread was fresh. Â  The filling was fresh. But the taste just wasn't there. Partially because there really wasn't an option of sauce(s) other than the yogurt sauce already included in the Falafel. I'd come back to give it another try maybe in the daytime.

SO delicious, I really really liked Frankies 457. We got there early enough so we didn't have to wait (which I heard could be bad). We started off with the Antipasto which was incredible. Â Cheese and meat...obviously good, but on top of that there were sauteed mushrooms and roasted cauliflower. Â This has officially put me on a mission to replicate the cauliflower at home, it was THAT good! For an entree I got House-made Cavatelli with Faiccos Hot Sausage & Browned Sage Butter and my boyfriend got the Meatballs with Pine Nuts & Raisins. Â  The Cavatelli was so delicious, the sauce was tasty and the sausage was just the right amount of spicy. Â The Meatballs were also quite impressive. Â I'm a tough critic when it comes to red sauce, and this was to notch. The ambiance is pretty old school Italian and the service was great. I highly recommend Frankies!

Incredible pizza... Â crispy crust/delicious toppings and pretty much the friendliest service imaginable. Â We ordered four pizzas to take out and they gave us free bottles of soda and free drinks while we waited. Â We felt like family.

Just a normal weeknight with the kiddos in NYC, looking for interesting food finds. Been past this place many times without noticing it, so excited to try it for the first time given the Yelp reviews. Service - 5 stars for the hostess, 2 stars for our waiter. Â 3.5 stars downgraded to 3 given that having a good waiter is more important. Â I didn't have a reservation and they were full with other people coming in. Â We were going to be turned away but then, the hostess understood that we were with kids and going to be wandering the cold NYC streets looking for an alternative. Â She said "wait" and made some changes to the seating to accommodate us - what? accommodate average people with young kids, nice! Â HOWEVER, as to our waiter. Â It took him forever to get to our table, forgot to bring my wine, never refilled our waters despite repeated requests, had our hand up to inform him of our missing wine and then subsequently other problems with our food - we had our hand up for about 10 minutes before he came around each time,including the bill. Â In a small restaurant - seriously? Â  Pro - Fun decor - skeletons and interesting photos. Pro - they divided up our kids' meals into 2 without us asking. Â NICE! BUT Food - this had so much potential: - shrimp appetizer, yummy and spicy but our toasts on top were burnt beyond recognition with bits of black burnt bread inside the shrimp bowl. Â Was that a bit of pepper I ate or a crumb of burnt bread? - Mediocre guac - creative and amazing sauces & toppings on the chicken mole and the sole fish, but both meat/fish pieces were overcooked and dry. Â My fish would have been 4-5 stars if not overcooked. Â  - great lamb, mushrooms and mashed, but the garlic tasted salty and like that garlic out of the jars you find in a supermarket (and I love garlic, how can I write something bad about garlic). Â  Unfortunately, this bad garlic was on everything in this lamb dish, I had to scrape it off. Â I've never scraped garlic off in my entire life and am still having nightmares about it. Increase wait staff, don't overcook the food and prepare your own garlic - I'll come back if you do!

Spumoni! I have a cousin that cannot pronounce it LOL and it's the only thing she likes. Go figure. I've only come here for ice cream; simply the best around. It gets packed here during the summer with a lot of kids and cars are triple parked out front. But hey, that's how you know it's good. Plus the boys that scoop your ice cream are so cute!

Pluses: very nice atmosphere and friendly, attentive service. The Hemingway cocktail is pretty good. Presentation of the food was excellent, I loved how the ropa vieja looked in a bowl made of plantains on a bed of yucca. Unfortunately, the flavors were just okay. Perfectly okay but nothing special and a little on the bland side. My plate was also a starch overload: rice, plantains and yucca with the meat--the dish could have used something green. Maybe this is just how Cuban food is but I think it could be something more than this.

Good food, good location, great people watching. The burgers here are delicious, as is the tuna. I can do without the long wait and stuck up servers, though. I will say that they have a surprisingly good selection of Chardonnay!

Came here twice on our trip because the food was so good! When you get there write your name on the list at the door. Line might be a little long but it moves quickly and is worth the wait!!!! Staff is super friendly.

cafe gitane is currently my favourite spot in the city. i've been to both locations, and although i enjoyed the beautiful tall windows, sunlit room of the west side location, this little cafe near prince st. station is my fave. it's super crowded and squishy, and if you happen by on a cold day, your glasses will fog up for a whole few minutes being so warm and cozy inside. me and my girlfriend stopped in after shopping at the nearby market for some really late brunch, and i love that it was still crowded. i ordered a watermelon juice that day- it was delicious. both baked egg dishes are simply delightful. the smoked salmon sandwich is also very good...... and although i loved the idea of lemon and avocado on toast, i didn't quite find it as special. i can't wait to try the cucumber juice the next time i come in!

I really dont understand the amazing reviews about this place...food was just plain bad, drinks not well mixed, guacamole has no taste, the staff is friendly but for a saturday night at 11 in nyc the place was empty. Really disappointed and wouldnt go back there.
Lovely. BYOB. Wine, muscles and desert here is a must. Â  Perfect place for a date night.

This is my Sunday Brunch spot, and will be till the end of time! If you get here early on a sat/sun, just after 11am there is no wait. On Sunday's after 1pm the wait is about 1hr. But, well worth it. The wait staff is wonderful! So accomodating and spirited. The pancakes are bites of fluffy, heaven, with the pumpkin seed butter and maple syrup. They really give the pancakes at Clinton St, a run for their money! HEY! Martha, try these!! The coffee is perfecto, each time. And, the mini treats they leave on your table are just fabulous, The best carrot cake, chocolate crossiant. Other yummy things, include the chicken sandwich, the bullseye eggs and your everyday breakfast plate. Everything is made to perfection and presented handsomely. ahh, i love this place! The decor is so homey, (not shabby chic) but, so country with a bit of an NY twist. And, their featured art is always magnetic.

I am not sure what all the great reviews are all about. Â Food is fine but nothing spectacular and the service is awful! Â At $32 or so per entree, plus wine, small plates and dessert it is not inexpensive, at least $60 per person. Â There are far better places for less or equal money. Â Our service was horrible, at best. Â  Our waiter recommended several dishes, each of which they were out of. Â He had to return several times before he found something on the menu they had not run out of and this was a Saturday night of Memorial Day weekend at 6 pm, very early in the evening still. Â  If you order wine, be sure it is red and they leave the bottle at your table, otherwise you may be sitting there all night for a refill. Â We had to practically beg to have our glasses refilled and when we requested he leave the bottle at/near the table, he said he couldn't. Â We were catching a movie and did not have time, we ended up leaving a little less than half the wine at the restaurant not because we couldn't finish but because they would not let us. Â  Then to add insult to injury, we were charged for each dish that was ordered but they were out of. Â We needed our bill adjusted twice! Â I would pass on this place. Â  The only redeeming quality is the garden out back, even then, not worth it!

What an excellent surprise - Wild Edibles had the most delicious lobster roll and mussels I've ever tasted. Â  The place itself is small, with just a few short tables and a bar surrounding a seafood stand selling fresh fish and crustaceans - as a result, it's very fishy-smelling. Â Not fancy in the least, with a friendly staff and pretty extensive menu for how small the place is. Â I didn't have crazy expectations coming in, especially due to the signage outside being pretty lame. All that being said, the food was absolutely awesome. Â My boyfriend and I were bingeing on New Orleans-Style mussels, white wine and old bay spiced french fries, and additionally split the freshest, crispiest, lightest lobster roll I've ever had. Â 5 stars hands-down if the review were for food alone. Murray Hill has a lack of secret fantastic places like this, so I'm really glad I've found it. Â Also, I'll have a great recommendation besides Luke's when friends are looking for good lobster rolls!

i went there for brunch, didn't even realize it was locanda verde until i saw down. Â  ambiance is great, very laid back feel to it and not uptight at all. Â staff was attentive. you must must get the sheep's milk ricotta... I would come eat here just for that. Â It is by far the best appetizer I've had to date and tingles every sense in your mouth. Â it's that good. i don't remember what i got but my friend got the polenta waffle and it was cooked to perfection. definitely coming back again...
Very good food. Chicken with eggplant was excellent and I'm not a huge fan of eggplant!

Delicious and affordable two words most people Â hunting down a restaurant want to hear. From the rice rolls to the soup dumplings everything's a treat.Tthere's something there for everyone not excluding those with less adventurous Â eating habits or food allergies. I would highly recommend this restaurant to those looking for an authentic Hong kong dining experience.

Ippudo is amazing. My friends and I went here for dinner because one of my friends just bacame a ramen chef here. It was delicious. We had some chicken wings for an appetizer. Then one of the waiters brought out the cucumber appetizers that was probably one of the most delicious recipes that I have had that consisted of cucumbers. For the entree, my friends and I all got different types of ramen. The special wasabi ramen was probably one of the best. It wasn't too spicy, but it was just plain good. You can tell that their noodles are fresh and the broth that they use is just so incredible. My friend that works there said that all of their broths are cooked over 24 hour periods and that the recipes for the broth and the noodles are both closely guarded secrets that only two people know. Anytime there is a secret recipe, it is reason enough to go. This time it just happened to be tasty and delicious!

Peaches Hothouse is now one of my top choices for fried chicken in the city, and I'm not sure whether it's a good or a bad thing that it's also in my neighbourhood. For $13, three pieces of fried chicken with toast, pickles, and a side? That's a much better deal than some of the other hipster places in the city. The fried chicken comes in three levels of spice: regular, hot, and extra hot. We opted for the hot and my friend went for the extra hot. It does feel like the spices can be a bit inconsistent, but the fried chicken is consistently crispy and tasty without being greasy. So far, we've had the mac and cheese, butter beans, collard greens, and bacon-potato salad as sides -- my favourite is by far the bacon-potato salad, which is both creamy and delicious, definitely cooling and tasty for this summer's heat. Even though Peaches Hothouse is in a remote location and a fair walk away from the subway, this place gets stupidly packed on the weekends and evenings -- it can be a good hour wait, but it's completely worth it. Thankfully, the bar is full of creative cocktails and will let you wait at the door with one of them.
Cute For dates. Outdoor seats And Thursday has Live music. Meats trump pasta for value.
Great service but my chicken was a bit dry. The mushroom and basil waffles were heavenly! The bacon flavor was just ok. Bathrooms were gross- there was a water leak in one.

Stumbled upon this place one Saturday afternoon walking around the Flatiron. Â The sign for $1 oysters and a $12 burger caught my eye so we went in. Â Unfortunately we were tricked because this deal was not valid until 4 or 5. Â Why put the sign out if you aren't offering the deal? Â To trick people, that's why! Â Jerks. Â Oh well, the menu looked interesting so we figured we would try it anyway. Â Playing right into their trap. Â Thankfully, the food was good or else I would have left pissed off. Â  We started with the Duck Confit Salad which was very good. Â Kind of a small serving for $15 but they do give a whole leg of duck which was unexpected. Â There's a good balance of sweet and savory with the blood orange and truffle soy vinaigrette. Â For entree's I got the Bulgogi hot stone bowl and fiance got the Spicy Pork Tacos. Â We shared them and were both very happy with our order. Â I don't eat rice bowls often so I don't have much to compare to but I thought this one was very tasty. Â The ribeye was tender and sweet due to the marinade. Â This played nicely with the spicy sauce they give you on the side. Â The best part about this dish was that the rice lining the hot bowl crisped up adding a great texture to pair with the rest of the soft rice and the crunchy veggies. Â I couldn't stop eating it even though I was stuffed. Â  The restaurant space is pretty large and it looked like they have a private sushi room in the back so this place could be good for parties or segregated dining. Â Who doesn't love segregation, am I right?! Â  The food did take a while to come out on a slow afternoon which is why I'm downgrading a star. Â That and the trickery they pulled. Â Besides that, I would probably come back and get that hot stone bowl again and hopefully enjoy some happy hour oysters.
Solid negroni. Ask for the special vermooth. And these guys fight crimes. It's a daring menu- but I'm game for trying.
We loved it. Chicken pie is a must, shrimp and Cajun grits was delicious. Nice atmosphere, the owner is a gem.
Unreal Lunch Today! I have to say this is the coolest place I have been to on the west side. UNREAL bowl of fries. Go there HIGHLY recommended!!

Burger was good, but for one burger and a coke, 17 bucks is way too expensive. Especially when all you get is the burger. Fries and such are extra. I would expect that to be at or under 10 bucks for a burger as small as this.

3.5/5 to be accurate; been here 5 times, not because I adore it but because the preferred destinations nearby were packed or closed Food (3.5/5) being a soba-ya, the quality of the soba is good yet the soup lack of flavour and the dishes are salty in general, with overly greased tempura; this being said, however, certain sets are not bad for a quick lunch: bara chirashi, Kamo nanban w/ soba, nabeyaki for winter salvage; goma tofu and kaisou salad make fair starters, and milk tofu to finish. Lastly and sincerely, a 4.5/5 does apply to the decently done Unaju Ambience (4/5) well decorated, including the bathrooms Service (4/5) friendly

My new neighborhood favorite - great food and great service at a reasonable price. Â The waitstaff and the bartender were friendly and helpful. Â Porchetta and fluke were extremely tasty, and the pie was very good too.

This place just recently flagged on my food radar. Â And it probably would never have if I weren't playing around with my mobile Yelp app. How I discovered it? Is irrelevant. Â What matters is I did, with my short review. Restaurant. Â In itself, average in appearance. Â Nothing really stands out, and nothing offends you. Â Well, maybe except the feeling of knowing it will be a quick meal with no reason for sticking around. Â  The two friends I came with all ordered the Two8Two burger. Â This burger of theirs is simply finger lickin good. Â Perfectly cooked, well seasoned on its own, but with Poblano peppers on top, drizzled with their special Two8Two sauce...you momentarily lose your breath as your taste buds climax...repeatedly! It was that good. Hands down, I consider this as one of the best burgers I've had in my past. But at $9 a pop, you get a small patty on a small bun with zero sides. My friend not caring about his cholesterol levels had to order seconds. Personally speaking, I would rather pay $10-$13 dollars for a larger patty and a side of fries or salad. Â This should work out in their profit margins. Other highlights are their Spicy Bloody Mary with bacon salt covering the glass rim. Â Be careful with the heat and your throat locking up. Â Otherwise, it's a damn good drink. I'm pretty certain that anyone who tries his or her burger will leave very satisfied.
Brooklyn's #1!!!! Square slices like no other. Spumoni's great, too! (Part of Best NY PIzza: The Haiku Series)

Always had great service and the food is great. Happy hour is good considering the area. Bartenders are always so friendly and they know how to make a real drink. They also gave me comp vip tickets to the comedy show although I never got to make it to the show. I really enjoy this place even when its packed. Its especially the best when not packed though since it is rather narrow.
Excellent burgers, cool vibe. Â Definitely a recommended stop.

Came here for a soup dumpling fix that was satisfied after 5 (x8) orders of the reg. pork. Shanghai lomein was flavored nicely but felt that they skimped out on the meat. The walnut shrimp (Fried Jumbo Shrimp with Wonderful Fruit Sauce) wasnt so wonderful. Probably cause Ive had better. The mapo tofu was good but a bit too salty. Place was clean, smells outside though. Free candy at the counter. Yay!

Champs, I love you. If you were a person instead of a place, I'd like to think we'd be best friends. I've been more times than I can count and I've never had a bad meal. My absolute favorite is the macro bowl, which is a yummy blend of hummus, brown rice, black beans, tofu, steamed kale and sauerkraut. I'm also addicted to the tempeh buffalo wings and the chicken biscuit. Honestly, the only thing I don't like about this place is how long it takes me to decide what to order because EVERY FREAKING THING sounds AMAZING. For honesty's sake I will say my friend once got the tuna melt and we weren't blown away. I've had chickpea based vegan tuna that I am obsessed with (Terri in Chelsea does it especially well), but this soy based tuna definitely was not my favorite. Another issue is that sometimes service, although nice and friendly, has been less than speedy. But this place still deserves 5 stars in my book, as it's hands down my favorite vegan place in the city.

Pizza was just okay. Service was horrible. Seating was even worse. Pizza was forgettable - not bad but definitely wasn't worth the wait on a cold evening and definitely not all that it's hyped up to be. Our waitress was not helpful, pushed us into ordering more than we needed and was unfriendly. We were seated in the dead of winter upstairs where I can only imagine they closed-off a summer roof seating area with plastic and some metal and then put heaters in there. It. was. FREEZING. I had to keep my winter coat on the entire time and would have worn my gloves if they could have been kept clean while eating.

Kinda pissed that I didn't see the alligator on the menu. Get the friend chicken beignets!!!! I'm not kidding! Â I also got the jambalaya mac and cheese I had it before but this time is was a little too salty. Collectively, my friends ordered catfish, oysters, corn with spicy mayo and parmesan cheese, a bunch of other stuff. Rainbow shots etc... Yep good times!

The dumplings were cheap but mediocre. Â The dumpling skin was too thick and the filling wasn't special. Â They don't make the fried dumplings to order so they come out room temperature. Â They were also too burnt for my liking. Â No special sauce on it either. The place itself seemed a bit dirty. Â I got a noodle soup and at the end, you dump the soup in a large plastic bin near the trash can. Â I understand the efficiency of this place but that is something that should be done in the back by an employee, not a customer.
Just paid my first visit and it lived up to the hype. Â Ordered a number one and it was pretty much perfect. Â Need to try the meat ball next time. Â It was empty at 2:30pm on a Friday.
Friggin' Seafood Heaven. 'Nuff said.
ahh..the seasoning on the rotisserie chicken is outtasight! very cheap,too!dig it!

overall foodie experience was great. friendly wait staff. arepa was mouth-watering( it had chicken & avocado). venezuelan plate 1 was good, although the pulled pork was a little on the sweet/tart side. passion fruit natural juice a must. will definitely be back!

Our family of four enjoyed our dinner overall, with two of us thinking food was pretty Â good and two of us thinking it was okay. Decor is appealing and ambiance is energetic and family-friendly. Servers are very friendly and attentive. My one criticism is that Tony's advertises that the family-style platters serve 2-3 people, so when we chose two different platters thinking it would be plenty for four of us, we were surprised to learn we'd have to order a third platter of pasta. The eggplant and veal parm platters we'd selected did not include pasta on the side. Â I thought that was lame, especially with the rather hefty price for a simple pasta side dish. Bottom line is one platter does not serve 2-3, because we needed 3 platters to serve 4.

My new favorite place. Let me start by saying that I am a stickler for attention to detail when I go to places. The atmosphere was dim and intimate, but at the same time it was a great place to have a drink with friends. Once you walked through the doors you felt like you were transported from the busy concrete world of Manhattan to an energized pub that surrounded you in wood. My girlfriend and I stopped by after running into a few places that were packed. An issue that I would later be happy about as it lead me to Church Publick. The waiter was the nicest guy I've ever met and really wanted you to have a great dinning experience. We sat at this large booth that provided a nice amount of privacy from the other patrons. The menus were a nice touch as they came in a slightly burned file and the drink menu was in a leather portfolio. For appetizer we ordered the a delicious jerky sampler. The platter contained a jerked mushroom, teriyak beef and jerked chicken. I ordered the Pan-Seared chicken with mashed potatoes and carrots (highly recommended). The chicken was juicy and delicious. My girlfriend ordered the big salad, which she couldn't finish but she enjoyed immensely. I will be back real soon.

I went to Bouley for a romantic dinner with my boyfriend. Â Of course, I was running late and everyone was very gracious in never mentioning or making a big fuss about it. I'm not a foodie but my boyfriend is. We had the tasting menu and everything was delicious. Â There isn't more I can say about it except it it delicious. Â You will be spoiled and any post-Bouley cuisine you have will not be enjoyed. I do find, however, that the service was a little omnipresent (good/bad depending on how you look at it) but not intuitive. Â If you're going to "be everywhere", shouldn't you imagine I need something if I'm staring you down? Â I didn't take anything away for that because it was that one time. Summary: Food's delicious Go to impress someone No babies

This place is great. Â The staff is friendly and the prices are low. Â They make their own tortillas and they are divine. Â I'm partial to the al pastor quesadilla, it's amazing and comes with a few pickled veggies on the side, a nice compliment. Â I've also had the burritos, they're huge and tasty. Â I'll definitely be back to try some of the other options.

Attractive setting and decor. Â Liked the lobster tacos very much and we shared the paella. Â Toloache is better than most of the local Mexican sit-down meals; the food is quite good and the drinks are well conceived. Â I like the mezcalritas which have a little extra zip compared to tequila ritas. Music is loud. Â I don't blame the restaurant for the fact that one of the customers felt the need to shout her conversation at the people who were sitting 12 inches away from her. Quirky things we noticed are that for such a nice bar, it is unfortunate that customers have a direct view of the kitchen. Â The bar has a TV that shows local Mex-TV with no volume so, you get images of news, soccer and UFC. Â UFC? Pricey but good.

The service was great and the food was amazing. Â I would definitely come back. Â I especially loved the mezza royale because you can try 13 different items but not meant for 2 people its more for 4 people.

Location, location, location. Were it not for those 3 words, this place would be rated no higher than 2 or 3 stars. I can understand how people like it for the reasonable prices, but I'd rather pay 30% more for food thats significantly better than this. Tried the macaroni with sausage, tasted like boxed macaroni with pasta sauce in a jar topped off with an extremely porky tasting sausage. Having skipped lunch I was starving at dinner, but could not get myself to finish this plate. Friend ordered the seafood linguine, looked great, except it has no flavor whatsoever. How do you get seafood to taste like nothing is beyond me. If this place was on the UWS or in midtown, it would have shut down by now. Funny how people are so easily influenced by the location of a restaurant. If you want similar prices, same ambience and 100 times better food, I suggest you check out Celeste on the UWS. If you must eat in Soho, goto Rubirosa which has hand made pasta's for only a little more.

Came here for my birthday, and it was the best surprise! Amelie is tucked away in Greenwich amidst a number of other great finds, and is cute, Â modern and trendy. It's filled with a soft red light and quirky touches (some lights are in the shape of bottles, etc), and is great for setting a romantic vibe if eating with a SO. There's also a standing area in the front which is great for larger groups. The owner is super nice and eager to share his expertise about wine. If you make it for happy hour, I recommend getting the three-wine glass sampler! He helped us pick three wines that would go with the dishes we ordered, and I feel like we learned lots about wine pairings and flavors that evening. The food was also excellent-- we ordered the steak tartare and octopus salad, which were both light and sophisticated in flavor. It wasn't incredibly filling, but this is to be expected at a french restaurant. Highly recommended for a chic and memorable experience!

I went there for my sisters birthday with 9 people. The service was amazing. The waiters were extremely nice. When we got the birthday cake, they gave everyone a free glass of champagne. The food is great - we were partial to the smaller dishes - the tuna taquitos and the empanadas were fantastic. This was a great place for a big party. Can't thank the staff enough for making it a great night.

Came here for lunch with a friend and it was great. The lunch special comes with two appetizers and an entree, and the restaurant gives off a pretty relaxing and chilled vibe for me. I ordered a spicy basil noodle with shrimp/chicken dumplings and crab cakes. The dumplings were average but I wouldn't recommend the crab cakes. They didn't taste anything like crab cakes, and they were also dry and over-fried. The noodles, however, was alright. I'm a person who likes a little kick in the food, and the noodle wasn't too spicy but was also flavorful. Would definitely come back for lunch again, it's a steal when all that food comes under $10.

Maybe texmex isn't my thing, but also flavorless pork shoulder is definitely not my thing. I needed a burrito fix and thought I'd try this place out one afternoon. It was relatively quiet, considering there were like four people seated inside. But the music was BLASTING. I am in my mid-twenties and I work at a bar, so I have no problem with loud music. But this tiny shack had their music blasting in my ears at 2:30pm and I found myself rushing to finish my food so I could leave. I got a burrito with the bbq pulled pork shoulder. Meh. It was flavorless. I couldn't tell when I was biting into a part of my burrito with meat or with rice. The only thing that had flavor in my meal was the corn and the hot sauce I was desperately pouring onto it. I suppose I'm not a huge texmex enthusiast and would just prefer straight up Mexican food, but I will not be coming back if I'm ever hungry for a burrito again. I'll go to Chipotle just a few more doors down instead.

the reason i am rating with low stars is that i had poor service and the hot wings seemed like they were marinated in catchup im sorry but they were not good if the description says hot wings then i expect spicy but other then that order the cheese cake it was amazing
Good but not great. I'll definitely go back again when I want banh but am not in the mood to travel far.

If you know how difficult it can be to locate a fresh, tasty, homemade Greek pastry, you have no more worries; welcome to Anthi's. It was the best birds nest and baklava I've ever had (and I lived in Astoria for a year). All the types of baklava you can get at delis and even upscale restaurants are never made in house; it's too difficult and too time consuming. Here the owner takes immense pride in every Greek food item that is for sale. A custurd cake called galaktoboureko is so delicious, orgasmic even. The spinach pie was excellent as well. Cash only, take out only.

What more can my review say regarding the high quality foods and service? There is simply not much more to share other than my personal preference dish- the broiled scallops. Oh my gosh these scallops are absolutely, without doubt in the world of seafood restaurant scallops, home cooked Mom meals too- the very best scallops I have eaten. Â The service was great as the wait staff is kind, knowledgeable and courteous. Â I have been to Taverna Kyclades three times in the last couple months and am trying to make this "gem" my Sunday lunch spot. Â Awesome food- hands down!

OK... Â So, came here a few weeks ago for one of our company's holiday dinners. Â It was my first visit. Â Immediately upon entering, the one thing that surprised me was how tight the interior is... Â I mean any possible space that could have a table has one. Â You are literally "up on" the people sitting next to you. Â While I didn't order the Black Label burger, the lady next to me did, and she didn't finish it all. Â I almost chimed over to ask if she was gonna finish that, because I would've only needed to move my plate over 6 inches to transfer the leftovers from her plate to mine. Â :-) Now to the food... Â As I mentioned earlier, I didn't order the Black Label burger. Â But I wish I did. Â Instead, I opted for one of the specials of the night, which was a skin-on sea bass served with a classic lemon based sauce. Â I have no complaints about the quality of what was served as it was sauteed and then pan roasted to perfection. Â However, it was missing a certain je ne sais quoi which left me wishing I ordered something more gratifying. As for the appetizer, I ordered the roasted bone marrow with baguette soldiers and shallot confit. Â While it looked quite impressive, it was actually underwhelming. Â I think the issue here was that I was expecting too much as several friends told me that I MUST order it because it was amazing. Â  Â  The one thing that was amazing, and was the highlight of my meal, was the Grand Marnier soufle. Â It was served with a creamy vanilla ice cream and the combination of flavors was fantastic. Â That is the only thing I can recommend without hesitation! As for the service, it was fairly attentive, and we were promptly seated upon arrival. Â Next time I visit I'll try the Black Label burger.

came here for lunch during Restaurant week and was really excited to try another Tom Colicchio restaurant. however, i was slightly disappointed. a friend and i shared the duck pate and the campanella pasta dish for appetizer. both were delicious. for the entree, i ordered the leg of lamb curry dish with roti. i thought it'd be an actual leg of lamb with curry sauce on it but it was literally curry that you can get from an indian restaurant. super disappointed with this one. was this supposed to be novelty? either way, it wasnt that great. the roti was good but thats about it. my friend ordered the red wine braised beef with polenta cake. it was way too salty and overall just not that impressive. we both got the donuts for dessert..they were too oily and reminded me of carnival food. i guess it is a really good price, $25 for a three course meal... i've heard dinner is much better though

So glad Yelp led me to this place! Ever since vacationing in Maine, I've been kind of obsessed with lobster rolls. I strolled into this place at a perfect time...5 pm. Why so perfect?? Well, first they have a happy hour where all their craft beers are $3. Can't beat that. Second, the place was pretty empty so I was able to quietly enjoy my roll and beer, and I did not wait in line. :) Now the roll. It was a little smaller than I expected, but it was packed full of big lobster chunks. The lobster did have a sauce, seasoning, and some butter, but everything was light and perfectly balanced. The lobster peices were completely intact, not overly beaten by mixing, and it had a nice texture to it---plump, al dente-ish, juicy, etc. I don't know a ton about lobster, but it tasted super fresh to me. I LOVED the powder seasoning over the top of the roll. I thought the price was a little spendy ($15 for lobster roll only), but since it was fresh, excellently prepared, and delicious, I can get with that price! If you go at happy hour, you can get a roll, beer, and chips for the same price as a soda combo ($18). That's a meal deal to me! Oh yes, and the staff were super friendly.

I got the Matador combo to split with a friend. The chicken was awesome, and I loved all the sides it came with. Service was very good, and the restaurant is very spacious. I'd recommend splitting the Matador between 3 people instead of 2. Definitely a great deal, and I'll come back here often!

Great Place. Great for groups, met some co-workers for after dinner drinks. They have plenty of seating and regular tables to make you more comfortable. The noise level is pretty decent, we were able to have normal conversations with each other. As for the food: I ordered the salt and pepper ribs and the Mesclun salad....... DAYYYYUUUMMM. Who would've thunk that regular salt and pepper ribs could be so tasty. Â This is hands down one of the best meals I have had at a bar!!!! We also ordered The Nutella Ricotta Calzone, which is AMAZING!!! It's enough for 2-3 people, it's warm gooey but not too sweet! Geez, I'm salivating just thinking about it! I'm a happy chick, can't wait to go back!

Excellent food and great service. All servers took extremely good care of us in a very genuine way. Would definitely recommend. Also, my wife is gluten-intolerant and they catered for it extremely well. Not only does the menu have heaps of gluten-free dishes, but they made sure every they told us each dish was gluten-free when they brought it back out. Thanks! Just a quick note - they were booked out when we went (Sat night) so recommend you call ahead.

Not bad The idea was really nifty - Gourmet grilled cheeses with a variety of different fillings. Â Unfortunately the food was a little bit of a let down after we were looking forward to a delicious piece of comfort food. Â Mine was rather small for what we paid and didn't really ooze the warm comfort feeling I expected. The service was a little on the slow side too.
It's just ok...

A great local dive bar in Williamsburg. The place has great music playing, lots of ways to entertain yourself like Buck Hunter, Darts, Pool, and lots of board games like Apples to Apples. Also, can you drink any cheaper than this? Shots of jameson for $3!!!! That is just not right. Guinness for $5 and tons of great beers for that price or less. The bar definitely is going to be packed on any weekend night, but if you can get to the back, you'll be set.

Grimaldi's is the best pizza that has ever hit these lips. There's always a line outside, but it moves quickly. I do recommend breaking up your party into smaller groups if you have a large group. The wait was much longer for our party of 6. However, it was soooo worth it. Once we were seated, the pizzas were out within about 10 minutes of ordering. Try the Brooklyn Black Cherry soda bottled right there in Brooklyn. Delicious. The fresh mozzarella, the hint of fresh basil and the fresh toppings coupled with the coal oven baked crust is what makes this pizza heavenly. Well worth the wait and we'll be back again and again. They also apparently opened a Manhattan location around 20th St that we were unaware of. Brooklyn is a bit of a trek, but I like going over there just to hang out in Brooklyn! If you are unfamiliar with the subways, make sure you take the BLUE line down (A, C). Puts you off very close to Grimaldi's.

Amazing. Â The Tom Kha Gai is to die for....one of the best soups I have ever had. Â Followed up with a Red Curry and Thai ice Tea (all included, along with an appetizer, on the lunch menu at $12.95. Delicious and a bargain to boot.) Definitely worth the trip, and another, and another!

Ever since I moved to NYC years ago, every one I know has said omggggggggggg you have to go to Calle Ocho for booooozzzy brunnch. Ugh. My friends made a reservation for a Sunday for brunch. For brunch, this is great for groups up to 10, just 2 people or a small group of 4 or 6. The space is big, so you won't feel like you're on top of other people, however it does get pretty loud once 20 something year old girls have slurped down a few unlimited sangrias and a bite of toast for breakfast. The bread basket was memorable and I devoured it. I had the Calle Ocho omlet and was impressed. The food seemed really fresh. The sangria selection was cool, too. I had never seen that many flavors and it was fun to try some different kinds. I hear you have to make reservations months in advance for brunch, but I've also heard you can do an unlimited special Sunday nights but they don't advertise it. Keep me posted.

I'm no empanada *expert* but I know that this place is delicious! Wasn't there for a full meal, so only ordered two empanadas: the Cuban, and the figs, caramel, and cheese. The service was friendly and attentive, and the decor is cute.

One word: perfection. Everything from start to finish is beautiful, fresh, perfectly seasoned and amazing. I've been here a few times and every time my meal is fantastic and leaves me wanting more. Â The marriage of flavors is a revelation and the menu changes seasonally, so you will always be tempted with something new when you return. The atmosphere is gorgeous and I love the attention to detail. Every plate and piece of flatware is different, giving it a kitschy feeling. Â  I'm not going to emote on ABC because nothing more needs to be said. Â This place is a must try, you will not be disappointed.

Eh, if it weren't for Yelp, the experience would've been pretty unmemorable. There's one menu, all day. Same prices and it's open 24/7. I had the arroz con pollo and a side of sweet plantains and my friend had the cuban sandwich and sweet potato fries. I'm specific about my sweet plantains. Years of hanging around spanish moms have made me a total plantain snob. I like them slighty browned, soft, and sweet. This wasn't good ... and the whole plantain was just sliced in half. Arroz con pollo is supposed to be chicken on the bone but this was just chopped up chicken breast ... sort of like a mini version of chicken nuggets (bleh, I dislike foods that remind me of McDonalds). The rice was .. hard. Not soft and flavorful like I like and the dish had way too much bell pepper. It was the only thing I could taste. My friend's sandwich looked good though. It was crunchy but when I tried one of his fries, it was soggy. Like really soggy. I don't like soggy fries. Oh well, I guess it really is like a diner. Diner food is usually mediocre, I don't think I'd waste money coming back here unfortunately.

best pizza EVER!!! outside of italy, of course. i come here every time i'm in new york, and then dream about it the whole time i'm not there. wish there was one in san francisco. but this is the OG. just the simple margherita pizza is to die for. *YUM*

The food I had here would easily battle for the worst meal I've had in the 6 years of living in NYC. The service was ok, nothing great, but I'm really not here about that. Â The beer and wine selection is pretty decent. But the food... oh man it's bad. I keep wanting to like you, Smith. But, it's honestly bad enough that I'm taking the time to come here and tell people about it. Â Please don't go to The Smith. My friend and i had Â had a belly ache the rest of the day and we were totally turned off food for a good two days after. Save yourselves, don't eat at The Smith.

Best arepas in the city (ok, it's Astoria, but it beats them all). Hands down. And @ prices that are ridiculous. The staff is super-friendly, too! A good friend of mine brought me here and now I'm addicted. I literally live on the other side of the city, but still manage to get here every few months. They are divine. I love the baby shark arepa, but have tasted them all and can't find a single problem with any of them. This place is a blast. I shouldn't be writing this review and should totally keep this secret secret, but...hey... it's only a couple of weeks after Christmas... :-) Amazingly recommended.

This interestingly named bar is a gem in a neighborhood that you do not expect it to be in! They open at 5pm and the kitchen opens at 6pm. Parking can be hard to find, unless you are willing to pay a meter. Â  With that being said, I had a great experience with my sister on her birthday last night at this place! We came in for a drink before our reservation at 6pm at Traif restaurant which is around the corner. The waitress was so warm and inviting, offering recommendations on their very extensive menu of alcoholic beverages. They have whiskey galour and so much more!!!! The waitress helped us make sense of it all and was so attentive. Our candle light went out due to a draft and she came over within 30 seconds with a lighter to light it back up :-) The decor was warm, hip, and intimate, great to sit and have good conversation over a drink. The music was great as well, from rhythm and blues to rap to rock. I ended up having a delicious Beer Cocktail made with lemon, champagne, beer, and bourbon that all came together beautifully, with explosions of different flavors with each sip. My sister had the Bourbon Hot chocolate which was delicious and very flavorful. The hot chocolate was creamy and rich, followed by a kick of bourbon! The complexity of each of the drinks were apparent, yet the ingredients all came together like a beautiful symphony in your mouth. The bartenders definitely know what they are doing. The cocktails are $10 each (well worth it). I will be back to try the different drinks on the menu and the food, which I hear is very good.

Another gem in Chinatown, Love their BBQ and especially the duck and roast pork. My favor dish is their wonton and beef tripes noodle soup. Â Since it is so close to my Church, we like to bring take out or eat in as often as possible. Â Keep it up Noodle Town.

Just had brunch here and it was the best brunch my boyfriend and I have ever had so far. I had the smoked ham sandwich with a side of bacon and he had the chef's breakfast. Everything was delicious! Great start before our getaway to the Poconos :)

Food is awesome! Drinks are good too. Didn't like that my date and I, had to sit so close to another couple (who spoke a little bit too loud) but the service was good and the flourless chocolate cake was mindblowing.
went for brunch. varied crowd, good food, great cocktails.

Highlights of the night: -Some of the best Italian food made outside my own kitchen. -Homemade limoncello (absolutely delicious!), and the man who shared his secret limoncello recipe with us. -Spending over two hours there, not because the service was slow (it was perfect!) but because we were having that good a time. Very accommodating to our large group, especially since we made reservations. It was a busy Saturday night there, but not unbearable. I can't wait to head back.

Steak bacon cheddar meatballs with mushroom gravy over a generous portion of chef's choice of market greens (arugula, broccoli, sauteed spinach, white beans, apples, garlic kale) for $8 - yummilicious. Risotto with prosciutto and chives - savory. Peanut butter cookie chocolate ice cream sandwich $4 - divine. Food was great and a bang for your buck. I know it's called the "meatball" shop, but I was impressed by the fresh local greens. The chicken and beef meatballs are tasty. I liked the spicy pork, but didn't love it. It wasn't as flavorful as the others. Downside is the small space, long waits and voices carry so It can get super loud. In warm weather, you can just get take out and sit in the park.
Two words: perfect bar.

Sake always spells adventure. Deceptively strong, this clear liquor always hits me harder than an Acme safe in Toontown. We started down a staircase that looked like it was headed to a basement, and found a Japanese restaurant down there! The place was packed, so we figured it was busy for a reason and left our name. The wait was about 10 min for a party of two, but would likely have been significantly longer with a larger group. The seating was those long picnic table benches immediately next to strangers (a NYC staple that I cannot seem to grow accustomed to). That's alright because we had a bottle of sake on the way, and that's enough to make you forget the neighbors. The bottle we picked was $45, which was on the cheaper side of the options with others listed at upwards of $100. They had roughly 30 different kinds to choose from, so a decent selection if you know your way around a sake menu. Most of the menu was fish or meat dishes, leaving limited options for veggie-saurs like myself. I did try the vegetable maki (spring rolls) which were served with a thick plum dipping sauce that was a significant step up from plain old soy sauce. I also had the tofu salad, which was sliced tofu over lettuce with asparagus spears and tomato slices. The tomato tasted like fish. This is not normal and especially gross when you're not expecting it, so I am concerned that the chef used a dirty knife to slice them. I made the executive decision and decided to pick off the others, and just set them aside. The dressing on the salad was good. It came in a soup bowl and had to be ladled on, but it had good flavor. The service was meh. Food came out as it was ready, and in no particular order. There were people bustling around constantly, but they never seemed available. It was an effort just to get the check. At least the sake was good. But overall, skip it.

We were very excited about this place. Food is better than average. We would like to go there regularly but I am afraid the professionalism expressed by the kitchen does not extend into the dinning room. I like tentative service but these guys are constantly at your table trying to take the plates away. Even when the plate is full. Couldn't finish a sentence before someone was asking me an insincere question about the food or whatever. LET YOUR CLIENTS RELAX AND ENJOY THEIR MEAL.

Went here with my best friend on our way to New Jersey for an Anime Convention via Penn Station. Before hopping on that NJ Transit we decided to grab lunch here. (I looked up on yelp beforehand places to eat around Penn Station). When we walked in we were greeted by the friendly and oh so beautiful waiting staff. It wasn't too busy around 5:30pm on a Thursday, there were two couples dining here at the time. Both appeared to be Hispanic, so I knew this spot had to be legit. Soccer played on the TV while Spanish music played on the radio. I was digging the atmosphere. They don't have a lot of space to use, and they made it work. Our lovely waitress explained the days special and took our drink orders. Inca Kola all day! Anyone who grew up in the hood knows what the business is. 30g of sugar a serving type of stuff. That super sweet, super bad for you, super yellow kind of soda. My buddy got the Pollo Saltado, and I got the Lomo Saltado. Beef (or chicken, respectively) stir fried with onions, tomatoes, and french fries served with a side of white rice. It didn't take too long to come out. Portions seemed just right, not too big, not too small. The beef for my Lomo Saltado was honestly a little dry and tough. But this dish itself was very flavorful, the onions still had a crunch without a harsh onion taste, and the tomatoes were great not soggy or anything. The fries still had a crisp to them which blew my mind, because it still absorbed a lot of the juices from the dish! White rice is the great equalizer, giving you something to mellow out your tastebuds when your dish is exploding with flavor. Every ingredient was well represented and worked in harmony. My only complaint was the beef, which should be the star of a dish like this. So all in all, I'm giving the Lomo Saltado a 3 and a half. My best friends Pollo Saltado, well... I never asked him about it, but he ordered ANOTHER ONE to go. So I guess it was good XD. I also ordered the half rotisserie chicken with rice and beans to go. So let me touch on that for a bit... My hotel in New Jersey didn't have a microwave so I ate it cold. BUT I still REALLY liked it. I can't speak on how it would taste fresh since I ate it like 3 hours later, so I won't give it a rating, just know that it's very flavorful, plentiful, and that green sauce is MONEY. Couple of comments based on other reviews: Seems they have a bathroom up and running for customers now, its very close. The only weird thing is the sink is outside of the bathroom. And the WATER situation seems to have improved. Previously, many customers complained about the place only serving bottled water. Well, when we ordered water we got, presumably tap water free of charge. I really wish I got to try more dishes before I wrote a review, but I couldn't contain myself. This is a really nice spot to eat, conveniently located outside of penn station. The rotisserie chicken is a great value and the staff is wonderful. I know I'll be back soon.

If you can call in, that'd be nice. Came here, said it'd be a 1.5 hour wait, came back, said it'd be another 45 min, came back, said it'd still be a wait. Â Finally decided to just order some eggs and blueberry pancakes to go. Btw, during this waiting time, my other friends and I (there were 5 people total) ate at the Meatball shop, Sugar Sweet Sunshine, got drinks at the cafe across the street, and had coffee at Dunkin Donuts. So anyways, yes the hash browns were delicious, the eggs were like any other eggs, the blueberry pancakes were fluffy but I'm not much of a pancake girl. Â I liked the buttery sauce that goes on top of it, but would I come back for this long wait? Â Nah. Btw, they pretty much close the line at around 1:15pm and run out of a few pastries/muffins by then.

This is a pretty good tapas place, but unless you are a wine drinker, your libation options are DANGED limited (cider or beer, and not much selection there). It is a long and narrow joint that can get very hot in the winter as some of the building steam pipes run right next to some of the bar tables. Â That said, the blistered peppers are f'awesome, and they do croquetas como Dios manda. Â But, as with most tapas places in the city, they don't really have the full Spanish joy and variety one would hope for...it is good, but not stellar. It is not overbearingly loud, so first dates are possible, especially with a table at the room in the back.

To be honest with you, I realllllllly wanted to like Lombardi's Pizza!!!! And despite their history and popularity, I couldn't help but feel that they were a bit overrated. I came here on Friday and we ended up ordering a large mushroom pizza ($23.50), a large pancetta pizza ($23.50), and two of their famous clam pizza ($28.00/each.) I was super excited to finally be able to take a bit of history but was slightly disappointed at the taste. Don't get me wrong, their pizza were decent but definitely not memorable. Instead of being soft and chewy, their dough was a bit dry and flavorless. The cheese was minimal and the toppings were sparing. The only thing that was intrigued me most was their two-dozen claim pizza! Apparently, their clam pizza was part of the restaurant's original menu when they first opened up in 1905. During the turn of the century, NYC had an abundant amount of clams so hence, their clam pizza was borned. Surprisingly, all their restaurants are scattered around the block and therefore waiting is not long. It's a perfect experience for tourists and even locals alike. I would rate their pizza 3 stars but because of their rich history, they earn themselves an extra star for the New York experience which of course is priceless!

WATCH OUT FOR CHICKEN BONES! needed to post this on yelp. after almost breaking a tooth (there were two bones and then I stopped eating the chicken) I would not recommend getting the chicken. Stick with the gyro meat instead. Just not worth the risk. White sauce is tasty.

Wonderful little brunch restaurant. Has a great atmosphere, the staff is extremely friendly and accommodating. The decor is very European, a true French feeling. The food is absolutely fantastic and they have a good variety of brunch menu drinks. I'm definitely coming back here!

I'm a bit of a label whore-- I saw the "Michelin Recommended" sign on the door and swooned.....but maybe it's not what's on the outside, but on the inside that counts, right? Â At least that's what Sesame Street taught me. The menu emphasizes simple, non pretentious food that makes you wonder, "could I make this at home?". Â I came here for a late lunch and ordered the calamari (served with red sauce with a nice kick from the chili oil), fried polenta (deep-fried triangles with a sprinkle of parmesan cheese), and had a slice of the pizza funghi (excellent chewy bread. Â This was the highlight of my meal). Â Everything was executed very well and again, very simple and unfussy. I always feel sheepish yelping restaurants like Barbuto-- with a celebrated chef and glowing industry reviews-- but for me everything was "just alright". Â The converted garage doors and exposed kitchen with brick oven in the back all make for a nice, casual setting and yes, the food was good and the service was prompt. Â Not a destination restaurant for me but can definitely see it as a great neighborhood spot.

Not thinking of coming back again as a group. Â Afterall there is one restaurant in St. Marks that I can compare this restaurant to. Â I didn't think this place was that fabulous the reason I said that is: 1. The entrace is on the second floor and it is small. Â When me and my boyfriend got there already two people standing Â who we didn't know at first was part of our meetup group were trying to get a table. Â Just too crowded at the entrance. Â After a second or two another couple came standing behind me and I stepped on her toes by mistake which I felt very sorry for. Â She was wearing open toes shoes and I was wearing Nike sneakers. Â Ouch! Â The waiter/waiteress should've have let the two people in front of us to be seated inside the restaurant first. 2. We were seated in a small booth that could accomodate 8 people. Â Thanks to Jeff's warning that we could possibly get the booth that says "watch your head". Â Even for me shorter than 5 ft. 2 in. needs to be sure that my head does bow down so I won't hit my head. Â Only once I entered through that door and twice I just went in through the side which didn't have that odd entrance. 3. Â We didn't get a waiter that likes us much and we haven't tipped him yet. Â I could understand being a waiter/waitress is never that easy to begin with. Â I kind of notice that there are times when we order some things on the menu he didn't understand us. Favorite new find in Chelsea! Gorgeous, cozy outdoor garden seating area (although the chairs are a bit rickity) and great food. Steak tartare appetizer was solid but the stand-out was the merguez dish. Perfectly spicy and on a nice bed of yoghurt/cous cous/chickpeas. Husband got the burger - enjoyed it as well but found it a tad sweet and the toast (bun) was too crispy. Told the waiter and he said that's a common complaint (so why still so crispy?). Overall - great experience, already looking forward to going back.

Omar plate was too citrus-y for me and I'm not a fan of pink pickles in my salad so it didn't work for me, however I must point out that the meat was juicier than I expected. Â Freddy Jr. Plate was better, less citrus more savory which merits a 3 1/2 stars. Â I read many yelpers are fans' of the chicken platter so next time I go I know what I need to get. Â  Love the free falafel they give out as we wait for the food to be prepped.

I was reluctant about reviewing this place, because there are already so many reviews for it. However...one never knows how a review might help another and I am always ready to help others whenever I can! After a very long train ride down to this neighborhood, we walked and walked and finally grabbed a cab since we were completely lost trying to find this place that apparently serves the best breakfast in NYC. We would have taken a taxi from the start, but our daughter wanted to experience the subway, so away we went on the train...by the time we found the right street, we noticed we were right near Katz's Deli, which we also wanted to try - so we decided we'd stop there first, since now it was practically lunchtime. (I'll write that review later) We found Clinton street and found a very long line to eat some really delicious looking food...we walked up and decided to just order some pastries and lattes to go. Pastries were very good, not the best I've ever had, but very good. I cannot give more stars because I didn't experience eating a full meal. NOTE to visitors...this is a CASH only place. Ok, I get it - cc fees are high and it sucks to pay them, unfortunately, when you are traveling using cc's is the most convenient way to get around, otherwise you need to carry a bunch of cash with you that could get stolen, etc. Long story short, it was good we only had pastries and coffee, I would not have had enough cash to cover breakfast - which by the way, if you are wondering about the prices being less because of the cash only "business" they are not. Bottom line...I'd love to try their breakfast, I hope they take cc's in the future.
Loved this place. Â The beef goulash was delicious and I loved that it was BYOB.

I just moved to New York City from Austin, TX and I was super excited to find organic BBQ anywhere in the city! Especially with an association to my former town (Austin Rocks!) There are some reviews that say the meat is dry... I've gone several times and sometimes it's juicy - sometimes it's a little dry. I think it depends on the batch. Overall, I think they have a very nice selection of food and sides. I love the cole slaw. The mac and cheese is tasty. I've written a longer article about it here goo.gl/JPC25
Cozy ambience, good pasta, reasonable prices

I have been a few times but today they seem to have become too cool for school. Â If you feel like waiting for a table when several are visibly available (and even set) then this is the place for you.

If you use your imagination to picture a great tapas place in Chelsea just a few blocks from Meatpacking District, you would probably come pretty close to a place like Salinas. The almost-palindromic restaurant is trendy and pretty lively, and I'm sure it's a frequent pit stop for groups who are planning on hitting a club afterwards. My group was seated in the bar area so we didn't truly soak in the ambiance of the restaurant's core, but a quick peak instead while en route to the restroom revealed a much bigger area than I had assumed. Decor and atmosphere aside, the food at Salinas is great. As with any tapas place, it's worth trying out as many items as possible, even if your memory of what you ate gets a little hazy after a while. The highlight dish for me was probably the octopus, which was thick and charred perfectly to retain just the right amount of texture and flavor. I'm also very impressed by the blood sausage with its rich flavor really coming out thanks to the fantastic seasoning. The special of the night was the suckling pig with tender, juicy meat and fantastic crispy skin soaked in a sweet reduction. Maybe most surprising for me was the grilled chicken entree which I did not expect much from, but it certainly delivered on flavor. Also great were the artichokes and the patatas bravas, but I was slightly less impressed by the rice with octopus (though that might just be attributed to the aforementioned seared octopus which I think would dwarf just about any other octopus-based dishes). Be sure to accompany your food with a selection from the solid list of Spanish wines. The wine menu helpfully splits choices according to style, body and flavor profiles so you can pick a bottle you'll like without a full knowledge of Spanish wines. And that pretty much rounds up the package for Salinas. The food, drinks, service and atmosphere are all great. I'm certainly going to try and make my way back here some time to sample the rest of the menu.

Everyone I talked to told me I had to try their Kati Rolls, however I was not impressed. Service was not great & the roll itself was very dry and tasteless. I got the paneer roll and the paneer was not flavorful, spices were lacking and there wasn't enough sauce. I would ask for extra sauce on the side. Also make sure you keep cash on you, they do not take card for any purchases under 10 dollars I believe. If I'm in NY again I would maybe give this place another try, but not on the top of my list for places to eat.

I love this place so much that one time, they sat me next to Leonardo Di Caprio and I embarrassingly had to leave my table after ordering wine because my friend and dinner companion got stuck at work. Â I was sad to leave Leo and sadder I didn't get to eat at ABC Kitchen that night. The beet salad is amazing. Â So is the lobster.

Despite the other glowing reviews, our table did not find it so good. I don't know whether it was what we ordered or the chef that night, but it was not worth the price. We had the eggplant wrapped goat cheese which the server recommended, and that was nasty and I couldn't finish it. Then we had a mediocre veal pasta that was not even worth it. All in all I will not be back.

Has been a go-to spot for mid-week delivery. They tend to be fast, Food is good, mainly salmon or steak dinner. Mostly get the salmon/quinoa combo. Sushi is eh at best, and inconsistent. Avoid delivery during weekend when food can be downright awful, maybe because kitchen too busy. Ramen is fine but not comparable to ramen-only places where lines are much longer. Management is smug, cancelled a seamless order w/o notice because item was only available at lunch, though menu never said so. But then never bothered to call to call for replacement item. 45 min later wondering where dinner was! Lots of restaurants shutting down one block over on Greenwich. Makes me wonder if they are short-timers as well

Great wings, ribs, and pizza at relatively cheap prices. Had a decent beer selection also. The only thing I didn't like that much was my cocktail, the La Candela, which had too much ice. The Tartufo pizza was particularly good. The decor was dark with a lot of wood. I liked it. There is a backroom where they sometimes have music and upstairs that is a little less pub-like.

I live nearby and everytime I pass by I just Â need to get the corns. It's irresistable. It is a little difficult to dine in here tho as the cafe is extremely crowded.. and small. But I guess the good food would make it up.

Great place to get my Korean fix on a budget, and when I went it was bustling with activity, so you know this place is a winner! I'm berating myself for not checking it out sooner, but better late than never! As soon as me and my friend found a place to sit, and she returned with her tray of tasty delights, I headed straight to the hot buffet section and loaded up my tray with fried chicken, clear noodles with veggies, beef wrapped around string beans, kimbap, and bulgogi... and it came out to around $7....and it made me full (with room for dessert at Red Mango). The decor isn't anything to write home about, but this place is more of a deli, as other reviewers mentioned, than a sit-down restaurant, although there are places to sit. It's also a great place to eat at if you're alone- you may have to share a table with someone, but as long as you get to enjoy your meal that shouldn't be an issue. Filling, tasty Korean deli food at an inexpensive price = A Miracle on 32nd Street!
Mehhhhhh. The fries were soaked in a chemically cheese glop. The truffle burger was AOK. Solid 5 out of 10.

I went to Tuome as part of a self-guided tour of "what's new and up-and-coming" in NYC this fall. I wasn't disappointed, but nor was I really amazed. (Note - I just read the NY Times Review today and I'm a little surprised by the enthusiasm for things that I've seen a lot of before, but my complaints are the same, so maybe there's something there) Service - just fine, attentive but not overly so and quite friendly and enthusiastic about what they are serving Ambiance - spare and industrial/cabin hybrid. Not overly fussy but clearly on trend. Restaurant designers just can't seem to get enough of all those Edison bulbs these days... Wine - short but interesting by-the-glass list. Props for diversity. Food - we had a few small plates, sides and one main between two people... Deviled Egg: If there's one thing I'm absolutely going back for, it's this! LOVED IT Scallops: Perfectly cooked, like butter, but the veggie puree with it is too sweet and really distracts Octopus: I came specifically for this dish and found it was neither here nor there. Really well cooked, but both my dining partner agreed that the bacon distracted from the octopus and was too salty to compete with the delicate flavor of the foam Corn: Too sweet, a bit too liquidy, and nothing particularly special Sticky rice: Yummy comfort food, but nothing I haven't had before Conclusion: I'd go back to have those Deviled Eggs, and maybe try some of the other things the Times raved about... always worth a second shot, if it's even possibly to get in!
Went back here after four years and nothing has changed. Â That's one of the only times I can say that and mean it as a compliment!

Decent brunch, but not very memorable. Met up with some friends on a Sunday. Place was just busy enough to be lively but not crowded. I ordered a Delta omelet which had crawfish, shrimp, gruyere and served with grits. You get a choice between grits, home fries, or toast, but grits are the obvious choice, because you could get toast or home fries at any old brunch place or diner. My omelet was nicely filled with lots of cheese and seafood. The thing that brought it down was that it seemed more cooked than I'd like. I like my omelets to be soft and fluffy. This one was firm and practically chewy. The grits were really good though, you cant go wrong with those. My friends' orders seemed better than mine, and if I went back, I'd probably order shrimp n' grits instead. Dinner menu looks better than the brunch menu.
One of the best brunch spots in the area. Great food, prices, and service. But the BEST part about this place are the doughnuts. Holy shit! So good.

I believe this place would have received 5 stars from me if I wasn't waiting for Â almost 2 hours in the cold. Â They also had run out of the clam pizza by 5 pm... But other than that, the pizza was very very good. Â I demolished the entire pizza including the crust. The white pizza had huge blotches of cheese, which was my favorite out of the two. If there is no line, I will be back.

Came at 4:15, waited for two hours before we were allowed to sit and order raw food. Were given the same story about the kitchen being overwhelmed,etc but considering how many tables were empty, they could have let us sit and drink beer while we waited... Thanks Time Out for Misleading us here.

For a dominican place, it 's okay. Sophies is the same price but you get wayyy more food there and much much better. The sweet plantain at margons suck, it's undercooked and really dark indicating using old oil so they don't cook it as long so it won't turn black. Their porkchops are soooo tough, so stringy. Their beans are okay, not much flavor. Their fried chicken is the only good thing.

expectedly casual atmosphere- good friends - I was hoping high artichoke fritters were ok i reluctantly ordered the only fish entree ( fish and chips ) buddy quote " that s not boring i am sure its fish and chips " fancy" battered like a wet corn dog + limp undercooked fries = sad was glad to order an after dinner armagnac to soften the soggy blow five minutes later the bartender was decent enough t apologize that there actually wasnt Â any armagnac but they did have some single malts. felt like i paid a lot of money for a failed student project

The old Calle Ocho was really good however the new one sucks big time. The food was extremely bland and even the sangrias were not good and I tried 4 different ones. I was extremely disappointed since I always enjoyed the original restaurant.

I don't think you can go wrong with anything on the menu. Â It's all really good. Â The staff is nice, too. Â They don't take reservations, but they'll call you when your table's ready, so you can hang out at one of the bars down Vanderbilt while you wait. Â For anyone that's experienced a wait at Totto, this is a great policy. Â Don't forget: straight cash, homie.
Their ramen was overrated, it was good but not amazing and expensive, although pork bum was really good, I would give more stars if they have pork bum ramen

Gaia Cafe is an amazing little spot that just opened near my block. Â Its real-deal Northern Italian food cooked by a great lady who learned home-cooking from her Mama and her Gramma! Â The prices are great, the food is even better and the service is mindful and homey. Â Its the kind of place that New York needs - come and enjoy the Gnocchi, Lasagna, Mortadella (she also sells imported Italian cold-cuts and cheeses!), great coffee and sweets. Â  Its a daytime place for the most part but its brand new and maybe she'll stay open later (as she does on Saturdays) as time goes on. PS - Free wifi too :)
Phenomenal, Authentic Thai Food. Glad I found on Yelp! Came at lunch, sat right away. Bangkok Noodles with Shrimp and Panang were spot on - amazing flavors. If you like Thai, this is a can't miss.
Really yummy - the meatball mini sandwiches are a must.

When I visit NYC, I always try to hit up Mamoun's no matter where I am staying. Â They consistently have the best falafel and shawarma I have ever tried. Â Service is always lighting quick and friendly.

Came here after reading all of the positive reviews. Arrived at the beginning of happy hour. Approached the bar and there was a barback and the bartender standing around. Since it was my first time here and many places have oyster happy hour only at the bar, I asked if the oyster happy hour was only at the bar. Then both laughed at me and then said "uh, the happy hour is only for outdoor seating" - There was no outdoor seating. Then they continued on with each other saying where happy hour was not (in the snow, upstairs, basement, etc). Putting down your customers isn't the best way to greet them. I was meeting a friend here, so I was going to wait for her and then head somewhere else. After she arrives, staff passes by and we ask for drinks, and oysters, but the guy didn't even wait around for us to finish asking before leaving to put in the drink orders. I guess he heard us because the oysters came and they were watery and bland. If you're coming for the dollar oysters, I recommend going to Ten Bells down the street, Mermaid Inn on 2nd Ave or even Essex, close by. The rude service and the terrible oysters left a bad taste in my mouth.

Yes, Il Baretto is worth every star I can give it on Yelp. I love this place so much because the food is authentic Italian goodness and so are the staff. When I step in, I feel like I've been transported to a little bistro in Milan or Florence. A perfectly crafted cappuccino and panino, along with some friendly banter with the staff, and voila -- attitude adjustment without jetting off to the Amalfi Coast! I just read that another reviewer was irritated they had to hail the server for the check. Hm... how do I put this? You don't get it. The folks at Il Baretto aren't going to rush you along. They want you to stop and smell the vino rosso. In addition to delectable sandwiches, salads, small plates, and entrees, the staff serve up real Italian charm. In this stressed out city, Il Baretto is an oasis of gentility.
expensive, decent ramen.

Mi piace!!! Â Authentic Neapolitan pizza! Â Sure, you can find a lot of places that claim to be authentic Neapolitan, but how many of these places are staffed by Neapolitan people? Â The service is quick... Â Our pizzas were out in less then 10 minutes from the moment we ordered. Â I ordered the "Laura" which was topped with tomatoes, mozzarella, mascarpone, Â speck, and rosemary. Â Definitely the best Neapolitan pizza I've had. The place is nicely decorated and they have outdoor eating space in the back. Â My only complaint is that there was a large group with several small children, and the a**hole parents allowed the kids to run loose like wild animals, screaming and what not, disturbing everyone around. Â So other than that group a**holes it was a great experience. Â I'll definitely return, but will ask to be seated as far away as possible from small children.
Really cool place. Try as much as you can then go back and try the rest. Korean beef tacos are my favorite.
Delicious food, friendly service and tasty wine. We've been back twice and will come again. Lasagne like my mamma made.

You will probably accidentally order more than you can consume the first time around because everything is so cheap. Â For people who have never tried sesame pancakes (like me), I would describe it as a mix between bahn mi and navajo fry bread. It is good, a little heavy but worth it for the price. Â Seating is a little meh, I will admit. Â I am rating based solely on the dumplings and price because you don't go to hole-in-the-walls for cleanliness right?

Awesome beer selection and really inventive menu. The knowledgeable, attentive wait staff will happily aid you in selecting beer and building your menu for the evening. Came with my girlfriend and her friend, and sat on the enclosed outdoor patio in the back. 2 orders of house made beef jerky (amazing), an assorted cheese plate and beef heart tartare: all were incredible. Pricey joint but worth it, and you can still enjoy yourself without totally breaking the bank. Will definitely return.

Two words: Â French toast. Â (Legen....wait for it...DARY!) Brunch, mid-week lunch and dinner are great here, but brunch is an experience. Â It does get to be a scene (with the occasional East Village celeb spotting), so reservations would be a wise move. Not a big fan of the table crackers/bread basket (I got a helping full of cracked pepepr). Â Cocktail menu is great. Â A must-try for the French toast alone. Â It might just change your life.

After trying the food at Smorgasburg, I knew I had to stop in to the restaurant. As soon as you walk in the door, you feel welcome. I sat at the bar to place an order to go. Jon, one of the owners immediately greeted me and was so helpful and answered all my questions about the menu. Fried chicken biscuit with the jezebel sauce...amazing.
