Ordered the mini biscuits-HOMEMADE peach jam...so incredibly delicious. Loved my fried green tomatoes too-definitely will be back for sure(the red velvet cake looks soooo good) GO!!

Awesome place for some cheap Korean grub. Too bad I only discovered this place during my last night in town! Amazing selections for good prices in Manhattan. Kimchi fried rice, spicy chicken, spicy pork, kimbap galore, banchan, etc. Great for those lonely nights and you don't feel like cooking, haha!

Great food, adorable cozy place with a teeny tiny kitchen that puts out great fresh food! I had the chicken avocado salad and it was the perfect size! Will definitely be back! Now accepts credit cards which is also much easier than cash only.

It's too bad that some of the previous reviews were based on what this establishment used to be. Everything has changed. Â With the new owners, new menu, new decorum and new philosophy, I rate this restaurant an A+. The staff is friendly, the menu is great, the food is fresh, and the atmosphere is airy and comfortable. I have nothing bad to say about 983 and will continue to go back.

BEWARE!! I believe my Debit Card # was lifted from someone working at the counter. This place is poorly managed and has outgrown its small space. They have too many people behind the counter and it is total chaos just to get a take out order. It is too bad because the food is great and affordable. PAY IN CASH!!!!!!!!!!! I've also gone in there when it hasn't been Â busy and was seated at a table and completely ignored for 20 minutes so I just got up and left.

Score: Average. The Sushi was good, but not so many choice. The curry noodle was ok. The Chicken rice was ok. The cold soba was ok. The Environment is great tho. A lot of Japanese. But the food is really soso.

Oh LadurÃ©e, you are so yummy. Our favorites include the pistachio and coconut. Pairs perfectly with some tea. Just a sweet slice of Paris in NYC. Go, enjoy and be prepared to drop some $ (yes, it's expensive but after trying to unsuccessfully make macarons, I leave it to the experts!)

My Italian born husband and I have been here many times. We first wandered in not knowing Osteria Morini's yelp ratings or favorable reviews and were pleasantly surprised. They serve real, deceptively simple, Italian food like we would find in Italy (which is not something that can be said of most "Italian" restaurants in the city). Â The staff is friendly, the food never disappoints (even the table bread they serve is to die for), and the entire restaurant has the warm, un-pretentious familiar feeling of being in a small family restaurant in Italy.

This place I have loved dearly, even before the name change (formerly Get Fresh Market & Table). The food is always fresh, revolutionary, and well displayed. Last night my boyfriend and I went there for a post-Valentine's Day date (we both had the flu the day of). Â There was no one else in the restaurant, which gave us a cozy, intimate dinner. The waitress was phenomenal. Â She was pleasant and helpful, but not in the way of our romantic date. She talked with us about the food, about our relationship, and pulled all the stops for us to make the night a great romantic evening for us. Â  She even put on a slow song for us and we danced in the middle of the dining room! The food was divine. Â I mean, my boyfriend and I have a great, deep appreciation for good food, and we left more than satisfied. What we had: ~The Cheese Board is always a huge success here. Â You can't go wrong with it. Â I'm not a huge fan of blue cheese in general, but even that was edible! ~Clams with pork belly was really delicious. Â The clams were like no clams I've ever had (and I'm from New England), and the pork belly was not overcooked. ~The Vegetable Plate is always inspired, and always great. Â I had an array of fresh and tasty veggies for my palate. Â I love their soups. ~Boyfriend had the turkey burger which was huge and apparently amazing. ~Granitas were so light and perfect that even though by this time our stomachs were stretched fully, we could stomach a little more. ~We got two complimentary chocolate truffles fresh from the new pastry chef, which made my heart break (in a good way). We finished the night incredibly stuffed, and high on an amazing meal and wonderful date experience. They cater very well to my gluten free diet, and that always is a plus for me as well. The only downside is the pricing, but considering how amazing the food is, I think it's worth the cost.
Great food always. The hirata buns are awesome and the ramen bowls are even better. I never tried the other stuff on the menu though.

Great new bar on the Upper East Side. Â Loved the octagon shaped bar!!!!! Â Wonderful for conversation and an overall comfortable feeling. Amazing craft beer and bourbon selection, not to mention incredibly creative and tasty specialty cocktails. They really paid attention to detail with the lighting and beautiful wood. Â I will be a regular for sure!!

Jenga! Jenga! Jenga! Not your traditional beer garden, more like a very large restaurant that only serves beer and beer food + a more modern decor. Â Facebook-Like! Â I appreciate the ample board games available like jenga, scramble and I don't know what else. Â  Fun times here.

I've been here 3-4 times now and don't know why I come back. Even though I enjoy the coffee and atmosphere, I always leave thinking I should never come back- poor service and expensive mediocre food. I wait forever looking to flag someone down to order something and still need to ask for things twice, or get my check even with my coat on and wallet out. And to top it off I had hair in my food, which they didn't comp. I should really start going somewhere else.

This was a great neighborhood choice before a Sunday evening show. My friend remembered having dined at a ramen place w a long long in the are and I found a couple by searching yelp. Line was formed despite 5pm hour. They took our order outside and seated us at the counter where we watched our food prepared. Tried the pork bun which was moist and delicious and dined on spicy chicken ramen w a cold sake. Loved everything.

VH and I stumbled into this place totally randomly on a nice Indian summer afternoon in November. The place is kinda small, with a long communal table plus another smaller 4 tables, a bar, and a small open kitchen. There are a few interesting pictures on the walls, and a projector attached to the ceiling seems to indicate that perhaps they show movies and stuff occasionally. I like this simple decor with some nice little touches. Both my gf and I tried the caipirinha ($8 with Pitou, $10 with Leblon), which was tasty, refreshing, and with the right amount of alcohol (that kind of kick that you feel after 20 minutes or so). We tried the Prato Feito: you choose 4 small dishes for $9. Our choices were farofa (toasted yucca flour), beans, couve (sautÃ©ed, chiffonaded collard greens), and abobrinha (sautÃ©ed, julienned zucchini). They were all very good, apart from the farofa, which is just some sort of flour you add to the beans if they are too loose. We then ordered feijoada (a stew of beans with beef and pork meats), which apparently is Brazil's national dish. In fact, I would suggest you get this dish: the beans taste better with pork and beef (trust me on this: I'm a doctor), and the dish comes with collard greens. I also liked the fact that the chopped greens for the dressing came in a shot glass: nice touch! Both our waitress and the bartender were friendly and good. If you don't mind the eyesore on the other side of the street (one of the ugliest buildings this side of the iron curtain), I would say this is a good spot for a relaxed, unpretentious, and somewhat cozy date.

Sorry, Cookshop - you've got a magical 111 reviews, but I just feel compelled to leave my own, so here comes 112. I took my deliciously handsome boyfriend here for dinner for his birthday, and we had a deliciously handsome waiter who served us a deliciously handsome meal. Â I was glad we had a reservation - the bar area seemed to have many people waiting. Â And we were whisked to our table right away - felt good! Â Additionally, the sommelier, Richard, visited our table twice - once with a food request we'd made, and once to talk about the wines. Â He was great. Nice room - the small herb plants along the east wall are a nice touch. Try the viognier - at $65 a bottle you might think twice, but I'm telling you DON'T. Â Just do it. We had delicious Island Creek oysters (Massachusetts oysters that give West Coast oysters a serious run for the money), an amazing dandelion salad with squash, plus the purslane salad with roasted hazelnuts was a little piece of heaven right here on earth. We also enjoyed a tasty Long Island striped bass, and the scallops were absolutely perfect. Â Dessert was a saffron semolina cake with a YUM saffron sauce and grilled peaches. Â A really great end to a terrific meal.

Having visited MP Taverna several times since it opened last year I had found it to be a welcome addition to the restaurant scene in Astoria. A Greek restaurant with a modern twist, food was always excellent and the staff was always well informed and attentative and would have easily given it 4 stars. Recently though I must say standards have dropped. Management keeps changing as do the servers and barstaff and for some reason all their good servers seem to have left. Most of the main menu dishes are hit and miss ( and I would have expected them to refresh the menu since it opened over a year ago ) and even recently some of their "specials of the day" resemble more that of an italian eatery. Has Mr. Psilakis totally ignored his Astoria business and left the complete running to his staff which also day by day or should I say visit to visit are less and less greek or have any knowledge of greek food or customer service ( and that goes from the management who if they can be forced away from their cell phones, to most of the servers to even the hostess at the door who for some reason cannot answer a simple question). And since I am Greek and praise Mike Psilakis for his concept, I will visit MP again and give it another chance though having always recommended it to friends I will wait to see if the MP owners will try and get it back to it's original concept.

Fantastic little place in the East Village! Aesthetic, Australian-inspired decor, beautifully plated meals, and a fabulous cocktail selection. Definitely take the server's recommendations on the specials, Alan surely did not disappoint! Flinders Lane is also an excellent place to check out for brunch!

service - our waiter was nice, but not very helpful. Â one of the other servers actually came by because we had a question and we thought he was very helpful. Â my hubbie and I are vegetarians so he went through the menu to see what dishes could be altered to meet our dietary restrictions. roasted mushroom app - not what i expected at all. Â it was a cold dish (i was thinking hot for some reason) with some hearty grains and ricotta salata. Â Overall it was very unique and tasted healthy, but I'm not sure I would order this app again. cacio & pepe - DELICIOUS! Â I couldn't believe how a simple dish could taste this fabulous. Â The long strings of pasta were perfectly cooked and accompanied with just the right amount of black pepper and cheese. Â  gnocchi - we got this with tomato sauce. Â the gnocchi were little pillows of perfection. Â they were light, but still filling. Â the slightly sweet/slightly tangy tomato sauce was very good. Â  i wish there was something a little extra to make this dish really stand out. Â  I would definitely come back for the cacio & pepe!

After reading all the good reviews about this place on Yelp, I was really looking forward to eating here. My parents were in town so I figure'd we could check out Sanford's for bunch on a Saturday afternoon. Luckily, I was able to make a quick reservation a couple hours before because otherwise I think the wait would have been pretty long. While the ambience is pretty nice, I was actually disappointed by the food. It wasn't bad, and I wanted to like it more than I did, but it just tasted like your standard brunch fare that you could probably get at a chain restaurant. I had the croque madam, which is a bit of a heavier item, so maybe that's why; but my father wasn't too impressed with his meal either (smoked swordfish). Maybe I'll visit again and try one of their more unique items or try dinner since I really want to like this place. Unfortunately, my first visit was pretty average.

Food portions are huge and prices are very reasonable. The cheesecakes are famous for a reason!!! The cherry and strawberry cheesecakes are my favorite, but the strawberry shortcake is delicious as well!!!

I LOVE the Hope Garage! The owner is very sweet and makes you feel welcome. The bartender Derrick is awesome. I've made this my favorite late night spot. The food is good, Plus the kitchen is open until 4am! Can't beat that.

Had a great dinner here with friends the other night. We're staying in the neighborhood and were really happy to find a place that was so willing to accommodate dietary needs. The server was really sweet. I forgot her name but she had long blonde hair. She was attentive but not overly. The food was phenomenal. I had the lobster eggplant ravioli and was thoroughly impressed. Most places I have lobster at tend to over butter the dish, but this was perfect. I just wanted to note that I saw the staff having family meal together when they were closing the place down. It says a lot about a group that work together and then still want to dine together afterwards...probably a good reason everything was so perfect during our visit. Â They were all wonderful, and we will certainly be back. Our friends live right around the corner and are excited to bring other friends here as well. Thank you. SD

Love this place, I've been here a few times including my birthday. Good food, strong drinks and they serve large sized tapas. fyi- I don't think they normally take reservations unless it's a special occasion or large party. Â I am definitely thinking of trying their brunch one day...

Stopped for lunch and ordered the burger and frites. Â Burger was a sodden mess of overcooked spinach, greasy onions and some cheese. Sitting on a pair of greasy toast that I used a steak knife to cut through. Â Frites were great. Â Won't be stopping there again. Â Service was OK.

Went there for the first time last night and was greeted by Emily herself. Had camp Randall, Angelina, and banana pudding for dessert. I was going to give this place four stars for friendly service, delicious pizza and wine, and a great (though a tad too loud) atmosphere. Then I read the negative reviews complaining about being asked to keep a screaming baby quiet, about not getting prompt take out pizza, and about how Williamsburg has infected Clinton Hill. And I was reminded how awful restaurants are where they don't try to minimize screaming kids, where they prioritize pick ups and deliveries over those customers who are eating in, and the snobbery and poor service of many wburg joints. And am increasingly thankful that Emily was not any of those things. So 5 stars it is!

Best BBQ in NYC hands down. I've had everything on the menu and it's unreal. The burnt ends are my favorite item on the menu, but they're all amazing. The staff is very friendly, filled with BBQ bros and friendly girls. It's one of my favorite places to go for a quick meal. They also give a lot of fix-ins on the side, which is great. I've gone there solo and ordered for a party on the Super Bowl, they never fail me.

My family and I decided to go here for dinner on a Saturday night. The staff told us the wait would be about 35 minutes. We waited more than an HOUR AND FORTY FIVE minutes before they even THOUGHT about serving us. This is dishonest to customers and prevents honest people excited to have a meal at a nice place from having a meal on a timescale that they determine (based on the word of the staff). Had I known this place would keep my family in paralysis for nearly 2 hours, we would not have considered going. This is particularly offensive for a business that does not allow for reservations. My recommendation: if you have any sort of plan within 4 hours of dinner, don't even think about this place.

I just moved into the neighborhood so I'm systematically trying the restaurants around me. After seeing slightly better than average reviews for this place, I figured I'd give it a try. Â It was also the only sushi place (there are 3 within a block) that had a crowd on a Wednesday night so I went for it. Â I got the 3 Flavor Fish Sushi Dinner which is 2 pieces of ahi, salmon, and yellowtail sashimi with a "special roll" that I couldn't figure out what it was. Â It was enough food for 16 bucks and the sashimi was good enough, the roll was a bit below average, but the real object of my scorn is the wasabi. Â It smelled like some sort of distasteful synthetic variety, tasted the same and wasn't really as "hot" as I like it. Â Kinda put a pall over the whole meal. Â  I may go back to try some their other dishes, but not until I try ALL the other sushi joints nearby.

I gave this place 4 stars because it is a very good option for the area. Food was great - spicy calamari was really flavorful and not too heavy, rice balls and kale salad were also really good. The portions were hit and miss - calamari and rice balls were more than expected and the kale salad was much smaller. Â  Only snag we hit was we were sitting at the bar and service was not great. We were sitting there with empty wine glasses for 30 minutes without him checking on us and it wasn't that crowded. We finally decided to work at getting his attention for another glass but when it took 10 more minutes of trying to catch his eye for him to come over, we just asked for the check instead. Â So if you're at the bar, be very proactive...

The first thing you will notice is how nice one of the watiress is here. She is so lively, warm, and inviting. She makes sure that all your needs are taken care of. After you get over on how friendly she is, you realize how small the restaurant is. It is very dim and very small. I kept on bumping into other tables and chairs when I went to the bathroom. However, the place does have character. The food here is so fresh and delicious. I would highly recommend almost everything on the menu. If it is your first time here, I would definitely try the patacones. Although the plaintains are fried, it is not overly greasy and does not induce a food coma. The portions for the patacones are big enough to satisfy you without making you feel sluggish and guilty. The texture of the arepa is so light and fluffy on the inside, but crispy on the outside. I like how it is baked instead of fried and it holds all the juices from the filling. The platters might seem expensive because they are double the price of the patacones, but the portions are so big that it is definitely worth it. You will be stuffed and still have a whole meal to take home. Even if the portions are big, I like how they do not skimp on quality. All the components, the beans, rice, plaintains, were delicious, nicely seasoned, and not over cooked. You can tell that the restaurant really prides itself on the quality of food it serves. I do not know about the desserts, but we were too full to try them. The only down side was the other waitress. She kept on pressuring us to order more food even if we were full. She also kepto insisting that we get dessert. We told her no and asked her to give us the check, but she walked away and did not get us our check for about ten minutes. Then we asked her for the check again and she kept on trying to sell us desserts. She left when we refused and did not bring the check so we asked the other waitress if she could get it for us. Overall I would still go here again. Everything is fresh and cooked on order.
Too long of a wait for a Ramen, Yes it's good but not good for a 90 min wait for a soup.
4 Stars for the food and environment.. but NAY for the way they climb on top of stove top and over some food..

I went to Pure on a whim last night because I was craving Thai food! The restaurant has a rustic design and tight quarters. Its probably not the best place for large groups. I started with the crab and veggie wrap and than had a delish noodle bowl filled with vegetables and chicken. It was spicy and awesome! I would love to go back to try more of their offerings. Service was also great.

Such a great evening. The staff was amazing. Incredibly friendly and helpful. The food was delicious, American with a flare and such creativity. Great cocktails and good prices. My friends and I loved it. Will definitely go back

This is the best Thai restaurant I have tried. The decoration is great. The food is superb and the price is reasonable. The staffs are nice too. The only problem is there is a line of people whenever you go since this place is so popular!
Yummy yummy gnocchi in rosÃ© sauce with a Cesar salad light on the dressing perfect. Not a lot of space probably 8 seats total for seating but as it says it suppose to be to go.
Here again this evening and still solid as always. Fast, friendly service and excellent pizza. You can't lose!

The fluke and moules frites were nice but most of the classic French dishes that i've tried where unable to keep up with the quality that i'd expect form a place with such a professional staff and nicely styled garden. I haven't had brunch here yet but I have a feeling that it might be what they're best at.

This place rocks. Healthy authentic Japanese and amazing counter service. I always get the suki yaki, sweet potato and kinoko rice balls. The miso soup and dessert options are also amazing. This is an absolute regular for me!

I am not a big oyster eater so can't really comment on the oysters we ordered except the happy hour deal of half dozen east coast oysters and one beer for $12 seems like a good deal. What I really enjoyed are the Fettuccine with Clams and Scallop of the Day. Both are very fresh and cooked just right to retain the sweetness of the scallop and the tenderness of the clams. The crab cake is nothing to rave about.

My dining experience at Ippudo from putting the name on the list to final completion of the meal took a total of 5 hours. Yes, that is a long time... and yes, we had a party of 7 people, which is probably why. I ordered the akamaru modern, which is the original tonkotsu ramen, with pork chashu, cabbage, scallions, and some sort of garlic oil. The broth was amazing-- creamy and tasty just like how I imagined an excellent tonkotsu would taste like. However, I wasn't such a big fan of their ramen and wished that the bowl had included more ingredients. I also got the pork bun, which is another one of their must-try items. OH MAN. Now, this little appetizer was uh-mazing. Loved the pork belly, cooked perfectly. It's juicy and fatty and melts in your mouth. The actual bun is light and fluffy, which goes well with the flavorful piece of pork. YUM. Anyway, my friends and I came here during my birthday weekend, so I was pleasantly surprised with a birthday dessert! I got a green tea creme brulee, which was your traditional cream brulee with green tea ice cream. The plate was beautifully decorated with "Happy Birthday, Cassy!" Plus, the entire staff brought it over and sang the birthday song... so of course, I have to say A+ for customer service! (Well, at least for the actual waiters and waitresses; Â the hostess up in the front can be a little intimidating and less friendly than one would like). So, bottom line: if you are in NY, I'd say yes, go and try their ramen and pork bun! Just don't go with a large party or you might wait forever. Or go a little before they close, so you can snatch up some seats.

Flew in and came straight here after dropping my stuff off at my friend's. Â It was already probably 11pm, but its never too late for empanada mama (which is open 24/7)! Â I seriously chose to come here because of the lovely name. Â I don't even remember the other restaurant option I had... it never even had a chance. We ordered the large pitcher of sangria, which we felt we were highly misinformed, but in a good way! Â The waitress said the large pitcher could adequately quench the thirst of 2 - 3 people, and since 3 people of our party of 4 were planning to drink, we figured it was a good deal. Â No, it turned out to be a great deal! Â 3 Â of us had more than 3 refills, each! Â Good thing for cabs home! Â  We shared the yummy plantain chips and guac, and I had the tasty jalapeno tuna empanada. The rest of the night was a blur and it sure was fun! Â Definitely coming back for more of that delish sangria!

Brunch. We walked in behind a small group who had no reservation, but since we did, we were escorted to our table instantly. Which was impressive considering our table was the ONLY open one in the spot. Nicely done, fabulous Hostess Goddess. Shrimp and parmesan grits are served in a bowl and they were delicious. Lots of (clear) shrimp which appeared to be (raw) undercooked, but they were not. I prefer my shrimp look as if they're cooked thoroughly, but that's just me. There's a monkey-something cocktail that I tried and loved. but boy would i have loved it more if it were served in a big 'ol cup bc the champagne flute left me wanting. and parched. but mostly wanting. I'll be back! love, Nicole getunstucknyc.com

Great place , with great food and service. One word describes everything there: DELICIOUS! Try out the samples, and pick anything you like with no worries about the prices, the quantity or the quality of the food. Everything is served the right way, the right taste, at the right time. Definitely suggest it to all taste lovers :)

Beef soup dumplings are one heck of an invention. Â You taste the chewy dumpling exterior, then the warm, savory broth floods your mouth upon first bite, then finally sink your teeth into the well-flavored morsel of beef. Â Dip it in a soy, ginger, vinegar concoction. Â It doesn't get any better than this.

I used to think this was the best pizza in the city. But of late it hasn't been so good. They seem more interested in chatting amongst themselves. Than not burning the pizza. Come on guys. Step up your game.

I dont eat meat anymore - life without bulgogi=misery...So i was happy to find this restaurant and try some new things. Its about the tofu. Â my friend and i split a potato/vegetable pancake (t5 on menu) and some kind of tofu/soybean sampler entree (a combo of T2, T6 and T8) and got to try an array of dishes-a tofu porridge, perhaps bland but i have a feeling its supposed to be that way. a hot spicy tofu soup and another tofu dish. i dont know what it was but im not complaining. Im not gonna say that this is the best korean food ive ever had, but the offerings were different and i liked that. two entrees and 2 beers cost $56 with the tip. perhaps a lot, but to try something new, it was worth it.

Important: If you don't plan on drinking wine, don't bother going! The tapas were very good, but it's the wine selection that compliments your food that makes your visit worth it. 3 of us shared about 5 or 6 tapas. Oh yeah, it's crowded like the 6 during rush hour. Make reservations!!!

Are you underpaid? Are you overworked? Are you in a rut? Are you stressed, and tired, and broke? Are you sick of the vapid twits who seem to be EVERYWHERE and make you wait, piss you off, breathe your air, and are gradually pushing you toward homicidal mania? Me neither. But if I was any of those things, I would stop by Bogota Bistro's happy hour. Nothing cheers you up and makes you forget your problems like reasonably priced booze in a fun atmosphere. And it really is the happiest of hours. $3 Negra Modelos (and other inferior beers, like Corona), $5 mojitos, and the place is just LIVELY. I've only had the guacamole as far as food is concerned, but the platters going out all around me looked dope, and everything tastes good when you're all boozed up, so I'll be back.

We tried the fried pork dumplings, the boiled shrimp dumplings, and the peking duck sesame pancake. Â They were all okay. Â I'd try other places before going back here. Â The cost is mind blowing, but the food was meh. Â I guess I shouldn't have expected more from cheap food. Â I think the hot sauce and maybe the soy sauce are watered down. Â I wouldn't mind spending an extra dollar to ensure my condiments weren't messed with.

BEST french fries in NYC, hands down! Â My friend's cousins took us here during my first jaunt through NYC. Â I was completely starving by the time we got there, so when I found out that there was a 1.5 hour wait, I thought I was going to pass out. Â Luckily, there's so much to explore and see in SoHo that I ADD'ed and forgot about my hunger. Â Let me tell you -- That 1.5 hour wait was completely worth it! Â I ordered the toasted french ham and gruyere sandwich and fell in love with it. Â  I loved the atmosphere here, too -- so lively and so busy! Â  I'd love to come back here and check out the other food on the menu 'cuz everything sounded delicious!

After a long hiatus we returned for dinner. Â As predicted, we stood outside for 35 minutes before being seated at a family-style long array of connected tables. Â No privacy here, though it's really great to see what everyone's eating to help you decide what to order. Â Service was borderline terrible, we waited so long just to get drinks and you can tell their staff is spread very thin (everyone is sweating and rushing and stressed out). Â Beyond that, the food was amazing. Â We had the disco tots, bacon mac and cheese, and chicken and waffles. Â Worth every calorie. Â  I really wish management would hire more staff and expand their seating. Â They should also get rid of the bar space - total waste of space in an already cramped area if you don't serve alcohol. Overall, Queens Comfort is worth the wait if you're okay with eating in an hour and don't mind getting very little service but really bangin food.

I had pretty high expectations for this place, given how much I had heard about it. Atmosphere is very cozy and waiters are very attentive. The Truffle Burger was good but not great, especially for the price. It was just very heavy and although it wasn't bad, it wasn't for me. We did end up ordering the donut ice cream though and that was way better than expected! Cinnamon chocolate chip is the way to go. Overall, I would come again maybe if someone else wanted to but I much prefer Bareburger or Five Napkin for a similar price but more satisfying meal.

I had the miso tsukemen ramen, and I loved how thick and al dente the noodle was. The miso broth was a bit salty, but over all it was good. The portion was large too, and had me very very full. My friend got the shoyu ramen, and that was delicious as well. The broth had an extra oomph compared to other places that I have tried. However, I think the broth portion was lacking in volume. I think that compared to the amount of noodles, there was way too little broth. I would definitely come back.

Forgot to review Mark's when I first ate it. The sliders are great and I think it's worth the money. Perfect for just hanging out with your friends and having a good time. The chili-cheese fries were super good too (just a hint of spicyness mm). The staff is really nice! The waitress complimented my hair which made my day :).
I came here with my girlfriend and we got some paninis and beer, we sat outside since the weather was cooperating. The food beer and service was great. Overall a very relaxing lunch.

A bustling small restaurant in a cool part of Chelsea. It was packed when we went but that just added to the atmosphere and didn't take away from the experience. We had been to a baseball game so didn't want to have something too heavy, this place had more than one answer. The food was spot on, loads of choice, so any market sides to choose. Garlic broccoli and sweet potato fries are a must. Everything tasted and looked very fresh and it wasn't mega expensive either, really good.
This place is just a dream come true. Crispy, rich sauce, and full of goodness. The staff is always sweet as pie. I love this place when I feel like being indulgent!

Best pizza I've had in New York. Went on a Wednesday night and waited about 30 minutes for a table of 9. Not too bad. Had a drink at the bar while we waited. The place wasn't super crowded at 9pm. We had: 1) Margherita pizza - EXCELLENT EXCELLENT EXCELLENT 2) White pizza w/ Spinach - just ok 3) Deluxe (?) pizza (pepperoni, sausage, mushroom) - pretty good but not as good as the Margherita 4) Meatball pizza - really good. The meatballs were very flavorful. If you like thin crust pizza this is the place to go. Their pizzas also are not made with a lot of tomato sauce. I ate every bit of it. Even my crusts. Definitely will come back here whenever I visit New York again.
Best pizza in NY hands down, and possibly in the world. Â Watching Dom make pies is like watching art.

The baked beans are a must get side item We ordered the pork belly, brisket, ribs, sausage and pulled pork....all of which were delicious. Its not quite like the southern barbecue you can get in the South but I do enjoy Fete Sau's take on barbecue. Â Our favorites were definitely the pork belly and the ribs. The restaurant had a great ambiance about it and was casual. We went on a Wednesday and there was a queue at dinner time however the line moved pretty quickly and you are able to grab a drink at the bar and head back to the line.

Carmine's. Carmine's. Carmine's. Without fail, before today... I loved you. Our affair spans the years. The calamari, the daily special - hello - the chicken Marsala. Usually without fail, you perform expertly. Tonight. Not so much. The service sucked from nearly beginning to end. Sent the special back - it was still Luke warm on the second round. Server: Kris. Yikes! No good. Since when did this turn into a tourist trap?!

This Â is a great place for a date or a nice night out with friends. The service is quick, I never have to wait long. Everything is delicious but I highly recommend the pad see yue. It's the best thing ever and the portions are huge so come with a big appetite. Some cons include: cash only and overcrowding on weekends, however the price and yummy food are worth it. I'd like to thank my boyfriend for taking me here.Also I didn't listen to his suggestion as to what to order. I got something that was also delicious but not as delicious as the pad see yue. Now that is what I order when I visit. So great!

The lamb plate is very flavorful and the addition of the ranch dressing really hoes well. Â The hot sauce is very hot but the ranch help cools it a bit. Â The best thing about this cart is you get a large amount of food for 6 bucks. Â The chicken is ok but I would pass in the future.

I came here on a Saturday night around 8:30pm and it was poppin' aka PACKED WITH A TWO HOUR WAIT. They have this weird space heated tent bar outside which kind of makes this restaurant more run down looking than it already is. Anyway, I don't know if it's because I was exhausted from waiting forever to eat but to me, the pizza was not worth this long wait. If anything, only the dough was very good and this spicy oil they had on the side. I don't think I'll be back with this wait time.

Guilt-free-good-eating is the one word for this place! I'm not vegan or gluten-free but the food here is delicious and so flavorful, I was definitely taken by surprise. What happens when you don't feel bad for eating "healthier" alternatives for food? You overeat. And that's what I sure did! I had a salmon burger along with my brother and we split the vegan lasagna because we were just too curious. A lasagna made of just tofu and eggplant, strange but really not because it was genius! Somehow the lasagna didn't oddly topple over, nor was it bland because the tomato sauce was overflowing with the right aroma and flavor. And because of the tofu, it was almost extremely filling so I now know why one small/medium sized piece counts as one whole entree. By the time we devoured that and struggled through our salmon burgers because the toasted multi-grain bread couldn't handle all that salmon meat, we could barely move. So of course, we wash everything down with some organic drinks - a sweet cider for him, and a chenin blanc wine for me. I was so happy with my meal, I couldn't resist getting a vegan&gluten-free chocolate chip cookie on my way out...and silly me, it was $4! Even with all that food, I wasn't taken by surprise by a painful food coma but rather a full tummy that was stuffed all night till the next morning. Just proves that natural foods make your tummy happier and my tummy would love to venture back to Siggys.

Don't understand the hype. Waited over an hour for lunch on a Saturday. My husband and I ordered the avo tuna and char siu buns to start, the mega ramen for him and the spicy ramen for me, both with added bamboo shoots and egg. The avo tuna didn't seem that fresh, everything was a little grey. Â It was also overly dressed and super salty. The char siu buns were a hot mess- haphazardly thrown together with too much bun for the couple slices of meat. Sadly, the ramen was also disappointing. While the chicken broth was tasty it was not as good as its pork-based brethren. Â The noodles while fresh tasted like al dente spaghetti. Â And although the egg was perfectly cooked, the yolk was cold. In the end, I am glad I tried the place out but I doubt I will go back. Â The food is just not worth it. Sadly, the best part of our meal were the two empanadas and the fruit shake we got around the corner at Empanada Mama while we waited in line. The one good thing going for Totto Ramen is the service-- Â the hostess was super sweet and the service was lightning fast.

Simply amazed by the food at this restaurant! Plus, I had been hyped up about going here, its my sister's favorite place ever, so there was the potential for a HUGE let down. I was not disappointed. Can't wait for another big life event to have someone else take me here! (because its waaaaaay to expensive to pay for myself)

Delicious and cheap. They really do pull the noodles by hand too. The space is dingy and a little run down feeling, but don't let that turn you add as THPN is legit. I've eaten here at least a dozen times and have never been disappointed.

Glad I got to finally try this place. The food is really good. I had the Mediterranean Sea Bass with the lemon potatoes on the side, while my boyfriend had the Kyklades special. We also shared the grilled octopus since everyone was raving about it. The fish was perfectly grilled and flaky. I liked the seasoning, but some people might find it bland. From the special, my favorite was the stuffed crab. The flavors were spot on and it was delicious. The octopus was great too. Overall, I had a good experience here and the waiter was friendly and attentive. I'd definitely go back.

Ate here a week ago and the food was decent but the service ruined the experience. It's a good looking restaurant with a good looking menu. The apps were very delicious (brussle sprouts, croquettes) as were the unwanted desserts. Post-appetizers is when it all went terribly. There was a 20 minute gap between when the first and last entree came out, with no forewarning from the server. No apology either for that matter, the server simply said "you have to wait 15 minutes until it the last dish will be ready". When it still hadn't arrived after 15 minutes, they offered to comp desserts, which appeared to be a nice gesture. However, immediately after ordering two desserts, they quickly brought out a miniature version of a third, unrequested item. It may seem petty to say over yelp, but it played out in a very misleading and unprofessional manner by the server and Bao herself. We ended up being charged for the two desserts we ordered, even though it was stated they would be complementary. They claimed bringing out a third unwanted dessert was their compensating gesture although they never gave us an option to chose the item they brought us. After all of this, we had another issue where one of our ordered desserts was brought well in advance of the other. When the latter dessert finally arrived, it was the wrong item. Again, no apologies. We asked to cancel the order and they said it was too late to do. Still ended up being charged for it. This place could be a great gem, but its poorly managed and poorly executed. I don't like to be harsh, especially when a place is new or shows promise, but there seems to be zero care for the customer at this establishment.

What an amazing latin-fusion brunch. Keep your pants up while looking at my brunch pics please! The bacon wrapped dates, the patatas bravas, the creamy croquettes - all mind-blowingly good. My girlfraaands and I split a few different brunch entrees and all were amazeballs. We had the shrimp brunch entree and the ham and cheese brioche one and everything was fantastic. We also got hooked up with dessert because my friend knows a friends who knows a friend. Dessert was delicious and decadent, just like it should be. Needless to say, I rolled home that day LOL

I'm going to have to echo the wisdom of Peter D. on this one: get two adobada tacos. You may look at the menu and think, wow! carne asada sure sounds good, or, gosh, I'm in the mood for pollo today. It doesn't. You're not. Don't do it. Getting less adobada tacos when you could possibly have more adobada tacos is one of the great tragedies of my yet young life, along with the time that I dropped a fresh warm-out-of-the-oven Oreo brownie on the ground. Get corn tortillas for your tacos, because that's what the cool kids do. Help yourself to the self-serve salsas, but remember: spicy means actually spicy, not gringo spicy. And then perch on some bench in a corner of Chelsea Market and thank your lucky stars that you are eating twice the amount of adobada.

I love Cafe' Gitane! My sister and I eat here nearly every week because it is so well-priced for the quality of the food and wine. Another plus is that the ceviche' salad is amazing and you can hop over to the bar and ballroom at The Jane afterwards for cocktails, which is always a good time (if you aren't there too early).
Have only been there for lunch but the BLT was mighty good!

Don't make the mistake of believing this is super authentic Greek food. It is, however, super delicious cart food. After a lot (A LOT) of meals here, I have settled on the Chicken combo with the works. The rice is buttered up, the chicken is tender, and the food look very messy. Couple points: -- I've tried the lamb, and it just doesn't do it for me. It is heavy, but not particularly juicy, and the edges are done a little weird. -- The food is cheap. Probably $5-8, depending on what you order. -- Avoid lunchtimes (like 12-1) during weekdays. You are just asking for lines. -- I suggest you eat it all -- the food starts to look really weird if you keep it overnight/more than 1 night Â  Â  :-/
It's good and simple, the food is not complicated, very straightforward which is what a lot of restaurants lack these days...but I would not go out of my way to get some pies-n-thighs.

Love this place. I had almost everything on the menu and wasn't disappointed. The vibe is cool, the prices are great, the staff is very friendly. The pickled peppered wings are amazing! Â I wish they served brunch every day. Other then that I highly recommend this place if your looking for a chill spot and some good eats.

Cafe Mono I think I'm in love!! My husband and I went here for a late night dinner after scoping the place out for quite some time. The spot is small, cute and well appointed. The staff is attentive and accommodating. The food.. wow.. soooo good!! We shared 4 dishes and a dessert and everything was amazing!!! We will definitely be back to try more items from the menu!

We came on a Saturday around 1 pm. Pretty large space, they have an outdoor section as well, which is nice when weather permits. Not many people were around, so easy to just walk in and get seated right away. The kitchen and wood-fire ovens are right by the door, so it's a bit of a different set up and the dining area is in the back. Lots of wood and open space. There's also a private bar area that's secluded from the rest of the restaurant. Service is friendly and it's easy to flag someone down if you need anything. The pizzas are good, but just not great. It's definitely not the best Neapolitan around. The quality of the dough isn't as high and the crust isn't cooked well. I'm tired of hearing the line "it's a hot oven, so it has to be burned a bit" when asking for the pizza to be lightly done. The crust does not have to be burned or charred even. It's perfectly possible to pull out the pizza a few seconds before it chars or burns because plenty of Neapolitan places accommodate for that request all the time and do it perfectly. One of the pizzas we actually had to get redone entirely because it was black. Not charred, but just literally the color black around the crust and on the bottom. Granted, they were really nice about it and didn't hesitate to remake it. Of course, this time in a completely exaggerated way so that it was served practically raw. But it's just because they don't have good command over the process, which is really exactly the reason you should go elsewhere if you can. It's not bad food, it's just not a great version of it. I will say, they have some pretty non-standard pizzas, like the sweet apple, which we tried. It has ricotta, apples, brown sugar, bourbon vanilla extract, nutmeg, cinnamon, and butter. It's very heavy and rich, but surprisingly the sweetness is balanced by the ricotta and it can be eaten as a meal and not just a dessert. It's an interesting concept that works out, so if you want something totally different, give it a try.

I have walked by this place many times during brunch hours and is usually full so I thought mmh this should be good... Finally I looked it up on yelp and saw the ok reviews; but I decided to go anyway. Â My brother was visiting and he was in the mood for French food so we decided to go there for brunch on a Saturday. We got there and there were a couple of tables open, the host or manager (not sure, but it was a guy) sat us at a table at the corner. A good 15 minutes passed and our server did not notice us, until I tried to make eye contact with a few people that seemed to work there, and finally our waitress came to our table. Â She took our order and just brought us water when I had asked for coffee also. Â So I had to ask her to please bring us coffee and orange juice like 3 times. The only reason I give this place 3 stars is because of the food. Â I got the croque monsieur and it was AMAZING, if I ever go back will be only because of that dish; although I wonder if I can just take it to go? My brother got eggs, and they were good. CASH ONLY!!! I was pretty disappointed with the service; too bad because this could be a neighbourhood gem.

They oysters "Happy Hour" made getting a donzen oysters not only affordable ($1.50/oyster) but delicious. Â We had the dozen oysters and 2 appetizers (beef tartar & Salt and Pepper Shrimp) and were too full for dessert. Â The Beef Tartar was outstanding and all the extra warm bread they gave went wonderfully with it and the shrimp were perfectly cooked and tasty. Â The wine selection was vast and we were able to find a nice pairing for our meal. I see "good for kids" as an option. Â There were plenty of families with kids at the restaurant but those must've been some rick parents. Â This is not a cheap restaurant and to bring kids there might not be the best for parents on a budget.

Outstanding. I've had some amazing cheese grits in my time but these were hands down the best ever. Â Honey chicken biscuit sandwich is Â a perfect food, sausage gravy smothered chicken biscuit is nearly so, and the beer selection is one of the best in this part of Manhattan.

I must say the Tony salad is awesome! I have been there twice for lunch, last year and this year for a coworkers birthday lunch. There were 6 of us. The food and the service was unbelievable. It is very rare for me to have both great food and the service. Â We had order the Tony salad & Calamari for appetizers. For the main entrees we had chicken marsala, Penne w/Broccoli, Garlic & Oil and the special of that day with chicken. The food was plenty and we had left over for lunch the next day. We can eat, but so much left overs. If you are looking for non so expensive dinner with a big group....go to Tony Di Napoli! Also the ambiance is fascinating too...check out the portrait paintings. Mangia!

Hardly a secret: this Mario Batali spot is excellent. Stick to the pastas and the charcuterie. Enjoy the wines. And try out the Amari, if you're not already familiar. Amaro Nonino is the best place to start.
Obviously an awesome place. Just be prepared to wait, Â Fette Sau is always packed!
i love this place! amazing Udon soup! The vegetables are good too! Definitely try the teriyaki chicken! The service is good too and fast! I used to go all the time there! nice beer too!

Great service, very good food! I would recommend, and the prices are reasonable. I got eggs benedict, it was made like the classic eggs benedict from my childhood. Definitely recommended... very old school diner

While the Famous Brooklyn-based chain has now taken its act to Broadway in Manhattan, the Times Square version has a lot to work on. The place looks fabulous, sporting an outside patio so folks can enjoy a meal outside and a nice interior with beautiful people, great lighting, stylish furniture, and a well dressed staff. The food however, is not impressive, especially the infamous cheesecakes. The cheesecakes were heavy, creamy, and had a texture about them that seemed to indicate they weren't as fresh. The sandwiches seemed quite large, but nothing different than any other chain TimesSquare restaurant ala TGI Friday's or Applebees. The prices are a bit high for diner wannabe food but the setting is Times Square, hence, it may seem cheap compared to other restaurants in the area. Service was all over the place, with food runners and wait staff bustling back and forth, however, our waiter had ignored us for most of the night. He got some extra tip when he decided to hook us up with a free piece of cheesecake because they had run out of a few other types that we wanted. All and all, this place is no better than the other corporate chains that sport their niche in the food world and their niche (cheesecakes) is unfortunately nothing to write home about.

I am extremely happy to have visited such an amazing restaurant. Not only was the service great but everything we ordered from appetizers to dessert was exquisite. It was my first time there as well as my first date with my significant other and it was the best place we had ever visited hands down. The enviornment was beautiful, classy, romantic and if your into jazz then you will enjoy it themore, that was the cherry on top! We had spinach dip for appetizer, first entree was spicy tuna roll sushi and another tuna sushi with a japanese name. Second entree was Filet mignon with mashed potatoes and brocolli and crab cakes with cole slaw and french fries. Dessert was the apple pecan pie, which was so delicious! Anywho, I loved the waiter, the food, the food presentation and the enviornment. We will definately go back.

I'm struggling to find many ways you could better this concept. Anything associated with the (still?) controversial Jane Hotel seems to receive some dirt by association, but as an outsider enjoying a weekend in New York, I was very impressed by this little cafe. Â Confident on it's own, yet a charming compliment to it's adjacent historic hotel. The atmosphere, menu and concept are well thought out and confidently executed. Â This same confidence, however, might be the catalyst for the slightly below par service. Â  Everything I saw at Cafe Gitane screamed "me" and I'm wondering if this is the affect it has on everyone one of it's patrons. Â It was filled with a very hip crowd that seemed more like neighborhood regulars hanging out than people wanting to be seen or fit in at a flash-in-the-pan hot-spot. Â A record player sits on the bar, spinning vinyl LPs of Belle & Sebastien and the like. Â  Flatware is adorable & elegant. Â Adorable waitresses sported adorable mint green shift dresses and painted their under-manicured nails an opaque mint to match. Every server there seems to be the young, hip, indie girl that makes knitting cool and reads Martha Stewart's advice on being a sixties-esque modern housewife and host that i want to marry but never will. Â They seem such an intrinsic part of the ambience, giving you the impression that they hand-picked the dishes and checked seersucker napkins out their selves. The problem is that we weren't greeted when we entered... and were confused as to whether we should seat ourselves or not. Â Did not get our waters till after our food had arrived and had to ask another waitress for our check. Â Were we discriminated against because they figured we weren't locals? Â This took a star off the rating. Â If i returned and the service was just as humdrum (adorable and cute though it may be) it would not bring me back a third time. Â The frustrating thing is that the vibe we got was this is what they wanted. The warm ambience made us want to be their friends and hang out... how could my warm nature not compell them to reciprocate? Food was excellent. Â French Morrocan... don't ask me exactly what it means, but it was all very coherent and good. Â  I had the smoked trout salad, my girlfriend, the orange blossom waffle. Â We were fighting with our adorable flatware over each other's adorable entrees. Â Her mint iced tea was so RIDICULOUSLY refreshing that I ordered one for each of us to go. Â The fruit salad was... a fruit salad. Great, poised, comfortable, hip, little cafe that seems it could, indeed stand the test of time. Â I would like to see the service a little warmer or i'll fight the urge to return.

I've had this place bookmarked for the longest time, and I was finally able to visit this past week. There are many pros to this tiny wine bar, but the number one being how engaged the owner is with the place and the customers. She clearly had a vision of what she wanted the place to be like and has completely "nailed it!" The menu is not extensive but everything is organic and truly delicious. Service is fast... Maybe because there aren't many tables to keep up with. I ordered a sangria thinking it's a wine bar/ tapas place and it should be good, but unfortunately it was watered down, and they filled half a glass with sangria, and half of that was fruit. I got two sips of water with fruit and a drop of wine.. But I guess that was a good thing. I'm sure it was a one-off and it will be better next time. They don't serve any soda since "Heidi thinks it's the devil" how awesome!! I love it even more since it's a short walk from my apartment. Will be back for sure.
This place is no-joke DELICIOUS. Just amazing.
Excellent service from the servers and the food is delicious. The hostess is polite and welcome. Professionally run overall, would Â come back again..

At 6PM on a Thursday night, the wait for a table of two was just under an hour. And though I usually shrug off any wait longer than 20 minutes, I'm happy that the boyfriend and I parked our butts on a small bench outside and waited. The tapas proved to be some of the more innovative we've had in a while, and we'd return. The restaurant is on the narrow side and nearly half of the space is taken up by the bar. This translated into seating that isn't really the most comfortable: if you are not sitting at a packed bar, bordered on one side by a line of people waiting, then you are seated at tall stools, with your feet dangling, at tiny tables against a wall. There is a private dining area in the back for larger parties, and a table (or two?) for 4-6 people-- but ultimately, this place is very much a tapas "bar." Still, crowded, noisy, and hot (there's a somewhat open kitchen) are all part of the festive experience, and are nothing that a little wine can't mediate. While I can't say so much for our waitress, the hostess was extremely friendly. So friendly that-- oh, wait, was she hitting on my boyfriend??? She greeted patrons with a smile, never giving that better-than-thou attitude that so many hostesses adopt at a crowded hotspot. Always warm and (a little too!!!!) friendly, she definitely set the atmosphere for the night. Unfortunately, our waitress did not have the same luxury. I don't think there was one point during the night that she was not running around. Service thus suffered, that though serviceable, was a little harried. We started with a pitcher of red wine sangria, strong and not-too-sweet. The menu is separated into hot and cold plates, along with a variety of cheeses and desserts. Patanas bravas were sufficiently spicy, and the croquettes were delicious. One of my favorite plates was the crispy fish, that though somewhat unappetizing in presentation, were explosive with flavor. The paquetitots with jamon Serrano, artichoke, and manchego were the highlight of the night. It came with three pieces and the boyfriend and I actually fought over the last one! The chorizo con chocolat that everyone raves about was interesting but not to my taste. I found the toasted bread it was served on to be too hard--almost painful, in fact. The tuna stuffed with marinated white anchovies was also a big miss, and I would pass on this for something on the specials list. We also had their house cheese plate to end our meal, and while the valdeon was superior, the manchego was stale. Â  I caution that plates are extremely small. Everything really is just a "taste," which probably makes Tia Pol better for dates than a group. Prices do add up. I can't recall what else we ordered but I do remember the bill being a little on the extravagant side. Of course, the real raison d'etre to try out or even return to Tia Pol is the dessert. The leches fritas, fried milk with drunken cherries, were amaaaazing and something I still think about today! Warm, custardy, fried packages that were simultaneously sweet and sour, they were the perfect, luxurious ending to our meal. I would not hesitate to return just for a glass of wine and dessert at the bar--provided the wait isn't too long.

I was pleasantly surprised. The cocktails and wine menu were above avg.The food absolutely lived up to the hype. We ordered from the pre fixe in the tavern and I have to say, the shrimp was out of control. I would probably skip the fish next time and opt for the mushroom lasagna b/c others are raving about it on here. My bf had the lamb ragu and the porkchop and really enjoyed it. The crowd was a little difficult to define, however I'd definitely go back. Service was impeccable.

Went here for a Sunday brunch and had to wait about 30 mins. First thing that hits you when you enter...the whiff of butter. Wow, love it. Â The place is small but charming and the crowd was a little on the upscale side. I went with 2 single buddies and there was a lot of eye candy there for them. I digress. When we sat down, we ordered the salmon Benedict, waffles, chocolate croissant, and coffee. The coffee was amazing, best I've had in the city. The waffle was good but the buttery chocolate croissant was out of this world good. We ordered a 2nd one. Service was standard but the food was great. Â One of the better brunch places in the city.

By far one of the most authentic Turkish restaurants in the city, complete with a knowledgeable staff and Efes beer. Â  Warmly lit with candles, the first floor is cozy and romantic, while the second floor is more apt to crowds and parties. Â A big neighborhood spot, regulars crowd the bar and seem to know the maitre de and hostess on a first name basis. Â Indeed, they will both recognize you after your first visit here. The vegetarian platter is a sampling of various Mediterranean cuisines, served with traditional Turkish bread still warm from the oven. Â The kebobs are cooked to perfection, but the real winner is the branzino fish served with a side salad and warm lemon dressing. Â If you are lucky, you may be able to get one of the gracious waiters to de-bone your fresh catch table side. Definitely worth a visit, especially if you can't make it to Istanbul!

Might be my favorite restaurant in NYC. Great atmosphere - good for a group, good for a date, good for just about anything except a business meeting. Get the homemade pasta. It's not fancy and the dishes are not necessarily complicated, it's just solid, unpretentious, fresh, delicious food. I'm obsessed with the artichoke salad and the caprese always seems to taste better here than other places. Cash only, very intimate.

Love , love, love Brickyard! The staff, service, food, drinks, ambiance, are all excellent. They have a great bar scene in the front and a cozy, more relaxed dining area in the back. Perfect for any occasion and would highly recommend this gastropub. This is definitely in my top 5 favorite places to drink/eat in the city!

Love this place. I eat here at least once every 2-3 weeks, and order delivery also. The food and service is consistently great. I love the tomato soup, the avocado and goat cheese sandwich, and the chicken entree. Brunch can get a little crazy because the whole village eats here, but other than the wait for brunch, this place can't get any better.

Service - 1 star Vegetarian options/food - 2 star Ambiance - 3 stars Uniqueness - 4 stars I am averaging it to 3 stars but service was painful. From not having cutlery or water, to our wine being mixed up, and waiting forEVER to receive the check, service was so bad that it ruined the rest of the experience.

went for brunch with my fellow yoginis after class today. ordered the feta, spinach, kalamata olive omelette. delicious fluffy omelette with perfect proportion of ingredients. as usual, the roasted potatoes rocked (possibly the best roasted potatoes in the city). shared chocolate cake for dessert. their whipped cream is special. orlin has one of the better brunches in the city. i've been coming here for over 10 years and the quality has remained consistently good thru-out, which is why i'm giving them 5 stars. they have great sandwiches and the dinner entrees are solid. the prices are very reasonable, too. great low-ceilinged, exposed brick wall interior.

Totally mediocre. Â This was my third attempt at brunch. Â The first two times, I thought that I must have gotten the wrong thing. Â This time, I blame them. Â Got a curry chicken salad sandwich with fries. Â I make roast chicken at home quite a bit, and make chicken salad with the leftover bits. Â It's a way to make sure that nothing goes to waste. Â Good when I do it at home, but for $14 at a restaurant, they need to give you the prime meat, not the left over gristle and bits of wing meat they didn't serve last night. Â But that's just what this was == bathed in a salty mayo with an oil slick of tinned Thai curry hanging out in only one corner of the pita. Â I looked at the plate thinking, they charge money for this? Â Fries were okay, but not as good as the average diner. Â I'd give it one star, but the server was nice, and the place is pleasant inside even if we were jammed up against the next table.

The place is really cool, one of the more unique restaurants I've seen. I'm giving my two star rating solely based on one dish, as a cautionary tale to vegetarians eating here. The dish in question is the veggie burger (18$) The burger itself tasted like clay and had barely been cooked. It was very unpleasant I opted for the kale side (which adds $2) which was raw, and hadn't been softened as someone experienced with kale so it doesn't taste like leaves. Â  Both my dining companions has the filet mignon and we're pleased. So if you're coming here as a vegetarian, order something other than the burger, or eat before you come The service was friendly The place was hopping The venue was really standout

Nice dining experience. We had the tasting menu with paired wines. The menu was heavily slanted towards seafood....which was disappointing. The quantities were very limited...even for a tasting menu. The restaurant is small..20 seats...which was fun. The food was good but very little...."I cannot wait to come back entrees". With all the restaurants in NYC I would recommend others!
OVERRATED! OVERRATED! Sad face. Service was magnificent, though.

Oh that damn corn! It IS the BEST!!! Yummm! Â I never knew that you could make corn on the cob taste sooooo goooood. You can almost make a whole meal out of that corn. Don't forget to squeeze some lime on it. Your dreams will be filled with corn! The place gets overcrowded. So you may find yourself waiting for a seat outside. It's worth the wait.

Came here on a sunday night with friends for food & drinks. The price was very reasonable and it uses an open type of seating so you get to enjoy the view and experience the outdoorsy feel. But the food was not outstanding, wine selections were not large either. i got the House-made Pappardelle which was a bit blend and tasteless. I guess it's just not my type of pasta. I really like the Truffled Creamy Polenta my friends got. that was really good and the Orecchiette was good too!

We stayed in NYC for a few days and didn't find this place until our 2nd last day. I wish we knew about them earlier as they had great pancakes. My daughter who's very picky loves their pancakes. Great food, service and value. Its a very small seating area (around 10 people) but worth the wait.
Pizza is awesome, get anything with the Mike's hot honey on it, including the ice cream sundae. Also buy a bottle to take home! Â It's everything I want in a pizza and more. I wish I lived closer.

I ordered the artichoke slice and while I loved the creamy cheese and artichoke, I found the crust to be too thick and a bit soggy on some parts...so I was a bit disappointed. There's a bit of a line when I went but it moves fast.

Habana is a great place to grab a drink outside and we have been going for years. Our go-to meal is corn and a Cuban sandwich with (cheap) beers. It's also really great for families, with lots of space for kids to play or to park the stroller and weekday activities. But, surprisingly there is NO changing table, which can be difficult if you need one in their small bathroom! On really nice, warm days it can be hard to find a place to sit, but weeknights in the early fall are generally not crowded and chill.

This place is absolutely on point. Â Food is really precisely made, nicely plated. Â Flavors are pretty good, and considering the outside view of the storefront, the inside and decor is pretty solid. Â Service also matches. Â Really a 5-star for the category it is: simple, clean local Thai restaurant (this is NOT where you go as a jumpoff (pre-going-out) spot.

I can't complain or add anything other than the crab meat soup dumplings were "the bomb." This place never disappoints every time I come to JSR! The new hostess was much more professional and courteous. She even said thank you as we walked out the door. It was a nice pleasant surprise.

my family and i went there after hearing so much hype about the place. we ordered a large pizza with olives, sun dried tomatoes, sausage, and mushroom. it was both terrible and awesome. i've never had such salty olives before. maybe i'm just not familiar with real italian olives. but that pretty much ruined our pizza. the sun dried tomatoes just tasted like soggy tomatoes and not the bright strong flavors i would usually expect. the sausage was very mediocre as well. but the mushroom tasted like mushrooms so i guess that's good. but all the pizza around the toppings was pretty good! the cheese was delicious and the dough was tasty. but yeah the sheer amount of crappy toppings could not overcome the delicious crust. maybe you should just get a cheese pizza? NOTE: there is only one bathroom and it's pretty nasty. so yeah...
Working in the area, this place is always busy and always fresh. Â Compared to all the other food carts, Halal Guys are waaay better than everyone else. Â Taste is great and sauces are incredible.
Nice new American meal - and great bar.

I personally really liked this place, and had high hopes considering this is the sister restaurant to Traif. We did the prix fixe menu here and had around 10 different dishes, some more unique and appealing than others, but all in all quite delicious. Everyone raved about the carrots, and while unique, I didn't feel like it was anything special in terms of taste. My only bit of sadness here is that I would've sworn that this would've hit the spot for my boyfriend, seeing as he LOVESSSS Traif and loves Mexican, but this just didn't have enough Mexican, or Latin notes to their dishes. It was still, at the end of the day, very New American and Traif-like, which, for me, is still fab.

I love pickles. I love pickle backs. I love pickles so much, I actually have been making my own pickles for over 3 years now. Enter Jacob's Pickles, sounds like the best place for a pickle lover right? We stroll over to meet another couple for brunch one morning and we wait about an hour for a table - which is typical of NYC on a Sunday morning. We're seated and we order. This is where it gets complicated, I wish the waitress had told us about portions - they are HUGE - like Claim Jumper's huge. I just couldn't. We ended up dumping a lot of food. Minus 1 star. The pickles. Sigh. Not great, my homemade ones are better. Minus another star.
Heaven on earth! I love to go there and just walk around and look at all the amazing products. Their cheeses, meats, fish, fresh pastas... Everything is amazing!
Took some out of towners here for dessert after a Broadway show because it was nearby. The place is fine, just nothing special. Good for kids, bad for people who know cheesecake :-)

Went to Print for my birthday celebration, and I have to say I was thoroughly impressed! From the sustainable "farm-to-table" theme, to the classiness and helpfulness of the staff, to the food itself, I was extremely pleased with Print. It is also attached to a really cool rooftop bar if that's your sort of thing. If you're into blood orange (that's their go-to fruit of the moment), this is the place for you!
Only been open for 7 months and they have a lot of customers. The small menu and personable staff make the experience comfortable with an affordable menu. The knock is the food took 20+ minutes.

Wanted the oxtail ragu but they were out, so I ordered the steak instead. Yet again, a meal destroyed by recommendation. Funny thing was that the one person who stayed vegetarian was perfectly content. Somehow, the chef managed to screw up the steak, the fish and the pork. Not coming back.
Wow!! Amazing middle eastern food My friend recommend this place so me and my boyfriend went there And we definitely enjoyed it! The food is great the service is quick. We will definitely come back!
Went for brunch, and thought the food was fantastic. Bloody Mary's were delicious, and the overall vibe of the place was great. Would recommend for brunch or for a date for dinner!

I liked the food here, but I wasn't a huge fan. They have some specialty brews by the bottle, and as others have mentioned, there is a $15 all you can drink beer option. I ordered a can of stout. Was good. Can't remember the brand, it was some kind of microbrew. Shared a few dishes: pig's jowl (gellatinous texture, tasty if you're into it; I like it, but not sure it's everyone's taste), quail adobo (best dish of the night; very well seasoned, cooked nicely), curry noodles (slow heat that builds; didn't realize it was quite that spicy and I was glad to have my glass of stout handy), a crispy pata (roast pork) dish (unmemorable, came with a liver pate that was good), and a beef dish (unmemorable, was a bit dry). everything was tasty, but nothing I would really crave after having it. coconut rice was overcooked and slightly too mushy for my taste. Didn't have any of the desserts; a filipino friend we were eating with had tried two options in a previous meal and didn't like their version of the halo halo, so we went elsewhere for sweets.

friendly staff, cute kitch, lots of long beards, heavy metal, $3.00 PBRs, I can't say it was without charm, but the BURGER WAS DISGUSTING. Â I asked for it well done and the bartender--friendly as can be--said "it only comes one way." Â I asked what way was that? Â He said they serve 2 thin patties stacked on top of each other. Â He promised they were delicious, though. Â I almost walked out but he looked SO sincere. Â I thought, well, if they're thin patties they will probably be at least medium. Â WRONG. Â Fried on the outside, bloody and cold on the inside. Â Really vile if you don't like that sort of thing. Â I will say, though, the place was packed and everyone seemed to be having a good time so if you don't feel like drinking at home, it is a viable option. Â Just eat first.

Formerly Bistro Lafayette. This new incarnation of the Clinton-Stuy eatery is immensely better! I ordered delivery so I can't speak for the ambiance or servers but I can definitely say that the person taking my order was pleasant and the food arrived within 30-40 minutes. I got the cajun catfish sandwich - DELISH. My BF got it as a wrap - dually yummy! Keep up the good work!!!

Cute, very charming place. Â Small, no lines. Â Quiet section of Alphabet City. Â Cute staff. Â The noodle texture was perfect, the toppings delicious. Â However, the ramen broth was just too thick...in mouth feel and in seasoning level. Â The seasoning was delicious at first, but halfway through the bowl, we were on salt overload. Â We spent the rest of the day trying to re-hydrate, trying to cure ourselves of our salt-induced cotton mouths...which then resulted in our salt-water-bloated bellies.

for the longest time i didn't know what the hell a macaron was. all i knew was that the gossip girl characters always had them around . . . and, wow . . . the color of those macarons! how could any girly girl resist? needless to say, when i discovered that this NYC laduree location was the only laduree store in the u.s., i knew i just had to visit and experience this gem! i went on a random weekday after work, about 30 minutes before close. and, of course there was a line. although, this line was inside as opposed to outside (which was the case when i'd walk by on weekends). i stood in line as other patrons oo'ed and ahh'd at the delightful colors, deciding which flavors to get. i patiently waited, wondering if there would be enough macarons in the flavors i wanted to try! but, no worries . . . as the chic laduree attendants brought out more trays of those delectable goodies! ample supply, my friends. i hardly remember all of the flavors i picked out as my visit was long ago. but, my favorite was defniitely the pistachio. i also tried cherry blossom, caramel with salted butter, rose, and vanilla. these are VERY sweet concoctions, but they are still so enjoyable. crispy outside, gooey inside. and, i love how specific the flavor profiles are. they are boldly angelic tastes. these will forever be the gold standard of macarons and as such, i am afraid to try others as they will probably pale in comparison. needless to say, if you're in NYC and you've a moment (or several, if you're here on a weekend), then stop by laduree for an exquisite parisian experience.

What a great spot. Â I'd give this 5 stars, but I'm trying not to be a star whore. By way of bias disclosure, this is just the kind of place that I like. Â Relaxed, casual, yet passionate. Â Everyone was passionate, passion about the food, passion about the drinks. Â Passion right down to the tunes they played. I ate at the bar and was greeting by an extremely professional and extremely friendly bartender. Â She knew her drinks and she knew the menu very well. Â She also had plenty of good food/wine matching tips. Â Not to mention just being really nice generally. I started with the hen of the woods with a mushroom puree, kohlrabi and pickled hon shimeji. Â I thought the idea of this dish was really genious, particularly combining mushrooms with a mushroom puree. Â I've already copied the idea in my home kitchen - imitation being the highest form of flatery, need I say more. Â The textures and flavors worked really well together. Then I had the octopus with onion puree, faro and broccoli. Â It was perfectly balanced, particularly that little touch of heat from the harissa. Â The octopus was tender, although I prefer it when it has slightly charred crust. I would definitely go back here. Â Great atmosphere and food.

Honestly, the best guacamole I have ever had! So yummy! Their taquitos were really good too. The pork one may have been better than the chicken. I had the shrimp quesadilla as a main and it was great also. Can't wait to go back.
Excellent. But Grimaldi's has it beat.

Very fun place to go -- great food, great drinks at decent prices. Definitely crowded and the wait for a table seems crazy (I have a friend who works there that helps out on this) but the hour or two it takes to get seated can easily be spent at the bar. Definitely recommend.

Impeccable service.The staff are all very pleasant and know what they are talking about. Our waiter was really sweet, recommended amazing wines & chesse spreads that were fantastic. Glad my friend & I got there for the happy hour Flights..... Let's just say I flew away :) and dinner was marvelous.
Nice crowd. Nice atmosphere! Good times. Not sure about the prices...I didn't pay.

3 months after my visit I'm finally writing this review. So I visited Joe's Shanghai on my 2nd trip to NY (Feb). Came here Sunday for lunch and the wait was about 30 mins. I guess it's not bad compared to how many people was there. Xiao Long Bao (crab meat) - skin is too thick but the fillings were good and juicy. Xiao Long Bao (regular) - skin is thick too and the fillings were not as good as compared to the crab meat ones and it was also juicy. Shanghai Fried Rice Cake - It was good but I've had better. Shanghai Fried Noodle - also pretty good I would come back here again for their Xiao Long Bao but just wished their skin could be as thin as Din Tai Fung's. Price here is a lot cheaper than Din Tai Fung's tho.

I was probably expecting too much, but still it was so disappointing. I had been craving for the good sushi for months, so I made a reservation here after many research. One of my foodie friend told me that this place is no longer good, but I ignored that....and I really should've not.... We ordered Omakase and specially told the waiter we like special parts. I know Omakase is a chef choice, but I thought Omakase is also a conversation between chef and customers. However, what they brought was really plain fishes, pretty bad presentation, and most of all taste was just okay. I couldn't believe that the taste was just okay. When you are paying average more than 8bucks per that piece of sushi, I am expecting more than that. The way of sushi made and rice were good, and the fish was fresh (except Uni).
