But freshness does not always mean good fish. Other than Fatty tuna, they didn't really have taste, like no taste. It is not because I don't know what fish taste like. I've been eating sushi and sashimi since I was kid, and my family loves sashimi from white fish. I kept praying that next sushi will be better. I even tried to brainwash myself that this place is good. But after I had Uni which is my favorite normally, I just gave up. After all those no taste sushi, Uni showed me one strong taste. It was bad and stinky. I think the atmosphere and service quality are great, but no point without good taste. The reason that I give 2 stars is because of Uni and not worth the price. Otherwise, I think it's 3.5 stars. Definitely skillful sushi. Anyway I don't know if I should not expect too much from sushi in US, or the restaurant had a bad day. I was very sad.

3.5 stars. I came here for dinner with a couple of friends after a long day. All I wanted to do was have some good food and this place did not disappoint. We were started off with some bacon popcorn, would've been really good if it could've been a little less salty. After getting started with that, everything was on the salty side. We ordered the foie gras, pork belly, Korean bbq wraps and cu-buns. I really like the foie gras because the way it melted in my mouth went great with the tangerine. I definitely recommend it. Thought the cu-buns were pretty good too. They also have an extensive beer menu, goes great with the food. There's kind of a hipster vibe, like a restaurant out of Williamsburg or something. Overall, a good place to grab a bite!

I went here on a first date about a year ago. ive never been to a restaurant like this before than, and didnt really know what to expect. It was a small cozy place, only a few tables. Paper menu, which my date commended because it means they change the menu often, i guess according to season. I ordered the porkloin medium, with a spicy carrot puree. it was so delicious. i can still taste it a year later. This was the restaurant that turned me on to REAL food.

A small place with a crowd at all times, but worth the wait! Their ricotta pancakes were sweet, but very heavy...in the sense that the pancakes were not the fluffy texture that I'm used to and prefer in my pancakes. Â These pancakes felt quite dough-y. Â The honeycomb butter is everything though. Truffle fries are so good and stayed crispy even towards the end of the meal...I could eat these forever. Â It's like a bad habit and similar to the way I approach tortilla chips and salsa. Â Can't Stop, Won't Stop. I also had the Gem Lettuces salad which was also really flavorful and somewhat of a reprieve from the Five Leaves burger I also had. Â Overall great meal.
This French Bistro is a true original. A true "New York" culinary experience. Walking in the door is like walking back in time. The food is always great. Open for Breakfast, Brunch or Dinner.

After the first line of this review you'll know why it's excellent all around Bacon fat popped popcorn, amazing! Â And that just the starter The trooter is excellent, to satire its the most succulent pig's feet burger ever, before you say "pig's feet?!?!?" yes, it is just that, but imagine the most succulent pulled pork, chopped an grilled as a burger, that what this was excellent as well! The ox tail is also incredible, with the onion reduction its a little cube of goodness, Korean BBQ wraps are great as err the mussels, all and all a great place, a gem of the neighborhood

Party Bowl: I love how the party bowl sushi pieces were circular as opposed to the usual rectangular shape. The challenge with the circular shape is that the sushi pieces had more rice than fish. Pork Betty: The housemade pork betty on the other hand was delicious and is definitely my favorite part of the meal. Get it with the egg. It will be worth it.
I come here just for their bloody mary's. Â  The food is good here too, but the bloody mary's are as good as it gets.

Dear 53rd and 6th Halal Cart, Please move to Seattle. I dream of eating another tasty lamb gyro on a street corner in the freezing cold. I don't care if it makes a huge mess and drips all over my yoga pants. Maybe some day I will be able to experience another HUGE chicken/lamb and rice plate with delicious sauces and soft pita bread. Mmmm....... Until then, I will dream of you. Thanks for the memories. xoxo, Midge

Went here last week for brisket and collards. 5 stars for brisket, 5 stars for service, 2 stars for greens. It seems silly to have another BBQ place within walking distance of Dinosaur, but if you don't feel like waiting for two hours, this is a good option!

Great combos and the line is still really busy at 2pm but not out the door (on a freezing cold day). Ribs, brisket, and pulled pork were really good. I would definitely try the chicken next time (after seeing the person in front of us order it). The meat is great, the coleslaw, pickles, and onions that came with it were really good. We also got the yam with walnuts and also got the beans.

The beer here was incredibly good. I came away with a new appreciation of imperial porters. I'm not sure that I would make it my regular place due to the space being too small. Everyone bumped into everyone on the way out (including the over-indulged guided out by their surprisingly patient friends). But I had a good time and it fit my mood! Also, the doorman (at least last night) was awesome!

I'm still salivating for this lobster roll nearly 6 hours after eating it... The lobster roll looks a bit small initially but Â it's larger than the one at Pearl Oyster Bar (also it's much cheaper!) The bun is a thick roll brushed with butter and heated on the grill. The lobster used for the roll is fresh, in giant chunks and delicately mixed with just the right amount of mayo. It's then topped with some chopped scallions and a dash of some spice (that didn't contribute much to the taste, IMO, but did look aesthetically pleasing). Amazing :]

8:30 PM reservation for four after a Yelp Elite event on a extremely Cold,dreary and rainy Tuesday evening in the last week of October. I have read much about La Sirene from my fellow Yelpers and although I was excited I managed to curb my enthusiasm. Â The location of the restaurant is literally a block away from the Holland Tunnel, meaning unless you have heard about this place you most likely will never know of its existence and I must say after having had the opportunity to experience La Sirene, I am glad I am able to share in the knowledge of its existence. Very small place, fits maybe 16+ people, but very comfortable and cozy like a old world cafe. Â We were greeted with smiles by the owner Didier and a very cordial hostess, I should've asked for her name. Â They kindly checked out coats in for us. After reviewing the menu here is what was ordered. Appetizer: - Escargots a la Bourguignone - Half dozen roasted escargots in butter and garlic sauce - Moules Rochelaises - Mussels cooked with curry, diced apples and light cream There was also a small appetizer dish with four items, carrot puree, eggplant, squash and au gratin. Â Although they were all good, my favorite was definitely the squash followed by the carrot purÃ©e. The escargots was very good. Â The mussels were fantastic, very balanced taste where the curry wasn't too overpowering as curry usually is. Â This is my first experience with a curry dish at a French restaurant and I was impressed. Entrees: - Magret de Canard Poele Sauce Montmorency - Duck breast with Cherry, Port and Red Wine Sauce. - c'est magnifique! - Onglet PoÃªlÃ© Ã  la Facon Luchonaise (Medium) - Seared Hanger steak thinly sliced covered with a Roasted Garlic and Parsley Sauce. Â The steak was so tender, juicy and flavorful. Dessert: - CrÃ¨me BrulÃ©e - One of the best I have ever tasted, light and airy yet flavorful. Although the food was very delicious La Sirene would've garnered a 4 star ranking from me, but with such attention to his customers' satisfaction and happiness that Didier exudes and with such love and passion for what he does, La Sirene is deserving of nothing less than 5 stars. Â An experience that highly recommend. Cash only! You can reserve through La Sirene website. Verdict: Â As good as it gets!

This place is so so. I'd give it 2 1/2 stars. It's annoying if you are trying to go with a large group. They don't take reservations. We had a group of about 12 tonight. Not everyone was there right at 7. A few cane later. Â They told my friend they wouldn't give us a table until everyone was there. That sat us separately as 2 tables in the upstairs room above the kitchen. Room was spacious compared to the regular dining room. Our tables weren't near each other so we waited until a nearby table left. Then they let us move closer to our friends. Star for that. Pizza in my opinion was just ok. Good crust...that's partly because NYC has good water. Sauce was kinda meh...like they opened a can and poured it out. No spices or flavor. Cheese and toppings were fine. Our group ordered tomato and mushrooms on one and sausage and peppers on the others. 3.00 for every topping seemed a bit steep.
Great imported italian ingredients for super fabulous panini. Atmosphere like a typical european bar.

Interesting. If you have had a stressful day at work with the fellas and you want to go someplace and feel like your hard earned dollar really equates to you being a cultured debutante...head here with your work chums. Whiskey out the ears. You'll have so many whiskey options it'll remind you of your drunken co-ed days. You know, dancing on tables, hot-wiring cop cars, needing your stomach pumped. Just kidding. My how far we have come! Just sip and enjoy. You know, swirl the whiskey around in your glass. No one else knows what they're doing. Fake it til you make it! But seriously, so many whiskey options. Who knew? I liked their mixed drinks. I got the Jamaican Ting. It was great. They also had hot toddy, which smelled amazing. The small plates were interesting. I didn't think they were anything to write home about (maybe because my mind was going WHISKEY WHISKEY SOPHOMORE YEAR OH NO)...they were interesting, but seemed to dig into every culinary trend out there right now. The beef tartare was good. But what girl can say no to a huge plate of raw meat, wink wink. Ahem, sorry (told you sophomore year was crazy jk jk jk). The poached egg with grits was tasty. We were all devouring those free biscuits that they kept bringing over. Now those were delicious. Eat about 3 of those per whiskey drink and then say goodbye to any possibility of a hangover. Smoke a cigar outside of this place and you'll pretty much exude Dick Tracey confidence and panache. Honestly, I'm not sure if this place really appeals to chicks. I don't know many girls that like whiskey. However, again, if you want a boys night out, this is the place!

Was psyched to try Clinton's on a Wednesday evening when it was not busy at all. Their famous Maine blueberry pancakes with maple syrup was so delicious! As the little girl from Despicable Me saids "IT'S SO FLUFFY I'M GONNA DIE"!! I liked their version of the chicken and waffles, but it was not the best I have tried. I prefer Amy Ruth's. Their black and white milkshake was delicious as well. If you are desperate to try Clinton's famous pancakes, come on a weekday. Don't even bother going during brunch hours on the weekends.
What was ordered and how I rank it. Â  Â Steak n Eggs, Pork Belly, Halibut & Scallops Risotto. In that order. Delish!

Amazing BBQ!!!!!!! Â Knocked the rating from a 5 to a 4 because my spare ribs were not consistent. Â  Food: (4/5) Spare ribs were great. Â I ordered the meal and got 1/3 of a rack. Â A couple ribs were moist and perfection, a couple were a bit dry. Â The baked burnt beans were great to try, I'm not a baked bean person so I won't order again but they were tasty. Â BBQ sauce in the middle of the table was so good. Â I drenched my Decor (5/5) plenty of seating and the BBQ smell is heaven. Â We went on opening day (60 degrees and sunny) they had the store front open, created such a great outdoorsy vibe. Â  Service: (5/5) Super Friendly

Brunch at Traif was exactly what I hope for, a delicious retreat from the chaos of NYC. Â Service was friendly, helpful, and knowledgeable. Â Food was inventive without over complicating classic dishes. Â Great Bloody Marys , yummy salad with Gorgonzola flakes, and infantilizing egg sliders to name a few. Â I will definitely be back.

Although this restaurant chain has been featured on cooking shows for their dumplings, this particular location is overrated. The minimum wait on a weekday is over half an hour, and the service is terrible. Â What's worse, those waiting in line hover over your table and overtly drool over your meal. Tasty. Insult to injury after the wait was the fact that there are only two choices of dumplings. My suggestion is to find another dumpling place that actually has more variety. Chinatown has too many options, and one shouldn't feel compelled to go to this one.

I live right around the corner, and Bedouin Tent is my jam. Everything is always super fresh and tasty, and the portions are large enough that I usually save some for a second meal. If I happen to be craving Bedouin Tent on a weekend, I'll opt for the Chicken Ouzi (available Friday night - Sunday night, for some reason), which is a huge, wonderful combo of chicken, rice, veggies, almonds and raisins, baked into phyllo dough. Otherwise, I get the assorted salad platter (with an extra pita). I get the beet salad, the chickpea/spinach combo, hummus, and two servings of labna, which is a tart yogurt that tastes almost like the smoothest, tangiest, creamiest cheese-like thing ever... it's hard to describe, but GOODNESS it's addictively wonderful. So much food for so little money; can't complain at all. The takeout guys are always super nice too. I did eat in the other night, and the service wasn't super attentive, but it didn't bother me too much. The only objection I really had was that I ordered Loomi, a drink made with black limes that tastes almost like very citrus-y tea. The waiter insisted that I try it before he would let me order it, and he brought a small sample in a Dixie cup. That's all well and good, but he didn't return to ask if I would want to actually order it (which I still did), so I spent awhile trying to flag him down to get him to bring it. I didn't get it until more than halfway through my meal, which kinda sucked. But hey, nitpicking. If you want to order it, just insist, I guess. Oh, and cash only!

Stopped off here for a drink before heading over to Perry Street for dinner [by the way AMAZING FOOD & DRINKS!!!], very charming place they serve beer & wines only. I ordered the Pinot Grigio which was just OK but it was cold and that pretty much matter the most...nothing worse than having a warm white wine UGH! If you get the 2 seats in the front window be prepared b/c you will get a lot of smoke in your face. I'd go back again to check out the beer selections was too crowed to hear or see all that was there.

Cafe Katja...as if this place needs another glowing review. So cute, so quaint, and the service is so friendly! The food is delish. The spatzle...ohhh lord, the spatzle. Hands down best I have ever had. I still dream about it sometimes. I also had the beef goulash and it was so tender and lovely, I was very sad to see some left on my plate, but I was SO full. Boyfriend had the bacon wrapped pork loin (!) and loved it as well. Also, OK this is going to sound weird, but their bathroom is so nice compared to so many other Manhattan restaurants. I'm knocking them one star only because they were out of, like, three of their beers when we went--kind of odd for an Austrian sausage-and-beer restaurant.

What a wonderful way to sample a wide variety of tasty and delectable dishes in a cozy and intimate setting. Â  The wine seleection is extensive and the wait staff is quite knowledgeable about what wines pair well with your food choices. Â One gets a big bang for the buck in this small neighborhood eatery. Â  As this is a very popular restaurant, Â make sure to make reservations well in advance.
5 stars times a billion more! D E L I C I O U S Expensive but worth it! The bread basket is a MUST and the puppy scramble #1 eggs are #1 because there is nothing better! Yum yum yum

The gnocchi was pretty good--I was surprised that it was a bit fried, but maybe I'm not classy enough to know how gnocchi is typically prepared. Melted in your mouth and very filling even though the portions look rather small. The atmosphere was very nice for a group dinner and the service was pretty good. My friend got a "big salad" but it was definitely not worth the price! Could've paid half that much at Chop't. Get a pasta if you want something worth spending $20 for. There is a photobooth downstairs which was fun with friends.

In full disclosure, I did not pay for my meal here. I had helped a friend move to an apartment nearby and lunch was taken care of as a thank you. That being said, I would come back here with my wallet and get exactly the same thing. I split a margherita and bianca pizza with my fella, and we really enjoyed both of them. Crispy thin crust, fresh basil, generous helpings of cheese, we finished every last bite and only regretted that decision a little bit. One personal pizza is more than enough for one person, but not enough to bring home leftovers, so you might as well just finish the whole thing in one sitting. Certainly not the best pizza, or even best thin crust pizza that I've ever had, but I'd rank it significantly above "serviceable". An okay beer selection (four taps, some more in cans and bottles), but Lea gets the fourth star because of their excellent service. Every person we spoke to was friendly, and when they found out one person at the table had just moved to the area, we got some complimentary cannolis as a "welcome to the neighborhood" treat. So if you're wandering around Cortelyou wondering what to eat, stop into Lea for some pizza. Your stomach will thank you.

You're not getting out of here for under $80 a person at the absolute minimum, so the sooner you accept that, the more fun you will have here. My husband and I took our friends here for a birthday dinner and had a great time. I was expecting stuffy service and small portions, but that wasn't the case at all. I left full and absolutely satisfied. When we arrived, one of our party was running late, but we were seated nevertheless (shocker) and ordered drinks while we waited. They have a great bourbon/whisky selection and an approachable beer selection, so we all started with that, then later on into the meal, we got into the cocktails (which were interesting, but honestly, I'd rather just have a nice glass of something instead of a mixture of liquors I've never heard of). Anyway, the food: it was excellent. We started with the oysters and pork sausage ($18 for 4 oysters and 2 sausages, but the oysters were the best I've ever had and the sausage was super rich) and the bone marrow. Both were great and the marrow bones were Fred Flinstone sized. For mains, our friend and I had the famous $26 burger - 100% worth it. It was cooked to an absolutely perfect medium-rare, was super juicy, incredibly flavorful, and really just showed off the awesome meat that they use. I'd order it again in a heartbeat. The fries were really crispy and plentiful, too. My husband had the mussels in a curry broth, which were lovely. Not a bit of sand or grit, lots of flavor, and the mussels themselves were big and meaty. My other friend had the steak, which was again, cooked to a perfect medium-rare and too big for her to finish. We ended the meal with hazelnut crepes (again, a big portion, too big for the four of us to finish, and wonderfully caramelized on top) and a few glasses of sambuca. Our waitress was attentive and pleasant throughout the entire meal, the space was gorgeous, and I felt transported back to ~Old New York~. Definitely a special occasion type place, but worth every penny! I'd love to take my parents here someday, and maybe another pair of meat-loving friends.

I will stop trying hipster Asian restaurants. I will stop trying hipster Asian restaurants. I will stop trying hipster Asian restaurants. These are notes to myself, but perhaps they will be useful to others. Â Perhaps you too have been lured by blogosphere buzz and the insouciant air of the serving staff. Or perhaps you were drawn in by the slightly punishing music. The only problem is, well, the food. The coconut rice is very good. Â The pork jowl with watermelon and chicharron is the kind of dish that sounds really cool but lacked the intensity of flavor you're expecting. The mango salad is adequate but nowhere near as good as the mango salad in Thai places in Elmhurst. It just lacks that burst of pleasure and complexity of flavors. Finally, we had the sizzling sissig, which receives so many raves on here. My wife and I find the enthusiasm for this dish bewildering. The ratio of fat to meat in the pork pieces is ridiculous. Even if you are fan of pork fat, eating this dish is an unpleasant experience. Essentially the only protein you're getting is from the egg that is cracked on top. Hipster asian restaurants feel to me like *concept* restaurants. You are going there to enjoy the *idea* of the food you are eating and to enjoy the idea about yourself as the sort of person who enjoys eating at that restaurant. Â My own grubby materialism prevents me from partaking in this pleasure.

Always great! Super cute spot! The Seafood is always fresh, service is always on point. My Husband and I typically sit at the bar and have a great experience every time. This is not a big place so try to get there early. I love the clams and the selection of oysters they offer, this is one of the best spots to get seafood in the city. Not to mention the great selection of craft beer that the staff gladly allows you to sample. The service at the bar and the food don't disappoint!

Cafe Gitane is one of the first places I go when I get into the city. I always, always get delicious, healthy food. The Chicken Peanut Satay is my favorite with chicken skewers, jasmine rice and a carrot mint side dish is absolutely superb. Filling and perfect! Also, the fruit bowl is a great healthy late night snack. I highly recommend this cafe, everything is divine... plus the location makes for great people watching! Oh... cash only so be prepared!

Everything on the menu is pretty tasty here. The menu appeals to a diverse set of people. Good vegetarian options (Mac and cheese, interesting salad choices, good breakfast fare served all day). My personal favorites are the green eggs and ham (scrambled eggs with goat cheese and pesto served with ham steak) and the steak and eggs. The cocktails are nice as well.

One of the best Chinese restaurants in town for sure! Basically I'm quite satisfied with every dishes I had during las two visit. Â They can get very busy which is understandable, but the waiters should definitely be more attentive to costumers. I don't think they have figured out a good way to deal with the peak hours yet. Given the price they charged, they definitely should improve their services to make my money worth spent.

A little on the expensive side, but totally scene-y, in a good way. One feels glamerous and all New York eating in there. The food wasn't memorable, but the cute little tables and the only-in-New York line around the block on a gorgeous sunny day was. Luckily, my girlfriend doesn't believe in lines and somehow just walked in and got the hostess to seat us? That was something I can't ever pull off. I went here on one of my first trips to NYC from Phila, and it was like 'wow, coming from Los Angeles, this, we can do.'

I think Piora had an off night... The food was excellent. Â We had the monkey bread, tuna crude, rigatoni, and sea trout. Â All were really delicious. Unfortunately though, we waited something like 45 minutes between the first and second course. Â  The staff was very upfront about the wait in the kitchen, and as a result they showered us with free booze, dessert, and a cheese tray. Â This was a nice touch, but after sitting down at 830 and leaving at nearly 11:30, we were kind of over it. Â Free dessert only goes so far when you have to wait for it nearly 20 minutes too! Hopefully its a fluke - the space is beautiful and the food was really good.
Yum. The sangria was delicious. The food was equally good.

We've now been twice, and I have to say . . . Pancakes? Superb. I find the maple butter to be a bit too rich, but the house raspberry jam makes up for it. Buttermilk biscuits? Good, but dry! Darn. Fried green tomatoes? We loved them the first time, then perhaps built them up in our imagination. The second time they were really greasy, not very green, and just not the same. Will we come back? Sure. But most likely for dinner, with a group of 6, with a reservation. UPDATE UPDATE UPDATE! For the pancakes: Scratch the maple butter and instead use the honey tabasco that comes with the fried chicken. Oh my word. It was a freaking revelation! TRUST ME.

Just a little pricey, and the food didn't look exciting enough to bother ordering. They were out of house made beef jerky, which was kind of disappointing. The beer list, on the other hand, is really well put together. The draft beers especially are full of esoteric microbrews, which lead me to the 4x4oz beer flight, served on a cute little paddle. $6 during happy hour, 2 more the rest of the day. Outside of happy hour, there's isn't much to drink under $6. They have a decent cocktail list, two drinks based in good rum and fentiman's ginger ale. The one which also contained pineapple, lime, ginger reduction was okay, but needed clearer flavors. Bar seemed to be stocked with good liquor. I'm tempted to give them a bonus star for banning children after 5pm. My bartender was super friendly and attentive at midnight on a weekday.

Went there a few nights ago for dinner--hadn't been in a while--and they just do everything right here. Â We were immediately escorted to our table, met with a friendly server who recommended a fantastic bottle of chardonnay. The decor/ambiance is perfect, and although it wasn't packed that night, the room had a good vibe and the bar was fairly crowded. We had heirloom tomato salad to start, then for entrees the lumache (duck sausage pasta) and the glazed halibut. Â Both were perfectly prepared and delicious, and just the right amount. Overall it was an excellent experience and I'll definitely be back.

Went here with my partner for a much anticipated dinner. I love beer and gastropubs and she was super psyched to take me to the Spotted Pig. Then a burger requested medium came out rare. Not even rare, more like what the French call blue -- nicely browned on the outside but RAW on the inside. When we sent it back they brought out the SAME burger, which they had returned to the grill even though it was cut in half. Of course it was gray and disgusting on the outside. Asked for the manager after waiter told use that Spotted Pig had a Michelin star so "I think we know how to cook a burger." He also muttered "It's not my fault I just bring out the food." When the manager came over -- he and the waiter were lame hipster friends -- he told us if we didn't like it we could leave. I think they were trying to be snobby but they reminded me of Beavis and Butthead -- a couple of clowns in fedoras. Did I mention we were surrounded by tourists, like really tourists, from the Midwest, carrying things like bags from Dylan's Candybar? Not that I have anything against tourists, but I didn't get why Beavis and Butthead thought they were too cool for school, since The Spotted Pig seems to have degenerated into the Hard Rock Cafe. Bottom Line: Skip it!
All you need to know, and all you will know after going: bacon wrapped dates. Get some!!
Amazing food. Laid back. The right kind of noisy.

If you work or live in midtown - you know how frustrating food options can be. Friedman's has solved this seemingly impossible situation! This place is truly a gem in a neighborhood full of over-priced/unhealthy spots catering to tourists. Space is rustic yet modern, with an earthy palette and warm lighting in the evening. Service was great, our server was super sweet. Definitely an intimate restaurant during weeknights (can't speak to weekends) which was perfect for catching up with my best friend, and would be nice for a date night. I've had lunch delivered and gone for a sit-down dinner and both experiences have been amazing. Their salads are large and composition is deliciously balanced. My favorite: Grilled Salmon Salad (dill dressing is light, yet just creamy enough). And the brussel sprouts are to die for! After the first time I had them, I couldn't stop thinking about them! Being that I work around the corner - I have to restrain myself from getting lunch here every single day [poor wallet]. My friend and I tried to go for brunch on a Sunday morning, and the wait was about 45 minutes. Unfortunately, we couldn't wait - but I'm looking forward to having brunch here soon!

Hi! Stopped in by myself one night after work for a nice meal. I felt welcomed, it wasn't over crowded and the service was nice. Bread came with my meal, ordered a diet coke, and had Penne Arrabbiata: Tomato, basil, roasted garlic and spicy red pepper. It was truly delicious...I had to finish it and didn't take any home! Good prices, for the quality of food that you get, the attentive and welcoming service, peaceful atmosphere, and bread...etc. There was a family with toddlers next to me, and another family with teenagers. So, seems welcoming to all ages. Could also be a nice data, romantic place. Casual enough for nothing over the top, but romantic enough w/good food for something special. Enjoy!

I dubbed thee " brooooo bar ". That's what i kept hearing as i sat at the bar looking at the happy hour menu. dude#1 - something something Broooo dude#2 - Â :: getting louder:: YEA Broooooooo both dudes - Bwahahahhahahaha :: super loud:: Fools Gold is quite spacious and i foresee this place becoming a mad house almost every night of the week. Friendly bartenders who are well versed in the art of craft beer/ whiskey. Myself being a non-beer drink had no interest in this aspect buttt they do have what seemed to be an extensive variety. Happy hour runs from 11am-7pm which includes - certain beers ( the ones with " * " next to it on the menu) for 5 dollars - 1 dollar oysters ( dozen per person is the limit) - sandwich and beer for 12 bucks I was even surprised to see that they serve Katz's corned beef here as a sandwich but hey, I'm not complaining! They also have a few tv scatter around the place so you can get your sports watching on. Great place for a guy's night out or just grabbing a drink. So what are you waiting for, brooooooooooo?

The people hurling five stars at Lombardi's are obviously victims of a group mindfuck. While waiting for some pants to be hemmed at Uniqlo, I ambled over here since I'm sick of people asking if I've been. Yeah, it was the "first ever" pizzeria and it's famous, etc. so fine I'll try it out. Usually, there's a line, but a street festival in Little Italy seemed to have drained off the usual tourist dregs, and I got in right away. The establishment is nice in a tourist trap sort of way, with "professional service," the obligatory photos of barely recognizable celebs awkwardly smiling with the owner up on the walls, and a kitschy menu on which things are "famous" (and therefore expensive). That's right, $17 for the small margherita, delivered with ho-hum table-turning-over service. Is it possible to say a pizza is too crusty? This one was not only 20% crust, with only a thin layer of cheese and sauce, but it left a burnt crust taste in my mouth I don't even suffer at the street pizza joints. I had to ration out my tap water to wash it down, since no one ever came to refill my glass. Cash only, which makes me wonder what this place is a front for. If any "friends" of Lombardi's are reading this, please don't "ace" me. Go to Emporio, instead, right up the street. No lines, hotter hostess, more impressive for a date.

Great service and great food that caters to locals and welcomes nonnatives. The pulled pork sandwich was solid and the beer was from local breweries. Shout out to Alex the bartender who was extremely friendly and welcoming.
This place changed sushi for me. I foresee many summer sushi picnics.

Way too much hype. There was nothing special about this place. Go to Chipotle across the street. I got a carne asada quesadilla. First and foremost, it was not a quesadilla. It was a burrito with a slice of cheese without beans and rice... The meat was okay, a little better than Qdoba and Chipotle, but nothing really to write home about. Overall, the blend of flavors was a little lacking. I think the problem was that there wasn't enough ingredients for it to be a burrito and there wasn't enough cheese for it to be a quesadilla. Honestly, not worth it. It's a cute place. But at $8 a pop, find a different taqueria.

It's my first week at my new job in the Financial District and I have been eager to find and try all the hot spots for coffee and food. Let's just say, I wasn't expecting a food mecca in this area, but there are a few great places to check out. I don't drink too much coffee, maybe one cup a day, but when I do drink it, I want the good stuff. Meaning, I'm looking for a hipster/trendy shop where I am most likely going to shell out around $4 for a cold brew. Not a Starbucks or Dunkin, and especially not the crappy java from the work cafeteria. As I ventured out this morning looking for a caffeine boost, I opened up Yelp to see what was around. Unfortunately, my phone service is absolutely terrible around my office so I went for a short walk hoping to run into a decent place. Luckily, I ran into Blue Spoon (which is literally steps away from my office). Their outdoor sign enticed me as I read that they brew Intelligentsia coffee and offer breads and pastries from Balthazar and Ceci-Cela. I was immediately greeted with a smile at the counter and surprisingly there was no line. It's summer so I went for a cold brew ($4) and picked up a fresh piece of fruit, although I was extremely tempted to try the delicious looking pastries and bread from Balthazar and Ceci-Cela. I'm happy to have this place right around the corner from my office. I'm glad I ran into it when I did, otherwise I would be still walking all the way to Hudson Eats at Brookfield Place to grab a Stumptown cold brew from Black Seed.

If you're looking for an authentic Japanese food in Williamsburg, I recommend this place and Bozu, which is also located on Grand St. Prices are very moderate and their sushi is very fresh. I can't wait to go back!

This place never fails me. Great, friendly service. Fresh lobster stuffed to the brim on a perfectly warm buttered and toasted bun with a little smack of that special powder stuff they put on top. Paired well with Cape Cod chips and an ice cold Maine Root soda (may I recommend the blueberry soda?) On our most recent trip, my brother and I shared the Noah's Ark. Half a lobster roll, half a shrimp roll, half a crab roll, bag of chips and soda per person - the Noah's Ark is for two peeps. My favorite is the lobster followed by the shrimp and then the crab coming in third. Crab was the only one that was "okay" and not "SOOO AMAZING" We even had a whoopie pie and you would think it wouldn't be that great - nope, it was equally good. Get one while its cold! It was my brother's first time and he seriously won't shutup about it. And to top it off, they have a loyalty card! Whoot whoot. I like businesses who treat their loyal customers well also known as ME.

We were early for our dinner reservations at a different restaurant but stopped in for a drink (also to escape the driving snow). The bartenders were attentive and helped us to snag 3 seats when they opened up. Small beer selection, but passable and my wife had a glass of very nice Cab Sauvignon. Overall ambiance is nice and they were quite crowded but I assume that is always the case from what I read in other reviews. A quick glance at the menu makes me want to come back for lunch or dinner but I am a little put off by some of the other yelp* comments about "euro trash, tourists and d-bags". Get over it and accept the fact that a popular restaurant will always attract some people you might not particularly like.

Service is friendly and attentive, but staggered. Â We waited 15 minutes for our entrees after our appetizers were cleared. Â  Food wise, I don't understand the hype at all. Â If you're a lazy 20 something (like 90% of my east side neighbors seem to be these days) who hasn't ventured further north than Murray Hill or further south than Houston St., you might think the food is great, perhaps compared to the dorm food standard you left behind at college last year. Â  But the reality is, while serviceable and not exactly bad, this was among the most uninspired, plain, and flavor free meals I've eaten in NYC in quite a while. I had high hopes for the corn soup special. Â Well, it was corn soup I suppose. Â Special; not so much. Â In the middle of corn season, I expect corn to taste like corn. Â This was one of those ubiquitous, one note purees that attempts to win you over with color and texture, hoping you'll forget that it doesn't really taste like much, especially the main ingredient. My entree was another "special", lobster and corn agnolotti in a "tomato cream" sauce. Â It was overcooked. Â The pasta was floppy with zero bite. Â The lobster was soft and stringy and tasted fishy. Â Also, for some reason, each pouch of pasta was unpleasantly filled with a burst of hot water. Â And I swear on a stack of Olive Garden menus, the "tomato cream" sauce looked and tasted exactly the sauce found in a can of Spaghettios. Â Don't get me wrong, I loved Spaghettios when I was 9. I'm sure overcooked fishy pasta in a Franco American-esque red sauce was not what the chef intended, but that's what I was served. Â  I recently had a meal that was literally 10 times more flavorful and properly cooked at a chain Italian restaurant in a mall in Nyack. My experience has been that when you wait a long time between your app and your entree, and your entree is pasta, your chances of getting good pasta are pretty slim. Â La Follia did not prove me wrong. To be fair, this is 3rd Avenue we're talking about. Â It's not exactly a culinary hotbed, and locals here aren't typically reaching for the stars when it comes to dining out (and I've been starving in this neighborhood for 20 years, so I know). Â This place has a built in neighborhood customer base as predictable as its menu. Sorry La Follia. Â I'm sure you'll do fine without me.

Capri is a cute little, authentic Italian cafe. Seating is tight to say the least. I ordered a salad to go: the insalata della casa with mixed greens tossed with cucumbers, tomatoes, sweet red onions, carrots and basil in lemon extra virgin olive oil dressing. I added herb-crusted grilled chicken and fresh mozzarella (impossibly soft and definitely worth trying), and it came to around $7, not at all a bad price for premium ingredients. Â The soups and pastas on the regular menu and specials menu also sounded very Â tempting, so I will have to go back to try them.

After reading a few reviews, I decided to make reservations here for my wife's birthday and I must say, I was not disappointed at all. Â  We were a little early for our reservations and they sat us right away. Â The staff were very friendly and service was great. Â I had the skirt steak and my wife had a pork dish and they both were excellent! Â I just wish that the portion size was bigger as it was a little on the small side. Did I mention, they had hand-rolled cigars there for you. Â That was a great end to a good night.

Extremely authentic Italian restaurant located right in the heart of the east village. The ambiance and decor make you truly feels as if you are in Italy. The waitstaff as well as the manager were warm and welcoming. I started off with a Piadina di Riso (flat bread, pancetta, sopressata,prosciutto) which was delicious and the perfect amount for my friend and I to share. We then went on to split the Avocado e Pere salad which was equally as delicious. I chose the Melone e Gamberi risotto and my friend ordered All' Isolana. Both were recommended by the waitress and turned out to be great decisions. We couldn't pass up the desert menu after seeing they had tiramisu and I am glad that we didn't. It was the best tiramisu I have ever had. I would highly recommend it. The best part about this restaurant: everything is 100% GLUTEN FREE!! New fun facts: The restaurant is no longer BYOB. They have a good and affordable selection of beer and wine! Overall it is a great addition to the neighborhood that you don't want to miss out on!
This place is just delicious. I don't know why I am not rating it a 5. It is really close. I loved everything I ate and try to find ways to get back there. Yum.

Good, Italian, Food! Friendly service, casual environment, and some damn fine raviolis! Itd probably be a good spot to bring a date to and spend some dollars. Â I had been here a long time ago and it still holds up as a really good spot in NYC. Price to portion ratio is probably a 3 outta 5, but everything else about it is 4 stars and up! Malatesta, worth checkin out sometime.

Their butters are to die for. I have had pumpkin pancakes, as well as a few others and they never disappoint. The lines and wait can be a bit on the long side (at least 30 minutes) but it goes by quick and is worth the wait. Only down side is they do not have brunch drinks BUT this place is a good breakfast classic.
Enjoyed it.

I've been meaning to get around to this review for a while, but was prodded into action by the recent closing after a failed health inspection. About that: I have two girls, 11 and 14 who I love very much. And i wouldn't think twice about taking them to Di Fara the day they open back up. Dom marches to his own beat and I'm sure that runs afoul of the type-A types at the sep of Health, who have their job to do and an important one. But whatever grade the inspectors gave him, The pizza is a bona fide A+. Thin, blistered, great cheese/sauce balance, all christened with grana and Basil by Dom himself the minute it comes out of the oven. Â Truly great The good news about the dust up with the Health Dept is that maybe the line will get a little shorter. Alway my biggest obstacle in deciding whether to make a trip down to Ave J.

The soba is great - had the salmon and ikura don. The skin on my sashimi was left on the salmon so it was very tough and unpleasant to chew and swallow.. Service is also super efficient. My main reservation is that it's really overpriced..

Oh man, this place is a great find! My friend told me about it so I went looking for it. It's a little far from my office, and the line was pretty darn long, but it was worth it! Add soon as I got near the place, the smell told me it would be worth waiting in line for. It didn't disappoint! Â I can't believe how much food you get for such little money. I can eat a good amount of food, but this was far too much to finish.

Was walking SOHO yesterday looking for a good place and noticed this place packed on a Sat. afternoon. Â The brunch combo was excellent! Â Pumpkin soup with fresh Parmesan and pepper. Carbonara with ham..all for $10! Â The red recommended house wine perfectly complimented the 2 dishes. Â WIll definitely make the trip to SOHO just for this place.

Ok so I consider myself a dumpling master because I grew up eating them and I now make them myself.. . This place is like McD in China, so worshipped so falsely. The pork inside of the dumplings are way way too oily, Chinese people usually would not use such a high ratio of fat/ Lean mince pork. I guess that explained how cheap they are selling these for, way too cheap even for such a fatty pork content. Anyways, it was worth trying it out, I got both the boiled and the fried version, definitely recommend the boiled ones, the fried dumplings are boiled then fried, I think you really don't need that extra grease on the outside. Super busy on weekends, super uncomfortable small Â shop, the girls don't take names, so I was surprised that she remembered who ordered what, 20people at a time.

Typical of what a LOT of Williamsburg restaurants are. Overhyped, overpriced, decor-oriented, and very sub-par food. I'm going to cut to the chase. The Scotch egg was a good starter at a good price. The artichoke appy was a tiny serving for an entree price, and not worth it. The entrees that my girlfriend and I had were the Halibut and Lamb Kebab. Halibut...expensive and dry. Lamb...DID NOT TASTE LIKE LAMB. I couldn't identify what taste it was, so I sent it back and ordered the pork belly instead. Pork belly is supposed to be somewhat fatty...yes, but it's not supposed to be 95% fat and a smidgen of meat. Tried the desserts....MEH. If you have money to burn, and just want nice ambience, then this is your place. If you want good food, to go with nice ambience, there are PLENTY of better places than RYE.
Yesterday I visited this place for the fisrt time, my friend recommended. Must say pizza here is outstanding! I fall in love with their pepperoni pizza:) lol

Too full to write the review, LOL...anyway I loved everything we have ordered, especially the oden, this is actually the best oden I had in new York city! The kalbi and sashimi were authentic as well. Uni was fresh and tasty. Last but not least, they served plum wine that was just about the right level of sweetness. I Will definitely be back, provided that the line was not too long:)

Excellent beef chow fun with veggies. Â  I've also had the porridge, wonton soup and other rice plates here. Â  I grew up and live in SF so good chinese food has to come with some level of minimal service and at a good price. Â This place meets my standards and I'm pretty picky. Â  The waiters are friendly and don't roll their eyes when I ask for ice water and their fairly attentive during the busy times. Â  I've been probably 5x when I'm in town on business and have yet to have a meal I didn't like.

I've lived across the street from this place for over a year and finally went, with fairly high expectations. Â We went on a Monday so it wasn't too busy, service was so so, nothing to write home about. My date and I shared three small plates, of which only one I really liked. Â However, The gin and grapefruit cocktail was delicious. The place seemed kind of dirty and low rent for a place that had such a good reputation. Â We had a fruit fly buzzing around us all night. Overall, I've had better Filipino fusion food just a few blocks away.

Tastiness all around. I've been here a few times now and order something different every time. Well, except for the roti canai which I ALWAYS get. Their rice dishes and noodle dishes are my favorite, with the Indian Mee Goreng with tofu being at the top of my list. Definitely spicy, but nothing that will scar you for life. Hubs has ordered their crab dish and finished every last piece of it, it was that good. Their coconut drinks served in actual coconuts are pretty cool. After you finish the coconut juice you can ask them to take it back and slice open the coconut so you can taste the sweet coconut meat on the inside. Service was also really fast. Seating, ordering, eating and getting the check took under an hour, even though the place was packed.
i had a pleasant experience in this restaurant, the staff is attentive and fast, the food taste good, one of the best choice you can make for a quick lunch in downtown
Excellent food. Prompt service. Very reasonable. Two thumbs way up!

Quite a boisterous scene upon entering the dining room, however this is New York so I'm used to that sort of thing. We managed to snag a table right next to the kitchen so I was able to catch a glance at all of the deliciousness passing me by... Pardon me for drooling. We started with a bevy of crostinis, that's the thing there (these were so delicious they didn't make it to the photo shoot) and proceeded to devour some risotto roulettes. I had the Sea Bass, it was cooked to delicate perfection. Dessert was had, yummy, (again didn't make it to the photo shoot) but by this time I had consumed several glasses of wine and was ready to make my exit, stage left. Morini thank you and goodnight! *"Maria's Don't Miss" FIve choice crostini -Maria Taylor "What's new In New York"

The food is good and the management amazing as always should be, this is real Cipriani style, like in Venice. The general manager , Anna , is always smiling and super nice, thank you for this, a real place!
Been a staple for years! Actually ate in the dining room as well and gotta say it was pretty good as well for a local place!

So where do New Yorkers go on a rainy Sunday morning when not scattered down busy streets? Stuffed inside this bustling brunch spot in Tribeca. I stumbled upon Locanda Verde on NY Mag and heard about Andrew Carmellini's local cult following so I decided to give it a shot. Boy, it did not disappoint. It's rustic, homey ambiance was warm and inviting, perfect for a rainy day. We started off with the Sheep's Milk Ricotta with truffle honey and burnt orange toast - never thought in a million years that this combination is a hit! The scampi and grits with coddled eggs had the perfect combination of spice, sausage, and shrimp. Cutting into the coddled eggs revealed perfect yolky centers. I also had a bit of my friend's shaved porchetta's sandwich. Slightly overwhelming to look at initially but annihilating it will not be a problem. The spread they use definitely had a kick to it. My glass and coffee cup were never empty and service was on point. Price point is a bit high for brunch, but hey, this is NY. I now understand the cult following that I may have been inclined to join if I were a Yankee. I recommend getting there early or have a reservation. It became packed just right after we got seated around 11am. Definitely a must if you find yourself roaming around TriBeCa!

Long wait. I mean- really long and they don't even do take-out or let you take a doggie-bag when you're done eating but it's so good that I give it a 5. It's that much better than Ippudo and for less money. We live in Murray Hill so we have to cab it to get to this Hells Kitchen restaurant but it's worth it. We live near other Japanese noodle spots but nothing has impressed us more than Totto Ramen.

Clinton St. Baking Company= Â huge, fluffy PANCAKES with EXTRA SWEET MAPLE BUTTER SYRUP. I have to start off with the pancakes and syrup because it's the best part about this place! Those pancakes were so fluffy I thought I was going to die! ! The syrup is the best syrup I have had. It is light brown and it perfectly blends with the taste of the pancakes. I was amazed at how well the syrup blended with the pancakes. It's like that syrup was meant for that pancake. The chocolate chunk pieces on top of the pancake also went perfectly with the pancakes and syrup. The chocolate chunk pieces had the right amount of sweetness. The pancakes get 4.5 starts, but too bad it costs $13 for 3 pancakes. I ordered the grilled chicken sandwich which also costs $13. The grilled chicken sandwich includes tomatoes, avocado, bacon, chipotle mayo, and lettuce. All the condiments were fresh and it mixed well with the grilled chicken and bread. The portion size was decent and I was satisfied with the sandwich even though it isn't to die for. The meal also comes with slaw, a pickle, and chips that tasted great (salted perfectly). I went on a weekday afternoon and didn't have to wait for a seat. The service was excellent. The only negative thing about the service was that my friends pancakes arrived a couple of minutes before mine and my other friend's meal. This is definitely a spot to check out. Although the prices for food are expensive ($13 for 3 pancakes are you serious?), the portions are big and the food is delicious!
Cuban sandwich was excellent. Side dishes were served a bit cold but also very delicious! Would definitely come back

Food: 5 Decor: 3 Service: 4 Price: 4 This is one of my favorite place in midtown. Decor is nothing special, and the place is located in the basement. Relatively small space leads to long wait, which is more painful because they don't take reservations. What you can do is put your name down and they will call you, which is a slight upgrade. Almost everything here tastes yummy. Sure there are some more adventurous dishes, but most of the choices are not exotic at all, which is a plus when you take a person not used to Asian/Japanese cuisine. Â Yakitoris are definitely something you should go for. Kimchi & pork stir-fry, beef with fried garlic and cod spaghetti are all pretty good. Okonomiyaki (Japanese pan cakes) are sometimes a hit or miss but usually good enough. Daily specials (one of my favorite is eel tempura) are always a good choice. Don't expect sushi though. Don't go for cocktails, as they are super weak. Beers are relatively cheap and sake are more so. If you like sochu, go for the bottle. Price for food is pretty decent as well, esp for the midtown area.

My new favorite place. I am usually not a big fan of Jean-George but this one is a winner. This is the first place where I have made a repeating weekly reservations. Decore is fabulous, which resonates well with ABC Carpet. You can see Pipa. Don't forget to taunt or say hello. Must try "Roasted Butternut Squash" and "Mozzarella with Olive Oil and Sea Salt". Ask for some truffles as they just started to carry them. --------------- WARNING: DO NOT WEAR PLAID BUTTON DOWN SHIRT and BLUE JEANS. YOU WILL BE MISTAKEN FOR A SERVER. *AKA Thom Browne outfit.

It's going to be really difficult to go back to plain old chicken fingers or buffalo wings. MUST ORDER: Salted Carmel: Sounds disgusting in theory but was actually one of my favorites. It's totally got that sweet and savory thing going on. Think, chicken and waffles. Badda Bing: It's like a really AWESOME and way more cool chicken parm. So delicious. Original: They honestly just make a fantastic chicken finger. It's perfectly crunchy, tender and surprisingly not greasy. They also have a ton of interesting sauce choices. One think I really appreciated was that they chose 4 different sauces for us that complimented what we had already ordered.

this ticks almost all of the boxes for me... good location, nice ambiance, the food is great, it's very affordable. i had an amazing roasted brussels sprouts and baby carrot salad, my friend had a grilled chicken salad, and we had two drinks... less than $35. the food was great, better than great actually. the drinks were good. the only thing lacking was the service. the place wasn't crowded but the waiter was slow and inattentive
Was ok for the price but not special. Their coffee is not special either. Sweets are ok but a bit pricey for the quantity and quality.

Loved, loved, loved it. We got there at 6p (that's when Yelp says it opens- but it's actually at 630). After an hour long ride on the subway, I wasn't thrilled to wait in line, but WTH- it put us in line first. Ah, yes- line. People queue for this pizza. We waited until 640p, watching the two younger people run around, and the older legend work his dough. When they let us in, it was mere moments until we were served two beautiful slices of oily, basil-decorated cheese pizza. There were different types of cheeses used, and you could tell. You could discern the salty sauce, the perfect oil... Each ingredient stood on its own. A few minutes later, we had another slice- I ordered mine with garlic and onions. There was SO. MUCH. GARLIC. And it was beautifully browned, slightly sweet, and dispersed perfectly. The onions were sliced thinly and in manageably short pieces, so I never got a long, stringy one that caused any sort of mess. This pizza was simply exquisite, and well worth the wait. Pay no mind to the naysayers, who probably insist this pizza isn't amazing because they could hardly be bothered to do what everyone else is doing. My advice? Stop trying to be different and too cool for school, get your ass in line, and enjoy some seriously amazing pizza.
beer geek happiness pork sandwich was orgasmic home away from home

For a place that is lit predominantly by candle light, Lucali is bright bright bright. And I don't mean just in terms of luminescence. Simply put: the pie is delicate yet powerful, and independent from the crutch of toppings like meats and peppers. I know folks rave about the shallots, but i consider their being out of them as a blessing. The basic ingredients were executed perfectly. Imagine a mouthful of subtly salty mozzarella and aggressively seasoned tangy tomato sauce, and both upon a backdrop of semi-sweet (but not charred) crust...all encasing a bouquet of fresh basil. THAT, is what you'll get with each slice. It's awesome. Â  I'll add that the service is excellent _once_ you're actually seated, and it's BYOB, yeeeeow what a winning hand.
One word for this place, UNIQUE!!!! Food is amazing, service is great and definitely different! Love coming here!

This place deserves 6 stars.. Excellent service, respectable wine list and truly fantastic food. The fair is prepared simply and very high quality ingredients are used. Atmosphere is the best at lunch in my opinion but dinner is pretty great as well. My girlfriend and I just ate there again and we're super happy with everything. Highly recommended for those who appreciate mediterranean/middle eastern food!

i'd really rather not eat street-cart food, but halal is definitely one exception. i used to only get chicken over rice b/c i didnt think i'd like the lamb, but oh gawsh their lamb meat taste like meatballs! spicy halal meatballs (thats what she said -__-) my friends & i try to drive out their at least once a month.. i think its almost that time! ooh cant forget white sauce & very little hot sauce!!!

A very pleasant and tasty dinner. Â Friendly and informed staff. Â Wonderful little plates of savory yumminess (the rare steak was a bit overboard on the garlic). Â Very good wines by the glass. Â Casual and airy room, perfect on a summer night.

Heard about this place from a couple friends. It's small but definitely worth a trip! Ordered the bronte burger. It was made really well and it's super filling. Recommend this place just go in with an empty stomach!

I came here expecting such great things such I had a couple friends who liked this place and said it was a good date place. I agree the decor and ambiance was great but the food was not up to par. Deviled eggs had very little effort into them- just whipped yolk with a chip and pickle on top. Had the chorizo shrimp, which was decent but not worth the price. The Vietnamese duck sandwich was horrible- flavors did not blend well at all. Lamb skewers were the only mildly redeeming factor. I will only be back here for wine, if at all.
Adorable place, haven't tried the food. Â Went here for a drink with a friend. Â The sangria did not disappoint.
THWAP THWAP THWAP THWAP that's the sound of a good bowl of noodle soup.

Good points: Nice ambiance, friendly service. Bad points: Chicken poboy was served on old bread that was so tough and rubbery it was hard to take a bite of the sandwich; I had to twist and tear to get a bite off; not pleasant. My friend's shrimp tacos were served on tortillas that were stale and hard as a rock. This was at 7:30pm on a weeknight. We both left half our food uneaten, not for lack of hunger. Also, having no wine on the menu at all is a very strange/disappointing choice. I asked if they had red wine, and luckily they did, but just two choices ("malbec and pinot noir," no further details available). I WANT to love this place, but this was a disappointing experience overall. Maybe I'll try again in a year? That's actually worked out well at some other new-ish places in the neighborhood.

The 5 stars are for the Cuban Sandwiches. I have never eaten one before trying one here and I'm now hooked! When we got to New York, it was snowing and we were freezing. We were on our way to Havana Central when we saw the sign for Margon. Remembering that their prices were more reasonable than Havana's, we went in. The place is small and galley-style. The cook at the front that makes the sandwiches asked us "Two Cubans?" We said, "Sure." It was very satisfying and we went back for seconds a couple days later!

Best comfort food I've ever had. Went here for dinner! Try the Dogg Pound (three corn dogs with various dipping sauces), the pretzel crusted fried chicken, and their corn. The service was also great and they had a great selection of beers! Great place for a gathering of about 2-5 people. The atmosphere was also great!

Well believe it or not today it is not about Long Island City. We went to the West Village and looking for a place to have lunch and we find Buvette completely by chance. We did not even look at the menu, it was looking so pretty from outside and it was so crowded that we say OK that is the place! So now I have to say that as French alien in NY, I do really avoid to go to French places, because most of the time, I am feeling more in Disneyland than in Paris. And no matter if you consider the food or the decorum. it is always something wrong that ruins the experience. Second note is that the 2 things I am missing the most is cheese and charcuterie. So now back to the place. When I saw the little cute menu (everything is cute in this place), I said to my wife I can't believe it they have everything I am always missing in NY. The menu is really simple but it is what we like, Salads, croque monsieur, Charcuterie, cheese and desserts. All the essentials nothing more and nothing less. We ordered the rabbit confit, the rillettes, pate de campagne to start. And when it came, it was official, I felt in Paris sitting at the bar of a bistro, enjoying real serious simple food with my wife. Everything home made (we even found a rabbit bone in the confit), great taste, plain. Bread perfect, the cornichons (also homemade) perfect and most important in sufficient quantity (that is normally never happening and I always need to reorder 3 times cornichons to finish my pate elsewhere). Not to say also the portions are sufficient to give you a chance to enjoy more than one item. After that we shared a croque monsieur forestier. Cheese perfect the mushrooms tasted like forest. Again simple but efficient. And last but not least the cheese. I was bluffed, because instead of offering French cheese that are (unfortunately) most of the time uninteresting, they had a small selection of Vermont cheese (for me the only region I know in the US where the cheese tastes like cheese is supposed to) and it was really heaven. We did not make the dessert but the mousse au chocolat and the tarte tatin were looking more than appealing. It will not be complete without talking about the wine menu that is also as impressive as the rest (and also for really reasonable prices). We had a bottle of Bourgueil, that really made the experience perfect. The place is not only cute but also warm and romantic and they have a really small back patio for the last nice days. It is crowded and it works on a first come first served basis but it is a part of the charm. And last but not least, after we talked to our waiter, we found out that the chef was coming from California, maybe it explains why everything was so French authentic... Was this review...?

Very creative concept, but if you're Korean and you know Korean food, you'll recognize that the ssam burrito is somewhat bland and flavorless. People rave on about the pork buns here, and while I do admit that they are good, they're way overpriced... and let's be honest: when have you ever really had a BAD pork bun? You can't really go wrong with them (unless they're really just terrible). I was hoping to embrace this place and regard it as highly as some of the other Yelpers, but if you're familiar with how the food is supposed to taste (in terms of authenticity), then it's hard to be as lenient in the review. And yes, I know it's a modern approach to Korean/Asian fusion, but bulgogi should ALWAYS taste sweet and tender, not dry and dull! All in all: It's a nice little change-up if you need to take a break from Chipotle for something a bit lighter, but it's not something you're going to fully convert to and swear by.

So I had to meet someone here. Wasn't too thrilled about it, don't really care for the East Village and places that serve $1 hot dogs, well I don't know. And then I walked in.... It's the quintessential Irish Bar. Classic Bar foods, tons of beer on tap, and a very well poured glass of Guinness. The setup is actually really nice too, great long bar to the right, few tables to the left and a back room full of tables. Great place to go for drinks after work, to hang out with friends, or well frankly just hang out at the bar, old school.....No TVs....loved it. Ill be back soon.
Food is good but the wait was not well organized for large parties. Hostess was not smart enough to make better seat arrangements to accommodate first come customers.

Pork it over! So much bacon I couldn't Â even handle it. BarBacon features the three B's: Beer, Bacon, Bourbon. (Well..I'm sure you can think of more B's but these are the most relevant) Table service was a little busy, as expected from a new bar/restaurant, but we were able to kill time at the bar for some happy hour drinks. Half off beers and wells. Great selection of craft beers which we hoarded before 7pm. First B in the books. Bacon comes next, and of course we got the bacon flight: Jalapeno, Maple, Applewood, and Pepper. I personally enjoyed the Maple the best. Sweet and syrupy to complement the salty. All the bacon was on the crispier side, and although not my preferred form of bacon, I was still very satisfied. For my main entree I ordered the Bacon Lobster Roll. YUM. The bread was a bit hard, but did a good job holding the lobster meat and bacon bits together. These were thicker pieces of bacon, but still on the crispier side. Bacon really does go well with everything, because each bite seemed to be better than the next. My friends ordered the Bacon Burger, BLT, and Bacon Grilled Cheese. Solid portions from what they told me. Notably, the grilled cheese was more bacon than cheese which my friend did not seem to have a problem with. Admittedly his tomato soup on the side tasted more like marinara sauce. Can't win 'em all I suppose. After we overloaded our bellies with porky goodness, we went for the last of the B's: Bourbon. I'd be lying to you if I said I remembered all 4 that we ordered, but we essentially ordered a flight of different Bourbons. Neat and in the proper nosing glasses for optimal tasting. I'd say we made the most of our BarBacon experience. Definitely not the last.

Disappointing service and food. We were told by the host the wait would be 20 minutes. Â Over one hour later, we are finally seated, but waited at least 20 minutes to put in our order. Â At least a half hour later we complain that we have not received our first course and are given some bread and olives. The first course arrives - Kale with white beans and trout, which was delicious. Our main courses finally arrive 45 minutes later and and flavors are lacking. Chicken parpardelle is tasteless, Cobia is overly salted and flavors are not good. Â The only thing which was good was the pork chop. The restaurant graciously offered us free dessert for the inconvenience, but alas the bread pudding didn't make up for the earlier missteps. It's a shame because the restaurant is beautiful, ambience is great and music selection is pretty awesome.
Loved the food! The wood burning stove pizza was the best! Â Loved the arugula pear salad and roasted potatoes. The service was excellent too.

Despite the fact that they don't take reservations, and that you will probably have to wait for a table at dinner, this place is the bomb dot com. The first time I came here I was surprised to find a simplified menu, but it's not what you think. Despite the amount of options, you'll be more than satisfied with what you order. Their Mazemen brothless ramen hits every flavor spot you would want it to. It's topped with cod roe, seaweed, scallions, bacon, yuzu, and sake butter. YUMMAH! I hope they keep it on the menu forever because I crave it all the time now. I like this place for their simple layout and chill atmosphere. Friendly staff as well!

This place is right around the corner from my house. This is a problem. I could very easily find myself ordering from Vesta every night of the week and never getting tired. Local, seasonal ingredients, good local wine and a waitstaff who now knows us and treats us like regulars. The menu changes quite often and I have never had a bad thing here. They do food right. Also- The baby Jesus cake is what I'd order for my last meal. Hands down.

After a half hour wait, I ordered the "trust-us" combo which came with a truffle burger which was very salty, horrible from the first bite. The truffle fries tasted worse than the regular fries, which were tasteless. It was the worst burger I had in a long time. Bear Burger is 100x better.

Love it, Love it, Love it.... Great restaurant... great food. try there meze's... its like appetizers... Try it. we are regular here... i miss the summer, it is great to sit there in the summer outside.

well worth the wait on a Friday or Saturday evening. I've only had the artichoke pizza, but my friends have ate the crab one and raved about that as well. Pretty simple menu, slices under $5-but large. This place serves beer! Apparently they're opening a few others in the city
I'll start by validating my taco credentials with full disclosure of the fact that I'm from San Francisco. It is my opinion that this is the best taco on the East coast. Get involved.

I visited from out of town and had the pork bund and some noodles. The option to fill the broth with more noodles for just over a dollar was great. That really filled me up. The pork buns my wife still talks about to this day. Everything we ordered was absolutely delicious. This is one of the best restaurants I've eaten at. If I ever come back to New York Shitty, you'll find me here.

I love Champs. I eat there twice, maybe three times a week. It's super addictive. I have pretty much worked my way through their entire menu. I like the idea that I can have a shitty day, get off the train a the Lorimer stop, walk a couple of blocks and drown my sorrows into the Buenos Dias salad. Or for a more meat-like, full-flavored dish, the MonteCristo. Their cook is a genius and I want his phone number. Champs is a lovely, amazing neighborhood place in the heart of Williamsburg. The only downside I guess would be its size - it's trying to accommodate as many people as possible, but just so you're warned, if you come here for brunch on a sunday, be prepared for a whole hour wait. (this is Williamsburg, this shouldn't be surprising if you're local. Have you tried going for brunch at Pig & Egg?) But it's fine, because you get to drink coffee while you wait, and hopefully there won't be any blizzard next time you're around. The most tantalizing thing about Champs for me is the cake display. Cakes, pies, cheesecakes, cookies, cupcakes - they're all so delicious and come in such a variety of flavor, I'm pretty much going to develop diabetes just looking at the case. A wonderful thing would be to stop around 5 or 6 on a rainy day during the week and console yourself with one of their massive slices of cake and a coffee. It would soothe even the most savage beast. (I'm referring to myself here.) Note: you don't have to be vegan or vegetarian to appreciate Champs' food. I've taken omnivores there before and they loved it. They loved the variety of options, they love discovering vegan cheese and eating more vegetables, and they love that no one will try to take deserts away from them. The waiting staff is adorable and always remembers me; because I divide my time between the East Coast and another continent, they've been known to give me free cookies when I roll into town. I'm not mad. I'm always up for cookies. No one rushes you, no one tries to make you leave your booth before you're absolutely done. The music is great, and I have to say, what first drew me in was their amazing neon sign on the front: "death before decaf". What more could you ask? Oh, you mean the "go fuck yourself" embroidery on one of the walls? You'll learn to love it.

I was told about this place by my friend that used to live around the corner. I've come here about 5 times and have only stayed around long enough to eat once. The wait is always at least an hour. This last time, a Wednesday evening, it was 30 min. I like that they call you on your phone to let you know when a table is ready. My date and I ended up sitting at the corner of the bar which we did not mind. The place is tiny and was packed with people which is good and bad in different ways. The bartender was very nice but he seemed too busy take care of everyone in a normal amount of time. He had to serve everyone at the counter (food and drinks), and also make the drinks for the entire restaurant. For some reason our food took an abnormally long time to come out... close to 40 minutes for two entrees is kind of ridiculous. I don't know why we didn't say anything. I ordered the shrimp with green rice which was okay. The green rice was delish but the shrimp was overcooked and chewy. My date ordered the al pastor tacos and the pork was definitely overcooked and dry. The chips and salsa we ordered was good and fresh but the not-so-greatness of everything else kind of overshadows that. I'm willing to give this place another chance but they better bring their A game!!

I really enjoyed my meal at Gato. Â I wasn't sure what to expect, because although I love Bobby Flay on TV, I was skeptical that his new hotspot restaurant in NY would actually be good food and not just hype. Â  I was pleasantly surprised. Â The space is great - it's very spacious and well decorated with a Spanish/Mediterranean feel. Â Although I thought the menu was a bit of a stretch to incorporate cuisines of so many different regions, I really loved everything we ate. Â The veggie paella, as others have mentioned, was delicious. Â We also loved all the seafood dishes we tried. Â The menu has a lot to choose from, and it's easy to do shared plates or order separate entrees, whatever the party prefers. My only complaint is the cocktail menu -- I didn't think any of the drinks stood out as very interesting -- there are definitely better cocktails showcased on Brunch at Bobby's!

I became a regular; maybe the best value for bucks Italian restaurant in NY. they serve real italian food, simple and tasty so do not expect fancy topping on your pizza or fettuccine alfredo (it does not exhist in Italy!). Pizza is excellent, several choices of home made pasta. Good and easy wine list with decent bottles priced in the low 30. I prefer the tables in the front; the back can get loud sometimes. If you do not understand the menu, order randomly, I never had a bad dinner

Benares is truly the total package. The atmosphere is warm, with dim lighting and nice decor. The service is wonderful, everyone was really kind and attentive throughout the entire experience. The food was also really great. I ordered the Salmon Tikka which was cooked to absolute perfection. I don't think I've ever had salmon that was that wonderful, and I look forward to trying it again. For dessert, I had the Atom Bomb, a chocolate lava cake with rose ice cream. It was as tasty as it sounds. The only reason that Benares gets 4 stars instead of 5 is because our water glasses were rarely refilled and the naan we ordered never came out. Even with that the Salmon Tikka was so good that I'm willing to let both of these go and come back to Benares for round deux.

I live down the street from Balvanera and have been awaiting its opening eagerly. I was not disappointing. Upon entering we were greeted by a polite host and a lovely waitress. We decided to go for 8 of their appetizers so we could sample as much of the restaurant as possible. I wont go through each one I will just say....get the carrots....they are insane! Superb place and you should go. Just save me a table please.

I have tried pretty much everything that's regularly on the menu, with the exception of the daily specials that change. I bring literally EVERYBODY I know here, had a few birthday celebrations (although you should def get reservations for dinner, as they run out of food quickly, and they close quite early 7pm). My favorites are the Elegante panini (homemade bread!), Spinach and gnocchi, the arugula salad, ANYTHING with their buffalo mozarella cheese (that's imported from Italy weekly).
Great food, great atmosphere. Â A bit crowded, but that's always the sign of a good find!

A really great place for an overpriced drink. Â It gets crowed. Â I go for a good work shmooze/ to get drinks with clients. Â The snacks are good and portions are small with excellent presentation. Â The non-alchoholic drinks are good too! service is fast but often a wait if you show up at 5.

Food/wine was good here, but this place is too packed and seating area is not spacious enough so that we can't take enough time to enjoy food/drink. There is only one communal table; and the other way is bar area. Interior is really awesome - the entire wall is full of wine bottles. I don't mind sharing a table with other group of people, but the table is so small to share. It's much smaller than the big communal table at Le Pain Quotidien, for example. When we came here for Saturday dinner at 7pm ish, the place was almost crowded already. (They don't take reservation). No extra space to put our jackets or bags. As a group of people were seated on the other side of the table from us, our dishes started to be mixed with theirs; oh lord, I don't like this kind of messy dinner. We liked wine, appetizers, and main pasta dish that we ordered, but I don't think I will come back again unless it is in the late weekday afternoon so that most of the space there is available for us.

I'll make quick work of this. Every menu item is a no fail situation, gluten free or not. DELICIOUS. Open late, don't go during dinner rush because there are only about 6 tables and you'll wait an hour (WORTH THE WAIT.) As a gluten free individual, I love having as many choices as "normal" people. 5 beers, pizza, risotto, panini, tons of deserts. Make room you'll want one of everything. God f'n bless you Risotteria and PLEASE open a cafe in LA!

Great Attentive Service & Delicious Food. While the wait for brunch can be a tad bit long, Cafe Cluny is great. Cute ambiance, friendly staff and yummy brunch (including unlimited coffee refills). The space is a bit small, but that's typical with most Village cafes.
