this place is on the moon. seriously. i was soo not prepared for the long ass walk that commenced in DUMBO with my mom - and her bum knee, of course - in tow.* but, what can i say? it was mama o's first night in town and the bro and i wanted to take her somwhere special. and, despite the two dreaded h's - the hike and heat - what a lovely experience it was. lemme preface that the food is a solid three stars but the thoughtful service more than makes up for it. (plus one.) for example, not sure if it was the best business decision, but the waitstaff held a table for a party of eight that was more than 45 minutes late. instances like that are impossible to find in NYC ... or any other establishment for that matter. we started off with the sweet potato and goat cheese croquettes for appies as well as the house rolls. the rolls were sweet and doughy but i wasn't a fan of the croquettes. for some weird reason, they tasted and smelled like unwashed, oily hair ... how i know this? don't ask. as for entrees, i had the lamb salad while the rest of my fam had the scallops. (i would ordered the latter as well, but felt that i needed to add some diversity to the table!) i throughly enjoyed my plate and felt the soft-boiled egg that came with was a nice touch ... until i ran into a huge hunk of fat midway. mmmm, lamb fat. FYI - the scallops were smothered in basil which i loved. we ordered cookies and the pecan sundae for dessert. i didn't try the cookies - they looked overdone - but the sundae was layers of yummy goodness. in fact, i think mama polished it off which is jarring because i've never seen her do that in my 25 years of being her daughter. since ma is totally traditional, some call it backwards, the bro - the man of the house (ha!) - footed the meal. however, i'm not complaining - this night was one of those rare instances where i fell into my proverbial baby of the house role, black car home and all. * - karma sure is a bitch - i think god was punishing me for being a fat brat in my youth. each block she whined, "are we there yet?"
Oh, damn.

the cart is one of the best in new york. Â people love the white sauce. Â I'm not the biggest fan of it the white sauce because its a little too creamy. Â  they quality of the chicken is A+. Â I prefer it to be more seasoned (more indian spices) but its overvall a great experience. Â  The downer is that the lines are long even with them working like dogs. Â  Keep up the good work guys. Â  i give 4/5 starts because there are other carts that have more seasoned chicken and less heavy white sauce. Â  BTW, this is a must do in new york city. enjoy

A real UWS gem. Don't be fooled by it's Olive Garden decor. This place provides some top notch cuisine with reasonable prices - a far cry from some of the other theater district or places around Lincoln Center. I'll definitely be back!

3.5 stars. Grill 21 is easily the best Filipino restaurant outside of Queens. Like Bamboo Grill in dirty jerz, I know the owner, ok, my parents know the owner. So on the first experience, not only was the food free, it was legitimately scrumptious! Almost all of the dishes were done nicely, with the exception of the BBQ which I had better elsewhere. Like most Filipino restaurants, you will find the same items on the menu. Some of the things I've ordered: Â ~ if i butcher any of the spellings on the dishes.......deal with it. Â  Bicol Express (very good) although I prefer the Southern Philippine version - spicy. Arroz Caldo (very good) Kilawin (Excellent) Inihaw na Baboy (Excellent) Caldereta (very good) Kare Kare (good) BBQ (good) Halo Halo (very good) - that means "mix mix" in-case you were wondering ;-) The space is small but nice. Probably can accommodate 25 max. The room had exposed brick (which I love) & a couple of paintings - not really sure what the hell they were of. Service was struggling since they only had 1 person working the whole room. Probably the owner's nephew who just arrived from the Philippines & getting sweatshop wages or working for food. One last thing. What surprised me the most about this place is that they actually have presentation with the food! Yes, they "plate" their dishes! If you are Filipino then you know why this is a nice surprise. Typically, we like to just pile the food on the plate. "Refined-Filipino Cuisine" is almost unheard of. However, there is a downside to plating a dish....less portions my friend. So in the big scheme of things, yes, the place comes out pricier than expected. The only other place I knew of which came close to this place was Cendrillon, which is now closed (shitty).

The all you can eat pasta is 22 dollars. Which would be a great deal if the pasta actually tasted good. Instead, the pasta sauce is at most mediocre, the noodles were unenthusiastic..I love to eat and I love buffets. The fact that I couldn't finish even one plate of my pasta says something. In fact my favorite part of the meal was the antipasta and the bread with the hummus/olive oil dip. It is for tourists. It's what you expect a standard Italian restaurant in NYC would look like. The pricing does not justify the mediocrity of food served here. Frustrating. Also tried the Pollo al Limone. The skin had a nice crunchy texture, but the chicken breast was too thick so it was a little dry. Really wanted to enjoy this meal... but I can't help wish that I saved my money and went to Eataly instead.

This may be the best mexican restaurant in NYC! Â  Went there with a group of 4 after seeing some theater and the service was friendly, the drinks very well made and the food ... well the food was phenomenal. Â Full stop. Â Phenomenal. Â  Try the guacamole trio which was innovative with sweet, spicy and mild versions of the dip and had a tremendous roasted tomato salsa. Â  Other outstanding items inclue the skirt steak tacos (perhaps the best thing on the menu), the hamachi ceviche, the short rib mole and the marinated cod. Â  Although I am not generally a fan of churros, these churros were crispy and just the proper sweetness with both dulce de leche and chocolate sauces. Â  Toloache is not a cheap mexican restaurant with entrees in the $20-30 range, but as an upscale restaurant it holds its own with other cuisines. Â As a mexican restaurant, it holds itself far above the competition. Â  Definitely go.

Pros: really good thin crust pizza with great toppings. The calamari was also tasty Cons: small space. I suggest going early to beat a weekend night rush..especially if you're a big group Slightly pricey but the portions are definitely meant for sharing with large groups

I went for brunch with a big group and we had a blast! great food and oh boy! their sangria's are the best part. They are complimentary with the purchase of any meal. GREAT DEAL! great music! great ambiance! BUT! make a reservation without one you will never be able to get a table...

Tough call, as I really wanted to dig the experience. Decor was egregious, as were some of the staff (others not at all!). Everything we ordered radiated a clear taste of sea and brine, which is not to everyone's liking, but I think you take your lumps when you order good seafood in a great place, and so this is more to personal taste. We didn't have the time for the menu tasting, although it sounds like it's a required kind of experience here. I have a feeling that could add a star or two by itself.

The atmosphere is welcoming and busy, the whole store shouts a greeting when you walk in! The staff is extremely friendly and helpful in recommendations. I went with a group of six and the Akamaru Modern and their Sesame Special were amazing. This is the best noodle soup, not just the best ramen, I have ever tried. The noodles are perfect--there's this unique and wonderful texture to them, almost creamy. The broth complements the noodles perfectly, and let's not forget the pork buns. The buns are BOMB. It is on the pricey side, at $9 for two buns and $10+ for a bowl of ramen, but the portions are large so you can share a bowl AND it's totally worth the splurge. Will be coming back!

Uh rude. Thoe waitress was incredibly mediocre. She literally brings the bowl of noodles from one side of the counter to the other. Doesn't refill our waters at any point during the meal. When the check comes, I tip $4 on a $28 check and she complains because it's not quite 15%. She demands more money and tells me that I HAVE to pay her. I relent because she's making a scene in a very small space. Thanks but no thanks. I'm definitely not coming back.

Well this is a hard place to review. Â Beautiful ambiance, fresh cut flowers everywhere and a very nice owner that checks in with you periodically. Went here with my two brothers and G for her bday dinner. Â This really isn't a tapas place, as they do charge entree prices for about 3-4 bites. $55 for a pitcher of sangria is a little steep in my opinion, although one brother did say it was the best sangria he has tasted. Â Sunny, who had his drinks made sans alcohol, was very impressed with the cocktails. Â  Paella was just ok. Â Ams liked his fish, and G liked her chicken. Â Quail wrapped in bacon with apples was not worth it. Â Would have preferred Hooters wings. Â  Bathroom situation - one for hombres and one for chicas. Â This equates to a log jam of people trying to pee and/or wash hands. Â  All in all, will I be back? Â Probably not. Â Would it be worth checking it out for your first date with a girl you are trying to impress? Â Absolutely!

Frankly, this cafe is not for everyone. Grey dog has the tastiest, freshest food, and the most helpful staff you could ask for IF IF IF you have the patience for a lot of disorganization: What to expect: A long line that moves quickly. When you enter the Grey Dog, it seems CRAZY! Â  ( Is this the LINE? Who has placed their order? How do we get a table? How long is the wait? Can you even see the menu from here? How hungry are you? This line looks ridiculous...") What to do: Breathe. DON"T get intimidated or frustrated by the seeming chaos...somehow, these cats have it under control....by the time you place your order, your table is ready--no matter if you came to the Grey Dog for brunch, lunch, or dinner. I've been to this Chelsea location for several meal periods (Sun brunch, Sat lunch, Thurs dinner)...each meal period with similarities and differences, and each time getting a table. And, every time, I've been satisfied with the food and service. Foods to try: Have Â a Philly Wrap or a Veggie Wrap, have the subtle yet yummy farro-asparagus risotto or the spinach with mushroom and garlic "small" plate, order the melon and berries "side," Â commit to your own entree or share a bunch of "sides" (which are definitely plated for two)...with the food, I haven't gone wrong yet. Substitute regular fries for the sweet potato fries and experience a pleasing balance of sweet and savory. Tip: if you are visiting Grey Dog with a friend who gets evil when hungry or has a low tolerance for crowds, go to the counter and get a laminated menu. Your friend will stop complaining about "how no one can possibly read the menu from on/in line" and you all will have your debate about whether to try somewhere else interrupted by a guy with a colored bandana telling you your table is ready.

Wow, the food was phenomenal! A bunch of my friends and I had dinner at Sakaguru, we ordered a variety of small plates and everything was delicious down to white rice. Â The rice balls were excellent as well as the fried chicken and beef. Â  The most favorite dish I had? Â Chuwanmushi! Â Wow, it was an egg steamed to perfection with salty sauce on top and seafood inside. Â The consistency was so smooth and all the ingredients fresh. Â I fell in love with this dish and it was worth every penny. Â  Their service could use some improvements - one of the waiter had an attitude problem. Â Other than that, you must search for this place and eat their food.

Went here for dinner last week. It is the only place of its kind within 10 blocks. Pleasant decor, polite servers, and the complimentary foccacia with tzatziki was delicious. I could eat four of those. Some of what we ordered was excellent, such as the scallops, although the chicken entree and coconut shimp were average (but not overpriced). They dont accept credit cards, which is odd. I will definitely go back. If it wasnt so close to my apt, I would have given it 3 stars.

I don't often give 5-star reviews but hands down, THE best pizza in the city that is known for its pizza. Having recently been to Naples I can say without a doubt, the most authentic napoletana pizza you can get. Â I recommend the Brutta Ma Buona pizza which translates to "Ugly but good", heavy emphasis on the good part. The atmosphere is eclectic as well, with chairs, etc on the ceiling. Buonissimo!

Best pizza ever!!! Â There's always long line ups but I picked up a pizza to go. Â  We were at a bar down the street when I went to pick up some Roberta's. Â It was so good that I just couldn't stop eating the pizza while walking back to meet my husband and his friend. Â I'm not even normally a big pizza person either but they are just really well made.

Waited for an hour, and this better be good. And it is. it was worth waiting for. Ordered: Hirata Buns (2 pieces) - Steamed buns filled with pork, served with Ippudo's original spicy buns sauce - totally recommend Akamaru Modern - yum. The broth is so tasty.

I love their food. I had mango chicken with brown rice. This is definitely going to be my staple order. This was absolutely delicious. I also had the chicken nuggets everyone was raving about. It is soooooo good. It tastes like actual chicken. The sauce was great. Delivery was under 15 minutes. If I can cook this stuff at home, I would b a permanent vegeterian. I wonder how many calories I induced today???

I was very impressed with the ambiance of the place. Â Wonderful spacing and I like the mood of the lighting. Â My sister told me how amazing their bread is and I have to agree. Â It's wonderfully delicious. Â Unfortunately, each time you ask for more they bring less and less. Â It was also the best part of the meal. I had the Pollo Peruano with a side of plantains and yuca fries. Â It was alright. Â Not the best Latin food I've ever had but it did the job. Â I see so many reviews about their drinks. Â I outta try some next time. The service didn't impress me either. Â Our server wasn't very attentive as he forgot about our bread and I had to ask someone else for it. Â He also seemed really flustered about us changing seats. Â The ladies were cold where they sat so we swapped seats. Â What's the big deal?

Really cool and fun place - the open kitchen is different for a thai restaurant and it was nice to see all of the dishes getting prepared. I tried the Chiang Mai Fries, Zucchini Pad Thai and Kale Fried Rice. We loved it all!

The Umami Burger slogan is "U never forget your 1st." Well, I respectfully disagree. Â My experience was entirely forgettable. Â To be fair, my expectations for Umami Burger were sky high. Â I had read all the reviews and press and was expecting a life changing burger. Â Instead I got a burger that was just good. Â Good is not bad. Â But it's not life changing. Â It's three stars instead of five. Â  I walked in on a Sunday afternoon and was able to secure a seat at the bar right away. However, it took the bartender a good 5 minutes to even give me a menu. I decided on the truffle burger because I had read it was one of their specialties. Â I was very disappointed. Â It wasn't that the burger was bad. Â It was just that it was ordinary. I'm not coming to Umami Burger and paying $15 for ordinary. The best part of my meal was the truffle fries, which came with four dipping sauces including the house ketchup (nothing special), a creamy orange hot sauce (my favorite), a garlic aioli, and jalapeÃ±o ranch. Â But my experience was a little tainted because I only got two of the dipping sauces at first (not entirely sure why) and when I asked the bartender for the remaining two (three times), it took about 10 minutes. Â By that time, I had eaten a good portion of the fries. Â If it was a busy Friday or Saturday night, I could excuse the tardiness but this was just a lazy Sunday afternoon. Â The bartender was seemingly overwhelmed, which is unfortunate because it led to a less than desirable service experience. One quick tip. If you walk in and the downstairs bar or table area is full, you should walk upstairs. Â When I went up to take a look after finishing my (mediocre) meal, I saw that the entire bar was empty and only a few tables were full. Â Surprising, but good to know if you're waiting for a table and starving. Â  Perhaps my expectations were too high. Â But I always hope to be overwhelmed rather than underwhelmed. Â Oh well.

Came here for brunch today and had a lovely experience. We came around 12:15 and was told there would be a 45 minute wait, which is annoying but pretty typical. (Side note: we were told we could sit outside immediately, but given that it was about 45 degrees and looked like rain any second, we declined. The patio does look like it would be lovely in nicer weather though). My boyfriend was getting hungry (you wouldn't like him when he's hungry) so we decided to sit at the bar instead of waiting for a table, which actually turned out quite well. Each had a cup of coffee, which was strong without being bitter. I then got a bellini, which was fine but expensive (can you ruin fruit and champagne?) and the Cookshop Scramble. Good LORD was it good. I got it with bacon and the caramelized onion just took it to a whole other level. The biscuit was great, and even though the Best Biscuits NYC award goes to Bubby's, it was still awesome. I also had a side of the raisin-walnut toast with jam (blackberry? I'm not sure) which was also killer. My boyfriend got the huevos rancheros, which he devoured, and though I only got a bite, it tasted awesome, especially with the lime creme fraiche. In terms of service, the bartenders were nice but not overly so, and I can't really comment on the waiters. We really enjoyed our food and I will almost certainly be back (the grilled cheese and the pancakes in particular look great).

Ive been here too many times to count because its my favorite restaurant in park slope! Amazing food all over the menu. You cant go wrong. Service is great and the drinks are strooong so enjoy every sip! The wait is well worth it.

Good service, good food. Loved the skewers and the raw fish. Don't bother getting the normal stuff like agedashi tofu.. It's not worth the money. For the price of the restaurant you want the unique stuff. Long wait, for a seat but they call you so I guess you can walk around for an hour or two.

The best sausage in New York. I've brought friends here who don't even like sausage and they've loved it. There's always a couple rotating varieties that compliment the dozen standards on the menu -- all are delicious. The sides are also great: sauerkraut, pretzel bread, pickles, etc. Good selection of German beers on tap.
don't know why everyone loves the dumplings..thought they were gross. shanghai noodles were good, but nothing special

If Napoli style pizza is your thing, this is your place. I love the thin, crispy crust and fresh ingredients. It's a slight pain that they do not take cash, but that's ok. When in Little Italy, I try to hit them up.

We tried to come here last Saturday night around 9:00pm and there was a 3 hour wait.... I mean, really? That's just crazy. The host (rudely) said we wouldn't even be able to get a table before they closed. It may or may not be the restaurants fault, but that automatically docked off some stars. I've heard the food is incredible so until I taste it and see what the service is like I'm leaving it at 2 stars.

Nothing better than watching the man on the hallway slamming and pulling dough around to make them stringy and hand them to the cook in the kitchen to prepare for you. I have tried pretty much all the variety of soups and sides to go with the noodles.

I came here this past Saturday night with a large group for a birthday dinner. Â The venue was selected because the fiancee of the birthday boy knew Alan, a manager. Â We were seated in a Â semi private room with a great table and our servers were fantastic- attentive, fun and patient while working with the large group. Â  The reason for the 1 star is simple. Â At one point in the evening, a transgendered host/hostess came over to the table and made what was probably the most racist comment I have heard in public over the last decade of my life (called some of my friends cab drivers who happen to have brown skin). Â I was dumbfounded. Â I took it in stride so we wouldn't derail the fun the bday boy was having. Â I shudder to think that someone who looks like they got hit in the face with a frying pan before their skull fully developed as a child and has a set of cankles that would make any NFL offensive lineman jealous would be so shallow. Â It's a shame because other than this person's wildly unacceptable treatment of guests, this review would have read much differently as a great place for a large group meal. Â Never again.

There is kitschy, overbearing French dÃ©cor and menu items that force oh - to - much FRENCH in your face (French Roast, anyone?), then there is French dÃ©cor that is minimal and pleasant with a tempting menu to match: Cue Petite Abeille. When I walked in, I imagined a larger space overall...though there is cramped yet ample room in the rear of the restaurant, the front / bar area is narrow and crowded with a dozen patrons patiently waiting for their Saturday morning brunch. With a few chairs in sit on at the bar, the 45 minute wait was made less grating by the abundance of "The Adventure of Tin Tin" children's books to read. When you were done with that, the menu, scrawled on large chalkboards over the bar area, gave you time to contemplate and whet your appetite. I can speak for the hot cocoa and the Dame Blanche waffles: -Belgian Hot Cocoa: The large is awfully small, but it is packed with an incredible amount of rich chocolate that is, thankfully, not overpowering. The whipped cream and foam on top cut the richness of the cocoa perfectly. -Damn Blanche waffles: A thick, rectangular Belgian waffle is topped with vanilla ice cream and whipped cream. A small pot of melted Belgian chocolate sauce is served on the side. I poured the chocolate sauce into each individual waffle square. I devoured the damn thing like a ravanous 6 year old kid who was overwhelmed at the concept of eating something dessert-like for breakfast. I was so upset that I didn't have a spoon to collect the leftover chocolate / melted ice cream conglomeration on my plate after my waffle was gone; I vigorously and stubbornly attempted to collect as much as I could with my fork, but to little avail. I thought about licking my plate...honestly...no shame... If you are prepared for a slightly long wait if you arrive for brunch at noon (...which is to be expected, of course...it's feckin' New York City!), the food IS worth it. One of my friends got a special lobster omelette, and another got one of their hamburgers with fries. Both ladies approved. (And after stealing some fries, I can attest to their delicious crispy outsides and their creamy insides...PERFECT.) TrÃ¨s magnifique!
Cannibal has the unique ability to finely shred animal parts and turn them into a vegetable salad. The beef jerky is delicious. Would definitely go again if given the option.
I ordered lunch from here the other day and it was delicious! They delivered within 15 min. I loved the mango tres leches and the arepa sandwiches!

Came here for dinner on a Friday night. Easy to make reservations same day and I was excited because I don't go to Chelsea often and I had heard great things about their brunch... This looks like a restaurant you would find on Lincoln Road on South Beach. Just not my cup of tea. I Don't like big warehouse style restaurants that lack character and remind me of PF changs. So already I was less than impressed. The food was costly and not worth the price tag in my opinion. I had the scallops and mussels entree which was very disappointing. The sauce was bland and it was more like an appetizer. The drinks were good and innovative and The bread came with a hummus like spread which was good. Would not return for dinner. Maybe I'd try their brunch for some much acclaimed bloody marys.

How can you hate on a tasty, surprisingly large sandwich that costs $3.75? I'll tell you how, you complain about their water selection. C'mon, Saigon, how're you only going to have SmartWater? With the sport cap? Terrible. But yeah, that's some damn good banh mi. Perhaps not the best, but at that price? In Manhattan, of all places? I might even buy some jewelry for my girlfriend at that counter right there because I saved so much money. Not really. She doesn't even get a sandwich; she should just be grateful that I let her sit next to me as I eat mine.

Gathering outside this place as if it were giving away free food, I overheard little snippets from people before I entered: "Voted one of the 100 Best Places to Eat here in the city!" "That sesame pancake that woman is making is making my mouth water!" "I come here all the time...I'm kinda a big deal...." Well, the hustle and bustle of it all made me lead my boyfriend and his best buddy into this dumpling haven. Â We were like entering into the promised land or something with how wide our eyes were with wonder, and my stomach doubled over in yearning after smelling all the delicious smells that make Chinatown amazing! How to make it at Vanessa's: 1) Go as far back into the place as you can go, and TRY to get toward the counter to look at a menu; decide quickly so you can order just as quick. 2) Have money ready to pay upfront; KEEP YOUR RECEIPT! 3) Lean over the counter and admire how these women work their cooking magic! 4) Ask for forks with your take out; your dumplings won't make it home for how cheap these prices are! Â  Stay hungry my friends, and keep Vanessa happy by seeing her often ok?

I live by Samurai Mama and decided to give it a try for a date. The place is very nicely decorated and the food is pretty yummy except that most of my dishes I had that night were very salty. I don't mind salt, but it was a bit annoying. I've eaten at quite a few Japanese restaurants and Samurai Mama is okay in my book, though I doubt I'll ever have a craving for it.

I was meeting a friend from college who I haven't seen in the longest time and we wanted to catch up over brunch. I was glad I heard about Cafe Cluny through Yelp. The cafe provide a cute cozy atmosphere to catch up. The wait staff was understanding that we weren't in a hurry and wanted to catch up with each other, so he did not hurry us at all . We ordered the french toast and short rib hash to share. I really liked both dishes but I felt that there was too little french toast! It was so good that I inhaled the french toast in matter of seconds! The short rib hash was tasty if you mix the poached eggs with the hash. Overall the food and the service was great! Plus being from brooklyn where some brunch spots wait time is 1+hr...it was a relief to only wait 15 minutes for this popular brunch place.

Through a sea of endless streets and passing cars comes the ever so delightful aroma of garlic and food being prepared. This is what drove me as I was walking up the block to Briciola. The wonderful smell of old rustic Italian food with lots of garlic and delicious sauces. Honestly a little hole in the wall where if you blinked you could miss it. Its small but ever so quaint atmosphere entices you to stay and wait for a seat even if it is kind of crowded. When you walk in, the feel and look of the place is so rustic and takes you, in my opinion, straight to Italy. The exposed brick walls, one wall full of wine and on the other full of Italian groceries, and from the rafters big hunks of Prosciutto hanging just playing with you because they look soooooo delicious to eat. I got there at about 10:30 on a saturday night and it was filled with people already, not that it can hold too many in the first place. At the bar you can seat about 10 people, and I'm actually being generous with that number. But you can also stand behind the bar where there is a wooden ledge just big enough to hold your wine glasses and little appetizers. The feel is warm and cozy and the atmosphere is just perfect. You just feel like you are at home when you sit down and enjoy the ambiance. Now to get onto what the main star of the night was, the Wine and the Food. Davide, that was the name of the "bartender" or waiter for the whole wine bar, handed over a small hand written board which in turn was the actual wine list. Not that many wines but all seemed great. I first had a glass of Chardonnay, I normally don't like Chardonnay because I always have a bad stigma of California ones being very oaky and buttery, but this one was delicious. Slight oak, hardly any butter notes, and just the true flavor of the Chardonnay grape shined through, now that's what I call Chardonnay. After that I actually wanted to order a bottle of the Barbera they had on the wine list but he was out of that so he suggested two other wines that I might like instead, a Pinot Nero or a Cannanou. Davide actually let me sample the both wines before I made my decision on which one I wanted. The Pinot Nero was nice, light, slight ripe cherries and blackberry notes played while meshing with the ever slight hints of oak and earth. Then I tried the Barbera, and I must say it was sublime. A dark, rich, full bodied wine, with dark ripe cherries, blackberries, and currants. Also the full body earthy and oaky component appealed to my senses and the nose on the wine was amazing. I knew that was the wine I wanted. So now after choosing my wine and looking at the menu I was hungry. I ordered a few appetizers, so I will slowly and in great detail get you readers hungry as I describe each dish (I am devious like that I know). The first dish was shrimp scampi marinated with garlic and olive in a bed of beautiful tomato sauce with a basket of bread on the side. The shrimp was cooked perfectly and the garlic infused into the shrimp as well as the sauce made the aroma and taste of it that much better. I always say eating food and drinking wine involves all of your senses, and here at Briciola you will use all of them and some. My second dish was Burrata on Prosciutto. Burrata, for those of you who don't know, is the softest and most most delicious mozzarella cheese, and when done right it's as if you are drinking mother's milk. It is that Good!!! And the prosciutto was soooo delicious and so lean it was like butter when you eat it. It was the perfect compliment to the Burrata. Finally I had the gnocchi in a sauce of tomato and garlic. The gnocchi were cooked perfectly, small little pillows of deliciousness and the sauce made it delicious beyond belief. Honestly I wanted more bread to soak up the sauces that each of the dishes came in because it was that good!!! The wine, the food, the ambiance, was all great. I even made a couple of new friends that I sat next to and had a great time chatting with and having a great conversation with. Will I go back to Briciola??? Of course I will without a doubt. I have a feeling this little hole in the wall will be my new watering hole after work, luckily I don't work so far from here.

We arrived around noon on a Saturday and the wait was 2~2.5 hours!! Â My husband had huevos rancheros and said that it was superb. Â The side order of sugar cured bacon was too sweet for my taste. Â I ordered fried chicken sandwich b/c it was way past breakfast food time for me. Â The sandwich was good, but not to die for. Â I'm happy I experienced it, but not sure if it's worth over 2 hours of wait time.
Best Thai food I ever had. Â  Golden Triangles for apps.... Entree- Best Pad Thai I have ever eaten... But Spicy Basil Noodles-- wow. Â  Its a great date spot as well :)

This place gets a "thumbs in the middle." Â On the one hand, it's a welcome change of scenery from the many cafes that line 30th Ave. And the fried pickles, although just a little too thickly breaded, are tasty and worth the five bucks! I've had dinner with a couple of friends here and overall we enjoyed it that night. Â I remember my salt-n-pepper ribs being better than expected, and so simple. Â No sauce necessary. Â On the other hand, we all tend to remember our last experience most vividly, especially when it's not a good one. Â I've been back for Sunday brunch, and didn't enjoy it. The service could barely be considered service at all...or at least that's how it was when we stopped in with out-of-town guests on this particular Sunday. (Brunch has a pretty limited menu, by the way). Twice my friend had to get up from our table and walk over to the bar to get our drinks from the bar tender, as our server had apparently forgotten, or perhaps in the case of our request for waters (for those of use who don't drink) couldn't be bothered. Once our server came by to refresh a cup of coffee for one of us, but then she completely bypassed the other coffee drinker at our table without so much as a glance. She stalked away as he was in mid-plea for a refill as well. One of us yelled "Excuse me..." after her and by then she was already half-way across the restaurant. She turned and came back, but she had the most condescending smirk on her face. Â It was so awkward. Â It's not like we were messing with her. Â Why wouldn't she have refreshed both coffees or asked the other person if he wanted a refill as well? Needless to say, because she just couldn't seem to get it together, another server and the bartender both had to make up for her short-comings on service. Then there was the big confusion over tea--we ended up with four separate cups of tea for two people because by the time our server got around to it, our bartender had already brought out our tea-for-two. Â But the server left the additional tea there anyway, since she'd already gone through the trouble...I guess? Â I don't know, it was weird! As far as the food was concerned, my stack of three blueberry pancakes left even more to be desired. That's all you get: Â three blueberry pancakes, and they're not that sizable either. Â My order arrived with a hair in the top pancake, where the cook or server could or should have easily seen it. Â (It's not possible it was my hair because I don't have hair and it was actually cooked into the pancake). Â They were kind enough to comp my replacement order, but after a string of other SNAFUs, it was really the least they could have done. I won't be going out of my way for this place again--certainly not for brunch. Hate to say it because I really love brunch. Maybe try dinner though, or just sitting at the bar and noshing on some fried pickles. Â The three stars are for the bartender and additional server who picked up the slack, the fried pickles, and the time we did enjoy ourselves.
Burgers are amazing, bartenders are down to earth, and drink prices are very reasonable! Plenty of TV so you can catch any game on while enjoying a cold one

They brew intelligentsia coffee....enough said. Great location a few minutes walk from my work. Great prices on Balthazar Bakery pastries. Panini are actually grilled until melted unlike many places around. Employees at both locations have been great. Coffee is one of the best around, this coming from a drip coffee snob with a french press and a pour over in my office for my coffee. They also sell their custom blend of intelligentsia which is great and no shipping charges like when I usually order beans from intelligentsia. Tip there is only one door. Over by the condiment bar, its a window not a door FYI

We came in a large group for a company party. The food was haute culture but not very interesting. The desert was very interesting. Most of the group loved the desert. Â The appetizer and soup courses were very small. The mushroom ceviche was very sour. The main entree were good but not great. Our waitress did a great job for the large table. But sadly her coworkers were incompetent Â and/or careless that she had to pick up the slack. When the food came around, the servers did not care if they placed the correct order to each person.This occurred repeatedly for in each course. The most uncaring server was the one who got our drinks. He had 2 drinks in his had and I could see he was moving around the table without knowing whose drinks they were. So he sits the first drink in front of a empty chair and then the second drink he quickly places in front of one of our Â guests and runs away really fast. The person notices him placing the drink and tries to call server out asking whose drink it is, but the server ignores the call. From the other reviews it seems my experience was not the norm. Maybe with a large group they do not have adequate staff. Note our waitress did her best to correct the incompetence of her colleagues. Kudos to her.

A hole in the wall fast chinese food restaurant that specializes in bbq. Â I really love their roast pork, duck and chicken. Â I got the duck and pork combo with fried egg and Â rice which was delicious. Â The service is quick, food comes out fast and it's a crowded and loud place to eat but it was good and I would go back again.

MMM mmm. One of the few restaurants I make it a point to frequent whenever possible. As everyone already knows, they make the best soup dumplings around. This time around, I tried to crab dumplings for the first time, and the (boiled) pork dumplings. Both were delicious, and it's tough to say, but I think the crab soup dumplings take the cake by just a hair as far as the soup dumplings go. Other than the dumplings, I have only had beef and chicken dishes, but both times they have been delicious, and provide more than enough to share between 2 or a few people.

Pizza is fantastic. Three stars docked because a couple was *changing their baby's diaper* at the table next to mine and the waitstaff did nothing to stop them. I enjoy eating pizza, but I do not enjoy eating pizza with the smell of infant feces in my nose. And, yes, I did submit a 311 complaint.

Cheaper than food should be. More delicious than almost anything. So Chinese it hurts. You have to pick the ambiance... and I say this place is romantic because 1.) Dumplings 2.) It's hot and humid inside and 3.) Dumplings.

Frozen margaritas here are the bomb along with the corn and fish tacos. I went to Mexico a couple of weeks ago and I can honestly say that this place outdoes a lot of the places I went to over there. I originally gave Cafe Habana four stars but after going there a second time over this past weekend I have to downgrade it. First of all, the hostess that was working that night knows nothing about time. She told my boyfriend and I that it would take 45 minutes so we toured around the east village for 30 minutes. When we got back she told us that she had passed our names "a long time ago" and that she was already on the second page. Then when I asked her how long it would take again she said another 20 minutes... So after waiting 30 minutes I joked to my boyfriend that she probably didn't write our names down and just to make sure, he went back to ask and.. She didn't. Again we waited. I'm sorry but, even with the corn and the frozen margaritas and the fish tacos, as a hostess you really need to estimate time well or at least be able to write a name down.

Great food! superberb service.Everything was so delicious, one can forget that the food is health. The decor is inviting and warm ( I went for lunch and did not want to leave). Definitely on my list of faves- Bravo!

Phenomenal baked Mac N Cheese! Comes out bubbling hot and has a thick consistency. Huge serving for 8 bucks!! Loved the Fried Catfish sandwich too...def one of the best I've ever had...served with a side of amazing crispy spicy french fries! Overall, Juniper was a nice discovery last night with some friends. It's a small place so I wouldn't go there with more than three friends. The Asian lady who serves everyone is super nice and was really accommodating with our champagne and cupcakes we brought for a celebration! Will definitely return to Juniper soon!!!!

Don't kid yourself! This was a nice attempt at quality ribs. Maybe I am being too critical, but I am from Memphis, TN the home of ribs and blues. The dry rubbed ribs here are decent, your best bet here is to go for the pulled pork or a sausage. I wanted to give this place a test drive, so my partner and I ordered everything: a slab of ribs, 1 lb. of pulled pork, 1 sausage, a small order of baked beans, and the broccoli salad. The verdict: babyback ribs (average and cold), pulled pork (average and cold), sausage (good and cold), baked beans (very good and cold). Something must have been wrong with the food warmer because all my food was cold. The quantities we ordered were just enough for two people and totaled $45 for the food and $13 for our drinks. The scoop: Very casual. After several beers the ribs will taste better. No one appreciates a place that serves food cold, layered on wax paper for $45, then expects you to go to the bar to pick up your water and beverages. On a busy night, bring a friend or two. One person can guard the table while the other two split duties: bar/food line. Then you can regroup and sit at the table together. Otherwise, good luck carrying your tray to the bar to pick up your drinks only to find all the tables full. The owners of this place should rethink their service strategy, especialy for the price. Cool space and cool vibe. The bar has a neat setup. You can purchase beer by the 1/2 pint, pint, or gallon.....yelp...a gallon. This is a great place for groups. If the food was served hot and the beverage setup was different, I would have rated it 2 1/2 stars.

Comfort food at its finest. Imagine an ooey gooey grilled cheese, grilled with butter to perfection,your favorite cheese snug like a bug between fresh/ artisanal bread and a spread to complement. Delicious. Washed down with a beer? Â Brilliant. At risk of over using adjectives, all I can say is go. Eat. Try the Gouda and Great Blue Hill. You won't want either to come to an end. And yes, the coffee is excellent as well. And here ends my review as I used my last descriptor.

AH-MAZING. Love love love Despana and wish we had one here on the west coast!! I came here on one of my last days of my NYC vaca and was blown away with the quality of meats, cheeses and little bites. Â I bought a small fortune's worth of treats to bring back home (can't wait to try the uni and lobster pate spreads during summer picnics!) but stayed long enough for some lunch. Â Their signature Despana sandwich is to die for. Definitely stop in Despana if you're looking for a quick bite or to buy little treats for family/friends.

Definitely a fan of this bar. Â A buddy took me here after we were trying to decide whether to go straight to Radegast or drop by The Levee. Â He said, we can get big expensive beers now or go to a dive bar and grab some cheap drinks. Â I chose the latter and I don't regret it. Â Bud Light is $2 all day? Â I ended up grabbing a Fratboy--Budweiser and a shot of Jager for $5. Â That said, I can't imagine what the happy hour prices were like. Â  They have a pretty great selection of beers that I wouldn't expect a place like this to have--Racer 5, Abita, etc. Â Their cheap lush-centric cocktails are worth mentioning too such as the Gatorita which is lemon lime gatorade and tequila for $7. Â  Jump in here for cheap drinks and free cheeseballs! Â I definitely wish this was closer to where I live so I don't have to look for happy hour prices when I could have just gotten drinks here.

Eataly is the place to be! If you are in NYC you MUST experience all the gastronomic pleasures this place offers. If you know good quality, and your palette is refined, you will fall in love at first sight. The place dedicates the appropriate amount of attention to the details that the untrained eye may not notice at first. All I have to say is that if I had children, I would purchase most delicacies for them specifically from Eataly. Oh, and of course I will spoil myself here a few times a week :)
This is a classic French Bistro Restaurant, with the best Roasted Bone Marrow I have ever had!! Excellent service and the ambiance is very warm and intimate.

Dinner (3.5 - 4 stars): Brussels sprouts - not bad; contained grapes, puffed rice, tomatoes, cilantro, mint, lime...perhaps a bit too many flavors going on. Bone marrow and steak tartare - good. my friend calls it meat butter. Rabbit pasta - good, with tasty rabbit sausage, though i still can't tell the difference between rabbit and chicken. Cinnamon/pomegranate ribs - good. saucy. messy, obv. ever so slightly overcooked.
Eataly is what you make out of!

3.5 stars. Cookshop is good. Not great, but good. I loved the service, the atmosphere, the location, and a good part of the menu. We were five for a Sunday night dinner and there were no serious complaints around the table. It was also a bit of a reunion / get together so company can have some influence on reviews. I opened with the mushroom broth soup which was amazing. I think the best dish at the table. I went with the Mezze for a main, which is a bit off base for their menu, but it's the veg option. It was okay. We had two pork mains and the tuna. The pork got solid reviews, the tuna was a bit over done. I can't remember the last main - not a great thing - but there were no complaints. Desserts were split - not stunning, but good. Five with a few drinks came to about $235, without tip. Probably more than the quality called for, but it's Manhattan. I'd go again, I'd recommend it.
Sometimes I get a whole duck and stuff it in my face. It tastes so good...but my stomach doesn't feel so good afterwards.

The decor is lovely. All the food is very good. Service is very professional. A very polished, well-run restaurant. There's a vegetarian tasting menu too! I wish I had more to say. I guess I could go through every dish and tell you how good it was, or talk about the professional service (very attentive, by the way). But everyone else has already said it. Â The one thing that made it a four-star instead of a five-star experience for me is that the whole thing just seems like it wasn't meant for me. All the people wearing button-up shirts with shorts, spending what to most would be a lot of money for lunch, just kind of made me feel a little funny. Don't get me wrong, the restaurant is great. Just maybe not the place for me.

Great place for coffee and dessert! We went there yesterday. I had espresso with hot cream and a cheesecake and my boyfriend had beer with sausages. Everything was great! I wanted to try other desserts too but decided that I'll do it next time Place is little bit noisy and we had to wait Â in line for about 5-10 minutes. Waitresses were really nice. Location is great-all the museums around you. I highly recommend it.

I almost gave this place four stars just because the pizza burnt the roof of my mouth and I am still recovering. But just like the wait in line, time heals all and it won't be long until I am enjoying pizza again soon! We didn't wait "too" long in comparison to the people at the end of the line on our way out. Our mushroom, onion, and black olive pizza came quickly and was just as delicious as I imagined. The people here aren't overly friendly because they know they don't have to be. While I liked the ambiance of the place, I think next time I would grab it to go to enjoy down by the park or in the comfort of my room. I'm lucky to live close enough to Grimaldi's to make it my go-to pizzeria. Now the trick is to figure out the perfect timing to get in and out. But that's a game that I'm willing to play. However I now know to eat a little before so that my hunger pains Â don't lead me to eat a scalding hot slice in exchange for the repercussions!

This place is everything I could ever ask for and more. First and foremost...rum. Their rum selection is fantastic. As a bit of a rum fanatic I must say that there was a great choice of rums for all kinds of drinkers, both mixed and up or on the rocks. Their rum menu gives you a good detail of what each is like, where its from (which is important in the rum world) and what its best for. They had some on there which I haven't had before and was very eager to try. After many different straight rums and mixed drinks I can officially say that a rum bar like this is a fantastic idea with a perfect execution. Now onto the food. My wife and I sat in the back garden which was a nice size, a good vibe and a great atmosphere. You pretty much forgot you were in Brooklyn. Their happy hour was great, their food menu has a number of outstanding selections and their arepas are excellent. We had the one off the special menu and three others I can't remember how to pronounce and none of them failed to deliver in both taste and size. It's a definite hit and a spot we'll return to again in the not-too-distant future, most likely with a group of friends too. Nothing like good food (at a very reasonable price), good drinks (their happy hour $2 PBR's and a shot of rum for a buck more) and even better...rum.

The BEST Thai food I've ever had, hands down. I'm slowly working through the menu and I've never been disappointed with any of the dishes. The portions are big for the price, so you'll have leftovers for sure. I always get take-out though, so I don't really Â have anything else to say.

Interesting crepe shop with some traditional combined with Asian inspired flavors on the menu. Â Another distinguishing factor is that their crepes are served in a hand-rolled cone shape, which has its merits...and flaws. Â  By rolling up the crepe, you get a nice wide, cross-sectional view of what's inside, and every creation looks delicious. Â It's also handier to eat, because you can hold it in your hands and walk around taking bites without making too much of a mess...there are also no tables in the shop for you to fork and knife it. Â  There are some negatives to this, however. Â  Because the pancake wrap is made first, then laid out to put the toppings on, by the time it gets to your hands, it is already cold. Â  Which is a shame, because they truly do look beautiful, and a clear effort is made. Â Another minor problem is gravity. Â Any crepe you order with sauce, ice cream, chocolate, or anything liquid (basically all of them), will have a disproportional concentration of it end up in your final three bites because it all drips to the bottom. Â  The ingredients used here are general of solid quality, and very fresh. Â The menu is well thought out, and the toppings and flavors in each crepe is well-balanced and tasty. Â However good, I just can't enjoy a cold crepe that much. Â Unfortunately the feature sets Â Eight Turn Crepe apart also is the cause of its biggest flaw.

This place is a terrific locavore/seasonal banh mi sandwich shop. They have fairly standard pork banh mi sandwiches, but they also have a lot more fish (the Cambodian influences, apparently), and they have many specials using ingredients they pick up from the Greenmarket. On my visit, they had a pork belly sandwich with pickled rhubarb (really good, although the rhubarb could have been chopped smaller), some Spanish mackeral, a asparagus with garlic scapes, and other seasonal sandwiches and sides. The blood orange lemonade was fair, but they have good root beer. I'm looking forward to trying a lot more of their menu! 4 stars for the food so far; 5 stars for what they're trying to accomplish as a restaurant!

A village institution at this point, La Laterna still packs them in with a consistant formula of light italian fare, fine desserts, and enjoyable jazz music. In the middle of the NYU nuttiness in the area, this is a fine place for adults to get totgether and have a drink. I worked there briefly many years ago,and returned to happily discover nothing has changed. The prices are still affordable, the ambiance still romantic, the staff still charming. The coffee still the best around. Perhaps the finest feature of LL is the covered grotto that feels like dining al fresco, withou getting rained on or sitting on a west village sidewalk. Many a romance has begun or been rekindled by the fountain that sits in the center of the grotto. Yet this place is not exclusively for dates or drinking. There is a healthy lunch trade and its a very chlll place to catch up on your reading or emails in the afternoons. Nights, of course, are louder and darker. If there is a significant drawback to the place it is that it can feel cramped at times. The restroom and downstairs area get pretty packed for the music and with a single bathroom for each gender, there is often a wait making it further crowded. Yet all this is a small price to pay for one of the west village's seminal cafes. Far more enjoyable than those found further down Macdougal in my opinion...

Lanterna is a decent Italian restaurant in the West Village. The menu is really lacking on actual pasta dishes. There's a large list of pizzas and a few lasagna dishes to choose from along with some calzones. Many affordable Italian wines are available by the bottle, so I'd expect there to be some pasta dishes too. I mean there's not even a simple spaghetti dish or penne a la vodka. This is the first time I came across an Italian restaurant that doesn't have any single traditional pasta dish on the menu. Right when you're seated, there's a small cup of grated parmesan cheese that's waiting to be drizzled over a fine pasta dish and I didn't see the need for this after realizing there's nothing to use this for, other than the pizza. We went with an order of the mushroom pizza and lasagna al pesto. I've never seen pesto lasagna before so this was something I was looking forward to trying out. The dish was small and very hot with the edges nice and crunchy. There were a good number of layers but I didn't feel that the pesto flavor exploded in your mouth. Luckily, it didn't appear as oily as some reviewers wrote, so it was pleasant to see this. The pizza itself was okay, a bit chewy on the crust and not very thin. The sauce was tangy but the cheese slid right off with the first couple of bites. They offered red pepper and spicy olive oil for additional seasoning to the personal pie. Service is attentive and they come often to refill water and pour some more wine.

I had brunch and had no wait (around 10:30am) so I am not sure if it is b/c of the bad economy or what. Had the french toast with potatoes and bacon. mmmm, for $15, you also get tea/coffee and OJ, not a bad deal!

Good stuff! Â Came here for the prix-fixe brunch and had the special (an arepa with scrambled eggs and chorizo), although the huevos rancheros received some serious consideration. Â The plate was huge, even without the black beans and rice. Â I tried washing it down with a mimosa and some coffee, but still couldn't finish it all. Â All this and no wait for a table. Â After standing on line for more than one disappointing brunch in this town, I can tell you I'll be back.
Kimchi ramen and kale salad. Â Just get it. Â Please get it. Â Amazing.

This new ippudo is wonderful. It is a lot more open than the original restaurant downtown, has a shorter waiting time, even a little upstairs area that could probably be used for a small group, and all with the same great food we have all come to know and love from this name. I recommend this branch over the downtown location if only for the better lighting and shorter wait time.

Pricey but worth every bite!! The food here is so good!! Tiny place, gets crowded, the hostess at the door is a bit snobby but whatever I ll take it, for the delicious variety of flavors I ll over look the attitude received at the door. Â Great selection of Wine amazing service and just an all around fabulous experience! Will be back for more!!

This place is awesome. So glad I came here. Great beef brisket sandwich (and u can even ask for a fattier cut). Is it as good ad Franklins in Austin TX, oh hell no. But it's still really good and you can get away with spending under $10 for lunch provided u order tap water - if u have learned nothing from me in all these years it's that u must never let restaurant profit by ordering such things as soda. The sandwich includes add ons like cole slaw, jalapeÃ±o shreds, etc. Nice not to have to schlep up to Dinosaur for good bbq (this place much better anyways imo).
Loco Tuesday's makes my week. As well as that, their variety of foods and drinks are off the charts, and overall it's a very clean and well kept place. Would definitely recommend the calamari!

Was recommended to me by a bunch of people that work in the area. Hands down the best pizza I've had in New York (so far, been to 8 places). Shit, I've only been here for 11 days...(goes to search for closest retail location with spanks for men) If I'm getting pizza near SoHo, I won't go anywhere else.
Solid food. The friendliest staff. Busy brunch still gets to the table in just the right amount of time. Also a great place to go sit and read your morning paper.
Great neighborhood Bistro. Â  Anthony was really fabulous. Â And everything can be made gluten-free. Ravioli and a red velvet cake. Â Wow!

We were keen to trying this place bc of the reviews. Food was 3.5 and service was 2. There apparently was a system failure and they lost al their orders. It still took 45+ for our food. And another 25 min for our bill. Several diners walked out bc of frustration. The chicken was good but slightly dry. The ceviche was spot on with the grilled shrimp and roasted corn nuts. Sad about the service bc we would've stayed for dessert.

Cool spot. Definitely worth a visit to all the BBQ inclined! More importantly, they have one of the best, if not the best, selections Rye though. They have this one called Blue Hill (or something like that)... so good, so expensive ($35 a glass), but well worth it. You'll definitely see me at the bar! Rye makes me feel good. I give Fette Sau four stars on their Rye selection alone. Although I recognize the brilliance of this restaurant, it was actually Fette Sau that inspired me to give up meat! Like any all-American country boy, I grew up on the type of food Fette Sau serves. So after years in the big city, I welcomed a little slice of back home. However, after gorging there one night, I was just so full and bloated that I felt disgusted with myself. It all tasted very good though.

I don't completely understand the hype about this place. I think the idea of it is awesome. A fry place thats open late with a huge selection of home-made sauces?! How can that possibly go wrong? It can go wrong by overpricing the crap out of something that should be humble food. The place is tiny, which isn't bad. The bad part is the huge line that forms to get fries. The fries themselves are fantastic. Thick with a crispy outer shell with a soft and tender interior. The sauces are tasty, but all mayo based and can get a bit heavy and fatty. The food here is great, but its not worth the hype, line or price in my opinion.
Great beer and liquor selection! Â Bar tender chick at night is very knowledgeable about the beers. Â Wish i could try the food menu but the kitchen closes at 12 midnight.
I just love this place, It has great food with fantastic service. I had the spaghetti with calamari and it was awesome!!! Will be coming back for sure!

Oh this place...the food, the food is really tasty, good old fashioned comfort food. The margaritas are great, and the atmosphere is wonderful. Why only 3 stars? The service. UGH! We live in the neighborhood so we come here fairly frequently, often enough that the bad service isn't just a one off. It's ALL THE TIME. They have a small staff but it's like they could really care less. 15 minutes to get a drink order in? That's just crazy. Last time we were there, throughout the whole night the server kept standing over by the POS system talking to a bartender. Every table around us was complaining, no one could get an order, get a refill or get their check. It seemed so obvious but the guy really didn't seem to care at all. In fact, neither did the bartenders or anyone else. Our drinks actually got made and then sat on the bar for a good 5 minutes. I almost went up and got them myself. We keep going back despite the crappy service because I like the food, but this last time may have been the last. With so many places to pick from in nyc why go somewhere that doesn't seem to want the business? TLDR: pro: food is tasty con: service sucks, always, without fail

Friendly and efficient staff. Â Saturday night at 8 pm, place was pretty packed. I didn't think the pizza was anything special to me. Â The crust was too thick for my liking. Â I think the best one we had was the pepperoni pizza. Â Don't think I'll be coming back.

Oh how I love thee! Let me count the ways... Peasant salad has a lot of olives. Roasted lemon potatoes are fantastic. Rice pilaf is flavorful. Grilled octopus is succulent. Beets; the fact they offer it is a plus. Kyclades Special solves the problem when you can't decide should you have shrimps or scallops. Bass (forgot which one) is in-friggin'-credible. Free dessert, best sweet thang I had in a long time. Thanks to my cute mistress, my Greek senses have awakened! And oh yeah, thanks Taverna Kyclades, for taking care of my burning desire to consume all delicious seafood possible!

Came here for Sat brunch, right before the rush started. Everything on the menu looked interesting and good. I was in the mood for something sweet but also meaty... So went with the chicken and waffles, with banana foster sauce. Ask for a rub or flavor on the chicken (flip the menu)! Â The waitress didn't mention it but I asked for the spicy and they delivered. Banana foster sauce for the waffles was amaaaazing! I was spooning that stuff up and eating it alone. The spicy chicken was also very flavorful (though chicken itself was on the dry side) and the spiciness worked really well with the syrupy sweet sauce. Waffles themselves were stale/bland tasting though and would have been super boring by themselves, so I'd say the side sauce is a must-add. The reason for the bad stars though.... They forgot my bub's entree, completely. As in the waitress somehow forgot to order it...and since she never came by to check up on us or make eye contact we basically weren't able to tell her til I was almost done with my meal. Luckily we had a side of fries as an 'appetizer' so he could munch on those while we waited 30 mins for them to re-order (As a side note - their regular fries are NOT worth it, they're ridiculously priced for what are literally the most normal, regular typical fries ever). The eggs in purgatory he eventually received were alright - interesting combo with the hot sauce. Luckily the waitress comped his meal. Usually that would redeem a place, but not this time. Their service in general was horrible - waitress seemed like she had the potential to be nice, but she never made eye contact with anyone! Want water? Have fun walking up to someone yourself. She also had a habit of walking very very fast with her head turned away from others, so good luck snagging her even if she's right behind your table. It made for a really frustrating experience and the food wasn't nearly amazing enough to make up for it.

Chicken and rice, chicken and rice, what to get but chicken and rice. Everyone tells me to go to the Halal cart to get chicken and rice. So after landing, the first stop was to get some chicken and rice. I enjoyed the food and thought it was good but I think it would have been more enjoyable if I was drunk because it seems like the type of food you want when you are buzzed or drunk

I plan to be back at Grape and Grain in two shakes of a lamb's tail, like greased lightening, posthaste, in a jiffy minute, hell-for-leather fast. And with bells on. 'Cause I think I found my new favorite wine bar. Reasons why: The artichoke pizza. A huge plate of olives, which were *all* good. Matt, the lovely bartender. Swivelling bar stools. A bathroom that I'd like to duplicate in my own apartment. A wonderful list of whites and reds that any wine lover (and by wine lover, I mean wine lover, not wine snob) could sink her teeth into. It doesn't hurt that my first visit visit here, last night, was with my dear friend J, who announced -- over Gruner and beet salad -- her brand spanking new, hot off the fire, city-hall, full-of-love marriage to a great man who I hope will cherish her forever, as she deserves. Congrats, lady J! And congrats, Grape and Grain, for winning me over. I can't wait to come again!

Ok, first, pardon my english. Second, luckily, I had a chance to try their food (in huge quantities (-: ) and to compare it with food in Serbia because I am from Serbia. I couldn't believe that some Serbian meals are even better 5000 miles away from Serbia... Thanks to big effort of the owner, which I saw by myself, that everything has to be perfect. And it is. Definitely, worth to try! Finaly, i've spent there couple months, crazy people in there, with the owner the craziest one. I CAN'T WAIT TO GO THERE AGAIN ! ! ! probably the best korean restaurant in k-town for soon dooboo...hands down. Â their tofu is homemade, and has this gritty weird texture...that's definitely an acquired taste. Â if you go as often as i do, you will learn to love it too. seafood soon doo boo, all the way!! their dumplings is also extremely good. Â This is the ONLY thing i allow myself to order whenever i go here. Â it can't be beat.
Just heavenly! Â I love it. Big portions and just a great taste of freshly homemade noodles.

This restaurant is so cute cute cute. Â Its only the cutest little corner and its great for people watching, yes even from inside the restaurant. Â We actually stopped in at a wine store and picked out something because they let you BYOB. Â I had the cavatelli and soft shell crab. Â The cavatelli was amazing. Â I would get it again as an entree and my friend got the chicken and the meatball sliders, not sure how he managed to eat it all. Â But, he said it was too good to pass up. Â The dessert was just okay, I've had better. Â I can't wait to go back, maybe for brunch next time.

Stone Street offers many dining options. Â But none of the choices merit a trip to this short Â yet historic stretch of the Financial District, were it not for the attractive setting--pedestrian-only, cobble stone, with outdoor seating. Adrienne's surely benefits from this unique setting. Â But this is a pizza joint that could hold its own profitably in any part of the city. Â The large square pizza is an amazing deal for about $15-20. Â The crust is crispy to the touch and taste, and the cheese and sauce are a delightful combination. Â Adrienne's also has a number of other Italian options, but most are quite mediocre ... I guess you cannot get a baby without the bath water, so to speak. Bring your friends to Adrienne's on a weekday evening, and rejoice in the thought of breaking bread with 20-something members of the 1% club, making a healthy living at 85 Broad. Â If you are what you eat, you might yet become a well-paid banker.

This restaurant makes me happy that I no longer live in New York City. If I ever had to pay $150 for 11 pieces of mediocre omokase again, id have to shoot myself in the head. Again and again. Not to say LA and SF don't have equally pricey sushi experiences - they do - but any restaurant that's upwards of a bill per person really has to justify it. Yasuda would at least be a major source of contention in those cities, and definitely not the toast of the town, the way it is in NY. Now, on to the specifics: None of the fish have origin statements, so you're just as likely to be eating snapper from Oyster Bay as you are the Sea of Japan. (That's, of course, if they had snapper, which they don't). Nor do they have amberjack. The fish selection is surprisingly limited). I asked for Amaebi (sweet shrimp), which should be raw, and got a normal, cooked prawn. (If you don't have it, just own up to it and say so). The scallop, an easy home run for most restaurants, was really quite average. And my Uni was served half way through the meal. (I saw another patron receive it as his second piece). So much for a well-thought out omokase. Honestly, sushi dojo is a much better NYC option at half the price.

This place blows. First let's talk about the line and it's truly uninspiring way they deal with it. Why bother having a line if you're just going to pick and choose who gets in from the freaking line! Why bother waiting! Retarded way if dealing with a line Next let's talk about the service, or lack there Â of. We come in and they seat us and we order. We're thinking that it'll be 20 minutes for a pie to come. Let's go 1 hour into pour seating and we find out they're cleaning the fucking oven. Really?? Tell your customers that before sitting them! We would have gone else where for f sake! I'm surprised they're still in business If I could give no stars I would, don't ever come here. Ever

Awesome. Based on the Chipotle style of ordering (but better), there are an almost overwhelming number of options. I haven't tried everything on the menu, but I'm getting there slowly. For the best value, go with the platter. You get three of the premium fill-its and a pita on the side. For $2 more you get almost double the food and can build your own pita, ensuring the ingredients are evenly distributed just they way you like it. It's a win-win. It's a lot of food but everything is so delicious you'll have no problem finishing. What makes it even better is that every meal comes with FREE HUMMUS, and this hummus is delicious. The food: All of the meats are delicious. Steak is my favorite (perfectly medium rare....YUM), with chicken and gyro both coming in at a close second. The falafel is also great. They'll even make it gluten free if you ask. If you only get one fill-it, make it the babaganoush. I could eat an entire tub of the babaganoush. It's my favorite thing on the menu. I also recommend the couscous, spanish eggplant if you like spicy, and the beet salad. My girlfriend loves the veggie grape leaves. Portions are incredibly generous. You will not leave unsatisfied. Customer service is great. They're very accommodating and if they seem perturbed by all of your questions about what each of the delicious looking dishes on the line are, just remember that they get asked these same questions 10 million times a day. As I said before, if you have a gluten intolerance, just ask for the GF falafel and they'll make it fresh. Also, almost everything else on the main line is gluten free. My girlfriend and I seriously became obsessed with The H&P Co. for a while after discovering it and went like 4 times a week. If you're a regular, or plan on becoming one, ask them for rewards card when you check out. They don't advertise it, but it has saved me a few bucks, which is always great.
Decent, well done food. My pasta was a little salty, but my other dishes were quite tasty.
I was really impressed by Jungsik (pronounced Cheongshik). It deserves the rating as a Â Korean Michelin 2 star restaurant. And, it deserves the price! The sweet potato tart was amazing too!
Wolf and Deer is the best. Edwin and Frank, the bartenders, are great. Drinks are amazing. Atmosphere is lovely and the prices are fantastic!
Ridiculously good sandwiches. Don't bother with any of the sides,

I went here last night for dinner because I had heard good things and wanted to check it out. Â It started out as a fine experience but slowly went downhill. Â The food was mediocre and the host and server were drunk by the time we left. Â The host was so drunk that he came over to see how we were doing and was leaning all over me, seemingly unable to control himself. Â When we left it seemed the entire waitstaff was having a cigarette break and outside and didn't even look up. Â I will definitely not be going back.

I am so happy that this place opened near us! Affordable prices, yummy pasta, great customer service. What more can you ask? This is hands down the best Italian food you can get in the area. That's right, I said it.

Rudest server ever! stopped by for coffee and dessert one late afternoon. A server (kid with long hair) told me they "just don't do that". I asked again as the place was empty. He looked at me disgusted and pretty much asked Â me to leave. Will never come to this place. Unfortunate as i've heard the food was good. Then i went to Lievito next door, sweetest servers ever.
Food is wonderful ***Breakfast cut off time 11:45 Chicken meatball with pesto (highly recommend) Lobster roll with fries was good too I give three stars because the service is pretty bad..:(

Ippudo is easily the best ramen I've had. Lines and waiting for Ippudo can be crazy, but they make it easier by taking your number to call/text you when your table is ready. You can also have a drink at the bar while you're waiting if you wanna throw back a drink. Their happy hour is Monday through Thursday 5-7pm and 10pm to closing. Â  Their Hirata buns are so good. They're pricey at $9 for two but so worth it. I tend to go for miso ramen and their miso ramen is a good choice. I really like their broth and noodles. A bowl of ramen at Ippudo is a little pricier than your average bowl of ramen but you get what you pay for: quality ramen. It's so good that I went here multiple times during my last couple of trips to New York. When you're in New York, Ippudo is a must!

Came here on a Saturday night around 9pm, it was very busy, we waited 2 hours, but absolutely worth it! There will always be a wait, I mean that is expected from a good place no? It was actually my second time here (after Japan). First time was when I was a teenager-long before my palettes developed OR before I learned about fine gourmet foods. I have also tried a fair share of other ramen places in America, but I have to say Ippudo is definitely the best tasting one, the most similar to the great cafes in Japan! I LOVE every spoonful! I recommend it for every ramen lovers!
The Shrimp dumplings w/ black egg noodle soup is great. Â As well as rice noodles with mixed sauce. Â Infinite ice is a nice way to end the meal too.

I could spend an entire day at this all Italian market/restaurant. So much to see, smell and taste. I only wish I lived in New York so I could try the fresh pasta or buy the fresh fish. Eataly is like an Italian symphony, people behind the counter doing there business, like making pasta, cutting cheese, making pizza, brewing espresso. Had a sandwich at I Panini, one of the many restaurants. Ordered the Prosciutto di Parma with mozzarella, I loved the Prosciutto but thought the bread could have been better. Considering they have a bakery department. Some of the restaurants have table setting but otherwise you take your food to tables and stand to eat. This could be difficult depending on the time of day. We had to have a latte from Caffe Lavazza and cannoli from Pasticceria. Yummie, Yummie. Could I be in Italy? Yes!! This is a must see and eat for all you foodies!!!! They also have a great market with items you can only get in Italy. Mario Batali is a master. Â Praying that they will bring Eataly to Los Angeles.

Yes, I waited an hour for a table. Yes, it was freezing outside. And yes, I had about a million other things to do that day and was practically wasting my time. Let me say this: totally worth it. From the potato pancakes with the smooth herbed sour cream to the omelette to the tomato basil soup (and don't forget the hot chocolate!), almost all of the menu is delicious!! (i say almost because I'm not a huge fan of their signature mac and cheese... a liiil too cheesy for me) Ambiance: check Good service: check Cute, trendy, totally gay host: check (I forgot my credit card at the table and he definitely ran a block to chase me down! how cute!!) Anyway, definitely come here, you won't be disappointed BUT make reservations. OH and omg, did you know they are open overnight? BROWNIE POINTS.

I love when you accidentally find a place and you have no expectations and you're pleasantly surprised. Â Boqueria was just that. Â I had just flown in from LA and met up with my brother for a snack. Â We were on our way to someplace else, but then walked by Boqueria and then turned around and walked back in. Â It was the list of cheese at the front that lured us in. Â We shared a nice selection of cheeses, olives and a bottle of wine. Â We considered eating food there but we were waiting for our parents to arrive and thought we should wait. Â We're such good kids! Â The food we saw (but didn't taste) will definitely bring me back the next time I'm in NYC.

Double Windsor is a great neighborhood bar that I've been to many a time. Awesome food and great beer selection. Here's why I can't give it 5 stars: - They stopped using Balthazar bread and now use Amy's. Amy's is alright, but it's a huge downgrade for the sandwiches (burger, pulled pork, chicken), which constitute most of the menu. Hopefully this is a short-term change! - The chicken sandwich is my favorite. Delish. But I personally prefer less meat on sandwiches. When I recently asked them to put 1 chicken breast patty on my sandwich instead of two, the kitchen incredibly said "no." According to them, because the Â meat is actually one chicken breast, pounded out, cut and piled on the sandwich, they wouldn't be able to use the other half. Even when I said I expected to pay full price, they wouldn't do it. So, instead of the kitchen throwing out the other half, I had to disassemble my sandwich and do it myself. - The seating situation in here is just annoying sometimes. We came here because my friend had heard that this is one of Anthony Bourdain's fave restos.
