Â Bathrooms are clean and sanitary. Perfect place for a date or a night out with friends!

Of all the restaurants I've hit up in the last few weeks, this one came in near the bottom of the list for me. The place has a good vibe and belongs in it's classy Chelsea location. It was a very clean place, but a bit too crowded (it was rainy a lot so the patio was closed...). Â  I ordered a chicken cobb salad- easy enough for any "cafeteria," right? Sadly, no. The salad and ingredients were all just okay, the chicken was overcooked and dry. A friend got the same salad but with steak, another got the mac n' cheese sampler, another got a roasted chicken (?) dish, and tomato basil soup. Everyone's dishes seemed good, just weren't anything spectacular like we'd been told to expect. Â All that bad stuff out of the way.... who wants to talk about the waiters? DAAMMNN!

I'll reserve final judgment until I visit again but based on my first visit: get over yourselves. We walk in, place is empty, two people behind the bar and no one acknowledges us. We looked at the menu and would have stayed but 2 mimutes later still no one has addressed us and we are standing at the bar right in front of the lady. Maybe she was on the blob. Like it or not they are in the service industry so if they want to stay in business then they need to up the 'service' part of their business. I'll go again soon and hope I get to retract the bad first impression.

These are one of the cheapest and the biggest Vietnamese sandwich you'll find in New York City. Â With that being said the price has risen again and now the roast pork sandwich costs 4.50. Â This is the second price increase I have seen since I discover this place. Â Part of me is happy that I will get less coins back, but the cheap part of me doesn't want to pay that extra quarter. The bread here is more "toasted" or harder than Paris. Â I personally like a cruncher bread but I can understand people who don't. Â You have to be carefully biting into the sandwich because if you are likely to scrap the roof of your mouth your first time. Â However I have master this skill avoid doing so every time. Â Just remember nothing worth while comes easily and keep at it. The roast pork is also harder here which I also like. Â I love the texture and the sauce they use. Â I could just eat a bowel of the roast pork by itself. Â That would a be a dream come true for me or a heart attack. The sandwich here are packed to the brim but it is mostly at the middle of the sandwich, where you first start eating since they are cut in half. Â The sandwich gets smaller as you get to the end of them which make it easier to eat. I also appreciate this place shut down on 6/24/2013 when the water was off. Â I know they make an attempt to be clean. Â Paris was still open and manage to run a business without running water. Â I am not sure how they clean anything.

This restaurant is teeeny. Â My friend had warned me that this was a small restaurant and I wasn't expecting it to be THAT small. Graffiti is about the size of some other restaurant's lobby area. Â  With that said, they make the most out of the space and it's really a cute, cozy space. Â Most tables need to be shared. Â Our party of 4 had to share a table with a couple who obviously were on a 2nd or 3rd date, which made it kinda awkward (probably more for them than us). Â  Food is excellent. Â We ordered an array from the menu and was really pleased that the kitchen can accommodate and prepare half a dish with meat and the other half vegetarian. Â Each dish was really balanced with various spices and textures. Â Loved the hummus pizza, pork and eggplant buns, and we had a yummy hazelnut chocolate dessert as well. P.S. Â you need to check out the bathroom at Graffitti. Â It's the teeniest bathroom I've ever been in.

Where to even begin with Northern Spy - everything is spectacular. While I haven't paid it a visit since the new executive chef and pastry chef have taken residence (May 2014 from my understanding), I can speak to its fare under the former chef and pastry chef. In one word, extraordinary. The menu is delicately crafted, seasonal and local. The food is by far some of the best I've ever had (and I've had many 5-star, wonderful meals). Don't be afraid to ask questions about what will be on your plate. The staff are well-educated and willing to answer questions. A few menu stand-outs: the pork stick rolls, duck fat fries, lamb burger (lunch) and pickled eggs. We once had the BURGER for dinner, which was a special. It was honestly the best burger I've ever had; I wish it was a menu staple (hint hint, powers that be). Check out the Sunday Supper menu, too. This three-course meal for $27 is a steal. And don't be shy during lunch hours - I think some of their better food is served during that time, including a usually insane pastry on the counter. Save some room! The dining room is cozy, to say it kindly. Sometimes things are tight, especially during busy nights and holidays. But one simply can't fault Northern Spy a single star for its square feet. Plus the staff and hostess (Alyssa/Alissa - however you spell it) are warm, wonderful and top-notch. If I could eat three meals a day here, I would. Sadly, my wardrobe and wallet would have a few things to say about that :)

I'd been looking forward to this restaurant for awhile and knew I was probably in for a good meal when I realized they are owned by the same people as The Smith. I got the Jane benedict with spinach and poached eggs over a shrimp and crab cake. Â I actually wasn't a huge fan of the cake itself- there was a lot of breading, which to me, made it taste oily. Â I really prefer crabcakes that highlight the meat rather than smother it with breadcrumbs. Â The hashbrowns it came with were DELICIOUS though; I could've eaten a whole plate of those. Â My friend got the vanilla bean french toast which we both enjoyed. Â  Overall, a good meal. Â They also were super accommodating when my out-of-town friend got lost on the way and was 45 minutes late for our reservation- they were still able to squeeze us in despite a busy Saturday brunch crowd!

Minimalistic stunning, airy, classy and relaxing. Simple, quality food - farm to table - with a 'chef's interpretation' on each dish. The salads are meals in of themselves and fish is perfectly prepared. Great wine list!

On my trip to NY last week, we tried many pizza places in search of the best. Lombardi's was my FAVORITE! So delicious- perfectly cooked thin pizza, with fresh mozzarella and tomato sauce. YUM! We got ours with pepperoni and garlic-sauteed spinach. Our waitress was not the friendliest, but the food was great!

Spending extra time in the Financial District after working with a client. Walked a few blocks to check out this place. Unfortunately, it was closed for a private event. My client caught wind my disappointment and luckily - they deliver. This was one of my top 3 meals. Ever. I had the Taste of Maine which includes the trio of rolls and a side of massive crab claw. Each bite was HEAVEN. Soft, buttery, delicious, and pure. No filler. Healthy servings of quality seafood nestled in clouds of bun. I will absolutely be making this a must-have every time I visit NY.

I too am a huge Beyonce fan & I must admit I learned of this restaurant because they frequent here. Well...I was thoroughly pleased. I came from NJ to celebrate my B'day and although the wait was 45 min the Hostess was so kind to get me in sooner; and not only that but since I told her I would wait outside in my car, she came out and personally got me and my family...who does that?!?! The food was amazing! I had the EGGS HUNTINGTON...Poached eggs, buttermilk biscuit with hollandaise. Since I told my waiter I didn't eat pork, he substituted the ham for spinach. To top it off...the Mimosa's were fantastic! I was even surprised with 2 complimentary Jelly Donut Balls with a candle...xoxo! I have found a little hidden treasure here & I will def be back!!!
Best burger I've ever had. Â Period. Reasonable portions (but they don't stuff you) Â Tasty fries and good beer selection. Â What more do I want?

Fish, don't you ever change. So I kinda love seafood (I've developed an allergy to shrimp in the last 5 years, and that's one of my life's greatest tragedies), I think that should be made clear before I go on in review. And Fish is definitely the place for you if you LOVE seafood. They have a bomb red, white and blue special (6 oysters or clams with a choice of a class of red, white or a can of pbr) for $8, they have a lobster FEAST (new england clambake style), all you can eat crabs on the weekends, and about every kind and combo of sea creatures you might want (scallops with bacon, fresh uni, shrimp scampi, tons of fish, seafood paella...). Cheap seafood might sound iffy, but not at Fish. Everything is fresh and delicious in all its briny seafood goodness. The wait can get pretty long (but you can get food to go!), so I would definitely make reservations. It's in the village though so you can window shop and walk around the neighborhood to pass the time. The restaurant itself isn't very huge and can be kind of a tight squeeze, but well worth it!

Tiny as fck but that adds to the romantic, charming environment that this place exudes. Went here with several coworkers after work one late evening. It was packed but we were able to get a high top table. We were a bit tight and had some bags on us from work, but that didn't affect our experience. The food was fantastic - we mostly got seafood so shrimp, squid, etc. Each one was cooked really well - not super chewy, delicious broth. We also got the patatas bravas - yumyumyum. Crispy, hot and a nice portion. Will come here again with less people probably. It gets tight with a group of 4/5 people here.

Brunch was quite good. Â I tried the pumpkin waffles and the omelet. Â The waffles were good but i wished they had a little more pumpkin flavor. Â The omelet was excellent. Â The cider mimosa tasted mostly of champagne. Â I'd go back but be sure to get there before 11 because that's when the crowds come.
food is good. They really try. Service is at its best... I like it. Nice hood place! I wish they have a better wine list --its too generic.

The place is wonderful. Not one bad thing to say about it. Shot sizes of wine are a great idea. Wine selection was interesting, I didn't recognize one label. My Primitivo was unbelievable. Mussels' broth was to die for, fresh mozzarella was light as air, everything was perfect. Guys, please, don't get spoiled by your success, the way some other great Astoria restaurants did. If you become very hot and trendy, please remember that restaurant hunters come and go, but long time Queens residents pay your rent.

I have to say I am a big fan marrow on toast, it was made perfectly, enjoyed it a lot. Our waiter Carlos, was very good and also the owners came by at our table which were very nice. Highly recommended
Very cute place with great food and outstanding service. Â We had fish, meat, octupus, and desserts. Â Everything was delicious and authentic. Â Make reservations way in advance.
great ambiance/atmosphere very good service very tasty drinks

clearly 1 of the best places for sushi in NY. NOT for sushi amateurs. i don't mean for Â that to be an insult, but it'll be hard for to appreciate sushi of this caliber one considers a california roll sushi, or the concept of wasabi placed under the fish is confusing. just go to sushi samba if that's the case and save yourself the trip and money. otherwise, the toro is phenomenal. sit at the sushi bar w yasuda and have him give you every type of toro, yellow tail and any other fish you like. personally, i love the tazmanian trout. it's fantastic. keep in mind, yasuda will keep feeding you at the pace you eat until you say stop or pause. don't be shy about saying either, because he won't be shy about tossing more your way. will certainly be going back whenever i can afford it!

I've come here twice now. Â The first time, Laura Bush and the twins were having lunch behind me. Â And Isaac Mizrahi was dining to my right. Â It's that kind of spot. That being said, the food is tasty and the decor is gorgeous (duh). Â I will fully admit that I contemplated throwing the beautiful silverware into my handbag...who needs a full set anyway? Â  It's just a pain in the ass to get a reservation sometimes. Â I mean, unless you're, like, famous.

By far the coolest hangout in Cobble Hill and if you go after 10, surprisingly easy to get a group table. Â Beautiful space with glass and exposed brick that matches those multi-million $ brownstones all over Henry St. Â I've found the food to be hit or miss - love the meatballs and white anchovy bruschetta; think the paninis are too bland and thick. Â Josh S - next time skip the baked eggs (you're right, too dry) and go for the poached eggs with tomato hollandaise...to die for.

Got the potatoes pancakes, Korean bbq chicken, and bimbimbop....seasoned well with korean spices, all the sides were worth trying, and the hot tea has a smokey rice and honey taste. My fave of all the sides was the crunchy fish...I had extras :) Only reason I didn't give a 5 is bcuz my friends suggest they had korean food in Maryland that is a lil better. Overall, this was a great first time Korean experience. I lived in ATL for a while and had yet to try it.
Sliders. Cheese fries. Guinness milkshake. Ridiculous. Tiny little place gets packed on the weekends but its all a good vibe and good food. Would go again.

Fries! Â I salivate. Â Love it! Â I finally got here, after wanting and wanting. Â What took me so long?! A bit crowded, not a lot of seats, but come on, how much rent are you going to raise off fries. Â OK so I only liked the sweet mango chutney mayo, I didn't really like the other two. Â I even put some vinegar on some, reminding of jolly old England. Â I love the cones of fries, and the bar has little holes so you can put them in. Â Only 2 tables and a 4 seater bar, so it's tight, and when we were leaving there was a whole bunch of people, doing a double row, so it was tight getting out. Â I love the sacks and sacks of potatoes as decorations. Â I liked the refried twice fried fries that sneak in. Â I'm going back here soon. Â Sorry to gush so much but I liked this place.
Love it! And we didn't even eat yet..you can just get a good vibe walking into this place! Everyone is friendly and looks happy to be here. My stomach is rumbling...

The hype is worth it. The price? Well, that's personal preference. Are you willing to pay $2.70 for a deliciously authentic macaron? I sure am. Tiny place that can't be missed because they have huge displays of macarons in the window. I went on a rainy Tuesday afternoon, and there was STILL a line, but it wasn't packed. The store sells other items, such as perfume (?) and chocolates, but I wouldn't spend my money on anything else but the macarons. They had 16 flavors available, when I went, and I wanted one of each, so I got a box of 18. It cost me $55, but this is where I splurge. I may not buy pretty clothes, and I may not buy fancy electronic gizmos, but I WILL buy macarons! Customer service varied on the employee. The male employee didn't seem as friendly, but the woman at the register was peppy and cheery... probably to distract you from the fact that you just dropped $50 on 18 silver dollar sized snacks. So Laduree has gotten much recognition for having some of the best (if not THE best) macarons in the city. After trying them, I can see why. They don't skimp on the filling, but it doesn't overwhelm you either. It's a nice ratio of cookie to filling, and the flavors shine. Pistachio tasted like Pistachio (which is not too common, surprisingly), and the fruit flavors were refreshing and tart, while the sweet flavors were not too sweet... juuust right. Their featured flavor "Strawberry Marshmallow Candy" or something of that sort, was awesome. Tasted just like strawberry milk, which I love. Caramel is my favorite flavor of all time, and theirs were perfect. Of course, the filling is caramel, but there's also a hint of buttery saltiness that adds a whole 'nother level to the flavor profile. Mmm... Laduree may be among my few exceptions of places that I revisit in the city. Another reason why they are so expensive is apparent with their packaging. They have beautiful and/or cute packaging. They have these new color Hello Kitty boxes, that Hello Kitty fans will adore. I was tempted to get one, but the beautiful light blue classic French box caught my eye. I'm going to try to collect as many different boxes as I can... that'll be one way I justify my future trips to Laduree. Anyways, Laduree is a must-visit store for macaron lovers in the city, but if you're not the type to splurge on sweets, then I wouldn't recommend it... although, you do only live once, so why not start with a macaron?
This is my favorite pizza in all of NY!! I can't get enough of their artichoke slices. Yes, sometimes there is a line but it's worth the wait:) SO AMAZING!!!!!
Very good burgers & sides with an emphasis on organic and sustainable ingredients. Onion rings were great. Will be back to try the more exotic meats.

While they have great sandwiches, the fact that they will not remove a single sprig of cilantro for someone who is allergic is ridiculous. Â I will not eat there again. Â There are too many restaurants in NY to deal with someone who refuses to make any modifications even for someone who has an allergy!!!

One of my best Japanese places in the town. Everything is in high quality, much better than how it looks. Never tried Japanese hot pot and pork tonsoku before, they are so good! Especially pork tonsoku, crispy outside, tender inside with the right amount of flavor. Addicted. Must make reservation ahead.

The Bad - Says $10 minimum in order to use credit card The Good - Yummy dumplings (veg, pork, chicken) - Yummy sesame sandwiches (it is on the top 100 sandwiches list--heard it's better in chinatown and cheaper) The Bottomline- Worth checking out especially if you are a fan of dumplings. Their sesame sandwich is pretty awesome: either pork or beef. Both good as well as veggie. Their steamed buns are something to try out too. Veggie one not the red bean. This location is a bit better than the union square one.

We bought out the small private room in the back of the restaurant for our wedding celebration brunch, We actually got married in the room as well. We had 19 of our closest friends and family, although the room comfortably seats 23. After the ceremony, we had a 1 hour cocktail hour accompanied by pork nuggets and fried cheese curds served family style. There was more than enough room for people to stand and mingle. Following the cocktail hour, we enjoyed a brunch menu of 4 entree options selected by us, along with 3 sides which they generously additionally offered us. We also had a personalized printed menu with a photo and title for our special day. We purchased our favorite cake from a local bakery which was presented and then sliced and plated by them gratis. The pacing and abundance of food and drink was perfect. We were able to play our own pre-approved music through the restaurant's sound system adding to the lively feel we wanted for our wedding. The room also has its own volume control and heating and a/c which kept the room cool on the warm Fall day. The decor was perfect for us as is with the additional of simple hydrangeas and gingham placecards but could easily lend it's self to any theme due to its simplicity. We really can't say enough good things about the restaurant which was chosen by us firstly because of the care that is put into producing food that is both simple and uniquely crafted resulting in a phenomenal flavor experience or in a word, delicious! The restaurant's event coordinator came in on her day off to make sure everything was perfect. Never once did we have to worry about or ask for anything. We requested our server due to great service we received on our last trip East last summer. Prior to the wedding we ate here 4 times including our dinner the night before for some friends and family who came from out of town. I would like to point out that I no longer live in Brooklyn contrary to my Yelp profile. Char No.4 is always a destination for us while we are in NY. We were happy to learn that we were their 1st wedding. The level of customer service we received was only exceeded by the staff's excitement around the event. Char No.4 now feels like family.
DELICIOUS! If you order delivery they will do it... and fast!

Had a delicious brunch here today. The vanilla bean French Toast was to die for! We got that and the egg white spinach omelette which was also tasty. The only thing negative I would say is that the tables are so close together. It definitely felt packed in there.

Most important thing: worth the hype and worth the price. Walked up to what looked like a little hut, ordered "the dirty." From the minute I saw it steaming on the skillet I knew it would be good. Bread was thinner than in most grilled cheeses, it's buttered up and well toasted. Not too much cheese, all the ingredients went perfectly together. Left me wanting another one immediately after. I actually think I'm going to have to get one once a week, and I am someone who really cares about my diet. Enough said. If you enjoy grilled cheese at all, it is a must. Yes you could probably make some of these at home (which I might), but just not the same. Plus they deliver too! Enjoy. (I chose 4 stars because I wish it was an actual restaurant with seating. If the weather is bad you are out of luck..... which I was tonight because it was raining.)
Truly authentic Italian food. Very nice staff. A meal I will remember for a long time. 10/10

I want this lasagna all day, every day. As a newly-converted vegan, I've been dying for a well-made lasagna, and I've been disappointed in all the vegan restaurants in the city. This was one of the first places I've found that offer a vegan lasagna that ISN'T raw. I couldn't even tell that it was made with eggplant instead of actual pasta. The dish was so flavorful that all of those "healthy vegan" swaps went undetected. I'm fairly certain celery was involved, which seemed unusual to me, but I liked it. I can't wait to try brunch here.

Really enjoyed this place! Went with two girlfriends. Got a great bottle of Chianti, and I don't normally like Chianti. Loved the tuna tartare and calamari for starters. Then had a great pasta with truffle oil and wonderfully cooked cod. The staff was knowledgable, polite, and quick.

the beer selection at this place allows me to forgive it for the fact that 1) it's named after a U2 album 2) it's in an absolute nightlife wasteland and 3) some of their beers are a bit overpriced. like i said, the beer here is the draw. very much geared toward the high ABV beer geek kind of crowd - often they tap rare beers that they don't even have the alcohol content posted, which is somewhat terrifying. heavy on porters, stouts (imperial, oatmeal and traditional irish), strong ales and IPAs, which is right up my alley. if you're a nerd for belgians, you're better off somewhere else - you've got a lot (read: too many) options elsewhere in the city. never had the food, but i could see it being a slight step up from your typical pub grub. i discovered today that they have "IPA fries" and i'm not quite sure what that means, but chances are better than not that i'd like it. oh, it's also across the street from my office, which is both a positive and a negative. positive because my job drives me to drink quite often, negative because i'd almost never go there on a weekend due to its proximity to work (and everything else that goes on around the ESB...). give it a shot if you like good beer and you're in the neighborhood. pretty much every neighborhood south of 59th has a similarly themed bar, though, so i wouldn't go out of my way for it.

Hyped crap. Â It's a freakin' sandwich, go make one. Â Go eat something interesting. Â This is NYC. Â Go get some brazilian, indian, tibetan, italian, go get something better. Â Go to a good american place with something going on. Â Get some GREEK food. Â Not worth your money or time. Â The food belongs in an overpriced part of Manhattan. Â If thats your kind of thing you will think it's special, but it's not. Â This food does NOT represent Astoria well at all.

I had the Veggie Burger with fries and loved both! The fries were perfectly soft yet crispy and the burger was juicy and had a great flavor! It was probably one of the better veggie burgers I've ever had. The service was also great- very fast and friendly. Pricing was about average. So overall, I was very satisfied!

This place came highly recommended by my dinner companion, as she was excited to take me into the city for my last night. Of course I ordered the beef brisket on white bread and it was delicious. Perfectly seasone and tender with the correct fat to meat ratio. Every bite better than the last. I was a little surprised to see it didn't come with French fries.... Maybe that's normal in NY, but in the end I was stuffed without them. My friend ordered the pastrami Reuben and confirmed that her sandwich was equally delicious. We had a very attentive server that made sure we had plenty of refills. I think we were lucky because the place was pretty busy but we didn't have to wait for a table. Also our server seemed to always be nearby if needed. They have a cute little sleigh on their patio, that I probably should have capitalized a photo op, but it was cold outside.

The staff is friendly and attentive. The food- I had the Pork Bon Mise to eat and the Rye Devil to drink- was FANTASTIC! I need to get here with much more regularity. If you like hanging out on Fulton then this is where you need to go for good food and drinks.

A dig near my place. Â Open when it's warm. Â It's usually pretty crowded but if you stalk tables like an Asian it's all good. Â I'm Asian so people are intimidated by my crossed arms, watch checkin', and eye rollin'. Â Imma real threat to folks in the UWS. Pat Lafrieda meat for their burgers. Â I've had a few and the consistency can be a little meh. Â More often than not though you'll get a decent burger. Â Wish they toasted their buns. Beer is fucking expensive. Â Just bring your own. Â I doubt they'd give a damn. Â I saw some people bring their own food and take up the table space. Â Seriously, gtfo if you didn't at least order one thing from the counter. I tried their cold cauliflower soup. Â Flavor was good but it needed a good blend. Â Cauliflower was still kinda chunky. Â Immersion blender, they don't have one it seems.

I finally found a BBQ joint that lived up to it's hype. Â I can't wait to go back. Â The prices were reasonable, the staff was warm and happy, the food outstanding. Â They even had my favorite beer, Kentucky Bourbon Barrel Beer. Â The only disappointing thing was that my corn bread was bland and a bit stale but I will forgive them for that. Â  I loved the decor and that the seats were not on top of one another. Â I can't wait to go back. Â Definitely make reservations though. It gets very crowded.

Cute, little intimate restaurant. Servers look like real Parisians. Excellent location. We had a simple mixed green salad that just had different kinds of lettuce. Had a fabulous, sweet onion dressing that made the salad so delicious. I had skirt steak with fries. They were skinny, golden and friend to perfection. A little bit garlicky. the steak was buttery, juicy and delicious. My wife had the pork tenderloin with black rice. Very good. Great NYC dining experience! It was our first and one we will remember. P.S. The sodas aren't bottomless here like they are back home. They charge you for everyone! Oops.

Had the spicy Tuna roll, vegan gyoza, miso soup and 2 Sapporo drafts. Everything was great, the gyoza especially. Waiter was a bit OCD and insisted on air-drumming throughout most of his charade. I'm sure he's a nice guy. I'll surely be back for take-out and maybe to dine-in on a busier night when I am not as high.

Ambiance is excellent. Price is bad. When I first arrived at the restaurant I was enamored. It is at the end of an alley and feels like you've been transported away from Manhattan and into a log cabin. The upstairs is spacious, candle lit, and romantic. The spaciousness of the upstairs cannot be over-emphasized. It doesn't feel like an NYC restaurant. However, I ordered the $25 stew and was still hungry at the end of dinner. The waitstaff was great but the price and small amount of food will keep me from coming back often.

I love this place! I work right in the empire state building and the place is right up the block. Also being able to get plastered and make my way home is a plus. The 11am-7pm happy hour is great for getting buzzed at lunch or for after work. Look out for the $5 margaritas, cosmos, and martinis, and pretty big portions of nachos. Recently went again for a friend's birthday and the bill was around $115 bucks for like 8 of us. No complaints here!

5 stars just for the burgers. Seriously, probably the best burger I have ever had in my life. I thought Stand was good, but this place...amazing. It tends to be crowded which can be annoying, and sitting right by the bar, but if you can sit outside, it makes the whole thing even better. Service is always very good and staff is friendly. Go here!!!

This place is so cute. Love the decor. I have to come back and try the food again. I was having a shitty day, so I can't really judge the food. The service was great, so I will be coming back. My friend had the duck and loved it. He's a picky eater, so I trust his judgement!

I was at Pace University for an event that ended around 9pm on a Tuesday. Not much going around this area (especially post Sandy) but my homeslice introduced me to this spot! Also, I was still on a little bit of a Cinco de Mayo high, so the experience was even more fun. You get tex-mex and seafood. It's bright, colorful, and casual. Tuesdays are for taco specials! They had two dollar tacos; the crawfish taco was three dollars. It was actually a lot spicier than I thought it was going to be and pretty tasty. I never believe servers re: spice levels unless they're eastern. Haha - a little stereotypical, yes. I threw down some coronas, enjoyed a taco after a long and exhausting day with some of my best friends. Also, take into consideration that my girlfriend got the original frozen marg (a white color) and didn't like it too much. If you're looking for a chill night, decent food and don't want to spend too much come for the specials. Outside of that, I'm not sure if it's worth the cash. It's a fun spot though and the table service was good. Although, they weren't that busy on a Tuesday night way out under the BK bridge.

Solid all around. Friendly vibe and staff. Great food - mix of comfort, savory, and healthy. "Market Sides" are awesome (quinoa/avocado/tomatoes my fav). The Vegan Rancheros are awesome. As are the newly added vegan meatballs! Def my new go-to dish. Love the late delivery (until 11pm). 983 is a staple if you live in the neighborhood. Without a doubt.

I had dinner at Cafe Ghia, on what I learned was their opening night, last weekend and it was phenomenal. I can't believe it was opening night. The service was impeccable and it seemed like the menu was something that's been curated over time. The beer and wine selection was great. They had a few familiar choices, but I'm anxious to get back and try some of their beers that I've never heard of. On top of that, the prices were so reasonable that a second round was a no-brainer. The food was incredible. The homemade apple chutney was delicious and the cheeses they paired it with were great choices. That will a go to each time I'm there. I caught a glimpse of their brunch menu and I will undoubtedly go back for that. I highly recommend Cafe Ghia.
Great place, great atmosphere. Really good wine and awesome food ! And the service is very nice. I will recommend it to everyone !

LOVE this little spot! Happy hour from 5-10pm Monday - Sunday. Tasty lychee martinis & yummy tapas. I've tried the grilled asparagus, spring rolls, ginger chicken wings, calamari and the fried chicken dumplings all very tasty. The place itself is very narrow and gets packed fairly quickly. I would make a reservation a head of time or you may have to stand most of the evening. If you're not good with crowds this may not be the place for you. But if you like lychee martinis, yuenglings and yummy tapas for a reasonable price in NYC this is the place for you!

I don't often eat dinner near my office - Friday nights call for escaping the workplace. But it was raining and windy, so my bf and I were in the mood for ramen. Zutto had many open tables: intimate enough for a foodie couple, but a long communal table in the center of the room means that you can also bring a large group of friends here. We decided to share the Miami roll - I simply cannot resist salmon roe! The roll was decent, but I'm not sure if sushi is their strong suit. The ramen, on the other hand, was exactly what we were looking for! I ordered the tonkotsu hokkaido ramen while my bf had the miso ramen; we both had a topping of the onsen tamago (poached egg). The tonkotsu broth had amazing depth to its flavor, with sesame seeds and pickled ginger that were refreshing to eat between bites. The ramen noodles had great texture and seemed freshly made - nothing resembling the curly packaged noodles you will find at other ramen eateries. The pork jowl chashu was melt-in-your-mouth tender! And the poached egg was well-worth the extra $2: thin egg white that does not overwhelm the thick, creamy yolk inside. We finished by sharing the brioche bread pudding topped with caramelized banana and a scoop of vanilla ice cream. Warm, creamy, and sweet - this dessert hit all the right notes. The waitstaff was extremely knowledgeable and friendly, recommending certain dishes that were their most popular and good to share. I guess they are accustomed to having to explain everything to the high-maintenance clientele in this area: I watched one of the waitresses have to sit down with a needy couple for a full five minutes and explain the entire menu to them! All in all, this is a wonderful restaurant to get your ramen on, although it is a bit pricier than I would like. Although, it's well within the price point of this neighborhood.

Best macarons I've ever had. There is no question that these little treats are amazing. The store is stunning. I loved the girly Parisian decor. The service was very quick and the staff is really helpful. I tried quite a few of the macarons, and I didn't have a single complaint. The salted caramel was heavenly. Probably my favorite of the bunch. I also really liked the raspberry, congnac, and lemon basil. The flavors were really great. The prices are sky high, but these macarons really are THAT good. You can save a couple bucks if you don't get your macarons in a pretty gift box. Tourists: get the boxes. They're worth it. Plus, if you're taking these treats home with you; the boxes do a pretty good job of protecting the delicate macarons.

I know people have already said this...but Ancora is truly a hidden gem. Â Food is fantastic, but it is the service and friendly atmosphere that truly set it apart. Â Free grapa to close the meal is a great touch.

After reading the previous reviews, I think they are skewed upwards by the lack of competition in the west village in the Gluten-free genre. Â I give 2 stars for a combination of poor service and mediocre food. Â I was here on a Saturday night with a party of five and was crammed into a table for 4 (i.e.: 2 2-person tables pushed together). Â Then when the table of 2 next to us opened up we were not allowed to annex that space. Â The party of three to my left had 2 2-person tables, why shouldn't five people have three? Â Dock another star for our server also being extremely inattentive. Â I agree that the breadsticks were excellent, but the risotto was only mediocre. Â If you are going to name your restaurant after a dish it should be phenomenal.

Wow - what a disappointment. We came here for our 6 month anniversary and I had imagined a delicious, home-style farm to table experience, with vegetables shining through and plates that rose beyond the sum of their parts. What we got was much less than that - there were fresh vegetables, but the flavor combinations were maddeningly incomplete, or tone-deaf. Imagine mexican corn (with paprika, and some sort of mayonnaise...umm yum) completely overrun by terribly bitter sauteed radicchio. A strudel of fennel that had no flavor except for the dough, sitting in a red paste that had nothing - no flavor at all. Or how about a duck breast atop too few potatoes, screaming for some sauce to tie it all together (I initially thought the kitchen forgot to add it). Or a blackberry peach cobbler that didn't have nearly enough cobbler and peaches that had absolutely no flavor. I don't get it - this place seemingly has a lot going for it - cute, tucked away location, amiable JCrew model servers..and yet the only words I can think of to describe the culinary experience is aggressive. misguided, and immature. With some tweaks the kitchen could turn out truly complete dishes, and make this the nourishing place I had hoped for. Sorry to dump but it really fell short of expectations, especially for such an occasion.

First off, if anyone is a fan of 'Friends' then you have to try this place out. It's located in the building used for the 'Friends' show. They have a couple of amazing appetizers. I was really impressed with the meatball sliders and the duck breast. Foie gras is usually my all time favorite, but I felt the foie gras at Little Owl was only ok. I would definitely order the meatball sliders or the duck breast over the foie gras. The lamb t-bone entree is delicious and its cooked to perfection. They marinate it perfectly so there is no gamely taste left on the lamb. The lamb is definitely my favorite entree at Little Owl. We also ordered their pork chop, which supposedly is one of their trademarks. However, I was severely disappointed. I felt the pork chop was too dry and it was a bit flavorless. The waitress noticed that I wasn't enjoying my pork chop and she asked me if I wanted to try another entree instead. I ended up getting the veal cheek dish and this one was pretty good. Its a very savory dish and the meat is extremely tender. It can be a bit on the heavy side though, since they wrap the veal cheek in cheese. Service at this place is wonderful and for that, they get 1 extra star =). The bill is presented to you in a cute little red book, and it adds a cute charm to the experience.

If you like roast pork, then come to this phallic named restaurant Â in Â Chinatown, that makes some of the best in the city. Â I also like the steamed vegetables in fish sauce, and the beef chow fun. This place is dirt cheap and always packed.
Their pizzas are great. The ingredients are fresh and the dough is just right.

You should never judge a book by its cover. Â This place isn't that great on the outside. It looks a little outdated and dirty but you have to remember is the food that count. Â The rotisserie chicken is nice and not dry. Â It's easy to have white meat dry out. Â It's busy so im assuming they keep the chickens going or the door. Â I wish it was closer so i can take out more often.

This restaurant is, hands-down, my favorite restaurant in New York City. I've gushed over other restaurants before, but this one takes the cake. I've been to Tia Pol about ten times now (actually, I've lost count) and I can't get enough! I love their tapas-style platters, especially the patatas bravas, crema de hÃ­gado de pollo, and almejas al vino. My favorite dessert is the flan. They also have specials that are not listed in their menu, but are equally absolutely delectable. All of the dishes are sized just right, so that everyone at the table can share with each other (or surreptitiously hog it all to yourself -- that's what I do). There's a pretty good wine menu, but their house sangria (choice of red or white) is what I always order; it's fruity, but not too sweet, plus you can order a glass or a whole pitcher. The restaurant's layout is good for traffic-flow as well. The space is small, but they've done a great job with it. Patrons can sit at the bar, at a small table in the main area, or at a larger table in a backroom area. If you're going for dinner, I definitely suggest making a reservation because this place gets quite packed. Not only do I keep coming back here because of their ridiculously tasty food, but also because the atmosphere is relaxing, fun, and intimate -- think: old, modernized warehouse. And just in case I haven't fully convinced you to go here yet... Did I mention that their pricing is excellent for my grad-student-sized wallet, as well? This is my go-to spot for any occasion or hangout and I am never disappointed.

I've gotta be honest. Â With the number of years I've been on yelp, one of the most anticipated restaurants I had yet to try was Piccolo. Some of my trust worthy web friends I've connected on yelp are in love with this place. Â So don't blame me when I expected a whole lot of goodness on my plate. Â My friends, I don't take consistent raves lightly. Well, fast forward to a night a few months ago and I was waiting breathlessly in anticipation. Â My friend and I hit up a bar a few blocks away from PA and drank away a few brain cells and taste buds. Â Usually, this helps. The setting is one from an old school Italian movie where the servers know your first name and there are kisses on cheeks when you arrive. Â Red and white table clothed tables and lots of chubby waiters who have pens behind their ears and their pad ready to take your order. I know this is going to receive a few gasps but I did not fall in love with this place. Â We ordered the appetizer of proscuitto and melon which I'm not sure is a winner wherever I have it. Â The thought of thinly sliced pork heaven and green cantoloupe have never been a sexy combination. Â  Lets march on to the entree. Â I ordered the Mellanze Rollantini, simply stated is eggplant stuffed with ricotta cheese, proscuitto and tomato sauce to top it off. Â How can that NOT be good? It wasn't. Â It was bland and unseasoned. Â I usually love a good eggplant, sauce and cheese combo. Â It usually calls my name with a deep sultry voice when I see this combo at pizzerias. Â I usually succumb. I did this time and it hit me. Â I got bamboozled.

Stopped by here yesterday for mother's day with my family and we thoroughly enjoyed ourselves. Â First of all, the spacious and bright floor plan is the perfect vibe for weekend brunch. Â The blood mary is light, if you're looking for something more on the refreshing side, post-hangover. The pickle in the blood mary was awesome! The food was simple, yet done right. Â I had the burger and my sister had the shortrib "hush" Â and both were delicious and satisfying. They could really benefit from a cocktail menu, but I'm sure it will come in time. Â I'm so happy this place opened in my neighborhood, where a good brunch spot is seriously lacking!

Been here the Valentine's Day special menu. Was a little blown away by the price at first, but realized that this was cheaper than if we came on a regular day and ordered each dish seperately. Had a set menu of 6 courses, all small portions. Started off with the bacon popcorn, yum! They gives this to all customers even on the regular menu. I don't remember everything we ate, but one thing I liked was the staff was very friendly. Each time they came up to serve a plate, they described each dish with great knowledge. It made the experience a little more special. There were hits and misses with each plate, but presentation was excellent. Sometimes dishes were a little too salty, and this is definitely not the place to eat if you are trying to eat healthier. I like the experimenting of different composition of flavors but not every dish was a success. This would be a place I might go to on occasion for a special event, I don't know if I can eat this type of food on a regular basis. It's also not ideal for large groups. It's a nice cozy setting.

If you are looking for novelty pizza that will have your tastebuds orgasming all day or night try the Artichoke slice. To all you food snobs...yes it is huge and yes it is messy but whoever said food was supposed to be neat. Be the Animal you are and dig in. I don't mind standing on a corner devouring a nice messy slice after a night out with friends. If you are searching for the perfect NY Slice try the Margarita (did I spell that right?) I haven't tried any of the other slices yet but I will soon...I say using your hands makes the food taste better. ENJOY!

I just created a YELP account to write this review. You can imagine how bad my experience must have been, compelling me to write this review. I went to this place with very high expectations, waited for an hour and 10 minutes and left without even getting a table. Yes .... this is how Public treats their customers. The two hostesses are rude, snobbish and I don't understand why. While we were waiting for one of our fifth friend to join us, one of them went to the extent of saying -" Maybe you should tell your friend not to come." I was stunned! How on earth do they get away with this. In any case, if you have high tolerance for BAD SERVICE .... check it out. I would give this place zero stars since I didn't even get to try to food. I ended up going to Lovely Days next door and believe it or not I loved it. We ordered Egg Fritatas, noodles (spicy), pancakes - all were excellent. I am definitely going back. Ofcourse, I am a fan of their Bloody Mary.

Now, ive eaten at a lot of different places in NYC, and I dont like to go to the same place twice even on different visits. But this just made my list along w/ Gordon Ramseys Maze and the Redhead in the East Village(see other reviews) of "must eat here while in NYC". We tried them on a food tour, it was our last stop. Holy hell are these people geniuses. We actually stayed after the tour guides left to order a full wafel. they were super nice, and funny and i think at this point it goes w/ out saying that the food was awesome. We even broight some spekuloos home w/ us! During the rest of our trip when people asked what we'd done so far and we mentioned "food truck tour", every time their faces would light up and ask "Did you get to go to Wafels and Dinges?!" Amazing.

An absolutely picturesque place to visit after a Broadway show. My boyfriend and I saw Pippin and after ventured to Joe Allen's at the suggestion of Yelp reviews. Its this quiet not-too-descript place, tucked away keeping it more quiet and intimate. The interior stunning. A little dim however its odds and ends collection of curiosities that line the walls glimmer nicely in the lower light. The waitstaff were knowledgeable and were able to explain some of the ingredients in dishes we were interested in. The peel and eat shrimp were succulent and fresh, the dip served with them flavorful. Chris ordered the Steak Tartare with a Malbec wine. The dish WAS TO DIE FOR. It was perfectly seasoned and not too dry or pasty. I ordered the Fettuccine Alfredo Pesto with a Magic Hat beer. The Alfredo pesto was rich and zesty with sweet, whole shrimp scattered about the dish. We finished our meal with an order of the homemade chocolate chip cookies served with vanilla ice cream. It was the perfect goodnight kiss of flavor to conclude a delightful meal that was just as entertaining to our palettes as the prior show was to our eyes. Can not recommend highly enough.

Thank you Penelope for bringing a great affordable brunch/lunch option to Midtown. Fantastic Brunch dishes and great Vegan options fill out the menu in addition to the amazing baked goods they have on hand daily. And they have great sourdough bread for the sandwiches, which for this California native is like a life preserver.

This is my 2nd time visit to this cafe. This time came with $29 groupon for 2 ppl. Totally worth it. No reservation require. Went for dinner on Sunday at 7pm last week. Seated right away. Tried their salmon fillet and chicken cutlet parmigiano last visit, salmon was amazing and the chicken was ok. This visit with groupon bf ordered lamb shank and he likes it. And I got the Mac and Cheese it's tasty. Also a side of Penne Vodka super yummy. 2 mini salads, 2 drinks- house wine and Doc's Cider( big btl). And of coz we finished all our meal and desserts to-go. With both visits we leave with our happy tummy! :)

As long as I don't have to wait forever, it's good. Great food, fair price, acceptable noise level for me! The only thing that bothers me is there always seems to be a fly or two -____-; but um still good! I recommend fried chicken gizzard & agedashi tofu.
Not sure what the hype is about. Â The food is decent, nice. Â Staff was decent, nice. Â I had heard so much about it I kinda wanted to blown away but wasn't. Â Will definitely give it another try.

Shakshuka two poached eggs in tomato pepper sauce with side of hummus and pita - i love this dish. brunch is usually brunch, but i finally found something different and pretty filling too didnt like it so much for dinner. the chicken schwarma wasnt very good (tasted kind of burnt) but the risotto was above average half price on bottles of wine monday-thursday... pretty good deal
This is my go to spot for mexican food. Â Deeeelicious.
Great sushi, fresh and tasty, only thing is....drains my pocket, very very expensive. So I can't come too often, but definitely will be back.

Came here for dinner and really loved it. Â The location on quaint little Cornelia Street in the West Village is superb. Â It's like the cliched setting of postcard perfect Manhattan from the movies. Â You really can't beat it. We were seated in the charming garden in the back. Â It was crowded and the tables were very close together. Â Which isn't great in terms of privacy, but there was a fun little moment when it turned out that the two women next to us were discussing where one of them should buy an apartment while I was talking about possibly purchasing a place in Greenpoint next year. Â They overheard us, a short conversation ensued and it was a nice little pleasant interlude. Our waiter was very helpful and his insistence on being right about everything would've been annoying had he not, well, been correct about literally every suggestion that he made. Â When I chose a pasta dish from the menu, he told me to get the special instead. Â And he was right. Â Every single suggestion he made was perfect. Â And he ended up treating us to a glass of lovely dessert wine. Â So I officially like that guy. The food is fantastic. Â I had burrata with heirloom tomatoes, which was perfection on a plate. Â The creaminess of the burrata was contrasted nicely with the firmness of the dark red, almost purple tomatoes. The pasta special was ravioli with burrata and sun-dried tomatoes in it. Â Wow. Â Just superb. Â The pasta was prepared perfectly al dente, and that slight firmness was complemented by the softness of the cheese and the saltiness of the tomatoes. Â Yum. I had the fish special. Â Again, lovely. Â It was a sea bass. Â My friend ordered the sliced steak with arugula and parmigiano. Â His was better than mine, but both were delicious. Ricotta cheesecake for dessert. Â Another winner on the menu. Â I really liked it. I would give this place five stars for food, but only four stars in total because it's really quite pricey for what you get. Â It's one of those Italian places where you really have to order three courses in order to feel full. Â Portions aren't huge. Â And at about $20 per course, it's an expensive meal. Â Ours came to $250 for two people and we each only had one drink. Â That's a lot. Â But you'll want to order an appetizer, primo and secondo or you'll leave hungry. Â I just feel like $20 for six ravioli, no matter how delicious they are, is a lot of money. That said, no regrets. Â Loved the place and will definitely go back.

OH MY GOD SO GOOD! Lupa is the best restaurant in the city. Â My most recent favorite combo of dishes is their decadent Escarole, Pecorino, walnut and onion salad, a buttery Butternut Squash tortellini, and followed by non other than their famous Pistachio gelato. Â All of this I sloshed down with a bottle of Gavi di Gavi Piemonte wine. Â SMASHING!

I'll admit it... I didn't give Balthazar its fair chance to shine as I treated it as my Pastis substitute. When I was here, I basically jumped at the opportunity to order my favorite stuff from Pastis.... yes you guessed it... the chicken liver and foie gras mousse! The crowd here is more low key, slightly touristy and not as hip as Pastis'. The good thing though is that they have their own bakery and raw bar. YAY! to fresh oysters~

Definitely worth a visit if you get the chance while in NYC. The line is always out the door but sometimes they can overestimate the wait time. I was once told two hours and was seated within 20 minutes. Although that was a pleasant surprise I wouldn't hold my breath next time for the same luck. The ramen is really good and I love the decor and overall ambiance of the restaurant but I think you can also find really good ramen in other places in the city that may not have the same hype but also won't have the excessive wait.

Like everyone else on here seems to be saying; great food served wicked late, well-chosen beers, and nice cocktails. Service is solid and good; words I chose carefully because one time it was warm, spectacular service that made me feel as if I'd lucked into my new favorite place in the city, while another time it was perfectly adequate with nothing particularly warm about it but no mistakes. Whatever, I don't need my hand held every second! So far I tried the putine which was exactly what my tipsy self needed, fried pickles which were a huge order and tasty, and the seasonal burger which was messy but absolutely delicious (at the time the seasonal burger had creamed spinach & mascarpone on it). The beers are great even though I'd prefer something that doesn't expand my midsection as quickly as it does. With that burger I had a bitter, a saison, and a summer ale. Definitely worth a visit! CASH ONLY
I love this place. Â Food is great. Â Mojitos are delicious. Â Awesome music. Â Great atmosphere. Good service. AND!! there's as guy hand rolling cigars in the corner on the main floor.

Cannot express how awesome this place is!!! Food is amazing. The place is so local feeling. I love it!! Â We sat at the bar and would recommend to others to sit there. Chatted with the owner and the bartender throughout the whole dinner. They are so funny and such genuine people. I would go here again and again and again and will recommend this place to anyone who wants some local seafood! We will go back for the oyster happy hour soon!!

I love this place. Â It's an intimate, brightly lit, cozy destination. The service is warm and attentive. The menu strikes the perfect balance light healthy dishes (tuna and Greek salads) and comfort food (burger, sandwiches, Â The breakfast items are delicious- shakshuka, grilled halumi with tomato. Simple and delicious. I can't wait to try the rosewater waffle!!

I had been dying to go here for as long as I can remember and boy am I sorry I waited so long. They have quite an interesting menu of Asian fusion infused items served almost tapas style, which I don't mind because you can try more things on the menu. I had their special oxtail tacos of the day which were so moist and tender the juice was dripping down my hand. (Damn you really need to write reviews the next or same day because my old age is getting to me.) I will return soon enough for an updates review.

i will give 4 stars if the wait time is shorter. went there for lunch still about 20 mins wait. for the food...it is ramen...i personally think all the ramen in manhattan are not that different, the appetizer is good though but not that impressive.

Got the Beef Chow Fun to go. Picked this place because I was looking up the best noodles to get during lunch break in the area. The Beef Chow Fun was inedible for me - it smelled so horrid. The brown sauce must be made from organ meat that has fermented into a dog food/diarrhea smell, it had me gagging and it tasted so bad. I threw it out immediately and had to open all my windows for hours to get the smell to disperse.

Get the fried chicken biscuit sandwich! (I had to cut to the chase just in case you don't have time for a long review). A delicious, thick, impossibly juicy breast of chicken awaits you, nestled inside a fluffy country biscuit. If that doesn't entice you, then revel in the knowledge that for less than ten dollars, you're eating fried chicken that makes the chefs at Momofuku look like amateurs for a tenth of the price. Easy to miss, this place is barely wider than its front door-- but if you can sidestep your way in, you'll agree it was worth the shimmy.

their host is awesome! we asked him to play a practical joke on a friend before letting him into the restaurant and he was totally into it! their drinks are delicious and try the bone marrow poppers..
Get a Sangria pitcher v a glass ;) Stopped here for my breakfast / late lunch today. Ordered: - Octopus salad - Duck sausage Both were good. But Octopus salad was a bit too salty for my taste.

so i grew up on ave J and 21st, sort of, and i've got to say that as Dom gets on in years the pizza is getting burnt more often, and sadly, he has no protege. there was a pace, by the time he got done making one pie, the one in the oven was done, but he's a little to slow for that now, and all the hype has just made it harder for him. His real 'salad days' were the late 80's to the mid 90's. hell, it's not even off the 'd' train anymore. He is ny style pizza, and when he's gone all that will be left will be fakes.

Trying to get a cheap asian fix (insert pun here)? This would be the place to. As a Korean myself, I don't think the korean food here is breathtaking or amazing. It's great for what it is... a quick bite with a small price tag. They have great variety and the ready made lunch boxes are great. Pick any of them, they all taste pretty good! Thank you Woorijip!

Great pasta. Really great pasta. I got the fresh pasta with proschiutto, rosemary, sage, and hot peppers and it was some of the best pasta Ive ever had. Everything that isn't pasta is just so-so. Affordable prices. Cozy and busy but charming.

Went with friends on a Monday night. Â Only about a 15 minute wait. Â We only had the pizza, with pepperoni and meatballs. Was very good, not greasy at all. Â toppings and cheese was very fresh. Â A must visit for the New York pizza experience.

Have to echo all the amazing reviews of this place. Â Came with my husband for dinner late Saturday night. Â We had an appetizer plate with some cured meat and the vegetable spread. Â The spread was delicious. Â Then we split cheese spatzle and it was SO good. Â Kind of like a mac and cheese dish but with mini dumplings instead of pasta texture. Â I had a hefeweissen. Â I love beer and this was the BEST hefe I have ever had, perfectly flavored. Â And the service - AMAZING! Â The waitresses were so nice and helpful. Â The atmosphere in this place was awesome. Â I want to go back ASAP!

Came here with my family, the restaurant is kind of small but so many people. We wait around 15 minutes Â to get a table. Â Most of the customers are chinese. I like the dim sum and some other Chinese food. This is a good place to go if you like Chinese food.

Even if the food was crap I'd go for the atmosphere and the Guinness. As it turns out they have one of the best corned beef sandwiches in captivity, a great turkey club with fresh turkey and outstanding bacon and Â the french onion soup is a great move because it gets you free Irish soda bread. I tend to pass on all of these in favor of their burger, the same great bacon piled onto a near perfect cheeseburger on a kaiser roll. I feel I shouldn't post this because I don't want you taking my seat. But now you know.
Terrific Barbecue with by the pound meats and by the 1/2 pint to gallon craft beers. Community picnic tables.

Artichoke Shmartichoke! Â If you like waiting forever for so so pizza served up too hot and with a lot of attitude then this place is for you. And that Lurch Robot guy in the front needs to get a life.

First off, I would like to be upfront and say that the food is quote good and full of flavor. However the biggest thing that irked me was the size of their platters. The are in that awkward place between the size/price of an appetizer and the size/price of a normal main dish platter. In a regular restaurant I would maybe spend $10 on an appetizer and $20 on a main dish, and this is if I am feeling particularly hungry. Here I literally had to get two "main dishes" which amounted to about $35 and still left fairly hungry. If you just want an expensive but flavorful snack, this place is good. But if you are looking for a place to eat this may not be the best value. The interior is also a bit strange. It tried to pull off the ambiance of a restaurant with candles and a darkly lit setting, but the white plastic bar tables are strangely positioned and are cold in nature. Bottom line, the chef is great and the ideas behind the dishes are wonderful. But unless this place changes its value proposition it will not last long. Suggestion - keep the prices, double the size of the portions. People will flock. Good luck. Siana

Probably the best meal I had while visiting New York this last go round. Â And even though it was busting at the seams with people, we managed to wrangle ourselves to the bar for a pre-dinner drink while we waited for our table. I'm still unsure why my SO ordered me a mojito at a French restaurant. It was fine, but I made the switch to wine pretty quickly. The four of us sat outside, and were quite pleased with the people watching. We started off with the mussels, and had the pork tenderloin for an entree. Â A third of the way through my meal, I switched dishes with Kevin and finished off his butternut squash ravioli, which was so rich and tasty. Luckily, it was also a little bit sweet, so when I was too full for dessert, my craving was satisfied.

Highlight: Five stars, not necessarily for the food which is delicious but, for the experience. My man told me to pick a restaurant and he'd take me out for a little date night action. I dropped Gramercy Tavern. We got a 5:30 reservation! Totally fine, we wanted to check out a movie after so it worked out. (Five stars for Silver Linings Playbook as well). From the minute we entered the door, the level of service was exquisite. One almost forgets when it's been awhile without fine dining how nice it is to be promptly attended to. We start off with a few drinks and take a gander at the menu. Now the menu: you have a choice between a three course meal for $80ish or a seven course tasting at $110ish. We weren't trying to stuff ourselves to the gills so we thought the three course would be plenty. It was. I'm not going to give a complete breakdown of my meal except the highlights: the smoked trout app - get it. It literally tastes like butter that melts in your mouth; it was my favorite part of the meal. My man's sea bass was also a delight while my lamb entree though was extremely good and i found to be quite big, could not compare to the fish entree. I also ordered the special app of the evening, duck dumplings, which I did not enjoy though my man did. I just personally found the duck very overpowering and that's not my favorite flavor. They were cooked perfectly though with the skin being slight charred. The dessert was decadent. We did find that the peanut butter semi freddo was the winner in the dessert field and they do keep the sugar flowing with free petit fours and coffee cake as a take home for the next morning (what a nice touch). Ultimately, I thought to myself, for $88, a 3 course meal with extra bites here and there is a really good deal. If I went out to a local spot in Jersey City and ordered an app, entree and dessert we are hitting up $50-60 and that is without the amazing service (no bread plate or water glass went empty), the high quality of food (even if I ultimately found the meal itself 4 star worthy) and being able to check in on your Yelp app to the Gramercy Tavern. The experience is amazing and I think the price tag is worth it. So, get that special someone, head to GT, order any of the fish items and sit back and be served.

On a recent lovely Saturday evening, we were strolling from a gallery in Chelsea through the meatpacking district trying to figure out where to get a drink that was not the meatpacking district and not staggeringly crazy. I suggested Otheroom...you can always get a seat at the Otheroom, even on a lovely Saturday evening when the entire city of New York is out and about! Well I was wrong. It was packed. No matter though, it was still adorable and delightfully dark and still played music that I love and still has great beer and wine. Even better, the seats at the open air front window emptied, we settled there and had a lovely view of the outside. As I sat, a feeling of calm washed over me and I realized I was completely content just being right there. (Trust me, I don't use these words lightly- this is quite a rare and notable occasion in my life). Yay! ps: minus one star because the secret's out.

I love this little hole in the wall! Have been meaning to visit for a while, and it definitely met the hype. Shared a small and three sauces with a friend, and it was the perfect amount. The fries are delicious and the teriyaki, sweet mango chutney, and rosemary garlic were all great. Seating is limited, but it was pretty empty when I went on a Sunday afternoon. Definitely a must try!
I just had my second prosciutto and (organic) tomato Â sandwich here, and it was great! I loved it, fresh and tasty! Go for it...
Ate here for a really late lunch and it was awesome! I ordered the pull pork and that was just tasty!!!! I just wish they had some rice to go with it. :(

I love fries. I love mayo. I love flavor. I love Pommes Frites. I tried Curry Ketchup Especial and Sweet Mango Chutney and both were very distinct and good. Get the small, unless you're making this a meal or sharing. The guys behind the counter were super nice and even though they were busy they took the time and let me try the various mayos I wanted. The fries are cooked to order and comes PIPING hot. I love the flavor profiles and freshness of the place. I wish I could eat whatever I wanted because I would probably eat this once a week, but since I want to live past 40 I would have to limit how often I come here. It's good though and if you're around the area you should definitely give it a whirl. It's also open late for all you drunkards(not me of course)

If you don't give this place 5 stars you're an asshole. Â  - The food is great. - The food is cheap. - They have a few good craft beers on tap. - The good craft beers on tap are cheap. - The restaurant is the perfect size. - The perfect sized space has a nice decor. - The perfect sized space with a nice decor was crowded, but didn't require a wait at 8:30pm on Thursday. All in all, everyone in this place was just, well, happy. FOOD: House Made Soft Pretzels: unreal. Â Perfectly salted and so soft. Â I don't know if I've ever had a pretzel this good. Â On top of that, the Kentucky-style beer cheese is SO flavorful. Â It has a perfect consistency that allows it to spread easily on the pretzel without dripping, but isn't so dense enough to cause the pretzel any bodily harm. Â It bounces off the salt perfectly. Buttermilk Fried Chicken: Has a great crisp to it that doesn't cause the meat to dry out. Â I don't know what she puts in that breading, but it's exactly what I want on my fried chicken, forever. Â The dish comes with a good sized leg and a breast--both of which have their own unique flavors that caused my girlfriend and I to engage in a 20 minute debate over which was better (no one won). Â  Oh, and don't forget the side salad and the slice of cornbread. Â The side salad was a great compliment to the chicken with some fruits to contrast that great breading. Â The cornbread tasted like a little butter fairy snuck onto my plate between bites to lightly glaze each bite with liquid buttery delight. Â It's the best cornbread I've ever had. Mac & Cheese: a generous portion for a side with a modest, but effective layer of breadcrumbs that sealed in the thick cheesiness below. Â Superb. EXPERIENTIAL DETAILS: This place is in a league of its own. Â They make it comfortable and inviting enough, so you don't mind wearing a tee shirt and jeans there, yet their wait staff treats you like you're paying for a fine dining experience. Â Glasses of water are always full. Â Go to the bathroom, and you'll come back to a folded napkin. Â They give you a great piece of sweet bread to start. Â And if you don't order desert, they give you these individually wrapped mini cinnamon bun cookies to go. Â They're so damn good. Â They could easily charge $6 for two of them in a normal dessert, but instead give them away for free. Â That's the type of sh*t that will get me to come back. Â Bravo. All in all, I spend $63 + tip for 4 beers, an app, a meal to share, and a side. Â We were both totally satisfied and full, and I couldn't wait to sing The Redhead's praises. Â GO!

The best lobstah roll in the city. Â It's awesome that it's also $15. Â Best deal for this sandwich. Stay away from Luke's lobster which doesn't have as much personality as these rolls. Â Another good place for lobster rolls is Ed's Lobster but you'll be paying at least $27 for those.

Had to grab a quick lunch before catching our flight out of NYC. Â Had seen the zagat review signs in the window and the clerk at the hotel recommended it. Â Food was good and fast! Â The server was really nice and allowed us to sit by the windows as we had our luggage with us. Â We also had some drinks we wanted to consume before going to the airport and upon asking the server if we could drink it in the restaurant, he allowed us to do so! I'd like to be able to try a few other dishes, but that will have to wait until we go back! I'd recommend going with several other people and eating family style, as with any asian restaurant, so that you can try several dishes without getting overstuffed or breaking the bank!

Thanks to the gorgeous weather yesterday, the fiancee and I went on a trek from our usual stomping grounds on 30th Ave over to Ditmars (during my runs to the airport and/or the Park, I've seen lots of new stuff popping up all over). My fiancee had read about this place and suggested it for lunch, and once we saw the sign outside advertising lunch specials + a draft beer or glass of wine = $10.95, we were sold. FOOD: decadent. Definitely the star of the show. I went with the grilled salmon, which came with a side salad and yellow rice with a lemony taste. Despite having ordered the lunch special, this was a *huge* cut of salmon. I was so full afterward that I couldn't make it through the rice and barely touched the salad. My fiancee ordered the burger (beef) with goat cheese and bacon, which was also supremely delicious. If you're feeling frisky, try the kangaroo burger. Apparently this is their main staple, and when we come back, we're gonna give that a whirl. DRINKS: looks to be decked out with a full bar, and they have a pretty decent wine list. We both went with the house lager (Australian) and omg it was good. It had a nice and light fruity taste (but not overbearingly fruity) to it, and is the perfect summer beer. Both of our beers came with the lunch special. PRICES: on weekends you can either order brunch, which comes with a free mimosa or bloody mary (pretty standard) or you can order the lunch special, which comes with a free house beer or glass of wine (better deal IMO). The bill for both of us for two lunch entrees and two beers, including my fiancee's additions to her burger, was less than $30. SERVICE: while initially very attentive and very good, it faltered near the end. We had to actively try and catch someone's attention to get our plates cleared and the check. While certainly not enough to dampen our experience, it was definitely noticeable. However, our server's knowledge of the food and drinks was spot on, and he was quite friendly. Will come back again! And I just saw that there's going to be an Elite event here. Great choice Yelp!

yeah, the name is seriously dumb. Â but the food is seriously cheap and tasty. Â their bbq sandwich is great, as are the veggie burgers. Â and they serve food late, which is desperately needed in this neighborhood. Â the beer selection, however, leaves much to be desired. Â it looks like they tried to come up with a good selection but don't seem to understand what that means. Â they've got beers from a couple of countries, for example, but the beers they chose are the bud equivalents of those countries. Â the environment really seems to depend on who's there--i've gone and seen happy locals on some nights, drunk frat boys on others. Â nonetheless, i'm happy and think it's a good addition to the neighborhood.

I don't care if it's like being in Japan! This place is outrageously overpriced, compared to other similar places in the city. Not to mention the ridiculous small portions. At least they could serve a little more for the price. Let the people who want to throw money away go there. Enjoy the true Japanese experience!

I am in love with their cobb salad with steak. medium rare. bacon on the side and no beans and... one extra egg in there . Best salad Cafeteria offers. It is so good, I can't imagine anyone trying to make one that can be just as good as Cafeteria's. I've been coming to Cafeteria since I was in High School. Majority of the waiters are gay but it's fine with me because I don't think they want my yellow ass. The scene here is pretty lively so sometimes don't be suprised when there is a wait during peak eating times or when there is something going on nearby ( barneys wearhouse sale). It all started...after a couple of hundred rounds at the driving range over at Chelsea piers, we would hit up Cafeteria to eat because the portions were big. Flashfoward a couple of years later, I've introduced a couple of my food obsessed friends to Cafeteria and you know the deal... the chain goes on and on. Cafeteria has done me well. When i'm depressed, I come here and eat their 3 flavor mac and cheese. When i'm happy I'll eat their short rib sandwich. god man. the food is great. Â I'm so glad I got to experience you when I was young. p.s - once I tried to order the three cheese mac to takeaway. They said they can't. What a bummer.

Came here on a Saturday night with a group of 8 people, arrived around 8:30 and wasn't seated until 10:30. Smaller groups would have been seated a lot sooner than a group of 8, I had better luck pulling a rabbit out of my a$$ than to be seated. It's a popular restaurant and the wait is to be expected. Finally got a chance to dine after the long wait, Had the meatball appetizer and Merguez Â for entree, a second choice since they seem to have run out of the skirt steak. The meatballs were juicy and delicious and melt tender in your mouth. The merguez is basically a small gauge sausage link similar to breakfast sausage. The sausage alone seemed dry in the mixture. Preferably, Â a sausage mix should have at least 25-30% fat, yes I make my own sausages if you must ask. Eaten together with it's accoutrement , tzatziki sauce and pickled vegetables, the flavors merry together in a blissful bites. In the end, despite having a long wait to be seated, the food did deliver and inevitably, that's what counts the most.

This is where you take people you need to impress. :) I planned a corporate dinner her last month. They are a pretty laid back group, but they like to eat well, drink well and be surrounded by a nice environment. Vitae seemed to hit the bulls-eye. We had about 15 people and were able to reserve a table upstairs which was really nice and semi-private. Let's start with the good stuff because we drank like sailors. I had a spicy margarita - let me tell you that word spicy is serious. I asked the waiter how spicy it was, he looked at me so serious and said "SPICY." I decided to go for it and ordered it mild. Another co-worker ordered spicy. HAHA mine was SO hot - I don't even know how he drank his. Anyways.... the food was delish. We tried one of almost everything on the menu appetizer-wise and enjoyed EVERYTHING. I will say, the lamb meatball sliders were my absolute favorite. I mean it - don't go here without getting them. A over sized lamb meatball with mozzarella cheese on a soft slider bun... y mouth is watering just thinking about it. I had the shrimp risotto for dinner and was pleased. It could have used some salt and pepper but it was filling and delicious nonetheless. Overall, everyone was very satisfied and I can put another successful planned night on my book!

Burgers, Mac and cheese, Fried pickles... drool, drool, drool. We came on a Tuesday night and, while it wasn't packed, every table was taken (at first... luckily, one became available about 15 minutes after we arrived.) I started with a Rye Root Beer, which basically tastes like a spiked root beer; delicious. The pickle martini was interesting (I've actually made this at home before because McClure's - the pickles they use - actually has the recipe on their jars... but, of course, SF makes 'em better). The spicy margarita was too sweet originally but I asked them to adjust it a bit and then it was good, has a slight kick with each sip. We shared a burger and he said he could make a better one at home, but I liked that it was simple - just lettuce, tomato, onion and pickle - but well cooked and reminiscent of burgers you'd grill when you're having a BBQ.
