Yeah, I know what you're thinking. New restaurant, name as generic as humanly possible. Can't be that great, right? Wrong. The easiest way to understand this restaurant is as a new entry in the category of spots like Walter Foods -- well-executed, slightly-elevated American cuisine offering the right kind of atmosphere, a solid wine/beer selection and excellent cocktails. Plus a raw bar, naturally. Grand Street does all of those things Walter Foods, plus you can actually get in there (for now) on a busy night and not wait forever. I didn't expect the food to be as good as it was; I didn't even need it to be as good as it was, but I loved it. The burger is outstanding and blows WF's out of the water. The appetizers were executed well without fail, from the fried homeji mushrooms to the pate (don't skip the pate). Yes, they have mac & cheese. Yes, it's great. But the thing that will bring me back to this place -- and would bring me back if it were half as good a restaurant, frankly, is the staff. I'm not sure I've met a friendlier, more laid-back front of house crew anywhere in Brooklyn or Manhattan. They went out of their way to make us have a good time, were fun guys to talk to, and never let the drinks run dry. At times it felt kind of like being at a great dinner party thrown by them, with a bunch of other people we didn't know hanging around. I can't recommend this place highly enough. My one regret is that the more positive mentions it gets, the less well-kept of a secret it'll be. Oh well. These guys deserve it.

Full Disclosure: I'm a regular. This has quickly become my go-to spot for both upbeat and relaxing dining. Chef Hugo is warm and personable, and he comes out of the kitchen to ask his guests how they're doing, how they like the food and his vibe is one of the warmest I've ever encountered in NYC. Ordinarily, a warm-hearted pleasant chef is only part of the equation, and were it not for each dish's carefully curated charm and flair, this restaurant might come up wanting. And yet, it doesn't. La Slowteria exceeds its own charm with great dishes night after night. Â  An example: tonight I went in and ordered steak & bacon tacos. I received 2 of the largest tacos I've ever seen. Before that arrived, Hugo sent me an appetizer. I've been here a lot, and yet I'm always surprised. Hugo is a true scientist when it comes to food, and you can see his impassioned flair in each dish. He often surprises guests with mezcal-soaked cherries as a digestif which are a total delight. The staff is witty and quick with a helpful recommendation. It's often rare to find a crew that gels so wonderfully in a restaurant, and yet everyone working here seems to really enjoy what they're doing, quite a refreshing shift from many other succulent dining experiences.

Either my standards are too high or Niu Noodle House has spoiled me. Pretty good. Not great. I wasn't expecting culinary excellence, but what I got was average. I was expecting just a hint more... That hole in the wall ambience is something I personally enjoy. No frills. No expectations. Just bottles of vinegar, soy sauce, and Sriracha on wobbly tables and counters, with containers bursting with chopsticks and plastic forks. Want a drink? Go to the fridge OUTSIDE of the front door. (Ballin'.) I ordered the noodle soup with oxtail. I remember being upset when I visited Xi'an because the oxtail was delicious, but I got a singular vertebrae. I had the opposite problem here: I got multiple vertebrae, but the oxtail was just horrible. Honestly. I did not enjoy it at all. All portions were extremely fatty, and the little bits of meat I did find were bland, chewy, and an unappetizing gray color. Extremely disappointed. They sure picked the wrong ox tail for this soup! The broth? Fine. No complaints. A few dashes of soy sauce were needed to enhance it, however. The noodles? Excellent, thank goodness! They made up for the bad oxtail, in my book. Soft and toothsome. I wasn't overwhelmed by them, though I did spend a lot of time bent directly over my bowl to ensure as little splashage as possible when biting through them and letting the remains drop back into the soup. Though the soups are supposed to be the stars of the menu, it's the fried dumplings that got me. Yes! AMAZING! Had my "Selfish Only Child" genes kicked in, I would have squarely stolen all twelve from Yan and Lori. However, I exhibited fine manners and we each got our equal fill. But DAMN were they tasty! Hot and fried perfectly brown on the outside, with delicious meats and surprisingly crisp slices of chives on the inside. Oh! If I ever go back to Lam Zhou, screw the soup! I'm a dumpling girl when it comes to this establishment! Dinner for three was $20.50. It's hard to do much better than that.

A really great greenpoint bar-nice back area, generous dance floor, cheap food menu etc. Â Also the cute tatted bar tender who made me a perfect manhattan doesn't hurt either:) It would be a five star for me, but the decor/theme is a little sportsy which works against the aesthetic strengths of the space, imho. Â i am looking forward to seeing the direction this place goes. Â highly recommended overall~!
Awesome food! The pizza is one of the best I've had and the "Shrimp Penne" is to die for.

Eggs Benedict and the chocolate mousse both were excellent, no complaints there. Waiter informed me they don't serve decaf then ran and looked around and found a bag and brewed up a pot just for me. A+ service was awesome, very friendly. The only reason it's not a 5 for me is the music was terribly depressing, but that's just my opinion. It is a little odd not being a hipster inside this place, but they can't be held accountable for that, it's Brooklyn. Â Definitely will come back if I'm in the area.

Went here for late drinks/snack recently and thought it was a nice gastropub. It was pretty empty at 10pm on a Monday night. For drinks, we had wine and a cocktail. The cocktail was delicious (a bourbon cocktail) and the wine was alright. The short rib taco was good, innovative sauce, braised and shredded. The shrimp ceviche wasn't really ceviche. I think the shrimp had been cooked, and it was served in some trashy but tasty ketchup/salsa sauce. All in all, I thought for the location, and the prices (given the location), it was a pretty good deal. I'd come back again if I had to stick to dining in the area..

I can officially say that I've met the man, the legend himself - Mr. Paulie Gee. Â Paulie "stuck it to The Man" and decided to pursue his passion for pizza. Â Don't let his nerdy appearance fool you: this guy knows his pizza. Â On that particular evening, Paulie was making his rounds at each and every table. Â He was especially grateful that I had come all the way from Northern Westchester to sample a few pies. The Gates of Eden salad is an excellent way to start off the meal. Â The mixed greens and gorgonzola cheese were nicely balanced by the sweet candied walnuts and dried cherries. Â The salad is perfect for sharing size because it's important to leave room for pizza. Out of the pizzas that I have sampled, my favorite by far is the Cherry Jones. Â If you're ordering a whole bunch of pizzas, ask this one to be brought out last because it could technically be dessert. Â The creamy fior di latte and gorgonzola cheeses, combined with the sweetness of the dried cherries and honey is such a treat. Another favorite: the Anise and Anephew, which was an interesting combination of fennel, fior di latte, and guanciale. Â I've never had fennel on pizza, but I loved how that mild licorice taste paired with the creamy cheese. Â  The Red, White, and Greenberg is another pizza that artfully masters combining sweet and savory ingredients. Â Fior di latte cheese and guanciale were combined with super-sweet red onions and tangy arugula, making me wish I had room in my stomach for another slice. The limoncello dessert pizza, however, was a disappointment. Â Limoncello is typically strong and distinctive, but the pizza topping was much more reminiscent of a sweet custard with just a hint of lemon. Â Additionally, my first impression of the crust was "Wow, this is salty!" which is probably not what I would have anticipated from a limoncello (or even a nutella) dessert pizza. Make sure to take a trip to the bathroom while you're here - the locks on the doors are pretty cool! Overall, I think it is the creativity, willingness to experiment with unusual pizzas, and quality of the cheese that makes Paulie Gee's truly memorable.

Came at 6:30 and place was more than half pack but we thankfully we got seated for 4 people. The place is hard to move around in since all the tables are mostly tightly packed together. The server didn't bring out the bread and olive oil until we placed our orders. The bread was nothing special; cold and stale but the olive oil has a very nice fragrance but no flavor. For appetizers, we got the mussel and fried artichoke. Mussel was well worth the price and very delicious, recommended. The fried artichokes with the fried green 'leaves' is a Total miss. It was fried and had no flavor. A skip For entrees we shared, Â tagliolini ai frutti di mare (seafood pasta), lasagna, and gnocci in gorgonzola sauce. For me, the seafood pasta was the best dish here then the lasagna. You can tasted that it's fresh pasta. The gnocci, though tasted fresh, tasted kind Â of one tone. Not saying it was bad but it wasn't that great either. All the entree portion was not filling, it is def not meant for sharing. Also the reason I didn't give it 5 stars because proportion is kind of small and the tight space made it uncomfortable to sit in. Would I come here again? yes, for the price, it's nice to try different dishes at that price. For 4 people, the bill (not including tip ) was $55.

I'm very glad NY has a Katsu place. No, its not Maisen (Famous Tokyo Katsu place in a former bathhouse) but it'll do the trick. Lots of Japanese folk in here, business guys (salaryman), couples, etc. Ok for families too. Katsu-curry is pretty good, but stick to straight up Katsu. In the front they have grab and go take-out Katsu-sando (sandwich) if you need a quickie fix. *I'm not sure where Mary K ate, but there are NO Hispanic waitresses there. maybe she was smoking crack at a different place. I have eaten here 100+ times and I worked across the street.

brunch review Service was all right...a bit above average. I'd say 3.5/5 stars. The croissant with bananas and chocolate was not as amazing as it sounded. The croissant seemed a little too burnt for my taste. Who serves a burnt croissant? Too much chocolate and not enough banana. Poached eggs, corn grits, and pork sausage...HM, I'm not a fan. The eggs were fresh but I did not enjoy the rest of the dish. Corn grits was corn grits, nothing to say about that. The sausage was very salty, and the sauce that came with it, all over my grits, was far from the line of decent. I would have preferred just the sausage-no sauce needed. I had trouble finishing it; I just didn't like it. Cookshop scramble was mediocre, nothing special. The biscuit was meh, I've had better. Maybe the other dishes are far superior? I'd hesitate to come back here.
quiet, nice view
Best pizza I've ever tried on this side of the Atlantic. Long wait and lines no matter what time of the day you go.

my bias began two years ago when i wasn't hired after working through a five hour brunch shift on a snowy st. patrick's day. i was paid thirty dollars cash, an order of eggs benedict, bottomless coffee and some special habanero taquitos that the bored chefs made without solicitation, piling them onto a plate and urging me to "eat more" every time i passed it. when management informed me one week later via lengthy, apologetic text that they "couldn't fit me on the schedule" i spitefully avoided the place, which proved difficult because i live around the corner, and all of my roommates had begun flings with the bartenders. ashley became addicted to momi's vegetable lasagna and i accompanied her on these drunken dinners, sipping tap water as she hit on the bartender with the ponytail, who offered us free desserts for being sexy/loyal customers. as management shifted from the brittle haired douche with the phony accent and a new girlfriend every week to the bald french men who spent last wednesday night in my living room playing my records at 3am as ashley sobbed and listed the worst qualities of her ex-bf, my irritation with momi softened. mollica invited me to dinner in our hood, and texted me from his seat at mominette, which prompted my involuntary groan both because of my bias, and because he didn't give me a chance to select another option. i arrived late and ordered only after mollica and adam both received their pork chop and burger, respectively. i talked and ordered the duck hash while mollica ate and listened. (silence is always an indicator of enjoyment.) adam engaged me in conversation and at the end of the meal admitted that his burger "wasn't anything special." when the waiter took my order for duck hash he warned me that it was "very light." i appreciated his honesty, although i assumed as much because it is listed under appetizers. i informed him that i didn't mind it's lightness so long as it was delicious. my duck hash arrived in a the shape of a can of pinto beans, with a circular, organic fried egg sitting at its apex. because the duck came shredded (the same shape as lo mein beef) the texture of the bird's flesh was lost on me. I did feel some of the ends of the duck shreds were crisp, but the mash of potato that served as the bed for the duck was overwhelming. the darkness of the dining room also capped my ability to savor everything, since i couldn't see what i was eating, and my phone died mid-photo. it's a superficial criticism to ask for more meat but i love to eat ducks and could have used a few more shreds tbh. only a bone remained on mollica's empty plate. he owes me $5 bc momi doesn't accept credit cards (its written in tiny print at the bottom of the menu).

Authentic NYC Pizza at it's best. We stop here each time we are in New York. It seems to be a favorite among the locals as well. The staff are always courteous and service is top notch. If you want authentic NYC Pizza, go here!

Am I missing something? I'm looking at all these 4-5 star reviews and I'm wondering if I ended up at the wrong restaurant. I love empanadas as much as the next person, but this place really did not do it for me. And I really wanted to like it too, as it's only a couple of blocks away from my workplace. Started off with the guac & chips. The guacamole seemed to be lacking in lime and the chips were all right. I've had better. Could've just made this at home. Oh, also there was a hair in the guac. My boyfriend and I got 5 empanadas between us. The cute little paper bags they come in that tells you what each one is was nice, but I didn't get the right ones anyway. I had ordered a beef empanada and got the spinach & feta cheese. No worries, since I was thinking of ordering that one anyway but really?? I can foresee this being a huge problem if someone ordered something to go and didn't realize they didn't get what they paid for until they got home. SUPER tight space. It's like eating lunch in a hallway. My coat and other winter layers took up half my seat. Their only saving grace is the service. Waiters were very friendly and the food came out relatively quickly. And the sauce they give on the side is pretty yummy as well. I'd be willing to give it another chance if someone's willing to pay for everything. Otherwise, my search for awesome and cheap empanadas continues!

I love this place! Great soups and Greek salad and spinach pie and tuna sandwiches. I've been a fan for years. The dining "room" is small and cramped but prices are low and the food is always fresh and delicious. I've only been there for lunch and look forward to going back for dinner. Services is fine -- not special - but more than adequate for a special little SOHO secret gem

This place was fantastic! Â While vacationing in New York, we were searching for a delicious champagne brunch near the park. Â  Unfortunately, it seemed like everything was ridiculously overpriced and the menu wasn't that impressive. Â Calle Ocho, however, was perfect! Â Sangria brunch...much better than champagne brunch! Â The food was so flavorful and the portion size was not too big and not too small. Â It did feel a little crowded at times with some of the tables being so close together. Â The sangria station was awesome - so many flavors to choose from. Â I really liked that you got to choose your own, but sometimes the line can get backed up with everyone crowded around at once. Â I'd definitely return to Calle ocho on my next trip to the Big Apple.

Overrated. Â I've been to the other location on multiple occasions, and this new one on upper west was calling! Here's why Ippudo is getting the overrated award for the week: long lines, menu item after menu item sold out (at 4?), and the one thing I was hoping for, a big steaming bowl of vegan ramen, is significantly smaller and more expensive than his pork-based brothers. Â  Disappointing.
cheap & cheerful great spot for a quick lunch

A pretty good Ramen house. They cook fast though, so I didn't expect perfection. Some people like their noodles a little on the overcooked side, like myself. #softnoodles. That's a little tougher to get here, due to the sheer volume of customers. But still, quality stuff.

Went to Lombardi's after seeing it on Food Network and been the oldest Pizzeria in the U.S. I lived in Italy and this pizza is not even close with the low end Pizzeria in Perugia, Rome, Naples, Venice and other places. Poor service, extremely expensive and the staff was ok. They were not rude but not friendly. The wanted 40 bucks for a t-shirt. I can get a NY Yankees cheaper than Lombardi's. Save your money, go some where else and do not fall for the tourist trap.

Unlike every yelper here, I came here for dinner with a group on. Got here at 7pm on a Thursday night, seated ourselves, greeted by a server and told him we were using a group on, and everything was smooth sailing. The group on included two entrees, two drinks, and two desserts for $29. No restrictions on the meals just only on the drinks. So we got a red and white sangria. A little watered down but still good. I got the baked macaroni with salmon, not even a big fan of fish but I do enjoy mac n cheese. REALLY AMAZING! the mac was crusted on the top and very cheesy in the middle, and the salmon was a great touch. My date got the roasted lamb shank, which was tender and juicy. Desserts: got the chocolate brownie..a true crack on a plate goodness & date got the Tiramisu--she wasn't used to the texture of it but it was still great. Only had to $5 tax plus tip. Not a bad value for the meal experience. If I'm around the hood I will stop back in again.

They have breakfast tacos, by far some of the best savory breakfast/brunch I've had in a while. The brisket and ribs during dinner service are topnotch. Seating doesn't seem to be a problem in the morning. People have been talking about seating like it defines the entire experience. In fact I enjoy that people have to be patient to get seated here. The food is off the hook, that's what matters. So far I haven't been let down

After three months spent in college dorms, the first thing I do when I get back to the city is get me some roast pork. Big Wong is known for their roast pork, chicken, and duck over rice and they do it especially well. It was a raining Wednesday afternoon so it was crowded like always. My waitress sat us on the round table in the back and took my mom and I down. We shared a plate of roast pork and roast duck and a bowl of rice for each of us. Honestly, I think the pork was especially good and the duck was especially fatty today just because it brought back those nostalgic feelings. It was $17 for the whole meal and it filled us both up; Don't hesitate because they do speak enough English to get your order down and back to you.
I can't wait to go back again!

I wanted to find fault with this place so badly. I was so annoyed all of the times I tried to go when it first opened and was rebuffed for lack of a reservation. Then, on a whim, I managed to book one about an hour beforehand and had an amazing meal. The food (I had the special pasta and he had the shellfish/lobster combo) was amazing, including the funnelcake (srsly! funnelcake!) dessert. The service was impeccable and the bread is ridiculously good. The food isn't fussy, though it's incredibly well thought out and creative. I would go back in a second.

AVOID WEEKEND NIGHTS! Â Our group of 9 met in the downstairs Taproom on a Saturday night. Â We put our names on the list for The Parlor & waited for nearly 2 hours with no luck. Â I'm sure we would have had better luck if our group size was 4 or less. Â The Taproom was extremely crowded, loud, & the bartenders were obviously overwhelmed. Â There were a couple occasions where it took nearly 15 minutes to get a drink. Â However, even with all the negatives I mentioned, TDR's atmosphere & signature drinks (had the Grog, Old Fashion, & Martini) far exceeded my expectations. Â I am definitely looking forward to trying this place out on a weekday night or during the day. Â I have a feeling my review of this place will quickly turn into a 5 after my next visit.

Pretty damn good. I could drink the warm maple butter by the gallon! I had the french toast and BF had the blueberry pancakes. If I had to do it over again, I'd get the pancakes. There's a reason this place was featured on Bobby Flay's Pancake Throwdown! Expect long waits for weekend brunch.

I don't know how anybody can give this place a rating other than 5. The best pizza I have ever had. I don't like long waits. For this pizza, I don't mind the wait though! This place has a two hour wait after you go there and give your name. They don't take reservations. My husband tells me that he will never forget the expression in my face after I had the first bite of this pizza. We ordered our pizza with pepperoni, roasted garlic and shallot. It was out of this world. The use high quality fresh ingredients and amazing cheese and tomato sauce on the pizza. I will go back here again and again. I would only order the pizza. I don't recommend the calzone. Service was friendly and great. The ambience is cozy and warm.

With so many solid ramen spots now scattered throughout Manhattan, Ippudo no longer boasts the crazy two-hour wait typical of years ago. At least, that's not what I experienced. When three girlfriends and I visited this Thursday, we waited just 30 minutes before being seated. But perhaps we got lucky. Though Ippudo is cheap for NYC, $14 to $16 for a bowl of ramen is not. This ramen, however, is worth every penny. The broths are flavorful and complex; far beyond the watered-down, simple taste of what you'd get from instant ramen. The noodles themselves are perfectly al dente, and the toppings - from eggs to spicy paste - offer a fun customization option that can greatly enhance your meal. Ippudo's appetizers are solid, too, and the pork buns are an absolute must! The spot itself is chic and cool, and surprisingly open. It's a cool little restaurant to bring out-of-towners to for a cheaper unique experience. Just be careful with the drinks, as it's the $10 cocktails that cause the bill to run up. If you want more noodles in your soup, don't forget to go Kae-dama. For $2, a waiter will bring you another heaping scoop and drop it in your broth (so make sure you don't drink too much of it). And don't forget to do like the Japanese and sluuuurp! It shows appreciation of the meal... and if the noise level at Ippudo was any indication, you better believe everyone there was more than content with their experience!

3.5/5 for me here I popped in with a larger group for a dinner around 8pm on a Thursday evening, and the place was very lively. Â The bar up in the front had people eating along the whole thing as well as all the tables, maybe due to the MLB playoffs and Thursday night football game? Â Regardless, a good scene if you are looking to pop in for a drink and catch anything on TV . We sat for dinner around 8:15pm when they were ready to seat us in 1/2 dining halls. Â The atmosphere was a bit more upscale with the linen table clothes and dim lighting, so it is a perfect spot for a date should you need a place. Â The menu was very vast but focused on fish (you guessed it) and meat. Â  For starters, I tried the Lobster Bisque which was pretty standard and had some lumps of meat. Â For entrees, I tried the Halibut that was cooked very well and had some simple flavors as well as the NY Strip that was cooked to order. Â As some sides, there was some Lobster Mac n Cheese that was ok and the herb fries that were good. It was priced as a fish/meat restaurant in the city should be and after all the food and drinks with the tip, we ended up paying around $100 a person. Â The service was attentive and not over-bearing so I appreciated that especially with a larger group. Buon appetito.

I would commit a felony for this meal. Â One of the best sushi experiences you can have in the country. Â Not cheap, but also not outrageously expensive considering the quality. Yasuda is known for the rice. Â Skip the sashimi and go straight for the sushi. Â The premium you're paying for is the rice + fish combination which = sushi heaven. Â  Temperature of the fish is perfect (too many places serve ice cold sushi). Â Rice is unparalleled. Â Cut is superb (everything is sooo tender). Â The eel is unlike 99% of the eel you get at sushi bars. Â It is fresh and is Yasuda's specialty. Â Salmon roe is also done in house and is amazing. Â Tuna* is ridiculous. Had the omakase (chef's choice) at the sushi bar last time i went. Â 20+ pieces of different fish for ~$150 after tax+tip. Â Not a bad deal considering the quality. Â  Note - sushi neophytes would be better off elsewhere. Â This place is quite costly and if you don't appreciate pure and traditional sushi, save the money. Â  *Yes, they unabashedly serve (endangered) bluefin tuna. Â And I ate it. Â And loved it. Â Sorry mother nature.
Yup ... its ny thing!.. its delicious at 3 in the morning when your slurring!

Perfect location for a good late night snack wrap The guy at the counter said the most popular wraps are: The howling (7.95) Brothers Grimm (6.95) The hanging chairs are awesome but there are only 2. I would have a blast if I were inebriated. Â The food was also delicious. Â Restaurant doesn't have much seating, kind of like a Papaya Dog around the edges of the restaurant. Â But seriously, try it.
Love this husband and wife duo. Â  Their korean fusion is great. Â  Love the atmosphere, and how hard the couple works.

This is my go to place for the best ramen in Manhattan. Sure, there's normally a 1-1.5 hour wait to get seated.. But if there's that kind of wait, it must be a good place.. I'd say the best time to go here and have a reasonable wait is around 11:30 AM, any later than that.. Good luck to you! It's so worth it though! If you manage to have patience and get a seat, you've gotta try the hirata buns and samurai rib for appetizers.. Akamaru modern ramen for the main entree, though any ramen is just as good! And ofcourse for dessert, mascarpone cheese and ice cream is the must try! It's also worth noting that they finally opened up another location in midtown. Enjoy!

I want to like Moto, really. It seems like North Williamsburg gets all the good food, so I'm grateful for the few restaurants that line the long stretch of Broadway. Moto appeared to be a cute place the first time I came with the vintage francophile shtick, but now it feels more like I'm going to Applebees or TGIFridays with random junk tacked to the walls. I want to say I've had good service, but I'm kind of unsure if I've even actually had service. Someone seats me every time, and whoever is behind the bar eventually will stroll over and take my order, and I'm pretty sure whoever is working in the kitchen will come and bring it out my meal, but that's pretty much the extent of service at this place, especially when you realize the cutesy wine bottle of water on the table is more for their benefit. It always takes forever to get the bill. Maybe this lazy behavior is just part of the "authentic Paris feel", but it's not cutting it for me. I've had everything on the menu, which appears to never change. Nothing has wowed me ever besides maybe the Date Cake (yum!), although the Swiss Alps Mac & Cheese remains a favorite, and the Ham And Cheese Baked Eggs at brunch are quite tasty. The live music is usually pretty good, although more than once I've had a tip jar come by my table in a pretty aggressive way. It's just like being on the JMZ, without the mariachi bands! Moto, I want to like you. You're close to my apartment, you are appealing on the surface, and people are probably going to migrate to the Hewes stop and throw cash at you for the sheer novelty of the experience. But step up your game, because I'm already seeking out something new in the 'hood.
Run, don't walk to Bushwicks top restaurant. Inexpensive and 5 stars! Can't beat that with a stick!!

Best brisket I ever had (and I'm a BBQ lover from Texas)! Must get: Brisket Pork belly: melts in your mouth and full of flavor on its own Baked beans: mixed with burnt ends and sausage! THE BEST baked beans I ever had in my life. They were definitely my favorite item at Fette Sau. Recommend: Beef tongue: super tender Key lime pie: not very sweet, but very good Pass on next time: Pulled pork: like others have said, it was dry and not very flavorful. Better when sandwiched in a bun, slathered with sauce. Ribs: smokey but super dry. I was expecting fall-of-the-bone pork, but I could barely tear the meat off the rib. Pickles: not as sour as I like my pickles to be Broccoli: it was good but with a plate full of other deliciousness, may not be worth getting Sausage: spicy but also not very flavorful On to the negatives: Got there on Sat at 6:30pm and the wait in the freezing cold was about 1.5 hours. There were some non-locals inside who were done eating and just taking up space while people were lined out the door, around the corner, painfully waiting! This place is not a bar, people! And the staff said and did nothing about it. There is only 1 guy cutting up the meat, which seems pretty inefficient. But I guess if he was able to work faster or had more people helping him, more people would be with plates of delicious meat but no place to sit.

Great little French restaurant tucked in the West Village. Loved my coq au vin. Friendly staff and great ambiance. The wait was only about 15 minutes on a Thursday night, which was an added bonus after putting our name on a 1.5 hour waiting list at The Meatball Shop. Our table was a little small--and not just NY small, really small. But other than that, we had a great dining experience.

This place has hands down killer food! the Escargot is cooked perfectly i have has snails a couple times before and left feeling like i had just eaten a bunch of chewy snails... here it is tender and flavorful. Â Same goes for the Moule Frites, Duck Confit Salad and Mac n Cheese! My s/o and i love to come here and order every app on the menu just because we can never decide.

I've been dining at this Chelsea restaurant since it opened and it has gone through many transitions. Unfortunately, my two most recent dining experiences were less than stellar. The problem is that the current chef has a habit of combining ingredients that fight each other rather than compliment each other. This evening, I ordered Roasted Eggplant Soup with white bean crouton and blistered tomatoes. What I received was a soup that was so overwhelmed with garlic and tomato, that the eggplant couldn't be tasted. Â My entree was Atlantic Salmon with Couscous. What I received was a sliver of Salmon that was cooked medium well rather than medium rare (as I was told the chef prepared it) and the Couscous was a spicy concoction that, while delicious, didn't mesh with the Salmon which tasted Â fine, but nothing more. Dessert was a shared chocolate hazelnut parfait with dried fruit compote. What arrived at the table looked nothing like a parfait but both my dining partner and I enjoyed it. Â Service was excellent given the number of tables that our server had. So, to sum up: my problem with this restaurant lies with the current chef who seems to pair flavors that fight each other rather than compliment each other. The food is very good, overall, the decor is fine but if you are there when the restaurant is full, you'll have to speak VERY loudly for your dining partner to hear you . I really enjoyed my meal here, but it could have been far better!
Large menu and portions. No reservations or alcohol. Good times and food.

Suffering from a bo zai fan addiction as of late, I was really excited to read about this place. They also have the kind of small cheung fun with peanut sauce, oyster sauce and sesame seeds that I really like but can never find anywhere in New York. So really excited is probably an understatement. Half of the long weekend I could not wait to get to Tuesday night to try it! I had read on some chowhound posts that this place had better bo zai fan than both a-wah and yummy noodles. We got off to a really bad start here as there were two of us with a lot of bags and stuff, and since we were seated at a four person table, we put our stuff on the two seats we weren't using. It was a Tuesday night. They had hardly any business. The waitress made a big deal out of it. Of course if it got crowded, we'd move our stuff to free up the space. Not sure why she had to get us into a bad mood right from the start. Then one of the other waiters came by to take our order and he just asked a bit rudely if we were ready to order. So, no points for service. But whatever, on to the food... We got the steamed rice noodle rolls w/peanut and oyster sauce, the beef brisket and tendon and the pork meat patty w/salted fish bo zai fan. The beef brisket was good. Nothing to complain about, nothing spectacular. I would order it again. The cheung fun was awesome. Not only was I happy to find it in NY, but I was also happy that the pieces were rolled so tightly, how many of them were and how hot they were! My wife thought there was too much sauce. I liked the extra sauce. Now, the bo zai fan. The positives are that they give you quite a bit of the pork meat patty, the pork meat patty is quite tasty and there are lots of seasonings with it and that they are not cheap with the salted fish. However, I think they over did it with the salty ingredients. It is good that they stingy on the seasonings, but they also need to be in control of them. Some bites were just overbearingly salty, and I believe I did a pretty good job of mixing the rice. The worst part on the bo zai fan though was that it had no bo zai fan flavor! The rice was moderately crispy at the bottom, so the texture was nice. But there was just something missing from the taste. Â My suspicion is that this is due to them using a cast iron pot to cook the rice rather than a clay pot. I think maybe the clay pot caramelizes the rice bit more and allows the slightly sweet/carbony flavor to move up into the pot of food. Without it, it tastes like crisy rice cooked in a metal pot. Not bad, but lacking the flavor that makes the dish unique. It also happens to be the flavor that caused me to go there in search of bo zai fan. So I would not recommend the hot pot rice here. I believe there are better finds elsewhere in Chinatown. I would recommend the steamed rice noodle roll. It is the best I have had in New York. I would also recommend getting it to go, unless we were particularly unlucky last night with the service.

I am addict of the cuban sandwich and the other day a lady was having the last cuban sandwich of the day next to me and when I asked they said hers was the last. Â However this place cheers you up with many other options like fish tacos and of course the fantastic corn!!! I love it

My fiance and I wanted to try a new-to-us place. Even though I'd been to Sanford's a handful of times, it had been a couple years since my last visit, so we decided to go there. The first time I went to Sanford's was back in 2008ish, when it had more of a sorta-fancy diner vibe. They've since remodeled (in 2009, I think), and I've been there since the remodel, but that "diner vibe" always stuck in my head. So when I described it to him, I said, "you know, it looks really fancy, but it's like a nice diner." Yeah, I totally forgot what it was like. While they do have a few sandwiches that you'd find in a diner, overall, the menu is not at all diner-like. The only thing that's diner-like at this point is the booth setup, and even those don't look too diner-like anymore. (I just used the word "diner" too many times and it has lost all meaning.) I got the chicken avocado club, he had the falafel wrap. Pretty simple, but we both ejoyed our food. Plus, the sandwiches came with good sized house salad and our choice of fries or blue tortilla chips (he upgraded his fries to sweet potato for an extra $1). With all of that food, we had enough to bring some home for lunch the next day. Score! Considering the amount and quality of the food, it was definitely a good value. Also, the busboys are great - our water glasses were never below half-full, and we're big water-drinkers. (This is something of A Thing for my fiance.)

Cheap cheap cheap, and so delicious! The sesame pancakes are phenomenal - get the duck. And the dumplings are great for the price (not the best I've had, but GREAT for $0.20 a piece). It is a hole in the wall (literally only 5 seats, two of which are basically in the doorway), so don't expect to sit down to eat.

Dining at Zizi is a casual but cool experience. The place is small but it was easy to get a seat on Monday night. We ordered: Pita and yogurt Crazy Baba Gravlax Limona Roast veggies Shawarma w/ hummus Braised short ribs Everything we ordered was delicious! Surprisingly, the standout for me was the crazy baba- highly recommend. It was nicely seasoned with a rich creamy texture that almost reminded me of avocado. The pita bread was fresh made, warm, and fluffy. Everything we ordered was tasty. Definitely a relaxed and comfortable option for last minute dinner.

One of the best dinners that I've had in a long time. A friend has wanted to try this place out for a while, and so, we made reservations for the night and were seated immediately upon arrival. There could have been more space between the tables, but coming from Manhattan, I'm used to eating in close quarters with dining neighbors so it didn't bother me as much as it would others. Ordered some cocktails, which were really delicious. I like how their cocktails have unique ingredients, which reminded me of drinks from a mixology bar. Now, food. Bacon wrapped dates stuffed with blue cheese was my favorite dish of the night. It was melt in your mouth good. Second favorite was the scallops on a bed of risotto. The bacon doughnuts were quite delicious too at the end of the meal, so that would be my third favorite. We ordered seared foie gras, broccoli rabe with truffle toast, and breaded lamb as well. Although all were good, I wouldn't order them again next time like I would the other three dishes. Overall, I'd give this place a 4.5. Food came out with perfect timing in between each dish. It was also an open kitchen, so you can see the chef creating your food. However, minus .5 since I would've been more comfortable with more space and three out of the six dishes were good but not 5 stars good.

Xixa offers an affordable tasting menu at $40 where I felt like the food kept on coming. Â I felt satisfied with the amount of food for the price, it is a tapas spot after all and for two people about two plates came out at a time. The cuisine is described as Mexican, but I feel like they are definitely trying to do something more, starting off perhaps with a Mexican concept then twisted with modern, American, and several other global influences. The meal started out with an amuse bouche of room temperature butternut squash cubes. Cute, tiny and sweet start to the meal. I liked most of the courses, especially the duck (my favorite-duck lettuce wraps). I thought it was a creative menu, very well thought out and composed. The drunken shrimp were cooked well in a deliciously spicy sauce that reminded me of the flavors of New Orleans. The lamb meatballs were an interesting concoction-a mixture of what tasted like middle eastern flavored lamb, served in marinara sauce on top of a spaghetti-like-pasta tossed with black beans. I thought this dish might have been a little over the top, incorporating too many components put together, although it was flavorful. Â I'm not a fan of beef tartare but thought the marrow that complemented it was good, although the blue corn tortilla shells tasted burnt. The two desserts were the best of both worlds, a fruity option of jalapeno sorbet with churros Â and banana chocolate ice cream with a black sesame paste on top. I didn't think the black sesame went with the other parts of the dish, but I am happy whenever black sesames is in my meal. The tasting menu meant constant interruptions of food descriptions, and I thought the one question I asked came with a little attitude, unless I was paranoid. Otherwise the wait staff quite friendly and on the ball; while they chose small glasses for the water, it was hardly ever left empty which was well appreciated (but that dude's job would be easier if they were larger!) I am sure sitting in the booths is great, but I don't recommend the tables in the front left, because the chairs just didn't seem fit for comfortable dining.

Lovely, sweet, darkly lit /cozy spot that makes NYC special in land of famous chef 's over hyped mega restaurants. Best f onion soup, duck kassoulet was devoured by my date (14 yr old son ) he also slammed the escargot which was delish. I had the potato n bacon casserole- yum. Profiterole sauce Devine but ice cream n pastry just ok. Out the door under 100 made this the best deal in the city for this country girl's n foodie son trip. Yes, close to u neighbor...... sweet locals Magen n her nice s Carolina hubby were given my leftover wine. But a new York treasure if u r tired of snooty servers n overpriced gramercy tavern meals.....enjoy!

Breakdown of their specialty burger: Soft bun A sliced ring of pineapple (yum) Pickled beet Â (Really? yes, adds great flavor) Burger fried sunnyside up egg (Oh, baby!) onions lettuce tomato Soft bun The burger was an experience! The beet and the pineapple really sets this burger apart from the rest! The egg is also just an awesome high cholesterol touch! The burger is quite big and difficult to fit into your mouth, but with a little smooshing, it'll work just fine! The bun can't really stand the weight of it all and eventually collapses, but by that time your already hooked and willing to scoop up all that fell on the plate! BUT!!!! To top it off!!! Fries in truffle oil!! Come on!!! They really out did it here! Forget the ketchup and hotsauce! No need for condiments here! I'm itching to come back!

The food was ok, but the service was just bad. On May 22nd, afternoon, we ordered food to go and the person taking the order seemed so annoyed and unhappy to be there, she seldom talked and just nodded. Not sure what her problem was, but she made it very unpleasant to order from this restaurant. With so many choices in this beautiful city, Â why would I spend my money at a place that gives me such an attitude?? I'm not going back there...

I have to say this place is pretty great....From the dark lighting (for mood but of course) to the wine and beer only menu to the tapas that they offer and the rocking music that they play....everything was on par and great...There ended up being live music on the night I was there and they were a great duo....overall I throughly enjoyed myself.

A great restaurant in lower Manhattan! Their Mediterranean seafood salad (with olive oil) was divine. Calamari, shrimp, scallops boiled, lightly salted, and dressed in olive oil. Amazing. A must try. Their grilled sea bass was also great. The only drawback is that the restaurant is noisy. The noise level made it very difficult to talk across the table. It gets very crowded too, more like a mix of a busy bar and dining area. Food is good though. Service was not prompt but OK.
This place is just simply amazing. No need to look at the menu because the specials are infinite. Always a favorite of ours in every aspect, food, service and anything else you can think of.
Hands down best blueberry pancakes i've ever tasted! right downto the texture & syrup. service was ok but the menu was great. i'll definitely come back for more.

If you know about Pio Pio in NYC it's all about the Peruvian chicken and green sauce. Great roasted chicken which comes quartered and endless green sauce to dip it in. Just ask and they'll bring over another dish of the heavenly flavorful green sauce. It really goes with everything. Dip their empanadas in them as well. Highly recommend any of their ceviches as well. Well balanced cold ceviche that cooks the mix of seafood and spicey at that. It's great for groups as this is the largest of the pio pio chain but it does get noisy. Nice decor and ambiance and the waitstaff was helpful in making our table happy with presenting a birthday cake for one of my friends. Recommend going family style as it's plenty of food by ordering the mixed chicken plate that includes the chicken, fries, rice and beans, beef sausage, and platanos. The sweet maduros was great as well and with a order of the peruvian fried rice we were stuffed with a group of 7. I'll definitely be back.

came here yesterday. WTF happened to the food. Tasted fine, looked sloppy. Sounds like the recipe of a once authentically good restaurant turning into another average thai joint in nyc (we got enough of those, what happened sripaphai???) Service kind of sucked, but i wasn't expecting much. Just really disappointed in the quality, think over cooked and or over saturated with the flavors they were famous for in the first place. They still have a place in my heart but the last trip was utterly upsetting. Put the heart back in the kitchen sripaphai, don't let the nyc transplant wealth get to you, its POISON!

Ah... good ol' faithful Vanessa's. How I Love thee. You were always there for me when I needed some quick snacks and a trip to the bathroom. You were there for me when I needed some herbal tea. You were there for me when I had only 3 dollars in my pocket and was starving to death. You were there for me when I needed a place to stay late at night. You were there... Don't ever leave me.

Oh this place has got it goin' on!! Came here on a Sunday afternoon and you could just feel the excitement here. Everyone was oohing and awing over food, licking fingers, taking pictures of the food, etc... I chose the chicken biscuit and home style potatoes. Amazing. Buffalo style chicken in a biscuit with honey and butter all over it made me a happy girl. To top off the meal I had a lemon poppy seed donut, heavenly. Of course I felt like I needed a day of fasting afterward, but a meal like this every once and a while just makes you feel satisfied. I would have given five stars but the seating situation was a disappointment. My husband and I were seated next to a couple at a table for four. Like, as in sharing a table for four!! It was quite awkward. I felt like I could not move or even talk at a normal tone. I think the couple next to us felt the same way. I would have rather waited an extra 10 minutes and had our own table then being seated with another couple. So that was a little greedy and tacky on Pies n Thighs part if you ask me. Very memorable little place, can't wait to go back.
This place was awful. My partner got really bad food poisoning from their pulled pork burgers and the service wasn't great. Stay away unless you want to be sick for days.
4 dumplings for $1! Super cheap and pretty good. I've also tried their sesame pancakes, but I would advise you steer clear of those; they're oily and lack any real flavor.

This is by far the best dumpling place I have eaten at. Soup dumplings are a 10/10 with their juicy and sweet broth. The outside is perfectly thin as we'll Fried dumplings are also the best I've had maybe due to the sweet soy sauce Their sesame chicken is actually big pieces of chicken crisply fried w sauce and broccoli on the side. A great poportion! Service is fast, the place is clean and the quality is great.

Great great great snack food for a quick drop-in before and/or after the bar. Was wtih friends and tried almost everything, to my surprise the Bean Taquito done "chronic" style was my favourite. Fast service, too. Will definitely be heading back.

What's not to love. The maÃ®tre d' or owner (I have never quite figured out if he owns the place) is just a lovely lovely man. I've been coming here for about five years, and I pop in every few months. He always remembers me and greets me so warmly. Once I was there with my 18 month-year-old daughter who was freaking out because of time zone changes. He brought her ice cream outside and kept coming out to check on us. Very nice warm person. Great bartender I am pretty sure there is a new chef. The menu has changed. Croque Monsieur until about 4 PM. To die for. French onion soup. Also to die for. Bartender makes a killer white Russian They put up with my crazy mom and her dog in the stroller. If that doesn't say it all, I don't know what does. (Don't worry it was within health department guidelines) You cannot go wrong here. Â Great food and great people and great service.

I'm being honest here, but New York trumps California when it comes to pizza. Â The best pizza I've had in Cali (Zachary's at Berkeley) falls a bit short compared to this place. Â The crusts are perfect and the sauce is unparalleled. Â  If I ever decide to move to NYC, I can see myself dining here a lot.

This review is long overdue since I have been here twice already. Â The one thing that stands out about this place is the impeccable service. Â I have eaten at a fair share of nice restaurants and I remain impressed with the level and grace of the service here. Â The food is to die for- the portions appear to be not large at all however there are so many courses and in betweens that you leave there feeling very full and very satisfied. Â The service is synchronized (meaning everyone gets served at the exact same time- pretty much one waiter per person) and they are also very helpful when it comes to pairing wine selections with the dishes. Â Make sure to sit in the back- that's where the service is but be sure to make your reservations 4 weeks in advance! (unless you have an amex!) Â  My second trip there was for a dinner in the private dining room which was extremely elegant and very quiet- perfect for an intimate group that wants some privacy. Â I highly recommend having dinner here, it is so worth the pretty penny!

My bridesmaids and fiance surprised me with dinner here in the summer for my birthday. I had been wanting to try this for a while and was ecstatic to finally experience this "farm to table" restaurant. The decor was absolutely gorgeous. I loved the chandeliers and the garden in front of the open kitchen in the back. We shared dishes of ceviches, mushroon pizzas, and ice cream on caramel popcorn. All very yummy. Overall, the experience was great, made even better by amazing company.

My favorite stop in NYC!! Fridays they have Blue Mountain espressos!! Love the brewery upstairs and the individual markets inside make this my first stop every time I get to the city. Â Staff is always friendly and helpful and will always point me in the right direction.

Hmm I was kind of disappointed because I thought this was THE place in Harlem for fried chicken and waffles. I ordered the Al Sharpton, which is chicken and waffles, the standard choice obviously. The breast was sort of dry but it was still okay. The thigh was better because it was less dry. The waffle was pretty good though! The only complaint I had was the dry breast; everything else was fine. But I had ROSCOS and that was the BEST I ever had so I was sorely disappointed :(. The staff are nice though. And everything on their menu is named after famous black Americans who ate there, such as Al Sharpton, Jesse Jackson, Obama etc etc.

My go-to-place in my hood when I need something dependable and consistent. It's not unusual to see this place jam packed each night with a pretty even mix of locals and tourists. Â You can thank the warm atmosphere, friendly service and nice mix of classic American favorites. Personally I recommend their French Dip sandwich and nicely prepared burgers. Â The latter is always well cooked and the meat always arrives perfectly juicy. Â One of my favorite entrees is their shrimp and grits that's lathered in a tasty lobster bisque. Â The flavor is rich and the dish is perfect for those cold winter nights. As for the dessert - you can't go wrong with their banana cream pie. Â While the portion is pretty substantial (you'll be fine sharing this with someone) - the taste is pretty balanced and it doesn't come off as being too sweet or overwhelming. Â The texture of the cream filling, coupled with sweet bananas and tasty crust, is just divine. Â It's a perfect way to wrap up a good meal. Since this place gets crowded pretty much after 6pm every night, and they don't take reservations on open table, you should plan on either arriving early or calling ahead to ensure you get a seat, especially if you're looking to catch a show.

Overall great dining experience. The service was absolutely top notch. Food was very good but portions on my fiancÃ©es pasta dish seemed very low for the price when compared to the price/size of the seafood medley entree I got, which tasted great. I'd go here again, and recommend it to others.

GIANT SECURITY GUARD: "IS THAT OUTSIDE FOOD? CAUSE WE DON'T ALLOW OUTSIDE FOOD IN THIS RESTAURANT??" SNARKY LUU SISTERS: YES. BUT, THESE ARE LEFTOVERS. WE'RE NOT EATING IT HERE, WE JUST STOPPED FOR A FOURTH MEAL AFTER DINNER. RUDE. It was my last night in NYC and you bet your bottom dollar I was going to eat until I was uncomfortably full cause hey, anything worth eating, is worth overeating. And that is exactly what I thought when I sister jokingly suggested that we stop by Habana Outpost after a large dinner at Calle Ocho and I seriously took her up on the offer. We ordered the corn on the cob: grilled corn, mayo, parika and queso fresco--YES, PLEASE! This treat was reminiscent of our days in Highland Park in LA when corn on the cob used to sell like hotcakes from those questionable food vendors (if you can call them food vendors..) pushing around a cart in 80 degree weather and ringing a bell! EXCEPT, the corn on the cob at Habana did not give my sister the shits like the cart guys used to (who knew mayo sure was questionable in 80 degree weather when it's stored in a cart). Definitely a place to dine at, Habana Outpost serves all kinds of delicious Cuban food and their corn on the cob sure is something worth trying! AND, they show movies on Sundays during the summer just projected on a wall--it's a very lively experience with a ton of patrons! Fun fact: Habana Outpost is the first solar powered restaurant in NYC!

Nook is off the hook! I apologize for the lame play on words, but this place a great little find in Hell's Kitchen. I came here for my friend's birthday dinner, and expected a big fancy place, but it was a small and cozy restaurant that became very intimate with a group of people I just met. With the great BYOB with no corkage fee, each of us 6 girls brought in our own bottle of wine. The waiter was extremely friendly, probably because he kept on having to pass us each time because we were sitting at the table in the back right by the kitchen. It was very crowded, but what do you expect from a nice, trendy restaurant in Manhattan? Now for the food. We started off with complimentary bread, it was not out of the ordinary amazing, but it was decent bread. It could have been heated up a little to have that warming feeling because it was freezing outside, but the bread is just stacked in its baskets on the counter in the back. Appetizers - we got the mushroom cigars ($7.50), which were two pieces of flaky, thin dough that wrapped delicious mushrooms and other things that I could not tell because it was too dark. It came with a little portion of salad with balsamic that was a great touch to balance the savoriness of the mushroom cigars. Entrees - a few of us got separate dishes, and I got to taste a bit of everything Tuscan Chicken ($17) - I would rarely order chicken at a nice restaurant, because it is usually something that I regularly each at home or at the dining halls. But, this chicken was sliced up in pieces already and had a somewhat pesto sauce in the middle, and it was extremely tasty! I had a few bites from the person across from me, and two people ordered this and finished it completely! I definitely enjoyed this a bit more than what I ordered. Sashimi Peppered Tuna ($17) - yum yum! It is a bit random to have sushi type food at an American restaurant, but they made it amazingly. It was extremely tender and soft and slid down my throat so smoothly. ("That's what she said") Thai-Marinated Grilled Rack of Lamb ($21) - I had a piece of the lamb from the birthday girl, but it was honestly not the best lamb that I have eaten. It was not that flavorful and a bit dry. I would recommend trying some of the other dishes unless you are really in the mood for lamb! Steak Frites ($21) - I ordered the Steak medium rare and it came with the famous rosemary fries. The fries were pretty normal, and I expected a lot more from all of the reviews on yelp. It was only slightly seasoned and it was good and crispy, but not that magnificent. The steak was very juicy and tender, and extremely flavorful. It was lot of meat to handle (sorry, I did it again), and I could not finish even half my steak and shared with everyone else on the table, but I did take bites of everyone else's food. This dish also came with a portion of salad with balsamic vinaigrette like the one from the mushroom cigars. It was a good diversified portion of meat, starch, and veggies. I would definitely come back again to Nook, especially because of the awesome BYOB!
This place is great. Â I especially love the oyster flights. Â They're a good deal!

Crazy busy, tight inside, shared table seating, but that does mean you get seated reasonably quickly despite the crowds. Green beans are a little too much dried beef-- not delicate in taste as a result. Not bad though, but disappointing. Xiao long bao in pork form are pretty decent, the pork and crab are even better, but the end product is just average. They lack the delicacy or the presentation of the better places I've had, and while the taste was pretty acceptable, the taste again lacked the explosive bursts of flavor on your taste buds of the best places.
Great wine, great pasta and great space! I enjoyed the fresh mozzarella and prosciutto! Their version of the watermelon tomatoe salad is rich, full of complexity and a must have!!

Dropped in for a pre-event bite with Helena H and some other elites the other night. We shared the mini cachapas app and I had the catira arepa. Mini cachapas- corn pancake with cheese. It tasted good but would've been better if the cheese were more melted. Catira Arepa- chicken with cheddar cheese. Hmm, I'm going against the yelp grain here and will say that it could have been better. The filling (and there was a lot of it) itself had good flavor. However, I was disappointed with the arepa itself. The sweetness from the cornmeal was missing, I didn't mind that the arepa was grilled, but the flavor was missing. oh well. it was okay but in the words of brandy, "almost doesn't count".

Nice old timey feel but really just average pizza. Not bad, but nothing great either, and especially for the price I expected something better. However, I prefer to have more cheese on my pizzas and the margherita style is really more about sauce. So, I guess that's part of the reason why. But honestly, there wasn't a whole lot of flavor in the crust either, or the basil.

Come for the pork buns, stay for the ramen! Â These are my favorite pork buns in NYC, slightly edging out Momofuku. Â I just like the sauce and the mayo flavor better. Â We also had the appetizer ribs which were very tender and delicious. The ramen is really good, too. Â You can rack up the price pretty quick by adding extras to the ramen, but really it would be fine without the extras. Â So, you have to come here at least to try the pork buns, but you'll certainly find many other delicious things on the menu.

I really liked this place and definitely plan to go back, maybe when someone is visiting because it was a pretty fun spot. I knew I was in for a treat when you walk in and the first thing you see is a bar with top ramen under glass! We went on a friday night with two friends at around 11pm and had to wait about 30 minutes for a table, but it was totally worth it. Â My roomate had seen the place on that TV show "The best thing I ever ate..." and it did not disappoint. We got the the fried peppers with yuzu salt--deelish. Then we all got ramen--no complaints and they will even give you an extra helping of noodles for a couple bucks if you have broth left! Â The only thing I wasnt crazy about was green tea marscapone dessert we got.

I go here occasionally with my girlfriends. They do not take reservations so many times we just end up waiting for a table at Von, the bar right next door. Â The host is so friendly and accommodating, he will enter Von and grab you when you're table is ready. You can even bring unfinished drinks from Von to Bianca! Â Bianca's atmosphere is so soothing and the smell of delicious food penetrates the air. Â They serve high quality affordable food. Â The space is cozy, its a small restaurant, however I never felt cramped. Â This place is not good for large crowds, but perfect for a group of four or less.

SO many people know so LITTLE about food, and the fact that they are allowed to review restaurants on Yelp makes Yelp itself a faulty application. Â I will begin all my reviews this way, because I am tired of seeing bad reviews for good restaurants. Â Reviews that are based on 'Small Portions', or 'too expensive prices' , or the worst 'too hipster'. Â You know what? Â Get a job. Â Make more money. Â Stop Stuffing yourself. Â Lastly, stop complaining about these so called 'hipsters' who have already come and gone. Â  Marlow&Sons has consistently lived up to it's reputation. Â It is busy because it is good. Â It is OPEN because it is great. Â If they did not serve great eats they wouldn't survive in this competitive hood. Â Go eat there if you havent, and if waiting in line or eating small dishes is a problem, then don't go. Â  Â Great Food, that is for certain.

I actually wanted to give a zero or minus rating, if I can choose. It was the worst dining experience in NYC ever. The service at the door was terrible and super unorganized, although it was not busy at all as we arrived. You felt that you were not welcome at all. The host girl (not sure Chinese or Japanese or Korean) was so rude and mean. She looked at customers with dirty look and evil eyes for the first minute she saw you, questioned customers with unpleasant tones as if you were criminal. I asked her whether she knows how to smile and whether she knows that its a Jap restaurant and the service should have Jap standard? But she still didnt feel that she was wrong at all and no apology was made at all. Upon departure, she gave me another evil eye. I have been here many times. Although the past experience was not great either, but never as bad as this time. I am not going there any more, boycott this one forever, because I dont want to see her ugly face any more.

Absolutely without a doubt some of the most delicious pizza I have ever tasted! Their signature slice is huge, creamy and an absolute delight! Its definitely the place I hit up for late night pizza. Great price for great food! Win/win!
Definitely a fan of Kobeyaki and will visit again just to have the Udon soup. Â Great service and the atmosphere is like a cafeteria if you don't mind loudness.
Place is always busy but the waits are not long. Good, honest food and plenty of it. Bustling atmosphere but the service is good.

heres how it went... me - can i have one chicken and one beef halal guy - $12 Â please me - no no I want one of each Halal Guy - yes $12 please Me - awww they must have only given one, oh wait what the heck there only $6 each, when breakfast cost us $19 a plate at a diner..... love that NY street food

I very nice Italian Family Serving Style Restaurant. Â Right in the heart of the Theater District. Â We initially had sticker shock when looking at the menu outside the front door and saw how much a "meal" costs. Â But with some reluctance we went inside, and to our surprise, we were seated immediately. Â We really had no understanding of "Family Style", and we ordered spaghetti and meatballs, lasagna and a mixed greens salad appetizer. Â Our waitress asked how many others were coming. Â We said it is was just myself, my wife and my 6 year old son. Â She very politely informed us how much food we had just ordered and asked if we really wanted to order everything. Â She easily saved us $30 and we still didn't finish the salad or spaghetti/meatballs. Â The spaghetti and meatballs meal can easily feed 3-4 adults. Â I just felt the waitress went beyond what she needed to give us great service. Â That means a lot in my book and earns extra respect bonus points. Â  Seems like a great restaurant for large groups because you could sample many different things. Â  Prices weren't that bad (by NYC standards)when you realize that your total is divided by the number of people in your party. Again, can't say enough about how nice and polite the staff was with our visit. Â We look forward to returning on our next trip back to NYC.

I've lived in the area my whole life and last night was the first time I went to The Castello Plan. A friend of mine suggested we meet around 10pm at a local spot. Cool. We weren't there for dinner. Just meeting for a drink and light conversation but we did try one of their small plates. Stewed Mushroom Crostini: the bread was absolutely delicious but its kind of hard to mess up toasted bread with butter. The mushroom concoction was alright. I'm a HUGE FAN of mushrooms and I felt as if the delicate mushroom flavor was overpowered by a heavy handed sprinkle of dill (mixed into the cream sauce). Bottom Line - it was good.. but just good. Nothing special. Brooklyn Crossing: classic vodka with a garnish of pickles. I'm a vodka gal. Vodka is my liquor of choice. This was HORRIBLE. TOTALLY GAG-WORTHY. I know the bartender is adept at drink making but i really don't know what went wrong with my drink. I tried to force myself to drink it but every time I sipped, I felt like vomiting ;( My friend couldn't stomach it either so that was a waste of $12 ={ It wasn't crowded at all when we were there (since it was late) but it is a small space. We didn't have much interaction with the serving staff since we sat at the bar. ~ I'll probably go back since I live 5 minutes away and I do want to try their Hamburger ASAP .. me love hamburgahhhh! But it's not any place to lose your shxt about. Feel me?
I was lucky enough to be there before it's crowded. Well, to be exact, my friend who lives a couple blocks away took a table for me before I came in. Pumpkin lovers, their pancake is GREAT.

I'm 3 for 3 at Supper. I've had several pasta entrees, all delicious. The panna cotta dessert is hands down the best, followed by the homemade tiramisu. The ice cream dish is fun as well... the servers bring out a double shot of espresso and pour it over the ice cream. Overall, great atmosphere, awesome food.

I got the Saigon Shack Special Spicy Pho, and while I was confused by the meatballs & pate (Vietnamese ham), I got over it as soon as I took a bite. The pho broth base & noodles were pretty good! I was also excited to swirl my Sriracha & hoisin sauces together on a sauce dish and dip the contents of my pho, and dump the entire plate of bean sprouts + Jalapeno + basil + lime into my soup. I also enjoyed the cubed beef bun (over vermicelli, but you can get it over rice as well), and really appreciated the abundance of veggies as well as the shallot sauce the beef was sauteed in. Be sure to get a fried egg as well ($1 extra). While the food is objectively delicious and unmistakably Vietnamese, this place is still catered to an American palate (hence, subjectively a 3 but objectively a solid 4 stars). The pho definitely needs more green onions & cilantro, their fish sauce needs to be more "fishy," and they need to up the acidity of the pickled vegetables. I'm still in search for that authentic bowl of pho with tripe & tendon in Manhattan, but until then, Saigon Shack will be the place to scratch my pho itch. Cash only!
One of my favorite - not so best kept secret - places in NYC the service is always on point and I've never been disappointed no matter what I've ordered. Love u fish!

I had lunch here the first time almost 2 months ago. I was so intrigued by the dessert menu, I decided to come back for desserts only. This obscure 2nd floor establishment does not resemble any of the Japanese food joints that line up line up along St. Marks Place. It's the kitschy Zen decor which separate it from that prototype. The serenity of the atmosphere can make you fall asleep. I was tempted to do yoga on the spot, but I didn't want to offend my lunch buddy. I had the Cha-An set A with ice mint tea, my lunch partner had the set B. I was intrigued by the soy milk quiche with mushrooms & scallions that came with the B. It wasn't tasty, but it was pretty interesting to look at. The dessert portion was small, but it was big on taste. The black sesame creame brulee is the only thing on the menu worth raving about. I liked it so much that I came back Â & only ordered that. In lieu of the full tea selection, I treated myself to a lychee martini. This is definitely a place for those who like dining alone.

I hardly ever write reviews, but felt compelled to this time. I used to love this restaurant, the fried chicken is amazing. Service was always top notch and not too crowded if you go early. But unfortunately the owners ended the lease on Blue Ribbon Sushi next door and decided to merge the 2 restaurants together. What has resulted is an overly crowded restaurant unable to keep up with the the flow of customers and level of service. Our waiter, who seemed very inexperienced, didn't come by for at least 15 minutes. He then forgot to give us menus and proceeded to tell us specials and then asked us, "is there anything else I can get you?" We told him he can give us some menus! It then took over 30 mins to get our appetizers and more than an hour for the food. When I walked through the restaurant on the way to the restroom I noticed many tables who were still waiting for their food. Once we got our order, however, the taste and quality did live up to it's standards. Other waitstaff did also come by to check how the food was, etc, but I was still really disappointed at how different the restaurant felt prior to the merge. Blue Ribbon Sushi was a pretty nice restaurant, with it's own decor and setting, and it's a shame to see it water downed to a side menu at the Brasserie. Last but not least, the busboy clearing the table dropped utensils twice on me and my daughter when clearing the table. Thank goodness one was just a butter knife and not a steak knife! He tried to apologize but was so embarassed just ran away after the second time! I'm not sure if they just got a bunch of new waitstaff, but I was pretty appalled. C'mon Blue Ribbon guys - you gotta work on training - while you're at it, bring back Blue Ribbon Sushi!!

I was recommended this place by a foodie friend in NYC and it did not disappoint. It's a busy place and you will need a reservation. Everyone that worked here was very friendly. The menu has a great selection of courses and a wonderful selection of Italian Red wine. We kept our meal small since we had been eating all day. We started w the meatballs---to die for could have eaten this for a meal perfect to split for two people. We both had pasta dishes---the cappelletti (super rich but yummy) and another mushroom pasta. This place would be perfect for a group of people to try a lot of dishes and share...portions are perfect sized (some might say small but perfect for the dishes served). Our server gave excellent recommendations (wish I could remember her name---sorry we also had a bottle of wine). The prices are far below what I expected based on the quality. Do yourself a favor and check it out.

Good Dominican food, strong sangrias and always great service. Small spot but lively and servers know their stuff. CASH only - which can be annoying because theyre not the cheapest, but still a good time. I wish I would have remembered the very first server's name - she was awesome! Family owned so they care about quality.

This is my ideal type of italian restaurant. Â The service is excellent and they make you feel like you have been going there for years. Â The chef/owner knew at least two of the tables around us and spend a good amount of time sitting with them. Be prepared to ignore the menu completely...the waiter will come over to list at least 30 additional items. Â Both my boyfriend and myself ordered the specials and everything was delicious. Â  I cannot wait to take my family here. Perk: valet parking

Delicious Italian food and great service. They don't make places like this anymore. The decor is nothing fancy but it is what Â makes it charming. Â In this world filled with cookie-cutter restaurant chains, It is so nice to find a place that is truly one of a kind. Â  There is no way this place deserves anything less than a 5.

Totally awesome breakfast/brunch spot. Â If waiting for hours at Clinton St. Bakery isn't your thing, then this is a great alternative. Â (Though the lines here can get long too if you get here too late, so up and at em' in the morning!!) I totally give props to the french toast here. Â Aside from Jane near NYU, this is definitely one of the best french toasts you'll get in the city. Â Add some bacon on the side and you'll have the perfect sweet/savory combination. Â The waffles here were also fantastic. Â And if you have room, might as well throw some blueberry pancakes to the mix because it was also excellent. Â The pancakes were fluffy and very very tasty. Â One time I had to come here with 3 people just so we could all try the different options. Â That's how tasty the food was. The service was hit and miss. Â The hosts were very friendly and did a great job of cleaning up a table quickly to get us seated. Â The waitresses were okay but on multiple occasions they were slow and not very attentive. Â The wait for the food can sometimes be long too. Â But overall that doesn't really detract too much from the breakfast experience, and kudos to the one kind waitress who recommended the french toast. Â It was definitely worth chowing down on. Great, now I'm craving french toast ... :(

Brunch is available, since fall 2011, with prix fixe brunch to come in a few weeks. Spend the $9 for their Lobster Claw Bloody Mary. It's like an appetizer in a glass: tall, spicy, seasoned, cold Bloody Mary garnished with a thick, juicy lobster claw, already peeled. If that isn't enough, it also comes with an olive or two, a pickle, a wedge each of lime and lemon and a tall stalk of celery. Eat the Lobster benedict and savor the memory for the rest of the day. As always, order at the bar and they will bring to your table. Staff are very pleasant and welcoming.

Been meaning to try Noodle Village for a while. Â Finally, after an awesome Yelp event, my 2 friends and I found ourselves at Noodle Village at 10pm. It definitely exceeded my expectations. Â The inside of the restaurant was spacious and clean, the waiter was very kind and courteous, and there were probably 20+ noodles dishes. I like that you can order, thick, thin, egg, or udon. Â  I had the beef stomach with egg noodles. Â It was really good. Â  The meal for 3 people and 4 dishes came out to about 26 bucks before tip. Â  Not bad at all.

My date and I came here for a late dinner before venturing out to play some mind games. It was exciting walking in knowing that this was an establishment co-owned by Jay-Z. Seriously, when you look at Jay-Z and you try to think of food, what do you get? Well, I'll tell you what I didn't get. I didn't expect the pomme frittes to be so cruncy on the outside yet so soft and buttery on the inside. There was so much of it that despite us both attacking the plate from two sides, we couldn't finish it. We ordered a few plates to try and was pleased with all of them. They were exotic and adventurous, but nothing that I would think twice about trying. The decor was dark and romantic. The music wasn't too loud. Despite the busy crowd, the waiters were very attentive. Overall, I left with a happy tummy. What makes this review a 5-star was what happened afterward. So my date and I went to Fat Cat afterward to play chess. We walked there..which is really not that far...but at night it is. After agreeing it was a tie, we decided to leave for the night. I decided to call my friends in the area and met up with them; ditching my now kind of creepy date after a few drinks. Â Only then, did I realize I've lost my wallet but still have my phone. My friends came to my rescue and we decided to look for my wallet. This is now 3am on a Friday night. We walked around aimlessly because my phone has died at this point and with no one sober, direction became a blur. After an hour of wondering, I finally saw the restaurant.. The guys in the restuarant were cleaning up at this point and was startled by me pounding on the glass door. Finally someone came close enough for me to scream I think I may have left my purse in there. He opened and asked me to describe it. He finally lead me upstairs into the employees' secret chamber and gave me my wallet (I promised I wouldn't dish out on this secret chamber). Nothing was taken from it. My cards, cash, everything, still in there. Dear Spotted Pig, I love you for your food, decor, and mostly, I love you for your people. :)

So I'm going to rate this on a tougher scale than usual because the place seems like it's trying to be in a higher league. Food: it was good, but the portions were tiny and very expensive. Â I actually just had the beet salad, which was good (the gorgonzola was delicious!). Â My friends' meals were also tiny... one was surprised to get a raviolo, which we figured must be the singular of ravioli since there was definitely only one thing on her plate. Service: What's up with the pieces of bread being placed on your plate one at a time? Â I don't know if that's supposed to enhance the experience or freshness, but I found it rather intrusive.
