Â Plus, despite the waiter's invitation to "take our time" I felt at each stage of the meal that we were being hurried. Â Maybe we were a bit slow, but they should be perceptive enough not to mistakenly take the bill when we haven't even opened it yet.

These guys know how to throw down when it comes to sandwiches that arent the usual thing you would get at a deli. Theyre only by my office on Mondays unfortunately but I'll take it. So far Ive tried the Moroccan Kofta Brochette which was really tasty with this spicy green sauce, onion, peppers, cilantro, and Ive also had the Merguez sandwich which has lamb sausage with onions onions and peppers. Try them out, theyre nice people too and its only like 6 -7 bucks for lunch.
Best Indian food I've ever had. Honestly. I've tried the chicken tikka masala, the scallop appetizer, the garlic and chili naan, and the lamb shank. Â All were DELICIOUS.

My rating is based on the food and service. This place has been open with the same staff for about 24 years now. And their food hasn't changed. The Ropa Vieja with Black beans and Rice is my favorite! Their Bistec Empanidazo(breaded steak) sandwich is great too!
everything here tastes awesome...my favorite is the kimchi fried rice. its to die for. i would travel from queens just to stock up on this stuff.
Service was very warm and sweet. Â Loved the presentation. Â Food tasty!

one of the VERY BEST cheap eats in NY or Anywhere. But it's also super delicious, forgetting the unbeatable 5/$1 price. The huge cast iron grill creates the best crunch to the pan-fried dumplings. Â Go for the boiled 10/$2 if you want a healthier eat. Scallion Pancakes, focaccia-to-die-for for $0.75 Â a piece. Â Worth the subway ride & a walk to eat here! This is a real place that you go for food. Â For hipster ambiance, go down to Vanessa's..

This review is based on my time there about 5 years ago. Although from what I hear, it hasnt really changed. The seating style is family oriented. You gather around a fire pit and eat. The ramen are just killer, i mean oh my gosh, they are soooooooo good. Upon entering the eating area, all the staff yell out a greating to you as you come in. Its a bit weird because you arent accustomed to it but its fun. We had a small wait about 15 minutes but thats nothing compared to the wait time you will experience during dinner. We entered during the early afternoon. The staff are friendly, the food is awesome. I had the pork belly ramen and meat buns. I was impressed, I had ramen before in other locations and I could care less for it. But this location, it made me a fan of Ramen again.

We ate here two times this weekend.. no kidding.. after the first meal we invited some friends to join us on Sunday night. The food is terrific and the wait staff is attentive. We ate in the garden both times. The inside space is long and arrow and there really is no decor. It is a difficult room Â to make cozy and welcoming. I so wish the owners luck but it would seem that they will need to have a fast turn over and a full room in the colder months when the spacious garden is not available.

I thought this place was a little bit overrated. Service: Great. Very attentive, and everything was fast. They also answered all our questions about the menu without getting annoyed. Decor: Very cool, goes with theme. The drinks menu goes with the theme as well. Food: Decent-sized portions. The meal I got was okay. I got some sort of sandwich (can't remember exactly what) and fries. Good Lord, these were literally the saltiest french fries I can ever remember having in my life. They were salty to the point that I had to stop eating them because I genuinely felt nauseous. This never happens to me. I barely ever complain about food. If I don't like it, I generally comment "Meh". I will say, in retrospect, this may have been a mistake and I probably should have asked the waiter for a different set of fries, that weren't so darn salty. But hindsight is 20/20. The drinks were okay--but extremely expensive. Probably won't go back, just because it is really very pricy. If you've got some extra cash to burn and love Shakespeare, maybe try it!
great food, very affordable, cool vibe at night
Loved every minute of this dining experience, from the impeccable service to the delicious food. Â  My favorite dishes: Fish tacos, Cod and Calamari.
Best grilled fish

Lobster Shepherd's Pie: A (heavenly delicious with the mashed potato on top) Fisherman's Stew: B (extremely salty but the ingredients are fresh and edible) Scallop Salad: A (seared to perfection) Grilled Calamari: B+ (the calamari was good but a bit too charred and they OD'ed with seasoning in the sauce) Fried Oysters: B+ (delectable but not sure how I feel about the seaweed on top of the oysters...) Service: A: water refills were constant, nice! B: certain utensils were missing for our meal, wth? C: the clam chowder took forever to get to the table, as in we-almost-got-the-bill-and-was-ready-to-leave-Â­forever, wtf? Maybe I'll like Fish more the second time around. In the words of the Terminator, "I'll be back."

Came here on a Thursday for dinner with 2 friends. It was pretty empty but still felt cozy. We were seated quickly and our waitress was really great, giving us lots of good recommendations (mac & cheese and kale salad were amazing). The drinks we got were about half and half - I didn't love the bartender's Old Fashioned but his Manhattan was excellent. One star off for the lack of vegetarian entrees. To be clear, their appetizers and sides had lots of options and were delicious, but if you're doing a farm to table concept you need to have more than one option that's on par with your meat dishes (no, mac & cheese doesn't count). Otherwise really great!

As a self-proclaimed fried chicken connoisseur, I was dying to try Blue Ribbon. When the time finally came, I was uber excited. Since we didn't foresee this event, we were dressed in raggedy-Soho-shopping-ready clothes. Luckily, the wait staff was beyond friendly and did not make us feel out of place at all even in shorts and tanks. The food was definitely out of this world good. We shared the Beef Marrow & Oxtail Marmalade for the appetizer then the fried chicken as our main. The bone marrow was good and went really well with the oxtail marmalade. The fried chicken was also finger-lickin'-good, but I didn't think it was the best I've ever had. I also thought both dishes were quite pricey for what they were, but I suppose you're also paying for the ambiance and service so s'all good. Overall, the service was fantastic and the food was great. I'd definitely come back and can't wait to try other Blue Ribbon restaurants!
Rating is for their mojito only. Â Verdict: Delicious (and better than Esperanto).

I square this pizza will change your life! Seriously though, they're the BEST! When I'm on my death bed, this will be one of the last 3 meals I'd want to eat (c'mon did you really expect a foodie to just have 1 last meal?). Uh huh it's THAT good. Do yourself a favor and just order a half tray since you can get 12 slices for $19. If you have left overs, the pizza taste almost just as good the next day heated up. Win win situation.

Great music. Fantastic food and you definitely cannot beat the prices!!! The music is also very well selected. The only issue I had was the staff being inconsistent and speaking spanish when they wanted to talk about guests coming in. I think its very rude. Other than that, highly recommended.

I got the spicy ramen with chicken, and it just tasted okay. The broth was savory, but the flavors weren't phenomenal and were pretty flat. I came with a group for an early dinner, and even though the place wasn't that full, the waiter didn't bring me a menu, water, silverware, or napkins. I had to ask for each individually, and each time it took a long time for me to be serviced. Not a pleasant experience, unfortunately. I'm not also not a huge fan of ramen in general, so I can see how some people would love it.

I really wish I could give this place a better review but my overall experience was ruined by the super loud I can't hear anything but your music experience...:(. I ate there, the food was good and the drinks were good also but the whole experience was dampen by the blasting loud horrible music. I go to raves and listen to loud music but this was extreme.

I tried Hummus & Pita Co. again and have to give it a higher rating. Â And no, I didn't go the free lunch offered by Dave (owner/manager?). I had mentioned in my initial review the food itself is good, but my main complaint was the layout. Â They changed the layout since the first time I went, and it's definitely better than when they first opened. Â The fill-its and toppings are separated, and it's not nearly as confusing as it used to be. Â The staff was also really patient and walked customers through the ordering process. As for the food: - Falafel was good, still fried but moist. Â Preferred it to the shwarma. - Get the Spanish eggplant, a really tasty Fill It - Grape leaves were pretty good, but a little sour

I'm so glad to have found a hip and good colombian restaurant. The food was really good, the plantain chips with aji is great... a little bit crowded but that's what you'd expect at any restaurant on a friday night. Overall, I really liked the ambiance, the service and food. I recommend the Colombian grilled Trout platter. My husband had the bistec encebollado with yellow rice and red beans and the cilantro mashed potatoes (which is green and not that great).

'Overpriced' is not a word I apply lightly, particularly with regard to sustenance. I espouse chewy commodities with 400% margin, like coffee and cocktails. Upscale Italian food. Tapas. Fro-yo. Â  But Williamsburg's a treasure trove of artsy cheap eats - and Rye's Manhattan prices (~$25 entrees; ~$12 cocktails) and understated elegance seem audaciously inappropriate when set so near the same, barbed-wired, broken-glasses south stretches of Havemeyer and Driggs that houses Pies 'n Thighs. Furthermore, the food is, well, food. Chicken. Fish. Salads. Calamari. The meat medley meatloaf sandwich was notably large and in charge, and more than stomachable at $14. The same dessert parade that weaves through Midtown power lunch palaces - pot de creme, creme brulee, chocolate cake, fruit tart. I will tip my hat to the barkeep - I sampled three on point cocktails - but I'll be saving my bills, moving forward, for something a little more interesting.

I was so suprised by how big this place is inside! Great for meeting a large group of friends. Prices were reasonable, food was good, and there were a few more choices on the menu than most standard Thai joints. Will def return

This place is amazing! I live literally 2 min walk away from this place and always wanted to try it out but would end up in the city instead for dinner. Finally tried this place out. My boyfriend and I went around 8 for dinner and we were seated right away. The place is very small so seating is a bit tight. I did feel I would be a little close to the people next to me but it doesn't bother me too much because people really don't care. We were sitting outside since the weather is still nice enough for that. We were offered either sparkling water, sealed water, or regular water and their water was in a glass jar which I love. The menu was small enough that I didn't spend ages deciding on what to get. They have all their alcoholic drinks and specials written on the wall which I think was pretty cool. Bread and olive oil and balsamic vinaigrette was given to us. First we order the veal meatballs and fried calamari as appetizers. They came out really fast which I didn't even expect. I always try to stay away from veal but these meatballs were so good! They were so tender and the fried calamari was amazing. I love fried calamari but a lot of places would over cook them which ends up being a little tough even when they were crispy. For entrees, I ordered the cavatelli broccolino and my boyfriend ordered the branzino al forno. The dishes were a nice size portion, not overly huge like a lot of italian restaurants. I loved my boyfriend's dish because the lemon sauce was just perfect. It went very well with the fish without overdoing it. The cavatelli was delicious. The sausage to pasta proportion was perfect so that I wouldn't be fishing around for more sausage or having too much sausage and don't know where the pasta went. We will definitely return to this place for dinner and brunch because I do see that this place is always packed for brunch too.

This restaurant is absolutely wonderful... The food is original, fresh and delicious . There are many vegetarian, gluten free Â and vegan options. The smoothies and juices all look amazing. The chick pea fries are a "must". Today i had the kale salad and my daughter had the spelt pancakes. Next time i want the chick pea burger . We will definitely be coming back!

I love pizza, especially in NYC. Â California just doesn't compare (although a few places are close). I came here for a family dinner and immediately loved the scent of fresh pizza in the air. Â We ordered a plain pizza, a pepperoni pizza, and one with truffles (in the form of truffle oil I think). They were scrumptious. Not only were the pies bubbling hot when served, but the crust had that distinctive "crunch" when you bite into it. Â The sauce was flavorful and robust, the mozerella cheese nice and soft. I'm torn between this place and Lombardi's as being my favorite in NYC.

I fell in absolute love with Jimmy's after my very first bite of deep fried deviled egg. Since that fateful day it has become my favorite diner in the 5 boroughs. I'd like to think that statement carries some weight, as I hail from NJ. Literally everything I've ingested at Jimmy's in my several dozen visits has been uber-yummy. I have never received a plate of food that wasn't done as well as it was the last time I had it. Anything fried here is stand-out good, notably the eggs, chicken, homemade tater tots, etc. They do a KILLER burger, and a hella good milkshake - get the key lime pie flavor, with bits of graham cracker crust in the shake. Your stomach will thank you, even if your heart doesn't.

I went here last night and I was so upset. I am not a picky person but this waitress was so rude. She was so rude to us it was just so awkward and really killed the atmosphere for us. The food wasn't bad but it definitely was not good! I still can't believe how rude and awful the waitress was. I will never go back in here and this restaurant does NOT deserve anyone's business.
Overhyped Food is good but service blows Always feel rushed when I come here
Not impressed. We got the chicken Marsala. It was blahhhh Would not recommend. Pick another spot.

In a neighborhood where there aren't a bunch of new and exciting restaurants, East Wick has set up shop in between East Williamsburg and Bushwick in Brooklyn.Â The restaurant itself is simply designed, but filled with grand, custom-made wooden benches by a local artist. And since it's located on the corner, during the day, the natural light cheerfully floods in from the wrap-around windows.Â  I visited for brunch, and at a more than affordable $14, you get your entree, coffee or tea, and a brunch cocktail. I ordered their Green Omelette (spinach, chives, feta cheese,Â with roasted potatoes, market greens). The food was delicious. The greens were perfectly dressed with a wonderfully sweet vinaigrette, and the potatoes had a nice crispness to the skin and tender on the inside. The omelette was generous in size and the ingredients were liberally filled inside the eggs, making this a healthy and substantial meal.

What a cute little cafe! I used to live in the area and had never made it here somehow. I didn't get to try the food, but everything coming out of the mostly-open kitchen looked delicious and the people at the tables around us looked quite pleased. The space is much bigger than you'd anticipate and the back garden is oh-so relaxing. The servers are all very young, but they are friendly and efficient. We needed to move tables to accomodate a large party and the manager was very nice, sat us elsewhere right away, and offered us a free drink. I will be returning!
I've been here twice and both time it was excellent really nice service staff.
Delicious and tasty food!! clean, diligent and friendly. That food is made with love at least that how I feel. The restaurant dÃ©cor is like an art gallery, they display wall paintings for sale.
Great place, very nice and relaxing atmosphere! Good and delicious, fool of flavor and enjoyable food! Â Love it

We went there on a Saturday night for a friend's birthday dinner and drinks.The place is small and quaint, with bright dark orangish red walls, and VERY FLAVORFUL food. Their margaritas list is really good. We tried the Tamarindo, Pepino and the classic and I loved all 3 of them. The bartender is also friendly enough to have concocted the recipes to our personal tastes - less/more sweet, less/more sour! We had their grilled cheese with chorizo, watermelon salad, guacamole, and a black bean appetizer and they were all out of this world. These weer served with teensy fresh corn tortillas - which were made to perfection. For our entrees, we had the Camarones Adobodas (essentially seasoned grilled charred shrimps on green flavored rice,) (my favorite), chicken nortena (again spicy and delicious), baked grouper - and we had absolutely no complaints ! All very well cooked and absolutely delicious. Desserts: tres leches cake, banana pudding (my favorite), and citter sweet chocolate pudding with walnut crunch - its a crime to make desserts that good :-); Needless to say, all this food was shared amongst 4 people - you know we were all overloaded with delicious food, good drinks, and very friendly staff. Will go back there again :).

I never "yelped" Â before, if that is the correct term to use. But I was completely blown away with the decor and the atmosphere. The restaurant is completely beautiful ! With it's amazing high ceilings. The food was okay, a little mediocre for such a beautiful restaurant, I honestly was expecting better quality in food... But our server Jamie was completely amazing, very tentative and very quick to accommodate us. The music in the restaurant was extremely loud.... And there was so many people when we walked in it was almost impossible to walk thru the crowd. Besides this, I'll be back to grab a beer some time.

I've often walked by this cute cafe when I was living on 9th Ave. and only made it in this past month. I have to say, I wasn't disappointed. I always enjoy a good crepe and it was nice to be sitting enjoying some wine while your crepe was being prepared close by. My friends frequent the place for tasty savory crepes- I did enjoy my crepe du jour of vegetables and cheese. I hear the creme brulee is also super tasty. For a quaint, laidback brunch/lunch, this is a good place to go if you're in the area. It is a little crowded but when we were there (it was earlier in the evening on a Sunday) it wasn't too terrible.

After listening to the story of why is called La Pulperia we even love this place more. We had lunch on wdnesday and it was an amazing experience, despite been seated near to 4 old crampy ladies complaining that they had to get on time to the theater so they could get something free!!! Our server "G" was very attentive and kept a smile all the time despite the hard time this 4 ladies were trying to give him, why people go to restaurants with attitude?? We ordered El Chilango by our server recomendation and it was just amazing!!! I don't drink cocktails ever and I have to say I felt in love with it!! The lobster taquitos were amazing, the music the lighting and again the personal and caring service that "G" gave us put this place in our number 1. Choice for our future visita to NY. I wish we have places like that in NC!! We will definetly come back!!

I've gotten Luzzo's take out before, and knew I was in for a treat at this place. Â They still don't have a liquor license, so they just gave out a glass of wine to everyone on the house. Â They had two reds and one white to pick from, which was very nice. Â The bread we started off with was delish - like pizza dough bread... yum! Â I ordered the bruschetta - bread was delish, and lots of tomato. Â I also got the small bufalo pizza which was just incredible. Â The sauce was amazing - had a bit of tang to it! Â The Luzzo's take out that I had isn't quite as good as this place (not sure if I eat there it would be the same). Â Also the portion was pretty large for a small - served on a cutting board too. Â The large was only two bucks more and was HUGE... I should have gotten that and eaten it for lunch the next day. Â The service was great, the food was awesome... I'd definitely recommend and return! Â It was pretty busy for a random Tuesday night, so I'd definitely make reservations.

I had hoped that the high reviews would mean that the chances of it being a negative experience would be unlikely. Â We arrived on Sunday right as it opened and made sure we were behind the other groups that arrived ahead of us. Â When it was our turn, my husband said, "Two please." Â The response, "We say good morning here first." Â We sat down and I said to my husband, "I hope the food is better than the attitude." Â The server came over and took our order. Â My husband asked for a coffee Americano. Â The server up sold him to the French press coffee for two, which was gross and full of coffee grounds. Â The server convinced me to get the fresh squeezed orange juice. Â I specifically asked if it was actually fresh squeezed. Â He said "oh yes, it is." Â Then I see them pour orange juice out of a Tropicana bottle (the same one I happen to have in my fridge.) Â The didn't even fill the glass and even put ice in the it, so I felt duped. Â I ordered a crepe and my husband got an omelet. Â It was very underwhelming. Â I would opt for Le Barricou over this place for sure. Â We will not be returning here again.

The sign said, "best cheesesteak in nyc," so we stopped. Two wit whiz, fries (free, courtesy of yelp), and a soda. Water- on the house. Really fantastic. Bread is soft and fresh. The stuff inside was everything I hope for in life. It just might be the best cheeseteak in nyc.

I don't know what kind of people gave this place low ratings because Petite Crevette is shockingly ah-MAAAA-zing. Seriously. I am not often impressed with seafood restaurants in NYC so stumbling upon this spot in Brooklyn was such a pleasant surprise. EVERYTHING IS SO FREAKING DELICIOUS!!!! I had the crab corn chowder, fried oysters and salmon burger and my friend had the lobster with shrimp, mussels and scallops. We even got a free glass of wine and dessert with dinner (we made nice with the bartender and our server). I can't wait to come back!

As a working Chef (trained in Italy). I was not too impressed by the Pizza there. For all I know it could have been an off night. So I'll give it another try later on in the year. One point I have to bring up here. The old fellow called Patsy really, really made a pest of himself tonight. For one he was way too chatty cathy for our taste and forced us to have espressos that we didn't want. My advise is this: He should take some pointers from our / his beaded server that was Highly professional and Very discreet. Come to think of it why is that kind of server working there?. Either way give it a try!
delicious !!! eveything I order off the menu was delectable !!! from the Fried chicken box with Mac & Chesse to the pecan pie I had for dessert !

I LOVE this place. Except for the wait times on the weekends for brunch. But that's because the brunch is so damn good and so many people want to try it! It's $15 for a meal, coffee and juice etc. It's so affordable and so tasty. I'm pretty sure they have a $25 deal with brunch as well that includes Bloody Marys etc. I can not recommend the place enough. Our eggs were not poached to perfection (or rather they were over-poached), we were fine and didn't even complain, but the amazing hostess came by and said she'd make us all a new batch (there was 8 of us) and she did so promptly and they were perfect! I havent been to W'burg location for dinner yet, but I'm sure it is just as brilliant as the weekend brunch!

My go-to restaurant in Park Slope. Great during the summer as you can go outside on the patio. Prices are very reasonable, portions are big and the food is always good. I particularly like their curries and the salmon special with vegetables that they sometimes offer.

Best southern food I've had since I moved to NYC. I ordered the fried chicken box and it was some off the best chicken I've ever had. The breading was crispy and delicious and the inside was moist and amazing. The biscuit that came with it was great and the gravy I got as my side perfectly complemented the biscuit.

It's four stars because I love nostalgic places, it helps me to get away from this busy modern bustling NYC and realize that this city has sweet old charms. Â  Great cocktails at your quality average $15 price tag. Three stars for the food. Â I would only come back for the Black Label Burger. Â Fries were also good, crispy and crunchy! Â  Bone Marrow was meh-ok. Â I had better elsewhere. Â Cote de Boeuf was ok. Â I don't think it was worth the price tag. Â The carrot was drenched in butter. Â Thank goodness salad was just drizzle with dressing. Dessert - souffle was meh. Â It was a bit overcooked. Seating - If I was closer to the front, I may had been bothered by the crowd that was standing by the bar (either drinking or waiting for a table). Â Good thing, I had a corner booth, so no one was towering over me. Â Perhaps it is nicer in the back room away from the bar area?

Having gone to culinary school in Switzerland, I ate my way through Germany, Switzerland and Austria. Cafe Katja is serving better food than many of the meals I experienced while living there. The liter beers were ice cold, the sausage and sauerkraut perfect and the dutch white asparagus were the best asparagus I've ever tasted. They must have been half an inch around and extremely juicy and flavorful. Dining here brought back many memories of Europe and recreated dining experiences I am most fond of. Will return soon!

Came to Freemans on a Saturday night with a party of 8 - we were late by half an hour but they were nice enough to hold our table for us, despite how packed the place was. Freemans was super quaint and classy - very rustic as well - with large distressed wood tables, mismatched wooden chairs and an assortment of stuffed game covering all inches of wall. It became pretty obvious after awhile that the owner had a special affinity (or fervent hatred) for birds, since anyone could have easily mistaken the bar for an aviary. Service was friendly, though food came pretty slowly - it took them close to 30 minutes to come out with the artichoke dip for the table. Food was pretty good, but nothing too special. I got the seared sea scallops and I tried my friend's pork loin, both were solid, just not amazing. The wine selection was decent (are you sensing a 3-star pattern yet?) yet we still ordered 4 bottles. I probably won't come back here (maybe I'll give brunch a shot), but if you do, make sure you know how to find the place before you venture out into the cold - in between Bowery and Christie you'll find a slightly renegade alleyway called Freeman's alley, just follow the alley into the net of Christmas lights and you'll have stumbled upon the right place.

Great BBQ in Brooklyn,....THe DInosaur name did not disappoint. Â We were all very happy with our food. Â Great sides, great Ribs and Chicken. Â Spacious place with a great vibe! We will def be back soon, I hope

Not sure how to review this exactly. The wait wasn't too bad at 10pm on a Thursday. My friend and I hung at the bar while we waited for a third, ordered a few drinks and a round of the pork belly buns. The bartender ended up giving us a second round for free because no one claimed them. That was fabulous, but already was feeling full. The buns were great but momofuku's are slightly better (sorry!). When we were seated we ordered the classic and modern ramen and more buns. The ramen was definitely good, almost too modern/clean tasting for my liking. But honestly, as good as the food was, $20/bowl is NOT worth it. It's just not. You can make pretty great ramen at home for $1 with an egg and some siracha. So I'm a little torn. I think it's a rip off that could only happen in NY, maybe LA, but the food was so good, it's hard to complain too much!

I've been there a shamefully high number of times over the years and I am pleasantly surprised that the quality of the food has remained impeccably high. Ever the minimalist, I keep it ultra simple and get a plain "old fashioned" and it is DIVINE. The crust is chewy and flavorful (a little yeasty in a good way), sauce (made of San Marzano tomatoes if memory serves me correctly) is savory yet a little sweet and cheese is the perfect, mild accompaniment to the perfect slice of pizza. Just like my nonexistent Nonna would make ;-)

Lovely place for lunch. Â I had the fish sandwhich and it was delish. Â The portion was great , great combo on flavors with a nice little salad. Â They had some local brews and the hamburger, which I got a bite of, was well off the chain. Â Check it out for sure. Â I got a coffee to go and it did the trick. Â Prices are reasonable, staff is nice, can't miss. Â IN a nice part of Brooklyn right near the library and fun places to walk

HANDSSSSS DOWNNNNNN one of the favs!!! they have the best sangria known to man!!!!! the rotisserie chicken is something from another world!! the price points are good & their sauces are amazing!!! **** ATTENTION SINGLE DUDES IF YOU WANT TO TAKE A GIRL OUT TO A NICE 1ST DATE & MAKE SURE YOU GUYS HAVE A GREAT MEAL & GET A GREAT BUZZZZZZZ THIS IS THE PLACE!!! YOU CAN LITERALLY BE STUFFED & SILLY BUZZED FOR 60$ NO JOKE!! orrrrrrr if you want to do a bday Â or family style dinner this is a great place ti feed a lot of ppl with a nice atmosphere & affordably. one of the best places... anyone that doesnt love this place to me is a hater! there is nothing not to love! been going since i was a kid to the 1st location on northern blvd & watched these guys grow!! the food is amazing & theres nothing else that can be said otherwise to me.. amazing!!!!!

Was intrigued by all the hype and people saying it's "the best they've ever had." I've been to so many taco joints over the years that it would be hard to recall which is the very best, but that said, just off the top of my head I can safely propel Los Tacos into my top two or three. Easily. The absolute key here is the homemade corn tortillas. You get a choice between flour or corn, both of which are amazing, but I stick to corn. Before you even take a bite, as you lift the taco to your mouth you can smell the freshness of the corn in the tortilla. Amazing. Pork, chicken and cactus tacos were all fantastic. Pork was my fav, ever so slightly better than the others. It's nice that you can see the person making your taco and can tell him/her exactly what you want and don't want in it. Los Tacos lives up to the hype!
Cute, cozy and quiet atmosphere. Had duck breast, burger, and bass. Highly recommend the duck breast. It was juicy and flavorful.

I had one of the best meals of my life here. We had the scallops with black pudding, soda bread, and the beef wellington. everything was seasoned and cooked perfectly. We also ordered whisky/scotch flights and the waiter was very knowledgeable in helping make our decision. He was attentive without being pushy and the atmosphere is very romantic.

Bomb Diggity!!!! I've been a fan for years, and I'm so glad they finally got the press that they deserve. But now I have to wait longer for my chicken platter, but it's damn worth it. By a million miles, this is the best mobile vendor in NYC period.

I came here on a freezing cold day for lunch. It's a hike to get to 10th avenue, since there aren't any subway lines riding that far east. But walked in this cute red theme restaurant. The tables have this warm cozy place, with red plates. Remind me having a picnic with plastic red plates. On the bar, they had red radishes. Sat towards the back, we had restaurant week menu. And a bottle of wine for 24.07. Everything was good, very simple, great flavors. The frisses with bacon and sunny side egg. Creamy salad dressing and delicious. My friend had the celery root, hmm! And the Entrees, good portion of mussels with a thai cocunut sauce. Hmm the fries could of been more crispy. The only neg thing was the dessert, it didn't lead up to the other food. Cookies and milk, hmm reminds you of home. But the chocolate chip cookie was hard and not fresh. Taste like store bought not house made. Otherwise cute atmosphere, love the bar area. Great service.
jon, buy your own wifi you douchebag. it's a cafe, not a library. and cafes in nyc aren't required to have bathrooms if they are under a certain amount of seating.

I am not what you would call a ramen connoisseur but I do love an occasional bowl of steaming shoyu ramen or tonkotsu ramen. This place is as close to the real thing as you can get without boarding the next ANA flight to Tokyo. A small, simple place that packs a big punch. The standard shoyu ramen with pork is just to-die-for. The pork melts in your mouth and the noodles are cooked to perfection. Can't wait for winter to roll around again so I can go here and steam up my face with a hot bowl of ramen!

Have you ever been promised something, felt the anticipation build, but was sorely let down? Well, that's my fairytale with the Halal Cart. So many people have posted pictures and proclaimed their undying love for the chicken and rice dish from the famous 53rd St. & 6th Ave. cart that I HAD to put this onto our 'Must Eat' list. One brisk Thursday evening as we strolled along Fifth Ave., I suggested to the fella that we try the Halal Cart for dinner. Just like Grimaldi's, we had arrived just before the dinner rush came. After a short wait, I cheerfully greeted the employees and ordered two chicken and rice dishes. While I was paying, the fella was grabbing a couple of the pre-packaged white sauces and hot sauce to take to along with our dishes. Just as he grabbed the white sauces, one of the employees rudely yelled, "I give you sauce!" Now fully aware that we'll be given sauce, the fella put the tiny containers away. (The gentleman not only scolded us for taking the pre-packaged white sauces, but continued to scold others after us!) Minutes later, we got our dishes and walked off to a nearby spot to sit and chow down. I opened the container and...NO WHITE SAUCE. All I saw was the pita bread, rice, and chicken. LIES. Slightly peeved that we got scolded for no reason, I walked back to the cart, and kindly showed the men that we apparently did NOT get any of the white sauce we were told we'd receive. A different employee kindly nodded his head in approval for us to grab the sauces (1 container/each). Jeez! Anyways, we walk back to our spot to finally try this "amazing" dish. I took a couple spoonfuls to the mouth before I looked at the fella and said, "This is it?" It literally was just minced chicken and thin-grained rice to me. Which is perfectly fine, but definitely not up to par with its hype. Â The white sauce definitely did make things creamier and tastier, but I shouldn't have to conceal my whole dish with the sauce, right? Even if I wanted to, I apparently couldn't! Maybe if the food could redeem this cart of the disrespectful attitude that we came across, I would be more forgiving on the rating. Unfortunately, it can't be done.
YUM! Sucked down my two tacos like I'd never seen a taco before in my life. I had a steak taco on flour and a pork taco on corn. Pile on the pico de gallo and go to town.

Amazing taco truck that delivers, in Sunset Park, the home of the authentic taco. I always get two chicken and a spicy pork, and they come with grilled spring onions and fresh, homemade hot sauces. No heavy melted cheese or sour cream, just simple, fresh, real mexican (onions, cilantro).
The best restaurant I've ever been to. All the staff are really friendly. Food was good. Service was excellent. Will definately be coming back here.
I had a great experience here...service was good and the food was delicious. Â It was a loud and crowded atmosphere, so it's not the place to go if you're looking for a quiet dinner.
Food is pretty good with a big drink selection. It is a little awkward at night with a big bar crowd.

I'm not even a huge cajun/creole fan, but I love this place! Â Great ambiance and good food. Â If you're waiting for a party, sit at the bar, they have hurricanes to go with their Nawlin's food. Â The bartenders are heavy-handed, so be careful! Â  :)
Food is good but the cheesecake is out of this world.
what can i say when you want a quick bite, this place is awesome. i personally only like the buffet line, but ill still get the prepackaged stuff. quick, cheap, and easy
1 hour and 45 min wait is what the matra d told me

I had the pleasure of dining at David Bouley on 9/1/14 or at least I thought it would be a pleasurable experience. On arrival my wife and I were greeted and were told that our table was almost ready. So we took a seat close to the door, and when the pompous maÃ®tre 'd appeared, he looked at us, and then looked over his seating chart. He Â had a young lady seat us rather than do it himself as he had just seated the customer before us. After passing by many available tables upstairs, I noticed that we were heading to the back of the restaurant and down the stairs to a small dining room that was nicely appointed; however, little did we know but we had just been relegated to the "David Bouley Dungeon for Tourists." Â As one who has dined all over the world, I started to say something, but bit tongue and looked forward to a great wine and food experience. From here we went down hill. I asked for the wine list and with the help of the sommelier,we chose a half bottle of a small grower champagne and a half bottle of an 09 Burgundy. Interestingly, both bottles were retrieved by the sommelier and shown to me while he held them in one hand. The champagne was immediately tasted and served and the Burgundy was tasted. While toasting our champagne the sommelier started pouring the Burgundy which startled me; however, I chose to keep quiet and wait on the food. (By pouring both wines either the sommelier was either trying to sell me more wines or he just did not want to come back to the dungeon again to serve the Burg. To my chagrin, it was both.) So now we settle in for the great dinner. It was anything but that. We chose not to have the tasting menu and ordered a la carte from the menu. We both chose the wild mushrooms with Toro. Both appetizers were barely warm at best and my wife's Toro was fishy. Again we still had faith but told the waiter about the Toro. When the waiter tried to tell us that the Toro tasted that way, I could not hold my tongue any longer, and let the waiter know that I had eaten Toro many times in Japan and stateside, and if fresh, it does not taste fishy. He later came back and said it was because of the marinade--I just shook my head at his comment. Next my wife had the salmon, and I had the duck prepared as Chef saw best. To say the least when I took my first bite, the dish was barely warm again. At that point I confronted the waiter, that I thought David Bouley was suppose Â to be a great restaurant, and that Â it was obvious to me that the Chef was not even at the restaurant. The duck was quickly removed, and I was asked if I would like another dish. I was reluctant, but agreed to the striped bass which was prepared perfectly and was served nice and hot. By the time my dish was served, my wife's salmon was cold and now needed to be warmed. It did however come back quickly. (On a good note, I was not charged for the duck or bass; however, to get something free at DB was not my intention, I came to have a great dining experience.) Â To make up for all the issues, we were plied with deserts. Thanks but no thanks--I do not need all the sugar and my wife did not care for desert that night. So that was our night at David Bouley which I will never set foot in again as I consider it not a good restaurant. However, on the whole, the service was good but you cannot eat the service. The sommelier obviously was over serving the wine and certainly did not want to return to the dungeon. Per the food, well my review speaks for that abomination. The maÃ®tre d' at the front of the house is pompous and appears to only greet and seat those he knows; however, on leaving, I thought I was his best friend--I just turned around and gave him "the look." Also, I never once saw him show his face in the dungeon. Lastly, if you are from out of town, insure you are Â not seated in the dungeon where I believe you are not treated as the patrons upstairs. New York has too many great restaurants to chance getting a mediocre food Â and wine experience as we had at David Bouley. Â  Bill Nunnelly

We came here for our anniversary. Â We had the duck, which was over salted. Â  Unfortunately, the food was not the issue, but rather the service was awful. The waiter asked us if we wanted dessert and listed our options, instead of taking our order he took the liberty to pick the dessert for us. Â We did not appreciate his choices. Â  For better food and service, try AL DI LA, instead.

LadurÃ©e is one of my bookmarks in NYC that I have been meaning to get to during my last few visits to the Big Apple. However, during those previous visits, I kept prioritizing LadurÃ©e lower than other places because it seems a very French place to visit and I needed to get my NYC-specific places out of the way first before indulging in the wonder and glory that is LadurÃ©e. If you have never heard of LadurÃ©e, all you need to know is they make a famous macaron. (I keep wanting to type "macaroon" and my auto-correct keeps insisting I am typing "macaroni". Language! Funny!) There is currently only one LadurÃ©e location in the states and it is on Madison Ave. They are opening a Soho location soon, which will eventually be a full restaurant. Macaron Salads? Macaron Fries? Who knows? The point is that (for right now), they make one thing very, very well: the macaron. Here are the reasons I am qualified to judge a good French macaron: 1. I eat something sweet after every meal. 2. Once my French teacher, Madame Castenson, in High School said that my haircut made me look French. 3. I have seen the movie Sabrina approximately 6 million times. 4. I have a miniature replica of the Eiffel Tower on my desk at home. You may not think that those reasons are valid, but I assure you, they are. When you walk in, you can clearly see there are no tables and chairs. You must dÃ©part (translation: dÃ©part is "depart" in French) with your macarons and be happy about it. They fly the macarons in every week from Paris in these perfectly macaron-sized plastic containers. At $2.80 each, you could fly to Paris and eat them for the same price. Wait, that doesn't make sense. You could fly to Paris and have a comparable experience, but it would cost you more. That math works. One notable thing: the staff MAY have fake French accents, which I find hilarious. When I was ordering, I got "oh oui, zee choco-lah un" as a response... and then, they started talking to each other about blue skirts and the accent disappeared. I hope it is part of their training. Fake French Accents 101 for Employees. Hysterical. In the store, I was immediately in a blissful place. Tickled by the possibly-fake French accents and surrounded by sugar is a good experience for me. But MAN, there were some nasty people around. I mean REALLY snotty customers. One female customer's nastiness (read this in your wickedest and most loud Wicked Witch of the East voice): "You don't have the ribbon with the buildings on it?!? Then, how will the box be decorative!?!?" Undeterred by the disagreeable customers, I chose six different macarons. Don't judge. You try and do it, tough guy/girl. Just try and chose under six from their list. Anyway, I chose awesomely. How do I know I passed this test? Because I ate them and they were fantastic. Obviously. My flavor selections: Caramel with Salted Butter, Vanilla, Chocolate from Columbia, Gingerbread, Coconut, and Coffee. Just phenomenal. The macarons are light with no air bubbles. They aren't too big or too small. They are just right with the perfect amount of filling. Whether you go to Paris or head over to Madison Ave in NYC, you won't regret purchasing these little treats. I recommend a minimum of six. Quantity and quality. Bon Appetit!

Went there for brunch. Food is good, and service is also good. The ambiance however is main draw which makes for a unique and memorable experience. The building is a restored tenement house with lots of charm.

Wow, this place is a tiny, crammed, wacky mess...and I love it. Â Plastic pig lights strung across the wall, cheap old posters of veggies, the world's tiniest bar and the world's most overworked bartender, itty bitty tables so close to your neighbor that you could eat off your plate, and about an hour's wait even on a weekday evening. Â And yet I still loved it. Â The ambiance was effortlessly hip (as opposed to trying-too-hard hip), and the food was delicious. Chicken liver toast as an appetizer was yummy and a hearty portion (two slices per serving). Â The nightingale cocktail was divine. Â Five stars for the sheep's milk ricotta gnudi -- which are basically little round, plump raviolis -- and the divine butter sauce they serve those sitting in, omg. Â An excellent dish to share if everyone at the table wants just a bite or two, which is more than enough given how rich they are (portion size is seven per plate). The burger was good (NOT the best everrrr, but really good -- juicy meat, buttery bun, oozing melted blue cheese). Â I wonder what it would have tasted like without the blue (Roquefort) cheese...because it's an unusual cheese to put on a burger, and I wonder if some of the hype is just simply due to the novelty of that taste on a burger. Â However, the meat patty itself definitely was very juicy and the bun was perfect, so I'll give the burger as a whole the benefit of the doubt. Â The super skinny rosemary fries really made that burger dish sing. Â I'd suggest ordering a side of the fries no matter what you get (as the table of four girls next to us did). Service was great -- unpretentious but polite, and appropriately attentive. Â The hostess was particularly jolly, which kept me entertained while sitting at the bar waiting for a table. Â (The bartender was not so jolly, but she was so darn overworked that I'll let it slide.) Not a five-star experience, mostly because it's a little overpriced for what you get, but a solid four stars. Â Try to go on off-hours (if there are any), or come prepared to wait a while.
Try their pecan pie bars. You will thank me. Good coffee.
This is the second time I have had brunch here. Service was pleasant and the food was very good.

verlaine deserves 5 stars simply for the unfailing awesomeness of their 4-10pm, every single day of the damned week happy hour. can you really beat a 5 buck lychee martini? they are strong, they are almost cosmically tasty. the bar snacks are also yummy; even the humble peapod makes an amazing appetite-whetter. this place does get stupid-mobbed on the weekends (i dont bother ever going then), but on a tuesday after work it is a fairly unbeatable budget destination.

Its better than a-ok cause the $5 lychee martini till 10pm is suuucchhhh a sweet deal, especially since its well made and im not a lightweight plus its a good atmosphere and crowd, but i wouldnt exactly give it a 4 cause the food fell short of fulfilling. wish there was a 3.5 option, grrr. Will just give it a 4 cause food aside, its def a solid happy hour choice. Foreword: Im a lush! anyhow, so last week friday had to meet up with a girlfriend to catch up, have a drink, have a bite, and have a nice atmosphere and crowd on a tight budget. Friend was very hungry. I had a long week and needed to unwind with libations, im usually wine and champagne, but anything in a stem glass is ok with me and she said if she drinks today shes in the mood for hard liqs so cocktails it is. So spent a half hour post-work yelping aggressively to finally decide upon Verlaines: Happy hour till 10, lots of hype for the $5 lychee martini, serves food, mixed crowd in a little lower east side lounge style spot and im already downtown. Seems to fit the checklist perfectly. We arrived 4:48, place was super empty and we were "kindly" asked to leave until they open at 5 sharp. Take a look at a laughable thrift store across the street and a peek at the steven shoe store up the block, return to Verlaines at 5:09 only to find the place almost crowded! geez, a lot happens in 15 mins, this place must have major rep, or maybe just cause its friday? Anyways most of the booth seating was all reserved so we just pulled up on the bar. "Hey 'Tender, hit us with those lychee martinis." I was ready: round one, Fiiight! It was great! smooth, fruity, chilled, yet heavy on the liqs! and only 5 bux! 2 peeps could get hella twisted for under 50 bux! oh boy this meant trouble. So we order food, seems they have a thai/organic menu. I didnt care, i just focused on my buzz, was just trying out the food for future reference, my homegurl hadnt eaten all day tho so she was serious bout her eats. Kitchen doesnt open till 6. I ordered the garlic teriyaki shrimp kabob and she had a curry chicken, both came with a side of coconut rice. The food was just decent, sounded better on the menu and i felt it took a lil long to come out, but the portions were VERY small, and prices were double digits. Not budget friendly for the hungry friend to get full off of so I secretly chugged 2 more martinis while my friend went to the bathroom and then we bounced so she could grab some cheap eats down 1st ave. She had a burger at sugar, we had some girl talk, but then i realized i was way more sober than i was in the mood for so i dragged us back over to Verlaines. Downed another round of the lychee's. Was about 9ish, place was super packed, crowd was good, mixed, artsy+after work+downtowners and brooklynistas, 20's-30's i think there was good music? dont remember....actually yea there was music cause i remember i had to shout to have a convo with my friend the first time and later i kept pointing out and bigging up the DJ upstairs, just dont remember exactly what he was playing but i was feeling great. Friend is a lightweight, had to work later and didnt want to be buzzed and was done drinking so we left. But then i looked at the time, its a friday night, i had a long week, and i was seriously just NOT done, dragged her back in for a third time, opened up a tab this time and just ordered 4 martinis in one shot for good measure. Was determined on definitely not leaving buzzless this time. Last thing i remember was sitting down at someones table double fisting my 7th & 8th 'tini, smiling, fist pumping, and telling my friend "I love this song!" Needless to say i woke up the next afternoon naked on my bedroom floor not remembering how i got home and my "tight budget" exploded into a negative checking account and 2 overdraft fees. goodtimes. lol BOTTOM LINE, place is not huge, small narrow, LES style bar/lounge, its probably not as packed on a weekday but if ur coming on a friday get here as close to 5 as possible if u desire a seat. Dont come starving nor for an intense conversation, come for drinks and and lounging and mingling, the food is just there for nibbles and isnt very pocket friendly and the music is a bit loud. Most importantly, Go HARD on the $5 lychee martini, and dont close your tab until your 50% blood/alcohol. You'll save a lot on tips and overdraft fees that way, lol

Love their namesake slice, which is essentially just artichoke dip and cheese on top of foccacia bread. You really can't go wrong with fat, cheese, and carbs. I did have a bad soggy slice here once (it was actually my first slice, but I decided to give them another chance and have been a fan since). No seating though, and the long line has deterred me a few times. I'm not much of a "foodie" type who would be willing to wait on line lines for food, nor do I enjoy eating on the street so I prefer their restaurant location on the West side.

I like that there are 3 separate dining areas for unique experiences. The front room feels like a diner, I didn't sit in the middle, but the back is great because there is an open 'window' so you feel kind of like you are outside. They definitely offer some nice juicy chicken. I thought the cornbread to be a little dry, and didn't like the collards. They had a seasonal watermelon salad with jalapeno that was refreshing yet spicy. I think it is pretty cool that they offer 'wine coolers' I tried both the cucumber and watermelon and they were only $6 a pop!

PORK BUNS! Get your own order of pork buns because you will not want to share! I personally liked it more than the ramen I got, which still tasted pretty good. When you enter the restaurant, look to the bar on your left and notice the sumo wrestler attached to one of the beer taps ;-) Prepare to wait a bit to get seated. We went in around 10pm and waited around 15 mins on a Friday night.

Finally I make it ! I want it to be here for a long time. I'm happy I wait, the food was great, the service was excellent, I seat at the bar and I fell great. Eggs Benedict are to die for! The food is amazing, but I only give 4 stars because I only wish they will be more affordable , maybe to include the coffee with the $16 $$ plate.

I really do love this place. Yes I know that Clinton St. Baking Company has been touted as having the best pancakes in NYC and that is often debated, but whether you think they're the best or not... they're some pretty dang good pancakes. The problem is, as with any place that gets any publicity in New York, the line. Also for me, Clinton St. is kind of a trek, but hey, the breakfast is worth it. The blueberry pancakes are light, fluffy, and delicious. The french toast here is delicious as well, the eggs benedict well poached (this is what I always get when I try a new brunch place), and the sugar cured bacon is awesome. Come on a weekday, come early, take the schlep, come at some weird time, but get here somehow to get an amazing breakfast/brunch.

Bueno indeed. I met my charming date here for pre-NYE cocktails and nosh, and the atmosphere was so festive, we ended up staying past midnight. This family-run restaurant evokes a chic, yet warm atmosphere that makes you feel as if you are at a friend's house for dinner. The Peruvian-themed food is sublime, flavorful, unique. Ceviche, eggplant and foie gras appetizer, and duck were all standouts. The drinks are also fantastic and well-blended -- the pisco sours are deceptively sweet masking a strong amount of intoxicating alcohol. I wasn't keen on the azteca -- a potent concoction of tequila, bitters, and st. germain -- and the bartender graciously let me change my drink. Again, watch the pisco -- it'll have you salsa dancing on the tables if you're not careful.

I love eating here! My to-go to place in the neighborhood. Their service is excellent & their food is amazing. I recommend getting the shrimp fried rice, its amazing. You can't beat the lunch special, roughly 8 bucks!

Yes! They got their liquor license. That means a cold beer to wash down their unbelievably delicious Bicol + garlic rice. If crack tastes like this, I'd be hooked. Â Bone marrow here is killer as well. Enjoy

What I love most about this city is it's uncanny ability to continue to surprise you. The moment you think you've tasted the best sushi this town has to offer, you wind up shocked and in complete gastronomical awe with something new making love to your taste buds! Tucked away on 43rd street in a pretty inconspicuous location lies Sushi Yasuda, hands down some of the best sushi to ever touch these lips. If you're going to come here, you must do it right and get a reservation at the bar...reminded me of all those small carved out restaurants in Asia where businessmen would go right after work to eat and get sloshed. The whole experience and aesthetic at Sushi Yasuda is fulfilling, from watching the sushi chef craft each morsel of fresh sushi for you, to the decor mimicking the zen-like ambiance in Kyoto.. this place does it right! The sushi was flavorful and probably some of the freshest fish I've eaten in my entire life. Each piece was crafted to perfection, with the rice being at room - warm temperature. We went through the entire round of sushi offerings and I fell in love with the Arctic Char, the fresh-water and sea eels, the fatty tuna, the octopus and the scallop (o lord, the scallop). If you're looking for a traditionally inspired sushi experience, Sushi Yasuda is the perfect spot. Even in Mr. Yasuda's absence, this place kills it!!! Don't miss it!!

This intimate spot serves up some seriously delicious brunch. I got the poached organic eggs, my friend ordered the shakshouka, and we shared the patatas bravas. Â YUM! Â All of it! Even the coffee was good! Â (The waiter informed us it was from Columbe) I look forward to returning!
Not as good as before. Â Service and food. Â  Don't feel like high end japanese restaurant anymore

tough to review traif. Â food is really good. Â wait staff and service good. it's a small plates restaurant and we were told to order 2-4 per person (we ordered 3 per person x 3 people = 9 plates). Â we were seated in what looked like a nice room which was plexi-glassed to their backyard garden. Â so...it was all good until...we saw the rats. Â yup. 2-3 big ones crawling around just outside the plexi-glass and up the vines onto the roof of the enclosure over our heads. Â so how do i review a great restaurant with it's own rat- zoo? Â up to you.

What a great pasta joint! They have a great prix fixe menu, but we decided to order off the a la carte. We came by on a Monday night fairly early but the tables started to fill up shortly after we ordered. We didn't try their entrees as all of us opted for the pasta and two apps to share (arancini balls and beef carpaccio). They do pasta right, so anyone will be pleased with that. Will definitely be back for their entrees. Half off all bottles of wine!!

I came to this place with my brother to grab a Tuesday night meal. I was excited by the prospect of hanging out in the West Village; I rarely make it down that far. My most telling story about this place is that my brother's chair wasn't level, so he folded up a stack of napkins to level his chair. When we were leaving, he slid his chair back and knocked over a "B". I shrugged my folders and thought to myself "ya, that's about how I feel also". I ordered the Lamb Massaman Curry which was superior to my brothers dish of fried rice. It was like a fusion between between pot roast and a more typical massaman with peanuts. There were great caramelized onions and potatoes that were cooked separately so that they retained a little crunch. And large portion size. Overall, I would go back if I was a local in this area, but seeing as I am not, I kinda doubt it. :)

Let me start off by saying... Every one has to try this place out at least ONCE. The dumplings are Simply Amazing! I love this place because of the food and atmosphere. The food is some of the best Chinese I've had. Every dish is good and the servings are very generous. The restaurant is very different. There are about 10-15 large round tables. The place is always packed so you have to share the table with people you dont know. It is a fun enviroment. Even if you take a date it can be an ice breaker. The only negative thing I have to say about this place is that it got a "B" from the NYC department of health. A lot of people don't look to much into the rating, but I do. If it got an A, this place would easily deserve 5 stars.
Strange location, but great food and great service. Get the roasted provolone appetizer...ohmigod.
Very cozy setting with friendly service. Â Not your run of the mill Greek food, and very reasonably priced. Â Great date sport, we will be back!

With 3 carts all within a few steps of each other and vampire-friendly hours, these guys are hard to miss. Their locations via their website: 53rd St & 6th Ave "Original Location" (in front of Hilton) / 7pm to 4am 53rd St & 6th Ave Â (across 6th Ave from above location) /10am to 5am 53rd St & 7th Ave / 10am to 5am Ordered the chicken over rice & mixed some of the white and red (HOT!) sauce into it = MMMMMMMMMMMMMMMMMMYEAAAAAAAA! Just as good as all the 3000+ reviews say. Just $6! And a Gatorade for $2. $8 for a NYC dinner? WIN. Very speedy service.

Took me two tries to fall in love with this place, but I am so glad I was talked into going the second time! Three words - Cote de Boeuf - a gorgeous medium rare porterhouse for two, with generous slabs of roasted bone marrow. Paired with a few fresh, bright salads and some good cocktails, and it was a perfect meal for three. We topped it all off with their Grand Marnier souffle, just delectable. I've never been much of a souffle lover, but this one came out steamy, sweet, and as soft as a puff of cloud. Definitely one of the more memorable meals that I've had in NYC; and frankly Minetta's steak beats some of the bigger names in NY. Will be going back!

I love you Jacob. Â The whole place was so well thought from the decor to the root beer on tap to the creamy grits and the siracha in little ketchup bottles. Â After fried bologna, root beer is my second passion. Â  So, Sandy Plus 2 day my group and I decided to venture to Jacob PIckles for some much needed drinks and gluttonous dining. Â The 2 hour wait for a table didn't stop us from pounding awesome brews and rum/root beers at the bar. Â We ordered some fried pickles while we were waiting as well. Â The pickles were just what I wanted with a craft bier: salty, crunchy, tangy and greasy. Â (sidenote: the bar fills growlers) For dinner we all had the various smothered fried chickens. Â I wasn't expecting the fried chicken to be a breast filet, but it didn't disappoint. Â You get two huge pieces. Â The grits are definitely a must. Â Squirt some siracha in them and it's addicting. Â The biscuits were a little on the dry side for me, but nothing jam/preserves they have on menu wouldn't solve. So Jacob Pickles was so awesome I went the next night and got rum/rootbeers only, which are on the more pricey side of $12, and tried the leek country sausage which was pretty standard. Â Came with more french fries 10 drunk girls can deal with. Â  Don't expect the best service as the seating can get a little cramped if you're at one of the long tables with various other dining groups. Â  There's so much more I need to try, everything looks so good. If you want a cocktail-meal get the bloody mary, it's definitely more meal than cocktail. It's definitely my spot now. Â Packed, but worth the wait.
Really cheap, really different, really tasty. The brisket (seasonal) is amazing and is a really large portion. The corn is solid. I will try everything on this menu.
as good as they say. this place will always have a huge line, so dont be fooled by the other vendors lurking around. $6 for a huge bowl of food that can last 3 meals...as good as it gets!

I've been here a couple of times, and both times I've been disappointed. The food has no taste, but I keep seeing the huge crowds and think, maybe it's me? The service is top notch, and the energy is incredible, but I can't eat the ambiance. Whenever I think that I can cook better than your establishment, it's usually not a good thing.
Cash only - don't forget. Fantastic food - slightly anemic service - great prices. If the wait isn't long, Bianca is an obvious choice.

I love soup noodles! And Super Taste is quite good, cheap and fast! I ordered the duck soup noodle and the soup base did not disappoint. They were very generous with the duck meat. The noodles were good but not too memorable for its "hand pulled" quality, IMHO. There was no veggies to be found in my bowl, which sucked for me but I'm sure its a delight for the carnivores out there. The venue itself is the typical absolutely-no-frill-eatery in Chinatown; the lady who takes the orders will be yelling and barking orders into the kitchen. No, she is not mad at you. The downside for me is that they use disposable bowls.... Yes, they run fifty cents to a dollar cheaper than some other noodle place but I'm willing to pay the extra buck for washing the reusable dinnerware.

Umami Burger is more about novelty than anything else. It's a very good burger. I appreciate the interesting play of umami flavors. It makes the burger certainly more interesting. But is it better than say another high quality burger that you would pay a similar price for? Doubtful. To each his / her own, but to me Umami is just another example of the variety of options we have when it comes to dining in NYC. Is it worth trying? Yes. Is it worth the crazy wait? No. If you have to wait more than 30-40 min, do yourself a favor and just come back another time. Chances are good there is another yummy burger a block away.

Avoid this Restaurant Â at all costs...Wasted 26.00 on a large pizza 8 slices of CARDBOARD! Â This is A tourist Trap! I am a native New Yorker..born on Long Island and know what real pizza is..This was a waste of time ....I just want my money back! Hot as hell and they bring us up to the roof...no air conditioner ...we wouldnt sit up there...yuk should of known....should of kept on walking should have read these reviews... We ended up taking the kids to a pizza joint at penn station before we we headed for the train couldnt leave manhatton without the kids tasting the real thing....

Didn't live up to the hype for me. Old restaurant with nice decor. over priced and boring tasting menu when we went - service is meh..There are many more restaurants in this city to try. Don't bother with this one.

Delicious delicious delicious! It's the Chipotle style ordering but with potato as the main ingredient. It will come in all shapes and sizes like curly, baked, wedge, waffle, tots, and traditional. You can get as much veggies as you want and ten for the "protein" addition its a little extra but totally worth it. I had the crispy tots with pepper jack and swiss cheese topped with broccoli and bacon. Customized to perfection. They have other set combos but customizing is the way to go. I love potatopia!!!
Very good food and service. Pappardelle bolognese was excellent, spaghetti with pomodoro also was excellent. We ordered a latte to finish our dinner date. It was also very good. Highly recommended!

Boom! Date night kids. Location - Han's. That's right, ya heard me. Keeping it spicy. Any heat loving aficionado knows Szechuan cuisine is on top of that list. One of the main ingredients is Szechuan chili. My god, fiyahh. Han's quenches that heat thirst and some more. Decor is your simple layout that includes Asian inspired art on the wall along with wooden chairs and tables. Nothing fancy needed especially when getting toasted is your main goal. Waiters were mostly on-point except for forgetting the drinks. No biggie. On our Menu was - Wonton in Chili Oil 6.95 (6) Dan Dan Noodles 7.95 (8) Mao Pao Tofu Spicy Hotpot (10) The numbers in parentheses indicate the spicy level which is from 1-10. Great thing about it is that they can adjust the level for you for any dish. We left everything at default cept for the hotpot which we chose to dumb it down to level 5 ( so what, we're rookies!). Dishes are served family style meaning as soon as it's finished cooking, they bringing it out. Wontons were freaking awesome! It had some type of butter taste to it but you feel the numbing sensation after. A must get. Dan Dan Noodles were insane. 2 words: "The Gospel". Mao Pao wasn't my favorite as it lacked any desirable taste. I'd say try just for the sake of trying, if not..skip. Spicy Hotpot is a mix of everything from seafood to beef in that spicy chili/peppercorn oil sauce. We had it at level 5 which was good but slightly uncomfortable for the heat novice in us. I can't imagine level 10. I recommend getting it if you have 3-4 people in your group. The recommended is 2 but if you're ordering other stuff, this is perfect. Not to mention it's about 24 bucks. Overall, a solid place to pig out at when you're getting the feen for fiyahh. Really good stuff. HandyNasty? Me thinks not.

Things I liked: 1. The really grumpy old Italian guy who is in charge of the line/tables. Maybe I've watched a few too many episodes of Sopranos, but I could kind of see him smacking someone around for messing up an order, or comping a pizza to the local don. Anyway, it made me happy. 2. The cheese. Fresh mozzarella..yum. 3. The pizza comes out SO quickly. Which is nice, since you usually have to stand outside forever to get a table. Things I didn't like: 1. The line and the waiting. 2. The expectations! It was not the best pizza in New York. It was good pizza.. but one side of our crust was burnt, and I do not like burnt pizza. I'd go back..if the line is shorter. And I second the advice about the Brooklyn Ice cream Factory. Or maybe just skip to dessert...

Really loved this place! Was an unexpected gem during my visit. The owners were very helpful, if you have any questions about food in the city. The food is very fresh and quite flavorful. The roasted chicken was good enough it didn't even need the super tasty dipping sauce that came with it (so I ate some with, some without ha). Really great value. You can't beat the quality of the food for the price. Stop by and give them a try, you won't be disappointed!

As the weather cools down and the nights get longer the body and the soul craves some comfort food. Yet as someone who spends hours at the gym, I don't want to walk out of a restaurant with that sense of guilt that so many of us experience after a sinful meal. The restaurant is small but its an ideal place to run into to have a quick meal while enjoying the trendy design. As I looked out into the diverse crowd that can so often be mesmerizing to watch out of the window of the restaurant, I dug into my steamy hot potatoes on a chilly afternoon just as Halloween was setting in. Potatopia is a perfect combination of a comfort/health food that can still leave a girl feeling like she looks good and feels good, even with a belly full of potatoes (yes its possible, just order the right stuff!). I got the baked potato with oil instead of butter and loaded with plenty of veggies and grilled chicken, don't forget the garlic which pairs great with the potatoes. The red roasted pepper sauce was to die for and the perfect "cherry on top" to my yummy meal. The ingredients have strong flavors paired with a hot potato and a crispy skin seems just like the prefect combination of texture and flavor.

It's pretty hard to hate on this place but I found a way. has anyone eaten here lately? Sure it was great when the whole pork pie hat thing took off for the first time back in '05, but now the meat is fit for a chinese restaurant, you know those bullet proof ones? Pretty sad because it used to be so good there, but I guess the ....economy....something. Still, its busy, If you sprayed the corner of Elizabeth and Prince with 12 gauge double ought shotgun shell you would collect a lot free swiss cheesed Marc Jacobs and Varvatos.
the land of halal guys is awesome! they have several carts around the block going east, west and north.

Falafel was good, but not great. Â I think the chain, Maoz has better falafels. Â Interior is cozy. Â  Was a little pricey. Â  It would be nice to allow people to choose toppings. Â Free water. Â I only came here to give it a try after looking at the yelp reviews. Â Might go back.

Been here twice, once on a first date and again with a group of ten. Both very pleasant experiences. Can't say enough good things about Bistango, but I'll try. Small place on the corner, place seats maybe about 30 or so? Tables and chairs with one wall of bench banquette seating, bar in the corner of the restaurant. Ambiance is warm but clean and modern, lighting (I went at night) subdued and could be called "romantic". Most folks smartly dressed, but it's laid-back enough that no one will likely raise an eyebrow at presentable denim. Service is excellent. Attentive but by no means overbearing. As other interviews have stated, diners are asked if they have any food allergies- a nod to the gluten-free, celiac-friendly choices available on the menu. Owner seems like a gentleman and was present both times I visited, clearly takes pride in the place. Side note, cleanup was friendly and discreet when I managed to spill red wine on my date on that first date I mentioned. And yes, she was wearing white. Food is very good and reasonably priced. Humble Italian roots have me lean towards the red sauce-type stuff, and it's present on the menu for the less adventurous. Happy to see broccoli rabe widely used in dishes, speaks well of authentic Italian (i.e. in what I had, and loved, a cavatelli dish w/ sausage, excellent and something I'd come back for). All pastas are available with GF pasta...the dishes at the 10-guest party I attended were all gluten-free in deference to the guest of honor, and I really couldn't tell much of a difference...and I love gluten. Oh, and the red-velvet cake is easily the best I've ever had, and I've had it all over.
Delicious, flavorful, and spicy when needed. Never got a delivery order wrong. Very filling lunch specials.

I had very high expectations for Ippudo, but was a little disappointed. The 1.5 hour wait was to be expected on a weekend for lunch, but the lack of alternate broth options was a little disheartening--really? Only four options and three of them are pork broth? Would have liked to see some chicken broth on the menu. The ramen was very overpriced, and was a little too heavy for my taste--I don't think I'll be returning to Ippudo anytime soon.

The omokase is not on the menu, but ask for it...it's money well-spent. Such technique and such subtleness. The grilled cod was silky, buttery, and smoky and may have been the best piece of cooked fish I have eaten all year.

The two times I've been here I thoroughly enjoyed my three piece fried chicken meals with Mac and Cheese and a biscuit that I would saturate with honey. Â I would take off layers of the biscuit and pour honey on each layer, thus stretching the biscuit to compliment each bite of chicken. I'd have their chicken again. It's been sometime since I've had fried chicken outside of KFC, so I don't have much else to go on...at least for now. The servers I had were attentive and polite and as for getting a table in this small restaurant, I never had any problems as each of my visits were not during their mad dinner rush.

Pleasantly surprised by this place! Had brunch here with some friends and we were all pretty satisfied. The sweet potato fries with sage were amazing -- I'd say almost the best I ever had. Steak and eggs were average; nothing to complain or rave about. The Alfie Burger was delicious. Each entree came with a drink -- bloody mary was delicious, as were the lychee bellinis. The place was not busy, so service was attentive and efficient. Would definitely come back to try their happy hour and craft beers.

Dined here for the first time for a celebratory dinner. I'd been to the sister restaurant Xixa for a yelp event and decided to give this place a try. Reservations are a bit of a hassle. You have to call during their evening hours, have someone take down your name, number, and reservation request, and then someone else calls you back the next day or two sometime during the hours of 2-5 to tell you what's available. Yeesh. Makes me appreciate OpenTable even more. The place was packed when we got there and super loud. I'm fine with the casual atmosphere but it was awkward being constantly bumped and squeezed past by servers and busboys. (Note: Try not to get the table right next to the serving area) Also, although I appreciate the intro to the menu as it was our first time at the place, lay off the hard sell. Our server kept pushing us to get 5-6 dishes for the two of us, but we held our ground and stuck with the 4 we chose. Result: We were STUFFED after those 4 dishes! (Moral of the story: Listen to your tummy, not your server) All complaining aside, the food is FANTASTIC. It's worth 5 stars on its own. We ordered the strawberry cinnamon baby back ribs, twisty beef fat bread, foie gras, and sweetbreads. The ribs were sticky, sweet, and oh-so-tender. It's a weird sounding combo, but the cinnamon and strawberry works great with the meat. The foie gras was buttery, fatty, and just all around gobble-worthy. The accompanying egg and potatoes were nice, but sort of extraneous. Great flavors with the maple syrup and hot sauce. Â  Â The twisty bread baked with beef fat came with ricotta and a meat marmalade. It was super filling and rich, but tasty. The veal sweetbreads were sooo good! So soft and tender. Loved the mushrooms and artichokes too.

I was expecting disappointment when I wandered into this small storefront after seeing the immense amount of 5 star reviews on Yelp, but holy crap this is the real deal. As others have said, $2.50 will get you a small-ish container which is shoved full of pork and rice. It looks small, but let me assure you that you WILL struggle to finish it. I eat a ton of food on a regular basis, and I could barely finish this monster. If you don't like salty food, don't come here. If you're in any way diet concious, DON'T COME HERE. If you like amazing pork, definitely come here.

Finally found my delivery pizza place. Â Pies are large. Â Crust is thin. Ingredients are fresh. Â Prices are fair. Delivers to Brooklyn Heights. I don't know what else to say...it's just really good pizza.

Always heard about this place, but never got a chance to visit until recently! I went on St. Patrick's so the place was full of drunk people eating pizza for lunch haha. Â The wait wasn't too bad but I had to wait for about 15 minutes longer after I ordered since they were out of the Artichoke pizza. Tried the Margherita first, and I gotta say, it is one damn good Margherita. Â The tomato sauce is great and they don't skimp on the basil. Â Not whole leaves but it is shredded up and at least every bite you can get a little bit of basil. Â I love the thinner crust on the Margherita since there's that crunch factor! Â It might be a little too simple for some people, but a good Margherita lets me know that they take pizza seriously. As for the Artichoke pizza, generally I'm not a fan of any white sauce pizzas but I'll make an except for Artichoke. Â The Artichoke pizza is creamy and cheesy. Â It's pretty much a spinach & artichoke dip on a pizza crust! Â The crust is thicker than the Margherita so if you are a fan of chewy crusts, then the Artichoke pizza is definitely better than the crust on the Margherita.
