Â (Fyi, I do know that Mamoun's is perennially shut down by the Health Dept for health violations...and, as someone concerned about health, that certainly does give me pause...but hell, anyone who has also read Kitchen Confidential will shudder even when entering the doors of NY's finest 5-star restaurants.) Â All in all, for $2.50 you certainly get your money's worth.

Located in the Theater District, Becco is some of the best Italian food in a city that has a lot of very good Italian restaurants. Â Prices are reasonable and portions are huge. Â If you walk out Becco hungry then something is wrong with you. Â They also have a extensive wine list as well and you can find something good at just about any price point. Â The staff is courteous and attentive. Â The space is very cozy and tables are packed in tight, so if your claustrophobic, be prepared. Â The pasta specials are all you can eat with servers bringing around three different pasta dishes that you can eat as much as you want- tremendous value! Â  Make reservations well ahead as this is a popular place and space is pretty limited.

Thanks for the tip Yelpers, the Razor Clams were awesome. Pretty much everything was awesome. Incredibly tiny restaurant, but we got lucky with a table that was practically outside. Service was great, the way that our server parsed the dishes was perfect and he gave us a great wine recommendation. Extra points for the great music selections. I love a place were 4 people can order 14 items, and that be perfectly acceptable. Don't worry - we ate it all. Highlights were the olives in the olive oil, the seared fois gras, the charcuterie plate, the oxtail-stuffed peppers, the skirt steak with onion, and the gamey goat. If only we could have ordered one of everything...

I've probably had Halal Guys more than any other "restaurant" in NYC and still get cravings on the regular. This place is definitely more than the sum of its parts. I always get the mixed over rice. The chopped up pits of lamb each has a little bit of char. The chicken is garlicy. The white sauce is tangy and sweet while the red sauce is insanely spicy but blends perfectly. Mix it all together and you get a bowl is deliciousness. No extraneous bell peppers or giant pieces of filler onion like other chicken and rice carts. It's unique, filling, and punches you in the taste buds. Sure it might clear out your bowels afterwards but definitely leaves you wanting more next time.

this place is pretty inconsistent. sometimes it's pretty good and sometimes it's....not. also, i can't decide what offends me more; the fact that they charge $2.25 for a CAN of soda, or that they deliver said soda warm.

Came here for lunch during my annual trip to the city. Immediately, I felt at home here. The vibe is casual and lively and the staff is friendly. I ordered the special Brussels sprout salad and it was divine. I also got their signature omelette and I have to say it was cooked to perfection. My pet peeve is when I order any egg dish and it comes over cooked. This place knows how to make an egg dish and won't disappoint.

how is that possible that of all the AMAZING restaurants in the city that i crave a street cart the most?! and the most often (at least 3-4 times a week. just being honest.) this food is crack. absolute crack. it doesn't have to be drunk food at all. you can eat it sober, sleeping, upside down, for breakfast/lunch/dinner/dessert/who cares! i could literally bathe myself in that white sauce, no really, i'm excited just thinking about it. don't be scared of putting a lot on, literally douse the entire platter and love it. however, BE CAREFUL of the hot sauce! it is soooooo good but a little bit goes a long way! the price definitely makes it that much more awesome because it's SO cheap ($6) for a TON of ridiculously delicious food. totally worth the wait, however long it may be, and the trek, from wherever you may be.

I am always a happy girl when my boyfriend comes back from NY and brings me a banh mi from Banh Mi Saigon. "Ah! He brought back Banh Mi Saigon again! He really loves me!" I think in my head, smugly. Actually, he brings back a whole brown bag of them and I'm allowed to pick out which one (sometimes plural if I'm greedy) I want to eat but please don't ruin my fantasy of true love. I am a fan of DIY cilantro and pickled veggies stuffing. That way I know the veggies will still taste fresh and crunchy when I bite into the sandwich. I also like how the sandwiches are cut in half, for convenience and easier devouring. (Translation: I can ransack through the brown bag and mix and match the flavors.) The prices may go up slightly, the location may change, I may not be from California blah blah blah -- all these things to me are irrelevant and do not affect that the banh mi itself is STILL inherently delicious and cheap enough in NY that my boyfriend can bring back a whole sack of them with the support of his viet mama. This...........must be.........true..........happiness. *whimpers*

We are lucky to have this wonderfully unique restaurant in our neighborhood! My boyfriend and I come here often, and I have to say that everything is very consistently excellent- from food, to drinks, to service, to atmosphere. The Drunken Munkey really knows how to entertain, and entertain perfectly. My usual meal consists of the amazing Pani Puri as an appetizer, the delicious Butter Paneer Tikka Masala, and a Dark and Stormy (or Bramble, depending on my mood.) Both the food and the drinks are made with great care and excellency. Drunken Munkey has, by far, the best Indian food I've ever had. Like I said, the Upper East Side is really lucky to have this fun, unique, exciting, interesting, and most importantly- exquisitely delicious restaurant in the neighborhood. Very highly recommended.

I think there's something wrong with me. Â I love the sauces, don't get me wrong, but the fries just don't do it for me. Â I feel like some sort of EV-fry-freak or something, because everyone seems to love this place! Â The few times I've gone I've had soggy or too-overcooked (teetering on the precipice of burnt) fries.

Such a cute authentic ambiance. We felt like we were in a country home in some ukranian village. You will spend the first half of the meal just looking around at all the trinkets and decorations on the walls and even ceiling. Â The food was delicious and so fresh. Not like other restaurants that add tons of butter and fancy extras to dress up their dishes. The ingredients speak for themselves in these hearty meals. Only bad dish was the borscht- I am not used to bell peppers and sweetness in that soup. Would def not recommend.

At 4 in the morning there was a 15 minute line!!???! What??!!! Ok too old for this sh*t. But my friend promised the Mac and Cheese was good. So we waited.....and waited.....and waited....and waited! One friend ordered a mac and cheese trio, 3 ordered steak and eggs, and one ordered truffle Mac and cheese. I ordered a simple omelet with Caramelized onions and gruyere cheese. The first omelet came with mushrooms, the second came without onions. I was aggravated. How on earth can you mess up a simple omelet? Not once, but three times?! I eventually told her, our waitress, to just give me some Caramelized onions and I sprinkled them on myself, but it wasn't the same *sad face*. The steak eggs eaters seemed happy....the truffle mac and cheese looked burnt. Not well done, but burnt. He didn't eat it. Overall I have to say that my food was ok. The "ambiance" is nice, but I think the lighting in there is exceptionally dim so you don't know what you're complaining about. The food is not pricey, but I have definitely had better service at a diner. Booooo!
Have been there several times and it never disappoints.

First off, the portions are GINORMOUS. The staff was very friendly and they loved that my girlfriend and I were from California. They were very accommodating and they made sure we were happy. The food was pretty good and my only complaint was that you have to like the same thing that people in your party like because the portions arent individual.. everything is family style. My girlfriend is a bit on the picky side when it comes to pasta so I had to kind of pick what she liked. I was okay with it because I am not too picky but there are a lot of dishes i wanted to try. Other than the big plates, it was pretty good. Definitely would recommend for big parties.

This place is, to say the least, unusual. You really feel like you're eating in a kitchen: there's not even a bar or counter to separate you from the stove and cooking area. You get greeted by a less than friendly Cantonese guy in a Hawaiian shirt, are told to pick a table, and handed a plastic cup of tea and a menu with half a billion items on it, most of them around $5 (are you telling me you can prepare all of these items in this tiny kitchen??). I ordered the chives and pork dumpling noodle soup ($4.25), which took a little while to prepare (10 minutes as the waiter warned me, but hey... 10 minutes aren't going to stop me when dumpling soup is involved). The soup turned out to be quite good: four dumplings, which I thought were really tasty in spite of not being fresh (they were pulled out of the freezer), and thin yellow noodles in a pretty good broth. Not the best dumpling soup I've had in my life, but certainly not the worst either. I'll have to go back and try the wontons.

Great dinner for not too expensive! Gluten free friendly too. My friend and I split the hummus (which they can bring fresh raw veggies for), the spinach, and we each had the grilled chicken entree, which was cooked to perfection and served with Harissa. Loved it!

When I was in NYC we were just walking around, soaking up the NYC air and one of our friends said, if you haven't been to Eataly let's go. Basically this place like a mini Italy transplanted to NYC. Everything you want is here, but pretty pricey. But I can see the appeal, where you can meet your friends or bf for light dinner or grab a snack or sweet.

My friend and I capped off our Brooklyn Heights evening with a trip to Jack the Horse Tavern. Â Walking through the door on a Sunday around 7:30, we entered a busy restaurant full of stylish yet cozy decor and a lot of happy diners. To start, I had the red and green lettuce salad with manchego cheese, plums, and herbed croutons. Â It was fresh, a good size, and well-dressed. Â Next, I had the polenta with tomatoes and a soft-boiled egg--a satisfying savory plate. Â We split a side of perfectly cooked brussel sprouts, which also had a few bright, delicious veggies (I think they were pickled radishes?). Â My wine was good as well (and the description on the menu of "agreeably aromatic" made me laugh). Â My friend may have fallen in love with her mac and cheese. Â  Also, the tavern has good lighting and a good bathroom. Â Service was solid. Â For instance, they ran out of the risotto and let us know before we ordered that they had replaced it with a new offering--also a good sign about a restaurant that they are running out of dishes on a Sunday before 8pm. I would happily go back next time I'm in the area.

Went there on a rainy Passover monday for a late lunch with a girlfriend. Both of us ordered the set lunch Â that Â started off with the butternut squash soup. It was delicious! It's not your typical thick hearty soup. Light, not too sweet, was it truffle oil or something else that made it more savory? It was just plain salt, it had a bit of complexity to it. Â Perfect soup for a wet and cold afternoon. Next, Â I had the crispy skate salad. The portion was overwhelming for me. It was good. I wish it wasn't so heavy on the tartar sauce and they gave it a bit more of a tang to it. Maybe vinaigrette on the side? We noticed the ladies beside us ordered a la carte and every dish of theirs seemed smaller than ours, but perhaps they ordered small plates, sides and not main course. My friend enjoyed her ravioli, she devoured that but left the ragout meat since it was filling. We both had the sundae to finish off. We thought we were full, but when we started having the salted caramel popcorn sundae with fudge and all .... we were in heaven. Initially we thought one scoop of ice cream is sufficient, but we devoured the two that came with it. It was that good. I spent the next 2 hours trying to walk off just the fudge. Going out of order here... basil lime daiquiri was nothing to write home about. It was way too sweet even though it was really strong. We almost wanted to ask for that in a Bellini format instead. Service was good. I didn't like the fact there were a few of us at the bar with 2pm reservations and they kept us at the bar for a while when clearly there were tables in the back with place settings ready for patrons. It was silly. Really cute atmosphere, great little flower arrangements everywhere, yet the place is lively. Hope I will return soon!
I agree with most. This place is local jewel.. Very simple food, nice and youthfull environment with friendly and accomodating staff.. Not much to say here, just an all around awesome local eatery...

A mi me gusta mucho la comida italiana. Y este lugar la verdad se merece Â mis respectos con el salmon a la vodka.....el lugar es grande y no es tan ruidoso. Muy buen lugar para. Pasar un rato agradable con la familia o amigos Los meseros. Son muy. Atentos.. La. Verdad Tonys es un lugar al que si quiero regresar.....

I had a pleasant experience here last weekend. 1 star for ambiance, 1 star for the service and 1 star for the wine (lots of options at reasonable prices!). Â Unfotunately, the food doesn't really deserve any stars in my book. Â Nothing was bad, but nothing was great either. The mussels that everyone else has been raving about were MINIATURE. Â Tiniest mussels ever. Â Our server took them off our bill, which was very cool, but they really should not have been served in the first place. Â It's a shame because the sauce they were served in was excellent. Our steak and fish entrees were blah. I would probably give this place another try. Â I really did like the vibe. Â Maybe they were just having an off night with the food?

One of my favorite places to get a steak in NY. Â I appreciate the variety of cuts and sauces available for the steaks, my favorites among them the hotel butter and shallot bordelaise. Â No one ever gives me a hard time for ordering my filet mignon or strip steak well done, and when cooked that way, they are never dried out. Â The salad and french fry sides are very tasty, and I also enjoy the french onion soup. Â I wish they would bring back the shrimp risotto with lobster sauce that they seem to have replaced with a vegetable risotto, perhaps to appease the vegertarians who ought to be dining elsewhere than at a place proffering sweetbreads and roasted marrow bones (a deliacy adored by my more adventurous friends). Â The wine list, which includes half bottles, is nice, Â particularly the Bordeaux. Â I also appreciate that they have always used paper shopping bags for the leftovers, which you will most likely have since the portions are generous.

From the flippant moniker of this restaurant, I was expecting a much more nouveau-hipster type of establishment. But Williamsburg in general seems to be moving past the 'hipster' thing, and actually becoming much more like how the East Village was 15-20 years ago - a place where you can find unusual boutiques, interesting galleries, and really excellent food. The atmosphere here effectively evokes rural Japan (and, yes, I have been to rural Japan). It's almost off-puttingly classy, in a rustic way, considering that I was stopping by for a quick, solo lunch, not a romantic dinner. There's a large communal table, but I was glad to see that there are also a number of more 'private' tables for those who prefer not to dine with strangers. I ordered the chirashi - and it blew away all my expectations. This was the best chirashi I've ever had - and that includes in Japan. It came with a soup, salad, and a bit of pickled appetizers... and all of it went well beyond the standard formula used by most NYC Japanese restaurants. High quality ingredients, beautifully presented, artfully flavored. I felt guilty that I couldn't linger over my meal, as I was running a tiny bit late for an appointment - every bite of deserved to be savored.

The staff here is friendly, the booths have their own TV so you and your group can watch the game you want to, and the drinks are decently priced for the area. The food is also good. I only have one complaint, which is enough to bring it down to four stars from five: The quantity of the food is ridiculously small on a plate for what they market it as. I ordered a plate of coconut shrimp (the day's special) and got three shrimp on the plate. Those three tasted great, but not really enough to make up for there only being three. Anyway, I'll definitely go back, but more for the the drinks and the sports than anything else.

Sat at the bar with a friend one Sat. night. Â Nice enough bartender BUT, -one fish taco appetizer cost $8.95 -the nopalitos salad must have had an entire box of salt dumped in it. You can find better Mexican food for cheaper elsewhere.

I went there with family and kids at Xiao Long Bao for lunch, and we all love it. We have a mix of spicy and non-spicy dishes. Â We ordered a few noodle soup and from their set lunch menu. Potion size of which is just right, with just rice and the dish plate, and nothing of the nonsense stuffs that I wouldn't even touch. We also order the Kung Fu Xiao Long Bao, and pan fried dumplings, to share. I'm quite impressed by the xiao long bao which is juicy in the inside, and the bao skin is thin yet strong enough to hold the juice/soup inside. Service is friendly and attentive. Prices are very reason, with set lunch menu under $10 ($7.95 per), and noodle soup, xiao long bao, and dumplings all under $13. We were in the neighborhood and just walk. Public transport (metro) is convenient enough, though I wouldn't drive into the area just for the meal. But if I'm in the vicinity, I would surely try it again.

Had the white pizza once, no sauce, it's to dry for me. But had the regular pizza with varies toppings, it's so good. The dough gets a little soggy, but makes it chewy like extra mozzarella cheese. Always a wait and little pricier than your delivery pizza, but worth it. This is a place i have cravings for.

Great tasting katsu, too little of a portion though :( The pork katsu is delicious though, juicy and tender served with a grind -your-own sesame with a mortar and pestle donkatsu sauce. The cabbage salad with a miso/mustard dressing was a great side dish and the service was wonderful. I'm not sure if the portion was small because I came at an odd time or if it was because I grabbed a take out order. I basically only got about 5 small slices of pork but would have expected a bit more meat given the price.
There's a bunch of imposters, but there is only ONE 'Original Halal Guys' cart! I always get the chicken & rice with extra white sauce and it never dissapoints my stomach!

Brooklyn is known to have some of the best pies known to the Americas and after sampling so many pizza joints in Brooklyn, probably the best I have ever tasted is right around the corner of our house!!! After living here for over a year, Didn't even know we were missing out on one of the best pizzas my tastebuds have ever known. I'm sorry tastebuds, but now you can now be oh si satisfied . The bread!!! Is it the water? The moisture & them pasture in the oven ? Chewy thin , crisp and the sauce is too die for. Kids were over the moon with their pasta which u tried and almost switched to eating theirs. No line, no over hyped advertising , just a great family Italian restaurant who likes kids.

My thanksgiving dinner spot this year with the whole family and special guest, John F. The turkey special wasn't bad for restaurant food. This was my first portion controlled and no leftover holiday. Support your local food shelter.

I would eat here daily if I could. Beautiful, interesting food and very vegetarian friendly! That roasted carrot salad is to die for. The sunchokes such a treat. Even the pizza had three different cheeses and fresh mushrooms with such great flavors.

Whenever I hang out with my friend Jas in Brooklyn, we tend to end up here! Â They love her and we love their food and friendly service! Â Let me back up and elaborate: Â CHEAP and DELICIOUS food! You really can't go wrong with anything you order. Â Their pad thai is as good as any and their curries are on point! Â I love that besides their regular menu, they also have a list of specials which all always sound appetizing. Â Makes you wanna come here with a big group and just order it all! Â Tried the crispy duck curry today to share and love it - the pineapples and peppers really made it special. Â  Only thing that you should yield to i that they are CASH ONLY so don't forget to stop at the ATM before coming in. Â Also, try to come when the weather is nice so you can enjoy their rear patio. Â We always get lucky and never need to wait at lunchtime, but always see people chilling at the bar to be seated as we leave. Â Drinks are cheap though so no worries - cheers!

This place is amazing! I recently went when I was in town and I had so much fun there! The bartenders are really friendly, they play great music, free cheese puffs, and decent pricing for alcohol. Definitely a fun place to go to with friends if you're looking for some place chill to hangout. If in live in New York I'd definitely be coming here more often. Will be visiting on my next trip out east.

This is the ideal spot for some classic Mexican favorites. I have now been to TLES three times over the course of a year, and each time I am pleasantly surprised by the quality and authenticity of the food. The chips are addictive enough to spoil your meal... so pace yourself accordingly. On my last visit I ordered three different tacos: Pescado (fish): battered and seasoned nicely. Pretty mild in flavor which makes for an ideal starter. Carnitas (pulled pork): Moist, flavorful, and stuffed to brim with stewed pork. Can't go wrong here. Cabeza (beef head/cheek): Don't be scared... The flavor is dominated by intense spices and the meat is cooked long and slow - as to limit any anatomical identification. Even timid eaters will be pleased. If you are craving solid Mexican fare - this is the place to be.
Best thin crust I've ever had. I could eat an entire pizza by myself. Delivery has never been more than 15 minutes. If you want more cheese I recommend the tomato with mozzarella appetizer!

Num Pang's Sandwich just right after a long flight from Seattle. Â I am really surprise that coconut shrimp is not deep fry which is a major departure from the normal coconut shrimp and is a big plus in my book. Only con, we went too late and they sold out of majority of their famous items. Friendly service cash only.

My adult daughter and adult son recently spent 4 days in the city,so time was very valuable.We choose this restaurant as our last place to dine before heading to the airport.Absolutely wonderful experience.The atmosphere,the service and the food!! Not to forget we saw Tony Bennett walk in..I think this man should certainly know good food from poor! I had their Gondoletta Pasta..it was amazing...like heaven!! I will certainly be back.Thank you Villagio...you left a great memory with this foodie!!
This place is Fantastic!!!!! The wings are amazing, solid ribs and the brisket is to die for. Great atmosphere!

Waited three hours to have brunch here on a Saturday afternoon and was starving when we finally got sat. We were sat in a small two top next to the window where servers were picking up their orders. Â The server was nice and as attentive as she could be with how busy it was. Took my wife and kid to have lunch, very disappointed. I should have known this is not an authentic Mexican place. Their servings are for children-after lunch we grab some buns in chinatown. Food is mediocre, if you really want real Mexican food this is not the place. The sides are a joke-I got the tortilla for $3.00 and they gave me like 4 really tiny tortillas, maybe I'm used to real authentic tortilla but this thing is really a joke. This is trying to be cool tortilla but if you are really hungry this is not cool.....

I went to Barrio Chino a few months ago (I know, I really behind on my Yelping) and loved it! I will have to write a more comprehensive review the next time I come here (and there will certainly be a next time). From what I remember, the food was very good, the prices were not too bad and the service was great! It's kind of a "hole in the wall" place (which I sometimes find makes very good food), so do not let that be the reason you do not try this place.
I am about to make a bold statement here... best pizza in NY?
delicious pizza! no doubt, one of the best in NYC. friendly staff, reasonable price. highly recommended!

Amazing hidden gem in Chinatown. Â Dirt cheap dumplings (5 for $2) bursting with chives and pork. Â Can't go wrong with steamed or fried. Add some of the soy sauce and siracha hot sauce. Â Wish i lived closer!

Now how could you possibly go wrong with a too-cool name like the Great NY Noodle Town? Advance word from the likes of Michelin and the NY Times was so strong that Jamie W. and I thought it would be well worth braving the Bowery after sitting through the heavy-hearted histrionics of Larry Kramer's "The Normal Heart" on Broadway. It was close to midnight by the time we arrived on a still-humid night in Lower Manhattan, and the compact place was doing bustling business with both night owl diners eating in and insomniacs waiting for their take-out orders. We were seated with a couple of party-hearty girls in their day-glo spandex at the round table smack dab in the middle of the restaurant. Waiters were speeding by us with plates of hot food, so prospects for a great meal looked good. We perused the lengthy laminated menu while swatting a couple of fruit flies on the glass-top table with alarming precision since the humidity was bringing some of the wild indoors. Since the roast ducks were hanging so prominently in the window, I felt we needed to get an order of it for $9.95 (see photo). It was excessively greasy, so much so that I couldn't finish the last pieces - which is a rare incidence for me, quack-lover that I am. Because of the midnight hour, I ordered a steaming-hot bowl of the Pork Stomach Porridge (Congee) for just $3.50. This was an absolute bargain with the pork innards a nice, chewy contrast to the creaminess of the rice (see photo). I found this to be the most satisfying part of our meal. Jamie went for the $6.95 plate of Beef Lo Mein which was mixed with Chinese broccoli and bok choy on a Pyrex glass pie plate (see photo). Pretty good but honestly nothing special. In hindsight, we probably should have held out for the soft-shell crabs, which is their seasonal specialty or perhaps the roast pig, which looked decidedly less oily than the duck. Oh well, given their dedicated clientele which includes the likes of David Chang and Robert DeNiro, it's definitely worth another shot on perhaps a more wintry evening. FOOD - 3 stars...late night noodles and congee for the midnight snacker or the party animal clubber, take your pick AMBIANCE - 2 stars...well, they have been shut down for health violations before, so I'll just say that we survived without any stomach ailments SERVICE - 2.5 stars...get to the point with the waiter and you'll be fine, no time for chit-chat TOTAL - 3 stars...go if you're hungry but order wisely...and bring your own fly swatter
Great food and a good wine list. Â Finished off with great service. Â Had the spaghetti and lobster and a Super Tuscan. Winner!

The place is small so it wouldn't be good for big groups but I like it quaint and cozy. Everything I ate here was absolutely perfect and I finished EVERY SINGLE PLATE. I started with the le parisien salad with vinaigrette dressing and got the pappardelle pasta with roasted cherry tomatoes, basil, and asiago cheese. For dessert, we got some warm cream puffs with vanilla ice cream on the inside, drenched in chocolate (don't know the name because they didn't give us a dessert menu and the waiter just told us what they had). Waiters were nice and friendly. It's a bit pricey, but worth the experience. Can't wait to go again :D
comfortable and friendly. Â The food was great as was the service. Â A perfect place to watch a game or just to meet friends for drinks. Â I recommend it highly.
Awesome!

I guess the ramen craze goes on and I still don't get it. Came here on an early Â weeknight after work, was told the wait is 45 min. Still more reasonable than the wait at Ippudo, but eh at least it wasn't that cold. Got seated after 30 min and handed the simple menu. So I guess its the spicy ramen. Food came promptly but I mean comon, ramen is ramen. Personally I have not been to Japan but can't say how much more special the broth of a ramen can get. All is said and done, it wasn't worth the half hour wait and $25 bill for two bowls of noodles.

After walking around the city checking things out and shopping, I came accross Boqueria. Â It was pretty busy on an early saturday evening, but we managed to get seat at the chefs table overlooking the kitchen. Â Was a bit warm being so close to the ovens and such, but the tapas were very much worth it. Â  Opted for the 18 month old Manchego, Cod Cakes, Shrimp with Garlic and the Jamon Iberico. Â  Closed my eyes and felt I was in northern Spain. Â The ham was proudly displayed on the counter for all patrons to watch the chef slowly slice it right off the pigs leg (so cool to watch). Â The Cod was lightly fried and served with a not too powerful garlic aioli. Â The food was really good, the service was quick. Â Boqueria, you will see me again.

this is definitely one of the best mediterranean restaurants in the city- so much better than boulud sud, where the air is stuffy and the food so ridiculously salty it leaves you parched for hours. the not-so-bloody martini is pure perfection- a refreshing and unique take on tomatoes that i have yet to experience anywhere else. highlights on the menu include the duck shawarma, brussels sprouts and the mixed grill (the sauces are to die for). desserts are somewhat underwhelming but i'm usually too stuffed to want any anyway.
The food here is great. Always get the chicken curry. Inexpensive. Also free water. Every time I'm near I try to grab a bite. Not a lot of seating, so don't go during lunch time.

What can I say but purely phenomenal! I went with a small group of friends on a Saturday night so naturally the place was very busy. They estimated a 1.5 hr wait but we got seated in half an hour. We all got the fried chicken since we heard all the stellar reviews and let me just say it was FANTASTIC!! The chicken was crispy, full of flavor and very moist. I could eat it over and over again. It is a definite must if in the downtown area!

oh my goodness i had the BEST pizza of my life! The sauce, toppings, and bread were all in perfect ratio. It's been almost a year since my visit to NY and i crave pizza from this place. Howdy from Texas!!

5 stars for ambiance! Great intimate date-friendly restaurant in the Theatre District. It's a favorite for theatre-people and is great pre or post-show. Intimate dim lighting. Cute bar with a pub/cellar vibe, complete with friendly, chill bartenders. Not too formal, but not too casual either. Coat check is available and she is very friendly, as is the hostess. They accommodate very well at this joint! It is intimate and away from the touristy trash down the road. Also, celebs often frequent. Service is very friendly and very attentive. They answer questions about menu and dishes very well and make great recommendations. The menu is very simple so if you don't like anything on it you're kinda screwed, and the only thing I order regularly is the cheeseburger with fries. It's an NYC-theatrical institution and will always be a recommendation by the wait staff there, definitely not the best in town, but very good. The meatloaf is also good. The other sandwiches seem dry from personal experience. All prices reasonable (2 $-signs in my opinion). Excellent dining experience for a couple looking for a cuddly candle-lit quiet night out, or a small group. Intimate, delicious, non-pretentious, convenient and cozy!

There is (almost) always a wait here. Fortunately, there's a cute, expensive-looking French place across the street with a bar. Habana staff will let you put your name down and go across the street, but check back halfway through the wait time; if you're not there when they call you, they seat someone else. The food is decent. The corn is the thing to come here for. It's as amazing as every reviewer below me has said. The margaritas are a let-down (especially since they are so good at Habana Outpost - the summertime-only, Brooklyn take on this joint).
Very good. I will come back again.

This kitchen knows how to cook a chicken. I had the best eggs Benedict of my life, served on a biscuit with shredded chicken and cubed ham on top. My wife had the chicken and waffles and they were amazing. Crisp crunchy skin and airy, buttery waffles.

I came up from South Jersey to this restaurant with the notion of trying exotic meats and I could not be any more disappointed.. The only exotic meat offered was chicken and beef. We ordered the lamb lollies for appetisers and it was made well. Unfortunately, when it came time for main course, it was not the best experience. Â We placed our order for filet mignon and roast chicken. Not only did it take more than half hour for food to come out but we kept getting served tacos and sliders-thrice! We decided to cancel our dinner and pay for the appetiser and drinks. The chef was gracious enough to come out a few time to apologise as well as treat us with our meal on the house. Word to the wise-call and inquire to see if they have stock first before getting there. On a positive note, their ambience was quaint and homely. Â Their staff would regularly come around to see if guests were doing well.

I'm a fan of their drinks, their ambiance, and the location. I'm happy every time because it feels timeless when I walk through those doors. I'm awed by the lighting, and even the bathroom. Maybe it's because I'm in San Francisco, but it's one of my favorites to date! Thank you Freemans for making my holidays in NYC so enjoyable. xo

The food is great, one of the best in the city. Cash only- they can afford that. Service could be better, you always feel kind of urgency while eating, once you you had your last slurp and the bowl is empty, you're instantly being given the check, no questions- like do you need anything else?did you want another drink? So it's a 30 min experience with at least 1 hour wait. But certainly worth it once in a while.

Had lunch here on 7/12. Â The signature chicken dish was extremely good. Â It was very flavorful, skin was crispy (for the most part) and meat was very juicy. The roast potatoes we good, but I wouldn't get them again. Â They felt more like deep fried rather than what I am used to as roasted. Had a glass of their Pinot Noir with the chicken, great fit. Come, eat, enjoy, its that simple.

Only been for drinks - and sat at the bar. Can't comment on the food. The Caipirinhas just weren't sweet enough for my taste. There are no happy hour drink specials - so we might as well have gone anywere. The decor is interesting. The bartenders are super friendly, and this place becomes packed after around 6:00pm. Come early!!!

Wow.. I love this place. Old setup give classic look specially after drink. Cheap and nice happy hours. Its nice hangout with games too. This gets 4 star just because, rest room is pain here. But still an option and good place to hang with friends after work.

I've been purchasing Groupon deals (since last year summer?) and I always leave the place with happy belly :). I've tried many groupon deals and usually they're mediocre or just below average. But Cornerstone certainly exceeds your groupon standards! The waiters are super friendly and explain to you what's available for groupon deals. They were just really friendly in general (yey! finally a friendly service in NYC). I've always tried their dinner and their lamb dish and salmon dish were excellent. Lamb was so soft it was literally melting in your mouth, and salmon was so fresh and well seasoned (no weird or strong seasonings). We also tried their dessert dishes: tiramisu and affogato. They were a little too heavy since they put so much whip cream on top. Tiramisu consisted 80% of cream cheese topping and 20% bread. Affogato was alright too; too much whip cream on top and three bite size of ice cream on the bottom. Overall, it was a really good experience! I'm willing to come back for brunch menus.
This is awesome place ..., Wonderful meal & fabulous service! Dhruv Chhajed

I came here with two vegetarian female friends and the food was amazing. Cozy, intimate space with wonderful, attentive service. I ordered the fresh mozzarella with the marinated red peppers over proscuitto and was so into my dish that I didn't even glance up when my friend Anna asked me a question, attempting to draw me into the conversation. As she said, "It's like you're on a date with your appetizer, a very successful date." We all got pasta dishes. I loved my friend Tara's dish that had beautifully roasted eggplant, but wasn't a huge fan of the butternut squash ravioli that I ordered. I know how hard it can be to get butternut squash to be silky smooth so I was sympathetic. For dessert, we got the warm caramelized apple tart with vanilla gelato and it was simply divine. I will definitely be back when I get a chance.

Stopped here for a happy hour dinner. Â Really tasty burgers and I was pleasantly surprised by the wings. Â On point. Big selection of craft beer. Â They also mixed up their own beer cocktails which looked really good. Â One that we tried was a pecan bourbon and Guinness. Â You wouldn't want to binge drink those but as something to sip on, not bad.

I went to Cabana on a Saturday night and service was good. We were greeted by a friendly hostess. The waitress was also friendly and checked on me and my wife several times during the course of our meal. The restaurant appeared clean. We did have to have our water glasses replaced because they were dirty. The waitress gave us new glasses with no problems and was apologetic. The food was okay. My wife and I had the chicharron and white rice and beans. I felt the portions could have a been a little bigger and the beans could have been better seasoned. The beans were very bland and tasted as if they were taken from a can. The chicharron was crunchy and delicious. Overall, the food was not terrible but I have certainly tasted better and for a better price.

Ended up going to Pulperia when a nearby spot had a 1 hour wait. A quick Yelp of places nearby yielded this relatively new 4+ star Mexican place so we decided to try it out. The ambiance and interior was a great mix of modern decor with some rustic pieces. Not too loud, not too quiet. Our waiter, Daniel, was very friendly, knowledgeable and attentive. When our appetizer took a little longer than expected he gave us chips and guac without us asking, which were quite tasty but nothing crazy. We got the lobster taquitos to start which came on mini fried wonton wrappers and were a great two-bite, refreshing appetizer - I would highly recommend! Then we shared the albondigas (lamb meatball dish) and papardelle. The lamb meatballs were fantastic. A nice caramelized outside, and tender, juicy, and flavorful inside. The papardelle I was less crazy about but my friend enjoyed it. Finally, as we were finishing up our meal, Victor, who is presumably the manager or owner, came and asked us how are meal was and how we liked the place (as this location had just recently opened). After a few minutes he offered us a pineapple-infused pisco punch that was fantastic. The food alone would warrant a return visit, but after we saw the great service and hospitality, we have even more reason to return. I would highly recommend this place.

Ridiculously over hyped. Â Yes, the dipping sauces were cool. The Â best ones were the Vietnamese pineapple and mango chutney like everyone else is saying. However, they are not worth being so pricey and not having salt already come on them! It still deserves 3 stars though because the guys behind the counter are super nice when it comes to trying all the sauces and bringing you your food. I also liked that they have holes in the table for if you're extra lazy and don't wanna hold the french fry cone while having fun with the dipping sauces. It probably is a really good drunk food place but I've had better at Press 195.
Simply the best restaurant in Forest Hills. I'm pretty sure I had every item on the menu and it's just always amazing food.

Perfect time for Ramen, with chilling/breezy weather outside. Â  I had the Totto spicy ramen. Â The ramen came out pretty quick after the order was placed. The broth was spicy as designated in the dish name. Â The thick broth gave it a different flavor, although I would have preferred a lighter less oily broth. The ramen noodles were a little hard, which my preference is for them to a bit on the softer side. Â It would have been nice to have a choice of broth style and noodle style.
i love there foooood! recommend to everyone!

I think Â Pylos is Greek for "We Hate When People Under 30 Come To Our Restaurant Looking Like Crap So We'll Treat Them Like Crap and Mess Up Their Order." Once again, Egg Whites were the culprit.
