Â Better not talk back to me! Â My companion had my back and told Dude that yes, indeed, I had specified egg whites only, but Dude just said "Well maybe I didn't hear you." Â Um. Â Lame. Â Response. Â It should have been "Oh I'm terribly sorry! Â Can I replace it and then give you unlimited free mimosas?" Arrrrrrgh. Â Next time I am saying that I am deathly allergic to egg yolks or have an unnatural fear of yellow foods. Â  Then we'll see what happens (Two Stars for.......the nice busboy.)

Southern-style comfort food has certainly become a really trendy thing in NYC, with chicken and waffles appearing on so many brunch menus across the city that you'd think the novelty had worn off. Buttermilk Channel capitalizes on this trend and finishes a cut above the rest by just making really damn good food. My favorite thing I've tried here is the short rib hash, which was the bomb. Seriously, get it. I also tried the pork chop and cheddar waffle and was actually not a huge fan because of the excessive breading on the pork chop. The cheddar waffle though was great.
Ear-splittingly loud and crowded. Â Good craft beer selection on draft. Â Multi levels. Â Wouldnt go out of my way but a decent choice in that nabe.
Everything was delicious but my favorites were the Sizzling Sisig and Whole Fried Fish. Get the coconut rice on the side to savor all the sauce.

My favorite restaraunt for the big city, its priced right, the food is all fresh and hand made pasta, the atmosphere is perfect for any type of gathering, and the price is set exactly right for quality, quanity, and overall satisfaction. Big thumbs up!
The best and fresh sushi I ever experienced. Excellent service. I will return again and again!

Salads here are great, friendly service, great atmosphere (nice corner spot for outdoor seating as well) and all for a very fair price. I come here maybe a bit too often but I think it's truly a great spot even for takeout.

The food wasn't bad. Â The atmosphere wasn't bad. Â The service wasn't bad. Â But nor were they very good. Food: 3 stars. blood orange bellini, rhubarb cosmopolitan, and wine list (5 stars). The drinks and bar area were absolutely fabulous. Â By far some of the my favorite cocktails in the city, and I spend a lot of time drinking cocktails. ramp and goat cheese toast (3.5 stars). Â The goat cheese had great flavor and texture. Â It was smooth and melted in the mouth. Â However, all that I could taste was the goat cheese as it overpowered the rest of the dish. Â There was also a (tasty) mystery green puree on the toast - I had to google after the meal to be sure that it was actually a ramp pesto, as it was hard to catch our waitress for more than 30 seconds. kasha and bow-tie pasta, veal meatballs (2 stars). Â The sauce was boring. Â It tasted like a reduced veal-beef broth with a mild olive oil with semi-caramelized onion. Â They tried to increase the acidity with lemon, but the dish need something more hearty - like tomato. Â The meatballs were overcooked, and the rosemary element of meat ball did not fit the dish's palate. Â The pasta was also too dense. But the kasha added a wonderful crunch. Â I will definitely be adding kasha to my own cooking in the future. swiss chard side (4 stars). Â It wasn't the freshest or best chard, but it was really quite good. Â Although not amazing, it was very enjoyable. black sea bass with chilies and herbs (3 stars). Â My sea bass was overcooked. Â (My friends was slightly less overcooked, but still overcooked.) Â And I couldn't really taste the chilies or herbs. Â But in some ways this was the most interesting (and promising) dish. Â The broth that the sea bass was served in was divine, and the crunch on the outside of the sea bass was utterly satisfying. Â Note that we didn't finish this dish. Â I'm pretty sure that our waitress assumed that we didn't like it, and it was not included on our bill, which was quite nice of the restaurant. soft shell crab (5 stars). Â Our waitress suggested a soft shell crab with a spicy sauce (off of the specials menu.) Â It was wonderful. Â The crunch of the crab legs. Â The spiciness of the chili sauce. Â The freshness of the accompanying greens. Â All of the flavors and textures blended perfectly to make a wonderful dish. Ambience: 2 stars. Â Yes, it is hip. Â Yes, you might see someone famous. Â But, oh my, did that place hurt my aesthetic sensibilities. Â The art work (creepy glossy prints/paintings of birds and bare trees), the lighting (an odd assortment of mismatching white chandeliers), and the chairs and tables (cheap, plastic-looking, but I'm guessing sustainable) were hideous on their own and even worse in combination. Â They completely clashed with one another and with the farm to table theme of the restaurant. Â The music choices were also quite strange - pop-y in all of the bad ways. Service: 3 stars. Â I must take the blame for arriving late to our reservation. Â We (a party of 2) were 10 minutes late for a 10 pm reservation. Â When I arrive late to a reservation, I acknowledge that I might have to wait a bit for my table...but there is waiting, and there is waiting. Â We weren't seated until 10:35 (give or take a few minutes,) and despite our 25 minute wait, nobody checked in to apologize for the delay. Â At a place like ABC, I expect the hostess to check back in with us with updates. Â It is important to note that (about 20 minutes into the meal) they comped 2 cocktails for us as an apology for the wait. Additionally, our waitress (while extremely nice) seemed to always be in a hurry, and when our dishes were dropped off, they were not "introduced." Â I generally believe that nicer restaurants should describe the dishes as they serve them to you. Â (There were quite a few dishes where I was wondering what exactly the accompanying elements were.) Â Despite the lack of attention, everyone was very nice, and the restaurant was very generous with our bill.

Small restaurant with dumplings and noodle soup - cheap and simple, this place is easy to miss being off the beaten path. Pick up dumplings here cooked at 12 for $3 or 8 for $2, and soups are $2-5. Tasty dumplings here. Fillings are quite stuffed inside, which is a nice change from many places that go light on the insides. Seating is simple, a few tables and more. Key is the garlic-soy sauce mix on the table, though. Makes so tasty! Not necessarily the cleanest place, but it is good for hand-made dumplings and noodles. Love the metal plates. Ask for spare plates if you want.

Had this food delivered for lunch. Â Two different meals for two people. Â We both ate very little and threw the food in the trash. Â I love Thai food and this was a bad as it gets. Â Not sure how there are 4/5 star ratings....

I'm reluctant to give this place such a good review... once people find out about it, it could become packed! Part of the joy is that there seems to always be an empty table. BUT, it's so good, I gotta do it. Of course the food is the main thing. GREAT! Stuff you would never think of (if you're not Panamanian) "Cow's Foot Soup With Pigtail." I know, but this lentil-based feast is the best new thing I've had all year... and it's DECEMBER! You should also try the CU CU, a corn-based concoction like something between rice and potatoes, but with more flavor than either. The food, though delicious, is not spicy. (We may have been served FOR GRINGO TASTE, I'm not sure.) You can-- and should-- get jerk sauce on the side, and add it to everything. Oh yeah, don't miss the meat-filled cassava! Besides the food, (EVERYTHING cooked by Veronica a culinary goddess), the 100% Panamanian staff, and the other patrons (all Panamanian except us from the look of it) are so friendly you'll just want to pack your bags and go there-- Panama that is. --Eat Club is a roving group of NY gluttons. A different restaurant every month.

A great selection of beers and cider on tap. The food was pretty good. Got the fries, tots and their special the strawberry jam and pate were excellent. The grilled cheese with bacon jam was buttery, crisp and melty. The sausage and biscuit was good bit had some pickled onions and green beans that complemented the dish but I am not a pickled fan in general. The portions were pretty good sized.

I've always enjoyed being pampered by having cheat meals during the weekend, but nothing comes close to comparing to eating the bone marrow here. Just can get enough of it. In terms of the famous Black label burger, I think it's alright.

We ordered the 5 course tasting menu with wine pairing..The food was very good, some of the best tagliolini I've had. By the time we left I was definitely full and a bit intoxicated. The food was good but I'm not sure it was worth $500 for two.
3.5 stars for the food. Very poor service and overly high prices drop it to 2 overall.

I'm torn between a glowing review, owing to the entirely awesome margarita pizza.. and a scathing one.. due to the "working man's slice" being $3 or $3.50, I can't remember. Felt a little like.. why hadn't I dressed up more to go get pizza, which was weird.
thanks

My first trip to Las Ramblas was in January of 2006 - been back over a dozen times since, which is a fun fact considering I have never lived in NYC. Natalie is the owner and oftentimes, will be your waitress. Â She and the other staff I've encountered are incredibly nice and welcoming. The small space is definitely part of the restaurant's charm. Â  Expansive Spanish wine list, good sangria (although I feel it might need more alcohol) and with the exception of 1 dish on the menu (the patatas bravas) we have loved everything we have eaten here, and we've probably tried about 95% of the menu. Â A few of our favorites are the olives, piquillos con morcilla and the gambas san martin. In the Summer there are a few outside seats which is cool, but I really dig the tiny inside space, with the water feature on the wall and small high top tables. Â Sounds strange, but the one stall unisex bathroom is really cool. Love the whole intimate experience at Las Ramblas and can't wait to go back!

Our group of 5 was treated like "royalty" by our waiter Emin. He attended to our every needs and thoroughly explained what we were ordering. Â We were surprisingly seated in a lovely upper level curved shaped booth overlooking a fantastic view of the entire restaurant. This was our first visit and it won't be our last. The food was excellent and professionally prepared and served. The deserts were over the top and exceeded our expectations! Tony's Di Napoli is located at a very convenient location next to several theaters in the area. Don't pay attention to Dana C's review. We got more than what we paid for. A true bargain in mid-town!

I find this place to be a bit friendlier than the one in the East Village. Â But overall, the wait time and the ramen are pretty much the same. I'm still not a huge fan of their ramen. Their standard char siu that comes with the ramen is super dry and lack any flavor. I always have to add the additional topping like the pulled pork to give some kick to it. I guess that's how they get me with the additional $4 topping to the already pricey $15 bowl of ramen. Â  I think I'm much more satisfied eating my Nissin instant noodles at home. Next time, I'll just come for their pork buns and cucumber salad, which are probably my two favorite things from them
Try the arepas. Â Seriously. _C$

If you are looking for a great Brunch, Yuca is the place. For $14.00 you can get a coffee, a drink and great food. They have wonderful selection of dishes to choose from (you have to try the Crab cake Benedict or the Arepa Benedict) . The brunch drinks are the best - big , strong and very tasty the only problem is that some times it is get very busy and Â you have to wait for a few minutes , BUT ...it's worth any second of your time .

Walked in on a Sunday night for dinner around 630-7pm ish and we got lucky! Â No wait! Â Looked over the menu and there is so much to choose from! Â Our waiter was friendly and took our order promptly. Â  We started with the meatball bruschetta (yum) and the stuffed artichoke (good). The bruschetta is a perfect size so you still have room for other dishes! Â I hate it when I get full off appetizers and can't eat my meal! Â The artichoke was good, next time if i go back, I'll probably try something else though. Maybe it was too much breadcrumbs and not enough cheese on it for me? Â Not sure but it wasn't my favorite. Â For my entree i decided on the gnocchi (yum!) and my sister ordered the whole wheat fettuccine (different in a good way & yum). I loved my gnocchi and the sauce was yummy! Â The cheese in the sauce made it creamer and tastier and the gnocchi was simply amazing! My sister enjoyed her fettuccine and it was good. Â i had a couple of bites and the lemon flavor def put a twist on the typical fettuccine dishes you see in Italian restaurants. You have the choice of ordering an entree as a single serving or as family style. Â We decided on the single dishes and the portions are a good size! Â I was stuffed after all this food and had no room to try dessert! Our waiter was amazing and wasn't overbearing or inattentive! Its rare to get good service and good food now days! Overall I loved the food, atmosphere, wait staff, prices and would definitely recommend trying this place!

Our reservation was for a large group of 14 people, the cartering manager helped us created 3 courses menu. They printed out guest name cards and placed nicely so our guest knows where to be seated. - 5 stars service in this case The food is well prepared, the flavor combinations is creative, refreshing and satisfying. Â The waiters are knowledgeable and attentive. It is not easy to take care such large group of people. Highly recommended everyone's favorite: Â toffee pudding with hot caramel sauce - 5 stars for their food and 4 stars for their service I am giving 3 stars because we were promised the restaurant will be given us a complimentary champagne, but when we asked for it during the dinner. The manager said it was a confusion. There shouldn't be a confusion, the restaurant should have honored what we have been promised. we weren't so pleased with this part of our experience.

You and me, baby, ate nothing but mammals should be the theme song to this place We wandered into the Cannibal during our recent trip to NYC for some afternoon libations with friends. It was around 3 PM and the place was full but luckily a big group was leaving as we walked in. The vibe was really cool; the space is small and we were seated in a high traffic area, but we managed. The TV was playing Â a college indoor track & field championship for some reason but nobody was watching the TV anyway It took a while to get through the beer list/Bible. The beer I tried (Captain Lawrence Liquid Gold) was a really refreshing Belgian style ale. If you can't find a beer you like in this long list then you should switch to Zima. After all that drankin' we got hongry so we decided to look at the food menu. The choices are quite interesting (if I ever return I'm trying out that pig's head). We decided to get the country pate and a cookie. No complaints about the pate, the taste and the texture were awesome. The cookie took forever to come out of the kitchen. When we inquired about the status the waiter flipped the dial to "bitchy for no reason" and told us we needed to be patient and the cookie was not ready. We finally got the cookie and we assumed it would be warm and fresh right out of the oven. Not the case. It still was a good cookie (chocolate, molasses, and ginger). Minus 1 star for the diva antics of the waiter but otherwise this place was awesome and it's now on my list of dining destinations in Manhattan.

It was a good meal. Some highlights and lowlights. 1. The carrot and avocado salad was probably the best carrots I have ever had. They were grilled and flavored nicely. 2. The devil egg was very good and only $4. 3. I had the skirt steak. Little but too chewy but good. The sauce was tasty. 4. My hubby had the burger. Said it was amazing. 5. The runners and hosts all were very nice. Lowlights: 1. Very long wait and no reservations can be made. Waited 90 minutes for a table on a bench outside. 2. Tight fit. They have to pull the tables in an out for you to get in. 3. Our server was not very friendly. She did not ask how thing were or check in with us at all. Really was a great meal. Would have have been five stars if not for the server. Highly suggest this place.

With all due respect to the kitchen, this place should be best known for its amazing selection of American spirits. Â In particular, brown liquors from states where banjo music should make you tighten the belt and stand up straighter. That's right: Â whiskey. Â whisky. Â bourbon. Â They have an amazing selection of Southern spirits. Â I was there on a date but found the bartender more interesting to speak with, given his encyclopedic knowledge of bevs. Â That said, my date got cuter after each sampling. And that's the best part... just about everything is available in a 1 OZ size, so you can take a couple of sips and see what you like without investing a small fortune, though you might still spend a small fortune given their selection of premium spirits and fine foods. Â  I suppose you can go there for a typical dinner and sit in a booth. Â But you are probably better served - conceptually - sitting at the bar where you can peck at the plethora of bottle-encased pleasures. Â  In other words... you can go to many places and do a little wine or beer tasting. Â But if you want to kick things up a notch and have a much more robust experience, Char No 4 will put hair on your chest and fire in the belly. Or in the case of my date: Â hair on the chest and belly. Â But she had a nice personality.

I have been here 4 times in the last two months. Had brunch, lunch and dinner here. Jeezzzz catfish how do i love thee let me count the ways... the food is crazyyy goodddd. Make sure to have the bread pudding for dessert... dont share get ur own.

A friend and I decided to try JoJu out after hearing how amazing their sandwiches are and we were sorely disappointed. We ordered a sandwich each, I opted for the Classic while my friend had the Lemongrass Chicken. We also got an order of their specialty Bahn Mi fries which were quite good. The bad bits were the actual sandwiches. I'm frankly unsure of where to even begin. The meat was not well seasoned, the bread was so crunchy and overly toasted it cut the inside of my mouth and the ingredients used simply didn't taste good. The chicken in my Lemongrass Banh Mi kept falling out as well. Â In comparison to Saigon in Chinatown, these paled horribly. My friend and I did not finish our respective halves of the Banh Mi and even though we took it out with us, we ended up chucking it into the trash on the way to the mall. It just wasn't worth carrying it.

Terrific beer selection, and the food is a pretty good bargain. Â If you like mussels, they do them pretty well, and it's a pretty huge portion. Â The burger is pretty tasty, and a very good deal. Â If you like good beer, and enjoy a big pub meal for a good price, this is a really solid choice.

What an amazing experience! The food is incredibly fresh, innovative and delicious. We were given a celery granita to begin, to cleanse our palates. It was so delicious and very fresh. We then shared the cheese plate (LOVE the tomato mustarda, and the cheese was lovely and so creamy), then the breads with house made caraway butter with sea salt-amazing! The lettuce salad was flavorful and tasty, For my entree (yes, I was STILL eating) I had the pork chop. I have literally never tasted a more tender and juicy piece of pork in my life. Â I think I had a dream about it last night. I also want to mention the incredibly helpful staff. The service was superb. The decor is kitschy and cozy- it was the absolutely perfect spot for a rainy evening. I had a peek at the garden and I know it's the kind of place that will draw crowds near and far. I am so happy to have The Pines so close by- I will definitely be back!

We arrived at Traif on Saturday, December 27, 2014 at 7 PM. Williamsburg was extremely quiet Â as I imagine most of the residents returned to their true homes for the holidays. We were dressed up as it was my girlfriend's birthday. I parked about a half block away. When we went inside we were greeted by a very pretentious male host. He stared at us for a second and asked if we had reservations to dine with them tonight. I said we did not have reservations. The restaurant was 80% empty. There were probably 3 tables that had guests dining. The host had the nerve to tell us they could not accommodate us and he had to check but he might have had a seat at the bar because it gets pretty busy on weekends. My girlfriend and I looked at each other and walked out. How can an empty restaurant refuse service. We walked by a half hour later and the restaurant was still dead. I could understand if it was a busy night but clearly it was a holiday weekend and the neighborhood was quiet. I really wanted to try the food here and I am very upset that we were basically refused. We returned to our car and 5 mins later we found a restaurant in Manhattan.

Wow the food is good!!!! I had the shrimp etufee! Yum! Even the fries were so well seasoned. Had to take one star off due to them not taking credit cards for delivery.:-(. I really wanted to order more food but that didn't go well due to no credit card on deliveries.
Corn on the cob. 'Nuff said. This place makes me want to fly across the country and go to NYC.

What's all the hype about? I tried a few dishes, but the ceviche, octopus, and quail egg/chorizo all managed to be pretty bland. Jamon serrano was decent, probably your best bet. Cool features: Open kitchen (you can see your food being prepared), nice selection. Not-so-cool: Strategically placing coat and bag on either side of you so as not to involuntarily cuddle with your neighbor.
Great place, awesome ambiance, superb staff, cleanliness, and most importantly GRREEAAAT EATS. Highly recommend!!

How random & remote is this place? Â  I am digging the pie's here. Simply beautiful. And the atmosphere is kinda random too, but i really like it. If you find ourself lost or bored witht he strip joints near by come over here for good service, great pizza, and a nice atmosphere. Â whish i could say the same of the neighborhood...
I just don't understand the hype. Â I did not find it tasty at all. Â There was so much olive oil the crust was transparent and the third kind of cheese on there was way to salty.
Why go to any other fast food place when Kati Roll is an option? Well priced, fast service, and delicious! Make sure you get extra sauce... Wish there was one near us in the Palm Springs area!

i was visiting my mom in NY last spring, and we were looking for a dinner spot to meet up with some friends. i found this place on yelp, and it was the perfect spot for a sat night dinner. the menu is quite extensive...so it was hard to choose between several items that i wanted to try. i ended up with a goat cheese ravioli. it was good, but not "i HAVE to have this dish everytime i come here" kind of thing. anything with goat cheese is going to be yummy to me, so you cant really go wrong. what i really loved about this place was the ambiance. cute, quaint restaurant. we sat right at the open window...eating our meals and sipping on tasty red wine. it was perfect. service was also great and i would certainly come back here on another visit.

Had an awful experience here. One of the main ingredients of the Sabich sandwich is egg plant and they were out of it! They were also out of the lemonade. My isreali sandwich was pretty bland and tasteless. There are so many other better middle eastern options in Union Sq- stay away!

Yes....this place is cozy. Very cozy. Which means you'll be very intimate with the people sitting next to you. The table edges are so close to the point that Â you will have to get up and scoot your table outwards for any person sitting/getting up. We got a strawberry-nutella-banana-on-bread (I know i know....6 dollars for something I can make at home. But when i want chocolate on my weekend mornings I am willing to dish out a couple of bucks for it). Divine. Although perhaps not Nook's doing but the combination itself. We also ordered scramble eggs with bacon, chives and tomatoes. Sounded simply enough, maybe even mediocre. But what we got was amazing. The bacon was delicious (AND FATTY), and every single bite was something we wanted to savor for hours to come. This place definitely takes 'scrambled eggs' to a whole new level -- it didn't even look like it (although, the only experience with scrambled eggs in the past few years have been with my school's dining hall food so my expectations might be significantly lowered). Home fries were fantastic as well. Definitely a go-to brunch place in Hell's Kitchen.

I have been coming here for a while now ... and i love it each time !!! Small but cozy .... Food gets 10/10 ... curedmeat sampler = banging Â  Pretzels are absolutely the best ever .... Dinners are amazing If you don't try this place out ... its your loss

One of my favorite slices of pizza in NYC. The lines can be long but it's worth the wait and the slices are pretty big so bring your appetite. The artichoke slice is creamy and delicious, I tried a slice of their top sellers margarita and artichoke. I loved the margarita. It was my first pizza bite during my trip to NY and it was everything I hoped it would be. Flavorful and crispy crust mmMm. The artichoke was a bit heavy but the sauce was garlicky and so delicious. My only complaint is that there was too much sauce almost like I was eating pasta sauce. And the crust was not thin but rather bready. If the proportions of sauce to crust was better this would've been my favorite. Overall, great spot especially late at night. Sometimes the pizza is burnt so that's bad. Everyone should try it out at least once.

I stopped by here with my brother for some breakfast. At the Brooklyn location, they automatically give you free mini pastries while you wait for your order to come out. but not so at this establishment... or perhaps just not for our table for 2, I'm still not sure. as for the food. it's decent breakfast and cup of coffee. but really 2 eggs, sausage and toast with homefries and a cup of coffee x 2... for almost 40 dollars? A bit overpriced if you ask me.

The soup dumplings are soooo goooooood. Â I don't know that it beats San Francisco, chinatown soup dumplings, but these were realllly good. Â But even better than the soup dumpling was the yellowtail fish served in the most delicious sauce. Â If you go here, you must try the fish. Â  As true NY style, we shared the table with 2 other parties, even though there were plenty of other tables available. Â However, it didn't take away from the food at all. Â Go check it out.

This place was fantastic. It is probably best to make reservations because when I got there the place was packed! Luckily I was by myself and managed to find a seat at the bar. The bartenders were quick to attend me and when they asked what I was drinking I didn't have an answer for him. So he surprised me with something he called The Sweet Transvestite. This drink was a bit small but was packed full of flavor. By the end of the meal the people to my left and right were drinking the same thing. I myself had about three of them. Then came the food. I had s brussel sprout dish as an appetizer. And some lamb as the main course. MY GOD! The food was expensive but so worth the price. The lamb came out cooked to perfection. Not a single bit of fat was on the lamb bites and it was still warm and pink in the center. The appetizer actually did its job by increasing my appetite. The dessert was very sweet and a perfect finish to the meal. I left that restaurant wanting to go right back in for seconds. Unfortunately I had other things to do.

Had dinner there tonight. Pickled mussels were an absolute hit! Lamb and my husband fried chicken tasted yam. Service knowledgeable and Â attentive. Great wine choice and my husbands beer was spot on. Chef is brilliant, will return for sure!
For the price and the quality of the food this place is amazing. The grilled octopus is probably the highlight of the place.
Fries were delicious! You can't go wrong with anything that's fried!

I just moved here from San Francisco and this place was very good they have a frente Greek food here I had to fish next time I might try any of the p**** the people who work you're a very professional and courteous unlike the retard swear that I experienced in Astoria at this dive down but they go called niforos corner home refuse to serve me for some God on my own reasons. said something about his wife being a bitch but anyway this restaurant was very good

Was here late on friday night and we sat at a table with the beer tap. I dont know if I have ever seen this! You get to sit there and pour your own beers...priceless. Â This place is so perfect if you want to go out but not be at a club. Â I didnt eat because we came after dinner, but I will be back and try food for sure. Â 5 stars for beer table and atmosphere.

UPDATE: They are way too big for their own good now. They actually have the dumplings pre-packed on this cart on the weekends- and just hand em over after you order. They're not even hot! Epic FAIL! I've always been a big advocate of Vanessa's Dumpling House.. they have cheap dumplings, soups (love the spicy wonton!) and killah sesame pancake sandwiches (mmm roast duck!) .. I especially have always dug the Chicken and Basil boiled dumplings- even though they take some unreasonable 20 minutes + to cook every time. I will often grab some food and head over to Fontana's Bar, across the street down a few doors, and get some $4 Svedka cocktails to accompany the meal.. Sometimes I swing by in the morning to grab some warm soy milk on my way to the train.. All over it's super cheap and a great little meal. But the fried dumplings are just not where it's at anymore. The skin is WAY too thick, dried out and almost leathery. Upon opening the dumpling you'll find the meat to simply fall out of the hardened shell, onto your styrofoam plate, into a pool of their watery soy and generic chili sauces. Stick with the boiled! Otherwise take the short walk down to Prosperity Dumplings for some truly spectacular dumplings.

Great location for those in the financial district. Â  Surprisingly, when I went for lunch one day, there was barely a line. Â Not sure if that's a good or bad thing. Â But, the burger was delicious. Â The meat's a little saltier than most burgers I've had, which is a positive. Â Fries are perfectly crunchy. Â The shakes are thick but very good - just sweet enough.

I'll admit upfront that I'm a Yelp virgin, and I only write reviews in special circumstances. Tonight was clearly one of them. Earlier in the day, I heard about the Meatball Shop through my gf who happened to be perusing Daily Candy. She suggested that we check the place out for dinner; I happily gave it to my carnivorous desires. Little did we know that the restaurant had not yet opened, and that tonight's event was set aside for "friends and family." When we arrived at 84 Stanton, we quickly realized that something was wrong. The restaurant windows were covered in paper, and everyone inside seemed to know each other. Someone even whispered, "It's a friends and family event." As we stood there confused, the owner, Michael, quickly came to our rescue. He quickly invited us to join the party and sat us down at a nice cozy table. We were officially adopted. The meal itself was scrumptious, and the meatballs top notch. We ordered the meatball platter and some meatball sliders, experimenting with different 'balls (regular, sausage, salmon, chicken) and sauces (regular, mushroom, parmesan, meat sauce). When that wasn't enough, we went for round two, ordering another set of sliders, fully personalized to our taste buds (meatball hero - you'll get your turn next time). Finally, we finished things off with a home made espresso ice cream sandwich, snuggled around two walnut meringue cookies (delish). Throughout our meal, the service was fantastic, with Michael and Naomi, our waitress, checking in on numerous occasions despite the large turnout. The ambience of the Meatball Shop was also great. The space is cozy, with one large table in the center surrounded by small tables, a nicely stocked bar and open kitchen. The mood itself was energetic and upbeat, as the crowds bantered away and scarfed down their 'balls. Thanks to Michael and the staff at the Meatball Shop for a joyous meatball adventure. I'll be back again in no time to enjoy these delicious spherical proteins. This time, it'll be official.
Pretty yummie ... not quick. Â If you want anything other than the #1 (pork banh mi) you should call first and pick up later. Â It's also surreal to eat in the middle of a jewlery store. Â I like it.

I used to eat spicy beef noodles for breakfast and lunch almost every single day while living in China. After a bit of yelping, I trekked over to Lao Bei Fang with high expectations, but found the noodle soup (beef and tendon, #27) disappointing. Service was fast and you get a HUGE portion for $5.50, so the price is right. Unfortunately, I could barely make it halfway through before feeling like the grease was congealing in my stomach. I have no problem with grease when a dish is worth it, but the broth itself was pretty flat, with little dimension beyond the initial saltiness. They were generous with the toppings but the beef was average - reasonably so though, considering the price. Same with the noodles, fresh and homemade, but far from the best I've had. TLDR: Come to this bare-bones joint if you want to fill up on a hearty meal and free tea, but don't go out of your way expecting a culinary epiphany or hole-in-the-wall gem. I'll update if I ever come back to try the dumplings!

Every trip to NYC requires the morning expedition to find breakfast. For some reason this place didn't pop up in Yelp, even thought it was a block from our hotel. We were on our way to a bagel place on 35th or 34th, but just happened to pass this place. At first we almost didn't go because of the prominent mentions of "gluten-free", then we noticed that those were just options. I had the breakfast sandwich -- delicious and so filling, it lasted me all day. Husband had the breakfast wrap with turkey -- he liked it save for the slightly sweet salsa they use. Coffee -- delicious, plentiful, and refillable! Only minus: it was colder inside than outside. On a brisk November morning. Â We ate in our jackets and scarves.

How much for 6 macarons? $14.00 plus 30 stuffy minutes in line behind a self employed man in a houndstooth wool poncho and counting how many women had purses more expensive than my rent. (And thats without the fancy gift box.) The store is very french, feminine, and classic. Glass displays, pastel colors, and bright wide windows make it a very beautiful shop. There are myriad little gifts and treats to add to your order in case macarons were not enough for your wallet. It definitely caters to the Madison Avenue crowd (and the 10+ women in line in front of me with fancy purses). A short and sweet menu offers the macaron flavors flown in fresh from Paris. After you give your order to the super sweet sales women, you finally get to savor what you have waited so long for. Here's a play by play of my 6: Â  Â Rose - great flavor, delicate yet strong enough to really enjoy the rose. Perfect cream to cookie ratio and cookie crunch. Â  Â Orange blossom - WAY too much cream, but great scent, very subtle Â  Â Cassis blackberry violet - This has got to be the signature cookie. An amazing flavor, strong, a bit tart, but sticky due to jam rather than cream filling. A bit too moist. Â  Â Pistachio - excellent marzipan type cream, perfect consistency. Â  Â Orange passion fruit - another jam based cookie with marmalade. Marmalade flavor is very strong and cookie is also sticky. Â  Â Caramel with salted butter- tastes like toffee! filled with caramel rather than cream, and intense caramel taste. Hands down favorite is the Cassis. I would brave the line just for these - I doubt you can find another like it in NY. Overall, the cookie consistency tended to be moister than they should (and it wasn't a humid day). The cookie is also not very large comparatively for the price. Therefore, for the price point, the wait, the size, the impact to the environment (seriously, flying cookies in from Paris?), and the consistency, I'd think twice about getting in line again unless I was buying a gift.

The TOM YUM SOUP was outstanding! Â Its simply the best thai food Ive ever eaten. Â  When they ask how spicy you want it, the medium is more than adequate. Â The VERY spicy is TOO spicy, and I LOVE SPICY FOOD. The drinks were avg. but everything else is great!
I Eat here about 3 times a week lol. The food is awesome, the people are friendly, and the prices are the best.

You must come here to try the most interesting brunch dish...Lengua Y Papas: grass-fed beef tongue and potato hash with pumpkin seed mole and sunny-side up eggs. So. So. Good. As Raphael said, it's the brunch that tastes you back! They don't serve brunch booze here so you have the choices of French-pressed coffees, teas and juices. I had an orange juice but for $6, I felt a little ripped off by that, no matter how freshly squeezed it is. Oh well. The restaurant is easy to pass by because there's no big signage outside. I know because I walked past it several times trying to find it! But once inside, you see what a beautiful restaurant it is! It's simple and rustic in decor, which gives it a casual, airy atmosphere. We came here at 11am on a Sunday morning with no wait so it seems like it's best to come before noon, as that's when the brunch crowd seems to start gathering. Even if there is a wait, I think it can be worth it. Their brunch menu has some interesting takes on dishes and all sound delicious. Service is fast, friendly and they never rushed us, even though it was evident that there was a growing amount of people waiting for seating. Now I wish I lived in Park Slope.

Absolutely loved my meal here and can't wait to go back! Service was great in a nice space Stand out dishes: App -crab risotto (to-die-for!) -charred carrots Entrees -kale, mushroom paella -halibut with saffron-tomato sauce Dessert (complementary sherry and biscotti!) -blackberry crostata -bread pudding Plus I got a photo with Bobby Flay! He happened to be out of the kitchen at the moment so I pounced :)

Really nice and fun atmosphere with a lovely smell of fire in the air. The sausage was super well seasoned. The ribs were decent, but were too fatty for my taste. The sides were really good too (sweet potatoes, and slaw). The selection of beers also make this place a great spot.

First, eating five of Prosperity's dumplings was a mathematical experience. I ordered five for $1 and then began thinking about how much I could get for $5, then $20, then $114, and then $1056, testing my multiplication skills in the process. Second, eating Prosperity's dumplings was a delicious experience. Prosperity's pork and chive dumplings were plump, sizable, crispy on the outside, and juicy on the inside. Definitely bigger and better than the other 5-for-$1 dumplings that I had at Fried Dumpling. Finally, eating Prosperity's dumplings was a humbling experience. I thought about the mediocrity that I eat for far more money in New York, and I was awed by the consistent excellence of Prosperity's handmade dumplings.

I used to work over NY Penn Station with direct access to Koreatown and the huge assortment of restaurants there. But my favorite place of all time was HIT Korean Food & Deli. I used to come here at least 1x/week and my favorite was their bibimbap - made with organic, home grown vegetables! Yes, it really makes a difference. Nothing else has ever compared to the delectable assortment of veggies in HIT's bibimbap. I now live in SF and I'm desperately searching for a replacement for HIT because it's something I miss so dearly. Note: it's more of a lunch spot than dinner spot (closes at 6:30pm if I remember correctly - although they'll stay later if you call in an order for takeout).

Chris C and I decided to be adventurous - we walked into a random restaurant on a friday night and hoped for the best. In a city full of restaurants this can sometimes be risky. We got lucky once... Fish is a no frills place, minimal decoration, but plenty of cozy, friendly atmosphere. Our waitress was all smiles, and informative. After much debate, Chris C and I went for the scallop ceviche and the lobster special. the scallop ceviche was a little too cilantro-y for my taste, about half way through, it was all I could taste. The lobster was good - fresh and the meat was tender and juicy. They do have a couple of specials, all you can eat blue crabs and oysters paired with beer/wine - deals that would make me stop by the next time I'm in the neighborhood

This place is known for their tofu. It's good! I like the variety you can get, even though I usually just end up with the beef or seafood. The tofu is different from the typical soon du bu. There's a slightly different texture - less silky and more milky - than the tofu I'm used to. I like the change. I still like BCD better, which is supposed to reopen in K-town at some point. They also have a lot of good sides, which they will of course refill time and time again.
One of my favorite places for lobster rolls. Been there many times over the years. Also good potato chips. Haven't tried much else there.

Good German food w tasty beers and fair prices, nothing fancy. Cramped on space and non reservations. Friendly service. I'd go back but Zum Schreinder has outdoor seating and is more lively, if that's what you're looking for.

Awesome food, ambiance, and service. All around a great restaurant, tucked away in Woodside, away from the tourist and far enough to keep away the ungrateful and shall i say hipsters. The best time of year to go is summer to sit in the back in the garden/patio. Â  I'd suggest after your meal to take home one of their desserts in the fridge. YUM.

Had an opportunity to try these out at the Union Square Holiday Market and they were definitely a popular booth. So popular that the boyfriend and I came back for seconds... First round he got a plain and I had one with strawberries; verdict: Â Yummy! For the second round he got the strawberries and I went with the dulce de leche... This was less yummy I have to say. The dulce de leche was way too sweet in my opinion. The waffles are truly delicious all by themselves, so a fruit, tart strawberry was a nice balanced combo.

The hype around this place is kind of ridiculous. I've been wanting to eat here for the longest time, and last night I finally did. I arrived at 5:30pm on a Friday night and fought my way through the thick crowd of people to scribble my name on the list. I managed to secure myself about 1 foot of square space to patiently stand and wait inside the makeshift alcove. During the 1.5 hours that passed (I kid you not), it felt like being in purgatory. They would call names every 5-10 minutes or so, and the crowd would shift as the lucky bastards made their way to the front and entered the gates of heaven. At 7pm, we were those lucky bastards and walked through the door to two empty seats at the bar. The service is attentive and lightning fast, and this makes sense given the mob scene outside. We ordered immediately, as we'd had more than enough time to be pondering this decision during the last hour and a half. Our choices: seared tuna appetizer (AMAZING), miso ramen with pork, and mega ramen with extra noodles. The mega ramen was pretty ginormous, the broth rich and flavorful with a distinct garlic taste. The miso ramen, in comparison, has a heavier broth with no garlic flavor. Both were delicious in different ways. Our seats were the first two closest to the door, and every so often I'd turn around to see 20 people standing at varying heights on the steps outside and staring intently through the windows with hunger in their eyes, almost like they were watching us eat. It was at this point that I realized how crazy this entire experience was. For 1.5 hours I was one of those people, and all for a bowl of ramen. Delicious ramen, yes, but ramen nonetheless. Do I regret it? No, because I can now check this off on my Restaurant Bucket List. But would I come here again and join the ranks of the starving souls standing out in the cold? I don't think so. My ultimate verdict in the battle of Totto vs. Ippudo: I prefer Ippudo. In my opinion, it is more worth the wait.
kale salad.

Maman created the most special evening of my life! Â We had our engagement dinner here and Elisa & her boyfriend (the owners) did everything to make sure everything was perfect. Â The food was served to us family style with delicious tuna, and south of france inspired vegetable dishes. Â They played our favorite music, had our photos everywhere, and created the most romantic ambiance I could imagine. I cannot recommend this place enough, especially for private parties! Â They have a great space.

Had an amazing experience at Ardesia a few nights ago. Â The service was very attentive and unpretentious. Â The music was great. Â I noticed a Hungarian white on the menu and before I could blink the bartender had poured me an extremely healthy taste. Â  The food was way above my expectations. Â Small portions but perfect for two people to share over the course of a few hours and a few glasses. Â We chose brussels sprouts, cauliflower, wittewurst and goat cheese crostini. Â Every choice was absolutely perfect. Â The sprouts had been braised in lime and fish sauce and I am still craving them at this moment. Â If we had just ordered that and our wines the night would have been a success. When the weather turns nice expect the outdoor patio to be packed. Â I hope it is. Â I hope I will be returning to Ardesia again and again over the years. Â It is a nice dose of cozy!

AMAZING. Â The best meal I've had in a long time. Â Mouth on fire, tongue blazing, as is the signal that you've just had an authentic Szechuan meal. Â This is not Chinese food for the faint at heart and that is why I am in love. Service wasn't the best...who cares. Â They ran out of Taiwan beer... who cares. Â It gets packed in here... just come early or wait. Â It's worth it. My cousin and I came here and ordered the following: *Dan dan noodles: great taste & noodle texture. Â The guy asked us if we wanted veggies instead of pork and then all 3 of us laughed at the suggestion. Â The pork was fabulous. *Beef & Tripe in Chili Oil: Â I love tripe and I cannot lie. Â This was wonderful and mouth numbing. Â I wish I could eat this daily. *Double Cook Style Pork Belly: Â Wonderful taste and a good relief from the heat as this didn't have spice (although had a TON of flavor). Â Basically this is stir fried bacon and it is heavenly. *Dry pepper style Chicken: Â Was recommended to us by the waiter. Â I thought I heard him describe it as "chicken nuggets" but I ignored that description. Â However, that is exactly what it looks like. Â Don't let it dissuade you... it is delicious. I will need to come back here time after time as I imagine the menu contains gems on end.

The only thing stopping me from eating healthier is time and money. This is the first quick lunch that combines great organic paleo style recipes that taste great with reasonable prices and a chill vibe in a great location. I loved the bowl of shredded veggies and stewed Moroccan chicken. I can now go paleo without eating boring kale and nut salad w a little greasy protien. This stuff is awesome.

This is one of my favorite upper west side restaurants. Â  Food is pretty reasonably priced and the atmosphere is good. Â  This is a good place for group gatherings. Â Most entrees are under $20. Â Was here on a Sunday and the place was pretty crowded which is a good sign. Â My favorite dish was the sheep's milk dumplings. Â  The old Kefi was a little bit more generous with portions but I still like this place.

Most of my favorite food isn't necessarily mind-blowing, rather it's just right on most levels, spectacular on some. It's food I would eat every day. These tacos are just that, and, if I lived closer, I could see myself getting to know the people here pretty well. I had one each of the meat tacos and couldn't pick a "best" out of them. Joint food is my favorite genre and, to me, this place is perfection.

VH and I came here with a friend last Saturday Night. They don't take reservations, but we were seated in about 15 minutes, and while waiting we had something to drink at the bar: VH and Megan had a glass of Cava, while I had their Maker Marks cocktail. The place is nice and cozy, with exposed bricks and a chalkboard band along the main wall. The kitchen is partly exposed. Overall I liked the ambiance, although if you're looking for something particularly romantic perhaps this is not the place for you. We had a bottle of 2007 Il Corzanello Bianco, a nice and dry white wine from Tuscany ($36), very crisp. The menu is slim: six small dishes and six entrees[1], but focusing on a few items rather on a larger menu pays off: all the dishes we tried were absolutely delicious! For starters we shared the antipasti (cured lamb neck, cured pork neck with dill pickles, pickled mushrooms, carrots, and warm olives; $12), and the shaved fennel and radishes salad (with spiced walnuts and parmesan; $9). The fennel salad was particularly tasty and crunchy. For entrees, I had the lamb ribs with chick peas, olives, mint and lemon( $17); the meat was super-tender, coming off the bones so easily. My gf had the roasted chicken breast with mashed potatoes, swiss chard, pickled and roasted mushrooms ($18), which was incredibly flavorful, with a nice and crunchy skin. Megan had the pan roasted cod with brown butter, black tuscan kale, and white sweet potatoes ($19). So good! We also shared the special bread pudding for dessert ($7), which was good but a bit dry: I would have liked to have some kind of sauce with it. Service was impeccable, both at the bar and at the table: despite the small size of the restaurant, there were 4 waiters, all attentive and nice. This restaurant is definitely very well managed. One thing that was missing was bread: we weren't given any bread at the table, unfortunately... --------------------------------------------------Â­--------------------------------------- [1] I was very intrigued by the grass fed beef burger, which comes with pickles, cheddar cheese, potato skins, lardo butter, AND a Brooklyn Lager for $15!!! I guess I'll have to come back...

I'd been meaning to try this place for awhile since I always pass by the lines and hear rave reviews. Finally a friend of mine suggested we try it. The wait was ok - 10 or 15 minutes, decent price, friendly enough - they split our huge slices in half so we could easily share. The margherita was my favorite - the ingredients were very fresh although it was a little more burnt that I prefer. The spinach artichoke was very creamy and heavy, not my taste - but I have high standards since I have an awesome recipe. Pricewise its a little steep for a slice but the ingredients are higher quality and the slices are enormous. While it was good, I was a little annoyed with the hype. I've learned that much of ny (esp. the village) is all about hype and rarely have I found a place that was worth the wait or hassle to secure reservations. (cupcake shops and trendy asian fusion restaurants come to mind.) So if anyone tells you this is the best pizza ever and worth waiting for an hour you will probably be disappointed or you will be so hungry you will think it is the best slice ever. But if you want a good slice and the line is short, then go ahead and indulge.

We really enjoyed our dinner at Perilla. The ambiance is simple but sophisticated. We tried the duck meatball appetizer. It was really well prepared. They definitely had a kick to them, but they were absolutely delicious. They were probably the highlight of our dinner. I ordered the hanger steak, which was just okay. The sides were pretty blackened, and I really felt like I could only taste the charred pieces rather than the delicious middle. My husband had the golden snapper, which was just okay as well. I don't think we'd order either again. For dessert, the lavender donuts were incredible! So fresh tasting, soft, and the filling was perfectly sweetened. Good experience at Perilla. We will definitely try again.

Beautifully seasoned. A little spicy but tons of flavor. Everyone loved the jerk chicken. I had the jerk seitan and it didn't disappoint, either. The rice and peas were simple but not bland. I'll gladly (no pun intended) come back here again and again!

THeir black label burger is the best burger I've ever had! Reservations are a must, but there is often bar space + that's good enough for me! Wonderful, helpful staff. The bartenders are the best, the hosts are so lovely! I miss Amandi - she was my favorite!

Okay so we stumbled across this. Stalled before going in to see a menu (from outside looked rundown). Was impressed with seeing inside. A lot bigger than first thought. Clean and tidy with a dated look. Was offered warm rolls to begin with from a basket. Food was amazing. We had burgers, pasta and chicken pie. We all cleared our plates. We also had deserts, wine and soda. The bill for 4 of us was only about Â£60! Bargain :)
Some really good food here. Mac and cheese got the most praise but I actually liked the cheeseburger better.

Not an average Mexican restaurant for sure. Pretty sophisticated menu, anything we tasted over a few visits was great and tasty, especially the appetizers. I recommend "la rana" (guacomole) for a start with some typical Mexican cocktail.... Amazing!

The wife and I ate here on a Wednesday night because we heard "it's LuCali Pizza and Calzones without the wait and with a liquor license." It delivered in every way! First off, I love Mark Iacono's place on Henry Street in Carroll Gardens. Who doesn't? It's arguably the best pizza in NYC which is saying a lot! It's just that at 36 years old, I'm too tired too wait in 2 hr lines, even if its possible I'll see Jay-Z or some other celeb dining there. So we try Giuseppina's - We had a white pie with pepperoni and shallots . It was delicious. We enjoyed a bottle of wine which was nice being that we didnt have to bring it ourselves. It was reasonably priced and very delicious as well. Our server was attentive though the dining room happened to be a bit crowded Â (5 , 4 tops filled plus our 2 top). The owner, Chris who made the food in a dim lit environment (sepia toned) personally greeted us and we applauded his efforts. He was a very very gracious host thanking us for our patronage. The music made my night, a very interesting take on some of the greatest Frank Sinatra, Dean Martin and Lou Demaio pieces fused with some Michael Buble - I felt like I was in the 50's and it was awesome! We will definitley be back shortly.

We went for the Japanese Tea Ceremony, which is quite a bit different than most of the other reviews. Â That said, it was really, really fun to sit in the little teahouse and have the tea ceremony performed for us. I do love me some matcha, and our hostess was so gracious at explaining the significance of the tea house and the tea and every part of the ceremony. I have to say though, that kneeling for almost 45 minutes really made my legs hurt, and it made me sweat so profusely and in a way that I'm sure would be considered completely disgusting in Japan. Â Oh, and also, my companion had a bit of a wardrobe malfunction when standing up...so just be forewarned: *there will be much kneeling.* Â  Kneeling and all notwithstanding, we're definitely coming back.

Transportation to here was a little bit of a problem, as our limo driver actually hit a parked car while trying to deliver us down this tiny, tiny narrow street. Â  (It gets worse).... Â  Â And no, we are not some rich high rollers, we only rented a limo to take us on a tour of Little Italy as it was a flat rate that would end up being way cheaper than cabs. Â  Â Do consider it. Â  It was like $90 for 8 hours of unlimited travel. Â  Anyway, as highly recommended as this place came, I thought at first that maybe we arrived at the wrong place. Â  As it was smaller (and very narrow), than I had imagined. Â  The food was better than 3 stars, thus my 4 stars. Â  And while were were not drinking yet that evening, we were happy to try the free pours or samples of Italian wines that they offered. Â  Â That served perfectly with the lasagna and ravioli we ordered. Â  Â  Dinner was under 25 for us two, with Manhattan iced waters. Â  Â Service was nice, just a tad slow, but it was very busy. Â  Now back to the limo.... Â  When walking outside, our limo never showed up, as he said he was going to circle the area and come down the street every ten-fifteen minutes. Â  Â  After 30 minutes of window shopping (a lot of fake goods made in China, woo hoo), we realized that he was not around. Â  Â So when calling the limo company we were told that he was involved in an accident, where a NYPD Police car broadsided our limo and totaled it. Â  The limo company sent a private car, took us back to our hotel, refunded our entire fee and charged us NOTHING. Â  Â  Now, naturally we were concerned about our driver, and after getting home a few days later we were able to reach him on his cell phone, from the card he gave us. Â  Â He was fine and simply had a sprained wrist. Â  The accident was determined to be caused by the Police car that hit him, and for some reason we was quite excited that the police car had struck the limo in the exact same area, where he had , ahem, "brushed" another (parked) car when taking us up the street to Pellegrinos. Â  Amazing how things work out for the better good of all some of the time... Â  Â :) PS: The calamari appetizer was superb with a luscious home made red sauce....

This restaurant and bar has a rustic yet modern feel. Â During my late lunch visit, I was greeted by an attentive staff and a very friendly bartender I believe named Richard. Â The restaurant seemed to be filled with garment district and banking folks and folks who simply like the bar to meet up with friends or colleagues. Â My one surprise was my entree which was Arctic Char with fingerlings, mushrooms and brussels sprout leaves. Â The fish was nicely seasoned and sauteed however the accompanying items were cooked until they were almost carmelized and barely distinguishable. Â  Perhaps another entree choice, next time will be worth an additional star. Â However, the service at the bar was clearly 4 stars

Pretty sweet delicious Szechuan food although everyone dining there was non-Asian. The Dan Dan noodles were so decadent a must order if you ask me. Â The dumplings in a spicy soy sauce was so yummy you just want to take that sauce and dump it on top of your rice and let it soak it and partake on the Partay in your mouth

Took my Mom for a birthday supper (we hit the restaurant at around 4pm on a Sunday) so the place wasn't crowded at first. By the time we left, there was a full on theater crowd and it was quite loud. **TL;DR version** This is a great "fancy" restaurant to go to when you have a group of widely ranging tastes and eaters. Some people who want simple, traditional flavors (aka non-adventurous eaters like my Mom) and others who are willing to play with less familiar flavors and textures (like me!) **Extended version** The bread plate was interesting. White bean paste and olives were both deliciously savory ways to whet the appetite. The crostini sticks had good bite, but the actual bread (two kinds) was a bit hard for my taste. (The better to spread with white bean paste, said my Mom). Ceasar salad was pretty damn good. Leaves were nicely coated with dressing (not drowned or dry) and fresh, crunchy croutons. LOVE, LOVE, LOVE that they have a simplified wine list. A page full of $25 bottles. Reds, whites, roses and sparkling included. We picked a prosecco. It was crisp and fruity, without being terribly sweet. Mom had the lemon chicken breast. Succulent and fragrant. I had the try it all pasta special. It did not disappoint. Penne with short rib ragu (NOMLICIOUS), spaghetti with red sauce and the standout winner (which I wasn't expecting) was the vegetable canneloni with bechamel sauce. Decadent. Rich. And perfectly seasoned. Not mushy vegetables. Pasta with bite. So. Freaking. Good. Service was nice, too. The wait staff could've been a tiny bit more attentive, but honestly, they kept out of the way so Mom and I could eat, drink and be merry. Highly recommended for a non-hipster, non-pretentious upscale dining experience if you're in Midtown and randomly want some Italian.

This brunch was excellent! Eggs with Polenta. Service was great and friendly not the typical american friendly - just friendly, I had the feeling she really cared. Not a cheap restaurant. A nice atmosphere, growded. Reservation is needed for the typical eating hours.
BEST MEAL EVER! Â Their chicken and rice are magical. Â It's about a mile walk and 100% worth it. Â Very authentic and affordable.
Not a good idea if you are a small group like two or so. We left almost more than half of the dishes.

This was one of the stops on the Staten Island North Shore Restaurant Crawl. Has a really nice and elegant atmosphere- pretty decor. My group and I were greeted warmly at the door and we had an excellent soup with veggies and a puff pastry biscuit on top. After reading the menu, I would definitely come here for a nice dinner, especially in the summer since they have a nice covered patio outside.

I had high hopes for this place, given the stellar reviews, but it did not live up to my expectations. I've heard lines could be insane, but thankfully, we did not have to wait long at all. For a table of 4, we were seated in 10 minutes. I guess we were lucky, but not lucky enough to enjoy some really excellent food. We ordered a side of fries, a steak, monk fish with spinach risotto, the lamb, and the pork chop. The fries were good, and I actually like them better than Pom Frites. I guess I like crispier fries. But I digress about the fries. The steak was very average. It definitely was not worth it for the price, and it wasn't even tender, if that's what you're looking for. I can say my dad makes better steak. It seems like those steaks you can get at Costco, you know, the NY strip ones. The monk fish dish was probably the worse dish out of the 4. The flavors were ok, but the risotto was under-cooked and very watery. Also, I realized that I am not a fan of meaty fish. It was like eating chicken, but knowing it's fish. But overall, I was disappointed with the under cooked risotto. The rack of lamb was not good. It was very tough and extremely gamey. It was too salty, and unfortunately, the saltiness did nothing at all to get rid of the gamey lamb taste. I've definitely had better for a much better price. The pork chop was the best dish. Perfectly seasoned and cooked well. It was really delicious, and probably the only dish worth getting. For all this mediocre food, we paid almost $60 each for 3 people. I expected a lot better with the price. I am a bit disappointed. I guess this place is way too overrated.
Best tacos on the east coast, bar none. You must try the deep-fried quesadilla. It's decadent.

Went here for lunch with my friend on a Monday. There are tastings of cheese, meats and olive oil in the front of the store and the tapas counter as you walk further in. The dining room, which I found to have ample space, is to the left of the tapas counter. The tosta pulpo was incredible and inexpensive. It's a rare treat to be able to eat octopus on a week day for lunch. I wasn't as big a fan of the tortilla despana which tasted similar to a quiche. The food came pretty quickly and I liked the seating area which was clean and classy. I would come here all the time if I worked nearby!

My best friend lives about a 10 minute walk away and our visit from SF brought us to Traif. We arrived around 8:00pm on a Saturday night without a reservation and they didn't have any availability for a table until 10:30pm. However, they did have a couple of seats at the counter if we were interested so of course we leapt at the opportunity. Ambiance: it's very dark in here, cozy, perfect for a date night. Unfortunately sitting at the bar with stools with no backs and no place to hang our purses, it was tricky to have to eat with our purse on our lap the whole time! I would have to say the timing of the food was not the most ideal. Sometimes 2 things would come out but then there were times when we waited for awhile before anything came out. Food: 3 of us ordered about 6 different dishes: Carrot salad: We enjoyed this, the crunchiness and flavors were refreshing to the palate Seared dayboat Scallops: although the scallops were seared to the right temperature, the sauce was too sweet. Seared butterfish: This was ok, we have had butterfish in hawaii before and it melts in your mouth but even though it was seared well, the sauce seemed a bit too acidic for this fish. Hampshire pork belly: Way to heavy, even to share with the three of us, it felt really fatty We had waited for our sliders for a very long time after everything else came so we decided to cancel it. According to my party,one of the cocktail drinks was very good but the other one was a miss. So all in all, I appreciated being seated on a very busy Saturday night but can't say that I will be wanting to come back to Traif if I am eating in Williamsburg.

AMAZING!!!!! i LOVE this place. Â Their poached eggs over salmon is SO good. Â Their selection of beers is impressive (they even come with the respective branded cup), and with days where you have half off beers, what better place to go after work for steamed mussels and yummy imported beers than Petite Abeille? Â All the waiters are so sweet and nice, and their outside patio is cute too (not sure about now since it's much colder)... 5 stars, def.

The line is always long here but considering there are no fewer than three other falafel options within one block of Mamoun's, I have to assume that this place is the best. Â  Their falafel is always good for lunch or an anytime snack and the $2.50 price is awesome. Â Really - their falafel is the real authentic middle-eastern stuff. Â Stick with the falafel because the $5 shwarma sandwich was tasteless and generally bad. Â I'd add a 4th star because of the good falafel but because I can never get a seat at one of the two indoor tables, am not really a fan of standing in line, and don't love the other menu options I'm staying with the 3- stars.

Definitely not the best. Over hyped and over priced (CASH ONLY). Well i'm from San Francisco and I feel that all the places in NY is OVER hyped. I really liked Mama's back in San Francisco. I think my expectation was too high for Clinton St. Baking Company. I had high hopes that it would have been better or just as good as Mama's. Â  But I guess this place is okay for New York. Sorry I'm a California foodie snob.

GIMME MORE BALLS!! This place is small, crowded and has a long wait. BUT SOOO WORTH IT! I had been dying to try these balls since it was featured on Anthony Bourdain's No Reservation. I finally decided to drag the bf there for lunch on a saturday. The wait was 45min-an hour when we got there around 1:30. I liked that they take your # and will call you when your table is about to be ready so you don't have to wait outside in the cold (I think Clinton St Bakery should implement this service, but that's just me). Anyways, so we enjoyed a nice cup of coffee down the street while we waited our turn to taste those meatballs. I loved that the menu used a dry erase marker and you just select your options and turn it over to the waiter/waitress. I had 2 sliders (1 ball on a small bun)- beef with spicy meat sauce and spicy pork with the traditional tomato sauce. ABSOLUTELY DELICIOUS! The meatballs were so soft and juicy and the size was perfect. I thought the prices were their items were reasonable too! Diff meat options (beef, pork, veggie, chicken, special of the day) and diff plate options (4 balls in a bowl with sauce and foccacia bread, sliders, heros, etc) might make decision making tough but you definitely cannot go wrong with any of the options. Now onto the sweet stuff....the homemade ice cream sandwiches. Similar to the meatballs, you choose your cookie and your ice cream. Everything is homemade. BF chose the special cookie and ice cream of the day- chocolate peppermint cookie with Â white chocolate caramel ice cream. I had the chocolate chip cookie with mint ice cream. The mint ice cream actually had real mint leaves infused in it! Delicious. I think if the cookies were warm that would even give the sandwiches extra points but either way it was amazing. Definitely can't wait to go back there again. Oh and they give you a sample recipe when you get your check! Can't wait to try and make some!

Usually when a place like this gets a lot of hype, the reality tends to be disappointing. I've been to CSBC at least four times now and the food has never disappointed. And there are always lines out the door, even after years of being open. The biscuit with fresh made jam is a must. Their blueberry pancakes are hands down some of the best I've ever had. For those of you who like something more savory, the Southern Breakfast with sugar-cured bacon Â is amazing. Â I repeat, the sugar-cured bacon is amazing. Â  The best times would be Monday-Friday right when they open at 8am. There usually are no lines at that time. On weekends, the lines can start as early as 8:00 am. Any later than 8:30am and you may be faced with a 1-2 hour wait. If you're in a rush, they also have baked goods and coffee to go at the counter inside. And bring cash. This place is cash only.
I've only been for brunch - but it has a great vibe and tasty food at a good price point.

I must admit that their pork buns are to die for. The buns are so fluffy, the sauce is just right and the pork is cooked to perfection. We started off with these and had to order another at the end because it was that good. In fact, every dish we ordered was so good that we didn't leave a single drop of food on the plate. Â We had 2 orders of steamed pork buns, spicy port sausage with rice cakes, pigs head and sake lemonade. Everything was delicious and although I was little hesitant about ordering pigs head (just because of the name) it was really juicy and tasty. The sake lemonade was also really refreshing to drink with all the yummy greasy pork on a hot summer day. After all the food was consumed, we had desserts next door (cookies, cakes and pies), went home and crashed. If I had no regard for my calorie intake, I'd do this everyday.

This was absolutely fantastic. I got take-out and was very satisfied. It arrived hot and fresh, the pita was all warm and soft. I got the redpepper falafel and it was spicy and delicious just like they said. I highly recommend this place for take-out. The tabbouleh and hummus were winners too!
Been here many times and the food is always excellent. Â Some highlights are: bruschetta with sheep's milk ricotta and truffle honey, and all gnocci dishes.

It was our second time dining here this past weekend and we just love it here. It's mess-hall style seating so you sit where they put you next to whomever is there, so like it or keep walking. We were a party of 6 and lucked out with our own high-top right next to the DJ who played FANNNtastic music, btw!!! It is a F.U.N. albeit tiny establishment with an outrageously creative menu. We learned this weekend that they change their donut special every Sunday. Last year we enjoyed their strawberry frosted donut and this week it was this ridiculously sinful I-need-a-cigarette-now s'mores cake donut. It. Was. Ahhhhhmazing. While we waited about 1/2 hour to be seated, our time was well spent being amused by Mr. Entertainer of the Year (how I wish I had gotten his name!!) who was extremely efficient in accommodating everyone in line and making the time pass tirelessly in the melting heat of the sun with his spicy and not-so-spicy jokes :) HE alone gets 5 ***** stars!! So....a few things to remember: **CASH ONLY (ATM inside, tho) **BYOB (there's a packie next door) **NO reservations = potential for long wait ** usually VERY loud inside so keep that in mind if you're bringing babies/young kids

Malaysian cuisine. Large menu, good food. Â Dinner here is good with a large group, as they have the tables to accomodate you. Â I wouldn't say it is the best Malaysian food I've ever had, it's good. Â I really like the seafood fried rice here. Â I was a latecomer at dinner, so I had someone order me the duck with garlic and scallions and it was decent, but the portions of meat were kinda small. Â So I had to be the garbage man and finish up everyone else's food. Â The appetizers were in good portions and the food was cook perfectly. Â I would frequent again.

Though I've walked past this place a dozen times, I never went in, though always made a mental note to try it. Finally decided to go here, with my bf and our friends, and their wonderful son. We had a bevy of items, so a good portion of their food. It is safe to say the consensus was YUCK! The vegetables tasted old, briny, and sour, which don't quite taste like FRESH vegetables. The "manager"/waiter was too busy hopping on his tindr app to refill our waters, or answer why the beer was stale as hell. PASS!
I was expecting this place to be a sit down restaurant, but glad it wasn't because we were on a tight schedule. I had the fried dumplings and it was really good and so cheap. :)

The chicken wings are amazing!!! As is the mac and cheese, greens and candied yams. The portions are huge! Even though it may be packed in the place, the service is speedy. It's real soul food, trust me.....I grew up eating soul food, and this is basically the best I've had at a restaurant.

This place is amazing, i have never had anything bad here, i suggest everyone go as soon as you can, no matter where you live. the spinach pie is quite frankly th best spinach pie ever, same with the saganaki.

The food is excellent but the service has been quite poor during my last two visits. Last night on NYE, the "computer" lost my order. And the kitchen was horribly slow as it was during a prior visit. Disappointing after much better experiences in prior years.
Delicious fried rice with pork belly and egg on top! Just started offering brunch. Can't wait to go back!

After a leisurely stroll with my husband on Graham Ave, we decided to walk into this newly opened bar. Thank you fellow Yelpers! Without you, I never, and I do mean never would have found The Castello Plan. Much like many of the bars and restaurants on Cortelyou Rd, if you don't have an address and a good eye, you're likely to pass by this unassuming spot. I ordered the burger - medium and my cousin had the mussels. Everything was absolutely delicious. Not the best dessert selection and the wines are a little on the pricier side, but all in all I'm definitely a fan. Will be back the next time I'm in NY

A coal fired oven in Brooklyn? Grimaldi's uses 100 lbs of coal per day!!! This is how they get the thin crust crispy with a unique smokey flavour. Less is more here as there is just the right amount of ground tomatoes, mozzarella and basil in their FAMOUS Margherita Pizza. P.S. We didn't have a lot of time in NYC but wanted to hit Grimaldi's and L&B's for pizza. We booked the "Slice of Brooklyn" bus tour and didn't have to stand in line. It was smoking hot the day we went and we just walked in from an air conditioned bus! Â Our guide Paula did all the ordering etc. it was awesome!
