Â About 24 hours before we planned on eating, we originally made a reservation for 8. Â But the numbers changed several times over the next day - first to 9, and then to 11. Â Each time, the person answering the phone cheerfully changed our reservation without any problem (note - many of the tables at this restaurant are sort of "communal" affairs: long tables that can seat up to 20 or so, good deal for very large parties). Â Additionally, although we showed up 20 minutes early for our reservation (and were initially told that our table wouldn't be ready until the actual reservation time), we were seated within 10 minutes. (2) Staff: our party of 11 included two different families and 7 children of various ages, none of whom seems to have conceded that you can't get EXACTLY what you want in a restaurant, even if it isn't on the menu. Â Our waiter was incredibly friendly and dealt with all of our various requests without any complaints or difficulties. Â For about two hours, every time he came to the table (which was often), he was asked to bring something else - show up with one coke; asked to bring two more. Â We never had to wait more than a couple of minutes for him to show up, or for the table to be cleared after each course. (3) Food: this is the star of Jacob's Pickles. Â I cannot think of one thing the 11 of us ordered (6 different appetizers, 7 different entrees, 4 sides, and 3 different desserts) that wasn't delicious. Â Actual quote from my daughter: "I don't usually like fried pickles, but these were great." Â Both my son and daughter tried the cheese grits (neither had ever had grits before) and loved them. Â I am not a pancake fan, but the chicken and pancakes were amazing. Â Frankly, I was disappointed I ordered the catfish tacos (which weren't bad, but weren't as amazing as everything else), because it meant I didn't have as much room to eat off of everyone else's plates. Â Standouts for us included: fried pickles, biscuits & (sausage) gravy, chicken & pancakes, and sausage gravy smothered chicken. Â Loved all of the desserts we ordered. Will definitely return.
An authentic Vietnamese sandwich shop in Borough/Sunset Park. #1 on the sandwich menu is #1.

I had the $25 prix fixe - what a great deal, considering the high quality. Pork buns are mandatory. Â I had the Branzini, and the Thai iced tea parfait. The fish was cooked perfectly - I usually dislike fish with the skin still on, but this was done so well I inhaled the whole dish. Â The parfait was inventive - flavorful without being too rich. Loved it, planning on returning.

I went to G. LEE'S with a friend who highly recommended it and I truly enjoyed the food and atmosphere. Our waiter was very friendly and knowledgeable of the menu, both the drink and food menu. She gave really good advice. The cocktail drinks were delicious and affordable. I ordered the ribs and seasoned greens. The ribs were amazing and fell right off the bone. The greens was decent, I had better. Our waitress recommended the peach cobbler for dessert and boy was my mouth in for a treat. The peach cobbler was phenomenal with a side of vanilla ice cream. Really made me feel like I was in the South. Small restaurant. Seating can be limited. I went during the week so there wasn't much of a crowd. There was a live singer and small band playing while we ate which was a nice change of pace. I would recommend this spot to couples or a small group of friends. Great eating for an affordable price. Cannot beat that.

Melt shop that isn't very melt-y (see my picture) I ordered grilled cheese add on Tomato and caramelized onion, the sandwich was cold (I ate right outside on the tables so it wasn't sitting in the box very long) The cheese slices were not melted...The caramelized onion had a pcs Â of the tough outer layer of the onion cooked in. ick. Â The tomato was cut very poor, uneven too thick. Â  My 13 year old cousin can do a better job at making a grilled cheese sandwich. No good, won't be back!

I tried their Heaven Ramen ($8.50), White Noodles with Peanut Butter and Soy Sauce ($3.50), and various Wonton and Noodles dishes ($5.50-$8.00) and they are all pretty good. I'm not sure if their "no MSG" policy is followed though. Good prices, nice environment, and friendly staff. I wish I tried the Congee. Good for a casual lunch or dinner.

Came here a few weekends ago, with a friend whose not from here. I always order the chicken and waffles. I also ordered the grits and fried okra. My friend ordered the ribs. I visited Amy Ruth's over the years, since high school! And the food is still great. Service was great that night, as well.
they used to only be in carts at fairs. SO HAPPY that they finally got a store location in LES. I WILL BE BACK. TERRIYAKI BALLS FTW

Oh my mother &$@#! I sat here for 5 minutes, trying to begin my review without sounding like a perv. Â I still don't even know how to begin. Like juicy, meaty....burgers? Â Ready for a party in your mouth...? Â If you do not try the truffle burger, you are missing out-- and you should probably get your life together. Â The boyfriend & I stumbled in on a Sunday afternoon, it was pretty busy, but our wait was no longer than 15 minutes. (Win!) Â Our server was extremely friendly and made sure that we were always doing well, without being annoying. Â  The bf ordered the Big Umami Burger, I ordered the Truffle Burger, and we split an order of the truffle fries. Â I must say, my bf's burger was huge. Â I remember thinking to myself, "How the hell is that all going to fit in his mouth?" (no pun intended) Â I just watched him meticulously smash the colossal burger it into a more practical size. Â The flavors were just so complex, none of them being overpowering. Â I am forever hesitant on eating burgers after I tried the truffle burger. Â I mean....What's the point? Â Nothing can compare! I've come to the conclusion, that there is a burger fairy in the kitchen, sprinkling each burger with fairy dust (crack).

By far one of the best Halal Food Carts New York has to offer. I would have midnight munchies with friends and we would drive down to the city to grab us a platter of either a lamb, chicken, or combo. What makes it so tasty is the free pouring of sauce. When given our food we get to put the right amount of sauce in our platter before sitting on the side to eat or sealing it for later. The white sauce is delicious and a little hot sauce. There's also BBQ sauce if you want that sweetness flavor. They have been a popular choice towards new yorkers as well as foreigners who wants to see what the fuss is about. Best to go after drinking or when having the munchies for halal food. Enjoy your visit.
the restaurant is a great overall experience but the food is starting to not taste as good as it once did. Â Beautiful room and overall experience though.

At the "buffet" table: Beef: dry. Fried rice: no taste. Mushrooms: too salty. Kimbap: won't be getting it again. Japchae: fine. They have a variety and options plus a clean place.. but because of the overall bland+dry+no taste food I probably wouldn't come back. It's a good place to get some calories.
Expensive drinks and you will always stand but the drinks are so nice and the bar staff are friendly.
Great bar! Good lounge music! Nice decor. Good selection of beers and liquor. Will definitely be back. Great date place!!

The two of us luckily got in on a Friday night at 7pm without a reservation with absolutely no wait! The place was packed and you practically sit on top of each other but otherwise the food was delicious. We had the octopus and fennel salad which was our favorite; the octopus unlike most other tapas places was not cooked to death and still had great flavor and texture juxtaposed against the sharp bite of the fennel was a great match! Other dishes in the order of my liking: 1. Squid ink rice with seafood had perfectly al dente rice was a bit salty but flavorful and the little seafood that you get was quite fresh. 2. Tomato and garlic bread with serrano was good, but I am biases since I have a weird love for tomato and bread 3. Crispy potatoes was my least favorite if you ask me, but as for my bf I think it was his favorite, but I must ask isn't it suppose to be spicy? There was no spice to it what so ever. We also had a pitcher of the red sangria and it was quite bland, had much better elsewhere! All in all, the two of us was stuffed, couldn't even fit dessert, and a little tipsy for about a hundred dollars and that makes for a good date even if you are sitting on you neighbors lap and overhearing their every annoying conversation. Will have to save room for the churros next time and there will be a next time.

Ahhh! The epic battle over which NY pizza is best -- and the winner is: Grimaldi's! Hands down each and every time. BAMMM! Just like that. Hate lines? order to go.... Come here for the experience of it all and enjoy it; breathe it in. What's the rush anyway? I have been here winter, spring, summer, and fall. I have waited for a long time, I have not waited at all, and I have been here at that awkward time when the stoves have to be reset or whatever the hell it is they do to it. It's empty and you get seated right away during that weird time but since the ovens get shut off to be reset you can't get any food. I guess it's better to be seated and waiting sipping on some vino than to be out there on line. I order the pepperoni with the fresh basil. I can eat an entire pie by myself and most of the time I do, only here. It's just good. The crust is great, the pepperoni is great, the fresh basil is great, and the pizza in it's entirety is simply unmatched. You may find good pizza elsewhere with a hell of a lot less wait times, but never better than this. NEVER. P.S. place is cash only and the only ATM in the area never works. BRING CASH.
WHAT A GEM! Amazing service and great food. Sunnyside was in need of a place like this, and I'm so glad we got it :)

So I'm a bit of a Japanese food snob having been to Japan and lived in Los Angeles, which I contend has some of the best Japanese food in the U.S. That being said, Totto was tasty!!! Yakitori for those of you who don't know are essentially skewers of different foods. We also had a couple other dishes as well. Everything we tried was really good but I ranked them from favorite to least anyways. 1) Harami Skirt Steak 2) Maguro Zuke (tuna sashimi in garlic-flavored soy sauce) 3) Kawa (chicken skin) 4) Tori Dango (steamed rice dumplings with chicken meatballs inside) 5) Amakara Age (sweet spicy deep-fried chicken) 6) Bacon-wrapped asparagus The restaurant itself is inconvenient because it's in Midtown and rather standard in terms of decoration but I will definitely come back for the food anytime I'm in this area again.

Really? Â People still go there? Â They must be from out of town. I have an artist studio around the corner, and when it first opened, it was quaint, cozy and really really good. Love it. Great Spanish food. The samples are great and plentiful. After finishing their samples, we split a little chorizo sandwich. This place can be a little pricey; however, the samples are filling. So load up on the samples and split something. You feel like you got a full meal.

Popped in just for a snack and a glass of wine. The couple dishes we ate were fantastic!! So much that we booked in for next Saturday for a full meal.

I had heard this was the best burger in town. It's not. It's OK I suppose, not the best, not the worst. We sat at the stools behind the bar, next to the front door. Worst place to sit in the whole joint, we were practically ignored. Definitely make sure you get a table. I doubt I will ever go back. Well maybe if it was free. Someone wanna hook that up. Thanks.

You think I won't do it? I said as I looked up at him from my beer. I was surely a bit cockeyed, and I'd never had the best poker face to begin with. Bravado has, more often than not, been the villain that has forced me into many a complicated situation. I was suddenly terrified that he was going to call me out. "No way," he said wearing a wicked grin. He'd known me for too long, and he knew exactly how to press all of my buttons. "Fine," I said defiantly as I grabbed a menu off of the bar, "I've done it before and I can do it again. Just because I've not done something in the past does not make me a slave to it for the rest of my life. I'm a new man. I'm reborn. I'm the phoenix from the ashes!" I began to feel my adrenaline pumping in my chest. Me and my big mouth. It's funny the way life works. I'd been a regular at Cafeteria since it's heyday back in the early 2000's, and here I was sitting at the bar with a man I'd once courted romantically in this very room. The setting had changed, and Cafeteria was no longer the feral nightlife monstrosity it once was; but then again, neither was I. I sat with my ex, who was now no more than a friend, and now felt oddly familiar with my old self. I'd not seen this brazen version of myself in what seemed like forever. "Biscuits and gravy," I shouted to the bartender, "with scrambled eggs with cheese, please." We were back on the whole "egg thing" again. I had successfully managed to go through thirty-one years of my life without eating an egg, and I was for some reason proud of it. It was almost like a badge that I wore, and it could almost be seen as a character trait. It was just something that I didn't do. This is important, because as an artist and a generally free spirit, there was not a lot that I could say no to in this world. Although I would like to chalk it up to some long-winded defense about how inherently disgusting the egg is, it's only been fear that has kept me from eating them. Fear is the catalyst for stagnation, and stagnation had become something that I was not willing to tolerate in my new way of life. It was only a few months ago that I had attempted to eat an egg, and it was for all of the wrong reasons. I was in a fight with Him over something inane, I'm sure. He was mad, and I didn't know at the time how to convince Him that I'd do absolutely anything in the entire world to let Him know how much I loved Him. So I went to the bodega and bought half a dozen eggs. I scrambled them to the best of my ability, being as how I am neither a good cook nor do I know especially how to prepare an egg. With shaky hands I took a forkful of the yellow mess, and with my other hand steadied my phone to capture a video of me shoveling it into my mouth as proof. My stomach began to rise into my throat, and I felt as if I would vomit at any moment. But I took the hefty forkful and chewed it until I could swallow it. This was perhaps one of the things I loved most about my time with Him: it challenged me, and made me face my fears. Even if it were for all the wrong reasons. Eleanor Roosevelt once said "Do one thing every day that scares you." This time would be different. I didn't want to eat eggs to save my ass or get me out of a hairy situation. I wanted to do it for myself. I wanted to show myself that although it felt like it wouldn't at times, my life would go on. There is nothing that we as humans can't accomplish if we put our minds to it, even if it is such a little thing. Sometimes it's the little things that come across as our greatest fears, and it is up to us to put an end to those fears, because no one else can. It was a small battle, and yet it felt like a war. Me Vs. The Egg. Luckily for me, I had new artillery: Hope. "I'm gonna do it." "Fine. Do it," he said. "I am. I really... really am. Screw this. I'm not afraid. There's nothing to be afraid of," I said, and even as I said it began to quiver with anxiety. The breakfast stared a hole right through my soul and spoke to me of greater fears to overcome. Baby steps. I could take baby steps, and soon I would live a life without fear. Fear of eggs. Fear of failure. Fear of being alone. I could conquer them all if I could just... get myself... to take... the first bite. I closed my eyes and took a heaping bite. Within a matter of minutes I had cleared the plate. I dropped my fork with a clang on the bar and let my arms hang dumbfounded at my sides. I had done it. I was officially the bravest man in all of Manhattan. What mattered the most was not that I had done it to begin with, but that I had done it for myself. At the end of the day, I didn't die. I didn't vomit, nor cringe, nor wince at the wickedness of the egg. I had always believed that the world would cease to orbit once I finally overcame my fear. Truly, It made me stronger, and I could feel my blood pumping in my veins and a smile began to streak its way across my face. I began my life as sunny side up.

The place was fairly busy on a Friday night at 6 p.m. The time it took for us was 20 minutes for 3 people. (For the record there is no add-ons so your friends can't come in if you're already seated.) We got the classic tonkotsu ramen. The broth is very creamy and tasty. If you took a spoon of it and looked carefully you can see the crystals of flavory fat in it which tasted simply amazing. Â Overall, it was a good experience with nice service. A lot of people who work there know at least some Japanese and I like talking to others in Japanese. I'm not going to complain about the price since Japanese food can be pricey in the states. It feels reversed in Japan with American food. A medium pizza can cost up to $25 in Japan so it feels reversed.

I have to admit - I was skeptical. Â Even with nearly a thousand loud Yelpers a-yelping...I thought, maybe this is all hype? Â Well............I whole-heartedly agree with the rave reviews here! Authentic Japan ambiance (as someone who used to live there :} ) and excellent food. Â We kind of went nuts since everything sounded amazing -- 1. Sashimi plate - YES. Â Super fresh and beautiful. Overall, I'd say this is worth the splurge! Â Lovely!

Went out dinner and had the tasting menu. Everything was great but strawberry cinnamon glazed ribs are TO DIE FOR

I have been tracking NYC hummus fro 11 years now. Since Nish Nush opened, it quickly jumped to my #1 in NYC. This Hummus is no joke. It's the real deal. Trust me ... I'm a chickpea pro!!! Go get it ... you won't regret it!!!!

The check for the two of us came out to less than ten dollars and for the price it was good but a lot of the items are hit or miss so I can't give it more than an average rating.

Over hyped "fusion" restaurant. Â Bah!
Tucked away down an alley. Great find, eclectic decor, great service, fantastic food. Totally recommend.
The service wasn't terribly gracious, but they were friendly enough. Â I thought the place was very hip and the food was quite good. Â A-

Finally got here. I had the artichoke slice, and, man, this is disappointing for $4 per slice. Â Not much artichoke for that price either. Place was packed. I don't get the hype. It is just a little pizzeria making pizza that isn't so great. I should have had the regular sauce and cheese slice, maybe.

Empanada Mama was good, wasn't great. Â The plantain chips and guacamole were OK. Â The empanadas were really fresh though! Â I had the Brazilian and the Chorizo (corn). Â The passion fruit margarita was really yummy! Â I was told they were going to be $5 during Happy Hour. This is a delicious and standard brunch place. Stay away from the standard options, like mushroom frittata or pancakes, and go instead for their more unusual options, like the waffles and chicken or bluefish sandwich. The unique options is where they really shine. Service is impeccable, probably the best brunch service I have ever had. However, they did not have hot chocolate!!!! This made me very sad as I do not drink coffee and their peppermint tea came from a regular tea bag, which made me wince a bit at the $3 price tag. If you;re so into being farm to table, at least give me some freshness! In terms of their breads, the pumpkin bread is by far the best. The apple one was a bit sweet, even for me, a lover of sweetness, and the biscuit was excellent, but nothing can beat the pumpkin bread. One slightly odd thing is that a subway line is located just beneath the restaurant, so everything a train goes under, the whole restaurant vibrates slightly. It reminds of the beginning of an earthquake, but isn't particularly bothersome.

I've been here quite a few times now. Everything on the menu is fabulous. I especially enjoy the burger, fries and kale fried rice. I recommend making a reservation because they are strict with seating arrangements.

It's the kind of place reminiscent of an old mom n pop's breakfast joint or a cosy, happy family diner. The food was better 2 years ago compared to the fare they serve these days. Sometimes their specials are better than what they have on the menu. The biscuits though, are great! And though some may snub their pies, I find that they are in general very scrumptious. It's definitely worth a try! I must note that I do like the atmosphere here. I do brunch every Sunday (religiously) and unlike many trendy brunch spots, I find this place unstuffy or snooty with very friendly staff. I also love that this place gets lots of sunlight which (in addition to good food & service) is a big plus point for me.

The pizza at Grimaldi's is reallyyyyy good. I live in the area and have been here several times. I love the pizza. The crust is thin and crispy and the cheese is fresh. The only downfall is the line. Even on a rainy weekday, the line is usually a 45 minute wait. I'd say its worth it though.

Another great production from the JG empire. I took my wife to ABC for her birthday and we enjoyed a FANTASTIC meal. Can't wait to go back. My only hangup: I asked to hear more about the biodynamic wines (that they claim to have on the menu) and our server sent over the restaurant's "bar/beverage director". She gave us a short rundown on biodynamic wines and even some vineyards to check out on Long Island. However, she didn't really know which wines on the menu were biodynamic. I just thought that was strange.

Having passed The Smith (55 Third Ave, NYC) just about everyday that we've been in the City, curiosity has been growing regarding the "The Smithwich." Never heard of The Smithwich before? You're missing out. There's a chalkboard next to the service window that depicts a yummy ice cream sandwich made with two chocolate chip cookies. That would be The Smithwich. It taunts you as you walk by. The desire to patronize The Smith has been Â quelled by droves of East Villagers hanging out the door. However, on a hot afternoon, The Smithwich was calling. It also helped that the restaurant was nearly empty, including the bar. The Smithwich ($3.25) is a steal. To make it simple, two crunchy chocolate chip cookies protect a generous Â portion of vanilla Haagen-Dazs. The crunch, when my preference is chewy, is actually the way to go for a sandwich. It doesn't crumble and allows you to actually hold it. The cookies aren't too chocolatey and have that homemade taste and quality to them. If you think you can handle one on your own, it's not a breach of ego if you share. Two people is suggested to kill this thing.

I now have a reason to visit Sunnyside more often. I had a GREAT OVERALL EXPERIENCE here. The restaurant is a bit SMALL but it's very COZY and INTIMATE. It would be a perfect place for a date night. DECOR is very BRIGHT RUSTIC but with a SLIGHT EDGE and it doesn't scream hipster. SERVICE was EXCELLENT, courses were appropriately served time-wise, and they didn't rush us out even though we've been sitting for almost 3 hours. **The MENU here is so VARIETAL and everything sounds so good! I love how there are SO MANY OPTIONS in each category (esp different type of meats). Another plus is that their menu is VEGETARIAN FRIENDLY! DE MOLE NACHOS--REALLY SOLID nachos! Everything tasted super FRESH (ESP the chips) including the GUACAMOLE. Loved that their BEANS were WARM and their CHEESE GOOEY...this was a perfect pairing with the guac. They do give you a BASKET OF CHIPS and TANGY SAUCE to start but I would still recommend getting the nachos! POLLO CON MOLE POBLANO (PLATO PRINICIPALE)--Man, what can I say about that MOLE SAUCE?! It's something I've never had and I was BLOWN AWAY. It's TANGY, SWEET, SALTY, and sorta INDESCRIBABLE unless you try it yourself. The PORTION size was HUGE; I would probably SHARE this with another person next time. The chicken was a thigh and a drumstick together and the meat was FALL-OFF-THE-BONE TENDER. Staple beans and rice were great as well. My friend ordered a SPINACH QUESADILLA and it was STUFFED and NOT FLAT at all! I loved how they served it (cut into wedges and each piece leaned on another). I definitely will be coming back!! FYI CHEAP CHEAP FYI COME ON A WEEKNIGHT

Traditional Japanese food. Mackerel is their specialty witha a special kind flown in from Japan. The Ootoya is excellent if you're a fan of that type of fish. The beef is also very good. Make sure to get your meal in a "set" where it comes with soup, rice, pickled vegetables and egg custard. The custard isn't a sweet custard that many in the US would expect, but a savory custard. Think miso soup in a custard form. Interesting.

Perilla somehow manages to fly under the radar considering how good the food is. If I hadn't lived nearby, I probably wouldn't have have known that it even existed. But trust me, it's one of the most enjoyable, well-rounded dining experiences you'll have. Food is outstanding - I spent a solid 10 minutes taking tiny bites of the Spicy Duck Meatball to make it last as long as possible. It goes perfectly with the egg that it's served with and makes for a great starter. For the main I had the Arctic Char - balanced perfectly with mustard broth and potatoes. You know you're at a great place when the sides are just as good as the main itself. Service and atmosphere are just as good as the food. There is nothing pretentious or snobby about this place, and the waiter we had was extremely helpful in picking out a wine and narrowing down the menu options.

Definitely will be coming back! Being fans of New Orleans food, we were greatly surprised by Catfish. I had fairly low expectations, given the fact that most newer places in Crown Heights seem to fall short of their mark fairly often, but everything at Catfish was delicious. My only complaint is The Hurricane: I understand a 10 dollar Hurricane in NO, because they're huge! Not quite at Catfish. It's good, but you could temper the price. In either case, their food portions are pretty big and very reasonably priced. I was very happy with the overall experience. If I could give them a 4.5, I would.
Looking forward to being back.

Affordable place to eat at K-town! Pros: -Cheap -Packaged Korean food - fast -Buffet that charges by the pound -Fav: Kimchi fried rice Cons: -Extremely busy - no tables :( come with friends, increases your chance of getting a table -Crowded - place is small so when there are long lines, it gets really crowded

Note: This review is on Little Owl's Brunch only Whole Wheat Pancakes: Dear Allton Brown, I cannot believe you disappointed me! 3 of us came here for brunch one weekend morning about a month ago. In my boyfriend and I's quest to find NYC's best pancakes, we were extremely excited to hear Alton Brown profess his love for Little Owl's whole wheat pancakes on Best Thing I Ever Ate. As you can see from the reviews here, however, there are differing opinions on these pancakes. For me, they were just OK. No great flavor- the texture was ok. It is my firm belief that a great pancake should not need maple syrup. While I will still dip a great pancake in some maple syrup, it should not NEED the syrup. In my opinion, these whole wheat pancakes need the help of syrup, otherwise they are just blah. My friend also got the pancakes and she agreed that they were unimpressive. Nothing special. Poached Eggs Dish: My boyfriend and I split the pancakes and this eggs dish. The poached eggs dish is a cross between an eggs benedict (one of my favorite brunch items) and an eggs florentine. It was good- probably better than the pancakes, but I do believe this dish is overpriced. Spiced Fries: Nice taste, nice crunch. Overall, I was not overwhelmed by Little Owl. Everything was OK/good, but not was great. I probably won't return for brunch... perhaps one day for lunch/dinner, but I'm in no rush to return.
Great place solo or with friends!

My One Word: Gem! Fact #1: You will not be disappointed with their appetizers, but their main course can do some more work. The skin of the filet mackerel was too crispy and the meat of the fish was not juicy enough. Fact #2: Ice cream was ok, nothing too special.
This place is awesome! Â If you are ever in NY or a NY resident you should check it out!!!

I've now completed 2/3 of the trifecta of Thai restaurants in BoCoCa (the other two are Song and National). Like the others, food at Joya is inexpensive and service is quick. There's also a nice sized backyard dining area. The kitchen is completely open and there's an angled mirror so you can watch them work, which is incredibly impressive. I don't know how they do it, but even with a ton of delivery orders, it didn't take any longer than 10 minutes for our appetizers, and another 5 for our entrees. The menu is basically the same thing at all three locations. I had the grilled salmon and Brussels sprouts special (just because I wanted to see what Thai Brussels sprouts would be like). It was really good. The sauce had a sweetness to it, and the sprouts were tender (and there were a LOT of them). All in all, Joya is a great place when you're short on time or cash. Oh, and it's cash only!

For some reason, I was expecting Empanada Mama to be a tiny hole-in-the-wall, no-frills joint, so I was surprised to find that I was only half right. Â It is definitely tiny (about 10 small tables plus a counter that seats about 6), but I wasn't expecting the bold splashes of green and red on the walls, or the club music blasting out of the speakers (the music later changed to Justin Timberlake's solo ouevre). I had been meaning to check out this place for awhile now, so I was pleased when the opportunity arose during my girls' night with Haley P. Â The selection of empanadas was overwhelming! Â A whole page dedicated to the small, handheld pockets of flavorful goodness. Â I had never seen such an array of empanada fillings, and they went from the traditional savory to the sweet (Elvis empanada, anyone?). I decided to play it pretty safe since I had a good feeling I'd be coming back for many return visits. Â I ordered the Brasil (spicy ground beef, olives, onions), the Reggaeton (roast pork, yellow rice, peas, potatoes) and the Spicy Chicken (self-explanatory, no?). Â Haley and I shared a cheese arepa. Â  I was definitely not disappointed with my meal. Â I was actually worried that three empanadas and half an arepa weren't going to suffice for a proper dinner, but I was comfortably full by the end. Â The arepa was actually smaller than I expected since the last time I had one was at a Colombian restaurant and it was about 6" wide. Â This one was about 2.5" wide, but even more delicious because the arepa was so soft and the shredded cheese so melty. Now onto the main attraction: the empanadas. Â My favorite was the Brasil - that beef had so much kick to it, I dared not add any of the side spicy sauce they supplied. Â The pork in the Reggaeton was nice and moist, and the spicy chicken had a good flavor, but I decided to add some of the green spicy sauce to bump it up a notch (damn, that sauce was DELICIOUS). Best of all, the empanadas were at the low cost of $2.50-$2.75 each! Â And they certainly didn't skimp out on any of the fillings or flavor. Â Talk about cheap eats! Â The arepa was almost twice as much at $4.95, but it was still a good deal. Â We walked out of there only $22 lighter between the two of us. Â Not bad considering this was Midtown and so close to the Theater District! The only downsides were that the music was a touch louder than I would have liked, especially in a small place like this, and service could have been loads better. Â We sat at the end of the counter by the door and had to flag down the waitstaff any time we needed them. Â Not a great situation when you're dying for a water refill. Â And yes, the place was full, but they did have three people working the room. Still, I can't really complain too much considering the great deal we got for such a great meal! Â Not to mention the great company I had to make it all the better.

Head full of art from the MoMA and belly in need of stimulation? Â Walk the few blocks and treat yourself the Bengal Tiger. Verging of fast food Indian, the lunch special is tasty, hearty, hot and fast! Â At under $10 it is more than enough for one, we added in samosas (get some) and papadams (skip 'em) and we left stuffed and happy, ready for more art!

They have great burgers with several options for meat : lamp, elk etc. Â The sliders are scrumptious and melt in your mouth. Â The fries are fresh cut with a selection of hot sauces which are irresistible while milkshakes are simply addictive. Â I had banana, vanilla and pistachio shake mixed up. Â The symphony always plays in my mind when I think of this place. On top of that great service, Â with that I am there often.

I'm from the South and I've been thinking about finding a great Cajun place to swamp on some jambalaya or etouffÃ©e. Fortunately, I was walking around the 'Burg looking for lunch on Sunday and stumbled across Juniper. A waft of slow-cooked BBQ and a sign for catfish stopped me in my tracks. The downside of this story is they had just run out of pulled pork and braised ribs, but the upside is I had the catfish sandwich. It was light and crisp, well-peppered and topped with a perfectly balanced garlic aioli. And the french fries? Just as good. Seriously, come here and try the fries. I want to come back and try the truffle burger and the jambalaya (shrimp, chicken, andouille, mussels!). The service was quick and the server, she was very busy but still available (it's a small place) and, of most importance, friendly. The chef popped out and apologized for the lack of BBQ, but welcomed us to come back later for freshly cooked BBQ. It was tempting, but I was stuffed. I thanked him for the offer and will definitely be back. Which will be soon.

The first time I came here, it was a Monday. I'm not sure if there was a different chef or the place was too packed but the Eggs Benedict my group ordered were not what we ideally imagined. Second time around, the Eggs Benedict was made to near perfection. Although my friend's plate had some complications, the waitress was extremely courteous and replaced her dish with a fresh order. Other items ordered: Grand Moka - gigantic cup of mocha that made my day. Â  Cappuccino - super foamy and delightful

I have hesitated to review until I gave Batali's place a fair shake (four visits), because he usually does not disappoint. Â i have to say, maybe if he didn't call it Spanish, I'd like it better. I DEFINITELY Â don't feel like I'm in barcelona when i am eating there. Aside from the razor clams and the oxtail stuffed piquillo peppers, cannot conjure a mouth watering memory of anything else. Â  Further, the share-ability is not easy here and the pace they bring the food usually requires everyone to focus on the plate closest to them. Overall: service is way too fast, the food is very oily, seems like there is anchovy in everything (not a bad thing, just an odd thing), quality is high, taste is average, value is low Grilled Romaine salad: very wilted, hence very hard to share. saving grace was the large random anchovy on it. Â Random due to it being the only taut item on the dish. Skirt Steak Romescu: Steak was nicely cooked, but very hard to cut, too chewy. The romescu didn't add that much and this kind of dish would have been better as a pinxto rather than a larger dish. Oxtail stuffed Piquillo: one of the better dishes. braised oxtail. nice flavor (more italian than spanish) but pretty greasy. Razor clams a la plancha: These rock. always good. Â they were very oily last night however. Â chill on the oil perhaps? Scallops: Â Basic. a bit too citrusy, smaller bay scallops. Unmemorable. Fried oysters: Nice pureed tomatos around it, absolutely fine. Heirloom Tomatoes: good, very good. but why are they on a spanish menu? oh and then the visiting anchovy-always a welcome guest, but seriously more like a flat stanley. Patatas Bravas: we like them crispy, dusted with paprika. These were wet, whole baby potatoes with tons of tomato sauce around them. Â I didn't "get it". So as i said, quality is still high, just you can get better spanish elsewhere.
Great gnocchi! Glad I tried this place. Pretty good food, dock a star because of service not being too attentive.

Limp and lacking flavor sums up this New York favorite. The ceaser salad had a teaspoon of dressing, so little that we sent it back. The croutons tasted like they were made sometime during the era of Marcus Arelius, stale and without a single bit of seasoning. The pizza? You can get ten times better for $1 a slice on any street corner. We took two bites and sent it back. After complaining to the manager, he said that he tried the croutons himself everyday, evidently he's a fan of stale 3,000 year old bread. And seriously guys, don't send out a bland pizza that tastes like a water-soaked cracker. Epic fail.

Came here for the first time last night and instantly liked the place. Very chill vibe, though I hear during the day it's parents and kids central so I won't be stopping in then. I liked it for two major reasons: 1) - It's open late. I was hungry at midnight on a Saturday night and Â there were only two restaurant options in this area that stay open past 11P: Bar Tabac and Bocca Lupo. Bocca Lupo is easier on the wallet. They offer their lunch menu at night so don't expect any special dishes. The lunch menu consists of mostly panini and bruschetta options, perfect for a midnight snack. 2) - Dessert panini. Bananas and chocolate grilled in a panini served with whipped cream is perfection. I also enjoyed the fresh mozzarella, tomato and basil pesto panini but it pales in comparison to the dessert one. They have an impressive drinks menu that I'll have to try next time. And there will definitely be a next time.
HANDS DOWN THE BEST PIZZA I'VE EVER HAD!!! 2 of my buddies went with and agreed best pizza ever... We went to 2 other pizza joints in Brooklyn, and they didn't even come close...

THE BEST PLACE FOR LATE NIGHT FALAFEL! I can't imagine going anywhere else at 3:30AM when I'm hanging out in the East Village. Lines can be long but certainly not at the fault of Mamoun's (thus no star reduction). Â Service is very fast considering and the food is great. Beware of the hot sauce! I'm a pretty spicy food tolerant person and I made the grave error of slathering my sandwich in their hot sauce (I think it's homemade?) I was dripping drool (mm yummy imagery, I know) and tearing up after a few bites. Â Had to scarf it down just to not endure the pain for any longer than I had to. Â WORTH IT. Will be back again and again until I need a sextuple bypass surgery to unclog my arteries from all the fried chickpeas stuck in my heart roads.

I came here last night for a private dinner holiday party. The decor is so relaxing but the place is literally the size of my living room. The staff there were awesome and very attentive. And chefs ! Kudos to all of them. Now the food - HALLELUJAH- ! I had the vegan 'Jerusalem Artichoke Soup' for a starter and the salmon with roasted Â cauliflower and leeks dill in buttermilk sauce for my main dish . My mouth is watering while writing this. I never had vegan anything in my life and that soup was on point! For desert I had a pumpkin spice with caramel glaze cake and a side of Breyers ice cream (yall ain't low with the Bryers ice cream) lolol Overall an excellent restaurant - definitely try it out!

We were a party of 10 that had a reservation on a Saturday night for my brother's birthday dinner. The restaurant was a home run for a birthday celebration. The food was very good, reasonable. The staff was attentive and friendly. The flamenico show was awesome. The dancers take themselves very seriously. They performed from 8:30- 11pm with breaks in between. Â At the end of their show, they sang happy birthday to my brother AND then they had him come onto the dance floor to dance with one of the female dancers. This was the highlight of our night.

Intimate atmosphere; a little cramped for a larger group (we were 6 in total), but would love to go back just as a couple. Â Bread and olive oil on the table were both phenomenal; appetizers we ordered (caprese salad and mista) were nothing special. Â Tomatoes were underripe. Â Main courses varied -- folks who chose pasta were happy with their dishes; I had the sirloin steak and asked for it medium well, and it was overcooked and dry. Â The flavor of the sauce, however, was wonderful, as was the cheese that came with it. Â Not a rave review, but I'd give it a second chance and see what else they have to offer.

Cheap. Â Freshly-made. Â Hunger-satisfying. Â Succulent. Â Warm. Â Delicious. I live a block from this place and it's one of the reasons why I love my apartment! Â I eat here AT LEAST 1-2 times a week and literally have to say, "No no no no no" when I pass it on my way home. Â It's the best food for the CHEAPEST price. Â Nothing costs more than $3. Â I don't even take the napkins, plastic utensils, or bag that they usually give out for take-out because I live so close!! Â So ridiculous!!! I personally like the boiled dumplings (they come in 8) than the fried (which comes in 4). Â Yum. Â And I always, ALWAYS get the sesame pancake peking duck. Â Best $2.25 I've ever spent. Â If you get any soups or dumplings in soup, you're order will take longer since they make the food on the spot!!!! Â  How does it work? Â You order at the back of the house (please know your order before you get to the cashier...they have menus that you can look at or a menu outside!!!), they give you a receipt with a number on it. Â Then, you move to the right and wait for your order. Â The staff is great but whooooo, those accents can make hearing your number a little rough, lol. Â THEY DON'T CALL OUT NUMBERS IN ORDER!!! Â So please, don't FREAK out when they call a number that's higher than yours. Â When your order is ready, they'll call your number. Â There's limited seating, so have someone watch a table and grab a seat!! Seriously, you have to try this place AT LEAST once!!!! Â It's right by the Grand St. stop for the B & D trains. Â There's also a location on 14th street. Â GO THERE!

I think this is the kind of place I'd enjoy a lot more on a slow weekday rather than Friday night. Â Not going to judge a place on its wait but I want to get that out there. Service was fine even though it was busy. Â More issue on the more or less plain food. Â I was told the shrimp was very good but the instant I saw it on the table I knew I wasn't going to have a good time with it. Â They were small, shriveled, and clearly overcooked. Â Maybe shrimp was just a bad choice in general because traditionally tapas are oftentimes collected from a huge batch of pre-prepared food. Â Then again, I wasn't doing all of the ordering. Â Most disappointing dish by far. Â Although the sauce it was in was great and that's why we kept on ordering bread. For the most part, each dish was relatively lackluster. Â I was most entertained by the sauces included in the pan con tomate (which is clearly overpriced for what it is). Â Lamb skewers were done well, nothing wrong with those. Â Chorizo was just regular chorizo, at least there was a lot of it. By far, it seems like the dishes with potato are the stars. Â The croquetas were very good. Â Nicely fried on both times we ordered the dish with a light, savory, and relatively subtle filling. Â The mashed potato on the outside was great but the creamy filling was even better. Â Then the patatas bravas.... holy crap amazing. Â They could have been crispier in general but each potato piece was soft and covered in a very delicious aioli sauce. Potatoes. Â Just get the potatoes and carb up. Â That way, you can drink as much sangria as you want.

we're so glad we stumbled upon this restaurant. The line is always out the dooe, and the restaurant has so many rave reviews from newspapers and food mags. Â This is one of the top 2 xiao long bao places to go to in nyc. We love how the pork soup dumplings skin is not too thin or too thick, and the meat is flavored really well. If you come with a small group of 2 or 3, the wait is usually not too long. Â We always order pork dumplings and this tofu dish with spinach and brown sauce. Yummmmm. now that we have a baby, we stopped going to joes shanghai. Â The space is vey crowded and you will most likely share a table with other people. Â But it's fun sharing tables. You get to see what others eat. :)
We went there to taste the beef brisket and it is to die for very tasty and soft even my husband who ate the brisket that I brought home stated it is awesome it is really worth the travel.

i decided to try something new because it was my friend's birthday and I wanted to take her out to dinner. I googled Japanese restaurants and this came up as something good, so I figured I'd give it a shot. it's quite small and it's easily confused with the place next door. it was very loud in there, which is okay for a casual atmosphere, but I could barely make out what my friend was saying and she was sitting right next to me at the bar. we were a little disappointed when we saw the menu prices in comparison to the size of the dishes on the tables surrounding us, as well as the photos in the menu. we received friendly and fairly quick service. pleasant surprise : my order was a lot larger in reality than it appeared, so i think it was worth it. my friend was a little less happy with what she had ordered but I think that was just due to the taste of the sauce, which she was not expecting at all. perhaps if we had both ordered something different, we would have been happier with our experience there. unfortunately this was just 'okay' for us. the prices really aren't that bad, especially since it's so close to times square, but for us, the quality of food just didn't match up. I would consider coming back care maybe just to try out something different on the menu in the hopes of having a better time, but I'm not expecting a lot if I do come back.
Picklebacks are amazing!! Best homemade pickle juice. Great atmosphere too!

As someone who is embarking upon the Paleo Lifestyle, this restaurant was a Goddess-Send! The food is awesome. You can find a wide assortment of dishes where ingredients match the paleo diet and that you're not taking in artificial additives. There is even a selection of wine that is paleo friendly if I remember right. Great spot near 14th Street Union Square.

Hot, authentic, amazing. What are you waiting for? Go get some. I was visiting Manhattan last week and had a chance to eat at Han Dynasty with my best friend. Here's a short, but hopefully helpful, review. The place was packed at 7:00 on a Sunday night. True, it was dinner time, but it seems Han Dynasty is seriously blowing up. I was quickly greeted by the host and told a two-top would be a 45 minute wait. He entered my cell number into his iPad, which immediately sent me a text indicating another would come when our table was ready. I grabbed a seat at the bar and downed a beer while I waited for my buddy to arrive. A few minutes after he arrived, another bar seat opened up, so we decided to dine at the bar. The bartender was super friendly and helpful. He made three recommendations for us - all dishes we could share - everything sounded good and we pulled the trigger. Here's what we ate: 1) Dan Dan noodles. Phenomenal. Probably my favorite dish. Slow build on the heat and perfectly cooked noodles with minced pork. 2) Spicy cucumber. Slices of cucumber swimming in a greasy, spicy bath of sauce. Usually, this dish is too 'thin' (for me) in terms of the sauce (many places serve it drenched in rice vinegar with some kind of hot pepper flakes). Made that way, it's a very refreshing side for a summer BBQ. However, the spicy cucumbers at Han Dynasty are prepared in thicker sauce that stands up to cold weather too. Simply delicious. In fact, I tried to make this dish when I returned home. Definitely not as good as at Han Dynasty! Â  Â  3) Chicken wings. A pile of healthy wings covered in Szechuan peppercorns. Pretty darn tasty, and spicy as all get out. Outstanding meal! I'm really stoked to get back!

The food is OK, but they get marked down to two stars because of their crappy service in the dining room. At $20 for a tiny entree, this place has got to step it up on the service front. I went there twice, and both times the service was totally weird (server repeatedly and aggressively pushing bar menu after being told my drink order, draping sleeve through my entree to grab water glass, refusing to move us to a booth in an empty restaurant only to seat a couple in one right next to us an hour later - grrr!). It seems like some of the 4 and 5-star reviews came out of the bar. Maybe that's the secret? If I DO go back, I'll stick with the folks in the front of the house!

I went here for my one year anniversary this weekend. The food was so fresh and awesome. Servings aren't huge, but they are filling. There is a wine for everyone and the mozzarella and fresh prosciutto appetizer is awesome. Def recommend !!
Excellent salad nicoise. Great atmosphere. Had a really good gluten free sandwich from the takeaway store as well. If I lived in bk heights id be here a lot.

I have had food from here a few times- both take out and dine in. The pho beef is unfortunately not too flavorful although hearty in size and generous in the beef helping. I had their clay pot fish and rice dish which I enjoyed.

by far the best tuna sandwich in the financial district......served on a warm thick pocketless pita with fresh lettuce and slivers of red onion. Â we collectively take out from there at least once a week. Â try it...you will not be disappointed
OMG best sushi in the world! I'm going back to NYC just for this place!!! Go and spread the good word! Fresh and moist!

Delicious barbeque, great beer selection. I had pork jowls here last night, and they were amazing. Definitely high-quality stuff, and I like how they rotate through some of the more off-the-run cuts of meat. You can buy beer by the gallon. The downside, as has been alluded to in many other reviews, is the extremely long lines and the awkward seating situation. You'd think they'd want more turnover, so there'd be an impetus to move less slowly at the front counter.

The burger was incredibly well crafted. All I the flavors worked together very well and left me both full and satisfied. Add in some delicious beer and incredibly fast service, and Umami Burger makes a strong showing for one if the best up and coming restaurants in Greenwich. Denizens of the area have got to eat here.

I saw the reviews and wanted to try something new. This is definitely a new favorite spot for me and my lady. The decor is really nice and has an upscale feel, but it's not pretentious. The owner was very nice and welcoming. He said they have only been open a month so he was still working on getting a credit card machine and liquor license. The food was amazing! If you like salt and fat, you won't be disappointed here. The menu seems to be mostly small plates with tons of quality and flavor. The ribs were fall off the bone and flavorful. The dishes have a touch of Asian spin on them. The complementary dessert was so good. I have never had anything like it. It was some kind of Italian custard (forget the name, but not canoli filling) infused with Jasmin extract. It was so good. I will be coming back more. This place is going to be packed in a few months from now when word gets out about it. Go now to avoid the wait.

The concept is simple. And that's why Pomme Frites in NY has had many many many successful years in business. Excell in one thing but do it not just good but GREAT. Pomme Frites serves Belgium French Fries. THAT'S IT. You get to choose from a plethora of sauces. If you want to enjoy your fries with a beer? Go next door. They'll let you bring the beer in Pomme Frites so you can hang. How rad is that? A lot of restaurants all over the world try to specialize in many things, resulting in a menu with too many items. You'll have people order some, some more than others. Do one thing and make it the best. That's my two cents. I commend you Pomme Frites.
This place deserves 6 stars. Applause.

We made a reservation for dinner on Christmas day back in November for our party of 6. The restaurant cancelled our reservation 2 days in advance (December 23rd) because they decided to close the place for the holidays all of a sudden. They probably didn't get enough reservations or something... They tried to reach us by phone, but my phone didn't work properly in the US. So we got a cancellation email from Open Table. It didn't really matter that they could't reach us by phone, as they were cancelling on us anyway. We were very dissapointed. Being Belgians ourselves, we were looking forward to having our Christmas dinner here...

Cheapie Chinese at it's finest! Wah Fung may not be the most cleanliest place but it's what you would expect in china town. This tiny store front always has a line. So be prepared to wait a little! It'sonly $3 for delicious roast Â BBQ pork, rice, and veggies. You get a huge portion packed into a small container. It's like a clown car trick, because it really is a ton of food! After waiting in the line you might be better off paying $5 and getting the roast pork and duck combo. But seriously, this roasted BBQ pork is caramelized to a juicy char, be cautious of the really fatty pieces. Try to come earlier in the day because if you come close to closing you'll end up with the scraps.

Hell yea! Ate here last night and everything was superb. From the service to the drinks and of course the arepas. Delicious. I personally eat meat and found the chicken and pork amazing! Went with some vegatarian friends and they were equally impressed. Definately going back!
The catfish sandwich is a win every time. Its also BYOB.

OMG my fantasy? Living near this place. WOW, the food was amazing! My friends and I barely talked through our meal because we were so busy devouring the food here! We got the spicy beef (super-seasoned and tasty), veggie momo (good, but the spicy sauce made the difference), the chicken glass noodles (mouthwatering), and chili dofu (tender and filled with flavor) and shared everything family-style. Our favorite? The bocha tea. Seriously, I want to put butter in my tea and drink it everywhere! This place was incredibly packed starting at 7:30 on Saturday so make sure to get there early. Also, it's BYOB -- how cool is that?!?!?! The service was good but a bit slow. The only reason why I'm docking off a star is because the dessert was a let-down. Okay, my friends got green tea ice cream and the lassi. Those were delicious. But I got the rice pudding and let's just say, the restaurant took it literally. It's rice (like the kind that came with our meal) topped with strange-tasting yogurt (kinda like the Greek kind you put on gyros) and with a few slices of strawberries. I kept taking more bites just to make sure they didn't actually give me white rice topped with nasty yogurt. What?!??! But they did. So I wouldn't recommend the rice pudding, unless they change it and make it sweet or use the sticky rice. Otherwise, we had a great time. Really good vibe, nice people and hot, sizzling, tasty food and tea. What more could you ask for?
Pretty damn good. The bread basket is amazing

This place has actually really decent Vietnamese food especially since the style is very catered to the American population. Â Usually those kind of restaurants are a hit or miss and often miss, but this one actually hit the spot. Â  The service was kind of aloof and they didn't take cash, the place may have a chic Americanized Â look but it doesn't get more Vietnamese than that! :) Â  I ordered the Bun Thit Nuong. Â The meat was well cooked and had the charring taste that gives the authenticity of the word "nuong" (to grill). Â The pickled veggies were on par and not too sweet nor salty. Â The vermicelli was a good helping that wasn't too much nor too little. Â  Overall, good place to eat and a good find in the heart of Greenwich Village.
solid Peruvian food. I still missing the other option on 9th Ave Farmer's rotisserie, which I used to order from all the time, so Pio Pio has to now fulfill my craving.

This is my favorite Turkish place. I just joined yelp so I'm writing reviews of all of my favorite restaurants first. This is near the top of the list. The food is awesome and I love the small dishes, like a tapas place. It has the appropriate ambiance for a date also. The only thing that annoys me is that it closes way too early.

Really delicious! The first time I came here, I got an overly oily quinoa dish that almost turned me off completely to this place. After a few times back, I am glad to say I have changed my mind, because it's great! The people are really friendly and cool and the service is generally really good. My favorite thing there, Tempeh Wings, has been on the specials board for a while and I hope it enters as a permanent menu item. The Buffalo Tempeh "Wings" ($8) are probably one of my favorite appetizer type dishes of all time. Lightly breaded and fried tempeh with a coating of delicious buffalo sauce, served with a cool and creamy dressing, carrots, and celery. Such a refreshing departure from thawed may wah wings. These are hearty and wholesome in a way those drumsticks could never be. More please! Can't wait to explore more of their menu :) EDIT: Buffalo Tempeh is now a regular menu item! Thanks Champs!!!

Oh, how ordering off the menu was a huge mistake. I first came here years ago and remember not really liking the place since I ordered straight off the menu. Fast forward to today, the specials are amazing. Just remember, the waiter will shock you with the number of items from the specials, don't be dissuaded. Listen, I took notes, and order straight from the specials. If you forgot something, they will be more than happy to refresh your memory. The specials range from apps, salads, pastas, meats and seafood. The service was also top notch, it was very professional, efficient and attentive. They also change your plates and utensils after every app. They also, individually split the apps for you, so you don't have to fight over the food. I say this is one of my fav Italian restaurants. The food: Burratina- it's burrata, which is a mozzarella variant, and prosciutto. This was so freakin good. I think this was the fav of the night. Wild Meatballs- there were three different types of meatballs on the specials menu from reg, veg meatballs to wild game. We opted for the wild game. It was served with mushrooms and truffle oil. I thought this dish was nice, but the gaminess might be off putting for some, but not me. Gnocchi Duetto- it's Gnocchi served with crumbled sausage, mascarpone and Gorgonzola. This dish is not the most exciting, but the flavors were great. The Gnocchi was like "little pillows" and the sauce had the perfect consistency. I really liked this dish, but the flavors do get repetitive. Pork Osso Bucco- served with Gnocchi with a tomato sauce. I thought this dish was good but was expecting the pork to be more unctuous. The Gnocchi was nice and light. Fettuccine- served with crumbled sausage, sundried zucchini with a touch of pesto. This dish was a very grandmotherly dish, it didn't scream fine dining but it was such a comforting dish. I thought the pasta was cooked perfectly and the sausage and zucchini paired well. Lobster Ravioli- raviolis filled with lobster meat surrounded by lobster bisque. The flavors of the dish were nice. The flavors were a littlle too one note, but definitely a solid dish. Riccota Cheesecake- this was the only thing on the menu I wasn't crazy about. I wasn't a fan of the texture of the cheesecake and it seemed kinda dry.

When I am away at school I dream about L&B square slices. I have been coming here since I was a kid and it is one of my favorite pizza places in NY. Love sitting outside in the summer or simply taking a pie to go. Don't forget the spumoni ice for dessert! And to be clear, a spumoni ice is not just an ice from Spumoni Gardens. SPUMONI is an actual FLAVOR of ice (it's a mix between pistachio, chocolate and an almond tasting flavor, cremalata, which I don't know how to spell). Seems like someone below was confused about the ices.

the ceiling wit the clay pots is a nice unique touch to the place. the food was absolutely delish. we ordered the greek salad, along with the meatballs for appetizer and omg, so amazingly good! I got the lamb shank. it was tender, moist and well seasoned. the service is on point! great date spot and for groups, nice place to catch up. it gets super busy so make sure to make reservations!

Absolutely loved the atmosphere. The light buzz of conversation, along with the live jazz is very relaxing. The service was great, as was the food. I loved the shrimp dish I ordered, and their artichoke dip is the best I've had thus far. Dim lighting makes it very romantic, very personal. I would recommend to couples simply looking for a good night and great food in the city.
Great food. Some things are a little pricey

Artichoke Pizza Noms. A haiku sequence by sixgirlsonebathroom.com drunk at 4AM ate 2 bags micro' popcorn not yet satisfied craving for pizza we stumble to Artichoke million person line i'm drunk and hungry! impatient bros cut in line have u no manners? maybs a nicer bro could hit on me; get dessert with their pizza, wink buy a slice, walk home it's the size of Rhode Island i swallow it all wake up in the night food baby tries to escape did i eat a brick? Sunday morn, i wake barely fit into sweatpants whatevs, i'm single

This is my new favorite place in Chinatown! Â The Serious Eats article was spot on when it comes to this place - the dumplings are OUT OF THIS WORLD! Â They are juicy, full of meat and taste very fresh. Â I ordered the shrimp wonton, shrimp dumpling and cilantro and black egg dumpling soup (that was one dish!). Â This was also the PERFECT SIZE - one of the only times I've eaten in Chinatown and didn't need to be rolled out! Â  newyork.seriouseats.com/â€¦

There's something about the vibe here that feels so cozy and relaxing, I could even see myself as a regular when/if I ever move to Williamsburg. Perhaps its the dim lighting and attractive old-fashioned decor. Â I really love the fact that Brooklyn has good food at unpretentious prices and this place really fits the bill. Â For appetizers, I had a potato leek soup and steak tartar, both of which were really tasty. Â The tartar is seasoned with pepper, wasabi and topped with a raw quail egg. Â I also shared the wild mushroom risotto and a special salmon pasta of the day. Â The risotto was cooked perfectly and full of truffle flavor. Â The only downside was that the pasta was a bit salty for my taste. Â They also serve absinthe drips, which is basically 2oz of absinthe put through some sort of device where water drips through a tube onto a sugar cube to dilute and sweeten the liqueur. Â I did order one to try and really disliked the licorice taste. Â Overall, I'd come back again for dinner and brunch.
Authentic Chinese food very similar to what I had in china Try the spicy cumin lamb noodles with the tiger vegetables salad

I would actually like to contest the "don't get anything here except for the xiaolongbao" notion that a few of my fellow yelpers seem to be insistent on; I also ordered the scallion pancakes and the braised sliced beef as appetizers, and both turned out delectably as well. As for the XLBs, they're really a no brainer. If you come here after reading all the yelp reviews before this one and not get the XLB, it's like going to Katz Deli and ordering a hot dog. Or going to Spumoni's and asking for a hamburger. Definitely going to be coming back here anytime I have a burning desire to scorch the inside of my mouth.

Delicious Surprise! Â I live in the neighborhood's was hoping, praying for Anella to be good, and it was great! Â I can't wait to go back with friends. Â Loved the fresh food, and inquired, and found out a lot of it was locally grown. Â My only issue was the portions were HUGE, and the restaurant was not crowded hopefully if word gets out it will be a little bit more happening...ambiance-wise.

My second visit to do or dine really made an impression on me. Starting at the bar... the cocktail and wine list is short, but sweet (and good). The E666S tempura fried and served with bacon and culantro really made for a fantastic appetize! I want to know where they source culantro in NYC (I never see it at any Pho places around at all!!). I also liked the inventive Gyoza nachos, substituting (or upgrading) to gyoza instead of chips. Yes! The lamb breast, very flavorful and cooked to perfection. Very happy with the steak tartare with a unique garlicky twist and a quail egg on top. The presentation for the fish and chips was very nice too... A whole porgy fried and served on top of pub chips with a yuzu sauce! Too bad they don't take Amex :/

I'm a pretty hypocritical vegetarian lately. Â Tonight marks the 3rd night this week that I've consumed some type of meat. Â And we're not talking chicken, kids. Â It all started with a Chipotle carnitas burrito. Â It wasn't mine, but I stole a few bites (hey, their meat is organic, vegetarian fed, and free range). Â Next, I hit up the Red Hook Ballfields and one can hardly attempt to judge quality Mexican food without trying the meat (spicy pork huarache AND a chorizo taco, both quite fabulous thank you very much). Â  And tonight, my first five star meal in awhile, and at $20, tax and tip included! Â I love when a restaurant lives up to the hype, and while I only tried two dishes at Momofuku Ssam this evening, it was everything I dreamed it would be. Â First, the fried cauliflower (brussel sprouts aren't on the seasonal menu yet): crisp outside, moist inside, and salty! Â And then came the Ssam. Â No presentation here, just an empty plate with two tinfoil wrapped halves, resembling a Mission style burrito. Â (While I constantly lament the dearth of SF Mission style burritos in NY, the Ssam just might make up for it.) Â Packed with dripping pulled pork shoulder, this little bundle of joy was like a juicier carnitas burrito, the pickled mushrooms and kimchee distinguishing it from anything you might find in Mexico. Â I ate a bite, and another and another. Â Then I paced myself, determined only to eat half. Â I even succeeded temporarily, wrapping the 2nd half with the remaining tinfoil and taking it to go. Â I made it through the subway ride home without peeking in the take-away bag. Â But upon entering my apartment, when I awoke my sleeping boyfriend to share my gift, he sleepily and unwittingly turned my offering down and, unable to let it sit another day, I devoured the other half. Â  Now I'm full, and I'll have to drag myself from bed to hit the gym at 6:30 am tomorrow, as well as atone for my sins of the flesh (literally... get it?!), but it was all worth it.

If I could give zero stars I would. Refused to seat me until my friend arrived, which I could understand if it were moderately busy. However, this place is literally EMPTY- save for one table of three in a corner. Really? Get over yourselves. Ridiculous.

This place is all types of amazing! Really chilled spot in bed-stuy. A bit on the tiny side but that's pretty typical in NYC and the food makes up for it. Love their hot fried chicken which ranges from regular for the non spice lovers, hot for the ones who like a little kick and extra hot for the brave. As for sides, I always get the grilled asparagus or the bacon potato salad and I've never been disappointed. They also have an amazing happy hour with a nice selection of cocktails for $5!! Oh, you must try their french toast if you go for brunch. So good it makes you want to do a happy dance! Love the HotHouse! It's one of those places you can go to alone and have a meal by yourself- just sit at the bar and chat it up with your neighbor! Definitely one of my faves.

We were in NYC for spring break last week. Â Seven of us dined here last Thursday. Â Most people ordered the Lomo Saltado and I had the Camarones Cuzco. Â It was all excellent! Â One of the best meals that we had while we were there. Â  The filet in the Lomo Saltado was very tender and the sauce was perfectly complementary - not overwhelming. Â The same was for my shrimp entree (Camarones Cuzco). We had a reservation and we were seated immediately. Â The service was great - we had no complaints. Â My preteen boys both had the Lomo Saltado and each loved their meal. I will now have to find a new Peruvian restaurant at home because the ones I currently frequent will pale in comparison!

Oh. My. God. I am usually a fairly neat eater, not easily impressed by food, and highly unlikely to rave about a sandwich. But you couldn't tell it by the way I ate my Spicy Classic Bahn Mi at Hanco's this week. Ground pork, ham, a cucumber, and julienned carrots with daikon radishes combine with pate on a toasted baguette for an explosion of flavor. One of the best sandwiches I've ever tasted. There was a fair amount of srirarcha around, so I assume it is what was responsible for the spice. Extra points for using my favorite hot sauce. Although the coconut bubble was good enough, I disliked the notes of lavender. Pure coconut milk would have been perfect (and a little less sweet). I came just before the dinner rush, and grabbed one of the last tables in this 15 seater restaurant. Be warned: if you sit outside, you might be asked to move off the basement stairs. Amazing pork foodgasm= more visits to Hanco's.

Aw man, this place is so legit. Â It's hard to make a place on St. Mark's when there are literally 80 top-notch NYC eateries, but this place holds its own. Â  - Banh Mi TACOS. Â Holy crap. Â So good! Â All three kinds! - Basil lime fizz drink. Â Don't ask questions and get it. Not too sweet, just perfect. - You don't know what head cheese is? Â Don't ask and don't worry about it. Â Just eat it. Â If you're lactose intolerant, PERFECT, bc it has nothing to do with actual cheese. The staff is awesome. Â The prices are amazing. Â Everything is fresh. Â Their proud of their product.

Went with my family prior to a play. Everything was good food wise but I hate the idea of waiting for everyone till we can sit down. I was hungry! I could of ordered something prior to my dad being very late to the resteraunt. Otherwise, they will get you in and out in time for your show and you will be very full to boot.

WILLING TO FLY ACROSS THE COUNTRY FOR ANOTHER BITE OF THE PORK BELLY BUNS!!! They are seriously that amazing. Â The porkbelly literally melts in your mouth. Â The ramen is amazing too.. I didn't get the one that was recommended by yelpers but I absolutely loved mine, Karaka miso ramen! I LOVE LOVE LOVE THIS PLACE!!!! BEST RAMEN EVER!!!!!!!! so in love

Everything there is good. Â Everything. Great vegetarian options (beans, spinach, tofu, seitan, portobello), but for the most part I'm in love with the chicken ranchero and the steak. Â The nachos will throw a wrench into your digestive system thanks to copious cheese sauce, but they are SO. WORTH. IT. Â Just be sure to get the sauce on the side for takeout so the chips don't get soggy. Hooray for Boylan's and Jarritos selections.

I'm lucky we had a bunch of people so we could try a wide variety of things. Here is the break down. 3.5 stars but I'll round it up to 4. - Sizzling Sisig : 5* It's a bunch of "undesirable" parts grilled in a sizzling plate. They also have calamansi in here, and egg. It comes with a side of garlic rice. The price is pretty hefty at $16, but it was one of the best sisigs I've had. The flavor is very good and the added egg is a good touch. - Arroz Caldo: 3* A small porridge starter with ginger and garlic, with saffron. We added an egg in this. While it was pretty good, it tasted like something you could make at home or something you could get at a Chinese place for $4. Unless you are really craving some porridge, I wouldn't recommend it. - Fried chicken and Ube waffle: 4* The ube waffle is soooo good. Ube is a type of fruit that I've personally seen only in filipino cooking. I've never had that flavor before, and it is very very good. However, the chicken is kind of underwhelming. They do a batter-less fried chicken. The portion of the meat is a bit skimpy and the flavor is so so. Also kind of pricy for what it is at $17. - Silog breakfast - You choose the protein and it comes with garlic rice, egg, and pickled cucumbers and tomato. We tried both the tapsilog(beef tapa) and the tocilog(tocino, cured pork). Both had great flavors but i preferred the beef. The tocino had the better flavor, but the meat was pretty dry. Overall I felt like the price was a bit high for what was offered, but still good nonetheless.

I went here for my coworker's birthday. Â there were 10 of us. Â some of us had pre-fix and some of us had a la carte. Â I had a a la carte dish of lobster salad. Â They gave me half a lobster on top of a huge salad with grilled shrimps. Â I tried the mac and cheese and lobster risotto from other people's dishes, and they were all excellent. Â we ordered two pitchers of white wine sangria, which had a bunch of pear and mangos inside. Â It was a really good combination of refreshing and sweetness. Â They let us stay on as long as we wanted, and everyone was too full to have coffee later on.

If this kitchen is ugly, I don't want to know what pretty is! A friend was visiting from Boston and wanted to get the gang together and go out for some dinner and drinks. I wanted to pick a place that took reservations for large groups and had a good vibe for drinking. I made ressies on OpenTable for Ugly Kitchen for 14 people. We got there with plenty of time left for Happy Hour because it ends at 9pm! I ordered the cucumber peach martini and the ginger mint mojito. The cucumber peach martini was super refreshing, but the ginger mint mojito legit tasted like ginger ale! Loved both of my drinks. I checked in on Yelp and got free dumplings. They were just okay though. Kinda tasted like fried wonton wrappers with some peppers and cheese in them. We also ordered the spicy pork buns, fried shrimp and calamari appetizers. The spicy pork buns tasted like sloppy joes! I don't think they were the traditional ones because it was definitely more like ground up meat. Still very tasty, but I was expecting a hunk of pork. The calamari is a pretty small portion and I actually didn't get to try any of it. Fried shrimp was standard - tasted like coconut shrimp. For the entree, I ordered the pork belly while my friends ordered the pork sandwich, perilla cream pasta and grilled chicken. The pork belly is delish - fatty and meaty. A good portion size as well. The pork sandwich came with some amazingly spiced fries and the grilled chicken was flavorful and juicy. I thought the pasta was just okay though, I'd recommend getting all three of the other dishes before getting the pasta. Great service, great good, cheap drinks...annnddd FREE SHOTS! Would definitely recommend coming with a group of friends and getting your eat/drank on! ;)
