Â I love love love carmines but will NOT return on a Sunday!

I'm a sucker for fried chicken, and a sucker for pie, but having the two together as both the signature dishes sounds mind blowing so I had to try it. Expect a wait, especially on a saturday, but the it was less than 20min. The place is small and crowded, typical for ny standards, but the weather was nice enough that we sat in the back where they had outdoor seating. I ordered the fried chicken box, and my friend had the chicken and waffles. The chicken was hot, crispy and the seasoning was good, but didn't expect the biscuit too be AMAZING. I would say the best I ever had so far. My friend thought her dish, chicken and waffles, were okay, the waffle was too thick, and the syrup or sauce was kinda weird. As for the pie, our first choice (which I can't remember) was sold out so we settled for an apple pie. I was kinda disappointed, I can't say it was bad, but it was nothing special. If they could somehow incorporate their biscuits into the pie menu (like cobblers) that would be great. If I was in the mood for fried chicken (I always am) and in the area, I would stop by.
Cool place, big portions, good choice of meat, fresh veggies, hummus is yummmm! Good spot to stop by for lunch.

This place is great! If you want to wait 3 hours for OK pancakes, that is. Clinton St., as great as their food is, is another one of those incredibly overhyped places that draws in lots and lots of tourists who've watched the Food Network. In order to see what the big deal was, I headed over on a weekday for brunch, assuming we'd wait a little less, and boy, was I wrong. I ended up waiting about 3 hours and 10 minutes, I think, and just like Ippudo, the wait here made me want to start eating my own hair. Once we finally got our table, I didn't even need to look at the menu. The only thing on my mind were the ever-so-famous blueberry pancakes, which I ordered right away. But the service was disappointingly slow, as if we needed to wait longer after finally being seated, and once the pancakes came, I was officially ridiculously starving, to the point that I couldn't even tell if I was still hungry. I finally dug into my fluffy, beautiful pancakes, and yes, they were really delicious, and I scarfed them down instantaneously. BUT, they weren't so delicious that I would go through the entire experience again. At $14 a pop, I think these pancakes are, albeit really good, way overpriced and overhyped -- the insane wait and price just aren't worth it. I would much rather go to Union Sq. Cafe and have their pancakes (I actually think theirs are better) or even just make some myself. One more thing to note: The warm maple butter, as everyone on here has said, was really good, but they only gave me a tiny ramekin of it, and when I asked for more, they said they'd charge me $2. WTH? I'm already paying $14 for the pancakes, and you can't spare me another puny ramekin of your maple butter? It's not like I'm asking for an entire bowl of it, damn. If you're up for waiting to the point where you've forgotten your state of hunger, by all means, go for the blueberry pancakes. If not, but you still want to get a taste of Clinton St., get one of the pastries on their counter. They have great scones, and you don't have to wait at all. If you don't even want a taste of this tourist-infested place, it's OK. You'll find plenty of other places for pancakes.
Eaten here a few times ...... The pie is solid. Good old school atmosphere. Try the margherita.

It's not bad, but I prefer toki underground in DC or even daikaya better. Got their spicy ramen and it was decent. There was a bit of a wait but it was nice out and they had a little bench to sit on. Also got their pork bun and it was ok. Still love my pork belly buns better but not bad for what it is. Probably wouldn't get their bun again. Decor is very lackluster and the location is somewhat in a neighborhood setting. Overall, this place will satisfy your ramen kick if that's what you need!

Williamsburg was in need for a great felafel place . Thanks to Kabob Shack it has arrived. Â They make the most delicious felafels in town., but it doesn't stop there. The food is always Â made fresh. Â They have good homemade Â fries with special dipping sauces. Â that are absolutely addictive. Â The Pita sandwiches both chicken and Beef are also good. Â If that isn't enough, Â your food is prepared by Â friendly staff. The atmosphere is small and relaxing. Â The prices are so reasonable. Â  Any dish is under $10. Â The Felafels are $3. Â  They stay open late for the weekend crowd looking for a great snack. They also support Â local artist. Â I'm please to have this new gem in my neighborhood.

If I really wanted to consider the service here, I would have given them a lower rating but the dumplings are so good I let them slide on this one. Â Anyone with any expectation of real customer service from any Asian restaurant in NY or any large city for that matter is delusional. Â So just get over it and get used to it. Â Eat the food and keep your whining to yourself. Â Of course I wish this wasn't the case for the majority of the restaurants but it's reality so moving on to the food... The dumplings are a hundred times better than anything I can get here in Dallas, I know I know, it's freaking Texas, but perhaps my standards have been lowered by years of consuming sub par Asian food at the hands of Americanized Asians forced to alter their menus to appease the timid and bland taste buds of those so called adventurous eaters here down south. Â  We ordered the soup dumplings and a side of stir fried snow pea leaves both were excellent and left me feeling quite proud of myself as I can still manage to identify good Asian food. Â The filling in the dumpling was delicious, I could sit there for hours and eat one after another. Â That would not be a bad idea if it were not for the other strangers sitting at your table gazing at you while you dine. Â If you can look past the long lines, the rude and impatient wait staff then expect to find some good eats in what are their famous soup dumplings.

The view sandwiches were ok, I had the bulgolgi topped with an egg. Not bad, but not amazing. Â However...I fell in love with the kimchi fries. They are soooo good. If you guys do decide to order it...make sure to top it off with am egg.

So fast you will not comprehend how a sandwich was assembled, in under 3 seconds, before your very eyes. Good, too. We shared the hummus and the falafel sandwiches--great to enjoy while sitting in Washington Sq Park. Only complaint? We really just wished we could meld the two sandwiches together--the fillings definitely would have complemented each other nicely.

If you are like me-love brunch, eat a lot, but hate feeling grossed out after finishing your food because it's too heavy-Grey Dog is perfect for you. Went there for brunch on Sunday with two girl friends. We ordered Egg Sandwich on a Croissant, #5 Michigan Sandwiches: Herb Goat Cheese & Avocado on toast with Walnut Pesto, Celery, & Arugula, and Baked Oatmeal. We shared everything. The bread of the Michigan Sandwich was perfectly toasted: warm and crunchy outside, but still soft and "tender" enough for chewing- not too hard or dry at all. Arugula and avocado were both very fresh and juicy. Walnut Pesto and goat cheese were lightly distributed between the bread, adding great flavor without overshadowing other ingredients. I love the celery touch, and the dry cranberries tucked in the toast - def made the taste and the texture of the sandwich more complex and sophisticated. Overall, every piece of the sandwich was very well balanced. I got my egg sandwich without cheese, just out of curiosity. The end result totally exceeded my expectations. The absence of cheese actually helped me appreciate the subtle flavor of the eggs and the croissant more. Although I usually prefer running egg yolk since I hate overcooked dry eggs, I liked the eggs on my sandwich. They were solid, but somehow still kinda moisture. The amount of salt and pepper def hit the sweet spot. The croissant did not taste oily at all (maybe cuz we didn't add any cheese). It was soft and chewy. The sweet/buttery smell and taste together with its perfect temperate totally boosted the umami taste of the eggs. We ordered our oatmeal with brown sugar on the side - simple, but hearty and good. It also rinsed away the heavy taste (if any) from other food. Although the portion was huge, we still finished everything and left the cozy cafe satisfied. P.S. The guy sitting next to us was super nice, AND looked a lot like Matthew Morrison - pleasant "next-table bruch buddy" to have *wink wink :P
Best meal I've I had in the last 6 months! please open one in L.A.!!!

This is my newest best tapas bar in in NYC. Â As a DC resident, Â the food and service at Tia Pol was better than Jaleos, the famous DC tapas bar/restaurant owned by spanish chef Jose Andres. Thank you, Yelp, for the recommendation. Â  We just got into NYC on Thursday and staying in Midtown. Â Not our first time to NYC. Â We are usually are in the city for business (day-trip) and never get an opportunity to enjoy the city. Â Not this time. Â Anyway, it's Thursday, checked-in late to Hotel and we're hungry. Â Midtown was not in the cards for me. Â So, we Yelp for tapas bar and Tia Pol is number 2 on search hit. Â Read the reviews and decided to make the visit. After exiting the subway and walking down 10th, we almost passed the bar. Â The entry door is innocuous. Â Inside, the restaurant is about as big as a shotgun shack. Â But the closeness lends to the ambiance. Â This also means that on the busiest of nights, the wait for a table can last as long as 30 minutes, which was our quoted wait time. Â We made a command decision to have a drink and wait. After about 15 minutes, we got lucky and got a seats at the bar which may have made this visit, Â the best encounter for us. Â There we met Steve, the young and handsome bartender whom my wife considered quite cute. Â Even I agreed with her that he was cute. Â He was also friendly, outgoing and as women say..."easy on the eyes." Â I bet that helps with tips. Â  We met Zaida, a vivacious greeter and hostess. Â Upon first sight, she reminded me of Rachel Ray but slimmer and cuter with a beaming smile much bigger than her famous doppelgÃ¤nger. Â  The manager, whose name I forget (apologies) finally broke down later in the evening and gave us a beautiful smile which we had been working on attaining while we were there. The food was superb. Â We had the pan con tomate which is a staple of all tapas bars. Â However, the delivery was unlike any I had experienced. Â Not only was it a decent pan con tomate, it came with a small dish of escalivada (one of my favorites), a fava bean puree, and a third dish of salsa dish which I can't recall the name. The patatas bravas was the best patatas brava I have had in while. Â Perfectly prepared with a crunchy exterior and soft creamy interior. Â I recommend this dish anyone. Â  We had the falda de rez, one of the daily specials that evening. Â A nicely grilled skirt stake, medium rare, on a bed of white beans and spinach. Â Again, another dish well done and prepared in a manner that exhibited attention to quality. Â  We also had the pinchos morunos, lamb on skewer, which was we also concluded was quite good. Other dishes we had included: paquetitos de jamÃ³n, artichoke and manchego wrapped in serrano ham; crema de hÃ­gado de pollo, a creamy chicken liver mousse; and oreja, pig ears (which my wife would have no part of!). We had a pitcher of sangria with our meal which was more than enough for the two of us. Â While I considered the sangria a good basic sangria, I would have expected more fruit variety in it along with the green apples. Â I recommend adding some season fruit varieties to give just a little bit of heft. Overall, we had a great experience. Â Good Service, great food, makes for a wonderful evening. Â  Definitely plan to go back on next visit to NYC. Thanks Steve, Zaida and Manager! Â C u next time we are NYC.

Had it TWICE during my week long visit to Manhattan over Spring Break. As I was exhausted and starving after walking for about 80 blocks that day (mind y'all, I'm from SoCal, so the longest distance I've walked was probably a shopping trip at the mall), I felt like I was being rescued when I smelled the aroma from this place 3 blocks away. I didn't know if it's any good, but seeing that it had a long line, I decided to wait in line and order whatever the person in front of me does. I wasn't especially impressed with the food when I had it (I was probably way too tried from the day) but it was surely satisfying. Â Little did I know that I was already being cast under their spell as I could not get my mind off that plate of rice and lamb afterwards. I was staying at the Hilton which was right across the street so every time I walked by the cart, my foot just drove my body to the end of the line and waited there for another plate of goodness. I miss you, and I can't wait to go back and have it again.
Yup, the dinner buffet was delicious and Cheap! Love it.

Lovely, inviting cafÃ©, fresh pastries and good coffee! Also this place has prices that are low, it leaves you kicking yourself for paying $6 for that subpar bagel sandwich at the deli down the street. Ordered some pastries and coffee for my family before flying out of NY and was so glad it was across the hotel we were staying at. We ordered a drip coffee, lattÃ©, Argentinia Empanada, Blueberry and 7 grain muffin, Caprese and Turkey/ Cheese mini sandwich and two Guava and cheese Chaussons. The lattÃ© was brewed well, lovely lattÃ© art too. The Caprese sandwich was decent, Blueberry muffin was soft, moist with hints of Cinnamon. The winner was the guava and cheese pastry that was warm, flakey and sweet. All tasted fantastic with the coffee. Each pastry was warmed up-optionally of course, the coffee was good and strong and the service was quick, friendly. Such a great environment to sit around to lounge in and sip coffee, it's clean and designed similarly to Shake Shack ( black, wood grain, lights ). Great prices for good quality, a must and definitely better than most of the shops on the street without the upped touristy prices.

Verlaine has a cozy atmosphere which I just love. It gets really crowded as it gets later, but if you already have a good spot then it does not matter. Â Unless you leave, then there is no way your going to get your seat back. Â  Service was great and the bartenders were very attentive. Â Always asking if I want another drink when I was finished with mine even when the place was packed. Â  Overall I would definitely come back here, the lychee martini is good!

Pies N Thighs catered my wedding in January. They were great to work with and we had a wonderful experience. They were responsive to us from the first time we contacted them--immediately scheduling a tasting for us at the restaurant. Their catering manager was really great and we felt that she really wanted to work with us. She was great about coordinating all of the MANY details of the wedding and everything went off without a hitch. Several people told us that this was the best wedding food they'd ever had. My husband is from Texas and requested that they cut the meat in a different way to make it more like what they serve at home. Anyone considering using them as a caterer should know that the catering menu does offer quite a few options that are not on the normal menu--and that are a bit more elegant. We also wanted to have plenty of vegetarian options and this was not a problem at all--we had loads of choices.

Amazing food. I ordered Huevos Ransheros ... Normally you get unlucky in NYC ordering something like that. But it was delicious...then the blueberry pancakes was a great finale for the experience. This place is a 5 star.
Great food, great service, HUGE servings! The Fritti Zucchini and the Penne ala Vodka with Mushrooms are superb!
Wow, delicious. Rich, thick broth. Best ramen I've had in the city.

Mediocre but affordable Italian food. Â All family style dishes. Â Pasta was all undercooked and the meats were unimpressive. I thought NYC was supposed to have good Italian food? Â All 3 desserts I tried were awful. Â Tourist trap, pass!

Lovely location.I came here with a friend during the happy hour. We stumbled across it when our original happy hour location was too packed and noisy. Happy hour is M-F 5-7 pm. Really good drinks and awesome Â mac & cheese. I definitely recommend this place to everyone! It does get a little noisy & packed when the dinner crowd hits the restaurtant - If you are going here for dinner, see if its possible to make a reservation- Â the line is longggg

I took a bite.. and I swear, I think I was pregnant. Thankfully that was not the end result but I swear the day I do get a bun in the oven, I will remember Artichoke Pizza. I will name my first son after you. Thank you

I tried the spicy beef noodle soup, pork bone noodle soup, and the dumplings. The dumplings were really tasty and great. Well worth the 3 bucks for a large helping. The spicy beef soup was great. The noodles were firm and pretty delicious, though I didn't like the beef too much. It was a bit tough.\ The pork bone soup came recommended by a Fujianese friend, but I didn't like it too much. It tasted a bit bland, and the noodles were not as great as they were in the beef soup. Overall, this is a nice cheap place with good tasting food -- except maybe the pork bone soup.

Treat yourself to an ohhhhh-so-delicious lobster roll! Â Especially on a nice day- you can take out and eat on a bench across the street. Â These lobster rolls are perfect and addicting! Â  Lots of fresh lobster meat, savory buttery yet crispy bread, and most importantly- light on the mayo. Â  Two words to describe my lunch at Luke's: perfection. addiction.

I love this place. When we lived in the east village we'd make a point to go here once a month because it's awesome. The tapas are fantastic, as others have commented the potatas bravas are great. Everything is really good though, great menu and consistently tasty. I enjoy the sangria, they also have a great beer selection on tap (my husband prefers beer). They give you a buzzer so you never have to wait and can have drinks at bars across the street etc. Overall, my favorite tapas place in Manhattan not only for the food but the service as well.

If you are looking for a upbeat, energetic place to eat great comfort food with creative twists this is the place to eat! Perfect for a person who misses the American food their Mom used to make. Also perfect if you want to be part of a young scene.

Absolutely 4 stars. Â Cash only, great little joint. Â It's tight, so don't expect to come here for comfort, but do expect to come here for some great food. Â  I'm embarrassed to admit that I've not tried anything else on their menu but the pulled pork sandwich. Â Each time I go and try and order something else, I get sucked back into the amazing flavors of this damned pulled pork sandwich! Â The sauce is to die for - I can't help but order it each time. Eventually I'll venture onto new items on the menu. Â Everything here looks so good, and from what I know already, I'm sure it absolutely is.

If you want to know how good a restaurant is, order their simplest dish - it should tell you everything. That said, I ordered the spaghetti and it was the best spaghetti I've had outside of Italy. Service was amazing, the girls were super sweet and were able to answer any questions we had about the wine. The place is quite cramped though. I noticed a few reviews calling it "cozy" which is very generous of them. Its roughly the size of a small studio apartment and that on top of the communal tables makes you feel like you're on top of the other patrons. but after a few minutes you get over it because everything else makes up for it

Chicken pancetta pizza with pecan pesto and fresh mozzarella was delicious! The evolution salad was also fresh and full of flavor. Such a lovely space for big groups, intimate dining, or even a private party. Good beer selection too. Can't wait to get it again!

4.5: The pork buns are delectable. The fatty, slightly smoky & sweet, ultra savory sauce on these thick cut slabs of pork belly (Bacon is the thin cut version). The meat is enveloped between a pillowy white Asian bun, with a dab of mayo and a lettuce leaf for some crisp to complement the soft, saucy textures. A couple times, they've disappointed because they were rather dry. This has never happened on busy nights and weekends because the turn over is higher...but the wait can be dreadful. The ramen is hearty and fatty and salty and delicious. Better than any I've had in Manhattan. The MSG will make you want to nap afterwards.

Until very recently, Gaia has been my white whale. I've heard the ravest of reviews, but never seemed to be able to enjoy it myself - they're closed on Sundays, don't allow takeout during the weekend, close fairly early, and are packed on a regular basis. On my first visit with the Boy, we splurged with Potatoes and Meatballs in Tomato Sauce, 2 Militare, 2 Milanese, and a ravioli dish (that now escapes my shoddy memory). The woman behind the counter scoffed, saying we'll die after consuming all the food. Little did she know she was dealing with someone who has a black hole for a mouth. The food is fresh, delicious, and reminiscent of home-cooked, family-enjoyed meals (wait a minute, my family isn't Italian...). The menu is slightly confusing - no clear distinction between apps and entrees, and only paninis are marked. Overall, huge fan. Will be back.

Stopped by here for a quick simple meal. Â My friend said they supposedly have the best grilled cheese in NYC. Â I honestly don't have much experience to compare but I was thoroughly impressed at the Queens Kickshaw. My friend and I both ordered the gouda grilled cheese which came with some type of jam and jalapeno. Â The jam and jalapeno both gave the sandwich a subtle sweet and spicy taste that enhanced the flavor of the sandwich. Â It came with a simple spring mix salad which offset the cheesiness of the sandwich which was nice. Â I also ordered the tomato soup and while it tasted kind of like pizza sauce, it was pretty good. Â  The servers were also very attentive and helpful when we were picking with beer to order. Â I'm moving to Astoria soon so I think I'll definitely be stopping again soon.

If there's a better Italian restaurant in NYC, I'd like to know what it is. We've probably been here about a dozen times, and the food and service have been consistently exceptional. It's worth going for the flatbread and tomato dip alone. The way they have the waiters recite the 50+ specials, while always a fun shtick, is a bit annoying, as it's hard to remember them all and sometimes I have trouble hearing them due to the background noise -- I wish they'd just print them up and hand them out with the menus. Fortunately, the items on the regular menu hardly disappoint -- the buffalo mozzarella is among the best I've had anywhere, and their homemade spaghetti is incredible. if you're going to L'incontro, do yourself a favor and get a reservation -- I've had trouble getting in there on Fri/Sat nights without one.

What does Grey Dog want to be when it grows up? I guess "cafe" is the correct label for such a place, but it does nothing particularly well. That does not mean that there is absolutely nothing good on the menu; there simply is no category of thing you'd come here *for*. *It's not a coffee shop. Its brewed coffee is overbrewed and bitter. I am a huge coffee lover and can take a genuinely strong brew like a man (strong French presses, etc.). This is "mud." *It has wine, but it's not a wine bar. *It's doing the sandwich thing, but the two sandwiches we shared were just not too special. Edible, okay, meh. *The standard side for the sandwiches is potato chips from the bag. This is lame. In fact, I really *hate* when restaurants do this. They have fries available for $3.00+, and they actually looked pretty good. Gimme some fries, eh? *There is no wi-fi. This seems to be a New York thing: hey, we don't want people ordering one thing and using it as an office all day. I dig. But it's a pretty big place with a lot of room, so it would seem to be the very kind of place where they could afford to have people hanging out a bit. The positive The food is OK, and the prices are not bad. If you are in the neighborhood and need a bite that won't break the bank, this is not a horrible choice. You may also find something on the menu that does it for you. I, however, will not be going back to experiment.

I was a bit nervous coming here for dinner, as most of the Yelp reviews for this place were raves about the brunch. But, I had my heart set on dinner at a farm-to-table restaurant that wasn't quite as expensive as ABC Kitchen and didn't require a pilgrimage to Brooklyn--Cookshop fit the bill. The restaurant has a similar feel to its sister restaurant Five Points and the food is just as solid. While the group was a bit disappointed with the oily bread basket and tremendously bitter summer market salad, the assortment of mains we ordered were delicious. The Alaskan King Salmon paired with corn pudding and cantaloupe was an unlikely combo that worked brilliantly. The Niman Ranch Loin Pork Chop was tender and juicy. My boyfriend had the duck leg confit and was a huge fan. We finished with the strawberry shortcake and a few sorbets and left happy! Overall--enjoyable atmosphere, fresh ingredients, and inspired dishes.

Just left the place and again I must say.. I had a great time.. Had the Chuleta w spicey kale and it was by far just good, It was DELICIOUS!! Husband and son n law had the churrasco steak and my daughter had the salmon.. the only complaint we had was that it was all delicious!!!! But let me suggest the cuban tea or tea cubano which was great.. The food, ambiance, and service were all on point!! KEEP UP THE GREAT WORK!!! Great food, drinks, service!!! Â We will def!! Go back!!! Must give Wilson 3 thumbs up for making sure his customers were happy!! Thanxs!!!! See you soon!!!
Just be prepared to return here over and over again. It's cheap, fresh, delicious, spicy, savory, just so damn good. Cucumber salad, the cold noodles, oh hell! Everything is great!!!
belgian fries with TONS of different dipping sauces. Â my favorite is by far sweet mango chutney. Â definitely worth standing in line for.
Exactly what this neighborhood needs. The owners are very friendly and the food/coffee is awesome! Excited to try more things on the menu soon. Â We will definitely make this a regular spot.

My brother and I used to live in TriBeCa and found this hidden gem. Hands down the best hole in the wall for noodles and dumplings. The place looks grimy but serves some of the best Chinese food I've ever had. I also love the selection of Asian drinks in their fridge outside. The restaurant has a really interesting diverse crowd, the people that come here know what's up! Honestly, it is the best bargain for a meal less than ten dollars, $5 for a bowl of noodles and $3 for some Fried Dumplings (12pcs). It is a bit disappointing that they make the noodles in the back now, the guy used to stand at the table right outside of the kitchen door and pull the noodles. You know you're at a legit spot when you hear that "smack" sound of dough hitting the table. Like any place in C-Town, they are cash only. And if you're trying to celebrate the Chinese New Year with some delicious noodles - don't bother coming here, that's the only day they take off (seriously)! I've taken over a dozen of friends here, and they've all been back here with their friends.
Really cute place. Â Great music, great ambiance. Â Terrible service and even after we complained (which I never ever do) they still didn't try to do the right thing.
Great Customer Service

Fun vibe, good food, great service from Jean Marie! Â We stumbled upon this place after going to union hall. Â My boyfriend is a carnivore and I'm veg- great options for both. Â He loved the chicken wings and I loved the arroz con seitan. Â And the empanadas were great! Â Looks like they have an awesome happy hour until 11pm M-W, we'll be coming back!

So glad a friend recommend Terri. How come no one told me about this place??? Super cool spot to get your Sandwichfest on. The ambiance is nice as well. I got a Bacon Cheddar Chicken Ranch sandwich and it was so big that I was not able to finish it. The food here is so delicious and flavorful! I've tried few of the wraps here too and all have been well executed. Everything was perfect. The place was so friendly and the staff seemed to be genuinely happy to work there. The service is always great and the prices are very reasonable. A great sandwich for less then $9, is a steal. Terri definitely met my needs for some sandwich. They have great juices and smoothies too. I tried The Perfect Pear juice it was very refreshing - pear, celery and cucumber. YUM.

I just made the first order at the newly re-branded OBAO, formerly The Ember Room. Gone are the chocolate spare ribs, but in their place is a successful menu borrowed from their two other locations. The interior has new lights and a new Pho bar, but looks mostly the same. The new menu includes the Michelin-recommended "Spare Ribs on Sugar Cane Skewer," which I ordered. Both dishes arrived promptly. The ribs featured meat wrapped around a piece of sugar cane, then grilled on a gas flame. The resulting softness, flavor and nice char impressed me. Delectable. My only complaint: the chef could have bulked up the skewers with a little more meat. The ribs came with swiped dollop peanut sauce. Though a particularly good peanut sauce (this coming from someone who doesn't like peanut sauce), the ribs needed no embellishment. I also had the Michelin-recommended Pho-Bo. The flavor of the broth was fantastic--rich and savory. Though the meat (2 kinds?) in the Pho was a little chewy for my taste, I loved the noodles. I enjoyed the freshness of the ingredients and seasoning. I don't know that I've had a Pho, and I know it's the latest thing. I'm a convert, and now the bar is set high. (Let me know of whatever Pho places you'd recommend.) Luke, Yung, and Jen were all great (thanks, guys!). Congratulations to Chace. Ember Room is dead. Long live OBAO!

Yes!!!!!! Finally! An awesome seafood place for the peeps of greenpoint! Amazing lobsta and crab rolls. My heart also melted when I saw their wide array of booze to accompany my food...vodka lemonade WHAT!?!???!! There's a super sweet woman Â who brings the food to your table so even though there's so waitstaff, she makes up for it! Only one negative is the communal seating arrangement if you can't get a seat at the bar. However, that's probably more my problem because I really don't want to sit next to a group of unknown hipsters that can hear me while I judge them incessantly.

Excellent food and service. Our server, Tat was awesome. While I love authentic Japanese style sushi, I still want to be able to improvise from time to time and the chef rejected a couple very reasonable requests. Great quality, but the price and lack of accomodation was annoying.

This was definitely a cute spot. Â We went with a group of 8 for a Halloween/Birthday dinner. Â They take reservations, but were accommodating and forgiving that my husband and I were stuck in traffic and running late, so they sat the other 6 folks and everyone ordered appetizers while they waited for us. Â The staff won my respect INSTANTLY for that! Â So many places refuse to seat the party unless everyone is accounted for. Â The staff was so very friendly - I think that was my favorite part. Â I felt welcome and really enjoyed the ambience. Â The decor was mostly brick and subdued lighting, which would make it nice for a date. The food was very good. Â I wouldn't say it was the best Japanese food I've ever had, but it was fresh and they offered great choices. Â I have a generally weak stomach, but I left there feeling great that night and the next day, so the food was certainly clean and fresh. Â I had a spicy maki combination. Â My husband had the sushi/sashimi combo. Â I also had a white tuna appetizer that was thinly sliced and in a delicate sauce. Â This place is BYOB, so we were able to bring our own wine, which was nice. Â The corking fee was about $10 a bottle. Â I really hate corking fees, but they gave offer the first bottle with no fee, so that made it a little better. If you are looking for clean and respectable Japanese cuisine at fair prices with a nice subdued ambience, Zest is a very good choice.
Aloo masala hit the spot! Perfect walking food.

Excellent stuff here! The Islands has some of the best jerk chicken I've ever tasted. Served with great rice and beans and steamed cabbage. Big plate of food which is always nice. The Mac'n'Cheese is also pretty epic. Its worth the trip. Never sat down to eat here but it looks very cozy

A special night out called for a fun and festive restaurant and Calle Ocho definitely delivered! We arrived early and sat in a cozy nook near the bar area to wait for the rest of our party. Service was great and the drinks were pretty solid. Once seated, the great service continued as we were brought ceviche, bite-sized empanadas, melty cheesy croquettes, and paella - all tasty. The ceviche sampler was fun and easy to share. I highly recommend that. We also ordered a pitcher of sangria which lasted most of dinner. Fun experience in NY! I would definitely return.
The service was wonderful, we had two waitresses who were as fun as they were helpful, and I ate the best pie of my life. Not to mention it's a beautiful cozy setting. Definitely worth a stop!

I had to do it at least once, what you wonder? try the Short Rib Hash! Who would have thought of short ribs with hash browns? I mean I really was excited when I heard about this combo, but got even more excited when I read all the positive reviews that people gave it. Stone Park was a bit of a trek to get to from downtown Brooklyn for me, so I was excited when I finally saw the restaurant just a couple mins to 3pm. I was happy it was not crazy crowded which would made us have to wait. One of our friends was already there drinking her Bloody Mary at the bar so we were able to be promptly seated. I got a really nice feel from Stone Park, Â it was very inviting and calm. The exposed wood beams to white decor and large bay windows allowed a great amount of sunlight into the restaurant. We choose to sit right in front to soak in all the sunny goodness. Our waitress was very pleasant and accommodating. She did let us know that since the grits were so popular they had run out. Luckily for me I already knew I was getting the Short Rib Hash, so I was not disappointed but my other friends were. After reviewing the menu and locking in my choose I asked for a side of spinach to have some veggies in the mix and a glass of Bellini. I don't recall if they had a bottomless brunch so we opted for the individual cocktails. Once my meal came there was no turning back I knew it was going to be a love affair. Everything smelled so good, and looked even better, but the taste is what did it for me. The combination of crunchy harsh brown pieces with the rich ribs with my scrambled eggs and cheddar cheese was ---ohhhh la la delicious.

Brindle Room would get more than two stars from me but for one thing: the mussels they served me smelled of sewage. I ate a couple at first, thinking it must have been something else, but my dining companion smelled it, too. We called over the waitress (who agreed), and she took them back to the kitchen. They handled the problem well: didn't charge us for the dish, and offered us free dessert (hence more than one star). But they shouldn't have served them to begin with - my stomach felt off for hours, and had I eaten more I have no doubt I'd have spent the next 24 hours... Well, you can guess the rest. Disappointed, as everything else pointed to Brindle Room being a promising bet.
OK, bacon and brussels shows up on my bill as BACON. Enough said. YUM. The bourbon choices were to die for also! Will return!

I'll keep it simple instead of writing large, winding reviews... They have large selection of Tapas dishes, they have large proportions so I would be careful in ordering many dishes. The phoenix fries are good! Â I had the lambchop entree, which was good, but nothing spectacular, you're better off ordering the tapas/appetizers menus, ordering a few of those will be as much food Â as an entree dish. The beef kibbeh is interesting, but I probably would skip it. Â The brussel sprouts are pretty interesting unique too, but I probably wouldn't order it again. I would recommend trying some of the drinks! Â They are really good, but expensive and they give you such a small amount! if you haven't been here before, try the Prix fixe menu FIRST!! I've been here a few times! In fact, on "pizza fridays" at my office, we'd ordered enough pizza pies for about 50-60 people from this place, I don't know if it was because it was such a large order by 12:30 on friday but a lot of the pizzas would come slightly burnt. So I've been there 3 times on my own. I was never wowed by Grimaldi's. I would never stand outside on that freezing cold or desperately hot line depending on the season for some of this stuff. I will admit, it has a unique taste and is different, but that doesn't always mean 5 stars.

Keep in mind I'm no pizza connoisseur. Im happy with hot warm pizza from papa john's Â :) Best artichoke Pizza I've had. Definitely would return to eat again. Sauce was so deliciously rich and creamy, nice hints of the salty savory taste and just when you think you're gonna get bored with it, you get a sharp slap of some little bits in tomatoes in it. Bread was crispy yet fluffy, just enough to buffer the rich sauce.
I agree, I agree finger lickin good - For finger type portions ...

I Came here over the weekend with some friends for dinner and the food was delicious! For appetizer We had yeah he escargot and it was buttery and had an amazing pesto sauce on it. We also shared the chick pea salad and that I must say was really really good. We finished every bit of the salad. For entree I had the tilapia it was flavorful and Cooked just right. The mash potato was delicious as well, my friend's steak was cooked perfectly. The crazy luluc burger was pretty good. My other friend ordered the duck breast and that was cooked and seasoned perfectly. It was so flavorful and juicy. I definitely need to come back here for brunch. Heard the pancakes are amazing!

Absolutely fantastic. Best pizza in New York City. Di Fara is legend. I love watching Dom lay each piece of basil, one by one, on every single pizza. I mean, that alone deserves four stars... and then another star because it always tastes amazing. Well worth the wait and definitely lives up to the hype. I'm happy he got so popular but at the same time it's a shame because now it's always so damn crowded... but hey, cosi va il mondo.

Coffee is good but that's where the good ends. They have a sign outside which blocks the flow of traffic on a relatively busy street. Their workers expect tips so expect a dirty look if u don't give one. I've gone on 3 occasions over the past month and didn't have any change to give on 2 of those 3 times so dirty looks and eye rolls I got. Maybe if the boss paid employees better they wouldn't be so dependent on tips. Music isn't soft and light like Starbucks not that I want it to be but it's loud obnoxious music which would make it hard to have a conversation if u wanted to sit there and chat. Cheapest cup of coffee is $2.25 so this place is only good if ur willing to pay the much and run out of there.

Now this is what I call a good restaurant and believe me I don't say this often. Their Korean food is out of the world with really low prices. Â Service was good to. It is definitely on my list of restaurants to return to .
I would be so happy if this place was great as work very close. But in the 5 times i got food from here, i got sick twice. I gave them one last chance and got sick again!

Came here for a happy hour event that had the whole basement rented out. Â It was a big enough space, with a separate bar and waiter service, so good if you need to rent out space for a group. Â It just felt a little dreary down there and took a very long time to get drink. Â I would stay upstairs if you want more of a neighborhood irish/sports bar feeling!
Exotic Indian Cuisine! Love it!

Probably the best of the best in Chinatown! Truly a rags to riches story, I remember the owner when he had his little rice rolls cart years ago on Hester Street. He was always friendly and had the most affordable meals a fat kid can get after a grueling day of English, science, and arithmetic. Fast forward the years and here he is, running a shop around the clock and serving more than just rice rolls. Hanging on the window are the Cantonese barbeque goods that almost no one can resist: roast pork, more roast pork, chicken, and duck. A line sticking out the door is a positive indication and you're darn right I jumped on that line! Lo and behold, rice box heaven! Oh why oh why do you taste so good?! I am fighting off a losing battle against the itis while trying to sit comfortably as I type this so heed well... GET EVERYTHING!!

even though i cannot drink for beans i still love brunch places that include a drink with the meal brunch items are between 12-17 dollars + a choice of a drink (i got the white peach belini; light and refreshing) the grill chicken salad, mushroom omelet (HUGE), and the lobster egg benedict were all delicious. and the complimentary bread basket comes with 3 different types of breads. Â the raisin one is really yummy especially with strawberry cream cheese. i would recommend making reservations otherwise you are going to be hungry waiting till 3pm.
This cafe is one of the best where i ever been. I want to keep coming to this place to eat best lobsters in NYC. I hope that i can come with my friend to your place to have a great time
Good but Totto is better. However, their pork buns beat Totto hands down.

i had such high hopes for this place!! i got the chilorio brisket + cole-braised pork. the meat was obvs high quality and it was tasty but it just didn't WOW me like i wanted it to. there was pepper in the cola-braised pork, which i didn't enjoy but it didn't mar the taste of the tacos overall. the chilorio was better and i liked the pineapple salsa. i guess i'm just disappointed that it was suppose to be AMAZING and it was okay for me.

*Winter Restaurant Week 2012* This restaurant isn't really that hard to find; just walk east on 29th st, all the way towards the East River, and it'll be inside the Alexandria Center building. You'll pass, on the right, the adjacent Riverpark urban farm space (it's walled up with some windows for viewing) that supplies the produce you will be consuming next door. The farm looks like it's still under development, and is to be there temporarily until a new building is constructed in its place (at which time the farm will be moved elsewhere). Talk about "farm to table." For lunch RW, they only offer the RW menu, so you don't have to request the "cheaper menu." We had lunch (they offer 8 apps and 8 entrees) on MLK day. They don't do dinner for RW. Apps: Trevisano & Frisee Salad - Until now, I didn't know that Trevisano is a bitter red leafy radicchio. It seems like a lettuce that's better off cooked with something savory. The poached pear and spiced almonds in the salad were lovely. Braised Chicken Soup - There's more chicken, kale, and vegetables in the soup than soup itself, which is fine when you want a hearty but light start. Entrees Buckwheat Pappardelle - With minced pork ragu. The pasta was cooked on the soft side, but it was still delicious in the creamy sweet potato sauce. Roasted Arctic Char - Just like you'd expect from salmon. Desserts Chocolate Pot de Creme - A standard chocolate mousse/custard. Beignets - Comes hot; these hot donuts dipped in the espresso custard was the BEST thing of the meal. The chocolate dip was ok too. So the fare was pretty standard. Service was attentive. The view of the river was nerve-settling, and dining outside would be a must in the spring/summer. They do a $28 prix fixe lunch all year round.

I really like the pizza at Grimaldi's - I do. It is the best pizza I've ever had. And if you go right after work or for an early lunch there's no line to get in. But after my last experience there last week, I don't think I'll be ordering anything there anymore, not at this one. My husband had seen a calzone the last time we were there and that's all he could talk about for weeks, so when we got there that's what we ordered. Unfortunately they put too much into it, so it took 40 minutes to get it. In the meantime, we were able to notice how the tablecloth hadn't been changed in days. And how there were mouse droppings in the corner - EEK! I'm pretty sure calzones come with cheese and sauce in them, but this one was all cheese. We asked for some sauce on the side and the server brought it out in a mug. The mug was all crusted over with sauce - it looked like it had been left over from somebody else. And the calzone was cold in the middle. We ended up leaving right after which nearly made me cry as the couple next to us had a delicious looking pizza that came quickly and smelled so good. So don't get the calzone! And I'll have to try the Grimaldi's in Douglaston and pray its a bit cleaner. :(

The best thing about this place is the atmosphere. People from all walks of life (local, non-local, regulars, new comers etc). The wait staff is nice, but not the most attentive. The wine is ok. I've had a few mix ups with my orders and a few times where we waited a long while for someone to check in on us so we could ask for the check. My favorite thing on the menu that I've had is the grits and shrimp. Will probably return for that.

I'm confused....how did this place come remotely close to getting 4-Stars? Let's get one thing straight here people. Â Living a gluten-free lifestyle does not mean bland!! The Goods: The night did start off great. Â My friends and I were given yummy, sweet-ish, crispy on the outside, soft on the inside breadsticks. Â We also had the pizette as an appetizer. Â It had this yummy tasting ham (almost prosciutto like) on top. Service was outstanding. Â Our server was always there at the blink of an eye to make sure everything tasted well and drinks were refilled. Â In fact, the minute I realized we would not be having dessert, she had already laid down the check. Â Kinda creepy....but in a good way. Â A+ Â Top notch. The Bads: Now I really really did want to like this place. Â If your name is derived from the word Risotto, one would think you're good at Risotto. Â Right? Â Not such the case. The risotto I received was piping hot (in fact, the roof of my mouth is still peeling), overcooked, mushy, and bland. Â  And, as soon as my friend's boyfriend requested pepper, the rest of our faces lit up. Wow what a difference a little bit of peppery taste adds to the bowl. Â So if you do visit, make sure to ask for the pepper flakes. For me...I ordered my risotto with spinach and sausage. Â I kept searching for a bigger piece of sausage to overpower the bland risotto, but the sausage, much like the risotto, fell flat. Â  I mean, sausage is typically gluten free so there should be no excuse here. Â  Conclusion: I'm honestly hoping this place has seen better nights..but next time when I want a GF meal I'll take my money and try elsewhere.

I left this place well-drunk and stuffed to the brim. The space is tight, like most of your restaurants in the neighborhood, but I love the artwork and atmosphere of the place. Great drinks, and I loved the Yuquita Frita; Oh, I just can not explain my love for this. It seems like such a simple concept, deep-fried crispy yuca with a creamy cilantro sauce, but I've been trying to find the same sauce at other places with no luck. It was just plain out delicious. The Masitas de Puerco were succulent, savory little bits of spicy pork that we couldn't stop eating, loved the meat, onion sauce and potatoes spiced just right to accompany the meaty pork. (the only way I can describe it). It was a carnivore's dream. The Arroz con Pollo Criallado was also done just right - moist, greasy saffron rice with shredded chicken cooked just the way I like it - a little overdone. (Probably would not get that again though) I would definitely back here comparing it against some other Cuban places I've been, but 1) The service is slow, as everyone else highlights, and 2) this place is not cheap by any means. $17 for Arroz con Pollo is steep, to say the least.

I love it so much.I was very sad when we had to move from south slope to sunset park as I would not get to go there as often as I want, or just walk past it every day. But they delivered the food to our area too.
Yum! Delicious, cheap, perfect for lunch in Chinatown.

Refreshing, open, moderately priced fare in Chelsea...I like. I was wandering around Chelsea with my bestie, trying to find Bareburger...when we got lazy and stopped her instead. Bestie got the fish sandwich and I got the burger. Both were only $10. I asked for my burger medium...but I found it a little medium-well to be honest. But I am a stickler about those kinds of things. All in all, it was tasty. Cheese was extra $, so I skipped it. The fries were very crispy and tasty. It was also served with a few delicious pickle slices! Yum! Everyone else was chowing down on this (steak) salad that also seemed very good/popular. There is a school nearby, so prepare for it to get a little noisy if your dining around 2-3 p.m. Seating is pretty cozy, so if you're planning on having an uber-personal convo...you might want to save that for later.

I saw this place on Diners, Drive-Ins, and Dives, and I was really excited about trying it out. When I finally got around to it, I had the pulled pork hash, and I liked it, but I don't think I liked it enough to ever come back. I'm glad that I can cross it off of my never-ending Places to Eat in NYC bucket list though.
Easily puts Grimaldi's and Lombardi's to shame. This is the definitive pizza in NYC, but not New York pizza per se... the much purer Italian alternative. Great beer list too!
The best ramen in town. Â My only advice would be to go with good company. Â That way time will pass much more quickly when you wait in that long line.

2 words - YOGURT SAUCE. Don't know the proper name but its soooo good. I always get the falafel over rice and although the falafel itself isn't the best, they give you a lot and the rice and pita and everything else is yummy. And its only $6 dollars which is a okay with me.

Hungry? Broke? $1 for dumplings and $2.50 for a duck scallion pancake. I'm pretty sure you will be full after that, but go ahead, get another order of dumplings. Â  Make sure you drown your fried dumplings in the "sauce" and a splash of watered down saracha too!

My bro picked up the sandwiches, so I can't really attest to the "buying experience". Â He did say that the Chinese dudes working in the back took FOREVER (as in a long ass time) to make the sandwiches. Â I thought my peeps were speedy. Â Hmm. Â Anyway, I'm pretty sure they use a microwave to heat shit up (tacky), and it's a bit pricey for banh mi, but hey, this is the new, gentrified Bk! Â Slap an extra buck on there.

Why did it take me this long to find this spot? The food is amazing! Â Diverse lunch crowd, but don't let that scare you - These people know what they want. Spicy brisket is amazing. Great baguette, not too crunchy that it cuts up your mouth. Just enough spice even without the jalapeno to give it a little kick. So moist and enough of bread and meat ratio to make every bite wonderful. I'll be going out for lunch more from now on. // Update - one less star because of the inconsistency. First try was amazing.
like it, very good with good service

A true lobster roll lover I am, and have tried them all through Maine and New England. Tonight we ventured to the actual Red Hook Pound location through the horrible rain crap weather for some toasty lobster rolls. Got there around 8PM and the sweet counter girl couldn't have been more welcoming and awesome. She happily chatted with us about Maine and lobster, as her co worker (both actually authentically from there!) made our four rolls and got us clam chowder. Â yum! Our brains exploded while we ate these suckers. Sooooo good! The shop is adorable and cozy and they also have a sit down eat in space next store. We have had Luke's rolls-even shrimp as well and it tastes like crap-ola compared to these bad boys. Check it out, and I read they are at the Brooklyn flea and starting a street truck soon. There goes my summer weekly paycheck! But booyah so worth it!
The corn the corn the corn!!!!!!! Crowded and tight but food is cheap and filling- did I say get the corn?
It's really not possible to get good southern food in New York.

Appetizers were good. Had scallop carpaccio which was excellent. Duck meatballs were ok. Duck breast was terrible and steak was ok. After dinner I had to go running to the restroom. Evidently something went wrong. The whole experience was mediocre. Got there early, only two tables were occupied, they sat us in front of restrooms.I will not go back not recommend this restaurant. Service was proper.

Very comfortable ambiance, great, cooperative and attentive service. The breakfasts were well done. We had eggs florentine with french fries and the spinach omelette with home fries. Everything was very good.

Yummy!!! Super delish (what I think) is authentic NYC pizza. Service was fast and right outside my hotel. I also had the lentil soup which came with a delicious side of sourdough garlic bread (YUM) will definitely be recommending this place!

Great bourbon and craft beer selection at this new bar in FH. Â Although I haven't tried all of their menu items, the ones I've tried were pretty good and inventive. Â This is a definitely a nice new addition to the neighborhood.

4.5 stars... DeFonte's has been a Brooklyn institution since 1922. This bare bones sandwich shop is mostly a take out spot though there is a small counter to stand and eat at if you don't live nearby. If it's nice out then taking your food to Valentino park down Coffey Street or the park outside Ikea are nice places to go. They've got well over a dozen specialty sandwiches or you could create your own. Sandwiches come in small or large and vary from $8-10. Even the small is about 8" of packed deliciousness so a large could easily fill two people. Whether you go with the ham, roasted pork, turkey, meatball, chicken, or some other meat you know you're going to have a fantastic sandwich with fresh ingredients. I got the meatball parm which was absolutely huge and the juicy tender meatballs were among the best I've ever had, it was definitely worth the 28 block round trip walk from my place.

Park Slope is lacking good breakfast places but this one is very very good. It is a calm and laidback restaurant environment with a big open space that allows for a lot of natural light. I tend to get the chilaquiles w/scrambled eggs which are flavorful and fresh. Anything I've tried here has been very fresh. While their menu items tend to be on the pricier-end for their breakfast, lunch and dinner options, their food is great.

I came across SCRATCHbread at the Brooklyn Flea Market, after reading about them in Cooking Light. It was super cold outside, so I decided to try their salted caramel hot chocolate to warm up before I braved the outdoors. As I stood in line, I heard the guy behind the counter describe the hot chocolate as 'finishing' with a hint of salted caramel - or something like that. Usually, these kinds of descriptions make me roll my eyes. I like food as much as the next person, but let's not make it needlessly complicated. He was right, though. This hot chocolate DOES have an amazing taste of salted caramel after you drink it. It's pretty amazing. It's hard to describe, so just try it yourself. You won't be disappointed. At 4.00 a cup, the hot chocolate isn't Â cheap. If you're looking for an exceptionally tasty way to warm up and if you're a fan of rich chocolate, it's well worth the money. Give it a try!
Tasty whitefish salad and bagel. Gret coffee. Atmosphere is really lovely, quaint in a retro-Brooklyn way. Also came in for dessert and night. Awesome sticky toffee pudding with ice-cream. Fantastic.

LOVED this place, its so nice to sit outside on those picnic like tables on a summer evening and share some tacos, corn and beer with your friends. Real casual place with a mixed crowd, and I hear it can get really crowded but the day I went it wasnt so bad...I got two fish tacos for like 5 bucks. The fish could have been seasoned better, but overall it was a good taco and make sure u put some chulola(sp?) hot sauce on there!! Takes it from good to great. As everyone else mentioned, corn is great. I cant wait to go back, esp since they will be closing soon for the winter months.

Tia Pol is my favorite tapas bar in all of NYC. The staff is super great and friendly and has no hipper-than-thou-self-important ego (*ahem* Boqueria). It does get expensive depending on what you end up drinking and eating. It's also the most authentic Basque-region styled tapas bar I've encountered in NYC. My friends and I like to get the patatas bravas when we expect more than two glasses of wine a person. I love the navajas y almejas (razor clams and cockles), and to sop up the broth with hunks of bread. Sometimes, the quality of it varies. One time it was salty and they were out of razor clams (which adds a sweetness to the dish). The fava bean puree on bread, with crumbs of beyos cheese is soooo good. The almonds are a must. The pinchos morunos are perfectly seasoned. The paquetitos de jamÃ³n (ham) y alcachofas (stuffed with artichokes) are literally "little packets" and although they're yummy is a very tiny portion, even for tapas. Gamas a la plancha is a necessary plate to try. The huevos rellenos (stuffed eggs/deviled eggs) are picture perfect and taste just as good. The assorted spanish cheeses is also a great end instead of the traditional dessert. Â  The sangria jug is refreshing (but somewhat sweet) on a hot summer evening. You may have to wait for an hour and half or more for a bar seat but it's a worthwhile experience.

Went here for dinner pre-theater. Â I was running late but I told the hostess our predicament and she was ever so gracious. I got in and out with dessert in about an hour. Which isn't to say they rush you there- they absolutely do not, just saying that if you need to step it Â up, they're very accommodating. I had the sirloin with mashed potatoes and spinach. Â It was excellent! Â It was cooked perfectly (medium rare, being red in the middle but warm instead of gooey gel). The spinach was delightful and perfectly sauteed. The service was outstanding and it had a rather nice wine list. I would DEFINITELY recommend this place for a pre-theater dinner anytime! When I return to NYC, I do plan on returning here.

Maybe it was an off night, maybe I was off, but I didn't really love it. Â Maybe it's Yelp blasphemy, but Pylos was overpriced for what it was. Â  We came here on Friday night without reservations and she was starving. So, we settled for eating at the "communal" table on stools, which is the equivalent of sitting at a bar for the duration of a meal (until your ass goes numb). Â  As an appetizer we tasted the "trifecta" of spreads. Â I only enjoyed the cucumber dill / yogurt, but had no problem housing as much pita as the servers could bring. I ordered the pork shank with potatoes and leeks. It was good, but it was overpriced. Â She had the salmon over spinach and rice, which she labeled as "unique". I guess she liked it, but she also wasn't wowed by her meal according me polling her after said meal. It just wasn't the same experience that so many other Yelpers raved about.

After reading many positive reviews on Yelp about Luke's Lobster, my family and I put it on our list of places to eat while in NY for Spring Break. Â Now that we are back in CA and have reviewed our best and worst experiences, Luke's Lobster scored #1 on everyone's list. Â The Noah's Ark was the perfect way for us to each taste three amazing sandwiches without being too full to enjoy them. Â The only drawback was the tiny dining area - our party of four had a difficult time finding seats together because the room only offers 1 table (with 6 chairs) and a bar around two walls that offer a total of 8 additional chairs. Â Two customers had claimed the table for six and a second couple sat in the center of the wall of bar chairs, so my family and I had to move a chair from another part of the restaurant and sit crammed together in a place that was better suited for three at most. Â Good thing the food was so delicious - after one bite we didn't mind being crammed together in a corner.

This is the worst dining experience that we have had in a while. When you go to a place priced like Bouley, you expect the best. This is clearly not what we got, not even close. The service was very poor and the maitre d was very simply rude and arrogant. We had a horrible table that was in the way of all waiters. Food was ok bt nothing spectacular really. Don't go there.

When you open the massive doors and step inside, you feel tiny with its ultra-high ceilings and bar that stretches before you like the 8th wonder of the world. Â It's a great place for an after work drink or place to meet up and snack. Â The high-top tables nestled into the alcoves of banquets are intimate and all have a great vantage point to the rest of the bar. As for a place to dine, I am not sure I would go that far. Â Four of us went there after a show and it's a bit noisy with its sub-bass undertones, like the whips on the street with tinted windows and the bass rumbling in a 30 foot radius around it. I am not sure this is the best venue for what we had in mind. Â I liked the music, but there is nowhere to really get out of the way of it. As cute and hip as our server was, it was as if everyone got very good at lip reading. Â  I had the fish-n-chips which were flaky and not overwhelming. Â Our quest had the Chicken-pot-pie (which they are known for) and said it was ok, but nothing striking. Â Another had the bangers and mash which he said was ok and another had the pulled pork sandwich. Â Although our plates were cleaned, it was not something you would say--wow, we have to get back there. Â If I go back, and I am sure I will for out-of-town guests, it will be for a drink at the bar and maybe a bar menu bite or two before deciding where to go for the evening. It is impressive.

This is one of my favorite pizza places in NYC, and the world. I am a Italian American Brooklyn raised pizza snob, and I love it. It's my second favorite only to Grimaldi's, because I prefer a slightly chewier crust. Lucali's is hard to get into, and expect a wait (ours would have been one hour, so we ordered it to go- it took 10 min). You owe it to yourself to try it and get an authentic pizza in ny. There are too many mediocre pizza places...

Consistently tummy lovin good. A co-worker pushed me through the door of this delicious shawarma / Falafel makin' hole in the wall restaurant. Â It's tiny, fast, and freakin good. Â He had been going here for years and I certainly tasted why. Â It's all good, the shish-kebobs, shawarma's, falafel's stuffed in a pita with lettuce/tomato/hummus sauce... messy and good. Cheap eats at it's best!
Nice casual restaurant good for brunch, lunch, or dinner!

Great food, bad service, and loud. The food is great, in massive portions and of very high quality. Me and my two friends got the basic chicken and several sides (yucca, fries, beans and rice, and something else), and it was out of this world. Â With the portions the way they were, the three of us basically split a single entree and we still had about a quarter of it to take home. Â We also had the sangria, which was good but small servings for the price. Even though the menu looks expensive (15 for appetizer, 30 for most entrees), because we took advantage of the cheap basic chicken (16 for a whole chicken with no sides) and 4 dollar sides, we only ended up spending 20-30 each or so. The decor is avant-garde and interesting, but because it's all concrete and hard things, it is extremely loud, and we found it difficult to carry on a conversation. We were most disappointed by the service. Â The hostesses acted as though we weren't worthy of being there, and refused to even provide a time estimate of the wait or start the clock on our wait time until all three of us arrived. Â Even though the restaurant was Â¾ empty, they still took 20 extra minutes to seat us, and then sat three people at a two person table, which was pretty cramped. The entire time it felt like they were actively trying to drive us away. Â Our waitstaff were more polite but didn't seem to know the menu well (they couldn't describe how many glasses were in different sangria pitcher sizes), and the aforementioned volume issue made them difficult to understand. Â They also were REALLY trying to upsell, which I can understand from a business perspective, but it came across as really pushy. Â By the end we felt like we were being rushed out, but by that point we were happy to leave. One weird quirk: the combos on the menu, at least one we were looking at, are actually more expensive than if you order the separate chicken and sides than the combo, which we thought was pretty shady. Overall an interesting place with some REALLY great food, but if they decide you aren't good enough for them, prepare to be treated pretty horribly by the hostesses.

great place, still love the atmosphere, they used to have a dj on weekends, it's been a while since I've seen one, it's fine with me the music was too loud, the food is always great, love eating there, the prices are affordable =), the bar is okay, it's great place to come with some friends and looks fancy enough to come with for girl on a casual date. the only downside is their hours, they close early, so it's more like an early evening type of spot in my book.

Han Dynasty is undisputed proof that Phila is home to some culinary masterpices, namely Morimoto, La Colombe, Zahav, and now Han Dynasty. Â Get the dan dan noodles, crystal wontons, dry pot shredded beef, 3 cup chicken (for those who prefer milder flavors), and cumin lamb. Â The only dish that I felt was just decent was the tea smoked duck, which I prefer to order at New East in Phila. Â The scallion pancakes are decent but nothing extraordinary (I make my own from a tried-and-true Shanghainese recipe so I have VERY high standards for these). Â It's very busy but worth the wait and the servers are great. Â Another victory for Philly!

I loved it. Â The old time NY feel, the bustle of the bar/dining room, the affable, knowledgeable service and, of course, the food made it a great evening out. The Black Label burger is very good (although I'm not necessarily a fan of foie gras in my burger) and I was shocked at the percentage of people that order just the burger. Â You miss out on some other excellent options otherwise although the french fries alone may be worth getting one. We started with the calamari, shrimp, anchovy appetizer. Â For anchovy lovers this is a must have. Â The anchovies were huge. Â The calamari and shrimp were also cooked perfectly. Â The Pasta Za ZA was also delicious with scrumptious pancetta mixed in like small buried treasure. For entrees, we went with the specials for that evening. Â The King Atlantic Salmon was a bit on the small side but perfectly cooked and delicious. Â The sliced lamb entree with fava beans and snap peas was fantastic and mouth watering. The cocktails were a great mix of old classics and innovative libations. Â The dark chocolate dessert was the perfect sweet finale for the evening. Â  I will be back and hopefully soon.

I was torn between 3 and 4 stars. The beer list is what makes me want to give it more stars not the food. I really enjoyed the cask style ale they had as well as some of the stouts. They let you taste any of the beers on draft which is awesome. It was very crowded when we went so we had to wait awhile for a table before we could eat. When we did get sat, all of the tables are so close together, there was no room to move or even sit straight on your chair. Food is good, nothing too special but better than your usual bar food. I had the tacos and we got the guacamole as an appetizer. Overall, a cool place to hangout but it may take you awhile to be able to get a table to eat.

I'm not a cheesecake fan but definitely the best I've tasted. Â The carrot cake cheesecake was especially good. Â One complaint is when my wife and I ordered Bailey's on the rocks we expected $8-10 drinks. Â What we didn't expect was to pay $2 for "rocks"! Â Seriously? Â Good breakfast too.

The place is overrated. No doubt the vibe and atmosphere is nice and relaxing, however the food is just OK. The famous burger wasn't anyway near as good as shake shack. Honestly, I it's just average pub fare.

The katsu curry was delcious! Â It was stick to your ribs good - LOVED it. Â A good portion for lunch although maybe 1 or 2 more pieces of katsu would be good :) Â The cabage salad I found kind of funny. Â A heaping mound of cabage with their salad dressing was a bit odd to me being served before my order...but I still enjoyed it anyway. The only thing negative I'd have to say is that our waitress ( short Indian lady) was unpleasant and forgot a round of water for the table. Â Hopefully you'll get another waiter to serve you who won't throw your green tea to the table. I was so full afterwards, I wanted to roll up in a ball and go to sleep. Â I'd definitely go back again - Kudos to no wait during lunch hours, either!

Had to chime in again to say that I had yet another fabulous meal at ABC Kitchen, this time for easter brunch. Started with the Roasted Beets which were tangy, decadent, and delicious. Moved onto the Roasted Carrot and Avocado Salad yet again (it was so great the first time I ordered it that I couldn't help but get it again), and the Scrambled Eggs with Crispy Potatoes for my entree. The eggs were perfectly cooked; creamy and delicious, simply prepared. The potatoes were super crispy (just how I like them), and made for a delicious morning meal. My dining partner ended with the infamous Salted Caramel Sundae and happily devoured the entire thing. Once again, the service was friendly and efficient, the food came out in perfect time and was nice and hot, and the atmosphere completes the whole experience. I can't get enough of this place!

You're FAMOUS! Â  Walk in -- server screams "**Insert Indecipherable Japanese Shout-Out HERE**" The place goes WILD ---**CLAP CLAP CLAP** !!!! ....and you haven't even been served a lick of food yet!! Know this: 1.) Â Ippudo's ramen is the BEST in NY. Â Period 2.) Â Their pork buns are INSANE 3.) Â Not since "Up With People" has your presence been so appreciated (nay, your every MOVE! Â Returning from even the bathroom can garner shouts and applause!!) Depending on how crowded it is, and on how many are in your party - you may sit privately in a spacious 3-sided booth --- or side-by-side at a table, communal style. Â It's ok. Â Slop away, friend! Â You will likely not make a wrong choice with the menu. Â You can also be a fatty (no, no fatty GOOD! Â Fatty gets APPLAUSE!!!) and get extra noodles if your server spots you with some leftover broth (minor up-charge, and WORTH IT!!!) Take out? Â Doggie bags? Â NOPE! Â SECRET FORMULA -- not to be distributed!!! Â I mean, c'mon -- Caucasian servers running around speaking Japanese? Â The broth is an edible ROSETTA STONE!!!! Â Of COURSE it's SECRET!!! Take my money. Â I love you.

Best meal I've had in a while - I cannot wait to go back! Â Spaghetti was to die for and I even loved the dessert (I am not a dessert person at all)! Â The waitress was great, very knowledgeable about the wine list and bought us different types to sample based on the flavors we were looking for.
Simply put: the best. Â Try the white pie with canadian bacon and pure maple syrup!

Meh.... I wanted to love this place and I really liked it. Well, I liked it. Â  I had read the reviews and searched out a couple of must eat local joints for my last trip to NYC and I was truly excited to eat here and well, it was solidly good but not great. Loved the fries but honestly, the burger I had at the Shake Shack was better. Â Nothing was amazing. Maybe I went in with too high of expectations, but I think it was underwhelming. Or - maybe it was the smug, unenthusiastic service. Our server was irritated by our presence. It was a late Monday afternoon - we ordered drinks, appetizers, dessert.... the whole shabang. You would think she'd be excited. No real recs on the food - as if I was supposed to know what they all tasted like. She dropped by the table every 10-to-15 to show how annoyed she was to be working. We were not allowed to order appetizers while we decided on the rest of the meal and sorta shamed for not knowing what we wanted immediately and actually have questions about the menu. Â  My tipping point was the tip. Split by credit card and cash, Â the waitress just assumed that the 30 percent cash was hers and charged the rest to the card as if she had done something Â - like be civil to deserve it. Â I would have been able to overlook the mistake but again - her response to my questioning was just snotty , Â so I made her reverse it. I waited after college and in grad so I am a big tipper. But, nobody has ever overpaid me to do a shitty job so I am not likely to return the favor. Â I wish I had not tipped her but the previous server in me could not do it.

Absolutely love Don Peppes. I grew up in Howard Beach and my family has been (and still is) going there for years. Since I moved to long island, I haven't been able to have decent clams casino in a while. :) Their linguine and clams is out of this world and its family style so there's enough to go around. They don't have much of a wine selection, its red or white. Thats it. They don't tell you what kind or where its from ha ha gotta love it.

Very tiny and quaint and I really liked the music here. The brie with pine nuts and honey made for a delicious appetizer. I loved the scallops with the cauliflower and brussels sprouts. I could probably eat it everyday. My friend like her salmon as well. The chocolate souffle was very yummy too.

Get down and dirty with your the seafood lover in you. This place isn't for the clean diner. You'll have to love your shellfish to full appreciate the freshness of the seafood at the boil. Everything still has it's head attached. And for seafood lovers, we know those are the best parts. The recipe is simple! Add fresh seafood, a plastic bag a secret sauce and presto! Magic in your mouth. Add a nice cold beer and I'm in heaven. The inky thing that I can complain about is that everyone else agrees with me. The lines are now supper long and I can't casually stroll in any more.

We started with our wine order, which our waiter promptly forgot. Returning 15 minutes later our waiter asked if we were ready to order. We asked about our wine order. He asked if we had ordered. (apparently a good memory is not a requirement to get hired here.) After 20 minutes he returned with our wine but no opener. Returning with an opener he poured a taste and promptly left. His hands would never touch our bottle again. (self serve at $45.00 bottles!) The unisex bathrooms are a wonderful game of guess who, is anyone in there? Seriously, there is no indicator to tell you whether one is occupied. Love knocking on bathroom doors. Really LOVE the communal sink, where diners can regale each other with their excitement. This IS haute cuisine in New York! After making reservations one month in advance I was thrilled when our food finally arrived. My thrill left quickly thereafter. Â Salumeria plate came with 3 tablespoon plods of buffalo mozzarella, 3 pieces each of sopressata, prosciutto, and salami. (who knows the origin, our waiter certainly didn't.) Eat! No questions! A menu of Italian heritage without salad! Genius! (if there is any salad it is displayed in as clandestine a fashion as possible.) A single ravioli the size of a Starbucks coffee lid. A pasta served with a room temperature rabbit sauce, scant pieces of rabbit meat that could have been quail, or squirrel, or chicken... The 3x3 pear cake and vanilla-less vanilla ice cream were too horrifying to be unforgettable. One of the absolute highlights, and wow, I am still recollecting, was when our waiter brought new clean plates and simply placed them on our table. Both my dinner date and I looked up from our scant appetizer plates and marveled at the glistening white plates laid before us. empty. pointless. Our waiter had the brilliant explanation that we would need them for our next course. BUT WHY WOULD HE EVER BRING THEM WITH OUR NEXT COURSE??? When recalling the blank stares, unanswered questions, and numerous expressions that said "I would rather be watching my DVR" I cannot contain myself. Â Honestly, Danny Meyer's restaurants are known for their service, but; what we received at Maialino was the complete opposite. I swear that at one point I thought I was being Punk'd or something. I have often wished for a fine dining experience in New York that left me trembling with hunger and feeling unsatisfied, completely. (this MUST be how supermodels dine) This was sooo much more fun than simply setting my money on fire in an alley. (The value was equivalent.) All in all I am concerned that Mr. Meyer has been coerced into licensing his name to some mega restaurant chain. This restaurant shares NOTHING in either quality or service with any of Mr. Meyer's other restaurants. I have dined multiple times at eleven madison, union square, and even tabla (when there was a tabla). I stand amongst the devoted who patiently line up in union square park for a shake shack burger. I cannot and will not stand for Maialino.

Ok, the Cuban sandwich was excellent! The pulled pork was juicy, the sauce was creamy and the bread was toasty crunchy! Also had the shrimp tacos, which were ok but I really liked their rice and beans. The roasted corn was delish, must order that.
I love this place. The backyard is nice and big, the bartenders friendly and I really really dig the burgers. This is the perfect summer place.

Balls deep in finals a couple of weeks ago, my friend and I vowed that once we made it through to the end of the semester we would make every Sunday a Sangria Sunday. Now that summer is here, we had our first Sangria Sunday at Calle Ocho. I couldn't believe how ginormous the place was! And the loud Cuban music made it so very festive. My friend and I split the Gallitos: scrambled eggs, corn tortillas, chorizo, home fries. The chorizo was nummy. I took full advantage of the unlimited Sangria bar. I had the tropical sangria and the roja and was feeling pretty good at the end of the meal. I will definitely come back with a larger crowd.
