This is the kind of place that separates the people who are truly passionate about food-coupled experiences from the people who are just into fancy food and restaurants. Johny's is one of the most New York places I've visited. If you you're looking for a real New York diner, you've found it. To me, that means a few no-nonsense guys behind the counter, putting orders together quickly, with a healthy dose of attitude. What it doesn't mean are fancy ingredients, unique flavors or surprising textures. Adjust your decision to visit accordingly.

I've had this place bookmarked for a while as a "must try". So on Saturday since I was in the neighborhood I decided to stop in for dinner around 6pm. There wasn't any wait time and from the moment we stepped in, the staff greeted us (always a plus). We were seated immediately. Service: Our waiter was just what you want your waiter to be. Attentive and available without being annoying. We did not feel rushed at anytime and he made sure to stop by periodically to make sure we were okay. My Aunt has a dairy allergy and the waiter took the time to go through the menu with her and even went back to the kitchen to be 100% sure the dishes they discussed did not include dairy. This was extremely comforting as most places just "remove the cheese" thinking we won't notice it or say something idiotic like "you can't taste it" which instantly pisses us off! Food: We started with drinks, a glass of wine for my Aunt and for me a mixed drink that I can not remember the name of, lol, BUT i liked the unique taste of ginger the drink had. My aunt ordered the Red Trout and I had the Sweet & Spicy Catfish. Can I just say we F'ed our dishes UP!!! The fish was fresh and cooked to perfection. My aunt especially enjoyed her trout. I mean come on who can hate anything that involves bacon! My catfish was awesome as well. Being a southern girl I always find that most restaurants try to do way too much with catfish and it overpowers the true taste of the fish. But not Blue Ribbon. The balance was just right. Price: Some may think they're over priced but for the quality of food I think they were quite reasonable. The portion sizes were big enough and I was more than satisfied. I couldn't eat dessert because I would have been over the edge. Overall this is definitely going on my list of "go to spots".

Brunch is delicious. Â Hot chocolate is good; we usually get the eggs benedict and eggs w/ salmon with french toast / waffles on the side. Â Wait is long but if you can catch this place with a short line, the quality of the food and value is worth 5 stars.
great beer selection, good food, good music. Â Great addition to UES

OMG by far the best Macaroon place EVER. I Never ever liked macaroons because the ones I've tried were always too sweet or too soggy or just plain not good. that is until....i found Laduree!!! I have never had a yummy Macaroon unitl I found this place. In the summer time, definetly get the ice cream with macaroon on top. Seriously, the best dessert EVER. I have tried most of the flavors but all of them are delicious! If you can, try them ALL!! you would be in LOVE!

Tiny bar menu, really short. The fries could have cooked a couple more minutes, but tasty enough. The pork bun was OK. Service at the bar was pretty quick, by a pretty bartender. There was a decent sized crowd who seemed to be having a good time. Are we coming back? Don't know. There are so many other exciting places in East Village.

I couldn't stop smiling for 15 minutes. "Stop smiling, you moron. I was so embarrassed I can't tell you! It seemed that all the 25 people in the room were having fun at my expense. The ribbing went on and on. " But, there are times that nothing can make you stifle the mirth inside, and insensitive that I must have seemed to my oldest and dearest friend this side of the Atlantic, I burst out laughing. She was annoyed because at a party someone had asked her about restaurants, and she had mentioned a particular one where she had dined with me. Almost as an after thought, she had also spoken about the owner and how he had a nice, deep voice. Bang. Out came the knives. "I KNEW it was you! Even though Atif didn't mention your name in his review, we were all certain that it could only be you." Hearing which every one started laughing, and inquiring whether she still carried a crush on the owner :) My dear friend was shocked to learn that not only did I review restaurants, but that some people actually read those reviews! This despite the fact that I had mentioned my yelping to her many moons ago. Sadly, it is the people who are closest to you, that never give you enough credit for growth. Their perception of us is still stuck at a point in time and the resulting mental image doesn't change till they get a rude jolt. So, thank you, yelp for giving me the platform to do the mature act of sticking my thumb out at all the cynical friends, who endured my painful and obstinate insistence on a better dining establishment with jokes like: "Chill! You've got zag_t up your ass"! To, all you cynics: nyah nyah nyah nyah... pffft! :P And to all you yelpers, Thank you.... you like me, right now, you really like me! Ok, ok, so how is this related to Lupa? My friend (above) and I got 'I, Robot' as our server when we visited. "The man couldn't care if we were dead or alive or whether he had bumped an elbow into us while retreating from the table right next to us". Said my friend who is an active follower of 'The Art of Living', and one of the most laid back people one can ever find in life. Â Unsmiling throughout, it appeared that Mr. Sourpuss hated to be there that day and would probably have had a great career in the arts if it weren't for serving ingrates like us. He had trouble responding to our questions on the menu choices, had to be asked about the bread, and disappeared for lengths of time. Finally, when I ordered their (sublime) Tartufo for dessert, he had the temerity of asking me whether or not I should ask my friend first, before doing so!!!! Being a Mario Batali establishment you obviously are going to get good to great food. The dishes that are popular here include: Beets with Pistachio, cured meats (Prosciutto, coppi), Ricotta Gnocchi with sausage and fennel, Bucatini All' Amatriciana, Pork Saltimbocca... so for vegetarians and people who don't eat pork (moi), selection can be somewhat limited. But a sublime dining experience extends beyond the food to the ambience and service. Given the indifferent service, chattering crowds, lack of room and absence of a sense of relaxation, Lupa has "Miles to go before I sleep". Go for Lunch, I say.

I'm beginning to lose trust in the taste buds of my fellow Brooklyn Yelpers... This place was SUCH A DISAPPOINTMENT! The bf and I decided to go to Tom's for brunch yesterday. The food was TERRIBLE! This is how it went down: Let's begin with the syrup...the moment I began pouring I noticed the thick glue like consistency and it immediately grossed me out, I couldn't believe one can gag with syrup, well I did...oh and it was also tasteless. The french toasts looked like they had been pressed by an iron --I have no idea why. I took my first bite and that was the last, the french toasts were extremely hard and tasted old, just like the bacon and the syrup. The bacon was far from crunchy, instead it was hard and even difficult to chew. The scramble eggs were burnt and DRY! The cinnamon and banana pancakes were too doughy and only had 2 slices of bananas per pancake. The guy who took our order and never came back to our table, oh yea, I think you call those waiters, did not wait on us at all, we had to ask someone else for our bill. Total bad experience, $25 down Tom's diners drain. We will never bother to come back. Oh and that "only cash" deal is just inconvenient, stop being cheap and take credit cards, it's 2012!!!

Back when the Coast Guard was stationed on Governers Island this was a regular hang out spot for the Coasties. Years later we still frequent this spot as it is our official going away lunch spot for departing members! Sit at the Chefs table and try their Shepard's pie! The staff is friendly and the crowd is mature. You can feel the history around you. Great selection of beers too! Get the Oyster Stout.

Please keep in mind that I went in on a regular workweek Sunday evening. The place was relatively quite, and laid back (which is typical for a Sunday evening anywhere). The lighting was really poor and contributed greatly to my feeling that they really didn't want people staying there for too long that night. The staff were as attentive as they should be (with nobody really around), and were generally courteous. I really didn't try any of those drinks that other folks were raving about in their reviews. This was mostly because I had an expectation that the bartender was going to make us aware of any types of drink specialties the place may offer. Overall, the place is about as 'meh' as you can get.
Fine dining and standard prices. Food was very good I see why they are called Taste Good... Â Very affordable.

OMG OMG OMG OMG!!! AMAZING!!! You will want to stuff yourself like a complete fatass, and have them roll you home, because the food here is sooooooooo freakin' good!!! I cannot possibly express how amazing it is! One week, I ate lunch there 3 days in a row! Just thinking about it makes me want to go back now!!!

Ippudo still rules in my book (and San Francisco is sorely lacking in awesome ramen digs), but Totto hit the spot. Â The mid-town/center of insanity location is an odd place to find a place like this, but I was happy to find it and thrilled the ramen was really, really good. Why not great? Â The broth, while very, very good, doesn't measure up to Ippudo's. Â The noodles were perfectly prepared, pork was very good and the usual ramen accoutrements were all there in good measure. The space is small and seating is predominantly at the bar facing the cook/prep area. Â Service is fast and accommodating. Â This is an awesome stop if you love ramen!

Went here with two coworkers who raved about the burgers. I was a bit surprised the menu didn't include a turkey burger, but was happy to settle for the veggie burger instead (chickpeas, in case you're wondering). I have to say, I think Morningstar has a leg up on this place when it comes to veggie burgers. Mine was mushy, lukewarm and bland. The saving grace was delivered in the French fries, which were nicely salted. After seeing two other tables gulp down milkshakes I decided to order the root beer float and was a bit disappointed that it was merely your basic root beer float: root beer and a scoop of ice cream. Good, but nothing I couldn't get at Arby's for 1/3 of the price. The restaurant itself was like a meat locker - absolutely freezing. It's rather unusual for a restaurant to crank the air conditioning in mid-October, but that's exactly what Burger & Barrel was doing (and the temperature outside was in the low 70s, so no need). There are so few quality dining options for lunch in Soho, so I really had my hopes up for this one...but I think I'm going to keep brown bagging for awhile.

Ask for the pizza well done in order to get that crispy, chewy crust. The crust has a nice flavor. Pepperoni pizza was the best... the pepperoni was nicely charred and crispy. Our server had an attitude ... a bitch actually... the faces she made and her responses were downright rude. My husband, who is a very friendly person, wanted to tell her off but refrained for fear of her spitting on our pizza.

Great new SoHo spot where Country Cafe used to be... They've redone the space and it's adorable. I can't totally determine whether you'd call Vin et Fleur a wine bar or a restaurant. They have an all-French wine list of interesting picks, as well as a short French menu. We had the endive salad, mussels, and chicken paillard. Everything was delicious! A couple of complaints... Our waitress didn't have any suggestions about the wine list, and either the A/C wasn't on or perhaps they don't have A/C... it's very warm in there! Regardless, I'll be back when it cools down outside for amazing Frenchified eats at a reasonable price. SO much better than Cafe Felix down the street.

Surprising little gem in a quiet section of Greenpoint. I was drawn to this place based on the yelp reviews for their burgers, and while I didn't try the burger, others in my party seemed to enjoy them. Located in a narrow store front, there doesn't appear to be much seating inside, but you'd be surprised. The best part was the outdoor garden where we enjoyed our 330 brunch. While the menu was somewhat limited, they definitely offered a solid variety of breakfast and lunch favorites. I went with the chicken parm sandwich and the fries. The fries were AMAZING. Large steak fries that were cooked very well and not mushy. Â One of my friends boasted it was one of the best bloody Mary's he's had in NY. I stuck with the craft beer myself. Â The bacon was very good too. Unfortunately this place is extremely out it the way if you're traveling by subway. Nevertheless I will return if I ever make it back to that part of the hood.

Nook gets a solid 5 for the food, especially given how not expensive it is. So, how does a restaurant get only a 2-star rating with 5-star food? Simply put, they crowd the tables in so tightly that your meal is interrupted a dozen times to shift yourself and your table so other diners can get in or out of their seats. The crowding also means it's very loud, nearly impossible to have a conversation. I can't imagine Nook as a date spot, unless you and your date really enjoy not talking to each other and dragging tables around. If you're really lucky, you can get the table that gets hit by the front door every time anyone enters or exits the restaurant.

I literally wanted to eat everything on the menu. And I almost did. I tried the chicken biscuit, the gumbo, mac and cheese, pork belly cracklin, deviled eggs, and steak. My favorites were the chicken biscuit, gumbo, and the steak. You seriously cannot go wrong with this place. I wish I could eat the chicken biscuit every day.
This place is Thunderdome.

We came here twice during our week in NYC. It's as everyone has described, hole in the wall, off the beaten path restaurant. First time I got pan fried noodles with chicken. Chicken was pretty bland but the noodles were amazing. My mom got the shrimp with the knife shaped noodles. Second time back we brought my daughter with us. We were the only ones in restaurant for early dinner (around 430). It started off well enough. We ordered. I got the pan fried again but this time with beef. Daughter got the chicken and mom got some kind of seafood that I can't remember. We went with canned soda's this time because the water on the table is lukewarm and they don't have ice. We also ordered dumplings. Our food came out and there was no dumplings (first visit we got dumplings as an appetizer). I asked waitress when they would be coming out. She said "right away". Ok. We start eating. About 1/2 way through still no dumplings. By then a few tables were filling up. Waitress was hanging out in back. I finally got up to find her to ask her about the dumplings. She had a shocked look on her face then looked at our order ticket (like I hadn't ordered them) and said "they will be right out". No sorry, nothing. 5 min later another waitress brings them to the table, sets them down and walks away! Â She also never brought us our bill. Â We sat for a good 10-15 min with our empty plates in front of us obviously ready to go and she never came over. I had to get up and ask her for our bill. Needless to say she didn't get much of a tip. Our service had been much better on our prior trip. Unfortunately the bad service left us with a bad impression even though we loved the noodles!

When you're in the mood for something exotic and sophisticated at a quiet neighborhood restaurant, Miriam is the place to go. After going for dinner a handful of times, I've decided the way to do it is just to order all (or most of) the meze dishes instead of an entree. For some reason, I always end up enjoying these more than my main, and pricewise you'll come out even. They're flavorful even though they're small, and the variety is nice. My favorites: burekas, falafel, merges sausage, hummus and babaganoush. I've also been for brunch several times, and this is where they shine (and also make a ton of money judging from the line out the door on a Saturday morning). The Israeli breakfast succeeds where other brunches fail--it's a lot of food, but you don't leave feeling grossly full. My big complaint? Brunch is "cash only", while they take credit cards all other times (a practice I loathe on principle).
Get the cuban empanadas and the sancocho (ox tail soup) was delicious. Its big enough to be shared with two but it a little small place so when its packed theres no place to move.

I liked the elegance of the place, but have to say the dishes aside from 1 didn't "wow" me here. Â Dined a few weeks back, and don't remember much of that dinner besides awesome company and the meal delivered with a hefty price tag. The one memorable dish though(and my only reason to go back) was absolutely amazing. Â Unfortunate my friend's dish and not mine, the trofie nero was absolutely delicious, and definitely one of the best pasta I've ever eaten. Â I felt bad when all of us took a sample bite and I went back for my third bite! (it was THAT good) Will go back... just for the trofie nero next time!

The ambiance is definitely there. But is it authentic thai food? Nope. So don't come in with that expectation. Drinks on point. I'm big on asian cuisine so I felt like the food lacked flavoring, everything is made light to cater to other folks but being that I have tried authentic thai cooking before I could tell the difference. Thai ice tea (a drink I always try at every thai restaurant) isn't that great, a bit too bitter for my taste.
The food is wonderful here and they have the best Meat and Cheese plate. Â My only dislike: Limited seating areas and cramped areas.

I am not a huge fan of American brunch...and this place does not meet the standards of the best brunch places I have been to in NYC...So, in terms of food, this place is average. However, I would like to say it is a very quaint place, the setting is a bit traditional. The manager (maybe?) appears to be French. The service is definitely nice, they are very attentive -- I did not try any sangria myself, but my dining buddy definitely enjoyed it. For $13.95 including brunch + sangria/mimosa/coffee, it's not a bad deal in NYC.
amazing food. great atmosphere. I loved this place. all the waiters were so helpful. its a great date place bc its so quaint. Has a great neighborhood feel to it.

Came here with a few peeps. The bar gets pretty crowded, and it's probably not that worth it if you're unable to get a seat. The library on the other hand, is fantastic and has a nice, classy speakeasy vibe to it. The drinks are mostly pretty standard tasting, and a bit on the pricey end -- but hey you're paying for the ambiance. My friends got some pretty weird tasting drinks (one tasted like smoke...), but I got lucky and loved mine (Mott & Mulberry). Would definitely recommend checking out the Library and getting the Mott & Mulberry at least once.

It always confuses me when coffee shops try to bake their own goods for the sake of saying they're homemade. I say let the experts do their thing and focus on the coffee! Such is the case at Blue Spoon Cafe. They have croissants from Ceci Cela (voted NYC's best croissant) and other baked goods from Balthazar. The coffee is wonderful - I had a cortado and the friendly barista put a heart design in it. Get the coffee card - 10 drinks gets you a free one.

LOVE THE MUSSELS AND THE FRIES! Â You pick one of the Â 3-4 sauces to go with your mussels-- I'm on a quest to try all of them. Â The pesto and tomatoes sauce was delish-- I even ate the tomatoes and I usually hate tomatoes (or any veggies for that matter). The fries that accompany the mussels are one of the best I tried...yummy. Ironically, everything was great except for my pasta dish, but it's okay, I was full by then... Oh..I love how they're open until 2 am.! Why can't they have restaurants like that in the bay area?

I am an avid history buff and when visiting NY wanted to get a little "old time" in. The place is great from a true to life history setting. Sure, there are anachronistic touches, but those of us in the modern world wouldn't want all the benefits of sanitation of the 1700's. The service was spotty. While Kaitlynn did a good job of saving it, the first waiter that came by the table and took my order really ignored me as a customer. I ordered the Chicken Pie. It was more than just a pot pie, with a deeper flavor than you usually expect. The crust was a little doughy around the edges, but when paired with the ingredients inside was quite tasty. The chicken meat inside was of differing sizes and consistency- which I mean as a positive. There was both dark meat, which lent the better flavor, and big chunks of chicken breast. Lots of mushrooms, carrots and celery were in it without the filler of potatoes (at least I didn't notice them). It comes paired with a nice fresh salad. The dinner was $18, which I felt was well worth it. I opted not to have any dessert as $9 for apple pie seemed a bit steep and I had no one to share it with. Lots of options on the menu ranging from salads and burgers up to $81 steaks for two. A couple of different bars were available, and looked to have a full selection- the whiskey bar had a whole wall filled with choices. I would return. I wanted to see the upstairs museum, but it closes early.

Astoria's best seafood and worst management. Seriously, a 90 min wait that end up being 3 hours shouldnt be rewarded with eating there. People used to say they went to Elias Corner in spite of the service, but this place goes to new levels. New Yorker's mania for going to "the best place" in spite of the wait etc has hit Queens. Seriously, If you can stomach the clamor of a three hour wait (or "90 minutes" in "Greek time") you will love this place...

How often do you think about sadness? Like, what is really the cause of unrelenting sadness? Is misery a disease? Is my brain just broken? I've never put cheese on top of curry before I started eating here and now I am lactose intolerant. It is very sad.

I'm not an NYC native, but I was in town to visit my cousin and her husband. They decided to take us here and man oh man, this was just a fantastic dining experience. Everything from the food to the service to the timing was really great. I've been told tasting menus are the big thing in New York at the moment, so that's what we ended up doing. We were brought 7 perfectly sized and well spaced out portions including a fantastic cinnamon donut for dessert. The meal highlights were buckwheat noodles and a really yummy seafood stew. The wine pairings were great too. I'd go over every dish we had, but it sounds like the menu changes so frequently that it's quite likely they won't be on the menu when YOU go. Really, just go try it. You won't regret it. It was more expensive than we were expecting - it ended up being about $125 a head with the wine pairings. Definitely worth being aware of.

Went here for brunch recently, and it was really tasty. The food was terrific, and my friends and I had a great time. It got really crowded, though, so I'd definitely recommend getting there early or going with a reservation.

Great place for dinner. I've been here several times and I've probably enjoyed myself more and more each time I've gone. The restaurant is very nice, with friendly wait staff, a chatty atmosphere and good food. For those that haven't had Greek food before, definitely don't shy away. Kefi has a great menu with lots of options, so you'll find something you should like. I highly recommend the meatball appetizer and pretty much any of the pasta dishes. I've been here with small and big groups and the service has always been really good, with attentive waiters. One of my favorite parts of this place is that it's relatively inexpensive. Almost all of the entrees are under $20 and they're all delicious and filling. A great place to check out.

Brunch Review I am beginning to really love/hate the small plate concept. small plates don't always equal small prices. you sometimes just feel ripped off. Â Don't get me wrong, I LOVE tapas but not everything should come in a tiny plate! I think this entire review should be like their food, small but somewhat so-so satisfying. Good- gorgeous room Good- outstanding lattes/capps Ugly- bad furniture - hair higher than bottom of table, no legs go under Bad- tiny plates where food overwhelms plate space Bad- lack of kitchen - should be warm things are cold Good- though tiny, very filling (for a girl) BUT chicks would dig it BECAUSE - server was adorable in his apron - the cutesy-ness overwhelms the mediocrity and being a chick, I speak for all chicks. Â I will go back despite a so-so experience because it was so damn cute!
My first time at this restaurant. Â As soon as I was seated, they brought a cup of tea without asking. Â It was free. Just had #65 Hommade fish cake end cut soup $5.95. Â It was excellent.

One thing that you should get if you've got a big party is the whole lechon. Something that some friends always get for the holidays. The changes I've seen in the past years is the price of the bread being a little higher than it's competition. I'd still go here for fresh PanDeSal.

this place gets CROWDED so def make a reservation. Â kinda interesting..they bring you both sparkling and still water here and i don't believe they charge you extra. Â also, the extra large carafe is apparently a glass and a half more than a bottle of wine, which makes it an awesome deal. Â my friend had the mussels and fries which smelled amazing, and i chose the korean bim bim bop. Â unfort, they didnt have all the condiments that go along with korean food, so i wasn't all that stoked on my entree. Â however, the bacon and cream pizza appetizer was so good! Â the staff here is really sweet, and they sent over a bowl of homemade chips when they noticed that our appetizer hadn't come out yet. an awesome replacement for the UNO that used to be here!

Lupa "Osteria Romana" is the laid-back little brother of Babbo, that wildly successful pan-Italian brainchild of Mario Batali. Since this is a *Roman* restaurant, the focus here is on the cuisine of Rome's home region--Lazio. I've been here a few times, and--with the exception of one Friday night--found getting a table without a reservation to be remarkably easy. It's a dimly-lit space, fashionably cramped, with a bustling bar area. But I'm here to review the food because, well, that's just about all I really remember--after all, it's been over a year since I lived in these parts. My ordering was a little unconventional--my standard would consist of two "piatti primi," part of the "pasta" course of a full Italian meal, but perhaps their categorization of the menu was unconventional, because no pasta is to be found in their veal sweetbreads. So, on with a brief overview of what I'd have each time I'd go: 1. Bucatini all'amatriciana: a hearty dish of plump spaghetti-like noodles, rich with tomato, onion, and guanciale--smoked pig cheeks. Really, it's not terribly different from bacon, and that smoky chewiness is what makes the dish. Supposedly it's one of their most popular items. 2. Animelle (veal sweetbreads): Sauteed in beurre-noisette, with ramps (a type of leek). The brown butter gives a smoky flavor to the sweetbreads--hey, don't hate on thymus glands, they're grrrrreat! I seem also to remember there having been something like pecans or almonds in the crisp coating. In any event, they're divinely succulent and have a texture that is somewhat intermediate between a chicken breast and a properly-cooked liver. 3. Spiced Apician Dates with Mascarpone: It is what they say it is. 'Nuff said. Service, as I remember it, was attentive but dry. Frankly, my dear, I don't give a damn, because it's the food that counts.
Outstanding food and friendly and funny service staff. Â Great lunch specials. The Vindaloo is REALLY spicy!
very nice, small but cozy. and the food was good

I had a friend who came to town at the last minute and made reservations here for dinner. While the interior has all the necessary pieces for a bougie setting - red leather couches, brass touches - it isn't enough to allow you to forget that you're next door to a place that serves a signature artichoke pizza. The crowd looks to be 90% financiers. The service was surprisingly lacking. Nothing terrible; a drink forgotten, few check-ins, receiving a side salad when we were halfway through our meal. Still, I expected more. We ordered the oysters as an appetizer, which were good if not memorable. For an entree, we split the cote de boef with sides of pommes anna and spinach. The sides were nothing to write home about, but the beef was very good. The bone marrow that it came with was undercooked; when I pay $140 for an entree, I expect it to be properly cooked. Overall, the experience was underwhelming. I would come back if I were in the area, but I won't be bringing out-of-town guests here again.

I almost missed the store when I walked by E Broadway. But then from the street I caught a glimpse of the man tossing and pulling noodles so I knew that this was the place. I ordered beef noodle soup and it came in a split second. In front of me was this big bowl of noodle with thick flavorful broth waiting for me to devour every inch of it. So I did. The noodle was great, although they are slightly uneven sliced. Nothing to complain about, just that some of the strands are cooked more than the others. The slices of beef were yummy, and the best of it all is the broth. I drank mine and licked the bowl clean. It's not the best la mien I've had in my life, but it certainly is good, especially to a New York standard. $4.50 for a bowl of noodles and you got more than what you've paid for. Very good experience, and I'll be coming back to try the minced pork and dry noodles.

Dark but not mysterious... just a hot spot off the beaten path. Â Went there late night when the place was packed and ended up sitting outside, which turned out to be pleasant until it turned a certain time and a guy who worked there had to usher us back into the darkness. Â I mean, dark IS sexy and nice but not when you can't see the company you're with and have to hold on for dear life to each other so you don't get separated in the abyss. Â Might be a nice stop in the earlier part of an evening when it's not so packed and bumpin'.

Wow. What a fantastic restaurant. My mother was in town visiting from Boston and I was planning on taking her to my go-to Apiary (see review) but they were booked, so I opted for Hearth. I have been meaning on trying this restaurant for a while, but was always torn away by the $$$$ open table gives it. MAN was it worth it - and wasn't nearly as expensive as I was thinking. Amazing cuisine, innovative, fresh, organic, farm to table. Service was a bit on the casual side, but our focus was so revolved around the food, it didn't matter. I hear the menu changes daily (or rather frequently), based on what is available at the markets, etc - regardless every dish we had was fantastic! Atmosphere is casual yet sophisticated and cozy - perfect for a winter date night ;) Hope you all enjoy this place just as much as me and don't be afraid of the $$$$ that open table gives it!

I don't care what anyone else says, this is the best brunch in Williamsburg. I'm always surprised that this place seems to be a lot less busy than Egg or Dumont but I prefer it by far. A strong solid cup of coffee, a bellini, Â fluffy goat cheese omelette, and a fresh fruit salad and I'm in heaven! Wait staff is always attentive and friendly. The decor is cute, simple, and a little bit retro. Hooray to Walter Foods!

Excellent place - I found the service very good, takes a little more time to get your order but they really take their time to make it fresh. Â Everyone was very friendly and seemed very happy too. Â I ordered the falafel sandwich - very generous portion for $4. Â  The falafels themselves are made very well - the hot sauce adds a lot to the sandwich as well. Â I had a side order of french fries - not that great but they were OK. Â  I would love to come back and try some of their other items - looked awesome. Â Its a comfortable and decent sized place.

Ok, I kick started my Yelping with a rant, so I might as well start reviewing all the places I've been saying "I'm gonna Yelp" for the past, um, 6 months or so. I had eaten at Sanford's once before they closed for renovation, and it was meh. The food was alright, but definitely in the diner category, and I remember service sucking. This is definitely not the same restaurant in any capacity. The first thing you'll notice is how pretty it is, even from the outside. They also have their (extensive) menu displayed in a case out front. Brownie points for being open 24/7. When you walk in, you no longer feel like you're entering a diner, as you did before the renovation - it's the farthest thing from it now. Earthy wooden walls, mosaic tiled entryway, contemporary decor but with a very warm approach. Back to the menu. Honestly, everything sounded appealing to me...and when I say everything, that's saying a lot considering how many options they have. I chose the organic rotisserie chicken entree, which came with 2 sides and a salad. My friends both got sandwiches (one wrap and one flatbread) and they were given a potato option and soup or salad as well (we weren't expecting so many sides, especially for an $8 wrap....great value). All of the food was tasty and we had no issues with any of our dishes (I am Miss Bad Food Karma, so this makes me happy). More brownie points and surprises: One of my friends had chosen chips as their potato. I was flat out expecting Lays. They brought out a plate of fresh made potato chips. Amazing. Service WAS something to write home about. Waitress was alert and friendly. Waters were filled before empty, and dishes were cleared promptly. I will definitely go back. I will re-review and potentially award a 5th star if the service and food keeps up (I hope!).
Wonderful coffee! Friendly staff. I will return.

This food is on par with what I had in Rome. Â Fantastic, fresh, very reasonably priced, warm service from the lovely owner. Â The homemade pastas and cannolis were to die for! Â This would be a great spot for a romantic dinner date. Â It's not in a scenic neighborhood, but perfectly safe, despite being a little sketchy-looking when you're walking from the train. Â Go forth, and support this awesome local business!

I was a little afraid to come here last week b.c of the dreaded wait time but fortunately we went a little before the lunch rush. When the hostess took us to our table we were greeted by the entire staff - I wanted to mention this because it caught me off guard while I was attempting to check into this place on yelp. Â  To begin we got a round of the pork and chicken buns. Â I don't eat pork so didn't try that but I did have the chicken buns which were great. Â The chicken is mildly spicy and has some mayo. For the ramen since I don't like/eat pork, Â I went with the vegetarian. Â The bowl it was in was a bit high, Â I wound up using an extra seat cushion so I could properly eat. Â I'm short so trying to eat out of a high bowl was a bit of a struggle. Â I have to say while the ramen was good, it wasn't the world changing experience I was anticipating per the previous yelp reviews. Â  The broth was a bit heavy on the bitter side but I'm assuming this is because it's a soy based sauce. Â  Our server was great, she had accidentally spilled water near me but was quick about getting everything cleaned up and brought me a green tea ice cream to make up for it. Â  Overall I had a great experience here. Â If I was forced to wait 2 hrs before trying ramen here I would probably have been extremely disappointed. Â I would come here again but only while there isn't a wait.

What a fun night! Kiwiana is a cute, quaint and lovely restaurant with a mountain of charm. Â  The space is small yet sufficient and is a bit rustic, country and elegant. I noticed someone had there wedding reception here and I could easily see it being the perfect space for a small brunch reception. The food is simple but exceeds your expectations with every bite. Â On my visit, my date and I had the soup of the day, butternut squash. It wasn't atypical but lovely nonetheless. The white bait with lemon and tarter was a treat. Â The malpeque oysters tasted as if they were directly from the sea. Â The star was the fried chicken dish which came with three perfectly seasoned and crispy pieces. Â  I looked over the dessert menu but couldn't force another bite. Â It looked amazing and my eyes wandered down to the date sticky toffee so now Kiwiana is on the top of my "go back for seconds" list. Â  The service and ambience is cool and I would highly recommend for a casual dinner night. I don't know what it is, but Kiwiana makes me wanna smile.

Great pre or post theater spot. Â As mentioned - BYOB (do yourself a favor and stop by 9th Ave Vintners and not the overpriced liquor store a block south of Nook), tiny, and cash only. Â One of the tastiest and least expensive filet mignons in midtown - seriously, I dream about that filet and the red wine reduction that accompanies it. Â Mushroom cigars and pepper crusted tuna are also standouts. Â Fun, different "hidden gem" type spot that's perfect for impressing family (or your significant other's family) who've bought tickets to a Broadway show and you want to treat to a nice dinner without breaking the bank.

Great value, with respect to the quality of beers - really well priced. I went to the Double Windsor with 2 friends on a hot & humid Saturday at around 5:30pm, so it wasn't crowded at all - maybe at 40% of capacity. We went to pregame, do a few shots and grab a bite before heading to the Siren Music Festival on Coney Island...sponsored by Bud - so we went to get a buzz with good, quality, strong beers. The Windsor afternoon crowd was mixed, from age 22 to 62, everyone was just chillin, having burgers, salads and having a good time. Seemed like a no stress spot you could drink at all day. The bartender was this really laid back easy going type who didn't say much...except to suggest a good beer. Most beers were strong and cheap - good bang for the buck. The cider beer was also quite nice. The Whiskey shots were $5 each and the service was quick. Likes: - Great quality beer selection - The inexpensive beer flight (sampler) - Great burger - Easy going staff - Good atmosphere - Good service - burger came out fairly quickly - Close to the train station (1 block) Dislikes: - N/A It's definitely a good spot worth checking out, there is no sign, so it's a little incognito and plain Jane, but it works well. Extra points: I left my favorite hat there, I called 20 minutes later and they grabbed it and held it all night until one of my friends could pick it up...nice customer one service. I will definitely be back again, next time I will get the Ribs, they looked AWESOME. Happy Drinking!

So the main reason to come here is for the fried chicken; and of course you are going to want to get the fried chicken spicy. Â But a word of advice; build up to the Extra Spicy Fried Chicken. Â It's something else; not that it's not worth it. Â But that it isn't for a novice.

ive been here twice i like perilla. the duck meatballs are seriously to die for. very good. i just wish there were more. as for my entrees, i ordered the steak the first time. it was good. i wasn't blown away by it honestly. the second time i ordered the dory in a green curry sauce (phenomenal). i say steer clear of the steak. i've had better steak in other restaurants, but the green curry was light and not too spicy. perfect complement to the fish :) i'm always up for going to perilla!

Tried out their two kinds of wonton (ordered as one dish) and their steamed jiao zi (dumpling). Was very impressed. Even though three could all share the same fillings but the restaurant made an effort to highlight one dominant flavor in each by their names: the shrimps (two in each!) in the small wonton, the pork meat in the large wonton, and the chive in the jiao zi. Each filling is a little more complex in terms of the number of ingredients they used, which might put off some traditionalists. The ambiance was also good and the stoneware and chopstick holder add another nice touch.

OMG!!! This is a FANTASTIC brunch spot, and while I want to save it for myself, it happens to be too good not to share. The food is delicious, especially the Pecan Pie French Toast! I only gave them a 4/5 because of the decor and the noise level. The place is VERY plain, and looks unfinished, and not in a very posh way. As for the noise I understand and even enjoy a lively establishment, however hearing the music blaring over brunch is a bit much, especially when it's "get down on it", which I find oddly inappropriate for an 11am brunch on Sunday. Overall, give this place a try and see what you think...

Despite all the dining choices available in Manhattan, we still always find ourselves having a meal at Joe's Shanghai. Â They've got some of the best xiao long bao (aka soup dumpling) outside of Asia. Â  Come here and order yourselves a steamer or two of the pork & crab dumplings. Â The fat shanghai noodles are also very good and so are the rice cakes. Â Joe won't do you wrong, so go ahead and give him a shot.

A few weeks ago, I joined some friends for a brunch at this restaurant I had heard and read so much about. I was very excited to finally tried it..........Starting with an excellent coffee ( the coffee is a really really good coffee!!!!) and well seated in a very vibrant space .....I looked over the menu but It was so hard to make a choice. everything looked so appetizing Â Finally our matronly , ' I'm tough and I' m not taking any shit kind of attitude " took the order. I guess it is part of the charm when restaurants make you feel they do Â a favor to serve you. .....But the favor stopped there and it's me and my friends who did them a favor to accept the food they served us. The pancakes were burned to the ground and I mean burn !!!! The poached egg Huntington was half hard boiled seating on a mealy and floury biscuit covered with a non descript Hollandaise sauce, the short ribs hash was simply boiled meat. Never had the chance to taste their drinks. We ordered them, asked again , but they never came.....;)
I love this place. Â When you get lunch, they always throw in a bunch of free crap, and I'm super-cheap, so I like that. Â The food is great, despite the opinion of some reviewers here. Â Me likey.

Ate here for the the first time tonight and it quickly has jumped to the top of our favorite Fort Greene restaurants. Â  The cooking was just perfect -- absolutely fresh ingredients with simple tasty accompaniments and sauces. Â  Favorites were the snap peas with mint, Â the grilled octopus, and the roast carrot dish. Â The dark chocolate pot au creme was yummy. Â  Great vibe to the place -- chef/owner Matt is super friendly and it's the kind of neighborhood place where you expect to see people you know.

A small hidden gem in the UES, I found Heidi's House after a trip to the Met. Seating was cozy and tight, and the lighting was dim for food photography but great for happy hours. Speaking of happy hour, they have a great selection of beer and the owner really knew her beer. "What's good here?" "Everything is good here." That is actually the only correct response for a restaurant. If there is something that's not good here, why serve it? I was considering a cider originally, but was convinced to get an Allagash white beer that did not disappoint. We ordered the mini guacamole to share, but they accidentally gave us a regular-sized order. Mildly spicy and addictive, we finished the entire plate (it would have been wasteful otherwise). For my main, I got a mini mac and cheese with bacon. Cheesy, creamy, salty, crispy, it was everything I would wanted my mac and cheese to be. I left the place a few pounds heavier, heartier, and happier.
Best tacos I have ever had, they are amazing. I just wish they would expand the'r delivery range. They would get so much more business if they delivered to Bed-Stuy. Come on guys! Don't discriminate!

We went here for dinner with a party of 12 people. We chose the pre fix menu. The food was great, but the attitude towards some of the things that happened was just unacceptable. One person was vegan. Besides charging the normal rate per person, they charged an additional 40 dollars because they made her roasted vegetables. We loved the falafels and ordered an extra portion. When they are making so much money off a table, you would expect that to be free of charge. But it wasn't it. One person did not show up, but they still charged for that person. The lack of flexibility and greed were really astonishing. I used to go to this restaurant and pay a bill of around 60-70 per person. This day it cost us 140. Perhaps the price of a star Michelin restaurant. I would not go back and would not recommend it to anyone else.
Delicious!

Landed in here last night for dinner and we had a great time. Â Fantastic service, great food and solid attention to detail with the Thai flavours. Â The menu has good selection and the interior is very warm and welcoming. Â It might be my new favourite Thai place and it is definitely the best newest secret in UES/Yorkville. Â Definitely, go! I know I will go back! Â Thanks Up Thai!

Went yesterday and fell in love!! Delicious food, healthy organic ingredients , in a great space-- what more could you want.?? I had the red rice, chicken salad and kale salad with Â a bottle of the homemade pomegranate iced tea. Â Yummm!! Would reccomend to anyone and everyone!!

Best ragu I've had yet, and at a reasonable price. I'm not sure why people complain about the "pricey-ness" of the restaurant. Have they not tried Michael White's other restaurants? The other pastas Â were very good, as well, though perhaps on the salty side. All in all, this is by far the most cost accessible MW restaurant. From a value perspective, I love this place.

I came here for a dinner of 4 and the food was great! I got the homemade beef lasagna and it was good meanwhile 3 of my other friends for the penne with mushroom. They were all delicious. We had the mushroom pizza? for appetizer and some salad. The bread they gave us was pretty salty.. I did read it in other reviews that some of the food was salty but I didn't taste too much salt on my entrees, if anything the bread was just blehh.. I do recommend this place for sure! I had white pinot grigo wine and it was perfect with my entree!

Alrighty, if there's a way to die, this just might be it. Duck confit poutine, for chrissakes. Â To be fair, this was a special they had this night, so I'm not sure how often they have it. If you're not familiar with poutine, it's a French Canadian tradition of french fries, cheese curds, and gravy, all mixed together. While cheese curds sounds nasty, it's actually pretty heavenly. It's not too different from cottage cheese, just without all the cream or milk, just the curds. Combine them with gravy and french fries, and there's the basic version; add duck confit and you have a recipe for heart failure. Super delicious heart failure. We actually went to Brindle Room for the burger, which a friend of mine had heard was pretty spiritual. Um, he heard right. It was pretty insanely great (to quote the late great Steve Jobs). The meat was juicy and tender and it was prepared perfectly. It came with a kale salad with parmesan cheese and almonds that lent some sort of health credibility to the affair, or a least, slightly lessened the guilt from the poutine, and oh yes, I forgot to mention: the STEAK TARTARE. So, if you care about your tastebuds more than your arteries (and you should), go here. Â The ambience is quite nice and the staff and service were impeccable.
Owner is awesome. Food is delicious. Ambience is solid. All good in the hood.

very quickly becoming my go-to place for drinks in the summer. Â it's nice because you don't have to sit at a regular table, you can sit at the bar. Â they open their windows, making it feel like you're almost outside. Â the drinks are reasonably priced, and quite strong. Â and, most importantly, i love margaritas. Â and sure, they come from a machine, but i love em anyway.
The white pizza is really good!! The regular cheese was just okay!! The service was pretty good!!:)
Great quality and exceptional value! Â The oyster and PBR special is key and finish up with the entree of fried ispwhich clams with double fries!

This tiny restaurant serves awesome (buttery) seafood and (decadently rich) dessert and it's BYOB...which obviously makes it that much better. Â The service is wonderful with both the server and the chef taking the time to get to know us and just hang out. Â It's a great date spot and also a great spot to come with a group of friends but definitely make reservations! Â  The mussels (the classic one) and the cassoulet were my favorite but you really can't go wrong here.

If for no other reason, you should dine here just to have a bloody mary. My personal favorite is the Star of the Sea which comes topped with a fresh oyster. I haven't yet had the chance to dine here for dinner, but it is on my wish list as there brunch is outstanding. Service is always good, but at times you can feel rushed because there is often a wait. It can get nosy in the dining room, so if you are looking for a place to hold an intimate conversation, look elsewhere. The french toast and any of the egg scrambles are great as are the homemade pickles (I am a sucker for pickles). Bottoms up!

Had to wait for 30 minutes to get seating for a party of 2, BUT it was well worth it! The food was superb: We started of with the Avo Sushi. Who would have thought avocado marinated in some special soy sauce would taste that good. I highly recommend this to anyone who visits Totto Ramen. Also, check their pork buns; their very delicious. And of course, the reason we went their: Ramen! I had their Pork Paitan ramen and it was delightful! The broth was really tasty and the toppings made the dish even better. I have to say I will definitely come back and try their other ramen offerings.
The most fantastic brunch I have ever had. The apple omelet and the bloody marys are delicious. Can't wait to come back and try more!

So overrated. I've been a few times, most recently for dinner. The host was awesome--so nice, attentive, and answered questions when we sat down. After that, it went downhill. They messed up the menus they gave us and handed out lunch menus to part of the table, instead of dinner. And then instead of catching this when they took our orders, they apparently took what they thought we said and decided it meant something similar-sounding on the dinner menu (maybe because it was so loud? This was another problem--expect to not really hear whoever you're eating with. I've sat outside as well, and it was actually less loud than inside). So part of the table got the completely wrong meal (the guy serving it literally took a minute to believe them and tried to convince them that no, they'd actually ordered salads, instead of apologizing immediately). So we ended up waiting for the reordered food to be made (at which point they deigned to bring us our drinks, AFTER most of us had been served our main meals). There was a brief verbal apology for the meal mix up (nothing for the ridiculously late cocktails). You take over 20 minutes to bring us cocktails and mess up someone's meal, you should probably put a round on the house--or at the very least bring fries or SOMETHING so that the people who didn't have their food could munch while the rest of us could start without feeling guilty. And then one of the servers had the gall to complain after we got the bill that they didn't usually split bills between credit cards, but he'd do it "just this once." Okay? Not necessary to say if you're just going to do it, particularly when you know for a fact that our entire meal was messed up. The food was alright. The veggie burger is not the best--kind of bland and definitely overpriced for what it is, but a good veggie burger is a difficult find so it was not uniquely bad. The servers disappeared for long stretches of time, particularly between dinner and dessert. It's worth noting that the first few times I was there, it wasn't bad, but my last couple of visits make me think that they've gotten complacent in their reputation. This is a city with a ton of incredible restaurants...I'd say go to another.

Found this place after searching for Indian restaurant. The staff was really friendly, and the food is amazing. Their vindaloo is extremely spicy, but I liked every bit of it. Wife got the lamb curry and she loved it. It's a tiny but lovely place with good food.

I know I'm late on my reviews but better late than never. I visited NYC last year and I must say the halal guys' chicken/lamb and rice was absolutely bomb! Whatever that white creamy sauce was made of, it's so tasty. I love spicy so I add a little bit of the red sauce (it's a good kick but be careful!) Actually I must say I wasn't enjoying it as much because I was skeptical & def wasn't drunk! Lol. But our group bought extras so I ate it second time during our stay.. And yes indeed good sober or drunk food. I hear that there are lots of fake "halal guys" cart/truck so be careful you're buying from the right guys. I also hear they move their carts from corner to corner on 6th & 53rd. Â  Enjoy!

Delicious food. I loved the avocado salad and wish roasted chicken tasted like this all the time! Service was friendly and attentive, Â the ambience is great. I loved the beautiful twig wall coverings and decor.

Came for a friends birthday with a party of Â 10. Got a semi private room downstairs. Food was very good. Loved the guacamole and the 2 or 3 ceviche options, so much that we got another order of each. I had the braised beef and the texture was great as was the taste. Will definite come back.
This was an excellent place. Big portions, good food. I look forward to going back.

Wow! This is by far the best Thai food I have had in Brooklyn! The service is amazing! Lets start with the staff very friendly and courteous. The decor is dark and romantic to hip and fun! Great for a first date to dinner and drinks with friends. Now the food is mouths watering! I had the woo-sen with shrimp (glass noodles). Yummy definitely my new favorite Thai restaurant in Brooklyn ..... Sea what?
This could be a great addition to the neighborhood. Â Nice menu and a clever concept.

I'm not much of a drinker. I'm what most people call a "cheap date" or a "why not?" or a "really? you only want water?" So that was my preface to the fact that I came here with a bunch of people who wanted to drink. I can only rate on what I had experienced, and if I remember correctly, it was something with ginger. Or maybe it was the Mia Farrow (non alcoholic grapefruit spritzer)...or maybe i did imbibe some alcohol, because my recollection is fuzzy. hmmm... Either way, the crowd was nice, the ambiance on point (warm, but not cramped), and the wine list extensive. The sommelier knew what he was talking about. Unfortunately I didn't really care enough to listen, but he sure sounded knowledgeable. I came with a large group of 7, with 2 Wine-ies who came as strangers and left as gay lovers. Just kidding - but they way they were orgasming over the different wines, you would have thought so. We were seated comfortably and the service was great. I'm reserving some stars b/c I'll be back here to try out the food and give it a real rating. I don't care if that's unfair. I'm saying this place is already A-OK, so why not check it out for yourself and tell me what to eat when I do go? ^_^

Love this pizza. At first I could not see paying $20+ dollars for a pie, but when I went into the restaurant and sat down, it became all worth it. The experience is wonderful and the pizza is really good. There is a lot of history in that place and interesting people to meet.
Never a disappointment! My go to for Mac n Cheese - Salmon Benedict - Truffle Fries!

Like everyone else, we *tried* to go to Clinton St., but the wait was 2hrs by the time I had rallied my family to get moving that morning. Â At 10:00am on a Sunday, Cornerstone had 3 tables open still, so we were seated immediately. Â  I ordered the pancakes, and they were fluffy and delicious. Â My hubby got the baked eggs and he enjoyed it. Â My parents both said they enjoyed their meals too. Â We also ordered freshly squeezed orange juice. Â The waitress felt bad for my toddler who I usually don't give juice to, so she gave her one for free :P. Â Of course, she loved it. Â  Towards the end of our meal, the service became rather spotty as a line started forming outside the restaurant. Â My parents suddenly decided they wanted tea and coffee, but flagging down the waitress took forever. Â  Pricing is very reasonable. Â It's cash only, so come prepared :).

Everything here is great. The burgers are awesome and for those who want a healthier option you can get ask for a turkey burger (which is not on the menu) Also you can try the chicken parmesan under their appetizers. The chili cheese fries are to die for. If you are in the mood for breakfast try their waffles, always fresh and delicious.
The food was spot on and the service was excellent. Â Came here for Father's day and George and his FOH team did a really great job making for a great meal and experience. Â Great beverage program.

This place already has a TON of good reviews already, so I'll just say second Melissa P.'s description of the place - shabby chic is right on. Â I'm going to make Food Network references here but the place kinda feels like a mix between Ina Gartner and Sandra Lee (cuz Sandra is can be shabby chic except for when she gets carried away with the themes), but I the food is more Ina minus all the butter (I hope). Got the chicken meatball salad - meatballs were really good. Â One of the best tasting healthy meatballs I've had. Â Great texture and the salad helps make it lighter. Â  Definitely want to give the brunch a try.

The sandwiches are amazing. I'm addicted to the spicy chicken sandwich with a chai bubble tea. The seating area is kind of awkward...but its not really a dine-in sorta place. Â It's truly a gem in this neighborhood, and very happy I found it. It's easy to miss, I've walked right past it a few times. Look out for the chalkboard sign, its really the only thing with the name on it. The staff is great, and I've never waited more than a few minutes for my food, and it's always good.

i wanted Ilili to be bad because it was suggested by the UN people because it could have supported my belief that NYC has more mediocre overpriced food than any other city because it is just a little too pretty but, in the end, the food was delicious. the fries are what every french fried potato in the world should aspire to the okra overcame my tactile reservations the Baba Ganoush did classic, better the shrimp popped it worked

Sometimes, I think i shouldn't dole out five stars so easily, but Mamoun's in Greenwich absolutely deserves it. I'm ADDICTED to these things. And its priced so well! At $2.50 a pop for a sandwich, who said you can't eat well during the recession? I've tried most of the things on the menu, and I haven't been disappointed by any of them. But my favorites are the baba ganouj and the namesake falafel. First timers, please don't dismiss this place if there is a long line because the service is super fast. I would say from the time you put in the order to the time you receive the food -- under 30 seconds. I am definitely a Mamoun's junkie.
Really good tacos and burgers. They have homemade lemonade too which is good. May be a tad hard to find if you don't keep an eye out, it's definitely a hole in the wall. Clean though.

This is probably the first time the YELP has failed me in choosing an eatery. Â BIG TIME. Â 4+ star for the joint... i really can't understand why. Â We were in chelsea area and was looking for a brunch plc... something new and different. Â Ocabonon showed up w/ rave review and we were excited. first this plc is located right across a parking lot and holiday inn exp, not exactly prime location, but thats ok. Â if the food is good, ppl will come. Â Got there and the place is empty, as in not even ONE customer. Â Alright, perhap 3pm brunch time is bit late for most, so we sat down. the owner was ver warm in welcoming us.. but then he disappeared (doesnt bother me). Â now, here is when everything went downhill. Â It took a LONG ASS time for the bus boy to get us a glass of water and he sure can't keep us hydrated as our glasses were empty several times. Â the waiter isn't well versed w the menu. Â he couldnt remember the special (and there were like 3 options, one of which is CAESAR SALAD) - THATS A SPECIAL?! Â He was like, umm, i forgot, i need to look it up. Â OK ... we ordered our food and sat there and waited awhile (no bread or anything offered). Â the food arrived and it was very ho hum. for the price that it charged, i felt very cheated. Â it didnt taste great and the portion was small. Â Since i was somewhat still hungry, i got ropped into ordering dessert.. thinking you can't really go wrong w/ macaron in a french place. Â WRONG. they were very limited w/ their flavor options and they were SUPER sweet AND VERY one noted. Â i had better ones at mcdonald in barcelona! all in all, i regret coming here. Â $60+ for brunch is not cheap and we were not satisfied. Â service is much to be desired and food was subpar.

It was about a 15 minute wait for us to get a seat at the bar to eat our first restaurant style Ramen. I must say I was pleasantly surprised. I ordered the soy based with pork and egg and it was good to literally the last drop. Â I also split the salt and pepper wings which were too great. As of right now, they don't serve any beer and or wine. But I guess a cold class of water is best for a big bowl of Â broth and noodles. I will be back.

Literally the best Italian food I've ever had. Lets begin with service... Service is always on point. They are all friendly, funny, and do not bother you too much, just the right amount of hovering if you know what I mean. The owner always comes and asks you if everything went well and so on. The menu: short, sweet, and true to their roots. Small handwritten menu that has great items for everyones taste. My personal favorite is the spinach gnocchi...you honestly will not find one like it anywhere. If you have a sweet tooth, you need to get the Panna Cotta, its the perfect light and sweet treat after a heavy meal like pasta. Also, great prices for amazing food. The ambience: its the perfect little hideout when you want italian comfort food done right. maybe no more than 10 tables, candle lit, and very homey. Never too busy, which is amazing for the city. its always been my little secret spot but they're so good I just had to share. Enjoy!

Wow that's some good BBQ! Â For around $16, I got 2 meat selections, 2 sides, and a cornbread. Â Definitely perfect place to go when you are starving. Â The ribs and pulled pork were well seasoned, as well as mac and cheese and baked beans. Â The delicious cornbread muffin added a little extra. Â I will definitely be taking my brother and dad here - for sports watching too.

Holy crap this place was good. Â Believe the hype. Â I have seen a lot of good reviews of this place and heard it is always packed, but I figured a meatball sub could only be so good. The restaurant is a bit on the small side, but has a charming, worn-in rustic feel to it. Â It almost seems like a country kitchen. Â We went there on a Friday night around 7pm with hopes of eating and catching a 7:45 movie at the Angelika. Â When we got there it was paaaaaacked. Â The wait was 45 minutes, oy. Â But here is a little secret. Â There are two high top tables between the front widows and the bar, that have no stools and are ignored by most people. Â But, you can order the full menu. Â One of the two opened up after about a minute of us grumbling about the 45 minute wait. Â Score! We both ordered beef meatball heros on whole wheat, mine with provolone, hers with mozzarella. Â  The heros come with a lite side salad with diced apples - a nice touch. Â  The bread was rustic and crusty, the sauce was a sweet marinara and the meatballs were moist, well seasoned and basically pure heaven. Â We washed the heros down with glasses of Sangiovese. Â The whole eating experience was comprehensive awesomeness. Â  The service was good too. Â They were very busy, but took good care of us and were prompt about getting us drinks and the check (as we were in a rush). My wife summed it up best, "The Meatball Shop is awesome!"

I was a lil hesitant about walking into this place because unfortunately it is situated in an extremely "Colorful" neighborhood in the middle of Corona. I peeped inside through the front door first and shocker- noticed right away it was really packed full of non Corona residence patrons in there. Â The service, the REAL toasted/sliced Cuban bread, as well as my delish meal was EXTREMELY satisfying and will never judge a restaurant based on location ever again! Hidden gem!

As I try to increase my yelp reviews I decided I would take some time and add my favorite restaurants in Brooklyn. Applewood is great restaurant that uses ingredients from local framers and butchers for all there food, local as in the North East. The food is very innovative. Their menu changes seasonally and always has good variety of dishes that will please anyone. On the weekdays they have tasting menu that is awesome and once a month they have farmers dinner where the farmers come in and talk about the food you are eating, which is an idea that I love. It is a little pricey but makes it a great place for dates or friends from out of town. The atmosphere looks like a country house in the mid west, but it is cozy, in the winter they have a fire going. They are also known for the Brunch and they do not take reservations for brunch. There sweetbreads are soooo good.

Pretty good organic / vegan food for reasonable cafe / deli prices and it's in my neighborhood so I will be frequenting there more often. Â So far, I've had their mixed salad, beet salad, chickpea "tuna" melt, roasted vegetable sandwich, and a green juice. Â  The salads are pretty good, but not spectacular or memorable. Â  The chickpea tuna melt was good, but very heavy because each bread slice was 2 slices thick - I think I had a white bread "hangover" after that. Â I really wish they'd use better quality bread. Â The roasted vegetable sandwich was pretty good and not quite so "bread heavy." The green juice were really good (and at $6, a pretty good deal compared to the blueprint juices I get for $10).

I recently visited Baoburg for the second time just to satiate the strong urge to taste their garlic shrimp - Gambas Al Ajillo. The first time I went to eat there, I was following a vegan diet for religious reasons. My friends ordered several dishes (mostly non- vegan), and the aroma from each one of them stuck with me, especially garlic shrimps and thus I was back for my share and more. Both visits to Baoburg have been wonderful. The staff were not only friendly and warm, but also very attentive to guests' Â at every table. Even the owner, Chef Bao came to our table to check on us and asked for feedback in general. I personally enjoy trying out food at mom-and-pop shops, and one thing that is an absolute delight, as well as a surprise, is visibility to the kitchen - a surprise because kitchen is a busy place and one wouldn't like to expose that area to the guests, and delight because a clean and well managed kitchen suggests that hygiene is a priority for the staff. And Baoburg earns my applause for that!! Although the restaurant is small in area, it sure offers much more than just a table, chair, and food. The service is great, food is flavorful, presentation is classy and appetizing, ambiance is cosy, and the staff is personable. You don't much after a long day at work than just that. I would definitely recommend Baoburg to anyone and for sure I am coming back.
Fabulous! Fluffiest and tastiest gnocchi in all the land! Great wine list and friendly staff! Good work, Mario!

Wife and I spent our anniversary seeing The Screwtape Letters at the Westside Theatre in the afternoon and then having an early dinner here at Maialino. Â We are long time fans of Danny Meyer restaurants and this one obviously did not disappoint. We started at the bar where she had some type of almond and cherry cocktail (unfortunately, I do not recall the details) and I had the Pig and Pepe which was a margarita with some crushed red pepper coasting the top of the glass. Â At the bar they serve these amazing cheesy, crunchy breadsticks which reminded me of a grown up and elongated version of Tid Bits. We were promptly seated at 5:30 when dinner service began. Â  We started by sharing the salumi misti. Â Speck (smoked prosciutto), mortadella and soppressatta with a small dish of olives. Â Excellent start! Next, she had the prosciutto and melon. Â Funny, because we had just been reminiscing the previous day or two about this classic combination. Â She loved it. I had the fried artichokes with anchovy bread sauce. Â Perfection. Next, she had the insalata misticanza...spring lettuce, lemon and olive oil. Â Simple, light and refreshing. Â Perfect dressed...of course. I was torn between the ravioli al uovo...ricotta, brown butter and egg yolk, which I had read many good things about online, and the agnolotti with fresh corn and ricotta salata. Â The waiter recommended the latter since it was very season and just appeared on the menu around one week ago. Â The agnolotti was excellent. For our last course she had a primi...the spaghetti carbonara and I went with the pig's foot with beans. Â Both were outstanding. Â I can't wait to return and get the shareable pig for the table. Along with the two dishes our waiter, as an anniversary present, comped us a dish of the ravioli al uovo. Â An incredible and decadent dish that required an additional slice of bread for the remaining sauce and yolk. Â  We passed on dessert due to very full bellies. Service was perfect...of course. I am ready to go back right now!
Great wine and food! I would definitely come back. This place is a bit quirky. Interesting decor, offbeat waiters.

Had dinner with my friend the other day... Â wasn't crowded. Â I ordered the dumplings and some other dishes (I don't really know since it was my friend who ordered it). Â The only thing I would recommend to ppl is the dumpling (the crab one) - that one should rate 5 stars but the other dishes really dissatisfy me so I have to deduct 2 star. I probably will go back again coz the dumplings are really good and I'll probably order something different next time.

Came here on Friday night with a friend for a quick gut-punch dinner. Went with their standard "Bowery" burger, which was really good. At $10, it's an incredible value for the area. A few blocks away, comparable burgers will run you $15. Patty is house-made and they understand the meaning of medium-rare in this kitchen. The beer list here is also awesome. 20 beers are always on tap, and not a single one is bad. The standard tap list is also complimented by a great selection of seasonal drafts and bottles. Didn't try a cocktail but I am definitely going to come back soon to give them a go. Bartenders are friendly and attentive. Ambiance and general noise level in the place is dark and quiet, which is always appreciated.
I still love this business, but they need to do a better job of seasoning the spinach pie. Â It is too bland.

Authentic presentation of Alsatian food. Limited menu, but adequate choices. Relatively small and reasonably comfortable. Worth a visit if you're nearby though not so special to make the effort from a long distance. Not a place to visit on a regular basis due to lack of variety.

I live in the neighborhood and finally stopped by a couple of weeks ago. The hours are somewhat limited (8am-6pm daily), but the sandwiches are amazing. The Shrimp Po Boy is quite good, but my favorite is the Beef (Braised short-ribs with wild arugula, cherry tomatoes, & horseradish sauce on challa bread)... amazing! The staff is also very friendly, which is an added bonus.

I realize this is Tex Mex and not authentic Mexican, but I just don't think cheddar cheese works well in tacos. Â I didn't really like the fried chicken or fried avocado tacos. The brisket is great though, as is the al pastor. Chips are home-made which is always a plus. Guac a tad spicy but very good.

Dinner. Â The 4 of us came here after reading about their Fried Chicken. Â It was really good and you get a generous portion of it. Â We also tried the almonds (not bad) and shared the trout which we thought was only okay. Â I remember also trying an anchovy vinagrette salad that wasn't bad either. Â  Overall, nice atmosphere. Â I don't think we were completely impressed though but still very enjoyable.
Mediocre. Try Numero 28 for the best pizza in town (a few locations but one nearby). Spunto (and its sibling spots) is also very good.

this place. fuck me. the wait is ridiculous on most nights but if you can get in ... you will enjoy some of the finest pizza and company the world has to offer ... that is all. no wrong can happen with this decision. make the decision. wait for it ...

Yum. The sliders were priced nicely (~$3 per slider). Â We ordered the bacon slider, which has bits of bacon in the beef patty, a regular slider, and a turkey slider listed from favorite to least favorite. Â I didn't like the turkey slider because it had a kind of weird rubbery consistency. Â All the sliders come with grilled onions. Â Mix the Jalapeno sauce with the Chipotle sauce; you won't be sorry! Â Seating is really really really tight and the place tends to get quite loud especially later at night.

Nice place for smaller groups looking for good drinks and smaller bites. I stopped by with a friend on a weekday evening without a reservation, but we managed to get seated without more than a few minutes wait. There are quite a few shared tables, so you might have to share a table with another small group. For a drink, I ordered the Player's Club, which was a nice, refreshing drink, and sampled my friend's Henry Ward Beecher, which had quite a kick to it. For food, we split the pork belly mac and cheese and an order of the gnocchi, both of which were very good. The former was good but not other-worldly good and a bit heavy, while the latter was quite light and tasty. The venue itself is not very well lit and somewhat loud but is generally conducive to nice conversation. All in all, I'd consider coming back to try some of the other dishes while enjoying the company of a few friends.

Went to Wallflower last night with a group of 4 (including myself). The cozy ambiance at Wallflower is extremely welcoming - especially when the staff is very friendly, attentive, accommodating. etc. Service is VERY good here. We did the a la carte menu and our entrees were the Loup de Mer, Sea Scallops, Barley Risotto and the Pork Tenderloin.. all delicious, and filling. The food here is all about quality. Between the 4 of us we tried 2 different cocktails each, and even had Xavier Herit bring out something he crafted that wasn't on the menu. Definitely recommend and will definitely be going back.

Places like Juliana's rarely meet expectations, let alone exceed them. And this is a pretty wild scenario to begin with: elderly Patsy Grimaldi is going to reclaim his building from the hucksters using his name to franchise increasingly mediocre pizza worldwide? I don't mean to wax emotional, but this is like sending up a hobbled Kirk Gibson to hit in the pitcher's spot and expecting him to hit a home run to win World Series Game 1. Then that shit happened. Cue the brake lights in the Dodger Stadium parking lot. I first came here in 1990. And the pizza now is every bit as good as it was then. Same oven, same crust, same char, same chew. And they have better toppings. And they have pretty reasonable salads. And they have acceptable calamari. What the hell is going on? Juliana's has reclaimed the crust mantle from Totonno's. And the cheese is better. And the sauce is better. And we're talking about Totonno's, which was the ne plus ultra of pizza until three hours ago. Not only that, but this shit should make Dom Di Fara embarrassed and ashamed. Here he is, this annoying Midwood crank who only makes your pizza nicely if he feels like it. If he doesn't, it's his art and you're out $35. Well here's Patsy Grimaldi slinging his old pizza, slinging some ice cream, and slinging some wine and beer. And he's coming around and telling your ugly kids how beautiful they are. And he's asking where you live and wondering why you didn't drive. Sure, he's assaulting you with Frank Sinatra. But he's also proving that you can live past 60 and make a superior pizza without acting like an aloof prick. WHOA!
This is a great family-style Italian restaurant and I enjoy going here whenever I'm visiting New York City. Â The food is very good and the restaurant atmosphere is nice.

Wow.. I really liked this spot. Â I found it on yelp after tirelessly looking for a place that was good for groups and took reservations. Â I wanted something French instead of Italian or American. Â They accomodated us easily.. First.. this place is decorated interestingly. Â Tables have movie theater seats.. it's dark but intimate. Â Clean and you don't feel like you're sitting in on the conversation next to you. The best part of this place.. the waiters were all French! Â So nice.. and amazing accents. Â I don't think I could understand what my waiter Julien said three times because I was so in love with his accent. We got a bottle of wine which was fantastic. Â He actually let us try it before we bought a bottle so we got one we really liked. Â  Then came the food.. two of us got the prix fixe (3 courses for the price of $25.. what a steal). Â Our last friend got the cheese plate (3 cheeses) and the lamb chops dish. Â She loved both the cheese plate and the lamb chops... didn't even finish the lamb chops. Â So.. the prix fixe was pretty good. Â Tried the escargot. Â Very good.. probably the least oily one I have ever had. Â I don't know what the green sauce is.. but it's good. Â I also tried the shrimp bisque (soup of the day).. I should have passed and got the pate. Â It was okay.. but just wasn't that good. Â Tried also the duck confit.. really good. Â Crispy on the outside and tender on the inside. Â Delicious veggies it's plated on top of. Â The dessert was a little bit of a let down.. creme brulee didn't have the best sugar crust.. seemed like it had been made a while ago.
