Â The chocolate molten cake tasted okay.. but wasn't that great as well. Â They did sing to my two friends (as it was their bday) in French. There was a minor mishap at this place. Â Some lady had an anxiety attack and two ambulances came.. but it didn't seem to disturb any of the patrons too much. Â  Love this place.. I would definitely swing by again.. only if there weren't so many amazing restaurants in NYC.. yup, I'd be a fatty if I lived in this city.
Very cozy place with solid food and friendly service. Good people vibes. I had the Blueys, which hit the spot. Cash only, no reservations.

Soup dumplings are the specialty at Shanghai Asian Manor and I don't think we saw a single table without at least one order at their table. Â They don't serve it without pork though so I didn't taste any of that, but my family did give good reviews about it. Â  We also ordered the Beef Pan-Fried Noodles and the Scallion Pancakes. Â Note that both are actually deep-fried. Â While the scallion pancakes were enjoyable, I actually prefer them to be made by lightly browning on each side in a pan instead. Â I did not like the Beef Pan-Fried Noodles at all. Â Definitely NOT ordering that again. Service is very rushed and quick (the Chinatown way). Â Don't expect a lot when you come and you'll be fine.
Cheap and tasty food, the perfect combination! Go for the rice bowl was big enough for two people.

Welcome back Mundo! Â I was delighted to hear they are open again & I was looking forward to see what they've created. Menu was very similar to their old one with some favorite dishes available (red sonja, carrot dip, veggie wrap, etc) but I was actually hoping for a food more options. The other reason for only 4 stars is the portion sizes vary between tapas style & entrÃ©e and it's not very clear on the menu. Â I loved everything we ordered but we needed to order side dishes to supplement. Â  Decor, Location, Â Service...5 STARS! I will be back & I'm bringing friends to ensure they stay around for a long time! I truly wish Willy & the gang continued success as they aspire to give the neighborhood what it is lacking. Keep your eyes out for new dance nights for their large downstairs space!

With it's outdoor seating, Habana Outpost is a great place to take in the summer sun and throw back a few ice cold beers and margaritas. Their Mexican corn is a delight and their Cuban Sandwich is both satisfying and delicious. I look forward to going back to try more of their dishes!
Best arepa around!! The small place just got a little bigger Get any arepa and a cold beer and you will be happy!!!
Good food and great drinks. Highly recommend for brunch! Return ? Yes Frequency ? Occasionally

The decor was nice, and the service was very friendly. Â I pretty much stops there though. Â  I ordered the classic burger, Â with no fries and no drink... just a quick burger, and it took a LONG time. Â Two women who came in 10 minutes after me got served before I did. Â When my burger finally arrived, it was bland and dry. Â It was supposed to be cooked "medium" Â but what I got tasted like cardboard. Â In the end, it cost $14 with tip for a really bad plain burger. Â  I came in with high expectations and was pretty disappointed. Â I usually eat my burgers out because they do a better job than I can cooking at home. Â My go-to places are usually 5 Napkin Burger on the upper west side, or any of the 5 Guys Burger chains. Â As I read this, I think maybe there's something magical about the number 5? Â But I digress. Â  I suspect this has something to do with whoever is behind the grill, because other posters have had great experiences.

After all the hype and the reviews warning me the food was great, but the service was crappy, I had a great experience here. It is in a hole on Moore St in Bushwick as mentioned ad nauseum. The fact that you have to destination here made it fun to get through the nondescript, crappy front door and see what a fun place they have. Â Hipsteriffic, comfortable, some communal tables, cool garden out back (where we ate) and great eats. Service was decent. I liked that our server was honest about what she liked on the menu and could describe textures and how heavy the hand was on ingredients in each dish. Had the Carrot, smoked ricotta, arugula salad Scallops with lardo and nectarines Split the Banana Hammock, Margherita and another special pizza Captain Lawrence beer (bottle) Good for them that they have made this place in the middle o'nowhere a destination. It was a cool adventure to try it.
We had the BEST time ever! The service was great the food is unbelievable and the atmosphere pleasant. Very recommended !!!

I had my daughter's baby shower at Palo Santo and everyone had a wonderful time! Â Gonzalo was a wonderful help before the shower, telling me all about the menu and how they handle everything the day of the event. Â He was even more accommodating Â to me the day of the shower. Â They have a great wait staff and the ambiance of the back room was very nice. Â The food was delicious!!!! Â If you are thinking of having a party here, don't hesitate,you will have a great time.
Great vibe. Good Food. Average service. Would go again. Artichoke dip was unreal.

La Lanterna was the first restaurant I ever ate at when I moved to the city to go to college and it's still one of my favorites in NYC. I don't live in the city any more but I still make it a point to visit whenever I'm back. The mesclun salad with duck, salmon pizza and lasagne (either bolognes or pesto) are my favorite dishes. The desserts and coffee also do not disappoint. Aside from the food, the service is great. Everyone I've ever taken here loves the place.

Let's get it out of the way. Service: 2 stars. The few tables to sit at were dirty. My friend had to ask a waiter to clean our filthy table. "Clean" meant get rid of the menu with coffee on it. Really disappointing. Our food was initially given away to someone else, but the excellent waitress apologized and gave us these cute little cookies to munch on. Food: 5 stars. Wow. The food is excellent, fresh, and well prepared. Essentially perfect. And it's a steal! Most things on the menu are 5 or 7 dollars. The paninis and baked dishes are great--I want to try everything! The owner is very pleasant and likable. Remember not to be in a rush, because the place is slow. Portions are fairly small, especially considering this is Italian, which is great because you get to try more things. At Gaia's prices, you really can't complain.

Innovative. Ground breaking. I would say this restaurant marks the beginning, or rather the mainstreaming of eco-dining here in New York. While the trend has been around for a long time, it's nice to finally have a real temple of eco-obsessive gastronomy to worship at. Oh, and the food is just flawless. Clean, straightforward, married to the market, screaming of seasonality. The whole experience is flawless. Favorite place in New York right now. Can't wait to see copy cats pop up.

Been living in Brooklyn for almost a year and decided to go see what the big deal was about Grimaldi's. My friend and I decided to order out, so we started calling, trying to get it to go. Nobody every answered. So we decided to grab the dog and walk over. We get there and the man tells us we'd have to wait in line, that we can't place an order to go. After much argument, he took our order and we waited outside for our pizza with everything on it (why not?!) and for $45 it definitely wasn't worth it. It was super salty and Â the crust was soggy. I had a stomach ache all night because of all the salt. My body is definitely not used to it! All in all, I'd say go once, but agree with Juan J.--it's definitely nothing special.
By far the best pizza in miidtown and perhaps NYC!!! Go for their tomato/basil.
Every time I'm in Brooklyn I have to stop here for a brat on a pretzel bun, with fries and I pick out a beer from an array on tap unmatched in your average bar. Great fun and food.

So good! Definitely worth a visit. Not busy when we went around 7pm. Margherita pizza with meatballs were amazing! White pizza was good as well but very heavy and filling. Not too expensive since the large pizza was huuuge and easily split between several people!

Go get a Bronte sandwich! Go get a Bluey sandwich! Heck . . go get any of the damn sandwiches that come with an inclusive side salad dressed with one of the best salad dressings I've ever tasted! Run . . Don't walk! Their sandwiches are fantastic. Juicy, flavorful & served on crusty & moist toasted ciabatta bread! This place is as small as a large closet but soooo worth it. I crave this place!
yes. especially if you're visiting and just out for a walk. class, character, and a good product. I will return.

I have eaten at Spotted several times, and have failed to ever write a review. Â Yes, its sceney as of 5 or so years ago, and the vibe is stellar, but coming from restaurant management myself, I really only have one complaint. Part of a servers job, especially when they are speaking to someone who may have a little bit of an idea where they're coming from, is to not only sell dishes but not necessarily to upsell every course. Â Additionally, when a guest puts full faith in a server to order for them, it is tasteless for a server to select only the priciest menu items and beverages. Â  I have really enjoyed my visits, but being someone who enjoys having the restaurant's selection, having servers order high and over-order each time is discouraging in the quality of staff.
Went back. Had the Churrasco. Medium rare, extra sauce = amazeballs. And the staff are fantastic. Such a fan.
Great spot. Â Took us about two years to get a table for 4, but it was worth the wait. Â Service was excellent. Â Food was creative and delicious.

A pretty decent sports bar (especially considering the "near penn station" location). Â The Happy Hour had decent specials, and the service was pretty good. Â The burger and fries were also yummy, and at the better end of bar food in the area.
Felt like we had a "real New York" experience - hole in the wall feel with outstanding pizza!! Expect to stand & eat & get the lasagna pizza it is delish!!

okay, i know i raved about JANE but seriously.. DO YOURSELF A FAVOR AND GO EAT AT CLINTON ST. BAKING COMPANY. yes the line is oh so very long and ridiculous and you probably could have finished a meal elsewhere within the wait time given to be seated at clinton st. Â but you know what, it's so worth it. trust me. it's not very close to any subway station and it's hidden in LES. it's a very small, cute, quaint space, with no personal space for anyone sitting inside. there's not much of a waiting area so you are left to wait outside on the sidewalk. but while you wait, you can munch on their scrumptious muffins which can be purchased right next to the hostess station. i've been here multiple times and the best advice i can give you is to just go early. lol just go early so you wait a max of 30 minutes to get seated. that and BEWAREEE!!!! CASH ONLY!!!!!!!!! in terms food, it's so delicious it makes me wish there were more brunch places like this in southern california. their sugar cured bacon is so sweet and savory and SO THICK! awesome bacon if you are a bacon fan :) i have tried buttermilk biscuit sandwich, brioche french toast, and pancakes with warm maple butter buttermilk biscuit sandwich - such a classic breakfast meal, i know you can probably get a cheaper deal at mcdonalds, but seriously... i prefer food quality over price. the homemade tomato jam is nice and warm on the buttery biscuit and you can save some of that biscuit and spread some of their homemade raspberry jam too. soooooo goood i'm just drooling.... D: brioche french toast - very fluffffffyyyyyy and sweet. so sweet it's ridiculous especially with the caramelized bananas, roasted pecans and the warm maple butter. but i really cant go through breakfast/brunch with just sweets, so i would add some bacon with this order ***PANCAKES WITH WARM MAPLE BUTTER - BLUEBERRY PANCAKES are so bomb. it's so good. that's why i added the stars in the beginning lol. other than their buttermilk biscuits, this is their signature. i swear to God, yes you can get cheap ass pancakes are the local diner or ihop or make it at home with some shake n pour, but their pancakes, are so delicious and fluffy and butter with their wild main blueberry in between every stack. their warm maple butter is such a great complement and it doesn't make it taste too sweet or overpower the buttery fluffy pancake. it's so good, you gotta order this if you ever go there. :)

Wow big surprise - this is a great sandwich shop! I went with a buddy of mine at 3:30 PM on a Saturday afternoon a half hour before closing and a time when it is not so crowded. Everyone was relaxed and friendly and Hector, who has been there 42 years (the owner?), gave us a history of the place and the neighborhood as he took down the umbrellas from the picnic table (after we had finished)l next to the shop. I ordered the pastrami and cheese with hot peppers and mustard. Now I could have eaten the whole thing but I would have been stuffed and had nothing to eat tonight, so I summoned all Â my will power and only ate 1/2! And as another reviewer noted, it is as good as Katz's - actually less fatty than what I had there - and less expensive. My buddy had the famous steak pizziola. He really liked it but compared the meat Â to his grandma's pot roast which worked for him. I tried a little piece and have to say I prefer the meat in a real Philly cheese steak. We agreed that the bread is exceptional and the fact that they toasted it was another plus. So once again, DeFonte's has picked up some more fans!

I don't even know where to begin! Seriously, best meatballs ever. The concept is neat. They hand you your menu with a marker and you mark right on the menu what you want. You can choose the kind of meatball, cheese, sauce, whether you want it in a sandwich, on top of a salad, with different sides...the options are endless! Also, save room for dessert! Homemade cookie ice cream sandwiches...need I say more?
dumplings check. Â Kimchi rice and steak double check!

What a great surprise! Â My husband and I were on our way to the place across the street - can't remember the name but also great - and walked by Alameda. We decided to have a cocktail at their big bar. Super friendly service. Delicious martini. We decided to get an appetizer. Delicious. Boquerones. By this point we were settled in so we stayed. The food was perfectly cooked and the vibe was just what we needed. Dim lighting, friendly atmosphere, good music. Will be a regular!

Delicious- they use califia almond milk as well, and the espresso is expertly pulled- no burnt shots here. The avo toast is delicious- the bread pulls apart easily and is some sort of multi-grain or wheat mix. We chose to top ours with a fried egg (#yolkporn) and they did the honors of dusting the dish with red pepper chili flakes. Win all around. The seating is a bit hunger games-esque because there isn't a lot of it, but this spot is hot. However, as they are moving to tableside and seating service, this issue should be worked out nicely.

Good for a harried lunch special. Â Dreadful for a dinner date: Sub-par service, ugly decor, garish loud elevator music and dinner menu is overpriced. I was impressed with the Katsu during a quick crazy crowded lunch experience here a few years ago - came twice for lunch actually. Â  But this week had a bad meal here. Â We had a pissy waiter. Â He made it clear that we were interfering with his plans to leave. Â  Â  We asked to split a large beer which he described as "double size" Â but then he brought it to us already poured into one giant glass. Â  When we clarified that we had wanted Â two glasses he looked exasperated and bonking a second giant glass onto the table proceeded with trembling hands to pour from the first giant glass into the second giant glass, Â spilling beer all over the table, then mopping it around and stomping off without any apology at all for the dramatic mess nor any offer to bring a fresh beer which would have been appropriate, given the amount that was lost in the transfer. Â  the katsu wasnt Â hot or crispy as during the lunch rush. Â  We got the chicken pork and shrimp katsu. Â It was lukewarm and just tasted okay. My date was not impressed. Â He left most of it on his plate. Â  And by comparison to their lunch specials the dinner price was high (around $20 instead of $12 or so) Â  The waiter was pushing us to pay and sign the tab while we began eating. Arrived without reservations on 03 October. Staff treated our party very professionally. Wait time was predicted with reasonable accuracy. Food was great. This was particularly impressive given this places tourist attraction status.

Being a Californian who has sampled burritos in the Bay Area as well as SoCal, I consider myself somewhat of a burrito afficionado. For years, I've found NYC disappointing in the burrito department. I am here to tell you, Cali expats, you can stop crying into your Chipotle because finally someone has managed to do it. The fine gentlemen of Dos Toros thoughtfully crafted this menu and I couldn't be happier. I'm over here all the time and the burrito is consistently fat, tender, and juicy. Long line? It goes fast. No seats? Get it to go. Run, don't walk.

We stumbled into this place after wandering around for an hour trying to decide on a place to eat. The service is friendly and welcoming, and though we couldn't sit in the backyard (private event), the dining space is cozy and laid back. The place is BYOB (which I wish we'd known ahead of time)...and has some of the best fried fish around (sandwich and fish & Chips. Who knew?!? We were looking for decent, and were pleasantly surprised to find fantastic!! If we're ever in the neighborhood again looking for food, we won't have to wander long.

When I'm looking for a cheap meal in a dense urban area, this is the ideal. It's small and the bathroom backs up to the food prep area but the food is awesome and dirt cheap. From my vantage, this place is very authentic, accents so strong that I barely understood the staff. However I think I could have just said yes to whatever they suggested and been completely content. Will def come back whenever I'm in the neighborhood.

Even though the Sushi seems to be great by the reviews. I will never know because they messed up my reservation by writing down 2 when it was supposed to be 3...and did not want to accommodate. I ended up at Masa and had the best Sushi experience anyone could have in the U.S.

Room Service was a pleasant treat in the mixed bag world of restaurants that is 9th Avenue. Friends and I wanted Thai, which this street has plenty of, and so, using on my sweet Yelp'ing skills, we settled on Room Service. First, the ambiance is great. We were seated near the front, which I didn't care much for, especially due to the drizzling evening, but that was a small detail. Everything is themed as if you were in a hotel. From the menus to the check, that is the goal of the place. It works well, but as myself and my party remarked, it was as if this place could have been serving any type of dish. Wouldn't have surprised me if they were a Mexican or Hamburger place. They had a pretty extensive drink selection, ranging from about 10-15 cocktails, as well as a whole separate 10ish versions of a Mojito. I ended up getting a Cherry Mojitio, I believe. For the $13, it was was vastly underwhelming in terms of taste and alcohol content. Surprise, Surprise. The menu had a large and extensive selection, as well, which is always a pretty good thing. The appetizers all seemed fresh and original. I got the dumpling soup that was in a clear broth and for the $3 or so, it was very tasty and worthwhile. For an entree, I settled on the Peanut Sauce Fried Rice And Big Shrimps Satay. This was a mountain of amazing rice with a great peanut sauce that was filled with, my favorite, raisins. The shrimps, all 4 of them, were tasty but a tad overcooked. Overall, a great and creative dish. Very filling but, then again, it was a mountain of rice. So would I go back? It's around the corner, has great ambiance, and I'll probably end up at a place where my drinks cost the same as my entree anyway, so, yeah, sure...I'll be back.

One night for a great dinner in NYC and we went to Balthazar. We loved it several years ago, but I was worried that it had deteriorated. Not so! Although the place is densely packed and more than busy, the service was excellent and friendly. The steak au poivre, salmon, and duck confit were all fabulous. The bread pudding for dessert to die for! We would go back, anytime!

Loved the Adobado and Carne Asada burritos! Speedy service and they make your burritos fresh. I just wish they had seats, had to have my burritos standing up. I've seen long queues to order here during the weekends. 8/10
The Pork Betty is the bomb- my son after lunch at Momo's. The owner if friendly and the staff is great! Will be back!

I had been eager to dine at Mediterranean restaurant Balaboosta for a while now, and an eating buddy was recently able to get our party of four a reservation. Â Considering the rezzie had to be made a few weeks out (for a Thursday night, no less), I was looking forward to seeing if the food lived up to its hype. Â Would I be pleasantly satisfied, sorely disappointed or fall somewhere in between? As there were four of us, we decided to order a variety of starters before delving into our entrees. Â We first started with a traditional dish - the hummus "mortar and pestle" with tahini, lemon and roasted garlic. Served with warm seasoned pita, the hummus was well seasoned, garlicky and hearty. Â We quickly made history of this dish - yum! The only thing that was roundly agreed by the table was the temperature at which this dish was served - the hummus was cold, and it is traditionally served at room temperature. Â With this one small adjustment, this appy would have been perfect. We also ordered the fried olives & organic labne with harissa oil. I'm usually not the biggest fan of olives (ok, I tend to avoid them entirely), but I'm always willing to give food a second, third or fourth try. Â I was so glad that I did because these fried olives were warm, crispy and pleasantly tangy, while the labne with harissa oil added a cool and creamy contrast. Â I totally would have licked this dish clean if I were eating alone. Ha! Our third appetizer was crispy cauliflower with currants and pine nuts. My picture of this dish is a tad blurry, a common side effect when I get excited about food. Â I never thought I'd be excited about cauliflower, but I really loved this preparation (errrrm, I'm sure the battered and fried-ness didn't hurt, haha). Â As expected, the cauliflower was served hot and crispy, and was extremely scrumptious. Â If all veggies could taste like this I would be ALL over that. We finished our appetizer selection with a special - the calamari salad on a bed of frisee (first photo). Â Frisee is one of my least favorite greens (seriously, I pick out all traces of frisee from my lunch salad), despite my best attempts to like it. Â I didn't change my mind this night, but that had nothing to do with the dish itself - the calamari, grape tomatoes and tangy vinaigrette tasted fresh and light. Â I give this dish two thumbs up. For our entrees, my three eating buddies all ordered the grilled lamb chops with Persian lime sauce, roasted sunchokes and pearl onions. Â  Mmm, did they choose well. Â I snuck a little bite off a buddy's dish, and the lamb chops were tender and flavorful without being gamey, and the Persian lime sauce was at once cool and rich. Â The roasted sunchoke mash was mild and absorbed the flavors of the dish beautifully. Â I would definitely order this dish if I dined here again! I decided to live on the edge a bit and ordered something a little different - for my entree, I chose the grilled whole branzino with baby root vegetable salad, roasted potatoes, and lemon-dill sauce. Mmmmm - I love whole fish! Â The outside of the branzino was satisfyingly crispy, while the meat was tender and juicy. Â The accompanying lemon-dill sauce perfectly complemented this fish, while the roasted asparagus was perfect for a warm summer evening. We finished off the evening with the banana-date pread pudding with yogurt ice cream. There was a reason that 3 tables around us all ordered the bread pudding - it was lusciously decadent, with a crispy exterior and satisfyingly chewy middle. The tang of the yogurt ice cream prevented this dessert from becoming cloyingly sweet, while the heartiness of the pudding itself made for a solid end to this meal. My dining experience at Balaboosta was highly satisfying, with excellent food, lively decor, and knowledgeable service. Â If you ever find yourself in SoHo with a hankering for Mediterranean fare, give a Balaboosta a try - you won't regret it! Fresh and well-prepared Mediterranean fare in a lively atmosphere.

Great food and drinks, but the waitress Natasha is the worst! I'm sitting here in the place writing this review because I have so much free time waiting for her to walk by. Pays you no attention and you constantly have to wave or get the busboy to talk to her. I would starve if I had to rely on her! If you come try not to sit in her section.

Recommended cheap eats. Great staff. No booze. Filling and fairly hearty. Arepas at Arepas CafÃ© are warm and filling, but not jumbo American size, which is great because the staff will recommend you eat two. I've tried three, which were all fantastic: mami (pork, cheese, avocado, $6.50); domino (black beans and cheese; $3.75); Guyanesa tropical (Guyanes cheese, sweet plantain, avocado, $6). The sauces are on the table for a reason, so use them. Pabellon Criollo ($11) was a gorgeous homey plate of shredded beef, rice and beans, and soft sweet plantains. Viva la cheap eats!

Loved the chicken & waffles here. The waffles with banana foster sauce was especially tasty! The buttermilk fried chicken here is unique and goes well with some hot sauce and ranch sauce (available upon request). I'm very much glad with my choice and I wouldn't hesitate to come back and try other things on their menu. bon apetÃ­t.
Late night Mexican food at its finest! My Hibiscus Margarita was yummy, so was my spicy chorizo quesadilla. I will definitely come back here on a regular basis! Service.. A+

Great spot!!!!!! I loved the ambiance of this place and I will come back. The food was "OK". Service and drinks were great!!! I think this is a great location for a bday dinner. It is really loud, so not the kind of place where you can have a normal conversation. Trendy, beautiful, and tasty enough for me to come back.

Great great cocktails. High quality booze, reasonable prices, fantastic bartenders with innovative drinks. The Dr. Isaacman was a spectacular off-menu cocktail. As a cocktail snob this place is highly recommended.
Good and really in-expensive for the area. Good treat but a little overrated. Took a long time as well since they misplaced our order.
LOVE: Â  -Cobb -drink list -outdoor patio -burger

Very authentic Japanese ramen. I love the aura of this place also, very "hole-in-the-wall", exclusive feel to it. The servers and cooks are mostly Japanese and they all have a quirky style that I love. I feel like I step into a small part of Japan when I was there.

The first move is to put a clamp on the nipple The next is to gently cradle its bottom Bring it so close to your face that you can feel the heat of its meat Tenderly, teasingly Nibble on its supple, nubile skin One small bite releases a rush of fragrant aromas Form a flower with your lips, and suck out the savory dew from within Go ahead, pour a few drops of special sauce down your delicate bao hole And in one fell swoop, like the animal that you are Shove the whole blessed thing into your gaping, waiting, greedy, bottomless maw And masticate, oh MASTICATE like you've never masticated before! IS THERE ANYTHING MORE INTIMATE THAN EATING XIAO LONG BAO?!?!?!?! When it is over, swallow wipe yourself and say, "Wow mom, that was delicious. Let's order another basket!"

I had high expectations for Luzzo's since I'd heard great things and the 4-star Yelp rating. My guest and I had the Arugula pizza (#5 on the menu) which has tomato sauce, mozzarella, and Â prosciutto. Â The prosciutto was so salty that it ruined the pizza. Â Removing the prosciutto made the pizza edible but it was still a loss. Also, I like pizza with a fair amount of sauce on it. Â Luzzo's pizza sauce had a nice flavor but they didn't put enough on the pizza. Â This is a common problem I have with NY pizza, so I'm probably in the minority and will request extra sauce if I eat at Luzzo's again.

This place is phenomenal. I have eaten at all the top fine dining restaurants in NYC (Per Se, Eleven Madison Park, Jean-Georges, Daniel, Gramercy Tavern, etc.) and Gato definitely outshines most of them in its food and customer service. The atmosphere/ambiance is elegant, cool, energetic and airy (def not stuffy). The staff is so attentive and nice- there is always someone there to bring you something but they aren't annoyingly hovering- they just seem to appear at the perfect time to fill your water glass or bring you a new plate and they are all really really friendly. The food is exceptional- I had high expectations for Gato and heard that Bobby Flay is there almost daily but I figured he wouldn't be there that evening because it was Easter Sunday. But, he is sooo awesome and committed to his diners that even on Easter Sunday, Bobby Flay was in the kitchen cooking. Yup, Bobby Flay was cooking delicious food for an entire restaurant of people on Easter Sunday. You can just stop reading the review right now and go make a reservation. But if you are still reading- His food surpassed my expectations. Everything we ate was outstanding (we had appetizers, main and dessert menu). He uses tons of different flavors in his dishes, making each plate so special and yummy. You'll like the eggplant dish even if you don't like eggplant. It's that good. Many NYC restaurants miss the mark on some component that makes for a great dining experience- either the ambiance, service or food. But not Gato. Gato does it all so wonderfully. And it's hard to get a reservation here because it's actually really really worth the meal unlike some other places. Definitely part of the top 5 NYC restaurants. Must go. You'll love it! PS- I got to meet Bobby Flay (twice) while there and he is such a cool nice guy.

I went here because the chef won season one of Top Chef. Â There, I've said it. I was here for brunch, and at the waiter's suggestion had the grits with tasso and a deep-fried egg. Â The grits were nice and creamy, the egg wasn't tough and was perfectly liquid in the center, and the tasso and shrimp in the grits gave it a nice heated flavor. I also tried their cheese plate, which had some nice local stuff that I hadn't heard of before, and the popcorn sherbet, which had a great texture. Service was friendly, food was great, prices weren't insane. Â If I lived here I would be back a lot.

The LINGUINE NERE alla MONSIGNORE rocked my world. The service was great as well. My coworkers ordered the GNOCCHI alla BABA and CALAMARI alla LUCIANA which were both excellent. The atmosphere is loud but nice. Not fine dining but a great over all experience.

Beyoglu is my favorite restaurant on the Upper East Side. Great atmosphere, great food, reasonable prices, and somewhat hip (as far as the UES goes). I usually opt for the veggie friendly mezze platter for the appetizer along with the donar or iskender kabab for my main. Great for sharing with a date or group. They also have Effes Turkish beer and a selection of Turkish wines. Not the best the Mediterranean has to offer, but an interesting experience nonetheless. Also, had a great grilled octopus appetizer a while back. They seem to have many seafood options, though I typically stick with the kababs. Bottom line, if you find yourself on the UES, this is an excellent option for great food and atmosphere at prices that won't break the bank.

This place is a must see and spend destination for Asian tourists. The macaroons were fairly priced. I can't really say the same for the other merchandise sold in the store. I purchased macaroons in the Donna Karan anniversary box which was pretty cool. All were delicious. The gentleman that helped me was so kind and enthusiastic. I wish I remembered his name!

Did someone say lobster for $20??? I had to stop by after hearing about this deal. Also got the roast duck. Cheap, good food, mad ghetto perfect combination for 4 star. Not the best chinese food I've ever had but definitely a good deal.

The food at Aurora was amazing. I was there for a Sunday brunch with a group of friends and ordered the Parma Eggs Benedict. The roasted potatoes was perhaps the best item on the plate. They are so incredibly soft and flavorful on the inside and it melts in your mouth.
Solid brunch spot with amazing views of the Museum of Natural History!
I MISSSSSSSEEEEEEEDDDDD U SO BAD chopsticks lickin' tonkotsu ramen! This place to die for!!!!!! ICHIBAN

Inatesso is one of our "go-to" neighborhod places when we want to entertain friends. It is consistently enjoyable and more dependable on weekends than the Stone Street places. Â The wait staff is great, service is prompt, food is great especially the variety of pizzas. Try it.

The staff here was incredibly courteous, one of the best restaurant experiences I've had in the city. We were there at peak time on Saturday night and had drinks across the street during the wait, about a half hour. Our server asked us right away if we had any allergies or concerns about the menu, and explained which items contained wheat/nuts and how they could make modifications for us. I had the gf spinach ravioli with ragu sauce, and it was delicious!

I hardly ever write reviews but I felt like I had to since this restaurant is amazing--and not just for celiacs and gluten avoiders. The pizza was the best gluten free pizza I've had so far (and I've tried a lot). The risotto and salad were equally fantastic, and the service as well. We were there on a Friday night, so there was a little bit of a wait, but we were greeted right away and asked if we wanted drinks (standing up by the door). We ordered a bottle of wine and it was brought over right away. I don't remember who the waitress was, but she was fantastic and welcomed us with a Southern hospitality that you rarely see in New York.

Was in the city for the weekend, and what a place to have a relaxing meal. I particulary loved the ceramic pots has light fixtures on the ceiling. The prices are reasonable for a restaurant in NYC. Â My boyfriend and I shared the dinner and ordred the dipping sauce with tzathiki(spelling?), fish roe and eggplant. They also gave us regular hummus which was to die for. We also ordered a curried meat and a vegetable soup that incredible . For the entree we had the lamb shank with giant bean purree. And finally for dessert we had drained greek yogurt served with sour cherry spoon sweet, thyme scented greek honey and walnuts. All in all, 5 stars to Pylos. I can't wait to dine here when I come back to the city.

The most money I've ever spent on RAMEN! but worth every penny for ambiance and flavor. Â  I didn't realize until afterwards that I had drank about 4 or 5 cups of water during my meal because of the saltiness which contributes to the taste. Â Noodles were PERFECT. Â  Â  I also ordered some $30 steak appetizer which turned out to be 3 tiny peices of meat...felt ripped but no big deal since I was in good company. Â  Stick to the RAMEN.

I was told to try Ippudo but it was just too far away for our schedule. Fortunately, I found that there's a rival called Totto Ramen that was closer to us. We got there at 5pm and we were the first to put our names in (for a table of 4). Soon after people were pouring in to get their names on the list. The two tops were seated before us. We waited for about 30 minutes. When we sat we saw why - there are only 2 tables for 4. There is 1 table for 2. And the rest is bar seating. While we were waiting there were a lot of Japanese speaking employees running around. I was thinking, "oooh, bet this will be authentic" Though, I guess I wouldn't REALLY know because I've never had ramen in Japan. I got the miso ramen, my mom got the vegetable ramen, and the other two in my party got the chicken paitan ramen. The noodles were perfectly al dente. The broth was ok. I think it was a red miso. Can't say it was the best broth I've ever had. The others had a chicken broth, which my mom loved.

For that late-nite-after-partying-soak-up-all-the-crap-you-Â­drank at the bar/club slice of pizza, Artichoke does it pretty well and for less than $5 bucks. This isn't for the lactose intolerant so if you can't stand the cheese or you forgot to take your lactaid, gluck to the people around you. The place lives up to the hype with a giant piece of ooey-gooey cheesey artichoke slice that honestly taste like eating artichoke dip on top of a pizza. That being said the crust is thicker than your usual NY slice so don't think you'll be getting any thin crust here. The slice can be definitely shared by two inebriated friends or one hungry man-child. Definitely worth a try...and if you're still hungry.. Halal guys just opened up their new cart and soon to be storefront across the street. ** groupon just posted a deal for a $24 or 48 at the chelsea location

A great find. Â Reminds me of an old work lunch favorite in Boston. Â Anyway- I had a tuna pocket with feta and spinach, delicious. Â Matt had a speciality sandwich with chicken and hot sauce that he loved. Â The only thing Â we didn't like, the fries, and the rest of the food well made up for that. Â I will definitely be back for more!
Great selection of craft beers, really like the bar set up. My only complaint is that they don't do flights...

The buffalo wings and the fries alone gives this spot 5 stars!!! I was really impressed!! The chiptole mayo was a good sidekick to the Â fries as well.BUT the wings were some of the best i ever had! Perfectly fried to perfection.. ummmm umm um!!! The downside to Bonnie's was the can of soda for 1.50 and my under cooked and under seasoned turkery burger.. smh ...the service was ok... had to ask for a refill on water but Other than that i will definetly be back for the wings (they were that good)!!

This is a standard hungover Saturday midafternoon delivery spot for when I crash at Leo's. Which is just about every other weekend, if not more frequently. Hennyways. Pad thai = good, calamari = very good. Greasy, quick, relatively cheap, and not too tough for a recovering tummy. Rock. Oh yeah, and it tastes good.
Excellent food. Excellent beer selection. The skirt steak on a baguette roll was one of the best sandwiches I've ever had. Bartenders super friendly. Great atmosphere.

I came here for dinner recently and was not very impressed with the pizza. Â When I read thin crust I thought back to Italy and this was certainly no where near the quality of the thin crust pizza I had in Italy. Â For pizza I had the 4 Stagioni and split the fried calamari appetizer. Â Not bad, just disappointing, especially considering the prices.

Great, fresh food, friendly and funny staff, memorable West Village setting -- what more can you ask for! Three of four of us had the special of black fettichini with shrimp, asparagus and tomato. It was great, light homemade noodles with fresh ingredients and the perfect amount of seasoning. It is a big dish (one man was too full to finish it, and women shared one order with no trouble). The ravioli was also a hit, though a much smaller portion. Cash only. Beer and wine only. No noticeable air conditioning but a nice breeze through the open doors/windows.

A-ok, meh, coulda been better. Â My steak wasn't cooked to order, but I was afraid to send it back... Lost a star when the waiter (read: NYU student or recent grad who is miserable this is the best job he could find after throwing down $100k in loans) had a problem with me asking him to repeat a few items. Would return if someone else pays.

The food is incredibly fresh & delicious, all hand made, and Â no preservatives. They have a friendly staff & a fantastic Human Resource Manager. I would recommend the shrimp roll , unda chicken, and the Mango Lassi. AAAAAAAAmmazingggg !!I give them an Â A+ on food and staff. 5 star, would recommend for catering!

I booked a table for 2 at 8pm. When we got there by 8pm, the host tells me my reservation was for 6pm (I can be pretty sure that i repeated 8pm more than once to make sure it was made clear enough). At the same time all I see is a huge line and I think that I better start heading out elsewhere to have dinner. They made me wait a couple of minutes, and they told me that there is a table for us 2 ready at the back of the restaurant, which is usually for walk-in clients. It turned out to be a beautiful table, next to the oven where they cook their delicious pizzas and with an opening on the ceiling with plenty of natural light. The service was excellent, nice suggestions from the waitress and the food was delicious. We had one of their pizzas and 2 appetizers and it all was delicious. We had the house wine which was excellent and they brought some deserts on the house for the problem when we came in. All and all I can only say the experience and they way of handling all kind of situations seemed to be perfect for my taste. I must say prices are right to what you have. They'll see me around in future.
Free sample of truffle mayo...delicious Got mine with chutney...so so good. Â I'll be back soon.

It is a very crowded restaurant. Food was good but the waitress was not - refused to offer my Vegan friend any options - he asked for lettuce & tomatos, and she said that this Italian restaurant had no tomatos. I asked for a Drambuie with dessert and she said they did not have any. I had to correct her because I had seen a bottle at the bar while waiting for the table. Would have been a great experience with better waitstaff.

I enjoyed this place. The only thing that was bad was our waiter. He was the slowest waiter I've encountered in a long time. We got some empanadas (beef and ham and cheese). Both were good. We also had the mac and cheese with pork belly which was delicious. It had a little kick to it, but nothing major. Our last bit of our meal was the cubano sandwich. I've had better cuban sandwiches though. Not my fave. The yucca fries were some of the best I've ever had though. The waiter took forever to take our orders. Instead he thought it was better to work on the computer with checks for 5 other tables. I understand that you have a lot of tables, but making a table that hasn't been greeted wait, every minute is another minute that our order isn't being worked on in the kitchen.

Every time I eat here, I end up telling myself "never again" as I waddle away shamefully with my face covered in white filth and sweating profusely because I've decided to put entirely too much red sauce again. Then I come back for more.
Not is good as I remember, they still have the half off Belgian beer on Monday's which is a must, since the beers are outrageously priced.

I tried it tonight at about 6 pm. Won't return. Service and food (classic, tomato soup and Oreo shake) were sub par. Ordering was fine. Heard him call out my shake order, and said my order would be ready in 5-7 mins. The soup and grilled cheese were up but my shake was not. Wasn't made. So I waited another 3+ minutes. Grilled cheese was not as fresh and hot as I thought it would be. Soup and shake were ok, nothing great. The other notable thing is the were at least 5 other employees around the outside of the stand. Some going in and out while I waited for my food. Just seemed very laxed in regards to workers hanging out. Likely, that is why my order wasn't quite interesting enough. Too many distractions.

Great, basic Italian fare. Don't judge the food by the small, bare bones ambiance. All the pastas I've tried here have been delicious and the vegetarian soup of the day (zucchini at the time) was amazing, probably the highlight of the meal. Wine is nothing to write home about but is reasonably priced. Only complaint is the service: very slow at times. Was eating here with my friend and his entree came out significantly later than mine, no apologies or explanation from the staff. (Also there were a couple small bones in his pasta, which the waiter said was how it was supposed to be but seemed pretty strange). Cash only. Used to love coming here and would give it 4 or 5 stars but the service my last time dining here really left me with an unpleasant impression.
taking subway on a stormy snowy day on x'mas day...and they are open! LOVE the food, extra sauce plz!
Came here with a local & pumped that I did. Â Don't leave here without getting the Pork Buns. Started with those & had the Totto Ramen. Great meal!!

Wafa's is a great little family run place with tasty food and great prices. We have yet to dine in, just takeout so far but everything we've tried has been great. The falafel sandwich is wrapped in a delicious flatbread, not pita and has a nice array of veggie toppings and a hotsauce that, in my opinion, could bring a little more to the table than just heat, however, its still a delicious falafel. The lamb shawarma comes on the same bread as the falafel and is also rolled up, and chock full of delicious toppings. One word of caution, the flatbread doesn't stand the test of time too well so all the more reason to eat quickly. Do yourself a favor and stop in, they will not disappoint.

The lines are ridiculous on late weekend nights, but damn is the food good. Leftovers for when you're sober are even better. Combo plate all the way!! If only I lived in NY.. I'd be all over this place like their white sauce on rice! AHHHHHH MY DREAMS ARE MADE OF THIS!

I've been to Rattle N Hum on several occasions.. and I can safely say that it's the beer selection which brings me back, sometimes against my better judgment. The problem? This place gets PACKED with the post work rush (which happens to be the only time I'm in the area) Is it worth standing in a tight spot while having multiple people bump into you as they walk past just to get a few very excellent beers? That's for you to decide. (Oh, and the food is pretty mediocre too)

Great pie made with love from the founder himself! Delicious ingredients and a firm crunchy crust makes this place live up to its "best in the state" reputation. Don't let the wait time or price scare you away because this pizza does not disappoint!
oh my FUCKING GOD. You know the deal. This place is the Truth.

Been coming here for the past 9 years. Always get the "mixed with everything" (chicken/lamb/rice/lettuce). Extra white sauce! Gotta be careful with the hot sauce, cause it's REALLY spicy. I remember when a platter was just $5, but the price increase never really bothered me. The only thing that DID bother me is when they stopped including tomatoes with the lettuce. That was YEARS ago, but tomatoes compliment that dish well. Still though, this is great stuff, and I sometimes order 2, so I can have one for lunch the next day. FAT!

This place has always been on the top of my picks for visiting friends. Clean place, great food, very friendly service. Watch out for their "quiet birthday celebration"! First tried this place a few years back, second time right before heading down to Miami for some "real" Cuban cuisine, which turned out not nearly as good as what we had here. If you have never tried Cuban cuisine definitely start here, and if you are familiar with the dishes you probably have heard of this place already. Highly recommend their Ropa Vieja, one the very few places that shred their meat to such thin strings. Most other places just do large chunks. Their ox tail, which was a new item on the menu few years ago, has quickly become a permanent item because it really falls right off the bone. The sides are what brings the meat dishes to life. Their Fried sweet plantain is prepared to the right amount of crispiness and burnt smell of the brown sugar. Appetizers like Plantain chips with garlic sauce, and newly added crunchy toasted bread at the start of the meal really brings out the appetite. Not so crowded, at least during lunch and afternoon on the weekends. Good for group. Very reasonable pricing. Groups of 3 or 4 avg $20-25 per person full to the throat. P.S. I only give out one 5 star for each cuisine. Updated as new experience comes around.

I Love it Here. I have been about a dozen times and the food never disappoints me. It is a unique spot in a "trendy" locations. Hells Kitchen is packed with good eateries but this one always stands out for me. I love going before a show - the Prix Fix cannot be beat!! 22.95 for dinner for a salad and ENDLESS homemade pasta. The pasta is so fresh and so tasty. It allows for you to try different items on the menu and refill whatever you liked the best(any or all). Becco is also EXCELLENT for lunch. I love the breadsticks, the bean spread and the breads and olive they start you out with. The $25.00 bottle wine selections can't be beat. The wines are crisp and tasty. The waitstaff is very very knowledgeable. The only weird thing is the bathrooms which are practically int he kitchen and are unisex. It is a really great experience for a New York eatery and everyone I have ever taken there has always loved it and has gone back. GREAT SPOT!

Love this place. The sandwiches are reasonably priced compared to other joints in the city. Drinks such as the thai iced tea is delish. Perfect combination of meat and veggies. Bread is ALWAYS, ALWAYS for the many years I've been a customer, is ALWAYS crispy and light. Seasoned meat is on point and the veggies, mixed with cilantro and some spicy peppers are to die for. I can eat this stuff everyday. It's busy, but service is fast. You're and out within minutes. Definite place to visit from all walks of life.

Maybe I got lucky, like win the lotto lucky, but I only waited about 5 minutes to be seated here (might help I got there at midnight Saturday night). That being said, this Ramen is the best ramen I've had outside of Japan. And I ate Â A LOT of Ramen in Japan. First off I'd like to put this out there: IPPUDO beats MOMOFUKU. Why? Because you get better portions for better prices. Momofuku is like the $100 hotel restaurant steak compared to the $40 Ruth's Chris that tastes exactly the same, and for your money you can get more. So yeah, I just said that. Started off with the Hirata pork buns - good sized pork buns with crispy edges, a sweet sauce and a little bit of spicy mayo (nice touch). Then moved onto Ramen. Akamaru Modern with extra sliced pork (seriously, just ask for the extra pork, and you'll love it). Served with a thick thick succulent broth - it tastes like they've been stewing it in a huge pot with an entire pig for days and days - was amazing. The noodle (made in house) had a perfect amount of chewiness and texture - did I mention it was made in house? The pork...oh the pork...more of the similar pork from the Hirata bun, the pork is fatty and salty, which is to say Â AMAZING. Yes, so order more. Another nice touch, is about halfway through eating it, you can tell your server "Kae Dama" and for another $2 you can have another serving of noodles added to your dish, which basically ill give you a nice 2nd bowl of ramen. If you're splitting your ramen, its a perfect way to satisfy both - if you're like me and you're a fatty - it'll satisfy your craving for more. People complain that they don't think $14 for a bowl of ramen is a good deal. I'll give you that, $14 is crazy when you consider $1 ramen packs at Â the market $7 bowls of pho at a viet restaurant, and $10 bowls of pasta at Italian places. BUT SERIOUSLY guys, for an authentic, flavorful, and satisfying experience, $14 is a great deal - and when you compare it to the cream of the crop ramen houses (Sapporo, and Momofuku come to mind) its just within the field of play.

I have no problem driving from Staten Island and sitting in traffic just to get there for lunch and order their Steak with French Fries and Arugula salad ! Atmosphere: The cafe looks tiny but it's actually very roomy! It reminds me of those adorable cafÃ©s you see in French movies. The "indoor" backyard area is my favorite to sit in! Designed so cosy, romantic and overall just beautiful ! This place is a great date spot or a place to go with friends. Food: Out of all the items I've ordered, the steak with arugula salad is just heaven ! Â It's honestly cooked to perfection. The salad is very light and has a light zesty taste. The French fries are perfectly crispy and the steak just melts in your mouth! The only down fall I would say is having to wait until 6o'clock for it to be available to order since it's just on their dinner menu. Customer service: Besides the fact that all the waitress look like European supermodels, they are extremely professional, and courteous ! They don't annoy you by coming to your table every three seconds asking "is everything okay" and they do not leave you without water ! They have the perfect balance. You never wait for a check to long or your food to come out. This is honestly my favorite place to go to eat when I come to Williamsburg and I highly recommend it !

Went here with my husband and another couple on 4/30/11. Â I ordered the BBQ pork (#1) and husband ordered the #4 (cold cuts w/Pate). Â The sandwiches were pretty big, which is always a good thing. The bread: Â All 4 of us disliked the bread. Â It was waaaay too crispy. Â Not "fresh bread crusty" type of crispy, but over toasted to the extreme type of crispy. Â I had a hard time biting into it, and it made a HUGE mess with all the crumbs. Â The bread was the worst I've had on a banh mi ever. The meat: Â The BBQ pork was a bit strange. Â It was small little pieces, and it was sweet and dry. Â There was also not enough of it, and it was all at the bottom of the bread and not evenly spread out. Â My husband's cold cuts w/Pate were tastier, since the pate moistened the overly dry bread a little more. The veggies: Â I liked the pickled carrots and daikon very much. Â The daikon had good flavor. Â The cilantro was fresh. Â No problem with the veggies, best part of the sandwich. Â I asked for spicy, but spicy it was not. Â I ended up adding Sriracha. Overall: Â I was really disappointed in this sandwich. Â A few days before I stumbled upon VNam Cafe in the east Village and got 2 sandwiches from there. Â They were really good (4 stars in comparison). Â With as many amazing reviews as this place gets, I was really disappointed and will not come back. Â Maybe others haven't had a really good banh mi, and think these are great? Â I don't know..they are not great if you know how a banh mi SHOULD taste. Try VNam Cafe instead, the bread there is WAAAY better!

Whatever happened to this place over the past few years?!?!?!?! I'm shocked at how watered down their square slices are. If I wanted water in my pizza I would leave it in the rain not order it. The sauce started getting sweeter also (I'm assuming they make a simple syrup, and drench the pizza with it). Thanks but no thanks!

Outstanding. Ordered a variety of small stuff including oysters, a salad, and an unbelievable soft-shell crab sandwich to split. Everything, including the wine and service, absolutely top notch. Not expensive at all for what you get. This is New York for chrissakes. Would go again for sure. Hmm. Maybe this weekend. Yum. Thank you Marlow and Sons. Keep up the good work.
Someone please send me a plane ticket so I can have dinner here again. The Calamari was unforgettable... Plus I miss Astoria!

Well, nice try, but needs work. Â Rattle N Hum claims to have over 60 beers on tap, with a heavy emphasis on American craft beers. Â In reality, it's more like 30 or 40 and almost all of those weren't available the Sunday I stopped in. Â They were out of the first 3 or 4 things I tried to order and my friends weren't having luck either. Â The bartender was good, though; she made suggestions and did the best with what management has given her to work with. Â There's a full bar, didn't check to see if they have wine. Â The menu is standard Irish pub far; we tried the sliders and the wings, both of which were pretty good. Â It's a smallish place with a bar and about 15 wooden tables. Â Here's hoping they get their act together.

Hip to the max. Â Went for dinner and thought it was OK-nothing special. Â I understand when your menu changes daily you don't have many options. When we got there basically the menu was a salad cheeseburger/hamburger or and omelet, no chicken sandwich on at all (which I had heard to much about!). Â  Bummer! Â Got the cheeseburger because basically had no other options and ordered it Medium. As we're waiting a pretty long time for our food (place is not busy) we see 2 chicken sandwiches pass by us. Â So maybe its a cool hidden menu thing and you just need to "know" how to order it? Personally I hate stuff like that. So our burgers came and they were decent. Definitely over cooked for medium-no pink inside at all (same with my boyfriends). Overall-good but most likely not going back
Good food

Some of their food is really great, they're open 24 hours, and they have a very central location (Right by the N train.) Â Pitfals are: not-so-tasty fries and annoying staff (at times). Â The wraps are really yummy, though.

It's a must at least once. Every time my CT friends are in town we end up there at 5 am. Watch the sauce though - they love to put on a lot and if you cant handle it, it's not as enjoyable. You can put on your own sauce. The line moves quickly or you can go across the street....no seating so take off your heels!

Ha, yes, I remember it well. Â I've talked to some of those snooty NYcers myself. Â But oh well, their lost, because The Grocery. Â Had dinner with my family here once. Â And the experience was great. Â We had clams (sprinkled with garlicky goodness), trout stuffed with mushroom, homemade sausage, and two other entrees I think. Â It was under $100. Â The space is small but the food is crazy.

Really great service - the host was not present and the guy who welcomed me apparently does not know how to seat a guest, but other than that our waiter was very friendly and accommodating and another server thanked me and called me by my last name on my way out (I had made a reservation) which made me feel very fancy. The food was pretty good too. I had the mushroom linguini and the person I went with had the cauliflower pizza.

The place is small, but it's cute. They only have tables for 2, so it's not the best place to go if you have a large group. Â The table next to us had 4 people, so they just put 2 tables together. The chicken pad thai was disappointing and had a strange after taste. (kinda like sausages) The noodle was hard. I've definitely had much better before. The best part was the thai iced tea. Â It's unique because you get to mix it yourself. Â They bring out a tray with a glass cup filled with "tea" ice cubes. Â Yes, ice cubes made with actual tea so it doesn't dilute the drink and make it tastes all watery. The tea is in another glass which you pour into the cup of ice yourself. Â The syrup and milk are also in separate glasses. Â You're pretty much mixing your own drink here, so you can control the amount of sweetness you desire.

This place has great malaysian/chinese food, it's pretty authentic all around. Â Great curry noodle soup or the hainan chicken dish. Check out some asam stingray dish too if you want to try something different. Â Get an order of roti canai as well. Decor is good, staff is not bad. Â  Con: Â the male "dyed blonde hair" chinese owner/casher got very bad breath and bad attitude. Â He just wants you to pay and get out of his restaurant. Â  need better friendlier service..

Had dinner outside here recently. The place is nice while still feeling comfy. I ordered the BBQ brisket tacos which were very tasty but small! Not filling. It was okay because I stole some of my boyfriend's chicken fried steak, which was nice and juicy. You won't believe me but the way they cooked his okra (also stole that) made it actually taste good! They have a lot of interesting menu items.

Wtf is a tapas? Had some vague idea before this weekend that "Tapas" = small, experimental appetizers that are fairly expensive. Needless to say, low on my list of mouthventures. My date picked this place. I had no idea what Alta was, or that it was a tapas restaurant. Tucked away in plain sight on a residential stretch of greenwich, easy to walk past (twice). **************************** SETTING: The ambience is every female's rustic wet dream. What panties? All dark honey toned, warm wood, spacious but cozy. Our waitress was great, patiently responding to our questions, making excellent wine suggestions. She also took time to mention the restaurant's history when we remarked on the beautiful interior. The owner wanted to mimic Spain/Europe experience as much as possible. Alta is converted from an old church, and that really really shines through in its structure and atmosphere. ***************************** FOOD: An experience best geared to those with sensitive palettes, to pick up on subtle shifts and marriages. We chewed everything slowly, "savored" and "hummed" and "lifted our brows" like cultured foodies do. /// Most enjoyed: - bacon-wrapped something something with almonds (anything bookended by these are obvious win) - lamb meatballs with something something sauce and perfect egg -- absolutely scrumptious. - The earl grey gelato that comes with one of the desserts rendered everything around it unacceptable. -- /// Only Okay: - Tuna tartare revealed cascading layers of bland and salt. It wasn't bad, I enjoyed it, but don't count on it being the highlight of your meal. - Carpaccio of Black Bass: we didn't know what a "carpaccio" was, so what came out kind of looked like a garnished plate of semen. I expected I'd have to scoop it out with a spoon, but fear not. It is not semen. It is a paper thin sliced pancake of bass. Not bad at all, tasted mostly like lemon with a fresh, interesting texture. All the dishes we had that night (6) were good though. ********************************* FINAL TIPS: - 3 tapas plates recommended per person - Better for couples - (6) plates + (1) dessert will run you ~ $100 or more. Add a bottle of excellent wine, and you'll push $150. - Excellent date place. We stayed there for about 3 hours by accident. * 4.5 stars as a date place that I would THOROUGHLY enjoy being taken to. * 3.5 stars final verdict ONLY because 1) I do not see myself returning frequently, for 2) I'm not [yet] a baller. Highly Recommended.

2 stars or 1, really not sure. Â Tried pork taco, chicken- both seemed way overly cooked and dried out. Â Flavorless, not juicy as a taco should be. Â The tortilla though actually had some flavor to it. What did look amazing? The huge nachos platter served next to us. Â Now that might be very good!
Good food! Small space & long wait on Sunday

Sweet heavenly, other-worldly, transcendent pancakes. Â I didn't know pancakes could be so wonderful, but these are not your dad's Saturday morning flapjacks. Â  Served with amazing maple butter, served with wild Maine blueberries or banana and walnuts, these pancakes are truly the best you will ever have in your life. The biscuits, served with truly, truly, truly incredible raspberry jam are amazing, too. The rest of the menu looked terrific, but I'm never going to be able to order anything else as long as these pancakes are on the menu. Take note, though, the wait time is insane. Â No really. Â INSANE. Â B. and I went on a Monday we'd both taken off, thinking we brilliantly would miss the weekend crowds, and at 11:15 the wait was 45 minutes. Â When I left at 12:30 the wait was over an hour. Â An hour long wait on a MONDAY. Â Who are these people? Â Don't they have jobs? Â I don't even want to know the average wait time on the weekends. I'm not generally a fan of brunch and even less of a fan of waiting for it, but I daresay this was worth it. Â Phenomenal.
ehh..okay you can't get better than 10 dumplings for $2. Â But the dumplings are just okay. Â Although crispy, the meat tastes old and its way too oily. Â Good for those on a budget and in a hurry.

Nice Happening spot in Park Slope Brooklyn, Great Vibe inside good music in the background and Â the really nice bar area was packed. I went Saturday after the Puerto Rican parade At the pier. It was wall to wall packed. The people in the other restaurants looked sad they had not stopped by Bogota instead of their restaurant . The menu offers a number of apps and entrees from all over Latin America not just Columbia . I had the Steak with onions. Outstanding!! This is the place to be over in park slope.

Hard place to find, and even harder place to seat. Â There is always a long wait since the restaurant is very small. Â If you come with more than a group of 2, you're going to have a bad time. Â If you have a group, come before they open, and hog your seat that way. Â  The food is good and light. Â Don't expect to be completely stuffed when you walk away. Â For the prices, I would've expected a little more substance and flavor. Â We ordered two brunch specials, and it took a while for the food to come. Â Once we finished, we still felt hungry and not completely satisfied. Â Sadly, it took us two tries to get a table which only made it worse that the food didn't live up to the expectations.

This review is purely based on the Korean BBQ and not the hotpot. I came here a few weeks back craaaaving some KBBQ and decided to try this joint. It's been open for a while now and I've been trying to come...but they never take reservations on a Friday evening and the wait time is usually 1-1.5 hours. I came here on a late Sunday afternoon and got seating for 2 right away. The KBBQ comes at $25.99(?) per person..which isn't too terrible. They offer a pretty decent meat selection and the house specials were quite tasty. I don't remember what it was at the moment, but i'm sure you can see it on the menu. It's AYCE, so you don't have to worry about not getting full..although some of the meats gets tiring after the first plate. Don't forget to order the seafood pancake too, it was a bit wet...but quite flavorful as well. I had to drop a few stars due to the LOW fire and the lack of korean based sauces. The fire was set really low and whenever I tuned it higher, the server will lower it back. This got quite annoying as I wasn't able to get a nice sear on the meat. I think the servers were given strict orders to keep the heat low to avoid damaging the plates. There were tons of sauces to choose from since they also serve hotpot...but where are the korean sauces for this KBBQ?! The servers were quick, SUPER nice, and extremely helpful. Don't remember her name..but the chick with the fauxhawk was our server. Probably one of the best servers/waitresses I've ever had. Will definitely try the hotpot next time I go.

I love the food it's some of the best Greek I've had and if I were judging on food alone I've give 5 stars, however to eat you have to through the obnoxious east European wait Â staff. In all the times I've been I have not walked away feeling warm and fuzzy about the experience. However will be going back, soon hopefully.

I had a groupon for this place so I decided to go one night with my girls. The mussels were eh. The fries were really soggy and way too salty. I've had mussels before and I'm sure it wasn't supposed to taste like that. We got a bottle of wine which was dirt cheap. Thats a plus. My friend had the chicken and she said it was moist. Maybe I just picked the wrong thing from the menu?

Well if you have read my previous reviews you know I loved Traif so when searching for my next dining adventure I was excited to give Xixa a try. They did not disappoint! One really cool thing they do that I wish Traif did was the 10 course prefix for $40 per person. I was a bit nervous to try it at first because hey they could give you anything and maybe we wouldn't get to try the stuff we wanted the most. They were great and happily took our request when I asked for no fish. I even mentioned that the only fish option I would be up for trying is the "fish and chips". They were so great he even had them bring us that as one of the 10 courses. When we saw the 1st course they brought out we were confident we would be full after 10 - they do look small but well planned to make sure you are nice and stuffed by the end. Also, we definitely got 12 dishes, not 10. AMAZING! 2 desserts - hell yes. Here are a few things we tried that stand out in my mind: chicken sopes - tasty little tortillas with chicken liver which was surprisingly delish (I've never had liver!) foie gras - DELICIOUS - very sweet/savory type dish I adored it but it was a bit sweet for the BF fish & chips - it was not as I was expecting, kind of ceviche like duck lettuce wraps - SO good, this is how duck was mean to be tasted. The lettuce was crisp and the duck so juicy carnitas of pork belly - I am so torn about pork belly as it is usually too fatty for me but this was my dream come true.. perfectly succulent meat. churros with jalapeno sorbet - separate the sorbet was weird but all together it was amazing and very fresh One thing I am really sad about is no carrots for us to try! Oh well, just means I have to come back for a 2nd visit! Definitely make a trip to Xixa, you won't regret it!

Bruschetta = AMAZING! This place is a welcome addition to the neighborhood as it helps increase the options from minimal to just above limited. The big plus for me was that they generally have at least 2 vegetarian options. Portion sizes are the "just enough" ballpark. The ambiance is pretty nice as well with the dim lights, photos and exposed brick. I hated olives but for some reason this place made me enjoy them. They offer olives and bread when you sit and can bring out balsamic and olive oil if needed.

Don't get me wrong. I'm still a fan of Natureworks, but I had to take away one star after my last visit there. Since it's near my office I usually walk over and end up deciding last minute what I want versus ordering through Seamless. I was pretty set on a falafel sandwich, but I wasn't too sure. Once I got there, I went ahead and ordered a falafel sandwich with a side of vegetarian chilli. It was close to 1:30 or 2 PM so the place wasn't as packed as it tends to get. Afterwards, I proceeded to walk back to the office and sit down to enjoy my meal. To my horror, when I got a couple of bites into the falafel it was hard, like it hadn't been cooked through the entire way. Now, I am by no means an expert in the art of falafel making, but I'm pretty sure it's not supposed to feel like a rock either when you bite down on it. Same thing with the vegetarian soup/chilli. Not all of the beans had been thoroughly cooked so when you bit down on some they were extremely hard. I LOVE Natureworks but they are going need to get it together on the falafel/chilli making department. I won't be ordering either item for a while.
Great Burgers and Milkshakes! best deal in the area- unlike the overpriced bedford ave places...

What can I say that hasn't already been spoken by other true Yelpers? Â  We waited 45 minutes on a dark, rainy Tuesday evening. Â Huh? Â This must be good... The "Host" was cute, let us to our table in great spirits. Â How could we not get pumped up about this?? Luckily the menu is small because I was ravenous and could not deal with indecision at that point. Â Ordered pickled cucumbers as an app (recommended - fresh & zesty) and spicy veggie ramen. Â Surprisingly, this was excellent. Â Broth was definitely comparable to the miso broth, except not as creamy. Â Great flavor & spices. Â There were a ton of veggies in there that were extremely fresh and unique. Â  I did make one sad realization. Â Avocado does NOT belong in ramen. Â This is a first. Â I eat avocados in every way, shape, and form on a daily (or near daily) basis, and this is the first time that I haven't liked an avocado in some sort of food concoction. Â It hurts me, but skip 'em.

Best overall bowl of ramen so far in NYC. Was it worth the one hour wait? For a bowl of ramen probably not, but it was good. The broth was salty yet not overpowering and had a good flavor and the ingredients were well put together and the noodles were also cooked very well. The pork buns were the best non-bbq style pork buns i've had. But the bbq pork at ippudo still wins, this is still pretty damn good. For what its worth, I'd recommend everyone try this place, maybe at non-peak times, but still be prepared for a little wait. I'd definitely return when i'm craving ramen, just at non-peak times because long waits for ramen are killer.

Yuca Bar was a recommendation from some local barman, we were a group of 8 and we were seated easily enough. Â The service was excellent, we all had so much fun with the server, she was super friendly and had a very good humor, always smiling, which we loved! Â Also the manager was super nice checking us out, and making sure that we had everything we wanted! We also loved the decor...we were talking about the place and the FOOD all night long... the food, OMG!!!! Is so delicious! We ate almost all tapas, and it was hard to choose the best one, Â but I would say I loved the mussels and the arepa vegetariana the most....wait and the ceviche tasting!!! VERY good! THE DRINKS!!!! Â LOL!!!!!! Super well done!!!! Was just perfect!!! All my friends wasn't planing to drink a lot...but we simplify couldn't cause the drinks were so good! I had met the "caipirinha" in Brazil and I loved, but at yuca was BETTER than Brazil!!! Most of my friends din't know it, Â and they also loved! Drinks are very good prices, the caipirinha was made with a good quality cachaÃ§a (Leblon) and Â was a huge drink comparing to any other caipirinha that I had before... Â  but the real reason that I'm giving it 5 stars is.... EVERYTHING Â :) At the end we were super happy and satisfied, and our server recommended the desert TRES LECHES, which was INCREDIBLE delicious! LOL!!! I can't wait Â to go back! They also said that they have a Brazilian night every thursdays with brazilian music, food and drinks.....I really want to check that out! Sounds great! :)

You can't really go wrong by adding spicy mayo, pickled carrots and cucumbers to any sandwich. Â So far had the shrimp and the spanish mackerel and really liked them both. Tried a bite of my friend's pork belly and it was kind of amazing but superfatty.

Historic Classic Awesome Cool Bar in Historic Classic Awesome Cool Downtown Neighbourhood. My cocktail was fantastic and my food was great. Â I sat at the bar upstairs, I was a woman alone, and felt very comfortable. Â I had a few hours to spare and wanted to check out a hip place. Â I felt like I stepped back in time, to a more civilised place. Â I would return.

BUT PLEASE--Make sure that every montadito that is supposed to have "crispy onion" on it Actually Does! I have too regularly found that orders that are supposed to have this topping DON'T...get on the ball, kitchen. Otherwise, what's not to like here?!

I am glad to see a place to stop in and get some delicious (homemade?) dessert and a cup of coffee. Cute place, and very full for 3 pm on a weekday. I've only been there once. My friend and I had two pieces of pie and some coffee. I got a key lime meringue and she got some towering chocolate special. Both were very good.Our visit cost $20, not cheap, but....Didn't try the lunch food but the place was full of others enjoying it. I'll be back for more dessert in the future!

The Adjarian Khatchapuri was amazing and the best I had outside of Adjaria. Waiters are nice and friendly, they are from Georgia and very helpful to navigate the menu and advise on the different dishes. Nice backpatio. Will definitely go back.

One of the best restaurants I've been in manhattan. Impeccable service, delicious and fresh product, intimal and inviting atmosphere. I fell in love with Pylos menu and its Mediterranean inspired cuisine. (Greek cuisine has many commonalities with Italian, Spanish or Israeli). The lamb, the fish and the moussaka are a must. You better go in a group so you can share and try as many dishes as possible. It's a pity just to try one or two (portions are big) considering how delicious everything is!

for the hype that was around this joint i was expecting punch in my face type of meal. Â and explosion of flavor in my mouth. Â but i was a bit disappointed. Â the only thing memorable there was the soup dumplings and dont get me wrong, they were quite tasty. Â outside of that, the food was so-so. Â food was either salty or bland. Â the meal didnt really seem to fit. Â and for china town food this place is pretty expensive. Â i definitely recommend you hitting up shanghai cafe. Â much better spot.
I always order the same thing here every single time -- the orlin burger. What can go wrong with a signature burger?!
Awesome! I could have 5 slices... The best experience in the summer
The pasta special is a great and always tasty!

So refreshing to have a different place to order from for lunch at work, ordered chicken Caesar salad and it was really, really Â good, the chicken was super moist and tasty, their clementine soda is really good too, can't wait to try everything else, and prices are very reasonable for this area! Hope they stay that way !

Ironically, in a city with a plethora of good eats, this is one of my favorite places (by places, I mean cart) to grab a bite to eat. Â They serve only a few items: chicken over rice, gyro over rice, and falafel over rice. Â The most popular item, as you've probably noted from other reviews, is their chicken over rice. Â You have two options for meat: chicken and beef. Â Being a greedy carnivore, I could not pick between the two and just opted for both. Â I was very happy with my decision. Â The meat is obviously halal and is chopped on the grilled. Â The rice is saffron-infused (it's yellow/orange). Â I found the rice to be extremely flavorful and this is coming from someone who is not big on rice (yes, an Asian who doesn't love rice). Â You are also given several pita triangles to accompany your rice, but in the future, I'd just opt for more rice. Â The final touch to this wonderful meal is sauce -- you get three options: yogurt-based white sauce (tzatziki-like), hot sauce, and a brown BBQ sauce (?). Â I added one part white sauce and one part hot sauce. Â Yummy! Â I would not recommend this ratio if you are intolerant of spicy foods; go easy on the hot sauce. Â  There was not much of a wait, but I was there on a Thursday at 11:30 PM and it was raining. Â I hear lines can stretch down the street and around the corner. Â This is a great cart to grab food from after enjoying nightlife in the city. Â A heaping container of food is only $6. Â I will be back each time I visit NYC.

First time here, definitely will not be the last.. Gourmet pizzas, great service, great atmosphere..
