Would like to see something other than pizza or salads as an alternative dish, but that's just a personal opinion.. The Brownie Sunday dessert was judged AWESOME by our whole group so make sure you try it..

After church on the way back north to see the marathon 2013, my friend suggested that we go in for Brunch. Â My Frittata with fresh yellow and zucchini squash was delicious with New York cheese melted over. Â The fresh Italian bread was the best bread that I have had in New York City. Â My friend had smoked salmon on a bagel with an egg on each half. Â It looked so good and my friend devoured it all!' Â I just wish I liked smoked salmon. Then for dessert we shared a sunken chocolate cake topped with vanilla ice cream drizzled with hot dark chocolate sauce. Â It was so good I wished I could have liked the plate clean

I have nothing but love for this place. If you're a healthy foodie, have food allergies, seeking healthy take away foods before your flight or train, juice or smoothie seeker, love chocolate, love gluten-free foods, anal retentive about your ingredients, then this is the place for you. Hu Kitchen is a casual eatery with quality foods from quality resources and ingredients. The best I've seen yet. in NYC. You can take away or sit at a table. Table service does not exist. I'd like to think of it as an upscale Pret A Manger. I'm happy that a place like this finally exists in New York City! I hope to see Hu Kitchens around the world!

The only reason I'm giving this two stars is because I really enjoyed the dumplings. Ok: I got the peashoot and garlic dumplings. They were boiled to perfection. The outsides weren't gross and hard or too gooey. The flavor was pretty fantastic. Honestly, I wish they would have filled them up a bit more and they should offer another veg flavor to keep things fresh and interesting. The sauce was great as well. There are six per order served on a leafy bed. Then I ordered the "key lime pie". Umm.... Key lime pie is NOT supposed to be a frozen white unflavored lump. It was DISGUSTING. It tasted like it had been in the freezer for months and was one of those crappy store-bought ones. Bad idea. The service here is TERRIBLE. I came in on a Friday at about 3 in the afternoon. It was dead. There were 3 servers and 3 tables (mine included) that were occupied. The server I had was completely rude and too busy talking to her co-workers to actually do her job. One of the other servers actually had to give me my check. I looked at it and couldn't really read the writing but it turns out they tried to overcharge me almost $10! I found this out after waiting for the server to come get the check for 20 minutes. What the heck? I'm clearly sitting here waiting for you and you just ignore me and chat with your friends. They expected me to just leave a $20 bill for a check that should have only been $12 at most. Sorry, your service definitely didn't warrant an eight dollar tip. I wouldn't come back here again after the poor treatment and subpar food I got. I can find amazing dumplings elsewhere.

Hands down the best pancakes I have every had in my entire life. Place usually packed but the food is worth it, just be sure to make a reservation. I really thought the place would be overrated but it wasn't. It lives up to the hype. Steak and Eggs here was more than decent. The steak was a small portion but turned out to be enough and the $12 mimosas here are good too even though I didn't want to spend $12 on a mimosa. The fried chicken served on a biscuit here is awesome. It comes with a sauce, possibly a mayo? It made the sandwich and its great for sharing. Again, those pancakes are a foodgasm!

Tried the chicken liver mousse, fried oyster, pork chop, and the burger. The chicken liver mousse lacked the flavor that I like. The fried oysters were standard as was the burger and the pork chop. If we didn't have a discount, it would have been too much for the meal but with the discount it was about right. It is a small place with loud music but they didn't seem to have a record of our reservation which was a little odd.

My girlfriend and I went here last night, and we had an unfortunate experience. Things started off OK, drinks came out right away, and were good. When we ordered our food, we got a bad feeling because the waitress didn't write anything down, and asked us to repeat what we wanted multiple times. We were only two or three bites into our appetizers (oysters, and crab cakes) when our meals arrived. Timing wasn't perfect, but at least the food was correct, despite having to repeat our orders to her multiple times. I ordered a burger, cooked medium. After my first bite, I discovered it was VERY well done. Which surprised me, since the food came out so fast. A waitress came by to ask how our food was (not our waitress) and I told her that it was OK, but my burger was not medium, it was well done. She said sorry, then our waitress comes back and this is what she said: "The same thing happened to my friend here the other day. Sometimes when the meat is in the fridge, the red color goes away, and turns brown. But it's fresh, I promise. It's also cooked medium, it's only the color of well done because of the fridge." Really, what can I say to that??? I barely ate half the burger. It was just terrible. I know a well done burger when I taste one. Did she think this was my first time eating a hamburger? Wow. When the bill arrived, there were errors on it as well. There is a sign on the table advertising "Whackey Wednesdays" where you get a $2 draft beer for each appetizer purchased. Well, I had three beers and all were priced at $6. We ordered 2 appetizers so I think technically 2 should have been $2. I brought it to her attention, and she stared at the bill for quite a while, then said: "I'm sorry, I've only been here for one week, and I'm training someone new tonight. I'm not sure how to fix this." She then took the bill over to the bar, and spoke to someone sitting at the bar. I assume it was the owner or the manager. When she returned with the bill, she had taken $4 off the bill. The manager and/or owner didn't come over to apologize or even greet us after our problems. We will not be back, and we do not recommend it to anyone.

This place has been open for less then two months and it already has over 85 reviews? Gee wilikers, you'd think this place was the Second Coming of Jeebus or something. Because I don't have a spine myself and always succumb to peer pressure, I came here yesterday. My first thought: this place is tiny. Like "I could fit my car into this place" tiny, that's how tiny it is. You had two tiny tables on the left, and three tiny tables on the right. Against the wall is a really small bench. It was so small I had to keep adjusting myself to prevent myself from falling. Luckily it was mid-afternoon so it wasn't too crowded. Only a few knucklehead NYU students kept coming in and out of the place (I call them knucklehead because even though they were sitting 6 inches from each other they were very loud talkers). I guess I should talk about the food now, yes? I wasn't too hungry so I only ordered two soft grilled chicken tacos. And I have to admit, they were probably the best tacos I've had in this city. Sure, that's not saying much because my standards for a good taco is Burritoville (hush you). Â The chicken was still hot, really fresh and quite tasty. The salsa wasn't too hot, which was good for me. And the hot sauce added just enough hotness to it that it made the taco even tastier than it already was. Bonus points for the fact that they carry Boylan's sodas. Okay, they didn't have ginger ale but their sugar cane cola is just as good. I also like that they are a "Green" establishment, so they recycle everything, even the plastic forks and knives. Good for them and good for our planet! Yes, I have become one of the Dos Toros sheep. Yes, I succumb to peer pressure easily. Yes, I will be back in about 5,4,3...

I've been here 4x now and without a doubt the ramen here is outstanding. Â  Excellent chicken broth and noodles. Â This small ramen joint has a authentic Japanese feel to it. Â The base chicken broth is so rich and delicious. Â The flavors are so deep and complex. Â I'm in heaven when I am here. Â Don't bother with the spicy broth, it interferes with the lovely chicken flavors. Â Haven't tried the miso. Â  Ippudo and Totto Ramen are the best in NYC.

I heard, on good authority from a few good friends, that I absolutely had to eat here on my recent visit to NY. I am so glad I did. Our experience was a meal I will not soon forget. We had a late lunch reservation at 2 on a Monday and the place was packed. I loved the decor, especially the tiled floor with the large B. The tables are close together but it allows for sneaking a peak at what other order and conversing if you're feeling friendly. We started with drinks and apps. We shared the french onion soup, goat cheese tart and the foie gras. Shared soup? Yes we are close like that :) The goat cheese tart was my favorite- so creamy and flavorful, yet light and fluffy. Then the guys both ordered duck confit and I had the steak frites. I was drawn to the pork cheek and polenta but as I looked around the restaurant, almost every table had the steak frites on it! So I knew it had to be good. It was! The steak was cooked perfectly, the fries amazing. I shared with the guys so I could get a few pieces of duck. Fall off the bone tender and the veggies were outstanding. We contemplated dessert but decided to head elsewhere to fulfill our sweet tooth. I did have my eye on a neighboring tables pavlova- it looked divine! We occupied that table for the better part of 2 hours and I never felt rushed. My glass of water stayed full and the plates cleared immediately after being polished off :) I will come back here anytime I visit.

I went here on a Thursday night with the boy. I was surprised to see how busy it was at 7:30 - it seems like since there are so many options in Hell's Kitchen, the restaurant part of restaurants aren't too packed in that neighborhood. We waited about twenty minutes for a table, which wasn't too terrible. The tables are really close together and it's quite loud, so it's not a great spot for a first date unless you know that you'll be going on a less busy night. The food was very good, and it was quite cheap. My tofu pad thai was only $9, and our entire meal, with tax and a 20% tip, came out to about $45 (this included 2 entrees, an appetizer and 2 drinks). Service was fine, not amazing, but they were so busy that I couldn't blame them for not being too attentive (which I'm not a fan of anyways.) I'll be back when it's not so busy. It was actually hard to talk in the restaurant because of the noise. Great prices, great drinks and a cute, albeit noisy, atmosphere.

ABSOLUTE GARBAGE! We ordered delivery tonight from Stix. I honestly do not know where to begin... The "pan seared" calamari was deep fried. The corn on the cob was literally 1/3rd of an ear of corn for 3$. The shishito peppers appetizer consisted of 7 tiny peppers for Â 8$. The 11$ Greek salad was tiny. Their signature dish "the Stix" were disgusting. They were the fattiest, gristle filled chunks of chicken I have ever tasted. One bite was all I could stand. Since we ordered through grub hub, we called them to see what could be done to remedy the situation. Grub hub called the restaurant and were Â told that "we filled the order, it was delivered, so we will not issue any kind of refund" If we had eaten in the restaurant , we would not have eaten it or paid for it, but because we ordered take out, we got screwed... With tip and delivery this meal 92$. The only thing we got that was decent was the shrimp skewer. If I could give them Â ZERO stars If I could.

Really enjoyed this place. It's trendy, cheap, and good. Three things that don't always go together. It looks very stylish and no prices on the menu expensive, but its not. I got an empanada, since that's obviously their specialty. Pages full of their speciality empenadas ranging from $2 to $3 each. Like their name alludes, they certainly had a lot of fun coming up with their different types of empenadas. I ordered the shrimp, crab meat, and scallop filled "Viagra" empenada. It was delicious. I admit, I only really noticed the shrimp, cuz it was on top, but still yummy. My friend tried 3 different ones and dubbed the Cuban (ham, pork, mozzarella, and sofrito sauce) his favorite. I was tempted to try the Hawaiian (pineapple and ham) or the Broccoli and Beef Teriyaki one. Got the dried plantain chips ($2). Sliced down the middle, rather than in circles. Bland at first, and then just kind of addicting and subtly sweet. My friend got a side of white rice ($3) which was a very decent size bowl. Had to add salt to it though.
Freaking good. I'm not a New Yorker but I could move there just for this stuff. 'nuff said about this one b/c I'd just be repeating everyone else's praises!

Tasked with the mission of finding a place to get grub before a Nikki Lane show at Mercury Lounge I scoured the area for places to grab dinner on a Sunday during the time of day most places are still serving brunch. After compiling a list I called Black Tree and was impressed with the whole locally sourced thing as well as them using the whole animal for their dishes. Â I figured I'd found a winner. We got there about 4-ish and it was fairly quiet inside. The place has an industrial rustic vibe to it and the staff had us seated quickly. Our server was friendly and throughout the meal explained everything to us and checked on us regularly so that portion of the visit was great. Once we got in and were handed menus and mulled over drinks and then finally ordered drinks we realized that there was not one dish available from the animal of the week. Not one!!! It was 4pm on a Sunday. Could they really have been sold out already??? Â Had we not ordered drinks I would had left but we were a party of 5 and decided to make the best of it. Â We really should have been told before we sat down. I feel that if your restaurant specializes in something and you can't offer your specialty, you're pretty much disappointing your customers. Â I know I definitely felt let down, I was so looking forward to the rabbit on the menu. We ended up ordering a few apps and 5 sandwiches. Â What made the experience even more disappointing was that everything we ordered was really good and it made me want the items not available even more. Â The ALS we had were the Dipalo Burrata which was amazing its a definite must try. The bread they served was also amazing! We also had the Heirloom Tomatoes with fresh Mozzarella which was good also. The sandwiches we had were a mixture of the Spring Pig and Short Rib. The spring pig was the better of the two and the mix of flavors worked well. The short rib was good too but it fell a little short for me. It almost tasted like brisket and not short rib but it was still good none the less. I liked the place enough to return but if I do I'll be sure to call ahead and find out what they have available. I encourage you to do the same.

I returned to Ippudo since moving back to New York and once again, I was left rather unimpressed. Â We lined up to put our names in at 5pm (when they start taking reservations). Since we were in a large group of 6, we had to wait for everyone to be present before they could sit us down. Â It was about an hour wait before we were seated at a nice booth. The pork belly buns were not as great as I remembered and the ramen, though tasty, was not terrible mind-blowing for its steep price. Â Spending nearly $35 on average ramen felt unnecessary and factoring in the wait time, I definitely would not go back.
Best. Thing. Ever.
Good food. Fair price. Great service!

I did not know anything about this place until last week when a friend took me there for dinner. The food was very good, I do not know anything about Cuban cuisine but I know good food and this was good food. I ordered the paella for the entre and the caviche for appetizer. The portions were just right. I really want to go back and try the oyster shooters and the Sunday brunch. Â I will have to go back I am assuming from all of these reviews.

So i finally came back for the Ramen...twice. I gotta say while i liked the Ramen, Â I did feel that the broth and fatty pork COULD bea little less greasy. Personal preference since I never enjoy greasy food. This could be the authentic version of the Tonkotsu Ramen and perhaps that's why people like this place so much. we all love fatty fat foods. I stil adore em pork buns!

Was visiting a friend in NYC and he convinced me to try the "In-N-Out" of New York. Â Granted he said comparing the two would be like comparing apples and oranges, but at least I have a baseline since I am from Cali. Â I won't focus at all on the comparison, and I'll just review Shake Shack for what it is. Â Verdict? Â I was blown away. Â I had an order of Shack Stack and Fries. I went there for lunch on Monday and ended up at the sandwich station. Their Monday special sandwich is pork arista - thinly-sliced roast pork on a baguette with olive, salt and pepper. It's $11.80 and worth every damn penny. I'm almost glad I don't live or work in this neighborhood because I would drop too much money here. The pork arista is flat-out awesome. Word to the wise: eat half there and save the other half for later in the day. I had a three-hour food coma.
THE BEST! Every single dish of their is filled with flavor it makes your taste buds dance! I wish they opened up one in Chicago!
The cheeseburger really is that great - thick, juicy patty, great flavor, cooked to order. For the price, this is hard to beat. Cozy, intimate atmosphere.

Let me start by saying that i don't usually write reviews but this time i feel like i have to, it was 4 of us and as soon as we steeped in the Hostess was giving us an attitude, why i don't know. I am not sure whether the hostess is the owner or an employee, but for some reason she was upset at us as soon as we walked in, with an attitude and as a result she forced us to seat by the kitchen even though she had 2 or 3 tables available. Pretty much she ruined the experience, we all walked out saying NO WAY going back there. Our check was $300 so its not like we were siting for a couple of drinks. The waitress was actually very nice but the hostess was really weird and impolite.

Had a great experience here. Â Friendly staff offered to not charge us if we didn't like the pizza... darn! we had to pay. Â I had a slice of mushroom pizza. Â The mushrooms were excellent. Â Next time I'm in the area, I'll swing by here.
Truly legendary, the meal melted in my mouth. Try everything because they are all good.
Great Sushi, the freshest Salmon I've tasted this side of BK.

Bocca Lupo is my of my favorite neighborhood restaurants. Â The staff is really nice, the food is great, and the prices are even better. Â  Having been there a million times over the years, I love that the food is consistent. Â For dinner, I would recommend their pasta special and the pizza. Â For brunch, EVERYTHING is good, but the egg dishes are the best. Â It's winter, so the baked eggs is especially appropriate. There are only 2 things to be aware of: the strollers, but if you go for dinner after 8pm or brunch after 1pm, you should be fine! Â And since they do not take reservations, it's not a sure thing for a group.

So with these prices, why don't you accept cards? Now that Square is out, they should definitely get it. It would make things so much more convenient. Anyway, although the pizza was good, it didn't blow my mind. It did a few years ago, so I really don't know what happened. I'd rather go to my $1 pizza slice place and stay full, rather than come here, eat a $5 slice (dividing the pizza by how much we paid) and then getting hungry an hour later. But definitely a must-go for tourists.
Customer service not very good.

There is something special about Char No 7 that attracts the coolest people from all boroughs, spanning all ages. Â We snagged a 9pm reservation day off, were sat in a cozy area in the back (near the bathroom). Our waiter was delightful, bearded and offered us alternatives if we didn't like what we had ordered. Â We started with the arugula salad which was just that. Â Not super inventive, but we ordered it, so it's our fault for not being wowed. Then came the cheese curds. Â This should be the new popable snack. Â I can see it at high end sporting events (uhhh, Kentucky Derby maybe). Â Tangy little cheese balls fried to perfection, dipped in an andouille sauce. Â Really stellar. We also shared the Salmon that came with mushrooms and kale in a lemon vinaigrette. Â It was cooked perfectly, but the portions aren't' huge, so I was still hungry for dessert. Â  We ordered the smores pie, which was really interesting, gingerbread crust, marshmallow top, and served chilled. Hot toddies were in order for the cold night, but I'll be back for their whiskey tastings, definitely glad I went.

Went here again for the second time and was still impressed!! There is always a line to get in before the restaurant opens up at 6pm. Â Make sure if you have a party of 4 or more you arrive at 5-530 to be seated within the hour!! Â My boyfriend and I split a pie with basil and it was AMAZINGGG. Â If this place was near my house I would be there 3 times a week I love it that much. Â The bill came to $30 with one pie and 2 sodas. Â Cannot wait to return!! Â A must-try for NY pizza.
Cassava cake and coffee are fabulous!

Don't be embarrassed if you are wearing a suit, waiting in a never ending line, sitting in a nearby bench that is reserved by the bums, sweating your balls eating out of a to go box...It is all worth it! Oh, be careful with the hot sauce...I will not go into details about what happened to me last time. FYI: The workers' yellow t-shirt logo had apples in them. Â IF you are confused about which cart I am talking about.

CHOW DOWN BRAH. Great place to catch the itis. Corn is banging brah. The sausage, egg, rice and beans, str8 grub brah. Honestly, i only came to this place for one reason like everyone else; the corn cob sprinkled with crack. The crack consists of cheese and spices. I don't recommend anything else unless you are starving and you are not familiar with Hispanic dishes; the sasuage egg rice and beans will be an angelic bliss for that starving fat kid in you.

The menu is small, they have a section for small plates and larger plates. The small plates were $15 each, and the larger ones were around $20 something. I ordered 3 small plates, thinking it would be able to fill 2 people up, but boy was I wrong when the servers brought it to my table. The food was literally the size of my palm. Such small portions. Who are they trying to feed, dawrfs? They should replace the word "small" with bite size. The food tasted good, but I feel like for what I'm paying it could've been better. I also had to get up to walk over to the front to flag my waitress down a couple of times since they sat us all the way in the back in their outside back area. I'm just saying if you're super hungry, and want attentive workers, don't come here. It's a waste of your time and money. BUT if you want something a bit on the pricey side to munch on while drinking, and want to be left alone forever, this could be your spot to go to.

Fascinating format. It's like halfway in between a store and a restaurant. Lots of good Korean food here. I got some chicken that was like General Tso's... but better. Less sweet, more tangy and spicy. Same kind of chicken meat. Home run. There were noodles (weird rice noodles or something like it) with spinach and bits of beef... fantastic. This is great because you can get in and out real fast. We were in a rush, got some prepackaged food. and ate it. And it was cheap!

The food here is fantastic but the staff tempered the experience a bit. The yakitori was delicious! We had the asparagus with bacon, scallops, duck, and steak, all scrumptious! The cold udon with dipping broth and the agedashi tofu were both also fantastic - probably the best agedashi tofu I have ever had! Finishing off the meal with the frozen banana coconut milk and tapioca pudding was the perfect touch. However, if you come here during prime time on the weekends, be prepared to wait about 45 minutes. Unfortunately the waiting space is atrociously designed! There is a long bar area where patrons are dining around the yakitori preparation. Behind the diners' seats is a small pathway and then a meager space for people to sit while they wait for their tables. The area is so small that the waiters coming by every few minutes bump your legs and say excuse me expecting you to recoil into some invisible space between your butt and the wall. As someone with a boot on my leg from a stress fracture, the constant bumping and rearranging was especially unpleasant. (If you have any sort of orthopedic issues, I would not recommend this place. You have to climb up a flight of stairs before the bumping even happens.)

A joke - just not a funny one. Â I took the previous reviewer's challenge and went back. Maybe I would have found a whole new experience as JB said -- except they couldn't seat or serve me. Â Let's back up -- we're talking 8:45 on a TUESDAY night. AND I'm by myself, so knowing they had crowds, figured I'd get a seat at the bar, grab a pint and a plate of fried clams and be on my way. Wrong. The bar only had chilled seafood and raw bar items. Umm, OK, that makes no sense but I didn't argue. Seeing Â a long list, I inquired about a spot for 1, just lil ole me. "I won't be able to get you in tonight, we close at 10." Â "I wont be able to get you in"? What is this, a trendy bottle service club in Soho on a Friday?! It's a fish shack in Red Hook for gawd's sake. Before shuffling off I took a walk to the top level , and saw seating for at least 30 people open, set up and unoccupied. Tempted as I was to alert the hoards on the 'the list' about all these open seats, I just asked a sweet-seeming young waitress, who said you had to put your name in downstairs. WHen I told her they said they couldnt seat me at all tonight, then glanced toward all the empty tables , she replied "I know, I'm as baffled as you are." Well, at least it wasn't just me. Will I try again? Perhaps, since we have to go to Fairway anyway. But it left a foul taste (pun intended). P.S. Sea Witch on 5th ave in the slope to the rescue. Â Fried clams several bucks cheaper than BC's, nice staff and incredibly nice quiet back garden with torch lamps, a pond , landscaping and plenty of seating. I guess I've learned if I ever go looking for my stomach's desire, I won't look any further than my own backyard. Because if it isnt there, then I never really lost it begin with. Sigh...

I've heard about the Meatball Shop a zillion times, and aside from the ridiculously long wait, (I waited 45 minutes at 10 o'clock on a Thursday) everything ended up working out. The sides were great, and my friend can't stop talking about the espresso ice cream cookie sandwiches for dessert. Â The meatballs were of course delicious and the menu was fun to fill out. Unfortunately I felt kind of rushed, the server (who was very disinterested in what was happening around her) seemed kind of pushy and never asked us if we were enjoying anything or needed anything else, she just took things away without asking and dropped the bill before we were done. Still a good experience, but when I go out, I like to have take my time, and it seems like the Meatball Shop is about moving people in and getting them out. Â The food is good but on the whole I'm not totally won over by the place as an experience.
Great coffee and customer service. They use iced coffee cubes!!

Went for brunch with a group and was really impressed with the food and service. The Â Bulalo Has is to die for, the broth and the garlic rice are just divine in and of themselves, but the marrow on the side just takes this over the top! My wife got the chori burger, which was super amazing too. Wish we had room in our bellies to try some other stuff. Service was really great, helpful and knowledgeable The only downside is that the drinks are overpriced. Good but overpriced

Cash only, which is the only downer...so be prepared to bring a wad of cash. Â Love their papaya salad, beef jerky, noodles, pad thai, soft shell crab and veggies!! Â Service was attentive, although they seem to be busy all the time. Â All the times I have been here, they have been packed every time. Â So you come for the food mainly, which is fine by me, just as long as their service remains as it is now.

Adrienne's makes awesome pizza! Â Taste really good. Â Must dine in, don't take out. Â Just a bit pricey, but I'll still come back once in a while. Â  If you are going for lunch on weekdays, better get there by 12 noon sharp to avoid waiting in line. Â One time we got there at 12:10 and it was completely full, and the next time we got there at 11:55 and we got seated promptly, and witnessed the place got filled up in just a few minutes.
WOW, amazing place....great selection of food, only problem is that it gets overcrowded....

Ambience, interior decor, service and the food were absolutely amazing. Simple but delish plates combined with extraordinary fast service. I need to admit i had times that i waited way more for a simple sandwich at lunch. Only advice is find something around to kill your time for an hour or two if you don't have reservations on a fri/sat night.

I LOVE THIS PLACE.......except Â when I walk in and get the 2-hour wait response from the greeter!! Nevertheless, the layout and ambiance are GREAT (especially the merry-go-round of empty beer and liquor bottles) above the tables in the smaller room. Staff is great and the Buffalo wings are to die for.....not my typical buffalo wings I'm used to from a bar, these are prepared a much different way and they taste phenomenal. I tried my son's ribs....wonderful....the MAC n' cheese, greatest and literally my favorite of all time. I really do love this place. I can't say enough about the food....even the blue cheese (if it is) is soooo good. One visit, I simply had a burger and even that was a notch above, including the fries. I can't say enough about Dino BBQ....you just have to come and try it, especially if you like BBQ type food......I'm sure you will find something to fall in love with.

Yesterday I was on vacation in NYC staying at a hotel a few blocks away and wanted to hit a great NYC breakfast spot. Â Penelope's was recommended by the hotel concierge. I arrived and put my name in. I was by myself. Â The host asked me if I wouldn't mind sitting at the bar and I said I would love to. Â The expected wait for a seat at the bar was about 15 minutes. Â Other people in groups were told 45 minutes to an hour wait for a table. Â The restaurant was very busy and after about 40 minutes of waiting outside on a beautiful day, I went inside to check on my seat and the host said it would be a few minutes longer. A few minutes later I was seated. I was thrilled to see that they had crab cake eggs benedict as a special. Â I've never had it before but I love crab cakes and I love eggs benedict so it seemed like the perfect choice for me. When my meal arrived I was immediately disappointed by its appearance. Â Eggs benedict is supposed to be topped with holladaise sauce and the egg yolks are supposed to be soft and runny. Â My egg yolks were hard as rocks and there wasn't a drop of hollandaise sauce to be found. Â I tried the dish anyways, but the taste of dry hard cooked eggs on top of crab cake with no sauce was a complete turn off and it was quite shocking to me that such a dish would be allowed to leave the kitchen of a reputable restaurant. Â I re-read the description of my dish to make sure I didn't misunderstand it and indeed the description said that the dish was prepared with hollandaise sauce. Â I spoke with the manager on duty and explained to her that my dish wasn't prepared properly and the reasons why. Â She was very professional, apologized, and I didn't have to pay for it. Â As an added token, she gave me a cupcake in a cute little to go cup and said that she hoped I would come back again. Â  On my way out I visited the restroom first, and as I stepped through the hall where the kitchen is into the restaurant to make my exit, I noticed another plate of crab cake eggs benedict leaving the kitchen looking exactly as mine did... rock hard dry eggs and no hollandaise sauce...unbelievable! I was disappointed with my experience here. Â My meal was not prepared properly and the fact that I was a party of one and waited so long for a spot at the bar was too much. Â I was a hostess and server in restaurants for several years back in the day and in my experience a party of one is seated quite quickly. Â  However, people don't line up at this place for an hour every Saturday and Sunday morning for nothing so next time I am in NYC I will give it a second chance and maybe order something more safe like bacon and eggs.

Just ok... Came here for brunch. The prixe fix was good - $14.95 for a yummy cocktail and entree and I assume coffee - but we never got ours. Soccer was playing. I hate soccer!!!!! The caparinhas are good though. The eggs benedict were good, fine, the yolk exploded so I was satisfied but some bits of it were cooked through so I wasn't COMPLETELY satisfied.... Kinda like fake-good sex, where it's rough and fun but you don't get off? Kinda like that.

I've had brunch there quite a few times and everyone is always very pleased with their food. I've had a couple small issues with the manager explaining silly rules for large groups. We even left once, but their food and nice covered back garden makes us go again!

This place is really small.. they have probably one long table and everything else is pretty small (2-4 people with a sushi bar). Â  It took me a month in advance to make reservations at this spot. Â Of course I also had a table of 14 people. Â Fair warning.. if you do not love unusual foods, this may not be the spot for you. Â When I say unusual.. I mean pork cheeks, pork feet, hot pot, etc. Â They do have other stuff but let's be honest.. you should probably get the specialty stuff. I didn't get to try a lot of things because I partly didn't feel too hungry. Â The highlights I thought were: ** Tuna Sashimi Salad (quite lovely and big to share) ** Pork Cheeks (Yum.. I loved it) ** Beef Tongue (Yum... mmm) ** Garlic Fried Rice (I thought it tasted pretty good to be honest.. I think my table was afraid of the reprecussions but I just brushed my teeth afterwards) I had a few beers and ended up talking most of the time. Â I know the comments were that the sushi wasn't that good. Â I would have tried the hot pot but it would have been impossible to split. Â The seaweed salad was a bit too tart for me with all the vinegar.. it's also not the traditional one that I am used to. Â I didn't try the fried chicken.. I imagine it was probably good. Â We also got some pork cooked two ways.. their specialty.. it was just okay. Â As I was also dissapointed in their famous dumplings with pork collagen which were also just okay. Very affordable.. came out to $28 per person for all that we tried. Service was a bit slower than I would have liked.. but they were nice and pleasant. Â Didn't clear the plates as quickly as would have been desired. Â Food came out pretty slowly.

The place is tiny which isn't what I was expecting when I read it was a brewery but the pizza is definitely delicious. We went there are reading it's within the top 10 best slices in NYC and I'd have to agree with that. We just got a plain but the cheese and sauce was just perfect and the crust...amazing! I found myself craving some more after the first slice!

Tried to give this place a try last night and I couldn't do it. It stunk so bad I almost puked. The smell of halal and Â rotten garbage bags mixed into my nostrils was not pleasant. Porter potty type smell, yuck. I don't know how people can just stand by the garbage and eat D-: ! Xo

ok shame on me, sure the place is very good but to wait an hour for table and then to sit in a cramped dining room. Â I've had way better breakfast but still this place is good. Â The big winners were the milkshake and the butter/syrup for pancakes. Â the pancakes were good and so was the Hueveros Rancheros but not outstanding. Â The place is really small like 36 seats and those seats are cramped by new York standards, think you have to move the tables to sit down and 6 inches between you and the next table.; I will not return, but I would if their was no wait.

This place was an absolute b****h to find (we were also very jet-lagged) but worth the bickering it caused my husband and I having from being lost. A lady from the restaurant had to come outside to find us and when we saw the place I was embarrassed we couldn't find the place for half an hour walking back and forth on Great Jones Street. We did the tasting menu and my favorite was the uni croquette and the branzini. The staff was very sweet and fun, Â we ended up having sake with everyone before we left. Email the place and hopefully you'll score a reservation! *Fun little fact of the space, it was once Andy Warhol's studio.
Very good pasta!

Alright, the food's pretty tasty- people who dine here are interesting, the alley it's down is cool, you feel cool inside, etc. Â  However, this isn't a "hidden treasure" in any way, everyone on earth goes here at least once - and since i live near it, i am frequently asked by european tourists " Which way is Freeman?" All i want to know is... WHY does the staff look like they're fresh off the Oregon trail??????

The 2011 Spring Class of She Creates Change (SCC) had brunch at B4 to celebrate the Holidays and the New Year. I chose B4 by doing a search on Yelp. I was motivated by the reviews, the ranking and the close proximity to Brooklyn. On Sunday, I got there early to scope out the place. To my pleasant surprise the place was roomy, warm and inviting for a party of 8. The atmosphere was just right to talk, laugh and exchange gifts. When it was time to order - I selected the Sweet Potato Waffle and Fried Chicken - Boy did I hit the jackpot with this dish. By the way, I was the only lady that didn't have anything green on my plate and I have no regrets. The waffle was paired with seasonings that transported me back to Grandma's Sweet Potato Pie during the Holidays. I could taste the cinnamon and perhaps nutmeg dancing around in my mouth. The fried chicken was the right balance of tenderness, moistness and crispiness to create mouth-watering deliciousness. I insisted that everyone at the table try my dish - without hesitation everyone's mouth was treated to an explosion of yummy delight. The service and attention were on point and the prices were pleasing to my purse. The Chef/Owner came out to greet our group to say thank you for choosing B4. Additionally, he invited us to come back for dinner. I will be back soon if not for dinner definitely for brunch.

I had lunch there on a Saturday afternoon, and it was fantastic. I love Greek food, and a friend recommended I try this place because it was the best in Astoria. I have to say I was impressed! There was a long line when we got there, but since there were only two of us we lucked out and got a table right away. The lunch specials were really reasonably-priced, and the portions were MUCH bigger than I expected! Our bill came to a total of $20 and we definitely were stuffed and had lots of leftovers. Next time I think we'll plan on sharing a dish! The atmosphere was definitely relaxed despite it being extremely busy, and the staff was very friendly. Overall it was a very good experience.

The food gets 3 stars for being "good enough" but not really great. The salad was definitely the best part - it was pretty good. I wasn't as impressed with the 20% gratuity which wasn't really well labeled on the bill. I guess my waitress thought she was extra great, because she decided to keep my change and plop herself at the bar to chat with the staff. Hope you enjoyed the 26% tip, because I won't be back.

Been coming here for years and am happy it got recognition on the Food Network, for I do believe it is one of the best finds in Jackson Heights. Now the main problem is the wait to be seated and food orders to go, has doubled. Good for Rincon. Â Bad for the hungry patrons. Â  Either way, this restaurant is worth the trip and wait . . . just don't go there starving! Calling in orders ahead of time is best so the wait is minimal, because even after you're told how long your order will take, you'll still have to wait 10/15 min. Â  Maybe the wait wouldn't be so painful if they started taking Visa and MasterCard. :-) I'll be back soon.
It's so good. That's all. Eat here!

waited for an hour and half for sunday brunch... in the rain...no outside or inside waiting seats. jason and i became homeless bums. Â if we had cardboard we would have made a sign and tried to get money. the sign would say "we may be homeless but we still have a sense of fashion" ** needless to say, no funds were acquired by our attempt to look homeless to get money to pay for the food at clinton street baking company.. we didn't even get anything to pay for our tea/latte that we got at some other brunch place while we were waiting to go eat brunch at clinton street baking company. once inside, we defrosted and were seated in the back booth. i love that there are so many booth seats. i love booth seats. they're the greatest. the service sucks. you;d think if you had to wait so long that once you did actually get seated they would treat you with something more than rushed indifference. Â granted i understand the hostess hating life. she gets people who come in hungry and then has to tell them to wait two hours so by the time they get seated they are really really hungry. not a good equation. but the waitresses? no. be nice. bring my water fast, and get me a straw. now the food was delicious. D-E-L-I-C-I-O-U-S. i can understand why the main chef was on throw down with bobby flay. the biscuits with strawberry jam make me smile like a five year old getting her first barbie. the frittata=yes. the eggs= yes yes. and the pancakes=full throttle foodgasm. if this was a review of food alone it would get a 4.5. but it's not. it;s a holistic review. food. star service. meh price. meh wait time. oh hell no. **i was in a juicy sweatshirt and he was wearing ralph lauren. yeh, we suck at being bums

If chicken and lamb on rice with white sauce and hot sauce was healthy for you. Â I'd eat it for breakfast, lunch, and dinner. Only reason I don't eat this for lunch every day is I work far from it and I am a little scared what that hot sauce does to your stomach. otherwise. Â I don't think any other halaal cart can stand up against this place.
I'm sort of in love with this place. The food is delicious, they have some pre-made rolls in the cooler in case you don't have time to wait, It's cute inside, it's guilt free.. yeah.. I'm a big fan.

I used to come to this restaurant for their tartar bowl, which was amazing and my favorite dish of all time. But they don't have it anymore or anything similar to it, so I haven't been frequenting Soba-ya as often as I used to. When I do come here, I order the Kamo Namban- the broth is good and so is the duck, but it doesn't stand out. The restaurant itself is cute and the servers are diligent. Overall, Soba-ya provides a mediocre restaurant/soba experience- I wouldn't go out of my way just to eat here.
2008: Pros: Â One of the best Pizza place in NY Cons: Â Long wait! Â maybe that's part of the charm though...

Went in last night for dinner - one of my favorite places. You know it's going to be a good meal when everything is made from scratch. The menu isn't very versatile, it's noodle soup, pan fried noodles, and dumplings. But you have the option of 6 or 7 different types of noodles. Got my usual - an order of pan fried homemade pork and vegetable dumplings. Normally it's enough to stave off hunger until the meal comes out. I could easily inhale about a dozen or so of these dumplings. Instead of getting a soup (which is the perfect order for a cold day), I opted for the shredded pork chop and shrimp pan fried noodles. I would definitely recommend it. I can't wait to tell all my friends about this place.

I came here as part of a New York Cares project, so I was eating with a bunch of people I had only met a couple of hours earlier. That meant I couldn't get nearly excited about the food as I usually get when eating. Loud moans and finger licking are sadly cultural taboos. But loud moans and finger licking was going on my head. I'm not really a dumpling expert and I know I should go to Chinatown more often since I live so close, but it's just never the first thought I have when going out. Vanessa's may have changed that. We had a little bit of everything and my favorites were the shrimp dumplings and the veggie dumplings. The only thing I tried and didn't like was a black bean pastry that had a weird balance of textures. Definitely come check this place out if you're nearby.
One word: Â Hellboy.

Giving it four stars based on the awesome patio they have toward the back. I forgot I was in NYC and thought I was on vacation somewhere. Kitchen was closed by the time I got there so I can't give my opinion on that. Nice and tranquil, would like to return. They have a good wine list as well.

This place is pretty much packed all day long especially lunch, late lunch, dinner and late dinner! Every amazing thing you heard about this place is allllllllllllllll true! ! ! I tried... GRILLED CORN MEXICAN STYLE - addictive! Cuban Sandwich - your belly will thank you! Lime Lemonade - sweet and TART! I sat at the window inside the place and people outside could not stop staring at me eat!!! So what to do in this situation??? Look them straight in the eye while taking a big bite out of your food and say - MMMMM! That seemed to stop them from staring... kinda.

Really delicious food in a small restaurant with cute decor. The waitstaff is attentive and helpful. They give you your own pitcher of water but also refill your glass or you. There is a nice variety of dishes. If you ask for something to be spicy it actually is spicy! The food was fresh and prepared fairly quickly. Â For an appetizer, the vegetable dumplings were amazing! Not your usual veggie dumplings as they had ground peanuts in them. The Thai iced tea was delicious and served in a cute little vase.
For dinner - super loud, super crowded, food is okay. 1 Star. For brunch - much more relaxed, food is better. They overcharged us by 15%, but fixed once we inquired. 3 Stars.

Don't expect a light, simple pizza ("Neapolitan"). Â Dom makes a spicy, thick, complex slice. It took me about half of a slice to even begin to make sense of what I was tasting. Understanding this is important because a lot of people travel a long way and wait for a long time for Di Fara pizza, and you should know what you're getting into. That being said, this isn't really my type of pizza. But it IS a hellava(n) IMPRESSIVE pizza. It's like Beethoven (or, Animal Collective)--even if you personally wouldn't want it every night, you can recognize that it takes a lot of talent to create.

It takes forever to get into the place. We had to make reservations a few weeks in advance! Once we finally got in, the food was relatively good and not too expensive. The sangria was also AMAZING. The service was a little on the slow side but if you don't have somewhere to be afterwards it's not a problem.

Fabulous Italian! We ate there last night. It was perfect. Beautiful ambience with al fresco dining. The fresh pasta melts in your mouth. The meatballs were amazingly moist with great flavor. A truly amazing wine list. So affordable for this fabulous dining experience. I couldn't have been happier!

Pretty good spot for brunch. The food is priced reasonably for a nice, cool venue but the drinks are a bit expensive and nothing special. The service, although friendly, was a bit slow and confused. They brought the wrong drink, charged us the wrong amount, and refilled my coffee instead of bringing my friend another one when she ordered one. They also forgot one the entrees but brought my friend a mimosa on the house. It was a nice gesture, but her dish did not come out until the rest of us were all done with ours. We got the donuts to share which were really fresh, but we were not a fan of the dipping sauces. The baked eggs were a hit, the French toast, a bit too buttery. The BLAT and eggs benedict were good.

Always packed and always a wait to get a table, so put your name down and then grab a drink or four at a bar nearby. The food is good, but my review is limited having only had tacos and guac. Guacamole is DELICIOUS (better be for $10), the chips come out warm and are more like freshly fried wonton/pita chips than corn tortilla-- so much better! We ordered 4 types of tacos: fish, steak, cactus, and calamari. They were all really well flavored, each with a different vibe. My favorite was probably the steak for its slice of avocado and well-seasoned meat. Cactus was different, I wouldn't reorder. Our Waiter couldn't remember our order and kept insisting that we ordered pork tacos-- funny situation when she kept coming back to the table to confirm. Otherwise, she was nice and pretty attentive.

Unlimited hot pot!! everything was absolutely delicious, they even have soft shell crabs! and the price is very reasonable. $21.99 per person at this Chinatown location, and $18.99 at the Brooklyn location. Servers were also very hospitable and were willing to make suggestions on the items we should pick. No complaints! only thing is, make sure you try to come a bit earlier. We went at 8pm and the wait was a little over an hour.
Great coffee shop. Tasty blueberry muffin. Cool atmosphere. This place is very small though - only a few tables so might be better to grab something to go.

So with all the hype, I was expecting something special though I was not exactly sure what the Umami burger would taste like, with all the odd ingredients and the secret Umami sauce. Did it meet expectations? Â Yes. Â I had the Umami burger, which was Â incredibly tasty. Was it the best burger I've ever had? Â Hard to say as the tastes were so different from what I what I associate with a burger that the comparison is tough to make. The meat is a little more coarsely ground than average and meat/bun/topping ratio was at the right balance. I am inclined to like these flavors especially (I think). Â I do not have a sweet tooth like most people and instead relish meats, cheeses, mushrooms and anything else that gives off that full savory taste. I'm also down with fried chicken skin and the dried shrimp my mother uses for flavoring too. Â  So this was really a home run for me and every bite rocked. Â If we are calling this a burger than it might just be my favorite burger. Â It lacked the size of a good pub burger, the char of a shake shack burger and the oniony-beefy taste combo you get in a more 'classic' burger but that didn't make it less delicious. The more unusual flavors in the umami burger didn't overpower it all and the bun was very suitably an unobtrusive backdrop. I'm leaving this at 5 stars but only for a probationary period as I am going to go back and to re-evaluate. Â Oh, the cheesy tots were pretty good but I wouldn't do back-flips for them as I might for the burger. Â We had a 20-25 min. wait on a Sunday at 7 PM and the service was good for 2 people.

One of my fave restaurants in the City. I've eaten here a number of times - in the main dining room and also at the bar for happy hour - food is consistently good and excellent service. The hosts/hostesses are always cheery and in good spirits. They don't charge you for ice tea refills - a rarity in NYC restaurants. Their bread basket is delish. Great happy hour specials at the bar during week nights and the crowd is anything but pretentious. A classy and quality italian restaurant - one I take most family and friends visiting from out of town.

the boyfriend and I celebrated our anniversary here, and what an experience! We both had the regular tasting menu. Â Everything was absolutely delicious. Â The roast duck was simply the best we've ever had. Â The service was prompt and friendly, and the atmosphere was romantic and intimate. Â The price tag was hefty, but worth it.

Absolutely delicious pastries and a nice comfortable place. They seem fixated on cleanliness, which is a good thing but can I Â finish my delicious chicken and waffles...please!!! Granted it's a new spot and they are getting Â things together but their menu is disappointingly inconsistent, their shelves are mostly empty and... what no coffee? "The machine was turned off, this is not a coffee shop", Â well there's is something called instant coffee, just add water... This place has an exceptional baker and a throw down cook, once you get over the emptiness and them not having what you came for..... You will love what they have.

After a busy day of playing tourist at Coney Island my parents and I wanted to head out for dinner at a nice Italian establishment in Little Italy. Â Luckily our family friend lives in Lower Manhattan and suggested going to Rubirosa. Â He also called to make a reservation, which was helpful because the restaurant is quaint in a good way. We sat down and ordered a bottle of wine one of the cheapest ones on the menu but was good. Â Afterwards we got a pizza to share for the table. Â The pizza was very good an up-scale version of New York style. Â After our pizza we were ready to order our entrees. Â  I decided upon the potato gnocchi which is one of my go to meals at higher end establishments because it is so good! Â My dad settled for the rigatoni and our friend decided on the black and white tagliatelle. Â The gnocchi was really good, I finished the whole thing. Â The portion was also a decent size. Â  Afterwards we shared two deserts for the table which were good one being the seasonal cobler. I enjoyed the food and atmosphere at Rubirosa the only thing is I wish they would have been playing some Andrea Bochelli or someone similar playing throughout the restaurant.
The best of the best. Â Please come to Las Vegas.

I love the food here, everything I get seems to be delicious. Â It's got a nice mix of Mediterranean, Bistro, and American influences. Â Cute little restaurant tucked away in the Lower East Side, but feels very European.

I've been to this place for nearly 3 years, and yes I see what has been changed and decided not to go to this place anymore. 3 years ago I came here every week, just because I was impressed by their passion and the food art. Yes, they used to have macaron, and you can barely get food repeat on those food set. Then about a year passed, they raised the price, the drink was no longer come with food set anymore, and macaron was disappeared on the menu. The dessert portion was getting smaller, and the food set started repeating several times. This year, they raised the price again, and things either disappeared on the menu or substituted with cheaper choice. I mean, seriously I rather go find somewhere else than spending 30+ in this place, trust me, I'm truly disappointed with this place.
I aways come back Â this place. because, food is good, open late, cheap, neat;) Love it!

This place is gorgeous. While they offer coat check, there's no need for it -- plenty of room for winter coats on chair. I wasn't a huge fan of the baba Ghannouj (it was way too sour for me). Since we got there for a 9:30pm dinner, the waitress helped us secure the LAST ORDER of the duck shawarma -- it was so decadent and delicious. And made me feel special. The grilled octopus was good, but I didn't go crazy for it. The brussel sprouts were a pleasant surprise -- the portion was pretty generous for a tapas-style place, and typically brussel sprouts don't taste that good, but this place had it laced in this magical sauce, walnuts, and grapes that made this veggie taste amazing. Frankly, I'd go back to this place solely for those duck shawarma wraps. And the brussel sprouts.

good food, lot of hype, and definitely a lot of waiting... 3rd time trying to get a table, and finally snagged one with an hour wait. Ordered the following: half a bird, biscuits, cheddar waffles, and mac n cheese. (talk about heavy meal) biscuits were good. bit too dense for my liking - heavier than most biscuits. Chickn Jus was great with a side of sea salt sesame, and thyme leaves. Would've liked that flavor in a more compact way. Mac n cheese - good. but what mac n cheese isn't? But their breadcrumbs were very noticeable unlike many others. Chicken... chicken....you can tell that it had uneven coating. Not too crunch exterior, however, an extremely juicy meat. You get a hint of the sweet tea brine that they're known for, but eh. I could positively say that this is not the best fried chicken you'll find in nyc. Cheddar waffles. VERY fluffy and soft, with a light chew. They could chop up the scallion a bit more tho.. check it off the bucket list and move on.
Man! I'm a sucker for grilled cheese... Paired w a glass of wine and a friendly staff. It's over. I had the 3 cheese and the mini tomato soup for dipping. Unreal. I shall be back.
nailed it.

Hands down the best dining experience I had while visiting the NYC area during the holidays. Â Came here with a group of 8 after a friend suggested we try out the pizza. Â We ended up getting some of the best customer service I've ever received thanks to Danny or Denny (I believe) and the other staff that served us that night. Â He just went above and beyond to make sure we had the best night and I truly thank him for that. We had shrimp appetizers, some kind of fried fish, breaded mussels or clams (I just know they were delicious, ok!) salad, steak, fish, pizza, fries, and the biggest dessert I've ever seen!!! Â I literally wanted to throw up (Hunger Games style, as a member of my group put it) so that I could keep eating more, MORE, MORE! lol....pizza was great, but I truly enjoyed the rest of my meal as well...to the point that I was wondering how they managed to serve me the best broccoli I've ever had in my life (lol). Â I will definitely come back if I am ever in NYC again!!

My favorite wine bar in the city! Delicious and not heinously expensive. The cheese platters are awesome; the green grapes are a nice touch. Ambiance is great, and service is super friendly--especially the French guy!

I'm going to go ahead and give Bea the 4 stars it SHOULD deserve due to the incredible environment, the fun atmosphere, and the incredible food. I say "should" because they have a service issue that is primarily about attitude and lack of attention that is really too bad because the owner and other employees are trying hard and are so friendly. They've made a couple of bad hires, in my opinion, and it needs to get fixed because this a real gem that is badly needed in midtown. I live around the corner and hope to visit many times in the future. We loved our cocktails, and the food was really outstanding. The movies on the brick walls reminded me of San Francisco and LA restaurants but with a Williamsburg industrial touch. Crossing my fingers for a better experience next time ... but off to a good start.

We heard really good reviews about this place so we've wanted to try it for awhile. We went there yesterday around 2.30pm and there was still a 30 minute wait. The guy at the front looking after the wait list is a real character. The staff are all really friendly. I asked the wait list guy for recommendations and he said his favorite was the Totto Miso Ramen but the Spicy Ramen was the most popular so we ordered both. I had the Totto Miso with extra spicy bamboo shoots. My husband had the Spicy with extra pork belly. The Totto Miso broth was very flavorful but a bit salty for my liking but the noodles were good, very chewy which is the way I like it. The bamboo shoots were supposed to be spicy but it wasn't. If you're after something traditional go the Totto Miso. For the carnivores, there's the Niku Ramen which is an extra large bowl of ramen with lots and lots of meat. We didn't have it but the guy sitting next to us did and it looked really good. I think Ippudo is still better but this place rates second.

This review is only for their take-out service and so far, I'm loving their pizza! It's not the typical New York Style pizza. It's the genuine thin-sliced Italian style pizza where you don't feel guilty about eating the whole pie. My default is usually the margherita pizza and Venturo's was absolutely delicious. It was a nice balance of tomato sauce and mozzarella cheese. Oh man, I can already smell it as I'm writing this. Maybe I'll order one tonight.

from the bread basket to the dessert and everything in between we enjoyed ourselves. the space is open and airy with huge windows that allows for lots of light. Â service was friendly and were helpful with ordering although we felt we over ordered based on the waitresses recommendation-that's okay because we enjoyed it all! pastas tasted homemade Â and were by far our favorite choices. menu was seasonal Â using fresh ingredients and presented beautifully. Â We told the host it was a friends birthday and was bummed that the dessert didn't come out with a candle or acknowledgement BUT the confetti cake was such a delicious dessert -tasted completely different then it looked and we were pleasantly surprised !

My BlackboardEats 30% off coupon for Boqueria was expiring, so my bestie and I hightailed it over there on a recent Thursday evening. The Pink Grapefruit Sangria looked intriguing, so we ordered a pitcher. While yummy and refreshing, its alcohol content was disappointingly low. (If it was present at all.) By the time we reached the bottom of the jug, both of us were still 100% intact. What a shame. We split the following five tapas selections: 1) Patatas Bravas (crispy potatoes): Though the description made this starter sound plain, it turned out to be deliciously salty. (Apparently, Russians aren't the only ones who know how to properly season potatoes. (P.S. You should see the wonders they pull off with McDonald's fries. Mmm. Mmm.)) 2) Cazuela de Queso Fundido y Chorizo (Mahon cheese and house-made chorizo fondue): This was the heartiest of the selections. (Upon finishing my portion, I started to suspect that we had made a mistake in ordering three more items.) 3) Bunuelos de Bacalao (salt-cod fritters): I thought this one would hark back to the time I spent in Portugal. But Boqueria pulled the rug out from under me. The outside shell of the balls is deep fried and crunchy while the inside is a lovely puree. 4) Gambas al Ajillo (ruby red shrimp): A nice intermediary dish: My tummy silently thanked God when I saw these tiny morsels on the skillet. 5) Albondigas (lamb meatballs): I wasn't a fan of these. I was initially a little upset that the meal ended on a somewhat low note. Still, I saved the leftovers for the following day. And, to my astonishment, the reheating process (among all the original sauces), gave the meat a hefty upgrade. I had heard that Boqueria is a great place to socialize. No surprise there. The tables stand very close together. There is a counter that fosters a communal spirit among solo diners. I recommend arriving around 6:30p because by 7p, the restaurant was at full capacity.

the atmosphere was similar to cafes in vienna, but it wasnt anything special. i ordered the apfelstrudel, which was amazing, but a little pricey. i also ordered some grunertee, which i liked. the person with me ordered heiss schokolade and marzipan cake, very dissapointing....i cant say if the hot chocolate was similar to that in vienna bc i never had it there, but it was pretty tasteless and expensive. the marzipan cake was kind of dry, but it was ok. Â its not something i would order anyways so i cant really say if it was good or bad really. i liked the place because it reminded me of my time living in austria, i saw that someone ordered some almdudler, that is awesome that they have it! i used to drink it all the time when i was there, i will get it next time i go.
Two words: TASTY and INEXPENSIVE I actually have a lot more positive words, but I will leave it at that!!!

This place sits at a 3.5 for me. After seeing Grimaldi's featured on the Travel Network many times this past year, I KNEW I had to Yelp Bookmark it and try it if ever I got the chance. So, as luck would have it, I was set to go to the Brooklyn Philharmonics Concert @ the BAM on Sunday... and so with my girlfriend (a Brooklyn native), we headed over to Grimaldi's immediately thereafter. It took about an hour to find parking, but luckily, I had my girlfriend wait on line in the meantime, which worked out perfectly because we were pretty much seated as soon as I found parking. We actually ended up having to share a table with another couple (which was kinda awkward) and the food didn't end up coming out for another hour. So, in total, it took about 2 hours. The pizza was pretty good (we ordered a pie with sausage, ham and onions), but I didn't think it was the best I've ever had. It was definitely up there, but a bit hyped up and not completely worthy of a 2-hour wait. Would I go back? Sure, but only if I was with another Grimaldi's newb who insisted on it.

My friend and I came here on a Thursday evening around 5:15. Â There were only 2 other customers so we got to sit wherever we liked. The decor is cozy and inviting, lots of wine bottles up on the shelf. Â There are 2 large windows which make for a great lighting throughout. By the time we left at 7 pm, the place was almost packed. Â Between everyone's conversation, and the background music it was a little hard to hear my friend across from me, but at the same time, the place did feel lively. Â The crowd was mostly middle-aged and diverse. We felt very comfortable. There is one very tiny bathroom which was clean. Now for the food. Wow. Â We were brought a tiny loaf of focaccia bread with oil and rosemary on top. Â It came with a dip I believe was yogurt and cucumber. I hesitated trying it but then wound up wanting to lick the tiny bowl. It was very refreshing. Â We shared a starter of coconut shrimp (5 pieces). Â I have tried this many other places but this was the best I've had. Very crunchy (maybe panko) and flavorful. Â The dip is chipotle mayo. I don't like mayo so I wasn't going to try it...but I did...and it was very good. Like a golden tartar sauce. Â For dinner she had a grilled chicken sandwich which resembled a panini and came with a salad on the side, already dressed (like a light vinaigrette). Â I had the chicken pita which comes with hummus and tahini sauce. I asked for green sauce on the side. Â The pita was delicious! Â The chicken is chopped small so it was easy to eat. Â There was also a brown sauce on the side that was too spicy for me but still flavorful. Â  Our server was very attentive and polite, even as it got more crowded. Â We were not rushed at all. We had a wonderful first time there and I will definitely be back. Â CASH ONLY. 1 block from the F train at East Broadway. 3 blocks down from the J,M,Z at Essex Street. Quiet neighborhood. Â Our whole meal, with a soda and pellegrino came to $38. Â A group would fit nicely here, but during busier times I think it would be hard to fit more than 6 people together, so there could be a wait. Â I think it would be best for older children during the busy times. I'd feel a little nervous here with my toddler because it's hard to get around the tables when it's crowded and I don't think the 2 of us could fit in the bathroom.
Tastiest tourist trap EVER.

Came here on a Tuesday for dinner with some work colleagues. The service was phenomenal. The staff was very accommodating, seating our hungry crew prior to our reservation. Food was excellent, everyone was pleased with what they ordered. I was slightly disappointed in the Brussels sprouts side- I was expecting the whole sprout and a kind of 'melt in your mouth' experience, but the leaves were peeled off and they weren't cooked as long as I am used to. We still ordered two servings for our table, so they were good, just not as I had my heart set on.

I want to cry because I just realized Taim is thousands of miles away from me. Everything about this joint is tiny except the servings. I only had the falafel sandwich (Harissa) which now, in retrospect, i achingly regret because I really should've had one of everything on the menu. After a five minute photo shoot of my puppy-sized sandwich, I ate it so fast I don't even remember what happened. I do remember the Tunisian spices from the falafel, the creamy hummus and tahini sauce making savory love, and the mess I was making on the pavement whilst practically sprinting to union square. Five stars for a great Taim in the city :-)

We loved our time at Trattoria Trecolori. We dined at the restaurant on1/21 with a large group of 13. We found the service to be wonderful, the food was great, and staff was extremely accommodating for such a large group of people. Would highly recommend!!!!!!

These burgers are enormous, juicy, and really tasty. And that's a good enough reason to go here. Another is the pickles they bring out while you're looking through the menu. I think could seriously eat a million of these salty-pint-sized pickles, they're just that good. I wasn't feeling too adventurous when I came here so I ordered a good ol' fashioned American Cheeseburger. It was super juicy and tender. You may need a snake-like dislocate-able jaw to get this burger in your mouth, but you won't need World's Strongest Man like muscles to chew it, it'll melt in your mouth. The fries are also crispy and cooked perfectly. A little ketchup and you're good to go. The one downside I can find is the mini-sized parking lot. If you have a small car like me, it'll be fine. But if you drive a behemoth, good luck parking. Also, if you sit in the front of the building it can get really hot because the grill is in plain sight and pretty much in the dining room. You'll leave full and satisfied. Next time I go I think I'll try one of their spicy burgers, I need more jalapenos in my diet.

A sampling of opinions on Han(Dy) Nasty: "We got a HOT one tonight! Dude, I liked what you did with the starters but the rest of the evening was a little bit pitchy for me." -Randy Jackson "You showed versatility in your menu crossing over Taiwanese and Sichuan dishes and you stayed true to your Philly roots. Your take on Sichuan food is needed in this town" -Paula Abdul "If you are considered the best Sichuan restaurant in town, then we, as NY eaters have failed. The three cup chicken and Kung Pao chicken was about as relevant as my local China Wok's take. The cumin lamb is a soggy, greasy catastrophe. Missing the fragrant toastiness of the spice, it was a bit like ordering a hamburger and only getting the bun." -Simon Cowell "At least a 45 minute wait for a table??? Nothing can be that good!" -The disgruntled New Yorker who does not wait for anything "Well, as for the much touted Dan dan noodles they were habit forming sweet and creamy but I was also hoping for the vinegary backbone of iterations elsewhere. Double cooked pork belly was bland as were my salt and pepper shrimp. I'll just stick to the Ma Po Tofu, String Beans and Beef noodle as my current faves. A perfectly good spot to meet up with friends who haven't heard of Legend, La Vie or those that don't want to ride the 7 out to Flushing." -Slightly wary anonymous. Does not like waiting in line for Chinese. "Please don't hate me Dave H!" -Anonymous who likes Mr. Everywhere.

Deceptively small from the outside Trattoria Dell'Arte is quite a large venue that caters to the pre-Carnegie Hall concert masses. On a recent weekday evening, it was festive bustling mayhem even at 6:15pm. They make great antipasti (we especially liked the cauliflower) and their pizzas are large, cracker thin, and delicious.The prosciutto and arugula version, with shaved parmesan, is sauceless but not remotely lacking in flavor -- the crust tastes as if it's been suffused with garlic. Celebrity sightings of the evening: Richard Belzer and Kenneth Branagh (not together).

after a new renovation, the place feels a lot more comfortable, although tables are still tightly squeezed together. they make THE best scallion pancakes. and possibly the best wine chicken. we also like to get crab pork soup dumplings. they're quick and usually pretty nice.

Some of the rave reviews here are a bit over the top... But, it is def a good place to eat. Â Had the dumplings, which were juicy and rich. Â Onion rings were a little underdone and greasy. Â Burger was spot-on. Â BBQ ribs were good, but seemed as if they were microwaved to get hot. Â Would have been better if stored in a very low warming oven. Â Service was excellent and is what really will have me return. Â BTW: Â what also is great that in Red Hook you can easily park on the street!!

At $88 for dinner, Gramercy Tavern ranks amongst the more affordable of the event restaurants in NYC. Â  Both the tavern room and the dining room are elegant and beautiful, but maintains a casual touch reflecting its location, which is lacking in comparison to GT's stodgier counterparts uptown. Â This balance is reflected again in the service, which is on point to a T, but not overbearing nor judge-y nor catering only to the gray-haired contingent. Service is on point, great recommendations and knowledgeable. Â Food is stellar and bursting with New American freshness. Â Only slight negative would be that its not as creative or fusiony as other places, but GT does what id does with gusto. Really exemplifies the Woohoo! Â As good as it gets! rating.

4 stars for a NYC Mexi joint. 3 stars if Dos Toros were in Cali. 2 stars if it were in The Mission or Baja California. This place is better then Chipotle or Baja Fresh but nothing to write home about. I am happy they are here though within a stone's throw of my office. You can't have enough less then $10 lunch options. There is certainly room for improvement though. How bout a salsa bar? Maybe some cup o beans side? Or a soup? Would a small handful of tortilla chips with our burrito's kill ya? If these guys are from SF, let's see some of the SF love. If tiny trucks in LA can have those options, no reason why this place shouldn't.
Great team, great food with a trademark style you can taste.
Came here on a Monday Night in the Spring for my Anniversary dinner.. Perfect place for a Romantic Date.

Most people look for "genuine" or "authenticity" when dining or traveling. This place is filled with genuine and authentic: The affable man who took my reservation, in an efficient, helpful and gentle way despite his obvious busyness; the ambiance of the restaurant - cozy, unpretentious and tasteful; in the open kitchen, the chef, Nina, an "Italian grandma" from Campania (taking turns every night with other Italian Grandmas), who delivered us big plates of delicious Italian specialties... That's it, you're there, in this little gem of a neighborhood restaurant every big city person is always looking for. But my gratefulness goes largely to our waitress, who embodied kindness. She was busy, but available for us, had a great smile, was very friendly but not overwhelming, made sure we were having a great time through a multitude of actions. And most importantly, no fabricated attitude. You just can tell you're dealing with a good person. For those who are sensitive to these qualities, it makes everything better. The menu is filled with outlandish and colorful dishes, like a stuffed half of a sheep's head, slices of tripe, lamb hearts or lamb testicles, which enhances the exoticism of the place and offers bragging rights for next morning conversations. The other dishes are pure Italian specialties, each very original and appealing, but I'll let the menu speak for itself. Note that there's also a page for "tonight's chef's specialties", so you can be sure that the Italian Grandma knows what she's doing. And, as the name of the restaurant implies, they have a big wine list, with extended descriptions to help us navigate the insane maze that is Italian wine. Obviously every review is subjective, and a good or bad experience may be a fluke, but I have a feeling this is the kind of place that works every time. That I felt compelled to write my first review ever about a restaurant is my way of thanking the staff for offering me and my fiancÃ©e an amazing moment yesterday night. It's just off the Staten Island ferry. Make sure you make a reservation, and come early.

Arguably one of the best margherita slices in the city and their artichoke slice goes without saying. Â There is a reason why they always have a line and why people are always standing outside (even in the middle of winter) eating their slice(s).

This place has a great vibe - cute, cozy decor and friendly servers. I've been there a few times. Overall, the food is tasty, but I do not recommend the veggie burger. It lacked flavor and the ciabatta bun was too tough. I get that some restaurants throw a veggie burger on their menus as an after thought to satisfy vegetarians, but it was only one of 10 or so items on the brunch menu, so I expected it to have packed more of a punch. That said, I would go back and order the pancakes - they looked delectable.

I stopped in after leaving behind the severely overpriced drinks and other madness at M2 Ultra Lounge (seriously, with the Ultra Lounge? C'mon guys...) And I remembered, I love that Cookshop is my neighborhood watering hole. I exchanged a familiar hello with the barkeep, ordered up a Greyhound and let relaxation set in under the dim lights. Should you be searching for me at the end of the night, there's a good chance I'll be at the bar at Cookshop.

fresh, natural food! all the dishes were great 1) steak tacos were tasty. homemade torillas and marinated steak with cabbage. the sauce was great too. we had multiple sauces from the sweet chili to salsa verde to thai basil and all were great and can be paired with any of the dishes. 2) crab cake special was one of the best ones north of maryland! 3) lamb lollies were great. does not have the domestic lamb taste since it's grass fed and natural australian lamb. the spice/herb dry rub was fantastic 4) tile fish and mahi mahi fish dishes were both light and made great. the rice pilaf as a side was light and had a lemon spice which accented the rice 5) the tim tam tiramisu was the best part. never had caramel in a tiramisu and it was fantastic.

i've had dumplings from up and down the West Coast and all over Taiwan and China, of the homemade and frozen varieties. Prosperity Dumpling does not disappoint. Yes, it is literally a hole in the wall and when I went, there were some poorly mannered, obnoxious, and hormonal teenagers lingering outside talking about pubic hair. But their price is unbeatable (it's nearly comparable to the cheapness of the homeland) and you get some awesome dumplings. I only got 10 dumplings, as it was an early evening snack, but it was very difficult to exercise self-restraint after I saw, smelled, and essentially inhaled the dumplings.
