My only complaints are the little pool of grease that accompanied them in my little styrofoam box and that of my 10 dumplings, about 2-3 of them had holes, making them structurally unsound. But that's getting nitpicky about a meal that was literally $2.00. If you like dumplings, GO. You won't be disappointed!
one of my favorite brunch spots. Â the food is outstanding and the price is surprisingly low! it's tiny and quaint and practically perfect in every way.

Great menu if your into game meat. I am a huge fan of game meat and its somewhat hard to find a restaurant that will serve it on a regular basis. Thank you yelp for helping me find this place ! Â  Appetizer - Grilled kangaroo on a coriander falafel: kangaroo was thinly sliced and tasted slightly jerky. -Pan-seared foie gras: All i can say is it was delicious Mains -Ricotta cavatelli with carrot Bolognese, Thai basil and cashew pesto: This was delicious the bolognese had a sweet tomato flavor and you can taste the shredded carrots cooked in it. The portion seemed small to me but halfway through i was actually getting full i almost couldnt finish it but it was SO good i did anyway. Â  -Grilled New Zealand venison loin, Cabrales dumplings, oyster mushrooms and salsa verde: the venison was tender and the salsa verde did not overwhelm the flavor of the meat. Dessert -Sticky toffee pudding with Armagnac ice cream and hot caramel sauce: I was told this was the most requested dessert and i understand why. The flavors blended well together and the caramel was not too sweet. Overall service was great and the menu is creative i have to come back and try brunch one day especially with all the reviews i have read.

This is a bilevel restaurant- the ground floor is vibrantly beautiful & fast paced while the 2nd floor space is a dimmer and warmer-- Â where families and ol' time couples are more commonly seated. Â Yes, i was seated upstairs. Â  We had a crab cake appetizer- about 6 small crab balls and a unique, spicy dipping tartar sauce. Â It was OK. Â For entrees, we tried Iskender Kebab (thin slices of lamb and beef on pita bread,yogurt, tomato sauce). Â The pita bread was crunchy and flavorful like croutons- in a blind taste test, I'd probably think this was a very flavorful pizza with meat topping. Â Not to offend anyone! Â It was DELICIOUS. Â The other main meal we ordered was Tavuk Izgara (grilled chicken breast with rice and a big section of chopped raw veggies such as carrots, onions, and lettuce). Â It was definitely the healthier of the two and pretty good but it's not something specific that will draw me back to Beyoglu. Service was impeccable. Â My water cup never ran dry haha Surprisingly, this restaurant was quite bustling on both floors on a Monday evening! Â Food was good.

One of my favorite spots in the city. It's is literally a hole in the wall. Upstairs seating, cash only. But good god everything here is delicious skirt steak, pork belly... Do your self a serious favor and check this spot out.

This was an incredible dinner. Â You can tell a great deal of love and attention goes into every aspect of your experience. Â I would recommend getting there early as it seems to get VERY crowded the later in the evening it is and the tables are a little tight.

One of the very best dining experiences you can have in the city. Food is a consistently delicious, superbly fresh, creative, and packed with flavor. Service is lovely, and the husband & wife chef/owner team create a delightful vibe. You'd be hard pressed to find such terrific food in a more inviting, less pretentious spot than The Grocery. Food and wine are very reasonably priced. Special, special place.

I came in here for a quick bite, and DANGGGGG this place was busy on a Thursday night. The line to order wasn't huge, but there were several people waiting for their orders to be filled and their tummies to be satisfied. My friend and I weren't super hungry, so we each decided to get an order of shrimp dumplings, which cost 4 dollars/order. Though there were LOTS of people waiting, we didn't wait that long for our food, which was really nice. I wasn't really expecting that much food, but was surprised to see that there were 8 plump shrimp dumplings in my take out box. Score! :) The dumplings were piping hot and DELICIOUS. I didn't have a spoon to enjoy the soup as much as I could have, but the dumplings were juicy and honestly, some of the best dumplings I've ever eaten. Unfortunately, I wasn't very hungry and was only able to eat half of my order. If you are looking for some cheap, filling, DELICIOUS food, come here. Don't be scared by the crowds because you get your food relatively fast and it's freaking worth it, it's that good :)

The food was really good but I had to wait over 45 minutes on Mother's Day of all days when it wasn't even that crowded so if anyone goes here bring a snack because they didn't even bring us snacks until about 5 minutes before the meal finally came out.plus the service just wasn't good at all.

I've been here several times and I can't stop! It's just a couple of blocks from my school and their lunch special of free salad and appetizer with any meal definitely rings right with my college wallet (-; This is the one of the only places I go to for chicken pad thai, always good, flavorful, and great portion sizes too. The place is tiny, not a place to go for large groups (4 people max) but the atmosphere is sunny and the so is that of the two waitresses who work the 6 or so tables. Definitely a keeper!

The best ramen in the city. The broth is very rich in flavor and the noodles are always cooked perfectly. It's great to have on a nice breezy day. I always find myself coming back to Totto when I'm in the mood for ramen. The only negative aspect of Totto is that it's a hole in the whole tiny little place with a long line. Since this is an issue I always go early to sign in and grab some drinks with a friend in the area. Great place. Absolutely worth 5 stars.

I take people here for happy hours all the time. Â It is the unique sort of place that impresses locals and out-of-towners alike and their happy hour prices are decent. Â Another great time to come is during lunch. Â Splurge your calories on their mac and cheese (bonus: get the mama's peppers and kale version) but remember that their salads are also a safe bet. Â Their happy hour cheese plates are light, so plan on a few for your group. Â  Love spending my paycheck on the cheese upstairs while watching them make cheese beyond the glass walls. Â They have nice gift boxes for the holidays as well.

I had to open a yelp account to write this review. We were at Catfish on a Saturday night. The line wasn't too bad and the drink selection seemed quite good. But I arrived super hungry and made a terrible decision to order their roasted chicken. Guys, DO NOT GET THE MEMA'S ROASTED CHICKEN HERE! It came undercooked and tasted very rubbery. I didn't see anyone order this so maybe it wasn't a popular item. They either rushed the oven roasting to bring this over or they precooked and microwaved the meat, resulting in the rubbery texture. When I got to the part near the bones, the meat is almost raw. I had to stop eating immediately. For the rest of the night I couldn't stop thinking about this chicken at Catfish and I felt like throwing up many times. Ew, just ew.

The Aegean in your plate! Mom and grandma must be in the kitchen, because everything was perfect. The bread was fresh and warm, the olive oil infused with oregano and herbs, the lemon potatoes so yummy, the fish so tasty and ideally grilled. Oh yes, and the free baklava at the end was the epitome of being in heaven. As good as it gets!

Came for the price fixe brunch - I thought the deal was good. Service is a bit off - food was OK - I am hoping dinner will be better. Asked for syrup - never got it Asked for whipped cream, came from a can, got it after asking 2 different people 2 times each. Ordered the adult lemonade- got it about halfway through the meal-my date was done with her Mimosa by then. I would reccomend the brunch - its a great deal I am coming back for dinner, hopefully I will see their A-game. PS The Brunch menu shown is not the same one given. Now the deal is $17.50 any breakfast item, a side, and a drink.

David Chang's Momofuku restaurants are all the rage in NY so I had to try the food to see what he is all about. It was easy to walk in and get a table for 3 for a Sunday night. Let's get down to the nitty gritty. The steamed pork buns were fantastic. Tender, fatty, juicy, thick-sliced piece of pork tucked in a soft, fluffy bun. I could have have had a dozen and still would be craving for more. I also had the pork shoulder steak which really underwhelmed me. It didn't have much flavor besides salt and there were some grisly pieces to the steak that were unappetizing. I also got to try one other dish, the sichuan beef tendon that one of my friends had. I was expecting to the tendon to have a texture of rubber bands but surprisingly it was like eating cold al-dente noodles. Something I was glad to try but not sure if I'd order it for myself. I'm glad to say I got to try David Chang's cuisine but unless something remarkable like reservations to Momofuku Ko come my way, I'll venture out to try other places that NY has to offer.

Better for dinner than brunch, Nook serves a charming mish-mash of Euro-food (occasionally French, sometimes Hungarian, maybe Italian or German). Â  For dinner, the much-praised mushroom cigars are standouts, and the goulash is excellent. Â The steak frites is a good fallback choice as well, thanks to the great rosemary fries. The brunch options are all pleasant enough, but even a lazy cook like myself thought I could do many of the better choices at my own house after a trip to Whole Foods. Â I've had the spinach, goat cheese and tomatoes egg scramble, which was...fine, but didn't excite me much, where the dinners at Nook really HAVE. Service is...hard to comment on, since it's basically a one person show -- when we were there last, it was actually the owner who seated/served. Â But, given the challenge of wearing many hats, I've not found the service to be an obstacle -- in fact, it's rather charming. Hyper-tiny, as you've no doubt read, and be sure to BYO.

This place gets packed, but the wait is very well worth it. Service was a bit slow and at times inconsiderate, the reason I say inconsiderate, is because we were seated near the door in the dinning room, and Â the waiters were purposely keeping the door open when asked to close it because it was Â getting very cold. Food is rather good however. The burger that is served on an English muffin with Â fries and curry mayo(out of this world) and ketchup is pretty good, the kale salad is delicious, and so is the chicken sausage appetizer. Â I wasn't too impressed with the dessert as the Apple Crisp was a bit too on the sweet side, but over all everything was yummy.

Small and quaint with a hint of charm. Â Crown Victoria will satisfy your tummy with comfort french food and a dash of Â korean flair. Â  Croque Monsieur Â and Kobe Beef Burger were our choices for lunch. Â Both good, and I love that the burger has add ons such as kimchi and organic fried egg, but I hate that the burger becomes too big to bite into. Â  It's one of those burgers where the meat patty is big and juicy but way too thick when combined with everything else. Â So it ruined my appetite a bit when I had to cut my burger into small pieces in order to have a combination of all flavors in one bite. Â Annoying. But all good.

Forgive Me For I Have Sinned In a state of low energy due to my fast of only consuming green elixirs for ten days... and on day four I CRACKED but found myself in a State-of-Bliss. Ahhhhhh, sliced to perfection: jalapeÃ±o, cilanto, daikon, carrots, cucumbers perfectly seasoned in rice vinegar. And the best part of it is the sandwich: (Not the Baco-bits in No #1) **People the One to Get is the No #6 Buddhist Chay which is so flavorful! Medley of mushrooms, baby corn and vegan strips in a light sauce. As I sat on the bench with crumbs down my jeans bite after bite just thinking "Gotta love the French for colonizing Vietnam." Â Best Sandwich Ever Invented!!!! I thank you Saigon Banh Mi for being there... but I have to say your bread could use some help. Closed on Mondays.

I'll keep it very simple. Â Food was excellent and the service was the best you're ever going to encounter in NYC. Â I eat out with my family at least once a week and the services in most restaurants in NYC just plain suck. Â I get really pissed off because I still have to tip them but the service here was so good that I was so happy to give them a 25% tip.

been eating here since i was kid - although the quality of the soup dumplings has fallen over the years (they used to make them fresh in restaurant but now they are premade and frozen I believe) they are still top notch. I always get the shanghai thick noodle with the soup dumplings and would recommend this restaurant to anyone. A lot of tourists come here so expect to wait to be seated.

Nice little bar with ample parking nearby! This place has good food, drinks and a very nice wait staff. Came here for Clint H's bday and they actually gave us all free birthday shots! They have DJs in the back and a nice layout which gives off a very relaxed vibe. Or maybe it was just Sunday. Either way, it was nice. Drinks are half priced till 9 I believe, so be a quick drinker. Really nice place to have an event, if I was taking public transportation, I would say its a bit out of the way but since I was driving, it was perfect.

After having gotten a $270 ticket for running a red light on my bicycle, (Yes I will attempt to work this factoid in every social media outlet I use because I am bloody miffed about it) I felt quite poor. Poor enough that I didn't think myself worthy of a full entree at Northern Spy even though I still hankered for good food. And I'm so glad that Northern Spy's dinner menu has some snacks on it, which meant I could have both variety and cheapness. Score! I ordered for myself the pork sticky rolls and the chicken liver mousse - both of which were incredibly delicious. The pork sticky rolls are like Cinnabons but more like Porkabons - pulled pork was rolled into the spirals of the fluffy bread. The chicken liver mousse was kind of a party in my mouth. At $6, it's like the poor man's foie gras - I even saved myself a bit so I could have the chicken liver for my final bite. I also split a side of the duck fat fries and got to try a little bit of the lamb entree. The lamb? Perfectly cooked. The duck fat fries were large, chunky wedges - didn't think the duck fat or the dipping sauce tasted particularly special but it wasn't bad. Really conscientiously-made and thoughtful food here - would come back again.

We'd been meaning to try Chuko for some time, but we don't like standing on line and and waiting. Â Early on a Friday evening in August seemed perfect. And perfect Chuko was. First, we had a small bite, the Bun. Sweet, juicy pork lodged in a soft bun with a sweet and slightly spicy mayo? sauce. Delicious! Second, crispy Brussels Sprouts with fish sauce and Bacon. Delicious Again! Third, the ramen. And I've gotta say, maybe the best ramen I've ever had. Miso and pork (again sweet and juicy), with noodles that were toothsome. Again, delicious. Attentive and polite service. Chuko is five stars!

Perfect little french restaurant that's BYOB. Decadent food at very reasonable pricing, We were a group of 10 so we literally ordered everything on the menu and everything was delicious. Super nice service and quaint atmosphere, albeit very small. I would definitely visit again soon!
Ox tail heaven on Fridays. One of the gems of the Times Square area-- and there aren't many.

I sought our Risoterria because it was close to work and had a massively gluten free menu. When I arrived I had no idea what to expect and found it to be a sorta loud dinerish restaurant with a bit of a 50's vibe to it. It's loud, upbeat, and the food is fabulous. They start you out with gluten free breadsticks, which have a nice crunch and chewy texture that makes you think they can't really be gluten free (they aren''t veggie though as they do have milk powder and gelatin in them - but if you're ok with that you'll love them as I did!). They have a wine special (by the bottle) that is reasonable. We were there tonight and the special was $15 a bottle. Quite a deal! We started with a spinach, corn, fresh sauteed shiitaki, asparagus spinach salad with a lemon dressing. It was really quite nice. I think it had a bit of white truffle oil in it. It was tasty, the shiitakis were sauteed perfectly. I might add a bit of salt to it though. My partner had the 3 mushroom risotto and I had the lemon pine nut risotto. His was tasty but I would add in some white truffle oil to bring out the earthiness. Mine was delish. I wish it came with shrimp or scallops to give it a bit of protein..maybe they'll read this and offer it as a suggestion one day? But it was simply delectable. I would easily order either again. The girl sitting next to us ordered the "Wednesday night special" and I quickly made a note to order that next time. We ended our meal with a piece of gluten free tiramisu....which was so huge, so tasty. They made it with chocolate cake rather than the typical lady fingers. I would have like for the cake to be utterly drenched in espresso...my only complaint. We didn't leave a crumb at any rate. Service was friendly, upbeat, and perfectly attentive. It's rather loud in here and people are seated quite close to each other. It's not a place for an intimate dinner by any means. Plan on having fun and getting to know your neighbors! :) I definitely plan on coming back and bringing my friends that have gluten issues as I do.
Great service, reasonable prices for the area. Â The veal martini was delicious, as was the pasta spacial with spicy Italian sausage. Â Ricotta cheesecake was also a pleasant surprise.
Ordered kimchi fries , lemongrass chicken , strawberry lemonade green tea & thai iced tea . They were so good HANDS DOWN! I willl definitely come back again :)

I was meeting an old friend for a long overdue catch up and she suggested we meet at Market Table - a fantastic choice. The restaurant is quaint with a relaxed, rustic feel. And the food is top notch. My friend started with the honeydew & yellow tomato gazpacho. She raved about it, confirming it's as delicious as it is pretty. I had the beet salad for my starter. Gorgeous beets are served with goat's cheese, horseradish crÃ¨me, hazelnuts and dill. I love dill and the herb gave the dish an extra flavor boost that set this salad apart from most beet salads. YUM! For our main dish, we both ordered the Veal Cutlet which I highly recommend. The veal is dredged in flour and fried. It's served with artichokes barigoule (artichokes braised in wine with mushrooms), celery root puree and topped with radishes that add texture to the dish. It was mouth-watering delicious. I had to ask for extra bread to scoop up the broth and puree.

I have always used Yelp to find Â restaurants but never took the time to review any..... until now. Â This place is great. Â I was looking for a romantic restaurant to take my boyfriend to for his birthday and stumbled on this gem. I had an amazing experience here. The ambiance Â of the restaurant is very romantic and intimate. Â You can sit at the back in the garden or in the basement where they have a live jazz band. From Â the moment Â you walk into this place you are greeted with great service. We had a waitress Â that was very attentive and very patient Â in explaining the menu. There are a lot of options and it can be a bit overwhelming for someone who isn't familiar with Italian food but everything I Â had was great, Â my boyfriend loved his food too and he is very picky Â . I have been to a lot of restaurants Â in NYC Â and this is Â one of the best so far. Great service and great food.... Worth every penny.
Good food, good service, Â busy and loud but a nice neighborhood option. Don't come up from midtown just for this - but in the area with friends - as I was - sure.

Place is great - definitely a good spot for some drinks - although I didn't try any of their cocktails. Had the porchetta sandwich. Great value but the portions are just a little bit too tiny. Glad I ordered some fries otherwise it just wouldn't have been enough. Staff was friendly and helpful at all times - can't say anything bad at all.

As a Vietnamese girl who grew up partially in Westminster/Garden Grove (aka Little Saigon), I can honestly say that Banh Mi Saigon has, hands down, THE BEST BANH MI SANDWICH that has ever touched my taste buds! My only concern is that the price is more than I'm used to paying for a banh mi sandwich ($4.25), but it is absolutely worth it! I had the BBQ pork sandwich (Sandwich #1) and it was oh-so heavenly! The bread is crispy at all the right edges and soft on the inside. MUST HAVE.

Wow! Â Just had a delicious meal at Yakitori. Every chicken and beef related item was so tasty, fresh and unique. We ordered the chicken breast skewer, short ribs, flank steak skewers, chicken soup, croquettes, and udon. My single fav was the soup, it really hit the spot but as i said before every item we ordered was fantastic. Dont forget to order sake and some dessert too! You gotta try the black sesame ice cream!!

One thing comes to mind when I think of Song: Bang for your buck. Not only is this restaurant trendy and good in atmosphere, its cheap. I'm a lover of the cheap eats so you must imagine my surprise when I looked at the menu to find a majority of the food was around the price of $6. I went once with my buddies (3) and we left with full stomachs and healthy wallets, our total was around $30 after food, drinks and an appetizer. The price for the food and the portion (which is surfeit) would leave you thinking that your night would end with a bathroom call right? WRONG! Song is simply amazing. -Cheap, good food -Friendly staff (from my experience) -Nice area The only problem I do have with Song is the music, its quite loud and you have to almost shout to hear someone whose across from you. If you can't stand a loud atmosphere, bring earplugs - the food and price is worth it. :) Sidenote: It takes a while for a seat around the evenings/nights, it's best to go early for a quick seat.

To trek from Bay Ridge to Williamsburg via subway to have some arepas is nothing to snark at! Caracas is pretty friggin worth it. I tend to get there no later than 6 (it tends to crowd rather quickly after work) be sure if you get there later to wait at least 30min, least being emphasized. The staff is friendly and the vibe is very chill. The only issue I have is that the music sometimes can be alittle overwhelming for dinner conversation. The margaritas here are wonderful and the sangria is not that bad. The tostones are delicious, especially when you add the house sauce that is on the table. And I believe I have not had one bad experience with any arepa I have eaten. My favorites are the La Surena, Los Muchacos, and La Mulata. And now ...... ode to the house sauce (crack sauce)! This concoction heightens every meal that I have had. Do I dare to place it in my margarita???? Do not be shy to eat it by the spoonful. My arepa partner and I definitely are capable of clearing more than half of the bottle in one sitting since we place it on every bit. Keep doing what you are doing, I'll keep coming back. Besos (covered in crack sauce of course)

With 300+ reviews for Roberta's on here already, there isn't much more for me to say. 1. Â Delicious food. 2. Â Fresh ingredients. 3. Â Interesting recipes. 4. Â Great location. 5. Â Warm friendly ambiance. 6. Â Good service. 7. Â Bud in the can. 8. THE BEST ROASTED CHICKEN AND KALE THAT I'VE EVER HAD. 9. Â SAKE BLOODY MARYS FOR SUNDAY BRUNCH. 10. Â And they have their own garden and radio station out back. Â Your favorite restaurant prolly doesn't have that shit. Â Admit it. And the beverage manager there, Kip, really knows his stuff and runs a good show. Get some.

I know I will receive a lot of flak for this one, but I have to be honest. I recently enjoyed a Thai meal in Manhattan. Shocking, yes, as usually I either roll my eyes or audibly scoff any mention of Thai food outside of the few very good restaurants in Queens that exist. Sure, Pam Real Thai Food is ok, but now it has a little Hell's Kitchen competition. You walk past a cute miniature kitchen preparation area in the front when you go in, but all of our food came from the back, so I am unclear what is done at this station besides the point of sale machine. The restaurant is very well designed, in a modern way, but still remains Thai in feeling, with bad pop music playing on the stereo and many lovely details. I dined here during lunch, so the prices reflect that. Dinner prices (and portions) are more, by $2 or $3 an item. The lunch portions are sufficient though, two entrees and an appetizer filled the two of us fine. The beginning of the meal was not wonderful with the som tum ($3) which unfortunately seemed to be using very unripe papaya. It also just failed to bring the heat like it should and was generally uninteresting. Luckily our entrees made up for this, starting with the wok curry paste with pork ($7), which had string beans, eggplant, bamboo and basil to go with the pork. The dish had three stars next to it on the menu, meaning as spicy as it comes for this restaurant, and it sure did live up to that. The peppers here are not subtle at all, my forehead started beading with sweat immediately. It was then that my opinions started coming around on this place. Also enjoyed was the Ratchaburi crab & pork dry noodle ($7), which had enjoyable meats but really shined with its homemade egg noodles. $2 is a small price to pay for the addition of pork crackling, which gives the noodles a great crunch or can be eaten on their own. The service here is very polite and maybe too attentive, but it all added up to a surprise, and a Thai restaurant that I would not be ashamed to bring people to. Will wonders never cease.

Very good wine. Good dishes for sharing. Energetic and warm environment. It gets a little bit scene-y as the night wears on, but it's tolerable. Quality control-- A few weeks after I ate there, I got an email explaining the restaurant had a hepatitis scare. Thankfully, I wasn't at risk but a little freaked out nonetheless.

I'm going to try my best to confuse people as much as possible by the end of this review... FAVORITE JAPANESE RAMEN SPOT IN NYC 1. I was spoiled. The first couple times I came here, I did not have to wait since I was a tourist at the time and could make the off hours during the weekdays. 2. Best Noodles hands down of all the places I have been to in the USA *disclaimer* I like noodles on the softer side, but not the overcooked/overdone kind - making them perfectly this way is incredibly difficult to do, and I feel like Ippudo has mastered this. 3. Minca has the best Pork - but Ippudo ranks second in my book 4. Totto has the best Broth, but Ippudo ranks second in my book The combination of best noodles, and almost best pork/broth combination makes Ippudo my favorite. Also, out of all the major ramen spots - the best pork buns I've had AND this is big - shrimp buns are AMAZING. just try them. trust me. unless you hate shrimp. then don't. Honestly, of all the hot spots where you have to wait an hour or 2 for good ramen, I mind this place the least, because you can stand at the bar, grab some drinks, eat some shrimp buns, and hopefully talk to the people you are with, which is why we go out to eat in the first place, right? ;)

Located on the quieter side of Forest Hills. Â It is a little out of the way if you don't have a car to drive here. Â But it will be worth the trek!! Â Small restaurant but layout of tables and chairs makes it feel more spacious than it actually is. Â The waiters (sons) of the woman that runs the restaurant were all very friendly. Â  I noticed many patrons know the sons by name or their mother by name. Â Definitely lots of regulars. Â The babaganoush was flavorful. Â The chicken shawarma was served in a burrito wrap instead of pita? Â Not a biggie. Â Meat was grilled to perfection. Â  The dessert made with a very good flaky filo dough stuffed with cheese (mozzarella?) and topped with crushed pistachio and something else was VERY TASTY! Â I think it was called Knafeh? Â I'm not a big fan of cheese but it was just delish! Â Good thing I didn't go with my safety dessert (baklava) whenever I'm eating Greek or other Mediterranean foods.

Great southern feel. I ordered fried chicken with a side of kale (because I am healthy like that). Hands down the best fried chicken I ever had. Orgasmic is the first word that comes to mind. I have been through many places with the "best" fried chicken and Peaches totally blows them out of the water. Plus, the kale was amazing too. Only downfall is the size of the place. If it is full you will have a long wait, but it is worth it. I do not recommend this place for more than four people. No space. One last downfall is the wait. The staff is very friendly and polite but waiting for your food may take longer than you expected on a busy day (which is everyday). But if you have a lot of time to spare, love southern food and enjoy your company this place is great place.

When I talk to my friends about NYC (especially food), they always seem to ask if I'd been to the Â "Chicken and Rice Guy." Â So this guy is like a local celebrity...and for good reason... the food here is great. Â  How great? Â Well.... late at night, there was still a line at least a block long. Â I was scared I'd be waiting forever, but they got serving down to an art form here. Â Everything went by very efficiently and smoothly. Â Portions were pretty decent and were great for a late night snack. Â I had some leftover and let me tell you, it also makes a good breakfast haha. At the end of the day, yeah, it's still street food... but it's really good street food--so much so that no trip to New York should be without a pitstop here.

I used to live a couple blocks away and I could not stop going there just for the corn. It's sooo good. You have to try it!!! The best thing about the restaurant is that there's 2 and they're right next to eachother. If you're with your friends you can eat at the "restaurant", but if it's crowded or you want a quick bite, just go next door! If you can, go on a Sunday morning for their brunch. You won't regret it.

Had an excellent brunch today at Hope Garage! The last time we tried to dine here, the place was a bit packed, so this time we made a reservation on Open Table. However, when we arrived around 12, the place was sparsely populated with maybe 2 other parties. The server was extremely accommodating and let us sit down even though our whole party had not yet arrived (it seems like less and less places allow this). While we waited for our other friends, the waitress made small talk and got us some beverages. Lucky us, we had walked in just as she was putting the finishing touches on a fresh batch of white sangria! Once our other friends arrived, the waitress promptly came over to take our order. Although the restaurant had grown a little bit more crowded by this time, she was extremely attentive of us. I ordered the pork belly blt and Rusty ordered the chicken and waffles. Friends ordered the frittata and the banana foster french toast. The food came out within 10-15 minutes and everything looked and tasted great. Loved the pork belly blt, but next time, I will have to go with the french toast or chicken and waffles, those dishes just looked AMAZING. At the end of our meal, the waitress treated us to shots of the "Hope Lemonade," to congratulate one of our pals. She was so nice, never rushed us (even though we probably wore out our welcome by at least 30 minutes). I also love the artwork in here. The decor has a modern rustic feel. I definitely recommend making a reservation (just in case they get busy). Can't wait to visit Hope Garage again!

Best Boozy brunch ever! This place is really good for big groups//birthday parties. The food is tailored to the size of your group - Â (same price - but you get more food when you have more people in your group) Â  since we had a group of 9- we got 3 pizzas, 3 Â brunch plates and 2 sides. Â We also all opted for the half liter of drinks-- honestly that was actually more than enough drinks for us- you can get like 4 drinks in that half litter- and it's 10 dollars cheaper than paying for the AYCD deal. Â Also if a member in your group can't drink alcohol they can opt for orange juice (which is freshly squeezed- and quite delicious) The food is served family style and they take in account of how many people you have in your group- since we ordered egg Benedict's and french toast- they gave us 9 individual ones, and when we ordered the steak and hash and sausage side - the portions were HUGE. Â Everything was really good- and my favorite was the truffle oil pizza. In the end there was so much food leftover we had to take it home. ** ohoo and huge tip- don't be late- they will dock that time off of your reservation. Â They allow you to sit first if your whole party isn't here- that way you can start drinking Â whilst your tardy friends miss out in the beginning**
5 stars based on the double cheeseburger my husband got. Best burger I have eaten in a VERY LONG time.

So glad to finally have come here! Amazing juices, salads, etc. Great post-gym or healthy lunch spot and very cozy inside. I had a green juice and the turkey burger over salad with caramelized onions. The turkey burger was very well seasoned and delicious over greens. The service is very friendly, patient and warm. I can't wait to come back and try additional menu items.
This place is great. Â The food is good and the service is excellent. Â I will definitely be back.

The Good: Great steak cooked to a true medium, well seasoned with simple flavors The Bad: Drinks were hit or miss (I had one good cocktail and one I had to send back to be remade, which didn't come back with any improvement) The Ugly: It took us an hour to get our entrees, although to be fair our server did apologize for the delay at least three times...still an hour wait for an entree is a little excessive. Outside of that, I didn't find that the food was an actually fusion of flavors so much as pairing Korean and Argentinean foods. Â Case in point, skirt steak with a kimchi dressed salad. Â The steak was Argentinean...the side Korean...not really a marriage of the two. If you want a point by point breakdown and pictures, pop over to the blog. Â I'm giving this place six months.

This place has become my new go to favorite spot in Brooklyn for Italian. I have gone here for lunch and dinner and both times were a great experience. The food is very affordable and the ingredients are simple, fresh, and tasty. The service is also top notch. Atmosphere: Â  Â  Casual layout and homely feel. Some tables can be near each other, but chatter was not too loud. Service: Â  Â  Top notch, even when busy. The wait staff is great at refilling wine/water and also takes plates up fairly quickly. They also give more bread if asked. Food: Â  Â  For dinner I had the salmon over spinach. It was very simple but cooked to perfection and the seasoning was spot on. The spinach was also fresh and sautÃ©ed with some garlic, and after a squeeze of lemon it was great and light. I had the cheesecake for dessert and it honestly tasted more like crem brule... which is great for those that like crem brule, but it definitely did not taste like a traditional cheesecake. Â  Â  For lunch a few days later I had their lunch special that included an appetizer and an entre for $11. For the appetizer I got the famous meatballs. It came with two meatballs in marinara sauce, and I made sure to get some fresh grated parmesan cheese. The meatballs tasted great, had some fresh basil and parsley. The marinara was also light and tasted good with the bread. I had a pasta entre with fresh pesto sauce and grilled chicken. The pesto was great and adhered throughout the perfectly cooked pasta (sorry I do not know what kind of pasta it was, but it was similar to a penne with no hole in it). It was a good amount of food for a lunch special and I was stuffed, but just ate until the bowl was empty anyway. I highly recommend this place to anyone. The portions are good and the prices are actually unbelievable (they charge pizzeria/restaurant type prices but their food taste like a top notch restaurant). Lastly the staff is very friendly and attentive.

Fabulous little place for a petit-dejeuner. Feels like you're in Paris! Best crepes I've had stateside and incredible environment. Would most definitely recommend for the experience alone! Bon apetit!

Would have liked to have actually eaten here. Â After about an hour waiting, they finally start calling names out. Â I did not hear my name. Â I was within 4 feet of a crowded waiting area the entire time. Â Another 10 minutes go by and I look at the name list, and see my name is crossed off. Â I asked about this, and the whispering guy manning the list says "oh,, I will put your name back on the list" Â The BOTTOM of the list! Â So now I am supposed wait another hour, instead of getting the next one available. Â That is not right. Â I left.
Great if you like good food and Belgian beers.

Have been here twice now. Â Very solid place. Â Extremely busy, so I highly suggest making reservations if you're dining with a group. Â Otherwise eating at the bar is fun. Most recently I dined with 4 others and we tried a bunch of stuff. I have to say that the pastas here are pretty spot on. Â They are cooked perfectly! Â The apps and other dishes are well prepared and quite delightful, but definitely try a few pasta dishes. Â As for desserts, the olive oil cake and the crostata were my favs. Â I don't think any of the desserts are so wonderful they are musts, but if you're in the mood for something sweet, it doesn't hurt to try. The service is great. Â Not overbearing but just what you want it to be. Â The ambiance is laid back and not pretentious. Â  If you're looking for hearty italian food, this is not the place for you. Â But if you're looking for some great quality food, but don't want to roll out of the restaurant, this is a great option. Â Definitely on the more pricier side (portion to price ratio), but worth it.

I've been going to Lombardi's for years and it has always been my favorite pizza, but on my most recent visit, the crust on their margarita was slightly thicker than it used to be, which, in my opinion, ruins the pizza. Â Their service was also the worst I've ever encountered there (aside from the bar tender who was incredibly nice). Â The experience left a bad taste in my mouth (literally and figuratively) and I don't think I'll be inclined to go back anytime soon. Pros: Â Their sauce is great and the amount of cheese is perfect. Cons: Â Staff is becoming increasingly rude, Â too many tacky tourists, cash only policy.
Place is awesome, been for both dinner and brunch , food is amazing and you can't beat that it's byob! Can't wait to go back

Kimchi Grill is good and cheap. I tried three burrito fusion dishes there (I believe I tried the chicken, beef, and pork), and they are good but, again, nothing to write home about. If you're on a budget a need a good, cheap lunch, I'd recommend this place.
Delicious, affordable, and comfortable. Exceeded my expectations! Go with the $1 shot of rum.

I've now been to The Smith a number of times for brunch and it never disappoints. If you make a reservation, they usually seat you right away. I usually go in groups of 2-4, so not sure if having a larger group would cause any issues. Ordered the salmon benedict this latest time around. Wasn't blown away, but nothing to complain about either.

Sweet Mother of All That is Holy - This is Great Soup. Bisque, Chowders, Broths, Stew and Jambalaya ....you name it, the Soup Spot makes a delicious version of it for a tasty Midtown lunch. My Co-workers had raved about this place for months. So, finally, I gave it shot. Wow. Just Wow. Every day, a selection of more than fifteen soups - home-made, fresh, unique, filling and delicious.The best part? A large bowl is $5. AND it comes with a bit of bread and a small piece of fruit. (the fruit is a surprise - ya never know what kind you'll get. Apple good, plum bad). As mentioned, the bad part is the line outside. It grows in length proportionately to how cold it is outside. While it moves pretty quickly, that can end up being one long line. Also, no place to eat inside...everything is to go. Still, the bad doesn't take away any from the soup. It is really pretty amazing. The Crab, Salmon and Lobster Bisque is my favorite. The the staff now all wear hats with a particular nice touch; they all read, "Yes! Soup For You!"

Caught the fever for manchego & chorizo in Spain last week and stumbled on Despana this week. The samples are plentiful, the flavors are great. The best part? It's completely reasonable! A half pound of the stinkiest Spanish take on blue cheese is $9.00. Hard to beat that even at the grocery store.

I have lived in Brooklyn for years, and finally decided to give Roberta's a try. I said to myself: "I better go, just in case it's worth the hype." That was a month ago and I have already been back twice more. I also debated going again this past weekend. I love the food and the atmosphere. Visited once for dinner and twice for brunch, and it was consistently excellent every time. The pizza is best shared amongst a group, as the crust will get a little floppy as it cools down. If you're eating a whole pizza by yourself, the last pieces won't live up to the first ones. That said, I've tried 3 different pizzas and enjoyed them all. The fingerling potatoes are fantastic, and the Rye n' Gosling's is my new favorite drink. The servers are all very on top of things and took good care of my date's dietary restrictions (for those that are gluten-free, the pizzas and breads are obviously out but I'd still come frequently just for the salads and non-pizza dishes). The brunch ribs are GF, and may be the most underrated thing about this place, which is saying a lot.. Roberta's is perfect for chowing down with friends, birthdays, brunches with your parents, random 3PM meals, wedding receptions, probably Winter Solstices and Flag Days as well. You won't regret it.

Hands down the best. Nachos, tacos and burritos are tasty. As as staff very friendly. My wife had order the tacos la pastor and they must had been the bits and ends of the pork. They exchange them for something else without the hassle. Worth the trip.

A friend of mine who is a Chef had been wanting to try this place for a while we wet for dinner on a week night. We had reservations but there was a light wait so we grabbed a round of cocktails at the bar. Drinks were good. The ambiance is trendy/casual. Service was good. We started with the Crostini (olive oil poached tuna, rabbit confit & preserved lemon, buffalo ricotta (YUM) & nepitella pesto) and the Lardo, duck liver mousse. For our entrÃ©es we both ended up trying their Gnocchi Verde (fennel Â sausage, mushroom, escarole, white wine)....it was delicious, LOTS of flavor. Â We finished with desert chocolate hazelnut custard & gelato and the white chocolate-almond semifreddo. The meal was really good & we had a lovely evening.

This place proves that size isn't everything. The cafe is smaller than a NYC apartment (ohh yeah) and fits about 20 on a good day. The kitchen is just big enough for one person to move around in..and from the limited amount of space and tools that the cook has to work with, you would be surprised at the quality food they churn out. I have found my new #1 burger place in the country. Having lived on the West Coast, I constantly lust for In-n-Out. Last night, I began my affair with the Bronte burger. Sweet chili sauce, fresh greens and tomatoes, and cheese over a thick succulent juicy medium-rare burger patty, paired with a tasty side salad. I was full from the soup and pumpkin salad (also very good) before I got to my burger, but I still managed to scarf the whole thing down even though I was bursting. I just didn't want the taste to end. Greed can be a painful thing. p/s: CASH ONLY

Likes: Gyros over rice, chicken over rice, lettuce and pita bread included, 3 sauces available: creamy white, bbq and red hot, only 6 bucks, not much of a line later at night thankfully, can sit by the fountain and risk getting your bum wet or walk a few blocks down to rockefeller plaza to enjoy your meal Dislikes: Be careful you don't accidentally go to the wrong halal cart if you want to try the original ones. Â Their umbrella says the original halal cart. Â Plus the line is longer.
this is probably my favorite ramen in nyc so far. wasn't too impressed w/ ippudo or momofuku. and this place is less crowded so that's nice.
Pretty good. Â Small and cozy menu, but a bit far & pricey

Food is fine, but it's pricy for taking a lunch that you might get something even better for dinner at a comparable price range. Â We spend $74 for a lunch Â for two which I believe the food is far off the price. Â I can't tell much different between freshly made soba and precook one, if I do need to spend that amout of money for lunch, I would go something else in the area close by.
Great pizza and cool place better than anything else relatively close to the Garden.
Grimaldis is our go to NYC spot. Â Hope it is not true about it shutting down!

Five stars. Â I was wowed by New York. Â So sue me. Went to see a matinee performance of Jersey Boys at the August Wilson Theater and then an early dinner at Becco. Â It was crowded even for a early dinner. Â Very efficient for a very busy place. Â Great menu. Â But I could just kick myself for not saving room for dessert. Â Nobody at my table wanted desert, so be careful. Â You might want to skip the salad or appetizer. Â Of course, if you do not eat dessert, then just ignore the last comment. Â Sister ordered a mixed seafood and the scallops were perfecto. Â The rest of us ordered the pasta special. Â You get three pastas of the day and all you can eat. It was wonderful. Â This was al dente!!!!! Â You do not ask for it that way. Â It comes that way and it was wonderful. Â If you need your pasta cooked more, you might want to request that. Â There was no lack of service here. Â They even had a guy come around with this table scraper to scrape up all the crumbs from the sloppy eaters. Â There was NOT A SINGLE CRUMB on my section of the table. Â LOL. Â Becco is a very affordable place for the quality of food and the attentive service. Â You do not have to dress up for this place, but you do have to wear clothing. Â I must say though that if you are going to eat there, for God's sakes wear a sport coat with your jeans. Â It makes dining there a bit more special. Â My only gripe with this place was one I could make for many places: Â PLEASE MR RESTAURANT OWNER, HAVE THE GUY WHO CUTS THE WONDERFUL BREAD THAT COMES IN THE BASKET CUT THOROUGHLY THROUGH THE LOAF SO I DO NOT HAVE TO PICK IT UP AND RIP IT APART WITH MY HANDS. Â PLEEEEEEEZE. Â I would eat here again in a heartbeat. Oh, one last thing. Â Skip the Caesar salad. Â Way too much salad Â dressing, OR, tell them you read this review and both my sister and I thought it had too much dressing and that you do not want your salad over-dressinged.

Not your traditional Mexican fair that you expect but if you're game, this is a really good opportunity for something new and delicious. I had the best experience here. Portions are served like tapas, small plates for sharing. The Broccoli Jalapeno Guacamole was AMAZING. The Steak tacos with the bone marrow is very unique, rich and delicious. Spicy Rock Shrimp Gorditas... just the name should have you salivating OMG. Also a dish of scallops and lastly Carne Asada. Everything was absolutely AMAZING. Intimate setting and wait staff very attentive. Will definitely go back. The only con was the area the restaurant is located in.. up and coming but not the Williamsburg I expected to be in but food is worth the trek.
This place serves some nice fries, but you may have to wait quite a long time for them.

EMPANADA MAMA! I've been wanting to come here for a while now. We started calling my grandma 'malasada mama' after we came here (she's from Hawaii). I couldn't wait! Unfortunately we had to wait over an hour for a table. Even though it was a weeknight, I mean come on we came with party of eight so I wasn't surprised for how small the place was. We actually got to sit all together, which was nice. I looked at the menu, I couldn't believe how many kinds of empanadas they had. This mama definitely loves making empanadas. We just ordered a whole bunch: Brasil, Reggaeton, Spicy Chicken, Viagra, and Cuban. And there wasn't bad one in the bunch. But holy crap, they weren't joking with that Spicy Chicken. Shit is DAMN spicy but OH SO DELICIOUS. The watermelon salad was refreshing, the guacamole and plantain chips were yummy, and their salsas were perfect complements to the empanadas. This restaurant is one of kind. I'm sure there are other empanada restaurants in California (probably very few and even fewer as good as this place), but to me this is a New York staple. Definitely coming here again when I return to the Empire State in August!

As a Greek i must say the food is very legit. Â Nice decor and always busy. However...my gf and i only got two legs of octopus...not sure if that's standard but seems skimpy for $18... Also tip must be payed in cash

Ambiance: Pretty casual and comfortable, open, and inviting. Dimly lit and conducive to groups meeting for food and/or drinks. Staff are very friendly and warm - great with recommendations and totally willing to make new drinks if you don't like what they concocted. Drinks: Over the summer, they had a really amazing raspberry drink (I think it was raspberry juice, vodka and lime). Unfortunately, it's seasonal so they don't have it anymore. Now, they have a Pomegranate Gimlet that's sweet and delicious. They have a broad selection of hard alcohol, a pretty good list of wines and a decent list of beers. Food: We ordered the cheese plate and pork chops, both of which were delicious. Chef also sent some complimentary snacks - foamy pumpkin/squash soup and warm buttered buns. All in all, a great and affordable place spot!
The soup was amazing and the pork fried dumplings were delicious!!!!!!!! I will definitely be back. Although the corn soup is an egg drop soup so beware if you don't like the egg.
Delicious ramen. Â Super tiny place and no reservations. Â Cash only

The Farm was greattt!!! Friendly service and very good food! We got here at the perfect time at 5:30pm and were the first ones to be seated. Dinner tonight made my day. The bread and olive oil was amazing. My friend and I had to ask for seconds. My burger and fries were perfect. The meat was juicy and thick. It was good on an english muffin. The fries were nicely seasoned. I do recommend the Butternut Squash Ravioli too. We didn't have room for dessert but I'm glad we decided to try it for dinner. Thanks for a great experience.

Brunch was excellent as expected. Though the Steak and Eggs caught my eyes at first, I cheated on them with some Salmon eggs Benedict ! And I kid you not, zero regrets! The crunchy potato pancake under the amazing poached eggs and smoked salmon (i.e. amazing Mediterranean version of hash browns fried to perfection) was a great compliment to this the salmon and eggs. A must try. As for service, yes it was a long wait. But totally worth it. The wait staff are very nice and courteous too. I would specially recommend this place for a birthday brunch, but make sure you arrive early to put your name down. They don't take reservations for brunches. Loved it! Happy 32 years Cafe Orlin!

Awesome!!! This hidden gem in the East Village is a must visit restaurant. A friend and I were so impressed with this venue that we recently visited twice in one day! if you're there for lunch, try the chicken and egg sandwich (read other reviews of the dish on Yelp--it appears like others have been equally impressed with this sandwich). It was very flavorful and unique!! Also, try any of their fresh made soups--we had the squash soup, which was tasty (it's naturally flavored, so if you like your food a little more seasoned, add a bit of salt). One think you must definitely check out are their desserts--if nothing else, you MUST try the homemade caramels--dark chocolate and sea salt was one of the tastiest things I've ever put in my mouth!!! As for the atmosphere, it is quaint and lovely. The service is top-notch as well. Â It also appears that the place is set up for wifi because there were a couple of people parked with their laptops in a couple of booths near the back of the restaurant.
The best pizza in Brooklyn

Love this place, big fan of middle eastern food. Falafel are great, very tasty shawarma plate, plenty of food for two and the price is unbeatable. Ask your shawarma with extra spicy sauce, you will not regret it.
I love bourbon and whiskey and they do too!
New favortie place. The drinks are great and the food might be better.

I work nearby, so have been several times lately, including watching a World Cup game. Â This cute little bar has many types of craft beer, and I like that they are accessible -- through not having a super long list and through the spot-on descriptions on the paper menu. Service, if not believable, is at least friendly. Â The place is very male heavy, especially starting around 4pm on weekdays, so this is smart place for a single girl to come prowl. Â  Also, there is a happy hour where some of the beers are $5. Â It's usually hard to snag a table on the small patio in the back, but at least you can stand outside if the weather is nice! Â (Since the bar is a little dark.)
Good sports pub and gotta love a name like this. Strong after hour place with a banking and corporate crowd.
Great restaurant! Very noisy but great food. The Ramen we had was delicious.

Stopped by for the second time this summer. First time around me and two friends made the mistake of buying dessert here. Don't waste your money on the dessert menu! However, I remembered how tasty some of the dishes passing by looked and made a mental note to try their food menu. I stopped by yesterday with a few people from work, we were all satisfied and happy with our choices. Also they serve Breakfast till 4, which I think is pretty awesome. Also there are some vegan friendly choices and that's a good thing when you're hanging with a variety of people. Make sure you sit outside on a nice day, very comfortable and relaxed environment. Good food and a great place for chatting it up. I'll be back.

The BF and I came on a Monday evening and it was really chill. We sat on the back patio and it was quite pleasant. Margaritas were tart and tasty and the beer selection is perfect. It's not overwhelming, and it's really well curated. The mac and cheese is INSANE. It was like a vat of high end melted cheese. So delicious. The grilled cheese with pickles and fancy mustard was top notch...and of course those fried pickles....though, I sort of wished there was more pickle to batter ratio. Another nice thing was when the waitress forgot my BF's beer for like 15 min, but then remembered and comped it. I would love to go back, but it sounds like the weekend is crazy so I'm glad I came on a Monday.
Excellent food.

When I saw the words "Bacon Jam" in yelp reviews for this place I promptly put the computer down and slapped myself in the face for not eating here sooner. Â Bacon Jam? Â Are you serious? Â Eff yeah! Indeed they serve a burger that has "bacon jam" on it called the Bash Burger. Â After talking about it for a few hours after I got home, I tweeted the restaurant looking for some insight into what exactly is in "bacon jam" ... but I got no reply. The setting is very comfortable inside with great garden level people watching window perches, a very reasonable noise level, and very friendly staff. Â  The burgers were delicious, albeit mine was slightly overcooked. Â Nobody ever knows what "medium push" means and I realize that's being a little picky for a burger so I can't really complain. Â The bacon jam was as good as advertised and the fries were also excellent. Â I easily cleaned my very healthy sized plate and I wasn't that hungry. Â This was one of those meals that creates nap time. Â The burger was juicy and the bacon jam was nicely played. Â It had enough of a bacon undertone that you could smell bacon as you ate, but the flavor wasn't a super dominating taste. Â  I'm going to steal a line from another yelper and say this will definitely be my burger spot in the neighborhood. Â  I would have given it a 5 if they would have tweeted me back or if my burger wasn't quite so done. Â Next time I'll go with medium and see what happens. Â It might be magical... who knows.

After 2 mediocre experience at Ippudo, i decided to try Minca! I can say for the Ramen, Minca is a lot better! I loved their ramen noodles. They do give you a lot! I couldn't finish my bowl. I ordered the spicy ramen and cold tofu! This place is very small.....only seats about 16-17 people. They definitely need a face-lift.

Just the quintessential East Village brunch spot. It looks modest, but everything it does, it does well. The host is friendly and obliging, and our waitress was obviously a pro. She started by delivering a perfect cappuccino that restored my faith in humanity, or at least in caffeine. It was easy to navigate the menu after that. We decided to go for one sweet dish and one savory, and then share both. The pumpkin pancakes are hands down the finest pancakes I've ever had. Tasting of actual pumpkin, they're topped with a creamy, cinnamon-y sauce. This New England expat did not even consider adding maple syrup. No need. The Tunisian eggs (perfectly poached by someone who knows what they're doing) sit in a mildly spicy, tomato-based sauce. Try to mop it all up with the fluffy pita. Don't be dissuaded by the crowded patio. I'm mystified by its popularity, especially when the interior is so charming, but that's just me. Prices are quite reasonable, and Â portions are generous.
Brunch was reasonably priced and the food was excellent. Quality ingredients and service all around. Â Will be back!

Dinner, Friday night 10pm. Not too busy. Girlfriend and I each had a glass of Malbec and shared three dishes. The wine was really warm, and it was a hot night, so no biggie there. I just prefer it colder. Big glass a plus! NOTE: when it's nice out the windows are open. It is on the corner of quite a busy intersection (Houston and Allen), which makes for some real prime people watching. FOOD: Falafel balls: my girlfriend said she doesn't want to eat again so she will never forget the taste of these. Really one of the best dishes out there - you CAN NOT go wrong with these. Grilled shrimp saganaki: really nicely grilled shrimp in one of the best sauces I've ever had. It was lemony, spicy, and the wonderful halumi made it nice and creamy. It came with two beautiful pieces of grilled bread to dunk. We also got the figs and brussels which were okay - a little sweet for me. SERVICE: Our waitress was so nice and very attentive. The manager/owner came up a couple of times and made sure we were happy and doing well. I would love to come back for brunch and/or happy hour.

Discovered this little eatery purely out of circumstance while doing some touristy gazing on 32nd Street. Â Located across/adjacent to the H-Mart supermarket, almost directly across from Pinkberry, and next door to a few karaoke joints, we would have easily walked right past this delightful find without a second thought had it not been for the stream of (Korean) patrons passing in and out. Â Go with the masses (particularly the natives) and one can't go wrong, right? As others have noted, very affordable, yet tasty selection of hot (served/stored warm in sliding door metal ovens on the right--be careful to grab the actual dish, not the slightly more dressed up "sample" versions appropriately marked with a "sample" sticker) and cold dishes on the left and rear of the eatery. Â In the far right hand corner lies the kitchen, where a variety of soups are cooked (served with steamed rice, sliced kimchi cabbage, and radish). Despite patronizing the place at 4pm, it was thoroughly packed, so it took a bit of maneuvering to secure a table and chairs. Â  Well-lit, humble decor, and quite clean (fellow eaters were courteous with cleaning up their messes). Â All in all, a pleasant eating experience--great for those looking to eavesdrop or practice some Korean dialogoue, either spoken (the mass majority of my fellow patrons were Korean) or written (serving tray liners featured common English expressions with their Korean counterparts) Only thing missing from the experience would have been a "kamsa-hamnida" valediction as we exited! Â I look forward to a return visit

Slipped in here at 10 to five for a late lunch this past Saturday and our party of two had no wait (yay!). The kitchen was closed for their hour break so it's not such a huge surprise but we were delighted to enjoy some incredible frozen mojitos while we waited for the clock to strike five. The atmosphere was great: laid back and homey though it's incredibly tiny so let's just say you gotta be comfortable with someone accidentally eating off your plate (not me, I swear!). Everyone raves about the corn. I didn't order the corn. Just wasn't in the mood and that absolutely enchanting beverage that I was sipping up like a marathon runner downing water after a 5k race...oh my jesus so good...what was I saying again? Oh yeah, anyway a little booze and I felt like getting experimental and veering outside the Yelp reviewed items. The enchilada suiza sounded dope...and it was. Cheesy, hot, simple. I tried the cuban sandwich and it was aight...not as good as my dish IMHO. I'll go back and try the corn since it seems to have quite a cult following but in the meantime I can't urge you enough to give that frozen mojito a ride.
Great ramen! No more comment!

For Â all those complaining that this isnt the Original rays or that they came here for that, I have news for you its Prince street pizza and by far way better than the Rays that was here before it. I grew up in the the neighborhood and have eaten a slice in every pizzaria in the LES and East Village and I have to say this Place Rocks. Their square slice is beyond comparison. Im not going to compair Prince pizza to my other pizza haunts because they are all good in one respect or another, but Princes Pizza is top notch. Forget Rays its not here anymore. Whats here now is one of the Best Pizza joints in NYC bar None...oh and by the way stop Whining about lack of seating its an NYC tradition to grab a slice and go you should all be lucky that there is seating in here at all........

This place is small, but the flavors are big and bold. Â I only tried one sandwich here, but it gave me a reason to come back nearly any time I'm near Union Square. Â I had never had Cambodian food, but it is very similar to flavors from Viet Nam, which shouldn't be surprising as they are next to each other. I would liken these sandwiches to a banh mi, with the carrots, cilantro and the chili mayo. Â The pickled pear was a nice touch and gave it a great flavor. Â I picked the pork belly sandwich. Â It was tender, juicy and you really could taste the Chinese 5 spice. Â  If you are looking for a nice sandwich to take to Union Square and don't want a crappy chain, this is your place.

I had brunch at Almond with a group of 7 people. Â We started with lively conversation because the noise level was perfect for talking. Â We all had either Mimosa's or Bloody Mary's, since it was brunch time. Â After a while of catching up, we ordered. Â Most of us had very yummy eggs benedicts. Â I don't know what the bread type was, but it was better than the traditional English Muffin. Â One of us had a hamburger and he said it was very good. Â If I didn't live on the west coast, I would definitely go there again. Â I truly enjoyed the meal.
Achari paneer is awesome... reminds me of home... need three rolls to fill you up

First off, the portion is HUGE. yes, HUGE. You should come here with at least 3-4 more ppl. The food was good, but again, since their portion is HUGE, need to come in a group, but a bit too loud for a group conversation. A little dilemma...

The overall experience was good and the beers were tasty. Fun crowd, a little dark which is great when you're looking for it on a Friday night out. What was not so fun however was when I was over charged...Although the bartender had apparently refunded it, a week later it had not appeared. When I called with my concerns I was blown off by the day staff multiple times and told to reach out to my bank because it was no longer their problem, and then when I called again, someone took my info and said that it would take a few days to clear up...I am still waiting for the call. I may consider going back, but I will only be paying cash.
It was a really good Thai restaurant, the food is tradition Thai food. I ordered mussels, green curry, crispy pork and rice. Love the food!

A cool evening out can definitely be had at Himalayan Yak. The food is really good and there is such a variety to choose from depending on how adventurous you are feeling. There is a vibe here that makes for good conversation- between the hardware on the table, the menu and the documentary on the salt harvest that is playing on the tv's (with subtitles). I gotta say I was really impressed with the band that played (starts Saturday nights at 9:00). They only did two western covers... The rest of the songs (and they played for over 2 hours) seemed to all be traditional (from where? not sure). I can see bringing out of town or out of neighborhood guests here for an easy night.

SJ took me here for lunch one day, and after perusing the menu, I decided that rather than slaughter the pronunciation of the item I wished to order (poulet grille), I would ask the waiter to kindly say it for me. Me: *points at the menu* "How do you say this?" Waiter: *looks at me like I'm retarded* "Uh... grilled chicken sandwich." Despite being thought of as an idiot, I still thoroughly enjoyed my POO-LEH GREE-EY.

I won't try and beat Kyle's 1st and brilliant review but thanks to Kyle I made a little trek one lunchtime and scored myself a pastrami sandwich. My only complaint is that the bread is a little thin to hold the enormous amount of meat, and when you eat the sandwich it either spreads mustard all over you or the meat falls out. But all is forgiven when you taste the pastrami... Great neighbourhood find.

Can't comment on the food because we didn't stay long enough to eat. If you're okay with community dining then power to you my friend. We aren't, so sitting arm-to-arm with the other patrons was a no- go. We were practically in their plate...and the BF was temporarily Fished-out so the pungent odor from our neighbor's red snapper dish was especially unappealing. And I personally didn't care to hear anymore off Karen & Whitney's loud, long-overdue reunion chatter. We tried to move outside but it was a 45minute wait. Â He would have ordered the $21 Steak and I the $24 lemon crusted fish, but I just wasn't trying to share with Karen...or Whitney for that matter... Call me shellfish.

Prepare to wait for good food. It's a tiny place but they have outdoor seating. This becomes a problem though when it rains. We ordered the butcher platter - burnt ends, smoked pork belly and Filipino sausage. Loved everything! For $27 and it comes with 2 side dishes, coleslaw and corncake, it is a sweet deal!

After using the handiest, dandiest tool for searching and finding the best local hot-spots, Yelp, I landed on Malatesta - a quaint, charming, and cozy little spot in the West Village (I think) area. With no surprising shock that the wait would be a solid hour, we had some drinks to warm us before. Although our table wasn't ready yet when we first arrived, the hostess was more than accommodating and friendly. The not-so-terrible ten minutes of waiting paid off, as we were given the bad-ass, VIPesque table suited for large groups. There was about 10 of us and it couldn't have gone smoother. The thought a large group on a Friday night in NYC for dinner just screams chaotic, but the service was fast and diligent. Wine was served and bruschetta was delish. I couldn't pass up the gnocchi, which usually isn't my style. Though rich and decadent, I enjoyed every bite that I could physically finish without feeling like a big beluga whale. Their menu denotes a very basic, but solid Italian feel. Nothing too fancy or over-ambitious - just your basic pastas. But from the table chatter, everyone loved their pasta dish. All in all, this restaurant catered to a somewhat difficult, last minute request and was responsible for creating a wonderful, lovely evening for me and my friends. When back in the NY, I will certainly revisit Malatesta!

Wow!!! A tiny place on lower east side that serves amazing food. Four of us did their tasting menu, which meant we got just about everything on their menu. Â The Burmese Eggplant Salad, Pork Belly Adobo, and Green Rice Crusted Dorade were our favorites. Â Next time we're in NY, we are definitely going to do their suckling pig dinner.

Wow, I think I'm still full. Â I'll be honest, I know nothing about Polish food, I've never eaten at a Polish restaurant, and I couldn't pronounce most things on the menu. Â I ordered the sampler plate because I'm not as adventurous as I used to be, but everything as delicious. Â As other Yelpers have said, the stuffed cabbage is delish, as is the white borscht and pierogis. Â My meal was under $10 and I couldn't even finish. I came on a weekday afternoon after lunch, so I didn't have a problem with service, although I could see how it could be troublesome if it's busy. Â The restaurant itself seems really low-key and simple, but the best places are, right? Â I want to try other Polish places now, but I hope to come back to Lomzynianka soon!

Absolute instant five star. Â  So tasty, so cheap, so fast. Â That rare combo would certainly be enough for a five star in manhattan, this is just a great place to grab lunch or a quick dinner. Â  Cool right? Â yeah its cool, but the real reason Woorijip is on my short list of "I HAVE to show you this place when you come to NYC" locations is because this place doubles as the best pregaming spot ever AND is open late enough to serve as drunk food. Â  Seriously, if you are ever anywhere near K town at any time of day for any reason stop at Woorijip, grab some bibimbap, gim bap, or any of the other hundred different delicious options, and LIVE THE DREAM
I LOVE ARTICHOKE. The late hours will make any New Yorker happy. The huge slices given for the price is better than any meal.

The food was fun and delicious. The waitstaff was very congenial, helpful and friendly. We first ordered the appetizer platter and wanted to wait until we had eaten that to see if we wanted more food. They were totally good with that. Also, we had no reservation but they were able to seat us right away. Â I would totally recommend Â this restaurant. The only drawback Was the noise.

This place was a wonderful find. Being Christmas Eve, they had a lovely Prix Fixe menu: two apps, and entree and dessert. I think we could have walked away totally satisfied after the appetizers - they were so delicious, I was sorry to have to leave a lot on the plate to leave room for the entrees. Let me say this: I've never had semolina gnocchi before. If I ever go anywhere else, and it's on the menu, I will NOT order it, as there is no way it can live up to the deliciousness that was provided on my plate at ilili. As for desserts, I was so excited for the knafe, and it totally delivered. It was huge, and after all the other food, I was really sad that we couldn't finish it. Yes, I had trouble standing up from this meal. Yes, I'll probably do it again.

it's good, but i'm not sure if it's actually worth the wait. we got the goat cheese omelet and the french toast. the omelet was pretty good, with fresh cheese, and a tiny pile of greens on the side, along with 2 pieces of ordinary multigrain bread that seemed like it was from a supermarket. the french toast was very light and airy, but the bananas on top were just ordinary, and the nuts weren't caramelized. the maple butter dipping sauce was too liquid; i would've liked something more syrupy. it was difficult to get water refilled. in fact i ended up drinking my friend's. we got some muffins and a biscuit to go. the muffins have no muffin tops. the carrot one was decent but the spinach/cheese one shouldn't have qualified as a muffin; it was more like a biscuit. the biscuit was pretty good.
Good Vietnamese sandwiches

I don't understand how this place is still in business, everytime I walk pass this place it's always empty. As for my review when I went here with my GF I was here for Sunday brunch. The scrabbled eggs and tacos were very good, the toast was buttered and warm and gooey. The tuna melt was a bit pricy but passable. The lamb soup was a little stringy but hot and spicy. Overall I enjoyed by experience and it was definately worth it. With that being said it's beyond me why this place gets no business gets no business. Maybe it is the location, it sits right in the middle of a low density street and surrounded by housing projects where this type of food would be beyond most people's price range. If this spot had been on Canal or Soho it would be selling out.

I'm sure I've reviewed them before, but I needed to come back for more! Holy chicken! Their chicken soup blows my mind! Â And who orders chicken soup anyway? You guys.... it is SO special and good and different- yet familiar! Dar: never leave me, I need you, I love you. And your chicken kabob plater. And your prices. xoxo

This is a diamond in a sea of Quartz !!! I came to Â Confessional last week and was blown away with the intimate atmosphere, the food, the drinks, and most importantly, the service. The place was relatively busy, but we only waited a few minutes for a table and the manager was unbelievably sweet and accommodating . The food was fantastic...a great blend of Latino and Americano that really turned on the palate !! Try the lamb chops, the shrimp chicharron, the sliders, and every mixed drink you can handle.....this place is is fantastic!!! I'll be back often, and I totally recommend it to everyone!!!

I have been here numerous times (dinner, weekend brunch, quick swig of Bourbon late at night) and this place always delivers. The food here is amazing and a bit underrated. If you are a fan of Southern Food, you will not be disappointed by the beautifully executed menu. Also, if you like drinking the brown stuff, like me, it's always fun to take your time reading their whiskey menu in search of something new. The bourbon bloody mary is also amazing!

This restaurant was much bigger than I expected! It had great openness and large windows. My friend and I sat towards the left area in the back. Â As soon as we were seated we could not decide on a good choice so we asked the waiter and he asked if we wanted meat "YES" so he suggested the chicken and mushroom and the sausage with onions. Done and done! What a gigantic portion! I think we were both stuffed and even had leftovers. Â For $25 include a glass of perseco each, I will certainly be back.

The guy behind the counter didn't crack a smile, when I asked a ridiculous question about fried fries. He was like no -- we only fry are fries no baked fries here. The guy was all business. Taking my order not missing a beat. He started working away freshly pressing the dough for my wrap on a press then onto be cooked. Nary a feet away the other cook worked away at grilling the meats, cashews, and egg. Every component was made from scratch even the sauces. It was an assembly line of efficiency. Soon all that fresh goodness was soon tucked into the tortilla wrap. Counter guy soon became cashier taking my money. Oh my when I got a first bite into that sandwich...was I impressed. The uniqueness of the ingredients seemed to marry so well. Definitely one of the best sandwich / wraps that I have had in some time.
Average. The small plates are very good, but I was often disappointed by the wines (really expensive for what they are). The garden is maybe the most attractive feature of Gottino.

I've been here during lunch and dinner. The food is mediocre. The only thing I really enjoy is their chicken masaman curry. The calamari is over breaded. I would avoid any dishes with beef here, since they really do not use good quality beef. Service is always bad. Even with asian restaurant standards. They also need some sprucing up with their decor. Most of the couches are ripped. I'd prefer not to sit on a taped up chair when I go to a restaurant. People seem to like this place because the portions are large and it is one of the cheapest restaurants in Park Slope. However, I prefer quality so I would rather head to Carroll Gardens where Thai food is plentiful and delicious.

I dig this place even as the wait staff range from supremely conscientious and sharp-witted (good things) to insolent, mopey and sluggish (humorously bad things). The food also ranges from delicious Â and comforting to absurdly bland and leaden. Â But they let you stay and nuzzle your drinks, they have great signage hangings, they have that chicken paprika which melts in your mouth and is evocative of the womb, they give good ipod shuffle, they serve brunch during the week, they resent blase parents who permit their children to freak out in the aisles, they thank you when you tip 30 percent, Â they sometimes host River Alexander's Mad Jazz Hatters, a sublimely engaging and talented 20's Jazz band. I like boozing outside in spring while chewing through schnitzel.
Excellent bartenders! Very knowledgeable, these guys love their craft and it shows. Great vibe, great music, great desserts too.
Really cool vibe, super trendy, and good food at decent prices (in NYC, anyway.) From what I've seen there's always a line out the door-and their ice cream sandwiches alone were worth the wait :)

Service: Â 5 stars - the waiter was friendly, knowledgable about the menu and swift with service. Â He really made the dining experience for me. Decor: Â 3 stars - the restuarant is east village quaint. i like the bar in the middle. Food: 3 - we liked the food, we just didn't love the food. Â the only filipino food experience i have ever had was lumpia so i can't compare it from an authenticity standpoint. everything we had tasted good, it just wasn't anything overwhelmingly different or special. Value: Drinks are typical NYC expensive ($12) and food is the same ($16-25 for entrees). Bottomline: Given the # of restaurants in NYC I will only plot a return visit to those restaurants I rate 5/5. Â This one doesn't make the cut.
A gem of a place. Great if you order out and great if you eat in. The burgers are delish.
