Katz is better. good substitute pickle spears are too small club roll is real a small hero bread ice tea is huge. cannot use a straw corned beef was good pastrami is very good mustard is guldens

My absolutely favorite Seamless Web location! Miso-Glazed Salmon and 20-minute delivery times. Awesome chicken wings. Dumpling Soup is filling on its own if you want something light, warm and delicious! Next stop, seamlessweb...
The steak frite here is good. But the fish my table ordered was not. Feel like there are other better restaurants in Tribeca than this.

We came for new year eve's 4 course prix fixe menu for $75. It was just meh. Quite a disappointment given that I was looking forward to this highly rated restaurant. The decor was very modern and reminded me more of like a semi-bar-ish-diner. The prix-fixe menu said 4 courses, but it really should have said 3, because it's appetizer, entree and dessert. They added amuse bouche as a separate course, which I don't think is usually counted at nice restaurants. (Originally they gave us the 5 course prix fixe menu for $95, which was the same as the 4 course except for an extra "cheese course" and a glass of champagne). Appetizers: tuna tartare and lobster bisque. Both were fine but not that great. Entree: filet mignon and duck. The duck was better than filet mignon. We asked both to be medium rare but the duck came out at least medium, but still tasted pretty good. Both plates were drenched in sauce. Dessert: pavlova and banana creme brÃ»lÃ©e. The pavlova was basically a giant meringue surrounded by berry sauce. It was actually quite good. The banana creme brÃ»lÃ©e was a let down though. The sugar was overly hard and not brittle and the creme underneath was not the right texture for me. Service was very nice and friendly. But overall, just meh. Maybe they do better on a non-NYE night given they have such high ratings. But I am not dying to return atm.

The ramen did not disappoint again... always good. We got the miso ramen, vegetarian ramen, and their special ramen. I was nervous the vegetarian broth would be only so-so, but it was surprisingly good. They were accommodating in switching some of the contents in each bowl. Just wish they had to go containers for leftovers, and took reservations....

Best breakfast in NYC! Â No kidding, it's true. Â Unfortunately they shut down breakfast a little while ago and restarted with a limited menu but still: Â BEST ! Â Best bacon in the city (which might mean in the world!). Stellar greens ( and I usually hate salad with my eggs!). Superb coffee, perfect toast. Â Ice water without ice! And refilled without asking. Â Seriously, would never have guessed from the outside, hidden treasure Can't speak to lunch or dinner, but guaranteed the food is that rare combo of fresh healthy AND delicious ( and I'm a fried chicken type)

DO NOT ORDER DELIVERY. Â After being told the food would take 20-30 minutes, over one hour later we are STILL waiting. Â When I called, they had no answers nor any way of checking on the delivery guy. Â rather than being apologetic, they seemed annoyed I was calling. Â Horrible customer service. Â Will let you know if I ever get my food but doubt it. Â Don't order delivery unless you are prepared to wait an hour.
Love this place! Best Italian delivery in the east village. Try the veal or chicken parm and the pasta bolognese. Â Delicious!

As a newcomer to NYC who has heard so much hype about Grimaldi's, I had to try it! Not knowing what to expect at all, I definitely was impressed with the place. My only gripe is the 30 minute wait that we had on a Friday afternoon at 2PM, but it's definitely expected since everyone and their mother comes here. We ordered a regular small pizza with onion, mushroom, and italian sausage. Definitely delicious and fresh, since you can see them make the pizza and take it from the nice little coal-fired, brick oven. When they brought it out to us, it was piping hot (steam was coming from the top). The only issue we had was that by the last two slices, the cheese cooled to the point where it "stuck" the two pieces together and we had to "pull it apart". Oh well, that's inevitable! Only gripe about this place would be the wait and the fact they don't take credit cards! :( "Cash only"

Perfect place to grab stuff to take back to work or home, everything I've tried is pretty good, the hot bar was good the one time I tried it. It has a variety of options. I usually drop by for kimchi fried rice and kimbap which have been excellent every time. It has a pretty homey feel to it. Also the staff are very friendly and the prices are awesome!

I convinced a friend Cafeteria was my choice for his offer to buy me a birthday lunch. As usual it was crowded and as he tinkered with the meter I popped my head in to put our names down. I offered we'd be in the car standing by in front because it was quite crowded. I was reassured we were up in less than ten minutes. As my friend and I waited by the bar I thought I heard our name, though it was crowded and quite busy, I wasn't sure. I was snapped at by a staff member who would eventually be our waiter. Move to the bar please you can't stand here. Excited for my birthday lunch I replied we actually thought we heard our names. He huffed, 'what's your name?!' and sure enough someone appeared behind us to escort us to the table. We snuggled in with neighbors who seemed to be enjoying food that looked appealing. The staff member who snapped at us moments earlier, as it turns out, was our waiter. We were greeted with a 'glad we're passed that' smile. We put in our order and awaited our lunch while we sipped wine. The kale salad looked appetizing someone nearby got so we requested our waiter in hopes to add the salad to the order. Â The manager showed up to the table and, with a snarky attitude asked what we needed. Â I turned and offered my hand, hoping to break any ice or tension. Â Hi, I'm K. Â He looked at me as if I were filthy and shrugged with a handful of menus. What can I get you. The undeserved glare could have cut through glass. Â I can't remember the last time someone in a professional establishment didn't want to shake hands with their patrons. This was hurtful and broke the festive birthday mood. Restaurant patrons to our right, seated after us, were finishing their meal when we realized we were still waiting on our food; we'd never been given our order and they were finishing their meal. The snarky retort when we were standing in an area the staff member preferred we didn't, the manager looking with a contorted, disgusted expression when I genuinely extended my hand to shake his (people actually do that) and now we were just skipped or forgotten about. When I addressed this at the front kiosk the ill willed, reactive manager came over with an aggressive energy. What's the problem here?! We hadn't gotten our food and our neighbors who came after us were getting their bill. What did you order, he cut us off demanding. He was just plain disrespectful. My colleague suggested he go to his staff and ask (rather than treating us that way). The manager was so nasty that I told him we are actually not staying and it was outrageous to be treated that way. He then snapped, 'fine, just pay for your wine and find your way out.' When he didn't seek a solution to our query he aggressively scooped our wine. 'Fine, get out then'. By that point I asked for his name and he refused to get it. He was steaming by then, confrontational, unprofessional, rude, lude and acidic. I didn't want to address him. The new manager, a Russian fellow, was professional and tried his best to offer us information to follow up about our complaint, which the 'manager' who was so good at being rude and reactive failed to supply in a professional manner. He actually shoved a card at me and threatened just call, I'll be here. I need your name, I insisted. He refused, they'll know who I am was his come back. His grand finale was yelling in front of his customers: Will someone get these f*cking people out of MY RESTAURANT??!!??!! I should mention our neighbors next to us were sympathetic. We had had a good conversation about which mac&cheese to order and they tipped us off about the kale salad. We left hungry. The sister establishment, Delicatessen, also refused to give the name of the manager at Cafeteria and felt squeamish, even though we patronized the sister restaurant. I know people who have started their own businesses who train their staff to manage stress. Clearly, this manager didn't have the common sense or self discipline to not let his temper erupt for reasons unknown. Birthday assault. Cafeteria, this is just not ok.
mmmm pizza... so delicious yummy pizza =)

The meal started out flat-out amazing -- we LOVED their crispy wild boar belly and spicy duck meatballs (well worthy of being their signature dish!) Delicious, complex flavors. It was also nice of them to serve the boar belly already halved on two separate plates, so we wouldn't have to fight over it. However their entrees disappointed. Maybe we had too high expectations after being served such amazing appetizers? We ordered the chicken and the triggerfish and were not happy with either. Should've gone with their lamb tasting (sounded amazing) or duck breast like we usually would have, but we'd eaten so much French food lately that we were a little sick of lamb and duck. Anyway the chicken was WAY too salty and the triggerfish was "interesting" but not in a good way. The triggerfish was also advertised as served with "heirloom tomatoes" and was served with cherry tomatoes instead, which I imagine could have been heirloom but not what you usually think of when you read "heirloom tomatoes"! I also should have known better than to order that when the waitress described it as a "very mild fish" as I love fishy fish. Anyway they redeemed themselves with desserts, both chocolate souffle (dessert special and ordered in advance) and sticky toffee pudding were excellent. It's SO hard to find a real souffle, even at a high-end restaurant, these days and this definitely was a real souffle. I would've given them four stars had entrees lived up to their potential, but maybe next time? The waitress was very nice and price was while not cheap not unreasonable for the quality of ingredients and creativity of the cuisine. Not exactly rushing to go back, but may try it in the future if I find myself in the neighborhood.

I've heard only great things about Joya, so my friends & I decided to try it out. It was everthing that we were told it was, plus more. The food was out of this world. My friends & I all ordered a different bunch of things. I had the spring rolls, the tiger shrimp rolls and the Kang Masaman - ok so I went a little overboard but I couldn't help it. My highlight was definitely the curry - Oh my God!! I'm gonna say that it was probably one of the greatest curries that I have ever ordered and eaten out of a Thai restaurant. Joya has such a great vibe to it. Servers are overly happy and friendly. Prices are awesome - crazy cheap. Wish I had tried this place sooner...Might just head back there with the girl tomorrow for dinner.

Blowfish to Die For Yasuda and Sushi Seki go back and forth as my favorite sushi joints in NYC. Â Until last night, it had been a while since I came and I was fortunate enough to sit at the sushi bar in front of Chef Yasuda, who works M-F lunch and dinner. Â We had the flash fried blowfish as an appetizer - basically tasted like any white flaky fish, but good nevertheless, in a ponzu sauce with spicy radish/onion. Â Then, we ordered the sushi/sashimi combo - reasonably priced at $24. Â The great thing about this here is you can choose what kind of pieces you want, where all other places choose the fish for you if you get the "deluxe". Â Chef Yasuda was so friendly and humble....I almost didn't believe it was him. Â The pieces are smaller here than Seki, but again, you get your choice here, and they have so many more exotic options/daily specials here. Â Plus, Chef Yasuda rocks - he competed in Mr. Tokyo (body building contest).

Impressive selection although not my favorite IPAs' when I went last night. Still very good, fresh IPAs just not MY favs. Impressed by varietals and categoric abundance. Happy Hour deals although I don't think anyone is a fan of wheat bears anymore. Good bartenders redhead, blonde, happy, pleasant overall which is important. Friendly crowd of upbeat after works. Definitely be back. Best: 1 stop from Grand Central off the 6!
One of the best burgers I have ever had in my life.
Though its one of the famous chicken over rice places in New York, I feel over the years, the food quality has decreased though the price still remains the same.

Balls, balls, balls. MMMMMMMMM. I ordered the classic beef with the spicy meat sauce and it was amazzzzzzing.. then I ordered the spicy pork balls with the spicy meat sauce and it was heavenly! The balls are so moist!

food was good, but the portions here are absolutely tiny. Â if i had known, i would have ordered way more. Â i tried the gravy meatball sliders, and they were pretty tasty but they were just 3 meatballs and some bread. Â plus, there were only about 7 or 8 choices for brunch dishes. Â maybe dinner is better, but i was definitely disappointed and wouldn't come again.

This past Valentine's Day, I got all up in Zutto's buns. Their steamed buns, that is. Pervs. Specifically, it was the Short Rib version (with spicy fermented cabbage and tobanjan mayo) that stole my heart. This trio of Pac-Man-shaped sliders came packed with amazingly rich and delicious meat, and the buns themselves were big and round and soft to the touch. You know, just how I like my buns. Honestly, I could probably take down their whole selection of Chuuka Manjuu as a full-fledged meal itself, especially when the other flavors sound just as tasty - Kobe Beef, Tuna, Pork Belly, and Portabella. But I forged onward, deeper into Zutto's mouth-watering menu. We were told by our server that the restaurant prides itself on their ramen. And they ain't lyin'. Especially when there is a giant sign in the establishment that says the following: "Up to 120 lbs. of pork bones are boiled in a 24" pot at the highest heat for about 24 hours. Time and effort are the key ingredients in Zutto's Ramen. IRASHAIMASE !!!!" Now, I've never cooked real ramen. My prior preparation experience was nowhere near as extensive - instead, pretty much limited to a microwave in my freshman dorm room that teetered atop a TV/VCR combo. But when reading this sign, there were a lot of numbers thrown at me, along with an upper-case, multi-exclamation point, intense-sounding greeting in Japanese, so it's safe to say that when it comes to ramen, Zutto doesn't mess around. The broth in my Spicy Miso (red miso and pork based soup, topped with scallion, chopped pork, menma, white pickled ginger, sesame and chili oil) was the highlight - bold in taste, packed with more heat than actual spiciness, and finished off with a bit of smoky flavor for good measure. It was truthfully one of the better ramen bowls I've had in the city. I enjoyed finding ground pork balls swimming around in my soup, the noodles were thin and perfectly cooked, and my addition of pork belly for a few bucks more (of which they give you a generous amount) was a nice bonus for myself. And going back to the broth for a moment, it was fittingly a bright Valentine's red. Our server was very enthusiastic about everything Zutto had to offer, but some of her suggestions suggested were we not of the same palate. That evening's sake special of a 300 mL bottle at $30 she pushed was pretty mild (didn't really leave me with much of a buzz, either), and fell flat with so many other bright flavors surrounding us. Although, it should be noted that the beer, wine, and sake list is impressively extensive. Anyway, when we also ordered the Shishito Peppers as an appetizer early on, she seemed awfully sincere when she exclaimed, "I was really hoping you would order those!" These veggies were huge, but also bland, and unfortunately couldn't be saved by the thick lemon aioli served at its side. In the dessert category, the Brioche Bread Pudding (caramelized banana, house-made vanilla ice cream), in my book, beat out the Green Tea Ice Cream in a head-to-head match-up. It was very breakfast-esque in that it tasted like the classiest French toast stick you've ever had, covered in fruit and dairy. As for Zutto's decor, it's modern, while still being modest. The centerpiece of the dining room is actually a picnic table perfect for a large party. Therefore, it is by no means the most romantic spot in the city, but I knew that before making my V-Day reservations. What it is, is Japanese comfort food done very well. And if that sounds like something you and your date can get down with, then get at it - you two lovebirds, you.

Great place for the summer, the whole front of the bar opens up, great for people watching, or to be seen ! This place really got it together, opening before the Flying Pig Gastropub (where Johnny Rockets used to be). The staff here is hit or miss. One girl was very aloof, she seemed spacey (but nice!), one guy took our drink order and came back 15 min later (with only 2 other tables in the bar) yet another guy was sooo attentive and polite. So Hit or Miss. We were there for 3+ hrs just drinking, eating and chit chatting. Station House takes you away from Queens. Being inside, you really don't feel like you are in queens anymore. It's just so new for Forest Hills, a bar like this. Hip, low key, great atmosphere. I'm surprised that the Owner didn't walk around just to get to know Patrons. It was a Monday night, slow - perfect time to get to know people. --------------------------------------------------Â­--------------------------------------------------Â­----------- FOOD TRY: Kimchi Empanada's - Wow, these are REALLY GOOD. I want to eat 3 orders of these myself! Truffle Parmesean Fries - Can't go wrong with these! PASS: Ribs Thin Slabs, overcooked. Would prefer 4 fat juicy ribs over 8-10 thin overcooked bones. Beer Battered Meatballs - Overseasoned, Salty. Tasted like frozen meatballs. Poutin - These were good but perhaps there was too much gravy. The fries were swimming in it. And the "curds" were more like Mozzarella cheese. --------------------------------------------------Â­--------------------------------------------------Â­----------- The menu is awesome! Totally different than the usual fare on Austin St. Can't wait to come back. Even against the Flying Pig, I feel like Station House is cozier, more intimate. Love it! HAPPY HOUR MON-FRI 4-7pm, $2 off Tap!!!

For a burger joint, this place is well above average. Â The entire staff, from hostess to bar tender, was outgoing and attentive. Â Our table all chose burgers (with special sauce). Although the burgers were beyond any acceptable grease and salt levels, they were fantastic tasting. Â However, for the $16 price tag, the patties were on the smaller side (the benefit is that they come with fries and 2 o-rings which are rich) All in all, this was a positive experience and I will be back.

The girlfriend and I loved this place. The list of foods we had is as follows: beef tartare (special). A bit too citrusy, but not overwhelming. The beef could've been chopped a bit finer, but it was good, none the less. On the lighter side, tossed with lemon or lime juice instead of being bound by egg yolk. The garlic croustini they served with it though was delicious. Mix in a simple arugula salad and it made the dish. Next the crab dip, which I think was our favorite. The crab was thick and rich, accompanied by homemade tortilla chips and fresh veggies. I loved that they both give you the chips and fresh veggies, because not only does it make you feel a bit less guilty from consuming all the richness of the food, but the texture and flavor profiles both vessels create, gives for a satisfying meal. The chip; crunchy, rich and the veggies; crisp, flavorul. Finally the paella. At first, I was a bit hesitant. Seeing pictures of the food here on yelp prior to coming in, gave me doubts. I know traditionally, paella is a layered dish. All ingredients being added methodically, and precisely incorporated into the dish along the cooking process. The pictures on yelp looked to me like the rice and the seafood/sausage ingredients were cooked separately. By the time it arrived and I had my first sniff and taste, it didn't matter. The flavors were astounding! The rice had great texture and seasoned well. And the protein ingredients were absolutely dead on. Very hearty, very vibrant. And the wines. It made it a fun dining experience. Being able to pick out from a plethora of wines by the glass so to pair with your food, so to explore and taste by themselves, made you feel like you were a guest in someone's house... Heidi's, might as well be. Laid back, cozy, and welcoming. All makes for a great, satisfying night out, dining with, in this instance, my girlfriend. We'll sure be coming back again. And this time, saving room for dessert.

Had I known about this place when I lived in Manhattan I would've either moved to Brooklyn or made the trek a lot sooner, instead of eating at Nobu when and if we were ever lucky enough to get a table or be able to afford it. Â Now I can satisfy my cravings for sushi on the regular since I live across the street and eat here several times a week. Â Indeed, I just got a take-out Bento Box lunch special today which comes with soup and sald for $10.05! Â You can't beat that! Â I must say, though, their seared yellow tail appetizer is melt in your mouth fantastic and my go-to dinner is either the dinner combination box for under $20 (which I can never finish no matter how hard I try) or the Monkey roll. Â The wait-staff is always pleasant as are the chefs. Â I can't believe a previous commenter said something about not getting thrown something for free after years of service. Â At these prices, do you really need to? Â You're getting a steal of a deal. Â My husband and I regularly have lunch here together and our bill is always under $25 with the lunch specials. Â Can't beat the price, the quality, or the coziness. Â When we were thinking about moving we looked at each other and said: Â can't live without Iron Chef House (or Mister Video next door).

Never had Malaysian food prior but it's basically a combination of a variety of Southeast Asian cuisine. We got the roti canal appetizer, new siam noodles, 1/2 hainanese chicken, shrimp with eggplant Malaysian style, and the beef rendang based on all the yelp pictures and recommendations. All that was probably enough for a family of four, and came out to be $50 after tax. For the 2 of us, we had enough for lunch for both of us the next day. I personally liked the roti canal the best- curry was great and the bread was nice and chewy. Everything else were good, but nothing really stood out. I did see someone eating a curry noodle that seemed pretty good, ill try that next time. Also, regret not getting the satay chicken or beef. Looked like everyone was getting that.

This place is fantastic. Â Where else in NYC can you get a meal for $2. Â I usually get the bag of 50 frozen ones and enjoy them at home. Â The dumplings here are some of the best. Â The skin is just the right thickness and texture. Â Each dumpling comes with a good amount of filling and it is so juicy when they come out hot off the pan. Â YUM!

This bustling noodle shop specializes in "beef" noodles, the freshly-made and hand-pulled noodles in broth. The portions (about a quart) are generous. The noodles cook while you are eating with a plastic spoon, from a metal or plastic bowl -- the crockery varies in a charming way. The various cuts of beef make for an amazing broth: slurp up the noodles first, and then focus on the meat and the broth. The minced-meat and onion dumplings (#13) in clear broth is also very delicious, and not distinctively beefy like the other soups. The balance of meat and broth in the #2 is something close to perfection: the bowl of noodles I enjoyed here is one of the most memorable dishes I have ever eaten. The small and crowded seating area appears intimidating, but everyone is there to enjoy a bowl of noodles; you will find the communal tables quite welcoming. The waitresses take no guff and brook no queue-jumping, but do not hesitate to plant yourself in any open seat.

I'm a huge fan of Wild Edibles; love eating dinner at the bar. Â Previously, have given it 4-5 stars. But I'm wondering if new management is in place or the regular staff is off for the holiday. Had a plate of calamari dumped in my lap and no offer to cover the dry cleaning, comp the calamari on the bill or buy us an extra glass of wine. The restaurant, usually packed on any week night, was empty tonight when we walked in (8:45pm). Â  Service was off....why are you talking to another patron while holding our appetizers? Â  Makes you wonder......

Been here twice in three weeks, both times had a great meal and good service. Â I was a big fan of Convivio before it closed, so I was excited to try Morini - the pastas are not as good as Convivio, but the flavors are there. Â Great meat and cheese plates, just a solid overall experience.

While I understand that not everyone will be a fan, Di Fara is definitely a must try! My friend spoke highly of this place. I went to Midwood High School back in the day and I never tried it until this year. My friends from Staten Island and Queens came to Brooklyn and we all went together. While I had high expectations, I was pretty confident that it would fall short since I heard such great reviews. We arrived a little after they opened and we were able to find seats for the 5 of us. We ordered the plain and the one with meats (I forgot what it's called). Yes, the plain gets finished with fresh basil and olive oil. However, it was the perfect combination. The meat pie was delicious as well. Extremely flavorful! Being a New Yorker, I didn't think pizza could ever taste like this. I loved it so much, I tried coming here with my cousins. They're brooklynites and have never tried Di Fara as well. Unfortunately by the time we arrived, they were closing. Now that they're back from break, we're going to make another attempt. Can't wait!

I was so excited about Saraghina when I read the reviews.. I think that reason alone.. left me with high expectations. It is literally OK. I am from Jersey and know Italian joints.. & Saraghina isn't one of them.. Since there are disappointingly few options for good food in BedStuy.. Saraghina will see me often. I tried all pizzas (went w/ a group and did a tasting)..and they are extremely small and lacking season.. Overall.. it is Ok.. literally -- We thought it was byob and brought wine.. since they have a license ..they didn't allow us to drink it :(.. Nonetheless, Saraghina is the perfect date spot. I feel the ambiance makes up for the cuisine.

The best meal we had in four days in NYC. The Penne Bolognese and the roasted chicken were excellent. Everything came to our table properly prepared and hot. Don't let the name fool you into thinking this is just a tavern.

I love the ambiance of this place. We had a table that was half inside and half outside on a beautiful night. It was great date spot. Tasty Indian food and even better drinks. I ordered the Pimms Cup and I suggest you do the same!

Definitely my kind of DUMP. We walked into Prosperity Dumpling probably with a maximum capacity of 5 customers. The cool thing we noticed later on walking pass this shop was the STEAMY windows at one point in time. It definitely makes for more curiosity as to what's happening behind those windows. As most have noted, the prices make it feel like you're paying in Chinese RMB. Definitely perfect Snacks of choice and when purchased in bulk can make for an inexpensive Meal. Watching the handful of Women in the back doing the assembly line of tasks in the open-kitchen provides that comfort feeling that real people making good clean food for customers. Inexpensive pricing doesn't always translate to good bite-size savoury Dumplings but in this case they definitely seasoned everything quite well while I tend to enjoy the Chives & Pork Boiled Dumplings(10/$2.00) more so than the Fried(5/$1.00) version. I prefer the slight CHEWY bite of the wrap than the crunch of the Fried.

I'm told this is the 2nd oldest bar in the city, we walked past the 1st oldest on our way to Burp Castle. It had a great vibe, Hooegaarden on tap (my new favorite beer), and the smallest bathroom ever, so cute! Wish we had stayed longer since the rest of our night was a bust, but we stuck to our one drink maximum.

Came for dinner to celebrate my 9 yr anniversary. Service was great and the staff went above and beyond with free bubbly and a mini coconut cake to celebrate. I'd recommend the 5 course tasting menu --we ordered the chef tasting and the vegetable tasting, both AMAZING. One might think the vegetable tasting would not be worth it but so many of the dishes were creative takes on preparing vegetables--you'll never look at veggies the same again! No disappointments and a few good surprises. Gramercy is definitely one of my top 5 favorite restaurants in NYC. Definitely make a reservation in advance, even if you're planning to dine at Tavern (the more causal section of the restaurant).

this is a casual italian spot right in the midst of soho shopping land. reasonably priced, decent variety, good music (yeah oldies) made for a solid middle of the road italian option. we had 6 hungry and thirsty girls, so what we ate: rice balls, spinach salad, mad calamari, grilled branzino with veggies, steak and fries, norma pasta (plus a few other pastas i didnt taste), and nutella sandwiches for dessert the calamari was really good, would definitely recommend this. rice balls were large but didnt wow me. spinach salad was small and came with goat cheese instead of the gorgonzola stated on the menu. my grilled branzino was light and flavorful but the portion was really small (i had to pick at friend's pasta dished to fill up even after sharing the apps). the steak had a nice marinade on it. and the norma pasta was a hearty vegetarian option for those that swing that way. the nutella sandwiches were a bust - way too much brioche bread and not nearly enough nutella goodness. and certainly not worth their $9 price tag. bottles of wine run avg $40-60 and while i wasnt thrilled with our cab sav bottle it did the trick. service was attentive though over the course of the evening i did get the sense the most of the people around us were friends of either the servers or hostesses. nonetheless we got good service even without being on the in. this is an ok option for moderately priced italian if you are in the area and need to take a load off.

I can only review on the falafel, because that it is the only thing I get there. I should probably try other things on the menu, but the falafel is just too good. The falafel itself has a crisp exterior while the interior is the perfect density- not too mushy, but not too firm. The pita and fillings are great, and of the 10+ times I've gotten their falafel over the past few months, only one failed to maintain its structural integrity. I usually get the classic falafel sandwich as I'm a purist, but the spicy falafel and the spinach falafel are both good as well. Orders are served quickly and fresh. Wish there was more seating inside.

Great weekend brunch, although, yes, you'll probably have to wait in the line outside. I haven't been there for any other meals yet, but keep coming back for brunch! Delicious benedicts and a charming (if cramped) West Village setting.

M suggested Peep and I said Hell, No! M, then suggested Boqueria and I said hell, why not. I never been here before and always been curious about it. M was raving to me about their Patatas Bravas - crispy potatoes, "salsa brava," roasted garlic aioli. Didn't understand why M was raving about this particular tapas. Potato was dry and dude, you couldn't even taste the shiesty helping of barely drizzled aioli. But M seem to chomped away and couldn't stop eating them. I only had two bites of this and I was done. I glanced over the menu but was reluctant since wasn't sure if I had full control of ordering but I mentioned I was curious about a few items. I love eggs...SERIOUSLY, LOVE LOVE LOVE them and I love Quail and their eggs! So of course, I wanted to get Cojonudo fried quail eggs and chorizo on toast. This sounded better on the menu...cute though, but I never cried out God after it hit my mouth. M mentioned that K always orders the Bocata De Boquerones - pickled white anchovies, goat cheese apple, grilled country bread but M didn't realize this dish was a sandwich not under their tapas section. The waitress who adorned her ears with navy coloured long featured earrings advised they could make a tapas version with olives and petite size baguette I don't mind anchovies, I am actually trying to eat more of them due to their high levels of Omega 3 but M was a bit hesitant since M's not fond of fishy things. It was good, but I feel like they could did something more with this tapas version. I love seafood, so we got Gambas Al Ajillo ruby red shrimp, garlic, guindilla pepper - this was my most favourite dish out of the entire meal. It could have been spicier, but the waitress was no where to be found to ask for spice or black pepper. I would come, back but with someone that's not stuck on their potatoes.

Frankly, I'm shocked that this place hasn't gotten more attention. Â  The food is incredibly fresh, the staff is pleasant, and although I always take mine to go, the place has a nice dining room area in the back. Â I wouldn't say that I love that many places in midtown, but I truly love the gyros from Turco.

Meh. This is probably the longest I've waited for a table in NYC, and for just mediocre food. As we walked by Nevada Smith on my way to meet friends at The Smith Sunday afternoon for brunch, I turn to my boyfriend and say "We are not going here, right..." In hindsight, maybe Nevada Smith would have been the better option. Initially I was relieved to see The Smith and its beautiful brunch ambiance and the bustle of the restaurant. Little did I know that bustle would come back to bite me in the arse. The staff at The Smith have no idea how to give an honest wait time estimate. We were a group of 8, admittedly a large group to accommodate. However, I did not appreciate the complete falseness in what we were told our wait time would be. After given an estimate of 45-60 minutes, our wait time actually ended up being double that, just shy of 2 hours. In the cold. With the staff having zero sympathy / interest in seating us. Finally, the manager had a bright idea of putting together two empty tables of four. Novel idea. So we finally sit. When it comes time to waiter failed to mention that a complimentary drink / juice is included in the price, so half the group had to then order a beverage when he came back to our table. The food came out in what felt like under 5 minutes, crazy. The french toast is good, but I've had better.. There are some unique dishes on the menu (potato pancakes benedict); however my omelet was quite bland. The home fries were tasty, but no reason to come to The Smith for brunch and experience the long waits and not helpful staff.

I'm gonna go ahead an give Coppelia 4 stars although my most recent visit doesn't quite warrant this many. Â I have been here several times for breakfast, but my prior visits (which would have been rated 4.5 stars) were more than a year ago. Â I recently was out in NYC late night which is quite rare for me these days. Â As we were celebrating a BDay in the Meatpacking, I knew the perfect 24 hour venue for a hangover prevention meal was nearby Coppelia on 14th St in nearby Chelsea. There was no wait for a seat although nearly all tables and bar stools were occupied upon entering. Â This place has a more fun vibe at night than I have experienced during the day. Â Long story short, one friend ordered food to go which came out promptly; 2 other friends and myself ordered a total of 2 apps and 1 sandwich to dine in but unfortunately 2 or 3 of us were overlooked!! Â My first friend received his yummy Flautas right away. Â At the time they were delivered, I inquired if our food would be coming out soon and received confirmation as such. Â Needless to say I had to inquire with the manager after 30 minutes had gone by and still no food! Â I get that they were busy, but geesh! Â You get a pass this time Coppelia, but next time it might be a good customer service decision to apologize for the delay? Â  We eventually received our food: Â Nachos and a Torta de Milanese sandwich. Â Clearly nothing that should take 40 mins to receive. Â It was yummy, and gone in 60 seconds as we were starved by then!! Â We eventually ordered a round of Yucca Fries as well and those came out hot crispy and tasty. Â Food still good, I can give them that.
X

I'll Have Another..scratched from The Belmont Stakes. DOH!! My friend Tod, now with no prospect of witnessing horse racing history, thusly decided to forgo his flight from Chicago. I had intended to treat him to dinner at the new Atera, in the former Tribeca space, Compose. So, I had to scramble to find a willing replacement. Fortunately, my lovely friend Victoria (never call her Vic or Vicky) stepped up to the plate last minute and joined me in Chef Matthew Lightner's new inner sanctum of modern gastronomy. Having staged at the World #1 Noma in Copenhagen and #3 Mugaritz in Spain and then at his award winning Campagna in Portland, Oregon, Lightner harnessed these experiences and crafted a unique oasis that has made quite the initial splash in the NYC restaurant scene showcasing the trendy New Naturals culinary movement. Though a minute space, Atera is the antidote for claustrophobics with its vaulted ceiling and airy comfortable dining room. Adam Platt (NY Magazine) cites "the frosted windows shield the dimly lit room from the outside world, and in the evenings, the entrance of the eye-and-ear clinic next door is hidden behind thick green curtains. One entire wall is covered with an arrangement of potted plants designed to look like foliage in a wild forest, and diners nibble at their omakase dinners at a slate-colored bar, which is made from polished concrete and built around the gleaming open kitchen, like the bridge of a ship." High-end counter dining is quite the fashion these days and Atera holds its own with the likes of the Momofuku Kos and Brooklyn Fares. Atera offers a 10-course "foraging" tasting menu at $150. The tasting includes an introductory parade of "snacks" or amuses which were a mix of hits and misses. The highlights of these mini-bites were a delightful duet of Stuffed Jerusalem Artichoke Skins with Buttermilk, Brassica Flowers and Chickweed. Foie Gras, liquefied, then frozen, then molded into the form of a peanut was a guilty pleasure. Meringue Lobster Roll Sliders were a tiny, tantalizing tease. I could have done without the Mojave-dry Malt Cracker and Savory Black Sesame Granola. They basically tasted like Wheat Thins made out of bark..from a dead tree. Finishing the opening "snacks" was a clever faux Razor Clam shell made from dried bread and painted with black squid ink to mimic the striations on the shell. Stuffed with ocean fresh sliced clams, this dish just embodied all the smells and tastes of the sea. Atera has a vast wine list at moderate to expensive prices. To save a bit on the tab, try some of the more reasonable in-house cocktails like the Vesper with Gin, Vodka, Pineau des Charantes and Cardamom or the addictive "Milk Punch". The service at Atera is extremely choreographed and efficient. One never waits for the next course. Chef Lightner makes the time to converse with his guests when the opportunity presents itself. The main event commenced with a hypnotic presentation of Yogurt, Shad Roe, Rhubarb and Licorice..a plating the likes I haven't witnessed since Corton. This makes sense because Sous Chef Victoria Blamey worked with the eccentric genius Chef Paul Liebrandt for a time as well at Mugaritz alongside Lightner. Don't mess with this woman..she is ALL business on the line..the epitome of cool in the kitchen with the focus and concentration of a laser eye surgeon. Diver Scallops with Yuzu, Gin Botanicals and Pickled Green Strawberries were a delicate balance of joy and artistry. Victoria and I were absolutely inamorate of the awesome Peeky-Toe Soft Shell Crab, Toasted Shrimp and Angelica Root GelÃ©e. I had read raves about the Squid with Cured Lardo and a Squid-Pork Sauce, but was disappointed to discover it was not being served on this night. We did get the squid in "noodle" form in a broth that was just satisfactory. I needed something to cheer me up and the Dried Beet with Trout Roe and Crustacean Sauce was just what the doctor ordered. How Lightner can make a beet impersonate a mini fillet mignon in look and texture is beyond me. It was brilliant. An all-white plate of Halibut, Garlic, Whey and Chamomile reminded me of Inaki Aizpitarte's wizardry at Le Chateaubriand in Paris. Squab and Pheasant Black Mushroom Sauce, Pear and Tarragon were delicate and memorable. The last of the savory plates was a luscious and fatty Mangalista Pork Fillet with Wheatberries, Lamb's Quarters and Prickly Ash Moutarde. Desserts at Atera are whimsical. Meyer Lemon and Wild Ginger Cream encased in a shell resembling a rock with green moss was a fine palate cleanser. A modern, modular take on Strawberry Shortcake looked like something out of a Frank Lloyd Wright design. A Parsley Root Banana Split with Marshmallow brought us back to our childhood. A play on a Mexican style "churro" with Salsify, White Cardamom and Cinnamon followed by caramels and truffles meticulously carved to duplicate hazelnuts and walnuts closed this inspiring meal. Dinner for two with drinks, tax and tip was $525.

Man. Â I'm so disappointed. Â I was in town for a weekend getaway and staying in midtown. Â I wanted to try my old faithful, Sylvia's, but after doing some research decided to try something new. Â So I made the trip to Sylvia's Sunday evening and I ordered a very safe fried chicken, mac n cheese, and greens. Â A friend had the honey dipped fried chicken, greens, and candied yams. I had the mocha espresso and it was the best Coffee I have ever had! I am dreaming about going back. I want it ! I want it! I want it!

No need for a long,drawn out review here. The table was splattered with grease,the napkins on that greasy table had ketchup on them,the food was served on plastic plates and my gf's beer mug had a lemon seed in the bottom of it. Yelp really should allow zero stars.

Very nice, not so much a gastropub but a great bar with great food. The place gets ten out of ten for the lighting, design and atmosphere. Best Blood and Sand! Cocktails are really good too. Cute bartenders with even cuter accents. Service not so quick and is really hard to find but overall really well done space and nice fit for 10th street. Great for drink parties.
Best burger I have ever put in my mouth. Shack stake has the crispy portabella a must try! So good my husband went up for a second burger.

I went here with a friend who loves food as much as I do! We shared everything (so we could try more things.) This included: the chopped salad: (celery, cucumber, hearts of palm, beets, balsamic vinaigrette); warm goat cheese profiteroles with herb and roasted red pepper salad; grilled quail with sauteed mushrooms, bacon and cherry tomatoes and a dessert tasting plate (only $15!!)with small portions of these: creme brulee, blueberry crumble, nutella clair, lemon tart, chocolate mousse and tiramisu...which we were NOT able to finish! They don't serve wine by the glass, instead by the half bottle as VERY resonable prices. A half bottle being 2-2.5 glasses we paid $12 per half bottle. It allows you to easily change wines by course. YUM! I also liked the decor...we sat upstairs where it was more airy and light filled, as well as more quiet. The staff was attentive and swift - not pushy and allowed us to order a little at a time and figure out as we went if we wanted more courses. If you're in Tribecca, check out Landmarc, you'll be glad you did. They will be opening another location in the Time Warner building targeted for Spring 2007.

A+ Pizza-amazing Service-great It was a long wait but worth it. While waiting an hour to be seated we had drinks at the tiki bar in the back. Loved that the grapefruit juice was freshly squeezed. My greyhound was excellent. Once we were seated it didnt take long for our pizza to get to our table. I polished off an entire margherita which was amazing. For desert i had coffee and ice cream which was perfect. Staff is friendly. Cant wait to go again.

probably the best sushi I've had in NYC to date. the food is fresh, the clientele is great and the owner is a really cool guy. the only reason it didn't get five stars is because they are cash only. this is mildly inconvenient bc they're not exactly cheap and i don't travel with more than $20 on me BUT luckily, there's an ATM right next door
very good fish, fresh and very tasty. Can't wait to go back to DINER. The prices are OK, it worths a visit!

Definitely the real deal. The chef is not clowning around, both the executive chef, chef de cuisine, and entire staff. The duck meatballs more than lived up to their reputation. Impressive. The calamari and watercress salad is good and definitely worth $12, but the fried cooking style is not my favorite. As far as entrees it's interesting, the char costs $11 less than the grouper but is far superior. The char is pretty reveatory.Had a great bottle of Austrian white wine for $39 served in very serious wine glasses. Good thing I'm making so much money I don't know what to do with it so I can come here all the time.

Lovely place! Went to Jane for dinner with the girls and ended up having a yummy meal at a trendy little spot for a pretty decent price (we ended up payin 35 each, and had some vino) We ended up ordering all the appetizers + a risotto and sharing. Everything was delicious, but you MUST get the ricotta gnocchi, I mean WOW, that plate was orgaaaasmic (pardon my bluntness). It had been a long time since I was sooo blown away by a dish. I will definitely be coming back for more...

I want to like this place but, unfortunately, I think 'Meh' is indeed the most apt description. If you are ok with poor service, an ok but not great (read, over-hyped) burger, then it's worth the low prices, but otherwise I wouldn't recommend.

Very reasonably priced bowls of udon (~$9). They have combinations with a smaller bowl of udon and a bowl/dish of another entree for around $13.50, which I like because I could try more things. Udon was nice and chewy (not mushy) and the broth was hot and flavorful. I had the Uyako-Don (chicken/egg/sauce over rice) with the Udon. Both were tasty. The sauce that the Uyako-Don came with tasted mostly like soy. I had only a medium appetite, so I packed half of my Uyako-Don and took it home as leftovers. Friends had the soft shell crab and the katsu curry. Both liked their dishes too. We didn't get beers, but they have beer specials all weekend and during happy hour (5-7) on weekdays. I liked the ambiance, with the open kitchen, the japanese signs handwritten with black marker.

Went for girls brunch and was pleasantly surprised. Good prices, interesting but not specifically Thai inspired decor- the chandelier in the middle of the room is the big elephant in the room. Staff were lovely and food was just fine and best of all they dont rush you when all u want to do is catch up with your friends.

I walked passed this place a couple times and it was really cute and cozy from the outside. It looked like a cold place for a small bite and a drink. So looking to get out of the house for a while, we stopped here for a little light brunch. I like the place, it wasn't too crowded. Food: Pork Belly BLT: pork belly was delicious, bread was dry, could use more lettuce, BEST home fries EVER! Fritta: delicious, served with toast, a side salad and BEST EVER home fries I'd like to try this place for dinner.

we were looking for the perfect little charming place to eat around the holidays and jane fit EXACTLY what i had in mind. we actually stumbled upon it after i turned down nearly 60 other restaurants because they just "didn't feel right" or the menu was too blah. all of a sudden, we turn a corner and ta-da, cutest little restaurant ever. the staff is super friendly and our waitress was very informative. get the toasted gnocchi as an appetizer - it's amazing. i had the steak salad and he had the salmon, both equally delicious. MMMMMMM and for dessert do not pass up the milk & cookies. if you're looking for a relaxed setting and a good meal, go to jane. it was a wonderful little discovery. i'm sure we'll be back.
Ugh
This place needs another review like I need another hole in the head but what the heck. Nicely priced and tasty. The very essence of a local Brooklyn restaurant.

I have eaten here four or five times as it is in my neighborhood. Â The food and service is typically very good at a reasonable price point. Â I only knock off one star as they sometimes over-season a dish so as to make it too hot. Â To their credit, they have quickly replaced the item when it was brought to their attention. Â Other than the rare seasoning misstep, I highly recommend Benares.

I'm really quite surprised that I have yet to write a review of Great Jones Cafe considering the number of times I've been here over the years. That aside, I've only ever had brunch here, but of the brunches I have had, they've all been excellent. In terms of decor the space is pretty austere, but evokes somewhat of a Southern vibe. (It actually reminds me a little bit of nearby Acme). All in all, a solid choice for Sunday morning NoHo brunch.

The famous Laduree. When I first came to this location, they were strictly just selling macarons, but now they do have other pastries. But of course they are known for macarons, and they are still delicious. My favorite is pistachio.

** Brunch Review ** Perfect Brooklyn brunch. Friends and I came for brunch on a Saturday a few weeks ago. We were lucky to be able to walk in and snag a table (usually there's a wait). Sat up in one of the elevated booths in the main room so we could watch the action at the bar. Beautifully decorated -- looks just like Sweetwater or some of the other places around town -- mix of restored and new items. Servers have very cute little uniforms (bowties and all) just adding to the charm. Service was usual brunch -- fast, efficient, friendly. The food was wonderful -- tasty and fresh. Easily could recommend this place as a "better than your average" place in Williamsburg.
Balthazar is classic romantic. This is where I had my first champagne. Â Exceptional food and service.
LOVE the fries! The burger was so-so.
Tasty cappuccino!!!!! I was shocked how good it was. Cute place with very helpful & super nice people :) I will try their food next time :)

The smith has wonderful food and drink options and an adorable atmosphere. It's a little pricey for what I usually like but is a good treat every once and a while. Despite being packed all the time it didn't seem too crowded at the table. Thursday prime ribs are on point!

Everything at Ippudo is great... two of my favorites are the pork buns and the green tea creme brulee. The huge wait time is worth it the first few times you go, but less so after you have been a few times.
Not the best date restaurant, but definitely good wonton noodles! Â ($4 including tax, who can beat that!) Â  Note: I see a lot of non-asian people ordering soft shell crabs here too.
Hole on the wall in the heart of fidi, $6 for a pabst beer and shot of house whiskey, can't beat that right?

Hands down one of the best places I've eaten at in the city. Staff was really down to earth and friendly. We had to wait a bit longer than expected after we were called for our table but my friends and I were given free beer tastings during the extra wait. The food was to die for. The oyster recommendations given were great. Puts other oyster bars to shame. My favorites were the east coast selection. The salmon tartar was so flavorful. It was an explosion in my mouth. Only thing I don't recommend is the bottled cider w/ ice always a bad idea to water it down. It gets super crowded here so I recommend mentally preparing for the wait, but its totally worth it!
good hours, large wine selection, amazing chewy bread, pretty dark lighting
Had the chicken noodle. Very good soup and the gentleman working was super friendly.

Biddy Earlys is nomore, welcome to Woodrow instead. Compared to Biddys, this was 10x better. Came here for an old coworker's happy hour or more like "welcome back to nyc and don't go back to cali". Although they didn't have any well drink specials anymore but their $6 sangria was on point. Nomore beer pong instead it has 3-4 small tables. The layout is still the same but it's replaced by dark wood all round. It makes the look a lil bit sophosticated instead of dirty biddys. I appreciate the new look and the new vibe. It's def a chills place to be if you want a drink and catch up with old friends.

This place is what is wrong with Brooklyn. If you want to be treated like you're annoying the staff during your entire meal, here's the place to eat. We got some cocktails and starters. The cocktails were good. The starters were very tasty - mac 'n cheese, cornbread, and brussels sprouts - done right. I'll give them credit for the well done food. We tried to get something vegetarian for our friend - only one choice on the menu, so he tried to order a side of fries. "So, uhh, we... don't really do sides.... you can order the chicken plate and get them." Paid and left after that. Sorry for the inconvenience!
My favorite restaurant in NY. Great for brunch or for a romantic dinner. Â Not obnoxiously expensive, and the food is great.
halfway done w/ this Cuban sandwich - Â great! Â $6

A VERY good burger. Being from California I'd been hearing about this place for a few years but never made it out on a visit home (it always lost out to the tried-and-true In-N-Out). However, this past Sunday, our group of 6 made our way here for lunch. They have the somewhat annoying policy of not seating you until "everyone in your party has arrived," so we had to wait about 10 minutes (with a NOT full restaurant at 11:30am) for two of our friends to lock their bikes outside before they got a table ready for us. Once seated we decided to all share three of the appetizers (note: they come out BEFORE your burgers, not alongside). The deep fried pickles were made of spears of sour pickles - came with about 5 sticks. They were ok. The onion (tempura) rings were also only ok. Lastly we got the "smashed potatoes" which were literally smashed potatoes. It's like they roasted 5 small potatoes and smashed them down flat. Which I do not recommend. Next time I am over-ruling my friends and ordering the fries. The ones the next table over looked delish. Umami burger redeemed itself when the burgers came out. The original looked very bare, but it was awesome! I particularly loved the parmesan crisp inside. I thought that the truffle burger was tastier (and had more umami), but I don't think I'd be able to finish a whole one on my own. I split both burgers with Hubby, which was perfect. At about $20/person, this place is pricier than Shake Shack, but a fun, new addition to the burger neighborhood in NYC.

I am very disappointed with SoCo. I initially visited SoCo for a romantic dinner a few years ago and it was delicious! Pricy, but delicious. More recently I attended a happy hour on a Friday after hearing about it on a teacher happy hour listing, and was very pleased. The drinks were good and the food was delicious! I sampled the Mac and cheese, mussels and wings. Last Friday, I organized a happy hour at SoCo, convincing my co-workers to make the trek past our usual bar to SoCo. I get there a little early to reserve some tables and happen to mention to the host (I think) happy hour, and his response: we don't have happy hour on Fridays. I mentioned to him that I was there literally the week before for happy hour and he said he didn't know why, but they no longer have happy hour on Fridays. In my processing this, right after I called my friends and we quickly headed back to our usual spot where there is always happy hour and tasty eats, I contemplated whether there was a special event that Friday there was happy hour. But then, I remembered that there were other people there, non-teachers, partaking in the happy hour. Â Also, while the drinks and food were good, the service was very poor at the bar despite the large amount of staff present. The staff was busy, enjoying blue shots and photographing drinks. Perhaps this was for promotion purposes, though I can't imagine this requiring so many people. I digress. This decision to take away Happy Hour on Fridays tells me that SoCo does not value it's customers. I guess SoCo is doing so well it can afford to not make the gesture of a few hours of reduced prices at the end of a work week. Thankfully, I live and work in areas of Brooklyn where I have many, many options.

Chinese fast food mainly to seek pork, meat, fried noodle with rice. Cheap and on-the-go for the typical New York state of mind who laid the claim of always being busy. Albeit, quality of food is not the greatest as my personal taste finds it rather salty and greasy to clog one's cholesterol. Â Service is average but in a orderly fashion for fulfillment of patron's orders. Â Quantity is plentiful yet surely increase one's weight gain and cholesterol. Â I do not believe beverage are available. Â In this ailing economy cheap and plentiful are what drives businesses from sourly tanking. Patron's notes: Â only one measly table and one measly chair; always a long line outside. Â Drink plenty of fluids during and after a meal be it small or large from Wah Fung Number One Fast Food.

Ths place gets three stars because it is a cool bar and I really WANT to like this place. Â Really love the Pepsi Cola sign and has a good drink list. Probably wont be heading back for dinner again. Â Food was pretty bland and unsatisfying. Slow service, even sitting at the bar.

This place is a lifesaver for broke college students. We stop by here for food whenever there's nothing left to eat in the dorm, and it's always good food at reasonable prices. Â I'm a big fan of the eel lunchbox, $6 and it lasts for another snack too! It's not exactly gourmet, but it is tasty and fills you up. Also, free water (in human-sized cups, not the little dog ones you get at Food Gallery 32).

Love this one more than the one to the west side of NY. Have Tried Hirata buns, tempura and miso ramen. The soft boiled egg was just the perfect match. Dessert was great as well. The best thing was that we waited only around 5 min on a Friday night. Gotta come back!!

....Take the cannoli. My fiancÃ© and I came here with his cousin for dinner and the food was excellent. It's best to come here with several people because everything is served family style and you're going to want to try several dishes. We ordered the house chilled aka cold red wine to start. It's terrible but it becomes drinkable once it hits room temperature. We ordered the baked clams and mussels in red sauce for appetizers and the veal Don Peppe and shrimp Luciano for our entrees and everything was amazing with the baked clams being the best dish of the night. They were perfect. The food is consistently good and the service is service. They bring the food. That's it. Unfortunately, we didn't have room for dessert but we've tried some in the past and they are very good. Come here with an appetite. You'll need it.
This place makes me so happy! Best Sunday brunch. Love the house eggs.

WHY DON'T WE HAVE THIS IN SF?!! :(! I would be the happiest person in the world if we had a cart out here. I ordered the Halal chicken and rice and it was perfect! It is a big size but you should definitely order your own and drown it in white sauce ;) I finished my left overs the next day and it was still amazing.

The atmosphere was charming and hip, but I didn't think the food lived up to its atmosphere. I got the Paperdelle pasta dish (sauteed leeks in olive oil and bread crumbs) and shared the Bianca pizze (brussel sprouts, ricotta and parmesan). The pasta itself was tasty, it seemed homemade but it was unclear to me if it was. The first bite of the pasta dish was really enjoyable, however after a few more bites it started to seem bland. Same onion-y/leek-y flavour that got a little boring. The bread crumbs added an interesting texture though. The pizza didn't come together for me. I was excited about the brussel sprouts on a pizza (brussel sprouts are the best!), but I didn't feel like it was a cohesive dish because it felt like I was eating brussel sprouts and then pizza (or vice versa).

Great little find in an alley near Soho! My boyfriend and I were looking for a dinner place at the hotel on yelp and he wanted regular American food, nothing too fancy. It isn't easy to find this in NYC so when I came across this little gem that was walking distance from our hotel we were sold. If we didn't go looking for it we never would have found it. It is completely unmarked in huge back of an alley. We walked in on a Saturday night and were seated right away. The tables are very close together but it was ok. I got the filet which was cooked perfectly and delicious. It came with mashed potatoes that were great. My boyfriend got the 5 cheese Mac and Cheese and it had a nice crispy topping and it was also very good. We got the cheddar bread appetizer as well and were very happy with it. Also had a nice red wine, but I'm not sure what it was. All together it was a great night and I think the bill was a little less than $100. For a nice dinner with appetizer and wine I consider that normal in NYC. The place was really busy and both bars were packed as well. I think there was an upstairs too. Great little gem, def recommend looking it up and going if your in the area.

Cute little place - casual but welcoming. Â We didn't have a problem with service though I noticed we didn't get a bread basket like the other tables for some reason. We tried 2 different personal pizza (round ones), both were really really good. Â I am a fan of thin crust pizza and I thought it was one of the best thin crust pizzas I've had in NYC. Â  It felt light, sauce was not heavy and afterwards, I did not feel too full like I usually do after eating pizza. Â  I would definitely go back again. Â Highly recommend if you are in the area.

This is a standout restaurant. Expertly executed Classic French bistro food. How lucky are we to have the former Executive Chef at Bouley here in our neighborhood! The onion soup is the best we've tasted. The lobster risotto is no joke. The poison du jour was so tasty. So much more there to try. And the brunch there is equally excellent. Â  Go!

Pride and Prejudice (C'mon, you KNEW this would happen one day!!) It is a truth universally acknowledged, that a single man in possession of a large appetite and seated in a chic restaurant serving a cuisine not his own - must be guided through the experience. However refined the cultural sensibilities of such a man maybe, he is rightfully considered a village bumpkin who must be saved by his discerning female dining companion from the faux pas that's just waiting to happen. Elizabeth, however, had different motivations. As she surveyed the clay pottery hanging on the ceiling, she took in a moment to cast a glance at William T. Fitz (W.T.F.) Darcy. He seemed an odd mixture of reserve, sarcastic humor, and a sense of personal pride in his taste that bordered on arrogance. While charmed by his well-bred manners, she had been slighted by his response to her suggestion that they dine at Pylos. "There isn't a single Greek restaurant outside of Astoria that would not be a punishment for me to dine at. Would the experience at such an assembly indeed be much superior to that of consuming gyros in the wee hours of the morning after a tete-a-tete at a speakeasy?" While lively and with a playful disposition, strong minded Elizabeth found this position rather ridiculous and was determined to give him one of her set-downs. As the server poured a glass of Cabernet / Agiorgitiko (Monemvasia Peloponese 2003), she leaned forward to inform Mr. Darcy that she would like to decide their fare for the night. She disarmed him laughingly, "I do so that you might have the pleasure of despising my taste." Darcy leaned forward: "Indeed, I do not dare." The first appetizer was Poikilia, a trio of dipping sauces - Tzatziki (thick, tangy yogurt dip), Taramosalata (lemony fish roe), and Melitzanosalata (grilled eggplant and extra virgin Greek olive oil). Â As she dipped the warm pita bread in the dip, Elizabeth inquired of Darcy's views on human weaknesses that exposed one to ridicule. She also asked whether he found the Tsatziki similar to that served by a street cart vendor. Darcy ignored the latter question and chose instead to clarify the difference between vanity and pride. Soon, the next appetizer was brought to the table: Ta Afrata Keftedakia Tis Dianas. The fragrant and flavorful meatballs were as close to perfection as Elizabeth had ever encountered. When she saw Darcy eating quietly, it dawned on her that amazing as they may taste, it appeared that he had resolved that no sign of admiration should now escape him. Steady to his purpose, he scarcely spoke ten words through this course. The third of the Mezethes was now upon them: Octopus braised in sweet and spicy red wine served with fava puree. As Elizabeth shook her head, Darcy smiled ever so slightly while drawing the attention of the waiter to bring them some lemon to enhance the flavor. The waiter returned soon and brought along the final appetizer for the evening: Saganaki Tou Merakli - three Greek cheeses melted in a pot. Darcy commented upon the conscious preference of the Mezes over the entrees. Elizabeth paused to respond, "Surely, one as culturally aware as yourself, Mr. Darcy, would know that is the preferred way to enjoy the cuisine?" Darcy struggled for composure, "I might, perhaps, wish to be informed why, with so little endeavor at civility, I am thus rebuked." In the absence of a response and to overcome the uncomfortable silence that followed, Darcy commended Elizabeth's restraint in forgoing chocolate (Ouzo spiked chocolate mousse) that was dear to her heart in favor of authenticity - the warm Galaktobourekakia (buttery phylo triangles filled with Greek custard and drizzled with cinnamon and honey). After a few bites of the excellent pastry, Elizabeth addressed the issue, "I trust, Mr. Darcy that you never allow yourself to be blinded by prejudice. But, it is incumbent on those who never change their opinion to be secure of judging properly." Darcy responded agitatedly, "I have no wish of denying that I did everything in my power not to concede my earlier judgment. But, my feelings will not be repressed anymore. You must allow me to tell you how much I ardently admire and love the food at Pylos. It is decidedly worthy of one's affection, and not beneath it."

Stopped here to grab a sandwich to-go over lunch. Their "classic sandwich" is a great deal - around $5 for about a 10-11 inch sandwich. It was tasty and filling but the meat was pretty fatty, which was a little too much near the end. However, I'd order it again because it's fast, cheap, and easy. Looked around and saw most people eating pho, which I will definitely be trying the next time I'm back!

I'm from DC and there is nothing close to this level of Ramen! We had the pork buns, which were our of this world. Ramen was fantastic. I added an egg and I think it was well worth it. They must have used an immersion cooker because it was perfectly soft boiled.

Oh boy this place is good. My biggest gripe was that it being New Years Day, I was more-less too hungover to really go wild. I had to pass up my favorites, curry and larb, but still had a fantastic, albeit smaller meal. This is one of my girlfriends favorite restaurants. She lived in Thailand for a year and can speak Thai and said that this is one of the only places that makes various Thai desserts and dishes that you can't get in other places. We had the watercress salad which was fried watercress and various seafood in a bed of fish sauce. The fried oil of the watercress and the fish sauce were solid. We also had papaya salad and these sausages. The salad was good but the sausage was nothing to write home about. The best part of our meal were these tapioca balls filled with some sort of nutty savory mixture eaten with greens. It was amazing and I've never seen it served anywhere else. I badly wish there was a restaurant of Sripraphai's quality in DC...

It gets busy, so expect a wait -- even during off hours. Solid ramen, good portion sizes, decent prices, and a friendly staff. One of the better ramen joints in the city, though Ippudo is still probably my favorite. I'd go back. They also have their own take on the Momofuku/Ippudo style pork buns. The pork is thinner and they use a tartar sauce with it, which is interesting. Worth a try for $3.
I always love going here. We've ordered just about everything and enjoyed it all!
Yummi Mexican food. Burrito my favorite

Wow, this place is pretty good! Awesome for NY standards. I wish the hot sauces were a little more spicy, but everything else is pretty awesome. Ingredients are fresh, the flavors are right and it really tastes like authentic street tacos!
I dream of these fries almost every week. Love the vibe and food is good in general but they have the best fries in town!
If you face away from the street, you can pretend you're in Paris at this tiny brasserie/cafe. Â A very authentic feel and delicious food.

I don't normally find myself in this part of Brooklyn ever, but since my friend from out of town was visiting and we had plans to visit the nearby Morbid Anatomy Museum, I figured I would give this place a try. I was slightly worried that there would be a wait because I knew that this place is popular, but thankfully, we got seated right away. We also got here at around 3PM, hence the quickly getting seated. I'm imagining the menus are different at dinner time or during the week, but we came here for brunch, so we had brunch items. I had their roasted mushrooms, spinach, and goat cheese scramble while my friend had their eggs huntington dish. We also shared an order of their cheddar waffles. I thought my food was quite good as did my friend. We thought that the cheddar waffles would be savory, but they were actually sweet and they came with maple syrup. The texture of the waffles was amazing as well: crunchy due to the corn meal, sweet from the powdered sugar and probably sugar in the batter, and slightly savory because of the cheddar. No complaints about the service, either. Since this is quite out of the way for me, I'm not sure when I'll ever come back here, but if I happen to be in the area, I'd love to stop on by again.

In the A&E Biography of my life, they will show stills of me at Balthazar throwing my head back and laughing with a glass of wine in my hand looking totally happy (and hopefully on a good-hair day). Â Balthazar is one of my favorite restaurants, not only in New York but anywhere. My friend Bruce took me there for the first time years ago, after whetting our appetites with gimlets and mac & cheese at the Soho Grand. Â Last weekend we tried to figure out exactly when it was when we were there together. "Um, 3 years ago, 4?" "Hmmmmmm....I can't really remember, I think we were kind of drunk." "We were always kind of drunk back then" "Ha ha, yeah, those were the days." "Wait, I know!" "What?" "It was the same day I bought those Prada buckle shoes!" "Omigod those are my FAVORITES" "I KNOW!" "OK, so I got those 5 years ago" "5 years ago it is." So 5 years later, I decide it's time for us to go again. Â Saturday morning, I woke up my dear friend Bruce, who was hosting me for the millionth time after I my flight got canceled due to weather (UGH)...by jumping on the bed and saying "Guess. Â Where. Â We. Are. Going. To. Brunch. Today?" Â Big grin. (groan) "Where?" "BALTHAZAR!" "No way!" "Yes, I scored a reservation, so get dressed and look good. Â We're catching the train in half an hour". Fast-forward to us arriving at Balthazar after braving the LIRR, Penn Station, and the slush and ice of the city streets. Â AHHHHHHHHH. __________________________________________________Â­____ Entering Balthazar, you are in Paris, New York, and Heaven all at the same time. Â The place is buzzing with waiters and patrons, and it has that old-world feel of an institution that has been there for years. Â The high ceiling and huge tilted mirrors on the wall are incredible, and reflect the many tables and booths of Â all varieties of people hovering over wonderful plates of food and engrossed in conversation. For starters, Bruce ordered his favorite dish of all time, the Goat Cheese Tart. Â Oh my, it was so good and creamy, with caramelized onions adding to the richness of the dish. Â Garnished with house-made sundried tomatoes and a smidge of tapenade, you could easily make a light meal of it with a soup or salad. Â Simply perfect. Â  I had the steak tartare. Â Best ever. Â Generous portion of the most tender meat, perfectly seasoned, with lightly toasted crostini and a mixed green salad. Â God. Â I could eat this dish by the bucket. Bruce had the Beef Stroganoff for his main. Â Talk about comfort food - home-made broad noodles and butter-soft beef in a rich & creamy sauce. Â I would definitely recommend it on a chilly winter's day. I had the grilled Trout - entirely upon the recommendation of the server. Â How she convinced me to eat a fish that I normally don't care for is beyond me, but her description sounded so delicious that I could not resist. Â And she was entirely, entirely correct. Â The fish is grilled to a crisp, with a balsamic reduction on top, all sitting on a bed of baby lentils and vegetables. Â I enjoyed every delectable bite. Everything at Balthazar is always wonderful, down to the bread and butter. Â There is a reason it is such a popular hot spot - not because of trendiness, but because their food is fantastic and the wait staff is excellent. Â You will sit close to your neighbor, but enjoy it. Â We ended up meeting a wonderful couple who we talked to for a full hour after finishing our meal - the perfect cap on our experience. Like the ultimate pair of Prada shoes, dining at Balthazar is something special to treasure. Â A bientot! P.S. The cookbook is available for sale, and features many of their classic recipies including the Goat Cheese Tart.

I hear a lot of complaints that this place is overrated, and it's probably true. I'm always a little shocked when I walk by and see the lines. I enjoy the food, the service is always friendly and the ambiance at both locations is lively and fun. But wait times that rival even Momofuku's Noodle Bar are straight up unreal for a restaurant of this quality. So if you come across The Meatball Shop and the wait is reasonable, stop by! Their innovative menu allows you to pair your balls of choice (including a very well-executed veggie ball) with a preferred sauce and serving style, from sandwiches to straight up ($3-10). Sides are reasonably priced ($5) and reflect the daily offerings of fresh, seasonal ingredients. And the root beer floats ($5)? They're just right. It's delicious comfort food served in a convivial environment at a very affordable price point, and I have nothing bad to say about it. But it's not life changing, and I would never wait more than 20-30 minutes eat there.

I had family in over labor day and they absolutely loved this place. Great food, knowledgable staff, and tasteful decor. A little loud and cramped, but that means that food is that good! Highly recommend.

Went here for the first time this past Sunday to try out the brunch and was pleasantly surprised. The prix fixe was14 dollars for a myriad of choices, mainly regarding different styles of eggs, which comes with a drink of your choice (coffee, mimosa, bloody mary, a glass of wine), potatoes, fresh fruit, and a heft basket of croissants and muffins. The service was pretty good, being that there weren't many people in the restaurant at the time (3PM on a Sunday) and my inner kid enjoyed the crayons they provided to draw on the paper which covered the tablecloths. I ordered the corned beef hash with poached eggs and a mimosa and my boyfriend had the eggs benedict. Both orders were very good and came out quickly. The potato side was extremely good but it was a small portion. All in all, a good value for the price. I would definitely recommend it for brunch again.
What a wonderful place. People are friendly service is good. i like the XLB and the braised pig feet, so tasty. Lovely decorated. Good choice;)

My Crustacean allergy can turn an average trip to a typical Spanish restaurant into quite the itchy/puffy adventure so I usually just stay away. Â Despite this, a friend convinced me to join her at Casa Mono one night this past winter and I was hooked. Â I've been back several times tasting everything and anything that will not turn me into an elephant man look alike. Â  Even though the portions are decent for tapas style, the bill really adds up quickly, usually averaging about $100/per person if you also order a mid-price bottle or two of delicious Spanish wine. The service is a bit snippy which is usually a huge turn off for me, however it serves as an indicator of just how serious these people are about their fabulous tapas and wine. One night we arrived early with no reservations, so even though they put us on a timer and kicked us out promptly when the timer was up, they let us take our nearly full 2nd bottle of wine to Bar Jamon next door.

Burrito Box is an excellent alternative to Chipole. Â One day I was craving for a burrito run. Sick of spending an arm and a leg going out the night before... I was desiring lunch on a budget full of flavor with a satisfactory proportion of meat that can be dutifully assisted by the tangy, green salsa that impresses more with taste than spice in the squeeze bottles on the counter. Â Well what better place to go than a place near the place I live. Â  The burrito are served piping hot and with a good portion of meat veges beans and of course rice. Â  Very filling and will put you into a diabetic coma (j/k) Â I recommend the wraps Â they are filled with generous portions of meats and veggies. My favorites are the wraps... Â any wraps will do they simply are....Scrumptious! Â  Oh yeah free chips with lots of salsa! Burrito Box is small and a hole-in-the-wall. Â  The people there are friendly and if you eat there, help yourself to some chips and salsa. Â It only sits about 6 or so. Â It will fulfill any Mexican-food craving in this part of town! Recommendations: 1. Â Beef: Flank steak wrap 2. Â Vegetarian: Â Portabello Mushroom Burrito Accepts credit cards (bonus) Â and they deliver!
