Don't know why this place is categorized as "American"...it is Indian "fusion" (I hate the term but can't think of another term at the moment) with a twist. Chef Mehta's (an Indian guy) Tapas style menu reflects his pastry chef experience. The food is tasty but at a premium considering the portions. The one think that I have an issue with is the layout of the place. The tables are way too big for the space and there is very little room to maneuver. The designer of the space had no idea of maximizing of what they had to work with.

This restaurant absolutely lived up to the hype. Â While the wait can be quite long, they provide you with cookies, water, orange slices and fries. Â They have anything you want to order and as my dad said he "hasn't seen a ham steak like that since Wyoming". Â Worth the wait and they are accommodating to larger groups. Â Best part is, you can also order delivery from them! Â Our food cam pretty fast and hot and the bag was filled with about 12 lollipops. Â So that was fun.

On the advice of a co-worker I went to Benito's Â while in New York. 4.5 stars ?????? No way ! We got the lunch special. a chicken parm and an eggplant parm and we we disappointed in everything we got. Salad, looked like previous nights left-overs. Chicken parm, tasty but a little tough, Eggplant parm was great if you like sauce and breading ! If you actually want eggplant in it you really have to look hard for it. Paper thin , one layer deep surrounded by double thick breading. We ordered clams on the half-shell but the waiter said they were bad and did not serve them. On a positive note the waiter was pleasant and obliging { plus he would not serve bad clams }. Overall I would pick any neighborhood Italian place in Philly Â over Benito's in Little Italy It might just be a big tourist trap overall !

What a lovely treat! Â I stopped by on a Monday night and ordered the BBQ ribs. Â They are cooked with Cola and the meat just dropped off the bone. Â The flavor of the sauce was incredible and I can't remember the last time I had ribs this good! Â Their lava cake is also great as a kicker dessert. Â Warm and friendly atmosphere. Â The staff was especially great and attentive and personable. Â Glad to have found a new restaurant to frequent!

Ramen was the perfect pit stop for lunch with the cold freezing and dry weather we suddenly got ourselves into it during our mini get-away. Â Happily, we only had to wait for about 20 minutes, which was not bad at all! Â As we walked into the venue, we were greeted loudly by all the workers. Â Always delightful and so energetic those ramen workers are, especially when it is coming from pure Americans and not from Japanese workers :) . Â The decor was awesome for a ramen restaurant! Â So modern and so upscale compared to the ones in SF! The pork buns were delicious. Â Soft and the pork with mayo and spices blended well together. Â For 2 buns though, it was quite costly, but this is NYC! I decided to order the Akamaru Modern since I love some garlic infused in my ramen bowl. Â Of course, I had to order the extra side order of Nitamago that cost me $2 !! Â The noodles were a different version than what I usually eat. Â They were plentiful and had a great presentation. I am not sure if it is because everyone overhyped it for me, but since I've had my share of ramen around the Bay Area, everytime I have Orenchi in Santa Clara, it hits the spot perfectly. Â When I had Ippudo, they didn't have the same effect on me!

Probably the best steak i've ever had. Amazing. The bone marrow is a must. I still think The Breslin has the best burger. Great bar area when you first walk in. Classy old school decor. A must go to place in NYC.

My friends and cousin came with me to Lombardi's because I wanted to go here after hearing so many good things about it. When we first stepped in, we were told that the wait would be 45 minutes and that we should put our name on the list and come back then. So that's what we did. We walked around the neighborhood, came back after 40 minutes, and then saw that our name was crossed off the list. My friend was so ticked off that she confronted the hostess, and the hostess said, "well, I called your name, but you didn't respond." My friend: "you told us to come BACK in 45 minutes!" The hostess's response? "You should have been here." And then she asked us if we wanted to be placed at the end of the list in this incredibly rude tone of voice. NO. We DON'T. Good thing that another host came to take her place, saw the whole problem, and immediately had us seated. Then we were seated. We had sausage, mushroom, and another meat (can't remember) on our pizza with lots of extra garlic. One of my friends who loves pizza could not stand the sausage at all. She said it tasted like cardboard. After I tasted it, I definitely felt that the texture was too rubbery. Why don't they used crushed sausage here? The pizza crust itself was good, but I think this place is pretty overhyped. I rather go to John's Pizzeria in Greenwich than this place. The sausage AND the crust are good there.

Food was amazing. We had the Â Crab risotto and the octopus for and app and for entree the Squid ink fettuccine Â and the Â halibut. The fettuccine was great.. Everything taste fresh and the service was great. I defiantly recommend Gato and I will defiantly be back.
great italian food, friendly staff. they always remember my name. amazing! gluten free pasta too! love this place

I have not tried any items on their dinner menu yet but I was here today for brunch. Really bad experience: -I did not know they served alcoholic cider so the waiter made fun of me to my face for that. -I ordered the Roasted Veggies and Eggs for $12 - they brought out 2 sunny side eggs, some potato wedges and asparagus. All of that for $12..... and the seasoning was just nothing extraordinary. Totally disappointed. I felt ripped off

All the reviews are true. Clinton Street Bakery is friggin' awesome! There are many places to get breakfast. Whether you choose giant plates for $5 at franchised operations, or great tasting mom and pop joints, breakfast menus usually consist of your usual pancakes or waffles, omelletes and choices of meats. So what makes Clinton Street worth the 1-2 hour wait? Yes, it's true. The wait is insane. Clinton's delivers the best breakfast you'll probably ever have. Everything is made just perfect. All the items on your traditional breakfast menu is done a little different. Their pancakes and waffles have a secret house sauce that you'd want to kill the chef for. Their sandwiches are made with the best ingredients and all of their meats are roasted/grilled right there and then. If you ever visit New York, you have to try Clinton Street Bakery. It's well worth the wait.

While we didn't try any of the food, Uva is a great place to get a decent glass of wine on the UES. (Most glasses ranged in the $9-$12 range--me and my girlfriend both had a lovely sauvignon blanc and prosecco.) The decor was also cute (think vintage rotary phones on the walls) and would be perfect for a date. The only downside, which you can't fault them for, is that this place gets absolutely packed on the weekends.

I'm a huge fan of John McDonald and Josh Capon's other restaurant Lure, so naturally I fell in love with B&B as well. While the restaurant is small, their food is great and happy hour prices even better (half price apps and drinks). The Bash Burger is what they're famous for - get it. Also love their chicken lollipops and short rib tacos.

Have had pizza from here a few times - catered to a couple events and once by just passing it. Delicious NYC pizza. Really into the thin crust pesto one. But the Sicilian slices are really what I'm into here! Love a nice, hot, crispy slice now and again!

Good place for brunch - has lots of seating so the wait is not too long, and all the usual staples (eggs, burgers, fried stuff) are present in abundance. Bloody Marys to spare to cure the hangover, too. If you want to stray from the usuals, get onto the deep-fried string beans with aioli - those are a mouth-watering shared appetizer.

First--this is in Chinatown. And, Joe's Shanghai is a dumpling house. For those of you who complained about service--perhaps you should eat uptown, at a place that costs a lot more. Second---my review: I went in at 4 pm on a Friday. I had just been at Chambers Street Wines (a great place) and was craving soup and dumplings. Duh! I zigged and zagged my way to Joe's Shanghai. The hostess asked if I minded sharing a table, which I do not, and so I was sat immediately. I ordered pork and crab soup dumplings and drank my hot tea as I observed what everyone else (with their bigger appetites) was eating. Virtually every table had dumplings on it, and for those who were eating more there was fried rice, vegetables and tofu and scallion pancakes. People seemed happy. I paused to study other tables' soup dumpling eating techniques. For the most part people seemed to have a handle on it, which made me think I was dining with regulars. My soup dumplings arrived. I took a minute to show off my technique with my table mates whose dumplings were plopped down at the same time as mine. They looked confused. I was not. The texture of the dumplings is very nice. The soup was tasty but it was thicker and more oily than I expected. Also it was very salty. I like salt, and so I was satisfied with the flavor, but I only mention it to let those of you who don't like salt know: these are salty dumplings. The meat of the dumpling was all right. I didn't think it was awesome. The first two bites of the dumpling were my favorite: the skin and the soup. The second two bites were more judicious--waste not, want not. All in all I was pleased with my visit. I asked for my check and left $2 on top of the included gratuity (which had only amounted to $1, since I had only had the dumplings). I am already looking forward to eating these pockets of goodness again. Soon, I hope.

From what everyone on Yelp says and what Google has told me, the dollar pizza I have been shoveling down my gullet for the last decade is not real Italian pizza. Here I was thinking I was a native New Yorker, pizza connoisseur... Fuck it, I still love my dollar pizza but I love Sottocasa too. It's definitely soggier than other "pizza," but it wasn't like a bad or inedible soggy... ya know? It was actually ridiculously tasty, the crust was thicker and had a good crunch to the outside while the center of the crust was thin and wet with tomato sauce and topped with spicy sausage (definitely the best topping ever), everything tastes fresh and amazing. I'm not sure how this perfection was achieved in like 3 minutes (that's how long it took for our order to come out) but I'm not complaining. Price point wasn't crazy but it wasn't cheap by pizza standards either, it ranges between $9 to $18 for a relatively small pizza, relative being the very important key word here because it was filling enough for the two of us. I know it sounds expensive because you can get a 16" pie for like $8 nowadays but this pizza and NY pizza is a completely different experience, not even in the same categories of food in my opinion. Non-believers, go give it a shot and if you hate it... then Idk but by the looks of the reviews, the owner is happy to refund the haters. I want to say it's authentic Italian but how the hell would I know? I just know that it tastes really good.
The manager contacted me to make amends for her employee, and she was very apologetic and gracious. I still like this place, but that was a horrible mark on my experience here.

I don't know dude... the pork belly sandwich itself was fatty, juicy, and satisfying but the blood orange lemonade was wayyyyy too sour for my taste even after adding a ton of syrup it didn't taste so good. And eating that sandwich was a huge mess. Definitely not bringing a date here. There was seating upstairs which reeked of cleaning fluids. It really did not add well to the aroma of my pork sandwich. I guess it could have been a four star but it had some misses.

Came here to try out the eclectic menu since traditional Filipino food had been a bit lackluster from my prior experiences. The atmosphere is romantic, a little reminiscent of maybe being in a nicely decorated tropical hut. My friend and I started out with a couple Pacquiao's Punches and then went straight for the meats. Â The fertilized duck egg is literally duck fetus in a shell, I'll honestly say it tasted a little weird and mildly unpleasant. Â The spam fries were essentially batter-coated pieces of hot dog, nothing particularly special. Â The Longga hot dog was quite good, mildly spiced and covered with some nice shredded pickled papaya. Â The show-stopper was the lechon, a nice thick piece of super-crispy pig skin and fat on 1 side and tender pork belly meat on the other with a mix of vegetables in some sort of vinegar-based sauce to cut through all the fatty deliciousness. Moving onto the entrees, the special of the day was a Filipino-style fried chicken served on top of a blue yam waffle that had the distinct taste of caramel, all covered in coconut "gravy" that made the dish more sweet than savory but overall still very good. Â The sisig, a mish-mash of pig unmentionables on a sizzling hot cast-iron dish, was 100x better than sisig I had in the past (probably because I had beef last time), especially with this condiment sauce they provide that I think is probably 10% MSG by weight to go with their famous garlic fried rice. We capped the meal off with coconut flan (traditional, good but not mind-blowing) and an assortment of sorbets (purple yam, avocado, and mascarpone I think). Â Total bill came out to $115, reasonable given how much we pigged out. Â Most of the menu was ok, but the sisig and the lechon make this joint worth coming back to if you delight in all things pig.
Excellent food, atmosphere and drinks!
Great food, great staff, and great ambiance. Oh by the way the food is unbelievable not great, but unbelievable.

After a month of futile attempts of searching for good middle eastern cuisine in the area, I come upon this tiny cart and this just blows all the competition away. Spending quite a long time in Egypt and the Middle East, I've been spoiled by all the great food I had consumed over there and when I got back to New York, I was seriously "homesick" for good egyptian cooking. I was even prepared to shoot, stuff, and grill a dirty pigeon myself (don't judge, try the hamaam when you go to Cairo, you won't regret it) when I've tried various restaurants in the Little Egypt strip here in Astoria. Not to be disrespectful to the great chefs there but the cooking has been Americanized a little bit which takes away the authenticity and flavor, sad to say. I took one bite and I was transported back to dusty, polluted Cairo, with its 70 million strong mass of humanity, swirling all around, with the blare of taxis adding to the cacophony of prayer calls. And for $6, it can't be beaten. True, Mr. Freddy is not from Egypt but somehow, his cooking sure tastes like it. Added bonus is you get to speak colloquial Arabic and they understand! Alhamdullilah ... i got a craving appeased before i booked another ticket to Cairo.
What more could you ask for? Cheap and DELICIOUS Thai food. Everything is great, but especially the calamari and pad kee mow. Service is really fast as well. CANNOT go wrong

In the city, it's hard to find a place that isn't trying to rush you out the door with a full belly, but at Pio Pio the friendly service and relaxing atmosphere made me lose track of time- almost. We came in and were promptly seated. The owner/manager came over to us and recommended a few dishes after we said it was our first time. He recommended Â us the seafood special, which he said was off menu- but delicious. His persistence won out and we ordered that with the half chicken. I expected the seafood was about to go bad, which was why he was so adamant about us ordering it, but it was delicious and flavored well. It came with mussels, half a spider crab, and shrimp- all in good amount served with dirty rice. Halfway through the meal i needed to use the restroom which was out of service- but the manager allowed me to use the one in the back for the kitchen (i assume). As i went to wash my hands and I found the door knob in the sink, whipping around to find of course- the handle missing. After the walls began to cave in for a bit- i realized I had my phone and called my friend whereupon i'm told the manager took one look at her confused face and jetted to the back to help me out. Funny story eh? The manager stayed friendly through the meal and even after as he led us to the door. Before we made our departure he waved his hand and made 3 business cards appear out of thin air- saying he also did real estate. Haha - funny guy. 4 stars for the food and 5 for the service.

Came with a friend after work. Great atmosphere place, hard to get a seat but not too long a wait. The table is communal which I love as we ended up making friends with two brits opposite and two Chicago guys next to us. Food is very meat centric as you would expect from a butchers shop cum restaurant but for once perfect sized portions and so so tasty. We had the pork belly with Pomegranete glaze, Lamb tartare and these brilliant Kanoodled pretzel things (pretezel smashed up, reformed and fried in butter, sounds odd but well worth trying). Waiters were also great and matched to the laid back cool of this place. Recommended.

I'm a fan and I'm all kinds of excited about being one of the first to review, but have these other people been to Craft? If they're going to be so educated on Colicchio and on top of new openings, get your stars straight! Craft is unbelievable and "as good as it gets", Riverpark is really good and "fan-worthy." Most notably, the service is great. There's something to be said about a great restauranteur who picks out good people for new ventures. From the moment that I made my first phone call to them, to being escorted to my table, to paying the bill--the service was excellent. Ambiance is also really nice and they do a good job of muffling the sounds from the FDR with good music. Most importantly, the food was delicious. You really can't go wrong with pork belly. YUM! Great steak frites off the bar menu and then tastily flavored seafood stew with the halibut. Nice drink selection and just continued good service. One downfall: bathroom in the big corporate office lobby outside the restaurant...

Yerba Buena is a small charming restaurant occupying what is little more than a storefront in Alphabet City. We visited on a slow cold night in December and were greeted with extraordinary courtesy and attention. The food - best described as "pan-latin", was creative and at the same time sufficiently familiar to make one feel comfortably at home. While everything we had was terrific, what stands out is the almost "old world" quality of the staff - rarely seen these days. Professional and attentive but not cloying or insistant. A real class act. We will return.

This review is solely for the fried dumplings. Given that there are no similar options in the area, this place is a great spot for super cheap eats - you can spend $5 or less for a filling lunch (or dinner). That's something that's rare ANYWHERE you go. That being said, their fried dumplings pale in comparison to other dumpling places, such as Vanessa's or Tasty Dumplings in the city. It seems that because they're so busy during lunch hours, the dumplings are already pre-fried and packaged in styrofoam boxes. While this makes for a less-than-a-minute wait for your food, the dumplings have lost their crispiness, and the juices have slightly congealed, meaning that you miss out on that drippy satisfaction from biting into a freshly fried dumpling. If you've got a craving for dumplings, I've been told that their steamed dumplings are better, so I would stick with those.

BEST RAMEN EVER. What the heck was Morimoto inhaling when he rated Momofuku Noodle #1 over Ippudo? I would gladly brave the 45 minute wait for a bowl of Akamaru (with extra pork belly + egg) and a pork Hirata bun. Bliss. Compared to its other ramen counterparts (Menchanko Tei, Momofuku, et al), Ippudo is far superior in ambience, decor, and most importantly, taste and flavor. Hands down, one of my favorite restaurants in NYC for its consistently excellent ramen. End point.

Ive been looking for new places to eat around my neighborhood and let me just say Queens Comfort is it!!! You might miss it or mistake it for something else if you dont pay attention. I loved the environment and my bf was overjoyed about the classic batman show that was playing. The food is bomb as hell!! I had the cap'n crunch french toast sticks... SOOOOO GOOOOOD!!! Melts in your mouth, such good flavor, great crunch I loved it. My bf had the breakfast burrito and he couldnt even finish it thats how much of a monster it is! I had the open face egg mcruffin which gave me life!! the cheese and thick chopped bits of bacon were divine. I cant wait to go back and feed my face some more!!

So, i'd have to say. This place lives up to the reputation. I went here with my husband about 3 weeks ago for dinner, and it was quite a pleasant experience. We were greeted seat in no time. The setting was pictures of comfortable, intimate, Â yet pulsating with energy of what a city like NYC has to offer. We started with some drinks, I had a bramble and my husband had an old fashioned (which he swears is the best he's ever had... Delicious)!. Then for appetizers, we had the ravioli and the beet salad which were outstanding. I had the chicken for a main course and was cooked to perfection. My husband had the scallops which melted in his mouth. Our waitress was an instrumental part of the experience because she was sweet, attentive, yet not intrusive. All in all it was an excellent evening, one I will repeat.
Dear God. Â I don't think I've ever had food this amazing in my life. Â Expensive as hell, but if you have the coin I highly recommend it.

I really have slipped off on my restaurant game recently but this place has restored my faith in the restaurant world once and for all. Their simple menu items are not to be mistakened for anything less than of a delicious dish. I came here with a couple friends for dinner and we ordered their infamous gnocchi and a lobster risotto special as starters. Both were delicious and beautifully presented. I've never been a huge fan of gnocchi, but this place does it well. I had the salmon as my main course and the fish was fresh and grilled lightly to greatness. The sauce, mushrooms and butternut squash complimented the dish beautifully. I really can't say much more but how great the food is- you would just have to try it for yourself. However, I can speak on behalf of the waitress that attended to our table and she was PERFECT. Of course many NYC restaurants nowadays provide you with a refillable water bottle on the table but only ONCE did I have to pick up the bottle and fill it for myself. The waitress still attended our drinks and met all our expectations. I can't wait to introduce this place to friends and family in the future.

One of my favorite food establishments in K-town... heck in New York City. Â I guess the concept is "fast-food Korean," but it's so much more than that. Â There's pre-made dishes (e.g. dduk-bbok-ee, bulgogi bab, kimbab) you can purchase for $3-4, a buffet bar where you can pay per lbs.(?), and even a small kitchen in the back with daily specials. Â I actually bought a soon-tofu meal for $6! Â It was no So-Kong-Dong, but it's probably the best bang for your buck. Â Also, it's a great pre-party spot if you just want to buy some sojus or beers and drink hassle-free for cheap... oh, and korean snacks for anjoo too!
If you're, 25-60, this place is great, good conversation, great place for both boring and spirited political talk, great bartender in the old Irish mold, some celebrity sitings too.

My husband and I were coming in for a matinee yesterday December 23, 2013. Of all the restaurants I researched online and called for reservations, Trat T was the best choice! Our reservations were for 6:30pm. We arrived to a very busy filled restaurant at 6:15. I got a spot at the bar amazingly while my husband waited in the long line to check in. Both the Hostess and Manager were very helpful, and with all the craziness and people trying for there attention, they were very pleasant. Â While we waited at the bar, a charming waiter suggested a delightful red wine to try which we were very happy with and bought a bottle for dinner. We didn't wait long to sit and the manager was very apologetic for the wait (even though it wasn't long at all, 20 min) The food was traditional Â Italian with some special chef dishes thrown in. I'm picky being 100% Italian and growing in in a very old school, everything is made from scratch household. So I'm a tough critic! This was great! Pasta's were cooked aldent..the sauces were delish and not runny or acidic at all! The waiter was attentive and very polite, like he was your friend for years! the manager was walking around to tables to make sure everyone was happy. The chef even came out a few times. We are DEF going back!!!!!!!
Vegetable dumplings are awesome. Really inexpensive but the space is really really tiny, but its good nonetheless.

For my first trip out to Brooklyn, I decided to go to Buttermilk Channel after hearing some good things about it. Â The wait was about an hour long, so I had high hopes. Â Unfortunately, I was disappointed. The place was loud- very loud. Â I found it a little difficult to hold a conversation over the noise. Â Atmosphere-wise, it wasn't anything spectacular, the usual dim lighting, some exposed brick but this part seemed a little out of place with the rest of the minimally decorated white walls. Service was...interesting. Â First of all, when I asked for a wine recommendation and told the waitress what kind of wine I liked, she said "I know exactly what wine to get you", and left the table without telling me what it was or anything about it. Â The wine itself was ok, not really what I was looking for. Â When I asked what her favorite things on the menu were, all she said was "Everything is good. Â But a lot of people order the chicken and waffles". Â She didn't really offer any helpful information or details. Â Later in the meal, when she handed us the dessert menu and I asked her what she recommended, she said she had never tried any of the desserts on the menu so she didn't know. Â Isn't it part of the waitstaff's job to be knowledgabel about the food the restaurant serves? On to the food: - Sweet potato and goat cheese croquettes: Â completely boring an unforgettable. Â Basically it was a fried ball of mashed sweet potato, without even a hint of goat cheese, or any other flavor. - Cheese plate: Â the cheese itself was pretty good, although we didn't really get an explanation of what they were, but the biggest issue was the bread that was served with it. Â It was completely charred! Â What kind of restaurant serves its customers burnt bread? - Fried chicken with cheddar waffles: Â The chicken itself was pretty good; moist, crispy skin, the way fried chicken should be, although I wouldn't say it was particularly memorable. Â The cheddar waffles it was served with was actually kind of cold. - Duck meatloaf: Â more of a duck patty than meatloaf, this was an amazing dish that I absolutely loved. Â Served on a bed of creamed spinach and topped with a large crispy onion ring, the flavor was incredible. Â I almost licked my plate clean. - Chocolate chip bread pudding: Â I was told it was served warm, but it actually arrived room temperature, with the top of it slightly warm. Â It was extremely dense and aside fromnt he bits of chocolate, it was kind of bland. Although I'm glad I went for the duck meatloaf, I definitely won't be back for another visit.

Made the trip from Long Island to meet friends from Staten Island who heard that this place was good. Ambiance-zero stars, crammed into a tiny table with very plain decor. Â They didn't carry my favorite wine, merlot, which is not an unusual wine to say the least. Â I ordered the duck. Â The presentation on the plate was very unappetizing. The duck was very dry, filled with bones which was embarassing to have to pick out of my teeth in front of my companions. Â The waitress never asked us during the meal if everything was okay, which it definitely wasn't. Â My friends ordered dessert which they seemed happy with, but after my abysmal experience with the entree I was afraid to order dessert. Â Prices were higher than average and I eat out regularly. Â Rock music was loud, jarring, not really in keeping with the theme of dining at Grandma's unless your grandma likes blasting music unsuitable for hearing your companions' conversation. Â My husband thinks they turned the music up at the end to get us to leave so that we would leave because the next sitting was supposed to start. Â When we got back to Long Island we threw together some food at home because we were very hungry. Â I have never written a restaurant review before but this place made me so annoyed I had to write this.

Food was great. A little better than I was expecting. Salmon Benedict was nice. Eggs were cooked properly and it was a bit smokey. Waffles were not overly sweet despite the syrup and banana brÃ»lÃ©e. Did take a while to get seated though.
I like Lombardi's just a tinsy bit better, but this place is still really good. The price isn't the greatest.

Viewing Million Dollar Jewelry at Christie's can work up an appetite. So I was off to a small hole in the wall restaurant on 10th Avenue, when I remembered that I bookmarked a recommendation from fellow Yelper Chris D. To be honest, I was just beat from walking those long avenues. Haha........ As I approached 9th Avenue, I found Istanbul Kebab House storefront with a couple of sandwich boards up front. It had daily specials and deals; like free soda from 2 to 5 PM every day of the week with purchase of sandwich. I was sold. As I walked in, there was this huge chunk of meat on a spit. Now I was ready to chow down. Stay out of my way since I love Gyros, Shawarma and Doner sandwiches. This is a very small place with 4 or 5 four top tables. It is decorated with Turkish period carpets on the wall and a TV playing background Turkish music. The place was very welcoming and wifey and I just felted right at home. We ordered one hummus as an appetizer and two Shawarma sandwiches. The hummus was creamy, cold and very tasty. It came with a basket of pita, side of Turkish hot sauce and yogurt base sauce. Lots of flavor here when you dip pita in different sequence of items or sauces. Very nice. The Shawarma is one of the BEST in NYC. A definite top 5 in my book. It was moist with flavor and a spice profile from the Middle East that was just delicious. All the components was perfectly prepared. The ratio of meat to pita to veggies to sauce was just perfect. Just writing this I could taste the flavor of the lamb with that spicy Turkish sauce. Ouch! Good............... This is a must place for Gyros. If you appreciate a good Shawarma sandwich make the trip to 9th Avenue, you will not be disappointed. This is a must destination place for this style of food. Wonderful................

Very cool spot with a unique feel. Â It is a bit narrow though, but that's also one of the things that makes it what it is. Â We ordered some prosciutto, dates stuffed with goat cheese, capresse salad, risotto, and wine. Everything was good, including the service, except for the risotto. Overall we enjoyed the stay and look forward to coming back and trying other stuff on the menu.

Best late night snack ! Cheap and good ! Empanadas: Jumbo Italiano, Americans, TJC ( spicy tuna melt), Cuban and Romeio and Juliet ( sweet one with Guava Sauce and cheese :))))) Guacamole is really good as well ~ with banana chips
Only been here for brunch and it was fab. Waiting to test out their dinner.
Best invention ever created! I'm completely obsessed. I get the baked sweet potato with bacon and load it up with all the veggies possible. Mouthwatering good! And a very solid cheap find for NYC
This place is really simple and clean. I had the cuban sandwich which was very good, maybe a tad too greasy. Seating is limited. Staff was very friendly.

Love Almond - Go here maybe once every two weeks. I'm biased and live on the street but anyway its a great spot for dinner or brunch. The menu changes every season so you can always find something new!

I am no ramen expert but these were the best noodles...ever. Came here on a Friday after work, the wait time for 2 people at 6pm was 30 mins.. The waiting area is practically non existent so be prepared to stand really close to everyone else.The dining area is also ridiculously small. The pork buns are such a must. Unbelievable how good these things are. The bun alone is so soft and melts in your mouth. The pork is delicious. I also had the modern ramen with the miso paste and a boiled egg. The bowl was huge and the broth was amazing. The broth was so good that when the noodles are done, you must just pick up the bowl and drink whatever is left. So good, so so good. So filling! I will definitely come back here for a ramen fix. Would never bring a large party though. I think the best bet is during an off time or early evening.
Super good authentic sushi without the nonsense rolls. Â Go!!

This place is great. I usually get the grilled steak or chicken ranchero burrito, but they sometimes have special burritos that are cheaper (barbecue pork or mole) and those are awesome, too. Their salsa is phenomenal, and they always give free chips and salsa with to-go purchases, as well as free chips if you decide to stay there. I've tried the tostada salad, which is pretty good.

hands down best place to go for late night and some good ol' shawarma. i will never forget the first time i came to this jewel of a place. after a long day of walking around the city and chilling in the evening at fat cat (nearby pool hall/jazz/bar), i was pretty ready for some late night food. came into the restaurant, not expecting much, and got the shawarma sandwich, as i tend to stick to the basics when visiting an unfamiliar restaurant for the first time. needless to say, i immediately fell in love with the first bite. not to mention the hot sauce, which seriously must have crack in it or something, or else why would i keep wanting it with every bite despite the fact that it was making me hiccup from extreme spiciness?! anyways, back the the sandwich- the lamb was so tender and juicy, and everything in the sandwich was fresh and tasty that i am currently salivating as i am writing this review and cant wait to go back and get myself another one of those damn sandwiches

Good authentic cuban food is harder to find then one would believe. Most Cuban resturants I've been to in the city are more cuban fusion than they are truly authentic, and while that's doesn't mean the food is bad, sometimes I just get a craving for my abuela's Â palomilla. This place is pretty authentic. My twin sis and I came here for a nice meal, that wasn't too expensive and we throughly enjoyed ourselves. We actually both ordered the palomilla, mine with maduros, hers with tostones. both also came with blackbeans and rice. Our steaks were perfect. the onions have a great flavor and the olive oil they used was really tasty. The black beans were flavored a bit differently then I am used to, but they were nonetheless delicious. For dessert we split the tres leches, and both had cafe con leche's. seriously this was great cuban food. There is so much on the menu that I want to get next time I go, that I'll probably become a regular. the decor and atmosphere was great, and it even had a little window for drinks and snacks like all the real cuban restaurants in cuba and miami. go to this restaurant. you will not be disappointed.

The food is very good, and at these reasonable prices an excellent deal. The drink specials, from unlimited Sangria brunch to Mojito Madness Mondays ($5 Mojitos), make this a great destination for fun gatherings. Above all, the service is stellar! Twice I've been here with challenging parties (one, a group of 16 all drinking for brunch, and the other a party of 12 where 6 canceled only a few minutes before the reservation time) and both times experienced gracious, friendly service from waiters who really made the whole experience. I really like the food. I really like the drinks. I really like the prices. I LOVE the service and the big group-friendly set up. Highly recommend, especially for large groups.

very cosy and romantic place... flowers everywhere ;-) and nice food as well. the mussels in white wine sauce were excellent. reasonable pricing and charming service. be aware - reservations only from 6 person on...

I have a feeling that this won't happen again, because the food is so great it can't stay a secret for long!! We walked in at 8:30pm and sat at a table in the front window. Our waitress, Khadija, was really friendly and informative when we had annoying questions about the specials, spice details and what the exact pieces of chicken would be etc. The manager, Ally (I hope I spelled it correctly) was super friendly as well, and came by our table to see how everything went. We ended up ordering the Mike's hot honey fried chicken in combination with the lemon honey butter and spiced pecan waffle. The flavors were amazing, the chicken was nice and crispy. A side of creamy and rich (but not overly salty or excessively cheesy) delicious mac and cheese and a jalapeÃ±o cheddar corn muffin were just enough for both of us. We had just enough room for the special dessert, warm raspberry and biscuit bread pudding topped with a scoop of vanilla ice cream! Great experience overall, would definitely go back soon to try some of the other combos!

Wow. This place is BAD! Whoever rates this more than 1 or 2 stars has no taste buds, or is able to taste something that isn't there. I went with 2 friends last night, and we literally ordered one of each item off the menu. Everything tasted exactly the same -- bland. REALLY BLAND. The fish tacos? Bland. The flautas? Bland. The torta? Bland. The everything else? Bland. A few exceptions to the bland rule: Â 1. The steak was not bland. It had the flavor of about a pound of salt. 2. The flan. WTF? It was the consistency of a really thick sponge. And super hard. If you want mexican food, please go somewhere else. Like any other restaurant. (edited to include the fact that the margaritas were pretty terrible as well)

I live in the neighborhood and have been Alice's for breakfast, lunch, dinner and to get food from their prepared food takeaway counter. The room is beautiful, large, open, airy with skylights and very charming repurposed salvage from old buildings. The food is excellent, fresh, lots of choices, daily specials, simply prepared, easy to understand dishes, not too quirky or kooky. The service from the waitstaff to the management to the chef, who will come and talk to you, is impeccable. Â Friendly, attentive, extremely accommodating. If you had a bad dining experience here you probably won't be happy anywhere..

I'm reviewing WE as a seafood market not as a restaurant. After the ammonia-infested shrimp that they sold me as "fresh" shrimp for $18.99 / lb last night, there is no way in hell I'm ever going back here. Â I always hear never to order fish from a restaurant on Monday nights, but I had no idea that held true for seafood markets. Â Especially a seafood market that I'd consider to be one of the more legit ones around here. I'm just disgusted and annoyed.

What a great wine bar with awesome food! My dad and I went last night and sat in the cute little outside garden in the back. Shared a great bottle of red wine reccommended by our waiter in our price range, and ordered a bunch of dishes to try. The crostini were my favorite, especially the cheese and sundried tomato and the artichocke and mint. Later after we digested and got to talking we ordered a trio of cheese and meat plates. The cheese the waiter suggested was delicious and the salami with hot spicy oil on top of it was really tasty! The ambience was great with the massive marble bar and baskets of fruit everywhere. We will definitely be back very soon!

In terms of pizza quality, this place is up there. Â  Â The crust is good, thin and crisp. The sauce is done well - tastes freshly made with a very clear, as opposed to tart tomato flavor. Â  Cheese is fresh bufala mozzarella. Â  Perhaps it could use a more liberal sprinkle of basil. Â  Pie wise, it actually comes close in taste to my personal fave, Lucali but doesn't quite achieve that restaurant's perfect tomato/mozzarella ratio. Â  Â It still is quite tasty, though, and I prefer it over Keste. The establishment, as noted, won't set records for service, but heck, this is a glorified pizza parlor so realistic expectations should be in order. Â  Â  I came on a non-peak night so things came out relatively quick for me. Â  Downside is the prices are rising, whether due to demand or rising price of ingredients or whatnot....up to $17 for a personal (12") bufala pie, fancier ones are in the low $20's...

Wow. Cheap! Great large fried dumplings (these are thick skinned not like the wonton dumplings or gyoza) 4/$1?!? Â The sesame pancake sandwiches are also large and cheap. Tried the duck filled one and it was tasty. Fast service.

Tiny dining area with crammed in customers, bumping elbows....and yet....you will still find smiles on all the diners' faces. Â That's because this place serves up some pretty delicious dishes. Â  They're quick, efficient, friendly enough. Â Tried their lobster special and I'd have to say...how delightful. Â The seasonings were just perfect, light, tasty, super affordable. Â Try one of their flavored asian teas to compliment your meal.

Good news! Their kitchen closes at 1130 or later on Saturdays! Â  Bc we rolled in around 1045 and they were happily still seating and serving. Got the staple items of the sashimi tuna (with the delish pink sea salt) and the spaghetti. Â We came in famished and just devoured everything from the bread basket to the entree. Â Scarpetta definitely does it right... even down to splitting the pasta into 2 dishes for us and serving them like adorable little nests of delicious spaghetti. Â  I make it a point to come here every few months... bc it's just that wonderful.

Very happy with our dinner and drinks here. Â Unreal selection of whiskey. Â  We had a fun group of 6 there last weekend and they treated us right with booze and tasty food. Â Hot tip - get the whiskey and rye deal on the dinner menu right now! Â 9 bucks for a pint of great beer and an ounce of bourbon. I had the pork chop - perfect. Â My friend across from me had the shrimp - delicious. Â Another companion had the fish and it was cooked just right. Â  Come for the whiskey, stay for the food and enjoy yourself.

OK, so the wait was unbearable (45 minutes out in the scorching sun!). Â The pizza we'd ordered came to us very late - later than people that came after us. Â When it finally came, the pizza was.... good - but not the best. Â  My friend and I decided to take it out and enjoy it at the park nearby with a view of the city skyline. Â If it weren't for the lovely summer day and my good company, I don't think the pizza would've been anything too special to remember...

We tried this place on a whim just because it was close to our location and the reviews looked nice. Boy were we surprised. The food was amazing. It was cozy and had such a welcoming atmosphere. We will definitely return on our next trip back to NYC.

If your in a rush and in the area which has mostly "sit down" places along 9th Ave.... this could be a quick bite. Don't get it twisted , this is not an authenctic Mexican taqueria in Hell's Kitchen . This is strictly a take-out joint with Americanized burritos and tacos. It's def not a food destination by any means , just a "lets get sumthin quick cuz I'm starving and we are in Hell's Kitchen" kind of place. Not bad ...but then again nothing special

the smith is consistently good, and they turnover fast, which means i am not waiting a long time to get a table during a weekend brunch .. the vanilla bean french toast is def the way to go, especially when you split this sweet dish with something savory ...... also, a Â fun, hip scene .. i also enjoy eating at their bar, which is long, spacious .. highly recommend this place !

Been here twice. Â The food disappointed both times. Â It wasn't bad, just, not great. Â I would give it two stars, except that the look & feel of the place is perfect, which made me like it despite the disappointing food. Menu items tried: - the duck curry entree whose name I don't recall - okay - the jungle curry chicken rice thing - very bland (granted, I asked for the spice to be toned down a bit, so this might have been my own fault) - the steamed veggie dumplings - more like peanut dumplings, interesting and peanut-sweet, but I wouldn't order them again - the crispy tofu - actually, pretty good. Â And I don't even like tofu much. There's more but nothing that really stands out. Service was very friendly, if a bit confused. In Pure's defense,and to argue against my own review, I feel I should note that... A) A lot of foodies I know really like this place, and B) I went here shortly after a trip to Thailand, and pretty much all Thai food tastes like nothing, after you've been there and had it fresh. Â  So... I will go back and give them another shot. Â It's a cute place with lots of fans.

My group of 6 dined at Jolie Cantina for brunch on New Years Day, and it was a great experience. Â I was able to make a reservation at 11AM for a 12PM seating, which I appreciated. Â I ordered their croque madame, which came with fries & a salad that were not at all an afterthought on the entree. Â Everything was great and I regret being unable to finish my fries! Â Others in my party ordered the steak sandwich, crab benedict, Jolie omelette, pancakes, and their burger - everyone raved about their meal and said it was the best one they'd had in awhile. It can be a little noisy in Jolie Cantina, but I found the music volume to fluctuate. Â When they music wasn't loud enough so that I couldn't speak to my friends, I was a little ticked (maybe because I was also hungover?), but then - miraculously - the volume was turned down and I could hear again! Â Another diner must've said something, for which I am grateful. I highly recommend Jolie Cantina for brunch since that's the only meal I've dined there for, but considering how much everyone loved their meal, and not only 'brunchy' items were ordered, I'd also recommend for dinner.

Have you ever wondered what a $17 quesadilla tastes like? According to this place, it tastes slightly worse than the $5 one you get at your local Mexican joint. But the quesadilla was the best thing about my experience here. The drinks are overpriced to the point that whoever runs this place might actually be delusional enough to think he/she runs a place that people want to go to/have heard of/care about. By comparison, The waitstaff makes the North Korean army seem friendly and like they have their sh*t together. Amazing how people in the service industry can be so confrontational and rude. Literally never seen anything like it in the world, let alone in a New York restaurant/bar/lounge for overweight tourists/whatever this dump is trying to be. Especially if they're serving $17 quesadillas. Looking forward to this place's inevitable closing in the next few months and the subsequent Chipotle/Whole Foods that will open on the site. At least the staff their is trained to be civil to their customers.

Love the decor and chandeliers and mirrors.. Fast service..had the coconut juice..flat noodle with chicken nice and spicy.. Pad thai was nice too..loved the whole energy of the place ..would definitely Go there on next Friday night.

If your in the UWS the place to go for Greek food would be here. Large restaurant with a downstairs and upstairs. Decor is standard and doesn't wow you and even with a reservation prepare for a bit of a wait. You come here for the greek food. Great apps with hummus and yogurt and their Octopus was grilled perfectly. Had the pressed chicken and it was made great and very flavorful with a bit of crunch from the pressing. If in the area i would stop in again.

I am a huge fan of Jeffrey's Grocery..so since these are the same owners, I figured that I would love this restaurant just as much. Â Based on the food alone, I would probably give 3 stars, but based on service and treatment, 2 stars is being generous. To make a long story short, I walked in with 3 girls without reservations. There was a bit of a misunderstanding with the seating so the Host (so we thought) offered us a free round of wine. When we received our bill, we noticed that the round of wine was on the bill, so we politely told the waiter about the host's offer and questioned him about it. Welllllll, that was a mistake. A big debate ensued.. with the waiter, then the bartender, then the manager, then the host, then the waiter again, and then the manager again. All this for a round of 3 glasses of wine? If we truly misunderstood the host's offer (although I really cant see how all 3 of us misunderstood), so be it. Â The manager or host should have said to our faces, "Sorry girls, you're mistaken" and kept it moving. The back and forth debate and snide looks between the miserable female manager and host went on MUCH longer than it should have. It was so embarrassing..for them of course. Â  Also, we didn't get seated at a table. We ate at the bar which was really uncomfortable. Not an enjoyable dining experience...the bar area was a bit packed and the restaurant is teeny tiny. The food was pretty good though. Not thrilling in my opinion, but good.
The best food and people! it's the kind of food that makes you roll your eyes and moan!

After so many good reviews, I was so disappointed to have a bad experience at Penelope. The waiter acted as though it was an imposition to wait on us from the second we sat down. I ordered the pumpkin waffles, which arrived cold, but that's not too surprising given that it took a half an hour to get our food. I was a waitress at one time in my life so I can forgive a lot, but cold food and an attitude problem are not among them.
I really liked brunch here -- they make a simply excellent fried oyster po-boy. nice service -- responsive and let us linger. Â plus, the bathrooms smell nice.

My bf and I have driven past this place a million times and although it's easy to miss among the slew of restaurants on Metropolitan, every time I see it I'm like, "oh yeah, we should try that place!" Â Nothing about the restaurant's facade or awning grabs your eye except for the fact that it's states Lebanese Cuisine. Â That alone had sparked my interest as a lover of all things Mediterranean. The decor is simple but cute. Â The menu for lunch is very descriptive and explanatory for those new to the cuisine. Â And if you still don't get it, the waiter is there to help with answers and good suggestions. For appetizers we got a meat pie, a cheese pie, and the fattoush (a fresh, citrus-y salad). Â The fattoush was huge even to share and the waiter later told us we were impressive since it's their biggest app. Â We went to town on that thing! Â The meat pie was seasoned with cinnamon and paprika, and was delicious and hearty even if it was just a few bites. Â The cheese pie just tastes like the definition of comfort food. Â I was expecting more of a spinach pie-type pastry (a la greco) but I was more than satisfied with their take on it. For my main I got a lamb shawerma platter with a side of tabouleh and okra. Â And before I continue can I just say the fact that you're allowed not one, but TWO sides for your meat platter is just extremely charitable of them as their portions are large. Â My bf and I were able to try more of the menu this way while filling our bellies to the brim. Â Both the lamb and chicken from our shawerma platters were juicy and delicious. The okra and mujadarah were also superb! Â Absolutely nothing bad to say about this place, and everyone else in there seemed like regulars. Â I hope to be one of them in a week! Everything about this place screams homemade and authentic. Â Just come hungry, make room for baklava, and be prepared for leftovers!
Food was good. Staff was nice but....... Music was way too loud and it's annoying to have to raise your voice just to order lunch. It's a restaurant not a club.

I've wanted to try Champs for a long time. Fortunately I had the time to do so. I had the southern biscuits and gravy as I'm always trying to find ways to tweak my recipe at home. The biscuits were good, not outstanding. The gravy was too salty for my taste, but that's not uncommon. I had some pretty darn good iced coffee as well. It wasn't the usual burnt coffee bean iced coffee so many chains have. You could actually taste some decent notes. The atmosphere is quirky in a good way, with an abundance of hipsters. The staff is very friendly, with fast service. I'd return as there are lots of great looking items on the menu.
This place is trash. I would get better service in a dumpster. The food is disgusting. The place is cramped. The bitch who served us was the rudest bitch I ever met.

I visited Ilili for a late lunch. Â I sought it out based on Yelp reviews and I wasn't disappointed. Â My party had three entrees. Â Mine was tile fish (they were out of bass on the menuu). Â The entrees and sides were fantastic. Cooked to perfection...just the right amount of spice and flovoring so as not to overwhelm. Â Well done. We also ordered desert to go as we had an appointment to get to. Â Definitely a return trip when we are in the area again. Â On the pricey side, but the quality justifies it.

I can understand why people love this place(cheap, good portions) but I've had much better dumplings in my life. I guess that's because I'm Asian and my mom spoiled me with awesome homemade dumplings growing up. The sesame pancake with duck is pretty good. This a good spot for a cheap meal. I routinly come back here because it's so close to where I live and the prices are unbeatable. However the wait time kinda sucks and seating is pretty limited.

Came here last weekend because all the hypes from yelp. Â Unfortunately couldn't buy it. We ordered beef pan fried noodle and a vegi dish. Â The vegi dish was ok. Â It doesn't taste that fresh though. Â The pan fried noodle was massive. Â But the noodle was not crispy at all and the beef was very hard to chew. Â We ordered the soy sauce chicken as some yelpers recommended. Â It was a so-so.. All in all, if you want a cheap big Cantonese dish. Â This is the place. Â But don't give too much expectations. Â I'd prefer New Wonton Garden for the same kind of food.

Zagat Award? Check. Yelp favorite? Check. New York Magazine, NY Times, Time Out New York, Village Voice Article, and Frank Bruni recommended? Check, Check, Check, Check and Check! Really? Are you serious? This can't be right. I ordered exactly what this place was known for, Kamonan (duck and scallion) with soba noodles. First thing I noticed was that it was covered in oil. Then I tried the soup. It was sour. The scallions? Raw. The slices of duck? Bingo, at least they did something right. The nabeyaki udon dish however, was done right. The soup was intricately flavored, the udon was cooked to the perfect consistency and the whole dish was nicely presented. I'm tempted to come back and try the cold soba dishes and hoping that tonight was just a fluke.

Bean and lentil soup is just a colored water soup. Â I had to protest as I know what beans and lentils look like and they just insisted it's pureed. Â Really? Â I don't think so. Â Asked for my money and they did. Â  Skip this place! Such a disappointment after trekking there after such decent reviews!

This place is OK. The decor is nice, nothing fancy or trendy and very small and crowded. The staff is very friendly. The hummus and the bread is delicious. I ordered a kind of a grilled chicken plate and it was awful, very but very dry and cold that was really bad. when I complain they nicely took the plate out of the bill and offered other choices but I was turned off and didn`t want anything else. Just wanted to keep the good taste of the hummus and bread. My friends they ordered the vegetarian mazze plate and some kind of lamb plate and it was very good. I guess I got the wrong plate that night. I definitely will go back to try for second time but there are other great Turkish restaurants in the City.

A little overpriced for what it is, but still delicious. A sandwich will cost you around ~$10, but they are pretty average sized. I had the award winner which was great, friend had turkey. Turkey sandwich has a lot of turkey in it so is pretty worth the price. Must try fried chicken and tater tots next time.

My boyfriend and I came here for a late dinner after having watched Cinderella on Broadway. We wanted to try a variety of things at least so we ordered the carpaccio di manzo, the trecolori, and the linguini nere alla monsignore. The carpaccio di manzo (raw slices of filet mignon, arugula salad, roasted peppers, fresh slices of parmesan cheese) was very tasty. The roasted peppers give it added flavor, and I really enjoyed it. Keep in mind it is raw and very thinly sliced, but as a salad, it is pretty filling nonetheless. The trecolori was a dish of cured meats and cheeses. I really enjoy eating meats and cheeses especially when I have wine, so I was quick to pick this item to order. There was a lot more cheese than meat though, because the cheese was cut thick - it resembled the shape of a string cheese - maybe a little bigger and the cheese alone could have filled you up. As for the meats - there were about 4 different meats, 2 slices of each at least and I wish there had been more. Â The linguine nere alls monsignore is the seafood with squid ink pasta. The restaurant took the liberty of splitting the dish for us without us even asking. When they first brought it out for us, we thought they mistakenly heard our order and gave us two orders of the pasta, but when the bill came later we realized they just split one order for us so we each had a plate of it to make things easier. Let me tell you for $22, you get more than what you paid for. The trecolori and carpaccio were about the same price for what I feel was less. Â One half of it alone had the right amount of pasta and a decent amount of seafood (more than I would have expected - an assortment of shrimp, mussels, clams, squid). The squid ink pasta was something different I had never had, and it was really good. I was just so full after the trecolori and carpaccio, I couldn't finish my pasta - but it was good! definitely a must try. The staff here is very attentive and nice and very polite. They are always checking up on you to see if you're doing okay, and quick to clear empty plates and dishes to lessen the clutter.
Get the hog, or anything else. Everything I've had so far is excellent.

I love this place! I really felt I was part of history coming here. The cozy dining area is full of historical significance (damage to the wall from bombing attempt), charm from the colonial period, and mystery as this was George Washington's place of politic/military business and watering hole. Â And extra bonus- the food was fantastic (at least what I ordered)! Most historical landmarks cover up their food with all their folklore, tales, and list of famous patrons to create that "experience" that people come to receive upon their visit. You get all that here, PLUS GREAT FOOD! True, I'm a huge American History buff, and I can talk for days about the JFK assassination, but I digress. Could I have been affected by the smokescreen secondary to this historical landmark tavern? Perhaps. But I suppose you need to visit for yourself and make your own determination. This is DEFINITELY one of those places you take outside visitors to NYC for the first time. Of note, go there early in the month; they have very limited complimentary tickets to the museum upstairs when you dine at the Tavern and usually run out quick. Of course, free for you and guest with Military ID. OOHRAW!!

The Best Pizza EVER! Â  Get the sausage and pepperoni, you will die and go str8 to heaven Â after you eat it... Just look @ my pic, I freakin live in that place... Thank you Ralph for the great service....

Great, authentic Chinese food and very inexpensive. I was stuffed and full paying only $2.50. Unfortunately they are closed right now for remodeling and won't open until beginning of 2008. I like the place, a classic hole-in-the wall in the truest sense. 5 stars.

This place makes me happy! Â I enjoy the atmosphere. Really laid back. I wouldn't mind so much standing up to eat if i had to. Its like eating at like a fair or something. Lots of people to watch. I had a cheeseburger thinking it would just be something to put in my stomach, but I ended up loving it. I like that char grilled taste. Also, the frozen mojitos are nice. Perfectly sweet. I'll be back again soon for the corn.

Fabulous BBQ with succulent ribs and great beer selections. I'd give it 5 stars, but after a certain hour the line to get into this place extends down the block and I'm not waiting an hour and a half for anything or anyone - come on folks, at some point you should consider that there are plenty of other great options out there too where you don't have to follow the crowd like a lemming!

Just OK, the staff is nice and the food is okay. Nothing really special, but I like the reading material if I am alone at my table, and the breakfast food is correct. OK if you need a warm cup of hot chocolate or tea in a cold afternoon but nor worth going out of your way.
Good Sandwiches and great Coffee.

53rd and 6th has been one of New York's Famous stops. i've been going to this place now for the last 6 years. its not to die for or something you have to try before you die :-P. its very cheap and you get your money`s worth! the food is very tasty and you must try the while sauce on anything. I sometimes take it home and use it on other things ( confessions ) the line could extended forever and that's why there is another on the other side of the street. its the same exact thing. Bottom line : its definitely one place i miss since i moved to California

How happy was I to finally go here, on a rainy and cold April day? VERY. I just wanted everything, so I got half of everything, namely; sweet and spicy cucumber salad, with hunks of crisp cucumber swimming in a slightly spicy sesame-y soy sauce- two dollars, good enough for two 4 panfried pork and chive dumplings-tasty, fresh, and perfect with some of the not too vinegary dumpling sauce and a hit of sriracha-one dollar boiled vegetable dumplings-these my friend got-mild and savory-around two dollars for a mess of 'em sesame pancake sandwich with peking duck, carrot and cucumber-a hefty two dollars and twenty five cents-nice, but a little heavy. But maybe that's because I mowed all the aforementioned treats first. OH, and iced tea-housemade-sweet and so pleasant-kind of red-beany sweet. Dunno how much it was, but I can tell you it didn't break the bank!

First off, let's talk about how the bathroom smells and feels like a camp lodge hot sauna/relaxation room. It's comfortably warm and it smells like a pine forest. I forgot I was in NYC for a second! Okay, now onto the food. They have a good selection of domestic beer on tap and in cans. The price tag may seem high, but wait until you try the variety of waffles, chicken, and southern inspired appetizers and sides. Then check out the dessert menu. This place has a great feel, really friendly staff, and is an all over nice place to grab dinner!

Everything I've ever had here was amazing. From the food to the service. I can cosign on the fried chicken, shrimp & grits, biscuits (YUMMY), grilled corn and 6 out of their 7 daily free cookies. My only complaint is that the portion of the shrimp and grits has changed. The $12 bowl is laughably a snack. It's barely an appetizer. BUT....it's still a damn good for Â 5 tablespoon of grits and 3 shrimp dish.

It is unfortunate that I chose to come here on a really cold night, hungry and as my first food choice in New York. After walking for blocks from my hotel on canal, I decided to come here because I had bookmarked it and it was "walking distance" from my hotel. Well, it wasn't as close as I thought, we were pretty tired and hungry, and this hole in the wall (literally a hole in the wall) "restaurant" if you can even call it that, is hidden in an obscure alley in Chinatown. The place was so small and cramped, we couldn't even go inside, and it was freezing outside, so i decided to order to go. It seemed that the cashier wanted to hurry things up and I felt pressured to order and hurry along since the space was so limited. So I ordered the popular items, and I watched as they bathed my meal in grease, and packaged it all up in a matter of seconds, except for the wait for my vegetable dumplings which apparently are uncommon and took more time to prepare. So I was so hungry I ended up eating my meal outside as I walked to my hotel because I didn't want it to get cold. Yes, the food is pretty cheap, but in this case I'd rather have quality over quantity. Too greasy, too fast and the restaurant space/environment is terrible. I'm only giving this place 3 stars because I was so hungry and it was so cold, that it was somewhat of a relief to eat something hot, even if I felt like crap afterwards for eating so quickly. Bottom line, it is not worth the effort to come here, as "authentic" as they claim to be, doesn't necessarily make them the best tasting.

I want one of these by my house in San Francisco. A perfect spot to grab a quick lunch. Considering all the Indian food I've eaten over the past few years, I was surprised to learn a kati roll is a common snack. Anyway, great flavors, I thought two rolls was a perfect sized lunch, though could be a touch large for some. I'd recommend asking for some chili paste as the flavors are great but not too spicy. I will be back for lunch every time I'm in town.

This became my go to place when I moved to NY from Cali. It's the spot for shawerma and falafel - both great sandwiches. It's more of a grab a bite and go kind of place. Some of the staff from ten years ago is still there and they're always very friendly and helpful.

This place is great for a NYC brunch. The restaurant is quite trendy and had a good ambiance. I would recommend their lemon ricotta pancakes and fried chicken & waffles. However, I didn't think there was anything too special about the Mac Attack (a little pricey for mac n cheese). The waiter was very nice, prices were a little high (but manageable), and overall a good experience. The only problem was that there was a lot of uncontrollable outside noise from cabs and cars. Update 3/30/10: Meatloaf (with mashed potatoes and Â green beans) were oh so good...

Yelp really let me down on this one. Â The words "over-hyped," "unremarkable," "unimpressive" are what come to mind when I think of Pates Et Traditions. After reading all the stellar reviews we were initially pretty excited to walk into this little restaurant to find an open table for two. Â  After doing our research we ordered the seemingly most Yelped about items on the menu. Socca -Some sort of bread which turned out to taste like some kind of really greasy salty carbohydrate that someone might improvise on a camping trip. Â I considered sending it back because it was so salty, but we didn't want to get off on the wrong start with the waitstaff so we slowly nibbled on it until we could politely discard it when the entrees came. Shrimp curry crepe - This was nothing special. Â It was neither good nor particularly bad; merely just edible. Â I think it is tacky that they use small frozen shrimp in the crepe. Â It should not be difficult to get fresh shrimp. Â  Onion, fig, goat cheese crepe - Meh, whats the big deal. Â Again neither good nor particularly bad. Â The goat cheese was at least mild. I'm really perplexed why the majority of the Yelp reviews are raving about this place. Â It's very over-hyped. The crepes are completely forgettable. Â  With so many excellent options to eat in nyc, williamsburg etc. I never plan on returning nor would I recommend this place to anyone. Â  It's not a bad meal, but again I found to be very average food with above average ambiance. Â The restaurant does have a cozy feel.

Obviously not much has changed in my opinion here, but I did want to comment upon the tasting menu -- which my group of 5 indulged in last night; it was absolutely divine. At first we thought that there is no way in hell that the small plates brought to us one by one could feed us all, but the cumulative effect of the 11 courses really does add up to a satisfying amount of food. The chef's selection is excellent, and at $40 a pop it's really worth it to give the tasting menu a shot if you haven't already tried a good deal of their menu. Just note that everyone at the table has to participate, and the tasting menu is for a minimum of 3-person parties. Also, their key lime pie is the best I have ever had.

Taim serves the best falafel on Earth. That includes the falafel in Israel. That includes the falafel anywhere the human beings exist. This is a fact, not an opinion. It would be impossible for a better falafel to exist than what Einat Admony and her team serve at Taim. The space is tiny, the lines are huge, and there is almost no seating, but who cares? You'll be so overjoyed after one bite that you won't care. Taim does a better job of layering their sandwiches than any place I've ever visited. You don't get all toppings on the top and dry falafel on the bottom. Every comes together in harmony -- the falafel, the cabbage, the Israeli salad, the impossible hummus and the spectacular hot sauce. If you can get a seat, I like going with one of the platters, which are giant and unreal. The mixed platter lets you try all three flavors of falafel. The harissa is my favorite. I also love the sabich -- but it's so hard to pull myself away from that chickpea goodness.

I visited Ippudo Westside and enjoyed a wonderful lunch experience. Â  Started with the Shishito pepper appetizer. Â Nice flavor ... and I do enjoy my veggies. For the main course I ordered the Akamaru. Â  According to my wait person, Â the Akamaru is both the most popular as well as her favorite ramen dish. Â It comes with a delicious broth and ramen (of course!) Some finely sliced scallion and oh-so-tender slices of pork. Â Yum!! I am eager to try the other dishes on Ippudo's menu for future visits.

Work right next door, and frequent Peaches at least once a week. I highly recommend the Brunch Punch to drink, and either the Cobb salad, french toast, or turkey meatloaf to eat. Sweet potato fries and grits are great. I've never ordered anything that I haven't liked. My coworkers report the same experience.

I made a reservation at Verlaine's for my sister's last night in NYC after reading reviews on Yelp. The deadly Lychee martinis intrigued me and at $5, how could I say no?! Our waitress was super sweet, especially since we were 40 minutes late to our reservation. However, as the night progressed they forgot a couple of our drinks. . Everything they say about the Happy Hour cocktails are true. The bartenders are heavy handed and though it may not seem strong first, after 2...ok, 6 of them you'll be stumbling out of the club (like I did). The food was good, but nothing to really rave about. No dance space here, but since Fat Baby is right next door they don't need it. Solid spot to start the night off at.

Went there for drinks and bites with my co-workers!!! Loved the Riesling from Mosel they have on their wine list. We shared the Wings, Tuna Crudo, Cauliflowers and Brussel Sprouts--they were all amazing. I highly recommend the wings--by far the best I've had in years!! Tuna was bite-sized but tasted great. Cauliflowers and Brussel Sprouts were refreshing and quite unique. Loved the decor and the ambiance.

Went there again with 2 friends on Tuesday evening. I wonder why it took me one year to go to the Boil again! It was still as delicious as I remembered! It was the first time for my friends, and they absolutely loved everything! Definitely the best seafood restaurant!

This is one of the BEST Halal carts in Manhattan. Think about it. Almost 2000 people decided that it was a good use of time to post a review on Yelp for a... Â food cart? Â Yes, and most of the reviews are 5 stars. Unfortunately, I live 2 hours away from this wonderful food cart. But, whenever I am in the city, I always try to get some food there. It's cheap. It's quick. It's delicious :)

Went for dinner. Â Had a very nice time. Â The food was delicious. Â  Appetizer: Filet mignon carpaccio, asiago cheese, truffled mushrooms. The carpaccio just comes from together as you pick it up with your fork; very tasty. Entrees: Bistrot steak frites with a red wine thyme sauce, glazed shallots. You don't realize it at first, but it's pre-cut into perfect little bite-sized morsels. Duck confit with crispy potatoes, wild mushrooms and frisee salad. Very good; the sauce they used tasted amazing. I'll have to try their brunch sometime!
Not my favorite sushi experience ever, plus I do not like being rushed through a meal. Â  However, the Ikura was incredible, the Hotate and the Mirugai excellent.

Yum-O! Everything we had was a delicious!!! Homemade pasta was to die for, and we loved the octopus appetizer. What's great is that I came with two other people, and the split up each entree so that all of us could taste each dish. That was a huge plus!
If you know me, you know I love this spot. I wish they delivered.

I went here thinking it was going to be very similar to AA Plaza (in Flushing). There are much fewer choices here, but what they do have, they do it well. I have been here multiple times and I can get stuffed for $4! The dumplings are 5/$1. Unbeatable!!! Pretty cool how they don't really burn 'em considering how many are going at once. These taste good on their own, but even better with a little hot sauce and soy sauce. I once got the boiled dumplings, because somebody ordered 300 fried dumplings right before I came in. The boiled ones are just not as good. The place is usually packed, so I eat at this mini-park outside of an apartment complex... there are a few benches and it's less than a block away. The beef pancake is very filling but it's just aite. I feel the meat is too chewy and the star anise flavor is a little overpowering. If you've never had it, try it, it's affordable. Hopefully you'll like it more than I did. Dumplings are 5/5 stars Beef Pancake is 3/5 stars If you're nearby, even if you're full, just drop by for "$1 of dumplings"

For July 4th my date said he wanted to take me somewhere that he had heard numerous positive reviews about but had not tried himself and so to La Pulperia we went. The restaurant is below street level and very easy to miss but I'm so glad we found it. The lighting is dim, the music is soft, and the overall ambiance is romantic. I myself am a very picky eater so I was worried when I looked over the menu and didn't see many options that I jumped at. I thought I would just end up eating a side or two and then make my date take me somewhere else for some quick take out but I was completely wrong. We ordered the Beef Empanadas and Taquitos de Langosta for our appetizer. Both were amazing, I favored the taquitos because I felt that the flavors were refreshing for such a hot day. For my meal I ordered the Sangria Braised Short Ribs with Cauliflower Puree and Chimichurri sauce and he ordered the Fish Ribs. The ribs fell apart with not much effort and the Chimichurri sauce was amazing. My date enjoyed his fish ribs but I didn't try them. For desert we ordered the Flan which had hints of lemon, unexpected but still good. The staff was extremely helpful, the busboy recommended the taquitos for us and the waiter brought me two types of white wine to taste because I couldn't decide on a cocktail. I am 4 days out from our meal and craving a return visit in the near future. Thank you La Pulperia for such a great experience.

This should be on every cheap eats list in NYC. Â I have only tried their wraps, which are made-to-order and oh so fresh. Â Love the hummus and chicken ones. Â It's cash only and super tiny with no seating, but in warmer weather you can just walk a few blocks to Central Park to enjoy your meal. Â Best value on the UWS.

I absolutely love this place. True it is tiny. I have had the most delicious green plantain sandwiches.. The trick I use, come on an off hour during the day and you receive delightful customer service and great food for reasonable prices.. hmm I am hungry..

If this were in the Washington, DC area, I'd give it 2 or 3 stars. In NYC, it's pretty good considering the price and how much food you get. Â  For dinner for 2, you can split the chicken and a side for about 25 including tip (no drinks), which is pretty good for eating out. The chicken here is flavorful, but definitely not as good as the places down there. Â Too bad they don't use charcoal to grill these chickens. Â The dark meat was excellent, but the breasts were a bit on the bland side. Â Good thing the waiters were able to hook it up with extra green sauce. They really make good use of the space here. They pack us in like sardines, so if you're a bit on the portly side, you'll definitely bump into a bunch of tables while moving around.

Sushi Yasuda has the best salmon and fatty tuna(toro) I've tasted in America. Pretty close to the sushi in Tokyo. I tried the Omasake menu before, good but nothing to write yelp about it. I recommend just to stick with the sushi. Very fresh and very satisfying.

Yes the food was delicious!! but yes maybe a bit overpriced? bf got the popular cassoulet, and I got the quail with cranberry and walnut sauce. Both dishes are about $30. I guess there are much more expensive french places. Restaurant is small and cozy...you might have to rub elbows with people at the next table.

I've tried their restaurant in Soho and bakery in NJ. I had a chicken club sandwich and it was amazing! omg, how can it be so tasty?? i think it was one of the best sandwiches I've ever had in my life! also, bakery in NJ is awesome too. the price is reasonable and their pastries....made me speechless.. you must try!

Love love loveeeee this place! Went with my family last night for my dads 69th bday and it was GREATT! This was my parents first time tasting an italian family style cuisine and they were floored by how amazing everything was. The waiters were detailed, engaging and delightful, the host was friendly, and the food was unbelieveable. My bf even wanted to take a food coma nap, wake up and go again lol we loved the cleanliness, atmosphere, and attitude. will def go again

This place is AMAZING. Probably one of my favorite places to get brunch EVER! I'm not a vegan so that's saying a lot!
