The wait can be a little much on nice weekend days, especially if you come by early (say 11-12). I'd recommend coming here after 1, I tried that and the wait was short. Onto the food.... sigh..it's so good! Â So on my first visit I tried the "Soltero Bowl" and after they brought it they told me they accidentally added tofu scramble on it as well... AWESOME! this made the dish even more tasty, but it was so good, I had a hard time finishing it but I did! Everything was seasoned perfectly. I also had a bite out of my boyfriend's Tofu Rancheros, pretty good as well. Next time I went I had the Drunken Cowgirl, probably one of the best chili I've had, really good. The burrito is also awesome. I feel like an idiot describing all of their dishes cause all I can say is their food is AMAZING, well seasoned, and doesn't make you feel gross after cause most of their food is not very greasy. Their coffee is just ok though. Also service is great, friendly and helpful people!

Went here for a dinner party.extremely professional service. While I wasn't blown away by any dish the food overall is very good. What did blow my mind was this; the check. $580 dollars for 14 people (drinks included)!!!!! 14 people at a Well known NYC restaurant in the middle of TImes Square for $580 is just unbelievable!! I give the food 3 stars but the overall experience and value pushes it to a 4 Thanks!!
This Â is a place Â I will Â never Â get Â sick of Â awesome Â staff Â good Â food Â and perfect location.

Found this place through Yelp, and then started eating here three times a week for lunch. Had to stop that to curtail the expanding waistline, but WOW. It's definitely my favorite guilty pleasure right now, and I start getting withdrawals if I don't eat here once per week. My favorites: Steak burrito with everything -- I like the green sauce, red sauce is a bit too spicy for me (but I can't handle much spice), and the pork taco (with just the cheese and pork is incredible).

Won't echo too much of what's been said 597 times (as of this minute), but: gorgeous atmosphere/decor very friendly service - although drinks took a very long time to be served super tasty food, highlights of which included the kabocha squash toast, the roast chicken special, the asparagus/fried egg special, the gnocchi with ruby red shrimp, and the (duh) salted caramel sundae I know that the issue of kids in fine dining establishments is a perennially prickly one, but when we entered ABC Kitchen (for Sunday dinner, not brunch, mind you - at least I've learned to expect these antics with brunch crowds), there was a young child on a scooter by the hostess station scooting around the front restaurant area! Â He was running wildly through the dining room throughout our meal and definitely detracted from our experience. Â I'd love to see restaurants like ABC Kitchen draw a harder line on such issues - "no scooting in the restaurant" doesn't seem too controversial to me.

This place is an attention-grabber if you're walking by. It looks pleasant, but the experience of dining there was proportional with its prices. For a little bit more, you can find better food and wine in a setting that's more spacious. I like small places and I knew what I was getting into, but somehow the atmosphere at Briciola doesn't quite make up for its size. The staff was earnest, friendly, and sincerely pleased to have a crowd on a Thursday, but it seemed stretched by the dinner rush around 7 PM. None of our food excelled, but it was all fine. The best dish on our order was rolled eggplant filled with goat cheese. The wine was fine, too. It was drinkable and reasonably-priced. Here's the deets for two (10/09/14): Montepulciano, glass - 8 Sauvignon blanc, glass - 8 Shrimp scampi - 9.5 Burrata special with prosciutto - 16 Rosso di Montalcino, glass - 10 Eggplant roll with goat cheese - 9.5 TOTAL - 75.13 with tax TIP: The small plates are good for sharing. TIP: All the seating is what could be described as community. There's a community table in one room, and the bar in the other. TIP: We didn't try any of the pasta. It's a house specialty. Perhaps some of the other reviewers are awarding some more stars for the pasta. TIP: You can reasonably eat here for under $30 PP, and probably under $20 depending on how much wine you drink, or not TIP: Might work for pre-theater, but you should arrive early because every seat could easily be full during the dinner rush.

My favorite hotpot restaurant in NYC. Â Typical HK-style hotpot with many hard-to-find items outside of HK. Â A bit of a trek to get to from Manhattan, but well worth it. Â If you're going on a weekend, make sure you have a reservation because there's always queues. Â  Must eats: 1) FRIED FISH SKIN - deep fried fish skin that you flash boil just enough to get semi-soft. Amazing. 2) Fuzhou fish balls - fish balls stuffed with pork. Â What's not to like? 3) Fish roe fish balls - fan of xiao long bao? These balls have the same surprise-in-your-mouth effect. It's good to go half-half on the soup (spicy/non-spicy). Â The pork-bone non-spicy broth is milky thick, opaque, and delicious.

Crappy Service... The woman attending must've had a bad day, but seriously don't take it out on the customer/guest. Â Barely had a chance to be seated before getting bombarded by negativity and rudeness. Â Probably a good place, but the immediate negative vibe from the witch was not congruent to a pleasant meal.
This place is great! my roomate and I have been looking for a bar/restaurant in the area and skytown has not only delicious and nutritious food but hospitable staff. So happy its nearby!

They used to have belgian fries. Now they have steak fries. Sometime in 2006 the shop must have changed ownership becos that's when it changed. Stuff that changed: fries became thicker steak fries, no longer belgian fries prices went up - including extra charges for sauces portion sizes went down Stuff that stayed the same: dark, grungy wood decor staff, though not the same, were still cool wait is still never more than a few minutes To their credit, now that they charge for sauces, they give them out in standard sizes that are quite generous as opposed to the dollop that they used to give. Â These new, thicker fries are just not as good as the old ones. The disappointed nostalgia will keep me from returning.

$6 for a whole container stuffed with rice and your choice of chicken, lamb, combo?! Awesome!! White sauce is super delicious and spicy sauce is good, too. But be careful not to pour too much of the red - even my friends who love spicy.. say that it is SUPER spicy so if it's your first time, try a little just to be safe instead of dropping the whole thing in there. Lines are usually super long but so worth it for $6! You def get Â full from this. I usually split it with another friend. The Halal Guys are friendly/professional and super efficient with time. They are very dedicated and I hear they were out there even during the hurricane last year! Now.. that's hard-core! Keep up the good work, you guys!!!

I was pleasantly surprised by this place. Although their menu consists of mostly fried meat that I usually stay away from, the curry is quite addicting and I find myself happily shovelling anything smothered with it into my mouth. I've ordered the plain and chicken katsu, but last time I tried the sausage from my friend's huge Grand Slam plate, and I'm def ordering sausage next time. Â Add a boiled egg for variety and you've got dinner for $9 and change. As I said, friend got the Grand Slam, and dunno if anyone should be finishing that much food at once, but it def was worth the price (one of every type of protein and lots of rice). Just wish they had slighty more variety (how about some root vegetables in the curry for some texture?) and as another yelper has pointed out, they never give you quite enough curry for all the rice so you are left with uncerimoniously plain rice at the end.

my party was a little late so i had a beer at the bar. unfortunately, it wasn't as cold as i expected so she had it on the ice for a little while longer. great decor space but the ceilings were a bit low which made it a noisy place. the waitress was friendly and knowledgeable. we had some great eats. everything was wonderful: Salmon & Avocado Tartare, Seared Tuna Salad NiÃ§oise (didn't have as much tuna as i expected), the Whole Fish was great and very tasty but you definitely need to work on it, Chicken Milanese, and the rosemary fries -- WOW!

Their chips and guac are sooo fresh. Fish tacos and pork belly tacos were REALLY good. Interesting margaritas as well - some very spicy so caution yourself. It was a nice casual date atmosphere (I came with a girl friend and it was perfect!), I will be back!

First, fantastic food. Second, fantastic atmosphere and comfortable seating. Third, fantastic service. There's not much more to say. Try the gyoza and garlic chicken appetizers. Since this is mainly an udon and ramen house, go for what the house does well and enjoy it heartily. Prices are reasonable and portions are well measured.

We had nachos and Huevos Coppelia, which are basically Eggs Benedict. Nachos were super yummy and the chips were flaky and crispy. I appreciated how they stacked the chips on the side so they didn't get all soggy. The Huevos Coppelia were rich and delicious, on a buttery biscuit base with cheese sauce on top. My only regret was that I ate too many nachos to finish the dish.

Small place with huge flavors. Â Prices were extremely cheap but everything had distinct flavors. Â  BYOB and order food at the register. Â  We ordered to share and everything was delicious. Â Would definitely try to stop by again next time I'm in NYC

This place is worth the wait you are bound to experience. Â The food is top notch and the coffee was delicious. We went for breakfast and had three different items; all great. Â Get the pancakes or the French toast or omelette; and make sure to have the biscuits. Â You really can not go wrong. Â Only problem they have is trying to accommodate everyone who is trying to get a seat but hey, they have takeout.

Great restaurant. We had few courses of meals and few bottles of wine. Their $.25.00 wine selection it's fantastic idea. Service was very on top if it and super friendly. I'm very impressed and can't wait to go back there. I loved their dessert selection simple and delicious !!

On a trip to NYC we caught an early show and at 9:30 or so ended up wondering around for a place for late dinner. Â WOW!!! Â This is the most amazing Italian I have ever had. Â Hubby and I had the antipasto to start, both had the unlimited pasta special and shared a bottle of wine and a dessert sampler for two. Â Let me just say that the past was just stupid good! Â We both ate so much that we were still full and skipped breakfast the next day! Â I just can't do justice to this little Italian spot - it was so quaint and full of character. Â Definitely put Becco on your must-eat list!! Â No one could possible leave here hungry or unhappy.

The food here was surprisingly good. Â I'm not sure why I expected it not to be good (I assumed it would be lame tourist food place), but what I got was solid British pub food. Â Nice juicy hamburger for me, and my dad got a delicious beef pie. The servers and bartenders were extremely friendly and the beer selection was good.

Ok.. So this is the real Halal Guys food truck! Literally!! There's so many in NY but this is the right one to go to because the food is way better!!! They are also open after bar hours and thats the best time to have Halal!! Lol! I usually get the lamb and chicken mix! And please dont put too much hot sauce! Ppl who never tried halal guys should just have 2 drops or even 1 and that should be hot enough for u! Take my advice!! And please bring some extra white sauce with u, u'll thank me later lol

Came here for a social networking event. I honestly wouldn't have pegged it as a sports bar, but big tv screens, reasonably-priced drinks, good food, good atmosphere - I liked it. The waiters constantly made sure there was always food on the table. Nachos plate is huge and tasted pretty good except for the fact that I wish they would have spread out the sour cream and guac more evenly spread. Would not suggest getting the Mediterranean Platter: the pita bread was cold and hard, hummus wasn't anything special. Signature Sample is also a good choice for large groups - as a vegetarian, I found the basil/tomato/mozzarella bruschetta very good. It had a bit of a smoky taste; bread was lightly toasted to a nice, soft crunch. The place itself isn't that big, but it's very clean and classy (which is not usual for a sports bar, but something I really liked.) Good place for happy hour or sports viewing events.

Value. Â Entree + 2 appetizers for $7 for lunch, enough said. Â Ordered the drunken noodles, not the best ive had, but pretty decent. Â Had to order extra spicy, and it came out decently spicy, not too hot. Â for apps I ordered the dumplings with peanut sauce and the curry puff. Â The dumplings were mushy but the cream puff was decent. Â All in all a great Value for lunch.
I love this place....the noodles and dumplings are both incredible. I thave only been 3 times but i thnk about going here on a weekly basis. Â You can buy frozen dumplings in bulk to go as well.....

When you think of NYC Pizza, you -- hopefully -- don't even consider the trash that litters the streets of this city, eg Domino's, Papa John's, et al. You likely recall the 5,000 "Original Ray's Pizza" and the variety of Italian-entitled places scattered through these streets. Mama's, Luigi's, Mario's...they're all over. Oddly enough, many seem run by Spanish-speakers, not true Italians. But I digress -- this is about the food, not the geography. These here-and-there pizza joints are certainly decent enough; they deliver average, zesty sauce, reasonably tasty toppings, and somewhat chewy crust with three-minute-in-the-oven, paper-plate-plus-plastic tray efficiency. Then there are real, solid pizza makers that do very odd, but very tasty, things with ingredients, and offer up something very similar, but nearly superior, to what pizza can and should be. Like Ovest. Once you get past the too-cool-for-school hipster crowd blocking the entrance, you find yourself in a semi-lit, cozy space with a good bit of semi-acceptable noise, pedantic, unfortunately odoriferous bathrooms, a nice, filled bar, and brick and candles dotting your visionary landscape. Then you peruse the menu and find the Martha and the Capricciosa and you wonder what kind of strange voodoo is taking place inside these four walls. And then you sample their magic and you realize you're no longer in Kansas. Our visit last night included the rice/cheese balls (a nice, updated modern twist on an otherwise dated classic that was extremely delicious) as well as the above-mentioned pair of pizzas. While the Capricciosa was heavy on the briny, salty flavors of ham and marinated artichokes and olives, the Martha was -- in a word -- orgasmic. The atmosphere is either a plus or a minus, depending on whether you're there for the food or the eye candy; but truthfully, if you sample some of Ovest's pizza fare, you'll be thankful regardless of whether you went for the pizza or not. You'll be leaving knowing it will be the pizza that brings you back.

Your basic charming French bistro in Williamsburg. Dark wood, subtle lighting, surprisingly large space with a big back room. While they're apparently known for brunch, their dinner service was broadly excellent. Classic bistro dishes: coq au vin, steak frites, mussels. A good, short, very French wine list. Service was friendly and efficient. One of our dishes came out underdone and was taken off our bill without our asking for it. Overall, a worthy inclusion to the 'burg casual night out.

Horrible... I went there with some friends saturday night. It was one of the worst experience I've in a long time. The food is awful and so is the wine. The atmosphere however was great! If you go to a restaurant for the food stay away from that place.

I've been going to Five Leaves for years now and it had always been great, but the last two trips have completely changed my opinion and I won't go back. This morning we arrived just as they opened at 8am. Our waitress took our order at 8:10 and we never saw her again. After an hour we got our food, which is annoying but could be made to be a non-issue if the waitress expresses any level of attention at all. Instead, after 45 minutes, we had to ask another waitress to check on our food for us. It was clear that our order was passed over because about a dozen different people that came in after us got their food long before us. When it came time to ask for and pay the bill, our waitress was still no where to be found. We asked the hostess to get her and after 10 minutes, the hostess came back to ask if we had gotten our bill. We hadn't. Eventually another waitress came to drop it off for us. The food here is great, but some members of the staff flat out don't care. I would chalk this up to a fluke if it happened only once but we've had very similar experiences twice in a row now. I love their food, but it's not worth the aggravation of paying someone to ignore you.

I've been to grill 21 a bunch of times and keep on coming back. I've tried so many other filipino restaurants in jersey and nyc but this one has that home grown taste to it. The prices are a little more than I would like but the portions and deliciousness make up for it. Food that I think are must trys if you're a pork lover like myself: crispy pata, lechon kawali, and chicharon. The service is good. The space is small so make a reservation just in case.
Euh, why the high rating really? I can cook up a way better burger at my desk in midtown using nothing but office supplies. Beer's good though.

Boss was in the mood for Indian food but since none could be found, a coworker suggested this place instead. Typical Japanese curry items but done very well. Items come in multiple sizes (S/M/L/XL) with about a $1 difference between each size. All this affects is the amount of rice they give you. Service is very quick and the store's pretty much always packed during lunch time. The curry sauce is pretty good. Spicy, not all that hot with the typical sweetness that's indicative of Japanese curry. The katsu (breaded & fried) chicken, pork and shrimp were all quite well done being sufficiently crispy on the outside and tender/juicy on the inside. You can also order a sliced up boiled egg to be added as a side. Also standard is a big mound of shredded cabbage which is pretty bland. I guess that's to offset the heavy taste of the curry but I'm not a big fan of the cabbage. Pricing is pretty standard for lunch, ranging from $7-13 or so depending on how hungry you are. It's not something to be had every day since one can only have so much deep-fried food on a daily/weekly basis but it's not a bad place to go for lunch in general.

Nice little quaint place in LIC. Had to try it based on the rave reviews. Seats about 30 I believe. The staff was very attentive and nice and I was the first of four to arrive in my party and almost 30 minutes early and they had our table waiting for us and the place was at capacity! That was a pleasant surprise and the hostess didn't even question where the rest of my party was. She was very respectful and so was our waitress who came frequently enough to make sure all our needs were met. We ordered the guacamole which was fantastic. Bigger than your average size and fed the 4 of us enough as a starter. I ordered the carne asada and it was delicious!! It came with a side of deliciously creamy black beans and roasted poblanos which were the best I've ever had!! My friends got the oysters, lamb, and a soup and they were all impressed! We finished our meals with flan which was sprinkled with fresh vanilla! Incredible! Will def. come back!

I'm updating my review to 4 stars because of the frequency of my visits to Eataly now. My office moved into the neighborhood so I have gone in many times to grab something for lunch or to bring home food for dinner. Sometimes after a stressful day at work I'll stop in just to smell the hunks of aged parmigiano reggiano. One of life's joys. I have found the best deals are at the focaccia stand. You can buy a large square of fluffy focaccia for $3~4. Toppings range from mild ricotta and zucchini to spicy sausage and peppers. They recently introduced a thin cheesy "Italian quesadilla"-like option and a heavenly sweet focaccia that is drenched in butter and sugar. Any of these are satisfying and affordable options for lunch. I also love the pastry station and have tried several chocolate-y, almond-y desserts that cost more than my focaccia lunch. The panini station is a ripoff if you ask me. The bread is too crusty and cuts up my mouth and they don't include a lot of the cured meats in the sandwiches. A few years ago, they used to make some panini with focaccia bread but not anymore. I wish they would bring that back. It can be very crowded and crazy, especially at lunchtime and in the summer. I'm glad I work nearby and can do my shopping and snacking during off peak hours.

Nothing in Astoria compares to Vesta. Added bonus: the menu is local and seasonal, so you can walk in three months later to a whole new set of dishes, especially on the dinner menu. Brunch: L'Italiano for poached eggs that look like dollops of whipped cream, or Warm Bankee for the truffle oil in the polenta Dessert: get a Baby Jesus, for the love of God Soup: WHATEVER IT IS, GET IT. I dream of the special time of year when the butternut squash soup comes around and one taste eliminates all evil in the world, but the soup is the menu item that changes most often, and it's universally a good choice.
The food is great but not fabulous. Â It is more abut the ambience an drink menu. Â FYI gorgeous decorations but the most uncomfortable bar stools ever!

Been going for years and the quality stays the same - I love that! Â The weekends are definitely croweded so be ready for a wait. Â We snuck in on our last trip during the week and it was easy to get a table. Â The real draw for me and my husband are the pancakes! Â Just the best darn pancakes and a good atmosphere.

Coming from Lebanon, and having tried a LOT of "Arabic" restaurants here in the US, I have to say that this is one of the BEST. Â The freshly baked pitas are just the right thickness, and come piping hot out of the oven. Â The Zaatar (thyme) pitza is deliciously authentic, and closely matches the Man'oushe it aims to replicate. Â The baba ghabbouj is excellent, bursting with the flavor of garlic and charred eggplants, and the falafel are crispy, with all the right spices. Â The chicken sandwich is better than the meat, and the spices on both smack more of South Asia than the Mediterranean. The caveat is that you have to be careful what to order, because not all items on the menu are created equal. Â The foul (beans) are bland and the hummus is runny and to be avoided at all costs. Â Mmm, but when I stick to the good stuff, I can close my eyes and almost pretend that I'm back home....

Hands-down the best sushi/sashimi in the NY...maybe in the US. Â I love the pure, calming ambience. Â You have to sit at the sushi bar (Hiro is our man - Yasuda himself may make great sushi, but he's not all that enjoyable to talk to). Â My favorites: of course the fattiest grade tuna, try all 4 types of hamachi, any of the grilled eel -- melts in your mouth.

First, there's not too many Filipino restaurants in the greater NY area except those in Queens or NJ. Maharlika is an attempt at a classy or gourmet Filipino restaurant in Manhattan. It was better than I expected, but the overall taste delivery falls a bit short of true Philippine cooking. It does a better job at presentation than taste. The 'sisig' special was disappointing. The classics -- adobo & kare-kare - were the better choices. I wouldn't frequent the pace, but sure I would go back again with friends who would like to try it.

Tried this place for the first time today. I noticed it last week and I think its a few months old. The huge windows and clean open space caught my attention. This area totally needs a gourmet deli like this one. The prices are same as delis around here but food is well prepared and fresh not like the sub-standard food in this area. The hot/cold salad bar is $6.99/lb for quality that you would expect from Dishes or Mangia. I had some of the fish which was a bit overcooked but all the veggies I tried were really well seasoned and yummy. Breath mints highly recommended if you eat those garlic chips that they toss on the veggies. Definitely want to try out the different food stations. Plus they have a really cool 2nd floor seating area that overlooks the lower level.

Been eating here for years whenever I'm in the area....and it never disappoints! Such consistently tasty food and the prices are so reasonable for the serving sizes. Love their phad-see-yew. Mmm I can taste it now!

I came here with a friend and must say the food was great! the lemon chicken was delicious but the sheep milk dumplings were out of this world. The server Anna talked me into trying this and offered an exceptional wine to go with it. Anna really knows her stuff and made my dining experience the best i ever had. i will surely be going back and take any more recommendations from Anna.

My friends took me here saying that they had found a place better than Lombardi's. I'm obseeeeeessed with Lombardi's, and with pizza in general lately, so I welcomed the challenger with open arms. We decided on the meatball pizza and started with a caprese and a caesar salad. The tomatoes and mozzarella were huge and pletiful and fresh and tasted great with a splash of balsamic vinegar. I know it seems so silly and simple, but it's easy to make a crappy and unsatisfying caesar salad and this one was the opposite. It was delicious and had the perfect amount of dressing. Our pizza was definitely good. Huge leaves of basil and thick slices of meatball and toasty crust. I personally wouldn't go so far as to say it was better than Lombardi's, but it definitely didn't disappoint. I should also point out that our server was incredibly sweet and attentive and personable. A great local pizza joint.

Granola crusted french toast, Granola crusted french toast, Granola crusted french toast, Granola crusted french toast, Granola crusted french toast... ...I was hoping that maybe if I said it 5 times, it would suddenly appear like Candyman. Along with a big veg & egg or the goat cheese and sundried tomato scramble, and I'm good to go for the rest of the day. Eat here at your own risk. That brunch, it haunts my dreams.

oh how grateful i am for Antonioni's. I have been crying to my boyfriend, yes absolutely not figuratively crying... literally, how LES needs an amazing pizza/pasta place that isn't some rip off. coughGoodFellas! we had the lobster pasta, primo pizza, and anti pasta. WHAT A TREAT. The pasta was amazing. It was the good stuff- FRESHLY HOMEMADE. sounds like a plan. The water girl could do with a little help, as she doesn't understand 'no ice, please'. We asked that of her three times and gave up. Ice seems to be a must when it comes to water here. Service is a tad slow as well. However, that could just be because they opened just a week ago and are still working out the kinks. however displeased i was over my ultra cold water and slow meal arrival, I will gladly return in the coming days for more of that amazing pasta (the sauce was divine to boot) and solid pizza

How have I not reviewed Il Bambino yet? It is without question my favorite place to grab a panini. You really can't go wrong when you come here. basically anything and everything that you order off their menu will be delicious. Their hidden (or perhaps not so hidden) gem are their soups, unfortunately they don't make soup during the summer but Autumn is coming and so be ready. their soups comes with a pesto crustini which compliment Â each other Â like any other inseparable duo, ie. peanut butter and jelly, grapes and brie. Another thing i love about Il Bambino is their unapologetic love for all things pork. if you come here on Friday, Saturday, or Sunday for brunch you will be presented with their brunch menu which include items named, Notorious P.I.G., Sir Oink a-lot, and the like...

Almost every time I come it's good, but today I was really ticked off. My food took 40 minutes to come and wasn't even great! Also, they didn't give us one penny off. That is why I rate it two stars. Come here at your own risk of dying of starvation.

Amazing yummie roll. I went on a Saturday at 10:45 and the place was packed. Chicken tikka is amazing! The place is small with limited seating but Bryant park is close by so to go is a good option. 5 stars! My new favorite place!

Go early in the week and avoid the fuss and this place is a amazing . The portions are small but rich enough that you don't want too much and very reasonably priced for the area. I recommend the Rabbit pie and the Oxtail on toast Extensive wine list ...great ambiance , my only gripe is the staff . I sat at the bar and couldn't work out whether the staff all hate each other or just the customers. Its borderline between is he an expert or does he have an attitude . Don't let this put you off , just laugh like its a scene from ' sleep no more '

Thoroughly impressed with this place. Gave an extra star just because. I found it on yelp and was expecting a little take out joint but lo and behold it's actually a very spacious, beautiful, simple and rustic restaurant. Stopped by to get dinner on the way to a show at the knitting factory. We sat outside (there are just a few seats available). I ordered the grilled vegetable sandwich which was delicious. Large chunks of freshly grilled peppers, onions, tomatoes with fresh warm greens, yum. My bf had the burger and fries, which he said were probably of the frozen variety. We also got the garlic bread which is a large flat bread with real garlic and oil. It was delicious. Service was OK. Waiter was friendly (and super attractive) though we did have to make sure we spoke clearly so he got our order right. If I am ever in the area, I would definitely return.

I had lunch here recently. Excellent tacos but I'll have to come back a few times for me to really compare them with my other favorites. The restaurant itself is simple and casual and the menu does seem to be fairly authentic. Reasonable prices as well. I just wished the service was more attentive. They got my order wrong but at least at what they gave me (fish tacos instead of the cabeza) was also good.

I took my bf here for his birthday recently. Made reservations 5-6 days in advance. We sat at the bar and had Yasuda himself as our chef. We pretty much left it up to him, and pointed out what we especially liked. it was a completely enlightening experience, the preparation of each piece was simple and the flavors were delicate. Yasuda let us know when there was already soy sauce in the sushi so that we dont over-do it. We were both mmmm-ing away after each piece. everything was exceptional and fresh and super tasty. My favorite part was when the chef would give us some background as to each piece we would eat, where it came from, why its the best there and how to eat it..he would also tell us the heath benefits of certain foods! I loved that i learned so much about sushi that night. It was a delicious and fun experience, its a bit expensive but worth every penny.
Awesome burger has this special sauce on it and the fries are really good! Love the spinach and artichoke dip for the homemade tortilla ships
One of my favorite restaurants in the area. Their Bhan Mi is better than anywhere in chinatown/ Little Italy imo. Prices are great too.

I was in NY for a 'work' week that included dinners at places like Momofuko Ko and Per Se. By far the most fun and enjoyable dinner I had was at Public. A group of 6 of us were there on a Tuesday night and we were treated so well and with such warmth and care it was truly memorable, not an ounce of pretentiousness . John and Jeff took care of suggesting dishes for us to share and amazing wines to go along with each dish. We had the hama oysters, an amazing smoked salmon salad, Â the foie, kangaroo and the venison all were delectable and then for desert the sticky toffee pudding and a selection of sorbets and ice cream. We asked if the chef and pastry chef could come out at the end of dinner so we could thank them and they were both super humble and extremely gracious. Great place and I would definitely go back.

Overall great meal and good service. I loved the decor for the "home" feel. They start you off with bread with a Delicious white bean and olive oil dip. Classic play on bread and butter. We got the buffala mozzarella with tomato and basil. The mozz was so damn fresh! I got the Veal special on Monday night, and it was VERY fatty but tasty as well. Skipped wine, but the cellar looked full and robust I really have no complaints - I`d say 4.5

Came in for a quick bite. Bought an al pastor taco. Very tasty! Spiced just right (which on a scale of 1-10 of spicy, 10 being the spiciest, I'd give it a 7.5). The pork was very soft and I loved the pineapple that was in it. Tortilla tasted yummy too. Will be back to try some more!

Got here at like 4 or 4:30, no wait at all (the place was half empty!). Cool interior, lots of Asian-inspired decor. We were seated at a U-shaped community table, which was kinda cool. You are far enough away from most of the people at the table so it's not too awkward. Started with the pork buns- exceptional. That pork is so damn good, along with the slightly spicy sauce that is in there as well. Also had the black pepper chicken wings- also good, very peppery (obviously) but kinda sweet at the same time. She had the Akamaru and I went with the anniversary special. She liked hers but we both agreed mine was better. Why? The broth. It just seemed to have more flavor. The ingredients in each of our dishes was pretty similar so not sure what the differences are but go with the special. The noodles themselves were good, not amazing or anything. And again, the pork in the soup was awesome.

This review is for a delivery order. My colleagues all ordered sandwiches, which everyone enjoyed. The only gripe was that some thought the bread was a bit stale. We also ordered a pound of the homemade mozzarella, which was delicious. You can also ordered sliced Italian meats. A half pound of the sweet soppressata with a long baguette left us all as very happy campers. I ordered the pasta pomodoro, nothing special and it was overcooked. To be fair, it was hot and probably just continued cooking itself during the delivery. The salads were also just okay. Then again, Italians aren't known for their salads. I would stick to the deli options and sandwiches here.

LYCHEE MARTINIS. THE BEST COCKTAIL DRINK EVER. WHAT VERLAINE'S IS KNOWN FOR. If you're a dude, just man up and get this girly drink. You will love it. Don't be ashamed because every dude in there is getting the Lychee Martini too. This place is a cool kick it lounge to go to. It has a good amount of people in here and doesn't get to the point where it is packed. I like it because you can casually drink and just chill with your friends. I must say, this drink could be a creeper one. It tastes so good you don't realize how much alcohol is in it. The best is left for last in this drink! You get a fresh lychee at the bottom. It tastes so good because it was marinating in your drink the whole time you were sipping on it!

Fun bar, good music, and strong enough drinks. There was quite the line when I went but if you have the endurance most of the people will just say "screw this" and leave and you'll actually not end up waiting all that long. You simply must persevere. The food actually looks pretty good too so maybe the plan should be to come for like a 9:30 or 10:00pm dinner and just stay.

If you're a meat lover, you must come here to try out this restaurant!! There's so many meat, so many flavors!! Thinly sliced marinated beef. YUMMMMM! Come with a group of friends and start grilling! Bet you'll enjoy and have fun! Must try the green tea crepe dessert! It's made with 100 thin layers!

Battersby offers an exquisite tasting menu with minimal pretentiousness and exceptional care to details. Perry L got us a early dinner reservation for our one year anniversary. Seven dishes! (Perry knows I love tasting menus. I'm spoiled. Don't tell him!) While the storefront is rather nondescript, the dining room teeny tiny, the kitchen even tinier - the backyard patio is an urban oasis of calm and romantic in a upscale casual Brooklyn way. (Do keep in mind the risk of mosquitoes.) If you enjoy cocktails and wine, the menu is large and varied. The table next to us had several rounds of drinks, so I assume they are top notch. From the beginning, service was impeccable. Kind, eloquent, well timed, and frequent. Part of this has to do with the fact that we reserved the seven course tasting menu, which guarantees a certain level of care and constant table refreshing. I didn't care. They were lovely. On this mid-August day, the menu consisted of: -Tomato watermelon gazpacho amuse -Tuna tartar with shaved foie gras spoons -Rosemary flatbread with whipped ricotta Hamachi (yellowtail tuna) with cucumber yuzu dressing Homemade mozzarella with heirloom tomatoes, basil, and pickled peaches Potato gnocchi over corn puree Sweetbreads and polenta Big eye tuna over tomatillo gazpacho Lamb over roast eggplant with salsa verde and dandelion -Grapefruit sorbet Banana pudding/pineapple cheesecake -Coffee cake - to go Items with the "-" were complimentary, but were still made with a high level of care. The amuse was a mouthful of tart and creamy, rich but fresh. The tuna tartare could be a stand alone appetizer - very fresh, large diced tuna, well seasoned, and liberally coated in shaved foie gras, adding a second layer of umami. I loved the flatbread and whipped ricotta - clean, earthy, comforting food with quality details. I loved the hamachi, potato gnocchi, and lamb the most. They were clever flavor combinations, prepared with the best quality, and made my tummy very happy. The hamachi was particularly beautiful, with edible flowers, a bright green sauce, and festive flecks of red sea salt. The gnocchi melted in your mouth, super soft yet flavorful. The lamb was cleverly plated and served perfectly medium well. It paired well with the tame eggplant, which added a hint of sweet. Dessert was well plated, but didn't swing home for me. We shared the two dishes and neither one of them packed the banana or pineapple punch I was waiting for. While the deconstructed presentation was clever and I appreciated the use of iced creams, the desserts appeared more of an afterthought, failing to signal to me that the lovely dinner was really over. I was satisfied, so no need to stop by 16 Handles or anything, but I hoped for a little more. Overall, Battersby is a lovely place, creating a memorable and delicious experience. Service and ambiance are lovely, but due to the high price point (and small servings for non-tasting menu diners), you may want to reserve this one for special occasions.
Great selection of fine Asian cuisine..my two favorites are the spicy lemongrass Kalbi short ribs and the Singapore lak sa..

The food here is good, and the baked goods are always fresh. Their dinner menu is a good size and is pretty varied. The cod fritters were amazing, the artichoke salad is fresh & delicious and for the entree I'm a bigger fan of their pasta than their meat dishes. The decor is really cute and the atmosphere was laid back. The waitress was really attentive, and they didn't rush us out. One of my neighborhood favs!

Most of us know Little Owl as the restaurant in the FRIENDS building. It is also one of the top 101 restaurants in NYC. We had been planning on checking out the Little Owl for a while and finally ended up going there on a Sat night around 8 PM. The wait was close to 2 hours. They took our numbers down and suggested that we have a drink or 2 in neighborhood bars which we ended up doing coz we REALLY wanted to try out the food there! We were called within the 2 hour timeframe and were promptly seated. The service here is really good. We tried the lobster bisque, the famous meatballs and some other entree. The food was OK. nothing to write about but the overall experience was good.

Potato power! Stumbled upon this place while walking around in the West Village. Who doesn't love potatoes?! This is a small establishment with a decent amount of seating and tables. You order your potatoes (mashed, fried, curly, sweet, etc) and add toppings to it. There are so many possibilities! Â Ask questions if necessary. Â I had their smashed potatoes with veggies on top. I also had a Harney & Sons Peach Tea... it was just aiiiight. They were pretty efficient when taking our order and it didn't seem too long of a wait. Everyone was pretty nice and my potatoes were crisp but flavorful....not greasy at all. It's a unique concept and I'm happy that they have a location in NJ for when I'm craving potatoes.

What on earth is going on with Yelp? This place is totally overrated. The food is the definition of average. There was nothing special about anything we ate. We had the "special" octopus salad, the eggplant app, the penne pasta and the short rib. It was very surprising that Yelp had 4stars with like 800 reviews. It's definitely a 2.5/3 star place and that is only because the vibe is awesome and it has a good crowd.... Pass

This place was pretty awesome. I cant believed i lived here this long and i didnt notice it. It is difficult to think about this stuff exisitng when i dont know about it. It is not with out its falws but it was still pretty bawler.
Not only was the food amazing, but the service was superb. Especially the hostess - who was lovely and went out of her way to help make sure that we had a wonderful evening.

Got the 1/2 Chicken with beans and rice and it was delicious. Refreshing to find a cheap, satisfying meal in Midtown. Would take this meal over a lot of the trendy "5-star" spots around the city. Ceviche is awesome. Stick to the peruvian classics, pollo and ceviche. You will not be disappointed, service is great too!

It's so crowded! It's better if you go as a couple, you'll be seated faster. Seafood here is amazing. Good prices if you know what to pick. All fish fresh and well cooked. Delicious, I can't wait to go back!

So, so, so bad. I really don't understand the high rating cause I felt really uncomfortable and gross dining here. Yes, the food is cheap, but you really get what you pay for. The peanut butter noodles were literally just half-assed noodles in peanut butter, and they weren't even worth $3. Def. not coming back.

As far as the food and experience are concerned, five stars for sure. Â Only reason I peel a star off is because they don't take reservations and the wait can be long if you go during peak hours (7:30-9:30). Â But if you can get a table here, GO GO GO GO GO!!! People love the ramen here and they're right, it is excellent. Â But I think the small plates are the real reason to go. Â The sesame cucumber is always refreshing and salty and delicious. Â The shishisto peppers I could eat all night. Â And their pork buns are some of the best in the city. We love Ippudo!

Tacos? Phenomenal. Guac? Surreal. Only reason I didn't give it a 5 is that it's pretty small and can get a little warm if you eat in. Â If you want some fast, very reasonably priced, and delicious Mexican food in the E. Vil - go to Taqueria Diana! I got the Rajas and Chicken tacos with Chips + Guac on the side. Was full enough off of the tacos that I didn't even finish the Chips + Guac. Pro tip: Bring the guac home for some late night food!

This was my first time, and I would definitely return to this upscale but unpretentious restaurant. We started with drinks - the Jalisco Pear was the most deliciously complex cocktail I have had in a long time - followed by a dozen raw oysters with an assortment of delightful sauces. Chose sea bass and pork for the dinner entrees and we shared them. Both were wonderfully flavorful and perfectly prepared. Dessert was a tray of artisan cheeses and port. The service was perhaps the finest I have encountered in a restaurant. They really made us feel special. It was quite expensive, but we did splurge on oysters, cocktails and dessert. The entrees themselves were reasonably priced for the quality.

An authentic Japanese restaurant some place other than St. Mark's! Awesome sake options. Â Great prices. Â Overwhelmingly large menu, and always always consistently great food. Â I have never been disappointed. Only warning I have, waits for this place can get ridiculous, especially on weekends (not Ippudo ridiculous, but an hour/hour and a half at times). Â However though, you can put your cell down on their wait list and they will call you when a table is ready. Â So just put your name down, grab a drink around the corner (not at Tonic..) and come back when you're called! Â Definitely worth the wait.

Paprika is one of the few restaurants I've given a 5 to. Â I still think it deserves it (though it's maybe closer to a 4.5). Tonight, we had: Arancini rice balls, with saffron and mascarpone. Â So nice and creamy, and the outside is fried perfectly. Â Absolutely terrific with the creamy marinara sauce. Â I could eat like 10 of these (it only comes with three - sad face). The grilled branzino. Â Great crispy skin, good sauce, great olives, capers, and tomatoes. Â A really flavorful dish, everything goes well together. I also had the Spaten german beer. Â Meh, it didn't really go with the food. Â But I've ever been a fan of whitebeers. Â A white wine would have been the better choice for what we ate - not the restaurant's fault. Paprika continues to impress. Â A slight bit crowded, though, as always.
i really like this place. Â the udon is always delicious and the gyoza is unbelievably greasy and crispy. Â couple that with some beer and you've got a combo that's hard to beat.

Basically, the staff is fantastic and the food is always excellent. Â One taco is sufficient for a little gal like me, two is a serious meal. But if you need something more substantial, get the bibimbahp, served dolsut (in hot pot, worth the extra charge) with protein options for vegetarians. Also, the Ttukppokki appetizer is dangerously addictive. I Â this spot!

adorable tiny cash-only BYOB date spot. bring a hungry, iron stomach, as i have not had this much cheesiness in one meal in ages. Â the recent special scalloped potatoes with bacon came adorned with chunks of bacon fat. Â i avoided them but sopped up the rest. Â the seafood "kassulet" was similar in grease and caloric content- i think we ate our day's calorie count in one fell swoop. Â warm, charming atmosphere. pleasant servers. Â very hardy food, not for the weak stomached. Â recommended to try at least once; but truthfully not sure it lives up to the 5-star hype.

This is the summit, the absolute zenith of street food! The Combo Plate with Red and White Sauce has blown my mind on more than one occasion, it's so good you run the risk of having an out-of-body experience. I'm not joking. People may dislike Bobby Flay for some reason or other, e.g. he's arrogant, he's a ginger, he was on Entourage, etc. (that last one is the one that gets me), but there's no denying that he can cook. He's truly proving it here at his new restaurant, as he is actually there, on the line, every night (so far), and the food he's turning out is excellent. I was there for the early bird special, as the only reservation I could manage was at 5:30 PM, even though I checked OpenTable the day reservations opened up. This place is definitely the hyped spot of the moment, due to Flay's celebrity and the big news that it's his first new place in NY after several years. When we arrived, there was already a line of people waiting to get in - yup, to eat at 5:30 PM. We ate quite a bit in spite of the early seating: - Olive and Focaccia Bread (complimentary) This is nothing special, just your typical plain bread with some olive oil and sea salt. It's pretty good though and is a good snack while perusing the menu. - Lamb Tenderloin - Eleven Layer Potato - Chorizo Crepinette ($17 for all 3) You must start with a few small bites (emphasis on small) from the "Bar" section of the menu. You get to pick 3 out of the 14 different choices here for $17. These were really tasty, but like they tell you, they are just little bites to get started. The Lamb Tenderloin was 3 little slices of rare lamb that were very juicy and delicious. The Chorizo Crepinette was another little bite that was just enough for two people to share and each get a bite, and was also quite good. The best of the bunch was definitely the Eleven Layer Potato, both because it tasted the best, and because it was a lot more food than the others. It's a tall stack of several layers (maybe not quite 11) of potatoes, which are so creamy and buttery soft. This one is a definite must. - Gato Salad ($12) I never like ordering salad, but I loved this one. There were so many flavors going on with all kinds of great ingredients, like ricotta salata, pomegranates, and crunchy wheat, which should replace croutons in all salads. This is definitely an excellent choice to start for something lighter and more refreshing to counter the rest of the meaty, oily stuff. - Pizza with Lamb Sausage ($17) Speaking of meaty and oily, this pizza was really great. I normally avoid pizza at non-pizza places, but I'm glad we tried it, as it was as good the pizza at many high-end Italian restaurants. $17 is pretty steep for a pizza, but you do get a decently large sized long pie cut into 6 satisfying slices. This is definitely the appetizer to order. - Steamed Halibut ($29) This was an amazing piece of fish. It's a really thick, smooth filet with so much flavor in both the fish itself and the saffron-tomato broth underneath it. - Kale and Wild Mushroom Paella ($27) Every table here was ordering this, and with good reason, as it was definitely the best bite of the night. I initially balked at the idea of a meatless paella, especially since I also don't particularly like mushrooms, but this was incredible. Not only is there plenty of delicious kale and mushrooms, but there are also some excellent crispy artichokes, and most importantly, a beautiful runny egg to top it all off. You must definitely order this one for an entree. It's much smaller than most paellas you see at places that usually serve them in massive pans, but it's so satisfying nonetheless. - Complimentary Biscotti They brought out 6 biscotti for the two of us to enjoy with our desserts. These were quite good, with a lot more flavor than you would ever expect from the typically bland cookies. - Espresso Soaked Bread Pudding ($11) I wasn't blown away by the desserts, but they were both very good. This one was great, and so smooth you didn't really need teeth for it. It had such a deep espresso taste, and was closer to a tiramisu than a bread pudding. The mascarpone crema and cocoa flavors were really delicious as well. - Fromage Blanc Cheesecake ($11) Unlike typically good cheesecake, this was not dense at all, and was actually quite soft. The best part of it was the almond crust and the caramel sauce, which combined with the smooth cheesecake made for such an amazing bite. I wasn't a fan of the blood orange slices on top, but putting those aside, this was really excellent. As mentioned above, Bobby Flay was out and about in the restaurant, looking too busy to really mingle with any of the guests. He did go over to talk to his wife, who was by herself at a nearby table, but he didn't show any love to Ivan Orkin, also seated next to us. As evidenced by this crowd at 6 PM, this place is already hopping and will be crawling with celebrities and high profile food personalities for several months to come. The food and value might be closer to 4 stars, but the overall experience with the great, exciting atmosphere, beautiful dining room and impeccable service makes this one of the best new restaurants of the year.

You know what you see a lot of these days? Paninis.* They are so common, and so often underwhelming. Bocca Lupo, the charming neighborhood spot in the heart of Cobble Hill, serves some of the best paninis around. They have the absolutely perfect texture that rides the line between crispy and doesn't extend into roof-of-the-mouth-cuttingly crunchy territory. They are stuffed with exactly as much filling so as to be full without falling apart. The ingredients are fresh and well-seasoned, and the combinations, if not unique, are classics for a reason. (The pancetta, asiago and egg combination is a fancy bacon egg and cheese that hits the spot at brunch or lunch, and the sausage, mushroom, broccoli rabe and taleggio option is always a good decision.) Paired with a surprisingly good bourbon cocktail or a selection off their very decent wine list, one of these paninis is the perfect afternoon meal. And may I just say, Bocca Lupo seems to attract such a pleasant, local clientele. Once, the parents at the next table actually apologized for the essentially non-existent noise made by their exceedingly well-behaved children. Doesn't it always seem like the people who should apologize are the ones that never do? __________ *I know panini is actually the plural form, but I'm an ignorant 'murican and it sounds wrong to my ears.

It's fucking delicious, if I do say so myself. That's what my waitress said, as she delivered my lamb breast. And although my virgin ears were soiled forever, I have to admit that she was absolutely right. The lamb is fatty, and not for the faint of heart...but it's dangerously good. The cumin and other spices pop with each unctuous bite, balanced by the acidity of the lime...and it's fucking delicious, if I do say so myself. When I first came in, I wasn't sure what to expect from Do or Dine. After all, they claim to serve drunk food, which to me means whatever crap I can find at 3 am. And yeah, some of the flavor combinations remind me of what I might have thrown together under the influence of the wacky tobacky* and whatever alcohol I could scrounge back when I was broke and limited to my parents' cabinets. The only thing is, my man in the kitchen is much, much better than I am at this. And he has better ingredients at his disposal.** How else do you explain something like Nippon Nachos? Cheese and pico de gallo and sour cream over potstickers? Love it. Mexican and Chinese, Caribbean and French, there is no unifying theme to the cuisine, but it's unique and flavorful and best of all, so very affordable. Nothing is over $20, not even a solid meal like the fish and some chips: a whole sea bass, served over some damn good fries. Do or Dine has hit that sweet spot of seriously tasty food and not taking themselves too seriously. Just read the menu, and you can tell. Their mussels: relaxed. The Caesar salad is entitled, "Et tu brute?" And served with a knife stabbed in the back of the romaine. The description for the foie gras doughnut: "Yes, it's true." And they even have a Snickers Ice Cream Bar on there. Why? Because they like them, and they are perfect as is. Chicken "Halalipops"? Yes, please. It's two large drumsticks, cleaned until they actually resemble lollipops; the skin is crispy, the flavors are spot on, and the light dipping sauce, a goat yogurt-based ranch, was perfect. The bleu cheese on the side seemed to be more of an afterthought, with no good way to eat it all together...but I smeared it on the chicken anyway. Perhaps the overall effect is a bit greasy, but that's what drunk food is for; how else do you soak up the alcohol? They are very much still refining things, so I wouldn't expect perfection just yet. Hell, last time I came in, they were building benches for the dope backyard. But they are doing big things over here in Bed-Stuy, and from what I've seen, it's all good. Awesome food, awesome vibe, awesome staff, awesome music (I heard some Lupe, some Girltalk, some stuff I didn't recognize, but liked all the same). I think Ad-Rock said it best: Check-ch-check-check-check-ch-check it out. Oh, and read the "About Me" section here. It's priceless, and I love them for it. ___________ *Merely mentioned for effect. I have no knowledge of said tobacky, especially if you are my mother, or some sort of law enforcement. **Or at least I'm assuming, because I didn't see Wheat Thins and BBQ Sauce in Hot Dog Buns on the menu.

UWS Peruvian food. Signature Chicken dish was good, the green sauce with it is like crack, however I feel like this place is overrated. Â Yes the rotisserie styled whole chicken is good, but it is comparable to boston market if you take away that magical green sauce. Â The chicken was pretty moist, came as a whole chicken and had decent flavors. Price was reasonable, staff friendly, decor wasnt the best and definitely not the worst. Â I dont know if I could say that I will return even though it is so close to my apt.

They have ma la tang!!! Mmmmmmmm my fave!! Not spicy enough for me though. I do get my fave small eats here.. such as scallion pancake, pork fried bun, and all the other small bun goodness. I am curious about the hot pot here though. I will definitely come here to try it.
Better than filet mignon.

The Little Owl is a very small, very nice, elusive West Village restaurant that I've tried to get a reservation at for about a year and a half, but every time I call for a reservation they're booked to all hell! Thankfully, Jim came to the rescue. Do you guys want the secret to getting a coveted reservation to a much talked about hot spot restaurant in they city? Well here it is, ssshh, ok?: Call four weeks ahead of time and take any time they throw at you, even if its an early bird 6:00 or a graveyard 9:30. Taaadaaa! Luckily, the long wait was well worth it. We sat at a very nice two-top by the window where we watched all the beautiful West Villagers walk their dogs in their knit sweaters and tall boots on a picturesque fall day. It was all very J.Crew catalogue. The restaurant itself is very small, but not in a poky, cramped way. Actually, the small table count makes it very neighborhoody and casual in a tossed together, but still serious about food way. My favorite thing about The Little Owl were the tiny, delicate finger bowls of Maldon sea salt on every table. Maldon sea salt is wonderful and delicious and makes everything better. Here's what we ate: cava, a beer, a very nice olive oil, and a tiny blue bowl of Maldon sea salt ricotta cavatelli with fava beans, pecorino, and tomato broth gravy meatball sliders made from beef, pork, veal, and pecorino crispy chicken with asparagus home fries, lemon, sherry and dijon red snapper over seafood risotto spiced fries with chili aioli chocolate lava cake and coffee ice cream The meatball sliders were the highlight, definitely living up to the hype. The only negative was the chocolate cake was a little dry. Creepy fact: an older couple sat next to us and ordered the EXACT MEAL as us, dish for dish. What does that mean??
STIX is delicious, great ambiance and good service. The farmer's bleu is my favorite salad there. An added bonus, they have hot toddies!

They serve artichokes pizza in heaven to all the saints and good people of this world. It is freakishly good. So much so that the downside is an addiction that leaves you craving fortnightly. The unfortunate piece of that is you're not the only who craves and you can end up queueing for ages. That being said its a small price to pay for easily the best pizza in the world. Ever

Only been here once but sure to come back. Duck foie gras.... out of this world!!!!!!!!!!!! Crepes are unlike any i have ever had. And I have had a few.... Can't wait to try more stuff.... Wine list can maybe use a couple of, not so common, French wines.
Amazing brunch experience .. The food is delicious and was matched with excellent service. Will definitely be back.
Good spot, gets lively on Friday nights and they have Kung-Fu Cinema Nights of Wednesdays once a month I think!

The Jeffrey is a most welcome surprise addition to my usually boring/ E. midtown work hood. The beer selection is fantastic, the ambiance is dark and cozy and the crowd is laid back. I sampled some of the happy hour brews (wish they offered more) and a yummy hot pretzel, both were perfect. Â My co-worker and I both had other plans that night but wished we didn't so we could just hang and enjoy the vibe. Only downside was our server, she was sweet but maybe stoned? She couldn't remember anything we ordered or even that she owed me change from the bill - she was all, "Oh you wanted that money back?" Poor thing I was harshing her buzzzzzz.

We went here based on Yelp reviews when my boyfriend and I were looking for a good date night. HOLY COW! Absolutely 100% incredible. Excellent beer selection for IPA/hoppy beer lovers. The rolls are absolutely amazing. Words can't describe them! My boyfriend and I had 6 each. I'll probably dream about them. The server was more than happy to keep bringing more out to us. The meals are the perfect portion (after an appetizer and all those rolls). To start, we ordered the crispy pork belly. It was not overpowering for an appetizer. The tastes complement each other so well. I ordered the scallops...I wouldn't have changed a thing. Perfection. I went with the smaller portion so I could keep eating the rolls. My boyfriend ordered the duck breast and was extremely satisfied. The entree's different tastes all went together so well. We were extremely impressed. After dinner, they gave us mini cookies as a completementary dessert and a pastry to go for checking out coats. The restaurant has only been open since March and I expect great things to come. Great place for a work dinner, family dinner or date night. And it won't kill your wallet either!

Short Review: The food was good. But, I would only come back if there was a shorter wait and if I got a better server. Longer Review: My gf, gf's little bro, her best friend and I met up here. We hit the busiest time here on a Sunday for brunch. I got duvel for the long wait. The place is small so all the wait was done standing. I believed we were skipped because we were standing by the door and no one came out to check. When we sat down, our waiter thought he was the Sh!t. He should have taken out a pad to write down our order. The friend ordered the Benedict dish. I think my gf go a French toast dish. The little bro ordered a savory dish. And I ordered a madame thing with melted gruyere cheese. My gf ordered a hot chai and the friend got a coffee too. I wanted to order another dish because I was so hungry and glutton but I didn't challenge the guy's memory. Before the food came out the waiter brings out a chilled chai and coffee. And on queue he forgot something with our order because the place was so busy and he wanted to cut corners. The food did not come out at once. So, one at a time we were watching each other eat. I paid with a credit card and the waiter did not bring a pen for me to sign. No wonder there is a wait. This guy is so forgettable that he doesn't want make money. I could have easily padded this bill by ordering another plate and a few rounds of beer. He did not deserve it.

A real hole in the wall, Turco offers pretty average Turkish and Middle Eastern food. A gyro platter is disappointing when the best thing on it is the mildly spicy red sauce. (The cacik sauce is thin and doesn't really add anything.) The rice was soggy, and they shouldn't have bothered with the pallid "salad." (Paying for the chopped "shepherd" salad instead would be a mistake, because it's drowned in a pool of dressing.) There are a couple of standouts, though: I would return in a heartbeat for any of the lamb-based sandwiches (doner or adana kebab), as the meat is flavorful, the portion generous, and the bread stellar. Â (It's pita-shaped but thicker and more traditionally Turkish.) The sigari were tasty but could have been crisper. Service is noncommittal, although the shy cashier in the headscarf did bring our food to the table. Beverage choices are minimal and boring, apart from a Turkish yogurt drink. There are only a few tables, and the heating is so heavy-duty that half of them are uncomfortable. It's probably busy around lunch, but if you're looking for a cheap pre-theater snack, this place might be a lifesaver.

The never disappoint me. I had not been here in at least 7 years and I saw 2 of the same waiters so clearly everything is great from management on down to food. I liked the new additions on the menu (new for me anyway). The honey chicken and all the variety of waffles. Of course everything taste great.

Went out to grab lunch and felt the siren call of Uncle Gussy's. Â Pork Souvlaki sandwich with fries $8 and just delicious. Â My only complaint is the fries don't stay hot but it was a long walk. Â People in the truck are nice and friendly. Â I will be going back more often. Â No line since I went after two PM. Â The tzatziki sauce was amazing!

This place is overrated and priced. I went there with my friend for lunch. It has a good atmosphere and service but the food is so not great. We had calamari, crab toast and mushroom pizza. The calamari was ok. Nothing to be amazed about. The toast was sort of burnt. The crab tasted like canned crab meat. I was recommended the mushroom pizza but I didn't like it at all. I really don't understand why this place is so popular that I couldn't even make a reservation for dinner.

It's all about the ROAST MEAT. Get the pork or the duck, throw it over white rice or in a bowl of noodle soup. Slurp it down with beer or tea, and go to town until there's nothing left but bones. If you are craving something else, there is no shortage of other restaurants. Eating successfully in Chinatown means finding out the unique specialities of a particular place. Here, the cleaver reigns!

I love the constantly rotating beer selection here, and the fact that it's right across the street from me is a huge plus.. They also have some killer food;. Their fries are a top choice for me to munch on while trying out new beers.

I vote this my favorite happy hour place in Astoria. They have a great beer selection and one of the most incredible happy hour food specials I've had the pleasure to eat. My go to are the lamb burger sliders for a buck each (wah?! Yes.). I could eat about a dozen of them. Another great feature of this place is the decor and layout, it's perfect for summer drinking and people watching (if you're into that). All this together (plus good service btw) make this one of my favorite places in Astoria.

Have been thinking about this place since I stopped there two years ago. Â (Has it been that long? Â How could that be?!?) Â I had time to kill before seeing a Fringe show down the street, so I revisited the sandwich I had the last time -- the Genoa Salami Panini (fresh mozzarella, roasted pepper tapenade, and sundried tomato and basil mayo). Â  Ate it at the counter with an unsweetened iced tea. Â Even better than I remember. Â The tapenade is divine.

Great find in an otherwise culinarily arid neighborhood. Â Try the meat lasagna, you will not regret it. Â The salads, sandwiches and desserts I tried were all very good. Â Not many people know about this place, so I reluctantly write this review in hope that it doesn't contribute to turn a hidden gem into a crowded restaurant. :)

I went to the Redhead on a Saturday night with my boyfriend and we were lucky, it was relatively empty, when we got there. I got there before my boyfriend and ordered a drink at the bar. I didn't find anything that spoke to me on the drink menu, so I asked the bar tender if it's possible to get something that weren't available on the menu? She replied "absolutely". So I ordered prosecco with a splash of elderflower liquor. One of my favorite summer cocktails (actually all year around). Just by that I knew it's a great place and bar. When my boyfriend arrived I asked the bar tender if I could order the same drink while seated and again she kindly replied "of course! I'll let the waiter know!" As soon as we were seated, our waiter asked me if I'd like the prosecco with elderflower liquor? I was surprised and happy, he was taking care of that and replied "yes please". The menu is fairly small, but enough to choose from. They have "shares" which is basically bar food, then appetizers and main courses, as well as sides. We went with the notorious bacon peanut brittle to share, the pretzels as an appetizer and the buttermilk fried chicken, that comes with salad on the side and the fried green tomatoes with ranch dressing as a side. The portions are just right for sharing. We also each got a dinner roll with home made sweet butter. It was delicious. It's basically southern cuisine with an upscale twist. It's great. The place is small, so it can get packed easily. It's better to get there early (especially on the weekend). We skipped desserts, because we had to catch a movie. But I would definitely come back. Great food and great service, as well atmosphere! I can only recommend.

I went to Beco on a regular basis and enjoyed the food/atmosphere until the bartender (curly hair works on weekends) mistook me for some another black women that had run out on her bill. After accosting me in front of the entire restaurant I paid the bill and left. What's insane is that the bill I supposedly ran out on was 17$! First let me say that I am black, and I also do not steal and we do not all look alike. I urge anyone/everyone to not frequent this place.
Fantastic meal at a good price. Friendly staff. Great random find when staying at the nearby hotel.

Limited lunch menu on Sundays! There is a combination of brunch and regular lunch on Sundays. After my first visit, I went back on a Sunday hoping to have some calamari again but sadly it wasn't available. Their calamari is very very good. Different from the usual calamari you may see in other Italian restaurants. its comes sauteed with roasted tomatoes and served soaked in the tomato sauce! We also had Mercato which was great. They seem to use very fresh ingredients. My main dish was Pollo parmigiano. Also very tasty.

We loved our lunch at the little wine bar. Three of us shared several apps and a couple of pastas, plus some very good and authentic Italian wines. Â The white asparagus with poached egg and prosciutto was very good, as was the lobster salad. For pasta we stuck with two homemade items: tagliatelle with osso bucco sauce, and a fresh lasagna. There is a reserve wine list that's a bit pricey, but the regular list is terrific and inexpensive. Service was wonderful, the pace leisurely a la Europe but not annoyingly slow. We will return

1. make reservations 2. BYOB 3. if you were born in the 80's, try not to make the cute waitress feel old if she checks your ID 4. start with Mushroom cigars 5. end with Rack of lamb and prepare to sleep well
overall, the food was ok. i like their special pad thai (ate two of them). nothing crazy, nothing fancy...just a good place to grab decent thai food.
Always perfect

This place is the tops. It's in my hood, the food is A+, and they really know how to take care of their customers. Â What else could you possibly ask for? PS: Giuseppe is the man, and the baby jesus cake lives up to all the hype: it IS incredible!
good authentic Italian food. Venue is intimate and cute. Tried the paperdelle oxtail ragu..was nervous it would come out too oily from the oxtail but the sauce was great and pasta was cooked well!

Pra quem quer experimentar um hambÃºrguer sensacional, acompanhado de batatas fritas incrÃ­veis! Se gostar de cervejas, vai curtir a seleÃ§Ã£o da casa! O atendimento Ã© Ã³timo, o preÃ§o Ã© bem adequado e o ambiente Ã© Ã³timo tanto pra ir de casal como com os amigos.

This place is tiny but really cozy & chic.. The prices are moderately low, and the portions are perfect for someone with a small appetite.. The service is also great, only thing I can suggest to them is use less oil.. My meal was a little on the oily side but not bad overall

Portion sizes weren't as large as I was led to believe from other reviews. I had the Rigatoni Focaccia and it was okay. I feel like it could have had at least one other vegetable besides the sundried tomatoes - it tasted a little one-note. My friend had tortellini which was on the blander side. Our waitress was sweet and attentive but brought two cokes when only one of us had asked for it. When I mentioned it, she said they gave her two, so she brought two! lol

My desire to eat at Ipuddo finally took over and I won! Â My fiancee said, "it's very good but, there is a long wait". Â So, on a night she is running her Champagning event I stayed in to get over a cold with the thoughts of warm Bombay Sapphire (the six herbs help I promise) and spicy ramen. I had no idea how great this experience would turn out to be! Â First, I asked the hostess her favorite dish on the way to be seated (20 min for one at 7:30) of course the highest price and highest additive was her choice. Â I stuck with my original plan of the Karaka Men (happened to be her dish of choice) but to add the Bakudan (their original spice) not the Kakuni (pork belly also most expense add in) as recommended. Well, once the food came out in 5 min or less I tried the spice stand alone... Â Perfect! Â this will add the flavor I want plus that kick, for that little bit of sweat feeling . Â I finished the noodles without eating much of the broth in case I was to say, "Kae-dama please". Â Which is asking to add another serving of noodles to your dish, only if your broth isn't too low. Yeah, that happened! And I thru the Pork Belly in there because I just eat one F'in amazing dish and my girl isn't here to say I've had enough (best move ever at this place!). Â So, not now chief I'm eating in the zone! (to quote my new F'in hair cut). Â I blissfully, selfishly and shamelessly enjoyed the most amazing ramen dish (or 2, the pork belly was worth it!) that I could have imagined! Â  Yes, the fried steamed bun sliders (pork, chicken or eggplant mushroom) looked great and I'll probably order them when I go there with my girl (AKA: the ration nazi) to pair with my one helping of ramen. Â And this Ramen dish will be...Karaka Men ($16), add Kakuni (pork belly - $4), and Bakudan (awesome spice - $2). Â  And to those that don't like the price...go spend $5 less, eat shitty ramen and complain about it. Â Or spend that $5 and feel like King Author returning from slaying 2 dragons, getting your brains f'd out by 4 wench's and being full on ramen and drunk on grog!

Oh, it was terrible! Â How Yelp has let me down. Â The ambience is depressing, like when a ship is about to go down. Â The ramen was deplorable! Â Why was the broth so sweet? Â It tasted like someone dumped a bottle of hoisin sauce into the "tonkotsu" broth. Â A real tonkotsu broth should be milky and fatty, this was just clear and dark brown. Â I hated the mushroom topping and the handful of pickled ginger, made everything ten times sweeter/saltier. Â Who puts those kinds of sweet mushrooms into a tonkotsu ramen anyway? Â Usually it should be the woodear kind. Â Watching the sushi chefs prepare the sushi was kind of gross, chopping away with wild abandon! Â Lets just say Im not too enticed to try the spicy tuna here after watching it get made!

Eh... not impressed. Â Portions were far too small in most cases, and most of the food really didn't strike me as anything beyond nice restaurant stature. Â I wasn't disgusted by any stretch, but for the whopping bill, this needs to be better. Â All in all a decent place, but it was really way too full of itself. I haven't had the chance yet, but Upstairs at Bouley has drawn rave reviews from many friends of mine, so I'll give that a shot instead. Â Apparently its a very different menu and quite a bit better. Â We shall see... I hope so.

Thousands of years ago, man hunted animals and cooked meat. I can imagine our ancestors sitting around a fire, tearing away flesh from bone and snapping sinew in a joyous celebratory meal. Â That tradition can be relived today - minus the blood, guts, fur, and other unpleasantness of hunting and killing your own food - at Morgans. Â Big tables, ample outdoor space and a great selection of BBQ make this an idea spot for a group get together. Â And, the bartenders and not only good, but smoking. Â I'm hoping they don't catch me staring. It's simply good BBQ with an awesome selection of mac n' cheese from Elbow Room. Â (Why these two were ever separated, requiring separate bills is beyond me since they seem to share a kitchen and are right next door). So, why three stars? Â The table service. Â It's, not that good. Â I'm not one to focus on service as the main criteria for a bad dinning experience, and the service isn't bad. I's simply consistently mediocre. So consistent that i can't assume it was simply an off night. Â  Case in point, running out of food. Â Now, a good BBQ place should run out of food. Â That's actually a good sign, suggesting several possibilities: 1. they cook just enough for what they think the need, 2. they cook only the best ingredients, which means their high standards keep them from using sub-par cuts, 3. BBQ takes time, so they can't just throw something on the grill and have it ready to go. Â What is bad, is the servers not knowing what the kitchen is out of and then taking 10-20 minutes to let you know that your 1lb order of fatty brisket isn't going to happen. Â  If I want good Chicken, or pulled pork, or brisket, there are other options within walking distance. Â But if i want good chicken, pulled pork and brisket, Morgan's is the only game in town. Â Best bet, sit at the bar. Â If you find out that your 1lb order of fatty brisket isn't coming, a shot of whiskey from the cute bartenders should make you forget there was a problem.
Love! Great food, friendly staff and awesome service. Love the all vegan gluten free options!

For the price, the variety and the portions this spot is tough to beat. I was so impressed with the variety of toppings, the freshness, the textures, the flavors. The falafel bowl with fried eggplant and Israeli salad was full of flavor and nice and juicy, just the way I like it. It easily could have (and probably should have...oops!) fed two.

I really liked so many things about this restaurant: the delicious and well priced food, the homey neighborhood feel, the almost kitschy round tables with checkered table cloths, but most of all, the kick ass animal print wallpaper. I love, I want. I found the food to be extremely good value for money. The mussels, listed under the salad/starters section was a meal within itself. I also took the seafood salad which was loaded with fresh oysters, octopus, squid and cupped in leaves of radicchio. My friends had an assortment of pastas and pizzas which they seemed very happy with.
