We had: 4 starters (roasted fennel, fries, fried artichokes and mussels) 4 entrees (meatballs, 2 pastas and 1 seafood salad) 2 bottles of wine (a surprisingly delicious chardonnay, which is not a what I would usually choose, and a Pinot) The damage was 50 bucks each, including tax and tip for 5 people. Not bad for a hot new NYC restaurant! Will definitely be makign this my neighborhood go-to.

Seems to me that this place is all about who Â you know in order to get good svc ( no wait time , "VIP" experience) Â and the clientele seems a little trashy, HOT97 style ( no offense but if I want to go to a "rich ghetto" atmosphere I'd stay in my own hood " I've been waiting to come here for months and finally got the chance to. I was highly disappointed in the long wait to be seated and the food was just OK. The highlight of the night was actually leaving and walking around the piers and enjoying the view.

All I can say is...yum I have been there twice, and both times I was pleasantly surprised. The breakdown is as follows: Service: 4-5 stars. Most of the time there is someone nearby who will help you. The second time I was there I had a new waitress who wasn't very professional, but it was obvious that she was just new and everyone deserves a chance. The wine she recommended was good though, so props. The Wine: Love it! Both times I tried different wines (Chateau Tire Pe Bordeaux and Domaine du Trillol Cucugnan) and both were great. My bf tried the Cotes du rhone Domaine Â De L'Espigougette, but I wasn't a fan). The Food: This is where the YUM comes in. We had the AVOCADO CREVETTES SAUCE COCKTAIL appetizer. The combination of the shrimp and avocado was wonderful, we finished everything down to the lettuce leaves. For entrees I had the SAUTED HALIBUT: lemon sauce with chorizo and the GRILLED TUNA NICOISE. The Halibut was extremely flavorful and tender, the sides complimented it quite well. The Tuna was a DREAM! It practically melted under my fork and in my mouth. It came in the form of a salad, and filled me up very nicely, while not weighing me down. My bf had the EGGS BENEDICT, which was a great choice as well. The hollandaise had a nice tangy taste, and the eggs were cooked perfectly. He tried the steak the second time, it was quite good, but nothing compared to the tuna. For desserts, the creme brulee was delicious (not too sweet and with the perfect crunch), but the moose was extraordinary: the dark chocolate was good but not crazy special, but the white was absolutely decadent (and I am not a fan of white chocolate). The Atmosphere: intimate and romantic, while not being pretentious. The maitre'd was friendly and funny with a very thick French accent. He made a few nice jokes and came by to check on us without being to bothersome. Overall: This was originally a cozy little place I happened upon on Yelp, but after going there twice it has become a favorite for my bf and myself. I will definitely be coming back and recommending it to friends.
Had the brioche sandwich with classic tomato sauce and meatball. Was fantastic and bill only came to 42

So I came here for their famous live octopus. It was alright. Okay, so I felt the suckers on my tongue and it's trying to wiggle out my mouth. Too bad, you going down bish! Got the seafood hot pot and boy was it ginormous. It can be overwhelming if you came with less than 3 people. You won't be able to finish it honestly. Though it was a big pot of food it wasn't anything worth noting nor worth getting second time around. It was very salty and tasted nothing else but salt. We had the watermelon soju and that was refreshing. This place was just hype to me. Not much of a culinary awakening. Consider me un-wowed.

Came here a few nights ago with some friends and had a great time as usual. They have a terrific selection of craft beers and whiskey. The lamb burger was a little disappointing but everything else was great. We had the empanadas, meatballs, pork belly, and finished with the fried twinkles.

We came in around 9pm and the place was crowded. We waited around 10 minutes to our table, and it is all worth it. Despite the fact that kitchen was closing, we were able to get our hands on the famous Thai desserts. OMG, best thing that has ever happened to me after a long day at work. Â I will visit again!

I've always walked by this place and tonight I decided to finally give it a try. SO GOOD! Everything was amazing. The entrees did take awhile to come out, but these things happen. The deliciousness made up for the wait. Our server was great. I don't usually eat desserts but for some reason I went for it. The flour less chocolate cake was perfect. I'll definitely be eating here again

Food was to die for! I came here with some friends who live in the Manhattan area and it was a truly memorable experience. The server was down to earth and so helpful with picking a wine, and was just the right amount of attentiveness. The food did take a bit longer than we expected but they gave us some complimentary pasta while we waited. Notable items were the roasted mushrooms, the hamachi tartare and the oricchiette, amazing. Such a wonderful all around experience. Would definitely return.

Great food, amazing portions, and surprisingly affordable. Doesn't get much better than this when it comes to writing to-the-point, succint reviews :) You really can't go wrong with the carne mechada, the catira, or the arepa pabellon.

I was thoroughly disappointed. Â The first warning sign should have been the disenchanted waiter standing outside the door not trying to escort customers inside like every other restaurant in Little Italy. Â When we entered, it took a couple of minutes to be seated as we were ignored for a bit. Â (This is a tiny place.) Â The crust of the bread was quite hard, not delicious but not terrible. Â The chicken cacciatore was very unpleasant to look at and not all that pleasant to eat. Â Everyone in my group left very disappointed and feeling quite gross. Â I will never go back and recommend you never try it.

Good place, their spicy wonton are awesome. The only bad thing is that they take a good while to make, and if there's a line (which there often is on evenings) it takes a long time to get your food. Count on 20 minutes. The system works like this: you order at the counter furthest away from the entrance. You pay and get a receipt. They then call out your number when your order is done. If you've ordered something that takes a long time to cook (like the spicy wonton) you'll have to wait a while.

This was by far the best meal that both my husband and I have ever had!!! Â As soon as you walked in you were greeted with the fresh smell of apples from their floor to ceiling wall of apples. The service was exceptional and they provided us with excellent recommendations for both our meals and for the wine pairing. Â We were served an amuse-bouche with every single course of our meal. Â The Procini Flan was the best appetizer I have ever had. My husband ordered the chocolate souffle for dessert (which he confirmed tasted amazing) and with that they brought us a pineapple/coconut amuse-bouche, a complimentary grilled peach & sorbet dessert, PLUS a tray of a dozen housemade chocolates. Â And finally on our way out the door, after we had eaten the best food ever to our hearts content, they sent us home with a take-away lemon tea cake. The overall experience was absolutely exceptional. Â It is a must try in NYC.

Well, I love Bar Toto, and now I love Bar Tano. Same great atmosphere in a smaller place. It's a bit younger and more hipster, but that's because of the nabe - further along the rough edges of the Slope as opposed to right in there. But, they have the same diverse wine selection allowing me to purchase a $20 bottle of a very decent Montepulciano or opt for something more expensive if I feel like it. And the food is delich. I've not been there in the evening where I hear it turns a bit more into a bar, but I look forward to it.

Brunch was the best here. Â Where can you find tater tots, sausage, and egg inside a burrito? Â Well, look no further, you have arrived. Â With a bouncer dressed in 90's shades waiting to take down your name before you get tackled trying to get a table ignoring the already starved patrons ahead of you, to the 80's theme tchotkes that surround you, and of course the painting of Davy Crockett, complete with matching mat...it has a certain ambience of relaxed and coolness. Â I would say it is full of 20 to 30 somethings enjoying a delicious breakfast in a hip environment. Â I would most likely come back and with friends.

Very little normally can compel me to review a restaurant, let alone a restaurant as seemingly trendy as Scarpetta, Â but the bread and the spaghetti with tomato and basil are so freaking good that I'm going to break my yelping virginity. Well as long as yelping while drunk and gloriously full counts.

We just had an amazing eating experience here at Piacere. Every dish was complex and flavorful. Pizza dough was light and melted in your mouth. The zucchini timbale was sublime, we had a beet and fennel appetizer that was delicious. We had two pasta dishes we shared. Their orrecetta pasta which was homemade with a variety of flours was the best ever with fresh wilted spinach. We had a pasta dish with wild boar that was amazing. Service was great and the restaurant feels like home. Owner Marco uses organic ingredients from local sources and it shows in the food. This will be a regular stop for us

Tchoup Shop is my first taste of New Orleans in Brooklyn. Deep Fried, Heavy, Bold and Filling! Everything on the menu sounds interesting! My friends just want to order every single item on the menu - Soft Shell Crab Amandine ($14) - Grilled Handmade Bacon ($9) - Jumbo Lump Crab Smoked Sweetheart Cakes ($14) - Duck and Okra Gumbo ($8) - Char-b-que Oyster (5 for $10) - Famous Buttermilk Biscuit ($2) Until I said Stop no more let's finish what we ordered first! (FYI, this is the third full meal of the day and it is not even 2 pm yet!) Watching the chef preparing our food at the makeshift popup kitchen is a treat in itself. I definitely would come back to Tchoup for a repeat visit as the menu changes every week and just love the casual set up of the place! And of course food taste much better with friends and some awesome beer selections at dba!

Great music. Cheaply priced beer. Nice people. Good burgers and chicken sandwich with brie. Fries are good too. They even play Black Sabbath now and then-- to keep the annoying people at Blue Ribbon, which is next door. What more do you want?

Great ambiance and decor. Not a large food selection during lunch time, just sandwiches, empanadas and appetizers. The Cuban sandwich was very flavorful. Don't expect a typical Cuban restaurant menu. Drink menu was vast and unique. Overall it is a great hangout place for drinks and a quick snack.
Best pizza EVER!!!!!!!!!!!!!! i will eat it each and everyday

4 stars for space, 3 stars for the food It was dark out by the time we got to M. Wells, and the slice of light coming from the bright room in a brick building felt like we'd come upon an abandoned space, re-purposed by culinary hipsters. Oh wait. But that's to say, walking into M. Wells is half the magic. The public school experience I certainly wish I'd had. Beautiful wood desks, with those wrought metal chairs and cheap granite we all remember. Green chalkboards and a stainless steel kitchen. Â  Menu is on the chalkboard, so being ever the docile pupils, we spent a comical 2-3 minutes squinting across the room before a waitress brought over some printed menus. Fizzy Lizzy and Sixpoint to drink, marrow and escargot to start. Arrives on a divided plate (cute) with some toasts and teal plastic scoopers. We're all kids on the inside, even when we're eating grownup foods! Â One long slice of marrow, with a few snails and topped with herb butter crumbs. Tasty for sure, but not as luscious as this dish has potential to be. The toasts especially were a big dry and brittle, could've used more give, maybe with a thicker slice or some generous buttering? Next up, meat pie and rabbit bucatini. A bunny virgin, I was excited to nosh on some Bugsy. No exaggeration: tastes just like chicken. Nothing wrong with that. But something about the bucatini, though tasty, made it hard to eat. Â It wasn't the richness; fat + cream are no obstacles of mine. After a few more bites, the sauce seemed oily but not creamy, and peppery to the point of astringent and drying, necessitating many drinks of water. Before receiving our order, we watched other diners pick at their bucatini and mocked them from the comfort of our beverage-lubricated lips. Ha! Those no0bs. What weaksauce. But we ate our words, quickly. Lessons for bullies at the school of PS1. Â  The meat pie was pretty delectable. The crust is out-of-this-world flaky and buttery, with just the right touch of salt. Dreamy. If M. Well's reputation didn't precede it, you might be frightened of meat pie's innards. Chopped meats, crispy chicken skin, escargot, maybe even some rabbit, fell out of a infant-sized (ok, maybe fetus-sized) meat pie. They were all delicious and the most pleasant reminder of public school mystery meats. This one though, we had no trouble of taking down. Dessert? And why not. Balsam fir chiboust, which we admittedly Googled despite our foodieness. Apricot, orange, and fir flavors were distinct and vibrant in the chiboust, impressive. Cake was a touch saccharine, but enjoyable. Overall, it was a treat, but definitely not a meal I could eat more than once a year.

I ate here after my visit to the Brooklyn Museum, it is pretty close by. It's a lively Panamanian restaurant. The place is pretty small and can get crowded quickly. It can get noisy as well, I remember a lot of people talking and laughing as well as a band playing next door. If I lived closer I would eat here more often but probably get it to go. I had steak with rice and peas and a passion fruit drink. Everything tasted great and the drink was really good.

This was our first time here. Unfortunately, it was one of the worst dining experiences I've had in NYC. And, oddly, we'll be back... The location is scenic. The initial ambiance was relieving. Our server was prompt, knowledgeable, and made spot-on recommendations. The meal was satisfying, especially the tang of the risotto. And for this, I would have given the restaurant 4-5 stars. But, the manager on duty was a complete jackass. Throughout most of the night whilst we were there, he would talk over the music. Not in the sense of "food up" or something. No, the ass would play recorded Beavis and Butthead clips. Or, he would mumble. Or, just a whole shitload of other things that destroy whatever ambiance the owners were trying to create. Awesome, dude... We were overhearing other tables complaining amongst themselves. We asked the server who we could call and she was embarrassed to say it was the MOD. I'm sure it's a great spot any other night of the week. But I'm guessing if anyone else writes a review tonight for Booca, you'll see similar posts. Dude, get a life and don't destroy the work that the owners and the staff that give a shit have put into the spot. Ugh.

As a San Diego native, there are few things I miss more than rolled tacos that live up to the hype. These definitely do. We tried the beef and the pork, both classic and cheesy style and everything was awesome. They were crunchy, flavorful, and taste just like home. I agree the "seating" (bench or standing table) is a bit awkward, but when you just need to chow down, it's hard to be bothered. I wouldn't be mad if they served Jarritos or Penafel to drink, and maybe even served bunuelos as a sweet treat. Keep up the great work and I'll be back.
official spot, run by official people. these guys are on to something. also two thumbs up for pioneering a neighborhood.

It's been two years since I had my first bowl of ramen (ever!). Â And what can I say, definitely a five star if my mouth still waters thinking about it! The broth was rich in flavor and noddles were super fresh. Â Ippudo's definitely raised the bar for my ramen expectations. The raw octopus appetizer was delicious, too. Only downside to the experience was the three hour wait, but I guess it was worth it. My only suggestion is to return to the restaurant at least half an hour before your projected wait time, because you will have to start at the bottom of the wait list if you missed your name call. It was torturous.

Tyler Florence, you rock! Went here for lunch yesterday and absolutely LOVED the tomato basil soup. Â This is FAR from the Campbell's fresh-from-the-can-with-that-odd-tinny-taste soup. Â It's perfectly seasoned, with right amount of cheese, just a bit of a tang (sour cream?), and tomatoes, yes, visible ones! Â I rave over this soup. Now, my friend's mac n'cheese appetizer (fontina & cheddar) was quite excellent and a good size for the $8. Sadly, my attempt at 2nd appetizer-as-entree of pork turnovers was quite tasty (flaky pastry, well seasoned tender pork, served atop a purple cabbage slaw, and a yummy sweet-n-sour sauce on the side). But the portion size was teeny tiny.... SIGH, quite disappointing. Â Thank good ness for the fact that my friend needed help with finishing her mac n' cheese. Overall? excellent food, and friendly service. Â But gee, this is a rather pricy lunch.
Yummy

Love this place always! Try the arroz con ollo or the arroz chaufa. Delicious. And they have a variety of mojitios, incl a watermelon mojito. There is a quaint outside dining space in the back of the restaurant. Great service. A must try when in Park Slope. Affordable and tasty meal!

Overall very satisfying Restaurant Week experience. Â Service started a bit disjointed, including long seating queue for people with reservations (1 hostess that appeared new, plenty of staff standing idle) and hunting down servers. Â The dining room was also inconsistent, with the ground floor definitely being more attractive than the second floor. Â The bar scene is quite vibrant and would be great for an energetic pre-date (since it is a bit loud). Â That said, the food does shine through. Â The appetizers and tasting dishes are truly the gems at this restaurant. Â The chicken liver, beef tartar, arnabeet mekle (cauliflower) were phenomenal. Â We were basically sopping them all up. Â Portions were great for sharing and each person gets 2!

Been here a couple times and almost everything here is good. Few gripes though...the place is really small so it isn't very comfortable. The prices are also pretty high. I don't remember exact prices but a pie with a topping or two runs in the mid $20s. That would be fine if the pizza was really really good. But unfortunately the pizza is only very good. There are better places in New York but Lombardi's is definitely still up there and worth a visit if in the area.

I get that this place is a New York institution and it really does give off that vibe. The second you walk through that first entrance, and are met with another wooden door, and then greeted with a heavy red velvet curtain (and not one made of sugar and icing), to the rich, luxurious red leather benches and dim lighting, and its soulful music styling gives it that historical, rich feel. But I was a bit disappointed with this place. The hostess and host were kind and gracious, seating us amazingly immediately on a Friday night. Our waitress' assistant (I never know what to call them) was always helpful and happy - filled our water, replaced our water bottles, even replacing our paper table liner when it got dirty after we finished our dinners, in preparation for dessert. But our waitress? Not so great. She sometimes had eye contact, other times suffered from shifty eye syndrome and kept looking everywhere else in the restaurant but at us. She smiled maybe once and that was toward the end when she gave us our bill. She asked us not once (which I consider a courtesy), but twice whether we wanted the souffle dessert, both times of which we had said no thank you. Just all in all not the best experience with the waitress. Thought it was just her demeanor but she seemed to be having a good time dancing to Al Green! Now to the important stuff - the food. Yes, the black label burger IS really good. You can actually taste the difference with the meat. We had it medium rare, so it was beautifully grilled or charcoaled or pan fried, however they did it, on the outside and was still wonderfully meaty inside. It was served with very simple additions, a soft chewy bun to soak up all the juices and to not overshadow the meat, a slice of ripe tomato, some onion smear, and a slice of butter lettuce. It was definitely one of the better burgers I've eaten but was that burger plus a strange-tasting pickle and some inconsistently fried fries worth the $26 price tag? I think it was worth that one try, but I'll probably order something else next time if we go back. We also ordered the oxtail and foie gras terrine and the bone marrow appetizer. The oxtail and foie gras terrine had some really contrasting flavors and was great when paired with the table bread, since the acid in the dish was a bit strong. It paired well when you put the acid with the richness of the terrine on top of a little piece of chewy bread, but probably not worth $16. The bone marrow appetizer though definitely worth the $17. You get three huge bone marrows, the best looking one on top of course and beware! Those bone marrows and that plate is hot hot HOT, which is good since it keeps the marrow warm longer than a few minutes. The bone marrow is rich, perfectly roasted, and when you sprinkle it with that extra bit of salt they give you with the bread, it's phenomenal. It's elevated to a completely different level when you eat it with the sweet jam/sauce that it comes with, but either way scrumptious! This could be eaten as an entree if you order a side or an appetizer. Note: They don't make reservations for groups larger than 6 people because of space restrictions.

Was a little skeptical of this place, given half the diners are non-Asian and ordering stuff like sesame chicken. Everyone recommended the beef noodles but I had the Fujian dumplings noodles. It was really good, but the dumplings were too salty for my liking.

I really really wanted to love this place, based on the reviews here. Â And, don't get wrong, there's nothing bad about the ramen here. Â However, it just didn't blow me away. Â I ordered the Toroniku ramen (slow cooked pork), but it was just a little bit too salty. Â And the price, $11.50? Â Seriously, not cool. Â Noodles were fine, but didn't have that wonderful spring and elasticity that I associate with the really good ramen noodles. Â Broth was also a bit salty. Â Dumplings were pretty mediocre. Â And the place is like way off in the boonies of the Lower East side. Â So basically alright ramen, but not really worth the price. Â On the plus side, the servers are very cute and friendly and totally let me loiter around at a table while I waited for my late friends to get there and didn't pressure me to get out, despite the growing crowds of people waiting to get in. Â  Sorry Minca, Ippudo still beats you out for quality ramen in NYC.
Love, love, love this place! The food is wonderful and the atmosphere is very romantic.

I loooove the alley. It's one of the coolest nooks of NYC, and I am so happy to finally patronize a business there. I have to stop ordering Filet Mignon. I think I don't actually like Filet Mignon! The food was great, not spectacular. I expected slightly better. I ordered such fancy things as plums wrapped in bacon with blue cheese, filet mignon, and a pumpkin popover. I got a jalapeno-infused tequila cocktail. Also great but not spectacular. I am a real snob though. We had to wait half an hour for a table. While that's not too long of a wait, we are organized enough to make reservations. Yet they apparently only take reservations over 6 people. I hate that. All of these old faux-rustic places throw me into an artistic crisis. Did they intentionally make it look old, or did they preserve a relic? If the latter, how did people back then respond to this place, and what would they think of us? I'm starting to get resentful of this trend. And all the candles near old books on wooden shelves made me really nervous. This place Â is a real fire hazard.

I get it, WIlliamsburg is full of some awesome food joints, you can get pretty much any kind of hipster food here---but if we are in the area and my friends are begging me to try someplace new, I say nay! We are going back to Pies N Thighs! The fried chicken box is a must if you're a first timer--once the biscuits come, it is a rite of passage that you smear it with a drizzle of honey. Don't ask. Just do. Only then are you truly ready. The Deliciously crisp chicken is a crowd pleaser, especially when dipped into a combination of honey and hot sauce. I absolutely love pairing it with a side of collard greens--slightly sour yet a great balance to the indulgent fried chicken. Should you be looking to obliterate your diet plan even further, you can opt for the decadant mac and cheese--drizzled with a little bit of hot sauce, this side is truly a popular favorite. Don't dare leaving Pies N Thighs without testing their prize line-up of desserts! Any and all pies are awesome, but my favorite is their donuts. Moist, delicious and completely acceptable to purchase 10 of them as take-out and lie to your friends saying they're for your family, but you're actually just going to eat them later after midnight in the closet--especially if it's their pecan donuts.

Alta is a very nice little place. Especially as a result of scanning reviews on Yelp, we choose NOT to give waiter our order for courses as we went. This helped pace the meal nicely for a more leisurely dining experience. We found many of the dishes mentioned in this space to be enjoyable with particuar mention to the short ribs (albeit a bit on the salty side). Service was good but not very warm and/or friendly.

The Victorian atmosphere was a little over the top, but I love a theme! I loved the LONG marble bar and large room. Service was pretty fast even though the place was packed. There was a HUGE selection of beers and the food looked good. Overall a great bar in a convenient location! Â Looking forward to visiting again!

Ruined my diet, had to wait in line, only serves beer, service model reminiscent of a Chipotle: AND IT WAS GREAT. You walk in, and the hostess tells you there's a bit of a wait, despite several open tables. Â Confusing, but I see something strange is going on as there's a line snaking around the counter - people are placing their orders and picking up paper boxes at the cash register. Â You can skip the line, though, to order a beer - so I tried a wheat brew that wasn't awful (I really don't drink beer.) Hostess came over, pointed us in the direction of two stools at the wall, over which we put our coats and got in line. Â The menu is pretty simple: Meats, single portions or by-the-pound. Â Chicken, Brisket, Ribs, Pulled Pork...all the usual suspects. Â Sides: edamame salad, baked beans, cole slaw, sweet potato casserole. I went for the pulled pork, sans bun, which was awesome with homemade bbq sauce. Â Tom had the brisket, which was charred and salty. Â Both were so good, not too fatty, and not overly ridiculous portions so you don't feel like hell afterwards. Â The sides, however, were really my favorite - the sweet potato, maple and walnut casserole was outrageous, and I loved the baked beans too! A fun alternative to Hill Country if you're looking for awesome meats and southern sides, in a unique atmosphere, right in the EV.

everyone has an opinion. it's true! i mean, f*ck, i use yelp. of course i want you all to know what i think. but, as far as i am concerned, i think the ear inn's burger is not good. i like burgers; i eat them whenever they are available, especially if everyone raves. raves including but not limited to; best burger in new york, best burger ever, best burger on the west side, etc. so, i came all the way from brooklyn to go to lunch here. it's WAY over on the west side, and contrary to what the map says, the ear inn is not technically INSIDE the holland tunnel. i order the legendary burger and while i wait, i take in the old OLD bar, dusty ephemera and quite a few business lunch drinkers. i like the bar part. i love old things. dusty old man bar spaces. burger came. man alive. dry. boring. NOT medium-rare (i.e. no bloody juice). i didn't finish it. that's saying something. so, i guess people like this place, but i am not one of those people.

This falafel is just as good as Bobby Flay said it was on Throwdown, which is how I heard of it. Â The flavor of the green falafel sandwich was definitely by far the best falafel I've ever had (it blew Mamoun's away, for me). Â I can't wait to go back. Â I'd like to try everything there.

Busy and loud, hustle & bustle - great for after theater family dining so portions are large - for two of us one order was enough for dinner & lunch the next day - given the size of the portions a great value for very well prepared tastey food.

At first I thought you buy stuff from the counters and the seated areas are like a food court where you eat it. Â Nope. Â Basically, look above, there are signs that indicate mini "restaurants" serving ONLY: Vegetables, Fish, Pasta/Pizza, ETC. Â So basically, you have to choose what kind of food you want to eat prior to sitting. Â I wanted pasta, my boy wanted fish. Â Of course, we ate pasta. Both things ordered were yum: Spaghettone Cacio e Pepe: $14. This wins. Â Creamy, buttery sauce, w fresh black pepper. Â REALLY SIMPLE, DONE WELL, DELICIOUS. Pasta was super AL DENTE...mmmmmmm Paccheri al Sugo di Mare: $18. Â Red color w a spice kick. Â Al Dente pasta as well. Â Clams, shrimp, friends of the ocean, you get the idea. Though the quoted wait times are long, if you stand around they will usually seat you a lot faster. Â Otherwise, time flies when you go to look at the products in the shop. Â It is a fun Â unusual place, but only a mad man would come here looking for a peaceful meal. Â This place is a freaking ZOO.

LOVE LOVE LOVE! Ok I think I might actually like it better than Ippudo, I know, that's like insane. Â I loved this place. Â The wait was a bit annoying (30 min Sat. 6pm) but kind of expected since Ippudo have 3 hour lines sometimes. So the place is extremely tiny, they pretty much have bar seats and only a few tables. The pork is amazing! It is fatty but it doesn't make you feel like it's too oily at all, just mouthwatering deliciousness. The broth is also quite good but not overwhelming with salt and fat. Compared to Ippudo, I liked the pork here better and the broth as well. Â I also tried their squid skewers which again was amazing. Â Very very satisfying all around. Side note, they don't do take out, delivery, or even doggie bags, so only order what you can finish. Very ODD! And cash only, which again, very annoying! Â  It was also awesome to watch the cute boy work his way around in the kitchen because it is totally open to the bar so you can see everything. =)

Best Thai food in the city, hands down. More authentic, tastier, and spicier than any other thai place I've tried. They have a super extensive menu and most of the stuff is awesome! This is a huge restaurant with a beautiful outdoor seating area. You can also get a lot of tasty looking food and dessert that's already made to go. I notice there were lots of thai families eating out here as well which is a great sign. I don't think I've ever seen that at the other thai places I've been to! What we had: thai coffee with milk $3- very good, sweet, mocha-y tom yum soup small $5- sour, spicy, delicious. perfectly cooked shrimp chicken coconut soup small $5- sweet, and smooth soup. good! crispy watercress salad- loved the seafood and spicy sauce that accompanies the watercress crisps. green curry with duck- such good curry! goes great with the coconut rice soft shell crab with garlic, chile, etc $18- a good deal for soft shell crab. Very crispy! Wish there was more of a sauce Steamed thai sea bass- $25- what?! so cheap for a whole steam fish! delicious! Pad thai- I've had better pad thai. Flavor wise, it was alright, but the consistency of the noodle was mushy and sticky. The service could've been better at this place though. Things came out very sporadically and you have to catch them or else, they don't come back for a while. Bottom line is I am not going to another Thai place again.

Super fabulous that this place is open 24 hours. Â My friends and I tried the entire dessert menu and were not disappointed. Â Even after a full dinner, looking at the entrees of the people around me had me drooling.
Loved the drinks selection and the food was great too! I recommend the grapefruit grog and the truffle fries!

I have to be honest I was very disappointed with Emporio. However, because it was completely due to service I'm giving it three stars. A friend and I went here looking for a lunch spot. They had a sandwich board outside advertising a pre fixed 15 dollar lunch. However, upon arrival they said they switch to dinner at 4. REALLY? This was followed by a 5 minute wait at the hostess stan while the manager was yelling at the hostess for supposedly throwing away the lunch menus. In the end my famished friend and I, not wanting to spend the cash on dinner, ordered a bowl of Â soup. Of course not satisfying our hunger pangs, but It was fine. Â Hopefully, I'll have a better experience the next time around.

After a long awaited journey, I finally trekked all the way to Totto Ramen to gorge upon The RAMEN of all ramens. Blistering cold, snow, sleet and rain in the middle of the afternoon; and yet, the foyer of Totto was packed with angry, disgruntled customers. That's when I figured out this place is the real deal. Having to wait a measly fifteen minutes (because sadly I was dining for one), there was a target on my back because the wait list wasn't getting any shorter, I scurried in and quickly took my seat. It's quite and experience to see where and how all the magic happens and I think this is one of the most unique things about this place. Totto ensures the customer that making and crafting ramen is not just a streamline process but it's truly an art that gives birth to a scrumptious, hot piping soup to be enjoyed by all walks of life. The chicken ramen was my optimal choice. Word to the wise, extra add-ons are a MUST. Since I was a novice, the bamboo shoots and seasoned boiled egg were the only options I chose. Next time, the spicy bamboo shoots will be my victim. Chicken broth, simply exquisite and it was the perfect dish to power me through a brutal, wintry day. The ramen was perfectly cooked and neither too soft or too chewy, just the right consistency. Could have used a few extra slivers of chicken to compliment my ramen but I guess that's why they have add-ons for a reason. Regardless of that fact, is was still a very filling meal. Totto Ramen, you have truly outdone yourself. You deserve to be hailed as a master among all ramens and gladly submit to your each and every will.

Wow, what a great find! I had dinner here the other night with my good friend, and it was the perfect place to catch up and eat some delicious food. The menu has all my favorites: risotto, panini, pizza...and lots of interesting wine choices. Others have commented that the portions are too small which I don't really agree with--my friend and I had a panini each and the hazelnut torte and it was definitely just the right amount of food. The wine list is a little daunting at first because it's just organized by red and white and there are lots of (fun, interesting) unfamiliar varietals, but the prices are friendly so that helped me not be so scared. I picked somewhat blindly, but was very happy with my wine. I think this place probably has a pretty good wine-expert behind the list, so I wouldn't worry too much about picking something you don't know. All in all a fantastic place.

Having read a positive review in the NY Times (two years ago) and having also read many positive reviews online, we looked forward to eating at this restaurant (in early 7/08). Â The food was indeed really delicious and the interior was charming. Â *However*; the service was inattentive (for example: Â we had to ask for more water *three times* over a period of at least ten minutes before finally receiving it [and it's not like our server ever bothered to notice that we had almost no water left]). Â Plus; when I added up the bill, I discovered we'd been way overcharged for the borscht. Â I brought it to the attention of our server and he brusquely informed me that we'd ordered cold borscht. Â Indeed we had - but he never told us there was an extra charge, *nor* was it mentioned on the menu. Â In fact; when I pointed to the borscht and asked if it was cold or hot, he said "you can have it either way". Â Initially he wouldn't budge on the price, but finally he gave us (each) a whopping $1 off (we were still overcharged by much more). Â Too bad for him, because we decreased his tip accordingly. I'm giving five stars for the food and one star for the service, for a rating of three stars.

I heard about this place from a somewhat unlikely source, one of my fiance's professors. Apparently he comes here all the time and loves it. Cant say I blame him either. to start we got the red, white, and blue special which, as every one here says, is a great great deal. I don't drink so she got a glass of the white and we shared the oysters which were fresh as can be plump (seriously two were as long as my hand) and briny and just delicious. We also got the angels on horseback because honestly why wouldn't you. If you like oysters and you like bacon you'll like these. And if you don't like oysters or bacon ... get that looked at cause there's something wrong. So yeah that app is raw oysters wrapped in bacon with a cocktail sauce on top. Absolutely divine. The salty bacon with the fresh sweet oyster and the spicy cocktail sauce... it has everything. For the entree I had the fish and chips and a bowl of the lobster bisque. She had a pan roasted snapper with BBQ shrimp and cheddar grits. first the portions are big which is nice. Second the food is top notch which is better. My fish and chips was the best I have had yet. The batter was light and crispy the fish flaky and tender and the tartar sauce was really good. It was sweet and tangy and I think (as does my fiance) that they put a little apple in it to give it the sweet. The fries were also very good. I'm not one to rave about fries, but as far as they go these were nice and crispy outside and smooth and fluffy inside.. so yeah just right. Her Fish was perfectly cooked and nicely seasoned, the grits were great, the shrimp though .. kinda lacked. They were maybe a little over done and their BBQ sauce wasn't that great. But that was the only misstep of the night. Service was great always checking in just to make sure things were okay and clearing as things were finished. Its a bit cramped inside but despite that it was still very comfortable which can't always be said for small restaurants. Will I come back here ... you bet I will and we'll probably get two RWB specials this time.

Greatness: Amy Ruth's in a word is greatness. The food was very fresh (I had the honey dipped fried chicken) and required a next-day gym venture (but no complaints on that end...I ate some of the skin, but what I was supposed to do, it was dipped in honey? ). Â  Â  Â  Â  Â  Â Parking: a pain...a real pain but for some of that food, a gas price debate is superfluous. Â  Â  Â  Â  Â  Â The only annoying part: I believe they are expanding, so there was some drilling going on next door (to the point of pictures on the wall about to come tumbling down). Â  Â  Â  Â  Â  Â  Check out the clothing shop next door. Good deals there and some nice sneakers. Food and sneakers, my day was made.

I can respect the concept, it is a license to print money. My issue is say with Berkshire Pork, you could certainly taste the difference if it was grilled or sauted but to coat it with brown sugar and cinnamon and smoke it all night is going to muddy the flavor and ruin the reason for eating it. You eat Berkshire to have a nice med rare double chop or medium Berkshire Porterhouse. Â It is good, it is actually better cold or room temp so you can taste the sweet and spicy in the bark. Burbons are pretty pricey so stick to beer. The sweet tea is also from a bottle, not home made. Again, this concept is sleek and clean and prime for franchising. I would buy in. Oh, and they gave us the bone with our short rib, giving us our grand prize of a $20 short rib bone!

Great little place that specializes on spatinental cuisine. According to their website this is "their brand of healthy food prepared with farm-fresh, locally grown and wholesome ingredients. It is inspired by Mediterranean and Asian cuisine, using ingredients such as cilantro, ginger, soy, sun-dried tomatoes and pesto to liven up the sandwiches, salads and entrees." Also nice mood music sets the tone.

Picked up take out on Saturday night, not only there was a line, they also were out of most things on the menu. I got Kofta and my hasband got a mix grill of chicken and beef. I thought both dishes were very good and huge size. My husband is a big guy and he can eat but even for him it was two meals and for me 3 meals. I think we will back to try much raved falafel.

Love this place! The lamb taco is SO good! Succulent is the word everyone I was with decided was most appropriate to describe it. Margarita are made nice and strong. Had two of them and was feeling nice and toasty. The food is so cheap, unfortunately the liquor is not. We got a round of tequila shots which were 10 each...but I guess alcohol is never cheap. Anywas, I will definitely be back! To try that cactus taco and flan. This place is popping so make a reservation! It'll save you time , and make sure your whole party is with you! What are you waiting for? GO!!

Hands down the best Greek restaurant in NYC. Started with spreads and then grilled calamari with chick peas, which was perfectly prepared. Then had the waiter guide me and ordered the duck baklava with figs. I didn't want to put the fork down. Â The side of mashed potatoes and feta was beyond delicious and the baklava for dessert was the icing on the cake. Will definitely be a regular here.

Very, very good, and very, very interesting. Beer-based macaron with caviar filling? Check. I've only eaten at one other Michelin rated restaurant, and that was the former 3 star Robuchon in Las Vegas (it's no longer ranked, but I've heard not because it was stripped, but because Michelin no longer writes a guide for Vegas). Atera is "only" a two star, but in terms of technical skill I feel Atera completely blows away Robuchon, while being a better deal as well. As is normal for creative foods, you may not *love* everything, but you'll be hard pressed not to recognize the creativity and artistry. There was really only one item that I thought was lacking - the heart of palm with bone marrow ragout, but the rest were pleasant or interesting surprises. I'll have to post up the menu later, but there were far more tastings than I thought. At around tasting #7, I thought I had made a terrible mistake, thinking that I had overpaid and that the meal was soon coming to an end. Nope. By tasting 15, I was getting pretty full, but it keeps on going well into the 20s! Service was excellent. The restaurant is cleaned every 3 hrs or so, and it's just very cool to watch the staff do their thing. Disciplined, like a fine, precision watch. After the meal, I was invited to tour the downstairs kitchen, where there is another set of staff that do prep. After nerding out over the chef's copy of The Modernist Cuisine, I nerded out over the overhead heavy duty, reeled power cables, and the racks and racks of Oxo-housed ingredients. Definitely cool.
great reverse pizza sauce on top of cheese gets busy and very crowded but they maintain great customer service i go there anytime i can

Love love love this place I've been going to Caracas for over 5 years now (ever since I saw them on throw down with bobby flay). Always go for the same arepa de pabellon and I just don't have the words to describe the taste yummy!! The service i give 2 stars to, you almost always have to flag down a waiter for attention. The restaurant is pretty pricy for a quick munch and it's always packed try to go for lunch if you really want a table. Enjoy :)

Another one of my favorite places for brunch. I usually go here on weekends and the place is packed! Go figure, their foods great. I fell in love with their Nutella French toast and pesto breakfast croissant. I've also tried the benedicts and omlets. It's a cozy place.

Have been going to this place for awhile now. Have not had a bad meal yet. It is very unique restaurant with a changing menu. The chefs list where they get their ingredients from which are either from local organic farms around NY, NJ and PA. Has an nice selection of wines and beers. Come early around 6ish to avoid the lones.

Sooo happy for these guys, a crowded, happy restaurant 2 weeks into it. Doing justice to the interesting, authentic choices on Avenue C (for cuisine?) Steampunk meets dried florals and some rope & iron things, shelves with objects.... Â Ingenious lighting in the warped wood of the ceiling. Best music. Â you can't believe it was the horrible chinese takeout place. Comfortable and welcoming, delicious 'freakin' salad, the perfect schnitzel, a ravioli with apples, onions and pine nuts. Gracious waitstaff, excellent recommendation on the wine. Really wonderful, can't wait to be back.

This is the freshest Thai food you can get. Â Yes, you are going to pay more than your local dive Thai place but it is well worth it. Â The papaya salad is among the freshest things I have tasted, the Chiang Mai "fries" and coconut-accented corn chowder are a delicious treat, and the basil chicken is dee-lish. Â Definitely place a half order for the chicken dish - the portion is HUGE! Highly recommend this place for its great ambiance and fresh, delicious flavors!

BRUNCH REVIEW: Don't be fooled by what I'm about to say. I expected brunch to be a long wait, but I didn't expect the estimated 30 minute wait to turn into 1 hour and 30 minutes. Â Not to mention, the host FORGOT about us and when confronted, he played it off like he didn't forget and that he knew we would "want to have our own table to ourselves".... which is why he let other people in first. But once we went inside... we had to share a table regardless!! TOTALLY PLAYED US!!!!!! Â But lucky for him, I don't judge a restaurant's service and staff on a one-time experience.. the weekend crowds must be rough for him. Besides that, where to begin? BYOB!!!!!! They generously chill your beverage for you in their fridge while you wait for your table. Â Buy yourself a bottle of dessert wine, or a bottle of champagne and make your own Mimosas. I HIGHLY Recommend: -Discot Tots, VERY generous on the proportions. -Roasted Pork & Apple Cabbage Empanadas, better than your average empanada. -Chicken & Waffles, don't need to say anymore! -"Down By Law" Eggs Benedict, each bite feels like a potential heart-attack but it would be so worth it! I DON'T Recommend: -Breakfast Nachos, oh boy what was I thinking? It was pretty much a giant omelette on top of nachos..bleh. Â  -Atomic Fire Balls, I just hate it when restaurants try to sell you Sriracha. It should be a free condiment like Ketchup. -The Pig Mac (non-brunch item).. when I read all the good reviews about the brunch food items, I should have listened. But of course I had to try The Pig Mac sandwich ..which I deeply regret. I was basically force feeding myself to finish it, leaving no room for the rest of the good food. Ambiance was slightly below average, but the food makes up for it. Â Definitely a place to bring your friends....if you guys don't mind waiting!

Just an awesome slice of your "not-so-NYC- typical-slice" of Â pizza. The artichoke pizza is intense, and if you are not ready for it, the flavor will knock your taste buds into the next millennium! The crust is thick with a solid crunch, the sauce is ever-so creamy, and the cheese is aplenty! You can only really eat just one slice before you OD on the artichoke and spinachy goodness, so eating more is not recommended! The crab slice is also an interesting find, however, it lies second to the main attraction and the more-than-often forgotten stepchild to the artichoke and spinach slice. If you haven't been infected by the gooey yumminess of the artichoke slice, try the crab slice first, go home, recover, and come back the next day for the artichoke. A great find!
Everything here is good, everything. Feeling overworked? Add some truffle to your lunch - or pesto, basil has to make you happy.

Love their pancakes!!!!! Yum! Have also had their mussels, they were ok, not impressed with that, but great coffee! Â Watercress salad was good too! Â This is a great spot for outdoor dining, and picking up coffee to go. Â Hate drinking out of mason jars, that's just too trendy for me.

This restaurant is hands-down, the best meal I have ever had! Â We've been to Babbo, Mesa Grill, and many of the popular eateries in NYC and this place blew them away! Â We had the tasting menu and every single course was great. I can't believe this place has been around for a couple of years and it took me so long to find it. Â We're already planning our return.

Definitely enjoyed this place. Came for my bachelorette dinner. Â We had a large table downstairs (there were seven of us.) The restaurant was super busy (it was a Saturday night) but our server was still very attentive. We had ceviche appetizers, mojitos, and several of the entrees and loved them ALL! I honestly can't remember if we had dessert, but I do remember they gave us rum shots before we left. The prices were reasonable for a New York restaurant. Â They were extremely accommodating when my MOH was booking the large party. Â If you have a group and want to try something fun, consider Cuba.
Good food, good vibes.

I absolutely loved this place. It has three floors - the first floor was completely empty, but the tiny 2nd floor bar was pretty full. My date and I managed to grab a table and order some happy hour drinks - nothing spectacular, $5 wines and sangria. Our food was AMAZING. I ordered the scallop and shrimp skewers, and they were perfectly cooked and seasoned. The sauce was so good - tangy and sweet. My date ordered the mushroom ravioli, which was very good, but a very small portion. Our entrees were pretty much the same price ($15-$16) but mine was certainly a better values. Seriously, those shrimps and scallops were MASSIVE. We will be back for sure. I think this is the best $50 dinner we have had yet in Manhattan. I'm not sure why people call it a tourist trap - maybe because it is on Restaurant Row? It's not at all, and the bars on the 2nd and 3rd floor are super cute.

I use to go all the way to Brooklyn for my banh mi sandwich crave, not anymore joju is my new banh mi home. For the past month I have tried the pork sandwich, chicken and the Korean banh mi not once have I've been disappointed with the quality,size and taste. They also make killer bubble teas which save me the trouble of having to go to quickly for my drinks. joju thank you for the good service I look forward to my next vist

This review is coming after a couple of months from being there. Â What i can tell you is this if you love tapas, you are a foodie fool for not going there!! Do you understand me. Â It has been a couple of months since being there but I still remember how amazing it was. Â They make this dish with Brussels spouts and it will blow you away, so what we ordered it twice! The layout is pretty nice and even though we were seated in a small area in the back that you had to walk through the kitchen, it was well worth it to get a glimpse of how the magic is done in this place. Bacon wrapped dates, shrimp and chroizo , all of it was delicious and size portion was perfect for two people. Â The menu has enough to choose from so that it would satisfy any foodie with any preferences. Â  A couple of tips, makes reservations and bring cash. Â I think they only take cash or AMEX.

The place looks great, warm (i love the room in the back, with the fire place), music is not too loud, and the decor is very well "french-ised", actually. But let's talk about the FOOD! We went there for dinner, 6 of us. French, some living in New York, some visiting from France. We took advantage of being 6 to order a lot of dishes of the (long) menu : appetizers, main courses and desserts, passing forks and spoons to one another. And everything was very, very good! Appetizers were wonderful and originally paired (the duck and barley moved some of us), the steak tartare was very delicate (quail eggs, horseradish...) and obviously made with a very good meat. And so on. When the main courses came, our eyes wide opened : meat like coq au vin was delicious with an unctuous and rich and super tasty sauce (and as French people living in New York, Â believe us, we taste a lot of mediocre coq au vin), the lamb ragout was stunning, the kind of dish that you finish with your bread to wipe every drop of sauce (yes, we kept ordering bread all night). And then the FISH... We tried the skate, the tuna and a salmon as a special. Being a little nervous since it was white tuna, and white tuna is easily dry. It was for me the best surprise of the night. These pieces of fish were incredibly well cooked, seared, etc! Soft, moist, tender, TASTY!... Honestly, we really felt that our plates were exceptional that night. Not to mention the garnishing, very nice and modestly complex (purple potatoes, shaved fennel, pattypan squash...). The desserts were great : a place where the ice creams are made onsite always has my favors! For me, le Barricou is a hidden wonderful bistrot, honoring the new "bistronomy" movement, where simple food and high and technical gastronomy are associated on the table. Bravo! ps : one last thing! Wine is very reasonably priced.

i'm usually a fan of the crispy thin fries, but these fat belgian fries are just as yummy and crispy. it's a large serving so it will fill you up. the sauce choices are excellent. my favorite is the vietnamese pineapple. M and i also tried the mexican ketchup which was only ok and the bleu cheese whuch we found to be too strong. i say go for the sauces you know you won't find anywhere else especially if you're from out of town. the next time i'm in nyc again, this is definitely a must.
This place was delicious. Â Quaint little spot with a small menu. Nice selection of wine though.

I'm sorry to say that with only one previous visit (which resulted in adverse stomach issues for two patrons), my second visit was a total disappointment - Not related to food, but service related instead. This was one of those situations where my party was unable to pass go. 2 persons of a three party arrived to be seated. We were denied seating - the entire party had to be present. When asked could we order drinks while we waited. Again we were denied service. A total disappointment.

I ate here during a dinner function, so it seems like my experience is a bit different from the majority of other reviewers who came for brunch or walked in for a dinner. I was pleasantly surprised to find that the atmosphere was casual for its location on the upper west side. All of the restaurant's staff were very polite and friendly, and the servers were very attentive. All of the food was good (I wouldn't go as far as to say it was spectacular), and the presentation was especially nice. The most memorable part of the meal for me was the dark chocolate "bag" I had for dessert, which was quite literally a bag formed out of dark chocolate filled with fruit, raspberry mousse, and topped with whipped cream. Although it was difficult to eat, it was very amusing and really tasty. I would say this is a great place to eat if you're in the upper west side looking for some place to go.

I chose to try this place with couple of my friends for a Sunday lunch and it was one of the best decisions I've made in a long time. Started off with a plate of fried green tomatoes which had a a nice crunch and lots of flavor from the toppings, and a plate of poutine which was the best I have had so far in NYC. Ordered the House special which was also great, but the star of my entree was definitely the potato salad. The plate itself didn't look that big but it was definitely filling. Will definitely go back!

Overall food is good. Giving it 3 stars instead of 4 because it took around an hour and half for the food to be delivered at work. Lesson learned: order way ahead of time and remember to ask for hot sauce on the side because they are not included in the order.

My wife and I were extremely hungry - but decided to wait for 1 hour based Â on the reviews here on Yelp. Â This was our first time having ramen - so we didn't know what to expect. First and foremost - the service was awesome. Â The servers were extremely friendly and helpful. Â Even though the place was packed to the brim, our waiter took the time to explain the different ramen choices to us. Â He didn't rush us at all. For an appetizer we ordered the pork Hirata Buns. Â We loved them. Â They have a spicy mayo/mustard sauce on them (which I guess is a Japanese thing) that is unforgettable. Â Definitely order these if you like chashu pork. Â My wife loved them because they reminded her of manapua from our trip to Hawaii. For dinner, Â my wife ordered the Akamaru Modern with Nitamago. Â Definitely great ramen - but it lacked the flavor of my dish. I ordered the Karaka Miso Ramen with Nitamago. Â Definitely spicier (not too spicy), definitely more flavor. For dessert, we asked if they had some type of mochi ice cream - but unfortunately they don't. If you are in the city and are craving ramen - definitely stop at Ippudo - but be prepared to wait.

Good price, great food and the guys at the counter are actually really nice. We hit this up for a late 'dinner' after we missed our reservation and just needed something to get us fed and in the mood to booze. For the rest of the weekend, I have had falafel withdrawal. The only knock is that it can get so crowded and uncomfortable in there, and there is nowhere to sit or hang out. Still, this place is worth a check-in.
pan slices are great here

don't waster your time & effort waiting in line trying to taste 2nd tier ramen. just go to "ippudo"! it's 2 dollar cheaper, but tase, quality sucks. if you will wait, ensure to sign name in 30min before the opening and wait there, or they will take your name off.

I'd give it two or maybe even three stars if I were younger for its youthful ambiance. Â The decor is fun and the the staff look like they are enjoying themselves. But, for me it's just too loud and the food was ewwww. Â It feels like a good place to go with a big group for drinks if you don't really want to talk to one another, if that makes sense. Â The food is pan-Latin American meaning the menu is way ambitious. Â I had a number of their empanadas and they were down right terrible. Â  Â My husband ordered their arepas w/ cheese and wow, they were like flat pounded discs with a slab of melted cheese on top?? I was really confused. Â I don't know if the house has a specialty that could redeem this place in terms of food and I hate to say it but I don't think you could drag me there again.

Let me start by saying that the decor is very nice. The sushi is pretty good. Each piece is shaped exactly the same size (sort of an ellipse rectangle). The service was really excellent. My sake cup gets its own cute bamboo floor mat of its own. Maybe sushi is ordered differently in New York or maybe just at Yasuda but in L.A. each order comes with 2 pieces. Not a big deal, just something to note so you always have to say the exact number of pieces. I can see why others might give this place a poor review based on the host. He basically wants you to dine at the restaurant no more than 1 1/2 hours. I get it, it's popular and the place seats around 40. Usually sushi restaurants display their fish through the window display at the bar for a very specific reason (transparency). For the purpose of nice decor, the glass window is replaced with bamboo. Rather than showing you their fish through the window, they mark Â the fish that is fresh that day on the menu sheet with a red pen (since you can't see the fish at the bar). Again, this is also minor. The thing that I did have an issue with is the fact that the sushi chef decided on my behalf just how much soy sauce and/or ponzu sauce to put on my nigiri so that the sushi comes pre-sauced (on stuff that is normally not sauced at all). I also noticed that there were pieces of kosher salt on my nigiri. Let me just say that I've eaten at lots of very good and usually expensive sushi restaurants in Los Angeles but never have I had a chef decide for me to pre-sauce my sushi (especially since I did not order omakase). If that was what they were going to do, then don't put soy sauce on my table because the message you're sending is that I still have control over my own soy sauce and wasabi. It's one thing to order something that naturally comes with sauce like unagi, albacore with ponzu sauce but it's not normal that simple yellowtail, salmon have sauce. I know some people like ponzu on their salmon and I've even seen jalapenos on yellowtail but to me that just detracts from the simplicity of the original taste. I will say that the sushi was very good but pre-saucing a normally un-sauced piece of nigiri bothers me and is the reason why this place gets 3.5 stars rather than 4 stars. It lost 1/2 a point for pre-saucing my nigiri and the general snottiness of "we're exclusive and we don't need your business" attitude.

With a party of 8 during a holiday week and on a Thursday finding a reservation was a bit hard but, Emporio pulled through. Yay for that. They don't seat you until your full party is there which was a bit annoying but once seated in the back room, life is good. The restaurant itself is so charming and for being as large as it is nailed ambiance. Rustic, candles every where, light music in the back ground, this place is perfect for a casual get together, date night or what have you. The menu consists of a few gourmet pasta options, salads, a few entrees of the likes of chicken under a brick, steak, etc..as well as brick oven pizza; something for everyone. I myself went with the pizza with mozzarella, broccoli rabe, sausage and hot peppers. It was really good. I would have liked that the hot peppers actually be hot peppers not just flakes but, other than that the pizza was large, filling and solidly good if a little bland. A little kick at all to the pizza would definitely have me up the review. The wine list is extensive with a nice variety of wines organized by regions in Italy. If wine isn't your thing the beer list isn't as extensive but, definitely had some nice gems on it including Six Point. Overall, this place is warm, inviting and has a great ambiance with a large variety of options for even the pickiest eaters and at a reasonable price makes this spot a great option in the 'hood.

Fresh Salt is my favorite restaurant in the South Street Seaport. It's a block away from all of the madness and has two of my favorite dishes downtown. 1. The Salt Sandwich is delicious, you have to try it. 2. Quiche specials, they come with a small salad and are amazing. It's a great spot for lunch and late night drinks, while I've never gone for brunch I am sure it's pretty good as well. Keep in mind it's a small and cozy spot, so if you have a large group it might take a while to snag a seat.

I don't need to write as long of a review as the people below, we just had bad food and atrocious service, and we were charged a lot of money for it. We got the pre-fix: - were seated 45 minutes late despite having a reservation - courses were brought completely out of order - we had a party of 9, received our courses"family style", but got fewer than 9 portions for each course - two of our courses were under-cooked - the drink pairings showed up late--we'd get the pairing after we finished a course and were on to the next one - at no point were made to feel like this was anything less than business as usual, and totally reasonable. The food that was cooked was good, so it was a shame.

This is my first Yelp review ever because the kindness of the people at La Goulette cannot go unwritten about. I just went in to get takeout for dinner (I'd been there before and had a freaking AWESOME merguez sandwich, so I decide to go back). I ask the middle-aged woman at the counter 17 questions because I don't know what I want, and she is all smiles and helpful answers. I decide on a salad after pondering the babaghanoush. She asks if I want a side of it because it's apparently super delicious. I say no, it will be too much food with the salad (but also because I didn't want to pay 4 more dollars). I pay and sit to wait for my salad to take home. Suddenly, I hear her calling my name (which she has learned form seeing my credit card and is miraculously pronouncing correctly). She has made the cutest little dish of babaghanoush and pita chips for me to try while I wait. Seriously, it was the sweetest thing ever. I'm smiling, and saying, "Oh my goodness, thank you!" The dude at the counter is smiling, saying "It's really good, right?" (Which it is. Smoky, eggplanty, creamy goodness). It is basically an all-around babaghanoush love fest. They have my salad ready, and the dude asks if he's put enough hot sauce on my salad. I ask for a bit more because I like things spicy (such awesome customer service). My salad (which I am now eating, and it is fresh and yummy) is waiting in a bag on the counter, and the woman tells me to take my time with my delicious babaghanoush sample. So I do. Basically, this story illustrates the lovely family-run feel of La Goulette. Put with their delicious Mediterranean/North African food (frankly way better/less greasy than other places serving pita sandwiches and the like), it is among my favorite low-key takeout options in Williamsburg. LA GOULETTE, JE T'ADORE!!!
Awesome atmosphere and friendly staff. The Hamachi Tartar, Charred Octopus & Pumpkin Tiramisu are incredible.

Love the vibe here. Â Borderline-speakeasy style, it smells fabulous inside (when was the last time you were in a fresh-scented bar?!) and the crowd is fabulous-looking. Â You know I love that. Â Only spotted 1 group of tourists last night and even they were acceptable-looking. Â I shall make this my regular after-work hang. Didn't try the food, but it certainly smelled yummy. Â For a nice refreshing cocktail, try the West (but only if you like lemon/lime tartness). Â Most cocktails run $13. Â If you're feeling spendy, spring for the Billionaire's Drink ($15) but make sure you like the taste and smell of Bourbon. The psychic out front is a cute idea but save your money. Â I dropped $20 on her on a whim and my "reading" was more vague and scripted as I could've ever imagined.

Finally got to try this place out with my boyfriend!! Â The place is warm and inviting. Â The bar is located right in the front of the restaurant. Â There are a few tables in the front. Â There are more tables in the back of the restaurant and the back of the place is the open kitchen. Â We got there about 10 minutes after five on a friday night. Â There was only one other couple there, but by around 5:30, the place was getting packed! Â So I suggest you go early! Â Also, don't forget, this place is CASH ONLY!! Â the waiters are all very nice. Â They come by with a jug of water and the plastic gloves and they even tie your bib for you! Â :) Â  Everything is disposable, so you get these little paper plates and plastic utensils. Â For me, I didn't really like that they give you plastic gloves (like the ones you see in medical offices). Â I work in health care, and for me, those gloves might have things on them that are not good when ingested. Â I would have preferred the cheaper kind of gloves ( like those clear, plastic , one size fit all gloves). We ordered the soft shell crab basket- it comes with a little bit of coleslaw, tartar sauce, and french fries. Â It was very yummy! Â The crab is small, but usually softshell crabs are kind of tiny. Â We also ordered a pound of clams and the combo A- it is a pould of shrimp and a pound of crawfish, which comes with a piece of corn on the cob, sausage, and potatoes. Â You can pick any sauce you like, from no sauce, to garlic butter, old bay seasoning, lemon pepper, or the BOIL SPECIAL: which is all the sauces together! Â You also have a choice of spiciness: mild, medium, spicy and fire! Â I am a big wuss and can't take heat, so we opted for the mild (and anyway, old bay seasoning is spicy enough for my liking!) Â We also decided to order a side order of bread (it's garlic bread, they pretty much just used their oyster slider's buns and toasted it with garlic butter). Â The bread is great for moping up the yummy sauce! The food came out pretty fast, and the waiters are very helpeful, always around to clear the table, and change out the shell bucket for you. Â It was kind of awkward eating there because the waiters were waiting by the open kitchen, so I felt like I was being watched. Â The clams were great! Â The clam meats were HUGE and juicy! Â I didn't taste any sand at all, so they cleaned it well. Â I did find empty shells in there ( and I made sure it did not fall into the bag) so that made me a bit sad. Â The shrimps were HUGE, and cooked just right, very juicy, and the brains were yummy. Â The crawfish were also very big and came out of the shell. Â The sauce is great, just enough spiciness to leave my mouth tingling, not at all numbing. Â The sausages were yummy, corn and potatoes were great in the sauce. Â  The seafood I would say was fresh, but my boyfriend did say that he found a couple crawfish kind of gray in color. Â The garlic bread was great dipped in the sauce. Â I just dipped it right into the bag that held the seafood, but if you're uncomfortable doing that, you can always ask for a spoon and just pour it all over the buns! Â You can also get other sides like rice, vermicelli, extra sauce on the side, just to name a few extra sides. Â They also have a wide selection of beer and wine. Â A good place to just relax and hang out and have some fun!

I want to give Cafe Ollin les stars due to the service but I can't because the food is so delicious. The problem with the service is the dine-in wait time. I've been here many, many times and I've never waited less than 45 minutes for my food. This is ridiculous because friends in the neighborhood have told me that if you order delivery, it takes 30 minutes total. I think the restaurant focuses on having really good delivery times but force their dine in customers to wait. I actually sat near the waitress/hostess once, heard her take a telephone order and the person came in to pick up their order, all while I was still waiting for my food. My food arrived about 20 minutes later, even though I had placed my order before that person called in. Not good. I always go when I'm not in a rush. They make some of the best tortas around so I suffer through the long wait.

Go to there. Â Immediately. Â The lamb burger is the best burger I have ever had, ever. Â My family and I have been there about 5 times in the past month, and we are guaranteed an amazing meal everytime. Â Two giant thumbs up to the chef!
Yelp did not lead me astray on this recommendation. The small pizza is huge. We did ours half and half - prosciutto & the blanca. Both were so good and totally what you want when you think NY pizza.
Outstanding food. Loud music. Hipster neighborhood. Â Enjoyable experience. Great prices. Personal favorites were the bacon wrapped dates.
amazing pizza

Same great food as the other locations, less wait! I've been three times and have yet to wait for a table, love the bar area, occasionly stop in for a veggie plate snack! The ambiance is bright and cheery.

have you not tried Sanfords yet? if no then get on it - good for takeout (worth the 45 minute potential wait) or swing by after work (may want to call ahead for reservation, or sit at the bar). solid wine selection available, food has lots of flavor, and solid staff. go go go.

Super cute place. Great to get work done, as there is free wifi (fast) and tons of outlets! The cashier was super friendly, and the excelsior sandwich and kale salad was excellent. Highly recommended :-)

Moto might just be what I miss most about NY. Â How can you beat walking into a hidden spot through a large, tin-clad door, stepping over a washtub bass being played in a band teleported from New Orleans circa 1930, and sitting down for a super-fine meal under an exposed light bulb swinging on 6 feet of old electrical cord. Â A little slice of heaven, shaped like a slice.

I really like the food here, I really do. But what frustrates me each and every time is the spotty and extremely unfriendly staff that work here. Â It doesn't matter that we are plunking down $100 per person, the attitude here seems like they are taking US out for the night instead. Â First of all, the bald waiter with the black rimmed plastic glasses must either have horrible eyesight, deaf ears, or generally pretends to not see us when we practically have to wave and shout him down. Â Yes, I've walked my bill and change over myself twice, that's how bad it was. The hostess was also incredibly rude when we asked her why we could not sit at an empty and non-reserved table by the window (she practically spat out 'because you are five!'). How dare us waste her one precious space. That's it, we've sampled the menu thoroughly. Never going back again.

I wish i could eat this everyday if it wasn't so expensive..but i guess it's worth it. The boyfriend and I decided to come here for dinner and we ordered 2 of the Akamaru Modern ramen and pork buns and they were DELICIOUSS. The most AMAZING AND EXPENSIVE PORK BUNS I HAVE HAD IN MY WHOLE LIFE. Â Knocked one star off because poor me can't afford this everyday. :c

Passed by this place a few weeks ago and just by glancing inside I knew I was going to come back and try it. Â The interior is beautiful! Â All grey, black and silver with a huge chandelier as the centerpiece of the long restaurant. Â Luckily, the food is also just as great! Â I had Tofu Pad Thai with a bowl of Tom Yum soup. Â It was really delicious, came out quickly and perfect portions. Â The staff was very friendly and attentive. Â I never went with an empty drink, which is definitely a must! Added Bonus: Â They have a daily lunch special for about $7 where you can choose from a list of appetizers, entrees and you get a side of rice. Â This leaves more money to spare to try one of their yummy mimosas! They have between 6-8 with different juice combos. Â So fun!

This place was outstanding. I took my fiancÃ© here for his birthday. Â He's obsessed with the food network so I figured i'd give Scott Conant a try. Parking garage was near by which was very convenient. It was Â hard to find but worth the search. When you walk in Â you get that cozy feeling. Everybody was very nice and welcoming. The food was delicious and the portions were decent. Everything was so fresh. I had the duck which came medium rare. It was interesting but rather tasty. My fiancÃ© ordered the octopus ink pasta with seafood. Everything was out of the shell already which made it easier to eat. Overall, our experience at Scarpetta's was a memorable one and I was very pleased with everything. Hearts, Ali&Charlie

Stopped in for a cup of coffee and a quick breakfast, and I didn't want to leave. Â Great little place tucked away from busy 7th, 8th and 9th Avenues in Chelsea for starting a day touring Manhattan. Â Highly recommended!

I have been here many times and am always happy with the food. Â Unfortunately, the dining experience is more than just the quality of the food. Â On my most recent visit to Hillstone I experienced such unprofessional service that it must be addressed. Â It is NEVER acceptable to make your guests feel uncomfortable at a dining establishment. Â I highly recommend some retraining and I'll assume that the lack of professionalism was a result of her inexperience. Â As a lifelong resident of New York City I have been to many restaurants and not once, in my 50 years have I ever experienced anything quite like it. Â Not good. Â At all. Â I will definitely reconsider coming back here given the low bar that is obviously set for staff.Once is too much.

This use to be a little secret spot that my friends and I use to go. Now that the words been out. Everyone comes for their infamous dumplings and such for prices that may be considered pennies in NYC. Simply said their toasted sesame pancake sandwich is great. No matter if you pick the beef, chicken or tuna. Yes folks. They have Tuna as well! So don't just get the pan fried dumplings or the soups. Try other things. Explore your palettes! I'm sure you can fill yourself for less then $10. Down one star due to crazy lines on busy days.
Bread is a bit on the stale side but other than that the Pork Pate, #4, was amazing!!

I went for brunch. I had the eggs benedict, as I am accustomed to having when I go out for a nice brunch. Very delicious, and a bit different than the traditional version. Also, props for this dish since it wasn't swimming in a pool of hollandaise (there was just the appropriate amount). I didn't have a cocktail, but my fellow brunch-goers tried their version of a bloody mary. I had a sip - again, very tasty. I was very pleased with the food. In addition, I had a lovely chat about urban transportation planning with the bartender while I waited for my fellow-brunchers to arrive. Mad props for that! I will definitely be going back in the future - maybe I'll try dinner next time!

Ava and crew are simply the best. Â Yes, you do have to seat yourself and it's pretty much first come first server, but the staff busts their humps Â to help. Â I got there on Friday night at 6:00 and most tables were taken, but stood around a bit and was able to snag one. Â The fried pickles were great and the mac & cheese also good. Â We will definitely come back and there's no doubt that this is a really chill spot in Queens.

Stopped in with my boyfriend late at night. There was not much of a line. Had the famous artichoke slice. Super expensive and looks a lot better than it tasted. It was just a creamy, salty mess. Not worth the billion calories.

I loved my first dinner at The Green Table. Rustic country kitchen feel with the added bonus of exploring Chelsea Market before and after. Kind of a pain that the restaurant doesn't have its own restroom, but the space is just fantastic in every other way. I made a reservation for a small group and we received excellent service. My whole party commented on the many unique options on the menu, and I was especially pleased with the number of vegetarian friendly dishes. I look forward to visiting again when they rotate in a new season's menu.
