I've only been for brunch but it was awesome! Â First off - mad props for the brunch panini names such as Sweet Ass, Sir Oink-a-Lot, Wake and Bake but my favorite was the Notorious P.I.G - word! seriously though - food was great, service was great and the backyard patio was really nice! Â I had the Pass the Hash which was great! Â Highly recommend this place for some good eats!

Soup dumplings were just okay... Some had absolute no soup some had... The reason why I gave them 1 star is because the waiters were absolutely obnoxious. Can not believe how rude they were. Would not comeback here again.

Came here on a Tuesday night and was seated immediately. The restaurant is cozy, the staff is friendly, and their prices are very reasonable. The Black Taglierini black squid ink pasta is amazing. I'm salivating just thinking about it. The flourless chocolate truffle cake is the best flourless chocolate cake I've ever had. It's extremely sweet with some bitterness from the dark chocolate, very heavy, thick, rich, and delicious. It really is like eating pure truffle. I think about it a lot and sometimes day dream about that cake. I want it right now.

Having lived in California and Phoenix, and always seeking out Mexican food, this is some of my favorite in all of New York. It's so fresh, and is just like what you could get at a nice restaurant in Mexico. They grow some of their own veggies in the backyard, the drinks and juices are great and it's good for dinner or brunch. One of my favorites anywhere.

Got in line around on Saturday night at 6:30 pm and waited for about 20 minutes. Â I ordered a combination lamb and chicken plate which was $6.00. Â Given the taste and the value, you really can't go wrong here. Â I usually use a lot of their white tzatziki sauce mixed with just a little bit of the red sauce for a small kick of heat. Â The flavors are excellent. Â The meat is juicy and everything together makes a really delicious meal. Â Service is rushed, but it's a cart and they're interested in moving volume. Â Overall, an excellent cheap eat that I end up craving. Â I will definitely go back.

Stopped at Joe's for dinner while visiting NY and was impressed! I highly suggest the pork dumplings - they are excellent and great for sharing! The helpings are pretty big so we split out entree as well. Something to be aware of prior to going is that it's a little noisy, you may be seated at a table with other people - there were 3 of us and we sat at a table with another group of 5 - and it's CASH ONLY!
Great local spot! Try the lunch sandwiches and salad everyone I have had so far has been great. I would stay away from the chocolate it was oddly thick.
I like the soft cooked pork sandwich more than the pancake. Â It's tender and juicy. The vegetable and fries sauce are tasty. But it's kinda small there, so recommand you to sit outside.

A great date place! Â The thing to get here is the flammy. Â Super duper thin crust 'pizza' with your choice of toppings. Â We got the jardin with caramelized onions, tomatoes and shrooms with emmental cheese. Â You pick it up like pizza but the flavors are not italian, there is no pizza sauce or mozz cheese. Â I could easily eat one myself, but we wanted desert so we split the jardin along with a green salad so we could also indulge in the banana split flammy. Â the green salad was just ok, the house dressing is delicious but the salad itself was just chopped lettuce with a couple tomato wedges.. Â What I also like about this place is they offer wine by the 1/4l and 1/2l carafe. Â  Overall, La tarte Flambee is a fun tasty place to go. Â They take reservations and I would recommend making one unless you are coming on the early side.

Guacamole. Mango steak salad. Fresh grapefruit margs. Everything here is delicious and the atmosphere is very chill - great music, friendly service and awesome bar. The only downside is the wait. Â The restaurant is tiny and trying to get a table on any night of the week could be a 2 hour wait. Â Go for lunch on the weekends - they open up all the floor to ceiling windows when the weather is nice and the wait will be minimal.

Malaysian cuisine isn't always on the top of my crave list but this place is definitely my favorite for a quick and delicious meal. Crowded, yes, but worth the short wait. Â Located in Little Italy (next to the famous Ferraras), this restaurant tailors to those who enjoy a little spice in their meals. Yes, a lot of their Malaysian dishes do have a little kick in it but if you're one of those who can't tolerate, you can always default to their Canto style dishes, which are not spicy. But after all, you are at Malaysian restaurant, right? My friends and I came here for dinner one night. We ordered Roti Canai (Indian Pancake), Singapore Mai Fun, Grilled Jumbo Prawns, Sauteed String Beans w/Shrimp, and Sarong Burong (fried taro stuffed with shrimp, chicken and mushrooms). Everything had a lot of spice in it except for the Sarong Burong. Each dish averaged about $8 - $15, which isn't too bad. My favorite is the Singapore Mai Fun. Even though a lot of other Chinese restaurants make this, but I somehow enjoy it here the most. It's not as greasy compare to other places and this place has more flavor.

Went here for brunch on a Sunday at 11am. We were told there was a 45 minute wait (the restaurant doesn't take reservations), but we got seats at the bar in 30 minutes. The space is clean and modern, and our waitress was very kind. I wanted to love the place, but the food was only okay. We both ordered the chilaquiles, one with steak and one with chicken. Both portion sizes were huge, but not very flavorful and pretty acidic. It was also quite noisy, so much so that we both had a hard time hearing the waitress. Not sure I would go again, but the food on other peoples plates looked pretty good.

My friend and I came around 3:30pm on a Saturday and were seated immediately and were told that the kitchen will close at 3:45pm. The dÃ©cor was definitely not what I expected from a regular brunch place as a lot of items on the walls and on the shelves were very amusing. The disco tots were awesome. Even with a thick layer of sawmill gravy and cheddar on top the tots were crispy. Now I can completely forget about the soggy ones from school cafeterias. I also had the American Hardcore Benedict that came with warm honey, praline bacon, and buttermilk biscuits. This one was too sweet which could be that preparation was rushed in the kitchen before time was up. My choice for the next visit will be the buttermilk fried chicken over waffle that I saw other people ordered. Btw - cash only!

A bit expensive... $9 for two pork buns but boy.... they were so addictive and awesome ! Dripping in pig fat, great with hot sauce. The raw oysters smelled FISHY.... but no lasting gastro issues... The grilled hamachi neck (special that night) was awesome but the LOL (loin of lamb) was rather disappointing and the crispy lamb belly was not very crispy ... maybe it was a skinless lamb.... Tom salad was delicious but the long bean dish was rather tasteless Strawberry shortcake w Creme Fraiche was awesome and def worth another visit. Wonder whether five hungry guys can finish a Bo Saam ???

If there is one thing polish people suck at, its Bim BIm Bap in a stone hot pot! Thank god Little Dokebi opened. Its the perfect addition to the Mcgorlick park area of little poland. There is Hite on tap, delicious little appetizers and Korean taco/burritos! No table side bbq which is good because the place is small and I dont always want to smell like roast meat :) Â and the banchan are kinda sparse, but you ain't in K-town Dorthy so shut yo mouth! And then open yo mouth for the stone hot pot, its sizzling good!

Amazing sandwiches, catfish and steak sammys are my fave.. the corn is delicious and their custom fruit salad is off the hook- NOTE: usually a line outside, during the day service is great and friendly, at night however the cashier is very unfriendly not helpful, waited for my food while it sat in front of her and had to ask her to see if it was mine and it was, got it cold :( not appreciated.

This is one of the prettiest restaurants that I've ever been to! First, there are beautiful rose arrangements everywhere! Â Of all colors! you walk into the restaurant and it smells like roses. The atmosphere is modern and warm, but they also do a great job of combining that with nature and use of natural lighting. Their back porch seating is right below an open roof so it's perfect for the summer. The food is delicious I really like the pork belly special and the paella is simply devine, I wish they have more meat tapas options

Outstanding. The arrepas were light, and the fillings were delicious. Best michealada I've ever had, seriously, w fresh ginger and jalapeÃ±o. Authentic, great music, prompt service, and new dishes I hadn't enjoyed before. Octopus and smoked paprika appetizer that literally melted in my mouth. Get here now.

Went for lunch when Gueros was closed, but honestly Chavela's would've been the first choice if I'd ever been here before. The lunch special is 6.95 and is plentiful and delicious. I got a chicken mole tostado and a avocado taco. My friend got fried eggs with potatoes and toast. I got a michelada on the side too and it was one of the best I'd have in a while. The inside of the place is beautiful too. Want to go back for brunch, dinner, whatever.

So I met a friend for Brunch at Pies Â and Thighs. Party of four, we ordered the chicken biscuits with honey & Hot sauce, country fried steak, pecan dough nut, lemon poppy dough nut, stack of pancakes with fruits and walnuts and biscuit and gravy. Â  The 2 doughnuts were ordered first, colossal size and divine.... we all loved it. The pecan doughnuts are the best doughnuts I've had to date, its a perfect balance of crunchy, sweet dough.. enough to satisfy your gustatory desire. The country steak was served with cheese grits done to perfection, creamy with the perfect consistency Â ( not too runny or stiff) and egg. The other dishes were good but not worth writing about. My story of the pecan doughnut: From my seat I notice they were down to 2 Pecan doughnut, I quickly called our waiter over and ordered 1 to go. Yes I was full but I could not miss the opportunity to have one later that day or for breakfast the next morning. The next morning my cousin from Boston got a taste and with the first bite she ask 'how far is this place from here?' I said 20 minutes. Five minutes later were were driving over to Pies & Thighs. Â  The place is small and cozy, the staff friendly, the food is really good my advice is to get there before 12 noon on the weekends.

My first meal in my second visit to NYC, and I've been craving Num Pang sandwiches ever since. My friend and I came late at night and unfortunately the best two meats were out. We settled for other recommended sandwiches, the catfish and tiger shrimp. The catfish sandwich was absolutely amazing. The bun was toasted to perfection and the catfish just melted in your mouth. Both of these worked in tandem with the sweet tangy sauce and BAM you got heaven. The tiger shrimp sandwich was great too, thanks to the great bun and sauce. Will definitely be coming back!

My guy found this place and usually I'm a bit skeptical to his choices because I'm the foodie in the relationship, but he did good.... real good. This place has amazing food. Â The pita bread is warm, freshly-baked, and delicious. Â It goes great with their baba ganoush, which has a nice smoked eggplant flavor. The salad with the light vinaigrette was a great complement to the falafel. Â The falafel was delicious and not overly crispy, but had a great dense flavor to it. Â The size of the falafel is larger than most Mediterranean places that I've been to as well. Â The stuffed grape leaves were excellent, but I've never tried it before so I don't really have much of a comparison. Â I didn't quite enjoy the spinach and onion pie because it was stuffed with too much spinach and it wasn't seasoned very well. Â  They also give you little bites of almond cake with your check and it was sweet and fluffy. Â  The price is right and I can't wait to go back for more.

We went to American Flatbread after an event across the street, and it was the perfect place for a late dinner and hanging out with friends. The flatbreads were delicious. Sometimes I'm skeptical of "non-traditional" topping combinations for pizzas, but the clearly have a good sense here on where to push the envelope. Really nice flavor combinations and nothing too far-out or trendy. They have a really nice wine list and good bar selection. The service was excellent too. Really enjoyed our waiter, and all the staff was really friendly. This is definitely a good place to go in groups, and the flatbreads were great for sharing. It would be nice if there were some more sharable options among the salads and appetizers. All in all, I really enjoyed this place and look forward to going back. Compared to American Flatbread restaurants in New England, they've done a great job at "Manhattanizing" the concept. It still feels like the comfortable, enjoyable places I know from "apres-skis" in Vermont, but it's a little more sophisticated and upscale -- just what I'd like to have in NYC.

Disclaimer: I studied in Japan for 4 months. I didn't eat ramen every day, and I don't claim to be an expert, but this does at least allow me to compare ramen to what I ate in its country of origin. Additionally, a fun fact: going out to eat by yourself in NYC drastically reduces your wait time. I went to Ippudo at 7pm Monday night, and only waited 10 minutes to be seated. The decor is definitely more modern, but beneath that is an undercurrent of a ramen house. There are booths along the sides, and in the main space are large tables for 10-12 people. I sat with a number of strangers, who were already engrossed in their meals. The smell was great, and the staff were all shouting in Japanese as customers were seated. You can see the cooks behind a counter working in teams to fill orders, and I recommend taking a look if you're sitting nearby. I was conflicted between trying a more traditional dish (since this was my first time here) or eating their BBQ pork special. Luckily, the special runs until June, so I asked for the Akamaru Modern (a pork bowl with miso paste) with kakuni (braised pork belly). The meal far exceeded my expectations. The broth was delicious without being too salty, a common occurrence for ramen shops (and common complaint from customers). The pork was tender and flavorful, and ordering the kakuni was clearly the right idea as I finished the main pork very quickly. The noodles were light and soft without being mushy, and the greens were amazing. It's the first time I wished there'd been a few more greens in my ramen. I planned ahead of time to eat the noodles quickly so I could get the second helping (a call of "kae-dama" will get you more noodles if you have enough broth remaining), but it turns out I didn't need to plan at all. While the broth was great, I devoured my noodles quickly, taking more time with the second serving and my remaining pork and veggies to enjoy it all with the soup. Final verdict: I have some fond memories of eating ramen in Japan. I think most Westerners who get to visit look forward to their first Japanese ramen and built the experience up in their memories. With that in mind, I can easily say that Ippudo's ramen was as good, and quite possibly better than, the best ramen I had in Japan. As a caveat, I couldn't use Yelp at the time to find the best ramen in Tokyo or Osaka, but I definitely believe Ippudo ranks up there with the best of them. I haven't visited Totto Ramen or some of the other popular ramen places in NYC yet, but if any somehow blow Ippudo away, I'll revisit this review. As long as I list this as 5 stars, know that Ippudo remains king as far as my palate is concerned.

got the spicy pork meatball hero, pesto sauce, mozzarella cheese, side salad to-go, which you just go straight to the register and order to the employee. $9-10 each hero was, and the bread was nice and crispy, not too soggy with the pesto sauce that is soaked up by the bread with the chewy mozzarella cheese. but the meatball themselves, which the name of the store should stand up for, were too dry inside...three balls per hero! despite them, i loved the salad, made with fresh veggies and apples.

I gave this restaurant 4.5 stars because it's simply delightful. I visited it last week just after watching Chef Jehangir Mehta on the Next Â Iron Chef. His preparations really are as mouthwateringly good as they appear on TV. The restaurant interiors are beautiful. I especially loved the delicate chandelier that overlooks the room. I'm a small person so I didn't find the space cramped but I understand that a six foot something person might have found it small. The size shouldn't be a big deal after a while (with enough $25 wine in your stomach you're bound to get comfortable. Even if you don't drink don't worry. The people there are so sweet you'll feel comfortable soon anyway). I love the Tapas style portions. This way I can try a lot more. I like to have small meals. Even their pork buns don't weigh heavily on your stomach. I definitely want to go back. I wonder if he'll make some of his recipes from the show... I wouldn't mind trying that lobster curry and rice preparation that won him the first test this week. Sounds delicious... PS- They have a very sweet contest of their own going on at Graffiti. You can design a unique Graffiti envelope (for them to deliver their bills in) and send it to Jehangir Mehta and if he likes it you could win a chance to have dinner with him at Graffiti. I read about it on his personal website. I think I'm gonna give it a stab.

I loved this place! The appetizers were amazing! I tried the rotoi, beef skewers, and chicken wings. They were all good. As for the actual entrees, they were good but not great. I had the beef chow fun and It was decent. I was really won over by the appetizers! Thai iced tea was also yummy and I loved the coconut pudding dessert! Def recommend!

This place is great! Super cute atmosphere....very much a true Italian feel. The service was nothing over the top, but worked! I tried the calamari app which was awesome, I had the special salad which was fantastic, and the pasta with Ragu sauce for dinner! I was pretty much in heaven. They have some decently priced wines. Overall the whole experience was awesome! I will definitely go back!

I walked in here not really knowing what to expect. Even though it wasn't close to deserted by any means, I was surprised this place wasn't more crowded on a Friday night. I shared the cheese platter, it came with the traditional 3 cheeses with bread. It also came with a jam spread, ridiculously good never-tasted-such-good-in-my-life blueberries and a mini pear (which I forgot what its called). Thoroughly pleased with the cheese platter. I just had the kimchi pancakes for my entree, it had a good crispy texture and a spiciness to them. Thumbs up. Apart from the flies that came in noticeable numbers halfway into our meal.
Took my girlfriend here the night I proposed. Fantastic food, on point service and great ambiance for the special occasion. Will be returning next time we are In town.

I've been here for business lunches twice - their duck fat brushed rolls brings me back every time!! I've been able to get reservations a day or two before through OpenTable without problems. But day of, I've seen the hostess turn away people at the door or suggest them eating at the bar as their reservations are booked up. So definitely get reservations!! The service here is pretty great - they bring refills of those duck fat rolls every time they're out - the first time I came here I think we ate 6 pans of them! SO GOOD. I've had their burger, which is insanely good. I wasn't that big of a fan of their seafood crepe (it was a bit too fishy for me), and their appetizers have always been delicious. Their steak tartare is really good, and we had their beet salad last time which was surprisingly good - I'm usually not a fan of beets but it was delicious. Will definitely return!

known as "Houston's" in other cities... And if you are fan of Houston's, you'll LOVE Hillstone!!! Of course, the name change allows them to jack up the price on the same menu items.. Oh well, the price of living in NYC

Um, seriously? Me and my bf came here after checking out the Museum of Moving Images and this place is seriously legit. It's a mini Brazillian hole in the wall buffet/churrascaria and it's super cheap! We paid 8 dollars each for a plate full of declious meats and sides and left super happy and full! I love this place and the workers are friendly and nice and answered every question I had ("question" as in me pointing to things with my head tilted in confusion, while they yelled out Â what they were,"beans!" "pork!" "chicken!") I can't wait to go back!

Love this place. Desserts are a little on the small side considering the prices. Drinks and ambiance are fantastic. Great place for conversation for business or with friends. Also owned by the same group that opened The Ace Hotel two blocks up. Service is unmatched for the area. Truly fantastic. Date Rating: 8 Pick up Scale: 6 Strong Suggestion: don't come hungry.

After going there at 4am last night (no we only had 2drinks all night), i think all the hype are from people who went there when they were drunk! We were at Kiss and Fly, so decided to swing by for a late night snack. There was a LINE at 4am in the morning? REALLY? we got a table after 20mins, while waiting, a couple of ppl cut us off when they go up to "bouncer" to bitch, and after the 2nd group cut us off, i got annoyed and went up to the bouncer and told him the 2 girls just cut us off, and he let us in and apologize, so i was fine with it. The place is trendy, dark and loud (drunk people!) We ordered the mac attack (a sampler of regular, bacon and truffle oil), slider and country fried steak. Mac was good, slider sucks country fried steak was so-so. Again, we weren't drunk so i guess we were not enjoying it as much as the rest of the people in the room. A little pricey for the kinda of food you get but it's fine. 18% gratuity included as well (FYI) Overall, we probably wont return because i dont think i'll like to wait in line for mediocre food.

Tiny place first of all. The lunch specials were very much on point. You cannot go wrong with anything on the menu. I personally love the Thai Iced Tea, that would be my absolute favorite part of coming here. The menu is standard Thai food.
Great spot, good burger, wish there was more on the menu, but damn those fried pickles are the best thing I have ever had.
Food is sooooooo good! Â Bartender is very nice!
mia favorita. hands down best house wine this side of the pond. cash only.

Since 2009, Bouley has improved dramatically. David Bouley seems to have refined his menu/s and zeroed on the dishes that not only explode with flavor but are also healthy. His artistry begins with the incredible rolls. Then the apricot walnut bread is to die for, not to mention the fig bread and the dried cherry bread. He seems to be using more organic ingredients. Last visit for example, one of our two desserts on the $55.00 five course lunch tasting menu, organic strawberries in an ameretto mousse which was amazing. The duck was melt the mouth delicious. The porcini mushroom flan was loaded with crabmeat and better than ever. The oysters tasted of caught ten minutes ago freshness. And the chocolate souffle was its usual amazing self. This meal coupled with our amazing Christmas Day lunch in 2011 prompted me to pump them up to five stars, but the service which was spectacular on Christmas Day 2011 left alot to be desired at lunch a couple of weeks ago.

Another great addition to our burgeoning scene along 3rd Ave. So far I have only been lucky enough sample their breakfast pastries and coffee. Great apple turnover to go with my macchiato. The space is really cool with a friendly staff. Â Looking forward to returning to try what looks like a great dinner menu. Go Third Ave!

Standard Brooklyn brunch fare with correspondingly standard prices and wait time. The one and only memorable menu item is the pancakes. I daydream about them regularly. We usually order savory brunch items and order the pancakes as dessert. That way, the pancakes get the unadulterated attention they deserve and you can enjoy them at their crispiest. Avoid the coffee.

So happy this is in my hood. I've gone twice just for the octopus (amazing) and the scallops in brown butter with dried cherries (heaven). The crispy cod could be a little crispier, but the grilled bread is super yum. They have an incredible cocktail/beer/wine list with a gazillion choices by the glass. The bartenders are warm and friendly, professional and pretty hot also. You have to get there early though, if you want a seat. They fill up quick and you don't want to have to go wait in line at Taverna Kyclades down the street.

Amazing farm to table style place. Communal tables which I'm not a fan of but the food is so incredible that I would sit in anything to eat here. I don't know how there isn't a line out the door for this place. We got the beet salad (literally the best salad I've even eaten in my life) and the beet veggie burger (I forgot what it was called), absolutely amazing! The fried red bliss chips dipped in their homemade spicy mustard and beet ketchup were also incredible. And it wasn't expensive at all.

OK but nothing special. We were a party of five on for Sunday brunch and is the Cookshop worth waiting for? Not really. We were a mix of out-of-towners and Upper Westsiders so none of us know Chelsea well and we Â simply stumbled across the Cookshop. We had a good time as we hadn't seen each other for a while but no one said, 'Wow, this is a great dish'. I had the frittata which was dry and the salad was unexciting. No bread of any kind served with it. Won't look for an occasion to go back.

I'd last dined here several years ago - which I had great memories of the place. This time was the worst dining experience I've ever had, and I felt I had to share it as others appear to be feeling the same. I'll start with the positive. If your attending a party, and you don't mind yelling to be heard, and you don't care about the food being edible, hot or cooked, and you don't mind being squeezed into a space at a table that puts you right in the face of your co-diners and, dealing with the attitude overload of the waiters, and being bumped into every 2 minutes then this is the perfect place for you. Oh - and the terrible cold draught on the back of your neck throughout. Amazingly this place was packed - unbelievable! Have people lost their minds? After waiting 45 minutes for our cold uncooked entree to arrive we paid the bill and left without eating it. Oh - and, as a by-the-way in 2010 who's hanging stuffed animal heads as decor?, And cleaning? Anyone heard of it. It's one thing for the environment to be shabby-chic, its another thing when its just plain dirty.

The food is excellent, but the staff is embarrassing. They've unapologetically messed up my order three times. Today was the same old thing except when I called to ensure the persisting problem was not repeated, I got a whole lot of tude from the lady in the "delivery department". Look lady, I'm paying $15 for a falafal that should cost $4 -- this stuff should come wrapped in gold leaf.

Dare I say this? Â This might have been the best bowl of ramen I have ever had. Â Blow-torched chashu. Â Crushed garlic upon request. Â Chicken based soup. Â Oh goodness. Base rate for a bowl is $9.50, which is so much cheaper than Ippudo. Â Cash only. Â Small parties only - no more than 4 people. Â Fun to sit by the bar and watch them make the bowls of ramen and blow torch the meats. Â This is a must try for all ramen lovers. Â Worth the wait.

not much to say about this place other than it is just an all around outstanding mediterranean tapas restaurant. i've been here 6 or 7 times and pretty much every dish they make is delicious. we've brought 3 or 4 different friends and every one has agreed with our opinion. and the atmosphere is great. dark wood floors and walls, very west village.
Their miso ramen with pork was yummy. The sweet potato beer was really good, but pricey for bottled beer. I wouldn't go back unless they turned on the ac.

4.5/5 for food, 5/5 for atmosphere, 5/5 for service Amazing restaurant. I loved almost everything about this place. I enjoyed its interior as well as its lively atmosphere. This restaurant is genuinely what you would call a "fun" eatery, and the food/wine was excellent as well. I will be coming back very soon and often!

The Artichoke Slice!!! Every time I pass by this place, there's a line going around the corner. So on my way home from Trader Joe's one night, I stopped by and picked up a slice of their artichoke pizza. It was AMAZING!!! Quite on the oily side, but definitely to die for pizza. The crust was perfect chewy goodness. And on top of that, the cheese. Oh my god the cheese. I would definitely have to go back and give their other pizzas a try. The wait was about 10 minutes for them to heat up your order (although mine came out a little black burnt on the bottom).... If you wanted a whole pizza, you had to wait at least 20 minutes. The real downer of this place was the girl who took our order - had a bit of an attitude.

I was on the quest to find a delicious, melt in your mouth type of restaurant for mine and my boyfriends anniversary. I did my research, and realized that I wanted to try La Sirene, a BYOB French joint I have had my eye on for quite some time now. When I arrived, I was surprsied to find that the restaurant wasn't as cute or quaint as described in previous reviews. I know it has recently been redone, so that could be the reason. Since we had brought our own wine (no corkage fee, which is tough to find in NYC these days) we knew we wanted to get a little crazy with the food. When my boyfriend and I go out to eat, we share everything so we can taste more. We definitely left feeling full and happy. Here is what we got: French Onion Soup: Â We started with the french onion soup, even though it was a 100 degree day in NYC, because I had read online that it was the best french onion soup that people have ever had. Since I love french onion soup we ordered it. However, it really just tasted like your run of the mill, normal french onion soup. It was good don't get me wrong, but it definitely wasn't anything special. Probably unnecessary because it filled us up early on in the meal. Tartelette De Chevre Frais Aux Echalotes, Truffles, Raisins Confit Et Voile De Vieux Gruyere goat cheese tart with shallots, truffles, grape and a veil of 180 days aged swiss cheese: This tart was absolutely amazing. I am a sucker for truffle and goat cheese, and who doesn't love a good pastry? I highly reccomend this dish to anyone that goes to La Sirene. It was melt in your mouth delicious, a favorite part of my meal. Tournedos Rossini: Based on Yelp reviews, I knew that the tournedos rossini at La Sirene was a must try. This was my first time tasting fois gras, so I was Â a little nervous but it turned out to be amazing. The steak was cooked to perfection and I LOVED the fois gras! I definitely get the hype! Kassulet Toulousain De La Maison cassoulet toulouse's style (cannellini beans, tomato, garlic duck confit, slab bacon & pork sausage all braised with duck fat): My boyfriend and I were both actually pretty disappointed with this dish. Our waitress had warned it would be heavy, but I thought she meant becuase of its fatty succulent goodness. It turned out to be a stew, with not much flavor. I was expecting this to be exploding with flavor, but there was definitely something lacking. I definitely wish we would have gone with something else. Maybe the lamb. I do reccomend La Sirene, although all the dishes weren't my favorite. I definitely recognize quality food when I taste it. I would just avoid the Kassulet, because although the description sounds insanely amazing, it just isn't.

I work in the area and decided to pick up lunch from Song due to the good reviews on Yelp. Needless to say, I'm extremely disappointed. I went into the restaurant to place the order and the hostess was very rude. She took my money without giving me a receipt and did not even tell me how long it would take. She basically made no attempt at good service because I wasn't sitting down in the restaurant. I could forget this if I didn't receive my order of Pad See Yew and find that it's burnt--the noodles, the eggs, and the beef. There are distinct char marks on everything and it tastes disgusting. And of course, I can't very well send my order back into the kitchen. Perhaps my experience and food would be different if I was sitting down in the restaurant, but it is unacceptable to treat takeout orders with such disregard. I will not be returning to test the sit-down experience.

I was disappointed at how small the place was, but that part is my fault for not reading more of the Yelp reviews first. I'm giving Johnny's 3 stars because the banana pancakes & home fries were excellent. However, my coffee was cold, and the waiter never came around to offer a refill. We also waited at least 15 minutes before the waiter even came to take our order. He finally came up and asked what food we were waiting for, and we told him we hadn't even ordered yet. Overall- great prices, we paid less than $20 for 2. If you're looking for a cheap breakfast in the city & aren't claustrophobic, this is your place.

Ugh, I feel like I wasted date night here. Â I thought the pizza here was going to be fab, but it really didn't hit the spot. - I thought the pizza was way too thin. Â Maybe I just like to eat a lot, but having two slices did nothing for my hunger. - While the crust was really good, the rest of the pizza didn't hold itself up well. Â  Maybe the mushrooms we got on the pie weighed it down? Â Who knows. - Service was not great. Â The restaurant wasn't even full, yet I felt like our waiter was rushing us. Â It would have been nice to have a relaxed meal. Â  - The large pie is a bit expensive for what you're getting. Â I'd rather pay some extra $$ and get an amazing pie from DiFara's next time.

I came here with my boyfriend on a Tuesday night. We had tickets to a show at 7 and we got to Juniors at around 6:15, so we were in a hurry. We only waited for a little while before being seated. The waitress was really nice and was able to help me find a item on the menu that accommodated my wheat allergy. She was also understanding about us being in a hurry and gave us our check right when our dinner came. Â Overall our experience was great and the food was good.
Came here for dinner and was very impressed. Everything we ordered from appetizers to the main course tasted amazing. The service was decent and the decor was cozy.

An excellent meal; if it was a bit more reasonably priced, I would feel comfortable with a 5 star review. Â Unfortunately, unlike their sister-restraurant Littleneck, you are paying for every penny of enjoyment you are getting at The Pines. We were a table for four. Â We were greeted by a host who told us there would be a 90 minute wait, but also that we were the next table of the list. Â I scanned the room and saw people halfway through their entrees--I said, "you think those people will be there for another hour and a half?" Â He said, "well, I was just being conservative." Â One drink at Canal Bar and 45 minutes later, we were seated. Â  The Room: I love the ambiance of this place. Â It has a great vibe and the seating choices are excellent. Â Also, the backyard looks amazing for when it gets warm. Â Definitely a great date spot. Â  The Drinks: 14 dollars for cocktails is pretty annoying, even if they are excellent. Â 14 dollars for a cocktail that I could finish in 3-5 sips, sucks even more. Â The cocktails are beautifully presented, but should be 11 dollars. Â  The Food: We had the Apples (really great), the greens (should be more in the serving--ordered two of them), and the sweet potato (a knockout) to start. Â I think the appetizers were all great, the apple and sweet potato were 5 star dishes, the greens probably a 3.5. Â  For entrees, we shared the streak and tileflish, and I loved both. Â The steak was prepared perfectly and the titlefish was also delicious. We had dessert as well, but it was not particularly memorable. Â  Overall, I really liked the Pines. Â But if I am choosing between Littleneck and the Pines in the future, I will likely return to Littleneck first because there is a lot more bang for your buck.
If it wasn't for the hostile, bored hostess this place would get 5 stars. The server was knowledgable and great and the food was incredible. A slightly on the pricey side but well worth it!

Table for 4. Reservations for 6pm. Tuesday night. Being a HUGE french bistro fan...(having dined at Le Express, Pigalle, Pastis, Payard, Rive Gauche, Brasserie, Cafe Centro, Jubilee, L'Ecole, Steak Frites, AOC, & Florent) ..it was definetedly time to try BALTHAZAR. And I was impressed. We were seated right away, at a nice comfy table. Waitress was really nice and informative. It was pretty packed for a tuesday night, so always get a reservation. Now on to the food... Four things you must try when you go are: 1) Onion Soup Gratinee Â - it is really really good. The cheese is plentiful and really is Â perfect with the soup. The more you eat it, the better it gets. Â I know, $11 for soup is a bit nuts, but worth it. Share with a friend! 2)Chicken Liver & Foie Gras Mousse - So creamy and delicious, served room temp with a frisee salad and toasted country bread. Better then the cold Liver Mousse at Le Express, but comparable to Jubilee's. 3) Escargot - they are served in the shell (which now i understand why there were toothpicks on the table). I was not able to fish it out with my mini fork, but delicious and the parsley butter garlic sauce is comparable to Le Express. Soak your bread in it! 4)The Duck Confit! --the Duck Confit is served with a mushroom sauce and a Frisee salad. Perfect way to cut the grease of the duck. It was a nice big duck leg and roasted perfectly. Skin was crunchy, meat was tender. yumyum. We also ordered the Seafood Ceviche (which is cooked calamari, prawns, crab in a lemon vinagrette) served on nice big Radicchio leaf. And the Seared Halibut entree. Though not memorable dishes..they were both decent. I am definetedly a fan. This place doesnt deserve 5 stars, because they are a bit overpriced for the food. But overall, excellent well prepared food. Out of my list above, this one is in the top 5.

Interesting to see Sweet Science/James' response to our reviews was just as prefabricated and generic as the burger patties. Rather than making up - or getting someone to write - a 5 star review that attacked us, a simple apology would have gone a long way. Clearly you have a lot to learn about customer service. And burgers.

As you walk in, you are definitely taken by surprise by the place. It is such a beautiful space. This is not a typical bar in the neighborhood. I loved the interior, ambience and the rustic decor with beautiful wood furnishings. This is the perfect spot to go for happy hour or for dinner, whether it is with a bunch of friends or with your date. Â  It is a plus that they have happy hour specials until 7pm. That includes not only wine but also a select list from their cocktail menu. Â And if you check in with the Yelp app you get beer and a burger for only $15! The tartufo pizza straight from the wood burning oven was amazing. Everything was perfect about it and I can't wait to go back and try more of their food.

Went on a Tuesday for happy hour around 5:20pm. Happy hour is 5-7. Â The wait was about 30-40 min. It's 6 oysters and a craft beer for $12. I got a glass of wine instead; which is $16. It was pretty worth it. I tried all the happy hour oysters and they were great! You can choose from 4 different oysters. I enjoyed the west coast oyster (only 1 west coast oyster during happy hour) the most. It was small, but thick and not as fishy. It was enjoyable! Don't expect to get full off of happy hour. I would recommend getting other entrees as well.

I had long been wondering about Hearth. One Monday night, we decided to finally give it a try. Something about the cold starting to set in and the overcast weather made us want a comforting and hearty meal: Hearth delivered on both. First, we ordered drinks from the extensive and inventive wine and spirits list. I was in the mood for something warming and in the Scotch realm. Our server suggested I try a drink with some smoky mescal, maple syrup, and vermouth. I forget what the drink was called (SORRY!), but it was delicious and well worth it. My boyfriend ordered a whiskey drink that was equally tasty. I'd like to go back and try some more of the cocktails. We decided that we weren't hungry enough, so we skipped the appetizers. Again, I'd be delighted to go back and try them - we would have ordered nearly every one, if we had the stomach space. Â For entrees we ordered the branzino, with chickpea and some sort of kale-like green. The skin on the fish was PERFECTLY crispy and salty. It was laid on a chickpea puree, then topped with some crispy greens. The textures were perfect, and to add to everything, they topped it with the fried chickpea skins - delicious crunchy, salty bites to complement the food. My boyfriend ordered roast lamb that was served with breckle (a roasted and crispy serving of brisket meat/fat that melted like butter in your mouth). The lamb was perfectly cooked medium rare. Rosemary garnished the dish and was used wonderfully, and in the exact right proportions. We split Hen of the Woods mushrooms on the side were awesome, if not a little salty. Our server suggested a wine pairing for each, and the wine was fantastic! I believe I got a languedoc - it was light and buttery and went really well with the fish. We finished it off with what has become my newest favorite dessert (I have like, one a week): peanut butter pie. It was comprised of layers of peanut butter filling and rich chocolate! NOM!

Rarely do new spots hit the mark so well, the place is an instant favorite. The soft shell crab is in season as I write this and it's the best I've ever had. Small plates, oysters, cocktails - the have it all.

After getting our takeout home, we were delighted by the enormous portions and wonderful flavor of the side dishes that came with our vegetable curry (red beans and rice, and some sweet cabbage). These were more than a meal in themselves, and we spent the whole next day looking forward to the leftovers. The lemonade was also delicious. The vegetable curry was tasty, but the other flavors stole the show. We went rather late and they were out of the vegetarian dishes except the curry. So, vegetarians might want to go earlier.

This review is long overdue, but is finally coming into existence. The Farm offers a solid, high-quality, organic fare complemented by great service. Love their burger, spinach/portobello salad, portobello sandwich, and special dishes! Actually, specials deserve a special note, since they are always outstanding.

I came to this restaurant with my family for my SPECIAL birthday dinner. The first thing I realized was how great the service was, they kept checking on you and making sure everything is good; however, it became a little bit overbearing. The bread that came out was fantastic. It was served with a few different sauces and was out of this world. I ordered as an appetizer the yellowtail, the polenta, the short ribs, and the mozzarella. Other than the yellowtail, which was meant to be served cold, everything came out ice cold. The mozzarella was disappointing, as were the short ribs. The yellowtail I loved, it was very clean and fresh. As a main course, I ordered the spaghetti with tomato sauce, the fois grah ravioli and the short rib pasta. Not one of them was good, and all of them were cold. I don't suggest coming here for a special night, you will just be disappointed and upset.
my favorite hangout spot with friends. Its a nice little cafe tucked away in an area just a few steps from the big busy street.

I am a TOTAL FAN of Yuca's Tuesday night happy hour! We all had Sangria (they have red and white) and then shared a bunch of (half off!) tapas. The shrimp quesadilla was our favorite, then the coconut fried shrimp and the ribs were DELICIOUS. Everything was pretty much GREAT except I caution you to stay away from the queso. No bueno. Chunky and has pieces of meat/bacon in it...nothing special. Overall, great place for happy hour and yummy tapas. We will def be coming back!

The pork belly is to die for! I'm definitely coming back to try the other items on the menu! So good! There's also healthy options & a huge array of comfort foods. Good portions, affordable, and definitely worth the experience! The sausage gravy is definitely something to write home about.

I'm so glad they're just a few blocks away. I don't really like pizza but when that pizza has mushrooms and vodka sauce on it with fresh ingredients I get easily addicted. And so does my roommate. Plus they have a two slice drink recession special that beats most other meals in this area. Yesss!
Best Ramen I have tasted !! Everything was amazing !! Service was great !! Line was long but it was worth the wait !!

Old school restaurant where ambiance and service are irrelevant because food is most important thing in this place.KYCLADES is not innovative seafood restaurant in any way but rather simple Â seafood place where food speak for its self.That s the reason i love this place!

We went there on Friday night, and waited for 15mins to get the seat. Everything looked fine til the food came. All the food we ordered were disappointed. We had tge shrimp dumpling, takayori, beef tongue. Those were either too salty or stuffed with whole bunch of starch inside. Japanese cuisine was never supposed to be like that. I am way too disappointed

First off every restaurant should offer the entire menu at a set price. Seriously. If Mcdonalds came out and said ok you can order the, "Big Mac D" menu and you get one of everything how awesome would that be? Drunken college students all over the world would be lining up to order it. Alta offers, "The Whole Shabang" which as implied above is the entire menu. I've done it twice with about 12 people and it was awesome. Think of a machine gun but instead of bullets it shoots small plates of great food. I would suggest you tell them to bring them out slowly because even though we made that request both times the food still came out rather quickly. Aside from the whole menu this is a GREAT place to bring a date. Tapas are great to eat as you'll be talking most of the time and you can nibble on small food. The atmosphere is also dark and has that romantic feeling you want assuming you actually like the girl. Come here! You won't regret it.

I just ate there today for brunch, so I can't review the wine bar element. Overall, the food was interesting and really quite tasty. Â Although it's simple, the ingredients were fresh and of noticeably high quality. Â The prices wee also great. Unfortunately, the service was unconscionably slow. Â we waited about 15 minutes at our table before they even took our order, and didn't get out food until about 25 minutes later. Â Once we got our food, we had to point out they had forgotten part of our drink order. There were empty tables, so it wasn't like they were getting slammed. I'm willing to give them another go since they were just profiled in TONY and might have had an insane morning before we got there.
Cheap and delicious. Great coffee and paninis.

I just finished having a great meal and plenty of drinks at Sabor, but the glutton in me had to come to Rincon. Thanks to my glutton I found a Cuban spot that I'd like to come back to. I initially came here for dessert but then I looked at the menu--casava con carne, jamon y pernil con queso, y bacalao. Oh man! I haven't had some of this stuff in so long. How could I deny myself the pleasure? :) Yeah, so I ordered a bunch of appetizers with some Spanish beer then finished off with some flan. Everything was perfect and the price was super cheap. They may not be converting to dollars or something, which is fine by me. This is just a simple old school restaurant without the loud music or glitz & glamour like some other Cuban places. I love it.

Puerto Viejo is my favorite restaurant in Brooklyn. Go visit them and you'll see why... in the meantime, I'll explain, my 6 main reasons: 1) THE FOOD!: An incredible selection of wines, homemade sangria, freshly made authentic dishes, bomb maduro, and THE BEST mofongo dominicano on the planet. Everything is reasonably priced, and very affordable for the large portions! Their plantain chips and homemade garlic sauce will knock you off your bar stool or chair. You'll be addicted (mark my words). Â  2) THE ATMOSPHERE/ SERVICE: Greetes by smiles, warmth, and beautiful decor the moment you walk in, you KNOW YOU'RE HOME. The lighting, plant-life and physical set-up. I LOVE THE BAR, the smiles, the bathroom and the personal touches around the place that make it so home-y. Perfect for just a cup of coffee or a 4-course meal, any time of day/night. 3) THE FAMILY VIBE: Owned and run for 25+ years by the most adorable, hard-working couple this planet has seen, the Abreu's. This family joint lives up to its name and reputation, and goes beyond it, improving its standards for flavor and experience CADA DIA! Their genuine, hospitable air comes through the presence of their two sons, and lovely daughter Maritza, also a singer who performs at P.V.'s awesome nightlife events. There's always some cousin, Tio, or neighbor coming through, like the Dominican version of "Cheers" where everybody knows your name and they're always glad you came! :) 4) COMMUNITY PRESENCE/INVOLVEMENT: They put on awesome all-ages live music and spoken word shows that welcome all kids of folks from the community into the space, to wine, dine, dance, and converse about issues relevant to our people, from Brooklyn, to Cali, to the Carribean. No where else in the Crown Heights area will you find a more welcoming place to bring family, friends, revolutionary thinkers, and community activists to enjoy a meal, a drink, and a good time together! 5) THE STORY/PERSEVERANCE: Not only did they SURVIVE a major fire in their building, but they are THRIVING in its wake! They have not only re-built, but totally TRANSFORMED Â and re-decorated the space, turning a beautiful old building with its rustic charm into a truly modern cafe/lounge feel that is welcoming and warm. 6) THE FOOD: Did I mention THE FOOD!? SOOOO BOMB!!! ;) LOVE LOVE LOVE LOVE LOVE THIS PLACE! ... Truthfully I was there every day for a week. I never wanted to leave! Although I'm back in California, typing about them from 3,000 miles away, they are still in my heart and mind, and on my taste-buds! :) If you haven't already tried them, CHECK EM OUT! if you have, tell them hello for me, bring a friends, and write a review... spread the word so that truly 'family-owned' restaurants in NY can grow in this tough economy! Also on: menupages.com/restaurantâ€¦
A good friend of mine told me about Beyond Sushi. We had given them a try and i must say it was pretty good including their vegan sushi. I recommend this place
Want to see your bar- Tender's tummy? I don't, but Come here and you will* *but seriously this is a beer and sausage place. Only.

White, gay male owner (of Song and National as well) accused me of not paying the bill. Â My friend paid AGAIN to avoid drama. Â The owner grabbed me by my arm, threatened to punch me in my face and continued to scream "cunt" and "dyke." He randomly mentioned his Black lover and daughter, as if to erase his racist, homophobic, or sexist comments and actions. Tons of witnesses. Waiting for police report. NEVER eat here again!

This place deserves a 5 star for the food alon! Â  Love those little salty peppers. Â Chicken wings were great too! Â But the modern keeps me coming back. Â I don't have any patience to wait and hour and a half for a bowl of soup but this is NO ordinary soup!

I'm not too familiar with the Fort Greene/Clinton Hill area, so this place came as a very nice surprise. What I found was: great food, a great place to hang out, and good beer. Also, everything is reasonably priced. And eco-friendly. If you're a vegetarian, the guacamole/queso sandwich is a great option: flavorful and filling. Also, the corn and plantains were incredible. In sum: all smiles, no complaints.

This place is pretty amazing as restaurants go. I love the food but sometimes the space is always a hassle. There is a long line as the day progresses, by nighttime you better be prepared to wait a bit before getting seated. So every time I go I feel like I have to beat the rush to snag a seat for me and a friend. Other than that this is a cute place that has really good comfort food, like Mac and Cheese and their Artichoke Dip is something beyond what I've had before! The food is best eaten in the restaurant then take out usually because you get priority and food always tastes great when hot! The service is so wonderful! The staff are always in a friendly mood and always ready to accommodate to the customer needs. I never had a problem or issue with the staff. I love to go here on rainy days for their comforting cup of coffee and their lovely service. Penelope's is a great place especially as a Baruch student its a quick get away from the hectic life of school to relax and enjoy the delicious meal that is provided.
This menu is really creative and the food is excellent. The only thing better may be the cocktail menu. We tried several and they were all wonderful. Definitely a solid dinner experience.

I came here for lunch. The food tasted mediocre but the presentation was very beautiful and creatively presented. Service was great as well. Peeky toe crab - decent Tomato soup - OK Gnocchi - good Hyssop dessert - OK

After a long day of taking my boyfriend's family shopping and whatnot downtown it became evident that we a) were STARVING and b) had no reservations for dinner. Had I known this would be the case I would've done my blackberry-yelping sooner. However, it was Valentine's Day weekend. In Manhattan. On a Saturday. Talk about impossible finding a place to eat/get a reservation? Lanterna, because I like to shorten it, came in the clutch. Strolling around Houston and getting a drink at a bar down the street I managed to make an executive decision to trust my fellow yelper reviews and attempt to get a table. It happened! We got a table for 4 downstairs. The restaurant itself is very overcrowded. When you walk in it almost seems impossible to get past all of the tables and chairs to get to the stairs in the back. We managed to do it, although I am sure my shopping bags hit some patrons on my way (I had a few drinks, leave me alone). We decided on a bottle of wine, which I cannot recall the exact one, but it was not terrible at all. The atmosphere is very dark. Very dark. The downstairs was cold also. There is a back door exit from the basement that will take you right outside but everytime someone opened it the entire area would be freezing. The staff was friendly yet chaotic. We were helped by more than one waitress, but I'll give them credit - the food was fast and it WAS the night before Valentine's Day. As far as the food goes, the lasagnas were great. Served extremely hot, they had a bit more cheese and bit less everything else. Overall the portions were nicely sized for the price of the meal. For dessert the tiramisu was an excellent choice, well worth the $5-or so to cleanse the palate and leave a delicious taste in your mouth. Overall, with 4 entres, a bottle of wine, dessert, and kahlua capuccinos (which are a must, obviously) the meal was only around $150 which I could not complaint at all! Overall a pleasant experience, although I would try to go back on an evening when it's less chaotic and I would like to check out the bar that's (awkwardly) attached in the basement.

Want to spend $21 and feel like a baller? Here's a step-by-step guide: 1) Find two friends who concur with the notion of "Let's ball out." 2) Order one (1) ceviche and the Matador Combo 3) Be blown away by the melty-velvety glory of what seemed like Peruvian sashimi 4) Laugh hysterically at how effing lucky you are when the waiter lays down plate after plate of citrusy salad, subtle french fries with lil' baby snausages, GLORIOUS spiced and tender chicken (a lot of it), fried plantain things with a sweet garlic dipping sauce that reminds me of other 'crack sauces' across the world, rice and beans that are very much alive...oh, and the creamy green sauce they bring! Dip your fries in that, as well as the sweet garlic sauce that comes with the plantains. 5) Laugh you're head off because you are LUCKY. Twenty-one dollars without drinks including tip. The ambiance is moving and celebrity-like, in my humble, cheap, scrapping-by opinion.

Best pasta in the city. You can taste that everything in homemade and fresh. There is always at least a 30 minute wait for this place, but it is worth it. I had the bolognase and my friend had the gnocchi, which was the best of the two. I also recommend having the tirimisu. It was amazing. I give it five stars because it is delicious food and a great price. You don't have to break the bank for a meal here.

One of the most lowkey dope vibe in Cobble Hill yet. I love the ambiance, the wait staff and most importantly, the food. ESCARGOTS- Do it. MUSSELS with Thai Curry-Oooo La La LA FRENCH ONION SOUP- Meh, Can be too sweet My fave yet is their RISSOTO. Ever changing, mushroom, aspargus, all so made perfectly. My dude loves the steak frite and lemme tell you what's even more dope...the FRIES. ADDICTIVE CRISPY THIN FRIES. MMMMMMMMMM Price Range- Expected $$ but fair, not shabby Do it up and get a bottle of wine-worth it. FRIES FRIES FRIES FRIES Gulp.

Really I want to give this place three and a half stars. Listen, the menu sounds great, but I had a veggie burger (which I don't usually get) and my friend got sliders. My burger wasn't very good at all. Her sliders were, but they weren't filling at all. But both of those things were more expensive than they should've been. I like their beer selection. She got some pasty pumpkin drink which wasn't very good but cost as much as the burger. Well I'll tell you what, this place has a great vibe and when I went in there, the crowd was really....normal and not obnoxious in any. That and some cool employees, and really I'm not going to be unhappy. But who knows. I can see the stars aligning and this place being a blast.

Service: The service here was absolutely awesome. Â I had made a reservation for a large group of 12, and changed the size of the reservation two times, but they were still more than happy to help me change my reservation and were very accommodating. Â Water was refilled a couple of times throughout the meal. Â The waiter & cashier were both very courteous and polite, and didn't rush us to pay. Food: The food is what brings down the review to a 3-star review. Â We were served bread two ways after we ordered. Â There was bruschetta and plain Italian bread to dip in olive oil. Â The bruschetta was quite flavorful, but the Italian bread required lots of chewing. Â  For the main course, I ordered a Roasted Codfish, which was on the "Today's Special" menu. Â Portion size was quite decent, and presentation wasn't bad. Â When I started to cut the cod, I was excited to taste it because the layers of the fish just fell apart by themselves. Â However, the texture of the fish really threw me off. Â It was rather chewy and stringy for codfish, to the point where I started to think that the fish they served was from the refrigerated aisle of the supermarket. Â The inside of the cod also was quite bland. Â The other parts of the dish were fine, however. Â The potatoes had a nice charr to them, with soft and warm meat. Â There was an abundance of spinach to help balance the meal. Â The sauce was flavorful with lemon, but I wish there was more wine to it, since after all, it was a lemon white wine sauce. Ambiance: Quiet, a nice place to bring a date

Horrible service. Unless of course you are a hipster. I came here with my wife and kid because of Yelp. The server looked at us and said "You can have a seat but I don't know where you are going to put that stroller". I understand it is a small place but he basically didn't want us to be there at all. I assume it would have ruin their "hipster" atmosphere since everyone in the restaurant matched perfectly to the "hipster" stereotype. It made my wife and I so mad , so we left. Their arrogant attitude just is off putting.

Went here on a Saturday and unknowingly made it in time for brunch. My friend wanted to try balut, but we couldn't because there's a particular brunch menu. It was really crowded, but we didn't have to wait long. The servers are extremely helpful and friendly and don't hesitate to explain things. Even the bartender came over to talk to us! I ordered the flip'd chicken & waffle. The ube waffle is SO good but the anchovy-bagoong butter puts it over the top. It's buttery, salty, and ever so slightly fishy (strange I know, but it's the bomb). The macapuno syrup is basically like a light, silky caramel and pairs so well with the butter. Salty-sweet is a popular combo for a reason! They give you two big pieces of chicken and it's batterless, but the skin is crispy nonetheless. Friend ordered the dasilog: the silog breakfast with bangus, a crispy fish. He liked it, but he also ate one of my chicken pieces to fill him up. I want to go back to try everything else... and the ube waffle again...

This place is quite a few blocks away from the nearest subway. I went here on a quest for a great noodle soup but left disappointed. The tasty hand-pulled noodles were not tasty. It was just okay and I've had better and didn't have to walk far away either! The broth was weak, the noodles were okay. Nothing special. Their tables were nasty, seems like they never wiped them, nor their glass door.

I gained access to a secret club a few weeks ago and I was too intimidated by their scare tactics to discuss the gritty details...until today. If you're like me, you like variety. When perusing a menu I have to quell the urge to order five dishes and try a few bites of each until the point of satiation. To be able to eat three incredible, perfectly proportioned sandwiches from Lamazou in one sitting is a dream come true for most, and a reality for our lunch club. The rules of the lunch club are as follows: 1. Go early. Each sandwich takes five minutes for them to create and a queue of more than five people at the deli counter means a significant time commitment for your sandwich...ahem, make that three sandwiches. 2. No tomatoes. A certain founding member will not tolerate them and even threaten your expulsion should she find one in a sandwich. 3. Order by number. Some examples of excellent past orders... Â  Â  - #18 - Manou: sliced buffalo chicken, smoked gouda, sundried tomatoes Â  Â  - #20 - Smart Duck: Smoked breast of duck with brie & cornichons Â  Â  - #16 - Â Lamoretti: roast beef, cheddar & cornichons Â  Â  - # 19 - Butterfly: Black pepper patÃ©, munster, cornichons and butter 4. Ask for them to slice each sandwich into threes. 5. Get a peanut butter bomb if you're feeling particularly indulgent. It was actually worth the caloric commitment to taste the peanut butter gelato encased in a milk chocolate shell. 6. While you wait, be sure to check out all the imported Italian products lining the shelves. 7. Pay with cash. They take credit card but the 30 seconds you save with cash will make the rest of the club happy. 8. Split up the three chunks of the three sandos and enjoy three versions of deliciousness for the price of one! So now that I've broken the cardinal rule of Lunch Club and let the cat out of the bag. Let's just hope that they take pity on me...and want that third sandwich enough to overlook any indiscretions.

Excellent Italian-American food in Brooklyn. Â My favorite and also I think the best. Â However, with this being true it is now completely over run. Â It gets so busy that it's literally not worth going if you're not going to be there before 6 on Thurs, Fri, Sat. Â The last time I ate there we had a table for 4 at 2:00 on Sat and walked right in and we seated. Â Would definitely go again, definitely will go again. Cookbook rocks as well.

Came here for what it's famous for - brunch. I love how they give you fresh squeezed orange juice AND coffee. However, the orange juice was warm. If it was cold, it would've been perfect. ): I got the FBLT (F for fake) which was some sort of soy bacon just to try it out. Not bad, but I think next time I'll go for real bacon. It was CROWDED when we got there, but we were seated after 20 minutes even though they said we'd have to wait an hour, so that was a pleasant surprise. Service was so-so, but I guess that's because we were in a corner that's particularly uncomfortable to reach.
food overpriced and small portions good sangrias waiters are kind of alpha-doggy-like

One of the best Sicilian slices in the city, all. 5 boroughs. L&B has been serving up Brooklyn for years. The upside down Sicilian slice. He'll yea I'm a fan. Great dough, sauce, and cheese. That's it , simple! I hear they have great spumoni as well. Time to go back and check it out.
awesome brisket+BBQ - terrible terrible coleslaw and OK sides

I would choose a rainy day to trek out to Mamoun's. Squeaky feet and wet jeans did not at all hinder my ability to both enjoy and devour the food at Mamoun's. The falafel sandwich was enough to fill me up, but being arrogant I thought I could handle the baba ghanouj (w/ pita) as well. Overall, I thoroughly enjoyed the extraordinarily cheap food. Just a few notes: space is very small, so you'd probably be wise to take your food to go and enjoy it at Washington Square Park. Also, cash only... but with prices this cheap, it's not too big of a deal!

When I found out a Bahn Mi joint opened up in my neighborhood I was ecstatic! Â There are no good Vietnamese sandwich places in Queens and when I get my Bahn Mi cravings (which is often) I have to travel all the way to Brooklyn. Â I am happy to report, Joju's does not disappoint! Â I've had the Bahn Mi at Pho Bac and other places in Queens, but their choices are limited and the sandwiches do not taste fresh and must be taken To-Go. Â  FOOD: I had the Grilled Pork chop and also the BBQ Pork sandwiches with spicy mayo. Â They were really good - I loved the warm crusty bread (can be chewy at other Bahn Mi places) and the meat was very flavorful but not too salty. Â I wish they put a little more meat because it was so yummy, but for less than $5 a sandwich, what would you expect? Â The spicy mayo was great but not too spicy. Â However, you can add your own amount of Sriracha sauce available on the tables there if you like it super spicy. Â My friend had the Grilled Lemongrass Chicken Bahn Mi and said that it was yummy and the meat was very tender and juicy. Â I will have to go back another time to try the Bulgogi Kimchi Bahan Mi. Â Since I'm trying to cut down my sugar-intake I had the cold jasmine Green tea - not too sweet yet flavorful and healthy. Â It was ok.....but I was eyeing my friend's Iced Vietnamese Coffee with Mocha and whipped cream the whole time.... SERVICE: Â The service was great when I arrived - there were not too many people yet. Â I had just beat the lunchtime rush. Â When it did get busy, there were a lot of people waiting but no one seemed to really mind since it was so hot outside. Â My advice is if you don't want to wait 10min or if you're ordering a lot of sandwiches - call it in beforehand. Â The staff there is super friendly and really tries to cater to your needs. Â  AMBIENCE: Â Very chill, minimalist atmosphere and very clean and new. Â The bathroom was surprisingly really nice. Â I think they had around 4 or 5 tables there. Overall, I enjoyed my food experience at Joju's and will be going back soon when my next Bahn Mi craving hits and will update my review....

This restaurant is right up my alley. LITERALLY!! (Well, Walworth isn't exactly an alley, but you catch the drift). I work up the block on Willoughby Ave and it is super hard to resist popping in for a bite now. I went there on a date and all of the menu choices were different, appealing, and savory! Tried the mussels and ate them all. My date had the braised lamb. Little known fact: it is B.Y.O.B., so I brought a delicious Spanish Cider from Bed Stuy Beer Works and it was THE combo breaker for dinner.

this is such a hidden treasure! it's on the side of ABC carpet&home and currently under scaffolding so i think everyone's first time might get confusing just finding it. but when you enter.. it is just beauuuuttiiifullll! it turns me into mush every time i go. i would say i have the equivalent of beer goggles on when i'm inside, the setting and food is so perfect that i think everyone starts looking better. that does get a little dangerous when i start drinking because they also have interesting cocktails and sodas, be adventurous! abc is all about sourcing local food so everything tastes amazingly fresh. i think apps are the strongest feature with the peekytoe crab as its superstar and for dessert, the only thing you should order is the salted caramel sundae with candied nuts and popcorn, everything else is a waste of space. seriously. service is... what it is for such a trendy place. if you make a reservation or is john mayer you have nothing to worry about and will have a pleasant experience. if you just want to drop by for a spontaneous lunch/dinner here just grab a seat by the bar, it's first come first serve and the full menu can be ordered. enjoy!
Cafe Steinhof has great decor, service, and food. Â Dining there is a great experience. Â It is highly recommended.

If you are looking for an old Italian restaurant family style, look no further. All plates are to be shared as the portions are generous. Reasonably priced, cash only. We had the stuffed mushrooms and linguine with white clam sauce and the taste is still lingering in my mouth. Two thumbs up, there will definitely be a repeat visit.

Mamoun's Falafel is a great choice late at night when you are very hungry and hardly any other restaurants are open and it is too late to go to the store. Â Mamoun's is a great choice after drinking, after socializing, after eating at another restaurant for dinner, after meandering aimlessly in the village, after coming back from a visit to Queens via the Long Island Railroad, etc. Â The simple fact is that Mamoun's is simply great all-around. I really appreciated that their food is so affordable. Â I ordered the combination platter and for just $11, I got chicken kebab, hummus, rice, falafel, and tabbouleh salad. Â I love their pita bread and tahini sauce. Â I also love the big portions. Â  It's not the most authentic Middle Eastern food I've eaten (take it from a Middle Eastern girl), but it's still pretty darn good, especially late at night. Â I hear the lamb shawarma is great too. Â  I would definitely recommend Mamoun's and would love to visit again.

Tuk Tuk was a fortunate happenstance; when the original dinner plans fell through, a few friends and I scrambled to find a back-up plan for the night. Tuk Tuk was one of the first options that showed up on our Yelp apps and happened to only be a few blocks away; as we didn't have many other alternatives in LIC and the reviews appeared to be fairly promising, we quickly headed over to the other side of Vernon Boulevard. The interior of this restaurant is modest and bright, even during the evening; the white walls appear out of place, at first glance, but offer a nice contrast to the darkened floors and the "traditional" dining ambiance. When we arrived, there were only a few other diners present, so we were quickly seated and given menus and glasses of water for the night. We each decided on our own entrees, but decided to share one of their more popular mains as an appetizer of sorts, just to sate our curiosities. First, the Kau Gling, which we shared as an appetizer. As one of the few options labeled "Majorly Spicy", it was almost impossible for me to avoid ordering, and I somehow managed to persuade my friends to also join in the order. It's a dish comprised of stir-fried beef served with a variety of vegetables (cucumbers, broccoli, and string beans) and a scoop of white rice. While I didn't find it particularly spicy, the beef is tender and flavorful, with spice and acidity contributed by the lemongrass, tumeric, and Thai chilies added to the mix. The vegetables are simply steamed before plating, but were a nice contrast in between bites, and seemed to bring some relief to my friends. And being a creature of habit, I decided on the Chicken Pad Thai (extra spicy, please) as my main. Our server had no problem noting the adjustment in spice levels, and in due time, a compact plate of steaming rice noodles was placed in front of me. There's all the typical ingredients that you'd expect - diced tofu, crushed peanuts, egg, and crisp bean sprouts on the side - all in a compact, yet surprisingly hearty serving. I was delighted to find that my request had been taken seriously, and the additional dose of chili peppers was significantly present. From what I tried of the other dishes, they were all solid across the board; the roast duck was well-cooked with a crisp skin, and the steak was also surprisingly tasty, even though it was served with a nontraditional side of mashed potatoes. While LIC doesn't have a dining scene that can compare to most areas of downtown Manhattan, it does have a few scattered gems throughout its neighborhood. Tuk Tuk is definitely one of these, serving quality Thai food at reasonable prices. It's a viable option when in the area, and might even be worth a separate trek even if you reside in another borough.

I've been here a few times (and some of those times might have been in the other location but they look the same and I... confuzzled) -- none of those times were really extraordinarily memorable. But I keep coming back to try other items I haven't tried. This time, I had the special of the day, sukiyaki cold soba with dipping soup. It was tasty, but the tempura crumbs soaked up the soup very quickly and made my dipping sauce... solid. Coconut dessert was delicious, but it was made with frozen fruits and the whole thing quickly congealed... We came here because the other location was busy. This one is bigger and was not crowded at all. They still rush you to order and finish though, but that might just be customary. I'll probably come back again and not be blown away.

This is a solid spot for Thai food- ginger sauce with chicken is great, as is the pineapple fried rice. Mojitos are nice and strong, and they have a fantastic deal on Mondays (I think) that gets you an entree and 2 apps for $10! Only complaint is service tends to be slow, but overall a nice place to stop in for dinner.

Total love for Taim Falafel for their great felafels and super fast delivery. I've only ordered delivery, never been to the actual place - but I am convinced their service is faster than if I was to walk down their and order! Order always arrives within about 20 mins. I love their harissa felafel, so crispy and delicious! They are on the small side, but taste good so I am still happy. I always order the felefal plate, which comes with felafel, hommus and 2 salads, pita.. If you order an extra pita this is enough to feed 2 people. Â Their salads taste fresh and yummy too, and you can ask for alternative salads to the standard ones provided in the plate. All in all a great delivery option when you need a fast fix of food that still tastes fresh and healthy!

bring a wheel barrow to carry yourself out because you will not be able to move after you eat here. the food is soo good and thick you will not be able to stop eating. the cappucinos are great as well as their pastas and ravoli's. do not leave without trying the garlic bread as well. one of my all time favorite italian resturants. the only down side is they didn't have the greatest deserts and since its a huge restaurant it was loud.

Great service! Inventive menu with shared small plates the salt and pepper shrimp was good , foie gras enjoyable and the sweet breads great. Â It's a small place and it's a little further east than indicated on yelp. Â It is definitely worth the trip to Brooklyn for dinner here. Â Reasonably priced too.

Where to begin!? I work in the Flatiron District and wanted to try something new. Barn Joo has been on my list of places to dine but never got the chance until the other day. After getting out of work early I decided to give their Happy Hour a shot. Best deal I've encountered yet. They have $1 oysters, $4 draft beer, $5 wine, $6 sangria, $7 specialty cocktails and food options. The best part of this deal is that it's every day! I tried their Smoked Manhattan and it was just decadent. A very well balanced drink that really speaks to the pallet. I've heard and read that they're wings, specifically their soy-garlic flavored wings, were really good so I had to give those a try. Trust me, it's something everyone should order. Juicy chicken on the inside and crispy yet nicely glazed on the outside. Even though it was busy, the bartender's were still able to make me feel acknowledged. Overall, a great experience on all levels. Will have to try their wheel of prizes next time I go!

Why is there a line? And why is the line so long?. These are the words that all newcomers to 53rd and 6th say when they try to buy a plate of chicken over rice with white sauce. The secret is, the is line so long which is why you get on in the first place. This halal cart is a touch above the rest, but enough to remember as the goto spot anytime of day or night. The chicken has a quick turn around so it tastes fresh, even with all the seasonings. Add hot sauce, white sauce, bbq sauce and ask for the not so well know peices of pita and you have an excellent meal. Even my mostly vegan gf stole a large chunk of my meal, smiling the entire time.

I heart Ramen! Since I was on vacation, I came here in the middle of a workday. Even so, the wait was still about 30 minutes. But it was definitely worth it. =) I heard if you finish all the noodles, they come by and give you more. I wish I heard this tip before i tried ippudo though! perhaps it'll work for you!
Only three stars for a forgettable prociutto-stuffed chicken breast and spotty service. Bonus points for having Blue Point Toasted Lager on tap.
Awesome food and fairly priced. Best soulfood in Harlem

Steak was greasy. Yuck. My experience at Runner and Stone was out of convenience. I was looking for a nice place to have dinner, before heading to a concert at Barclays. The place in general was great, drinks were ok, but the food is nothing to even mention. I should have ordered something else. I did however, have a great salad.
