It was fried pig ear and a fried egg on top...Weird right? It was the only thing I had that was good. Ok, Let's do this... PROS: Good Location in Brooklyn. A little bit in the cut... but you can walk from local hotels. Clean Friendly staff/ waiters CONS: Small menu Not a great steak... (I asked for med rare, got well.) Drink menu limited

Best Sicilian Pizza Pie EVER! They double rise the crust, and then put the cheese on, THEN the tomato sauce. Any other pizza, FUGGEDABOUTIT!!! P.S. I went on the "Slice of Brooklyn" bus tour and didn't have to wait in line because Paula made our reservations and ordered as much pizza and soda as we could eat and drink. Definitely a consideration if time is an issue for you as you travel.

Okay, so my TV hasn't worked in years and so my only exposure to Top Chef has been the ads on the subway. And I have no idea who Harold Dieterle is. But, regardless, I am now a huge fan. Perilla is a small, warm spot (the decor reminds me of Kitchen 22 for some reason) with a small-medium sized bar and a bunch of tables. The service was warm, but what impressed me was the food. I am not a fan of a bunch of fancy things being mixed together to make something worse... the gastronomic equivalent of Paris Hilton. (Was it Thomas Keller who said that you can only ruin foie gras and truffles. But something like cauliflower... well that you can only make better.) What Dieterle does is impressive along the T. Keller sense, as he meshes sublime and simple flavors to make something subtle and wonderful... more a gastronomic equivalent of Charlotte Gainsbourg. I really enjoyed the duck meatballs, the monkfish cheek appetizer (special) and the pork belly (a.k.a. bacon with more fatty goodness than anything). Delicious! The duck main course was perfectly cooked on a bed of greens with a foie gras sauce I would have drank, it was so good. Prices were reasonable... get in this week and they take 10% off your bill for "growing pains" week. But go. Eat. Enjoy. And support this little spot. It deserves it way more than Paris Hilton deserves to get out of jail.

The food is okay, when they have any. Â Went here on a Friday night and the host told us what they had left in the kitchen; fries and some pork dishes. What restaurant tells you there is NO MORE FOOD IN THE KITCHEN. Those words should never be said to a fat person at heart. So, that was disappointing. Now I come from a long line of southern people and one thing you do not do is not have any food in the kitchen. I was disappointed and didn't think that I would go back or even tell anyone about it. But my boyfriend made me give the place another shot. (This time there was food) and it was okay for a BBQ joint. Would I recommend? Only if you're desperate.

Went there on halloween around 2pm. Had been wanting to go for quite some time an after trick or treating with my son and his mom I suggested we stop here as I live around the corner and have been dying to try it. Food was excellent and moderately priced. For the three of us it came out to $30.They had some nice soothing music on and it was very cozy. The bathroom is very clean but the service leaves a little bit to be desired - but ah so what. I'm looking forward to coming here for dinner, I woud say this is a perfect place for a date, brunch or dinner with the parents. I even see people stop here for breakfast before work. I defenitely suggest this little place.

I thought it was a bit odd that they seated you next to strangers at a round table, but we quickly got over that fact. They have two soup dumplings, one containing just pork, and one containing a mixture of crab and pork. Hands down, the crab and pork one is the best! The flavor was spot on. I felt the pork soup dumplings lacked in the flavor department. A must try! Cash only!

I went here for lunch with my family. They honored my reservation, which is unusual in the restaurant business. We were seated at a nice comfortable table. Service was prompt and attentive. We all had different items for lunch and no one was disappointed. Stand outs are; white shrimp salad, huevos rancheros, pulled pork sandwich and a juicy burger with a fried egg on top. Do Not miss the fresh ginger margarita. One of the best in the city. I will def retur.

Good, but could be so much better... The duck meatballs are very good... Â (but they're still just meatballs, so not super exciting or "different") Also had the Octopus garganelli app... Â Also very good but nothing to hype about. My wife had the Stone Bass... Â I like hers more than mine. Â The fish was overcooked and dull. Â The accompaniment of the pistachios was incredible but with the overcooked fish the dish never sang to me... I had the duck... Â which was cooked pretty good. Â Nice medium/medium rare. Â But the rest of the dish seemed detached and overly sweet. The cheese plate we had after the meal and the Coconut Thai chili drinks were actually the highlights of our meal... Â Which is a shame that our main courses fell so flat and I spent over $200 for 2. Â (There is a restaurant in Philly that blows this place away for $30 per person...)

The food BLEW MY MIND! Literally the best thing I have tasted in the Bedford-Stuyvesant/Clinton Hill area. Throughout the entire meal, my fiance and I thought "I wish we could have our wedding here!" We will definitely visit again!

One of the most flavorful Malaysian Cuisine I had. It's so tasty and it's always a great experience every time I come. The waiters are very friendly and attentive, except sometimes when I need a refill for my water. The price for the amount of food given is also acceptable. One of my favorite spots in Elmhurst
A convenient spot for business lunches. The food is delicious but a little slow so make sure you're not in a rush.

Having been a Park Slope resident, my wife and I tried Rose Water. Â Seriously disappointed. Â We left before we even received our beverages. Â The service is horrible Â They are too arrogant. Â 50,000 restaurants in NYC, do not need this attitude.

In a tourist-driven, delicatessen-infested area that is so desperate for quality food options, Hagi is perhaps the one (and only) choice for food. Â While the space can be intolerable at times and the speakeasy feel makes it less conducive to quality conversation, you would happily take the plentiful food choices which yakitori and izakaya lovers will vouch for in a heartbeat. The menu is traditional izakaya and every plate is consistently perfect in terms of flavor and texture. The sake options are plentiful and Hakkaisan is a personal favorite. Come with the knowledge that it will always be fully patronized, but for the quality of food you are getting, it is well worth the wait.

Eclectic menu but good food. A bistro air with Asian-Americn-Frech-whatever mix of dishes. Very reliable for lunch or dinner. Clearly the top line restaurant within walking distance of Columbia. That's not saying a lot though. My main complaint is that the menu changes very infrequently and there are seldom specials, so you end up with the same dishes all the time.

Malatesta thrives on its small but well-executed menu. We came with a large group for a friend's birthday, and it was a thoroughly enjoyable experience. Â Everyone loved the delicious, fresh house made pasta, and the pleasantly low bill that came at the end (average pasta dish $10-$13). The spinach gnocci is a must-try: I can still taste the tender, creamy pillows of pasta mingled with a delicious cream sauce. Â The tagliatelle al ragu was also tasty, but if you were to pick one dish - - gnocchi. Â To end the meal, go with the tiramisu, which although nothing out of the ordinary, does not disappoint. My only warning is the place can get pretty loud at night, so it's hard to have a conversation with anyone not sitting within 2 feet.

I came here with my roommate and girlfriend for brunch yesterday afternoon. There aren't many tables in the restaurant, and with the windows open, it very much had the feel of a small Parisian cafe (or at least what I remember them to be like from visits long ago). The service was decent, although I would say that it was a bit slower than I have experienced elsewhere. I didn't mind it that much, given it's a slow holiday weekend, but I probably would've been less blase about it if I was in a rush. The food itself was simple and light, which I really enjoyed. I got the French toast, which was indeed fluffy and definitely on the lighter end of French toasts I've had in the past. You get loads of sugar sprinkled on top, with apple compote on top - a nice complement that isn't too strong and overwhelm the toast with syrup on it. I sampled the wild vegetable omelet my girlfriend had, which was much lighter than other omelets I've had - most likely due to no cheese. The vegetables were a wide variety, though, and the herbs added a dash of flavor that you usually don't get. We got a pot of mussels for the table to share; these were delicious (especially the broth in which they were cooked), but I did feel like they may have been steamed a little on the long side. For brunch, I was also sorely disappointed with the orange juice - every city I can recall serves fresh OJ on their brunch menu; Le Parisien serves up OJ that tastes like concentrated Minute Maid with ice in it. The beverage aside, the rest of the meal was very pleasant. $13 for brunch is a pretty decent deal, and they have a good selection of choices for the meal. I'm not sure if I'd come back frequently - there are an abundance of good places in the neighborhood - but it's a solid alternative to a place like Penelope's.

it was good to try, but the portions are small, and i like small portions. Â not actually enough to REALLY get a good bite. Â the pita was meh, and the sauces were the same. Â i like hummus place or yummus in Bushwick better. Â i'd even say i like maoz better...at least i can make my own sandwitch.

Tread carefully when it comes to asking for extra spice. The first time I experienced Bonnie's was with a friend who-- I kid you not-- is a buffalo wing eating champion from Upstate New York. He suggested we try Bonnie's to eat some wings and beer. The ambiance was alright, the counters were clean, the guys working seemed friendly. He told them "She likes spicy food, so can you make them hot... and then some?" I was totally ready for it. Until I took two small bites out of one chicken wing and was crying literally uncontrollably for 20 minutes. The heat was MEAN. My friend couldn't even go past 3 wings. I have never before experienced spice like that in my life. It was inedible. Someone gave me a glass of milk but I wasn't okay again until I brushed my teeth and got rid of the remaining sauce in my mouth. We had others try the wings we took away, and they agreed with me. I gave them another chance and tried the wings again, it was much better. What I find funny is that I could tell my server recognized me as the girl crying from the wings he couldn't look at me in the face.

Woohoo! As good as it gets! - At least in this neighborhood. Collard GREENS. So we all know this is the place. Yesterday, I had a sad, though convenient experience. I walked up to Veronicas at 12:40 PM on a Friday, when it was actually kind of nice outside, and there was no line. None. Usually would be 25 people. There was a guy paying. That was it. At first I thought it must be some other stand. I asked the nice man who takes my money after Veronica gives me my food. He said its been like this for awhile. The Economy. Yes. It was near the holidays, in winter. But there was NO LINE. While this is great for me, and means I'll be going more often, it was also sad. Really sad. So this is a shout out to support the restaurants you love in these times, if you can. Veronica's is one of those places that deserves your support, and you'll certainly leave happy.

For an enchanting evening! Had reservations for a booth for two at 8PM, our table was ready, my wife could sit facing the window so as the snow started the romantic setting became perfect. The Rosemary olives on the table when you arrive are high quality and delicious. The French bread with creamy butter is also terrific and plenty of it. We had the duck terrine as an appetizer and the duck entrÃ©e and shared both which gave us room for a little dessert. The wine recommendation by the waiter was also perfect, a French wine of course. This place is definitely a keeper.

Incredibly mediocre wood oven pizza. Â Avoid the margherita pizza. Â The dough is completely flavorless and they are very skimpy on the cheese. Â I don't need 100% of the pie covered with cheese. Â I don't even need 75% coverage. Â This was around 30%. Â The sauce is nothing to write home about either - thin, no depth at all. Â At least the herbs were very fresh. Pasta was cooked well and had a good sauce, but came out lukewarm like it had been plated well before the pizza was ready. Â I would describe the serving sizes as "adequate" but not generous. Overall disappointing.

I spent a year reading reviews about this place. On surveys of outer borough places to eat, Kickshaw seemed to be a way for Serious Eats, Bon Appetit, etc to pay lip service to the fact that there might actually be somewhere decent to eat in Queens. So I was a little hopeful, a little scared to actually GO to the restaurant/coffee bar in question. However I can now say with confidence that I was pleasantly surprised. For brunch, I had one of the pour-over coffees, which was really fantastic. All of the various dishes we ordered were delicious, filled with butter, but not served in gut-busting proportions, which was nice. I had the egg sandwich, which was really delicious and only 5 bucks. 5 bucks! Come on. If this was served in Manhattan it would've easily been $17, $18, $22. The price of a hardcover book. But here: 5 bucks! We also had the bread pudding, which was delicious, and I sampled the roasted vegetables with an egg, which was as delicious as you'd expect, with crispy brussels sprouts and halved tiny potatoes. Really looking forward to going back for a non-brunch meal and sampling the prodigious beer and cider list. I had the impression that this place was just overpriced grilled cheese--that's really not the case. It's a cute, casual little restaurant that I hope to visit often. I wish there were more places like this in Astoria!
Great food and good sangria! Â Watch out for the old people that get pestered by big groups.

I am going to be coming here a lot. Â  My dinner last night here was DELICIOUS. Â I got the Buta Kim-Chee Nabe hot pot. Â Thinly sliced pork belly, kim-chee, tender tofu, soft-boiled egg, chives, and egg custard and pickled carrot/cabbage on the side. Â It was seasoned beautifully, at the perfect level of spice and heat. Â  Photo here: instagram.com/p/nb5SERMcâ€¦ Last night was unseasonably cold and wet - we ran inside in the middle of a downpour - and this hit the spot better than ANYTHING ever has to counteract this kind of weather. Also, how have I never had egg custard before??? Â Mind BLOWN. Â It tasted like buttered toast - same kind of umami richness - but with even more of a delicate consistency than panna cotta. Â It was a warm, savory delight. Â I'm salivating now just thinking about it. Best part? Â At $20 for the dish, it was enough food for two meals. Â Granted, I think I eat small - my dining companion finished her whole dish. I haven't even mentioned the ambiance, gorgeous decor, supremely clean bathroom, and Sakura the incredibly friendly and informative server at the counter area. Â This Â experience was perfect.

Solid 4 star East Village restaurant. There was a bit of a wait, but it was worth it as we got to sit outside with our group. Waitress was awesome and guided through what is a funky but solid Gastropub menu. Somewhat of an asian influence to the menu. Every dish seemed to get better throughout the meal. What we ordered: Brisket Jerky (good, smoky, and spicy as it went on) Deez Nuts (Nice lime/spice kick with smoked meat, pretty good) Pickled Veggies (refreshing after first two dishes, but wouldn't get again) Crispy Pigs Ears (Great, crispy and savory) Chicken Wings (Curried w/ Cilantro, very solid) St. Louis Ribs (Maybe the best dish of the night, perfectly smoked) Goat Neck (Excellent, goat-y, flavorful with coconut rice) Will definitely go back, very reasonable for the amount of food/beers we had. Tuesday night is Brisket night, and Thursday is Crawfish night, so thats worth a visit alone.
Not crowded at all on a Sunday afternoon. The guac is decent but nothing out of the common way. However, the meat arepas are nothing short of succulent.

Really great place in the heart of downtown Brooklyn, Bijan's somehow is able to straddle the nearly invisible line between great food and can't-be-beat Brooklyn prices. The cocktails in particular are stupendous, with a seven hour HH that is somehow longer than the the "regular priced" drinks. I also really like that all of the bartenders are very chill, relatable people, who can be themselves and still make a great drink. Get the chicken wings and the Lamb burger!!!!

The grill cheese at the Melt Shop is so goood, if you eat their sandwiches everyday they are probably going to kill you. I ordered the Truffle Melt -- Havarti, Truffle Oil, Arugula on a Sourdough. The sourdough was toasty and crispy, combined with the gooey melted cheese, fresh havarti and arugula, and a hint of truffle oil I felt like I was in heaven! I tried the tots previously and they were very good as well. Keep in mind that you will need to wait 5-7 minutes for the sandwich and they only accept credit cards. Service is very friendly so give it a try!

Pleasant space and very nice bartender, but my meal of an appetizer, a beer, and a side of polenta totalled $60 with tip. Â The grilled octopus appetizer was weirdly fatty. Â The polenta was nice, but did not need the too healthy sprinkling of rosemary leaves on top. Â Lots of places in the city to get similar meals for far less.

This place is very tasty, the staff is attentive and friendly. I first discovered this place with a couple of lady friends. The staff was very nice to us (even after I'd shown up very late, causing our trio to monopolize our table for about three hours). Since then my boyfriend and I have gotten delivery and take out from Dar. Delivery has been very prompt (under 30 minutes and food was warm!), when we get takeout they always bring us water, and on the chillier nights mint tea. Overall, very nice restaurant. Homey feel, while also offering consistently classy and delicious food. I highly recommend the chicken shwarma wrap. Deeeelish.

The guy who worked in the front hooked us up with a table. Came in at 7:00 and was immediately seated because someone canceled their reservations. That was a plus. Our waitress was a little too overly attentive.She asked us if our food was okay at least twice for EACH plate of food we received. I'm sure her intentions were good but it can get quite annoying. We ordered the scallops, oysters, clams,crab cakes and the clams fettuccine. The food tasted good, especially the scallops. Now, up to this point, Upstate would probably still receive 4 stars. However my bf caught food poisoning from the food. He spent the entire weekend sick and had to take off work on Monday. Â We're thinking it might be either the raw clams or the raw oysters. Â I remember eating the clams and it had sand inside of it. Perhaps, it was not properly cleaned.

We made a last-minute decision to eat here. Food was very good, oysters were fantastic, octopus was prepared perfectly. Rabbit entree was very good, presented nicely and seasoned perfectly. Service was very nice. The restaurant was hopping and I look forward to trying it on a future visit. The drink list at the bar is very creative. Love the setting and atmosphere and hope very much we will visit here again in the future!

Let me just say that food wise it was a 3.5-4 star ordeal, but service was what pulled the overall rating down. We managed to get a 5:45pm reservation and the host at the door was super friendly and greeted me before I sat down. It is a very intimate space with tables a few inches away from each other so hearing other conversations is inevitable. Our server, Jorge R. (At least that's what it says on the receipt...short chubby bald guy with an accent), immediately started giving us an attitude when taking our order and was really impatient when we had questions about the dishes and substitutions. Okay fine, I would have brushed it off if he had not seemed pissed at us the entire freakin night and then proceeded to explicitly write on the check that gratuity is not included with a big circle around the 18-20% guideline. I've never seen that before especially from a restaurant of this caliber and the table next to us were two male Asians and he explicitly explained to them that it was not included either. As I said, it is a small place so I literally did not hear or see him do that to ANYONE ELSE, not even the table full of five middle age Caucasian ladies next to us, which he seemed way happier and friendly to serve. Even our water boy had more patience and kindness when I had to keep asking for condiments for the bread. I found Jorge's behavior extremely offensive and judgmental and it just ruined my dining experience. Meatball sliders weren't what they hyped up to be...it was big on the herbs. I also read if you get a nice server, they comp you on a fourth slider if you're sharing the dish. Well obviously that did not happen with Jorge. Pork chop was chewy and beans were subbed with brussel sprouts and the sweet and spicy sauce for that was not spread out consistently. Fried chicken was the winner of the meal and the sauce fantastic...was not dry at all like majority of other places. Personal preference but brussel sprouts could've been cooked a bit more. Great portions. French donuts with nutella and cinnamon were underwhelming and dry, and souffle, like others said, was more of a lava cake with really good espresso gelato.

Je t'aime Buvette! This small gastropub, tucked in the West Village, is super cute and charming! For 12pm on a Friday, it was very busy but we luckily got seats right away at the bar, where my companion and I could watch the action. We shared the Croissants, which came with butter and raspberry jam. They were tiny croissants but still great! They were soft, flakey and just melted in your mouth. He had the Frits l'Americaine (sunny side eggs with bacon & sage) and I, the Poached (poached egg over artichokes and fava beans). Mine usually comes with kale but they didn't have that, which was a-ok with me. Both dishes also came with toasted bread with drizzled olive oil on it. I loved the mix of textures on my dish, as well as the perfectly cooked poached egg. The portions are small but I was very full after mine. I can see the small portions being an issue for dinner but I think they were perfectly-sized for brunch. For drinks, I had the Chocolat Au Cafe (espresso & hot chocolate). Loved it. I plan on coming back to check out their dinner service. Rendez-vous anybody?

I came here on a cool spring night, and opted to take a seat indoors. I got the steak burrito and a frozen margarita. The steak was a long, thick slice, and pretty juicy. It had some rice and beans in it. It wasn't exactly bursting with flavor, but it was satisfying. The bottle of hot sauce at the table took it a long way. The frozen margarita was alright. Everything was a bit too underwhelming and expensive for me to want to come back. Still, there's probably something to be said for outdoor seating in the summer, easy food, and a place to eat in Ft. Greene.

I've walked passed Empanada Mama several times, and every time its packed! Granted, the space isn't that big so it's pretty easy to fill. Regardless. This was my first time here as a patron and I enjoyed it! It was a food adventure for me. I've had empanadas before, but every one has their own way. This adventure was to find empanadas with fun fillings. It was a success! My taste buds and my tummy were satisfied. :) I usually take food porn photo but I skipped this time (sorry). The service was friendly and the food came out pretty quickly. No complaints all around. I would definitely come back!
You only need to know one thing when you go to Malatesta: spinach gnocchi with gorgonzola sauce.

I went in to try the veggie dumplings here. While the fried pork dumplings are available immediately, the veggie dumplings are boiled and so you have to wait 10 minutes or so for them. They tasted fresh and were piping hot when I got them. They don't have a ton of flavor on their own, but with soy and sriracha sauce, they're a great little meal. I like that the place is clean and busy.

The best thing about Tia Pol was the authenticity. All the food really really REALLY tasted Spanish. Â Part of the my enjoyment at the restaurant was reminiscing and reliving my past life in Spain (now about 6 years ago)....which, understandably, might not be your experience. The food was great, though at times a bit pricey. Â The chorizo con chocolate was amazing, definitely the best thing we ordered. Also the paquetitos with jamon and manchego were incredible .... but very expensive. Definitely avoid the tortilla espanola .... it was really dry, with a really high potato to egg ratio and barely any onions. Â That was a waste of money. The drink with manzanilla and sprite was AWESOME, again, perhaps because it had a particular Spanish taste that I remember so fondly. Â But seriously, it was a great coctail type drink, in the style that I like (aka not tasting too much like hard alcohol). I would certainly go back again to Tia Pol. Â  Oh, and to reiterate other reviews, GO EARLY. Â We showed up at 5:50ish on a Friday, and by the time we left there were hungry patrons waiting for our table.

i've been just about everywhere in the lower east side and 3 days ago i tried the meatball shop, FINALLY. and honestly, if there was no food in the world but the meatball shop for the rest of my life, i would NOT get sick of it! this is the best food by a LONG SHOT ive had not only in the lower east side, btu for the price, maybe in all of nyc. in fact, ive already been back...i will pack on the pounds for these balls. it's totally worth it. my first time there i got chicken cordon bleu meatballs (ahsodiuasdisau so amazing) over brocolli in a parmesean cream sauce with a brownie cookie and mint ice cream for dessert. second time i split a bunch of sliders with my boyfriend (chicken in mushroom gravy, buffalo chicken in bleu cheese, spicy pork in spicy tomato, beef in parmesean cream, etc)..everything is perfect. i even called today just to see what their special balls were and may make a stop by later tonight it takes a lot for me to give 5 stars but this place deserves it. maybe they put crack in their meatballs but this shit is addicting
Not bad, not great either. The outdoor seating is cute.

Dependable "Cajun style" downtown Manhattan bar and eatery with good bartenders, drinks, an informed selection of bottled beers, and decent food. Â  And considering it's been busy for nearly every night of the twenty years it's been open, the place is in remarkably good condition. Â The portions can be massive, too--the pulled pork sandwich is both an eye and mouth opener--and the side of garlic mashed potatoes is positively giant. Â  It's not cheap, but remember: this is downtown Manhattan, folks--the center of the universe--where even 'humble' burgers, beers and fries are gonna cost you.

It took me an hour to get to Rosewater from Manhattan. When I arrived Â one of our party of three was already waiting. Â Even though Rosewater was almost empty Â the two of us Â were told we could not be seated until our party was complete......."Owners policy". I glanced around and counted ten unoccupied Â tables, the staff were firm, we could not be served. We opted to eat brunch at a more customer friendly restaurant a block away.
GREAT food. the bread was great, my pasta was superb, the appetizer was divine, and the desserts were amazing. good atmosphere and great service.
i had a great lunch here with their pre fix menu. amazing soup with delicious beans. very warm and cozy feel inside, very comfortable. great staff and very attentive. will def be back.

Reporting the lunch burger of course. It's solid for sure, but I guess my burger scale has been forever altered by Umami. Â The burger itself was juicy with good charred crisp. It was packed a little tight though, and then the factory bun and American cheese weren't so gratifying. Again I think I've been spoiled. A year ago I probably would see this burger in a much better light. Â Fries were delicious and service was great.

Referred here by our old friend Kazu at Sushi Kaito in Encinitas, CA. Â The quality of the product served here is very high and our server was top notch. Â This is not your neighborhood sushi place where good quality food is tossed around and everyone has a blast while it is happening. Â This is a much more staid atmosphere, almost antiseptic. Â I suppose that is what one should want out of a sushi joint, but I missed the fun. Â Come here if you're looking for sushi of impeccable quality in a quiet, reserved atmosphere and you have a pile of cash you'd like to spend. Â Don't come here for a great sake selection or Asahi Dark, because they have neither.

The quality of the restaurant deteriorated a lot! Â Time to move on to the other well deserving Thai restaurants in the area - and believe me there are several others in Hells Kitchen. Â After almost choking on the minuscule bones of the short rib tips, I asked the manager to adjust the check. Â He was bargaining about the situation making me feel almost criminal about it. Â The chicken satay was rubbery with no peanut sauce. Â The curries me and my friend ordered were "meh". I've been to Thailand a couple of times and the Thais believe in delivering utmost hospitality to their patron's experience, which was not the case here. Â Also, Thais do not eat their meals with chopsticks and rather use forks and knives in an effort to westernize their society as mandated by King Rama V. Â I was laughing along with my friend at the surrounding customers who eat their food with chopsticks for that "authentic" experience. In summary, walk out of any Thai restaurant that have chopsticks.

After watching their profile on the Â Food Network Triple "D," I decided to give 'em a try since I had to be in the area on Sunday, January 29, 2012. We arrived 'bout 5:30 and the place was full of people. However, we were seated immediately. I had their famous Ropa Vieja with Black beans and white rice. My companion had their steak and onions. My dish was delicious but slightly too sweet to eat the entire portion. The Black beans were slightly bitter on their own but when eaten together with rice, it was ok. My companion's steak was well under seasoned. It lacked flavor and thus, she left more than half behind. The chorizo appetizer is a "must have." It was full of flavor and not too salty. Our bill was $80.00 which included the Tip, 3 glasses of wine, Â an avocado side, and two 2 flan desserts. Â I felt that the $80.00 tab was excessive for rice and beans with some meat side dishes....I don't know and quite frankly, can't understand what all the rave is about. I must say that the Flan is the 5 star of the evening. There is no way that this place can command 5 stars....they are either over rated or people simply don't regularly eat Cuban/Spanish Food.

Really wanted to like, and will try again, but was disappointed. Â The kitchen was really slow, and my medium-rare burger came out medium well, after waiting 30+minutes. fries cold, which is annoying. perhaps they need to get out the kinks, and the breakfast looked good, but would have sent back my food had I another hour to dedicate to lunch.
Charming space and delicious food. We had a really meal here!

I haven't even gotten the chance to eat here yet but I'm already in love with it. An eclectic selection of well priced beers on draft plus delicious looking brick oven pizza makes this place amazing! The guy who runs it all, Bam, is really friendly and seems to know lots of the regulars, one of which I look forward to becoming. He recently got a good bit of publicity for his natural jerky which I can't wait to try. Going to have to go back for pizza! One thing to beware of, this place is CASH ONLY! I didn't know this and ended up having to use their ATM which ultimately slammed me with around $4 for withdrawal fees between the ATM and my bank. Ouch!
Fantastic BBQ, probably the best in NYC. Get there early if you don't want to wait in line. They open at noon on the weekends and usually it's easy to get in.

I quite enjoyed my experience at SoCo. It was my first Time here. The atmosphere was different, very funky, cozy, however can get a bit loud. My party of five had the cozy private booth in the back, a step higher than all other patrons which was cute. The bathrooms were clean, small, sinks outside we're a good utilization of space. Â One unisex bathroom, one male, one female. Onto the food: I started off with a peach cider which was great !! (kopparberg) and house tap water. For an appetizer I had the chickpea sliders, once I took a bite, it all went to mush, needless to say I'm glad it came with fries because I was NOT a fan of the sliders by any means, the mush texture in my mouth was... For lack of a better word, gross. My party had the chicken wings, ribs and gumbo, they enjoyed it but raved about the ribs most of all. For my main course I had the buttermilk chicken (two fried chicken thighs) with a red velvet waffle (dusted with confection sugar). It was to die for!!! So perfect, every bite. Highly recommend this main course. For desert I got the brownie Sunday, very very very good! Now the service: My waitress was pleasant however slow. It seemed like waiters/waitresses had tables all over the place instead of having a consistent section, which made things look slightly chaotic... They could improve on better direction of house staff. Side note: I got a side order of Mac and cheese(HUMUNGUS THREE PEOPLE COULD SHARE EASILY) Â I saved one thigh half a waffle and mostly all of my Mac to go... The buss boy packs my order with the Mac smushed ontop of the waffle and chicken being lazy to place the Mac in a separate container and didn't even close the to go container properly... I couldn't get over how stupid of a move that was... All and all I'll be back I recommend going early, we had 6pm reservations, got out at 815 pm, and it was just beginning to get very loud and crowded. Â The bar area remained packed however. Â Nice large bar area.

Fantastic lunch here. The food was fresh, and it felt like I was transported back to Italy. Service was friendly and extremely quick, even with a packed restaurant. If you're hitting up the museums with out of town visitors, take them here. If you're hanging in Central Park or need a break from shopping, check out Via Quadronno. Insalata Ruspanted con Ventresca di Tonno $16.50 Organic mixed greens with marinated tuna San babila (AMAZING) $13 Smoked ham, brie, fontina, rucola and pate Tiramisu di San Dona $15 (DEFINITELY WORTH IT) For two - tiremesu a la rustega Venetian style

I adored their food, menu specials, service and the terrasse for spring! We got piadina with arugula, it was delicious! Then the homemade spinach gnocchi a la Gorgonzola sauce and the spaghetti a la chitarra and it was divine! Especially the gnocchi !!! Apparently the wine was very good. The espressi were perfect... We'll go back to try another of their italian specialty. The mussels looked good !!!

The beer is delicious here!!! Food, not really worth it. Biggest mistake is the prawns they are a huge rip off. Unflavorful plain old cheap cocktail shrimp for 16 bucks is the ultimate rip off. Â  The fish and chips was also kind of a rip off as well , cause despite the nice quality of the fish it was just one little peice. My friends had the burger and the chicken & mushroom pie and those looked pretty good, but they weren't over joyed. Once again the beer here is delicious but food is just not worth it. Well except for the spiced nuts, i would definitely get those again.

Not sure if it was because it was during San Gennaro. But the entrees where not good. Veal cooked without care. Rigatoni was too soft and no sauce just meat. I did like there appetizer I do admit but the entrees not good.
Quincy T is right they are some racist bastards. Â but they're some racists who know how to make the best sandwiches in NYC.

This place is great for catching lunch on a busy day. The service is quick and the food is authentic. Not really a group restaurant, come here alone. My friend says it's akin to an American diner. I am still amazed by how different Spanish is in different countries. Next time I come I'll remember to ask for "habichuelas" not "frijoles"!

We ate at the Farm several times and quickly realized it was one of our absolute favorite restaurants in NYC. Â So when, suffused with Brooklyn pride, we decided to get married at the Picnic House in Prospect Park, there was really only one restaurant we seriously considered for the catering. Â We chose our menu, with the Farm folks helpfully suggesting combinations that would both work well together and fit within our budget, and awaited the day itself. In most cases, this review would now continue by telling you how well the Farm staff executed our agreed arrangement, i.e., off-site catering of our event. Â However, it turns out that our wedding was scheduled for Saturday, August 27, aka Hurricane Irene-pocalypse in New York City. Â As calls started trickling in on Friday with several friends and relatives cancelling last-minute, we thought, well, I guess we will just have a cozy, pre-storm gathering at the Picnic House and that will be that. Â And then the Picnic House called. Â As of 1pm Friday afternoon, we were told that we may have to end our wedding early, which seemed like a major inconvenience until 5pm, when they called to tell us the Park would be closed and the permit for our wedding would be cancelled. Â Then the truly furious last-minute wedding planning began. I spoke with Gary at the Farm many, many frantic (on my end) times that Friday night and Saturday morning and he and the whole staff at the Farm were truly amazing. Â First things first, Gary made some calls and, just as we were starting to convince ourselves that the 60 or so remaining guests would be able to deal with cramming into our 5th floor 1+ bedroom to watch the festivities and enjoy their lunch (presumably while standing?), he called to say that he would be able to shuffle things around so that we could have the ceremony and reception at the Farm itself. Â Crisis averted! Â  As if that weren't enough, when we arrived, fashionably late, on Saturday, the Farm crew had decorated with beautiful flowers (from the Farm's nearby sister establishment, a flower shop/bar called Sycamore) and arranged the restaurant in a way that was ideal for passed hors d'oeuvres, the ceremony, lunch, and, with just a couple of adjustments, dancing. Â Our guests gushed about the food, and I for one made sure I tried every dish--the duck rillette hors d'oeuvre, smoked pork shoulder, and grilled whole trout were especially memorable--all of which were, as expected, awesome. Â And the whole staff was very helpful and pleasant, despite the impending natural disaster and last-minute chaos. Â In fact, when we walked in, Gary was there to welcome us with Champagne and a relaxed smile. All in all, I think we would both say that the wedding ended up being much more what we had hoped it would be in the first place, before the guest list swelled uncontrollably--a fun, informal, intimate party with our families, good friends, and some seriously delicious food. Â Many, many thanks to the folks at the Farm for improvising so well and making that the case.

I can't believe I am just finding this place! My friend had her birthday dinner here and it was amazing. I had the homemade ricotta to start and it was so good, they should sell jars of it to go, I would buy it once a week. Â I ordered the chicken entree...it was the best chicken I have ever had. I got to taste a little bit of everyones entrees and I seriously can't say enough about this food, it's delicious. We were all very impressed. The cocktails were also very well done. The service was ok but the food was so good it deserves 5 stars. Â I'll be coming back soon!

Ate at Catfish this past Sunday for brunch. Â Their Bloody Mary was excellent. I had the catfish poboy. Â First of all the catfish was not fried and it was hard to tell it was catfish. Â The bread was hard too. The place itself was nice but the heavy metal music was so loud you couldn't even have a conversation.

Octopus salad was outstanding. I never knew octopus could so tender. Not much greens, so it's not a healthy option, but it's just plain delicious. Pappardelle with sweet sausage was also deeee lish. And the homemade focaccia bread was warm and oh so good. Prosciutto was also tasty, but when is it not. Plus I had pata negra the other day so I'm spoiled. Delivery was super fast and everything arrived fresh and warm.

SO disappointing! Â  This was my second visit. Â The first, though not memorable, was nice enough, and since it was in a convenient location for out of town guests, I thought a return visit would be Â fine; I honestly regret the choice! First of all, the service was poor. Â I had to take my father's coat at the table and seek out someone to check it. Â Our table was repeatedly interrupted mid-sentence for inane questions/comments from waitstaff. Â Two Â of our dishes were served to the wrong person at the table, which is unimpressive at a five-top. Â  In terms of the table, we were seated two on one side, three on the other. Â I couldn't hear or see one member of my party because of the table setup. Â The music was so loud that it inhibited conversation considerably-and I'm young (and love the velvet underground and the clash!). Â I don't know how the older members of the group managed at all. Â When we left, I heard that someone had asked that it be turned down a little; it was not. Secondly, the food was not up to standards for a restaurant of this type. Â I've been to other Colicchio restaurants, and there was clearly something wrong here in comparison. Â My baked ricotta was nicely flavored but inedibly hot, which left me way behind everyone and slowing down the pace of our meal. Â It was served with nothing to spread it on and also no spoon. Â An embarrassing amount ended up on the table since Â it was too flaky to be eaten with a fork. Â My biggest disappointment, though, was the quinoa "risotto." Â I was excited to try this hybrid of two of my favorite carby indulgences. Â Instead of the creamy dish I anticipated, I got a wet plate of one-note quinoa, like the last helping of a grain salad with too much dressing, or a bowl of brothy grain. Â I left lots on my plate, but no server asked if I was satisfied. Â Obviously, I skipped dessert--why waste the money or calories? Â People at my table enjoyed the pumpkin panna cotta, which they said was excellent, while I suffered through bitter and weak coffee. Tom, I expected better! Â I won't be back.

How does Ipudo not have FIVE stars? Â I'm ADDICTED! Â Every time I'm in NYC, I brave the lines and go for the Akamaru Modern...and the rice...with extra mayo...and pork...and dessert...OK, that's it...then bedtime for a few hours to sleep off the meal!
One of best food cart options in midtown. Â The hot sauce is good and really hot!

I organized a pre theatre get together upstairs at 3 Monkeys last night and it was terrific. Andrew, the GM, was extremely helpful in securing a corded off space for our group and with choosing the menu. The food was excellent, delivered promptly and hot. Everyone commented on how delicious it was. We used the upstairs bar and each of us paid for our own drinks which eliminated a complicated bar tab at the end. The noise level was high but that is because everyone was enjoying themselves! Would definitely go back with small group of Â friends or have another large gathering. It is nice to find a quality bar in that part of town with good service and delicious food.
Great place. Great booze. Great History. Check this place out if you're in the area! Also, they serve beer from the Porterhouse Brewing Company which were all excellent.

For a place with the word Stein and Hof in the name I'd expect a little more beer selection. Â There were only 5 beers on tap and the bartender knew little about them. Â The food may be pretty good here since the people eating appeared happier than the people drinking.

I haven't had a bad meal in a while, particularly because I am super-OCD about eating, but my dinner at Calle Ocho was quite possibly the worst meal I've had in the City in recent memory. From the sub-par gazpacho (heirloom tomato-based) to the taco tray, I was WAY under-whelmed. Â The gazpacho was bland and uneventful. The taco tray contained shredded dark meat chicken : (, tough and overcooked flank steak, and easily the most "fishy", yes "fishy", shrimp I have ever had. Look. The bacon wrapped dates were delicious, but so is bacon-wrapped anything. Â  Maybe I had a bad order, but should there be a "bad order" at a fairly popular restaurant in NYC? Â Drats. On the bright side, with better menu selections, it looks like it would be great for groups or a bite to eat after the Museum of Natural History.
Simple: If you love eating healthy and you're a rich ass mofo, you'll find this place acceptable. If you're poor, or if you don't mind eating Rafiqi's, you'll find this place unacceptable.

Just about everything about The Farm is excellent. Food, service, atmosphere ( love their outdoor space). We have enjoyed oh so many wonderful brunches here from the coffee to the omelettes to the seasoned fries, we are devotees. We always leave with the impression that we paid too little given the portion size and quality of the food. Service is always efficient and friendly.

first off, a large bowl of noodles is $5. second, they really hand pull those noodles right in front of you. it's like watching a free show and you know what you're about to eat is freshly made. third, it takes longer to pull the noodles than it is for them to cook and serve it with the beef tendons and soup. this means you will eat in less than 3 minutes of ordering your noodles. fourth, the broth is tasty and the noodles are al dente and flavorful. fifth, if you don't try this when you're in town, you would be missing out.

Only came here because of all the reviews, but man oh man yelpers, how you deceived me just this once. This place is terrible. Food is very mediocre. Very weird set-up. Â Tried the kimchi fried rice and it was horrendous. Only good thing was the chicken, but tasted like panda express. Last time I waste my money here. Avoid!
Smells, tastes, and looks like Italy. Â So you can excuse the service. Get the gnocchi and be happy. Prices are delicious too, so long as you have the green, not plastic variety.

I usually go to tapas restaurants with my female friends, because guys seem to always have the same reaction when they hear the word "small plate". Â I won't tell you everything I've heard, but I've responded with "no, I'm not punishing you", "no! I don't hate you!", and more recently, "no, you're not ordering Five Guys before we eat dinner". Â So I shouldn't have been surprised by my bf's reaction to my proclamation that I wanted to try a place that serves "small plates" - he answered "sure" with his mouth, but the ice cold grimace (or was it a snarl?) that formed after he walked away could probably rival that of a starving, angry pitbull, so I already knew I had a situation on my hands. But since I usually (always) get my way, Â I set out to Traif last night with bacon on my mind, a cynical man in tow, and a tinge of faith - on a mission to indulge and transform. Â As it happened, (in order of plate): Raspberry and Blueberry Salad with Cherry Tomatoes and Baby Spinach (Remarks that he's definitely still thinking he'll be hungry after dinner - but he offers a mostly continuous nod - a quiet but distinct form of approval. Says something quietly about the berries tasting fresh, but with sizable cynicism.) Sauteed Broccoli Rabe with Roasted Portobella Truffle Toast (Several understated but audible "mmm"'s; a lighthearted fork battle. Â He insists on drawing the "property line" in the center of the Texas Toast, and I notice he alots himself an extra 1/2 inch, at least.) Seared Foie with Fingerling Potatoes and Ham Chips (A wide eyed grin. Â Finally, a "wow" is heard coming from the other side of the table. Â Several offcolor statements made about the benefits of fattening ducks.) Bacon Wrapped Blue Cheese Stuffed Dates (The forks are gone. Â Hands are in, and the dates disappear within seconds. He scans the area to see if anyone has seen him lick the bacon fat off of his fingers. Restraint is present, but becoming elusive.) BBQ Braised short rib sliders with Sweet Potato Fries (The fries are smashing in and flying out of the mini tub of chipotle aioli. Â I feel a piece of short rib on my face. Before I can grab it, he picks it off my face and eats it. Â It becomes obvious that restaurant etiquette has officially taken a backseat, and he remarks at how surprised he is that he's actually...full.) Bacon Doughnuts with Dulce de Leche and Coffee Ice Cream. (It's over. Â After stating he was full from previous dishes, and after one bacon/ice cream double bite, he lunges. Â First at the donut, then the ice cream, cyclically. Silently agreeing with our eyes that this was not quite enough, one of us, I can't remember who - orders another plate.) Upon leaving Traif after dinner, I believe I saw him wave goodbye to the little pig on the door of the restaurant and saying "See ya soon!" Mission accomplished.

i am a Southern Girl. I have eaten & made ALOT of biscuits in my lifetime . The biscuit I had at Sunday Brunch at The Spotted Pig not only brought Â tears to my eyes but MADE me tip the guy who made the biscuits $20. Â Did I mention I am USUALLY Â a cheap Southern girl? Damn that was the best biscuit I have EVER had! Very nice staff( unlike Bar Pitti the night before ). Go here ! Get a biscuit!

Just had a wonderdul dinner at Bouley. The food is spectacular. The prix fixe is a great value. The restaurant itself is beautifully decorated, with wonderful soft lighting. Â I would definitely recommend Bouley to others with confidence.
Super Essen!!! Selbstgemacht Nudeln. Gnocchi sind mehr als nur empfehlenswert. Nachspeise Coconut Pudding ebenfalls sensationell. Mmmmmmmh.

Not sure if the owner in this establishment was the one from the older Wonton Garden restaurant that is on Mott... Someone told me they're the same staff from the Mott one and they've moved onto this location and renamed themselves to HK Wonton Garden. Anyway, love their wonton noodle soups! I prefer the noodles and soup here but I could tell you that even though they don't include an entire shrimp in their wontons like they do over on Mott they're still very good. Will return for their other noodles!

We had just gotten in on the red eye and were looking for something to do that would keep us awake. Â We decided to take a suggestion from a friend and walk the Brooklyn bridge and then go to Grimaldi's for some pizza. Â As we approached, we saw the line. Â Is that line for the pizza place? Â Really? Â Tired and a slight bit dejected we decided to wait it out. Â Boy am I glad we did. Â Easily in my top three best pizza joints that I have experienced. Â I am drawing a blank on the other two right now. Â  If you are going to New York, do yourself a favor, walk the Brooklyn Bridge and wait in that line for some Grimaldi's pizza. Â Absolutely incredible.

Very cheap! $1 dumplings! Filling, fast service and cheap, there is nothing you can complain about! Best dumplings ever. This is a must go! This place used to be a small spot but they renovated and moved next door to a bigger store! AMAZING dumplings and pork sesame buns. i love it! Service is great too!

Been to both the LES and Astoria locations, and experience-wise, Astoria's is way better (not that service is bad in the LES one, just that I liked this crowd a bit better). I highly recommend their crab meat covered shrimp. They are beyond delicious and sure to fill you up. I had them with both Horta and the potato fries, and lets say that the potato fries were the crowd's favorite. Also, their calamari appetizer is great.

We waited in line for some time, before being seated. Which I thought was a good sign. I looked up the reviews prior to being seated and thought this place has to be great. Once assigned a table and getting ready to be seated, we were asked immediately what kind of dumplings we wanted to order - even before drinks. I thought, another good sign. Everyone that comes here MUST get the dumplings. Between the 8 of us, we ordered 2 regular pork and 2 pork with crab meat. They came out in a flash. Once I bit into my first dumpling, I knew this wasn't the place. The filling was extremely salty and not that flavorful. I was uber-ly disappointed. Thank goodness the dumplings were such a good deal. Also ordered was... Shrimp Pan Fried Noodles Twice Cooked Pork General Tso's Chicken Salt & Pepper Calamari Mushrooms & Bamboo Shoots I personally am not a fan of the General Tso's Chicken, so I didn't sample it but it was gobbled right up. The Twice Cooked Pork was decent. A little peppery which was good. The Shrimp Pan Fried Noodle and Mushooms with Bamboo Shoots were drenched in thick sauce that covered up all and any natural flavors anything had to offer. It was sad. Additionally, the mushrooms were not fresh and nor was the Shrimp. I felt like everything had a generic standard sauce out of the bottle taste, and felt it was not worth the wait in the long line. I looked around, and then saw the entire restaurant were Americans. *sigh* When I return to this fantastic city that never sleeps, I will be sure to check out more of Chinatown to find the real hidden gems. Because this place is super overrated and not worth it at all. One good thing, is they have reasonable prices on some of the dishes. Another bad thing, is they only accept cash so be prepared.

A friend was moving out of NYC, and organized a brunch here. Â You are greeted warmly by the staff, which makes you feel immediately welcome in a room with lovely decor. Â Given the size of the group, they did not make us wait until everyone arrived to seat us (which was good, since a few people showed up almost 45 minutes after the start time!) I decided to indulge my curiosity and ordered the frittata, which was prepared with ramps, asparagus, pecorino cheese, served with mixed greens and grilled bread (which I barely touched, because of the shared bread baskets served beforehand). Â It was a perfectly balanced medley of vegetables, and the eggs were light and fluffy. Â  Our guest of honor asked for the maple bacon sticky buns, which were, as she called them, "diabetes on a plate." Â The bacon garnish was just enough to add savory flavor to the sweetness of the maple syrup, and the buns were so rich that you only needed two bites to fully experience it. Â  They have a great cocktail menu - I tried a couple (couldn't remember the names - yeah, they were that good), but one had bourbon (chose that one in honor of the Preakness Stakes going on that day). Â  What's cool about their website is that they have tags on their ingredients which allow you to view where the ingredients are from.

Queens Comfort sucks. Â It doesn't take a genius make food moderately tasty if it's fried and slathered in butter and fat - which is pretty much how I would describe every single thing on their menu. Â For the love of God, please offer at least ONE option that doesn't end up making you feel sick, filled with regret, and take you one step closer to diabetes. Â  The crappy, unfriendly service and overly-pretentious hipster vibe don't help their cause either.

A lot of selections, great prices. They've expanded and added more seating as well as a warm buffet styled Bon Chon area. Food is mediocre but for the convenience and feeding your cravings I say stop on in!!!

This place is so tiny! Good thing I planned to order take out and bring it to Washington Square park to eat. Â There was only one guy working during dinner time on a Thursday night. Â I felt bad since we had so many orders! Â  Food was awesome. Â I'm really grateful to have a place where it's cheap and delicious. Â I was a little bit thrown off though because I wanted to share a double, but they don't give you more meat just more rice. Â I wasn't aware that you can buy a pork cutlet as a topping as opposed to buying another meal for that 2nd piece of meat! Â Just a FYI for others who wants to share one of those dishes!

Can't believe I've never been here before! The food was fantastic. My fiance had the original burger, and I had the short ribs (comes with mac and cheese and these amazing buttery brussel sprouts). Everything was juicy and delicious and flavorful -- we scraped the plates clean. It's a bit overpriced, so I won't be coming here often, but definitely as a nice treat. Would like to try the beer and the dessert, Â which we passed on this time.

Went out to dinner here last night with some friends. Reasons I liked this place: -Bread served was excellent and paired well with the delicious olives. -House red wine was amazing; reminded me of when I was back in Rome this past semester. -The atmosphere also reminded me of the beautiful rustic nature of the restaurants that line the streets of Trastevere in Rome (perhaps even more physically appealing than the ones there). -The waitress was extremely pleasant and helpful and the man in charged of refilling our waters was very prompt. Great service! Reasons I didn't like the place: -I knew when I ordered the squid ink tagliolini it would either be a hit or a miss. I was expecting it to have a very unique flavor, but the pasta itself was bland. The dish could have used more salt to bring out the flavors of the white wine sauce and the pasta itself. While the portion was helpful, it just was not a satisfying or tasty meal. I would definitely give Da Andrea another shot because of the service, wine, and bread alone. That sounds odd but when the atmosphere is so inviting I am more than willing to try again! Just stay away from the squid ink!

you can't blame the guys at this fry bar for being a bit short with their customers; lines are out the door and they don't get a chance to breathe. that being said, i was a bit disappointed with the service at my last visit. you can't win 'em all. part two of our mini food tour- got the regular with frites sauce (free btw) and mango chutney. always mango chutney people, make the right choice. we also tried their new figs & sage, that was delicious. sat in the chairs outside in the post-winter chill and pigged out. the tiny crispy bits are my favorite, yes the ones probably laden with oil and grease but whatever they're the best. standard fries fix in the city.

A family member of mine worked here previously and always raved about the place, with an open invitation to stop by. Finally I did, and have since been back on a few occasions. I always start with a Mac Attack, last time we ordered Fish tacos as well. Excellent! They were a little 'fishy-er' than I like but great nonetheless. For entrees I have had chicken and waffles, as well as various burgers and truffle fries, and the Calamari salad. All of these were great each time I have gone. The nights when its crowded are the most annoying. Everyone is too important for their own good which can be slightly bothering when all you want to do is get a table and eat. Late nights are my fave because its less crowded which is a plus because the seating is very close together so the less people the better. Weekends can get a little ratchet as far as the crowd is concerned. Desserts consist of (for me) deep fried oreos, one word; YUM! Vanilla milkshakes are particularly creamy and have a very smooth taste. The red velvet yodels are also a winner. Drinks wise, I tend to play it safe: blackberry lemonade, wild berry mojitos, and as a one time treat, an espresso martini. I have yet to be disappointed by this place!

A little too fancy for my liking, but the food was still good. Came for restaurant week with a group of girls, which worked out perfectly. We were able to try all the appetizers on the menu. We started the meal with a tasting of rose and it was literally a tasting. Most of the items listed were delicious, and it really started the meal out right. For the main dish, I had the cod and it was so good. Cooked perfectly and while it was a small piece, it was delicious. My friend paid the $9 for the lamb chops and while it was good, it definitely wasn't worth it. Stick to the menu, don't get anything with a supplemental fee. For dessert, we had one of everything on the menu and I liked the cheesecake the best. The candy bar was a little too chocolatey for me and the clotted cream tasted like soap. Not exactly my kind of dessert, but the cheesecake was the best of the three. The waitress was good, but she seemed a little snotty. She knew we were here for restaurant week and while she answered our questions, she seemed to have this attitude where she was just doing her job, but didn't think we were good enough to be at the restaurant. A little slow with a few things, but she got the job done. While the food was good and the restaurant looked amazing, I don't think I'd come back. The portions were a little small and for tapas it was extremely pricey. Just not my type of food, but it was definitely worth giving it a shot.
The food was fine but pricier than expected and the waiter was a little bit pushy on upselling our party. I've had better bibimbap, basically.

This was round two of my friend date for shabu shabu. Shabu Tatsu was much more fun and a better experience than Momokawa because the hot water was in the table and not on the side. The food isn't of as good a quality as Momokawa but it was more bang for your buck. Apparently the lines get really long here but we were not busy when we got there. When we left, there was a ton of people waiting outside. I would come back, it was tasty.

This was one of the best meals I've had in NYC in a long time - which is saying something, given that I love to eat out, and at nice places - and from such a chill, unassuming, and not break-the-bank expensive place! Service was delightful and attentive, and the food was spectacular. Loved how the chef paid homage to the seasons and to things like well-sourced meat but without turning it into one of those irritatingly precious Farm-to-Table situations. New York has great food, but rarely have I had a meal where everything we had hit the mark perfectly. My favorites were the squash salad (sleeper hit of the menu!), the corn agnolotti, and the grown-up ice cream sandwich. Seriously, go to this place. You'll be able to say you were there back when it was possible to get a table...

As good as a wine bar can get. We were seated at the wine bar's new extension by Chef Mehta himself. The service was excellent and the food phenomenal. Graffiti offers small plates but boy did we wish they were bigger! My girlfriend and I ended up ordering the whole menu and dessert. Everything was sooo delicately delicious. The wine selection is great and surprising affordable too. I will definitely be returning to this little spot.

The Ramen was phenomenal. I went for lunch and they offer a lunch special where you get 2 courses, or it could of been 3. It offered a starter, salad, and ramen. If in N.Y.C. do try. It's wait the wait.
yummy tapas and beautiful place. I was there 7-8 months ago so I don't remember the details of what I had I just remember we ordered a lot and everything was good ....

How could this little gem have flown under my radar all these years? Â I dipped in here last night to have a drink or two at the bar with my good friend, and we ended up having dinner in the dining room, which by the way, is cleverly nestled in the back, intimate, and cozy. Â  Everyone from the host Nora, to our bartender Joseph, to our handsome waiter Artan, was ridiculously friendly! Â And the food was great! Â For appetizers I ordered the Pa Amb Oli, Spanish bread with olive oil, garlic, and salt, and my friend ordered the sauteed shrimp with wild mushrooms. Â She kept going on about how good the broth was lol. Â But I was too distracted with my own Atlantic cod with mussels which also came in a well seasoned broth. Â Artan did a great job juggling our table along with several others, and of course he invited us back again, so I would be rude to not take him up on that! lol All in all, great experience, met some great people at the bar, and Salinas will be on my list of regular spots from now on. Â Love the atmosphere!

Best local Brazilian spot. Fish fritters and lentil salad were a great way to start your meal. Caipirinhas are great ! Felt like I was in Ipanema. Best duck I've had in a while, definitely recommend it. Â Carne guisada was also a hit. Â Didn't try desert, awesome spot , will go back for sure.
I came here on a weekday night and only had a short wait. Â The grilled fish was fresh and perfectly seasoned, and the oysters are briny and flavorful. Â Will definitely be back.

Great spot for Brisket and Pulled Pork. Â This place is no secret so the line can get fairly long. Â My friend and I will come here on off days or at off times and there can still be a fairly long line. Â But they have a pretty solid beer and whiskey menu to enjoy while you wait. The Brisket and Pulled Pork are amazing. Â The sausage is good but not great. Â The spareribs were very tasty but the ones that I've tried haven't been loaded with meat. Â It's fun to load up and try the various meats but it can and will get expensive. My only real complaint lies in the sides. Â The beans are good but they're over $5 for a small order. Â There's no starch side like mashed or baked potatoes. Â There is a potato salad option but I am not a fan of potato salad. I try to get here every few months and thoroughly enjoy it when I do despite the small complaints. Â If you have yet to try Fette Sau, go try it.

One of the best places I've been to in a long time. The wait can be long at times, especially since there are no reservations but well worth it. The Sheppard's Pie was absolutely amazing as well as the Kale salad. The dining room has an excellent atmosphere and its the perfect place to bring a date for wine and some great food

Nothing's better then moving to a new neighborhood and trying all the local spots. Â Well, I guess finding a gem amongst the local spots would be better -- and Beyoglu happens to be one of them! Â Only a block away, I have probably eaten here at least once a week since having moved to the Upper East Side about two months ago. Â The prices are perfect relative to portion-size and a steal relative to quality and taste! Â I will say that their hummus is top notch (probably some of the best I've had in a long time) - very fresh - and the bread that comes with....simply to die for! Â It's inexplicably good!! Â Other menu highlights include their signature chicken, spinach pie/pastry appetizer, and their baklava (amazing if you're a pistachio/baklava fan). Â What's more, the great service! Moreover, Beyoglu makes for a great date spot as well as catch-up-with-friends place. Â The outdoor seating is a nice bonus on a lovely day or beautiful evening. Â I will most definitely be coming back here, the question is, how often!!

I stopped in here for a pre-shopping brunch with a friend one Sunday after discovering a 45-minute wait at Balthazar. Â Soon after we entered we realized that they weren't open yet despite the door being wide open. Â The hostess was very welcoming though, and told us to wait one minute as she checked to see if the cooks were ready for service anyway, which they were. (Major brownie points!) Â  I ordered the classic Eggs Benedict, which came with a side of roasted potatoes. Â Everything was savory and delicious, and the English muffin had a nice, almost chewy texture--not soggy like with some Benedicts. Â To round out my $15 pre-fixe brunch with cocktail included, I ordered a prosecco drink with pear/apple puree. Â It was refreshing and crisp, although it wasn't brought to me until I was nearly done with my meal. Â I'll accept this small service snafu, since they did start serving us before the restaurant was even open. Â I almost forgot, the bread they brought before the meal was SO delicious, I had to stop myself from eating the entire basket so I would have room for my eggs. The decor is very rustic European, and the atmosphere is pleasant and inviting. Â I would love to come back for dinner sometime.

My burger head friend proclaimed Mark "the best burger ever" one day, which is a bold statement. I'm not going to go THAT far, but yes, these are some tasty sliders. The sliders come in regular and bacon; I tried one of each, which was sufficiently filling as a snack or light meal. The bacon was the bomb; much more flavorful than the original, with gooey, almost liquid cheese. I tried the legendary Guinness Shake, too. Not bad, with a hint of Guinness flavor, but not necessarily something I would feel compelled to order again. Â Good stuff and cheap, too.

After years of waiting and unbelievable patience, I have finally had the chance to eat at David Chang's Ssam Bar. We came early for lunch to make sure we had seats and even then, there were people already inside dining on buns and even the Bo Ssam itself! We sat at the bar and were greeted kindly by the waiter & waitress; We were waited to often so we did not run out of water and had plates cleared when finished. I wanted to try a variety of Chang's creations so we got a couple of dishes. First, the Steamed Pork Buns were freaking delicious as they were publicized; Though I still prefer Ippudo's Hirata Pork Buns, these were pretty good. The Duck Bologna Sandwich was surprisingly good considering the lack of interest I have in bologna, probably the best thing I had here. Lastly, we got the Duck Rotisserie Set which came with fingerling potatoes and a variety of sauces; It was very fun eating it, making the lettuce wraps and just being hands on makes it an experience. The complete meal was outstanding and its a sure thing I will be back despite the outrageous prices!

We ordered delivery tonight of two Picnic Plate (spare ribs, fried chicken, grilled corn and a biscuit) and...It. Was. Great. Where to start? The biscuit was first on my radar and before I added any butter to it, I saw that it was already prepped with butter and sweetness (maybe honey or maple). The fried chicken was perfectly cooked, neither dry nor underdone, with a crispy breading that had a touch of maple. My guy says it was some of the best he ever had: "Excellent". He was expecting KFC style and this was entirely different and of course much better. People may be used to processed fried chicken like the Colonel's, but the real thing is a treat. The spare ribs were crispy on the outside and moist on the inside, as they should be. A smoky mouthful of delight. The grilled corn was a bit petite (ahem) but flavorful and had a kick (Tabasco butter perhaps). Service on the phone was courteous and helpful, and delivery only took about 20 minutes tops and the food was piping hot. We can't wait to go in and have brunch soon. This place is an awesome find.

I found the South East Asian specialties here less appetizing then a place like Chinatown's New Malaysia. Some of them even tasted like they were prepared from the 3-in-1 instant dish mix packets you find in an Asian grocery. However they do posses gems like the Stingray in banana leaf. It is a bony large fish covered in a pungent spicy paste. My wife is European and is pretty uninitiated with South East Asian aromatics like shrimp paste, bird's eye chili and lemongrass. I was afraid she would be repulsed by the Stingray but despite the spice level she trooped on and raved over its deliciousness. So yeah, the dishes are mostly satisfactory but the Stingray is excellent.
I love their dumpling and spring roll. But Â there is one thing that i dont like about the place is that you have to share table with people that you dont know.

Ok, so that decides it, I need to move to New York and spend lots of time at Ellary's Greens. Â  EG is a newer spot in the West Village where the focus is on healthy food. Â As their posted mission more or less states, "We won't feed you anything we wouldn't serve our kids." There are plenty of healthy places sprouting up (oops!) all over the city these days. Â What sets Ellary's apart is that while much of its offerings are vegetarian or vegan, there are some meat options. Â What's great about that is that the meat eaters don't feel like they're being dragged to a hippy dippy vegan place and the vegans aren't going to meat palace. Â It's somewhere everyone can be happy. Â That sounds like a good goal. Â Strive to be healthy and allow for a balance of choices if that's your thing. Before I get to the food, I have to say that the place is beautiful! Â They totally redid the space, power blasting the walls to expose the brick and laying down new floors. Â Below the ceiling is a a layer with a leaf cutout motif that softens the lighting while supporting the green theme. Â It's a very comfortable and inviting space. Â I first stopped in after eating down the street. Â We were full, but we had to see what was happening in this beautiful space. Â We were warmly welcomed, just as I have been on my two recent visits. Ok, so now for the main event, the food. Â I went for breakfast and had the tofu scramble. Â It was seasoned with chipotle and served in a gluten-free wrap. It was quite tasty and not too filling. Â That left room for a good-sized serving of fresh fruit, which was nicely presented. At dinner, I had the red quinoa salad, which included kale and was quite filling and delicious. Â Even yummier was the while bean soup. Â It was so good I had to ask if it really was vegan. I was almost sure there was cream in it. Â There wasn't. Â The folks at Elllary's are Â excellent at turning healthy ingredients into outstanding dishes. Â Another example was the chocolate mousse. Â If you only order one thing here, get the mousse. Â It's that good! Â It's creamy and rich and guess what? Â  There's no dairy in it. Â Instead it's made from fresh avocados (really!), cacoa, and a tiny bit of coffee. Â The cream on top is made from coconut milk with a bit of banana. Wait, how do I know all this? Â Well, the owner, Leith, told me all about it before I left. Â She is so excited about the food that you want to rush back and try new things. Â Vegan wine? Â Ok! Â Coconut breakfast bar? Â Sure. Â Obviously, this is a labor of love! Â Speaking of love, once Leith had excitedly shared all that Ellary's has to offer, she gave me a big hug. Â A hug from a restaurant owner in New York City? Â Yup, for real! Â  Hope to see you there soon!
I imagine this is what going to the cafeteria in a wealthy Korean high school would be like. Â Plus booze.
clean, delicious and quick what more can you ask

If you are all about the slow food movement and enjoy under-spiced thai food come here. Â otherwise, i suggest move on to one of the many other thai restaurants in nyc where the service is faster, the food is more flavorful, and where the bill won't make you jaw drop open. Â  on the plus side, the place is very beautiful, very hip, and the waiters are lovely. Â therefore, if you prefer ambiance over Â eating - pinto is the place to be

Fools! Â People are swooning over the "Sunset Menu", while their Prix Fix lunch is unbeatable. Â For $8, you get a salad, a choice of appetizer, and a main dish. Â There is a wide variety of possibilities, but I went ahead and got the salad,fries with spicy mayo, and the red curry. Â  Also, I ordered their signature Iced Tea for $4, which is a little expensive, but well worth it. We went for lunch on a Saturday, and the place was virtually empty, but started to get busy while we were dining. The Iced Tea was awesome. Â It comes with these 2 cubes of frozen tea, and you add milk and tea yourself. Â Although I am sure you can get creative and mess with the proportions to get cool combinations and adjust to taste, I poured in all of the milk, all of the tea, and all of the simple syrup. Â It was delicious, although a little small. Â The tap water was continuously refilled, however. Â The glasses for the water were tall and skinny, so they ran out pretty quickly, but the well-dressed waiter came by and replenished it from a really cool pitcher every few minutes. The salad was meh. Â Not enough dressing, not enough flavor. Â Saladful, I guess.Also came in a cool plate. The fries, however, were awesome! Â Perfectly crispy, they were more home fries than anything else, chiefly because they were cubed, the way home fries usually are. Â Fried to a crisp and well seasoned, they went very well with the dipping sauce. The Curry was phenomenal. Â Don't get me wrong, it was not as spicy as I would have liked, and the portion size was not great, but it tasted divine. Â Just enough bamboo shoots and other vegetables. Â Also, the rice went perfectly with it, and the chicken was perfectly succulent (I believe in the description it said it was free-range), and the vegetables fresh. I guess I would have to say that this is the place Spice is trying to be. Â Stylish in decor, silverware, and wait staff, it is still well priced and delicious. Â Great neighborhood, it really has the feel of eating at a small, exclusive restaurant, without being overly pompous. Â No, they do not give you a vat of Curry like they do at Spice, but the service is exponentially better, the prices are the same, and the food tastes better. Â There are minor faults, but the strengths more than make up for them.

It's fine! I've been a few times now for breakfast and lunch. The portions are substantial and relatively inexpensive and the food is always good- they didn't lie when they named it "Bushwick's Living Room". It's pretty comfortable, and no one minds if you hang for a while. I've had the Cobb Salad, an egg breakfast, and also tried a side of sauteed mushrooms- everything was exactly how I wanted it to be. Â Drinks are cheap, coffee hot and the space well-decorated and warm. It's a very welcoming place, especially in the winter.

I went to Artichoke for the first time last night and had some of the best pizza I've had in NYC. I split slices of artichoke, sicilian, and margarita with one of my friends. I loved them all, but especially the sicilian (the artichoke was delicious but I don't think I could finish a whole slice since it is so heavy...). Â I just wish there were some place to sit....even so, I'll definitely be coming back. Mm pizzaaa
Great value for the money! French toast was excellent and the eggs benedict were very good. Mimosa was great! Service was very good and the atmosphere was just like Paris. Would come again!
