Ordered take out from here. Â Food is fairly decent priced, but tastes was mediocre. It wasn't bad, but it just wasn't great. Â I'd expect the meat to be the items that got my attention, but it was actually the rice and an egg custard item that I really enjoyed.

this place is hard to miss on 53rd and 6th. The line basically covers the block. the particular we went, they were giving free food because some of their former employees have started a food cart right next to them. The same colors, same name, and the same logo. for justice sake, i wanted to support them. regardless of what happened between the other guys and these guys, i don't think that is the right way to find justice. their white sauce is amazing, but what is great is the hot sauce. do'nt be fooled by the little container...one is plenty enough for the entire thing. my date and i were under the impression tat we were boh getting free meals but they served one for free and charged the other. we were excited to get free food and were a little disappointed but we got half of our meal for free. :D

Hmmm waffles with strawberries and whipped cream. Â Need I say more? Â Okay I will. Â Great prices for the quality and quantity of food. Sit outside because the inside can get loud especially with the kids.

The food here is amazing. We ordered the mini meatballs for appetizer and had the caprese salad and fettuccine for entrees. Everything was so fresh and delicious. However, this place loses one star for extremely slow service.

Love the xiao lung bao here, but i really hate how cramped it gets because tons of tourists come here. It is good but i think it can be overrated at times and it has become more of a tourist place, so although I do like the food, I prefer having my own space and not cramped with tons of other people.

Everything is delicious, local, and fresh. Last night we had chorizo and fava bean pasta, seared cod and mushroom risotto. They were all great. Then we topped it off with chocolate hazelnut pudding. Amazing. Great for brunch and an early dinner.

BYOB places in the city are rare gems, so that's already 5 stars in my book. We came for a girl date to celebrate the arrival of my friend's wine that she had ordered when she was in Napa. So BYOB was clearly appropriate. I had the Spicy Citrus Marinated Shrimp while my friend had the Pan-Seared Atlantic Salmon and we also shared a side order of rosemary fries. We both really enjoyed our food and the fries are as good as they say they are! My shrimp dish came with a little mound of couscous and spinach in the center with alternating shrimp and lemon wedges surrounding it. Definitely visually appealing. Our waiter and I believe also owner, was super friendly and accommodating, until the end of our meal. I guess my friend and I were taking a tad bit too long on a Friday night to finish our bottle of wine, so he told us that we had to leave as he needed the table. I'm pretty understanding of this, as the restaurant is legit like a hole in the wall, but it would have been a better experience had he not rushed us out.

My Japanese friend told me about this place. So one day, when I was around the area, I decided to try their ramen. I was skeptical at first, because I saw that their ramen is similar to Momofuku's.. they both have pork slices, but after tasting their freshly made ramen, it changed my perspective. [I ordered the Akamaru Modern.] Not only was the ramen good, their soup was good too. I didn't have to feel guilty for leaving some of the soup behind. Their pork buns were also delicious. It had some pizazz, they put some spicy sauce that brings out the flavor. For the $13 ramen and $3 for an extra rice ball (lunch special), it was filling. Definitely a place to try.
Love this place. Drinks - strong and delicious Wings - spicy, yummy, sauce is perfect The food is excellent, the service is great, and I can't wait to return.

Food is really good but the prices are a bit high. They also haven't done much to reinvent themselves. This place got so many accolades in the past for being such a fantastic restuarant but I feel like Astoria's restaurant district has grown so much since then and they definetely have more competition if they want to be number one. The place is also super dark and there isn't ample waiting area in the front entrance. it's definetly worth trying out.

Having worked in FiDi for almost a decade now, I never actually realized that there were no options for good food, or even real food. Upon being introduced to Chopping Block, I had only wished that they had moved here sooner. Their sandwiches are delicious, unique, fresh, and organic. Best of all, their prices aren't high and is generally cheaper than most restaurants around here that offer crappy food. We have been ordering from Chopping Block for months until they closed down for renovation. We hear that they are reopening this month and are very excited to be able to eat their sandwiches again.

Wow. I was blown away by Degustation! The food was more than delicious and was definitely different than anything I had ever tried. As a good tasting menu should, there were about two dishes that were a bit strange, but still fun to eat. The bread and goat milk butter is to die for, as well as the croquette. Definitely a great place to go for a new and delicious food experience.

Tiny hole in the wall spot with a nice casual ambience. Â There's only about 5 or 6 small tables, so I wouldn't come here with more than 4 people. Â It's BYOB, so hit the liquor store right down the street before you go. Veg dumpling was good, liked it better than the Thai fresh roll which was a little bland. Â Both have a nice sweet dipping sauce. Original Thai Basil dish has a kick to it, pretty spicy. Â Massaman Curry was pretty standard, very rich sauce. Â Drunk Man Noodle was my favorite, definitely go for a noodle dish here! Bottom line - welcome addition to the neighborhood, good for small groups.

For the last three years, I've made a point to stop into Il Bambino every time I've visited Astoria. The cheese, charcuterie, paninis, crostinis and PEANUT BUTTER HOT CHOCOLATE entice me to the point where I experience a mega does of choice anxiety when it comes time to order. I've eaten at Il Bambino at least half a dozen times, and the service is always friendly and impeccable to the point where I find myself WAY overtipping and loving it. If I don't spring for the stinky, savory proscuitto, gorgonzola & fig panini, I find myself opting for several smaller crostinis. The goat cheese, honey and rosemary oil selection is always a favorite, and the recently discovered avocado butter, chorizo and chili oil crostini makes me nearly weep with joy. Creamy, salty, otherwordly delight. Taking a nutella or peanut butter hot chocolate to go is a near-perfect way to end lunch at my affectionately titled Bambinis. Altogether fresh, fabulous and a must-eat for out of towners.

One of my favorite people watching spots. Everyone from tourists to the very eclectic can be found here. The seating is not very spacious or comfortable, but it's the price you pay to enjoy a meal in true NYC style. The steak frites is my favorite on the menu.
Best Artichoke pizza in town I come from the bronx downtown to 14th street to get this pizza and they never disappoint

Stopped in on a whim one day after walking by on the way to Macy's. Â Honestly, I wasn't expecting much given the prices, but I was unexpectedly blown away. Â 10 of the best and freshest boiled dumplings I have ever had for 3 bucks. Â Such a good find in the neighborhood.

So upsetting when a great place goes down hill. I raved about their brunch & decided to finally come back after 2 years. What a huge let down. My eggs florentine was not good. The eggs came out cold & spinach minimal atop a soggy English muffin. We ordered potato pancakes to try, total bust! We didn't even eat 1 & waiter couldn't care less, didn't even ask if anything was wrong. The French toast was good but not great. Skip this hole in the wall & make a reservation to Norma's.

Really Good. Awesomeness. Meat station is outstanding and cheap! Food is always delicious and fresh at the buffet. They rotate and replenish the buffet pretty often. It's a small but efficient little cafe. I always walk out happy from here!

I have been here more times than I can count. I bring my family, friends (from Paris) and even had a party here. Â The food is great, the service excellent. Â It is the only restaurant worth going to on the Windsor Terrace strip.
Great food, in a fun casual, atmosphere. Don't go in thinking of it as restaurant, think of it as a catered picnic with your family and friends.

By far one of my most favorite restaurants in NYC. The brick walls and wooden floors along with the open space make this a typical restaurant around America rather than another place in New York where everything is cramped. We had the: Chicken Liver Toast - very delicious and crispy bread. Cured Meats and Local Cheeses - who doesn't like Prosciutto and cheese? Marinated Olives - I'm not a usual olive fan but I liked these. Pretzel Dusted Calimari - You can tell these are a step above any other calimari you've ever tasted Mushroom, parmesan, oregano, and farm egg pizza - the farm egg just made the pizza. One of my favorite dishes of the night Roast suckling pig - the skin was crispy and the meat was very moist Turkey (Thanksgiving Special) - What's there not to like about Turkey and brussel sprouts with stuffing and mashed potatoes? We ended the night with - Warm Donuts - decent Sorbets - tangy and fresh We also had 2 bottles of red wine. All of this food came out to be around $80 per person for a table for 4. That isn't too bad if you go to other places in New York. Overall, the food was excellent, however, the desserts were subpar. I would recommend going to this restaurant over most New York places.
The wait time is kind of ridiculous but very tasty food and lively and fun atmosphere. My rating system out of 20: Taste: 7/10 Presentation: 3/5 Creativity: 4/5 Total 14/20
I ordered from here via grubhub and the food was great! I love indian food especially when it is done right!

Food was tasty, especially the pork tamale and the talapia special. The seasoning was good, but very salty... I was chugging water by the end if the meal. The "tapas" are actually huge, entree sized portions and we ended up ordering way too much food. I feel like our waitress could have given us a heads up about that.

Probably my favorite bar in Brooklyn. I've been going to this bar since it opened and the beers have only gotten better. The atmosphere is great and the people are super nice. When they first open they didn't have food, but once they did, the food is amazing. I would recommend the Burger or the BLT if they have it.

So new york pizza, eh?? dont get me wrong, it was pretty freakin awesome...but its just pizza, maybe cuz im from san diego, and just do get it...but its pizza..at least i can say i tried it, i had a huge smile when i had my first bite, but after a couple of minutes, i was over it.
Amazing penne vodka.

If you like butter, this is your place. If you like bacon, Traif is it. This reasonably priced southern French crepes were buttercentricly delicious! Shrimp curry crÃªpe and mussel and spinach crÃªpes were very nice. The curry crÃªpe had just a hint of curry flavor and didn't overpowered a well balanced crÃªpe. The not so fresh mussels weren covered with butter and made good. Unsuccessful crÃªpes that night was Savoyarde (potatoes, camembert, bacon and onion), camembert wasn't well melted yet and felt too greasy with cheese and butter. I would like to have a just a slash of lemon juice over it to cut the greasiness to enhanced the crepe but if you can drink alcohol, those dishes would wonderfully work with a glass of rich red wine. Â  What I loved the most was Socca (chickpeas pancake) from the appetizer. We had a plate of different appetizers (Provencale Plate) and Socca shined the most, a touch of salt on it was very nice. It was like a pancake comes with Malaysian Roti Canai. Next was Pissaladiere, finger cut small pizza were not like typical pizza but Foccacia with topping with a sweet onion and anchovies. Least favorite was black olive tapenade. It was too salty but worked well with a garlic toast that came with. For non-drinker table like ours, everything was way too heavy or some too salty and we could not go for yummy looking dessert crÃªpes after. I must come back just for dessert crÃªpe soon!

The brisket in this place is AMAZING. I'm hard to convince with food (especially brisket), but this place caught me off guard. Their brisket is unique, only when you eat it and compare it to any other brisket you will understand what I mean. I have eaten here several times and I thought that it was about time to let others know. I would suggest more side dishes. Although the ones they have taste good. The employees are friendly and the place is clean. I hope this place does not change.

This place would've gotten 4 stars from me since they do have great oysters and entrees. Â BUT... My friends & I went here for a bday dinner. Â We got there at around 5:30 and decided to hang around the bar for a bit while we waited for 2 other people in our party to come. Â There was 5 of us and only 3 seats available at the crowded bar. Â Myself and my other girlfriend decided to stand behind our friends while we waited for our drinks. Â The hostess came charging down the aisle between the seats and bar and said w/ such attitude "OK, you ladies can't block the aisle like this because there's no way for me to go back and forth!" Â I was so shocked to receive such abrasive attitude from this hostess...has she not seen how other bar areas function in the city? Â It would've been totally fine had she said politely for us to move aside! Â Anyway, not wanting to make a big stink out of it, my friend and I decided to just wait outside. Â Little did we know that at around 7-8PM, the bar was even more packed and more people crowded the precious aisle way but the hostess didn't say one word to any of those people (and I witnessed this bc our table was next to the bar!). Â  Later on in the night, when we all received our orders, our one friend still had not gotten her meal...and we were all almost half way done w/ our meals! Â I flagged our waiter down and asked him what's up. Â He told us that the kitchen accidentally thought she ordered the tuna burger - instead of the tuna steak. Â I suspect had I not asked him where her meal was...he would have never came over to explain to us where her meal was!!! Â Hence we waited another few minutes for her order to finally arrive! Â  Then again when we ordered our dessert, it took a good 15 - 20 minutes to get 2 orders of banana pudding and fried ice cream out to us. Â By that time, we were ready to just get the check and leave but the waiter assured us it'll only be a few more minutes (it did come shortly after he said that). Â  Anyway, the bill finally came and there was a tacked on 20% gratuity already. Â This place definitely did not deserve the 20% gratuity for it's SLOW service and RUDE hostess...but because it was a bday dinner, we didn't want to make a huge fuss. Long story conclusion - I'll probably be back for the awesome $8 for 6 oysters and a glass of red wine or beer deal...but if you're not in a rush and don't mind abrasive manners from a hostess, this is your place to be.

Just leaving a perfect valentines day dinner Lobster risotto spectacular, and that takes a REAL chef. Super props to an awesome waitress KAT awesome attitude and really made it special. Knew all the details, sold the specials and hooked up the oyster app! Special thanks to her and WALTERS

Super delicious and cheap!! The soup dumplings were awesome as well as all the other dishes we tried like the drunken chicken and the pork with preserved cabbage. There is a wait usually so make sure you plan for that.

A really great spot to sit back and sip on some tea. Â The prices rangefrom $5 - $15 or so for tea and that includes refills. Â The desserts are about $7 or so a piece but are really good. Â I strongly recommend their flan and creme brulee. Â Neither are overpowering with flavor, but instead of a very subtle yet noticeable taste. So it's not the cheapest spot out there, but if you're stumbling around in the EV and want a different place to hang out besides a coffee shop or a bar, give this one a chance.

I have to say, the food at this place was darn good; it has the un-fanciest atmosphere imaginable. Â I had the hand-drawn noodles in their beef noodle soup. Â It's pretty cool to see the noodles stretched out for you 1+1=2+2=4+4=8+8=16+16=32+32=64...dunk it into the boiling water for a second, add broth, beef, bok choy and cilantro, and presto. Â It hurt my feelings when they forgot that I had ordered, and I was sitting there for a while wondering where my soup was, but when I got it, I was pleased. The lady who made my noodles was really nice too. Â I was the only non-Chinese person in the place, and there were lots of good vibrations, friendly chatter unintelligible to ignorant me. What I could understand, however, were the unambiguous, unselfconscious slurps of satisfaction from every diner. If you can't get a hug on a windy, rainy Monday, I'd say this soup is the next best thing to warm you.

Pizza was...OK. Certainly no where near something I would recommend. I'll be honest- Fresh mozzarella is not my thing, but that does not have a hand in my review. Very hard to find a parking place #1, and #2, the people i came in contact with were RUDE. Granted, the door man who is a staple at the place, does have to deal with a few Bozo's coming in, but that's the food biz, you should never EVER become an asshole yourself in response to a middle eastern family walking in that happens to turn you off. Sorry we ALL can't be Italian. #3- (While I was waiting in line) I told him I came from New Haven (2 hours away) just to try some Brooklyn Pizza, he says to me- "I've had Pepe's Pizza (On Wooster Street in New Haven) and said the clam pie (that they are famous for) wasn't good at all. He wrote off the place pretty hard. Pepe's has been around since the early 1920's and this guy was out of line on all counts. My honest review? No big deal really, won't go back. Ate in my car and enjoyed it, but that's it. One other thing.... Anyone gives me a pizza wrapped in butcher paper again?...can keep it. Btw?... Best pizza on earth is Pepe's in New Haven (a few more locations now). I've had some of Brooklyn's so-called best pizza, and none...NONE, can hold a candle to Pepe's. Hands down.

Everything from Japan is good. I've heard that many times. Â Really? Â Not from Amerika? I dunno bout that, but they are amazing. Japanese people are all about hospitality. Â It's like, "Our customers are the gods" Â They treat their clients well. Â So there is no waitress with crappy bitchy attitude from old skhool diner by you, yo. Their dishes... Just beautiful. Â Well, it's the way to serve tea, but still, you don't wanna see the glasses from IKEA, right? So I went down there with my friend to try their tea. Â WOW. Â I didn't know green tea could be served like as they do. Â Authentic! NO sugar. Â If you are spoiled by Arizona tea, don't even bother. Â But taste good.

Went for drinks on a Thursday night between 8 and 930, right after sunset. This place looks like a beach bar where you'd remove the sand. Its a somewhat quiet spot in the middle of north6. And guess what real estate and outfitters tenant do not ask crazy prices: 10$ margaritas and southsides! That's a deal!

This review is mostly for the Gelato. I call it Gelatoland. Â It's that good. With a medium, they will give you two scoops (of generous size). Â I love the Salted Caramel and the Chocolate. I've also eaten dinner here, and it was quite good.

This place is rapidly becoming one of my favorite places in NYC and I haven't even had dinner here yet. Â Overall I am stunned at how relatively little overall hype and number of reviews on yelp this place has received. Â  While much of the acclaim that does exist is often directed at the burger, Â which well deserves the praise, Â I feel at least as much praise should be lavished upon the chicken sandwich, Â which is unquestionably Â the best I have ever had. Â  All of the other dishes I have tried have been exceptionally well prepared and incredibly delicious, particularly the previously mentioned burger, apparently fashioned from scraps sourced from a New Jersey Â steakhouse, Â and the Shrimp and Grits which is also the best I have ever eaten, although my other shrimp and grit experiences are quite limited being a native New Yorker who hasn't spent nearly enough time in the South.

Their portion is pretty big (at least for me), so come here when you're HUNGRY. Â There's ALWAYS a line but it moves pretty quickly so don't worry about being the 50th person on a night. Â There's seating one block down if you don't want your back to be wet from sitting under the fountain

Definitely one of the few places who make decent Tonkatsu in the city. I went to Roosevelt Island and took the cable car back to Manhattan, walked to this restaurant on Sunday night. It was a perfect meal for fresh stroll out. Meal is almost $20 each, Hire Katsu or Hire miso Katsu is good. Some dinner set also is okay. Of course, I love their cabbage with sauce. Draft beer, cocktail, wine or sake are available. Yes, a lot of Asians too and many of them(ladies) talk long long time. lol It was a pleasant dining experience and you should try this at once if you are a Tonkatsu fan.
the best bodega you could hope for! the sandwiches are amazing, staff friendly and snack stock on point! I make it a point to come here when I'm in the neighborhood.
Bartender didn't even know how to make a snakebite and tried to convince me that stout doesn't sink. Yes, I know stout doesn't sink that's why I ordered this drink.

A cute space to service great Mediterranean food! My friends and I sat on benches in the middle of the restaurant and enjoyed a delicious lunch. I shared the Tuna salad and the Chicken Prego. The Tuna salad was delicious and had one of my favorite ingredients, avocado. Perfect size to share along with a tasty chicken sandwich that wasn't big at all, but in a good way! Aside from what I ate, my friend comes here often as she works a few blocks away and was raving about the cantaloupe juice. The drink was yummy and refreshing. Great place to grab breakfast or lunch!

Nice spot to check out on a nice day. I go there for the strong and tasty mojitos and the corn. The crowd seems to be evolving every time I go, which I guess is a good thing because it's pretty diverse.

As someone who literally goes there 3 times a week (bc it's close to where I work), the quality is consistent and good, especially as it's getting colder, ramen becomes even more delicious to me than in the summer :) Although I'd never understand hours of waiting for ramen. Appetizers are my so great, I mean, comparing to their ramen, not that "special" among Japanese restaurants, but if is recommend anything - have some extra black mushroom in the noodle, adds different texture with the noodle! Oh, what I really hate about this place besides the occasional waiting, is the noise! It's just beyond my threshold! Plus, do the waiter/waitresses even understand what they are shouting about? Japanese? Really?

Delicious! I had the fried chicken, gravy, and biscuits. It was rich, well balanced, and the chicken was incredibly tender. Previously I had the fried chicken biscuit with honey and pickles. Everything was good, though I feel that the pickles were a little over-hyped for a restaurant that has pickles in the name. Service was attentive and cordial. Good, but nothing special. If you're on the UWS and need a great brunch/lunch place Jacob's Pickles is the place to go. Just bring your appetite.
Bit pricey, but food is always fresh, location is clean, very humble and relaxing atmosphere...

Really charming and intimate setting-- don't understand why the restaurant is called Snack, but the Greek food is great. Our favorites were the veal kibbe/ meatballs (they melt in tour mouth) and roasted feta which was off the menu. We had the mixed mezze starter which was also very nice, but all three dishes are more than enough for two people.. Our waitress was fantastic and really knew the menu inside and out. Will probably return soon...

I came to Uva with a big group this past week and we all really, really enjoyed it. I've been thinking about their meat and cheese plates all week and may have to go back this weekend! I'm a sucker for fresh pasta and Uva really gets it right. Their sauces are flavorful, portions are perfect and the service was really efficient. I'm so happy I found this place.

I can't give this spot enough kudos! I went here 2x last week and ate the same fried chicken entree. Simply fabulous and seasoned to perfection with collard greens (yes I said greens!) and mashed potatoes w yummy gravy. I don't eat fried chicken anywhere, so this was a treat. I'm going to have to take a break and order something else on the menu..

Could not take the San Gennaro festival anymore and found this lovely little restaurant. We ordered the fried olives, the hummus, smoked eggplant bruschetta, and Dave's grilled pizza. Delicious!!! Different flavors working together and we enjoyed them all. To top this meal we had the most fabulous chocolate mousse ever. The service was very nice and friendly.

Probably one of my favorite restaurants in NYC. It is a bit pricey especially for the small portions that they give you but overall I love everything else about the restaurant. The restaurant is new American with a korean-italian flavor infusion which right off the bat I thought was super unique! The place is pretty small so I would definitely make a reservation before hand. When you first walk in they check your coat. They whisk you to your table and will tell you a little bit about the menu and what specials the chef has for the night. you have an option of a tasting menu of I think around six different items for those who are indecisive or you can order from the normal menu. Our server was nice and knowledgable. He told us that since the potions are pretty small it is advised to get one appetizer per person and one entree per person as well as a pasta to share mid meal. They will also recommend the monkey bread at the beginning which is their bread service as they don't offer complimentary bread. Â I would say that if you are really hungry go for this setup but my boyfriend and I were perfectly content with the monkey bread, one appetizer for each of us, and one entree for the each of us. The portions are kind of small so again if you go hungry maybe you should order more. The monkey bread was really good and butter and came out with seaweed butter which I loved. The bread had a little bit of an asian spin on it since it tasted similar to those breads you could get at a chinese bakery except better. I got the scallops appetizer which was amazing. The corn that it came with had a really interesting flavor with the crunchy chicken skin mixed and the scallops were so flavorful. My boyfriend got the egg with fried chicken. The chicken was so amazing and deliciously crispy. The egg was good too but it had a kind of sweet and sour flavor kind of like sour cream. If you don't like sour cream don't get this but if you do it is really good! I ordered a special from the night which was a squash ravioli with porcini mushrooms and parmasean with cookie crumbs on top. This was super delicious and sweet but reallly fresh and the pasta looked like little dumplings more than ravioli. I highly recommend this to you if you love squash Â or sweet flavored entrees. The rohan duck I heard was a favorite and my boyfriend got that it came with beets and a plum lavander sauce and was cooked medium rare. This was really delicious too and tender and juicy. Red wines available are primarily is Italian but there are a lot of interesting cocktails. In white wines they had albarino and gruner veltliner which are two of my favorites and I don't see those too often at restaurants. Overall great experience. Interesting flavors, friendly staff, and romantic atmosphere. The place is on the dressy side just a heads up.
i think this is my second favorite to difaras (might be a tie with raginas in boston). Â love this place cuz its so cheap and the wait is never long and the pizza is amazing.

I had one of the best late night meals at Lam Zhou. Out of every store this was the only one that was opened late at night to cater to my rumbling belly's needs. I ordered a number 1 and in 5 minutes a bowl of aromatic hand pulled noodle soup came out from the kitchen. The beef slices were cooked just right but what really made the dish tie up together in the end was the broth. Â The broth was savory, not too salty and had just the right flavor to accompany the noodles and beef slices. I couldn't finish all the soup but I came pretty close to finishing it. I usually don't hang out near East Broadway but when I do, this place will be my go to late night spot.

Service was a little slow here just for a very minimal order. The food was just okay nothing to shout about. If you really love sake they have a very extensive collection. Drinks Â reasonably priced couldn't complain there so if you are trying to drink for cheap especially in time square you can go there. The only thing is they don't make cocktails it's pretty much beer and sake.

Really great atmosphere, and beer selection! I've been here a few times now and it's quickly becoming one of my favorites. Staff is nice, food is excellent. The only thing that I'd love to see, is a few more options for vegetarians.
Great brunch spot! The atmosphere and decor is beautiful and the food is great albeit a more limited menu than most other brunch spots. Their egg sandwich is fantastic!

This place was great - we had a group of 8 girls for a birthday party and they were very accommodating to our group! Â Drinks were strong, ambiance was cute. Â The only negative I could say is that the place is pretty small, but other than that I would highly recommend!

I've been here a few times, and I have to give this place mixed reviews. The good: the dumplings are amazing. Wontons are also very good, although for some reason the waitress had a hard time understanding me when I ordered them and they take longer to come out. I accompanied some friends here once, and since I'd had dinner already, I just ordered wontons - only to find that for $3, I could get a huge bowl of them. In general, the prices here are fantastic. The bad: I'm not such a fan of their noodles. I thought the knife-cut noodles were sort of soggy, in an overcooked kind of way. The hand-pulled noodles were thin and not as chewy as I would have liked. Broth for the noodles is pretty good though. The fish balls are mediocre, although it's nice that they're the Fukinese kind (with meat in the middle). The ugly: never, ever am I going to order a "house special" in a Chinese restaurant again. I'm not sure what I was expecting, but I got the works - tripe, beef tendon, and all other sorts of innards that I wasn't particularly fond of. It's definitely my fault for not checking first, but let this be a warning that what may be special to a restaurant isn't necessarily what you want to order. Will I come back? Yes, for the dumplings.

A vibrant and friendly brunch place that is definitely worth trying if you are in the Union Square area. Just make sure you are prepared for a 30 minute wait. A smaller party is always ideal if you want to get a seat within the 15-minute wait estimate. Prices are a tad pricer than your typical Moonstruck Diner per se, but they are pretty much in line with what you expect in the EV. Each item comes with a free glass of juice, mimosa, or bloody mary. Last time I went, we were treated with complementary filtered (tap) water and sparkling water. (That's a first!) Secondly, an order of French Toast on the house. Hot! They were soft and warm, but light on bananas and sauce. But you can't complain about free food. The poached eggs benedict is excellent and reliable, even if the salmon is a bit dry. The fried calamari is overly crusty, but it is definitely helped by a nice kick from the spicy tomato sauce. The rum pancakes are fluffy but low on the rum. The steak and eggs option offers surprisingly tender and juicy steak. Portions are generous, the wait staff is very friendly, and prices are fair. A great choice for brunch despite the long wait. And of course, food on the house is absolute gravy. 3.5 Stars!

These types of places are what make NYC such a culinary destination. Small, cramped, and full of flavor....loved it. My girlfriend claims their lamb sandwhich is the best ever and I got to say that everything I tried was on point. If I ever opened a place like this down south all the folks would go crazy over elbow room, but in NYC you can open up great things in someone's walk in closet and be doing good business. Great lunch spot in Soho and you should definately go

Mamoun's falafel is pretty good, but it's not great. The falafel balls are pretty tasty and nicely crispy and the portion size is good. But the pita is a bit lacking (maybe it's stale? maybe it's just not a great pita?), the toppings are kind of lackluster (mealy tomatoes in August? really?), and the ratio of toppings to falafel is too high. I asked for my falafel with the works plus hummus, loaded up on hot sauce, and ended up with a soggy mess. A delicious soggy mess, but still. I know I'll be back to Mamoun's. I've been there a few dozen times over the years and now that I go to school nearby, the $2.50 price tag for lunch can't really be beat. It's not the best falafel, but it's tasty and cheap and sometimes that's good enough.

Of the limited well known southern and fried chicken places I've bene to in my life, Pie N Thighs was by far the best I've ever had. Since my visited a few weeks ago, I have been thinking about the juicy and crispy drumstick I consumed although with the creamy mac n cheese spiked with a few splashes of hot sauce, large flaky biscuit and rich warm cornbread. The fried chicken plate comes with 3 pieces, biscuit and one side and cornbread for $2 is definitely a steal quicken how expensive a dinner in nyc can get. If I ever moved to Williamsburg, I would deifnitely be at risk for a heart attack from wanting to eat at Pie N Thighs. For the slice of pie we shared, we got the lemon blackberry which was satisfying for all. Although we asked about getting it a la mode, we were informed that they were still trying to get a license! Definitely a must try in Brooklyn and NYC. Cash only!

Waiters were very friendly and accommodating - chatting with us, suggesting food and drinks, and making good (slightly corny) jokes. Â  There's even a button on the table to call them and they would come right away. We ordered the assorted seafood hotpot ($80) for 5 people. Â The lobster was still alive and moving around. Â Unfortunately, the crab had already died. Â Their watermelon soju wasn't too strong but enough to enjoy dinner. Â The waiter also came back to check that we were cooking the lobster and sliced it up for us once it was fully cooked. Then for an additional $5, they fried some rice for us in the hotpot. Â We were already super stuffed but we finished it all! Â It was THAT good! Bathroom is also very clean! Next time, we're coming back for the octopus hotpot ($100)!!! Â It also comes with lobster and crab!

I'd crawl on my hands and knees from midtown just to eat the Mac and cheese here. It's that good. In fact, I feel like I just did it was so hot and humid out when walking over here. But it was worth every step. The hype is valid. Everything we had was amazing. My wife has been searching the globe for kick ass fried chicken for several years and I think I just found what she has been seeking. The pork chop was also delightful. Â They really want out of their way to accommodate my gluten free vegan friend too. The chef went through the whole menus and identified what she could and could not eat and made some tweaks for her too. And they were super busy as always. We waited 1.5hrs for a table. No joke. Â Enjoyed it all. You should too.

This is a tiny place for tiny people. Me and my poofy down coat felt like a bull in a china shop. If you're more than 5'5", try to get a seat in the back. The seating along the wall is for Lilliputians. My Inner Miser has been quiet lately. I heard "That's the $40 salad" and Via Quadronno woke him right up. This place is pricy. Don't let all the Italian distract you. You just paid $32.10 for a toasted ham & cheese sandwich on white bread, cappuccino, and tiramisu. The Il Toast is an adaqute panini. It needed something. Mustard? Something. I was underwhelmed. I was eying the Lasagna Bolognese but my Inner Miser hit me upside the head and said "$26 for something you can make at home?!?". I was chastened. Now the Tiramisu Tradizionale was a whole different story. Especially with the excellent cappuccino. It made up for the panini and then some. Actually, if that's all you come for, it would be worth the trip. The tiramisu, coffee and some conversation would be quite a pleasant way to spend the afternoon. The service is quick and friendly, if not as attentive as I would have liked. Feel free to flag down the nearest waiter for some water, a refill of said water, the dessert menu, and the check. I won't be eating a meal here on my own dime again, most likely. But I wouldn't turn down the tiramisu that's for certain. I'm free most Wednesday afternoons. Thanks in advance.

Fantastic place. Every single item was very good to great. The atmosphere rocks - giant windows looking out onto Carmine st. Wine bottles against the walls, roomy tables, friendly staff. We started with the wine tasting - 3 flights for $9, along with a Lagunitas IPA. The appetizers were all stellar - the best crispy calamari ever, drizzled with an orange chipolte-like sauce, perfectly seasoned and laid on top of a guacomole puree. Just amazing. The soft-shell crab special (appetizer) was as good as it gets. And the gnocchi was great - served in a flavorful brown broth, with tender lamb and cabbage (or something similar), olives, figs....well, it really worked. Great for dipping the awesome crusty, rustic fresh bread they provide. On to the mains.....I threw caution to the wind and ordered the whole fish (which our amiable waitress informed was impossible to de-bone). It was a "Porgy". Never had it, so i said what the heck. It...was....really, really good. The fish came apart easily, and sure there were bones, but easily avoidable. This nice plump white fish came bathed in a wine/butter sauce with golden raisins. Mama mia. We also ordered the Arctic Char - perfect-o. Crispy, succulent, just great. Finally, the crispy chicken w/ creamy mashed potatoes and cheese fondue.....holy crap. Amazing. Could not get enough of it. We were totally stoked. Just a great all-around meal and experience. For dessert, we got the upside down pineapple cake, and surprise, it was quite delicious. The espresso gelato was tops. Great place for the family, or a date, or friends. Goin' back.

I wish I could give these guys 50 stars. This place is delicious. I'm definitely a full scale carnivore but I do eat vegan a few days a week (weird, I'm a terrible person, blah blah) and this place cannot be beat. Spicy Mang is my favorite by far but La Fiesta and the sweet potato one are really tasty. It's such a clean place inside and they are super nice. I ended up going two days in a row and they remembered me. Seating is miniscule but with all of the surrounding places to sit and relax (i.e. the square, belfry, etc.), it's not bad. Do yourself a favor and stop in ASAP.

Their risotto with italian sausage.... delicious! Just had a bunch of their appetizers split between friends and they were all delicious. Their linguini was really tasty as well. Try it here, you'll like it.

The dumplings are good and the sesame pancake is fried to have a right crispy outside. What makes this place truly amazing is the price - so freaking cheap!! I came around 4pm and there were lots of people waiting. The line moved very fast. But simply don't expect to eat in the restaurant. The place is too small and crowded. They have fried dumplings ready but you need to wait for about 8 min to get the boiled dumplings.
Tiny place with terrific food, great atmosphere, and friendly staff. I wish I could eat breakfast here every day! :) Very good espresso drinks, too.

This place might hit a sweet spot for some but is frankly overpriced for food quality, which can be hit-or-miss, and service, which is stoner-esque. On one recent visit they took my order and my name. After a while, I noticed a server wandering around from table to table with what looked to be my order. In her wanderings the server approached another couple, who arrived well after us; they said they had ordered it, but also another sandwich. Then the server wander over to us; Â when I asked if the order was for Amelia she said she didn't know -- why bother?

Man, is this place fun. Frito pie, free cheeseballs, chili cheese dogs and drinks made with Gatorade?! Yes. It's true. The Levee is cheap, has pretty decent food (tho I was sad the bun on my chili cheese dog was not toasted) and they have the Dreamsicle. That is orange soda and vanilla vodka and it is as delicious as it sounds. Comes in a pint glass, drinks like candy...basically trouble in a glass. They also have great shot and beer combos (I particularly liked the Lonestar + shot of tequila combo...yum). I will be going back here frequently and staying forever. The area around the bar is pretty crowded but there are seats in the back and tons of board games. Watch out on those Dreamsicles tho, I had a hell of a headache the next morning. Yeah, must have been the soda...not the 5 drinks.

I loved it when I went there, but potentially only because my friend paid for me, and his friend was the bartender, so he kept on giving us free drinks at the waiting bar--now that I think about it, it was an extremely long wait, that didn't bother me only because of the free drinks. Â Any other way, I think I'd be pissed, or at least, left apathetically as "not being worth it." The ramen is very good, as well as other dishes there. Â However... what was it? Â $13+ or so for a bowl of ramen? Â PLEASE. Â That is abominable. Â That is almost like getting away with murder. Â Oh, East Village.... Â Oh, Japanese restaurants that have figured out they can make a fortune off of street food... But I guess if you're not from Japan and don't know that ramen should basically NEVER be more expensive than $8, it shouldn't bother you so much. Â And it's really good! Â Preferrably make friends with the nice guy at the waiting bar. Â And get a friend to buy for you. Just an FYI, I saw online that the Ippudo prices in Japan are around 700 - 800 yen, which would be around $8, which people still complain in Japan as "expensive for ramen."

I've never left a sushi restaurant with a fishy taste in my mouth and the worse part was that my husband also felt the same way. Â  The food itself wasn't bad. We had the spicy appetizer and the Monkey Roll along with the Three Style sushi with spicy tuna roll. Â Aside from the spicy tuna roll which was definitely fishy, the rest was tasty. Â Far cry from the best I've ever hard or even delicious, but sufficient to satisfy our sushi craving if not for the fact that we should NEVER EVER EVER leave a sushi restaurant with a fishy taste in my mouth. Â We were both so horrified that we feared that we had to run across the street to buy a pack of gum to get rid of the flavor and it took a while! I genuinely feared that I would get sick when I get home. I will NEVER return to Iron Chef. Â Don't be mistaken by the packed house, there are better places nearby, namely the one across the street which is DEAD, but SUSHI is unbelievably fresh.
Great staff, great atmosphere. Â Annie, Eamon, Dana, Karen and Gavin. Â Stellar! Â Drop in soon!

Wood burning fireplace? I said Â with eyebrows raised and stomach hungry as I read the sign. Â  There was sawdust littered all over the floors and vintage photographs strewn all over the walls. Instantly I was transported to Old Ireland. After perusing the menu my friend ordered the fish and chips while I ordered the Bacon Cheeseburger. His came with the soup of the day, which happened to be the carrot ginger soup. Eyebrows raised again and stomach hungry I tasted his. "mmm... interestingly good." Pretending to not have gotten the full taste of it... I tasted it again.. "mmm.." My burger came out and ironically the waitress said, "Here's your little burger"... So expecting a small burger I was surprised to find a ginormous blob of meat and bread on my plate. HUGE. HUGE with a huge portion of potato salad. Unlike other places, I was glad that Molly's gave so many options for sides that ranged from something other than fries. One of them being potato salad (my favorite). HUGE SMILE. :] I am satisfied.

Yelp keeps reminding me to write this review. It's now about 5 months late, so sorry that it's really short. Staff here is very friendly. Ordered the french fry salad (I think) first, and it was a pleasant surprise. I was not happy with the fish I ordered, but my girlfriend's meal (I believe it was the strip steak) was cooked very well and delicately. A bit expensive for what we were getting. I think there are better restaurants in the area. Would like to try again for lunch sometime.

Very fun place. Wonderful Irish pub atmosphere, lively and noisy. Food was great. Had the burger and fries. Burger was well cooked, juicy and flavorful. Fries just perfect. Topped it off with Irish coffee that was excellent. Only lower rating was due to having to sit at the bar for service. Once a seat opened up, the service was great.

I'm baffled as to why anyone would give this little gem anything less than 4 stars. Â This little treasure has it all: great, friendly service without being obsequious or pretentious; a small but serviceable wine list and good variety of entrees from pastas to fish and chicken all very fresh and well prepared; and a fun atmosphere. Â  All the food is super tasty. Â The most recent time I went I had the fish special (branzino), which was as good as anything I would have at a restaurant that would charge me twice as much. Â It was seasoned with the perfect amount of fresh herbs, garlic and lemon slices, wedged into the side of the fish. Â BF asked for a different sauce with his pasta and they were more than happy to oblige. Â  With much change under foot in this section of Chelsea, this restaurant remains true to its roots. Â Let's hope it stays that way and doesn't change too much. Â It remains one of the truly affordable restaurants in the 'hood and the food could not be improved upon, in my humble opinion. Â My fear is that by writing this rave review I will attract more people to this former hideaway and the folks at P.G. will get the hint. Â So, please folks, stay away, so this restaurant can remain exclusively mine and the thousands of others who are already in on the secret.

Some of the best food I've ever had and it makes you feel great. The ackee and sailfish in the morning is amazing and the vegetarian curry tofu with rice is great. I have never felt better after eating a meal and the juices are great both the smoothies they make and the prepackaged Sea Moss.

Ashbox Breakfast is such a nice breakfast alternative- no carby bagel here. Spring greens and really well done eggs make for a perfect first meal of the day. I'd recommend having the dish with tea rather than coffee. Although their coffee is just fine, tea lends itself much better to the Japanese flavors. Really nice staff, calming environment.

Listen, I'm not a sushi aficionado as in I've never been to Japan nor have I had West Coast sushi (elite status) since I was in San Fran about 6 years ago. NONETHELESS, I know that raw fish is to have a certain color and keen taste and fresher than the prince of Bel Aire. For this, and many more reasons (in spite of walking into what seems like an orange-lit opium den), I give Momo a 5 star. Pointers (I'm a fan of dashes): - Instantly greeted by a knowledgeable and sweet waitress - Sushi Bomb and sushi roll + miso soup for a $12 lunch is an unbeatable price. The flavors in my "Bomb" were so fitting; it resembles a Nagiri, but has more elemental complexity to it (shredded Phyllo dough Â for extra crunch- say whaaa?). I also had the Spicy Tuna with Jalapeno. -Cuteness: different Wasabi soysauces with miniature spoons. - Comforting: Brownrice seeped Chencha green tea. - Happiness: Mission to try a decent Japanese place near work for an unbeatable lunch fulfilled.

I almost hesitate to give this place a high rating because it's already too popular. My husband and I used to come here when it was called Houston's. Hillstone is FAR better. He had a burger that he is still raving about and I had the club salad that was by far the best I have ever had. The food is FRESH. The shoestring fries are sliced up when you order them . . . nothing frozen here. I think they make their own ketchup. The chicken on my club salad was super fresh and cooked just right; served warm on the salad. Prices are reasonable for midtown. Staff is very cordial and approachable. LOVE the jazz band; it adds a really nice atmosphere. Great if you just want to stop at the bar for drinks and some snacks. They also have some great steak and fish dishes that are a little on the pricey side. They also serve sushi. I only have two criticisms.If they are going to take reservations, they should honor them for the time that is booked. We waited 20 minutes past our reservation time, but the meal made up for it. And, proper attire should be encouraged; this isn't a casual beer 'n burger joint. Sneakers and jeans clash with the ambiance they are trying to create.

I wouldn't travel across the city for this brunch, but if I were within a 10 block radius in any direction, I would head there for sure. They make a huevos rancheros that is to die for..the veggies are so fresh (grilled corn especially) and their coffee is YUM. They are usually pretty crowded on the weekends so prepare for a wait.
Very good interesting food ! No reservation walked right in! Great pretzel and cheese spÃ¤tzle

Holy empanadas, Batman! I came here on the recommendation from Mr Queens himself, Jando S, and he did not disappoint. I ordered around 7 empanadas for myself, almost as a goof bc they were so cheap, and I am glad to have ordered that many bc they were straight off the hook delish. Favorites were the sausage, beef n cheese and breakfast. I enjoyed them so much that every time I was pulled away from the bag of eats, I would take an empanadas to go. Walk to the car? Empanada. Bring someone a power cord? Empanada. Blow up a balloon? Empanada. I had this stupid grin on my face every time I dipped one in to the little green 'salsa'. I can't wait to be back in Corona to try more of the flavors and taste some of those ices. -1 star bc the place is very tiny and I hate doing the shuffle for 10 min while people come in, order, get up etc.
Best burger I've had in a VERY long time.

Go for the bacon alone. Quite possibly the best bacon I've ever had. Seriously. And go on a Friday if you can, no wait and excellent service will greet you. I had the buckwheat crepe, and it was very good. But that bacon... oh that bacon. So, so tasty. The mimosas are overpriced, but a necessary brunch staple.

Nice restaurant ! Â I came to this place for dinner with my family last week. Â We chose this place among many others in Â K town because we love Tofu dish and heard this restaurant Â has a good reputation Â for Tofu. We had vegetable, Kim chi and seafood Soondobu. I personally chose seafood one. The broth was rich and full of fresh seafood. Tofu was very fresh and tasted like real home made one. They were served with Â various small side dishes of Ban Chan. Â Kimchi was especially good and fermented proper. Fried Covinia Â and the rest of seasoned vegetable were mostly good .I chose a moderate level Â for spicy. However, Kim chi Soondobu with hot spicy selected by my sister Â was really hot. We 'd better avoid it next time. Â  They served all Soondubu with rice cooked in individual stone pot. Â  The rice was was very different from the regular one in a bowl. The rice alone was worth coming. Â It was crispy with fresh taste. The service was attentive .

Delish. Cocktails - also tasty. We ordered quite a variety of starters and mains. And didn't forget the oysters. 'Tis the season, after all! As a group of 6, we even considered ordering 1 of everything! I have to say, the best dish was the Garganelli w/ Pecorino & Nettle. Phenomenal.

My girlfriend and I came here today for brunch. The food was good. We got the pineapple, egg in the hole?, chicken and biscuits, and the bacon donuts. It was somewhat busy so the service wasn't the best but it was expected. The only thing that was fantastic was the egg in the hole with the brie and portobello mushroom. The rest was just ok. BUT I would have given Traif 3 stars if my girlfriend and I hadn't both gotten sick from eating here. I don't know exactly what it was (we think it was the chicken and biscuits though) but this was the only food we had all day and she felt nauseous and I had bowel movements that I do not want to describe on yelp. Maybe it was a one time deal but it was not pleasant.

Just dip it in the green sauce. Â Everything. Â How do they get that stuff to taste so good? Â What is it made of? Â I have no idea how to answer those questions but the green dipping sauce on the table is seriously awesome. Â It has just enough spice to Â elevate the meal but not enough to overwhelm and take over the foods taste. Valentina and I split the Matador Combo which includes the Chicken Pio served with rice and beans, tostones, salchipapa and avocado salad and Yuca Frita. Â It was more than enough food. Â The chicken was cooked cooked in such a way that it almost melted in your mouth, and I'm talking about chicken here! Â Put some green sauce on there and you've got yourself one tasty chicken. Â I wasn't a huge fan of the yucca frita, that is until I dipped it into the green sauce. Â We finished off our meal with a pitcher of sangria. Â I have no complaints about the quality of food here. Pio Pio has a great atmosphere and is a really cool restaurant. Â Its actually a little unsuspecting as how cool the vibe and decor is in this restaurant. Â A completely filling meal for two and a pitcher of sangria was 100 bucks which in my opinion was a good price for the amount and quality of food we ate. Â The staff was friendly and very fast with the food and service. Pio Pio has all the qualities of a "As good as it gets" restaurant without being pretentious. Â There is a refreshingly light buzz in the air as you can tell everyone eating here is having a great time. Â A fun light atmosphere with great food means that this restaurant is great for a date night or a simple friends night out. Â  This is my type of restaurant. Â Enjoy.

In the movie "Re-animator" Jeffery Combs a.k.a. Howard P. Lovecraft's Â heart's desire is to give life back to the dead. This is course the story of Brooklyn. The rotting corpse of Williamsburg, Green-point, the South Slope, Sunset park...etc. Â Have been and continue to receive blood=money as they were the last places where the Capitalist-fascist could buy low and sell at enormous profits to satisfy their rapacious Â greed and lust. Folks who were priced out of Manhattan now face the irony that all of this re-animation has made Brooklyn the 2nd most expensive city in America right behind Manhattan. Â Is Â Queens Â the new Brooklyn and The Bronx the new Queens? The Universe is laughing is there a Texas size asteroid heading our way. It's now 5th Avenue turn for a transfusion. What was once a dessert of faceless buildings and anonymous store fronts is now slowing getting its "color-back." I even noticed and Art Gallery near 20th street. Let's hope it does not suffer the same fate as 4th Avenue, now the home to "luxury" -read- price gouging condo's built by immigrant architects just off the boat from East Germany. I missed the memo Â where expedient ugliness has become the new standard model. Speaking of the late Eastern Europe, the one good thing to come out of it, besides the Stasi and Marcus Wolf, Â is the wonderful food. Â The restaurant KORZO has taken the best and delivers it with great style and panache. Everything on the menu is wonderful. Â Having eaten there several times Â I highly recommend you stopping in for dinner and to sample their wonderful selection of beer and cocktails. They have an art gallery in the back with some very interesting paintings but I would have preferred portraits of Uncle Joe Stalin, Eric Honecker, Bela Kun and Janos Kadar for company. The only drawback is that it is right next door to a Tattoo Parlor! Â What is it with these god dam tattoos? I mean what!!!!! Â -what happens when you are 60 and the ink has faded and gravity has started its remorseless work? Hey Grandma is that a Jackson Pollack on your butt?
A little too noisy inside, but the delicious food makes up for it. Everything was fresh and perfect. I'll be back.

Food is decent and CHEAP. The falafel sandwich is the most famous menu item and is $2.25 a pop, perfect late night or quick snack food. I prefer the babaganoush sandwich or spinach pie (greasy and small/flat though it may be). Service is as fast as possible; the guys really want you in and out quick. They've given me the wrong order a few times because they were in such a hurry. Nevertheless, usually there's a line out the store and up the steps into the streets late nights and at meal times. Take your food to go if it's busy; so not worth being jostled by the crowd, especially if a few of them are wasted.

This is probably my favorite brunch place in the city so far and I've only been here once, which is testament to the amazing experience I had... foodwise. The wait is very long. I waited about 1.5 hours for a table of 2, but I've got to say it was worth it. Being a huge fan of brunch, I don't mind waiting a long time for good food and don't think the restaurant should be dinged for being so popular. My friend and I both ordered the prix-fixe brunch. It's a good deal at $14.50 for a main plus an alcoholic or non-alcoholic drink. Being the value-driven consumers we are, we each ordered one of the two alcoholic drinks of choice - Apple Cider Mimosa and Pomegranate Bellini. Both drinks tasted SO good and weren't too strong for 1pm on a Sunday (I was happy to leave without looking like a cherry). Every dish on the menu looked so good! It was a difficult decision, but we ultimately decided on the Salmon Wrapped Poached Eggs and the Pumpkin' Waffles. What I loved about these dishes aside from them being absolutely delicious was that they were very unique options that I haven't seen anywhere else. The poached eggs were cooked just right and the yolk-soaked bread plus the salty smoked salmon was a perfect combination. To this day, I still dream about the Pumpkin' Waffles and I don't even like waffles. The plate was a perfect balance of salty & sweet, and I highly recommend this dish if you like pumpkin/apple pies. YUM! I have been recommending this place to my friends for over a year now and am waiting for the day when I feel like waiting 1-2 hours again. Maybe when the weather gets a little warmer...

So happy to have a quality Mexican food place in the neighborhood. Very good and interesting food. The owner is very friendly. Fun to eat there when the windows are open (though the Way Station patrons next door can be annoying)--also great for take out.

This place is great for large groups. Just watch out for the reservation times - they only only take an early reservation and a 9:30. The 9 of us got the entire menu - "The Whole Shebang" - and were able to finish it, but just barely. This food comes erratically - fast & furious at times, and then slower at others. That actually works out okay, because the slow times give you a few moments to pause and actually talk to your friends. My favorites (from what I remember) were the beef short ribs and the bacon wrapped dates. There was a "chef's surprise" (?) which was phyllo wrapped goat cheese that others who tried it loved. The only thing I really didn't like was a grilled octopus. The octopus was really tough and had a bad over-smoked flavor. Everyone liked their sangria and other drinks. I think the white sangria was the consensus winner. Lava cake (yes, even after all that!) was delicious.

The food is amazing, I haven't had a horrible dish yet. Â Out of the several times that I've been there, I've witnessed that the manager is a bit rude towards customers (including myself and our group). Â The rest of the service is amazing though. Â I continue to go back time and again for the great food (especially their burger!).
Good but some days horrible quality but some days probably one of the best things i have ever eaten!

AWESOME place. As authentic an izakaya as you could find outside of Tokyo. Great sake selection. Great prices. Great decor. You would never even know you're right in Times Square once you get downstairs and inside. Helpful hint: Get there at least 45min before you plan on eating, leave your name and number with the host. Then go saddle up at one of the bars nearby instead of waiting in the stairwell.

I happen to love risotto, so a place called Risotteria should do a wonderful job of keeping me happy, right? It was pouring outside. My girlfriend and I had just tried to go to S'Mac and failed (they were still closed for the holidays, no!). I decided it would be a good idea to try out Risotteria, so we headed on over. Soggy and hungry, we walked along Bleecker and into the small space. I didn't realize how small until our server pulled out our table for my girlfriend to sit. Yes, you read that right, she pulled out the table, not the chair. You're pretty much elbow to elbow with the people next to you, but it's not uncomfortable, to be honest. So, we sit and start going over the menu. Unsurprisingly, it was mostly risotto, and also unsurprisingly, it was mostly gluten-free. Having never really ventured into this culinary territory, I didn't know what to expect. Would it have the same texture? The same flavor? Would I enter withdrawal and go on a binge of Minute Rice? Let's find out... I ordered the Saturday special, which was risotto with mozzarella, shrimp, garlic, and hot peppers. My girlfriend had hers with roasted chicken, olives, and peppers. I must say, I really enjoyed my dish. It had just enough kick; the peppers didn't overpower the other flavors, and the shrimp was tasty. Yay to delicious risotto, nay to asking for a Coke and receiving The Little Bottle That Could (TM). A second nay because they didn't offer any fruit juices. Also, the complementary breadsticks were a little strange. Perhaps it's because they were gluten-free, but they just didn't have the same bite that I was used to. All things considered, I'm not sold on the place yet. I'll give it a second chance, on a day when I'm not water logged and disgruntled.
Will not be coming back to Bianca. Horrible place & service.

I've only been here a few times but everytime I come here I love it!! Its so delicious...I never though I'd like pork that much. Â I just feel sad for the little piggies that had to sacrifice their lives for my delicious meal. Plus the all you can drink beer is really cool.

Fabulous food! fun, cozy, loud, charming, LARGE portions, good NYC value. This wonderful restaurant has the BEST Italian food I have ever had! Â Started with the artichoke salad then had the butternut squash ravioli. Â Sampled everyone's meal at our table, all were delightful. Â The tiramisu was so scrumptious. The table wine was smooth. Â Make a reservation and enjoy!

My french toast was AMAZING, served with real maple syrup, and a bargain at only $10. Dining companions all had savory crepes which were well received. Bread was yummy. French ambiance. Only drawbacks were that the restaurant was pretty loud even as the rush came to a close, and my home fries were way too salty to eat.

I would give this place five stars except I'm continually frustrated when I go in there for a bite to eat alone in the evening. The cost is $8+ for a half chicken (the smallest order you can get) and then if you want to order a side, that's another $6+ for one side. So for a single person a chicken dinner is $16 or more after the tax is added. That doesn't make sense. Why the restaurant owner doesn't have some kind of combo plate for dinner is beyond me. I'm sure she'd have way more people coming in for that. If you don't mind spending that much for a (very good) chicken dinner, then I recommend this place. Or if you come in 2's or 3's it's a nice option. But coming solo, I wouldn't do it. There are other places in the area with a similar casual vibe for less. UPDATE: I've discovered my favorite thing to order here: the chicken thigh wrap. It's ridiculously good. Juicy, full of good stuff. I start to crave these and have to come back for more.

One of the best pizzas ever tasted......4 stars rather than 5 because they are SLOW....I saw what was going on with speed to took my slices cold so I didnt have to wait.....and even room temp, was one of the best I ever had...speed up the service stop yapping about nonsense in the back.....then would be 5

Beyoglu was pretty busy the night we went so I had high hopes. Â However, the service and my dish were very under par. Â We were a party of 5 for a birthday dinner. Â We shared some appetizers....and then waited...and waited...and waited. Â Our waiter did not come by to ask if we wanted another drink or to apologize for the delay in getting our entrees. Â When I politely asked him as he was zooming by us if we would be getting our meals soon, he looked perplexed...and then proceeded to blame the dish I ordered (the shrimp casserole) for the delay...saying it takes awhile to make the casserole. Â I'm sure I then looked perplexed because I've never heard of such a thing - it wasn't anything more than shrimp and veggies and cheese. Â Very odd. Â Then we waited some more and they brought our food. Â When he served my dish, he again said the casserole was the reason everything was delayed. Â (I couldn't believe it - as if it was my "the customers" fault.) Â And to top it off the shrimp casserole wasn't even good...the shrimp were tough and they had tails on them still (which seemed odd cutting into a casserole and coming up with a tail shell, no?) Â  It was so obvious to all of us that the waiter made the "casserole delay" up as an excuse (and a ridiculous one at that)....he could've just said the kitchen was backed up, my apologies. Â  I live in NYC and have eaten at so many restaurants and this by far is one of the worst I've experienced service-wise, I'm sorry to say. Â I will not be returning and would never recommend this place. Â Be forewarned.

A quaint Italian wine bar and cafe that suits the romance for two. With a friend to end the night which earlier includes a Russian and Turkish Bath house, we ventured to Sofia for everlasting spirits. The rear of this dinning room was formerly the office of an art gallery by the artist Ulla Darney. Space is clean and facilities are immaculate clean with all the warm cozy comforts of home. Â Sofia is charming and alluring. Â There is no modern decor which does not make it overpowering. Â Music overhead from a speakers in the facility. The Margherita pizza at $14.00 can be shared for two accompanied by a glass of wine. I love fresh basil embedded in pizza for a balanced favor. Sofia uses organic ingredients to concoct an Italian feast of a Sunday dinner with family and friends, yet somewhat pricey. Staff is extreme attentive courteous, welcoming warm and respectful to accommodate patrons' needs. As I was undecided what genre of red wine to inhale while my friend, being a typical male, was confident and assured to order a German white Riesling that was no doubt deliciously sweet. The wine list is extensive from worldwide regions, not exclusive from Italy. Â The waiter reassured my decision to produce four samples of red wine that we had the pleasure to intake. Â Ultimately I choose the Pinor Noir, Knightsdale Mendocino 2009 at $14.00 where the "Earth's soft tannins appeal to the dash of plum and medium bodied feel" entices me seductively. Â The wait staff are knowledgable with wine. Â With a faulty table top and leg our wait staff was able to produce a quick fix with coasters for stability. The Tartufo shared was a sweet ending.

This is really it. Finally came during a happy hour to enjoy cheaper craft beers and The Jeffrey's ever changing menu. I was hoping to snag a seat outside in their outdoor space, but it was clogged up like it should be. Again. The music. If I could create a bar, it's slowly becoming an identical copy of The Jeffrey (except not on the fuckin bougie UES).

brunch was yumm-o. super casual and friendly service. a real neighborhood gem. the weekly skillet special was two fried eggs with mushroom and asparagus in truffle oil, served with two buttery slices of white bread.
The pizza sauce tastes worse than from a can, watery like consistency. Toppings thrown on, too much ricotta on white pizza. Garlic crisps were soggy flavorless leftover pieces of crust.
One of the best burger joints in town, Soft buns, Always a table avail. Nice happy hours. It would be a 5star if they can figure out how to make the breading stick to the onion rings, that's it.

Lots of fun. Large tables all around us and draft Sapporo kept the laughs coming. We ordered our dinner in waves waiting to see what we craved. Calamare, shrimp apps, edamame, short ribs, fried bananas and green tea ice cream. All good choices. Next time I'll try the pho. Our neighbors were rendered speechless by theirs.

I made reservations for a party of 6 two weeks ago on OpenTable and asked to be seated by the windows. Reservation confirmed. 5 of the 6 arrived together (1 was parking his car) and we were told we needed all 6 to be seated - there is a 15 minute grace period where afterward you lose your reservation and have to wait for an available table. Once we were all together we were seated by the windows, phenomenal view of the East Side of Manhattan, direct view of the Empire State Building. The setting has very dim lighting. We immediately got our menus - which to all of our surprise LIGHT UP! Our waitress was Priscilla (she was awesome) We ordered drinks, a pitcher of red sangria, appetizers and our entrees (all together) Everything came orderly; the drinks were YUM! Henny Mojitos and Patron Mojitos were strong and sweet, the red sangria was really good as well. We had the freshest guacamole. Chef Kelvin stopped by our table with complimentary arepitas with braised short rib - so delicious. After loud laughing, reckless NC17 conversation, reminiscing and planning vacations our entrees came... 4 out of the 6 had the Churrasco which was JUICY, slightly charred and AMAZING. The other two (including myself) had the Surf & Turf... Are you Dominican? Have you ever had Mangu? Yes? Well then you haven't had mangu like this... Sweet baby Jesus it was GOOD! The scallops were perfectly seared ... Man my mouth is watering. After another round of drinks and another pitcher of sangria we ordered the dessert sampler which included: warm lava cake, piÃ±a colada tres Leches, coconut flan, a guava and cheese fried roll and ice cream... We DEVOURED that plate. I cannot stress how great the service was. We wiped down those plates, not a crumb was spared, the food was delicious, the drinks were on point, the ambience set a great mood, the vibes were of joy. Priscilla was very attentive and sweet. Chef Kelvin came by our table twice making sure we were a happy bunch and happy does not describe the level of content in which we left BOTW. We promised to go back when the weather was a bit warmer.

Great cocktails friendly bar staff! The food was amazing! Hanger steak Â cook perfect med. rare & truffle fries were crispy and flavorful, made from fresh potatoes. My wife had the pork belly special all she said was" Holy Swine". Â We been there to the bar before for cocktails our bartender was Alex he was great. We only had the Â wings OMG they are the best in the city. He made us wild cocktails with ginger and tequila and my wife had pump up the jam. He made us promise to come back for dinner. Â It's our new local. Oh I almost forgot we went on Friday during the snow storm and they have a REAL FIREPLACE!!! Yes

Had a wonderful time w/my sister and girlfriend at SoCo. Â We arrived after Â 12am and even though the kitchen was closing, the owner /manager still allowed us to come in an order dinner. Â The service was awesome and the food left us speechless. Â I would def go back and would recommend it to all.
No credit cards, except American Express? And so we have to go out in the cold to find an ATM? Lame.

There are few times when an establishment may deserve 5 stars; however, when I have to rack my brain to think of any negatives and come up with none, I'll say its deserved. Friendly, attentive, and Accommodating staff. The food was 'Delish' . If you chose to go, which i strongly recommend; have the Herb Marinated Skirt Steak. You won't regret it. This one is on my list! Affordable as well.

This place did not disappoint. Delicious herbed ricotta, truffled polenta, seafood soup with perfect scallops, clams, shrimp. Incredible wine and cognac + desserts of pumpkin semifreddo, coconut gelato. Great service and very attentive though struggling a bit with the volume of clientele. Won't knock em for it, however, as they went out of their way to make up for any delays.

There is nothing awesome about Penelope. Â Sure, it's OK...the food is decent, the decor is cute, but an hour or more wait-time on the weekend for mediocre food? I don't get it. Â There are places nearby with shorter wait-times and better food. Â I guess I just don't understand what everyone's paying for. Â It's certainly not the homefries. Knowing there'd be a ridiculous wait on a Sunday at around 10:30-11:00am, my friends sent me early, iPad in hand, to put our names down and wait patiently as they woke up, got ready, and moseyed over. Â The wait turned out to be about an hour or so, but if you bring a book and want to partake in their free coffee while waiting on a country-style bench as people congregate around the host stand, it's not such a bad queue. When we were finally seated in the small dining room, I immediately glanced around at the other plates (come on, you know you do it, too...people just respond better to visuals of the food than their listing on the menu!) to see what looked good. Â A theme emerged: french toast. Â Cross-referencing my sights with the menu I was handed, I realized this must be the "famous" nutella french toast that everyone talks about. Â OK, I'll bite (pun most definitely intended), give me this freaking french toast. I have to know what the ruckus is all about. While it was definitely the best dish of the morning, it wasn't absolutely knock-my-socks off. Â I've definitely had better (I'm talkin; to you, Cafe Luna, the object of my desires). Â The toast was fluffy and light, and certainly not a spot of soggy or dry...but the streaks of nutella were more for coloring than flavor, and the dish tasted more like buttery bread than nutella. We also ordered the spinach pie - It came in a giant, tall slice on the plate with some "mixed greens" (wilted romaine tips). Â While it looked pretty, it did not taste homemade and I immediately feared it was mass-made (there or elsewhere), frozen, and thawed/cooked when needed. Â Dense, bland, underwhelming - I wouldn't suggest you order this, as it was not a stand-out item by any means. As a breakfast-staple, we also ordered an omelet with homefries. Â Both were bland and under-seasoned (dire need of salt all around), and the homefries were too-overcooked (sat under the heat lamp too long?) and dry/crunchy. Â Do yourself a favor and get the fries instead of the breakfast potatoes - Those fries looked like a Glamour Shot. Â So dandy. Value commentary: Like most brunch-y places, they offer a pre fixe menu: $15 gets you coffee/tea and juice OR a mimosa along with the entree. Â For $9 you can get many of the entrees alone, so if you're having the pre-fixe with coffee rather than a cocktail, it's probably a better deal to just order them separately. Â You'll save money that way (and the small glass of too-sweet, too-thick fruit juice, no refills, they give you does not make up the difference you're paying). Â My advice? Â Decide whether this will be a boozy-brunch for you, and if not, go rogue and order a la carte.

AMAZING food! Hubby and I came here for a late lunch after furniture shopping in Chelsea. We got the smokey mac n cheese as a starter and it was soooooo tasty. Chunks of thick bacon with oozy cheese and twirly macaroni. I had the grilled cheese with tomato and bacon on a muffin and it was so yummy. Husband had a tuna melt which he loved too. New favorite spot

I just had a dinner at Traif for the first time... I thought the chef was Â genius. They need a bigger space. The restaurant was packed all night. The hostess was very sweet and friendly as well as the wait staff.
This place was a lot of fun. Â The servers are really nice and the flavor of the crawfish is great. Â I wasn't crazy about the softshell crab but I did get a bag of crawfish which was banging.

A chicken and rice cart with exactly zero frills. We got the chicken and rice to share. Even though it is $6 US, there is a lot of food and we actually shared one between two of us. Don't expect courtesy or much in terms of service as they've got a long line and need to keep it moving! Tip: Wait in a long line and check out the menu on Yelp before you order. There are only about four or five choices, so it should be easy (for you indecisive peeps like me) and will help keep that long line moving.

The partridge was inedible, and for a Michelin star the rest of the food was mediocre at best. The service was awful, and the level of arrogance required to refuse a patron mayo / garlic aioli for French fries is more than I can fathom. To make matters worse, the table we were seated next to (read: on top of) was a low brow gang of yuppies. I definitely won't be back. Dat burger was dank tho.

The food is a bit better than I expected not that bad at all, its a different style than most food but the flavors tend to balance themselves out, and the steak seems to be cooked properly. The only problem with this place which gave it 3 stars instead of 4 is the pricing for small portions. Granted the prices were reasonable maybe 1-2 years ago because someone had says it was $15 a meal, now its more like $20 a meal. I had the rack of lamb and rib eye steak. This place is great for taking your friends but a bit small so it may be crowded at times. They have take-out which is great.
