The meals were great but small , the rib eye steak had the proper texture I ordered and the rack of lamb was fine. The rib eye steak could use slightly better sauce pairing, now even though the food was great and better than most typical spanish and colombian places that try to be authentic, the food really is not worth the price. I had the steak medium rare. Your paying $40 for 1.5 meals and while great its not something out of the world or something complex or though of. Since many places don't serve food even close to this caliber if you want latin/mexican food you should try this place if you can afford it. This is food that is not that extraordinary but served and cooked the way it should be , since most restaurants and places don't do it properly this place deserves at least 3 stars. Granted its not your ordinary style of food that is normally cooked up and its not simple take-out food that is normally but its not out of the world its sort of in the slightly higher than Â middle range of food. I would like to give a 3.5 stars but yelp doesn't allow for .5 ratings in between aka 4.5 or 3.5. If you go here with friends I recommend maybe ordering an appetizer and maybe 3 dishes and sharing them possibly.

My boyfriend and I were looking for a nice place to go for a late night dinner and we stumbled upon Mominette. The friendly bartender greeted us the second we walked in (and somehow remembered me when I came in 2 weeks later!) and told us we were welcome to sit in the garden for dinner and he would let the server know we were back there. Garden? Whaaaat? We waited about 10 minutes for the server to realize we were back there (and my boyfriend ended up tracking him down and asking for menus). Food: Delicious! Absolutely wonderful. I have been back twice now, just for the food. The mashed potatoes are INSANE, asparagus covered in garlic and butter and a perfectly cooked steak. But, the mushroom truffle risotto was what made me come back. I craved it and when I came back for the risotto, they had taken it off the menu. I almost cried. Why, Mominette, Why? My steak was still delicious but that risotto needs to return. Also, I have asked about the cheese plate each time I come in and each time I was told that they "don't know what's on the cheese plate but I'll go ask" and then when they come back, "we're not doing the cheese plate tonight." Service: I am a server so I understand that people are rude and usually demanding assholes, which takes its toll on any server. But some advice for the future: I wasn't sure who our server was. We had 3 different (not so friendly) servers coming up to us at random times and helping us. But their communication must have been terrible because we ended up having to order the same drink 3 times to our 3 different servers. Overall, I will definitely be coming back here. The food is incredible and I'm such a bitch for a garden.

I give this place 3.5 stars - it is definitely a great value for the price. Came here on a thursday morning with my husband so there was no wait. I was really looking forward to the pumpkin pancakes that everyone seemed to be raving about but I was a little disappointed with the one note flavor. The staff were all very pleasant and attentive. The bathrooms were clean but tiny. Would recommend this place for the value and atmosphere. Good brunch place to go to with friends.

Cute little Italian cafe on the happening block of 31st Avenue. Small inside, but they have an outdoor garden. So many paninis and crostini to choose from, and their salads are HUGE. Plus they're cheap! Three of us ate (2 crostini and 1 panini, plus a brownie) for less than $30.

Delicious food. Â I got the pork chop and it was great. Â I loved the seasonal options and that they served maple butter with their bread. Â You can really tell that the owners/chefs really care about the food that is made here. Â I loved that the runners described what was on every plate before serving it. Â Our waitress was very attentive and seemed experienced. Â I highly recommend ordering a cocktail from here, they are unique and better than any other place I've had in NYC. Â It is impossible to get into this place, which is proof of its popularity and quality. Â We booked a reservation a month in advance for a Saturday night and the only openings they had were at 5pm and 9:30pm. Â I'll probably be back for lunch since I'm not into booking reservations that far in advance. Â I took a star away because I think some of the items on the dinner menu are over priced. Â My boyfriend ordered the strip steak which was more than $50 but was disappointed with it. Â Overall I will definitely be back, but most likely for lunch/brunch or drinks
Dined with my wife, seated in smaller room which was great. Â Server was the best, very helpful with wine and entree selections. Â The food was wonderful. Not huge portions, just right.

Really the best sushi I've had in a while. Creative sushi rolls, like the Salmon Guacamole (Yum!). Also, the pork gyoza was super yummy, and the sauce that came with it too. Did I mention that their coke comes in a bottle too? It tastes better that way, according to my boyfriend. The service was awesome too, very attentive.

Great BBQ place for summer, with outdoor picnic tables. There are no table service, first come first serve base for tables. Just like Williamsburg style, very chill and relax. This place is always pack so if you are really hungry, eat something first just because the wait for ordering line could be half hour wait. They move fairly fast. Suggestion would be to come with a few friends, grab a table Space, grab a beer while waiting in line, take turn waiting in line. The brisket is a must, they cooked it so well that it literally melt in your mouth. And the beef ribs is awesome too, along with their burned bean as side. Â So what to do after eating all these heavy meat BBQ? Grab a whiskey at their whiskey bar, they have a great selection of American whiskey, from rye to bourbon, perfect after a heavy meal of meats.
Why can't you choose 0 stars? Â This place is trying so hard! Â Full of burnt pizza and a staff of douchebags! Don't waste your time...

After reading the reviews on Yelp, I was really excited to use my blackboard eats discount at their soho location. I came here for brunch on saturday and I left the restaurant not as enthusiastic about it. It might be because I came for brunch instead of dinner, but the food portions were very small compared to other tapas places I've been and the entrees were also average at best. I got the buttermilk pancakes with fresh fruit and I was a little disappointed that the blueberries were baked into the pancakes instead of served on the side. My friend got the steak and eggs which were good - but not off the charts good. For tapas we ordered the dates (3 dates), which thought were a bit too sweet and the quail egg with chorizo (2 slices of bread) which was just okay. Overall great location and cool decor - but average food. oh and the waiter wasn't that friendly either - try smiling a little next time!
There is absolutely no point in eating there. Fries are basic and sauces are super fat.

Very similar to Bay Area's Gordos. Bit on bland side, definitely suggest getting hot sauce to give it a little more kick. Many other reviewers have compared it to Chipotle. One clear difference between the two is Chipotle is much saltier. Dos Toros' meat is superior, but not its salsa. If Dos Toros was in the Bay Area, I'd give it 3. Given your Mexican food options in NY (and the East Coast in general), I think it deserves 4 stars.

Often a place can be measured in terms of how they deal with a mishap. Juventino is smooth and professional under pressure. My friend and I went there for brunch and when the waiter brought us our drinks (2 french press coffees and 2 mimosas), he accidentally hit the edge of the tray, lost balance, and the drinks tumbled onto us. Within seconds, several staff members were there cleaning up, taking care of us, and apologizing courteously. Both my friend and I have worked in the restaurant business, so we understand that these things happen and we didn't expect anything. But the manager came by and said "Please order whatever you want, brunch is on us" and he gave us a few recommendations on what to order. What made it extraordinary is how often they came by to check in on us, to refill our glasses, and to make sure we were okay. It wasn't overly apologetic, just a genuine "We want to make sure you enjoy your brunch even if you're soaking wet." The 5 stars is not just because of this mishap. The food is OUTSTANDING, the atmosphere makes me want to move in, and the staff was superb. If I lived in Park Slope, this would be a weekly treat for me!

So good. Best french toast for brunch with mango and strawberry salsa that's not too sweet and not too bready. mmmm The staff is welcoming and sweet although sometimes a little batty, but true to soho nature. Â Great coffee and vibe. love it.

My bf and I went there for dinner. Â While we were waiting for our table, we ordered a ginger margarita and basil lime daiquiri. Â I absolutely love the daiquiri. Â It was simply perfect with the basil and lime combo. Â  For appetizers, we started with crab toast and raw scallops. Â I wish the toast was thinner and the crab had more crab flavor. The scallops were divine though. Â They had a citrusy flavor and also sprinkled with crushed peanuts and basil. Â They were thinly sliced and served chilled. I don't remember what else I ordered, which was a pretty good indicator that they were not memorable.

My family is thousands of miles away so instead of a big Easter family meal I decided to give Minetta Tavern a try. It was rainy and V and I were ill-prepared for the NY bipolar weathering. Sorry to Isa and Marco, we needed the homesickness remedy and couldn't wait--a fat juicy burger can cure almost anything. The place will seat you at the bar if you don't have a reservation, which I honestly prefer as the bartenders are entertaining and the eavesdropping is good. I chose the Kill Devil Punch cocktail and it was just the right mix of citrus with rum ($15). There was no room for appetizers as we rushed them to get us a round of burgers. If you order it medium it comes out medium rare and if you order it medium rare it comes out rare the French-speaking bartender explained to the guys next to us. I recommend them medium as they are just pink in the middle. The Black Label burger is better than the Minetta Burger in terms of tastiness (must be the extra meat added in)--I don't know what the guy with the quick tip was talking 'bout. The french fries/pomme frites are delicious side (as always). The crowd is a mix of tourist/regulars/foodies. I think the mayor on Foursquare (Enzo) is a bartender here, which would make sense. I will probably be back if a tourist friend really wants to go as the blk label is definitely worth a try. I wonder if I should add cheese to it...
I'm almost afraid to write how awesome this place is.
I was just here and I totally dig this place! Â Will definitely be adding this to my short (sorry, I'm more of a foodie than a drinkie) list of acceptable nyc bars!
Cute little lunch place in soho! Food was delicious and the service was quick and friendly. Definitely worth a try!

Upside: Â Succulent pulled pork with LARGE pieces, not just threads. Â Tasty barbecue beans, nice snap peas (which are incorrectly labeled as edamame), zippy slaw and pickles. Â  Inexpensive for a group if you order by the pound. Meh: Dry, under-seasoned brisket, forgettable chicken. Â Everything improves with sauce, bottles on every table. Â (I know, barbecue is better without sauce...but not here.) Lousy: Ran out of ribs, told us to get in line again 25 min later. Â We didn't. Â Awful high school cafeteria atmosphere -- terribly loud, people hanging over you like vultures waiting to capture your table. Â Do NOT come here on a date or to have a comfortable meal with friends. Â No wine, just beer. Â  Bottom line: Â Some of the meats were enjoyable but overall not a great meal. Â We might return to carry out the famous ribs, but would not dine-in again.

I've been here multiple times with big and small groups. Â The experience is always good. Â Some dishes that came recommended from a Malaysian friend: roti canai, beef rendang, chow kuey teow, seafood scramble egg chow fun (my fav), hainanese chicken, king pork buff, oyster omlette, chicken &/or coconut rice. Â I would also add the garlic chicken to the list. Â (Note: oyster omlette last time was a bit raw).

I love the style, love the atmosphere, and enjoy the variety of beers! Bartenders a hoot! and it's great to wine down with friends at this joint. Haven't got the privilege to taste their foods. Hence the 1 star down. Other then that it's a cool spot. I recommend it to all if your downtown and no where else to go.

2 reasons for 3 stars -Food and prices are, like, exactly the same as VP2 or Red Bamboo. I've never been to the actual restaurant, so I'm not sure if the presentation/environment is similar. -They deliver to Kensington (Prompt, juicy, sugarcane drumsticks. Nom.)

Just finished dinner this evening, because i lived in houston for several years, i am a fan for cajun creole food. Decided to finally try this place, we ordered a side salad, fried chicken (little overcooked), crawlfish etou, jambalaya, mac/cheese, lima beans, and collard. The lima with ham was fantastic , full of flavor. However, the only problem i had was that the dishes were high on the sodium side. I think it is always best for customers to add to the sodium intake as they please, it is always easier to add into the taste, versus extracting it. Other than that, it was not that bad. Again, having high blood pressure, with the high sodium would prevent me from being a regular. I really wanted to try the oyster po boy though.

I have been here 2 times so far, and its been great. My first visit was unexpected and I had just ate so I only had a drink, but the second time i decided to try the sliders. They are sooooo good, and really aren't that expensive at all. Â The staff are friendly and attentive. Good music, cheap glasses of wine, very chill environment. I definitely will be coming here often.

Preface/background: I am now more focused on quality and am always looking for a great deal (read: value). Less meat, no more 2 Chipotle burrito eating. Got the basic burrito aka veggie burrito for $8.25 - I like the rice better than Chipotle's - tastes a little more authentic and not as cilantro-y and lime-y. And their fresh veggies are tastier than Chipotle's too. Got the mild sauce and no cheese or sour cream. Even though I didn't get those ingredients, it still tasted good and I was stuffed. I'd say it's a little more flavorful than Chipotle - the ingredients directed my taste buds to understand what the flavor was trying to be. Whereas Chipotle seems more like a middle school classroom with all flavors of awkward with no real direction. Not that I don't like Chipotle, but I kinda just wanted to make an analogy. I'd come back here. I got lucky and got a seat, but the place seems pretty small so it's a risk. But the table turnover seems pretty quick, because by the time I came in, all the tables were taken, but by the time I got my burrito, a table freed up. I'm getting hungry again...

I love wontons! I try it to look for great wontons in every city that has a Chinatown. Â These wontons are great! Â Big and tasty and you can smell the wonderful aroma as you bite into them. Â I had the wonton noodle soup with roast duck and it was delicious. Â Would definitely come here again when in town and will also recommend to friends & family.

I affirm every positive review about the lobster roll. I agree that the lobster here is equally as tasty as any I've had in New England. My husband and I enjoyed sitting at the outside tables and people watching. We especially enjoyed watching those people who were drooling over our lobster roll. :) they gives you a ton of very fresh and sustainably sourced lobster in every roll, perfectly prepared on a toasted roll. It doesn't get any better than that. Be sure to check out the Maine State Seal from Senator Muskie's office on the wall. Dirago! The most expensive sandwich" was what I thought I was ordering, and "the most expensive sandwich" is what I still remember eating. Ok it's good and value wise it's probably reasonable given the hard work to harvest the meat from the sea creatures, but it's not something I would go back to, just too expensive!

One word: Overrated. The elote (corn) was overrated and when served to us was kinda cold/room temperature. The server also barely made eye contact with us. The grilled chicken salad was subpar and the steak enchilada was rather tasty but not the best I've ever had. I did like the yellowish/orange rice though...maybe I'm a Cuban/Mexican food snob since I grew up in Miami and lived in LA for many years. FYI this is not solely Cuban food people although the name would indicate otherwise
An awesome strange place with great food offering!

Been here a couple times for their dinner menu and red/white/blue deal. Â They have recently raised their price a little. Â The red/white/blue deal with the half dozen of oysters weren't on the par, clams were quite good though. Â Appetizers and other dishes were good too but nothing outstanding and memorable. Seafood quality is so so, atmosphere a-ok. Â Convenient location in west village is a plus. Â The HH deal is pretty sweet so this is a 3 star.
Favorite!

Came here with D on a Friday, it's a cute casual spot with a fun vibe but the food was nothing to write home about. D was looking for an izakaya and we settled on Robataya. We ordered the pork belly which was plain slices of pork served with a side of sauce (highlight of the dish which says a lot) and a touch of yuzu pepper. It was good but the sauce was really its saving grace, reminded me of katsu sauce, minus the tang and a bit more savory. We also ordered the whole fish which was tiny and not worth the price tag. It was also super salty. Â Again, nothing special and also ordered a side of taro which was plain grilled taro. Had to dip it into the remaining pork belly sauce to give it some oomph. Finished dinner with the salmon ikura rice that other Yelpers raved about, and it was again, nothing special (and not worth the price tag). Â  Maybe people come for the bar side seats or for the sake but we has neither so it was an underwhelming to say the least. I will most likely not return since Blue Ribbon Sushi Izakaya (love!) is just a quick cab ride away.

Once you've had L&Bs square slice, it's hard to give a fair review to anyone elses. I went with two different kinds of slices, their Original Prince Slice ($2.95), and the Prince Perfection Square Slice ($3.75). The Original Prince is great. The crust is the best part. It's crispy, but not overly done. The slice is plain with just cheese, and marinara sauce, which are both spot on, and you can tell they use quality ingredients. If you enjoy a thicker crust, then I'd definitely go with the Prince Perfection Square. Like I said, it's hard to judge sicilian pizza when you've had L&B, but this is a pretty great square slice. It's the same toppings as the Original Prince, cheese and marinara. You won't go wrong with either. Like every pizza place, they heat them up before serving them, so they come out ready to burn your mouth. The place is pretty small, a few small tables, and a bar along the wall. Employees are friendly, and the atmosphere is your typical New York Pizza place. If you're looking for a step up from the often terrible dollar pizza places that are on every corner, but don't want to spend a stupid amount of money on gimmicky pizza, this place is perfect. Simple and delicious.
I loveeee their hokkien udang mee here!

I honestly, never write reviews but felt like I had to after our experience... We rented out a table for my friend's birthday, and the whole night they were treating us like criminals. They gave away half of the space we had reserved because not everyone arrived on time, and when more people showed up, we asked if we could have the table back and they got very defensive and said "whoaaaa guys calm down." Our waitress kept yelling at us because we had a party of 30 and some people were ordering from the bar, not from her, but they had given our table away and only 6 people could sit down! The final straw was when they wouldn't let our friend in because he was Asian. Literally, that was the only reason the Bouncer gave. Don't come here.
Amazing and cheap. Their pasta dishes are incredible!

Its amazing that a place can not care about service at all, as mentioned I used to frequent here for their average food (never a wait to eat there hence we kept coming back.......) The service has always been poor at Rabbithole (something you can pick up on from most reviews here). However I didn't let it deter me because but have since learnt its poor management that hasn't trained the staff. I apologize in faulting the servers when the owner seems to not know how to run a business. It seems that anyone who has given a negative review was in fact at fault and not the restaurant (Francine's/Axels reviews are proof and point). Even positive reviews will point out that its disorganized, the last two times we have had the incorrect food brought out, incorrect items on bills, food cooked incorrectly and never once had a server being polite not to mention waiting for extended periods for servers to come check on us. Its clear from the berating essay from the owner to my previous Yelp review that I was indeed at fault for these issues (and anyone else with a negative review). The owner has indeed lost the plot, the other review left 5 days before was indeed my girlfriends review of the restaurant and had nothing to do with me, just goes to prove how much he has lost the plot. I would care to point out a tip or gratuity is something that is added to the bill at the discretion of the customer when they feel service has been adequate or good, I chose not to tip as I felt the service was awful and beyond the already incredibly low standards I held your restaurant at. If you are in the area try out one of PT, Potlikker, Wild, Brisket Town, Bistro Petit, La Superior or ISA as they are all on the very same doorstep and cook your food to a higher standard and without the attitude. There's no point in giving your business to someone that doesn't want it; and will not be doing so in the future and would recommend you to try out any of the above restaurants as you will be catered for and served with a smile and attentive nature unlike here. Oh and please feel free to post another dissertation in response to my negative review it just helps point out how little you care about the customers and strengthens all of the points about poor customer satisfaction.

I haven't had a very good solid bowl of ramen in some time (haven't been to ippudo in years), and the other local options weren't really weren't doing the job. I had heard about how Mu Ramen previously had a pop-up but never had a chance. The hype was building up for this place before I got here, and was prepared to eat 2 bowls if it was the real deal. Â Here's the breakdown. Tonkotsu 2.0 - I always envision a tonkotsu being very fatty, thicker, with a rounded out flavor. Mu's tonkotsu was as not as fatty as I was used to, however, it was very well balanced and flavorful. It was combined with thinner noodles which complemented it very well. Sometimes ramen at other places can be underwhelming and bland, too salty, or overpowering, but this bowl at Mu ramen had the right balance of flavor, noodle, and pork jowl. I gladly finished the entire broth, ready for another bowl. Spicy Miso Ramen - This broth was extra hot, spicy but not too spicy, and a good, strong flavor. This ramen had thicker noodles than the other ramens here, which seemed appropriate. Attention to detail: The soup spoons are huge. Really huge. and for such good broth, it's fitting. Makes it much easier to finish the broth and to hold your noodles in. U & I: This appetizer Â seafood rice bowl, including uni, ikura, roasted nori, spicy tuna, Â wasabi, and sushi rice, was very good. It's served in a small rice bowl. I don't know if it's worth $15, but it is really really good. It's definitely a winning appetizer for me. I could probably eat two of these. Unipo: I only tasted a small spoonful from my friend's bowl, but it wasn't my cup of tea. I guess i'm not a fan of rice porridge's in general, even if you add shaved truffles and other quality ingredients. Staff: I definitely prefer mom&pop or chef owned and managed places because there's so much extra attention and care. The co-owner Heidy takes her time to welcome you to their shop and to explain all the dishes. Everyone pitches in to serve the food, refill water glasses, etc., even Chef Smookler. You can definitely feel their imprint on the place. That special touch is something a lot of places don't have in general. Decor: I normally don't really care how my ramen places look or feel, but Mu Ramen definitely made an effort to make this place feel relaxed and laidback. The reclaimed wood tables, benches, cool ceiling design and lighting, definitely a nice spot. Also they had a nice mix of 90s hip hop and current music with a beat in the background. This was cash only, so definitely be prepared if you're ordering a whole bunch of appetizers and ramens. I got there at 20 minutes before the 5:30 opening on a Wednesday, and was the first group in line. However, the line slowly built up by 5:30. Since I was the first one in, there were no complaints. However, possibly because it's a new spot and they want to treat each customer with care and respect, they only slowly filled up the seating. I can imagine the lines being pretty bad later at night with every group ordering various appetizers. As a general suggestion, not sure if they wanted to keep the place to a 22 seater, but it would be cool if they added bar seating to the side wall, though that would ruin the ambience, just a thought. Final thoughts, I will definitely return time and time again. All ramen should be this good, just my 2 cents. Finally found a close enough spot to frequent other than Ippudo, special Mitsuwa japanese food festivals, or Japan.

I returned to this place just a couple days after trying it. And plan on returning many more times. This time around I got the Williamsburger ($14.00) with a Veggie Patty. Its an interesting combination and on paper, doesn't really sound too good, but I really wanted to try something different. It's sour cream, applesauce, burger, topped with a small potato latke. This thing was so gigantic I had to take the top bun off to eat it! It may not sound too appetizing, but it was surprisingly delicious. Severely messy due to the size, but worth it. It comes with fries, but I substituted for their perfect homemade tater tots. Once again, run to this place! It's really a gem.

Overall we had a really delightful evening at Riverpark despite a few minor things. My parents had a long layover at JFK and came into the city to meet me for dinner. I chose Riverpark because we were dining pretty early and I knew my mom would appreciate the view of the East river. We arrived early for our 6:30 reservations and were seated promptly at a table next to window. As an FYI,most of the window tables are for two and they say they are "first come, first serve" even with a reservation. Such a nice view, you don't even notice the FDR. The inside of the restaurant is great too, sleek and well done. Our server Erin was friendly and attentive.The menu makes great use of the produce grown right outside of the restaurant. For starters, i had the consomee, my mom had the grilled calamari, and my dad had the smoked ricotta gnocchi. All excellent and perfectly portioned to leave room for the entrees! For mains I had the sea bass, my mom had the chicken, and my dad tried the lamb. I really did not like the sea bass itself. The flavor seemed off, even a little fishy. It may have been the white anchovies. I did love the vegetables it was served with though! I would say the chicken was the best out of the three but someone in the kitchen was heavy handed with the salt. We rounded out the meal with a smoked chocolate ganache and caramel popcorn dessert that was new to the menu. The smokiness of the ganache was almost too much for me but overall it was good! I should mention we tried some GREAT wines, I didn't want to stop drinking. My dad said the wine list was well put together and he also noted that the mark up was outrageous. Total bill for the three of us was $500 but we did drink a lot of wine. Not in any rush to go back for dinner but Â I do want to go back to try brunch out on the terrace! The view make this a great place to take fellow New Yorkers or out of town visitors!

This place is freakin fantastic. Â  Came at a prime time pregame hour on a Saturday night. Â Our group of 3 were able to snag a table within 5 minutes of walking in. Â The space of Ward III is great becuase there is space. Â You won't be enhaling the sweat of whoever you are sitting next to, a great advantage to have. Â  Loved the sultry, friendly, classy vibe - the interior decor is a take on the prohibition era (which isn't anything I haven't seen before but it works). Â Our server was attentive, continually refilled our water glasses without us asking. Â The music was on the loud side but not loud enough that you have to scream. Â I loved the music, think Matt Wertz pandora mix. The drinks were fab, I customized my own drink. Â (If you've been to Boston's Drink, this is very similar). Â I told our waitress what I felt like drinking, wintery, gin based, and berries and the concoction came out absolutely wonderful. Â Also, the menu lays out all the adjectives that you can say for your customized drink, gives you ideas of what you might want to drink that day. Definitely a comback joint, definitely heading back here! Great drinks, friendly vibe, and space for my bum to sit.

The food here is awesome! Food is well made - not greasy at all. The menu is small and so the restaurant. They also have a lot of home baked croissant which you should try. It can get crowded during the weekend so get there before noon.

This restaurant has amazing food and service. There were only a few things that made me really regret going here. One of them was the fact that all the employees were dressed upscale casual, except one which had cheetah print yoga paints and a rainbow colored crazy shirt and as a manager of a restaurant that didn't sit well with me. Another thing that really threw me off with that place, just take a look up and you will see at least an inch of dust caked on the ceiling fans.

I went here Friday night with my husband and my sister. Â We had such a good time! Â The waitress, Janet was extremely friendly. She let us know it was going to be a few minutes and she kept coming over to update us on how much longer the wait would be. The service was wonderful, friendly and knowledgeable of the menu items. We had the Fried Calamari appetizer which was very tasty. I ordered the Tagliatelle ai Gamberi (Shrimp, fresh tomato & arugula in a light tomato sauce$11.95). It was excellent. The pasta was cooked perfectly and they did not skimp on the shrimp at all! My husband ordered from the specials, he had the Smoked Salmon and Asparagus in a light cream sauce over Farfalle. He loved it and I had a taste of it and I must admit I was a bit jealous! My sister ordered the Penne Alla Fiorentina (Spinach cream sauce finished with fresh ricotta cheese $8.95). Â It's such a simple dish but don't let that fool you, it was excellent. For dessert we had the Chocolate Mousse and the Tiramisu'. Wonderful choices. We will definitely be back. You can't beat the prices or the service. Plus, the food is AUTHENTIC and that's hard to find these days!!

First time been here. Come cuz of the good review. I ordered the Mango Salad, Loved it, the source and the ingredient all awesome. I love the Stew Duck Noddle Soup as well, the duck is flavorful and very tender. Their Tom Yum soup is a little flat to me. The fish I ordered is not too fresh to me. Other than that everything is great!!! I definitely will go back again, they have lots dishes on the Manuel.

Swung by Little Collin's to pick up lunch on a nice summer day. The small place was bustling with people around 1pm - always a good sign! I went with the Chicken sandwich (~$10) - pricey for a lunch! However, I waited patiently as they filled my order (and a ton of others!) and skipped on my way with sandwich in hand. The bread somehow stayed amazingly toasted yet soft. The chicken was nice, tender, & juicy! And you just can't go wrong with bacon. I'd be interested in coming back to try one of their drinks and another sammie if I'm feeling particularly hungry!

EHHHHHH not such good pizza... very disappointing. I came in to order take-out and got a glimpse of all the mediocre ingredients they used such as store-bought no-name brand mozz cheese. Â Isn't this suppose to be a staple ingredient in pizza? HUH? anyways, I received the pizza- first few bites were "okay" but then it just went downhill... worst part was- awful aftertaste and overpriced. Â Poor tourists...
Great coffee pour over coffee is a must to try. If you are fan of Stumptown coffee you should stop by. Quiche is great also for a snack
Old NY meets whatever is going on here now. The food is simple and authentic and delicious. Brooklyn Heights encapsulated in one restaurant.

Living away from my dear Brooklyn the past three years, I totally missed the boat on Lucali. Was brought here by two buddies last weekend and was properly introduced to this much-hyped place. We made it to the 'second seating' (really, you'll call us back to tell us when a table's free? ok!) and I enjoyed every minute of it. We ordered two pies- one with basil, another with shallots (stupid me- why didn't we just do one pie with two toppings? Is that even allowed?). Both were fantastic, of course. Ambience- nice and cozy. Great seeing the open kitchen and the folks at work. Pizza- delicious. Hype- a bit much. While I'm really glad I went, I honestly don't know if I would make a habit out of this. Good thing my old haunt Abilene was just around the corner to kill the time as we waited for our seat...

What a charming place, with three distinct dining areas, each cuter than the last. Great for either intimate date or larger celebration. The individual areas feel incredibly cozy, unique and romantic. I liked the back room the most--think warm and inviting like grandma's kitchen. Food is good. Decent pasta and fish. Flavorful vegetables. The waiter-recommended after-dinner amaro is a good choice.

First of all- kudos to this place for serving all diets, vegan, veg, carnivoire. Yay! Sometimes as a vegetarian, I want to go somewhere reliably veg with someone who is not veg-- places like this are the perfect compromise. The cheese nachos were... well, just wayyyyy too cheesy. Gave me digestive issues :-/ But hey, they were DELICIOUS! The little green jalapeno salsa? Amazing. Small side of chips w/ salsa Â + sour cream with every order. Veg chili was absolutely fantastic and perfectly hot even after my lengthy stroll to a bench in Central Park. Don't count on being able to dine at this place, very busy and cramped.

Probably my favorite neighborhood spot for a nice dinner. I love how they are tucked away on a residential block in the heart of Boerum Hill. I've been here several times but recently came with my aunt and uncle on a cold windy night. Rucola really hit the spot. The ambiance is warm and inviting and the staff is friendly and helpful. The wait can get long and since they don't take reservations, come on the early side! Food- we started off with some of the vegetable antipasti, specifically the marinated olives, balsamic roasted beets and eggplant caponata. It all went superbly with the great bread they bring to the table. I don't even like eggplant, but they somehow made it so tasty that even I enjoyed it. For the main I got the sardi- a housemade pasta with butternut squash puree, kale and mushrooms. It was excellent. They have tables for small parties and then they have one long table in the center of the restaurant, good for big groups or just family style seating with strangers. Can't wait to go back again soon.
Awesome burnt ends!!!!!
Been there three times already..... in the recent two months, wish i can find more places like this. kind pricey, but definitly worth it. Fish taco there is amazing!!!!!

YUMMY BISON BURGER Where in NYC can you get (Bison, Ostrich, Wild Boar, Elk burgers), Bareburger! I'm partial to things that aren't your normal run of the mill. This place takes the cake on variety of burgers. Not only do they have such a wide variety of meats, you can also choose from an equally wide array of ways to have your burger meat cooked. They also have fried pickles! double yum. I am definitely going to be back! Great for families, groups, service is great, the decor is nice considering it's a burger joint. There wasn't a wait on a saturday afternoon as well.

I worked at Cafe Gitane about 4 years ago when I had a fondness to this petite French-Moroccan cafe. Being my first job in the city, it became my home for a small while and surely I was properly fed from the menu when my shift came to an end. Of course this gave me an opportunity to fill my belly with anything I wanted from the kitchen, though after awhile, I grew tired of the meals eventually. But it had been a long while since I last took a seat on the cold vinyl red banquette with a recent trip to Gitane, and I was somewhat sadly disappointed with the flavors and freshness of my food; that very same fare that once brought comfort to my senses before my evening strolls back home. Â My apologies Gitane, but your place is just "eh", your staff lacks consideration and your couscous was not so tasty afterall. Stick to a morning of cafe creme and baguette or it can even be quite nice to sit on a stool at the countertop bar and rendezvous over rosy kir royals and lillets to start your evening off like a 60s French picture. Keep it simple and bring some cash.
Outstanding sandwiches -- one of the best brisket sandwiches I have ever had. Â Meat was crazy tender and juicy. Â Well worth it.

DON'T WASTE YOUR TIME or MONEY!!! Â You can eat much better in so many less expensive and less crowded, much more civilized restaurants than this place. Â You can also shop at many places with greater variety and much less expensive prices and the food comes from ITALY NOT MADE FOR EATALY!!! Â This place is a ripoff with a number of rude senior staff members . Â It's a tourist trap! Â I ran into a group of Italian tourists who walked around and laughed at the place. Â Anyone who has been to Italy knows better than to believe this place!
I love this restaurant! Fun ambiance and yummy food.You can't go wrong coming here. They also have great drinks!!
keeping my fingers crossed brooklyn ice house stays the way it is now forever, coolest bar in brooklyn (for locals)

I gave this place three stars instead of four because although there are some outstanding dishes, there are also some serious misses; although the busboy was fabulous and just the right amount of attentive, the waiter was huffy and pushy, so this place is a bit skitso. Also, keep in mind that this place is not entirely Argentinean but more fusion-e. The good: Outstanding tuna carpaccio was meaty and a significant portion. Mashed potatoes were very authentic and delicious in the creamy Argentinean style. My friend got the steak salad and she said it was very good, but not amazing, which is what you would expect of an Argentinean restaurant. Very reasonable prices. The blah: Waiter was frazzled and easily annoyed, was a little too pushy about us getting more food and drinks. For desert we had the Charlotte, so kudos to this place on even having that on the menu because it is a very traditional Argentine dessert, but then the thing itself was terrible: cheap ice-cream, cheap chocolate sauce and not too much of it. Just bad. The neutral: Ambience is nice and chill, albeit not really Argentinean. Overall, this place is just fine. Don't think I would go back, but I might order the tuna carpaccio to go.

Wow!! The best Thai food I've had in manhattan! I've been dying to find a place that makes Thai food the way I've had in Thailand and this is the first place in manhattan that makes padthai right (not super sweet). I stumbled on this place with a friend who lives in the area and it seems to have popped up out of nowhere. But we were so glad we found it. The decor is really cool and has a nice grungy look. The chef was this really nice thai woman and took the time to talk to our group. I don't usually write reviews but this place is new and i really want to support them. Go check it out!

I really enjoyed this. There was no wait. Maybe it's also because I went on a Thursday morning, but either way it was good. We got potstickers and then one order of the famous dumplings without crab. Upon first bite, nothing is impressive. It's like... eeehhhhh... just keep eating. It'll grow on you. It's not overly stuffed with stuff and the flavors are really simple and so good. The soup was kinda heavy for me... and is that really soup or just all fat? Yes, the watch your table like hawk. After you put a dumpling on your plate without even eating it, your check is immediatly on your table... That was the case for us, and there were only 2 other parties in the restaurant.
I thought this was great coal oven pizza. Had meatball, mushroom and onion and everything about it was great. I've heard it's not the best pizza in NYC, but it's the best I've had since moving here.

1300+ Reviews and 4.5 stars? I have to think Yelpies are responding to the incredible value here. Yes, it is cheap. Like ridiculously cheap. 5 dumplings for $2 cheap. Great. But who cares if something is cheap if it's not a fun experience or really delicious? We went for a 1pm snack on Sunday, and were jammed inside like sardines. This created a similar experience to renewing your license at the DMV, the Village Halloween Parade, or standing room only Williamsburg concerts. We stalked out a few seats, and the door opening kept hitting me in the back. It was about 20 degrees outside, and 40 degrees inside due to the draft. The dumplings took about 15 minutes to come out, so not only are you waiting uncomfortably, being pushed around, and freezing, but you're dealing with it for an extended period of time. The dumplings themselves? Ok, pretty good. Not the best I've ever had, but formidable. I think I should go back in the summer and eat them on the street. I would probably have a better experience.

Ok, so, I finally had a chance ant went back. this place is great! My first impression of the place was not very good and Â I almost crossed it off my list but then my good friend insisted i try again. and i'm so glad she was right! I ordered something different this time and everything was delicious! big fan, totally coming back :)

My friends and I dropped into Emporio on a whim and actually had a lovely lunch. Â We were seated in the back room, which was lovely with tons of natural light - felt like I was on a garden patio. Â The service was a little slow, but the food was pretty good and they had a great $15 prix fix brunch. Â They also had a cool looking cocktail menu and any place that assumes I'll be drinking during a Saturday lunch is okay by me.

I have been wanting to try this place since seeing it on the food channel. I have to say the fact that they only source ingredients that are within 300 miles of NYC did not stop them from creating such delicious items. The place is rather small and is easily missed if you do not know the actual location or not trying to look for it personally like I was. The ambiance is pretty nice especially combined with the waitress who was socially interactive especially for first timers in the place, she easily pointed out her favorites and why she enjoyed them. I had the winter pig however its better to get it with everything on it which means bacon and fried egg to add flavor and depth to the sandwich. Otherwise, if it was sample plainly, the apple chutney is rather overpowering as it gives a sour and sweet taste which is highly unusual and combined with either basil or rosemary there is an unique taste. I felt it was complete when combined with a fried egg and bacon. Black Tree's beer selection is not to be trifle with as it is quite large and everything is local so it gives another chance to sample what New York has to offer or has been hiding. They change their menus often depending on what is offered and when I visited it on Friday, it was quail and rabbit. I was able to sample the loin and rabbit sliders which were pretty good especially when it was braised in some rabbit stock that made it soft and full of flavor. Black Tree is definitely a place one has to visit just to see how a restaurant with its own prerogative to serve locally source ingredients can do wonders depending on the chef's own imagination and expertise. One can only imagine what type of delicious dishes awaits as the seasons change and ingredients become available. Be sure to keep a lookout for Black Tree. Recommendation: The Winter Pig w/ Fried Egg and Bacon Rabbit Loin and Sliders (If it is still offered) Choose a beer, I do not have a particular favorite yet so maybe next time.
Excellent service!!!! By far the nicest staff I've encountered in a while.The food is incredible...The restaurant decor is so beautiful...I like this place!!

I have eaten many varieties of hand held meat pies from many cultures and these were exceptionally good. The two that I order were the Brasil, filled with ground beef, olives, sauteed onions and potatoes. Wonderful as they were, I'm glad I order 2 as I generously gave 1 away to a future 12 year old gourmet eater. My second was no other , the Viagra as a power burst to my taste buds with a seafood stew blend of shrimp, succulent scallops and crab-meat Â combination to set your taste buds Â in a frenzy. All this for less than $10! Go treat yourself.

Aside from how they keep their glasses turned over on the table make me feel like I'm kissing my table each time I sip water, it was a lovely place to have eggs florentine. Their rosy potatoes were good too, but I wouldn't call them fries. They would though, and they do. They're very friendly too, which is nice and only slightly overbearing. It would be nice if it was bigger, but then it wouldn't be a nook. It would be Open Space. So they get imaginary points for not selling out.

Sesame Pancake #19 - Beef or #20 - bbq pork. COME ON. the dumplings I thought were just okay, but the sesame beef or pork sandwhiches, at under $3 each are hard to beat. Really. The girls behind the counter can be pretty shrill, and the place is usually packed, so plan on taking your food to go.
the place good nothing much. the food delicious, big portions, but a little pricey. we will be back.

Delicious burger!! My husband and I split one and it was perfectly cooked. The kitchen split the burgers in half for us and put fries on two plates so we each had our own plate, which was a nice touch. There were onion rings on top of our burger which were sooo good! It wasn't overly loud in this restaurant either, which was nice. I will be going back!!

Great pizza!!! Â I wanted to give 4.5 stars...but sadly giving 4 stars. Â The best pizza in the Clinton Hill, Fort Greene and Navy Yard areas. They have about every kind of pizza you can imagine. Â Fresh sauce, quality ingredients, thin crust, thick crust, square pies and specialty pies. Even after tasting their garlic knots (which I normally refuse to eat because I just don't like big balls of dough) I was astounded at how good, flavorful and garlicky they were! Â Their salads are super fresh, big portions and homemade dressings. Â Yum! Â I cannot attest to any of their other menu items, but will try some other things on the menu if I can pull myself away from the pizza.

HIGHLY RECOMMEND THEIR JUICES! I was feeling a little under the weather and desperately needed a juice and ginger shot - always my remedy! Unfortunately or Fortunately I wasn't near my apartment so I ran across this juice shop (actually recommended by another friend) and one of the green juices and a ginger shot! Was absolutely great!

First impression.... love it! Hot, attentive bartenders! Sexy, candlelit atmosphere. The drinks are a little expensive but then again I'm from Melbourne Beach, FL where a glass of good wine is $4. My friends moved to NYC a couple months ago and brought me here on my first night in the "big city". We just went for Happy Hour on a Thursday night and I was very impressed. I had no desire to eat there because it seemed a little crowded for that. I saw couples that appeared to be on first dates and kinda felt sorry for them. The food looked good & all but it wasn't the right atmosphere for that. Happy Hour, perfect! I enjoyed it so much we went back on Saturday night but it wasn't as good. We were with a larger group and were seated in the back room. I preferred the view of the hot bartenders at the front bar. We stayed til closing time and as we said adieu, the bartenders handed us girls all chicken noodle soup!!!! The BEST chicken noodle soup I've ever had and for that I give them FIVE STARS. Thanks Milos! Good times!!

L'Artusi never disappoints. I came for brunch and ordered the Carbonara: Pasta cooked al dente served with a perfectly fried sunny side up egg and pancetta. The more traditional brunch items were satisfying as well. My friend shared a bite of her order: blueberry pancakes served with ricotta cheese and topped with real maple syrup. One bite left me unsatisfied and yearning for more. I ended up finishing her leftovers for dessert.
They are selling bootleg liquor that does not come in a box & comes at outrageous prices. Â The sales people are slovenly and mean. Â The wines & liquors are fakes and so are they

Finally checked out this place after hearing so much about it. It has a great atmosphere to just hang out with friends. My favorite sandwich was probably the BBQ pork... the bread is so warm and toasty. I definitely want to go back and try more of their options! Bonus points for awesome, friendly, fun service!

I've been going here for years and it's the best bar and restaurant in PS. Â The food can be pricey to some but it's worth every penny. Â Perfect waiters and the best bartenders in the neighborhood. My only (minor) complaint is that they aren't open as late as they used to be years ago. Â Cold lobster at 3 a.m.? Â Beautiful. Forgot to mention some of what I had here: lobster, crab, steamed clams, duck sandwich, seafood paella, peel and eat shrimp, oyster bar - which is one of the best in the city.

If I was solely rating the food, I would definitely give this place five stars. Â My three girlfriends and I planned for a last minute Sunday brunch. Â I literally live 10 steps away, therefore I told my friends to call me when they get there so that I would walk down. Â Even though the place was pretty empty with maybe 30% of their tables filled, they refused to seat them until our entire party showed up. Â When I showed up, we were still waiting for our fourth friend who got held up, therefore we told the host it would just be three so that we didn't have to wait standing. Â He actually removed the fourth chair from our table which we then had to ask him to put back when our friend showed up exactly 5 minutes later. I mean come on, was that necessary? The waitress was very nice and the food was yummy, however the "we are doing you a favor by allowing you to eat here" attitude needs to go. Oh, and when we payed with four credit cards, instead of splitting the bill evenly, the waitress charged us all different amounts and did not even tell us. I mean, mistakes happen but just a heads up would've been nice. In summary, I can ignore bad attitudes/hospitality when I have delicious food on my plate. Â Will definitely be giving this place another shot.

I came to Lombardi's one day by accident, a friend and i were looking for a place to eat and somehow stumbled onto Lombardi's. I am a obsessed with pizza by the way and for years my fav was grimaldi's (but then they sold it and now its not a solid five stars anymore :( ) Anyway, strolled into Lombardi's and ordered a pie with black oil cured olives and a little fresh garlic...when the pie came it looked delish! the smell was unbelievable and then we tasted it and wow! it was one of those hard to replicate moments. Maybe it was that moment, that night, but my friend and I swear we made love to pizza that night! It was awesome!

Fantastic food, drink, and service. While the place may be so crowded at times that you'll wonder if you'll ever get served, the bartenders make each drink with their undivided attention--worth the wait. Plus, they always serve with a smile. Oh, and kudos on the burger.

1st timer and I'm hooked!!! Â Atmosphere and deco fab!!! Â Food, yummy and small enough to taste it all and still booze it up. Â And the desserts - perfect sampler sizes to have um ALL!!!!! Â  Great place to chill, munch on many different things, drink and enjoy your friends and background music!!!!

I LOVED this place. I felt like I was transported straight to Japan. The flavors and presentation were perfect. I got the Friday special - chirashi sushi donburi. So. Yummy. And for $8.75?? A steal!! I also got a mochi donut dipped in chocolate - after I gobbled it down I promptly bought another one. After eating my Japanese mother's cooking my whole life, I can safely say this is REAL Japanese food and I highly recommend. If I lived closer, my wallet would be in danger because I would go ALL the time.

A great deal for this neighborhood, but the restaurant didn't quite pull it all together. Atmosphere and menu were interesting enough, but the tables & chairs felt a little downmarket. The dishes were all adequately prepared but some were better than others. The artichoke terrine was excellent but the cheese plate was ordinary; the scallops were slightly better than ordinary. Beers were all bottled. Cocktails were interesting and good but not amazing. The crustinas were a bit to crusty. The service was pleasant and reasonably attentive, but even though we were assured the tapas would come out staggered, all of the dishes arrived at once. To their credit our server offered to send them back. The place has potential if they work a few of the bugs out.

I read about Peaches in Time Out mag and told my boyfriend about it. Â Well we headed out and Â went to the wrong Peaches, which we found out were by the same owners. Â We left and headed out to the right Peaches Hothouse and it was closed:( Â Last weekend we tried again and success..it's small but we found our way @ the bar. Â The waitress @ the bar was super friendly and funny..i felt right at home. Â We ordered the shrimp and crispy grits as an appetizer...we really enjoyed it...the sauce that the shrimp came in was so good with rooasted peppers and tomatoes. Â At this point, I couldnt wait for the entreee which of course, was CHICKEN. Â He had mild and I went for HOT..it was HOT but I was able to enjoy the chicken. Â  I had white meat and what I was ecstatic about was the fact that .breast (chicken, that is) was still so tender. Â My side was kale with garlic..it was more soggy then crunchy..i like crunchy but it was still good. Â My boyfriend had chicken and mac and cheese. The mac and cheese is good. Â I'm sure it has some smoked gouda in it...love it! Â They give you three pieces which I wasnt able to finish..doggy bag, of course. Â I also had a drink. Â I forgot the name of the drink but it was interesting. Â It was lemonade, bourbon ( i believe), ginger, mint and blueberries. All in all...the staff was personable and friendly. The food was good, drinks delicious and they will be seeing us again.

I normally don't inhabit crowded bars with only one bathroom, but for Employees Only, I'll make an exception. But before I continue, here is my disclaimer, lest you think I'm a biased yelper. I grew up with Jason, one of the owners. But in all honesty, I love EO. Ever since they opened, the place has been a labor of love and study in details. Their cocktails are divine (nothing tastes like overwrought cough syrup) and the food is outstanding. (Way better than your typical pub grub.) The crowd is diverse... a mix of after work suits, Baby-boomers, Generation X, Generation Y, the under-employed, the over-employed, and the questionably employed. With a garden in the back and a great old-school 20's vibe, EO is at once the neighborhood bar that you truly wish were in your neighborhood and the restaurant you want to eat at every night. Service is super friendly and the place doesn't have a single whiff of elitism. So yeah, I love EO. And if you swing on in, pony up to the bar, and say hi to Jason, I'm sure you'll see what I mean.

Caffe Linda is exactly what I look for in a neighborhood italian spot in NYC. Â It's small, charming, not at all touristy, with good food. The appetizer selection is limited. Â I usually just have a salad and some bread. Â Then I move on to the pastas. Â Most of them are excellent. Â They are cooked al dente so they have some chew. Â They go a little heavy on the sauce, which is crowd pleasing in America, but not strictly authentic. Â There's also a modest wine menu and cocktails. So many of the italian choices in midtown are outrageously expensive for what they are. Â Caffe Linda is reasonable (for NYC). Â You should get away with dinner for 2 for about $50. If you live here, are staying or visiting midtown, Caffe Linda is a terrific choice for Italian.

Ok so I don't understand the hype associated with this place! I went here yesterday and ordered a shawarma and thought it was quite mediocre to say the least. I have definitely had much better shawarma. However i think this place is not famous for its shawarma its most famous for its falafel. My friend ordered the falafel and she loved it! So go here only if you want falafel not if you are in the mood for eating meat! Go toward the famous halal carts if you want to satisfy the meat eater in you!

Really lousy food and I dragged my two New Yorker friends there after seeing the rave reviews. It was completely empty when we got there and when we left, only one other straggler in the restaurant. Never again.

Of the Yakitori's Totto is a good one. Â  Â I brought a few of the uninitiated to this little walk-up around 7pm. Â The place was crowded and we had to wait around a few minutes until the previous party vacated. Â Seated, we were served and attended to quickly. The decor lacking the trappings of the trying-to-be-Japanese, is clean, and muted in a modern way. Â  Â We ordered about 10 dishes to share among 5, and added to the order as desired. Â The service was good, and the lady's advice on dishes was great. Â The food was excellent. Â For the price, the fare was interesting, tasty, Â and fresh. Â (Get the Tuna with Avocado if they still have it, it's amazing) Â All in all, a memorable meal.

First time having Filipino food, and I loved it! My friends and I came to the restaurant 15 minutes after our reservation but the seating hostess was kind enough to still seat us four. We immediately were greeted by a very knowledgeable waitress, who helped us pick out our food and even taught us how to cut the Bistec with the fork and spoon ( no knife? oh snap! Friend #2 and I kept cutting the bistec with the prescribed method, but #1 got lazy and used a knife. Or maybe I think she just really enjoyed the steak that she gave up and went with the knife to get as much food in as possible because it was Oh.so.good. What can I say, we were newbies). Two of my friends, as well as myself, ordered the Bistec.As the Bistec comes with rice, Friend #2 ordered white rice, while Â Friend #1 ( it was her birthday!) and I split a large garlic rice ($1 additional for each our plates) with our Bistec. The garlic rice was simply DIVINE. The garlic is not at all strong, but is a slight aftertaste to this fluffy rice. The bistec marinade was not too sweet, and not at all overpowering, and the meat was beautifully tender. It is a LOT OF MEAT for the price! The onions were surprisingly really yummy too as they soaked up a lot of the marinade! Friend #3 had the fried chicken and waffle. She mentioned that the Filipino Pride Chicken 'n' Ube Waffle Â fried chicken was nothing spectacular, but the "fishy spread" on the waffle made the waffle taste amazing. BTW, its $21, not $17. A lot of food, a great night, and great attention in a cute ( yet overly hipster clientele and staff, fo sho) Â setting made this catch up night with friends great. Did I mention they gave us fried chicken skins ( not something I was used to, but tasted good!) for the table while we waited,free of charge? And their Tagalog word of the day, and the homey decor with family pictures and other Filipino knick-kacks were great convo starters. A fabulous tiny place! FYI: only cash is accepted - there is a small dessert list ( only two desserts, which both had a lot of coconut) -the place is pretty tiny - reserve in advance. We came in on a Monday night, and it was almost full for a Monday night.

We tried Zizi for the first time last night and we felt like we were being treated to a beautiful home cooked Middle Eastern meal prepared to order and served by friends. The space is super cozy, cool but not overdone. The menu is really intriguing -- we wanted to try everything and we can, because the prices are super affordable. We've certainly eaten our share of falafel, schwarma and pita but everything we ate had an unusual, fresh and delicate twist. Stars of the night -- the gravlax with lightly fried cauliflower, homemade pita with tahini spread, and falafel. Ask for the homemade hot sauce. It's made with harissa, smoked paprika, and a dash of sriracha and it's addictive! I'm super excited someone has created a beautiful place where we can experience real Middle Eastern food. It's time falafel moved beyond street vendors. We can't wait to go back!

I loved jacobs pickles but the other night the service wasn't there. They were rude at the hostess table and rushed us out. I went to some other spots around there and decided I wanted fried Oreos. When I went to pick them up I was short changed by 10 dollars and the hostess argued with me so I just left. I'm sad this happened at one of my go tos.

Crabs heaped on a platter doused in Old Bay are plopped down on our newspaper covered table. We put on our bibs and proceed to crack, pull, tear our way into the pile. It must have taken an hour and a half to work our way through the first platter of all you can eat crab. When the waiter came back and asked Â  us if we were ready for the second platter. We surrendered.
Great atmosphere good pizza didn't love the calzone just to much cheese for me Would definitely go back

Another raving review about this place - this is the best spot in the wintertime to warm up with some delicious soups. They have some great vegetarian ones - apple butternut squash, black bean, and one I just discovered the other day which was a wonderful green chili with corn. They rotate the menu, but with over 20 different soups to choose from you're sure to find something. Another reviewer commented that the fruit is subpar, which I agree happens on occasion, and the bread is only good for dipping not for eating by itself - but with the price of $4 for a small soup, bread, and fruit you really can't complain. The line may look long but moves fast. Sometimes they run out of a few of the more popular soups if you show up too late in the afternoon. I tried to swing by here one Satuday because I happened to be in the area, but it was closed so I think it's a place specifically catering to the workplace lunch rush. There is no indoor seating - takeout only.

I still love this place. Lately, whenever I go with a friend, we just get two unda chicken rolls and two achari paneer rolls and split them. If you can handle it, tell them to make it "spicy" and put extra onions in the achari paneer roll (otherwise you may find it dry). But whenever I make the chicken roll "extra spicy," it comes out WAYY to spicy. So I wouldn't recommend getting the chicken rolls "extra spicy."

The best Colombian restaurant in Brooklyn, the service is great, the food is amazing and the drinks are delicious!! My favorite dish is bandeja Paisa, its just perfect at Bogota Bistro!!! Will be coming back very soon!!
Can't go wrong with the chives and pork dumplings. Two dollars worth can feed 3 people plenty. Delicious!
Took my family and friends last m ok nth. The food was really bad. The service wasn't good. I wouldn't recommend this place.

The Thirsty Koala!? Intrigued by the name? You should be! This Australian newcomer to the Astoria neighborhood lives up to it's fun name by providing tasty Australian food, reasonable prices, and even a Koala beer. It's not often you see Kangaroo on the menu. Here you can get kangaroo a steak and even burgers. Â If you are like myself and not into eating "Skippy the Bush Kangaroo", the Mahi tacos are incredible. Initially I thought I needed to order more food, because 2 tacos do not sound very filling, but these tacos are loaded. Save a bit of room for dessert, because the pavlova is a must try. The only thing missing is more koalas. While they have the cuddly creatures near the bathroom. I would love to see more koala themed things around the restaurant. I will definitely return.

We had a 9:00 reservation, so by that time we were all very hungry. Â We sat down and ordered 10 items or more. Â I was impressed by the items ordered from their "specials" menu. Â From their main menu, the agedashi tofu and the fried mash potato donuts were awesome. Â We ordered hot sake, medium priced, and it was really good. Â Best sake I've had, granted I haven't had much. Â We had dessert special which was mango pudding, very good. Â Overall seems like a really good restaurant for authentic non-sushi Japanese food.
Everything is absolutely divine. Â I don't think there is anything that I don't love to buy and eat....generally all on the same day!

My family and I just went there for Sunday Brunch a couple of weeks ago and I gotta say that we all LOVED the food. I ordered the burger (wasn't in the mood for eggs) but my sister in law ordered the Eggs Florentine and they were perfectly poached. The Mornay sauce was to die for! My cousin ordered the Steak Sandwich and it was unbelievable! The service was top notch, everyone was very accommodating, they even deducted $5 off from the order when I checked in thru Yelp! OH and the Bloody Marys were absolutely amazing! :)
Great burger and be sure to grab a beer while you wait in line for a table.

I love this restaurant. I went for my birthday in June and liked it so much that my boyfriend and I went back for our anniversary. Â  The food is fantastic, but it is the service that makes me want to go back again and again. Â The waiters are knowledgeable, charming and go out of their way to make your experience special. Â It was hard to remember all of the specials but the waiter was very patient with repeating them and also checked with the kitchen multiple times about ingredients because of my food allergies. We split the zucchini flower appetizer (yummy!) and then I got the risotto with pears and gorgonzola Â cheese (warning: this is extremely heavy and you'll have definitely have leftovers). My boyfriend got one of the pasta specials (homemade linguine with shrimp) and enjoyed it. Â  It's not cheap -- total with tip came to $150 with cappuccino for me and a mid-range bottle of wine (no desserts) but definitely worth it..

We were pleasantly surprised to have happened onto this little Thai restaurant! Â The decor was small but exquisite. Â The food was good and authentic! Â The best Thai iced tea ever! Â All the soup noodles used a different type of noodle, which was quite refreshing. Â The duck noodles were by far the best! Â Definitely will go again whenever I'm in town!

i've only been here for brunch. 3 out of 5 times i eat here it's been good so 3 stars out of 5. last time, the rib hash was great, today i had the BLT and it was nasty. the service is great but be careful what you order.

E have the cookbook, so went in with high expectations. Â Atmosphere was great, staff was friendly and responsive. Â The food? Â Well, the escarole and canellini bean soup was a little bland, as was the sauce on the eggplant. Â The mushroom and truffle oil croustade was great. Â Both entrees, the cavatelli with hot sausage and the house made linguini with lava beans were ok (the hot sausage was terrific). Â In short, we didn't get the flavor experience we were hoping for, but are glad we tried it.

Heaven. Try the breadsticks - yes gluten-free breadsticks - and you'll understand. Obviously, their risotto selection is robust and delicious. The place is a wee-bit small. My brother astutely commented that it was filled with "like, 90% skinny white chicks..." Regardless, you must try the breadsticks.

A perfect college starving student place to eat. Deliciously hot fries served in a paper cone and tons of flavored dips and sauces to choose from. I've spent many nights out on a stoop next to the place (as the restaurant itself is really crowded and the splashing oil from the deep fryer frankly kind of scares me) inhaling fries, literally sucking in air as I eat because they're scalding my tongue. Lots of the dips are tasty, and you're allowed to try some. I like the sweet mango chutney mayo, the wasabi, peanut satay, and curry ketchup. I get dragged here pretty much every time my sister is in town because she loves this place so much. This place definitely complements a night of beers very well.
very good food and speed, entertaining waiters

Great! There were 5 of us... we all got entrees, plus four appetizers to share, plus drank at least 2 beers each... and our bill was just barely over $100! What? Amazing. Our server was nice, the food came out super fast, and it was delicious. The portion sizes are so generous... we could hardly finish everything (but we did, don't worry).
Everything has already been said. Just go there early and try it!

Portions are good. The beef cubes and the spicy pho are above average. Don't order the spicy pho expecting a spicy broth because it is not spicy. Just add Sriacha to make it spicy. It is good for NYC but below average compared to orange country pho places.

I loved this place. I think my bf would have give 4 stars but my meal hands down 5. Â The pork chop was UNREAL. Holy crap - I may say it was one of the best pork chops I have ever eaten - EVER. Â The tempura green beans were delicious - and they had a special appetizer of asparagus with fresh grated parmasean - holy crow that was delicious. The desert - this pistachio semi freddo was pardon my language fucking amazing. My bf ordered the eggplant parm - it was a little on the small side for him and not as good as the pork chop - it was good though just not as good as it gets. The waiter was awesome - so knowledgeable attentive and nice. Â Overall a great meal and I would def go back even without my BBE code.
Best dumplings ever! Make sure to bring a cooler and buy the frozen ones to take home! It's 50 for 9 bucks!

The pizzas we had here were really delicious. Â We had a margarita pizza and also a sausage pizza. Â The salads were sizable and tasty and our server was great. Â The wine selection was really nice, too. Â After eating so many midnight slices this was some real quality stuff. Â Will be coming here again the next time I am back in town.

The price is right at this quaint SoHo Italian spot on Prince. Took friends here on a saturday night (Granted was snowing lightly) and there was luckilly seating available, all though by 8 pm it was full. The decor is relatively no frills but that didnt bother me. The waiter was attentive and funny, suggesting items off the menu (and playfully coercing our one friend to get a peroni beer after the other 3 of us ordered). We split the green salad and Crostini Pomodoro as an appetizer, and the Crostini was toasted nicely on the bread with the tomatoes on and mozzarella. Â For my entree I chose the Fusilli Della Linda, and it was seasoned just right with the diced chicken and zucchini. I ended up splitting with my brother a Chocolate Mousse and it for sure hit the spot. I dont think anything on the menu was over $16 dollars, yet the food tasted great and was authentic. I heard they have a good lunch special here, that may be my next plan of attack. Yet another solid itailan place added to my lexicon to return to in lower manhattan.

If I could I would give this place 3 Â 1/2 stars but I felt nice so I rounded up. Overall great pizza, slightly fancier than your typical pizza joint. I came here for a work lunch and found my self devouring at least 5 slices. I think my boss had at least 8 slices! Service was good and pizza came out fairly quickly. Â We ordered the old fashion pizza with pepperoni and mushrooms. Yum!

Had the Soho Square and felt let down by all the hype. The dough was unique and intriguing since it was thick and doughy but at the same time not heavy or dense. The toppings however were very ordinary- just your run of the mill tomato sauce and melted cheese.

It's weird... whenever I'm thinking of brunch places in Williamsburg, Cubana Social comes to mind, but I'm not excited. And I think it's because when I picture it, it's normally not that crowded/busy on a weekend morning. So it must not be awesome, right? Wrong. I'm always wrong. And reminded why I love it here. The food is delicious. And while I *do* think that the service is hit or miss & generally pretty slow, as long as you're not in a rush, who cares? Really cool space. Good food. Nice staff. I've never had a wait. Check it out.

How was this place been around for years, and I'm only now discovering it? Made a reservation via OpenTable for the same day and got in with no problem. Ended up sitting at the bar with a girlfriend and having a leisurely meal. We started with a couple cocktails and snacks, and had immediate and friendly service from the bartender (aside: I think her name was Allison). The menus change daily, and I appreciate the open floor plan of the kitchen and it's cleanliness! Started with an M'Peared Martini and a Dewar's and Cherry cocktail, Steak Skewers, Bruschetta with figs, and Radishes with Butter. Everything is done extremely well, beautifully, and thoughtfully. The placement of the plates, the decor of the restaurant, everything seems to be thought through. For the actual meal, we shared a fantastically light and affordable bottle of Busey Pinot Noir ($48) and had Rotisserie Chicken. This simple bird did not disappoint, accompanied by market fresh variety of cauliflower, sweet potatoes, and carrots. To close we had glasses of sparkling Rose with a Cheesecake Panna Cotta that was accompanied by Graham Cracker crumbles and soaked cranberries. The end of a perfect meal. I'll definitely be back, and can't wait to try it for brunch!

Such a fan of this place! The gnocchi is the best I've ever had, so so light with a beautiful creamy sauce. My partner had the pasta with prawns and zucchini, perfectly cooked pasta! We also had the eggplant with ricotta and spinach with a tomato sauce - divine! Would love to come again!

Taste GREAT Malaysian food! Â I've had the Singapore Kari Laksa (fish curry soup with noodles) a few times, and it's been fantastic. Â The Roti canai that they served is as good (or better) than any roti I've had in india. Â One of my friends got a simple ginger chicken dish with white rice that also turned out to be incredibly flavorful and memorable. Â The portions are large, the prices are cheap, and the staff is fairly friendly. Â Even if you have no idea what to get, it seems like you can't go wrong here. Â Amazing!

I found this cafe restaurant three weeks ago and have been here more than 7 times! Guess this place breaks my record in NYC!!! I tried CC' egg wrap, house wrap, three soups and one sandwiches...everything is amazing. Hummus is the best I have ever tried so far! they also got good wine & desert! You have to try the carrot cake!!! Chef Thomas(sorry if I spell wrong) prepares food with his heart and trust me you'll feel it. Place is cozy, service is excellent, price is reasonable. I am leaving New York in a month. This is my first yelp review and maybe the last. I will definitely miss the food here.

I came here with my boyfriend for valentine's day dinner. We both love breakfast for dinner and he had heard about the pancakes. All I can say is amazing. Absolutely amazing. The mini biscuits you get when you sit down are delicious and crumbly, just as biscuits should be. All sorts of food envy and delicious smells wafting around. We decided to each get our own entrees and then share the pancakes. I ordered huevos rancheros and my boyfriend ordered eggs benedict. Delicious. I had no problem cleaning my plate. And the pancakes. The pancakes! We ordered the fresh coconut pancakes. Light fluffy pancakes with shredded coconut and caramelized pineapple with warm maple butter for dipping. OMG. Food so good it will make you want to slap your mama. Truth. The only downside, IMO, is that the tables are pretty close together. You can pick off your neighbors plate if you want to. There is literally no space. The place is quite small. But the food is so good that it. Just. Does not. Matter.

My boyfriend I eat here regularly and by "regularly" I mean at least once a week. No joke. I've had everything on the menu at this point and then some. Everything is enjoyable. Right now they have a scallops and sweetbreads dish that is delicious. My boyfriend always gets the burger and the kale salad. Both are two of my favorite dishes on the menu as well. The fried chicken is also really good and a menu staple. I like the Redhead Fizz cocktail but for a regular night's dinner I get a red wine by the glass and all of those options are well priced and very good. If you go during the middle of the week you usually don't have to wait long for a table for two! All in all, it's tough to beat this place on value plus great food!

The wait here is crazy. Â I've been here for dinner two times after 11pm and the wait is still an hour. Â It's totally worth it though! Â  I always get the burger with the rosemary fries (the best!) but I make whoever I'm with get something more adventurous. Â They do such a great job making unusual Â ingredients delicious! Â The last time we started with a nettle pesto and goat cheese bruschette - totally different but so tasty. Â My friend had the pig's ear stuffed with sausage and sweet breads. Â Sounds weird but it was so good and the textures actually worked really well together, a little chewy and crispy but soft on the inside.
