BEST CLASSIC SQUARE PIZZA EVERRR!! but, with a little classy twist -- crispy crust, with a fluffy bed of cheese and a vibrant red blanket of tomato sauce ON TOP. and just as a disclaimer: the sauce is far beyond from anything like marinara. i'm truly grateful that L&B is a mere 5-minute drive from my bf's place as it has become a frequent option for lunch/dinner. i don't even have to call ahead of time, because the turnover is so high. the pies are always guaranteed fresh and steaming hot. the crustless center squares are the perfect slice of geometric food heaven. just writing about it puts me on cloud nine...

This place is my friend's favourite ramen joint in NYC, and she took me here when we hung out. We went a little early so we could get a reservation in; it was a 45 minute wait but in East Village there's loads to browse around so waiting was no issue. When we were seated, I was already in love with the atmosphere! Had a bar seat, which I was actually okay with, seeing the chefs make food is one of the great things about sitting at the bar. I ordered the hirata buns (with pork) for an appetizer as per suggestion of my friend, and was SO impressed. The sauce mixed with the wonderfully tender pork and the pillowy bun was beyond my expectations. I've never had anything that good to date. Also ordered the Calpico High (calpis + shochu) as a drink, great stuff. When it came time to order ramen, I got the Akamaru Modern. Service was fast, the ramen came out in less than 10 minutes. The presentation of the ramen was beautiful, I was delighted with the speed + look of the food, so I was definitely holding the ramen to be good--or great, as my friend kept insisting. It was THE BEST ramen I've ever had. I've gone to many ramen joints in Japan, Taiwan, Arizona, and California, and Ippudo NY definitely topped them all. The broth wasn't too spicy, it was just enough to be absorbed into the noodles for the great chashu flavour I was craving. The noodles were chewy, and definitely added a nice texture to the rest of the items. I saved the pork for last, and it was definitely the highlight. Perfectly soft, well-rendered pork that melts in your mouth--I had never been so happy with a meal. Definitely left stuffed, I'd do anything just to go through this experience again. I still dream of it now. I passed by a Ippudo Ramen in TW and JP months after coming back from NYC, but never had the chance to stop inside and have another bowl, but I trust Ippudo NY to be the best.

The gal and I had a very odd eating experience here just last night... There were a lot of things that could have been improved: 1. Both her tomato-mozzerella salad and my haricot vert salad were pretty unquestionably overdressed. As in, too much dressing. 2. We sat another 20-30 minutes awaiting our main course without having our appetizer plates cleared and without receiving the extra bread we asked for. 3. We were being gawked at by the clientele there. Yes, I'm 6'8", but the customers were on the older side and were intrigued by our youth, I think. Also, it may have been that we actually adhered to the BYOB policy rather than the BYOWine which everyone else was conforming to. That is, we brought a growler and the whole restaurant's reaction was: "OMGZ, WHAT IZ THIS BROWN JUG THINGS?!?!?!?!" Except they were too old to know what "OMG" might have stood for. 4. 144 Union St.? Guys, you're on fucking Hicks. Come to terms with it. That said, the entrees were pretty delicious, but nothing superlative for what we were paying. The appetizer quality, plus all these nagging side problems is more than enough to lower it to three stars though.

We had our work holiday party here, and at one point my boss promised the manager that they'd good a lot of good buzz on Yelp between Alli K., Lily T., & myself. So if my boss says it's happening, I better do it, huh? I could not have enjoyed the experience at Green Table more. I'll let Alli K.- our party planner- talk about how it was to work with them, since I wouldn't have any idea. But it's a charming little space- very rustic looking and warm. And the food was absolutely delicious- bruschetta, braised short ribs, steamed kale, and a fabulous chocolate cake. Wonderful wines as well. This place made for an excellent party location, but it will certainly have to make for an excellent lunch or dinner sometime too- it was too yummy to have just once!

I remember my first time. Â Walking by. Â Smell wafting. Â I walked in, slightly nervous. Â It seemed like I was an outsider here. Â People seemed to be waiting, almost indifferent to the long wait--maybe the small space prevents anxiety-inducing pacing (chinese window anyone?). Â  I've become a regular. Â I've realized the nature of patience present at the Islands is a cordial slow burn...the anticipation is part of the experience. Â  I order the same thing every time. Â I've had to limit my weekly jerk chicken quota, and sometimes, I think a 12-step program will be the only thing to save me...but it's hard to stop when my jerk chicken fantasies make salivating during work Â feel so right.

We went to dinner here for my mother's birthday on July 27, 2013. The service was excellent and the food was out of this world. Â Our waitress was so attentive and helpful. Â  My mom raved about her martini, apparently it was the best tasting martini she has ever had. The bartender is some kind of magician with mixology. Â For appetizer we shared mozzarella cheese wrapped in prosciutto and toasted. Â We also shared scallops. Â Both were amazing. Â Everyone loved their main courses as well. Â We got duck, risotto, gnocchi, and a crepe with seafood medley. Â So delicious. Â Everything was great and we will definitely return. Â Next time we will save room for dessert.

This restaurant is incredibly quaint and charming. Space is very tight and is usually packed, which makes for an energetic atmosphere! Expect waits, unless you're lucky. This place is very popular. Came here for brunch and was pleased with their fare. Â I appreciated how light and healthy their food was in comparison with other brunch places. Ordered their roasted artichoke provencal, which made me feel like I was eating a meal in France. Husband ordered the eggs benedict with smoked salmon - awesome! Prices are a bit above average, but I do think you get what you pay for. Next time I would like to try their mimosas!

We were here for the paella event. Â Great food, service and people. Â We like to have a bite here then shop at the store and around the neighborhood before heading to a park to take a nap. Â That's our Sunday ritual. Â A+

We made a trip out to here on a Sunday afternoon at the end of June. Of course, they had no fresh lobster!! Â How could you not be prepared for a summer weekend for customers making a trip to the far reaches of Brooklyn for some fresh lobster, when that's just the business you are in?? We ended up with lobster roles, which for the price were about 1/4 the size we would have eaten in Cape Cod or anywhere else in New England. Â The prices were outrageous. It's one thing paying those prices for Lobster in midtown or TriBeCa, but on the far corner of Red Hook, it's a bit outrageous. Presumably it's their opportunity cost of selling some sucker off the eps treat a lobster roll or selling wholesale to the latest TriBeCa hotspot. My recommendation, is stay away. Your better off just getting the lobster from your local eatery. Â Although it tasted fine (hence two stars not one) I didn't see the value.

This place nails it. Â I can't think of a better restaurant in a 10 min radius. Â Perfect location for a wine bar and they do it very well. One drawback is that its so awesome and there is no other legitimate option around so its PACKED all the time. Â  Thats a good problem to have I think. Â  Food is fantastic but standard and the service is great, just keep in mind this place will be PACKED.
The cheapest, best dumplings. Â Don't forget to try the sesame sandwiches though; also pretty dang A+. Â I've been going here forever, it seems like.
Love this place! We had incredible service here, cheap prices, and tasty food. I recommend the grilled calamari.

Just like the other reviewers - decent sushi, byob for first bottle of wine, free edamame if you check in. Â I also thought the service was really nice and the atmosphere was relaxed.if you are curious, we also ordered the deep fried cheesecake with green tea ice-cream. Â So not good for you but isn't that what dessert is all about? Â Also, just a note that the dessert is $6 and not $5 like it says on the menu. we didn't bother saying anything though because it already felt like quite the deal with the BYOB and free app! I will be back.
Believe the hype.

Always a winner every time I go! Wine list is very cool, they have a huge tome that shows the map and region of each variety. Open kitchen where you can sit at the chef's counter to watch them prepare your food, although my favorite area to sit is the second floor as it is more spacious and has natural light from the skylight. Food is amazing - homemade pasta dishes and seafood is highly recommended. Recommended appetizers/crudos: beef carpaccio, hamachi, scallops; Pasta: garganelli, orecchiette; Pesce: grilled octopus; Carne: grilled quail sooo good. Great for work events, romantic for dates, fun for groups, all around perfect!

my favorite date spot in all of brooklyn. it's romantic, the food never disappoints, the place is really well put together, and the wine is purty tasty. also, you might be surprised to hear some classic jazz and bluegrass during the week if you catch it at just the right time. but if you wait that long (ie prime dinner time), be prepared to stand for awhile! try the ribs and mashed potatoes. yummy!

One thing I would HIGHLY recommend - the young coconut soup! Â I've never had ANYTHING quite like it and it was AMAZING!!!The coconut was almost noodle-y in texture. Â It was a special on the menu... I hope next time I go they have it. One thing I would NOT recommend - the pad thai. Â I don't know, maybe I'm just an ignorant white person who has always eaten the Americanized version of pad thai so the real deal did not suit my sensibilities, but this just tasted slightly gross to me after maybe the third bite or so. Â It was very sweet and almost tasted ketchupy to me.
yummy!

I've been waiting for this place to open up after NYT review, so I decided to try on a Friday night right after work (only two stations away from the office!). It was raining and yelp map totally screwed me up in terms of locating this place, but I got there and the place was packed only two weeks into its opening. I was told the wait was about 1.5hr and I was depressed. Then 20 minutes into the wait, the whole restaurant closed down because the broth for the night was not good - whawhat? Yeah..but what was good about the shutdown was that they guaranteed a seat for me and my friend the following night for our wait. So my adventure began again on Saturday night from Jersey City (home). Surprisingly, given that I had to cross two rivers, it only took about 45min to get there via Path to 33rd then E at W4th St. So not bad. My friend and I got there exactly at 5:30pm for the opening. It was still raining that night, but there were a good line of people already at the door. I was so glad that I didn't have to wait again. I wanted to sit at the bar and see where the magic happens and it was an excellent choice. We started with the mussels and even though it looks pretty plain - it was soooo damn good. It was the freshest mussels I've eaten with broth that had depth. It just felt like warm savory ocean floating in my mouth, amazing! I know mostly people have uni and yeah uni is great, but this was way more interesting in the way they elevated a cheap shellfish like mussels to this level of goodness! We both ordered the Mu Ramen and gulped down in 15 minutes bc it was so delicious. It's oxtail based soup so it tastes like korean sulungtang but with more savory scrumptious to it. The broth has depth as it was probably boiled down for hours to get the right flavors. And they add the cucumbers in the broth that makes it a clean aftertaste. It's a totally different kind of ramen experience that makes you wonder about the flavor. It was seasoned absolutely perfectly without even being able to think that it's salty. If your idea of a good ramen is the salty, fatty broth with addictive umami taste (kinda like junk food taste which I do crave sometimes), this ramen may not be for you, but if you are a person who appreciates new ramen experience, this is the bowl to have! We also ordered the stuffed chicken appetizer but that was just okay. The chicken was super moist and was so impressed given that it was piping hot, but the flavors weren't quite a knockout like the mussels and the ramen. Delicious nonetheless! Overall, a very enlightening experience and I appreciated their gracious service and flavors!

This may shock some people but Laduree's macarons were not the best macarons I've ever eaten in NY. They were good, but not good enough for me to take a trip out of my way then to wait in line for 30 minutes before finally getting in my order.

A group of us went to eat at this place and we were not aware that you needed to make reservations to eat brunch since most all places in Williamsburg do not take reservations at brunch time. Â The person managing the place that day was not the least bit accomodating to us and treated us as he could not be bothered. Â It seemed like we were annoying him with wanting support his business. Â I wonder if the owneres of the place know that this is happening or do they not care when hiring. Â He did not offer to put our name on the list. Â We had to ask him to place our name on the list and he seemed to not want to do it. Â So we all left and went to Walters Food which treated us like paying customers. Â I have heard from several friends that the food might be good but the service is not great or friendly. I would even go as far as saying that they rather cater to a specific race in their establishment but can't be sure. Â I hope they make changes to their staff sooner rather than later because eventually it will affect their business.

Came here on a Wednesday night around 6pm and was seated right away. We just missed the crowd because by 630pm-7pm there was quite a wait. First off, the service was just fine. Not great. Our waitress did the basics fine but no real "engagement" from her. My friend ordered the fish tacos, and they were huge. She said they were good but nothing fantastic. I ordered the scallops, and they were fine but again nothing fantastic. The scallops were on a bed of pureed peas. The pureed peas were good but it was a ton of pureed peas and only 3 scallops. Long story short, with all the great places in NYC i don't want to waste a night out on a mediocre place, which is what I'd rate Friedman's.

This place is a little overrated in my opinion, but the Sangria is great! Reminds me of a Cuban place in San Francisco. The empanadas that they make are quite large. My friend and I tried the following: Viagra - just lots of seafood in it, but not that well seasoned Cuban - yum! Philly Cheesesteak - it wasn't as bad as I expected it would be The plantain chips were great, and the guacamole was homemade. Because the guacamole is homemade, there are lots of variations to it. The people next to us had a lot of cilantro and tomatoes in their guacamole, and ours well let's just say was mostly avocado. Regardless though, the plantain chips and guacamole with the sangria were the highlights of this place. Empanadas were a little disappointing.
Best lobster roll in NYC by far! Thank goodness they are open again after Sandy. Get out and show your support Â for this awesome Red Hook restaurant.

I've been living downtown in the Financial District for over a year now and Blue Spoon coffee has been my perfect go to coffee place. They brew good coffee and during the weekdays you can get sandwiches, soup, or salad (although I would opt for the soup they always have delicious flavors and variety) The only red flag I throw is the credit card minimum of $4.00...makes it tough to get coffee on the go if you don't have cash.

The fried pork chops here are amazing. I came for brunch with a new friend and her mother, since I am without a reason to celebrate mother's day in NY...mine is on the west coast. I have walked past several times, but it seems like the type of place you don't go to alone. Â Now that I am meeting more people in the area, I will have more people to come back to this yummy spot again. And now that I have been inside, I see that I can eat alone at the bar, which isn't so daunting.

This place is amazing. Â Seems like there would be more options for great ingredients, healthy, vegan and gluten free options in NYC. Â This place knows what it is doing in that arena, and it does not taste like health food. Â  The drawback of course, is how expensive it is. Â However, you are paying for what you get, which is high quality, healthy food. Â And that is something I am worth investing in- but I wish there were some way to bring down the price to make it less of a splurge

Have I not reviewed Casa Mono, the first and last place where I will ever try a fried sardine? Â Ugh, I just gagged a little thinking about it. Â If you think you ever want to try fried sardines, either do it here or on the Portuguese coast. Â It's a bit cheaper to do it here, once you factor in airfare. Â Well, let me tell you, these aren't just any sardines. Â They are MASSIVE sardines. Â Big, fat sardines that taste like fish. Â I know, what the hell was I expecting? Â I took a bite and spit it out. Â Into my napkin. Â On a date. Â Yup. Â That's the kind of girl I am. Â  Moving on. Â Pumpkin and Goat Cheese Croquetas. Â Yeah, you've just got to get them, especially in the fall. Â I love pumpkin. Â A hit. Â Rabbit three ways (at waiter's recommendation), awesome. Â Crispy pork belly, ohhhhh melty porky salty goodness (and the sunchokes nom nom nom). Â  Steak with some onion marmalade business. Â  It's teensy-tiny, and there's normally a wait, but hotel concierge was able to secure us a very, very tight spot. Â I don't understand the table--it was low enough (b/c it has a shelf on which you may store your purse)--to hit my knees. Â My 6 foot tall date looked like he was sitting at a kindergarten table. Â  Amazing wine list, dark woody atmosphere, lively kitchen and staff. Â  A must-try, but I don't know if I'll be back. Â It wasn't overwhelmingly amazing, even though my mouth is watering a wee bit.
Over priced pizza not worth the wait. Better pizza in other places in Brooklyn.
Great pizza, Great location, Great Staff!! This is one of the best pizza places I have ever been to.
Classy restautant with style and history. Very nice food and wonderful wine selection. Prices are not to high and deffinately worth.

A wonderful addition to the LES!! My wife and I enjoyed a delicious dinner at this beautifully renovated space on Rivington St. Each dish (octopus, cauliflower salad, collard greens and a special pasta) was loving prepared and crafted (we sat at the bar and watched the chefs prepare each one) The staff was congenial, helpful and made for a fun evening! I am sure we will be back soon, even from Brooklyn!!

If you haven't been to Mamoun's you haven't been to NYC. Â Truly, the savior of all the late nights when you had a few drinks and just need that falafel and goodies stuffed pita. Â That first bite proves me right every time. Â Hilarious and amusing looking crowd, too. Â Come, check it out.

This place was great! I would highly recommend to anyone visiting the Hell's Kitchen area of New York City visit this restaurant. The food was amazing the atmosphere was great and the staff was very friendly treat yourself and check it out!

WOW. This place is just WOW. Â We came here early Sat evening and it was surprisingly not packed at all. They have $12 happy hour that comes with 6 oysters and a beer. The oysters were sweet and fresh and slurp-worth. The Spanish mackerel over a bed of greens was cooked nicely, not dry. The fettucine with clams was just so delish! I loved it. I thought the portions were just right. I would definitely come back for more fresh seafood.

Much shorter line this time, although my palpable excitement at being able to eat lamb-rice made the queue seem like the 4 hours I once waited as a younger man for the Batman Ride when it first came out at Six Flags Magic Mountain. Â Bad analogy, I know... I think I could eat this everyday... Â it's just a perfect blend of savory, spicy, and oily... Â with equal parts groin-grabbingly good ground lamb with heavily spiced rice, and the white and red sauce really push it over the edge. Â No fist bump from the worker this time I'm afraid, as I remember the trials and tribulations I had from the last time I slathered my plate with "the red". Â  Strangely enough, leftovers were even tastier the next morning in my hotel room. Â God, this food is so good.
Get anything here, it's the healthiest it can get. Food, service - both awesome. Can I give 10 stars?

I fear about rating this place too highly as I don't want too many people to know how wonderful it is! Â Cosy and delightful setting, lovely well-cooked and presented food. Eat at the bar for a really laid back but delicious experience.

It was solid, and I'm glad I finally went. First, they had a really awesome Chardonnay on the wine list (yes, I know, why am I ordering Chard at an Italian restaurant? Â Answer: I wanted a full bodied, oakey white). Â However, after the Chardonnay our table switched to Chianti to have with our pastas and mains. We decided to get a bunch of apps. Â And I got the short ribs for myself. Â They were delish! Â I also tried some of the polenta, which was by far one of richest, creamiest polentas I've had in a while. We also decided to share a bunch of the pastas. Â We Â got the farfalle, spaghetti, duck & foie ravioli, and the short rib & bone marrow agnolotti. Â All yummy. Â The ravioli and agnolotti were my faves. Â I really enjoyed the spaghetti too, but think it's been a bit overhyped... Entree: Capretto. Â In other photos online, I've seen it on the bone, but mine was not. Â It was still good though, but I could've gone for a bit more goat flavor. Â I also tasted some of the duck. Â Delish. Desserts: Left something to be desired. Â We ordered desserts (I also ordered Hennessy). Â Not memorable. Â SO, we then decided to order a cheese course. Â Now, that was yummy and well worth it. Â The cheeses were soft and topped/paired with a sweet component. Solid. Â I'm glad I finally made it. Â Will I go back? Maybe.

A hasidic Jew and a shiksa walk into a bar... called Xixa. Xixa, which is apparently the Spanish spelling of "shiksa," is a gorgeous new Mexican restaurant (I know right??? Spanish/shiksa... other than the link to traif, it makes no sense) in a dusty corner of hipster Williamsburg. It is aesthetically beautiful, the food is the best I've ever had in Brooklyn... but the service... oy vey! It was really busy when we (yes, hasidic Jew and shiksa) came in last night. The hostess told us we could sit while she cleared off a two-top for us, so we hung out on the couch for a few minutes. The aesthetic of this place is seriously beautiful - warm and cozy and almost-rustic-ish. I love the wild cotton sprigs in vases, and the warm blue-ish color of the walls I'd really like to steal for my room. The hostess was oddly over-accomodating as we waited (and didn't know at this point, due to winter weather gear, about our soon-to-be-revealed identities - so in no way do I think her behavior was prejudicial) and kept updating us about every minute as to the status of our table. My dining companion noted that it seemed like the waitstaff were all acting (and over-acting) - and this became more and more clear as the night went on. So, the table clears off and the hostess tells us that it's a tight squeeze to get back past the bar (it is slightly cramped, but have you been to Bario Chino in the LES? THAT'S tight - this was fine) and like starts telling people at the bar to move (wtfff). Okay, maybe she does that to everyone and not just curvy shiksas - so I let that it go, and basically ignored her as I slipped just fine through the crowded space that no one had budged in (eye roll). But when we sat down, she also made a big show of saying how "comfortable" the chairs were (they are bigger and more plush than the ones in the front for the Beautiful People). I decided to completely ignore her comments about this ridiculousness, but instead started composing Yelp review notes in my head. I mean, really? Anyway, they give you the wine/tequila menu first, it's true. We weren't about to get fershikkert so the by-the-bottle-only wine list wasn't on our agenda for the evening. They do have a few beer selections, but oddly enough there's no cocktail menu. I totally get that the focus is tequila and mezcal, and I love me some mezcal - but I was really hoping for a nice, well-crafted tequila cocktail. Jew boo would have had a drink too, had there been cocktails - but as it was I ordered a mezcal, recommended by our equally-as-awkward server, which was totally delicious regardless. Thennnnn they let us order. Oish. So, about our server. It was the weirdest thing ever, definitely the most forced and awkward serving experience I've ever had... it was like every question I asked, he assumed I asked because I was in some way displeased. I asked about cocktails, and he said something to the affect of an apology for me not liking tequila (I love good tequila! WTF! I was just asking if you had cocktails). When he asked how we were doing with the menu and I said that between the two of us, we don't eat meat or shellfish, he basically couldn't function. Just chill, seriously, people. We will figure it out. At Xixa, they want you to order all your plates at once - which seems like an inappropriate request me. With tapas usually you usually can't tell how full you're going to be after just a few... especially here, where the tapas are extraordinary minuscule (but seriously delicious and beautifully plated). But, we'll go back to the continuing weird service in a minute. THE FOOD HERE IS AMAZING! More than five stars!!! Holy mother of God (or not! haha), what was happening in my mouth?! Admittedly snobbishly small portions, I have to say it was completely worth it. The "nachos" were the only miss. I wouldn't order them again. The esquites dish was excellent, the edamame was the most flavorful I have ever had, and the melted cheese dish with tortillas (ironically not the nachos!) was our favourite. We also got dessert - the churros, which were out of control with the cranberry sorbet and a creme brule dipping sauce. But, sorry, I still can't get past the service. Our server dropped my fork and my credit card on the floor... and every time he asked me how I liked something, I told him, "omg it's so good." He then proceeded to apologize and tell me he was sorry I didn't like it?! Dude, either you are so caught up in your act that you're not listening... or you really are not very smart. It's too bad the service at Xixa is so awkward - as noted by other reviewers, because otherwise this place would be five stars. Oh and, just sayin, this place needs a new name. It's just confusing, and like the service, it's pushing it to make it work.

Completely sublime! Â The entire experience was absolutely perfect. Â Great attention to detail in the ambience, and especially the food quality. Â We started with the Raw Yellowtail. Â It was some of the best quality I have ever had and was seasoned to perfection. Â It melted in your mouth. All four pasta's were fantastic. Â The duck foie gras raviolis were especially a stand out. Make reservations well in advance and go!

This is one of my favorite spots in New York. Â They have an amazing, Â rotating selection of craft brews on tap and they always choose great wines too. Â At first my boyfriend found this place to be too girly (with the tin roof and candles and all). Â But with such a great selection of beers, he's become a big fan too. Â It's become our go-to place for drinks after dinner. Our only worry is that they recently sold the place and we are not as fond as the new wait staff as the old ones. Â But so far, the new owners have stayed true to form.

I'm going to basically agree with the sentiment on here. Â Very good ingredient first food. Â Had really excellent crab toast, carrot and avocado salad and halibut. Â The preparation of the carrot (deep flavor substituting it for a protein) was one of the more interesting dishes I've had in NY (I eat out plenty). Â I found myself thinking about the food more after this dinner than anywhere I've eaten in quite awhile. They also have a well constructed menu and wine list. Why not 5 stars? Â A few reasons. 1. Â It is painfully loud. Maybe they should get some carpets from ABC carpet. Â I wouldn't go with a group larger than 4. 2. Â It's a scene with models etc. Â Maybe that's your thing, but I don't personally feel it adds to the experience. Â I found myself laughing at the collections of people and behavior at some of the tables...i.e a family of 4 with small children eating at a table for 8 at 11pm. Â Wife was clearly a model/had been one. Â Other restaurants probably wouldn't have tolerated this sort of thing, but I suspect they were special. All this excitement makes getting reservations exceedingly difficult if you don't have a personal assistant to stake out your reservation (to be clear I don't really hold against them being popular maybe just a bit on how/to whom they seem to allocate reservations). 3. I don't know why some places do this, but can I have one server to take care of me for the night? Â I think we had three people. Â It's strange and disconcerting. Â I mean to bring over my meal or whatever fine, but why is one person explaining the menu and another then taking Â my order? Â Bizarre. Overall though its a destination place and deserves to be. Â I'll be back, but there are some things holding it back.

I'll keep it simple... Service - Poor Food - Uninteresting Value - Way over priced Sad thing is that I had bookmarked the restaurant almost 6 months prior. Heard lots of great reviews but fell way short of expectations. Next.

I was not impressed. I got famous buttermilk chicken, nothing special, I didn't like it. But since a lot of people did, I guess I'm very spoiled or something happened with my chicken in the kitchen. But place is very cosy, perfect for a date.

I loved this place. Â It was my go-to place during the week I spent in NYC. Â The bartenders were always friendly, and they recognized me after my 2nd visit - a Yuengling was always at the ready when I walked-in. Â  Prices were incredibly reasonable - $3 pints of Yuengling? Â Yes, please. Decent jukebox, and for the most part, the regulars seemed cool and nice. Â I met a super nice couple there who shared the great neighborhood bagel and pizza places with me. Â  It was a bit rowdy one night; some kids were really whoopin' it up, but they mostly kept to themselves. Â Just a lot of screaming and squealing at times. Â Otherwise, it was fantastic. Go. Â This is a great bar. Â Never ate here; but the drinks & service were perfect.

The service here is horribly awful. Â It took us an hour to get a table on a Tuesday night. Â The food is overpriced. Â It's crowded. Â The waiters are beyond rude and disinterested. Going here was a really awful experience. Â Except for the deviled eggs, those were delicious. I recommend steering clear of this restaurant unless you want to leave poor and introverted.

2.5 stars First of all, this restaurant is quite large. You'd never know by walking in the front door but there is a large dining room downstairs. The restaurant is supposed to be known for its chicken and ceviche. I didn't get a chance to try the chicken, but the mixto ceviche was decent. The lomo salto was just average. The quality of meat was good, but the dish itself wasn't anything special and expensive for what it was. The worst thing about this restaurant is the service. At 3 pm with a half empty restaurant , we expected faster and better service. The good took forever and our waiter was always no where to be found. This place has potential but I won't be back.

Called the day ahead and was told that yes, they will be open at 7:30AM. I planned my breakfast before a plane trip for this. Got there at 8:30AM, not open. Some clueless employee standing outside wondering about the same thing. I waited until 9:30AM, still not open. Does anyone know how to run a business here?

Oh my, I forgot to write a review for Casa Mono! My wife and I have been many times and decided to go back to an old favorite. There are very few dishes that I don't love. Â If I don't love it, it's probably because I don't like the ingredient, not because of the preparation which is always top notch. Well this time I tried the veal cheeks over lentils. Â DAMMMMNNN!! Â I've had veal cheeks a few times but this was the best. Next time I have to go back for my all time favorite, bone marrow. Go there!! Five Stars!

Came here for a birthday party. Kinda small and cozy place. We had about 14 people. Full bar with a good selection of draft beers. The appetizers seemed to be better than the entrees so if you're coming here with a group, I suggest getting that instead. The bone marrow was very good and had a lot of marrow inside. The spaghetti bolognaise was disappointing, but I ordered it mainly for filler. Sorry, but I can make better pasta than that. Had much better for cheaper. Food took a while to arrive. Might come back to see if lunch is better.

I have been meaning to get to Lupa for the longest time! I had a great meal here. Â I ordered the special which was a house-made pappardelle pasta with a lamb ragu and ricotta salata and my guest had the duck.. oh the duck.. absolutely fantastic. Â We had the sardine app which was equally delicious. Â This way out-shined Babbo.

Wow! Â This place was great. Restaraunt was nicely appointed staff was friendly and service was very good. We got the heirloom caprese salad and grilled octopus to start. Both were very good. The octopus came with a tomatoe sauce on it that I could have done without. I thought it masked some of the flavor of the dish. It was still good just not my preference. For dinner we had the lobster spaghetti which had a 1/2 of lobster in it. It was incredible. We also had the large ravioli with ricotta and a easy egg yolk in the middle. That was also very good. Dessert was just ok I thought. We had chocolate gelato with cherries as shaved chocolate. It was a lot of chocolate on one dish for me. Also got a blackberry tart with corn gelato. Yes I said corn gelato. Some things should not be turned into gelato. An ice cream dish that tastes like corn is not something that sounded appetizing, but had to try it. I was right. Â Tastes like cold corn. Not good, but now I know. Wine list was extensive and is set up by region. Areas of Italy I had never heard of along with varietals I had not seen or tasted before. They only offer Italian wines, but after a quick chat with sommelier she recommended a great bottle at an affordable price (under $80). I was shocked that she did this and I appreciated her not trying to steer us to a more expensive bottle when we were unsure with the selection in the first place. Â I would definitely recommend reservations as the place was packed and it was a Thurs.
pizza is off the hook, but the wait sucks!!!!!

This is a solid place for banh mi if you're in the area but not one I would travel more than 10-15 minutes for. Â I got there around 3 and had a chicken (#2). Overall a bit sweet but good pickles, spicyness, and garlic mayo. The two things I wasn't a huge fan of were the keys. The chicken was a bit dry and I wish was shredded. Also, maybe because it was late in the day but the bread was a bit stale. Â So good in the extras but wish the main parts were better.

The atmosphere is 100% classic Americana and the smell of burgers and wings is enough to make your stomach growl. The place was clean and comfortable. The service was quick and friendly. Here's the thing; I ordered a turkey burger. It LOOKED outstanding - huge, stacked with toppings and the thing must have weighed at least two pounds but when I took my first bite I was literally stunned at how bland it tasted. I had to douse the bun with ketchup just to get some flavor into this burger and even then, it wasn't enough. Two bites in, the burger just fell apart into two pieces, as if the meat patty was made out of bread crumbs and water. Halfway through the burger I honestly began to wonder if I'd gotten some kind of vegetarian patty by mistake... I feel weird writing this because I REALLY wanted to like this place - everything about it is outstanding and all the other reviews are glowing with praise. It's just... the burger tasted like... bread and... wet bread. For what it's worth, my dad is a butcher and I grew up on red meat so I know my burgers. Â I plan to come back to try some other items on the menu. I'll be sure to revise this review after I've given Bonnie's another try.

Sakagura is truly an amazing spot if you manage to find it. It is located in the basement of an office building and upon entering feels like you've been whisked away to a typical japanese spot in tokyo. Â The sake selection is endless and the food is out of this world. Â Keep in mind however that izakaya (japanese tapas) tends to serve very small portion and that is consistent with japanese customs because they believe in quality over quantity and they also hate to waste food. If you are a big eater like I am then I suggest the following: 1) be prepared to shell out about $50-60 pp , drinks not included. 2) have a light snack before you come here. Don't forget to finish off your meal with their chocolate souffle. it's probably the best i've had in the city. Â Cha-an (japanese tea house) in the st-marks area serves desserts straight from sakagura and we'll leave that magnificent tea house for another review, another day. Â  Overall, a great first date place or business dinner spot and if you are a guy you will definitely impress your date/ associates with this hidden gem. very cosy and casual.

Very different went for Israeli Independence Day , THE MEATBALLS ARE GREAT! Tried the fried Cauliflower calamari sausage and another appetizer (don't remember what it was) and all of the skewer I think the shrimp skewer could have had more shrimp but the lamb and vegetable skewers were my favorites. I had the ginger crisp signature cocktail which is the #1 reason I am going to go back it was very quietly comfortable with outstanding service
Skip the $1 grain free roll--not worth it. Â Other than that addition to the reviews, I agreee with everything that has previously been posted about Hu.

I came here on a desperate whim with a friend, looking for a respite for my poor dear feet after a long Saturday and a missed brunch reservation elsewhere. So basically I didn't read the reviews first. Upon looking at them afterward I understand the complaints made but I had one of the best food experiences of my life here. The outdoor seating was spaced with plants to have some distance from others, the drinks were phenomenal (pimms cup, bloody, truffle whiskey sour) albeit the service when it came to drinks was pretty slow. Not the end of the world. But otherwise the servers were pretty attentive and our waitress was very sweet and personable. Â  As for the food. TRUFFLE HEAVEN. Whoever makes the menu obviously loves truffles as much as we do, nearly everything we are was truffled in some way or another. We started with the truffle burrata special, I moved on to the ricotta with lobster (and truffle peelings), my friend moved on to the fluke and fennel dish and we shared a side of truffle sautÃ©ed asparagus. Yet by the time dessert time came around we still wanted more truffle. So screw convention. We got that special burrata plate again for dessert. No regrets, no shame. You're jealous it's cool. Ok yes the prices are high but everything that passed our lips was delectable and when we asked for something we got it relatively quickly for a pretty full restaurants. I would go there again in a heartbeat next time I'm willing to spend the money.

I am a Brooklyn native, but had my maiden Difara experience today. (Before today, I was an avowed L&B Spumoni Gardens devotee, and would never eat pizza anywhere else in Brooklyn.) L&B remains great, but Difara is...beyond comprehension better. Had I experienced this earlier, I may have never had the resolve to watch my carbs. Now that I have, the battle may be forever lost. Owner Dom is an adorable older Sicilian gentleman who makes every pizzza by hand...using fresh Â buffalo mozzerella, basil leaves, porcini mushrooms...a brick oven. I'm still salivating hours Â later. City dwellers, it's worth the trek.

While the food here is probably great, the service is horrible. I went in last night with four other people and asked how long the wait was. We were snapped at by the hostess who seemed extremely frazzled by the question. I understand everyone has bad days, and she later apologized, so all was forgiven. We went and got drinks elsewhere, and we came back when we got the text that our table was ready. We chatted with the hostess and started following her back to the table. We were then snapped at by ANOTHER woman because they needed an extra minute to wipe down the table, and they wanted us to wait in the front area. If the hostess said this, we honestly did not hear it, and was that really worthy of being snapped at again?! We wound up leaving because after being snapped at by TWO separate people, we just did not feel right giving them our business. I was extremely disappointed, as we just moved to the area, and we planned on this being a regular spot. Everyone in this neighborhood has been friendly and wonderful, except for the people here. Probably will not give this place another try, but Prime Meats next door was excellent!

There are times I've been to Amy Ruth's and had a less than ideal service experience. My recommendation is to avoid the "brunch" crowd and just come here for dinner when they serve the same good food and the waiters aren't as slammed. I wouldn't wait in line for Amy Ruth's. I eat a lot of soul food: it's much bigger than chicken and waffles, y'all. If you really like chicken and waffles, you'll probably like it, but it's worth saying there's better options on the menu, which you may like if you order to your taste and not to the hype. See, I've had better waffles and I've had better chicken (just not on the same plate). Â I think their fried wings are much better than their fried chicken entree, and I always go for their fried catfish and mac n cheese, because fried catfish is awesome.

The best Michelin Starred restaurant Â in Manhattan without a Michelin Star... Â Simply fabulous dinner. Â My wife and I had the amazingly affordable tasting menu. Â All of the courses were in wonderful fall colors and design. Â The service was simply outstanding to go along with a world class meal. Â Ambiance is hip, but elegant at the same time. Â The bartender was highly creative offering us a cognac based cocktail with apricot and coffee liquors. Â A combination that I would not have come up with, but it worked amazingly well. Â Our server was very personable and delivered course after courses at an appropriate cadence. Â The food was a cross of elegance and seasonal freshness! Â All in all, I can't wait to return to the Eddy! Â As my good friend Arnold said, "I'll be back!"

The first thing I noticed about PT was that there was no one there at 8 pm on a Thursday. Usually not a good sign, but I was hungry and we were already there.* We walked outside to the secluded garden, which was quiet and perfect for a low-key meal. And in truth, everyone there was destined to eat well: the three of us, another couple in the corner, and the mosquitoes. No one else wanted to eat a house like I did, so we just shared three dishes. 1. The parmesan asparagus appetizer had wonderful flavor, even if they were the saddest, skinniest specimens I've seen in a long time. 2. I found that I enjoy my buddy's mom's linguine with clam sauce** more than PT, but theirs is still very nice. The clams were a bit tough, but there certainly were a decent amount of them. 3. The generous portion of pork tenderloin wrapped in puff pastry was actually juicy and well cooked, and the potato, carrot and zucchini accompaniments were also well-executed. My only complaint would be that the sauce between the pork and puff pastry seemed to be dijon mustard, straight out of the bottle. This would've been fine, but it was decidedly reminiscent of a ham sandwich. Also, in the darkness, one of my companions asked if it was wrapped in bacon, and after that I was disappointed it was merely puff pastry. Overall, PT is a solid Italian spot with a lovely garden. Just beware the mosquitoes in summer. *This is how many of my decisions are made. **Not a euphemism.

One of my favorite places in the entire city. Insanely huge portions for the money and the half-a-chicken is perfection itself. The wine is good, the water is freezing cold and the tostones are my favorite appetizer. There's a huge fridge of Goya juices (just like you used to drink as a kid!) and sodas. Everything is delicious because it's homemade. Highly recommended.

My new favourite restaurant... Menu small, well thought out.... Interesting food combination and taste sensations! Lay back attentive service from knowledgable front of house staff. Small eating house with a great vibe!

Wanted to enjoy the weather & grab a bite to eat with my family. Loaded up my trusty Yelp app and found "The Thirsty Koala" from the reviews it seen like a Yelpers paradise. The staff was very informative and tentative, the decor was warm and welcoming children friendly. I arrived here during happy hours 4pm-8pm Â Monday - Friday Wine $4 Draft beer $3 Cocktails 2 for 1 $8. I ordered a few "Hooky Dooly caipirinha" excellent cocktail extremely mild taste with basil leaves, strawberry, lime juice, brown sugar and Brazilian light rum, they were generous with the alcohol. We ordered the BURGER WITH THE LOT (GRILLED PINEAPPLE, BACON, EGG, BEET SLAW AND CARAMELIZED ONION) I ordered it with beef I decided to pass on the kangaroo meat today. The burger was excellent with all the toppings, it was juicy and rare just the way I like it, the fries were crispy outside and soft inside. I also ordered the MARINATED SKIRT TACOS ( cooked medium rare ) PICO, CABBAGE, PEPPERS, CILANTRO, CHIPOTLE SAUCE. My steak was a little over cooked, the chipotle sauce had just the right amount of heat, overall a enjoyable meal. The atmosphere, customer service, food and drinks definitely bought out the Thirsty Koala in me.

The burgers, the fries, and the wait! Holy shit the wait. Stand there for 45 minutes waiting to get a table on a busy night (hence the wait), but you know its worth it once you sink your teeth into a Bistro Burger. There is something about that slab of meat cooked to a tender perfection, with those three pickle slices sitting daintily on that ruffled paper plate for you to snag. But wait! Do you want fries with that? Ha! You know answer will always be yes and with good reason. These fries, very thin yet crunchy. They are cooked in the same oil that our our favorite pig Babe was fried in giving them a wonderful bacon-e taste. Safe beer selection of McSorleys Dark or Light, Sierra Nevada, Guinness, and others suds grace the taps of this landmark establishment.
Love the different sauces ...and the frites!!! You can get sauces on the side (I prefer to get it layered and 2 different sauces) I always stop here when I'm in the area for a quick meal. :-) YUM!!!

Absolutely amazing food & service. The interior design, location and ambiance is very high end expensive but you're paying the best in the business to take you by the hand and you certainly get what you pay for. Recommended.
Great GREAT GREAT! Best falafel in town. And above all a great value for money.

Flambees were delicious! Environment was cozy and therefore a bit loud but was overall a great experience. Really nice people who own and work here. Very sweet servers. The flambees were perfect in size. Came with a friend and shared two savory ones and one dessert. We had the traditional w/ swiss cheese and the jardin. Traditional was a bit heavier with the cheese but jardin was a perfect veggie compliment. My absolute favorite was the chocolat fraise. Perfect end to our meal!

Yelp Friends please dont shoot me for rating this place 3 stars.I know its tremendously popular.This review is only for take out and I promise I will update my review once I have dined in. After reading some of the last reviews on Empanada Mama, I was determined to at least try their take out atleast.We tried twice the same week and their service is very efficient.They even offered to bring our order to the car. Somehow the empanadas failed to hit the spot.They were pretty inexpensive at $2.80 each but somehow the flavor was not something that will stay with you long enough to come back for it again.We tried the chicken, mushroom, spinach Â all whole wheat and baked.And we also tried the fig and cheese for dessert.They were all good..Just lacked a flavor profile. There are tons of other things that I would like to try which I would leave for when we dine in.They are open 24 HOURS which is a such a plus for midnight snack and I know Ill be picking up food from here often.

This place is delicious! And has a great ambiance. The dining area is huge, high ceilings, feels like I'm sitting on the porch of a tropical home in the Caribbean. The mojitos were amazing, even had a bit of raw sugar cane which was a nice touch. The appetizer cheese buns were a great start to the meal. I ordered a steak dish which was great but I can't remember what it was.

This place is fantastic! The servers is attentive and friendly, the atmosphere is nice and the back yard is pleasant. Everything I have tasted has been delicious and healthy and flavorful. Â The fig/chocolate/graham dessert is decadent. Â Interesting drinks and tons of vegetarian options overflowing with veggies and flavor.
My favorite restaurant in the city! Â Great fries, great place. Â The goat cheese sandwich has been my favorite sandwich for over 10 years. Â Love.

Cafeteria sucks. So much. Never been late night, not my part of town. The food is not even plain, it's just like ... the bare minimum required to call something an "eggs benedict," or whatever, which I guess if I was an avante-garde theorist I might be interested in a discussion of "pancakes as such," but I'm looking for a decent meal. I've been here a few times, and left basically pissed off every time, so I won't be back. It's just occasionally a convenient spot for me. The aesthetic is beat too. It's like a sad attempt at minimalism but it's actually just the owner is probably lazy. The service is pretty much absent. I love the gays and I'm so psyched that they run their own part of town, but next time I go there I might ask one of them where a decent place to eat is. Cuz it's not Cafeteria. I had an eggs benedict, she had a cup of yogurt, I had orange juice, she had a coffee. Twenty-fucking-seven dollars, not including tip. And the receipt said "18% Gratuity is customary for good service." What a fucking crock this place is. Sorry about the language.

Came here with my bf when we first started dating. We were all over each other and really gross - probably ruining many of your dining experiences. I apologize. We were already drunk and went here on a whim. Good decision. Burger hit the spot. I know everything tastes better when you're sloshed but despite my inebriation, I was Â able to see that this was indeed an excellent burger. Open til 4am - awesome late night spot. I no longer eat meat so I can't give the burger another go. If they add a veggie burger to the menu, I'd be all over that though [hint hint CB]

If you're wishing for some fantastic Mexican/Cuban food, look no further! Â Out of all the restaurants on yelp, this place caught my boyfriend's eye. Â He read that the corn here was amazing and o..m..g...it was awesome!! Â The apple and spinach salad was great as an appetizer with the corn and the main course was delicious! Â I had this corn masa "boat" meal with rice and beans. Â The rice and beans is delicious too! Â We had to wait about 40 minutes on a Friday night (which I guess wasn't too bad) and it was a bit crowded and tight but it was well worth it!! :)

waited an hour which was reasonable. the food was fantastic.. i had the pork buns , the wings, and akamaru with pork loin and egg. i thought i was gonna have a heart attack with so much pork but i didn't care this time. i think ippudo ramen has a little bit more flavor that what i usually get from mitsuwa. the ambiance is great, though it can get loud inside. i would definitely go back but this won't stop me from ramen hunting.

Nestled on the second floor of the Setai Hotel, Ai Fiori takes you on an exhilarating tour through the culinary flavors of Italy. If you're looking for a dining experience in New York with inventive dishes, an extensive drink selection, and exceptional service, Ai Fiore should be on the top of your list. From the moment we walked into Ai Fiore, we sensed a restaurant with impeccable service and an appreciation for their customers. We arrived on a bustling Saturday evening around 8:30, without a reservation and were graciously escorted to their hip and modern bar, just outside the restaurant entrance. Although the specialty cocktail list was limited, the bartenders were quite knowledgeable and suggested the Royal Blush, a refreshing, well-crafted cocktail. Midway through our drinks the maitre d' approached and escorted us to our table, a quaint and cozy corner of the restaurant. Upon our seating, we were immediately greeted by the waiter and welcomed to the restaurant. I will admit the wine list is quite expensive and perhaps a bit overwhelming, but the sommelier kindly walked us through the menu and helped us select a full-bodied red that would compliment a variety of entrees on the menu. From starting out with the fresh rosemary roll to the finishing up with the caramel apple sorbet and everything in between, the food exceeded all my expectations. The main courses definitely stole the spotlight: the braised beef cheek and rack of lamb were both so tender and flavorful. We started with the grapefruit/crab/avocado appetizer, which was tangy and beautifully displayed. In between the appetizer and entrÃ©e they brought out a little soup that was wonderful and between dinner and dessert a couple of homemade chocolates. I cannot say enough good things about this restaurant. The service was so superb and attentive without being overbearing or interrupting the evening. The food was interesting, beautifully plated, and most importantly, absolutely delicious. While this is certainly a pricey restaurant, I can't think of anywhere I'd rather eat in New York for a special night out.

Such amazing pizza! Every time I'm in the neighborhood I make it a point to stop in here. The Broadway Breadcrumb square is my favorite and I would absolutely recommend it. The stuffed prosciutto balls are also very good. :)

D - is for Delicious, as I found the food they served. I - is for Ironic, as the hipsters I there observed. N - is for Nourishing, as their organic ingredients must be. E - is for Eggs, found in the feta herb omelet served to me. R - is for Return, which I won't be able to do today. but not for lack of want/ quite simply because/ i live 2500 miles away! :(

they make their own buckwheat noodles. i had hot soba noodles Â soup with shrimp tempura, and added half boiled egg, It was very good! not spicy, or dashi (stock) was just right. Just a lil wish is that they could give out some more negi. Overall, I think food from this place is somewhat authentic.
Love this place. I went for my birthday and the whole place sang happy birthday to me. Their pizzas are soooo good.

Oh how I love thee. Â British gastric pub and good food? Â Who would have ever thunk it. Â The boyfriend and I were here for dinner and really enjoyed how lively the place was. Â We dined upstairs and the place was actually beyond capacity. Â  The bf sat on the outside and had his chair bumped every 15 seconds! Â There really wasn't any room to move at all. I'm sure that's the usual experience for any new yorker (umm...the subway during rush hour anyone?), but it was quite odd for us. Â While we were reveling in it all, our beer and food came. Â I can't even begin to describe how excited we were. We started off with the gnudi--deliciously tender potato dumplings in a rich cheese sauce. Â Oh, its orgasmic. Â Then came the roquefort burger and steak. Â The steak was delicious, but the roquefort burger was out of this world! Â Our only regret? Â Not ordering the devils on horseback--another specialty of the house. Â Next time :) Hey, we're from CA and truly enjoyed our New York dining experience. Â Was Spotted Pig ridiculously crowded? Yes, but it really made our dinner more interesting. Â Do you wait a tad long for food and is it a bit difficult getting your server's attention? Â Yes, but once you get your food you won't care. I can't wait to go back. Â Ooooooh gnudi.
Craft cocktails and authentic indian cuisine! loved every bite and savored every sip!

Their dinners are better than their brunches, and their drinks are good no matter the time of the day. They have a pretty solid bar selection and great baristas mixing some extremely flavorful cocktails. I tried to adjust my internal clock to daylight savings time by running to Saxon and downing a few, and it worked! Lol love their drinks and will def be back for more.

I've come here twice (once for weekend brunch, once for lunch), and both times it was nothing short of amazing. I had the duck hash and it was to die for. Today, the roasted chicken plate left me wanting more. All for such low prices for what you're getting! Absolutely fantastic. I highly recommend LIC Kitchen, and will certainly be back for more.

I wanted to have some fresh juice so I came in here only to learn that they do NOT make any fresh juice on the spot- they are all bottled. So I ordered a smoothie and was disappointed that the orange juice they use were straight from the commercial store bought carton (not even organic)! Very disappointed. I think I will go to the street cart for fresh juices and fresh smothies from now on- fortunately in wall st area, there are many great ones.

It's nice when a restaurant [if you want to call this place a restaurant] lives up to the hype. Â Which Artichoke does. Â Mind you, I'm not even a pizza person. Â Except for a soft spot in my heart for PIzzeria Uno, of all things [their crust is like eating a croissant], I'm not even that crazy about it. But I read about the place. Â And I saw the lines. Â And I knew it was something special. Â So I went at lunchtime on a rainy day and had the artichoke spinach pizza. Â The five stars is for that - I haven't tried anything else. Â No, wait. Â The five stars is also for the lamp that sits in the window of the restaurant - the base of which is a woman's leg in fishnet stockings and stilettos. Seriously, though. Â This pizza is incredible.
