Stopped here for a quick drink before eating at a nearby restaurant and it was an adorable stop. There was a good crowd, great menu and quick service. The food options looked good too. While I wouldn't head out just to come here, its good to know its in the neighborhood!

I believe everyone who said that they had a horrible experience there, but I was not one of them. Â We went with a large group for a birthday celebration and all the seating and arrangements had been made beforehand, so things actually went pretty smoothly. Â The food was way better than I expected considering all Â the negative reviews. Â In fact, I would say the food was very good. Â The views can't be beat and the staff was all quite friendly. Â  It's clear from the other reviews that there are a lot of kinks to work out, and I'm not sure why they've been so ill prepared. Â It does seem that their kitchen is not big enough to serve all the seats in the restaurant. Â That said, we had a great time and we look forward to going back.

They really tried to be outstanding but they were not (there is great potential). It was pretty loud and we had a small table right next to the bar so it was busy. The red wine selection by glass was not great (mostly wines from France if I remember correctly), it was served too warm and the wine glass was not clean. The food was good but it also had its price, I really liked that the plates were preheated.

Nice little eatery tucked away from the chaos of the city. Â The food was decent and fairly reasonable for NYC prices. Â The waitress wasn't very attentive and we bused our own table and went inside to pay.

Don't expect great service in this candle lit, tin tiled ceiling, italian restaurant. Â The garden in the back invites you to spend hours lingering over your glass of italian red and in the fall there is a small bonfine pit. Â Wether you're inside or outide in the garden, don't expect quick refills. The unfortuntely shoddy service casts a dim view on the well chosen european menu and the interesting wine selection.
Great food, friendly staff, nice ambiance. Â  Although they tend to get packed on weekends, their brunch menu is really good and they feature live jazz music. Â Definitely worth the wait.

Sun-dappled, cool breeze rising, yet pleasantly warm, rustling trees, and a good friend~ an already winning end-of-summer Sunday morning was made perfect by a memorable experience at Jane's for brunch. First, upon entering this popular establishment (reservations are definitely recommended), one is struck by the cool, modern, and stylish decor. Though crowded, pockets of intimacy are to be found and we found ours by a door towards the back open to the sidewalk which the kind and gracious hostess allowed us to take. Second, service was provided by an amazingly bright and vivacious server who deserves credit for her beautiful smile and friendly demeanor despite the obvious demands of a heavy brunch crowd (thanks Emily!). And finally, the food.. fantastic. The delicious initial bread basket alone would have sufficed for a filling breakfast but what's the fun in that? These were followed by side orders of scrambled eggs (two eggs but huge) which were truly perfect (silky, moist without being runny) and Crispy Grit Cake which were satisfyingly crunchy yet mealy inside for a a nice take on a traditional breakfast item for those who love grits . Vanilla Bean French Toast was delightful for a vanilla-lover and creme brulee lover as myself. Thick cut, soft, fragrant of vanilla.. it was almost a shame to douse the toast with the included real maple syrup. And finally, a taste of my friend;s selection of the Benedict Jane was also delicious although I shall defer to those who love more their poached eggs and hollandaise in the morning. A wonderful and memorable experience~

The only negative which results in one less star is - the tables are TOO CLOSE TOGETHER. Â  After a long day at work, bf and i were enjoying our drinks, raving about all the yumminess in front of us, a perfect evening until four teeny boppers with loud shrieky voices, wanted all their dining neighbors to hear how uninteresting their lives were... ay ay ay.. but otherwise we enjoyed everything we ordered - ham/sausage plate, pea salad with carmalized scallions, stuffed dates, baby squid and a few others.

These fries are addicting! I'm not a big fry person but these are so good! My favorite sauces are the mango chutney and the pomegranate Â teriyaki mayo. The frite sauce is good to if you don't feel like paying $1 extra for sauce. I wouldn't get the peanut sauce, it tastes just like chunky peanut butter and I think it is way to over powering. Get some fries to go and head to union square for some prime people watching any time of the day!
All I have to say is yum! This place is wonderful! I look forward to heading back here really soon

Lovely meal at Olivier tonight. Â Arugula salad and deliciously prepared fish. Â Yummy tarte tatin, my husband's favorite, deliciously caramelized. Â I would like to see a little bit more wines by the glass on offer. Â Other than that... great. Â We will definitely be going back.

a few months later I feel I should review the food not just the bar, maybe I am maturing. It Â may have been said before, but the farm burger is fantastic, Fries always good, they have great specials and I love the outside in the summer. Charming decor, nice lighting- you know- not too bright. Sit at the bar for dinner, is casual and everyone is chatty.

This is a diner on viagra. Â Very creative menu, stylish decor, packs of servers. Â I admit that they cram people into tight spaces and tables are close to each other. It's a classic trendy resto that deserves its due for being an institution for so many years. Â Even give credit for the stylish wash rooms. The food is excellent. Â Basic dishes made better. Â Original recipes that rock. Â Lovely, properly sized bar.
I love bringing new friends here. The roti is a must to start. Get the chicken broth rice. Service is fine. Ladies bathroom is a bit awkward. I recommend not going if you're shy.

I ordered breakfast Christmas Eve for myself and 6 co-workers. Â The food was alright, nothing exceptional. Â I was charged an 18% service charge on a takeout order because that's their policy for any orders over 5. Â Secondly, the person taking the phone order up charged all of my orders an additional $1 for white meat without asking if that's what I wanted. Â I'll never order from this restaurant again nor will I recommend it to anyone.

This place was totally delicious. I felt like I was straight in a cafeterÃ­a in Santurce or Barrio Obrero, Puerto Rico. Had the filete de pescado with tostones y ensalada. I couldn't leave without my cafÃ© con leche. I'll be going back next time I visit NYC.

I don't typically like pizza, but my friend dragged me here for (New York style?) pizza when I was in New York the other day. Â I was incredibly impressed. Â Her friends were already in line and so we got a table relatively quickly. The atmosphere is definitely toward the younger crowd (Brooklyn Heights in general, perhaps). Â The table is incredibly cramped for the five of us, but this added to the ambience of the restaurant. Â People are here for the good food, not to have great dining. Â We got three pies which actually satisfied all of us. Â Normally, I don't like mushrooms or olives, but this pizza actually melded everything together so that my disliked foods didn't stand out. I liked folding the slice lengthwise to eat it. Â Thin crust, which didn't border on my distaste of too much dough. Â One of the best pizzas I ever had. Highly recommended. Â Near the High Street subway station.

I can't tell you how much I loooove bianca!!! It's a charming cute place where they serve the yummiest italian food. It's definitely my favorite italian restaurant in new york. Their tagliolini with seafood is what I always end up getting. I also love their salmon with spinach and potatoes. Their pasta with sausage and broccoli rabe is really good too. They have an excellent wine selection and the service is always friendly. The only thing that I find annoying is their cash only policy.

I would have never found this little gem if It had not been recommend by a friend. I don't know why I didn't hear of it earlier. But perhaps it't best to keep it off the Brooklyn foodie radar. Food was lovely: delicious, perfectly seasoned with heat and fresh flavors. And I appreciate the attention paid to using local suppliers Ans seasonal ingredients. The restaurant itself is warm, and charming, perfect for a romantic occasion. And the service was impeccable. Our server had the prefect balance of attentiveness, knowledge without smothering us. I look forward to going back again and again. I enjoyed the grilled calamari, fresh tortillas (yum!) and fish tacos.

For whatever the reason, I was waiting for this place to open so when it did I was there!!!! The atmosphere is welcomimg and their choice of beer is top notch!!!! I'm slowly and surely becoming a regular.

Walked by on a Sunday afternoon and saw that they were open with only a 3 person line. Â My boyfriend and I each got a spinach artichoke slice. Â I'll agree with others that the guy who takes the money at the counter is a bit 'rough around the edges' but we got our pizza quickly. Â No complaints on the size of the slice - big enough to have to hold with two hands. Â Also saw them making a spinach artichoke pizza and using 1" cubes of cheese. Â WOW... that's a lot- and they look like pretty quality ingredients. Other than that though I'll admit that the pizza wasn't to my liking. Â They add olive oil in addition to the cheese so it makes for a very very very greasy/oily slice - which I didn't love. Â The artichoke spinach combo tasted great but was overshadowed by the amount of oil- Â I was only able to have a few bites before it became too much for me. Â  I'm not sure if the rumor about them putting cream in their pizza topping is true but I'll tell you that I'd rather have cream than the extra olive oil. Bottom line - Go at least once to see what it's all about. Â If you like it, great if not then you know that you can move on.

Yelp reviews narrowed our dinner choices on this side of Manhattan to a small group of 4 star, $$ restaurants and we ended up at Penelope. Â I am glad we did. Â Nice starters, humus plate and artichoke dip which was my favorite. Â Very good cup of chicken soup followed by tasty arugala salad with white beans. Â Lots of variety on the menu including a number of vegetarian selections. Good service. Â I'm a fan and will be back.
Really fun place, good energy. We started with some champagne at the bar, then had great dinner. Moules frites was good. Reasonably priced wine list . A slice of old Paris in New York. To be redone.

Too many have raved that this is the best Thai restaurant in NYC. It's on Eater 38 for as long as I can remember. It's good decent thai food, but nothing mindblowing. If I don't happen to be near there, I probably would not think it is worth traveling out of the city for it. I guess since Thailand is so far away, this is as close as it can get. It's ok....i guess...a little over-rated...and way too much fried dishes...my favorite dish is probably the cassava dessert.

Terrible customer service and extraordinarily rude, even when the restaurant was half empty. Â This restaurant needs to get over itself. The hosts are rude/pompous "you can't sit at the bar unless you are ordering food. If you want to drink you can go next door", Â the food was disappointing (too salty, small portions for the price). Plus the items I used to come back for have changed, for the worse. Â  And to top it off, my waitress basically ignored me, to the point I had to ask the chef/cook for my check. My recommendation is to skip this place!!! It's gone DOWNHILL and there are too many amazing restaurants in NYC to waste your time and money here.

Dinner review. Came early and caught the last 30 mins of Happy Hour, $5 Old Fashioneds are my favourite Old Fashioneds. And they are fashioned by a bartender with a beard more awesome than Zeus. We then took a table for dinner. The Long Island duck was great, the meatloaf sandwich excellent, and the service from the fabulous Danielle was perfect in every way. We had desert but I can't remember what it was because of Old Fashioneds + wine but I'm sure it was delicious too. You should go there.

Ai Fiori is a lovely restaurant with brilliant staff in the wonderful Langham Place hotel! It is a very posh restaurant and so the meals are fairly small but full of flavour. As we were short on time we had arrived there early and so the restaurant was empty and we found ourselves almost being watched by the staff which was slightly off putting. The staff were all helpful and friendly however giving advice on the meals. Some of the main meals we had ordered were more flavoursome than others such as the fish meals whereas the pasta meal that I had wasn't the most filling or the best of choices in hindsight. The desserts however were incredible! I had the chocolate mousse which came with a dissolving lemon cream which was one of the nicest things I have ever eaten! Overall the restaurant is very nice although a little expensive for the small portions.

I'm surprised by these ratings. Â It's possible I Â went in on an off day but I did not think that this place was memorable at all. Â  I was really excited to try this place from the reviews but after ordering a few items I was genuinely confused by the excitement. While the wafcos seemed like an interesting idea in theory, after one bite they completely broke apart and it was a mess. Â I can appreciate that I think they tried using their rotisserie in the chick wafcos but adding chunks of the actual fat from the dark meat areas completely grossed me out. Â The protein platters were pretty simple and under seasoned and my biscuit was not completely cooked. Â The outside was initially very good but the inside ruined the taste. Â I probably should have tried some of their desserts which all sounded great but had a hard time getting through the meal, so opted to pass. The business owners were very friendly though and were probably the best part of my experience.
Great pasta. Lots of unique flavors. Homemade mozzarella. Prices are down to earth too, which is the reason to go here when in downtown Manhattan.

Happend to be in the area and was looking for someplace to eat. Â We stopped in here after reading the reviews on yelp. Â I originally passed it and looked in thinking, "Man it looks hot in there" because the whole front was open. Â Not realizing that was the place I was looking for but I took a chance. Â We had lasanga w/ a mixed vegetables on the side, spinach ravioli, tomato and mozzarella. Â The bread to start was slightly different. Â  Tasted homemade similar to pizza dough. Â Either way it was delisious. Â The tomato and mozzarella was fresh and tasty. Â Our dinners were both very good. Oh and the mixed vegetables were real mixed veggies they put together not from a bag. Was very happy I stopped in and I will be back. Â Also, it was not hot in the restaurant at all.

4.5 Stars. Just moved into the Ditmas Park/ 'Victorian Flatbush' neighborhood a week ago, and Ox Cart Tavern opened several days later. Went there the other night with a few friends for dinner and drinks. The ambiance was nice: Welcoming, flatteringly lit, somewhat rustic, vaguely hip. Wooden or metal rustic and-or vintage tables, many by large windows. A 6-8 person wooden bar in the back overlooking a partly open kitchen. The staff were friendly and accommodating. The food was quite good. (Hope it doesn't go downhill, as sometimes happens, if and when the place becomes popular and stays around for a while.) Though none of us were craving burgers, we were persuaded by the creative and appetizing descriptions of the burgers on their menu, all ended up ordering them and were not disappointed. The fried bologna sandwich looked intriguing-- likely good, because someone would either have to be supremely confident in their craft or delusional to advertise such a seemingly low-grade dish, and the quality of the food we had recommends the former. Ribs brought to another table looked very good. The desserts brought out-- traditional sundaes and floats-- seemed decent. For next time. Beer selection was quality but a bit sparse, they say they are getting more in soon, wine selection good and wine-pours generous. Their liquor license is being finalized, so no liquor as yet. The one aspect I didn't like (hence 4.5 stars) were the two oversized Â television screens at either side of the bar-- at the time, showing a baseball game. They seemed incongruous and distracting given the particular low-key dining and hanging-out vibe. The idea is probably to attract the probably relatively high percentage of sports watchers in the area, and it very well might. But sports bars usually aren't my thing, and if this becomes the general vibe, I'll have to make my regular haunts a little farther away on Cortelyou. They also offer free wifi-- although, considering the current vibe, and that they open in the evening, it would seem a bit awkward to sit there working on a laptop. It seems that they're simultaneously trying all channels to see which one is most profitable, and hopefully this experimentation will settle into an atmosphere organic and welcoming rather than unnatural and offputting. Definitely a welcome addition to the neighborhood: so far the only decent bar/restaurant in the southern Ditmas Park area. May it be a harbinger of more.

Wasn't a fan of the hashbrowns here. Had to use a TON of ketchup and salt to overcome my lack of desire for them. I love potatoes. I love any product made from them. I especially love hashbrowns. However, I don't really dig hashbrowns that are made from what seems to be lumpy mashed potatoes that were then lightly fried in a skillet. I enjoy the shredded stuff that is buttery and crispy, which these aren't. But. BUt. BUT. The biscuits here are AH-mazing. So incredibly delicious. They are the type that are flaky, buttery and will stick to the roof of your mouth if consumed to quickly. The jam that is served with them is wonderful. Not overly sweet or too bitter... just perfect. I think it was raspberry, but wasn't 110% percent certain. Delicious. I didn't try anything else on my first trip, but I also didn't want to take away all the mystery in one go. I like to build into love. I went on a Sunday morning at 10 am and got my food to go. I ate it in the sunshine at a nearby park. Other folks who decided they would wait on a table were told that there would be an hour wait. The prices are swell and the food is worth it. For a biscuit and a side of hash browns with a small coffee, I paid 8 bucks. Not that bad for a tasty NYC brunch. Also, it is key to note that this establishment is cash only. So bring plenty with you.

Suanne L. and I were both in the midtown/Corporate Office USA area and decided it would only be appropriate to go on a lunch date. Â After perusing our options, we settled on Becco. Â I did not know this until Suanne told me so, but apparently this is one of Lidia's restaurants? First of all, the restaurant is huge and winds around. Â I knew I was going to get lost when my maitre d' led me to a table WAY in the back of the restaurant. Â Pretty sure I almost made a wrong turn into the kitchen. We had olives and a nice basket of assorted bread at the table to snack on until our waiter took our order. Â The spread was great and had undertones of basil. Â I opted for the Sinfonio Di Pasta Â because it seems like it's the thing to do at Becco (when in Rome, do as the Romans do). Â This is so out of character for me because 1) I was brought up that pasta is a side dish and not a meal and 2) from a cost standpoint, pasta is one of the cheapest things for a restaurant to produce en masse and then mark-up the price. For a starter, I selected the seafood and veggie platter. Â It was nice, a plate of grilled and marinated vegetables, along with some octopus. Â The three pastas for the day were a mushroom ravioli, a penne with beef and onions, and spaghetti in a marinara type sauce. Â All of the pasta was al dente, which was great. Â The penne was the best of the three, but I felt like the pasta was lacking a certain something. Â Maybe I was expecting to be wowed by fresh pasta like the way my grandma would make, but the pasta just did not have that. Â The pasta was definitely not inedible and not Olive Garden grade, but it's not the best there is. I would like to come back, though, and see what the rest of the menu is like.

Want to romance a date with a taste of Spain and some sangria in SoHo? Â Boqueria is the perfect choice - here's why: FOOD: Awesome tapas! Â We tried the Bombas de Barceloneta, Cojonudo, and Albondigas. Â Each was very authentic and savory. Â  Albondigas: rich from the quality of the lamb to the creamy dollops of sheep's milk cheese. Â Cojonudo: SMALL - two tiny pieces of bread and chorizo with two perfectly cooked sunny-side-up quail eggs. Â  Bombas: three small bombas with creamy garlic aoili and plenty of seasoning SERVICE: Our server was awesome, making good recommendations, spending just the right amount of time with us, so on and so forth. AMBIANCE: While my date said the spot's decor had a cafeteria vibe, I didn't really get that. Â I liked the high-top seating and the lighting... it is cool how the bar is up front, there is a chef working on prep in the front window, and then in the back is a NEAT and TIDY exposed kitchen. Â  Bottom Line - great spot for tapas in SoHo, be prepared to drop $100 as a couple

From what I have tasted so far, the food is great! I would definitely recommend the eggplant appetizer- best eggplant I have ever eaten. Service was mostly friendly. I only had 2 concerns: 1) They don't have an option for brown rice instead of white rice 2) Traditional Laksa comes with rice noodles, however Â staff refused to substitute the egg noodles they use, for rice noodles when we asked. Aside from these complaints, I would highly recommend this restaurant for good South East Asian cuisine.
Who doesn't like Woorijip for lunch or the Korean munchies ? Only bad thing about this place - aaalways soo crowded !

I can say this is the best Thai restaurant in NYC. As a Thai person, the food really close in Thailand. I brought foreign friends to visit here. They can do a flexible flavor for my friends who can't eat spicy ones. I love the service. They are friendly and professional. Keep doing a good job.
Came here for a happy hour a year ago. Really liked the ambiance, and the cocktails were delicious. Small plates we had were tasty too. Would come back for a dinner since I love med food

I really liked this place! I went for dinner with my boyfriend and its a great date night spot. Â It was buzzing with people, REAL candles on the table and delicious food. Â We shared the burrata to start which was so creamy and delicious, I def recommend this! I had ravioli with mustard greens which was also very good. Â My boyfriend has the veal meatballs which he enjoyed. Â All the food tasted very fresh. I would definitely come back!

For years before moving to NYC, I was looked at strangely for always dipping my fries into mustard...spicy brown mustard at that! Â All the ketchup embracing sheep would sneer at my etiquette blasphemy. Then, I moved to the capital of the world and discovered places like Pommes Frites existed. Sure, eating here frequently will make your ass as wide as the East River. Â But, you got dipping sauces galore to choose from. Â I expanded my horizons and was soon dipping my frites into all sorts of things. The place is a bit of a dump but c'mon...you're in the East Village and you're probably drunk when you're ordering.

Whenever my friends and I are in the mood for a burger, this is where we come. Â I can honestly say that I prefer this burger to any other I have tried in the city, in Astoria, in Miami, ANYWHERE. Â The bun is buttery, soft, and the perfect vehicle for the tastiest, juiciest burger you will ever have. Â Trust me, you will not leave a single bite behind. Â The fries are amazing (hint - dunk them in the smoky sauce, and while you're at it, why not add some to your burger in lieu of ketchup?). Â :) Â Don't miss out on the fried pickles either. Â They are fluffy bites of heaven. Not in the mood for a burger and fries? Â You should try the to die for macaroni and cheese. Â It is super creamy and delicious. Â They also have a great brunch menu, great brunch drinks and special prices on brunch drinks on the weekend. Â This is also one of the few bars that actually has happy hour specials on weekdays, and my wallet and I thank them for that. Â  The wait staff is amazing - Â always super friendly and great service. Â Additionally, the bartenders are also great and happy to serve you. Â Come to think of it, I've never seen anyone who works here in a bad mood. Â Have your Shazam activated and ready while you're in here too, because they honestly have the best music ever. Â Take my word for it, this bar is beyond travel worthy - so hop on that train and check it out. Â You will love it!!

wowsers! i was totally suspect of this being some gimmicky nyc foodie thing to capitalize on the western fascination with all things india & pop media. and maybe it is? but you know what else it is? fucking fantastically flavorful and fun! such a cute little spot at a great price point. i stopped in from the rain (and a failed bead shopping adventure in the fashion district! ohhhh bambi deer dress you shall remain nakedly beadless!!!) ok... anyhow. kati does it up right. fast. cheap. yum. think punjab street food fare but super user friendly for your less courageous food friends and still tasty enough for your seasoned international couch surfers ;)~ i had the chai. excellent. fresh chutney... not really unique but def. fresh and comforting. the paneer roll and the unda chicken (tikka plus eggs!!!) omg. perfectly hits the spot. cant wait to take a date here :D

I was excited to come here, not just because my boyfriend's name is Jacob, but because I LOVE PICKLES. My sister and I arrived and it was fairly crowded. Surprisingly, we only waited about 5 minutes before sitting at the communal table. We ordered the combo of 4 pickle types, but that was toooooo much for two people. It was nice to get the variety, but totally ruined my appetite with vinegar. We ordered two beers and a biscuit to cleanse the pallet, but we ended up going somewhere else for dinner. 5* for our waiter though, he was AWESOME.
Solid tacos and margaritas, i like the fish tacos the best.

I really, really wanted to like this place but when all was said and done, I could only justify 2.5 stars. The place is small, which is ok, but the tables are uncomfortably close together and it's very loud inside. The food was good and the wait staff was nice, but they weren't very attentive (other than the water boy who earns an A+). Once the food was served they never checked back to see if everything was ok. The bread was stale and it would've been nice I have some parmesan cheese with my meal. When I was finished eating they never brought the check. After 15+ minutes I pulled out my credit card and stopped a waitress and asked for the check. She surprisingly asked, "don't you want desert dear?". I said ok and tried the chocolate cake. It came out instantly, but it was just ok -- after throwing my napkin over the desert and pushing it away to show I was done, another 10 minutes passed and still no bill. Nobody ever came to check on me to see if everything was ok during dinner or after desert. Overall, the food was just ok and they were great at seating and serving, but after I received my food I felt abandoned.

Overall an "OK" experience. Came her for Valentine's Day with the bf. The food was good....service was fair at best. There was an average of about 15 minutes between our courses and they forgot the amuse portion of the pre fixe menu. And.....the bus boy had major issues with invading personal space! I'll be back to Aurora but it will definitely be the WillyB location.....always stellar there!

Going to Paris this summer with my fiance, so figured I'd prep a bit. Wow. No wonder why this restaurant is a New York City mainstay and so popular. Amazing service. Â Attentive and full of knowledge. Maybe even a bit too smart. Great looking staff- guys and girls. Am i allowed to say that as a straight dude? Why not! Â Went for breakfast with coworkers- tried a couple egg dishes, oatmeal, etc. All really good. For sure would go back.

Meh, It's okay for a chilled night if you have a great group of friends with you, don't expect to come here to find a fascinating crowd. The food is quite good, and very well priced. The atmosphere is cosy and noisy. It's a cute place, but, as I said, don't expect it to be a crazy night.

You know what the greatest thing in the world is? Going back to the place you haven't been for eleven years, and loving it just as much as you did the first time. My friend and I stumbled on Corner Bistro more than a decade ago while visiting Manhattan and it has since become a nearly fabled experience--for the fact of its great atmosphere, awesome jukebox and tasty, tasty burgers. The same friend now lives in Manhattan and together we returned to the fabled spot to find it somewhat more crowded than in 1997, but the place was still as raucously charming as I remembered it and the burgers were still out of this world. It is not a place to be missed if you're a burger connoisseur traveling or living in New York City. Just don't expect any warm fuzzy service, and if you sit at the bar, don't be afraid of being splashed with a little beer.

I am not Â crazy about the food here... I get that their thing is kangaroo meat, but their vegetarian/vegan options are really not tasty... I got the vegan tacos and I didn't really want to finish them. Just very bland and not a pleasing texture either... ick idk. Just bad. I know people will say that's the price I have to pay for being a vegetarian, but I know many other establishments that tackle this obstacle just fine ;) I know my friend wasn't too keen on her fish and chips either and left a lot of it untouched. (Our boyfriends chowed down on the delicious kangaroo burger in the meantime lol. Apparently that was a hit!) That being said, our waitress was fantastic, and the free draft or glass of wine with lunch specials is a really great deal.

Delicious! I took a date here and we had a fantastic experience from start to finish. The sommelier was very helpful with the wine selection (glasses of the Vina Albredi Tempranillo Reserva 2007 Rioja Alta) and the food was perfect. We ordered: ~ Brussels Sprouts w/ squash puree, lime - who can resist roasted brussel sprouts? The smell alone is worth the order. ~ Hamachi Tartare w/ sweet potato, wasabi, ponzu, shiitake - yummy! ~ Pork Belly w/ hominy, chili broth, lime - great ~ Short Ribs with mashed potato, red wine, shallots - fall apart delicious! The portions are sizable for tapas but it was phenomenal experience. Will return again!

I felt like I was Italy! So a wonderful afternoon. Road the bikes down for summer streets and stopped for a lovely afternoon. The bread smelled so good! Yummy focaccia and French bread. We had lasagna and linguine with clams. Great memory and we will be back!

What happened to the Song I remember? When Song opened, they had amazing food, larger than needed portions (I heart leftovers), and good wait staff. I've kept coming back since I live nearby, and it seems that over the last year, they have slowly gotten less and less impressive. They are usually hit or miss, but I took my mother who was visiting, hoping for a 'hit'. First off, our waiter looked and acted like he either, a) was transititioning into becoming a full-time zombie waiter b) had been awake for 3 days c) didn't care We tried repeatedly to get his attention, but whenever he would look our way he would only look at our plates, not noticing me turned around, directly facing him, while trying to make eye contact. I also don't think I even heard a real word come out of his mouth the entire time. Seriously, I could be wrong, but I don't even recall him making an affirmative sound when we were ordering so we could tell he got our order. Now normally I respect the quiet type, but the problem is that my girlfriend has allergies and we tried for 10 minutes to get the waiter's attention to see if there was any gluten in the summer rolls, we literally gave up... I got the Pad See Eww, which I've had many times both at Song and elsewhere, it was slightly burnt for sure and tasted sweeter than the dish should be. Song, please, go back to whatever you were doing before, because at this rate I don't think I'll return. Not to brag or anything, but I make better Thai than you do at this point. My Last comment, the music is too loud, I'm no old fart or anything but it's damn hard to have a conversation.

For all the hype surrounding this place, I found it only to be "A-OK". The portions are VERY small and if you expect to be full, then you might be shelling out a lot of dough (dinner for two came out to be around $180 w tax and tip, plus we ordered a cheap bottle). For that much money, if you can't wow me with your extremely tasty dishes, you'd at least better make me full and tipsy. Alas, neither was the case and the overall experience did not quite match the expenditure. I did enjoy watching the chefs cook everything and they did seem to place a lot of care into making each dish. As you may have heard, its much like MomofukuKo where the chefs cook it in front of you except that instead of the chefs actually serving you themselves, there is a waitress in behind the bar explaining and serving the dishes. It was like a cross between hibachi without the cool knife tossing show, and a Waffle House. The croquettas were very tasty as was the rabbit. However, there wasn't much food. I didn't find the octopus to be be any special. I had to end up ordering another plate of croquettas. Had I not gone with a lovely date, I may have been a little angry at the whole thing.

Great pizza, but was infuriated to see that even out in Bucshwick the 'half glass empty' cocktail trick is taking place. Â I ordered a $15 cocktail. Â I try to avoid doing that usually, especially at brunch (whoops). Â When I received the cocktail it was in a small glass only filled half way. Â It literally looked like someone drank the first half of my cocktail. Â I've seen some establishments in Manhattan do this, but come on, we can't bring this practice to Brooklyn. Â It's a $15 cocktail people. Â $15! Â You can get a dress at Forever 21 at that price. In the defense of Roberta's, I really should have said something. Â They deserve to know that this will not fly. Â The only reason I didn't speak up was because I could tell my guests from out of town didn't want any trouble. Â Next time though, next time.

Although perfectly competent, Adrienne's PizzaBar epitomizes FiDi to me. Â Relatively mediocre pizza (don't get me wrong - it's fine, but nothing I would ever seek out) at sky-high prices, all at high-high volume. The best meal you can get here is the "old-fashioned" square pizza, Â together with a glass of sangiovese. Â Sure, the sauce isn't garlicky enough, and there's something unsatisfying about the crust, other than the little fried bits around the edges, but it's pretty good and makes you at least remember good pizzas you've had in the past. But, while you're eating, you'll wonder why you didn't just go to the slice shop down the street, get a cola, and save $20.

This place was amazing. Â Delicious, beautiful food. Â I'm a slightly picky eater, and this place is one I would easily visit again and again. Â  We got the "meat lovers" combo of arepas for a group of 3, along with the appetizers yoyos (deep fried plantains with white cheese) and tequenos (deep fried white cheese wrapped in dough). Â EVERYTHING was amazing. Â We couldn't stop eating the appetizers and could have eaten more even if we were full. Â Then the arepas came, which were incredible. Â Perfect texture combos, flavors, everything. Â We were completely satisfied. Â  Highly recommended.

I've passed by this place almost everyday for the past two years on my way to work and finally decided to try it. Went in for lunch on Thursday with a friend, the food was great, but the service really made it awesome. Our server (red headed girl) was so nice and incredibly friendly, and actually honest with her suggestions. The Â zucchini fries that came with my friends wrap...insane. 4 stars only because it is a tad pricey for what you get, but otherwise I definitely reccomended.

This place reminds me of Long Island summertime. Since I live just down the street I probably eat too much Lobster Joint. The portions are large so they are good for sharing, My wife and I basically do two orders. Appetizer of fried oysters, a lobster salad, and a bowl of clam chowder. $34 Fish and Chips, and lobster roll with side salad, and side vegetable. $35 Since the is limited table service and often a full house we usually get it to go: The only thing I have had here that wasn't good was the burger and that was a while ago so I don't even know is they are using the same patty. Their kitchen is also open late which is great.

I tried the merguez (lamb sausage), beef and feta "cigars", and mint iced tea today. Â All were delicious. Â  I can't wait to return to try the lemon chicken over couscous. Â  The sausage sandwich is delicious. Â I can't be too effusive, because I am not a huge sausage lover. Â The sausage are nicely flavored, and the bread is perfect. Â I am not a big bread fan, but this bread is just as I like it...soft, flaky, flavorful. Â I think there should be one or two more sausages on it, and definitely more veggies. Â I got the hot sauce on top, and boy it was hot. Â I am good with hot food, and this made my nose run it was so hot! Â There are 3 hot sauces to choose from, so you don't need to be as masochistic as me. Â I felt like the fillings were skimpy, although tasted great. Â  The tea perfectly compliments the food, so I would recommend you don't skip it. Â My only complaint is that $3 for an iced tea seems unreasonably high. Â It is delicious, but how about $1.50 or $2? The beef and feta "cigars" (basically borek, or phyllo rolls) are so good. Â They are $3 for 2. Â Great snack. Â They come on a few mixed greens. Â The sauce they pour over the rolls is wonderful. Â  I always find it frustrating trying to find food trucks lately...they don't seem to park in the same spots all the time, and you have to be a socially networked Sherlock Holmes to track lunch down nowadays. Â Anyways, I found the truck on 38th and Broadway. Â  I walked my lunch over to Bryant Park and enjoyed the beautiful weather with some great food in the park. Â Life is good. Â  This truck puts the halal chicken over rice meals to shame. Â Gourmet food from a truck! Â The bar has been raised! Friendly service, cute chef, great food! Â I would return and I would recommend.

Classic spot. Low key with most amazing drinks you can ask for. Had dinner as well and the steak tartare was delicious. Potatoes on point . Brussel sprouts were great also. Oysters were a little off. Otherwise Take a date here, you won't regret it. I'm a regular from now on

Hands down, my favorite restaurant in Ridgewood. What a great addition to the neighborhood. The back patio was great during the summer. The staff is very friendly and attentive. The food is AMAZING. Everything I've had was delicious. Pollo Pastor taco, Chili Relleno, and the corn are just a few of my favs. The desserts are always on point too. I hope this place sticks around, its a real gem.

We were wandering around my old neighborhood on my birthday, and looking for a nice happy hour spot where we could sit outside...thanks to my amazing happy hour phone app, we kept going into places to see if theyd let us do the hh specials outside, so we could sit in the sun...after about 5 places said no, only at the bar, we were about to give up. Walked from Riviera (vomit from past experiences) across the street and thought we'd give this our last ditch effort, and if they said no we'd just sit at the bar... SUCCESS! they said we could sit outside! and it was pretty empty since early for HH, so we had our pick of tables. Â We'd just had margaritas/coladas at my favorite, Tio Pepe, but i don't like tequila, otherwise would have for sure tried the Cucumber Margarita she said was their specialty (actually I ordered it, but changed it to a glass of the house white). We had dinner in 2 hours, so didn't want to get anything to eat (plus honestly i dont get how people can eat when its hot as F outside??), but the white was a good quantity, and as I'm not a huge wine fan, as good a white wine as anywhere else, and only $5 (which many of the other places who wouldnt let us sit outside had as their prices also). I'll be back, to sit outside and try the cucumber margarita and sangria!

Wondering if I caught them on an off day or not. Saw all the good reviews on Yelp that made me want to try it out and we ordered delivery. The Al Pastor burrito was pretty bad. Rice was dry and stale, pork was dry, nothing notably good at all. Only good thing was they give a pretty good size. The 1/4 chicken was pretty bland also. Sticking to SeÃ±or Pollo for some awesome chicken with nice prices! As for tacos, there's TONS of better places out there!

The sizzling sisig is a must try here, I liked it a lot better than the sisig at Maharlika. Would definitely come back just for this dish. The pork jowl was alright, tasted like the chef got a little lemon-happy it was too citrusy/sour but the brussel sprouts were grilled to perfection. Overall, it was an ok experience. They have an open section so you can see the chefs at work but I almost wish it was hidden because they were not very professional looking, I don't see the point of having an open kitchen here.
Best Mexican in East Village.

Good roast meats here, given the quality of the stuff in Chinatown I would say they are the King Of the Hill on most days. One thing though, is that I NEVER EVER eat in. The service sucks (sucks even for a Chinatown joint standard) and they treat you like someone who has killed their family and devoured their pets.

After hearing good reviews about this place I finally gave it a try. This is basically a bar with an open kitchen that seats around 25 people. I liked the atmosphere but I find it weird that the chefs weren't interacting with the people. I am not asking for the chefs to talk to me for an hour or even 30 min, but if I ask what are you cooking answer me, no eye contact either ... a little weird I'd say! Well I am happy to say the food really was delicious and amazing quality. I tried many many dishes and here we go: -croquetas with potatoes and white fish in a saffron sauce good but not the best dish there - Spanish tortilla with quail egg was yummy - salad with blood orange and sheep milk cheese very tasty and refreshing - sea trout with a potato leek sauce and potatoes YUM loved this light dish -oxtail stuffed squid with a oatmeal rissotto my favorite dish here simply amazing - beef tenderloin was cooked just right -The dessert was amazing too.. caramelized torta.. which was a brioche caramalized on the spot yum! I am glad I got to try this spot!
when in doubt (in china town) just drop in to this place and you wont be dissappointed

Unreal food but the delivery experience is atrocious. They constantly leave you on hold for over 5-10 minutes when attempting to place an order so I generally hang up. Online delivery absolutely needed here

i gently caressed the buns, pouring fiery hot sauce on its supple skin. slowly i brought it to my lips and nibbled, careful not to hurt it but unable to contain carnal desire. a highly indecent moan involuntarily escaped my mouth and the lower half of my body jutted forward lewdly, much to the chagrin of my fellow patrons. that...is how my first meal at shanghai asian manor went.
Joe's.. you are always true to me. Pork & Crabmeat Soup Dumplings. 'Nuff said. (2 orders is enough to split btwn two)

Totto Ramen has done a stand up job in growing as they did from their first couple opening weeks where they were working their kinks out - to today's high standards. Allow me to illustrate. I had previously complained about way too much garlic in my ramen during my first visit (flickr.com/photos/507721â€¦). Now, the proportions are much much better and do without a full layer of garlic over the whole bowl. Totto Ramen has, in essence, redeemed themselves in my eyes. I really do enjoy the Miso Ramen. And although I cannot stomach spicy, they do offer an "Extreme Spicy Ramen" too (which I hear is quite enjoyable for those that enjoy a tasty fire in their mouths). One of my favorite dishes that can be found on printed signs along the window or walls is the Yaki Uni Don. If they are offering this and you enjoy sea urchin, I would highly recommend ordering it. As the description noted, Yaki Uni Don is torched sea urchin with the chef's special sauce served over rice, cucumber, and Kombu seaweed. Diner represents everything that's cool about Williamsburg, and none of the things that suck about Williamsburg. Â It's privately owned, intimate, extremely high quality, cute (the building tilts west -- seriously), stylish, and fun. Â It's not a haven for tourists, it's not a scene spot, and it's not pretentious. Â The service has always been friendly and, despite a menu that doesn't read too differently from an old diner menu, the dinner specials are the type of fare you'd expect at top-tier Manhattan restaurants. Â Add to the mix their sister spot next door, Marlow & Sons, and Diner is really a Southside powerhouse.
Visited sunday april 7th staff rude Â 9 dollar mixed drinks hardly any alcohol. Food terrible.They add a 20% GRATUITY!!! only 2 people.

Off of the first floor of ABC Carpet and Home, Jean-Georges Vongerichten's ABC Kitchen carries through the store's inspiring, dreamy and artistic vibe. Decorated in white with wooden beams and beautiful chandeliers, the space is both elegant and rustic. The menu is locally sourced, hence its "local organic home" tagline. This was the perfect spot to catch up with old friends. Here's a review of the dishes the four of us ordered family style, each of which was served with a beautiful presentation. For the full details and pictures, visit my blog. Cured meats and local cheeses - OK Roasted beets with housemade yogurt - HIGHLY RECOMMEND Bibb salad (this was one of the night's specials) - HIGHLY RECOMMEND Line caught tuna sashimi marinated with ginger and mint - MUST HAVE Crispy soft shell crab, red watercress, sweet and sour chili glaze - RECOMMEND Whole wheat pizzas - MUST HAVE

This place is a hidden gem. Its on an old gorgeous cobblestone street tucked away a block from the south st. seaport. The place is small and cozy, but the menu and service are great! Love the decor too. Just a pleasure to be here instead of crowded noisy places in financial district. Going here for the 3rd time, and i know there will be many more!
Some of the best pizza you could ever try.

Ate at Salt & Fat and Momofuku Ko on the same weekend. Honestly couldn't tell the difference, except for a huge disparity in prices. Got 11 out of 17 items on the menu and all were equally amazing. Get: Yellowtail tartare, Shaved Foie Gras, Uni Toast, Roasted Berkshire Pork Belly Wasn't ecstatic about the Oxtail Terrine. The Lychee Panna Cotta with Yuzu Sorbet for dessert. Pros: Everything. Cons: Regret not getting all 17 items, especially the BLT buns.

My NYC foodie friends recommended that I have lunch here and I'm glad I did. Â I sat at the counter and had the highly recommended pork buns and modern ramen bowl. Â Food was fantastic, my waitress was attentive & helpful and the atmosphere was so much fun. Â I love how they yell out the orders in Japanese (even the non-Japanese workers do this). Â Would eat here again anytime.

This is the best pizza I have had in NYC and it's in my neighborhood...score! Â The servers are great. Â The wine selection is a little limited. Â This place has become one of my favorite restaurants.

This place is great. Â I do not like that I cannot substitute things on the Menu. Â I understand your reasoning and I'm not trying to be difficult. Â I do have certain allergies, so it would be nice If I can order what I want..sheesh. Either way I love the food here..so maybe they can put this review on my tombstone.

One of those rare ctown places where you absolutely need a reservation if you want to get a table during a decent hour without waiting too long. We came during a torrential down pour and thankfully we had a reservation. Surprisingly the weather did little to deter people from lining up to eat here. Good thing they have a long walkway lined with seats just for this purpose. As most people have pointed out, the $22 AYCE hot pot is good, for it's value and quality of ingredients. For $30, you can do both hotpot and Korean BBQ which is what the 4 of us did. I found it overwhelming to gorge on hotpot and bbq at the same time so I think I'll only do the hotpot next time. For the hotpot I went with the spicy soup base, basically a sichuan style broth. From the sauce station, I chose sa cha sauce, garlic, scallions, vinegar, sesame oil and chili oil. We also asked for raw eggs to mix in with our sauces. I loved the sauce I made for myself but if it doesn't float your boat they offer 20+ mix and match options. The veg and meat selections we chose were all pretty fresh and good so no complaints there. I think my favorite was the tofu skin because of the way it absorbs all of the flavor from the broth and is ready in about 10 seconds. For kbbq we chose mushrooms, pumpkin, filet beef and boneless steak. The quality of the meat was pretty standard for the price. I'm not sure if I'd return to try other selections off their bbq menu because they haven't quite figured out the logistics of their bbq grill top. The grill tops were not oiled so one round of meat cooking turned our grill tops charcoal black. For our 2 plates of meat we did 3 grill changes! We had to refuse profusely when they offered to change it the 4th time. We didn't bother ordering more meat cuz it seemed like more hassle than it was worth. 99, please oil the damn grills!! Service wise, 99 is in a class of it's own. Servers refill soup stock, bring out additional meat/veg orders and change out bbq grills with impressive quickness. You'll definitely get your money's worth in the allotted 2 hour window.

So far I've been here for lunch and happy hour. Â Staff is very courteous and attentive. Anyone who goes must have the Phonecian fries... they are one of the best fries I've every had!! Lamb burger was juicy and very tasty. Â Happy hour drinks are very good, but some of the happy hour food items are hit and miss... Rkaykat bil Jibneh - HIT. Â Mini Kibbeh bi Laban - MISS. Overall great experience, will definitely go back.

mmmm meeaatball... we stopped in to get our meatball fix. my girl being a veg, it's a perfect place, as they have vegballs to offer... she ordered the samwich with pesto and a side salad. Â i tried a couple balls (the buffalo chicken and the pork with spicy (pork) sauce) and had a side of greens. my balls were good (ha). not great... sad to say, but good. my sweetheart's sandwich seemed to make her happy... though she mentioned pesto would not be her first choice next time... but enough about that. let us talk about the dessert... design your own ice cream sandwich. Â good lord... yes! sooooo good. i recommend the mint chip. no matter what you do for the cookie. Â  i crave that mint chip. prepare to be wowed. all in all, we will be definately be back for some balls and cream sandwiches.

I called ahead of time to make a reservation because Open Table would not allow me to make a reservation during happy hour (5-7 everyday even weekends!). I arrived to a packed place but Â this was expected. After all it was 6 pm on a beautiful Saturday afternoon. I arrived with only half of my party and was seated in a fair amount of time. I thoroughly enjoyed my food and wine selections, the ambiance and the Â the cute touches like the petite bread sac and the books they give the receipt in. However, what I did not appreciate was the lag between our arrival and our orders being taken. We were seated at 6:15 and no one took our orders until 6:48. I really would have liked to try more happy hour priced wine flights but due to the slowness of the waiter I could only order one. Even when the number of patrons had dwindled down the staff seemed distracted and unattentive. At least twice I remember us flagging someone down to place another order. SMH. This was truly disappointing in light of the fact that I heard so much about their customer service.
Great atmosphere, great sushi, great addition to the neighborhood! I've come back multiple times and enjoy trying their new options.

Disappointing. Â Decided to give it another try since the food was good on our first visit. Â  Â  And I had been getting updates from the owners via email that they got even better brisket. What a disappointment. Â The pulled pork did not have the authentic smoked BBQ taste. Â Seemed like it was boiled and the brisket lacked flavor. Â Plus we were there around 6 pm on Saturday and they were out of ribs and sausage so they only had pork and brisket. Â They also changed the counter service. Now is sit down service, which I usually prefer. Â  Well service would not be the word I use. Â It took over 30 min to get out food and no one checked on us during that time. At the end the server mentioned that "oh sorry your food took so long" but by than it was too late. Â Sorry Delancy you are not a BBQ place for this Longhorn girl!!!! Â Bring back your previous brisket recipe and counter service!!!!

The Jane was ok. We liked the food but thought it was too expensive for what it was. The food is good but not exceptional. We would go back if someone else suggested it but it's not top on our list of places to check out again. Their milk and cookies dessert was good too but they put the ice cream in the milk. The cookies were pretty tasty and warm.

If your are looking for a nice quiet ramen place then this is not the place for you! As soon as you enter they cheer and chant whatever it was in Japanese which was cool I guess but they do it again after you order too. I just wanted a nice quiet dinner alone. The seating also places you at a table with others if you are a party of 1-2 peoples. And its a noisy place when packed. The atmosphere was dark and dim. The staff were attentive and polite. The ramen are all 15$+ I wouldnt order the Miso ramen it wasnt that great and I recommend the special house ramen instead for 17$. That being said, if you have been to ramen chains like samurai noodle then you are not missing much. they taste the same. Except that Samurai noodle is 5$ cheaper.

Gotta love this spot. It's two blocks from my home and it has such delicious goodness coming from that kitchen. Not to mention the cool and chill eclectic brand of people who populate the restaurant. The servers and the service was responsive. We were sat quickly and tended to quickly as well. The breakfast was delicious. I had a French omelet. Super-fresh. Goat cheese and smoked salmon. What more can I say?

Very good Thai food at reasonable prices. My only complaint was cold rice but I called it to their attn and they quickly and cheerfully replaced it with a hot bowl. Best Thai green mango salad that I have had ANYWHERE!

My partner and I needed a place to grab a bite New Year's Eve night before we headed out to a party. We were thinking of Croxleys because I love their cheap wings but then we decided to instead try out this cute little cafe. It was very warm and welcoming when we stepped in and we were seated right away. I was starving so I ordered the eggs, which come with potatoes, whole wheat toast and a little salad. I was very pleased with my meal because it tasted good and it was very filling. My boyfriend ordered the chicken parm with spaghetti and it was delish but he couldn't finish it all. Also sampled a pitcher of sangria which tasted wonderful and came abundant with chunks of fruit. I would definitely stop here again because it's a lovely little corner cafe with polite service and tasty food.

Went here on a whim the other day. It's been in my bookmarks to try for such a long time. I was a little worried thinking that the portion size might be a little too small for me cause I'm a slob and don't know when to stop eating a good meal but when I got here I was a little intimidated by the way this place is set up. I thought I was walking into someones basement or something like that but was easily relaxed when I saw all the patrons laughing and enjoying this place. Ordered the meat platter to start off and was pleasantly surprised at the quality of meats that were served for this dish. I couldn't wait to get my entree now. The liver and eggs. Creamy scrambled eggs with big chunks of Foie Gras on delicious bread. Although I could have eaten 5 orders of this, it was awesome. Everything on the menu sounded great and different. Â Never had anything like this. Place is a little pricey for what you get but the food is top notch. Great place with great staff. They also sell their homemade flavored jellys and jams.
I have been to Tuome twice and both time have been great experiences. Â This latest time I went and had the Pork for 2 which was delicious and perfectly cooked as was the side of peanut noodles.

Before I mention anything at all, this is one of BONO'S favorite brunch spots when he's in the City. Bono! Two different friends of mine met him two different times when he was dining on the patio. Anyways, This is one of the BEST brunches I've ever had in NYC...and for the price, too! This place is definitely the kind of place you'll want to take your mom, aunt, or best friend when they're visiting: white tablecloths, fresh flowers on tables, etc. Read: this place is probably not great for rowdy groups. You get a coffee, a brunch drink, and an entree- all for less than $20! And they even brought us a bread basket with different pastries before, too! This definitely helps me not be hangry. (But seriously...) TIP: Make sure to make reservations if you can! My friend and I were lucky because we got there early and there were just two of us. But otherwise, I've heard wait times can get kind of crazy.
Went here for brunch a few weeks ago...and it was really enjoyable...the food was delicious and well put together....it was a nice atmosphere, not too expensive either!

this place was recommended by my friends ...we all went there together, as i was visiting nyc. Â they wanted to go because they said that it was so cute and reminded them of portland (which is where i live). they were right! so cute and portlandy. the food was really great. there were 3 of us and we shared 3 things...a sandwich, a salad, and a hummus thing....all of which were excellent. we also shared a pitcher of belgian beer (even though it was the afternoon---vacation style), which was served in the cutest old lemonade pitcher thing. Â awesome! i will definitely have my friends put it on their lists of places to go if they are gonna visit the big apple.

the food was good although the apple wings didn't really taste much like apple. They were good though. The atmosphere is borderline nice but it's a bit disheveled and not quite neat in this space. Feels not disheveled enough to be a dive bar but not put together enough to be a trendy kind of place, so I'd say it's missing on a cohesive identity. The mushroom fettucine was really good and the serving size was excellent. Also the drink specials for happy hour were pretty good deals.

Spicy noodles: huge portion, tasty, cheap. What's not to love? I like the decor--I've used that paint color in my own domicile, so perhaps I'm biased. I was a little puzzled why the menu only has beer and wine, yet there's a full bar. Is it because I was there on a Sunday at 6? Is this a blue law or something? My closet alcoholic brain is easily confused. And not from New York. The cash only thing sucks. They do redeem themselves a bit by being fast, both to bring food and to wrap it up. But I definitely want to come back and try some of the other things on the menu. And one of those giant vodka bottles in the back. I'll bring cash, I promise...

Obvs my favorite place in the universe. Everything is delicious and everyone is so nice. The cinnamon buns, especially the maple walnut pumpkin or whatever ones are giant and just unbelievably good. A vegan's paradise and my friend's who aren't vegans also extra love all of the baked beauty here!

Came here a little before 2pm on a Friday in August, and was pleasantly surprised that the wait would only be around 5 min. Granted I was only one person, but there was barely anyone waiting outside (though the interior was pretty full). I had the Totto Spicy Ramen with the seasoned boiled egg as a topping. The ramen was pretty good, though the egg was what shined. This was not your ordinary boiled egg. The yolk was golden perfection, not a hint of green/grey at the exterior and was cooked just enough so it wouldn't be runny. The egg seemed to have been marinated in soy sauce, so the exterior was stained light brown. God, I would have ordered three of these babies if I had no self control.

It was ok. Â I came here on Saturday around 11:30a with a group of 12. Â There weren't many people which was good for us. Â I had the chicken burrito, roscoe on a stick, and mango juice. It feels like it's a gastropub, but it isn't one. It's a coffee shop basically. That's kind of disappointing. I got tuna/avocado tacos that were delicious. My girlfriend got a salad with a generous helping of avocado. I love places that are generous with avocados. Happy hour is 4-7 everday, and I got a delish IPA.

This is truly the best pizza in New York.This is an incredible place to visit. I live in Manhattan but I went to this small pizza place in Midwood,Brooklyn because I saw on Time Out Magazine that DiFara Pizza was nominated as the number #1 Â place of new york. The owner makes each pizza one by one and people are patiently waiting as he slowly prepares each pizza. Some BOMB bbq in Williamsburg at Fette Sau. Â I was skeptical, as I always am, when someone says: 'we're eating in Brooklyn'. Â *shudder* Â  But I made the short trek through the L tunnel, and I'm glad I did. Â I had the Top Sirloin, Broccoli salad, and the Key Lime pie. Â Top that off with a large selection of draught beers and you have one happy Devin. Â The sirloin was delicious, with that smoky char outer edge, and the inner red tender meaty goodness. Â All said and done, it only put a $15 hole in my wallet. Â DELICIOUS AND AFFORDABLE. Â Seating is like cafeteria bench style and is first come-first serve. Â Also, a huge line will form on peak days and hours, BEWARE Â (but it's worth the wait).

Walked into Stix with a few girlfriend and had a great time, this place is certainly different from the 20 restaurants in the few block radius! The food was yummy and super healthy! I especially loved the skewered lamb and tuna. Stix is also great for groups since you get to share everything. Desserts are great too, hands down best part was the chocolate cake! The service was great as well, the manager came up to us several times to make sure everything was great, it is definitely refreshing to enjoy such a friendly atmosphere. If you are looking for a fun atmosphere, with great food at reasonable prices, this is the place for you!

God I love this place. I've been going for years and it is so consistent, it's mindblowing. EVERY SINGLE TIME I order the Coconut Shrimp Sandwich the shrimp are grilled PERFECTLY! It's kind of amazing cause strangely most people don't know or care to cook a beautiful prawn going into a sandwich. They do and do so so consistently. The bread from Parisi is awesome. The pickled carrots and cilantro and spicy mayo are all so delicious. The Bluefish is awesome when they have it as is the mackerel. The cauliflower is always very good and their summer gazpacho is always perfectly balanced. They are usually very busy and efficient with blowing thru their line. I love Num Pang. I rarely get so excited about going for a "sandwich".

H-Y-P-E....it's a word that can make or break a place. Â Luckily, Cafe Habana lives up to the hype and then some: - superb grilled corn on the cob - margaritas, micheladas, mojitos - while waiting for a table I've tried the trifecta of "M" cocktails and they are made to perfection. - rice and beans are fo'real.....authentic, flavorful and delish! If only it wasn't so damned crowded all the time...it would totally be 5-star worthy!

A couple of the pancake dishes are pretty good, especially the Danish pancakes. The other dishes are decidedly not worth the wait on weekend mornings. The fries and oranges on the waiting line are a nice touch.

I must admit, having been a huge fan of Wombat (who previously occupied the space), I didn't want to like this place. Â Finally went in after months of holding out, and now I cannot believe I waited so long. Â Nice cosy atmosphere, diverse yet non-initmidating menu, and nice staff make it an easy place to hang out. I have to echo what most are saying about the creamy polenta- it is DELICIOUS. Â As is the broccoli rabe, and the meatballs, which taste like they were made with love, which makes sense, considering the recipe belongs to the mother of the owner of the place. Â We've already been back several times and have every intention of making it one of our regular spots!
best ramen in the city! must must must order the pork buns to start with. they dont' take reservations so expect to wait. lunch is easier to get into than dinner.
I frequent this place. Love their po boy sandwiches. U must try the sweet potato fries, come back on a weekend for brunch and try the french toast and hot peaches yum :-)

4 of us ate here and all enjoyed our food which included a Filet Mignon, Chicken Boiled in Vinegar, Grilled Salmon and the Seabass Special. We were unable to eat dessert due to the Portion Sizes which were very large. We enjoyed a lovely bottle of Nero Sicilian Red Wine.

why all this fuss about this cart it normal and there are a lot of carts serve better food than this one ,they raised the price 1$for the plate and they serve less amount of food so stop exaggerating please

I think this is the best round slice in the city. Â That being said, go during off-peak hours on a weekday because the wait is pretty awful. Â $5 a slice is also a hard sell, but I can only rationalize it because watching Di Fara make each pie by hand is kind of amazing - I'd suggest getting a whole pie for the best deal.

Absolutely the BEST (and that's an understatement) breakfast I've ever had!!!! I read about Clinton St last year and the reviews were so phenomenal I knew it was a must stop when I went back to NYC. My friends and I went Memorial Weekend and stopped in for breakfast on a Friday morning. Even though we were 7, the wait was only about 30 minutes. Now on to the good stuff: FOOD!!! We each ordered something different and tasted each others food and I must say, there was nothing, and I mean NOTHING that wasn't good. I had the much talked about french toast. It had savory bananas, pecans, and the most amazing maple butter! It was heaven on a plate! My friend ordered the blueberry pancakes and let me tell you, I'm not a fan of blueberries on pancakes but this was something else. The pancakes were fluffy and moist, and the blueberries gave it this subtle sweetness that just made me want to rub it all over my body!!! Their homemade jam was another thing we couldn't stop raving about. It was so amazing I had to ask if they sold it and much to our disappointment they didn't. It was so good we each wanted to stick it in our purses and walk away. All I know is every morning I wake up and dream of the moment I will be reunited with Clinton St. Baking Company!!!
Pastas are amazing, and prices are reasonable for the awesome value. Â  Very difficult to get reservations, but if you don't mind early dinner it is worth it!

Pretty awesome place. 2 for $5 pulled pork is definitely a win as everyone else says. Huge selection of beers from all over the world, I'm no beer connoisseur, but if you are this is your place. We went during lunch time and saw two different families that brought their kids in. Pretty cool to share the pulled pork with your 10 yo son/daughter. Fries were tasty and crisp. They also have a good selection of board games. Jenga FTW! I think this place was once owned by Alan Corey, the guy who wrote A Million Bucks by 30.

First of all... order the pork dumpling soup. Multiple orders if you are with more than couple people. Tell the waiters what you like, and trust them. This place couple possibly be the best Chinese I have ever eaten next to House of Nan King in San Francisco. Do yourself a favor, if you are in NYC and go there

Best. Pizza. In. NYC. Period. I heard about the wait - but lucked out as it only took about 30 mins to get seated, even on a Saturday night. Â I think it also helped that I was only with one other person. We sat upstairs, over looking the lower dining room. Â It's a no fuss place - simple menu. Ordered a large pie and it was served quickly. Â Light, airy dough, just enough sauce and toppings. Â Perfect balance of flavors. On the loud side - but the price can't be beat. Â For one topping, large pie and a soda/bottle of water - $20.

I've been here a couple of times for dinner, and it's always lovely! Yes it's small and crowded and can get noisy, but I think it's still intimate, and not overbearing. Â Cash only and byob always makes for a last minute dash to the atm, but as long as you prepare ahead of time, it's not a big deal. Â  Â  Â  Â  So. The food. Â The bread and butter is delicious. I've had the onion tart more that once, and while it's not my favorite onion tart I've ever had, it is really good. Â The onions are prepared wonderfully, and the frisee salad it's garnished with is really nice. I have had the chicken paillard, simple, but good. Â The salad was simple and fresh, and the chicken was cooked well. Â Overcooked chicken drives me crazy, so that was lovely. Â I've also had the warm kale salad and SHUT UP it so good. If you're debating between that and something else, GET IT. Â I've also tasted the Bouchee a la Reine, the french onion soup, and managed to miss out on the escargot, just got the sauce. Â All really really good as well. Â The food is fairly priced for the quality, and is well prepared. Â Service is pretty good; things can take a second because of the amount of customers vs. servers, but the people have always been super nice and made good suggestions (See: Kale Salad.). Â Both times I've it's been at around 8 on a Saturday, and have been seated almost immediately. Â I think we lucked out, because I know there can be a bit of a wait. Â The second time half our party left and two of us just hung out for a bit, finishing our wine before our show, and they were very nice about it. Â The food is good, the service is good, and if you're bringing white wine, for goodness' sake make sure it's already cold. Â I'll definitely keep going back, but I'm not sure if I'll be trying new things or just going back to that damn kale salad.

Nam Nam. One word that is said twice has the same appeal to me as Mahi-Mahi, Couscous and the famous saying about New York City. "The city so nice, they named it twice". This is what I was feeling as I took a bit of my Classic Banh Mi. This is a new spot that just opened up in "East" Wiliamsburg. It's good to have a Banh Mi spot in every neighborhood I go to. The place is very welcoming and with a "feel at home" vibe. There is seating outside if you prefer to smoke or people watch while you eat. Every new place I go to get a Banh Mi, I always go for the classic. I think about if they can't get the classic right. What about all the other sandwiches? I was proven wrong. The bread was warm and toasty and the sandwich was filled with thick cuts of meat. I love how they use pate spread so each bite has some in it. I was really satisfied with the sandwich. For the price of $5 you are seriously stuffed. Too bad I don't live in the area. This will definitely be one of my stops whenever i'm in the area. They have Bubble Tea...
That's one tender octopus!!

I've only visited once before visiting the city for a show, but man...I can't stop thinking about Kati Roll. The food is cheap, fresh, and crazy tasty. Â Think Indian burrito. Â Excellent flavors, vegetarian options, super portable, and it hits the sweet spot between snack and meal. Â The rolls are a bit greasy, making KRC a perfect treat late night after a couple drinks. Â Here's hoping a Kati Roll opens in Philly!

I had brunch here last Sunday morning with my boyfriend, brother, and his girlfriend, and the experience couldn't have been better. Â Between us, we got the artichoke dip, 2 orders of the egg-white omelette, and 2 orders of the grits/poached eggs. Â We were so full, yet all cleaned our plates - the food was fantastic. Â The artichoke dip really is as good as everyone says. The location, at the end of a mysterious alleyway, is also great - it feels like you've stumbled on a secret. Â The taxidermied animal heads populating all wall space in the entire restaurant are a bit weird, but interesting. Â Our server was friendly and efficient. Â  I normally hate mimosas - too sweet - but I think they make theirs with fresh squeezed OJ, because they were delicious. Â Boyfriend (French and picky) loved his French 75 cocktail, and trust me, that is HIGH acclaim. Â  We didn't have a reservation, but as a group of four, we were fine. Â We just made sure to show up before noon. Â Really can't recommend Freemans for brunch highly enough.

There are no adjectives that can possible do this place justice. Went here with my boyfriend and some friends and everything was beyond perfect. I was a little apprehensive about the group seating ( it's long tables used by all rather than smaller personal ones) but I quickly got over that with my first bite. The brisket is perfection as is the ribs. Moist and tender. It melts on your tongue. There are a variety of sauces on the table to choose from. The vinegar is AMAZING and the habanero is a kick in the tastebuds. The cider they offer is delicious. A little smoother than Angry Orchard. Trying to find parking is a holy nightmare but quickly forgotten once you walk through the door and smell the magnificent aroma of perfectly prepared pig. Def returning!!!!

I really love this place. I been there twice once for dinner and the other for brunch. Dinner was really good and they had great healthy options with a lot of flavor. Brunch was amazing it's $13 which includes 2 drinks (mimosas, screw drvers, bloody Marys) and a selection of coffee, tea or hot chocolate, I tried the crab cakes eggs benedict which were delicious and the steak skillet which was awesome. I can't wait to visit again.

Chicken empanada was off the chain and very inexpensive. Also had the garlic shrimp w red beans and yellow rice. That was just ok. I wasn't super impressed w the garlic sauce or w the beans. But loved the berry sangria and will definitely go back in the future to try something else for the entree.
A nice neighborhood gem . Â Don't just order a pizza . Â I had the pappardelle, the portion was a bit small but done very well .

GOOD LORD!!!! Â this Â place is GOOD!!!!! Â OK calm down!!!! Â Deep breaths!!! Â alright first of all upon entering this place it is once again a fire hazzard :( Â but cozy. Â The fries are freshly made and you have the choice of about 20 different sauces to try from. My girlfriend and I ordered the irish curry, wasabi mayo and one thats called the war sauce. Â It contains a mixture of onions, peanut satay and frite sauce. Â  The irish curry was your typical curry. Â It was ok but it wasnt a WOW with the fries. Â The wasabi mayo on the other hand was great and with a kick it would knock you off your feet. Â The war sauce was also great with a peanut oil base and onions it brought the flavor out of the fries. Â  My favorite was the wasabi mayo but i still didnt try all of them so i dont know which is the best. Â The fries are great and are made by pinoy pride and are of high quality. Â Crispy and flavorfull. Â  The prices are good and of course i just wish the sauces were free. Overall very good place. HELL one of the best places to go in NY. GO NOW!!!!!

this place has had some serious help from overzealous PR campaigns that have hyped it beyond belief. Â after eating here, and THEN reading the reviews, it all makes sense. Â its a severely overpriced restaurant serving tiny portions of sub-par Asian fusion food. Â whats sad in NY today is that it really isnt about the food. Â its about concepts, ingredients, intentions, and backgrounds, which to me, is just all bs if the food doesnt measure up. all these 4 and 5 star reviews are from people who are easily wowed and amused and have nothing else to compare this to. Â also, get some toothpicks.
Overpriced. Sorry, M.O.B. I just wasn't that impressed.

gouda mac-n-cheese..meh, OK, but not as great as some of the reviews make them out to be..sandwiches are pretty big served with a heap of seasoned semi-greasy fries..meatloaf was huge and the tomato salsa/sauce (although a bit on the salty side) was a flavorful touch to an old reliable meatloaf-mashed potatoes-green beans dish.

Brooklyn might be the new Manhattan. I feel myself liking Brooklyn more and more now. Am I turning into a hipster? Probably not, but Brooklyn does have pretty interesting and tasty restaurants, and Bogota Latin Bistro is one of them. We came for a late lunch, after rock climbing over at Brooklyn Boulders. The interior was fab and cozy. Definitely an awesome place for some lunch and good conversation over cheap drinks and tasty food. My friends ordered the pina colada, and a passion fruit frozen margarita. Both drinks were delicious, but for me, was too sweet. For those with a sweet tooth and hates the taste of alcohol, these are the perfect drinks. I decided not to get one because I did not want to climb the walls drunk. For lunch, I ordered the Cuban Sandwich, my friends ordered the chicken and rice, and fish tacos. They also ordered sides of tostones, and this mashed up plantain thing. The Cuban Sandwich was a little on the dry side, but the chipotle dip that came with it made it taste a lot better. It would be a lot better if the pickles and cheese were spread out more evenly. Towards the end, I was just eating chunks of bread. The fries that came with the sandwich were kinda sad, unfortunately. Burnt and brown flimsy looking sticks ended up on my dish. Other than that, nothing really went wrong, except for the mashed up plantain dish. It was really bland, and my friend who is a lover of plantains, said this was one of the worst he's tasted.
