Â On the other hand, my friends really enjoyed their dishes and scoffed theirs down in fifteen minutes. They still managed to make compliments about the food though. I would say that the food was pretty average, but at least the portions were huge, and the drinks are cheap if you go during happy hour. I would come back again for some drinks. It is also an awesome place to get some free condoms. Towards the bathroom, you will see a huge jar full of them. My friend witnessed two old men grabbing many. I see they get lucky. I grabbed 4 and gave one to each of my friends.

I uploaded my photo of the slice I had on 9/18/14. I did not do anything to the slice or the photo, it is original photo. Arrived after the lunch crowd expecting a spare slice to be leftover for a quick purchase. That did not happen, had to wait for that spare.slice to buy for 2 hours and 17 minutes. Placed my one cheese slice order and was told it would be at least an hour and a half before any single slices would be available. Spent that time by hopping on the Q train, went to Coney Island, had two Nathans hot dogs and returned to DiFara 1 hour and 25 minutes later. Was told that I had not missed my slice and it would be about another 45 minutes for my slice to be ready. So roamed around the neighborhood which is a Jewish neighborhood with a very low crime rate and went and had a pastry from the Jewish bakery across the street. When the slice arrived it was quite small without much sauce spread on it. There was a tomato clump near the end, cheese was heavy towards one side and slight on the other. Basil leaves were plentiful and evenly spread. Took several photos of top, sides and the bottom crust. The bottom crust was evenly cooked and crisp. When starting to eat this slice experienced a flavor rush similar to a macaron where you are overwhelmed by strong ingredients. Had to slow down to try to figure out what the flavor rush was caused by. After eating this slice spent about a half an hour outside the open window and studied what the pizzamaker was doing. Spoke to a few people waiting for their pies and read reviews and history of Difara. Here is my advice; retire the founder, originator and expert pizzamaker asap. It is not right to have anyone in this elderly state making every pie, maybe a few hours a week but every pie, every minute, every working hour? People need to stop being selfish and urge him to keep working. There is an entire family working there that can make equal pies and for Â respect all customers can tell the family that the pies they are making are almost as good as the originals and that way everyone is content. For those of you reading my review wondering if it is worth the cost and the wait for single slices the answer is no. If you have several people and $30-$35 to split and blow on a pizza pie then do it. The flavor rush was due to the oil from the melted cheese and olive oil. If my slice was better I would give this review 3 stars, if I had split a pie with others I would have given the review 3 or 4 stars. Is this the best slice of pizza in all of NY or the USA or the world the answer is no. Is this one of the most flavorful pizzas the answer is yes. I recommend going to Pizza Suprema located just soutwest of penn station for quick service, lower cost and a sauce mixture that has its own unique flavor rush. For those on a budget recommend going to Patsy's in east harlem. The cheese only slices are only $1.75 when bought at their takeout area which is next to their restaurant. The slices are from a coal oven with a very tasty sauce and oily cheese. No flavor rush but three slices at $5.25 with at most a 15 minute wait compared to $5 with over a 2 hour wait ar DiFara is no comparison at all
Bahn Mi made fresh and delicious. I have always had a pleasant experience with the girls who work there. All very friendly with a warm & welcoming smile!
Soup Dumplings! Order the shrimp and crab soup dumplings but eat/slurp carefully, those suckers are hot!! Also the scallion pancakes are delicious!
My wife and I still love this place after several years. Â Consistently great. Â One of our go-to's on the upper east side.
Average at best. Not much flavor and price point is not good for the size.

the chicken was amazing!! i was disappointed when my friend and i were refused entry into their outdoor eating area after ordering our food. they said it was table service. if you want to play that card, Â you better get your wait staff ready.to explain your policy.

Made a reservation for Saturday at 7. Party of five. Arrived on Saturday at 7. Many people waiting in the tiny vestibule and outside. Our table wasn't ready until 7:25. And it was a four-person table and they smushed three chairs on one side and two on the other. Couldn't even put the odd chair at the head of the table as there was no room. Service was good. Food was as expected and not too pricey. For some reason can only do three credit cards max. The one in Hells Kitchen is far larger and actually honors reservations.

I had an excellent experience. The food was DELICIOUS and reasonably priced. I loved the food so much I told the table next to me I was going to "Yelp them HARD! " Every dish I had I enjoyed thoroughly. The green sauce was everything! It was tike KABLAM! definitely recommend. Â Sangria was refreshing and did what it was intended to do. Even the music was amazing, I was singing along throughout my meal. I will be back Empanada Mama! Did you hear me? I will be BACK!!!!
Cool ambiance, great food, awesome service. Tomato soup was best I've ever had. Ever had. I shall return. Â Make reservations via Open Table.

We've walked past this place so many times that finally last night we decided to try it. The food was definitely above average. We got the chips and guac app (perfect ratio of chips to guac and pico de gallo) and the carnitas for two (which probably could've fed a family of 3-4). The food was great and very authentic. The noise level was borderline obnoxious (we literally could not hear each other), but I guess that was to be expected as we can usually hear how crazy it is in there just from walking by. I would highly recommend this place for a birthday celebration or just for a night out to enjoy great food and some (loud) company.

To welcome our new coworker I was tasked with finding a fun, yet not too expensive, restaurant near work. Â I'd heard about Market Place and thought that the fresh fare and large bay windows would make a perfect work lunch. Â I was not disappointed. Â We ordered the quinoa hushpuppies with capers and lemon which were fantastic (you dip them in a chili sauce that's unbelievable), the beet salad with goat cheese, horseradish creme, soft herbs and hazelnuts which was also flavorful and fresh and the black angus strip steak sandwich with fontina, ciabatta, spinach, salad, and horseradish. Â The sandwich was fine... it was too much bread so I mostly just ate the steak off it. Â I would totally come back here and highly recommend it. Â I feel like this would be a great brunch spot too.

What's there to say about Balthazar that hasn't already been said? I've been here twice for lunch now - once I got the chicken sandwich, the other the burger. The main event is the pomme frites (aka french fries) and the bread - but this is no surprise since it's famous for its baked goods. Solid Soho french-inspired cuisine. Huge fresh seafood selection. Takes reservations or easy seating if you get there right around 12.

what a cute underground joint. we had a choice to sit at the table but opted for the bar instead, it was a more fun atmosphere especially with the different sake bottles in the back. our waiter was super friendly and helpful. we ordered the roasted duck, black cod, deep fried pork, Agedashi Tofu and topped it off with the black sesame creme brulee. i'm not a big sake fan but how can i not drink sake here, we shared a carafe. my friend has been to the sake tastings they hold here and said it's good. they hold it the back room and have around 10-15 sakes to try and they bring out some nibbles throughout. i would come back again to try out the other dishes!

Good food, well priced. I enjoyed the Victoria Lac Salmon entree - the lemon grass curry sauce with sauteed onions was creamy yet a tad spicy, especially interesting when combined with grilled salmon. On the flip side, Â they don't include disposable flatware or bread with the take-out order...maybe I just expected more from a restaurant with a price point like this one.

We had to start: Corn Polenta - basically grits with a poached egg on top. Not bad... Beef Carpaccio - I am not a fan of raw beef... so wasnt too thrilled with this one. Mussels - this was really good! Â save the bread and dip it in the broth. Main dishes: Pappardelle with ox tail - wow... so good. Â A bit more ox tail would have been nice... Gnocchi - good! Â Altho reading too much Yelp reviews kinda set me up for a bit of disappointment. Risotto - also good. Taglierini - also very good. Â nice and creamy and shrimps seemed pretty fresh. Overall, I would go back... but it wouldnt be the first place I would think of when I am really hungry an craving Italian.

So they just started taking same day telephone reservations at 3pm. I called on the first day they started to do this and was given an option of 8:45 pm or 9:15 pm for a party of three. I opted for the earlier reservation and arrived around 8:20pm. If you are late by 10 minutes then you loose your reservation. It was my first time trying mu ramen and I wanted to see what the hype was about. As we arrived we sat down on the benches around the front. There was a large communal table with seating for 22 in the middle. The waitress said we were too early and would be seated in about 20-25 minutes which would have been our reservation time. Well, that time passed and we watched couples and groups sit down before our eyes. It was a bit frustrating because a couple just walked in without any reservation and was given seats. The waitresses could have put an extra stool and my friends and I would have been fine to sit there. It was about 9pm, 15 minutes after our reservation and the waitress apologized and quoted us 5 more minutes. We sat about 9:15-9:20 pm, aka despite having a phone reservation we still had to wait. And that day it was really poor weather. Finally we were seated and ordered the u&i and okonomiyaki for appetizers. The uni in the u&i tasted a bit fishy and was not as fresh. We all loved the okonomiyaki which was a bite of hot and cold; hot being the scallion pancake on the bottom and cold being the smoked trout. We all ordered the tonkotsu 2.0 which was the best dish of the night. The broth was super tasty and rich. But it was loaded with a ton of salt. The waitress refilled my glass a couple of times. As of right now they don't have a liquor license so they don't offer any wine or beer options. It was a perfect bowl of ramen on a rainy day but the wait isn't worth it. Either come early for dinner or super late when they are about to close.
First time. Loved it. Had Cuban food before but this was the best yet. Friendly staff. Gave us samples. A must!!

MOST UNFRIENDLY ESTABLISHMENT I HAVE EVER ENCOUNTERED. I attempted to have lunch at Juventino on a quiet Thursday afternoon - not weekend brunch or an evening dinner. The restaurant itself was completely empty, with a handful of folks dining in the back garden. Â The hostess or waitress immediately turned our party of 4 (3 adults and a 2-week old sleeping baby) away insisting we leave our stroller out on the curb. Â Clearly we could not do that - we do not carry a bike chain and lock for our stroller. Â We offered to leave the stroller frame in the front of the restaurant (the carseat could have been removed from the frame) but were told that was unacceptable and against the restaurant's policy. Â Seeing the hostess was not going to budge, we took our business elsewhere and will never again attempt to eat at Juventino and will tell our extensive network of Brooklynites to withhold their business as well. Â  Such a shame - does this restaurant not want the business of young families in Park Slope? Â Perhaps they should have opened in another neighborhood. Â I wouldn't support a restaurant that is so quick to exclude and enforce 'policies' when they barely have any customers in the restaurant for lunch. Very disappointing, Juventino.

Gaia's food is amazing but I don't think she treats her customer very well. Â We called about 5:45pm for dinner. Â Gaia said, we must arrive before 6:30pm. Â  When my party arrived at 6:18pm. Â She refused anymore patrons. Â Her reason is because she ran out of food. Â If you run out of food, why tell your customers when they are on the phone with you? Â You welcome them to come make the trek just to tell them you will cannot serve them? Â  Great way to piss off your customers.

Have had dinner here a few times and I have to say it holds up. The bone marrow poppers are delicious - as is the salmon and the apple 'tufahija' dessert! The Fraise Sauvage was quite refreshing for a strawberry infused beverage and pretty much all of the gin cocktails are fabulous! Great date place too - love that they take reservations! Have gotten really lucky with last minute rezzies on a Friday night -- thanks Eric!

I usually head straight towards the back and get some spicy tuna kimbap. If it's crowded, just stick your hand between people and grab whatever you can get. Since I've ate their kimbap so many time, I know exactly where to stick my grubby little paw. Haven't brought anything from the buffet but my friends love it. I love it too... probably because I mooch a bite or two off them all the time. Somewhere across the cashier, there are these light green, pink, white tri-colored blocks of smushed rice. Don't let the colors fool you into thinking they're some sweet fun mochi-like dessert, they're not.

Definitely a good date spot as long as you don't have an extra loud nasally New Yawker next to you since the tables are really close. Â Service was great; friendly and available though not overbearing. I had a couple of very generous pours of wine which was nice. Â They also bring out some delicious rustic bread with a white bean/garlic/olive oil dip which was unlike anything I've had before but was very very good. Â It's not a puree; the beans are whole. We started with the Panzanella which was the best I had ever had. Â The bread still had a little bit of crunch to it, it was nice and bright and acidic, very fresh tasting, and the tomatoes were nice and cold. Â I am totally going to try to make this myself at home. Next up we shared the risotto of the day (pear and Gorgonzola) and a special tagliatelle (with prosciutto). Â I was a little afraid of a sweet risotto, but it was smooth, creamy and delicious, if entirely bland looking. Â The tagliatelle was salty to the point of being inedible, though switching back and forth between a mouthful of the two helped. Â  Â The people around us seemed to be enjoying their dishes, and based on the Panzanellla I'm convinced that I'd be able to select better options the next time I went. Â Overall, I liked it and would return to give it another shot.

Seriously the BEST lasagna I have ever had in my life! Super rich with amazing flavor and there pasta is made fresh daily. It is simply a MUST order! My friend ordered the gnocchi with gorgonzola and that was also amazing, although I would get the lasagna if it is your first time here. I went on a Sunday night and there was no wait for two, but crowded however and if I lived in NYC I would definitely be back for more! Pros: fresh pasta made daily, cheap (lasagna was $12, gnocchi $9), delicious Cons: cash only, no reservations

Just want to say I am consistently impressed with S&F. Still the best scallops I've ever had. Had the crispy port trotter - amazing. Perhaps the most interesting recent dish was dessert - sweet corn sorbet, apple miso sorbet (perhaps the best) and thai iced tea sorbet.

Chef Dom is a genius. Â Haven't had anything yet that wasn't incredible. Â Service is outstanding. Â Perfect neighborhood restaurant. Â Ive been coming regularly since they opened and will continue to do so. Breakfast gnocchi for breakfast, pasta and lamb Bolognese for dinner highly recommended but you can't go wrong with anything on the menu. Â Coffee and tea are great too. Â Lastly, nice patio just opened up!
This place has the best falafel pita I've ever had. Â  Enough said.

Definitely a great place to eat if you're looking for something fast and filling. They don't have many options of meat but each one is crafted well. The tacos are a good size and their guacamole is to DIE for. The service is good - pretty fast. However, the place itself is more of a taco shack than a restaurant. There's one large table and some seats at the bar but besides that, I would not recommend coming here with large groups.
Grilled Corn. Tostones with garlic sauce. Insane good.

24hrs. Quick. Many sandwich options. Good service. Beer and more. What else do need from a corner deli/market? I got a Pho #1 hot and it was a very good sandwich. Tender roast beef, fresh herbs, delicious sauce, and creamy avocado + bean sprouts. Can't go wrong.
Awesome for a super-casual brunch! Babaganush Plate was an interesting first time try! Wood Smoked Salmon came with a fresh salad. Both delicious!
GREAT pies ! Yummy !

This is a hidden gem. Â The only have beer and wine and the place is very tiny but the food is heavenly. Â My g.f. and I got there at around 7pm and there was 2 tables already filled. Â I left for 5 minutes to go to the ATM and grab cash because this place is cash only and the nearest ATM is at a bodega down the block. Â When I came back there were 2 more tables filled and people at the bar. Â With in a twenty minute period every seat in the house was filled. Â  The red wine on the menu was just perfect. Â Not too dry and had a fruity taste to it and it was reasonably priced. Â Then we ordered appetizers which were very filling. Â For a moment I felt as if I was in Spain eating tapas. Â We ordered Olive Miste which was this bowl filled with all sorts of olives that seemed home marinated. Â We also ordered La Piadina which was flat bread baked with mozzarella, tomatoes & arugla (but I think they also had ones with prosciutto and pancetta). Â  The waiter was also the bartender and he just seemed like a super hero because he even took take out orders on the phone while still being very attentive to every customer. Â  The meals were incredible. Â I am originally from Boston where we have North End (Italian part of the city) where everybody goes to and waits in long lines to taste the most amazing Italian food in the country. Â I can vouch because I've been to pretty much every state in the country and god knows how many cities numerous times. Â There was a mom and pop Italian restaurant that came pretty close in northern Italy but other than that almost every mom and pop restaurant in the North End triumphed. Â Anyways.... Â The ravioli di fungi e ricotta with gorgonzola cream was one of the most flavorful dishes I have ever eaten in my whole entire life. Â I've lived in Italy for 6 months and went back there again recently and even in Italy I never had anything as flavorful as the ravioli dish I had at Testo. Â  I made the decision that when the time comes for my last meal I will request for food to be brought to me from this restaurant. Â That decision was made when my g.f. gave me a bite of her Tortelli di Zucca con Olio Tartufato. Â  In English: Butternut squash filled tortilla with butter sauce and truffle oil. Â Imagine the perfect blend of garlic and truffle oil and the sweet taste of butternut squash which I typically shy away from eating. Dear Testo chef... if you are reading this, which is highly unlikely... BRAVO! Â  p.s. with 2 Tiramisu's for desserts our bill was still was 3x lower than at any other place in Manhattan.

My wife and I eat here often. Â The food is great and the prices are reasonable, so much so that we elected to have a baby shower here. Â  Marc, the head chef and owner was great. Â  He created a custom menu and lived up to his word. Â  There were no broken promises and our guest were not disappointed. Â This speaks volumes about the character of the owner and his establishment. Â If you're planning an event, birthday party or shower in the Park Slope area, this is the place you want to do it. Â They have excellent food, service and ambiance.

It's our "go to" place for breakfast and brunch. It's a nice casual neighborhood place. Â The food, service and ambience are fabulous. Â We love the Penny egg sammich, bacon egg and cheese on a croissant with a dollop of pesto. Â So yummy! Â The oatmeal is outstanding along with the yogurt and fresh fruit. Â  If there is a wait for a table sit at the counter which is very comfy!!!

Three words: Smoked Pancetta Pizza. Thin crust, so flavorful and crisp, topped with a delicate tomato sauce and fresh mozzarella topped with thin strips of smokey pancetta, its light saltiness balanced beautifully with the sweetness of the sauce and--OMG--black garlic.... little black morsels of sweet deliciousness. if you live in the Slope, are visiting the Slope, or just want to scarf down some out of this world gourmet pizza, I *highly* recommend Toby's!

Thanks J.Waxman! I have to say I've never had roast chicken that is so moist! I should say, I never order chicken anywhere, BUT HERE!! My brother was in town this past weekend and I figured I will bring him to Barbuto to check out JW chicken. Made my reservation weeks ahead so I don't have to worry about it when the dates get closer. This garage like restaurant is great, there is a private room table by the entrance and a couple of tables in the kitchen. The ambience is really cool and chilled, staffs were very professional and the food was just top notch good. We tried the bruschetta, gnocchi, steak, chicken and seafood stew. Everything tasted great and for such a well known chef, I was surprised when the bill came (in a good way). It was definitely an experience I'll rave about and suggest to my other friends to check it out.

i love this place on nfl nights. wings are 25 cents and you can get certain drafts for $5. i love the beer selection and the bbq wings are to die for. see your there on game day! they have a drinking club there, if you drink 40 different beers ( they ahve a checklist) in 30 days, you get a special mug with your name on it, in adddition you get discount for all the beers. try the sam adams utopia, its quiet good.

Sometimes I like to treat myself to an afternoon snack of a dozen oysters & steak tartare, and I rotate between Balthazar and Blue Ribbon. Â Not sure which I like better since both are fantastic. Â Not sure I'd want to dine here during the dinner rush -- seems like it would be a bit too chaotic, but then again the waitstaff all seem quite professional. Â  I heard the breakfast is great, but I never wake up in time for it.

My girlfriend and I were looking for a place that was a little off the beaten path, had good reviews, and not far away from the house since we just gotten a dog. She found this place. It's small, but has a rustic feeling to it and the staff is very friendly. Our waitress came over right away, and showed us a wine special. It was a white that regretfully I missed the name, but it was so delicious, and exactly what she described it as. Sandy, Summer feeling, and a pear after taste. It was perfect to pairing to the chicken I eventually ordered, along with the beet salad. Very delicious. Granted, not exactly cheap dining, but tough to find in Cobble Hill/Boreum Hill. I don't mind paying if the meal is delicious, and this meal was very delicious. I will definitely be returning to this spot for more.

Went for the Dry Aged Beef Burger and was not disappointed. Â The flavor imparted by the dry age shines clearly through in this dish which is best served medium rare. Â Accompanied by excellent french fries (on the thin and crispy side) that were perfectly seasoned. Also ordered the roasted bone marrow appetizer which was fine (I mean, it's bone marrow... it's going to be good) but the same dish at DBGB was executed better. Also had the potatoes aligot as a side. Â This dish is mashed potatoes on steroids, as it is whipped with cheese curds to the consistency of a super thick beschamel. Â These potatoes were tasty, but slightly under seasoned, so I spooned them over the fries which elevated both. However, what almost stole the show from the burger, were the cocktails. Â Stepping into the toasty bar and having an expertly crafted Old Fashioned, Murray's Sour, or Stella Rose is quite an experience. Â Enzo did a great job with these drinks. Â  Definitely recommended.

Well this place was insanely disappointing. Â This was a Yelp fail... don't know what other reviewers were doing but wow it was bad. Â  Menu was not descriptive and we have food allergies so this is a problem. Â We got a dish that didn't list tomato where it was the primary ingredient. Â Instead of being polite and offering to take the dish away and replace with something else the incompetent waitress argued over whether the menu listed tomato for the dish - which it didn't - she confirmed later. Â She slid the fish onto a plate and told us to pick around and then brought tough broccoli as a substitute. Â She was just really bad. Â She also brought a salad with peppers and again we can't eat those and was annoyed when I sent it back. Â The waitress did almost nothing and the poor bus boys did most of the work. Â  We were charged for the full $18.95 fish even though we couldn't eat half of it. Â  My chicken with skin, on the bone, was extremely dry. Â Impressive that someone can fail at making roast chicken. Â  DO NOT GO HERE or be prepared to be disappointed.
Best Mexican in the area. Blows the competition out of the water with the quality of the food and the service.
Service was great! The new location is much bigger and more intimate, really enjoyed the Food & the Sangrias is on point!
Get 10 friends and order the Bo Ssam Dinner. Â It is truly amazing! Â Best meal experience in NYC.

Many months ago, when I booked my hotel for this winter trip to new york, I began scouting the area on yelp for cheap eats. Being somewhat unfamiliar with the east side of midtown and being a vegetarian at the time, I came across the melt shop and bookmarked it. Â  After reading it over and looking at the pics, I decided I probably would not go - it was just a window in a little partially subterranean courtyard of what looked like office buildings. Probably fine for a working lunch but I didn't think it would work for a weekend trip. Fast forward to the Sunday of my actual trip. After a several transfer subway ride to Brooklyn, an aborted subway ride up to some obscure bar Uptown, and finally a trip back on the E train from times square, I found myself exiting the subway, exhausted, hungry, Â & disoriented somewhere around Lexington and 50-something street, in an oddly familiar looking courtyard. Like a bloodhound in search of grilled cheese, I recognized where I was & knew the melt shop's little window had to be nearby. Once found, the employees were nice (I think I looked tired and a little lost.) I ordered "the classic" because we had already had a big brunch. It was served up in about 5 minutes in a little box for about $4. Â Wish I had ordered the "shop tots" to go with it, but all around friendly employees and a solid grilled cheese sandwich for the price.

We came here because of a Scoutmob deal and will definitely be returning. When we got to the restaurant, there were Victorian Christmas carolers singing outside the entrance to welcome us in. We split five small plates for dinner (fried chicken, chicken pot pie, duck tater tots, beet 'whoopie pie,' and grilled cheese) and were really happy with all of them. Great flavors and balance, clearly just good ingredients. The staff were really friendly and the ambience was lovely. Definitely recommend!

This is one of the most medicore tacos I've ever had. It is a cross between SF style and Tex Mex, but fails to deliver. First of all, sliced cheese on the tortilla? Then the tortilla, which is actually good, sticks to the paper wrapper, making the whole thing fall apart. The hot sauce is weak, the meat underseasoned, the salsa flavorless. Basically, cheap tacos for the student set.

I really like it here - the food, service, price, all mesh. Â Like, you know those places with totally amazing food & mediocre service or vice versa? Â This is none of those, eg nothing is amazing nor mediocre, everything's just right. Â Most entrees could use a hit of salt (oddly even ones with cured meats?) but a minor complaint because I can spiff it right up myself. I love a lot of things on the regular menu, but usually try to go for the special pizza to try something new. Â Would in general say come here for the pizza, not the pasta, as it is well..a pizza place. Â But really nothing is bad (see above). Service is casual but attentive. Â The winding layout makes me happy & I feel like this is a very 'new york' kind of place, whatever that means to me. Â I even dig the house wines.

Initimate, understated, authentic. Came here for tea ceremony with my boyfriend. Seated in small tea room with another couple. The room was very cozy (slightly stuffy) but the tea ceremony was so captivating I forgot about the space constraints. For $20, the tea ceremony was a worthwhile experience and perfect for dates/out of towners. Stayed for lunch after the ceremony. Had one of those lunch sets-can't quite recall exactly what the dishes were (unagi? something mushroomy with chicken?) but remember enjoying them immensely. Will be back, not as a regular, but definitely for special occasions.
Hands down...Best dumplings in Queens. Noodles hmmmmmm,.

A classic, old school brooklyn establishment...is it the best pizza or best food ever, no...Is it as good as what it once was, probably not....but it is a staple of kings county, and is a classic family establishment that is great in the summer....it's like the Â urban Italian equivalent of the classic 1950s rural burger joint on the side of the road where the highway ended...... it is what it is....and I for one enjoy it...
This place is practically the only thing at South Street Seaport that is back in fighting shape after Hurricane Sandy (as of June, 2013!) As good as new. Drunken fish soup is still the best.
Cool place for a relaxed brunch or dinner in the West Village

Just went last night...I wanted to like it more than I did, but still a solid 4-stars. The wine list is diverse and extremely reasonably priced (the bottles are anyway - and why would you not just order a bottle?). The bean dip was excellent, and the other apps we saw looked really good. The music was good - a mixture of 80's and modern stuff. Romantic and friendly vibe, with nice dim lighting. Oh, and I think I heard people ordering beers they serve at the "sister" restaurant next door that specilizes in micro-brews, but I'm not 100% on that part. For dinner we tried the mozzerla sandwich and the portabella pizza and were let down on both accounts, so, minus one star. I will be back - for a pre-dinner bottle of wine with a snack.

The oldest pizza place in the US. Â Terrific. Â Go simple, as with all the best places NYC. Â Don't load the pizza up with stuff. Â Just sauce, cheese and, if you insist, one more thing. Â That's it. There can be a wait, especially on weekend. Â So, expect that.

After several perfect meals over the last month, I just wanted to stop here and chime in with these raves. This place is just completely wonderful. As everyone mentions, this is not a large restaurant. There are four counter seats, and two tables for four. However, if you can't be seated right away, they'll take your number to ring you when you're up, and in the interim, you can hang out at Blind Barber's airy new coffee shop right next door. As everyone also mentions, there is no menu, just a choice of fish and either hot or cold mugicha. But be sure to get there early for any specials! The set itself, while constant in design [soup, rice, fish, greens, pickles, egg], always reflects what's freshest. The miso may have ramps one day and asparagus the next. The dark greens under the tofu cream change, as do the pickles, and even the brown rice offers variety in its toppings. Only the tamagoyaki seems to arrive the same each time. All in all, it's a thoughtful and balanced meal of healthy and delicious food. Look, I don't want to be even more repetitive, and there are already some well-written reviews here that cover most of this, so the bottom line is: The service is friendly and fast. The interior is well-appointed, and insanely pleasant. They did lovely things with such a tiny space. But most importantly, the food is consistently excellent and - holy hell - affordable. If I were ever to use #feelingblessed with a straight face, then it would be for every meal I get to eat at Okonomi. I'm so in love.

Came here for takeout one night and had a good experience. Good thing we wanted to do takeout because theres only enough seats for like 8 people. The staff is friendly, the food was cheap and good, and I like that the owners have a sense of humor as evidenced by their funny signs on the wall (sorry cant remember what they said at the moment....kind of kills the story) I'd come here again.

I love the ambiance of this restaurant, and our brunch was great. Â The waitress was a little overwhelmed, but it was all good. Â I would highly recommend, and take anyone there for a very nice place to enjoy brunch.

A very cozy restaurant, warm ambiance and decor, with smallish tables crowded for dinner and if it lacks for memorable food it compensates with location and energy. Bread and lobster ravioli were good. If you are in the neighborhood - stop by for a glass of wine rather than cocktails since their french martini lacked not just the orange peel.

This was a fantastic spot for brunch. The scones ($6) were both outstanding and a fantastic deal. There were 3 kinds of scones, 2 of each, for a total of 6 awesome scones. Really good. We actually kind of filled up on these. We also split a poached eggs and hash plate with a small salad. Also great. We were greeted warmly when we came in and our server was perfect. Based on our brunch experience, we definitely plan to come back again.
Choosing the best beef brisket noodle in Chinatown was difficult. But this place had good wanton noodle. The soup that came with the dried noodle had just the right amount of salt & sugar and flavor.

I was starving when I got to the Mark, and I was pretty convinced that there was no way that sliders could satisfy me. Wrong. Not only was I satisfied, but I was able to be totally gluttonous and order two different kinds of burgers - one regular double cheese burger, and one bacon cheeseburger. The bacon cheeseburger is phenomenal. And, just as important, they have really tasty sauce options. A spicy jalapeÃ±o sauce, bbq, ketchup, yum! Their fries are also good.

Of course the cheesy-egg-bread is outstanding and craveable. Â It is also so rich you need a minimum of 3-4 people to tackle it. Â Beyond that, the other food was very heavy on the oil and just Ok. Â We sat in the back garden, which was kitchy and made me happy. Â Our waitress was nice but very lacking on her knowledge of Georgian wine. Â She described a red by-the-glass as "like a pinot grigio but heavier." Â She then just recommended the most expensive thing on offer. Â It was more endearing than annoying. Â Anyway, this was overall a good experience and I could see just getting the bread to soak up some booze and to bring a cheese-filled smile to my face.

Had dinner here last Friday night with a group of four. Arrived around 6:45 and waited for a table for almost an hour, but it is absolutely worth it! We got seated inside, which is small and loud but charming, great atmosphere. Had two bottles of a great white wine. The peasant salad was incredible, and we couldn't get of dipping our olive bread in the potato and garlic dip. Spanakopita was great, the filling was so well done. Entrees included a whole red snapper, scallops stuffed with crab meat, and pork kebabs, all of which we loved. Complimentary dessert at the end of a bread pudding type thing, heavy on cinnamon and a great way to end a fantastic meal. When we left the line for a table was huge. But will definitely be returning, no matter how long the wait is!
Great food and setting. Visited a friend at LiveStream and was so pleasantly surprised by this place.

Went with friends from work for lunch, good lunch spot - nice decor and funky background music, easy to relax, talk and unwind. Â I had chicken panang curry, which was excellent, it had just the right amount of spice and creamy coconut milk. Â My friends had the pad see ew (which she thought was just a little salty) and pineapple fried rice, which she thought was good. Â Food tastes fresh, which makes it better than several other Thai places in the Hell's Kitchen area in my opinion.

This is just a really great bahn mi place. i have not had one bad experience here, the service is always great and quick. One of the more exceptional places in Elmhurst. After trying a few of their stuff, I always go back to the bulgogi bomb me, get if if you haven't yet! The only downside to this place are their drink offerings and their weird sandwich ingredient arrangement, you never really can get the perfect bite lol. I would pass on the in-house drinks since you can get a better version of nearly everything there within a few blocks. The price is spot on for the value. All in all a great spot to eat at if you're around the area.

What can I say? It's cheap, fast, and satisfying. A very typical Chinatown restaurant... Don't expect the best service. But when I'm in the area, and I'm hungry, this is a quick and easy option. I like to get the roast pork and duck combo, which is only $6.50 or around there, and is pretty filling! I've tried other things here and there on the menu too and everything's okay. Nothing to crave over, but I'll probably be back.

Good wine list and comfortable environment, despite the blasting music that may or may not have been intentionally left a few notches too loud. I appreciate the fact that it's located a bit off the beaten path. The food was tasty, but I couldn't get over our forgetful and inattentive waiter. We ordered one bottle of wine, one appetizer, and one sandwich. We were brought the bottle of wine we ordered, the appetizer we ordered, another appetizer we didn't order, and no sandwich. The place was practically empty, so we couldn't figure out why it took over 40 minutes for our sandwich to come out. We began to theorize that they were freshly baking the bread which is the only way we could justify the wait time. Turns out our waiter forgot to put in the order for the sandwich... ...and then we were incorrectly charged on our receipt. Come for the wine. It's reasonably priced, and they can't really mess up that order.

It's really possible that I came here at an "off" time of 2 a.m. but I was completely disappointed with Amy Ruth's famous fried chicken. It was so dry and tough to chew they might as well call it leather. The waffle was bland and not even the butter and syrup could save it. Fortunately the candied yams were on point. Seriously the best part of this restaurant was the old-skool R&B jamz playing in the background. Nice knowin' ya Amy Ruth's

I recently went to Roberta's for the first time with a friend. And the pizza was delicious. I would say it falls right under Motorino (and lets face it, Motorino is near impossible to beat). Plus, Roberta's has a more upbeat atmosphere with outdoor seating as well. A little bit of a hike from Manhattan but well worth it.
Amazing pizza... Their sweet Italian sausage topping is incredible. Have some brooklyn lager with it.

Been there twice. The food is great. Tried chicken, pork, lamb all excellent Â (my favorite is lamb) the fries are amazing and we loved the corn. Perfect dips. Warning: Keep space for dessert Â and try perhaps some of the best coffees in New York. A superb addition to the New York food scene.

I was desperately in need of soup noodles int the am after a fierce night of drinking. It is my hangover ritual that has been celebrated for the last 10 years. It used to be Pho when I lived in California, but now that I am in NY and Pho is terrible it has become Nippon noodles. I am growing tired of Ramen so I jumped into Soba-ya for something different. I feel so amateur now because I ordered Udon at Soba-ya. I was still in a haze the the punishing my liver absorbed 8 hours earlier and wasn't fully aware of where I was eating. Next time Soba for sure. Udon lunch box was pretty boring. Udon noodle in soup which is what i wanted, but it was forgettable. Tempura was pretty good. Grilled piece of salmon was so dry I couldn't eat it, but i did love the boiled veggies. They were braised in something sweet too. But i like mush veggies. I will go back and get Soba next time and update this review.

Wow this place is great -- it's authentic and the food is delicious. When I went, we ordered the roti canai as an appetizer, Singapore kari laksa, char kway teow, and the beef rendang over rice. The roti canai was good, but nothing to rave about. The laksa and the beef rendang were AMAZING. They both had distinct tastes and they were so flavorful! The char kway teow was very good as well, but it wasn't as good as the two other dishes. Everything on our bill, with two sodas came out to $25!!! This is a hole-in-the-wall type of place so if that's not your thing, I would not recommend going here, but if you're all for it, GO TRY TASTE GOOD AS SOON AS YOU CAN!
I'm from California and these are some of the best tacos I've ever had in NYC every bit feels like home . :)

I got a lunch groupon for ponty. Never tried Senegalese food before so I thought I'd give it a whirl. Boy, am I glad I did! Â I had the Mac and cheese which is an appetizer but can easily substiute as a meal for those not too hungry. Entree was the nikolokoba and it was perfection. The pepper sauce is richer than other pepper sauces and Ali (the chef) puts some kind of cilantro seasoning on it that puts it over the top. Definitely need to come back here.

Really love the idea of locally and seasonably grown food. Â Went for brunch. Â The tables are quite tight and close together which makes it hard to have a private or quiet conversation. Â The noise level at times can be disconcerting. Â The menu sounds terrific. Â Service is quite attentive (perhaps too attentive and a feeling of wanting to 'turn over the table' quickly). Â We had two different types of eggs. Â Mine were not cooked as requested and were sent back to the kitchen. Â Ultimately, all tasted quite yummy including all of the bread products. Â Focaccia gets a 5 star as do the the Butter Biscuits. Â We enjoyed our meal but not as much as when we ate at Back Forty (right around the corner) which has a very similar approach but in a larger venue, broader menu, and stronger cooking.
Was excited to try, especially since a Texan transplant recommended it to us. Pulled Pork Â sandwich was dry. Brisket and potato salad was delish. Beans aren't my thing but definitely unique.
The HOT fry chicken was awesome! The butter bourbon cake was a sweet finish to delicious meal!

Visited Employees Only on a return trip to the city. Â Loved the decor, crowd and overall vibe. Â Drank a Fraise Sauvage-- one of the best cocktails I've had in a while. Â Highly recommend the drink menu. Â Food was a mixed result-- 2 of my freinds ordered the pork chop with lentils. Â It was a huge serving of tough/overcooked pork and a heap of bland lentils. Â My pasta dish (with olive oil and sausage) was excellent though. In summary, try to get a good recommendation from your server on the food, but you can't go wrong with any of the drinks.

I walked in and said in true gay fashion, "OMG this place is soo cute." Too bad that like many other gay men, this restaurant is just as superficial. I really wanted to like this place but nothing I had was good. We came after dinner and walking around so we were just got drinks and dessert. Wild Berry Mojito - God. I think I became diabetic after a sip. This thing is too sweet. I even poured my glass of water filling half the cup and it was still too sweet. White Grape Martini - unnecessarily more expensive than other drinks and tasted like cough syrup. I'm glad I was already pretty buzzed by the time I ordered it or else I wouldn't be able to down that shizz. Banana Split Waffle - I really wanted to like this. It was so pretty but nothing tasted right. The waffle was flavorless and overly dense. Way too much whip cream, and even the ice creams were weird. Strawberry too tart, Chocolate was crumbly. The only real plus about this place is that it's 24/7 but it's still spendy. Even if I ordered all the wrong things, you shouldn't put something on a menu if you can't make it well or it doesn't taste good. Hell, I even got a suggestion from the waiter (Wild Berry Mojito) -- but he did phrase it as one that is "very popular" so not sure if others' actually like it or the description reads pretty. Think I'll only come back if someone's paying for my meal.

UN-BUH-LIEV-ABLE. Â and yes, I know how to spell, this meal was worth creating a new word for. Â waited quite some time for a table--but it's my own fault. Â i Â didn't make a ressie. Â I ate in the Tavern on this cold December evening--the manager made it a point to stop by the tables several times during our meal to see how everything was going. Â I guess she overheard our party speaking of a particular beer--5 minutes later a beer course was brought out, compliments of her. Â The same thing happened when we were torn between two desserts. Â I swear they have people walking around just to eavesdrop on conversations. Â i honestly don't remember everything i ate, because it was a few months back and i'm just now catching up on my yelp reviews, but i remember everything being amazing. Â just another gem that's the part of the USHG family. Â New York based restaurant groups have a lot of learning to do from Mr. Meyer.
Just love the atmosphere and their original couscous! No show off there. Just simple! Perfect!
Too narrow. Too cramped. TV is too big. Bleh. Meh. Eh. I love when bars try to class themselves up by serving microwaved chicken wings on West Elm plates. Yup, totally fooled me.

We finally made it to Ippudo last night 1/10/10 after several failed attempts. I was on vacation for 2 weeks and every time we attempted to hit this Ramen hot spot we were greeted with a 1.5 hr wait time. We assumed that a Sunday night at 5:30 would be be a safe bet, but once again there was the inevitable 1.5 hr wait time. We decided since it was early we would settle in and enjoy a bottle of Sake and wait the wait to see what this Ramen was all about. The bartender was sweet and we chatted with some other guests that were also waiting. Everybody seemed to be having a similar experience with the hostess. She was very rude and didn't seem to care that you were willing to wait the extensively long wait time. After about 45mins I went back up to check on our status and the hostess responded with " It's only been 45mins, you still have many people ahead of you, it will be a while!" Â This was not very encouraging and I was hoping for a " Thanks for your patience, we will be with you as soon as we can". After about an hour and a half our table was finally ready. We were very hungry and ordered the Pork Bun appetizer for 2 which was very yummy and had a great spongy bun with delectable pork. Next we both got a Ramen. I had the "Modern" Ramen( a broth consisting of Miso and their signature broth) and my girlfriend had the Special Ramen which was a (creamy chicken broth with their house broth) The Noodles were very thin and al dente but very fresh and flavorful. There Â was not enough of them though. I have been to many many Ramen spots and I have never ever needed more noodles. At Ippudo it's almost as if they know they are not giving you enough noodles and put a note in the menu saying you can buy more noodles for $2 if you still have broth at the end of your meal. Overall the Ramen is quite good and has very complex flavorful broth and they have some creative app choices. The downside is the wait is far too long and it is too pricey for a Japanese street food. I have been all over Japan and have never paid $60 plus for 2 bowls of soup and an appetizer. If you have the extra cash and a surplus of time check it out. I however will be at Rai Rai Ken for my next Ramen meal on 10th, where I can eat a hearty bowl of Miso Ramen wait 20 min or less and still walkaway with some change in my pocket:)
Great place. Very friendly waitstaff, an interesting clientele and great food. Would go back in a heartbeat.

The best noodles I've had outside of Asia. I had the Karaka Men Ramen, spicy pork noodles with an extra poached egg, and they were great. I initially didn't feel that full, so ordered some Hirata pork buns. These were fantastic. However this is when all the food took the full effect. It appears as though the noodles take a bit of time to fill you up. The place is very quick, but not to make you uncomfortable. It is also very noisy inside. Not the ideal place for a quiet lunch. I will be back for more.

Hidden away on the second floor of the popular East Village dining district, this Japanese tea house is so unique that it's as if you are sipping tea in a tea house in Kyoto. Â The wonderful tea aroma and the serene ambiance makes this place idea for a special date with friends (limited to only small number of friends). Â Although small, it comes complete with a tea room and superb selection of Asian tea. Â But my favorite has to be their artistically and deliciously prepared Japanese dessert course. Â The 3 course dessert omakase with tea pairing is heavenly as the chef delicately prepares variety of desserts and surprises you with gentle and fresh flavors. Â I've been there several times with 1 or 2 other friends and we've never been served the same dessert as one another. The service is always excellent and the chef even offers private cooking classes on weekdays. Â Japanese tea ceremony is performed every Friday and Sunday (see their website for detailed schedule) so not only can you enjoy delicious tea but also learn about the art of tea making and drinking.

Pizzas pretty good here but I wouldn't call it the best in Brooklyn. It's always packed in there; especially between the hours of eleven to two so the wait is usually more than ten minutes. Plus they're super expensive(which I guess is like every standard pizzeria nowadays). Though at this place it's dam near five dollars for one slice :( What happened to the days when there used to be two slices plus a drink for five dollars!! Oh the good-ol' days!

Pros: solid family style. Had good salad, vodka rigatoni w mushrooms, and chicken cutlet Tony's. Good flavor all around. Found a reasonable bottle of chianti for $25. good deal for 4 @ $150 in NY. Light, delicious NY cheesecake and berry dessert with cannoli creme. Cons: frigging constant friggin noise, bus boy brings the food out, brought it to the wrong table, and the fought with the waiter about it in front of us. Waiter was there when you needed him but no real connection. Forgot to tell us the specials. Cold.

Absolutely love this place. I've been several times for both brunch and dinner and it never disappoints. Some favorites are the nasi goreng, crispy chicken, beef rendang and finish with the ice cream. The flavors here are just incredible

I went with Hallie C and a few others here for our book club meeting. When we walked in, I thought: HOW CUTE! Malatesta has a very relaxing yet inviting vibe. We sat down, earlyish and had some tasty prosecco and lots of pasta. It felt like a New York version of Italy, because the service is better than most in Italy. The house prosecco is tasty and has a nice flavor. I got the seafood pasta special. The fish was fresh, the pasta was cooked to perfection and the red sauce wasn't too acidic (always a plus). I would come back with my mom for a girls date or with a boy for a real date. Either way, I would check it out again. I really enjoyed the time there and was so relaxed that i could do it again.

This used to be Three Monkeys before it burned down, but somebody told me it's the same owners (I don't care enough to verify if this is true or not). Great late night (read: drunk off your ass) food. The carnivore's delight was a... delight. Meaty and exactly what I needed to soak up the alcohol in my stomach. Wraps are anywhere from $7 to $9. They take credit cards, but there's a minimum. I forget what it is, but I happily paid for it. Line can get kind of long, but it ebbs and flows, as the LES is wont to do.

Solid lunch option in mid-town. Nice atmosphere, quiet but bright, modern decor. When seated, you're given warm bread rolls brushed with duck fat and sea salt, as well as an amuse bouche. I've had the lobster pappardelle, risotto, Arctic char and scallops dishes. All were delicious. High quality, tasty. Classic enough for traditionalists but also trendy and unique. Reservations during the weekday lunch hour are not necessary.

This food is amazing! went there after a play and had a very late dinner with a large group. We got the back room where you had to go through the kitchen to get to and saw all the cooks and servers on the way. The waiters were very attentive and the food came out as it was made in large plates of pasta for the aps along with a great salad where you served yourself. The Entrees were off the menu and I had the Filet steak which was as good as any steakhouse. The wine was great as white and Red was served. The Pasta was middle of the road although I might have been last to get off the big plate. It was a short walk from most theatres and worth it. Not quite a 5 but reasonable priced compared to the others in this category

More classic than Death & Co., but not quite Milk & Honey. I like their infusions, and the bartenders are knowledgable and willing to talk to you about why the drinks are made the way they are. I feel like if I'd come here on a busier night, I wouldn't have liked it as much as I did. It's a cool place. I just can't see myself willing to brave the masses for it.
I am very much in live with cheesecakes at Bubby's!

I could not resist taking an odyssey to my neighboring borough to have a bite of the supposedly luscious mac & cheese. Â  Brooklyn is not a strange land to me- in fact, I consider myself as a "Brooklyn wannabe resident." Commuting from Queens to Brooklyn is generally a piece of cake but my subway ride to JTH Tavern wasn't exactly the norm: there was a crazy old drunk man, 2 teenagers who seemed not to have a sense of what personal space is and a guy who decided to just knock on the conductor's door [side bar- the man operating the train actually stopped the train and opened the door, to the horror of every passenger on-board]. One could just imagine the colossal hope that Jack the Horse Tavern will be worth the unnecessary inconveniences. To my relief, JTH Tavern's celebrated first course entree made me forget about the previous ordeal (at least for the time being). The mac & cheese was beyond satisfactory. The aroma was a teaser, I couldn't help salivating as the dish was placed in front of me. I took my first bite and I was transported to what felt like a fluffy room filled with things that made me melt and fall in love. It was an epic moment when the smoked Gouda and fontina cheeses and the cavatappi pasta melded in exquisite harmony. The wise move of choosing the mentioned cheeses added a sophisticated depth to the dish (something that I wish every mac & cheese have). It was savory, sweet and a little bit salty. The smoky element was also there. My favorite part was the texture- it was crunchy upon the first bite and when bitten, it just melts in your mouth. The mac & cheese brought coziness and warmth. It was quite challenging to remain civilized when consuming it.

Some friends advised me to go to Minetta Tavern for dinner, telling me that the food was good ..... and not wrong! I took the Oxtail And Foie Gras Terrine and is was really the right choice! `I'll be back for sure to sample other dishes, beautiful surroundings, just like me pretty well the atmosphere of the room .. very good service, I recommend guys;)

Holy shizznikity! Â When did this place become the bomb spot? I came here every month or so when I lived in New York until 2006 and it was always a good time. Â Fresh fries, yummy dipping sauces, low-key environment. Â And they served poutine, which appeased my Canadian now-husband. Â So when I happened to be in the East Village late at night last month, I thought, why not return to a beloved haunt? And wow, was I surprised. Â Not by the change in food - the fries are pretty much the same as I remembered them to be. Â I'm talking about the popularity. Â The line was way, way out the door. Â It was packed inside too. Â The service was pretty good so the line moved fast, but hot dang, since when did this place become such a hot spot? A regular size is more than enough for even 2 people, and while they offer a whole slew of dipping sauces, I'd say stick with the freebie frites sauce (european mayo), which is very tasty even if it is more simple than some concoction featuring mango or chipotles. Â And if you don't have a drink, buy one there, since otherwise you'll be hella thirsty but not motivated enough to get back in line.

I've been here a few times for brunch and thoroughly enjoyed it each time. The menu has such a wide variety of comfort foods, salads, sandwiches, burgers, breakfast, etc. that anyone will be able to find an item that will satisfy their craving. I highly recommend the shrimp and grits which are creamy and delicious and served with a biscuit. The chicken and waffles are also amazing and a massive portion that could easily be split. There are a few varieties of macaroni and you can get a sampler tasting which is quite filling. Everyone at the table thought the truffle mac was the best. Service is great, ambiance is trendy and modern, and it's open 24 hours. Just expect a short wait for brunch (they don't take reservations).
The lasagna pizza is the bomb! Would rate it a 5 but pizza is a little greasy and service isnt the best.

Yeah.... that 1+hr wait, the family who sat at a table an extra 30 minutes after they finished their course really irked me off. The servers were pretty cool. The food was probably the best damn Viet I've ever had. I reallly didnt think anything can one up my pho banc in elmhurst... Must haves: viet iced coffee ( better than sripaprhai iced coffee homemade limemade pork loins fried egg on top tomato fried rice crab spring rolls like you've never tasted banh xeo fried egg appetizer (i'm spelling this wrong sorry) beef cubes are best damn beefed tender cubes you've had after the wait, i vowed to never come back with my party, however i quickly changed my mind when Â tasted the food. oh man. So from hereon, i will be getting takeout :) until they open a new location.

Mm tried the lobster roll here, and it was so delicious! Â I'm thinking about giving this 5 stars, but I feel like it's a big wrong to give such a high food rating to a food truck. Â hmm... anyway, i would love to come again. Â Just wish it wasn't all the way in Brooklyn! :(

Came here for a bday with 3 friends on a Friday night, with a reservation. Place was crowded but not overly packed, but service was still really sub-par. It was on the later side, but still. - Out of most of the things we wanted - Took FOREVER to get drinks, service, etc. - Waiter acted like he was doing us a favor by seating us Food was good, not great. Portions were fine, not amazing. Price was so-so. Village-esque place in terms of layout/decor. Wouldn't refuse to go back, but def not on my list of fav places.

wow. Â their bunh bo hue was amazing and the best I have ever had (outside of vietnam/home cooking). Â It really depends on how much spice you can handle because this one made my friends lips puffy. Â There's a lot of meat in this bowl of noodles... 3 slices of beef, 2 pieces of pigs feet, 2 pieces of fish cake. Â The braised beef was tender, the pigs feet and the fish cake had a nice firm texture. Â I would skip the appetizers since the noodles itself will fill you up for $6.95.

Dar rules! Seriously they have the most amazing pita bread the size of a flying saucer. Â They also have an amazing breakfast pizza (get it without the eggs) that is out of this world. I highly recommend Dar if you are looking for flavor and freshness!

This is a pretty cool spot, just like the name it is very narrow. But it opens up to an awesome outside area in the back and I can't wait to chill here when the weather gets better. The drinks are great, priced accordingly. If you want to enjoy a good cocktail I recommend this place.

My son arranged a dinner for my husband's birthday, party of 12. Â We were lucky enough to have the bottom floor of the carriage house, one of the most beautiful rooms in the city, adorned with gorgeous fresh flowers all around the room and the table. Â We had a lovely cocktail hour with fresh meat and cheese, olives and bruschetta on the table when we arrived. Â We chose the burrata, artichokes and meatballs for appetizers, spinach agnolotti and gnocchi with pesto for the pasta course and the steak and sea bass for the entree. Â We had the chefs selection for dessert of beautiful fruit tarts and melt in your mouth macaroons. Â It was a magical night and special thanks must go to our amazing waiter, Lucca, who took care of us. Â He was personable, attentive and made the night even more special. Â Thank you, Lucca, and the staff at Palma, for an amazing evening!

This is a brand new place owned & operated by a couple. They work the floor since they're still so new. They were as nice as could be. Reasonable prices across the board, and considering I don't think I've ever had Hawaiian in NYC, absolutely worth stopping in. The poke is fantastic, and the kalua pig is tender & moist. Honestly, though, I think the spam fried rice stole the show. We're heading back tomorrow to try the burgers, but I don't think we'll be disappointed. Withholding just one star since they're so new. Would like to see how consistently they can deliver quality meals at their price points and it'll also make a difference once they get their liquor license.

Really cute spot right off the Highline. Friendly Italian staff. Bufala Pizza was authenic Neopolitan - chewy charred crust, tangy tomato sauce, and fresh buffalo mozzarella! .Fried artichokes are worthy of all the previous raves.

Your must-see in New York City might be the Statue of Liberty, but for me it is Radio City Music Hall and Taim, the crown jewel of falafels! I had begin to think that perhaps time and distance had made my tastebuds grow undeservingly fonder, but not so. If anything, I had forgotten how magically delicious their balls are. Before you go, take note that it is a teeny spot with very limited counter seating, and we usually just end up eating on one of the two benches out front. If you're lucky, perhaps you have a falafel getaway where you can take your order and munch. You have three choices of falafel: traditional, harissa or roasted red pepper, and they are all worth trying. Plus, they have whole wheat pita as an option! On my last visit, I ordered a red pepper falafel pita with everything. There are very few fares that make me uncontrollably utter noises of satisfaction, and Taim falafel is one of the proud few. They also have some creative beverages, including a ginger lemonade and smoothies, but I am generally too distracted by the falafel to remember to sample anything else. If I were a billionaire, I would fly to Manhattan routinely for a fix.

This place was just alright for me. Â The first time I tried coming here, I didn't end up going as the wait was 40+ minutes & the waiting area was packed. Â It was as if we were waiting to go into a fancy club or something. Â My friend & I ended up going to Menkui Tei a few blocks over. So I finally got to go here for lunch. Â My friend suggested we leave our offices at 11:40am to beat the lunch crowd. Â We only had to wait 5 minutes! Â By the time we got there, some patrons were already done eating...haha. Â The restaurant is actually bigger than I thought as there is a whole other area once you turn the corner down the restaurant. We got the Hirata Buns in Pork as an app. Â These were pretty good as the pork was really tasty & comes in a man-tao bun with lettuce. Â For an entree, I got the Shiromaru Hakata Classic w/a boiled egg as my friend's friend told me this was the popular ramen here but my friend's order of Akamaru Modern looked more appetizing to me. Â The ramen was hearty & great for a winter's day but nothing spectacular to me. Â I feel like you can go to plenty other places (without a wait) to satisfy your ramen craving. For dessert we got the Lady M Mille Crepe Cake, again...great but nothing spectacular. Â Not sure if a slice of cake is worth $10 either. I definitely wouldn't wait a long time to eat here.

Dinner, atmosphere and service was all excellent. Small venue adds charm to a delightful evening. Â I dined here with a friend on a Sunday evening as part of my farewell ny tour. Â Everything we ate was delicious. Â It was only two of us and the portions are decently sized so we split almost each course. Â Would love to go back and try more on the menu. Â We had the infamous "Joey Meatballs" sliders, which were fantastic. Â We also split the eggplant appetizer which was flavored well and had a fresh tomato taste. Â For our main, we split a fish special over risotto, accompanied by a side of spicy corn. Â Everything had great flavor and tasted fresh. Â Would definitely recommend to others.

If you're ever in this area, you have to check out De Mole. Â A hidden gem in the 5 boroughs, IMO. Â Guacamole is pretty good here, although I've still yet to have better guac than Toloache. Â When I was here, I ordered steak tacos, medium-rare and they definitely exceeded my expectations. Â Mind you, I came here with a friend who lives in the area and was not expecting too much. Â It was a pleasant surprise.
Great fish!! Generous servings!! And great service!!!! Recommend St. Peter's grilled fish, shrimp Shish kebobs and fish soup!

Affordable authentic homestyle thai food. Wonderful staff. Friendly and helpful on suggestions. It's a nice neighborhood kind of place. Ordered the crispy pork with basil over rice and the crab fried rice lunch specials. Can't go wrong. A satisfying meal. The pork was crispy and tender and it matched well with the rice. I'll definitely be back in store and for delivery as well.

First review ever but definitely worth it. Affordable fresh pasta, online reservations, and same-week availability--what's there not to love? I had the gnocci with assorted mushrooms, which was superlatively incredible. I would have licked the plate clean if I hadn't been sitting in the middle of the restaurant. Pasta was light as a feather, sauce was decently creamy without being too overbearing (the server actually cautioned me when I asked for fresh parm on top), and the mushrooms were flavorful. Also tried the grits/poached egg appetizer. Was good, but would have preferred to leave even more room for the pasta! Host allowed me to move my reservation up the day of, seated me although my friend was late, and even turned up the heat a tad when I voiced concerns that there would be a draft from the door. Prices are reasonable, especially for the portion sizes.

Had a delicious meal here. Â Cute, quaint, spot to meet up with friends. Would definitely go back. Â I got a fish dish, and my friend got a beef special that was very good. Â I would definitely go back.

There are many things about Noodle Village that I like which are rarities in Chinatown. Â My favorite part about Noodle Village is that it is MSG free. Another is that they accept credit card, but it is just that you need to meet the minimum of $25. You can also sit here comfortably without feeling cramped. Just these three things alone should entice you to make it over here!!- but wait, there's more (but I want to preface with that these things aren't rare in Chinatown): The service here is great- the people here are so nice. The food is amazing. The portions here are good for sharing, like most places in Chinatown. I like it even more because I really like the food here. I love the different choices of congee to get here, and my favorite is the rice pot. The dumplings here are also very tasty! This place is good for groups or just a quick late night date.

This is a great, inexpensive izakaya in a cool basement setting. I first tried it on a weeknight early, dining solo, sitting at the bar near the entrance. Had the ebi mayo (tasty), saba shioyaki (cooked perfect), and katsu don (good, but a little on the bland side). Service was quick, friendly and efficient. Best of all - $3 pints of draft Sapporo! Is this NYC? You'd be hard pressed to get Bud Lite at dem prices even in Nebraskee. I enjoyed my midweek experience enough to bring friends back on a Sunday for dinner. My hungry friends and I impatiently waited until 6PM for opening, killing time in the bland environs of that section of midtown (no, I do not want to go to the top of the Empire State Building, Mr. Shillmeister 1, 2, 3, 4 and the rest of you). Finally the minute arrived and we made our way down the steps only to be greeted with the warning that it's jazz night and it's a bar only. Bummer. Hence the docked star. Where is the announcement that on Sunday Mew Izakaya tranforms into a jazz club? There's nothing on their website because there is no website. Their Facebook page mentions music, but nothing about any bar only policy on Sunday. Sign outside just lists hours. And who wants to listen to jazz at 6PM anyway? Correction, who wants to listen to jazz anyway? I can understand not seving food while jazz is being performed as it would lead to more projectile vomiting than Mr. Creosote on a Dunkin Donuts binge, but how about some advance warning? Maybe a sign in the restaurant? On the tables? Outside? It could be simple: "Warning - jazz on Sundays! No dinner service." Oh well. At least I wasn't stuck there trying to eat while "enjoying" what sounds like someone trying to clean a saxophone with a Siamese cat.

Mexican food in most of the northeast has become synonymous with Tex-Mex. Casa Enrique serves real authentic Mexican and is easily one of the top 5 restaurants in LIC. First, the tacos. Each order comes with two tacos, and I've had the chorizo, suadero, pastor and pescado. It would be hard to pick a favorite, as they are all incredible. And despite their relatively small size, they pack some serious flavor - there are always multiple toppings and ingredients that make them more than the sum of their parts. For dinner, I've tried a bunch of things, and recommend the chile relleno if that's your thing since it's great. But you should only order one thing here - the Mole De Piaxtla. If you haven't had mole sauce before, it's a dark, slightly thick sauce, in this case containing dry peppers, almonds, raisins, plantain, sesame seeds and chocolate. Casa Enrique's is wonderful, and served over always-juicy chicken and rice. it is my favorite dish here and well worth the trip. For dessert, I've had both the Flan and the Tres Leches and both were among the best I've had of each. I haven't been back on site since they get their liquor license, but they now serve cocktails as well. I got delivery last week and the dishes managed to be just as good as they are on site. The only reason for not giving a fifth star is the slightly disengaged service every time I've been there. This isn't as well known as some other LIC places but it's certainly one of the best.

Meal: Dinner (takeaway) Rationale: When my boyfriend lived on 117th Street, within their delivery zone, we ordered delivery from CafÃ© Ollin regularly. It pains me to say we took it for granted. Now that we live in Jersey City, we must take special trips, few and far between, to visit friends still in the area, with whom we ritually participate in the sacrament of Ollin. Food (the ritual): First comes the call to prayer - climb to the highest accessible point and yell the Word of Ollin into the phone. Ask Ollin for the following gifts: one burrito de vegetales to be consumed in its entirety by each individual, and at least one order of vegetable nachos for every two participants. It is a sin to ask "have I ordered enough food to get free soda?". Heretics will be cast out. Second comes the period of anticipation - have a beer or two to lower your spiritual barriers; you are about to merge with the Source of Flavour. Third is the greeting of the messenger - the doorbell rings; Glory to Ollin! Form a procession down the stairs to the front door. Demonstrate reverence and piety to the messenger by offering a sacrifice of the likeness of Andrew Jackson. Obtain the parcel and carry it swiftly upstairs to the dining table. Fourth, the sacrament of Ollin - behold, the parcel is heavy; it is weighed down by two litres of free Jarritos orange soda. Take it into your mouth and allow it to cleanse inferior flavours from your body. The blood of Ollin. Behold, the nachos are colourful. They are covered with many vegetables from near and far, stringy white cheese, and mysterious white sauce. Take it into your mouth and be awakened by the confluence of diverse, bright flavours. Accept the slightly low ratio of chips to toppings; it is the Will of Ollin. Behold, the burrito is enormous. Use a fork and knife to take it into your mouth and be filled with the sacred light of perfect tortilla, rice, and beans, with mysterious white sauce and assorted vegetables throughout, and optional red and/or green sauces; feel your core become one with the Source of Flavour as you finish the entire burrito. The body of Ollin. Praise to Ollin! Last is transcendence - such energy and light is not easily channeled by the human body, and you will be tired. Sleep, dream of Ollin, and awake renewed; Ollin is our eternal salvation, forever and ever. Service/Atmosphere: The Temple of Ollin is on East 108th Street, but I have not yet worked up the nerve to enter. Until such a time, the ritual of delivery will be our favoured option. Somewhat long waits and occasionally confusing telephone ordering are the Will of Ollin, and must not be questioned. Glory and praise to Ollin! Conclusion: Amen.

Only great food can make me forgive a 1hr wait to be seated It was meant to be for me to end up here and I'm glad I did. The kitchen at SOB's was closed and the other restaurant we just couldn't find. After walking past the red awning with no writing 3 times we figured this had to be the place and it was. It place was packed! Small intimate location but still very friendly and nice. I noticed the manager walking around and touched every table to make sure everyone was ok. Half an hr came and it looked like no one wanted to face the rain outside. 4glasses of wine later we finally were able to get a seat. We had the sautÃ©ed calamari for starters and it was pleasantly delightful. I thought The Shrimp ProvenÃ§al was delicious. I actually ordered the Sweet and Spicy Catfish but I switched plates because my date didn't like the spinach. The ravioli really tasted great. But I agree a little less spinach would have been perfect. The Catfish was a perfect 10. Mash potatoes were creamy and rich the flavor of the catfish and the seasonings all blended perfectly together. This is absolutely something I recommend. I do think they need a few more $$$ though the cocktails for $15 bucks were only required 3 sips! Â  Overall great first trip I actually want to give this place 4 1/2 stars. Good all around

My favorite lunch spot in NY (so far). I just had dinner here for the first time a few days ago, but I've been somewhat of a "regular" for lunch. The tasting menus for lunch and dinner and delicious. I have yet to be disappointed by anything. It's kind of funny counting how many waiters come to your table in the course of your meal. I think the highest count I've gotten is 12. I always feel full, happy, and satisfied after a meal here. And the good thing is, it won't empty your wallet. The big lunch tasting menu is only about $50. This is CHEAP for a Michelin 2-star. The bread is also very delicious. I can't help but constantly ask for more (especially the pepper bread and the garlic bread). And of course, the coolest part, walking in and out of the place. There's a huge wooden door and a little hallway of TONS of apples. The smell is awesome.

The standard bearer for a good neighborhood Thai restaurant. Reassuring signs in a Thai restaurant: Thai-run and many Thai people to be found among goers; fresh ingredients, and the ability to pack the restaurant day in and day out; I'll even throw in the fact that the bathrooms are really clean (self-changing toilet seat liners? Â Who does that?) That said, once a restaurant attracts the amount of reviews on Yelp as SriPraPhai, you have to wonder if this place is starting to wander into Michelin star territory, don't worry, it's not. Â My four stars mean that if you live in New York City, you eventually have to visit this place. Â It does not mean that you have to come to New York City to eat here. Â And if you're in between, as in a tourist, I don't know what to tell you. Â Just don't get pizza at Two Brothers and think you're getting New York pizza. Safe bets will be pad thai and drunken noodles, you'll be satisfied with your choice. Â I've had the red snapper, saute mock duck and the chive fried dumplings. The mock duck actually was not bad, seasoned well (which means my taste buds were melting off only towards the mid- to end- dish), though abundant bamboo shoots, which seems to be a theme in other reviews in other dishes. The chive dumplings a bit on the doughy side, didn't really do it for me. Â  The red snapper, which I got with the ginger sauce (because I didn't want to burn my taste buds off) was deliciously crispy and satisfying. Â However, I did notice that it was a little dry. Â  Thai iced tea was expectedly sweet like a mofo, and was very glad it didn't come in diabetes inducing portions. Â Mayor Bloomberg would have been proud! Kudos to this little gem in Queens, I'll see you again soon.

YES. THIS is what I was looking for when I scanned Yelp for a ramen shop in NYC. My dream of a rich, complex broth brimming with delicious goodies was popped by Totto Ramen, which had a very bland broth and little in it, but Ippudo saved the day! There can be a wait so come early.
Intimate Italian restuarant! All the food looked delicious, and I choose the butternut squash gnocchi! Loved the atmosphere and there was no wait...

4.8 Great night out. Really a perfect version of the comfortable, lively, non annoying cross between gastropub and steakhouse. A bit like Lugers cross spotted pig.
