This is the least annoying restaraunt in nyc. Start to finish, friendly, earnest appearing, and efficient service. Food simple fresh and expertly preapared. Crispy fresh Montauk bass with mushrooms, carrots, Pasta Dish, heireloom pestp tomatoes and souffle chocolate with (must ask for) a single scoop of vanilla, Celebrities cool approachable in the house hanging with bouncer(ie. Jimmy Spdr). Much more to try cant wait to go back. Appears as best solo dining bar spot I think in the city. And I rarely say this but the bar tenders are outstanding. A lively buzz feel without even a hint of pretension. Highest rating. So glad we chose over costata which would have been exactly twice. Laurence

Couple of weeks ago, the hubs and I decided to give this vegetarian place near us getting awesome reviews a try. Made the choice to dine there...Wrong decision. Not mad at the simplistic decor but we sat right next to the huge glass window where 1000 people were walking and cars constantly honking. I'm sorry but Flabush ave (East Flatbush side) is not the most pleasant street to dine on. People walking by were giving us all types of Â stares (curiosity, judgment, curiosity, smiley faces, hunger, hatred....you get the drift). We felt like Â monkeys on display. Â  Not to mention the resident bum popping in and asking for money.Next time...will order from home. On to food, I liked how it didn't smell like hot grease Â in there. Our plates came out right away. - Eggplant with garlic. Beautiful presentation. Â the sauce was awesome, best garlic sauce ever taste. Â  -mango chicken, as many have mentioned, was also good. The fruits and veggies were really fresh. -Portions were sooooooo huge, we got 3 meals out of our dishes. They also had good healthy drinks. We had pina colada and vanilla soy shake Sadly, something about vegan food does not fully go with my stomach. I enjoyed the chicken nuggets at first but for some reason they were hard to digest. Like my stomach was NOT happy. Come to find out, me and the hubs both had GI Â distress later on. Traced the source back to the nuggets. Not sure what ingredient in them is causing this....the fake meat? the oil they used? who knows. Still giving this place a 4 for the food. Â Still giving it a chance and trying out more stuff from the menu.

For my birthday this year, the Count and I went to L'Artusi- an Italian restaurant located in the West Village. We walked in to a dimly lit restaurant with neo-regency decor consisting of dark blue walls and white trims. A long 30 seat bar lined the wall with polished white marble and handsome friendly bartenders decorating the other end. The restaurant is two floors with a small and intimate dining area on both floors. We were taken to our seats at the bar- typically our favorite spot in a restaurant to dine. Wine: The wine list at L'Artusi is extensive mostly made up of Italian wines ranging from region and price (see wine list). We ordered a bottle of the 2008 Antonelli Sagrantino "Contrario" ($70)- a wine from Italy's Umbria region. The region is known for its Sagrantino (a tannic grape that creates long-lived wines). Antonelli wines, especially the one we tried at dinner, are lush, deep and full bodied. Food: As with most of my dining experiences, I had already researched the menu and knew exactly what I wanted to order. We started out with a few Â starters to share including the cheese plate and the roasted mushrooms (see menu). The roasted mushroom dish was out of this world. Â A mix of mushrooms, pancetta, ricotta salata topped with a runny egg yolk. I loved the mix of flavors- you could say it tasted like a mushroom omelet served Italian style. The runny egg mixed with the cheese and mushrooms led to a creamy and delectable dish. Of course the pasta came next. Gabe Thompson- executive chef/part owner of L'Artusi is famous for his hand made pasta. We ordered the potato gnocchi and the bucatini pasta. We decided to stick with the pasta and skip the meats as most have recommended the restaurant based on their pasta and wines (although I really did want to try the quail). The potato gnocchi was very good topped with a lot of Parmesan cheese. The handmade gnocchi was one of the best I've had. It was the sauce that I was not a big fan of. The ragu sauce had a sweet aftertaste to it. I'm not sure what the sweet ingredient was but I definitely preferred the Count's Bucatini sauce. Usually, he would have switched his dish with mine but this time he was too into his meal to even care about my discontent. Oh well. I carried on eating. The Bucatini pasta definitely won the best dish of the night for us. It was the first time I had Bucatini- a hollow pasta similar to spaghetti. The sauce consisted of a mixture of tomatoes, pancetta and spices- and tasted exactly what a pasta sauce in my mind should taste like. Dessert consisted of a pumpkin flavored tiramisu- a chocolate chip pumpkin bread infused with espresso-rum syrup topped with ricotta and brown sugar. Service: The service was impeccable. Our bartender/server was extremely friendly and went out of his way to suggest wines and dishes to accommodate us. After he saw that I was unhappy with my gnocchi he asked if there was anything wrong. I only said that I preferred the sauce from the other dish better. Five minutes later a server brought out a side bowl of the sauce for me. Â It was unbelievable and made me very happy.

My first visit to the Chef Michael White empire was not a disappointment, albeit only for lunch. Â It's in a great location in the Setai hotel, and you walk up an elegant stairwell (I felt under dressed - lots of blazers). I started with the chilled zucchini soup, basil, lemon. Â It was refreshing, and my only qualm was the portion size for the soup, even for fine dining. Â I think it was only about 4 to 5 spoonfuls. Â For entrees, the roasted skate, white bean puree, was simply and straightforwardly done with a chicken jus. Â Appreciated the crispiness, unlike the skate at Jean Georges. Â  My friends loved their tagliatelle with broccoli rabe pesto, and devoured it quickly. Â Although the portion was small, it was heavy and filling. Â Definitely plan on trying pasta dishes next time, since that is supposedly his forte. Dessert was well simple and well done. Â The rich chocolate tartaletta was perfectly sweet yet bitter, and topped with gold flakes. Â The ligurian olive oil cake was nicely paired with the tangy berry sorbet, lemon creme. Â The cake was rich like pound cake, but also less moist. Â Even with the limited menu I tried, I certainly plan on trying the rest of the Altamarea group's restaurants and will update when I have tried more of the menu. Food (8/10) Plating (4/5) Service (5*/5) Decor (5/5)

Came here for dinner this past Friday with three of my friends/former coworkers. One of them chose this restaurant and although I was worried about him making the choice, I was happy with it in the end. Three of us got there around 6:30 but we were waiting for the fourth person to show up. Once we walked in we asked for a table for four but were told that they can not sit us without the full party being there. We were a little annoyed with that since it would have been the same sized table for three or four people but we understood it since we would just be holding a table for longer or just sitting at it without ordering anything. The restaurant does not look appealing at all from the outside, especially with a sign that says "diner" on it, but the inside is a completely different story. Although there are stools by the full bar and some of the seats are booths, the place did not look cheesy whatsoever. I liked the color combination which made the place look inviting and the place seemed very clean, which for me is completely non diner like. They have multiple menus on their website which add up to a lot of options but their dinner menu alone is more limited, yet for me it definitely enough choice. I ordered the pollo sandwich which is a grilled chicken sandwich with tomato guacamole and chipotle mayo and I also ordered yuca fries. The sandwich was very good, I enjoyed every last bit of it and the yuca fries were good as well but be warned it comes with somewhat spicy ketchup which was not very good for my very sore throat (laryngitis bah). The one thing that was surprising to me was that the sandwich did not come with fries or a side salad which is more typically the case at other places. My friends seemed to enjoy their food as well (which included empanads along with other dishes) but were somewhat critical to the authenticity of it since they are both of Latin heritage. My other friend ordered the chocolate-chipotle glazed chicken wings and although she could not taste the chocolate, she seemed to enjoy it quite a bit. Aside from not seating us when it was just the three of us, I was very pleased with the service. Our waitress was sweet and quick and not too overbearing and they were quite flexible with last minute changes as well. All in all, I enjoyed my experience here and think I will be back if I am ever in the mood for Cuban food

Their bahn mis are amazing. The bread is toasted to perfection, the spiciness is precise and you get what you ask for. Â The herbs and fresh veggies make the bahn mi here one of the best in the city (I still have to find a better one, but I am not excluding the possibility). This is a fantastic place for vegetarians, aside from what's on the menu, the owner always is willing to make the fresh summer rolls vegetarian.

I love this place for brunch although they only take reservations for a group of 5 or more which makes getting a table difficult on the weekends. Egg benedict and french toast are consistently amazing and are worth the wait. I have only experienced ok service here which is a shame because I want to give it more stars.
Very good food, great service. Fish seemed very fresh, though I went with the spreads and red meats instead. Octopus is a must try. Back again soon.

I would come back to Patzeria over and over again. The pizza is so delicious! Thin crust, tons of toppings, amazing flavors, reasonable prices? What more can you ask for in a pizza? I tried the tomato/basil pizza, the grandma pizza (a square cut, thicker pizza with sweet tomato sauce), and the lasagna pizza (tastes EXACTLY like lasagna, is a bit heavier to eat and very filling. Their garlic knots are also very good (very garlicy, oily on the outside). The only thing I would really say negative about this place is that there isn't a lot of seating areas. People usually sit on stools or stand, crowded inside, or there are a few seats outside. If you wanted to have a big group eat Patzeria pizza, it would be best to do a carry out I think.

I love Hu Kitchen. Â The food is so tasty and healthy. I love the selection and the balance of what they offer. Â Great ingredients. Â Not only healthy food, also really high quality treats like chocolate and tasty granola. Â I just ordered off seamless and I was impressed by how well it travelled. Â The packaging was conscious and they have an option for no plastic, etc. Â YUM. Â This is one of my favorite restaurants in NYC.

The only reason I hesitated writing a review is because I want this to be my best kept secret. I am absolutely in love with everything that juliana's has to offer. Service... From the moment we walked in, everyone is so kind! They have a small staff but are quick to help the moment they are free. The owner is there almost every evening and is kind beyond words. It's such a refresher compared to a lot of service here in the city.

Delicious macaroons. The line can get overwhelming. Best strategy is to know your order when you hit the macaroon counter. Fun fact: Macaroons are flown in from France 3 times a week; Monday, Wednesday and Friday.
BEST CORN EVER. I normally don't enjoy eating corn on the cob, but Cafe Habana's is the exception. It's sweet and savory and spicy and juicy and AAAAAH. Oh, and the Cuban sandwich? Get that.

Ever since moving to Forest Hills and discovering Yelp I have been begging my fiancee over and over again to go to Wafas. Â It's always too far of a walk (we don't have the time) or she isn't feeling Mediterranean or some other (in retrospect) absolutely stupid excuse. Finally a friend of mine came down and I convinced him to go so she had no choice but to come with us. Â  Got there and totally forgot that it is BYOB, but that's okay because there is a liquor store right next door. Â But I would still suggest bringing your own stuff because the wine I bought there was not very good and kind of pricey. But anyway, you are all saying STFU and get to the good stuff. Â Alright, fine. Â Be that way. The place is nice and clean. Â Nothing special ambiance-wise, but when you get the food you just won't care. Â We started off with some Babaganoush. Â It was among the best I have ever had. Â Very creamy and nice and garlicky and tasted very fresh. The main courses come with 2 side dishes, we got wide variety among the three of us and everyone of them was great and, as with the appetizer, everything tasted very fresh. I wish I could remember the name of the dish I got, I had never heard of it before but it was kind of like a sausage patty. Â I think it started with an M. Â Very tasty. Â The chicken my friend got was cooked to perfection with a great amount of spice. Â  This friend of mine is the only person I have ever gone out to dinner with that will actually send a dish back simply because he does not like it. . .and I have seen him do it a number of times. Â He raves about this place and often threatens to come back down just for it (that and Nick's pizza). The craziest part is how friendly the staff is. Â The waitress was attentive and the cook came out and talked to us for a while and demanded that we come back again. Â We couldn't stop complimenting him. Definitely will return.

Lord, this place rules so hard! Â Every person I've ever taken there has raved about it. Â Everything is so delicious. Â I could eat their pork buns forever...no really...like for eternity. Â The staff are amazing and the vibe is really great. Â I've never had a bad wait staff experience and I've been there many times. Â Their happy hour 2 for 1 is perfect while you wait to be seated. Â That's right, folks. Â Some things are worth waiting for and most nights you will have a wait to get seated. Â I find if you plan to go there and put your name down at least an hour in advance of when you want to get seated, you can't go wrong. Â Central Bar is right near by so you can always pop over there for a pint as well to pass the time. Â (They have a pretty decent spread of beers at that joint, by the way.) Â The seating (long large tables) at Ippudo lends itself to meeting new people and adds to the fun of the experience as well, if you ask me. Â Even their desserts are fantastic. Â I'm just gushing at this point but, long story short...Ippudo is just as wonderful as all the hype. Â Go go go!

Eataly reminds me of the vast food emporiums found in high-end department stores in Japan, only with nothin' but Italian food. The enormity of the place is a little staggering, and there's lots to be found in the nooks and crannies, like a fresh mozzarella bar, a salumi counter (with salumi from Seattle's Salumi -- natch), and rows and rows of everything from dried pasta and canned sauce to fresh produce and grassfed dairy. But in some ways, the overwhelming nature of Eataly is a negative. It literally pounds you into submission. And honestly, strip away the celebrity gloss, and it's just an Italian food emporium. We bought nothing. BUT: We did sit at the Le Verdure counter to chow down on some veggies (we'd just downed a couple of burgers at Shake Shack), and loved it. The service was attentive and efficient, and the food was simple and fresh. The price tag was high (fifty bucks for, essentially, two smallish plates of vegetables), but we're money-stupid. And the dishes we ordered were nothing short of amazing: Grilled Japanese eggplant with arugula and caper vinaigrette, and roasted porcinis with shaved, raw butternut squash, frisee, carmelized onions and aged balsamic. The raw butternut squash and porcinis, in particular, were revelatory. If I could give a separate rating for Le Verdure, I'd give it four stars.
Waited for an hour+ and almost missed my flight but the juicy deliciousness of our pizza was well worth the wait. Simply the best pizza I have ever had.

I was fooled. I think mgmt had all their friends fill out positive reviews on Yelp to get their 4/5 stars and ~700 reviews. The service was awful. The server we had was rude and had a very confrontational manner. The food was ok but I have had better. We were seated in the front of the restaurant by the big windows, at the end of the meal my friend had come back from using the restroom and when she went to sit down the front window open and her chair (with her on it) fell out the window! It was not our fault the establishment didn't have their windows locked/unlocked. They didn't even seem surprised nor did they even bother to comp us for any part of our meal. I will not ever go back and nor would I recommend any one else.

You literally cannot go wrong at Uva. Everything is so amazing! I highly recommend the gnocchi.. I would eat it every day if it wouldn't eventually make me weigh four hundred pounds. I would definitely say this is my favorite Italian in the city, hands down!

Woorijip is my favorite fast food locale in the area even though it's a bit high on the sodium content. It's perfect for moderately adventurous eaters as it has a never-ending assortment of hot/cold salad bar items as well as lots of fun Korean Â beverages. They also give you the choice of having a simple cup of h20. The place is always crowded but turnover is brisk so somehow you can always find a seat in the back.
This place has all it take to make a killer brunch - an amazing bloody mary, an amazing burger (topped with some slices of beef tongue!), great fried chicken and yummy little doughnuts for dessert.

Got the real late hungries? Â Well, if you like cheesy, melty, mouth watering salivating pizza unlike anything you've ever tasted before this is your place! with some Artichoke faste to boot. The server told me that there's a pound of cheese on each slice! at least that's what I think he said! Â if your counting calories.... walk away and quickly!!! Be prepared to wait in line, any where from 5 - 15 minutes. And being that there is no place to eat (other than the sit down attached) you will take it out in a box or sit outside on the 2 or 3 benches. Make friends on line!

I love the homemade chocolate banana crepe. I love the mussels and fries combo. I love the cider. I love the food! You get the picture. Relaxed, quaint environment -- probably not good for large groups, but great for a date, or hang out with a girlfriend.

We came here because I thought it was not too expensive, the menu proved the contrary..... 15$ appetizer, 30$ entrees are not very cheap. However, we had our own bottle of wine with us (another place with BYOB had a 2 hour waiting), which we could drink for 25US$. Fair enough. Atmosphere is very nice, I like the interior a lot, especially the ceiling! We started off with the grits, nice texture. Good flavour. Quite heavy though. Some warm bread was surfed, savory-muffin like. Nice, although I don't like warm bread, it should be on room temperature, so the dough is cool and not too fluffy. I know from other reviewers on Yelp that Americans like it hot, though. I am European, just so you know. Next up was the duck. I don't get the complaints. It was absolutely great. One of the best I've ever had (and I've been to tons of high-end restaurants). Service was OK, not overattentive, which I prefer. But again, that's Europe vs America.... Conclusion: certainly not cheap, but very, very good.

I have minor contention. The name of this place is hard to remember, and it's pricey. Â Whitman and Bloom sounds a lot more like an accounting firm, than a fine dining restaurant. Â That said, wow! Â I drank a glass of Guinness and loved it. Â I typically don't like Guinness for it's bitterness, and never order it. Â That was just the drink order. Â We had shared the Chicken Liver, the Roast Beef Ribeye along with the Mushroom Soup and a cured meat plate of some sort - I forget the name. Â I'm no restauranteur, not by a long shot. But, if you're looking for a unique dinning experience, the food here is that. Â These are really unique dishes that taste GREAT ! Â The general theme, and bottom line for me was this: Â Every dish that I ate, I really loved, but I couldn't exactly figure out why I loved it. Â Chicken Liver Pate in a cup? Yeah! gimme a spoon. Â A Roast Beef Ribeye with about a spoons worth of fattiness? What? I like fat!! Since when? Who am I?

Seems like the classier of the pio pios. It is much larger than it looks from the outside. The lower level has interesting wall decorations that make you feel like you're on the inside of a nest. The chicken is very tender, juicy, and well-seasoned. The rest of the food seemed a bit underwhelming considering the prices. But I suppose with the atmosphere, that may be expected. The chicken matador was enough for 3-4 people. Loved the chicken. The rice/beans and salad were alright. The hotdogs, fries, and plantains were eh. It's often crowded, so make reservations though they are pretty accommodating. We had a reservation for a group of 7 but had to add 2 more on arrival, which they initially denied, but then accommodated us, saying we'd have to squeeze. But there was plenty of room. The sangria is quite good. I don't normally have sangria, but it was highly recommended by a friend. She was right.

Quick bite, lunch dinner, sneak into theater meal - whatever - this is the spot. Everything is fresh, delicious, filling and so affordable. If the line looks long, just wait. Take the next bus. Just wait for it. It will move quick and the staff is quick and friendly.

bar beer and wine. it's whatever. clams small. butter is good with bread. octopus good char, flavor. expensive. butcher's steak perfect, inexpensive. favorite steak in the neighborhood. prepared well every time. shoulder blade chop (lamb) delicious. get the butcher's steak though. pan-fried mashed potatoes very rich, delicious. spinach gratin good, not memorable. sea beans (special) very good. i miss. m-e-t-h-o-d man.

YUMMY!!!! While I write this, I'm drooling a little thinking about the lunch I had here. I feel so bad for Jason J. and I wish he had tried the sandwich I got. It was the Chicken and egg sandwich, same as Scott B. Truly magnificent. The place itself is small and cute, reminds me of a place you'd find on the coast in NC. Â The homemade caramels are to die for! Seriously, get some. No, really, REALLY, it's A.MAZ.ING. Get the sea salt one. Truly orgasmic. Â I can't wait to go and try their brunch one of these days.

I've been here about four times and their pizzas are consistently excellent. Â I've waited over an hour during peak times and there have been times that I've been seated right away. Â I went this past Friday for the first time in a few years and boy have I forgot about how good this pizza is!!! Â In fact, the line was so long that if it wasn't for my boyfriend who was born and raised in Queens I probably would have just left. Â He's been trying to come here for the past few years and each time something gets in his way so he was determined. Â  Anyway, not much to add to the reviews on here. Â I like the onions, mushrooms and sausage on the original pie. Â We also ordered a big pie to go with sardines which was great for breakfast. Â The bf ordered spumoni for dessert which is actually cake not ice cream. Â My one only complaint is that the pizza crust was a bit burnt to the point that you couldn't eat the crust. Â I mean it's bound to happen where there are lots of pies in the oven but bit disappointing since we waited +1 hr. Â Good thin crust though.

mmmm mark..... you scratch my little burger and a beer itch. cheap and oh soo tasty... just what i want you to be. solid food for the carnivores. and some nice beers to wash 'em down with. (think - bacon *in* the beef of the bacon sliders.... mmmm baccoon...) mark, i *will* be back.

When my friends suggest "Brunch at Calle Ocho" Â i know it means a: fun filled day of free delicious breads and muffins, Â unlimited Sangria for everyone, and a flavorful eggilicous breakfast. Â  Do I really have to say more? Just don't forget to make a reservation because sitting in the main dining room definitely tops the front section.
Not sure what the fuss is about. Came here for brunch today and had Eggs Norwegian. To be honest, the only thing I liked about my dish was the homefries.

Beautiful place with tons of TV's, helpful servers and cold beer. Wings are decent but we were told we could not have blue cheese or ranch dip. The chef disapproves. WTF! Lobster Mac and cheese more like breadcrumbs and pasta. Overall place has promise. We'll see if the culinary end catches up to the other more favorable aspects of the place.

I've known this place for a while now and it never disappoints. Best place for late night munchies in the East Village. They have a crazy huge selection of sauces... I usually get the fries with garlic aioli - so good.

The food here is fantastic. The veggie burger is heaven. The desserts are to die for. However, the service leaves a lot to be desired. The waiters are rude and make you feel unwelcome, and try to rush you through your meal. That said, as long as you know what to expect from the service, the food is a must have.

This place is INSANE. Part restaurant, part grocery store, all Italian emporium. This thing is monstrously huge. The restaurants (emphasis on plural!) are spaced throughout the grocery shelves and displays, making it a bit of a maze. But what an enticing maze it is - good thing I ate before I shopped, otherwise I'd have bought way more than I'd planned. The groceries are a bit more expensive than your average Trader Joe's, likely because they're all imported from Italy - the distinction that makes Eataly unique. Not everything is amazing, but it is all authentic. At any rate, this review focuses on the restaurant - specifically, their penne. Now, when you tell them al dente, you had best mean it. Mine was, admittedly, just shy of undercooked - which is in fact how I like it. But then, I sometimes snack on raw pasta while preparing it, so Eataly's "al dente" is not for everyone. Still, the sauce is an absolute star - just right, none of that weird sweetness I sometimes find. Freshly-grated parmesean adds a classy touch to a table with a great view of the UPS truck idling outside. Though the staff may have been a little too classy for me - a fifth star could have been earned by smoothing out the gruff staff. Still, it didn't exactly put me off my penne and at a whopping $13 for an acceptably-sized plate, it didn't break the bank either.

I seriously didn't think it was possible to fall deeper in love with MoMo. But, surprise, I have. Every visit tops the last, and every bite continues to blow my mind. Phillip (the owner) is so incredible and his excitement and passion for food makes the experience that much more exciting and passionate. Trust his advice when ordering. Things I've recently fallen for: Tofu Salad (what the hell is going on with that tofu. I want to eat it daily), Kinpira (whaaaaaaaaaaat), and the vegan "eel" bomb. They never fail to impress. Hands down, my favorite.

Extremely tiny store. Went here on a Friday at 4:50pm, where the store was nearly empty. Good sign! Usually the line is towards the next store by 5:30pm. Had the Totto Chicken Paitan Ramen - the simplest one in my point of view. Loved it! Ramen was cooked just right, the broth was perfect, and the chicken tender. Yum! I would come back here when I have the energy to wait in line or am hungry extra early!

heartttttttttssssssssssss tia pol is the SH*T! despite the long wait, the hostess was super gracious and agreed to take my cell number while we wandered around waiting for a table to be ready. When we came back, she remembered my name and told me a table was being cleared for us. Now on to the important stuff - food and drink. We ordered a pitcher of red sangria, which to our chagrin came in a rather TINY almost individually sized carafe. But DAMN did that thing last, and we can drink! I'm not sure if it was the ice melting or what, but it really packed a punch and we got 7 or 8 glasses out of it. Also, the waiter kept returning to repour it for us anytime we were almost empty. By far the best dish there is the squid in squid ink with rice. The scallops with chorizo in pureed melon are a close second. My boyfriend and I tried to recreate both dishes the following week, but after seeing how much scallops and squid ink cost (around $30 a jar! and they give you like HALF a jar in the dish) we realized we had really gotten a bargain at tia pol. They were also super generous with the bread so we sopped up ALL our deliciousssssss squid ink. Will definitely be going back there. Great deal for tapas and they excel at seafood. Although I didn't try them, their salads looked delish too!

After hearing about this from like everyone alive I finally tried it on a cold winter night. Â And there is no better night to try a place like this. Â It's super cozy inside and we were lucky there was no wait for a table for two. Â Saw a huge party outside freezing for an hour or so though. The meatballs are SO AMAZING. Â I had the beef with spicy meat sauce and dare I saw it's the best I have ever had. Â Also tried the reindeer slider which was delicious but I think the sauce makes the meatball. Â To wash it down the perfect thing is cream soda with homemade vanilla ice cream float. Â Renewed my love for floats completely. Finally, the ice cream sandwich for dessert was OUT OF THIS WORLD. Â The chocolate cookie was super moist and super HUGE. Â Homemade mint ice cream was perfect with bits of mint inside but never too rich. Â  I think I also had a salad or something to balance my meal. Â Whatever. Â Come for the balls (meat and ice cream) and floats.
Get the salmon miso soup! Â I have never seen it anywhere else and it is awesome!
My after-work dinner goto place. The brisket taco is amazing !

Yea, this pizza is awesome! Got the spinach and artichoke slice and it really taste like the best spinach and artichoke dip I've ever had on a thick pizza crust. Â Delicious, filling, and creative. Â As much as I would like to taste the other options don't know if I could ever pull away from that spin/artichoke, I'm sold! Â Also love the fact that the place is so small, no seats, no fancy decor, the pizza does all the talking here.

This place has the best octopus I have ever tasted in my life, and this is from someone that grew up in Astoria surrounded by wonderful Greek places serving up killer octopus. I dare say that they even beat out the old Titan next door. Â  This is not traditional Greek food in terms of preparation, it's obvious they are employing modern French culinary techniques, but I think it works, and it makes mp stand out from the already amazing Greek restaurants in the area. This is one of my favorite restaurants in all of ny, and my fave in Astoria. Everything I've had here is amazing, and service is always warm and welcoming.
Not a fan for chicken & waffles. But I guess it was my first experience. Other things on the menu are not so good.

I heard that the Apple Strudel was to die for so I bookmarked it because my bf likes apple desserts...I don't at all. But, I liked this one :) We came here after the Guggenheim, which has a really interesting Italian Futurist exhibit at the moment. We were waiting for a Restaurant Week reservation and didn't want to eat anything heavy and ruin our dinner. Coming to Cafe Sabarsky was perfect. We got 2 different teas. They come in these tea pots & one would have been enough to share, but we have different tastes. I liked the Fruity Tea and he liked the Oolong. I think I had 4 cups myself! haha The Apple Studel was delicious. I liked the fluffy whipped cream and the way that the apple was sliced really thin. The dessert was light and exactly what we needed. You can peruse around the border of the cafe and check out the other desserts too, which I refrained from doing because I have too much of a sweet tooth. Speaking of which, I would like to come back and try the hot chocolate when it gets colder! mmmm After enjoying the antique ambiance and our apple studel, we took a walk in Central Park. It was a delightful afternoon!
Hands down the best falafel ever. Fresh and delicious. Only loses a star because it's a tiny, busy place and the setup is a little stressed. Still, so fawking good!

I'm not sure what the hubbub is all about? Â Its average falafel at best. Â But with its hype and rating so high, i expect much much better. Â It's not really that great, and the cabbage in there is a nice try to mix things up and be original i guess, but i don't think it works that well. Â I would opt for one of the many many more authentic falafel joints instead of Taim.
simply amazing! corn. mole. tacos. try any of those and you won't be disappointed!!

Everything was great... except for our waitress. The waitress was not personable and engaging as she was with the table sitting aside from us (an older couple)... When I asked about two different things on the menu, she responded in a very condescending manner. It was my first time visiting with my husband and baby, and I was unfamiliar with how the food was paired or if it was accompanied with anything. Instead of a friendly response, I got, 'it is what it says it is' tone.. When the couple was greeted sitting next to us, the same server greeted them with a background food knowledge of their produce, food and companies mission statement.. with us.. (maybe she was being discriminatory cause we had a stroller), she was very hasteful and I felt rushed!!.. I didnt have a chance to really look at the cocktail menu.. so when I asked for a suggestion, she gave me 3.. but didnt tell me anything special about any of them to entice my selection.. I tried again, to ask about a 'refreshing drink' and she responded, 'like i said, its either this one, this one, or this one'...So I just went with the Thyme cocktail... I dont know, the food, ambience, decor, and atmosphere outweighed the service by far... Our nieghboring table was very cordial and hospitable.. The wait staff just seems over worked and over it.. and you know what... It wasnt packed wall to wall like an ordinary brunch day, due to the holiday.. so I dont understand all the dreery faces and our waitresses rushing manner, (we did make a RSVP 3 weeks in advance) ... Cheer up! Its a beautiful place and cause to be apart of.. Was just very disturbed by the waitresses service.. Next time, I will address it and ask for a different server..

I suppose it was good. Â Innovative pairings of ingredients on menu. Â Note: you won't be seated unless your entire party is present. Â Open 24 hours, but a little too formally trendily for late night eats... 1. Food: Average. Â Mac n cheese with truffle oil, cornmeal calamari, pork chops with roasted pear, salmon BLT, and country fried steak. Â Pork chops on the dry and overcooked side, despite the request for medium. Â Should had the fried chicken & waffles - alas, cholesterol. Â Friend's country fried steak tasted deliciously buttery. Â  2. Service: Good. Â Cool suspenders on the waiters. Â Glasses well filled. 3. Atmosphere: Sat in downstairs lounge, which was a bit claustrophobic with its low ceilings. Â Try to be seated upstairs if possible. Â Door to basement storage in lounge kept on clanging, and there were whiffs of stale and stagnant air. Â Cool rocking ottoman-styled chairs, though.

This place is great. Delicious food, hot, fast and unpretentious. It's a treat to watch the guys behind the counter, too - they're so fast and proficient at making your food. Very friendly and welcoming.

So tonight we decided to give the place a second chance. Â We live in the neighborhood and were coming home from a movie. Â The place we though would have a lively "bar" or "nightcap" scene. Â We entered the door and walked up to the bar to be greeted by an awestruck bartender with a hipster mustache who had to ask the hostess if the restaurant was still open or not. Â Clearly it must not have been as two tables were sat, and 6 other people were having drinks at the bar. Â It must have been closed. Â So the two of us as well as the three behind us left in a embarassed fury and happened to walk right past the owner. Â Maybe hipsters should stick to EMO and Music and stop opening restaurants. Â Who TRAINS these people. Terrible Terrible Terrible. Â We are going to give it one more shot, after all, they did just opened....and it is Greenpoint.

Soooo good! My family is from Thailand and I've never been able to find Khao Man Kai in the city--and there's is great! They're thai iced tea is fresh, made with condensed milk and amazing! They're larb, pad ka naa, pad thai, pad see ew, and som tum are all very good also. Definitely come here if you want more authentic thai food on 9th ave.

This place is fantastic. We came for restaurant week and lunch was unbelievable. I had the following: appetizer: mushroom & farro insalata Â (good) entree: Sweet Corn Agnolotti (incredible) dessert: tartufo (fantastic) We sat at the bar and the service was great, the food was fantastic. I just moved to NYC 6 weeks ago, but so far this is one of my favorite restaurants. We'll definitely be back.

Delicate and original rendition of original Italian recipes. Â Well crafted menu where each dish we ordered was cooked to perfection and amazingly spices. Â friendly atmosphere of the wine bar complementing the family style of the restaurant. Â Great place

The broth is significantly better than most hot pot places; Â fresh and tasty. The prices per dish can be expensive ranging from $5 to $10 (if you get their specialty ones). I ate here a few times with my bf and the bill can come up to $80-100 for just the two of us! Â Depending on the types of foods you get. Â But we were plenty full each time so it's worth going once in a while!

After coming away profoundly disappointed by Noodle Bar last year, I came to Ssam Bar with a bit lower expectations than I probably should have. Still, I had a great meal here and was reassured that I like Dave Chang for a good reason. Duck Liver Mousse: not quite foie, but still great. Tripe with chiles: tripe can either be totally delicious or absolutely fucking wretched depending on how it's cooked and who cooks it. Luckily, this was the former. Great texture, great spice. Shanghai noodles: probably my only real "meh" moment. Just not that exciting; no ingredients really popped out or excited me. Pork belly bao: compared favorably to my own personal favorites, the ones from The Chairman truck in SF. Chard and fried onions: veggie special the week I stopped by, and probably the best dish of the night. Great preparation - tasted of sesame oil and garlic, and the fried onions were a great touch. Trout with pistachio sauce: the sauce was a great touch here. Light, nutty, but not overpowering, it cut through the flavor of the trout well. Fried rice cakes and sausage: kind of a porky ddokboki thingie, but this one really stood out for me. I ate most of it, and didn't allow my dinner mates to get too much. I am a greedy pig at times. All in all, only the Shanghai noodles really missed for me. Other than that, great food, and it wasn't busy - that kept up my lucky streak for NYC this summer. For whatever reason I missed every rush and big line...

A friend took me to check out this place and we got lucky and missed the crowed that quickly formed after we entered and quickly ordered. There seems to be three choices: Artichoke, Margarita, and cheeseburger from what I remember. As we got our food with very little wait we grabbed a spot in front of the store where make shift tables are available. From what he tells me is that at times the line can get long, and soon after finishing his sentence poof I turn around and there was a line that stretched onto the sidewalk. After taking a few bites I was really impressed that it tasted just like Artichoke and the crisp bread gave it a similar taste to eating spinach artichoke dip and baked pita. Artichoke presents a tasty, crisp, warm, and filling pizza with a flavor that at first seems weird in pizza form but soon you appreciate the adventurous flavors that each bite has. I'll definitely be back to try out the other flavors and to satisfy my strange new addiction for artichoke pizza.
Everything was great! Â From the wait staff right to dessert.

When I ran by here the other day and saw the Stumptown sign in the window it was as if the clouds parted above me and angels began trumpeting. Quality coffee, in my neighborhood? Steps from the dog run? Surely life cannot be this good. Yes, it can. And my husband said his breakfast sandwich was the best he's ever had. While he is given to hyperbole, I still take that as a rousing endorsement. Neighbors, please go and keep this place afloat, I implore you!

I rarely stumble upon places that A/ i can squeeze a foot into, or B/ that actually turn out to be worthwhile. This place was a magnificent find. The second cheapest bottle of wine turned out to be rather nice, the atmosphere was top notch and the food was just superb. No complaints. I dont think we spent more than $45 a person (didn't order appetizers/dessert). I ordered the monkfish, not knowing what monkfish even was - and holy crap was it bloody amazing. Go here. I know ill be returning...
The very best gluten free pizza crust I have ever eaten. Â The Kalua Pork pizza is amazing. Â We are definitely looking forward to eating here again!

Stopped in Â with a friend after a long bus ride up to NYC for the weekend. We were seated right away as it was around 10:45PM on a Thursday night. Started with the pork buns, and then had the Akamaru Modern. I'll be honest... both were really good but it didn't blow me away or reach the expectations i paced when i tried to come last year and was greeted with a 1 hour wait. But all in all, Ippudo is a place i'll definitely want to come back to in the future but i probably wouldn't go out of my way or even wait more than 20 minutes for. Quick Tip for you beer lovers: Try the Japanese Stout they have along with the pork bun. Pretty good combo!

This is the restaurant in the area that I always recommend to people. Tagliatelle with boar ragu is my go to dish with the house red wine. The goat cheese crostini is another favorite. This place is consistently solid. Dinner for 2 at the bar is always a pleasure.
yumm

So the 2 ramen places on my list of places to go was Ippudo and Totto ramen and it could be because I ordered the right thing but I have to say that I liked Ippudo more. Â I normally pick the hole in the wall over the nice fancy shmancy place and to be honest the prices are pretty high for ramen but it's just sooo good that it deserves no less than 5 stars. Â I had their special, the black pork sesame ramen, and I just have to say that the first slurp of noodle I had - a tingle of sesame oil that got sucked up with the first slurp of noodle knocked my socks off. Â I didn't expect to be that impressed by the ramen here but the more I ate the more I just couldn't stop. Â The soup flavoring was amazing, the black pork was tender, and the flavored egg was cooked perfectly. Â I didn't leave a single drop of soup in my bowl. Â I have to say though that people who don't eat it fast enough didn't seem to enjoy it as much. Â They had more noodle than soup left and at some point noodles start getting soft so slurp away and do it fast and loud if you want to enjoy it at it's prime! :)

They should put the phone order taker in a quiet back room. Â Everytime I call I end up shouting into the phone and more than once my order has been effected and once didn't show up at all. Â They need to work much harder on front of house service. Â This isn't a club or a hangout..it's a job in the SERVICE industry. Â All the little annoyances really do add up.

I think it is overrated. Â  I had a gelato sorbet that was way too gooey and sweet. Â Furthermore, there is almost nowhere to sit----a few uncomfortable bar stools. Looks fancy, but I get the sense that it's much ado about nothing.

The food was good no problems there. In fact it was very tasty, how ever i was still hungry and was already 20 bucks in. That was a little off for me. A little cheaper and i'll go here 3 times a day even though they open at 6 pm. Bummer

We went there for brunch and I have to say I don't understand the high ratings for this restaurant. Yes, it's cute inside and the waiters are rather friendly, but the food didn't do it for me. The strawberry rhubarb juice was watery and not what I expected, the strawberry chunks in the salad were pointless, and the chocolate blueberry cake in lieu of bread or toast was tasteless.
Nice decor, great food, good customer service

I write this review after calling the restaurant 3 times at 6 hour intervals. The hostess assures me that Andrew will return my call but he does not. We went to Locanda Verde for lunch during restaurant week. There was no indication on the menus that they were partcipating even though they were listed on the restaurant week website. When our bill came we were charged for a la carte lunches. Upon returning home I called the restaurant and the hostess confirmed that they offered a $24.07 lunch consisting of an appetizer, main course and dessert which is exactly what we had. She took my name and number and assured me that the manager would return my call. He didn't. The next day at 11 am I called and explained my story again. No reply. At 5 this evening I called again. The manager was in a staff meetin but would return my call by 6. Â It is 5:30 now and I doubt I will ever hear from Andrew. It's not that the food wasn't good. But a restaurant is more than good food. It's about HOSPITALITY. Comically, the last hostess said she would send Andrew the manager an email. I asked her were he was. She replied, "the next room" 5:45 and still no reply I'll keep you posted.

Have ordered almost everything on the menu, all of which has been delicious! If you go make sure you get the scallops, pork buns, and fried chicken OMG outrageous! Only downside, place can expensive if you visit with a crowd.

How fantastic is this place? Â Maybe its because they take their crepes so seriously- maybe its the "Amelie" ambiance this place has... its cheesy but the wear and tear on the interior of this restaurant make you feel like you've encountered a secret spot in Bon Marche! Definately try the leek and goat cheese crepe- with a giant Pelligrino to complete the experience. Â Or wine...

This small local establishment definitely made me a fan overnight! I work in the area and was looking for a new flavor, and I have found it! My first order were the Breakroom Fries, which were messy and filling; exactly what I needed after a long day at work. My second order was the Taco Platter (Tempura Fish Taco and Pork Belly Taco). The flavor was unique and reminded me a lot of Los Angeles - which is a plus! I would be curious to see how the tacos would taste with corn tortillas verses flour tortillas, but that's just me because I'm Mexican. Other than that, I will be frequenting this local spot. Great service, young staff yet fun and professional, and great tasting food!

I came here for brunch the other week. There was a bit of a wait, but honestly where in NY is there not going to be a wait for brunch on a Sunday at noon? As my regular, I ordered the blueberry pancakes. One thing that I had never seen before, but was most delighted by was the oatmeal inside the pancakes. These were the best pancakes I have had all summer. The flavor, that seems so obvious to go well together, had never occurred to me before. On top were fresh strawberries, raspberries and blueberries. While I was certainly full after having eaten one of the pancakes, I of course found myself eating almost the entire other one, before I made the waitress take it away from me. The restaurant is very open which I love and has a great feel. The staff was very accommodating and I could most definitely see myself going back for a second round!
My favorite mexican steak tacos. great taste and authentic. LIved in california and it was easy to find mexican tacos there, but not so easy here. I was looking for a while and I am happy I found it.

Lets just start by saying saying time i come here i leave happy and full. Get the roast pork with the gandules and black beans!! The sweet plantains are a good plate to share between 2 people and the flan is really good. Food is just really good and authentic. Very family run feel, really nice and friendly.

We went for my niece's birthday. Â We had a great time. Â Good food and great service. Â I had the seafood risotto, it was very good. Â Their sangria was very good, as well. Â It was the first time I tried black berry sangria. Â The staff was very friendly. Â The owner was there and he greeted us when we came in. Â I would definitely recommend this restaurant to friends and family. Â My sister has been there three times in two months, she loves it. Very cute restaurant.

3.5 stars! i like the food but the service could be improved!! I am a much bigger fan of Â their sister restaurant Luzzo's in east village (although the atmosphere at Da mikele is nicer) the pizza crust here is thicker & more bready than the one served at Luzzo's, w/ a crispy bottom!! i think they specialize in square pizza vs. the neopolitan at Luzzo's ---complimentary foccocia style bread before your meal! ---large Capricciosa (square pizza): yummy!! the large was enough for 3 of us to share! ---large Vegetali dell'orto (square pizza): not bad ---grandma pizza: thick crusted w/ a nice crunch as well! not bad although I would've liked more cheese... it was almost unnoticeable! why the SERVICE wasn't up to par? we made an RSVP for 10 people, which was great! but by the end of the meal they stopped refilling our waters, even after we asked... and after 2 hours they kicked us out because they had another party coming in.. rude!! NOTE: "da mikele" might not be the first thing you see on the sign out front!! a little bit confusing if you don't know the exact address!! they offer Apertivo hour, free appetizers at the bar from 5-7pm mon-fri just like their sister restaurant Ovest!! i'll be back!
Love this place. No better spot to get a really great meal and a flawless cocktail while spending a minimal amount of money. And if you're feeling luxurious, go for the lobster- you won't regret it.

Food was excellent, will be returning. Ordered the brisket for two, antibiotic free and prepared perfectly. Initially they said they had ran out so we decided to go elsewhere, until they magically found more? It was an odd situation but the staff was very accommodating and created an amazing experience. Great craft beer draft menu. IPA, Belgian, and sours.

This was rated one of the best ramen places in the city, before all the others came along 5 years ago. Yesterday I came here again to try and remember why it's always so packed. On a Sunday at 3pm, there was still a 45 minute. So my friends and I walked down to get dessert Â before dinner. Once I got the text and the call from the restaurant we quickly went back and claimed our table for 3. I like the decoration of the entire restaurant. The bar is lined with ramen under the cases. Bowls are decorated and hung on the wall. My friends and I ordered 3 bowls of the Akamari Modern with a poached egg. And for starters we ordered 2 orders of the pork belly buns. The pork belly buns came in orders of 2 for $9. There were three of us, so we ordered 2 orders! Our ramen came and it such a delightful site! It came with three pieces of sliced pork! And the egg came poached perfectly. The noodles were long and just the right chewiness. The broth was deliciously made from miso. I never pay for overly priced bowls of ramen where I can make at home with shinramyun, but ippudo was exceptionally good for a once in a while treat!

I love this restaurant because it's warm, spacious, and very clean. Â I think this place has an amazing atmosphere and feel, but I don't think I could afford it all the time. Â I like their use of organic materials - I had their mushroom egg pizza and spinach with goat cheese. Â I would like to visit again, but I do know I need to watch my wallet :)

I ordered from Butcher Bar again because I was really craving BBQ and there aren't many delivery options in Astoria. Â I was pleasantly surprised! Â It came quickly and was fantastic! Â So good I ordered it again the next night... Â They responded to my last review which I appreciated but didn't want to seem like I was looking for a freebie so I didn't order again. Â People are very inclined to write when it's bad but not so much when it's good so here's the skinny. Â I had burnt end rib tips both times and they were soooo good I couldn't not get them again. Â The brisket and the pulled pork were also delicious. Â The green beans were much better but just ok. Â I wish they had collard greens. Â Hint hint... I hope this consistency continues because I will be ordering again! Â Thank you!

Loved this place: Sat inside at the counter Menu featured seasonal ingredients & written on a receipt Wanted a light appetizer so ordered the charred string beans, it was delicious Ordered the grass fed hamburger as my main. Burger was great & fries were crispy Had the concord grape mousse. This was outstanding. Meal was reasonably priced & would definitely come back!

I would give 3 and a half stars. Its good food def!! The decor is awful. enchiladas were slammin but too expensive. The guac was really not that great. I will say the carne asada dish was really good.

These sandwiches are hefty and reasonably priced. Â Yes, they are greasy, but the menu offers a wide variety of creative combinations. Â Seating is sparse, but the cooks at the bar-style seating are extremely friendly and attentive.

One of the best ramen and pork bun I ever had. MUCH better than Momofuku and even better than what I had in Japan! I was in Japan about a month ago and they were showing some documentary about Mr. Kawahara(the owner) on TV. It was pretty cool.
Their ramen is really good but the wait is always so long - you have to get there extremely early that's the only downside.

3 week reservation notice? 10 minute wait after I MADE my ridiculous reservation? I was a little put off by the people up front. But the restaurant is a different story. Calle Ocho is fine, but it is no better than any of the other brunch places around. It's a scene, and has unlimited, decent Sangria. I probably would only come back if I needed a brunch place for 4 or more people (lushes).

1. Pork 1. Steak 1. Chicken Yes please one of each! First visit was a trial run I tried everything and played it safe with the meduim sauce. Pork was the best and I could have done the next level hot sauce. So I have a plan for next time. :-) Meat is very fresh and flavorful. Steak has a strong pepper taste. Line gets crazy out the door near dinner time. I will be back, I likey.

What to Â say? Pretty disappointed... As latino myself, I was expecting more from the food from this place considering how pricey it is and the good reviews it has on yelp. I went with a group of 12 peeps around 2pm on a Saturday during brunch (somebody from the group did the reservation the day before). The experience was mixed. Some of them liked the food but, as a latino myself, I can only give 2 stars to this place. The service was ok, not particularly great. If you want to experience the traditional warmth of Colombian people there are better restaurants in Queens for that. I ordered Bandeja Paisa. The white rice was dry; the black beans tasted like if they just came out of the can with no added flavor at all; the decent portion of beef was ok ; and the chicharron (pork skin), somewhat dry and not crunchy, was the "highlight" of the plate but still just average compared to other places I've been. I also tried the Arroz con Pollo that my girlfriend ordered and again, below average latin food. For dessert I tried the Tres Leches cake that was 50% frosting and the other 50% tasted like just regular cake? Worst Tres Leches I've tried to this date? Â As far I can remember. There is nothing in particular that attracted my attention and that would make me go back, there are too many good places with much better food and service at a subway ride from here. For the quality, and even considering the neighborhood it is in, this is under average pricey latin food. Please, hire a Colombian grandma' to help you improve the food!

Standard american fare kicked up a notch. I guess they're known for their mac 'n cheese. We tried the trio wich was not bad, but a little bland. I've def had better mac 'n cheese so it was a little disappointing. Otherwise everything else was pretty good. I had the calamari salad which was huge and quite tasty. Tried the mashed potatoes and the chicken and waffles off a friends' plate. Bit of a wait and crowded, but a good place to go in Chelsea.

Happy to be the 101 review! Ever since I moved to Brooklyn, I had come here with my girlfriend at least once a month. We know we will keep coming back as long as the quality remains the same. For now, it has kept improving each time. Little details seems to matter here. Thank you, Barboncino. Barboncino is alive. The restaurant is well taken care of. The dinning room seems to be a reflection of the owners unpretentious approach. By not trying to be Italy (that's impossible), Barboncino has a great ambiance. It is little gold pebble found in the middle of the street. The pizzas are great. Every now and then I find my all time favorite pizza (with capers and anchovies), in the specials. All the pizzas are great, specially the simplest ones! The ingredients are of the freshest quality, so can't go wring with any pizza! They have Peronni beer on draft, and that's always refreshing. The bar area is cool too! Finally, the prices are is what gave Barboncino a five star rating. Great balance between price and quality. Ill be back for sure, probably Â tomorrow!

This pace was just OK. We had the "Tony's Shrimp" and Ravioli Bolognaise, then a classic sundae and gelato. Food came on time and tasted OK. As per the reviews here we heard 4 "Happy Birthday" songs during our dinner. You can get better Italian at Sbarro's on Broadway to be honest. Service was friendly but I don't think I'd go back.

Had one of the best meals I've had in a long time last night. Â A good friend took me out for my birthday, and this dinner was quite the birthday present. Â We split the beef carpaccio and seared scallops to start--both were unbelievably good. Â And the kitchen split them and plated our portions for us, which is always a nice touch. Â She had the arctic char, which she loved; I had the skate, which was to die for. Â We also split the brussel sprouts with pears and bacon (!!!!!!). Â From start to finish, all the food was so fresh and seasonally-prepared. Â Top all this off with a great bottle of red, and fantastic, laid-back service, and this was a memorable evening. Â Great space, very open and airy, yet cozy at the same time.
Best mexican food I've had in New York so far! Downside is that there is no seating available inside the place. But you can sit outside, and enjoy their delicious food!

Sushi Yasuda is very good. However, I wonder, for the price, is it really the BEST Sushi in NYC? I feel like it is very good, but for the price I don't think it is worth it. There are a ton of very good sushi restaurants with fresh, tasty fish. I don't think Yasuda is the end all, be all of NYC Sushi.
Amazing. Â The bake is mind blowing, the fish is fresh and tasty, the price is right, and for now it's Byob.

Being the spice queen that I am, Saxon & Parole had me at hello with their Bowery Fix cocktail drink. The drink is made up of the following: Espolon blanco, mezcal, yellow chartreuse, fresh bell pepper and chili oil. It kind of reminded me of a spicy margarita but it had a little more of a kick to it, which was nice. By suggestion of the waiter, I also ordered a Chamomile Sazerac(Cognac, rye, chamomile, peychaud's bitters). If you ever wanted to try a man's beverage for the hell of it- then this is a friendly starter. The scent and after taste of the chamomile lightens up the heaviness of the brandy and whiskey in this cocktail. Â We started out with a plate of mussels. Nothing impressive- basically just mussels tossed in a spicy marinara sauce. We paired this with their french fries which were really great. Served with a Sriacha-like ketchup(good) and blue cheese mayo(which I did not try). For dinner, I ordered the seared salmon which came with sweet potato puree, grilled scallion, and caper-raisin emulsion. While the presentation was pretty, my first taste of the salmon was lacking flavor. There were little splotches of sauce of some sort around the fish (couldn't quite make out what it was) but it did not do the dish justice. Grilled scallion was okay. The sweet potato puree was only enough to decorate the plate-wasn't able to get a good enough taste. One friend had ordered the hanger steak(currently I do not eat meat) which looked very flavorful-they even offered some of their homemade bbq sauce for the side. Another friend ordered the roasted organic half chicken with charred fennel, kalamata olives, orange, and sundried tomatoes. She had no complaints. The chicken looked tender and it was described as a mediterranean type dish. Â  Our waiter was attentive and friendly. Overall, Saxon + Parole receives an A for drinks, and a B- for dinner.

I love, love, LOVE this place! Â The ambiance is so very mellow and intimate. Â Best for one-on-one time with your best friend or your signif other. Â Very attentive service if they are not busy. Â There can be a wait since the place is pretty small. The food is excellent. Â Small portions but each bite is extremely tasty. Â I love how the flavors are perfectly balanced. Â They had an entire meal for $17 to $20. Â If you go before 7 pm, you can try their afternoon special or afternoon tea special. Â The first is a rice bowl with some sort of protein (salmon, chicken, unagi). Â Rice is sooooo good. Â Comes with Genmaicha. Â The latter seems to be English-influenced with two types of sandwiches, baked goods, sample of desserts, and choice of tea. Happy hour from...4 or 5 to 7 pm. Â Buy a drink and get free appetizers. Believe me, you're going to want to go for lunch...and dinner....and afternoon tea....and late-night dessert....

New Yorkers are partial to standing in line for something they can walk up to for free. How else to explain the once endless queues at Magnolia, even after cupcakes proliferated the city, or those that continue at Big Gay Ice Cream or for the cronut? Sure, you can argue that this particular store is doing something significantly elevated from the competition, but I could name a few places putting out ice cream on Big Gay's level without such a wait. This is even stranger when it comes to Wah Fung Number 1 Fast Food, which serves a menu of roast meat that can be found at literally dozens of places within a few blocks. And Wah Fung has some disadvantages over the competition - there are no tables, the taped over menu is confusing to read, and no circulation against the heat. But yet a line snakes out the door day in and day out like no other place. The reason is the price. One used to be able to get a dish of roast pork, noodles and rice for $2.50. It's now $4, but the size of the portion is absolutely ginormous. So I hopped in the one recent Sunday afternoon to see, as they say, what the hype was all about. Line took around 20 minutes, wherein you are treated to the sight of one man switching from piling rice into a dish, cleaving rows of roast meat and taking money all in the course of a few seconds. Now, this place almost certainly could reduce the line by employing two or even three people, but while waiting it became clear that the line was a key part of the business model. 'We're waiting, so this must be good.' After finishing my meal on a nearby park bench - thankfully it wasn't too hot or it would have been hard to consume - I've got the following three thoughts: The char siu is in the upper quarterlie of what we get in New York. Crucially, it's not too dry and maintains the sweetness of the glaze. It's legit. The portion is massive, including about a pound of rice. Why is this so big? It may seem like a value, but unless you've got three people, most of this is going in the garbage. It's not that great of a deal. A char siu fan hovers around $5 at many places in the neighborhood, which also come with such amenities as seats, no line and free tea. So while I can't knock the food, I'll push back on this being the only way to have this fare in the City. Just because there is a line doesn't mean one has to stand in it.

Great Philly cheesesteaks! Â Better than the ones I've had in Philly actually... Â Great beer selection on tap. Â Free wifi, large tvs for all your sport likings, and pretty good music selection. Â Priced well. Â Great place to chill with your guy friends. Adam the bartender is great with recommendations.

Great spot. One of the best pizza spots in Brooklyn and that is saying a lot. Though, there is a lot more here to offer than just pizza. The sandwiches and the regular restaurant all have amazing food. Not to mention the spumoni. If you're looking to dine in I would highly recommend the chef's table where they give you a little sampling of everything.

I've never been to a Vietnamese sandwich shop before, but I have to say it was excellent. The roast pork sandwich, served warm, which included cilantro and other veggies was really very different, with flavors your just not accustomed to. Really very good.

It's not like the food or drinks were bad here, so I feel a little guilty only giving it two stars, Â but the yelp suggestion for two stars - "meh. I've experienced better" fits the bill perfectly. I had heard the place advertised as a farm to table restaurant, so I was excited to try the food, especially the burger. Walking in, the place had much more of a sports bar feel to it than a farm to table place. Two large TV's. Granted, it's a bar AND restaurant, but I was just confused by my first impression, I guess I was expecting something more warm and homey. The place was clean (although since it just opened a week or so ago, it should be). But I found it to be sterile in both cleanliness and personality/atmosphere. Back patio was big and nice. The burger was good, but nothing to write home about. The employees were all very friendly and polite though. They all seem eager for the place to succeed, so I hope it does, just via patrons that like a more generic sports bar type place than myself.

The Disneyland of Italian food. It is going to be crowded, it is going to be expensive, but if you love all things Italian or want to learn about Italian food this is the place. Lose the atitude, buy a glass of wine to walk around with and gawk with the rest of the tourists.

Nice bar with delicious truffle fries! Me and the fam came here while waiting for our table at The Boil to be ready and we were not disappointed. Our only disappointment was that our table was ready in 10mins instead of 30mins so we couldn't enjoy One Mile House longer. Great chill spot for a group of friends. Definitely recommended.

The tapas at this restaurant are some of the most unique I've ever had. Â My absolute favorite of the evening - fried goat cheese with lavender infused honey. Â I NEVER saw this one coming but it's an unbelievably perfect balancing act - Â crunchy and gooey, salty and sweet. Â The lavender seems like it's coming from left field but absolutely belongs. Â Do not pass up the opportunity to try this one! Â  The brussels sprouts were highly recommended. Â I love brussels so I gave them a try. Â Pretty damn tasty. Â Maybe not the best I've ever had but the apples are an interesting touch that I've never seen before and they do complement the brussels well. The empanadas are great. Â I mean how can you go wrong with tender pork encased in crusty pastry??? Â The dipping sauce is the true standout. Â Fresh and herby but not overpowering. I also though the spaghetti peperoncini was above and beyond your average spaghetti dish although not everyone at the table was as impressed as I was. Â It was my first taste of bottarga and there are some other elements of the sea mixed in. I'd absolutely order it again. I have to say almost everything that I had at this restaurant was a new flavor experience for me and that's not an easy thing to achieve. Â The ambience is outstanding. Â Very cozy and intimate. Â Great for a date or a group of friends. Â Just don't expect a cheap meal.
Not a bad place... Got seated right away, food and drinks came quick... I had better arepas, but would definitely return...

Diana walked up to me, She said I'm all yours tonight* Though they'll probably be on PayPal in store soon enough given their penchant for Taquerias (or as they like to spell it, taCquerias), redeemed an Eat24 PayPal offer here* for a rajas taco and a veggie burrito (to not double up, even though veggie burritos are usually as bad as they sound). Both lived up to the hype, and within crawling distance of Otto's, this makes for one of NY's only respectable taco strips. *The Eat24 search mechanism is so botched, so lucky I just scrolled through the PayPal listings (and not ashamed to say that I find the sheer number of 'Offers' joints that pop up whenever they run an eat24 deal overwhelming and like to just get it out of my way)

I've been here twice and it's been very good both times. It's tasty and fun with a good wine list and yummy sangria. Â Nice place to hangout with friends too. Â The ice cream sandwich was not that good though- pretty gross chocolate chip cookies. Â Skip dessert here.

Ugh had a terrible experience here at a late brunch. Â The service was truly terrible and the bathrooms were disgusting. Â  Food was good, mezze much better than the mains, their homemade pita is exceptional. Â However, I wouldn't recommend this place. Â Ugh, I get annoyed just thinking about it.
I am sold.. besides the wait.. these guys are very friendly... and are not cheap on the sake :) The chicken broth amazing, noodles delicious. Dreams are to be had.

Cafe Habana I love you and I am in NYC and I am coming to get some corn!! Seriously, I have been coming here for years and it's the thing I Â miss the most about not living in NYC anymore. I make sure to make it a stop when I am back and I always order exactly the same thing. Cafe con leche, omlette caribe and the famous grilled corn. YUM. The perfect start to a leisurely day in Soho.
Bartender, short hair one, Â is a prick, if they dont know you he will treat u like crap.BarÃ§a Peyna should have never moved there !!!!!

Although I personally reside in Los Angeles, Bubby's may be my favorite restaurant in the world. Â Located in Tribeca on Hudson and North Moore, the restaurant is a staple for each time I visit the city. Â I always loved the restaurant because my best friend brought me there a few years back and I tasted the best pulled pork sandwich I had ever had in my life. Â But my most recent New York trip solidified my sentiment that is, in fact, the best restaurant on Earth. Â Aside from every single menu item being delectable, all of their food is locally grown! Â All meat is from grass-fed animals! Â All eggs and dairy products are hormone-free! Â They PERSONALLY know all farmers they purchase their food from. Â All fruits and veggies organic and pesticide-free! Â And they sell copies of Michael Pollan's books signed at the front! On top of the top quality food that they have obviously dedicated much time and effort to, the food is out of this world delicious. Â I had the best oatmeal I have ever tasted in my life there: Steel Cut Oatmeal with Sauteed Bananas, Locally Grown Apple Slices, and Dried Cherries and Dried Strawberries. Â It was literally heaven. Â I added a bit of organic maple syrup and melted with joy. Â My mouth is salivating at the mere memory. They serve hot biscuits instead of bread. Â They have GRITS! Â The blueberry pancakes are insanely fluffy. Â The pulled pork sandwich is the best and least greasy on earth. Â Their pies are famous, but I'm always too full to sample! Â One day....I bet they're heaven. If you are ever in New York, or are are resident, this restaurant is a MUST! BONUS: Justin Timberlake and Jessica Biel were sitting literally the next table over when I was there for brunch last Wednesday! Â He is smokin'. Â She had cute shoes and a body to covet. Â Fun celebrity sighting and they obviously have great taste in food!

This place rocks the house. No frills, yet cozy, the interior welcomes you in on cold nights, (like tonight) and they get the food right out to you. I live a few doors down, and wind up eating there more nights than not out of the week. The desserts are off the hook as well; pumpkin pie, apple cobbler and big fat cookies grace the display window where you order. The items that I've had so far have been absolutely delicious. The Philly Cheese Steak on challah bread, the brisket sandwich, and the quesadillas are to die for. All super-fresh ingredients, a great selection of breads, and a nice looking brunch that i have yet to try. This was SORELY needed in this neighborhood with so very much lousy food around. I'm thrilled its there and everyone in the immediate vicinity should give it a shot.

Very well done, especially for brunch service. Food is simple but inventive as evidenced by the one-page menu. The red flannel hash (slightly runny fried egg atop finely diced beets and corned beef hash with side green salad) and chocolate brioche toast were standout items. The charm is in the details of execution (beet mustard for the hash and sea salt sprinkle for the toast). As an alternative for the typical mimosa or bloody mary, the iced tea here is actually worth noting (good balance of mint and citron). Stopped by around 12pm on a Saturday. Was seated in 5 minutes at a shaded patio table. Bonus: service was friendly and efficient. Love!
Came for a late brunch. Food was just OK. Service just OK. Kind of rude. Restaurant was too hot. Dont think I would come back.

Nice? Food is decidedly on the good side, but I'm just not a big fan of the rather high price-to-quantity-of-food ratio this place offers. I do realize it's a tapas joint, but when you're paying $9 for probably four average-size pieces of shrimp in a tiny bowl...meh. The Angry Garlic Shrimp described above was my friend's dish and everyone looked sympathetically at him when it arrived since he's a pretty big guy. He was indeed rather angry after seeing how little food there was. My Turkish beef dumplings were wonderful though! They're definitely not the size dumplings you expect...more like lots of tiny little wontons. The order came with a generous slathering of yogurt sauce that went very well with it, though I do wish the sauce came on the side since it blocked out the taste of the actual dumplings. When I reached the middle of the dish where most of the sauce was, I was basically eating tiny-wonton-textured yogurt. Although it certainly wasn't a lot of food for the price, I felt like the king of the table after seeing how small everyone else's dishes were. Wahoo. Our group also shared the recommended phyllo cheese rolls and they were great too. Again, insubstantial and gone in too few bites, but they're like good, fancy cheese sticks. Also don't use the dipping sauce that comes with them! The rolls taste so much better without. Overall, food is definitely pretty good, but there was just way too little of it; all of us left hungry and like we hadn't eaten at all :( Service is very lovely and attentive.

Met a long lost friend here for dinner. Â The service was great. The Meze platter was great. But the entrees, not so great - got the Iskendar Kabab and the Doner Kabab, and they were uninspired and bland. Â Honestly, I've had better food from a Halal truck. And they should really not let their waitstaff take long, stinky dumps in the only bathroom, when there is a line of customers waiting to go! Haha, that was the classiest part of the experience! To sum up, definitely go for drinks and appetizers, but not for dinner or ambiance or a restroom! Â Agora, which is a block away is a much better bet.

This place is great. The food is awesome, the service is excellent and the ambiance is really cool. Little bit of a wait before you sit down to eat but the bar made up for it :) Â Have and will continue to recommend it.

Loved this place! They have a really cool atmosphere (40s-50s music played at an acceptable volume for talking, and for some reason there's sawdust on the floor but that's cool) and the food is fantastic! I got the turkey burger with cheddar cheese and sauteed onions and it came with fries and a horseradish mayo. It was delicious! We also got mozzarella sticks and potato skins which were both huge and very yummy. The drinks are really well-priced too but it can get expensive with all the add-ons for the burgers being extra (also if you order more than one drink it naturally adds up). We were all more than satisfied though and you could even get a second meal out of it if you weren't ravenous to begin with. :)

I work around the neighborhood and had gotten Gyro's form local pizza place in the neighborhood that are decent. But as soon as i tried Mamagyro I was converted. Not only that the price is incredibly affordable it taste's AMAZING!!!! They don't only gyros, but also great salads as well. I got a side order salad from them the other day and they had this apply tangy dressing on top of a mix green. for $3 and change. pretty good deal . They also have an array of dips that you can get with toasted pita bread's. Dish I recommend. Beef Gyro with the tzatziki sauce. Mama's Spanakopita (its a spinach and feta pie) Chopped Salad (romaine lettuce, chickpeas, beets, red onion, red pepper, radish, shaved celery, tomato, Greek Cheese, with Balsamic Vinaigrette and pita chips) Taramosalata dip. Ever since I found this place I have eaten a Gyro at least once a week.

When I went into the restaurant I've got to admit that I was already feeling a little harassed and when faced with too many options I panicked. I knew I wanted the pork belly but the lad behind the counter wouldn't put that on a salad for me even though I said I didn't eat gluten. Instead I foolishly went for the safe option. The Roasted Chicken 'Chimi' salad. Whilst it was an ok salad with its pestoy chickeny goodness it paled in comparison to the pork belly sandwich that my partner had. His was a sandwich made by the gods. The pork was juicy, succulent and ram jam packed full of flavour. I know it's their prerogative to decline customer 'pickiness' but it kind of left me feeling more than a little cheated.
