Okay, so I honestly have a huge problem with this place. Granted, I've only been a few times, but I was unbelievably disappointed each time. I have several issues with Cafeteria, but they can all somehow be traced back to its ridiculous level of pretension. And, yes, I understand. It's in the heart of Chelsea, a neighborhood that's filled with the martini-lunch crew during the day and is booming with the meatpacking district clubbers in the evening. I get that this place appeals to a certain clientele. Â  But it's not the pretension that bothers me so much as the fact that its so undeserving of it. Pretension when it's deserved is so much less obnoxious. But this place is just...the food really isn't that great, the waitstaff is indifferent at best, and the hostesses couldn't care less if you have a reservation because you're going to be waiting anyway. Then, the bill comes. I ordered a scotch the last time I was there (and it will absolutely be the last time), which was $15. Not that big of a deal, because I ordered a really nice scotch. The problem? They charged $1 for the ICE in the glass. I've heard of places doing this before, so it's not just Cafeteria's problem, but when I asked the waiter about it, he had no idea why. Because, let's face it, it's tap water. They're not paying for it. Charge me $15 for a glass of scotch, fine. You can even charge me $1 for the ice if you don't break it out on the bill because, hey, I'll never know. But if the bill says: $14 Chivas Regal $1 Rocks I'm going to have a huge problem. Folks? Avoid Cafeteria. Avoid it like the plague.

Great experience..food, service, etc. A rarity in the city for having space between tables. I went on a Saturday night and the place was filled with women..appears to be a popular girls night out spot. We had the following (and my ratings).... lentil soup...8/10 apple pear salad...8/10 wheat pizza w/ jersey tomatoes and buffalo mozz...8/10 black sea bass...7/10 (too much sauce as with all fish dishes at JG restaurants) sundae w/ salted caramel ice cream, peanuts, pop corn, whipped cream and chocolate sauce...9/10
MY bf and I try to go there as much as possible. There wings are killers so dedicated. I enjoy there burgers also. They have amazing fresh fries. Everyone should try this place so amazing.

Came here with some friends for a happy hour after work. While they don't have a happy hour special, the food and drinks are relatively cheap so it's not an issue. I had a fish taco, guacamole and chips and a mango margarita. Â Total was about $20 so not bad at all. The fish taco was pretty good and the guacamole was ok. The margarita was tasty. It's It's a great place to hang out with friends because of the outdoor backyard type setup which I really like. This is a regular hang out spot and I'll be back!

I LOVE going to Bubby's. I love how they source their ingredients, using local, organic dairy and produce, are open 24 hours (so dope!) and all that good stuff. Anyone who cares about what they put in their body knows organic food is more expensive. Period. If you're complaining about prices, go to a cheaper Sysco (Monsanto) supplied restaurant. Breakfast is hand downs my favorite meal., good anytime of day. Bubby's does blueberry pancakes PERFECTLY. They're fluffy, and fruity and big and I love them. I wish they had breakfast all day. Whatever, no stars lost for that. The only reason I'm giving Bubby's a 4 is because every time I order bacon it's tough as leather! I ordered their really juicy and delicious burger earlier and destroyed the top of the bun trying to gnaw through the bacon on it. Lame! Overall, food is simple and yum, service is pleasant, atmosphere is awesome-reminds me of a warm countryside joint- and I like what they stand for in terms of supporting local farmers and sourcing organic food. This is a really neat spot to have a meal and I'm a big fan. But, come on guys, address this bacon issue, please!
McSorley's and deep fried bacon; what more does one need? Wait for a table in the back and order the Bistro Burger.

I'm not sure what I can say that the other 3,000+ people haven't already said. Ippudo is outstanding. If you're a beginner, order the Akamaru Modern. After that, start branching out and trying the other delicious ramen noodle soups. Add in the seasoned soft-boiled egg. YUM. I feel lucky that I live in NYC and I can eat here every night if I want to. I heart you Ippudo.
We were here with a large group. The food was very good, but it's the staff that will bring me back. They're friendly and efficient, and they made the evening more enjoyable. Go.

Here I feel like we definitely got a ton of bang for our buck. Down home cuisine, big flavors, big portions, and a cool crowd. We had the honor of speaking with Chef Kingsley who answered all our questions and treated our group like family. When asked, what is your speciality at SoCo; he responded "everything". And boy was he right! We ordered a little of everything -- collard greens, red beans and rice, salmon, chicken and ribs. There was no room left in our stomachs for dessert but we will be back! The cuisine touched our southern hearts. Â  While dining, an elevated, live DJ will immerse you with soulful music and beats to keep the happiness flowing. My friends and I have the soul food discussion on occasion: like who makes the best? What borough dominates in comfort food cuisine? Â We never all agree on the best, but we do agree that soulful food /creole etc. is an area where few succeed. Either the food is too salty, too sweet, or there are too many over processed ingredients. SoCo was none of the above -- the presentation and ingredients are what created lasting memories for us...Lobster, Shrimp and Grits: served with a spicy tomato broth atop country creamy white cheddar grits. Amazing! Blackened Salmon: Two salmon filets with grainy mustard, roasted plantains and green beans. Outta sight!! Where Brooklyn at!?! says Notorious BIG. Uhhhh SoCo, my brutha. lol Get up and throw up your hands in the air for a tasty find.

I've been to CUBA many, many times. It's one of my favorite restaurants in the city and always a go-to when guests are in town. The service is great, atmosphere fun and the drinks and food are INCREDIBLE! Love this place and plan to go again very soon.

They should just rename all their pizzas to stomach cancer. Every pizza was not charred, but straight up burnt. I don't understand what all the hype is, but then again accepting something as being cool and not knowing why is what being a hipster is all about.

Went to Roosevelt Island for the day, and had lunch at the Riverwalk Bar & Grill. Â Absolutely yummy burger and fries! Â Hadn't had one in a while, and the Texas Burger hit the spot. Â Service was great, our waitress was very nice and friendly. Â Will definitely come here again next time I take the tram!

My only experience with the food here is through their outpost at the Brooklyn Flea. I knew not of their history on the Food Network, and if did I might have gone with the dumplings. But instead, I was excited to see New Orleans food at a stall and ordered an oyster po'boy. Now, this sandwich was not a po'boy. Po'boys are made on a particular type of French bread that you either have to make yourself or import from the two companies that make it in NOLA. This was on some sort of teensy, brioche-like roll. And while it was topped with pickled onions and remoulade, it was also not an oyster sandwich--it was catfish. By the time I figured it out, it was too late to return it and get the right order. Also, I saw this place making sandwiches with slices of packaged white bread. That is not okay. Seriously. For any reason. So, whatever you want to call that sandwich, it was good. The fish was juicy, the pickled onions nice, and the remoulade tasty. But it was not what I ordered, and it was smaller than my fist.

Since I've only been here at lunch I'm only here to review the service & the food. The service here is great. They definitely do not rush you, they actually give you ample if not too much time to look over the menu, chat a little before figuring out what you want to order. But not so long that you feel neglected -- the waitress and (who I assume is) the owner are both super nice and are always smiles. Now, the review of what we're all here for...the food: Jalapeno cornbread - 95 cents each, pretty sizable chunks of bread. Just enough sweetness, brushed with honey, baked to a perfection of crunchy crust and moist interior, the bread is pretty tasty! The little flecks of jalapeno give it that unique, savory taste and leaves you with a lasting impression. Pulled pork sandwich + cole slaw (as sandwich topping) - Looks great, big portion, $10.95. The pork is juicy, covered with BBQ sauce, and shredded to just the right size. But when I ordered it the cole slaw tasted a little like dishwasher liquid? But it's one of the most popular entrees there so it was either an off day or I was just imagining things. The pork and BBQ though were very tasty -- zingy, savory, and tender. Hot dog + potato salad - We only got 1 (there is an option of getting 2 hot dogs) for $5.95. It was a good deal, just the right portions for lunchtime. The hot dog itself was fantastic!! Sweet, savory, tender, delicious! The bun was okay and the potato salad was okay. Next time I go I'm definitely ordering 2 hot dogs...assuming I'm hungry enough. Jambalaya + jalapeno cornbread - The jambalaya is pretty packed with stuff though I can't really remember what...it's been a while. It comes on a plate and I doubt you'll be able to finish it all. All I remember is that it was okay. Oyster po'boy + french fries - French fries were nothing special. The oyster po'boy was good though! I would've appreciated it if the other sandwich stuffings were juicier (tomato, red onion) or maybe in bigger slices. But the fried oysters were tasty, you could definitely taste the little buggers, and there was a nice little zing with the dressed lettuce inside the sandwich. $10.95. That's it folks! So all in all both times I've visited it's always been a good experience. The place is pretty small though, maybe accommodating about 30 people on 10 or so tables, so if it's peak munching time then you may have to wait. But so far we haven't waited longer than 5 minutes to get a table. Bon appetit!

Yum! Â From the food to the waitress to the bevvy's -- this is a great find! Â We had brunch, and everything was cooked perfectly. Â The random people we were sitting with at the communal table gave us bites of their food. Â This is the kind of joy Palo Santo evokes. I feel exactly how Jasmine M. does... hesitant to spread the word. Â However, when I saw the place mobbed a few nights ago, I knew the secret was out. Â Enjoy, world!

This place is great, Danny is doin it big! I really went to town here... Â stone crab claws, bib lettuce / bleu cheese / bacon salad, and then the surf and turf which was a hangar steak with a lobster tail. The hangar steak had some sort of horse radish cream sort of sauce over it which i could have done with out, but I like meat to be just that. Meat. The home fries were great tho. The lobster club and the fried chicken looked RIDICULOUS. I'm going back tonight for a bite and a cocktail.

I was expecting to really love Penelope. It's so very quaint and everyone always talks about coming here. When I saw there was no line, I convinced M that he would prefer a nice salad or sandwich over the greasy Chinese meal we were walking toward. I ended up with the hummus and avocado sandwich, and he got the fish and chips. The food was perfectly fine on both accounts. The bread on the sandwich could have been toasted, but the side salad was yum and M's fish was cooked well. Then again, it's a cold sandwich and deep fried fish. Nothing on the menu looked like it would make your heart skip a beat. But-- it's hard to enjoy a meal with your hubby when you're elbow to elbow with very loud, obnoxious women, talking about how they "like New York because it's a grid" and whether you "need a car to live in Brooklyn". This was two separate conversations, by the way. It's also hard to enjoy a meal when your $9 sangria is sugar water with papaya cubes and ice. I still need to have a girly brunch here, but in the meantime I'm not rushing back.

Do you go to restaurants for the food? Me too! So forget that the decor is a little ad hoc (and not in that charming, intentionally mistmatchy way), forget that the layout is a little awkward, and forget that service can be "loose" (though very warm and friendly). The food is really great. The prices are really great. Order things and enjoy, it's actually pretty comfortable in there despite the little things that are off. Go sit in the back, or at the bar counter. Things to get: Order like 2 sides of the housemade chili/tomato hot sauce. They don't offer it on the menu but it's absolutely awesome. This sauce packs heat, beware. NORI TACO SALAD. That thing is so good! It's like a nori tostada: a deep fried nori shell with deliciousness inside. SO good. Put that hot sauce in it. JAPCHE (with spicy pork added). YUM. It's a glass noodle stirfry. Put more hot sauce in that too if you want. With any of the BIBIMBAP make sure you ask for an extra side of the fermented soy bean paste and a side of the red chili paste (the sweet one). And probably add some hot sauce to that too. And then slurp up whatever hot sauce you didn't finish, straight from the bowl. There will be FREE BARLEY TEA to appease the burning, don't worry.

Yes! Â Good old fashioned down home cookin... I get the salmon with peach butter, yams and greens (I think it's called The Honorable Bill Perkins). Â Cornbread is perfect. Â The salmon pairs well with the butter and is absolutely delicious except on the rare occasion that they let it sit too long in the window and it cools off before it gets to you (then it's not so great, but hey...). Â Yams are solid. Â But I dare you to find better collard greens anywhere! Â Sometimes a tad bit salty, but always amazing, with a really distinct flavor. Â I've never had anything like them. Â Lemonade is also homemade and pretty good. Â But yeah, collard greens all day and tomorrow...

I had high expectations for this cart after reading all of the reviews. Â After watching Wicked, I had to make a stop here to pick up some food to eat back at the hotel. Â I got the chicken/lamb rice combo. Â I usually get weirded out by white sauces since I'm not into anything ranch or mayo-like. Â But I had to put some in it in order for it to not taste so dry. Â The hot sauce is hot...I only put a couple of drops and mixed it up to get some kick to it. Â Overall the food was ok, maybe better after a late night of drinking I'm sure. Â I've never eaten at another halal like cart to compare it to so maybe my opinion is not as valid...but it is what it is!

I was really excited to try this place after all the positive yelp reviews, and I got more once I got there and was smelling the food. But it didn't live up to the hype: Black Label Burger - I don't get it! This burger might be slightly better than others but not 5-star worthy! None of the 3 other people I dined were that impressed either. Choux Farcis (stuffed cabbage) - came highly recommended by the waitress but was bland Champignons Poeles (mushrooms) - probably the best part of the meal but even this was a bit salty

Love this place. But don't love the wait. Â If you can suck it up and have a drink elsewhere (I suggest Freemans) while you wait, then you will enjoy yourself. Â The meatballs are great, I always get the beef and chicken ones with parmesan cream sauce. Â The risotto is awesome but the polenta is my absolute favorite thing to go with the meatballs. Â A low key meal that's tasty and affordable? Yeah, I'm hooked. Â And you have ice cream sandwiches? Â Genius!

Great sandwich marred by abysmally slow service. I ordered a beef meatball sandwich with provolone cheese and spicy ragu sauce, which was delivered fairly promptly, but then spent nearly half an hour trying to get my check and pay it. Â The service wasn't mean, just forgetful, and horribly inattentive. Â I was annoyed, but the guy sitting next to me at the bar was furious, since he had told the waiter that he needed to leave in a hurry for an appointment. Â  The sandwich itself was delicious, and a decent size. Â I thought the meatballs were of top quality - moist as well as flavorful, and not too hard (indicating that they don't use much filler). Â However, I probably won't be going back regularly until they get their service under control.

If you like your beef still moooo-ing then this place is for you. Â Steak and burgers I love medium rare with some salt and pepper and this place doesn't disappoint. Â I think the meat was a bit on the bland side but they have plenty of salt shakers lying around. Â There is definitely a bar feel when you get here and you know the burgers gotta be good b/c this is a total guy shop - I know, I went into the bathroom and there's NO paper, NO soap = NO hand washing - definitely a place where everyone knows your name. Â Other than general hygiene the burgers here are pretty good. Â I think their bread could seriously use some work but the meat seems like they got their dirty hands on that correctly. Â I say keep the patties bloody and replace that stale dry bread with something worth eating like cardboard (anything's better than the current bread). Â Service is pretty good though, fast and friendly and I'm sure the drinks are pretty good but I didn't have any. Â I read the fries suck ass here so i don't have anything bad to say about that. Â Overall I would recommend this place but if anyone's eaten at Fuddruckers I still think their burgers taste better.
Delicious Brunch place and love their beet salad too.

We ordered brisket, ribs, Jamaican jerk mac and cheese and baked potatoes. The ribs was so tasty and we didn't even need knives. Brisket was so good. The seasoning was on point and melted in my mouth. But the Jamaican jerk wasn't good at all. They had pineapple on it which I don't know why, it Â was just terrible. It needed to be in the oven for 10 more minutes, more cheese and the jerk chicken needed seasoning just a cup of hot mess.

A raw bar and outdoor seating for brunch make this venue a must try. I'm bummed they removed the brunch biscuits & gravy side dish. It was pork green chile and oh so tasty. Can't go wrong with their Fried Chicken n' Pumpkin Waffles to start your day. Wash it down with a Fig Side Car.

Such a good deal! Â For only $6, I got the "Mix of Chicken & Gyro Over Rice". Â The serving was big enough for my lunch and dinner. Â The white sauce lent a nice creaminess to mix with the ingredients. Â The hot sauce*** is actually pretty spicy (not terribly though) - and I'm used to eating spicy foods. Â It's a good thing this cart isn't posted near my apartment or else I'd be tempted to eat here every day! ***UPDATE: Upon a 2nd visit, I learned the following crucial lesson the hard way: If you see 3 bottles of sauce to choose from, do NOT, for the love of your taste buds, use the dark red sauce from the bottle that looks fullest. Â This motherf*cker is so insanely spicy we were sweating profusely and crying!!! Â And that's saying something for someone who can pop banana peppers like they're candy. Â Trust me, avoid it like the plague unless you only want to taste your tears. Â We had to throw away half of the plate - anything the red sauce had touched - because it was THAT bad. Â There ought to be a skull-and-crossbones disclaimer on that bottle!!!

THE Pork chop. On the Menu its the only entree with "the" in front of it. Why you ask? Because it is THE greatest pork chop ever. Oh man it was soo gooood! ordered it medium, it was cooked perfectly! The soft shell crab appetizer is mouth watering. Loved every bite of it. and they have yummy bellini. at the end, they give you the check in a little black book, where you can write notes and stuff. very cute and romantic cosy place. very busy so you should probably make reservations. The server was so one-on-one and so knowledgable i thought she was the owner. Highly recommend!

Cute little bar on the UES. The beer selection and ambiance is on point. The food and staff could use some improvement - the staff was slow to take orders and had to be called over because they were busy chatting, our food took a while (on a non-crowded Monday night), and we had to get up to ask for utensils as well as napkins after we were finally served. I know they don't have table service, but come on... The food was average (and they make a better burger next door just sayin)

I came for brunch/lunch and will definitely be back again. I've been to Grey Dog's Coffee in Union Square many times before and always loved the food - I was happy to have a consistent experience here at the Chelsea location. I was surprised that it was not too crowded during the weekend at noon, but definitely no complaints on that-- we got to sit at one of the high top tables outside and people watch, so it was perfect. The menu is extensive and it's hard to pick from all the delicious choices! Most recently, I had the Roasted Turkey Brie, Plum Tomato, & Raspberry Mustard sandwich on cranberry walnut bread. They do a great job with creating flavorful and healthy options. The food is very fresh and the portion size is remarkably big. The staff was also really friendly and accommodating, which made the overall experience that much better.

The place really is great, the ambiance and the music is a very catchy place where I'm a group of friends you are bound to have fun. That being said, the reason I give it 3 stars is because of the quality and the service that we received particularly. I couldn't help but notice that people who arrived later than me where served first, and we had to wait almost 45 mins for our food. We where sitting in the bar area and they would ignore us completely, but when the food came it tasted great, but the solemn reason why I do give it 3 stars is for the waiting of the food and the poor service that they gave us. Other than that, its pretty good.

Most of these 5 stars come from their soup dumplings. Â Take the soup dumps out this place, i'd give it a 3 or 4 stars. Â Put them back in, and they'd get 7. Â We've had quite a few of their other dishes which are good, leaning towards very fucking good but their soup dumps are mind altering beyond words. Â At least my limited vocab. Â Mostly Chinese people dining here at any time. Â Anyone who's had their soup dumps and knows of a better place in manhattan, let me know.
If you have not been it is a must, excellent meal and nice Borolo wine with dinner. Make it a point to go there if you have not.
Great vibe friendly staff wonderful covered over backyard. rare to find a spot with this much seating. Brunch was okay dinner selections much more flavorful.

After all the amazing reviews, I came in expecting some of the best ramen of my life. Unfortunately, Chuko isn't such a place. That doesn't mean that it isn't very good - it is, but it isn't the best. I suspect people are loving it's location more than comparing it to great ramen places around the city. I went at 5:30 on a Sunday evening and got the last table before a line started to form outside. My girlfriend and I had the brussel sprouts with miso on top, instead of fish sauce, since she is allergic to fish. I'm not sure how much this may have changed the dish, but it was delicious and I couldn't stop eating them. They were crispy but still well soaked in the nutty, miso topping and the portion was perfect for the both of us to split. I had the kimchi, she had the pork bone ramen. The kimchi was good, just spicy enough, and the poached egg was a nice touch. Thick, well cooked noodles made it a filling dish. Hers was fairly standard, good and salty, but a little bland overall. We split a bottle of the snow sake, as I'd never had unfiltered sake before. It was a nice, novel addition to the meal, and at $20 seemed well priced since we both got about 3-4 fingers of sake out of it. The waiter was attentive about refilling our water, which was appreciated since I was very thirsty that evening, and it's not always easy to keep track with only a few waitstaff and a full place. I'd certainly go back if I was in the area, but I don't think I'd wait more than 20 minutes for a table or go out of my way to go back. I'd rather spend the time I'd wait for a table and venture into Manhattan for some far superior noodles at close to the same price. Also, sort of annoying it's cash only but I suppose it's a nice gesture that they have an ATM in the restaurant, even if the fee is $3.00

I love, love, love Cafe Orlin! It's never so busy that you can't get a table, the food is reasonably priced and it's the BEST place for people watching. (Recently I took some friends from Ohio there for lunch and we saw the son from "War of the Worlds" - so now they think it's a celeb hangout) Service can sometimes be spotty, and there is an obscene percentage of Europeans (Orlin must be in a visit NY tour book) but it's worth it. During the colder months you can't go wrong with the butternut squash soup - creamy but not too sweet... amazing! My lunchtime favorite is the goat cheese salad, but that doesn't keep me from sneaking a few of my companion's fries - also fabulous.

I've celebrated my birthday at Swift two years in a row, and both times have had a great experience. Rob, the manager, is great about reserving tables, and the waitstaff is friendly and efficient. The big "Last Supper" table in the back is a favorite, as are the endless pints of black 'n' tan. I haven't been here for the live music on Tuesdays, but it's on my list. Along with Puck Fair (owned by the same people) this is one of my favorite bars in New York.

I came to Maharlika back in September for someones's birthday with a party of 10. It was Sunday brunch. They had us wait until all of us were there before they seated us. We all got our menus and took our drink orders first. I cannot remember which drink I ordered, but it was good. I had ordered the Eggs Benedict with potatoes and salad. The Eggs Benedict was really good. We were probably in there for about 2 hours. And the place was constantly busy. It is a small Filipino restaurant. What was cool was their t-shirts that the employees were wearing. They said something like "My best friend is Filipino", "My ex is Filipino". LOL. It was awesome. It was also a great experience here. I respect the fact that they are able to handle large parties with care. Not many places can do that and makes it look more hectic than it is.
This place is very delicious. Â It's very small and crowded, which is the only downside, but its otherwise good and very affordable.

The burger is always rated as one of the best in NYC and it has been a while since I ate here. Came on a Friday afternoon and the place was full of European tourists. Guess the inclusion into travel books makes Corner B a must eat at place for Euros but they should just read Yelp instead to find out the best burger places to eat at. Got the Bistro burger and it was $6.75 and the burger itself is much bigger than the bun. The bun was thin and fell apart while eating the burger but the cheese and bacon along with tomato, lettuce and onion make the flavor of the burger something you want to eat. I ordered it medium and it was more or less medium. The meat itself was good but didn't have a tremendous amount of flavor. The fries ($2.50) were good and crunchy but lacked salt, which was easily fixed by me adding it. McSorley's ale for $2.75 a pint was a deal. Overall I remember that the burger used to be better or maybe my tastes have changed. Good burger but not the best in NYC. Cash only.
Quintessential American Italian food prepared with good ingredients. It's a better experience if you go with a regular. Over all a NYC classic .

Staying in NY for the summer and go to this place almost daily with my roommates. Staff there is great and meat portions are huge. Healthy and good price. Thought I lost my sunglasses a couple of days ago and went back to ask if they found them. Steve(Owner) and my man Nick took 20 min out of their day to go through tapes to find out what exactly happened. Nick even followed up later to see if I found them (I left them in a different place). Bottom line: Awesome food, great staff, Nick is awesome and says hi to us every time. Definitely come check it out. Hope it'll be huge and expand to California so I can get it when I'm back at home.

We had one night in Â Manhattan before heading upstate and I picked this place based on its yelp reviews which were dead on. Â Located inside a nice hotel, ambiance is upscale but not stuffy. Â My husband and I ordered the 4 course priix fixe. Â We had the crudo which was fresh and very tasty, it was on their list of specials. Â The lobster salad was light and delicious, had eggplant and pesto sauce, I normally am not a fan of eggplant but Â I am now. Â The trofie Nero is a must order, we savored each Â bite to the last morsel. Â My main was a generous piece of halibut which was perfectly cooked and served with a light drizzle of basil sauce. Â The desserts were good but did not really stand out in comparison to the rest of the meal. Â Would come back if in NYC again .

Wednesday all you can eat mussels is a MUST TRY! They use to have a more extensive mussels menu but the current 4 choices are still very yummy. My favorite is their grand mere (bacon with beer batter), perfect flavor for mussels! It also comes with a free side of fries and beer. LOVE IT!

Come for the BBQ pulled pork sandwich and the chili. They'll change your life and lift your spirits in the worst of days. The burgers look AMAZING, haven't had one yet but it's really impressive to watch how they grill them in front of you.

My favorite neighborhood diner, the food outshines that at similarly-priced restaurants, but the space feels low-key and comfy. Â I love most of their breakfast dishes, though not a huge fan of the omelettes, they lack the distinctive flavors of the huevos pericos (my favorite) or blue cornmeal pancakes. Â Also I found an eggshell in mine once. Â The muffins they bring with the meal (sometimes you need to specially ask for them) are a nice touch. Service is fine, a little variable, and the tables are rather cramped. Â I personally like sitting at the bar.

SO. FREAKING. AMAZING. I came here for the #eatdowntipup following Hurricane Sandy and booooy did I made the right choice. This is the kick you need on a dreary, cold, depressing day because the meal was amazingly tasty and heartwarming. Everything was cooked to perfection (I got the Battenkill River Valley Pork, my friend got the Roasted Chicken, and we shared the Duck Fat Fries), the flavors adjusted to perfection, and I just can't stop raving about it. I really can't. So good. The wait for food was a little long, but I did appreciate them telling us even before we decided what to order the approximate time it took to make the roasted chicken (30min). That cuts down on uncertainty, and it was just courteous, you know? Definitely give this place a try and some love!

Discovered Sugar Freak's unsuspecting Fleur de Lis as I was getting acquainted with my then-new neighborhood in Summer 2011 and my life hasn't been the same since. So far, everything I've had on the menu has been delicious. Seriously - I didn't even knew I liked deviled eggs until I tried theirs which were topped with more deliciousness! Great entrees, haven't tried any drinks yet, but for a sweet tooth like mine, their desserts hit the spot (aka the beignets with bananas foster dipping sauce)! Decor is an adorable mish mosh of casually quaint shabby-country - my favorite are the booth seats and their padded cushions. Pay attention - you might miss their subtle Fleur de Lis "sign" but come hungry, and leave super duper satisfied! They've got me sucked in, and I'm not complaining!

This review is based on Riverpark's Restaurant Week prix fixe menu at $25/person. The location and restaurant are lovely, and the service is quite good. For starters, I had the cured Atlantic salmon, and my husband had the gazpacho. The salmon was satisfactory, but my husband's gazpacho was my favorite bite on our whole NY trip. Rich, flavorful, light. Fantastic. I ordered the prawns, and I was disappointed in the portion. I think I got four prawns; maybe five. The prawns in the light broth were delicious, I just wish there had been more. I was especially left hungry because the bitterness of the Shishito peppers and radish that accompanied the prawns did not pair well with the sweetness of the prawns. The pairing did not work well for me. The menu online lists artisanal cheeses as an option for the dessert course for a $3 supplement; however, the wait staff were unaware of that and said that the restaurant did reserve the right to change the menu, and that they didn't have anything prepared. A bit of a disappointment. The portion size and strangeness of the bitter element in my main course, as well as the unavailability of the cheese plate were missteps. However, the setting is relaxing, and the gazpacho and prawn in broth were two delicious bites. You also can't beat the price. A lovely way to spend your lunch.

3.5 stars. Stix is a decent and healthful sit-down dining addition to a stretch of space that might otherwise have you stopping at Shake Shack and Live Bait - neither of which are bad things in my book, for the record! Â But it's nice to know that there's a slightly more virtuous alternative nearby on E. 23rd Street. We came to Stix after a show at Gramercy Theatre, and the ambiance was nicer than I would have expected for the location - dimly lit and pretty! Â Good food all around, with most dishes made for sharing. Â We had the spread "symposium" platter of hummus, tzatziki, eggplant spread, etc. (I've had better versions of all, but it's hard to go really wrong with this sort of thing), served alongside tasty grilled whole-wheat mini pitas, which were readily refreshed throughout our meal. Â Next came the eponymous stix (still can't really get on board with that word) - we had a mix of chicken, tuna, veggie, and the chef's special (a lamb/beef combo that's slightly unfortunate looking, but we enjoyed it nonetheless). Sides of kale and brussels sprouts were ample and yummy. Â We didn't get a chance to try the greek yogurt bar, but I was certainly intrigued by the idea and would like to go back to try soon. Â  Service was friendly and on top of its game, and the manager greeted us at the end of our meal - always appreciated.

This place was pretty good and a good option if you're looking for Japanese comfort food in the FiDi/Tribeca area. Â The portions were bigger than I expected. Â The buns came in set of two, which was a surprise. Â The short rib one was really good, the meat tender and flavorful. Â I'm normally not a fan of pork belly, but since there were two buns, I ate one and the meat was tender enough, but not melt in your mouth, but still pretty good. Â I eventually discard a slab of the fat because it was a little too much for me. Â The calamari was pretty standard and nothing special. Â Too much of the sauce if you ask me. Â The same goes for Fried Rock Shrimp. Â The portions were big like I mentioned, so I didn't bother eating all the seafood appetizers because they weren't really worth filling up on. Â  I got the Wasabi Shoyu ramen, and it was pretty good. Â It doesn't compare to the ramen at the famous ramen places, but for no wait and no other good ramen place for another what, 20 block radius, I would say it was satisfying. Â They really load up on the ginger and it was a little overwhelming for me, so I personally would ask them to hold off on the ginger next time. Â The noodles were al dente and the soup filling and thick enough. Â I will be back here to try another dishes.

Love this place and in the Summer I generally make an excuse to get to this neighborhood and get myself a Cuban sandwich and some corn. Â The place may have become a victim of its own success with long lines and waits at peak times, but if you can get in early or late you'll be fine. Love cool spots that remain unpretentious and still remain kid-friendly, happy to bring out-of-town visitors here and the communal seating encourages a friendly vibe. Â Nice drinks too!

Another brilliant hole in the wall. It's like they imported this restaurant directly from Germany/Austria. The cute waitress with an accent enriches the experience even more. You walk into Â a small, but cozy place with a bar and a row of seats and tables. When I was ordering I asked for the waitress's recommendation for the best authentic German experience. I ended up getting the Beef Koulash, a lager beer, and splitting a meat appetizer plate with my 2 friends. The food was very delicious, hearty, and appetizing. Nothing too fancy with crazy flavors or whatnot, but rather their style is simple, clean, well made food + a cultural experience. I'm definitely sold on coming back to this place in the future. I really liked my friend's cheese stuffed sausage, salmon, and kale. Very memorable meal. Definitely would keep this as a safe go to spot.

Place is small but packed! Personally I prefer it more than Ippudo plus no long wait! The pork was really tender. Not a big fan of pork but ate a lot of it. The bowl is a little more than 1 person's serving - we shared 2 bowls between the 3 of us. Would go back.
My fav spot in NYC! The drinks are amazing especially the Hot Scandal by far my fav and the plantains with the shredded beef to die for! Def a must when in NYC! Come confess! I did ;)

The best burger ever made, hands down, no competition. Their BURGER alone got this place a Michelin star, so forget everything you know about burgers and come try this one. Â I come here every single time I come to NYC because this is not just the best burger I have ever had, it really is one of the best things I have ever put in my mouth, ever. Â The fries are really good, too. Â The beers are great, and they have a good selection, and while their house brews seem a little expensive (shouldn't house brews be cheaper?) they do have Pork Slap Ale if you're feeling cheap but still want a decent beer. They have some very tasty and very interesting appetizers. Try the deviled egg. Â It sounds plain, but man, it is so damn good. The gnudi was SO GOOD. Â The devils on horseback, OMG delicious. What a cool place. Â Such great food, they definitely have a world-class chef working here, you can tell. Â There are no reservations, so if you don't want to wait for a long time (1-2 hours), come early, and come before Thursday. Â Even then, expect a wait of at least 45 minutes, but you can walk down to Hudson for a drink; I recommend a little tapas bar called Caliu, which has 2 different sangrias, and when we went there we got the BEST little cheese plate for free just by checking in with FourSquare. Â It's totally worth the $6 or whatever it normally costs, it was really, really good. Â There's also a cool little bookstore called BookMarc another block down on the corner of 11th and Bleecker. Â There's lots of other places to check out, too, it's a great little neighborhood to walk around in.

If you prefer cocktails as your drink of choice, this place is for you. Â It's the only place I know where they can make a cocktail taste like a 5-course meal. Â OK, I exaggerate, but seriously, when you drink one of their 19th-century inspired cocktails, there's a taste explosion. Â There's a lot of different flavors that come from all these combinations and infusions. Â Watching the mixologists doing their stuff is a treat. Â The cocktails are available on the 2nd floor, The Parlor. Â Regular drinks like beer and wine are available on the first floor, The Taproom. Â You seriously need to have something to eat if you're going to drink here or you'll fall off your chair. Â I had the beer batter fish and chips, one of the large plates. Â It's a meal that will fill you up and neither the fish nor the fries were greasy. Â The fries are Belgian style, so addictive. Â The decor is like 19th century NY, I think, so there's a great atmosphere. Â But bottom line, you are coming here for the cocktails.

The chicken and waffles are to die for!!!!! I loved the service as well. My waiter, Lawrence was very attentive, polite and such a cool guy. He was also a cutie. This is now my favorite spot!! I give this place 2 thumbs up!

You can't beat a happy hour that lasts til 10pm and has delicious $6 strong lychee martinis! Yum!! I had 3 of them and I was practically stumbling out of the place lol.. You definitely get your money's worth here and it's a cool atmosphere too. As for food, a friend of mine got the ginger chicken wings which were pretty good. I'll definitely be back here!
This place totally rocks! Their ramen is excellent but those pork buns are to die for!!!

Great beer selection. Food selection is interesting and pretty reasonable for this part of town. Haven't had the ribs but they look fantastic. Meatballs are really good. Kind of a loud place, cool if you like that kind of thing but not really my scene.

My boyfriend and I came here after extensive search for oyster specials. Â It is a laid back, small restaurant, with dark and gloomy settings (perhaps the weather had something to do with it since it was rather a gloomy day). Â Anyways, on to the food. Â How can we come to raw bar and not have any oysters? Â So right away we ordered a dz blue points, and devoured them immediately, lol - they didn't even have a chance to breathe! Â They have a Red White Blue special for $8 where you can get 6 oysters and a choice of house wine or selected beer on tap. Â Can't beat that! Â As for our entree I ordered a burger and he ordered the tuna sandwich, both came with very well seasoned fries. Â The wait staff was very friendly and the food came in a timely manner, everything was well seasoned and we were extremely pleased that we came. Â You better believe we are returning for more oysters! Â While we didn't order lobster, the table next to us did and let me tell you, that crustacean was HUGE! Â I may want to try that next time. Â We highly recommend you try this place out if you are looking for some great deals on fresh oysters - YUM!

The food is def very good, and I did enjoy the signature spaghetti (and LOVED the burrata), but not sure it's worth the price tag. Also, the tables are kind of close together for such a pricey restaurant--I get that it's nyc and the space is small, but being able to hear the four girls next to us the entire time during dinner (They got there maybe a few minutes before we did) definitely affected our experience. (Thankfully they weren't ditzy...or else it would have been a lot worse.) That said, the bread basket is amazing!! And followed fellow yelpers advice and got the guava dessert--also divine. If you don't mind paying more for normal food done well, then I'd recommend giving Scarpetta a whirl--def worth trying once.

I just had the danish pancakes and they were amazing. Fluffy with a nice hint of lemon flavor. Â We also ordered sweet potato pancakes and they didn't disappoint either. Â I love that they serve flavored butters on the side. Â We also really enjoyed the service and the ambiance. Â Overall, great brunch place.

LOVE IT! I came here with one of my lady friends in early September for a Saturday brunch. Â We shared the Jambon eggs benedict and one of the Belgian waffles on the specials menu (peaches & strawberries). Â All the food was well prepared and tasty, but a little on the expensive and small side... but as I tell myself, that's NYC! Â Expensive and small. Â After I finished my half of both the eggs benedict and the waffles, I was still left hungry. Service was a little spotty. Â The waiter failed to bring us bread, so I had to ask him for bread at the end of the meal. Â I was still hungry, so bread was something I needed to fill my tummy up. Â When asking for a refill of water, I had to ask multiple waiters, so that got to be annoying since one after the other kept on forgetting until finally one remembered. That's not so good... But overall, the food is good. Â I Â liked it. Â It was tasty, but too bad it was so expensive for the small size you get. Â Next time, I want to try their special promos on weekdays since it would make their food a little more affordable!

Dumplings for a Dollar enough said! This place gets busy toward the end of the day. I get 2 orders of Pork Fried Dumplings with chives, Vegetable pancake and a bottle of Snapple for $5. Me and my girlfriend usually take it to go Â and sit at the park nearby and eat out of a plastic container plate because it gets busy and theirs nowhere to sit inside.

Since this restaurant opened recently, I was really surprised by the hr wait. But in any case, it moved along quickly. The host was really interesting.. I couldn't tell if he was sarcastic or being genuinely nice, or possibly overwhelmed w the amt of diners AS (after Sandy). It seems like every restaurant is serving American (new) cuisine, and this place is no different. It has its Brooklyn spin to it, i.e., oysters, kale. Â That's not to say what they make isn't good, it is. Just as a side note, I think that BK as a whole needs a new culinary revolution.. everywhere you go, it's the same riff on the same on trend local blah blah seasonal ingredients. Or, ramen. Anyway, back to Mayfield. Service was attentive despite the # of diners. Food was satisfying. I had the cuban sandwich w fries. It was sweeter than I'm accustomed to, but it had a good ratio of meat to bread to sides. My friend had the fried oysters. We split the brussel sprouts - the mustard seeds were tasty. The food menu isn't very extensive or complicated but there's plenty of drink options. Overall, thought this place was good. I won't be back to wait on the hr long line though.. but would come back if i wanted a drink plus side of food.

I went to Edi & the Wolf with a group of 7 people and it was really fun! Definitely make a reservation if you're coming with a group though! We were seated in the back "garden" area which looked like a creepy/cool greenhouse. It was much quieter back there though and a great spot for a larger group. The front of the restaurant was a little small, and I'm not always a fan of communal tables but the energy and atmosphere were good. As it got later in the evening, the front section of the restaurant seemed to be a really fun place to hang out and enjoy some drinks. Â  Â  The food that I was able to try was wonderful! I wish I could have tried more of the smaller plates, but I Â certainly didn't leave feeling hungry. My favorite dish there was the spatzle. It had such a great flavor and the portion size was generous. One serving is plenty for about four people to share. For my entree I got the Schlutzkrapfen (goat cheese ravioli) which was excellent. I thought the presentation was a little plain, but the flavors made up for it. I sampled my boyfriend's linguini with the mussels and clams, which was pretty good, but I'm definitely glad I got the ravioli instead. My friends at the table had great things to say about the pork belly and schnitzel, but I didn't get to taste them for myself. Â  Â  Overall, the food was very rich, flavorful, and unique. I left feeling very satisfied and I would definitely go back again if the opportunity arose!

I wasn't really sure what to expect at Paprika; all I knew was that it was not supposed to disappoint :-) After eating there once, I can already tell that it's some place I could eat at again and again. As we were eating, my girlfriend compared it to our favorite restaurant near our apartment (which we eat at very regularly) and we agreed that if we lived in the East Village, this would be a regular spot for us. The salads are delicious but huge; the waitress smartly advised us to share one. Indeed the waitress was full of good recommendations. It's rare to be at a restaurant so busy and get such friendly and quick service as we got at Paprika. The pasta was the real standout here. Each bite tasted better and better. The large portions, served in deep bowls piping-hot felt very homey; this is more of a hearty, home-style Italian than "fancy" Italian. Â Paprika stands out in my mind as a place that makes the sort of Italian food that I cook for myself at home, only much better than I can do it :-) When the bill came I was struck with reverse sticker-shock: $40 for dinner for two? It was then I realized that Paprika must actually be from some sort of alternate universe where fresh pasta grows on trees near fountains that flow with veal ragu. It's a universe I wish I could eat in every night. I would Â have paid an extra 50% for my dinner without question. Â But then I don't think I would have found this place quite as special. Â The value at Paprika is the real deal: You can stuff yourself silly for $20 . . . and then hit up the Dessert truck at Astor Place for only $5 more!

Came here with my friend a few months ago cause of all the yelp reviews. Wasn't an awesome experience but I must say, this place was beautiful and fancy. Good for couples and this place was quite small. The food was alright but was definitely presentable looking. The waiters were attentive cause we were like the only customers there. One con; there's absolutely no service(phone wise) inside the restaurant. And guys... the thai ice tea may be cute and all but it wasn't the greatest. Just giving ya'll a heads up!

Wow! What a great surprise! I've visited a ton of Eastern European countries, but this is much different... actually a combination and variation. Something BURAK-like spinach pie, German-like sausage, Bulgarian-like stew... but also something added to make it different. The spicy sausage was the winner for me, though there were a lot of runner-ups. The best bet is to look at the pictures. If it looks good, it's good! The beer was okay, lightish like Bulgarian beer. (When we were there there was no Serbian beer. We drank the Moldavian, Nicksicko.) Service was good, though if you're still there near closing time, you'll get the sense the staff wants to go home.

My favorite place for authentic Viet sandwich! I've been following them all around for over 10 years! They moved a couple of times and that never stopped me from following them! Â I always order the number 1 which is so satisfying. Their meats are always fresh and great service as well! Coming back for more!!!

Would give this restaurant a ZERO if Yelp offered the option. I used to think this place was cool & chic. UNTIL THE DAY THEY GAVE ME FOOD POISONING!!! I always thought the couscous dish tasted strangely sour at times.. If I listened to my instincts, I wouldn't have ordered it again. They obviously make it in a huge vat early in the week, and then microwave it out in single servings. Had my head stuck in a toilet puking my brains out for 6 hours straight. Will never go here again. Steer clear unless u enjoy playing Russian roulette with your health.

Hey guys, you should be cutting up some muffins, etc. and passing them around outside until "your tired, your poor, Your huddled masses yearning to" eat good food can get in!! Â If you hate waiting for a table I have bad news: your more than likely going to have Â to (both times I went I cooled my heals outside for 45 minutes to an hour) and you should do it too!!
