Â So show up earlier than you want to actually eat, grab a scone and coffee to eat while you wait outside and have a great breakfast. Â Even with the crush of people the hostess and waiter were calm, kind and collected.

does anyone else not fully understand what all the fuss is about? not that I had a bad experience here, everything (food, service, wine) was just fine. our server was nice but not a superstar. the pizza was tasty but the crust is a little chewy for me -- I actually prefer rosco's (big crispy pizzas) down the block.
Amazing woodfired pizza.

We saw all of the reviews and positive feedback, and it wasn't too far from our hotel, so we decided to try it one morning. There's definitely a difference between a Sunday and Monday morning in terms of the line. Sunday morning there was an hour and a half wait! (we consequently went elsewhere) I regret to say I did not order the french toast, apparently the most popular thing on the menu. The eggs and toast were just fine, and nothing too special about them. But that's what were going for. The place itself was so cozy, with a large dining area. They had a lot of baked goods that looked delicious. Next time I'm there, I'll be getting the French Toast!

I stopped in this afternoon with a friend to grab a late lunch and a beer while in the neighborhood and I'm an instant addict. I ordered the sashimi roll and the soft shell crab bun and both were a delicious explosion of flavors. Being a big dipper, I especially loved the spicy mayo and wasabi mayo dipping sauces with my meal. I also used them with my friend's sweet potato fries which I think I ate half of (half being an understatement, sorry)... they're a must. The ingredients are very fresh and everything is put together in a way that feels cared-for. Â  Friendly service, a pretty interior and cool music add to the experience. My only complaint is that I don't work nearby, because I know I'm going to wake up wanting that soft shell crab bun. Definitely looking forward to trying out more of the menu next time I'm in the area.

Very fresh, tasty pizza. The place gets crowded early but it's worth the wait. The pizza is not too thick, not too thin and the crust is soft and chewy. The sauce is flavorful yet not overpowering, the cheese is fresh buffalo mozzarella. Wine is very reasonably priced. The staff is attentive and chat in Italian. Yes, the pizza is a bit pricey but the fresh ingredients totally justify the price.

We have been to Emporio twice, but my second visit prompted this review. Â The food there was quite good on both occasions, but the awful service we experienced on the second visit was enough to take this place off the top of my list. Â  We had a reservation and had received a confirmation call that afternoon, but when we showed up, they told us they did not have our reservation. They told us they could seat us up front near the bar, but it was incredibly noisy at that point and we asked if they had any tables in the back. Â The hostess said no immediately without even checking. Â That should have been our cue to go. Â Still we sat up front and I got up to use the restroom within a minute which is near the back of the restaurant where i saw quite a few empty tables. Â Grrrr. Â  We stayed and ordered but our waitress could not have seemed less interested in us the whole time. Â When our pasta came out we asked for some extra cheese and she literally rolled her eyes before coming back and sprinkling just a tiny bit more on it and walking away without even asking if that was enough. Â I'm sorry, but shouldn't I be entitled to eat my meal the way I like it? Â  Emporio is a cute spot with good food but only go there if you feel like being treated like sh*t.

I gotta admit, this is my least favorite Gyu-kaku locating in NYC. Â The waiters are a bit slow with responding and I had to like wave a few times for the waiter to finally get my check especially when there are only three tables of customers. Â There aren't as many options in the Happy Hour menu as the other locations. Â They don't even have my favorite dish--the tuna crunch?!?! Other than that, the food tastes pretty much the same as the other locations.

So this place has been on my list for awhile now. I love these quaint, candle lit locavore havens in the EV (the beagle, terroir, upstate, the redhead); this one did not disappoint. Like most restaurants like this in the EV, no reservation policy, so we knew we'd have to get lucky at 830 PM on a Friday night. Â we did! a couple tables for two were available. we got: Apps: Fried green tomatoes (only 2!? they came with crab and were large but still..TWO slices?) so yummy, wish there were more. flatbread: amazingly yummy and for $2 you get a BIG portion. It's more like a foccacia.; soft and thick and springy. Â  pickled eggs: such a weird concept but really good. dinner: KALE SALAD: really great, fresh and tasty. my date got chicken with gnocchi. he said it was great. we got another order of the bread and added a side of roasted corn. This corn was so great as well and a large portion for a 'side' the menu is big enough so I'd love to go back to try a few of the other dishes. not a ton of Vegetarian Entrees (maybe one?) but the awesome apps, sides, salads/soups make it easy to TRY a lot and leave satiated. Bill was about $100 for two and we got two drinks a piece. a nice night out.

So far the worst food experience in NYC. Service was so terrible and rude that we couldn't even enjoy meal. Waitress literally throw receipt on the table. My friends were visiting NYC and they want try restaurant in chinatown and Big Wong was our worst mistake! Food is ok but this all situation was ridiculous that we ate our appetizers and took everything else out!

Very cool spot and even cooler if you are into whiskey and rye The interior is very small and intimate and dimly lit, which makes it a perfect date spot. The staff is friendly and very helpful in explaining various drinks on the menu We personally love to get the pickled vegetable platter with our drinks. Â The platter is delicious and has a bunch of the usual and unusual pickled suspects like lotus root and mushrooms The drinks here are great and they have a few nice mixed drinks making use of rye and whisky as well as some wines. Definetly a worthwhile spot, especially for a date or a drink with one or two friends

4.5 stars rounded to 5 I've been hearing such amazing things about this restaurant from all my friends and fellow yelpers that I knew I just had to go try it out. Reservations can be annoying to schedule since it is by email (heather@traifny.com), and you end up playing a bit of email tag back and forth, but we were able to snag a table for 4 at 7:30pm on a Friday night easily just two weeks before. We began the night with some delicious cocktails (the Apple Cobbler tastes exactly like Apple Cobbler!) while we perused the menu. If it's your first time at the restaurant, the list of tapas like plates can be quite daunting. We decided to put ourselves in the capable hands of the chef and go with the Chef's Tasting ($45/pp), and I'm glad we did! There were no bad eggs all night. Every dish that we had was at least a solid 4 out of 5 stars and there were some that were simply superb and knocked the ball out of the park. We especially enjoyed the hampshire pork belly, burrata cheese, bone marrow with grilled sardines, and the panna cotta. My only problem with the service was the pace of the meal. Each plate came out quickly and sometimes, several plates all at once. At one point we had so much food on our table that we couldn't even fit any more plates! I understand they don't want you to linger given how popular the place is, but -0.5 because I just don't like the feeling of constantly being rushed throughout the meal. Can't wait to check out Xixa next door! **TIP: Try to go with at least a party of 4 and get the Chef's Tasting for $45/pp. You won't be able to try as many items if it's just 2 in your party, and they will charge you a surplus for the tasting.

Two words - Super awesome Not sure how they do it, was there this week and the place was packed to the gills at 2 PM, food was once again outstanding - don't know how they pump out such high quality with he amount of volume they do. Staff was nice, bread is awesome too. I walked out in a euphorious food coma Another great point is he reasonable prices. Make sure you try the mozzarella tomato salad - the tomatoes are like candy

if you have a gluten allergy, you need to go here! the owner is really nice and makes sure you are taken care of. the food was fantastic and being able to eat a real italian dinner with a gluten allergy was awesome!!!

I've spent a lot of time in Tokyo and this place definitely makes me feel like I'm back! Â Excellent ramen - but the real star of the show is the Chicken Bun! Â Service is friendly and excellent - but expect a wait - people are willing to stand around an hour or more for a reason! My only complaint is that they have been frequently running out of menu items early in the day - don't deprive me of those aforementioned Chicken Buns Ippudo! Bonus points for the fun music.

Whether it's pouring or blizzarding or hot as heck ... you're sure to find a line. Mixed platter + extra white sauce + just the right amount of hot sauce = perfection. Only first-timers drizzle on the hot sauce thinking they can handle it. But like the thousands of reviews before me, THIS AIN'T YOUR ORDINARY HOT SAUCE. Take it easy or else you'll suffer the next morning... Whatever you're doing guys, keep it up! Will be back here every time I visit!

Great rustic atmosphere, great servers and amazing food and cocktails. The owner pays a lot of attention to detail in this place . Good place for dinner, breakfast, brunch, lunch or to grab a drink with a friend.

I LOVE Becco and I don't think I know anyone who has been here and had an unpleasant experience, either. Â I can't even count how many times I have been here, but I have never been disappointed. Â I've had their fish, their chicken, their lamb chops, and of course the imfamous all you can eat pasta. Â You definitely need to make a reservation because this place gets beyond packed, especially before show time.

First time I tried this place, and I won't bother to return. In summary: Basically the worst pad thai I have ever had (and I have eaten it a lot). Ingredients are obviously not fresh. We went around 6pm when it was fairly quiet and people were arriving for dinner. I had the summer rolls; they were bland and refrigerator-cold, and very obviously they had not been made fresh. My pad thai was also bland, and had a very distinct burnt taste, which turned out to be from the eggs, which had lots of black, charcoaly bits; after picking out lots of burned bits of egg, I decided there was no egg left, and the dish tasted burnt, so I told the waiter I would not pay for it. He merely took my plate away without saying nothing, but to their credit he did remove it from the check. My friend's vegetable pad thai was very bland -- the tamarind sauce was hardly present, with none of the classic tartness at all -- and for some reason it was served with broccoli. I observed some other dishes being served to other people, and they did not look particularly inviting. Lastly, while the place looks decent inside, the back garden looks like a cheap tourist destination. Very haphazardly decorated with plastic furniture, and they haven't even bothered to remove the price tags from their plants, which are still in their black plastic pots.

Best Venezuelan restaurant in NYC - although I have never had Venezuelan before. Meals are large so don't over order unless you HUNGEE Get the appetizer sampler. Solid mix to sample from. La Bandeja Dona Barbara. Get this! Â Damn good. Three meats (crispy and cooked to perfection), avocado, and other yummy veggies I don't know about. Small place but under the radar with a solid gay waiter with a great accent.

The wait is a little long but I totally think its worth it. The food is AMAZING! I love the tacos and they make a great flan. One time on a crowded day we were waiting for a seat and someone cut in front of us and stole our seats. The host saw and asked the people to move. Overall, really great place and I can't wait to go back.

This place has gorgeous interior with huge stained glass and nice pictures. Waitress and hostess were cute too, a big plus. ;-) 3 of us were here on Memorial weekend Saturday to start the second day of partying around 1 PM. The place understandably was empty. The hostes tried to seat us in a tiny 4 person table. When we asked if we could be seated at a bigger 6 person table, she made a big deal out of it saying we might have to give up the seat if big party comes in and that we have to order lot of stuff. It was ridiculous considering that the place had 4 customers at the time and it was 1 PM on Saturday. But she was very cute, so all is forgiven. We started with drinks and ordered Mac with Cheese and 2 steak and egg. I am very picky about cooking the meat to the right temperature. You should know that by now if you were reading my reviews. My friend ordered it medium and medium rare for me. Good news first. Drinks were good. We ordered some of their specialty drinks, mimosa, vodka martinis, McAllans, and few other drinks. I am happy to report that they were all good. Waitress was friendly and quick. We were in a goofy & happy mood. She was ready for our jokes and conversation. A+ for her. Now the bad news. My steak was overcooked. The biggest sin in my book. You can't even call it a steak, rather a small strip of beef. You really have to be careful when cooking such a thin piece of meat. The grill cook obviously wasn't paying attention. It was cooked all the way through, well-done in anyone's definition. They would get 1 star soley based on the little amount of food we ordered. But the drinks and friendly waitress saved this place from getting one star.

My boyfriend googled "best carbonara" and this place came up. And it was pretty good. It is much less creamy and more peppery than some other versions of the classic dish, but just as good. The meat was crunch and flavorful. I got the ricotta gnocchi with sausage and fennel. It was very very good. The texture of the gnocchi was fine and wonderful, the sausage gave it a fantastic flavor. As for dessert -- have to go with the tartufo! Hazelnut gelato with a hard chocolate shell atop a dark chocolate sauce. No words for how good this is. Â This was my first time at Lupa, and it won't be my last.

This place was popular even before the big banh mi bang. Â  The number one sandwich is the best, sliced meats with crunchy pickled radish and a fresh sprig of cilantro slathered with a creamy spread. Â Please, only come here for the sandwiches. If you search for soul soothing pho, venture elsewhere. Â I find theirs to be a tad sour and altogether unsatisfying. Â  It's a very small place with about 5 tables but I guess dine-in is not their strong point since I never had to wait for a seat. Â Warning, not good for big groups!
good beer selection could be faster in bar service it look everyone knows everyone have not yet tryed the food soon.
If you go on weekend (fri-sun) expect a wait. I come to peaches to get my fried chicken fix. Great portion, spicy & juicy fried chicken is the best!

they serve lots of food, I could enjoy a meal and full dessert. I love sweets and I like the fact that they have a number of different sweet. The space in the back is little pretty, and the reason for 5 stars. Food may be on average or little better, but that space is unique thing that you need to enjoy. I had pizza, reasonable price and taste was good. cappuchino also good!
Super restau Ã  NY, la dÃ©co est top, la nourriture est excellente et les prix raisonnables ! Que demande le peuple !

We had a wonderful family dinner at Benito One - my parents were in town and were so tired from doing all the touristy things. This place looked inviting and non-pretentious, and boy were we ever welcomed when we came in. Â The staff were so kind and attentive, and seemed genuinely interested in getting to know us. The pasta was fantastic, and the wine went down a little too easy. Â All in all, it was a completely comfortable experience.
This place was amazing, my husband brought me here, it was very warm and cozy inside. It was well decorated, I loved the pictures. definitely recomend this place to anyone!

I love their falafel sandwiches, and seriously how does that guy make and wrap the sandwiches so fast??? The falafel sandwiches are only $2, and tastier than others I have had. The only downside is, it is SO CRAMPED in there, and people will fight you for a seat.
one of my fav places in ny

While in the city during the polar vortex we seeked out new places to eat. Â We found this place strictly on Yelp reviews. Â The photos of their food looked great so we made reservations for dinner. Â This style of restaurant is what I really enjoy. Small maybe 10 tables max, it's very small and intimate. Â  So the reviews state that the Brindle Room had a hamburger to die for. Â As much as I avoid burgers when traveling I thought I would change it up a bit. Â All of the burger reviews I saw stated it was the best, most tasteful etc. Â So we ordered some appetizers and wine and of course I ordered my burger. Â When my food came out and I saw this burger I was very deflated at the visual. Â It was an average portion size, but I should be to blame for expecting a 2 lbs burger that Adam Richman would eat. After my first bite, I vow to never profile food again. Â I don't know what they do to but they do it great. Â It was one of the best burgers I have ever eaten. Â The burger was not listed on the menu as past reviews stated though the staff did mention they had it before I had to ask about it. Â  I finally had a burger in my many holidays to NYC and it was a great one. Â Try it. Â You'll like it!

This place is really as good as it gets in terms of flavor and value. Â The lamb and chicken are both so well seasoned and tender. Â You can eat them with or without the sauce because they are so good by themselves. Â Combo plate comes with salad, rice and pita. Â This is absolutely one of the best meals for $5! Â Satisfies your taste buds, fills your stomach, and doesn't empty your wallet.

I found this place when I googled best crabcakes in NYC. Â CBS News put out a list in August 2011 that included 9 restaurants, Cafe Triskell was the only one listed in Queens. Â Although I am a die hard Manhattan girl! After looking at the reviews for the places in Manhattan, such as Jean George, Four Seasons, and Le Gigot to name a few, I found Cafe Triskell to be the only one to have 5 stars and consistent reviews. Â After dining there last night, I am a Cafe Triskell fan !! Â The owner is friendly, the wine list was great (red), and apple cider! Â The crab cakes were melt in your mouth. Â The crepes were very authentic (European). Â The chocolate with toasted almonds and the lemon sugar were totally worth my drive to Queens! Â I have too many good things to say and not enough time. Â I have plans to return next weekend!
I'm 100% polish and we go here whenever in Greenpoint. Authentic, homemade polish food!! The polish platter is soo good and soo cheap! The white borscht (zurek) is fantastic! Tiny but great.
very good. Â  Just too expensive.
I got the roti canai and calamari for takeout- A+ for both. I would be happy to eat here multiple times/week. Plus, the owner is the sweetest! Love this place.

The Dan Dan noodles are definitely worth the hype. The chicken wings will make you cry but it's so worth it. Favourite new place... I end up here at least once a month and it doesn't look like I'll be stopping anytime soon.

I was in the mood for a great pizza today and I had Luzzos bookmarked for a loooong time. I walk in today to an empty restaurant. This place has an old school vibe. It really reminds me of Johns Pizza in the village but without the writing on the booths and walls. I've been hearing about this pizza style from Naples so I order a small pizza with Anchovies and a glass of Montepulciano d'Abruzzo which is my favorite pizza wine. Pizza comes out really quick and I noticed the dough is light and not too much charr for a coal oven pizza. One bite and I was hooked. Creamy dreamy fresh mozzarella with sweet sauce. Just spot on. "This" is the place if you want to impress out of towners looking for real NY Style pizza. If your on the West side, then it has to be Co. If you want to meet in the middle, Artichoke. Can you tell that I love NY Pizza? :)

I came in for pick up on the way home from a long car ride. I gave my order to the lady and she put it in. In the meantime, I sat overlooking the pizza preparation area. I must admit the pizza looked and smelled great. Next to me was a woman and her son who were anxious for pizza, having waited already more than 20 minutes and saw several people served before them who arrived after. These people eventually got their pizza, but it still gave me some concern. After 20 minutes I went to the cashier and asked how much longer it would take for mine to be done. She looked up my order and apparently it was "forgotten" even though it was in the system, and said it would be another 20 minutes. She didn't offer anything complementary, and didn't even seem to be offering to put my pizza in next, as they shouldn't take 20 minutes to cook. I asked for my money back and walked out, and relayed the disappointment to the members waiting in the car. 20 minutes and nothing to show for it....can't give more than a 1 for that service.

3.5 stars: Good, but not all it was hyped up to be. This place was in my bookmarks for quite some time. Â Being from San Francisco, I love eating Filipino breakfast. Â So, I've been trying to find a good place to get silogs. Â  The day my friends and I were here, they were wrapping up a food network/cooking channel show/interview. Â Therefore, it was still pretty hectic and crowded. Â (Yes, that was a while ago. Â I'm guilty for having this sit in my drafts for so long.) Having read a few reviews, we decided to get the chicken and waffles, sigsig, and tosilog. Â Everything was good, but not as great as the reviewer made it out to be. Â I do have to give them credit for creativity on the chicken & waffles though. Â I've never had ube waffles. Since there aren't many Filipino restaurant to choose from, I would probably return. Â If you're in Brooklyn, Umi Nom also serves silogs during lunch time, just saying. yelp.com/biz/umi-nom-broâ€¦

Bronte Burger is the Best NYC Burger to land on Ciabatta bread! After Yelp-searching "burger", "New York, NY", Ruby's caught my eyes. I've been on a burger devourment streak. Â Along with marathon training comes the desire to repair damaged protein and cravings for meat (sorry "Earthlings"!). My Detroit Tigers ballcap wearing buddy and I met up at Aussie-themed Ruby's last night on a mission to experience this much-talked about Bronte Burger first hand, or more like first mouth! We started up with Australian bottled brews (sorry folks, no draft beers here). Â I had an amber James Boag (good), and my friend had a Lucky's. Â Lucky's came in the coolest beer bottle in the shape of a fat lucky Buddha! Â  See picture: 1.bp.blogspot.com/_zqFoqâ€¦ The Bronte Burger (premium ground beef with herbs and onions mixed into the patty, tomato, greens, swiss cheese, mayo, and a sweet chili spread) arrived with a nice salad. Â For $11, this is a good deal. Â The burger itself is thin, but moist and the meat is of good grade. Â The toasted Ciabatta and fixings made this burger delicious! Â The meat itself is not a hearty juicy slab of beef, but it is fitting for the Ciabatta and doesn't leave you with greasy hands. Â The sweet chili spread gave the burger a sweet taste, which will surprise you at first, but actually matches well. The next time I go, I am going to order a Whaleys Burger, which comes with a pineapple slice, beets, tomato, greens, and a fried egg! Â Weird combo, but after the tasty Bronte, I trust Ruby's. Ruby's is VERY easy to walk past. Â The space is small, though they make efficient use of it. Â Just go to the bathroom and you'll see. Â On your way, you'll catch a full view of the tiny kitchen and their panini griller. Seating is very limited, so I do not recommend going in goings. Â Two is a good number, 4 might be a stretch, but anything above that... good luck! Â I'm not sure if Ruby's takes reservations. Â Also, it's cash only.

Loved the wings, and the cheesecake is New York good. I won't go into detail because you have heard it before. I loved the service at the bar, they were all nice and eager to make our experience great.
the food is totally awesome, the service is great and workers so very friendly. high recommend it.

Had Dos Toros for dinner last night. It was raining out, and it was dinner, so no line. we were able to get seats, though other people who came after us were waiting. we split: Burrito with chicken and guac (which I loved, my wife thought it was blah) Quesadilla with steak and guac (which my wife loved, I thought it was good) chips with guac Our fault for ordering the chips with guac, i would have been happier with salsa. I thought the food was very good and love the idea of the greenware.

Came here for their oyster special and ended up with the oyster special ($8 for 1/2 dz including your choice of white/red wine or beer), clam special, AND their wasabi Salmon entree. Â All were VERY good, and the service was wonderful, the atmosphere romantic but relaxed. Â Definitely coming back soon, hopefully next time they'll have their sea urchins available too!

What does one do when he has jury duty downtown for lunch? Â Well, you can go to your favorite Chinese spot, or you can really take advantage and go somewhere that usually has a ridiculous wait at night or on weekends. Â Joe's Shanghai definitely fulfills the latter so off I went. Â  No wait for a table of one, sweet. Â I went with the standard order of soup dumplings and scallion pancakes, figured I'd keep it simple. Â Five minutes later the food finally appears...making this a good spot if they cut your lunch break at jury duty, though does that ever happen? Anyway, soup dumplings were pretty standard, nothing that stood out among other places in Chinatown. Â The scallion pancakes though? Â They were top notch, can't think of a better spot in Chinatown off of the top of my head, they felt like they were double fried for double the yumminess (and probably double the fat).
Awesome guys, Anthony and Maurice, running the place and I can use my debit card without feeling weird about it. Also they have goat cheese in their sandwiches. The best possible cheese.

Oh good god! This was heaven explodin in my mouth! Those who are fond of fried chicken, this is THE place to go! I had their Ludacris and my friend had President Barack obama. Yes their dishes have awesome names! Ludacris is chicken wings with two sides and Barack Obama is chicken with two sides. For choice of sides I had coleslaw and french fries. French fries: perfectly cooked and fried. Soft on the inside, crunch on the outside. They were not too long. Perfect cut as well. Coleslaw: I am not a fan of anything spicy, and have never dreamt of coleslaw spicy.Their coleslaw is spicy and IS good. Chicken Wings: I tried it and it literally exploded in my mouth. Perfectly cooked chicken, thin but crunchy crust on the top. This is not your KFC. This is a five star deserving chicken. With the ranch as my dip,it was H-E-A-V-E-N !:-) They get a star knocked off because of thiercustomer service. We had to wait a while, and then i had to try to get the attention of a waitress. it was annoying. Same when it came to paying the bill. my friend had to get up and give it to them. Otherwise the estabslishment is a five star. Also, Â gets bonus point in my books for cleanliness. For a small place in East Harlem, this place is very clean, and the decor is cute. P.S. They seem to have good breakfast menu as well. Will certainly come back for that.

My two cents: -COME EARLY (before 6:30pm) -come with 4 people or less -ask that your entree be easy on sodium My girlfriends and I came at 6:15 on a Wednesday night and we were glad to have come early. The seats started to fill up fast. By 7:00, this place was jam packed. Â It was impossible to hear my friend seating two seats away from me. I advise not to go here during peak hours, or be prepared to take turns yelling across the table. The interior here is just beauuitful. Â It was decorated in detail with christmas ornaments and lighting and had the cozy, I'm-indoors-next-to-a-fireplace-on-a-christmas-day atmosphere to it. Â Very family-style. Â Perfect for a girls get-together on a cold winter evening. Â  My only reservation was that the Tagliolini Ai Frutti Di Mare pasta was TOO SALTY- a problem I have with many restaurants. Â At first, I assumed it was just my sensitive tastebuds, but my friend who also got the same entree also said hers was on a sodium overload. Â Also, my plate had the worst pasta-to-seafood ratio. Â I had so much seafood leftover by the end of the meal. Â It also did not help that there was no pasta leftover to pacify the sodium imbalance. Â I also tried my friend's lasagna, and it wasn't the "best" lasagna I've ever had, as I have read in the Yelp reviews. Despite the negatives, I still had a good dinning experience here because of its cute interior decor and good company. Â The food just tasted like salt.

What a terrific maitre'd!!! Â I felt so pampered! Â haha I wish they were all like that! Â Good service and ambiance. Â So-so brunch fare. Â Skip it and maybe try dinner instead. Narcissa is adjoined to The Standard Hotel and conveniently located near Cooper Square, so you'll find mostly tourists and some locals here. Ambiance (daytime): -Lighting: Good with plenty of filtered sunshine streaming in, especially in the dining area with the open kitchen. Â  -Seating: Spacious and comfortable for parties greater than 2, otherwise you'll most likely be in the cramped two-top section. Â Outdoor seating also available in a small garden (closed for winter). -Decor: Although I appreciate the neutral color scheme, when combined with the layout and booths during the daytime, it is very reminiscent of an IHOP... Food: -French Toast Bites: Overhyped and slightly undercooked. Â Tasted like Cinnamon Toast Crunch, but without any crisped edges - so pretty soft and boring throughout. Â It came with maple syrup and lemon curd butter, the latter of which proved to be too saccharine - even for me. -Eggs Benedict: My friend liked it, though said it was nothing special. -Brunch Cocktails: Good selection. Â Wish I had tried the Tangerine Dream! Â It sounded delicious... Coat check available. Â Mutliple clean, spacious single-stall BRs located downstairs, just like the ones you'd find at any Standard hotel/club.

I really enjoyed my lunch at Ootoya. I haven't gone for dinner, but the portions for lunch are immense. Maybe even a bit too heavy. I know the ambiance is different than the Ootoya chain in Japan, but it was kind of nice. Very serene and contemporary. I ordered the Kimchi Nabe, which came with rice, pickled vegetables, miso soup, and egg custard. SO MUCH FOOD. Flavors were great. Egg custard was delicately flavored with a hint of salt and felt light on the tongue. The Buta Kimchi Nabe was an explosion of flavor with kimchee, pork, tofu, egg, and chives. I can't wait to go back. I want to try everything.

Yummmm, Pinto is so good! Â It's definitely a little hidden and VERY tiny but the food is amazing and really reasonably priced. Â We got the dumplings as an appetizer, and I got the crab fried rice in young coconut for an entree. Â It was so delicious, and the presentation was beautiful. Bottles of wine are only $28 and the one we chose was quite tasty!

Very nice spot~great huge cheese plate with lots of salad and fruit. A total meal in itself. Bread was soft, hot and yummy with the fresh butter. Wine list was very good. Service was friendly, fast and pleasant. I was there at a slow time, so I didnt go through a long wait, but I could see how quickly it might fill up. Really wanted to try a crepe for dessert, but was just too full~will try next time. All in all , a lovely spot.

Good fast lunch in midtown. The line can be long, but moves quickly. Don't plan to sit, there's never room and the rolls travel well. Go eat in Bryant Park. The mixed veggie roll and chicken tikka are both really good. Good level of spice (for NYC, which I generally find a little bland). They'll make it spicier if you ask. Get two rolls (three if you're a big eater). I eat very small portions and usually want more than one roll to fill me up. It's about $5/roll.

If you were to judge Room Service by first appearances, it would be that trendy little Thai place you love to hate: sure, it might be pretty, with stylishly-dressed staff and a fancy cocktail menu-- but the food is shit and the prices are extortion. Fortunately, Room Service provides all of the glitz and glamor of a sceney place without the prices you'd expect. While the food is far from remarkable, it's generally all tasty and you will be shocked at how cheap everything is ($3-5 for appetizers, entrees starting at $6/7). The long bar and larger area in the back makes it seem perfect for a large group or for a girl's night out, and the bartenders and host/ess are friendly. I wouldn't mind returning, especially for a quick dinner with the girls. Room Service has this gothic/disco feel to it-- lots of black, dark colors, and mirrors, along with a giant chandelier, ghost chairs, and other ornate furniture with blaring dance music. This could all easily seem overdone and tacky but, because the prices are so reasonable, the experience ends up feeling like a steal. Come when you are looking for a loud, festive dinner. All the atmosphere/environment (and, I warn you, noise) of hipper neighborhoods without the cost.

It would've been a perfect five star rating if the place wasn't stifling hot. Came here after the lunch rush was over and got seated immediately. I ordered the katsu lunch special and my mom tried this chicken dish (I forgot the name). She said that she wished she ordered a katsu dish as well since her lunch was just okay. The katsu was moist and crispy - so good!! I love that the salad portion is huge and the dressing is on the table so you can drench it to your hearts desire like I do! Oh and the best part, the tonkatsu sauce is in this big jar and you can scoop all the sauce you want. I find that most Japanese restaurants that I go to don't give you enough tonkatsu sauce and I always have to ask for extra. Can't wait to go back!!!

If you are from Southern California, this place will change the way you view NYC Mexican food. Come here for your fix - awesome decor, great staff, strong drinks. They have legit refried beans that will make you think of Roberto's back home. Let's make this post search friendly for the Socal kids: San Diego, Los Angeles, California
Great craft beer selection. Love the atmosphere. Food is excellent, haven't had a bad meal yet.

Little Owl is a cute little space with all-American food done fairly well. Â We got the requisite sliders (I found these so-so, to be honest), the cavatelli (I liked this a lot, my husband thought it was eh), the lamb shank and the chicken (both good). Â  The thing is, we'd been to Red Cat recently and I felt they did very similar food but just slightly better. Â Anyway, with the difficulty in getting a Little Owl reservation, it's doubtful we'll be back to soon anyway, but worth a shot if you can get in.

AMAZING! Â This is just one of many words I would use to describe this fine restaurant. Â This place was a last minute recommendation by a friend and it did not disappoint. Â The dÃ©cor and ambience was very nice. Â I had called ahead for a lunch reservation and once we arrived we were promptly seated. Â We ordered the following appetizers: Â Jalapeno Hommus, Lamb Meatballs, & Garlic/Cilantro Shrimp. Â Each one of these dishes was scrumptious and perfectly flavored. Â We decided to order from the price fix lunch menu which includes once side and one main entrÃ©e. Â I am a huge lamb fan and was excited that Ilili had such a variety of dishes with lamb. Â After going back and forth between what to order I decided on the Braised Lamb Shank sandwich. Â I would not regret this choice! Â The lamb was perfectly cooked and flavored. Adorable, delicious, and friendly! I would give it 5 stars if my friend was as impressed with it as I was. Â Came in for brunch, sat at the window and watched the world go by while sipping mimosas and munching on yum food. Â A great way to spend a Saturday if you ask me!
Beautiful set up. Loved the BLT.. Try the fried Oreo (guilty pleasure)!!

Great tasting lunch place. If you are looking for very spicy Indian food, however, you might not be as pleased. Â I didn't think the India roll upgrade would make much of a difference but after i accidentally ordered it I haven't switched back to regular rolls since. Â The extra dollar per roll is worth it. ORDER FOR PICKUP. There is always a long line and unless you want to wait 15 minutes to order then wait for another 10 to get it, the pickup option is best for you.
Very nice atmosphere, the prices are fair and the service is impeccable. I loved the food here, they have a nice wine list and wide selection. I will come back on my next visit to astoria!

Brought my mom and grandma to Jane for Mother's Day brunch and it was really nice. Our waitress was incredibly nice and the hostess was as well. Our food was really good and love that brunch comes with fresh squeeze orange juice or a drink (they dont serve alki before noon). Overall, had a great experience at Jane and would def head back for another brunch. :)

Expected more. Purposely held off while the former chef of Dumont and Dressler worked out the kinks, but it still seems to be missing the basics. First, our wait was an hour and a half. If I weren't watching the inefficiencies of the staff, I could have been more patient. Table turn was slow with credit cards collecting dust on tables and the seating strategy was flawed and slow as well. Thought we could chill out at the bar but the wait was spilling onto the street so we left to visit a neighboring bar for a drink. When we finally did get seated, we were delighted that we got upgraded from the 2 top they were going to squeeze the 3 of us into and got a perfect 4 top in the back. We ordered mac and cheese to start but it came out with the meals. It was more like mac and cheese soup and although a variation of the famous Dumont mac, it was runny and easy to abandon. Two of us ordered the skate, which was light and delicious, also different from the Dumont version. My friend ordered the short rib sandwich which was good if not petite, especially compared to the giant bowl of fries that over powered the table. Water service was prompt which made the wait seem even more outrageous, as in, if more people were focused on turning tables than aggressively filling water glasses, it could have been better. The music went from perfect to weird, ranging from Otis Redding to The White Stripes which seemed the throw the vibe back and forth. We went ahead and ordered the fried donuts and ice cream, which were as good as the hype, I suppose. Service overall was mediocre but not offensive. Overall: Food was good but not worth the wait. I'd like to see more vegetable experimentation and more diversity from the Dumont staples. It's heavy on the meat. I am not a vegetarian but I couldn't order the popular meatloaf sandwich made of veal, duck, and some other kind of meat without wading through some moral hesitation, but I have heard it is amazing. The biggest issue was management strategy , and the macaroni soup. I might be likely to try it again after some time has passed, but for now it's a thumbs down.

Whoa...all the good reviews for this place...so of course we were excited to try ABC Kitchen out. Â If you want to go here, definitely put in for reservations before hand. Â Although not all the tables were utilized, there was still a 30 minute wait for those who who came in without reservations. Â The space is a decent size and the decor was nice. Â Hostess staff very friendly when entering. Â Our waitress, however, could be a little warmer. Â I had asked her questions about the menu and her response was, "whatever you like to eat." Â And then I asked her if she tried any of the items I referred to, and she said no. Â What kind of waitstaff doesn't know what menu items taste like? Â I'm sure she gets these questions all the time? Â For appetizer we ordered the calmari. Â It was good...tasted like any calamari we would get anywhere else. Â For entrees my husband ordered the akaushi cheeseburger with herbed mayo and pickled jalapenos. Â Perhaps we shouldn't have gone to Shake Shack the night before as my husband said he preferred the shake shack burger. Â I ordered the crispy shrimp, romaine, market vegetables and carrot-sesame vinaigrette and a side of brussel sprouts. Â There were plenty of crispy shrimp, although nothing exciting to write about for this $25 salad. Â Our bill amounted to over $100 since I ordered a beverage. Â Overall, food was OK but not amazing and not worth $100.
Always solid and efficient service. It's very much a diner not a fancy place just good food made and run by good people!

Came here for brunch with a friend I hadn't seen in two years. Great experience. Waiter was super friendly and checked up on us regularly. Food was super delicious, servings are pretty large. We were stuffed to the brim, but kept on trying to stuff our faces. Interior design was easy on the eyes, but nothing stood out in particular. Ambiance was great, perfect for catching up. Would definitely come back.

Lots of meat, rice, and salad for an inexpensive amount. Depending on the day, the season, and the time of day counts when you stand in line to get food from the halal cart. The chicken and rice is pretty tasty and you can gorge your food with limitless amounts of white sauce, brown sauce, but be careful of the hot sauce. A lot of hot sauce can make your food possibly inedible. That happened to me and my friend a few times because we dared each other. You have been warned.

*I'm sorry this is SOO LONG guys* It's hard to give this a solid rating because after the wait we were all so tired and hungry that we were there less than 30minutes. I think it could have been a significantly more enjoyable experience if we were more strategic about it. 2 hour wait for 3 people on a Wednesday night! Strategy: have at least one friend come early and put your name in, then explore all that the st.marks area has to offer :) It's kind of hard on a weeknight because most people don't get off til 6-7 and by the time you get here it could easily be 7-8p which means your not even getting seated to eat til 9-10p which can be pretty late to start eating for most people. If you have one friend that gets off earlier and can be there by 6 and doesn't mind stopping in to put your name in, then you are golden and should be seated around 8 :) Â  Very nice inside, but kind of noisy and open kitchen so you can see the chefs at work. All the servers were hipstered out with tats and the whole bit. They do some table sharing, but your spaced out not crammed next to strangers. Â  Not the best place ever for a vegetarian.. though I didn't get to ask detailed questions about the appetizers because it was already past 10p and we went straight for the entrees. Even though there wasn't a huge selection of vegetarian options, at least they have some, and by the quality of this spot and confidence in the servers' voices you can trust that they are ACTUALLY vegetarian. The majority of the tofu ones on the menu some kind of pork or broth involved. I think there might have been 1-2 vegetarian friendly appetizer choices and two "specialties" (which seem like they are too small to be an entree unless you are getting appetizers and dessert). There was only one vegetarian ramen.. It's the "Wasabi Shoyu Ramen" which was kind of deceptive to me because I expected it to be at least a little spicy and have some wasabi flavor with that being the first word in the name.. but unfortunately it had ZERO spice (heat) and wasn't strongly wasabi tasting. It was very hot temperature wise as it came immediately the whole three steps from the kitchen. I love that.. I love HOT foods. I also love spicy foods so I was kind of bummed.. in retrospect I should of requested sriracha or chili oil or extra wasabi! The bean curd in my ramen was extremely sweet, really if taken out and paired with ice cream it could have been a dessert! I didn't mind it at all but wished that they had cut it up more or at least given me something to break it apart with. Same deal with the nori, it was really good, but in one huge piece when I would've preferred to have the flavor in more than one giant overwhelming bite. My friends shared the Pork Buns, they both have extensive experience with these and unusually high standards, but they enjoyed these. Not the best they've ever had but definitely top 5. They definitely preferred them significantly more than momofuku's. One of my friends got the Shiromaru Hakata Classic, the first ramen menu item, I believe he got the braised beef on top as well. He said it was one of the better ramens hes had but he was a little disappointed that the braised meat was tougher than he thought it was supposed to be. He had the same issue with huge chunks of meat and would've preferred more even distribution of ingredients like I wanted in mine as well. My other friend, who happens to be the pickiest by far, had the Karaka Miso Ramen and enjoyed his the most. The meat in his was much more finely chopped. Also, when he order the server (the only actual Japanese one in the whole restaurant that night) said that this was his favorite ramen there as well. Next time I will definitely be taking advantage of "Kae-dama, a system that offers you an extra serving of noodles for $2 extra. Â When you have almost finished your first serving of noodles, order by saying, "Kae-dama, please". Â In a few minutes the server will bring you another 'ball of noodles.' Â This time I was too full from our snacking exploits around St. Marks during our 2 hour wait. Man.. am I bummed I didn't see the dessert menu! Everything looks AMAZING!! I'm coming back just for dessert! The best sounding desserts: Mascarpone Cheese and Ice Cream Â  Â $8 Matcha Brulee Â  Â $8 Green tea flavored creme brulee topped with gelato Â  Annin Sorbet Â  Â $7 Sweet tofu custard topped with your choice sorbet (Blood Orange or Pear flavors) excited for my dessert update :)

Left a bad taste in my mouth--literally! Not only was the service poor and very slow--with the waiter forgetting to bring one of the appetizers and then disappearing so it was hard to get the missing item--but the food was quite mediocre to poor. The fried artichoke appetizer was fairly good, but the saltibocca di pollo had an unpleasant oily, smoky flavor that overpowered all of the ingredients. Tasted like the food had been doused with liquid smoke or something similar. I was unable to eat some of the dessert biscotti because they tasted like someone had put salt instead of sugar. Given all the excellent reviews, I can't understand why my friends and I got such a poor meal--for a rather high price. And that oily, smoky flavor is still in my mouth hours later.

This place is gotten so famous within such a short period of time as famous chef is running the place. Very nice decor and hot location, many people are looking to have dinner here. It was so hard for me to get a reservation here. It was the day that my girl friend was returning from Korea so I was looking to have very special dinner time. I was very excited. We had several choices that people were recommending on reviews. We had the bar snack, which you are given to choose 3 foods from their bar menu for good price. Food portion is bit small but I think it was quiet good deal at restaurant like this place. Scrambled egg were too salty and bread were burned too much. Meat and crab risotto were kinda salty too. As I had so much high expectation, Â it was very disappointing dinner we had here. If I have to wait this long to have a dinner at this place, I would rather choose some place else to go.

Il Bambino may be my favorite restaurant in New York, where I lived for over two years. Â Of all the good places to eat in New York, I visited Il Bambino more than any other. Â Expect VERY good, fresh food for a VERY manageable price. Â There's food for foodies and food for Joe at this Astoria establishment. Â For starters, try the marinated sardines. Â Even those who are not crazy about seafood will enjoy these rich, salty, oily fish on top of crispy, chewy, thin bread. Â If you're looking for something light after your appetizer, try a mozzarella panini, which comes with fresh tomatoes and basil pesto in it, or a crostini or two. Â For a heartier meal, try a Bacon Butty panini (if you're there for Brunch) full of bacon, avocado and blue cheese. Â It satisfies your hunger and your tastebuds perfectly and, judging by the crowds you see here on the weekends, it probably cures hangovers faster than you can say "Cheese Us Christo!". Â The garden in the back is nice if the weather's nice. Â If you're with friends, it's easy to share because lots of the items on the menu arrive in halves. Â Get there hungry and leave content, and smelling of roasted, toasted wonder. Â Don't leave this off of your vacation itinerary and, for pork's sake, eat here if you live in New York!

Deeeeeelish. A diet deal breaker for sure but you gotta risk it for the biscuit. They had a radish salad as a special but I left my bunny at home. My burger was a blue cheese explosion of goodness. Shoestring fries made eating fries seem delicate and lady like with garlic and rosemary galore. My friends had the marinated olives and enjoyed them. Our waiter was adorable and a rare gem in NYC - a hot kid who doesn't act like a prick! Comfy atmosphere and love the neighborhood. YAY!

You know a place is great when you cant name the best thing you ate because they were all just.so.good. Â  We debated ordering the tasting menu, but ended up going a la carte. Â We had: bacon tater tots scallop crudo oysters burrata ribeye panna cotta I can honestly say everything was excellent. Â Even the bathroom was clean and maintained nicely. Â Will definitely be back soon.

This is a pizza review, not a restaurant review. Nice "rustic atmosphere" space, friendly service for a neighborhood trending snobby. Emporio is probably a good place to bring a date, as evidenced by the couple next to me playing out the eternal human drama (young lady going on and on about how young gentleman doesn't respect her feelings; young gentleman haplessly explaining in a "reasonable" way how she's misinterpreting his total lack of empathy). On to the pizza: it's alright! I mean, if you're jonesing to spend eight times what you normally would, in addition to tax and tipping someone 20% to bring it to you, for the material equivalent of two dollar slices, you can't go wrong with Emporio. And, I suppose, there's all that great shopping right in the neighborhood. I ordered the mushroom and sausage pizza with fiore de latte (foodie talk for "cow's milk") mozzarella. It was quite large, probably too large for most people (not me), and looked gorgeous. The crust was thin, crispy, and good, but I thought the toppings were distributed with a bit too much restraint. Not every slice had enough cheese to taste like cheese, and the mushrooms seem to have been counted. Remember when you were a kid and large pies were like $6 *with* extra cheese? And when you picked up a slice, all that disgusting extra cheese would just slide right off, but you'd pick it up and stuff it into your mouth anyway, burning the roof, but then bite into the now-just-a-piece-of-dough-with-some-sauce-left slice anyway so you'd at least get some bread and tomato flavor in there? And then sit around clutching your guts for the rest of the day, because, even at the age of 11, you managed to give yourself heartburn garnished with a stomachache? I do... what happened? Anyway, when I open my pizzeria ("Hot Cheese Pies from Satan's Assholeâ„¢"), I'm going to put so many toppings onto my signature overpriced gourmet pies, the customers will be required to sign waivers against having their thighs scalded by errant mortadella or rogue truffles. Emporio is among the better thin-crust expensive pizza joints, in the same company as, well, Co. (and Franny's and Pulino's and blah blah blah). But I had a realization today about this whole pizza thing. Pizza is a comfort food, right? We don't tend to judge it by the quality of the ingredients that go into making it as much as we judge it by--as we need from it--the unparalleled emotion of that first bite. That first bite, it transports us to our pizza-craving childhoods (unless you didn't grow up eating pizza i.e. you're a Commie-Nazi), and we forget in that moment the regional origin of the organic olive oil, the traditional crafting of the artisanal ham product, and on which slope of fertile Mt. Vesuvius the tomatoes were grown. It just doesn't matter. In fact, you can hardly taste any of those things. If anything, strange flavors just get in the way, and I've yet to eat one of these fancy-shmancy pizzas that has such unique, "I'm blown away!" flavors that I'm ready then and there to abandon the reliably superior satisfactions of the ubiquitous street slice. So I think there might be a philosophical problem at the heart of the gourmet pizza craze, one that even those caught up in it, myself included, must struggle to ignore. This is a problem that can't be solved with expensive ingredients (n.b. basil is a weed and all the brick ovens in the world are no substitute for hard New Jersey water and mafia-supplied, pre-packaged dough slabs) and probably won't be solved at least until the opening of Hot Cheese Pies from Satan's Assholeâ„¢ (see you there). Until then, you could do worse than breaking a crisp Andrew Jackson at Emporio.

After walking by this place a million times, I finally stopped in to try it. Â It was delicious. $7 for fries is a bit steep, but damn I like fries. Got pineapple chutney, mango something, and honey mustard. First two were delicious. Third one tasted like honey mustard, so I don't mind.

Definitely five stars. Â My favorite was the wanton soup and the noodles with peanut sauce. Â Prices are cheap for good quality food. Â The service was great! Â The lady at the counter was so sweet and nice :)

conveniently right next door! I miss the sushi place before this, but their Ramen is SO good here. yummy. They only except cash though - and bills no larger than 20. That is not convenient. And for this reason I subtract one star.

This is my favorite Thai restaurant in NYC. Â The food is AMAZING - much better and more consistent than many of the other Thai restaurants in the area. Â Nice sit down atmosphere in a fresh metropolitan decor. Â The staff is just lovely: Kind, friendly, knowledgeable, and helpful. Â I highly recommend the calimari, Ming Ka Na, sate moo, curry puffs, roti, any of the fried fish or duck entrees. Â And the prices are extremely reasonable. Â  Go, try it. Â You'll thank me after...

Very New York! Love the standing only room by the cheese, cured meats, and wines. Also, really enjoyed the waiter service to the table. Â It was just a bit too chaotic in there for my liking. Â I did go on a Saturday. Â Also, the price was way too high. Â I mean I get it with the location and all, but seriously. 40 per head for cheese, salami,veggies, and a glass of wine? Â That's too much. Â Would come back though next time.

I lunch fairly often in this neighborhood... it's very possible I have had lunch at every restaurant walking distance from Ciccio, and I have to say Ciccio really stood out from the pack from me. Â The decor is awesome, sort of rustic city disrepair (exposed and distressed walls) meets glossy modern ikea-ish style furnishing. Â The vibe in the restaurant was also very good, even though the tables are a little close together. Â Service was welcoming and on point, if you're in a rush they'll get you in and out, but if you're in the mood to linger for a bit, that's cool too. Â Great olive oil for the bread and used on the sandwiches; they have a soup and half sandwich lunch special that seems like a good deal. Â I tried the squash soup (both soups on the lunch menu are vegetarian, Yay!) and wanted to eat the entire bowl. Â I also had a bit of my friend's mozzarella sandwich, which was good. I had the Strisce Alla Chiantigiana which was delicious. Â I customized it to not include the beef cheek, but I bet the meat would knock this dish out of the park. Â The waiter and my coworkers recommend the vegetable lasagna, which I will certainly try on my next visit.

This place is GREAT! The staff is friendly and helpful. The host actually came outside and flagged me down when my phone died. Not to mention BACON! Go for the Bacon flight, and if this is still on the menu the "Lobster loves Bacon" Mac n' cheese. Beyond delicious! Get your ass down here and have some delicious food!

I was a bit bummed when I stopped by Pure Thai Shophouse with an out-of-town guest and they were not open, so I figured I'd check the line at Totto Ramen. Â Shockingly there was none, so we stopped in and immediately got a table (Wednesday, 3:15 PM). Â Now it was pushing 90 degrees outside which may have kept folks away, but we were not deterred. Â Two bowls of spicy ramen arrived almost immediately after we ordered them and we were in heaven. Â We were sweating like the proverbial lady of the evening in a house of worship, but we were in heaven nonetheless. Â The bowls are huge and the flavors are even bigger. Â Worth a visit for sure.

43rd between 2nd and 3rd has become my favorite block. Sakagura, Soba Totto, Sushi Yasuda make a holy trinity of amazing Japanese restaurants, brought to you by the letter S. Sakagura is a lovely, cavernous restaurant, and it quite literally feels like a cave once you start spelunking down the series of stairs underground and losing your AT&T reception on the way. Â My brother and I made last minute reservations on a Monday, and they had a 7:15 pm availability at the bar. Â We arrived ravenous and left with satiated appetites, full but comfortably so, ordering: HIYAYAKKO : Â Chilled Tofu Topped with Grated Ginger , Scallion and Bonito Flakes Â $5.00 (solid, nothing extraordinary) IKA SHIOKARA : Â Sliced Raw Squid Cured in Salt and a Squid Liver Marinade Â $5.00 (warning: this was good but very salty) ONSEN TAMAGO : Â Soft Boiled Egg Topped with Sea Urchin and Salmon Roe in Cold Soup Â $9.00 (the waiter recommended we each get one, but the uni was decent enough of a serving to be shared) SEAWEED SALAD : Â Assortment of Seaweed Topped with a choice of Citrus Vinaigarette OR Sesame Â $8.00 (the sesame dressing is incredible) SANMA ONIGIRI : Â Cooked Rice Balls with Shiitake Mushroom, Pickled Radish and Mountain Vegetables Wrapped with a Whole Baked Pike Mackerel [3pcs] Â $10.00 (this was wonderful-crispy rice balls wrapped in crispy mackerel) UNI SOBA $22 (honestly loved this more than the Uni Soba at Soba Totto and Soba Ya- the broth sets it apart from the rest) SESAME CRÃˆME BRULEE $9 (solid, nothing extraordinary) Like most Izakaya places, Sakagura is a great place to try a little bit of everything, and I will definitely come back to work my drunken way through the extensive sake menu.

I walk by this restaurant every day, as I live only a few blocks down, and had been wanting to try it. My boyfriend and I came on a Friday night around 7:30 and were happy that we received a table withing 20 min. The atmosphere of this place is great - perfect lighting, cozy seating, and a great backyard seating under a tent. A wedding party was also going on in another outdoor area and didn't interrupt from the romantic mood of our dining at all. The food was excellent and perfect portions. We had two different types of pasta, a crostini and then the tiramisu for dessert. The house wine is very reasonably priced and not bad. I would recommend Frankies as a great date spot in Brooklyn!

Amazing. Get the Bronte Burger, you will not regret it. The ciabatta bun is light but just the right thickness and size for the burger. I always end up tearing off bits of the buns at other burger places, but no piece of the Bronte was left behind. The beef was juicy and tender, approaching short-rib consistency. The sangria we had was quite amazing as well. The pumpkin salad was good and had a fair amount of pumpkin and bits of crumbly goat cheese. I went with a girlfriend, and we split the burger and salad -- it was just right for the two of us. Seating is communal and the space is small, but felt cozy rather than crowded. We showed up at around 7:30 on a Monday and were seated right away. 4.5 stars!
Great tasting ramen. It's a popular spot so the wait can sometimes be long. I prefer the ramen at this location over the newer Ippudo West location.

Amazing Indian food at really great price. Masala chai is surely one of the best you could find in New York. The manager and staff were really friendly and helpful. Will definitely come back to the place again and surely recommend to my friends and family. Keep up the great work guys and see you next time.

Supremely excellent Chicharrones. Â I really liked this Puerto Rican Taxi driver hangout when I used to work near by. Â Unfortunately I only discovered it in my last week there and now I work in midtown (booooo!). Â Good cheap eats, perfect ambience for what it is.

I think I've been here about 4 times since I moved to New York last April, and I haven't been disappointed once. Like a lot of people, I went to Perilla only because I'm a Top Chef whore and was hoping to catch a glimpse of Chef Harold. But instead, I was so blown away by the food that I could care less that he was two feet away from me at the bar. Just kidding... I was so psyched and couldn't contain myself when I saw him. I even rolled my eyes when I heard some friends I dined with didn't know Chef Harold or even watched Top Chef! BLASPHEMY! Back to the point. The food was amazing! Favorites at this restaurant are: -Spicy Duck Meatballs -Grilled Prime Hanger Steak -Sauteed Spaghetti Squash -Vanilla Scented Donuts YUM! They change their menu every so often and I try my best to taste EVERYTHING. You know, so I can review them for Yelp. But if you're thinking of visiting the restaurant for the first time, I would go for these dishes. Oh man, I totally just made myself really hungry at 2:44am. Crap! Service is excellent too. Great waiters, very kind and knowledgeable with the menu and wines. And with wine glasses so pretty you better get yourself a whole bottle and enjoy! :D

I dropped in here for a quick meal before another meeting. I chose the chicken chili verde, as I figured they could dole it out fast. Indeed, it did come out fast, and it was amply sized and spiced. A perfect, quick meal. I hope to be back to try more of the menu.

What is it with the ratings? Â Inexpensive ordinary food does not equate with great food. Nice soup dumplings, but that is about it. Joe Shanghai still rocks this corner of the market. You can probably do better at Pings, which is right across the street and has an exceptional location on Queens Blvd, near Woodhaven, NY. Ask for the Peeking Pork Chops, trust me, you won't be disappointed. Now go work on your culinary taste buds.

Full disclosure - been meaning to eat here since Top Chef Masters Season 2 and Tyler Florence named the chicken here the best thing he ever ate that was "better than [his]" on the Food Network. So naturally I had the chicken, as did my friend who, up until recently, only ate poultry and thus considers herself a chicken expert. Anyway- JW's chicken is a ginormous plate of food that can easily serve 2. I would have appreciated fair warning about that; the juicy goodness isn't going to hold up the next day as leftovers. Reading other people's comments and discovering that dishes can be done by half orders would have been very useful information at the time, for sure. I also could have used more room for the salted caramel gelato offered for dessert. Gotta say, though, the best thing I ate that night wasn't actually the chicken (which was pretty darn good). Winner of the evening goes to the side of potatoes. Nice and crispy with parmesan and rosemary; I was thisclose to eating the fried rosemary. Overall a lovely evening and a great meal. Marks off because the service could have been better. Hostess was a little snitty. Our server was fine, although he could have spared us the snark re: our group wiping out the appetizers clean in roughly 10 minutes. Hey, it was tasty (calamari and bruschetta). Don't judge...

Kefi was delicious! Â It was more spacious than I would have expected from outside. Â With reservation, my friend and I were seated downstairs in a corner booth. Â The atmosphere was inviting and cozy, an ideal place to dine with a few people or a group. Â The waitress was very helpful and great at recommending her favorite drinks and dishes. Â The octopus salad was seriously to die for, and the branzini was perfection. Â This will definitely be a go-to place on the upper west side. Â Try it!

BEST PORK BUNS EVER AWARD!!! Most delicious and delicate little pork buns you have ever had. Seriously. Love the Modern ramen and the pickled veggies are awesome. Ippudo is always well worth the (most likely) 45 minute wait.

This place is amazing. Â I have never seen Tanya " my food comfort zone is solidly in the American meat and potatoes category" D eat vegan food before. Â Nor any sort of african food. Â To make both happen at once is worthy of a nobel prize if not beatification, but unfortunately I am not on the nobel committee nor am i the pope, so I will have to do the best I can, which is 5 yelp stars.

I decided to try this place for lunch after seeing a lot of positive reviews. I have to say I was happy myself. It's not too far from where I work and they have healthy food options which taste good too. I ordered the 'Ultimate Plate' and the 'Alkaline Shake' - both turned out to be good choices. But, I have to admit there were so many other options on the menu that I would want to try, so I'm definitely going back to this place. The man behind the cash counter was courteous and pointed me to a much larger menu than what was in front of me on the boards in the restaurant. I have to say though, I felt the lunch was kind of expensive given that it cost me $20 (including tax and tip) for those 2 things. The plate was kinda big though, good enough to last me 2 full meals and I guess if the food is healthy, you've got to pay! One other thing that wasn't a deal breaker but not the most comfortable either that they have a small space inside the restaurant hence not enough tables to sit there and eat if you wanted to. Happy Eating!
for $18 i think your getting like half a lobster there. loved the bun that came with the lobster roll! the meal was great with the ginger soda + salt and vinegar chips
Cheese grits are off the hook
Finally I got there and I tried their food . Noodles were great and BBQ pork was much better than I have heared .

This place doesn't need another good review, but I can't help myself. It checks all the boxes: Great Food - I've only been for breakfast, granted, but everything here has been scrumptious. Moroccan scramble! Why would I ever settle for a boring two egg brunch again? The muesli and oatmeal are probably the best I've ever had - interesting and hearty twists on classics. Plus, I can get oysters with my breakfast. Great Service - Always accommodating, prompt, and attentive. Good Drink Selection - Yes, I will have a cocktail at an 8 o'clock breakfast (also, they are open early as opposed to many NYC places that don't open for breakfast til 11 which is absurd). Plus pretty tasty (though not spectacular coffee - I think it's an americano actually) Great Prices - By NYC standards, breakfast for two under $30 is pretty outrageous(ly good). Plus they have the common decency to be near a subway stop. A must before any Brooklyn day drinking excursion.
Came in for lunch with my dad. Â Great seafood soup and mussels. Fresh and perfectly seasoned. And BYO! The owner is pretty great too.

Best Barbecue in New York. No question. Hands down. Mr. Delaney (who actually was serving at the bar the last time I was there) is a genius. Even having been to Big Apple BBQ Block Party and trying barbecue from all over the country, this is the place to go. Walk in with a couple friends and order about half to a full pound of meat per person, but of all the options. Personally, the pork ribs are the best. What amazing peppery bark is on those ribs. For most, this place is all about the brisket, which is surely the best in NYC. Fatty, tender, peppery, perfect. Their huge beef rib is also a much try, at least to see meat torn off that huge bone (which they actually use as the door handle to the restroom). One thing I've noticed is poor sides at some barbecue joints, not this place. Best collard greens and potato salad I've had. The beans with meat, can't go wrong. Another wonderful thing is that after you order, you walk over to a station to help yourself to slice of thick cut potato bread, pickled peppers and onions, paper towels, and Crystal's hot sauce. Grab everything as you'll need. Then sit down, throw some peppers and onions on that bread, a slab of brisket, shake some hot sauce on, fold that thing, and enjoy your mouthgasm. Oh, did I mention how good of a deal this all is? I went with 4 friends, we walked away paying $14 each! For world class barbecue! In New York! I can come back to this place every week. Just go already.

This is the best place for: - Good sized Slices of Pizza - The worlds greatest slice of Artichoke Pizza - Getting Fresh Pizza - Good tunes while you wait (yes, you'll have to wait but worth it) - Late night munchies because it's open late! I crave their pizza at the oddest times. When I finally get there the aroma makes you want it so much more. It's a cute little place (practically a hole in the wall) so take your pizza to go or eat right there! My favorite spot? Under the scandalous leg lamp!

Sure, there might not be internet, the coffee is not the greatest ever, etc., but the charm and beauty of this place and the naturalness of its decor make it one of a kind. Â  Trees growing through the cafe, sunlight coming from the ceiling, truly a magical place. Â Come here if you want a quaint place to study or talk on a sunny winter day, avoid it if you would rather wait in the cold for 15 minutes for a cup of hand-drawn coffee or whatnot.

You walk in and BLAO! The entire staff greets every single customer walking in the dining area. I started off with the famous Hirata pork buns that everyone has been talking about and also ordered the Akamaru Modern Ramen with pork belly and a hard boiled egg. Wow. The food was delicious. I have never had better pork buns in my life. The pork was marinated and the buns were so soft and it just melted. The Akamaru Modern Ramen was the first "authentic" ramen I've ever had. Definitely the best way to start off my ramen spree, for I've begun trying other places (none can compare). They have a terrible wait time of an hour or so but it's fair due to the high volume and popularity, so reserve accordingly. ALSO, they offer call/text services to notice customers of their reservations! Sometimes you share tables, so get your social skills in action! They have a wonderful music playlist that ranged from trance and freestyle (90s) which I adore.

Love love love!! Hit up EV for a delightful brunch!!! I love the open airy atmosphere and the whole vibe the place gives off. Minimalistic and sexy! I came in strictly for the drinks, but began drooling over my friends salad.. I gave in and ordered. Thank god I did.. Crisp, light, and tasty! The place deserves 5 stars, but I docked one due to a watery sangria

An experience worth having, but portions are small. Â The tofu was nice, a little too jiggly for my dinnermates. Â I love tofu, so it was fine for me. We ordered the tororo soba since reviews said it was pretty traditional, but since we never had it before, the slimy consistency scared us a little... Â the taste was pleasantly full flavored. I ordered the sashimi omakase which was perfect for me, but not mindblowing. Everything was fresh and the ambience is great. We did not have much of a wait 10-15min for 4 around 8pm on Wed night. **Note: They only take reservations for 6pm, otherwise you have to walk-in and wait. Â Plenty of other places around in case the wait is ridiculous, so I think this location is worth a try.
Best lychee martini's. Â Great atmosphere!

Came in around three pm on a Saturday looking for a tasty escape from fifth ave. The restaurant is well kempt and the service was outstanding. I ordered the bangan bhattha and the chicken tikka masala. Both dishes came out quickly and were fresh and delicious. The bangan bhartha was one of the best I have ever had.

Really feeling this place. Â Actually came for a happy hour where they serve really amazing cider's, wines, and beers. Â Ended up staying here for dinner because the food looked so amazing. Â I'm a healthy eater and this place is right up my alley. Â Excellent meats, vegetables, all organic, no bs preservatives. Â Really hard to find, I wish more restaurants were following this trend.

If you want honest pure lobster, crab, or shrimp meat without much other ingredients, you would like their sandwiches. The sandwiches, however, are much smaller than you think though. Â I've ordered Taste of Maine, which consists of half lobster, crab, and shrimp sandwiches. Â The bread was delicious. The meats were not much seasoned. They tasted firm but not sweet. Â Overall a good experience though.

Yay for foie gras! Â Considering the fact that California no longer allows restaurants to carry foie gras, getting my hands on these suckers was a treat. All I can say was that it was delicious. Their Black Label Burger is a must get. Â The burger was meaty, juicy, and cooked to perfection. Â Time to go run 5 miles now... -_-

I went with the Black Label burger (as do most). It is fantastic. This place has a great throwback atmosphere. The Black Label Burger does not include cheese, as my guess is that the chef does not want to overpower the amazing earthiness of the burger. There is a cheaper burger with cheddar that I would likely try if/when I get back here.

Come here for lunch or sometimes late night when nothing else is open. Â Pretty much your average Chinatown restaurant. Â The service is OK. Â Its really small and tight in here. Â Also, the place feels sticky icky so I just eat and get out right away. I always get the Roast Duck, Pork, or Chicken over egg noodles or rice. Â Its pretty good but sometimes they give you the really bony pieces or one that's been sitting around for a while and not fresh anymore. Â  Decent place for lunch but there are a lot of other options in the area. Â I prob won't be eating in anymore and prob will just order a whole duck or chicken to go since you have a better chance of getting a fresh one and its cheaper.

Cramped but yummy! Great Thai food, my hubby had the garlic beef and I had the crab/pork dry noodles. Mine was a little bland but my hubby's was awesome.Oh and the curry puffs yummmm. A pretty good choice, I wish I would have been more hungry I would have tried more on the menu.

Went here for the AYCD special (and basically all you can eat) for $55 excl. tax & tip. The food was delicious Italian and they really didn't skimp on the wine. Great spot if you have a work-sponsored dinner or even for a date, nice and intimate. Â Also came here with the parents and we were subject to a bit of a wait for three at around 8:30/9 on a weeknight (expected) - the food was as delicious as the first time around and they let us pay for the wine by the quarter bottle, so if we only drank 3/4, they'd charge us for 3/4 (we ended up finishing it). Â Due to our wait earlier in the night, the waiter brought over shots of grappa on the house and enjoyed one with us. Â Great little spot and Frank's (owned by the same people and nearby) is also a great option. Â Just beware of cash-only.

I was on a Taco rampage over the summer. Finally decided to check this place out, it's a great taco place around St Marks, the best part was the guacamole. You have to pay extra for just guacamole, but they give you a big tub of guacamole, so I think it was worth the price. Tacos were eh, the pita chips went well with the guacamole, it was a bonus that they make it themselves.

Friendly staff is what drew me in (not that I need more friends). The bruschetta is HUGE and under $7. The space is absolutely cavernous, to the dark sultry dining rooms in the bottom section, to the light and airy lantern garden in the back, there's enough room for everyone. Spent a very lazy Sunday afternoon here noshing on tidbits and drinking wine and couldn't have been more pleased. They have been inducted into my hall of greatness.
So fast. So cheap. SO. GOOD.
Delicious food and cozy atmosphere. Service could have been a little better but overall a good experience. I would go back :)

haha gigantic portions. i like the steak. it is smokier than what i'm used to but i like it. I grew up in texas so I'm picky when it comes to mexican food. I give it a thumbs up for its price, convenience, and being in the east coast. the regular salsa has a black peppery kick to it. the the extra hot sauce is more astringent/ acidic...but it's tasty. I'll try half and half next time.

Always good food. The hor fun is always a slurpy goodness! The duck and roasted pork is probably their best dishes. Nothing too special with this restaurant, the waiter service sucks. The services there are too rushed and pushy. I ordered a beef brisket noodle soup once, and i accidentally blurted out two types of noodles and the lady rudely told me to correct myself. I think the servers are MUCH nicer to the tourists than the locals. It's very dirty in there, the floors are always greasy for some reason? Thank god for their good food, otherwise, i rather go some place else....

Very unique dining experience for Bed-Stuy. Â Looks unassuming and I had some doubts, but it was highly recommended by a few co-workers. The menu is ever changing and it's also BYOB w a liquor store half a block away. Can't beat that. Wife and I tried several apps and enjoyed the fish with fries and duck for the mains. Â My duck was slightly over cooked but still very good. Â Her fish and the donut foie gras were the highlight of the evening. The service could be a little better, but I'll give them a pass this time. Â Can't wait to see what's on the menu next.

If you're feeling a little bit under the weather and you're in need of some comfort food...like a big bowl of soup, then this is the spot. Â It helps that this place is right around the corner from me, but even it it weren't, I would still check it out.
