Â the duck confit and sour cherry filling hit those savory sweet notes and the green chile sauce on top balanced out the dish. Â after that, i wasn't shy, i dug into a grass-fed cheese burger with house cured chorizo served with a harissa aioli sauce and delicious cured pickles. Â best of all, it was topped with those skinny, crunchy potato sticks you can never seem to get enough of. jack had the fish special; a panko crusted hake. Â it was also very good, nice and crispy on the outside and a perfectly firm and tender center. we went at around 7pm and luckily were able to get a table for 4 but you may want to make a reservation if you're going on a friday or saturday night. Â the vibe is casual, the music is good and the food is very tasty. Â definitely give it a try~

Thanks to fellow Yelpers, we came here on a whim for Sunday brunch. As expected with long waits at any NYC brunch eatery on weekends, it wasn't any different with LV. But lady luck was on our side. We managed to nab the last table outside (as the weather was nice to sit out then); otherwise, we were told the wait for a table inside would be over an hour. For a brief look, the inside seemed elegant with high ceiling and many windows, and it appeared to be a good place for gatherings with friends. Anyways, back to us being seated outside and probably because of that, our server was great. Attentive and helpful with giving suggestions for us first timers. After hearing about the ricotta, ricotta, and the ricotta, we (you probably guessed it!) decided to go for a ricotta overload. We started with ricotta cheese with honey and herbs along with orange flavored toast. It was a pleasant combination. Probably a bit too much cheese for not enough toast, but that's a minor point. We then got their (famous?) lemon ricotta pancakes - ricotta-based pancakes, lemon curd, blueberries, and powdered sugar. The tangy lemon curd was the highlight for us in that dish. The chefs were skimpy with the curd on the pancakes, but we were able to get extra without additional cost. Overall, we had a nice brunch. I would go here again if I were in the area (sadly, I don't like ricotta enough to go out of my way to this place).

I frequent this place so much, I'm calling myself Empanada Papa. I've tried almost all their empanadas and it's like a mouthgasm every time. Their tutti frutti is also delicious that one time, after speaking so highly of this place, I came in with a friend just for drinks (after being so full from a previous dinner, but still not wanting to pass up the opportunity of coming here) and the waiter seemed annoyed that we weren't getting food. I can understand the feeling, being a waiter myself, but to automatically add the tip just for two rounds is a low blow to me. It's kinda like "hey, these two kids aren't even getting food, they're probably either cheap or have no money, so let me put the tip just to be safe." Not cool. I usually tip even for bad service so that hurt me, admittedly, a little more than it should have.

My friend was looking for a good brunch place and found Cafe Orlin on the web. We went there for a late Sunday brunch around 2 pm and it was still packed. We waited half an hour to get our table, having a cup of really good espresso on the sidewalk. We were starving so I was looking at other people's places to choose something and be ready with my order as soon as we get the table. It was totally worth the wait! The food came very quickly and was delicious! Generous serving of really good eggs and New York steak, enough for at least two Mimosas! I highly recommend that place and I'll definitely go back!

Always good, comforting food. Â Nice wines, the oysters rock. Â Had the bone marrow, and while it was a little too much meaty butteryness for myself, I can see why others would love it. Â Calamari is tender. Good, good, and good.

I get the pork soup dumplings, often. Yum. The shanghai noodle soup with veggies was good too. Service is nothing special but I've never been left waiting long for anything. You will have to ask for refills on tea, generally - but at least the tea is free and they bring you the first one without asking (as it should be in a real asian restaurant!). Good prices. If they could make things cleaner (the dishes I've gotten were ALWAYS dirty), I'd give 5 stars.

It's not often that I find places in Soho/Nolita that I find to be both fun and a value, however Cafe Habana ticks both of those boxes. I stumbled upon this place while wandering the neighborhood in seach of some grub. Music and the sweet smell of delicious food poured out onto the street. We waited for 45+ minutes, but came without reservations on a busy night, so it was to be expected. The inside of the restaurant is kitchy, but a lot of fun. Atmosphere oozes out of every pore of this establishment. I had the Cuban sandwich and Mexican Corn. They were perfect, and my meal was well below my $20 cap for a cheap meal. A fantasic little place well worth the wait!
Drunk at whatever time of the day...always a good time to go to Mamoun's Falafel. It's cheap, fast and tasty. It hits the cravings and works.

In a few rhyming words, here's what you need to know about Totto: The wait is ridiculous The ramen is delicious The preparation is meticulous But oh so expeditious! The restaurant is cramped and tiny But I don't want to sound whiny If you like your ramen spicy, Pour that sesame oil, oh blimey! Come hungry, no need for panache But off to the ATM you may want to dash As they accept none other but cash Then enjoy a great meal in a flash!
This stuff is gross when you are sober, but heavenly gross when you are otherwise.
Great empanadas-it's tough to decide which to get! Â The hot sauce is soo fresh, you can taste the cilantro.

You would think a place you have to book weeks in advance would be one the finest dining experiences you can have. Sadly, like many other NYC landmarks, this does not live up to the hype. A complete disappointment.

As a die hard Arab, I never ever knew Arabic fusion could taste so good! This is not your traditional Arabic restaurant so don't walk in expecting basic kabobs and hummus. What you'll find here is a culinary twist on traditional Middle Eastern dishes so behold an explosion of unexpected flavors in your mouth. I am literally obsessed with every menu item at Ilili. Their mezza (small bite) plates are my absolute favorite so I always end up ordering 4-6 plates to share for a group of 2-3 and we're always satisfied.I've loved everything but I have to bow down to their duck shawarma which is to die for, their Phoenician fries with fig garlic dip (even though the name is a bit offensive to Lebanese people who love their Arabic background), kibe naye (meat tartare so it's definitely an acquired taste) and their veal bacon wraps. Sometimes, Ilili has a stand at Madison Square Eats from time to time and I LOVE going there to grab lunch. So why do you ask I give this place a 4 star? It's because I ALWAYS have to wait 30+ minutes regardless of what time my reservation is or how busy the place seems. I just hate the wait. Also, if you're seated upstairs in one of their "private rooms" it's strangely and uncomfortably intimate with a bunch of other dinning strangers so ALWAYS sit downstairs in the big room.

Was at Table 87 last night with family. What an experience pizza was best in New York City charred just right as friendly waiter names Danny brought it fresh out of coal oven. Crust was thin and sauce and cheese evenly dispersed on pizza. Danny reccomended red wine for our table to go with pizza and the scene felt like I was eating a family dinner at my grandmothers home when I was a child. Table 87 is now my to to restaurant for friends and family. As I said earlier best pizza I ever had.

My cousin and I came here for the 5 course tasting menu. Â This is located in Tribeca, very near the METRO station. Once you walk through the door, you smell a very "apple" scent because there were rows of apples lined up along the wall. Â  They took my coat immediately at the door. We were seated in a quiet spot toward the end of the restaurant. I'm not saying I am a fan but the food was just okay. Tasting Menu: 1) Chilled Kumamoto Oysters, Oscetra Caviar Homemade Radish Pickle, Thinly Sliced Live Sea Scallops Parsley Juice 2) Maine Day Boat Lobster Roasted with Tri-State Strawberries, Baby Fennel Organic Petits Pois 3) Organic Colorado Rack of Lamb Local Rainbow Swiss Chard, Lacinata Blue Kale and Black Mint Â PurÃ©e, Roasted Garlic Shoots, Hurley Mountian Chive Fingerling Potato PurÃ©e 4) Soup (pear soup) 5) Mango and Passionfruit Dome Fresh Rosemary Cocoa and White Coffee Ice Creams (My cousin got this dessert) 6) Hot Valrhona Chocolate SoufflÃ© Vermont Maple and Vanilla Ice Creams Chocolate Sorbet (I got this dessert) There were an added tiered dish with petite fours sweet treats at the end of our meal. Â When we headed for our coat check, we were given an apple cake courtesy of the Bouley bakery across the street. I enjoyed the variety of breads brought to our table: hazelnut, raisin, cranberry, rosemary, and olive. Â  SERVICE - I did not like the changing guards of the waiter service. I think we had 4 to 5 waiters throughout the evening. See my photos

I want to start off by putting you in our shoes, we were hungry, my girlfriend, her older brother and I arrived a little after noon. The place looks nice and I was enjoying the smells. We were all excited for a yummy first meal of the day. We could either wait 15 minutes or sit at a high table with stools, stools are like the Indian style version of sitting at a table in a restaurant. Â The waiter came with water and announced that he would return in a bit for our drink orders. We were there to eat and since this wasn't my first rodeo I can pick out what I want to eat and drink from a one page menu without a Super Bowl halftime show length break. He came back and asked what we wanted to drink. We got three lattes, one iced. He didn't ask about food and brought three pieces of bread. After taking too long to bring the drinks (we were sitting across from the bar) and at least one of the "hot" lattes was luke warm, he took our order. It took a while. My iced latte was not very good so I wanted to try sweetening it a little but there was no sugar or colon cancer sweetener to be seen. I walked up to the front and asked the hostess where to obtain some sugar because I couldn't find any waitstaff and she said sorry that our waiter didn't bring out the sweeteners with our coffee. You know when you go to a movie Â that you arent too excited about and there are a lot of commercials and you forget what you are seeing, that was this wait. We got to see a guy making waffles for a while and judging from the look of them we probably just should have ordered them, when in Rome. Our food was finally delivered by someone else and my girlfriend's brother got a completely different omelette (this one was drowning in feta) my girlfriend's sandwich came with mayo after that was the ONLY special instruction that came from our thee orders. Mine looked right. We couldn't find our waiter so we told another one what happened and they removed the wrong orders, this waiter apologized. I shared my fries, and nibbled on my burger (apple juice, coffee and a protein shake over 4 hours in the morning is not enough for this growing boy). The correct foods were eventually delivered and only then did our waiter swing on by to ask how our meals were (as the other server was placing them on the table) my girlfriend's brother told him that we had just received the correct meal so we were just about to start, and instead of saying sorry or giving anything close to an apology he asked if the meal was better now, WTF does that mean, two of us still don't know you douche bag. The watering was bad, he barely came before the meal and didn't water at all during the meal. The burger was far from spectacular, this was a 15 dollar 9 ounce cheese burger and I know a place where i can get a tastier one for 5.50 less than two blocks away. My gfs sandwich lacked flavor, had mushy tomatoes, a small amount of avocado, cold defrosted chicken and bread that was too hard. Her brother ate the whole omelette but what can I say, we were hungry. The waiter didn't show his face again until the waters were past second waters due to ice melt and we were obviously done. I was bumped into by the waitstaff way too many times due to my middle stool seat. They never offered to bring more bread after we scarfed it down. And the waiter came with the check once again acting like he hadn't Â completely screwed up our order. Overall I give this place two stars because I liked the feel and the hostess combined with one waiter were nice. Otherwise the food is at best underwhelming and overpriced and the service hovers just above the county jail variety.

I'm from Brooklyn, and been around a lot of pizza joints, this one takes the prize as best pizza ever. Totally fresh with great ingredients. I see people complaining about the burned pizza they get; it's Mr DiFara making it, so it's gonna have some burns (maybe). So it's unusual. I'm not gonna go on about the wait, the line, the heat and lack of space. Go there with a plan, one finds a seating area and waits, while the other gets in line and order. Go, enjoy it. It's worth the damn wait. Trust me.

strolled into a Spritzenhaus on a balmy December evening to meet a friend for drinks. Having never been here before I was blown away by the fire place, the sheer space available, and the beer list. ***fire place - a real wood burning fireplace (meaning the smell is fantastic, you don't often smell wood burning fires in NYC) that is open on all sides, meaning seating is available if you choose to want to snuggle up next to the fire. ***the physical space - sorta warehouse-y but certainly not cold. there are long wooden tables in the beer hall style as well as more intimate 2-person tables for when you don't want to feel like you're at Oktoberfest. there is also a massive bar that snakes around half the space. ***the beer list - I'm not a beer snob, and I don't turn up my nose at the occasional bud light (judge me, go ahead), BUT I do like to try different things when the opportunity presents itself. spritzenhaus gives you a huge range of options sorted by style (lager, ale, etc) and makes note of flavors and highlights of each beer - which for those of us outside the beer cognoscenti, is helpful in making decisions. finally, they have a strawberry beer (Fruli) I had previously only seen and enjoyed in England. my delight at seeing this available really sold spritzenhaus for me. while I was here on a quiet Tuesday night (around 8-11) it never felt boring or dead (even though there were even a few people getting work done on laptops). also, I didn't try any food, this is why I can't give a 5 star review (yet) but I'll definitely be back to determine whether the brats match the brews (what a cheesy way to end a review).

Stumbled upon this place one night with my boyfriend and we loved it. Intrigued by the Mexican French fusion, we ordered a lot from the menu including the steak, guacamole and mussels -All delicious! Unfortunately we didn't know it was bottomless moules frites night, so we will definitely be returning. Great, fun casual atmosphere and the staff is really nice!

OMG, this place is insane!!! The food was nothing short of AMAZING. I've actually been bored lately when it comes to restaurants as it seems like the same old crap. But that's not the case here. Avocado fries, almond crusted tilapia sliders, mini apple pie turnovers, maiz (which sounds boring on the menu but is delicious), and pumpkin cheesecake (by far the creamiest, smoothest cheesecake I've ever eaten) are just some of the delicious things we tried. And everything was reasonably priced. By the end I was stuffed to the gills and I didn't throw down mucho dinero either. Our waiter was funny too. A bonus considering most waiters seem to be going through the motions. I will definitely be back!
The meat is not halal, but they have enough vegetarian options to make me happy : ) the falafel and stuffed grape leaves were yummy.

We stumbled in by default, as it was the only place with an open kitchen (it was post 11pm). Â We were greeted by a friendly bartender who advised the kitchen's open till midnight. The friendliness of the place didn't end there - as our waiter (whose name I forget, dang) couldn't have been friendlier. Â Even the bus boys were upbeat and attentive! You would've thought it was 6pm, not 11:30pm, as we never felt rushed and the food was certainly made with love (except for the asparagus dish, which was a bit bland), especially the ribs and mashed potatoes. It should be mentioned that it's "Dine In Brooklyn" week, so we got a great $25 deal, but still, the food, service and cleanliness of the place was certainly 5-star worthy. We'll certainly be back!

A wide selection of beers with reasonable prices. The few times that I've been here, it wasn't crowded and I could easily talk to my friends. The wait staff is friendly, attentive, and happy to leave you alone when you indicate this. Otherwise they come over a lot to check up on you (but in a nice way). It's exactly the sort of friendly down-to-earth bar that I would want in my neighborhood.

I was back in NYC last weekend, and my buddy buddy drag me to The meatball shop. ( I pleated for thai food at Elephant.. but i lost the bet Rock, Pepper Sissor) We waited 45 minutes. for our table. 1. Cuuute Host. 2. Spicy pork with mushroom sauce and provolone = made by hands of god. 3. The meat ball is out of this world. 4. beer selection is ok. TRY Pork ball with parm cream sauce and provolone on white. Spicy pork with classic Tomato sauce chicken meatballs with Parmesan sauce Work it up to everything in the kitchen Platter. I don't even like waiting for tables in Los Angeles, or Chicago Culinary scene. Â but NYC is whole different animal. and TMS is great example of that. Â  I can't wait thill I go back!

Excellent food, especially if you are a bacon/meat lover like I am. It's certainly not light fare but it sure is delicious. Country fried steak was great! The jalapeÃ±o cornbread was awesome as well. Good service too which I'm a big stickler for. The bread pudding was good but not spectacular.

An awesome place for breakfast, lunch or brunch. They have a unique system going that keeps the line moving pretty fast- while you stand in line to order, a waiter/waitress will assign you a handkerchief and reserve a table, and once you've sat down they come bring your dishes! Prices are average for any brunch/lunch spot in the area, but their sandwiches (had the turkey with Brie and apple which was delicious) are great and in good portions.

I've only had brunch here (salmon/poached egg/english muffin/hollandaise sauce/french fries) but it was a good experience. Â Too many more good restaurants in Carroll Gardens and Cobble Hill to return to this one though.

This is undoubtedly a great meal. I've just never eaten such high end "Korean" food but that's my baggage. The waiter also promptly corrected us, it's not a Korean restaurant it's a french/spanish restaurant reinterpreted by a Korean Chef. So if that concept doesn't sound too complex to you then this is a great place. I had the octopus, the pork rice and wagyu beef steak. I also tried the pork jowl and oysters. Now fried oysters typically arent my thing so Ill leave that off the list but everything else was excellent. The food was well prepared, well cooked with great ingredients. This is not a cheap place, its located in a slightly desolate (ie hard to catch a cab) area of Tribeca and you'll be paying 130+ dollars on the low end. If you think that's all fine, then its a good meal. Just dont think you're having a typical Korean meal.

I liked the restaurant and the overall feel of the place, but I think the staff needs to be more careful with the language they use in the kitchen, because even though it was in Spanish....there were Spanish speaking patrons (myself included) who heard things that shouldn't be discussed at work. Maybe they should make the kitchen a little less open so they can continue their bonchiche.
Ok, yes, it's written Meatpacking all over it, and yes it is fancy and pricy (ouch! the price of wines really hurts)... but the food is amazing.

I live quite close to this relatively new spot and hadn't gone in, in part, due to pretty consistent empty houses on my strolls to the laundromat and because of the somewhat silly name. Just never really crossed my palate radar. Though, I figured last night I would give it a try, and in true TREAT YO SELF fashion, I did just that. I'm not a table for one type of guy, but a coffee table for one person I most certainly am, so takeout it was. Aided by a $10 coupon from Delivery.com I got the Stuffed Root Vegetables (stuffed with ground lamb) which came with chickpeas and tahini yogurt. I also got the Babaganoush, which was probably the best I've ever had (though I only started eating it about a year ago, so my experience is somewhat limited...but still!). So, in summation, silly name but excellent food that forced me to eat all of it at once because I didn't want to stop despite being sorta full. I will be back very soon and will have to work my way through the menu.

Awesome! Awesome!! Awesome!! (Did I say awesome?) We decided to give it a try before the Killers Concert Saturday. A bit confused upon arrival since the old Indian restaurant signage is still up-with the Do or Dine logo (looks almost spray painted) on the weather shutters. Awesome touch though. Since there are small plates we jumped right in... 1- Fois Gras Donut with Berry Jam and Powdered Sugar: God personally came down from heaven and made this FRIGGIN SEXY pastry for us to destroy. Creamy foie inners and an oozing of the jam. Light, fluffy and life altering. 2- Smoked Beef Heart Pastrami with House made Mustard and Gerkins: NOTE-This was the BEST plate of the night. AWESOME!! See for yourself. 3- "Bone, Slugs & Hominey" (marrow, escargot and hominey fritters) with Creme Friache: I was thinking they should have this on special every, "First of the Month." But, a tad bit too hominey-eee. 4- Jerk Chicken and Waffles with Foie Gras and Honey Butter: AWESOME!! I could eat this for breakfastbrunchordinner. 5- Flatiron steak with other things (I was getting a little drunk by this point so I dont remember what it was served with or on??): I DO remember it was tasty and we didn't leave any. The music was AWESOME and very much on point. The Dranks were well executed (Even the alginate sphere shots). Would I go back again? See you there. Quick TIP: Reservations are taken only between the hours of 5-6 and 11-1.

Love love love this place! So very Brooklyn. Â Great ambiance. Â Cute, medium-small restaurant, with seating in the back "green house". Â  For a trendy lil spot, was shocked to find the middle eastern food to be fantastic (grew up eating this food!). Â  Get the baba ghanoush, cucumber yogurt (awesome! very thick, but fresh from cucumber!), and the charmoulla lamb tagine (so tender and flavorful).

I randomly walked by Walter Foods one afternoon and was immediately drawn by the classic look of the front doors and the decor inside. Â I've now been twice for dinner, making sure that I wasn't completely jaded the first time before handing out 5-stars. I'll admit that I got the same main both times (pepper crusted fillet with peppercorn sauce and smashed potatoes). Â I'll have a hard time ever going back here and not getting that same thing. Â It easily rivals any fillet I've had at the big-name Manhattan steakhouses and paid twice as much for. Â If you're a steak lover (especially with peppercorn sauce), you'll love it. As far as starters go, I got the clam chowder the first time. Â I had complained about the lack of good clam chowders in the city (and still do), but this was a solid effort. Â The second time, I got the special salad which was a charred peach, goat cheese, yellow bell pepper, onion, and arugula salad with a lemon vinaigrette. Â It was quite delicious, and I'd highly recommend it if it's an option. Dessert both times was a fresh peach cobbler of which my dad said "I've died and gone to heaven". Â I'd have to agree with him. I was a little worried going back the second time because I had read a few negative reviews in July, but I'm happy to say it was just as good as the first time. Â The wait staff is very good and knowledgeable, the decor is unpretentiously classy, the music is great, the food and drinks are both fantastic - that earns 5-stars from me.

What a great burger. The quality of meat was fantastic, I had the truffle. Our waiter forgot to put our order in so it took nearly 45 minutes to get our food. Once the manager was notified, he came to apologize, they took a percentage off of our bill and gave a us a complimentary dessert. The waiter was awful, the only reason a star was deducted. But Management handled the situation wonderfully. I will go back, and would recommend.

Sweet Afton, you're good! That statement was so unoriginal, but screw you. I'm the one who said it. The worst thing you'll experience is second-hand embarrassment. Sweet Afton bears no relationship with the Afton Alps, and one certainly doesn't experience the wintery slopes in the suburban-urban neighborhood of Astoria. The waitress carries this voice that is a good mix of nasality and breath. I felt comfortable the moment she talked to us. Ordered the Afton Burger, what else? My mind wandered back and forth between the fries and deep fried pickles. I chickened out. Fries, it is. Surprisingly, the fries arrived first. We naturally got excited and our stomachs contracted at the thought of a good hunk of meat. Nope. Didn't happen. Nasal-breathy waitress brought us another basket of fries, on the house which we generously shared with the two lesbians across from us. Gotta love 'em. Rotund and petite at the same time, the burger sated my appetite. The spicy pickles plus the beef? Partay in my mouthay. Sweet Afton, I'm coming after you. And I won't come alone.

Huge tip: Whenever possible, try and order for takeout. My friends and I tried to get in yesterday at noon for brunch but they said that it would be a 3 hour wait. A 3 hour wait!? Crazy. Anyways, the hype is real. We ordered for takeout this morning thanks to the advice of our fellow yelpers and we were able to pick up the food (for four) in 20 minutes. Not bad. The wild main blueberry pancakes were perfectly fluffy and tasty. I really liked the blueberries themselves and the apple/cinnamon/buttery-tasting syrup. Will definitely return again.

Unbelievable Cuban sandwich that is worth the trip alone. Went here on late on a Sunday night so there was no wait which I guess is sometimes an issue with the area being what it is. Service was quick and portion to price ratio was very good. Would definitely come back.

Went here to get a snack after a night of drinking and it was delicious! I got 3 falafel sandwiches: the first one, I made a mistake by putting a lot of the red sauce and man it was spicy! so I threw that one away. And cause it was delicious, I ate 2 sandwiches. Cause I ate it when I was drunk, I went back when I wasn't drunk to confirm the deliciousness. And the verdict is...its still amazing! Small place but its GOOOD! Go easy on the red sauce though~

Absolutely AMAZING. I AM A FAN... A HUGE HUGE FAN. So I would not say I've tried all of nyc's falafels to say that this is the best but I've certainly had enough to warrant a good amount of credibility. I went to NYU, mecca for falafel shops. Mamoun's was just cheap falafels smothered in tahini with wimpy vegetables and a weak pita. Maoz was a once a week lunch because of the unlimited toppings. I've also had University Pita, Olympic Pita, Pick a Pita, Chickpea, Crisp and Pita Express. I may have missed a few new and random ones around St. Marks and University Pl. Oh and the falalfels from the Halal cart up at 53rd and 6th. I was a bit hesistant to come at first because I had always been a big fan of the unlimited salad toppings at Maoz but I read the falafels and pita here were unmatched. I have to say it is very true. You can really tell these are really good falafels when the light crispy balls have to be eaten right away. You can't toast these up again because they immediately lose that quality. Maoz, you can toast up again and they're almost just as good but these have that unique, straight from the fryer goodness. I came here with my mom and were lucky enough to snag a seat by the window. Our order: 1) Green Falafel sandwich with everything - deliciously traditional and flavorful 2) Harissa Falafel sandwich with everything - great flavor with a little heat The sandwich is stuffed to the top with the cucumber/tomato salad and lettuce. The hummus smear is very generous and is so smooth and delicious. If you order it "with everything" it comes with israeli pickles, pickled jalapeno peppers and a s'rug (cilantro chili hot sauce) and amba (mango fenugreek chutney). I loved it. Â I asked for extra s'rug and it really gives off flavorful heat without making you want to cry. It does overpower the taste of the falafel and tahini so try it with and without. I had the wheat pita pocket and it is warm and fluffy. I prefer them much more over the thin and crispy ones. This pita I could eat alone! It's also thick enough to hold all the contents without exploding and becoming a mess. I am jumping on the Taim bandwagon. I can't wait to go again... and again... and again!

While there is often no reason to venture beyond 9th Avenue (Hell's Kitchen) since these blocks are filled with Thai restaurants, bakeries, supermarkets and of course, the nearby Time Warner building, on the oasis of 10th Avenue, it finally got some love from Rex Coffee. This committed cafe is dedicated to serious coffee with its pour over and drip from Counter Culture beans. Best coffee is sometimes best paired with sweets, right? Well, there is a pastry program for your browsing and eating. Â You've got the pain au chocolat, muffins, cookies, and of course sandwiches if you want something substantial to be called lunch. As this requires a bit of walking from the busier area, this would be a perfect location for some quiet time, sip on some high quality caffeinated beverages and engage in some serene moments, must lacking in the nearby Times Square.

People keep giving negative service reviews, but the service here is awesome. I have had the same guy (manager or owner?) serve me every time I come here. Orders come quickly, they are attentive without being int eruptive to my conversation. Coffee gets filled. Turn around and nod for the check, I never once felt like I was waiting for something, and this is when the place was completely full and had two people at most working the tables. One of my favorite spots in this neighborhood. I have had dinner and brunch here.
Typical bar food, we got the chicken strips, chicken wrap and Mac and cheese bites. Probably wouldn't go back again, food was pretty tasteless.

Tried Juni for a client lunch 3 weeks ago and we were both blown away with the quality of food, impeccable service and price! Everything that was served was a work of art and each bite was divine! Deliciousness included: - avocado, prawns (Aussie speak for shrimp) and cucumber blossoms - hanger tenderloin with truffle - deconstructed pavlova? It wasn't called that but that's what it tastes like. I need to find the review that I read that said this would be in the Michelin Guide for 2015 as they were right!

Jane is SO freaking good. I went here for brunch again this past weekend and my girlfriend ordered the Benedict Johnny. I hate hollandaise sauce so I didn't think I'd want to even try it. Well, the Benedict Johnny has roasted tomato hollandaise and it was so good!! Other good things to try for brunch: Â Salmon Scramble and Vanilla Bean French Toast (be warned that the French Toast is HUGE). Â They only problem I have with this place is that their drinks are freaking expensive and I am a huge fan of the complimentary beverage of choice for brunch which apparently you can only get on Sundays. I might just have to go next Sunday!! Â It's really great to sit outstide when it's a nice day out and watch people walk by while you're enjoying your brunch. Â  I've never been here for dinner but I'm sure it's great.

Ordered: 1. Pork buns appetizer- decent for the price. Tasty pork. 2. I don't remember the ramen names but we got their specialty with pork which was good. I liked their ramen better than Shin Sen Gumi which seemed al dente. The thicker than usual broth with garlic flavor was TASTY! I ended up splitting a 2nd order of ramen with my friend for $2. It is added to your existing bowl of broth. Ambiance: Cool place for parties or even a date. Semi-dark..enough light to see everyone and menu, BUT dark enough for a lounge/club feel. Waited for 45 minutes for 2 people to sit at the bar. Enjoyed watching the chefs cook. Didn't eat the cucumber appetizer but it looked tasty.

Its is cute and cozy. The service is very nice. I was excited after reading reviews and ordered my favorites. The garlic and herb shrimp appetizer were cooked to perfection but too little garlic flavor and served in a vat of oil. The Bacon Â Mac and cheese had good flavor but the pieces of bacon were big ( 3" ) Â fatty, flacid, Â & really undercooked in it. The paella was not traditional, no shells etc. But Â we liked Â it alot ! Â The burger was fine. Â .Overall ok but the bill was a bit high for the meal we got and we Â had expected better.

This was a really wonderful meal. My friend and I shared the gnocchi, Di Stefano Burrata and the Fettucine for dinner. Everything was delicious. Gnocchi was amazing!! The decor was really pretty and the rooftop bar was AMAZING!

I went with a party of 5 on a Sunday afternoon. Â We called ahead that morning, asked for one round and one square pie, both plain, for 1:30. Â It was a rainy day, so when we walked in at 1:30 exactly our pies were just out of the oven, waiting for us on the counter. Â Not bad. This pizza is absolutely delicious. Â I liked the square better, for some unexplainable reason. Â The slice was delicious and complex, thanks to the exceptional quality of the ingredients used on each pie. Â The parmigiana cheese that Dom grates onto each slice melts into the bubbly mozzarella - the delicate tomato - and the olive oil drizzled on top and the fresh snipped basil all make this the best slice in NY. Still though, a slice of pizza is just a slice of pizza - and its a difficult thing for a slice of pizza to live up to the hype that is Di Fara.

I don't care if Joe's Shanghai is a tourist trap (my NY friends told me so); the crab & pork xiao long bao here were so juicy & delicious. Joe's Shanghai is a pretty small restaurant. If you don't have a large party, chances are you will have to sit with at least 1 other party at a round table. We tried the crab & pork xiao long bao (juicy dumplings) & the jelly fish appetizer. Both were delicious & reasonably priced. We didn't have to wait for a table around 4 pm but I imagine this place is packed during peak lunch/dinner hours. Service's decent for a very busy restaurant. Gratuity is automatically included. Cash only.
Great pizza. Great atmosphere. Nice location
Great place for breakfast , Orange chicken and broccoli beef Â are one of my favorite. Although they have brown rice , so if you take care of your health , they have smth ))))

REALLY cheap and delicious Japanese katsu and curry. I love this place. If it was closer, I'd be here way too often for my own good. I order the Grand Slam (for only $13) every time, and it could easily be made into two meals, even for me. Sure perhaps not the greatest Japanese curry I've had (Curryya and Sapporo East are arguably better in my mind), but easily the best bang for your buck. Bring friends and come hungry!

As extensive as the menu at this AYCE hotpot joint might* seem, the food selection is actually very limited. They charge additional for almost everything that are the basics of hotpot - IE: Beef Balls. In addition, the service here is extremely slow, and it could take over half an hour to receive the food. Not only is the service slow, the service is also bad and extremely unprofessional. The kitchen/waiters always fail to give you the exact items you ask for, as there are always certain ordered items missing. Even if something is not missing, they don't give you a proper amount. I was with a party of 8, and we asked for ramen enough for the table, and the waiter brought back 2 little ramen blocks. We are not 8 babies, and we were not gonna divide 2 blocks of ramen between 8 people, but that was our only choice, because our second order of ramen took almost 40 minutes. But guys, it's not just the service and all, it's also the food. The food here is not fresh, and even their sauce station is missing a load of items. The broths they have are horrible and bland, and all the meat were beyond frozen. It was as if my beef and lamb decided to trip it to Alaska before arriving at 99 Favor Taste. That's only the hotpot portion of it all though... The BBQ shucks too. Do NOT get suckered into the BBQ. We thought whatever additional few bucks per person, let's try it, and it was a horrible experience. The food did not cook on their useless electric grill. Our chicken gizzard was grilling for over one hour and was not cooked. The usual "kalbi" meat at KBBQ that takes a few minutes to sizzle up also took over half an hour. Our useless waiter blamed it on the AC that we had open above our table. He said it was because we chose to put the AC on high, that the cool air from the AC was affecting our grilling process.... SAY WHAAAT? Well even if that were to be true, why did you guys friggin put the AC above the grill knowing it was going to slow down the grilling? Either way, nothing made sense to me, and I call this place bullshit.

Been here3 times now- twice for breakfast and once for dinner. Â Dinner was mediocre (got a mediocre salad) and very rushed (although understandbly given how crowded it was). Â Breakfast on a Thurs at 8AM was fantastic. Â No wait, superb service (my coffee mug was never empty), cozy atmosphere. Â The pumpkin waffles were excellent (just enough pumpkin spice in the waffles, accompanied by a delicious maple syrup) and the penny egg sandwich with pesto sauce was solid. Â We also ordered a side of cranberry nut toast with cream cheese and nutella... yummm!

In NY we can find almost any food ranging from takoyaki, boureka, Â chocolata con churros, pancit, pao de queijo, injera, palaÃ§inka, arepa, laksa, etc... you name it. However, it took me a while to finally find a place that makes gnocco fritto in NY!! Yay!! Ever since I tried my first delicious homemade gnocco fritto (It's also called "torta fritta") in Parma, I became a fan! Gnocco fritto is basically fried savory dough you eat it with prosciutti/pancetta/culatello/salami/cheese, and it's one of the most appreciated meals in Emilia region. Bianca's gnocco fritto wasn't as good as my friend's nonna's, but for $9 I won't complain! I wish they mix both cheese and meat instead of making us choose one or the other. I tried the tagliolini ai fruitti di mare which was highly recommended by a friend. The overall flavor (tomato sauce based) was good but I wasn't too keen on the pasta quality.... I prefer slighly more al dente. The salmon was OK, it was pretty standard. Bianca is a solild 4 star restaurant considering the quality and price. Because of the reasonable price, the place gets packed even on weekday night. Pros: Inexpensive and delicious, gnocco fritto, fast service, "cozy" Cons: Cash only, no reservations, very crowded and cramped

I can't believe I never knew about this place in Hell's Kitchen! Among a bevy of mediocre restaurants along 9th avenue, Pio Pio is actually a nice place to plan a meal with friends. Firstly, huge space and an undoubtedly great spot for birthday / group dinners. My friend requested to be sat downstairs and I was shocked (as I consistently am in NYC) at how much space the restaurant had in the basement. Extensive list of pisco cocktails, and each one reads like some delicious, tropical paradise. They also have a huge selection of ceviches - we went with the tuna tartare, which tasted incredibly fresh and had this great sesame sauce drizzled over it. For our mains we bit the bullet and went with the Matador's Combo which my friend ASSURED me would be way too much food for the 2 of us and of course she was right. It comes with a whole rotisserie chicken, sides of salad, fried plaintains, rice and beans, and salchipipas (french fries and cut up hot dogs). This is Latin American comfort food at its best, and at $36 a steal. If you're ever bamboozled for dining options in Hell's Kitchen, Pio Pio is a sure bet.

What a hidden jewel. A great idea, Japanese tapas!!! Â The food was absolutely delicious & the staff was exceptional. Â I was in New York celebrating my 44th birthday and was craving Japanese food so we searched & found this little treasure. Â  My mother, cousin and I dined on chicken meatballs, Â chicken with root vegetables, pork tenderloins, chocolate souffle, black cod & a couple of other dishes & they were all delectable. Â The next time I am in New York I will definitely dine there again. Â A must try!!

Really, really nice spot. This is not your typical happy hour bar. It's clean, spacious, and inviting. My internship finished and we celebrated by taking over a large table upstairs, looking over the lower floor. The cocktails are expensive, but strong and tasty. The Good Girl was a pink, frilly flavor experience! The popcorn was delicious, as was the Caesar salad flatbread. To be honest, the drink combined with some Fireball were so potent that I'm having a lot of trouble remembering the minute details. Brotip: The bathrooms are punyyyy! I remember that part.

I was told this was one of NYC's best bars..now i know why. It was only appropriate that i left NYC on this closing note. It was a night for the books. A wonderful experience. I'm appreciative of the staff who situated us in a cozy corner; it felt as if the world was ours and we were the only two ppl there.. Â I loved the recommended drinks, they do know their alcohol. Definitely a great date place, easy soothing music to wrap up the week if you've had a long rough week..music wasn't too loud that you couldn't talk, it was just perfect.. Though i will say the scotch egg wasn't very good at all. I've had these in Hawaii and they made it much better. But other than that, it was simply an unforgettable time at the Dead Rabbit. Interesting name for a parlor, one that i want to go back to again and again..

My go-to midtown falafel spot. Period. I love walking in and seeing all the colors of the food. The folks here are really friendly and know what they're doing. Their pita bread is freshly made before your eyes, dusted with sesame seeds, which totally makes it and elevates it to astronomical levels. Like warm, soft, delicious pillows! Their falafel itself is very simple--moist and flavorful. Fried perfectly. Slap it together with hummus, hot sauce, lettuce, tomato, cucumber salad, tahini and stuff into the pillowy soft pita? You've got the perfect $5 meal that will fill you up and keep you satisfied... All day long. I'm telling you, you'll have the 'most productive' afternoon... aka taking a trip to food coma city. I've also had the bulgur salad, which is very hearty and comforting. I'm here on almost a weekly basis... even tho it's 2 blocks farther than Maoz (which I'm not really a fan of, especially the lines). I'll walk the extra walk for a delicious falafel. Best falafel in midtown. There, I said it.

I love Italian food & I love to cook. Â If you are in any of these groups, this is a must see. Â My friend sent me here on the last day of my first trip to NYC, and it was a great way to end the vacation. Â I later found out this is one of Mario Batali's places (might have ruined it for me before going since I am not really a big fan of his, he reminds me too much of a chef version of Comic Book Guy from the Simpsons). Â  They have any possible thing grocery wise in Italian cooking you could want. The same goes for the food selection. Â There are multiple food bars to cozy up to with seating behind them. I chose the pizza/pasta bar. Â It was amazing. Â I was offered the bread, but I quickly rejected it because I wanted to eat the good stuff. Â I ordered a Margharita pizza and just to fat kid it up, I also ordered one of the fresh made pastas (can't remember the name) but it was on the right side of the pasta menu options and it had short rib in it. Â This was a killer one-two Italian combo. Â I was stuffed and was about to go into a food-coma, but I fought through it to make my flight. Â It was an amazing meal. Â It may have been a $40 lunch (after tip), but it was so worth it. Â Prices were very reasonable in there. Â My bill was so high because I was a pig and ordered 2 entrees. Â I also went to the gellato bar and ordered a salted caramel & chocolate gellato (best gellato I have ever eaten ~$4). Definitely check it out even if you just are looking through the grocery section.
Incredible food. Incredible service. A real experience.

I got there at 5:30 on a Saturday and the line was only about 15 min long, though it took 40 min for them to bring us pizza after we ordered. Really great thin, fluffy crust, with fresh tomato and cheese. And by thin I really do mean thin - by the time the pizza cools, the crust is pretty much soggy from the toppings. This is meant to be eaten right after ordered. All in all, it was a very good pizza - I'm just not sure it merits the long wait times and all the hype.

Heard great things about this place. Â The food is spectacular. Â The pork buns and the chicken buns were delicious. Â  Â The staff is extremely friendly and attentive. Â We had the hirati milk for dessert. Â Nothing I've ever had before but was delicious. Â If you want to have dinner there...arrive at 4:30 instead of when it opens (at 5pm) because this place is a packed house by 5:10.

We ordered take-out and were pleasantly surprised... Friendly staff. Â Not a bad wait for a busy night. Â Definitely a WIERD location, though. Went in- awesome ambience. Â Super stoked to eat in the restaurant next time. Good quality cheese and sauce and crust was crispy yet tender. Â Very good.

I've been dying to try this place since it opened and finally made my way here yesterday. The food was delish. I got the fried pickles and the grilled cheese and sweet tea cocktail. I LOVE fried pickles and these were different than any I've had before - kind of a tempura batter and so tasty. The grilled cheese was perfect and cut in to fours! My fiance was still hungry after his grilled cheese so he ordered the mac and cheese. I was all 'oh i'm too full to have anymore, but i'll try a bite." Lucky for me the waitress brought two forks; I couldn't stop eating it! The ratio of cheese to pasta was fantastic - way more cheese than pasta. So happy to have a cozy bar like this in Astoria. I will definitely be back.
Love!!!!!!!!! Stuffed under $4! Insane!!

Stopped by here for the first time for lunch and everything sounded so delicious! It's a cute truly Italian pizza joint. Beautiful outside eating area. Staff was very friendly and attentive! I got the traditional margherita pizza and it did not disappoint!! So delicious! I wish the sauce was a tad bit sweeter for my tastes but I definitely see myself coming back to try the other pizzas. The pizza is enough for 1 person and not too much there's about 4 pieces for each pie.

Recently took a trip to NYC and Scarpetta was on my shortlist of restaurants to visit. Â This place really does live up to the hype! Â I started out with the tomato and burrata appetizer and it was perfect. Â Loved the flavors and portion size. Â The bartender was great and gave really good recommendations and knew details about every dish I asked about. Â I went with the simple spaghetti with fresh tomato basil. Â This was by far the best pasta I have ever had. Â It was so simple, but executed perfectly. Â teh fresh pasta was amazing and you could tell the ingredients in the sauce were fresh and quality. Â I finsi

An enjoyable 3.5 star Japanese BBQ chain - solid food that lets you get hands on because of the grill but beware this can get pricey. My friend had a Gilt City deal here for $25 for $50. While Gyu Kaku has awesome lunch specials (i.e. the Manager's which is just $10 for a bowl of rice, salad and some chicken BBQ), you can only use the deal for the dinner menu. Â Though, we were kindly allowed to use the deal during lunch - we just ordered from the regular menu. Â You should note that the lunch specials are good though-there were drinks for half off and lots of "lunch happy hour" options for the apps. We ordered : -an app to start: the citrus soaked salmon- very citrus, and very good, thin, slices of semi cooked salmon. 1) Short ribs BBQ which had some soy- didn't eat this as I don't do beef but my friend liked it. They were cut thin and well marinated it seemed. 2) Basil Chicken- green and well doused with basil flavor..love that the grill added a smokey flavor to the meat. 3) Sea bass- cooked and simmered in a red/tomato-esque sauce with mushrooms. This was good- but a bit too little in portion. All BBQ was in the $7-10 range, which is actually overpriced if you think about how little meat you get - the mark up is in the grilling. (i.e. 5 pieces of ribs, 5 pieces of chicken). Our gracious waitress (who was so sweet, minus that she was not on point with the waters) thoroughly explained how the grill works and how long we should cook everything. We had two sides of veggies: garlic spinach (this was good- retained lots of water when grilled but the garlic flavor was good and came out nicely), and the mushroom medley- which was nice when grilled. Got a good sense of the smokey flavor- it was a "medley" of all kinds of mushrooms- shitake, button nose.. mushrooms are always yummy methinks. in the end, I had a good experience at Gyu Kaku and would come back- it'd be fun in a big group. :D
Got the special shrimp n grits! Very, very good. They were also really good about filling our water, which is really important.

You know why hipsters are so skinny? It's cause they eat Diner sized portions. OK,OK I kid, I couldn't help it. Came here cause my friend lives in the neighborhood and the reviews here seem to be great. Even though it was less than a hour after opening, outside seating area was already full (which was a shame cause it was a beautiful day), as was most of the inside. We had to settle for eating at the bar area, which was not a bad thing. The menu is literally a long strip of paper with crudely handwritten menu for the day. Unique, I guess. Our waiter/bartender took our order of poached eggs and a spinach/chicken (or tuna, couldn't remember to be honest) salad and two orange juices (should have gotten the bloody mary's, they looked awesome). Food took almost 20 minutes to arrive, which would have been acceptable given the busy atmosphere, but that attitude took a complete 180 when saw it. The first thing that popped into both our minds was, 'Is this it?'. My friend and I had a feeling this would be the case as we were waiting for our food and glancing at what other people had ordered. We saw the person next to us eating pancakes, which looked amazing and would have made a great side dish. But as small a portion as it was, it was considered a $13 dish. No thanks. Here's the thing, the food was pretty good. Well the spinach salad was OK, not bad. My poached eggs over toast was actually pretty tasty. Both had a mishmash of fancy sounding ingredients which I guess added to it's overall pleasant taste. But everything is completely overpriced for the portion size. Either make it a couple of bucks cheaper (and have an appetizer section) or double the portions (or add more sides to the dish). Our total with tax and tip was $50. That's two dishes and two drinks. Completely and utterly over over priced. The orange juice alone was $10 (one small $4, one large $6). Granted it was very fresh (not store bought, for the price is better not have been). Look, things will not change. This place has a long list of regular customers and people who swear by it. Which is completely fine as it is a very unique establishment in a very young and hip neighborhood. As we both were not fully satiated by the meal, we headed over to Fette Sau and downed some ABSOLUTELY DELICIOUS barbecue.

Yes!!!!! Make sure before you come to Bakehouse, that you get their GiltCity deal because then it makes it so worth it. $50 for 2 people and you 1 bottle of wine, 1 appetizers, 2 entrees, and 1 dessert. I came here with my 3 roommates for a date night and we had 2 of these GiltCity deals. This was everything we ordered with the deal: Red Wine(2): Alright, probably one of the worst red wines I've had. But hey, a bottle is a bottle so I managed to enjoyed it. Mussels Appetizers (4): There were a ton of mussels and the sauce of a mussels was unique and incredibly flavorful. Steak Tartare (3.5): There's an incredible amount of horse radish in this steak tartare so at first bite, it had this really unique tartare flavor, but it got addictive really fast and soon we couldn't stop eating it. House-made pappardelle (4.5): I loved it! I wish there were more serving size wise, because I felt like I could eat 3 servings of it. The pasta was delicious and the mushrooms added into it just made it so much more better. I highly recommend this dish if you're a pappardelle and mushroom lover like me! Fresh Cavatelli (3.5): this dish was really good too. The cavatelli was really good but I'd say it wasn't that special of a pasta dish compared to the other ones we tried. Grilled Organic Chicken (4): Size wise, this was probably the best deal. It was a perfectly grilled chicken that was extremely tender with these sauteed kale that i could not stop eating. Something about the way they sauteed that kale made it to die for. Chocolate Moelleux (4): If you like chocolate, you will probably like this. It was chocolate covered in chocolate covered in chocolate. It was really rich in flavor but chocolate lovers will probably love it. Banana Pudding (4): I don't see this on the menu anymore but I really liked it. The pudding was a tad dense, but it was still really good.

Since moving to 9th Avenue a few months ago, I've tried lots of good places locally but this is the only one that I find myself coming back to again and again. Sergimmo is a little neighborhood Italian deli that seats about 15 that I doubt I'd have ever found amongst all the other restaurants, delis and bodegas along 9th if it weren't for yelp. The Il VIP is quite simply the best sandwich I've ever tasted. Absolutely top notch ingredients prepared in the perfect ratios. The sweetness of the fig spread works perfectly with the salty prosciutto and creamy mozzarella. The bread is also truly excellent - light and fluffy inside with a satisfyingly crispy crust, all whilst being solid enough that you don't need to worry about the whole thing falling apart. Also has decent coffee. There's no table service. Make your order at the counter and have a seat (you pay when you leave) as it can take them a little while to prepare things. Most of the staff are great, on one occasion was given some mozzarella that they'd just finished making to try. One word of warning, it's certainly not cheap (think $20 a visit for a sandwich and drink with tax and tip) but it is worth every last penny.

I went here on a Thursday night to satisfy my craving for some delicious steak. After eating at Landmarc, I was definitely satisfied! I started off with some calamari and French Onion Soup. I liked the calamari better than the soup, it was not too chewy and the spicy marinara sauce was a nice touch. The soup was lacking a little compared to other places I've had it. Then I ordered the Rib Eye with the peppercorn sauce. It was simply amazing. It was cooked wonderfully (I got it medium rare) and the sauce was a great complement. The fries that came with it was also quite delicious. The whole thing was so good I almost ordered another one! To top it all off I got the creme brulee for dessert. Again, wonderful. The only thing to criticize is the tiny portion size of the desserts! The waitress also suggested a great wine that complemented our meal very well.
Thin and sweet crust. Delightful. I had the veggie pie and it was amazing. A big fan.

A wine bar is a place to go to have a glass of wine-not water. If you are going to drink water, choose a different place other than Heidi's. It is a small, cozy neighborhood place like Cheers but much smaller. I love the place and adore Heidi and her husband Ed. They did all the work themselves. The location use to be a dry cleaner and it is unreal what a wonderful comfortable place they created. The cuisine has the same personality as the place itself. Delicious dishes that are warm and comforting like the mac and cheese, the paella-every dish is sensational. I have met many new friends hanging out there. This is just what the Upper East Side needed. An intelligent couple finally created a place we were all looking for but did not know we could find. Accolades to Heidi and Ed!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!.
love this place. great empanadas, their green sauce it's amazing!

3.75 stars. Â I stopped in at L'Artusi during my last business trip to Manhattan. Â First, a disclaimer: Â if this place were in Memphis (where I live) it would get an easy 4-plus stars, but in NYC my standards are higher. The atmosphere is great: Â spacious for the West Village, three different bar areas, comfortable stools, and inviting decor. Â The butter lettuce salad I had was gorgeous, but the generous covering of gorgonzola was overpowering. Â The sausage and pancetta gnocchi was everything I thought it would be (salty, manly, filling), even though it lacked any extra dimension. Â I was pleasantly surprised when the chef sent out a complimentary tasting of his parsnip ravioli, which was subtler and generally fantastic. Â The braised quail was the most disappointing dish I tasted -- a little rubbery and drowned in balsamic -- but the accompanying brussels sprouts were perfect. Â  Don't get me wrong -- I still enjoyed my meal (and the overall experience), but almost everything was just a little off balance. Â Less hammer, more scalpel.

I now have a favorite restaurant in NYC. My friends and I loved this place so much we came twice within three days. LOVED: The bacon-wrapped dates (second time, found out we could just request dates because neither of us is a fan of olives) Spare Rib -- the noodles are some magical beet infusions that are oh-so-pretty and delicious The beet salad -- ridiculously fresh and tasty The Catalan flatbread with the truffles. YUM. Also tried the goat cheese balls in honey and lavender, which I was surprised to find I liked, the sea urchin risotto (probably my least favorite), the sweet potato ravioli, and the almonds (tasty, but not as amazing as the waiter made us think it would be). My only gripes about the place are the inconvenient reservation policy (must confirm on day of), and that the desserts weren't particularly great. But loved the savory food so much that I forgive them. Only accepts AmEx.

+ some if the best restaurant empanadas I've had (and I live in San Antonio = very large hispanic population and food). + large selection + around the corner from Totto Ramen, so when you're starvin' marvin and stuck on the waitlist for a seat in Totto Ramen, you can stroll to Empanada Mamma for a small, inexpensive to hold you over. - wait can be longish around rush times (lunch, etc) - It's located in the NYC and I'm located in the SATX...very long drive for me (1800ish miles) - small dining area

Situated in Red Hook this place is definitely worth the trek. A small intimate space with excellent hosts and food that makes you want to come back you can take a first date, take your spouse, take your parents, anyone will feel welcome and special here. There is an intimate dining room in the back if you have a function or larger group. Or you can sit almost communal style in the main room.

Giovannis is the best. For 15 bucks, the best steak ever. No frills but the warmth and family atmosphere more than make up for it. One of those all-star places that works for family dinners, date nights and brunches with your girlfriends. Love this place!

Hmm...I've been here about twenty times, according to my punchcard. FYI, filling up the punchcard means you get free 'junk,' like plates and stuffed animals, not free food. That disappointed me. Honestly, I don't think the food here is particularly good or memorable, but the four stars are for price, convenience, and variety. Woorijip's just had major renovations, so the place looks less like a cramped deli now, and more like a spiffy buffet...though for some reason, I prefer the way it used to be. Seemed like there was more food then. On to the food: I recommend the rice cakes in the spicy red sauce, and the kimchi fried rice isn't bad either. In general, stick to the spicy foods. The tofu, jap chae, and sushi for instance, tend to be tasteless, at least to my buds. Maybe that's because they're sitting in the fridge. I also really like the glazed sweet potatoes they occasionally have in the back, and recently there's been a weird enchilada/burrito thing with bulgogi that doesn't really taste Korean at all. It has bell peppers and is wrapped in a taco. Enough said.

Spent a wonderful weekend in NYC.This place was great. The food presentation was lovely and the bar as well as the bathrooms were VERY clean. Very much enjoyed the outside bar. I would highly recommend this place and will visit many times over. Heather you ROCK! the best waitress and very efficient.

Maybe I mis-ordered? My pasta with the lamb ragu was good, but nothing special. The prosciutto-wrapped burrata was pretty good, but you really can't go wrong with cheese, in my opinion. Maybe I should have ordered the lobster crepes, like one of my dining companions. Hers looked pretty tasty. I did enjoy our waiter, who kept humming throughout the evening!

I went to Ai Fiori for restaurant week today and it was absolutely amazing. The food was unique and flavorful, the ambiance classy and elegant. The service by the staff was top notch from the coat-check to the waiter. Â I highly recommend this place!

Cafe Orlin is not one of those glitzy brunch places that seem to have sprung up all over manhattan...and that is part of the charm. It has a small outdoor area, but other than there is nothing special in terms of ambiance. I would say they serve one of the better coffees compared to other brunch places and the food was, although nothing stood out, just right. Both tasty and the right portion. For brunch, isn't that all we need? Good coffee, comfort food and the laid back atmosphere. I don't know if it is worth the wait though, because sometimes the line can get pretty long. Service can be a bit slow, especially when the place is full. You would think they would have a couple of extra staff on those sunny weekends to fix this problem. One of those places where if you do visit, you won't be disappointed. But also one of those places you don't really crave for.

Bread [free] 2.5 Cappuccino [$3.50] 3 Guacamole & Chips {1/3 portion} [$3] 2.5 Caesar Salad {1/3 portion} [$3] 1.5 Hanger Steak Sandwich [$12] N/A Less: Failed to deliver Hanger Steak Sandwich [-$12] + FOOD [$9.50 + tax + tip] 2.37/5 Wait time: 5-48 minutes Server lost portions of our orders Rejected Foursquare check-in offer + SERVICE: 0/5 Saturday, March 15, 2014: evening Jovial setting hampered by terrible service. Arrived in a group of 3, and shared side dishes (marked as 1/3 portion). Dim lighting and downtempo music greeted us tastefully. Server took our orders and misheard our request for "just water" as "soda water," but withdrew the beverage after we clarified. Served bread 5 minutes after order and appetizers after 15 minutes. Two entrees ordered by our group (including my Hanger Steak Sandwich) were not served 48 minutes after order. Server claimed we never ordered those entrees when we asked about them. Complimentary bread arrived pleasantly warm with a serving of mildly salted butter. Texture was a bit stiffer than preferred. Cappuccino was topped with a thick layer of froth. Fairly rich and moderately strong. When receiving check, waiter refused to accept Foursquare check-in offer for free large coffee with order because "a cappuccino isn't a coffee." Guacamole and chips were quite ordinary. Guacamole and salsa resembled store-bought mixtures, but chips were crisp and savory. Poor value considering price. Caesar salad was heavy on dressing and light on toppings. Lettuce tasted stale while dressing overpowered every other ingredient. + SUMMARY: No reason to visit with more appetizing and better attended options in restaurant-dense neighborhood

It's good...for New York. Maybe I sound a little snobby coming from SoCal, but it's greasy! I know Chinese food has a reputation of being so, but this was a little much. Also, not the flavors I was expecting. That said, I appreciated the fact that the noodles were handmade. If you're lucky enough to be sitting by the kitchen, you can hear and watch the master chef at work. I went with a few friends on a not particularly busy night, but had to wait a while, and one if our orders was wrong. I heard the chef and hostess arguing in the back, so there must have been some confusion. But it was worth the wait and would definitely come back knowing what to expect.

Gorgeous. Ok, I'm talking about the loungy, upscale decor, huge space and the servers. After hearing great things from a friend who dined here for dinner, I decided to give this place a try for brunch. Â Who can resist a $25 brunch that includes your choice of: -OJ, grapefruit juice, or coffee -Mimosa, Bellini or Pom Cava (think pomegranete juice with sparkling wine) -Appetizer -Entree Not bad, huh? Â Everyone loved my order of the Kashkaval Eggs in Cocotte (truffle infused sunny side up eggs!!!). As for side orders, Â Ililli makes the best grilled beets ever-- you just want eat them forever. Â The fava beans and lamb sausage were pretty good here. Top that off with excellent, attentive service, best unisex bathroom set up and good looking servers, well, what's not to love? Â Only reason why I gave it a 4 instead of a 4.5 or better is that some dishes were ok and the drinks could have been stiffer or better quality.
Hidden Little Gem. There may be long waits but it is worth it for the corn!! Sandwiches are alright! But the Corn is deliciosa~

Excellent draft selection at The Jeffrey. Â Fun crowd and hip decor. Both of my bartenders were Irish - very cool but what's up with that? I enjoyed the charcuterie + cheese plate accompanied by a bucket of tasty bread. The $6 pretzel was overpriced. I would def return to you.

I came across to this restaurant last Saturday and I couldn't believe what I tasted. Their food is so good that I cant stop thinking of getting back right away. Now, I can't stop talking about their tuna tartar w/ Japanese eggplant and the strawberry baby back rib! Awesome place!. Definitely will be coming again very soon!

i have been waiting to check out this place for years. seriously. i have eaten at the NYC version several times but heard the bklyn outpost is really where it's at. we finally ventured out on a recent beautiful weekend and Habana lived up to the expectations. the outdoor area is really fun, bright, and inviting. it was crowded but manageable so we snagged some seats in the shade under a big umbrella then went for some frozen mojitos. these were delicious! a little sweet so i mixed it with some sangria for a change of pace the second round, but overall very good. the food looked and smelled delicious but we didnt get a chance to try. i really loved the eclectic crowd here. and the dj spinning tunes to keep the mood going.

This place is amazing I looove coming here when I'm in the city it's just amazing fine pizza I truly recommend it to everyone that comes out to New York you won't be dissapointed place is small but their pizza is so worth coming in and eating in

It was pure luck that brought us to Cuba in Greenwich Village as we were simply wandering around and felt hungry. Â Delicious, authentic food in a warm environment. The competition in this neighborhood results in high standards and Cuba more than meets them.

I guess there was so much hype about this halal cart that I expected our dinner to be sort of a religious experience. Â This wasn't the case. Â However, pouring your own white sauce is a huge luxury, and the food is quite delicious. Â Definitely make a trip out here. Â Totally worth it.

I didn't have to wait too long since I went right after work. 10 minutes? But after eating here, I think it's worth a wait, at least once. This place is tiny! I remember once I tried coming on a saturday afternoon and there was a massive crowd hovering outside (at least thirty people camping out in 30 degree weather, such troopers). The wait was estimated to be 2 hours.. Be sure to write down your name on a clipboard and run, not walk, past the other couple who is also headed towards the same clipboard. I had the Miso ramen. Broth was very flavorful, cha siu was tender, juicy, mouth watering.. Great stuff. Could have eaten more veggies if they threw it in but I was so satisfied with the broth that I wasn't really complaining. My date got the spicy ramen, which was also great, but more unique. Â One of my favorite things about this place was that as we were eating at "the bar" seating area, we got to watch them stir these huge vats of broth. I know it's compared to Ippudo, but I would say it's a completely different experience. If you liked to be stroked and petted while you eat your bowl of noodles in a room filled with trendy lighting and fancy walls, then go downtown. But if you like a 'bare bones' experience of just ramen, then come here. Honestly, I prefer the more down to earth variety, but to each their own (we are still talking about noodles here, right?). In any case, the ramen is good at both places.

I don't get the hype over Locanda. The restaurant itself has a sexy yet rustic industrial vibe. The service is good, but the food....that is where they lost me. The food is very fresh and you can tell the ingredients are all high quality, but the flavor profile on the dishes I ordered really wasn't anything exceptional. Blue crab crostini - 3.5 stars - very fresh but no wow factor Sheep's milk ricotta crostini - 4 stars - the ricotta and olive oil are delicious and very smooth Tartare - 3.5 stars - very fresh and good quality, but again no wow factor for me Pumpkin angliotti - 3 stars - I love pumpkin so I thought I would love this dish. However I found the pumpkin flavor to be too subdued and a bit overpowered by the balsamic. Overall, this is a decent restaurant with a great vibe but doesn't live up to the hype / crazy competition over reservations.

So this place will piss some people off and make others drool. Â These type of places always do. Â Its good food. Â Real good. Â But the crowds, popularity and oh god, the wait, is really too much. Â I'm lucky I live a block away so I can put my name down in person (they dont do reservations) and go home for the 60-90 minutes normal wait time. Â The sorry people who drive to the spot, in their hummers and maybachs, have to wait outside often standing up the whole time. The pizza is just fantastic and the calzones gigantic - and that pretty much all they sell. Â It's BYOB but the'll serve water or soda if I remember. So here is the synopsis. Â LOTS of people, great gourmet oven baked pizza (with the tasty burned spots too), but a long fuckin wait.
The best ramen in NYC. Hands down... The wait is over 1.5 hours, so only the patient and determined will get to eat here.

This is where I fell in love with buckwheat noodles. Â I used to work close to this tiny place. Â Never actually ate in the restaurant; but I used to order everyday for lunch. Â Its to die for. Â Awesome wonton soups. Â I'm a vegetarian but I hear the pulled pork sandwich and steak salad are great

What a place! Went with my long-time girlfriend, and was taken by surprise. Â The Sangria was excellent, the Margherita pizza and spinach & artichoke dip tasty as can be, and the atmosphere lovely. Â The staff is inviting and attentive, and the location is easily located. Â Go!

I think Lombardi's is essentially a 2 Brothers with a coal oven, excess seating and a hostess with a microphone. It's decent/good pizza though admittedly, I'm no pizza connoisseur. The pie slices I ate didn't seem like anything special to me in comparison to a lot of other pizza slices I've consumed from mom and pop pizza shops in NYC which use gas powered ovens. Anyways, we ordered a handful of pizzas and I decided to be a douche and plucked an anchovy off a piece of pizza from one pie and it was nasty and overwhelmingly salty. In fact, that anchovy was like putting a tablespoon of salt in your mouth. Thinking that I may have gotten a bad piece, I downed some water and tried again later. Wrong move. Those anchovies ruined an otherwise good pizza. My friends...I don't know. They were digging that nastiness and finished the pie. The lower dining area is vastly better than the area on the 2nd level. I felt like I stepped back into the 80's after dining upstairs. Customer service was adequate and attentive. Overall, I probably won't go back again. Sometimes I see lines wrapping around the corner and wonder why people don't just walk over to Ray's on Prince Street or up to 2 Brothers in St. Marks for some $1 slices. They don't accept credit cards either. You would think that being such a big restaurant, they'd be ok with taking a small hit in merchant fees, but I guess they want to stick it to the tax man.

I came here with a bunch of friends at around 11pm Thursday and got the only long table (table for 10) in the restaurant. RECOMMEND Chicken skin - crispy yet juicy, full of chicken flavor - strong taste of soy sauce and salt Tonkatsu Ramen - flavorful broth and chewy ramen Salmon, Mayo, Spicy Cod Roe Mayo - Crispy outside, savory salmon NOT RECOMMEND Beef Tongue - tough and overcooked YOU DECIDE Mini Nabeyaki-Udon - light broth with chewy udon - a lot of ingredients and delightful to eat, but portion is ridiculously small Okonomi-Yaki - very salty, sweet and full of pork flavor - amazing treat after clubbing, but it took a really long time (over 20 minutes) Hit or miss. Just pick the good dishes and Sake Bar Hagi is goood.
Such a cute and quaint brunch place. Â I recommend the French toast and a cup of coffee next to the window.

When NYers are willing to wait 2 hours for food -- you know it's good. I would normally walk away if there's a wait for longer than 20 minutes but the memory of their crunchy, thinly sliced potatoes kept me holding on. Â Props to the owners also for handing us free wine for waiting! Once you're seated, you'll see why the wait was worth it. Â  My friends and I are fans of their grilled sausage and the fried zucchini & eggplant with garlic dip. Â We took a mental note to get the grilled octopus next time because that looked so tasty on our neighbor's table (I get food envy). And of course, the seafood is fresh and tasty here. Â My bf splurged this past weekend and got the Kyclades Specialty for $32 and included HUGE stuffed shrimps, scallops, lobster, crab legs and stuffed fish. Me on the other hand, I'm a land lubber so I always get the chicken kebab which comes with this delicious chilled greek yogurt and cucumber sauce. Â I like to double carb my meals here with rice AND sliced potatoes cause I can't give up on either .. I just love them both (please don't make me choose). Dinner always comes with a free dessert, which (I think) is a Greek custard wrapped in Phyllo dough, so save room!
Great beer, great service, great food! Â Try the Pasta Carbonara...really excellent!

Balthazar is an all-around great place to eat. Â I love having brunch there (their sour cream waffles with berries is absolutely amazing), but this was my first time going to Balthazar for dinner. Â  We started off with king crab legs, which were chilled over ice and seaweed and served with a side sauce and lemon. Â I loved the lemon juice with the crab legs and it was a great way to start the meal. Â We also ordered Brandade De Morue, which is a combination of salted cod and mashed potatoes with lots of cream and roasted garlic, served on toasted bread. Â An interesting combination, right? Â It was really tasty (especially with the toasted bread...carbs on carbs!). Â It's a great hors d'oeuvre and doesn't seem too difficult to re-create. For our main courses, my mom ordered the grilled brook trout with spinach, lentils, and asparagus. Â My mom really enjoyed the fish and it tasted very fresh. Â The asparagus was also really tasty, and the only complaint was that there might've been a little too much vinegarette on the fish. Â  My date ordered the cheeseburger, which was tasty, but I was a little disappointed with the bread. Â I love love LOVE Balthazar bread (seriously, it's the best) but the bread for the cheeseburger was a little too crusty. Â I think the bun should've been softer on the inside (the core) but maybe it was just toasted a little too long. I was originally going to order the duck's Shepard pie, but at the last minute, I decided to order the Saturday dinner special: braised short ribs with mashed potatoes. Oh. My. God. Â My braised short ribs were freaking AMAZING! Â The vegetables (carrots, leeks - possibly, and onions) were all really delicious as well. Â The mashed potatoes were so buttery and creamy and paired well with the short ribs (which were marinated with red wine and then braised. Â The meat literally fell off the bones (I took them home for my roommate's dogs) and the meat wasn't too salty (which is sometimes a problem with braised meats, in my opinion, since you're cooking it with all these sauces for such a long time). Â The mashed potatoes were perfect (not too salty and just creamy enough that you could still taste some of the potato chunks) and the braised short ribs just melted in your mouth. Â Wow...it still makes my mouth water as I think about the dish. Balthazar is such a great place to go after a long day of shopping in Soho, or a safe place to get a great meal. Â It's also a great spot for brunch on the weekends or coffee on the weekdays (it's a celebrity hangout during the week and many celebs/producers have their own tables). Â It's great for a first date (maybe a blind date!) because if you can't think of anything to say, you can look up to the ceiling and mention how quirky the playing cards that are sticking to the ceiling are. Â It's also great for a party because there are so many different dishes for everyone at the table to order. If you want to view my pictures from Balthazar, you can check out my website: gracenotesnyc.com. Â Happy eating!
