Checked out this noodle shop after a stop at Fried Dumpling at Allen Street for dumplings to go with my fiancee, and if not for the noodle neon sign we would have totally missed it. Upon walking in, we sit ourselves at a table (there's one large round table, a few square 4 seaters, and a counter with stools) and looked up to see the menu on the wall. Actually there are 2 menus, a short one in English (consisting of the hand-pulled beef noodles and dumplings) and a longer one in Chinese (which consists of a wider selection of noodles and dishes). We simply ordered 2 bowls of the beef soup noodle and this guy starts pounding noodles onto a steel table which invariably became the noodles in our bowls. $4.50 gives you a hot bowl of fresh handmade soup noodles with chunks of tender beef. The noodles has a chewy consistency yet it is neither sticky, soggy, nor too starchy. I can't wait to go back for more.

My favorite brunch in the entire world. I love house eggs, and I crave nothing more. I come almost every saturday, sometimes saturday and sunday, and alot of the time.. I go alone. I sit in my corner my the window next to the bar.. and I never need a menu. The espresso is very good and close the espresso I have had in europe, and I dont usually drink espresso or coffee, but I always order a latte or americano here because they know just how to make it. The staff is friendly, and low key, and the food never takes long to come. I hope moto stays forever, and I will forever visit moto. Love always.- Mel.

I was there this past Sunday with friends for brunch and like always when I go to Yuca Bar, Â the food is good there eggs Benny (WOW!!!!!!!) Â The place is always alive with good vibes and the staff always friendly and they give great service. What can I say, Â for Brunch it's Yuca Bar for me and my friends...

The restaurant itself is unique and beautiful. Â I had an upstairs table with a great view of all the action at the tables below us. Â From the street it looks like a very tiny little townhouse restaurant but inside it is much bigger and more interesting than you would expect. On a relatively busy weeknight, our five tapas were out of the kitchen and on our table almost immediately. Â Great service but would have preferred a slower pace. Â Our dishes were cold by the time we were able to make much of a dent in them because they were served in such quick succession. The lamb meatballs ($7) were tiny but quite yummy and not too rich. The shrimp + chorizo skewers ($9.50) were also tasty The brussels sprouts ($9.50) and flatbread Â  ($10.50) were just okay. Â  I didn't really see the big deal with either of those dishes and wouldn't order them again. Â Our waitress said that they were very popular and I don't quite see why. Â I have ordered tasty brussels sprouts at several restaurants and these did not stand out. Â Baby octopus was interesting but again, at $12.50 I wasn't too excited. Â  Maybe I would come back here on a date because the space is so unique and the foods so interesting (well, if you like FOAM served with 90% of the Â dishes). Â  My expectations just weren't met. Â  **They only take AmEx and Cash. Â A reservation is essential**

My girlfriend and I tried the Brisket, Ribs & Pork Belly. We've had BBQ from Texas to Memphis to NYC and this place can hang with the best of em. Everything was very juicy, even their ribs, which only use a dry rub were extremely flavorful. However, the seating is picnic bench style which means you will be sharing a table with another group, something most people are not used too. This may even leave you waiting with your food in hand while you wait for a seat to clear. You must go to the counter to receive your food, you will not be served. Bottom line, Food is 4 stars, Atmosphere is 2 stars.

Solid middle eastern food. Nice staff and knowledgable about GF / DF allergies. They were willing to accommodate where they could. If this place is too pricey for you, check out Taim next door- same owners and AMAZING falafel

I am so glad we discovered this place! The food here is simply amazing! I am normally not a sandwich girl, but I would eat a sandwich every day if it's from this place. So far I've tried the meatball parm, mexicano, anthony & son, and their knockout fries, and everything was YUM!! The thing with sandwiches that turns me off is lack of flavor, but this place packs so much flavor into everything!! You place your order at the cashier, pay, grab a table and they bring it out to you. Nothing really to complain about service wise, though I will say our first time here was better than our experience today. Everyone was friendlier the first time we went, today was just "ok," and I'm glad today wasn't our first time. Not that anyone was rude, just the overall vibe we got wasn't the same as our first go. I did notice the staff was different today from our first time. This place is casual dining with great food! Will continue to go back so long as they keep making their yummy flavor packed sandwiches!

DON'T WASTE YOUR TIME AND MONEY After dining here for several years the Owners sold the restaurant. The New Owners are Nasty and Don't Appreciate their patrons. The Waiters are Unprofessional and DO NOT ACCURATELY describe their dishes. When your meal arrives it is quite different than the description and there is no way the Owners will take this into consideration. Â They Expect you to Pay for the meal that was incorrectly described by the waiter and if you would like a different dish Pay for that as well! THIS IS NOT CONSIDERED CUSTOMER SERVICE!!!!! I HIGHLY SUGGEST THAT YOU PASS Â ON THIS RESTAURANT... THERE ARE "MANY "OTHER" ITALIAN RESTAURANTS IN SOHO THAT SERVE BETTER FOOD AND THAT WILL APPRECIATE & RESPECT YOUR PATRONAGE!

We came here because the wait for Root and Bone was over an hour, which turned out to be a very good thing. Â The food and service were excellent, the menu is reasonably priced, and we were seated immediately. Â Our party ordered the sweet potato waffle with fried chicken, farmer's omelet and lemon ricotta pancakes. Â I tried the waffle and omelet, and would order both again - but the fried chicken and waffle was good enough that it would end up being "the usual" if I lived close enough to go here regularly. Â The chicken was both crispy and moist, and the red-eye gravy was rich and tasty without being too thick and gloppy. Â The bloody mary was very good - nothing spectacular, but for $5 I was very happy with the taste, strength and size. Â After the meal we chatted with the owner, who was very friendly. Â Based on what she said we may have been lucky to not have to wait, so it might be a good idea to make a reservation. Â There is enough space at the back to accommodate a couple decent-sized groups - up to say, 8 people, or more if they combine tables.
My official favorite place in the world.
Great taste of south asian cuisine. We had stir fried water cress with malachen sauce and it was delightful. This place is cash only. As it is fairly inexpensive, it should not break your wallet.

Zutto is a pretty basic japanese restaurant with really good buns, specially recommend the spare ribs which are great and fairly priced. Also ate the sashimi and sushi which were ok but not even close to the buns. The service was ok but maybe not the most observative waitresses around.

Aside from the service being slow, the food did not taste nearly as good as everyone here on yelp said it would.. I ordered the fillet Mignon sandwich and my Girlfriend ordered the Duck special. We came out disappointed. I have to say though: the place does look nice and cozy, really nice ambiance to it. I just wish they took as much care about the food quality as they did for the decor

I think I am in love... I absolutely adore this place and would most def come back to try the rest of the menu. Tried the chef's selection (I know nothing special) but it was huge! There was 2 of us and it filled us up pretty good and we sort of regreted ordering another app + entree but it was worth stuffing ourselves full. Tried the veal speidini and it was delicious with the Rigatoni and parsnip side. My favorite would be the parsnip just because I loved parsnips... the Rigatoni was a bit too buttery but had a smooth texture that melted away in your mouth. Sadly did not get to try dessert as we were too full... I love the ceiling!

As the new kid on the block, Monument Lane does a good job of landing itself in the consideration set, but what that set actually is (comfort food? Â gastropub? Â new American?) or how Monument plans to distinguish itself from the competition remains to be seen. My friend and I stopped in for an early dinner a week after the restaurant opened its doors. Â Upon first glance, Monument definitely has the typical West Village, cozy, farm-to-table decor down (accompanied by the requisite servers in plaid shirts), and the service was pretty good. Â Monument also seems to welcome feedback as they present your bill in a little notebook where guests can leave comments/doodles; hopefully the staff actually focuses on the comments and not the doodles. We started our meal with the whole wheat pretzels with gouda dip (an appetizer I don't see very often; liked the dip). Â We then moved on to fresh ricotta fennel with lemon and grilled half artichoke (I was a fan of both) and ended with the spice-crusted lamb sirlion with rosemary barley and English peas (very satisfying, loved the barley). So while the food itself was a rare 4 for 4 for me, my memory of Monument Lane is unfortunately dominated by two incidents: our server telling us that their tap water is thrice-distilled and that they couldn't offer the dessert we wanted because the chef wasn't satisfied with the day's batch of it. Â Yes, there is such a thing as TMI. I have Monument Lane on my list of restaurants to revisit once they've figured out what direction they want to push in and what's actually worth focusing on.

I wanted to like Jane, but I have to admit I was disappointed. The service was great, our waitress was very nice and when we had trouble with an uncooked dish, the manager was quick to help take back everyone's dishes to keep them warm while we waited. When they returned with the warmed and further cooked dishes, they also brought out a plate of gnocchi, which is always a nice gesture. Â  However, dinner was mediocre, from the salmon and avocado tar tar to the pork chop and soft shell crab. The dishes had very little flavor. Points should be awarded to the cocktails though: the raspberry mojito was very fresh and went back easy. So easy, we barely cared about the uncooked meat that had arrived earlier.

Friend raved about the wonton and noodle soup here so we decided to head here for lunch after a late night out. Key words: late night out. So... this review may be slightly biased due to nausea BUT I was a fan of the wontons bulging at its delicate seams with meat and the soup was delish. There was about a five to ten minute wait because every table at the place was packed. Will update after eating again sans nausea.

3.5 stars. Came with a group of 10 and ordered the pork shoulder (in advance), pickles, corn and several orders of buns - BLT and normal. Â  The pork shoulder was a thing of beauty when it arrived at the table. Â I didn't expect it to have so much meat. Â We had tons of leftovers, which they wrapped to go. Â I wasn't 100% satisfied, but I probably should have used more ssamjang (red paste) on each wrap as it wasn't that spicy.

You MUST try this place's Banh Mi! It is by far the best Banh Mi I've ever tried in my life! I especially love the BBQ pork and chicken Banh Mi! The BBQ pork one is only $4.25 whereas the chicken is the $4.75. That is still cheap! If you had to decide on which to get I'll get the BBQ pork! I always get the spicy because I love anything spicy! I am crazy cause on top of getting spicy, I put sriracha in my Banh Mi too! The Banh Mi is so filling, I usually get one half for lunch and then the other half for dinner because I can't finish it! They put a lot of ingredients in it! It's so worth the money! GO GIVE IT A TRY AND YOU'LL FALL IN LOVE!

I came here because I'm currently on a mission to find as many good Buffalo Wings spots as I can in NYC. Â  Bonnie's Grill's menu stated that their Buffalo wings come in 10 or 20 pieces with a choice of medium, hot or hotter sauce. Â I love my spicy stuff really hot so when it was time to order, I told them "give me the hotter wings or whatever is the hottest that you have. " The server looked at me and asked have I ever eaten their hottest wings before to which I replied no but I can eat really hot stuff. Â He looked at me again and said that he thinks I better stick to the hotter sauce that is on the menu. Apparently there is a another hot sauce that they serve that is so hot that they keep it off the menu. Â Ohhhh, secret menu stuff. Â That's so neat. Â Wonder how many people knew it existed? Â Now I just had to try it. Â  The server was apparently worried about my safety. Â Aww, awfully nice of him. He gave me a small sample of the off the menu sauce and I guess he expected to see me cry or tear up or something. Didn't happen. Â The way the server explained it to me, most people that ask for really spicy finds out that they can't handle it. Â When I told him it was bearable after tasting the sample, he then proceeded to make the hottest wings that they had for me. The wings were very good. Â Crispy on the skin and moist where the meat was. It was also not too salty which some Buffalo Wings tends to be. I liked the secret sauce that they gave me but I must warn everyone it's a lot hotter then what most people could stand. Â Definitely ask for a sample of the sauce before ordering the hottest off the menu wings. Â Not as good as my beloved Pluck U's Buffalo Wings (although their hottest sauce is even hotter then Pluck U's death sauce) but it's close. Â  The cheese that they used for the dip is disappointing. Â Instead of a blue cheese dip, it tasted something like a very thick mayo sauce with a small hint of cheese in it. Â  I also ordered fries on the side and have to say they were delicious. Â Shoe string style with a nice crispy skin and soft interior. Â I ordered the small order and even that amount was so much fries that Â I couldn't finish it. The place is pretty small. Â There is a long counter space right in front of the cooks that takes up half the restaurant. Â The rest of the space is taken up by what I remember to be nine small 2 customers tables which they mix and combine for larger groups. On my way out they told me that the next time I'm there, just remind them I was able to handle their hottest Wings and they will make it for me. Â Yep, I definitely would. ********************************** Heat level of the hottest buffalo wings from a scale of one to five, five being the hottest. Â 5

After having been to Xixa multiple times, I was dying to try Traif. When I finally went, it completely lived up to my rather high expectations. Since there were three of us, we opted for the chef's tasting menu, which at only 45 dollars per person, is pretty reasonable. For that price, you get about 10 small plates to share plus two desserts. You can request a couple of dishes, but the rest will be the chef's choice. We got the following dishes: --sweet potato soup (amuse bouche) --tuna tartare with eggplant tempura --salad with apples and cheese (can't remember which kind) --prawns with Texas toast --baby back ribs --pork belly --fois gras with egg and bacon --skate cheeks --pan seared scallops --short rib sliders --spaetzle with rabbit --vanilla panacotta --bacon donuts Of those, my favorites were the pork belly, scallops, and short rib sliders (and I'm not even a meat lover most of the time). My least favorite was the skate cheeks because it was prepared kung pao style, which I'm not a fan of. Everything was really good, though. We had a reservation because it was a Friday night, but we just got it day of, so my feeling is you could probably wing it and go without one, especially on the early side. I'm sure I'll be back here soon!
You want corn? This is the perfect place for you! The food is ok, not my favorite but the corn is the best thing on the menu!

It smells wonderful in here and it's probably freshest pizza in this part of town. Evenstill, it's nothing to write home about. If anything, go here in the evening just for the lively atmosphere of the unpretentious sort - hey, it's hard to be snotty when you're noshing on pizza.
Cheeky Sandwiches was delicious. Fluffy biscuits, creamy gravy & perfectly cooked fried chicken. All cheffed up by a sweet guy with massive guns! Go, eat and enjoy!
Good taste, really a nice place to go and try Chinese food! Â Remember to make a reservation before you go cuz it's hard to get the place immediately!

If you're reading this review, you probably already know about the awesome red, white & blue oyster special. So I'm not going to tell you about that. You don't need me to tell you that it's the real reason to hit Fish up, or that the fresh Bluepoints are so huge that you actually need two bites to finish some of 'em. I'm also not going to tell you about how the waiters might unapologetically drop things all over you if you make the mistake of sitting near the kitchen door. Nor am I going to mention that the tuna burger was dry and mediocre, but that the fries and the no-joke wasabi sauce are awesome. I thought about it for a second, but I decided it wasn't necessary to report that the Angels on Horseback (bacon-wrapped oysters with horseradish AND cocktail sauce) are intense, but can't be bad if you like all of those things. What I REALLY want to tell you about is the woman who was having a complete and utter breakdown in the doorway. It was frightening, mesmerizing and a little bit funny, all at once. But on second thought, I'm a little bit sick of you being so nosy. Mind your own business.

Weds nights. $2 sangrias (in a nice large mug) $1 montadito (ie. small sandwiches) Wanna how to rock this place like a pro? 1. Arrive fashionably early. I suggest 430pm. 2. Grab a table. 3. Write down your orders. They provide a stack of paper to write your orders on. Get a sangria (either red or white) and a bunch of montaditos and appetizers. 4. Line up and order. The line gets long later on, so order as much as you can. I recommend buying at least 3 cups of sangria. 5. Pick up sangria. 6. Return to table and drink like a fish. 7. Wait for them to announce your name so you can pick up your sandwiches. 8. If you are still sober and hungry, repeat steps 3-8.
My favorite Malaysian place in town! Delicious noodles and soups. They're roti is the best. Remember to bring cash as they don't take cards.

The food is pretty amazing here, and I've never had a bad experience. Service is also great, and they always give a lot of ban chans (side dishes). Although it is kind of pricey compared to some other Korean restaurants, they give you big portions so I would advise to go with a lot of people. Great drink selection, and if you order take out, they have amazing and reasonable lunch specials! I'd say it's one of the best Korean restaurants in NY. No joke. I grew up eating a lot of Korean food, and I have to say that their food is pretty legit. There's a wait most of the time so I would try to arrive early, but I'm really lucky because I basically live one block away! Yay!

The decor was mainstream. For brunch we ate pasta and egg Benedicte with extra salmon on it. The salmon was watery and the pasta was over cooked. The staff was not very helpful. It was an overall bad restaurant experience.

When you first walk into Sea Witch you'll find yourself in a small space with a walk up window and a menu along the wall with a number of great looking options from a clam roll, and schnitzel sandwich, to hamburgers, and fish tacos ($7-14) . Great if you want to get some food to go or to take it into the bar. If you don't want to wait they have those buzzers normally found at places like Applebees, the perfect solution to grab your first frink and head into the back yard if it's nice out and there's room. If you want to see the most beautiful and creative back patio of any bar in the city, look no further than Sea Witch. They've transformed the space with a number of seats on a bed of rocks complete with some natural appropriate plants, a koi pond, and a little stream, it's very well done. Lighting comes from a few strands of lights and a old school looking lantern at each table. It almost feels as though you're out in a campground. In addition to the back yard the bar has the coolest bar stools I've come across as well as a large fish tank along the back wall. The fish tank could definitely use some work but it's still a great feature. Prices are quite reasonable with beers starting at $4 (most are 6-7). I'll definitely be back to try some of the food and take advantage of that back patio again.

This is an awesome, awesome place. They sell everything - fresh pasta, gelato, ice cream, 100 types of olive oil, sauces, salt, blah blah blah. It's a little pricey but the ambiance is great. 3 things: 1. The fresh pasta can't be refrigerated for more than 3 hours. You can freeze it though. 2. The layout is crazy and a mess when it's crowded, I got lost a lot. 3. The wine store's entrance is from the outside and you can't get to it from the inside.

I never knew there were such things as Spanish sandwiches, my experiences of European sandwiches limited to bratwurst and double-crust pizza. The store itself is beautiful and just a pleasure to walk around and sample the numerous cheese, ham, olive, and oil samples and admire the cases of products. The sandwiches themselves have so far been great, and not particularly pricey for a fancy sandwich. Someday I'll man up and try the $25 ham sandwich, but the $8.50 chorizo and manchego sandwich is satisfying enough. Great bread too. There is a small seating area if you like sitting on stools. Otherwise, my plan has been to order, eat all the samples, then take the sandwich to the park or back to the office.

I used to love this place when I lived in Brooklyn Heights 10 years ago. Now the quality has declined and it's a crowded tourist trap/become a chain with multiple locations. The pizza is still good, but not like it was not and worth the wait (which used to be much shorter) anymore

This is not often said, but a very big shout out to the Mexican chefs who throw down in kitchens across NYC, Little Owl included. In glancing at the kitchen, every single cook was of Latin American descent. And they were killing it behind the stoves. These guys whipped up one of the most delicious pieces of halibut ever. The corn and pesto sauce surrounding it were SO delicious. It was simple, filling and light. I would happily reorder this in a heartbeat. The pork chop was a heavy portion, but incredibly savory. The restaurant was nice enough to split the portions for my boyfriend and I. For dessert, the beignets were .... Meh. I made up for this satisfactory choice by ordering the warm chocolate soufflÃ© with espresso ice cream and GOLLY was that the right dessert decision! The ice cream was like a great cup of coffee and the chocolate was rich. I wanted to pick up the plate and slurp the remnants. After said halibut, pork chop, soufflÃ© and beignet, I had to smile as I walked past the kitchen and heard a chorus of Spanish phrases and Mexican slang. Hats off to these guys!

I'm not going to go into great detail because the other reviewers have pretty much wrote essays and covered everything. Just go try it! They have an awesome selection of meatballs (and I wasn't even a fan until this place) plus the ambience is super chill.

I really cannot say enough. Â This restaurant was absolutely outstanding. Â We had the chefs tasting menu which I definitely recommend. Â The staff is incredibly friendly, knowledgeable, and helpful(we had Ben and Joel who were outstanding). Â The food was utterly amazing. Â I'm literally just finishing my dessert and the entire experience here has been as absolutely amazing an experience as I can ever have had. Â I ABSOLUTELY LOVE THIS PLACE!

Star rating is for the food only. Customer service rating would tank my review. (more on that in a few) Met up with a friend for a sunday brunch, we were seated fairly quickly (which was nice). Â Both ended up getting the smoked sausage scramble. Â While not mind blowing, it was not horrible either. Just meh. ok. mediocre. Â The mashed potatoes were interesting. Pretty tasty actually. Â There were other things on the menu that actually sounded promising. (Like the pancakes, the table next to us ordered them, and they look pretty damn good.) Anyways, on to the real reason for my review: the horrible customer service. Like other reviews have stated, this place is tiny, and packed. So that being said, we knew that the one waiter working the place was super busy. Â So we figured we'd order our food AND drinks at the same time. Â And we did. But when my friend asked to get a coffee AFTER giving our food order, the dude rolled his eyes and said in an exasperated zone "That's what I just asked you.". Â Sorry, but no. You don't ever roll your eyes IN FRONT of a customer, nor do you turn give attitude to people who were nothing but pleasant just because we skipped over the "what you would like to drink" part of your speech, especially considering we said we were ready to order. We really should've just walked out right there. But we didn't cuz we were hungry and we were already seated and ordered. So we got our food...nom nom nom. No coffee ever came out. And then we asked for our bill - surprise surprise, coffee listed on the check.

Ok. Just get a beer at the bar. Beautiful view. Not expensive. However I made the mistake to eat here. 1 1/2 hour wait. Sit down and are told that about a third of the entrees are not available. Food mediocre and really expensive for what it is.

It was rainy yesterday but the meatball shop was unbelievably packed. Seeing this, I was excited. I arrived late so I didn't have to wait but the wait time for my friends was about 30 minutes. Two of my friends ordered the hero special (Mediteranian Lamb), my other friend and I ordered the spicy pork naked balls with mushroom gravy. The spicy pork and mushroom gravy was fantastic, it was truly delish. However I can't say the same thing with the special, I think the bread and balls combination they made is blah. The bread itself was hard to chew, the spices in the special meatballs were too strong. I felt I was smoking cumin. But not all is bad in the hero combo, the salad that came with the meal was refreshing and finger lickin' good - I know, it's just a bunch of greens, sue me. I love the dressing and the freshness of it. We ended the meal with an ice cream sandwich espresso flavor with special cookie (chocolate cookie with mint on top) and chocolate chip cookie. I love the special cookie but I may be partial since I love chocolate mint. The ice cream was just ok though my friends love it and the other cookie was not memorable - I had better. The atmosphere was definitely not something I enjoy, we could hardly talk to each other since it's so loud and crowded. But who goes there for the ambiance?

I like the Tunisian version if middle eastern food. La Goulette is a new addition to Williamsburg. The restaurant is clean, has great Arabic music, really nice employees, and good food. The hummus is very thick, yet flavorful. The hummus and chicken shawarma have great taste and balanced spice. There are numerous vegetarian options, salads, baba, hummus, tabbouleh, falafel, etc... If you need suggestions this is a good place to be more adventurous.

I made a reservation on a Thursday evening for a group of 10 friends to meet for a glass of wine. Â I recommend a reservation for a larger group, because the last time we tried to go without a reservation, we were turned down due to lack of room to accommodate us. Â I arrived 20 min before our reservation and was led to the area in the back with couches and low tables. Â Only 6 friends showed, but unlike other restaurants that constantly hound the customer if their entire party doesn't show up, I experienced excellent, prompt service. Â We all sat around and enjoyed our wine without any badgering. Â It's a cozy spot for a glass of wine- I'd like to try the tapas next time!

I've always been turned off by the line at Artichoke, especially because it's pizza and waiting in line for pizza reminds me of my college days when I was broke and so when I graduated and found a job I vowed never to wait in line for a slice of pizza ever again.... Until my boyfriend consistently asked if we could try Artichoke, "is tonight the night, darling?" to which I consistently replied "no, hun, you're not getting any tonight... Artichoke pizza I mean" but after many months of asking (pleading) I caved in last night since the line was short and I was in the mood for a snack. So we waited in the (short) line and received a HUGE slice of artichoke and spinach pizza for $4. Â It was delicious! Â I didn't think the cream of spinach "soup" was runny at all and though there wasn't much artichoke in the pizza it was absolutely yummy because they don't just add the standard mozarella, I'm pretty sure there was a ton of parmesan cheese in it too. Â Anyway, I was pleasantly surprised and will be goin back to try the other flavors (crab, margarita, sicilian). Needless to say, I am now a fan which might be a problem since I still refuse to wait in line for a slice of pizza (this one time was an exception). I guess I'll start sending the boyfriend since it's his fault I got into Artichoke anyway. :)

The pork buns are delicious. Overpriced, but very savory. I ordered the Akamaru Modern as a suggestion by my friend. It was tasty, but not nearly as good as Minca's ramen. The pork was too hard/tough and the noodles were too soft. On top of that, it was not a cheap meal. The hostess was snarky as hell but the waiters were pleasant and attentive. In general, it was good but overpriced, I would go to Minca over Ippudo.

Ordered the chicken sandwich and the beef sandwich so my best friend and I can share. The chicken sandwich was the size of my palm and smelled delicious. And it tasted amazing, the chicken was moist, very flavorful and the biscuit was rich and buttery, melted in my mouth. The beef sandwich caught me by surprise, the flavors were very interesting. You can taste a few different flavors going on all at once, nothing like I've ever had before. The bread reminded me of french toast. I will definitely return again and recommend this place to others. *This place is kind of hidden, I almost walked past it without knowing so keep your eyes wide open!

Yesterday was the first time I had ever tried Tibetan food. Cafe Himalaya is decent. The food portion is small and it's nothing special. The reason why this place would get 4 star is because it's BYOB and the food is CHEAP! DIRT CHEAP! Each person would roughly pay around $10 including tips and tax for a dinner meal. Plus its BYOB, what can go wrong? My gfs and I were at Cafe Himalaya for about 3 hours and we brought 2 bottles of wine and the service was great!! If you love BYOB and NO CORKING FEE and CHEAP food... then you must check this place out!

Just went there tonight. The food was just ok, nothing worth writing about and definitely not worth the 2 hour wait in the summer time. The 1 star is for the waitress who spilled my entire beer on my lap and on my friend's shoe. She was apologetic and I told her it was okay. She got me another beer but didn't have the common sense to comp that beer. Not only do I smell of old bay but also stale beer.

My wife and I looked for a place to meet with an old friend who was in from Cleveland. I selected Caffe Linda since it was in close proximity of his hotel. We were treated as guests not patrons. The food was fresh, well prepared and delicious. I had the special of the day, the Branzino fish filet which was perfectly cooked. The room tends to be very noisy when full so if you're looking for a quiet place this may not be for you. But the service and food made up for the loud ambiance many times over. I'll go back again no doubt.

Even IF Prosperity has better dumplings (it does), it's still not enough of a reason to not give it five stars. As a place to eat, Vanessa's has a few things going for it that Prosperity does not have. Â Adequate seating is one, a less intense ambiance and friendlier atmosphere helps round it out as a more comprehensive eating experience. Â I also believe that they have a slightly more expansive menu. Either way, the food is REALLY good, even if the dumplings aren't the best on the street, and it's cheap. Â DEFINITELY worth trying at least once.

cheap alcohol. (delicious) vegan options. casual atmosphere. friendly and knowledgeable staff. THE place to take out of town family, or friends. Unfortunately, if you don't make a reservation, you'll end up waiting about an hour for a table. Usually, it's worth it. If you're starving, go next door to NANA.

The service at the restaurant is top notch, everybody is extremely attentive to your needs and you do not feel at all rushed which is always a good thing. The asian bar tender could try to be a little more friendly - maybe he was having an off day. We ordered the monkey bread followed by the duck and suckling pig for mains. Overall, the food was nicely prepared. The pork was cooked to perfection, the duck lacked a little in flavor. I felt the sauces for the meats were too bold and over powered everything else on the plate. My biggest complaint about the food is that they over salt absolutely everything: the bread, the meat, the sauce, the seaweed butter was completely inedible. I feel like I received a week's worth of salt in that one meal.
Decent food - what's the big deal ? As for the pastries, man do American get them wrong !

My friend and I ended up here on a whim on a Sunday evening when the movie we were hoping to go to at a local theatre was sold out. Like some believe, everything happens for a reason because wow, this place was an amazing way to cap off the end of a great weekend. We walked into a dimly lit, comfortable, ambient not-so-hole-in-the-wall atmosphere. The waitstaff greeted us, telling us to sit where we would like. We both ordered the house red, which was a 2011 Vrabel (a wine that I was unfamiliar with). It was amazing and for $8 a glass, it was a good deal. We ordered the Crazy Baba, a Babaganoush with feta and basil, for an appetizer, which was amazing and I highly recommend starting with it. The pita bread that arrived with it was the perfect dipping agent. For dinner, I ordered the Fatoush salad, which the waiter kindly commented, "If you're hungry, I would get something else along with it" (which I'm thankful for because I was hungry and the Fatoush wouldn't have been enough). The Fatoush was awesome, fire-roasted onions, tomatoes, feta, and all. As a compliment, I also ordered the Falafel appetizer and OMG the falafels were FANTASTIC! Perfectly cooked with a crispy outer crust and velvety soft inner. My friend ended up ordering one of the special entrees of the night, which was a salmon dish that she absolutely loved. Besides the great food experience, the service was perfection. Our server was very charismatic and dedicated to making our evening as good as it could be. Side note: the background music is quite enjoyable and not what you would expect for a middle-eastern restaurant (The Weeknd's new album). So that part was obviously pretty cool, too. All in all, ZiZi's is a great addition to the williamsburg food scene and totally worth a visit (or two, or three, or four....).

Despite some pretty constant changes in management and wine list, this place never disappoints. Â The food has remained consistent across three or four managers in the last year, and even as the wine list and availability is changing, there is always something new and interesting to taste. Â Ian the bartender is one of the best things about the Upper West Side, and it is a great treat to be able to occasionally watch some major sports event without having to stand in a crowded bar drinking beer. (love my beer and college football, but sometimes it's just not what you're in the mood for, ya know?) Â My husband and I particularly love the "salad pizza" or Vegetarian flatbread if you want to get technical, and the option to add perfectly cooked flank steak to most options is great!

LAZY WAITRESS, DISAPPOINTING MANAGEMENT, SKETCHY CHECK PRACTICES...GONE DOWNHILL Last summer, my friends and I came here a least a dozen times and always had a great time. Â We prepared to re-initiate that trend last night and unfortunately had such a horrible experience that we will never be back. Rather than go to a real mexican place on Cinqo de Mayo, we came here, where they serve some mexican food, precisely because it wasn't crowded. Â They did have signs up all over saying "Come celebrate Cinqo de Mayo at Cowgirl Seahorse" so it seems they at least expected that they could be crowded. Â After waiting at the bar for 10 minutes for drinks that never came, we decided to just sit down and order drinks at our table. Â  We waited another 10 minutes for our waitress to come over to our table and bring menus, another 10 minutes for her to take our order, and another 20 minutes for her to bring us part of our drink order. Â I think I did not have my first drink (except for a bucket of hot-warm coronitas) for an hour. Â In the meantime, my friend saw her mango margarita sitting up on the bar for a good 15 minutes before it was brought to her (sitting at a table no more than 10 feet away from the bar). Â We had similar odd service throughout the meal (we were never brought plates, so forced to eat off our napkins and the waitress was MIA the whole meal). Â Two and a half hours later, we are done eating and the four of us were getting ready to leave when 2 friends who were meeting up with us walked in the door. Â We had them sit down and they each ordered a drink and we asked for our check at the same time. Â The check arrives (before the drinks) with 20% gratuity added. I dispute this (not only because service was HORRENDOUS), but because the menu says 20% gratuity added for parties of 6 or more, and we were a party of 4 until about 2 minutes before that moment. Â The waitress says "well you are a party of 6 now." Â I asked to speak to the manager who, rather than appreciating the issue, said "well if its a problem, I'll take it off." Â Are you kidding? Â Yes, of course it is a problem. Â Oh, and on top of that, she had charged us for drinks we never ordered, and one of the last drinks we ordered was wrong. Â The manager came over with a new check, and blamed the problems on a slow bartender. Â I can appreciate that, but if that is the case, a good waitress is present, explains the situation etc. Â Such was not the case here. Â Frankly, she struck me as a lazy model who had no interest in working hard. Â And, I was less than impressed by the managers' people skills. Â On top of it, we had to have the bill amended again because the last drink order was wrong, and taking the 8 dollar drink off the bill only brought it down by $1. Â So we are convinced there are some shady practices going on, but didn't have the energy to figure it out (in fact, I would always recommend checking your credit card receipts from here...I did have an issue here last year where I was overcharged on my cc bill)....shady.
Have to order a full pizza so make sure you go with friends! So delicious and reasonably priced!

This place is entirely inconsistent. Â I never write YELP reviews but the fact that their people never apologize for being 2 hours late is just entirely unacceptable. Â Not only was my food late with no-second thought but it was cold and soggy by the time I received it. Â Not worth it do not waste your time.

Good restaurant. Â The food was very good but I didn't feel that I experienced it enough by getting the 3 course dinner. Â If you have time, do the full tasting menu. Â Also, get the cheese as your dessert because they give you all types of good pastries/treats from the chef. Would definitely return.
It was too full on a Sunday night, but the food was great! We ordered two pizzas, all of them were very good.

This place is the best! Wonderful and unique food with an ever-changing menu. I live down the street and am so glad they're in the neighborhood. I've had most of the menu at this point and it was all great. The beet salad has this delicious whipped goat cheese and candied walnuts. The carrot soup is really rich and creamy. The burger and fries is also to die for. I also come here regularly just to drink at the bar. The decor (including some amazing art in the front room) is pleasant to be around, it's never too loud and the bartender Johan (I hope I'm spelling that right) is an awesome, funny dude. They always have a nice variety of beers on tap. Right now the Southampton Double White and the Ithaca flower power are particularly good. All in all, definitely go and you won't be disappointed!

Moist moist glorious balls of meat covered in sauce with a limp piece of bread is what you get when you order the Naked meat balls. At a little less than 2 dollars per ball, I was hoping this place meets the hype and it did. Having ordered both the Basil Pesto and Spicy Meat sauce versions I have to give the edge to the pesto. The pesto gave the meatballs a unique salty flavor while the nuts in the pesto provided a nice crunch. The Spicy meat sauce tasted ordinary, not bad but what you would expect from a meatball. I would imagine this to be great drunk food, get at it yelp. p.s the super long answering system for the phone is annoying, I waited so long that I thought I was calling for tech support.
A friend of mine brought me here. He loves it! I am ok. So... you decide.

I felt a bit weird going to a tour- guide-touristy-famous-for pizza joint, but I am glad we came. For your pizza, you pick your base and add your toppings, with the option of small and large. There are salads and calzones as well, but you come for the pizza. They have beer, wine, and sangria. But surprisingly, they do not have dessert or coffee. A bit strange for an Italy place, but it's NYC. The service is efficient bordering on rushing you outta there and it's cash only. Overall, tasty pizza. But I'll probably pass on going again.

After my negative review, I received a message from the owner, Sean. Sean offered a sincere apology and asked for more info regarding my bartender so he could address the correct employee. I feel bad giving such a harsh review based upon one poor employee's actions. Sean offered me a 2nd shot at his establishment; unfortunately I am home in LA. Next trip to NYC will have me stopping in the District Tap House. Any owner who cares this much and has the beer selection District Tap offers, Deserves a second chance! Thank you Sean!

I really wanted to like this place, because it's so close to my apartment and it's open 24 hours, but unfortunately, my experience today left something to be desired. The hubby and I decided to try this place out for brunch based on yelp and reviews from friends. I was really excited about the prix fix menu especially. For $16 you get 2 drinks, as well as coffee, tea or cocoa, and an entree. Pretty sweet deal. However, once we were seated (around 11am), we realized that they didn't start serving alcohol until noon on Sundays. Ummmmm what? One of the reasons brunch is so popular is BECAUSE it's the one time it's acceptable to drink alcohol before noon (and I'm only half kidding about that). I mean, I'm sure it's some kind of liquor license thing, but still, that's just silly to me. I didn't want to wait an hour just to get drinks, so I decided to forgo the prix fix and just ordered an entree a la carte. I settled on the Zucchini, tomato and ricotta frittata. Honestly, it was pretty gross. Not only did it look really unappealing, but it also tasted like crab/fish. Note: neither crab nor fish are ingredients in the fritatta (as far as I knew). I'm assuming it's because the skillet in which they served the fritatta once held some kind of seafood, but it definitely turned me off to the whole thing. The potatoes that were served on the side however, were pretty tasty. My husband ordered the steak skillet which he seemed pretty happy with. My other qualm with this place was the service. It wasn't the best. It wasn't horrible either, but it just was really inattentive. I don't think the server ever even asked me how my food was, because if he had, I probably would have mentioned that it tasted like fish. Also, when we were done, we asked for a box, the server boxed up our food.........and then we stared at him for five minutes with nothing in front of us, before I finally asked him for the check. I mean, I would think the whole asking for a box thing, would have maybe given him a clue that we were ready to go, but whatever. Just not a great experience overall. I'll try it again though. It's so close, I might as well. I'll let you know how it goes.

You could say that after reading about Momofuku Ssam in a recent GQ, I was so enthralled that I traveled 3,000 miles to eat here. Truth is, work was the impetus for coming east, presenting the perfect opportunity to check it out. I was not disappointed. Two days later, the memory lingers well. Atmosphere is full of energy, and the decor is modern and inviting. We were lucky to get a table near the window, the perfect urban dining setting. Definitely try the steamed pork buns. Other yelpers and the GQ article author are not kidding - they are amazing, maybe the best ever. Serving them sort of like a sandwich with hoison sauce as the spread is genius. Beyond pork buns, the hamachi was good, the beef tendon excellent and the grilled mahi mahi incredible. Only negative was the wine - most bottles are above $50, with glasses in the $12 - $16 range. That's not for me. Instead, I recommend their $5 korean beer. The perfect complement to an otherwise delicious meal. For those of you who might be going out later, we went straight from dinner to TiÃ«sto, and had the fuel to dance all night. It was the perfect amount of food.
It's fine. Â It's overpriced, small portioned and plays it safe. I'd say, skip it.

Roberta's is so good that I feel like a professional should be writing this review. Roberta's is so good, in fact, that if it weren't in the strange no man's land known as Bushwick it would probably give the also awesome Motorino a run for it's money. Roberta's is always packed - partly because there is literally nothing in that neighborhood aside from a weird strip mall with a supermarket, a liquor store, and some type of warehouse for computers, but mostly because of how awesome it is. Really delicious pizza, stellar calzones, delicious dessert. The Hen of the Woods mushrooms are a great starter, so is the meat and cheese plate if you're willing to throw down $20. They used to have a pizza with egg on it (something my wife loves) but don't anymore. Something tells me that they'll make it for you if you ask, though. If you live in the neighborhood, you've probably been there, if not - it's worth the trip as long as you're ok with the desolate neighborhood and thousands of hipsters on every corner.
I have tried so many sandwich places in nyc, and this is the best so far. Their sandwiches are different from most sandwiches elsewhere. I order from here at least twice a month.

Ok, I love Risotto, and I am picky. This place was amazing! It's a tiny restaurant where they have to move tables out of the way for you to get in to your seat, and you have to wait an hour to ninety minutes to get in at night, but it is worth any inconvience! We split the pizza and risotto, to try everything they had. Both were delicious! They have fun toppings for the pizza and delicious additives to the risotto. The breadsticks were amazing too! All of these were gluten free! At the end we tried this gluten free apple pie, which was a delicious finish to our meal! We also enjoyed that they had a wine of the day that was priced so well you couldn't say no to adding a bottle to the order. The waitstaff was friendly and the decor was nothing special, but the closeness of you and the person you are with in the restaurant makes it a cute date place! We plan to go here every time we are in NYC. That is how good it was.

I LOVE this place! Â Best Thai food I've ever had! Â The food always comes really quickly, and the staff is really nice. Â The only drawback is that the restaurant is usually pretty empty, so the atmosphere isn't fabulous. Â But the food is incredible, so it's always worth it. Â I highly recommend the Pad Thai and Pad See Ew.
Perfect.

Don't be fooled by the "hole in the wall" atmosphere. The food is great & service is friendly & efficient. I had the falafel & hummus. Really one of the best falafels I've had in a long time. My husband had the spicy lamb on pita & loved it. Highly recommend this place
Really really good coffee! Â  Must get their biscuits! Â The best biscuits I've ever had. Â  Everything here is fresh and simple.

After seeing the Black Label Burger on both Anthony Bourdain's No Reservations on Food Network AND on Good Eats on Cooking Channel, I knew I had to come to this burger mecca. In calling to make my reservation, I soon discovered that they only took reservations 30 days out, so a **TIP** to those that have a certain date in mind, be sure that you call that date-30 to be sure you'll get a reservation cause from what I hear they get booked up pretty fast! Fast forward, to THE big day! The bf, another couple, and myself, arrive 15-20 min early and they seat us without any issues. The place has an old NY feel to it. The staff is very attentive. I don't think any of our glasses were ever less than 80% full and if someone stepped away to use the restroom, a waiter would come over and fold the napkin. Onto the food, my girlfriend had the Bone-in NY Strip ($48) which she enjoyed thoroughly, my boyfriend and guy friend shared the Dry Aged Cote de Boeuf ($110) which came with Roasted Marrow Bones and Sucrine Lettuce Salad. These were MASSIVE cuts of beef. It's stated on the menu that this item is for 2, but from the look of the plate, all 4 of us would have been full from it! It was very good. We also ordered a side of Pommes Anna ($9) which was a delightful dish of potatoes that were soaked and cooked in butter. It was AMAZING! I, OF COURSE, had the Black Label Burger ($26) which is a selection of prime Dry-aged Beef Cuts w/ Caramelized Onions & Pommes Frites. Was it everything I hoped for and imagined? It WAS good - I'm not going to say it wasn't BUT I'm not sure if it's because I had the highest expectations EVER for this burger and all, but I've enjoyed other burgers more. Was it worth the $26? That's arguable in my case. It was a good burger but I don't know if it should be $26. Maybe my palate just can't distinguish between really good cuts of beef and fast food burgers? It's def worth a try, but if I ever return I'll probably try ordering something else. Why the 5 stars still, even if my burger dreams were shattered? Because the service and quality of food were outstanding.

What a nice spot isolated from the more popular neighborhoods. Â We came here for lunch on a chilly Saturday afternoon and was pleasantly surprised. Â Quick service and cash only, if i recall correctly. Â  We ordered a dirty chai, peach blossom tea, Egyptian eggs Benedict, and grilled flank steak panini. Â Drinks were good, made exactly right and was the perfect option for a chilly day. Â Eggs Benedict was different and filling, but definitely tasty. Â The panini was not so great, however. Â The grilled flank steak was more of a cold cut roast beef meat and cold. Â Could've used some more heat on the panini, but overall a good experience.

Adorable place but uncomfortable seating and less than gracious servers. Food was average to good...out of some things unfortunately. Great wine list. Pricey for the atmosphere. Would try it again if it was convenient.

Delicious, cheap meal and a must-try if you've never had it! You do get sick of it very quickly though as the rice is greasy and the sauces are pretty heavy, but definitely get it if you're in New York for the first time. Get it with both the yogurt and hot sauce for the best taste!

Scott Conant might be a douchebag, but his restaurant is beautiful and the food is great. For appetizers I had the Creamy Polenta, Mozarella in Carrozza and the Crispy Fritto Mizzo. My entree was the spaghetti which it was supossed to be the house specialty. Pasta was like no other pasta I had on my life but at the end of the day it was only spaghetti. I paired my food with a nice bottle of Barbera D'Alba which was absolutely phenomenal. We had no dessert, since this was the last restaurant on our gourmet tour. I was thinking on giving this place 5 stars, but since he was a prick with Fabio on Top Chef I will only give him 4.

Once my bf said "the lasagna taste like Chef Boyardee" I knew I was over it. Cons: Â  -Cold bread -Menus are on the wall. Not a con for me, but if you go to Carmines make sure you Â have your glasses or your contacts are in. -Very loud -I had a question about the lasagna and the waiter looked at me and said, "we can't exclude the veal. do u know how long it takes to prep this?" I don't give a #$%@ if you have to milk the cows to make the cheese, if I wanna know about an ingredient, don't question me or get an attitude about it. -oh the waiter never told us his name. I can't even tell you the name of the guy who sucks lol -The food doesn't really have a homemade taste to it. Or maybe it's because my lasagna just tastes better. Pros: ..................................................Â­.don't hold your breath on reading the pros..............................................Â­.............................maybe i can edit this the next time I go back. If I go back.

Amazing and innovative coffee! We stumbled upon this place after having sushi next door and noticed the coffee being boiled in what almost looked like test tubes! This elegant Japanese cafe pours you individually brewed/air pressed coffee in delectable and adorable coffee tea cups. The coffee was amazing, the service (by the bar tender right in front of you) was on point, the food was small but tasty, and the location really does take you to another little piece of the world!

Very good Ramen, with superior broth. Â Overall good service and presentation. Usually you'll have to wait a while to get seated so be prepared. I'd def get the extra meats and add ons, Â to add to your Ramen. Def worth a try, but don't think I could be a regular here.
Just okay. Â Wouldn't rush back because the food isn't worth the wait.

Beautiful food served in a beautiful setting. Â It may be gimmicky, but I totally fell for the way the ingredient providers are honored on the back of the menu (they do deserve part of the credit because every item was really vibrant and fresh). Â As for specific recommendations, the pea salad and roasted lobster were especially noteworthy, but everything that was ordered was great. Â Side-note: the bottle of Cava that polished off this perfect meal (along with some amazing salted caramel frozen treat) was amazingly well-priced... a pleasant surprise.
Pretty enjoyable, had a nice time and would go again, but less awe-inspiring as I'd hoped.

Comfortable, cozy, and casual laid-back atmosphere beckons you to relax and enjoy your visit. Â The staff are very friendly and appear more than happy to assist- even in saving your table for you (bandana marker) as you wait in-line to order food at the counter (no traditional waiter service). Â After placing your order and paying, you are free to sit back down. Â Servers will then bring your food to your table for you. Â  Don't skimp on the tip! All in all, a very pleasant experience in Chelsea.

This place. It's all about the wide hand-pulled noodles. You can get it in almost any permutation and combination. Just close your eyes and imagine. I know most people who came here would advise you to get the Big Tray Chicken with a serving of noodles, but thats not what I'm going to do. I'm here to extol the goodness of the Spicy Vegetable Hui Mei. First things first, it's not spicy. But it more than makes up for it with chinese lily buds, tofu, bok choy, and black fungus. In my books, it's an extremely balanced and well thought out dish. Cash only.

First day here in NY and it's raining :( We don't get to check into our room for a couple of hours so we lug our bags around East Village searching for breakfast. This place was tiny but extremely busy and turning tables like nobody's business. Food came out nice, fresh, and quick. Huervos rancheros was sooooo good! Wish we lived here to come more often. Great place for brunch, just expect a wait. I am Sad we did not have enough room for their sweets though!
Great service and love that the chef was hands on in the kitchen! Love the bread and butter served in the beginning. I highly recommend the lobster w/Texas toast appetizer.

This was my third time at the restaurant and I definitely loved every single time I've been here. Â Usually we need to wait for a table for at least 30-45 minutes but we came at around 5:30 on a Friday and there was no wait. Â There was actually no wait even when we left at 6:30ish. We ordered the cuban sandwich and the huevos rancheros a caballo (which is huevos rancheros with a strip of grass fed steak). Â Both were delicious! Â The steak was perfectly medium rare. Â We did not need to wait long for the food at all. Â Can't wait to go for my next visit.
Gotta get the squares...just amazing!! Make sure you get it fresh...I heard not fresh is not the same...

The walk to the Royale was long and rainy and by the time I reached this non-descript pub in the east village, I was soaked to the bone and as hungry as a wolf. With a Molson in front of me, from my perch at the bar, I ordered the Bacon Royale -- a burger with lettuce, tomato, onion, pickle and four thick slabs of bacon -- along with some fries and onion rings. Minutes later the burger arrived along with the sides. I munched on the fries for awhile and chowed down a few rings, both of which were salty, crisp and delicious. Now it was time for the main event as I took my first bite of a Royale. Immediately I was aware this is a contender for NY's best burger. The meat was perfectly cooked and the egg-white bun enhanced the flavor and consistency. By the time it was gone, I was comparing the Royale (favorably) to Corner Bistro and Back Forty. My only qualm with this place came when I was paying the bill. They don't accept credit cards. Luckily I had enough cash to cover my burger and beers. And it was worth it.
A classic...but odd hours.

i think this place is overrated. i went there today with my friends, and we ordered to go. while we were waiting for the chickens, we got in the line to use the bathroom, which is right next to the kitchen on this narrow hallway. we were already nice enough to step aside while waiting on the line, but the staffs were like so rude and such a dutchbag! they kept asking us to wait "outside" for the food, but hey!!!! can't you see that we were waiting to use your damn bathroom?! also, it's not our fault that you have such a tiny a$$ space! you totally didn't need to say, "you're still waiting for the bathroom?!" what kind of attitude is that?! treating your customers like this?! this is so unacceptable! alright, drama was over. now, let's focus on the food - chicken. i got the chicken biscuit. the biscuit is warm and buttery, which is good, but the chicken was over fried and dry. i do not like it that much. plus, the mac & cheese was also just ok. my friend ordered the super bowl, which i believe that it was supposed to have 5 pieces of chicken in there, but when she got it, she only got 4 pieces! i don't know if they were doing this in purpose because she kept having the bathroom and food waiting argument with them. whatever that is, it's still not cool! so, if you really want to come here, just make sure that you're not going to use their god damn bathroom, otherwise, they will ask you to wait "outside"!!!!!!
Clean, Fast and delicious. I live two blocks away and will grab a couple gyros, hummus, greek yogurt and sodas for under $20. Great value and they are extremely clean.

The first time I ate dinner at butcher bar was just a week after it opened, and I was largely unimpressed. Â Very casual eatery, decent food but nothing memorable, modest size portions and a bit expensive, it was not sure I'd return for a while. Â Thankfully, after too long away, I returned and had a great meal. Â The quality of the BBQ is very good. Â Not amazing, not the stuff that will keep me awake at night, not life changing, but very good. Â The burnt ends are by far the best thing they serve. Â However, the seasoning in general is a bit underwhelming. The place itself is small and cozy, the temperature a bit hot, the service excellent and very friendly. Â The layout of the menu still confuses me a bit but we settled on splitting the beef and pork platters. Â Aside from the Burnt Ends which as mentioned are quite excellent, the pork belly was my second favorite. Â Very smokey, appropriately fatty, served like small pieces of deep fried thick bacon, very tasty bites, although I would have loved a light vinegary sauce to contrast the fat. Â Ribs and pulled pork were good, brisket was just alright. Â  Sides, drinks and dessert were largely forgettable. Â The baked beans being my favorite side, the mac and cheese was flat on flavor. Â The complementary apple cake was small and dry. Â Same for the small corncakes. I recommend this place for a casual dinner, or take out, and definitely for the burnt ends. Â In terms of flavor it is not at all the best BBQ place in the area, but its much more of a sit down dinner place than say John Brown Smokehouse. Â Recommended.

Good Lord! Â 7 for tapas, make a reservation. Â Always make one for huge groups! Flamenco performance transported you to the streets of Barcelona where dreams are made of Rioja and Serrano Ham. Â Casual and homey. Â Get inebriated on culture and a myriad of fruity sangrias. Â Paella, Tortilla Espagnola, Croquetas de Jamon, Pulpo a La Gallega, Gambas al Ajillo, Mejillones Rias Baixas- Winners at our table. Â Bread flows like wine, so you can get your sauce on. Escargot was a little goopy and all I tasted was garlic-but whatever. Empanadillas de Atun- Amazing. Â  Great Service, they understood my terrible muddled Spanish and didn't shrug me off like a gringo. Â The service was rapid and attentive. Beware- if you tell them its your birthday, guess who's dancing with the Flamenco dancers....Do you even lift?

Would like to give this place 3.5 stars but since it is not an option I rounded down because the dipping sauce could have been better. Actually I think you should be able to make your own dipping sauce mixture. At least they could have some different vinegar options, like ginger. Plus I don't feel so bad about the downgrade because the wrap consistency was not the best. But as late night cheap eats go it's pretty good.

I wanted to bring my bf here because yelp told me to. Also the breakfast/ brunch simply looked divine. We got there around 11:20 and had about 5 parties in front of us. But because they had to switch to lunch soon, we were given the lunch menu. :( I'm sure they are great, but nothing really stood out. Fortunately, the waiter let us order the breakfast. He said he would put the order in first and it would be ready by the time we got seated. YAY Everything on the breakfast menu looked AMAZZINGG. I ended up getting the penny sandwich with croissants, and my bf got french toast with a side of grilled ham and a glass or grapefruit juice. I'm not sure if we were just hungry but the food was very good. Just everything you would hope for in a great American breakfast.

I'm not sure why i havent been here sooner. Â I've been a long time supporter of Taim so I haevnt really bothered with anyone else, but then one drunken night i stumbled into Mamouns ordered a Falafel and said make it HOT. Â As i was waiting i saw that they even bottle and sell the sauce. Â I was thinking this must be really good, i tell the guy to make it VERY hot and let me have some sauce on the side. First bite was like heaven, 2nd bite was like Â firey hell, but the good kind of heat. Â You know the kind that makes you sweat yet you keep eating it and you ask your self if you should order another one and get a bottle of sauce to go.

Long lines that move fast at any time of the day! Cheap food. Don't be fooled by the other halal carts on the other corners- these guys are the originals I understand...food was fresh and pretty good. Not sure what all the hype was about though? The white sauce is not very flavorful- the red sauce is hot but gives it a nice kick. Couldn't determine if I had ground beef or lamb tasted like a mix of both. Chicken was shredded chicken sort of fried up. Pretty good but not 5 stars in my book. Probably one of those things you have to try at least once...

Love this little bar/burger joint. My cousin brought me here the first time and I fell in love with the bacon grilled cheese. It taste so good. Try it! Also the boozles are pretty good but the bar is a bit narrow and usually packed.

Great drinks and surprisingly good dishes. (Surprisingly because their drinks are raved about but I never paid attention to the food reviews.) Must orders include the lamb appetizer, the beef carpaccio, and the ragu! Can't go wrong with any drink - our table of 5 loved every drink we got - and our drinks were all different, both rounds.

I went here not long after it opened, in September. There was a wait, but it was relatively brief. Perhaps because it wasn't so slammed yet, on a weekday lunch, they could take extra care in meal preparation. I ordered my bowl of ramen just the way I like it (hakata classic with pork belly and egg), and he ordered the spicy version. OMG, I finally believed the hype. It is definitely better than the best in DC (although in DC, it's a different style--Sapporo style). And although I like spicy foods, I much preferred my broth to his. Yes, I do believe it's the best ramen I've ever had outside of Japan. Have to give them props. We also ordered a pair of pork buns, which of course were decadent. And wished we had double stomachs to try many of the small plates that aren't available, I believe, at the other location. They looked amazing. The problem is coming here and not being able to resist the ramen in order to try the high-end izakaya-looking food :S.

It's really good here, the brunch is worth it. Â The outdoor seating is really cool and you're surrounded by flowers. Â I really like sweet potato fries and have a hard time finding them and they carry them here (I've seen in the other reviews that's why I found this place..) Â And the servers are super sweet. There are a lot of locals there plus stragglers that come from the museum around the corner. Don't be shy!

I attended Almond for brunch. They required my friend and I to wait about 15 minutes while there were a mulititude of open and available seating. I can understand holding places for reservations, but over ten tables is quite ridiculous. Once the host caught my friend's irratated demeanor we were sat within the next minute. The atmosphere was very stuffy and condescending. The waitress was very flat and unhelpful. Did not check up on us once to see how we were doing and had to hunt her down to heat up my coffee. The food tasted satisfactory in the moment, however I have been sick (throwing up/glued to the bathroom) ever since I left at noon and it is now 11pm. I do not think they practice good food handling. I do not recommend this restaurant.

The food here was so fucking GOOD that I dreamed about it ALL night after dinner The appropriate feeling that overwhelms you is an orgasmic excitement and satisfaction in your tummy. The food here was delicious, lip smacking, luscious...if I were to continue...the adjectives I use to describe the food would go on forever. So I came here to celebrate a birthday...so we wanted to eat like kings, but with a healthy conscious in mind. We ordered the Kale Salad - very refreshing, Fried Fresh Tomato - Scrumptious and rich, Elysian Field Lamb - mouthwatering and juicy, Roasted Chicken, Alaska Baked Cookie, and Spy Cup - this drink is strong and tasty - one of the best cocktails I have had at a restaurant I have to say the Alaska Baked Cookies was the best. It is probably the second best dessert I have ever tasted in my life. It was charming, appealing, enchanting and most of all rich in flavor. I thought I was in heaven for the brief moment while eating this delicious cookie. The service here was impeccable if I can give this place 10 stars I would. They went above and beyond. I am sad I did not remember my waiter's name because she was awesome. She messed up my drinks, to compensate she gave me the drink for free. The Alaska Baked Cookies took awhile to come, she gave it to us for free. We tipped her a lot for her work.

After attempting to go to Bacchanal for a pre dinner drink and being treated horribly, we decided to go to Piacere instead. I'm glad we did, I cannot speak about the food, but will say that without a doubt we were treated exceptionally well, and were given the royal treatment. Based on the service and the food that I saw being delivered to other tables, I look forward to going back for dinner.

Had a great brunch early April. Â The duck burger was like chicken, but otherwise everything was very good. Returned for 530 seating for dinner later in April. Â When the host told me he was checking on the table, I told him we'd be having a drink at the bar. Â He kept telling us our table was ready even though we were just getting our drinks. Â He finally got the hint when I told our bartender we're being rushed along. Â  My hangar steak was the best I've ever had. Â The girls had fish, which they loved. Â My side of risotto was excellent. Â Wine list is varied with reasonable pricing. Overall very good service from our waitress - Cynthia (?). Â Bread and water service was great. Â My pet peeve - TOOOO DARK!!!!! Â Dont be ashamed to show color of food. Â Or maybe some couples dont want to be recognized???? Â Cmon, a little more light - please. Â Aside from host misstep, this would have rated 5 stars. Â Will come back.

Cafe Steinhof is a wonderful German place. Â It seems to be a combination of a cafe/bistro and bar at night. Â Although it may have a huge variety on the menu, they have encompassing portions and it's worth the wait. Â I like their service and their hospitable waitstaff. Â I love the sausages and the delicious food. Â It does have rare beers and unique dishes. Â I had the seafood ragout last time I went, and the time before that I had the chicken schnitzel which left me very satisfied. Â All very delicious indeed! Â I also noticed a dessert menu which led me to my choice of berries and cream. Â Just scrumptious!

Buster's is a wonderful lunch spot. Â I decided to go after reading all the positive reviews. Â The restaurant is clean and simple, just tables and chairs. Â The chef is cooking in the back. Â Somehow I felt a connection to the owners although we did not converse much. Â I ordered past primavera, the daily special, and I was delighted. Â The veggies were yummy --- yes that's right --YUMMY. Â I can't even remember what was in there- artichokes, mushrooms, asparagus, perhaps? Â They were cooked perfectly and tasted heavenly. Â A perfect lunch dish. Such a nice place to stop and have a real lunch meal. Â I'll be going back.

In a little spot covered in wood. The tables are pretty small, but they should be able to do a table for 6. They have BYOB at $2.79/person. Just bring beers or bottles of wine and they will serve it to you. I had the get the burnt ends obviously for $7.49 for 1/4 pound and $5.49 for pork belly. Â They little plates of food weren't filling. While the brisket part of the burnt ends were moist and delicious, it lacked a crust or charring that is the whole point of the meat. The pork belly was freshly cooked to order. It was hot, fatty, and salty slices of thick bacon. I recommend it. My friend's mac and cheese was cold. On the other hand, their sauces were really good. I would mix them as the habanero BBQ sauce is quite spicy and the other ones have a really good amount of smokiness. They offered us apple cake at the end. It was boring, dense, and dry, though it would be decent with a jam or frosting. The BBQ wasn't out of this world and the prices weren't great.

Their juices are great! I've tried all of them, and the cucumber is my favorite- super refreshing and surprisingly tasty. I ordered a huge cookie as well (perfect- tasted great w/o being too crunchy or too soft) and the other pastries look amazing. Lastly, the staff was helpful and friendly. I'll definitely have to do some more sampling on my next visit.

Taco combo - which comes with black beans and yellow rice. Had the chicken, shrimp, and chorizo tacos. Shrimp didn't taste like anything. Chicken was a bit saucy. Can't judge the chorizo since my fiance ate it. Rice and beans were a bit on the salty side. . . .it was aight. Nothing to rave about.

I went to B4 this past Friday night for a friend's birthday. Our table was ready when we got there, the bread was fresh and warm and the staff was immediately accommodating and friendly. After sharing several delicious sides as appetizers, NY cheddar mac & cheese, lemon parmesan roasted cauliflower and sweet potato planks with sesame peanut sauce, I moved on to what I swear is the most delicious pork chop I have EVER tasted! This pan seared heritage pork was topped with a fennel slaw I wanted to take home to eat everyday and a cherry reduction of sorts. The place was so great, I actually took my sister back for her bday just this past tuesday (4 days after my first visit) and she had the pork and felt the same. The new Spring asparagus, leek, lemon and goat cheese pizza was great that night too. We finished the meal off with a strawberry rhubarb pie that I wish was a bit warmer... but if that my only complaint on food then you still get a 5 in my book. I can't wait to try their brunch. The menu looked just as delicious.

What a disappointment . Of all the fabulous eats in the city, we blew it. The food was average at best though the short rib was by far the star. The breadbasket must have been staged around noon, all the top pieces were hard as rocks, you had to dig under for the good stuff. The real "experience" was our inattentive, dismissive, inept waiter that really blew the night. Maybe he was pissed because we arrived at the table with drinks but it was like he hated us and couldn't be bothered with us from hello. After dumping menus he came back 10 minutes later and said ready to order? Â Can you talk to us about the menu? Oh, I didn't I tell you the specials? Â Um, no. I wanted to know how the meatballs were. Oh they're good, so good we don't have any he dead panned. Great, thanks. Â He took our order and pretty much deserted us from there. No water, check in, hey anybody want another drink? How about a glass of wine?Without listing every basic service missed, it just got ugly and annoying from there. When he heard us talking about his crappy service, and saw the overturned water glass he totally bolted and sent the manager over. Really? So what he snitched us out and is trying to make us look bad? Hope this saves one traveler to the city a wasted culinary evening. Pick somewhere else. Go to Gallo Nero around the corner. Went there Friday night and it was fantastic.
Only giving three stars because it was my first time. Classic Pho was good and spring rolls hot and delicious. Â Quick service, clean atmosphere. Â Nice overall.

Place is nicely decorated which is perfect for a special occasion. Service was ok, it wasn't outstanding considering the price. Ordered the a la carte menu and I had the crab appetizer & oysters which were outstanding. For the main course I ordered the Long Island duck and my husband had the lamb. Duck was good and it was a nicely sized portion. On the other hand the lamb that my husband received was not good at all. In the beginning the waiter brought it out prior to putting it in the oven to show how it would be cooked,thus we had high expectations.When the meal came out it was very undercooked, and once we notified the assistant waiter, he attempted to reassure us that its supposed to be like that. We got the head waiter and Â sent the plate back and got cod instead. Waiter came back and confirmed that it was "severely" undercooked, yet did not offer to comp anything. It took 10 mins to prepare the fish dish and my husband ended up eating it by himself, since I was done with my duck, not wanting for it to get cold. Â Bread cart was great, wine list was good, and deserts were ok. Â I still prefer, restaurant Daniel, which is similar in food and price, but has much better service.

Just finished up a brunch here - it was fantastic. Really, what's to hate? We were, admittedly, 20 minutes late, and the staff was still super polite and seated us promptly. The sangria was boozy and the food was pretty decent. I really couldn't have asked for more. See you there!

I really enjoyed the atmosphere here. The food was good. I personally did not like the Cesar salad. I think this place is a bit over priced but the food is delish. And the best part is the shots of course=)

restaurantbrat.com New York City is obsessed with exclusivity. The secret speakeasy, the members-only clubs, the private sample sales - whatever the occasion or venue, the fewer people who are able to gain access, the more desirable said access becomes. I've seen some cool things in this city, from the phone booth entrance at PDT to the nondescript door to Milk and Honey, from the keys that open the side door to Apotheke to the hidden underground caverns of La Esquina and Sakagura. Do I think this trend towards exclusivity is a good thing? Not necessarily. Do I like it? As much as it makes me sound like a Class A Douchebag (which I am not)... why yes, I actually sort of do (or am I?). I have to admit my bias though - it's a lot easier to like something when you're a part of it, and a lot easier to deride it for its superficiality when you're not included on the VIP list. I will say, however, that a lot of these secret establishments place more emphasis on the scene than on the quality of the food and drink. Apparently the key to pulling a young, beautiful crowd is shabby chic decor: in a coincidental twist of fate, these hidden gems almost without exception favor dim lighting and brick walls. And not nice, uniform red brick either - we're talking ugly unvarnished brick here. Brick that looks like the "Before" picture in a Proactiv commercial. So imagine my amusement when I heard of a brand new hidden spot - an uber modern (read: no bricks, proper lighting) Japanese restaurant hidden behind a butcher's shop. With an impossible-to-obtain phone number. An authentic NYC outpost of a Tokyo favorite. A secret place so secret that even my foodie friends were stumped.
