Â We looked back and realized it was actually very clearly by the door we had just walked through and moseyed back over there with our tails between our legs haha. Â They could have been a little more friendly :'( Â after all, it was Valentine's day. Â  We were quickly seated by a friendly and attentive waitress at a small table for two near the front of the stage. Â We took a moment to take in our surroundings fully - the decor was limited to paper asian umbrellas hanging from the ceiling, that had lights and flowery things inside. Â One was hung up above each table, and it made for a pretty mood. Â I had been hoping it would be more miraculous as I've heard a lot about other parties of theirs - especially the midsummer parties, so I was a little disappointed, but also appreciative. Â  The waiter quickly brought out some kind of dehydrated vegetable chips with a very spicey olive oil with different kinds of olives in it. Â They were fun to eat but rather salty. Â  We took a while to look over the menu and listen to the nice low key jazzy music playing from the live band. Â  There was fake smoke everywhere, giving a somewhat surreal look to the place. Â And some of the waiters and patrons were obviously a part of the show and doing small surreal acts from time to time - like dancing, or dropping a handkerchief. Â Not really as much as I thought it would be though. Â  The menu was beautiful and each meal contained such fanciful ingredients. Â It was hard to pick. Â We could each pick one appetizer, and one entree. Â The dessert was shared. Â We could also each choose a special cocktail - and there was an open bar for the whole night. Â  The waitress was nice enough to let me order a "virgin" version of one of the cocktails - as I'm allergic to alcohol haha. Â I really wish I could partake in the open bar ;) Â  The cocktail was pretty and had black cherries and pomegranite seeds. Â  My partner's alchoholic cocktail was very strong and she said it had a unique taste - so I'd imagine most drinkers would like that sort of thing! :P I ended up choosing an appetizer of -- I'll remember the most basic ingredients as there were quite a bit --- white asparagus, with I think Himalayan pink sea salt, smoked paprika?, edible flowers, and so on --- My partner got the impressive oyster dish that comes out in a box of richly seasoned salt. Â Each oyster had all kinds of tasty herbs in it, and they tasted very fresh. Â I've never had oysters like that - it was also nice that when you eat them, you get a bit of the seasoned salt from the dish clinging to the oyster and it's delicious. Â  Mine - while quite impressive and I was of course so excited to get to eat so many edible flowers - was again, very salty! The saltiness overwhelmed any of the subtle flavors in any of the components of the dish. Â I'm not a very "delicate diner" either - so this would probably totally overwhelm someone with a really particular palate. Â  The oyster dish was salty too, as expected - but the oceany taste and herbal/spicey seasonings did not get lost in the dish. Â  While we were waiting for our entrees to come out, we decided to pull apart the container that had previously held the vegetable chips that we finished. Â It was a brown paper that had something typed on it. Â It turned out to be a creepy confession from someone that had killed a rabbit or something - it was really interesting. Â  A neat photographer man came out at some point and took our photograph together. Â He said the photos would be available for us to pick up - but we were not fully directed where to get them and when, and that kind of fell by the wayside. Â  To be continued ---- this is already too long

Holy cow. Somebody punch me in the face. Chef Jehangir Mehta's menu blew my mind. Even with high expectations going in, I was very impressed. Â What a treat to actually be served by Mr. Mehta himself. Â He was so kind and personable as he explained each dish he put down in front of us.. even though the restaurant is chaotic being so tiny and so crowded. I won't go into detail on each dish because I could write pages. I'll just say that each was presented beautifully and the flavor combinations are true genius. And if you walk by the kitchen, which is the size of a closet, you will be shocked that such beautifully prepared food comes out of there. Â My menu: Watermelon Feta Salad, Mint Sorbet Pickled Ginger Scallops, Candied Red Chili Green Chili Shrimp, Mirin Daikon Moong Salsa Chickpea Crusted Skate, Mint Yogurt Sauce Warm Truffle Almond Strawberries, Pepper Ice Cream Forgive me, for I have sinned. Â After eating the truffle almond strawberry dish I felt I had committed a crime. Â Each dish I had before desert hit all the right chords. Â The desert was unique and delicious (who doesn't like truffles), but its so sinful I might try something different next time. *Be very aware that this is a TINY restaurant. Â I mean TINY. Â You will be sharing your tiny table with other guests. Â But after a glass of wine and your first dish (do the watermelon feta salad), everything will be juuuuust fine. Â If sharing space with others is an issue for you, then wait til his Tribeca location is open (which should be soon). I highly recommend going on a weekday instead of weekend (it will still be packed). No question I will be returning.

We were lucky enough to discover this place pretty much the first week that they opened. Â Walking around the neighborhood one random night I was stopped by the owner Charlie for a quick chat about his awesome new farm to table restaurant. Â Life gets crazy sometimes and after weeks of walking by and saying "Man we still have to try them" Â we wondered in one night. It could not have been a better experience. Â If memory serves me we tried pretty much every side dish on the consantly rotating menu and were unable to even narrow down the race for a favorite. Â Our entree choices of meatloaf and ham were absolutelly mouth watering. Â The wine list is all local which is fun for us since we spend some time at long isalnd wineries every year. Eventually finding a Longisland blueberry port from this place we had ignored it has since became a staple. All this deliciousness is housed in a cozy space that feels like an escape from the maddness that can sometimes be midtown west. Â  Over the last 6 or so months we have seen the staff embrace everyone that comes through the door like they are family. Â  Make a reservation because these guys are officially on the map. Charlie still takes the time to say hello though.

If you're looking for some Soup Dumplings, Joe's Shanghai will most likely be the restaurant to pop up at the top of the list. There are 3 locations, and I visited the one in Chinatown. Ambiance and friendly service are non-existent at this restaurant. Yet, you'll find the restaurant always full of customers looking for some good food. The tables are communal, so, be prepared to dine with others and have the opportunity to strike up some fun conversation. While they're best known for their Soup Dumplings, there's an extensive menu of dishes to choose from. But never mind. Just order the soup dumplings (crab and pork) and a scallion pancake. For me, these are their two amazing dishes. Other dishes here can be hit or miss.

I try to stop by here at least once when I'm in the city. I really should branch out and try more items on the menu, but I like my "normal meal" so much, I haven't yet. The first thing I always get is the passion fruit Arnold Palmer. If you like tart, you'll love this! My mouth is watering and cheeks are sucked in writing this! I usually get an appetizer, but it hits the stop - Fish Tacos. The pico de gallo is fresh, and the lettuce/cabbage is crisp. The fish is cooked perfectly and seasoned well. The flavor is great. I usually accompany this with the truffle french fries. Fries are always good regardless of where they come from, right? Cafeteria is no exception.

I had a truly wonderful experience at Gramercy Tavern for an anniversary dinner. Â The waitstaff went out of their way to help us celebrate with a champagne toast and desserts with "Happy Anniversary" written in chocolate sauce. Â Normally the idea chocolate writing would make me roll my eyes, but I promise it was very tasteful. Â I was very impressed with the service. The Sea Bass with swiss chard, capers, pine nuts, onion sauce course and Warm Chocolate Bread Pudding dessert were standouts in a line of exceptional dishes. If I could afford it, I would come back here in a heartbeat.

Is it summer vacation for service at New York restaurants? Great food can't be saved by a cluster f...of mistakes in how the food appeared or often just did not at a recent dinner on the back patio. Â Yes the food is good and the patio beautiful. Â But if you want to average a 100 tab per person, Â figure out this one. Â When you serve a cheese course you need to bring a knife so we can actually eat it. Â  Maybe service is just a thing of the past.

Wow what a great experience!!! Came in this weekend for the first time with my gf, we liked it so much we went back last night We were greeted outside by the host Rob, he took the time to explain to us the menu which was posted outside, he then walked us in to show us the inside and were wowed by the beauty of the restaurant, he told us the wait was about 20 min and than brought us wine outside as we waited for a table, thanks Bud i had a great feeling about the place from there on ..we sat in a beautiful booth and had Arnold as are waiter, he was a really nice guy too and took care of us.....We had the Meatballs and Calamari for apps...hit the spot....the pizza was also amazing ,so thin and crisp..i love the coal taste Came in again last night and had another wonder evening saw Rob again who i found out was also the manager which explains why he was so caring towards us , had another glass of wine outside while i waited...waiting never felt so good as me and my girl sipped wine on the corner of 99th on a beautiful brooklyn night, got a booth again and had another great waiter sorry i could remember your name bud...food was great again had baked clams and the eggplant parm and it knocked socks off I could seriously eat here every night i will def be back this weekend. Great Food Great service P.s. can't believe people wrote bad reviews about this place

Husband and I happened upon this place one night, around 9pm on a weekday. Â The weather was beautiful, and there was a wait for tables, so we sat at the bar along the wall. Â The space is SMALL, I mean, even for New York. Â  Husband loved the pork ribs, spare ribs, something like that, on the appetizer menu. Â I had two kinds of dumplings, one of them peanuts/veggies, was outstanding. Â  I was so enamored with the peanut dumplings, I asked about delivery. Â They will not deliver to my apartment, which is in the neighborhood, only about 10 blocks down. Â  I would prefer carry-out/delivery from here, since the space is really that small.

MY MOST FAVORITE PIZZA EVAR!!! My friends and family have called me a traitor because I'm supposed to have an allegiance to Chicago-style deep dish (anyway, deep dish was invented by some guy from TEXAS!)...this pizza perfection is achieved using a coal brick oven, turning the dough into a great balance of tension between chewiness and slightly charred crunch. (But I must admit that the last time I went was a little *too* chewy and gave me a sore jaw the next day). You can see them assembling the pies in plain view, using the simplest but most delicious ingredients - fresh buffalo mozzarella, basil, and a balanced tomato sauce. Their sausage is also excellent - tasting exactly how Italian sausage is supposed to taste like, complete with caraway seeds. Sublime simplicity! Plan your trip accordingly because the wait can be really crazy, in addition to the 20 or so minutes cooking time. Last time I went was a Saturday night around 8 pm and we waited about an hour in line. I've also been many times during the week and mid-day when I have had little to no wait. Â If you're going to have a large party, expect longer waits. Oh and it's cash only, though there's an ATM inside the restaurant. Don't forget to hit up the Brooklyn Ice Cream Factory after your meal! It's always nice to have a quality pizza experience without the need to slip into stretchy pants afterwards. Sorry, Chicago. You are the Second City, once again.
Red Velvet Waffles, fried chicken, YESSUH!!!!!! and that mac n cheese is top 5 dead or alive.....enjoy yourself

We went today for our usual mixed berries and nutella with strawberries crepes but the chef convinced me to try the mascarpone strawberry crepe... At first we weren't too sure but I'm pretty game to try new stuff so i forgo my usual mixed berries for the Mascarpone... And boy was i happy, because once that first bite went into my mouth, I wanted to eat the fork, the plate, My fingers lol just about anything that came into contact with that crepe, Its THAT delicious. If you're a fan of sweet crepes, this is a must... Give it a try, you wont regret it... It's not on the menu so just ask for it, Happy Eating :)

Walked out of raining NYC street and into Cinque Terre! Â Wonderfully charming restaurant with creative food (e.g. Zuppa Di Pesce - a fisherman's stew, baked under a flatbread crust with mussels, clams, calamari, scallops and shrimp in a light tomato broth). Has great rustic ambiance; the back courtyard with small lights shining like stars is elegant and comfortable. A gem.

Got the roll with the avocado and sweet potato...really Â yummy. As well as one piece mango sushi and one piece seaweed sushi (which has rice in it too). Very good. Also got the cucumber mint lemonade, delicious and refreshing. Service was so friendly. I like the combo deals. But it does get expensive since one roll is $6.50 and you likely need two-three to get full. Can't wait to come back and try more! Not good for groups, seating probably 4 to a table max and only 3 tables.

I've been here several times & it is safe to say that the food here is amazing. Jared is usually my waiter. I know absolutely nothing about Filipino food, so he usually helps us order the good shit. Love that guy!

I usually feel tears of happiness gather when I am handed a giant over filled paper cone of hot fresh right-out-of-the-oil frites by the amazing friendly patient ladies behind the counter. Â The fries are hot fresh and well seasoned. Sometimes I just eat them without any sauces. However, I have made it a personal goal to try every sauce once and I have gone through half the list. I want pommes frites to exist forever. and ever. and ever.
heaaaaaaad cheeeeeeeeese bahn mi. bag of chips and viet ice coffee 8$ that hit the spot. yum.

This was a nice find. Good food. Casual atmosphere. Pasta and wood fired pizza. The waiter made some recommendations which we took. Delicious! Wonderful flavors. Food was served quickly and service was attentive. Grateful to yelp community for helping us find this place. Seemed like a community gathering place that we would not have seen otherwise.

I had a friend visiting from Utah and while this area is full of restaurants, it was challenging to find something we'd both like. She's an all-american steak-loving gal, while I just wanted something under $15. We walked by Fukurou, took a look at the menu, decided that the price was right, and walked inside. First step in, the waiter asked if she could take my coat. This automatically gets two stars. The brick exposed walls, dim lighting and wooden tables create a cozy Â environment. The seating is intimate but provides enough space for each person. We were seated at the sushi bar and could see the skill and finess dedicated to each meal. This made me especially grateful when the chef brought out my salmon and salmon roe and offered to mix it before me. Upon first bite, it was nourishing and tasty. The texture was smooth and the roe offered a sharp burst of flavor. The food was excellent, the staff was great and I will certainly be back again.

Cuban food for lunch, how can you go wrong. The restaurant is not fancy. Just good food. One can tell by the take out line when you walk in the place. Minimum 15 people in line waiting to place their orders. There is sitting area in the back. Usually parties of 2 get right in, we had a party of 3 so we had to wait a bit for a larger table. They had a daily special as well as the standard foods. Good food at a fair price. Who can ask for more in NYC. We will definitely go back again.

Song and Joya are great. The food, atmosphere and service are all good. The owners are warm and generous. My wife and I have been going for years, and they always treat us to dinner and drinks around the holidays. I love this place.

Food is great but delivery is the WORST. Ordered from Seamless. Two hours later, no food. Call to inquire, blame issue on Seamless. Best I get is half hearted apology. Lost my business. If you want food from here, better order it today to eat tomorrow.

Let me begin by saying the service is phenomenal. The attention to detail, the way the servers take care of the customer is great. The crowd varies but generally it is a good mix of locals some t&b, and tourists. The bread basket is an assortment of freshly baked breads that are made on premises. The pancetta and cheese wrapped into one of the breads is delicious. Appetizers: The Creamy Polenta with truffled mushrooms is a must. I ask for some red peppers flakes to add another depth of flavor. Entree: Hands down Scott Contant has the best Tomato and Basil Spaghetti in the city, so that is a must. The halibut is perfectly cooked and does not need to be wrapped in lardo. You can request that. Desserts: Are less desirable. I would say mediocre at best. One last tip, if you enjoy Ginger ale as much as I do, I highly recommend ordering it at Scarpetta. They order it from Fever Tree which makes high quality natural beverages
pretty decent pizza but there are a good amount of them in the city as well.

Eating some Cremolata as we speak and it's phenomenal. Hit the spot on this hot summer day. Usually I can get a Half Tray and eat 6 slices by myself, but today was just too perfect to pass up on the spumoni. Perfection. If you come and order a regular slice, go home. It's Sicilian or nothing here.

I am confused as to why this restaurant claims on OpenTable that it has a Michelin star - I could find no evidence on the Michelin site that it does and ever has - This is what they write on OT: * Thank you for choosing a top Zagat rated, very popular, Michelin star Italian restaurant in New York, Trattoria L'incontro. It will be an..." Â Please let me know if I am mistaken because otherwise it is misleading.

Very good food, only one complaint, the gouda melt I chose had a black bean spread but I only found it in one corner of the sandwich which was disappointing because it tasted really good. Wished it has been spread out more evenly. Â  The service was eh. The server only said about three actual words to me as though he was trying to communicate telepathically. Over all, I'll be back to try other items.

I was totally psyched when I found out there was a Boiling crab-like restaurant in NYC.. I came on a Saturday night and waited 2.5 hrs then found out they had run out of craw fish cause a party of 12 guys ordered close to 100lbs ... Â I chose not to leave because i really wanted to try this place and the fact that i had already waited so long. Fortunately although the wait was long and they had run out of craw fish, their service was exceptional. My friends and I resorted to shrimp and clams and I have to admit it was better than boiling crab. Their shrimp was huge and their sauce was thick and very fragrant (a little salty but they has really good brown rice to help with that). The server was very apologetic about running out of craw fish and gave us an extra half lb of clams in each bag that we order and additional 3 corns. Overall it was a great experience and the food was great and would definitely go back but will either go on a week day to avoid the crowd or have it to go.

After a couple drinks and a pizza I came here and try a falafel pita sandwich w hot sauce and I died! Sooooo spicy! And let me tell you, I'm real ok w spicy foods. This place has some really crunchy falafels that taste just right. Not overly spiced. I may have heartburn but who knows I take pepcid before drinks to reduce the "asian glow" (which is real unattractive btw.)

I love Cheryl. Not only is she the sweetest, warmest chef/restauranteur in this neighborhood, she also changed my whole world via pancakes. Breakfast/brunch: free cocktail with your food. yup. PANCAKES. i dream about these pancakes you guys, like when I'm at work, out of town, hear the word pan or cake or am at some other restaurant that dishes out some mediocre half cousin of what she can create back there in her tiny kitchen (seriously how do that work in a space so small). Smoked salmon hash. yum. Lunch: The mussels. they are the best value on the menu, get it with rice; you'll be waiting for the server to walk towards the back so you can lick the bowl. Dinner: Escoveitch fish - piping hot, has to be so fresh or this technique isn't gonna work, and the crisp is just perfect. I could eat this whole thing by myself. (don't let me) Seafood soup (don't recall the actual name) - it has various kinds of fish and shellfish, dip their bread in it and just try to tell me that the broth isn't to-die-for. Bring mom and dad here when they come to visit, go here on your 1st, 2nd, 3rd date or anniversary, come here alone on a weekday, or have your birthday here. Its a great restaurant and while you're there seek Cheryl out, she'll make sure you have a great meal.

This place is totally decent. Started with the roti canai (that the waitress haughtily mispronounced): fluffy and hot and delicious. The mee goreng was also pretty good. Not the best, but the best for six fiddy. I also thought the huge fish were cute, but then my boyfriend told me that they were food, not pets.

Stumbled upon this adorable little local cafe for lunch a few years back, but the food was so good I even still remember the mushroom tart + frisee salad that I had for lunch that day. It was a beautiful summer day, so we sat at one of the tiny outdoor tables on the stoop. Dying to go back - for dinner as well as brunch. Did not know it was BYOB last time, so I will be back with a bottle of wine!

Luzzo's is a great place to go and have pizza - not really worth ordering other items. Â The waiters are very authentic and funny and the pizza is good. Â I would say 3.5 stars, fourif they can make it less soggy in the middle! Yes, another place that does that sometimes...

Ramen is the quintessential cold weather street food. This place combines unreal quality with fast service. This isn't. Sit and spin joint. It is a tight, line out the door, hole in the wall. But the Ramen! The broth is the best I've tasted and would be a prize from a French chef any day. As rich and deep as any duck fat inspired soup, this is all Japanese. The char sui pork bun is delightful. If you are a ramen newbie maybe you don't get it yet and can wait. If you know good noodles and the joy of a perfect broth after getting chilled, then go for it. You and the forty people outside, whether they are chatting in Mandarin or Japanese, are going to enjoy it even more for the wait in the cold!

I say this as a native New Yorker: despite how ordinary the pizza is, Grimaldi's is something every resident needs to experience at least once. Â  Come when the weather's nice for a perfect, somewhat kitschy, somewhat classic, somewhat lame, and yet somehow entirely perfect date. Walk over the Brooklyn Bridge, wait on the deceptively long line, pour your date a glass of water from the water cooler outside, meet a few strangers, and you've paid your dues to park your toosh at a narrow table with no elbow room. The decor is straight-up pizza shop: waxy red gingham tablecloths, carafes of house red wine, and a brick oven handled by a bunch of hairy-armed Italian guys. The pizza, though somewhat soggy, is loaded down with an almost absurd amount of mozzarella, sauce, and toppings, with a crust that is soggy in the middle but crispy and slightly scorched on the end. It is without a doubt delicious, sitting heavily in your stomach. When you finish and pack up the leftovers, skip the meager offering of desserts and drag yourselves over to the promenade for a scoop of ice cream at the Brooklyn Ice Cream Factory. You're guaranteed to wait on yet another line, but again, it's part of the experience. Despite the amount of tourists it attracts, I am adamant in my conviction that Grimaldi's and Brooklyn Ice Cream Factory are quintessential New York joints. So suck up your pride and go! Â  I am completely serious when I say the line-waiting is essential to enjoying Grimaldi's. There is a location in no-man's-land Queens (Douglaston) that serves a superior pizza (perfect crust, sauce, cheese) in a similar setting without ever having to wait. And because of that, it really doesn't feel the same and the pizza just seems overpriced. It seems counter intuitive, to enjoy a mediocre pizza more when you have to wait for it, but its entirely essential to appreciate and pay homage to the pizza mecca that is Grimaldi's Brooklyn.

Came here last night for Brooklyn Dine In week and we ended up getting dishes that were not on the prix fixe menu. The pasta is AMAZING!! Try the butternut squash ravioli! It was really tasty. All the pasta are homemade and the sauces are not salty at all! We also love the Mozzarella di bufala appetizer. The fish dishes were also really good too. Prices are reasonable. The place is small so make reservations! The only con is that there is only one waitress working so service can be a little slow. But we will definitely go back there to try the other dishes!

I don't understand why more people aren't giving better reviews because I had nothing but a good experience at Brooklyn Crab (only minus was them not calling like they said they would when our table was actually available and almost giving away our table...). The crab and lobster were fresh and delicious. The waiter was really personable and helpful when it came to helping me take apart Â a lobster or know to efficiently crack into those littler crab-legs. The sides were simple, if actually a bit of an afterthought to the rest of the quality of the seafood. I know it's traditional to have steamed potatoes, but the broccoli was overly garlicked-and sort of forgettable. Bonus for serving bottled rootbeer and having an excellent "crab shack" environment.

#*%$!&@ love this place! For gluten free people, I haven't found any "artisanal" pizza that's better than this. Ironically enough, the risotto isn't anything special in my opinion. It's not bad, it just doesn't really tickle my fancy and I can't ever come here without wanting the hot soppressata and olive tapenade pizza, and I always ask for goat instead of mozzarella, and it's always ridiculous. They have fantastic consistency with their food and the breadsticks are to die for. It's not too overpriced for the area, a little more than you'll pay at other pizza places, but I definitely think it's worth it! I would recommend this place for anyone.

After years, of pushing my boyfriend to go to brunch/breakfast, he finally agreed. Â Not being a morning person/ not being a fan of breakfast, Â he was very reluctant whenever the subject came up. Â Considering ourselves foodies, it felt like such a shame/ let down to Â be omitting Â breakfast from our dining experiences. Â  Today was the day that he finally gave in and that all changed. Â =) Upon entering the place, we knew that we were about to embark on one yummy culinary adventure together. Â (It was 130 in the afternoon on a Thursday in November) The place was packed and full of life. Â IWe waited 5 minutes for a seat at the window, facing Clinton Street. Â  Let me just say the food was EXCELLENT. Â Good quality with variety and flavor. Â My bf ordered the spanish scramble ($13) and I had the southern breakfast ($14). Â We also had the french onion soup ($8) and the apple cider ($3) to share. Â  To start, the apple cider was warm and came in a large cup. Â As it was fall, it was a nice addition to our breakfast. Â My only comment would be that it lacked some sweetness, so we added one packet of sugar, which made the drink just right. Â  Next came our french onion soup with a whole slice of sourdough bread soaking in the center, complete with cheese on top. Â Has to be one the best french onion soups that I have ever tasted. Â As a fan of french onion soup, I have always struggled with the saltiness that lingers on my taste buds when I have consumed even just a few spoonfuls. Â  For the first time however, it was just right. Â It had plenty of onions and lots of flavor. Â Not salty at all. Â =) My bf had ordered the spanish scramble, which had 2 pieces of sourdough toast , homefries and a 3 egg scramble complete with onions, chorizo, scallions and monterey jack cheese. Â There was (homemade?) Â raspberry jam on the side, which my bf enjoyed very much on his sourdough toast. Â  Again, as a proponent of flavor and not of saltiness, his food was spot on. Â  The proportion of eggs to ingredients/fillings was perfect. Â No need to be digging around for some egg and some chorizo/onion/scallion. Â Each bite was perfect. Â  For those of us that eat meat, Â we all know that Â anything bacon is good... but sugar coated bacon is HEAVEN. Â My mouth is watering just thinking about it. Â My meal came out and it was like I said, heavenly. Â SIX, yes, SIX sugar cured slices of bacon stood out from the rest of the food on the table. Â  Once you taste it you will never go back to regular bacon. Â When I come back if I don't order the same breakfast, the sugar cured bacon is a MUST. Â  My meal was definitely a "southern breakfast" Â complete with cheese grits and 2 slices of fried green tomatoes. Â The idea of cheese grits was appealing, but after a few spoonfuls, they were a little too rich. Â I would have preferred traditional grits with maybe a touch of butter to balance the taste of the sugar cured bacon. Â  Between the two of us, the bill came up to $40 plus tip. Â Definitely worth the price for the amount and quality of food. Would come back in a heart beat, and recommend to anybody looking for a place to eat. Â  Although I have heard that their fluffy pancakes is what this place is known for, I am not disappointed at all for not ordering them. I am not a pancake person and that's that. But if I did order pancakes, (since they were featured on bobby flay's throwdown and other food network shows), I would have to order a side of bacon too ;) Â There are tons of reviews on yelp on their pancakes, this is just not one of them. Â  After completing our meal, my bf asked "Is this place open late?" The answer is YES...Their breakfast is served ALL DAY everyday, and they are open until 11pm, except Sunday. Â As it was a weekday afternoon, Â there was no line outside. Â I have heard that on weekends, people sometimes wait an average of one hour to one hour and a half outside. I see why people would wait on line to eat here... Â So my advice would be to come on a weekday if you can, otherwise be prepared to wait. One last thing- Â this place only accepts credit cards at dinner.... Â  Breakfast and lunch is CASH only All in all, my efforts at getting my bf Â to eat breakfast, was a huge success. Â We may not necessarily come back for breakfast at "breakfast time", but we will definitely be back.
Very good Ramen, but 2nd to Ippudo in Ebisu/Tokyo.

Had the chicken biscuit sandwich, and the half and half po boy. It's kind of small, but I'd rather have a small, very well made sandwich than some nasty behemoth of a sandwich. Biscuit was a little too soft but overall it was an okay sandwich. Po boy was well made except the shrimp was tough as heck. I don't know if I've been spoiled by all the po boys I've eaten in New Orleans but this place just seems okay. A good alternative to your normal sandwich shop but nothing to go out of your way for.

This is just going to add to the hundreds of reviews already in place. Â So let me keep it short and sweet for those who want suggestions and and thoughts: All you can eat pasta... worth the meal. Â The pasta is fresh and delicious. Â I had the opportunity of eating the mushroom ravioli (wow), rabbit ragu (tasty), and the penne (good, not spectacular). Â Came with salad and fabulous bread. Â  Service was great, very much an italian feel. Â  My date had the Lemon Chicken. Â There is no pasta and he wished he got something else. Wine - 20 dollar bottles are worth the money. Â  Overall, you'll be carb loaded and ready to take a nap when you're done here! Â  Bon Appetite!!
Very nice. Â We had the vegetarian platter and the iskender (lamb) kebabs. Â Both were very good. Â Lots of food, relaxed atmosphere, reasonable prices.

Hands down the best pizza I have ever ate. Crust was thin and crisp. Toppings were great but honestly sauce and cheese are all that's needed. Everything is made fresh and with the best ingredients. Line was not too long with about a Â  Â  15 min wait. it's worth the trip Â I could eat this pizza everyday.

Here's to a new David Burke restaurant!! Â I liked the decor of this place, with cute pieces of fabric up on the ceilings, the cute seats, etc. We came here for lunch, and had fabrick's club burger (nice 'n juicy) as well as the grilled skirt steak, which came with potato and cheese fritters. Â The fritters were ok (I liked the fries that came with the burger better). Â The steak itself was a bit too greasy/oily, as my plate was covered with it! Â That didn't make that dish too appetizing overall :/.

Fantastic paninis. Must try if you are at this place. Though not much of a choice for a vegetarian, you can make it thru with a happy tummy from whats available on the menu. Crostini platter: Another thing that wont disappoint you. Though the overall cost was on the higher side, the taste makes up for that.

It is normal restaurant , not bad and not good ! It's too expensive and the wine it's not typical France wine! When i had finished I was still hungry , the dishes are not completely full of food! The location is good very elegant.

If you are reading reviews of Umami to decide whether or not this place is worthy to dine at, STOP READING AND GO! Truffle burger is the best. I LOVE truffle oil and this burger is full of it! Sweet potato fries are dusted with brown sugar. It sweetens it nicely but not too much. They give you about 4 condiments to try while you dine. It is so much fun to try different sauces with the fries. Each one was great. My favorite is their ketchup because it is mixed with truffle oil. =) In order to avoid a long wait, you need to go for early dinner at 4. Also, going in a small party will help you sit so you can EAT!

While we sat for 45 minutes waiting for our table the host & waiter were very nice but negligent.
