Â Our bill comes. Â NOTHING is comped and the appetizer ("snacks") we were offered while waiting is actually on the bill. Â Really Pig & Khao, it's $4. We Â can afford it, but like....really? Â P.S. - the "snacks" here are actually not that amazing...they do not live up to the rest of the menu. The wait staff was friendly, a bit apologetic and the food is great but this was just ridiculous. My friends and I were honestly shocked and won't be going back.

Slamming! Â All meats cooked perfectly! Â Flavorful sides, even vegetarian options, Wafcos a must. Down to earth menu, affordable, a gem to the neighborhood. Â Thanks for a great meal, we will be back.
Lots of pros and cons.......can easily be overwhelmed ... it is zoo! Expensive.... I do like the concept..... they have it in foreign countries.... it just takes a while to get used to it....

will never visit again. will never recommend again. used to be one of my lunch go to's. was happy to see that they had customers, Â besides my table, for once. Until I realized the waiter couldn't handle more than one table. My guest and I were literally Â ignored for 20 minutes. The final straw was when we noticed him taking an order for a table that walked in 10 minutes after us... There's like five tables in the whole place. Looks like these guys will be back in Staten Island sooner than later.

Very much enjoyed the trip, I went there after work with a colleague. The waiter Cory was excellent, very attentive and helpful! I had the Skate special which was likewise excellent, cocktail drinks were also, well, excellent. Had nice selection of whisky also. Overall a great place to grab a bite to eat in a fairly upscale setting, I'm a fan!

I just spent $97 on a lunch with my friend. $97.. *_* Some of my friends think I'm outta my mind. Well.. guess what?? I don't give a FCUK! This place was that damn good. Some suitable hash tags would be: #foodporn #dessertporn #fatpplproblems #NoFcuksGiven Located right across the street from Central Park, tucked away inside a museum, this is a nice little gem. Has a rustic, old fashioned, and cozy feel to it, with warm wood walls, dim lighting and a grand piano in a corner of the room, Cafe Sabarsky could be an excellent date place or perhaps a business lunch even. My friend got back from Syracuse University recently and I wanted to take her somewhere that she'll probably never forget, and Cafe Sabarsky didn't disappoint. The dining experience was awesome..the food was amazing. Like fatasses, we each got a chilled iced drink for starters, with house-made whipped cream and a scoop of vanilla ice cream. I had a chilled iced coffee and she had a chilled, house-made chocolate milk. Both were pretty damn good, and yes, before ya'll start judging, we did have dessert for apps. #NoFcuksGiven Next, I had a piece of delicious, moist, perfectly cooked and seasoned Atlantic Salmon cooked medium, while she had a Roasted Bratwurst, riesling sauerkraut and roasted potatoes and dijon mustard. That sausage was surprisingly good. Perfectly seasoned, and cooked to perfection. My first time having German sausage and it was an awesome experience. For dessert, I had a slice of Pistachio, Nougat Chocolate Cake and she had a Quark Cheesecake w/ Raspberry Meringue. No words. I'm done. No words can describe the sensation that was coursing through my taste buds.. loll :D
Tacos are excellent. Be sure to order guacamole and beer.

The food is mediocre at best, but the concept is awesome! Tons of premade Korean food and alcohol at your finger tips! Perfect for drunchies. The prices here are extremely reasonable and it's open super late. They also have ample seating inside and there are tons of people chilling inside even at 2 AM.

I neglected to share my thoughts when I was here last. First off, it's refreshing to have authentic Dominican flavor without having to travel to find it. Also, it's nice to have a great offering that is priced well. The chicharones (con hueso) are reeeeedonculous. Actually, everything is. They're not open Sunday, but the Saturday brunch is amazing.

First time here finally after having to cancel 2 times. Worth it because I have been wanting to try here. Had a good time. Food was good but not great. The appetizers were more memorable than the entrees. The atmosphere is very cool and nice. not stuffy at all. I ate in the dinning room but from what I saw people eating in the tavern part of the restaurant it actually looked more appetizing. Delicious open crab ravioli with razor clams and escarole And mind blowing Quail with beets and cranberry sauce. SO AMAZING. These were the apps. For entrees, I got the Flat Iron Steak & Braised Short Rib red cabbage and puffed potatoes which was very salty. nothing too exciting. My husband got the Roasted Venison Loin but then got it changed to Sturgeon salsify, cipollini, fingerling potatoes and lemon-fennel sauce because the venison was a little too funky for him. My husband liked the Sturgeon but I didn't think it was anything great. Â I had better fish at Craft. Our server was very nice about bringing back the venison for the sturgeon and Â also threw in an extra dessert on the house because the table next to us was very loud and obnoxious. Service is excellent. I would go back but try the tavern side next time or maybe go when the menu changes in the dining room.

BarBacon is a new addition to the Hell's Kitchen family. Here, you'll find several things: -Not a vegetarian in sight. -Enough sodium intake as the Dead Sea. -Unusually delicious ways to incorporate bacon into every item imaginable. -Lamb bacon. You heard it right. Having only opened about 2 weeks ago, this place is brand-spanking new. And from the looks of it, they're doing pretty well for themselves! My friend and I arrived at around 6:30pm and it was pretty packed. With low lighting and a very nature-y feel, I felt right at home. I also really liked the fact that you weren't bombarded by the smell of bacon like some places. To your left you'll see the bar which offers plenty of space to mingle while sippin' on some crafty beers. To your right you'll find the restaurant area with both high and low tables. Yes, the menu is concise but it's surprisingly diverse. From the classic bacon cheeseburger to bacon bahn mi, you're sure to find something that suits your pork needs. Bacon Tasting: (HIGHLY recommended) this app consists of 4 types of bacon, 2 pieces each so you and a friend can share. Here's the flavors if you will: -Nueske's Applewood Smoked Bacon: classic, thin, crispy feel-good taste. -Father's Country Maple Bacon: by far my favorite. Why not take it up a level and make it even more unhealthy? Add sugar. *Cue heavenly sounds* -Nodine's Peppered Bacon: my least favorite. But still good. I felt like it needed to be paired with a merlot. Too much pepper in that bite for my liking. -BarBacon Lamb Bacon: most interesting one of the night. Slightly gamey and pretty thick sliced meat. It was a true fusion of lamb chops and bacon flavor in one. Don't miss out on this gem. Applewood Smoked Bacon Grilled Cheese with Tomato Eggplant Soup: Delicious. The thick fontina and gruyere was oozing out of the Toasted Semolina (from Amy's Bread!). The bread had fennel and golden raisins which balanced the salt of the bacon and cheese. That sweetness was a wonderful touch. As for the soup, it was a perfect pairing for dipping the sandwich. It was tart and hearty. Tip: Happy hour is at the bar but for the time being (since they're new) you may be able to snag that 1/2 off special at your table. The Sixpoint is the recommended pairing that goes well with bacon. And it sure did! Creamy and delicious beer. If you have a love for pork, unique pairings and a relaxed, casual vibe... BarBacon is your calling. I'll be returning for sure. Don't worry about eating like a pig*. It's all good. ___________________________ *Too much?
food is good. fun environment. only downside is it's hard to get seats!

I have returned to Fish on several occasions to take advantage of the Red, White and Blue Oyster special they have. I am obsessed with their Tuna and Salmon Tartare, and their Mussels with Lemon butter broth and french fries. Â Fast service, laid back and casual vibe and the price is great for all that you get!

You would think that at $8, the fixed lunch menu would be just decent. But it was really great food! You get the choice of an appetizer, a dish, and it comes with a salad. Such a good deal and I really enjoyed it!

Spicy ramen broth is super delicious. Â Noodles are fresh and toothsome. Â It's hot in there and really tiny. Â Very authentic feel with the men behind the counter bantering with guests and asking where they're from. Â $11 for spicy ramen so it's not super cheap, but I'd gladly pay it again,

Finally tried Ssam for the first time (I know, I know.... sorry, I'm a busy guy). Â had the pork buns and the rib sandwich. Â Both were totally amazing. Â And cheap. Â If you can get a seat, you're not really going to find better food at a better price anywhere in the city.
Amazing Benedict's and French toast. Go go go, but make a reservation or go early because the wait is insane.
they have the best food, and the best thing in the world is they have kool aid of the day. waitress are very friendly
Great sliders at a solid price. I'm a fan of their cheese fries, although the chili-cheese version leaves a little more to be desired. It's a great price for a quick bite.

Not sure it deserves all the hype...and I'm a big fan of dell'anima and L'Apicio. Â  First of all, the decor seems over advertised. Â Of course the space is going to be a bit cramped as it's in prime West Village territory, but it seems like they could have done more with the aesthetics, and frankly, I hate being on top of other couples at dinner. Â "But it's New York, what do you expect?" Well, I don't recall being on top of other patrons at ABC Kitchen, Barbuto...or even L'Apicio. Â Plus, L'Apicio scores big points in my book for their sweeping floral arrangements. Â I understand that L'Artusi is going for a cleaner look, and making due with the space, but the only thing that really caught my eye was the beautiful wine cellar room, reserved for large parties. It was a Sunday night, and our waitress was really exuding the "you are my last reservation of the week, I can't wait to get out of here" vibe, coupled with the "no, you need to order THIS expensive bottle of wine, that mid range one SURELY won't do" song and dance. Â Eye roll. Happily, the roasted mushrooms, pancetta, fried egg and ricotta salata was so out of this world I was able to forget some of my earlier gripes. Â For mains, boyfriend had the orrecchiette with sausage, salumi and pecorino, and I had the gnocchi with lamb shank. Â The orrecchiette was really, really delicious, and I ended up stealing a lot from his plate. Â The gnocchi left a little something to be desired, despite being what everyone raves about. Â I feel like I've had a half dozen better gnocchi dishes in the city (Spotted Pig, Frank and Barbuto come to mind). Perhaps I was just in on a "good" night but not a "great" one. Â Again though, I'd recommend L'Apicio and dell'anima over L'Artusi at this point.

This place just opened and is probably the best spot in the Garment District. Â The service is spot on, the decor makes the entire restaurant and the food is out of this world. Â The intent of sharing each dish is amazing for a table for two or even a larger group (which was what we did this past weekend). Â If you don't get enough to drink downstairs they have a rooftop bar with a direct view of the Empire State building which is out of this world - one of the best rooftops in this city.

I love the drinks at this place. There's a spring something or other that is super delicious. The south baptist is also a must for beverages. As for food, I've only gotten the appetizers so far. Love the country ham...you HAVE to get this. Scotch egg isn't bad, with quite possibly the BEST bacon ever. The crab cake is good, but small. The duck rilette (pate) is good, but not something I'd say rush to get.
very lovely place. the atmosphere is phenomenal. love it!

Very good! We are quickly making this cash-only restaurant one of our regular places. Meals center around their incredible homemade pita bread. Â The baba ganoush is absolutely amazing - the best I've ever had. Â I also highly recommend the "pizzas," which are pita bread topped with goodies. Â We've also had it delivered a couple of times and our orders were prompt, hot, and accurate. Â It's a gem.
Great pizza, blah blah blah, I could eat it for breakfast, lunch, and dinner..... you get the point!

After years of Starbucks dedication, a caffeinated epiphany has altered my coffee-drinking experience for as long as I wander the streets of midtown west. The Luna Cafe (121 w 29th) houses a strong brew, french-inspired pastries (authentic macaroons), and a trustworthy staff. this is no "press a button coffee comes out" type places: these guys do it right. plus the prices beat grumpy & stumps

For our anniversary, I didn't want to go too crazy. I suggested some grilled cheese or ramen, but the beau insisted on doing something a bit nicer. Applewood it was (although I'm still craving ramen). It was a Tuesday evening so they were only about half-full, which meant that the staff had plenty of opportunity to be attentive, and they were. The wine list was average, but well-rounded. The first thing that made me say "I'm so glad we did this instead of grilled cheese" was the bread basket, brought around by a server with a trio of homemade spreads to try with it. Both the bread and the spreads were delightful. For dinner I opted for one of the few vegetarian things on the menu (I can always count on a pasta or risotto this time of year!). My risotto was artfully presented and I thought it was really flavorful. It definitely was nicer than what I could make at home (which is how I justify spending money at $$$ places). The beau was more than pleased with his veal, an infrequent treat. When the dessert menu came around (I've read other reviews and I did note that they asked if we wanted the menus before giving them to us), it didn't take much convincing to split something. Good food, good portions, and overall a good experience. I don't know how anyone sits right in front of the fire, but it was nice for atmosphere (as were all the pictures of animals that were coincidentally also on the menu hanging on the walls). Is it a place to go on the regular? Not if you're frugal, but it's a good splurge for special occasions or a rare attempt at feeling classy.

Hi, I visited Bareburger in April 2014 on one of the Sundays with my husband and parents. My parents were visiting form India. We had a horrible experience in terms of service on 34th and 3rd location. We were party of four and the hostess was not allowing us to take two tables and join them in one since the table for four people was occupied. She asked to sit outside. That day the winds were cold Â even though it was sunny. I again requested her that my parents are feeling cold, if we could sit inside. Still the manager was reluctant do it. After almost 40 min she allowed us to sit inside when the table for four was vacant. I see that Bareburger's sole aim is to sell its burger with ZERO service. After few days I gotta chance to have a conversation with Bareburger marketting head since he was visiting our school. I told him the experience I had. He promised me that he will send me an invitation to the same location and a gift voucher as an apology. its already been 72 hours and I haven't heard anything from him yet. Â I am not asking for any gift voucher or any invitation. My whole point in writing here is to let the others and the bareburger know how I feel after all this incident. I have totally abandon Bareburger. They are not just loosing one customer instead 1000. Word of mouth plays an important role here. I am so upset with Bareburger that I would never ever go there again. I believe they only know how to position their products but not the people and the service.

The resturant is amazing even though im not a vegetarian. My favorite dish is the faux shrimp Lo Mein as well as their Faux Calamari I would recommend this to anyone and one who is Â acarnivore eater should go at least once their food is always freshly prepared.
If you love fresh and simply prepared sea food Kyclades is the best choice around. The sword fish and baby shark are delicious. Outide dining may be available but come early or be ready for a wait.
Excellent whiskey list and an excellent Manhattan. The biscuits make this Southern boy proud. The brick chicken was delicious.

my friends and I went for a 2 hour bottomless brunch. $20 for an entree and unlimited drinks was an unexpected and awesome deal. the food was solid and Italian themed with quality ingredients and generous portions. side note: they refilled our drinks nonstop. we couldn't even keep track of how many we had. we will definitely be back!

Though it was not MY birthday, I got to sing happy birthday to a gal that was pleasantly surprised by her date with a cake and a firework type of candle that was just too much fun! This led to a fun atmosphere that made way for the mouth watering dishes that were to come. -Ceviche: Mediocre, tangy, shrimp and avocado dish w/lettuce..good for those that like to fit their veggies in during a meal. -Paella Valenciana: Saffron rice, shrimp, scallops, calamari, clams, mussels, chicken, chorizo, peppers, sweet peas...this; my friends, made my day. -Cuban sandwich: chicken, avocado, and tidbits in a crispy thin wrap. So good! -Pulled pork over rice: You can def tell that the pork has been cooked over a long period of time; the flavor and succulent qualities were not compromised. -Sangria: Delish! Fun setting to catch up w/friends and great service!

Great place for brunch! The biscuits with sausage gravy were AMAZING! great vibe and ROCKING CHAIRS out front. zomg It's been weeks, but I can still taste that savory sausage gravy melted over the flaky warm biscuit asitdribblesdownmychinandontomynapkinwhereilickitaÂ­gainbecauseitssogoodandiamdroolingrightnow..... Great vibe, compact scene. You enter into a waiting room, where you can entertain yourself at the bar. I honestly don't remember what else I ordered because the sausage gravy biscuit is still dominating my memories. However, I remember being extremely pleased with the rest of the meal as well. A little pricey for the frugal consumer, but its a great place to take your girlfriend on a brunch date. Or, if you prefer, that girl (what's her name again?) that is still dressed in her clubbing clothes from the night before. Or, if you prefer, that guy (what's his name again?) that is still trying to get your number from last night. Actually, this place is great for any of the above AND any of the below. They have a COW eating a FAKE patch of GRASS. awesome. They also have ROCKING BENCHES (making that awkward morning after even more romantic for you lovebirds out there).

Best pizza I've had in New York. Â Go with the signature sqare or pepperoni square, but definitely the square pies. Â The crust is a great balance of chewy and crunchy. Â It's thick in order to balance out that extremely flavorful sauce, which is insanely delicious. We ordered this for a lunch meeting at work recently, and it was very late (delivery for them sucks, so be warned) but as soon as it arrived and people saw where we ordered it from, there were literally multiple gasps around the room. Â Once you eat here, you'll understand for sure. If you want the more expensive, fancy pizza experience go to Lombardi's down the street. Â But honestly, that's more of a tourist thing, "I ate at the first pizza place in America!" Â It's good pizza there, but this place is amazing pizza. Â And it's much cheaper too. Â It's not a fancy or comfy place to sit; it's small and crowded. Â It's just all about the pizza.

A review that is long overdue. Went here last year while in NYC. Awesome, awesome, awesome!!! The sandwiches are HUGE and absolutely delicious. I got the pork sandwich and it probably ranks as one of the best banh mi sandwiches I've ever had. The sandwiches have a good meat to condiment ratio and are reasonably priced. The place is extremely organized and well-run. Will definitely come back here when I'm back in the city and would recommend to all others!

I've been here a total of three times and every time, Tom the chef-owner always checks in, gives a recommendation and spends a few minutes talking to us. Tonight was special though-- even Deedee the server sat down with us and told me I was ridiculous for deciding between the Cobb and Mac&Cheese... the choice was clear. And it was! It was the richest, creamiest mac and cheese, even tastier that Sarita's in the East Village whose specialty IS mac and cheese. Felt like I was punched in the mouth with cheese. But truly, everything on the menu is great (I can personally attest to the pulled pork sandwich, burger and sweet potato fries). I mean, if you're a vegetarian, you might be limited by the selection and I feel sorry for you but if you're a good meat-loving human being, you're in luck! The best part is that there were only two tables in the restaurant and Tom sat with us and talked about his dishes, his childhood in New York etc etc. He gives the place such a friendly, neighborhood vibe and personally, I love how the horn-rimmed glasses and plaid wearing populace has steered clear of it so far (though I admit their arrival would herald the success of the place)... probably because the music selection is not as hip. It does win points for irony though... imagine Savage Garden side by side with Led Zeppelin. This is definitely my number one grub spot for the Bedford stop.

I absolutely loveeee cafeteria! I've seriously never had a bad meal here. I love their truffle fries! The fried calamari is fresh and super delicious with their homemade dressings on the side and the turkey burger is filling and cooked perfect. But most of all the desserts are killer! The fried Oreo dessert is like heaven in my mouth! I've always had fried Oreos at the San gennaro feast in little Italy and these fried Oreos murder those one! Great service , love the ambiance, and appreciate the complimentary biscuits they give at dinner. Oh ya $30 carafe of sangria gives you about 7-8 drinks is amazing. Love love love this place!

I was a huge fan of this place before they switched locations. Â The new location is smaller and not as trendy or fun. For our appetizer, my husband and I Â shared the Dulce. This was delicious and the best part of the meal. Based on the waiters suggestion, my husband ordered the Tilapia for his entree. Â When it came he felt it was bland and left something to be desired. I ordered The Gallitos (listed as an appetizer) for my entree. They were absolutely huge and in this case quantity had nothing to do with quality. The chicken was bland and the steak was so fatty and chewy. Â I didn't even try the shrimp. To make matters worse there was an elderly man with a 16 year old mail order bride sitting next to us and half their conversation was about sex. If the food and my pregnancy werent enough to make me throw up, this conversation was not helping! I was also disappointed that they don't have guacamole (something i was craving). But the free cheesy balls were yummy. We will not be returning to this place.

So glad this was the random bar my friends and I chose to walk in to. We were looking to just kill some time before we headed to another place and this place definitely was a good choice. Right off the bat, getting into the bar was nice b/c of the front man Samuel, who had a good sense of humor while we were going in and wasn't a typical douchey bouncer. We got in and the place was pretty spacious and had plenty of bar space. We sat at the bar and I went right for the whiskey. They have a wide selection of it and Cory the bartender was helpful and quick in helping me choose a new whiskey to try. My other friends were indecisive on what they wanted to order but Mario, the other bartender was able to help them out by suggesting a few interesting drinks. They have these all natural fruit, vegetable, delicious mixed drinks and they were awesome. Not your ordinary artificial tasting, filled with sugar kind of drink. They were really fresh tasting and really refreshing. So gooooood. Then, we closed our tab of with a bottle of wine and we all thought it would be some ridiculous NYC tab, but it really wasn't bad at all. If your around the area, it's definitely worth stopping in for those fruity/vege-y mixed drinks (I forgot what they were called, its on the menu!)

Decided to come here because I heard that Grimaldi's was going to close soon. Pizza was Awesome!! Unlike the other yelpers, I didn't have to wait online for an hour. It only took like 10 minutes. Came here on a Tuesday during the afternoon. Ordered: Large Pizza ($14) with Sausage ($2) and Extra Tomato Sauce ($2) Tasted really good with the extra tomato sauce!! Simply yummy. I like the fact that they added basil leaves onto the pizza - it gave the pizza a great taste. Cons: - service was kind of slow (in terms of the waiters - it took them a while before they came over to take our order and to give us the bill but I guess they got their hands full) - seats were kind of cramped in there - AC was too strong but hey its a pizza place so it's bound to be really hot in there without AC (I should have brought a cardigan with me)

For a city of its size, Manhattan still has a dearth of decent coffee shops which offer reasonable shots of espresso. The Jeffrey is a combination gastropub and coffee bar, which is perhaps an odd mix. I assume they are just trying to maximize the rent utilization, seeing as to how the two target crowds will likely be temporally separate. The Jeffrey offers coffee out of Brooklyn Roasting Company, and they pull a pretty reasonable shot of espresso. I was impressed that they freshly ground the beans before pulling my shot, and appreciated that the barista asked me questions about what I wanted. For example, she asked me whether I wanted it for here or to go, whether I wanted sugar in it, and whether I wanted to finish with soda. For me, it always makes me feel bad when my espresso comes on a saucer with a spoon because I never use it, and it's just extra stuff to wash. Plus I hate feeling compelled to drink the soda because I just like to enjoy the finish. That being said, those are all minor points, and it comes down to the quality of the shot. The steam wand looked immaculately clean, which is the first time I look at to determine whether to order an espresso. If the barista doesn't even take the time to wipe down the steam wand, how can you trust them to do the more annoying parts of espresso machine maintenance? The shot was pulled from a bottomless portafilter with what I think it was a triple basket, but I'm not sure because I wasn't really paying attention. The espresso was well balanced and remarkably easy to drink. The blend is very mellow, sweet, and creamy. On the flip slide it doesn't feel particularly complicated, but it's very tasty. It's a good everyday espresso. My only complaints would be that the finish is really short and the shot was surprisingly cold. My shot was pulled into a Bodum Pavani cup, which from my experience usually results in a mouth burning sip of espresso even from a room temperature cup. Interestingly, I was able to gulp down the espresso without any difficulty.

Always crowded with a friendly staff, but the food sucks. I went there one day for weekday lunch and had the burger with the truffle fries and that was the only time it was good. The brunch honestly SUCKS. They messed up all the eggs, the yolk was hard and the whites rubbery. I was embarrassed I had my friend trek all the way out here from chelsea and wait an hour outside to eat a meal like this. The waitress and bartenders were sweet and offered free bloody marys and new food, but even then it was still not tasty.

This is the best restaurant in the city! Â You have to go to Don't Tell Mamas after..Becco's 3 pasta combination for 23$ is unbeatable and the atmosphere is 5 star. Â Their 25$ and under wine list makes it equally as fun. Â Its 5 star dining at its finest!

The flavors of Ba Xuyen's banh mi were very similar (and the closest I have had in any of the boroughs) to sandwiches I have had in Vietnam. If your looking for authentic - you will get it here fo sho.
I have had my best piiizaas here, roasted peppers pizzaaa is yummylicious!!!

One of my fave lunch spots in Midtown. Always packed with lunchers for a good reason--it's that delicious. Kati rolls are like Indian burritos... super flavorful meats or veggies wrapped in flatbread. Portable, filling, yummy. Aloo masala roll--classic, spicy curried potatoes with tomatoes, peppers, red onions and cilantro. Packed with intense flavor. Chana masala roll--spicy chickpeas, tomatoes. Simple, hearty and flavorful. Mixed vegetable roll--my new favorite. Perfect, complex, absolutely scrumptious. Slightly sweet beets, crunchy peanuts, juicy raisins, corn, julienned carrots, red onion, cilantro... a mix of flavors and textures--there's alot going on here, and I'm a huge fan. So 2 rolls are good enough to fill you up, it's definitely affordable and worth the wait, especially at lunch. However, if crowds aren't for you, go after 1:30 or 2ish. Give it a shot... it's totally delicious!

I have to give them five as there was nothing I didn't like about them. Right from the waiting time. We had good company around us. They can use that spot for the networking ground. We were seated and greeted well. Food was amazing. You can read other reviews that talk about recipe breakdown. Everyone one has their opinion. Don't follow those, have one of your own. Just go and enjoy. PS:- their spicy or the 10 chillies spicy is not that spicy. Don't let that scare you.

A nice neighborhood restaurant. Stopped by last night for dinner. We sat at the bar since there were only two tables left but both were tight squeezes. The bartender was very attentive and friendly. The restaurant is cute and cozy, but the tables are very close together. The bar was spacious, although there was a big party in the front of the restaurant and I got elbowed a couple of times. The big party was also very loud, with one man who extremely loved shouting. So I'm not sure if on a normal day it would be so loud. Kind of made my experience worse. The heat was also blasting, so it got really hot at times. But if someone opened the door and held it open, it would be super cold. They should invest in one of those plastic entrances to diminish the effect of the draft when the door is open. The food was overall ok. Not great, but nothing bad. The cacio e pepe was fine, but even for a pepper pasta, it was just a bit too much pepper. Some bites were of huge chunks of peppercorn. And the spaghetti was a bit undercooked with a very hard center. The shaved salad was a lot of shaved root veggies. Not my favorite, but the dressing was good - sweet, tart, and well seasoned. The pizza was fine. We ordered the one with capers and anchovies so I was expecting something more on the salty side, but the toppings were few and far between. At least the bottom wasn't soggy, but it was a little flimsy. I also had a ginger ale - house made ginger syrup with club soda. Simple but delicious, and it inspired me to go home and make ginger syrup that same night! Overall, an ok neighborhood restaurant with a friendly staff.
first restaurant where i ate and felt grown up. Â everything is great. Â sort of crowded and noise level can be too loud. Â there is downstairs seating if you want to talk to your company normally.

Amazing pizza and desert. The truffle oil pizza's and tiramisu was delicious. I myself am Italian and live near San Francisco and have to say this was some of the best pizza I've ever had. The spicy olive oil is also ridiculously good. This place is a must.

Comforting, piping warm bowls of ramen and freshly made noodles. I would recommend the spicy ramen vs. the classic. I absolutely loved their pork buns! One of the best I've ever had. The chicken for the chicken buns are deep fried breaded chicken which was also pretty good. Service is excellent even when there is a full house.
Glad this spot just opened up in the neighborhood. Classic Brooklyn spot. Looks and feels dark and dingy, a tastefully crafted atmosphere. Great food and staff.

Been going to this place for years. Â It is the best falafel in NYC. Â The restaurant is tiny so be prepared for long lines and not a chance at getting a seat. Â I usually get mine to go and head outside. Â It's so cheap you'll be back for more!

an authentic home cooked japanese meal. Â I love their meal sets because there is just the perfect amount of food. Â It is a little on the spendy side, but to have a nice little place to take a good friend for a special occasion, I think it's a perfect spot. Â you want to splurge a little, talk a lot, and enjoy that you're treating them. Â the mood is nice, service flawless, and for those with dietary restrictions, they are willing to accommodate. I love their matcha drink. Â they float just a little bit of sweet red bean in unsugared matcha and it's perfect. Â not too sweet but not too bitter. Â Their desserts are actually hit or miss to me even though everyone loves their desserts. Â I've had a lot of desserts since for the meal sets, they come with whatever the chef decides and I felt that some of them are amazing while others make me head two streets over to spot dessert bar for a real dessert that will hit that sweet spot that I reserve for semi asian desserts. Â  a nice date place or friends and family place. Â you can reserve a tatami room if you call in a party in advance. Â you can also order desserts in advance to take with you. Â note: it's cash only and because it's upstairs, it's not really ADA accessible which sucks cuz I'd love to take gramma there. ah...and we can't forget the best part. Â ladies, the women's bathroom has a toto toilet. Â uh huh. Â bidet it up and let it blow you dry! Â  enjoy!

The Jane is an all around 5 star restaurant. The food is never a fail and the service is always great. The fried artichokes are out of this world. I highly suggest this restaurant for any meal. You will be very satisfied.
Eh. Ok, I get the whole oldest pizza place thing. But it's New York. There is amazing pizza everywhere. The service was hasty and the pizza wasn't that great. Don't think I'll be back anytime soon.

Ordered online for breakfast delivery last week. I've no idea why this place is so popular. I got waffle and easy hard eggs, just average. The delivery was not bad, in 30 minutes. It might be better if I go to the place in stead of choosing delivery?

I went to dinner here with my bf. I loved the cozy little restaurant, though my bf does not appreciate sitting table to table with the neighbors..... We ordered the mussels for the appetizer [8 bucks]. It was delicious and a good size portion for the two of us to share. For the entree He got the seafood pasta; which was soooo tasty. [12 bucks] I got the filet mignon which came out in thin slices. [15 bucks] i should have listened to my friend who said you stick with pasta when at an Italian restaurant. I didn't like the steak much. i felt it was over-seasoned and i couldnt enjoy the meat. but my bf really enjoyed it and finished the rest. Overall the ITALIAN food was awesome and the cozy atmosphere and affordable prices were nice =)
A colleague of mine, who is a vegetarian, spied my chicken over rice the other day, and got a Homer-like drool look on his face. It's street meat good enough to tempt vegetarians. Â Enough said.

Finding a bargain in the city is scarce but these guys def have the recipe. Dont let the long line make you stray, these guys are quick to serve and keep the line moving well no matter what time. At $6 a plate, there's nothing that can beat these guys. The rice is what makes it what it is. Im an eater and find it hard to finish the serving they provide, not because its not good, but the fact that they give you a HUGE serving! Def check them out if youre in the times sq/rockerfeller ctr/radio city area!

This is a cool little spot. Â Prices are reasonable and the vibe is hip. Â There was nothing to complain about from our party of six. Â Do not be afraid to check this place out. Try: Crab Avocado, Brook Trout, Gnocchi, Special Cocktails

I give it 4 stars but really I wasn't a big fan (3 stars) because it was packed and we sat at a table with people 1 foot on either side. The service was great and the food came out super quick. I thought that the Moroccon breakfast wasn't that good but it was presented great and was huge. Maybe I'm just not a fan of that dish in general. Great atmosphere. Would love to try the place again if it was less busy.

A solid place for brunch. Great food, great drinks, and good prices. I had made a last minute reservation for a group of 10, but half of my party cancelled just before. The staff was more than accommodating and set us up at a table right away, even though most of us were late. That was because at noon, we were the only people in the restaurant. Despite a great brunch, I took a star off for the atmosphere. It would've been better if there had been anyone else in the restaurant and a bit more lively. That said, it was snowing so maybe we came on an off day. I will have to try it again. I got the salmon sandwich and was very happy. Definitely try the caipirinha-- it was delicious and deadly! Everyone enjoyed their food and drinks a lot.

Whennnnn the moon hits your eye like a big pizza pie thatsssss amoreeeee! That explains the look on my boyfriend's face when our large Margherita Pizza came out. Never have I ever tasted the most perfect thin crust pizza. The bottom was crispy white still having a decent amount of tomato sauce on top. Amazing. As we walked in, we were asked if we wanted to be seated in the front or back. Either one worked for us, we were noobs. I'm glad we were brought into the back because we got a quick walk through the kitchen, I was like a kid in a candy store. This is a must eat in terms of food tourism. Make sure you bring enough paper, its cash only here.

I was very excited to come here for the first time! We arrived by 10:30am and tried to get our bearings because we were not sure how it all worked. We finally decided on pizza and pasta. We ordered a margherita pizza topped with prosciutto and tagliatelle with braised short rib ragu. The bread they brought out first was nice and fresh and the olive oil was great. The pizza came out and again, very fresh, but it was sort of soggy and all the toppings were sliding off. That got on my nerves. Then the tagliatelle came out which was absolutely amazing. The tagliatelle were chewy and al dente and the sauce was delicious. Good food but a little pricey for the portions. We browsed a little more and ended up buying some fresh butternut squash ravioli to bring home. (they were wonderful in a sage brown butter sauce) 2 things: I was hoping this was more like a food court style setup so I could get a bunch of food and bring it back to the table, but it wasn't. You have to choose what typeof food you want and then sit in that area. 2. This place is COLD. I'm sure it's hard to heat the place but I was freezing during my meal. I would love to come back and try the other stations they have. It is a pretty cool place!

Cool open kitchen layout, and really nice host (or manager?), but very disappointing brunch fare. Â No wonder brunch reservations were easy to get! Â  -Lemon Ricotta Pancakes: Not flavorful. -Parmesan Biscuits with sausage gravy and poached eggs: Â Looked pretty gross, but tasted okay. Â I take umbrage at the biscuits which didn't taste very good, plus they looked more like English muffins... Coat check available. Â Two single-stall bathrooms in the front.

Ah, the World Famous Grimaldi's pizza! Was it delicious? Heck yes. I was actually pleasantly surprised. My expectations were already high, so I was praying my dreams of the deliciousness wouldn't be shot down. My friend and I ordered a large ($18) pie that was half regular and half white (YES, you can do halfsies) then also added some pepperoni and sausage to give it some meat. This pizza was love at first bite. In fact, we finished the large! Perfect thickness and easy to hold. The pie itself has just the right amount of toppings except the cheese (hence the half star deduction) - not enough for me! I'm a cheese lover, so I was a little disappointed in that department. Other than that, I have no major complaints. Great location, outstanding food, and quick mediocre service. Quick Tips: 1. Cash only. 2. Walk across the Brooklyn Bridge after you eat, it's the perfect way to burn the calories you just devoured. 3. Enjoy the pizza with a Brooklyn soda on the menu. Perfect way to wash down a couple bites! 4. Rumor is that the line gets INSANE! I came right when it opened so we pretty much walked right in. We did see the formed line after we ate though. Come early!

I used to live around the corner from this place, and it was the highlight of my day when I got to come here. I've enjoyed the coffee, cappuccinos and cookies here. I had an amazing biscuit here on a few occasion and just could spend the day here. This is the place I miss most after moving out of Brooklyn.

Went for brunch...not as great as everyone claims. Â Don't get me wrong, the food was delicious but it was definitely over-priced. I had the longsilog ($14- double what I have paid elsewhere)...their garlic fried rice is to die for. Â But then again, so is my mom's! Â The drinks were just ok...the Pacquiao punch really does pack a punch though! The service was great...our server was really friendly and attentive. If you're looking for great Filipino food at good prices, go to Queens or NJ. Â If you're looking to cross trendy/modernized Filipino food off your bucket list, go here. Just once. No need to return. There are better places out there.

So glad we were able to stop by dinner finally. Â We didn't make it for happy hour oysters but that is okay. Â They didn't have a table available (no reservations) but luckily there were two seats available at the bar. Â  We sat at the end of the bar - which got us the closest view to the oyster shucking station and the kitchen. Â It was awesome watching the chef in action. Â  We ordered the following: Appetizers: 1/2 dozen oysters - different varieties Beer steamed wild caught clams Uni with salmon roe and raw egg Entrees: Cioppino Diver scallops with zucchini and mushrooms We were pleased with everything we'd ordered. Â The oysters were super chilled and fresh. Â The steamed clams were super plump. Â Love love the cioppino - normally not a fan because the broth generally tends to be on the blander side but not Upstate's version. Â Nicely seasoned tomato based broth giving enough flavor without overpowering the seafood. Â Couldn't stop dipping the toasted bread in the broth. The diver scallops - 4 huge pieces nicely seared - only wished it was served with risotto (as seen in other Yelp photos). Â  Excellent seafood quality, flavor and with most dishes under $20 - this place is rocks like no other! The bartender (Shane) was awesome - checking on us frequently.

I thought everything was just ok. There wasn't anything that screamed come back. The restaurant was comfortable but our table was too small. The bread that came with the butter tasted a bit on the stale side. They also served roasted garlic with it and that kind of saved it. Our salad starters were just ok as were our entrees. Wife had the roasted chicken, nothing special. I had the pork three ways. It was pretty good but i wouldn't order it again. Â I also had three oysters and they were very delicious and fresh. The service was very pleasant. I like the look of the place and on a hot night it was nice and cool inside and i love that. I felt the menu was a bit limited and with all the great places around these days i dont know if i will make it back here.

I really loved the food here. We went for lunch on a beautiful spring day and easily got three seats next to each other at the bar. The bartender was pleasant and efficient, so no problems there. The sangria was okay - not remarkable. I didn't pay much attention to the rest of the wine list, to be honest. The food was obviously of very good quality and well-prepared. I'm not over the tapas concept yet because it suits my attention deficit disorder - I can also take food off of someone else's plate without feeling guilty and there's nothing wrong with that! The fried garbanzos were nice, and the olives were really good - not overly bitter for my tastes as some Spanish olives tend to be. Their take on bruschetta was okay, but it pushed us over the line into too much food. My favorite thing was the red peppers stuffed with tuna and Spanish potato salad. Oh my. So good. I don't eat lamb but my pals liked it, and I wasn't in the mood for potatoes, but they liked those too. Overall this is a really solid choice for a glass of wine and some way better than average tapas. I'm just glad we were there when it wasn't crowded and we could enjoy the open awning and the relaxed atmosphere.
Beer is ok. Â Place is a little too loud and too crowded. Â The nachos are great though.

The line moves surprisingly quickly, and by they time you're done handing over the cash and gawking at the giant mound of chicken on the griddle, your round aluminium box of chicken and rice is ready for some serious eating. The white sauce rocks - you can always help yourself to more - but watch out, the hot sauce is lip-burning HOT!

Oh, Walter. Can I call you Walter? I feel as though I could fall in love with you, but you'd end up breaking my heart. You, with your bowties, and your plump, beautiful oysters;* you are both classy and classic, simple and elegant, and just a little bit out of my league.** You are so distinctly American, in all the best ways. Your food is hearty, but refined; flavorful, and skillfully prepared. Your menu is concise, and I feel as though I would be happy with any choice I made. And now that you serve lunch, I want you at midday. The steak salad is nearly perfect, combined with the blue cheese, frizzled onions and roasted red peppers atop a bed of spinach. And toss in just a couple perfect, West Coast oysters...afternoon delight. __________ *Not a euphemism. **OK, a lot.

A true original. This place is not Tex Mex - it is authentic, with an interesting and inventive menu. The chef/owner is very congenial and welcoming, and deserves much applause and recognition for his efforts to bring something a little different to Carroll Garden / Cobble Hill's Mexican scene. (I'm deducting a star only because I'm an old geezer and for me the music was a tad too loud and the decor a little confused.)

Meh, indeed. Always follow your gut people. My gut told me to not go here, but sadly it was the only reso I could find on a Saturday at such short notice. I can't complain I had amazing food prior to this one so I'll take a hit for the week. I'll try and make this quick. The place itself is very quaint, the decor is inviting and somewhat relaxing for it being so busy. The servers and hostess were very nice. The drinks were stupidly expensive here. I hadn't complained all week having dropped hundreds of dollars on meals before this but for some reason this really stuck out like a sore thumb. We started with the Crispy Cod. The batter was perfectly done, the fish was not greasy at all. The mash potatoes had an interesting tang. It all worked and was quite good, but it all went down hill from there. I ordered the Chicken Souvlaki which came with chips. The chips were really good! Light crisp and not greasy. The chicken soulvaki tasted off to me. I kept getting hints of bitterness in the chicken and salad inside the wrap. I picked out what I could and filled up on chips. I had a bite of the lamb burger. Holy over seasoning batman! it was an assault on my taste buds. The meat didn't shine through at all. At least it was juicy and not over cooked. But way overpowering. It was kind of odd because the presentation of the burger was really nice too. Looks can be deceiving. The lamb shank was okay, nothing special really. I'd say it was the safest dish on the table. The pork chop was awful. It was a dense, over cooked dried sponge. I wish I could have a do-over on this night. But oh well... you win some, you lose some.

wow.. single handedly the most expensive breakfast i have ever had... have you ever payed 14 (16 with tips!) for some pancakes?? The classic tomato sauce was really good. Subtle sweetness, all around great flavor. The classic beef meatball had decent flavor, but was kind of tough. As soon as you walk in the door, there is an open kitchen area to the left. Â We were seated quickly, because we arrived when they first opened on Saturday. Â It was hot outside and we just walked through two blocks of annoying waiters from Italian restaurants trying to hassle us into eating at their establishments. Â The interior is covered in dark wood, cool clean smelling air, an almost Zen environment in comparison to Little Italy and the summer heat outside. I am almost embarrassed to say that this is my first experience eating at a Malaysian restaurant. Â Sure, I have drooled and even cooked some dishes from rasamalaysia.com but have never been out to get the real thing. Â Therefore, I do not know what is authentic, or even what it is supposed to taste like. Â Hopefully I will move somewhere where I can sample this food more often in the near future and become an expert. Â But for now, I just know that it tastes great. We were so thirsty that we ordered four specialty drinks, ranging from $2.75-3.50. Â The Coconut Juice, was served in a talk gold glass with slices of coconut in coconut juice. Â The Malaysian Tea was a red milk tea with a slight cocoa taste to it in the same style glass on ice. Â My favorite was the Lychee Drink, which was diluted lychee juice on ice with five canned lychee fruits. Â It was very refreshing. Â The last was the Fresh Coconut Juice, which is a peeled coconut with a hole drilled in the top, enough to stick a straw in. Â While the Fresh Coconut tasted amazing, it created suction that took a bit of work. For appetizers, we ordered the Roti Telur ($3.95), which was an egg filled paratha with a curry chicken dipping sauce. Â I felt that with the stuffing, the pancake was too heavy and will definitely order the Roti Canai ($2.95) in the future. The dish that I was looking forward to the most was actually the Mee Goreng ($5.95) because of my various online readings and photos of heavenly experiences eating Mee Goreng from food stall vendors. Â However, here it had a strong vinegar flavor, but I did love the chewy consistency of the noodles. Â I would love to try this dish at other places to see more variations. The Nasi Lemak ($5.50) arrived on a leaf shaped platter. Â I have seen many variations of this dish on actual leaves that you unfold and find your meal as a present, must be nice. Â The kitchen was nice enough to substitute Beef Rendang instead of the Chicken Curry for this dish. Â The Beef Rendang was rich and filling with bite sized perfectly seasoned tender bits of stewed beef. Â The pickled dried anchovy with onion relish tasted great, and so did the mixed veggie pickles. Â My favorite would have the be the coconut rice in the center though, the flavor and chewy texture was to die for. Â  All of their vegetables dishes looked great from the descriptions, so it was hard to choose just one. Â I have always wanted to try shrimp paste and I love water spinach, so we went for the Kang Kung Belacan ($9.95) and were not disappointed. Â I have only eaten water spinach at dim sum with garlic or oyster sauce, but the shrimp paste gave it a better depth of flavor since it was meaty and slightly smoky. Â All of their vegetable dishes looked great, so we will definitely try more of those in the future. Â  Like I said before, this was just a small taste, and hopefully I will learn about and sample more Malaysian cuisine in the near future. Cash only, and their menu is on their website: penangusa.com

Can I just say Amazing. The chef has out done himself. The whole experience from the staff to the food was excellent. Servers are charming and attentive. Â The property is oozing with charm and love the whimsical play on the garment district with old sowing machine parts used in the furniture and decor. Visited here for Valentines. I was immediately impressed with the interior design, the ceiling is decorated with clay pots. The menu was a 3 course prix fixe. Â We shared the artichoke heart moussaka (anginares moussaka) and the fresh california spinach salad (not on the regular menu) for appetizers; I had the baby lamb chops with porcini and garlic mashed potatoes; and for dessert the only option was the Crisp phyllo Napoleon layered with Greek yogurt. Pros: the baby lamp chops were amazingly delicious. The dish served 4 fatty lamb ribs which were the best ribs I've had. Cons: Made my reservation a month beforehand. The seating assignments are a bit cozy. The food aside from the baby lamb chops were just above average. I was not a fan of the dessert. Will probably return at some point for the baby lamb chops!

There are experiences, and there are life experiences, and there are life-changing experiences. Technically they're three shades of one happening, and what happened to me here falls squarely within the latter. This is fairly life-changing pizza. It's good. Really damn good. Downright incredible pizza. Some of the best if not best that I've ever had. These folks follow the tried and true method of doing one thing and doing it well. There are only a couple of options here, and you have to know about them to order them. Otherwise you order a pie, or a slice. It's hand-tossed dough, marinara, fresh mozz, and olive oil baked to perfection, then topped with fresh basil, more olive oil and grated parm. It's simple. It's made to order. And it's downright perfect. I guess you can get a square pie with thicker crust. You can get meat added on if you know that's an option. And, well, they do sell some sodas. But it's all about the pizza here, and the same guy has been doing it for ages. The downsides to this concept are immediately apparent. They open when they want to. They move as slow as they damn well please. And they only accept cash (as far as I can tell). Also this joint is way the hell out in Midwood, which is a trek for anyone from anywhere except Midwood. On the upside, the people-watching here is excellent. We made a pilgrimage here and showed up on a Sunday afternoon, to find the gate down but the window open, and a group of people hovering out front. It took maybe 10-15 minutes to make my way to the front of the line, and another few to converse with the dude writing orders on a lined paper pad. The quoted wait for a pie was two hours. Two. HOURS. But since we come from way out west, and made the trek, we waited. It took the full two hours for our pie to arrive, and was it worth the wait? Yes. For many reasons. First, it's delicious. The sauce, the flavors, the fresh basil, the crust... all good. Second, it's delicious. Third, this was my only chance to get it. If I lived in town, would I do it again? Sure, occasionally. But now that the taste of this pie is indelibly imprinted on my brain, I can always sweetly recall the wonders I experienced when consuming this pie while I wait a much, much shorter time somewhere else. But I'd still make it happen. Dom's only going to be slinging pies for so much longer, and I'd want to get as much of this in my belly as possible before he's done. This is serious business folks, and it takes serious dedication to do business here. But if you appreciate good food, it's your line of business.

This is an Indian white table cloth dining experience. Â You'll see interesting twists on familiar favorites plus traditional dishes. Â Well thought out and excellently executed food. Â Friendly and fast service in Midtown. Â They have a full bar too. Do yourself a favor and give them a try.

We went to dinner last Saturday at Salinas. Â Gorgeous ambiance, as you pass by towards the back of the restaurant there is a table with fresh cut flowers, AMAZING!!! We got a table in the back and roof window was open, so we were sitting under the stars. Waiter came over right away, very friendly and very knowledgeble. Â We ordered what he recommended and everything was beoyond amazing. Â All the appetizers, entries, desert to die for. Â We would come back anytime!!

Amazing food! If you haven't tried it you're really missing out! Soo many healthy choices, there's something for everybody. The food is very flavorful and unique and not too expensive either. Definitely check this place out if your tired of the same old food choices.

WOW!!! Food was great, drinks were great, awesome decor and atmosphere. We wound up getting 11 courses for four people and shared everything. Don't miss the chicken livers. Staff was knowledgable, but a few dishes we ordered were 86'd. Ill definitely go back to try the dishes that werent available. Reservations are a must!!!
Horrible service. Food was below par. And it reeked of rotten seafood. They should call it POOPSHOP!
Food good. Bar service not good. My friends and I were there last night and kept having to beg the bartender to refill our wine and sodas.

My favorite part about the restaurant is the owner features a different mother/grandmother each night, as their specials for the evening. The owner looks for women from different regions of Italy. The chef changes every night and so do the specials. I like this concept because it doesn't bore the customer. There is always something new to try, along with regular staple items. the burgers here are huge! loved the experience but some things just didnt seem too fresh

This place is always so packed and booked up on opentable! Anyways, we came on New Year's at noon. Â I really liked my Louie strawberry lemonade drink! Â Yummm. Love their empanada options - tried the following: Spicy Chicken Seafood Americano Cuban Chicken with Peas (in corn flour) All were tasty, hearty and generous amounts of filling.

Ridiculously amazing! We went with a big group for a birthday dinner and it was excellent. They were extremely accommodating to the 18 of us. I recommend the clams with the special boil with all of the sauces!

Absolutely fantastic wine bar to visit on the UES!! Â The service here couldnt be better and more friendly. I love this place. I can't believe I haven't reviewed this before. Each time I go to the City, I try to eat here. I told a group I was this last weekend that we had to go... and, as always... Great food, great atmosphere! Loved the old antique feeling of the restaurant. Our server was amazing, he was very helpful on menu options and recommended our appetizer and it was awesome! My wife and I can not wait to return!

I've been here twice. During my first time a couple years ago, I thought these dumplings were the best of the best. This cozy wine bar serves up some excellent cocktails.

Don't let that 2nd Yelp picture of the Corner Bistro's menu fool you. Those prices have certainly increased since the first time I discovered this place several years ago. The Bistro Burger is still the same delicious hockey puck thick patty with cheese and bacon. Not the absolute best burger ever in NYC, but definitely way up there which warrants a visit here. Only gripe is that the price is definitely closer to $10 now when it used to be such a steal back then. Not too much of a beer person, but cheap light/dark McSorley Ales on tap too. Everyone at my table ordered the steak frites, and we all agreed we'd had better. This place screams Upper East Side. Elegant. Beautiful. High class. Expensive. The shop is so gorgeous, it looks as if someone took the store front right out of Paris & transplanted it here in NY. Â The specials change all the time, but the classics like penne arrabiatta, bolognese are always great. Â The owners are straight from Milan and this place has been there for at least 10 years already still going strong.

had the same sort of experience as the previous bad reviews... long wait, horrible service, overpriced not very good food.. Â  only couple things to add are, oysters from the raw bar were obviously not fresh (smelled really fishy and left fish smell on my hands) and the atmosphere suck.. unless you like hanging out with wasted, obnoxious, 30 somethings reliving there frat boy days

I had heard so much about Pio Pio from multiple people, I finally decided to try it this past Sunday. Â I went with my parents and my husband in celebration of my dad's birthday. Â I specifically chose the HK location as I heard it was the best one in the city. Â I immediately loved how subtle the door sign was, and the restaurant design and space layout is pretty cool. Â We ordered a ceviche sampler as a starter which was good but I think it was overpriced..$29. Â The saffron rice and beans as a side is a must. Â We split the jalea which was delicious and ever so slightly fried so that you didn't feel gross and greasy after eating it. Â My parents split a sea bass over green rice (I can't remember the name of the dish) and that was pretty good too! Overall, I'm happy with the place and see what the buzz was all about. Â Service was good (not spectacular, not bad, but good) and I would definitely come again.

Best pork bun ever. I could leave it at that... but I also really enjoyed the spicy rice cake whatever thing. The rice cakes are kind of crispy and the flavor is good. I wish I could round up 10 people to get that big ol pig... Also! everyone seems to enjoy the duck rice. I want that too.

Had the opportunity to try Jane for brunch when a friend from out of town came back to visit. I have frequented Jane many times for dinner and I love the vibe of this place. Yes, it can get a little loud in here but still at an acceptable level. The bread basket was delish as it was served with strawberry butter. I had the crab cake with eggs benedict. If you order off the brunch menu, you get a free cocktail or orange juice. I opted for juice while my friends went for the alcohol. Food and service was good. Others on the table had the lobster with eggs benedict and we shared an order of Creme Brulee french toast. Divine! Definitely an enjoyable experience. And yes, RESERVATIONS are a must.

This is very solid resturant and didn't disappoint, really 4.5. It is much better looking inside then outside. As a chef and resturant owner I was looking to avoid manhattan's prices for food I could make myself. After checking the reviews we decided to stop, we almost didn't go inside because of the outside decor. Inside is beautiful and our waiter joe was very good. Honestly the best service I've had a resturant cool, collective.. Not hovering, cracked just enough jokes that made us feel very comfortable. The food was honest and very good the only thing that keeps it from being five stars is some of the slight lack of seasoning, but honestly that could just be a shift issue. It was Monday lunch I doubt there A team was on staff. By no means did we not enjoy or visit, I left very happy and satisfied. I would recommend this place very highly, just don't expect John besh to be serving his grandmothers deconstructed Ã©touffÃ©e. It's a great choice and worth a stop. Those giving 3 stars and below probably sprinkle bam seasoning on everything havnt been off the island. i'm from out of town but would probably head back just to try the gator burger.

I went here on a Saturday at 8 PM for dinner with a buddy because it had good yelp reviews. Pros: Good Scotch selection, not too loud so we were able to have conversation, shepherd's pie was tasty. Cons: Pricey, server wasn't very engaging, more of a 40 something crowd.
Heaven in a pita wrap. Â Puts everywhere else to shame.

Love it, and excellent!! Â The food was absolutely delicious and the drink was yummy as well. Â The service was great and the price was right on for the quality, service and atmosphere. Â Definitely we would return, can't wait!!!

Long walk from the street to get there, but wonderful view of the East River and excellent new American cuisine make it worth the journey. Pricey, but lovely indoors, however sit outside for the view. Sea food and pasta creatively done.

What a gem this place is. I must've walked by this place 3 times before finding it as the the store name isn't very visible. There is a plaque on the store front with the name of it and the menu engraved in dark colors so it wasn't easy to spot. It's located right next door to a ramen joint which was confusing since it looked like it was the same restaurant. Came here with a friend who's a regular here. It's a small, chill spot with great 60-70s reggae. The food would be described as Thai, French fusion. Although, I came here for a weekend brunch, you could order anything on the menu. I tried the Sober Bao Benedict which is a fried asian bun under pulled pork, spinach and poached eggs. The entire combination along with their version of spicy hollandaise sauce was pretty much perfect. The yolk from the poached eggs oozing onto the rest of the food was just heaven in my mouth. It was also served with amazing crispy potatoes with tomatoes. I also tried their spaghetti with shrimp which was also just as good. The herbs in there really enhanced the meal. Everything was so fresh and delicious. The baked cod with risotto was also amazing. For desert, I tried the grilled banana tamales that came with vanilla bean ice-cream and coconut milk dulce de leche. The sweet yet salty coconut milk dulce de leche combined with the sticky rice, ice-cream and bananas was heaven. The head chef was there when we went and was really friendly. I definitely plan on coming back to try out their other dishes.

I've been here a few times late night after hours and its pretty decent... The service is not the best...but the decor is chic and modern looking... The food is pretty good. I've gotten the fried macaroni and cheese spring rolls pretty much everytime I have been here...delicious. I've also had a breakfast platter and friends have gotten the salads before. It's not a four start dining experience but its where a lot of people go in the city for late night eats....treat it as such....

This is one of the sweetest places you could go for brunch in New York. The food is fantastic, but it's really about the ambiance. My only warning is that the tables are quite small, so a larger person could (seriously) be uncomfortable. I had the croque madame, which was full of flavor and quite large. Their jams are also worth trying. I have also tried the vegetarian croque. It's tasty, but has a strong woodsy-mushroom flavor. If you feel wary about that, try anything else. It's a great date spot, but I think girlfriends would really love this place.

My fav. tapas place! Â A bit on the pricey side but worth it. Â Love the decor and great staff. Food was super tasty and on a Tuesday at 7:30 pm, place was slowly getting packed. By the time I left at 9, the place was full. Â  Recommended: manchego cheese plate. tastes so good with the tiny piece of fig they give. Cojonudo - Fried quail eggs and chorizo on toast Gambas al Ajillo - Shrimp, garlic and Guindilla pepper in olive oil Patatas Bravas - Crispy potatoes, salsa brava, roasted garlic allioli Croquetas Cremosas - Creamy croquettes; three each of mushroom and Serrano ham AlbÃ³ndigas - Lamb meatballs, tomato sauce, sheep's milk cheese paella was alright and this duck special they had for the season was good too. Flan was alright, nothing special.

Looks like these yelp reviewers are some critical SOBs. They say "so good" and give it 4 stars, c'mon son. I'm giving in 5 just outta spite. I'm a cheap bitch but this place is the tits. Looks like I've found the spot for my Korean food fix. The food is very well balanced in flavor, not too salty, not too oily. Â The options really make this place. You can do buffet after 5 (split in half, hot on one side, cold on the other), or pick up some meals that are shrink wrapped, there's even a microwave to heat it up if you'd like to. Â It's mostly vegetarian, but the meat dishes are also well made. There's a great choice of beverages, including some Korean delights. It's a miniature cafeteria, or I guess in Korea it'd be normal size. Come in and grab a little of this, pick a little of that, get healthy!

I finally made it to La Sirene, after literally months of wanting to check it out. We went on a Saturday night (if I remember well) without a reservation, and the place was packed. We got really lucky as a table of four had just become available, so we only had to wait for a couple of minutes. It's really cramped and cozy in there (think Ivo & Lulu, which is just next door), but it was a very pleasant evening. The cuisine is French and mainly seafood. We shared a bunch of things: we started with the moules provencales (steamed mussels with tomatoes, garlic, white wine, etc: very tasty!) together with the sauteed duck liver salad, which was also excellent (and interesting enough it was real duck liver, not pate). We then had the whole roasted fish of the day: sea bass, which indeed came whole with the head and everything else as expected (the best to prepare fish if you ask me): it was great. We also tried the seared duck breast and it was just as good as the rest. Great food, BYOB, very friendly service (Didier, the owner and chef, took the time to come to our table and chat with us), all for very reasonable prices... what more do you need?

Our well laid plans to conduct a pizza tour in Trenton, NJ was overcome by events. Â Rather than sulk, we made the most of it by having a pizza tour in lower Manhattan instead. Â I mean, it's not like NYC isn't known for its pizza. Â First stop: Â Rubirosa. Â  Rubirosa has a really nice feel about it when you walk in. Â Even though it sits on Mulberry street, it doesn't feel like a tourist haunt at all. Â It has character, and it's pretty laid-back and comfortable. Â The service is efficient and invisible. Â  To try and get a good sampling of the menu, we opted for a plain pizza with their 50 year old recipe sauce, a pesto pizza, and a third pizza split between their vodka sauce and their sausage. Â Shockingly, the plain pizza was underwhelming. Â All of that tradition and heritage added up to a less than memorable sauce. Â It was kind of embarrassing. Â However, I can safely say that Rubirosa more than made up for it with the other two pies. Â The vodka sauce was incredibly good. Â It was amazing that this was the exact same pie as the plain, with only a change in the sauce. Â All of a sudden, I was intrigued and instantly in love with that sauce. Â It was smooth and very flavorful and coated the crust nicely. Â This was really well done. Â Similarly, the pesto pizza was rather good in its own respect. Â The freshly made pesto boasted a really good quality olive oil. Â It smelled and tasted wonderful. Â The only thing I didn't like about it was the non-traditional inclusion of cherry tomatoes. Â They are simply not my thing, but I ate around them with no worries and was quite content. Â I am a sucker for a good thin pizza, and I walked away trying two particularly good ones at this stop. Â Definitely recommend for the pizza.

I went to Buvette with some friends on the recommendation of a friend who is a chef (at Peels, but she also has worked in many illustrious places - French Laundry included!). It did not disappoint. Lovely small plates, good wine and a charming atmosphere. *If you like anchovies - their anchovy butter toast is to die for!

I don't see what all the fuss is about. Â I had such high expectations of the burgers at this place and I was disappointed. I've had much better at other places in the city. I thought the burger was kind of small and it wasn't that tasty. Â I felt like it lacked seasoning or something - it was too bland. I don't know, I just didn't like it. My friend had the chicken sandwich which was super thin as to where they pounded it so much the bun was huge in comparison to the meat. The fries were okay. Â However, I did like the happy hour specials - $3 or something beers for before and the server was nice enough to give it to us at 7:01 p.m. Good happy hour alcohol specials, but not so much the burgers - I did not think it lived up to all its hype.

I am so happy that I found this place! The roasted duck gumbo was amazing, and I'm sure I'll be going back a couple of times because I need to try everything else on the menu. I'd say the atmosphere is more than cozy -- borderline cramped. Overall, spatial issues aside, I am a believer! Â I am looking forward to my next visit.

Yum! Â The food here is great -- very flavorful and fresh. Â I was exploring the area with my mom, and she thought it seemed like a cute place to eat. Â As is usually the case, she was right. Â I had the tuna ceviche salad and my mom had the hearts of palm salad. Â Both salads were refreshing and light; neither was drenched in dressing. Â I only wish we would have ordered an appetizer or two, because everything looked delicious as it was coming out. As a plus, the waitstaff was friendly and there was only a short wait.
For a slice place, this is about as good as it gets. I recommend the Pepperoni Sicilian slice. Â Its a touch pricier than your typical slice, but well worth it.
Best Korean tacos I've had on either coast! Spicy pork and Korean BBQ Short Ribs really really good - and quite different from each other. Korean Fried Chicken was excellent.

The atmosphere was great. The clay pots on the ceiling and the front opened to the street was nice in a warm spring evening. The Greek music in the background was great. The staff was very attentive. Now, to the actual food. While it was pretty good, it didn't really blow my mind. My entree, the moussaka, was the best. The Greek salad I had however was not very fresh. I guess I'm spoiled from homemade and authentic Greek food to be very impressed. But overall I'd still recommend it. Portion sizes are small-ish but filling.
Overrated! Â I guess if you get here early enough where you can get a seat it would be nice, but that never seems to happen to me!
Yummy !!!! Where do I begin.. Â A friend of mine recommended that I go to this amazing place with full of spices in the food and WOW it was amazing. Â My favorite was the Jumbalaya

Total hole in the wall that does a booming business. Â Eating a Cuban sandwich with a $3 Presidente at the counter felt like vacation, not a work lunch break . Â Seems like they have a ton of regulars as everyone was joking with the people behind the counter.

I went to Palo Santo this past Saturday for a friend's birthday dinner. The place was recommended to the bday boy by another friend of ours who knew the chef/owner to Palo Santo restaurant. Because my friend had connection, we got free oysters, glasses of champagne and extra desserts on the house. Pretty good. =) The place is quite lovely inside. For the appetizer I ordered the Anticuchos which is organs meat that came out kabob style. For the entree I forgot the name but it was a rabbit dish. The rabbit meat was soft and saucy. I wish the dish came with white rice because it got a bit salty for me. It does come with this corn pancake topped with black beans. Overall the entree was pretty good.
