However, I see that as a good thing. Like the dessert, I was told that there were only 5 rabbit left for our table of 14 people. The restaurant does not over order things which means they will run out something but which would also mean they do not keep old things in the freezer and the food the desserts are always going to be fresh. We were the last party left... Oh well. Overall, it was good food in the good restaurant with good friends. =D From my friends' orders, they all stated their dishes were good; Pan Roasted Bluefish and the Steak dish(Forgot the name). As for the appetizers, Tortilla, Avocado, and Blue Cheese Salad.

So delicious. Takes away the anger from being robbed at FlashDancers. In the future, just go to Halal Guys and skip FD's. Get the combo and a couple whites and a little less red sauce. No joke the red is hot as hell. But at least they are honest and dont steal your drinks like FDs.

Late night drunk food at its best! There is something about being in the city late at night, drunk or tipsy that sparks the conversation, the idea, the topic that always begins with..."I'm madd hungry...Are you guys hungry??hmmm... How about... CHICKEN AND RICE???" This is exactly how every drunken night in NYC turns out. I don't blame everyone though, this place really serves some good chicken and rice! There is a difference, like all restaurants, between this cart and the many other carts you can find in NYC. I absolutely hate it when people say so many things are the same, especially when it comes to franchised restaurants but that is another story. Back to the important things about this cart. This place is KNOWN for chicken and rice. We don't say, hey, let's go to 53rd and 6th halal cart. We say who wants some chicken and rice! That item has been associated with this cart which is a pro and a con. It's a pro because it sorta sends out that message of how good the chicken and rice is, but it's a con because people may not even realize that the lamb that they serve is also reealllllyy GOOOODDD. I often order the combo because you get half chicken and half lamb, which satisfies my hungry and taste for both meats. The most IMPORTANT thing to remember is to add that white sauce though. Without it the dish becomes dry and somewhat forgettable. It's not that the white sauce is that good, but the white sauce bring everything together perfectly. Because of the way the meat is prepared, the texture and flavor of the rice they use. All this for $6!!! That's another reason we are more inclined want chicken and rice because this is were you get the most bang for your buck. TAKE HOME TIP! Alright, you either couldn't finish all your chicken and rice or decided it take some home to eat tomorrow. The question is what is the best way to reheat you chicken and rice? Microwave???NOOOOOO. Microwaving tends to dry out the food and somehow loses a lot of its flavor. The alternative to this is my preferred, simple and easy method 1. Taking out a non-stick pan and DO NOT ADD OIL, (there is enough oil still in the food that will release after warming). 2. Dump the chicken and rice in the pan and start heating up. 3. After you hear the rice somewhat start to sizzle take a tablespoon or two of water and drop it in the pan and then immediately cover. 4. After 1-2 minutes take out the cover, stir until all the ingredients are nice and hot and serve on a plate. 5. Don't forget the white sauce!! Make sure you either have left over white sauce or a whole container. Add it to the dish at the end like you would if you just bought it! Doing it this way will preserve the flavor, rehydrate the food by steaming and keep the original texture since your cooking it over a pan.

We settle for Burrito Box beacuse there's nothing like it in the area! A Cali-style burrito place, there are plenty of options for meat-eaters and veggies alike - brown rice, lo-carb burrito shells, salads, chile con carne, BBQ chicken and the like. Take-out orders get a bag of greasy (and addictive) chips, and eat-in patrons serve themselves from the massive rubbermaid container on the counter. This place takes in a huge amount of business, so unless you've called in your order, be prepared to wait at least 10-15 minutes after work on a standard weekday. The burritos are huge, but the quality isn't amazing - sadly, you don't quite get what you pay for. That being said, I won't cross this option off my list given my dislike of The Man (aka Chipotle). If you're craving a burrito without the highest of expections, try Burrito Box!

2 words. Awe. Some. Group of us was taken here by our Greek friend. He literally knows everyone in the place. Downside - No reservations. Luckily the Belfry is around the corner (picklebacks!) so we killed some time and arrived with a lovely buzz. Now for the serious part - the food. Just fantastic. Grilled Calamari - yes yes and yes. Ordered a 2nd one later cuz it was so tasty. Â  Tuna steaks on skewer - yum Some bread thing with fried cheese - yum Mussels in marina - yum (see a yum trend developing here?) We got free raw oysters too. Had an entire fish, salad with amazingly good feta, salmon (not a fan of salmon so I may be biased, but I did not like this one dish), and some other things I can't remember plus tons of side dishes. Overall it was an excessive amount of delicious food and didn't hurt the wallet too badly either. Your meal comes with dessert I think, I was too full to even think about ordering dessert. Course when they put it in front of me, I groaned and accepted my fate. Took one bite, realized it was necessary (mandated by the stomach gods) to finish it. I recommend going to take a nap after. I will definitely be coming back here on the reg.
Very good down-to-earth home cooking. Â I recommend this place to all living or visiting New York City.

We came to eat here before we saw the show Then She Fell. I was a little annoyed when they refused to seat me because the other two people in my party weren't there yet and we then had to wait about another 30 mins since she gave away the table. However, the food here more than made up for that! The Spinach Gratin was out of this world. I am craving it right now! I ordered the Butcher's Steak, it was a nice portion and very tasty. My friend ordered the chicken. When the waitress told us that it was literally going to be an entire whole chicken with the head and feet, we just HAD to order it! They soak it over night in sweat tea. It was really moist and flavorful. Â The upside pineapple cake was really really good too. Everything we had was excellent. And the prices were very reasonable...$16 for a hanger steak? Definitely coming back!

Close to TBC's apartment and we all strongly encouraged her to make this her new Third Place. Â Great ambiance and REALLY great staff. Â We had the regular Bloody Mary and it was just right. Â The savory crepe was perfect amount and we wondered why it wasn't more crowded. Â  Nice outside space for comfortable nights. Â A really excellent find at the Crown Heights/Prospect Heights line.
The females are very nice but the male waiter acted like a gangster. Dry pot lamp is recommended. Others so so. Especially the three cup chicken-below standard.

The crust is perfect for those of us who like a very thin, crispy crust. Â Oddly, Table 87 does not have a pepperoni topping, but offers soppressata. Â The sausage is not crumbled, but sliced length wise. Â Moving beyond these oddities, the margherita slice is delicious. Â You can eat in or take out and they even sell slices. Â Really nice gentlemen take your order. Â This pie is a lot like Grimaldi's and Lucali's; nothing like Sottocasa. Â $38 for two pies.

Super Taste is worth the trek to the depths of C-Town. This cozy little shack serves very fresh noodles in a variety of meats ranging from-pork, beef, mutton and even eel. The freshness of the noodles is evident through the elasticity of each bite. Yelper's advice is correct about the dumplings- really good! Dumplings only come in one flavor- pork and chive, the only caveat. Did I mention 10 dumplings are only 3 bucks?! whoa. Big Yelp Tip! Add fried egg to any order of noodle or rice dish! I found this out after I finished my meal when I saw some 5 year olds eating fried eggs with their noodles :( I was so jealous....

I really just cannot get behind Sunshine co. $16 for steak and eggs and the steak they give you is thick, but smaller than your palm. I estimate that it was 4 oz... It wasn't anything special either. Everything here is a little smaller portion than you would like and not a great value. And the flavor profile they are going for is just a little underwhelming for my tastes.

I traveled from Manhattan to 8th Ave for this famous sandwich place. It is clean, simple and sends off aromatic fragrance of Vietnamese cuisine. I am here to seek their Banh Mi and my mission was complete with satisfaction. The banh mi is $4.5 each, which is about as much as that in the city. We got the number 1, which is the pate with ham and pickles sandwich. The baguette is toasted to just crispy on the outside and soft on the inside. The spicy sauce is creamy and hot. The combined sensation of spiciness, warmth and juiciness and freshness all at once. The bread is definitely better than Banh Mi Saigon because they still grill your sandwiches when you order instead of mass producing them and keep them on the stand-by. I just wish it is right by my house! I could eat this all day long with that aromatic Vietnamese coffee!

Had an AWFUL experience at Mogador. Rude, condescending waitress. PLEASE NOTE: If you have any food allergies, are wheat-intolerant have Celiacs, or require any food substitutions, they will NOT accommodate your needs.

Best customer service I have ever had from a restaurant in NYC. Â The woman taking my delivery order could not have been more helpful or friendly. Â To boot there was pad thai at my door step in under 15 minutes! Â Perhaps I am not qualified to review as I am not an expert on Thai food, I just know that the dishes were not as I would prefer them. Â However, the food was hot, the service was great and the prices were reasonable. Â Worth a shot if you are looking for that special thai place to call, "yours."

All I can say is Ramen!!! Â We came here recently while on vacation from California. Â In California, there's a big Ramen craze too, but not like Ippudo! Â It was another level of Ramen...of course there was a huge wait. Â We waited for almost an hour, it was worth it since it was freezing cold outside and that bowl of Ramen really hit the spot. Â One thing I did find was the portion of noodles was pretty little and there was barely any meat or anything else. Â I think they can give a bit more considering what they charge for each bowl. Â Service and everything else was fine, I'd be happy to dine here again on my next visit to NYC.

My wife is Turkish and we've been to Turkey together many times. Everything here was excellent. The octopus salad was incredibly tender and char-grilled to perfection. The kazandibi (browned milk pudding) was creamy and rich, yet refreshing. The istavrit (horse mackerel), little fish flown fresh from Istanbul, were fresh and perfectly crispy. The size is really great and $6 for mixed chicken and gyro is really a deal. Always the long line but moves pretty fast. Worth a try.

WAY better than I remembered. Service was also much better this time. Between the 6 of us, we were able to try many different dishes: Personal favorite: SEA URCHIN RISOTTO! Â  Other faves: Seared Foie Gras Philadelphia Truffle Surprise ~ basically cheese wontons with truffles PEI Mussles Brussel Sprouts Jumbo Shrimps Braised Short Rib Definitely coming back here.

I use to come here all the time since they were still a small store next door, but stopped and went down a few blocks to Prosperity's. But I still come back here for their Hot and Sour Soup which I think is the only thing that's better.
Very good soba shop. Â Good lunch specials with yummy side things. Â Zaru soba is good, as are hot soupy ones.
I'm a fan. Oysters are fresh, their house brews are tasty (try the Porterhouse Red), and I've also had the privilege of meeting the owner, who's a great guy with tons of stories.

F all you non-burrito lovers. This place is amazing and the best burrito I've had in NYC by far. And it does taste PRETTY close to the burritos at Gordos they are modeled after. I left happy and very satisfied with my yummy burrito. Go. NOW!

This is one of those places in Chinatown that's almost always packed with kids in the early afternoon on weekdays looking for a cheap after school snack. And what a great snack it is. I usually grab two orders with a diet coke and take it across the street to a nearby park to consume rather than piling in the tiny counter space. Â It's really one of the best deals in NYC for anyone looking to eat on the ridiculously cheap side. And it's delicious!

I don't eat oysters, but my wife does and she loves it here. Â I've enjoyed a number of other dishes though and really do love this place as they use quality, local ingredients, and everything is prepared fresh. OK, so the oysters aren't terribly local, especially the west coast ones, but they are all incredibly fresh - but everything else pretty much is local, such as the Day Boat Cod they had one night. Â Even the cheese comes from NJ. As I said, I don't eat the oysters but that's what most people come here for, and the empty platters and happy faces indicated something was right with their choices. The varieties seem to change every day based on what comes in fresh, and they give you a nice little cheat-sheet so you know what you're eating. Â Still not interested in trying those things any time soon, but if I did, it would probably be here... Â  I'd talk about the awesome beer selection, but I can't sample any of it sadly... Â I was still impressed with the list of the 8 or so they had on tap, a lot of which I've never even heard of, which is shocking to me considering my past expertise in that field. Â With my recently-discovered allergy though, I'm just craving some draft sorghum beer... maybe next time?? Â The wines (even by the glass) are equally amazing and different. Â They'll help you pair the right wine to your dish, and it always seems to be just right. Â  The first time we came, we were the only people there and chatted with the owner, but the next time it was PACKED and could barely get a seat. Â If that continues, they're gonna need some more waitstaff because this is probably my new favorite place to eat in the East Village and I'm not always completely patient. Â  The vibe, however, is perfect and intimate, albeit a bit too dark for comfort (I do like when I can actually SEE my food before it goes in my mouth) - also, the varnished countertops are beautiful but useless as they are not quite flat and are as slick as an ice hockey rink, but the owner said he was going to be fixing that ASAP. Â In the meantime, hold on to your drinks!! Overall, an awesome addition to the East Village, and hopefully part of a growing trend of fresh, locally-sourced and delicious food!
My friend and I found this place on yelp. The staff is super enthusiastic. We had pani puri as an app and dosas. So good!! They even gave us free rice pudding after.

Came here for a sponsored dinner and got to eat in the back dining room, away from hectic hungry tourists. Their pastas are amazing! Love that it's unlimited and they just keep serving you. I'm not into Italian so whenever I write a review for an Italian place, it means I really liked it! I would come back if I'm in the neighborhood and was famished. Surprisingly my favorite of the night was the turkey ravioli. Chocolate mousse.
best drunk food EVER! Â  Best taste! Best Price! Â Quick as lightning! If i was on my last dollar i would spend it on Mamoun's

Friendly service and big selection of veg dishes, both northern and southern. Â The spicier, the tastier. However, both my dining companion and I both got sick from the meal, as well as my mom for whom I bought takeout. Â I had severe abdominal pain and distress for a week. Â Never again.

I'll reiterate what others have said. The $26 Black Label Burger here is like a gift presented by Jesus himself on the day of his resurrection. "Hey, world, I'm back from the dead. And since I know you all like burgers, here's something else..." Yes, it is obscenely expensive and perhaps it isn't even "worth" $26 -- perhaps no burger is worth that kind of cash. But if you enjoy burgers... I mean, really enjoy burgers, then it is absolutely necessary that you try this ridic-a-burger -- at least one time in your life. My one time? 11:30pm, post-low-key birthday beers (at Blind Tiger Ale House) on a Wednesday night. A brief wait for a spot to open up at the bar and that's all I needed. Although my friends and I were concerned about a long wait, even for the bar -- because getting a table wasn't going to happen in a reasonable amount of time -- our wait wasn't too long at all and in the meantime the bar provided ample distraction with its solid whiskey selection and great cocktails that packed a punch. Will/Bill was a very good bartender. While I waited I noticed the crowd was not people in their 20s, but rather mostly 30s and 40s with some 50s as well; and mainly lots of suits and casually decked out people to amp up the atmosphere. And then, like I said before, God floated down from the heavens and said, "Mitch, please enjoy this delicacy and spread my gospel to the world." He then he provided me with a burger (no cheese necessary) that put all others to shame, along with a side of french fries similar to McDonald's in shape but much less greasy. I devoured my burger, ordered another glass of bourbon, tipped my bartender, stumbled out and somehow made my way home. Perhaps it was the alcohol that fogged my brain that night, but I like to think it was the burger that clouded my memory. Overall impression: take out a second mortgage if you have to and eat this delicious burger at least once, because this is one of those trendy late-night places with a signature item that will continue to beckon until you finally give in.
Unpretentious little gem of a place. Loved the chili chicken but would come back to try the other dishes. My husband loved his chicken dish too!
Very delicious, and cheap. Fulfilled my dumpling cravings, great snack. Little crowded, and not a lot of place to sit down but over all worth it.

Splendid splendid little spot for lunch. I didn't elect to avail myself of the drinks, but the food was excellent. After a bit of waffling and some advice from the cashier I ordered the focaccia pizza of the day [grilled eggplant and tomato] and some of the faro salad [much like tabbouleh but with faro instead of cracked bulgar wheat] both of which were perfect and well-portioned both for lunch itself and for the price. Heck, the bathroom was even clean.

Coming for dinner, there wasn't much of a wait for a Sunday. Â Bread was served to my and my girlfriend with the option of either spicy olive oil or the traditional olive oil for dipping. Â We opted for spicy. Â It was alright it didn't have much of a difference to the traditional. Â For starters, we had the fries with gorgonzola dipping sauce and the ahi tuna tartar. Â The tartar was so tender, fresh, and moist, it made me excited for the actual entree to come. Â Fries were meh. Â They were about 3-4 clumps of fries which made me think if the fries were either frozen or sitting under the heat lamps for a while then refried to make it seem piping hot again. Entrees, I had the red snapper and my girlfriend had the mushroom crusted virgin chicken. Â The red snapper came with saffron risotto, black olives, surrounded by tomato clam chowder. Â The risotto was cooked perfectly, but the tomato clam chowder was more like tomato soup. Â I don't know if they intended it to be like this or not. Â I didn't taste my girlfriend's chicken, but from what she told me, "It was bomb." Â She tried to cut a piece of chicken off for me, I saw the juices pour out, and from what I can tell it was moist. The service was average. Â The lighting was dim, and romantic; but you could still see the person in front of you. The music was fun to listen to: Peaches, Johnny Cash, Â Nickelback(lol), etc. Â It was better than the generic restaurant music at other places.

AMAZING is the only way to describe the sushi here. The fish is so fresh and the taste unbelievable. Its so fresh and tasty, you barely need washabi or soy sauce. Actually, the sushi chief tells you not to and shows you the proper way to eat sushi. You will completely offend him if you dunk it in soy sauce. For the best experience, definitely sit at the sushi bar. The chiefs are pleasant, attentive, helpful, and ready with any recommendations. The atomosphere/decor is very stark and simplistic. The waiters appear a little abrupt. Expect to see lots of business lunch's and dinners here. And you absolutely must make a reservation. This is a true sushi place. They only serve sake and Japanese beer (little disappointing for me, but sushi completely makes up for it). No special, funky rolls here. Its SERIOUS SUSHI.

It's pricey, no getting around that, but it's also good. Had the steak...probably price $8 too much. Nice selection of drinks as well as variety of food. Service also very good. I went for dinner but would like to go back for brunch. I hear that's wear it's at.

Dos Toros is my favorite place to get a burrito in Manhattan, hands down. My favorite burrito is the basic burrito, meaning a ton of rice, beans pico de gallo, melted cheese and guacamole/sour cream. I try not to go more than once a week, because I don't want to get so fat I can't squeeze into a seat on the subway ride home, but it's hard to resist. It's not super cheap, even the basic burrito is going to cost $7.00 or more, depending on what you add. At peak hours, the line can get very long, and there is limited seating. However, if you go during the off-hours and eat it as you walk, or on a bench in Union Square, it's a wonderful experience.

Wonderful brunch this morning - except for the sausage which I am glad is homemade but was way to garlicky and salty. Â Service was good even though they were very busy this morning. Â It was hard for our server to maintain his cheerfulness with so many tables but he never ignored us, which often happens with subpar waitstaff during busy times. Â We will definitely be back soon - the lumberjack breakfast (eggs and bacon between two waffles) is calling me.

The beef balls with red sauce and polenta brings me back to eat my sicilian grandma's cooking. I like ordering the daily veggies with my meal. Dessert - the espresso ice cream is a must! It's also good as a cookie sandwich!

I've been here several times, so I'm not quite sure why I've never written a review before. It's great! First off, this place is popular. So come prepared to wait. The staff is very kind, especially the proprietor, Cheryl. She may just be the one to step out and add your name to the waiting list. I'm typically biased against brunch places that don't offer unlimited mimosas. I've been spoiled by competitors, what do you want me to say? However, whenever I come here I happily order anything from the menu and enjoy each and every bite. I can't lie it's really good. Plus the staff makes you feel as though you were a friend invited over to eat at their home. I'm an eggs and bacon girl myself, but I hear lots of rave reviews about the French toast. Additionally, I appreciate that Cheryl's isn't simply a weekend wonder, they open their doors during week to offer brunch as well. I mean, who decided that you don't deserve pancakes and a mimosa when you take a Tuesday off of work? Thanks for squashing that unwritten rule Cheryl.

Truffle Burger and Sweet Potato Fries were delicious!! I can't enough of their sweet fries! I also tried the truffle fries thinking it was be as great as the sweet fries but I was wrong. I don't recommend truffle fries because they were too salty and had this weird cheesy flavor to me.

Everyone always references this place when I mention my neighborhood (Ditmas Park), so I guess I was expecting something great. I got the farmer's breakfast. It was good. That's it. Good but not great, and I have definitely had better brunch in the neighborhood for half the price. Service was ok but there were long waits, as well as a long wait to get in. Plus, they are somewhat holier-than-thou, which is annoying. You're not all that.

Going it Iris is like walking down a dirt road in upstate new york and finding a little cottage filled with delicious food and stumptown coffee. you completely forget that you're in brooklyn. great date spot. grab coffee, then go walk the brooklyn heights promenade. (maybe 2 blocks away?) the ladies will love it.....

Of the few times I've been here, the fries have been consistently good more often than not, so I'll look past a few of the "less crisp" fries on this last trip (not a totally lost cause at all...most of the fries were great). I always go to the Garlic Aioli, Horseradish and Mango Chutney sauces. Â Each one had great flavor and this place makes for a great snack on the go, or just taking a break throughout the day.

At the risk of reducing my BBQ credibility, I only had the pulled pork sandwich with no sides and a bottle of water. In my defense, I ate a lot at work and by the time our 9 PM dinner rolled around -- I just wasn't that hungry... This place has that particular item nailed down. Even some of the best BBQ Venues have made me feel uncomfortably nauseous after eating pulled pork, because its too greasy for my wimpy stomach. This was definitely the Goldilocks "just right" sandwich. I didn't even gain 5lbs this morning! But in all seriousness, this was a great dinner option. The line moved quickly and tables opened up for our group of 6 right as we payed. Â Can't wait to come back and try more things off the menu.
I'm now having my mail forwarded here.

Surprise of neighborhood find. I do not like 'Mexican" food. I have now been initiated to real classic Mexican cusine at Ofrenda. Â Great service and drinks. Â This also is a true value for a high end dinner. We have already returned.
The food at pies 'n' thighs was fantastic. It's everything you heard and more.

Overrated. I don't like splotches of cheese. I prefer my cheese spread all over the pizza. However, the pizza still tastes good, I just don't think it's one of the best. I prefer Totonnos, Arturos or Giorgios. But, it's a fun place to go to since it's so famous and popular. It's fun to walk across the Brooklyn Bridge and then walk to the staple NYC pizza place. This place has no slices, you have to order a full pie. Very casual, fun, lively and crowded.

Runner & Stone serves a damn good brunch on Sundays. I'll be the first to admit that the wait sucks (even with two levels of seating, it was a 20 minute wait after we were given a 10-15 estimate). The spicy Blood Mary is deliciously spicy; I believe the rim was salted with a combination of celery salt, cayenne and black pepper. The almond croissant was probably one of the best croissant I've ever had. The inside was spongey and moist while the outside was flaky and warm; a unique combination along with the almond flavor. A half baguette is plenty to start out with (we actually ordered a whole at first, but we were brought half by accident, which was actually a good thing). It came with unsalted butter, but for some reason we didn't have salt or pepper available at our table. I also had the smoked sausage with two eggs. The sausage was good, but a little dry. The special of the day was a prime rib sandwich with hollandaise sauce. My friend ordered it and let me try some; they should definitely promote it to the main menu! We sat in the basement (where inexeplicably, there seemed to be a Sean Paul playlist on an iPod dock playing) and service was a little spotty. My friend ordered a second coffee and it never came. Instead they gave us the check, which we didn't actually ask for. But the food was good and the people were pleasant. Would definitely recommend. Just don't come on the days I want a table.

This place is so overrated! It's not worth the wait. I came here on a weekday at 6p-ish and it was crowded. I think we ended up waiting like 40 minutes. Joe's Shanghai is known for their xiao long tong bao (shanghai soup dumplings). First of all, good xiao long tong bao is supposed to be light, thin skinned, and flavorful. Joe's Shanghai's dumplings are thin skinned, and flavorful, but it's not light and is actually a little greasy and salty. Chinese food is not greasy! American Chinese food is greasy! Nothing else we ordered here was that impressive. This place isn't Ding Tai Fung. In fact, it's not even close. If you've ever had good Xiao Long Bao, I wouldn't waste my time coming here. If this is your first time trying it though, then I guess it's not a bad start. This place is really for those who've never had soup dumplings. Additionally, my boyfriend got sick from eating here. I personally prefer Shanghai Cafe for xiao long tong baos. The skin is not as thin but the flavor is better.

I love the food at Cafe Henri. Â The eggs Benedict are absolutely to die for, soooo yummy. Â The sweet apple crepe, is delish for dessert. Â I only go for brunch on the weekend and if you go during the busiest time (Noon - 2) service can be somewhat lacking and your wait can be pretty long (it's small and they don't take reservations). Â But, in my humble opinion, the food is worth the wait. Â I've been over a dozen times and have never been disappointed with the food. Â I've only had the brunch menu but have heard that the dinner is just as amazing. Â I will continue to be a regular customer and think you should try it out as well, esp. if you live in the area, you might just get hooked.
I've been to this place a couple times and It never disappoints. Brunch is great and I've always had nice service.

How come no one knows about this place?!? Have you ever seen chureng fun being made...like from scratch...or semi scratch? This is it.....this is IT! Its not a restaurant, this is to go or you eat on the window still. Â Menu is on the left in yellow, very cheap and sooo sooo affordable! Â It's been so long since ive seen price like that. You pick what you want, you tell her what you want, she ask if you can green onion or not, and you wait and watch her make magic. Takes about 1 minute top, and you get the steamy fresh rice roll, all curled and pretty. Â You can get your condiment: soy sauce, hot sauce, peanut sauce and i don;t know what the other is but its good. My new snack, heaven, save me cause i dont want to make lunch - spot!

FINGER LICKIN' GOOD FOOD!!! had some great friend chicken and sweet potatoes and greens here. i literally was licking my fingers at the end of my meal. my bf had the seafood platter (crab cakes, shrimp and Â catfish) with mac n cheese and greens. mine was better than his but his was still pretty damn good. thanks harlem for keeping soul food alive!

This is a stunningly good brunch option given the neighborhood. I never would have guessed such a fun little place would exist on this otherwise boring block. FIRST IMPRESSION UPON ENTERING: OMG I JUST WALKED INTO A WALL OF WAFFLES The smell was one of the most pleasant fragrances I can remember in my recent past. Soft mellow vanilla and caramelized batter wafting towards me with a backnote of syrup. Yum. The food is hearty but not overly greasy and just the perfect amount for a weekend brunch. There was no wait whatsoever which is kind of shocking on a Saturday at 1:30. The food is french/belgian which is something I'm not really familiar with, but after trying this I will make every effort to get familiar. The coffee is fantastic, I had a croque madam (grilled ham + cheese on hearty bread topped w. a fried egg) which came with pomme frites (twice fried french fries) and a nice little salad. Except that my fiancee ate most of my fries it was perfect. Next time we'll order a side of the frites, because they really were fantastic. She had a waffle topped w. strawberries and whipped cream which was one of the best waffles I've had in recent memory. I'll most definitely be back. I'll have to try coming in the evening for mussels and frites. The only downside was that the staff seemed a little overwhelmed. I had to struggle to get a coffee and that was served without milk. I couldn't get the waiter's attention but managed to lure over a hostess and she was able to take care of it.
It is good, not as good as the first time, the breadsticks were cold and hard this time, but my goat cheese and spinach pizza was good.
if you love good quality, traditional NY pizza, trust the generations.

Absolutely delicious. Got the soup dumplings with crab meat- holy moly, bursts of magical goodness into your mouth & the pork fried rice- good but not as fantastic as the soup dumplings. Was busy, waited about 10 minutes or so, not bad. Cash only. Service was decent. Did feel slightly rushed, but I guess that's what happens when people are waiting.
Good not great, best was the pollenta appetiser and the foie gras duck ravioli. The rest was decent, but not great

We got here just before the long lines started. Thank goodness, because a wait for this food would have brought my review down to 1 star. I love ramen, on the West coast I live near Sawtelle and we have our fair share of ramen joints. So I expected a lot out of this place because it's Manhattan, it's expensive, and the extensive reviews. When you charge $15 for a bowl of ramen, it better be pretty damn big or pretty damn good. The sad truth of my experience is that it's none of the above. We ordered some kind of a specialty appetizer on a sizzling plate with ramen noodles and sausage. It was tiny. It tastes like some kind of onion sauce and with meat, nothing special, and it costed about $13-15. Next came our ramen. Tried the modern ramen and there was a spicy one I forgot the name. Both on the salty side and reallly nothing special. I can think of so many other better ramen spots in LA that charge a lot less. Chashu, forgettable... The environment was nice and the service was great, but it won't make up for the food or the serious upcharge. So for my little trip, I decided to abandon eating ramen in NY altogether if this is such a highly regarded ramen restaurant. I hate it when restaurants overuse the word umami to take advantage of foodies that get turned on by it.
Not bad. I liked it. But my friend was not too impressed.

Beautiful space with beautiful dishes - that taste as wonderful as they look. If it's your first trip (and surely it will not be your last) get the dishes that make Scarpetta famous. Spaghetti, Duck & Foie Gras Ravioli, the Polenta, and indulge in the bread basket. This is no ordinary bread basket. If you're a Scarpetta vet, try the Halibut or any of the seasonal truffle dishes. The service is amazing and will remind you why people make reservations here up to a month in advance. That said, make a reservation. If you can't get one, order at the bar and check out the nergoni menu.

Juniors is known for their cheesecake and they didn't disappoint. It was creamy and perfect. We ordered the plain and it didn't even need anything to be added. For dinner we had the cheeseburgers, fries, and onion rings. It was a typical american meal. Everything was good but nothing out of the extraordinary.

Pros: * Relatively big slice of Pizza (I had the spinach-artichoke) * Good tasting, a little salty; the little pieces of artichoke were delightful * Slice is pretty thick, the crust is good; Â the cheese on top is wonderful Cons: * Sometimes there's a huge line for it * Place is uber-small (guess they want you to get the pizza, then get out) * The spinach-artichoke pizza is incredibly oily, a bit salty, too So-so: * $4.50 for a slice ... Not sure if that's a good price or not. Â For a pizza slice? Holy crap that's expensive. Â For a thick and relatively large one? Â I guess it's worth it... I would go back if I seriously was craving one of their slices. Â Besides that, I wouldn't stop there.
Defiantly the best banh mi in NYC. The number one is so tasty I love the freshness of the bread and crunch of the veggies. Very reasonable and fast service.

i've come to Luzzo's twice now since it seems to be the only italian restaurant in east village that comes to people's minds but after trying this place for a second time, this time trying a pasta dish, i have to ultimately say, it's only ok. while the atmosphere seems truely authentic italian which leads me to believe so is the food, nothing in the dishes i ordered truely had any bang. On top of that, for the prices they charge, i expect some goosebumps at least. all i can say is the most exciting aspect about the place is the bread and olive oil. the service is nice also.

This place has a fun vibe but is very loud. I could barely hear my friend even though she sat right across from me. They have a good selection of beers and food items. We got the guacamole and chips, Mac and cheese and a chicken pasta dish. Most people seem to have been getting the burgers which looked good. The items we got were just okay. Portions were big, and 2 beers + 1 cocktail set us back $60. Not terribly expensive considering how much left overs we had.
Food is ok. Nothing special. Not worth the money at all. Go somewhere else.

There is not much here I can add, but I loudly proclaim: get the gnudi! So, so delicious that I dreamed of it later. Arrived here at 5:30 on Friday for first dinner seating, it was already close to crowded.
Amazing german food, pretty busy, but very worth it.

Colicciuo and songs A pleasant surprise! I just want start my review with this comment. Â We didn't make a reservation. Â We were looking for a place to eat and we were literally just Â "window shopping". Â  I want to say this so this review doesn't sound overrated because of the "no expectation at all" factor. Ambiance: This restaurant has a taproom and dining area. Â They are close but separate and they both have their own "feeling". Â The Â Taproom is definitely more fast paced and dynamic Â than the Dining Room. Â Even though we were in the "upbeat" Taproom I could definitely tell that dining area also had a cool upbeat "attitude" and was a bit more quiet than the bar area. Â  The crowd was mixed. Â It seemed Â more of a Â family or "couples" type of gig. Food: Like I said, we didn't have a chance to experience the dining room menu so I will, against what the proverb says, have to "judge a book by its cover". Â I have to admit that the food and the presentation were great! Â  For an appetizer I had the bone marrow and my friend tried the prawns - both dishes were super! Â  For our main course I ordered the Skate. Â It was fresh and well cooked. Â I could go on and on about how good this dish was but time and space limit me. Â  My "partner in crime" Â ordered the Cavatelli pasta with a delicate mushroom sauce. As she said to me. Â "I don't want to eat this meal, because if I do it will be gone". Â That's how good it was. Â Also she usually finishes his meal. Â She couldn't finish this one! Â  All portions were unusually large for an upscale dining establishment such as this one. Service: The service was great from the beginning to the end. Â Our host was very "welcoming" and our server was polite and Â helpful. Â  He was well versed about the items on the menu and was also very knowledgeable regarding the wine list. Â You can tell the management cares about its customers. Â You feel they are "ever present" while running this restaurant "behind the scenes". Â  In general again, you can tell they care. Conclusion: I will definitely be coming back to this restaurant. Â Next time we are going to eat in the main dining area to get the full dining experience. This place definitely left a good Â "taste" in my mouth, both literally and figuratively. (Sorry about the pun). Â  Â I only have one "rhetorical question". Â  Why can't Del Posto operate this way? Â You would think some of the "customer care" would rub off, they are not that far apart from each other.
Greatest food cart in NYC

I had business on Canal Street in Chinatown, on the day of our second big snow storm (of many this winter). I knew The Meatball Shop was sort of in close proximity, so I trudged through the heavy blustery snow northbound on Allen Street. I can be fearless when I'm on a mission, like to eat someplace that's on my list. I got there at about 3:30 and there were a few patrons, but there were mostly empty tables. Since it was my first time there, I found the menu confusing, but my nice waitress, Rachel helped me out. I decided on the Naked Balls, pork flavor which were a special (not Spicy Pork, because I don't like spicy), with BBQ sauce. The sides I ordered were Mashed Potatoes, and Market Salad. I loved the Mashed Potatoes, and the Market Salad. And, I liked the BBQ sauce on the Pork Meatballs, but I did not love the Pork Meatballs, and I love pork. Yes, they were very tender and fluffy, but they did not taste anything like pork. These meatballs tasted like they had very little meat in them, and instead had a lot of filler in them. I spent $20, plus tip and still felt hungry, & unsatisfied. The ice cream sandwiches sounded good, but now I was not in the mood for it. Â  I was so disappointed, I had high expectations after reading the yelp reviews. Did I order the wrong flavor meatballs? I'll see, perhaps I'll give them another shot, the ice cream sandwiches alone could entice me.
Good pizza nice thin crust.

Debated if we should have given this place Â a 3 star or a 4 star... Reason being that the service wasn't that great. There was an middle aged man sitting at their bar greeting people as they came in and he seemed to be the owner or a main manager, we didn't have to wait at all to get seated. But the server was not as nice, didn't explain much to us and didn't give us change for the bill(so he ended up getting a lot more for tip that he actually would have). They DO NOT HAVE ALCOHOL here!!! So frustrated because all we wanted was a place for a beer and pizza. Pizza was good, we got small, pepperoni, with mushrooms and it was enough for my husband and me. It was delicious, but we ate something very similar in Long Island city and it wasn't touted as "world famous pizza". Either way, nice place to visit if you're in town, want some good pizza, have extra money to spend on tip

A fave of the locals. Â Excellent french inspired, olive-oiled themed dishes in lovely surroundings. Â The french fries are amazing, and I had quite an excellent pumpkin/shrimp bisque. Â A never-fail, solid option in the W. Vill.

Came here for the Tuesday 1/2 off tapas (plus happy hour), which is a great deal. Sangria: strong but not very fruity Guacamole: deeeelicioussssss. It's so smooth. Arepa Con Carne: the meat was way too salty, and the sour cream didn't help much. Meat to corn cake ratio was also greatly unbalanced. Texture of the corn cake was great though. Platano Relleno: my favorite of the three dishes. The plantain was cooked to tender perfection, and the meat on top complemented it nicely. Should've asked them to hold the sour cream, though. It's a small restaurant, but the waitresses are kind of hard to flag down.

Food is good, not great. I don't get all these 4 and 5 star reviews, but the bartender and host were pretty nice, so they get extra points for that. Our wait was a little long, though expected. The bartender was very informative and a good seller. He sold us on a seafood tray while waiting for our table. It was good. For dinner my husband had the fried chicken, which was pretty good, and I had We started off with the fried oysters (good), and the bone marrow and braised oxtail marmalade (too sweet for my liking, but my husband loved it). I had a dinner special, which clearly was not good because I don't even remember what I had. Would maybe be back for some drinks and seafood trays, cause this place is pretty poppin', but the dinner menu needs a little more exploration in the creativity department.

The food here is pretty unremarkable. I had a Boar's Head-esque ham sandwich with brie and allegedly horseradish-infused mustard on a baguette. It was decent, and a bit better than the $7 price might otherwise command. Decor is well-executed antique Americana. A fine place to grab a bite.

Everything here was perfect. Â My fiance and I are never in this neighborhood but we were driving back from Jacob Riis Beach and thought we should take advantage of being out in Brooklyn so voila, we found this place on Yelp and we were so so happy. Â We feel very accomplished when we eat a good meal-- does anyone else? We started off with a cocktail and a beer. Â The cocktail was great-- fresh with mint, not sugary at all and a good amount of alcohol. We ordered the roasted peppers with burrata cheese. YUM! Â The peppers were so sweet and I loved the grilled taste of them. Â Just a slight suggestion: take off the skin! Otherwise, an excellent start to our meal. We got two pizzas: one with artichoke and prosciutto and a margherita pizza with fresh basil. Â Both were delicious. Â This pizza is a doughier type of pizza. Â It's like how Roberta makes theirs, and although I like Roberta's pizza better, this is very comparable. Â The vegetables and the toppings on the pizza were so fresh and full of flavor. Â Pizza is a 4 or 4.5 but the review gets a 5 because of the whole experience and the appetizer! The server was sweet and calming. Â Again, the whole experience here was perfect. Â We also sat outside in the back, which was really nice at the end of a day at the beach. Â I'd go back again if I didn't live so far. Wish I lived closer!

Cuban food the way your mom makes it -- if your mom were a Cuban lady. I read Judy K's review and had this place bookmarked. Now I'm just said that I didn't come here sooner. You have to read Judy's review. I can't do any better. yelp.com/user_details_reâ€¦ Like other have said, the ropa vieja is just plain amazing. The beef is so tender, well seasoned and flavored with their red sauce. You really can't miss on this dish. I also ordered another side of sweet plantains. The Cuban food is good old-fashion homestyle. I love it. It's very much food that a mom or a grandma makes with lots and lots of love and plops with in front of you with much gusto saying, "Eat! Eat! You're too skinny! Eat!" And you helplessly shovel the food into your gullet about to explode, but can't stop because it's so food and comforting. Each entree comes with a choice of two sides and costs about $12-14. Unless you're really hungry or have a big appetite, there definitely will be leftovers for another meal the next day. Yum! The service is warm, friendly, and funny.
BY far the best bowl of ramen in NYC. I usually get the Akmaru Modern ramen. Why only 4 stars then? Because the wait can be longer than a pregnancy! They need to add 600-800 seats to this joint! lol
my fav

Great space, intimate underground type. Had a carafe of wine, the eggplant special (great portion size, delicious, and only $8!), linguine with clams, and the 16 oz Porterhouse special for Thursday nights. All of the food was great. It started to get really packed and it's not the biggest restaurant, so be prepared for possibly waiting at the bar (not a bad thing here, they've got some great wines). Finished the night with Sambuca shot on the house, which the bartender poured for everyone at the restaurant. Yay!

I believe that few things in this life are actually worth the hype (see: Miami, skiing, taylor swift). queens comfort is totally worth every bit of the hype and worth standing outside for the 15-25 minute wait (I've never waited longer). their menu is ever changing and always brings it with unique, mouthwatering dishes. i don't think i've ever come here without being heartbreakingly torn between at least three options. my only constant go-to is the atomic mac and cheese ball appetizer. if you can't decide on a starter, trust that you can't possibly go wrong with those. if you didn't already know, its byob. bring a bottle of champagne, they got you on the OJ and bam, unlimited mimosas that you don't have to pay an extra $12-15 for. i wish there was a way to give six stars. ps, cash only.

Went back to have grilled sardines, seafood pasta and greek salad. Of the three, salad was best. After the top review i gave them on my first visit, this time it is the polar opposite. Sardines were not flavorful and the seafood pasta dish was awful. Calamari was really undercooked, oysters underwashed as i experienced super crunch bites and the pink sauce was flavorless and did not even adhere to the pasta. Nothing about this dish was cohesive. Tasted like if they just flopped everything on my plate n did not mix it in pot prior to serving. No free dessert as our first time as it was lunch time so left rather deflated.

Love this place. Got the steak which was excellent. Next time ill try the chicken schwarma - looked good. Got a plate. Came w three sides - I liked the eggplant, babaganoush, and rice pilaf. Id recommend getting a rice or couscous for one of your sides to help balance all the strong flavors and toppings. Then there's yet a final vegetable station where u can top ur meal off with all sorts of goodies like red cabbage feta cheese cucumber etc etc. I'd also rec some tahini sauce on top. Couldn't finish my plate, will eat rest as a late night snack. Will def be back.

I don't get the hype. To me, they were just overpriced fries with an okay dipping sauce. I came in and the smell of oil immediately hit my nose. After hearing from so many people how great this place is, I wanted to try it myself. I got a small with the garlic mayo and to me, it was not worth $6 dollars just for some fries.
Came here after walking all across town & got the halo halo to go. Holy crap was it big. It was a meal in itself. Â I wil def come back to get another one.
GREAT food, good prices, great portion sizes. Â We randomly found this on yelp and it was super good! Â The decor is beautiful, the service is great, but honestly, the food was awesome. Â Try it!

Food: 3.5. Â Quality of experience: 1. Â Hence the above 2 rating. We had a reservation for the tasting menu, four people. Â We confirmed the day before. Â We showed up, and our name was not on the list. Â So we waited for an hour at a nearby bar until they called to let us know the table was ready. The cool autumn weather had arrived by this point, and they sat us outside in the back patio, which we didn't know was going to be the case. Â We ordered the seven course tasting menu. Â Not smart. Â For three hours, we shivered as we ate the food that came our way, none of which I remember in detail because I was concentrating on staying warm. Â I ordered a pot of tea just so I could hold it in my hands. I'm hoping by now, they've either shut down the back patio; installed heating lamps; and/or put cushions on those cold, metal patio chairs. The waiters seemed genuinely sorry about our wait and the cold, but their expressions were about all we got in the way of compensation. The restaurant is so small that if you're larger than a group of two and there's a wait (expected or unexpected--obviously confirming the reservation is not guarantee), ask if you'll be seated outside.

This place was lovely. We really enjoyed dinner. We ordered a small size pizza, half vodka and half rubirosa special and a bottle of the house wine. Everything tasted incredible. I recommend making reservations in advance as they were packed when we went. My only regret is not ordering dessert as we were stuffed from the pizza.
After just arriving in the city, dinner at B4 was just what we needed! Delicious food, great service, loved the chicken with rhubarb relish and the beet and carrot side dish was great!

Fantastic place to have dinner! Ribs were great, and so were the side dishes. Downside was the service: they were focused on getting the customers out as quickly as possible, becoming very grumpy when ordering a drink after dinner.

Hidden behind a sushi store front is Â Katsu-Hama. Â  This place has all kinds of katsu, the most I've ever seen on a menu. Â From ebi to salmon, to regular pork Â they'll serve it here. Â My bf and I decided to both get the berkshire pork; one got the curry katsu, the other a traditional katsu. Â We wanted to taste the difference between a regular pork tenderloin and the berkshire pork. Â Sadly, although more expensive, we realized that we should have gotten the regular pork tenderloin. Â We thought that the difference in taste/flavor would be equivalent to getting wagyu steak instead of ribeye. Â It was not. Â  Needless to say, we enjoyed our meal. Â According to the bf, the curry was better than the one served at 'Go Go Curry' because there were mushrooms. Â I did not taste it as I don't like Japanese curry. Â My hire katsu was served with a large portion of chopped cabbage/lettuce with dressing on the side, and a bowl of rice. Â  It was good but not amazing. Â I would probably go back if I was ever in the area. Â I've had better katsu at Onya.

Came here for a quick dinner before a show around the corner on a busy Friday night, having made reservations beforehand online. We were seated promptly, which was a relief given the tight space. Tables are very close to each other, so if you're looking for an intimate date night spot, this won't be it, as you can hear everyone's conversation around you. Unfortunately, the wait was excruciatingly long, and the food took about 25-30 minutes before it came (I even had time to purchase something from the pharmacy across the street and returned to my seat before the food arrived). That being said, the seafood was absolutely delicious. We ordered the seafood spaghetti and the steak with fries, but the latter was overcooked and the fries were nothing special. The white wine sauce, paired with an assortment of seafood, including mussels, shrimp, squid and scallops, were robust with flavor and I will be returning for that dish specifically.

This has become a favorite. We love the pork belly and pork shoulder. You come out smelling like bbq but that's a plus for us. If you're thinking of going, be ready to stand in line for a while, but it's worth it.

It think this is my favorite of the Grey Dog's Coffee locations. This place is spacious, relaxed and the staff are very friendly and accommodating. The menu and food speaks for itself (same as all the Grey Dog locations), but this place sticks out because the experience just feels smoother, more organized, and it's a bit less crowded than the other locations. I love the sandwiches here and the breakfast options. The smoothies are delicious too. Whether with friends, on a date, or even alone, this is a great spot!

I don't get what people are falling all over themselves about. Maybe I need to eat here again, but once i leave a place relatively unimpressed it's hard to want to go back, ya know? I went here back in July when me and 4 other tenants in my building were evacuated thanks to condo construction next door. The contractor sent us off for dinner and told us to 'do it up', which is really a perfect way to sample all a place has to offer. If only the service were not so... (what's the word - absent? bad? knowsnothing about the wine list? then disappears? absent?) sucky. Either way, here's the good and the bad recounted a few months after the fact. appetizers: The oysters were reallyreally good. Escargot tasted yummy but was gritty. ick. I think i finally decided I am not much of a fan of Steak tartare. entrees: My Duck confit was tough. Flavors were good but how in god's name can you manage to make fat-cured duck chewey? wtf? I was more than slightly confused. Jessica had surf and turf. It was an obscenely huge amount of really yummy food. I don't recall the other entrees - I think people were generally happy but not enthralled. dessert: obscene portions. really huge desserts - they were very good. If i go back again i will sit at the bar, get a big pile of oysters and a big pile of one of the cake-type concoctions.

Whatever you do, DO NOT COME HERE. They literally drown every dish in lime juice. I've never entered a restaurant where the food on my plate was untouched. This changed after I went to Mooncake Foods.
Over-priced Pizza!
PORK BUNS!!!! Akamaru modern with egg and pork, Â It's all Â Delicious!!! Place gets super busy so come or come when they are about to close.

I recently had ribs here and I could NOT believe what they're selling in harlem. The ribs looked like the worst cut out of the scrap box that fell off the truck in the middle of the night. I have 'never' been served slop like this before and I will never have their ribs again. In fact, the low grade of their ribs really makes me question everything coming out of their kitchen.

Party of 6. Probably waited for like at least 45 minutes. The place is pretty small. Long waits. We were seated right next to the door. It was breezy and cold. My friends ordered the corn. They really liked it. The food took a while to come out. The food was really good but my friend's food got cold because she was right next to the door. The overall service was slow. Maybe that is why the wait is so long. The food is worth the wait though.

This is my goto spot for a cheap, hearty and just tasty comfort meal late night. Chicken and rice with white sauce (get extra!) With some dabs of their hot sauce! I dream of this from all the way on the west coast Defin. Stop by and try it

Yum! I had a Cubano for the first time. The service was pretty good, it wasn't too crowded (went on a Sunday night). I didn't get very much information on the menu which was disappointing but I enjoyed my meal and would definitely go back.

Been to La Lanterna di Vittorio a few times with the same group of ex-coworkers. We always have a great time catching up here. I can't speak for the food, but the wine, cheese, and bread basket are always delicious, and it's all very reasonably priced. I especially love the greenhouse seating in the back.

Fantastic dining experience all around. Â Lovely ambiance, attentive and friendly service, and delicious food. Â The kale salad was great and the chicken liver mouse is incredible! Â The menu is varied and extensive and I look forward to many visits to sample all the lovely choices that Mayfield has to offer.

whoa these portions are huge! Entrees range from $17- 23 but there really isn't much of a need for an appetizer. Servers were very professional and knew everything about the current specials. Their drinks are also reasonably priced. We went with for a pitcher of white Sangria for 19 bux. Not bad if you ask me. beers were about $5 too! and as far as authentic Latin food goes, this is as traditional as it gets. There are several of these cabanas around the NYC area and its good to see that they haven't lost touch with what made them successful in the first place, great food.

The good stuff, Pork soup dumplings (crab dumplings? Â can anyone really tast it?), Shanghai Noodle Soup, and the Beef (or Chicken) Pan Fried Noodles, Chicken Rice Cakes. Â  the rest.. is M'eh... It's very Touristy. Â It's a long wait sometimes, and you have to have EVERYONE in your party to get a table.

Ordered from here last night. They combined two shawarma orders into one tin and sent two measly pieces of pita. That plus 6 tiny balls of falafel came to $50 for delivery plus tip. Stay away. The restaurant may be different but delivery was a rip off and horrible. The food was cold, dull and pasty.

The food, drink and environment here are all excellent. It was tough to carry a conversation with the live music, but the music was good -- so go here if you have dinner company you'd rather not talk to. I've had Cuban food at several different places around the city and this is easily Top 3. The bistec de palomilla is off the charts.
Very cozy restaurant and worth a visit. Â Pizza's are gourmet and all organic.

Having a husband from Austria, we decided to try Steinhof for our anniversary. The consommÃ© soup was pretty tasteless (needed salt and chives, but only had floating parsley bits instead) and the schnitzels, just so-so...Veal would have been better..Everything needed salt. They put the weiner schnitzel on top of a pile of pickles (cucumber salad?) so it got a bit soggy on the bottom. Â Bigger plates would have helped in that case. They have those little oval diner plates. The potatoes were dried out. The rice bland. The farmer's cheese appetizer was good, but not very authentic. Tasted more like veg cream cheese and the salad had ranch dressing:( I think the cook was Mexican? The waitress was nice, and the space cozy. But yea, there is bad rock/pop music a bit too loud as someone else mentioned. I can see it being appealing on a winter evening, esp on the $6 goulash nights. I'll stick to Blaue Ganz for more authentic Austrian fare.
Delicious little brunch place.

What a great, cutely adorned location for warming up from the winter cold, catching up with old friends over a cup o'joe and some twists on some breakfast favorites~ The decour in here is very cozy, warm.. something so different from the busy streets that you escape from once you step through the doors of Penelope. The waiters were so friendly, I felt so at home and welcome. In terms of the actual meal... my friend and I enjoyed the "Punkin' Waffles" and "Nutella French Toast." The Punkin Waffles came with a side of warm, apple-pie filling YUM.. which was quite a good combo when eaten with a bite of pumpkin waffle. The Nutella French Toast could've come a little more nutella-y, but the french toast was so fluffy and fried so nicely along the edges.. . so delicious. Not to mention, the french toast comes with a side of fruit, so refreshing :) My friend and I didn't opt for this, but I was definitely intrigued by the Apple Cider Mimosa and Pomegranate Bellini, two drink choices (other than coffee/tea) that you can choose to go with your brunch, as part of the Prix-Fixe option. Will definitely have to try those drinks, sometime! In terms of the wait: Party of 2, got their around 10:30am on a Saturday, got seated after 35 minutes.

I went to Lombardi's Pizza, so I could try NY style pizza. Â I wasn't sure what to expect, but I was pleasantly surprised. I ordered two large pizzas split among 5 people. Â  One had sausage and red peppers and the other one was a simple pepperoni. Although I'm used to greasy pizzas with a ton of cheese, Lombardi's was thin and not greasy at all. It was REALLY good and the perfect type of pizza for those who want to enjoy something on the lighter side. Â The server mentioned the ingredients were fresh and natural which was great to know! Â  I would definitely return here because this is the type of pizza I enjoy, but have had a hard time finding...
By far best new restaurant in NYC!
Clued-up Traif ! Your service is excellent. Many thanks with regard to maintain me personally inform. To learn more I'll be in contact.

I have been here twice and had two very different experiences, making it difficult to rate. 2 stars for experience 3 stars for the food The first time I came it was about 5:30 on a weeknight, so we got a table outside for happy hour. I ordered the turkey burger first, but since it was so small I got the sweet potato fries after. I eat beef, but try to go for a healthier option when it is available. I have been eating turkey burgers for years and I honestly think this was the best tasting turkey burger I have ever had. That being said I am sure most people who head to a burger join want the beef; more on that later. I think I had 2 beers, the burger and fries and it was around $20; not a bad deal (it was happy hour) My return was on a Friday evening 7pm-right when happy hour ends :( I ordered an organic pale ale (I didn't know beer could be organic too...) Since there are only 4 outdoor tables they offered us the option to share with another group, which I am really not into so we opted to sit indoors. Well...I didn't realize how 'child-friendly' this place was. The dimly lit room, techno music, and crying babies made me want to eat and run! I understand how helpful it must be for some people to have the option of bringing their children out to eat, and burgers are pretty standard child fare but the long bar that takes up most of the restaurant gives this place more of a bar (read: adult) feel and I just didn't expect it. I ordered the turkey burger again, still very good. It was hard to hear the person I was sitting next across from, who also got wet when a child spilled a drink on his leg. I tried the beef burger which was tasty but not amazing, the best part of both burgers was the 'special sauce' one of those mayo-ketchup combos. We tried the 'greek fries' which are basically fries with feta and oregano thrown on them. This is just impractical. It was nearly impossible to get the cheese on a fry. We resorted to using forks for our fries, a little ridiculous if you ask me! My last experience was really a deterrent. I would only go here if I could sit in the backyard and there were no children.

This place is popular! Went there around noon and the wait time is 30 minutes! But it was worth it. It's very clean, service is great, except the waitress spoke very fast. Ramen was a great treat. Also make sure to order the bun - couldn't quite remember the name but second to last on the appetizer list. Overall quite a pleasant experience.

The premise of this establishment is nothing short of sheer financial brilliance: Cheap raw materials (potatoes, vegetable oil, salt), a few fancy sauces, charge $10 and have a line out the door at midnight. Â Why can't I come up with such an idea to mint $$$$? Anyways the fries are good-I wouldn't say spectacular. Â Nice crusty exterior and fluffy interior, nicely salted, but the contrast between the two should be more pronounced. Also a great annoyance of mine is the fries towards the outside/opening of the container are nice, large whole piece, altjough when you dig, below the surface there are tons of burnt, barely edible remnants. Sauces are okay, had the sweet chili (more sweet than hot), barbecue (straight out of a bottle) and pomegranate teriyaki (tasted of nothing barely resembling teriyaki or pomegrante-tasted more like honey mustard). Although good fries I'd say its a bit overpriced and the sauces are below par.
I came back for a second time completely sober and it was still amazing, cheap falafel!

Great spot for date night or a night out with friends. All the pizza's on the menu are neighborhoods in Brooklyn which was a cute touch. Very interesting pizza ingredients that you wouldn't get from your typical pizza joint. Totally worth the trip to give it a shot! They even have a pizza with brussels sprouts...yes I said brussels sprouts!

I had the day off. I did. So a stroll along Smith, after a nice haircut (thanks Setsuko at Fumi!) was in order. Also it was time to eat. When I eat alone, the decision of where to eat while out is very difficult. I'm often overwhelmed by the way the restaurant looks and who eats there. Also I get very self-conscious. Probably why I don't eat out alone very often. Passed Seersucker, which looked great, but I couldn't really check it out that well, and wasn't feeling the menu that day. Same with Cuban. Both are lovely, I'm sure. Another time, friends. Jolie, which was empty (it was the first Friday of the year, lunchtime), was just where my stomach said: "Enough, Syl." Menu looked good, so I walked in. I often gauge service on how quickly people respond when I enter a place alone... ( I often leave, yes, soon after, I need to lower my standards. ) It didn't take forever. I was soon seated and offered a menu. I also wanted a drink. (My day off!) Every drink sounded delicious. But I also had a sore throat... sigh. So I asked, is there anything warm I could drink. The nice man (possibly the owner?) offered a tea with tequila + agave. I nodded enthusiastically. It arrived, a cup that looked a lot like hot water with lemon, but tasted much, much better. A great start. It was the Grande Pozole soup item that drew me in. On a cold January day, it's hard to resist soup. Plus, it had a key irresistible ingredient: OXTAIL. I ordered it, but I wasn't sure it would be that 'grande,' so I ordered the Kale Caesar. I asked the nice man if I should include the seafood addition. He was so nice - he said no! I wouldn't be able to finish all of that with the soup. When the soup arrived, I was astonished: it was truly grande. (The price, $12, made more sense then as well.) The tequila tea was a warm blanket for my throat. The soup, a delicious warm coating in my belly: a hearty mix of pozole and oxtail (delicious threads of beef that were sometimes awkward to eat for my self-conscious self, but delicious all the same.) They must've noticed that I love spicy too - and put a small plate of chili flakes beside the bowl. Good call, people!! I took in the whole thing. And I was full. Sigh. But wait! The salad was coming, oh dear. Could I eat it? And what if it was a very dense Caesar dressing, something that would mess with the deliciously hearty but not overbearing soup? Of course it wasn't dense. It was lightly dressed, but just-dressed enough to give a nice flavor. The beets were delicious and sweet, a nice balance to the kale mix. And I ate the whole thing. Yum.

Bright and classy shop on Madison. Â It fits right in with the surrounding boutiques/stores. Â Close to closing time there's still a line but it moves. Â The only thing is, there'll be a few flavors that are sold out... :( Â I must say, these are very good macarons. Â Super light with a flaky outside, slight chew right after and a lot of flavor from the fillings. Â They may look small but they pack a LOT of flavor and are quite filling. Â It'll still be a few bites to enjoy this delicious treat. Â If you're not doing this? You're rushing it! *chocolate: nice chocolatey profile but despite being a chocolate lover, this was only 4th fave. *praline: i usually love praline, having grown up on praline ice cream and whatnot but this was too nutty for me, almost to the point of almost being savory. *raspberry: you have the raspberry and you have the light flaky chew *coconut: a LOT of coconut flavor here. the filling is packed with coconut flakes and has a nice gooey texture. good but a tad sweet *black currant & violet: this was my absolute favorite. just the right amount of jam like filling and just the right amount of sweet and tart. I could go and get just these and be happy *coffee: second favorite, love anything coffee and this came through, tastes like coffee ice cream :) (thanks to the lovely door lady for pointing that out!) *pistachio: if you love pistachio ice cream or pistachios in general, get this. soooo good, i think it has tied with black currant & violet these are not cheap by any means but consider what you're getting: the best macarons + service + quality + beautiful packaging.

I try to not to eat any obvious carbs (potatoes, rice, bread, pasta, etc); therefore, I always find myself having a real hard time feeling full after a meal out, especially in New York, usually paying something stupid like $24 for a boring salad or a burger without the bun. Rabbithole has the most amazing filling salad I've ever had... it's the shaved leek and spiced bacon salad, which happens to include not only those two yummy ingredients but also some other filling things like parmesan cheese and avocado. Totally totally yummy and substantial for a mere $12. I think I've had it like 6 times. The ambiance is also pretty rad, and they've got a decent mixology menu which I always appreciate. Hoorah!

Amazing place!! The inside is very classy and nice for a fast food-esque place. Ordered the falafel trio platter, and was blown away by how great it looked! Lots of food, very colorful, and neat. The platter was plenty between 2 of us. Definitely going back again!

Love the weekend specials of cheap beer and cheap gyoza. Food here is quite cheap for midtown and you can get a side of udon in broth with virtually every entree. They also have this one Japanese pork taco on the menu that I'm strangely addicted to.
Good beer selection but you can get that at George Keeley's on the next block. The food is decent but over priced for comfort food.

Wow. Fantastic. I'm so glad that I was able to fit this stop in on my brief stay in Brooklyn. Â This place kicks Roberta's ass! (Sorry Roberta.). The crust is the secret weapon, the one-two punch, the cat's meow. Â They figured out how to get the right balance of just enough (carcinogenic) char. Â Why do other places feel the need to overdo in that area? The customers are a wonderfully and refreshingly diverse bunch. Love this place.
Love the bar tender and waitstaff.

Another amazing night at Baoburg! Had a gathering of 10 friends to celebrate a 25th birthday. Everyone was overwhelmed by the fantastic food!! We sampled so many dishes, no one could choose a favorite they were all so good. The duck, the cod, the ribs, the specials, the mussels, the beets, the Brussels sprouts, the truffle fries, each dish was amazing, unbelievably flavorful. Chef Baobao is one of the most talented chefs around. I can't say enough about what a gem this place is. Make sure to visit the next time you are in Williamsburg! Baoburg has food that will amaze you along with a great atmosphere. It's friendly and fun with a good wine list and a great waitstaff. It's small, I would recommend a reservation so you don't have to stand in line waiting for a table. Baoburg is of our all time favorite places to visit in Brooklyn and really one of our favorites anywhere! Try it, you won't be disappointed!
I didn't think artic char this well prepared could be had in NYC. Â Ordered medium rare and it was deeelicious. Â I will definitely come back.....prolly just for this dish!
Fresh oysters and seafood. Simple and on point. Will definitely come back, it gets crowded easily though, come with patience.

Pricey but the flavors in every dish was out of this world! My date and I went for the tasting menu with two glasses of wine. Everything was so flavorful and rich. Moreover, our waiter was so attentive and sweet.

To all my SoCal transplants or just people with any knowledge of what decent Mexican food is (no I'm sorry, Chipotle doesn't count), Taqueria Diana might be the closest and best thing we get out here in NYC. Opened by a homesick Californian (Matthew La Rue), this little establishment brings the flavors that have been missing out here for so long. Around the corner of St. Marks you'll find this little gem dishing out some amazing food. It's even open late til 4am on Fri and Sat! -Food- Pastor Burrito 4/5- good portions of spit roast pork, rice, beans, salsa, + your choice of extras like queso which I recommend. Definitely can taste the meat and spices that went into the marinade Nachos 4/5 - whatever meat you want from chicken to carnitas. HUGE portion definitely share unless your a giant pig which is also fine. Great for that hang over food. TIP: Don't forget to try out the salsas which is another gauge Â of how good a Mexican restaurant .and yes they have amazing salsas.

Totally lived up to the hype and was a truly wonderful meal. There were four of us and we started with the polenta which was so creamy, the mozzarella, and another dish that had a mix of jalapeÃ±os, calamari, etc. The bread basket is also delicious and has stromboli in it! For my main dish, I had the foie grais ravioli which was rich but so delicious. The three other people I was with had the spaghetti (sweet and simple), the linguini with lobster (light and creamy), and the short rib pasta (amazing). Everything was fresh and absolutely delicious. We had to get dessert and went with the banana bread concoction and the chocolate cake and both were outstanding. Add on two great bottles of wine and we had quite the night. The service was excellent as well. Go and enjoy!
Really cool place and everything is delicious. Ask for a sample of sauces and they will hook it up. I got the large poutine which was great, but I kind of wish I went with some sauces instead.

I'm not sure how I feel about this place. Â I grew up in San Francisco and am well-acquainted with Gordo's, the taqueria on which Dos Toros is modeled (according to the owner). Â I appreciate that these guys are trying to bring the San Francisco burrito to New York. Now, call me a snob (go ahead, do it), but these burritos just aren't as good as San Francisco burritos. Â Authentic burritos are not made (incredibly slowly) by hipsters. Â That said, authentic burritos are also made in much dirtier kitchens with much more questionable ingredients. Overall, I like this place. Â It's convenient and tasty; it's just not as good as it's hyped up to be.

Went here on a Sunday night with my gf and found that it was entirely empty. Â The waitstaff was very well informed and attentive. Â The suggestions made ended up being quite tasty. We had a pasta dish (the gnocchi) which was made on site and was extremely fresh and chewy. Â The salmon tartar was also quite fresh with subtle flavors underpinning the dish. Overall, I would have enjoyed a larger selection but what we had was tasty and adequate. Â I would definitely suggest coming here with a group.
Delicious dinner

A friend of mine had said she'd had a wonderful dinner here, and suggested it for brunch. Â Given my experience, I cannot believe this place has ever surpassed being awarded 2 stars, let alone 5... but I notice that the lowest marks relate to a brunch meal. Â So let's continue: I arrived on time and was told I could not be seated until the other part of my party arrived (table of 2, ample seats available at 10:15am, 15 minutes since opening). I wasn't thrilled by that but waited patiently. Â We were then seated and ordered coffee, but were left to chat for nearly 20 minutes before the order was taken by a somewhat snarky, preoccupied waiter. Â I agree: Applewood's apparel offerings should NOT top the menu. We had a lovely time catching up.. chatted away for nearly 45 minutes when my dining companion left to use the restroom and I clocked my watch: we'd been waiting AN HOUR for our order, which was 2 shallot and mushroom omelets, with biscuits, potatoes, and a side of bacon. Â Thankfully, the plates hit the table just before she returned. Â The omelet looked freakishly smooth and almost plastic-like given a place that seems very slow-food/rustic. Â Actually a real turn-off. Â I cut in and it was very poorly done: too runny and, here's the worst part: lukewarm. Â  I'm not a big complainer. I will muddle through a meal w/out grimacing, especially if it was someone else's choice. I ate most of mine, using the hot potatoes to warm the omelet bites. Â The apple slices gratis, on the side, were watery and disgusting.. .bland. I could've picked better apples from the bodega round the corner. It was truly pathetic. Â Halfway through, my friend asked if mine was cold and I had to reply yes. We both stopped eating and she apologized and confessed total disappointment with the experience. The conversation was much more rewarding than the meal.
