So here's the summary: Overpriced for an undercooked meal served cold, a waitstaff that never checked in after wordlessly dropping off the meal, and yes, it was very loud when at full capacity. I'm impressed by the dinner raves here.. someone must do something right, but it won't be the same one cooking your brunch. Skip it.

Please sir you must wait in order to dine, as in wait 1.5hrs for this famous Black Label burger that you must have just cause.. Well was it worth the wait, Firstly I was so damm hungry it would not have mattered so aside from that it was pretty sweet and melt in your mouth beef, so ya one of the better burgers Ive had in my sober times. Cause if your smashed any and all burgers are the best burgers you've ever had..

Being in NY, we had to try the Pizza. Â Since we heard so much about Lombardis. It did not disappoint. Â We had the meatlovers on one side and the sausage/pineapple on the other. Â  Something tells me dine in would be better than delivery though since it had soooo much grease and cheese, I can't imagine how that would taste 30 minutes later. Â hahah but service was quick. Â We did have to wait a while to be seated but we didn't mind since we had some wine at the bar. I would definitely go again.

I was disappointed when I went to Hop Kee but they're closed until CNY. But thanks to my New Yorker twin, Leo who recommended Noodle Village a few months ago. They automatically give you hot tea - a very good sign. Never trust a Chinese restaurant that asks if you want tea. Fish Balls: 2 skewers with 3 fried crispy balls each. 4/5 Braised Beef Brisket Noodle Soup HK Style and Beef Brisket and Shrimp Wonton Soup: The beef was tender, the noodles were firm and the broth was the typical Chinese soup base - not salty. There were potatoes in the soup. The wontons were tasty and had shrimp and pork inside. 4/5 Xiao Long Bao: The soup inside was nice and hot but won't burn your mouth. The bao had the right thickness and was not doughy. Â The broth was alright and slightly gingery. It was alright but not one of the best I've had. 3.5/5 Soy Milk: This is not the one you see in cartons at the grocery store. This is the legit soy milk - ancient Chinese secret status. You can get this either hot or cold. I'd drink this with every meal in China. You can taste soy and a bit of sweetness. 5/5 We beat the lunch crowd but towards the end of our meal, our server was trying to rush us out because there was a lot of people waiting for tables. To me, this is not rude. My people want to make business and there's nothing wrong with that, I completely understand.

Thursday around 7pm Wait was 1 hour and 15 minutes. Half way through, I asked myself. If I leave now, the half a hour is going to be waisted......so I stayed. I asked the two guys behind the counter, "What should I have for a fist timer?" The guy with a torch said, "Miso Ramen!". I also asked for Broiled Char-ciu Pork on veggies. I thought I expected so much after reading good reviews and the long wait but it was okay so as the broiled pork. Visually, taste, texture and most importantly Umami weren't apparently missing I rather spend my $20 for Ramen at Rockmeisha in West Village. Rockmeisha Ramen (they only have one kind Ramen) was rather smaller but it was solid! Will I cine back? Sure! Â I will give another try. I believe in my Yelp peers.

Based on the reviews I've seen, one word: OVERRATED. Downstairs is nice and cozy, very Euro-tavern looking. Decor truly is superb. That being said, food is alright (if overpriced for what you get, reheated lasagna and pre-made paninis that are sitting out all day, like at some bodega). There were four of us and we ordered four different types of dishes: only the pizzas were satisfactory (and the only ones made fresh, we're told). Desserts were adequate. Service isn't good. Long waits for food, no bread and olive oil and Parmesan like standard Italian fair, and the manager was relatively rude when it came to keeping a chair for a friend who was coming. He kept coming to the table every 2 minutes to see if he could take the chair until our friend came. And it's not some "secret place" at all, never has been as Emma L. says. It's packed with NYU-ers and is well-known in the neighborhood. Winter garden has awful temperature control: it's very warm for about 15 minutes, then you start feeling a cold wind, and then it's cold for about 20 minutes, and after that it slowly gets warmer. They explained it's because of the thermostat...
Very good all around.
Great meal couple years ago at Brooklyn Fonda. Not so much on Avenue B tonight. Nice vibe, great soup, plantains, tacos, but specials and guacamole only okay. Service slow, annoyingly so.

We came to this place 3 different trips to Nyc.. and had always enjoyed it. We were very hesitant since the Name change but decided to give it a try bc It was the first place ever did I try a Lychee martinee (nearly 8 yrs ago) before years later Houston finally picked up on it. Walked in an it wasn't really busy.. maybe 3 groups at different areas of the bar.. which really scared us..It's one of those "should we stay or run??" but it was already late-night from partyin' we decided to stay bc we were fortunate the kitchen was still open. =) Music genre was hip-hop n house. Good stuff. So first thing first.... I ordered my Lychee martinee, and it was just as delicious as the the times before. Check. Then we ordered bar snacks like..... Crab croquettes... melt-in-your mouth fresh. Check. Sesame honey ginger wings...juicy..crispy..tasty. Check. Salt n pepper squid with fresh jalapenos slice. Good seasoning but I Â  Â  Â  Â  prefer a little crispier. still... Check. Overall.. Drinks were perfect. Food was tasty and fresh. And I would definitely visit again, but try to go at a more "happenin' time" frame.

My review is based on my 2 visits. :D Tip: My best suggestion is to reserve a table away from the door during the winter and go when the owner is there. The experience is vastly different. BYOB with no corkage fee. Cash Only. 1st time: Overall 3.5 out of 5 Service: Owner wasn't there, 2 waitresses. We were sat closest to the door and we were FREEZING. I asked if we could switch seats and the waitress said they were reserved and politely refused. No one showed up and we froze - If they offered halfway through our meal to switch seats it would have made us so happy but they didn't. Other than the seating issue, the service was good. I didn't know it was cash only so we had to go to the ATM and they trusted me to go without leaving an ID or a credit card which we thought was very nice of them. Â  Food: - App: French Onion Soup - Tasted great but was served lukewarm. I really wanted something pipping hot because I was freezing so I was a bit disappointed. - App: Mussels w/Curry: The MOST AMAZING MUSSELS I HAVE EVER HAD. HEAVENLY. I can eat this everyday for the rest of my life and die happy. My favorite dish on their entire menu. It has a deliciously addictive quality to it too. - Ent: Baked Sea Shepherd Pie: I prefer dishes that have a little more bold flavors. After the incredibly flavorful Mussels w/curry, it was rather lacking. - Ent: Roasted Lamb Leg: Was delicious and I enjoyed every bite but each thinly sliced pieces was a bit dry/hard/overcooked. I'll order it again sometime and give it another chance. Â  - Des: Sorbet (Raspberry, Coconut, Lime): If you're a sorbet lover this place has fantastic sorbets. If you like citrus def try the lime sorbet. The coconut sorbet tastes like fresh frozen coconut juice. Just absolutely amazing. The raspberry sorbet was great but I prefer the lime and coconut sorbet. Â  2nd Time: Overall 5 out of 5 Service: Owner was there, 1 waitress. The owner called to confirm my reservation and reassured me I will have a table away from the door which made me really happy. The owner goes ABOVE AND BEYOND to please all his customers. He has such a genuine smile, enthusiasm and passion it's contagious. That alone makes your dining experience special. The waitress was a one woman waiting machine. Extremely attentive, polite, friendly, fast and courteous. If I owned a restaurant, that's the waitress I want to hire. The service on this night was the best I had in a very long time. Â  Â  Â  Food: Everything was made to perfection and I don't say that often. We ordered 2 Prix Fixe Dinners and it is an amazing deal. The portions are generous and the quality was superb. Â  - App: Pate: It's homemade, rich and delicious, especially smothered on their bread!! Comes with cornichon, pickled onions and a tiny salad. Was divine. - Ent: Mussels in White Wine: Fantastic! Delicate and incredibly delicious. If you don't like the idea of shellfish with dairy/curry, get this. Â  - Ent: Mussels w/Curry: See Above. Â  - Des: Sorbet: See Above. - Additional Des: Â Sabayon Chaud aux fruits du moment: My friend and I had a bite and we were left speechless. It is spectacular. A layer of fresh fruits with liquor(?) and topped with whipped egg yolk and then baked. The egg yolk turns into a thin layer of crepe. Every diner should try this desert!!

OH PIO PIO! Came here for a friend's birthday. The staff was very accommodating to our huge group. The food was SCRUMPTIOUS -- once we received our food, the table was silent as everyone indulged in the deliciousness. Try the red sangria and the matador!

Soooo... Where to start... Started the evening with amazing cocktails (Pink Picket Fence and the Rosemary vodka cocktail that I can't think of the name (too many cocktails). Let me just say, they were amazing. I'm born Â and raised in New Orleans and these drinks were top notch. When we walked in we noticed the huge portions so only order two entrees and an appetizer for three people. Which was WAY too much food. We probably have enough to all eat again. We ordered the mash potatoes with mushroom gravy (amazing), the honey chicken and pickles sandwich (fucking amazing), and the mushroom and Mac and cheese (holy balls, fucking amazing). We also ordered a pickle sampling. Our waitress (who was adorable and nice!) said we should hold out for dessert and I'm so glad we took her advice. The biscuit bread pudding is TO DIE FOR. It was insane. I am so excited to heat up the left overs. The only thing I have against this place is that it is so freaking dark in there. I get it, you want a certain ambiance, but I had a really hard time reading the menus. It's really not a big deal when you measure up to how good the food was. I wish I could rate this restaurant higher than 5 stars. I've been to a lot of great restaurants but this hits the top 5 I think. Highly recommend!

I had to give Robertas five stars. I actually exclaimed, "woohoo! As good as it gets!" as I left. My first time here was for a date on a packed Saturday night. Service and seating was slow, but we didn't mind. The place is BYOB, so just bring drinks and relax. We shared a margherita pizza, and it was outstanding. Our waiter was the lead singer of Love As Laughter, which I thought was funny cause I went to their cd release party the week before. They had a picture and a review in Spin this month, pretty solid band. My second visit was last Saturday afternoon with my parents who were in-town for a visit. They loved it. It was nice to show them a cool place only two blocks from my new apartment. We all got the mint lemonade, which was very sweet and refreshing. My dad got the Millennium Falco pizza, my roommate got the ham, pineapple, and jalepeno pizza, my mom got a toasted sub, and I got the most amazing calzone I've ever had. Its one of the only calzones on the menu, called Pepes' Calzone or something. It had spinach, ricotta, prosciutto, It was HUGE, with a big puffy and crunchy crust, it was amazing. There is an outdoor seating area with a very cool old Mercedes Benz outside. On weekends, they sometimes have private parties going on there. There is a back bar, which is usually open, and if you want to sit quick request to sit there. Stop by Brooklyn Naturals on your way there to pick up beer, they have a great selection. I will be a weekly regular here.

We visited NYC recently (March 2011) and decided to have dinner at Becco. Â Our first impression was good--quaint place, good cosmos. Â Then we got a jerk of a waiter (Carlos) and our pleasant evening took a real negative turn, and quickly!! Â Not a very accommodating place, nor does the management really care if you leave dissatisfied. Â Not smart business, as far as I'm conerned. Â In a foodie town such as NYC, I would not return!!!!!!

Lamb chops were exquisite and the gambas (shrimp) was packed with flavor. Red pear sangria was really tasty albeit not super strong. Like other reviewers mentioned, the place is extremely small and would not be good for a party of more than 4 people. Service was extremely fast and all the plates came out piping hot. Prices were reasonable for a tapas place. I will definitely be back.

Amazing food and drinks, pretty bad service would sum up Caracas. That doesn't stop me from going here all the time though. I get the pabellÃ³n arepa which is pure awesome. I also go out of my way to get the michelada here, which is honestly the best I've ever had (and yes, I've been to Mexico and had them there). The only place where this place seems to fall short is the service, more specifically, the seating situation. This place is extremely narrow, which results in some weird seating configurations, which the hosts never really seem to take into consideration. I've been here no less than 3 times where me and my group has been seated, served, and then asked to move to accomodate other parties mid-meal. I've also gotten lectures about how they will refuse to place two people at a table for three, and I've been asked to share tables with strangers more often than reasonable. Don't let that stop you from going and experiencing awesome food, but just don't be surprised if you have to play a bit of musical chairs while you eat.

I was surprised to find a new restaurant open up on Mott that was a Chinese restaurant so I had to check it out (most of the new spots in Chinatown seem to be Viet, Malay, or some kind of cafe/bakery). To me, this place was a rare chinatown find..clean, simple yet nice decor, cheap food, super nice and attentive staff (very hard to come by). I had the "hot pot rice" aka "bo jai fahn" ..the one with chicken & mushroom and another with various meats..I also had the cuttlefish balls soup. all in all, the food was just OK..had to add lots of soysauce to the hot pot rice, which wasn't too bad but it was sort of on the bland side. the cuttlefish balls soup had wayyy too much white pepper powder..I even smelled it while the waitress was bringing it over. The cuttlefish balls themselves were better, they seemed homemade? I won't be returning here again, since there are other better, cheaper chinatown spots (sadly, minus the great service but I'm willing to give that up).

I have been coming here for a couple of years and am now finding myself agreeing with those fellow yelpers that the pizza's a soggy mess. Â To add insult to injury, there's so much goo that our pizza was cold in the center. NOT GOOD. Â I dont mind not being able to pick up my slice of pizza but that would mean cutting it on my plate fom the center towards the crust. A cold center is not a good place to start. Â I so wanted to continue my love affair with Saraghina, but alas, I will hold on to the good times we once shared. sniffle, sniffle

Pros: I wouldn't travel out of my way to go here, but it's a great place if you're in the area and hungry. Â Food isn't the most authentic, but is almost always good. Â Also much cheaper than similar surrounding restaurants. Â Great place to sit out back for drinks in the summer. Cons: Almost always busy (it's cheap-ish).
Pho is very good with very little MSG

I was pleasantly surprised by this Filipino Gastropub. I'll admit I was fairly taken aback by the eight feet tall naked Filipinas plastered in the back room. Mostly because I've never seen Filipinas that ugh naked before while I am eating. But the food was not a let down. The dishes still have at heart the original taste of the traditional dishes but it kicks them up to a more modern level and with fresher ingredients. The atmosphere is interesting mostly because 98% of the diners were young Filipina women with their caucasian boyfriends unsurprisingly all the boyfriends faced the naked wall while the girls faced the wall with the weird glow in the dark Jesus paintings. I am looking forward to attending one of their Kamayan nights when all the tables are filled with meat and you eat with your hands in true filo-style! But it's a two week reservation wait.
The food here is good. Great value for the money and they don't skimp on the quality or quantity. Yes, there is not much to say that hasn't been said about this place.

Cool, intimate space with a nice bar. Good date destination. 30+ crowd. We shared two appetizers - asparagus + parma (good) and mashed potatoes (too mushy for my taste). I had the catfish + coleslaw which was tasty and my friend had the fish stew which she enjoyed. Total tab before tax/tip was $80

Deeeeeeeelicioussssssss! I'm from the South and we do crawfish boils all the time. There really isn't much to say, it's crawfish people. If you are not from the south, they boil it and season it. The end. They do it with a variety of seafood and it's just delicious. Crawfish is more about the community and sharing the experience more than getting a lot of meat from a small piece of crawfish. Yes, it is pricer than normal, but this is New York and the cost of everything is just higher. If you want a crawfish fix, look no further. What makes this place amazing is the spice mix (The Boil Special). It is better than, dare I say, the famous Boiling Crab?!? YES! I have testimonials of many from the south and west coast and the mix here is out of this world. It's is very addicting and you keep going back for more. The Boil use to take reservations, but due to them trying to be all cool and hip, they just don't do it anymore. If you com at 6 you probably will get away with a 30 min wait but anything afterwards, it takes anywhere from an hour or longer. Smaller parties are better, and I would recommend no more than a party of 4-5.

Fantastic. If you can get in. It's tiny--maybe only 20 people can eat there at a time, so get ready for a 1 hour wait minimum on weekends. But you'll have an experience you'll remember for years. Intimate setting, warm atmosphere, personalize service from Heidi (make sure you talk to her!), and a simple menu to choose from that keeps things from getting complicated. We had the specials hangar steak and gnocchi, but were drooling at every dish our fellow dining companions ordered, too. My advice--go on a mon/ tues night when you can get Heidi to yourself. Enjoy...

It's places like Joseph Leonard that make me wonder why I am so keen on sticking to the same restaurants all the time. NEW FAVE!!! My best friend has been harassing me about going here - telling me how much I will love it especially since it's in my hood. We went. I fell in love. We went on their 3rd anniversary so the bartender/waiter was in the best mood ever and was so nice. I had the french toast with peaches which was one of the most scrumptious dishes I have ever tasted. Wow. We shared the home fries which I enjoyed but didn't love - a bit too crispy on the outside and not enough "mush" inside. Oh and let's not forget that they have BODUM tea and coffee things - always makes me happy. Great service, adorable space, amazing service, and just all around thrilled that I finally went here!

Ate here over the holidays several years ago. Â Waited outside in the cold night for 2.5-3 hours in extremely long line. Â The pizza was good, but I was also pretty hungry by the time I got inside. Â It was nothing amazing. Â The service was terrible, however. Â The waiter kept trying to get us to leave after 20 minutes so he could bring more customers in from outside. Â He wasn't even nice about it. Â This is the type of place you go one time to say you went there and then you never go back again.

Sun dried coffee! It's been around for a while but I was first introduced to the layered, fruity flavor of drip coffee from beans dried outdoors at Little Collins. The barista was very knowledgeable and happy to chat about coffee, one of the reasons I left highly caffeinated, but with a smile on my face. The smile could have been a twitch too, or a lip cramp - hard to tell after the amount of coffee I had. I learned about the coffee bug in Hawaii and recent challenges with batches of beans that taste like 'carrot' after roasting an infected coffee bean. And also that the cliche of a distant, tattooed barista is less and less a requirement for good espresso, if Little Collins is any indication! They have a fleet of custom La Marzocco machines and the vegetarian sandwich I had was fantastic. Space-wise this place may be little, but just like the lane in Australia, which it appears to be named after, it's got everything to become a trademark in Manhattan's constantly growing coffee shop culture.

Good god. Jesus. Hail Mary. I used to live 3 BLOCKS from this divine culinary piece of heaven. And now I live thousands of miles away. My first stop when I land back in NY in LaGuardia, is straight here (its only 15 minutes away). I mean what can I say? The fantastic and hearty greek salad with warm, crusty bread. The delectable lemon potatoes. The grilled shrimp or calamari that will delight your mouth in ways I cant even describe. And best yet...the free dessert at the end, - galaktoboureko; a honey-custard like pie. You may have to wait in line, especially on a nice summer/spring day. But heck, wait. Because a) the area doesn't have anything like it and b) you'll leave stuffed, happy and forgot you every had to wait. If you live in Astoria, or NYC for that matter, please go and pay respect to the genius in the kitchen.
Veggei muffaletta = good. Fine-diced pickled vegetables are intriguing. So is "ben-yay" Seems to be good for breakfast, will have to come by some time if I ever get manage to up that early.

I'm the first to admit, there are a lot of great Italian restaurants in the neighborhood, and Rucola is yet another welcome addition. Â Charming, intimate, deliciously simple Italian fare, attentive, warm service, fair prices and great wine - it does get crowded, but it's so worth it.

I've been to Luzzo's a few times and it keeps getting better! Clearly one of the best places in NYC for real Neapolitan pizza, but they do other dishes really well... Last night I had the eggplant parmesan, and it was really delicious and the portions are a good size. Also had the shrimp and squid in spicy light tomato sauce -- also very good... My favorite pizza so far is the mushroom. Great imported cheese and a light crispy crust! Luzzo's is an all around solid east village Italian restaurant with amazing pizza (that one MUST try), and the service isn't so bad either... Â  I love this place --
You call this pizza... For the price... wouldnt you expect they would used fresh ingredients....

This place is great to grab a drink with some friends on a quiet night. The backroom is fairly large and often features live and authentic irish music. The many beers on tap were almost too much to choose from, but we settled with two large lagers. Overall I really liked this place and will be back in the near future!

I Â came here on a Saturday night with out a reservation and they told us they were completely booked. Â  So we went to sit Â at the bar which was also crowded. Â Luckily, I bumped into the host a few minutes later and he was able to seat us. Â I really loved the ambiance of the back room. Â I Â had no idea there was a second floor, and the food I don't even know where start. Â Now. I'm a very petite girl so I don't usually eat a lot , but that night I think I ate everything on the menu, and each dish was more delicious then the next. Â I would definitely go back and recommend it to all my friends. Â OH and mom, I Â ate Brussels Sprouts and loved them.

Fantastic meal! Each item had an incredible combination of flavors. And all this just 1 day after Sandy! "Thank you so much" to the incredible staff for pulling together so quickly after a hurricane to provide a wonderful meal to a couple out-of-towners!

I have been eating at Piora since I moved to New York about a year ago and it has become my favorite restaurant in the city (after August closed down!). Â All the menu items I have tried over over about 15 visits have been really excellent. Â I would highly recommend this place!

They have a decent list of draught beers and some interesting menu items including various pickled items (try the Brussels sprouts). The braised short rib and marrow eggs Benedict is promising, but the sauce has a heavy lime flavor, which doesn't really go with the dish. Something smokey and/or spicy like chipotle might work better. The service was pretty poor when we went. We had a great seat outside but Â we felt ignored. We twice had to go inside and request our waiter.

PASS! I went here on new years eve for lunch with two of my friends. We didn't have a problem getting seats, in fact when we got there, the restaurant was pretty much empty except for us and two other tables. We ordered the Crab and Spinach dip for appetizer and we had 2 Bash Burgers and 1 Mexican Burger. The crab dip had no crab and tasted just like a spinach dip (would not recommend). We each ordered our burgers medium-rare but they came to the table cut in half so that the juices drained out and soaked up the bottom bun instead of resting in the burger. Burgers should not come pre-cut! Both our Bash burgers came medium to medium-well, a wasteful way to treat Pat LaFrieda meats! Also, I did not get any bacon jam. My burger only came with cheese and a thin layer of carmelized onions. I only realized it after we left that the whole burger was missing bacon jam! My friend didn't receive any either and that was the only reason I chose burgers at B&B over Spotted Pig was for this bacon jam. The onion rings on top was a sad thin onion ring that was less onion and more just way too oily. I love a good crispy fried onion ring but by the look of the pictures, it seemed the ratio was terribly off. The sweet potato fries were also not thick enough and all you could taste was the oil and none of the sweet potato. Overall bill came out to about $80 for 3 burgers, 1 crab dip and sodas. So the way I see it, it came out to about $30 each for a burger that was overcooked, over seasoned with salt and underwhelming in size. I am by no means a big eater but even this burger was just not up to par to the other burger joints. My favorite for a consistent perfectly simplistic beef burger is Spotted Pig for the same price. The apps there are also 1000x better. B&B was disappointing.

Let's get the bad stuff on the table before I rave about this place: -There is little to no room inside -cleanliness is questionable Okay on to the good stuff: Prices are AMAZING! You can stuff yourself with less than $5. Dumplings are extremely fresh and tasty! Pork and Chive seems to be the most popular and with good reason. Behind the counter is this huge wok that has dumplings waiting to be devoured, so as soon as you pay they hand over the goodies. Definitely worth the trip to China town!!

I spend Christmas each year in the City. Decided i would try Balthazar last year...could not get a reservation. Â Tried again this year, and got one at 6 pm (only time available for the night I wanted). Â Guest and I get there at 5:55 and check in. Â They tell me that the seating does not begin until 6 and to have a drink at the bar (small space). Â Right at 6, chaos ensues....50 people (I assume all tourists like myself) flood through the doors wanted a table. Â If I had not pushed my way back to the front, I would still be waiting for my table. We are seated and the service was excellent. Â The waitress was nice and well informed. Â The food was a strong B+. Â I had french onion soup and steak au poivre. At the table next too us was a couple who decided to break up that night...and I had to listen to it....really? Â  I will go back if I can get a reservation at a time that is more reasonable...even though this is really a tourist place....
I love thier small tapas, atomosphere, and strong drinks! My favorite was squid ink paella... so yummy!

Perfect (dinner) meal here, two weeks ago. Â Incredible salmon. Â INCREDIBLE lamb burger. Â The waiter Erik (with a K -- I asked for the spelling to make sure I was giving a shout out to the right person) was SOOOOOO beyond nice and helpful -- he really made the meal extra special. Â Beautiful ambience -- great window seat. Â Couldn't ask for a more lovely evening.
Love this place! Â Great "pitza" - get the green Pitza. Â Great falafel sandwiches and some of the best hummus & babagaouj around. Â Just don't ask for just a little hot sauce unless you want a lot!

Freaken amazing...I don't know what's in the broth but my guess is some type of Japanese crack that causes you keep your head down for the next 10 minutes without uttering a word and slurping down all the noodles. Then after 10 minutes you're craving more noodles. Broth is amazing. I loved the bite with the broken down seaweed. I also loved the scallions that I tried to eat with every bite of noodles to give some nice crunch to every bite. Extra scallions might be a bit too much b/c they give you plenty. I really enjoyed the bites with the garlic pieces. Last, that boiled egg was the best I've had. The yolk had this really good flavor to it..I don't know what they did to it but it was delicious. The wait wasn't bad, we got there 10:10pm on a Sunday night and the 3 of us were seated around 10:45pm. Food came out within a minute of sitting down b/c the host had us put in our order before we were seated. I've had the other infamous Ramen place in NYC but this is my new favorite. TIP: make sure to write your name on the waiting list or give to host if he has it. Also, a party he called off wasn't there at the time but they came back later and he then allowed them to get the next seating.

Had dinner here with my wife on Saturday evening. Pros- Very good wine selection. Â Good choices of Burgundian Whites. Â Prices were reasonable for the wines. Â Overall meal pricing reasonable for the location at 48th and 3rd. Â Crab-cake and Scallop Appetizers were very good. Cons- Food was marginal. Â Nothing special. Â Sauces did not impress and fish was OK. Â Waiter was very inexperienced or just ad. Â Did not tell us of the specials but the neighboring waiter told his table. Â When I asked he said they were out of specials. Â Had white wine glasses but attempted to pour the wine into Red ones without a thought. Â Decor was nothing special. Â All in all not bad for the price but nothing to repeat for sure.

The food is pretty good for cafeteria style and the price is great. Â The only problem is the crowd that is in there at lunch will push you out of the way. Â Even when I had a cast on one arm, people wanted to get there first. Â You have to be willing to fight for your food.

UVA deserves a solid four stars for ambience, excellet food, knowledgeable wine sommeliers. Â Service was good. Food menu was great, expect a little pricey, but you get what you pay for. Buy wine by the bottle if you find one you like. Duck was amazing, gnocchi was good, brushetta was great, lightning was very dim and it was a bit loud in the restaurant but it was overall a fantastic spot to have dinner a long as you want to pay about $30 per person for appetizer, food, wine, and salad. Minus one star for not having real candles!! Otherwise fantastic!!

A wonderful and much needed addition to the neighborhood! Went with a group of four girls and we thoroughly enjoyed the market sides-- so many to choose from and so delicious. The garlic mashed potatoes, sautÃ©ed kale and quinoa with feta were among our Â favorites! Lots of vegetarian and vegan options for my friend too. A must is the Mac N Cheese with roasted cauliflower! The Bartender even made me my favorite drink of a Moscow mule with authentic ginger beer! Our waiter, Grant, was outstanding and so attentive. Couldn't have asked for a better meal especially for the price!
I don't get the poor reviews. 4 superb pork and chive dumplings for one measly dollar bill. A friggin steal.

How AMAZING is this place? My god, they just delivered my food and I've scarfed it down (i'm very hungry) in 10 minutes. I got the teriyaki "chicken" with brown rice (really really good) with the strawberry daquiri (AMAZING) The veggie roll that they put in there is so crunch and so delicious, my goodness. I'm definitely going to be ordering from this place again. You should too.

Had dinner at Jane with an overall good experience but there was nothing really special. It is a nice quaint setting good for a date or a family outing and our waitress was very kind and attentive. Their sister restaurant The Gage is well run, bigger, and I dare say tastier and Jane is a smaller, fancier, and a pinch snobbier version. Â  Their menu is a bit perplexing, are they American, are they Italian, are they French? Â Oh, they are American/Modern European... Â Well I know I wouldn't trust an American restaurant to make Italian, I trust an Italian restaurant to. Â I'm not a fan of cross-over restaurants trying to be good at everything instead of one or two specialities and I am sure I am not the only one. Â I mean who craves Italian or French and then decides last minute they'll have a burger because it's on the menu? Â Who would show up to a place that serves steak and fries for the most part and expect them to have an excellent tomato sauce for their one pasta dish? Â And who would pick a place that has everything when they are craving one genre? Â Being that they own multiple restaurants and they pay people to think about this.. maybe they should work on their identity after brunch here. The food: Burrata Appetizer: 4.5/5 Great Burrata and olive oil seeved with pressed crusty bread and very nicely seasoned tomatoes that were possibly roasted. Â I just wish they seasoned the arugula. Steak Frites: 2.5/5 Average at best, the steak was not seasoned at all and was not hot either. Â If it were not for ketchup salt & pepper it may have been unbearable. Â They should utilize the Rosemary in the cooking process instead of throwing a ton of it on top as an afterthought. Â The fries were thin and crisp but they should not have been the star of the show here. Jane Burger: 3/5 Good but not great. Â It was cooked medium even though we ordered it well-done. Layered Chocolate Cake: 4.5/5 Decadent, moist, and delicious with a beautiful presentation. Â We only wish they gave more! One more annoying critique, Sir Kensington Ketchup is excellent and healthier but if you are going to use it in a commercial setting you either have to use small one-time use bottles, request that they create a narrower rim on their large bottle (I'm sure you buy enough for them to listen), or put place it in a ramekin and serve it without label. Â You CANNOT put a bottle on a table that non-food professionals and non-health-conscious customers are going to be digging in with their knives and then put it on another table when they leave, it is unsanitary. The pictures and reviews make it seem that Jane has a really good brunch so we will definitely be back for that but I would not be in any rush to return for dinner.

There are three reasons to come here: The pulled pork, the rice/beans, the corn on the cob. Also if you, like me, live across the street. There is the added bonus of delivery (and delivery that accepts credit cards)- which I took advantage of yesterday for the simple reason that I was in a bad mood and it was Easter and I couldn't stand the idea of seeing happy peoples. So instead I forced a delivery man to walk across the street with the aforementioned three items. It added a whole new level to the term Lazy Sunday. The pulled pork comes apart easily and is, to sum it up concisely, perfect. The rice and beans are also perfect, although I'm not quite sure why. I hope it doesn't have anything to do with butter. The corn on the cob is spicy and cheesy, but less so when you scrape off the mayonaise that holds it all together. Not the healthiest of venues but a nice solid choice if you want something tasty, casual and are in the area. Plus there is take-out extension to the restaurant, it has tables and additional seating if you don't want to deal with the oft-crowded mess next door.

I've been to Adelina's 3 times now, twice in the evening for pizza and once for brunch. The mozzarella & pesto pizza was so good I ordered it again on my next visit, though I'll have to sample a bit more of the menu. Had the truffled egg on the brunch menu today, also delicious. Â The $12 Prix Fixe gets you that plus a coffee and fresh-squeezed OJ, a pretty sweet deal. Atmosphere is cozy, especially gorgeous on a sunny fall Sunday; the place has kept much of the charm of Gypsy (which used to occupy this space) and added a layer of rustic warmth. Prices are reasonable, and every server has been delightful. I bring friends here and they want to come back, what more need be said?

This place just screams DRUNCHIES! You go here after you almost maxed out your card from overpriced craft beers that are highly appreciated for their quacky names and arbitrary ingredients. That being said lets get to real deal here: Pros: 1. Surprisingly good food for what you pay. Compared to Mamoun's, this is WAY better. I always felt Mamoun's left me with serious acid reflux or you're "getting what you paid for in NYC." Oasis has proven that isn't the case. 2. Food is well seasoned. Not some halal meat with grease and lamb jizz. This is the real deal 3. The service is delightful. The employees are always helpful and willing to feed your inebriated needs at a whim. Cons: 1. I haven't tried everything, so I'm not an "Oasis Expert" but in my opinion some of the food on display does not look appealing. 2. It can be packed out at times so it can be hard to find some seating in there unless you smell bad and people will move for you. Would I recommend this place? Yes, only when my breath is spiced with alcohol and have a dire craving for hole meat in a pita shebang.

I should have asked for a knife to cut my burger in half, though I was skeptical the place even had any utensils. Everything comes in baskets and when I asked for a ketchup plate, the waitress returned with a little plastic cup. This made me believe that maybe they don't have real dishes and the like. Anyway, my ketchup and mustard spooged all over my hands, which is why it might have been easier to eat in half, but it was well worth getting a little dirty. The beef was scrumptious, the lettuce, tomato and onion fresh, and the cheese nice and melty. Oh and, the pickles were plentiful. The fries are just right and the chips are a nice little treat for something a little different. Most importantly, the back patio is a nice little spot to sit and kick back with a few beers and friends. If it's a little chilly out, they have some serious heat lamps too.
Uva is a nice Italian restaurant for a romantic dinner. The food is good and the service is polite and professional. I recommend uva for a romantic date.

I want to like this place with all the stellar reviews it received but the food is just okay. I went with 1 other person and ordered the Barley Tea and was sorely disappointed when they brought out a tiny glass no bigger then my hand. The reason I make this a point is barley tea...is usually free with Korean meals. I don't mind paying for it but if you're going to charge me for something that usually comes free, then it better be at the very least in a normal sized cup. We ordered the Seoul sandwich, "Famous" noodle soup, kimchee pajun, pork and kimchee spring rolls and the Korean meatball bun and a pork bun. The Seoul sandwich was the only really good item. Korean spicy paste (gochujang) pork, cilantro, lettuce carrots; very reminiscent of a banhmi sandwich not as spicy as I thought it would be but very good, very flavorful.The pork/Korean meatball buns were good. They were exactly what I was expecting and were flavorful. They were out of the pork and substituted a crunchy pork belly instead and was pleasantly surprised by the flavor. Â  The "Famous" noodle soup was atrocious....just really awful. I don't know how it became famous but I'm assuming it was famously awful. Little to no flavor and there was an overwhelming amount of flavors that just didn't go together. It seemed like more of an afterthought-soup where a bunch of random things were dumped into a pot and given an arbitrary name. The kimchee pajun was incredibly under-cooked and tiny for 9 dollars....just really gooey uncooked dough and no kimchee flavor. I had to pour the soy sauce over it to get any taste. The spring rolls were unremarkable and again, I could not taste the kimchee in it but it was not as terrible as the pajun. It came with a sweet dipping sauce that was forgettable. The service was so great, the interior was so cute and cozy that if I was hankering for a sandwich or some pork buns, I would totally go again but it's just so expensive for the kind of food it is and for the ridiculously small portions. Dotory is a new establishment so they definitely have room to grow but I was pretty disappointed by the inconsistency and sub-par food. I haven't tried the bibimbap but no one should ever get that dish wrong. Over all...unforgettable experience because the food was just so bad...

i love luke's lobster. we split the noah's ark -- with the lobster, shrimp, crab roll and crab claws. Â the pairing of the maine root soda to the sea salt and vinegar chips and rolls is perfect! whoever came up with that idea should get an award. also the perfect meal for a rainy day.

Went there after watching movie with my friend. It was just around 5:30 but the line was already long and I had waited for 20 mins. The dishes was just OK, I guess might be because there were no very good Â Chinese restaurant around that place, so this one was so popular. The service, however, was good.

Loved every dish tonight. The wild meatballs (made of venison and wild boar etc) with truffle oil is the best dish! Friendly service. Very crowded. Had a reservation at 8pm, still waited 25 mins to get a table.

Absolutely charming -- I couldn't imagine New York without Tartine. Â It's everything you love about the city: Â it's crowded, the food is unpretentious but amazing, and it's casual. Â I might have to wait 45 minutes for a table, but Tartine always delivers. Â Hands down, one of my favorite restaurants in New York!

perfectly delicious pancakes. crispy and buttery around the edges. dense yet still fluffy in the middle. huge chocolate chunks drizzled with melted maple butter. Â yum yum. hands down the best pancakes in nyc. but an hour wait?? i don't know. guess you have to try it once although it seemed like everyone there besides us were tourists. double smoked bacon was delicious and my dates eggs Benedict was on point. Â yes- a great nyc Â brunch spot. probably one of the best. would I wait in line for it again - no.

WELCOME TO HELL'S KITCHEN...You are the best thai restaurant in the area..I totally love their decoration ..BEAUTIFUL!!! Â  The restroom is very clean and chic..I ordered Â mixed puff, Pad nor neung kai..They were so flavorful and delicious..Then I ordered pumpkin custard and coconut pudding.They were awesome!! Â  Â  Good job At nine..

5 stars! Hamburglar, all tired & weary from his 10 hour flight, is hankering for some onion rings and a burger. Â  He checked his yelp app for places near his hotel. Â Why yes, what do we have here? Â Place was a stones throw away. Â He threw one, but his arm was way too weak from sitting so long in a window seat, rendering his dominant arm useless. It was late Friday night and the streets on this part of Hell's Kitchen was somewhat abandoned: Â One taxi picking up a tired hooker and a Latin guy trying to get his hot dog cart out of a manhole's groove. Â Entered this modest bar and bellied up to it (not easy as Hamburglar's roundness proved challenging) and ordered a Boston lager (in a NJ accent that surprised even Hamburglar himself). Â  So the burgers are king here? Â Well, let's see about that, Hamburglar thought to himself. Â He ordered the All Beef Burger with sauteed onions and pepper jack provolone with onion rings. Â His companion Grimace ordered the same but with cheddar/mushrooms and tater tots. Â These burgers were outrageous! Â Quality meat seasoned perfectly with medium doneness and juicy. Â Buns, soft and endured the duration of the meal. Â Onion rings were crispy and batter flavorful. Â However, their tater tots were the best Hamburglar and Grimace ever tasted. Â Let's not tell Ronald, they thought. Â He'd get upset, they agreed. Â Burgers: Â 5 stars. Â Onion rings/tater tots: Â 5 stars. Hamburglar didn't tell Grimace that he sneaked out late their last night for another burger fix. Â Burger slut. Â Stuff's that good. Â Come here to escape the glitz of the city and hunker down to some good 'ole eats they'd charge twice as much in the New/Old money parts of town. Â Ambiance: Â 3.5 stars + 1.5 stars (rare find)= 5 stars.

The only thing that makes this place a dinner is that it is open 24/7...other than that I really believe is a first class restaurant!! The food is always good, the service is quick and polite and I ABSOLUTELY love the hunger salad!!best steak salad I've ever had!! A great touch is the bread they always bring when you sit down...those dry pieces with the sesame on top...ugh!!!amazing!! I also love that they have early breakfast menu, meaning from 4 am!!!great choice for after a late night out! Definitely try this place guys!!

Wonderful dinner! Â We walked in Monday evening and although it was busy, got a table after waiting a few minutes. Â Offered us a great Barolo that was not on the menu. Â ordered the sheep's milk ricotta, which was good, but not amazing. Â The lamb sliders were great. Â Scallops were absolutely delicious- pancetta and zucchini on top, on a bed of sweet corn 'polenta' - perfect. Â The pesto pasta was also good. Â Great service, great food!
$6 for a lamb and chicken combo. Â It was tasty, yet there was so much food, I wasn't able to finish mine. Â  Be generous with the white sauce, and careful with the hot sauce.
These padrotes (mexican word for pimp) keep it mad real.

After having spent almost all of my money xmas shopping for family, I needed some good food for dirt cheap prices. This place definitely fit the bill, the roast pork was very tender and juicy as was the chicken. They definitely gave me my money's worth.For a very good amount of roast pork and chicken I only spent $5.00, I wish all food was this inexpensive! I'll definitely go back again.

You never know if a place with a celebrity chef that has several other restaurants in their empire can sustain high quality food to match the hype. Happy to report that Lupo holds true to the hype. First off my thanks to the hostess, we walked in with NO reservations and asked to seat at the bar and were quickly accommodated. The bar staff were attentive plus its more fun exploring the wine list at the bar. Â  Started with prosciutto de Parma sliced so thin you could see through it. Matched that up with a clam and their version of Israeli couscous -- clean and lots of citrus. Opted to go with the pasta carbonara -- this is a good test of a romana style restaurant. Sure enough the pasta was perfectly aldente and the sauce creamy not soupy and perfectly seasoned. Â  The "Tears of Christ" red was perfectly paired with the pasta. Next time I am doing the pork they had on the menu.

****The pork betty is one of the best, most succulent melt in your mouth pork belly I have ever had. Â Order this with a side of rice as it is salty and super saucy, so it's hard to eat by itself. Cool space, good service, communal tables...I am giving it 3 stars because the other dishes were not good. Â The sushi platter looks cool but it's just a lot of rice with ultra thin tiny pieces of sashimi. Like 90/10 ratio. Â The chicken karage could be crispier and it lacked flavor. Â The chicken is tender but you needed to dip it in the soysauce otherwise it was bland.
Love this place! Good cheap on the go Korean Food. Loves... Brown Rice Kimbap Ham & Cheese Kimbap (in doses) Kimchi Fried Rice Skip on their soup & salad!

I've been here twice. Once for lunch with my mom and once for a anniversary dinner with the BF. Both times were great but for some reason I have to withhold a star. I don't know why.. I don't remember much about lunch with mom (this was 2 years back) except of course she kept commenting on the amount of silverware being changed per course ("so unnecessary! poor dishwashers! i barely used that knife! ect"). so I'll just comment on my recent anniversary dinner. GREAT service. GREAT bar nuts. They sent complimentary champagne cause they knew it was our anniversary. We both got the fall tasking menu and BF got wine pairing. Food was good, wine was good, service was impeccable.They sent the pear dessert on the house as well with a cute "happy anniversary" scribble on the plate and sent us home with pumpkin bread muffins for the morning. I really can't complain about anything. It was an awesome meal with awesome service.

Nyonya is the last true Southeast Asian fusion restaurant I've been to and it did not disappoint. The food, the curries particularly were mouth-watering and fantastic. The first thing that hits you about the place is the smell. That smell! I wish my apt smelled like that everyday, they should bottle the aroma and sell it as incense. I also enjoyed a crab dish which was grandly presented and heartily shared among myself and friends. Nyonya's decor is dark with flickering candles and bustling tables. Loved it. Verdict: This is a reliable place for Malaysian and Singaporean food. Perfect for a date, girls' night, work dinner, or just chilling with a group of friends.

This place is good. Our food was good and I loved my cocktail despite another reviewer claiming they were average. First off, the ambiance is nicer than I had anticipated. It looks nice while still being approachable. Good for a date but still welcoming to families. To be honest, it was nice to see some families eating together. Â So overall, nice, but not pretentious. It was just my husband and I. He had made a reservation on OpenTable and we were seated right away. Our food was good. Not amazing, but the service was great, making this a very solid 4 star review (probably 4.5 but I feel like I need to scale back my 5 star ratings). According to our receipt Emily was our server and she was super friendly and welcoming with great recommendations. Throughout the meal we had a few different people clearing our plates, delivering food and checking on us, so it seems like a nice collaborative place to work. As a former server I always appreciate those good vibes and we were well cared for. To drink I had the Scarlet's Fever. It was DELICIOUS and different than my usual, but so refreshing without being too sweet (it was also Emily's recommendation). To eat I had the gazpacho, which was a bit disappointing. I would give it 2.5 stars but I then had a special, the grilled squid with canelloni which was smoky, warm, and satisfying. The two starters more than satisfied me and I even had some canelloni remaining. My husband had the cavatelli. Deep, rich flavor. Also, the olive oil they serve with bread when you arrive seems to be garlic infused and was a nice touch. We left satisfied and happy. Overall the awesome service maybe even outshone our food.
I had the shrimp + jalapenio grits; was okay but the shrimps were overcooked. Was there for a large party, average meal. For this price point there are many other great restaurants in the city.

Certainly the best pizza I have had in a while. If you are traveling to NY from Europe you might not consider a pizza in Brooklyn, and that would be a mistake. The pizza here is up there among the very best. The thin crust is delightfully light and the fresh toppings come through the tomato and cheese base with great aroma and texture. The restaurant is not big and you'll generally find a queue of people waiting. Inside your choice is simple, pizza (pie) or calzone, with a pick from 6-7 toppings. We managed two pizza between the four of us and the two boys could maybe have had a slice extra, but that would have been out of greediness. Â  I've tried a few acclaimed pizzeria in Italy and around Europe, but would be challenged to say this one does not rank up there with the best. Over 6000km from the pizza motherland, Lucali does the homeland proud. Note: they do not serve any alcohol, so head down the street and buy a bottle before visiting. They will provide glasses :)

This is the first time I write a negative review on a restaurant.... but this place was seriously the worse. Â I love Mexican food and was looking fwd to brunch.... my eggs were cold, the rest of my meal was sub par ( huevos divorciado). Â It was suppose to be unlimited drinking brunch but the waiter will disappear so Â I had 2 drinks. Â  Maybe dinner is a better experience here but they are definitely not equipped for a boozy brunch. Â Bad food, coffee, service, brunch.

I feel it would only be appropriate for my first review to be one of my favorite restaurants. The Meatball Shop is a rare breed of restaurant that fills so many needs. It's perfect for a low maintenance quick to please lunch or dinner, perfect for a quick snack, and perfect for those drunken LES munchies. I mean, it's meatballs! How can you really go wrong? The fun is finding your own personal combo of meatball/sauce/side. My personal favorite is the spicy pork meatballs with parmesan cream sauce topped over mashed potatoes, but I don't mind switching it up every now and then. They also have a daily special meatball and sauce, which I happily sample by way of there awesome sliders. Let's not forget about their homemade ice cream sandwiches. Like the meatballs, you can mix and match the cookie to your preferred ice cream. It's pretty big, but perfect for two people to share. I love the ginger snap cookie with mint ice cream, but keep an eye out for the daily specials on that as well. The staff here are always incredibly nice and accommodating, and their check the box style menu adds a little fun to an already great place. The only downside is that seating for dinner get's scooped up very quick, but the food is that good that I don't mind taking mine to go and grabbing a bench over on Allen St. Apparently I have become a semi-regular in this place as the staff have come to remember my face, and I'm hailing from Astoria.

This place is truly nothing special. Â It's your typical New York establishment that gets rave reviews simply because it is popular (or was popular at one time) with famous individuals. Â I also think it regained some of its' lost popularity after The Devils Wears Prada, as it seemed to be busier after the movie came out. Â  The food is decent, but frankly nothing that one wouldnt receive at most any slightly above average Manhattan eatery. Â I will say, however, that their pies are quite good, albeit substantially overpriced. Â On price, in fact, I notice that the prices increased quite a bit in the last few years if that's something that matters to you. Â I used to go 2 or 3 times per year simply because it was near where I worked, but I wouldnt go again. Â The last time I was there for lunch (and this is disgusting, hence I will never go back) I ordered a turkey sandwich. Â I bit into the turkey sandwich and was overpowered with the unmistakable taste of Chloraseptic. Â I am not a sqeemish person at ALL, but I seriously wanted to hurl. Â Obviously someone in the kitchen must have had a sore throat and was touching my food with bare hands after medicating himself/herself. Â SO GROSS!!!!

First, the location. Conveniently located in the mecca of superb restaurants that is the west village. Perfect for a pre-dinner or post dinner drink or two. They had an impressive beer selection for a tiny hole in the wall. We went in the heat of the summer, so we would have loved to sit outside, but the outdoor seating consists of one four person table and a window sill that you could presumably perch on? Still, they open up the windows and the breeze off the water is appreciated. Did I mention it's about a 3 minutes walk from the boardwalk along the Hudson River? Perfect place to take a date. Cozy back room for bigger parties.

Wow. Some of the best pizza I've ever had in my life. The crust is crispy on bottom and soft in the middle, balanced perfectly. Also I don't know what's in their cheese but it's not like any mozzarella I've ever tasted, it has an amazing flavor! Very fast and friendly service as well. I'll definitely be back. Also they only accept cash.

I had a mojito and some sangria along with dinner here on a busy Friday night. Â I came with a party of about eight friends and we all had a blast. Â Started off with some chips and guacamole which was amazing but for $8 I expected a little more guac. Â Anyway, I ordered carnitas and paella to share with a friend for the main course and it was sooo much food. Â The carnitas is actually meant for two people but I thought the portions wouldn't be so big. Â The sides were delicious as well...especially the fries. Â Damage done was about $50 for myself and another $50 for my friend. Â I thought it was worth it for all the food though.

I came here on Monday sep 3 after a concert .. The food was so delicious !!!!! My husband had dumplings and they were GREAT!!!! And I had the seafood fried rice which was really good as well... I wil defenetly recommend this Place ....

Delicious food!!! and they have StumpTown Coffee :) :) :) the only reason why I gave 4 instead of 5 is because when I ordered for delivery it took them over an hour to deliver it and I am only 2 avenues away. And when I got it it was cold. sadness. I usually walk there to order but this was a busy day for me. I now know NEVER to order during lunch or any busy times. Other then that the food is amazing... And the staff is pretty nice.

It's one of my most recent regrets that I moved out of Astoria (my old apartment is three blocks from this place) just a month or so before Sweet Afton came around. It's so good that I might've considered staying in the hood just to have this be my local. Yes, the bar feels like a transplant from that overhyped borough south of Queens, but they've also done a good job of making it feel like a part of the neighborhood. While the staff, decor and food are as good as anything you'd find elsewhere, there's an utter lack of pretension that is completely refreshing, from the second the guy with the warm Irish accent checks your ID at the door and calls you "darlin," (but not in a creepy way) to the way the staff comes around to check you have everything you need without smothering you. We went on a Sunday night, and the bar was just full enough to feel social but not so packed as to feel claustrophobic. We ordered with great excitement a couple of cheeseburgers and the fried pickles, and were not disappointed. I have paid $8 for burgers much less delicious elsewhere. The pickles lived up to the hype, although my only gripe is that for $4 they could've thrown in a few more - the tasty goodness was over all too soon. Bonus points for being located directly next to Seva, hands down Astoria's best Indian.

It's not all that much fun adding another five star review to an establishment that already has five stars across the board, but you do what you have to. Whether it's breakfast, lunch, or dinner, it's all pretty much through the roof. Â There's not a meal or a food item I've had from here that hasn't been excellent with a capital E. Â Roast chickens, salmon, and pork shoulder on the meat side, broccoli rabe, mashed potatoes (with garlic, I believe) and various pastas...all fantastic. Â And that was just last night. Only two food items I attempt to avoid when I eat out...pickles and oysters. Â And I eat the pickles here if they're part of the meal design. Â Hell, they could toss an oyster into a breakfast sandwich and I'd try it if this team whipped it up. Top of the line!

The rumors are TRUE! These big-ass burgers are mouth-watering and available in an overwhelmingly large variety! But don't worry...you can take your time picking out just the beef burger, turkey burger or veggie burger you want...the staff is patient and friendly! I recommend the Guacamole Turkey Burger (served with tortilla chips, sour cream and tangy salsa. Perfect spot for an after-the-game pig out sessions! (I went after the Yankee game and could not have been more pleased...or FULL!)

Invited by friends to this amazing place with lot of vegeterian dishes on the menu.. Very innovative , palatably delicious and visually very attractive dishes.. Busy busy super busy all d time speaks abt d ambience of d place..i love the roasted carrot and avacado salad..

The reviewers below me need to stop referring to "stoner food" as if it's a bad thing. Bottom line is, people just like to hate on "hip" places like this that are trying something different (the fact that the owner was on a Food Network reality show probably doesn't help), but the food here is absolutely out of this world. Given, this is not the place for someone who is unadventurous with their cuisine, considering nearly everything on the menu is kind of bizarre (i.e. dr. pepper glazed frog legs), but these guys can seriously back up their daring menu with incredible flavor. If you have the cash to spend and feel like doing something different, this is your spot.

I've been here 2 times already and I love their delicious food and drinks :) everything is very delicious and fresh ^_^ The place is a little tiny but cozy and the prices are very affordable . Great date night for Thai food or just lunch date as well. :) Really recommend the Tom Yum Seafood

Yum yum yum. Delicious XLBs to satisfy on a rainy night. The crab and pork XLB were soft and tender, and the soup was perfect. They came out steaming hot, and were a perfect pairing with the dry fried green beans we had. We also had the green onion pancake which was plentiful and devoured quickly. The wait wasn't too bad, we put our names down and went across the street to get foot massages (at Foot Heaven!). By the time we were done and relaxed, it was time for us to be seated. The restaurant is cramped, but you don't mind when you're stuffing your face full of tender soup dumplings.

very awesome Moroccan place. The food is very good, I love their back yard and the mood of the restaurant. I go their all the time now I found it for my mixt platter and my mint tea! I definitely recommend it.

I am a diligent Yelp/Trip Advisor comber. I make sure if I am going to a place, my money and time is well spent based on feedback from real people. I was optimistic about this place given the great reviews, but it was such a giant disappointment. I ordered online, and selected cash delivery, but they still charged my card. I guess it was just on file. Is what it is. Delivery time said 60 minutes, it arrived in 35, so not bad. But that's where the pros end. I ordered the BBLT, and couldn't even eat half of it - and it was large. For $13 a BLT better be. It was clearly toasted, so the outside crust of the bread was black, and a bulk of the bacon was so charred it made the whole sandwich taste that way. S/O ordered a burger, and it was the size of a McDonald's burger, tasted like a burger. Also not worth $13. My food was dry, charred, and difficult to eat. I threw it away. It was a $13 disappointment, and I won't eat there again. $30 later, we could have eaten at some chain like Chipotle for half as much and been 100% satisfied. Considered a second try for breakfast, but at these prices, I won't risk another disappointment and waste my money.
Solid pizza. Hard to say how good it was because I was already full. Nice atmosphere.

Meh. What else can I say about this place that hasn't already been said? Great frozen drinks, good grilled corn, average to below average food. The outdoor picnic area is great for chilling if it's not too crowded, but it becomes a nightmare the warmer the weather gets, in fact the entire intersection that HO is located on becomes a nightmare during summer nights due to HO spillover. HO.

Sometimes a place comes along where 5 stars are just not enough! This is one of those places. Beautiful candlelit ambiance and sleek romantic decor sets the mood almost before you even walk through the door. The restaurant is decorated with partitions so that no matter where you sit, it feels intimate. This, along with elegant and silky black wood finishes and with soft candlelight throughout really makes this a great date spot. The cocktail list has some very creative heavy hitters which made for a difficult selection but we loved the ones that we ordered- the 'luchador' and the 'sour monkey' (the sour monkey being my favorite). There were 3 of us so we all got to sample each of our dishes. We tried the veggie burger, the Cajun fish and the Joe Louis burger. The veggie burger was veggie goodness with its mayo sauce, the cajun catfish was flavorful and cooked to perfection and the Joe Louis burger had a wonderful mix of ingredients including caramelized onions, bacon and grilled pineapple. The level of service is also worth mentioning as we were shocked as to how attentive our waiter was, catering to all of our needs. In addition, everything was extremely well priced. Entrees that are usually well in the $30s ranged from $14 t0 $17. Overall, sweet science provides a superb dining out experience that makes this place quickly become a favorite!

Squid ink tagliolini w/ clams was so - so and the monkfish (special of the night) was mediocre at best. Nothing amazing and not quite a bargain. I would suggest venturing elsewhere. Good service nonetheless.

Yuca Bar is my new brunch obsession. First of all, the portions, they are HUGE. I never manage to finish my entire plate, so if you're that hungry person who is always whining about small portions, do it up. Secondly, Bloody Marys, I love them. Yuca Bar brunch comes with a bloody mary, screwdriver, mimosa, or orange juice included and the Bloody Mary is spicy, also huge, and delicious. God I love a savory beverage. Lastly, the choices. Crab Cakes Benedictos, Arepas Benedictos, Steak and Eggs with cilantro hollandaise sauce. I mean, this isn't just your average brunch. Even the basic eggs and meat comes with chorizo instead of regular sausage. Good stuff. Ok and really, really lastly: the home fries are half regular potatoes, half yuca. YUM. The whole deal with cost you $15-$16 bucks. Not bad, right?

Okay, the last thing I want to hear, after walking a half mile to a place with my baby, is that I have to leave him in his stroller in the corner because he might get burned from the hot entrees. Â Who tells a mother to leave her baby in a corner at a restaurant? Â The employee there must have assumed that I was going to go on a rampage with the stroller in the place. Â  Stupid. Aside from the idiocy, I wasn't fond of the food. Â It's good for a quick take-out for various Asian dishes, but other than that, I should have spent my time and money elsewhere.

Been here almost 4 times now? Â Classic New York Pizza, the crust is slight burned each time to create more of an authentic taste. Â My favorite has always been the classic Margherita! This place would definitely satisfy the pizza cravings but I wouldn't say this is the best place in NYC. Â Sometimes the bread comes out a little dry. Â The consistency knocked it down a few stars for me. Â But on a good day, Lombardi's does make the tummy happy!

a quietly pleasant nook less polished than its older brother snack taverna in the same neighborhood. snack however is far more comfortable and on an afternoon lunch break is choice place to eat. memorable foods include: greek salad, beet salad, avgolemono soup, melitzanosalata, roasted and vegetarian souvlaki sandwiches. the entrees are more expensive and come in smaller portions, so be proud you are good to your wallet and love sandwiches, it's alright, no worries. they keep a small and selective menu meant for the soho pocket. expect fair to helpful service in a low key upper middle class environment. vegetarian and meat-friendly without a hitch as greek/mediterranean food normally is [3.5 stars].

Very enjoyable dinner. The major pros: huge portions, quick service, delicious food, and very inexpensive. The only con it's super loud and tables are close together. We were a party of 3 people and were able to share the matador entree with plenty of left over , a group of 4 could easily split this. The tostones were a bit tasteless, the chicken was juicy, and avocado salad was fresh. The servers were attentive with refilling waters, but hard to get their attention for our check at the end of our meal. Worth coming to eat here , especially since it's very reasonable priced and large portions. A must try if in the neighborhood.

3.5 stars. Upon my visit last week, the interior surpassed my expectations. For some reason, I thought it was going to be a bit more casual and not as moody. But then I remembered that it was designed by the same people that did Manhattan Inn, hOmE. I enjoy both spaces a lot. I am glad that this type of aesthetic and consciousness has caught on. The bathroom details are pretty incredible at Paulie Gee's. The service was good but not memorable. On to the pizza. We ordered 4 pies amongst 5 of us. We had pretty big appetites from some casual tasting at Brouwerij Lane a few doors down. We ordered the: Marianna - Italian tomatoes, chopped fresh garlic, Pecorino Romano, sea salt King Harry - fior di latte, Italian tomatoes, prosciutto di Parma, Pecorino Romano, fresh basil Parma d'Or - fior di latte, baby arugula, olive oil, fresh lemon juice, prosciutto di Parma, shaved Parmigiano-Reggiano A special with sausage from Meat Hook All ranging from 11-17 dollars, I was a bit disappointed by the value. The pizzas could be a bit larger and the dough would be better if it was more airy and had more salt/flavor. Maybe some really good sprinkled sea salt atop the pizzas would suffice. Though I suppose for a highly anticipated pizza place with good quality ingredients, one can't expect it to be any cheaper. The Parma d'Or was by far the favorite - the arugula and the lemon juice were a perfect balance atop the heavier, but delicious, mozzarella and proscuitto. The un-favorite of the evening was the $3 mexican soda and $5 van leewuen ice cream... one's bill could really grow here without knowing it. I still think Pizza Moto, at the Brooklyn Flea, is far superior.

A friendly place, worth revisiting, but on the day I was there, the food was hit and miss. The high points were the pulled pork and the fried chicken, though the pulled pork was a bit small. Pros: The coffee is good. They serve real jam instead of those terrible jelly packets you get everywhere else. They try to make unique dishes, and the ones that succeed are excellent. Cons: They need to have at least one healthyish item on the menu, in case someone in the party isn't into comfort food. Also, they don't offer sides, so if your entree is small, you will leave hungry. They did create a side at my request (after asking the chef), but not everyone is as pushy as me. Worth a revisit, and a re-review.

This restaurant had become one of my favorites because it was unpretentious and the few times I've been had been uncrowded plus the food is excellent. The last time I went though it had been crowded and I felt like we were being rushed to finish our meal. Maybe it was also because I went later in the evening or maybe more people know about this place now. Because of that feeling, I would've rated it three stars, but the dish I had here the last time was so delicious that I just couldn't. I ordered a special, which was brisket pasta and my friend ordered the duck salad. The salad was good but not as memorable. The brisket pasta however, was one of the best pasta dishes I've had. The flavor of the meat was strong, juicy and scrumptious and the rest of the sauce carried that same flavor and coated the pasta pieces. Sometimes when a sauce is reduced to have a strong flavor it can be salty, but this wasn't, it was just perfect. If I came again, I'd try coming earlier in the night on an off-day to see if I could avoid the crowd.

Terrible. Â The service was horrible. Â The head waiter was rude, and refused to allow us to sit in the place because there was a "no stroller" policy, even after our waiter told us we could. Â  This was at 4:00 in the afternoon with 5 people eating in the dining area and about 2,000 square feet of empty space. Â We left. Â I came from the upper west side with my daughter to meet some friends. Â  What a waste of a subway ride. Â I will never go to this place again. Â Stay away. Â Stay far away. Â Wish I could give negative stars.

Does it live up to the hype? Yes. Hell yes. One real advice though: test out the red sauce before going nuts all over your precious chicken/lamb/rice. That liquid lava is pretty potent. I disregarded the advice my first time and ended up having to compensate with drowning it out with their white sauce - which made the dish even better. The line is long and it's late and it's cold. But there's a reason why there are still people standing there, waiting with you.

Dear Hagi, You did the impossible last night, I'm impressed. Somehow, you actually managed to satisfy my pork fat craving. I'm not sure how you did it but your bacon wrapped asparagus skewers were the best and worst things to ever be done to a vegetable. And I loved it, every single bit and bite of it. I don't think my mouth has ever been that alive-- or, erm, oily-- but in a good way, honest! My sauteed udon was chock full of tender pieces of juicy, fatty pork, and the huge portion was more than enough for me to take home and enjoy today. Your kara age was tender, juicy, succulent-- I'd give up nearby Sapporo's katsu curry if only you were open for lunch. My boyfriend still loves your spaghetti with mayo and cod roe and, after last night, I am beginning to understand why. And paired with Calpico water and cold Sapporo, I don't think I could ask for more. Thank you for being so kind to me, Hagi-- I always leave so happy! Love, lora PS. Are you ok? I just wanted to make sure. I was pleasantly surprised last night to find that there was no wait-- but could it be that the economy is affecting business?? Do the Barclays associates not frequent you as often as Lehman brothas and sistas did? Let me know-- I'll come more often to compensate! (Hagi is right across the street from them, and down the stairs)
Great views. But unfortunately, this low rent place tries to capitalized on tourist and new-New Yorkers. Paid 20 buck to watch fireworks on a flat screen.
Very cute cafe with amazing vibes. Only tried the baked feta and the couscous and both plates were delish. My new favorite spot in NYC.

The flavor was good, but the bread was hard and the meat was like pork jerky. Â I've had way better in California. Â The sandwich shop shares their space with a jewlery store, so that was weird too. Â It's really small and always packed with people.

Ok I get why everyone loves this place. Â The sauces and the fries are great. Â And surprisingly, the people behind the counter were super nice and patient given how crowded it was. Â But seriously, how much fries and sauce can a person eat?? Will be sharing with a friend next time!

Good Cuban food is harder to find than a parking spot in Soho in this city!!! So when a friend mentioned one day that there was a REAL AUTHENTIC Cubano-grill, hole-in-the-wall, fresh, amazing place down on Elizabeth St. in Soho (one of my absolute FAVE neighborhoods), we had to check it out. I think I died and went to heaven. The crowd outside the door, and the smell of fresh cilantro and braised pork wafted through the small blue door opening into a small cafe not much bigger than my bedroom...With stools by the window, and a measly table, I knew that I was here for the food, not the ambiance... The homemade lime-ade is the perfect balance and sweet and tart, essential for a hot summer day, and the Cubano Sandwich, words cannot even explain. The crusty outside pressed to perfection along with pork and beef, stuffed alongside a sweet and spicy sauce that I'm pretty sure I've never EVER tasted before. Don't miss out on this place because of the intimidating line and seemingly small amount of employees, the service is fast and friendly, and what's a 5 minute-wait when your downtown, surrounded by the tree-lined streets, characters of all shapes, colors, and sizes, and good vibes allllll around.

Racist and elitist ate there a while back. Great food everyone looked how do I say this kindly..... similar. The table system is designed to keep any minority out, I will save my money and fly to Italy

What can I possibly say that hasn't already been said here 4,000 times... literally 4,000 times. Â Chicken and lamb mix with rice, doused in extra extra white sauce and sprinkles of red sauce. Â Heavenly. Yeah, the waiting in line part sucks, big time. Â But we do it anyway, because it's worth it, and because we must.

It can be tricky to find a nice place for lunch in NY. in the late afternoon, so I'd say the hours here are great. One star off for insufferable hipster hostess, but otherwise, a rowdy and delicious upscale cafe with a menu tending toward the adventurous. I loved the pork buns (after I pulled off the slabs of fat), though my vegetarian friend found next to nothing that looked appetizing. We went with the pickled veggies, which did not impress her, though I thought they were freakin amazing.

Amazing, amazing, amazing! My 1st time in NY, googled best restaurants in the area and Rubirosa was on every list! Loved how quaint it was...i wanted to try something authentic and simple so that I can taste their sauce, because it's all in the sauce! Well, their sauce was orgasmic! I told them they should bottle it! Had the rice balls and they were cooked to perfection. Their banana split was a perfect ending to a great meal!! Can't rave enough about this place. Got back to Miami craving that meal all over again! Great service as well btw!!!

The French toast is amazingly good, Â they use thick cut bread, nicely pan fried on the outsides nice and soft yummy inside. Â I'd come back for just this dish, too bad that was my friend's order and not mine. Â  Â  I ordered the Eggs Benedict "Johnny" with turkey sausage, well, maybe this was just too healthy for me? the sausage was okay but lacked the sausage spices and maybe even salt? Â  On it's own it might have worked but in the eggs Benedict it didn't, the runny eggs + the bread made the turkey sausage Â more bland. Â  I saw other people's dishes it looked pretty decent. Â I can tell it's a solid place but nothing to rave about... ....well maybe the french toast deserves some cheering...
