First thing you will notice is how cozy this place is. It's wonderful. Â The ambience is like you step away from the busy street and be absorbed in the music they set up. Â Think soft jazz or soft trance. Every table has a little candle, and flowers and is welcoming. Â  The waiter we had was a darling, he was very attentive in helping us select drinks, food and recommendations. Â Unlike some waiters I have had in other places, Â he was doing things at the right pace. Â  The food! Â  Gosh, Â that day I was hungry and ordered so much. Â Gua bao to start with though a little pricy is refreshing, and filling for one large person. Â I'd say get two lol. Â The dumplings were crispy through out. And had very good stuffed pork. And my entree the avocado bibop was freaking good. I added some eggs and meat and it is worth it. Â I hope to go back again soon, Â every Â entrees you get will be stamped on a card where you can get a Â free one. Â I hope to claim it soon. Yay.
Love love love this place. The Cuban coffee rocks. The service is friendly and welcoming. Must have the home fries!!!!!!!!!! Don't expect much in atmosphere but that just adds to the experience!!!!

This place is definitely one of stops when Im in new york. Pork buns is always a think I have to have when I dine here. The ramen here is excellent . Soup is good, Texture or Ramen is good. I only wish they had one in sf bay area by where I live

Can't go wrong with this place, $10 Yuengling pitchers, free snacks, board games, cheap shots, good music, quick service, good crowd. Â Great place to end the night. My only tip would be to go on a wednesday or thursday to avoid the crowds, tho honestly it's still fun even when crowded, you just will be in line forever to use the john.... Â oh and frito pie all night.....not just one Brooklyn's best but one of the best in all 5 boroughs.

We've eaten a lot of bao in our lives. Â Really, more than a person probably should, and we've been mourning the loss of our favorite places, since moving here from Brooklyn. Â How happy am I that this place is awesome? Â The bao are delicious, and so enormous that they really make a meal. Â I don't understand what people are talking about, when they say the bao are small; these are the most generously portioned I've ever seen. Â The pork belly is perfectly cooked, and the fried chicken is seriously tasty, juicy and crunchy. Â Bulgogi beef is also well seasoned and very tender. The icing on the cake, though, is the philly cheesesteak scallion pancake. Â I know it sounds ridiculous, but trust me. Â  Great find in our new neighborhood.

Great service great food! Came here a little early so they let us sit at the bar and the bartender was great! Â Then the host sat us and made us feel extra special. THEN best dinner EVER we got the burger and fries of course which yup! Amazing! Also the duck egg salad! So great!
Biker bar at its best on Tues nights 6-9 come have a drink the food looks good also BIKES BIKES BIKES!

Upping the ante here and adding the elusive 5th pointy, geometric shape to their rating. My wife and I went back last night (yes, because the food is that good) and brought my brother in-law along with his wife. Â Magically the "El Diablito" came with tiny spoons and the portions were much bigger, not to mention that the layout was way easier to navigate. Â Cheers not only on the upgrades but for taking the time to listen to reviews, speaks volumes of the management. Â Also, and this is something i think all the reviewers overlooked, that dish is only $6!!! Â Staying in the app department we also shared the scallops which were killer and the seafood guac, no plate went un-licked, really well done all around and again it was creative and a very new kind of delicious. For main dishes my bro-in-law got the stew and loved it. Â His wife got the shrimp which she shared a bit of and it was just as excellent as the other dishes (my wife and I got the same thing as last time). We have not tried the desert yet, but I would assume good things. So, they have reached 5 stars in my humble opinion BUT I still stand by my other two suggestions and the reason being that I think it would help them generate more business. Â You are going to get a lot more repeat and frequent customers who can come in and get some excellent tacos, guac, beer and tequila especially with more than a quarter of the seating residing at the bar. Â Take Mesa Coyoacan for example, they have all the staples along side delicious more creative/fancy dishes. Â I just think that as good as the food is at Slowteria people will come back and back and back for what they know and there is less of a chance of lines out the door for their more complex dishes regardless of how good they are. Regardless, if you are contemplating trying this place, just go, there is no way you will not be seriously impressed.
Food is fine, but unspectacular. Portions on small side. Was looking for a less expensive alternative to another restaurant, but regretted not paying up.

I just don't get it. I went into this with high expectations, because I had read such great reviews on Yelp, so today, I went to try their Sunday brunch. I couldn't wait to try the French Toast. Almost every review raved about it! When we walked in, it was so crowded. People were waiting everywhere, and every seat in the house was full. We were told the wait for two was an hour. That seemed OK, not ideal, but I really wanted to try it, and we figured we could stroll around the neighborhood to kill time (the bar was too crowded to have a drink). We came back and hour later and wound up waiting another fifteen minutes. No biggie. My dining companion wasn't thrilled with the wait, but knew how much I wanted to test it out, so he was a trooper. A large party was called and when they got up from the bar, we were able to snag two seats and order a Bloody Mary. If you follow my reviews, you know how much I love a good Bloody. I was disappointed. While it wasn't terrible, it was too spicy and didn't have the strong flavor profiles to back it up. Don't worry, this story has a happy ending, I finished the whole drink :) Finally, we were told our table was ready. I have to give the host and hostesses credit, they were really, really friendly, and seemed pretty efficient. The wait had to do with the sheer volume of people who wanted to eat, the hosts were moving people as quickly as they could. Once seated, our server came right over. She was attentive the duration of the meal, and always smiling. I love when the server is awesome. That really improves the quality of the meal. Too spicy Bloody Mary aside, I was pumped to order. We went with the creme brulee brioche french toast, Benedict Johnny and cheesy grits. French toast: Pretty good. Not AMAZING. But really appetizing. Benedict Johnny: Decent twist on eggs Benedict. Not spectacular. Cheesy Grits: Lukewarm and the consistency of rice pudding, which was weird. They were unseasoned, so we had to add a ton of salt. The bread basket looked promising, and it did contain these over sized long thin cornflake-like crisps, which were really good, and there was a small container of strawberry butter, a spot of bright pink on the table. I was surprised at how little strawberry flavor it had, especially considering the brilliant color. I don't think I will be returning. The wait was much too long and the food was really not that good. I think part of the problem was my considerably high expectations which weren't met even halfway. If only they would have had a good Bloody Mary. I could have forgiven the rest of the meal. Oh well. On to the next one.

This place is so amazing! Without a doubt best sandwich of my life. We went there for breakfast, I had an egg biscuit sandwich and it was cooked to perfection, the eggs were amazing and the biscuit was so delicious. The service was great, friendly, quick and gave us the coffees on the house. We are definitely making it back here!
Innovative food, friendly service, and a beautiful interior. Â This is a great place for a late evening dinner.

Lupa Lupa Lupa... ohhh how I wanted to try you so. I was supposed to have a nice meal here one blustery Friday night with 2 friends before their move to far away Singapore. We couldn't get a reservation but after a nice phone call to find out if they take walk-ins, we decided to give it a try. Since the group as a whole couldn't make it out to eat until around 730pm, we decided that the 2 who were about to fly the coup could wait while the bf and I met them an hour later. They got there at 630pm and put their names down. The plan was set in motion. I (with nothing to do at the time) decided to keep them company and met them there to wait. Since we thought it would be boring to just wait there though, we decided to go to nearby Francois Payard Bakery and have some dessert before our meal. We sat. We talked. We waited. And by 730pm, our entire group was ready to eat. Just perfect! If only... We returned to Lupa only to find out from the host that we were supposed to call 20 minutes prior to inform them that we still wanted to eat there. What?! Never heard of such a thing. And even if that was their policy, how about you tell us that when we're putting our names down?! Alas, that did not happen. We were instead asked to wait another 45 minutes to an hour, and to call in 20 minutes to tell them we still wanted to eat there. Bad service might I say? Indeed I do. I understand the mix-up but could nothing be done to somehow compensate for it? Can we not have been placed at the next table and have been told, this time once, we could sit. Next time, we must call! If not, can we not at least have had our wait time cut in half so that our starving selves didn't have to bite our arms off before being able to eat??? It's too bad really. I didn't even get to eat there and I already have such a bad taste in my mouth. Amazing how you can be so off-put before even being seated. Thanks so much hostess for ruining a lovely meal with good friends that won't be seen again for a few years!

This place is super small but cute. It gets busy for Saturday brunch, let me tell you, you're more than likely going to wait 10-15 to be seated. The hostess took down my name and phone number and said she would call me back when seating was available. She did just that which I thought was very accommodating. We were seated with another couple which means we had to share a table & wasn't to bad but a little awkward at first. I ordered The All American ($13.00) and I LOVED THE TOAST AND BACON but my scrambled eggs were not dry enough and the hash brown was too oily & didn't taste like much. I wanted to take a picture of my food for you guys cause it was so nicely plated but since we were sharing the table with another couple I felt...weird =/ My partner had the Huevos Rancheros ($12.00) and loved every bite of it. lol =) Â  The coffee ($2.75 each) by the way needs work... Didn't like it. (oh and no refills) All in all I gave this place three stars (OK) because my brunch wasn't "amazing" like other fellow yelpers experiences with Fort Defiance but that doesn't mean I wouldn't be back to try other dishes. I do however want to try other spots in the area before returning here such as The Good Fork, Home/made and Kevin's right near bye. Hostess and waiters were polite and pleasant which is always appreciated. =) Enjoy ;-)

I took my girl to a no man's land part of williamsburg, stuffed her mouth with your fantastic pizza, beautiful crust and melted cheese, and watch her do a dance of happiness and i said: Never complain again about the size of your butt!! Life is good

My friend really hyped up this place as her fav place in the city. Â Usually that's the kiss of death, but not in this case. Come here for lunch. Â It's one of the best deals in the city. Â It will still be expensive, but nothing like coming for dinner. Â I did it twice. Â Both times excellent and memorable. Â  Â Second time for my birthday and everything was flawless. Â Actually just thinking about it makes me want to come back for lunch again! Â Some things that stood out- porcini flan, steak, and just at the end when you're pretty much stuffed this huge chocolate dessert. Â They also gave me a Â nice size cake to take home for my b day. Â awesome.

I had the tasting menu and it was a huge rip-off... so much that I ended up having two slices of Â pizza afterwards. The dishes are tiny, just a bite, like the one a chef sends for free before a meal. So even after 27 of them I was starving. (Disclaimer: I do not eat red meat so of a couple of dishes I just ate the garnish) Only a couple of them were spectacular, most of them were pretty average. I have been to many tasting menus and this has been the worst. Not recommended.

This is our new favorite bar in UES! I mean, we came here twice in a week, that says something! Cool round bar, easily accessible from every spot. There are high tables/stools, booths and just all around spacious to hang. We came on a Saturday night and on a Thursday night. Both nights were busy-ish, but not overly crowded. Very laid back bartenders. Now the winner of this place is..... their extensive list of cocktail/craft beer and whiskey. I had a couple of beer the first night, while the fiance had whiskey and the next time we were here, I had a couple of cocktails and he had different whiskey. It's like whiskey heaven for anyone who likes whiskey...Prices are reasonable, not too expensive. I guess we finally found a place we can say "this is our neighborhood bar" :)

The best pizza I've had in NYC so far. Â Thus only 4 stars because there might be something better out there! Â But after a year of temping around the City, this is some of the best I've found. This is pizza just the way I like it: crispy crust, flavorful garlic-flavored marinara. Â  Yes, I remember what it tastes like a year after I've had it. It's a tiny place just off the beaten path, the perfect place to take hungry tourist friends right after they get into the Port Authority. Â  Now I need to go back.

The male host in the front seems to be too good for his job. Very unfriendly and a bit arrogant. Ramen is ok, appetizers are ok. Everything was just ok. Nothing stood out but the snotty male Asian host in the front. Did check in for a free beer though.

this place is pretty good and probably a safe place to invite others. Â The sea bass is one of the best I have had. Â The duck dish was just ok since I thought it was cooked too rare. The special chocolate soufflÃ© that night was great!
Went there on Sat night. The place really has a touch of Havana within it's walls Music, drinks, dance, food. The whole neighbourhood has quite a buzz.

a friend suggest this place as a good spot to go os on this first date with a girl i just met, i really was pleased ,the food and service was Â good,the ambiance was very chill and a perfect atmosphere for the occasion,it was just far enough away from the vortex of willamburg that it wasnt't too crowded or loud and very romantic setting.i'm stillseeing that girl so i would say it made an impression that lasted.

I came here based on the ratings and number of reviews. I have NO idea how they've gotten the score they have. The place was hard to find amongst other Japanese restaurants, in a basement, smelled like fish and had a wait of 40+ min. With all the natives dining, I knew I had to eat here. They were out of avocado salad, had no low sodium soy sauce and their menu was sticky and held together with duct tape. Our order of edamame took over 10min which we had to ask for 2x and they tasted like they'd been microwaved a few times. No good. It was so noisy in the tiny cramped space as well. Definitely not peaceful, relaxing or a good place for conversation. I could go on but if this isn't enough reason to not like this place then I don't know what else it takes. There a million other Japanese places you could eat at, I'd never eat here again.

Incredible twist on good southern food. The chicken & waffles and mac & cheese where outstanding, the perfect balance of sweet, savory, chewy and cheese. We also had a chance to try some off the menu things and let me tell you, the kitchen staff know what they are doing. Wow! Drinks are equally good, with the SoCo Saint and Blueberry Bourbon Sour being the standouts. Staff was very friendly and the service prompt. Try going on a Tuesday night to avoid the crazy night and weekend crowds. It will be worth it.

Went there on a Sat, so obviously they were very crowded. Â Tap Room where you are sent to while you wait for a table up in the Parlor had barely any room to stand and it was so loud. Â When we were finally sent upstairs, things got much better. Â Though the music was rather loud (it's not a speakeasy after all), they also had a piano player playing Ragtime music, which was fun. They have mmmany cocktails. Reading through their cocktail menu can be a bit overwhelming, but wait staff is happy to answer your questions. Â Some cocktails are definitely better than others. Â Some of them tend to be very sweet, which I will avoid next time. Â They have small plates of food, which can crowd the small table very quickly; but my friends said they were all delicious.
Amazing beef gyros. 1 definitely was not enough. Tried the spanakopita as well, but it wasn't amazing. Seating is limited and it's the small joint, but the food is great.
I love this place! Happy hour rocks! Best mac n cheese ever!
Excellent neighborhood spot with great deals on healthy food. I love having this place on my block. Eating well (and cheap too) in NYC is a real treasure. I highly recommend this place.

Definitely a hip atmosphere, and the food is ok. But if you've already paid homage, and want much better food for a much better price try La Brique around the corner on Manhattan Ave. Don't let the dorky atmosphere fool you, the food is AMAZING, and they have a nice outside deck in the summer. Everything we've had has been great, but get the Lamb Chops or Filet Minion....as good as anywhere, and half the price.

This review is not for their food but restaurant hygiene. We went to have kati rolls and sat at the back on the wooden benches. Both my sister and I got contact dermatitis where the back of our legs touched the bench. We had red itchy blisters and mine got pretty bad. Also we saw some mosquitos in the restaurant too. I don't know about the kitchen but the eating space is not kept very clean and the benches definitely have something going on.

Very tiny restaurant and difficult to carry a private conversation due the close proximity of the tables, but amazing food! Â It's BYOB, so we enjoyed our bottle of wine. Â The food tastes fresh, and the chocolate mousse was a great end to our meal. Â Will definitely go back and try the brunch.

Cubana Social is just as pretentious as the hipsters that live in Williamsburg. I guess that's why it has gotten so many rave reviews by Billyburgers. But guess what? I wasn't not impressed. AT ALL. Pretentious Act Number 1: A glass bottle of room temperature water is brought to every table sans ice. Who does that in 90 degree weather? A cute idea but really stupid in 40 degree weather. Pretentious Act Number 2: The Cuba Libre. I know using Mexican Cola is supposed to be "better" because it's made of sugar but seriously...we should never ever forgo taste. I know you can't get Havana Club rum in the states but really....how bout some Brugal or Barbet from Haiti. And use some Coca Cola. Pretentious Act Number 3: The wack ass Latin Jazz Band. No one was paying any attention. I don't even think the band was paying much attention to themselves. Pretentious Act Number 4: The burger. Ridiculously ridiculous. Beef and chorizo make a greasy spicy mess. Pretentious Act Number 5: Playing old movies on the wall. Anyway, so happy I got that all off my chest. I gave this place two stars because the yucca fries (which were like $4) were better than the whole event and the waitress was really nice. Two things to remember: An ounce of pretension is worth a pound of manure--there are much better Cuban restaurants in NYC so don't waste your time or money in this place.

Anyone who is blown away by the Meatball Shop A. Isn't Italian and B. if they are Italian, haven't had legit meatballs. I know I'm in the minority here, but it's just ok. I've gotten the smash sandwich a few times which is usually soggy and the balls are bland...just doesn't do it for me...

I love the ballfields and this place comes pretty close. Sandwiches may seem expensive. But there huge. Even the small size can feed two and the large three. The roast beef is moist as can be. Can use a bit of salt. But u can always take care of that yourself. It's a cool area to explore on ur bike. Grab a sandwich and eat by the pier near Steves pies

Excellent food and service. We went based on yelp reviews and we were not let down . The service was fantastic and the pasta was fresh and tasty. I enjoyed the veal and the wife enjoyed the cheese ravioli.

Classy!.... for a diner that is. Heck the food is way better than some other places that pass for high-end and the portions are generous. I found the best pancakes in the city here, and I'm a serious pancake critic. The staff are on it and the atmosphere is welcoming. Â Yum!
Delicious pizza. Â The only problem you may face is waiting about 45 minutes for a table. Â IT IS WORTH THE WAIT, but be prepared!

I had been really excited to go here for a few months, and a break in the cold finally coincided with some free time and I found myself in the saddle, bound for Red Hook. Â After wandering to my heart's content and my stomach's rumblings for a while along the waterfront, I made my way over to Fort Defiance in the early afternoon on a Saturday. Â I arrived a bit before my friend, so I had a moment to have a coffee and take in the surroundings. Â  Fort Defiance is comfortable, nicely set up, and just pretentious enough to be interesting without being unwelcoming. Â The pour-over coffee was good, and the staff was friendly if a bit inattentive (more on that later.) Â  My friend arrived, and the barman helpfully suggested the Savannah as among his favorites. Â We ordered a chai and a Savannah to split, and they didn't have a problem with poaching the eggs instead of scrambling, since, let's face it, scrambled eggs are a waste of good ovulation. Well, the Chai was completely forgotten until we reminded them, which happens. Â The food was aggressively mediocre - a surprisingly bland fried chicken cutlet topped with a mostly tasteless gravy accompanied by a couple of not-flaky-at-all biscuits and poached eggs floating in their own vinegary water. Â (Note: I asked for the eggs soft, but there's a difference between runny yolks and just not really draining them.) Â The chicken was less southern-fried goodness and more lazy parent shake n' bake; the frying went no deeper than the breading, leaving a totally tasteless, basically steamed piece of chicken in the middle. Â  I won't say not to go here because there may be much better things on the menu. Â I will say I was disappointed; I didn't give them a chance to redeem themselves with a cocktail, which may have been a mistake as that list looked pretty good. TL;DR: Â Nice atmosphere and a friendly staff aren't necessarily enough to fry a chicken right.

I'm not quite sure what all the hype is about? I gave this place a try twice after all the press try have gotten over the past year or two. The fried chicken was decent (I would definitely recommend Brooklyn Bowls version over Pies). The sides were not edible. The collard green were soggy and cold and the beans tasted like pure brown sugar. It was all very bland. During my second visit here, I sat in the back by the open doors and my dinner was filled with lovely rats rummaging through the garbage cans 5 feet away from me. Never again.

What did the weather this 4th of July weekend and the pancakes at Clinton Street Bakery have in common? Both were off the charts! We (3 people) did indeed wait the typical hour (got there at 11:15, seated at 12:15) and thankfully the tree next to the restaurant kept us out of the melting hot sun and the light breeze kept us from completely melting away in the 100 degree weather. Â  Once we were inside, we ordered three dishes and share them all. Their famous pancakes (blueberry) = "best pancakes I ever had" and yes, the syrup is great and just perfection in texture and balance of flavor. Â And I'm not even a huge pancake fan but these definitely break the mold... so good. country breakfast (biscuits) = typical fare, cooked well with biscuits that were more toward the crumbly with a bit more crunchy crust. Â Good and massive, I generally prefer smaller more pillowy biscuits though. and the day' special clam roll = yummy, cooked on point and good sauce with an additional side of cheese grits = my gf gobbled it up and I only had one spoonful... so much for sharing! Strawberry milkshake = which was SUPER thick. Â It was good but even though it was a bit more"chunky" rather than smooth as I typically like in a shake. Â  The space has a small friendly NY neighborhood cafe feel. Â It can get pretty loud but you can definitely still carry on a decent conversation. Â  The staff was pretty attentive and service was fast and thorough. Â They've won another convert for brunch though my friend did say the burger and beer had left something to be desired. Â Still QPR for brunch is great! But if you have a craving for pancakes... definitely come here and enjoy the best!

A great little wine bar without any pretence. To me it is not hip or sophisticated, but that does not take anything away from this establishment. What impressed me the most about this place is its bartenders. The bartender I spoke to was nice and spot-on with wine suggestions. I arrived there around 8:30 on Friday night and did not have any problem finding a seat at the bar right away. There were two, three tables open as well, but I heard a bartender tell someone those were reserved. It started to get busier after 9 pm, so reservation may be recommended if you want to be seated at the table. The food menu is short, and even though one would expect that at a wine bar, I wouldn't mind seeing a couple more selections. I ordered meatballs, and they were simple and tasty. I also had chocolate lava cake; although I love my chocolates, it was very rich, and sharing it with another person would have been just right for me.
The pizza is amazing (and cheap) and the people is nice and honest. We left a bag with over 600 usd and came back running 10 minutes later. The cashier gave it back to us.

Maysville will receive two stars from me for TWO reasons. Â The first reason being that our waitress was super unfriendly and the second reason being that the ambiance was not great. Â The interior felt cold and the lighting was too bright (picky I know). Â But back to the waitress...she made my friend and I feel like she was just trying to get us in and out so she can move on to the next reservation. Â It just did not feel like she wanted any part in adding to the experience. Â She was kind of snappy. Â When she came to take our order and we said we needed a bit more time, she looked at me like I had just murdered her entire family. Â It was bizarre. Â I thought it was just me who felt this way but when I asked my friend after she walked away, he was kind of weirded out as well. Â So I recommend if you go here, to go eat at the bar. Â The staff still needs better training on HOSPITALITY. Â But now to the most important part..the dishes. Â I had the crispy grits and the chicken for an entree. Â The crispy grits were very good and the chicken entree was awesome. Â I think overall this restaurant has a lot of promise. Â If they put as much effort into their food as they can with training their staff I feel this review would of had a greater # of stars. Â Cheers!
Deeelish! Â The vegetarian ball is something I could eat every day.

So far, I've had their portobello sandwich and their spicy tofu sandwich, and both are decidedly tasty! They are always happy to provide extra Sriracha sauce (important) and they sell blood orange lemonade (yes, it's as good as it sounds). Prices are decent. Do it!

I had the Pumpkin Cheesecake- YUM. I previously reviewed Times Square and mentioned walking over towards Hell's Kitchen area instead of eating around Time Square... I hit this place first to grab a slice of cake knowing I wasn't coming back in that direction. It was a quick line and early on a early Sat. evening.

Nature Works restaurant opened just a couple of months ago but I have been a very loyal customer ever since. I try to eat there all the time not only the food is very healthy and delicious but also it is very reasonably priced. The sandwiches that I order are always fresh, never pre-made so they taste fantastic. The stuff is always very friendly and prompt. The place is very small but still has a few seats. Sometimes I eat in there but more often I take out. I highly recommend this place.

Pizza Hut with better quality toppings. Â That may bother some people but it's the truth, good or bad. Â We got the Â "Old Fashioned Pizza" which looked great when it came out. Â The pie appeared to be thicker like a sicilian (which I love) but this turned out to be a clever ruse as the pie was very fluffy (similar to Pizza Hut). Â There was no density, and this really bothers me as the texture feels very mushy, almost as though someone has already chewed the dough. Â The bottom of the pie was oily and had this flavor reminiscent of Pizza Hut & BJ's Restaurants, both of which put some kind of butter or oil on the bottom of their pizzas. Â  Also, when we were there the waitress asked the people next to us to leave since they were done and people were waiting. Â Personally, I think this is rude. Â In my experience so far the main thing I've noticed about NY vs LA is that they usually don't try to rush you out of a restaurant in NY and I prefer this. Â Being in the finance industry I get tired of people having ego's that they shouldn't have, and I don't need a restaurant to have it also. Conclusion, if you love Pizza Hut but always wanted a higher quality version than this is your place. Â If you are not a Pizza Hut fan then don't waste your time because you can easily find way better pizza in NY.
LOVE lobster! Â Try different rolls, beer on tap, cute outside eatiing area. Â Good service.

I had high hopes for grey dog and unfortunately it came up short. Loved the feel of the place immediately, menu prices didn't look bad and I like how u order at the counter. I had the pancakes and they were just a little too simple, needed something else to make them stand out. We also had the raw tuna tacos. Those were much better then the pancakes, I liked the salsa that came with it. I would give it a 3.5 overall, the food is just missing that extra something to make it really stand out.

Mmmm mmmm the dumplings here are so delicious. And the house made chili sauce is awesome. They also sell frozen dumplings 50 for 9 dollars you really can't beat that. A little bit of a task to find the first time but worth the journey.

Definitely authentic, hand made tortillas and fresh salsas. Great carne asada tacos and quesadilla de nopal. The salsa had great flavor, extremely spicy but mouth watering good. Line is usually long but moves fast absolutely worth it. Try the aguas frescas I love Jaimaica and Horchata and they also help ease the spice from the salsa. Order Corn tortillas that's the way to go both for tacos and quesadillas, flour takes away from the flavors.

I've walked past this bar on Sullivan Street for years and never noticed it...and boy, I had no idea what I was missing. Â This is one of the best bars I've ever been to. Â The drinks are good, the music is fantastic (but not overwhelming...you can really carry on a conversation here), but it's really all about atmosphere at Shades. Â This is a small bar, but it has super-funky low lighting, and black leather banquets that are really comfortable. Â The BEST part is...this place is right next to a creperie and it smells FANTASTIC! Â I'll be back soon!
Great food, easy ordering. Grandson suggested we eat there. Â Very happy

I went on a Sunday night and had a great time -- good service, great cheese selection, and excellent pizza. Â It's now part of my "regular rotation" of restaurants. They sell many of their ingredients on the back of the menu -- one of the items I would *highly* recommend is their olive oil -- it is advertised as being low in acidity, and it hits the mark -- flavorful but completely "un-acidic"., I split a cheese plate with my girlfriend (stinky cheese lovers have nothing to fear -- the Gorgonzola is good!) and then had the Vidalia onion and spicy provolone pizza. Â The shredded onion on the pizza was a great addition to the cheese. The drink specials are tasty, and the wine comes in glass, quartino, and bottle quantities for those of you who like wine. Â  The only thing I would warn fellow yelpers about are the bathrooms -- they open up onto a passageway that is frequented by the staff and next to the kitchen. Â Open the door slowly :)

Solid West Village restaurant. Â Lots of great food options. Â The cold vegetable soup gaspacho was excellent, and so was the tuna tartar. Â I cleaned my ravioli plate, so that says something as well. Â The restaurant has some outdoor seating, which is nice in the warmer weather. Â Decor on the inside is fair, 3 out of 5. Â Service was a bit off, could have been we had a new server, also felt rushed to pay and leave at the end of the night when there were still other patrons there. Â In the end, I will be a repeat customer.

OMG their sandwiches are delicious. And the interior is so cozy. The guy making the sandwich and drinks was a little...how should I say....out of it? But my sandwich was still beyond delicious. I would definitely come here to relax, drink some tea and have another sandwich. It's just a little out of the way but worth it. Oh but it closes early! At 7 or 8 I believe.

What a difference two years makes--and that ain't good. The whole place is remodeled: the romantic dim lights are now bright, there are fewer artifacts, the unique qualities of the place are gone. Worse still are the changes in the food--the tender hanger steak I'd dreamed about is a different and cheaper cut. Tough, I must add, and too done outside, not done enough inside. Only the fabulous sauce and Yukon Gold mash were unchanged. (The asparagus was replaced by really good baby spinach--acceptable substitution.) The service was the most unkindest cut of all--the server was spraying disinfectant on the adjoining tables, and it wafted in the direction of our drinks. When we asked for replacements, he told us that nothing had gotten in them, and he didn't replace them until we insisted--this was ginger ale and Coke, y'unnerstand, not even cocktails! Our crÃ¨me brulee came in a chipped ramekin, and the cashier had trouble breaking a twenty. Robert Irvine would have knocked a few heads together on this paragraph alone.

I think Ngam stands for Nom-Nom-Nom. The food here was seriously delicious! Generally I get a little concerned when I hear about 'fusion' food cause usually that means two things, 1) the price has been raised 2) flavors tend to get muted in an attempt to make it palatable for everyone and ends up being less authentic. Thankfully this was NOT the case here. The food had bold thai flavors and tasted great. Things I tried:: lamb roti potpie, and thai burger. Thankfully I had friends willing to share and I was able to try both of these things. The potpie had a roti on top of it. Came in a cute small iron skillet and tasted really great. Soft pieces of lamb and the roti on top was pretty good. There was no crust inside, just on top but its probably better that way since there's less fat. The thai burger was excellent. I was expecting some muted vague spice taste but instead it was extremely flavorful and packed quite a bit of heat. It's definitely worth trying since it's quite different from an ordinary burger you'd get.
This is one of the best drunk/late night/hungover food I've ever had in a while. Sum it up with cheap, quick and yummie..

Oh Tom's! You were one of the highlights of NY! :) Your breakfast hit the spot in many ways! The decor was interesting but totally cute in many ways! Your service was spectacular and the wait was no wait at all! You make breakfast time super cozy and enjoyable! I took a trip to NY with a couple of girls and one of our stops was Brooklyn. We had a day to wonder around and enjoy the town. It was great! But boy we were hungry! We yelped places to eat at and this was one that looked pretty tasty! We were RIGHT! Tom's! Your breakfast was soo tasty! Eggs Benedict with fluffy potatoes! A side of cornbeef hash to wash it down! It was worth the crazy walk through the cold! Great service! Friendly to all our request! I remember the bathroom was a bit small! But hey! Still.. you were good! :)

Alta is tucked away on W 10th Street and if you're not looking for it, it's easy to walk by this inconspicuous West Village restaurant. The interior of the restaurant is surprisingly large and has multiple floors. We were seated in an area of the restaurant next to the street-facing windows. Â To get there, our hostess us led us on a brisk walk up the stairs and through the kitchen - an experience that reminisces of "Goodfellas." For our date night dinner, we ordered 5 plates after contemplating between several exciting dishes on the menu. 1- Fried Goat Cheese I'm not a huge fan of goat cheese, but this starter dish was more than fine by me. Â The goat cheese came on a skewer atop lavender honey. Â The sweetness of the honey and the sourness/saltiness of the fried goat cheese turned out to be a great combination! 2- Scallops This dish was on the pricier side at $18 for 2 scallops. Â The scallops were damn good though and plated beautifully. Â If I had to choose again, I would still have gotten this dish. Â The pureed olive in the middle of the plated complemented the scallops well. Unfortunately, to prevent the scallops from overcooking, the temperature of this dish was slightly compromised. Â It was a bit lukewarm when it arrive at our table. 3- Peking Duck Again, I applaud the chef for the presentation. Â The peking duck was tender and tasty, although again, a bit lukewarm. While the temperature of the duck wasn't as hot as I would've liked it to be, it was still a delicious dish. 4- Lamb Tagine I had hoped that I could order the short rib dish that my friends had talked about, but I was informed that it was a dish that was offered only during the fall/winter season. Â The lamb was melt-in-your-mouth tender and the flavor was excellent. Â The boyfriend wasn't too much of a fan of this dish (he said there was something missing that he couldn't quite pinpoint), but I didn't find anything wrong with this one. 5- Hanger Steak Oh god. What a disappointing end to an otherwise decent meal. I'm curious as to how long they left this one out for because it was borderline cold. Despite the beautiful presentation, there wasn't much to highlight about this dish. The steak was overcooked on some parts (medium to well) and only one of the cuts was medium-rare. Â  I always try to save room for dessert, but after the few dishes that failed to impress, we were more than happy to pick up the check and leave. Â The common theme of lukewarm dishes really takes away from the otherwise beautiful presentation and delicious flavors.

I give it 5 stars because all the important things to me when I go to a new place was there, which are HOSPITALITY and GREAT FOOD. I went to this location based off of a friends review and he said it was good food and I wasn't let down. Plus everyone had good attitudes and personality. The location is small and isn't for lavish or long stay dates. I actually like that there wasn't a tv to look at. Sometimes you just want to eat! And if that's an issue then it's not for you but that just means your focus wasn't on great food.

Luluc has the feeling of a neighbourhood French bistro. I go here on a regular basis for late dinners after concerts and the waiters are always super nice and give us free desserts and special little things like that. Even after I accidentally tangled up a bunch of helium balloons in one of their fans. The salads here are really creative - I like the one with cilantro, chick peas and corn and the lobster-chorizo dish is really good as well. Lots of well-priced wines by the glass and good steak frites!
You can order a flight of bacon...need I say more. Never under estimate the healing power of bacon.

LOVE THIS SPOT...been here 4 times, once for daytime happy hour where I was downing Mojitos, and other 3 times on Saturday nights. Scenery is colorful & cozy (except the booth chairs does hurt your butt), pretty decent sized place, a dj, a full bar, and the wait staff are outstanding.. And the food??...is a mouthgasm. Â I've had different dishes everytime I've been there and I'm always impressed. The last time I was there I had the bandeja Paisa Columbian Platter which succulent steak & the pork was nice and tender, def one of the best dishes there, with generous portion sizes. Food always has flavor. Drinks: I was recommended something by the waitstaff based on what I was in the mood for and they usually were on the money. HIGHLY RECOMMEND this spot to chill with a group, grab drinks and eat some good food..make reservations before you go since wait time is about 45 mins

WHO'S CRAVING FOR SOME EGG SANDWICH? --------------------------------------------------Â­--------- Hands down the best egg sandwich i've every had. There's no one single word to describe the way this place cooks their egg. It is so fluffy and moist!!! Location: near empire state building. IF you want to feel like a tourist for a day and pay a visit to the empire state building, stop by here for brunch. I heard the wait on weekend is absolutely insane. Luckily I came here on Monday morning so we got seated within 10 min. Service was very good, the waitress and waiter were very attentive. Ordered for 4: Portion size here is quiet small, you can still share if you are looking for a lighter meal. PENNY EGG SANDWICH (x2): they ran out of croissant that day : ( So instead we got the penny egg sandwich with muffin. The egg is so moist and soft! The pesto sauce inside the sandwich pairs so well with the egg and sausage of our choice. It is a great combo. DEF my FAV! OMELETTE OF YOUR CHOICE: The omelette is also very good. You can pick 3 items of your choice for the omelette. What I like about their omelette is that it isn't super big to the point that it fills your whole stomach. They serve omelette with potato and bread. ABUELO'S EGG SANDWICH: The egg in this sandwich is more liquified. The egg juice will drips down which makes it more difficult to eat with hands. I cut up my whole entire sandwich which doesn't look very appetizing. The seasoning of this sandwich is very good but I didn't like the type of bread they used. Its more on the hard side. Overall, would definitely come back here again for brunch. Not sure if i am willing to wait hours and hours on weekend since the restaurant is quiet small. Goodluck

One of my favorite spots for lunch. Â I get corn quesadillas, sometimes two sometimes three. Â Pork and steak are very good, while chicken is tastier than any other chicken quesadilla that I've had. Unfortunately they don't have designated sitting space, so you'll have to run around to find something on your own.
great place ,always packed but the wait is worth it. excellent burger.and when it s sunny eat outside.
Recently Yelp reviewed Â about ceviche but I didn't mention mention the ceviche here at the restaurant Cuba. I haven't been a ceviche fan until the waiter really to try it. Really amazing!

I wish this place was bigger because it's a great place Â to eat "family style" so you can try almost EVERYTHING! We had a party of 6 and had to wait over an hour... but it was totally worth it. The thai iced tea comes out in a chemistry set... with thai tea ice cubes, thai tea, milk and sugar for you to mix to taste. The 6 of us shared 5 dishes and were all pretty full. The pad thai has unique taste.. almost like a bbq sauce kick. We also has the basil Â with tofu, crab fried rice in coconut, crispy chicken and five seeds and the lamb massaman. All very tasty!

A popular place for brunch so come early or be prepared to wait in line. The space is really cozy and the service is quite friendly. Food is not bad. Â The Abuelo's Egg Sandwich was made to perfection - with a slightly runny yolk, slightly sweet/tangy balsamic-mayo and savory ham on a soft roll. Â Delicious! Other than that, the nutella french toast sounds better than it tasted. Â It was on the dry side and did not have enough nutella. The brunch menu is not particularly inventive nor varied but I'd come back again if I was in the neighborhood, although I'm more curious about lunch/dinner next.

Been wanting to try Kiwiana for months and finally made it in last Friday night for dinner. Everything was superb. The special cocktail (called the "muffin top") tasted like a sophisticated lemon poppyseed muffin in a highball class. Doesn't sound as appealing as it was-it was amazing. The butternut squash soup was deliciously smooth and original. We had the fried chicken and the salmon entrees, both great. We were too full for desert but look forward to coming back to try some next time. It was a bit loud but the kind and attentive service and the great food more than made up for that.

Monday, I had my third visit since Feast's opening in March , and I have been wowed every time. The food is always amazing! The service is friendly, attentive and unpretentious. The decor has a playful sense of humor, comfort and elegance. The low lighting Â helps to create a sense of intimacy, while the seating and open kitchen develops a sense of a magical shared experience. It's fun to catch a glimpse of the chef in action and then to see that action transformed into delicious plate after plate presented before you. I also love the fact that once your table makes the decision of which feast to enjoy, you have nothing else to worry about other than the conversation of your table and what very reasonable and refreshing beverage will accompany your courses to come. Â Another great thing about Feast is that the menu changes frequently, so there is always something new to try. Â What the chef puts on the menu is beautiful, creative and delicious. Every time I've dined here I leave feeling like I just had the best meal of my life. What my table had Â that you should have too: Shellfish Feast, and because we are glorious gluttons... several a la carte items. We had beautifully dressed Oysters Escabeche; Crispy , light and adorable Oyster Po Boy Sliders; Creamy and petite Razor Clam Pizza; Seared Scallop with shaved fennel and citrus, perfectly cooked and Â humongous btw. Baby Clams with house made linguini, Mussels with fried hominy in white wine with crusty farmers bread, so great ! - mussels were beautiful, bountiful and excellently seasoned. Not to mention the house made bread Â with super crisp crust, perfect for sopping up the broth, and also... The Pig's Ear Taco was fascinating, fun, fried,a fantastic new experience for me ! Beet and Burrata Â with watercress - Loved ! BBQ pulled pork on fried green tomato Â with a green peppercorn sauce on plate, tasted like a sunny southern summer afternoon, Market Â Salad was Â zesty and refreshing! We also enjoyed the sweet Tomato Tartar Tartlet and Tempura Asparagus Fronds with an addictive dipping sauce. If that wasn't enough ... to set us over the blissful edge, Â we had two desserts the Ice cream filled cream puff drizzled in dark chocolate and topped with crispy bits of bacon which was a decadent and well balanced dessert, I can't stop thinking about it ! And the equally amazing Â shortbread cookie and mixed seasonal berry compote!

This place is like the anti JG Melons. Leave all pretention at the door. This place has a ridiculous line, that works itself down the bar, so plan on drinking a few before you even sit down.....which is damn easy cause they are dirt cheap. The burgers and fries are served on what looks like coffee filters, but they are delicious. And coming from a guy who has had 20+ dollar burgers all over the city, I prefer the $6 version at corner bistro This is a great place to start the night, and a great place to come with a few friends no matter if your an artist or a banker, people are friendly but keep to themselves. Better yet, go somewhere else, so I don't have to wait in line for so long.

What does one need to know about this place? BYOB - they have a one bottle per table policy. However, they do not say how large that bottle can be. Last time, I brought a magnum (wine not condom) and they happily accommodated us. The sushi during happy hour is cheap as balls. Stuff your face silly for $12. Is it gourmet? Of course not. Is it average? Definitely. In any case, it's surely worth more than the $3.50 you're paying for it. Also, check in for some free edamame. They forgot to bring it out last time but I was too stuffed, anyways. This place has been relatively empty the last few times I've been but seeing the rapidly accumulating number of reviews, I fear that is no longer the case. Here's to hoping that they keep their BYOB feature.

I've been here twice now and they have both been great experiences. Â The service is friendly and fast, and the food is delicious and memorable. Â Ive tried their beet salad, their pear and endive salad, and they have been full of flavor, light and refreshing. Ive tried their quatro stagioni and smoked pancetta pizzas and they are mouth watering good. Â The thin crust, and top-rated cheese fill your moth with robust flavors and at the end of the meal, you're satisfied and full without the bloat. Â I can't wait to try everything on their menu. Trivia nights are fun too. Â This is a great local restaurant and bar.

Beyond Sushi is my favorite restaurant in NY. The servers are SO friendly, as is the owner, Chef Guy. I've never had anything I didn't like there. I went there at least 6 times a week this past semester, and now that I'm studying abroad, it's the main thing I miss!!! Too bad Beyond Sushi doesn't cater to Italy :( I'm taking a taxi right there from JFK in June! Thanks Beyond Sushi for the best vegan food ever and amazing memories! Also, if you have the chance to take Chef Guy's sushi making class. DO IT!!! So much fun.
TRUFFLE MAC N CHEESE AND LOBSTER BLT. ultimate hungover food.

oh. my. god. When I hear someone say "this is the best pizza place", I tend to be skeptical. There's nothing too special about the atmosphere of this place. Â  For the most part, you have to go out of the way to get to it, even though it's just a short walk from the subway stop. Â But it looks like a typical pizza place. Friendly staff, small seating area, cash only, nothing special. But the pizza! Â THE PIZZA! Â DELICIOUS! Fresh basil on everything is wonderful! Â Definitely the best pepper and onions pizza I've ever eaten! Â Everything was just... amazing! Â Definitely worth the trek down there!

What a hidden gem!!! The space is small-- just a few tables and a bar in a little, narrow space. But it's totally worth waiting for a table. They offer to take your number and they will call you and give you a 15 min warning that your table is about to free Â up, which I think is so cool of them! But be warned- this place is best for parties of 2 or - max- 4. Larger than that and there is truly no way they can accommodate you. Atmosphere is warm, inviting, and cozy. They had board games that you can pull out and play with if you so desire, which was such a cute touch and added to the casual and friendly vibe. The menu is small and rotates often. They only serve beer and wine, but the selections were impressive for both and my friend and I had a spectacular Syrah. The boys had really good craft beers as well. We ordered a bunch of food and ate family style. Food was EXCELLENT! We had hummus, tuna tartare, olives, and two of the cheeses. Cheese was kind of skimpy in portion size, so order at least 2 or 3. Came with some jam and almonds, but it was definitely "snack" size, which is how they label it to indicate that the portions aren't going to be too huge. For mains, we tried the gnocchi, paella, assorted roasted veggies, lobster Mac & Cheese and chorizo Mac & Cheese. Portions again are small enough that for four of us, that actually was a good portion of food. The Mac & Cheese was insanely delicious, with a perfect cheesy crust on the top. I tried the paella and it was also fantastic-- generous on the fish and meat with less rice, which is the sign of a great paella. The gnocchi was also fantastic-- they melted in your mouth. All the selections were ideal for a cold, Jan evening. Highly recommend but make sure to call ahead and find out what the availability looks like, first!

I had dinner at Becco, and it was a wonderful meal. The place was packed and noisy, but the service was very attentive. The restaurant is bigger than it looks and we sat in one of the back rooms. The pasta is amazing, and they bring it out in pan right from the kitchen and serve it at the table. Portions are big and prices are reasonable. They have an extensive wine list but also serve by the glass. If you are in the Theater District and want great Italian food in a somewhat casual setting, this is the place to go.
Awesome food! Try the Bihari Lamb and Bihari Dal- loved it! Great service... Good ambiance ... Overall an awesome place..! Bit costly- but worth it

This review is purely based on brunch. IT WAS ABSOLUTELY DELICIOUS! After reading fellow Yelp reviews, my friend and I ordered the bread basket. Please note that it's not just bread. It has donut holes, mini muffins, banana bread, scones and other delicious mouth watering sweet goodness. I ordered their fried chicken on sweet potato waffles. The key is gravy. They smother it and it's absolutely delicious!!!!!!! Waffles were a little bland and not what I was expecting (I was expecting waffles to be completely made up of sweet potato, but it wasn't), but their gravy just makes everything better. Also, I had their salad and omelet. Perfectly seasoned and cooked and light. I highly recommend it with the fried chicken because it's heavy. GO FOR BRUNCH! It's a really cute place, layout is nice and how can you say no to bread basket filled with goodies?!

the wait staff here was very friendly, and the food was okay, but what happened after was neither. about 20 minutes after i left my stomach felt queazy and i had to go to the bathroom. i don't think it was food poisoning, but i know my body and i eat a very stable and consistent diet, so if i feel something gastrointestinal going on i'm usually pretty sure what the cause is. in this case since it had been about 6 hours since i'd eaten lunch i am extremely confident that it was what i ate here for dinner that did it. anyway, i thought i would call the restaurant and just give them a heads up, maybe tell them what it was that i ate so that they could be aware of it and flag it. might as well. well, i called to let them know that my stomach was queasy and i had the s#!ts but instead of acknowledging that there was any possibility that they were the cause of it, the maitre-d immediately denied that it could have come from them on the basis that it was a scientific fact. he said food born illnesses take hours to set in. first of all that's incorrect. faculty.ksu.edu.sa/hkoraâ€¦ this presentation from Hesham M. Korashy, PhD, Assistant Professor of Molecular Toxicology at Kansas State University explicitly states that "If symptoms occur within 1-6 hours after eating the food it suggests that it is caused by a bacterial toxin or food or a chemical rather than live bacteria. i felt symptoms 2 hours after finishing eating. so Dr. Maitre-D was wrong. there are plenty of other sources on the internest as well. bottom line: instead of recognizing that a customer had a complaint, recognizing the possibility it was their food and their fault and and apologizing for it, or even asking what it was that i ate, their staff effectively just told me that i was wrong and that it was something i ate for lunch elsewhere. blatant reappropriation of blame and disregard for the politeness to customers and the potential well-being of other customers. i've worked many years in the food service industry, and i have rarely heard a customer ever make a complaint which was not immediately returned with an apology. even if a customer is wrong, you should never put them in a position of error to their face - that's what the back is for, you go talk all the crap you want to the chefs and your coworkers, out of sight, out of range. i've dealt with plenty of complaints in kitchens over the years from diners calling in or bringing food back, and the FIRST thing i ALWAYS say to them EVEN IF I FEEL LIKE THEY ARE WRONG is..."i'm so sorry, what can i do for you to make up for this?". this guy didn't even apologize, he just patronized me. unfortunate. i didn't even have any intention of writing a bad review, i just wanted to call them and let them know what i ate and how i felt. but after that phone conversation i realized that if he wouldn't take my complaint then yelp would. i had ordered a soft shell crab special and a bunch of those antipasti vegetable buffet dishes that were sitting out exposed for who knows how long.
great food, great service and reasonably priced tasting menu @ 110 pp.

I have mixed sentiments about this place. Â I came here on a weeknight with a friend of mine who wouldn't stop raving about how amazing the food is. Â I expected there to be a wait around 7pm, but the restaurant was 75% empty. Â Despite there being empty tables, they sat us between 2 other parties of 2... not a big deal, but still annoying. Â I ordered the seafood pasta. Â The seafood was mediocre at best. Â Some of the mussels had sand in them and way too much undercooked calamari. Â The pasta however was amazing!! Â I kept digging around my plate trying to find more pasta only to find calamari :/ Â Oh well.. the place did fill up plenty when we left at 8-ish and there was a wait out the door. Â It was solid Italian food, but with so many options in the city, I won't be returning.

Got the standard: blueberry pancakes, maple butter, sugar cured bacon, apple cider, and a bloody mary. My friends got the biscuits and gravy, the waffles, and the cheddar grits. It's great. Was it worth a 2 hour wait? I don't know. It's definitely worth coming here once. Then you can decide whether or not you want to come back.

I eat here about once a month or more. The wait gets up to an hour during dinner time, but you can turn up early, leave your number, and go to the Irish pub across the street to drown your wait. It is worth it, compared to other yakitori places around the world (Tokyo, Hong Kong, SF) and in the city, this place more than holds its own in price for tastebuds. I mean, just look at the chefs (ok, they look little more like teenagers fiddling with a BBQ set, but most Asians look younger than they are anyway... and I digress). Hunched over your precious orders of skewers as they artfully flip, poke, fiddle and prod your dinner. Â  Of course, the proof of the pudding is in the eating. My faves non-chicken dishes are the skirt steak skewer (yes, I know its a chicken place, the kanji script translates literally into Chicken Man), deep fried fish cakes, tofu skewer, and for desert, the almond soya pudding with a side of red bean. It just melts in your mouth. Now onto the piÃ¨ce de rÃ©sistance - the chicken. I usually order the thigh, chicken wrapped asparagus, the sweet sesame chicken (dish, not a skewer). The exotic range from soft knee bone, tail, neck, heart, and other parts you never thought could be eaten. These are limited in quantity each day - your server will advise you if they are still available. If they sound too much of an adventure, at least attempt the "rare part of thigh". Trust me, it tastes like, well - chicken.

Watch Your Anus. That's my advice before you dig into their delicious and ass-kicking (literally) hot sauce and smear it all over their tasty offerings. Â This place is one of my go-to delivery joints thanks to their incredibly tasty and consistent Turkish offerings. Â  My suggestion is to go with their amazing sandwiches. Â The lamb gyro sandwich is killer. Â They don't cheap out on the meat and it's filled to the brim with lettuce, onions and tomatoes. Â Pour some of that creamy white or red hot sauce (or both) on the sandwich and you're in for a real treat. Â The price here is also good, with sandwiches in the $6 to $7 dollar mark. Â And it's totally worth your while. Â I also recommend the lamb kebab sandwich, though personally I think the gyro sandwiches have much more flavor. Â The platter versions of this food (meat + rice instead of a wrap) is good but frankly I think the sandwich options are tastier and more bang for your buck. The desserts here are also good. Â I've tried them all, but honestly only recommend the brown-top pudding. Â It's totally awesome. Personally I think you should opt for the delivery option here. Â It's a whole lot better than dining there. Â They get the food to your place pretty fast. Â Usually I never wait longer than 30 minutes with delivery usually taking about 15 to 20 min for a 7 block trip. Â Dining in isn't great because 1. the place is tiny as hell 2. you'll end up smelling like food big time 3. the ambiance is as exciting as a linen closet, though they do have a TV playing some random Turkish program or soccer game in the background.

After attempting to eat here short of a dozen times, I finally made it in today. Â Thanks to Lauren's bright idea about going there at 8:30 am for brunch - which to me defies brunch since it's too early. Â Let's call it breakfast for now. Â  Before I get started - let me digress a bit. Â Don't you just hate it when something is so hyped and you make the mistake of building your expectation so high and then you experience it first hand and then you just say "eh". Â So, I'm torn about why I am not raving about this place as much as I should. Â I liked my dish (spanish omlette), let me make that clear firsthand. Â Could it be that for the almost half a dozen times I attempted to eat here the line was ridiculously long and walked away? Â Did I build the hype too high in my head? Â Am I just frustrated about my many failed attempts??? Â  So, I decided not to give a bad review but to make this fair I will go back again soon. Â I should have tried their popular blueberry pancake, maybe I would feel differently. Â  After that, I'll have to edit my review if it lives up to its reputation. Oh.. I hated the fact that they sat us, a part of 3, at a table for 2. Â I guess that's what happens when the line is out the door by 8:30 am.

I loved this place. The food was great and the service was just as good, they don't ignore you but they don't breathe down your neck. The ambiance is great, kind of romantic but it is a little loud. I just had a could gripes that could be easily fixed. The tiramisu was awesome only AFTER you took all the chocolate sauce they drenched it in off. My bf got the lamb chops and they tasted amazing but they're served on this wood block which looks cool, but the juices ended up dripping all over his jeans(I'm aware that sounds dirty but there's no other way to put it). Â  All in all it was pretty good and we will be going back. Great tasty simple menu.
This place has done so much for this part of our neighborhood. Â We love you Habana Outpost!

I have this amazing friend who knows all the great cuisine spots that I overlook. Ngam, which is steps from my place, is amazing. Always walked by it, but didn't give it thought. Came here and really enjoyed. The servers are nice. They are accommodating, yet don't hover. I never felt rushed by them, which is a good thing in my book. Food was amazing. I had the spicy drunken noodles. Boy, were they spicy. At least to me. Thai iced tea was proportioned well & amazing. 90's R&B and rap played in the background too. Loved it.

Two of had dinner last week; neither of us had really had authentic Korean before, but after walking by this restaurant and seeing how busy it always was (and after reading the good yelp reviews), we had to give it a try. Â We had an amazingly friendly and helpful server who steered us to some great dishes and even warned us when we were about to order too much food. Â Loved the homemade tofu, the bbq chicken, the squid and the banchan. Â Looking forward to trying it again!

Decent beers, amazing steak burger, and pretty good fries that complement the burger pretty well. Poutine was pretty good as was the pasta carbonara with sausage. The pasta was even better when I mixed in their house made hot sauce. Complimentary dessert donut holes were a nice touch.
This place is simply delicious. And for a great price. Love it!!
Had brunch today and the food was fantastic. Not sure why negative reviews. The staff was very friendly and accommodating. Looking forward to going back and trying foie gras burger.

thats it, im sick of salt, im done with sodium i'm sick of pork belly i'm sick of greasy meals that make me wish i werent such a glutton i'm so sick of waiting an hour for noodles yet I cannot keep away from ippudo for more than 3 weeks at a time

I just had an incredible dinner here. It was my first time and I'm already planning my next...I ordered the duck and it was cooked perfectly. My friend and I stayed close to an hour after our meal, chatting away, and didn't feel rushed at all. The only neg is that we both had to ask for more water not once, but two times :( But other than that it was a great experience!
DO NOT GET THE PAD THAI. It was red and tasted like BBQ sauce. There were no peanuts to be found. Also, there wasn't any eggplant in the green curry.

I've been going to Blue Ribbon Brasserie since the day they opened. Â They still have some of the same staff members that opened this restaurant. Â Great oysters and other raw bar items. Â Excellent wine list as well. Â The menu has lots of choices and every one of them RULES! Â A must have is the Chocolate Bruno for dessert. Â It is SERIOUS! Â The Bromberg brothers have killed it in the restaurant scene in New York and beyond. Â They do everything right. Â Open from 4pm to 4am and packed til closing.

In my opinion the best Banh mi in the neighborhood. After having to suffer through some pretty sub par sandwiches from others, I'm glad I found them. Their bread is crisp, fresh and the perfect compliment to the chicken or pork. I haven't tried anything other than the sandwiches, but based on how good they are, I'm sure the rest of the menu is on point.

I've never witnessed anything quite like this but tonight me and two of my girlfriends were looking to bar hop and found ourselves here at Ear Inn where some random old guy offered to buy first round. When carded by the bartender we all pulled out our NJ, NY, and FL state issued IDs. With our ages ranging from 25 to 27 we expected all to be well - however two of us were very rudely turned away. When asked what the problem was the tender said my ID was fine but pointed to my two friends saying their ID's were obviously fake, threatening to call the police. When we said "please do" he said "just leave, we don't want them here." Me being the only white person - "them" very clearly referred to my two black companions. Please do not patronize this place. No one should be treated this way.
Excellent burger, good energy, friendly service, priced right.

Great atmosphere as you walk in. Â You greeted at the hostess stand and by the maitre d immediately. Â We had reservations and were see to our table right away. * The room is beautiful and classy * Service was outstanding * The fresh bread with a white fish spread was delicious * Â The jumbo shrimp from the raw bar were amazing. * Main courses didn't disappoint either * Â We were meeting friends and had no time for desert. Â However, on the way out the maitre d/manager invited us to have a free after dinner cocktail at the bar. Â It was a very nice gesture and the perfect way to end the experience at the restaurant. High marks for food. Even higher marks for service and atmosphere. Â Enjoy!

What a pleasant treat! Went here for dinner and while it I s totally out of the way unless you live in TriBeCa or Battery Park or work down there, it is totally worth a trip! The decor reminds me of chic restaurant in a ski chalet in Europe or Aspen. You'll know what I mean when you go. The service is superb, our server was quite awesome! We started with the abalone and wagyu tartar..that wagyu was amaaazing. I had the Jack Ryan cocktail..sweet and goes down very easy! :) I and the lamb, which was good.. But paled in comparison to the butterscotch desert.. I am still dreaming of it :)

Great food, great drinks. I like this place because as i bite into my first bite, for a very brief moment, I feel like I'm in Cali. But then reality sets in when I realize that the Guac costed me $7 (or something along those lines). Dios mio!

TWO CHECK-INs IN ONE DAY! WOO! We went here for brunch and love it so much that we came back to try their dinner menu. Both meals were outstanding. And the best thing was that they remembered us from the morning! This place is intimate, romantic, homey, casual, friendly, delicious...the only bad word to describe this place would be...cramped. But I forgive you because at least I am too busy stuffing my face with your delicious food to care about my food neighbors. Ceviche de Bife -- SO GOOD. Practically like awesome beef sashimi if that makes any sense...It just thin slightly raw slices of tasty meat heaven. To be more specific, it is seared rib-eye. Hanger Steak & 2 Eggs -- YUM. Nothing to complain about here. Price point is $11 for two perfect eggs, a piece of great tasting meat, salad, and potatoes? Just yum. Avocado Fries -- INTERESTING. I love avocado so therefore I like this. It basically slices of avocado in some sort of breading that's been fried? baked? I don't know. But it's good. Warm avocado, and a crunchy exterior mmm. Of course I was fat and just ate all of it myself, it would have been better to share because avocado=fat. Steak/some sort of beef -- Sadly I forget which one we ordered but it was so good!! And it came with two sauces that paired so well with the meat. I never really like eating beef but I just wanted to eat more and more! Price point is not bad either :)

Came here for lunch, restaurant was pretty empty, we were attended to right away, service was good. The space was much smaller than I expected. Now on to the food, eh I was a little disappointed I was expecting more based on the reviews, the food wasnt bad but it didnt blow me away. I ordered the shrimp po boy with fries, my friends all got the chicken and waffles and there were mixed reviews around the table. I may come back to try something else on the menu and update this review.
Amazing Pork Soup Dumplings , Crispy Pan Fried Noodle w Beef . Also try the Chicken & Green Beans w. Garlic Sauce. Consider this your inside Scoop.

After much review, we chose Gramercy Tavern as our one special dinner while we were visiting New York last week. We were sorely disappointed. For that amount of money, I expected the meal to be outstanding, and it was not. We have dined in many fine restaurants and we have never had an experience like this, where the food for the most part seemed uninspired. Some courses were good, most were just okay, like the squid ink spaghetti. Our experience was surprising since there are so many great reviews about this restaurant. Not sure if it was an off night, but for over $300, I don't think we will take our chance on this place again.

So worth a visit! Such a cute, French-inspired corner gem. Interior is homey, with postcards from all over Europe covering the walls. The area is calm, however I was there with my friend on a thursday right before noon. This is not a fancy place, but it got the warmth, which I value a lot. The prices are very reasonable in relation to the taste and sizes of the portions, which are not too big, thank god. We ordered the breakfast buckwheat crepes, which were very good! Home made straight from the back kitchen, which must have been small because we had to wait a good 25 minutes for our food, watching the few couples that had arrived before us getting their dishes. The one and only waiter, a French man, was very nice once I stopped him and started asking questions about the place. He spoke a little French with me. The only negative thing about the place is that it doesn't take cards, you can only pay in cash. However, there is an ATM in the little place hidden in a corner to not take away from the old-fashioned south-French interior design.

heres why i have to encourage others to go elsewhere. The empanadas were pretty good. SADLY THE SERVICE TURNS YOU OFF COMPLETELY. The long sliced plantains with the guac was pretty impressive. unfortunately- its staffed with TERRIBLE employees

This is a great place to hang out with friends. The food is delicious and the service is friendly. My favorites are the burger and quinoa salad. On the book shelf near the kitchen you can pick up a deck of Cards Against Humanity and see how rude your friends really are.

I don't care how trendy or crowded this place is, it's wonderful any time of the day, week, month or year. One of my very favorite restaurants for a variety of restaurants... Awesome decor Friendly and knowledgeable service Delicious food....both healthy options and comfort food wonders Fair prices Amazing morning buns Every time I return to NY I make a stop.

I went with my wonderful and lovely wife for an early V-Day, and it turned out that they extended restaurant week. Â  I hate restaurant week because all the restaurants cheapen their menu for all you cheap fools looking for a bargain. Â So I couldn't get the Steak and Sea Urchin Tartare, or the Short Rib Ravioli. I won't say what we had because most of it isn't on the menu (stupid right), Â but it was better than most. We'll go back to try the real food, because the fake stuff was still damn good.

Delicious roast pork sandwich, which, for some reason, they call homemade capicola. Never the less, the porcine has a nutty/meaty taste, it's moist without being fatty and mildly seasoned. The broccoli rabe has a nice 'green' taste and is crunchy. The provolone is sharp without being overly pungent and the bread (I believe it may be sourdough) has a riight-out-of-the-oven taste and texture, even though it was cool. In short: this roast pork/capicola sandwich gives D'Nic's, in Philadelphia, a very good run for the money.

This place is okay, definitely did not live up the hype. The wait was pretty average for a nice sunday afternoon brunch, nothing crazy (30-45 mins). The wait staff was very nice and gave us water on line as we waited. The atmosphere is very cute and warm. However, I did not realize just how small the space actually was. I went with two friends and we shared a table with two strangers which was just awkward and uncomfortable, I almost drank out of the man's glass next to me. The food was definitely not bad, but it was by no means amazing or worth the wait, not to mention my friend found a long black hair in her egg benedict (she has short blonde hair). My omelette was good but not worth $16 bucks. However, I will also say that none of us ordered sandwiches and those did look pretty yummy so I would tell someone going to consider those. All in all, I have a bunch of other brunch spots I like more, so will probably not return.

Ok I live down the block and finally made it in to porto. I have put it off so long because it is on one of the most dirty, disgusting blocks in all of brooklyn, which must put it in competition for dirtiest in the country. Its wedged between a nasty smelly asian wholesale fish monger (the stench in the warmer months is unbearable) and a poultry slaughterhouse of all things; it is directly across the street from a gang banger night club and a scary strip club. I assume they got the space for a song because I can't imagine a worse location location location if you tried to find one. The second reason I put off going into this place was because everytime I walk by it the chef is sitting outside chainsmoking with what I gather to be an owner (or the laziest manager I've ever seen). I recall in 'kitchen confidential'the author warns, don't eat at a place where you see the chef smoking outside all the time. Ok, now to the food. The servers were young and cool, and sharply dressed, which is comforting but incongruent with the casual atmosphere, and kind of weird having one half of the restaurant with employees dressed up like a cheesy quasi-fancy little italy place and then a bunch of sweaty slobs on the other side selling garlic knots and handling dough and cash without washing their hands in btween. Which is it? A wanna be fancy place or a certified dump? You can't be both, porto! The brick oven pizza was too thin and dry, the crust had no life to it, completely botched compared to the nyc greats. But ok, were not expecting defarros on this derelict block under the bqe.so I try the pasta and an entree. Definately better than the dishes in your typical corner pizza shop, but for the prices I could go to crispo in manhattan for chrissakes! The sauces are way too heavy and the plating was sloppy boardering on disgusting. Maybe the chef should get a nic patch and spend some more time in the kitchen. Now here's the deal breaker: this place had more flies than I've ever seen in my life. Literally thousands. They even have one of those translucent electric bug zappers over the bar next to the tv, like it was a budweiser sign!!! I know that its not appetizing, but is that even legal? What if a bug gets zapped and it winds up in the ice? Â and when I say there are more flies than I've ever seen, I mean anywhere. A decomposing corpse in the swamp would have less flies buzzing around it. A manure pile at a mexican collective would have less pests. My hand to god. I know that they're down by the river, and wedged btw the chicken slaughterer and the fishmonger, so its an uphill battle, but that's not my problem. dear god, I feel like I'm in an exorcism the flies are so persistent. There is no way they'd pass a health inspection. No way on earth. I give them six months. Eat at your own risk!!!

Last night, after seeing a play at the Al Hirschfeld theatre, we enjoyed a light meal at the bar. Â Service from the bartender was top notch. Â I found the the food was just so-so. Â I had a Caesar Salad, which was passable, but the NY strip steak was overcooked and the frites were greasy. Â Very well-executed cocktails. Â Cool atmosphere: Â Stanley Tucci and his wife, Felicity Blunt, were having dinner there with Patricia Clarkson.
Filipino food with a modern twist. I enjoyed the lamb adobo and the pureed sweet potatoes. My only complaint is that they only accept cash.
